Consider a global feed-poll throttle/lock (e.g. `feed_key` is defined on line 20 but never used) and tolerating the unique-violation.

title: SETNX followed by EXPIRE is not atomic; a crash leaves a permanent throttle key
body: `retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx(key, '1')` and only then `$redis.expire(key, 60)`. If the worker dies or redis errors between the two calls, the key is left with no TTL and non-staff requests for that embed_url are throttled forever. Use `set(key, '1', nx: true, ex: 60)` (atomic) instead.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`. With `discourseUrl = 'http://discourse.example.com/'`, an origin of `http://discourse.example.co` or `http://discourse.exam` passes. Impact is limited to an attacker-controlled frame height, but the check should compare `e.origin` against the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` exactly. Separately, the script assumes `discourseUrl` ends with `/` when building `iframe.src`.

title: `<%- end if %>` is a typo that only compiles by accident
body: The closing tag of the `if @topic_view.posts.present?` block is written as `end if`. Erubis emits `end if\n@output_buffer.safe_append='...'`, so Ruby parses the trailing `if` as a modifier whose condition is the next buffer-append statement. It happens to be truthy, but the template's output order is subtly altered (the following whitespace is appended before the conditional's output) and any later edit to this template can turn it into a syntax error or silently skip the header link. It should be `<%- end %>`.

title: Disqus importer loses --category and original created_at, and now hard-fails on unreachable links
body: The `--category` option was removed and topic creation now goes through `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which neither accepts a category nor passes `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` as the old code did, so imported topics are all placed in the default category and dated at import time, scrambling the forum's chronology. `import_remote` also performs an HTTP fetch of every thread link with no rescue; a single dead/moved link raises `OpenURI::HTTPError` and aborts the whole import run midway. Dry-run output also no longer reflects this network dependency.

title: Loading page reloads every 30s forever, each reload enqueuing a job, even when retrieval can never succeed
body: The loading view reloads unconditionally every 30 seconds. If the embed_url's host does not match `embeddable_host`, the embed user is missing, or the remote fetch keeps failing, `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` will never return a topic, so every open tab hits `/embed/best` and `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` indefinitely (the redis throttle only skips the fetch, not the request/job). There is no failure state or retry cap; consider surfacing an error after N attempts or backing off.

title: Feed parsing/import paths are entirely untested
body: The specs only verify that `execute` gates on three settings and delegates to `poll_feed`; `poll_feed` itself (SimpleRSS parsing, the `link`/`id` fallback, nil `content`, `scrub`, per-item import) is never exercised, nor are `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http`, or `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`. `absolutize_urls` is tested only for a plain `/path`, not protocol-relative or already-absolute URLs. Several of the bugs in this PR (nil content, protocol-relative URLs, deleted-post update path, failed PostCreator) would have been caught by fixture-based tests using FakeWeb (already in the Gemfile) with a sample RSS/Atom document.

title: `float: right` on `.small-action button` is ignored now that `.small-action` is a flex container
body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex` (via the `flexbox()` mixin), which makes its direct children flex items. Per the flexbox spec, `float` has no effect on flex items, so the `float: right` left on `.small-action button` no longer pushes the action button (e.g. the edit/show-all control on small-action posts) to the right edge. Because `.small-action-desc` has no `flex: 1`/`flex-grow`, the button will now sit immediately after the description text instead of right-aligned, a visible layout regression. Either give `.small-action-desc` `flex: 1` or replace the float with `margin-left: auto` on the button (and drop the now-dead `float: left` on `.topic-avatar`).

title: `align-items` mixin passes modern keywords unchanged to legacy syntaxes with a different vocabulary, and emits a non-existent `-ms-align-items` property
body: The `align-items($alignment)` mixin forwards `$alignment` verbatim to `-webkit-box-align` (2009 box spec) and `-ms-flex-align` (IE10 tweener spec). Those legacy properties accept `start`/`end`/`center`/`baseline`/`stretch`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`. The current call sites only use `center` and `baseline`, which happen to overlap, but any future `@include align-items(flex-start)` will silently produce invalid declarations for the very browsers the prefixes are meant to support. The mixin should map `flex-start`→`start` and `flex-end`→`end` for the legacy outputs. Additionally, `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a property any version of IE ever implemented and only adds dead bytes to the compiled CSS.

title: `margin-left: auto` does not right-align `.panel` in browsers that fall back to `display: -webkit-box`
body: The previous `float: right` on `.d-header .panel` was replaced with `margin-left: auto` inside a flex container. In the 2009 `-webkit-box` layout mode, which the new `flexbox()` mixin explicitly emits as a fallback for old WebKit (e.g. Android 2.x–4.3 stock browser, Safari 6), `auto` margins on box children are not honored, so the header panel (notifications/user icons) will no longer be pushed to the right in those browsers; it will sit directly after the title. If those engines are considered unsupported the `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` lines should be dropped from the mixins; if they are supported, the panel needs an explicit `-webkit-box-flex`/spacer approach or the `float` should be kept as a fallback.

title: PR title claims a performance optimization that the change does not make; description is a placeholder
body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" and described only as "Test 5". The diff replaces float-based layout with flexbox and reflows `.small-action` and category badge spacing; nothing in it measurably affects rendering performance (flexbox is not faster than floats, and the header's scroll performance hint `backface-visibility: hidden` is untouched). A reviewer or future git-blame reader will be misled about the intent, and the visual changes to `.small-action` padding/margins and the header panel alignment are not mentioned anywhere. The title and description should accurately state that this is a visual/layout refactor to flexbox and list the intentional spacing changes.

title: `float: right` on .small-action button is ignored now that .small-action is a flex container
body: `.small-action` is turned into a flex container via `@include flexbox()`, which makes `.topic-avatar`, `.small-action-desc` and `button` flex items. The CSS Flexbox spec states that `float` has no effect on flex items, so the `float: right` left on `button` (and `float: left` on `.topic-avatar`) no longer does anything. Because `.small-action-desc` has no `flex: 1`/width and the button has no `margin-left: auto`, the action button (e.g. the close/archive toggle) will now render immediately after the description text instead of at the right edge of the row — a visible layout regression for every small-action post. The button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the desc needs `flex: 1`) to restore the right alignment.

title: Right-alignment of .panel relies on `margin-left: auto`, which the legacy `-webkit-box` model emitted by the mixin does not honor
body: The `flexbox()` mixin deliberately emits `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` for legacy WebKit/Gecko engines (Android stock browser < 4.4, Safari < 6.1, old Chrome). In the 2009 box model, auto margins are not used for distribution and `float` is ignored on box children, so with `float: right` removed and only `margin-left: auto` added, `.panel` (the icons/login buttons) will sit directly after the site title instead of at the right edge of the header on exactly the browsers the prefixes are meant to support. Either drop the legacy prefixes (and accept modern-flexbox-only), or add a legacy-compatible fallback such as `-webkit-box-flex: 1` on `.title`/`.extra-info-wrapper` or `-webkit-box-pack: justify` on `.contents`.

title: Float-based header layout removed with no fallback for browsers without any flexbox support
body: `.title { float: left }` and `.panel { float: right }` were deleted and replaced solely by flexbox on `.contents`. Browsers with no flexbox implementation at all (IE9 and older, Opera Mini) will now render `.title`, `.extra-info-wrapper` and `.panel` as stacked block elements, breaking the header entirely rather than degrading. If any such browser is still in the support matrix the floats should be kept as a fallback (flexbox ignores floats on flex items, so keeping them is harmless for flex-capable browsers).

title: .extra-info-wrapper as a flex item has `min-width: auto`, so long topic titles will push .panel out of the header
body: Now that `.contents` is a flex container, `.extra-info-wrapper` (which holds the docked topic title and category badge) becomes a flex item. Flex items default to `min-width: auto`, meaning they refuse to shrink below their content's min-content width. The wrapper gets `order(2)` but no `flex: 1 1 auto` / `min-width: 0` / `overflow: hidden`, so a long topic title (especially one with `white-space: nowrap`, as applied to `.badge-wrapper`) will widen the item and push `.panel` outside the header or wrap the row, instead of truncating as the previous float layout allowed. Add `min-width: 0; flex: 1;` (with `overflow: hidden`/ellipsis as desired) to the wrapper.

title: Removing paragraph margins in .custom-message collapses spacing between multi-paragraph messages
body:
`.small-action .small-action-desc .custom-message p` had `margin: 5px 0` and now has `margin: 0`. Custom close/archive/pin messages can contain multiple paragraphs (the message is cooked markdown), so consecutive `

` elements will now render with no vertical separation and read as a single run-on block. If the intent was only to remove the outer top/bottom spacing for the flex centering, use `p + p { margin-top: 5px }` or zero only `:first-child`/`:last-child` margins.

title: align-items mixin forwards the modern keyword unchanged to legacy prefixes and emits a non-existent `-ms-align-items` property
body: `-webkit-box-align` (2009 model) and `-ms-flex-align` (IE10 2012 draft) accept `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`; the mixin passes `$alignment` through verbatim, so any future `@include align-items(flex-start)` silently produces invalid declarations for those engines (only `center`/`baseline`, the values used today, happen to coincide). Additionally `-ms-align-items` was never implemented by any IE version (IE11 uses unprefixed `align-items`), so that line is dead output in every compiled stylesheet. Either map the keywords inside the mixin or drop the legacy prefixes to avoid a mixin that looks portable but isn't. (Same class of issue in `order()`: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` is 1-based while `order` is 0-based, so identical values do not produce identical relative ordering against default items.)

title: PR title claims a performance optimization; the change is a layout refactor and the description is a placeholder
body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" but nothing in the diff affects rendering/scrolling performance — it swaps float positioning for flexbox and adds vendor-prefix mixins, which if anything emits more CSS. The description is just "Test 5". A maintainer reading the history will be misled about why the header, small-action and badge layouts changed; the title/description should describe the actual change (float → flexbox layout, vendor-prefix mixins) and note the visual changes (removed bullet margin, small-action spacing).

title: `float: right` on `.small-action button` is a no-op once `.small-action` becomes a flex container
body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex` (via `@include flexbox()`), which makes `.topic-avatar`, `.small-action-desc` and `button` flex items. Per the flexbox spec `float` has no effect on flex items, so the existing `button { float: right; }` no longer pushes the edit/delete buttons to the right edge; they will render immediately after the description text. Nothing else in the rule (no `margin-left: auto` on the button, no `flex: 1` on `.small-action-desc`) compensates for this, so the small-action rows lose their right-aligned controls. Either add `margin-left: auto` to the button or `flex: 1` to `.small-action-desc`.

title: `align-items` mixin passes modern keywords straight to legacy IE10/old-WebKit properties
body: The mixin emits `-ms-flex-align: $alignment` and `-webkit-box-align: $alignment` with the unmodified argument. The legacy syntaxes use `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so any future call such as `@include align-items(flex-start)` will silently produce invalid declarations in IE10 and old WebKit/Android while appearing to work elsewhere. The current callers only pass `center` and `baseline` (which happen to be shared keywords), but the mixin's contract is misleading. Additionally `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a real property in any browser and is dead output.

title: Legacy `-webkit-box` fallback does not support the `margin-left: auto` layout relied on in the header
body: The `flexbox()` mixin emits `display: -webkit-box` as the fallback for old WebKit (Android 2.x–4.3 stock browser, Safari <6.1). In the 2009 box model, `margin: auto` on children is not treated as free-space distribution, so the `.d-header .panel { margin-left: auto }` introduced in header.scss will not push the panel to the right on those browsers; it will sit directly after the title/extra-info. Previously the panel was `float: right`, which worked everywhere. If those browsers are still supported, the panel needs an alternative (e.g. `-webkit-box-flex: 1` on a spacer or on `.title`), otherwise the legacy prefixes are just misleading.

title: Removing the bullet margin-top fix leaves `.badge-wrapper.box` in the header offset by 5px
body: The diff removes `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px }` on the assumption that `align-items: center` on `.d-header .contents` now vertically centres badges. However `badges.css.scss` still sets `.badge-wrapper.box { margin-top: 5px }` globally (line 101), which in a centred flex row shifts box-style category badges 5px below the centre line while bullet and bar styles are centred. Sites using the box badge style will see a misaligned category badge in the header; the box margin should be overridden inside `.extra-info-wrapper` the same way the bullet one was handled.

title: PR title claims a performance optimisation; the change is a layout refactor with visible behavioural changes and the description is a placeholder
body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" and described only as "Test 5". Switching from floats to flexbox is not a performance optimisation and the diff intentionally changes rendering: header items are reordered via `order`, `.small-action-desc` padding changes from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`, and paragraph margins/padding inside small actions are removed. Reviewers and future readers of the history will be misled about intent and risk; the title/description should accurately describe the layout changes and their expected visual impact.

title: Local cache is populated before the limited insert, so a rejected device is admitted on its next request
body: `tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, ...)` before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`. When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the cache entry remains for ~29 minutes. On the device's very next request `localCache.Get(key)` hits, `tagDeviceUI` returns nil, `TagDevice` returns nil, and `Anonymous.Authenticate` issues an identity. The new device limit therefore only rejects the first request from an over-limit device; a reload (which the browser/UI will naturally do) bypasses the limit entirely, and the device is never written to the DB so it isn't even counted. The cache must be set only after a successful write (or removed on `ErrDeviceLimitReached`).

title: Device limit is trivially bypassed by clients that omit the X-Grafana-Device-Id header or have an unparsable address
body: `TagDevice` returns nil (no error) when the `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header is absent and also when `network.GetIPFromAddress` fails. Since `Anonymous.Authenticate` only denies access on `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, any anonymous client that simply does not send the device header (curl, scripts, API consumers, a browser with the header stripped) is authenticated regardless of the configured `device_limit`. If the limit is intended as an enforcement mechanism rather than best-effort UI accounting, requests without a device ID should be rejected when a limit is configured, or the limitation should be clearly documented.

title: Count-then-insert is not atomic; concurrent new devices can exceed the configured limit
body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` in one session and the INSERT/upsert in a separate `WithDbSession` call, with no transaction or lock. N concurrent first-time anonymous requests arriving while `count == deviceLimit-1` will all observe a count below the limit and all insert, so the stored device count can exceed `deviceLimit` by the degree of concurrency. Enforcing the limit in a single transaction (or with a serverlock/advisory lock) is required for the limit to be a hard cap.

title: Device tagging moved from a background goroutine into the synchronous auth path, adding a COUNT(*) plus write to request latency
body: Previously tagging ran in a detached goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout; now `TagDevice` executes inline inside `Authenticate` using the request context. For every uncached device this adds a `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM anon_device WHERE updated_at BETWEEN ...` (full range scan on a table that can hold tens of thousands of rows when a limit is configured) plus an INSERT/UPDATE before the identity is returned, and any DB slowness now directly delays or fails anonymous page loads. The local cache mitigates this per device for ~29 minutes but not for first requests or multi-instance deployments. Consider caching the count or using a cheaper check, and only blocking on the DB when a limit is configured.

title: Limit test does not cover the update path for an existing device or the cache bypass
body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only asserts that a second, new device gets `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. It does not verify that an already-registered device can still be updated when the limit is reached (the `updateDevice` branch returning nil), that a device whose last update is older than 30 days is rejected, or that the service layer (`TagDevice`/`Authenticate`) actually denies the device on repeated requests. The last case would have caught the local-cache bypass in `tagDeviceUI`.

title: anonymousDeviceLimit is typed as `undefined` and never actually undefined at runtime
body: `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` makes TypeScript infer the property type as the literal `undefined` (under strictNullChecks), so consumers of `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` cannot use it as a number without a cast. Meanwhile the backend DTO field is a plain `int64` without `omitempty`, so the JSON always contains a number (0 when unset) and the `number | undefined` declaration in `GrafanaConfig` is misleading. Declare it as `anonymousDeviceLimit = 0` / `number` and treat 0 as 'no limit', or make the backend field a pointer with `omitempty`.

title: New `device_limit` setting is not added to conf/defaults.ini, conf/sample.ini or the configuration docs
body: `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is read from `[auth.anonymous] device_limit`, but the PR adds no entry to `conf/defaults.ini`/`conf/sample.ini` and no documentation for the setting or its semantics (0 = unlimited, 30-day window, what users see when rejected). Administrators have no discoverable way to learn the option exists, and Grafana's convention is that every ini key has a documented default.

title: ProvideAnonDBStore signature change may break wire generation if the store is still listed as a provider
body: `ProvideAnonDBStore` now requires an `int64` argument and `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` now takes `db.DB` instead of `anonstore.AnonStore`. The previous signature implies the store was being provided via dependency injection (wire); `pkg/server/wire.go` is not in this change set. If `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` is still registered in the wire set, `wire gen` will fail with no provider for `int64`; if it is not removed and was bound to `anonstore.AnonStore`, the binding becomes dead. Please verify the wire set was updated.

title: Local cache is populated before the store write, so a device rejected by the limit is let through on its next request
body: `tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`. When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the error is propagated and `Anonymous.Authenticate` correctly refuses the request, but the device's cache key has already been written. On the very next request from the same `X-Grafana-Device-Id` (and for the next ~29 minutes), `tagDeviceUI` hits the cache and returns nil, so `Authenticate` succeeds and the device is served as a normal anonymous user even though it was never recorded and the limit is still exhausted. The device limit is therefore only enforced for a single request per device per cache lifetime. The cache entry must only be written after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds (or be deleted on `ErrDeviceLimitReached`).

title: Count-then-insert is not atomic; concurrent new devices can exceed the configured limit
body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` in one DB session and the insert/upsert in a separate `WithDbSession` call, with no transaction or row locking. If several previously-unseen devices authenticate concurrently (or across multiple Grafana instances, which share the table but not the local cache), each sees `count < deviceLimit` and all of them insert, so the number of active devices can exceed `device_limit` by the degree of concurrency. If the limit is meant to be a hard cap (it blocks authentication), the check and insert should be performed in a single transaction, or the insert should be made conditional in SQL.

title: Unauthenticated callers can exhaust the device limit with arbitrary device IDs and lock out anonymous access for 30 days
body: `X-Grafana-Device-Id` is a client-supplied header with no validation, and each distinct value creates a row in `anon_device`. With `device_limit` set, `Authenticate` now returns an error for any new device once the count is reached. An attacker can send `device_limit` requests with random header values and thereby block all legitimate new anonymous visitors; the fabricated rows stay counted for 30 days (`anonymousDeviceExpiration`) and there is no admin endpoint to delete devices (`/api/anonymous/devices` is read-only). This turns the limit into a trivial denial-of-service vector for anonymous access. At minimum the behaviour and the recovery path should be documented, and a delete/cleanup API or ID validation considered.

title: Device limit is bypassed by any request that omits the X-Grafana-Device-Id header
body: `TagDevice` returns nil immediately when the `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header is absent, and `Authenticate` then issues a full anonymous identity. Since the limit is only enforced inside `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, any client that does not send the header (curl, scripts, a browser with the header stripped) is never counted and is never blocked, even when the limit is reached. The new `device_limit` setting therefore cannot be relied on as an access cap; it only constrains well-behaved UI clients. This should be documented clearly for the setting, or non-UI anonymous requests should be handled explicitly when the limit is active.

title: ProvideAnonDBStore now requires an int64 and ProvideAnonymousDeviceService no longer accepts an AnonStore; DI wiring must be updated
body: Before this change `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` received an `anonstore.AnonStore` from dependency injection, which implies `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` (and a `wire.Bind` for `AnonStore`) is registered in `pkg/server/wire.go`. This PR changes `ProvideAnonDBStore` to take `(db.DB, int64)` and makes the service construct the store itself, but `wire.go`/`wire_gen.go` are not in the changed file set. If the provider is still listed, wire generation fails (no provider for `int64`, or an unused-provider error); if it has been silently dropped elsewhere, any other consumer of `anonstore.AnonStore` loses its provider. The wiring changes should be included in this PR and `make gen-go`/wire regenerated.

title: anonymousDeviceLimit is typed as `undefined` on GrafanaBootConfig and the backend never sends undefined
body: `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` without an explicit type annotation gives the class field the static type `undefined` (not `number | undefined`), so consumers of `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` cannot use it as a number without a cast even though `merge(this, defaults, options)` assigns a number at runtime. Additionally, `FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is a non-`omitempty` `int64`, so the backend always serialises a number (0 when the limit is disabled) and the `| undefined` in `GrafanaConfig` never occurs in practice. Declare it as `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;` (matching `loginError`) or type it as `number` with a 0 default, and make the DTO/TS types agree.

title: No test covers the 'update existing device when limit reached' path or the client rejecting a new device
body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only verifies that a second, new device is rejected. The new `updateDevice` branch (an already-counted device must still be refreshed when `count >= deviceLimit`, and a stale device outside the 30-day window must be rejected) is untested, as is the end-to-end behaviour in `Anonymous.Authenticate` returning an error on `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and the interaction with the local cache in `impl_test.go`. Given the limit now gates authentication, these paths should have coverage; a test for the cache interaction would have caught the bypass described for `tagDeviceUI`.

title: Local cache is populated before the store rejects the device, so the limit is bypassed on the next request
body: `tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`. When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the device's cache key has already been written with the 29‑minute default TTL. On the very next request from the same (rejected) device, `tagDeviceUI` finds the key in the cache and returns nil, so `TagDevice`/`Authenticate` succeed and the anonymous identity is issued. The device limit therefore only denies the first request per device per instance per ~29 minutes; a browser that simply retries (which the UI does) gets in. The cache entry must only be set after a successful create/update (or must be deleted on error).

title: Device limit is trivially bypassed by omitting the X-Grafana-Device-Id header
body: `TagDevice` returns nil when the `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header is empty (and also when the client IP cannot be parsed), and `Authenticate` only fails on `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. Since the header is set voluntarily by the frontend, any anonymous caller (curl, scripts, embedded dashboards, a browser with the header stripped) that does not send it is never counted and never blocked, regardless of `device_limit`. If the limit is meant to be an enforcement mechanism rather than a best-effort UI metric, requests without a device ID must be treated as over-limit (or at least counted), otherwise the setting gives a false sense of control.

title: Count-then-insert is not atomic; limit can be exceeded under concurrent requests
body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` in one session and then the INSERT/UPSERT in a separate `WithDbSession`, with no transaction or locking. Two or more new devices authenticating at the same time (or across multiple Grafana instances sharing the DB) all read `count < deviceLimit` and all insert, so the number of active devices can exceed `device_limit` by the degree of concurrency. If the limit must be strict, the check and insert need to run in a single transaction with appropriate locking, or the insert must be made conditional on the count in one statement.

title: ProvideAnonDBStore signature change likely breaks wire dependency injection
body: `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` now requires a second `deviceLimit int64` parameter, and `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` now takes `db.DB` instead of `anonstore.AnonStore`. Before this change `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` received an `AnonStore`, which means `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` (with a `wire.Bind` to `AnonStore`) is registered as a provider in `pkg/server/wire.go`. That file is not touched in this PR; wire cannot satisfy an `int64` argument, so `wire gen` / `wire_gen.go` compilation will fail until the provider and bind are removed from the wire set.

title: Device tagging moved from background goroutine onto the synchronous authentication path
body: Previously `TagDevice` ran in a goroutine with its own 2‑minute timeout so DB latency or failures never delayed authentication. It is now called synchronously inside `Authenticate` with the request context. For every anonymous device not present in the local cache this adds a `SELECT COUNT(*) ... BETWEEN` (when a limit is configured) plus an upsert to the critical path of every request, and the cache expires every 29 minutes per device per instance. On busy anonymous instances (public dashboards) this directly increases request latency and DB load, and a slow DB now stalls auth instead of just the tag. Consider keeping the write asynchronous and only doing the (cheap, cached) limit check synchronously.

title: ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned as a plain error with no status/user-facing message
body: `Authenticate` returns the raw `fmt.Errorf("device limit reached")` sentinel. The authn service and HTTP layer map unknown errors to a generic 401/500 with no indication of why the anonymous user was rejected, and the frontend has no way to show a meaningful message (the new `anonymousDeviceLimit` setting alone doesn't tell the UI that *this* device was rejected). Other authn clients use `errutil` errors with a public message and status; `ErrDeviceLimitReached` should be defined the same way so the response and logs are actionable.

title: Device-limit tests don't cover the update path, the cache interaction, or Authenticate
body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only asserts that a second new device is rejected. There is no test that an already-registered device can still be updated once the limit is reached (the whole point of `updateDevice`), that a device outside the 30‑day window counts as a free slot, that `Authenticate` actually fails with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, or that a rejected device stays rejected on a subsequent request (which would have caught the local-cache bypass in `tagDeviceUI`). `TestIntegrationDeviceService_tag` also keeps using `setting.NewCfg()` with limit 0, so the service-level limit code path is never exercised.

title: New `device_limit` setting is not added to defaults.ini/sample.ini or documentation
body: `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is read from `[auth.anonymous] device_limit`, but the PR does not add the key to `conf/defaults.ini`, `conf/sample.ini`, or `docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/`. Grafana's convention is that every configuration key appears in both ini files with a comment and in the configuration docs; without this, administrators have no way to discover the option or its semantics (0 = unlimited, counting window of 30 days, behaviour when exceeded). The PR description template is also left unfilled, so reviewers get no statement of intended behaviour.

title: enableSqlExpressions has inverted/dead feature-flag logic and always returns false
body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (so `enabled` is actually true when the flag is *disabled*), and then returns `false` in both branches. The feature-flag lookup is therefore meaningless and the variable name is misleading. While the net effect (SQL expressions always rejected) is the intended security outcome, this reads like a half-finished gate: a future maintainer trying to 're-enable behind the flag' by changing the first `return false` to `return true` would actually enable SQL expressions when the flag is OFF. If the intent is an unconditional kill-switch, drop the flag check and return false directly (or a constant) with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264; if the intent is flag-gated, fix the negation.

title: No regression test asserting SQL expressions are rejected
body: This is a fix for a critical RCE/LFI (CVE-2024-9264), but the PR adds no test that (a) `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` with `QueryTypeSQL` returns an error even when `FlagSqlExpressions` is enabled, (b) `NewSQLCommand`/`UnmarshalSQLCommand` fail for any non-empty SQL, and (c) `sql.DB.QueryFramesInto`/`RunCommands`/`TablesList` return errors. Without such tests, a later refactor (e.g. someone 'fixing' the odd logic in `enableSqlExpressions`, or re-adding a real DB implementation behind `NewInMemoryDB`) could silently re-expose the vulnerable path. Add unit tests in `pkg/expr` and `pkg/expr/sql` that lock in the disabled behavior.

title: Every SQL expression attempt now logs a misleading ERROR with the user's raw SQL
body: `TablesList` still escapes the SQL, builds a `json_serialize_sql` command and calls `duckDB.RunCommands`, which now unconditionally returns `not implemented`. The result is that every user attempt to use a SQL expression emits `logger.Error("error serializing sql", ..., "sql", rawSQL, "cmd", cmd)` followed by `logger.Warn("invalid sql query", ...)` in `NewSQLCommand`. The message is wrong (nothing is being serialized; the feature is disabled), it is at ERROR level for an expected/handled condition, and it dumps user-supplied SQL into server logs twice per request. Since the function can never succeed, it should short-circuit with a clear 'SQL expressions are disabled' error (and the now-dead `tablesFromAST`/`astError`/`existsInList` helpers and the `flatten` import can be removed) rather than exercising the old pipeline.

title: sqlExpressions feature toggle remains documented/exposed but has no effect
body: After this change the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle (`featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions`) is still registered and documented as enabling SQL expressions, but enabling it does nothing: `ReadQuery` returns `sqlExpressions is not implemented` and the `sql.DB` stub errors on every call. Users who follow the existing feature-toggle documentation will enable the flag and get a confusing 'not implemented' error. Either mark the toggle as disabled/removed in its registration and docs, or update the toggle description to state that the feature has been disabled for security reasons.

title: enableSqlExpressions computes an inverted, unused flag value
body: `enableSqlExpressions` assigns `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` — i.e. the variable named `enabled` is true when the feature toggle is OFF — and then returns `false` on both branches, so the toggle lookup is dead code. The net effect (always disabled) is what this PR intends, but the function is misleading: anyone later re-enabling the feature by changing the body to `return enabled` would enable SQL expressions exactly when the toggle is disabled and disable them when it is enabled. If the intent is to hard-disable regardless of the toggle, the function should simply return false (or be a constant) without the inverted lookup; if the toggle should be honored later, the negation must be removed.

title: Legacy SQL command path is only disabled implicitly via the stub error
body: The explicit "sqlExpressions is not implemented" guard was added only to `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery`. The legacy path (`UnmarshalSQLCommand` → `NewSQLCommand`, used by the rawNode/`buildCMDNode` flow for dashboards and alerting) has no such guard and is disabled only because `sql.TablesList` now calls a stub that returns "not implemented". That works today but has two downsides: (1) the user-facing error is `sql-invalid-sql` / "error reading SQL command", which wrongly suggests their SQL is malformed rather than that the feature is disabled, and the full raw SQL is logged at Warn level for every attempt; (2) the disablement depends on the stub remaining unimplemented — if `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` is ever filled in again, this path becomes live without any feature-toggle or defense-in-depth check. Add an explicit early return in `NewSQLCommand`/`UnmarshalSQLCommand` (or in the TypeSQL case of `buildCMDNode`) with a clear "disabled" message.

title: No tests cover the new disabled behaviour; existing DuckDB-backed tests not updated
body: The PR replaces the DuckDB engine with a stub whose every method returns "not implemented", and adds an unconditional rejection in `ReadQuery` for `QueryTypeSQL`, but adds no test asserting that a SQL expression query is rejected on either the reader path or the `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand` path. Any existing tests in `pkg/expr/sql` (e.g. parser tests exercising `TablesList`) or `pkg/expr` that previously relied on the real DuckDB implementation returning table lists/frames are not modified in this PR and will now fail (or were already skipped and thus silently prove nothing). For a security hard-disable, a regression test that fails if SQL expressions become executable again is important so the fix cannot be accidentally reverted.

title: FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle remains registered and documented but can never enable the feature
body: After this change, SQL expressions are rejected unconditionally ("sqlExpressions is not implemented") regardless of the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle. The toggle remains in the feature registry and in the feature-toggle docs with no indication that it is now inert, so operators who enable it will get an error with no explanation. Either the toggle description/docs should state that the feature is disabled pending a secure re-implementation, or the toggle should be removed/marked as such, so users are not misled into thinking the flag still gates a working feature.

title: enableSqlExpressions evaluates an inverted feature flag and then ignores it
body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns `false` on both branches. Two problems: (1) the variable named `enabled` is actually true when the flag is *disabled*, so if anyone later re-enables the feature by changing the final `return false` to `return enabled`, SQL expressions would be enabled exactly when the flag is off; (2) the flag lookup is dead code that misleads readers into thinking the flag still controls the behaviour. If the intent is a hard kill-switch, the function should simply return false with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264; if the intent is to keep the flag, the negation must be removed.

title: Users of the legacy SQL node path get a misleading 'invalid sql query' error instead of 'not implemented'
body: `NewSQLCommand` is still reachable through `UnmarshalSQLCommand` (the `rawNode` / classic graph path), which is not gated by the new `enableSqlExpressions` check in reader.go. On that path the stubbed `sql.TablesList` now always fails with `not implemented`, but the code wraps it as `logger.Warn("invalid sql query", ...)` and returns a BadRequest with public message `error reading SQL command`. Users who had SQL expressions in dashboards/alert rules will be told their SQL is invalid rather than that the feature has been disabled, which will generate confusing support reports. The stub error should be detected and surfaced as a clear 'SQL expressions are disabled' message.

title: No tests cover the new 'SQL expressions always rejected' behaviour
body: This PR changes `pkg/expr/sql` so that `TablesList`, `RunCommands` and `QueryFramesInto` always return errors, and adds a gate in `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` that rejects `QueryTypeSQL`. No test is added or updated to assert that a SQL expression query is rejected via either entry point (`ReadQuery` or `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand`), nor that it stays rejected when `FlagSqlExpressions` is enabled. Given this is the in-repo landing of a critical CVE fix, a regression test is needed so a future refactor (e.g. 'fixing' the dead-code in `enableSqlExpressions`) cannot silently re-expose the feature. Any pre-existing tests in `pkg/expr/sql` that exercised `TablesList` against a working engine would also now fail and should be updated or removed in this PR.

title: canManage() grants management of all groups to admins holding only the VIEW scope
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns true when the caller has either `VIEW` or `MANAGE` on the all-groups ("Groups") resource: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`. `canManage()` is the gate used by `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` (`auth.groups().requireManage()`), so an admin who was only granted view access to all groups can create top-level groups in the realm. This is a privilege escalation relative to the intended V2 scope model (compare `canManage(GroupModel)` in the same class, which correctly checks only `MANAGE`, and `UserPermissions.canManage()` which checks only `MANAGE`). The interface Javadoc in `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` ("For V2 only: Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") codifies the same mistake. The scope list should be `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` only, and the Javadoc fixed accordingly.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs and evaluates the wrong resource
body: In V2 a group's authz `Resource` is created with the group id as its *name* (`AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup` returns `group.getId()` and `getOrCreateResource` calls `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, ...)`), and no `setType(...)` is ever called on it. `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` nevertheless (a) iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups", ...)`, which only matches the single all-groups resource created in `init()` (the only one with a type), never individual group resources; (b) calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`, which does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` with a resource UUID, so the lookup always misses and silently falls back to evaluating the all-groups resource; and (c) adds `groupResource.getId()` (the authz resource UUID) to the result rather than the group id (`getName()`). Consequence: the method either returns an empty set (no per-group restriction ever applied) or, when an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission exists, returns a set containing a UUID that is not a group. Callers in `UsersResource.searchForUser`/`getUsersCount` and `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` then set `UserModel.GROUPS` to that bogus id, so user search/count is restricted to a non-existent group and returns 0 results for an admin who should see all group members. The current tests do not exercise this path (they only grant VIEW_MEMBERS on a single group, where the evaluator falls back to per-user `canViewByGroup`). The method should use `groupResource.getName()` for both the permission check and the returned id, skip the all-groups resource itself, and the individual resources need a type set (or a different lookup) for `findByType` to find them.

title: NPE when the Groups resource-type resource cannot be resolved
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` returns `null` when `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false (e.g. the realm has an admin-permissions client but `adminPermissionsEnabled` was later switched off) or when the "Groups" resource is missing. `hasPermission` immediately passes that value to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later `resource.getScopes()`, producing a `NullPointerException` (HTTP 500) on every group endpoint for any admin without the `manage-users`/`view-users` roles. A null check returning `false` is needed before the fallback lookup.

title: requireManageMembers Javadoc references the wrong method
body: The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` says "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns false", but the implementations throw when `canManageMembers(GroupModel)` returns false (a different scope: `manage-members` vs `manage-membership`). Additionally the Javadoc of `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` says "@return Stream of IDs" while the method returns a `Set<String>`. Since this PR adds the documentation specifically to clarify the scope semantics, these inaccuracies are misleading to implementers.

title: Removal of the global canView() short-circuit causes a policy evaluation per listed group in V2
body: Before this change `getSubGroups` (and `GroupsResource.getGroups`) computed `canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView()` once and only fell back to `canView(g)` per group. Now `.filter(auth.groups()::canView)` is used directly. In `GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)` there is no call to the global `canView()` first; each group triggers `resourceStore.findByName`, a `policyStore.findByResource` lookup and a full policy-engine `evaluatePermission` against the all-groups resource. For an FGAP admin with an all-groups VIEW permission (no `view-users` role) listing N subgroups now costs N policy evaluations instead of one. Either restore the one-time global check in the resources or have `GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)` check the all-groups permission once and cache it.

title: No negative test that an all-groups VIEW permission does not grant management, and no test of all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS on user search
body: `testViewGroups` grants the all-groups `VIEW` scope and only asserts that groups become visible; it never asserts that the same admin still cannot create a top-level group or update a group. Such an assertion would have caught `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returning true for `VIEW`. Likewise, none of the tests grant `VIEW_MEMBERS`/`MANAGE_MEMBERS` on the all-groups resource and then search/count users, which is the path that exercises `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (currently returning authz resource UUIDs instead of group ids and restricting the user search to a non-existent group). Both scenarios should be covered since the PR's purpose is to add the Groups resource type evaluation.

title: getResourceName does not resolve Groups resources, returning null display names
body: `getResourceName` only maps resource names for the `Users` resource type ("All users" / username). Resources created for the new `Groups` type via `getOrCreateResource` are named by the group id and created without a display name, so for group permissions this method falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` and returns `null` (and the all-groups resource is not mapped to a friendly label either). Any caller rendering permission resources (e.g. admin console listing of permission resources) will show empty/null names for group permissions. A `GROUPS` branch resolving the group (and e.g. "All groups" for the type resource) is needed, mirroring the Users handling.

title: V2 canManage() grants manage on all groups to admins that only have the VIEW scope
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) succeeds, i.e. when the caller merely has the 'view' scope on the all-groups ('Groups') resource. canManage() is what GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() enforces via auth.groups().requireManage(), so an admin granted only read access to all groups can create new top-level groups. This looks like a copy/paste of canView(); the interface javadoc in GroupPermissionEvaluator (lines 75-76) even documents 'VIEW or MANAGE' for canManage(), which is the wrong contract. It should check only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE (mirroring canManage(GroupModel) on line 79). No test covers the negative case (VIEW-all must not allow creation).

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In the findByType callback, hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) looks the resource up again by name using the resource's ID (hasPermission does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)), which never matches because V2 group resources are named by group ID. The lookup therefore always falls back to the all-groups resource, and when that has a VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission the code adds groupResource.getId() (an authz resource UUID, not a group ID) to the returned set. UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource put this set into session attribute UserModel.GROUPS, which the user store uses to filter the DB query by group membership. Consequences: with per-group permissions the set is effectively always empty, so paging (first/max) is applied before the in-memory canView filter and pages come back short or empty; with an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS permission the set contains a bogus ID so the user search returns nothing at all. Both calls should use groupResource.getName() (the group ID), as the V1 implementation does with resource.getName().substring(...).

title: NPE when the Groups resource-type resource cannot be resolved
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() returns null when supportsAuthorizationSchema() is false (feature disabled, realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled() false, or session.getContext().getRealm() differs from the realm whose admin-permissions client was resolved by root.realmResourceServer()). hasPermission() then calls policyStore.findByResource(server, null) and resource.getScopes() without a null check, producing a NullPointerException (500) instead of a deny. This is reachable e.g. for a realm whose admin-permissions client still exists after the flag has been turned off. A null check returning false is needed.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc references the wrong predicate
body: The javadoc for requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says it throws when canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false, but the implementations (GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers) check canManageMembers(GroupModel). manage-membership and manage-members are distinct scopes with different semantics, so the documentation is misleading. Additionally, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()'s @return says 'Stream of IDs' although it returns a Set.

title: getResourceName() not extended for the new Groups resource type
body: getResourceName() special-cases only USERS (mapping the all-resource to 'All users' and per-user resources to the username). For the newly added GROUPS resource type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is never set for schema-created group resources (getOrCreateResource creates them with the group ID as name and no display name), so permission listings for group resources will show null/raw UUIDs instead of 'All groups'/the group name or path. The Groups branch (and a 'group not found' check analogous to the user one) should be added.

title: Global view short-circuit removed; policy evaluation now runs per group in listings
body: The previous code computed canViewGlobal once and only called canView(g) per element when it was false. Now stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView) (and the same change in GroupResource.getSubGroups line 179) evaluates per group. For admins whose access comes from an all-groups permission rather than a realm role, every listed group triggers resourceStore.findByName, a fallback lookup of the resource-type resource, policyStore.findByResource and a full policy evaluation. Listing large group trees under FGAP V2 will be noticeably slower than before. Keeping a single canView() check before the per-group filter would avoid this.

title: switch on resourceType throws NullPointerException for null input
body: The new switch (resourceType) statement dereferences the string. Before this change a null resourceType resulted in name == null and the explicit IllegalStateException 'Could not map resource object...'; now a null value yields a bare NullPointerException. Callers that reach getOrCreateResource for non-scope policy types without a resource type would surface a 500 with an unhelpful message. Guard for null before the switch or include it in the default message.

title: No coverage for VIEW-all not granting manage, for DB-level group filtering, or for group members endpoint
body: After granting the all-groups VIEW permission, the test only asserts that groups are listed; it never asserts that creating a top-level group is still forbidden, which would have caught canManage() accepting the VIEW scope. There is also no test exercising user search with first/max paging or with an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS permission, which would expose getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returning resource IDs instead of group IDs, and no test of GET /groups/{id}/members (requireViewMembers) under VIEW_MEMBERS / MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions.

title: canManage() grants manage when admin only has VIEW permission on all groups
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either the VIEW or the MANAGE scope on the "Groups" resource-type resource (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`). VIEW must never imply manage. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() guards with `auth.groups().requireManage()` (the no-arg variant), so an admin who was only granted a view-all-groups permission can create new top-level groups and, by POSTing a representation with an existing group id, move any existing group to the top level (`realm.moveGroup(child, null)`). The interface Javadoc for canManage() in GroupPermissionEvaluator even documents this behaviour ("VIEW or MANAGE"), so the doc is wrong too. The check should only consider AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE, as canManage(GroupModel) does.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs and cannot find per-group resources
body: Three problems make this method return wrong data: (1) `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups", ...)` only matches the single resource-type resource created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init(); per-group resources created by getOrCreateResource() never get a type set, so they are never iterated. (2) The callback passes `groupResource.getId()` (the authz Resource UUID) to `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)`, which does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` expecting the group id (the resource name); the lookup always misses and falls back to the all-groups resource. (3) `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` adds the authz resource UUID, not a GroupModel id. The result is used by UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource as the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute and by getUsersCount() as the group filter. Concretely, an admin granted VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on all groups gets a set containing the UUID of the "Groups" resource, the user search is restricted to members of a non-existent group and returns zero users and a zero count, even though canView(user) would allow them. With only per-group permissions the set is always empty, so the DB pre-filter is silently skipped and results are filtered only after pagination (pages can come back short/empty). The new tests pass only because UserPermissionsV2.canView(user) independently re-evaluates group membership. The method should iterate the actual per-group resources (set a type on them in getOrCreateResource or query differently) and return `resource.getName()` as the group id.

title: getResourceName() has no handling for the new Groups resource type
body: getResourceName() special-cases only the Users type ("All users" / username) and otherwise returns `resource.getDisplayName()`. Resources created for groups via getOrCreateResource() have name = group id and no display name, so permissions on individual groups (and on the "Groups" type resource) will be presented with a null/empty resource name wherever this method is used (e.g. listing permissions in the admin console). Since this PR adds the Groups type to the schema, it should also resolve the group (e.g. return the group path/name, and "All groups" for the type resource).

title: switch on resourceType throws NPE for null instead of a meaningful error
body: `switch (resourceType)` on a String throws NullPointerException when resourceType is null. Before this change a null type simply left `name` null and produced the IllegalStateException "Could not map resource object...". getOrCreateResource() is reached from representation-to-model paths where the resource type may be absent for non-ScopePermission representations (throwExceptionIfResourceTypeOrScopesNotProvided only validates ScopePermissionRepresentation), so a client can now trigger a 500 with an NPE rather than a validation error. Add an explicit null check before the switch.

title: Feature check moved to registration time breaks runtime feature toggling
body: The listener used to be registered unconditionally and checked `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` on every event. Now the check happens once at registration, so if the feature is enabled after startup (the testsuite enables/disables features at runtime via Profile.configure and the testing REST endpoint), the cleanup of role/client/group permission resources on removal is never wired and orphan authz resources/policies are left behind. If this change is intentional, the runtime-toggle path must re-register the listener; otherwise keep the per-event check.

title: requireManageMembers Javadoc references the wrong method
body: The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` says it throws ForbiddenException if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false, but the implementation (GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers) delegates to `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. These are distinct permissions (manage-members vs manage-membership), so the doc misleads callers. Also `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` is documented as returning a "Stream of IDs" while it returns a Set.

title: No negative test that view-only group permissions do not grant manage/create
body: testViewGroups grants a VIEW-only all-groups permission and only asserts that groups are listed; it never asserts that the admin is still forbidden from creating a top-level group, moving groups, or updating/deleting a group. Such an assertion would have caught GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returning true for the VIEW scope. Likewise there is no test for an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission making group members visible via users().search()/count(), which would have exposed the broken getGroupIdsWithViewPermission().

title: Exhausted federated recovery-codes credential is removed from the wrong store
body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` now prefers the credential returned by the user storage's `getCredentials()`. When that federated credential reports `allCodesUsed()`, the code calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(id)`, which only operates on the local Keycloak DB. The ID belongs to the user-storage credential, so the call is a no-op (or, if the storage did not set an ID, passes `null` into the JPA store). The exhausted credential stays in the user storage, `isConfiguredFor(recovery-authn-codes)` remains true, and the user will keep being challenged for a recovery code they cannot satisfy until the required action completes. For federated credentials the removal should go through the storage (e.g. `disableCredentialType`) rather than the local store.

title: Login form throws NoSuchElementException when storage accepts recovery codes but does not expose them via getCredentials()
body: With this PR a user storage provider that returns true from `supportsCredentialType`/`updateCredential`/`isConfiguredFor` for `recovery-authn-codes` will own the credential, and the authenticator's `configuredFor()` will return true. However `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials()` has a default empty implementation, so `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` returns an empty Optional for any provider that implements validation but not `getCredentials()`. `credentialModelOpt.get()` (and `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()` on line 21) then throw `NoSuchElementException` while rendering the recovery-code login page, producing a 500 for every such user. The new implicit requirement that providers implement `getCredentials()` is neither enforced nor documented; the bean should handle the absent case gracefully (e.g. omit the code number) instead of failing the login.

title: Undocumented wire contract: raw recovery codes passed to user storage as an ad-hoc JSON array
body: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` sends the plaintext recovery codes to `CredentialInputUpdater.updateCredential` as a JSON-serialized `List<String>` in the `challengeResponse` of a `UserCredentialModel` with an empty id. Nothing in the SPI (`RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`, `UserCredentialModel`, javadoc, constants) describes this format, so third-party storage providers have no way to know what they receive, that the codes are unhashed, or that they are responsible for hashing them and for marking codes as consumed in `isValid`. A provider that does not hash will persist recovery codes in clear text. The format should be documented on the SPI (ideally with a typed model/constant, similar to how OTP uses the OTP policy type) and the javadoc should state the provider's hashing/consumption responsibilities.

title: Backwards-compatibility provider now depends on APIs that post-date 4.8.3 and can NPE
body: This class's javadoc states it is a frozen 4.8.3-era provider whose purpose is to prove newer Keycloak still works with old provider code. The PR adds an `@Override` of `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials(RealmModel, UserModel)` and uses `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`, neither of which existed in 4.8.3, so the provider no longer tests what the javadoc claims. Additionally `getCredentials` dereferences `getMyUser(user)` without the null check that every other method in this class performs, so a user removed from the map (or a user with a mismatched username case) will throw NPE from `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`.

title: Test storage never consumes recovery codes, so the new test cannot detect consumption/exhaustion regressions
body: `isValid` for recovery codes does a plaintext `anyMatch` and never marks a code as used, and `getCredentials` rebuilds a fresh `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` from the raw list on every call, so `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()` is always code 0 and `allCodesUsed()` is never true. Consequently `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` asserting `expectedCode == 0` is trivially satisfied and nothing exercises reuse rejection, second-code login, exhaustion → required action, or disabling (`disableCredentialType` and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` also ignore recovery codes, so admin/account removal of federated recovery codes is untested and would silently leave them in place).

title: Exhausted federated recovery-codes credential is removed via local store only
body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(authenticatedUser)` now prefers the credential returned by the user storage provider (`getFederatedCredentialsStream`). When that federated model reports `allCodesUsed()`, the code still calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`, which only touches Keycloak's local credential table. For a credential that lives in user storage this is a no-op (the exhausted codes remain in the external store and `isConfiguredFor` keeps returning true), and if the provider did not assign an id to the model (`RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues` does not set one) the JPA store is asked to find an entity with a null id, which throws `IllegalArgumentException` and turns the last successful recovery-code login into a 500. The federated branch needs to go through the storage provider (e.g. `disableCredentialType`) instead of `removeStoredCredentialById`, or skip removal when the credential did not come from local storage.

title: Login form bean still unconditionally unwraps Optional; federated providers without getCredentials() crash the page
body: The bean now looks up the credential via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` but still calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking presence. With this PR, `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.configuredFor` returns true as soon as the user storage provider's `isConfiguredFor(..., recovery-authn-codes)` returns true, so the recovery-code form is rendered for federated users. However `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials()` has a default implementation returning an empty stream; a provider that implements `supportsCredentialType`/`isConfiguredFor`/`isValid`/`updateCredential` for recovery codes (everything the feature otherwise requires) but does not override `getCredentials()` makes `getCredential()` return `Optional.empty()`, and the login page fails with `NoSuchElementException` (HTTP 500) for every such user. Either handle the empty case (e.g. fall back to a generic prompt without a code number) or clearly document in `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`/release notes that providers must implement `getCredentials()` returning a `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`.

title: getCredentials() dereferences getMyUser() without null check
body: `getCredentials(realm, user)` does `var myUser = getMyUser(user);` and immediately accesses `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp`. Every other method in this provider (`isConfiguredFor`, `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isValid`) guards against `getMyUser` returning null, which happens for users not present in the in-memory map (e.g. a user adapter still referenced after `removeUser`, or a user from a different component instance sharing the realm). Since `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` is now invoked from the browser authenticator and the login form bean on every recovery-code login, this becomes an NPE surfacing as a 500 instead of an empty stream. Return `Stream.empty()` when `myUser == null`.

title: Provider claims recovery-codes support but cannot disable or report them as disableable
body: `supportsCredentialType` and `isConfiguredFor` were extended to return true for `recovery-authn-codes`, and `updateCredential` stores them, but `disableCredentialType` still only handles OTP (recovery codes fall into the 'Unsupported to disable' branch) and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` never reports the type. As a result the admin REST `disableCredentialType` and the account-console credential removal for a federated user holding recovery codes silently do nothing, and the new test only exercises setup + login. The disable/remove path for federated recovery codes (the analogue of `testDisableCredentialsInUserStorage` / `testOTPSetupAndRemoveThroughAccountMgmtAndLogin`) is therefore untested.

title: Federated recovery-code test does not cover invalid code, code consumption, or exhaustion
body: `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` only verifies a single successful login with code #0. The test storage's `isValid` never marks a code as used and `getCredentials()` rebuilds a fresh `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` on each call, so `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()` is always 0 and `allCodesUsed()` is never true. Consequently the new federated-storage branches in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` (credential removal / re-adding `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES` when codes are exhausted) and the rejection of a wrong code for a federated user are not exercised at all. Add at least a negative login attempt and a scenario where the provider reports all codes used.

title: Unguarded Optional.get() can now throw for federated users whose storage does not expose the credential via getCredentials()
body: The bean now resolves the credential with RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user), which looks at user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream() and then local storage, and immediately calls credentialModelOpt.get(). Before this PR recovery codes were always written to the local DB, so the Optional was effectively always present when this form was rendered. With this PR, a user storage that returns true from supportsCredentialType/updateCredential/isConfiguredFor for "recovery-authn-codes" but does not override CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials() (the default returns an empty stream) will make the authenticator consider the user configured (configuredFor() uses isConfiguredFor), yet getCredential() returns Optional.empty() and this constructor throws NoSuchElementException, producing a 500 on the recovery-code login page. Same problem if the storage's getCredentials() returns a CredentialModel whose credentialData is not the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel JSON (createFromCredentialModel / getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() will fail). The bean should handle an absent/invalid credential gracefully (e.g. fall back to not displaying a code number) instead of crashing.

title: Raw recovery codes are pushed to user storage as an undocumented JSON blob in challengeResponse, changing behaviour for existing storage providers
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the plaintext generated codes as a JSON array and passes it as the challengeResponse of a UserCredentialModel of type "recovery-authn-codes" to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). This creates a new implicit SPI contract (storage must parse a JSON array of raw codes from CredentialInput.getChallengeResponse(), hash/store them, consume them in isValid(), and expose a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel-compatible model from getCredentials()) that is documented nowhere in the SPI or in this method's javadoc. It is also a behaviour change: prior to this PR recovery codes were always stored in Keycloak's DB regardless of the storage provider; now any existing CredentialInputUpdater whose supportsCredentialType() is permissive (e.g. returns true for unknown types) and whose updateCredential() returns true will silently swallow the codes, and the local fallback is skipped, leaving the user with codes that the storage cannot validate. The contract should be documented (SPI javadoc / release note) and the format of the challengeResponse made explicit.

title: User label and generation timestamp are dropped on the user-storage path
body: When the credential is handed to the user storage, only the type and the JSON list of codes are passed in the UserCredentialModel; credentialModel.getUserLabel() and the generatedAt timestamp (taken from the form and validated against the auth note in RecoveryAuthnCodesAction) are discarded. The storage has no way to receive them, so the label the user entered during setup is silently lost for federated users, while it is persisted for local users. Either pass this metadata (e.g. via the existing RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel JSON) or document that it is not supported for user storage.

title: removeStoredCredentialById is called with the id of a federated credential
body: optUserCredentialFound may now come from getFederatedCredentialsStream(). When such a federated model reports allCodesUsed(), the code calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()). That method only removes credentials from local Keycloak storage, so for a federated credential it is a no-op (or passes a null id if the storage did not set one), and the exhausted credential remains in the user storage. The user does get CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES added, so re-setup overwrites it eventually, but isConfiguredFor() keeps returning true in between, and disableCredentialType() would be the appropriate call for the federated case.

title: Test storage never consumes recovery codes and NPEs for unknown users in getCredentials()
body: getCredentials() rebuilds a fresh RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel from the raw list on every call and isValid() only checks membership in that list, so codes are never marked as used: getNextRecoveryAuthnCode() always returns code #0 and any code can be replayed indefinitely. The new test testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin asserts exactly that code 0 is requested, so it passes only because of this simplification and does not exercise the realistic case where the storage advances the next code / exhausts the codes (the allCodesUsed() branch in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator is never reached for federated users). Additionally getCredentials() dereferences getMyUser(user) without a null check, unlike isConfiguredFor()/getDisableableCredentialTypesStream(), so it throws NPE if called for a user not present in the map.

title: Recovery codes cannot be disabled/removed in the test storage
body: supportsCredentialType(), updateCredential(), isConfiguredFor() and isValid() were extended for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE, but disableCredentialType() still only handles OTP and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() never reports the recovery-codes type. Consequently neither the admin REST disableCredentialType nor the account console removal path can remove recovery codes from this storage, and there is no test for removing/disabling recovery codes stored in user storage (the analogous OTP flows testOTPSetupThroughAdminRESTAndLogin / testOTPSetupAndRemoveThroughAccountMgmtAndLogin exist but have no recovery-codes counterpart).

title: Class javadoc claims 4.8.3 compatibility but the provider now depends on APIs that did not exist then
body: The javadoc states this is a 'UserStorage implementation created in Keycloak 4.8.3' used for backwards compatibility testing and that future versions 'should work fine without a need to change the code of this provider'. This PR changes the provider to use RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, CredentialModel.setCredentialData(), CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials() and KeycloakModelUtils.generateId() on the OTP path, none of which existed in 4.8.3. Either the documentation should be updated to reflect that the provider is no longer a frozen 4.8.3 snapshot, or the recovery-code support should live in a separate test provider so the backwards-compatibility guarantee the test is meant to verify is not weakened.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an uninstantiable abstract class
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed from a concrete `DetectorHandler` (with a stub `evaluate` returning `[]`) to `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass`. `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares four abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`) none of which are implemented here. Because `MetricAlertFire` is auto-registered in the grouptype registry with `detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler`, any `Detector` row with `type == "metric_alert_fire"` will cause `Detector.detector_handler` (`group_type.detector_handler(self)`) to raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`, which propagates out of `process_detectors` and aborts processing of the whole batch. The previous stub at least ran safely; either keep a concrete stub implementation of the abstract methods or drop the `detector_handler` assignment until the real implementation lands.

title: Expected occurrences built with wrong group_key/value; assertions don't verify occurrence contents
body: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` the expected occurrence is built via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, ...)` but `evaluate_group_key_value` is invoked with group key `"group_key"` and value `10`, so the handler's real `build_occurrence_and_event_data` produces a fingerprint `["<id>:group_key"]` that differs from the expected `["<id>:val1"]`. Similarly `test_state_results_multi_group` builds the `group_2` expectation with value `6` while the packet carries `10`. These assertions can only pass because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` hardcodes `id="eb4b0acffadb4d098d48cb14165ab578"` and `IssueOccurrence` equality is effectively id-based, meaning every mock occurrence compares equal to every other. As a result the new tests do not actually verify that the hook is called with the correct group key, value, priority or fingerprint, and `assert_has_calls(..., any_order=True)` in the multi-group test would pass even if the same occurrence were produced twice. Either pass the matching arguments and assert on the handler's call arguments (e.g. via `mock.patch.object(MockDetectorStateHandler, 'build_occurrence_and_event_data')`), or give each mock occurrence a distinct id derived from the group key.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` was changed to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still reads "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". Implementers reading the docstring will get the wrong contract; update it to describe the dict keyed by group key.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract class and cannot be instantiated
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler` with a bare `pass` body. `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares four abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`), none of which are implemented here, so the class remains abstract. It is still registered as `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler`, and `Detector.detector_handler` instantiates it via `group_type.detector_handler(self)`. For any `Detector` row with `type == "metric_alert_fire"`, that property (and therefore `process_detectors`) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler ...` instead of returning a handler or logging and returning `None`. Previously the class was concrete (it returned `[]`). Either implement the abstract methods (even with stub bodies) or stop registering it as the group type's handler until it is implemented; there is also no test exercising this handler that would have caught the regression.

title: Expected occurrence in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe is built with the wrong group key
