body: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe`, the expected `IssueOccurrence` is built via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`, but `evaluate_group_key_value` is invoked with `group_key="group_key"`. `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` uses `handler.build_fingerprint(group_key)`, so the expected fingerprint is `["<id>:val1"]` while the handler will produce `["<id>:group_key"]`. `IssueOccurrence` is a frozen dataclass with field-wise equality, so `DetectorEvaluationResult.__eq__` will compare these as unequal and the assertion `== expected_result` cannot pass as written (or, if it does pass, it indicates equality is not comparing what the test intends). The call should pass `expected_result.group_key` ("group_key") and the actual value (10) to the helper.

title: evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list
body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` was changed to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still reads "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". Implementers reading the docstring will get the wrong contract; it should describe the dict keyed by group key.

title: Stale TODO comment about becoming a stateful detector
body: The comment `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction` is now inaccurate: the class directly subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` in this PR, so the abstraction exists and is already being used. The TODO should be removed or replaced with one describing the actual remaining work (implementing the abstract hooks).

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract class but is still registered as a concrete detector_handler
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler` with a bare `pass` body. `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares four abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`), none of which are implemented here, so the class is still abstract. `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` points at it, and `Detector.detector_handler` (models/detector.py) does `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, which will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` for any `Detector` row whose `type` is `metric_alert_fire`. The `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector...` comment on line 10 is also now stale.

title: Expected occurrence in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe is built with the wrong group key
body: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe`, the expected occurrence is built via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`, but `evaluate_group_key_value` is invoked with `group_key="group_key"` and `value=10`. `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` sets `fingerprint=handler.build_fingerprint(group_key)`, so the expected `IssueOccurrence` has fingerprint `["<id>:val1"]` while the handler will produce `["<id>:group_key"]`. `IssueOccurrence` is a frozen dataclass with field-wise equality, so `expected_result` will not equal the actual result and the assertion on line 546-560 fails (or, if it somehow passes, it is not verifying the fingerprint at all). The expected occurrence should be built with `"group_key"` (and ideally the same value) so the test actually validates the occurrence the hook produces. Similarly, `test_state_results_multi_group` builds `occurrence_2` with value `6` while the packet has `group_2: 10`; it only passes because the mock ignores `value`.

title: evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list
body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` was changed to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still states "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". Since the whole point of this change is to make the return keyed by group key to prevent duplicates, the docstring should describe the dict shape so implementers of other handlers are not misled.

title: Hung/dead flusher processes are never killed before restart because isinstance check fails for SpawnProcess
body: `_ensure_processes_alive` only calls `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. The processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which is `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` — a direct subclass of `BaseProcess`, not of `multiprocessing.Process` (`multiprocessing.context.Process`). The isinstance check is therefore always False in production, and `kill()` is never invoked. The previous code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally (catching ValueError), so this is a regression. Consequence: when a process is deemed hung (`cause == "hang"`), it is left running and a second process is started for the same shards. Two flushers then concurrently call `flush_segments`/`done_flush_segments` on the same Redis shards, producing duplicate segments to Kafka and racing on Redis state, while the stale processes accumulate (up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS per index). The same broken check in `join()` (line 346) means `terminate()` is also never called on shutdown. Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`.

title: Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched earlier in the test
body: `test_basic` does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at the top, and the new line `time.sleep(0.1)` resolves `time.sleep` at call time through the `time` module, so it calls the patched no-op. The comment says it gives the flusher thread time to process after the drift change, but it waits zero seconds. The race it was meant to fix remains: `step.join()` immediately sets `stopped`, and if the flusher thread observes `stopped` before running `flush_segments` with the new drift, `messages` is empty and `(msg,) = messages` fails. Capture the real sleep before patching (as `test_flusher.py` does with `from time import sleep`) or poll for `messages` with a deadline.

title: join() breaks out of the loop on deadline and skips terminate() for remaining processes
body: In `join()`, when the deadline has passed the loop does `break`, so any processes not yet visited never reach `process.terminate()`. The inner `while` already exits immediately once the deadline has passed, so the `break` is unnecessary and only has the effect of skipping termination of the remaining processes. On a slow shutdown this leaves spawned flusher processes running after the consumer's strategy has been joined (they are daemonic, but will keep flushing until the parent actually exits).

title: Inconsistent metric tag keys ('shard' vs 'shards') with a comma-joined multi-shard value
body: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` are tagged with `{"shard": shard_tag}` while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `{"shards": shard_tag}`. All three use the same comma-joined string (e.g. "0,4,8"), so the `shard` tag name is misleading and dashboards/queries cannot filter consistently across these metrics. Additionally, `flusher_unhealthy` (line 244) emits one point per individual shard with `shard=<int>`, so the same tag key has different semantics across metrics. Pick one key and one value shape.

title: Redis memory info is fetched once per flusher buffer although all buffers point to the same cluster
body: `submit()` iterates `self.buffers.values()` and calls `get_memory_info()` on each. Every `SpansBuffer` connects to the same Redis cluster, so each call returns the memory info for all cluster nodes; with N flusher processes this issues N× the INFO round-trips per submit and sums N copies of the same used/available values (the ratio is unchanged but the work is redundant). Similarly `record_stored_segments()` is called per buffer. Querying memory info once (e.g. on a single buffer) is sufficient.

title: Docstring claims one process per shard, but the default CLI setting is a single process
body: The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing", but the number of processes is `min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))`, and the `--flusher-processes` CLI option defaults to 1, so in the default configuration a single process handles all shards. The docstring should describe the actual sharding (shards are round-robin assigned to up to `max_processes` processes) and mention the `max_processes` parameter.

title: No test covers shard-to-process assignment correctness or the multi-process restart path
body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` only checks process counts and that the total number of mapped shards equals 4. It does not assert that shards are disjoint across processes or balanced (e.g. process 0 -> [0, 2], process 1 -> [1, 3]), and nothing exercises `_ensure_processes_alive` restarting one of several processes (per-index restart counters, per-index healthy_since/backpressure values, killing the old process). Given the isinstance bug in the kill path, a test that drives a process into the unhealthy state and verifies the old one is gone would have caught it.

title: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False for spawn-context processes, so hung flushers are never killed
body: Processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which yields `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process` (= `multiprocessing.context.Process`), so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` evaluates to False. In `_ensure_processes_alive` this means `process.kill()` is never called when a process is detected as hung (`cause == "hang"`). Before this PR `kill()` was invoked unconditionally. Consequence: a hung-but-alive flusher is leaked and a second process is started for the same shards; if the old one resumes, two flushers concurrently run `flush_segments`/`done_flush_segments` on the same Redis shards, which can produce duplicate segments to buffered-segments and double the Redis load. Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` (or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`) instead. The same wrong check in `join()` (line 346) means `terminate()` is also never called there.

title: join() stops terminating remaining processes once the deadline passes
body: In `join()`, when the deadline has elapsed the loop does `break`, which skips `process.terminate()` for every process not yet visited. Previously the single process was always terminated after the wait. With several flusher processes, any that haven't exited by the join timeout are left running (only the `stopped` flag is set, which a hung process ignores). The `break` should be removed so each remaining process still gets `terminate()` called (the inner `while` already respects the deadline).

title: Redis memory info is fetched once per flusher process instead of once per cluster
body: `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` returns memory usage for every node of the Redis cluster, not just the buffer's shards. `submit()` now calls it for each per-process `SpansBuffer` and sums the results. With N flusher processes this issues N times as many `INFO memory` calls to every Redis node on every submit, and `used`/`available` are each over-counted N times (the ratio happens to survive, but the values are wrong if anyone logs/reports them). Since the check is cluster-wide, it should run once (e.g. on a single buffer) rather than per process.

title: Inconsistent metric tag names: "shard" vs "shards"
body: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` are tagged with `{"shard": shard_tag}` while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` on the same code path uses `{"shards": shard_tag}`, and `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` uses `shard` with a single int. The same comma-joined value is emitted under two different tag keys, which makes dashboards/queries inconsistent. Pick one tag name.

title: Docstring claims one process per shard, but default is a single process
body: The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing", but `max_processes` caps the count, and the CLI option `--flusher-processes` defaults to 1, so in the default deployment all shards share one process. The docstring should describe the `max_processes` parameter and the shard-to-process distribution instead.

title: No test covers the real multiprocess path or process restart
body: Both new/updated tests pass `produce_to_pipe`, which forces the `threading.Thread` code path. The actual `mp_context.Process` branch (pickling the per-shard buffer, `run_with_initialized_sentry`, `is_alive`/`kill`/`terminate` handling in `_ensure_processes_alive` and `join`) is never exercised, which is exactly where the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` bug lives. `test_flusher_processes_limit` also only asserts the total shard count; it does not check that shards are disjoint across processes or that a dead process is recreated for the same shards. Adding a test that spawns at least one real process (or a restart test with a thread that exits early) would catch regressions here.

title: Hung/dead flusher processes are never killed: isinstance check against multiprocessing.Process is always False for spawn-context processes
body: `_create_process_for_shards` creates processes via `self.mp_context.Process`, where `mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`. That class is `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`, which subclasses `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` directly and is NOT a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process` (`multiprocessing.context.Process`, a sibling class). Consequently `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` on line 254 is always False in production, so `process.kill()` is skipped. The previous code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally, so this PR regresses the restart path: when a flusher is detected as hung (`cause == "hang"`), the old process keeps running while `_create_process_for_shards` spawns a replacement for the same shards. Two processes then concurrently `flush_segments`/`done_flush_segments` on the same Redis shards, which can produce duplicate segments to the buffered-segments topic and leaks a process on every restart (up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS per shard group). The same wrong check on line 346 means `terminate()` in `join()` is also a no-op for real processes. Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)` instead.

title: join() stops terminating remaining processes once the deadline passes
body: In `join()`, when `remaining_time <= 0` the loop does `break`, which skips the `process.terminate()` call for the current and all remaining processes. The previous single-process implementation always called `terminate()` after the wait loop regardless of whether the deadline was hit. With multiple flusher processes, a slow first process can consume the whole timeout and leave every subsequent process running un-terminated (they only exit once they notice `stopped`, which may be after a long blocking `future.result()` on Kafka). The `break` should be replaced by skipping only the wait (or terminating unconditionally after the loop).

title: Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched earlier in the test
body: `test_basic` calls `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` on line 15 and then, via `import time`, calls `time.sleep(0.1)` on line 62 with the comment "Give flusher threads time to process after drift change". Because the module attribute is patched, this sleep returns immediately and does nothing; the test still races between the flusher thread observing the new drift and `step.join()` setting `stopped`. If this was added to deflake the test, it does not achieve that. Either use a reference to the real sleep captured before patching (as `test_flusher.py` does with `from time import sleep`), or poll on `messages` until the segment appears.

title: Inconsistent metric tag key: "shards" vs "shard" for the same shard_tag value
body: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` are tagged with `{"shard": shard_tag}` (lines 185, 195), while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` on line 199 uses `{"shards": shard_tag}` for the identical value. Dashboards/queries grouping flusher metrics by tag will not line up across these three metrics. Pick one key (note `shard_tag` is a comma-joined list, so "shards" is arguably the accurate one, but it must be consistent).

title: Docstring claims one process per shard, but the default is a single process
body: The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing." In practice `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))`, and the `--flusher-processes` CLI option in `src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py` defaults to 1, so production runs a single flusher process handling all shards unless the operator opts in. The docstring should describe the actual behaviour (up to `max_processes` processes, shards distributed round-robin) and document the new `max_processes` parameter, which is currently missing from the `:param:` list.

title: _create_process_for_shard is dead code
body: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is defined but never called anywhere in the codebase (`_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards` directly with the process index). It also has a subtle hazard if someone later uses it: it starts a replacement process without killing the existing one for that index, duplicating flushers for those shards. Remove it or make it kill the old process first.

title: Redis memory info is fetched once per flusher process on every submit()
body: `submit()` now calls `buffer.get_memory_info()` for every entry in `self.buffers` and sums the results. `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info` reports memory for the Redis cluster nodes (not per assigned shard), so with N flusher processes this issues N times the INFO/memory round-trips per `submit()` and sums the same `used`/`available` numbers N times. The resulting ratio is unchanged so backpressure decisions are still correct, but the extra Redis calls are pure overhead on the main consumer thread, which this PR is explicitly trying to keep minimal. Query memory info from a single buffer (e.g. the first) instead.

title: `prisma` used without being imported
body: `getClient` now calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` but the file never imports `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma` (imports only include jsforce, rrule, zod, lib helpers and types). This is a TypeScript compile error and, if it slipped through, a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime, which would break every Salesforce calendar operation since `getClient` runs in the constructor.

title: Freshly refreshed Salesforce token is persisted but the stale token is used for the connection
body: After refreshing the access token and writing `accessTokenParsed.data` to the DB, the jsforce Connection is still constructed with `credentialKey.access_token` / `credentialKey.instance_url` from the old credential. The new access token is never used in-process, so if the old one was expired the connection still fails. Additionally `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure, so the `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` branch is dead, and `response.statusText !== "OK"` is unreliable (HTTP/2 responses have an empty statusText), which would spuriously throw a 400 for successful refreshes. The refresh also now happens unconditionally on every service instantiation instead of only when the token is expired.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses nonsensical computed keys, so sync-mode parsing always fails
body: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` evaluates `ZodString.toString()` which yields the string "[object Object]" as the property name. The resulting schema is `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]": number }` (the second computed key overwrites the first with `z.unknown().optional()`, or vice versa). It does not express "any numeric property is the expiry" at all. Depending on evaluation order the schema either requires a literal `"[object Object]"` number field (all real responses fail → `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned`), or is just `{access_token}` with every other field stripped by zod's default strip behaviour, dropping `expires_in`/`expiry_date` entirely. Either way, when `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set the token refresh for Google, Office365, Zoom and Salesforce is broken.

title: Placeholder refresh_token "refresh_token" is injected and can overwrite the real refresh token in the DB
body: When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the helper mutates `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. This runs in both sync and non-sync modes. In Office365 (`refresh_token` is `.optional()` in its schema) the result is spread over the stored credential (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`), so whenever Microsoft omits the refresh token the real one is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token" and persisted, permanently breaking future refreshes for that user. In Zoom the same value is written to `key.refresh_token`. The placeholder should never be written over an existing valid token.

title: Google credential key is overwritten with the zod SafeParse result object instead of the credential data
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `safeParse` result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed data. Previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the credential object directly. Now `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` persists `{success: true, data: {...}}` as the credential key. On the next load `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails because `access_token`/`refresh_token` are nested under `data`, so every Google Calendar credential that goes through a refresh becomes unusable. Should be `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data`.

title: Sync branch returns a raw fetch Response regardless of what the wrapped refresh function returns
body: Callers treat the return value of `refreshOAuthTokens` as whatever their own `refreshFunction` returns: Google expects a Gaxios response and reads `res.data`; HubSpot expects a `HubspotToken` object and reads `.expiresIn`/`.accessToken` and stores it as the DB key; Zoho CRM / Zoho Bigin expect an axios response and read `.data`. When credential sync is enabled the helper instead returns a WHATWG `Response`, so `res.data` is `undefined` (Google crashes on `token.access_token`), HubSpot computes `NaN` expiry and persists a serialized `Response` (`{}`) as the credential key, and Zoho reads `undefined.error` and throws. Only the fetch-based adapters (O365, Zoom, Webex, Lark) can work in sync mode. The helper must normalize the sync response into the shape each adapter expects (or adapters must handle both).

title: Call to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication
body: The POST to the self-hoster's sync endpoint sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no shared secret, signature or bearer header. The endpoint is expected to return live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user IDs, so anyone who can reach it can harvest every user's third-party tokens by iterating IDs. Cal.com already has `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` for the reverse direction; the outbound request should at least include it (e.g. in the configured header) so the receiving side can authenticate the caller.

title: credentialId passed where userId is expected
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's id as the `userId` argument. In sync mode this sends the wrong `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint (and would wrongly trigger sync for team credentials that have no user). `biginAuth` has access to `credential.userId`; it should be threaded through and used here.

title: In sync mode the O365 expires_in transform is bypassed, so the token is treated as always expired
body: `refreshTokenResponseSchema` converts the relative `expires_in` seconds into an absolute epoch timestamp, and `getToken` compares that against now via `isExpired(o365AuthCredentials.expires_in)`. When sync is enabled `parseRefreshTokenResponse` uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead, which (if it parses at all) leaves `expires_in` as a small relative number (e.g. 3600). `isExpired(3600)` is always true, so every Graph call triggers a new round-trip to the sync endpoint and a DB write, and the useful error logging that was removed in this diff no longer surfaces malformed responses.

title: Unvalidated input paths produce unhandled 500s and no method restriction
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on bad input, `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on a bad ciphertext or when `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is empty, and the handler accepts any HTTP method (a GET with no body reaches `.parse(undefined)`). None of these are caught, so the caller gets a generic Next.js 500 with no actionable message. Use `safeParse`, wrap decryption in try/catch returning 400, and reject non-POST requests. Also the secret comparison uses `!==` rather than a constant-time compare (`crypto.timingSafeEqual`), which is the norm for webhook secrets.

title: Decrypted payload is stored as the credential key without validation
body: `keys` is whatever `JSON.parse` returns (could be a string, number, null or array) and is written directly to `credential.key`. A malformed or non-object payload would create a credential that every CalendarService/VideoApiAdapter fails to parse, and the existing `invalid` flag is never reset to `false` when a credential is overwritten with fresh keys, so a previously invalidated credential stays marked invalid even after a successful sync.

title: No tests for the new shared OAuth helpers or webhook endpoint
body: The PR introduces shared logic (`parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens`) that is now on the token-refresh path of ~10 integrations, plus a new unauthenticated-by-env webhook that writes credentials. The author notes no tests were added. Given the schema-construction bug and the return-shape mismatch above, unit tests for both sync and non-sync branches (and for the webhook's auth / validation / upsert paths) would have caught these before merge.

title: Google credential key is overwritten with the zod SafeParse wrapper object on every refresh
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the raw `safeParse` result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed data. The previous code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (the token object). Now `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` writes `{success, data}` into `credential.key`, so on the next instantiation `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails and the Google Calendar integration breaks for that user. This happens for every token refresh regardless of whether credential syncing is enabled, i.e. it corrupts all Google Calendar credentials in production.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema is malformed; computed keys evaluate to "[object Object]" and all other fields are stripped
body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the string "[object Object]", so the schema is effectively `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown }`. Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, so when credential sync is enabled every parsed response only contains `access_token`; `expires_in`/`expiry_date` etc. are dropped. Callers then compute `Date.now() + undefined * 1000` (NaN expiry in Zoom) or lose the expiry entirely (Office365), causing the token to be considered expired/invalid on every call. The intent ('any numeric property is the expiry', 'allow other properties') cannot be expressed this way; use `.passthrough()` or an explicit schema.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with literal placeholder "refresh_token", which then overwrites the real refresh token in DB
body: When the refresh response lacks `refresh_token`, the function injects the string `"refresh_token"` into `data`. Callers spread this data over the stored credential (`o365AuthCredentials = {...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data}` in office365calendar, `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` in zoomvideo), so the genuine refresh token is destroyed and replaced by a bogus string. Microsoft legitimately omits `refresh_token` on some refresh responses (the schema marks it optional), so this corrupts Office 365 credentials even with credential sync disabled, and permanently breaks the credential once the access token expires.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported
body: `await prisma.credential.update(...)` references `prisma`, but there is no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` in this file. This is a type-check failure and, at runtime, a ReferenceError that makes every Salesforce CalendarService instantiation reject, breaking the Salesforce integration entirely.

title: Salesforce refreshes the token unconditionally on every construction and never uses the new access token
body: `getClient` now performs a refresh_token grant every time the service is constructed (no expiry check), adding an extra Salesforce API call per booking/availability check and risking rate limits. The refreshed `access_token` is stored in DB but the `jsforce.Connection` is still built with the old `credentialKey.access_token`. Additionally `response.statusText !== "OK"` is unreliable (statusText is empty on HTTP/2), so valid responses may be rejected with a 400. The refresh also bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential syncing (the point of this PR) is not applied to Salesforce.

title: Sync path returns a fetch Response regardless of what the wrapped refreshFunction would have returned
body: When syncing is enabled the helper returns a raw `fetch` `Response`, but several callers expect the shape of their own refresh client: hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` → NaN expiry, `accessToken` undefined), zohocrm and zoho-bigin expect an axios response (`tokenInfo.data` is undefined → TypeError), googlecalendar expects `{ res: { data } }` (`res?.data` undefined → TypeError). So enabling `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` breaks token refresh for HubSpot, Zoho CRM, Zoho Bigin and Google Calendar. The helper needs to normalise the response (e.g. return parsed JSON) and callers must consume it consistently.

title: credentialId passed where userId is expected
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential id as the `userId` parameter. When sync is enabled the self-hoster's endpoint receives `calcomUserId=<credential id>`, so it will look up or return tokens for the wrong user (or fail). Should be `credential.userId`.

title: appStoreMetadata is keyed by app directory name, not slug, so lookups by slug fail for many apps
body: `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` indexes the metadata map using the DB slug (e.g. `google-calendar`, `zoom`, `office365-calendar`), but `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by directory name (`googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`, `office365calendar`). For every app whose dirName differs from its slug the webhook returns 404 'App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug', so credentials for the most common apps cannot be synced. Look up by `Object.values(appStoreMetadata).find(m => m.slug === app.slug)` instead. The same slug/dirName confusion appears in callers of `refreshOAuthTokens` (`"zoomvideo"` vs `"google-calendar"` vs `"msteams"`), making the `appSlug` sent to the sync endpoint inconsistent.

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==` and no HTTP method restriction
body: The shared secret is checked with a plain string comparison, which leaks timing information and allows byte-by-byte guessing of the secret. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. The handler also accepts any HTTP method (GET included) and does not guard against `req.headers[...]` being an array. Given this endpoint writes arbitrary third-party credentials for any user id, authentication should be hardened.

title: Schema parse, decryption and JSON.parse errors are uncaught and surface as 500s
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse`, `symmetricDecrypt` (wrong key / malformed ciphertext) and `JSON.parse` all throw synchronously and are not caught, so malformed webhook payloads produce an unhandled 500 with a stack trace instead of a 400 with a clear message. Use `safeParse` and wrap decryption in try/catch.

title: Refresh failure now throws instead of logging and continuing; error details are lost
body: Previously a failed parse of Microsoft's token response was logged (zod error plus raw MS response) and execution continued. Now `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws a generic 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' with no detail, and the surrounding `getToken` has no catch, so the failure propagates to callers (availability/booking) and debugging information about why MS rejected the refresh is gone.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys evaluate to "[object Object]"; all non-access_token fields are stripped
body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are JavaScript computed property keys; calling `.toString()` on a Zod schema object yields the literal string "[object Object]", not a wildcard. Both keys collide (the second wins), so the schema is effectively `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() })`. Because `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, when credential sync is enabled every expiry/scope/instance_url field is dropped from the parsed result and no numeric expiry is ever validated. Downstream, Zoom computes `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` = NaN, Office365 never gets an updated `expires_in`, and Salesforce loses `instance_url`/`id`/`signature` from the stored key. Use `.passthrough()` / `z.record` or an explicit refinement instead of computed keys.

title: Google credential key is now persisted as the zod SafeParse wrapper `{success, data}`
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `safeParse` result object (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed data. The Google service writes this directly with `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so after the first token refresh the stored `credential.key` becomes `{"success":true,"data":{access_token,...}}`. On the next instantiation `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails because `access_token`/`refresh_token` are no longer top-level, permanently breaking the Google Calendar integration for that user in both sync and non-sync modes. The code must store `parsed.data` (and the same wrapper is spread by Office365 and Salesforce via `.data`, so those happen to be fine).

title: Injects the literal string "refresh_token" as refresh_token, overwriting real refresh tokens in callers
body: When the refreshed response lacks `refresh_token`, the helper mutates `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Callers then copy this into the stored credential: Zoom does `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` (line 120 of zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts) and Office365 spreads `tokenResponse.data` over `o365AuthCredentials` (line 264 of office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, where `refresh_token` is `.optional()`). In either case the user's genuine refresh token is replaced with the placeholder string, and the next refresh against the real provider fails with invalid_grant, forcing the user to reconnect the app. The placeholder should never be written back; callers should preserve the existing refresh token when none is returned.

title: Sync path returns a raw fetch Response but callers expect provider-specific shapes
body: When `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the `fetch` `Response` regardless of what `refreshFunction` would have returned. Several callers do not handle a `Response`: Google reads `res?.data.access_token` (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94-95) → TypeError; HubSpot treats the result as a `HubspotToken` and reads `.expiresIn`/`.accessToken` and stores the Response object as `key` (hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:192-198); Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `tokenInfo.data.error` expecting an axios response (zohocrm:217, zoho-bigin:96) → TypeError. So enabling credential sync breaks token refresh for Google, HubSpot, Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin. Additionally `response.ok` is never checked, so a 4xx/5xx body is parsed as a token.

title: Outbound request to the credential sync endpoint carries no authentication
body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no secret/header. The endpoint returns live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user IDs, so a self-hoster following this contract must expose an unauthenticated token oracle (or invent out-of-band auth). The inbound webhook uses `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`/`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`; the outbound call should send the same shared secret so the self-hoster can verify requests.

title: Credential id passed where userId is expected
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's primary key as the third argument, but the helper treats it as the Cal.com `userId` and posts it as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint. The self-hoster will look up the wrong user (or none), and team credentials (userId null) are not excluded. Should pass `credential.userId`.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService
body: The new block calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` but the file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This fails type-check and at runtime throws `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` inside `getClient`, so every Salesforce service instantiation rejects and all Salesforce bookings fail.

title: Salesforce now refreshes on every instantiation yet still uses the stale access token
body: `getClient` unconditionally POSTs to `login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` each time the service is constructed (no expiry check), which adds latency and will hit Salesforce refresh rate limits. The newly obtained token is written to the DB but the `jsforce.Connection` is still built with `credentialKey.access_token`/`instance_url` from the old key, so the refresh has no effect on the actual client. Also `response.statusText !== "OK"` is unreliable (HTTP/2 responses have an empty reason phrase) and will throw a 400 even on success; use `response.ok`. Finally, unlike other apps this call bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so with sync enabled it still contacts Salesforce directly while `parseRefreshTokenResponse` applies the (broken) minimum schema.

title: Webhook accepts any HTTP method and returns 500 on malformed bodies
body: The handler does not restrict to POST, and `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError that is not caught, so an invalid payload produces an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 with a useful message. Likewise `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on a wrong key or non-JSON payload. Wrap in `safeParse`/try-catch and reject non-POST requests with 405.

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==`
body: The shared secret header is compared using plain string inequality, which is susceptible to timing side channels. Also, if the configured header appears multiple times `req.headers[...]` is a `string[]` and the comparison always fails. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers and normalize the header to a single string.

title: No tests for the new sync helpers or webhook despite cross-cutting changes to 11 integrations
body: The PR introduces shared logic (`parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens`, the `/api/webhook/app-credential` endpoint) that is now in the token-refresh path for Google, Office365, Zoom, Webex, HubSpot, Lark, Zoho CRM, Zoho Bigin, MS Teams and Salesforce, and the author notes no tests were added or run. Several of the defects above (computed-key schema, SafeParse wrapper being persisted, Response vs. object shape mismatches, missing prisma import) would be caught by even minimal unit tests of the helpers with sync enabled/disabled and a type-check run.

title: Cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in the UI
body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop (which the installed-calendars page does not pass). Unlike `disconnectMutation`, it never calls `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. After the user confirms deletion, the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated" and the "Delete cached data" item (derived from the now-stale `cacheUpdatedAt`) until a full refetch, so the action appears to have had no effect and can be re-triggered against an already-empty cache.

title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt, reporting expired cache as live
body: The `groupBy` only filters on `credentialId` and takes `_max(updatedAt)`. Rows whose `expiresAt` is in the past are still returned, so the UI will display a "Cache Status: Last updated …" for a credential whose cache is no longer served by `getCachedAvailability` (which does filter `expiresAt >= now`). The status shown to users is therefore misleading; the query should include `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` or report expiry explicitly.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId on selected calendars, but nothing consumes them
body: The `allSelectedCalendars`/`userLevelSelectedCalendars` picks were widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. Only `findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated to select those columns; any other caller that builds a `UserWithCalendars` (platform API v2, other repository paths selecting a subset of SelectedCalendar fields) will now fail type-checking or need extra data fetched. Nothing in this PR reads these fields (the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache), so this is an unnecessary contract tightening with breakage risk; it should be reverted or the fields made optional.

title: Extra updateMany on every cache refresh with no consumer
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now issues `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {})` on every webhook/cron refresh solely to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. The PR itself notes the frontend does not use this value (it uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`). This adds a write touching every SelectedCalendar row for the credential on each refresh, with no functional benefit. Also, the `data` parameter is typed as `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` (which includes relation fields) while `updateMany` accepts `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`; the types should match.

title: Authorization failure throws a plain Error, surfacing as a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
body: When the credential does not belong to the caller, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` instead of a `TRPCError` with code `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`. tRPC maps unknown errors to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, so clients cannot distinguish an authorization failure from a server fault and the message is swallowed in production. Use `TRPCError` as other handlers in this router tree do.

title: Cache timestamp is hard-coded to the en-US locale
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` is used regardless of the user's locale, so non-English users get US-formatted dates (e.g. 7/15/25) inside an otherwise translated string. The component already has `useLocale()` available; the user's locale (or `i18n.language`) should be passed to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.

title: sed -i '' is macOS-only and the .env path is relative to the working directory
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD sed syntax; on GNU sed (Linux) `-i ''` is parsed as an empty in-place suffix followed by `''` as the script, causing "unknown command" and leaving `.env` unmodified. Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` resolves relative to the caller's cwd rather than the script location, so running from the repo root writes to a `.env` outside the repository. Also `cleanup` always `exit 0`, so the failure paths (rate limit, no URL) report success to callers.

title: dev:cron uses npx tsx but tsx is not a declared dependency
body: The script was changed from `ts-node` (a declared devDependency) to `npx tsx`, but `tsx` is not added to devDependencies. `npx` will fall back to downloading an arbitrary latest version at runtime (and may prompt interactively), making the script non-reproducible and failing in offline/CI environments. Either add `tsx` to devDependencies or keep `ts-node`. This change is also unrelated to the PR's feature.

title: No tests for the new deleteCache handler or getCacheStatusByCredentialIds
body: The PR adds a destructive mutation (`deleteCacheHandler`) with an ownership check and a new repository aggregation (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`) but includes no unit or integration tests. In particular the authorization path (another user's credentialId must be rejected) and the mapping of credentialId → updatedAt in `connectedCalendarsHandler` are untested; the PR description itself notes end-to-end verification could not be performed.

title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars query, so stale cache status stays on screen
body: `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop (which maps to `onChanged` in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` and is undefined in most call sites). Unlike `disconnectMutation`, it does not call `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. After the user confirms deletion, the dropdown continues to show the old 'Last updated' timestamp and the 'Delete cached data' item until a full reload, making it look like the deletion failed. Add an `onSettled`/`onSuccess` that invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`.

title: Throws plain Error instead of TRPCError, surfacing as 500
body: When the credential does not belong to the user (or does not exist) the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps non-TRPCError exceptions to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, so an authorization failure is reported to clients (and to Sentry) as a server crash rather than a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN response. Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or FORBIDDEN) consistent with other handlers in this router.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId, breaking existing callers
body: The `UserWithCalendars` type (exported and re-used by platform libraries) was tightened so that `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` must include `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. Any caller that builds this object from a narrower Prisma select (only `externalId`, `integration`, `eventTypeId`) will now fail type-checking, and nothing in `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` actually reads these new fields. Only `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated in this PR. Either revert the type change (the fields are unused) or update all producers, including `@calcom/platform-libraries` consumers.

title: Unused bulk write to SelectedCalendar on every webhook/cache refresh
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now runs `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` after every cache refresh, i.e. on every Google webhook notification. It touches every SelectedCalendar row for the credential (including calendars not involved in the refresh and event-type-level rows) solely to bump `updatedAt`, but nothing in the frontend consumes `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` — the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`. This is an extra write per webhook with no consumer, and it overloads the semantics of `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. The PR description itself questions whether it should be removed; it should.

title: Cache timestamp hard-coded to en-US locale
body: The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, ignoring the user's locale, time format preference and timezone (`useLocale` already exposes the locale). Non-US users will see a US-style date/time in an otherwise localized UI.

title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only; script fails on Linux
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is the macOS syntax for in-place editing. GNU sed interprets `''` as the input filename and errors out, so the GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL update fails on Linux developer machines. Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory rather than the script location, so running it from the repo root creates a stray `.env` one directory up. Use a portable approach (e.g. a temp file + mv, or detect sed flavor) and derive the path from `$(dirname "$0")`.

title: dev:cron uses npx tsx but tsx is not a declared dependency
body: The script was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, yet `tsx` is not listed in dependencies or devDependencies (ts-node still is). `npx` will attempt a network download of the latest `tsx` at run time, which is non-reproducible and fails offline/in locked-down CI. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency or keep `ts-node`.

title: No tests for new deleteCache handler or getCacheStatusByCredentialIds
body: The PR adds a new authenticated mutation that deletes user data, a new repository aggregation (`groupBy` on `credentialId` with `_max.updatedAt`) and a modified `connectedCalendarsHandler` that merges cache status into the response, but adds no unit or integration tests. In particular, the ownership check (another user's credentialId must be rejected) and the credentialId→cacheUpdatedAt mapping are untested. The PR description also states end-to-end testing was not possible locally.

title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in UI
body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop; unlike `disconnectMutation` below it, it does not call `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. The `cacheUpdatedAt` value that drives the 'Cache Status' section and the 'Delete cached data' item comes from that query. When `onChanged` is not passed by the parent (it is optional in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`), the dropdown keeps showing the old 'Last updated' timestamp and a delete action for cache that no longer exists after a successful delete. Add an `onSettled`/`onSuccess` invalidation of `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`.

title: Extra updateMany on SelectedCalendar on every cache refresh with no consumer
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now runs `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` after every cache population (called from every Google webhook and from unwatch). The PR description itself admits `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not displayed anywhere; the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`. This adds a write touching every SelectedCalendar row for the credential on each webhook purely as a side effect, with no functional purpose, and bumps `updatedAt` on rows that did not semantically change. It also relies on Prisma applying `@updatedAt` with an empty `data` object, which is implicit behaviour. This should be removed.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId on selected calendars but nothing in this module uses them
body: `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` were widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, yet `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` and its helpers never read either field. This tightens the public contract of `getConnectedDestinationCalendars` (re-exported as a legacy export for `@calcom/platform-libraries` / API v2 consumers) and forces every caller that builds a `UserWithCalendars` from a narrower Prisma select to add these columns or fail type-checking. Only `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated here; other callers (platform API, tests) are at risk of breaking for no benefit. Revert the type change or justify the fields.

title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError, surfacing as 500 for not-found/forbidden credential
body: When the credential does not exist or belongs to another user the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps generic errors to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) and logs them as server failures, whereas this is a client-side condition. Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or `FORBIDDEN`) so the client gets a meaningful status and the error is not reported as a server bug.

title: CalendarCacheRepository instantiated directly, bypassing the calendar-cache feature flag
body: The handler does `new CalendarCacheRepository()` instead of going through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, which selects the mock repository when the `calendar-cache` feature is disabled. The newly added `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` mock exists precisely for that case but is never reachable from this path, so a DB `groupBy` query is executed on every connectedCalendars load even for deployments/teams where caching is off.

title: Script uses macOS-only `sed -i ''` and cwd-relative .env path
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax; on GNU sed (Linux) `''` is treated as the input file name and the command fails with "can't read : No such file". Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory rather than the script location, so running it from the repo root creates/edits a `.env` one directory above the repo. Use a portable in-place edit (e.g. write to a temp file) and derive the path from `$(dirname "$0")`.

title: Cache timestamp hard-coded to en-US locale, ignoring user locale/time format
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` is used to render the 'Last updated' timestamp even though the component already has `useLocale()`. Users with other locales or 24h time format preferences will see US-formatted dates/times inconsistent with the rest of the app. Use the user's locale (e.g. from `useLocale()` / `i18n.language`) or the existing dayjs helpers.

title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` but tsx is not a declared dependency
body: The script now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` while `tsx` is not listed in dependencies or devDependencies (only `ts-node` is). `npx` will attempt to download the latest `tsx` from the registry at runtime, which is non-reproducible, requires network access, and prompts interactively in some npm versions. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency or keep using the installed `ts-node`.

title: Unescaped URL interpolated into raw-HTML post footer enables stored XSS
body: TopicEmbed.import appends `#{url}` to the contents without any HTML escaping, and the resulting post is stored with cook_method raw_html, so cooked == raw with no sanitization. The `url` reaches this code from the user-controlled `embed_url` query parameter (EmbedController#best -> RetrieveTopic job -> TopicRetriever -> import_remote). TopicRetriever only checks that the URI host equals embeddable_host; the path may contain `'` (a legal URI character), so a value such as `http://host/x'onmouseover='alert(1)` injects an attribute into the anchor. If the embeddable host serves any 200 page for that path, the payload is stored in a public post authored by the embed_by user and executes for every forum visitor and in the embed iframe. The url (and the title) must be HTML-escaped before interpolation.

title: Imported HTML is stored and rendered completely unsanitized
body: Posts created by TopicEmbed.import use `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim for that method, bypassing PrettyText sanitization entirely. For the RSS path (Jobs::PollFeed) the content is `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` with no filtering at all, and for import_remote Readability's tag whitelist still allows `<a href>` with arbitrary schemes (e.g. javascript:). A compromised or malicious feed/source therefore yields stored script injection rendered to all users (best.html.erb outputs `raw post.cooked`). Imported HTML should be passed through the sanitizer (e.g. Sanitize/PrettyText whitelist) before being stored.

title: `i.content.scrub` raises for standard RSS items and on Ruby < 2.1
body: SimpleRSS exposes `content` only for Atom feeds; plain RSS 2.0 items expose `description` (and `content_encoded` for the content module), so `i.content` is nil for most RSS feeds and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole poll (retry: false). Additionally, `String#scrub` only exists from Ruby 2.1; on Ruby 2.0 (current at the time of this code) it raises NoMethodError even for Atom feeds. Fall back to `i.content_encoded || i.description` and guard the encoding cleanup.

title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
body: The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. The code then strips all leading slashes and prepends the prefix, producing `http://host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, which is a broken link/image. Protocol-relative URLs are common in feed content and Readability output. Use `URI.join(url, href)` or skip hrefs beginning with `//`.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match instead of equality
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl. For `discourseUrl = "http://discourse.example.com/"` an attacker page at `http://discourse.example.co` (a prefix) passes the check. The impact is limited to controlling the iframe height, but the check should compare the parsed origin of discourseUrl for equality with e.origin.

title: open-uri fetch of user-influenced URL follows redirects with no timeout (SSRF)
body: `open(url).read` uses Kernel#open/open-uri on a URL derived from the `embed_url` request parameter. Only the host is validated; open-uri transparently follows HTTP redirects, so the embeddable host (or anyone who can place a redirect on it) can make the Sidekiq worker fetch arbitrary internal URLs. There is also no read/open timeout or size limit, so a slow or huge response ties up the worker. Use an HTTP client with redirect disabled or re-validated, timeouts, and a response size cap.

title: Every cache-miss embed request runs a full synchronous feed poll
body: perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when feed polling is enabled. This downloads and imports the entire RSS feed (creating/revising posts for every item) on each embed request whose URL has no TopicEmbed yet. The 60 s throttle is per embed_url and is bypassed for staff, so distinct URLs (or a staff member) can trigger repeated full feed imports on the worker and heavy writes to the database.

title: setnx followed by separate expire can leave a permanent throttle key
body: The throttle does `$redis.setnx(key)` and then `$redis.expire(key, 60)` as two separate commands. If the worker dies or redis errors between them, the key is created without a TTL and that embed_url is throttled forever for non-staff users (the topic never gets retrieved). Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (or setex-style atomic operation).

title: Concurrent imports of the same URL hit the unique index after creating a topic
body: import checks `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and later `TopicEmbed.create!`. The hourly PollFeed job and a RetrieveTopic job (which itself invokes PollFeed) can import the same URL concurrently; the second one creates a topic and post, then `create!` raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique on the unique embed_url index, rolling back the transaction and propagating an exception that aborts the rest of the feed import. Rescue RecordNotUnique and fall back to the update path.

title: Rails 3 lockfile not updated for new gems
body: ruby-readability and simple-rss are added to Gemfile and to Gemfile_rails4.lock, but the Rails 3 lockfile (Gemfile.lock, used when RAILS3 is set) is not updated. In deployment/frozen mode Bundler will refuse to boot in Rails 3 mode until the lockfile is regenerated, and the gems will be missing at runtime for `require 'simple-rss'` / `require 'ruby-readability'`.

title: Already-committed migration modified to add force: true
body: An existing migration is edited to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. Editing a migration that has already been applied elsewhere is unsafe: anyone who re-runs it (e.g. via `db:migrate:redo` or a fresh schema rebuild from migrations) will have the existing top_topics table silently dropped along with its data. The same `force: true` is used in the new topic_embeds migration; a new migration should not need it.

title: Stray `end if` in ERB only compiles by accident
body: `<%- end if %>` emits the Ruby `end if` with no condition; it only parses because ERB appends the next template text as `@output_buffer.safe_append=...` on the following line, which becomes the modifier-if condition. Any reformatting (e.g. putting another `<% %>` tag directly after, or a different ERB handler) turns this into a SyntaxError and the embed page will 500. It should be `<%- end %>`.

title: Loading page reloads forever and re-enqueues a job on every reload
body: The loading view reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely. Each reload hits EmbedController#best, which, while no TopicEmbed exists, enqueues another RetrieveTopic job. If retrieval permanently fails (invalid host, 404, user not configured), every open embed on the page will keep polling and enqueuing Sidekiq jobs with no backoff or stop condition.

title: Unescaped URL interpolated into raw-HTML post (stored XSS)
body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to the contents without any HTML escaping, and the resulting post is stored with `cook_method = raw_html`, so `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim and it is rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and as `cooked` on the main site. The `url` comes from the user-controlled `embed_url` query parameter (via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` -> `import_remote`); only the host is validated, the path is attacker-controlled and URI parsing permits `'`. A URL such as `http:///x'onmouseover='alert(1)` breaks out of the href attribute and Nokogiri's `absolutize_urls` round-trip preserves the injected attribute. Escape `url` (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape`) or build the anchor with Nokogiri.

title: Any unauthenticated visitor can create unlimited topics by varying embed_url
body: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `RetrieveTopic` for any `embed_url` that has no existing `TopicEmbed`. `TopicRetriever` only checks that the URL's host equals `embeddable_host` and throttles per exact URL (60s). An attacker who can set the Referer (or simply a visitor of the embedding site) can request `embed/best?embed_url=http://host/page?x=1`, `?x=2`, ... each of which passes the host check, triggers an outbound HTTP fetch of the page (plus a full RSS poll if enabled), and creates a brand new topic and post as `embed_by_username` because `import_remote` imports whatever 200 response comes back. This allows unbounded topic spam and outbound request amplification from unauthenticated requests. The URL should be normalized (strip query/fragment) and ideally only created when it appears in the feed or a per-host rate limit should be applied.

title: import_remote relies on open-uri being loaded elsewhere
body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` on an http URL but `topic_embed.rb` never requires `open-uri`; the only `require 'open-uri'` is in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`. When autoloading (development, or any process where `Jobs::PollFeed` has not been referenced, e.g. `feed_polling_enabled` is false so `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` never touches it), `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a filename and raises `Errno::ENOENT`, so embeds are never retrieved. Add `require 'open-uri'` in `topic_embed.rb` (and preferably use an explicit HTTP client rather than `Kernel#open`, which also executes shell commands for strings beginning with `|`).

title: `i.content.scrub` fails on RSS items and on Ruby < 2.1
body: SimpleRSS items only populate `content` for Atom feeds (RSS 2.0 items use `description`), so `i.content` is frequently `nil` and `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the whole poll (the job also has `retry: false`). Additionally `String#scrub` was added in Ruby 2.1; on the Ruby 2.0 this codebase targets it does not exist. Use `i.content || i.description` with a nil guard and avoid `scrub` or add a fallback. There is also no per-item rescue, so one bad item prevents importing all others.

title: `<%- end if %>` is a malformed ERB block terminator
body: The header `if/else` block is closed with `<%- end if %>`. Ruby treats the trailing `if` as a statement modifier and, because a newline after `if` is permitted, consumes the next generated buffer-append statement as its condition. The template only works by accident (the append expression is truthy) and any change to the following markup can turn this into a syntax error or silently skip the `end`. It should be `<%- end %>`.

title: Success spec mocks TopicView.new with a nil return, so the best template cannot render
body: `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` has no `returns`, so `@topic_view` is nil and `best.html.erb` calls `@topic_view.posts` on nil. The `after` hook asserts `response.should be_success`, so either this spec fails or the view is not actually being exercised. Return a stubbed topic view (with `posts` and `topic`) so the template, including the `end if` block and the header/footer branches, is genuinely rendered and verified.

title: Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten to wrong absolute URLs
body: `absolutize_urls` treats every href/src starting with `/` as site-relative and strips all leading slashes, so a protocol-relative URL like `//cdn.example.com/img.png` becomes `http://<host>/cdn.example.com/img.png`, breaking images and links. Check for `start_with?('//')` and prefix only the scheme (or leave such URLs alone).

title: setnx/expire throttle is not atomic; key can become permanent
body: `retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx` and then a separate `$redis.expire`. If the process dies or the connection drops between the two calls, the `retrieved:<url>` key is left with no TTL and that URL is permanently throttled for non-staff users, so the embed never loads. Use a single atomic `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (or a MULTI block).

title: Failed PostCreator result treated as success
body: `PostCreator#create` returns the `Post` object even when creation was rolled back (e.g. host-spam detection), in which case the post is unsaved with errors. `post.present?` is true for such an object, so `TopicEmbed.create!` is attempted with `post_id: nil`/`topic_id: nil` and raises `ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid`, and `import` returns an unsaved post to callers. Check `post.errors.blank? && post.persisted?` instead.

title: Origin check uses substring match
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`, e.g. an origin `http://forum.example.co` passes when `discourseUrl` is `http://forum.example.com/`. Impact is limited to iframe height manipulation, but the check should compare `e.origin` with the exact origin derived from `discourseUrl`.

title: Unescaped URL interpolated into raw-HTML post enables stored XSS
body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to `contents` without any HTML/attribute escaping, and the resulting post is created with `cook_method: raw_html`, so `Post#cook` returns it verbatim and `best.html.erb` renders it with `raw`. The URL reaches this code from the anonymous `embed_url` request parameter (EmbedController -> RetrieveTopic job -> TopicRetriever -> import_remote); TopicRetriever only validates the host, and `URI()` accepts `'` in paths, so a URL like `http:///x'onmouseover='alert(1)` produces `` stored in a public topic. Escape the URL (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape`) or build the anchor with a helper.

title: Kernel#open on remote URL relies on open-uri being loaded and follows redirects to arbitrary hosts
body: `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` but `topic_embed.rb` never requires `open-uri` (only `poll_feed.rb` does). If the RetrieveTopic job runs in a process where open-uri hasn't been loaded by something else, `open` is `Kernel#open` on a filename and raises `Errno::ENOENT` for `http://...`. Additionally, even with open-uri, redirects from the (host-validated) embeddable host are followed to any destination, so a redirect to an internal address lets an anonymous user make the server fetch internal resources and publish the readability-extracted content as a topic. Use an explicit HTTP client with redirect control and require it explicitly.

title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
body: `href.start_with?('/')` is also true for protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png`, and `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, producing `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.png`. Links and images in imported feed content that use `//host/...` form will be rewritten to broken URLs. Check `start_with?('/') && !start_with?('//')` (or use `URI.join`).

title: poll_feed crashes on items without content
body: `i.content.scrub` is called unconditionally. Plain RSS 2.0 items commonly have `description` but no `content` (SimpleRSS returns nil for missing fields), and Atom entries may omit it too, so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError and aborts the entire poll (with `retry: false`), meaning no items from that feed are ever imported. Fall back to `i.description`/`i.summary` and guard nil. The unused `feed_key` method also suggests intended conditional-fetch logic that was never wired up.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`; e.g. for `discourseUrl = "http://forum.example.com/"`, an origin of `http://forum.example.co` or `http://f` (any prefix) passes. Any page able to post messages to the host window can then set the iframe height arbitrarily. Compare the origin exactly against the parsed origin of `discourseUrl`.

title: Already-committed migration changed to force: true
body: An existing migration was edited to add `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics`. Editing a migration that may already have been applied in deployments has no effect there, while `force: true` silently drops any pre-existing `top_topics` table (and its data) on environments where the migration runs after the table exists. The same pattern is used for the new `topic_embeds` table. Prefer a new migration or drop the `force` flag.

title: Test description says 404 but missing embed_url yields 400 and test only asserts non-success
body: `params.require(:embed_url)` raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing`, which is rendered as 400, not 404 as the spec title claims. The assertion `response.should_not be_success` would also pass if the action raised any unrelated error (e.g. the referer check failing first), so it does not verify the intended behavior. Assert the specific status.

title: Stray `end if` in ERB only works by accident
body: `<%- end if %>` compiles to Ruby `end if` followed by a newline, making the next generated output statement the condition of a modifier-`if` applied to the whole header block. It happens to parse and evaluate truthy, but it is a latent syntax trap (any change to the following line can break the template). Should be `<%- end %>`.

title: `float: right` on .small-action button is ignored once .small-action becomes a flex container
body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex` (via `@include flexbox()`), which makes `.topic-avatar`, `.small-action-desc` and `button` flex items. Per the flexbox spec, `float` has no effect on flex items, so the `button { float: right; }` rule at line 309 no longer pushes the action button to the right edge. The button will now sit immediately after the description text instead of being right-aligned, which is a visible layout regression for small-action posts (e.g. closed/pinned/moved notices with controls). To keep the previous placement the button needs `margin-left: auto` (or `.small-action-desc` needs `flex: 1`).

title: order() mixin passes the same value to -webkit-box-ordinal-group, which is 1-based unlike `order`
body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` (legacy 2009 flexbox) defaults to 1 and is 1-based, while the standard `order` property defaults to 0. Passing the same `$val` to both means that in legacy-WebKit browsers an item with `order(2)` is given ordinal-group 2 while untouched siblings are at ordinal-group 1, whereas in modern browsers the untouched siblings are at 0. This happens to work for the current usages (2 and 3 are both > default) but the mixin is not a faithful polyfill; a caller using `order(1)` to move an element after its siblings would get no effect in legacy WebKit. Either document the limitation or emit `$val + 1` for the ordinal-group property.

title: align-items() mixin does not translate values for legacy -webkit-box-align / -ms-flex-align, and emits a non-existent -ms-align-items
body: The legacy properties `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` use `start`/`end` rather than `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so forwarding `$alignment` unchanged produces invalid declarations for those values (only `center`, `baseline` and `stretch` coincide). `-ms-align-items` is not a property any IE version ever supported and is dead output. Current call sites only use `center` and `baseline`, so nothing breaks today, but the mixin silently fails for other arguments; it should map the values or restrict accepted inputs.

title: PR title claims a performance optimization but the change is a float-to-flexbox layout rewrite
body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" and its description is just "Test 5". Nothing in the diff is a performance change: it replaces `float: left/right` on `.title`/`.panel` with a flex container on `.d-header .contents`, reorders `.extra-info-wrapper` via `order(2)`, removes the `.badge-wrapper.bullet` top margin in the header, and restyles `.small-action` spacing. These are user-visible layout changes with browser-support implications (flexbox requires IE10+), and reviewers/theme authors relying on the title will be misled. The title and description should accurately describe the layout change and any intended visual differences.

title: float: right on .small-action button is ignored once .small-action becomes a flex container
body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex`, which makes its direct children flex items. The CSS spec says `float` has no effect on flex items, so `button { float: right; }` (and `.topic-avatar { float: left; }`) no longer does anything. The action button (edit/delete on small-action posts) will now sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of being pushed to the right edge, a visible layout regression. To keep the previous placement the button needs `margin-left: auto` (as was done for `.panel` in header.scss), and the dead `float` declarations should be removed.

title: margin-left: auto does not right-align in legacy -webkit-box / -moz-box flex implementations
body: `.panel` was changed from `float: right` to `margin-left: auto` to push it to the right of the flex row. The `flexbox()` mixin deliberately emits `display: -webkit-box` / `display: -moz-box` for old engines (Android stock browser ≤4.3, Safari ≤6, Firefox ≤21), but those 2009-syntax implementations do not honour `margin: auto` on box children. In exactly the browsers the mixin is trying to support, the header panel (search/hamburger/user icons) will now sit immediately after the title instead of at the right edge, whereas the old `float: right` worked everywhere. Either accept that and drop the legacy prefixes, or add a flexible spacer / `-webkit-box-flex` on the title.

title: align-items mixin emits non-existent -ms-align-items and relies on value names that differ in legacy specs
body: `-ms-align-items` is not a property any version of IE ever implemented (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, IE11 uses unprefixed `align-items`), so that line is dead output. Additionally the legacy `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` properties use `start`/`end` rather than `flex-start`/`flex-end`; the mixin passes `$alignment` through unchanged, so any future call with `flex-start`/`flex-end` will silently produce invalid declarations for those engines. Current call sites only use `center` and `baseline`, which happen to be shared, but the mixin as written is misleading.

title: order mixin maps 0-based `order` directly onto 1-based -webkit-box-ordinal-group
body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` (2009 flexbox) is 1-based with a default of 1, while standard `order` is 0-based with a default of 0. Passing the same value to both means an element given `order(1)` would be placed at the same position as un-ordered siblings in legacy WebKit rather than after them. Current usages (2 and 3) happen to preserve relative ordering, but the mixin will produce inconsistent results across engines for other values; either offset the legacy value by 1 or drop the legacy prefix.

title: PR title/description do not describe the change; .valign-helper left as a now-meaningless flex item
body: The PR is titled as a header performance optimisation and the description is just "Test 5", but the change is actually a layout rewrite from floats to flexbox across header, topic, small-action posts and badges with visible behavioural differences. Reviewers and future readers of history cannot tell what was intended. Related leftover: `.valign-helper` (inline-block, height 100%, vertical-align middle) existed solely to vertically centre floated siblings; with `.contents` now using `align-items: center` it becomes an empty flex item and should be removed along with the markup that renders it.

title: `.small-action` becomes a flex container but its children still rely on floats
body: `.small-action` now gets `display: flex` (line 264), but `.topic-avatar` keeps `float: left`, `.small-action-desc .avatar` keeps `float: left`, and `button` keeps `float: right` (line 309). Floats have no effect on flex items, so the action button that was previously pushed to the right edge of the row will now sit directly after the description text, and the `clear: both` on the container is dead. To keep the previous visual result the button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the description needs `flex: 1`), and the float declarations should be removed since they are now misleading. As written this is a visible layout regression in every small-action row in topics.

title: Float fallbacks removed; header layout has no fallback in browsers without flexbox
body: The `.title { float: left }` and `.panel { float: right }` rules were deleted and replaced solely with flexbox (`@include flexbox()` on `.contents`, `margin-left: auto` + `order(3)` on `.panel`). In any browser that supports none of the prefixed/unprefixed flex display values (e.g. IE9, older Android stock browsers), the title and panel will now stack as block elements with the panel below the logo, instead of degrading to the old floated layout. If those browsers are still in the support matrix, keep the float declarations as a fallback (they are harmlessly ignored inside a flex container).

title: `-ms-align-items` is not a real property
body: The `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment`.
