Because `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, in sharing mode `refreshTokenResponse.data` is `{ access_token }` only: expiry fields are discarded (so Office365's `expires_in` and Zoom's `expires_in` are undefined → `isExpired` stays true and tokens are refreshed on every single API call; Zoom computes `expiry_date = NaN` on line 122 of its adapter and the stored key then fails `zoomTokenSchema.parse` on the next load). A permissive schema needs `.passthrough()`/`z.record` or explicit optional fields; this one needs a unit test.

title: Placeholder `refresh_token: "refresh_token"` overwrites real refresh tokens when spread into stored credentials
body: When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the helper mutates `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. In `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` line 264 the data is spread over the existing credentials (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`), so whenever Microsoft (or the self-hoster's sync endpoint, which per the comments 'should only contain the access token and expiry date') omits a refresh token, the user's real refresh token in the database is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token". Previously, with `refresh_token` optional and absent, the spread left the stored value intact. After this, any later refresh against Microsoft fails permanently and the user must reconnect. The helper should not inject a fake refresh token; callers should preserve the existing one when none is returned.

title: Sync-endpoint branch returns a raw fetch `Response`, but Google/HubSpot/Zoho callers expect SDK-specific shapes
body: When `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set the helper returns the `fetch` `Response` object, whereas the fallback returns whatever `refreshFunction` returns. Callers are written against the fallback shape: Google Calendar does `res?.data.access_token` (googleapis `GaxiosResponse`) → `data` is undefined → TypeError, swallowed by the catch and the expired token is kept; HubSpot treats the return as a `HubspotToken` → `expiresIn`/`accessToken` undefined, `setAccessToken(undefined)`, and the `Response` object (with `expiryDate: NaN`) is written to `credential.key`, corrupting the credential; Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `tokenInfo.data.error` (axios shape) → TypeError. So four of the nine integrations this PR wires up do not work in sharing mode. The helper should normalise the sync response (e.g. `await response.json()`) and each caller must handle that shape explicitly.

title: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by app directory name, not slug, so lookups fail for most apps
body: `appStoreMetadata` (from `apps.metadata.generated.ts`) is keyed by the app's directory name (`googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`, `office365calendar`, `office365video`, `larkcalendar`, ...), not by its slug (`google-calendar`, `zoom`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `lark-calendar`). Indexing it with `app.slug` therefore returns `undefined` for exactly the apps this PR targets, and the webhook responds 404 "App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug" even though the slug is correct. Only apps whose dirName equals their slug (hubspot, salesforce, zohocrm, zoho-bigin) would work. Use `getAppFromSlug()` from `@calcom/app-store/utils`, or select `dirName` from the `App` row and index with that.

title: Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId` where `refreshOAuthTokens` expects the user id
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFn, appSlug, userId)` sends `calcomUserId: userId` to the self-hoster's sync endpoint and uses `userId` being non-null to decide whether the credential belongs to a user. Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId` as that third argument (every other integration passes `credential.userId`). Consequences: the sync endpoint is asked for tokens for the wrong user (a credential id that happens to match some other user's id), and team credentials (userId null) are also routed to the sync endpoint because credentialId is always a number. Pass `credential.userId` instead.

title: Zoom sends `appSlug: "zoomvideo"` to the sync endpoint while the app's slug is `"zoom"`
body: Every other integration passes its real slug (`google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `hubspot`, ...) as the `appSlug` argument to `refreshOAuthTokens`, and the inbound `/api/webhook/app-credential` endpoint also identifies apps by slug. Zoom passes its directory name `"zoomvideo"`. A self-hoster keying their endpoint on the slug they used when pushing credentials (`zoom`) will not recognise `zoomvideo`, so Zoom token refresh via the sync endpoint fails. Use `"zoom"`.

title: Request to the credential sync endpoint carries no authentication
body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` only sends `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body, with no shared secret, signature or bearer token. The endpoint must therefore hand out live OAuth access tokens for any user id to any caller that can reach it, since the self-hoster has no way to verify the request originated from Cal.com. A `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` / `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` pair already exists for the inbound direction; the same header should be sent on this outbound request (and `response.ok` should be checked) so the self-hoster can authenticate it.

title: Salesforce now hits the token endpoint on every instantiation, and the refreshed token is not even used
body: `getClient` (called from the constructor for every booking/update/delete) now unconditionally POSTs to `login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and writes the result to the database, regardless of whether the stored token is still valid; previously jsforce refreshed lazily. The new `jsforce.Connection` on line 101-108 is still constructed with the old `credentialKey.access_token`/`instance_url`, so the freshly obtained token is stored but never used by this request. Additionally, this path bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce does not participate in credential sharing at all, and the check `response.statusText !== "OK"` on line 86 is fragile (statusText is not guaranteed; use `response.ok`). The `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` branch on line 92 is dead because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure.

title: Webhook secret compared with `!==` (not constant-time)
body: The shared secret from the request header is compared to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` with a plain string inequality, which short-circuits on the first differing byte and leaks timing information about the secret to an attacker who can make repeated requests. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers (as the Stripe/other webhook handlers in the repo do).

title: No method check and unhandled parse/decrypt errors return 500s
body: The handler accepts any HTTP method; a GET has no body so `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(undefined)` throws a ZodError that propagates as an unhandled 500. Likewise `symmetricDecrypt` (line 58) throws on a wrong key length or tampered ciphertext and `JSON.parse` throws on non-JSON plaintext, all surfacing as 500 with a stack trace instead of a 400. Reject non-POST with 405, use `safeParse`, and wrap decryption in a try/catch returning 400.

title: Updating an existing credential does not clear the `invalid` flag
body: When the self-hoster pushes fresh keys for a credential that Cal.com previously marked `invalid: true` (e.g. after an `invalid_grant` from Google or Zoom), the update only sets `key`. The credential stays flagged invalid, so the UI keeps showing it as broken and some code paths skip it, even though the synced keys are now good. The update should also set `invalid: false`.

title: No tests for the new shared token-parsing/refresh helpers or the webhook endpoint
body: The PR introduces a shared parser that is now in the refresh path of Google Calendar, Office 365, Zoom and Salesforce, plus a new credential-ingest webhook, with no unit or integration tests (the description acknowledges this). Trivial tests would have caught that the 'minimum' schema strips every field but `access_token`, that the helper returns the SafeParse wrapper rather than the data (corrupting Google credentials), and that the webhook's `appStoreMetadata[slug]` lookup returns undefined for `google-calendar`. Please add tests for `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (both modes), `refreshOAuthTokens` return shape, and the webhook's happy/unhappy paths before merging.

title: Google credential key is overwritten with the zod SafeParse wrapper object on every token refresh
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns the result of `schema.safeParse(...)`, i.e. an object of the form `{ success: true, data: {...} }`, not the parsed credentials themselves. In `refreshAccessToken` the return value is assigned to `key` and written straight to the DB with `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. The previous code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` which returned the plain credential object. After this change every Google Calendar access-token refresh (roughly hourly, regardless of whether credential syncing is enabled) persists `{success: true, data: {access_token, refresh_token, ...}}` as the credential key. The next time the service is constructed, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails because `access_token`/`refresh_token` are no longer top-level fields, so the Google Calendar integration becomes permanently broken for that user until they reconnect. The other call sites (Office365, Zoom, Salesforce) correctly use `.data`; this one must too.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported in the Salesforce CalendarService
body: The new code in `getClient` calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` (the import list contains only jsforce, rrule, zod, CalEventParser, constants, http-error, logger, types, getAppKeysFromSlug and parseRefreshTokenResponse). This is a TypeScript compile error (`Cannot find name 'prisma'`) and, if it slipped through, a `ReferenceError` at runtime inside the constructor's promise, meaning every `SalesforceCalendarService` instantiation rejects and the Salesforce integration is completely non-functional.

title: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` computed keys evaluate to "[object Object]"; schema strips every field except access_token
body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are computed property keys. Calling `.toString()` on a Zod schema object returns the literal string `"[object Object]"`, so both lines define the same key (the second wins) and the schema is effectively `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() })`. There is no `.passthrough()`/`.catchall()`, so when credential sync is enabled every other field in the provider response (expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token, scope, token_type, instance_url, ...) is silently stripped. Consequences: Zoom computes `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` = NaN (serialised as null), after which `zoomTokenSchema.parse` fails and Zoom breaks; Office365 never updates `expires_in` so the token is treated as expired and re-fetched on every call; Salesforce loses `instance_url`. The comment "Assume that any property with a number is the expiry" describes behaviour that is not implemented. Use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` (and an explicit expiry field) instead.

title: Sync branch returns a fetch Response while the fallback returns provider-SDK objects; several apps crash or corrupt credentials in sync mode
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns `fetch(...)`'s `Response` when `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, but otherwise returns whatever the app-specific `refreshFunction` returns. Callers are written against the fallback shape, so with syncing enabled: Google (`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` line 94) reads `res?.data` which is undefined on a `Response`, throws `TypeError`, is swallowed by the catch and silently keeps the expired token; HubSpot (`hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts` line 177) treats the `Response` as a `HubspotToken`, computes `expiryDate = NaN`, stores the `Response` object as the credential key (serialised to roughly `{expiryDate:null}`) and calls `setAccessToken(undefined)`; Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `tokenInfo.data.error` on a `Response` and throw. Lark and Webex expect provider-specific envelopes (`{code, data:{refresh_expires_in,...}}`, literal `scope` string) that contradict the comment "The response should only contain the access token and expiry date". The `refreshFunction: () => any` signature hides all of this from the type checker. The sync branch needs to return a shape each caller can consume (or callers need to normalise), and the endpoint contract needs to be documented per app.

title: Zoho Bigin passes the credential id as the user id to the credential-sync endpoint
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(fn, appSlug, userId)` expects the Cal.com user id as its third argument, but `refreshAccessToken` passes `credentialId` (the `Credential.id`), because `biginAuth` only forwards `credential.id`/`credential.key` and not `credential.userId`. With credential sync enabled this posts `calcomUserId=<credentialId>` to the self-hoster's endpoint, so the tokens for an unrelated user (whoever has that numeric user id) are fetched and written into this credential — both a functional failure and a cross-user token leak. `credential.userId` must be threaded through to `refreshAccessToken`.

title: Webhook looks up `appStoreMetadata` by slug, but the map is keyed by app directory name
body: `appStoreMetadata` (from `apps.metadata.generated.ts`) is keyed by the app's directory name (`googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`, `office365calendar`, `office365video`, `larkcalendar`, ...), not by its slug (`google-calendar`, `zoom`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `lark-calendar`). Indexing it with `app.slug` only works for apps whose dir name happens to equal the slug (hubspot, salesforce, zohocrm, zoho-bigin, webex). For the main apps this PR targets the lookup returns undefined and the endpoint responds 404 "App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug" even though the slug is correct, so credentials can never be synced for them. Use `getAppFromSlug(slug)` from `@calcom/app-store/utils` (or search `Object.values(appStoreMetadata)` by `slug`) instead.

title: Zoom refresh uses app identifier "zoomvideo" while the app slug (and webhook) use "zoom"
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoomvideo", credential.userId)` sends `appSlug=zoomvideo` to the self-hoster's credential-sync endpoint, but the Zoom app's slug/appId everywhere else is `"zoom"` (see `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` `appId: "zoom"`, and the inbound webhook resolves apps via `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug } })`). A self-hoster keying their endpoint by the slug they push through the webhook will not recognise `zoomvideo`, so Zoom token refresh fails in sync mode. Every other call site passes the real slug (`google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `lark-calendar`, ...); this one should pass `"zoom"`.

title: Placeholder string "refresh_token" is injected into parsed token data and persisted, overwriting real refresh tokens
body: When the parsed response lacks `refresh_token`, the function mutates the data to `refresh_token: "refresh_token"`. This runs in both the sync and non-sync branches. In the non-sync Office365 path, `refreshTokenResponseSchema` marks `refresh_token` optional; if Microsoft omits it, the spread `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }` now replaces the stored, valid refresh token with the literal string, permanently breaking the credential (previously the spread left it untouched). In sync mode the literal is written to the DB for Zoom (`key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token`) and Office365, so if a self-hoster later disables syncing all those credentials are dead. Callers that need a placeholder should handle it themselves; the shared parser should not fabricate credential material.

title: Request to the credential-sync endpoint carries no authentication
body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` as a form body, with no shared-secret header, signature, or other authentication material. The endpoint is expected to return live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user ids, so the self-hoster has no way (short of network allow-listing) to verify the request originates from their Cal.com instance; anyone who can reach the endpoint can harvest every user's third-party tokens by enumerating ids. The PR already defines `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`/`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` for the inbound direction; the outbound request should at minimum send the same secret header so the endpoint can authenticate it.

title: Salesforce now hits the token endpoint on every service instantiation and ignores the refreshed token
body: `getClient` (called from the constructor) now unconditionally POSTs to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` with the stored refresh token on every `SalesforceCalendarService` construction (every booking, update, delete), with no expiry check. jsforce already refreshes lazily on 401, so this adds a network round-trip and Salesforce API quota usage to every operation. The refreshed `access_token` is then not even used: the `jsforce.Connection` at line 106 is built from `credentialKey.access_token` (the old value), so the extra call only updates the DB. Additionally the success check `response.statusText !== "OK"` is fragile (status text is empty over HTTP/2 and not guaranteed by fetch) — `response.ok` should be used — and this path bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce ignores credential-sync mode and will keep calling Salesforce with whatever refresh token is stored (possibly the "refresh_token" placeholder).

title: Invalid body or undecryptable payload produce unhandled exceptions (500) and decrypted keys are stored unvalidated
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a `ZodError` on a malformed body, and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on a wrong key, malformed ciphertext or non-JSON plaintext. None of these are caught (the handler is not wrapped in `defaultResponder`/try-catch), so the caller receives a generic 500 instead of a 400 with a useful message, and the self-hoster cannot distinguish a bad payload from a server fault. The decrypted `keys` value is also written to `credential.key` without any shape validation, so a sender bug (e.g. encrypting the wrong object) silently corrupts the user's credential and only surfaces later when the app's credential schema parse fails.

title: Webhook secret compared with `!==` rather than a constant-time comparison
body: The secret header is validated with a plain string inequality against `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. String comparison short-circuits on the first mismatching byte, which leaks timing information that can be used to recover the secret byte-by-byte on a network-reachable endpoint. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers (as other webhook handlers in the codebase do) and reject when lengths differ.

title: `findFirst` by userId+appId overwrites an arbitrary credential for apps that allow multiple installs
body: Several apps (e.g. Google Calendar) allow a user to hold multiple credentials for the same `appId`. The webhook selects `findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` with no ordering and updates whichever row comes back, so a sync for one connected account can clobber the keys of a different connected account of the same provider. There is also no uniqueness constraint, so two concurrent webhook calls for a new user/app pair can both take the `create` branch and produce duplicate credentials. The payload should identify the target credential (or the provider account) rather than relying on `findFirst`.

title: No tests for the new webhook endpoint or the shared OAuth refresh helpers
body: The PR adds a new authenticated API route that writes third-party credentials into the DB and two shared helpers (`refreshOAuthTokens`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) that now sit in the token-refresh path of nine integrations, but ships no unit or integration tests (the PR description explicitly states tests were not added or run). Several of the defects in this change — the `[object Object]` schema key, the SafeParse wrapper being stored as the Google credential key, the missing `prisma` import in Salesforce, and the dirName-vs-slug lookup — would have been caught by even a minimal test exercising the webhook with a known slug and a test asserting the shape written to `prisma.credential.update` after a refresh.

title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in UI
body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. Unlike the `disconnectMutation` right below it (which invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`), nothing invalidates the `connectedCalendars` query after the cache rows are deleted. The `cacheUpdatedAt` value that drives `hasCache` comes from that query, so unless the parent happens to pass an `onChanged` that refetches, the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated ..." and the "Delete cached data" entry for cache that no longer exists (and the query is configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, so it won't self-correct). Add `onSettled: () => utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` to the delete mutation, mirroring the disconnect mutation.

title: Authorization failure thrown as plain Error becomes a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
body: When the credential does not belong to the caller, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps non-`TRPCError` exceptions to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, so a legitimate not-found/forbidden case is reported to the client as a server failure and will be logged/alerted as an unexpected error. Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or `FORBIDDEN`). Additionally, the existence check uses `prisma.credential.findFirst` with no `select`, pulling the full row including the OAuth `key` blob just to test existence; `select: { id: true }` is sufficient.

title: Unused extra UPDATE of all SelectedCalendar rows on every cache refresh/webhook
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now ends with `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`, an UPDATE of every SelectedCalendar row for the credential solely to bump `@updatedAt`. This runs on every Google push notification (which can arrive in bursts) and on the unwatch path. The PR description itself states the resulting `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not consumed anywhere—the UI reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt` instead. This is dead write traffic that also makes `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` meaningless as a "record changed" signal. Remove it (along with the now-unneeded `updateManyByCredentialId` helper) or wire it to an actual consumer.

title: UserWithCalendars type tightened to require fields the function never uses
body: `UserWithCalendars.allSelectedCalendars` / `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` in addition to `externalId | integration | eventTypeId`, but nothing in `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` reads those fields. This forces every caller (tRPC session user, API v2 via `@calcom/platform-libraries`, tests constructing users) to supply them—hence the otherwise unrelated change to `findUnlockedUserForSession` in `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts` that now selects `googleChannelId` into the session user. Any external caller that builds a user object with the previous minimal shape will fail type-checking for no functional reason. Revert the type widening and the session select change.

title: Cache timestamp formatted with hard-coded en-US locale, ignoring user locale/timezone
body: The "Last updated" timestamp is rendered via `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, so non-English users see US date ordering (MM/DD/YY) and 12-hour time regardless of their configured locale, and the time is in the browser timezone rather than the user's profile timezone used elsewhere in the app. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (e.g. `i18n.language`) and/or the existing dayjs helpers with the user's timezone.

title: Backfill sets updatedAt of all existing cache rows to migration time, producing misleading 'Last updated' values
body: `ALTER TABLE "CalendarCache" ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" ... DEFAULT NOW()` stamps every pre-existing cache row with the moment the migration ran. The new UI surfaces this value as "Last updated: {{timestamp}}", so for all existing users the cache will appear freshly refreshed at deploy time even if it is weeks old. Since `expiresAt` is always written as `updatedAt + 30 days` by `upsertCachedAvailability`, a more accurate backfill is available: add `UPDATE "CalendarCache" SET "updatedAt" = "expiresAt" - INTERVAL '30 days';` after the ALTER. Also the retained Prisma warning comment ("without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty") is no longer accurate for this hand-edited SQL.

title: Dev script is macOS-only (`sed -i ''`) and writes .env relative to CWD, not the repo
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD sed syntax; on GNU sed (Linux CI/dev boxes) the empty string is taken as the script and the substitution expression as a filename, so the command fails with "can't read ...: No such file". Separately, `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory rather than the script location, so running `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root (the natural invocation) creates/edits a `.env` one level above the repository. Resolve paths from `$(dirname "$0")` and use a portable in-place edit. This file (and the `dev:cron` change in apps/web/package.json) is also unrelated to the cache-status feature and would be better split out.

title: dev:cron now relies on `npx tsx`, which is not a declared dependency
body: The `dev:cron` script was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not listed in `dependencies`/`devDependencies` (while `ts-node` still is). `npx` will fetch an arbitrary latest `tsx` at runtime, making the script non-reproducible and failing offline. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it directly, or keep `ts-node`. This change is also unrelated to the PR's feature.

title: No tests for the new deleteCache mutation, cache-status repository method, or dropdown rendering
body: The PR adds an authorization-sensitive destructive mutation (`deleteCacheHandler`), a new repository query (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` with `groupBy`/`_max`), enrichment logic in `connectedCalendarsHandler`, and a UI component that replaces the existing `DisconnectIntegration` trash button with an ellipsis dropdown, yet no unit, integration, or e2e tests are added or updated. At minimum there should be a test asserting a user cannot delete cache for a credential they don't own, a test that `cacheUpdatedAt` is attached to the right credential (and null when no rows exist), and a check that existing Playwright flows which previously clicked the direct disconnect button still pass with the new two-step dropdown interaction. The PR description notes end-to-end verification was not performed locally.

title: Cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in the UI
body: The `deleteCache` mutation's `onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop; unlike the `disconnectMutation` right below it, it never calls `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. The `cacheUpdatedAt` shown in the dropdown comes from that query, so after a successful deletion the menu keeps displaying "Cache Status / Last updated ..." and the "Delete cached data" item until some other action refetches. In usages where `onChanged` is not passed (or does not invalidate this query) the UI is simply wrong after the action. Invalidate `connectedCalendars` in `onSettled` as the disconnect path does.

title: Extra updateMany on every Google webhook writes to SelectedCalendar for no consumer
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` is invoked by the Google Calendar webhook handler on every push notification. The new `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` issues an additional UPDATE across all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential on each notification purely to bump `@updatedAt`. The PR description itself states this value is not used by the frontend (the UI reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt`), so this is a dead write on a hot path. It also repurposes `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` (configuration change time) to mean "cache refreshed", which will confuse anyone relying on that column's original semantics. Remove it or scope it to an actual consumer.

title: No tests for the new mutation, repository method, or handler enrichment
body: The PR adds a new authenticated mutation (`deleteCacheHandler` with an ownership check), a new repository query (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` using `groupBy`/`_max`), and changes the shape of `connectedCalendarsHandler`'s output (`cacheUpdatedAt`), but adds no unit or integration tests for any of them. The description notes local testing was not possible. At minimum the handler should have tests for: deleting cache for an owned credential, rejecting a credential owned by another user, and the connectedCalendars enrichment mapping (including credentials with no cache rows and negative/delegation credential ids).

title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired cache rows are reported as live cache
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows by `credentialId` and takes `MAX(updatedAt)` without filtering on `expiresAt >= now()`. Every read path (`getCachedAvailability`) treats rows past `expiresAt` as non-existent, so a credential whose only cache rows have expired will still show "Cache Status: Last updated ..." in the UI even though no cache is actually being served. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the `where` clause so the status reflects what the cache layer will actually use.

title: Timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded en-US locale and browser timezone
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale even though the component already calls `useLocale()`, and formats in the browser's timezone rather than the user's profile timezone/time format used elsewhere in the app. Non-English users will see an English-formatted date inside an otherwise translated menu, and users whose profile timezone differs from the browser will see a misleading time. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (or the existing dayjs/timeFormat helpers) instead.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId that nothing in the PR reads
body: `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` were changed from `Pick<SelectedCalendar, "externalId" | "integration" | "eventTypeId">` to also require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, and `findUnlockedUserForSession` was widened to select them. No code in this PR consumes these fields (the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`), so this tightens the public type contract of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` (also re-exported via `@calcom/platform-libraries` to API v2) and enlarges the session user payload for no benefit. Any caller that builds a `UserWithCalendars` from a narrower select will now fail to type-check. Revert unless a consumer is added.

title: Unexplained removal of `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` loses compile-time validation
body: `findMany` previously asserted `{ where, select, orderBy } satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs`, which guaranteed the hand-written `FindManyArgs` type stays compatible with Prisma's generated types. The PR removes this with no explanation and it is unrelated to the feature. Without it, drift between `FindManyArgs` and the Prisma schema will only surface as a runtime Prisma validation error instead of a type error.

title: Handler throws a plain Error (500) and fetches the full credential row including secrets
body: When the credential is not found or not owned by the user, the handler throws `new Error(...)`, which tRPC surfaces as `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` rather than `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`, so clients and logs cannot distinguish an authorization failure from a server fault. Additionally `prisma.credential.findFirst` has no `select`, so it loads the entire row including the encrypted OAuth `key` just to check existence. Use `TRPCError` with an appropriate code and `select: { id: true }`.

title: ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's CWD, not the script location
body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` assumes the script is executed from inside `scripts/`. Running it the natural way from the repo root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) makes it read/modify `<parent-of-repo>/.env`, and because the script `touch`es the file when missing it will silently create a `.env` outside the repository and never update the real one. Resolve the path from `$(dirname "$0")/../.env` instead.

title: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS-only and fails on GNU sed
body: `sed -i '' -E "s|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD form of in-place editing. With GNU sed (Linux, most CI/dev containers) the empty string is parsed as the sed script and the substitution expression is treated as a filename, producing "can't read s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=...: No such file" and leaving `.env` unchanged. Use a portable approach (e.g. write to a temp file and `mv`, or detect the platform).

title: Failure paths exit with status 0
body: `cleanup` always runs `exit 0`, and it is also used as the exit path for error conditions (rate limit hit, failed to extract tunnel URL). Callers or wrappers cannot detect that the script failed, and the `.env` may not have been updated even though the exit code says success. Error paths should exit non-zero.

title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` which is not a declared dependency
body: `dev:cron` was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not listed in `dependencies`/`devDependencies` (while `ts-node` remains). `npx` will fetch an arbitrary latest `tsx` from the registry at run time, making the script non-reproducible and requiring network access. This change is also unrelated to the PR. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it directly, or keep `ts-node`.

title: Migration header warning contradicts the actual statement
body: The generated warning says the column was added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the statement below explicitly adds `DEFAULT NOW()` (and the schema has `@default(now())`). The stale warning will mislead anyone auditing migrations into thinking this migration is unsafe on populated tables. Remove or correct the comment.

title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars, leaving stale cache status in the UI
body: The `deleteCache` mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. Unlike the `disconnectMutation` right below it (which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`), nothing refetches the connected calendars query after the cache rows are deleted. `cacheUpdatedAt` is derived server-side from `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, so after a successful delete the dropdown continues to show "Cache Status / Last updated …" and the "Delete cached data" item, and the user can "delete" again indefinitely. This is only masked when the parent happens to pass an `onChanged` that invalidates the query, which `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` does not guarantee (`onChanged` is optional and not passed from every call site, e.g. event-type settings). Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled`/`onSuccess` of `deleteCacheMutation`.

title: Authorization failure throws a plain Error, surfacing as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
body: When the credential does not exist or does not belong to the session user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps non-`TRPCError` exceptions to a 500 `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, so a client probing other users' credential IDs gets a server-error response (and the error is logged/reported as an unexpected failure) instead of a proper `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`. Other handlers in this router family use `TRPCError` with an explicit code; this one should too.

title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired (unusable) cache rows are reported as live cache
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows by `credentialId` and returns `max(updatedAt)` without filtering on `expiresAt`. `getCachedAvailability` in the same file only ever serves rows with `expiresAt >= now`, so rows that expired are never used for availability. The UI nevertheless shows "Cache Status – Last updated <date>" and offers "Delete cached data" for credentials whose only cache rows are expired, which misrepresents whether caching is actually in effect. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the `where` clause (or expose the expiry so the UI can distinguish).

title: Unneeded updateMany on every webhook touches all SelectedCalendar rows and can fail the webhook after cache was written
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now ends with `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`, an UPDATE of every `SelectedCalendar` row (user-level and all event-type-level rows) for the credential, solely to bump `updatedAt`. This runs on every Google push notification (hot path) and also from `unwatchCalendar`. Nothing in this PR reads `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` — the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt` — and the PR description itself notes it is unused. Besides the write amplification, the call is outside any try/catch: if it fails (e.g. lock contention) the webhook handler errors after the cache has already been upserted, causing Google to retry a webhook whose actual work succeeded. Remove the call or make it best-effort.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires unused updatedAt/googleChannelId fields on selected calendars
body: `UserWithCalendars.allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` are widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, which forced `findUnlockedUserForSession` in `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts` to select those columns into the session user. No code in this PR consumes either field (`connectedCalendarsHandler` derives `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache`, not from `SelectedCalendar`). The change tightens the input contract of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` for every caller (platform-libraries/API v2, tests that build user fixtures) and grows the per-request session payload with per-calendar channel IDs, for no functional benefit. Revert the type widening and the extra `select` fields.

title: Cache timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded en-US locale
body: The "Last updated" timestamp is rendered with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` while the surrounding strings come from `useLocale()`. Non-English users see an English date/time format (MM/DD/YY, 12-hour clock) embedded in a translated sentence, and the user's configured timezone is not considered. Use the active locale from `useLocale()` (e.g. `i18n.language`) and, ideally, the user's timezone as other date displays in the app do.

title: No tests for the new deleteCache authorization or the cache-status enrichment
body: The PR adds a destructive, user-facing mutation (`deleteCacheHandler`) whose only guard is a `credential.userId === user.id` lookup, a new repository method (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), and a change to `connectedCalendarsHandler`'s response shape (`cacheUpdatedAt`), but includes no unit or integration tests. In particular there is no test asserting that a user cannot delete another user's `CalendarCache` rows, that deletion scopes to the given `credentialId` only, or that `cacheUpdatedAt` is populated/null as expected. The PR description admits local testing was not possible. Add handler tests (e.g. with prismock as used elsewhere in `packages/trpc`) covering the deny path and the enrichment mapping.

title: Script uses macOS-only `sed -i ''` and a CWD-relative .env path
body: `sed -i '' -E "s|…|…|" "$ENV_FILE"` is BSD/macOS syntax; on GNU sed (Linux, CI, devcontainers) `''` is parsed as the sed script and the substitution expression is treated as a filename, so the command fails and `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never updated. Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` (line 5) is resolved relative to the caller's working directory rather than the script's location, so running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root creates/edits a `.env` outside the repository. Resolve the path from `$(dirname "$0")` and use a portable in-place edit (e.g. write to a temp file and `mv`).

title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` but tsx is not a declared dependency
body: `dev:cron` now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, yet `tsx` is not listed in `dependencies` or `devDependencies` (only `ts-node` is). `npx` will try to download an unpinned latest `tsx` at run time, requiring network access and yielding non-reproducible behavior across machines/CI. This change is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it directly, or keep the `ts-node` invocation.

title: Removed `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` check from findMany without justification
body: `findMany` previously built its args with `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs`, which guaranteed the hand-written `FindManyArgs` type (kept narrow to avoid an atoms build TS crash, per the comment above it) stays compatible with Prisma's real argument type. The PR drops that assertion and passes the object directly. Since the call still type-checks against Prisma, the removal is unnecessary, and it silently removes the guard that would catch future drift between `FindManyArgs` and Prisma's types. This is also unrelated to the feature.

title: Migration header warning contradicts the statement that follows
body: The auto-generated comment says the column is added "without a default value" and that this "is not possible if the table is not empty", but the actual statement adds `DEFAULT NOW()` precisely so existing rows are handled. The stale warning is misleading for anyone auditing migrations and should be removed or corrected.

title: Stored XSS: embed URL interpolated unescaped into imported post HTML
body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to the article contents with no HTML/attribute escaping, and the result is stored as a `raw_html` post (rendered verbatim via `raw post.cooked` and in the normal topic view). The `url` is attacker-controlled: an anonymous client can call `GET /embed/best?embed_url=http:///post.html?x='onmouseover='alert(1)` with a `Referer: http:///` header (trivially set by a non-browser client). `URI()` accepts `'`, `(`, `)` and `=` so `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` passes, the blog ignores the query string and returns 200, Readability extracts content, and the footer becomes `` which Nokogiri re-serialises as two attributes. The script then executes for every user viewing the topic or the embed iframe. The URL must be escaped with `ERB::Util.html_escape`/`h` when building the anchor (and ideally validated/normalised before use).

title: RSS feed content is stored and rendered as unsanitized raw HTML
body: `poll_feed` passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` straight into `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates a post with `cook_method: raw_html`; `Post#cook` (app/models/post.rb:133) then returns `raw` untouched, so nothing in the pipeline strips `<script>`, event handlers or `javascript:` hrefs. The HTTP path at least runs Readability with a tag whitelist, but the RSS path has no sanitization at all, so any script in the feed (including syndicated user content or a compromised feed) becomes persistent XSS on the forum and inside the embed iframe. Even the Readability whitelist allows `href`/`src` values without scheme checks. Imported HTML should be run through the existing sanitizer (e.g. `Sanitize`/`PrettyText` whitelist) before being stored.

title: Anonymous users can trigger unbounded topic creation for arbitrary URLs on the embeddable host
body: Any request to `/embed/best` with an `embed_url` whose host matches `embeddable_host` enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job that fetches the URL and creates a topic authored by `embed_by_username`. The only protections are a Referer header check (freely forgeable by non-browser clients) and a 60-second per-URL Redis throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`. Because `embed_url` is stored verbatim (no normalisation), an attacker can vary the query string (`?a=1`, `?a=2`, ...) to mint an unlimited number of distinct URLs that all resolve to a 200 on a static blog, each producing a new topic and an outbound HTTP fetch, with no global rate limit. Additionally, every miss runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously (lib/topic_retriever.rb:41), so each probe also re-fetches and re-imports the whole RSS feed. Consider normalising URLs (strip query/fragment), only importing URLs that appear in the feed or match a path whitelist, and adding a global rate limit.

title: Feed items without <content:encoded> crash the poller and abort all remaining items
body: `i.content` is only populated for Atom `<content>` or RSS `<content:encoded>`; a plain RSS 2.0 feed that uses `<description>` (the common case) yields `nil`, so `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`. Because the loop has no per-item error handling and the job is declared `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a single bad item (nil content, a link that fails `URI()` parsing in `absolutize_urls`, a `RecordNotUnique` race with the retrieve job, etc.) aborts the entire hourly import and all subsequent items are skipped. Fall back to `i.description`, and wrap each item in a rescue that logs and continues. Note also that `String#scrub` only exists in Ruby >= 2.1; if the project still supports 1.9.3/2.0 (the Gemfile still has 1.9-specific comments) this line raises `NoMethodError` everywhere.

title: `post.present?` is true even when PostCreator failed, leading to NOT NULL violation
body: `PostCreator#create` returns the `Post` object even when creation was rolled back (e.g. `rollback_if_host_spam_detected` fires for a non-basic-trust embed user whose article links the same host several times, or the save fails); the object is unsaved with `id == nil`. `post.present?` is true for any AR object, so `TopicEmbed.create!` is called with `post_id: nil` and `topic_id` of an uncommitted topic, hitting the `null: false` constraints and raising `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` instead of returning nil. Worse, PostCreator raises `ActiveRecord::Rollback` inside its own `Post.transaction`, which is nested (without `requires_new`) inside the `Topic.transaction` here, so that Rollback is silently swallowed and does not roll back the already-created Topic until the later exception does. Check `post.persisted?`/`post.errors.empty?` instead.

title: Rate limiter is not bypassed when importing multiple feed items
body: `skip_validations: true` only disables model validations; `RateLimiter::OnCreateRecord` hooks (`rate_limit` on `Post` and `Topic`) still run in `after_create` and raise `RateLimiter::LimitExceeded`. Unless `embed_by_username` is a staff account, importing more than one new topic within `rate_limit_create_topic` seconds (default 5) in the `poll_feed` loop, or more than `max_topics_per_day` (default 20) in a day, raises and aborts the job. The Disqus thor task explicitly calls `RateLimiter.disable` for exactly this reason, but `PollFeed`/`TopicRetriever` do not. Either disable the limiter around the import or document that the embed user must be staff.

title: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs
body: `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png` (very common in blog/RSS HTML), and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, producing `http://embeddable-host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, a broken link/image. The same applies to `img[src]` at line 70. Check `start_with?('//')` first and only prepend the scheme, or use `URI.join(url, href)` which handles relative, root-relative and protocol-relative references correctly.

title: Stray `if` after `end` makes the next ERB statement the modifier condition
body: `<%- end if %>` compiles to Ruby `end if` followed by a newline, which Ruby parses as a modifier-`if` whose condition is the next generated statement (`@output_buffer.safe_append='...'`). It only works by accident because the buffer append returns a truthy string; the whitespace is emitted before the header button, and any future change to the following line (e.g. inserting another `<% %>` tag) would silently change behaviour or become a syntax error. This is not caught by the controller spec because rspec-rails does not render views by default. It should be `<%- end %>`.

title: New top-level assets (embed.css, embed.js) are not registered for precompilation
body: The layout references `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` and third-party sites are expected to load `embed.js` directly from Discourse's asset host, but the PR adds no change to `config.assets.precompile` (config/application.rb is not in the diff). In Rails 4 production, assets outside the manifest/precompile list are not compiled and either 404 or raise an asset-filtered error, so the embed would render unstyled and the blog-side `embed.js` would be unavailable. `embed.css` and `embed.js` need to be added to the precompile list (unless they are already there).

title: "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" specs are vacuous; poll_feed itself is untested
body: These two examples do not stub `feed_polling_enabled?`, which defaults to `false`, so `poll_feed` is never reached regardless of the url/username settings; the tests would pass even if those guards were deleted. Each should stub the other two conditions to true and only the one under test to blank. In addition, `poll_feed` (the RSS parsing, `link`/`id` fallback, content unescaping, per-item import) has no coverage at all, which is how the nil `i.content` crash slipped through.

title: Spec title claims 404 but a missing required param yields 400; views never rendered
body: `params.require(:embed_url)` raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing`, which Rails maps to 400 Bad Request, not 404; the example only asserts `should_not be_success` so the title is misleading. More importantly none of the examples use `render_views`, so `best.html.erb` and `loading.html.erb` (including the `end if` typo and `@topic_view.topic.url`/`small_avatar_url` calls) are never executed by the suite.

title: Already-shipped migration modified to add `force: true`, which drops the existing table
body: `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` predates this PR and has already run on deployed databases; editing it to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` changes a committed migration and makes any re-run (e.g. `db:migrate:redo`, re-applying on a DB where the version row was lost) silently `DROP TABLE top_topics` and all its data. The new `create_topic_embeds` migration uses `force: true` too. If the intent is to work around a stale dev DB, that should be done locally rather than baked into migrations.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of the configured Discourse URL, e.g. `http://forum.example.co` or `http://f` would pass for `http://forum.example.com/`. The handler only sets the iframe height so impact is limited, but the check should compare the message origin against the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` for equality.

title: Disqus import now depends on a live HTTP fetch per thread; one failure aborts the whole import
body: The importer previously created the topic locally from the XML (`PostCreator` with the thread title, permalink and original `created_at`); it now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read`. Old Disqus thread links frequently 404 or redirect, and `OpenURI::HTTPError`/timeouts are not rescued, so a single dead link aborts the entire run (the `ensure` block then restores settings). The `--category` option was also removed and the original thread `created_at` is no longer preserved on the topic, both silent behaviour regressions for existing users of the task.

title: Only the Rails 4 lockfile was updated for the new gems
body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` were added to the Gemfile and `Gemfile_rails4.lock`, but the Rails 3 lockfile (`Gemfile.lock`, used when `RAILS3` is set per the dual-boot logic at the top of the Gemfile) is not part of the change. If that lockfile is tracked, a Rails 3 boot with `bundle install --deployment`/frozen will fail because the Gemfile no longer matches the lock.

title: Embed URL interpolated unescaped into stored raw HTML (stored XSS)
body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to the post contents without any HTML/attribute escaping, and the resulting post is created with `cook_method: raw_html`, so `cooked == raw` and Discourse's sanitizer never runs on it. The `url` reaches this code from the `embed_url` request parameter: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `retrieve_topic` for any string, and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only requires that `URI(url).host` equals `embeddable_host` — the path and query string are unrestricted, and `'`, `=`, `(`, `)` are all valid URI characters. A request such as `/embed/best?embed_url=http:///some-page?x='onmouseover='alert(1)` (with a forged Referer) causes the page to be fetched successfully (query ignored by the origin server) and imported; `absolutize_urls` then re-serializes the broken anchor via Nokogiri into ``, which is persisted and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in both the embed iframe and the normal topic page for every visitor. The URL must be escaped (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape`/`h`) in both the href attribute and the link text.

title: Anonymous requests can create unlimited topics and outbound fetches via distinct embed_url values
body: For any `embed_url` not yet known, `best` enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job that fetches the URL over HTTP and creates a new topic (as `embed_by_username`) via `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. The only protections are (a) the Referer host check in `ensure_embeddable`, which is trivially forged by any non-browser client, and (b) `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, whose Redis key is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` — i.e. per exact URL. Since `TopicEmbed` matches on the exact `embed_url` string, an attacker can request `http://<embeddable_host>/article?1`, `?2`, `?3`, ... and every variant passes the host check, triggers an outbound HTTP fetch (plus, when `feed_polling_enabled`, a synchronous download and processing of the whole RSS feed inside the job via `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`), and creates a brand new topic. This allows unbounded topic spam and request amplification against the embeddable host with no authentication. At minimum the embed URL should be normalized (strip query/fragment or canonicalize) and there should be a global/host-level rate limit on retrievals and topic creation, not just a per-URL one.

title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs (//host/path)
body: `absolutize_urls` treats every `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')` as site-relative and rewrites it to `"#{prefix}/#{value.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png` (very common in feeds and blog HTML) also starts with `/`, and the `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, producing `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.png` — a non-existent URL on the wrong host. All protocol-relative images and links in imported content will therefore be broken. The check should exclude values starting with `//` (or use `URI.join(url, value)` which handles all relative forms correctly).

title: poll_feed crashes on RSS 2.0 items because i.content is nil
body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. SimpleRSS only populates `item.content` for an actual `<content>` tag (Atom); RSS 2.0 feeds put the body in `description` or `content:encoded` (exposed as `item.content_encoded`), so `i.content` is `nil` and `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`. Because the job has `retry: false` and the exception is unrescued, the first such item aborts the whole poll and no items from the feed are imported, despite the setting being described as an "RSS/ATOM feed". There should be a fallback (`i.content || i.content_encoded || i.description`) and a nil guard. Note also that `String#scrub` only exists on Ruby >= 2.1; if the project still supports Ruby 2.0 this line fails on every item.

title: raw_html cook method bypasses the sanitizer entirely for imported content
body: With `cook_method == raw_html`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim, so nothing in Discourse's sanitization pipeline runs. In the RSS path (`Jobs::PollFeed`) the feed item HTML is passed to `TopicEmbed.import` with no filtering at all, so `<script>`, event handlers, `javascript:` links, etc. in the feed go straight into `cooked` and are rendered with `raw post.cooked`. In the HTTP path, `Readability::Document` is given a tag/attribute whitelist, but ruby-readability does not validate attribute values, so `href="javascript:..."` and `src` pointing anywhere survive. This makes every visitor's security depend on the full integrity of the embeddable host's page content and the feed (including any user-generated fragments on those pages). The imported HTML should still be run through the existing sanitizer (or a whitelist that validates URL schemes) before being stored as cooked.

title: `<%- end if %>` is a typo that only parses by accident
body: The closing tag of the header conditional is `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. Erubis emits this as `end if` followed by a newline and the next generated `@output_buffer.safe_append='...'` statement, so Ruby parses the whole if/else as a modifier-`if` whose condition is the whitespace-append call. It happens to work today (the append returns a truthy string), but the block body now executes after the following text is appended, and any change to the surrounding template (e.g. removing the blank line or following it with another `<% %>` statement) turns it into a SyntaxError. It should be `<%- end %>`. The controller specs do not render views, so this template is never exercised by tests.

title: Loading page reloads forever when retrieval can never succeed
body: The loading view reloads itself every 30 seconds unconditionally, and every reload hits `EmbedController#best`, which enqueues another `retrieve_topic` Sidekiq job. If the embed can never be resolved (e.g. `embed_by_username` is blank or points to a missing user, the embed URL host does not match, the remote page 404s, or the import keeps failing), `TopicRetriever` silently returns and the iframe polls indefinitely on every open tab of every blog page, generating a steady stream of requests and queued jobs with no error state ever shown. There should be a cap on retries/time or an error view, and the controller should not enqueue a job on every single poll.

title: X-Frame-Options set to non-standard value "ALLOWALL"
body: `ALLOWALL` is not a defined `X-Frame-Options` value (only `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`, `ALLOW-FROM` exist). Framing only works because browsers ignore an invalid header and fall back to allowing framing; this is undocumented behavior and some user agents/proxies log errors or treat unknown values differently. Since the goal is to permit framing by `embeddable_host`, the header should be removed (`response.headers.delete('X-Frame-Options')`) or set to `ALLOW-FROM <embeddable_host>` rather than relying on an invalid value being ignored.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`. Because `e.origin` has no trailing slash and `discourseUrl` is expected to end with one, an origin that is a prefix of the configured URL (e.g. `http://discourse.example.co` when `discourseUrl` is `http://discourse.example.com/`, or `http://disc`) passes the check. Any such page that can get itself framed or opened by the blog can then resize the comments iframe arbitrarily. Compare the origin exactly (parse `discourseUrl` and compare `protocol + '//' + host`).

title: Throttle key SETNX/EXPIRE is not atomic; key can become permanent
body: `retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx(key, "1")` and only then `$redis.expire(key, 60)`. If the worker dies or Redis connection drops between the two calls, the `retrieved:<url>` key is created with no TTL and never expires, so every subsequent non-staff retrieval for that URL is treated as throttled forever and the embed stays stuck on the loading page. Use a single atomic command (`SET key 1 NX EX 60`, or `setex` guarded by a Lua script) so the TTL is always attached.

title: import checks post.present? instead of post errors/persisted?
body: `PostCreator#create` returns the `@post` object even when saving failed (e.g. `rollback_if_host_spam_detected` for an untrusted `embed_by_username` user), with errors set and no `id`. `import` only checks `post.present?`, so it proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!(post_id: post.id, ...)` with `post_id = nil`, which violates the `null: false` constraint and raises a database error out of the job rather than a meaningful failure, and the method may return a post object that was never persisted to its caller (`import_remote`/disqus import then uses `post.topic_id`). Check `post.persisted?`/`post.errors.blank?` and return nil (or raise a descriptive error) when creation failed.

title: Controller specs assert only `should_not be_success` and never exercise key paths
body: The test named "is 404 without an embed_url" runs with the default blank `embeddable_host`, so the request is rejected by the `ensure_embeddable` before_filter (403) before `params.require(:embed_url)` is ever reached; the assertion `response.should_not be_success` passes for the wrong reason and does not check the status code. Similarly "raises an error with a missing host" and "raises an error with no referer" don't distinguish which rule fired. Because rspec controller specs do not render views, `best.html.erb` (including the `end if` typo and `@topic_view.topic.url` usage) and `loading.html.erb` are never rendered by any test. Assert specific status codes and add view-rendering (or request) specs for the success paths.

title: poll_feed body (feed parsing and import) has no test coverage
body: Every example stubs `poll_feed` itself; none exercise the actual parsing in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (SimpleRSS item handling, `i.link`/`i.id` fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, calling `TopicEmbed.import`). As a result the `nil.scrub` crash for RSS 2.0 feeds and the entity-unescaping behaviour are untested. A fixture Atom feed and an RSS 2.0 feed (with `description`/`content:encoded`) fed through `poll_feed` with `open` stubbed would catch these.

title: Disqus importer silently drops --category option and original thread dates
body: The `--category/-c` option was removed and topic creation now goes through `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which has no way to pass `category` or `created_at`. Existing users of the thor task passing `-c` will now get an unknown-option error, and all imported topics are created with the current time instead of `Date.parse(t[:created_at])` as before, losing the original thread chronology. Additionally `import_remote` calls `open(url)` before `import` validates the URL scheme, so a thread whose `link` is blank or non-HTTP raises (`Errno::ENOENT`/`OpenURI::HTTPError`) and aborts the whole import run instead of being skipped. These behavior changes are not mentioned in the PR.

title: Already-shipped migration modified to add force: true
body: `create_table :top_topics` in an existing, previously-committed migration was changed to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. `force: true` issues `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` before creating, so anyone who re-runs or rolls back/re-applies this migration (or has a `top_topics` table from a different source) will lose that table's data. Editing migrations that have already been released is also unrelated to this PR's purpose; if the intent is idempotent setup, that should be a new migration or handled in `db:reset`, not a retroactive edit.

title: Stored XSS: unescaped URL interpolated into raw_html post footer
body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to the article HTML without any escaping, and the resulting post is created with `cook_method: raw_html`, so `cooked == raw` and no sanitization ever runs. The `url` is attacker-influenced: `EmbedController#best` accepts an arbitrary `embed_url` query param, and `TopicRetriever` only checks that its host equals `embeddable_host` (path/query are unrestricted). A URL such as `http:///real-post.html?x='onmouseover='alert(1)'` is a valid URI, is fetched successfully (most servers ignore the query string), and produces `href='...?x='onmouseover='alert(1)''`, which Nokogiri re-serializes as a live `onmouseover` attribute. Since the Referer check can be satisfied with a forged header from curl, an unauthenticated attacker can create a topic (authored by the configured embed user, typically staff) containing arbitrary JavaScript that executes on the forum's origin. The URL must be HTML-attribute-escaped (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape`) and ideally the footer should be built with a sanitizer.

title: Unauthenticated callers can mass-create topics and jobs via arbitrary embed_url values
body: Every request to `/embed/best` whose `embed_url` has no existing `TopicEmbed` enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job. The only guard is a forgeable `Referer` host check, and the throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is keyed on the *exact* URL string (`"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`), with no normalization of query strings, fragments, trailing slashes or scheme. An attacker can therefore request `http://<embeddable_host>/post?x=1`, `?x=2`, ... and each one (a) enqueues a Sidekiq job, (b) synchronously re-fetches and re-imports the entire RSS feed inside that job (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`), (c) performs an outbound HTTP GET + Readability parse, and (d) creates a new topic/post as the embed user because most servers return 200 for unknown query strings. The result is unbounded forum spam from a privileged account, unbounded outbound requests to the embeddable host and feed, and queue growth (the `RetrieveTopic` job does not set `retry: false`, so each 404/network failure is retried ~25 times). Additionally the loading page reloads every 30s forever when retrieval can never succeed. URLs should be canonicalized (strip query/fragment, enforce http(s) scheme), throttled globally as well as per URL, and ideally only URLs present in the feed should be importable.

title: raw_html cook method lets any later editor store unsanitized HTML
body: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == raw_html`, and `before_save` recomputes `cooked = cook(raw, ...)` on every save. `cook_method` is persisted on the post, so any subsequent edit of an imported post through the normal `PostRevisor` path (e.g. a moderator editing it from the UI, or the embed account being compromised) stores whatever HTML/JS the editor types, bypassing the sanitizer and the `after_post_cook` plugin filter entirely. Moderators normally cannot post raw HTML; this gives them (and anyone who gains the embed user's credentials) a persistent XSS vector on the forum origin. Consider sanitizing raw_html output through the HTML whitelist, or resetting `cook_method` to regular when a post is edited by anyone other than the import pipeline.

title: `i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds, crashing the whole poll
body: `poll_feed` calls `i.content.scrub` on every item. SimpleRSS only populates `content` from an Atom `<content>` element; RSS 2.0 feeds expose the body as `description` or `content:encoded` (accessed as `content_encoded`), so `i.content` is `nil` and `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`. Because the loop is not protected, one such item aborts the entire hourly job (`retry: false`), so no items from a standard WordPress/Blogger-style RSS feed are ever imported. Fall back to `content_encoded`/`description` and skip items with no body.

title: Unconditional CGI.unescapeHTML turns entity-escaped text inside CDATA content into live HTML
body: SimpleRSS strips `<![CDATA[ ... ]]>` markers but does not HTML-unescape the contents, which is already literal HTML. Applying `CGI.unescapeHTML` to it decodes entities that are part of the HTML text itself: `<script>` shown in a code sample becomes a real `<script>` tag, `&` becomes a bare `&`, etc. Since the post is stored with `cook_method: raw_html` and never sanitized, escaped markup that the blog author intentionally displayed as text is executed/rendered as markup on the forum. The unescape should only be applied when the element was not CDATA-wrapped (or the content should be parsed with a real XML parser).

title: `String#scrub` requires Ruby 2.1; no polyfill is provided
body: `i.content.scrub` relies on `String#scrub`, which was introduced in Ruby 2.1.0 (released 25 Dec 2013). The Gemfile in this PR does not add a backport such as `string-scrub`, and nothing in the diff adds a freedom patch, so on the Ruby 2.0 installs the project supported at this time the poll job raises `NoMethodError` on the first item.

title: Outer transaction defeats PostCreator's post-commit job enqueueing and leaks side effects on unique-index collisions
body: `TopicEmbed.import` wraps `PostCreator#create` in `Topic.transaction`. `PostCreator` deliberately enqueues `process_post`/`feature_topic_users` and publishes MessageBus/TopicTrackingState events *after* its own transaction so workers don't see uncommitted rows (see the comment in `PostCreator#enqueue_jobs`). Nested inside the outer transaction those jobs are now enqueued before commit, so in production (`queue_jobs: true`) Sidekiq can pick up `process_post` for a post that is not yet visible or is later rolled back. The rollback case is real: the scheduled `PollFeed` and a `RetrieveTopic` job (which calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously) can import the same URL concurrently; both pass the `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).first` check, both create a topic+post, and the loser raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` from `TopicEmbed.create!`, which is unhandled, rolls back its topic, and leaves already-enqueued jobs, user stat updates and publishes referring to a vanished post. Create the TopicEmbed row inside PostCreator's transaction (or use an advisory lock / `find_or_create` with rescue) and keep job enqueueing after commit.

title: Import pipeline is subject to per-user rate limits and new-user host-spam detection
body: `PostCreator` is invoked with `skip_validations: true`, but that does not bypass `Post`'s `rate_limit` after_create hooks (`rate_limit_create_topic`/`rate_limit_create_post`, 1 per 5s, `max_topics_per_day: 20`) nor `rollback_if_host_spam_detected`. Unless the `embed_by_username` account is staff, importing a feed with more than one new item raises `RateLimiter::LimitExceeded` on the second topic and aborts the whole poll; a TL0 embed account also trips `newuser_spam_host_threshold` after three topics linking to the embeddable host (every import adds an `Imported from` link), causing posts to be rolled back and spam alerts sent to moderators. The Disqus importer in this same PR wraps its run in `RateLimiter.disable` precisely for this reason, but `PollFeed`/`TopicRetriever` do not. Either disable rate limiting around the import, pass an option to bypass it, or document that the embed user must be staff.

title: Deleted imported post/topic leaves a dangling TopicEmbed that crashes updates and permanently breaks the embed
body: `TopicEmbed` has no cleanup when its post or topic is deleted. `belongs_to :post` honours `Post`'s trashable default scope, so after a staff member deletes the imported topic `embed.post` is `nil`; the next feed poll with changed content calls `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!`, raising `NoMethodError` and aborting the job. Meanwhile `topic_id_for_embed` still returns the deleted topic id, so `EmbedController#best` builds a `TopicView` on a deleted topic (404) instead of falling through to re-import, and because the unique `embed_url` row persists the URL can never be imported again. Handle a missing post (treat as no embed / destroy the row) and remove TopicEmbed rows when the post or topic is destroyed.

title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative (//host/...) links and images
body: The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png`, which are very common in blog/RSS HTML. `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes and the result is prefixed with the article host, producing `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.png` — a broken link/image. The same happens for `img[src]` at line 70. Only rewrite when the value starts with a single `/` (i.e. not `//`), or resolve with `URI.join(url, href)`, which also handles the plain relative paths (`images/x.png`) that this code currently ignores.

title: `open(url)` depends on open-uri being required by an unrelated file
body: `import_remote` calls `Kernel#open` with an http URL but `topic_embed.rb` never requires `open-uri`; the only `require 'open-uri'` in this PR is in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`. Whenever `TopicEmbed.import_remote` is reached without `Jobs::PollFeed` having been loaded first (e.g. the Disqus thor task or a dev-mode Sidekiq process with feed polling disabled), `open("http://...")` falls through to plain `File.open` and raises `Errno::ENOENT`. Add `require 'open-uri'` to this file (and consider an explicit timeout on the request).

title: embed.css and embed.js are not added to the asset precompile list
body: The PR adds `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` and `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` and references them via `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` and as the script the third-party site must include, but `config/application.rb` (which maintains an explicit `config.assets.precompile` list in this app) is not changed. In production, where `config.assets.compile` is false, non-precompiled assets are not in the manifest: the stylesheet helper falls back to `/stylesheets/embed.css` (404, unstyled iframe) and `/assets/embed.js` requested by embedding sites 404s, so the feature does not work at all outside development. Add both files to `config.assets.precompile`.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of the configured Discourse URL. With `discourseUrl = "http://discourse.example.com/"`, messages from `http://discourse.example.co`, `http://discourse.example.c`, or even `http://d` pass the check, since all are substrings. The handler only sets the iframe height today, but this is an origin check that will be relied on as more message types are added. Compare the origin exactly (parse `discourseUrl` and compare `protocol + '//' + host`).

title: `<%- end if %>` typo only works by accident
body: The header conditional is closed with `end if` instead of `end`. Ruby treats the trailing `if` as a modifier whose condition is the *next* compiled statement (the output-buffer append generated by ERB for the following whitespace/link), so the template happens to compile and the buffer call still runs before the branch. Any change to the following line (e.g. removing the blank lines or the logo link) can turn this into a syntax error or silently swallow the header. No spec renders this view (controller specs run without `render_views`), so the typo is not caught. Change to `<%- end %>` and add a rendering test.

title: Disqus importer silently drops --category support and original topic dates, and aborts on fetch failures
body: The `--category` option is removed and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` replaces the old `PostCreator` call that passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` and `category: category_id`. Imported topics are now created in the default category with the import time instead of the original thread date, changing the behaviour of an existing CLI without mention. In addition `import_remote` performs `open(t[:link]).read` with no rescue, so a single dead link or `nil` link in the Disqus export (common for deleted pages) raises `OpenURI::HTTPError`/`TypeError` and aborts the entire import midway, after `RateLimiter.disable` and blacklist changes have already been applied (restored by `ensure`, but the import is left partial).

title: Templates, feed parsing and import paths are untested; existing spec names mismatch behaviour
body: The controller specs never render `best.html.erb` or `loading.html.erb` (rspec-rails controller specs stub rendering), and `TopicView.expects(:new)` returns nil, so the `@topic_view.posts`/`topic.url` code and the `end if` typo are never exercised. `poll_feed_spec` only tests the guard conditions, not `poll_feed` itself (nil `content`, non-http links, CDATA handling). There are no tests for `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, URL escaping in the imported footer, or `absolutize_urls` with protocol-relative URLs. The spec at line 8 is titled "is 404 without an embed_url" but the request actually fails with 403 from `ensure_embeddable` (no host configured) and only asserts `should_not be_success`, so it does not test the `params.require` path at all.

title: embed_url is a 255-char varchar with a unique index; long URLs fail the import unhandled
body: `t.string :embed_url` creates a `varchar(255)` column. Blog permalinks with long slugs or query strings (the controller accepts any query string) can exceed 255 characters; the `TopicEmbed.create!` then raises `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` after the topic and post have been created, rolling the outer transaction back and failing the job each time the URL is requested. Use `text` (or validate length before fetching) and index accordingly. Also note `force: true` on `create_table` will silently drop a pre-existing `topic_embeds` table and its data if the migration is ever re-run.

title: Already-shipped migration modified to add force: true
body: This migration predates the PR and has already been applied on existing installs; editing it has no effect there but changes what new installs run. `force: true` makes `create_table` drop any existing `top_topics` table silently, so if the migration is re-run (e.g. after a manual rollback/replay or on a database where the table was created by `db:schema:load`) all top-topic data is destroyed without warning. Shipped migrations should not be edited; if a drop-if-exists is really needed for the test database, fix the test setup instead.

title: Rails 3 lockfile not updated for the new gems
body: The project dual-boots via `Gemfile.lock` (Rails 3, `RAILS3=1`) and `Gemfile_rails4.lock`. Only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` gains `ruby-readability`, `guess_html_encoding` and `simple-rss`.
