Booting in Rails 3 mode with `bundle install --deployment` / `--frozen` will fail because the Gemfile no longer matches its lockfile, and without frozen mode Bundler will re-resolve and rewrite the lockfile unexpectedly. Either update `Gemfile.lock` as well or drop the Rails 3 boot path.

title: .panel can be squeezed by long header content because it is a shrinkable flex item
body: `.d-header .contents` is now a flex container and `.panel` (the icons/login area) was changed from `float: right` to a flex item with `margin-left: auto` and `order: 3`. Floated blocks got a shrink-to-fit (max-content) width and never wrapped internally; a flex item defaults to `flex: 0 1 auto`, so when sibling content is wide the browser shrinks every item proportionally to its flex-basis. The `.extra-info-wrapper` sibling (order 2) carries the topic title, which can be hundreds of characters, so on topic pages with a long title the total max-content width exceeds the `.wrap` width and `.panel` loses a share of the overflow. `.panel`'s min-content width is only about one floated `li`/button wide, so its `.icons` and login/sign-up buttons wrap onto additional lines and the header grows taller. The icon panel needs `flex-shrink: 0` (or an explicit `flex: 0 0 auto`) so that only the title area absorbs the overflow, as it effectively did under the float layout.

title: Float fallbacks removed, so browsers without flexbox now get a vertically stacked header
body: The commit deletes `.title { float: left; }` and `.panel { float: right; }` while adding the flex mixins. `float` is ignored on flex items, so keeping those declarations would have cost nothing in flex-capable browsers but would have preserved the horizontal logo-left/icons-right layout as a fallback in engines that ignore every `display: *flex*` value (IE9 and earlier, Opera Mini, older Android stock browsers in some modes). After this change those browsers render `.title`, `.extra-info-wrapper` and `.panel` as stacked full-width blocks. If those browsers are still in the support matrix, the float declarations should be retained alongside the mixin includes.

title: align-items mixin passes modern keywords straight into legacy prefixed properties
body: `@mixin align-items($alignment)` writes the same `$alignment` value to `-webkit-box-align` (2009 box syntax) and `-ms-flex-align` (IE10 syntax). Those legacy properties accept `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so any caller using `align-items(flex-start)` or `align-items(flex-end)` will emit invalid declarations that old WebKit and IE10 silently drop, leaving the default `stretch` alignment there while modern browsers behave as requested. The current call sites only use `center` and `baseline` (valid in all syntaxes), but this is a shared mixin introduced for general use and should map `flex-start`→`start` and `flex-end`→`end` for the prefixed outputs, as the standard flexbox-mixin snippets do.

title: align-items mixin emits a non-existent -ms property and omits the -moz legacy equivalent
body: `-ms-align-items` is not a property any IE version implemented (IE10 used `-ms-flex-align`, IE11 is unprefixed), so that line adds dead bytes to every rule that includes the mixin. Conversely, the `flexbox()` mixin emits `display: -moz-box` and the `order()` mixin emits `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but `align-items()` has no `-moz-box-align`, so Firefox versions that fall into the `-moz-box` path get the ordering but never the alignment (they stay at the legacy default `stretch`). Either drop the `-moz-box` fallbacks consistently from all mixins or add `-moz-box-align` and remove `-ms-align-items`.

title: PR title claims a performance optimization that the change does not make
body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" and its description is just "Test 5". The diff replaces float-based positioning with flexbox and adds vendor-prefixed mixins; nothing in it targets layout or paint performance, and flexbox layout is not generally cheaper than floats. Anyone reading the history will be misled about why the header, small-action posts and category badges changed appearance. The title/description should describe the actual change (migrate header and small-action layout to flexbox, add prefixed flex mixins) and note the visual adjustments to `.small-action-desc` spacing and `.extra-info-wrapper`.

title: `float: right` on `.small-action button` is a no-op now that `.small-action` is a flex container
body: `.small-action` is converted to `display: flex` (line 264), which makes its direct children (`.topic-avatar`, `.small-action-desc`, and the action `button`s) flex items. Per the CSS Flexbox spec, `float` has no effect on flex items, so the retained `button { float: right; }` (line 309) and `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` (line 270) no longer do anything. Previously the edit/delete buttons on small-action posts were pushed to the right edge by the float; after this change they will sit immediately after the `.small-action-desc` text (which has no `flex: 1` or `margin-left: auto` counterpart) unless some other stylesheet happens to give the description a fixed width. This is a visual regression in the small-action post layout. The fix is to replace the float with `margin-left: auto` on the button (or `flex: 1` on `.small-action-desc`) and drop the now-dead float declarations.

title: `order()` mixin passes the standard `order` value straight through to legacy `box-ordinal-group`, whose scale is different
body: The new `order($val)` mixin emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group: $val` alongside standard `order: $val`. The 2009 box model's `box-ordinal-group` is a positive integer with a default of 1, whereas standard `order` defaults to 0 and accepts 0 and negatives. With the current call sites (`order(2)`, `order(3)`) relative ordering still happens to be preserved, but any future use of `order(0)` or a negative value will produce an invalid, ignored legacy declaration, and `order(1)` will be treated as "same as default" in legacy engines while moving the item after default siblings in standard engines. If the legacy prefixes are intended to work, the legacy value should be `$val + 1`; otherwise the legacy declarations should be dropped rather than emitting misleading output.

title: `align-items()` mixin is inconsistent with `flexbox()`: missing `-moz-box-align`, includes a non-existent `-ms-align-items`, and legacy keyword mapping is wrong for flex-start/flex-end
body: `flexbox()` and `order()` emit `-moz-box` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but `align-items()` omits the matching `-moz-box-align`, so any Firefox build that only understands `display: -moz-box` gets the flex layout without the vertical alignment (e.g. header contents would not be centered). The mixin also emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a property in any IE/Edge release (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, IE11+ uses unprefixed `align-items`), so that line is dead output on every page. Finally, both `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` use the keywords `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`; the mixin passes `$alignment` through verbatim, so a future `@include align-items(flex-start)` would silently produce invalid legacy declarations. The current call sites (`center`, `baseline`) are unaffected, but the mixin as written does not deliver the cross-browser fallback it appears to promise.

title: PR title claims a performance optimization that the change does not make; description is a placeholder
body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" and the description is just "Test 5". The change replaces float-based layout in the header, small-action posts and category badges with flexbox and adjusts spacing; nothing in it is a performance optimization (flexbox layout is generally no cheaper than floats, and no measurement is provided). The misleading title and empty description will end up in the commit history and make it hard for anyone bisecting a layout regression (e.g. in `.small-action` or the header `.panel`/`.extra-info-wrapper` ordering) to understand the intent. The title and description should describe the actual layout change and its visual effects.

title: Header `.panel` right-alignment relies on `margin-left: auto`, which the 2009 `-webkit-box` fallback the mixins emit does not support
body: The new `flexbox()` mixin deliberately emits `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` so that legacy engines (Android 2.x–4.3 stock browser, Safari < 6.1, old Firefox) get a flex layout. However, the header now positions `.panel` on the right solely via `margin-left: auto` (replacing the previous `float: right`). In the 2009 box model, `auto` margins on box children are computed as zero, so in exactly those browsers the fallback is targeting, the panel (user/notification/search icons, login buttons) will collapse to sit immediately after the title/extra-info instead of at the right edge. Previously `float: right` worked everywhere. Either drop the legacy prefixes (so those browsers fall back to normal block flow) or add a 2009-compatible mechanism (e.g. `-webkit-box-pack: justify` on `.contents` or `-webkit-box-flex: 1` on the preceding item).

title: Making `.small-action` a flex container breaks right-alignment of its action buttons
body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex`, but `.small-action-desc` has no `flex: 1`/`flex-grow`, so it shrinks to its content width instead of filling the row as the old block did. The `.small-action button { float: right; }` rule (line 309) therefore either has no effect (if a button is a direct flex child, floats are ignored on flex items) or only floats to the right edge of the now content-sized `.small-action-desc`, placing the edit/delete buttons directly after a short description like "closed 2 hours ago" instead of at the right edge of the post. Add `flex: 1 1 auto` (or `width: 100%`) to `.small-action-desc`, or use `margin-left: auto` on the buttons.

title: `align-items` mixin emits a non-existent `-ms-align-items` property and passes values through unmapped to legacy syntaxes
body: `-ms-align-items` is not a property any IE version ever implemented (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, IE11 uses unprefixed `align-items`), so line 121 is dead output in every compiled rule that uses the mixin. More importantly, the mixin passes `$alignment` verbatim into `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, which only accept `start`/`end` rather than the modern `flex-start`/`flex-end`; likewise `order()` forwards `$val` into `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`, which requires a positive integer (default 1) while modern `order` defaults to 0 and allows negatives. Today's call sites (`center`, `baseline`, `2`, `3`) happen to be valid in all syntaxes, but the mixins silently produce invalid legacy declarations for any other value, defeating their purpose. Either map values (`flex-start`→`start`, `$val + 1` for ordinal-group) or drop the legacy prefixes.

title: PR title claims a performance optimization; description is a placeholder
body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" and described as "Test 5". Nothing in the diff is a performance change: it is a layout refactor replacing float-based positioning of `.title`/`.panel`/`.extra-info-wrapper` and `.small-action` with flexbox, plus new vendor-prefix mixins, with visible rendering consequences (removed margins/paddings, new ordering). The misleading title and empty description will mislead anyone bisecting a header/small-action layout regression later and give reviewers no information about intended visual changes or browser support goals. The title and description should describe the actual change and the browsers the legacy prefixes are meant to support.

title: Local cache is populated before the limit check, so a rejected device bypasses the limit on its next request
body: `tagDeviceUI` writes the device key into `localCache` (29‑minute TTL) *before* calling `anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`. With this PR, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` can now fail with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, and `Anonymous.Authenticate` turns that into an authentication failure. But because the cache entry was already set, every subsequent request from the same device within the next 29 minutes hits the cache early-return (`return nil`) in `tagDeviceUI`, `TagDevice` reports success, and `Authenticate` issues a normal anonymous identity. In practice the frontend fires many requests per page load, so at most the first one or two requests from an over-limit device get a 401 and the rest succeed — the configured `device_limit` is effectively not enforced. The cache must only be populated after the store call succeeds (and a rejection should not be cached, or should be cached as a negative result that keeps rejecting).

title: Count-then-insert limit check is not atomic; concurrent new devices can exceed the limit
body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` and then, if `count < deviceLimit`, performs an upsert in a separate session. Two or more first-time devices arriving concurrently (very likely with several Grafana replicas, since the per-instance `localCache` provides no cross-instance dedup) will all observe `count < limit` and all insert, so the stored device count can overshoot `device_limit`. If the limit is meant as a hard cap (e.g. for licensing/abuse control) this needs to be done in a single transaction with appropriate locking or a conditional insert; otherwise the setting should be documented as a soft limit. Additionally the `COUNT(*)` runs on every cache miss even when the device already exists and will simply be updated, which is an avoidable extra query on the request path.

title: Device limit is only applied to requests carrying X-Grafana-Device-Id; omitting the header bypasses it entirely
body: `TagDevice` returns `nil` immediately when the `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header is absent, and `Anonymous.Authenticate` then issues a full anonymous identity. The header is set voluntarily by the Grafana frontend JS; any client that strips it (curl, scripts, a modified browser) is never counted and never limited, so `auth.anonymous.device_limit` is trivially circumvented and cannot be relied on as an access control. If the limit is intended to be enforceable, requests without a device id should be rejected (or at least documented as uncounted) when a limit is configured.

title: Limit tests only cover rejection of a new device; no coverage for existing-device updates or the service/client enforcement path
body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only asserts that a second, new device is rejected when `deviceLimit=1`. There is no test that an already-registered active device can still be updated once the limit is reached (the `updateDevice` success path and its `updated_at BETWEEN` window), no test that a stale device (older than 30 days) is treated as new, and no test at the `AnonDeviceService`/`Anonymous.Authenticate` level that a limit-exceeding device actually fails authentication on repeated requests. The last gap is exactly what hides the local-cache bypass bug in `tagDeviceUI`; a test issuing two `TagDevice`/`Authenticate` calls for the same over-limit device would have caught it.

title: Limit-reached failure surfaces as a generic 401 and warning-level log noise
body: `Authenticate` returns the raw `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` (a plain `fmt.Errorf`). The authn service joins it into the generic auth error, logs a `Warn` for every request, and middleware responds with a bare 401 'Unauthorized'; the frontend cannot distinguish 'device limit reached' from any other auth failure, so the newly exposed `anonymousDeviceLimit` setting cannot be used to show a meaningful message. The error is also logged at Debug in `TagDevice`, then re-logged upstream. Consider an `errutil` error with a public message/status so the UI can present the condition, and log at a lower level since this is expected behaviour under load.

title: anonymousDeviceLimit is typed as `undefined` in the runtime config and the backend always sends a number
body: `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` with no type annotation gives the class property the literal type `undefined`, so `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` in `@grafana/runtime` is unusable for numeric comparisons without a cast (any `config.anonymousDeviceLimit > 0` is a compile error). Meanwhile `FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is a non-omitempty `int64`, so the backend always serialises a number (0 when unset); the `number | undefined` type in `packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts` is therefore misleading as well. Declare it as `anonymousDeviceLimit = 0` (or `: number`) to match the wire format.

title: New `device_limit` setting is not added to defaults.ini/sample.ini or configuration docs
body: `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is read from `[auth.anonymous] device_limit`, but the PR does not add the key to `conf/defaults.ini`, `conf/sample.ini`, or the configuration documentation, and the PR description leaves the why/who sections unfilled. Operators have no discoverable way to learn the setting exists, its default (0 = unlimited), or its semantics (30-day active-device window, soft limit, only applies to requests with a device id). Grafana convention is for every new ini key to appear in both ini files with a comment and in the configure-grafana docs.

title: Device limit is bypassed on the second request: local cache is populated before the store rejects the device
body: In `tagDeviceUI` the device cache key is written with `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` *before* `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` is called. When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` (device not inserted), the cache entry remains for ~29 minutes. On the very next request from the same device ID, `tagDeviceUI` hits the cache and returns nil, so `TagDevice` returns nil and `Anonymous.Authenticate` issues an anonymous identity. The result is that a device over the limit is rejected exactly once and then admitted on refresh/retry, without ever being counted in the DB. The limit is therefore effectively unenforced (any number of devices can get in with two requests each). The cache entry must only be set after a successful create/update (or be deleted on error).

title: DI signature change for ProvideAnonymousDeviceService/ProvideAnonDBStore without updating the wire provider set
body: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` previously accepted `anonstore.AnonStore`, which means the production wire graph had a provider for it (`anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` bound to `AnonStore`). This PR changes `ProvideAnonDBStore` to require an `int64` device limit and makes `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` take `db.DB` instead, but `pkg/server/wire.go` is not among the changed files. If the old provider/bind is still listed, `wire gen` fails (no provider for `int64`, or unused provider error), breaking the server build. The wire provider set must drop `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and its bind (or the store should keep taking `*setting.Cfg`).

title: Count-then-insert limit check is not atomic; concurrent new devices can exceed the configured limit
body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` in one session and then the upsert in a separate `WithDbSession` call, with no transaction or lock. If N new devices arrive concurrently while the count is just below `deviceLimit`, all N read a count below the limit and all insert, so the stored active-device count exceeds the configured limit. The limit is only approximate under load. A single transaction with an appropriate lock, or a conditional insert (`INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < ?`), would make it enforceable.

title: updateDevice mutates captured args inside the WithDbSession callback, which breaks on SQLite lock retries
body: `updateDevice` does `args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)` inside the closure passed to `WithDbSession`. The sqlstore's `retryOnLocks` re-invokes the same callback when SQLite returns `database is locked/busy` (when `query_retries` > 0), so on retry `args` becomes `[query, query, clientIP, ...]`: the SQL string is passed as the first bind parameter and the parameter count no longer matches the placeholders, so the retry fails with a driver error instead of succeeding. The same anti-pattern exists in `CreateOrUpdateDevice`; the new function copies it. Build the full argument slice outside the closure (or construct it fresh inside without reassigning the captured variable).

title: ErrDeviceLimitReached is a plain error, so rejected users receive a generic unauthenticated response with no reason
body: `Anonymous.Authenticate` returns the bare `fmt.Errorf("device limit reached")` from the store. The authn service joins client errors and the context handler simply treats the request as unauthenticated, redirecting to the login page with no message; the frontend has no way to distinguish 'device limit reached' from any other anonymous auth failure, and `anonymousDeviceLimit` in frontend settings does not help since the limit value alone does not indicate that this device was rejected. Returning an `errutil` error with a public message (as other authn clients do) would let the API/login page surface the actual reason.

title: Device tagging moved from fire-and-forget to the synchronous request path even when no limit is configured
body: Previously `TagDevice` ran in a goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout so anonymous authentication never waited on the device store. It now runs inline inside `Authenticate` on every local-cache miss (COUNT(*) + upsert, two DB round trips) regardless of whether `device_limit` is set. On anonymous-heavy deployments (public dashboards) with a slow or contended DB this adds request latency and makes anonymous auth fail/hang with the DB even when the operator never enabled the limit. Consider keeping the async path when `deviceLimit == 0`, or at least bounding the DB call with a short timeout.

title: anonymousDeviceLimit is typed as `undefined` on GrafanaBootConfig although the backend always sends a number
body: `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` without a type annotation makes TypeScript infer the property type as literally `undefined` under strict mode. The Go DTO emits `anonymousDeviceLimit` as an `int64` without `omitempty`, so at runtime it is always a number (0 when disabled). Consumers of the public `config` object cannot write `config.anonymousDeviceLimit > 0` without a cast, and the `number | undefined` declared in `GrafanaConfig` does not match the actual contract (0 = disabled, never undefined). Declare it as `anonymousDeviceLimit = 0;` (or `number | undefined` explicitly) and document that 0 means no limit.

title: No test covers the limit through TagDevice/Authenticate, nor the update-at-limit path
body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only verifies that a second *new* device at limit=1 returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` directly from the store. There is no test that (a) an already-registered device can still be updated when the limit is reached (the `updateDevice` success path), (b) a rejected device stays rejected on a subsequent `TagDevice`/`Authenticate` call (which would have caught the local-cache bypass in `tagDeviceUI`), or (c) `Anonymous.Authenticate` actually returns an error for an over-limit device. `impl_test.go` was only updated for the signature change and always uses `setting.NewCfg()` with limit 0.

title: New `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` setting is not added to defaults.ini, sample.ini or the configuration docs
body: The PR introduces a new ini key `device_limit` under `[auth.anonymous]` but does not add it to `conf/defaults.ini`, `conf/sample.ini`, or `docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/_index.md`, which is the repository convention for every configuration option. Operators have no discoverable way to learn about the option, its default (0 = unlimited), or its semantics (devices active in the last 30 days). The PR description is also left as the unfilled template.

title: Local cache is populated before the DB write, so a rejected device is let through on its next request
body: `tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` and only afterwards calls `anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`. With the new device limit, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` can fail with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, which `Authenticate` turns into an authentication failure. However the cache key for that device has already been stored (29 minute TTL), so the very next request from the same device hits `if _, ok := a.localCache.Get(key); ok { return nil }`, `TagDevice` returns nil, and `Authenticate` succeeds. In practice the limit only blocks the first request; a page refresh bypasses it for ~29 minutes, after which the cycle repeats. The cache entry must only be set after a successful store write (or be removed on `ErrDeviceLimitReached`). This pattern was harmless before because tagging was best-effort, but it now defeats the feature.

title: Count-then-insert is not atomic; concurrent new devices can exceed the configured limit
body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` reads `CountDevices(...)` and then, if `count < deviceLimit`, performs the upsert in a separate session. There is no transaction, lock, or conditional insert tying the two together, so N concurrent first-time devices (e.g. a burst of new visitors, or several Grafana instances each with an empty local cache) all observe `count < limit` and all insert, leaving the table above the limit. If the limit is intended as a hard cap (licensing/abuse control) this needs either a serialized check-and-insert (e.g. `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < ?` or the existing `serverlock`), or the docs should state that the limit is best-effort.

title: Device limit is only enforced for requests that volunteer the X-Grafana-Device-Id header
body: `TagDevice` returns nil immediately when the `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header is absent, and `Authenticate` then grants the anonymous identity. Because the header is entirely client-controlled, any client (scripts, curl, a browser with the header stripped) can use anonymous access without ever being counted or limited, so the new `device_limit` setting cannot be relied upon to cap anonymous usage. If the limit is meant to be an enforceable cap, requests without a device id should either be rejected when a limit is configured or be subject to a separate check; otherwise the limitation should be made explicit in the setting's documentation.

title: ProvideAnonDBStore signature change is not reflected in the wire provider set
body: Before this change `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` received an `anonstore.AnonStore` via dependency injection, which means the server wire set had to contain a provider for it (`anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` plus a `wire.Bind(new(anonstore.AnonStore), new(*anonstore.AnonDBStore))`). This PR changes `ProvideAnonDBStore` to take an extra `deviceLimit int64` and constructs the store manually inside `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService`, but no change to `pkg/server/wire.go` is included. If the old provider/binding remains, `wire` generation fails (no provider for `int64`, and an unused `AnonStore` binding), breaking the build; if it is silently removed elsewhere, that change should be part of this PR so reviewers can verify it.

title: updateDevice mutates captured args inside a closure that WithDbSession may retry
body: `updateDevice` does `args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)` inside the callback passed to `WithDbSession`. `WithDbSession` re-invokes the callback on SQLite `locked`/`busy` errors (`retryOnLocks`), so on a retry the query string is prepended a second time and `dbSession.Exec(query, query, clientIP, ...)` is executed with one bind parameter too many, which fails and makes every retry attempt a guaranteed error. Build the full argument slice outside the closure (or inside it from a fresh slice) so retries are idempotent. The same pattern exists in `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, but this PR introduces it anew in `updateDevice`.

title: Device-limit tests cover only the rejection path, not the update-at-limit path or the service/cache layer
body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only asserts that a second new device gets `ErrDeviceLimitReached` at the store level. There is no test that an already-known device is still accepted (and updated) once the limit is reached, which is the main behaviour `updateDevice` exists for. There is also no test in `impl_test.go` that exercises `TagDevice` with a non-zero `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit`, and no test of `Anonymous.Authenticate` returning an error for a rejected device; a service-level test issuing two requests from an over-limit device would have exposed the local-cache bypass described in another finding.

title: New auth.anonymous.device_limit setting is not added to defaults.ini/sample.ini or the configuration docs
body: A new `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` key is read here, but the PR does not add it to `conf/defaults.ini`, `conf/sample.ini`, or `docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/_index.md`. Grafana's convention is that every setting appears in defaults.ini (so `grafana cli admin` / settings pages show it) and is documented, including the semantics of `0` meaning unlimited and what users experience when the limit is hit. Without this, operators have no discoverable way to learn the option exists or how it behaves.

title: ErrDeviceLimitReached is a plain error, so rejected users get a generic unauthenticated response with no explanation
body: `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is defined with `fmt.Errorf` and is returned straight out of `Anonymous.Authenticate`. The authn/contexthandler layers only surface `errutil` errors with status codes and public messages; a plain error becomes a generic 401/redirect-to-login, and the authn service also logs a warning for every request from the rejected device. End users hitting the limit see a login page with no indication why anonymous access stopped working, and operators get noisy warn logs. Define it as an `errutil` error (e.g. `errutil.TooManyRequests`/`Unauthorized` with a public message) so the frontend can show a meaningful message, and consider lowering the log level for this expected condition.

title: enableSqlExpressions has inverted, dead logic that is a trap for future edits
body: The helper computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (so `enabled` is true precisely when the feature flag is OFF) and then returns `false` from both branches. The function behaves as intended today (always disabled), but the variable name has the opposite meaning of its value, and the `if enabled { return false }` branch is dead code. The obvious future 'fix' of changing the final line to `return enabled` would re-enable SQL expressions exactly when the flag is disabled, i.e. for every default installation. If the intent is a hard kill-switch, make that explicit (e.g. `return false` with a comment referencing the CVE) rather than leaving an inverted, no-op flag check in place.

title: No regression test asserting SQL expressions are rejected even with the feature flag enabled
body: This PR is the in-repo fix for a critical RCE/LFI (CVE-2024-9264), yet it adds no test. There is nothing verifying that `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` returns an error for `QueryTypeSQL` when `FlagSqlExpressions` is enabled, nor that the legacy path (`UnmarshalSQLCommand` -> `NewSQLCommand` -> `sql.TablesList`) fails and never reaches `QueryFramesInto`. The legacy path is only protected implicitly by the stub `DB` returning 'not implemented'; if someone later restores a working `DB` implementation (or swaps in a different engine), the legacy `/api/ds/query` path would silently become live again with no explicit guard and no failing test to catch it. A unit test with the flag forced on, for both entry points, would lock in the fix.

title: Every SQL expression attempt now unconditionally emits an Error-level log with the raw SQL
body: Because the stub `DB.RunCommands` always returns 'not implemented', `TablesList` now hits the `logger.Error("error serializing sql", ...)` branch on every call, logging the full user-supplied SQL and the fabricated `SELECT json_serialize_sql(...)` command at Error level, followed by a second Warn log in `NewSQLCommand`. For a feature that is intentionally disabled, any user selecting the SQL expression type (still visible in the UI when the flag is on) will generate misleading error-level noise that looks like an internal failure rather than an intentional rejection. The disabled path should short-circuit with a single clear message before attempting to 'serialize' anything, or at least log at a lower level.

title: User-facing error text misrepresents a deliberate security disablement as 'not implemented'
body: The new guard returns `sqlExpressions is not implemented`, and the legacy path surfaces `error reading SQL command` (via the stubbed `TablesList`). Both messages suggest a missing or malformed feature rather than an intentional removal. Operators who enabled the still-registered `sqlExpressions` feature toggle (whose docs are untouched by this PR) will get contradictory signals: the flag exists and is documented, the UI offers the expression type, but every query fails with a message implying incomplete code. A message stating that SQL expressions are disabled (ideally with a reference to the security advisory) would avoid confusion and support tickets.

title: enableSqlExpressions has an inverted, dead feature-flag check and always returns false
body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (so `enabled` is true when the flag is OFF) and then returns false on both branches. The feature-flag lookup is dead code and the variable's name means the opposite of its value. The effective behaviour (SQL expressions unconditionally refused) matches the PR's intent, but the code reads as if it were flag-controlled, and the obvious future "fix" of changing the trailing `return false` to `return true` would re-enable SQL expressions precisely when the `sqlExpressions` toggle is disabled. Either reduce the body to a plain `return false` with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264 and the removed DuckDB engine, or fix the inversion if the flag is genuinely meant to be honoured. Relatedly, the `sqlExpressions` toggle stays registered and documented as "enables SQL expressions", so operators who turn it on now get an opaque "sqlExpressions is not implemented" error with nothing explaining why.

title: Legacy SQL command path fails with a misleading user message and spams Error-level logs with raw SQL
body: `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand` remain reachable through the legacy rawNode builder (buildCMDNode in nodes.go), which this PR does not gate. They now always fail because `sql.TablesList` calls the stub `DB.RunCommands`, which returns "not implemented". The resulting user-facing error is `errutil.BadRequest("sql-invalid-sql", "error reading SQL command")`, which tells the user their SQL is malformed rather than that the feature is disabled, and is inconsistent with the reader.go path ("sqlExpressions is not implemented"). In addition, every evaluation of any dashboard panel or alert rule that still contains a SQL expression now emits an Error-level log from `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:28` (including the full user-supplied SQL and synthesized command) plus a Warn from `sql_command.go:32`, producing persistent error-log noise for an intentionally disabled feature. Short-circuit `NewSQLCommand` with an explicit "SQL expressions are disabled" error before calling `TablesList`, and drop or downgrade the logging.

title: No regression test that SQL expressions are refused regardless of feature flag
body: This change is the in-repo fix for a critical CVE (RCE/LFI via DuckDB SQL expressions), yet no test asserts the new behaviour. There is no test that `ReadQuery` with `type: "sql"` returns an error when `FlagSqlExpressions` is enabled as well as disabled, nor that `NewSQLCommand`/`UnmarshalSQLCommand` refuse to build a command. Because the gate in `enableSqlExpressions` is written in a confusing, inverted way, a test pinning "SQL query type is rejected with the flag both on and off" is the main protection against the feature being accidentally re-enabled later (e.g. when the `sql.DB` stub is replaced with a real engine) without a security review.

title: enableSqlExpressions consults the feature flag but both branches return false (dead, inverted logic)
body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (note the variable is true when the flag is *disabled*) and then returns `false` in both the `if enabled` branch and the fall-through. The flag lookup is therefore a no-op and the naming is inverted. If the intent is to hard-disable SQL expressions (as the PR title says), the function should simply return false / the `case QueryTypeSQL` should return the error directly, with a comment referencing the CVE. As written, the code looks like a botched feature-flag gate, and a future maintainer is likely to 'fix' the inverted condition and silently re-enable the code path that led to CVE-2024-9264. Security-critical kill switches should not be expressed as misleading dead logic.

title: Legacy path reports disabled feature as a user SQL error ('sql-invalid-sql' / 'error reading SQL command')
body: `NewSQLCommand` (used by the legacy `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`buildCMDNode` path as well as the new reader) now always fails because `sql.TablesList` calls the stubbed `RunCommands`, which unconditionally returns 'not implemented'. The failure is surfaced as `errutil.BadRequest("sql-invalid-sql", WithPublicMessage("error reading SQL command"))` and logged as `"invalid sql query"` at Warn level. Users (and support) will be told their SQL is malformed when the real cause is that the feature has been disabled for security reasons, and the error ID/message is inconsistent with the `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"` error returned from `ReadQuery`. Return an explicit 'SQL expressions are disabled' error (and skip `TablesList` entirely) so the two entry points behave consistently and the message is truthful.

title: TablesList always fails via the stub but still builds a DuckDB command and logs at Error level with user SQL
body: With `NewInMemoryDB()` now returning a stub whose `RunCommands` always errors, `TablesList` can never succeed, yet it still escapes the input, formats the DuckDB-specific `SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')` string, calls the stub, and then logs `logger.Error("error serializing sql", ..., "sql", rawSQL, "cmd", cmd)` on every invocation. Every attempt to use a SQL expression (including probes by attackers) now produces guaranteed Error-level log lines containing user-controlled SQL, and the surrounding `tablesFromAST`/`astError`/`existsInList` code is unreachable dead code. The variable is also still named `duckDB` even though the PR says it removes DuckDB references. The function should short-circuit with a clear 'disabled' error (or the whole file should be reduced to that) instead of going through an always-failing DuckDB-shaped path.

title: No regression test asserting SQL expressions are rejected on either entry point
body: This PR is the in-repo fix for a critical RCE/LFI (CVE-2024-9264), but it adds no tests. There is no test that `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` returns an error for `QueryTypeSQL` (with and without `FlagSqlExpressions` enabled), no test that the legacy `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand` path fails, and no test that `sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto` / `RunCommands` return 'not implemented'. Without such tests, a later refactor (e.g. 'fixing' the inverted logic in `enableSqlExpressions`, or restoring a real `DB` implementation) could re-expose the vulnerable path unnoticed. Any pre-existing tests in `pkg/expr/sql` or `pkg/expr` that exercised `TablesList`/`NewSQLCommand` with valid SQL and expected success also need to be updated or removed, as they would now fail against the stub.

title: sqlExpressions feature flag remains registered/documented (as enabling DuckDB) and the UI still offers the SQL type, but the backend now always rejects it
body: After this change the backend unconditionally rejects SQL expressions regardless of `FlagSqlExpressions`, but the flag is still registered in the feature registry with a description along the lines of 'Enables using SQL and DuckDB functions', is still listed in the feature-toggles documentation, and the frontend still exposes the SQL expression type when the flag is on. Operators who enable the flag will get a working UI option that always fails with 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' / 'error reading SQL command'. The PR description acknowledges leaving docs untouched, but at minimum the flag description and docs should state that the feature is disabled (and no longer DuckDB-based), or the flag should be marked as non-functional, so users are not misled into enabling a dead toggle.

title: V2 canManage() is granted by the VIEW scope on all groups
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE on the Groups resource-type resource (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`). canManage() is what GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() checks via auth.groups().requireManage(), so an admin who was only granted the `view` scope on all groups can create top-level groups in the realm. This is a privilege escalation; the check should only accept AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE (mirroring canManage(GroupModel) which correctly checks MANAGE only). The GroupPermissionEvaluator javadoc for canManage() ("Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") encodes the same mistake and should be corrected too. No test covers a VIEW-only all-groups permission attempting to create a group.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes/returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In V2 a per-group Resource is created with name == group id (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup/getOrCreateResource) and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String groupId, ...) resolves it with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() however calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) with the authz resource UUID and then adds groupResource.getId() to the result set. Consequences: (1) findByName with a resource UUID never matches, so the code always falls back to the all-groups resource, meaning per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are never detected and an all-groups permission is reported for every iterated resource; (2) the returned set contains resource UUIDs, but callers (UsersResource.searchForUser/getUsersCount, BruteForceUsersResource) feed it into session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...) and getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds), which expect group IDs, so user search/count return nothing. Both places should use groupResource.getName() and skip the "Groups" placeholder resource itself. Note also that getOrCreateResource never calls setType(resourceType) on the per-group resource, so findByType(server, "Groups") currently only returns the placeholder resource created in init(), making this method effectively dead for real groups and leaving GET /users/count wrong for admins with only group-member permissions.

title: Existence of any per-group permission disables the all-groups fallback for that group
body: hasPermission() only consults the Groups resource-type resource when no specific resource named by the group id exists. Once a specific resource exists for a group (e.g. because someone granted VIEW_MEMBERS on it), evaluation is done only against that resource and the requested scopes; if the specific permission does not include the requested scope (e.g. VIEW/MANAGE) the method returns false even though the caller holds an all-groups permission granting that scope. So granting a narrow per-group permission silently revokes broader type-level rights for that group (e.g. canView(group) becomes false for an admin with view-all-groups). The method should fall back to the type-level resource when the specific-resource evaluation does not grant the scope, or evaluate both.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc references the wrong predicate
body: The javadoc for requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says it throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false, but the implementations (GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers) check canManageMembers(GroupModel). The two scopes (manage-members vs manage-membership) have different meanings, so the doc misleads callers about which permission is enforced. Also, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission's @return says "Stream of IDs" while the method returns a Set.

title: No cleanup of V2 group resources/permissions when a group is removed
body: The ProviderEventListener that reacts to GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent is registered only when the V1 feature (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) is enabled, and even then it calls groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false), which GroupPermissionsV2 implements by throwing UnsupportedOperationException. With this PR, V2 now creates per-group authz Resources (named by group id) and scope permissions referencing them, but nothing removes them when the group is deleted. Deleted groups therefore leave orphaned Resource/Policy rows in the admin-permissions resource server that keep showing up in permission listings and in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()/findByType iterations.

title: getResourceName has no handling for the new Groups resource type
body: getResourceName() maps Users resources to a human-readable name ("All users" or the username) but falls through to resource.getDisplayName() for everything else. Group resources created by getOrCreateResource() have name == group id and no display name set, so for Groups-type permissions this returns null (and the "Groups" placeholder gets no "All groups" label). Any consumer that relies on this method (e.g. admin UI permission listings) will show empty names for group permissions. A Groups branch resolving the group and returning its name/path, plus an "All groups" label, is needed for parity with Users.

title: MANAGE_MEMBERS cannot be used to create users in V2 because canCreateGroupMembers is gated on the V1 feature flag
body: canCreateGroupMembers() returns false unless Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. V1 and V2 are versions of the same feature and cannot be enabled together, so under ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 the newly added Groups MANAGE_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP scopes are never consulted when creating a user with `groups` in the representation; createUser() always fails with 403 unless the admin has the manage-users role or an all-users MANAGE permission. Either the gate should also accept V2 or the limitation should be documented.

title: Missing negative/edge coverage for new group scopes
body: The new test class only exercises happy paths for the Groups scopes. Not covered: (a) that an all-groups VIEW permission does NOT allow creating a top-level group (which would catch the canManage() VIEW bug); (b) that joining a group requires the group-level MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP permission (testManageGroupMembership grants both all-users MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP and the group permission at once, so a missing group check would not be detected); (c) GET /groups/{id}/members with VIEW_MEMBERS; (d) GET /users/count for an admin with only group VIEW_MEMBERS permissions (which exercises getGroupIdsWithViewPermission and would expose the resource-id vs group-id bug); (e) a group with a specific narrow permission plus an all-groups VIEW permission (fallback behaviour).

title: Per-subgroup policy evaluation before pagination in V2
body: getSubGroups() loads all subgroups (getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, -1, -1)) and filters with auth.groups()::canView before paginating. In V2, canView(GroupModel) does not short-circuit on a global permission: each call does a resource lookup, a policyStore.findByResource on the type resource and a full policy evaluation. For an admin with an all-groups VIEW permission on a parent with thousands of children this results in thousands of policy evaluations per page request (same pattern in GroupsResource.getGroups). The previous code evaluated the global check once (canViewGlobal); if per-group negative permissions must be honoured, consider at least caching the all-groups evaluation result within the evaluator instance for the request.

title: V2 canManage() grants manage on all groups when admin only has the VIEW scope
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` falls through to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it returns true if the caller is granted *either* `view` or `manage` on the type-level "Groups" resource. `canManage()` is what `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` enforces via `auth.groups().requireManage()`, and that endpoint both creates new top-level groups and (when an `id` is supplied) moves an existing sub-group to the top level. So an admin who was only granted a read-only all-groups `view` permission can create groups and restructure the group hierarchy. The per-group `canManage(GroupModel)` correctly checks only `MANAGE`; the type-level method should do the same. Note the new Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` ("For V2 only: Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") was written to match this wrong behaviour and should be corrected as well. `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testViewGroups` grants all-groups VIEW but never asserts that group creation is still forbidden, so the escalation is not caught by the tests.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz Resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In the V2 implementation the per-group authorization `Resource` is created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` with the group's ID as the resource *name*; the resource's own `getId()` is an unrelated UUID generated by the resource store. `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` nevertheless calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` (so `resourceStore.findByName(server, <resource uuid>)` never matches and it silently falls back to the type-level "Groups" resource) and then does `granted.add(groupResource.getId())`. The returned set is consumed by `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` as `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` and by `getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)`, both of which expect real group IDs to restrict the DB query to members of those groups. With resource UUIDs the membership subquery matches nothing, so e.g. an admin granted `view-members` on the all-groups resource gets an empty user list and a count of 0 even though `canView(user)` would succeed for every group member. The V1 implementation correctly derives the group ID from the resource name; V2 should use `groupResource.getName()` for both the permission check and the returned set.

title: findByType("Groups") cannot enumerate per-group resources because getOrCreateResource never sets a resource type
body: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` enumerates group resources with `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. However the per-group resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (server-spi-private/.../AdminPermissionsSchema.java line 121) via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` followed only by `updateScopes(...)`; no `setType(...)` is ever called. The only resource with type "Groups" is the type-level "all groups" resource created in `init()` (which does `resource.setType(type)`). Consequently the callback is invoked at most once, for the "Groups" resource itself, and groups with individual `view-members`/`manage-members` permissions are never discovered, so the group-based pre-filtering of user searches never works for them (results then depend solely on the post-filter over the page returned by the DB, which breaks pagination/completeness). Either set the type on resources created by `getOrCreateResource` or enumerate per-group resources another way.

title: Any per-group permission shadows the all-groups permission for every other scope on that group
body: `hasPermission(groupId, scopes...)` looks up the per-group resource by name and, if it exists, evaluates only the policies attached to that resource; the type-level "Groups" resource is consulted only when no per-group resource exists. The policy evaluator only collects policies directly attached to the given resource (the per-group resource has no type, so no type-based lookup happens). Therefore as soon as anyone creates a permission on a specific group for one scope (e.g. `view-members` for admin A), an admin B who holds `manage`/`view` on the all-groups resource loses those rights for that specific group, because the all-groups policies are no longer evaluated for it. The test `testManageAllGroups` only covers the case where no per-group resource exists ("fallback to all-groups permission"), so this is untested. The evaluation should consider both the per-group resource and the type-level resource (e.g. evaluate the all-groups permission when the per-group evaluation does not produce a decision for the requested scope), or document this as an explicit limitation.

title: Group-based search restriction hides users granted via direct per-user permissions
body: `searchForUser` now unconditionally sets `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` whenever `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. The JPA user provider turns this attribute into a hard `user IN (members of these groups)` restriction on the search query. In V2 an admin can simultaneously hold `view-members` on group G and a direct `view` permission on user Bob (Users resource type) who is not a member of G. With this change the DB query is restricted to members of G, so Bob is never returned by `GET /users` even though `UserPermissionsV2.canView(bob)` is true and `GET /users/{bob}` succeeds. The same applies to `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser`. The group filter should only be applied when the admin has no other (per-user or type-level) user view grants, or the result sets need to be merged.

title: getResourceName does not resolve names for Groups resources
body: `getResourceName` only special-cases the `Users` resource type (returning "All users" or the username). For the newly added `Groups` type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, but per-group resources are created in `getOrCreateResource` without a display name and with the raw group ID as the name. Any representation that uses `getResourceName` (e.g. permission listings in the admin console) will therefore show `null`/empty names for group permissions, and the type-level "Groups" resource gets no "All groups" label analogous to "All users". A `Groups` branch resolving the group (and its path/name) should be added.

title: Javadoc of requireManageMembers references the wrong method
body: The new Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` says it throws `ForbiddenException` if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false, but the implementation (both V1 and V2) checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`, which is a different scope (`manage-members` vs `manage-membership`). Similarly, the Javadoc of `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` says "@return Stream of IDs" while the method returns a `Set<String>`. Since this interface is the contract other code relies on to pick the right check, the docs should name the correct methods/types.

title: No negative assertions for scope separation (view vs manage, membership) in the new group tests
body: The new test class only checks that granted scopes allow operations; it never asserts that a weaker scope does *not* grant a stronger one. In particular: after `createAllGroupsPermission(policy, Set.of(VIEW))` in `testViewGroups` there is no assertion that `groups().add(...)` is still 403 (which would have caught `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` granting on VIEW); `testManageGroupMembership` only verifies success after granting both the all-users `manage-group-membership` and the group `manage-membership` scope, never that joining is forbidden when only the user-side scope is present (so a `canManageMembership` that always returned true would pass); and there is no test that `view-members`/`manage-members` on all groups surfaces users in `GET /users` (which currently returns an empty list because resource UUIDs are used as group IDs). Please add these negative/combination cases.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients never receive the new Groups resource and scopes
body: `init()` returns early when `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient()` already exists, and the new `Groups` type-level resource plus the `manage-membership`/`manage-members`/`view-members` scopes are only created in that initialisation path. Realms whose admin-permissions client was created before this change therefore have no "Groups" resource and no group scopes. For them `getResourceTypeResource(..., "Groups")` returns null and `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission` then calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)` (NPE/500 on any group permission check), and creating a group permission fails in `getOrCreateResource` with `ModelException("No scopes found.")`. Even though the V2 feature is preview, some idempotent upgrade of the schema (create missing type resources/scopes when they are absent) is needed instead of the early return.

title: switch on resourceType throws NPE for null resource type
body: `getOrCreateResource` now does `switch (resourceType)` on a `String`. If `resourceType` is null (the previous code handled this by leaving `name` null and throwing the descriptive `IllegalStateException("Could not map resource object with type [null] ...")`), a `switch` on a null String throws a bare `NullPointerException`, which surfaces as a 500 instead of a meaningful validation error. Guard for null before the switch (or include it in the `default` branch).

title: manage-members cannot be used to create users under V2 because canCreateGroupMembers is gated on the V1 feature
body: `createUser` falls back to `canCreateGroupMembers(rep)` when the caller lacks the users `manage` permission, which is the path that lets an admin holding `manage-members`/`manage-membership` on a group create a user directly into that group. That method starts with `if (!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) return false;` (the V1 flag). With only `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` enabled (the configuration this PR targets, since both versions of the feature cannot be enabled together), the new `manage-members`/`manage-membership` group scopes added here can never be used to create users, contradicting the scope semantics documented in `GroupPermissionEvaluator`. The check should also accept the V2 feature.

title: canManage() in V2 is granted by the VIEW scope on all-groups
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW or AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE on the all-groups ("Groups") resource: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`. This is a copy of canView() and is wrong for a manage check (compare canManage(GroupModel), which only checks MANAGE, and UserPermissions.canManage(), which only checks the manage scope). The no-arg canManage()/requireManage() is what GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup uses, so an admin who was granted only `view` on all groups can create new top-level groups (and anything else gated on groups().requireManage()). The interface Javadoc for canManage() was written to match this ("permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups"), so the mistake propagated to the contract as well. Fix: evaluate only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE here and correct the Javadoc; add a test that a VIEW-only all-groups admin gets 403 on group creation.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects authz resource UUIDs instead of group IDs
body: In V2, group-specific authz resources are created with `name = group.getId()` (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource/resolveGroup), so the group ID is `groupResource.getName()`. This method instead passes `groupResource.getId()` (the Resource entity UUID) to hasPermission() and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the result set. The result is consumed by UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource as `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` and by UsersResource.getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds) as a membership filter. Concretely: findByType(server, "Groups") returns the type-level "Groups" resource; hasPermission(<uuid>) cannot find a resource by that name and falls back to the all-groups resource, so an admin that has an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission gets `{<uuid of Groups resource>}` as its group filter. The user search then filters by membership in a non-existent group and returns zero users, and the count endpoint returns 0, even though canViewMembers() would grant access to every group member. The method needs to use the resource name for group resources and treat the type-level "Groups" resource separately (it is not a group ID).

title: Per-object resources are created without a type, so findByType("Groups") never finds group resources
body: getOrCreateResource creates the per-group (and per-user/per-client) Resource with `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` and only updates scopes; it never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. Only the type-level resources created in init() get a type. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission relies on `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` to enumerate groups the admin may view members of, so with the current schema it can never discover any group-specific VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission. Consequences: UsersResource.getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds) receives an empty set and reports 0 users for an admin who, per the new GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers, can actually list those users; and the user search is not pre-filtered by group in the DB, so pagination (`first`/`max`) is applied before the per-user canView filter and pages can come back empty while matching users exist further on. Either set the type on created resources or do not rely on findByType in the V2 evaluator.

title: Null resource from getResourceTypeResource is dereferenced
body: hasPermission() does `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later `resource.getScopes()`. getResourceTypeResource has three explicit `return null` paths (admin permissions not enabled on the realm, resource server is not the admin-permissions client, or the type-level resource is missing). realmResourceServer() only requires `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient()` to be non-null, so if the realm flag is turned off while the client still exists, or the session context realm differs from the realm being evaluated, every group permission check for a non-role admin ends in a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of a deny. Guard the null and return false.

title: getResourceName does not handle the new Groups resource type
body: getResourceName maps resource names to human-readable values only for the USERS type ("All users" / username). The PR adds GROUPS but leaves this method unchanged, so for a group permission it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Group resources are created by getOrCreateResource without a display name (name = group ID, no displayName), so the API that lists the resources attached to a permission will return null names for group permissions, and the type-level "Groups" resource will not get an "All groups" label analogous to "All users". Add a GROUPS branch returning the group name/path (and a label for the type-level resource).

title: Incorrect Javadoc on several GroupPermissionEvaluator methods
body: requireManageMembers(GroupModel) is documented as "Throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false", but the implementation (GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers) checks canManageMembers(GroupModel) — a different scope (manage-members vs manage-membership). canManage() (lines 72-78) is documented as granted by "permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups", which describes a view check and must not be the contract of a manage method. getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() (line 145) says "@return Stream of IDs" but returns a Set<String>. Since these Javadocs are the only specification of the differing V1/V2 semantics, they should describe the intended behavior accurately.

title: Cleanup listener registration now depends on feature state at startup only
body: Previously the ProviderEventListener was always registered and `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` was evaluated per event. The change moves the check to registration time, so if the feature is enabled after the session factory has been initialized (the testing endpoint used by the legacy testsuite's `@EnableFeature(..., skipRestart = true)` does exactly this, and FeatureDeployerUtil does not re-run registerListener), the listener is never installed. Deleting a role, client or group then no longer calls management(...).setPermissionsEnabled(x, false), leaving orphaned authz Resource/Policy rows for the removed object. If this is intentional, the runtime feature-toggle path must re-register the listener.

title: Tests do not exercise the paths that are broken in GroupPermissionsV2
body: The new test class never asserts a negative after granting an all-groups VIEW permission (testViewGroups grants VIEW on all groups and only checks listing), so the privilege escalation in GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (VIEW grants group creation) goes undetected. There is no test with an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission followed by a user search or `users().count()`, which is the scenario where getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns resource UUIDs and the search returns no users. testManageGroupMembership (line 283) grants both the all-users MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP and the group MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP permission and only checks success; it never shows that the group-level permission is actually required (removing the group permission and expecting 403), so a no-op requireManageMembership would pass. Also missing: GET /groups/{id}/members with only VIEW_MEMBERS, and MANAGE_MEMBERS granting view of members. Please add these cases.

title: Exhausted recovery-code credential from user storage is "removed" via the local store, so it is never actually removed
body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` now returns the credential supplied by the user storage provider (`getFederatedCredentialsStream()`) in preference to the locally stored one. When `allCodesUsed()` is true the code still calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`, which only operates on Keycloak's own credential store (local DB / federated-user credential table), not on the external user storage. For a credential that lives in the user storage this either silently returns false (credential stays configured, `configuredFor()` stays true and the exhausted codes remain in the external store until the required action happens to overwrite them), or, if the provider did not populate an id on the returned `CredentialModel` (as the test provider's `createFromValues` path does), passes `null` to the JPA store and `em.find(..., null)` throws `IllegalArgumentException`, failing the login that just succeeded. The federated case should use `disableCredentialType(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)` (or be skipped) instead of `removeStoredCredentialById`.

title: Login form now parses user-storage credentials with Keycloak's internal JSON format and throws if a provider returns a plain CredentialModel
body: The bean now takes the first recovery-codes credential returned by `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials()` (via `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`) and feeds it to `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel()`, which `JsonSerialization.readValue`s `credentialData` and `secretData` into `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialData`/`RecoveryAuthnCodesSecretData`, then calls `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()`. `getCredentials()` was introduced so providers can list their credentials in the account console; nothing in that contract requires the model to carry Keycloak's internal hashed-code JSON. A provider that returns a `CredentialModel` with only id/type/label (or with its own data format) will now cause a NullPointerException/JSON parse exception while rendering the recovery-code login page, i.e. an HTTP 500 for every user of that provider who reaches the recovery-code step, where previously only local credentials were consulted. The new format requirement is also undocumented. Either guard the federated branch (fall back to code #1 / handle parse failures) or document that providers must return a model built with `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues`.

title: Storing new codes in user storage leaves a previously stored local recovery-codes credential intact and still valid
body: Before this change, recovery codes for federated users were always written via `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential`, which replaces the existing local credential of that type. Now, when `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` returns true (user storage took the codes), the local credential provider is never invoked, so any recovery-codes credential already stored in Keycloak's own store for that user (e.g. created before the storage provider added support for this type, or before upgrading) is left untouched. `SubjectCredentialManager.isValid()` validates against the user storage first and then falls through to the local `CredentialInputValidator`s, so the old local codes keep authenticating the user even though they believe they regenerated them, while the login form (`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`) only shows the state of the federated credential. When the user storage path succeeds, existing local credentials of type `recovery-authn-codes` should be removed as well.

title: User storage only receives raw codes; userLabel and generatedAt from the credential model are dropped and the payload format is undocumented
body: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` hands the user storage a `UserCredentialModel("", type, <JSON array of raw codes>)`. The `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` built in `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.processAction` (which carries the user-supplied label and the `generatedAt` timestamp) is only used on the local-DB branch, so a storage provider has no way to learn the label or creation time the user set (the test provider ends up with a `null` label). The shape of the challenge-response string (a JSON list of 12-char raw codes with dashes removed) is also not stated anywhere in the Javadoc, so implementers of `CredentialInputUpdater.updateCredential` for this type have to reverse-engineer it. Document the payload format and consider passing label/createdDate (e.g. via `UserCredentialModel` notes) so the storage can persist them.

title: getCredentials() dereferences getMyUser(user) without null check
body: Every other credential method in this provider (`getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isConfiguredFor`, `isValid`) guards against `getMyUser(user)` returning `null`, but the new `getCredentials` override immediately accesses `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp`. If the credential list is requested for a user that is no longer present in the in-memory map (e.g. account/admin listing after the user was removed from the storage but a stale `UserModel` is still being used), this throws a NullPointerException instead of returning an empty stream, and since `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` is now called from the login form bean and the recovery-code authenticator, the NPE would surface as a 500 during login rather than a graceful fallback.

title: Recovery codes stored in the test user storage can never be disabled/removed
body: The provider now stores recovery codes and reports them via `isConfiguredFor`/`getCredentials`, but `disableCredentialType` only handles OTP and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` never lists `recovery-authn-codes`. Consequently admin `disableCredentialType`, the account-console delete path (which falls back to `disableCredentialType` for federated credentials), and the exhausted-codes handling in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` have no way to clear recovery codes held in this storage, and the new tests cannot (and do not) cover removal of recovery codes from user storage, unlike the existing OTP tests (`testOTPSetupThroughAdminRESTAndLogin`, `testDisableCredentialsInUserStorage`). Add recovery codes to both methods and a test that disables them.

title: Overriding getCredentials() for OTP (plus generating an OTP id) changes what the existing OTP backwards-compatibility test exercises
body: This class is documented as a frozen 4.8.3-era provider used to prove old providers keep working. The PR adds `newOTP.setId(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())` and makes the new `getCredentials()` override return the OTP credential as well. `getCredentials()` is a defaulted method that an old provider would not implement, so after this change `testOTPSetupAndRemoveThroughAccountMgmtAndLogin` no longer exercises the legacy path where the account REST synthesizes the `otp-id` dummy credential (`CredentialHelper.createUserStorageCredentialRepresentation`) and deletes it via the `-id` suffix branch; it now goes through the real federated-credential listing instead. That legacy path loses its only coverage. Keep the OTP behaviour of the provider unchanged (return only recovery codes from `getCredentials`, or add a separate provider for the new feature) so both paths remain tested.

title: New test only covers the happy path of the user-storage branch
body: `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` sets up codes once and logs in once with code #0. It does not cover: (a) a federated user whose storage provider does not support `recovery-authn-codes`, which is the new fallback branch in `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential` that must still create the credential in the local DB (previously the only behaviour for federated users); (b) a second login to show which code number the form requests after one has been consumed, or an invalid code being rejected by the storage; (c) that regenerating codes replaces the previous set. Because the test provider's `isValid` accepts any stored code and `getCredentials` rebuilds a fresh model each time, the sequential/consumed-code semantics of the authenticator are effectively untested for the user-storage path. At minimum add a fallback-to-local test for a federated user and an invalid-code assertion.

title: Pre-existing local recovery-codes credential is left in place (and still valid) when the user storage accepts the new codes
body: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` and, if the user storage accepts it, never touches the local store. Recovery codes are a single-credential type: the local `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential` path replaces whatever credential of that type exists. With this helper, a federated user who already has a recovery-codes credential in the Keycloak DB (e.g. created before the storage started supporting this type, or after a storage upgrade) will keep it when regenerating codes. Because `UserCredentialManager.isValid` falls through to the local credential providers whenever the user storage's `isValid` returns false, the old locally stored codes remain usable for login indefinitely, and the admin/account UIs will show two recovery-code credentials. The helper should remove any existing local `recovery-authn-codes` credential when the storage path succeeds (or at least document that storages must handle this).

title: Local-store removal is applied to a credential that may come from the user storage
body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` now returns the federated credential (from `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`) in preference to the local one, but the follow-up logic is unchanged: when `allCodesUsed()` is true it calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. For a credential that lives in the external user storage this does not remove anything there (it targets the Keycloak-managed credential table), so the exhausted credential stays and `isConfiguredFor` keeps returning true. Worse, credential models produced by storages typically have no id (the test provider builds them via `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues`, which leaves `id` null), so `removeStoredCredentialById(null)` reaches `em.find(..., null)` and throws `IllegalArgumentException`, failing the login after the code was already validated. The federated case should call `disableCredentialType(...)` on the storage (or skip the removal) instead.

title: Login form hard-depends on storages returning recovery credentials in Keycloak's internal JSON format (or at all)
body: The bean (and `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` line 83) feeds whatever `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` returns straight into `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel`, which deserializes `credentialData`/`secretData` as `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialData`/`RecoveryAuthnCodesSecretData` and wraps any `IOException` in a `RuntimeException`. A user storage that accepted the codes via `updateCredential` (it receives them as a plain JSON array in `challengeResponse`) and exposes them in its own format, or that validates via `isValid`/`isConfiguredFor` but does not override `getCredentials`, will cause either a 500 while rendering the recovery-code login page or a `NoSuchElementException` from the unguarded `credentialModelOpt.get()`. This undocumented contract is only satisfied by the test provider because it re-hashes the raw codes with `createFromValues` in `getCredentials`. The code should handle an empty Optional/unparseable model gracefully (e.g. fall back to code number 0 or an error message) and the required storage contract should be documented.

title: User label and generation timestamp are dropped when the credential goes to the user storage
body: The `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` built in `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction` carries the user-supplied label and the `generatedAt` timestamp, but the `UserCredentialModel("", type, recoveryCodesJson)` handed to `updateCredential` only carries the raw codes. A storage therefore cannot preserve the label/creation time the user chose (the test provider ends up with `userLabel == null` and a storage-side timestamp), so the credential shown in the admin/account consoles for federated users differs from what the user entered.

title: Backwards-compatibility provider is extended with new-API code, defeating its purpose
body: The class Javadoc states this provider is a frozen Keycloak 4.8.3 implementation that must keep working without code changes, which is what `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest` is meant to prove.
