The `response.statusText !== "OK"` check is also unreliable, since HTTP/2 responses often have an empty statusText, and it should check `response.ok` instead.

title: Malformed payloads cause unhandled exceptions and 500s instead of 400s
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on bad input (line 31), and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on wrong key or bad ciphertext or non-JSON plaintext (line 57). Neither is caught, so the request returns a generic 500 and the error may leak. These should be safeParse with a 400 response, and decryption failures should be handled explicitly.

title: Webhook secret is compared with a non-constant-time string comparison
body: The shared secret is checked with `!==`, which leaks timing information. A constant-time comparison such as `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers should be used for a shared-secret check.

title: HubSpot refresh reads `expiresIn` from the sync-mode Response, producing NaN expiry
body: In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch Response, so `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` is undefined and `expiryDate` becomes NaN. The stored token's expiry is then corrupted, so the token-validity check behaves incorrectly.

title: Zoho refresh reads `.data` and `.error` from the sync-mode Response object
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch Response in sync mode, so `tokenInfo.data` is undefined and `tokenInfo.data.error` throws a TypeError. Zoho Bigin token refresh therefore fails whenever credential sync is enabled. The same mismatch affects zohocrm/_CalendarService.ts.

title: Zoom expiry becomes NaN when the sync-mode response lacks `expires_in`
body: `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000)` assumes `expires_in` is present. The sync-mode minimal parse does not guarantee it. If it's undefined, expiry_date is NaN, and `isTokenValid` (`NaN < Date.now()` is false) never reports the token expired, so Zoom tokens are never refreshed again.

title: No tests for the new sync and refresh behaviour despite touching ~20 OAuth refresh paths
body: The PR adds a shared refresh path (`refreshOAuthTokens`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) and a webhook endpoint, and the description admits no tests were added. The bugs above (wrong schema keys, wrapper stored as key, missing import, Response vs token mismatch) would each have been caught by a unit test on these helpers.

title: Team admin check requires both admin and owner, so admins are denied
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. A user must be both a team admin and a team owner to pass. A plain team admin, or a plain owner, who is not also the other role is rejected with FORBIDDEN. The intended check is almost certainly `||`. Team admins and owners who are not the organizer cannot add guests as the feature intends.

title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive while the blacklist is lowercased
body: The blacklist entries are lowercased (line 71), but the incoming `guest` is compared as-is (line 77: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). An email such as `Spam@Example.com` will not match a blacklisted `spam@example.com`, so blacklisted addresses can be added by changing case. Emails should be normalized (lowercased) before both the blacklist check and the duplicate check.

title: Duplicate emails within one request are not removed before insert
body: `uniqueGuests` only filters out emails that already exist as attendees and blacklisted addresses. It does not deduplicate the `guests` array itself. A request containing the same address twice (or differing only by case) will create two attendee rows via `createMany`, and the calendar and email fan-out will also double up. The dialog validates uniqueness, but the API does not enforce it.

title: Database write happens before calendar update with no rollback
body: The attendees are persisted with `prisma.booking.update` (line 92) before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs (line 165). If the calendar update throws, the guests remain in the database but are missing from the calendar, and the caller gets an error. A retry then filters those guests out as existing attendees and returns BAD_REQUEST `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which is misleading and leaves the calendar permanently out of sync.

title: Email failure is swallowed with no error details logged
body: The catch block logs only the static string "Error sending AddGuestsEmails" and discards the `err` object, so the actual failure cause is lost. It should log the error (e.g. via the project logger with the error and booking id).

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails event-type metadata
body: Every other send function in this file gates host and attendee emails with `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` and accepts `eventTypeMetadata` or the disable flags. `sendAddGuestsEmails` has no such parameter and always emails the organizer, team members and attendees. Organizers who disabled standard emails for the event type will still receive these notifications.

title: Fallback error message is unreachable
body: `message` is built as a template string containing `err.data?.code` and `t(err.message)`, so it is always truthy. The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback never runs, and the toast will show something like `undefined: ...` when `err.data` is missing. The fallback logic should check the raw values before interpolation.

title: Hardcoded English tooltip text bypasses i18n
body: The tooltip content `"Remove email"` is a literal string, while every other user-facing label in this component and the dialog goes through `t()`. Non-English users will see English text, and the component already has `useLocale` available.

title: Label references an id that is not present in the DOM
body: The `<label htmlFor="emails">` points to an element id `emails` that is never rendered, so the label is not associated with any input. Screen readers and label-click behaviour are therefore broken for this field.

title: No limit on number of guests or input normalization
body: `guests` is an unbounded array of emails with no max length, and emails are not trimmed or lowercased at the schema level. This allows arbitrarily large requests that each trigger calendar updates and one email per attendee, and it is the root cause of the case-sensitivity and duplicate issues above.

title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, so a user must be both admin and owner to pass. A team admin who is not the owner, or a team owner who is not an admin, is denied, and the OR-style permission intent in the name is not implemented. The check should be `||`.

title: Calendar attendees are updated with the requester's credentials, not the organizer's
body: The `EventManager` is built from `ctx.user` and that user's credentials (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`). Any authorized actor (a team admin, or an attendee) triggers the calendar update through their own calendar, while the event lives on the organizer's calendar. The update should use the booking organizer's user and credentials, which are already loaded as `booking.user`.

title: Duplicate emails within the input are not removed and get inserted twice
body: `uniqueGuests` only filters out emails that already exist as attendees and blacklisted emails. If the `guests` array contains the same address twice (the schema does not enforce uniqueness, and the dialog check is client-side only), both copies are passed to `createMany`, creating duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails.

title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive while the blacklist is lowercased
body: The blacklist entries are lowercased on line 71, but `guest` is compared as-is on line 77. An input like `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses a blacklist entry `blocked@example.com`. Email comparison should be normalized on both sides.

title: Attendees are persisted before calendar update, with no rollback on failure
body: The attendee rows are written to the database (lines 92-106), then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs outside any try/catch (line 165). If the calendar call throws, the mutation fails with an error, but the guests are already saved, so the UI reports failure while the data has changed and the calendar is out of sync. The DB write and calendar update need to be reconciled or the calendar error handled.

title: Email sending receives raw input instead of the filtered guest list
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the original `guests` input rather than `uniqueGuests`. Guests who were already attendees are classified as new and receive the 'you are scheduled' email. Blacklisted or duplicate addresses are also passed through, and the function treats them as new guests.

title: Email failures are swallowed with no error detail logged
body: The `catch` logs only the static string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' and discards `err`, so the actual failure is lost. It also uses `console.log` instead of the project logger used elsewhere in this codebase.

title: Any existing attendee can add arbitrary guests to a booking
body: The authorization check allows any booking attendee (matched by session email) to add guests, with no restriction on booking status or time. Cancelled or past bookings are also not excluded. Each addition triggers emails to the organizer, team members and all attendees, which allows spam or abuse of the booking's recipient list. The permission model should be confirmed and restricted to the organizer and admins if attendees should not have this capability.

title: No limit on the number of guests per request
body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no max length and no uniqueness constraint. A single call can insert and email an unbounded number of addresses, which is an abuse and cost vector for the email provider.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails event-type metadata
body: Every other send function in this file gates host and attendee emails with `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` and the `hostEmailDisabled` / `attendeeEmailDisabled` flags. This function takes neither and always sends to organizer, team members and attendees. Hosts who disabled standard emails on the event type will still receive these notifications.

title: Subject uses attendees[0].name, which is often empty for new guests
body: New guests are created with `name: ""`. If the first attendee in the list is a newly added guest, the subject is built with an empty name (e.g. 'Guests Added: X with  at ...'). The subject should use the organizer or the booking's primary attendee.

title: Recipient header is malformed when attendee name is empty
body: `to` is built as `${this.attendee.name} <${this.attendee.email}>`. Guests are created with an empty name, which produces ' <guest@example.com>' with a leading space and no display name. Falling back to the bare email when the name is empty would avoid this.

title: Hardcoded English tooltip text bypasses i18n
body: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` is a literal string, while the rest of the component uses `t(...)`. Non-English users see English text, and the project's translation pipeline does not cover it.

title: Closing the dialog via overlay or Escape does not reset the entered emails
body: Only the Cancel button resets `multiEmailValue` and `isInvalidEmail`. Dismissing via `onOpenChange` (overlay click, Escape) keeps the previous input and the validation error, so the next open shows stale state.

title: Fallback in error toast is dead code
body: `message` is a template string that always contains the separator, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never falls back. The intended fallback is never shown on errors with no code.

title: Team admin check uses && with isTeamOwner, so only users who are both admin and owner pass
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. A team admin who is not the owner, or an owner who is not an admin, fails this check. The name says "admin or owner", so this should be `||`. As written, team admins who are not owners get FORBIDDEN unless they are also attendees or the organizer.

title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive while the blacklist is lowercased
body: The blacklist is built with `.toLowerCase()`, but the guest is compared as-is with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. An input such as `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses a blacklist entry `blocked@example.com`. The attendee duplicate check on line 76 is also case-sensitive, so the same address in a different case can be added as a second attendee.

title: Duplicate guests within the same request are not removed server-side
body: `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing attendees and the blacklist. If `guests` contains the same address twice (the schema in addGuests.schema.ts does not enforce uniqueness, and the client-side check can be bypassed), both rows go into `createMany` and the booking gets duplicate attendee rows, which then produce duplicate invites and emails.

title: Calendar update failure after DB write leaves guests added but reports an error
body: The attendees are persisted at line 92 before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs at line 165, which is not wrapped in try/catch. If the calendar update throws, the client gets an error and the dialog stays open, yet the guests are already saved in the database. A retry then hits the 'no unique guests' path. The DB write and calendar sync are not atomic, and the failure mode is not handled.

title: Email failure is swallowed with a bare console.log and no error detail
body: The catch block logs only the fixed string "Error sending AddGuestsEmails" and discards `err`, so the cause of email failures is lost. Other code in the repo uses the logger for this. Consider logging the error through the shared logger.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores eventType disableStandardEmails settings
body: Every other send function in this file checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` (or the hostEmailDisabled flags) before sending. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no event type metadata and always emails the organizer, team members, and all attendees. Hosts who disabled standard emails will still receive these notifications.

title: Subject uses attendees[0] name, which is empty for newly added guests
body: New guests are created with `name: ""`, and the organizer email subject in organizer-add-guests-email.ts uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. If the first attendee is a newly added guest, or the existing first attendee has no name, the subject is rendered with a blank name. The subject-building logic should fall back to a sensible value, such as the organizer name or the attendee email.

title: Invalid-email error is never cleared after a later valid submit
body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on a failed validation, but it is reset only by the Cancel button. After the user fixes the emails and clicks Add, the mutation runs and the stale error message stays visible, including after a successful add (onSuccess at line 36 does not reset it).

title: Hardcoded English tooltip text bypasses i18n
body: The remove-button tooltip is the literal string "Remove email", while the surrounding labels all go through `t()`. Non-English users will see English text here.

title: Error message concatenates the tRPC error code into the toast
body: The toast message is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, so users see text like "FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission". Also `t()` is called on raw server message keys such as `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which may not exist in every locale. The fallback `t("unable_to_add_guests")` is effectively unreachable because the template string is always truthy.

title: Retry counter is a read-modify-write on a stale value
body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` writes a value computed from the row read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap (or a manual call runs alongside the cron), both read the same count and both write count+1, so a failure is lost and the reminder takes longer to reach the deletion threshold. Prisma supports an atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`, which avoids this. The same pattern is used in the catch block at line 195.

title: Unguarded update in catch block can abort the whole cron loop
body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the catch block (line 190) sits outside any try. If it throws (for example the reminder was deleted by the preceding deleteMany or by a concurrent request, which makes Prisma raise P2025), the exception propagates out of the `for` loop. Every remaining unscheduled reminder in that run is then skipped and the handler returns an error. One bad row can stall the whole batch on each cron run. The update should be wrapped in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany`, which does not throw when no row matches.

title: Failure after a successful Twilio schedule increments retry and can cause duplicate SMS
body: If `twilio.scheduleSMS` succeeds but the following `prisma.workflowReminder.update` (setting scheduled/referenceId, line 169) throws, control goes to the catch block. That block increments retryCount and leaves `scheduled` false. On the next run the same reminder is scheduled with Twilio again, so the attendee can receive the same SMS twice. The retry counter now makes this path more visible. The success-side update and the failure bookkeeping should not be conflated, or the reminder should be checked for an existing referenceId before rescheduling.

title: retryCount deletion clause is not scoped to SMS or to unscheduled reminders
body: The new `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` branch of the OR matches any WorkflowReminder regardless of `method` or `scheduled`. Only the SMS path increments retryCount today, so the effect is currently limited. But a future email or WhatsApp retry path would have its reminders deleted by this SMS-cleanup job. Adding `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and `scheduled: false` to that branch would make the intent explicit and safe.

title: Comment describes only the date-based deletion
body: The comment on line 28 says the job deletes SMS reminders whose scheduled date has passed. The deleteMany now also deletes reminders after two failed attempts (`retryCount > 1`), which is the behaviour the PR is about. The comment is now misleading. The magic threshold `1` is also duplicated in no named constant, so its meaning ('deleted after the second failure') is not documented anywhere.

title: No tests for the new retry and deletion behaviour
body: The PR changes retry bookkeeping, the deletion threshold and the error path, but adds no unit or integration tests. Nothing verifies that a reminder is deleted after exactly two failures, that a successful schedule does not increment the counter, or that the catch path behaves correctly. The existing handler has no test coverage here, so regressions in this logic would go unnoticed.

title: Cleanup deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1, including already-scheduled and non-SMS ones
body: The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: SMS`, no `scheduled: false`, and no date filter. It matches any WorkflowReminder with retryCount >= 2. retryCount is only incremented on failure, but a row that failed twice and later succeeded keeps its count, and the success path (lines ~169-177) sets `scheduled: true` and `referenceId` without resetting it. Such a row is still deleted by this cron. The Twilio message stays queued, but the DB row holding `referenceId` is gone, so a later booking cancellation or reschedule can no longer cancel the SMS. Email reminders are also swept up. Fix: scope the retry clause to `method: SMS, scheduled: false`, and/or reset retryCount on success.

title: Unguarded DB update in catch block can abort the whole cron loop
body: The catch block now runs `prisma.workflowReminder.update` without its own try/catch. If that update throws (e.g. the row was deleted concurrently by a booking cancellation, which makes Prisma throw P2025, or a transient DB error), the exception escapes the `for` loop. All remaining unscheduled reminders in the batch are skipped for this run, and the handler returns an error. One bad row can therefore block every other reminder. Wrap the increment in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany` with a `where` that tolerates missing rows.

title: retryCount incremented from a stale in-memory value instead of atomically
body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` uses the value read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap (the scheduler is not guarded by a lock here), both read the same count and both write count+1, so failures are under-counted and the reminder can be retried more times than the intended limit. Using Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` avoids this.

title: No tests for the new retry/deletion behaviour
body: The PR changes what gets scheduled, retried and deleted (threshold `gt: 1`, increment on both failure paths, new cleanup clause), but adds no tests for the retry count sequence, the deletion threshold, or the interaction with already-scheduled reminders. The bug above would have been caught by a test of a reminder that fails once and then succeeds.

title: Unguarded update in catch block can abort the whole cron run
body: The new retry increment in the catch block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If the Prisma update fails (DB blip, connection issue, or the reminder was deleted concurrently, which makes update throw P2025), the exception escapes the for-loop and the handler. Every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped for this run, and the request fails. One bad reminder should not block the others. Wrap the update, or use updateMany, which does not throw on zero matches.

title: Retry counter is a read-modify-write on a stale value
body: The count is computed as `reminder.retryCount + 1` from the value read at the start of the run (lines 184 and 195). If two cron invocations overlap, or the value changed since the findMany, increments are lost and the reminder can keep retrying past the intended limit. Use an atomic update such as `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`.

title: retryCount deletion clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The OR branch `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` has no `method` filter, so it deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method, and regardless of whether it is scheduled. The SMS-only intent of this job is lost. Today only the SMS path increments retryCount, so this is latent, but any future increment elsewhere would delete unrelated email or WhatsApp reminders. Scope the condition to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and `scheduled: false`.

title: Unindexed retryCount filter runs on every cron invocation
body: The new `retryCount > 1` predicate runs inside deleteMany on every cron tick. The migration adds no index on retryCount, and the existing WorkflowReminder indexes do not cover it, so this OR branch forces a scan of the WorkflowReminder table on each run. Consider an index or a narrower predicate.

title: Reminders with no message are retried forever and never counted
body: Retry counting only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)` (the else branch at line 178) and in the catch. If the message is empty or sendTo is missing, neither path increments retryCount, so the reminder stays unscheduled and is reconsidered on every run indefinitely. This is the same unbounded retry the PR is meant to stop. Such reminders should also count as failures or be removed.

title: Retry limit semantics are not documented and the threshold is off-by-one in appearance
body: The code deletes when retryCount > 1, so a reminder gets two failed attempts before deletion. The PR description says 'after scheduling failed twice we delete', which matches, but the `gt: 1` threshold reads like 'delete on the second failure' to a maintainer. Neither the code nor the description makes the limit a named constant, so the intent is easy to get wrong when changed.

title: No tests for the retry and deletion behavior
body: The PR changes cron behavior (retry increment on failure, deletion after the limit, the new catch-path update) but adds no tests. Nothing verifies that a failed Twilio schedule increments the counter, that a reminder is deleted after the limit, or that a thrown error does not stop the loop.

title: Public findMany() removed from InsightsBookingService without a replacement for callers
body: The diff deletes `findMany(findManyArgs)`, which executed the scoped query against `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized`, and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a SQL fragment. Any caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` will fail to compile or run after this change. The PR description says only the integration tests were updated and does not mention this removal, so the breaking change is undocumented. The PR should either keep a query-executing method or confirm that no callers remain in the repo.

title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions because authConditions is always truthy
body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object (never null or undefined), so `authConditions` is always truthy. The `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches are therefore only reachable in the `authConditions` falsy case, which cannot happen. The code is misleading: a reader would assume the NOTHING_CONDITION fallback applies when there are no filters and no auth, but in that situation the auth fragment (`1=0`) is returned through the first branch. The logic should be simplified to make the actual behavior explicit.

title: Caching tests deleted with no replacement
body: The `Caching` describe block ("should cache authorization conditions" and "should cache filter conditions") is removed entirely. The service still memoizes `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, so this behavior is now untested. The PR description does not mention removing these tests. They should be restored, adjusted to the Sql format, or the removal should be justified.

title: Final integration test asserts exact row set against a shared table without scoping to test data
body: The `$queryRaw` test runs `SELECT id FROM "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" WHERE ${baseConditions}` and expects `toEqual([{ id: userBooking.id }])`. The query is not restricted to the test's own data, so any other booking in the database that matches the user scope and event type (leftover data or parallel tests) makes the assertion fail. The original test used `toHaveLength(1)` against the service result. The assertion should be scoped to the created IDs or check membership instead of exact equality.

title: Tests assert exact SQL fragment structure, making them brittle and weakly behavioral
body: Most authorization and filter tests compare `Prisma.sql` objects with `toEqual` against full SQL template literals, including whitespace-sensitive parameter arrays and operator ordering. These tests fail on any cosmetic change to the SQL and do not verify that the conditions select the right rows. The behavioral check is limited to one test that executes the query. The PR description says the tests were copied from the routing service, but this brittle pattern should not be propagated without a database-backed check of each scope.

title: Public findMany method removed and return types changed without updating callers
body: The `findMany` method was removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions`, and `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` now return `Prisma.Sql` instead of `BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput`. The constructor's `options` type was also widened. Any consumer that called `service.findMany(...)` or consumed the object-shaped conditions will fail to compile or silently change behavior. Neither the diff nor the PR description shows updated callers, so the PR cannot be merged safely without auditing usages across the repo.

title: Caching tests deleted without replacement
body: The entire `describe("Caching")` block (tests 'should cache authorization conditions' and 'should cache filter conditions') was removed in this PR. The service still caches `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` and that behavior is not tested anywhere now. The PR description does not mention removing these tests.

title: Final test no longer exercises the service's findMany path and runs against an unverified table
body: The former `findMany` integration test, which exercised the real service entry point, was replaced with a hand-written `$queryRaw` that selects from "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" using the conditions. This test no longer verifies anything the service itself returns, and it depends on the denormalized table/view being populated for the inserted booking (the booking is created directly in Booking, so the denormalized row must be produced by a trigger or sync). If that sync is absent in the test DB the assertion `toEqual([{id}])` fails, and if it is present the test silently depends on it. The test should document or set up that dependency.

title: Array-ordering assertions depend on unspecified query order
body: The org scope test expects `teamId = ANY` and `userId = ANY` arrays in a specific order (org, team, team2, team3). Those arrays come from `findAllByParentId` and `findAllByTeamIds`, which have no ORDER BY guarantee, so `toEqual` on the Prisma.Sql values can fail nondeterministically. Sorting before comparison or using an order-insensitive matcher would make the test stable.

title: Public findMany() method removed without replacement
body: The diff deletes `InsightsBookingService.findMany()` and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment rather than running a query. Any existing caller of `findMany` on this class will fail to compile or break at runtime. The PR description only mentions test changes and never mentions this API removal, so it is unclear whether callers were checked or migrated.

title: Caching tests deleted with no replacement
body: The `Caching` describe block (tests for `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` memoization) is removed entirely rather than ported to the new Sql format. The service still caches via `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, so this behavior is now untested.

title: Org-scope test compares ordered arrays whose order is not guaranteed
body: The expected Sql embeds `[org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` and `[user, user2, user3]` in a fixed order, but the service builds these from repository query results (`findAllByParentId`, `findAllByTeamIds`) with no ORDER BY. Because the test compares the full SQL including parameter values, it may fail or flake when the database returns rows in a different order.

title: Final test runs raw SQL against the denormalized table without the tests having been run
body: The PR itself states the integration tests were not run because of runner configuration problems. The new `$queryRaw` test hardcodes the table name `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` and quoted camelCase column names, and nothing confirms these match the schema or that the result shape `{ id }` is correct. A failure here would be unverified.

title: PR description misstates the scope of the change
body: The title and description describe a test-only update that 'works with the new Prisma.sql format that was previously converted in the service implementation'. The diff actually converts the service from Prisma object filters to Prisma.sql, removes findMany, changes the constructor option type, and alters team/org condition behavior (empty user lists are now omitted rather than producing `IN []`). None of this is called out, so reviewers may not assess the behavioral change.

title: Cache status is not refreshed after deleting cached data
body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation, it does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. Unless the parent happens to pass an onSuccess that refetches, `cacheUpdatedAt` stays on screen after a successful delete, so the 'Cache Status' line keeps showing a timestamp for data that no longer exists.

title: Timestamp is always formatted in en-US, ignoring the user's locale
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` hardcodes the locale even though the component uses `useLocale()` for every other string. Users on other locales see an English date format inside a localized sentence. The locale from `useLocale` should be passed instead.

title: Comment on updatedAt is inaccurate and @updatedAt has broader effects than described
body: The comment says the default is for 'legacy rows and future raw inserts', but the field's purpose is to track the last cache write. `@updatedAt` makes Prisma stamp the column on every client update, which is what the feature relies on, and the comment does not say so. Also, the migration's `DEFAULT NOW()` gives every pre-existing cache row the migration time as its 'last updated' value, so the UI will show a misleading timestamp for legacy entries. This is not documented.

title: Every cache refresh issues an unconditional UPDATE on all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential
body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` runs with an empty data object on every `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`. It rewrites `updatedAt` on all selected calendars for the credential, including ones unrelated to the cache, and the PR notes say nothing in the frontend reads that value. This adds write load on a hot path for no functional gain. It should be removed, or the cache status should be read from CalendarCache, which it already is.

title: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS-only and fails on Linux
body: The in-place edit uses `sed -i ''`, which GNU sed treats as a filename argument, so the script errors out on Linux and in CI containers. The script also hard-codes `../.env` relative to the working directory and does not check that `tmole` is installed before using it. It is also unrelated to the cache feature this PR is about.

title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx without tsx being declared as a dependency
body: `npx tsx` downloads tsx on demand if it isn't installed, and the version is unpinned, so the script behaves differently across machines. This change is also unrelated to the calendar cache feature and is not mentioned in the PR's review checklist.

title: No tests for the new deleteCache mutation or the cache-status enrichment
body: The authorization check (credential must belong to the caller) and the deletion of CalendarCache rows are new security-relevant behavior, but no unit or integration test covers them. Nor is there a test for `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` or for the `cacheUpdatedAt` mapping in `connectedCalendarsHandler`. The PR's test plan is manual only.

title: Remove-app behavior changed for the error-state alert without being called out
body: Previously the error-state alert showed the disconnect button whenever there was no delegationCredentialId. Now `canDisconnect` also requires `!disableConnectionModification`, and the error path also gets the cache dropdown. This is a behavior change that is not described in the PR summary and is not covered by the test plan.

title: Deleting cache does not refresh the connected calendars query, so the cache status stays stale
body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the parent's onSuccess callback. It never invalidates `trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, which is the query that supplies `cacheUpdatedAt`. Unless the parent happens to refetch, the dropdown keeps showing the old 'Last updated' timestamp after the cache is deleted. The disconnect mutation does invalidate that query in onSettled, so the two flows are inconsistent.

title: Cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded en-US locale instead of the user's locale
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the locale already available from `useLocale()`. Users with other locales see English-formatted dates, which is inconsistent with the rest of the translated UI.

title: updateManyByCredentialId with empty data is used as a write on every cache refresh
body: CalendarService.fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {})` on every cache refresh. Because SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is `@updatedAt`, this issues an UPDATE over every selected calendar of the credential, including event-type-scoped rows, just to bump a timestamp. The PR notes say this field is not displayed in the frontend and may be unnecessary. It adds write load to the hot refresh path and to unwatch flows without a clear consumer.

title: Unconditional SelectedCalendar bulk update added to cache refresh path
body: The new `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` runs after every cache population, including the remaining-calendars refresh in unwatchCalendar. It writes to every SelectedCalendar row for the credential even though the value is not used by any consumer in this PR. If it stays, it should at least be justified, or it should be scoped to the rows that actually changed.

title: updatedAt relies on Prisma @updatedAt, which raw SQL writes will not touch
body: CalendarCache.updatedAt is declared with `@default(now()) @updatedAt`, so it is only maintained by Prisma client writes. Any raw SQL or bulk update path will leave it stale, and the UI status would then be wrong. The comment mentions 'future raw inserts' but does not address raw updates.

title: Migration header warning contradicts the SQL that follows
body: The header says adding a required column without a default is not possible on a non-empty table, and the SQL then adds it with `DEFAULT NOW()`. The header describes a situation the migration avoids, which is misleading for future maintainers. It should be updated or removed.

title: No tests cover the new deleteCache handler or the cache status repository method
body: The authorization check (credential must belong to user) and the cache deletion are untested, as is the new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groupBy and the enrichment in connectedCalendarsHandler. The PR's own checklist relies on manual E2E testing, which is not a substitute for regression tests on an access-control path.

title: UserWithCalendars type now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId
body: The Pick types for allSelectedCalendars and userLevelSelectedCalendars gained two required fields. Any existing caller that builds a UserWithCalendars object without those fields, including platform-libraries consumers of this exported type, will fail type-checking. This is a silent contract change unrelated to the feature.

title: Session user query now exposes googleChannelId to the session payload
body: findUnlockedUserForSession is used to build the session. The change adds googleChannelId (and updatedAt) to the selected calendars. This value is a Google push-channel identifier that is not needed for the session and should not be broadly serialized. The change is unrelated to the cache feature and widens the data exposed through the session.

title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx, but tsx is not a declared dependency
body: The script now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`. tsx is not listed in apps/web devDependencies, so `npx` will fetch it at runtime, which is non-deterministic and depends on network and registry state. The change is also unrelated to the calendar cache feature and is not mentioned in the title. It should be a separate PR, with tsx added as a pinned devDependency if it is needed.

title: Rate-limit path exits with status 0 and sed -i is not portable
body: cleanup() always ends with `exit 0`, so the rate-limit branch and the 'Failed to extract URL' branch both report success to the caller. Also, `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS syntax and fails on GNU/Linux, where the script would error when updating ENV_FILE. The script also writes to ../.env relative to the CWD. The script is unrelated to the feature and is undocumented.

title: Cache deletion does not refresh the cache status shown in the UI
body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the parent onSuccess, and the parent is onChanged. Nothing invalidates `trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike the disconnect mutation, which does invalidate it in onSettled. The `cacheUpdatedAt` shown in the dropdown therefore stays at the old timestamp after the cache is deleted, until some unrelated refetch happens. The PR test plan explicitly requires that the UI updates after deletion.

title: No tests for the new deleteCache handler or cache status repository method
body: deleteCacheHandler performs an authorization check (credential must belong to the user) and a destructive deleteMany, and getCacheStatusByCredentialIds uses a groupBy with _max. Neither is covered by any test in the PR. The authorization path in particular should have a test that a user cannot delete another user's credential cache.

title: updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data on every cache refresh, bumping updatedAt for all calendars
body: CalendarService.fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache (line 1024 of the service diff) calls updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}) on every cache population. Because SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is @updatedAt, this rewrites updatedAt on every selected calendar under the credential, including event-type-scoped ones, on each refresh. The PR notes say this value is not displayed in the frontend, so the write is unused load and a misleading timestamp. The method also has no guard against an empty update, and the SelectedCalendar.updatedAt change is only justified in the notes, not in code.

title: Comment says CalendarCache has no updatedAt, which this PR now adds
body: The TODO above the findFirst orderBy says updatedAt 'doesn't exist yet' in the CalendarCache table. This PR adds that column, so the comment is now wrong and misleads future readers about whether updatedAt can be used for ordering.

title: Timestamp is hardcoded to en-US instead of the user's locale
body: The cache timestamp is formatted with Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) even though the rest of the component is localized via useLocale. Users with other locales see an English date format next to translated labels. The locale from useLocale should be used.

title: sed -i '' syntax is macOS-only and breaks on Linux
body: The script updates GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL with `sed -i '' -E ...`. The empty argument after -i is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed (Linux, many CI/dev containers) the empty string is treated as the script and the command fails, so the .env file is not updated. The script is not portable and nothing in the PR documents that it is macOS-only.

title: deleteCache does not check the credential's app type before deleting cache rows
body: The handler only verifies that the credential belongs to the user, then deletes all calendarCache rows with that credentialId. It does not check that the credential is a calendar credential, and the UI only offers the action for Google Calendar. A direct tRPC call can clear cache rows for any owned credential. This is low impact but inconsistent with the UI's restriction.

title: Cache deletion stays available when connection modification is disabled, and the Alert branch now gates on it
body: The previous code hid the remove button whenever disableConnectionModification was set. The new dropdown still shows the 'Delete cached data' action in that case, because canDisconnect is separate from hasCache. Meanwhile the error Alert branch (line 124) now also passes disableConnectionModification, which it did not check before. The intended permission model for these two actions is not stated or tested.

title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx, which is unrelated to this feature and not declared as a dependency
body: This change replaces ts-node with `npx tsx` for dev:cron, but tsx is not declared in this package's dependencies. npx will fetch it at runtime, which can be slow or fail offline. The change is unrelated to calendar cache management and should be split into its own PR.

title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation batch and skips DB cleanup
body: The cancellation loop runs inside a single try block. The query at lines 44-51 does not filter on referenceId or scheduled, so a cancelled reminder that was never scheduled in SendGrid (referenceId null) is sent to /v3/user/scheduled_sends with batch_id null, which throws. The catch then exits the loop, so every later reminder in the batch is not cancelled in this run and is still sent. Also, the prisma.workflowReminder.delete promises already pushed to workflowRemindersToDelete are never awaited because the Promise.all at line 74 is skipped, so rows for reminders that were successfully cancelled are not deleted. Each cancellation should be handled individually and the query should filter on referenceId not null.

title: Cancellations requested close to send time can still be delivered
body: The cron only picks up cancelled reminders when scheduledDate is within the next hour and it runs every 15 minutes. A reminder cancelled shortly before its send time (e.g. 10 minutes out) will not be picked up until the next cron run, which can be after the email has already been sent by SendGrid. The window or the cron interval should be tightened, or the cancellation should also be applied immediately when the send time is near.

title: Non-immediate cancel only flags the row, so the SendGrid email is not cancelled now
body: For reminders that already have a referenceId and are not immediateDelete, the function only sets cancelled=true. The SendGrid scheduled send is left untouched until the cron job runs, which may be up to 15+ minutes later and can be after the reminder time. Any caller that expects a cancelled booking to stop emails (handleCancelBooking, bookings.tsx requestReschedule, workflows.tsx step/event-type edits) is therefore relying on the cron timing, and this is not reflected in those call sites.

title: Commented-out testAction block has mismatched comment delimiters, leaving live code that references undefined identifiers
body: The `*/` at the end of line 901 closes the outer `/* testAction` comment that starts at line 848, and the `/*) {` on the same line opens a new comment that is closed only at line 1010. The code between (lines 902-967) is therefore live but refers to identifiers that are no longer imported in this file (dayjs, BookingInfo, getErrorFromUnknown). The `if (` on line 964 is also left without a body. This is unrelated to the PR's reminder logic, and the reindent in this diff makes the hazard harder to see. The block should be properly commented out or removed.

title: Prisma import is now unused
body: After removing deleteReminderPromise, `Prisma` (line 9) is no longer referenced in this file, which will trip lint/typecheck with unused-import rules. The value-style import of the type-only `PrismaPromise` is also inconsistent with the rest of the file.

title: Unrelated UI restructuring changes rendering for SMS_ATTENDEE steps
body: The wrapper condition changed from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded, and the phone block now renders its own container. This is not part of the stated reminder cancellation fix. For SMS_ATTENDEE steps, the previously rendered padded wrapper is now gone, a visible change that is not described or tested.

title: New cancelled column is nullable with no default
body: The column is added as nullable with no default, so existing and newly created rows carry NULL rather than false. Queries and code that treat the flag as a boolean (`cancelled: true` filter, and the schema type Boolean?) must now handle three states. A NOT NULL column with default false would avoid this ambiguity.

title: No tests cover the new cancellation flow
body: The PR changes reminder cancellation semantics across the cron job, booking cancel, reschedule, and workflow edit/delete paths, but adds no tests. There is no coverage for a cancelled reminder that is not yet scheduled, a batch with one failing cancel, or the cancel-within-one-hour window. These are the scenarios that caused the original bug.

title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation batch and blocks it on every run
body: The loop at lines 56-73 awaits `client.request` for each cancelled reminder inside a single try block. If the request throws for one reminder (for example SendGrid rejects a batch that was already sent or no longer exists), the exception skips every remaining reminder in `remindersToCancel`, and the catch only logs. Those reminders keep `cancelled: true` and are never cancelled or deleted. The query always returns the same ordered set, so the failing reminder is hit first again on the next 15-minute run and the rest stay stuck indefinitely. One bad row can therefore stop all cancellations, which is the same failure mode this PR is meant to fix. Each reminder should be cancelled in its own try/catch so that failures are isolated and the row is retried or logged individually.

title: Cancellation of reminders due within the next hour is deferred and can still send
body: For a cancelled booking, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is called without `immediateDelete`, so it only sets `cancelled = true`. The actual SendGrid cancel happens in the cron job, which runs every 15 minutes and only picks up reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour. If a booking is cancelled 5 minutes before a reminder is due, and the cron last ran before the cancellation, the email can be sent before the next cron run actually cancels it. The same deferred path is used by the reschedule flow in bookings.tsx. Reminders whose `scheduledDate` is inside the cron window at cancellation time should be cancelled immediately in SendGrid, and only the rest should be deferred.

title: Paid booking cancellation returns before workflow reminders are cancelled
body: The `if (bookingToDelete.paid)` branch refunds the payment, marks the booking REJECTED and returns early at line ~464. The reminder cancellation block (`updatedBookings.forEach(... deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder)`) is placed after this return, so workflow reminders of paid bookings are never cancelled. Customers of paid, cancelled bookings still receive workflow reminders, which is the bug this PR claims to fix.

title: Immediate-delete path cancels in SendGrid but leaves the reminder row marked as scheduled
body: When `immediateDelete` is true and a referenceId exists, the function cancels the batch in SendGrid and returns without touching the `workflowReminder` row. The row keeps `scheduled: true` and its referenceId, and `cancelled` stays null. The cron job never picks it up for cancellation because it only selects `cancelled: true` rows, so the row lingers until its scheduledDate passes. This affects the reschedule path in handleNewBooking.ts, which passes `true`, and it is inconsistent with the cancel path, which sets the flag and expects the row to be removed later. The behaviour across the immediate and deferred modes should be made consistent.

title: SMS cancellation has no retry and the DB row is only removed if Twilio cancel succeeds
body: In `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`, if `twilio.cancelSMS` throws, the function jumps to the catch and the reminder row is not deleted. Nothing retries the cancellation, unlike the email path, which at least has a cron. A transient Twilio error therefore lets the scheduled SMS for a cancelled or rescheduled booking go out. The same failure mode this PR fixes for email remains for SMS.

title: No tests cover the new cancelled-reminder semantics or the cron cancellation path
body: The PR changes the cancellation model (new `cancelled` column, deferred cancellation in the cron job, immediate vs deferred in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`), but no tests were added. Neither the cron cancellation loop, including its failure handling, nor the branching in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is covered. Those are exactly the paths where the reported bugs occur, so the regressions described above would not be caught.

title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation loop, blocking all later cancellations
body: The cancellation loop awaits `client.request` for each cancelled reminder inside a single try block. If the request throws for one reminder (for example because SendGrid already sent that batch, or returns an error for a stale batch_id), the exception skips every remaining reminder and jumps to the catch that only logs. The failing reminder is not deleted or marked, so the next cron run (every 15 minutes) hits the same reminder first and fails again. Other cancelled reminders in the window are never cancelled at SendGrid and their emails still go out. Each reminder should be wrapped in its own try/catch so one failure does not block the rest.

title: immediateDelete path cancels at SendGrid but leaves the workflowReminder row behind
body: When `immediateDelete` is true and a referenceId exists, the function sends the SendGrid cancel and returns without touching the database. The workflowReminder row stays with scheduled=true and a now-cancelled referenceId. Callers that rely on this path (handleNewBooking for the original rescheduled booking, and workflows.tsx when deleting a workflow or step) leave orphaned rows behind. The other branches (no referenceId, SMS) do delete the row, so this behavior is inconsistent. The row should be deleted after a successful cancel, or the caller should be documented to handle cleanup.

title: Cancellation window of one hour with a 15-minute cron can still let cancelled emails be sent
body: A reminder is only picked up for SendGrid cancellation when its scheduledDate is within the next hour, and the cron runs every 15 minutes. If a booking is cancelled less than about 15 minutes before the reminder's sendAt, the next cron run may happen after sendAt, so SendGrid has already sent the email. The window is not guaranteed to contain a cron run before send time. The issue this PR fixes is exactly that cancelled reminders are still sent, so this residual gap should be addressed, for example by cancelling immediately when the reminder is close to its send time, or by using a shorter cron interval.

title: No tests added for the new cancelled-flag flow and cron cancellation
body: The PR changes the cancellation contract (cancelled flag set in deleteScheduledEmailReminder, deferred SendGrid cancel in the cron, immediate-delete variant, and DB row deletion in SMS and email paths). None of this is covered by tests. The cron's failure behavior, the cancelled-flag set/unset rules, and the reschedule and cancel paths in handleCancelBooking, handleNewBooking, and bookings.tsx all need coverage to prevent regressions like the one this PR is fixing.

title: New nullable cancelled column has no default and no index for the cron query
body: The column is added as nullable `BOOLEAN` with no default, so existing rows get NULL and the schema models it as `Boolean?`. The cron filters on `cancelled = true` and `scheduledDate <= ...` on every run, with no index on either column, so it scans the whole WorkflowReminder table each time. A default of false and a composite index on (cancelled, scheduledDate) would avoid this as the table grows.

title: Reminder cancellation promises are fired without await inside forEach
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called inside `forEach` without awaiting. The handler then continues and responds while the cancelled-flag writes and Twilio cancels are still in flight. Errors are swallowed by the internal try/catch, so a failed cancel is silent. Using `Promise.all` with `map` would make the cancel complete before the response and keep the handler's ordering explicit. The same pattern appears in bookings.tsx and workflows.tsx.

title: Object of import() promises starts loading every app eagerly
body: Each `import(...)` in the object literal is evaluated as soon as this module is loaded, so all ~30 app modules are fetched and evaluated on first import of `@calcom/app-store`, whether or not they are used. The PR title says 'async import', but this does not make loading lazy; it only changes the access pattern. A consumer that needs one app pays for all of them. Lazy loading would need a function per entry, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, with call sites updated to match.

title: Rejected import promises are unhandled and any uncaught access breaks silently
body: Because every entry is a promise created at module load, a failing import (missing dependency, syntax error in one app) produces an unhandled promise rejection when nobody has awaited that entry. Callers that index the store without `await` (any call site not updated in this PR) now receive a Promise, so `"lib" in app` is false and the code silently treats the app as not implemented, e.g. `getCalendar` logs a 'not implemented' warning and returns null.

title: getCalendarCredentials now yields promises in the `calendar` field while staying synchronous
body: `getCalendarCredentials` is still a synchronous function, so `getCalendar(credential)` returns a Promise that is stored as the `calendar` field. Any other caller of this exported function that uses `.calendar` as a Calendar object (not awaiting it) will break. Only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to `await item.calendar`. Other consumers of this exported API are not updated in the diff and should be checked, or the function should become async.

title: Async forEach drops calendar deletions for recurring cancellations
body: The `.forEach(async (credential) => {...})` callback pushes into `apiDeletes` only after `await getCalendar(...)` and the inner loop. Nothing awaits the callback promises, and `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs with the array as it was before the callbacks finished. As a result the calendar deletions are fire-and-forget: the handler reports success before they complete, and any rejection (e.g. from `deleteEvent`) becomes an unhandled rejection rather than an error surfaced to the caller. Use `for...of` with `await` or `Promise.all` over mapped promises, as the non-recurring branch already does.

title: Async forEach makes the try/catch around calendar/video deletion ineffective
body: The `try { bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) } catch` block cannot catch errors from the async callbacks, since forEach does not return or await them. Previously `getCalendar` was synchronous and the try covered failures; now any error from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` / `deleteMeeting` is an unhandled promise rejection and the reschedule flow continues without logging it. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try.

title: Same async forEach issue: calendar/video deletions are not awaited and errors are unhandled
body: The `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` callbacks are not awaited, so the deletion of the previous calendar event and video meeting runs in the background. The surrounding try/catch no longer catches anything. Rejections surface as unhandled promise rejections, and the caller cannot know whether the deletions succeeded.

title: Reschedule mutation fires calendar/video deletions without awaiting them
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` is not awaited, so the mutation returns before the old calendar event and video meeting are deleted. Failures become unhandled rejections. Rescheduling can therefore report success while the previous event stays on the calendar, or while errors go unreported. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`.

title: Unrelated blank-line change in getCalendarCredentials
body: A blank line is added before `return credentials.length ? ...` with no functional change. It adds noise to an already large async conversion.

title: import() calls run eagerly at module load, so nothing is actually lazy
body: Each entry is `import("./x")` evaluated when the object literal is created, so every app module starts loading as soon as `appStore` is imported, regardless of whether it is used. The async wrapping therefore adds no lazy-loading benefit on the server or in client bundles. Entries should be thunks (`() => import("./x")`) and callers should invoke them on demand. Any rejected import is also created up front, so a broken app module can surface as an unhandled rejection even if nothing ever awaits it.

title: Making the forEach callback async moves getCalendar errors out of the try/catch
body: Before this change, `getCalendar` was synchronous, so a throw inside it was caught by the surrounding try/catch and logged. Now the callback is async and the `await getCalendar(...)` and `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` promises are not awaited by `forEach`, so rejections become unhandled promise rejections and the try/catch never sees them. The cancellation work also runs fire-and-forget, so the reschedule returns before calendar/video deletion finishes. The same pattern is in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.

title: requestReschedule fires async calendar/video deletions without awaiting them
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` discards the promises returned by each callback. The mutation then sends the reschedule email and returns while the `getCalendar` lookup and the `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls are still running. Any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection, and the client cannot know whether the old calendar event was actually removed. Use `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` and await it.

title: Async forEach pushes into apiDeletes after it has already been awaited
body: Inside the recurring-cancellation branch, `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` pushes to `apiDeletes` only after an asynchronous await. `forEach` does not wait for these callbacks, so `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs before the pushes happen. Those deletions are never awaited, their errors are unhandled, and the response can report success while calendar events are still being deleted. Replace the forEach with a for...of loop or `Promise.all` over the credentials.

title: Adapter creation is now sequential and awaits each app in a loop
body: `getVideoAdapters` used to build adapters synchronously in one pass. It now awaits each app import one at a time in a `for` loop, so N credentials cost N sequential module-load round trips. Resolving the apps with `Promise.all` would preserve ordering and avoid the serialized waits.

title: getCalendarCredentials stores un-awaited getCalendar promises as the calendar value
body: `getCalendarCredentials` is still synchronous, but `getCalendar` now returns a Promise, so `calendar` is a Promise on every returned item. Any consumer that checks `if (!calendar)` or uses the value as a Calendar synchronously will be wrong. A rejected `getCalendar` promise (for example from a failing CalendarService constructor) is also only handled when `getConnectedCalendars` later awaits it, so the rejection can be reported late or unhandled. The function should be made async and should await the calendar, or the field type should be updated to match.

title: try/catch no longer protects calendar/video deletions after switching to async forEach
body: The forEach callback is now `async` and awaits `getCalendar`. Its promise is never awaited, so the surrounding try/catch (lines 124-139) cannot catch errors from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting`. Before this change, `getCalendar` was synchronous, so its throws were caught here. Now any failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection, which can crash the process on Node or log noise, and the error handler that logs via `logger.error` is dead code.

title: Same regression: try/catch is ineffective around async forEach, errors become unhandled rejections
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` with `await getCalendar(...)` inside a try block. The callbacks are not awaited and the try/catch cannot observe their rejections, so calendar deletion failures are no longer logged and surface as unhandled promise rejections. The function also returns `true` before these deletions settle, so their outcome is never observed.

title: forEach(async) pushes to apiDeletes after the array has already been awaited
body: In the recurring-cancel branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })` does not await the callbacks. Later `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` and the `await apiDeletes` in the payment branch run while those pushes may not have happened yet. Calendar deletions can therefore be skipped from the awaited set, and their errors are unhandled.

title: Errors from getCalendar in CalendarManager.getCalendarCredentials are not handled
body: In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts, `getCalendarCredentials` calls `getCalendar(credential)` without await and stores the resulting promise. Since `getCalendar` is now async, a rejection (for example from the CalendarService constructor) is unhandled until `item.calendar` is awaited, which may never happen for credentials filtered out downstream.

title: appStore values are now Promises; any caller that does not await them silently breaks
body: Every entry of `appStore` changed from a module namespace to a `Promise` returned by `import()`. Any consumer that indexes `appStore[...]` and uses `.lib` without awaiting now gets a Promise, so `"lib" in app` is false and features are silently disabled, with no type error if the consumer relies on inferred types. Only the call sites shown in this diff were updated. Other consumers of `appStore` (for example `packages/app-store/utils`, `locations`, or web API routes) must be audited, and the PR description does not mention this breaking change.

title: Adapters are loaded sequentially in a loop, serializing dynamic imports
body: `getVideoAdapters` awaits each `appStore[...]` import one at a time inside `for ... of`. The previous code was synchronous and the imports are independent, so `Promise.all` over the credentials would avoid serializing the module loads on every busy-time or meeting operation.

title: Date-override zero-length check compares Dayjs objects by reference
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` uses `===` on two freshly constructed Dayjs objects, which is always false. The intended zero-length override check never fires. It should compare with `isSame` or the underlying timestamps.

title: A non-matching override on the same day makes the slot unavailable even when another override covers it
body: `dateOverrides.find` returns true on the first override for the same day that does not contain the slot (e.g. `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` at line ~123). When a day has several override ranges, e.g. 10-11 and 14-15, a 14:00 slot is rejected because the 10-11 override 'doesn't contain it', even though the 14-15 override does. The check should be 'some override contains the slot', not 'any override on that day fails to contain it'.

title: Date override day matching mixes wall-clock shifting with UTC comparison
body: The override start is shifted by the organizer's UTC offset and then formatted as a date, and the result is compared against `slotStartTime.format(...)`, which is in UTC. Slots near midnight can therefore be matched to the wrong override day, or be treated as having no override and fall through to the other checks. The override and slot must be compared in the same timezone.

title: Working-hours check is inverted for split shifts and ignores timezone
body: `workingHours.find(...)` returns true if the slot falls outside any single working-hours block (`start < startTime || end > endTime`), and then the slot is rejected. With multiple blocks in a day, a slot inside block 2 is outside block 1, so it is rejected. The check should be 'some block contains the slot'. In addition, `slotStartTime` is UTC while `workingHours` are minutes in the organizer timezone, so the comparison is wrong for any non-UTC organizer.

title: Slot end minutes are computed from slotStartTime, so the window is zero-length
body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime.hour()/minute()` instead of `slotEndTime`. The `start` and `end` values are therefore identical, and the `end > workingHour.endTime` condition never tests the slot's actual end. Slots that run past the end of working hours are not rejected.

title: Override timeZone may be undefined and is then interpreted in server local timezone
body: `timeZone: availability.timeZone` is spread into each override, but `timeZone` is optional in `TimeRange`. In slots.ts `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` with undefined falls back to the server's local timezone, which is wrong on the server and makes the override shift depend on where the process runs.

title: Override offset is computed from Date.toString() and only hour/minute of the shifted time is kept
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` re-parses a locale-formatted date string, losing milliseconds and depending on the server's local timezone. The shifted start/end are then reduced to `hour()*60+minute()`, dropping the date. If the timezone shift crosses midnight, the override start/end minutes are wrong (e.g. an override ending at 00:30 after shifting would be treated as 30 minutes after the start rather than the next day).

title: New test does not cover the fixed-host round-robin behaviour the PR fixes
body: The only added test checks that a single-host override yields identical UTC slots in another timezone. Nothing tests the main fix: a round-robin event with a fixed host having a date override should only show slots where the fixed host is available. There is also no test for multiple override ranges on one day or for split working hours, which the new checks break as noted above.

title: Date-override end check compares Dayjs objects by identity
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two freshly created Dayjs object references, so it is always false and the zero-length override branch never triggers. It should use `.isSame(...)`. As written, a zero-length override (start equals end) is not handled as intended.

title: Slot inside a date override skips the busy-time check entirely
body: When a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls inside it, `checkIfIsAvailable` returns true right away (`if (dateOverrideExist) return true;`). That bypasses the `busy` check at the end of the function. A fixed host with a date override who already has a calendar event or booking at that time will still be reported as available. This is the exact problem the PR is meant to fix (round-robin events booked while fixed hosts are unavailable), so the fix is incomplete.

title: Working-hours check uses the slot start for both start and end
body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of the slot end time, so `end > workingHour.endTime` is effectively checking the start again. A slot that runs past the end of working hours is not rejected. Also, `workingHours.find` returns true when any single working-hours block excludes the slot, so a slot inside a later block (e.g. 14:00-18:00 when there is also a 09:00-12:00 block) is rejected. The check should ask whether the slot fits inside at least one block (`.some` with start >= startTime and end <= endTime).

title: Working-hours rejection logic inverted for multiple availability blocks
body: The predicate `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` is true whenever the slot is outside one particular block. Since `.find` is used, any non-matching block causes the whole slot to be rejected, even when another block contains it. Users with split working hours (for example a lunch break) will see valid slots removed.

title: Override timezone may be undefined, falling back to server timezone
body: `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` is called without guaranteeing `override.timeZone` is set. The timeZone is copied from `availability.timeZone` in slots.ts, which may be missing. dayjs `.tz(undefined)` then uses the process's local timezone, so the computed offset depends on the server's TZ setting rather than the organizer's. The overrides' timezone should be validated or defaulted to the organizer timezone.

title: New timezone test would pass without the fix
body: The added assertion uses the +6:00 timezone and expects the same UTC slots (08:30-11:30Z) as the +5:30 case. Slot times are returned as UTC ISO strings, so this output is independent of the invitee timezone, and the old `getUTCHours` code would produce the same result. The test does not check that a date override adapts to a different timezone. There is also no test for the main fix: a round-robin event where a fixed host's date override must respect that host's busy times.

title: Date override day skips all busy-time checks and returns available
body: When any date override exists on the slot's day and the slot is not rejected by the override range check, `dateOverrideExist` is set and the function returns `true` at line 134 before reaching the `busy.every(...)` check. For a fixed host, a calendar event or existing booking overlapping the slot is ignored on any day that has a date override. This can allow double-booking, which is the opposite of what this PR is meant to fix.

title: Working-hours check rejects slots if any single working-hours range does not cover them
body: The `workingHours.find(...)` callback returns true for any working-hours entry where the slot falls outside it, and the `if` then rejects the slot when `find` finds any such entry. With several working-hours entries (multiple ranges on the same weekday, or entries for several users aggregated together), a slot covered by one entry is still rejected because another entry does not cover it. The check should ask whether no entry covers the slot, not whether some entry does not. Additionally, `start` and `end` at lines 141-142 are both computed from `slotStartTime`, so the end-of-slot is never checked against the working-hours end.

title: Comparison of two dayjs objects with === is always false
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares object references, not times, so the zero-length override branch (`return true`) can never execute. Zero-length overrides are therefore not handled as intended. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `valueOf()`.

title: Override timezone is optional but used unguarded, and the Date is round-tripped through a string
body: `TimeRange.timeZone` is optional (packages/types/schedule.d.ts), and this PR now passes `availability.timeZone`, which may be undefined. `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` with an undefined zone falls back to the plugin default instead of failing clearly, so the offset can silently be wrong. Separately, `override.start.toString()` converts the Date to a locale-style string and re-parses it, which drops milliseconds and depends on the string format. Passing the Date (or its ISO string) directly and guarding the missing timezone would be safer.

title: Timezone test does not exercise round-robin or fixed-host overrides
body: The added assertion only checks a personal event with one host and expects the same UTC slots for a +6:00 invitee as for +5:30. It does not cover the bug the PR fixes: a round-robin event with a fixed host whose date override limits slots, nor the busy-time bypass described above. No test covers the case where a calendar busy time on an override day should still block a slot, so the regression in the override early return would go undetected.

title: Migration crashes when no category matches embed_category
body: The lookup `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` calls `[]` on the result and then `['id']` on the row. `embed_category` defaults to '' and most installs never set it, so no row matches, `[0]` is nil, and the migration raises NoMethodError. The same pattern on line 15 (`[0]['value']` for uncategorized_category_id) has the same problem. Upgrades on typical sites would fail. The lookup should handle an empty result set, falling back to uncategorized.

title: Host values interpolated into SQL without escaping
body: Each host from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is spliced directly into an INSERT string. A value containing a single quote breaks the statement and aborts the migration. Use parameterized inserts or quote the value with the connection's quoting helper.

title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `self.host.sub!` is called unconditionally. If the request omits `host` (or sends null), `self.host` is nil and the save raises NoMethodError, which becomes a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard for blank host before the substitutions.

title: Host lookup is case-sensitive on the URI side
body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases only the stored column. The `host` taken from `URI(...)` is passed through unchanged, so a referer or embed_url with uppercase letters (e.g. `EvilTrout.com`) never matches a stored host. The input should be downcased before comparison, which also means `host_allowed?` can reject valid embeds.

title: No uniqueness constraint on host
body: Nothing prevents two rows with the same host, either in validations or in a unique index. `record_for_host` uses `.first`, so duplicates silently pick an arbitrary category for TopicEmbed imports. Add a uniqueness validation (case-insensitive) and ideally a unique index.

title: update and destroy crash with 500 for unknown ids
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a missing record, and `save_host(nil)` or `host.destroy` then raises NoMethodError. This should return 404 (for example via `find` / `find_by!`).

title: update action is a no-op that reports success
body: `update` never reads params or persists anything; it just re-renders the unchanged embedding. The client's `saveChanges` calls it with `{}`, so the admin UI looks saved when nothing was. Either implement the update or remove the route and the save action.

title: has_many with embed: :ids sends only ids, not the hosts
body: With `embed: :ids` and no include, the payload contains `embeddable_host_ids` but no `embeddable_hosts` collection. The client's `_hydrateEmbedded` then looks up each id in a root collection that doesn't exist and produces an array of undefined entries, so `embedding.embeddable_hosts` renders broken rows. The hosts need to be side-loaded (include) or the client must fetch them.

title: Unresolved _ids entries stored as undefined
body: In the `_ids` branch, `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for any id not present in the root payload, and `map` keeps those as undefined entries. Those entries are then assigned to the model's collection. Missing ids should be filtered out, and the `|| []` fallback is dead code because `map` always returns an array.

title: Fabricator files have swapped contents
