body: category_fabricator.rb now holds only the embeddable_host fabricator, while the :category fabricators were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. This is misleading to maintainers. The category fabricators should be in category_fabricator.rb and the embeddable host fabricator in its own file.

title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `self.host.sub!` is called unconditionally in before_validation. If the host attribute is nil (for example, POST /admin/embeddable_hosts without a `host` param, which `save_host` passes straight through), this raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. A nil guard is needed before the sub! calls.

title: Stored hosts are not normalized to lowercase, so mixed-case hosts never match
body: The validation regex is case-insensitive (`/i`), so `Example.com` is accepted and stored as-is. `record_for_host` compares `lower(host) = ?` against the lowercased referer/URL host, but the stored value is not lowercased. A host saved with uppercase letters therefore never matches, and embeds from that domain are rejected or import into the wrong category. Lowercase the host in before_validation, or compare with `lower(host) = lower(?)`.

title: No uniqueness validation on host, so duplicate entries are allowed
body: Nothing prevents the same host from being created twice. `record_for_host` uses `.first` with no ordering, so which category a host maps to becomes arbitrary when duplicates exist. The embedding admin list would also show duplicate rows. Add a uniqueness validation (case-insensitive) and ideally a unique index.

title: Migration crashes when no embed_category site setting row exists
body: `execute(...)[0]['id']` is called unconditionally. If the `embed_category` site setting was never changed from its default, there is no row in site_settings, so `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The migration then fails and blocks the deploy. The result should be checked for emptiness before indexing, falling back to the uncategorized category.

title: create_table with force: true silently drops an existing table
body: If embeddable_hosts already exists (for example on a partial or re-run migration, or a table created by another branch), `force: true` drops it along with any data in it. Dropping this table is unnecessary for a fresh migration and risks data loss. Remove `force: true`.

title: Host values from site settings are interpolated into SQL unescaped
body: Each host from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is spliced directly into an INSERT string. A value containing a single quote breaks the statement and makes the migration fail. Use parameterized execution or quote the value (for example with `connection.quote`).

title: destroy and update crash with a 500 when the id does not exist
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil. `host.destroy` in destroy (line 16) and `save_host(host)` with nil in update (line 11) then raise NoMethodError. A not-found response should be returned instead.

title: Missing embeddable_host param raises NoMethodError
body: `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is accessed without checking that the `embeddable_host` key exists, so a request without it causes a 500 rather than a validation error.

title: update action accepts changes but never saves anything
body: `update` only re-renders the serialized embedding. Nothing is persisted, so a PUT to /admin/customize/embedding reports success while discarding its input. The client `saveChanges` action calls this endpoint and therefore appears to save while doing nothing. Either implement the save or remove the route and client call.

title: saveChanges sends an empty update that does nothing
body: `this.get('embedding').update({})` sends an empty payload to the server, which ignores it. This is dead or misleading code, since host changes are saved per row by the component.

title: Spec only checks class inheritance; create/update/destroy are untested
body: The only test asserts that the controller subclasses AdminController. The actual behavior (creating, updating, destroying hosts, the uncategorized default for blank category, and the not-found and invalid-input paths) has no test coverage.

title: Embedding controller spec has no behavior tests
body: The spec only checks inheritance. The show and update endpoints, and the staff-only access check, are not exercised.

title: Fabricator contents are swapped between files named for the wrong content
body: category_fabricator.rb now contains the embeddable_host fabricator, while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb holds the category fabricators. Fabrication loads both so tests still run, but the file names mislead maintainers about where definitions live.

title: Topic is created with nil category when no host record matches
body: The category now comes only from EmbeddableHost. If no host record matches (for example because of the case-sensitivity issue above, or a host that was deleted), `category` becomes nil. The previous behavior of falling back to a configured category is gone, and nothing falls back to the uncategorized category.

title: Migration crashes when no site setting matches a category
body: The lookup `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` indexes the first row of the result. When `embed_category` is unset, or its value matches no category name, the result is empty, `[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. Most installs never set embed_category, so this migration will fail for them and block the upgrade. The lookup needs a nil/empty check with a fallback to uncategorized.

title: Host values interpolated into SQL unescaped
body: Each host from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is interpolated directly into an INSERT string: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. A value containing a single quote breaks the statement and aborts the migration. Parameter binding or quoting via the connection (`connection.quote`) should be used.

title: before_validation crashes on missing host
body: `self.host.sub!` is called unconditionally. If the request omits `embeddable_host[host]`, `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is nil and `host` is nil, so `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError. The controller then returns a 500 rather than a validation error. A nil guard is needed, and the validator should report a blank host.

title: No uniqueness validation or index on host
body: Nothing prevents two rows with the same host, and there is no unique index. `record_for_host` uses `.first` on `lower(host) = ?`, so when duplicates exist, the category a topic gets (via TopicEmbed.import) and the allow/deny decision are arbitrary. The migration also inserts whatever the old setting contained, so duplicates are plausible. Add a uniqueness validation (case-insensitive) and a unique index on lower(host).

title: Host lookup is case-sensitive on the URI side
body: The query compares `lower(host)` against the raw `uri.host`, which is not downcased. A referer or embed URL with uppercase letters (e.g. http://EvilTrout.com/page) never matches a stored host, so the embed is rejected. The argument should be downcased before comparing.

title: update and destroy crash on unknown id
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: ...).first` can return nil. `save_host(host)` then raises on `host.host =` and `destroy` raises on `host.destroy`. The client gets a 500 instead of a 404. Use `find` (which raises RecordNotFound, rendered as 404) or check for nil.

title: PUT /customize/embedding is a no-op that reports success
body: The `update` action only re-renders the current embedding and never reads params or saves anything. The client `saveChanges` action calls `update({})`, so any submitted change is silently discarded while the response looks like a successful save. Either implement the update or remove the route and client action.

title: saveChanges calls update with an empty payload
body: `this.get('embedding').update({})` sends no data, and the backing PUT endpoint does nothing. This action is dead or misleading and does not persist the host list. It should be removed or wired to something that saves.

title: Fabricator contents swapped between files
body: category_fabricator.rb now contains only the :embeddable_host fabricator, while the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. The file names no longer match their contents, which will mislead maintainers looking for category fabricators.

title: Controller specs only test inheritance
body: The spec only asserts that the controller subclasses AdminController. Nothing covers create, update, or destroy, staff-only access, the blank-category fallback to uncategorized, or validation failure responses. The same applies to embedding_controller_spec.rb, which would not have caught the no-op update.

title: No test for duplicate hosts, nil host, or mixed-case lookup
body: The model spec covers trimming and basic matching but not the edge cases the code is sensitive to: duplicate hosts, a missing host param (nil crash), or a mixed-case host or referer. The describe label 'allows_embeddable_host' is also a leftover from the removed SiteSetting method.

title: Migration has no test and an irreversible change
body: The migration moves data from site settings into a new table and then deletes the old settings. It has no spec, and the `change` method cannot be reversed, since the DELETE has no inverse. Rolling back loses the embed configuration.

title: Second `self.downsize` silently replaces the first, changing its arity
body: The PR adds `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` while the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) is still present. In Ruby the later definition wins, so the 5-argument form is dead code and any caller passing `(from, to, w, h, opts)` now has `h` bound to `opts`. Calling `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer raises or returns nil, so the call fails or silently ignores options. Duplicate method definitions with different signatures should not be merged like this. Either keep one signature or rename the new one.

title: Removed `OptimizedImage.dimensions` helper and changed `optimize` signature
body: The helper `self.dimensions(width, height)` is removed and `optimize` now takes a preformatted dimensions string instead of width and height. Any other caller in the codebase or plugins that calls `OptimizedImage.dimensions` or `optimize` with width/height will break with NoMethodError or wrong argument handling. The diff does not show that these callers were checked.

title: File size re-check may read a stale size and loop without effect
body: `tempfile.size` on an open Tempfile reads the size through its open file descriptor. `OptimizedImage.downsize` runs `convert` writing to `tempfile.path`. If ImageMagick writes via a new inode (unlink and create, or rename), the Tempfile's open handle still points at the old contents, so `tempfile.size` never drops. The loop then runs all 5 attempts with no effect and the original oversized file is passed to `Upload.create_for`. Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` or reopen the file to get the real size.

title: Downsize failures are ignored and the uploaded file is overwritten in place
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false on failure (`convert_with` swallows errors and logs), but the return value is discarded. The loop then retries up to 5 times on the same input, and a partially written or corrupted output is left at `tempfile.path` and uploaded. The original file is destroyed in place with no fallback. Check the return value, stop on failure, and either keep the original or reject the upload.

title: Client-side size limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
body: The check previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. It now always uses 10MB for images and attachments alike. Admins' `max_attachment_size_kb` and `max_image_size_kb` are ignored on the client, so the client may accept or reject files that the server would treat differently. The feature's purpose (accept large images and downsize them) is also undermined because the client still hard-blocks anything above 10MB.

title: 413 error message reports hardcoded 10 MB regardless of configured limit
body: The HTTP 413 handler now shows a 10 MB limit instead of the configured `max_image_size_kb`. The displayed limit is wrong whenever the admin has configured a different value, and the message misleads users about the actual cap.

title: Remote URL downloads now capped at 10MB instead of the configured image limit
body: The URL download limit changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. This is unrelated to downsizing, applies to all URL uploads, and ignores the admin setting. If the intent is to allow larger images, the download cap should be an explicit, documented decision rather than a silent change.

title: Downsizing applies to non-image-type uploads and to unbounded input
body: The condition checks `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` but the downsize step runs on any upload where the filename looks like an image, including SVG, which ImageMagick may rasterize, and `image_type` is not considered. There is no guard against a huge source file being fed into ImageMagick before size is checked, so the conversion cost is paid on arbitrary input size.

title: Duplicate `downsize` definitions are confusing to maintainers
body: Two `self.downsize` methods with different parameter lists appear in the same class, which hides which version is live. This ambiguity is what causes the arity bug above. Remove the unused variant.

title: Second `self.downsize` silently replaces the first, breaking the 5-argument form
body: The diff adds `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` while the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 is left in place. In Ruby the later definition wins, so the 5-argument form is gone. Any caller passing `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). The two overloads with the same name and different arities are a clear mistake. Either remove one, or keep a single method and update all callers.

title: `optimize` no longer returns anything useful for callers that depended on the old signature
body: `resize` and `downsize` previously passed width/height through `dimensions()`, which was removed. Any other caller outside this diff that calls `optimize` or `downsize` with width and height, or relies on the removed `dimensions` helper, will break. The PR does not show a search of all call sites to confirm this is safe.

title: Size check uses a stale `tempfile.size` after the file is rewritten in place
body: The loop re-reads `tempfile.size` on a Tempfile object whose descriptor was opened before `OptimizedImage.downsize` rewrote `tempfile.path` via an external process and ImageOptim. Depending on whether the rewrite replaces the inode, `File#size` on the open handle can return the old size. The loop may then run all 5 attempts needlessly, or stop incorrectly. The size should be read from the path (for example `File.size(tempfile.path)`) and the handle reopened or flushed.

title: Failed downsizes are retried silently and oversize images are still accepted
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false on failure (its result is ignored here), so a failing convert is retried up to 5 times on the same input with no effect. If the image is still above `max_image_size_kb` after the loop, nothing is raised or reported; the code proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with the oversize file. The user gets no clear error and the limit the admin configured is not enforced consistently.

title: Remote URL downloads are no longer bounded by the admin size setting
body: The download limit for API URL uploads was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hard-coded `10.megabytes`. Admins who set a lower limit now get downloads of up to 10MB for any file type, and the download is not checked against the setting before being written to disk. This is a behavior change that the PR does not justify or make configurable.

title: Client-side size check ignores per-type site settings and hard-codes 10MB
body: `validateUploadedFile` previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. It now always uses 10MB. Admin limits for attachments and images are ignored in the browser, and the hard-coded 10MB check also blocks any image above 10MB, which contradicts the server-side feature of accepting and downsizing large images. The client and server limits now disagree.

title: 413 handler hard-codes the limit instead of using the configured setting
body: The 413 case now displays a hard-coded 10 MB limit rather than `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. The message can be wrong for any site whose configured limit differs from 10MB.

title: No tests added for the automatic downsizing path or the changed behavior
body: The PR adds a new server-side loop that rewrites uploaded files, changes `OptimizedImage` method signatures, and changes size limits on both client and server. None of these changes have specs covering the downsize loop, the attempt limit, the failure path, the overload issue, or the size checks. The description is just "Test 1", so the PR gives no rationale or verification steps.

title: Second `self.downsize` silently overrides the first and breaks the 4-argument call form
body: The PR adds `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` while the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) is kept. In Ruby the later definition replaces the earlier one, so the original method is dead code. Any existing caller using `downsize(from, to, width, height)` now passes `height` as `opts`, and `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` / `opts[:allow_animation]` then raise on a String or silently ignore the height. The method is also now ambiguous for the two-argument-plus-options shape. Keep one signature, or give the new method a distinct name.

title: Removal of `OptimizedImage.dimensions` and change of `optimize` signature is an unannounced API break
body: The PR removes the public class method `self.dimensions(width, height)` and changes `self.optimize` from taking width/height to taking a pre-formatted dimensions string. Any other caller in the codebase or plugins that calls `OptimizedImage.dimensions` or `optimize` with width/height will now fail with NoMethodError or ArgumentError. Nothing in the diff updates or checks such callers.

title: Animated GIF path receives an invalid '80%' size for gifsicle
body: When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is on and the tempfile path ends in `.GIF`, `OptimizedImage.downsize` dispatches to `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`, which is not a valid WxH argument. `convert_with` returns false on the non-zero exit and the loop silently retries 5 times with the same failing command, then the oversized animated GIF is passed on unchanged. Animated images therefore never get reduced, and the wasted work is repeated for every upload.

title: Downsize failures are ignored and the final size is never verified
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false on failure, but the return value is discarded. The loop also stops after 5 attempts without checking whether the file is now under `max_image_size_kb`. If it is still too large, the code falls through to `Upload.create_for` with no explicit error about the reduction failing. Also, reducing by 80% of dimensions does not guarantee a size reduction of the required amount, so 5 attempts may not be enough for large images. The result is either an unhelpful later rejection or an oversized file stored silently.

title: Remote download limit no longer follows the admin setting
body: The URL-download size cap changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hard-coded `10.megabytes`. Remote downloads of any file type through the API can now be up to 10MB regardless of the configured limit. This is a silent policy change that is not tied to the downsizing feature, which only concerns images. Note that this also removes the bound that limited how much would be fetched for images that are then downsized.

title: Client-side size check ignores per-type site settings for all uploads
body: The check in `validateUploadedFile` now uses a fixed 10MB for every upload type, replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. Attachments larger than the configured `max_attachment_size_kb` now pass client validation and are sent to the server, which means the admin's limit is bypassed in the UI. Only images should have their limit relaxed, since the server now downsizes them. Attachments should keep using their own setting.

title: 413 error message hard-codes 10 MB instead of the configured limit
body: The 413 handler now always reports a 10 MB limit via `file_too_large`, even when the site has a different `max_image_size_kb` or attachment limit configured. The user is told a wrong maximum size, which is misleading. The previous code read the actual setting.

title: unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil, for example when a user receives a notification for a topic they never interacted with (watched category, mailing list, invited PM). The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises NoMethodError and the user gets a 500 instead of an unsubscribe. The action should create the row, e.g. via `TopicUser.change`, or handle nil explicitly.

title: Unsubscribe is a non-idempotent toggle on a GET link
body: The action flips the level: anything above regular becomes regular, anything else becomes muted. Clicking the link once on a watched/tracking topic moves it to regular, and a second click mutes it. The route is a GET reachable from emails, and mail clients and link scanners prefetch GET URLs, so merely opening the email can toggle state. The action should set muted deterministically (and a GET should not mutate state at all, ideally a confirm page or POST).

title: Direct save bypasses TopicUser.change side effects
body: `tu.save!` skips `TopicUser.change`, which sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` and publishes `notification_level_change` on MessageBus. As a result the open browser tab for this topic does not update its notification state, and the reason/timestamp are stale. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)` instead.

title: track_visit! assigns the topic id to user_id when a raw id is passed
body: `user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic` uses `topic` in the else branch where `user` was meant. Callers pass a plain integer user id (`TopicUser.track_visit! topic_id, user_id` in topics_controller), so `user_id` becomes the topic id. The visit is recorded against the wrong user, and a new TopicUser row is created with `user_id` equal to the topic id. The diff touches this line, so it should be fixed here.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url, which callers may not pass
body: `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}` (added in server.en.yml). Any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument while building the email, so the email send fails. The option should default to something sensible or the builder should guard against the missing key.

title: List-Unsubscribe header still points at preferences, not the per-topic link
body: The per-topic unsubscribe URL is added to the body, but the `List-Unsubscribe` header in `header_args` still points to `user_preferences_url`. Mail clients' one-click unsubscribe therefore does not offer the per-topic action, which is the feature this PR adds, and the header and body now disagree about what unsubscribing means.

title: No tests for the new unsubscribe behaviour
body: The only change is adding an `unsubscribe_url` argument to a spec fixture. Nothing tests `Topic#unsubscribe_url`, the `TopicsController#unsubscribe` toggle/redirect logic, the missing-TopicUser case, or that the rendered body contains the topic unsubscribe link. The controller action, which mutates notification state, has no request spec.

title: PR description is placeholder text
body: The description reads only 'Test 2', so reviewers get no summary of the new per-topic unsubscribe behaviour, the toggle semantics, or the unrelated refactors bundled in (routes reorder, topic-from-params rewrite, TopicUser formatting).

title: unsubscribe crashes with nil TopicUser for users who have no topic record
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` is not guarded. A logged-in user who has never interacted with the topic (e.g. a user reached by a notification email for a topic they only got via mention or digest, or whose record was never created) has no TopicUser row, so `tu` is nil and `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 from the unsubscribe link. Use `TopicUser.change` or find-or-create the record.

title: Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET that toggles, so mail scanners can change settings and a second click re-subscribes
body: `unsubscribe` changes notification level on a GET request, and the action toggles: if the level is above regular it is set to regular, otherwise to muted. Email link scanners and prefetchers that fetch URLs will silently unsubscribe users. A user who clicks the link twice gets re-subscribed, because the second request flips the state back. Unsubscribe should set an explicit target state (muted) idempotently, ideally via POST with a token.

title: unsubscribe writes via save! and bypasses TopicUser.change side effects
body: The action sets `notification_level` directly and calls `tu.save!`. It does not set `notifications_reason_id` or `notifications_changed_at`, which `TopicUser.change` sets, and it does not publish the `notification_level_change` MessageBus message, so open clients for the user won't update. The read-then-write sequence also loses updates under concurrent requests.

title: Ember template name does not match the route, so the unsubscribe page template is never rendered
body: The route is declared as top-level `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', ...)`. Ember resolves its template as `topic-unsubscribe`, but the file added is `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which resolves to `topic/unsubscribe`. The controller and view are also named `topic-unsubscribe`. The page will render with no template, so the feature's UI does not appear.

title: Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText
body: The property is spelled `stopNotificiationsText` here and in the template. It works only because both sides use the same typo. It should be corrected before it spreads to plugins or other code.

title: track_visit! uses the topic argument as user_id when a User is not passed
body: `user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic` falls back to the topic argument instead of the user argument. When a plain user id is passed, the query updates or creates rows for the wrong user, using the topic id as the user id. The line was touched by this PR but the bug was left in place.

title: unsubscribe_link i18n now requires unsubscribe_url for every add_unsubscribe_link email
body: The `unsubscribe_link` string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `MessageBuilder` renders it whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is set, and it only supplies `unsubscribe_url` here. Any other caller (including plugins) that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` without `unsubscribe_url` will now raise an interpolation error when building the email, both in the HTML part and the text body. Either make the key optional or fall back to a safe value.

title: Per-topic unsubscribe sentence appears for every email, not only topic notifications
body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` text now always includes the 'stop receiving notifications about this particular topic' line. That is correct for the notification path but misleading for any other email that uses this key with a generic or non-topic context. The message should be scoped to the topic emails.

title: unsubscribe_url builds on url, which includes the post number and slug
body: `unsubscribe_url` is `"#{url}/unsubscribe"` and `url` takes no post number here, so this is fine. However it depends on `slug`, which is lazily computed and may be empty for a topic with a blank title. The result is then `/t//id/unsubscribe`, and the controller's slug check redirects to a different URL on each call. Consider building it from `relative_url` or `id` only.

title: No tests for the new unsubscribe action or for the per-topic unsubscribe email text
body: The spec change only adds an unsubscribe_url argument to an existing builder test. Nothing tests the controller's toggle logic, the missing-TopicUser case, the 301 redirect on slug mismatch, or that the email body includes the topic unsubscribe link. The crash path above would have been caught by a request spec for a user without a TopicUser row.

title: Summary route constraints silently changed while adding unsubscribe routes
body: The diff reorders the moderator-liked and summary routes and drops `post_number: /\d+/` from the summary constraints. These are unrelated to unsubscribe and are not explained in the PR, which increases the risk of unintended routing changes. Keep this PR to the unsubscribe routes.

title: Unrelated refactor of topic-from-params route included in an unsubscribe feature PR
body: The file is rewritten from `var` to `const`, the `self` variable is moved, and blank lines are changed. None of this supports the unsubscribe feature. It increases review surface and merge-conflict risk. Split it into a separate change.

title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil when the user has never interacted with the topic (no topic_users record). The next line `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError and returns a 500. Emails are sent to users who may have no TopicUser row for the topic, for example users who were notified via a watch/category setting without a row, so the link can be clicked in a state with no record. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, ...)` or find-or-create the record before reading it.

title: State-changing unsubscribe happens on GET, so mail scanners and link prefetchers can mute topics
body: The unsubscribe action changes notification_level on a GET request (route `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) and also skips the xhr check. Email security scanners, link previewers, or prefetching clients that follow links in the notification email will silently mute the topic without user intent. Mutating actions should use POST (with a confirmation page for the GET), or the request should be otherwise protected.

title: Unsubscribe from watching/tracking only drops to regular, which still sends emails
body: When the current level is above regular (tracking or watching), the action sets it to regular rather than muted. Regular users still receive notifications for replies and quotes, so the link described as 'stop receiving notifications for this topic' does not stop them. The behavior also depends on the current level in a way that is not a clear unsubscribe. The intended semantics should be defined and the mapping fixed (likely always muted).

title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change, so reason, timestamps and MessageBus update are skipped
body: The unsubscribe path updates notification_level with `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`. This skips setting notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id (the user-changed reason), and it does not publish the notification_level_change on MessageBus, so an open browser tab keeps showing the old level. The rest of the codebase uses TopicUser.change for this.

title: List-Unsubscribe header still points to the preferences page, not the per-topic unsubscribe URL
body: In message_builder.rb the List-Unsubscribe header is built from `template_args[:user_preferences_url]`. The new per-topic unsubscribe_url is only added to the body text. Mail clients' one-click unsubscribe therefore sends the user to global preferences, and the feature's per-topic option is not exposed through the header. The header should use the topic's unsubscribe_url when it is provided.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url, which callers that set add_unsubscribe_link may not pass
body: The string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Any build_email call with add_unsubscribe_link: true that does not pass unsubscribe_url (the message builder merges only the opts given) will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when the body or HTML part is rendered. The only caller updated is send_notification_email; any other caller of add_unsubscribe_link breaks. Either pass a default or guard the interpolation.

title: No tests for the new unsubscribe action or the per-topic link in the body
body: The spec change only adds an unsubscribe_url argument to an existing case and asserts only that the List-Unsubscribe header is present and the preferences URL is in the body. Nothing checks that the per-topic unsubscribe URL appears in the body or that the link is correct. The new TopicsController#unsubscribe action (its nil-TopicUser case, the notification level transitions, the 301 redirect on slug mismatch, and the access check for anonymous users) has no controller spec.

title: Misspelled property name 'stopNotificiationsText' used across controller and template
body: The property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (with an extra 'fi') in both the controller and the hbs template. The name is consistent between them, so it works, but it is a misspelling that will be copied elsewhere. Rename it to `stopNotificationsText` in both files.

title: Unrelated refactor of topic-from-params route is bundled into the unsubscribe feature PR
body: The diff rewrites `topic-from-params.js.es6` (var to const, moved declarations, reformatting, and a switch from function syntax to method syntax) without any behavior change related to unsubscribe. The same applies to the dropdown-button, topic_user.rb, and notification.html.erb reformatting. These changes add review load and risk unrelated regressions. They should be split out.

title: Existing summary route silently loses its post_number constraint
body: The `t/:slug/:topic_id/summary` and `t/:topic_id/summary` routes were modified: the `post_number: /\d+/` constraint was removed from the topic_id summary route and the slug summary route's constraint was altered, and the moderator-liked/wordpress lines were reordered. These are unrelated to unsubscribe and change matching behavior of existing URLs. Revert the unrelated route edits.

title: unsubscribe_url is built from url, which ignores the Discourse.base_uri path
body: `unsubscribe_url` returns `"#{url}/unsubscribe"`, and `url` uses `Discourse.base_url` plus the slug and id. That is consistent with `url`, but the controller redirect uses `unsubscribe_url` (absolute), while the rest of the controller uses relative_url. Mixing absolute and relative URLs for the redirect could be fine, but the choice is unexplained and no test covers it.

title: Validation has a write side effect that inflates match counts on every validation run
body: `EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, which increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, and saves the row. Validation is supposed to be a read-only check, but every call to `valid?`, including repeated calls from `save` retries, controller paths, or `DiscourseHub` registration (`user.valid?` is called in `UsersController#create` before `save`), counts as a new block. The statistics become inaccurate, and each validation issues an extra UPDATE. The increment belongs in a separate, explicit step after the user is actually rejected.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count loses increments
body: `should_block?` loads the record, does `record.match_count += 1`, and then calls `record.save`. Concurrent signups with the same blocked address race on this, so some increments are lost. `last_match_at` is also overwritten by whichever save lands last. Using an atomic `update_counters` / `UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1` avoids the lost update. The `record.save` also runs model validations (including the uniqueness query) on every match, which is unnecessary for a counter update.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive while user emails are downcased
body: `should_block?` does `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` with the raw value, and the uniqueness check on `BlockedEmail` is also case-sensitive. The app normalises user emails with `Email.downcase` in several places (for example `change_email` and `find_by_username_or_email`). An entry such as `bad@spam.com` is therefore not matched against `Bad@Spam.com`, so a blocked address can register by changing letter case. The lookup and stored value should be normalised consistently.

title: Returning the full errors hash and submitted values is a new response contract
body: The failure response now includes `errors: user.errors.to_hash` and `values` with name, username, and email. The JavaScript client uses `result.errors.email` and `result.values.email` to add the address to `rejectedEmails`. Any validation error on the email attribute, including format errors and 'already taken', now causes the value to be blacklisted client-side until the user edits it. This couples the UI to server error keys and changes the API shape for every caller of `/users`, with no tests covering the new fields.

title: Rejected email is recorded for any email-field error, not only the blocked case
body: `createAccount` pushes `result.values.email` into `rejectedEmails` whenever `result.errors.email` exists. That includes ordinary errors such as an invalid format or an address already in use, where the user should see the specific reason. The client then shows the generic `user.email.invalid` reason for the rejected value, which hides the server's message. The list also grows without bound during a session and is never cleared.

title: Validator spec does not cover the side effect or the whitelist/blacklist interaction
body: The spec stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, so the real counting and saving behaviour is never exercised through the validator. There is no test that validating twice does not double-count, and no test that a record already failing the domain whitelist/blacklist skips the blocked check, which the `record.errors[attribute].blank?` guard implies. The new `user.email.blocked` message is also not asserted.

title: Concurrency and case handling are untested
body: The model spec covers the single-threaded happy path only. It does not test that matching is case-insensitive (see `should_block?`), and it does not test concurrent increments of `match_count`. The `be_within_one_second_of` matcher and the `Timecop` dependency are also used without a visible dependency in this change.

title: PR description is a placeholder
body: The description reads only 'Test 3', so the PR gives no explanation of the new blocklist behaviour, the response contract change in `UsersController#create`, or the removal of the email validator from `User` in favour of the new `EmailValidator`. Maintainers cannot review intent from it.

title: Validation has a side effect that inflates blocked-email match counts
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, and saves the record. It runs on every validation pass, not only when a user is actually refused. `valid?` followed by `save`, retries, or any extra validation call will count one blocked attempt several times, so the statistics become unreliable. Read-only checking should be separate from recording a block.

title: Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive while user emails are normalized
body: `where(email: email)` compares the raw string. User emails are downcased via `Email.downcase` elsewhere, and the uniqueness validation here is also case-sensitive. An entry like `Bad@Spam.com` will not match `bad@spam.com`, so a blocked address can register by changing case. The lookup and storage should normalize the email the same way.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count
body: The record is loaded, `match_count` is incremented in Ruby, and the record is saved. Concurrent signups for the same blocked address can lose increments. An atomic `update_counters`/SQL `match_count = match_count + 1` update avoids this.

title: New table added without a corresponding schema.rb update
body: The migration creates `blocked_emails`, but the change set does not touch `db/schema.rb`. Test databases built from schema.rb will not have the table, so `BlockedEmail` specs and any `User` validation that calls `should_block?` will fail with a missing-table error. The schema dump needs to be regenerated and included.

title: Signup failure response exposes blocklist membership to unauthenticated callers
body: The create endpoint is public and now returns `errors: user.errors.to_hash`. When an address is blocked, the response carries the distinct `user.email.blocked` message. Anyone can submit arbitrary addresses and learn which ones are on the blocklist. The blocked case should return the same generic message as other email rejections.

title: rejectedEmails array is shared across controller instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined on the prototype passed to `extend`, so every instance of the controller shares the same array. Rejected emails from one modal session persist into later instances. It should be initialized in `init` or per instance.

title: Domain whitelist/blacklist logic moved here without test coverage
body: The `email_domains_whitelist` and `email_domains_blacklist` checks were moved out of `User` into `EmailValidator`, but the spec only covers the blocked-email path. The moved behaviour, including the new `value =~` usage and `not_allowed` messages, is untested. There is also no test for case-insensitive blocking or for the validator being invoked from `User` validation.

title: should_block? returns nil instead of false when no record exists
body: `record && record.action_type == ...` evaluates to `nil` when no record is found. Callers relying on a boolean will get nil. The spec uses `be_false`, which passes for nil only because of RSpec 2 semantics, so the contract is loose and fragile.

title: Validation has a side effect that inflates blocked-email match counts
body: EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which increments match_count and last_match_at and saves the row. Validations are not idempotent reads: User#valid? is called explicitly in UsersController#create (`if user.valid? && SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?`) and again inside user.save, and change_username also calls valid?. A single signup attempt therefore counts as two or more matches, so match_count and last_match_at stop meaning how often the address tried to register. Any caller that validates a User for another reason (for example a console check or a background job) also increments the counter. The check should be a pure lookup, with the statistics recorded only when a registration is actually rejected.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count
body: should_block? loads the record, does `record.match_count += 1` in Ruby and then calls save. Two concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked address both read the same count and both write count+1, so increments are lost. An atomic SQL update (`BlockedEmail.where(id: ...).update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')`) would avoid this. Calling record.save also runs the model's validations on every match and can silently fail, leaving the counter unchanged.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive while users' emails are not normalized
body: should_block? does `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` with the raw value, and nothing downcases the address on the way in. User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] directly, so 'Bad@SpamClub.com' will not match a blocklist entry for 'bad@spamclub.com'. The blocklist is trivially bypassed by changing the case of the address. The code elsewhere uses Email.downcase for emails, so the lookup should normalize the same way, and the stored entries should be normalized too.

title: Response reveals that an email is on the blocklist
body: The create failure response now includes errors.to_hash, and the blocked case adds the message 'is not allowed.' under the email key. Anyone can POST to /users with a candidate address and learn whether it is blocklist-listed, and each probe also increments match_count. This is an enumeration oracle for the blocklist. The response should give a generic message for blocked addresses, or the blocklist error should be kept out of the client-visible errors.

title: Whitelist and blacklist behavior moved into the validator without tests
body: The domain whitelist and blacklist logic was moved out of User into EmailValidator in this change, but the spec only covers the BlockedEmail path with stubbed should_block?. Nothing checks that email_domains_whitelist or email_domains_blacklist still reject addresses, or that the not_allowed message is still added. The blocked-email check also runs only when no earlier error exists, which is untested. There is also no test that validation does not increment match_count for a valid address or a repeated validation.

title: Unique index on a non-normalized email column
body: The unique index is on the raw email string, so 'Bad@x.org' and 'bad@x.org' can both be inserted as separate blocklist entries. Combined with the case-sensitive lookup in should_block?, duplicate and inconsistent entries are possible. Normalizing the email before save, or indexing on a lowercased value, would prevent this.

title: Rejected emails stay blocked for the whole controller lifetime
body: rejectedEmails is an array on a singleton controller, and every address pushed by the failure callback is treated as invalid until the page reloads. Any server rejection for an email, including transient or unrelated errors such as a uniqueness or hub error, permanently marks that address invalid in the client. The client also never clears this list, and the only way to recover is to change the address. Since the server already reports the field error, the client should rely on the server response rather than keep its own permanent blocklist.

title: Feed/remote content is stored as raw HTML and rendered unsanitized
body: Imported content is created with cook_method raw_html, and Post#cook returns the raw string unchanged for that method. The content comes from an RSS/Atom feed (poll_feed.rb, after only CGI.unescapeHTML) or a remote page, and is not sanitized. Any HTML or script in a feed item ends up in cooked and is rendered in the embed view with `raw post.cooked`, which is served in an iframe with X-Frame-Options set to ALLOWALL. This is a stored XSS vector from third-party content, and it also skips the normal Markdown/sanitizing pipeline and the spam checks for these posts.

title: Unescaped feed URL interpolated into HTML attribute and link text
body: The footer is built as I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}") without escaping. The url comes from the feed's link/id field and only has to start with http(s)://. A URL containing a single quote or '>' breaks out of the attribute and injects markup into the stored post body, which is then rendered as raw HTML.

title: Caller's contents string is mutated
body: `contents << ...` appends the footer directly to the string the caller passed in. Callers that reuse the string (for example a retry, or a second import with the same variable) get the footer appended twice and a different content_sha1 each time, which causes spurious revisions.

title: Origin check uses substring match instead of equality
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any message whose origin string appears anywhere inside discourseUrl, not only an exact origin match. Partial matches such as a prefix of the configured host can pass. The check should compare the parsed origin of discourseUrl for equality with e.origin. The message handler then trusts e.data.height to resize the iframe.

title: Referer interpolated into a JavaScript string without JS escaping
body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` is placed inside a script block. ERB HTML-escaping does not make a value safe in a JS string context, so a referer containing a quote or backslash can break the script. The referer is also used as the postMessage targetOrigin. If it is missing, the call throws a SyntaxError, and a full URL with a path is passed where an origin is expected. Use a JSON-encoded origin computed on the server.

title: Stray `end if` in template produces an unintended modifier-if
body: The line `<%- end if %>` emits `end if` into the compiled template. Ruby parses `if` as a modifier whose condition is the next statement emitted (the next buffer assignment), so the header's logo link is wrapped in a meaningless conditional. The intent was to close the earlier if/else block with a plain `end`. As written, the template is confusing and the link logic is fragile.

title: One feed item without content aborts the entire feed import
body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no content element (i.content is nil). The exception propagates out of the `rss.items.each` loop, so every subsequent item in the feed is skipped. Items without a body should be skipped or default to an empty string.

title: Anonymous requests can trigger full feed polls repeatedly
body: retrieve is reached from the anonymous embed/best endpoint. The throttle is keyed on the full embed_url, so each distinct URL on the embeddable host bypasses it. Each new URL then runs Jobs::PollFeed synchronously, which downloads the entire feed over HTTP with no timeout. An anonymous client can drive unbounded outbound fetches and feed re-parsing by varying query strings.

title: Existing migration changed to force-drop the table
body: The change to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` modifies a migration that has already shipped. With force: true, the table is dropped and recreated whenever this migration runs on a database where the table exists, which destroys any data in top_topics. The original migration should not be edited; a new migration should be added if a change is needed.

title: NOT NULL column with default added to large posts table
body: Adding a NOT NULL column with a default to posts on large forums can rewrite the whole table and hold an exclusive lock for the duration, blocking writes. This is worth doing in batches or noting as a deployment risk.

title: Removed --category option without replacement or notice
body: The `category` method_option and its handling were removed from the Disqus import command. Existing invocations that pass --category now fail with an unknown-option error, or the option is silently ignored in other paths. The change also switches import from PostCreator to TopicEmbed.import_remote, which the description does not mention.

title: Test named as 404 but only checks non-success
body: The example is titled 'is 404 without an embed_url' but asserts only `should_not be_success`. Missing required params raise ActionController::ParameterMissing, which is not necessarily a 404. The test neither checks the status code nor covers the actual behavior.

title: Malformed ERB `<%- end if %>` breaks template compilation
body: The closing tag of the `if/else` at the top of the header is `<%- end if %>`. `end if` is not a valid way to close the block; the `if` modifier is left without a condition, so the template fails to compile. Any request that renders `embed/best` (the main embed path) would raise a template syntax error. The intended tag is presumably `<%- end %>`.

title: RSS/Atom item HTML is unescaped and stored as raw, unsanitized post HTML
body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` turns the feed's escaped markup back into real HTML, and `TopicEmbed.import` then stores it with `cook_method: raw_html`. `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for raw_html posts, so the content skips the sanitizing pipeline and is rendered as-is by `best.html.erb` (`raw post.cooked`). A feed item containing `<script>` or event-handler attributes becomes stored XSS in the embedding page's iframe and the forum.

title: Feed URL interpolated unescaped into HTML footer
body: The `imported_from` footer is built with `"#{url}"`, where `url` comes from the feed and is only checked with a `^https?://` prefix. A URL containing `'`, `<` or `>` breaks out of the attribute or tag. Because the post is stored as raw_html and rendered unsanitized, this is a second injection path into the post body.

title: Failed post creation is not detected before creating the TopicEmbed row
body: `PostCreator#create` returns `@post` even when validation or spam checks fail (the post is unsaved, with errors). `if post.present?` is true in that case, so `TopicEmbed.create!` runs with `post.topic_id` possibly nil. This raises a NOT NULL database error or a validation error inside the background job, rather than cleanly returning nil. The check should be `post.present? && post.persisted?`.

title: Feed items without content crash the whole poll
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item has a `content` element. Feed items with only a `description`, or no body, return nil from SimpleRSS, so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError. That aborts the loop, and all remaining items in the feed are skipped on every hourly run.

title: Each unknown embed URL triggers a synchronous full feed download
body: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever RSS polling is enabled and the URL is not yet known. That downloads and parses the entire feed and re-imports every item, with no timeout and no caching. Every distinct new URL repeats this work, so a burst of embed requests means many full feed fetches.

title: Anonymous requests can queue unbounded retrieval jobs for arbitrary URLs
body: For any unknown `embed_url`, `best` enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job. The 60-second throttle in `TopicRetriever` is keyed by the exact URL string, so each distinct query string or path on the embeddable host bypasses it. Anonymous clients can generate arbitrarily many fetch-and-create jobs against the forum and the embeddable site.

title: setnx followed by expire is not atomic
body: If the process dies between `$redis.setnx` and `$redis.expire`, the `retrieved:` key is left with no TTL. That URL is then throttled permanently. Use `SET key 1 EX 60 NX` or an equivalent single command.

title: Check-then-insert race on topic embeds
body: `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by a create is not safe under concurrency. Two jobs importing the same URL can both see no embed, and the second insert violates the unique index on `embed_url`, raising an exception after a duplicate topic and post have already been created in the transaction.

title: X-Frame-Options 'ALLOWALL' is not a valid header value
body: The valid values for X-Frame-Options are DENY and SAMEORIGIN (ALLOW-FROM is a non-standard variant). Browsers ignore unknown values, so the header has no effect. The iframe is actually allowed by the absence of a restrictive policy, and the header gives a false impression of a deliberate policy.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match instead of equality
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of the Discourse URL, not only the exact origin. The check should compare the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` for equality with `e.origin`. The impact is limited to setting the iframe height, but the check is wrong as written.

title: embed_url stored as varchar(255) with a unique index
body: `t.string :embed_url, null: false` uses the default 255-character limit. Article URLs with long query strings or paths exceed this and fail on insert in PostgreSQL. Since the value is also the unique key, a longer text column or an explicit limit with validation is needed.

title: create_table with force: true drops any existing table
body: Changing `create_table :top_topics` to `force: true` makes the migration drop and recreate the table if it already exists, for example after a partial or repeated run. That silently discards existing top_topics data. The change is unrelated to the feature and should be reverted.

title: Removed --category option without replacement or docs
body: The `--category` option is removed, and the import no longer passes category or created_at to the post. Existing scripts that pass `-c` will fail with an unknown-option error, and imported posts silently lose their category and original timestamps. The removal is not mentioned in the PR and has no replacement.

title: Test named 'is 404' does not test a 404 and passes for a different reason
body: This example has no embeddable_host set and no referer, so it fails in `ensure_embeddable` with InvalidAccess before the `embed_url` parameter is checked. The name claims a 404 for a missing embed_url, but the missing-parameter path is never exercised.

title: Stray `if` modifier on `end` makes the ERB template invalid or wrong
body: The closing tag `<%- end if %>` is a dangling `if` modifier with no condition. When ERB compiles the template, Ruby either fails with a syntax error or treats the following output code as the modifier's condition. Either way the embed `best` page, which is the main public embed view, breaks or renders incorrectly. The intended closing is a plain `<%- end %>`.

title: Remote/feed HTML is stored with cook_method raw_html and rendered unsanitized
body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html, so Post#cook returns the raw string unchanged and nothing sanitizes it. For the RSS path (PollFeed) the content is the feed's `content` field with only CGI.unescapeHTML applied, so any <script> or event-handler markup in the feed is stored verbatim. best.html.erb then outputs it with `raw post.cooked`, which is stored XSS in the embed iframe and in any other place the post is shown. Imported HTML should be sanitized (e.g. with the same tag/attribute whitelist used in import_remote) before it is stored as raw_html.

title: raw_html cook method bypasses the whole cooking and plugin filter pipeline
body: cook returns the raw text for any post whose cook_method is raw_html, skipping both PrettyText sanitization and the Plugin::Filter :after_post_cook hook. Combined with PostCreator (lib/post_creator.rb line 216) which accepts opts[:cook_method] from any caller, a code path that forwards user-supplied options to PostCreator could create unsanitized HTML posts. The cook method should be restricted to trusted internal callers, and sanitization should be applied to the raw HTML instead of skipping it.

title: postMessage targetOrigin is set to the full Referer URL, so resize messages are dropped
body: postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (scheme, host, port). Passing request.referer, which is a full URL including path and query, makes the browser fail to match the parent window, so the discourse-resize message is silently not delivered and the iframe never grows. Also, the value is injected into a JavaScript string with ERB output, which is fragile. The origin should be computed from the referer, or '*' should be avoided and the parent origin validated explicitly.

title: Origin check uses substring matching instead of exact origin comparison
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` treats any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl as trusted. This is a loose check that should be an exact comparison of e.origin against the origin parsed from discourseUrl. Messages from unintended origins can then drive the iframe height. The e.data.height value is also used unvalidated in `iframe.height = e.data.height + "px"`.

title: Behavior change: update_post now validates per opts but is also used by import paths without guard
body: The change from @post.save to @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) is fine on its own, but PostRevisor.revise! with skip_validations is now used by TopicEmbed.import on the update path with bypass_rate_limiter. A failed save here is ignored: update_post does not check the return value, and TopicEmbed.import then calls embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...) anyway. The stored content hash then records a revision that was never saved, so future imports will not retry the update.

title: Feed item without content raises NoMethodError and aborts the entire poll
body: `i.content.scrub` is called unconditionally. Feed entries that only have a summary, or no body, return nil for content and raise NoMethodError. Because this runs inside rss.items.each, one such item stops the import of every later item in the feed, and the hourly job fails each time. The nil case should be handled (fall back to summary or skip the item).

title: import mutates the caller's contents string with `<<`
body: `contents << ...` modifies the string passed in by the caller. PollFeed passes content from a parsed feed and import_remote passes doc.content, so the caller's object is changed. Calling import twice with the same string appends the footer twice, and the content hash for the second call changes. The footer should be added to a new string (e.g. `contents = contents + ...`).

title: Concurrent imports of the same URL can create duplicate topics or raise RecordNotUnique
body: The check `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by creating a topic and then `TopicEmbed.create!` is not protected by a lock. Two concurrent imports (e.g. retrieve_topic jobs for the same URL from different anonymous visitors, or PollFeed overlapping with a retrieve job) both see no embed and both create a post. One then fails the unique index on embed_url with ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, causing the job to error, and the transaction rolls back the post. The import should handle that exception or use a lock keyed on the URL.

title: X-Frame-Options value ALLOWALL is not a valid header value
body: The only valid X-Frame-Options values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN and ALLOW-FROM <uri>. Browsers ignore unknown values, so the header does not express the intended policy. Framing permission should be expressed via a Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive that lists the embeddable host, or the header should be removed deliberately with a comment explaining the choice.

title: create_table with force: true silently drops an existing table and its data
body: If the topic_embeds table already exists when this migration runs, force: true drops it and every existing embed mapping is lost. Each lost mapping means the next request for that URL creates a duplicate topic. A migration should not drop tables. Plain create_table without force is the safe choice.

title: Edited an already-shipped migration to add force: true
body: Adding force: true to an existing migration changes its behavior on any database where it has not run yet, and it will drop any top_topics table that exists at that time. Changing a migration that may have been run in another environment is risky. A new migration should be used for any schema correction.

title: Removed the --category option without replacement and changed import semantics
body: The disqus import command's `--category` option is removed silently. Users who pass -c now get a Thor error. The import also switches from creating topics directly to TopicEmbed.import_remote, which downloads each thread's link and creates a topic from the page, not from the Disqus data. Rerunning the import now appends comments to existing embed topics. The behavior change needs to be documented, and the removed option needs a replacement or a deprecation message.

title: Test named 'is 404' asserts only not-success and runs before the guard that actually fails
body: The example 'is 404 without an embed_url' does not check for a 404. Without stubs, the before_filter ensure_embeddable raises first because embeddable_host is blank, so the test passes for an unrelated reason. The missing-parameter path (params.require) is never exercised. The test should stub the host and referer and assert the status that the missing parameter actually produces.

title: No test covers the feed import logic in poll_feed
body: The spec only checks that poll_feed is delegated to when the settings are present. The actual item handling (URL fallback to id, nil content, the import call) is untested, which is why the nil-content crash in poll_feed goes unnoticed. Tests should cover items with missing content and invalid links.

title: PR description is a placeholder and does not explain the feature
body: The description reads 'Test 4', so reviewers have no information on the embed feature, the new feed polling and remote import behavior, the new raw_html cook method, or the disqus import change. The description should summarize these and the security implications of importing HTML.

title: Bullet badge margin-top rule removed without replacement
body: The diff deletes the `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule under `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper` and does not add it back elsewhere. The bullet badges in the extra-info wrapper lose their vertical offset, so they will misalign relative to the text. The PR does not mention this visual change.

title: order(2) and line-height change applied to a non-flex element
body: `@include order(2)` only has an effect when `.extra-info-wrapper` is a child of a flex container, and nothing in this diff makes its parent a flex container. The added `line-height: 1.5` on the whole wrapper is also an unrelated visual change that is not described. Either the rule is dead code or it changes the layout in ways the PR does not account for.

title: Small-action description padding change breaks the avatar indent
body: `.small-action-desc` padding changes from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`, removing the 4em left indent and the vertical padding, and `.small-action` becomes a flex row. The description text can now sit under or beside the avatar and lose its vertical spacing. Nothing in the PR justifies these changes, and there is no evidence they were verified against the small-action markup.

title: -ms-align-items is not a real property
body: The `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items`, which no browser supports. It is a dead declaration and suggests the prefix list was not checked. It should be removed, and the mixin should use `-ms-flex-align` only, which is already present.

title: order mixin maps to old box-model ordinal group with different semantics
body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based and only meaningful inside the old `-webkit-box` model. Emitting them alongside `order` for a `display: flex` element can produce ordering that differs between browsers. `order(3)` in header.scss therefore may not place `.panel` consistently across engines.

title: PR title and description do not match the change
body: The title says the change optimizes performance, but the diff is a layout rewrite (float to flexbox, removed `.title` float, reordered `.panel`) with no benchmark or rendering measurement. The description is just 'Test 5'. A maintainer cannot tell the intent or the expected visual effect from the PR.

title: Bullet margin-top removed and line-height added to whole extra-info wrapper without justification
body: In the `.extra-info-wrapper` rule, the `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` block for `.badge-wrapper` is deleted, and `line-height: 1.5` is added to the wrapper itself. The removed rule vertically offset bullet badges in this area, and nothing replaces it. The line-height now applies to every descendant, not just badges, so text and other children in this header area can shift height. The PR is about flexbox layout, so these visual changes look unintended and are not covered by the description.

title: `.title` float rule deleted from header without replacement
body: The `.d-header .title { float: left; }` rule is removed and nothing takes its place. If any header markup still uses a `.title` element, it loses its left placement. Under the new flex container, floats on flex items are ignored anyway, so the only way the element keeps its position is through the flex order. The author should confirm no header element depends on `.title` or add an explicit replacement.

title: Flexbox on .small-action makes its float-based children and clear ineffective, with padding removed
body: `.small-action` becomes a flex container, but its children still rely on floats: `.topic-avatar { float: left }`, `.small-action-desc .avatar { float: left }`, and `button { float: right }`. Floats are ignored on flex items, so these no longer behave as before. The `clear: both` on the container is also meaningless for a flex container. In addition, the `.small-action-desc` vertical padding and the 4em left padding (which reserved room for the avatar) were removed and replaced with `padding: 0 1.5%`, and the `margin-top: 5px` and `padding-top: 4px` were dropped. The left-side space that was reserved for the avatar now depends entirely on flex sizing, so this is a visible layout change in small action posts that needs visual verification.

title: align-items mixin emits invalid or misapplied vendor properties
body: The `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a real property and is never valid. It also emits `-webkit-box-align` alongside `-webkit-align-items`, which only has an effect on `display: -webkit-box` containers. Since `.contents` and `.small-action` use the modern `display: flex` value, the old-spec properties are dead code. These are harmless in most browsers but are misleading and should be removed or corrected.

title: PR description is uninformative and performance claim is unsupported
body: The PR description is just 'Test 5', so a reviewer gets no rationale for changing layout from floats to flexbox across header, topic, post and badge styles. The title says 'Optimize ... performance', but no measurement or reasoning is given, and the change is mainly a visual layout rewrite. Without the rationale, reviewers cannot judge the trade-offs or what visual regressions are expected.

title: Bullet margin rule removed from extra-info badge wrapper without replacement
body: The diff deletes the `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule nested under `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper`. Nothing replaces it, so bullet-style category badges in the extra-info area lose their 5px top offset and the vertical alignment they relied on. The PR's stated goal is performance, and this is an unrelated visual regression.

title: Float rules on children of the new flex container are ignored
body: `.small-action` becomes a flex container (line 264-265), but its children still rely on floats: `.topic-avatar { float: left }` (line 270), `.avatar { float: left }` and the `button { float: right }` at line 309. Floated flex items are ignored, so the avatar and action buttons will be positioned differently than before. Those floats need to be replaced with flex properties or the layout needs to be verified.

title: Unrelated spacing changes to .small-action-desc alter the layout
body: The padding of `.small-action-desc` changes from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` plus `margin-top: 5px` to `padding: 0 1.5%` (line 280). The left indent of 4em is removed, along with the `padding-top: 4px` on `> p` and the `margin: 5px 0` on `.custom-message p`. These are visual changes that a flexbox conversion does not require, and the PR does not explain them. They will shift the text and avatar alignment in small action rows.

title: Removal of the .title float rule and .panel float may break header markup
body: The `.title { float: left; }` rule is deleted from `.d-header .contents`, and `.panel` switches from `float: right` to `margin-left: auto` with `order(3)` (lines 17-19 and 36-41). These only work if every affected child is a direct flex item of `.contents`. Any `.title` element nested deeper, or any child that is not a flex item, will lose its float with no replacement. Nothing in the PR shows this was checked.

title: Flexbox mixins added without checking for existing definitions
body: New `flexbox`, `inline-flex`, `align-items` and `order` mixins are appended to the shared foundation file. If equivalent mixins already exist elsewhere in the stylesheets, Sass will silently use the later definition, and the mixin's vendor prefixes or argument handling can change every existing `@include` site. The PR does not show that the names are unique. Also, `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a real property and should be removed.

title: website_name leaks the website for TL0 users hidden from anonymous viewers
body: `:website_name` is added to the public `attributes` list (line 43) and is not included in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111). `website` is in that list, so for a TL0 user seen by anonymous/untrusted viewers the `website` key is suppressed. `website_name` is still serialized, with `include_website_name?` only checking `website.present?`. It returns the host and, for same-domain sites, the full path, so the hidden website is still exposed. The TL0 spec (spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb lines 11-14) does not list `website_name`, so the gap is not caught. Add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` or make `include_website_name?` respect `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`, and extend the spec.

title: String mutation via `<<` on a literal in the subdomain check
body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` mutates the `"."` literal in place. It works today only because string literals are mutable and not frozen. It breaks under `# frozen_string_literal: true` or future Ruby defaults, and is a confusing construction. Use `"." + website_host` or interpolation.

title: Path appended without checking it is present
body: The same-domain and parent-domain branches concatenate `URI(website.to_s).path`, which can be nil for some parsed URIs. Also, `website_host` is computed with `rescue nil` but the URI is parsed again in each branch. Parse the URI once, guard the path, and fall back to the host when it is empty, so the result does not end in an unexpected nil or stray slash.

title: Template depends on website_name, which is absent from some user payloads
body: The template now checks `model.website_name` and renders it. The previous client-side `websiteName` computed derived the value from `model.website`. Any user object that does not come from UserSerializer (for example models built from other serializers or the current-user preload) will have no `website_name`, so the link disappears even when a website is set. Confirm all places that render this template load the full serializer, or keep a fallback.

title: website_name is exposed to users for whom website is restricted
body: `include_website_name` checks only `website.present?`, but `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so for TL0 users seen by anonymous/restricted scopes the `website` key is omitted. `website_name` is not in that list and its inclusion check reads the raw website, so it is still serialized and reveals the host (and path, when the domain matches the instance) of the hidden website. The spec's 'doesn't serialize untrusted attributes' test does not include `website_name`, so this is not caught. Fix by applying the same `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` guard, or by adding `website_name` to the untrusted attribute list.

title: website_name leaks website data for TL0 users whose website is hidden
body: `website` and `bio_raw`, `location` and similar fields are listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so anonymous viewers of TL0 users do not receive them. `website_name` is not in that list, and `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?`. For an anonymous viewer of a TL0 user, `website_name` is therefore still serialized, and it now includes the URL path (e.g. `example.com/user`) when the host matches the instance. This bypasses the trust gating the `website` field relies on, and it exposes more of the URL than the host-only value did before. The TL0 spec's untrusted attribute list also does not include `website_name`, so the gap is untested.

title: website_name is parsed and computed repeatedly, and URI errors are swallowed by a modifier rescue
body: `website_name` calls `URI(website.to_s)` up to three times and `website.to_s` each time, and `website` itself goes through `object.user_profile`. The `rescue nil` modifier on the first assignment silently turns any malformed URL into nil with no logging. This is minor, but a single parse with an explicit rescue would be clearer and cheaper.

title: Path appended for a bare-root website yields a trailing slash
body: When the website is `http://example.com/` (path `/`), the same-domain branch returns `example.com/`. A website of `http://example.com` returns `example.com`. The two inputs display differently even though they point to the same site. Normalising the path (or treating `/` as empty) would avoid this.

title: No test that website_name is withheld from anonymous viewers of TL0 users
body: The untrusted attributes list checked by the TL0 context does not include `website_name`, and no test asserts it is hidden when `website` is hidden. Adding `website_name` to that list (and the matching serializer gating) would be covered by such a test, which would have caught the leak.

title: Template now depends on website_name being present, not on the website itself
body: The condition changed from `websiteName` (derived from `model.website`) to `model.website_name`. Because `website_name` is serialized independently of the trust gating on `website`, the link block can render for viewers who see no website URL. The `href` is then empty while the visible text still shows the name. This is coupled to the serializer leak above.

title: Tests stub Discourse.current_hostname but do not cover the 'same length' sibling-subdomain branch
body: The three new tests cover exact match, parent domain, and unrelated domain. The branch where both hosts have the same number of labels and share a registrable domain (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) is not exercised, so a regression in that comparison would go unnoticed.

title: PR description is a placeholder
body: The description reads only 'Test 6' and does not explain the behaviour change (website name now includes the path when the host matches the instance) or the reason for moving display logic from the controller to the serializer. Reviewers have no context for the intended change.

title: Pull request has no description or verification of the visual change

Over 30 stylesheet files are touched, and several of the replacements change light-theme values (see the other findings). title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. With user_count = 100 and limit = 50 it returns 3, but only 2 pages exist. The 'next' action then sets offset to 100 and loads an empty page, and showingLast stays false on page 2. The same applies to any exact multiple. The page count should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit).
