body: The case 'error when listing an object in the unified store is not implemented' tests a real List error path, so the name is misleading. The List behaviour itself (reads only from unified storage) is not asserted against the legacy mock either.

title: Unrelated dependency checksums added to go.work.sum
body: The go.work.sum changes add checksums for unrelated modules (grafana-azure-sdk-go, prometheus-alertmanager, otel exporters and others) that this mode 3 change does not touch. This suggests an unrelated dependency resolution leaked into the PR and should be explained or dropped.

title: No re-check of the cache after acquiring the write lock
body: The function reads the cache under RLock, releases it, and then takes the write Lock unconditionally. If several requests arrive while the cache is still nil, or while a dev-mode request is in flight, each one passes the first check and then rebuilds the manifest from disk (and possibly the CDN) in turn. Once a goroutine holds the write lock, it should re-check entryPointAssetsCache (for non-dev) and return it if another goroutine has already populated it. Without that, the lock only serializes the work and does not avoid the duplicate loads.

title: Write lock is held across I/O, including the CDN HTTP fetch with no timeout
body: The write lock is acquired before readWebAssetsFromCDN and readWebAssetsFromFile run, and it is held until the function returns. readWebAssetsFromCDN uses http.DefaultClient, which has no timeout. If the CDN is slow or hangs, every RLock caller, including all non-dev requests that only want the cached value, blocks behind the writer for the whole fetch, and the request context is the only bound. Before this change, cached readers never waited on a writer. Consider doing the I/O outside the lock and taking the lock only to publish the result, or at least bounding the HTTP call with a timeout.

title: No test covers the concurrent access this change is meant to fix
body: The PR fixes a data race, but no test is added or updated. A test that calls GetWebAssets from many goroutines (run with -race) and checks that the cache is populated consistently would confirm the fix and guard against regressions. The existing behaviour around cache publication on error (the cache is set to nil and the error returned) is also untested.

title: Write lock taken without re-checking the cache, and held across file and CDN I/O
body: The fast path reads the cache under RLock, releases it, then takes the write lock at line 48 without checking the cache again. Every goroutine that misses the cache during startup, or after a failed load, will queue on the write lock and each one re-runs the manifest read and, when configured, the HTTP fetch to the CDN. The lock is held for the whole rebuild (lines 48-70), including the network call in readWebAssetsFromCDN, which has no timeout beyond the request context. Before this change, readers never blocked. Now every request that reaches GetWebAssets blocks on the write lock for as long as a slow CDN takes to respond. Fix: after acquiring the write lock, re-read entryPointAssetsCache and return it if it is now non-nil and not in Dev mode. Consider doing the I/O outside the lock and taking the lock only to publish the result.

title: Error path caches nil and returns a stale-looking result
body: On error, result is nil and line 69 overwrites the global cache with nil, so the cache is cleared even if a previous good value existed (for example, in Dev mode where the cache is reloaded on every call). The function then returns nil with err. Callers that ignore err will get a nil pointer. This behaviour is unchanged by the diff, but the new locking makes it more visible: a transient read failure during a Dev reload now clears the shared cache for concurrent readers. Consider only assigning the cache when err == nil.

title: No test covers the concurrent access this change is meant to fix
body: The PR fixes a data race on entryPointAssetsCache, but no test is added or changed. A test that calls GetWebAssets from multiple goroutines, ideally under go test -race and covering both Dev and non-Dev environments, would show the race is fixed and would catch the locking regression described above.

title: Cache is not re-checked after acquiring the write lock
body: The fast path reads entryPointAssetsCache under RLock, releases it, and then unconditionally takes the write Lock and reloads the manifest. If several requests arrive before the cache is populated (first load, or every request in dev mode), they all pass the RLock check and each performs the full file or CDN load, one after another. Re-checking entryPointAssetsCache after taking the write lock would let later callers reuse the result from the first one. In dev mode the reload is intentional, so the impact there is limited to the first-load case.

title: Write lock is held across network I/O, blocking all readers
body: entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() is taken before readWebAssetsFromCDN(ctx, cdn) (line 56), which performs an HTTP GET via http.DefaultClient with no timeout of its own. While the CDN fetch is in flight, every other GetWebAssets call blocks on RLock at line 41, even if it would otherwise have been served from the cache. A slow or hanging CDN therefore stalls all page requests that call GetWebAssets. The lock should cover only the assignment to the global, or the fetch should be done outside the lock and the result stored afterwards.

title: A failed reload overwrites the last good cache with nil
body: On any error, result is nil and line 69 unconditionally executes entryPointAssetsCache = result. In dev mode, where the cache is reloaded on every call, a transient failure (for example a manifest being rewritten during a build) discards the previously valid assets, and the next call then fails too until the file is fixed. Storing the result only when err == nil would keep the last good value. The diff does not change this behaviour, but the locking refactor is the natural place to address it.

title: No test covers concurrent access to the cache
body: The PR is a data-race fix, but it adds no test that exercises GetWebAssets from multiple goroutines, such as a test run under go test -race. Without one, the fix cannot be verified and regressions to the locking will not be caught.

title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, so the feature flag is dead and the check is misleading
body: The function computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns false on both branches of the `if`. The result is always false, so SQL expressions are rejected whether or not the `sqlExpressions` flag is on. The flag check is dead code. The error 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' is also wrong for operators who have deliberately enabled the flag: they get a message that suggests the feature is missing rather than disabled for security reasons. A maintainer reading this will not see that the disable is intentional. Make the disable an explicit constant or a clearly commented early return, with an error message that says the feature is disabled for security reasons.

title: TablesList now always fails, so existing tests of SQL parsing are likely broken or unchanged
body: After the change, `sql.TablesList` calls the stub `DB.RunCommands`, which always returns 'not implemented'. Every call to `TablesList` therefore returns an error. The PR changes no test files. Any existing parser or SQL command tests that expect table names from a valid query will fail, and nothing in the diff updates or removes them. The rest of the function (the quote escaping and the JSON AST flattening) is now unreachable in practice. Either remove or skip those tests with a clear reason, or add tests that assert the disabled behaviour.

title: Stub DB type and NewInMemoryDB look like a working in-memory database
body: `DB` and `NewInMemoryDB` are exported from package `sql` and used as if they were a real engine, but every method returns 'not implemented'. `TablesList` on the stub is never called by the new code. Nothing in the file says this is a deliberate disable placeholder. A future caller could reasonably assume it works, and the 'not implemented' errors are surfaced to users as generic 'error reading SQL command' bad requests, which hides the real reason. Add a comment explaining the stub and why it exists.

title: Hashes for thrift, asmfmt, minio and others are moved from go.sum to go.work.sum
body: The diff removes `h1:` hashes for `apache/thrift v0.20.0`, `klauspost/asmfmt`, `minio/asm2plan9s`, `minio/c2goasm`, and `google/go-replayers` from go.sum and adds them to go.work.sum. The module graph is not otherwise changed. This suggests the lockfile was regenerated under a workspace, not with `GOWORK=off`. Anything that builds without the workspace (for example a downstream module importing grafana/grafana, or CI with GOWORK=off) may fail with missing checksum errors if those modules are still required. The go.mod removals (go-duck, thrift, go-which, orderedmap) should be checked against `go mod tidy` run with GOWORK=off so the dependency files agree.

title: Feature-flag documentation still describes SQL expressions as usable
body: The PR leaves the `sqlExpressions` flag registered and documented, but after this change the flag no longer enables anything. Operators who read the docs and turn the flag on will get a failing SQL expression with no explanation in the docs. The PR description defers the docs update, but at minimum the doc should say the feature is disabled for this security release, so operators are not misled.

title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, making the feature-flag check meaningless
body: The helper reads the FlagSqlExpressions toggle, negates it, and then returns false on both branches, so it is hard-coded to false regardless of the flag. The flag check at the call site in ReadQuery therefore never does anything useful. The disable is intended, but the code reads as if it honours the flag. Anyone who later edits one branch could unintentionally re-enable SQL expressions. The helper should be replaced with an explicit unconditional rejection, with a comment stating that SQL expressions are disabled for the security fix.

title: No test covers the new SQL-disabled rejection path
body: The PR changes ReadQuery so that QueryTypeSQL always returns 'sqlExpressions is not implemented', but no test was added or updated to assert this. Without a test, a future change that re-enables the path (for example by fixing enableSqlExpressions) would not be caught. A regression test should assert that a SQL query is rejected with and without the feature flag enabled.

title: NoData result is unconditionally overwritten by TableData
body: When frame.Rows() == 0, rsp.Values is set to NoData, but the next statement unconditionally reassigns rsp.Values to TableData. The NoData branch is dead code, so empty SQL results are always returned as TableData. This is pre-existing and not introduced by the PR, but it sits in the same Execute function being edited here and should be fixed (for example with an else).

title: enableSqlExpressions ignores the feature flag and always returns false
body: The helper computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns false on both branches (`if enabled { return false }; return false`). The feature flag therefore has no effect, and the function reads as if it checks the flag when it does not. Any future change that re-enables SQL expressions by fixing only the stub in db.go would also need this function rewritten. The function should be replaced by a plain, explicit disable with a comment explaining why, or the flag check should be restored and gated behind the real implementation.

title: SQL gate exists only in the reader; the security fix relies on the stub returning errors
body: The only explicit disable is in ReadQuery's QueryTypeSQL branch. The exported UnmarshalSQLCommand in pkg/expr/sql_command.go (line ~68) calls NewSQLCommand directly, and SQLCommand.Execute (line ~96) runs db.QueryFramesInto with no check. The code is therefore safe only because sql.TablesList happens to fail through the stub RunCommands in db.go. If any caller builds a SQLCommand directly, or the stub is replaced with a real implementation, the SQL path is reachable again. The disable should be enforced at NewSQLCommand and/or Execute, not only in one reader branch.

title: tablesFromAST indexes ast[0] without a length check
body: tablesFromAST does `flatten.Flatten(ast[0], ...)`. If the JSON from the backend is an empty array, this panics with index out of range. The stub now means this path is unreachable in practice, but the function is still present and reachable from TablesList if the DB is ever reimplemented. A length check is needed before indexing.

title: Stub DB silently replaces the real engine; parser JSON path is now dead code
body: DB.TablesList, RunCommands and QueryFramesInto all return 'not implemented' errors. Nothing documents that this is a deliberate security stub, and the TablesList parsing in parser.go (including the rawSQL quote-escaping and the json_serialize_sql logic) is now dead code that no test exercises. A maintainer reading this later could mistake the stub for a missing implementation and re-enable it without the required review. A comment stating the reason and the intended re-enable conditions is needed.

title: No tests added or updated for the disabled SQL expression behaviour
body: The PR changes SQL expression behaviour from functional to always-rejected, but no test was added to assert that a SQL query type returns an error, and existing SQL-related tests in pkg/expr were not updated. Without a regression test, a future change could re-enable SQL execution silently. The PR description also notes the feature-flag documentation was not updated, so the flag now does nothing while still appearing in the feature toggle list.

title: Removing the BuildIndex lock lets concurrent builds for the same key race and leak indexes
body: The mutex was removed from the whole of BuildIndex and now only guards the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write. Two callers can build the same namespace/resource at once, for example init() running while getOrCreateIndex is triggered by a Search or a watch event. For file-backed indexes both call `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same directory, so one fails. For memory indexes both succeed, and the second cache write silently overwrites the first, which is never closed or flushed to disk. The original lock prevented this. Either restore per-key serialization (singleflight or a per-key mutex) or document that callers must never build the same key concurrently.

title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding cacheMu
body: TotalDocs ranges over `b.cache` with no lock, while BuildIndex now writes `b.cache[key]` under `cacheMu.Lock()` and GetIndex reads it under RLock. The new `s.log.Info(... "total_docs", s.search.TotalDocs())` in searchSupport.init, and any other caller, can run concurrently with a background build from getOrCreateIndex or handleEvent. Go map read/write races can crash the process with 'concurrent map read and map write'. TotalDocs should take `cacheMu.RLock()`.

title: Errgroup goroutines write to shared outer variables err and totalBatchesIndexed
body: Inside the `group.Go` closure, `_, _, err = s.build(...)` assigns to the `err` declared in init(), and `totalBatchesIndexed++` mutates a shared int. Several goroutines run in parallel (SetLimit(initWorkers)), so this is a data race. A build error can also be overwritten or lost, and the value of `err` read after `group.Wait()` is not the error from the goroutine. The closure should declare its own local `err`, and the counter should be an atomic or be computed after Wait.

title: Startup now fails hard if lifecycle init or the full index build fails
body: Previously a failed Init was recorded in initErr and only surfaced on later RPCs, so the server still started. Now NewResourceServer returns an error when lifecycle.Init or search.init fails, and search.init blocks construction until every namespace is indexed. This changes module startup ordering and failure behaviour, and it runs lifecycle hooks (e.g. DB init) at construction time rather than on first use. Callers that construct the server before the database or other dependencies are ready can now fail at startup. This needs to be checked against the module wiring. Also, on this error path the `cancel` for the context created above is never called, so the background context leaks.

title: GetResourceStats never closes the rows result set
body: In the WithTx closure, `rows, err := dbutil.QueryRows(...)` is iterated but `rows.Close()` is never called, and `rows.Err()` is never checked. The function was modified in this PR, and the leak holds a DB connection/transaction resource until the transaction ends. Errors encountered during iteration are silently dropped, which can produce partial stats and a wrong index build. Add `defer rows.Close()` and check `rows.Err()`.

title: Postgres variant of the storage-server test is silently skipped
body: The new early return skips the test entirely for postgres with a comment that it is broken in CI. This hides any regression in the storage server startup path that this PR changes (the Init move into the constructor) for postgres runs, with no tracking issue referenced. The change is also unrelated to the stated PR scope.

title: Data race on shared `err` and counter in parallel index build goroutines
body: Inside `init`, each `group.Go` closure runs concurrently and does `totalBatchesIndexed++` (line 189) and `_, _, err = s.build(...)` (line 190). Both `totalBatchesIndexed` and the outer `err` are shared across goroutines, so this is a data race. A failing build can also overwrite another goroutine's error, so `group.Wait()`'s result may not reflect the real failure. The fix is to use a local `err` inside the closure and an atomic counter. This matters more now because the index is built synchronously in the constructor and the locking was made finer, so more builds run concurrently.

title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding cacheMu
body: `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` with no lock, while `BuildIndex` writes to the same map under `cacheMu.Lock()`. The commit removed the whole-function lock and only leaves the map write protected, so this read is now clearly unsynchronized. Concurrent `BuildIndex` calls (for example from `search.init` or a watch-triggered `getOrCreateIndex`) can cause a 'concurrent map read and map write' fatal error. `TotalDocs` should take `cacheMu.RLock()`.

title: Finer locking lets concurrent builds for the same key race and overwrite each other
body: Removing the function-wide lock means two `BuildIndex` calls for the same NamespacedResource can run at once. This can happen when `getOrCreateIndex` builds on a Search request while `search.init` is still building the same key, or when a watch event triggers a build. Both paths call `bleve.New` on the same directory for file-backed indexes, and the second call fails. For in-memory indexes, the second build silently replaces the cache entry, leaking the first index and any writes made to it. Nothing in `getOrCreateIndex` or `BuildIndex` deduplicates builds per key, and the TODO in `getOrCreateIndex` acknowledges this. A per-key singleflight or lock is needed before this change is safe.

title: Index build failures now make NewResourceServer fail hard, changing startup behavior
body: Init is now called synchronously from the constructor, so any error from `search.init` (for example `GetResourceStats` failing, or a bad index build) makes `NewResourceServer` return an error and the whole service fail to start. Previously these errors only surfaced as per-RPC errors and the service stayed up. The `once`/`initErr` mechanism also means the failure is never retried. The PR notes ask exactly this question about what depends on lazy initialization, and the description does not address the startup-failure behavior. Callers in module wiring and tests need to be checked, and the behavior change should be documented or tested.

title: Events written during the index build are never indexed
body: `init` lists resources and builds the index first, and only afterwards calls `WatchWriteEvents`. The SQL backend's poller starts from the latest resource version at the time `WatchWriteEvents` is called, so any write that lands between the `ListIterator` snapshot and that call is never replayed into the index. The index can therefore stay permanently stale for those objects. Now that the build runs at startup in the constructor and can take a long time, the window is larger. The watch should be started before the build, with events buffered and applied after the build.

title: Context cancel function is leaked when startup Init fails
body: `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(...)` is created earlier in `NewResourceServer`. When `s.Init(ctx)` fails, the function returns `nil, err` without calling `s.cancel()`, and any goroutines started by the lifecycle hook or by `initWatcher`/`search.init` keep running with no owner. The error path should call `cancel()`.

title: Unrelated postgres skip added to the storage server integration test
body: The PR adds a skip for postgres in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer`. Nothing in the PR's stated changes (lazy init removal, tracing, locking) relates to postgres. The skip silently removes coverage for the storage-server startup path, which is the path this PR changes, and the TODO gives no tracking issue. Either the test should be fixed or the skip justified in the PR.

title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows concurrent duplicate builds of the same key
body: The whole-function lock in BuildIndex was removed and only the final cache write is now locked. Nothing else serializes builds for the same NamespacedResource. getOrCreateIndex in search.go checks GetIndex, finds nothing, and calls build. Two concurrent Search or watch-event requests for a cold namespace can therefore both reach bleve.New(dir, mapper) for the same file-based directory. The second call fails because the path already exists, or the two builds race on the same index. Even in memory, the last writer silently wins and the other index is leaked. A per-key singleflight or per-key mutex is needed to keep the 'only lock the same key' goal without allowing duplicate builds.

title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding cacheMu
body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache with no lock, while BuildIndex now writes to b.cache under cacheMu.Lock at line 138. This is a data race on the map and can cause a fatal 'concurrent map read and map write' at runtime. It is called from search.init's log line, and the new log line is in the same area. The read should take cacheMu.RLock.

title: Shared err and totalBatchesIndexed are written from concurrent goroutines
body: Inside the errgroup loop, each goroutine does `_, _, err = s.build(...)` and `totalBatchesIndexed++`. Both variables are declared in the enclosing init scope and are shared across goroutines running with SetLimit(s.initWorkers). Concurrent writes are a data race. The error from the outer `err` can also be overwritten or misreported. The goroutine should use a local err and a local counter, or an atomic.

title: Constructor now blocks on full index build and fails startup on index errors
body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init synchronously, which runs lifecycle.Init, the full search index build for every namespace (GetResourceStats plus BuildIndex), and the watcher setup. Previously this work happened lazily on the first request. Consequences: process startup now waits for every index to build, and any index or lifecycle failure makes the constructor return an error and the whole module fail to start, instead of failing individual requests. The gRPC and HTTP servers that depend on this object may also be wired before the backend is ready. The description asks what this breaks. The answer is that the failure mode and startup ordering change for every deployment, and that should be confirmed against the module wiring.

title: Init failure in constructor leaks the cancelable context and background goroutines
body: When s.Init fails, NewResourceServer returns nil without calling s.cancel(). The context created at line ~229 and any watcher or broadcaster started during initWatcher are never stopped. Calling s.Stop or cancel on the failure path would avoid the leak.

title: Span name has a double dot
body: tracePrefix already ends with '.', and the span is named tracePrefix+".GetResourceStats", which yields 'sql.resource..GetResourceStats'. The other spans in this file use tracePrefix+"WriteEvent" with no extra dot, so this name is inconsistent and wrong.

title: BuildIndex still discards the span context, so the trace fix is incomplete
body: The PR says it fixes trace propagation by passing span contexts down. BuildIndex still does `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)`, so the ctx it received is not propagated to its children. The same pattern exists in sql/backend.go WriteEvent, ReadResource, ListIterator and WatchWriteEvents. The description overstates what was fixed.

title: Test is now silently skipped on postgres
body: A new early skip for postgres was added. The test is therefore no longer exercised in CI for postgres, and the 'TODO - fix this test' comment gives no tracking reference. This is an unrelated change that reduces coverage in a PR about index startup. It should be a separate, tracked change or be removed.

title: Call to non-existent zero-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
body: The condition calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition added in this PR is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in UsernamePasswordForm, and no zero-argument overload exists in the diff or in the file. The services module will fail to compile, so none of the passkey re-authentication fixes can ship. The intended call is likely `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

title: NoSuchElementException import left unused after test assertions were replaced
body: The diff removed the only uses of `NoSuchElementException` in this file (the `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` calls in passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey). The import on line 51 is now unused, which will produce a compiler/checkstyle warning.

title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() has no matching no-arg overload and will not compile
body: The new condition calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition added in UsernamePasswordForm.java is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, and nothing in the diff adds a no-arg overload. The services module will fail to compile, which blocks the whole PR. The intended call is presumably `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which is also what the surrounding `context.getUser() != null` check suggests.

title: NoSuchElementException import is left unused after the assertThrows removal
body: The two `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` calls were replaced with `MatcherAssert.assertThat(...)`, but the `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` import at line 51 is still present and no longer referenced in this file. Unused imports fail checkstyle/impsort builds in Keycloak, so this can break CI.

title: Conditional passkey UI is no longer rendered on the initial login page (no user set)
body: The block that calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) is now guarded by isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()). That helper returns false when user == null (`... && user != null`). On the normal first-step login, where no user is in the context, the guard is false, so the WebAuthn conditional UI data is never filled. The previous code filled it exactly in that case (`if (webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled())` inside the no-user branch). Result: discoverable passkeys stop appearing in the username/password login page, which is the main passkey login path, and the existing tests that expect the 'username webauthn' autocomplete and the webauth form on the first page would fail.

title: Error challenge drops passkey data when no user has been identified yet
body: challenge(context, error, field) now only calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true, which requires a non-null user. Previously the call was made when the user was null (the conditional UI case). So when the username/password form is re-rendered with an error before any user is identified, the passkey (conditional UI) setup is lost and the page no longer offers passkey login.

title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not match the declared method
body: In UsernamePasswordForm the only declaration added is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which takes one argument. Here it is called as `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no argument. Unless another no-arg overload exists (none is shown in the diff), this does not compile, so the services module would fail to build.

title: configureTestRealm(...) is called but not defined in this class
body: addTestRealms calls configureTestRealm(realmRepresentation). The method is not declared in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest, and the diff does not add it. If it is not inherited from AbstractWebAuthnVirtualTest, the test class will not compile. Even if it is inherited, the reviewer needs to confirm which realm changes it applies, since the diff does not show them.

title: Constant widened from protected to public without need
body: USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is changed from protected to public so AuthenticatorUtils (in another package) can import it. This exposes an internal authenticator note key as public API of an exported class. A public accessor or moving the constant to a shared util class would avoid expanding the public surface of AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.

title: NoSuchElementException import is left unused after the assertion change
body: After replacing the two Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) checks with findElement assertions, the NoSuchElementException import on line 51 is no longer referenced in this file. This will produce an unused import warning and may fail a checkstyle or lint build.

title: PR description is only a placeholder
body: The description reads only 'Test 1'. It does not explain the bug being fixed (passkey re-authentication with prompt=login), the approach, or the behaviour change to the conditional UI for users who are not yet identified. A maintainer reviewing this change would need that context, especially given the regression risk in the conditional UI logic.

title: Cleanup removes a hard-coded "alias" IdP instead of the created IdPs
body: The cleanup `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` binds the literal alias "alias", not the `idp-alias-N` identity provider just created. The method reference is evaluated immediately, so the 20 IdPs created in testCacheIDPForLogin (and idp-alias-20 at line 425) are never removed. They leak into the realm and can affect other tests or re-runs. The same copy-paste defect exists in testCacheIDPByOrg (line 303), and the new test repeats it.

title: remove() now always performs an extra DB lookup by alias
body: `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is executed unconditionally on every remove(). Previously the delegate lookup only happened when the alias key was invalidated. The result is needed only for the login-cache invalidation, so every removal now costs an extra query even when the alias is cached or the IdP is not login-capable.

title: Login predicate mixes org-aware wrapped model with raw updated model
body: In update(), `idpById` comes from getById(), which returns an organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() also returns false when the bound organization is disabled. `updated` is the raw model. The two sides of the login predicate therefore use different enabled semantics. If an IdP linked to a disabled org stays enabled, the predicate flips and login caches are invalidated unnecessarily. The result is over-invalidation rather than stale data, but the comparison should use consistent models.

title: REALM_ONLY and ALL cache entries are fragmented by organizationId
body: searchKey is set from organizationId for every mode. For FetchMode.REALM_ONLY the delegate ignores organizationId, so each distinct organizationId value produces a separate cached query holding identical results. This wastes cache space and forces redundant DB queries for the same realm-level result set. The search key should be fixed for modes that ignore the org id.

title: getForLogin javadoc omits the new BROKER_PUBLIC requirement for org-linked IdPs
body: The javadoc says an IdP is usable for login if it is enabled, not link-only, and not hidden on login. The PR changes getLoginPredicate() (line 254) to also require that org-linked IdPs have BROKER_PUBLIC set to true. The documented contract for getForLogin and the LoginFilter predicate are now out of sync. Callers relying on the javadoc will be misled about which IdPs are returned.

title: remove() now always queries the database for the IDP
body: `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is now executed unconditionally at the top of `remove()`. Before this change, the DB lookup only happened when the alias cache key was invalidated; the common path used the cached entry. Every removal now incurs an extra uncached DB read, even when the cache already holds the IDP. The lookup should be deferred to the branch that needs it, or the cached model should be reused for the login invalidation check.

title: Cleanup removes a non-existent IDP named "alias" instead of the created alias
body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` uses the literal string "alias" rather than the alias of the IDP just created. The same mistake appears at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`. The created IDPs are therefore never cleaned up, and they leak into other tests in the class and the shared realm. The cleanup should reference the actual alias (for example via a lambda that captures the alias variable). The same pre-existing pattern in `testCacheIDPByOrg` is copied here.

title: getForLogin javadoc omits the new organization public-broker requirement
body: The javadoc says an IDP is usable for login if it is enabled, not link-only, and not hidden on login. The `getLoginPredicate()` change at line 254 adds a further requirement: an IDP linked to an organization must also have `BROKER_PUBLIC` set to true. The documented contract no longer matches the behaviour, so callers relying on the Javadoc will get wrong expectations about which IDPs are returned.

title: Cleanup in the new test removes a non-existent IdP "alias" instead of the created IdP
body: The cleanup registration `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` targets the literal alias "alias", not the `idp-alias-<i>` provider just created. The 20 IdPs created by testCacheIDPForLogin are therefore never removed. They persist into later tests in the class and into other tests sharing the realm, which can change realm-wide IdP counts and login-list results. The same copy-paste bug appears at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`. Use the actual alias, e.g. `final String alias = ...; getCleanup().addCleanup(() -> testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias).remove());`.

title: remove() now always performs an extra DB lookup of the IdP by alias
body: `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is executed unconditionally at the top of remove(). Previously the DB lookup only happened in the branch where the alias cache entry was invalidated. Now every removal pays an additional query even when the cache-based branch is taken, and the result is used only to compute login-cache invalidation. This is a small but avoidable cost on a write path.

title: getForLogin Javadoc does not describe the new organization public-broker requirement
body: The Javadoc says an IdP can be used for login if it is enabled, not link-only, and not hidden on login. The predicate change in LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() now also requires that an IdP linked to an organization has BROKER_PUBLIC=true. That condition is missing from the documented contract, so implementers and callers of getLoginPredicate()/getForLogin cannot tell from the interface what qualifies an org-linked IdP for login.

title: AuthzClient.create() can install a stub CryptoProvider process-wide
body: CryptoIntegration is a process-wide singleton, initialized once on the first call to init(). AuthzClient.create(Configuration) now calls CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()). If the authz-client jar is on the classpath, the new AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100) is only chosen when no higher-order provider is present. Any application that creates an AuthzClient before keycloak-crypto-default or keycloak-crypto-fips is initialized will have CryptoIntegration.getProvider() return AuthzClientCryptoProvider for the rest of the JVM. Most of its methods (getAlgorithmProvider, getCertificateUtils, getPemUtils, getKeyFactory, getSignature, getAesGcmCipher, etc.) throw UnsupportedOperationException, so unrelated Keycloak crypto code later in the same JVM fails at runtime. The ordering-based selection only protects the case where the other providers are already on the classpath.

title: New abstract method order() breaks every existing CryptoProvider implementation
body: order() is added as an abstract interface method with no default. Every third-party or in-tree implementation of CryptoProvider that does not implement it will fail to compile and, if it was compiled earlier, fail with AbstractMethodError at runtime. A default implementation (for example returning a neutral value) would keep the existing contract working. The PR does not show that all implementations in the repository (including test code) were updated.

title: Providers with equal order are chosen nondeterministically and silently
body: detectProvider sorts providers by order() descending and takes the first. DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider and WildFlyElytronProvider all return 200. If two of them are on the classpath, the winner depends on ServiceLoader iteration order, which is not defined. The previous code threw an IllegalStateException for multiple providers, which made this misconfiguration visible. Now it is silently accepted, and the choice of crypto backend (FIPS vs non-FIPS) can change between runs or deployments. Ties should be rejected or resolved explicitly.

title: Ignored provider list is logged as a format string
body: logger.debugf(builder.toString()) passes a computed string as the format pattern. If any provider class name contains '%', the formatter will throw or produce garbled output. It should be logger.debugf("%s", builder) or logger.debug(builder).

title: Test only checks an encode/decode round trip, not DER correctness
body: The test converts the JDK signature to RS, back to DER, and then to RS again, asserting only that the two RS arrays match. A concatenatedRSToASN1DER bug that is symmetric with asn1derToConcatenatedRS would still pass. The test never verifies the converted DER signature with the public key via Signature.verify, and it never checks the DER output against the expected structure or against the JDK's own encoding. Adding a verify step on the reconverted signature would catch real encoding errors.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default KeyStore provider, not BouncyCastle
body: KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider() returns whichever provider backs the default keystore type (normally SUN). The method name and the CryptoProvider contract say it should return the BouncyCastle provider. Callers that expect a BC provider will get the wrong one without any error.

title: Most CryptoProvider methods throw UnsupportedOperationException
body: Nearly every method of AuthzClientCryptoProvider (getAlgorithmProvider, getCertificateUtils, getPemUtils, getKeyFactory, getSignature, getSecretKeyFact, getX509CertFactory, createECParams, etc.) throws UnsupportedOperationException. Because this provider is discoverable via ServiceLoader and can become the global provider (see AuthzClient.create), any code path that touches these methods will fail with an unhelpful exception. Either these should delegate to a sane default, or the provider should only be active in the authz-client's own scope rather than being registered globally.

title: Providers with equal order are silently resolved by ServiceLoader order instead of failing
body: The old code threw IllegalStateException when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath. The new code sorts by order() and silently takes the first one. When two providers share the same order, the winner depends on classpath/ServiceLoader iteration order and nothing is reported. Several existing modules declare order 200 (DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider, WildFlyElytronProvider), so for example a FIPS build with the default provider also on the classpath would pick an arbitrary one. This silently changes the crypto backend, which is a security-relevant decision. Ties should still be rejected, or resolved by an explicit rule.

title: New abstract method order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: order() is added as an abstract method on a public SPI interface. Any external or test implementation of CryptoProvider that is not updated will fail to compile. Since this is a new capability, a default implementation (for example returning 0 or some documented default) would avoid breaking implementors.

title: Provider is auto-selected for third-party clients but throws for almost every operation
body: AuthzClient.create() now calls CryptoIntegration.init(), which picks the highest-order provider on the classpath. For a third-party application that only has keycloak-authz-client, AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100) becomes the active provider. Most of its methods (getKeyFactory, getKeyPairGen, getSignature, getPemUtils, getCertificateUtils, getIdentityExtractorProvider, getAesGcmCipher, etc.) throw UnsupportedOperationException. Any code path in keycloak-core that calls CryptoIntegration.getProvider() for these, such as parsing PEM keys or RSA keys for client authentication, will fail with a confusing error rather than working. The exposure should be limited, or the unsupported methods should fail clearly and be documented.

title: Dead ASN1 encoding computed and discarded in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 build two ASN1Encoder instances and throw away the results. The actual return value is computed separately at lines 117-121. The dead calls do unnecessary work and suggest the code was not reviewed carefully.

title: Oversized integers in DER signatures are silently truncated
body: integerToBytes() truncates to the last qLength bytes when the BigInteger is longer than the curve size. A malformed or malicious DER signature with an oversized r or s is therefore converted into a different, wrong concatenated signature instead of being rejected. The later verification will fail in a confusing way, or in the worst case the truncated value could be accepted by a verifier. The value should be range-checked and rejected.

title: Test only checks round-trip consistency, not correctness against the JDK
body: The test converts a JDK-produced DER signature to concatenated R||S and back, then compares the two concatenated forms. It never checks the output against the JDK's own verifier or a known vector, and it does not test the reverse direction starting from concatenated values with a specific length. A symmetric bug in both directions (for example a wrong byte-padding rule) would still pass. Verifying the signature with the JDK after conversion, and testing leading-zero and short-integer cases, would make the test meaningful.

title: New abstract order() method breaks every existing CryptoProvider implementation
body: `int order();` is added as an abstract interface method with no default. Any existing implementor outside the modified files (third-party providers, test doubles, other modules not in this PR) will fail to compile, and any that is loaded at runtime will fail with AbstractMethodError. A `default` returning a fixed value (for example the current behaviour, or a lower priority) would keep the contract backward compatible.

title: Providers with equal order() are chosen arbitrarily instead of failing
body: Previously more than one CryptoProvider on the classpath raised an IllegalStateException. Now the list is sorted only by order(), and providers with the same order (DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200) keep ServiceLoader iteration order, which is not defined. Two providers with the same priority can therefore be picked nondeterministically, and the choice can change between deployments. Ties should be rejected or resolved by an explicit rule.

title: AuthzClient.create initialises the process-wide crypto singleton with a stub provider
body: CryptoIntegration.init is process-global and only runs once. If an application calls AuthzClient.create() before any other crypto initialisation, and only the authz-client jar (with AuthzClientCryptoProvider, order 100) is on the classpath, the singleton becomes AuthzClientCryptoProvider. Most of its methods throw UnsupportedOperationException. Later calls to CryptoIntegration.init with the real provider are then no-ops, so the stub stays in place for the whole JVM and other code fails at runtime.

title: Oversized r/s integers are silently truncated when converting DER to concatenated form
body: In asn1derToConcatenatedRS, integerToBytes(rBigInteger, len) drops the high-order bytes when the decoded integer is longer than len. The input DER comes from an externally supplied signature. A value that does not fit in the curve's field size should be rejected, but here it is silently reduced to a different number and the resulting signature is passed on to verification. Values with bit length above the field size, and negative values, should raise an IOException.

title: Malformed length produces NegativeArraySizeException instead of an IOException
body: read(int length) allocates `new byte[length]` without checking the value. readLength returns -1 for the indefinite-length form (0x80), and readNext then passes an adjusted length into read(). Malformed or indefinite-length DER therefore throws an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException from the signature-parsing path, not the IOException the callers handle. Negative lengths should be rejected up front.

title: Dead ASN1Encoder calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder instances, write the BigIntegers into them, and discard the results. The return statement on lines 117-121 builds the output from separate encoder instances, so these two lines have no effect. They should be removed; as written they suggest the encoding is being done twice or that the code is incomplete.

title: Test only checks round-trip consistency, not that the DER output is valid
body: The test converts the JCA signature to concatenated form and back to DER, then compares the two concatenated forms. It never checks that concatenatedRSToASN1DER produces DER that the JDK's Signature.verify accepts, and it never checks the DER structure itself. A bug that produced consistently wrong but self-inverse encoding (for example, a wrong sign byte on r or s) would pass. The test should verify the re-encoded DER signature against the public key with the JCA. It also does not cover the edge cases of high-bit r/s values or short signatures.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default KeyStore's provider, not a BouncyCastle provider
body: The method creates a KeyStore of the default type and returns its provider. That is usually the JDK's SUN or SunJSSE provider, not BouncyCastle. Callers that expect the BC provider (for example, to register or look up a provider by name) get an unrelated provider with no error. Returning null or throwing UnsupportedOperationException, as the other unsupported methods do, would be clearer.

title: NPE when the all-clients resource is missing in per-client permission check
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), if no per-client resource exists the code loads the 'Clients' type resource via getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the type resource has not been created (for example on a realm whose admin-permissions client was set up before the Clients type existed, or if the resource was removed). The result is a NullPointerException on every admin client-level check instead of a clean 'no permission' answer. A null check on the resource returning false should be added.

title: isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled throw in V2 but are still called on V2 paths
body: ClientPermissionsV2 overrides isPermissionsEnabled and setPermissionsEnabled to throw UnsupportedOperationException. AdminPermissions.registerListener still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on ClientRemovedEvent whenever the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled. When the V2 evaluator is in use (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled alongside the v1 flag), deleting any client will throw from the event listener. The listener needs to avoid the V2 evaluator or V2 needs a no-op/supported implementation.

title: Unused private method and imports left in new class
body: getEvaluationContext(...) is private and never called, and the imports for Scope, the static TOKEN_EXCHANGE, and the logger field are unused. This is dead code in a newly added file that will be flagged by checkstyle or confuse maintainers about whether token-exchange evaluation is supported in V2.

title: requireView() javadoc describes the wrong behavior
body: The javadoc for requireView() says 'Returns true if canView() returns true', but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException when the check fails. The same copy-paste error appears for requireViewClientScopes() at line 101-102, which says it returns true. Callers relying on the docs would expect a boolean.

title: Deleting a client throws UnsupportedOperationException when V2 permissions are enabled
body: The new ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2. ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (line 193 of that file) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. The listener runs on every client removal, so deleting any client in a realm with V2 enabled fails or leaves the deletion half-done. The listener needs a V2-safe path (skip or implement cleanup for V2) before merge.

title: Role and group removal listeners are now gated behind an unrelated feature flag
body: The whole listener body was wrapped in an ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ check. Previously the RoleRemovedEvent and GroupRemovedEvent handling ran unconditionally. The PR description says nothing about this change, and it alters cleanup behavior for roles and groups in any realm where the v1 flag is off. Either justify it or keep the original unconditional behavior for the existing branches.

title: NullPointerException when the 'Clients' resource-type resource is missing
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), if no per-client resource exists, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...), which returns null when the resource is absent. The next line then calls policyStore.findByResource(server, null), which will likely NPE. Realms whose resource server was initialized before this PR do not have the new 'Clients' resource, so any client-permission check in those realms can fail with an NPE instead of returning false. Add a null check and return false.

title: Existing realms lack the new Clients type and scopes; no migration is provided
body: init() only creates the Clients resource type and the configure, map-roles-client-scope and map-roles-composite scopes for newly created realms. For realms created before this change, AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource throws 'No scopes found.' when a Clients permission is created, and hasPermission finds no Clients resource at all. No upgrade path or migration is included, so these realms silently get no client permissions or fail on use.

title: getResourceName does not handle the Clients resource type
body: getResourceName only special-cases USERS and falls through to resource.getDisplayName() for everything else. Clients resources are created with the internal client UUID as name and no display name, so a client-scope permission lookup may return null or an opaque UUID for display. The Clients type should be mapped to the clientId, analogous to the user username lookup.

title: requireView() javadoc says it returns a boolean
body: The javadoc for requireView() reads 'Returns true if canView() returns true', but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException when the check fails. The same wrong wording appears on requireViewClientScopes(). Both should say 'Throws ForbiddenException if ... returns false'.

title: Missing all-clients resource type resource leads to NullPointerException instead of denial
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no client-specific resource exists, the code loads the 'Clients' resource-type resource via AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...) and passes the result straight to getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the 'Clients' resource is absent. That happens for any realm whose admin-permissions client was initialized before this change, since the diff adds no migration or lazy creation of the 'Clients' resource and the new scopes. The request then fails with an NPE (HTTP 500) rather than being evaluated as 'no permission'. The same unguarded pattern is in the fallback path of hasPermission(String) only indirectly, but hasPermission(ClientModel, String) is the one that breaks.

title: Listener cleanup for role/client/group removal is now gated on the wrong feature flag
body: The registerListener body is now wrapped in a check on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ. Previously the RoleRemoved, ClientRemoved and GroupRemoved handlers ran unconditionally. This PR does not mention this change, and it is unrelated to the Clients resource type. Realms that use only the V2 feature (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2) and not the V1 flag will no longer have permission records cleaned up when roles, clients or groups are deleted. The GroupRemovedEvent branch is also newly gated, which changes behavior beyond the stated scope. This should be a separate change or the gating should be justified.

title: getResourceName does not map client resources to a readable name
body: getResourceName special-cases the Users type, resolving the user's username for display. The new Clients type has no equivalent branch, so for client-object resources it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Resources created by resolveClient are named by client UUID and are not given a display name, so the permission UI/API would show a null or raw ID for client permissions. A Clients branch that resolves the client's clientId, mirroring the Users branch, is needed.

title: requireView() javadoc describes the wrong behavior
body: The javadoc for requireView() says 'Returns true if canView() returns true', but the method returns void and is meant to throw ForbiddenException when canView() is false. The doc should say it throws. The same copy-paste error appears in the requireViewClientScopes() javadoc at line 103.

title: canList() javadoc references QUERY_USERS for client listing
body: The canList() javadoc says it returns true if the caller has QUERY_CLIENTS or QUERY_USERS. For a client-listing predicate, QUERY_USERS looks like a copy-paste from the user evaluator. Either the doc or the implementation is wrong, and the contract should be checked against the implementation.

title: Existing RECREATE exit code silently changed from 4 to 3
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was 4 and is now 3, while the new FEATURE_DISABLED takes the value 4. Any CI script or automation that already branches on exit code 4 to mean 'recreate upgrade required' will now see the feature-disabled case instead, and the recreate case will be reported as 3. The PR does not call this out as a breaking change. If the renumbering is intended, it needs to be explicit in the description and release notes. Otherwise, FEATURE_DISABLED should take a new unused code and the recreate code should stay at 4.

title: setEnabledFeatures overwrites any features already configured on the deployment
body: createInitialDeployment calls kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES)). This replaces the whole enabled-features list rather than appending to it. If getTestKeycloakDeployment() or a future base deployment sets other enabled features, they are silently dropped. The List.of result is also immutable, so any later code that tries to add features to it will throw. The fix is to merge into the existing list, or to create a mutable list only when none is present.

title: Null-strategy test variants never enable the rolling-updates feature
body: createInitialDeployment() returns early when updateStrategy is null, before setFeatureSpec(...) enables ROLLING_UPDATES. The docs in this same PR say the Operator fails when rolling-updates is not enabled. So the testImageChange-null and testCacheMaxCount-null parameterized cases run without the feature and would fail or test the wrong path, unless the base deployment from getTestKeycloakDeployment already enables it. The feature enablement should happen for every variant, not only the non-null strategy.

title: Enabled features are overwritten rather than appended
body: setEnabledFeatures(List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES)) replaces whatever enabled features the base deployment from getTestKeycloakDeployment already declares. Any feature the shared test base enables is silently dropped for these tests. The list is also immutable, so any later addition to it will throw. Merging with the existing list would be safer.

title: Existing RECREATE exit code silently changed from 4 to 3
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was 4 and is now 3, while the new FEATURE_DISABLED takes the value 4. The update-compatibility exit codes are a documented contract for CI/CD and operator scripts (the guide's exit-code table lists 3 as 'not possible, must shut down'). Any automation already written against the old value 4 for 'recreate required' will now interpret a recreate upgrade as a feature-disabled error, and a feature-disabled run will be read as a recreate upgrade. The renumbering is not called out in the PR and no migration note exists. Keep RECREATE at 4 and assign the new code a fresh value, or document the break explicitly.

title: Null-strategy deployment returns before enabling the rolling-updates feature
body: In createInitialDeployment, when updateStrategy is null the method returns at line 106 before the FeatureSpec with ROLLING_UPDATES is set. The PR docs state that the Operator fails if rolling-updates is not enabled while the feature is in preview. So the upgradeStrategy() null-case parameterizations of testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount run without the feature and will fail or test the wrong behavior. The feature enablement should happen for all cases, before the early return.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses group resource IDs but V1 and callers expect group IDs from resource names
body: In V2, resources for groups are created via getOrCreateResource with name = group.getId() (resolveGroup returns group id as name). The V2 code adds groupResource.getId() (the internal resource UUID) to the granted set, not the group ID. Callers (UsersResource.searchForUser, getUsersCount) pass these IDs to session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS) / getUsersCount, which expect group model IDs. The result is that group-based user filtering never matches, so users visible via view-members/manage-members group permissions are silently excluded.

title: hasPermission looks up group resource by group id as resource name, but V2 resources are named by id too while the all-groups fallback is applied even when a specific resource exists
body: hasPermission(groupId, ...) calls resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). When the per-group resource is missing, it falls back to the 'Groups' type resource and only checks that some policy exists on it (policyStore.findByResource(...).isEmpty()), without checking that the policy actually grants the requested scope on that resource before evaluating. Evaluation then proceeds with the type resource; any permission bound to the type resource with any scope from the expected list is accepted. Combined with the missing-resource case for canManage(group) etc., this can grant scopes that the caller only has through unrelated permissions on the all-groups resource. Verify the fallback semantics match Users (which uses the same pattern).

title: policyStore.findByResource called on possibly null resource leads to NPE
body: If AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) returns null (for example the 'Groups' type resource has not been created because the realm admin permission client was initialized before this type existed, or the resource was deleted), resource is null and policyStore.findByResource(server, null) plus resource.getScopes() on the next line will throw NullPointerException rather than denying access. Null-check resource before using it.

title: V2 group permission management methods throw UnsupportedOperationException but are reachable from GroupResource
body: GroupResource.getManagementPermissions and setManagementPermissionsEnabled call AdminPermissions.management(...).groups().isPermissionsEnabled / setPermissionsEnabled / getPermissions / resource(). In V2 these throw UnsupportedOperationException, which results in a 500 rather than a proper error for the management/permissions endpoints when the V2 feature is enabled. Either guard those endpoints or return a meaningful error.

title: canViewMembers in V1 now grants on MANAGE_MEMBERS, changing semantics of requireViewMembers for V1 users
body: canViewMembers was changed to check VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE and MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE and requireViewMembers now delegates to canViewMembers. Previously requireViewMembers used getGroupsWithViewPermission(group), which granted on VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS too, so this is consistent, but the removed per-group method getGroupsWithViewPermission(group) also short-circuited on canView()/canManage() of users; canViewMembers only checks root.users().canView() which in V1 is fine. Verify no behaviour regression for callers that relied on the removed short-circuit for manage role holders.

title: V2 canView/canManage dropped ADMIN role check
body: The change removed AdminRoles.ADMIN from the role checks in canView(user) and canManage(user). Users with the realm 'admin' role (which previously short-circuited) now fall through to permission evaluation and may be denied access to users they previously could see/manage in V2, a regression for admin users. If the removal is intentional it should be explained; otherwise restore it.

title: canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership in V2 now grant via group membership but canMapRoles dropped the canManage(user) delegation
body: canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership previously delegated to canManage(user), which includes manage-permission and group-based manage checks. They now check MANAGE/MAP_ROLES directly and then canManageByGroup, but the group-based check uses canManageMembers, which in V2 also grants via MANAGE_MEMBERS on the group; this widens who can map roles/manage membership via group MANAGE_MEMBERS, which the schema doc does not state. Confirm this is intended.

title: evaluateHierarchy passes method reference to root.groups() evaluated eagerly
body: canManageByGroup uses root.groups()::canManageMembers and canViewByGroup uses root.groups()::canViewMembers. Method reference on root.groups() binds the receiver at evaluation time, which is fine, but canViewByGroup now calls canViewMembers which in V1 checks root.users().canView() per group, causing repeated permission evaluation for each group in the hierarchy (performance cost of N policy evaluations per user in list views).

title: registerListener now only registers when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled at startup
body: The listener registration was moved outside onEvent and guarded by a feature check at registration time. If the profile is evaluated before features are finalized, the listener is never registered and group removal events no longer disable group permissions. Previously the check was performed at event time. Consider keeping the runtime check or documenting startup ordering.

title: getGroups filter no longer short-circuits for users with global group view
body: The filter was changed to stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView) without the prior canViewGlobal precomputation. canView(GroupModel) calls canView() on every element, re-evaluating role checks and policy evaluation per group, which is a performance regression for large group lists.

title: getSubGroups filter re-evaluates global canView per subgroup
body: The previous code computed canViewGlobal once and reused it; the new filter(auth.groups()::canView) calls canView(GroupModel) for each subgroup, which in V2 performs policy evaluation per element. This is an unnecessary per-item cost.

title: Double semicolon in field declaration
body: The field declaration 'new GroupRepresentation();;' has a stray extra semicolon. Minor, but it should be cleaned up.

title: testManageGroupMembership has no assertion on the joinGroup result and relies on silent success
body: The final joinGroup call is not wrapped with any assertion that membership was actually created; a silently no-op call would still pass. Verify bob is a member of topGroup afterwards.

title: testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers does not cover view-by-all-groups or negative cases for group VIEW_MEMBERS
body: The test only checks positive VIEW_MEMBERS on the single group. There is no negative test showing a user outside the group remains invisible when only VIEW_MEMBERS on a different group exists, nor a test for getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returning the correct group IDs (which the V2 implementation gets wrong).

title: canManage() grants group management to holders of only the VIEW scope
body: In V2, canManage() calls hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). Because the scope list includes VIEW, any admin with a view-only permission on the Groups type passes canManage(). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup calls auth.groups().requireManage(), so a view-only admin can create top-level groups. The management check should only accept MANAGE, as canManage(GroupModel) already does.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource UUIDs and looks groups up by the wrong key
body: In V2 each group's Resource is created with name = group id (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource uses resolveGroup's group id as the name). Lines 121-123 instead add groupResource.getId(), which is the internal resource UUID, not the group id. Line 122 also passes that resource UUID into hasPermission, which calls resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), so the per-group lookup misses and the code falls back to the all-groups resource. The result is a set of meaningless IDs. Callers use it as a group-ID filter (UserModel.GROUPS and getUsersCount), so users reachable only via a group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission are never listed or counted. The fix is to use groupResource.getName() for both the lookup and the collected ID.

title: NullPointerException when the Groups type resource does not exist
body: In hasPermission, when the per-group resource is missing, the code loads the all-groups type resource via getResourceTypeResource and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the resource is absent (e.g. a realm whose schema resources were never initialised), so this throws an NPE instead of returning false. UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission has the same pattern for the Users type.

title: Impersonation context uses the target user as the evaluated identity
body: When a requester is given, canImpersonate builds a DefaultEvaluationContext with new UserModelIdentity(root.realm, user), i.e. the identity being impersonated, not the admin performing the action. Policies attached to the IMPERSONATE permission are then evaluated against the target user's identity. When requester is null, the context is null and evaluation uses the admin's identity. The two paths therefore evaluate different principals, so a policy such as 'only my admin' can allow or deny impersonation depending on whether a client id was passed.

title: Javadoc for getGroupIdsWithViewPermission describes the wrong return type
body: The @return tag says 'Stream of IDs of groups with view permission', but the method returns a Set<String>. The sentence before it also reads 'returns empty set', which is correct, but the two statements together are inconsistent with the signature.

title: Public helper searchGroupModelsByAttributes removed from a server SPI module
body: ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes was deleted. It is public in server-spi-private, so any downstream extension or provider code calling it will fail to compile. The only in-repo caller was updated, but the removal is an unannounced API break in a non-test module.

title: getResourceName has no display name for Groups resources
body: getResourceName special-cases USERS to show usernames and 'All users', but nothing handles GROUPS. Group permission resources therefore fall back to resource.getDisplayName(), which is typically the raw group UUID. The admin console will show opaque IDs for group permissions, unlike users and clients.

title: Group membership test does not cover the negative case or the view-members path via listing
body: testManageGroupMembership and testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers only assert the positive path. No test checks that a user in a group where the admin lacks VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS is hidden, and no test covers the all-groups Groups-type permission combined with a per-group view-members grant. Given the ID bug in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, the group-membership filter path is the one most likely to regress and is not exercised for V2 from the group-listing side.

title: canManage() grants manage to callers holding only VIEW on all groups
body: In V2 canManage() falls back to hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). Because the scope list includes VIEW, a caller who only has the view scope on the all-groups resource is treated as able to manage groups. canManage() is the no-arg check used by requireManage(), so such a caller passes requireManage() in addTopLevelGroup (GroupsResource) and can create top-level groups. Only MANAGE should be accepted in this check.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs and never finds per-group resources
body: The method is documented and consumed as a set of group IDs (used for session GROUPS filter in UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource and getUsersCount). Here it adds groupResource.getId(), which is the UUID of the Resource row, not the group ID. Also, per-group resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource are never given type 'Groups' (setType is not called), so resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) only returns the all-groups type resource. The callback then passes that resource's ID to hasPermission(groupId, ...), which looks it up by name and does not find it. The net result is that the returned set holds the wrong identifiers, and group-level VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants are not reflected in the user search/count filter. The V1 implementation used resource name minus prefix to recover the group ID; V2 needs the group ID, not the resource UUID.

title: NPE when the all-groups type resource does not exist
body: When no group-specific resource is found, the code loads the 'Groups' type resource via getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource returns null if that resource is absent, for example in realms created before the Groups resource type was added to the schema, since there is no upgrade path that creates it. This causes a NullPointerException on any group permission check for a non-admin caller instead of a clean deny. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2 but is new for groups.

title: Per-group canView evaluation replaces the cached global check
body: The previous code computed canView() once and short-circuited the per-group check. The new code filters with groupsEvaluator::canView (i.e. canView(GroupModel)) for every group. In V2 each call re-runs the admin role checks and, when those fail, a full policy evaluation (permission evaluation over the all-groups resource). For large group lists this multiplies evaluation cost by the number of groups. The same regression is introduced in GroupResource.getSubGroups.

title: Javadoc says getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns a Stream but it returns a Set
body: The @return tag on getGroupIdsWithViewPermission says 'Stream of IDs of groups with view permission', but the method signature returns Set<String>. Callers and readers will be misled about the return type and about whether the result is lazily evaluated.

title: No test that a view-only group permission cannot create top-level groups
body: The test suite checks manage-all-groups and per-group permissions, but nothing verifies that a caller holding only VIEW on groups is denied group creation (requireManage()). This is exactly the path affected by the canManage() scope bug, so the regression goes undetected. Similarly, no test checks that group-level VIEW_MEMBERS is reflected in the user list filtering via getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, which is also broken.

title: English reference path derivation is fragile and can point to the wrong file
body: The English counterpart is derived by string-replacing 'resources-community' with 'resources' and then regex-replacing any '_xx.properties' suffix with '_en.properties' across the whole absolute path. Any directory containing an underscore or matching the regex (for example a checkout path like /home/user/my_project/...) gets mangled, and the first replaceAll on 'resources-community' can also affect unrelated path segments. If the English file is missing, the verifier throws a RuntimeException, failing the whole build rather than reporting a message.

title: verifySafeHtml runs on the English source file itself and on files with no English counterpart
body: verify() calls verifySafeHtml() for every properties file, including *_en.properties. For the English file the reference is itself, which is fine, but for files whose key is absent in English the fallback is an empty string, so any HTML in a translated-only key is flagged as illegal without any source to compare to. Also the code calls the file-based bundle reader twice per file, and an IOException on the English file is converted to an unchecked RuntimeException instead of a MojoExecutionException, inconsistent with verify()'s error contract.

title: Anchor-tag check reports error but sanitization continues and can produce misleading diffs
body: santizeAnchors adds a message and breaks on the first unmatched anchor, but the value is still passed through the sanitizer and a second 'Illegal HTML' message can be emitted for the same key. Also replaceFirst with Pattern.quote removes the first occurrence in the value regardless of position, so a translation whose anchors are in a different order than the source can pass or fail for the wrong reason.

title: Substring computation can throw when diff indices overlap
body: The start/end prefix and suffix trimming is computed independently, so when value and sanitized are identical in a region that overlaps (e.g. one string is a prefix/suffix repetition of the other), start can exceed value.length() - end. Then value.substring(start, value.length() - end) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier for that file instead of reporting the problem.

title: Plugin now depends on owasp sanitizer and commons-text at compile scope without version alignment
body: commons-text and owasp-java-html-sanitizer are added as runtime dependencies of a Maven plugin, so every consumer of the plugin pulls them in transitively. commons-text 1.13.0 also pulls commons-lang3 and the sanitizer version is pinned separately; no dependency management or justification is given for these versions.

title: Tests use hasItem instead of exact-match assertions and the positive path is untested
body:
The tests were weakened from contains(...) to hasItem(...) and only check that some message matches a substring. There is no test that a clean translation produces zero messages, so false positives from the sanitizer on legitimate content (e.g.
or {0} placeholders) would go undetected. The noHtml_de test also uses a fixture key that is identical in structure to the illegal case, so it does not verify the allowed-tag path.

title: Fixture is named as the English file but the test only checks itself for illegal HTML
body: illegalHtmlTag_en.properties has an unclosed <div> and is verified against itself as the English reference, so the test is really exercising the English-file path rather than a translation. The test name suggests it covers translations; the fixture does not cover the translated-vs-source comparison at all.

title: Finnish totpStep1 replaced with a key whose wording no longer names the apps, and other locales copy the same change
body: Multiple locales (fi, sv, sk, zh_CN, lt in the account bundle, and login bundles) had the link-bearing totpStep1 text replaced by a generic sentence. The Lithuanian account change (messages_lt.properties line 101) replaces the translation with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), which is a clearly wrong-language string shipped to Lithuanian users.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: The totpStep1 value in the Lithuanian account messages is replaced with 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see untranslated Italian text in the TOTP setup page.
