The same Italian string also appears in messages_lt.properties of the login bundle and in the Lithuanian login messages (loginTotpStep1) and the account messages for zh_CN and other locales, indicating an accidental copy from another locale.

title: Hungarian emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml has a stray *** prefix
body: The line emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml begins with '***' in the diff, which becomes part of the key name and makes the property key '***emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml'. The real key is therefore missing from the bundle and the HTML body falls back to the default/English value or fails to render.

title: Lithuanian email HTML links changed to malformed attribute syntax
body: The change replaces unquoted href=LT"..." with href="..." for several keys, which is a correction, but the same diff also leaves 'nJei' and other typos. More importantly the diff is unrelated to the sanitizer; combined with the Italian totpStep1 change in other files this suggests unreviewed bulk edits.

title: Dutch emailVerificationBodyHtml closing tag typo introduced
body: The change to emailVerificationBodyHtml adds a closing tag, but the diff shows the original '' malformed fragment was reshaped; the final result is correct only if the fix is applied as shown. Given the verifier now flags malformed HTML, the corrected string should be checked against the sanitizer, otherwise the build check introduced by this PR fails on this locale.

title: Norwegian identityProviderLinkBody drops HTML from plain-text template
body: The identityProviderLinkBody (plain text) was changed to contain no <b> tags but the diff also modifies the HTML-producing template in the Norwegian bundle. Changing plain-text bodies to remove HTML that was placeholder-adjacent may be intended, but the change is applied to a body that the verifier only treats as HTML-free, so the change is not needed for the sanitizer and alters the email content without justification.

title: Slovak error-invalid-multivalued-size placeholder fix changes wrong argument
body: The corrected pattern changes {1,choice,...} to {2,choice,...} for the max count, which is correct, but the key is placed at the end of a file that previously lacked a trailing newline and the choice format 4<hodnôt is used for both min and max, so the plural form for values above 4 is still mishandled for the minimum part. Plural forms are not verified against the English source.

title: Czech multivalued-size message uses min choice on wrong argument
body: The new error-invalid-multivalued-size line in Czech uses {1,choice,...} for the minimum and {2,choice,...} for the maximum, which matches the English pattern. However the Czech line is appended after readOnlyUsernameMessage without a preceding blank line, and the same key is also present in the English source with a different plural structure, so translators' plural rules are unverified.

title: Duplicate error-invalid-multivalued-size key in login bundle
body: The login messages_en.properties now contains error-invalid-multivalued-size with the new choice syntax, and the admin bundle contains the same key. Keys shared between bundles with differing choice syntax can drift; the verifier only checks sanitizer rules, not cross-bundle consistency.

title: Changed English message format string to ChoiceFormat without escaping the choice literal
body: The new error-invalid-multivalued-size value uses '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' and the original used '{{2}}' double-brace syntax. The account UI is i18next-based, which interpolates with {{ }} and does not use java MessageFormat choice syntax, so the placeholders {0}, {1}, {2} are not substituted and the choice text is shown literally to users.

title: Path-based English file derivation breaks and can silently skip or misreport
body: The English counterpart is computed by regex-replacing `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` on the absolute path. Any directory component containing an underscore or the substring 'resources-community' (e.g. user home paths) can be mangled, and files without a locale suffix (e.g. messages.properties) would be rewritten incorrectly. When the English file is missing, the verifier throws RuntimeException instead of a MojoExecutionException, aborting the whole build with an unhelpful stack trace. Derivation should use the file name and parent directory explicitly.

title: Bundle re-read from disk instead of using already-read contents; checked I/O converted to RuntimeException
body: verifySafeHtml() re-opens the file via FileInputStream even though verify() already read the contents. The IOException is wrapped in a RuntimeException rather than the declared MojoExecutionException, so plugin failures surface as uncaught runtime exceptions instead of a proper Maven build error.

title: Policy field declared as package-private instance fields, and sanitizer quirks are only partially handled
body: POLICY_SOME_HTML, POLICY_NO_HTML and HTML_TAGS are non-final, non-private instance fields recreated per object. The sanitizer's known behavior of escaping numeric tags like <1> and braces is patched with ad-hoc string replacements (unescapeHtml4, replace "<!-- -->"), so legitimate ICU placeholders in translations can produce false positives or mask real problems. These should be static final and the normalization should be documented/tested.

title: Anchor replacement uses replaceFirst on the whole value, removing wrong occurrences
body: santizeAnchors removes the matched English anchor string from the translated value with replaceFirst, which can remove an anchor that is not the one just matched, and the loop continues scanning the original matcher over the unmodified value. Combined with the early break, mismatched or extra anchors can be silently accepted or reported with misleading positions.

title: Anchor check messages are added but validation continues; keys with missing English value are silently treated as English=empty
body: getEnglishValue returns "" for a missing key, so any translated key that has no English counterpart is checked against an empty English string. That means HTML in such keys is flagged as illegal and anchors are flagged as not found, yet orphan keys are never reported as a problem themselves. The behavior is undocumented and produces confusing errors.

title: Unrelated translation change to Swedish file (removing link text) is out of scope and loses content
body: The diff replaces the FreeOTP/Google Authenticator link text with a generic sentence in a community translation, dropping the apps list without any corresponding English source change. Similar unrelated content removal occurs in the fi, lt, sk, zh_CN account and login bundles, so translators' links to app stores are lost.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: totpStep1 in messages_lt.properties now reads 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. The Lithuanian user sees untranslated Italian text. The same erroneous Italian string is introduced into login/messages_lt.properties (loginTotpStep1) and must be reverted or properly translated.

title: Italian string introduced into Lithuanian login messages
body: loginTotpStep1 is changed to the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', replacing the Lithuanian text. Lithuanian users will see Italian in the TOTP setup page.

title: Malformed href attribute introduced in HTML email templates
body: The diff rewrites `href=LT"{0}"` into `href="{0}"` correctly, but the surrounding original text remains with typos and the verification fixes are mixed into unrelated edits; more importantly, the link fix changes rendered output in emails that users relied on, without a corresponding change to tests. Also the email-body pattern `{0}` is used for link in identityProviderLinkBodyHtml where `{3}` is the link; the same message in messages_lt uses {3} for link and {0} for another value, showing the translated HTML link target changed meaning.

title: Placeholder {2} choice corrupted to reference {1} in multivalued-size message
body: The fix changes the trailing choice to `{2,choice,...}` for the max count, but the original text had `{1,choice,...}` for max, which the diff edits in the last line. Other locales (cs) use {1} for the min count choice and {2} for max, so the Slovak message is now consistent; however the change removes the trailing newline ('\ No newline at end of file'), which is a minor formatting regression.

title: Multiple unrelated bundles were modified with HTML-only changes; lt/hr/ka keys wrongly recognized
body:
The change from `
` to `
` across many locales is cosmetic and not needed for the sanitizer; the verifier now passes via normalization for both forms, so these edits add churn to many translation files without functional benefit.

title: Stray `< p>` tag repaired but unescaped Persian HTML elsewhere remains invalid
body:
The fix corrects `< p>` to `

` in emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml. Other similar malformed tags in the same and other translation files (e.g. `` in tr, `` in nl) are only partially fixed, so the sanitizer will still flag or mis-render them; the fix set is inconsistent.

title: Norwegian identityProviderLinkBody now shows raw HTML in plain-text email
body: The plain-text identityProviderLinkBody change replaces `{1}` with `{1}`, which is the correct fix for plain text, but the change is unrelated to the sanitizer described in the PR and silently alters the wording of the text body (removing the emphasis markers) without a corresponding test.

title: Slovak impersonateTitleHtml fix drops a stray closing tag, but nearby keys still malformed
body: The change removes a dangling `` from impersonateTitleHtml. This is a valid fix but the same PR leaves other messages with mismatched tags in the same file, so the verification gate is not comprehensive.

title: Tests do not assert that clean files produce no messages
body: The new tests only check that specific messages appear (hasItem). There is no negative test that a valid translation (e.g. noHtml_en or a valid anchor case) yields an empty list, so false positives from the sanitizer would go undetected. The existing duplicate-keys test was also weakened from contains to hasItem, reducing its precision.

title: Fixture noHtml_de is paired with an English file that does not exist in the test resources
body: The verifier derives the English file by replacing the locale suffix with _en in the same directory. For noHtml_de.properties the expected English file is noHtml_en.properties, which exists, but the path rewrite (resources-community to resources) is never exercised by tests, so the derivation logic is untested.

title: New sanitizer and commons-text dependencies added to a Maven plugin without shading or version alignment
body: owasp-java-html-sanitizer and commons-text are added as compile-scope dependencies of a maven-plugin artifact. They are transitively resolved into every consumer's build classpath and may conflict with the versions Maven itself or other plugins use (commons-lang/commons-text). The new dependency surface is not justified in the description.

title: Choice format in admin message no longer matches the rest of the key set
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size now uses a ChoiceFormat for the {2} placeholder while {1} is used as a plain number, and the English message in the account UI keeps the same key with a different shape; the message has different placeholder conventions across bundles (some use {0}, others {{0}}), making the translations inconsistent.

title: English file path derivation breaks for non-community/any path and regex is wrong
body: The English counterpart is derived by replacing 'resources-community' with 'resources' and then replacing the regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` with `_en.properties`. The regex also matches any underscore in the directory path (e.g. under a path containing '_'), and `[a-zA-Z-_]*` is greedy across the filename. For files without a locale suffix (e.g. base files, or paths with underscores in directory names such as 'keycloak_theme/'), the replacement corrupts the path and `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` throws, which is wrapped in a RuntimeException that aborts verification of the whole module rather than reporting a message.

title: Verifier throws RuntimeException on missing English file instead of reporting
body: When the translated file has no corresponding English file (or the path derivation fails), verifySafeHtml throws a RuntimeException. The verify() method only catches IOException, so this propagates as an unchecked failure that aborts the entire Maven plugin run instead of adding a message to the result list. Also the English file is read even when the file being checked is itself the English file (for _en files the replacement is a no-op, so it compares a file to itself, which is harmless but masks the case).

title: Missing translation keys are silently treated as empty English source
body: getEnglishValue returns "" when a key is absent in the English bundle. containsHtml("") is then false, so a translation for a key that does not exist in English is checked with the no-HTML policy and any HTML in it is reported, while keys that legitimately contain HTML in English but were removed or renamed in English are not detected. Missing source keys should be reported explicitly.

title: Message string built from substring indexes can throw
body: The diff-highlighting computes `start` and `end` independently. When the value and sanitized strings overlap (e.g. one is a prefix of the other or the common prefix and suffix overlap), `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` can have start > end, throwing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and aborting the verifier. For example value='<b>x' vs sanitized='x' overlaps can produce this.

title: Anchor replacement removes first occurrence anywhere, not at its position
body: santizeAnchors uses value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "") which removes the first textual occurrence of the anchor tag, and the loop matches tags in the translated value against English tags by order only. A translation with a changed/extra anchor whose text coincidentally matches an earlier English tag can be silently accepted, and the matcher positions are not updated after the string is modified, so matching continues over a stale string. The `break` after reporting also means only one anchor error is reported per key.

title: Tests rely on fixture paths whose English counterparts do not exist in the test resources
body: verifySafeHtml derives the English file by replacing the locale suffix with _en.properties in the same directory. Fixtures such as noHtml_de.properties and changedAnchor_de.properties rely on noHtml_en.properties and changedAnchor_en.properties existing; this works, but illegalHtmlTag_en.properties is verified against itself, so the test for illegal HTML only passes because of the English HTML being the same as the translation. The tests also do not assert the absence of false positives (e.g. a valid translation producing no messages), so the sanitizer's acceptance behaviour is untested.

title: Illegal-HTML fixture is a malformed English source rather than a translation
body: The fixture `key=Some <div>tag</div` is an unterminated tag in the English reference file itself, and the test asserts 'Illegal HTML' for it. The fixture does not exercise a translation containing disallowed HTML versus an English source, so the test does not verify the intended rule that a translation may not introduce tags absent from the source.

title: Renamed fixture and weakened assertion
body: The duplicate-keys test was changed from Matchers.contains to Matchers.hasItem, so it no longer asserts the exact message list; any extra spurious message would now pass. Combined with the new verifySafeHtml running for duplicateKeys_en.properties, this weakens the regression coverage for the existing check.

title: Finnish translation replaced with a different, untranslated-language sentence
body: The `totpStep1` key was rewritten to a generic Finnish sentence without the links to the authenticator apps, dropping information present in the source. This is an unrelated content change to a translation, not a sanitizer fix, and removes the app names users need.

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The value `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, not Lithuanian. It will be shown to Lithuanian users in the account console and also drops the FreeOTP/Google Authenticator links that the translation previously contained.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: `loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian copied into the Lithuanian login bundle, so Lithuanian users see the wrong language and the links to the authenticator apps are removed.

title: Lithuanian email HTML hrefs now quoted but placeholders inconsistent
body: The HTML email bodies were changed to use `<a href="{0}">` and the identityProviderLinkBodyHtml/passwordReset links now use `{3}` and `{0}` respectively, while the text body uses `{4}` for the expiry. Changing placeholder usage in translations without checking argument order against the English source risks wrong values (e.g. expiry shown as link) in the sent emails.

title:
Dutch email HTML loses closing

tag mismatch fix is wrong direction
body: The emailVerificationBodyHtml line previously had `` (a broken tag); the diff corrects it, but the rest of the file was not touched, while the same file also still contains the malformed-looking unchanged content elsewhere. The change is only a partial cleanup of the markup, leaving the translation's HTML inconsistent with the sanitizer's rules.

title: Hungarian emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml key prefixed with *** garbage
body: The diff shows the line starting with `***emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml=` in the removed side; the replacement line is correct, but the removal of the stray prefix indicates an accidental edit that must be verified so that the key is actually emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml in the final file.

title: Multiple WebAuthn br tag changes are whitespace-only churn
body:
The `
` to `
` changes across many locales are cosmetic and unrelated to the sanitizer, adding diff noise to ~40 translation files; they do not fix any verifier failure described in the PR.

title: Slovak error-invalid-multivalued-size placeholder changed to a non-plural choice with wrong index
body: The fix changes the second choice placeholder from {1,choice,...} to {2,choice,...} while leaving the same message elsewhere; the new value uses four-plural forms with a choice pattern whose thresholds (4<hodnôt) are inconsistent with the English pattern used in other locales, so plural rendering for counts 2–4 may be wrong.

title: Czech error-invalid-multivalued-size choice pattern differs from English source placeholders
body: The Czech value uses `{1,choice,...}` and `{2,choice,...}` with 1<hodnoty|4<hodnot patterns while the English source has `{2,choice,...}` only; it is inconsistent with the key's intended single-count phrasing and the verifier's normalizeValue only strips choice patterns for specific keys, so this key may be flagged or render incorrectly.

title: English error-invalid-multivalued-size choice changed but other locales keep old placeholders
body: The base English message now uses a choice format for {2}, while many translations keep the plain `value(s)` form or use `{1,choice}` on the wrong index; the inconsistent placeholder sets between source and translations can cause MessageFormat to render differently per locale and the verifier's normalization only covers the admin key.

title: rawTokenId null check actually checks grantType again
body: The second requireNonNull uses `grantType` as the object and the message says "Null rawTokenId not allowed". The rawTokenId parameter is never null-checked, so a null rawTokenId is accepted and stored. The check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`. Callers such as encodeTokenId would then produce ids ending in ':null' or fail later.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and the wrong substring index
body: Two errors in one check. First, `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects exactly the token ids that carry the expected grant shortcut, so every CODE_TO_TOKEN, REFRESH_TOKEN, DEVICE and CIBA event assertion using this matcher fails for correct ids. It should be `!equals`. Second, the encoded prefix is `st(2)+tt(2)+gt(2)`, so the grant shortcut is at indices 4-5, i.e. `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`. The comment 'starts at character 4th char' is also wrong. As written, the matcher either fails for correct ids or passes for wrong ones, so these event tests cannot verify the feature.

title: testIncorrectGrantType passes only because of an NPE from a null session factory
body: The test catches RuntimeException and treats any exception as success. The provider is built with a null sessionFactory, and for grant shortcut 'ac' (absent from the map) getGrantTypeByShortcut calls sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(), which throws NullPointerException. The test therefore passes for an unrelated reason and does not check the intended 'unknown grant shortcut' IllegalArgumentException. It should assert the specific exception type and message, and use a stubbed factory.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method on a public SPI interface with no default. Any third-party or downstream grant type factory that implements OAuth2GrantTypeFactory will fail to compile and, at runtime, the encoder will be unable to handle it. A default implementation or a documented migration path is needed.

title: Unchecked cast of every OAuth2GrantType factory to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory
body: postInit casts each factory returned by getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class) to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory. Any OAuth2GrantType factory that does not implement that interface (possible for custom or older providers) causes a ClassCastException, which aborts server startup in postInit. The stream should be filtered with instanceof, or the failure should be made explicit with a clear message.

title: Null shortcut from a grant factory causes NPE during map population
body: If a grant factory returns null from getShortcut(), postInit inserts into a ConcurrentHashMap with a null key or value, which throws NullPointerException. The failure occurs during startup with no message naming the offending grant. A null check with a clear IllegalStateException would be safer.

title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed
body: The public `Context(Context context)` constructor was deleted from the public static Context class. Any code outside this diff that copies a grant context will no longer compile. The PR does not mention this removal, and it is unrelated to the encoding feature. If the removal is intentional it should be called out; otherwise the constructor should be restored (and grantType copied in it).

title: Access token jti claim format changes for every issued access token
body: initToken now sets the token id to the encoded form 'onrtac:<uuid>' instead of a plain UUID. The id is exposed as the JWT `jti` claim and in event details. Any client, resource server, or validation logic that assumes jti is a UUID, or that parses it as such, will break on upgrade. This wire-format change for all access tokens is not reflected in the PR description or in the tests that still check UUID-shaped token ids elsewhere. It should be explicitly versioned or documented.

title: Javadoc says shortcut is 3 letters but encoding requires exactly 2
body: The getShortcut() javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider slices the encoded context into fixed 2-character parts and rejects anything else. A grant implementer following this doc would produce an unencodable shortcut. The doc should state the exact 2-character requirement.

title: rawTokenId null check actually re-checks grantType
body: The third null check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` but it should check `rawTokenId`. As written, a null rawTokenId is accepted silently, so the error message promised by the message text never fires and a token with a null raw ID can be encoded as `...:null`.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring indices
body: The check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is wrong in two ways. First, the grant shortcut is at characters 4-5 (e.g. `onrtac` -> `ac` at index 4), so `substring(3, 5)` yields `ta`/`rt`-like garbage rather than the grant shortcut; it should be `substring(4, 6)`. Second, the condition is inverted: it rejects tokens whose grant matches the expected one, so the matcher passes for wrong grants and fails for the correct grant. The comment also contradicts the code ("starts at 4th char"). These assertions in expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh and expectAuthReqIdToToken are therefore meaningless or fail incorrectly.

title: Negative grant-type test passes for the wrong reason
body: testIncorrectGrantType expects an exception for `ofrtac`, but 'ac' is never registered in the test factory and sessionFactory is null, so the exception is a NullPointerException from getGrantTypeByShortcut, not the intended IllegalArgumentException for an unknown grant. The test would pass even if the lookup logic were broken in other ways. It should assert on the specific exception type/message, or register the mapping and verify the real failure path.

title: Unregistered grant type makes token issuance fail
body: encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException when the grant type has no registered shortcut. This is called from TokenManager.initToken for every access token, so any flow that sets a grant type not backed by a registered OAuth2GrantType factory (for example a feature-gated grant whose factory is disabled, or a value taken from the request) will fail token creation entirely instead of falling back to the UNKNOWN shortcut. The encoding should degrade gracefully rather than break login/token endpoints.

title: Javadoc says 3-letter shortcut but encoding uses 2 characters
body: The getShortcut() javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but every implementation in this PR returns a 2-character shortcut and the token ID decoder hard-codes 2-character slots (length must be 6 total). Following the doc would produce tokens that cannot be decoded.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: getShortcut() is added as an abstract interface method with no default. Any third-party or custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation compiled against the previous API will fail to compile or fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError, and postInit would then fail for the whole server. Providing a default or documenting the migration is needed for an SPI change.

title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed
body: The copy constructor `Context(Context context)` was deleted from the public SPI class OAuth2GrantType.Context. Code outside this repo that relied on it to clone a grant context will no longer compile. The removal is not called out in the PR description.

title: isAccessTokenId never enforces the grant shortcut (wrong index and inverted condition)
body: The grant-shortcut check in isAccessTokenId is broken in two ways. First, `substring(3, 5)` reads characters 4-5 of the token id, which is the token-type shortcut (e.g. 'rt'), not the grant shortcut. The grant shortcut is at indexes 4-5 (0-based), i.e. `substring(4, 6)`. The comment even says 'starts at character 4th char' but the code uses index 3. Second, the condition is inverted: `if (... .equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects exactly the correct grant. Because the substring is the token type, the comparison is effectively always false, so the matcher never checks the grant at all. Expectations like expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken therefore pass for any grant shortcut, and the new assertions add no coverage. It should compare `substring(4, 6)` with `!equals`.

title: rawTokenId null check duplicates grantType check and the message is wrong
body: The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. As a result a null rawTokenId is never rejected, and a null grantType gets the wrong message on the second check path. Should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`. Note that getTokenContextFromTokenId can legitimately pass a raw id, so the intended contract should be decided explicitly, but the current code does not enforce what it claims.

title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed from SPI class
body: The diff deletes the public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor of `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. This class is part of the server-spi-private API that custom grant type providers extend and use. Any external provider or extension that calls the copy constructor will no longer compile or link. The removal is not mentioned in the PR description and is not needed for the feature (the added grantType field could be copied in the old constructor). This should be kept or removed deliberately with a note in the upgrade documentation.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method on the public SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with no default. Every third-party or downstream grant type factory now fails to compile and, at runtime, the implementation is missing an interface method. Since the encoder now calls getShortcut() during token creation (postInit, getShortcutByGrantType), a deployed custom grant without it would fail at startup or during token issuance. A default implementation or a fallback should be considered, or this should be documented as a breaking SPI change.

title: Access token ID (jti / TOKEN_ID event detail) format changes for every access token
body: initToken now sets the access token id to `<6-char-context>:<uuid>` for all access tokens. Everything that consumes the token id (the JWT `jti` claim, the `Details.TOKEN_ID` event detail, revocation or any client logic keyed on jti) now sees a different format. Clients or external systems that assume jti is a plain UUID, or that parse event token ids as UUIDs, will break. The change is only described as an internal optimisation in the PR text, and the public-facing impact on the `jti` claim and events is not called out or covered by a compatibility note.

title: Recovery codes are written to user storage unhashed
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generated codes to JSON and passes them directly to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...). The local-DB path goes through RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues, which keeps only hashed codes (verification hashes the input with hashRawCode). The user-storage path has no equivalent step, so plaintext recovery codes are persisted into external user storage (LDAP, custom federation, etc.). Anyone with read access to that store can take over accounts. The codes should be hashed the same way before being handed to user storage, and the storage-side verification adjusted to match.

title: Recovery codes stored in user storage are never consumed and can be replayed
body: isValid for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks membership in the stored list and never marks the used code as consumed or removes it. The authenticator's 'all codes used' logic (RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator) works on the local credential model and calls removeStoredCredentialById, which does not touch federated credentials. So a recovery code that has been used can be used again indefinitely when the credential lives in user storage. The test added (testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin) only covers one successful login and never checks that a used code is rejected, so this gap is not caught.

title: Javadoc typo in getCredential return description
body: The @return text reads 'a optional  credential model' (grammar 'an optional' and a double space). Minor, but it is a public utility method's contract documentation.

title: Recovery codes are written to user storage as raw plaintext codes
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes `generatedCodes` (the raw, unhashed codes shown to the user) and passes that JSON as the credential data to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. The local DB path stores only hashed codes (via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel). Storing the raw secrets in an external user store (LDAP, custom federation) is inconsistent with the local path and leaks reusable secrets to a system Keycloak does not control. The stored form should be the same hashed form used locally, with verification hashing the input (RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode).

title: Recovery codes validated in user storage are never consumed and can be reused
body: In isValid for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE the code is only checked with `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...)`. Nothing marks the used code as consumed or removes it, so the same recovery code can be used to log in unlimited times. The local path tracks used codes and removes the credential once all are used (see RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.action). The federated path therefore silently breaks the one-time semantics of recovery codes. The test only covers a single successful login and does not catch this.

title: Removing an exhausted recovery credential only targets the local store
body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential may return a credential that lives in user storage (federated). When all codes are used, the code calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(id)`, which only operates on the local DB. For a federated credential the removal does nothing, so the exhausted credential remains and the user is not forced to reconfigure correctly. The removal should go through the credential source that actually owns the credential, or the federated case should be handled explicitly.

title: getCredentials dereferences myUser without a null check
body: getCredentials calls getMyUser(user) and immediately accesses `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp`. If the user is not present in the map (getMyUser returns null), this throws NullPointerException. Other methods in the same class (isConfiguredFor, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream) guard against null.

title: Test does not verify one-time use or regeneration of recovery codes
body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only logs in once with code 0. It does not check that the same code is rejected on a second login, that used codes are consumed, or that regenerating codes replaces the previous set in user storage. Those are the behaviors most likely to be broken by the federated implementation, as the isValid path shows.

title: Helper takes a delay parameter that is always 0 and has a misspelled alias
body: configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes accepts `long delay` but the only caller passes 0, so the parameter is dead flexibility. The config alias "delayed-suthenticator-config" is misspelled, which is confusing if it is ever referenced by name.

title: Raw recovery codes are sent to user storage while local storage keeps hashed codes
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes `generatedCodes` (the plaintext codes shown to the user) and passes that JSON to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. The local-DB path instead goes through `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel)`, where the codes are hashed (RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode exists for this). So the same credential is stored as plaintext in external user storage but as hashed in the Keycloak DB. Plaintext recovery codes are secrets, and this exposes them to the external store and any reader of it. The user-storage path should store the same hashed representation, or the design should be explicitly documented and justified.

title: Recovery codes validated in user storage are never consumed, so they can be reused
body: isValid for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks that the code is present in the stored list and never marks it as used or removes it. The authenticator (RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator) relies on the credential's used-code state to decide when to remove the credential and re-trigger code generation, and that state is never updated for user-storage credentials. Each recovery code can therefore be used indefinitely against this provider, and allCodesUsed() is never true for it. The reference provider should consume codes the same way the local provider does, or the limitation should be documented.

title: getCredential fallback ignores where a removed federated credential would be deleted
body: The authenticator later calls credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(id) on the credential returned by getCredential. If that credential came from the federated (user storage) stream, the removal targets local storage, where the ID does not exist, so the exhausted codes credential is never removed from user storage. The removal path should check which store the credential came from.

title: getCredentials dereferences myUser without a null check
body: getMyUser(user) can return null when the user is not in the in-memory map, and getCredentials then calls myUser.recoveryCodes and myUser.otp, causing a NullPointerException. Other methods in this class (for example getDisableableCredentialTypesStream and isConfiguredFor) guard against a null MyUser.

title: Recovery-keys test only covers the happy path
body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin sets up codes and logs in once with a valid code. It does not check that an invalid code is rejected, that a used code cannot be reused, or that the required action is re-triggered when all codes are used. Those are the behaviours the user-storage change is meant to get right, and the reuse case is exactly where the provider currently fails.

title: Same null-delegate NPE remains in the paged subgroup stream methods
body: The fix only guards getSubGroupsCount(). The three paged overloads (getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(firstResult, maxResults) at line 262, and getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, firstResult, maxResults) at line 268) still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. If the group was deleted concurrently and the cache entry is stale, modelSupplier.get() returns null and these throw the same NullPointerException the PR is meant to fix. The brief group listing path can reach these methods, so the same race can still surface there.

title: Background reader thread is never joined or stopped on failure, and may spin forever
body: The reader thread is started with new Thread(...).start() as a non-daemon thread and is never joined. It only stops when deletedAll is set at the end of the test. If any group removal throws, the main thread exits via exception before deletedAll.set(true), so the reader loops forever issuing admin requests and keeps the JVM alive. The test also does not register the created groups for cleanup, so a failure leaks them.

title: Exceptions from the reader thread are checked before the thread has finished
body: assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty()) runs right after deletedAll is set, but the reader thread may still be inside an in-flight request. Any exception raised by that last request, or by a request that runs after the assertion, is never checked. The thread should be joined before asserting so the result is deterministic.

title: Unrelated dead-code removal bundled into an NPE fix
body: The diff deletes the private helper groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement. It is unrelated to the concurrent NPE in the PR title and description. Removing it in the same change makes the PR harder to review and should be a separate change, or at least called out in the description.

title: Same unguarded modelSupplier dereference remains in the paged getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: The fix only guards getSubGroupsCount(). The three paged overloads (getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(firstResult, maxResults) at line 262, and getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, firstResult, maxResults) at line 268) still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. If the group was deleted concurrently, modelSupplier.get() returns null and these throw the same NullPointerException the PR is meant to fix. Either guard these the same way, or throw a consistent not-found exception.

title: getSubGroupsCount now returns null silently for a deleted group
body: When the backing group no longer exists, getSubGroupsCount() returns null instead of a count or an error. It is declared to return Long, so callers that unbox it (e.g. `long c = group.getSubGroupsCount();`) will hit an NPE at the call site, which only moves the NPE elsewhere. The caller gets no signal that the group vanished. The behaviour is inconsistent with isUpdated(), which throws IllegalStateException("Not found in database") for the same situation. Consider throwing the same exception, or documenting the null contract.

title: Background reader thread is never joined, so the assertion can miss exceptions
body: The reader thread is started at line 139 and never joined. deletedAll is set to true at line 155 and the assertion at line 157 runs immediately. A reader request still in flight when the loop exits can add an exception to caughtExceptions after the assertion has already passed, so the test can pass spuriously. The thread should be joined before asserting.

title: Exception during group removal leaves the reader thread spinning forever
body: If group(groupUuid).remove() throws (lines 152-154 are not guarded), execution skips deletedAll.set(true) at line 155. The non-daemon reader thread then loops forever, which keeps the test JVM alive and hangs the build. Wrap the deletion loop in try/finally that sets deletedAll, and consider marking the thread as a daemon.

title: Regression test only covers the brief groups listing, not the path that still NPEs
body: The test exercises groups(...) with briefRepresentation=true, but the NPE fixed in GroupAdapter is reached through subgroup and count access. The test never accesses getSubGroupsCount or the paged getSubGroupsStream overloads concurrently with deletion, so it would not catch the remaining unguarded paths. The method name createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti is also unclear about what is verified.

title: Same NPE path left unguarded in the paged subgroup stream methods
body: The fix makes getSubGroupsCount() null-safe, but the sibling methods getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults) (line 256), getSubGroupsStream(firstResult, maxResults) (line 262) and getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, firstResult, maxResults) (line 268) still call modelSupplier.get() and dereference the result directly. If the group was deleted concurrently, modelSupplier.get() returns null and these throw the same NullPointerException the PR is meant to fix. The concurrent-read scenario from the issue is therefore only partly addressed.

title: Deleted group silently reports a null subgroup count
body: getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the backing group no longer exists. Callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount pass this straight to setSubGroupCount, so a group that was removed mid-request is returned with a null count instead of being treated as missing. Returning null here hides the deletion rather than surfacing it, and the other GroupAdapter methods throw IllegalStateException('Not found in database') in the same situation, so behaviour is now inconsistent.

title: Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion can pass without reading concurrently
body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a reader thread, deletes the groups, sets deletedAll to true and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty. There is no join on the reader thread, so the assertion may run before the reader has performed any reads or observed any exceptions. The test can pass vacuously and does not reliably detect the race it is meant to cover. The reader thread is also not stored, so an exception thrown inside it outside the try block would be lost. The test should join the thread (and ideally fail on any exception it records) before asserting.

title: Concurrency regression test is not shown to reproduce the original NPE
body: The test is a best-effort race with no deterministic trigger, and the reader loop is a busy spin with no sleep. Nothing in the PR shows that it fails on the base commit, so it may not guard against regression of the NPE. The name 'groupUuuids' is also a typo.

title: Unrelated private helper removed in a bug-fix PR
body: The private method groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement is deleted here, but this change is not part of the NPE fix described in the PR. It is out of scope for the stated purpose and should be in a separate change or justified in the description. Any imports it depended on, such as StringUtil, should also be checked for being left unused.

title: Negative offset is passed straight to queryset slicing, which Django rejects
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, the code slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start_offset. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported"). The cursor offset comes from the client-controlled `cursor` query parameter (Cursor.from_string now accepts negative ints), so a crafted cursor produces an unhandled 500 for any admin who sends `optimized_pagination=true`. The branch does not deliver the advertised behaviour of reaching data beyond normal bounds.

title: Prev-cursor path passes an unclamped, possibly negative offset to queryset slicing
body: The new line `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` only clamps for next cursors. For a prev cursor, a negative offset (which Cursor now accepts from user input via from_string) becomes a negative slice start in `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, which Django raises ValueError on. This is reachable by any user of every BasePaginator-based endpoint, not just the audit log endpoint, and turns bad input into a 500. Also, for next cursors the silent clamp to 0 changes behaviour: a negative offset used to fail loudly and now is quietly treated as 0, so it can return the first page instead of an error.

title: Comment claims permissions are enforced at queryset level, but the code does not do that
body: The comment says negative offsets are 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' and that the code 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds'. The queryset is only filtered by organization_id and the optional actor/event filters in the endpoint; no per-row authorization is applied in the paginator. The enable_advanced_features flag is also derived from `is_superuser or has_global_access` in the endpoint, which is a coarse gate that the paginator itself never checks. This comment documents a security assumption that is false and will mislead future maintainers into relying on it.

title: Experimental paginator is switched on by a user-supplied query parameter
body: The new `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter selects a different paginator class and enables the advanced negative-offset path for superusers and global-access members. This is an unannounced public behaviour toggle on an endpoint whose publish_status is EXPERIMENTAL, with no feature flag, no documentation, and no tests. Any change in cursor semantics would then be exposed to clients that set this parameter, and the two code paths would need to be maintained in parallel.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result with only a minor change
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is almost a line-for-line copy of BasePaginator.get_result, and the same is true of get_item_key and value_from_cursor. The only real difference is the negative-offset branch, which is the broken path described above. The two copies will drift, and fixes to one (for example the typo-related ordering logic in build_queryset) will not reach the other. The paginator should either be a thin subclass with an overridden offset rule or be removed.

title: No tests for the new pagination behaviour or the new paginator
body: The PR adds OptimizedCursorPaginator, changes offset clamping in BasePaginator.get_result, and adds a request-driven code path in the audit log endpoint, but includes no tests. There is no coverage for negative cursor offsets, prev cursors with negative offsets, the optimized_pagination toggle, or the permission gating. The existing audit log endpoint tests do not exercise the new branch.

title: Comment in Cursor.__init__ describes a feature that is not implemented here
body: The added comment says negative offsets 'enable efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions in large datasets', but Cursor simply stores int(offset). The actual efficiency claim is not true: negative offsets either raise in Django slicing or are clamped to 0 elsewhere. Also, removing the implicit non-negative guarantee on Cursor.offset affects every consumer of cursors, and that is not mentioned anywhere.

title: PR description is a placeholder and does not explain the change
body: The PR description reads only 'Test 1'. It gives no motivation for the new paginator, no explanation of why negative offsets are needed, no description of the optimized_pagination toggle, and no rollout or risk notes. A reviewer cannot evaluate the intent or the risk of changing shared cursor behaviour from this text.

title: Advanced negative-offset branch raises ValueError from Django slicing
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, the code slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start_offset. Django QuerySet does not support negative indexing and raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The inline comment claims 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', which is incorrect. The advanced feature therefore always fails with a 500 for any negative cursor offset, and the 'access beyond normal bounds' behaviour it advertises is never reachable.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key cannot handle datetime sort keys
body: The endpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime'. get_item_key calls `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` directly on `getattr(item, 'datetime')`, which is a datetime object, so this raises TypeError on the first result. Unlike DateTimePaginator, there is no conversion to a numeric timestamp. Likewise value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value rather than a datetime, so build_queryset would compare a datetime column against an integer. Any request with `optimized_pagination=true` by a superuser or global-access member, with at least one audit log row, will fail.

title: Negative offset on prev cursors still reaches Django slicing and crashes
body: The new start_offset logic clamps negative offsets only when `not cursor.is_prev`. For prev cursors, start_offset = offset, which can be negative. Cursor.from_string accepts negative integers for the offset field (int(bits[1])), so a client-supplied prev cursor such as `123:-5:1` reaches `queryset[-5:stop]` and raises ValueError, producing a 500. This affects every BasePaginator subclass, including DateTimePaginator used by all audit log requests.

title: Silent behaviour change for all paginators when next-cursor offset is negative
body: The clamp `max(0, offset)` is applied globally in BasePaginator.get_result, not only on the new optimized path. Previously a negative offset on a next cursor raised an error. Now it silently returns the page from the start, for every endpoint using DateTimePaginator or other BasePaginator subclasses. This changes API behaviour for all callers without a gating flag, and the comment describing it as a performance optimization does not justify it.

title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported, but nothing enforces or supports them
body: The added comment says the Cursor enables 'efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions', but Cursor.__init__ merely calls int(offset), and the downstream slicing code in paginator.py cannot handle negative starts. The comment misdescribes the behaviour and will mislead future maintainers.

title: Unreleased experimental pagination switch gated by a query parameter on a public endpoint
body: The endpoint now switches paginator implementation based on a user-supplied `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter, gated only by is_superuser or has_global_access. This adds an undocumented, untested code path to a public (EXPERIMENTAL) API. The optimized path is broken (see paginator.py get_item_key), so any admin who sets this parameter gets a 500. The change also adds no tests and the PR description ('Test 1') does not explain the intent or the behaviour change.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result nearly verbatim
body: The new class copies most of BasePaginator.get_result, including the prev-cursor filtering and build_cursor call, and adds only a branch that is itself broken. Any future fix to the base logic would have to be duplicated here, increasing the chance of divergence. Overriding only the specific behaviour would be safer.

title: No tests added for the new paginator behaviour or the endpoint switch
body: The PR changes pagination behaviour (negative offset handling, a new paginator class, and a new endpoint branch), but adds no tests. Given that the new code paths raise exceptions for datetime keys and negative offsets, tests exercising optimized_pagination=true and negative cursors would have caught these failures.

title: Negative offset on a prev cursor reaches Django slicing and raises
body: In BasePaginator.get_result, `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` passes a negative offset straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` when `cursor.is_prev` is true. Django rejects negative slice indexes with ValueError, so a crafted or stale `prev` cursor with a negative offset turns into a 500 on every paginated endpoint that uses DateTimePaginator. The same applies to the new OptimizedCursorPaginator path.

title: Next-page negative offsets are silently clamped to 0, returning wrong rows
body: For non-prev cursors, `max(0, offset)` silently replaces a negative offset with 0. The cursor's offset is ignored, so the client gets the first page of results instead of the page it asked for, and the returned next/prev cursors do not match the page actually served. Before this change the request was rejected or errored; now it returns misleading data. The `extra`/`len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check at line ~192 also still uses the unclamped `offset`, so the two values disagree.

title: Advanced-feature negative-offset branch slices with a negative start index
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` (negative). Django raises ValueError for negative indexing, so the branch always fails. It is reachable from the request path because the endpoint sets `enable_advanced_features=True` for superusers and global-access members who pass `optimized_pagination=true` and supply a cursor with a negative offset.

title: Privilege gate comment claims permissions are enforced at queryset level, which is false
body: The comment says negative offsets are 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' and that the branch 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds'. The queryset is built identically in both branches, filtered only by organization and the request's filters, so no extra permission check is applied here. The 'advanced' behavior is just an alternate offset handling that is gated on superuser/global access. Relying on a misleading safety comment for a privilege boundary invites future mistakes.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result with divergent logic
body: The new class copies almost all of BasePaginator.get_result, including the prev-cursor handling, and then diverges (the negative-offset branch and the `offset` vs `start_offset` mismatch). The two implementations now differ in subtle ways, so fixes to one (such as the clamping change in BasePaginator) will not reach the other. The class also changes no pagination semantics for the default path, so it adds maintenance risk without a clear benefit.

title: organization_context.member may be None, causing AttributeError for non-superusers
body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `member` for any non-superuser. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is optional, and OrganizationAuditPermission can admit users without a member record, so this line can raise AttributeError and return a 500 for those callers. The check should guard against a missing member.

title: Undocumented, unversioned query flag switches the pagination implementation
body: The `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter changes which paginator runs and enables negative-offset cursors, but it is not part of the serializer, not documented, and not covered by any test. Clients can pass it arbitrarily, and the behavior is effectively an unreviewed API surface on an EXPERIMENTAL endpoint.

title: Comment claims negative offsets are allowed, but the code does not support them
body: The comment says Cursor offsets are allowed to be negative to enable reverse pagination, but Cursor performs no validation and the paginators either clamp (BasePaginator) or fail on slicing (OptimizedCursorPaginator) negative offsets. The comment describes a feature that does not work and will mislead maintainers.

title: No tests added for changed pagination behavior or new paginator
body: The PR changes shared pagination behavior in BasePaginator (affecting every DateTimePaginator user), adds a new OptimizedCursorPaginator class, and adds a new endpoint code path, but includes no tests. Negative-offset cursors, the superuser gate, and the optimized_pagination path are all untested, and the regressions described above would not be caught.

title: PR description is placeholder text
body: The description reads only 'Test 1' and gives no motivation, behavior change, or risk assessment for changing shared pagination semantics. Reviewers cannot tell what behavior is intended or why negative offsets are needed.

title: Negative offset is passed straight to queryset slicing and raises ValueError
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, start_offset is set to the raw negative offset and then used as queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django does not support negative indexing on querysets and raises ValueError, so the request fails with a 500. The client controls this value: a cursor string such as '1:-5:0' parses to a negative offset via Cursor.from_string. The comment that says this is 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' is incorrect; permissions have nothing to do with slicing. The same applies to the base BasePaginator.get_result path for is_prev cursors (line 182 in the base path passes a negative offset through when is_prev is set).

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result nearly verbatim
body: The new class copies most of BasePaginator.get_result (cursor handling, hits counting, prev-row trimming, build_cursor call) and adds only a negative-offset branch that is broken (see the line 882 finding). Any future fix to the base logic will silently diverge in this copy. The class also duplicates get_item_key and value_from_cursor, which are already identical to DateTimePaginator's behavior for the sort keys used here. The change should either extend BasePaginator with a flag or be reverted.

title: Experimental pagination path is gated by a client query parameter and an admin-only flag
body: The optimized paginator is selected by the client-supplied query parameter optimized_pagination=true, and it enables advanced features for superusers and users with global access. This ships an unreviewed, experimental code path (negative offset handling that the code comments describe as allowing 'access to data beyond normal pagination bounds') to production behind a user-controlled switch. The comment claiming permissions are enforced at the queryset level is not backed by any check in the code. Access checks should be explicit and tested, or the path should not be exposed.

title: Deploy will break in-flight segments stored as Redis sets
body: process_spans now uses ZADD on span-buf:s:* keys, and add-buffer.lua switched from SCARD/SUNIONSTORE to ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE. Any span-buf:s:* key written by the previous code is a Redis set, so ZADD, ZCARD and ZUNIONSTORE on it fail with WRONGTYPE, and _load_segment_data's ZSCAN fails as well. Segments buffered before the deploy (up to span_buffer_timeout / root timeout, and the queue entries still reference them) will error during processing and flushing. No key migration, dual-read, or key renaming is included.

title: Span eviction silently discards data with no log or metric
body: When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, zpopmin removes the lowest-scored (oldest) spans from the set. Those spans are dropped without any counter, log, or metric. The previous Python-side guard (max_segment_spans) did emit metrics and an error log, and that check has now been removed from _load_segment_data. Operators have no way to see that segments are being truncated.

title: ZUNIONSTORE sums scores for duplicate payloads
body: ZUNIONSTORE uses the default SUM aggregate. When the same span payload is present in both the source and destination sets (for example, a redelivered Kafka message), its score is doubled, so its end_timestamp_precise no longer reflects the span's real end time. This distorts the eviction order introduced by this PR (zpopmin evicts by score) and any ordering that depends on it. An explicit AGGREGATE MIN or MAX should be used, or duplicates should be otherwise handled.

title: Redirect loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 without updating dependent behavior
body: The redirect-walk loop bound was lowered from 10000 to 1000 and the explanatory comment about deep segment trees was removed. Trees with a redirect depth above 1000 will now be silently left unjoined, where previously they were joined. This is a behavior change that is not mentioned in the PR and has no test covering depth above 1000.

title: max_segment_spans is now a dead parameter
body: The max_segment_spans check was removed from _load_segment_data, but SpansBuffer.__init__ still accepts and stores max_segment_spans (default 1001). Nothing reads it, so the configuration is misleading: callers believe they can tune a span-count limit that no longer does anything. The Lua limit of 1000 is now the only span cap and is hardcoded.

title: Hard KeyError on messages lacking end_timestamp_precise
body: process_batch now reads val["end_timestamp_precise"] directly. Any span message without that field (for example from an older Relay or a schema gap) raises KeyError and fails the whole batch in the consumer, rather than being handled or defaulted. The rest of the code already uses .get() for optional fields such as parent_span_id and is_remote.

title: No tests for the new eviction, the 1000-span cap, or the optimized paginator
body: The PR adds spans-per-segment eviction via zpopmin and a new OptimizedCursorPaginator with negative-offset handling, but no tests cover either. There is no test that inserts more than 1000 spans and checks which survive, no test for duplicate payload score aggregation, and no test for negative or is_prev cursor offsets in pagination. The existing negative-offset bug would have been caught by a single test.

title: Negative-offset comment is wrong and the change clamps offsets for every paginator
body: The new comment says negative offsets are allowed for bidirectional pagination, but `max(0, offset)` on the non-prev path clamps them to 0. This is a silent behavior change for every BasePaginator subclass (DateTimePaginator, Paginator, etc.), not just the new optimized path. A client-supplied negative offset on a next cursor now quietly returns the first page instead of erroring. The comment misdescribes the code and the change is not covered by any test.

title: Negative offset slicing in OptimizedCursorPaginator raises on user-controlled cursors
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django does not support negative indexing on querysets and raises, so the request fails with a 500. `Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets from the query string, so any superuser or global-access member who sends `optimized_pagination=true` with a negative offset cursor triggers this. The inline comments claim the path is 'safe' and that 'permissions are checked at the queryset level', but neither is true: the path crashes and offsets are not a permission boundary.

title: Hidden query parameter switches paginator and cursor semantics for admins
body: `optimized_pagination=true` silently selects a different paginator (OptimizedCursorPaginator with negative-offset support) for superusers and global-access members only. This is an undocumented, client-selectable behavior fork on an API endpoint. Cursors produced by one paginator may not be valid for the other, and the 'advanced' path is the one that can 500 (see paginator.py negative slicing). The non-admin path gets different behavior from the same URL with no documented contract.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result wholesale
body: The new class copies almost all of `BasePaginator.get_result` and `get_item_key`/`value_from_cursor`, differing only in the negative-offset branch. Any future bug fix in BasePaginator (such as the `queryset.query.order_b` typo in build_queryset) must be made in two places, and the two will drift. The divergence that matters is only the negative-offset branch, which is the broken part.

title: Segments are silently truncated to 1000 spans with no metric or log
body: The script now `zpopmin`s the lowest-scored spans whenever a segment exceeds 1000 entries. Those spans are deleted from Redis with no metric or log, so data loss is invisible. Previously, `_load_segment_data` skipped oversized segments and logged `segment_span_count_exceeded`. That check was removed from Python in this PR, and `max_segment_spans` is now unused. The cap also silently drops spans that may include parts of the segment the user cares about, based only on end timestamp order.

title: Redirect-chain walk limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 without justification
body: The loop limit went from 10000 to 1000, and the explanatory comment about deep segment trees was removed. Traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 are now not joined correctly, with no metric or warning. This is an unrelated behavior change folded into a buffering-optimization PR.

title: max_segment_spans parameter is now dead and misleading
body: `max_segment_spans` (default 1001) is still accepted by `SpansBuffer.__init__`, but the check that used it was removed from `_load_segment_data` and the Lua script uses a hard-coded 1000. Callers passing this option expect a limit that no longer applies. The 1001 vs 1000 mismatch adds confusion about the real cap.

title: Hard indexing of end_timestamp_precise can crash the whole batch
body: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises KeyError if a span payload lacks the field. `process_batch` has no guard, so one malformed message fails the entire batch and stalls the consumer. The `cast(SpanEvent, ...)` only affects typing, not runtime validation. Consider `.get` with a fallback or explicit per-message handling.

title: Module docstring still describes sets, not sorted sets
body: The module docstring says spans are added to 'the set under set_key' and the glossary describes span-buf:s:* as sets. Storage is now a sorted set scored by end_timestamp_precise, and the score drives the new trimming. The docs are now wrong for anyone debugging Redis state.

title: No tests for the new 1000-span cap, redirect limit, or negative-offset pagination
body: The PR changes the span cap behavior (truncation via zpopmin), the redirect loop limit, and adds a negative-offset paginator path, but adds no tests for any of them. The existing test_basic/test_deep fixtures only use 4-5 spans, so truncation and the score-based eviction order are untested. The paginator changes have no tests at all.

title: Comment claims permissions are enforced by the queryset; it is not
body: The comment says 'This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' for allowing negative offsets. The queryset only filters by organization_id; the endpoint's permission classes gate access, and nothing in the paginator enforces permissions. The comment misstates the security model and should be removed or corrected.

title: Superusers without a membership cause AttributeError on organization_context.member
body: `enable_advanced` evaluates `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. The `or` only short-circuits for superusers, so a non-superuser path reaches `.member.has_global_access`. For an RpcUserOrganizationContext where `member` is None (a user with no membership in the org, who is then allowed by OrganizationAuditPermission only through other means), this raises AttributeError and returns a 500. The check should guard against a None member explicitly.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime sort keys; ?optimized_pagination=true 500s on audit logs
body: The audit log endpoint routes `optimized_pagination=true` to OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime'. Its get_item_key calls `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` on the raw attribute, which is a datetime for AuditLogEntry.datetime. That raises TypeError on any page with results. Unlike DateTimePaginator, it never converts datetimes to a numeric timestamp, so the new code path is broken for its only caller.

title: Negative offset from user-supplied cursor is not rejected for prev cursors, causing a 500
body: Cursor.from_string accepts any integer offset, including negatives, and Cursor.__init__ no longer rejects them. In BasePaginator.get_result, when cursor.is_prev is True the code uses `start_offset = offset` unchanged, so a negative value goes straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django raises on negative slice indices, so an attacker or a malformed client cursor produces a server error on every paginated endpoint that uses BasePaginator. The removed `if self.offset < 0` guard on other paginators is no longer applied here either.

title: Negative-offset branch relies on a false claim that permissions are enforced at queryset level
body: The enable_advanced_features branch allows arbitrary negative offsets and justifies it with 'permissions are checked at the queryset level'. Nothing in this paginator checks permissions; it only slices whatever queryset it is given. Any caller that sets enable_advanced_features=True gets unbounded negative-index access with no bounds or permission check in the code, and the comment would mislead future maintainers into relying on it. Also, Django does not support negative indexing in slices, so this branch itself raises.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result wholesale, with divergent behavior
body: The new class copies nearly all of BasePaginator.get_result and get_item_key but has already diverged (negative-offset branch, different count_hits/max_hits handling, no datetime support). Fixes applied to one copy will not reach the other, and the endpoint now has two paginators for the same purpose. The 'optimized' name also implies a performance gain that the code does not provide; it is a copy of the same query path plus a negative-offset feature.

title: zunionstore sums scores of duplicate members, corrupting end-timestamp ordering
body: zunionstore uses the default AGGREGATE SUM. When the same span payload exists in both the destination set and the merged set (for example a redelivered Kafka message, or a span re-added after a redirect), its score becomes the sum of the two timestamps rather than the latest one. The scores are later used by zpopmin for eviction and the code relies on them as end timestamps, so the eviction order becomes wrong. The same issue applies at line 53. An explicit AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) is needed.

title: Spans beyond 1000 are silently evicted with no metric or log
body: When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, zpopmin removes the lowest-scored (oldest) spans without any metric, log, or counter. Previously the Python side logged 'segment_span_count_exceeded' and dropped the whole segment; that check was deleted in buffer.py. Data loss is now invisible in operations, and the Python `max_segment_spans` parameter (buffer.py line 150) is left as dead config that no longer matches the hardcoded 1000 limit in Lua.

title: Redirect-depth loop limit lowered from 10000 to 1000 and its explanatory comment removed
body: The loop bound was reduced from 10000 to 1000 and the comment about segment trees deeper than the limit was deleted. Trees deeper than 1000 hops will now be joined incorrectly, silently, with no note in the code. This is an unrelated behavior change folded into an eviction PR, and it should either be justified and documented or reverted.

title: New required field end_timestamp_precise on Span breaks construction and consumer on older messages
body: Span gains a required `end_timestamp_precise: float` positional field. Any external caller constructing Span without it now fails with TypeError. In factory.py process_batch, `val['end_timestamp_precise']` is a hard KeyError, so a single span message from Relay that lacks the field will crash the consumer rather than being handled. This is a contract change that is not guarded or documented.

title: max_segment_spans constructor argument is now unused
body: The `max_segment_spans` parameter is still accepted and stored but is no longer read anywhere after the span-count check was removed from _load_segment_data. Callers who configure it will believe a limit is enforced when it is not; the limit is now the hardcoded 1000 in the Lua script.

title: No test covers the new 1000-span eviction or the score-aggregation behavior
body: The PR adds zpopmin eviction at 1000 spans and changes merge semantics to zunionstore, but no test exercises a segment above the cap or a merge where duplicate payloads occur. The existing tests only use 3-5 spans. Neither the eviction order nor the score sum behavior is verified.

title: No tests for negative cursor offsets or the optimized audit-log path
body: The new negative-offset and OptimizedCursorPaginator code paths, and the optimized_pagination query parameter on the audit log endpoint, have no tests. The datetime TypeError and the negative-offset 500 would have been caught by a simple test.

title: Allowlist eligibility is cached for 60s and the invalidation helper is never called
body: The eligibility result is cached under a key derived only from organization id and project ids, with a 60 second TTL. Changes to `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` are therefore not visible for up to a minute. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (lines 67-74) exists for this purpose but nothing in the PR calls it, so it is dead code and the stale window cannot be cleared on allowlist changes. The docstring calls eventual consistency acceptable, but the allowlist is a rollout control, so a removed project can keep getting upsampled counts for a minute.

title: Cache key built from Python hash() of the project id tuple
body: The cache key embeds `hash(tuple(sorted(...)))` instead of the ids themselves. Distinct project sets can collide to the same key, which would return an eligibility answer computed for a different set of projects. Using the sorted id list (or a stable digest) in the key avoids this. The same expression is duplicated at line 73.

title: Membership test is O(n*m) against a list allowlist
body: `project_id in allowlist` runs against a list for each project, so the check is O(projects * allowlist size) and is repeated on every request. Converting the allowlist to a set once would be cheaper. This is minor unless the allowlist grows.

title: Comments claim caching and late optimization that the code does not implement
body: The comments say the eligibility check is a 'cached result' that 'ensures consistent behavior' and that the decision is stored 'to apply later ... allows for better query optimization and caching'. The code just calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and copies the boolean into `upsampling_enabled`. The transform is then applied in up to three places, each recomputing from `query_columns`. The comments mislead maintainers about what is cached and why, and the duplicated transform blocks should be collapsed into one.

title: Unrelated change to a public error message
body: The topEvents validation message changed from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This is not part of the upsampling feature. Clients or tests matching the old string will break, and the change should be split out or justified.

title: upsampled_count is only defined on the discover function converter
body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count() as count`, and that rewrite is applied whenever the dataset is `errors` (`_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True for it). The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is added only to the discover dataset's function converter. Unless the errors dataset shares this converter, queries on the errors dataset will fail with an unknown function error. The PR's tests only cover the discover path through the endpoint, so this is not caught.

title: upsampled_count ignores the alias set by the caller and hard-codes sum(sample_weight)
body: The function returns `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no guard for events lacking `sample_weight`. The comment says the schema guarantees this, but the transform is driven purely by project allowlist membership. An allowlisted project with events that have no sample_weight will silently produce 0 counts for those events, and nothing in the query path validates this assumption.

title: Helper swallows all exceptions and is applied to every stored test event
