body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps its lookups and conversions in bare `except Exception: pass`. Failures are silently ignored, which makes test data problems hard to diagnose. It also runs for every event in `store_event`, so any test that stores an event with an `error_sampling` context now gets a `sample_rate` set implicitly. That side effect is not documented and is not limited to the upsampling tests.

title: Stray submodule pointer committed to the repository
body: The PR adds a file `sentry-repo` containing a submodule commit hash. It is unrelated to error upsampling and looks like an accidental commit. The PR description 'Test 3' also gives reviewers no context. Both should be removed or explained before merge.

title: upsampled_count is only defined on the discover dataset but is routed to errors too
body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is added only to the discover function converter. `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True for the `errors` dataset, and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` then rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count() as count` for that dataset. The errors dataset has its own function converter, which does not define `upsampled_count`, so queries against `errors` with allowlisted projects will fail with an unknown-function error instead of returning counts.

title: Upsampling eligibility is checked against the outer dataset, not the dataset actually being queried
body: `_get_event_stats` passes the closed-over `dataset` (the request's original dataset) to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, while the query itself is run against `scoped_dataset`. In the dashboard discover-split path the query is routed to `discover` or `errors` via `split_dataset`/`scoped_dataset`, so the decision to upsample can be made for a different dataset than the one that executes the query, which can apply `sum(sample_weight)` to a dataset that doesn't match the check.

title: Negated error filter also triggers upsampling
body: `_is_error_focused_query` uses a substring check `"event.type:error" in query`. A query such as `!event.type:error` (which excludes errors) contains that substring, so it is treated as an error-focused query and gets `count()` rewritten to upsampled counts. The check should parse the query or at least reject negated forms.

title: Rewritten column embeds an alias that the column parser may not accept
body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` returns the literal string `"upsampled_count() as count"` as a y-axis/column. Y-axes and selected columns are normally parsed as function names, optionally with arguments and no inline `as` alias. Passing an alias inside the column string is not part of the documented column grammar, so the query may be rejected or the response key may not be `count` as the tests expect. The alias should be applied by the caller, not embedded in the string.

title: Cache can serve stale eligibility and invalidation is never wired up
body: The allowlist eligibility is cached for 60 seconds under a key that does not encode the allowlist, and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called anywhere in this PR. Changes to `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` will therefore not take effect for up to a minute, and the docstring claiming invalidation 'should be called when the allowlist changes' describes a mechanism that does not exist. Either wire invalidation into the option update path or remove the dead function and fix the docs.

title: Upsampling applied without guarding against missing sample_weight
body: The transform assumes every event in allowlisted projects has `sample_weight`, with no null handling. Events lacking the client sample rate (e.g. older SDKs or events that bypass the sampling context) will contribute NULL/0 to `sum(sample_weight)`, silently undercounting errors rather than falling back to a plain count. The comment explicitly disclaims the check, but the data model does not guarantee it.

title: Helper silently swallows all exceptions
body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps dictionary access and float conversion in bare `except Exception: pass`. Malformed test data will silently produce events without the expected `sample_rate`, causing tests to pass or fail for the wrong reason. It also runs for every event stored through `store_event`, changing the stored sample_rate for all tests, not just upsampling tests. It should be scoped and not swallow errors.

title: Stray submodule-pointer file committed to repository root
body: The PR adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing a commit hash of the base revision. This looks like an accidental artifact (a gitlink or local checkout marker) and does not belong in the repository. It should be removed from the change.

title: Upsampled count assertions are not backed by stored sample_weight
body: The allowlisted-project test expects `count == 10` per bucket from two events stored with `client_sample_rate` 0.1, but nothing in the test setup sets a `sample_weight` on those events, so the expected value depends on ingest-side behavior that is not asserted or documented here. Without an explicit sample_weight the upsampled sum would be 0 or NULL, making the assertion either unverifiable or wrong. The test also never exercises the `errors` dataset, which is where the missing `upsampled_count` function would fail.

title: No tests for the cache path or the public entry point
body: The unit tests cover only the private helpers `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query` and `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`. The public `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (including the cache hit/miss logic and the cached-False case) and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` are untested, and there is no test for the negated-query case above.

title: Unrelated error message text changed
body: The error message for topEvents below 1 changed from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This is outside the scope of upsampling. Any client or test matching the old message will break and the change is not mentioned in the PR description.

title: Stray submodule pointer committed as a regular file
body: The PR adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing `Subproject commit a5d290951...`. This looks like an accidental submodule/gitlink artifact unrelated to the feature. It will confuse checkouts and tooling, and it should not be merged.

title: Cache key built from Python hash() of project IDs can collide and serve wrong eligibility
body: The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`, which is a 64-bit hash, not the project set itself. Two different project sets for the same organization that hash to the same value share one cache entry, so a query can be treated as all-allowlisted (or not) based on another query's result. The consequence is silently wrong error counts, since upsampled sums are returned for a non-allowlisted project set. Using the sorted tuple or a string of the IDs in the key avoids this.

title: 60-second cache of allowlist eligibility makes upsampling decisions stale
body: Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds, but the docstrings state the allowlist is read 'fresh each time' and that caching is 'safe'. Removing a project from the allowlist will still return upsampled counts for up to a minute. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` exists to address this, but nothing calls it, so the stale window is unavoidable. The documented guarantees in this module contradict the implementation.

title: invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code and cannot clear the real cache entries
body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere in the PR. Even if it were, it only deletes the key for the exact project list passed in. Queries that use a subset or different ordering map to other keys, and the allowlist change path has no hook to call it. It should be removed or wired in.

title: Cache-hit and cache-miss paths evaluate the dataset/query check differently and the allowlist is checked before the cheap dataset check
body: On every request, including all non-error datasets (spans, transactions, metrics), the cache lookup and allowlist read happen before `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` short-circuits. The dataset gate should run first so non-error queries skip the cache and option work entirely.

title: Upsampling decision uses the outer dataset and original request query, not the query actually executed
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is called with the endpoint-level `dataset` and `request`, but `_get_event_stats` may run against `scoped_dataset` (e.g. discover for split dashboard widgets) with a rewritten query such as `(query) AND !event.type:transaction`. `_is_error_focused_query` reads `request.GET['query']`, not the query being run. So a widget split into error events can run a discover query that is not upsampled, while the same query in another path is upsampled, giving inconsistent counts. The decision should be based on the dataset and query actually passed in.

title: Unrelated change to public error message text
body: The error detail changed from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This is outside the scope of error upsampling, changes an API response string that clients or tests may match on, and is not mentioned in the PR description.

title: Comments claim caching gives consistent behavior, which is not true
body: The comments say 'This cached result ensures consistent behavior across query execution' and 'allows for better query optimization and caching'. The eligibility is cached for 60 seconds and the transform is a pure column rewrite, so neither statement is accurate. The comments also describe a late transform that is actually the same logic duplicated in three branches. These comments will mislead maintainers.

title: Redundant reassignment of final_columns across three branches
body: `final_columns` is initialized to `query_columns` and then re-derived in up to three separate places with the same condition. Only one path runs per call, so this adds state and maintenance risk without benefit. A single computed value before the branches would be clearer and avoids the chance of one branch being updated and another missed.

title: upsampled_count assumes sample_weight is never null, which the test factories do not guarantee
body: The comment says sample_weight is guaranteed for allowlisted projects, but the factory change only sets sample_rate when the event contains an error_sampling context. Events without that context, which are common in tests and possibly in production, may have null or missing sample_weight. `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` over nulls can then return zero or error. Relying on an unverified schema invariant without a null guard is risky.

title: Helper swallows all exceptions silently and changes store_event behavior globally
body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps reads and conversions in bare `except Exception: pass`, hiding malformed fixtures. It is also called from the shared `store_event` factory used by the whole test suite, so every test that stores events with a contexts.error_sampling payload has its sample_rate silently altered. The change should be scoped to the tests that need it, and failures should not be swallowed.

title: Tests do not cover the discover-split, cache, or non-allowlisted-with-error-query paths that the implementation changes
body: The new endpoint tests only cover the top-level discover query with event.type:error and transactions. They do not exercise the dashboard widget split branch where scoped_dataset and the query differ, the cache hit path (including stale-after-allowlist-change behavior), or the topEvents path where upsampling is applied to timeseries columns. The unit tests in test_error_upsampling.py also do not test `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` or its caching at all. The highest-risk new logic is therefore untested.

title: Migration 0917 silently becomes a no-op on already-deployed environments
body: The body of convert_org_saved_searches_to_views is replaced with an unconditional return. Migration 0917 is a historical migration that may already have been applied in some environments (the test file tests/sentry/migrations/test_0917... that exercised it was removed). For those databases the data conversion they previously ran is not reverted, while fresh installs skip it entirely. Replacing a shipped migration body rather than adding a new one breaks the invariant that applied migrations are immutable, and the comment refers to a 0921 file that does not appear in this PR.

title: Org saved searches are never converted to views
body: The revised migration 0920 is also stubbed out to return immediately, so organization-visible saved searches will not be migrated into GroupSearchView. The comment points to a 0921 migration that is not included in this change, so the conversion is dropped entirely and users lose their shared saved searches.

title: Removed traceparent experiment option still referenced elsewhere
body: The options/defaults.py change deletes the 'grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent' option, but this PR does not show removal of its consumers. Any code that still calls options.get on this key will raise an unregistered-option error at runtime; the change should be verified against all call sites.

title: Broad exception swallowing and logging of exception object in get_environment_info
body: get_environment_info catches every Exception and logs it under 'error' in extra with the raw exception object. Failures are silently reduced to an info-level log, and passing a non-serializable exception object in extra can break log formatting. Errors such as DB failures are hidden from Sentry and monitoring.

title: Template is called via PRCommentWorkflow but defined on CommitContextIntegration; environment appended to title with no escaping
body: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, but the method is defined in the same class hierarchy used differently; more importantly the issue title and environment name are interpolated into Markdown without escaping, so titles containing Markdown or link syntax can break or inject content into the PR comment.

title: Error events are fetched with zip against nodestore results that may be misaligned
body: fetch_error_details zips error_ids with events.values(). nodestore get_multi returns a dict keyed by node id, and its values() order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so error titles/messages can be attached to the wrong event IDs. Use the mapping by node_id instead.

title: Timestamp default uses float 0.0 for error events while comparison also treats missing timestamp as 0
body: In fetch_error_details the event dict is accessed with data.get on a possibly None-less value, and the error-message generator compares error timestamps against event.get('timestamp', 0), which is in seconds for the breadcrumbs but may be in a different unit for nodestore error payloads, leading to incorrect chronological interleaving.

title: Logged event_data changed to workflow_event_data, dropping the consistent event payload
body: The log extra key 'event_data' now receives workflow_event_data (which includes workflow_env) rather than the shared event_data object, changing the structured log schema that downstream dashboards may rely on without any note.

title: Owner not validated against organization membership in create path
body: The new owner field is accepted and stored directly in create(). Owner validation (organization membership) relies on ActorField, but the detector is created with owner_user_id/owner_team_id without checking that the team/user belongs to the detector's project/organization, allowing cross-organization ownership assignment through the API.

title: Column fallback uses tableData optional chaining after dereferencing
body: columnOrder computes Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields) with optional chaining on tableData but then accesses tableData?.meta.fields[key] per key; if tableData is undefined, Object.keys(undefined) throws before the optional chain protects it, so the component crashes instead of rendering an empty table.

title: Feature flag branch renders an empty table instead of the real data
body: When the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature is enabled, the TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with columns=[] and empty tableData, discarding result.data, result.meta, and loading state. Dashboard table widgets for that org will show no data at all.

title: Attribute keys query lost its environment parameter and error/retry behavior
body: The rewritten hook drops the staleTime, refetchOnWindowFocus and retry options and switches to useQuery with a queryKey that does not include all dependencies such as the selected environments previously sent in the request. Stale attribute lists can be served across environment/project changes.

title: Hook no longer accepts enabled flag but callers still pass it
body: Callers such as transactionNameSearchBar previously passed attributeKey and enabled; the rename removed those props from the type, so the removed options silently stop controlling fetch behavior and the attributeKey is now ignored in the query key.

title: Visualize.fromJSON return type change breaks URL-state consumers
body: fromJSON now returns Visualize[] instead of Visualize while the persisted JSON still uses yAxes arrays; any caller that expects a single Visualize (or the isVisualize check that now tests yAxis) can mis-parse existing saved queries and URLs containing multi-yAxis visualizes.

title: Empty case leaves a dangling blank statement
body: After removing the Type rows, the COMPONENT case is left with a blank line where data was pushed, and the removed Type row also removes information users relied on in grouping debugging, with no replacement.

title: Serializer validation rejects reports with the same timestamp-age ambiguity and logs raw report bodies
body: On validation failure the endpoint logs raw_report and the full validation_errors at warning level, which can contain arbitrary browser-supplied body data, inflating logs and potentially leaking user URLs. The endpoint also now returns 422 for any single malformed report, dropping the whole batch that was previously processed.

title: Logger replaced with log_context logger without a corresponding import check
body: logger switches to log_context.get_logger, which changes the logging namespace from the module logger; logs previously filtered by module name will no longer match.

title: Migration 0917 is neutered but still registered and marked as post-deployment
body: The body of convert_org_saved_searches_to_views was replaced with a bare return, so the data migration never copies organization saved searches into GroupSearchView. The migration is still in the chain (and 0920 is also neutered), so environments that already applied the old code will not re-run it, and fresh/other environments silently skip the conversion. The comment points to a file '0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py' that is not part of this diff, so the intended correct migration may not exist.

title: Revised saved-search conversion migration became a no-op, losing data conversion
body: The revised migration 0920 was reduced to an early return, deleting the logic that converts ORGANIZATION-visibility SavedSearch rows into GroupSearchView rows. Its comment references a 0921 migration that does not exist in this change set. As merged, org saved searches are never converted and users lose their org-level views.

title: Analytics event recorded before feature-flag check
body: analytics.record is called for every request, including those rejected with 404 'Feature not enabled' and unauthenticated-feature requests, so usage analytics count traffic from orgs without the feature. It also runs before body validation. Move it after the feature check, or after successful assembly.

title: Parameterizer.parametrize_w_experiments drops ParameterizationRegex support but ParameterizationRegex remains in use
body: The change removes ParameterizationRegexExperiment and the isinstance dispatch in parametrize_w_experiments, so any experiment that is a ParameterizationRegex will now fail (its run method no longer exists). The ParameterizationExperiment type alias now only accepts callable experiments, which is a breaking API change for any caller passing regex experiments and removes the regex experiment tests without replacement.

title: Removal of grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent option
body: The option registration is deleted while the parameterization code and grouping config may still read it. Any code calling options.get on this key will now raise an unknown-option error. Confirm no remaining reader exists.

title: Default autofix automation tuning changed from 'low' to 'off' for all projects
body: The default is silently changed, which alters behavior for every existing project that never set the option (it stops autofix automation). This is also reflected in constants.py and tests, but it is a product-behavior change unrelated to the title/description, and it is not called out.

title: Error IDs fetched from replay query without guarding against missing fields and runs before pagination
body: error_ids is read via response[0].get('error_ids', []) from process_raw_response, and fetch_error_details is called eagerly on every request (including every paginated page), issuing Snuba and nodestore queries on each page. Also fetch_error_details zips error_ids with get_multi values, which is only correct if nodestore returns results in the same order and with the same length; missing nodes are silently dropped and misalign the zip.

title: Error events fetched from nodestore with a mismatched zip and no key-to-id mapping
body: In fetch_error_details, `zip(error_ids, events.values())` pairs IDs with dict values by iteration order of the returned mapping, not by key. If get_multi omits any missing node, every subsequent error is attached to the wrong event ID. Iterate over node_ids and look up each key instead.

title: Null max_segment_id skip hides a real data-inconsistency case
body: Returning an empty filename list when max_segment_id is None means recording blobs for that replay are never deleted, while the replay row is still archived by delete_replays. Storage for such replays leaks. The comment also contains the typo 'segements'.

title: Detector update uses 'detector_type' key that is never validated
body: update() reads validated_data.get('detector_type', instance.group_type) and then calls .slug on it; 'detector_type' is not a serializer field (the field is 'type', which is validated to a GroupType class). The result is that the type is never changed on update and instance.group_type may not exist on Detector, risking AttributeError when the key is absent.

title: Logging 'event_data' key now uses workflow_event_data but the outer scope variable may differ
body: The extra payload changed from event_data to workflow_event_data, which changes the log schema for existing log consumers and dashboards keyed on 'event_data' with the shared event payload. Mixed semantics across logs should be checked.

title: Serializer rejects validated age/timestamp combos incorrectly and returns 422 for legitimate reports
body: validate_timestamp and validate_age use truthiness of self.initial_data.get('age'), so age=0 is treated as absent. Also, the endpoint now returns 422 for any malformed report and stops processing the whole batch, where previously it accepted reports. This is a behavior change that can cause browsers to drop valid batches containing one bad report.

title: Browser report body logged with request_body removed, plus dead metric tag type change
body: The logger.info for 'browser_report_received' was removed by the test diff's removal of the logging assertion, reducing observability of the raw payloads that the endpoint is meant to collect for real-world data gathering.

title: noise_config added to DB query injection group type without validation of intent
body: NoiseConfig(ignore_limit=5) is added to DBQueryInjectionVulnerabilityGroupType, changing alerting/noise behavior for this issue type across all projects without a flag gate or accompanying test.

title: Summary query fires with enabled flag only checked on feature list, and tooFewFeedbacks logic is inverted-looking
body: tooFewFeedbacks is computed as numFeedbacksUsed === 0 && !success, which hides the summary only in the case of no feedbacks and failure; other too-few cases (e.g. success false with some feedbacks) show a summary component with null text. The name and condition do not match the described behavior.

title: Table widget under feature flag renders empty hardcoded data instead of query results
body: When organization has 'use-table-widget-visualization', TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with columns=[] and tableData with data: [] and empty meta, ignoring result.data, loading and errors. Users with the flag see an empty table for every table widget.

title: Attribute keys query no longer carries environment and its queryKey is not scoped to the endpoint
body: The old query included environment: selection.environments; the new makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions drops environment (commented as intentional) while the React Query key uses a fixed prefix plus query options, so cached results across page filters may be shared incorrectly. Also the hook's `error` is now returned but callers may ignore it, silently showing stale attributes.

title: Error wrapping loses the original error object
body: throw new Error(`...: ${e}`) stringifies the caught error and discards the stack and type, making debugging of attribute-key failures harder.

title: Attribute value hook no longer respects enabled flag or attributeKey
body: The hook signature dropped attributeKey and enabled, but callers like transactionNameSearchBar still pass attributeKey historically; the returned function is now a getter taking (tag, query). Callers relying on the old enabled flag to suppress requests will now fire requests unconditionally.

title: Visualize model collapses multi-yAxis visualizations, breaking existing URLs
body: The change moves from yAxes arrays to a single yAxis per Visualize, but fromJSON still accepts yAxes arrays and returns multiple objects; saved and shared links with multiple y-axes in one visualize entry now split into separate charts with different labels and stack behavior, and BaseVisualize.toJSON writes back yAxes: [single], changing the persisted URL format for all users.

title: Chart info now only ever renders a single yAxis, dropping the default visualization dedupe
body: getChartInfo takes a single yAxis and wraps it in an array; the previous dedupeArray guarding duplicate yAxes is removed, so duplicated series names can now appear in the same chart legend if the same yAxis is used twice.

title: Grouping variant 'Type' rows removed from UI with no replacement
body: All 'Type' key-value rows and their explanatory tooltips were deleted for every variant type, removing the only user-visible explanation of what kind of grouping variant is shown.

title: Analytics event name changed from underscore to hyphen
body: trackAnalytics('replay.view_html') was changed to 'replay.view-html', but the event key is part of the analytics contract; historical dashboards and the replayAnalyticsEvents map depend on the existing name, so this silently splits metrics.

title: Transparent mask gradient now depends on theme background instead of white
body: The transparent variant changed from rgba(255,255,255,...) to theme.background, which changes appearance in dark theme and is unrelated to the PR scope.

title: PR comment test compares against stale expected strings
body: The expected comments were rewritten to a new format and new environment suffix, but the GitLab test still uses self.another_organization while the GitHub comment-workflow test drops the culprit assertion; these tests can pass for the wrong reasons because titles are looked up by ordering from Group.objects without deterministic ordering in the updates test.

title: get_environment_info logs issue with an exception object in extra and swallows errors broadly
body: The bare except Exception logs the exception object as an extra value (not serializable in some logging backends) and silently returns empty environment text. Additionally get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title from a staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration, which is a name that does not exist in that class scope and will raise NameError at runtime.

title: Comment references a migration filename that does not exist
body: The comment points to '0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py' as the correct migration, but the revised migration in this PR is 0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py. The pointer is wrong and will mislead maintainers looking for the replacement.

title: Revised migration body was stubbed out, so org saved searches are never converted
body: The conversion logic was removed and replaced with a bare return, while the comment says the migration 'had an error and was never run' and points to a non-existent 0921 file. The revised migration is the one that is supposed to run in production, so existing organization saved searches will never be converted into GroupSearchViews. This is a silent data-migration loss, and the deleted test for 0917 removes the only coverage.

title: Parameterizer.parametrize_w_experiments drops the regex-experiment path but ParameterizationExperiment is now only callable experiments
body: The Parameterizer no longer distinguishes regex experiments; any caller that still constructs a ParameterizationRegex-based experiment (or the removed ParameterizationRegexExperiment) will fail at runtime. The removal of the public __all__ entry is an API break for anything importing it, and the removed tests were the only coverage for regex experiments.

title: Removes registered option grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent
body: The option is deleted while the 'traceparent' regex is still in DEFAULT_PARAMETERIZATION_REGEXES and tests still expect traceparent parameterization. Any deployment that has this option set in configuration or code that reads it will now hit an unregistered-option error.

title: Logging extra now uses workflow_event_data but the surrounding code logs per-workflow data
body: Changing 'event_data' to 'workflow_event_data' in the log extra alters the logged payload semantics; the field name is unchanged so downstream log queries keyed on event_data may now see per-environment data for the same key. Minor, but worth confirming intent.

title: Null max_segment_id skip hides rows from the deletion job without marking them
body: When max_segment_id is None, _make_recording_filenames returns no files, but delete_replays still archives the replay. Replays with no ingested segments are archived without verifying there are no leftover blobs; the comment says segments may be missing but the behavior silently skips any stored video/recording blobs for those replays.

title: Snuba query result indexed without checking shape
body: response[0].get('error_ids') assumes process_raw_response returns a non-empty list of dicts; if query_replay_instance returns no rows the code falls back to [], but for a missing error_ids key the default is fine only if the first row is a dict. Also query_replay_instance is now called on every request before pagination, adding an extra Snuba round trip to the summarize path with no caching.

title: Error events merged in by timestamp assumes breadcrumb timestamps are seconds, with the error sort mutating shared input
body: get_request_data sorts error_events in place via list.sort, mutating the caller's list. Combined with functools.partial reuse across pagination pages, error_events is re-sorted on each page. The per-page merge also re-emits every error before each segment's events that follows it, so the same error can appear in multiple pages or be dropped from later pages because the error_idx state is recomputed per page.

title: Strict validation now returns 422 for whole batch on a single malformed report
body: Previously invalid reports did not reject the request; now one invalid report in the array causes the entire batch to return 422 and the valid reports are not recorded. Browsers sending batched reports will lose all data for an invalid entry, and the new validation also rejects fields like age vs timestamp that the spec permits, changing behavior for existing clients.

title: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template is a staticmethod that calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, but it is defined on CommitContextIntegration
body: The helper references PRCommentWorkflow, which is not defined in this module scope at that point, so the call to _truncate_title will raise NameError at runtime when comments are generated. The base class method should use self or the class directly.

title: get_environment_info logs the exception object as a field and swallows all errors
body: A broad except Exception logs at info level with the raw exception object in extra, which is not serializable into structured logs and hides real failures (e.g. DB errors) behind a silent empty environment string.

title: Owner update applies even when not provided by user and clears owner on partial update
body: In update(), 'owner' in validated_data is checked, but ActorField is not required; when the owner is None-valued and a client sends a partial update that omits owner, the branch is skipped correctly. However when owner is explicitly passed as None it clears both fields, and the create path does not validate that the owner belongs to the organization, letting cross-organization actors be assigned as owners.

title: Module logger switched to log_context logger without a corresponding behavior test
body: logger is replaced with log_context.get_logger which may not support the standard logging keyword arguments used throughout this module (extra=...). Calls such as logger.info(..., extra=...) rely on the stdlib signature, and the change has no test coverage.

title: Analytics event recorded before the feature-flag check, and it uses the wrong event name
body: analytics.record is called before features.has, so requests for orgs without the feature still emit 'preprod_artifact.api.assemble' events. The event is also registered as PreprodArtifactApiAssembleEvent but recorded by string without the registered class being imported by the endpoint, so analytics metadata is inconsistent with the other preprod events.

title: processing_deadline_duration=60 may be shorter than check_single_auth_identity work for chunk_size=100
body: The task now has a 60-second deadline but processes up to chunk_size identities sequentially with external provider refresh calls; a full chunk can exceed the deadline, causing retries and duplicated work.

title: LoadingPlaceholder passes an empty columnOrder and sets no tableData; placeholder rendering is untested
body: The LoadingPlaceholder renders GridEditable with no columns and no data; this is only exercised in stories and has no spec. Minor, but it is public API used by chart.tsx indirectly.

title: TabularColumn type duplicated in a fixture file
body: TabularColumn is newly exported here while tests/js/fixtures/tabularColumn.ts duplicates the shape; fixture types drift when the canonical type changes.

title: Table widget renders a hard-coded empty table behind a feature flag
body: When the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature is on, TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with columns=[] and empty tableData, discarding result.data, fields, and meta entirely. Any org with the flag enabled sees empty tables for all table widgets.

title: Hook doc comment and removed enabled option leave callers without an enabled guard
body: The previously supported enabled and search options were removed from the hook, but the hook still performs an API request on every call with no cancellation or dedupe, which can cause duplicate fetches on each keystroke in transactionNameSearchBar.

title: Attribute keys query now runs through useQuery with a key that does not include the query function's inputs
body: The query key is built from makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions, which omits environment, while the queryFn captures projectIds from the closure; key and fn can diverge so cached results can be served for different project sets.

title: Variant type rows removed from grouping info panel
body: The 'Type' row with its explanatory tooltip is deleted from every variant case, so users lose the only description of what each grouping variant type means, and the COMPONENT case now has an empty statement block.

title: Visualize model changed from multi-yAxis to single yAxis, breaking persisted and URL-encoded visualizes
body: Visualize now holds a single yAxis, but parseBaseVisualize and saved queries still encode yAxes arrays; multi-yAxis queries from existing URLs and saved explore queries are silently truncated or split, changing chart definitions for existing users.

title: Writable field refs filter now uses isBaseVisualize but reads a yAxes array that the old code did not guarantee
body: findAllFieldRefs changed the filter to BaseVisualize but still flatMaps visualize.yAxes; combined with the Visualize API change this is inconsistent with the rest of the file which now uses yAxis.

title: Top-events suppression for multi-yAxis charts removed while chart still supports multiple visualize entries
body: The check that disabled topEvents when any visualize had multiple yAxes was deleted, so grouped top-N queries can now be issued for charts that the chart renderer cannot represent correctly.

title: Feature gate checked only in the component, but the hook still fires the summary request
body: useFeedbackSummary enables the query based on the feature flag but FeedbackSummary still calls it unconditionally, so non-entitled orgs issue summary requests that always fail, and the retry: 1 doubles the cost.

title: Analytics event renamed from replay.view_html to replay.view-html without updating the event map entry
body: The emitted event name changed to 'replay.view-html' while replayAnalyticsEvents.tsx still defines 'replay.view-html' as the key; the rename breaks existing dashboards and alerts that filter on replay.view_html.

title: Transparent mask gradient now uses theme background, changing visual output for transparentMask carousels
body: The transparent variant changed from rgba(255,255,255) white to the theme background, altering appearance in dark mode and not covered by any test.

title: minmax arguments are reversed for grid column
body: grid-template-columns: minmax(195px, 1fr) 1.5fr is correct now, but the removed rule minmax(1fr, 195px) was invalid; the change is fine but the list grid now also wraps FeedbackList in a new column container that is not covered by layout tests.

title: Changing the owner feature on create without validating org membership in the serializer
body: owner is accepted via ActorField without checking membership in the organization; test_owner_not_in_organization expects a 400 but the validator does not enforce it, so that test will fail or the behavior is untested.

title: GitHub user verification is skipped entirely for installations without an existing Integration
body: When no Integration row exists for the installation_id, the code returns `pipeline.next_step()` immediately. The new check that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub login matches `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` only runs when the Integration already exists (line ~501). If the installation webhook has not yet created the Integration, or the flow is reached in another order, the pipeline proceeds with no check that the authenticated user installed the app. That makes the OAuth step ineffective in exactly the path it is meant to guard, so an attacker could complete installation with an installation_id they do not own.

title: KeyError when the existing Integration has no 'sender' metadata
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes the key exists. `build_integration` only stores `sender` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy, and integrations created by other paths or before this field existed will not have it. For such an ACTIVE integration the check raises KeyError and the setup request returns a 500 instead of the intended error page. Use a safe lookup and fail closed with the error response.

title: Network failure in OAuth token exchange is not handled
body: `safe_urlopen` is called outside the try block that protects only `safe_urlread`. If GitHub is unreachable or the request times out, the exception propagates and the user gets a 500 rather than the 'Invalid installation request' error page used for every other failure in this view. Wrap the request in the same error handling, or return `error(...)` on exception.

title: Test for installation-not-found no longer exercises the not-found path
body: The original assertion checked for 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' from the 404 branch in `build_integration`. The test now sends a mismatched state, so it fails earlier with 'Invalid installation request.' and the 404 branch has no coverage. The test name no longer matches what it checks. Restore the original 404 scenario and add a separate state-mismatch test.

title: GitHub user check is skipped on first installation
body: The new authenticated-user check at the end of GitHubInstallation.dispatch only runs when an Integration with the installation_id already exists. When `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises DoesNotExist (lines ~481-482), the code returns `pipeline.next_step()` immediately, bypassing the check. The mismatch protection therefore does not apply when the webhook has not yet created the Integration, which is the case the PR says it guards against. The check should run on every path that proceeds to next_step, or the missing-Integration case should be handled explicitly.

title: KeyError when the stored integration has no sender metadata
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is accessed directly. build_integration only sets metadata["sender"] when state contains a sender, so integrations created without one (or with a different metadata shape) will raise KeyError and return a 500 during the install flow instead of the intended error page. Use a safe lookup and fail the pipeline with the error view when the sender is missing.

title: Network failure in the OAuth code exchange is not handled
body: `req = safe_urlopen(...)` is outside the try block, so a connection error or timeout raises an uncaught exception and produces a 500. Only the body read/parse is wrapped. The exchange should be inside the try or otherwise return the error view on failure.

title: OAuth authorize URL parameters are not URL-encoded
body: The redirect is built by string formatting: `state` and `redirect_uri` are interpolated into the query string without urlencode. A redirect_uri that contains `&` or `#`, or a state containing reserved characters, would corrupt the authorize request. Build the query with urllib.parse.urlencode.

title: Brittle hard-coded responses.calls index
body: The assertion changed from `responses.calls[0]` to `responses.calls[2]` to check the JWT header. This depends on the exact ordering of mocked HTTP calls, including the new OAuth calls. Any reordering breaks the test without a meaningful reason. Locate the call to the access_tokens endpoint by URL instead.

title: New OAuth failure paths are not tested
body: The PR lists three failure modes: state mismatch, a failed access_token exchange (wrong or reused code), and a GitHub user mismatch. Only the user mismatch is tested, and only on the reinstall path. There is no test for a bad state parameter or an access_token exchange that fails. There is also no test for the first-installation case where no Integration exists yet, which is the bypass described above.

title: Sender/user check is skipped entirely for new installations
body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, when no Integration exists for the installation_id, the `except Integration.DoesNotExist` branch at line 482 returns `pipeline.next_step()` immediately. The new check that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user matches `integration.metadata['sender']['login']` (lines 493-505) is therefore only reached for pre-existing Integrations. The first-time install, which is the main path the PR is meant to protect, never validates the authenticated user against the app installer. The PR description says the pipeline should fail on a user mismatch, but for new installs it will proceed regardless of who completed OAuth.

title: KeyError when the existing Integration has no sender in metadata
body: The check at lines 501-505 indexes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` directly. `build_integration` only sets `metadata["sender"]` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy (integration.py around line 376), so Integrations created without a sender (or with metadata lacking it) raise KeyError and turn the install step into a 500. Also `fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` may be None if the OAuth step was skipped, which would then be compared as a mismatch with no clear error. This should use `.get()` with an explicit failure path.

title: Network failure in the token exchange is unhandled
body: `safe_urlopen(url=..., data=data)` at line 423 is outside the try block that guards only the body read and parse. If GitHub is unreachable or times out, the exception propagates and the user gets a 500 instead of the friendly invalid-installation error. The same applies to `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` at line 434, which is also not guarded. Both calls should be wrapped so failures route to `error(...)`.

title: code parameter is not validated before the token exchange
body: `data["code"]` is taken from `request.GET.get("code")` (line 417) and may be None when the GitHub callback lacks a code. The request is still sent to GitHub with an empty code. This is harmless only because GitHub rejects it, but it causes a needless external call and makes the failure mode depend on GitHub's response rather than an explicit check.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the 404 path
body: The test was changed so the second request uses a mismatched state (`ddd023...`), so it now fails at the state check in OAuthLoginView and asserts only the generic 'Invalid installation request.' message. The original assertion for 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' from build_integration's 404 handling is gone, and nothing else covers that branch anymore. The test should send a matching state and assert the 404-specific message.

title: No test covers a successful user match for an existing integration or a new install without sender
body: The new tests only cover the mismatch path (test_github_user_mismatch) and the state-mismatch case. There is no test asserting that a matching authenticated user succeeds when an Integration already exists with a sender, and none for a first-time install, which is the path where the check is skipped. Tests also depend on hard-coded `responses.calls[2]` indices (line 257 in assert_setup_flow), which makes them fragile to any change in the number of HTTP calls.

title: Unrelated removal of the FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR module constant
body: The diff removes the public module-level constant `FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR` and inlines `provider_id == "github"`. This change is not part of the stated security fix. If any other module imports this constant it will break, and the inlining makes it harder to extend to other providers. It should be split into a separate change or kept as is.

title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass default, so `timezone.now()` runs once when the module is imported. Every `AssignmentSource` created in the process then gets the same stale timestamp rather than the time the assignment was queued. The field is serialized into the task payload, so the recorded time is wrong. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

title: to_dict() returns a datetime that is passed into Celery task kwargs
body: `to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)`, which keeps `queued` as a `datetime` object. `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes this dict as `assignment_source_dict` in `apply_async` kwargs. If the task serializer is JSON, which is the usual setup, enqueuing fails with a TypeError on every assignment that carries an assignment source, such as every inbound Jira/integration assignment. The outbound sync would then break for exactly the path this PR touches. Serialize `queued` to an ISO string (and parse it back in `from_dict`), or drop it from the payload.

title: from_dict does not restore `queued` to a datetime and accepts any value
body: `from_dict` passes the dict straight into the constructor, so a `queued` value round-tripped through JSON comes back as a string, not a datetime. The annotation `datetime` is then wrong for any consumer that reads it. Also, the broad `(ValueError, TypeError)` handling silently turns malformed payloads into `None`, which hides the loss of the loop-prevention context.

title: Tests do not cover the serialization round trip used by the Celery task
body: `test_to_dict` only checks that `queued` is not None, and no test runs `from_dict(to_dict())` or passes the dict through a JSON round trip. That is the path used by `sync_group_assignee_outbound` and `sync_assignee_outbound`, and it is where the datetime serialization problem would show up.

title: No test covers the deassign path with a matching assignment source
body: The loop fix is tested only for `assign`. The `deassign` path, which also now accepts `assignment_source` and forwards it to the outbound sync, has no test checking that an inbound unassign from integration X skips outbound sync to X. The inbound deassign flow in `sync_group_assignee_inbound` is therefore untested for the cycle-breaking behaviour the PR is meant to provide.

title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time, not per instance
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` runs once when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created in the process gets the same timestamp: the process start time. The field is meant to record when the assignment was queued, but it will be wrong for every instance. Use a default factory (`field(default_factory=timezone.now)`) or set it explicitly at creation.

title: to_dict() returns a datetime that is passed through Celery task kwargs
body: `to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)`, which keeps `queued` as a `datetime` object. The result is passed as `assignment_source_dict` into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(...)`. If Celery uses the JSON serializer, which is typical for Sentry, a datetime cannot be encoded and enqueueing fails. On the consuming side, `from_dict` also receives `queued` as a string rather than a datetime, so the round-trip does not preserve the field type. Serialize `queued` to an ISO string (or drop it) in `to_dict`, and parse it back in `from_dict`.

title: No test that deassign with a matching assignment source skips outbound sync
body: The new `assignment_source` parameter on `GroupAssignee.objects.deassign` and the matching-source short-circuit are only exercised for `assign`. `test_assignee_sync_outbound_unassign` only checks the `assignment_source=None` path. The inbound unassign path (`sync_group_assignee_inbound` with `assign=False`) is the one that can create the Jira-to-Jira loop, and it is untested for the case where the source integration matches the target. Add a test that deassigns with a matching `AssignmentSource` and asserts `sync_assignee_outbound` is not called.

title: `queued` is a datetime that gets passed through Celery task kwargs, which are likely not JSON-serializable
body: `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)`, which includes the `queued` datetime object as-is. `sync_group_assignee_outbound` puts this dict into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)` as `assignment_source_dict`. If the integrations task queue serializes arguments as JSON (the usual Celery setup in Sentry), the datetime makes `apply_async` fail with a serialization error. The outbound assignee sync would then break for every assignment that carries a source, which is the exact webhook path this PR is meant to fix. The tests only call `to_dict()` directly and never push the result through a task, so this is not caught. Either serialize `queued` to an ISO string in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`, or drop the field from the serialized payload.

title: Default `queued` timestamp is evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass default, so it is computed once when the module is imported. Every `AssignmentSource` created in the process then gets the same stale timestamp, not the time the assignment happened. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

title: `should_sync` is now called with two arguments on all installations, which breaks overrides that accept only one
body: The task now calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`. `IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync` was updated, but any installation whose class overrides `should_sync(self, attribute)` with the old one-argument signature will raise TypeError at runtime. The outbound sync path is then broken for that integration. Either update all overrides in the same PR or only pass the source when the method accepts it.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract class that cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but its body is just `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares several abstract members (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data). Because none are implemented, instantiating the class raises TypeError. Detector.detector_handler calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, so any Detector with type 'metric_alert_fire' will crash when its handler is built, where previously it returned an empty list. Either implement the abstract members or keep the previous non-stateful base.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: The docstring of StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate still says it 'returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`', but the method now returns a dict keyed by group key. Callers and implementers reading the docstring will expect the old contract.

title: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe expects an occurrence whose fingerprint does not match the evaluated group key
body: The expected occurrence is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...)`, so its fingerprint is `<id>:val1`. The call under test is `evaluate_group_key_value("group_key", ...)`, and the hook builds the occurrence with fingerprint `<id>:group_key`. The equality assertion compares the full IssueOccurrence, so the fingerprints differ and the assertion should fail. Either the expected group key should be "val1" or the occurrence should be built with "group_key". The test also passes value 6 while the actual call uses 10, which is misleading even though the mock ignores it.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: The class subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and its body is just `pass`. This PR adds a new `@abc.abstractmethod` `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, and the existing abstract methods `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value` and `get_group_key_values` are also not implemented. Instantiating the class therefore raises TypeError. `Detector.detector_handler` constructs the handler for every detector of type `metric_alert_fire`, so `process_detectors` will crash for those detectors. Previously the handler's `evaluate` returned [] and worked. Either keep a non-abstract placeholder implementation or implement the required methods.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: The docstring of `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` says it 'returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`', but the signature now returns a dict keyed by group key. Callers and readers relying on the docstring will expect the wrong type.

title: Mock occurrence builder ignores the value it is supposed to report
body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` never uses its `value` argument, and the occurrence does not depend on it. Several tests build the expected occurrence with value 6 while evaluating a different value (e.g. `test_results_on_change` evaluates 100, `test_dedupe` evaluates 8). Because the expected and actual occurrences are built the same way, these assertions cannot detect the hook being called with the wrong value or group key. The new hook's argument contract is therefore not actually tested.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: The class now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but its body is just `pass`. The base class declares `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data` as abstract. None of these are implemented, so `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(detector)` raises TypeError. `Detector.detector_handler` calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, so any detector of type `metric_alert_fire` will now crash in `process_detectors`. Before this change the handler returned [] and was instantiable.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: The docstring of StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate says it 'returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`', but the method now returns a dict keyed by group key. The abstract signature in DetectorHandler was updated, so this docstring is now wrong and will mislead implementers.

title: Renamed helpers `mark_failed_threshold` and `create_issue_platform_occurrence` are removed with no call-site updates in this PR
body: The PR deletes `mark_failed_threshold` and `create_issue_platform_occurrence` from `mark_failed.py` and replaces them with `try_incident_threshold` and `create_incident_occurrence` in new modules. Nothing in the changed files shows the other callers or tests being updated. Any remaining import of the old names, or any `mock.patch("sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence")`-style patch in the test suite, will fail with ImportError or AttributeError. The PR should either update every reference in the repo or keep backward-compatible aliases until they are gone.

title: `SimpleCheckIn` moved out of `mark_failed.py`; old import path no longer exists
body: `SimpleCheckIn` was defined in `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` and is now defined in `sentry.monitors.types`. Code that does `from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed import SimpleCheckIn` will break. The PR does not show a search for such imports or a re-export.

title: No tests are added or updated for the moved and renamed logic
body: The PR moves about 250 lines of incident and occurrence logic into two new modules and renames the entry point, but adds no test changes in the diff. Tests that exercise the threshold and occurrence paths should be confirmed to still pass against the new module paths. Any mocks that patch the old module-level names will need updating.

title: Docstring typo: "humam readible"
body: The docstring of `get_failure_reason` reads "Builds a humam readible string". This is copied verbatim into the new module, so the typo is now in a fresh file. It should be "human readable".

title: Renamed and moved helpers may break existing imports and mock targets
body: The PR removes `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, `SimpleCheckIn` and the status maps from `mark_failed.py`, and renames two of them (`mark_failed_threshold` to `try_incident_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence` to `create_incident_occurrence`). Any other module or test that imports these names from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`, or patches them with a string target such as `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence`, will now fail with ImportError or silently stop being patched. The diff touches only four files and includes no test updates or compatibility re-exports, so the repository state after this change is unverified for those references.

title: Docstring typo in get_failure_reason
body: The docstring reads "Builds a humam readible string". The text was carried over from the old module, and the PR is a move that already touches this code, so it is a cheap fix to make while the code is being relocated.

title: Schedule-type display computed into a copy that is never returned
body: `get_monitor_environment_context` copies the config into `config` and rewrites `config["schedule_type"]` to the display string, but the return dict uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original). The rewritten copy is discarded, so the schedule_type display conversion has no effect on the occurrence context. This was carried over verbatim from mark_failed.py, but the move is a chance to fix it or drop the dead code.

title: Renamed/moved symbols may break existing imports and test mocks
body: `mark_failed_threshold` was renamed to `try_incident_threshold` and moved to `incidents.py`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence` was renamed to `create_incident_occurrence` and moved, and `SimpleCheckIn` was removed from this module. Any code or tests that import these names from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` or patch `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence` will now fail with ImportError, or the patch will silently stop applying. The PR touches no test files, so the existing test suite is not updated to match the new locations.

title: Typo in docstring
body: The docstring reads "Builds a humam readible string"; it should be "human readable". Minor, but it's a newly added file.

title: isinstance check never matches spawned processes, so hung or dead flushers are not killed
body: The processes are created from `self.mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, so `mp_context.Process` returns a `SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process` (`context.Process`), so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is False for every real process. The kill in `_ensure_processes_alive` is therefore skipped. The old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. Now a hung flusher keeps running, and `_create_process_for_shards` starts a second flusher on the same shards. Two flushers can then flush and produce the same segments concurrently. The same check at line 346 in `join()` means spawned processes are never terminated there either. The check should be against `BaseProcess`, or the kill should be done for any process object that has `kill`/`terminate`.

title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep
body: The test does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at the top, and the module imports `time` and calls `time.sleep`. The added `time.sleep(0.1)` ("Give flusher threads time to process after drift change") therefore returns immediately and does not wait. The test relies on `step.join()` to flush, so the intended delay never happens and the comment is misleading. The wait should use a real sleep or an explicit synchronization point.

title: Flag help and default contradict the PR's 'one process per shard' design
body: The PR description and the flusher docstring say the flusher spawns one process per Redis shard. But `--flusher-processes` defaults to 1, and the help text says it 'Defaults to 1'. With the default, all shards of a consumer share one flusher process, which is not the behaviour the PR describes. Either the default or the documentation is wrong.

title: New parameter inserted before produce_to_pipe changes positional argument order
body: `flusher_processes` is inserted between `output_block_size` and `produce_to_pipe` in `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__`. Any caller that passes `produce_to_pipe` positionally will now pass it as `flusher_processes`, and the flusher will receive a callable as its process count. Adding the new parameter at the end, or making the arguments keyword-only, avoids this.

title: Inconsistent metric tag key: 'shards' here but 'shard' elsewhere
body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `"shards"`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `segment_size_bytes` and `flusher_unhealthy` use `"shard"`. Dashboards and alerts filtering on `shard` will miss this timer, so the key should be consistent.

title: Unrelated documentation change included in the PR
body: The CLAUDE.md change adds a 'hasattr() for unions' anti-pattern example. This has nothing to do with the multiprocessed span flusher. It should be split into its own PR or dropped so the change set stays focused.

title: Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep
body: The test calls `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at the top, so the `time.sleep(0.1)` added here is also a no-op. The comment says it gives flusher threads time to process after the drift change, but it gives them no time. `step.join()` then races the flusher thread, so `messages` may be empty and `(msg,) = messages` fails intermittently. The added `step.poll()` does not fix this. Use a real wait (e.g. poll until messages appear with a deadline) or restore the real sleep for this wait.

title: --flusher-processes defaults to 1, contradicting the one-process-per-shard design
body: The PR says the flusher should spawn a process per redis shard, and SpanFlusher treats a None `max_processes` as one process per assigned shard. But the CLI option defaults to 1, so production consumers that don't pass the flag get a single flusher process for all shards. The help text ('Defaults to 1') also describes behavior that differs from the factory/flusher default. Either default to None (per-shard) or update the PR's intent and the help text to match.

title: New parameter inserted before produce_to_pipe changes positional argument meaning
body: `flusher_processes` was inserted between `output_block_size` and `produce_to_pipe`. Any caller passing `produce_to_pipe` positionally now binds it to `flusher_processes`, which silently changes behavior (an int/callable mismatch that may not fail immediately). Add the new parameter after `produce_to_pipe` or make the rest keyword-only.

title: Restart of a hung thread-based flusher starts a second flusher on the same shards
body: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the old process is only killed when it is a `multiprocessing.Process`. For threads (the `produce_to_pipe` path), the old thread is left running and `_create_process_for_shards` starts a new thread on the same shards. Two flushers can then concurrently flush the same shard buffer. The previous code would have failed loudly here; now it silently duplicates work. Either refuse to restart threads or make the old one stop before starting the new one.

title: Unused _create_process_for_shard method
body: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is never called; restarts go through `_ensure_processes_alive`, which calls `_create_process_for_shards` directly. It is dead code that also duplicates the shard-to-process lookup, so it should be removed or used.

title: Inconsistent metric tag key: 'shard' vs 'shards'
body: The `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` metrics use the tag key `shard`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `shards` for the same value. Dashboards and alerts filtering on one key will miss the other timer, so the tag should be consistent.

title: test_flusher_processes_limit does not verify any flushing output
body: The test is named for the process limit but only checks counts and shard distribution, then calls `join()`. It never submits spans or checks that flushed segments reach the produce pipe for every shard. A regression that drops a shard's segments would still pass.

title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep
body: test_basic patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at the top of the test, and the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` is called through the same `time` module. The intended wait for the flusher threads to process the drift change therefore never happens. The test then calls `step.join()` right after the second poll, so it can pass or fail depending on thread timing. The wait needs to be done in a way the patch does not affect (e.g. a real wait captured before patching, or polling until the expected message appears with a deadline).

title: join() breaks out of the loop on deadline without terminating the remaining flusher processes
body: In the new join(), when the deadline is reached the loop does `break`, which skips the `process.terminate()` call for every remaining process. Previously a single process was always terminated after the wait. Now any flusher processes not yet joined are left running past join(), still holding Redis and Kafka producer connections, and they keep flushing after the consumer thinks it has shut down. The termination should happen for every process regardless of whether the deadline has passed (or the loop should `continue` instead of `break`).

title: New flusher_processes parameter inserted before produce_to_pipe changes positional argument meaning
body: `flusher_processes` was inserted in the middle of the `__init__` signature, ahead of `produce_to_pipe`. Any existing caller that passes `produce_to_pipe` positionally will now have it bound to `flusher_processes`, which is silently wrong rather than a TypeError. Adding the new parameter at the end, or making it keyword-only, would avoid this.

title: Class docstring says one process per shard, which the implementation does not guarantee
body: The docstring says the flusher 'Creates one process per shard', but `max_processes` caps the number of processes and the consumer CLI defaults `--flusher-processes` to 1, so with default settings all shards share a single process. The docstring should describe the cap and the shard-to-process mapping instead.

title: Inconsistent metric tag key: 'shards' here vs 'shard' everywhere else
body: The wait_produce timer uses the tag key `shards`, while the produce timer, segment_size_bytes timing and the unhealthy counter all use `shard`. Dashboards and alerts filtering on `shard` will miss this metric, and the two naming conventions make queries error-prone.

title: Unrelated hasattr/isinstance guideline added to the flusher PR
body: This documentation change adds a hasattr-vs-isinstance anti-pattern example that has nothing to do with the multiprocessed span flusher. The example also does not explain why hasattr is wrong for union types, so it is unclear as guidance. It should be split into its own change or removed from this PR.

title: Strategy close() permanently shuts down the shared queue pool
body: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` (and `join()`, which calls it) calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`. In `ResultsStrategyFactory.create_thread_queue_parallel_worker`, the same `self.queue_pool` is passed to every strategy the factory creates. StreamProcessor creates a new strategy on each partition assignment and closes the old one on rebalance. The first close therefore shuts down all queues and workers for the factory. Every later `create_with_partitions` returns a strategy whose `submit` puts into a shut-down queue, so messages fail or are never processed. Pool lifetime should be owned by the factory, not by an individual strategy.

title: Kafka commit function is invoked from a background thread
body: `_commit_loop` runs on its own daemon thread and calls `self.commit_function(committable)`, which invokes arroyo's `commit` callback. Arroyo's consumer is not thread-safe and expects commits to happen on the StreamProcessor thread that also polls. Calling commit from this thread can race with poll/assign/close on the same KafkaConsumer, and can produce undefined behaviour or errors during rebalances. Commits should be requested from the main processing thread, for example in `poll()` or `submit()`.

title: A missing offset permanently stalls commits for the partition
body: In `get_committable_offsets`, the loop breaks at the first offset in the range that is absent from `all_offsets`. Kafka offsets are not contiguous in general: log compaction, transaction control markers and deleted records all create gaps. If a gap sits at `last_committed + 1`, nothing past it is ever committed again, so the committed offset stops advancing and consumer lag grows without bound. After a restart, every message after the gap is reprocessed. The gap case should be treated as already complete, for example by skipping offsets that were never added, rather than as a blocker.

title: Queues are unbounded, so the claimed backpressure does not exist
body: Each per-queue `queue.Queue()` is created without a `maxsize`. Offsets are committed and the consumer keeps polling regardless of how far processing lags, so a slow downstream grows these queues without limit and memory use grows with it. The `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` docstring (around line 254) says the design provides 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', which is false for unbounded queues. Either bound the queues so `put` blocks, or fix the docstring and document the memory risk.

title: Racy assertion that total_items is nonzero right after submission
body: `test_stats_reporting` submits 10 items and then immediately asserts `stats["total_items"] > 0`. Worker threads may already have drained the queues by then, especially on a fast machine, so the test can fail intermittently. The assertion should be removed or the processing should be blocked until stats are checked.

title: Error-handling test's assertion contradicts its docstring
body: The docstring says errors in processing must not block offset commits for other messages. The test then asserts `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`, which requires that no commit happens at all. The worker catches the exception and still completes offset 100, and offset 101 completes too, so a commit for the partition is expected. The `or` makes the assertion pass whenever nothing is committed, so the test cannot detect the behaviour it claims to verify. The assertion should expect the committed offset to advance past 101.

title: Offset-gap test codifies the permanent-stall behaviour
body: `test_offset_gaps_block_commits` treats a never-seen offset (101) as a permanent blocker and asserts the commit stays at 100 until that offset arrives. This locks in the stall problem noted for `get_committable_offsets` and gives no coverage for gaps that will never be filled, such as compaction or transaction markers.

title: Graceful-shutdown test asserts almost nothing
body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_graceful_shutdown` sends five results and then only asserts that `factory.queue_pool` is None. It does not wait for or check that the queued items were processed or that workers exited, so it would pass even if shutdown dropped in-flight work. Similarly, `test_thread_queue_parallel_concurrent_subscriptions` is named for concurrency but does not check any concurrent execution.

title: Transaction name hardcodes a 'monitors.' prefix in a generic module
body: The worker transaction is named `monitors.{identifier}.worker_{id}`. This module is shared remote-subscription infrastructure, not monitors code, so the 'monitors.' prefix will misattribute uptime or other consumers' traces in Sentry performance data.

title: Closing one strategy shuts down the factory's shared queue pool, so later assignments silently drop messages
body: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` (and `terminate()`/`join()`) call `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`. The pool is owned by the factory (`ResultsStrategyFactory.queue_pool`) and is reused by every strategy that `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` builds. When StreamProcessor closes a strategy on a rebalance and then calls `create_with_partitions` again, the new strategy gets a pool whose workers have been told to stop and whose queues are shut down. In `submit()` the `put()` on a shut-down queue raises, the broad `except Exception` marks the offset complete via `offset_tracker.add_offset`/`complete_offset`, and the offset is then committed. The message is never processed and never redelivered. The pool should be owned and shut down only by the factory, not by a strategy that merely borrows it.

title: Offsets are committed from the background commit thread, outside the consumer's processing thread
body: `_commit_loop` runs on its own thread and calls `self.commit_function(committable)`, which invokes the arroyo `Commit` callable obtained in `create_with_partitions`. Arroyo's consumer and its `Commit` are designed to be driven from the StreamProcessor thread, which also calls `poll()`/`consumer.commit`. Calling commit concurrently from a second thread is not safe for the underlying consumer and can race with rebalance handling and poll. The commit should be marshalled back to the processing thread (for example in `poll()`), or the thread-safety of the consumer path should be explicitly established.

title: Queues are unbounded, so the claimed backpressure never happens
body: `FixedQueuePool.__init__` creates `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize`, and `submit()` uses a plain `put()`. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy`'s docstring promises 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', but nothing ever fills up. If workers are slower than Kafka delivers, the in-memory backlog grows without bound and the consumer never pauses. `poll()` only emits a gauge.

title: Worker shutdown relies on queue.Queue.shutdown(), which only exists on Python 3.13+
body: `queue.ShutDown` and `Queue.shutdown()` were added in Python 3.13. On older interpreters `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` raises AttributeError, which is caught and only logged in `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()`. Workers stay blocked in `work_queue.get()` forever. `shutdown()` then waits up to 5 seconds per worker (`worker.join(timeout=5.0)`) for up to 20 workers, blocking close for about 100 seconds. The version requirement should be verified, or a sentinel-based shutdown used instead.

title: Processing failures are logged and then committed, so the message is silently lost
body: In `OrderedQueueWorker.run`, any exception from `result_processor` is logged and the `finally` block marks the offset complete. The commit loop then advances past it, so the failed item is never retried and never reprocessed. The class and module docstrings state 'No item is lost' and 'Only commits offsets after successful processing', which is not what the code does. This should either be documented as at-most-once for failures or the failure should block or retry the commit.

title: Error-handling test asserts the opposite of its stated behavior and is timing-dependent
