body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` is named to check that errors 'don't block offset commits for other messages', but its final assertion `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets` requires that the partition is NOT committed. Per the worker's `finally`, the failed offset is marked complete, so the correct behavior is a commit to 102. The assertion passes only because the commit thread runs on a 1-second cadence and the test may finish before any commit happens. The test should wait for the commit explicitly and assert the committed offset.

title: Queue pool is shared across assignments and is shut down when any strategy closes, so a rebalance drops results
body: `create_with_partitions` builds a new `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` around the same `self.queue_pool` every time Arroyo assigns partitions. Arroyo closes the previous strategy on revoke, and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` / `terminate()` call `queue_pool.shutdown()` (queue_consumer.py lines 335-342). That shuts down the shared queues and worker threads for the new strategy too. Later `submit()` calls hit `queue.ShutDown` on `put`, which the `except` in `submit` swallows after marking the offset complete. The offset is then committed without the result ever being processed, so results are silently lost after any rebalance. The pool should be created per strategy, or shutdown should only happen at factory shutdown.

title: A missing offset in the sequence blocks commits permanently
body: In `get_committable_offsets`, the loop breaks as soon as `offset not in all_offsets`. Kafka offsets are not guaranteed to be contiguous (transaction/control markers, compaction, seeks). Any gap that is never submitted means `highest_committable` never advances past it, so the partition's committed offset stops moving for the life of the process and lag grows without bound. On restart, everything after the gap is reprocessed. The gap should be treated as complete, or the scan should be bounded to offsets actually seen (for example, iterate over the sorted `all_offsets` set instead of every integer in the range).

title: Docstring claims backpressure, but the queues are unbounded
body: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` documents 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', but `FixedQueuePool` creates `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize`, so `put` never blocks. If workers fall behind, the in-memory backlog grows without limit, and the Kafka consumer keeps polling and buffering messages. Either bound the queues (blocking submit) or fix the docstring and add a memory safeguard.

title: Arroyo commit callback is invoked from a background thread
body: `_commit_loop` runs in its own daemon thread and calls `commit_function`, which forwards to the Arroyo `commit` callback that the StreamProcessor provides. That callback was built for the processor thread. Calling it concurrently with the main poll/processing loop can race on consumer state, and the callback can run after the processor has begun shutting down. Commits should be marshalled back to the processor thread (for example in `poll()`), or the thread-safety of the callback should be confirmed and documented.

title: Flaky assertion: total_items > 0 right after submit
body: `test_stats_reporting` submits 10 items with a 4-group key, then immediately asserts `stats["total_items"] > 0`. The worker threads start consuming as soon as items are put, so they can drain all items before `get_stats()` runs, making this assertion fail intermittently. The test should not depend on timing for this check.

title: Error-handling test asserts the opposite of the behavior it describes
body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` is documented as 'errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages', and the mock makes the first call raise. The worker's `finally` marks offset 100 complete, so offset 101 is committable and the commit thread should commit it. The final assertion `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets` requires that no commit happened, which contradicts the test's own intent. It will fail when commits happen, and when they don't it passes for the wrong reason. The assertion should expect commit 102 (next offset after 101) for the partition.

title: Transaction name uses the 'monitors.' prefix copied from another consumer
body: The worker starts transactions named `monitors.{identifier}.worker_{id}`, and `ResultProcessor` uses the same `monitors.` prefix. This is an uptime/remote-subscriptions consumer, so these traces will be grouped under the monitors namespace and be hard to find or filter. The name should use a remote-subscriptions or uptime prefix.

title: Backup code consumed non-atomically, allowing reuse via concurrent logins
body: The backup code is verified by reading the encrypted list, then writing back the list with the used entry nulled in a separate update. Two concurrent login requests with the same valid code can both read the unmodified list, both pass the indexOf check, and both succeed. A single-use code can therefore be replayed. The check and consumption need to be atomic (e.g., conditional update or transaction with compare-and-swap on the stored value).

title: Used backup code is set to null but the code list is never pruned, and indexOf on null entries is fragile
body: Consumed entries are replaced with null in the array. Subsequent submissions of an empty or null-like input can match nulls in indexOf only if the input is null, and the request body backupCode is only checked for truthiness, so this is mostly safe; however the stored array keeps nulls forever and the JSON shape changes from string[] to (string|null)[], which the disable endpoint and any future reader must handle. Consider removing the entry instead.

title: Backup code verified without requiring 2FA enabled path to be sane; wrong input type can crash
body: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll is called on whatever the client sends. If backupCode is a non-string truthy value (number, object), replaceAll throws a TypeError causing a 500 instead of a 400. Also JSON.parse of decrypted data is unguarded.

title: Backup code used to disable 2FA is never consumed
body: The comment says the codes are deleted at the end, and the update sets backupCodes to null, so this does clear them on success. However the disable path with a backup code does not check that the code is still unused before the update, so concurrent requests can each disable 2FA with the same code; combined with the non-atomic pattern this is replay-prone. Same race as login.

title: Setup overwrites backup codes and stores them before 2FA is enabled, and returns them without a confirmation gate
body: Backup codes are written to the DB during setup while twoFactorEnabled stays false. Each setup call regenerates and replaces codes, which is intended, but the codes are shown to the user before they are verified and a backup code login path in login/next-auth checks only twoFactorEnabled, so this is acceptable only if the enable step is required. Additionally, symmetricEncrypt is called with process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY which is checked earlier, so ok; the real concern is that the plaintext codes are returned in the setup JSON response and cached by any intermediary.

title: Backup code blob URL is created on every setup and the previous one revoked by a stale closure
body: backupCodesUrl is read from component state inside handleSetup, so if state is stale the previous object URL may not be revoked, leaking blob URLs. The revoke condition relies on the previous render's value rather than a ref.

title: formatBackupCode is used before its declaration in handleSetup's closure order and the backup codes state is untyped
body: useState([]) gives an implicitly any[] state type, and formatBackupCode is a const declared after handleSetup; it works at call time but the untyped state hides shape errors. backupCodes should be typed as string[].

title: Closing the dialog after a backup code display does not reset the flow when the modal is dismissed via overlay
body: The Close button resets state, but dismissing the Dialog via onOpenChange (escape or overlay) skips resetState, so the backup codes step and the codes remain in state and the user can reopen into the DisplayBackupCodes step with stale codes.

title: Backup code login errors are mapped but the backup code field is never cleared, and password is still required
body: On an IncorrectBackupCode error, the form stays on the backup step with the old value; the errorMessages fallback and new branches are inconsistent with the errorMessages map used elsewhere. Also the 'Lost access' button clears only totpCode, not the password-related state, so the form submits with stale values.

title: resetForm called after success clears password field values but leaves the modal state stale on error paths
body: On failure paths the entered backup code or TOTP code is not cleared, so after an incorrect code the user must manually clear inputs; combined with the shared form, toggling Lost access does not clear errorMessage consistently.

title: Backup code login path bypasses the password check requirement ordering and TOTP fallback
body: When a backup code is supplied and the user has 2FA enabled, the TOTP branch is skipped entirely, but the earlier password check only runs when no totpCode is present. A request with totpCode and backupCode both present but no password skips password verification for CAL users whose password is set, since the password check is gated on !credentials.totpCode. The backup code path then succeeds without any password, which is an authentication bypass for users who know only a backup code and an email.

title: Migration adds column without considering existing 2FA users
body: Existing users who already have 2FA enabled get backupCodes null, so the backup code path returns MissingBackupCodes and they have no recovery path other than TOTP. This should be documented or the UI should prompt regeneration.

title: Backup code instruction text is inaccurate for the setup screen
body: backup_code_instructions says codes can be used to grant access without the authenticator, but it is also used as the description of the setup backup codes step, where the user is not told to save them now or that they are shown only once.

title: No test covers backup code login or the incorrect backup code path
body: The PR's stated test plan is to log in with backup codes, but no e2e test exercises that flow; the only new tests cover the setup download/copy and close buttons. The checklist also states no tests prove the feature works.

title: Backup code consumption is not atomic, allowing replay
body: The code checks the backup code index, then later writes back the re-encrypted array with the used code nulled, in a separate non-transactional update. Two concurrent login requests with the same valid backup code can both pass the indexOf check before either write lands, so one backup code can be used twice. The code is single-use by design, so this breaks the security guarantee.

title: Used backup code is set to null, but indexOf of a null entry and remaining codes are not validated
body: Setting backupCodes[index] = null keeps the array length, and the stored JSON contains nulls. Submitting an empty or whitespace string after replaceAll can match a null entry only if the input is null, which is not possible from a string, so this is mostly safe, but a user submitting an input that is the empty string bypasses the check because credentials.backupCode is falsy and falls back to TOTP. More concretely, the truthiness check on backupCode means an attacker-supplied backupCode of an empty string skips backup verification entirely; the backup-code path is only reached when the field is non-empty.

title: Backup code verification is not consumed and the disable path accepts an unvalidated body value
body: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll is called on a value that may not be a string (JSON body can send a number or object), which throws a 500 instead of a clean error. Also the used backup code is never consumed here, but the subsequent update wipes all backup codes anyway, so this is acceptable only if disabling is the sole consumer; the reliance on the later update is implicit and fragile.

title: JSON.parse of decrypted backup codes can throw unhandled
body: If the stored backupCodes is corrupted or the decryption key changed, symmetricDecrypt or JSON.parse throws, producing an unhandled exception and a 500 with no ErrorCode. The same unguarded parse exists in next-auth-options.ts authorize, where it aborts login with an unmapped error.

title: Setup overwrites existing backup codes before enable, invalidating the previous set on abandoned setup
body: Backup codes are written to the DB at setup time while twoFactorEnabled is still false. If the user abandons enrollment, the previously stored codes are replaced anyway, and the codes shown to the user are only persisted, not confirmed. Also, codes are generated even if the user never completes the TOTP step, so the displayed codes can be out of sync with what is stored if setup is called twice (the second call overwrites the first set the user may have already saved).

title: backupCodes state typed as untyped empty array
body: useState([]) infers never[] under strict typing and the later assignment from body.backupCodes is untyped (any), weakening type safety for the displayed and downloaded codes.

title: Blob URL created on every setup call but revoked only against stale state
body: backupCodesUrl is read from closure state inside handleSetup, so if the user retries setup in the same render cycle the revoke may target a stale URL and leak or revoke the wrong object URL. The download link may then point to a revoked URL.

title: Backup code errors are shown via next-auth result but the error message path for SecondFactorRequired still relies on ErrorCode mapping that drops IncorrectBackupCode in errorMessages
body: The new branches set error text directly, but the Lost access flow never resets twoFactorRequired on credential errors, and when a backup code is wrong the TwoFactor totp input is not shown, so the user cannot see the field they must fix. The error message localization keys are also added only to en/common.json, so other locales fall back to raw keys.

title: No test covers backup code login, the core feature of this PR
body: The only tests exercise TOTP enable and disable plus backup download UI. Nothing verifies that a backup code logs in, that a used code is rejected on reuse, or that a wrong code shows the new error. The TODO acknowledges this, yet the PR checklist claims no tests were added.

title: Backup codes stored as encrypted blob in plain TEXT column without versioning
body: The codes are JSON encrypted with the global CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Rotating the key makes all stored backup codes unreadable, and the authorize and disable paths throw an internal error rather than prompting regeneration. No migration path or key rotation handling is provided.

title: Unrelated tabIndex change on password visibility toggle
body: Adding tabIndex={-1} to the show/hide password button in the shared PasswordField removes it from keyboard tab order across the whole app, an accessibility regression unrelated to backup codes and not described in the PR.

title: Backup code path skips the TOTP check and does not consume the used backup code
body: When a backupCode is supplied, the handler validates it against the stored list but never removes the matched code. The code comment says 'we delete all stored backup codes at the end', but the final prisma.user.update only sets backupCodes to null when the 2FA disable succeeds. The disable path therefore accepts a backup code and still succeeds, which is intended, but the matching code is not invalidated if the update fails. More importantly, the backup-code branch runs whenever req.body.backupCode is truthy, so a request that also includes a valid-looking backupCode bypasses the TOTP requirement entirely; this is the intended lost-access flow, but nothing ties it to the login flow's rate limiting, so brute force against the 10 short hex codes is unthrottled on this endpoint.

title: Used backup code is stored as null inside the JSON array and never removed, leaving null entries and a race window
body: After a successful backup-code login, `backupCodes[index] = null` is written back as JSON. Subsequent lookups call indexOf on the array, so the used slot is null and cannot match, which is correct, but the array is never compacted and the update is a read-modify-write with no guard. Two concurrent logins with the same valid backup code can both pass the indexOf check before either writes, so one code can be used twice. The update should be conditional (compare-and-set on the stored ciphertext) or done in a transaction.

title: Backup codes have only 40 bits of entropy and are stored in a rate-unlimited path
body: Each backup code is 5 random bytes (10 hex chars, about 40 bits). Combined with the login path, which only applies the general checkRateLimitAndThrowError per email, this makes online guessing of a single code feasible for a motivated attacker over time, and it weakens the 2FA guarantee. Longer codes or a stronger rate limit on backup-code attempts would be expected.

title: Setup overwrites backup codes and secret before 2FA is enabled, and never clears them on failed enable
body: Setup writes new backupCodes and a new twoFactorSecret while twoFactorEnabled stays false. The backup codes are shown to the user only after the TOTP enable step, but the codes stored are the ones returned by this call. If the user abandons setup, the previous state is replaced anyway; this is acceptable, but the backup codes are also accepted at login only when twoFactorEnabled is true, so the display-before-enable ordering means users see codes that are not yet active. Verify the enable endpoint persists the same codes it displayed, since nothing in the diff shows the enable handler changed.

title: backupCodes state typed as never[] and the download URL is never revoked on close
body: useState([]) infers an untyped empty array, so backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode) and the render path rely on loose typing. Also the blob URL created in handleSetup is only revoked when a new setup starts; resetState and the close button do not revoke it, so the backup codes text remains in memory until the next setup.

title: onEnable is only called on close, so the parent refreshes state only after the user dismisses backup codes
body: Previously onEnable() fired right after the TOTP code was accepted. Now it fires only when the user clicks close on the backup codes screen. Closing the dialog via onOpenChange or the Dialog's X button skips onEnable and resetState, so the parent never learns 2FA was enabled and the modal's step is left on DisplayBackupCodes when reopened.

title: Lost-access toggle is only reset on success, so switching modes keeps stale backup code input and errors
body: The lost-access button calls resetForm(false) which clears backupCode and totpCode but the form is also used with a shared totpCode field. Toggling mode also does not reset the TwoFactor/BackupCode field registration, and on success the code only resets form values, not the mode, relying on setTwoFactorLostAccess(false) which is fine, but a failed attempt in backup mode leaves errorMessage from the previous mode visible until the next submit.

title: Backup-code error codes are mapped in onSubmit but IncorrectBackupCode is not in errorMessages, and the login form reuses totpCode for the 2FA step
body: Errors thrown from authorize surface as res.error values. The branch-based mapping works, but the login form still submits the TOTP input value as totpCode when in backup mode, and the backupCode field is only populated when the user is in lost-access mode. If the user switches back from lost access, methods.setValue('backupCode', '') is called but the stale totpCode is not cleared in that path, so a previously typed TOTP can be sent with a backup code, causing authorize to take the backup branch and ignore the code the user intended.

title: JSON.parse and decrypt on user.backupCodes can throw an unhandled error for corrupt data
body: symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse run without try/catch. Malformed or legacy ciphertext produces an unhandled exception that returns a 500 with no error code instead of MissingBackupCodes or IncorrectBackupCode, and the same unguarded parse exists in next-auth-options.ts authorize.

title: Backup code login and backup code flows are not tested end to end
body: The only new test covers download, copy and close on the setup screen. Nothing exercises logging in with a backup code via Lost access, a used code being rejected, or disabling 2FA with a backup code. The PR description says the change was tested manually, but the TODO left in the file confirms the login path is untested.

title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty
body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is undefined, null, or an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined and this throws a TypeError whenever location equals MeetLocationType, breaking booking creation for users without a destination calendar.

title: updateEvent/deleteEvent look up destination by the external id they are matching against
body: In updateEvent and deleteEvent the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares against externalCalendarId, which is null/empty in the fallback branch, so it never matches a meaningful calendar. The calendarId silently becomes undefined and the Google call goes to a wrong/default calendar instead of the booking's calendar.

title: Reschedule/update flows lose the destination-calendar-to-credential mapping
body: createAllCalendarEvents now iterates every destination calendar and, for those with a credentialId, passes destination.externalId into createEvent. Meanwhile CalendarManager.createEvent sets externalId and credentialId on results, but in the non-credentialId branch the calendar is created without externalId, so the booking reference gets no externalCalendarId. Later updates/deletes then fall back to default calendars, which can orphan or duplicate events.

title: Collective event pushes host calendars into the array that is later persisted to DB
body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` mutates the array built from the organizer calendar. When the organizer has no destination calendar, the array is null so the push is skipped, and the non-collective fallback is inconsistent. The final `destinationCalendar: { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } }` now depends on array order, so the organizer's calendar is only preserved if it is first; other changes can silently attach the wrong calendar to the booking.

title: teamDestinationCalendars is populated inside an async map and only used later
body: The push into teamDestinationCalendars happens inside the async callback of users.slice(1).map, and the callback runs during map invocation, so ordering is nondeterministic relative to `await Promise.all`. More importantly, the destination calendar of each team member is pushed without checking for duplicates, so the same calendar can be added multiple times when a user is both listed in hosts and attendees.

title: Team member attendee object gains firstName/lastName fields and email default changes
body: The teamMemberPromises mapping adds `firstName: ""` and `lastName: ""` and changes `email` from `user.email || ""` to `user.email ?? ""`, altering the team member data passed to emails and calendar events. Empty strings are not equivalent to the previous `||` fallback for null-like values, and these unrelated changes are not described in the PR.

title: loadUsers swallows dynamic-user errors and changes fallback semantics
body: loadUsers now throws when dynamicUserList is empty and converts all other errors to HttpError 500 'Unable to load users'. Previously an empty dynamic list just produced no users. Also `return users.length ? users : eventType.users` changes behavior when hosts are empty. These behavior changes are unrelated to the collective destination calendar fix and can break dynamic group bookings.

title: Unrelated user-visible string change
body: The additionalNotes text was changed from 'organiser' to 'organizer' in createEvent. This is an unrelated text change that alters emitted notes content for existing users and is not part of the stated fix.

title: Calendar.createEvent signature now requires credentialId for all implementations
body: Making credentialId a required parameter on the Calendar interface breaks all calendar implementations and callers not updated here (e.g. third-party or other apps calling createEvent with one argument). Type checking will pass only if every implementation was updated; the change should be justified or made optional.

title: Lark createEvent ignores the credential and uses first destination calendar
body: Lark's createEvent takes the first destination calendar regardless of which credential is creating the event, so with multiple destination calendars across credentials, each Lark call uses the same calendar id and events are not created on the calendar each host expects.

title: Dereferences possibly undefined first destination calendar
body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining. `evt.destinationCalendar` may be null/empty (the destructure yields undefined), so `create()` throws a TypeError for any event with a Google Meet location and no destination calendar, breaking booking creation that previously worked.

title: credentialId for calendar references no longer falls back to the destination calendar
body: The reference's credentialId was previously taken from evt.destinationCalendar.credentialId. Now it is `result.credentialId` only for calendar results, and `externalCalendarId` is `result.externalId`, which is set only by createEvent. Calendar results from the 'other_calendar' path or failed/undefined results can leave references without credentialId/externalCalendarId, so later updates/deletes fall back to the type-based loop and may update every calendar of that type instead of the selected one.

title: Destination calendar entries without credentialId and integration cause unscoped creation
body: In the non-credentialId branch, the filter `c.type === destination.integration` runs when integration is missing or null, matching nothing, but when multiple collective hosts share the same integration type each host's destination calendar triggers createEvent on all credentials of that type. Duplicate events can be created on the same account for collective bookings.

title: Team destination calendars pushed into evt.destinationCalendar for collective events without dedupe
body: `teamDestinationCalendars` is filled from `users.slice(1)` and then appended to `evt.destinationCalendar`. If the organizer's own calendar is already in the array or the same calendar appears twice, the event is created multiple times on the same calendar. Also `evt.destinationCalendar?.push` is a no-op when destinationCalendar is null, silently dropping the team calendars.

title: Booking destinationCalendar connects only the first entry
body: The booking is linked to `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` only, while the collective flow now creates events on several destination calendars. The additional calendars are not recorded on the booking, so they cannot be found later for update or cancel.

title: loadUsers swallows and remaps errors, and changes the hosts-empty fallback
body: The rewritten loadUsers throws a generic HttpError 500 for any unexpected error, hiding the real cause. The dynamic-user branch now throws if the list is empty, where it previously returned an empty list. The hosts branch returns `users.length ? users : eventType.users`, which changes which users are loaded when hosts exist but are empty. These are behavior changes unrelated to the PR's stated purpose.

title: Team member objects gain firstName/lastName and lose nothing, but email fallback changed
body: The teamMemberPromises mapping adds empty firstName/lastName fields and changes `user.email || ""` to `?? ""`, and the comment now says the organizer is not a team member even for non-team events where users.slice(1) may be used. Unrequested changes that risk payload shape differences in emails and webhooks.

title: Lookup compares externalCalendarId against itself, always yielding undefined
body: In updateEvent, the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the comparison is against null/empty and never matches. The selected calendar becomes undefined and the Google update is sent to calendarId undefined. The same bug is in deleteEvent at line 317.

title: Patch call uses selectedCalendar which may be undefined
body: In createEvent, the follow-up patch uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without the `|| "primary"` fallback used in insert, so the patch can target an undefined calendar when no destination matches the credential.

title: createEvent signature drift and new externalId parameter not consumed by calendars
body: createEvent now accepts externalId and passes credential.id to calendar.createEvent, but the Calendar interface and most implementations (Lark, Office365, CalDAV) do not use the per-credential selection. The destination chosen in EventManager is lost for those integrations, so events go to the primary or first calendar.

title: Primary flag computed from the first destination only
body: listCalendars marks primary only for the first destination calendar's externalId, ignoring other collective host destinations, so the UI may mark the wrong calendar as primary.

title: updateAllCalendarEvents now fetches credentials from DB inside a loop without error handling
body: The new credential fallback performs prisma queries per reference and any failure is caught by the outer catch, which returns error results for every reference. A single missing credential now turns a reschedule into failed results for all calendars.

title: Recurring cancel path reuses outer calendar and ignores per-reference credential
body: Inside the recurring branch the inner `calendar` variable shadows the outer one, and the deletion loop for every credential uses `updBooking.references` without matching credentialId. Deletions may target the wrong calendar account for collective bookings.

title: Removed console.error for failed update message
body: The `console.error(message)` call was removed in the catch block of updateAllCalendarEvents, so failures in updating calendar events are silently swallowed with no log.

title: Expected payload changed without a matching behavior assertion
body: The BOOKING_REJECTED expectation now asserts destinationCalendar is an empty array, but the test does not verify the collective multi-host behavior the PR claims to fix, and no unit or e2e test is added for collective destination calendars.

title: Dereferencing possibly undefined first destination calendar
body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, the destructured value is undefined and this throws a TypeError whenever location is MeetLocationType, breaking event creation for users without any destination calendar.

title: patch uses possibly undefined selectedCalendar
body: In createEvent, `calendarId: selectedCalendar` in the follow-up patch call uses the raw find result (possibly undefined) instead of `selectedCalendar || "primary"` used for insert, so the patch can target an undefined calendar and fail to add the hangout link.

title: Lookup compares externalCalendarId to itself
body: In updateEvent, the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only reached when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find compares against a falsy value and always returns undefined. The calendarId becomes undefined, and the update goes to an invalid calendar. The same bug is repeated in deleteEvent (line 317).

title: Collective team destination calendars are pushed into the organizer event
body: teamDestinationCalendars is populated inside teamMemberPromises, which relies on the side effect of a map callback; and the list is pushed onto evt.destinationCalendar when COLLECTIVE. Duplicates or a null destinationCalendar (evt.destinationCalendar is null when the organizer has none, so `?.push` silently does nothing) cause inconsistent behavior for collective events.

title: Credential lookup duplicated and destination loop may create events for stale calendars
body: createAllCalendarEvents now loops over every destination calendar and creates an event per destination, including fetching credentials from DB, but the non-credentialId branch passes all matching credentials for the integration without filtering by externalId, so multiple destinations of the same integration can create duplicate events on the same calendar.

title: createEvent in calendar services receives credentialId but Calendar interface change breaks existing implementations
body: Calendar.createEvent signature changed to require a credentialId parameter, but many calendar services (e.g. office365, lark, caldav in lib/CalendarService.ts) still take only one argument. The interface contract is inconsistent with implementations and the parameter is silently ignored by most of them.

title: Cancellation deletes calendar events but ignores promise results and errors
body: apiDeletes.push(calendar?.deleteEvent(...)) pushes unawaited promises; when the credential is missing from DB the reference is silently skipped, so cancelled bookings keep their calendar events without any signal.

title: Required credentialId added to Calendar.createEvent breaks implementers and callers
body: Making credentialId a required parameter on the Calendar interface forces every implementation and caller to change; the lib/CalendarService and other apps keep the old single-argument signature, which is a contract break that the type system only partially catches.

title: Webhook secret comparison is not constant-time and fails open when secret is unset
body: The secret is compared with `!==` against `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If that env var is unset/empty and the header is missing, `req.headers[...]` is `undefined` and `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is `undefined`, so the check passes. The feature-flag check at line 19 partly guards this, but the handler itself does not require a configured secret. Also the comparison is timing-unsafe. Require a non-empty secret and use a constant-time comparison.

title: Decryption with empty fallback key and unguarded JSON.parse
body: `symmetricDecrypt` is called with `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""`, and `JSON.parse` wraps the result. A bad key or malformed ciphertext throws an unhandled exception (500 with stack/no structured message) rather than a 400. Also `appointmentMetadata.slug` lookup uses the DB slug while the schema validation via `.parse` on line 31 throws a ZodError as an unhandled 500 for malformed bodies.

title: Credential lookup by appId uses metadata slug but credential is keyed by app slug and type is unchecked
body: The existing credential is looked up only by userId and appId, not by type. An app can have multiple credential types for one user (e.g. the same app slug with different types), so the update may overwrite the wrong credential row, or the create may duplicate one. Matching on `type` as well is needed to be safe.

title: Minimum token schema uses computed keys that do not validate what it claims
body: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` creates a key literally named "ZodString"-like string, not a wildcard. The schema therefore does not enforce an expiry number nor allow arbitrary properties, so the minimal-schema branch validates only `access_token` and silently drops the intended validation. Downstream code (e.g. Google, Zoom) then receives tokens lacking the fields they need (refresh_token is also forced to a placeholder string 'refresh_token' on line 26 when missing, which would overwrite the stored refresh token with a bogus value).

title: Placeholder refresh_token written into stored credentials
body: When the refresh response has no refresh_token, the function sets it to the literal string "refresh_token" and this value is persisted (e.g. Google, Lark, Office365 write the parsed data back). The real refresh token is destroyed, so future refreshes will fail permanently. The fallback should preserve the existing refresh token instead.

title: Refresh token and user data sent to an externally configured endpoint for every refresh
body: When sync is enabled, the function POSTs the user id and app slug to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT and returns that raw fetch Response as if it were a refresh result. The response is not checked for `ok`, and callers then treat it as a token response. A failing sync endpoint returns an error body that is parsed as tokens. The fetch also has no timeout and no auth header, so any caller reaching this path can be spoofed. Check response.ok and handle errors explicitly.

title: Sync path skips the local refresh and returns a Response, changing callers' contract
body: Callers such as Google use `res?.data`, Zoho and Office365 call `handleErrorsJson`/`.data` on the result, and Hubspot assigns `expiryDate` on it. The sync branch returns a fetch `Response` (no `.data`, no parsed JSON), while the normal branch returns an axios/googleapis result with `.data`. Mixed return types cause runtime undefined access in several services (e.g. Google `token.access_token` on a Response).

title: Zoho CRM expiry date is hardcoded to one hour from now
body: In refreshAccessToken the expiryDate is computed as `Date.now() + 60 * 60` (milliseconds, i.e. about one second) and the callback does the same. The token is treated as expired almost immediately, so every call triggers a refresh. The unit mismatch should be `* 1000` on expires_in.

title: Salesforce refresh uses unhandled fetch with no response check and missing prisma import
body: `prisma` is used at line 96 but is not imported in this file, so the module fails to compile or throws at runtime. Also `response.statusText !== "OK"` is an unreliable check (HTTP/2 has empty statusText) and the error is thrown before reading the Salesforce error body. Additionally the new token parse rejects responses lacking fields like `id`/`signature` that Salesforce omits on refresh, so refresh can fail for valid tokens.

title: Removed error logging loses diagnostics for failed token parse
body: The `console.error` branch logging the zod error and the Microsoft response was deleted. Now a failed parse silently falls through with `tokenResponse.success` false and the existing credentials are written back unchanged, so failures are invisible.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string or undefined, not a boolean
body: The expression `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` yields the env string value or undefined. It is used as a boolean in conditions, but the exported type is misleading and an empty-string env value is falsy while a non-empty one leaks the secret value into the constant. Use `!!` to coerce.

title: Redirect URI hardcoded and no longer matches the callback's slug source
body: The add handler now hardcodes `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback` while the callback still builds the URI from `appConfig.slug`. Changing the slug-based value to a literal is unnecessary churn and risks drift if the slug changes; it should remain `appConfig.slug` to stay consistent with the callback that must send an identical redirect_uri for the token exchange.

title: isTokenValid logic inverted in Hubspot, Google-style check uses wrong comparison
body: `(token.expiresIn || token.expiryDate) < Date.now()` treats an expired token as valid in the sense used by getToken and triggers refresh when the token is still valid, or vice versa; the expiry is also measured from expiresIn (a duration, not a timestamp). Expiry should compare expiryDate against Date.now().

title: Callback expiry computed without multiplying by 1000 ms
body: `Math.round(Date.now() + 60 * 60)` adds about one second, not one hour, to the current timestamp, so the stored expiryDate is effectively now and tokens are refreshed on every use.

title: Duplicate and unsorted env entries
body: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME and CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET are inserted out of alphabetical order, and INTERCOM_SECRET was already duplicated before this change. Minor, but the list is used for cache keys and should stay deduplicated and sorted.

title: Header name comment says lowercase but the default and lookup are case-sensitive
body: The comment asks for a lowercase header name, but Next.js lowercases incoming header keys only; the webhook handler indexes req.headers with the env value directly, so a mixed-case configured name would never match. The code should lowercase the configured name or the docs should say so.

title: No tests added for the new webhook or token refresh behaviour
body: The PR adds a new authenticated endpoint that writes credentials, plus changes to refresh logic in about twenty services, with no tests. The PR checklist explicitly says tests were not added. At minimum the webhook auth, decryption failure, and sync-endpoint error paths need coverage.

title: Computed zod keys make the minimum schema match nothing useful
body: The keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are not valid zod key definitions; `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the string "ZodString" (or similar), so the object shape validates a literal property named like that rather than an expiry number or arbitrary extra fields. The intended 'any property with a number is the expiry' check does not exist, so the minimal sync path does not validate expiry_date and may silently accept or reject token responses incorrectly.

title: Fabricated refresh_token placeholder is persisted
body: When refresh_token is missing, the function writes the literal string "refresh_token" into the returned data. Callers then store this in the credential key, replacing a real refresh token with a bogus value so future refreshes fail with an opaque error rather than a clear one.

title: Sync path returns raw fetch Response and skips the token refresh entirely
body: When sync is enabled, the function fetches the endpoint and returns the Response, but callers such as google, hubspot, zoho and zohocrm then read `.data` (axios shape) or call the refresh function's result shape. A fetch Response has no `.data`, so token fields are undefined and the stored credential is corrupted. Also the response is not checked for `ok` status.

title: Sync endpoint is called without authentication
body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only userId and appSlug with no secret or auth header, so anyone who can reach the endpoint configuration path can request tokens for any user id; the shared secret used by the inbound webhook is not reused here.

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality
body: The header value is compared with !== against CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. If the env var is unset and the header is also missing, undefined === undefined passes the check, allowing unauthenticated credential writes. The comparison should also be timing-safe and reject when the secret is empty.

title: Decryption failure and bad JSON cause unhandled 500s and no validation of key shape
body: symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse run outside any try/catch; a wrong encryption key or malformed payload throws and returns a 500 with a stack trace. The decrypted object is also written to the DB without any schema validation for the target app.

title: Credential lookup by appId uses wrong identifier, risking duplicate credentials
body: The lookup and create use appMetadata.slug, but the create sets type: appMetadata.type. Existing credentials created by OAuth callbacks use differing type values (e.g. google_calendar vs app slug), so findFirst may miss the existing record and create duplicates, and the findFirst is not scoped by type.

title: Schema parse throws instead of returning 400
body: appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throws a ZodError on invalid bodies, which Next.js reports as a 500 rather than a client error. safeParse with a 400 response is expected here.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string, not a boolean
body: The expression `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` evaluates to a string or undefined. Its use in conditionals works, but the exported type is wrong and the flag is truthy for any non-empty value, so the .env.example placeholder `""` values are strings that are truthy only when both are non-empty; the type should be coerced to boolean.

title: Salesforce refresh always happens and prisma is not imported
body: getClient now performs a token refresh on every construction, even when the access token is still valid, adding a network call per service instance. Also `prisma` is used at line 96 but is not imported in this file, so it will fail to compile/run.

title: Refresh failure checks statusText instead of response.ok
body: The check `response.statusText !== "OK"` is fragile (HTTP/2 responses have empty statusText) and wrongly treats failures as errors or successes. Use response.ok and surface the error body.

title: Removed error logging for invalid refresh responses
body: The diff deletes the console.error for a failed zod parse of the refresh response, so Microsoft error responses are now silently swallowed and the credential keeps stale tokens with no diagnostic.

title: isTokenValid logic is inverted in existing code and now feeds the refresh path unchanged
body: isTokenValid returns true when expiresIn-or-expiryDate is less than now, i.e. when the token is expired, yet getToken calls refresh only when !isTokenValid. The refresh call is also wrapped in a function that swallows errors, so failures leave a stale token with no signal to callers.

title: Empty doc comment and misnamed handler docs
body: The `/** */` above the handler is empty, providing no documentation for a new public webhook endpoint that changes credential data.

title: Header name comment and placeholder values are misleading
body: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME says it should be lowercase, but the handler reads req.headers with a lookup key, which is case-sensitive only in the sense Node lowercases headers; the comment should state this. CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is also not documented to say it receives unauthenticated user tokens.

title: Hardcoded redirect URI breaks the slug-based pattern and the appConfig reference
body: The redirect URI was changed from `${appConfig.slug}` to a literal 'zoho-bigin'. This is equivalent today but diverges from the callback which still uses appConfig.slug, and it is an unrelated behavioral edit inside a refactor PR.

title: refreshOAuthTokens receives credential.userId but credential is not in scope
body: Inside zohoCrmAuth the argument `credential.userId` refers to the outer parameter, which is fine, but the refreshed token expiry is set to Date.now()+60*60 without using expires_in, so tokens are marked valid for a fixed hour regardless of the real lifetime, and the sync path's Response object has no .data so zohoCrmTokenInfo.data is undefined.

title: Zoom refresh now accepts unvalidated responses in sync mode
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse uses the minimal schema when sync is enabled, so the zoom path no longer enforces scope and token_type, and key.expiry_date is later set from expires_in which may be undefined in the sync path, producing NaN expiry.

title: Expiry computed from expires_in which may be missing on sync responses
body: key.expiry_date is computed as Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000 but the sync path's minimal schema does not require expires_in, so the result can be NaN, which then makes isTokenValid always false and refresh loops.

title: Google refresh reads token fields from a value that may be a Response
body: res?.data is read from refreshOAuthTokens' return, which in sync mode is a fetch Response with no .data, so token.access_token and token.expiry_date become undefined and the credential is overwritten with undefined token fields.

title: Lark sync path response is passed to handleLarkError but the sync endpoint returns form-encoded params
body: The sync request sends URLSearchParams with calcomUserId and appSlug, while the Lark handler expects a Lark-shaped JSON response (code, data.access_token). The sync endpoint contract is not reflected in the code, so handleLarkError will fail on any sync response that lacks a Lark envelope.

title: Duplicate and unordered env entries
body: INTERCOM_SECRET is already listed twice in globalEnv, and the new entries are inserted out of alphabetical order (CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET after CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY), which will be flagged by the sorted-list check and makes the duplicate harder to spot.

title: No tests added for new webhook, sync, or refresh behavior
body: The PR adds a credential-writing webhook, a new encryption path, and changes to every OAuth refresh path, yet no tests were added; the checklist itself states none were written. The refresh-path changes in particular touch many providers and need coverage.

title: Minimum token schema uses computed string keys, not a real schema for expiry
body: The keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are computed property names evaluating to the literal string "ZodString"/"ZodOptional" etc. The schema therefore does not validate any expiry field and the 'any property with a number is the expiry' intent is not implemented. Under sync mode, refreshed tokens are accepted without checking expiry_date/expires_in, and callers that rely on expiry (e.g. Google, Zoom) can store undefined expiry, causing tokens to be treated as expired or never refreshed.

title: Fallback sets refresh_token to the literal string 'refresh_token'
body: When the response has no refresh_token, the function writes the placeholder string "refresh_token" into the parsed data. That value is then persisted to the credential, overwriting the real refresh token with a garbage value, so future refreshes against the provider fail.

title: Sync endpoint fetch has no error handling and no auth header
body: The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends the user id and app slug without any authentication, and the response is returned unchecked. A non-2xx response or HTML error page is returned as if it were a token response; callers like Google (`res?.data`) and Hubspot then treat it as valid tokens. Also the refresh path for user credentials is entirely bypassed when sync is on, so a failure in the sync endpoint silently breaks refresh with no fallback.

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality and undefined-safe
body: The header is compared with `!==` against process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. If the env var is unset, the header is undefined on requests without it and undefined === undefined passes, but the code path is guarded only by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED. Also the comparison is not timing-safe. Use crypto.timingSafeEqual and explicitly reject when the secret is empty.

title: Decryption and JSON.parse errors are unhandled and produce 500s; invalid input is not validated
body: symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse on reqBody.keys are not wrapped in try/catch, and appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throws a ZodError rather than returning a 400. Malformed or wrongly encrypted payloads cause unhandled exceptions. Also an empty CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is passed as '' rather than rejected.

title: App lookup and metadata lookup are redundant and the credential is matched on the wrong field
body: The code looks up the app by slug, then looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug and uses appMetadata.slug for the credential appId. The DB app row is only used for existence. Credential matching by userId+appId via findFirst also does not restrict type, so an existing credential of a different type for the same app would be overwritten with new keys. Creation sets type from metadata but updates never reconcile type.

title: prisma is used but never imported in CalendarService
body: getClient now calls prisma.credential.update, but the file imports no prisma client (the import list has no `prisma`). This is a compile/runtime ReferenceError when a Salesforce credential is used.

title: Salesforce token refresh now always hits the network and ignores the stored token and the sync path
body: getClient unconditionally POSTs to login.salesforce.com on every service construction, with no expiry check, and no sync-endpoint branch via refreshOAuthTokens, unlike other apps. This changes behavior for every Salesforce calendar operation (extra latency and requests per call), and self-hosters using sync will still hit Salesforce directly. The response.statusText !== 'OK' check is also fragile since HTTP/2 responses may have empty statusText, causing false failures.

title: Refreshed Salesforce key drops fields and writes parsed data that excludes instance_url
body: The persisted key is `{...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token}` but salesforceTokenSchema parses only listed fields, and zod strips unknown keys. Salesforce's refresh response includes instance_url, and it is in the schema, so that holds, but other stored fields like the original `expiry` info are lost; additionally the connection now uses credentialKey.instance_url (old) rather than the refreshed one.

title: Removed error logging and tokenResponse.success check changes failure behavior
body: The zod-failure console.error was removed, and parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on invalid responses instead of returning a failed result. The code then still spreads `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data`, which is dead logic since the function either throws or returns a successful result. Errors from Microsoft (e.g. invalid_grant) now surface as an unhelpful error instead of being logged with the MS response.

title: Zoom refresh computes expiry from expires_in which is absent in sync mode
body: After parseRefreshTokenResponse, key.expiry_date is set from newTokens.expires_in * 1000. In sync mode the minimum schema does not require expires_in, so expires_in can be undefined, producing NaN expiry_date and a token that is never considered expired or always considered expired depending on comparison.

title: Webex expiry only updated when expires_in present, leaving stale expiry_date
body: The refreshed token only updates expiry_date if expires_in is present, and the refresh path is now reachable through sync which may omit expires_in. The stored expiry_date then stays in the past, causing a refresh on every call.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string or undefined, not a boolean
body: The expression evaluates to the env string (or undefined), not a boolean. It is used in `if` checks and returned in the webhook gate, which works by truthiness but the exported type is misleading and an empty-string secret is treated as disabled while whitespace is enabled. Should be wrapped in Boolean().

title: Zoho CRM expiry is hardcoded to one hour regardless of response
body: zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.expiryDate is set to Date.now()+60*60 (missing *1000 is fine but expires_in is ignored), which is an existing pattern but now also runs for sync-supplied tokens whose lifetime may differ, so tokens can be treated as valid after expiry.

title: Zoho CRM callback expiryDate adds 3600 ms instead of seconds
body: Math.round(Date.now() + 60 * 60) adds only 3.6 seconds, not one hour, so the stored expiryDate is effectively now and tokens are immediately treated as expired.

title: Redirect URI hardcoded to zoho-bigin, changing the slug-based value
body: The redirect URI was changed from using appConfig.slug to a literal string. This is harmless now but removes the single source of truth and must match callback.ts, which still uses appConfig.slug; any future slug change will break the OAuth redirect mismatch.

title: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME added to globalEnv out of alphabetical order and duplicates exist
body: The new env vars are inserted out of order, and INTERCOM_SECRET was already duplicated in the list. Minor, but the list is clearly maintained sorted and this makes future diffs noisier.

title: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME comment says lowercase but code reads it directly from req.headers
body: Node lowercases incoming header names, so the code works only if the env value is lowercase. The comment states the requirement but the code does not normalize it, so a mixed-case value silently fails with 403 for every request.

title: No tests cover the new sync path or the parse fallback behavior
body: The PR adds a new sync mode affecting ~15 apps, a new webhook endpoint, and parse fallback logic, but the PR checklist states no tests were added. Bugs such as the broken zod schema and the 'refresh_token' placeholder would have been caught by unit tests.

title: Team admin/owner check requires both admin AND owner
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so a user must be both admin and owner to pass. A team admin who is not owner (or an owner who is not admin) is denied, and for non-team bookings teamId is 0 so the check is meaningless. The intent is clearly OR.

title: Calendar attendees updated before the guests are validated/persisted correctly and with no error handling
body: updateCalendarAttendees is awaited without try/catch, so any calendar provider failure makes the mutation throw after the attendees were already written to the DB, leaving the client seeing an error while guests were actually added. Also the handler uses the original booking object (before the new attendees) for eventManager, so calendar sync may not include the new guests.

title: Email sent with raw input guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests
body: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes the full input list, including emails already attendees or blacklisted, and the evt attendees list includes all attendees. Newly added guests are identified by 'newGuests.includes', so previously existing attendees are sent 'scheduled' emails and blacklisted emails are not filtered; should pass uniqueGuests.

title: Email failure silently swallowed with console.log, losing error details
body: The catch block logs a fixed string without the error object, so email failures are invisible in logs. Should use the logger and include err.

title: Guest attendees created with empty name and no check for duplicates within input
body: Guests are created with name "" and duplicate emails in the same request are not deduplicated before createMany, so the same guest may be added twice. Also the check at line 76 compares raw guest to attendee.email without case normalization, so differently-cased duplicates are added.

title: Organizer email subject uses first attendee name, not the new guests
body: The subject in organizer-add-guests-email.ts uses this.calEvent.attendees[0].name, which is the original booker, while the email is about newly added guests; also the attendees array may be empty causing a runtime crash on [0].name.

title: Crash when attendees array is empty
body: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name dereferences index 0 without a guard; a booking with no attendees would throw inside getNodeMailerPayload.

title: Mutation has no check that bookingId belongs to the caller beyond the handler; guests may be added to any booking
body: addGuests uses authedProcedure and the handler checks only membership; the attendee check uses user.email on an existing booking and the team check is broken (see AND bug), so the authorization relies on the flawed logic above.

title: Error toast message formatting is wrong
body: The message is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, which is always truthy, so the fallback t("unable_to_add_guests") is never used, and the raw error code prefix is shown to users.

title: Zod schema recreated on every render
body: ZAddGuestsInputSchema is defined inside the component body and rebuilt each render; it should be hoisted to module scope.

title: Attendee email uses subtitle 'emailed you and any other attendees' that is inaccurate for newly added guests
body: The subtitle text is reused from scheduled emails and the attendee is told they are receiving a calendar invite as in a new booking, but the email payload also sets status CONFIRMED and method REQUEST, which is a fresh invite for an existing event; behavior is questionable for existing attendees.

title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles simultaneously
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...). A user who is only an admin (not owner) or only an owner (not admin) fails the check, so the intended team-admin/owner permission is effectively limited to users who hold both roles. Should be ||.

title: Calendar update uses booking with stale attendees and never includes new guests
body: eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) passes the pre-update booking object, while evt.attendees was built from the updated attendee list. Calendar event references/attendee sync depends on the original booking; the mismatch can cause calendar updates to be inconsistent or fail. Also the error from updateCalendarAttendees is not caught, so a calendar failure after the DB write returns an error even though guests were already added.

title: Guest creation not atomic with duplicate check; duplicate attendees possible
body: The filter for existing attendees uses a snapshot read, then createMany inserts. Concurrent requests or case differences in emails can insert duplicate attendee rows for the same booking. No uniqueness enforcement or case-insensitive comparison is applied.

title: Blacklist check compares unnormalized guest email
body: blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased, but guest emails are compared as-is (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). A guest entered as 'Spam@Example.com' bypasses the blacklist. Attendee duplicate check is also case-sensitive.

title: Email send failures silently swallowed with no logging of error
body: The catch block logs a fixed string and discards the error object, so failures in sending add-guest emails are invisible in diagnostics. Also the handler reports success even when notifications failed.

title: Emails sent to all guests in input, not only newly added ones
body: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) receives the raw input guests, including those filtered out as duplicates or blacklisted, and the attendee mapping then treats them as 'new'. Previously existing attendees could receive 'new guests added' emails, and blacklisted addresses can get notified. Should pass uniqueGuests.

title: Booking lookup not scoped and permission checks leak existence
body: The booking is fetched by id without any restriction before authorization; the not-found error and forbidden error differ, letting any authenticated user enumerate booking ids. Also the attendee-permission path lets any attendee add guests to the booking, which is broader than the UI intent.

title: EventManager constructed with the requesting user instead of the organizer
body: new EventManager({...user, credentials}) uses the session user's credentials and destinationCalendar, but when an admin or attendee performs the action the calendar update should use the booking organizer's credentials. Calendar events may be updated through the wrong account.

title: Attendees who are existing guests receive wrong email template
body: sendAddGuestsEmails sends AttendeeScheduledEmail to attendees whose email is in newGuests, and AttendeeAddGuestsEmail to all others. This is inverted relative to the intent of notifying existing attendees about new guests, and the new guests get a scheduled-booking email with no 'guests added' context.

title: Missing blank line and inconsistent formatting between exported functions
body: New exported function sendAddGuestsEmails is placed directly after the previous closing brace without a blank line, unlike surrounding code; the same occurs before sendFeedbackEmail.

title: Organizer email subject uses first attendee name, not the guest context
body: name is set to this.calEvent.attendees[0].name, which may be an empty string for guests added without names (guests are created with name ''), producing subjects like 'Guests Added: X with  at ...'. Also replyTo exposes all attendee emails.

title: Guest attendees created with empty name
body: Guests are created with name "", and the email subject/greeting relies on attendee names. Emails and the UI will show blank names; this is not validated or documented.

title: Zod schema recreated each render and error message mapping is wrong
body: The schema is redefined inside the component on every render. More importantly, onError shows `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` which passes server message keys through t and prefixes error codes into user-facing text; the fallback `|| t('unable_to_add_guests')` is unreachable because the template string is never empty.

title: Validation error shown is generic and stays set after success
body: isInvalidEmail is only reset when cancel is clicked, not on successful add or on subsequent valid input, so the uniqueness/validity error persists incorrectly.

title: Hardcoded English tooltip text not translated
body: Tooltip content "Remove email" is a literal string instead of t(...), breaking localisation for the rest of the dialog.

title: Translation key 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' message is misleading
body: The message 'Emails must be unique and valid' is used both for client validation and as the server error code key, and the server's BAD_REQUEST when all guests are duplicates or blacklisted reuses it, giving a misleading reason.

title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles simultaneously
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` between `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`, so a user must be both admin and owner to pass. A team admin who is not owner, or an owner who is not admin, is denied. The intent is clearly `||`. Also, when teamId is 0 (no team), both helpers are called with 0 unnecessarily.

title: Email sent with raw input guests instead of actually-added guests
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the original input list, but `uniqueGuests` (after filtering existing attendees and blacklisted emails) is what was actually persisted. Existing attendees who were re-submitted, or blacklisted emails, are treated as 'new guests' and get the scheduled-event email, and the newly added attendees are not correctly classified.

title: Email failure silently swallowed with no error detail
body: The try/catch around `sendAddGuestsEmails` logs a fixed string and drops the error object, so failures are hard to diagnose. The handler still returns success even when notifications failed, which is inconsistent with the rest of the flow.

title: Calendar update runs after DB write with no rollback and uses unfiltered booking
body: Attendees are written to the DB (line 92) before `updateCalendarAttendees` is called. If the calendar update throws, the guests are persisted but the calendar invite is never sent, leaving inconsistent state. The `booking` object passed to updateCalendarAttendees is the pre-update snapshot, so the new attendees may not be reflected there.

title: Guests created with empty name
body: Each new guest is created with `name: ""`, so downstream emails and the attendee list show a blank name and the email template uses `attendee.name` in greetings and calendar invites.

title: Subject line uses first attendee name instead of the guest/organizer
body: In OrganizerAddGuestsEmail the subject uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`, which may be the booker, not a meaningful identifier, and can be an empty string for newly added guests if they are ordered first. This makes subjects inconsistent.

title: Organizer email replyTo includes all attendees and is sent to organizer
body: `replyTo` lists the organizer and every attendee, and the `to` address is only the organizer or team member. Replies from the organizer's client will fan out to all guests, which may be unintended and leaks guest addresses in the reply chain.

title: Templates exported from index but used via different naming
body: The new React templates are exported from the index, but the mail templates import `renderEmail("AttendeeAddGuestsEmail")`/`OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` by name. The naming pattern diverges from neighboring templates and is easy to mismatch when adding or renaming templates.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails never awaits or returns the reminder promise in related path and lacks team-member handling for attendees
body: The new function sends scheduled emails to existing attendees via AttendeeScheduledEmail for new guests, but `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` compares raw input emails case-sensitively against stored attendee emails, so mismatched casing sends the wrong template to the wrong recipient.

title: Keys by index cause input state mismatch on removal
body: Rows use `key={index}`, so removing an email in the middle shifts the remaining inputs. Since the component is controlled via value array, this can cause focus/caret glitches and wrong value display during edits.

title: Hardcoded English tooltip text
body: The tooltip content "Remove email" is not wrapped in `t()`, unlike all other user-facing strings in the component, breaking localization.

title: Zod schema recreated each render and duplicate check ignores empty entries
body: The schema is redefined inside the component on every render. Additionally, the initial state `[""]` contains an empty string, so `z.string().email()` fails and the user sees an error only after clicking Add; the dialog gives no guidance on which entry is invalid.

title: Error toast message concatenates code with translated message
body: `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` produces messages like "BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid" when `t` lacks the key, and `message || t(...)` fallback is dead code because the template string is never empty. The toast shows raw error codes to users.

title: Cancel/close does not reset invalid-email state on dialog dismiss
body: `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` closes the dialog without resetting `multiEmailValue` or `isInvalidEmail`, so reopening shows stale input and error state, unlike the Cancel button which resets them.

title: Organizer lookup uses booking.userId and fails for orphaned bookings
body: `findFirstOrThrow` on `booking.userId || 0` throws a Prisma NotFound error (not a TRPCError) when the booking has no organizer, producing an unhandled 500 instead of a clean error.

title: Cleanup deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1, regardless of method or state
body: The second arm of the deleteMany OR (`retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) has no `method: SMS` filter and no `scheduled`/`cancelled` filter. It deletes any WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1 across all methods (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) and in any state. The intent is to drop SMS reminders that failed twice, so the clause should be scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduled: false`.

title: Unguarded retry update in catch can abort the whole cron run
body: The retryCount update inside the catch block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If that database write fails (connection issue, deleted row, constraint error), the exception escapes the for-loop, so every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped for this run and the handler returns a 500 instead of the 'SMS scheduled' response. One failing reminder can thus block all the others.

title: Reminders with empty message or no sendTo never increment retryCount
body: The retry increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)`. If the message is empty (for example no reminderBody and template is not REMINDER) or sendTo is missing, neither the success nor the failure branch runs and retryCount stays at 0. Such a reminder is picked up on every cron run forever and is never deleted, which is the unbounded-retry problem this PR is meant to fix.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of retryCount
body: retryCount is incremented using the value read at the start of the run (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) rather than an atomic `{ increment: 1 }` update. If two cron invocations overlap, both can read the same value and write the same increment, undercounting failures and allowing more attempts than the threshold of two.

title: retryCount is filtered on in the cleanup query but not indexed
body: The new cleanup clause filters on retryCount, and it runs on every cron invocation over the whole WorkflowReminder table. Without an index (the existing indexes cover method/scheduled/scheduledDate and cancelled/scheduledDate only), this forces a full table scan on each run.

title: No tests for the new retry and deletion behavior
body: The PR changes retry counting, the failure path, and the deletion criteria, but adds no tests. Nothing verifies that a reminder is deleted after two failures, that successful scheduling does not increment the counter, or that non-SMS reminders are untouched.

title: retryCount cleanup deletes reminders of every method, not just SMS
body: The second branch of the deleteMany OR (`retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` constraint, unlike the first branch. Any WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders that this SMS cron never touches, will be hard-deleted on every run. The condition should be scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` as well.

title: Retry increment uses a stale in-memory value instead of an atomic increment
body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` writes a value read earlier in the run. If another worker or run updates the same row concurrently, one increment can be lost, so the row may survive longer than the intended two-failure limit. Prisma's `{ increment: 1 }` would avoid this.

title: Unguarded DB update in catch block can abort the whole cron run
body: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the catch block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If it throws (for example the row was deleted by a concurrent run), the exception escapes the for-loop and every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped, and the handler returns an error instead of `SMS scheduled`.

title: Reminders with missing workflowStep/booking or empty message never accrue retries
body: When `!reminder.workflowStep || !reminder.booking` the loop `continue`s without incrementing retryCount, and when the message is empty or sendTo is missing the `if (message?.length ...)` block is skipped, so no retry is recorded. Such rows stay unscheduled and are never cleaned up by the new retry-based deletion, so they are retried indefinitely on every cron run, which is the behavior this PR is meant to stop.

title: retryCount cleanup condition is not scoped to unscheduled SMS reminders
body: The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` or `scheduled` filter, so `deleteMany` removes every WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) or whether it was already scheduled. The intent is to drop only SMS reminders that repeatedly failed to schedule. As written, unrelated reminders can be silently deleted, and already-scheduled reminders that have a referenceId can be removed while Twilio still holds the scheduled message. The retry condition should be combined with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and `scheduled: false`.

title: Unguarded update in catch block can abort the whole cron run
body: The retryCount update added in the `catch` block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If that database update throws (connection error, record already deleted by the cleanup step, etc.), the exception propagates out of the `for` loop. All remaining unscheduled reminders in the batch are skipped for this run and the handler fails. One failing reminder should not stop processing of the others.

title: Retry threshold does not match the PR description
body: The description says the reminder is deleted after scheduling fails twice. The condition `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` deletes when retryCount reaches 2, which is after two failures, so that part matches. However, the cleanup runs at the start of the next cron pass, so a reminder is actually removed on the third run. The comment above the deleteMany still only says it deletes past-dated reminders, which no longer describes the code. The comment should be updated to mention the retry-based deletion.

title: `= ANY(${array})` with Prisma.sql expands the array into a comma list, producing invalid SQL
body: Prisma.sql interpolates a JS array as a comma-separated list of parameters ($1, $2, $3), not as a single Postgres array parameter. So `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` renders as `"teamId" = ANY($1, $2, $3)`, which Postgres rejects with a syntax error. Every org-scope and team-scope authorization query built this way will fail at runtime. The same pattern appears at line 168 (`ANY(${uniqueUserIds})`) and line 201 (`ANY(${userIdsFromTeam})`). Fix by binding a real array, e.g. `Prisma.sql` with `Prisma.join` inside `ARRAY[...]`, or by casting, e.g. `= ANY(ARRAY[${Prisma.join(ids)}]::int[])`. Unit-level assertions on the Sql object will not catch this, since the tests only compare the template structure.

title: Tests lock in the broken `ANY(${array})` SQL shape and never execute it
body: The team and org scope expectations (lines 296-298, 333-342) assert the exact `ANY(${[...]})` template, so they pass against the broken implementation. Only the final getBaseConditions test runs SQL, and it only uses user scope, which has no array parameter. No test actually executes an org or team authorization condition against the database, so the array bug goes undetected.

title: Public `findMany` method removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions`, breaking callers
body: The PR deletes `findMany` and changes `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` return types from Prisma where-inputs to Prisma.Sql. Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` (or code consuming the old where-input shape) will fail to compile or behave differently. The PR description only frames this as a test update and does not mention the service API change or list the callers that were updated.

title: Caching tests deleted without replacement
body: The 'Caching' describe block (cache authorization conditions and cache filter conditions) was removed entirely. The service still has cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions logic, so the cache behavior is now untested. The findMany test was also rewritten into a raw $queryRaw test that no longer exercises the service's own query path.

title: Filter condition returned unparenthesized when used alone
body: buildFilterConditions returns `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` without outer parentheses when it is the only condition.
