Callers that embed this Sql fragment directly into a larger WHERE clause, rather than through getBaseConditions, could get incorrect precedence with a surrounding AND. Wrapping the single-condition result in parentheses would make the fragment safe to compose.

title: Public findMany() removed and replaced by getBaseConditions() without updating callers
body: The `findMany` method was removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns only a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment. Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany(...)` will fail to compile or break at runtime, and callers that relied on Prisma `select`/`where` arguments have no equivalent. The PR does not show any caller migration, so this is a breaking API change hidden inside a test-focused PR. Callers need to be found and migrated, or the change should be called out explicitly.

title: Caching tests deleted with no replacement
body: The `Caching` describe block (verifying that getAuthorizationConditions and getFilterConditions return memoized results on the second call) was removed entirely, and the PR description does not mention it. The service still implements memoization via cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions, so that behavior is now untested.

title: PR description says the service was already converted, but this PR changes the service too
body: The description states the Prisma.sql conversion was 'previously converted in the service implementation' and that this PR only updates tests. The diff, however, rewrites insightsBooking.ts (new SQL-building logic, removed findMany, changed types and constructor option type). Reviewers relying on the description would under-scope the review of the high-risk authorization SQL.

title: Array parameter passed to `= ANY(...)` expands into a scalar list and produces invalid SQL
body: Prisma.sql serializes a JS array interpolated into a template as a comma-separated list of placeholders ($1, $2, ...), not as a single Postgres array parameter. So `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` becomes `"teamId" = ANY($1, $2, $3)`, which Postgres rejects with a syntax error. The same problem affects the user-id `ANY(...)` clauses at lines 168, 201 and the team-scope clause. Any org or team scoped insights query will fail at runtime. Use `ANY(${Prisma.join(ids)})` is also wrong for ANY; the array must be cast to a single array parameter (e.g. `ANY(${ids}::int[])` via a helper that binds a single array value, or `IN (${Prisma.join(ids)})`). The unit tests only compare Sql objects, so they do not catch this.

title: Team-scope user clause has the same ANY(array) expansion bug
body: `Prisma.sql`("userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false)`` interpolates a JS array, which Prisma expands into individual placeholders, producing invalid SQL for `= ANY(...)`. Team-scoped queries that have members will error out instead of filtering.

title: getBaseConditions returns unparenthesized OR expressions when only one side exists
body: When only authConditions or only filterConditions is present, the method returns the fragment as-is. The org auth condition and the eventType filter are top-level ORs (`A OR B`). Callers embedding the result in a larger WHERE with AND (e.g. `WHERE x = 1 AND ${base}`) get wrong precedence and can leak rows. The combined branch wraps in parentheses, but the single-fragment branches do not, so the result is inconsistent. Wrap every returned fragment in parentheses.

title: Public findMany method removed without replacement in this change
body: The `findMany` method, which applied the authorization and filter conditions to a Prisma query, was deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions` returning raw SQL. Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` (routers or other services) will now fail to compile or run. The PR does not show these callers being updated, and the description does not mention the API change.

title: Only one integration test exercises the SQL, and it covers a single scenario
body: The `toEqual(Prisma.sql...)` assertions compare the template object structure, so they confirm string shape but not that the SQL is valid or returns correct rows. The only `$queryRaw` test covers one user-scoped case. Nothing runs the org or team scope SQL against Postgres, which is why the ANY(array) bug above goes unnoticed. Add database-backed tests for org and team scopes and for the OR-combined conditions.

title: Caching tests were deleted without explanation
body: The 'Caching' describe block (cache authorization conditions, cache filter conditions) was removed entirely. The service still caches these values, so the behavior is untested now. The PR description does not mention the removal.

title: deleteCache removes cache for any credential the user owns, not only Google Calendar, and ignores delegation credentials
body: The handler only checks that the credential belongs to the user, then deletes all calendarCache rows for that credentialId. The UI exposes this only for Google Calendar, but the endpoint itself accepts any credential id. Delegation-credential calendars are looked up by userId rather than credentialId in the cache repository, so deleting by credentialId will not clear the cache entries that are actually used for them, and the success response will mislead the user.

title: Cache status is queried on every connectedCalendars call, including for non-calendar and empty credential lists
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is called unconditionally on every request to connectedCalendars, which is used across settings and onboarding pages. It runs a groupBy over CalendarCache for every call, even when there are no connected calendars. This adds a DB round trip to a hot read path just to populate a timestamp that is only displayed for Google Calendar.

title: groupBy on credentialId with empty array filter returns unexpected results and is not scoped to valid rows
body: When credentialIds is empty, Prisma's `in: []` yields no rows, which is fine, but the method also does not filter expired entries, so the 'last updated' timestamp shown reflects stale rows that were already expired or are being used for a different key. The status is per-credential max updatedAt across all keys, which does not represent whether the cache is currently valid.

title: updatedAt added with @updatedAt on a table that is written via upsert on userId-only paths
body: The new updatedAt column uses @default(now()) @updatedAt. Prisma's @updatedAt is set on every Prisma update, but the raw SQL migration uses DEFAULT NOW() with no matching trigger. Rows touched by raw SQL or by the legacy-userId update path will have inconsistent semantics, and the displayed 'last updated' value may not reflect when data was actually refreshed.

title: updateManyByCredentialId on every cache refresh bumps SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars of the credential
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}) after every cache write. This updates all selected calendar rows for the credential, including unrelated event-type scoped ones, on each refresh and webhook. It also has no effect on the UI as the PR notes, adding write load for no displayed value. The PR itself suggests it should be removed.

title: Dropdown hides cache deletion and disconnect for non-Google, and renders empty trigger when cacheUpdatedAt is a falsy-but-valid value
body: hasCache is `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`, which returns the Date object or null. The conditional rendering is then mixed with the early return on `!canDisconnect && !hasCache`, so for a delegated Google credential with no cache the component returns null, but for a delegated Google credential with cache it still shows the trigger yet hides 'Remove app' correctly. Behavior is correct but fragile; more importantly the early return happens after hooks, which is fine, so the real issue is the 'Remove app' menu item is hidden when delegation is set while the cache-delete item shows without any confirmation context for delegated calendars.

title: Date formatting hard-coded to en-US and ignores user locale
body: The timestamp uses Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US") rather than the user's locale from useLocale, so the displayed date is inconsistent with the rest of the translated UI. Additionally new Date(cacheUpdatedAt) is called on a value that may arrive serialized as a string over tRPC, so the type annotation Date | null is not what is actually received at runtime.

title: deleteCache mutation onSuccess does not invalidate connectedCalendars, so cache status does not refresh
body: The deleteCache mutation's success handler only shows a toast and calls onSuccess. It does not invalidate trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, so the cacheUpdatedAt shown in the dropdown stays stale until a manual refresh, contrary to the PR's expectation that the UI updates.

title: deleteCache uses a raw z.number() input instead of a shared schema and does not check the credential type
body: The new procedure defines its input inline rather than in a schema file like the other calendar procedures. It accepts any credential id and no integration type, so the server contract allows deleting cache for non-calendar credentials.

title: sed -i '' is macOS-only and the script runs unconditionally against the repo .env
body: `sed -i ''` fails on GNU/Linux, so the script breaks in Linux dev environments and CI. The script also rewrites ../.env in place without a backup, and the cleanup handler exits 0 even on the rate-limit failure path.

title: Confirmation text says action cannot be undone but the cache is regenerated automatically
body: The 'confirm_delete_cache' string warns that the action cannot be undone, which overstates the impact since the cache is rebuilt on the next availability request. Also 'cache_last_updated' is passed a preformatted timestamp, so the translation key's placeholder name is coupled to the formatting done in the component.

title: deleteCache removes cache rows without checking the credential is a calendar credential
body: The handler verifies ownership of the credential but then deletes all calendarCache rows for that credentialId. The UI only shows this action for Google Calendar, but the endpoint accepts any owned credential ID, so any user can wipe cache for any of their credentials. Also the access check does not limit to calendar-type credentials. Low impact but the contract is unclear.

title: Credential lookup for delegation credentials may miss legitimate rows
body: The ownership check uses credential.userId === user.id. Delegation credentials cached under userId in CalendarCache (in-memory delegation path) are not keyed by credentialId, so deleting by credentialId will not clear them, and the returned success is misleading to the user.

title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is called with an unbounded list on every connectedCalendars query
body: connectedCalendarsHandler now runs a groupBy on CalendarCache for every request, including for users without the calendar-cache feature and for empty credential lists. With an empty array Prisma `in: []` still runs a query. This adds a DB round trip to a hot settings query for all users.

title: updatedAt on CalendarCache is bumped on every upsert but the cache status is shown as the time of last fetch
body: The Prisma field uses @updatedAt, so the timestamp reflects the last upsert. Expiry-based semantics are not captured. Combined with the migration default NOW() backfilling existing rows with the migration time, the UI will show a misleading 'last updated' for legacy caches.

title: Migration backfills all existing cache rows with migration time as updatedAt
body: Existing rows get updatedAt = NOW() at migration time rather than their real last-update time, so the cache status displayed for all legacy entries is incorrect until they are rewritten. The comment in the migration and schema describes this as an initial value but it misrepresents the data.

title: Dropdown renders for non-Google integrations with disconnect action removed when delegated
body: hasCache is only true for Google Calendar but the dropdown is rendered for every connected calendar. For a delegated credential with cache present, canDisconnect is false and the cache section still renders, which is fine, but for a non-Google credential where canDisconnect is false the component returns null so the previously shown dropdown behavior is changed. The return-null check also means the `hasCache` expression type is `Date | false | null | undefined` rather than boolean, which is a type-quality issue.

title: Cache timestamp hard-coded to en-US instead of user locale
body: Intl.DateTimeFormat uses 'en-US' regardless of the user's locale, so the displayed timestamp ignores the app's i18n setting even though the surrounding text is translated.

title: Delete cache confirm dialog closes before mutation result
body: onConfirm fires the mutation and immediately closes the dialog. The error toast is shown after the dialog closes, and the loading state is not reflected in the UI, so a failed delete gives no visible context.

title: Unrelated refactor of findMany removes type-safety check
body: The change drops the `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` check on the args object in findMany, which weakens type checking for an unrelated reason in a feature PR.

title: Writing SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all credential calendars on every cache refresh
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now calls updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}) which updates every SelectedCalendar row for the credential, including those for other event types and calendars not being refreshed. Prisma's @updatedAt will bump all of them, so updatedAt no longer means anything per calendar. Also the PR notes say this field is not displayed, so the write adds DB load for no consumer.

title: Extra selected calendar fields added to session user query
body: updatedAt and googleChannelId are added to the selectedCalendars select on every session lookup, widening a hot query used for every authenticated request, with no consumer in the session payload shown.

title: Dropdown now shown for disabled/delegated states where disconnect was previously hidden
body: The previous code hid the whole actions slot when delegationCredentialId was set or disableConnectionModification was true. The new code always renders the wrapper div and passes through props, so the actions column renders an empty container in those cases and layout width changes for every calendar row.

title: New deleteCache mutation and cache enrichment have no tests
body: The new tRPC mutation with its ownership check, the connectedCalendars enrichment, and the new repository method are added without any unit tests, despite the PR checklist relying on manual verification only.

title: sed -i '' is macOS-only syntax
body: sed -i '' fails on GNU sed (Linux) and in CI containers, so the script breaks for non-macOS developers while the rest of the repo is portable. Also the script writes tunnel URLs into the shared .env without documentation.

title: Cache-related strings added but the UI reuses existing keys inconsistently
body: The new keys are added but the dropdown uses 'remove_app' and 'app_removed_successfully' for disconnect, and the mock/feature text says 'Delete cached data' for both the menu item and the dialog title, so the confirm dialog and trigger are indistinguishable.

title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx without declaring tsx
body: The script now relies on npx downloading tsx at run time, but tsx is not listed in devDependencies. This is unrelated to the cache feature and changes dev tooling without explanation.

title: deleteCache deletes all cache rows for the credential without checking it is a Google credential or caches by userId
body: The handler verifies the credential belongs to the user, then runs calendarCache.deleteMany by credentialId. This is scoped correctly for DB credentials, but the UI shows the Delete cached data action for any calendar integration where cacheUpdatedAt is set, and the mutation is not restricted to calendar credentials. Also, delegated/in-memory credential caches are keyed by userId (see getCachedAvailability), so deleting by credentialId does not clear the cache the user actually reads, making the 'Cache deleted successfully' toast misleading.

title: deleteCache input accepts any credentialId without shared validation or authorization on the router
body: The router inlines z.object({ credentialId: z.number() }) instead of a shared schema, and relies entirely on the handler's findFirst check. This is functionally guarded, but it is inconsistent with other calendar routes and gives no rate limiting or audit logging for a destructive operation on cache shared across the calendar sync pipeline.

title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is called with an empty array when no calendars are connected
body: connectedCalendarsHandler passes all credentialIds to this method; when the list is empty Prisma's groupBy with credentialId in [] works but the call is an unnecessary DB round trip on every connectedCalendars query. More importantly, the query runs for every credential on each page load, adding a groupBy over CalendarCache that is not indexed on (credentialId, updatedAt), a performance concern on large tables.

title: Cache status reports the most recent updatedAt across all keys, while the freshness of the cache used is per-key
body: _max.updatedAt across all CalendarCache rows for a credential is shown as 'Last updated'. The row set includes entries for multiple timeMin/timeMax windows, and since @updatedAt is only bumped on upsert, this may show a timestamp that doesn't reflect whether the cache is expired (expiresAt) or stale. Status shown is not a true cache health indicator.

title: updatedAt uses @default(now()) @updatedAt, but the migration uses NOW() with TIMESTAMP(3) and the schema comment is misleading
body: The schema comment says the default is for legacy rows and raw inserts, but the migration backfills all existing rows with the migration time, so every legacy cache entry reports a 'last updated' value equal to deploy time, which is misleading in the UI. The migration also lacks the Prisma-managed @updatedAt behaviour in raw SQL, so any raw update path will not bump updatedAt.

title: updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty update payload, which may not bump updatedAt as intended
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}). Prisma's updateMany with empty data only bumps updatedAt if the field is @updatedAt, which it is for SelectedCalendar; but this touches every SelectedCalendar row for the credential (including other event type scopes) on every cache refresh, adding write load on a hot path and changing updatedAt semantics that other code (UserWithCalendars.updatedAt) relies on. The PR notes concede this is unused in the frontend.

title: Extra full-table write added on every availability cache refresh
body: The new updateManyByCredentialId call runs after every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache, writing to all SelectedCalendar rows of the credential, even though the value is only used by nothing in the UI. This adds writes without a consumer and should be removed or justified.

title: Intl format hardcodes en-US locale while the rest of the UI is localized
body: The cache timestamp is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...) rather than the user's locale from useLocale, so non-English users see an English date format inside a translated sentence.

title: Cache section shown only when cacheUpdatedAt is truthy, but Date is passed through JSON as string
body: cacheUpdatedAt arrives from tRPC serialization (superjson or JSON) and may be a string, yet the prop is typed Date | null. new Date(cacheUpdatedAt) hides the type mismatch; with plain JSON the value is a string and the type is wrong. Type should reflect the wire format or the handler should guarantee Date.

title: Delete cache mutation onSuccess does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
body: After deleting cache, cacheUpdatedAt in the connectedCalendars query remains stale, so the UI still shows the old 'Last updated' status until a refetch. The disconnect path invalidates queries but the delete cache path does not.

title: Returns null when neither action is available, hiding the Alert/card actions layout
body: When the dropdown returns null, the wrapping div with w-32 still renders in the calling component, leaving an empty reserved area; the previous code avoided rendering the wrapper. Minor layout regression.

title: Disconnect action now shows for the error Alert card even when disableConnectionModification is not passed
body: The error-state branch passes disableConnectionModification into CredentialActionsDropdown, but the old code hid the action only for delegation credentials and not for the disabled-modification case in that branch; behaviour change without test coverage.

title: sed -i '' is macOS-only syntax and breaks on Linux
body: sed -i '' -E ... treats the empty string as a backup suffix on BSD sed; on GNU sed it treats '' as the script and fails. The script is not portable and fails silently for Linux contributors.

title: selectedCalendars select now loads updatedAt and googleChannelId for every session load
body: findUnlockedUserForSession is on the hot session path; adding columns to the selectedCalendars select increases payload for each request even though the session does not use them.

title: Comment says updatedAt doesn't exist yet in CalendarCache, now stale
body: The TODO comment states updatedAt does not exist in CalendarCache, but this PR adds it. The comment and the orderBy logic should be updated to match.

title: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with no referenceId deletes the DB row immediately and skips the cancel flag
body: When referenceId is null the function deletes the workflowReminder row directly. For reminders that were never scheduled in SendGrid (scheduled=false, cron-pending), this is fine, but the function is also called with reminder.referenceId for already-scheduled reminders in the non-immediate path, which only sets cancelled=true and never cancels the SendGrid send. The cron then cancels within the hour, but the email can still go out for reminders scheduled more than an hour ahead only if the cron misses them; more importantly the sendAt delay is ignored, so the deletion relies entirely on the cron job running every 15 minutes.

title: Immediate cancel path returns without deleting the reminder row
body: In the immediateDelete branch the SendGrid cancel request is sent but the workflowReminder row is not removed and cancelled is not set. The row keeps referenceId pointing to a batch that is already cancelled, so later operations (cron, reschedule lookups) act on stale state and the row lingers until the scheduledDate cleanup.

title: Cron cancels reminders one by one and aborts the whole batch on first error
body: The loop awaits client.request for each reminder inside one try block. If any single SendGrid cancel fails (for example the batch was already sent or was already cancelled), the catch logs and the remaining cancelled reminders in the loop are never cancelled, and the workflowRemindersToDelete promises for earlier ones are not awaited. They will be retried on the next run only if the failing one is still flagged, so other reminders can keep getting sent.

title: Cancelled reminders with no referenceId are never deleted or cancelled
body: remindersToCancel is selected by cancelled=true and scheduledDate only. Rows with null referenceId are passed to client.request with batch_id null, which fails, and the catch then aborts the loop, so one bad row blocks all others.

title: Promise array of prisma delete is built but Prisma client calls are lazy and typed oddly
body: The array is typed as Prisma.Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient, and the delete promises are only awaited after all SendGrid calls have completed, so a failure in the loop leaves them unawaited and rows may be left behind silently.

title: SMS reminder row is deleted immediately while Twilio cancel may have failed
body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the workflowReminder row unconditionally after twilio.cancelSMS. If cancelSMS throws, the catch swallows the error and the row is not deleted either, but more importantly the row is deleted even when the Twilio message is still pending in the non-cancelled path, so there is no record to retry. Also SMS cancellation is not deferred via the cancelled flag as emails are, so behavior is inconsistent.

title: Workflow delete uses immediate email cancel while the scheduledReminders query only returns scheduled rows
body: Deleting a workflow passes immediateDelete=true for email reminders, which hits the SendGrid cancel path that does not remove the DB row. The workflow is then deleted with deleteMany which cascades reminders, but the per-reminder cancel is fired without await and errors are only logged, so SendGrid sends may still go out.

title: Removed event types no longer scope reminder deletion to the user
body: The previous deleteMany was restricted by booking.userId = ctx.user.id. The replacement removes the DB-side deletion entirely for these reminders, so non-scheduled (scheduled=false) rows for disabled event types are never removed from the database by this path, leaving stale cron-pending rows that the scheduleEmailReminders job will still process and send.

title: Edited-step reminder cancellation uses forEach with async callbacks
body: remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) does not await deleteScheduledEmailReminder or deleteScheduledSMSReminder, so the mutation returns before reminders are cancelled and any error becomes an unhandled rejection. The previous explicit deleteMany on workflowReminder was also removed here, so rows for edited steps are no longer removed in the SMS path reliably.

title: Large block of indentation-only changes in testAction comment
body: The diff reindents commented-out code in testAction, which is unrelated to the fix and inflates the review surface without functional change.

title: Error message does not match the operation performed
body: The catch logs 'Error canceling reminder' for every branch, including the DB delete path, making failures in the cron-marking step hard to distinguish from SendGrid failures.

title: New cancelled column is nullable Boolean with no default
body: cancelled is Boolean? with no default, so existing rows are NULL. The cron filter cancelled: true excludes NULLs correctly, but code that treats the flag as tri-state adds ambiguity; a non-null default false would be safer.

title: Reschedule cancels previous reminders with immediateDelete=true inside try that cannot catch async errors
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder is async but is called without await inside forEach within a try block, so the try/catch never catches its rejections. The call is also made with immediateDelete true, cancelling in SendGrid without removing the DB row, leaving stale rows referencing a cancelled batch.

title: deleteScheduledEmailReminder without referenceId deletes DB row but never cancels; immediate path never removes DB row
body: When referenceId is null the function deletes the workflowReminder row and returns, which is fine. But when immediateDelete is true, the function sends the SendGrid cancel request and returns without deleting or updating the workflowReminder row, so a stale row stays in the DB with cancelled unset. The cron job's 'cancelled' sweep then never sees it and the row lingers until scheduledDate passes, and the reminder's referenceId stays unique-constrained against future use.

title: Cancelled-but-not-immediate emails are only marked; the 'cancel' status set by cron is applied only within 1 hour of send
body: Non-immediate deletion only sets cancelled=true. The cron (scheduleEmailReminders) only cancels reminders whose scheduledDate is within the next hour. Reminders cancelled earlier stay in SendGrid scheduled_sends and are sent later, which is the case the PR claims to fix; the window design should be justified, and any reminder whose booking is cancelled and whose scheduledDate is more than an hour out is still sent at its time if the cron's sweep is not reached before send. Also the row is never deleted if the cron's SendGrid call fails inside the try block, which aborts the whole loop.

title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders
body: The loop calls client.request for each reminder inside a single try. If any request throws, the catch logs and the loop exits, so all subsequent cancelled reminders are not cancelled in SendGrid and their rows are not deleted, and the cron continues to send those emails. Each cancellation should be wrapped individually.

title: Reminder rows deleted before the promise is awaited; Promise.all over unexecuted Prisma promises
body: prisma.workflowReminder.delete returns a lazy PrismaPromise; it is only executed when awaited by Promise.all, which is outside the per-reminder loop. Any rejection (e.g. row already deleted by concurrent deleteMany) is caught only by the outer catch and aborts remaining work. Also the workflowRemindersToDelete type annotation is a Prisma__ client type that is unusual for this purpose.

title: deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the DB row even when the Twilio cancel fails, and is now unconditional
body: The new implementation calls twilio.cancelSMS inside the same try as prisma delete. If cancelSMS throws (e.g. message already sent or not found), the workflowReminder row is never deleted, and the caller in handleCancelBooking/bookings reschedule ignores the error. Conversely SMS reminders that were never scheduled (no referenceId) now still get a row delete that may fail for rows already removed. The SMS path also no longer supports the 'cancelled' deferral used for emails, so behavior is asymmetric.

title: Reminder deletion is fire-and-forget; errors and DB writes are not awaited
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async but the forEach does not await them, and the earlier deleteMany of workflowReminder rows was removed. The cancel response is returned before the reminder updates complete, and any error is swallowed, so the booking cancellation can succeed while reminders are still scheduled.

title: Rescheduled booking's reminders are cancelled with immediateDelete=true for email but not awaited
body: The forEach calls the async deleteScheduledEmailReminder without awaiting, inside a try that cannot catch its rejections. Errors become unhandled promise rejections and the new booking flow proceeds before cancellation completes, so the old reminders may still be sent.

title: Edited-step reminders deleted with forEach(async ...) and not awaited; scheduled rows still reference deleted data
body: remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) does not await the async delete calls, and the previous code's workflowReminder.deleteMany was removed, so rows for edited steps are now only marked cancelled or deleted asynchronously, racing with the subsequent scheduleEmailReminder calls that create new reminders for the same bookings.

title: Broken JS in addedSteps / reformatted block: dayjs and BookingInfo not imported and PrismaPromise/Prisma value import
body: The import list now imports PrismaPromise and Prisma as values from @prisma/client, and the commented-out testAction block was reformatted with broken indentation/comment nesting. The removed BookingInfo import is still referenced by `let evt: BookingInfo` in the commented region (fine), but `PrismaPromise` is used only as a type while imported as a value, and the trailing comma-less `Prisma` import is inconsistent with the rest of the file. Type-only imports should not be value imports.

title: Changed signature of deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder breaks boolean-flag semantics
body: The third parameter immediateDelete is passed as true in some callers and omitted in others with no documented contract; the meaning (cancel now vs. mark for cron) is implicit. Callers in workflows.tsx delete a deleted workflow's reminders immediately while bookings use deferred cancel, which is easy to get wrong and is not tested.

title: No tests added for the new cancelled-flag cron path or the immediate/deferred branches
body: The PR changes cancellation semantics across booking cancel, reschedule, workflow edit, and cron, yet adds no tests covering the cancelled flag, the 100-pending-cancellation failure mode, or the 1-hour cron window.

title: deleteScheduledEmailReminder deletes DB row without cancelling in SendGrid when referenceId is absent, and immediate path never removes the DB row
body: When referenceId is null the function deletes the workflowReminder row, but when immediateDelete is true it cancels in SendGrid and returns without deleting the reminder row. Callers (handleCancelBooking, handleNewBooking reschedule path, workflows.delete, step deletion) then rely on the cron to delete it, but the cron only deletes reminders past scheduledDate and cancels cancelled ones within the next hour; reminders with immediate cancel leave stale rows whose referenceId is still a valid batch id, and a subsequent `scheduled` lookup or unique referenceId reuse can misbehave. The asymmetry is confusing and the immediate path is also missing the DB update that the non-immediate path does.

title: Cancelled reminder row is deleted even if SendGrid cancel fails in the batch
body: The loop awaits client.request for each reminder, but the surrounding try/catch wraps the whole loop. If one SendGrid cancel request throws, the loop aborts and all remaining reminders stay cancelled-but-uncancelled in SendGrid and will still be sent, while the already-pushed deletes are awaited. Also the delete promises are created without awaiting inside the loop, so a failed DB delete is only caught by Promise.all and not per reminder. Each reminder should be handled independently so one failure does not block the rest, which is exactly the failure mode this PR is meant to fix.

title: SMS cancel deletes reminder row before/regardless of Twilio cancel, and cancelSMS failure leaves SMS sent
body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder now deletes the DB row immediately after twilio.cancelSMS, all within one try. If cancelSMS throws (for example the message already sent or the API fails), the prisma delete is skipped and the row stays, and the caller ignores the failure. Meanwhile it deletes the reminder row even when no referenceId exists, which is correct, but the SMS path is never marked cancelled for later cron processing, unlike the email path. The two managers now use inconsistent cancellation semantics.

title: Errors in deleteScheduledEmailReminder are swallowed, so callers cannot detect failed cancellation
body: The function catches all errors and only logs them. handleCancelBooking and other callers are fire-and-forget (no await), so a SendGrid or DB failure silently leaves the reminder scheduled and it is sent to a cancelled booking, which is the bug this PR claims to fix.

title: Cancellation of workflow reminders is not awaited and no longer checks scheduled state
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach, and the previous guard `reminder.scheduled && reminder.referenceId` was removed. For unscheduled reminders (scheduled=false, referenceId null) the code now runs a DB delete per reminder, and the deletions race with the subsequent Promise.all and with attendee/booking reference deletes. Results of cancellation are not observed before the response is returned.

title: Cancelled flag set for reminders whose cron may already have sent them, and no reset path
body: Setting cancelled=true on reminders is only processed by the cron for those within the next hour. A reminder rescheduled back in (same referenceId, e.g. reschedule creating new reminders) is never un-cancelled, and the cancelled flag is never cleared on creation. Also reminders cancelled but already past scheduledDate are removed by the earlier deleteMany without cancelling in SendGrid, so they may have been sent already with no cancel attempt.

title: Cron cancel reads all cancelled reminders with no batching or limit
body: remindersToCancel is loaded fully and each is cancelled serially via an HTTP request to SendGrid. With many pending cancellations this can exceed the cron timeout and, since the outer try wraps everything, one failure stops the rest, causing the backlog to grow and reproduce the 100-pending-cancellations limit problem described in the PR.

title: Removed PrismaPromise/Prisma type imports while still referenced; import of Prisma as value
body: The import block now imports PrismaPromise and Prisma as runtime values from @prisma/client (they are types) and the type import from the same module was removed; PrismaPromise is still used in the update handler for remindersToDeletePromise. This can break the build under isolatedModules / TS strictness and is inconsistent with the rest of the file.

title: Reindentation of the testAction comment block breaks the commented-out code and the diff is unrelated
body: The large whitespace-only change inside the commented-out testAction block is unrelated to the fix and makes the commented block harder to restore; it also obscures the real changes in review.

title: Sender ID input for SMS actions no longer renders when phone number is not needed
body: The condition changed from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to `isPhoneNumberNeeded`, which hides the whole block including the phone number inputs for SMS_ATTENDEE actions. This is an unrelated UI regression not described in the PR; the sender ID field behavior for SMS_ATTENDEE is lost.

title: New cancelled column is nullable Boolean with no default
body: cancelled is Boolean? with no default, so existing and new rows are NULL. The cron filters with `cancelled: true` which is fine, but the field semantics are inconsistent with other flags; a non-null default false would be safer.

title: appStore entries are now un-awaited Promises, so consumers that index without await get a Promise object
body: The appStore object was changed from namespace imports to `import(...)` promises. Every consumer that reads `appStore[key]` and then checks `"lib" in app` or `"CalendarService" in app.lib` without awaiting will now get a Promise, where `"lib" in promise` is false, so the app is silently treated as not implemented. Any call site not updated in this diff (e.g. other files using appStore, getApps-related code, or the `as keyof typeof appStore` lookups) will break silently at runtime rather than fail at compile time, since the types still look plausible.

title: Lookup via appStore uses a dynamic import that can reject; error is not handled and the function now returns a rejected promise
body: `await appStore[...]` now performs a dynamic import. If the key is unknown, `appStore[key]` is undefined and awaiting it yields undefined (handled), but if the module fails to load (missing module, build error) the rejection propagates out of getCalendar and every caller, which previously returned null gracefully. This changes failure behavior for calendar lookup.

title: getCalendarCredentials still calls getCalendar synchronously, now receiving a Promise
body: getCalendarCredentials maps credentials with `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` without await. getCalendar is now async, so `calendar` is a Promise stored in the returned array. getConnectedCalendars later does `await item.calendar`, but any other consumer of this function (and the type of the result) now deals with Promises, and the function itself is still synchronous so the calendar is created outside the await chain. Its errors also become unhandled promise rejections.

title: forEach with async callback discards promises; deletion errors and completion are not awaited
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` does not await the async callbacks. The surrounding try/catch can no longer catch errors from getCalendar or deleteEvent (they become unhandled rejections), and the function returns true before calendar/video cancellations finish, so the reschedule can complete while the old events still exist.

title: forEach with async callback discards promises; cancellation errors become unhandled
body: Same issue as the vital variant: the async forEach callback is not awaited, so the try/catch no longer catches calendar/video delete failures and they surface as unhandled promise rejections, while the function proceeds to send emails and return true before deletions complete.

title: forEach with async callback in requestReschedule; deletions not awaited and errors unhandled
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` fires calendar and video deletions without awaiting them. Errors become unhandled rejections (possibly crashing or spamming logs), and the mutation proceeds to send the reschedule email and webhooks while the previous calendar events may still be being deleted.

title: forEach with async callback inside recurring cancellation; apiDeletes is read before pushes happen
body: `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })` is not awaited. `await apiDeletes` / `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs before these async pushes occur, so recurring-event calendar deletions are neither awaited nor guaranteed to complete before the booking is reported cancelled, and failures are unhandled.

title: getCachedResults filters out nulls only after mapping, relying on index alignment that may now be wrong
body: Calendars are resolved with Promise.all over calendarCredentials, preserving order, so index matching still works, but the comment about nulls is now misleading and the resolved calendars are not paired with credentials after any filtering. Low risk on its own, but combined with other un-awaited uses it is fragile.

title: `await apiDeletes` awaits an array, not the pending deletions
body: `await apiDeletes;` on an array does not wait for any of the contained promises. The payment-rejection path therefore no longer waits for calendar/video deletions before returning success, which is the pre-existing bug, but the async conversion of getCalendar makes the pushed promises even more likely to be missing from this array.

title: Payment app lookup returns null from a function whose result is not a payment response; wrong type on fallback
body: In the refund path, when the payment app is not implemented the handler does `return null` from within handler, which is not a valid cancel response and skips cancellation entirely after the booking has already been deemed to need refund handling. This was pre-existing but is now reached more often because the async lookup changes what the check sees.

title: appStore entries are now unresolved Promises, but callers still use them synchronously in places
body: The appStore object now maps each key to a dynamic import() Promise instead of a module namespace. Any consumer that accesses `appStore[x].lib` (or `"lib" in appStore[x]`) without awaiting gets a Promise, so the `"lib" in app` check is always false and the feature silently behaves as unimplemented. Call sites not updated in this PR (e.g. other usages across the repo beyond the 12 files, such as getApps/utils or payment/locations code that reads appStore synchronously) will break silently rather than fail loudly.

title: Mapping to import() promises changes the module type contract for all importers
body: Previously the default export was a map of module namespaces; now every property is Promise<module>. Any type-level consumer expecting the namespace shape will fail type checking or, if using `as`/casts, fail at runtime. The PR does not show a single shared type or helper (e.g. a typed async accessor) to enforce awaiting, so future callers will easily make the same mistake.

title: getCalendarCredentials calls async getCalendar without awaiting, yielding Promise objects as calendars
body: getCalendar is now async, but getCalendarCredentials still does `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` and stores the Promise in the returned object. Downstream code in getConnectedCalendars then does `await item.calendar`, which works only by accident, but any other consumer of getCalendarCredentials reading `.calendar` synchronously will get a Promise and treat it as a non-null Calendar, calling methods on it and failing.

title: getCachedResults relies on index alignment that is fine, but a rejected getCalendar aborts all calendars
body: `Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map(getCalendar))` now rejects if any single app import fails (e.g. a missing module), causing the whole busy-times lookup to fail, where previously only the failing calendar was affected. This is a behavioral regression for availability computation.

title: forEach with async callback discards promises; deletions run unawaited and errors become unhandled rejections
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` does not await the async callbacks, so the surrounding try/catch never catches errors from getCalendar or deleteEvent. Those rejections become unhandled promise rejections, and the reschedule returns before calendar cleanup finishes. The same pattern is repeated in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts, trpc bookings.tsx, and handleCancelBooking.ts (recurring branch).

title: Recurring-cancel calendar deletions run in an un-awaited forEach async callback
body: `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... await calendar?.deleteEvent ... apiDeletes.push(...) })` pushes into apiDeletes after `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` has already captured the array, so these deletions are neither awaited nor have their errors surfaced; the booking can be reported cancelled while calendar events remain, and rejections are unhandled.

title: getVideoAdapters now awaits each app sequentially, serializing imports
body: The for-loop with `await appStore[...]` per credential serializes module loading and adapter creation. This is a latency regression for getBusyVideoTimes and createMeeting with multiple credentials compared to the previous synchronous reduce; Promise.all over the credentials would preserve ordering-insensitive concurrency.

title: updateMeeting does not handle getVideoAdapters failure; createMeeting error path also changed
body: getVideoAdapters now can reject (dynamic import failure). In updateMeeting the call is outside any try/catch, so an import failure throws out of the update flow instead of being reported as success=false. In createMeeting it is also outside the try block, bypassing the sendBrokenIntegrationEmail/calVideo fallback.

title: await used inside a non-async callback context
body: The diff adds `await getCalendar(...)` inside the reference-deletion loop, but the enclosing callback is not shown as async in this hunk; if it is a non-async forEach/map callback the code will not compile or will leave the await effectively unhandled. Verify the surrounding function is async and the loop is a for...of.

title: Payment app lookup returns null from a mutation path after a warn, but the function signature expects a result
body: In the confirm mutation, when the payment app is not implemented the code returns null from inside the handler, skipping refund and status updates while the booking is still treated as rejected by the caller flow; the awaited appStore change does not alter this, but it reinforces that the missing-module case (now a possible import rejection) is not handled at all here.

title: Import promises are created eagerly, so every app module loads at import time
body: Each entry is written as `import("./x")`, which starts loading the module as soon as the object literal is evaluated. Any module that imports appStore therefore loads all ~28 app modules up front, which defeats the purpose of async loading. Wrapping each entry in an arrow, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, would defer loading until a caller asks for the app. Callers would then need to invoke the function instead of awaiting the property. Also, a rejected import that nobody awaits becomes an unhandled rejection.

title: Async forEach callback makes the try/catch useless and drops rejections
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` does not await the callbacks. The `try/catch` below only catches synchronous throws, so any rejection from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection, and the error is never logged. The function also returns `true` and sends the reschedule email before the cancellations have run. Use `for...of` with `await`, or `Promise.allSettled` over mapped promises, so failures are caught and logged.

title: Async forEach callback makes the try/catch useless and drops rejections
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` does not await the callbacks. The `try/catch` only catches synchronous throws, so failures from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` become unhandled rejections and are never logged. The function also proceeds to send the email before the cancellations finish. Use `for...of` with `await`, or `Promise.allSettled`.

title: Recurring cancellation pushes to apiDeletes after it has already been awaited
body: The `forEach(async (credential) => ...)` callback awaits `getCalendar` and then pushes `deleteEvent` promises into `apiDeletes`. Nothing waits for these callbacks, and `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs later with the array as it was at that point. Calendar deletions for recurring bookings may therefore be skipped from the awaited set, and their rejections go unhandled. Replace this with a `for...of` loop that awaits each credential.

title: Async forEach callback in requestReschedule ignores its returned promises
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` discards the promises from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting`. The mutation then sends the reschedule email and resolves, while calendar and video cancellations are still running. Any rejection is unhandled and invisible to the caller. Use `for...of` with `await` or `Promise.allSettled`.

title: getCalendarCredentials stores unawaited promises that can reject unhandled
body: `getCalendar(credential)` is now async, but it is still called without await, and the promise is stored in the `calendar` field. If the dynamic import of an app fails, that promise rejects. The rejection is only observed later, in `getConnectedCalendars`, so Node may report it as unhandled first. Also, the `.flatMap` callback no longer produces a value that matches its old synchronous meaning.

title: Video adapters are resolved one at a time instead of in parallel
body: The `for...of` loop in `getVideoAdapters` awaits each `appStore` import in sequence. The dynamic imports are independent, so this serializes module loading for every video credential. `Promise.all` over the credentials would avoid the extra latency.

title: Dayjs object identity comparison makes zero-length override check dead code
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two freshly created Dayjs objects with `===`, which is always false. The intended check for an empty override never runs, so such overrides fall through to the later range checks with unexpected results. Compare with `.isSame(...)` or compare `valueOf()` instead.

title: Override day comparison mixes server-local and UTC formatting
body: The override start is shifted by a computed offset and formatted with `format("YYYY MM DD")` using dayjs's local zone (`dayjs(date.start)` is not `.utc()`), and this is compared against `slotStartTime.format(...)`, which is UTC. The result depends on the server's TZ environment, so on a non-UTC server a date override can match the wrong day or miss the slot entirely. The comparison should be done in a single explicit timezone on both sides.

title: Working-hours end is computed from the slot start, so the end bound is never checked
body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` rather than the slot end, so `end === start`. The check `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore only tests the start time, and a slot starting inside working hours but running past the end is accepted. Also, the working-hour minutes are in organizer timezone while `slotStartTime` is UTC, so the comparison is inconsistent for non-UTC organizers.

title: Working-hours check newly applied to all availability checks using UTC day and mismatched timezone
body: checkIfIsAvailable now rejects slots outside `workingHours` for every caller, including fixed hosts whose `workingHours` were previously ignored at this point. `slotStartTime.day()` uses UTC weekday and UTC minutes, while `workingHour.startTime/endTime` are minutes in the organizer timezone. For organizers far from UTC, valid slots near midnight will be wrongly rejected or accepted. This is a behavior change beyond the described fix and is not covered by tests.

title: Override timezone may be undefined and `Date.toString()` round-trip is lossy
body: `override.timeZone` is optional in `TimeRange`, and `tz(undefined)` silently falls back to the local timezone, which yields a wrong offset. Additionally `override.start.toString()` drops milliseconds and relies on Date string parsing. Use `dayjs(override.start)` directly and handle a missing timezone explicitly (for example, fall back to the organizer timezone).

title: Shifted override minutes ignore day rollover
body: The startTime/endTime are computed as `hour()*60 + minute()` after shifting by the timezone offset, which discards the date. If the shifted time crosses midnight (for example, an override at 23:00 organizer time shifted to the next day for the invitee), the minute-of-day wraps to the wrong value, and the override window is placed at the wrong time of day. The override end is similarly affected. Offsets should be applied to the day-based timestamp, not the wrapped clock time.

title: No test covers the round-robin fixed-host date override fix
body: The PR's main claim is that date overrides of fixed hosts now restrict round-robin slots, but the only test added covers the invitee timezone change for a personal event. No test creates a round-robin event with a fixed host having a date override and checks that slots outside the override are removed. The new checkIfIsAvailable override and working-hours logic is therefore untested for the reported bug.

title: Working-hours check rejects any slot that falls outside any single working-hours range
body: The working-hours guard uses `workingHours.find(...)` and returns false if the callback is truthy. The callback is truthy whenever one particular range does not contain the slot. So for a day with several ranges (for example 9-12 and 14-18, or aggregated hours from multiple hosts), a slot inside one range is rejected because it is outside another. The intended semantics is 'outside all ranges', which needs `every`/`some` logic. Also `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of the slot end, so `end > workingHour.endTime` checks the start, not the end. Finally, the comparison uses UTC day and hour while `WorkingHours` values are minutes in the organizer timezone (per the type doc), so the check is evaluated in the wrong timezone. This is a regression that can remove valid slots for any multi-range or cross-timezone schedule.

title: Comparing dayjs objects with === is always false
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares object identity, not time. The branch that treats a zero-length override as a special case never runs. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `valueOf()`.

title: Date override logic accepts partially overlapping slots and rejects slots when several overrides share a day
body: `dateOverrideExist` is set true for any override on the same day, and `find` returns true (meaning 'reject') as soon as any override on that day does not contain the slot. Consequences: (1) with two overrides on the same day, a slot inside override A is rejected because it is outside override B. (2) A slot that starts before an override's start and ends after it (partial overlap) matches none of the rejection conditions. It falls through to `return true` and is accepted even though it is not fully inside the override. The containment test must be: slot start >= override start and slot end <= override end, evaluated across all overrides for the day, with a clear rule for when no override covers the slot.

title: Organizer timezone offset sign looks inverted for override conversion
body: `utcOffset = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` negates the organizer's offset. For Asia/Kolkata (+330) this shifts the override by -330 minutes, so the local day of the override is computed incorrectly. The same override is then compared against `slotStartTime.format(...)` in UTC, which mixes frames. The PR's timezone fix depends on this conversion, so it needs verification with a concrete example (an override near midnight in the organizer zone).

title: Override timezone conversion depends on an optional field that may be undefined
body: `override.timeZone` is typed optional in the flattened override (it is set from `availability.timeZone`, which `getUserAvailability` may leave undefined). `dayjs(...).tz(undefined)` then falls back to the local runtime timezone, which differs between server and browser. The computed offset becomes environment dependent. The code should either require the timezone or fall back explicitly to the organizer timezone that `getSlots` already receives. Also, `startTime`/`endTime` are computed as minutes of day only, so an override spanning midnight after the offset shift produces endTime < startTime and is silently dropped by the boundary logic.

title: New timezone test does not exercise the bug it claims to cover
body: The added test asserts that the same UTC slots are returned for the attendee timezone +6:00 as for +5:30. It reuses the existing expectation, so it passes whether or not overrides are adjusted correctly. It does not cover the reported case: an organizer override whose organizer timezone differs from the schedule timezone, where the attendee's timezone should change which slots appear. No test covers the round-robin fixed-host override fix either, which is the primary change in the description.

title: Date-object identity comparison makes the zero-length override check dead code
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct Dayjs objects with `===`, which is always false. The intended check (override start equals end, i.e. an empty override) never fires. Compare with `.isSame(...)` or compare `.valueOf()` instead.

title: Any same-day date override makes a slot available and skips all busy-time checks
body: When any date override exists on the slot's day and the slot is not rejected by the override range checks, `dateOverrideExist` is set and the function returns `true` before evaluating `busy`. A slot that overlaps a calendar event or existing booking for a fixed host is therefore reported as available, which is the exact double-booking the PR is meant to prevent.

title: Working-hours check rejects slots that are inside a valid working-hours range
body: `workingHours.find(...)` returns truthy if any working-hour entry for the weekday does not contain the slot. With multiple ranges per day (e.g. split shifts, or the aggregate of several users), a slot inside one range is still rejected because another range does not contain it. The check should be `!workingHours.some(...)` over ranges that contain the slot.

title: Slot end minutes computed from slotStartTime, so the end bound check is meaningless
body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` uses the start time, so `start` and `end` are identical. The `end > workingHour.endTime` comparison therefore only tests the slot start and never the slot's end. It should use `slotEndTime`. Slots that start inside working hours but run past the end are accepted.

title: Date override range checks ignore the override's own end for the day's boundary
body: The override matching logic only tests the day of `date.start` against the slot start day. Overrides that span midnight or where the slot start is on the same calendar day in the organizer timezone but the slot is on a different day in the invitee's timezone are handled inconsistently, because the UTC offset is applied to `date.start` and `date.end` but the comparison day is taken from the UTC slot time. This can match the wrong day for invitees far from the organizer timezone.

title: Override offset computed by round-tripping Date through toString() loses precision and depends on server TZ
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` formats the Date as a local-time string with seconds precision and then parses it again in the process's local timezone. Milliseconds are dropped and the result depends on the server/browser timezone, so the computed offset can be wrong. Use `dayjs(override.start)` directly. Also `override.timeZone` is optional in `TimeRange` but is passed straight to `.tz()` without a fallback, so a missing timezone silently changes the result.

title: Offset sign and day-matching logic for overrides is hard to verify and inconsistent with lib/slots.ts
body: `checkIfIsAvailable` computes the override offset as `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1`, while `lib/slots.ts` computes an offset as invitee-minus-organizer. The two use different conventions for the same override, which makes the shifted override windows in the two code paths disagree and is a likely source of the timezone bug the PR claims to fix.

title: New timezone test does not exercise the reported bug or the fixed-host round-robin case
body: The added test only checks that the same UTC slots are returned for a +6:00 invitee, with the comment saying the result should match UTC. It does not cover an organizer timezone different from the schedule timezone, a round-robin event with a fixed host override, or a busy calendar event that should block a slot on an override day. The round-robin fixed-host behaviour and the busy-time bypass introduced in slots.ts are not tested.

title: update action renders without saving anything
body: The `update` action never reads params or persists changes; it just re-renders the embedding. The admin page's saveChanges calls `embedding.update({})` against this PUT route, so any submitted changes are silently discarded while the client sees success.

title: update/destroy crash with NoMethodError on unknown id
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: ...).first` can return nil; `save_host(host)` then calls `host.host=` and `host.destroy` on nil, raising a 500 instead of a 404.

title: Category is silently reset to uncategorized when omitted on update
body: save_host unconditionally assigns category_id from params and falls back to uncategorized when blank, so any update that doesn't send category_id moves the host to the uncategorized category.

title: before_validation mutates nil host and mutates in place
body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when host is nil (e.g. a create request with no host param), and `sub!` mutates the string in place, which can affect frozen or shared strings. The presence validation is never reached because the callback crashes first.

title: Host lookup is case-insensitive only on the stored side, and host with port is not matched
body: record_for_host compares `lower(host)` against `uri.host`, which drops any port. Hosts stored with a port (the validator allows `:port`) can never match, and the stored value is never normalized to lowercase, so mixed-case input is handled inconsistently.

title: Topic created with nil category when no host matches
body: `eh.try(:category_id)` passes nil when the URL has no matching EmbeddableHost, so PostCreator falls back to defaults instead of the previous embed_category behaviour; import of a URL from a host not in the list is also not guarded by any host check at this point.

title: Referer host check bypassed by a host with no records but dev admin
body: The ensure_embeddable check is skipped entirely for development admins, and the removed 'embeddable hosts not set' guard means an empty table now only relies on host_allowed?; combined with the lenient record_for_host this loosens the embed origin restriction compared with the previous behaviour.

title: Migration SQL injection and fragile category lookup
body: Host values from the existing site setting are interpolated directly into INSERT SQL without escaping, so a value containing a single quote breaks the migration or injects SQL. Also `[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError when no row matches, and `category_id == 0` is used as a sentinel for not found.

title: cmd_tuples check on SELECT result is wrong API usage
body: cmd_tuples is meant for write commands; for a SELECT the row count is available via ntuples/num_tuples. The guard is unreliable and should be replaced with a row count check.

title: Removal of embeddable_hosts setting breaks plugins and existing callers
body: The `allows_embeddable_host?` method and the `embeddable_hosts`/`embed_category` settings are removed without a compatibility shim, while topic.rb, topic_embed.rb and other callers are updated only in this diff; any other code still calling SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts will raise.

title: Category save uses Category.findById result that may be nil
body: After saving, `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(...))` is set without checking the category exists, so a stale or nil category id leaves the badge rendering broken; also the save() props only include 'host' from buffered, so buffered changes to other fields are dropped.

title: saveChanges sends an empty update, so the Save action does nothing
body: `this.get('embedding').update({})` sends no data, so there's no way to persist anything from the embedding page; combined with the server-side no-op update, the page's save path is non-functional.

title: Controller specs only check inheritance, no behaviour tested
body: The new admin controller specs only assert the class inherits from AdminController. create, update, destroy and the category fallback are untested, which is why the update/destroy nil and category reset bugs go unnoticed. The same applies to embedding_controller_spec.

title: Unused local variables reintroduced in for_digest specs
body: The diff removes unused `topic =` assignments in these examples, which is fine, but the expandable_first_post? block was restructured so that the 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test no longer clearly isolates the missing-host case.

title: update action does not apply any changes
body: The update action just re-renders the embedding serializer and never reads params or saves anything. The client calls embedding.update({}) and the admin UI appears to save while nothing is persisted. Changes made in the embedding admin page are silently discarded.

title: destroy and update crash on unknown id
body: EmbeddableHost.where(id:).first can return nil; host.destroy and save_host(host) then raise NoMethodError and produce a 500 instead of a 404 for a missing or already-deleted host.

title: category_id blank fallback and uncategorized handling
body: save_host sets category_id from params and falls back to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id when blank, but does not validate that the category exists. A non-existent category id is saved, and TopicEmbed.import then passes it to PostCreator, which can create topics in a missing category.

title: before_validation mutates host with sub! and fails on nil
body: self.host.sub! raises NoMethodError when host is nil (e.g. a create request without host param). It also mutates the string in place, which can affect frozen or shared strings. Use a nil guard and non-bang assignments.

title: record_for_host lookup does not normalize stored host
body: The lookup compares lower(host) with the URI host, but the stored host can include a port (validator allows :port) while uri.host excludes it, so hosts with ports never match. Also the port in the referer is silently ignored, which may allow unintended matches.

title: host validation regex forbids valid hosts and host uniqueness is not enforced
body: No uniqueness validation exists on host, so duplicate entries can be created; record_for_host then picks an arbitrary one (first without order), making the associated category nondeterministic.

title: migration crashes when embed_category setting is missing and inserts unescaped values
body: execute(...)[0]['id'] raises NoMethodError when no matching category exists (nil[0]). Also host values from the embeddable_hosts setting are interpolated into SQL without escaping, so a value containing a quote breaks the migration or allows SQL injection during migration.

title: embeddable_hosts check uses cmd_tuples on a result and migration is irreversible
body: The migration uses a conditional on cmd_tuples from a SELECT, and the change method has no reverse for the deleted site settings, so rollback loses the hosts and category configuration.

title: imports ignore category when no embeddable host matches
body: eh.try(:category_id) yields nil when no host matches, so PostCreator gets a nil category and topics fall back to defaults, replacing the old embed_category fallback silently. The uncategorized fallback behavior was lost.

title: host check now trusts any referer matching a DB row without a referer guard
body: The old code rejected empty embeddable_hosts with a specific message; the new check only calls host_allowed?(request.referer). Since referer may be nil, URI(nil) raises which is rescued only for InvalidURIError, so a nil referer may raise a TypeError rather than a clean InvalidAccess.

title: category lookup uses categoryId which may be stale on save failure path
body: host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId)) runs after save; findById may return undefined for a category not loaded, setting category to undefined and clearing the badge, while the record was saved with that id.

title: delete ignores failure
body: destroyRecord().then has no catch, so an AJAX failure leaves the UI in an inconsistent state with no error shown; other actions use popupAjaxError.

title: saveChanges calls update with empty attrs against the non-persisting endpoint
body: saveChanges calls embedding.update({}) which PUTs no data; combined with the controller that ignores input, the Save action does nothing for users.

title: basePath replace only replaces first underscore
body: type.replace('_', '-') only replaces the first underscore; multi-underscore type names will not match ADMIN_MODELS. Use a global regex.

title: embedding edit label is lowercase and unused in templates
body: The 'edit' key is added but the template uses an icon-only button, so the string is unused, and the 'Post to Category' label wording is inconsistent with other admin strings.

title: expandable_first_post test asserts the wrong condition
body: The 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test no longer deletes or clears any host; it only passes because no host exists in the test, so it does not test what its name says.

title: describe name refers to removed method
body: The describe block name 'allows_embeddable_host' refers to removed API; also no test covers port handling, referer with path, or the nil/invalid URL cases of record_for_host.

title: category fabricators were deleted from the category fabricator file
body: The file now only defines :embeddable_host, removing :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators. Many existing specs (topic_spec etc.) use Fabricate(:category) and will fail; the content was moved to a file named embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, which is the reverse of the intent.

title: Admin embeddable hosts controller has no authorization on destroy/update lookup and uses unchecked nil
body: The update and destroy actions look up the host with EmbeddableHost.where(id:).first and never check for nil. A request for a non-existent id causes a NoMethodError (500) on host.destroy or save_host. Also the ensure_staff filter is inherited but the create/update path assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host] without a nil check, so a request missing the embeddable_host key raises a 500 instead of a 400/404.

title: Embedding update action does not persist anything
body: The update action just re-renders the serialized embedding and never saves changes. The admin UI calls embedding.update({}) expecting changes to be saved, but nothing is persisted, so the 'Save' path silently discards data. Host edits go through the separate embeddable_hosts resource, so this endpoint is effectively a no-op.

title: before_validation mutates host with sub! which fails on nil
body: self.host.sub! is called on the host attribute without a nil check. If host is nil (e.g. a POST without a host param, since save_host assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host] directly), this raises NoMethodError instead of producing a validation error. The sub! also mutates the string in place, which can alter frozen or shared strings.

title: Host lookup lowercases only the stored column comparison, not the input host
body: record_for_host compares lower(host) to the raw uri.host without downcasing it. A referer or embed URL with uppercase letters (e.g. http://EvilTrout.com/page) will not match a stored host, so it is rejected, while the stored value is normalized to lowercase only in the query. Downcase the input host before querying.

title: Category falls back to nil silently when no embeddable host matches
body: category: eh.try(:category_id) passes nil when the URL host has no EmbeddableHost record, and the migration/allow-list logic no longer uses a configured default category. PostCreator then places the topic in the default category handling rather than failing, and the record_for_host lookup for a URL with a path or port may differ from the host check in EmbedController, so imports can land in unexpected categories.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting is absent
body: The query selecting category id from embed_category uses [0]['id'] on the result. If no matching row exists, [0] is nil and ['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration on installs that never set embed_category. Also the host values are interpolated directly into SQL without escaping, so a host containing a quote breaks the migration or allows SQL injection from existing setting data.

title: Saved category is set from a possibly stale id and the new-host flow is broken
body: After save, host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(...)) runs, but for a newly created host, the buffered host value is not reflected in the record, and cancel() on a new record calls deleteHost without removing server state. Also save() passes props including only 'host' via getProperties, so category_id from categoryId is merged but the rollback on error is never performed.

title: Type normalization replaces only the first underscore
body: type.replace('_', '-') only replaces the first underscore, so a type with multiple underscores will not match ADMIN_MODELS. Use a global replace or normalize consistently.

title: Test asserts expandable behavior that was changed without covering the new contract
body: The expandable_first_post? tests were restructured, but the removed case that checks behaviour when embeddable hosts are absent is now only covered by a test that creates no host with a misnamed describe ('emeddable'). The embed_truncate-only path (no host) is not clearly asserted after the SiteSetting change, leaving the new contract untested.

title: Embedding host label reads incorrectly
body: The 'host' label 'Allowed Hosts' and the 'edit' string are lowercase while sibling keys are capitalized; the confirm_delete text says 'that host' without naming it. Minor, but the strings are user-facing in the admin UI.

title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently replaces the max_width/max_height version
body: The PR adds `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` while the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 is still present. In Ruby the later definition overwrites the earlier one, so the 5-argument form (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) now raises ArgumentError. Any existing caller using that signature breaks. Only one of the two signatures should remain, or the callers should be updated and the old one removed.

title: Animated downsize passes a percentage to gifsicle --resize-fit
body: The controller calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)`. For animated GIFs (when allow_animated_thumbnails is on), `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which emits `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. `--resize-fit` expects a WxH geometry, not a percentage, so the command will fail. `convert_with` then returns false silently, and the oversized GIF is uploaded anyway.

title: Downsize failures are ignored and oversized images are uploaded silently
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false on failure (convert_with swallows errors and returns false), but the return value is ignored. The loop runs at most 5 times and then falls through to `Upload.create_for` regardless of whether the file is still above max_image_size_kb. The user gets no error, and an image that exceeds the configured limit is stored. The loop should stop on a failed conversion and reject or report the upload if the file is still too large.

title: Remote URL download limit no longer follows the max_image_size_kb setting
body: The download size cap was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. Admins who lower the setting will now have URL uploads accepted up to 10MB, and the setting is no longer enforced for this path. The image-downsizing change does not require this change to the cap, so the regression is unnecessary.

title: Client-side size check ignores the per-type site settings
body: `validateUploadedFile` previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. It now hardcodes 10MB for every upload type, so `max_attachment_size_kb` and `max_image_size_kb` are no longer respected by the client. Admin limits are bypassed in the UI, and attachments can be accepted up to 10MB even when the site caps them lower. The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hardcoding problem.

title: 413 error message hardcodes 10 MB instead of the configured limit
body: The 413 branch now reports a fixed 10 MB limit instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. The displayed limit can be wrong for any site that has configured a different value, so the user is told the wrong maximum.

title: Commit/PR description is a placeholder
body: The PR description is just "Test 1" and does not explain the new behavior, the setting interaction, or the hardcoded 10MB change. A maintainer cannot review the intent or the regression risks from it.

title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently replaces the max_width/max_height variant
body: The PR adds a 4-argument `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` while the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 is still present.
