In Ruby the later definition wins, so the 5-argument form is gone. Any caller still using `downsize(from, to, w, h, opts)` now raises ArgumentError or passes the wrong arguments. The two methods should be merged into one signature, or the old one removed with all callers checked.

title: Removed `dimensions` helper and changed `optimize` signature without checking other callers
body: `self.dimensions(width, height)` is deleted and `optimize` now takes a preformatted dimensions string. `resize` and `downsize` were updated, but any other caller of `OptimizedImage.optimize`, `OptimizedImage.dimensions`, or the old `downsize` form (in plugins, lib, or specs) will break. The diff does not show such a search.

title: Client-side size limit is hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring the max_*_size_kb site settings
body: validateUploadedFile now uses a fixed 10MB limit instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. This applies to attachments too, so the `max_attachment_size_kb` setting no longer has any effect on the client. Admins who lowered the limit will see files accepted client-side and rejected only later by the server, and admins who raised it will be blocked at 10MB. The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hardcoding. This change is not mentioned in the PR description and is unrelated to downsizing images.

title: Remote download cap changed from max_image_size_kb to a fixed 10MB for all uploads
body: The URL download limit was `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` and is now a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. Remote files are therefore accepted up to 10MB whatever the configured limits, and the change is not described. If the intent is to allow oversized images to be downsized, that should be stated and the limit for non-image files should still be enforced.

title: Downsizing writes the output over its own input file and ignores failures
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` uses the same path as source and destination. ImageMagick reads and writes the same file, which is fragile and can corrupt the upload. `convert_with` returns false on failure, but the return value is ignored, so the loop just retries up to 5 times on an unchanged file. A failed conversion should stop the loop and fall through to a clear error. Writing to a separate temp file and swapping on success would be safer.

title: Downsizing applies to every image type and never checks the result against the limit
body: The loop only tries 5 passes, and after the loop the size is not rechecked. If the image is still over `max_image_size_kb`, the code continues to `Upload.create_for` with no explicit error, so the failure reason is unclear to the user. Also, the 80% scale is applied to non-animated formats such as SVG, where it may do nothing or produce unexpected output.

title: 413 handler reports a fixed 10 MB limit that may not match the server
body: The 413 case now always reports 10 MB, but the server limit comes from site settings and the web server limit is separate. The message can be wrong for the actual configuration.

title: PR description is placeholder text
body: The description is only 'Test 1'. It does not explain the feature, the new 10MB limits, the removal of the site-setting-driven limit on the client, or the signature change to OptimizedImage. Reviewers cannot assess the intended behavior from it.

title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the 4-argument version
body: `self.downsize` is now defined twice: at line 145 as `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` and again at line 149 as `(from, to, dimensions, opts)`. Ruby keeps only the later definition, so the first is dead code and any caller using the `max_width, max_height` form (the original API) now gets a wrong argument mapping: `max_height` lands in `opts` and the call fails or behaves incorrectly. Only the 3-argument form used by uploads_controller works. Remove one definition and keep a single signature.

title: Animated downsize passes a percentage to gifsicle --resize-fit
body: The controller calls `downsize(..., "80%", allow_animation: ...)`. For GIFs, `optimize` routes to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which calls `resize_instructions_animated` and emits `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects a WxH geometry, not a percentage, so the resize fails. `convert_with` returns false, the controller ignores that, and animated GIFs over the limit are never reduced. Animated GIFs need a separate code path or an explicit scale that gifsicle accepts.

title: Downsize loop ignores failure and retries the same conversion up to 5 times
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false when conversion fails (`convert_with` swallows errors), but the loop doesn't check the return value. A failed conversion leaves the file unchanged, so the loop runs all five attempts on identical input, wasting time, and then proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with an oversized file. The loop should stop on failure, and the oversized case should be reported to the user rather than silently accepted. Also, `tempfile.size` may be stale if the tool replaces the file rather than rewriting it in place, so the loop condition needs verification.

title: Client-side size limit now hardcoded to 10MB, removing the per-type site setting
body: The `max_' + type + '_size_kb` site setting lookup was replaced with a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. Admins who configured `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` will see their settings ignored in the browser, which is a regression. The server still enforces its own limits, so the client now disagrees with the configured policy.

title: Client rejects files over 10MB before the server can downsize them
body: The feature is meant to accept large images and shrink them server-side, but this client check rejects any file larger than 10MB before upload. Users uploading large images will still see the error, so the feature is ineffective from the UI. The check needs to allow images above the limit (or skip it for images) to match the server behavior.

title: HTTP 413 message now hardcodes 10MB instead of the configured image limit
body: The 413 branch previously showed `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. It now always displays 10 MB, so the error text can disagree with the actual configured limit that the server enforces.

title: API URL download limit changed from the site setting to a hardcoded 10MB
body: The remote URL download cap was switched from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a fixed `10.megabytes`. This changes the API contract: admins who lowered the image size setting no longer constrain downloads, and the 10MB cap is not configurable.

title: No tests for the new large-image downsize path
body: The change adds automatic downsizing in the upload controller, changes the `OptimizedImage` method signatures, and changes client validation, but the PR includes no specs. Nothing covers the loop, its failure handling, animated GIFs, or the duplicate `downsize` definition.

title: PR description is not meaningful
body: The description is only 'Test 1'. It does not explain the behavior change, the removal of the site-setting-based limits, or the 10MB hardcoding, so reviewers cannot assess the intent.

title: unsubscribe crashes when user has no TopicUser row
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` may return nil (user never interacted with the topic, or is anonymous so current_user is nil). `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError, producing a 500. Also `current_user.id` raises when not logged in, since unsubscribe is in the ensure_logged_in list only for the normal path; the lookup should handle a missing record, e.g. with TopicUser.change.

title: unsubscribe toggles state in a non-idempotent way and ignores the intended action
body: The action flips the notification level: if currently above regular it sets regular, otherwise sets muted. Clicking an email unsubscribe link twice (or a mail client prefetch/scanner following the GET link) will alternate between muted and regular, re-subscribing the user. An unsubscribe link should set muted deterministically.

title: unsubscribe bypasses guardian checks and uses raw params for lookup
body: TopicView.new is built with params[:topic_id] which may be a slug-less id, and the TopicUser update uses params[:topic_id] directly without ensuring the topic is visible to the current user. Notifications are then changed for a topic the user may not be able to see; guardian.ensure_can_see! should be applied.

title: unsubscribe GET is state-changing and exempt from check_xhr and CSRF-protected flow
body: The unsubscribe endpoint mutates state on GET (and skip_before_filter :check_xhr is added), so any third-party page can trigger a muted change through an image or link for logged-in users (CSRF-like). Mutations should require POST or a signed token.

title: unsubscribe_url is hardcoded to the topic path and ignores the post number and slug
body: unsubscribe_url builds "#{url}/unsubscribe" from url(), which uses the current slug. Routes also add "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" but the mailer now emits the slug form with `url` which may be a stale slug; the value is not validated against the actual route in the email, and the user_notifications path passes this URL into an email whose unsubscribe_link i18n key is also used by digest emails that do not provide unsubscribe_url, potentially rendering a broken %{unsubscribe_url} placeholder.

title: unsubscribe_link now references %{unsubscribe_url} for all emails
body: The shared unsubscribe_link string now contains %{unsubscribe_url}. Emails that add the unsubscribe link without passing unsubscribe_url (e.g. digest, admin or other MessageBuilder users with add_unsubscribe_link) will hit I18n interpolation errors or emit the literal placeholder text.

title: html template still uses %{unsubscribe_link} placeholder instead of the new per-topic link text
body: The template keeps only the generic %{unsubscribe_link} placeholder; the per-topic link text was added to the text/locale only, so the HTML email never shows the topic-specific unsubscribe option. Also `%{respond_instructions}` is now inside a div that previously had line breaks, which changes rendering but is minor.

title: misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText
body: The property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (extra 'i'), and the template references the same misspelling, so it works internally but the name is a typo that will confuse future maintainers and any other references.

title: unsubscribe strings contain HTML and unclear copy
body: stop_notifications contains raw <strong> markup inside a client string rendered with triple-stash in the template; the change_notification_state string lacks a trailing period, inconsistent with the other messages. Also the diff removes a blank line from an unrelated section.

title: unrelated formatting churn in topic_user.rb
body: Large whitespace and reformatting changes (scope, create_lookup, track_visit!) are unrelated to the unsubscribe feature and make review harder without functional benefit.

title: no tests for unsubscribe controller action or per-topic unsubscribe link
body: The only test change adds an unsubscribe_url option to a builder spec. No request spec covers the new TopicsController#unsubscribe action (mute/regular toggle, redirect, slug mismatch, anonymous access), and the message builder spec does not assert that the body contains the topic unsubscribe URL.

title: unsubscribe action crashes for users without a TopicUser record
body: TopicUser.find_by may return nil when the user has never interacted with the topic (e.g., an email link clicked by a user who was notified but has no row). `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a graceful response.

title: unsubscribe is a state-changing GET reachable without login and without CSRF protection
body: The unsubscribe route is a GET that mutates notification_level, and ensure_logged_in is applied, but current_user is nil for anonymous requests, so current_user.id raises. More importantly, state-changing GET requests are triggered by link prefetchers/mail scanners and are CSRF-able; the action also toggles between muted and regular rather than being idempotent, so repeated prefetch flips the setting back and forth.

title: TopicView.new called without guardian scope; access check missing for private topics
body: TopicView is built with current_user but the subsequent update applies to any topic_id the user can construct; if TopicView raises NotFound/InvalidAccess the rescue in show is not present here, so errors leak as unhandled exceptions. Also no check that the topic is visible to the user before mutating its TopicUser.

title: Toggle logic inverts intent and can unmute/stop incorrectly
body: If notification_level is above regular (e.g., watching/tracking) it is lowered to regular, otherwise it is set to muted. Clicking the link for a regular user mutes the topic, but for a muted user it stays muted with no way to re-enable via this link; behaviour is unclear and not idempotent for the unsubscribe semantics described in the UI text.

title: Placeholders are no longer wrapped in HTML elements consistently; %{unsubscribe_link} line depends on a template variable never supplied to the ERB
body: The template contains %{respond_instructions} and %{unsubscribe_link} placeholders, which are only substituted in MessageBuilder#html_part when add_unsubscribe_link is set. Any caller rendering this template without that option (or the substitution order) leaves raw %{...} text in the email.

title: unsubscribe_link now always includes the per-topic link, but the plain-text body text is built from the same key
body: The unsubscribe_link string now requires %{unsubscribe_url}. Callers that invoke I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) without unsubscribe_url (e.g., digest emails or other add_unsubscribe_link paths) will get an interpolation error or a literal '%{unsubscribe_url}' in the outgoing text.

title: unsubscribe_url uses post.topic.unsubscribe_url which points at the non-slug-less route with an extra segment
body: Topic#unsubscribe_url returns "#{url}/unsubscribe" where url includes the post number only when >1; for post_number>1 this yields /t/slug/id/5/unsubscribe, which matches no route (the unsubscribe routes are /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe), so the link 404s.

title: Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText
body: The property is spelled 'stopNotificiationsText' here and in the template; while consistent, the typo propagates into the public API of the controller and is easy to break when someone fixes one occurrence only.

title: Strings used in the unsubscribe page are inserted with triple-stash HTML from a translation
body: stop_notifications contains <strong> and the template renders it with {{{...}}} with the topic fancyTitle interpolated unescaped into the I18n string, allowing HTML injection from topic titles into the page.

title: unsubscribe_url may be built from a stale or unslugged url
body: unsubscribe_url interpolates url which includes slug; for topics where slug is recomputed lazily this can differ from the route that the controller redirects to, causing redirect loops with the slug mismatch check.

title: No tests for the new per-topic unsubscribe behaviour in the controller or mailer
body: The only change is to pass unsubscribe_url into a builder spec that never asserts on it. The new TopicsController#unsubscribe action, the redirect logic, the toggle semantics and the new unsubscribe_link text have no specs.

title: unsubscribe action crashes for anonymous users and missing TopicUser rows
body: `unsubscribe` calls `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)` but the route is skipped for login only via before_filter ensure_logged_in (which is listed), so this is OK for logged-in users; however `tu` can be nil when the user has no TopicUser record for the topic (e.g. they were never tracked or the record was never created), and `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError (500). Should use TopicUser.change or handle nil.

title: unsubscribe toggle bypasses TopicUser.change and its side effects
body: The notification level is set by assigning and calling tu.save! directly, instead of TopicUser.change. This skips the MessageBus notification_level_change publish, notifications_changed_at/notifications_reason_id updates, and observer callbacks, so open clients don't update and the reason is not recorded.

title: unsubscribe is a GET with state change and no CSRF protection against link-based toggling
body: The unsubscribe route is GET and mutates notification level, so any link or image embedding the URL can change a user's notification state (and the toggle semantics mean repeated/prefetched requests flip it back and forth). Email link prefetchers can silently toggle the setting. Mutation should happen on POST with confirmation.

title: TopicView.new with no guardian check on topic visibility before mutating
body: unsubscribe builds TopicView for params[:topic_id] using current_user, but it does not verify the user can see the topic before writing a TopicUser row; for private topics the user may still get a TopicUser row created or modified. Also TopicView.new raises NotFound only on missing topic; a missing TopicUser then crashes as noted.

title: Added render :show in format.html block is redundant/inconsistent and changes show behavior
body: Adding an explicit `render :show` inside format.html in perform_show_response is unnecessary for show, and because unsubscribe now also calls perform_show_response, unsubscribe renders the topic show template with the store_preloaded data; this couples the unsubscribe response to the full topic page and the topic route template, which the new unsubscribe Ember route does not expect.

title: unsubscribe_url built from url with post_number absent produces a URL that depends on slug
body: unsubscribe_url uses `url` which includes the slug; the email link is generated at send time and the route `t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` redirects to the correct slug when mismatched, but the non-slug route `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` exists too, so the generated link is fine; however the method is added without any spec, and it is called in user_notifications for every notification email, adding no guard for nil slug (slug falls back to ''), producing `/t//id/unsubscribe`.

title: unsubscribe_link now always includes topic link even when no unsubscribe_url is passed
body: The unsubscribe_link text now references %{unsubscribe_url}, but MessageBuilder#body and html_part call I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) for every email with add_unsubscribe_link, and digest and other emails that do not pass unsubscribe_url will render the placeholder literally or raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument, since the key is not provided. Only notification emails pass unsubscribe_url.

title: Template no longer includes the topic unsubscribe link placeholder in the html part
body: The html notification template uses %{unsubscribe_link} as a placeholder, which is replaced only in MessageBuilder#html_part; that is fine, but the new unsubscribe_link text is rendered as PrettyText markdown inside a div, and the %{unsubscribe_url} placeholder is only interpolated in the text body via I18n, so the HTML version shows an unexpanded or stale topic link. Verify both parts receive the topic-specific URL.

title: unsubscribe_link interpolation may fail for emails without unsubscribe_url
body: html_part and body call I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) whenever add_unsubscribe_link is set. The new locale string requires %{unsubscribe_url}; any caller setting add_unsubscribe_link without unsubscribe_url (e.g. mailing list or other mailers) will raise a missing interpolation error or emit a broken link. Builder should default unsubscribe_url or guard it.

title: Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText
body: The property name is misspelled ('Notificiations'), and the template references the same misspelling; it works but is a maintenance hazard and inconsistent with other names.

title: Route creates a topic record with store.createRecord on every visit
body: model() calls this.store.createRecord('topic', { id }) each time the route is entered, leaving unsaved phantom topic records in the store and the topic is then populated via updateFromJson; repeated visits accumulate records and may collide with the real topic model.

title: didTransition action returns true and sets application footer as side effect
body: The didTransition action is defined under actions but is not triggered by any Ember hook here; it is dead code, and the footer state is never restored when leaving the route.

title: No spec covers the new topic-specific unsubscribe link text or the missing-url path
body: The spec adds unsubscribe_url to the builder, but never checks that the body/html includes the topic unsubscribe URL, nor that builds without unsubscribe_url succeed (which the new locale string would break). No controller spec covers the new unsubscribe action either.

title: Validator increments block statistics on every validation, including the email-only check
body: EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value), which is a side-effecting method that increments match_count and last_match_at and saves the record. Every time a User is validated (including repeated validations on save, or validations that later fail for other reasons), the counter is bumped. The statistics become meaningless and every validation performs a write.

title: should_block? mixes a query with a write and ignores save failures
body: should_block? writes match_count and last_match_at as a side effect of a predicate-named method, using record.save with no check of the result, and without an atomic increment. Concurrent calls lose increments (read-modify-write race), and the method name hides the write. A failed save (e.g. validation on the record) is silently ignored.

title: Email lookup is case-sensitive while users' emails are normalized
body: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) compares the raw string. User emails are downcased via Email.downcase elsewhere in the codebase, and the blocked_emails table stores whatever was entered. An entry 'Bad@Spam.com' will not block 'bad@spam.com', so blocking is trivially bypassed.

title: Blocked-email check is applied to any attribute using the validator
body: The validator is generic (ActiveModel::EachValidator) but the blocked-email lookup runs unconditionally, and the error key is hardcoded to user.email.blocked. Any future use on other attributes will apply the block list and misreport. Also the not_allowed/blocked messages are added to attribute, fine, but the check is coupled to User semantics.

title: Returning user attributes and raw errors in the create response leaks data
body: The failure response now includes values from user.attributes.slice('name','username','email') and the full errors hash. This echoes submitted data back and exposes validation detail (including the blocked-email signal) to unauthenticated callers, which lets anonymous users probe whether an email is blocked via the 'is not allowed.' error, bypassing the generic message.

title: rejectedEmails is populated from result.values.email, which may be undefined
body: pushObject(result.values.email) is guarded only by result.values being truthy. If the server omits email (e.g. the field is absent), undefined is pushed, and the email check then never matches the real address. The entry is also never removed, so a user who corrects a typo stays blocked only for the rejected string, but a legitimately fixed email is still validated correctly; the main issue is the undefined push and unbounded growth of the array.

title: Unique index without a case-normalized value and no email format constraint
body: The unique index on email is case-sensitive, so the same address in different cases can be stored twice, and only one of them would be matched by the case-sensitive lookup. Normalization should happen at write time or in the index expression.

title: Validator spec does not test the whitelist/blacklist behavior it moved
body: The User email_validator and email_in_restriction_setting? logic was moved into EmailValidator, but the new spec only covers blocked emails. Regressions in the whitelist/blacklist domain checks are not caught. The spec also stubs should_block? so the side-effect bug above is never exercised.

title: No test for uniqueness, case handling, or save failure
body: The spec does not verify the uniqueness validation or case-insensitive matching, and does not verify that validation (not just should_block?) leaves match_count unchanged. The 'updates statistics' expectation passes while the validator incorrectly increments counts on each User validation.

title: should_block? has write side effects on every validation and is not atomic
body: should_block? increments match_count and saves the record each time it is called, and it is invoked from the EmailValidator on every validation of the email attribute. Read-only checks therefore perform UPDATEs, and the non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count (record.match_count += 1 then save) loses increments under concurrent signups. Use an atomic update_all/increment or move the statistics update out of the predicate.

title: Email lookup is case sensitive while emails are normalized elsewhere
body: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) does an exact match, but the rest of the code downcases emails (Email.downcase in change_email and find_by_username_or_email). A blocked address stored as lowercase will not block 'Bad@Spam.com', letting the blocked user bypass the block trivially.

title: Blocked-email check runs against nil or non-string values
body: validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value) without guarding against a nil or blank value; the email attribute can be nil if presence validation fails, and the domain check also assumes a string. This can cause a query with nil or an error in the validator chain.

title: Blocked-email check only runs when email changed, and the uniqueness check is now bypassed for validator order
body: The email validator is now declared with if: :email_changed?, and the blocklist check is added inside the validator. Existing users whose addresses are later added to the blocklist are never re-checked, and the presence/uniqueness validations moved to a single line, changing error ordering. Confirm the intended behaviour for already-registered users.

title: Create response leaks submitted values and error details to the client
body: The failure response now returns user.errors.to_hash and user.attributes.slice(...) which includes the submitted email. Combined with the blocklist, this lets a client probe the blocklist by seeing which errors are returned, and the change is unrelated to the stated purpose. The error payload should be limited to what the client needs.

title: rejectedEmails stores server-supplied email and never clears it
body: The rejectedEmails array is populated from result.values.email whenever the server reports an email error, and entries are never removed. If the user corrects the email to something else, the validation still uses contains() on the list, and a blocked email that the server rejected is rejected client-side permanently for the session. Also, the array is shared on the prototype via Em.A, which is a per-controller-instance concern only if constructed per instance.

title: action_type column has no default, and the model has no DB-level guard for it
body: action_type is null: false with no default; the default is supplied only by a before_validation callback. Inserts that bypass validation (update_all, raw SQL, or fixtures) will fail or the enum will be invalid. Consider a DB default.

title: Validator spec does not cover whitelist/blacklist behaviour or unchanged blocked-email path
body: The spec only stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and never exercises the whitelist/blacklist branches it was moved from, nor the case where a non-string or nil value is passed. Tests of the moved logic were removed from the User spec without equivalent coverage here.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so case variants bypass the block
body: should_block? does an exact `where(email: email)` match, and the uniqueness validation on BlockedEmail is also case-sensitive. User emails are normalized with Email.downcase elsewhere in the codebase (find_by_username_or_email, change_email), but blocked entries are stored and matched as typed. An entry for 'bad@spamclub.com' will not match 'Bad@SpamClub.com', so a blocked address can register by changing its case. Normalize both the stored value and the lookup (e.g. downcase), or use a case-insensitive comparison.

title: Validator has a side effect: every validation increments blocked match stats
body: EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value), which writes match_count and last_match_at on each call. Validations run on every valid? / save, including repeated calls within one request, failed saves for unrelated reasons, and the validation in change_email paths. The statistics therefore count validation attempts rather than actual blocked registrations, and every validation issues a write. Validation should be read-only; the counter update belongs in the actual registration path.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count loses increments
body: should_block? loads the record, does `match_count += 1` in Ruby, and calls save. Concurrent signups with the same blocked email race and lose updates. The save also runs validations, so if validation fails the counter silently is not persisted. Use an atomic SQL update such as BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?') or update_counters, which skips validations.

title: Whitelist/blacklist domain logic moved here without any spec coverage
body: The domain whitelist/blacklist checks were moved from User into EmailValidator, and the old email_validator behaviour is now only exercised by this file's two blocked-email examples. Nothing tests that email_domains_whitelist / email_domains_blacklist still reject addresses, nor that a blocked email is also rejected when it is on a whitelisted domain. The case-sensitivity bug above is also untested.

title: Referer host check is the only access control and is trivially spoofable
body: ensure_embeddable trusts request.referer to decide whether the embed endpoint may be served, and then sets X-Frame-Options to ALLOWALL. Referer headers are client-controlled and can be stripped or forged by non-browser clients, so any caller can fetch the embed page. Combined with ALLOWALL, the page can be framed from any origin. The check gates only on referer, not on a shared secret or origin validation.

title: Anonymous requests enqueue retrieve jobs without throttle bypass and can trigger remote fetches
body: Every request to best without an existing TopicEmbed enqueues a retrieve_topic job with an arbitrary embed_url. TopicRetriever only throttles per URL via redis setnx, so an attacker can enumerate many distinct URLs on the embeddable host to cause unbounded remote HTTP fetches and job queue growth.

title: Port handling in absolutize_urls is wrong for non-default ports and scheme
body: prefix appends the port unless it is 80 or 443 regardless of scheme, and uri.port for an https URL on port 80 or http on 443 is wrongly dropped/kept. More importantly the prefix is built with string << on a fresh string each call, which is fine, but the scheme check is missing: URLs with other schemes are not constrained here. The main consequence is incorrect absolute links for some URL/port combinations.

title: import mutates the caller's contents string and interpolates unescaped title/url into HTML
body: contents << ... modifies the string passed in by the caller (PollFeed passes i.content which is then reused), and the url is interpolated unescaped into an href inside HTML that is stored as raw_html and rendered without cooking, creating a stored XSS vector if the URL contains quotes. Since cook_method raw_html skips sanitization, feed content is stored and displayed verbatim.

title: Raw HTML from remote feeds/pages is stored with raw_html cook method, skipping sanitization
body: Post.cook returns raw when cook_method is raw_html, so remote content (RSS items or fetched pages via Readability, which is only partially whitelisted and not applied to feed content) is rendered unsanitized into the forum and served to readers, enabling stored XSS from any imported feed.

title: i.content may be nil and scrub is called on it
body: SimpleRSS items without a content element return nil for i.content, so i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole poll loop, skipping all remaining feed items.

title: open() of a URL uses Kernel#open which can execute commands or read local files
body: open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) with a string relies on Kernel#open, which in older Ruby interprets pipe-prefixed strings as shell commands and otherwise reads local files. Use URI.open/open-uri explicitly or a safer fetch.

title: embeddable_host comparison is case sensitive and ignores port
body: invalid_host? compares SiteSetting.embeddable_host to URI(...).host exactly, so a host with different case (Eviltrout.com) is rejected, and the controller's referer check does the same. Inconsistent with browser host semantics and may reject valid embeds.

title: Disqus import now fetches each thread's remote page and discards the post's per-comment creation
body: The import replaces PostCreator creation of a permalink post with TopicEmbed.import_remote, which fetches the live page over HTTP. Dry-run and offline imports now depend on network access, and the blank line left behind plus the removed category option break the documented CLI interface (the -c option is removed without replacement).

title: cook_method check returns raw content without any escaping for all raw_html posts
body: cook short-circuits to return raw for raw_html posts, bypassing Plugin::Filter :after_post_cook hooks and any sanitization. Combined with cook being called in before_create_tasks, posts created this way are never filtered by plugins.

title: skip_validations now changes save behaviour for all revisions, and return value is ignored
body: update_post calls @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) and ignores the result. Previously the same save ran, but with validations skipped on imported posts, rate-limit and spam validations bypass is now possible; the failed save is also silently ignored, so revise! returns true even when the post failed to save.

title: force: true on create_table will drop existing top_topics data on migration
body: Adding force: true makes the migration drop and recreate the top_topics table if it already exists, destroying any existing rows. Migrations that have already run are unaffected, but on a DB where the table exists this silently wipes data.

title: Adding NOT NULL column with default to large posts table rewrites the table
body: add_column with default and null: false on Postgres of older versions rewrites the whole posts table under an exclusive lock, which can block a production forum for a long time.

title: request.referer interpolated into a JavaScript string literal
body: The referer is inserted into a script string without JavaScript escaping. A referer containing a quote or newline breaks out of the string and injects script. Use json or escape_javascript and validate the origin.

title: Success assertions placed in after hook and error tests use weak checks
body: The response assertions are in an after block, so they run after each example rather than as part of it, and the tests are not checking the rendered behaviour for the loading case. Failures are reported confusingly and the 404 test does not verify the status.

title: Spec does not cover the update path's content_sha1 handling or the no-change case
body: The 'Supports updating the post' test does not assert the embed record's content_sha1 was updated nor that unchanged content skips revision, so regressions in the update logic would pass.

title: import mutates caller's contents string and re-appends footer on every call
body: `contents << ...` mutates the string passed in by the caller. In PollFeed the same `content` string is passed directly; in import_remote, doc.content is passed. On repeated imports of the same object or retries, the footer is appended again, and the sha1 computed afterwards changes every run, so the 'content changed' check always triggers a revision even when the source is unchanged.

title: Unescaped URL interpolated into HTML footer
body: The embed url is interpolated into an HTML anchor without escaping (`#{url}`). Feed items or embed URLs containing quote or angle-bracket characters can inject markup into the post, which is stored with cook_method raw_html and rendered unsanitized.

title: raw_html cook method bypasses sanitization for all posts with that method
body: cook returns raw content unfiltered when cook_method is raw_html, and the imported feed/embed content from remote sites is stored this way. This skips the Plugin::Filter and the pretty_text sanitizer entirely, so remote-sourced HTML (scripts, event handlers) is rendered on the forum for all viewers. Any remote page with script tags is an XSS vector.

title: Throttle key set with setnx then expire is non-atomic and can leave keys without TTL
body: If the process dies between setnx and expire, the key persists forever, permanently throttling retrieval of that URL. Use `set` with `ex`/`nx` options atomically.

title: open() on user-configured URL and no timeout or error handling
body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with Kernel#open allows command execution if the value begins with a pipe in older Ruby, and has no timeout. A slow or hung feed blocks the scheduled job indefinitely. Also `i.content` may be nil for feeds without content, causing NoMethodError on `scrub` and aborting the whole poll.

title: Nil content from feed items crashes the entire poll
body: `i.content.scrub` is called without checking presence; an item without a content element raises NoMethodError, aborting processing of all remaining feed items in the loop.

title: Referer check is the only protection and sets ALLOWALL on every response
body: The embed endpoint sets X-Frame-Options to ALLOWALL (not a valid value; browsers ignore it) and relies only on the Referer header, which is optional and easily spoofed or stripped. The check also raises for requests with no referer, but the embedded page is reachable directly. Framing permission is effectively unrestricted for any site that can supply the referer header.

title: Anonymous requests can enqueue unthrottled retrieval jobs
body: best enqueues a :retrieve_topic job for any embed_url; TopicRetriever throttles only per URL via redis, and the job can trigger fetching arbitrary remote URLs (SSRF-like outbound requests) for anonymous visitors, with an unbounded URL space.

title: request.referer interpolated into JavaScript string
body: The referer is inserted raw into a JS string literal inside a script tag. A referer containing a quote or closing script sequence can break out of the string; it is also used as the postMessage target origin, which is weak if the value is unexpected.

title: post.cooked rendered with raw
body: Cooked content from raw_html posts is output with `raw` without any sanitization; combined with the raw_html path this emits remote HTML unescaped into the page.

title: Origin check uses substring indexOf, allowing bypass
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, so an attacker origin that is a substring of discourseUrl (e.g. a short host or 'https://') passes. Also the empty origin passes. Should compare parsed origins for equality.

title: Disqus import now fetches remote pages and drops the category option
body: The import replaces PostCreator with TopicEmbed.import_remote, which fetches each thread's link over HTTP instead of using the exported XML content, and the category option is removed without replacement. The import silently changes behavior and the removed option is still referenced in documentation.

title: Adding a NOT NULL column with default on large posts table locks the table
body: add_column with default and null: false rewrites the full posts table on PostgreSQL versions before 11, holding an exclusive lock during deploy on large forums.

title: force: true drops existing top_topics data on migration
body: Changing create_table to force: true means running this migration drops and recreates the table if it exists, silently deleting existing data. Editing an already-applied migration also does not re-run on existing installs.

title: create_table with force: true in topic_embeds migration destroys data
body: force: true drops any existing topic_embeds table on migrate; on rerun after production use, all embed mappings are lost, and duplicate topics would be created on the next import.

title: Race condition creates duplicate embeds and topics
body: The find-then-create in import is not protected by a lock or by the unique index; concurrent jobs for the same URL (retrieve_topic and poll_feed) can both create a topic and post, and the second TopicEmbed.create! raises a unique violation after the topic is already created, leaving an orphan topic.

title: Update path ignores post cooking and embed url changes
body: On update, revise! is called with contents that were not cooked the same way and the embed title is never updated; title changes from the feed are silently ignored.

title: Update test does not verify the existing embed/post is updated
body: 'Supports updating the post' only checks that cooked matches new contents; it doesn't assert the same post id or a single TopicEmbed row, so duplicate creation would pass the test.

title: Spec asserts response is not success but description says 404
body: The test 'is 404 without an embed_url' only checks should_not be_success, so it would pass on any error, and the success-path after hook asserts on responses for examples that never set a response, making failures confusing.

title: Feed polling and embed settings lack validation and default off-safety
body: embeddable_host is not validated as a bare host; a misconfigured value of an arbitrary host lets any site embed the forum. feed_polling_url accepts arbitrary URLs fetched server-side without restriction.

title: user.try(:staff?) returns nil for anonymous users and staff bypass not enforced for jobs
body: no_throttle is passed as nil when no user is found, which is fine, but the job runs TopicRetriever which then fetches the remote URL for any staff member's request without a per-URL limit; combined with no-throttle, staff requests can hammer remote sites.

title: Unescaped URL interpolated into HTML and stored raw
body: The embed_url is interpolated directly into an HTML anchor (`#{url}`) and the contents are stored with cook_method raw_html, so the post body is rendered without sanitization. A feed item link containing a quote or markup (e.g. `'>

title: Raw HTML from remote feeds/pages stored and rendered without sanitization
body: Posts created by import use cook_method raw_html, so `Post#cook` returns the raw content unchanged. Content comes from remote RSS feeds or fetched third-party pages (import_remote uses Readability output, but PollFeed passes `i.content` directly). Script or event-handler markup from an untrusted source is rendered to all viewers of the topic and in the embed iframe, a stored XSS vector.

title: open() of user-configured URL with Kernel#open allows command injection on old Rubies and no timeout
body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Kernel#open, which on Ruby versions before 3.0 treats strings starting with '|' as shell commands. The URL is an admin setting, but it also has no timeout, so a hung feed server blocks the scheduled job indefinitely. Use URI.open or a Net::HTTP call with timeouts.

title: Kernel#open on a fetched URL in import_remote
body: `open(url).read` is used on an URL that comes from embed requests (TopicRetriever passes the embed_url from an unauthenticated controller parameter, validated only by host). Kernel#open with a crafted string and no timeout can hang or execute commands on old Rubies, and the fetch has no size or time limit.

title: Anonymous requests can enqueue unbounded retrieve jobs
body: For any unknown embed_url, `best` enqueues a :retrieve_topic job for every request. The throttle is applied only inside the job (retrieved_recently? via redis), so a flood of distinct URLs on the embeddable host queues an unbounded number of jobs, each performing an outbound HTTP fetch.

title: Referer check is spoofable and frame-embedding is allowed to all origins
body: The embed endpoint authorizes access solely by the Referer header host, which is client controlled and may be stripped. Combined with `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` and the postMessage target built from request.referer in the layout, the content can be framed by anyone who sets the referer. The layout's postMessage with an unvalidated referer string also leaks the target origin.

title: request.referer interpolated into JavaScript without escaping
body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` is placed inside a script literal. ERB HTML-escapes but a referer containing a single quote or backslash-sequence is not JS-escaped, so the value can break out of the string literal in the inline script.

title: Origin check uses substring indexOf, so it can be bypassed
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` checks whether the message origin is a substring of the forum URL, not equal to it. An origin such as 'http://a' or an empty/short string matches a substring of the forum URL and passes, letting other pages set the iframe height. The check should compare the origin for equality.

title: Port handling drops explicit default ports inconsistently and prefix may be built on nil host
body: `uri.host` is nil for URLs without a host, and the `prefix << ':port'` line mutates a string that may be frozen in some configurations. Also non-default ports on https (443 check only applies to one scheme) produce wrong absolute URLs for http on 443 or https on 80.

title: contents mutated in place with <<
body: `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string. In PollFeed, `content` is built once per item and reused; in TopicRetriever/import_remote the doc.content string is mutated, and the sha1 comparison on re-import now includes the footer added each time, so the footer is appended on every import call to the same string object.

title: Throttle key set with setnx then expire is non-atomic
body: setnx followed by a separate expire can leave the key without a TTL if the process dies between calls, permanently throttling that URL. Use SET with NX and EX in one command.

title: user.try(:staff?) passes nil when no user, but args may be a Sidekiq hash with string keys
body: Jobs are serialized through Sidekiq, so args keys become strings after serialization in some paths; `args[:user_id]` and `args[:embed_url]` may be nil, causing the InvalidParameters raise or silently skipping the user lookup.

title: Disqus import no longer applies category option and removes the option entirely
body: The --category option was deleted and the category handling removed, but the import now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote which fetches each thread's live URL instead of creating topics from the XML data. Imports now depend on network access to the old site and ignore the Disqus message content, a behavior change not reflected in the description or help text.

title: raw_html posts skip the cooking pipeline and plugin filters entirely
body: cook returns raw when cook_method is raw_html, bypassing Plugin::Filter :after_post_cook and all sanitization. Any post set to this method, including ones edited later, is stored unsanitized, and the before_save hook also calls cook so edits reuse raw content. Combined with the import path this is a security regression across the whole post model.

title: Adding NOT NULL column with default rewrites entire posts table
body: add_column with default and null: false on a large posts table locks and rewrites every row in PostgreSQL on older versions, blocking writes during deploy on large forums.

title: Unique index on embed_url with no length guard for string column
body: embed_url is a varchar with no length limit, and a unique btree index on long URLs can exceed PostgreSQL's index row size limit, causing inserts of long embed URLs to fail with an error that is not handled in TopicEmbed.import.

title: force: true on create_table will drop existing top_topics data
body: Adding force: true means that rerunning or running this migration on an installation where the table exists silently drops and recreates it, deleting all TopTopic rows without any warning.

title: save with skip_validations silently ignores failures
body: `@post.save(validate: ...)` return value is ignored, so a failed save (for example a validation error when skip_validations is false) leaves the in-memory post changed and save_reply_relationships still runs, and the caller receives true from revise!. Errors go unreported.

title: embeddable_host and feed settings exposed without validation
body: embeddable_host is an unvalidated string used as the sole referer check and also to decide which hosts to fetch from. No default validation or type constraint exists, so an admin mistake (e.g. a bare wildcard or empty string on a site that does not set it) can open the embed endpoint to any host.

title: Success assertions run in an after hook and do not verify the behaviour under test
body: The `after` block asserts response success and headers, but after blocks in the success context also run for the test that expects TopicRetriever and for the TopicView test where render behaviour differs. Failures are reported confusingly and the tests do not check that the loading template is rendered on the retrieve path.

title: No test for security-relevant behavior: HTML injection through URL and raw content
body: The spec asserts raw_html rendering but never tests that the embed URL is escaped in the footer or that script content is neutralized. The security regressions introduced by raw_html storage are unchecked.

title: PollFeed item processing and error paths are untested
body: Only the guard conditions and delegation are tested. poll_feed (parsing items, falling back to i.id, CGI unescaping, import) has no coverage, and the spec requires an unrelated process_post job file.

title: Removing the `.title` float rule may break the header title layout
body: The `.title { float: left; }` rule is deleted outright and nothing replaces it, while `.contents` becomes a flex container. Any header markup still using the `.title` class loses its float and will be positioned by flex rules it was never designed for. The PR does not show that the class is unused, so the header title layout is at risk.

title: `.panel` float removed and replaced with flex ordering without verification
body: `.panel` changes from `float: right` to `margin-left: auto` plus `order(3)`. This only works if `.panel` is a direct flex child of `.contents`. If it is nested under another wrapper, the float is removed with no equivalent layout, and the header can shift in ways the PR does not account for.

title: Bullet badge margin rule removed from extra-info wrapper without replacement
body: The `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule inside `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper` is deleted. Bullet badges in this wrapper lose their 5px top offset, which changes their vertical alignment. The diff also adds an unrelated `line-height: 1.5` to the same wrapper, which is not explained.

title: Small-action description spacing reduced without clear justification
body: `.small-action-desc` padding changes from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`, the `margin-top: 5px` is dropped, and the nested `p` margin and padding are changed as well. The left indent of 4em that reserves room for the avatar is removed, so the text can overlap the `.topic-avatar` column. These are visible layout changes with no supporting description or test.

title: `align-items` mixin emits a non-existent `-ms-align-items` property
body: `-ms-align-items` is not a real vendor-prefixed property, so the declaration is dropped by browsers and is dead output. `-webkit-box-align` also accepts only box-model values, so the mixin is misleading for the flexbox intent. The mixin should emit only valid properties.

title: PR description is empty and the title does not match the changes
body: The description reads only 'Test 5', so reviewers get no rationale for the layout changes. The title claims a performance optimization, but the diff is a visual layout rewrite (float to flexbox, spacing and margin changes) with no measurements or verification of the intended behavior.

title: Removing the .title float rule changes header layout without replacement
body: The diff deletes the `.title { float: left; }` rule from `.d-header .contents` and switches `.contents` to a flex container. Any `.title` element inside the header now loses its left float and is laid out only by flex defaults. Nothing in the PR shows that the markup no longer relies on this, so the header title position may shift or break on pages that render it.

title: Panel float removed and replaced with flex ordering that is not verified
body: `.panel` drops `float: right` and gains `margin-left: auto` plus `order(3)`. This only works if every sibling in `.contents` is a flex item with orders 1 and 2 set correctly. Siblings like `#site-logo` and `.icons` are not given any order, so the final arrangement depends on DOM order and browser support for the old `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` fallback. This needs checking in the rendered header.

title: Bullet margin-top rule removed from extra-info badges with no replacement
body: The `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule is deleted, and nothing else in the diff restores that spacing. Bullet category badges inside the extra-info wrapper will sit flush against the top of the line, a visible regression that the PR does not mention.

title: Small-action description padding and margins changed without explanation
body: `.small-action-desc` changes from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` and `margin-top: 5px` to `padding: 0 1.5%`. The 4em left indent that offset the icon column is gone, and `p` margin and the `> p` padding-top are also dropped. The text will reflow and the vertical rhythm of every small-action post will change. The PR gives no reason for this and no visual check.

title: Floats on children of a new flex container are ignored
body: `.small-action` becomes a flex container, but its children `.topic-avatar` and the `button` (with float: right) keep their float rules. Floated flex items are ignored, so these float declarations no longer do anything. Either the floats are dead code or the layout was not checked after the switch to flex.

title: inline-flex mixin emits multiple display values, including a legacy one
body: The `.bullet` rule now uses `@include inline-flex()`, which emits several `display` declarations, including `-webkit-inline-box` and `-moz-inline-box` alongside `inline-flex`. Browsers that do not understand `inline-flex` fall back to the legacy value, which can change the badge box model in old browsers. The previous single declaration did not have this effect.

title: align-items mixin emits invalid property and passes unsupported values to legacy box-align
body: `-ms-align-items` is not a real CSS property and is ignored. `-webkit-box-align` only accepts values like start, center, end, baseline, and stretch, so passing a flex-specific value such as flex-start through this mixin produces an invalid legacy declaration. The mixin also sets `-ms-flex-align`, which is the correct IE property, so the extra line is just dead output.

title: Mixins added as a block after existing ones with no check for duplicates
body: The flexbox, inline-flex, align-items and order mixins are appended here. If any of these names already exist in another stylesheet partial (for example the `order` mixin used in topic.scss), Sass silently redefines them, and the later definition wins. Nothing in the PR confirms that the names are unique or that the output of existing callers is unchanged.

title: PR description is a placeholder and the title claims a performance gain
body: The description says only 'Test 5', and the title says the change optimizes header layout performance. The diff is a set of visual layout rewrites with no measurement, no before/after comparison, and no statement of the intended rendering change. A reviewer cannot judge the risk without this context.

title: Removed bullet badge margin-top rule without replacement
body: The `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule is deleted, so bullet badges inside the extra-info wrapper lose their 5px top offset. Nothing in the diff compensates for this, so the bullet alignment in the topic title area will shift. The removal is not explained by the stated flexbox change.

title: order(2) and line-height change have no effect unless the parent is a flex container
body: `@include order(2)` only works on flex or box children. The diff does not make the parent of `.extra-info-wrapper` a flex container, so the ordering is a no-op there. The added `line-height: 1.5` also changes text layout for all content in this wrapper, which the PR does not mention.

title: Header .title float rule removed, layout depends on flex without verification
body: The `.title { float: left; }` rule is removed and `.contents` becomes a flex container, while `.panel` drops `float: right` for `margin-left: auto`. Any element still relying on the removed float or on normal block flow inside `.d-header .contents` will reflow differently. The change is a wholesale layout rewrite with no evidence it was checked across header states (logged in, anon, narrow widths).

title: small-action-desc padding and spacing removed, changes post layout
body: The padding `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` and `margin-top: 5px` are replaced by `padding: 0 1.5%`, and the `p` margin and `> p` padding-top are also removed. The left indent of the small-action text drops from 4em to about 1.5%, and vertical spacing shrinks. These are visual regressions in small-action rows (closed, pinned, etc.), not performance changes.

title: Floats inside a new flex container are ignored
body: `.small-action` becomes a flex container, but its children still use `float: left` (`.topic-avatar`, `.avatar`) and `button { float: right }`. Floats are ignored on flex items, so the float-based layout the rules were written for no longer applies. The author should confirm the intended positioning.

title: align-items mixin emits invalid -ms-align-items property
body: The mixin outputs `-ms-align-items`, which is not a real property in any vendor prefix set. Browsers ignore it, and it adds dead output. Its `-ms-flex-align` line is the correct prefixed form.

title: New flexbox mixins may duplicate existing definitions
body: `flexbox`, `inline-flex`, `align-items` and `order` are appended here, but the same mixin names may already exist elsewhere in the theme. Duplicate `@mixin` definitions silently override each other depending on import order, which can change output. Confirm no other definitions exist.

title: Inline-flex mixin adds prefixed display values that differ from the original rule
body: The original `display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline;` is replaced by mixins that also emit `-webkit-inline-box` and `-moz-inline-box` before the standard value. Vendor-specific box display values are not equivalent to flex and can conflict in older engines. The PR does not justify this change.

title: PR title and description do not match the change
body: The title says the change optimizes header layout performance, but the diff is purely layout restyling with visual side effects (spacing, float removal, margin removal). The description is only 'Test 5', so reviewers have no rationale, no before/after measurements, and no testing notes.

title: website_name leaks the profile website to anonymous viewers of TL0 users
body: `:website_name` is added to the plain `attributes` list, but it is not added to the `untrusted_attributes` list (lines 105-111). `website`, `location`, `bio_raw` and `profile_background` are all hidden for TL0 users seen by anonymous visitors, via `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. `website_name` is derived directly from `website`, so for a TL0 user it is still serialized. Anonymous users can therefore see the website host, and with this change the full URL path, which the restriction was meant to hide. The TL0 spec (spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb line 11) still lists only the old untrusted attributes, so it does not catch the leak. Fix: add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and extend the spec's list.

title: website_name leaks the website for TL0 users hidden from anonymous viewers
body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so for a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous guardian, `include_website?` returns false and the website is hidden. The new `website_name` attribute is not covered: `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?` and never calls `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. As a result the website host, and now the full path, is still serialized for those users, bypassing the trust-level restriction. Gate `include_website_name` the same way as the untrusted attributes, and add `website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` expectation in the spec.

title: Trailing slash appended when the website URL has only a root path
body: For a website such as `http://example.com/`, `URI(...).path` is `/`, so `website_name` becomes `example.com/` when the discourse host matches. The path logic is also repeated in three branches, so this edge case is duplicated and easy to miss. Normalize the path (e.g. treat `/` as empty) before concatenating.

title: Path-display branches are only partially covered by tests
body: The spec covers the same-host case, the parent-domain case, and the unrelated-domain case. It does not cover the www/forum sibling branch (same depth, shared parent), a website with no path, or a website with a trailing slash. Each of these exercises a distinct branch of `website_name`, and the trailing-slash case currently produces an incorrect result.

title: String#<< mutates the literal and website_host may be nil-safe issue in ends_with check
body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses `<<`, which mutates the string literal in place (fine per call since literals are fresh in Ruby without frozen_string_literal, but it is still a mutating operator on a temporary, and inconsistent with the rest of the method). More important: when the website host is a parent domain with an unrelated suffix match, e.g. website 'ample.com' and discourse 'example.com', the check is a plain suffix match on '.ample.com' so it is correct only because of the leading dot; the logic is fragile but works. The real issue is the first branch: when website_host equals discourse_host the path is appended, so 'http://example.com' with no path yields 'example.com' plus '' which is fine, but a website with a trailing slash yields 'example.com/' shown to users. Consider normalizing empty or root paths.

title: Hostname comparison uses discourse_host.split on possibly nil or differing host lengths
body: The method calls `discourse_host.split('.')` and compares segment counts without guarding against discourse_host being nil or having a port. For the 'same length' branch the comparison `split('.')[1..-1]` on a two-label host like 'example.com' is skipped only because length > 2 is required, but a website host with a different label count falls into the else branch where `website_host` is used directly, which can leak the full website host for unrelated sites. Behavior is not fully specified and is untested for subdomain cases such as www vs bare domain.

title: Rescue modifier swallows all errors from URI parsing and the path is recomputed multiple times
body: `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` is computed once for the host, then `URI(website.to_s)` is re-parsed on every branch. Parsing is repeated needlessly and, if the website is malformed, `URI(...).path` in the matched branches could raise after the host check succeeded. Parse once and reuse.

title: Template now depends on model.website_name, which is never shown to be set for the Ember model
body: The template switches from the removed computed `websiteName` to `model.website_name`. That is a server-serialized attribute and is only present when `include_website_name?` is true, so the link text is absent for users whose website is blank, which is intended, but the `title` and href still use `model.website` which may be restricted by untrusted_attributes for anonymous users while website_name is not restricted, so anonymous viewers can see the website path (including path) even when the website field itself is hidden for TL0 users.

title: website_name is not subject to the untrusted_attributes restriction
body: website and bio fields are hidden for TL0 users seen by anonymous viewers via untrusted_attributes, but website_name (which exposes the website host and now the full path) is serialized with only `website.present?` as its guard. The spec for TL0 anonymous users does not include website_name, so the leak is untested and the privacy control is bypassed.

title: Spec does not cover the case where website has no path or a trailing slash
body: The new tests only cover 'http://example.com/user'. There is no test for a bare domain website (e.g. 'http://example.com') on the same-host branch, which would show whether the output is 'example.com' or 'example.com/' and whether the rescue path yields nil. No test covers a malformed website or the TL0 anonymous visibility of website_name.

title: Badge-notification color in categories list still uses a lightness-only scale-color
body: The PR title says scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes, but in this file the `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` rule (line 115) still uses plain scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) and was not converted, unlike the other color rules in the same file. On dark themes this leaves the text color inconsistent with the rest of the list.

title: Duplicate selector for thumb-tack unpinned changed without need
body: The `.fa-thumb-tack.unpinned` rule was converted to dark-light-choose but it is a redundant duplicate of the parent rule; not a functional bug, but the change adds more noise to a rule already covered by line 39.

title: h3 color in topic-map changed from 20% to 50% lightness
body: In `.topic-map h3` the base color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) and the diff replaces it with the 50% lightness value for the light branch, silently changing the light theme color of mobile topic map headings. The lightness value should stay 20% for the primary branch, otherwise the visual change is unintended and not described by the PR.

title: group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50% silently
body: The `.group-member-info .name` color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and was changed to the 50% primary value on the light branch, altering the light theme appearance without any documented intent. Same unintended-change issue as the other lightness rewrites.

title: group-member-info .name color lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: The `.group-member-info .name` primary color was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), changing the light-theme color that the PR is supposed to leave alone for light themes.

title: custom-message-length primary lightness changed from 70% to 30%
body: The light-theme branch of `.custom-message-length` was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to 30%, making the counter text much darker on light themes. This is a visible regression not matching the PR's stated purpose of only adding a dark-theme fallback.

title: Duplicate lightness changed for topic-map h5 link
body: In the embedded-posts `.topic-meta-data h5 a` rule the light branch was changed from 30% to 70% lightness, a different shade than the rest of the file's conventions; the change is undocumented and reverses the emphasis direction.

title: Embedded topic-meta-data h5 link lightness changed from 30% to 70%
body: The `.topic-meta-data h5 a` color light branch changed from scale-color($primary,$lightness:30%) to 70%, making the link much lighter on light themes; this is an unrequested visual change.

title: Category badge notification color changed inconsistently with stated PR scope
body: The PR title says only `scale-color($lightness)` must use `$secondary` for dark themes, but the diff leaves `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` (line 115) and other scale-color uses unchanged in the same file, e.g. `#list-area .unseen` uses scale-color($danger). Partial conversion leaves some dark-theme colors unadjusted, so the change is inconsistent across the stylesheets.

title: Admin description color lightness mismatch with other converted rules
body: Several rules were changed to dark-light-choose with lightness values that do not match the original (e.g. desktop/topic-list header.scss and mobile/user.scss changed `.group-member-info .name` from scale-color($primary, 30%) to 50%, and mobile/modal.scss `.custom-message-length` changed from 70% to 30% of $primary). These silently change the light-theme appearance, which the PR title does not describe.

title: h3 color lightness changed from 20% to 50% in mobile topic-map
body: The `.topic-map h3` color was originally scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 50%), ...). This changes the light-theme heading color noticeably, unrelated to the dark-theme fix described in the title.

title: Embedded topic-meta h5 link lightness changed in light theme
body: `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` was scale-color($primary, 30%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 70%), ...). The light-theme (primary) branch is now 70% lightness instead of 30%, a large visual regression not covered by the PR description.

title: PR description is a placeholder
body: The PR description reads only 'Test 7' and gives no rationale, list of affected themes, or verification steps for a change touching ~80 color declarations across 32 stylesheets.

title: .custom-message-length light-theme color silently changed from 70% to 30% lightness
body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The replacement puts `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` in the light-theme slot of dark-light-choose, so the light theme now gets a much darker text color. The PR is meant to add a dark-theme fallback, not change light-theme output, so this is an unrelated visual regression for every light-theme user.

title: .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a light-theme color changed from 30% to 70% lightness
body: The diff replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), ...)`. The light-theme value jumps from 30% to 70% lightness, so the link becomes far lighter than before on light themes. The dark-theme fallback is the only change the PR title describes, so this is an unintended regression.

title: .topic-map h3 light-theme color changed from 20% to 50% lightness
body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new value uses 50% for the light theme and 50% for the dark theme (`scale-color($secondary, 50%)`), which changes the light-theme heading color and drops the intended dark-theme 80% fallback. Neither part matches the PR's stated purpose.

title: .group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
body: The original used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new dark-light-choose call uses 50% for the light theme, which changes the existing light-theme output. This is not a dark-theme fix.

title: .group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` for the light theme, so the light-theme name color is altered without being mentioned in the PR title or description.

title: No verification or description for a broad theme-color change across 32 files
body: The PR touches about 80 color declarations across 32 stylesheets, but the description is just 'Test 7' and no visual or compile check is described. Several hunks alter light-theme values (see the other findings), so a reviewer cannot tell which changes are intended without a before/after review of both themes.

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. With user_count=50 and limit=50 this yields 2 pages, but only one page exists. showingLast (currentPage == totalPages) is then false on the real last page, so the Next button stays enabled and paging forward shows an empty page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) instead.

title: next() moves offset to user_count, producing an empty page on partial last pages
body: offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count). With user_count=120 and limit=50, paging from offset 50 goes to 100, then next sets offset to min(150,120)=120. The request returns no members because offset equals the total, so the user lands on an empty page. The offset should be clamped to the start of the last page, e.g. the last page's offset is (totalPages-1)*limit, not user_count. group.js line 23 has the same clamp (offset capped at user_count), so the server-side empty result is reached through both paths.

title: members endpoint accepts unbounded limit and negative limit/offset
body: limit is taken straight from params with no upper bound, so a request with limit=10000000 returns every member of a large group in one response (the old code applied a limit only to automatic groups, and it was 200). A negative limit or offset is also passed to .limit/.offset, which can raise a database error (500) or behave unexpectedly. Clamp limit to a sane maximum (e.g. 1..100) and clamp offset to >= 0.

title: findMembers clamps offset to user_count instead of the last page start
body: offset = min(user_count, max(offset, 0)) allows an offset equal to user_count, which yields an empty page for any caller that stores an offset at the end of the list (for example after removeMember, which reloads with the current offset). After removing the last member on the final page the list shows nothing, even though earlier members exist. The offset should be clamped to a page-aligned start.

title: Stale CSS selector targets the old input id group-users
body: The group member input was renamed to id="user-selector" in group.hbs, but the rule `input#group-users { width: 600px; }` still targets the old id, so it no longer applies and the intended width is lost.

title: remove_member spec uses PUT instead of the DELETE route
body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route for remove_member is DELETE. The spec does not exercise the real verb and could pass even if routing changed. It should use :delete to match the route.

title: Specs for the new members endpoints and paging are missing
body: The PR removes the incremental add/remove specs and the update membership specs, but adds no coverage for the public GroupsController#members pagination (meta total/limit/offset, limit cap, offset past end). The new paging behaviour that the frontend depends on is untested, and the automatic-group specs depend on fixture id 1 existing.

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: In admin-group.js.es6, totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. With 100 members and limit 50 this yields 3 pages when there are only 2. The Next button stays enabled on page 2, and clicking it sets offset to 100, which requests an empty page. The same formula is used for showingLast, so the last-page logic is also wrong. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) instead.

title: members endpoint accepts unbounded or negative limit/offset
body: The public members action reads limit as params[:limit] || 50 with no upper bound and offset with no lower bound. A caller can request limit=1000000 to pull the whole membership in one response, which is costly for large groups. A negative limit or offset is passed straight to SQL LIMIT/OFFSET and will raise a database error (500). Clamp limit to a sane maximum and reject or clamp negative values.

title: create action silently drops alias_level
body: The admin UI sends alias_level in asJSON() when creating a group, but create only sets name and visible. A group created with an alias level selected in the form is saved with the default alias level and no error is shown. Set alias_level in create as update does.

title: Remove link shown for automatic groups because automatic is not in member context
body: The group_member item view renders each member as its context, so {{#unless automatic}} looks up automatic on the User object, where it is undefined. The remove link therefore appears even for automatic groups, where the server rejects removal with a 422. The flag must be passed from the group controller into the item view or the template.

title: Public group members page now shows only the first page of members
body: The public members endpoint is now paginated with a default limit of 50, and the public group/members template has no pagination controls. Groups with more than 50 members will show only the first 50 on the public members page, a regression from loading all members for non-automatic groups.

title: remove_member spec issues a PUT to a DELETE-only route
body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but routes.rb only defines remove_member under delete "members". The test may fail on routing or test the wrong verb. It should use :delete.

title: Coverage for incremental add/remove and non-existent users was dropped
body: The removed PATCH specs covered adding a non-existent user (silent success), removing a non-member, and the automatic-group guard. The new add_members and remove_member specs cover only the automatic-group rejection and one happy path, so the silent-skip behaviour for unknown usernames is no longer tested.

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. With user_count=100 and limit=50 it returns 3, but there are only 2 pages. showingLast (currentPage == totalPages) then never becomes true on the real last page. Pressing next there sets offset to min(offset+limit, user_count) = user_count, which requests an empty out-of-range page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) instead.

title: limit and offset from params are not validated
