Since init now runs at construction time and can fail, the failure path should cancel the context and release lifecycle resources.

title: Index build now blocks construction and can fail server startup without a timeout
body: Moving Init into NewResourceServer means the full index build (search.init, which walks every namespace/resource) now runs synchronously before the server is returned. Callers, including module startup, now block on that work and fail hard if any build errors, where previously the failure only surfaced on individual RPCs. The context passed is the unbounded background context with no deadline. The PR asks whether anything depended on lazy init. Callers that constructed the server and expected it to be cheap or to tolerate index failure are affected, and this needs to be called out and tested.

title: Stop no longer gates RPCs, and initErr is written without synchronization
body: Previously every RPC called s.Init, which returned s.initErr, so calls after Stop returned 'service is stopping' or 'service is stopped'. The Init calls were removed from Read, List, Create, Update, Delete, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob, GetBlob and Watch, so those errors are no longer returned after Stop. Stop also writes s.initErr without any lock while other goroutines may read it. Both are behavior changes that the PR does not mention.

title: Postgres variant of the storage-server integration test is now skipped
body: The new skip for postgres means the only test that exercises the storage server target with a real database no longer runs for postgres in CI. The change is unrelated to the PR's stated goals (init, tracing, indexing speed) and reduces coverage of the startup path that this PR changes, with no linked issue tracking the re-enable.

title: Concurrent goroutines write shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` during startup indexing
body: Inside `group.Go(func() error {...})`, the closure assigns to the outer `err` variable (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and increments the outer `totalBatchesIndexed` without synchronization. With `initWorkers` > 1 these run concurrently, which is a data race (flagged by `-race`) and can return the wrong error or lose the count. The closure should use a local `err :=` and an atomic counter.

title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows duplicate concurrent builds for the same key
body: The whole `BuildIndex` used to be serialized by `cacheMu`. The lock now only guards the final map write, so two concurrent `getOrCreateIndex` calls for the same namespace/resource (possible from Search and watch events, which both call `build` when `GetIndex` returns nil) will both build. For file-backed indexes (size > FileThreshold) both call `bleve.New(dir, ...)` on the same directory, and one will fail or corrupt the other. The second build also overwrites the cache entry, leaking the first index. Per-key locking (singleflight or a per-key mutex) is needed, not an unlocked build.

title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding the lock
body: `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` with no `cacheMu` read lock, while `BuildIndex` writes to the same map under the write lock and `GetIndex` reads it under RLock. Concurrent map iteration and insertion is a fatal runtime error in Go. It is now also called from `searchSupport.init` logging, and `search.init` can run while Search requests are building indexes. It should take `cacheMu.RLock()`.

title: Initialization now runs in the constructor and blocks/fails NewResourceServer
body: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)`, which runs lifecycle hooks, the full search index build for all namespaces above InitMinCount, and starts the watcher. Callers now get a slow constructor, and any Init failure (including a lifecycle hook that expects the server to be fully constructed or registered) makes the constructor return an error rather than letting the caller handle it. Callers must be audited for whether they can tolerate a long blocking constructor and whether lifecycle hooks depend on the returned server being usable, as the PR asks.

title: Event broadcaster now starts after the index build, so writes during the build are missed
body: The order in `Init` was changed so `initWatcher()` runs after `search.init(ctx)`. Any write events that occur while the (now potentially long) index build runs are not buffered by the broadcaster, so Watch clients subscribed through the broadcaster silently miss those events. Previously the watcher was started first to buffer them. The reordering needs justification or the watcher should be started before the build.

title: Init errors from search build are only logged and the server is left in a half-initialized state on Stop
body: When `search.init` fails, `initErr` is set and the constructor returns an error, but the search goroutines and lifecycle started earlier (`lifecycle.Init`) are never torn down because `NewResourceServer` returns `nil, err` without calling `Stop`/`cancel`. The background context created in the constructor leaks.

title: Postgres integration test is now skipped unconditionally
body: The new skip for `postgres` disables the only integration test covering the storage server target for that database, without any tracking issue beyond a TODO. The change is unrelated to the PR's stated goals and reduces coverage of the lazy-to-eager init change for postgres.

title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding the lock
body: BuildIndex now writes b.cache under cacheMu, but TotalDocs (called from searchSupport.init logging) ranges over b.cache with no read lock. Concurrent builds during init (errgroup with multiple workers) can cause a concurrent map read/write, which is a fatal runtime error in Go. TotalDocs should take cacheMu.RLock().

title: Removing the whole-function lock allows duplicate index creation for the same key
body: The lock previously serialized BuildIndex, which also prevented two concurrent builds of the same NamespacedResource from both calling bleve.New on the same directory / overwriting each other. With the lock removed, getOrCreateIndex (GetIndex returns nil, then build) can run concurrently for the same key from Search and handleEvent, leading to two bleve indexes opened on the same file path (bleve.New fails with 'index already exists' or corrupts state) and one index silently replacing the other in the cache. The PR narrows the lock to only the map write, which does not protect this path.

title: Eager Init in constructor makes startup failures fatal and can block/crash the process
body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) which runs lifecycle init, the full search index build over all resources, and starts the watcher. Any error (e.g. DB not ready, index build failure) now causes the constructor to fail, and the index build runs synchronously with no timeout before the server is returned. The PR's own reviewer note asks what this could break; callers of NewResourceServer (module wiring, tests) must now tolerate long blocking startup and a hard failure. Also the ctx used is the server's internal background-derived context, so no caller cancellation applies.

title: Stop() overwrites initErr and Init's once guard hides subsequent failures
body: Init uses sync.Once and stores the error in s.initErr; Stop sets s.initErr to a 'stopping' error. Since Init is no longer called on each RPC, a failed init is only reported once from the constructor, and any caller that later calls Init gets a stale or misleading error. Combined with removing the per-RPC Init checks, a server whose init partly failed (e.g. lifecycle ok, search failed) silently serves requests with no index or no watcher.

title: History, Origin and Search dereference nil search support
body: After removing the Init guard, History and Origin call s.search.History / s.search.Origin directly. When search is not configured (opts.Search.Resources == nil or Backend nil, so s.search is nil), these methods panic with a nil pointer dereference. Previously the nil Init path did not guard this either, but Search has an explicit nil check while History/Origin do not.

title: Data race on totalBatchesIndexed and shared err in init goroutines
body: Inside group.Go closures, totalBatchesIndexed++ is written concurrently by multiple goroutines without synchronization, and the shared outer variable err is assigned from concurrent goroutines (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`). This is a data race; the err assignment can also return the wrong error. Use a local error variable and an atomic counter.

title: Watch context is detached from the init trace context and goroutine loops forever on channel close
body: The watcher goroutine loops `v := <-events` without handling a closed channel; when the poller exits (closed stream), v becomes nil and handleEvent dereferences evt.Type, panicking. Also the watch context is context.Background() so it is never cancelled on server Stop, leaking the goroutine.

title: No tests cover the new eager initialization or the lock change
body: The behavioral change (init moved into constructor, per-RPC Init removed, locking changed in BuildIndex) has no accompanying unit test for concurrent BuildIndex or for NewResourceServer returning an error when init fails. The module server test change only adds a skip for postgres, which does not validate any of the changes.

title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not compile
body: The new condition calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only overload added in UsernamePasswordForm is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, and nothing in this diff adds a no-arg version. The services module will fail to compile, so the PR cannot be merged as is.

title: Conditional passkey UI is now filled only when a user is already set, inverting the previous behavior
body: Previously `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` ran when no user had been identified yet (`context.getUser() == null`), which is when the username/passkey conditional UI is needed on the first login page. The new guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` requires `user != null`, so on a fresh login the WebAuthn challenge and conditional-UI attributes are never set. The same inversion appears in the `challenge(context, error, field)` override (around line 137), which now fills only when a user is set. The intent was to fill when the user is present for re-authentication, but the no-user path that the existing tests (e.g. passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey expecting the webauth form on the initial page) rely on is broken.

title: Negative element checks catch every Exception, so they can pass when they should not
body: In reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey the `try { assertThat(findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee)` pattern catches any Exception, including unrelated WebDriver or matcher failures, so the check can silently pass for the wrong reason. Using `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` as the other tests in this PR do would make the assertion precise. The same pattern is repeated at lines 312-317 and in the other tests.

title: Calls a zero-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() that does not exist
body: The new condition `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` calls a no-arg method. The only definition added in UsernamePasswordForm.java is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which takes the user and is protected. No no-arg overload is added anywhere in the diff, so UsernameForm.java will not compile and the services module build fails. The intended call is most likely `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which would also make the skip-form decision depend on whether passkeys are enabled for the realm.

title: NoSuchElementException import is left unused after the assertThrows removal
body: The two `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` calls were replaced with `MatcherAssert.assertThat(...)`, but the `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` import was not removed. In this file it is now unused, which triggers a compiler/checkstyle warning and may fail a strict lint build.

title: util package now statically depends on a constant in the browser authenticator package
body: AuthenticatorUtils (util package) now statically imports USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH from AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator (browser package), while browser classes already import AuthenticatorUtils. This creates a two-way package dependency. The constant would be cleaner in a shared place, or the helper could live with the browser authenticators.

title: Conditional passkey UI is never set up on a normal login page
body: The new guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` returns true only when `user != null` (see the helper at line ~161). On a normal login, where no user is set yet, the call evaluates to false, so `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is skipped. The passkey conditional UI (the webauth form and autocomplete attributes) is therefore missing from the initial username/password page. The old code filled it when `context.getUser() == null`, so this inverts the condition. The same inversion affects the `challenge(context, error, field)` override at line ~137, which now only fills the passkey form when a user is already set. The new tests that expect `//form[@id='webauth']` on the first login page (e.g. passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey) would fail.

title: Call to zero-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not match any declared method
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is called with no arguments, but the only overload added in UsernamePasswordForm.java is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. Nothing in this diff declares a no-arg version, so this will not compile unless one exists elsewhere that is not in the change. The intent appears to be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

title: configureTestRealm is called but not defined in the diff
body: `addTestRealms` now calls `configureTestRealm(realmRepresentation)`, but this file does not define it in the diff and no import or visible inheritance source is shown. If it is not defined in AbstractWebAuthnVirtualTest, the test class will not compile.

title: Unused NoSuchElementException import left behind
body: After replacing the two `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` checks with positive assertions, the `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` import is no longer used. Checkstyle or the build's unused-import check may fail on it.

title: Negative webauthn checks use try/catch(Exception) and can pass vacuously
body: In reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey, the assertion `assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue())` throws NoSuchElementException when the element is absent, and the `catch (Exception nsee)` swallows it. The check passes whether or not the element exists in the wrong state, except via the unreached fail(). A `driver.findElements(...).isEmpty()` check would assert the intended behaviour directly. The same pattern appears at lines ~313-317.

title: PR description is a placeholder
body: The description reads only 'Test 1'. It does not explain the bug being fixed (passkeys during re-authentication with prompt=login), the behaviour change (username form now shown during re-auth when passkeys are enabled, and the conditional UI setup changes), or the reasoning for the new AuthenticatorUtils helper. Reviewers have no context for these behaviour changes.

title: Cleanup registers a literal "alias" instead of the created IDP alias
body: The cleanup `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` uses the literal string "alias" rather than the alias of the IDP just created. The cleanup therefore never removes the `idp-alias-N` providers, so they leak into other tests in the same realm. The same copy-paste pattern also appears at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`. The method reference should capture the actual alias.

title: remove() now always loads the IDP from the database
body: `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is executed unconditionally at the top of `remove()`. Previously the DB lookup only happened when the alias key was invalidated, and the cache path avoided it entirely. Every IDP removal now incurs an extra uncached DB query, even when the cached entry is present and could supply the same data for the login-invalidation check.

title: getForLogin Javadoc does not describe the new public-broker requirement
body: The change adds `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || BROKER_PUBLIC` to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()`, so an org-linked IDP now qualifies for login only if it is marked broker-public. The Javadoc for `getForLogin` (lines 150-158) still says an IDP is usable for login if it is enabled, not link-only, and not hidden on login. It omits this new condition, which callers and maintainers will need to know.

title: Cleanup registers removal of a literal "alias" IDP instead of the created alias
body: In testCacheIDPForLogin the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)`. The string "alias" is a literal, not the IDP alias, so the cleanup attempts to remove an IDP named "alias" that does not exist. The 20 `idp-alias-N` providers created by this test are never removed and leak into the shared test realm, which can change counts in later tests. The same bug appears at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`. The copied pattern in testCacheIDPByOrg (line 303) has the same defect, with an unused `final String alias` variable that was meant to be used.

title: Cleanup for idp-alias-20 uses the literal "alias" and does not remove the IDP
body: The cleanup `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` targets a non-existent IDP named "alias". The IDP `idp-alias-20` created here is never removed, so it leaks into the realm for subsequent tests.

title: remove() now always loads the IDP from the database
body: `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is executed unconditionally. Previously the DB lookup happened only when the alias cache key was invalidated. Every remove now costs an extra DB query, even when the cached entry is available. It is needed for registerIDPLoginInvalidation, but it could reuse the cached IDP for the invalidation of the id and alias keys.

title: Search key includes organizationId even for REALM_ONLY, fragmenting the cache
body: `searchKey` is derived from `organizationId` regardless of `mode`. For REALM_ONLY the result does not depend on organizationId, so callers passing different org ids each produce a separate cached entry (or a cache miss and invalidation via the `cached == null` path) for identical results. The query cache is also rewritten on every such miss, which causes unnecessary churn.

title: Cleanup registers a bogus alias, so the 20 IDPs created by the test are never removed
body: The cleanup `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` uses the literal string "alias" instead of the created IDP's alias. Every registered cleanup therefore targets a nonexistent provider and removes nothing. The IDPs `idp-alias-0..20` (including the hidden `idp-alias-20` and the org-linked ones) leak into the shared test realm and can change results of other tests that call getForLogin or list IDPs. The same pattern exists in testCacheIDPByOrg, but the new test copies it. The fix is to capture the alias in a final variable and remove that alias.

title: null and empty-string organizationId map to the same cache entry but can produce different results
body: `searchKey` is `organizationId != null ? organizationId : ""`, so a null organizationId and an empty-string organizationId share the same key. In the delegate, a null organizationId means 'any org' for ORG_ONLY/ALL, while "" is passed as a literal organization id to the ORGANIZATION_ID filter. For ALL mode the cached result for one can be served for the other, returning wrong IDPs. Use a distinct sentinel or key on Objects.toString with a prefix to avoid the collision.

title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER computes encodings and discards them
body: Lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder instances, write r and s into them, and throw the results away. This is dead code that does redundant BigInteger encoding work on every signature conversion and suggests the encoding logic was not carefully reviewed.

title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER builds r and s with a forced leading zero byte, producing non-minimal and wrong integers
body: The method copies each half of the signature into an array of length len+1 with a leading 0 byte, then calls new BigInteger(r). That is always non-negative, which is correct for the sign, but the DER encoding then writes BigInteger.toByteArray() of the value, which is minimal. The only real issue is that signLength/2 is assumed equal to each component length; for odd or mismatched signLength inputs the arraycopy silently misbehaves or throws ArrayIndexOutOfBounds instead of an IOException. Also the method is not used by the ECDSA verification path in the test, so the round-trip test covers only the happy path.

title: readInteger drops the sign-extension semantics needed for ECDSA components and does not check length
body: readInteger reads the content with read(length) and builds BigInteger(bytes) without validating that length is positive or that the value is non-negative. ECDSA r/s values from a malicious or malformed DER signature can be arbitrarily large or negative; integerToBytes then truncates them silently, so a signature with out-of-range components can be mapped to a different valid-looking concatenated value instead of being rejected.

title: readSequence loop can run forever or misparse when element length is zero
body: In readSequence the loop subtracts bytes.length from the remaining length; readNext returns the full TLV including tag and length. If the decoder returns indefinite length (-1 from readLength) or a zero-length element, length never reaches zero and the loop can spin or read past the sequence. Indefinite length is not rejected here.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the provider of a default KeyStore instance
body: The method creates a KeyStore of the default type and returns its Provider, which is not a BouncyCastle provider and is only the provider of an uninitialized keystore. Callers that expect BC (e.g. for registering or looking up BC algorithms) will get an unrelated provider, or the method may throw IllegalStateException on a misconfigured keystore type.

title: Provider order 100 ranks below DefaultCryptoProvider but most methods throw UnsupportedOperationException
body: CryptoIntegration now picks the highest order. This provider has order 100 while Default/Elytron/FIPS use 200, so it is chosen only when they are absent. But if it is selected (authz-client used standalone), every method other than getEcdsaCryptoProvider throws UnsupportedOperationException, including getKeyStore's siblings and createECParams, so any non-ECDSA path in the client fails at runtime.

title: Multiple providers no longer rejected, changing detection semantics silently
body: Previously multiple CryptoProvider implementations on the classpath caused an IllegalStateException. Now the highest-order one is silently chosen and the rest only logged at debug level. A misconfigured deployment with two providers of equal order gets an arbitrary pick (sort is stable but ServiceLoader order is not deterministic across classpaths) with no warning.

title: Ignored providers logged via debugf with non-constant format string
body: logger.debugf(builder.toString()) passes the built string as a format pattern; any '%' in a class name or future text will be misinterpreted as a format specifier and throw or garble the message. Use debugf with a format argument.

title: New abstract method order() breaks all existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: order() is added as an abstract interface method with no default. Any third-party or other in-repo CryptoProvider implementation that does not override it will fail to compile. Providing a default would preserve compatibility.

title: Test only checks round trip of concatenated RS, not that DER is valid or matches the reference
body: The test asserts asn1derToConcatenatedRS(concatenatedRSToASN1DER(x)) equals x, but never verifies the produced DER against the original signature or checks signature verification succeeds. A symmetric bug in both directions would pass. It should verify the signature with the converted DER and cover edge cases such as leading-zero/high-bit components.

title: New abstract method order() breaks every existing CryptoProvider implementation
body: `int order()` is added as an abstract interface method with no default. Any CryptoProvider implementation that does not implement it (other modules, downstream extensions, test doubles) will fail to compile, and a binary-compatible implementation would throw AbstractMethodError at runtime. A default implementation (for example returning 0) would avoid the break.

title: Providers with equal order() are chosen nondeterministically instead of failing
body: Previously multiple providers on the classpath threw an IllegalStateException. Now they are sorted by order() and the first is silently used. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so any combination of them (for example Elytron plus Default) resolves by ServiceLoader discovery order, which is not guaranteed. The wrong provider (for example a non-FIPS one in FIPS mode) can then be selected silently. Ties should be rejected or resolved by a deterministic rule.

title: Auto-registered provider throws UnsupportedOperationException for most methods
body: The provider is registered via META-INF/services and has order 100, so it is selected whenever no other provider is on the classpath. Methods such as getKeyStore/getSignature are partially implemented, but getPemUtils, getKeyFactory, getKeyPairGen, getSignature, getCertificateUtils and others throw UnsupportedOperationException. Any authz-client feature that needs them (for example client JWT or signed-token authentication through Http/TokenCallable) will fail at runtime with an unhelpful error rather than a clear configuration message.

title: CryptoIntegration.init is called on every client creation with a fixed classloader
body: AuthzClient.create(Configuration) now always calls CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()). The init is guarded by a singleton, so the first caller's classloader decides which providers are visible. In a container where the authz client jar is loaded by a different classloader than the application's CryptoProvider, the application's provider is ignored without any warning.

title: Dead ASN1Encoder calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder instances and discard the results. They have no effect and only add confusion; the actual encoding is done by the return statement below them.

title: getKeyStore uses format.name() while the other providers use format.toString()
body: Other CryptoProvider implementations in this change (DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider) call KeyStore.getInstance(format.toString()). If KeystoreFormat overrides toString() with a different keystore type string, this provider will request a different keystore type than the rest of Keycloak.

title: Ignored provider list is passed as a log format string
body: logger.debugf(builder.toString()) uses the concatenated class-name string as a format pattern. Any '%' in the content would be interpreted as a format specifier and could throw an exception. It should be logger.debugf("%s", builder).

title: Dead ASN1Encoder calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 create ASN1Encoder instances and call write(...) whose results are discarded. These are no-ops that only add confusion; the actual encoding is done again at lines 117-121. Harmless functionally but indicates a copy/paste leftover that a maintainer would want removed.

title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER produces non-minimal/signed-incorrect DER integers
body: r and s are built with a leading zero byte and passed to new BigInteger(r) then re-encoded via BigInteger.toByteArray(). This yields a correct minimal two's complement encoding, but the input is assumed to be unsigned big-endian of length signLength/2 with no check on signLength; if signLength is odd or the array is shorter than expected, System.arraycopy throws ArrayIndexOutOfBounds at runtime rather than a clear error. The method also never validates that signature.length >= signLength.

title: readInteger uses signed BigInteger from DER without validation
body: readInteger reads raw bytes and calls new BigInteger(bytes) which is correct for DER two's complement, but it does not reject empty content (length 0), which throws NumberFormatException instead of IOException, and readLength returning -1 (indefinite length) is passed directly to read(-1) causing NegativeArraySizeException. Malformed signatures from a server can therefore surface as unchecked exceptions.

title: readSequence loop can run forever or miscount on zero-length elements
body: In readSequence, the loop subtracts bytes.length from the remaining length per element. readNext returns header plus content; if the decoded length is inconsistent with the sequence, length may never reach zero or may go negative without error, and a malformed element with an indefinite-length marker (-1) is not rejected. Malformed input can cause misparsing or a hang risk rather than a clean IOException.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns a random keystore provider instead of a BC provider
body: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns KeyStore.getInstance(default type).getProvider(), which is whatever provider supplies the default keystore (usually SUN/JKS), not BouncyCastle. Callers that expect BC (e.g. BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER lookups) get the wrong provider, and the method creates a keystore instance each call. Most other operations in this provider throw UnsupportedOperationException, so the BC provider mismatch is a real contract break for any code path that reaches it.

title: order() of 100 makes the minimal provider win over full providers only if others are absent; CryptoIntegration selects by highest order
body: CryptoIntegration sorts by order descending and picks the first. AuthzClientCryptoProvider has order 100 while DefaultCryptoProvider, Elytron and FIPS have 200, so they win when present. However, AuthzClientCryptoProvider is registered via META-INF/services in the authz-client jar, and AuthzClient.create() calls CryptoIntegration.init() which is a no-op if a provider was already set. In the Keycloak testsuite and any app with both on classpath, the initialization order decides the provider, making behavior depend on who initializes first. The selection is therefore not deterministic for this design.

title: logger.debugf used with a non-constant format string
body: The 'Ignored crypto providers' message is built as a string and passed as the format to debugf. Any '%' in class names would be misinterpreted as a format specifier. Use debugf with a format argument instead.

title: New abstract method order() breaks all existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: order() was added as an abstract interface method. Any third-party or out-of-tree CryptoProvider implementation will fail to compile or load. A default implementation would avoid breaking the SPI contract.

title: getKeyStore ignores the format's provider and uses KeyStore.getInstance without provider
body: getKeyStore returns KeyStore.getInstance(format.name()) which uses the format name directly (e.g. 'PKCS12' or 'BCFKS' names) and may fail for formats not in the default JDK, while DefaultCryptoProvider uses format.toString() and BC provider. Inconsistent behavior with the other providers.

title: Test only checks round trip of concatenated form, not DER correctness
body: The test asserts asn1derToConcatenatedRS(concatenatedRSToASN1DER(x)) == x, but never verifies that the DER output verifies against the original JDK signature or matches the JDK-produced DER. A symmetric bug in both directions would pass. It also uses the EC keypair generated with default curve without checking the curve matches the algorithm's expected size.

title: Client-removed listener calls V2 setPermissionsEnabled, which always throws
body: The ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2. Its setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. Deleting any client in a realm under V2 can therefore fail or leave the realm in a half-deleted state.

title: Listener gated on V1 feature flag, silently disabling cleanup for V2
body: The whole listener body is now wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ). Previously it ran unconditionally. Under V2 (where only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 may be enabled), role, client and group removal no longer clean up permission state. This behavior change is unrelated to adding clients and is not explained in the PR.

title: Possible NullPointerException when the 'all clients' resource is missing
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, scope), if no per-client resource exists, the code loads the Clients type resource via getResourceTypeResource(). That method returns null when the schema is unsupported or the resource is not found. The result is passed straight to getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check, which can throw an NPE instead of returning false.

title: Client removal now calls setPermissionsEnabled, which throws in V2
body: The new ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, and clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2. Its setPermissionsEnabled() unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException (ClientPermissionsV2 line ~193). Deleting any client in a realm with V2 enabled and this listener active will therefore fail or roll back the deletion. The listener needs to skip or no-op for V2, or ClientPermissionsV2 must implement the cleanup.

title: Possible NPE when the all-clients resource is missing
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, scope), if no per-client resource exists, the code loads the 'Clients' type resource via getResourceTypeResource(). That method returns null when the resource is not found. The next line then calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) with a null resource, which can NPE. Even if it doesn't, line 224 uses resource.getScopes() on null. A null check on resource should return false.

title: canMapRoles and related methods ignore the MANAGE_CLIENTS realm role
body: canManage(), canConfigure() and canView() all short-circuit when the caller has MANAGE_CLIENTS. canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles only check the schema permission via hasPermission(client, ...). Callers with the manage-clients admin role can therefore be denied role mapping on clients under V2, even though the V1 contract and the interface javadoc treat that role as granting access. Confirm this is intended, and add the role check if not.

title: requireView() javadoc describes a boolean return instead of a throw
body: The javadoc for requireView() says 'Returns true if canView() returns true', but the method is void and must throw ForbiddenException when access is denied. The same copy-paste error appears on several other require* methods in this interface, such as requireViewClientScopes. This misleads implementers about the contract.

title: Client removal now calls setPermissionsEnabled, which throws in V2
body: The ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2. That class's setPermissionsEnabled (ClientPermissionsV2.java around line 193) throws UnsupportedOperationException. Deleting any client in a realm with V2 enabled will therefore fail or leave the realm in an inconsistent state. The listener should skip the V2 path, or ClientPermissionsV2 should implement the call as a no-op or resource cleanup.

title: Per-client resource shadows the all-clients grant
body: hasPermission(client, scope) only evaluates the client's own resource when one exists (lines 214-222). The all-clients fallback runs only when no resource exists for that client. If an admin has a realm-wide 'all clients' VIEW permission and later creates a client-specific permission for another scope on the same client, a resource is created for that client. The all-clients VIEW grant is then no longer considered for that client, and the admin loses access they should still have. The fallback should be evaluated in addition to, not instead of, the per-client resource.

title: Possible NPE when the all-clients resource is missing
body: In the fallback branch, getResourceTypeResource(...) can return null (for example when the schema is not supported or the Clients resource has not been created). The next line then calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) with a null resource, which causes an NPE on every client permission check instead of returning false. A null check is needed.

title: requireView() javadoc describes a boolean return instead of a throw
body: The javadoc for requireView() says 'Returns true if canView() returns true', but the method is void and should throw ForbiddenException when canView() returns false. The same wrong wording appears for requireViewClientScopes(), and the requireList/requireListClientScopes docs are similarly inconsistent with their methods.

title: Recreate exit code silently changed from 4 to 3
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changes from 4 to 3, and the new FEATURE_DISABLED takes 4. The update-compatibility command is documented as a scriptable, CI/CD-facing interface whose exit code is the contract. Any pipeline that already branches on exit code 4 for 'recreate required' will now treat it as 'feature disabled' and take the wrong action. The PR gives no rationale for renumbering an existing code instead of appending a new one. The comment about picocli ExitCode does not justify the value 3 either.

title: Feature name hardcoded in message instead of derived from the enum
body: printFeatureDisabled hardcodes the string 'rolling-updates'. The feature key is available as Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey(), so if the key is ever renamed the message will silently diverge from the actual flag. The same literal is also duplicated in the test assertion and in the docs.

title: Overwrites user-configured enabled features in the test deployment
body: createInitialDeployment calls setEnabledFeatures(List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES)) unconditionally on the FeatureSpec. If getTestKeycloakDeployment or a caller already set enabled features, they are replaced rather than merged, so the test base configuration can be silently dropped and the test no longer exercises what it was written to exercise.

title: Recreate exit code silently changed from 4 to 3
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3 and FEATURE_DISABLED takes the value 4. Any pipeline or script that already branches on exit code 4 to mean 'recreate upgrade required' will now misread a 'recreate' result as a feature-disabled error, or the reverse. The renumbering is not called out in the PR description. If the command is still considered preview, that should be stated explicitly, or the new code should be introduced without reusing a value that existing consumers depend on.

title: Feature-disabled test does not assert the exit code
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the error message. The new behaviour's key contract, documented in update-compatibility.adoc as exit code 4, is never verified, so a regression in the exit code (for example the renumbering above) would go unnoticed for the metadata and check commands.

title: setEnabledFeatures overwrites any features already configured on the test deployment
body: createInitialDeployment calls setEnabledFeatures(List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES)) on the FeatureSpec, replacing whatever enabled features getTestKeycloakDeployment() configured. If the base deployment enables other features, the tests silently lose them. The code should append to the existing list instead of replacing it.

title: Existing RECREATE exit code silently changed from 4 to 3
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3, and the new FEATURE_DISABLED takes 4. The command's exit code is a documented contract for CI/CD scripts (the update-compatibility guide tells users to branch on it). Any pipeline that treats 4 as 'rolling upgrade not possible' will now misread a feature-disabled condition as a recreate requirement, and the old value now means something else. The change is only justified if the old code 4 was never released; the PR does not state this, and the new code should be checked against the released behaviour.

title: Null-strategy deployments never enable rolling-updates, but the operator now requires it
body: createInitialDeployment returns early when updateStrategy is null, before the FeatureSpec with rolling-updates is set. The PR's own docs say the operator fails when rolling-updates is not enabled. The null-strategy case of testCacheMaxCount expects eventuallyRollingUpgradeStatus, so that test will run against an operator with the feature disabled and fail or behave incorrectly. The feature enablement must happen for every case, not only after the early return.

title: Feature setup overwrites any existing enabled features
body: setEnabledFeatures(List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES)) replaces the whole enabled list rather than appending to it. If getTestKeycloakDeployment or a future caller sets other enabled features, they are silently dropped. Merge the lists instead.

title: Feature gate runs before config validation and depends on Profile being initialised
body: Profile.isFeatureEnabled dereferences Profile.getInstance() and unboxes features.get(feature). If Profile has not been configured, or the feature key is absent from the map, this throws a NullPointerException instead of a clean CLI error. Nothing in the PR guarantees Profile is initialised before run() is reached.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects resource names as IDs via findByType on the Groups type
body: In the V2 override, the granted IDs are added using groupResource.getId() (the Resource UUID), but the caller expects group IDs (the V1 implementation used resource name suffix). Group resources in V2 are typically named after the group id via the 'all-groups' type resource, so the stored value is the Resource entity id, not the group id. Callers (UserPermissions/UsersResource count and search) pass these to session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS) and getUsersCount, which expect group model ids; the result will silently match no groups, so non-admin users with group-based VIEW_MEMBERS will see no members.

title: hasPermission looks up resources by groupId as a resource name, but group resources are named by group id differently and falls back to type resource incorrectly
body: resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) is used to find the group's resource, yet the 'all-groups' fallback uses getResourceTypeResource(...) and then checks policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). If the type resource is null (schema not initialized for the realm), resource.getScopes() / evaluatePermission will throw NPE at line 152 because resource is dereferenced without a null check on the fallback path.

title: canViewMembers/canManageMembers in V2 skip the group-independent MANAGE/VIEW fallback semantics and ignore user-level path
body: canViewMembers(group) only checks VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on the group or all-groups resource. The V1 contract and the Javadoc in GroupPermissionEvaluator say a caller with MANAGE on the group should also view members; V2 canManageMembership checks MANAGE but canViewMembers does not, so behavior is inconsistent with the documented interface.

title: canViewByGroup now calls groups().canViewMembers, changing V1 semantics and recursion through hierarchy
body: canViewByGroup previously used getGroupsWithViewPermission(group) which returned true for users with view-users roles and checked VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS. It now delegates to canViewMembers, which itself returns true when root.users().canView(), causing redundant evaluation per group for every user in the stream filter, a performance regression on large user searches (each user triggers permission evaluation across its whole group hierarchy).

title: canManage/canView/canMapRoles pass group-check results but canMapRoles in V2 now ignores MAP_ROLES semantics for group members
body: canMapRoles in V2 now grants access when the user has MANAGE on the user or manage-members on a group, and the MAP_ROLES scope check is combined with MANAGE in a single OR. This broadens who can map roles compared to the previous MAP_ROLES-only check, a security-relevant permission widening that is not covered by any test in the PR.

title: Inconsistent use of group.getId() vs resource names for group lookup in canView/canManage
body: hasPermission(group.getId(), ...) calls resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). Group resources in this PR are created by the schema with the group id as name (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup/getOrCreateResource), but GroupPermissions (V1) uses a 'group.resource.' prefix; any V2 group resource not yet created will fall through to the all-groups check and may grant access via the type-level permission without a per-group resource, which is intended but untested for the view path.

title: No test covers view of group members through GroupResource.getMembers or getSubGroups filtering
body: The new group-resource tests cover update/create/view listing, but never verify that a user with VIEW_MEMBERS can list members via /groups/{id}/members or that subgroup filtering in GroupResource.getSubGroups honours per-group view permissions after the canView(g) change. The regression risk from the removed canViewGlobal shortcut is untested.

title: getOrCreateResource switch without a default for null resourceType handled inconsistently
body: The switch on resourceType will throw NullPointerException if resourceType is null (switch on a null String), instead of the explicit IllegalStateException used for unknown types. Callers passing a null type from a malformed request will get a 500 instead of a validation error.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses group resource name as group id but resources are named by id only in V2
body: In V2 the group-type resource is looked up by type and the callback adds groupResource.getId() (a resource UUID) to the granted set, while callers use the set as group IDs for the user search filter. Resource IDs are internal store IDs, not group IDs, so the returned set does not match group IDs and the group-membership based user filtering in UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource silently returns wrong results. Resource name (group id) should be used instead.

title: hasPermission looks up group resource by name but uses null-group fallback wrongly for canView/canManage without group
body: hasPermission(null, ...) falls back to the all-groups resource and checks policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) with a resource that may be null if the Groups type resource does not exist, causing a NullPointerException rather than a denial when the resource type resource is missing.

title: GroupPermissionsV2 overrides throw UnsupportedOperationException for methods still reachable from V2 code paths
body: isPermissionsEnabled and setPermissionsEnabled throw in V2, but GroupResource.getManagementPermissions/setManagementPermissionsEnabled call AdminPermissions.management(...).groups().isPermissionsEnabled() and setPermissionsEnabled() on V2 when the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled, so these REST endpoints now throw 500 instead of returning a meaningful response.

title: canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership now fall back to group-based management without restoring the removed MANAGE check
body: canMapRoles/canManageGroupMembership in V2 now grant access via canManageByGroup (MANAGE_MEMBERS on a group), which broadens the permission model beyond what the schema documents for MAP_ROLES/MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP; this is an unintended authorization expansion relative to the stated scopes and is not covered by tests for the negative case.

title: canManage() replaced default check with hasOneAdminRole, dropping V2 permission-based fallback semantics
body: GroupPermissions.canManage() now only checks MANAGE_USERS role, while the removed canManageDefault delegated to the users permission evaluator. Callers relying on canManage() for the realm-level grant no longer get consistent behaviour with UserPermissions.canManage(), which uses the same role check but the base class is also used for V1 where permission-based realm-level manage was previously evaluated via users().

title: Javadoc for canManage/canView/canManageGroupMembership mentions group-chain permissions the implementation does not check for every method
body: The javadoc for canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership claims MANAGE_MEMBERS of the group chain grants access, and canImpersonate docs are inconsistent with code; docs and behaviour diverge, misleading integrators.

title: Group removal listener is now only registered under the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check at registration time
body: registerListener now checks the feature flag once when registering and no longer per event; if the feature flag state changes at runtime or differs between registration and dispatch, behaviour changes. More importantly the listener is now skipped entirely when the flag is off, which is the intended behaviour, but the change is unrelated to the PR's stated scope and untested.

title: Test class has stray double semicolon and no negative test for group membership view via users endpoint
body: The field declaration ends with ';;' and the view-members test only checks positive visibility; there is no test asserting that a user outside the group stays hidden when only VIEW on Groups is granted, which is the core security property of the new Groups resource type.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission adds resource name where group IDs are expected by callers
body: In V2 the resource for a group is looked up by ID (hasPermission(groupId,...) calls resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)), so resources are named by group id; this is consistent. However the V2 loop over findByType adds groupResource.getId() (the internal resource UUID) to the granted set, not the group ID/name. Callers (UsersResource, BruteForceUsersResource, getUsersCount) pass this set to session.users() as group IDs, so the filter compares the wrong identifiers and group-based user visibility silently returns nothing for V2.

title: policyStore.findByResource called on possibly null resource
body: When the all-groups resource type resource is not found, getResourceTypeResource can return null, and the code then calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) with a null resource, causing an NPE. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission (line 111). Null must be checked before the store lookup.

title: canViewMembers in V2 ignores the global view/manage permission and group-specific scopes inconsistently
body: canViewMembers returns true only for users().canView(), then checks VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on the group. canManageMembers similarly. But canManageMembership in V2 checks only MANAGE_USERS role and not users().canManage(), so an admin with manage-users permission via FGAP is denied membership management while canManageMembers passes; this breaks the documented contract in GroupPermissionEvaluator that canManageMembership is true for MANAGE on the group.

title: canView/canManage(null) evaluation grants via VIEW/MANAGE on all-groups resource only without checking ownership
body: canView() and canManage() call hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) which, when resource is missing, falls back to the all-groups resource type. Any policy attached to the all-groups resource with VIEW or MANAGE is treated as a global group permission, so a single-group permission can be interpreted as global list/manage rights through the fallback path when evaluated via groupId null.

title: isImpersonatable Javadoc/annotation placement leaves grantIfNoPermission undocumented and deprecation misplaced
body: The @Deprecated annotation was moved onto isImpersonatable while the Javadoc for it was removed, and grantIfNoPermission lost its blank-line separation. The interface now has an undocumented deprecated method immediately followed by an unrelated method, reducing clarity of the API contract.

title: Group listing no longer lets users with view-only global access see all groups
body: The previous code computed canView() once and short-circuited the per-group check. The new code calls groupsEvaluator::canView per element, which for V2 performs a permission evaluation per group (performance regression) and, combined with the now-empty set semantics, can filter out groups a caller with global view should see if canView(group) does not short-circuit on global roles consistently.

title: Permission resource ID check drops scope grants from all-users permissions
body: hasPermission now requires permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()). When evaluated against the all-users resource type resource, permissions returned are associated with that resource, but for user-specific resources the matching resource may be a different one; additionally getResourceId may be null for some permission types, causing NPE. The added check changes semantics without test coverage.

title: Stray double semicolon and unused topGroup initialisation style issue in test
body: The field declaration ends with ';;' and the test class sets a group name field that duplicates the group creation; minor, but indicates the test was not reviewed carefully. Also testManageGroupMembership contains a dangling blank line with trailing whitespace.

title: English file path derivation is fragile and can produce wrong or nonexistent paths
body: The English counterpart path is computed with regex replaceAll on the absolute path: replaceAll("resources-community", "resources") then replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties"). Any directory containing an underscore or the substring 'resources-community' elsewhere in the path, or a file without a locale suffix, will be rewritten incorrectly. When the English file is missing a RuntimeException is thrown, aborting verification for the whole module rather than reporting a message.

title: Keys present only in the translation are checked against an empty English value, and missing English file throws
body: getEnglishValue returns "" for keys missing in English, so the sanitizer decides HTML policy from an empty string and silently accepts whatever HTML the translation contains for keys that do not exist in the source. Additionally, a missing English file is converted into a RuntimeException rather than a MojoExecutionException, so the plugin crashes with an unhelpful stack trace instead of a verification message.

title: Unescaping HTML entities after sanitization can reintroduce unsafe markup in the comparison
body: sanitized = unescapeHtml4(sanitized) runs after the policy sanitizer. The comparison therefore accepts values in which entities such as <script> were decoded back into raw tags in the 'sanitized' string, and the check only flags a difference when the sanitized and original differ. Since value was also unescaped in normalizeValue, a translation containing '<img onerror=...>' is unescaped to a real tag before sanitizing, so the sanitizer does see it; but the post-sanitize unescape can turn entities the sanitizer intentionally kept into tags that the policy would reject, making the verifier's pass/fail result unreliable.

title: Anchor validation compares tags pairwise without checking counts or using the replaced value consistently
body: santizeAnchors walks anchors in the translation and in English with two independent matchers, and removes the matched English anchor text from value via replaceFirst on the translation. If the translation has more anchors than English, englishMatcher.find() fails and the message is added, but if it has fewer, extra English anchors are never reported. Also replaceFirst with a quoted pattern removes the first occurrence in value, which may not be the anchor just matched, so the check can pass or fail based on text position rather than structure.

title: Policy factories are instance fields with non-private visibility and the HTML_TAGS pattern is package-private
body: POLICY_SOME_HTML, POLICY_NO_HTML and HTML_TAGS are declared without modifiers at package level, while sibling constants are private static. This is inconsistent and makes them mutable from the package; they should be static final to avoid rebuilding policies per instance.

title: Tests rely on fixtures whose English counterparts are not present and do not cover the passing path
body: The new tests call verify() on *_de.properties fixtures, but the English path derivation resolves to *_en.properties in the same directory; the tests never assert that a valid translation produces no messages, nor that a correct anchor passes. The duplicate-key test was relaxed from Matchers.contains to hasItem, weakening the assertion so extra unexpected messages go undetected.

title: Fixture contains an unclosed tag that is also used as the English source
body: The fixture 'key=Some <div>tag</div' is malformed (missing '>'). The test asserts an 'Illegal HTML' message, but the failure may be caused by the malformed syntax rather than the intended illegal tag, so the test does not verify what its name says.

title: Translated instruction text replaces the link-bearing content with a generic sentence that drops the app names
body: The totpStep1 string is changed to a generic sentence, removing the FreeOTP and Google Authenticator references and links. This is an unrelated content change to a translation file that loses information users need to set up OTP. It appears to be a side effect of the sanitizer change rather than an intended translation fix.

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with untranslated Italian text
body: The new value 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' is Italian, not Lithuanian, so Lithuanian users will see a foreign-language instruction. The string should be translated or the original kept.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: Same problem as the account bundle: the value is an Italian sentence, so the Lithuanian login page shows untranslated content.

title: Hungarian emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml key prefixed with *** corrupting the key name
body: The line was changed to start with '***emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml=', so the property key is now '***emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml' and the real key is no longer translated. The HTML email body falls back to English or is missing.

title: Turkish identityProviderLinkBodyHtml changed whitespace inside tags and made the anchor unbalanced
body: The closing tags were changed from '' to '' and ' {1} ' spacing was altered; while '' is not valid HTML, the changes are unrelated to sanitization and break rendering of the email.

title: Dutch emailVerificationBodyHtml contains a malformed closing tag
body:
The line was changed from '

' ... '

U kunt' to '' which is a malformed tag, making the HTML body render incorrectly.

title: Lithuanian email anchors changed to invalid href=LT"..." syntax
body: Several anchors were changed from href="{0}" to href=LT"{0}" (missing the opening quote before LT), producing broken attributes in verification and password-reset emails and in the executeActions email. Links in these emails will not work.

title: Persian emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml change removes the space before a closing tag only by corrupting the markup
body: The original contained '< p>' malformed tag which was corrected, but this is a content-unrelated fix bundled into a sanitizer PR; unrelated edits make review of the real intent harder.

title: Slovak error-invalid-multivalued-size fix mixes change to plural form key
body: The new value uses {2,choice,...} for the second placeholder and fixes {1} to {2} for the maximum, which is a correct fix, but the trailing newline removal and reordering in the same file was not needed for the sanitizer change; the bundle also keeps impersonateTitleHtml with a stray closing removed, changing markup unrelated to the PR.

title: Czech error-invalid-multivalued-size message uses choice format with unexpected plural rules
body: The added choice pattern uses 1<hodnoty|4<hodnot which is a Czech plural rule that may not match Czech grammar for the value 2-4 (should be 'hodnoty'), so counts 2-4 render with the wrong form.

title: Multivalued size message now uses choice format that the admin UI does not parse with the same placeholder
body: The message changed from value(s) to a choice format but the admin UI in js/apps uses {{0}} style placeholders for this key elsewhere; mixing styles risks the key rendering literally in the admin console.

title: English reference path derivation breaks for non-resources-community and mangles paths
body: The English counterpart path is computed by regex replacing '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties' with '_en.properties' on the whole absolute path. Any '_' in parent directories (e.g. a checkout path like /home/user/my_repo/...) is not affected since the regex requires '.properties' suffix, but the file-name pattern is applied greedily from the first underscore-containing segment of the filename only; more importantly for files like 'messages_zh_CN.properties' it works, yet for the theme-verifier fixtures (e.g. 'noHtml_de.properties' -> 'noHtml_en.properties') it is fine. The real issue: files under themes/src/main/resources/ (not resources-community) map to themselves only when the locale is en, and for non-community English files the path is unchanged, so verifySafeHtml reads and compares a file to itself. Also if the English file does not exist the code throws RuntimeException, aborting the whole verification instead of reporting a message, which crashes the Maven build for any locale file lacking an English counterpart.

title: Missing English file or IO failure throws RuntimeException instead of reporting
body: verifySafeHtml throws RuntimeException on IOException for both the target file and the English file. verify() only catches IOException, so the RuntimeException escapes the Mojo, producing an unhelpful stack trace rather than a verification message. Keys with no English counterpart are handled, but a missing English file is not.

title: Anchor replacement removes first occurrence anywhere, not at the matched position
body: santizeAnchors uses value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "") which strips the first textual occurrence of the anchor tag, not the one the matcher found. With repeated identical anchors, or when the translation has an anchor text that appears earlier in a different position, the wrong tag is removed and the comparison against the English tag list becomes inconsistent. Also the English matcher is advanced in lockstep with no check that the number of anchors matches, so a translation with fewer anchors passes silently.

title: Policy and pattern fields are package-visible instance fields
body: POLICY_SOME_HTML, POLICY_NO_HTML and HTML_TAGS are non-private, non-static instance fields rebuilt per object. They should be static final constants; the policy factory is relatively expensive to construct and is needlessly recreated for every file verified.

title: Test resources for noHtml/illegalHtmlTag depend on sibling _en files that are not checked for the intended failure
body: verifyNoHtmlAllowed and verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected assert only that 'Illegal HTML' appears, using hasItem. Because verify() also aggregates other messages, these tests could pass for unrelated reasons (e.g. a missing-English-file path or anchor message). Assertions should be specific to the key/file, and the positive case (valid translation with allowed <b> when English has HTML) is not tested.

title: Fixture is unclosed HTML and the test does not verify it is the English file being checked
body: illegalHtmlTag_en.properties contains '<div>tag</div' (missing '>'), which is a malformed tag rather than a clearly illegal one; the test name suggests an illegal tag but the fixture tests a broken closing tag. The fixture is also an English file, so the test exercises the English path only, not a translation comparison.

title: Finnish totpStep1 replaced with a Finnish-less English-Italian placeholder string
body: The Finnish, Lithuanian, Swedish, Slovak and Norwegian account/login translations were replaced with lines that are not translations at all. Here totpStep1 in account messages_fi is replaced with a Finnish sentence that lost its meaning, and in messages_lt.properties totpStep1 is replaced by the Italian string 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. This shows untranslated Italian text to Lithuanian users. The change removes the link to the FreeOTP/Google Play apps instead of fixing the HTML sanitization, which is a content regression rather than a sanitizer fix.

title: Lithuanian account message replaced with Italian text
body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian account bundle is now 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see Italian in the TOTP setup page. The original Lithuanian translation was removed to satisfy the sanitizer rather than fixing the markup.

title: Lithuanian login loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: loginTotpStep1 is replaced by Italian 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. The Lithuanian translation of the app-install step is lost and Lithuanian users see Italian.

title: Hungarian emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml had a stray *** prefix in the diff context
body: The diff shows the key 'emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml' line prefixed with '***' in the change, which is a corrupt key name; the line in the file would no longer match the key and the Hungarian HTML email body would be unusable/ignored. Verify the key is not corrupted.

title: Lithuanian email href changed from broken to correct but other anchors left malformed
body: The change alters href=LT"..." to href="...", which is correct, but the full file still contains other malformed markup; the sanitizer change masks the original HTML error instead of addressing content that is actually broken in emails.

title: Norwegian identityProviderLinkBody changed by removing HTML and changing meaning
body: identityProviderLinkBody in Norwegian replaces {1} with plain {1}, removing the emphasis. This is an alteration of translated content made to appease a sanitizer rule, not a fix of wrong markup, and it changes the rendered message for the plain-text version too.

title: Dutch emailVerificationBodyHtml unbalanced tag change
body:
The change closes a

with '' typo fixed to '

' which is correct, but the associated diff indicates a broken closing tag was in the original; no validation was added to the verifier to catch this class of error, so the fix relies on manual edits across 40+ files.

title: Bulk whitespace-only edits across many locale files
body:
Dozens of login messages only change '
' to '
'. These are noisy diffs that do not change rendering, obscuring the actual sanitizer-driven content changes such as the Italian/Lithuanian substitutions.

title: Slovak error-invalid-multivalued-size uses wrong argument index in choice
body: The final key in the Slovak file's diff changes the second choice from {1,choice,...} to {2,choice,...} for the maximum count, which is the intended fix, but the original line in the Slovak file ends with a value using {1} for max; the changed line also removes the trailing newline. Also impersonateTitleHtml has an unmatched '' removed, a correct fix, but the diff for the other edits mixes content changes with markup changes in one commit.

title: Czech multivalued-size choice format has inconsistent plural forms
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size in Czech uses choice patterns '0#hodnot|1#hodnotu|1<hodnoty|4<hodnot' which is inconsistent with the other locales and with the English pattern; the value 1 uses 'hodnotu' correctly but the 2-4 case relies on the '1<hodnoty' rule with a '4<' boundary that drops the 2-4 distinction incorrectly.

title: Changed placeholder syntax breaks i18next interpolation in account UI
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size changes from i18next-style {{0}} placeholders to MessageFormat {0} with a choice clause. The account UI is a React/i18next app which interpolates {{...}} and does not evaluate MessageFormat choice syntax, so the rendered message will show the raw '{0}' and '{2,choice,...}' text to users.

title: Admin UI message uses MessageFormat placeholders while the admin UI uses i18next double braces
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size is changed to {0} / {2,choice,...} syntax, but this admin-ui bundle is consumed by i18next which expects {{0}}. Users will see raw placeholders and choice markup in the admin console.

title: Only a whitespace change for CLAIM.<NAME> in Chinese help text
body: The change removes a space before '>' in 'CLAIM.<NAME >' to 'CLAIM.<NAME>'. This is a correction of an unrelated typo that is bundled into a sanitizer change and does not match the sanitizer rationale.

title: Admin theme message switched to MessageFormat choice syntax without matching renderer
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size now uses {2,choice,...} syntax. Other admin messages in this file use plain {n} placeholders consumed by the admin UI; if that UI does not run MessageFormat choice evaluation, users will see literal choice markup.

title: Login theme error-invalid-multivalued-size uses choice format while previous wording 'value(s)' was intended as plural-neutral
body: The English message now emits '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' which requires MessageFormat rendering at the caller. Callers that format with simple substitution will print the raw choice pattern for every locale, and the change is applied to English but other locales (e.g. ka, ko) were given different forms, producing inconsistent behavior.

title: English source path derivation is fragile and can resolve to the wrong file or throw
body: The English file path is computed with replaceAll on the absolute path: 'resources-community' -> 'resources' and a regex '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties' -> '_en.properties'. Any directory containing an underscore or dash-letters before '.properties' in the absolute path (e.g. a checkout path like /home/u/my_repo/...) is rewritten by the second regex only at the final '.properties' occurrence, which is fine, but the first replaceAll also rewrites any path segment containing 'resources-community' anywhere, and for the admin/email files whose names have no locale suffix the regex can eat part of the base name. When the derived file does not exist, the code throws a RuntimeException rather than a MojoExecutionException, aborting the whole verification run for every module instead of reporting the problem.

title: Checked IOException from file reading is turned into unchecked RuntimeException
body: verifySafeHtml() reads the target and English bundles and wraps IOException in RuntimeException, while verify() is declared to throw MojoExecutionException for read failures. A missing or unreadable file therefore escapes as an unchecked exception that the Maven plugin does not handle gracefully, changing the error contract of verify().

title: Sanitizer output unescaped with unescapeHtml4 can mask real illegal HTML
body: The sanitized output is passed through StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4 before comparison, and the input value was also unescaped in normalizeValue. Because both sides are unescaped, an input containing an escaped tag such as <script> is decoded to <script> on the input side and then compared against sanitizer output that would have stripped it; the comparison is no longer a faithful check that the raw translation contains only allowed markup, so some illegal HTML in translations may pass verification silently.

title: Anchor validation compares only in lockstep and skips extra or missing anchors
body: santizeAnchors iterates target anchors and advances the English matcher only when it finds one; when englishMatcher.find() fails or the tag differs it records a message and breaks, but if the target has fewer anchors than the English source, extra English anchors are never reported. Also replaceFirst with Pattern.quote removes the first occurrence in the value which may not be the matched position, so the stripped string can be wrong when the same tag appears more than once.

title: Policy fields are non-private mutable instance fields and pattern fields are package-visible
body: POLICY_SOME_HTML, POLICY_NO_HTML and HTML_TAGS are declared without modifiers and are recreated per instance, though they are constant. The PolicyFactory construction per file is also wasteful; these should be private static final.

title: Tests use fixtures whose English counterparts are not present, so results depend on the path rewrite
body: The tests for illegalHtmlTag_en.properties, noHtml_de.properties and changedAnchor_de.properties rely on the English path derived from the fixture location (e.g. noHtml_de -> noHtml_en). Fixtures like duplicateKeys_en and illegalHtmlTag_en map to themselves, so the illegal-HTML test for illegalHtmlTag_en actually compares the file against itself and only passes because of the unterminated '<div>' tag; the tests do not isolate the behaviour they claim to verify, and no test covers a valid HTML translation passing.

title: Translation replaced with English-language/unrelated text and HTML links removed
body: totpStep1 was changed from a localized instruction naming FreeOTP/Google Authenticator with links to a shortened sentence. The new value is still a Finnish sentence, but the links the translation previously provided (FreeOTP, Google Play) are dropped, so users lose the download guidance. Several sibling PR changes (e.g. messages_lt in account and login) replace the Lithuanian translation with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), which is a wrong-language string shipped to Lithuanian users.

title: Lithuanian account message replaced by Italian text
body: totpStep1 now reads 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' which is Italian, not Lithuanian. The same wrong-language string is introduced in login/messages_lt.properties, so Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction.

title: Chinese string uses Traditional Chinese text and a different locale from the file
body: totpStep1 is set to '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：' which mixes Traditional characters (手機, 應用程式) into the Simplified Chinese file; it should be Simplified (手机, 应用程序).

title: Hungarian HTML email key corrupted by a stray '***' prefix
body: The emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml line was changed to start with '***emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml=' in the diff, which would be an invalid/unknown property key (the key becomes '***emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml') so the real key is no longer translated and falls back to the English default, and the literal '***' is left in a properties file.

title: Anchor href quoting changed in Lithuanian email HTML, adding links to a literal LT string
body: The original href=LT"{0}" was corrected to href="{0}" in the HTML bodies, which is a fix, but the change also affects emailVerificationBodyHtml etc. Meanwhile the properties remain with malformed markup elsewhere; ensure the translated email HTML templates still match the anchors expected by the verifier.

title: Dutch HTML body fix made outside the stated issue, still altering content
body:
The emailVerificationBodyHtml change fixes an unclosed

but the new string also includes an escaped quote change; these unrelated edits widen the diff beyond the sanitizer fix and risk unintentional translation changes.

title: Trailing key-value corrected but the multivalued-size choice pattern is wrong for some values
body: The corrected error-invalid-multivalued-size uses {2,choice,...} for the upper bound and {1,choice,...} for the lower bound; the choice forms in this file (0#hodnôt|1#hodnotu|1<hodnoty|4<hodnôt) do not cover the 2-4 plural case correctly for values between 2 and 4 in the second branch, producing incorrect grammatical forms.

title: Choice format in multivalued-size message is copied into the English key and changes rendering for admin consumers
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size is changed to use a {2,choice,...} subformat, but this key is consumed via MessageFormat without the same argument typing for all callers; the English string in the admin theme and login theme now both depend on the choice syntax, and the generic change to '{{0}}'-style placeholders to '{0}' in the js/admin messages also changes how the JS i18n layer interpolates the value.

title: Null check for rawTokenId is wrong (checks grantType twice)
body: The constructor checks `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` a second time instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted silently, and the message is also wrong. Should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

title: Token ID parsing throws on any non-encoded id containing ':' with wrong length
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId splits on the first ':' and throws IllegalArgumentException if the prefix is not exactly 6 chars. Any token id from a non-standard source (or a raw UUID with a colon, or legacy formats) causes an exception rather than falling back to UNKNOWN as done for ids without ':'. Callers (introspection, userinfo) that receive such ids will fail with 500 instead of degrading gracefully.

title: Token type derived from request-wide client attribute, not from the token being created
body: getShouldUseLightweightToken(session) reads session.getContext().getClient(), which is the requesting client, not necessarily the client the token is issued for (e.g. token exchange to another audience, or refresh flows), and the token mapper logic uses the same helper. The encoded token type may not match the actual token format produced, making the encoded context unreliable for the stated use (lightweight detection).

title: Unsynchronized lazy refresh of shared maps on every miss
body: getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut mutate the shared ConcurrentHashMaps during token issuance and token id parsing. The grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts maps are also written without any atomicity across the two maps, so concurrent readers can see them inconsistent.
