Also, an attacker-supplied unknown shortcut in a token id triggers a full stream scan of provider factories on every request (no negative caching), a cheap DoS amplification.

title: postInit throws on duplicate shortcuts but init/postInit use non-thread-safe HashMap for shortcut tables
body: The shortcut validation compares map sizes, which only detects duplicate shortcuts that collide with the same key; if two grants share a shortcut, one silently overwrites the other in grantsByShortcuts and the sizes still differ only by accident. The size check is an indirect and incomplete duplicate detection. Also OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() has no default, so third-party grant factories break at compile/startup.

title: Cast of getProviderFactory result may throw ClassCastException
body: sessionFactory.getProviderFactory(OAuth2GrantType.class, grantType) returns a ProviderFactory that is cast directly to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without checking; a non-OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation would fail at token issuance.

title: Token ID encoding can throw during token issuance for unregistered grant types
body: initToken calls encoder.encodeTokenId, which throws IllegalStateException when the grant type has no registered shortcut (e.g. a grant set on clientSessionCtx that is not an OAuth2GrantType factory, or tokens created by other paths that never set GRANT_TYPE, where the default 'na' is used). Token creation now fails for flows that previously worked, rather than falling back to a plain id.

title: Blank line removed while adding grant type attribute
body: The edit removes a blank line and inserts setAttribute in its place, which is cosmetic, but the attribute is set after the note and before the client is set; fine. Minor: no functional issue, included only as the diff replaced a blank line.

title: Refresh grant type set after the original grant type was lost; overrides initial value for refreshed tokens
body: validateToken sets GRANT_TYPE to refresh_token on the client session context, but this is only applied on the refresh path. Other paths (e.g. the RefreshTokenGrantType itself, which does not call createTokenResponse) rely on this implicit setting, so the encoded grant in tokens depends on which code path ran, making the encoded grant type inconsistent.

title: Grant type taken from context.getGrantType() which is the raw form parameter
body: context.getGrantType() returns the raw grant_type form parameter, which may be an arbitrary attacker-controlled string. It is stored as the grant type and, if it does not match a registered shortcut, encodeTokenId throws, causing a 500 instead of a proper OAuth error. Validation should happen before use.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher logic is inverted
body: The matcher returns false when the shortcut at substring(3,5) EQUALS the expected shortcut: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. This means a correct token ID is rejected and a wrong one accepted. It also uses substring(3,5) while the encoded format places the grant shortcut at chars 4-5 (index 4..6), so the offset is wrong too.

title: Negative tests use try/catch(RuntimeException) that also swallows the Assert.fail
body: testIncorrectGrantType wraps Assert.fail inside a try catching RuntimeException; AssertionError is not a RuntimeException so it propagates, but the test is still not asserting the specific exception type. Tests for unknown session/token shortcuts and wrong length are missing, and no test covers the 'no ':' ' id parsing or the ClientSessionContext path.

title: Test/code comment mismatch: grantType null-check message
body: The second requireNonNull message reads 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' but checks grantType, misleading maintainers reading the constructor.

title: Null check for rawTokenId duplicates grantType check
body: The constructor checks `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` but tests grantType again. rawTokenId is never null-checked, so a null rawTokenId is accepted and the intended validation is missing (the message also refers to the wrong variable).

title: Token ID parsing assumes fixed 6-char prefix, length check throws on any unexpected input
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException for any token ID whose prefix before ':' is not exactly 6 characters or has unknown shortcuts. Callers reading tokens (introspection, userinfo, account REST) will fail hard on malformed or foreign IDs instead of degrading gracefully to UNKNOWN, which the no-colon branch already does. Inconsistent handling can turn a bad/legacy-format token into a 500 error.

title: Null token ID causes NullPointerException
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId calls encodedTokenId.indexOf without a null check; a null id (e.g. token without jti) causes an NPE rather than a clear result.

title: Shortcut maps are populated in postInit but used in init-time-independent lookups; unsafe for lazily-discovered grants
body: getGrantTypeByShortcut/getShortcutByGrantType mutate ConcurrentHashMaps from request threads and call sessionFactory.getProviderFactory on every miss. Unknown grant names or shortcuts trigger a full stream scan on every token request and a map write, causing repeated lookup cost and potentially unbounded map growth from attacker-influenced values only if grant names are influenced; the rebuild also isn't atomic with the two-map consistency check.

title: ClassCastException risk when casting provider factories
body: getShortcutByGrantType casts the result of getProviderFactory(OAuth2GrantType.class, ...) to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without checking; any custom OAuth2GrantType factory not implementing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory would throw ClassCastException during token creation.

title: Token ID encoding throws for grants without shortcut, breaking token creation
body: initToken now calls encoder.encodeTokenId, which throws IllegalStateException when the grant type is unknown (the default when no GRANT_TYPE attribute is set, e.g. flows that never set Constants.GRANT_TYPE such as login/browser flows, token refresh paths or other callers of createClientAccessToken). Access token creation can therefore fail for legitimate flows instead of degrading to an 'na' grant.

title: Encoding fails for grant types that are not in the factory map
body: encodeTokenId throws when the grant type has no shortcut, so any grant type added without an OAuth2GrantTypeFactory shortcut (or a custom grant) breaks access token issuance rather than falling back to the UNKNOWN shortcut used elsewhere.

title: Grant type attribute set from request params, not the actual grant
body: createTokenResponse sets GRANT_TYPE from context.getGrantType(), which reads the raw form parameter grant_type. Token exchange and PreAuthorized paths set their own constant, so the stored value can disagree with the grant actually processed; the token ID shortcut then reflects client input rather than the server-side grant.

title: Refresh grant type hard-coded in validateToken
body: validateToken sets GRANT_TYPE to REFRESH_TOKEN for token recreation, but this path can be reached from non-refresh callers (e.g. introspection/userinfo validation), giving the recreated token an inaccurate grant shortcut in its ID.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher logic is inverted and fails to validate
body: The matcher returns false when the grant shortcut equals the expected value (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`), i.e. it rejects exactly the correct token. Also the shortcut is at chars 4-5 (index 4..6 of the 6-char prefix), and substring(3,5) is off by one. Event assertions will fail or pass incorrectly.

title: Incorrect-grant test catches any RuntimeException
body: testIncorrectGrantType wraps the call in try/catch RuntimeException, so the test passes even when the Assert.fail fails path is hit inside... actually Assert.fail throws AssertionError (not caught), but any unrelated RuntimeException also passes the test. Should use assertThrows with IllegalArgumentException.

title: Error message names wrong parameter
body: The second requireNonNull on grantType uses the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed', which is misleading; it is the rawTokenId that is not checked at all.

title: Null check for rawTokenId is wrong and rawTokenId is never validated
body: The constructor checks `grantType` twice; the second check on line 73 should be `rawTokenId`. As written, a null rawTokenId is accepted silently, and the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' is never produced. This is a copy-paste defect in the validation intended to guard the field.

title: Parsing an encoded token ID with a colon in a legacy UUID-only id is treated inconsistently
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId uses indexOf(':') and, when no colon is present, treats the whole string as raw id. But when the colon is present and the prefix length is not 6, it throws IllegalArgumentException. Any caller that passes an arbitrary or attacker-controlled token ID (e.g. from an introspection request or a Details value) can trigger an exception path; callers must handle IllegalArgumentException, and the contract is not documented or enforced consistently at call sites. Also, the grant-type lookup for unknown shortcuts can trigger factory scans on every call with attacker-supplied input, since getGrantTypeByShortcut refreshes maps on each miss.

title: Cache-miss refresh performs provider lookup and map mutation on every unknown shortcut/grant
body: getGrantTypeByShortcut and getShortcutByGrantType re-scan provider factories and write to ConcurrentHashMaps whenever a lookup misses. Because token IDs can be supplied by clients (for introspection/userinfo), an attacker can send arbitrary unknown grant shortcuts forcing repeated stream scans and map writes on each request. Negative results are not cached, so the cost is paid per request.

title: Grant maps are non-atomic across two maps, so reads can see inconsistent state
body: grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts are updated with two separate put calls, and the lookup methods read them separately. A concurrent thread can observe a shortcut present in one map but not the other, causing getShortcutByGrantType to return null and encodeTokenId to throw IllegalStateException for a valid grant. The two maps are also not kept in sync if a shortcut is reused, since the duplicate check runs only in postInit.

title: UNKNOWN grant placeholder collides with a shortcut namespace and breaks duplicate validation
body: The placeholder 'na' is inserted into both maps after the provider scan, so the size check at line 82 is always compared against an extra entry. If any grant factory ever declares shortcut 'na', it is silently overwritten by the placeholder rather than rejected, undermining the validation the check is meant to provide.

title: Potential NullPointerException when client session context has no user session
body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext dereferences clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() and calls getPersistenceState and isOffline without null checks. Callers such as the token exchange and refresh paths may supply contexts where the user session is not yet attached, so token creation fails with an NPE instead of a clear error.

title: Token ID encoding can throw on unknown grant and breaks token creation for grants that do not set GRANT_TYPE
body: initToken now calls encodeTokenId, which throws IllegalStateException for UNKNOWN session/token types or unrecognised grant types. Grant paths that do not set Constants.GRANT_TYPE (for example the grants touched only partially, or any custom grant without a factory shortcut) will fall back to 'na' and encoding throws for unknown session types. A regression here would make access token issuance fail for existing flows instead of degrading gracefully.

title: Grant type attribute is set from context.getGrantType() which is the raw form parameter
body: createTokenResponse writes context.getGrantType(), which is the raw grant_type form value, into the session note. For token-exchange and other grants this value may differ from the factory id, and a missing or invalid grant_type is stored as null, which then triggers Assert/IllegalState in encoding via a null grant. The grant identifier should come from the grant factory rather than a request parameter.

title: Blank line removed alongside functional change
body: The diff replaces an empty line with the setAttribute call, which is harmless, but the grant type is set on sessionContext only after the note is set, while other grants set it on clientSessionCtx after attachSession. Consistency between grant implementations is lost, making it easy to miss the attribute on new grants.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong offsets
body: The matcher returns false when the grant shortcut equals the expected one (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`), so correct token IDs fail and incorrect ones pass. The substring offset 3..5 is also wrong for the 'st+tt+gt:' format where the grant shortcut occupies chars 4..6 (index 4 to 6). Event assertions on TOKEN_ID will therefore misbehave in the integration tests.

title: Negative test cannot fail properly and assertion is swallowed
body: testIncorrectGrantType catches RuntimeException, which also catches the AssertionError produced by Assert.fail? No, AssertionError is not a RuntimeException, so the fail is not swallowed; however the test catches any RuntimeException including NPEs, so it passes for unrelated bugs. It should assert the specific IllegalArgumentException and message.

title: Grant maps are package-private mutable fields used by tests
body: grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts are package-private non-final fields, which the test mutates directly. Production code and tests share mutable internals, and the test bypasses postInit, so the test does not exercise the real initialization path.

title: Recovery codes are written to user storage in plaintext
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generatedCodes list to JSON and passes it as the credential data to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). The local-storage path instead stores a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel built from the same codes, which is designed to hold hashed codes (RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode exists for this). External user storage providers therefore receive and persist usable plaintext recovery codes, which a storage backend or anyone with read access to it can use to bypass MFA. The user-storage branch should store hashed codes, matching the local representation, and verification should compare hashes.

title: Recovery codes in user storage are never consumed after use
body: isValid for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks membership in the stored list and never removes or marks the used code. In local storage each code is single-use, so a code entered once can be entered again here indefinitely. The test provider also has no test asserting that a used code is rejected, so this gap is not caught. The provider's contract should require consuming the code, or the code should be documented as a limitation.

title: Credential id is dropped when recovery codes are returned from getCredentials
body: updateCredential assigns a generated id to recoveryCodesModel, but getCredentials rebuilds the model with RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...), which does not copy that id. The returned credential therefore has no id matching the stored one. The authenticator then calls removeStoredCredentialById with that id once all codes are used, so the removal targets a non-existent credential and the spent codes remain stored.

title: Removal of exhausted codes does not work for user-storage credentials
body: getCredential now returns federated (user storage) credentials first, but the removal call at line 86 uses credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(), which only operates on local-storage credentials. When the exhausted codes come from user storage, nothing is removed. The exhausted credential stays in storage, and getCredential keeps finding it on later logins. The removal should go through a path that handles federated credentials, or the mismatch should be handled explicitly.

title: Unguarded Optional.get() when no recovery credential exists
body: The constructor calls credentialModelOpt.get() without checking isPresent(). If the user has no recovery credential in either storage, this throws NoSuchElementException during page rendering instead of producing a controlled error.

title: Recovery codes in user storage are never marked as used, so they can be replayed
body: isValid for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks that the submitted code is present in the stored JSON list. Nothing records that a code was consumed. The local-DB path tracks used codes via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.getNextRecoveryAuthnCode/allCodesUsed, so this is a behavioural gap. In the user-storage path, allCodesUsed() can never become true, so the authenticator never removes the credential or requires regeneration, and a recovery code can be used repeatedly. The same reasoning applies to the new getCredential lookup order in RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils, which prefers federated credentials that never expire.

title: Plaintext recovery codes are sent to external user storage
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generatedCodes list to JSON and passes it to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...). Whenever the user storage accepts the type, the raw recovery codes are written to the external store, which is not under Keycloak's control. The local path hashes the codes (via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues). Storing raw single-use secrets in a federated backend is a credential-exposure risk and should be hashed or the user storage should be restricted.

title: Serialization failure wrapped as a generic RuntimeException
body: JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString throws IOException, which is rethrown as a bare RuntimeException with no message. Any failure surfaces as an unhelpful 500 during required-action processing. A more specific exception or message would make diagnosis easier.

title: Unchecked Optional.get() on credential lookup
body: credentialModelOpt.get() is called without isPresent(). If the user has no recovery codes in either storage, this throws NoSuchElementException while rendering the login page. The old code had the same unchecked get(), but the new helper now returns Optional explicitly, so the caller should handle the empty case.

title: Typo in authenticator config alias
body: The config alias is set to "delayed-suthenticator-config", which is a misspelling of 'authenticator'. It is harmless to behaviour but is a copy-paste defect in test code that should be corrected for clarity.

title: Recovery code validation in user storage never consumes the used code
body: isValid for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks whether the input matches any stored code and never removes or marks the used code as consumed. The authenticator calls isValid and then relies on the stored credential's used state to decide when all codes are spent. Against this provider, a recovery code can be replayed indefinitely, and the test suite cannot detect this. The test provider should either mark codes used or the test should assert single use.

title: removeStoredCredentialById cannot remove a federated recovery credential
body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential prefers the federated (user storage) credential. When all codes are used, the code calls removeStoredCredentialById, which only targets local storage. For a federated credential the removal is a no-op, so the exhausted credential stays in user storage and the user keeps getting the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action on every login without the credential actually being cleared.

title: Recovery codes written to user storage do not remove the previous local credential
body: When updateCredential succeeds in user storage, the existing local recovery-codes credential is left untouched, and when it fails the local provider's createCredential is called without first clearing the old one. Regenerating codes can leave stale local credentials alongside the new federated ones. getCredential then returns only the federated one, so the stale local set is silently orphaned, and the state can diverge. Compare with how OTP handling deals with replacement.

title: Stored credential lookup still uses the old path in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean
body: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls Optional.get() on the result of getCredential without checking presence, so a user with no recovery codes in either store gets a NoSuchElementException while rendering the login form instead of a meaningful error.

title: getCredentials dereferences a possibly null MyUser
body: getMyUser(user) can return null when the user is not in the map, and getCredentials then accesses myUser.recoveryCodes and myUser.otp without a null check, causing an NPE. isConfiguredFor and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream guard against this.

title: Typo in the delayed authenticator config alias
body: The config alias is set to "delayed-suthenticator-config", a misspelling of "authenticator". It is harmless for the test but is a copy error that will confuse anyone searching for the config.

title: Test does not verify that a recovery code is single-use against user storage
body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin logs in once with code 0 and checks success, but never checks that the same code is rejected on reuse or that exhausted codes trigger the required action. Given the storage provider never consumes codes, this gap lets the replay bug above go unnoticed.

title: Same NPE remains in the other paged/search subgroup methods
body: The fix only guards getSubGroupsCount(). The three paged variants, getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults) (line 256), getSubGroupsStream(firstResult, maxResults) (line 262) and getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, firstResult, maxResults) (line 268), still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. If the group was deleted concurrently, modelSupplier.get() returns null and these throw the same NullPointerException the PR claims to fix. They need the same null handling, or should delegate through a path that throws a consistent error.

title: getSubGroupsCount silently returns null for a deleted group
body: The new code returns null when the backing model is gone. GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount pass this straight to setSubGroupCount, and any caller that unboxes the Long will NPE. Returning null here moves the NPE to a different place rather than defining a clear contract (e.g. returning 0, or throwing a not-found-style exception consistently with the other methods that throw 'Not found in database').

title: Reader thread is never joined, so late failures are silently ignored
body: The background reader thread is started and the test asserts on caughtExceptions immediately after setting deletedAll=true, without joining the thread. A read that is in flight when the flag flips, and which fails afterwards, will add to the list after the assertion has already run, so the test passes while hiding the exception. The thread should be joined (with a timeout) before asserting. Also, the test never verifies that the deletions succeeded or that the groups are gone, and it leaves the 100 created groups without cleanup via managedRealm.cleanup().

title: Unbounded busy-loop of HTTP admin calls in a non-daemon thread
body: The reader loops with no sleep, issuing admin REST calls as fast as possible until the flag is set. If the main thread fails before setting deletedAll (for example, the fail() in the creation loop or a remove() exception), the flag is never set and this non-daemon thread spins forever, which can hang the test JVM. Wrapping the set in a finally block and making the thread a daemon or joining it would avoid this.

title: Same null-model NPE remains in other subgroup accessors the fix did not touch
body: The PR guards getSubGroupsCount() against a null modelSupplier.get() result, which is the case when the group was deleted concurrently. The sibling methods getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) (line 256), getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer) (line 262) and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) (line 268) still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. If the group was removed concurrently, these throw the same NullPointerException the PR claims to fix. The fix is incomplete for the same race.

title: getSubGroupsCount silently returns null instead of signalling a missing group
body: When the group has been deleted, getSubGroupsCount() now returns null, while the other accessors on the same adapter throw IllegalStateException("Not found in database") in the same situation. Callers that unbox the Long (for example to compare or add counts) will NPE at their own site, moving the failure rather than handling it. The behaviour is inconsistent with the rest of the class and is not documented in the GroupModel contract.

title: Reader thread is not joined, so the exception assertion can miss failures
body: The background thread that reads groups is started and never joined. deletedAll is set to true and caughtExceptions is asserted immediately afterwards, so the thread may still be inside a request and add exceptions after the assertion has run. The test can pass even when the race it is meant to catch occurs. The thread should be joined (or its completion awaited) before asserting on caughtExceptions.

title: Regression test does not reliably reproduce the NPE and leaves groups behind on failure
body: The test relies on timing between a busy-looping reader and 100 sequential deletes to hit the race, so it may pass on unfixed code. It also creates 100 groups without registering them with managedRealm.cleanup(), so a failure in the middle leaves groups behind. The busy loop issuing unbounded HTTP requests also adds significant runtime and load to the suite.

title: Unrelated dead-code removal bundled into a concurrency fix
body: The diff deletes the private helper groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement. This is unrelated to the NPE being fixed and is not explained in the description. It is only safe if nothing else in the file references it, and the change should be separated or justified in the PR.

title: Same NPE remains in the paged/search subgroup methods
body: The fix only guards getSubGroupsCount(). getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) (line 256), getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer) (line 262) and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) (line 268) still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) directly. When the group was deleted concurrently, LazyModel returns null and these throw the same NullPointerException the PR is meant to fix. They should null-check the supplier result and return Stream.empty() (or equivalent) like the count method does. Similarly, getAttributes/getFirstAttribute/getAttributeStream (lines 149, 155, 163) pass modelSupplier into CachedGroup.getAttributes, which dereferences the supplier on a cache miss, so a concurrent deletion can still NPE there.

title: Reader thread is never joined, so the test can pass without checking anything
body: The reader thread is started and then deletedAll is set immediately after the deletes, and the assertion on caughtExceptions runs right away. The reader thread is not joined, so it may never have executed a single read, or may still be running and adding exceptions after the assertion has already been evaluated. The check is therefore racy and can pass vacuously. The test should join the reader thread (after setting the flag) before asserting, and ideally assert that at least one read happened.

title: Busy-looping reader thread hammers the server and the failure path is swallowed
body: The reader loops with no pause, issuing a full brief group query as fast as possible for the whole delete phase, which adds unnecessary load and can slow or destabilise the test. Exceptions are only collected into a list that is never inspected until the race is over, and the thread is not managed by the test framework, so an uncaught Error in the thread would be silently lost. Also the group list is never cleaned up on failure. Consider a bounded loop or executor with futures.

title: Negative cursor offset on prev pages is passed straight into queryset slicing
body: In BasePaginator.get_result, start_offset is max(0, offset) for next cursors but is set to the raw negative offset when cursor.is_prev is true. Django querysets raise AssertionError on negative slice indices, so a prev cursor with a negative offset produces a 500 instead of a bad-request error. The comment claims the queryset 'will handle boundary conditions', which is false.

title: Advanced-feature path allows negative offsets that bypass pagination bounds
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result uses the raw negative cursor.offset as the slice start when enable_advanced_features is set. Negative slicing on a Django queryset fetches from the end of the result set (or errors), so a crafted cursor can read arbitrary rows outside the normal page window. The comment says 'permissions are checked at the queryset level', but the queryset filter only scopes to the organization and does not limit how far the offset can reach. This is an unauthenticated-looking bypass of pagination limits gated only on a user-controlled query flag and a superuser/global-access check.

title: Undocumented query flag switches paginator and exposes new cursor behavior
body: The endpoint now changes pagination behavior based on a 'optimized_pagination=true' query parameter that is not validated by AuditLogQueryParamSerializer, is not documented, and is not part of any API contract. Clients can send arbitrary cursors that now go through the negative-offset code path, which the regular DateTimePaginator rejects or clamps. This is an unreviewed API surface change.

title: Clamping non-prev offsets to zero changes existing behavior for all paginators
body: BasePaginator.get_result now clamps negative offsets to 0 for next cursors, but this change is applied to every BasePaginator subclass, not just the new one. Previously a negative offset with a next cursor was handled by the original code path; now the offset is silently rewritten, and the cursor returned to the client is computed from the clamped start, which can cause duplicate or skipped rows for existing consumers.

title: Docstring claims features that are not implemented
body: The OptimizedCursorPaginator docstring advertises 'Streamlined boundary condition handling' and 'Optimized query path for large datasets', but the implementation is a copy of BasePaginator.get_result with only the negative-offset branch added. No performance optimization exists, so the docstring misleads maintainers about what the class does.

title: Comment claims negative offsets enable reverse pagination, but the Cursor type change is unvalidated
body: The new comment says the Cursor class allows negative offsets for reverse pagination, yet Cursor.from_string still parses any integer offset and nothing downstream validates it. Removing the non-negative contract from a shared cursor type affects every paginator that consumes Cursor, and the comment does not describe the risks.

title: No tests added for the new paginator, negative offsets, or the query flag
body: The PR adds a new paginator class, changes shared BasePaginator slicing logic, and adds an endpoint code path behind a query flag, but includes no tests. Negative-offset and superuser-gated behavior are untested, so the crash and bypass risks above are not caught.

title: Optimized pagination gated on the wrong privilege check and exposed to any request parameter
body: The endpoint switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator when the client passes optimized_pagination=true and `request.user.is_superuser or member.has_global_access` holds. The gate is a fixed flag in the request, and the new paginator path enables negative cursor offsets (see paginator.py get_result), which lets a caller read rows outside the normal page window. The comment claims permissions are 'checked at the queryset level', but the queryset is unchanged and still filtered only by organization_id. Any privileged user can therefore walk the audit log in ways the standard paginator does not allow, and the justification in the comment is incorrect.

title: Negative offset clamped for next pages but allowed for prev pages changes semantics for all paginators
body: The change to BasePaginator.get_result sets start_offset = max(0, offset) only when not is_prev, and passes raw offset for prev cursors. This is applied to the shared base class used by DateTimePaginator and every other cursor paginator, not just the new one. Negative offsets on prev cursors now reach Django's queryset slicing, which raises an AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported') rather than returning a clean error, turning malformed client cursors into 500s across all endpoints using BasePaginator.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result ignores the cursor-offset clamp and misuses the negative-offset branch
body: In the negative-offset branch, start_offset = cursor.offset is passed to queryset slicing with stop = start_offset + limit + extra. If the sum is still negative or the slice start is negative, Django raises AssertionError. Also the later `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check uses the unclamped offset, so behavior diverges between branches. The logic is untested for these paths.

title: Duplicated class definition and dead-code style issues
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result with the only change being the negative-offset branch. The copy duplicates roughly 70 lines and will drift from the base implementation. The docstring's claims ('streamlined boundary condition handling', 'optimized query path') are not backed by any code change, so they describe behavior that does not exist.

title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported but the rest of the cursor pipeline does not handle them
body: The new comment says negative offsets enable efficient reverse pagination, but Cursor.offset is later used by build_cursor and _build_next_values/_build_prev_values, which add to offsets and assume non-negative values. The comment misdescribes the behavior and hides that negative offsets from client input are now accepted by Cursor.from_string without validation.

title: No tests for the new optimized pagination path or the negative-offset changes
body: The PR adds a new query-parameter-driven code path, a new paginator class, and changes shared BasePaginator behavior, but includes no tests. The PR description is just 'Test 1'. Regressions in the shared paginator would affect every cursor-paginated endpoint with no test coverage in this change.

title: Trailing whitespace on blank line and on order_by argument
body: Lines 72, 89 contain trailing whitespace, which will fail the repository's linter.

title: PR description is uninformative
body: The description reads 'Test 1' and gives no rationale, no explanation of the optimized_pagination parameter, and no note that it is a user-facing API change for admins. Reviewers cannot assess the intent or risk from the description.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on datetime values, so the optimized path always fails
body: The endpoint sends `order_by="-datetime"` to `OptimizedCursorPaginator`. Its `get_item_key` does `getattr(item, self.key)` and then `math.floor(value)` or `math.ceil(value)`. For `datetime` fields that raises TypeError. The cursor is also built from this key, so the request fails before a cursor is produced. Every request with `optimized_pagination=true` from an admin will return a 500. The class should reuse DateTimePaginator's datetime-to-millisecond key logic, not the numeric Paginator logic.

title: Negative slice start passed to Django QuerySet causes an error for negative cursor offsets
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, `start_offset` is the raw negative offset and is used in `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported"). A client that supplies a negative cursor offset therefore gets a 500 instead of a clean 400. The comment claiming the ORM 'handles negative slicing automatically' is wrong.

title: Base paginator silently clamps negative offsets for all paginators, changing behavior globally
body: The change to `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` applies to BasePaginator, which DateTimePaginator and every other cursor-paginated endpoint use. Previously a negative offset on a next-page cursor would error. Now it is silently treated as 0, so a crafted or corrupted cursor returns the first page instead of an error. For prev cursors a negative offset is still passed straight into a slice and fails. The behavior is now inconsistent and unrelated to the stated optimization, and it changes the contract of the shared base class without tests.

title: Cursor now accepts negative offsets globally, widening what untrusted input can produce
body: Removing any validation on `offset` in `Cursor.__init__` means cursors parsed from user query strings can carry negative offsets for every endpoint. Combined with the paginator changes, these inputs are either clamped silently or crash on slicing, depending on the path. The comment ('enables efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions') describes a feature that is not actually implemented and does not match the code behavior. Negative offset handling should be validated at the boundary, not allowed through the shared cursor type.

title: Undocumented query-param feature flag gates a separate, untested pagination path
body: The `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter switches the endpoint to a different paginator with `enable_advanced_features=True`, gated by `is_superuser or has_global_access`. Nothing in the endpoint documents this parameter, and the serializer does not validate it. The branch is effectively an experimental API surface that bypasses the normal DateTimePaginator path, and the optimized path is broken (see paginator.py:840). No test covers it.

title: Comment and docstring claim permission and performance guarantees the code does not provide
body: The `enable_advanced_features` comments say 'permissions are checked at the queryset level' and that negative offsets give 'efficient bidirectional pagination'. Neither is true. The queryset is filtered only by organization, and negative offsets are not supported by the ORM slicing used here. The OptimizedCursorPaginator docstring also promises 'optimized query path for large datasets', but it runs the same queries as the base class. These claims mislead maintainers about the security and performance properties of the code.

title: New paginator class and endpoint branch added with no tests
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator, the negative-offset logic, the changed BasePaginator slicing, and the new endpoint branch have no tests. The PR description is only 'Test 1'. Given that the new paginator fails on its first real request (see the datetime key bug), a basic test exercising `optimized_pagination=true` would have caught it.

title: max_segment_spans limit check removed from _load_segment_data
body: The span-count guard (`if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` that skipped oversized segments and logged an error) was deleted, while the parameter `max_segment_spans` still exists in __init__. Segments with arbitrarily many spans (bounded only by the byte limit) are now flushed, and the setting is silently dead. The PR instead relies on a Lua-side zpopmin trim to 1000 spans, which changes behavior: spans are silently dropped rather than the whole segment being skipped, and no metric is emitted for it.

title: zpopmin trims the lowest-scored (oldest) spans instead of excess spans being dropped intentionally
body: `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` removes the spans with the smallest end_timestamp, i.e. the earliest-ending spans, silently discarding data from the segment. The eviction policy is undocumented and the removed spans are never reported or metered. Also, `span_count` is derived from zunionstore/zcard results that were captured before the trim, and the max_segment_spans default of 1001 in buffer.py no longer matches the 1000 cap in Lua.

title: zunionstore with default aggregate SUM sums scores of duplicate members
body: Merging sets with `zunionstore ... 2 set_key span_key` uses the default SUM aggregation. Since the same span payload may exist in both sets (e.g. resent spans), its score is summed, corrupting the end-timestamp ordering that the eviction depends on. Using AGGREGATE MIN or MAX would be needed for correct scores.

title: Redirect-walk loop bound lowered from 10000 to 1000 without updating the documented limitation
body: The loop bound was reduced to 1000 and the comment about segment trees deeper than the limit was removed, so trees of depth 1000-10000 are now silently not joined, with no documentation of the new limit.

title: Negative offset is clamped to 0 for non-prev cursors, changing BasePaginator semantics
body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` silently clamps negative offsets for next-page cursors, while the prior code passed them through. Combined with the Cursor change allowing negative offsets, a negative offset now returns the first page instead of being rejected or handled, a silent behavior change to all BasePaginator users.

title: enable_advanced_features allows negative-offset slicing into arbitrary queryset positions
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, the queryset is sliced with the negative start offset. Django negative slicing is not supported and raises ValueError, causing a 500; alternatively it exposes unintended positions. The comment claims access 'beyond normal pagination bounds' and that permissions are checked, which is an unsupported authorization claim. Client-controlled cursors can trigger this path.

title: Advanced pagination gated by a client query parameter and unverified privilege
body: The optimized paginator with enable_advanced_features=True is activated by a client-supplied `optimized_pagination=true` query param for superusers or global-access members. This is an unreviewed experimental feature exposed on an endpoint, with negative-offset access enabled, and the gating logic (`request.user.is_superuser or has_global_access`) bypasses the normal paginator used for everyone else, so the two code paths can return different results and page sizes.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator and has a missing key-order fix
body: The new class copies most of BasePaginator.get_result, and its build_queryset is inherited. Its `get_item_key` ignores post-processing semantics, and it is never covered by tests. Duplicated logic will drift and this class is dead code unless the audit log flag is kept.

title: Zset payload payload dedup and deleted span metadata break done_flush_segments and tests
body: Spans are now stored in a sorted set keyed by payload. The `_load_segment_data` loop uses `zscan` values as tuples but `payloads[key].extend(span for span, _ in zscan_values)` runs after the size check that already consumed them; flushed spans can therefore be double-counted in `sizes` across pages. Also `process_spans` now requires end_timestamp_precise, and any producer omitting it in `process_batch` causes a KeyError that crashes the batch.

title: Hard indexing of end_timestamp_precise can crash the whole batch
body: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises KeyError for any span lacking the field, and `cast(SpanEvent, ...)` gives no runtime check. A single malformed message fails the entire processing batch instead of being skipped.

title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported but the Cursor type and callers do not handle them
body: The added comment says the cursor enables efficient reverse pagination for arbitrary positions, but nothing in build_cursor or the paginators validates or uses negative offsets for non-prev cursors. The comment misdescribes behavior and the change is a silent loosening of the cursor contract.

title: No tests added for the new negative-offset and optimized paginator behavior
body: The PR adds OptimizedCursorPaginator, negative-offset handling, the optimized_pagination endpoint branch, and the Lua eviction, yet only span-buffer test fixtures were updated to pass end_timestamp_precise. No test covers eviction above 1000 spans, the audit-log optimized path, or negative offsets.

title: Span-count cap removed from Python side while Lua now trims to 1000 silently
body: The max_segment_spans check was removed from _load_segment_data, so oversized segments are no longer skipped and logged. Meanwhile the Lua script now silently zpopmin-trims sets to 1000 entries, dropping spans without any metric or log. Segments with more spans than the limit lose data silently and the max_segment_spans parameter is now dead code.

title: zpopmin trims the lowest-scored (oldest) spans, not the excess
body: zpopmin removes the members with the smallest scores, so when the set exceeds 1000 spans the oldest spans are discarded. This is the opposite of what is probably desired for a bounded buffer and also the span_count used is from zunionstore which returns the union cardinality, so the trim count is computed correctly but the chosen eviction policy silently drops data from the start of the segment.

title: zunionstore with weights defaults sums scores; spans re-added with same payload are merged incorrectly
body: zunionstore uses the default AGGREGATE SUM, so when the same payload member exists in both sets its score is summed instead of kept. Since members are the raw payload and scores are end timestamps, duplicate spans moved between sets get their timestamp doubled, corrupting eviction ordering.

title: Span payload timestamp used as sort score makes ZADD of duplicate payloads ineffective
body: process_spans builds a dict {payload: end_timestamp} for zadd; if two identical payloads occur in a batch the dict dedupes them, which is fine, but the pipeline previously used sadd. Score-based sets also change the flush_segments/_load_segment_data contract (zscan returns (member, score) tuples) without any migration for segments already stored as Redis sets, causing WRONGTYPE errors on rolling deploy.

title: Negative offsets now reach the queryset slice path for is_prev cursors
body: start_offset is set to offset without clamping when cursor.is_prev, so a negative offset from a crafted cursor produces a negative slice index. Django raises an error for negative slicing (ValueError 'Negative indexing is not supported'), turning a bad cursor into a 500 instead of a 400 BadPaginationError. The 'Performance optimization' comments are misleading and the behavior change is not tested.

title: Advanced-feature negative offset path lets authorized-looking requests bypass bounds
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator allows negative cursor offsets when enable_advanced_features is set, slicing the queryset with negative start indices. The comment claims permissions are checked at queryset level, but the queryset is only filtered by organization, not by pagination bounds, so arbitrary negative offsets expose rows beyond normal page bounds and can trigger Django negative-indexing errors. This adds an unreviewed data-access path.

title: Advanced pagination gated by query parameter and privilege without tests
body: The optimized paginator is enabled by a client-supplied query parameter for superusers or global-access members, and the endpoint now differs in pagination behavior. There is no test covering this branch, and the 'enable_advanced' flag unlocks the negative-offset path in the paginator, expanding what an admin request can read in audit logs.

title: Trailing whitespace and duplicated paginate call
body: Lines with trailing whitespace were introduced and the paginate call is duplicated across both branches, which makes future changes error-prone; the branch only differs by paginator class and one kwarg.

title: Comment claims a performance optimization that the constructor does not implement
body: The added comment says negative offsets are allowed for efficient reverse pagination, but the code only does int(offset) and the behavior change is elsewhere. The comment misrepresents the code and the risky negative-offset semantics are not documented in the cursor contract.

title: KeyError if message lacks end_timestamp_precise
body: val['end_timestamp_precise'] is accessed directly; any span payload without this field now raises KeyError and crashes the batch processing step, whereas the other fields are validated as needed. The schema cast does not validate at runtime, so this should be val.get with handling or a documented requirement.

title: No tests for span-count eviction at 1000 or the removed max_segment_spans skip
body: The PR adds zpopmin eviction at 1000 spans and removes the max_segment_spans rejection, but no test exercises either behavior. Regressions in the eviction boundary or the Lua return path would go unnoticed.

title: Segment size and span-count guard removed, so oversized segments are no longer rejected
body: The diff removes the `max_segment_spans` check in `_load_segment_data` (the 'segment_span_count_exceeded' branch) entirely, while the constructor still accepts and stores `max_segment_spans`. The byte-size check remains, but the span-count limit that protected the flusher from huge segments is gone and the parameter is now dead. Segments with more spans than the configured limit will be loaded and flushed instead of skipped, which changes flush behavior without any stated reason.

title: zpopmin trims the segment to 1000 but the sorted-set score is end timestamp, and span_count after zunionstore may be stale
body: `span_count` is only set from zunionstore when a merge happens; when no merge occurs but the set already exists, `zcard` is used, which is fine. However when a merge happens, zunionstore returns the union size, and then `zpopmin` removes the lowest-scored (oldest-ending) spans, silently dropping spans from the segment on every insert once above 1000 spans. Dropped spans are data loss with no metric or log, and the eviction policy (oldest end timestamp) is not documented or tested.

title: zadd with payload as member collapses identical payloads and uses end timestamp as score
body: Switching from sadd to zadd keys members by the raw payload bytes. Duplicate span payloads now collapse silently (same as before), but the score is the span's end_timestamp_precise, and in `process_spans` the zadd is done in a separate pipeline before the Lua call, so a re-delivered span with a changed timestamp overwrites the score. Combined with eviction by lowest score, this can evict the wrong spans. Behavior is not covered by tests.

title: Missing end_timestamp_precise key raises KeyError for every span
body: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` is indexed directly, so any span event lacking this field (older Relay versions or malformed payloads) now raises KeyError and fails the whole batch, whereas previously such spans were processed. The cast to SpanEvent also does not validate anything at runtime.

title: Negative offsets are now passed to the queryset in BasePaginator, causing wrong results
body: The change to `get_result` replaces `queryset[offset:stop]` with `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. For is_prev cursors a negative offset is passed straight to slicing, which Django rejects (ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported) and for next cursors negative offsets are silently clamped, hiding the cursor's offset. Behavior of every existing paginator subclass changes.

title: Advanced-feature path allows arbitrary negative offsets to read beyond pagination bounds
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator honors any negative cursor.offset when enable_advanced_features is set, slicing the queryset with negative indices. Negative slicing on a Django queryset fetches from the end and bypasses the normal pagination window; the comment claims permissions are checked at the queryset level, but the queryset is just the caller's filtered audit log queryset, so this exposes arbitrary rows ordering-wise. The gate is only superuser or global access, which is a broad, unreviewed data-access expansion.

title: Undocumented optimized_pagination query flag switches paginator and enables negative offsets
body: A new `optimized_pagination=true` request parameter selects OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features for superusers/global-access members. This is an unannounced API surface, introduced in an endpoint publicly marked EXPERIMENTAL, with behavior that is not tested and not described anywhere. The `enable_advanced` check also reads `request.user.is_superuser` on an endpoint that already has permission checks, so the gate is ad hoc.

title: Comment claims negative offset support that the cursor does not implement
body: The added comment says the Cursor enables efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions, but Cursor only stores int(offset) and has no logic for negative offsets; the claim is misleading for maintainers and describes behavior the change doesn't deliver.

title: Lua loop bound and eviction limit are magic numbers that disagree with the constructor default
body: add-buffer.lua now hard-codes 1000 for the redirect loop and the eviction cap, while the Python constructor default `max_segment_spans` is 1001 and is no longer enforced. The three values are inconsistent and the Lua limit is not configurable, so the Python setting has no effect on the actual cap.

title: No tests cover the new eviction, zunionstore merge, or negative-offset paths
body: The tests only add end_timestamp_precise to existing fixtures. Nothing exercises the >1000 span eviction in add-buffer.lua, the zset-based merging, or the OptimizedCursorPaginator / negative-offset behavior, so the regressions above would go undetected.

title: Cache key uses Python hash() of project list, which is randomized per process and can collide
body: The cache key embeds hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python's hash() for ints is deterministic, but the tuple hash is not guaranteed stable across processes and can collide; a collision would return another project set's eligibility for this org. The key also ignores that eligibility depends on the allowlist option, so a stale value can persist for 60s. Use the sorted project ids joined as a string instead.

title: Cached eligibility is returned without re-checking, and cache.get of False is treated as hit
body: The cache stores is_eligible and the cached path returns cached_result and transform check. This is consistent, but the cache is keyed only by org and project ids, not by the dataset/request, and the allowlist is also re-read fresh elsewhere, so the 'fresh' docstring contradicts the caching added in this PR. Behavior differs between cache hit and miss within the 60s window, producing inconsistent results for identical queries.

title: Allowlist membership compares ints against option values that may be strings
body: project_id in allowlist assumes the option stores integer ids. If the option is stored as strings (common for options edited via UI/JSON), no project matches and upsampling silently never applies; if types mismatch in the other direction, the check fails silently. The membership test should normalize types.

title: count() rewritten to 'upsampled_count() as count' changes result semantics and may break aliasing
body: The transform replaces count() with an aliased function call regardless of whether the query's orderby, equations, or top-events column references 'count()'. Callers that look up the result by 'count()' key or pass the transformed columns into equations/orderby will break. The alias 'count' also may collide with a user-specified column of the same name.

title: upsampled_count ignores sample_weight existence and returns sum without guaranteeing column
body: The function assumes sample_weight exists for every event in allowlisted projects, but events without the context (for example, older SDKs or events stored before the change) have no sample_weight, so sum() undercounts them to zero or fails the query. The comment asserts a schema guarantee that the code does not enforce. The function also declares required_args=[] and default_result_type 'number' while it is used as an aggregate with the toInt64 wrapper, which truncates fractional sample weights.

title: Upsampling eligibility check runs on every _get_event_stats call, including per-bucket sub-queries
body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is invoked at the top of _get_event_stats, which is called multiple times per request (split-query flow, transaction queries). Each call does a cache round trip and option lookup, undermining the claimed performance optimization. The comment 'cached result ensures consistent behavior' is misleading since the value is recomputed per call.

title: Top-events path transforms columns but the non-top-events path reuses the same final_columns variable incorrectly
body: final_columns is reassigned inside the RPC branch and the standard branch, but the upsampling transformation is applied to query_columns each time from the original input, so the behavior is correct only because the branches are exclusive. The duplicated transform blocks are fragile; a future edit that applies the transform earlier would double-transform. Hoisting one transformation is safer.

title: Error message text changed for existing clients
body: The response detail for topEvents <= 0 changed from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This is an unrelated behavior change in an upsampling PR that may break clients or tests matching the old string.

title: Docstrings and comments claim performance and consistency guarantees that are not true
body: Docstrings say the cache is 'safe because eventual consistency is acceptable' and that allowlist reads are 'fresh each time', which contradict each other and the caching added here. invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but never called, so allowlist changes are not reflected for up to 60 seconds.

title: Factory silently swallows all exceptions when setting sample_rate
body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling wraps reads and conversions in bare 'except Exception: pass', hiding malformed test data and making tests pass or fail for the wrong reason. It also sets sample_rate on every stored event in test factories, which changes behavior of all tests that use store_event with error_sampling context.

title: Test setUp overwrites self.user and the authed user, and asserts counts that depend on upsampling not yet verified
body: setUp calls login_as(self.user) then reassigns self.user to a new user, so the logged-in user differs from self.user used in the event tags. The count assertions expect 10 for upsampled buckets (1 event at 0.1 rate) but nothing in the store path shows sample_weight is written, so these expectations are unverified and likely fail or pass for the wrong reason.

title: Transaction test asserts count of 1 for the transaction bucket without verifying the transaction was indexed
body: The transaction event is stored with a fixed trace id and no wait_for_event_count, so the snuba query can race and the assertions on data[0] and data[1] are flaky. The test also does not check the transaction path actually bypassed upsampling.

title: Stray 'sentry-repo' submodule file and 'Test 3' PR description
body: The PR adds a submodule pointer file 'sentry-repo' pointing at the base commit, and the description is 'Test 3'. These are unrelated artifacts that should not be merged into the repository.

title: Cache key uses Python hash() of a tuple, which is unstable across processes
body: The cache key embeds hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python's hash() for ints is stable, but the key is also not tied to the allowlist value; more importantly the cache stores only the boolean eligibility per project set for 60s, so an allowlist change is ignored for up to 60 seconds while the code comment claims this is safe. invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but never called, so the advertised invalidation on allowlist change does not happen. Also the cached value is the allowlist check only, so a cached True for an organization is reused regardless of allowlist changes.

title: Cache hit short-circuits on falsy check incorrectly typed; cache.get returns non-bool values
body: cached_result is compared with `is not None` and returned via `cached_result and ...`. If the cached value is False, the function returns False, which is correct, but the return type is not guaranteed to be bool when cached_result is a non-bool stored by another writer under the same key. Under mypy this is also an untyped cache value returned as bool.

title: Membership test is O(n*m) on a list read from options
body: `project_id in allowlist` performs a linear scan of the allowlist for each project, and the allowlist is a list from options. For large allowlists and many projects this is quadratic per request. Converting to a set once would be the expected approach given the stated performance goal.

title: upsampled_count returns sum of sample_weight over all rows, ignoring the upsampling eligibility and null weights
body: The new function sums sample_weight with no null handling or filter; events lacking sample_weight (for example non-allowlisted projects mixed into the same query, or events stored before the feature) will contribute null/zero and silently undercount. The comment asserts the schema guarantees the column for all events, but the endpoint does not verify this beyond the allowlist check. The result also silently changes the metric name the user requested (count() is returned aliased as count), which can break clients that expect the column type.

title: Error message text changed without need
body: The validation message was changed from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This is an unrelated user-facing API response change bundled into the upsampling PR, and it can break clients matching on the string.

title: Upsampling eligibility is recomputed for every _get_event_stats call, including per-widget split queries
body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is called at the top of _get_event_stats, which runs up to four times per request in the dashboard split path. Each call hits the cache and option lookup again; the comment claiming a 'cached result ensures consistent behavior' is misleading since the decision is recomputed each time and can differ between calls within one request if the cache expires or the allowlist changes mid-request.

title: Trailing whitespace and redundant variable aliasing
body: Lines with only whitespace after the upsampling check (and the duplicated `upsampling_enabled = should_upsample` alias) add noise. The comments describe 'late transformation' and 'caching' that do not match the code, which is misleading to maintainers.

title: Upsampling is only applied to the query columns in some branches; top-events and RPC paths compute final_columns but the non-top-events path reassigns it inconsistently
body: In the RPC branch the transformation at line 277 reruns from query_columns, discarding nothing, but in the top_events branch final_columns is only transformed when upsampling is enabled and then passed as timeseries_columns while selected_columns still uses raw fields. Count() is rewritten to 'upsampled_count() as count' but the top-events path also passes the alias string into the equation/orderby machinery that expects the raw function name, so orderby on count() can fail or sort incorrectly. Behavior differs between the top-events and standard branches with no test coverage for top-events.

title: Test factory silently overwrites sample_rate from contexts for every stored event
body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling is applied to every event stored through the shared store_event factory, and it swallows all exceptions. This changes the sample_rate of all test events that carry error_sampling contexts globally, affecting unrelated tests and hiding malformed data instead of failing.

title: Test setUp overwrites self.user and self.user2 after login, and assertions expect counts of 10 that the stored data cannot produce
body: setUp logs in self.user then reassigns self.user to a new user, and the tests assert count==10 for allowlisted projects while only one event per project per bucket is stored; the expected upsampled value depends on client_sample_rate 0.1 being applied through sample_weight, which the test never verifies. The transaction test also asserts counts for a dataset the feature should not touch, and the assertions rely on unverified behavior, so these tests are likely to be wrong or flaky.

title: Unit tests do not cover the cache path or the invalidation function
body: The tests cover the pure helpers but not is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, its cache behavior, or invalidate_upsampling_cache. The stale-cache behavior described above (60s staleness after allowlist change) is therefore untested, and the unused snuba_params/organization fixture data is never exercised.

title: Test module added to strict typing list without matching sentry-repo change being justified
body: The pyproject.toml change adds the new helper and test module to the strict mypy override list, but the helper's dependency on untyped Any for dataset and the local imports inside _should_apply_sample_weight_transform make this strictness claim unverified. Additionally a stray submodule pointer file 'sentry-repo' is added at the repository root, which is unrelated to the feature and should not be merged.

title: Stray submodule pointer committed to repository root
body: A file named sentry-repo is added containing a gitlink-style 'Subproject commit' line pointing at the base commit. This is unrelated to error upsampling and will break or confuse checkouts/tooling that does not expect a submodule at that path.

title: Python hash() used in cache keys is not stable across processes
body: The cache key uses hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python's hash for ints is deterministic, but hash() of tuples is process-dependent only for str/bytes; here it is fine by accident, yet the key is also not tied to the allowlist content: the cached eligibility is keyed only by org and projects, so after the allowlist option changes the cached True/False persists for 60s across all workers, and invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called from the option-change path. Using hash() also gives collisions that can return a wrong cached eligibility for a different project set.

title: Cached eligibility bypasses the fresh allowlist check and is inconsistent with the docstring
body: The docstring and _are_all_projects_error_upsampled note claim the allowlist is read fresh each time, yet is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects serves a 60-second cached value. The two statements contradict each other, and the cache hash collision risk means one project set can receive another's eligibility, causing upsampled counts to be applied to projects not in the allowlist, silently inflating counts.

title: Allowlist membership check is O(n) per project against a list option
body: project_id in allowlist scans the option list for every project; with a large allowlist and many projects this is quadratic in work per request. Convert to a set once. Minor on its own but in the hot path of every events-stats request.

title: upsampled_count aggregate ignores sample_weight semantics and returns sum over all rows
body: The new upsampled_count function is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no check that sample_weight is non-null. Events without sample_weight (or from non-allowlisted projects in mixed queries) contribute null/zero, silently undercounting, and the transform's comment that the schema guarantees the column exists is unverified. Also default_result_type 'number' is inconsistent with the 'integer' type used by count().

title: Upsampling is applied to the wrong columns: transform occurs only when top_events or rpc, and reassigns final_columns after use
body: The transform is computed inside each branch using query_columns, but final_columns is initialized once and the rpc/top-events branches each recompute from query_columns, so behavior is correct only by accident. More importantly, count() is rewritten to 'upsampled_count() as count' even though the response consumers and the zerofill/other-column logic expect the count alias semantics; the alias is embedded in a column string rather than passed through the normal parser, which may break equations and orderby referencing count().

title: Misleading comments claim caching and late optimization that do not exist
body: The comments say the cached result ensures consistent behavior and that the separation enables caching and query optimization; no such caching of the upsampling decision across query execution exists, the decision is recomputed per call. These comments will mislead maintainers.

title: Unrelated error message change alters public API response text
body: The topEvents validation message is changed from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This is unrelated to upsampling and changes an API response string that clients or tests may match on.

title: Blanket except-pass hides invalid sample rate data
body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling swallows all exceptions silently, including from a malformed contexts structure, and sets sample_rate on normalized event data in the shared test factory for all events. Changing store_event behavior for every test that includes an error_sampling context makes the test helper a hidden side effect.

title: Tests create organization and projects with unused fixtures and do not test cache or is_errors_query path
body: The main entry point is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects and its caching behavior, plus invalidate_upsampling_cache, are not tested at all. The snuba_params fixture is built but unused by any test.

title: Endpoint tests mock the options module but the cache is not cleared between tests and assertions are unverified
body: The new endpoint tests rely on the 60-second cache inside is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects without clearing it, so results depend on test ordering across the allowlist cases. Also setUp overwrites self.user after creating projects and assigns self.authed_user before reassigning, and the count assertions (10 per bucket) are not derived from the stored events, which contain only one event per bucket, so the expected value of 10 is suspicious and likely wrong.

title: Transaction test asserts count of 1 for a query that filters on transactions in an errors-focused path
body: test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events stores a transaction and expects count 1 in bucket one and 0 in bucket two, but the earlier error events fall in those same buckets with the errors query path; the expectation does not clearly isolate the transaction behavior and may pass for the wrong reason.

title: Migration body replaced with no-op but still marked as run
body: The data migration function is reduced to a bare return, and the comment points to a 0921 migration that does not appear in this change set. Any environment where 0917 was already applied keeps its old behavior, while fresh installs silently skip the conversion. The dependency chain and the referenced replacement migration need verification, since the comment references a file that is not in this PR.

title: get_environment_info logs exception object in extra and may hit Event/Group DB calls per issue
body: get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() and get_environment() for every issue in the PR comment loop, adding a nodestore fetch and DB query per issue with no caching. Also the exception is passed as a raw object in logger extra, which is not JSON-serializable for some log handlers. The broad except hides failures entirely.

title: Truncated title can be empty-ish and ellipsis appended to ASCII text unconditionally
body: _truncate_title cuts at 50 chars and then rstrips, but titles containing markdown special characters (e.g. '*', '[', ']') are inserted into the bold link text unescaped, which can break the rendered markdown comment link.

title: Log extra key changed to workflow_event_data but other logs in function still use event_data
body: Changing the logged event_data to workflow_event_data is a correct fix only if the workflow-specific data is intended; however the same function's other log calls still reference the unmodified event_data, creating inconsistent logs for the same event.

title: Analytics event recorded before feature check and with wrong endpoint scope
body: analytics.record is called before features.has, so requests from orgs without the feature enabled still emit the assemble event. Also the endpoint is project-scoped but the event is named as organization-level, and user_id is request.user.id which will fail for anonymous/auth-token requests (request.user may be AnonymousUser with id None).

title: Index access on process_raw_response result can raise on unexpected shape
body: error_ids is taken via response[0].get('error_ids', []) without verifying response is a list of dicts; and query_replay_instance is now called on every request before the feature check result is used, adding a Snuba query for every summarize call even when error context is disabled.

title: fetch_error_details uses zip with events.values() whose order is not guaranteed to match error_ids
body: nodestore get_multi returns a dict keyed by node id; zipping error_ids with events.values() pairs IDs with data by insertion order, which may not match the request order and can attach the wrong title/message to an error ID, and missing entries shift all subsequent pairings.

title: Strict serializer validation now rejects the whole batch on one bad report and logs raw reports
body: Previously invalid fields were tolerated; now any single invalid report returns 422 for the entire batch, which browsers will retry, and the raw report body (including user_agent/url) is logged at warning level, a potential data exposure and log volume issue.

title: Removal of ParameterizationRegexExperiment is a public API break
body: ParameterizationRegexExperiment was exported in __all__ and removed; any out-of-tree or dependent code importing it breaks. The traceparent experiment option is also removed from defaults without a migration path for stored option values.

title: Feature check happens after hook call but summary fetch is not gated by it consistently
body: useFeedbackSummary fires the API query gated by the feature flag, but FeedbackSummary returns null only after calling hooks; the summary request is still made for orgs without the feature when enabled is evaluated differently across components, and the isPending placeholder can flash for disabled orgs.

title: Table widget renders hardcoded empty data behind a feature flag
body: When the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature is on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns=[] and empty tableData, discarding the real tableResults. Any org with the flag sees empty tables with no error.

title: Attribute-key hook now runs its query with stale or mismatched cache key
body: useTraceItemAttributeKeys builds queryKey from makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions, but the query function passes no search, and useQuery is not gated on tag.key, so suggestion values for the wrong attribute can be cached and reused across attributes.

title: Writable aggregate fields filtered with isBaseVisualize but then read as yAxes while readable side uses yAxis
body: findAllFieldRefs now reads readable visualizes via visualize.yAxis (single) but writable ones via visualize.yAxes (array) after filtering by isBaseVisualize, so the two sides use inconsistent shapes and writable field references may be silently dropped.

title: Visualize.fromJSON now returns an array, breaking call sites expecting a single Visualize
body: Visualize.fromJSON changed return type to Visualize[]; callers such as updateLocationWithAggregateFields handle it, but any caller that previously used the result directly (e.g. useAnalytics, saved query parsing) now receives an array and will misbehave silently.

title: Keys query no longer passes environment or staleTime/retry options
body: The rewritten hook drops environment and the original query options (staleTime 0, refetchOnWindowFocus false, retry false), changing cache and retry behavior for attribute keys without explanation.

title: Removed 'Type' rows from grouping variant display
body: All variant types lose the 'Type' key-value row and its explanatory tooltips, removing user-facing information about what grouping algorithm was used, with no corresponding test updates.

title: Analytics event name changed from view_html to view-html
body: The trackAnalytics event key was renamed to 'replay.view-html' while the event map and type use the same key but existing dashboards and reports may filter on 'replay.view_html'; the rename breaks continuity of the metric.

title: Gradient replaced with theme background, changing transparent mask visual
body: The transparentMask right gradient now fades to theme.background instead of white, altering appearance in dark theme and inconsistent with the left mask definition.

title: update() sets instance.type from validated_data.get('detector_type') which is never provided
body: The owner update logic is added but the surrounding line instance.type = validated_data.get('detector_type', instance.group_type).slug references an attribute that does not exist on Detector (group_type), so updates without detector_type raise AttributeError.

title: processing_deadline_duration values chosen arbitrarily and drain_mailbox raised to 300s
body: Setting processing deadlines (30s, 300s, 120s, 60s) changes task timeout behavior for webhook delivery; a 300s deadline on drain_mailbox means failed tasks are retried far later, with no justification in the PR.

title: Default autofix automation tuning changed from low to off for all projects
body: DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT and the project option default both change to 'off', silently disabling autofix automation for every project that has not explicitly set it, a user-visible behavior change unrelated to the PR's replay bulk-delete purpose.

title: Migration body replaced with no-op for an already-applied/parallel migration
body: The data migration 0917 is rewritten to `return` immediately, and 0920 is likewise gutted. If any environment already ran the original 0917 or 0920, their data conversion is silently skipped on future runs; and the comment references 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised, which is not part of this PR.
