Removing the real conversion without adding the referenced migration means org saved searches are never converted.

title: Error IDs from the replay query are used without checking response shape; project_id unrelated
body: `response[0].get("error_ids", [])` assumes process_raw_response returns a list of dicts for the replay; if the query returns no rows or error_ids is None, `error_ids` becomes None and is passed to fetch_error_details which iterates it, raising TypeError. The endpoint then 500s instead of degrading to no error context.

title: zip of error_ids with nodestore results misaligns and drops ids
body: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes nodestore get_multi returns values in the same order as the requested node ids and includes a key for every id. `events.values()` order is not guaranteed to match, and missing nodes shift subsequent pairings, so error titles/timestamps can be attributed to the wrong event ids.

title: Error events fetched with default placeholders when data missing
body: `data.get("timestamp", 0.0)` defaults missing timestamps to 0, so error events with no timestamp are placed at the start of the timeline by gen_request_data rather than being skipped or handled explicitly.

title: Strict validation now rejects reports that were previously accepted
body: The endpoint used to accept any report dict and only record metrics. It now returns 422 for the whole batch if any single report fails validation (e.g., both timestamp and age present, unknown type, invalid URL). Browsers sending a batch will lose all metrics for a single malformed report, and the stricter `url`/`user_agent` requirements may reject real-world reports.

title: Regex experiments removed but parameterization of ParameterizationRegex still referenced
body: The ParameterizationRegexExperiment class and its branch in parametrize_w_experiments are removed, yet the `ParameterizationExperiment` type alias now only covers callable experiments. Any configured regex experiment (or the traceparent experiment option removed from options/defaults.py) would now fail at runtime with an AttributeError on `.run` taking a callback of the wrong type, and the removed option could still be referenced in code paths reading it.

title: Prompt tells LLM the output limit but is not enforced; 'AT MOST 55 words' conflicts with max_output_tokens=150
body: The prompt text was rewritten with contradictory guidance (for example 'Don't make overly generic statements' combined with the instruction to base summaries on 'proportional' themes), and the hard 55-word limit is only stated in the prompt, not enforced by parse_response. Output length is unchecked.

title: Default autofix tuning changed from 'low' to 'off' globally
body: DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT and the project option default both change from 'low' to 'off', silently disabling autofix automation for all existing projects that rely on the default, with no migration or changelog and no clear product reason in the PR description.

title: Logging event_data uses the workflow-specific event data variable
body: The extra field renamed from event_data to workflow_event_data changes the logged payload; this is a behavior change in logs but the diff does not explain it and the earlier group-level event_data reference is lost for debugging.

title: Owner handling in update() uses validated_data.get('owner') but create() does not validate owner belongs to org
body: The owner field is accepted from user input and written directly to owner_user_id/owner_team_id without verifying the user or team belongs to the detector's organization or project. A caller could assign an owner outside the organization (the test test_owner_not_in_organization asserts rejection, but the validator adds no such check).

title: Query key omits environment and type dependency inconsistencies; attributes can be stale
body: The useQuery queryKey is derived from makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions which excludes environment, while the queryFn uses a separately-computed projectIds; changing projects through `projects` prop vs selection can cause cached results to be returned for the wrong project set.

title: Table widget path renders empty hardcoded data behind a feature flag
body: When the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature is on, the TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with columns=[] and empty tableData, ignoring result.data, so every dashboard table widget shows no data for flagged orgs.

title: Removed Type rows from grouping variant display
body: The 'Type' row with explanatory tooltips is removed from every variant type, losing information (variant type and explanation) that users used to see in the grouping info panel.

title: Writable aggregate fields filtered with isBaseVisualize but read via yAxes
body: The writable branch now filters by isBaseVisualize and flatMaps `visualize.yAxes`, while the readable branch uses `yAxis`; the mixing of Visualize (single yAxis) and BaseVisualize (yAxes) shapes means writable aggregate fields containing Visualize instances (which have yAxis, not yAxes) will be dropped from field refs.

title: Analytics event name changed from underscore to dash, breaking existing tracking
body: trackAnalytics('replay.view_html') is renamed to 'replay.view-html'; existing dashboards and queries on the old event name will stop receiving data.

title: Gradient change alters appearance of right mask
body: The transparent right-mask gradient changes from a white rgba pair to theme background, altering visuals in dark themes without a corresponding design justification.

title: Comment typo 'segements' in new null-segment guard
body: The new comment says 'segements' and the guard skips deletion of blobs entirely for null max_segment_id; the comment should state clearly that no segment blobs were ingested.

title: Comment references a nonexistent migration name
body: The comment points to '0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py' but the actual migration added in this series is 0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised. Following the comment leads to a file that does not exist, so the pointer to the correct migration is broken.

title: Data-conversion migration silently disabled; org saved searches never converted
body: The body of the 'revised' migration was replaced with a no-op that says the correct migration is 0921, but no 0921 migration exists in this change. Any deployment will skip the saved-search to view conversion entirely, and the comment is misleading. The removed test for 0917 also means the conversion logic is no longer covered.

title: Logged event_data is the wrong variable in fire_actions_for_groups
body: The log extra now uses workflow_event_data, but it is inside a per-workflow loop where other fields reference the group-level event. Changing the logged payload silently alters what is emitted; if workflow_event_data is undefined in that scope it raises NameError, otherwise it logs a different object than before. Needs confirmation of scope.

title: Removal of ParameterizationRegexExperiment breaks public __all__ export and callers
body: ParameterizationRegexExperiment is removed and dropped from __all__, while ParameterizationExperiment is redefined as only ParameterizationCallableExperiment. Any code that imports or constructs regex experiments will fail at import time. The traceparent option is also removed from options defaults without a migration for stored option values.

title: Owner handling in update() is inconsistent with unchanged type/condition logic
body: update() sets instance.type from validated_data.get('detector_type', instance.group_type), which uses a key that is never present in validated_data (the field is 'type'), so type silently resets to the existing value. Also owner is accepted in create/update without verifying it belongs to the organization in the validator, relying solely on ActorField.

title: age/timestamp validators check initial_data truthiness, so age=0 bypasses mutual exclusion
body: validate_timestamp and validate_age test self.initial_data.get('age') / get('timestamp') for truthiness. A report with age=0 and timestamp present passes validation, violating the stated mutual-exclusion rule. Also the endpoint now returns 422 for any malformed report in the batch, changing behavior for the whole request.

title: Error IDs fetched via response[0] without guarding for non-empty snuba result shape
body: error_ids = response[0].get('error_ids', []) assumes process_raw_response returns a list of dicts; if the query returns rows lacking error_ids the endpoint silently sends no error context. Also the new query runs on every request before pagination, adding a Snuba round trip to the hot path.

title: Typo in comment ('segements') and loose null handling
body: The added comment contains a typo. More importantly, the early return for max_segment_id None is correct, but the MatchedRow type change is not reflected in fetch_rows_matching_pattern's query, which still uses max() that can return null for groups with no segments.

title: New equations parameter is accepted but not forwarded to the RPC query path
body: run_top_events_timeseries_query now accepts equations and passes it through, but the query() path and other callers were not updated, so equations-based top-N queries on logs still silently ignore equations in the caller chain that does not supply it.

title: Visualize model changed from multi-yAxis to single yAxis while persisted URL/JSON format still uses yAxes arrays
body: Visualize now holds one yAxis, but toJSON still emits yAxes: [this.yAxis] and BaseVisualize keeps yAxes arrays. Existing saved queries and URLs with multiple yAxes are split into multiple Visualize entries, changing layout and labels for saved explore queries. Callers such as useTopEvents and charts were changed to assume one yAxis, which drops multi-series overlays that users previously had.

title: Attribute keys query switched from useApiQuery to useQuery, losing the project environment param and retry settings
body: The new implementation drops environment, staleTime, refetchOnWindowFocus and retry options from the request and uses a generic useQuery with a queryKey that does not include the API path. Caching by queryKey may serve results across org or projects with the same options, and the environment filter that was previously sent is no longer applied.

title: Feature-flagged table branch renders hardcoded empty data instead of real results
body: When the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature is enabled, TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with columns=[] and empty tableData, discarding tableResults entirely. Users with the flag see an empty table for every table widget.

title: Fallback column derivation crashes when tableData.meta is undefined
body: Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields) dereferences meta without optional chaining on the first access, so a tableData object lacking meta throws, while other code paths use tableData?.meta and are guarded inconsistently.

title: Summary card renders while isPending is true only after feature check
body: The summary component returns null for the feature-gated path before checking isPending, but useFeedbackSummary runs its query regardless of feature gating in the render path. Minor: the query is enabled by the feature check, so the hook is consistent, but the isError branch hides errors silently with no logging.

title: Replacing FlexSpacer with Flex.Item changes layout semantics without tests
body: The FlexSpacer styled div (flex-grow:1) was replaced with Flex.Item grow={1}, which changes the rendered element and may alter spacing in tabs and filename layouts across many consumers. No visual or snapshot test covers this change.

title: Removing the 'Type' row drops the variant type information from grouping UI
body: All variant types previously displayed a 'Type' row with an explanatory tooltip. The change removes it entirely, so users can no longer see whether a variant is a component, custom fingerprint, built-in fingerprint, or performance problem; the tooltip explanations are lost too.

title: AI summary project now taken from replayRecord, but the URL project param is no longer used
body: The query uses replayRecord.project_id instead of the location project param. If replayRecord is undefined the project is undefined and the summary query is disabled, so the tab shows 'No summary' instead of loading, and the removed URL-based lookup is a behavior change not covered by tests.

title: Top-N now enabled for multi-series charts that previously disabled it
body: The guard that disabled topEvents when any visualize had multiple yAxes was removed, but the Visualize model is now single-yAxis and multi-yAxis queries are split. Top-N results with multiple y-axes can now be requested, which the backend and chart code were not built to handle together.

title: New owner validation tests lack a team-owner-not-in-org case
body: test_owner_not_in_organization covers a user from another org, but there is no equivalent for a team from another organization, so cross-org team ownership validation is untested.

title: GitHub user check is skipped when no Integration row exists yet
body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, when Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist (around line 481-482), the view returns pipeline.next_step() immediately. The new check that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user matches the installing sender (around lines 501-505) only runs when the Integration row already exists. If the installation webhook has not arrived yet, or the row is absent for any other reason, a user can complete the pipeline with an arbitrary installation_id without ever being checked against the installer. That defeats the purpose of this PR, and the check should also run on that path, or the path should be made to fail.

title: KeyError when integration metadata has no sender
body: The comparison uses integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]. build_integration only stores "sender" in metadata when state.get("sender") is truthy, so an integration without a stored sender raises KeyError and the request returns a 500 instead of the intended error page. Use a safe lookup and fail closed, e.g. treat a missing sender as a mismatch.

title: Network failures during OAuth exchange are not handled
body: The call req = safe_urlopen(...) on the access-token exchange sits outside the try block. Likewise get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) is not guarded. A connection error or timeout to GitHub raises an unhandled exception and produces a 500 rather than the install-failed page, and the user cannot recover without restarting the flow.

title: State and redirect_uri are interpolated into the authorize URL without encoding
body: The OAuth authorize URL is built with f-string interpolation of state and redirect_uri without urlencode. The redirect_uri contains a scheme and slashes, which can break or alter query parsing on the GitHub side. Build the query with urlencode to be safe.

title: 404 installation-not-found path no longer tested
body: test_installation_not_found previously asserted the specific 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' message. The changed test now only sends a second request with a different state and asserts the generic 'Invalid installation request.' message. The original 404 behavior is no longer covered, and the new assertion can be satisfied by an unrelated failure.

title: Brittle responses.calls index in assert_setup_flow
body: The assertion reads responses.calls[2] to find the JWT Authorization header. The index now depends on how many OAuth and user calls happen before it, so unrelated stub changes will break it or make it check the wrong request. Locate the call by URL instead.

title: GitHub user check is skipped for fresh installs
body: The new sender-vs-authenticated-user check is placed after the `except Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()` branch (around line 481-482). When no Integration exists yet for the installation_id, the pipeline advances without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to the installing user. The PR's stated purpose is to reject a mismatch, but that case is not covered. Only the 'Integration exists but no OrganizationIntegration' path is verified.

title: KeyError when integration metadata has no sender
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes a 'sender' key. `build_integration` only stores `sender` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy, so integrations created without it (or created by other paths) will raise KeyError and produce a 500 during installation instead of the intended error page. Use `.get` with a safe fallback and fail closed.

title: Authorize URL built without URL-encoding parameters
body: `redirect_uri` and `state` are interpolated directly into the query string. The redirect_uri is an absolute URL with its own query/characters and is not encoded, so it can be mangled or break parsing. Build the query with urlencode to be safe.

title: Brittle hard-coded responses.calls index
body: The assertion switches from `responses.calls[0]` to `responses.calls[2]` to locate the JWT-authorized request. This depends on the exact number and order of mocked HTTP calls, so any change to the OAuth flow will break it for unrelated reasons. Locate the call by URL instead.

title: Sender check is skipped entirely when no Integration row exists yet
body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, when Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, the code returns pipeline.next_step() immediately. The new check that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user matches integration.metadata['sender']['login'] is only reached when an Integration row already exists. So the user-mismatch protection that this PR advertises is not applied on that path, and the pipeline proceeds to build_integration without any verification that the authenticated user installed the app. The check should be enforced regardless of whether the Integration row exists, or the flow should explicitly require the sender to be known before continuing.

title: KeyError when an existing Integration has no 'sender' in metadata
body: integration.metadata['sender']['login'] is accessed directly. build_integration only stores 'sender' when state.get('sender') is truthy, and integrations created before this metadata existed, or created without it, will not have the key. The result is an unhandled KeyError (HTTP 500) in the installation pipeline instead of the intended error page. Use a safe lookup and fail with error() when the sender is missing.

title: OAuth authorize redirect builds URL without encoding parameters
body: The authorize redirect concatenates state and redirect_uri into the query string without URL-encoding them (f"...&state={state}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}"). redirect_uri is an absolute URL containing ':' and '/' and any '&' or '#' in it would break the query. Use urllib.parse.urlencode for the parameters.

title: Missing code parameter is sent to GitHub without validation
body: data['code'] is taken from request.GET.get('code') and may be None. The request is still sent to the access-token endpoint, and the failure is only detected afterwards via a missing access_token. Validate that code is present before calling GitHub, and handle a failed safe_urlopen (network error) explicitly, since it is not wrapped in any error handling.

title: Tests do not cover the state mismatch or code reuse failure paths
body: The new failure modes listed in the PR (state signature mismatch, GitHub rejecting the code/access token) have no dedicated tests. The only negative test added is user mismatch, and the bypass path where no Integration row exists is not tested. Also the assertion uses responses.calls[2] by index, which is brittle against changes in the number of mocked calls.

title: Default `queued` timestamp is evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass default evaluated once when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource gets the same stale timestamp rather than the time the assignment was queued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

title: from_dict swallows missing-key and unexpected-key errors silently
body: `from_dict` catches ValueError and TypeError and returns None. Payloads with extra keys or missing required keys (TypeError from the constructor) are treated as 'no source', so the loop-prevention check silently does not apply and outbound sync proceeds. Any schema drift between producer and consumer of the task payload re-opens the sync cycle without any log.

title: to_dict serializes datetime, which is not JSON-safe for Celery kwargs
body: `to_dict` uses `asdict`, which keeps `queued` as a datetime object. The result is passed as task kwargs through apply_async; depending on the serializer this fails or round-trips inconsistently. Serialize the timestamp to an ISO string, or drop it.

title: where_should_sync calls should_sync without a sync source, so inbound-status paths are unaffected but the signature is inconsistent
body: where_should_sync always calls `should_sync(key)` with no assignment source, so the new loop check never runs through this path. If it is ever used to gate outbound assignee sync, the same-integration check is silently bypassed. Either pass the source through or document why it is not needed.

title: Outbound sync check only applied to user assignments; deassign path does not verify source propagation
body: The assignment_source is passed to sync_group_assignee_outbound only in the user branch and in deassign. Inbound team assignments never sync outbound anyway, but the source is also dropped from the reassign path into remove_old_assignees, so no test covers the combined assign-then-deassign loop the PR is meant to break.

title: Test name has typo and there is no test for a malformed-but-complete payload
body: `test_from_dict_inalid_data` is misspelled. The tests also never cover a payload with a valid source_name/integration_id plus an extra key, which is the realistic drift case that from_dict silently drops to None.

title: Base should_sync signature changed without updating all overrides
body: IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync gained a sync_source parameter, but integrations overriding should_sync with the old one-argument signature will now raise TypeError when called with two arguments from sync_assignee_outbound task and where_should_sync paths. The change should be audited across all integrations.

title: queued default timestamp is evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource instance gets the same stale process-start timestamp rather than the time the assignment was queued. The field is then serialized via to_dict and sent to the task, so the recorded time is wrong. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

title: from_dict cannot round-trip the serialized queued timestamp
body: to_dict uses asdict, which yields `queued` as a datetime object, but it is passed through Celery kwargs (JSON serialization) and back. When it arrives as an ISO string, cls(**input_dict) accepts it without type checking, so `queued` silently becomes a string; the from_dict contract and the field type disagree. Also unknown keys raise TypeError and are swallowed, returning None and silently disabling the loop-prevention check.

title: should_sync signature change breaks other callers and overrides
body: should_sync now takes a sync_source parameter, but sync_status_outbound and other call sites (e.g. where_should_sync in utils/sync.py line 48) still call should_sync(key) without it, and subclasses overriding should_sync with the old one-arg signature will raise TypeError when called with sync_source from sync_assignee_outbound. The change is not applied consistently across the integration base classes and implementations.

title: Loop prevention only blocks outbound assignee sync, not the status sync path
body: The sync_source check is added to should_sync generically, but sync_status_outbound also receives assignment_source and the fix is only applied to the assignee path. The issue describes cycles from inbound webhooks, and the status path is not guarded, so a status-triggered cycle through the same integration is not prevented. Also the check compares the source integration_id to the org integration's integration_id, which is only correct if the source is always an Integration row, not e.g. a plugin.

title: assignment_source kwarg passed to implementations that may not accept it
body: The task now calls installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...) unconditionally. Existing integration implementations of sync_assignee_outbound whose signature lacks **kwargs will fail with TypeError when called. The abstract method signature in IssueSyncIntegration was not updated to declare this parameter, so the contract is unclear.

title: Assignment source is not forwarded on the create path or to subsequent re-assignments consistently
body: The new assignment_source is only used when the outbound sync is triggered inside the affected branch; this is consistent with the other paths, but there is no test covering deassign with a matching source integration, so the deassign loop-prevention path is untested.

title: No test covers the source-integration-matches path for deassign or the task-level parsing
body: Tests cover only assign with a matching source. There is no test for deassign with an assignment_source from the same integration, nor for sync_assignee_outbound task receiving assignment_source_dict, so the new deserialization path in the task (including the invalid-dict fallback returning None) is untested at the integration boundary.

title: queued default is evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass default evaluated when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created in the process carries the same stale timestamp rather than the time the assignment was queued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

title: from_dict does not handle the serialized queued value
body: to_dict() serializes `queued` as a datetime object, which is passed through Celery kwargs. Round-tripping through from_dict with a non-JSON-serializable datetime may fail in the task serializer, and from_dict passes whatever `queued` is through unchecked. The task argument is a dict containing a datetime, which is not guaranteed to survive the task broker serialization (e.g. JSON).

title: Inbound deassign path: assignment_source passed but outbound sync on other integrations still fires for the source integration in some paths
body: The deassign path in sync_group_assignee_inbound passes the source integration, but GroupAssignee.deassign only checks the features flag for outbound sync and then calls sync_group_assignee_outbound with assignment_source. Any caller of deassign or assign that does not pass assignment_source (such as the inbound status/other webhook paths) will still cycle back, so the loop protection is only applied to one entry point.

title: Assignment source is not forwarded in the deassign feature check path consistently
body: In deassign, the features.has check is called with actor=acting_user while the source integration is only forwarded to sync_group_assignee_outbound; behavior depends on the flag but there is no test covering deassign with a matching source integration, so the suppression logic for deassign is untested.

title: No test for deassign with a matching source integration
body: The new suppression behavior is tested only for assign. The deassign path, which also takes assignment_source and is the other half of the reported sync loop (unassign propagating back to Jira), has no test confirming outbound unassign is skipped for the originating integration.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is still abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: The class body was reduced to `pass`, but `StatefulDetectorHandler` now declares `build_occurrence_and_event_data` as an abstract method, and this PR also makes `evaluate_group_key_value` call it. `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` does not implement it, so it stays abstract. `Detector.detector_handler` then calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, which raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. Any detector of type `metric_alert_fire` will crash when evaluated. The handler needs an implementation of `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, or the abstract requirements need to be relaxed.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: The docstring of `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` says it 'returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`', but the signature and implementation now return a dict keyed by group key. Callers and implementers reading the docs will expect the old list contract.

title: Duplicate group key detection and its error log were removed silently
body: Keying results by group key means duplicates are now overwritten inside `evaluate` (`results[result.group_key] = result`) rather than detected. The previous `logger.error('Duplicate detector state group keys found')` path is gone, so a handler that produces the same group key twice in one packet now loses one result with no log or metric. This is a loss of observability that the PR description does not mention.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: The class was changed to subclass StatefulDetectorHandler with a body of `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares several abstract members (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data), none of which are implemented here. Instantiating it raises TypeError. Since MetricAlertFire.detector_handler points at this class, any detector of type metric_alert_fire will now crash in Detector.detector_handler / process_detectors instead of returning no results as the previous stub did.

title: New abstract hook breaks all existing StatefulDetectorHandler subclasses
body: build_occurrence_and_event_data is added as @abc.abstractmethod on StatefulDetectorHandler. Any existing or downstream subclass that does not implement it becomes uninstantiable, with no default or migration path. Consider a default implementation that raises NotImplementedError only when a result is actually needed, or clearly document the required override.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: The docstring of StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate says it 'returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult', but the signature and implementation now return a dict keyed by group key. This misleads implementers of the new contract.

title: test_dedupe expects an occurrence fingerprinted for a different group key
body: In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe, the expected occurrence is built with build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, 'val1', ...), so its fingerprint is '<id>:val1'. The call under test is evaluate_group_key_value('group_key', 10, ...), which builds its occurrence with fingerprint '<id>:group_key'. The DetectorEvaluationResult equality check should therefore fail, meaning this test is broken as written. The expected occurrence should use the same group key ('group_key') as the call.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but its body is just `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, none of which are implemented. Instantiating it (which `Detector.detector_handler` does via `group_type.detector_handler(self)`) raises TypeError. Before this change, `evaluate` returned an empty list, so the metric alert detector was safe to construct. Any detector of type `metric_alert_fire` will now crash in `process_detectors`.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: The docstring of StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate says it 'returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`', but the method now returns a dict keyed by group key. Callers relying on the docstring will iterate keys or call list methods and get errors.

title: Duplicate group keys are now silently overwritten before any occurrence is produced
body: In `evaluate`, `results[result.group_key] = result` overwrites any earlier result with the same group key. The removed code in process_detectors logged an error on duplicates. Now the first result is dropped silently, with no log or metric, and its occurrence is never produced. The dict removes duplicates by construction, but the loss is no longer observable.

title: Mock occurrence builder ignores `value`, so tests can't catch wrong values
body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` never uses the `value` argument. Tests such as `test_results_on_change` and `test_dedupe` pass `6` as the value while the evaluated input is `100` or `8`, and the assertions still pass. The tests therefore don't verify that the hook receives and uses the actual group value, which is the core of the new hook.

title: Public helpers removed from mark_failed module without compatibility shims
body: This diff deletes `SimpleCheckIn`, `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason` and `get_monitor_environment_context` from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`, and renames `create_issue_platform_occurrence` to `create_incident_occurrence` in a new module. Any existing import or `mock.patch` target that uses the old module path (for example `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence` or `mark_failed.SimpleCheckIn`) will now raise ImportError or silently patch nothing. The PR does not show a search of the codebase and tests for those references, nor updates to them.

title: Typo carried into docstring: 'humam readible'
body: The docstring of `get_failure_reason` says 'Builds a humam readible string'. Since this function is being moved into a new module, it is a good moment to fix the spelling to 'human readable'.

title: Public helpers removed from mark_failed without compatibility or test updates
body: The PR deletes `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, `SimpleCheckIn`, and the `HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP`/`SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP` constants from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`, and renames `create_issue_platform_occurrence` to `create_incident_occurrence` in a new module. Any other module, test, or `mock.patch("sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence")` target that still uses the old paths or names will now raise ImportError or silently stop patching. The diff does not show any updates to call sites or tests, so the PR needs a repo-wide search for the old names and updated patch targets.

title: Docstring typo carried into the moved helper
body: The moved `get_failure_reason` docstring in `incident_occurrence.py` (line 132 of that file) reads "Builds a humam readible string". This is a typo in a function that is now being newly exposed from a new module, so it should be fixed while it is being moved.

title: Public helpers removed from mark_failed module may break existing importers and mock targets
body: This PR deletes `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `SimpleCheckIn`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, and the status maps from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`, and renames the threshold function to `try_incident_threshold` in a new module. Any code or tests that import these names from `mark_failed`, or patch targets such as `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence` or `produce_occurrence_to_kafka`, will fail with ImportError or AttributeError. The diff does not show any updates to callers or tests, so this is unverified and needs a repo-wide search and test update before merge.

title: Docstring typo and inaccurate example in get_failure_reason
body: The docstring says "Builds a humam readible string" (should be "human readable"). It also gives "A failed check-in was detected" as an example output, but the code never produces that wording; it returns "A ... check-in was detected" with the specific status. The docstring should match the actual output.

title: Rename of threshold function is not reflected in any test changes
body: The function is renamed from `mark_failed_threshold` to `try_incident_threshold` and moved to a new module, but the PR changes no tests. Existing tests that exercise the threshold path via the old name or module path are not updated, and no new test covers the module boundary, so regressions in the move would not be caught by this PR.

title: --flusher-processes defaults to 1, so the PR's one-process-per-shard behavior is not the default
body: The new `--flusher-processes` option defaults to 1, and the factory forwards that value as `max_processes`. `SpanFlusher` then runs `min(max_processes, len(shards))` processes, so with the default every shard in the consumer is flushed by a single process. The PR description says the flusher should spawn a process per redis shard, but that only happens when operators pass a higher value explicitly. Either the default should be unset/None (meaning one process per shard) or the description and help text should say the default is a single process.

title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op in this test, so the wait for the flusher is not real
body: `test_basic` monkeypatches `time.sleep` to a no-op at the top of the test, and the added `time.sleep(0.1)` call uses that same patched function. The comment says it gives flusher threads time to process after the drift change, but the call returns immediately. The test then calls `step.join()` and asserts on `messages`, so it can race with the flusher thread and fail intermittently. The wait needs to use a real sleep or a deterministic synchronization point.

title: _create_process_for_shard is never called
body: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is added but nothing in the diff or the surrounding code calls it; restarts go through `_create_process_for_shards` in `_ensure_processes_alive`. This is dead code that also has a misleading name next to the plural method.

title: Inconsistent metric tag key between flusher timers ('shard' vs 'shards')
body: The `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` metrics use the tag key `shard`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `shards`. Dashboards and alerts filtering on one key will silently miss the other timer's data.

title: Hung thread-based flushers are restarted without being stopped
body: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, `process.kill()` is only called for `multiprocessing.Process`. For the `threading.Thread` path (used in tests with `produce_to_pipe`), a hung thread is left running and a second thread for the same shards is started. Both then flush the same buffer. This is limited to the test path, but it means restart behavior differs between modes.

title: join() stops waiting on deadline but does not terminate the remaining processes
body: In `join`, when the deadline passes the loop breaks before reaching the remaining processes, so those processes are never terminated. They are daemons, but the explicit termination step is skipped for them, so shutdown can leave child processes running.

title: Unrelated anti-pattern section added to CLAUDE.md in a span flusher PR
body: The CLAUDE.md change adds a 'hasattr() for unions' example that has nothing to do with the multiprocessed flusher. It also places an extra blank line before the closing code fence. This should be split into its own change or dropped.

title: --flusher-processes defaults to 1, so the PR's per-shard process model is not the default
body: The new `--flusher-processes` option defaults to 1. The factory passes this to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`, so with the default every assigned shard is handled by a single flusher process. The PR description says the flusher should spawn a process per redis shard, and the flusher docstring says the same. Production consumers that don't set the flag keep the old single-process throughput, which is the bottleneck this change is meant to remove. The help text 'Defaults to 1' also contradicts the 'one process per shard' behaviour. Either the default should be unset/None (meaning one process per shard) or the description and rollout plan should say the scaling is opt-in.

title: New flusher_processes parameter inserted before produce_to_pipe shifts positional arguments
body: `flusher_processes` was added between `output_block_size` and `produce_to_pipe`. Any existing caller that passes `produce_to_pipe` positionally will now pass it into `flusher_processes`, silently breaking the call. The new parameter should be appended after `produce_to_pipe` or made keyword-only.

title: _create_process_for_shard is dead code and would restart the wrong thing if used
body: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is never called; `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts by process index. The method also restarts the whole process that owns the shard, which kills the other shards' flushing in that process without going through the kill/restart bookkeeping (`process_restarts`). It should be removed or wired up correctly.

title: Memory info is summed across per-process buffers, which may double-count Redis usage
body: `submit` now collects `get_memory_info()` from every per-process `SpansBuffer` and sums `used` and `available`. Shards that map to the same redis node (or each buffer reporting the cluster-wide figure) will be counted multiple times, skewing the used/available ratio. The hard-backpressure threshold `spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage` then trips at the wrong level. Memory info should be de-duplicated per redis node or taken from a single buffer.

title: Inconsistent metric tag keys: 'shard' vs 'shards'
body: The produce timer and segment size metrics use the tag `shard`, but the wait_produce timer uses `shards`. Dashboards and alerts filtering on `shard` will miss the wait_produce data, and the same dimension is split across two keys. Use one key consistently.

title: test_basic relies on sleep to wait for a background thread/process
body: The test adds `time.sleep(0.1)` with the comment 'Give flusher threads time to process', then calls `join()`. This is timing-dependent and will be flaky on slow CI, and the test also changes from `django_db` to `transaction=True` without explanation. Synchronize on the flush result (e.g. poll until messages appear with a deadline) instead of a fixed sleep.

title: test_flusher_processes_limit only checks structure, not that flushing works across processes
body: The new test asserts the number of processes and shard distribution, but never submits spans or checks that segments from shards handled by the shared process get flushed. The multi-shard-per-process path, which is the new behaviour, is untested for correctness, and restart behaviour is not covered either.

title: Added 'hasattr vs isinstance' guidance is unrelated to this PR and misleading
body: The new 'WRONG: Use hasattr() for unions' example uses `x = 'hello'` with a `str | None` annotation and calls `hasattr(x, 'replace')`. This is not a real union-narrowing bug, and the rule as stated overgeneralises: hasattr is a legitimate duck-typing check. The change also has nothing to do with the span flusher. It should be dropped from this PR or rewritten to describe an actual problem.

title: isinstance check never matches spawn processes, so hung or dead flushers are never killed
body: The processes are created from `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, so they are `SpawnProcess` instances. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is False. The kill is therefore skipped on every restart. A hung flusher keeps running, and `_create_process_for_shards` starts a second process for the same shards. Duplicate flushers can then produce duplicate or fragmented segments. The old code called `kill()` unconditionally and only caught ValueError. The same check in `join()` (around line 346) means spawned children are never terminated at shutdown.

title: join() never terminates spawned flusher processes
body: The `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard in `join()` is False for `SpawnProcess` objects, so `terminate()` is never called. Processes that did not exit before the deadline keep running after the consumer shuts down. The early `break` on an expired deadline also skips the remaining processes entirely.

title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep
body: The test patches `time.sleep` to a lambda at the top, so the added `time.sleep(0.1)` returns immediately. The comment says it gives flusher threads time to process after the drift change, but it does not. The test can call `step.join()` before the flusher has produced anything, making `(msg,) = messages` flaky.

title: --flusher-processes defaults to 1, contradicting the one-process-per-shard intent
body: The PR's goal is one flusher process per Redis shard. The CLI option defaults to 1, so existing deployments get a single flusher for all shards unless they change the flag. The help text says 'Defaults to 1', but the factory treats None as one process per shard. The CLI default should be None, or the behaviour should match the description.

title: Unused _create_process_for_shard restarts a process without terminating the old one
body: This helper is never called. If it were, it would start a new process for the shard's group without killing or joining the existing one, which leaks the old process. It should be removed or fixed.

title: New flusher_processes parameter inserted before produce_to_pipe breaks positional callers
body: `flusher_processes` was placed before `produce_to_pipe` in the constructor signature. Any caller that passes `produce_to_pipe` positionally will now pass it into `flusher_processes`. Adding the new parameter at the end, or making it keyword-only, avoids this.

title: Shared queue pool is shut down when a rebalance closes the old strategy
body: `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` hands the same `self.queue_pool` to every strategy it creates, and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()`/`terminate()` (queue_consumer.py ~lines 335-342) call `queue_pool.shutdown()`. On a Kafka rebalance, arroyo calls `create_with_partitions` again and closes the previous strategy. The old strategy's close shuts down the pool that the new strategy is using. Afterwards `FixedQueuePool.submit` calls `queue.put` on shut-down queues, which raises, and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` logs and silently drops the message while marking its offset complete. Result messages are lost after any rebalance. The pool lifetime needs to be owned by the factory, not by each strategy's close().

title: Offsets are committed from a background thread, not the processing thread
body: `_commit_loop` runs in its own thread and calls `self.commit_function(committable)`, which is the arroyo `commit` callable bound to the consumer. Arroyo/Kafka consumer commits are not designed to be called concurrently with the consumer's poll loop from another thread, and the strategy's `poll()`/`submit()` run on the processing thread. This can race with the consumer's own commit/poll or with rebalance handling and produce undefined commit behaviour. Commits should be triggered from the strategy's poll/submit path on the processing thread.

title: A single missing offset permanently stalls commits for the partition
body: In `get_committable_offsets`, the loop breaks at the first offset that is not in `all_offsets`. Kafka offsets are not guaranteed contiguous (log compaction, transaction control markers, aborted transactions). If an offset is never delivered to `submit`, `highest_committable` never advances past it, and every later offset is treated as blocked forever. Consumer lag then grows without bound and the committed position never moves, so on restart everything after the gap is reprocessed. The tracker should treat the gap as a non-outstanding position, e.g. by advancing over offsets that were never registered and were below the next delivered offset.

title: Queues are unbounded, so the advertised backpressure does not exist
body: The class docstring claims 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', but every queue is created with `queue.Queue()` (no maxsize), and `submit` never blocks. The consumer will keep polling and buffering Kafka messages in memory whenever a slow worker falls behind, which can exhaust memory under a backlog. Either bound the queues and block or pause the consumer, or remove the claim from the docstring.

title: Shutdown discards queued work items without draining them
body: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` sets `worker.shutdown = True` before shutting down the queues. The worker loop checks that flag before each `get`, so items still queued are abandoned rather than processed. Their offsets are never committed, so they will be reprocessed later. This is safe for at-least-once delivery, but it is not what the 'no item is lost' guarantee in the strategy docstring implies, and nothing logs how many items were dropped.

title: Rebalance/recreate scenario is not tested, which hides the shared-pool shutdown bug
body: All factory tests create one strategy per factory and shut the factory down at the end. There is no test that calls `create_with_partitions` twice, closes the first strategy, and then submits to the second. Such a test would expose that closing one strategy shuts down the shared queue pool and drops messages.

title: Error-handling test assertion is too weak to verify offset behaviour
body: `assert len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets` passes whether or not the failed message blocks the commit. The test also says it checks that errors 'don't block offset commits for other messages', but it never asserts the committed offset for the successful message (101), so it cannot detect the regression it names.

title: `pytestmark` on a unittest TestCase class is ineffective and the Kafka test may silently skip or leak topics
body: `pytestmark = [requires_kafka]` is set on a Django/unittest `TestCase` subclass, where pytest markers are not reliably applied, so the test can run without Kafka and fail with an unhelpful error. The `finally` block also swallows all exceptions from `delete_topics` with a bare `except Exception: pass`, so topic cleanup failures go unnoticed.

title: Strategy close() shuts down the shared FixedQueuePool, which the factory reuses across rebalances
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() (and terminate()) call self.queue_pool.shutdown(). The FixedQueuePool is created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and passed to every strategy returned by create_thread_queue_parallel_worker. Arroyo creates a new strategy on each partition assignment and closes the old one on rebalance. After the first close, all worker threads exit and the queues are shut down, but the factory still holds the same pool. Any later strategy then calls queue.put() on a shut-down queue, which raises queue.ShutDown. submit() catches that and logs it, so messages are silently dropped and their offsets are marked complete, and the commit thread keeps running against a dead pool. The pool should be owned by the factory (shut down only in factory.shutdown()), or each strategy should own its own pool.

title: queue.ShutDown only exists on Python 3.13+
body: queue.ShutDown is referenced in the except clauses of OrderedQueueWorker.run (lines 132 and 142) and in the queue.shutdown() call path. On Python versions before 3.13 the module has no ShutDown attribute. The except expression is evaluated only when an exception is raised, so the worker thread would die with AttributeError as soon as get() or the processing block raises, instead of shutting down cleanly. The repo's supported Python version must be checked, or a sentinel-based shutdown should be used.

title: Queues are unbounded, so the claimed backpressure does not exist
body: The class docstring of SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy promises 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', but queue.Queue() is created with no maxsize (line 185) and submit() never raises MessageRejected. If the broker delivers faster than the workers process, items accumulate in memory without bound and the consumer never pauses. Either set a maxsize and reject messages when full, or remove the claim.

title: Offset gaps stop commits permanently and the scan is O(range)
body: get_committable_offsets iterates every integer from start to max_offset and breaks at the first integer that is not in all_offsets (lines 89-93). Kafka offsets are not always contiguous (compacted topics, transaction markers, deleted records). If an offset never appears, the highest committable offset stays stuck at the gap. Committed progress then stops for the life of the process, lag grows, and after a restart the same range is reprocessed. The loop is also proportional to the offset span rather than the number of tracked offsets, so one long-outstanding offset with large offset jumps makes every commit tick (under the partition lock) iterate a huge range.

title: commit_function is called from the commit thread, not the Arroyo processing thread
body: _commit_loop runs in its own thread and calls self.commit_function(committable), which invokes the Arroyo Commit callable. Arroyo's commit is normally invoked from the strategy's processing thread, and the KafkaConsumer is not documented as thread-safe. Calling it concurrently with the poll loop can corrupt consumer state or raise errors. The commit should be marshalled back to the main thread, for example in poll().

title: Error-handling test asserts the opposite of its stated behaviour
body: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling says errors 'don't block offset commits for other messages', but its final assertion is `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`, which requires that nothing is committed. Since the failing message is swallowed and offset 101 completes, the implementation commits 102 and this assertion would fail if the test ran to completion. The loop may also exit early, so the test can pass without verifying commit behaviour. The assertion should check that the partition is committed past the failed offset.

title: shutdown() cannot release a pool that a strategy has already shut down
body: Because strategies also shut the pool down on close (see queue_consumer.py close()), the factory's shutdown() path and the strategy path both call FixedQueuePool.shutdown() on the same object. The second call is harmless only because shutdown is idempotent in practice. Ownership of the pool should be clarified so that exactly one component shuts it down.

title: Kafka integration test swallows cleanup errors and uses private StreamProcessor methods
body: The finally block wraps admin_client.delete_topics in `except Exception: pass`, hiding failures that would leave test topics behind. The test also calls the private processor._run_once() and processor._shutdown(), which are not a stable API. The test is tied to internal Arroyo details and can break on unrelated library updates.

title: Queues are unbounded, so the advertised backpressure does not exist
body: Each per-queue `queue.Queue()` is created without a maxsize, and `submit` calls `work_queue.put` without blocking limits. The class docstring of `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` promises 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', but nothing ever fills up. If a slow downstream handler or a stalled worker falls behind, in-memory work items and their Kafka message payloads accumulate without bound while the consumer keeps polling and fetching. Either bound the queues and make submit block or apply poll-side pausing, or remove the claim from the docstring.

title: A never-arriving offset stalls commits for the partition permanently
body: In `get_committable_offsets`, the loop breaks at the first offset that is not in `all_offsets`. Offsets can legitimately skip on compacted or transactional topics, or when a message is dropped before submit. When that happens, the highest committable offset can never advance past the hole because the missing offset is never added. Commits for that partition then stop until restart, and the consumer group's lag grows indefinitely. The skipped offset should be treated as complete, for example by tracking the next expected offset from the broker rather than assuming contiguity.

title: Kafka commit function is invoked from a background thread
body: `_commit_loop` runs on its own thread and calls `self.commit_function`, which calls the arroyo `commit` callable provided by the StreamProcessor. The rest of the arroyo pipeline (and the consumer) is driven from the processor thread, and the commit callable and the Kafka consumer are not documented as thread-safe. Calling commit concurrently with poll or with rebalance handling can cause races or errors during partition reassignment. Commits should be issued from the processing thread, for example in `poll`.

title: Error-handling test asserts the opposite of what its name and the design promise
body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` is named to check that errors do not block offset commits, and the worker's `finally` marks a failed item as complete. So offset 101 is committed after 100 fails. The test instead asserts `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`, which requires no commit. The check also runs only 0.2s after processing, before the 1s commit loop runs, so it passes by timing rather than by design. The assertion should verify that the commit reaches 102 (the next offset after 101), and the sleep should be replaced by a wait for the commit.

title: Tests rely on fixed sleeps and polling of internal queue stats, which makes them flaky
body: Most new thread-queue tests poll `queue_pool.get_stats()` and `call_count` in loops with `time.sleep(0.1)`, then assert the result without any event. The commit tests can pass before the 1-second commit thread has run, and `test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_gaps` only checks commits that happened to occur within the window. Use threading events or the `wait` helpers already used in queue_consumer tests so the tests are deterministic instead of depending on scheduler timing.

title: Kafka integration test leaks processor and topic on assertion failure and bypasses the factory it claims to test
body: The processor is shut down only on the success path, and the factory is shut down there too, so a failed assertion leaves the StreamProcessor and its queue threads running. The `KAFKA_TOPIC_OVERRIDES` override is also set but never used by the StreamProcessor, which takes the topic explicitly, so the override is misleading. The `finally` block only deletes the topic and swallows all exceptions. Move processor and factory cleanup into `finally`, and remove the unused override.

title: Backup-code login skips the password check when any totpCode is sent
body: The password check is gated on `user.password && !credentials.totpCode`. Any non-empty totpCode makes the whole password verification block get skipped. The new backup-code branch (line 131) runs regardless of the password, so a request with the email, a valid backup code, and any non-empty totpCode logs in without a password. The login UI clears totpCode in backup mode, so normal use is unaffected, but the credentials callback is reachable directly. The consequence is that a backup code, which is meant to be a second factor, becomes a standalone login credential. A leaked backup-codes download is enough to take over the account. The same gate already lets email plus a valid TOTP skip the password, and this PR extends that bypass to the new code path. The password must be verified independently of which second factor is used.

title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, allowing reuse and resurrection of codes
body: The codes are read in the findUnique at the top of authorize (line 73), checked with indexOf, and then the entire array is written back here. There is no transaction, row lock, or conditional update. Two concurrent logins presenting the same code both pass the check and both succeed, so one code can be spent twice. Two logins presenting different codes race as well: the later write overwrites the earlier one with a stale array, which restores the first code as valid again. Consumed codes can therefore come back to life. The update should be conditional on the value that was read (for example updateMany where backupCodes equals the value read, retrying on mismatch), or run inside a transaction with a row lock.

title: Backup codes are unreachable on the external TOTP screen (IdP/redirect login)
body: The 'Lost access' button exists only in TwoFactorFooter. When totpEmail is set, which the signIn callbacks produce via loginWithTotp for accounts with 2FA, footerText uses ExternalTotpFooter, which offers only Cancel. The BackupCode screen therefore cannot be reached for those users, so the backup codes feature does not work for them. Even if the button were added, the identityProvider guard in next-auth-options.ts (line 113) rejects non-CAL accounts when totpCode is empty, so the backend would also need changing. The feature should either be offered on that screen with the backend path fixed, or the gap should be documented.

title: Dismissing the dialog on the backup codes step permanently loses the codes
body: The Dialog's onOpenChange is passed straight through (line 166). On the DisplayBackupCodes step, Escape, an outside click, or the close icon dismisses the dialog with no warning, and onEnable is not called. By this point the enable endpoint has already succeeded, so 2FA is active on the server. The codes are stored only encrypted, and no endpoint returns them again, so the user ends up with 2FA on, no copy of the codes, and the parent never notified. Their only way out is to disable 2FA. Guard onOpenChange on this step, or treat dismissal like the Close button, and tell the user on this screen that the codes will be shown only once.

title: missing_backup_codes tells users to generate codes in settings, which is not possible
body: The message reads 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' Nothing in this PR provides a settings UI or endpoint to generate backup codes. They are created only during the 2FA setup flow, and disabling 2FA clears them. Users who enabled 2FA before this change, or whose codes were cleared, are sent to do something that cannot be done. The text should describe a real recovery path, or regeneration should be added.

title: Unrelated tabIndex=-1 on the shared PasswordField visibility toggle
body: The show/hide password button now has tabIndex={-1}. PasswordField is shared by every password input in the app (login, signup, password change), not only the 2FA flow, and this change is unrelated to backup codes. It removes the toggle from keyboard tab order, so keyboard-only users can no longer reveal a password they are typing. Either drop the change or justify and scope it separately.

title: The new backup-code login path has no test coverage
body: The PR's own test plan step 2 (log in via 'Lost access' with a backup code) has no e2e or unit test. The TODO on this line acknowledges the gap. The authorize backup branch in next-auth-options.ts and the backup branch in disable.ts are also untested, which is how the password-gate bypass above went unnoticed. At minimum the tests should cover: a backup code logs in once, a second use is rejected with IncorrectBackupCode, a wrong code is rejected, and a backup code without the password fails.

title: Password check skipped whenever totpCode is non-empty, which also bypasses it for the new backup-code path
body: The password verification is gated by `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`, so any non-empty totpCode skips the password check entirely. The new backup-code branch (line 131) runs whenever credentials.backupCode is non-empty, regardless of totpCode. A request with a valid email, a valid backup code, and any non-empty totpCode (for example 'x') logs in without the password ever being verified. Backup codes are meant to replace only the second factor, but this turns them into a single-factor credential (email plus a 40-bit code). The same gap already exists for TOTP, but this PR adds a new route that depends on it. Password verification should not be skippable by supplying an unrelated second-factor field.

title: Backup code consumption is an unlocked read-modify-write, allowing double use and restoration of spent codes
body: The code is read and checked at lines 139-145, then the entire array is rewritten at line 149 with no transaction, lock, or conditional update. Two concurrent logins using the same code can both pass indexOf before either write lands, so one backup code can be spent twice. Concurrent logins with different codes also race: each writes back its own copy of the array, so the later write can restore a code the other request already nulled. Use an atomic compare-and-swap on the stored value (or a transaction with row locking) so that consumption is single-use.

title: Users who reach 2FA via Google/SAML cannot use backup codes at all
body: When 2FA is triggered after an OAuth/SAML sign-in (totpEmail set), the footer is ExternalTotpFooter, which only has a Cancel button, so the 'Lost access' toggle is never rendered. Even if the UI were reachable, authorize() in next-auth-options.ts (lines 113-115) throws ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled for non-CAL users when totpCode is empty, so a backupCode-only submission is always rejected for these users. Users who sign in with Google or SAML and lose their authenticator therefore have no recovery path on the login page. Either wire backup codes into the external TOTP flow or state this limitation explicitly.

title: Closing the backup-codes step via X/Escape/overlay skips the Close handler and loses the codes
body: During DisplayBackupCodes the Dialog's onOpenChange is passed straight through, so the close X, Escape, and overlay click bypass the Close button's handler. By this point the enable request has already succeeded and 2FA is active on the server. onEnable() is never called, so the parent is not told 2FA is enabled, and the codes are discarded with no way to view them again. No regenerate endpoint exists in this PR. Route dismissals during this step through the same handler as the Close button, or block them until the codes have been acknowledged.

title: tabIndex -1 on the password show/hide toggle removes it from keyboard navigation for every PasswordField
body: This change is unrelated to backup codes and is not mentioned in the PR description, but it applies to every PasswordField in the app. tabIndex={-1} removes the visibility toggle from the Tab order, so keyboard-only users can no longer reveal a password they typed. The button has only an sr-only label, so it is effectively unreachable without a pointer. This is an accessibility regression. If the goal was only to skip the toggle on the login form, handle it at that call site instead.

title: type="password" passed to PasswordField overrides its computed type, so the show/hide toggle does nothing
body: PasswordField renders type={isPasswordVisible ? 'text' : 'password'} and then spreads {...props} afterward. The type='password' passed here wins, so the input never switches to text. Clicking the eye toggle changes the icon and label but the value stays hidden. This was previously a plain TextField; the swap introduces a dead control on the enable-2FA password step. Drop the explicit type prop.

title: Non-string backupCode from JSON body throws an unhandled TypeError
body: req.body.backupCode is taken from a JSON body without type checking. Any truthy non-string value (number, object, array) makes .replaceAll throw, which escapes the handler as an unhandled exception and returns a 500 instead of a JSON error. Check typeof req.body.backupCode === 'string' before normalizing it.

title: missing_backup_codes tells users to generate codes in settings, but no such action exists
body: The message says 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' No UI in this PR generates codes outside the initial setup, and the setup endpoint refuses to run once 2FA is enabled. Users who enabled 2FA before this change (backupCodes null) are shown this message on login and sent to a screen where they cannot act. Their only path is disabling 2FA with a TOTP code and re-enabling it. Reword the message or add a regenerate action.

title: Enable test asserts on a switch behind the open backup-codes dialog, with a known-vacuous assertion left in place
body: The PR adds a FIXME stating that this assertion 'passes even when switch is not checked'. The enable test also never closes the backup-codes dialog that now sits on top of the page, so the switch is checked behind the modal. The assertion is therefore weak and knowingly so. Close the dialog and assert data-state='checked' as the disable test does, rather than shipping a check the author has already identified as not validating anything.

title: No test covers logging in with a backup code, the core new behavior
body: The TODO defers backup-code login testing, but this is the main user-facing addition of the PR (the 'Lost access' flow). Nothing exercises the authorize() backup-code branch, the consumption of a code, rejection of reuse, or the new error messages. The disable-endpoint backup path is also untested. At minimum, add an e2e test that logs in with a code, confirms it is accepted once, and confirms reuse is rejected.

title: Copy button shows success toast without awaiting or handling clipboard failure
body: navigator.clipboard.writeText returns a promise that is neither awaited nor caught, and the success toast fires unconditionally. On insecure origins or when permission is denied, the write fails (or navigator.clipboard is undefined and throws), yet the user is told 'Backup codes copied!'. Await the promise and show an error toast on failure.

title: Plaintext backup codes and blob URL persist in component state after the dialog closes
body: resetState() clears password and step but not backupCodes or backupCodesUrl. After the dialog is closed, the plaintext recovery codes stay in React state, and the blob URL that encodes them is never revoked on close (it is only revoked on the next setup call). Clear the codes and revoke the URL when the dialog closes.

title: Backup codes stored reversibly instead of hashed
body: Backup codes are stored with symmetricEncrypt, so anyone holding CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY, or a DB dump together with that key, can recover every unused code and log in as the user. These codes are bearer secrets. Because they are random and high-entropy, a one-way hash (for example SHA-256 with a comparison on the submitted code) would suffice and remove this exposure. Severity is low because the same key already protects TOTP secrets.

title: Backup-code login skips the password check whenever totpCode is non-empty
body: The password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new backup-code branch (line 131) runs whenever `credentials.backupCode` is non-empty, regardless of totpCode. A request that sends email, a valid 10-character backup code, and any non-empty totpCode is authenticated without the password, and the TOTP is never checked either. The login UI clears totpCode in lost-access mode, but the NextAuth credentials endpoint can be called directly. The TOTP branch already has the same password-skip pattern, but this PR adds a second path that needs only the backup code. Password verification should run for CAL users in every branch, so that the backup code or TOTP is an additional factor rather than a replacement for the password.

title: Backup codes can be dismissed without being saved; 2FA is left enabled with the UI out of sync
body: The codes are shown only in the DisplayBackupCodes step, which is reached after the enable endpoint has already set twoFactorEnabled=true. The Dialog still receives `onOpenChange`, so Escape, an overlay click, or the X button closes the modal without calling `onEnable` or the 'Close' button. The codes are never rendered again and there is no endpoint to retrieve or regenerate them, so they are lost. The parent is not notified that 2FA is on, so its switch stays unchecked. Toggling it again then fails in setup with TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled. If the authenticator is later lost, the user has no recovery path. The step should ignore dismissal (or require an explicit acknowledgement), and the dismissal path should still notify the parent.

title: Backup code single-use is not enforced atomically
body: Consumption is a read-decrypt-null-encrypt-write sequence with no transaction or compare-and-set on backupCodes. Two concurrent logins with the same valid code can both read the unconsumed array (line 139), both pass the indexOf check, and both write back, so one backup code yields two sessions. The whole-array write can also resurrect codes that a concurrent disable (which sets backupCodes to null) just cleared. Use a conditional update (for example, compare the old encrypted value in the WHERE clause and check the updated row count) or a transaction with row locking.

title: Users who arrive via external-provider TOTP cannot use backup codes
body: When totpEmail is set (2FA for a Google/SAML sign-in), the footer is only ExternalTotpFooter (Cancel), so there is no 'Lost access' action. The server also blocks backup-only submissions for non-CAL users: in authorize, the ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled check (next-auth-options.ts line 113) fires whenever totpCode is empty. A CAL user who has backup codes and then signs in with Google using the same email goes through loginWithTotp, so they can never use their backup codes and have no recovery path besides their authenticator. Either expose backup codes in this flow and allow a backupCode to satisfy the non-CAL check, or document the limitation.

title: tabIndex=-1 removes keyboard access to the password visibility toggle in every PasswordField
body: This change is unrelated to backup codes but applies to the shared PasswordField component used across the app. Setting tabIndex to -1 makes the show/hide button unreachable by Tab, so keyboard-only users cannot reveal a password they are typing. This is an accessibility regression. Drop the change or justify it separately.

title: No tests exercise backup-code login, backup-code disable, or single-use consumption
body: The new server logic (backup-code branch in authorize, backup-code branch in disable.ts, code consumption, MissingBackupCodes/IncorrectBackupCode errors) has no test coverage. The PR checklist says no tests were added, and the only addition is a TODO. The enable/disable e2e flow only checks the download, copy, and close buttons. A regression in backup-code verification or single-use enforcement would go unnoticed, and the password-bypass issue above would not be caught. Add tests for: login with a valid code (consumed afterwards), reuse of a consumed code, wrong code, and disable with a backup code.

title: Password visibility toggle does nothing because the caller's type="password" overrides PasswordField's type
body: PasswordField renders `<InputField type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"} ... {...props} />`, so props spread after the computed type. Passing `type="password"` here (replacing the former TextField) forces the input to stay masked. The eye button toggles its icon and label, but the field never shows the password. Remove the explicit type prop.

title: Assertion is vacuous: expect(promise).toBeTruthy() always passes
body: `isChecked()` returns a Promise, so `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` checks that a Promise object is truthy and always succeeds. The FIXME above it acknowledges this. The PR edits this block but keeps the vacuous check, so the enable test does not verify the switch state. Use `await expect(page.locator(...)).toBeChecked()`.

title: missing_backup_codes text tells locked-out users to generate codes in settings, which is not possible
body: The message 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' is shown on the login page, where the user is not authenticated. There is no 'generate' action in settings: codes are created only by disabling and re-enabling 2FA, which itself needs a password and TOTP or a backup code. The message points users to a non-existent action.

title: Copy button reports success without awaiting the clipboard write
body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` is neither awaited nor caught, and the success toast is shown immediately. If the write is rejected (permissions, insecure context), the user still sees 'Backup codes copied!' and the rejection is an unhandled promise rejection. Await the write inside try/catch and show an error toast on failure.

title: Submitting an empty backup code in lost-access mode fails silently
body: With an empty backupCode and empty totpCode, authorize() skips the backup branch and throws SecondFactorRequired. The client handler then calls setTwoFactorRequired(true), which is already true, so nothing changes and no error is shown. The HTML required attribute is disabled by noValidate, and the zod schema does not cover backupCode. Validate that backupCode is non-empty before submitting, or show an error when this case occurs.

title: Unguarded property access crashes create() for Meet bookings without a destination calendar
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` can yield `undefined`, but the next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining. handleNewBooking now passes `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, so `evt.destinationCalendar` becomes `[]`. For a booking with Google Meet location, this throws a TypeError inside create() and the booking fails. The previous code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. Fix: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

title: Organization slug and requestedSlug conditions are inverted
body: The original code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })`. The new code is `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})` (line 153). This flips the logic. With billing disabled (self-hosted), the org is created with no slug. With billing enabled, the slug is written immediately and the requestedSlug approval flow is bypassed. This change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose and is not mentioned in the description.

title: updateEvent resolves calendarId to undefined when externalCalendarId is empty; deleteEvent falls back to primary
body: The new fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy.
