It then compares `cal.externalId` against that falsy value, so it matches nothing and returns undefined. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. As a result calendarId is undefined and the Google update fails for booking references that have no externalCalendarId. The same bug is at line 317 in deleteEvent: the lookup returns undefined, so deletion silently targets 'primary' and the event remains on the calendar the user actually picked. Fix: select the destination calendar by credential or take the first destination instead of comparing against externalCalendarId.

title: Video references are saved without credentialId, so cancelled video meetings are never deleted
body: The previous code set `credentialId` to `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results. The new code sets it to `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so every video reference is written with credentialId undefined. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is truthy (`if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)`). Cancelled bookings will therefore leave the video meeting (Zoom, Daily, Meet, etc.) alive.

title: Office365 and Lark createEvent use the organizer's destination calendar for every credential
body: createEvent takes `[mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar` and builds the URL from its externalId, ignoring which credential is calling. For collective events, the team member's O365 credential is therefore asked to write to the organizer's calendar id. Graph returns 404 and the member's event is never created. The Lark createEvent (packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts around line 128) has the same flaw. The Google implementation avoids this by matching on credentialId. The stated goal, that every host with any calendar app receives the event, is not met for these providers.

title: CalDAV createEvent silently creates nothing for team hosts whose calendars don't match the organizer's destination
body: The filter `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` uses the first destination calendar, which belongs to the organizer, even when the call is made with a team member's credential. The team member's CalDAV account has no calendar with that URL, so the filter returns an empty list. responses is then empty, `responses.some((r) => !r.ok)` is false, and createEvent returns a success result with a uid. The member gets no event and no error is surfaced.

title: Destination calendars without credentialId lose their externalId, so events land in primary
body: In the else branch the destination's externalId is dropped: `createEvent(c, event)` is called without it. Google's createEvent resolves the calendar only by matching a destination with the credential's id, so for a legacy destination calendar with no credentialId the event goes to 'primary' instead of the calendar the user selected. The reference then stores externalCalendarId as undefined. The previous code used destinationCalendar.externalId for both the insert and the stored reference.

title: Hangout-link patch uses an undefined calendarId and its promise is neither awaited nor caught
body: The insert falls back to 'primary' (`selectedCalendar || "primary"`), but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. When no destination calendar matches the credential, which is common when a user has no destination row, selectedCalendar is undefined. The patch is built with an undefined calendar and is fire-and-forget, so the description never gets the Meet link and the rejection is unhandled. Fix: reuse the same resolved calendar id as the insert.

title: Recurring-cancel deletion runs once per calendar reference, causing duplicate deletes
body: The loop now iterates over every calendar reference, but the recurring branch builds `promises` from the full updatedBookings list and the user's calendar credentials. That block does not depend on the current reference, so with N references every updated booking's event is deleted N times on every calendar. This wastes external API calls and can trigger rate limits. The recurring deletion should run once outside the per-reference loop.

title: Team hosts' destination calendars are dropped when the organizer has none
body: evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The collective-host calendars are then added with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`, which is a silent no-op on null. In that case no host other than the organizer receives the event, even though their calendars are connected. Build the array explicitly (`[...(base ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`) instead of pushing onto a possibly-null value.

title: Webhook payload destinationCalendar changes from object to array without notice
body: The field is part of the webhook payload (see the e2e expectations in apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts). Subscribers that read payload.destinationCalendar.externalId or similar will break. Empty values are also inconsistent: handleNewBooking emits null, while confirm, cancel, and reschedule emit []. For collective events the payload now also includes every host's DestinationCalendar row, with userId, credentialId, and externalId (often the account email for Google). This is a breaking, undocumented API change that also widens the data sent to subscribers.

title: Collective and multi-calendar behaviour changed without tests
body: The PR checklist states no tests were added, yet this change reworks destination-calendar routing across EventManager, the Google/Lark/Office365/CalDAV services, and booking cancel/reschedule. The regressions noted in this review (null-safety on the Meet branch, video credentialId, legacy destination routing, updateLocation references) are the kind of thing unit tests of EventManager would catch. At minimum, existing EventManager tests need to be updated for the array shape.

title: loadUsers error handling leaks Prisma error messages as 400s and masks other failures as 500s
body: The catch block turns any Prisma known-request error into an HttpError 400 using `error.message`, so raw database error text goes to the API client. Any other error, such as a thrown Error from the empty-dynamicUserList check, becomes a generic 500 'Unable to load users', which discards the real cause. Database failures should be a 500 with a generic message, and validation errors should keep their specific messages.

title: updateLocation writes calendar references without credentialId or externalCalendarId
body: CalendarManager.updateEvent does not return credentialId or externalId in its EventResult. The new `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined` and `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` therefore store null for calendar references. The previous code fell back to evt.destinationCalendar. Those references are then used by handleCancelBooking, which takes the legacy path and deletes by uid on every calendar of that type, or targets 'primary' for Google, so the real event is left behind.

title: Reschedule with newBookingId deletes only the first old calendar event
body: After updating calendar events for all references, the merge path still picks a single old calendar reference with `booking.references.find(...)`. Bookings with several calendar references (the collective multi-host case this PR enables) keep the old events on the other hosts' calendars.

title: Confirming a collective booking never includes team hosts' destination calendars
body: The confirm handler builds evt.destinationCalendar only from the booking's destination or the organizer's. Unlike handleNewBooking, it does not add collective hosts' calendars. Bookings that require confirmation are therefore created only on the organizer's calendar when confirmed. The same gap exists in the Stripe and PayPal payment-success paths, which also build evt from the booking and organizer only.

title: Dynamic-user query drops the organization select without explanation
body: The findMany for dynamic users previously selected `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`. That select is removed here with no replacement. Any downstream code that reads users[].organization will get undefined. The change is unrelated to the PR's purpose and should be justified or reverted.

title: Google Meet fallback dereferences a possibly undefined destination calendar
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the array is empty, but line 119 reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. So when the location is Google Meet and no destination calendar is set (null or []), `create()` throws a TypeError and the booking fails instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

title: Video references are saved without credentialId
body: The `credentialId` mapping in `create()` was changed to `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Previously non-calendar (video) results kept `result.credentialId`. Now every video reference is stored with a null credentialId. handleCancelBooking.ts only deletes the video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set (around line 491), so cancelled bookings leave the Zoom/Daily/etc. meeting behind. The seated-cancellation video update path has the same dependency. Restore `result.credentialId` for the non-calendar branch.

title: Destinations without credentialId lose their externalId and can create duplicate events
body: For destinations without a credentialId, `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the destination's externalId. The result therefore has `externalId` undefined, and the booking reference is stored with a null externalCalendarId. Google picks its calendar only by credentialId, so the event goes to 'primary' and later update/delete cannot find the right calendar. The previous code stored `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. In addition, this loop runs once per destination against the same list of credentials of that type, so N such destinations and K credentials produce N×K events.

title: Per-destination calendar is only honored by the Google service; other calendar apps still use the organizer's calendar
body: CalendarManager calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. The destination externalId is only attached to the returned result, so the calendar implementation never sees which calendar this credential should write to. Only the Google service resolves its calendar by credentialId. Lark (googlecalendar-style `destinationCalendar[0]` at larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts line 129), Office365 (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts line 75) and CalDAV (lib/CalendarService.ts line 161) always use the first destination, which for a collective event is usually the organizer's calendar. A team member's Lark or O365 credential therefore targets the organizer's calendar ID with the member's token, which fails. The collective-event fix works only for Google.

title: CalDAV reports success when no event was written for a team member
body: The filter keeps only calendars whose externalId equals the first destination's externalId. For a team member's CalDAV account that URL does not exist, so the filtered list is empty. `responses` is then empty, `responses.some((r) => !r.ok)` is false, and the function returns a uid as if the event was created. CalendarManager records success=true, the member never gets the event, and no error is logged.

title: updateEvent calendar fallback is always undefined
body: The fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. This branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate compares against null/undefined and never matches. The result is `calendarId: undefined` for `events.update`. Booking references with a null externalCalendarId (legacy rows and rows written by the no-credentialId branch in EventManager) can no longer be updated, which breaks reschedule and location edits. The previous code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`.

title: deleteEvent fallback never finds the destination calendar and defaults to primary
body: Same dead predicate as in updateEvent: `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always returns undefined. `calendarId` then becomes 'primary' (line 322), so cancelling a booking whose reference has no externalCalendarId deletes from the user's primary calendar, not the calendar the event was created on, and the event remains on the destination calendar.

title: Hangout patch still uses selectedCalendar, which can now be undefined
body: The insert now falls back with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `events.patch` (line 168) still passes the raw `selectedCalendar`. That value is undefined when no destination matches the credentialId, so the patch is sent without a calendarId. The patch is fire-and-forget with no callback or catch, so the failure is unhandled and the hangout link description is silently not updated. Use the same fallback in the patch.

title: Team members' calendars are dropped when the organizer and event type have no destination calendar
body: `destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one (around line 1067). `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so every collective member's calendar is discarded. This is the scenario the PR is meant to fix. The array may also start with a team member's calendar, which the calendar services then treat as the organizer's main calendar.

title: Recurring cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference of each instance
body: The PR changed the top-level logic to iterate over all calendar references, but this recurring-cancel path still uses `updBooking.references.find(...)`, so only the first calendar reference per instance is considered. For a collective recurring booking with a second calendar reference (for example the team member's), that event is never deleted. The calls go to every calendar credential with the first reference's uid, which fails silently for the other accounts.

title: Recurring deletions are repeated once per calendar reference
body: This block sits inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. Each iteration re-runs the same deletion of every updated booking across all calendar credentials. With two calendar references and a recurring series, each instance's event is deleted twice (or more), producing duplicate API calls and duplicate entries in `apiDeletes`. The deletion should run once, outside the loop.

title: Inverted condition: organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled
body: The original `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` spreads `slug` when billing is disabled. The rewrite `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` spreads it only when billing is enabled. The behavior is inverted for both self-hosted and cloud deployments, and the change is unrelated to the destination-calendar work in this PR. Revert to the original predicate.

title: loadUsers error handling turns client errors into 500s and leaks Prisma messages
body: The new try/catch wraps the whole user-loading path. The `dynamicUserList` validation at line 728 throws a plain Error, which is not an HttpError, so it is rethrown as HttpError 500 'Unable to load users', losing the message and the 4xx status. Conversely, Prisma known-request errors are rethrown as HttpError 400 with the raw Prisma message, which exposes internal details. The old code let these errors propagate unchanged.

title: Webhook payload destinationCalendar changes from object to array without a breaking-change note
body: The event object is sent as-is in BOOKING_CREATED/REQUESTED webhook payloads (`...evt` in sendPayload). `destinationCalendar` changes from a DestinationCalendar object (or null) to an array (or null here, [] in other paths). Existing webhook consumers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` will break. The e2e test was edited to expect `[]` for BOOKING_REJECTED while still expecting `null` for BOOKING_CREATED, so the payload is now inconsistent across events and the contract change is undocumented.

title: Organization relation dropped from dynamic-group user query without explanation
body: The `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` selection was removed from the dynamic-user query. The PR does not explain why or add a replacement. If any downstream code in this handler reads `users[i].organization` for dynamic group bookings, it now receives undefined. The removal should be justified or reverted.

title: Error logging removed from updateAllCalendarEvents catch block
body: The `console.error(message)` call was removed. The catch now returns fallback results with success=false and emits no log, so calendar update failures disappear silently. The `message` string is still built but never output.

title: No tests cover the new multi-destination create/update/cancel logic
body: The PR states no tests were added. The new multi-destination logic in createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents, and the Google calendar-id selection, are where most of the defects above sit (null-calendar regressions, dead predicates, lost credentialIds). A unit test per destination shape (with and without credentialId, empty and multiple destinations) would catch these.

title: Office365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar, so other hosts' invites fail
body: For COLLECTIVE events event.destinationCalendar now holds one calendar per host, but this code always takes the first entry (line 73) and never checks which credential is running. CalendarManager.createEvent forwards credential.id, and EventManager passes destination.externalId, but that externalId is only echoed back in the result and never reaches the service. For a team member's Office365 account the URL becomes /me/calendars/<organizer's calendar id>/events, which does not exist in that account, so the member never gets the event. The same pattern exists in Lark createEvent (calendarId taken from destinationCalendar[0], around lines 128-129 of the Lark service) and in CalDAV createEvent (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts filters calendars by the first destination's externalId; for a member's account nothing matches, no object is created, and the call still returns success). Only the Google service selects by credentialId, so the collective fix works for Google only.

title: Google deleteEvent falls back to 'primary' instead of the event's calendar
body: When externalCalendarId is falsy, the expression searches destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals that falsy value. It never matches, so calendarId becomes undefined and the code falls back to 'primary'. The previous code used event.destinationCalendar?.externalId here. On cancel, the delete goes to the user's primary calendar instead of the calendar holding the event. Google returns 404 and deleteEvent resolves silently, so the event stays on the real calendar with no error. This is reachable for references without externalCalendarId, including those the new EventManager code creates without it.

title: Google updateEvent passes undefined calendarId when externalCalendarId is missing
body: Same mistake as deleteEvent: when externalCalendarId is null, find() compares cal.externalId against null, never matches, and selectedCalendar becomes undefined. The previous code fell back to event.destinationCalendar?.externalId. Now calendar.events.update is called with calendarId undefined, so updates fail for every reference without externalCalendarId. The new EventManager paths produce exactly such references (see the updateLocation and create findings).

title: Google Meet description patch uses selectedCalendar, which can now be undefined
body: The insert uses 'selectedCalendar || "primary"', but the patch call below uses the raw selectedCalendar. When no destination matches the credential, the patch gets calendarId undefined. The patch is not awaited and has no error handling, so the hangout link description update silently fails for events inserted into primary. The same resolved calendarId should be used in both calls.

title: Google createEvent ignores destinations stored without a credentialId
body: The lookup matches destinations only by cal.credentialId === credentialId. Legacy DestinationCalendar rows with credentialId null never match, so the event goes to 'primary' instead of the configured externalId. The previous code used calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.externalId directly. EventManager's no-credentialId branch (createEvent(c, event) with no destination) makes this path reachable, so users with legacy destination rows get their bookings created in the wrong calendar.

title: Unguarded destructured element can throw when no destination calendar exists
body: mainHostDestinationCalendar comes from array destructuring, so its static type is DestinationCalendar, not DestinationCalendar | undefined. When evt.destinationCalendar is null or empty and the location is Google Meet, this line dereferences undefined and throws a TypeError inside create(). The previous code used evt.destinationCalendar?.integration, which was safe. Booking creation fails for these events. Use mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration.

title: externalCalendarId is dropped for destinations created without a destination id
body: createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent(c, event) without destination.externalId in the no-credentialId branch, the fallback branch, and for other_calendar integrations. CalendarManager.createEvent then returns externalId undefined, so result.externalId is undefined and the booking reference is saved without externalCalendarId. The previous code persisted evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId. Later update and delete calls then have no calendar id to work with (see the Google updateEvent and deleteEvent findings).

title: updateLocation writes calendar references with no credentialId or externalCalendarId
body: CalendarManager.updateEvent returns only appName, type, success, uid, updatedEvent, originalEvent, calError and calWarnings. It never returns externalId or credentialId, so result.externalId and result.credentialId are always undefined here. editLocation.handler persists these via references.create, so the new calendar reference rows lack credentialId and externalCalendarId. The previous code fell back to evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId and externalId. A later cancel then takes the legacy no-credentialId path in handleCancelBooking, which deletes using all calendar credentials of that type and no calendar id.

title: Webhook payload destinationCalendar changes shape and empty value is inconsistent
body: evt is spread into webhook payloads (sendPayload with ...evt), so destinationCalendar in BOOKING_CANCELLED and other webhooks changes from a DestinationCalendar object or null to an array. This is an undocumented breaking change for webhook consumers. Empty is now [] here but null in handleNewBooking (BOOKING_CREATED/REQUESTED), so consumers checking for null get different values per event type. The e2e expectation change from null to [] in webhook.e2e.ts (line 249) confirms the public payload changed.

title: Cancel loop repeats recurring and legacy deletions once per calendar reference
body: The former single if was turned into a loop over all calendar references, but the recurring branch does not depend on the reference. For a recurring series cancelled with allRemainingBookings, it deletes every updated booking's events across all user calendar credentials once per reference, so a collective series with N references issues N times the deletes and pushes duplicate entries into apiDeletes. The legacy no-credentialId branch likewise re-runs for each reference lacking credentialId. The loop should be restructured so the recurring deletion runs once.

title: Team members' calendars are silently dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null
body: evt.destinationCalendar is null when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar. Then evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...) is a no-op, so for a COLLECTIVE event the team members' destination calendars are never added. EventManager sees no destinations and falls back to a single calendar for the organizer, so the other hosts never get the event. Initialise the array before pushing, or build the combined list in one place.

title: Organization slug condition is inverted
body: The original code was '...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })', so slug was set when billing was disabled. The new '...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})' sets slug only when billing is enabled. Self-hosted instances (billing disabled) will now create organizations without a slug. Billing-enabled instances will get the slug immediately, bypassing the requested-slug flow. This change is unrelated to the PR's collective-host fix and is not explained in the description.

title: Calendar update failures are no longer logged
body: The console.error(message) in the catch block was removed, but the message is still built with the error details. Failures in updateAllCalendarEvents now return error result objects without any log entry, so the cause of a failed calendar update is lost.

title: organization.slug removed from dynamic-group user select without explanation
body: The findMany for dynamic group users dropped 'organization: { select: { slug: true } }'. The PR description does not mention it. If any code later in handleNewBooking reads organization.slug for dynamic-group bookings, it now gets undefined. Confirm there are no remaining readers or restore the select.

title: loadUsers catch-all turns client errors into a generic 500
body: Any error that is not an HttpError or PrismaClientKnownRequestError, including the new plain Error for an empty dynamicUserList (which is a client input problem), is rethrown as HttpError 500 'Unable to load users'. The original message is discarded, and a request validation problem looks like a server fault. Prisma known errors are mapped to 400, which is also a questionable classification for database failures.

title: Multi-destination calendar creation has no tests
body: createAllCalendarEvents now loops over several destinations, fetches credentials from the DB for other hosts, and handles the no-credentialId path differently. updateAllCalendarEvents also loops over multiple references. The only test-file change is one e2e expectation. Several regressions listed above (missing externalCalendarId, dropped credentialId, wrong calendar selection) would be caught by unit tests that run EventManager with a two-destination collective event against mocked calendar services.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported, so every Salesforce calendar operation fails
body: The new token-refresh code calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` inside `getClient`, but the file's import block (lines 1-20) never imports `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. This is a ReferenceError at runtime and a TypeScript compile error. `getClient` is invoked from the constructor and its promise is stored in `this.conn`, which create, update, delete and contact lookup all await, so those operations reject once this lands.

title: Salesforce token is refreshed on every service construction, bypassing the sync endpoint
body: Previously constructing the service made no network call. Now `getClient` always POSTs to login.salesforce.com and writes the credential row back, even when the stored access token is still valid. CalendarService instances are created per availability check, booking and settings page, so this adds a Salesforce login request and a DB write each time, which can run into Salesforce login rate limits. The refresh also does not go through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so with app-credential sync enabled Cal.com still refreshes with its own consumer secret instead of the self-hoster's endpoint, contrary to the purpose of this PR. The `response.statusText !== "OK"` check is also fragile (HTTP/2 responses carry no reason phrase) and discards the error body.

title: Sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but every caller reads a parsed token payload
body: In sync mode the function returns the `fetch` Response from the self-hoster endpoint without parsing it or checking `response.ok`. The local branch returns an object with `.data` (Google, zohocrm, zoho-bigin) or token fields (HubSpot). Callers therefore break in sync mode: Google reads `res?.data` (undefined), so `token.access_token` throws inside a catch that silently keeps the expired access token. zoho-bigin reads `tokenInfo.data.error` outside any try block, so a TypeError propagates and every call fails. zohocrm reads `.data.error` inside its try, so the refresh is skipped with only a log line. HubSpot reads `expiresIn` and `accessToken` from it. The `() => any` signature hides this from the type checker. The sync branch should `await response.json()`, check status, and return the body in the same shape as the local branch.

title: HubSpot refresh in sync mode writes a fetch Response object into the credential key
body: With sync enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch Response, so `hubspotRefreshToken` is a Response. `expiresIn` is undefined, so `expiryDate` becomes NaN on line 192. Line 198 then stores that Response as the credential `key`. Serialized, it becomes an empty object or Prisma rejects it, so the stored access and refresh tokens are lost. `hubspotClient.setAccessToken(hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken)` then receives undefined. The error is swallowed by the surrounding catch, so the failure is not visible.

title: Placeholder 'refresh_token' value overwrites the real refresh token
body: When the refresh response has no refresh_token, this sets it to the literal string 'refresh_token'. Callers persist the parsed data, so the real stored refresh token is replaced. Office365 calendar merges `tokenResponse.data` over the stored credential, so a Microsoft refresh response without refresh_token overwrites the real one, and the next refresh fails with invalid_grant. In sync mode this placeholder is produced on every refresh, because the minimum schema strips refresh_token (see line 8). The function should leave the field undefined and let callers keep the stored token.

title: Minimum token schema uses computed keys that stringify to '[object Object]'
body: `z.string().toString()` does not produce a key pattern. ZodType has no custom toString, so both computed keys become the literal property name '[object Object]', and the second overrides the first. The schema therefore validates only access_token, and the comment's rule that numeric properties are expiry is never enforced. Because z.object strips unknown keys by default, refresh_token, expires_in, scope and expiry_date are removed from the parsed data in sync mode. Callers then persist a key without its expiry, and Office365 keeps the old expires_in, so the token is treated as expired and refreshed on every call.

title: Sync-mode condition does not match refreshOAuthTokens, corrupting team credential refreshes
body: This branch uses the minimum schema whenever sync is enabled and the endpoint is set. `refreshOAuthTokens` only uses the endpoint when `userId` is also set (its line 5). For team credentials (userId null) the refresh runs locally and returns the real provider payload, but this function still applies the minimum schema. Fields are stripped and the placeholder refresh token from line 26 is written, so with sync enabled every refresh of a team credential (for example Google Calendar) corrupts the stored key. The two conditions must match, or the decision should be passed in explicitly.

title: Helper now throws instead of returning a result, making caller success checks dead code
body: The function previously returned the safeParse result, and callers checked `.success`. It now throws on failure, so the `.success` branches are unreachable: Office365 calendar's `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data`, zoomvideo's `if (!parsedToken.success)`, and salesforce's `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)`. Office365 also lost the console.error that logged the Zod error and the Microsoft response body. Either document the new contract and clean up the callers, or keep returning the result.

title: Sync request sends app slug 'zoomvideo' while Zoom credentials are stored under 'zoom'
body: The refresh call passes 'zoomvideo' as the app slug, but the Zoom callback creates credentials with `appId: "zoom"` (zoomvideo/api/callback.ts line 73) and looks them up by appId 'zoom'. The self-hoster's sync endpoint keys tokens by app slug, so a request for 'zoomvideo' will not find the Zoom token. The slug should match the credential's appId.

title: Shared webhook secret compared with non-constant-time !==
body: The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which returns early on the first differing byte, so response timing can reveal how much of the secret matched. This endpoint authenticates requests that create and overwrite credentials for any user. The comparison should use crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers.

title: Malformed input produces 500 errors instead of 400
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on an invalid body rather than returning 400. Likewise `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` at line 57 throws on a wrong key or corrupt ciphertext. Neither is caught, so the handler returns 500. Wrap both and return 400 with a generic message, so a sender can distinguish a bad payload from a server fault.

title: findFirst followed by create is a check-then-act race that can create duplicate credentials
body: The handler reads with findFirst and then creates or updates. The schema does not enforce uniqueness on (userId, appId), as the Lark callback comment notes. Two concurrent deliveries for the same user and app (for example sender retries) can both see no row and both create one. Later lookups then act on an arbitrary duplicate.

title: Sync update replaces the key but does not clear the invalid flag
body: Refresh failures set `invalid: true` on the credential (for example invalid_grant in the Google, Webex and Zoom adapters). This update replaces `key` with fresh tokens but leaves `invalid` as is. A credential that was flagged invalid will keep the flag after a successful sync, so it stays excluded even though it now holds valid tokens. The update should also reset `invalid`.

title: New credential-writing endpoint and sync refresh path have no tests
body: The PR adds an endpoint that writes credentials for any user and a new token-refresh branch in several adapters, with no tests (the PR checklist says so). The bugs found in this change, such as the missing prisma import, the placeholder refresh token, the broken minimum schema and the sync response shape, are the kind unit tests on parseRefreshTokenResponse, refreshOAuthTokens and this handler would catch. At minimum cover: invalid secret returns 403, malformed body returns 400, create versus update, and each provider's sync-mode response handling.

title: Comment understates the response shape the sync endpoint must return
body: The comment says the response 'should only contain the access token and expiry date'. Callers need more: parseRefreshTokenResponse expects refresh_token, the Webex and Zoom schemas require refresh_token, scope and token_type, Lark reads refresh_expires_in, and HubSpot reads expiresIn. Self-hosters following this comment will build endpoints that fail. The documented contract, including that the body is JSON in the same shape as the provider's response, should be stated accurately.

title: Google refresh stores the safeParse wrapper instead of the parsed tokens
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse result ({ success, data }), not the parsed data. Here that wrapper is assigned to `key` and written to credential.key on every token refresh, regardless of whether sync is enabled. The stored key becomes { success: true, data: {...} }. On the next call, googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) in googleAuth (line 75) finds no top-level access_token/refresh_token and throws, so Google Calendar stops working for that user after the first hourly refresh. Other callers (Office365, Zoom, Salesforce) correctly read .success/.data. Return or store `.data` here.

title: Sync-mode schema computes keys from z.string().toString(), dropping every field except access_token
body: z.string().toString() is a constant (Object's toString, '[object Object]'), not a key pattern, so both computed keys collapse into one property and the second (z.unknown().optional()) overrides the first. The schema therefore validates only access_token. Zod strips unknown keys by default, so when sync is enabled (line 16) expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token and other fields are removed from .data. Callers then compute with undefined: Zoom computes expiry_date = Date.now() + undefined*1000 (NaN, serialized to null, which makes zoomTokenSchema reject the stored key); Zoom and Google also persist the refresh_token placeholder; Salesforce saves a key without instance_url; Office365 keeps its old expires_in and refreshes on every call. The intended 'any numeric property is expiry' needs passthrough or a different shape.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string 'refresh_token'
body: When a refresh response has no refresh_token, this writes the placeholder string 'refresh_token' into the parsed data. Callers persist that value: Office365 (CalendarService.ts line 264) spreads tokenResponse.data over the stored credential, overwriting the valid refresh token with 'refresh_token'. The next refresh then sends a bogus token and fails with invalid_grant. In sync mode the minimum schema always drops refresh_token, so every sync refresh replaces it. Leave the field undefined and keep the existing refresh token instead.

title: Helper both throws on failure and returns a SafeParse result, so callers' .success checks are dead
body: On schema failure this throws, yet on success it returns the safeParse wrapper. Callers that check `!parsed.success` (Zoom VideoApiAdapter around line 108, Salesforce around line 92) can never reach that branch, and the error text is generic. Office365 previously logged the provider's response on schema failure; that logging was removed in this PR, so the provider error is now lost. Pick one contract: return the parsed data or throw.

title: Sync branch returns a raw fetch Response that callers do not expect, and status is never checked
body: When sync is enabled the function returns the fetch Response from the self-hoster's endpoint, while the non-sync branch returns whatever refreshFunction returns. Callers are written against the latter: Google reads res?.data (line 94 of googlecalendar CalendarService), and a fetch Response has no .data, so token.access_token throws. The catch swallows that and the stale access token is used silently. zoho-bigin and zohocrm read tokenInfo.data.error / .data.expiryDate on the result and throw TypeError. Hubspot treats it as a token object. Also response.ok is not checked, so a 500 HTML page is passed on as if it were tokens, and there is no timeout, so a hung endpoint blocks every calendar or video call for that user. Normalize the sync result to the shape each caller expects and check response.ok.

title: HubSpot refresh writes the sync Response object into the credential key
body: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response. hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn is then undefined, so expiryDate becomes NaN (line 192), and line 198 stores the Response instance as the credential key. A Response does not carry the token fields as enumerable properties, so the stored key either becomes an empty or garbage object (losing accessToken and refreshToken) or the update fails. The catch at lines 203-205 only logs, so nothing surfaces. The HubspotToken annotation on line 177 hides the mismatch from the type checker.

title: Zoho Bigin passes the credential id as the Cal.com userId to the sync endpoint
body: refreshAccessToken receives credentialId (credential.id, the row id) and forwards it as the 3rd argument of refreshOAuthTokens, which is the userId and is sent to the self-hoster's endpoint as calcomUserId. In sync mode the endpoint is asked for tokens of user <credential row id>, which is not necessarily the credential's owner. The returned tokens are then written into this credential (lines 102-109), which can attach another user's Zoho tokens to this user's credential. Pass credential.userId, threaded through refreshAccessToken.

title: Zoom refresh sends appSlug 'zoomvideo' but the Zoom app slug is 'zoom'
body: Zoom credentials are created with appId 'zoom' (zoomvideo/api/callback.ts line 73), and the webhook resolves app slugs the same way. Here refreshOAuthTokens is called with 'zoomvideo', the directory name rather than the app slug. A self-hoster's sync endpoint keyed on appSlug will not recognize it or will look up the wrong app. Use 'zoom'.

title: Salesforce CalendarService uses prisma without importing it
body: The new refresh code calls prisma.credential.update (line 96), but the file's imports (lines 1-20) do not include `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This is a TypeScript compile error, and at runtime constructing the client throws a ReferenceError, so every Salesforce calendar operation (contact search, event creation, availability) fails for all users. Add the import.

title: Salesforce refresh checks response.statusText === 'OK' instead of response.ok
body: statusText is the HTTP reason phrase. It is not defined for HTTP/2 responses and is often empty, so a successful refresh can be rejected. The thrown HttpError also reports statusText with a fixed 400 regardless of the real status, and the response body (which contains Salesforce's error_description) is never read. Check response.ok and include the status and error body in the error.

title: Salesforce refreshes its token on every client construction, bypassing the sync endpoint
body: getClient now posts to login.salesforce.com and writes the credential row on every CalendarService construction, even when the stored access token is still valid. Each calendar operation therefore costs an extra network round trip and a DB write, and concurrent operations each refresh and overwrite the same row. The refresh also goes directly to Salesforce with the Cal.com consumer secret and does not use refreshOAuthTokens, so with CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set Salesforce still refreshes on its own, contrary to the sync design. Refresh only when the token is expired and route it through refreshOAuthTokens.

title: Webhook secret compared with !== instead of a constant-time comparison
body: The shared webhook secret is checked with plain string inequality, which short-circuits at the first differing byte and leaks timing information. For an authentication check on a network endpoint, compare with crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers (for example, hash both values first).

title: Invalid payloads and undecryptable keys surface as unhandled 500s
body: appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throws a ZodError on malformed input (line 31). symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse (lines 57-59) throw on a wrong key or non-JSON plaintext. None are caught, so the caller gets a 500 with a stack trace in logs instead of a 400, and a self-hoster's retry logic will treat client errors as server failures. Use safeParse and wrap decryption and parsing, returning 400.

title: Concurrent deliveries can create duplicate credentials for the same user and app
body: The handler does findFirst (line 62) then create (line 83) with no transaction or lock. Two deliveries for the same user and app can both see no row and both create one, unless the schema has a unique constraint on (userId, appId), which this PR does not add. Later lookups that take the first matching credential may then pick a row that is not the one just synced.

title: Sync update leaves a credential flagged invalid even after fresh tokens arrive
body: Refresh failure paths set invalid: true on the credential (for example googlecalendar CalendarService lines 112-118 on invalid_grant, and Webex/Zoom invalidateCredential). The update branch here only writes key (lines 73-80), so after the self-hoster pushes fresh tokens the credential stays flagged invalid and remains unusable in code paths that check the flag. Clear invalid on update.

title: Documented sync response contract is narrower than what the callers read
body: The comment says the endpoint should return only the access token and expiry date, but callers read more. Google reads expiry_date. Hubspot reads expiresIn. Zoom, Webex and Office365 video read expires_in, and Office365 video stores the whole response as the credential key. Lark parses a {code, data} envelope and needs refresh_token and refresh_expires_in. Following the comment gives NaN expiry, or in Office365 video expiry_date = now (line 84), which forces a sync call on every request, and loses refresh tokens. The actual contract (field names, units, envelope) should be documented, for example next to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT in .env.example (line 240, currently undocumented). The PR description also says docs are required, but none are included.

title: No tests for the webhook, the sync refresh path, or the schema helper
body: The PR adds a webhook that writes credentials, a refresh indirection touching about twelve integrations, and a new schema helper, and the PR description says no tests were added. Several defects above (wrapper stored as the key, stripped fields, placeholder refresh token, wrong userId, missing prisma import) would be caught by unit tests of parseRefreshTokenResponse and refreshOAuthTokens with sync on and off, and by webhook tests for auth, validation and create/update.

title: Google token refresh stores the Zod SafeParse wrapper as the credential key
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod safeParse result ({ success, data }), not the parsed data (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts line 29). This line passes that wrapper directly to prisma.credential.update as `key`. With sync disabled (the default), every Google access-token refresh (about hourly) overwrites the stored key with `{ success: true, data: {...} }`, which has no top-level access_token, refresh_token or expiry_date. On the next GoogleCalendarService construction, googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) fails in googleAuth, so Google Calendar breaks for every connected user. Other callers (zoomvideo, office365calendar, salesforce) read `.data` from the same helper, so this call site is inconsistent with them.

title: prisma is used in the Salesforce CalendarService but never imported
body: getClient now calls prisma.credential.update (line 96), but the file's imports (lines 1-20) do not include prisma from @calcom/prisma. This fails type-checking ('Cannot find name prisma') and throws a ReferenceError on every Salesforce connection, so the Salesforce calendar integration cannot be constructed.

title: Zoho Bigin passes the credential id where refreshOAuthTokens expects the user id
body: refreshAccessToken receives `credentialId` (the Cal.com credential primary key) and passes it as the third `userId` argument to refreshOAuthTokens. Every other provider passes credential.userId. With CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT enabled, the self-hoster endpoint is asked to refresh tokens for calcomUserId equal to a credential id, which is a different user. The returned tokens are then written into this user's credential, mixing accounts. The fix is to pass the user id (credential.userId) and keep the credential id only for the DB update.

title: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response that callers treat as provider data
body: In the sync branch the helper returns the fetch Response without reading the body or checking response.ok. The non-sync branch returns a provider SDK or axios result, and callers read it with .data, .expiresIn or .data.error. With sync enabled these reads break: googlecalendar CalendarService.ts line 94 reads res?.data (undefined), so the TypeError is swallowed by the catch and Google tokens are never refreshed; hubspot CalendarService.ts line 192 derives expiryDate from expiresIn (undefined, giving NaN); zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts line 96 reads tokenInfo.data.error, which throws a TypeError that is not caught; zohocrm CalendarService.ts reads zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error inside a try that silently logs. The helper should parse the body, check status, and return the same shape as the non-sync branch.

title: In sync mode the HubSpot refresh writes a fetch Response object into the credential key
body: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, so hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn is undefined and expiryDate (line 192) becomes NaN. Line 198 then persists that Response object as the credential key. A Response has no token fields, so the stored key ends up with no access or refresh token (at most an expiryDate of null). If Prisma rejects the object instead, the refresh fails silently in the catch. Either way the HubSpot connection is never refreshed and its stored tokens are lost. The sync body must be parsed to JSON and the expiry derived before anything is persisted.

title: A missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string 'refresh_token' and persisted
body: When the validated response has no refresh_token, this assigns the literal string 'refresh_token' and returns it as valid data. Callers persist it: office365calendar merges tokenResponse.data over the stored credential and zoomvideo sets key.refresh_token from it. In sync mode this always happens, because minimumTokenResponseSchema (lines 5-11) strips every field except access_token, so the real stored refresh token is overwritten with the placeholder. A later refresh (after sync is disabled, or for a provider that omits refresh_token) then fails with invalid_grant. The fallback should keep the existing refresh token rather than invent one.

title: Schema selection here does not match the sync condition used in refreshOAuthTokens
body: The minimal schema is selected when only the env vars are set. refreshOAuthTokens also requires a userId before calling the sync endpoint. So for team-owned credentials (userId null) on a sync-enabled instance, the provider's direct refresh response is validated with the minimal schema, which strips expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token and instance_url. Google and Zoom then persist NaN or placeholder values. The schema choice should use the same condition as the branch that produced the response, or be passed in by the caller.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys collapse to one key, so the expiry requirement is never enforced
body: z.string().toString() returns the default '[object Object]' rather than a meaningful key name. Both computed properties (lines 8 and 10) therefore use the same key, and the second (z.unknown().optional()) overwrites the first. The intended rule 'any numeric property is the expiry' is not enforced, so a sync response containing only access_token passes validation with no expiry. The schema should name the expiry field explicitly (for example expiry_date) and validate it as a number.

title: Zoom sync-mode refresh computes expiry_date from a field the minimal schema strips
body: In sync mode parseRefreshTokenResponse validates with minimumTokenResponseSchema, which keeps only access_token, so expires_in is removed. newTokens.expires_in is therefore undefined, expiry_date becomes NaN, and it is persisted (serialized as null). The next getToken calls zoomTokenSchema.parse, which requires expiry_date to be a number, so the credential fails to parse and Zoom calls reject with 'Zoom credential keys parsing error' until the user reconnects.

title: Zoom refresh sends appSlug 'zoomvideo' but the credential is stored under appId 'zoom'
body: The Zoom callback creates credentials with appId 'zoom' (zoomvideo/api/callback.ts) and the installed-app path also uses slug 'zoom'. The sync request here sends appSlug 'zoomvideo', the directory name. A self-hoster's app store keyed by the Cal.com app slug will not find the app, or will find the wrong one, so Zoom sync refresh fails or returns the wrong credentials. The slug should match the stored appId.

title: Webex sync response is validated against the full Webex schema, bypassing parseRefreshTokenResponse
body: Zoom and Google route refreshed tokens through parseRefreshTokenResponse so the sync endpoint only needs to return an access token and expiry. Webex does not. This line validates against webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires an exact scope literal, token_type, refresh_token and refresh_token_expires_in. A sync endpoint following the documented contract (access token plus expiry) is always rejected with 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'. Also, expiry_date is only updated when expires_in is present (lines 103-105), so an endpoint that returns only an expiry never updates it. Webex should use the same helper as Zoom.

title: Salesforce now refreshes its token on every client construction and bypasses the sync endpoint
body: getClient runs from the constructor (line 57) and now always POSTs to login.salesforce.com and writes the credential row, even when the stored token is still valid. Every availability check, booking or list call that creates a service instance pays a network round trip and a DB write, and concurrent instances race on the same refresh token. Because this bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, Salesforce still calls Salesforce directly in sync mode, which defeats the PR's purpose. The statusText !== 'OK' check on line 86 is also unreliable (HTTP/2 responses have an empty statusText) and should check response.ok. Finally, the minimal schema applied to this direct response strips instance_url, so the stored key loses it when sync is enabled.

title: Webhook credential update does not clear the invalid flag
body: When a provider returns invalid_grant, the code sets credential.invalid = true (googlecalendar, webex, zoom and invalidateCredential). This handler replaces the key with freshly synced tokens but never resets invalid. A credential flagged invalid therefore stays invalid after the self-hoster pushes working tokens, and any code path that skips invalid credentials keeps skipping it. The update should also set invalid to false.

title: findFirst-then-create lets concurrent webhook deliveries insert duplicate credentials
body: The lookup (lines 62-70) and the create (line 83) are separate statements with no transaction or unique constraint covering (userId, appId). Two deliveries for the same user and app, such as a self-hoster retry, can both see no row and both insert. Later reads use findFirst and pick one row arbitrarily, so the app may keep using a stale token. The comment about upsert does not address this race. Wrap the lookup and write in a transaction, or enforce uniqueness at the database level.

title: Malformed payloads and decryption failures escape as unhandled exceptions
body: appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) throws a ZodError on a bad body, and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) (lines 57-59) throws on a wrong key or non-JSON plaintext. Neither is caught, so the caller gets an unstructured 500 rather than a 400 with a stable message. Use safeParse for a 400 response and wrap decryption and parsing in a try/catch.

title: Webhook secret is compared with !== instead of a constant-time comparison
body: The shared secret is compared with the !== operator, which short-circuits on the first mismatched character and can leak timing information about the secret. The route is the only authentication on an endpoint that writes decrypted third-party credentials, so use crypto.timingSafeEqual (hashing both sides first so lengths match).

title: Refresh replaces the whole credential key with the raw refresh response
body: The stored key is overwritten with responseBody. In sync mode that response is the self-hoster's minimal payload (access token and expiry, per the comment in refreshOAuthTokens), so refresh_token and other stored fields are dropped from the credential. A later non-sync refresh then has no refresh token to use. The new fields should be merged into the existing key, as the Zoom and Google paths do.

title: isTokenValid is inverted, so expired tokens are never refreshed and valid ones always are
body: isTokenValid returns true when token.expiryDate < Date.now(), meaning the token is expired. getToken then does isTokenValid(...) ? resolve() : refreshAccessToken(...), so an expired token skips refresh and the stale access token is used, while a still-valid token triggers a refresh on every call. This is the path the PR wraps in refreshOAuthTokens. Also, line 219 stores expiryDate as Date.now() + 60 * 60, which is 3.6 seconds in milliseconds, so the stored expiry is wrong as well. The pre-existing defect is in code this PR modifies and should be fixed alongside it.

title: Sync request carries no authentication and its response is not status-checked
body: The outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug, with no shared secret or signature, so the endpoint cannot verify that the request came from this instance. The reply is then trusted to overwrite stored tokens. There is no timeout and no response.ok check, so an error page or a stalled endpoint is handled as a token response. The inbound webhook already uses a shared secret, so the outbound call should send one too, with a timeout and a status check.

title: New credential sync and refresh paths are shipped without tests
body: The PR checklist states that no tests were added. The new endpoint (secret check, decryption, create/update logic) and the shared helpers (refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse) have no unit tests. Defects in this PR, including the SafeParse wrapper stored as a key, a Response treated as token data, the placeholder refresh token, and the zoho-bigin user id mix-up, are the kind that tests of the helpers' return values and the sync branch would catch. At minimum add tests for refreshOAuthTokens in both modes and for parseRefreshTokenResponse's return shape.

title: Team admin check requires owner role too (&& instead of ||)
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, so only a user who is both admin and owner passes. Plain team admins are rejected with FORBIDDEN, even though the variable name says admin-or-owner and the UI shows the 'additional guests' action for any booking in the list. The operator should be `||`.

title: Guest blacklist is bypassed by uppercase email addresses
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased when built (line 71), but the incoming `guest` is compared as-is with `includes(guest)`. An input such as `Spammer@Blocked.example` is not matched against a blacklisted `spammer@blocked.example`. The guest is then inserted as an attendee and receives an invitation sent in the organizer's name. The guest should be lowercased before the comparison.

title: Duplicate guests in one request are not rejected server-side
body: The `uniqueGuests` filter only removes emails that already match an existing attendee, using a case-sensitive comparison. It does not dedupe within `guests`. The uniqueness refinement exists only in the client dialog, and the zod schema does not enforce it. A direct API call with `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` or `["A@x.com","a@x.com"]` creates duplicate attendee rows via `createMany` and sends duplicate invitations.

title: Attendees are committed before the calendar update, which is not guarded
body: The attendees are written to the DB at lines 92-106, then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs with no try/catch. If the calendar call throws, the new attendees stay in the database, the calendar is not updated, no emails are sent, and the user sees an error. A retry is then rejected at lines 80-81 because those emails now match existing attendees, so the calendar invite can never be sent through this flow. The DB write and the calendar update need to be ordered, compensated, or made transactional.

title: Raw `guests` input passed to email sender instead of the filtered list
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the original request list, not `uniqueGuests`. Any address in the request that is already an attendee (or blacklisted) matches `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in `sendAddGuestsEmails`. That attendee then receives a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` invitation as if newly added, instead of the 'guests added' email. Passing `uniqueGuests` fixes this.

title: Email failure is swallowed without logging the error
body: The catch block discards `err` and writes a fixed `console.log` string. The error is lost, and the mutation still returns success, so a failed email send is hard to diagnose. The error should be logged with the logger, including `err`.

title: No cap on number of guests; any attendee is authorized
body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()`. Each guest triggers a DB insert, a calendar update, and an invitation email with an ICS attachment sent in the organizer's name. The handler also allows any user whose email matches an existing attendee (addGuests.handler.ts lines 52-54) to do this. A single attendee could send unlimited invitations to arbitrary addresses through the platform's mail infrastructure. A reasonable limit on the array size is needed.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails settings
body: Every other send function in this file checks `hostEmailDisabled` / `attendeeEmailDisabled` or `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` before sending. `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends unconditionally to the organizer, team members, and attendees. It takes no metadata parameter, and the handler does not pass one. Event types where the organizer disabled standard emails will still receive 'guests added' emails.

title: Misleading error when all guests are already attendees or blacklisted
body: When every submitted email is already an attendee or is blacklisted, the handler throws `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which reads as 'Emails must be unique and valid'. A valid address that is already on the booking therefore gets an error suggesting the input is malformed. A specific message such as 'guests already added' would be accurate.

title: Check-then-insert race can create duplicate attendees
body: The existing-attendee check reads `booking.attendees` at lines 26-42, then `createMany` runs at lines 92-106 with no transaction and no uniqueness constraint on (booking, email). Two concurrent requests (double submit or two tabs) can both pass the filter and insert the same guest twice, producing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails.

title: Error toast shows raw tRPC code and the fallback is unreachable
body: The message is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, so users see text like 'BAD_REQUEST: Emails must be unique and valid'. Because the template always contains ': ', `message` is never falsy, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is dead code. The toast should show the translated message, with the fallback applied explicitly when there is no message.

title: isInvalidEmail error persists after closing or succeeding
body: `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is set on validation failure but only reset by the Cancel button (line 91). It is not reset in `onSuccess` (line 39) or when the dialog is dismissed via the X or Escape. The stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' message appears the next time the dialog opens, even though the input was cleared.

title: Hardcoded English tooltip text bypasses i18n
body: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` is a literal English string, while the rest of the component uses `t()`. Users in other locales see English text for this control, and the string is not in the locale files.

title: No tests for the new permission, dedupe, blacklist, or email-routing logic
body: The handler contains authorization branching, the guest filtering and blacklist logic, and the calendar and email side effects, but no tests are added. The AND-vs-OR permission bug, the blacklist case bypass, and the wrong email list passed to the sender would all be caught by unit tests. The dialog and the email templates are also untested.

title: Team admin/owner permission check uses AND instead of OR
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, so a caller must be both admin and owner. A team admin who is not the owner fails the check and gets FORBIDDEN, even though the UI shows the 'additional guests' action to them. The intended check is an OR of the two conditions.

title: Guest blacklist comparison is case-sensitive on the guest side
body: The blacklist entries are lowercased on line 71, but the incoming `guest` is compared as typed (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Submitting `Spam@Example.com` bypasses a blacklist entry `spam@example.com`, which defeats the abuse control the env var exists for.

title: Guests array has no size limit; any attendee can mass-mail arbitrary addresses
body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no max length and no per-user rate limit. Each new guest receives a calendar invite and an email containing booking details, and the handler also sends an email to every existing attendee. Any authenticated user who is merely an attendee (the handler allows `isAttendee`) can send a single request with thousands of addresses to third parties through the platform's mail infrastructure, with no cap.

title: Duplicate guests in one request, or case-variant duplicates, create duplicate attendee rows
body: The filter on lines 74-78 only removes guests already present in `booking.attendees` (exact, case-sensitive match). It does not dedupe within `guests` itself, and the server schema does not enforce uniqueness, so the same email sent twice passes and both copies go into `createMany` on line 102. Case variants such as `Bob@x.com` and `bob@x.com` are also both inserted. The result is duplicate attendee rows and duplicate invites. The uniqueness rule is enforced only in the client dialog.

title: Guests are persisted before calendar sync, and calendar failure is unhandled
body: The attendees are written to the DB at lines 92-106. `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` at line 165 is not wrapped in try/catch, unlike the email call. If the calendar update throws, the request fails after the guests were saved, and no invites are sent. A retry then hits the dedupe check on lines 74-81 and returns BAD_REQUEST, so the user cannot recover without manual DB cleanup. The writes should be ordered or wrapped so that a calendar failure does not leave persisted guests with no invite.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` returns the calling user's credentials, and the `EventManager` is built from them. When a team admin or an attendee (not the organizer) adds guests, the calendar event belongs to the organizer's connected calendar, so `updateCalendarAttendees` runs against the wrong account's credentials and either fails or does not update the organizer's event. The organizer's credentials are loaded on line 38 (`booking.user.credentials`) but never used.

title: No check on booking status or time; guests can be added to cancelled or past bookings
body: After the booking is loaded, the handler only checks existence and permissions. It never checks whether the booking is cancelled or rejected, or whether it has ended. A direct API call can add attendees and send calendar invites for a cancelled booking, which effectively reactivates it on the guest's calendar. The UI hides this action for cancelled bookings, but the server does not enforce it.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores eventType disableStandardEmails metadata
body: Every other send function in this file gates host and attendee emails on `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and always sends to organizers, team members, and attendees. The handler also does not pass the event type metadata. Organizers who disabled standard emails for this event type will still receive add-guest emails.

title: Existing attendees who were re-submitted get the new-booking email
body: The handler passes the raw `guests` input (line 168 of addGuests.handler.ts) instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`. Here, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` therefore matches existing attendees who were in the request, and they receive a full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the 'guests added' notice. The function should receive only the newly created guests.

title: Email failure is logged with console.log and the error object is dropped
body: The catch block logs the constant string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' and discards `err`, so the failure cause is unrecoverable from logs. It should use the project logger and include the error. Swallowing the error is intentional, but the diagnostic detail should not be lost.

title: Misleading error when all guests are already attendees or blacklisted
body: When every submitted guest is already an attendee or on the blacklist, the handler throws BAD_REQUEST with message 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' ('Emails must be unique and valid'). That message does not explain the real cause. Blacklisted addresses are dropped silently, and the user is told their emails are invalid even when they are valid and simply already present.

title: Error toast shows raw error code, and the fallback is dead code
body: `message` is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, which always yields a non-empty string, so `message || t('unable_to_add_guests')` on line 44 never uses the fallback. The user sees raw tRPC codes such as 'FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission'. If `err.data` is missing, the toast starts with 'undefined:'. The toast should show the translated message, with the fallback used when it is absent.

title: Validation error flag is never cleared, so it persists after the user fixes input
body: `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is called on validation failure, but it is only reset by the Cancel button. After a successful add, or after the dialog is closed via the overlay or X button, the 'Emails must be unique and valid' message is still shown the next time the dialog opens. The flag should be cleared on success and on open/close.

title: Hardcoded English tooltip text is not translated
body: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` is a hardcoded English string in a shared UI component that elsewhere uses `t(...)` for all user-facing text (for example the 'Add another' button). Non-English users see English here, so it should use a translation key added to common.json.

title: No tests for a new permission-gated mutation with dedupe and email logic
body: The PR adds a mutation with authorization rules (organizer, team admin/owner, attendee), blacklist and duplicate filtering, calendar sync, and email fan-out, but no unit or integration tests. The permission `&&` bug and the duplicate-insertion problem would likely be caught by even basic tests of the handler's branches.

title: Team admin permission check requires being both admin and owner
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Because owners are also admins, this reduces to 'is owner', so regular team ADMIN members are rejected with FORBIDDEN even though the variable name and intent are 'admin or owner'. The operator should be `||`. Team admins see these bookings in the list and get a permission error when they try the action.

title: Notification uses raw request guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the original request list, while the DB insert uses `uniqueGuests` (existing attendees and blacklisted emails removed). In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, any attendee whose email is in `newGuests` gets the full AttendeeScheduledEmail (booking confirmation) instead of the add-guests notice. So an email the user re-submits that is already an attendee receives a confirmation it should not get. The function should receive `uniqueGuests`.

title: Duplicate guests are not rejected on the server, and existing-attendee match is case-sensitive
body: The filter compares `guest === attendee.email` exactly, so 'A@x.com' is not treated as a duplicate of 'a@x.com'. Nothing dedupes entries inside the `guests` array itself, so a request with the same address twice (or two case variants) creates two Attendee rows via `createMany`. The uniqueness check exists only in the client dialog (the zod refine in AddGuestsDialog), and the server schema (addGuests.schema.ts) does not enforce it. Duplicate attendees then get duplicate invitations and emails.

title: Guest blacklist is bypassed by changing the case of the email
body: `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` entries are lowercased when parsed, but the incoming `guest` is compared as-is with `includes(guest)`. An address such as 'Blocked@Example.com' passes when the list contains 'blocked@example.com', and the guest is then stored and invited. Guests should be normalized (lowercased and trimmed) before both the blacklist and duplicate checks.

title: Calendar update runs with the caller's credentials, not the organizer's
body: The EventManager is built from `ctx.user` and that user's credentials. But `booking.references` and the destination calendar belong to the organizer (`booking.userId`). When the caller is a team admin or a matching attendee rather than the organizer, `updateCalendarAttendees` uses the caller's calendars against the organizer's calendar event, so the new guests are not added to the organizer's calendar or the update fails. The handler already loads `booking.user` with `credentials: true` (line 38) and never uses it.

title: Guests are committed to the DB before the calendar update, with no rollback
body: The attendees are written at line 92, then `updateCalendarAttendees` runs at line 165 outside any transaction. If the calendar call throws, the new attendee rows stay in the database, the mutation returns an error, and the notification emails at line 168 are never sent. On retry, the same guests now match existing attendees and the request fails with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', so the state cannot be repaired from the UI. The calendar update and notifications need to be ordered or wrapped so a failure does not leave partial state.

title: Email failure is swallowed with a plain console.log and the error object is dropped
body: The catch block logs a fixed string with `console.log` and ignores `err`. The cause of a failed notification is lost, and the mutation still reports 'Guests added'. The error should be logged with the project logger and the error object included.

title: No booking status or time check; guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings
body: After loading the booking, the handler checks only permissions. It does not reject cancelled or rejected bookings, or bookings that have already ended. The UI only offers the action for confirmed upcoming bookings, but the API accepts any booking id. A request for a cancelled booking still writes attendees, updates the calendar event, and sends 'guests added' emails for an event that is no longer happening.

title: Unbounded guest list enables email spam to all attendees and the organizer
body: `guests` has no max length, and no rate limit applies. Every successful call sends an email to every existing attendee and the organizer (and team members). Any user who passes the permission check can add an arbitrary number of guests in one call and repeat the call, causing mass invitations sent from the platform. The handler's attendee branch (line 52 of addGuests.handler.ts) also lets any booking attendee, not only the organizer or an admin, trigger this. A maximum array size and a per-booking attendee cap should be enforced.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type disableStandardEmails settings
body: Every other send function in this file takes `eventTypeMetadata` and checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and always emails the organizer, team members, and attendees. Event types that disable standard emails will still send 'guests added' emails. The handler also does not pass the event type metadata.

title: New guest records are assigned the organizer's timezone and locale
body: Each new attendee is stored with `timeZone: organizer.timeZone` and `locale: organizer.locale`. The guest's real timezone and locale are unknown, but these values are persisted as if they were the guest's, and later drive how that guest's emails and calendar invites are rendered. Storing a neutral default or leaving the value unset would be more accurate.

title: Error message is misleading when guests are filtered out as existing or blacklisted
body: When every submitted guest is already an attendee or is blacklisted, the handler throws 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' ('Emails must be unique and valid'). That text describes a format or duplicate-input error, not 'these addresses are already on the booking' or 'these addresses are blocked'. Blacklisted entries that are mixed with valid ones are dropped silently with no indication to the caller.

title: No tests for addGuests authorization, filtering, or notification logic
body: The new handler has a non-trivial permission matrix (organizer, team admin/owner, attendee), a filtering step (existing attendees, blacklist, duplicates), and a calendar and email side effect. None of it is covered by a test in this PR. The inverted admin/owner condition noted above is the kind of bug a basic handler test would catch.

title: Fallback error message is unreachable and the error text includes the raw error code
body: `message` is a template string that always contains a non-empty `${err.data?.code}: ...` prefix, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never falls back. The user also sees raw codes such as 'FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission' or 'BAD_REQUEST: ...'. The fallback should be applied to the translated message, not to the concatenation.

title: Dialog state persists across open/close, so a stale validation error and old entries reappear
body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on a failed client validation, but `onSuccess` never resets it. Closing the dialog through Escape or the overlay (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`) also skips the reset in the Cancel button, so the old emails and the error message remain. When the dialog is reopened, the user sees the stale error and previously entered addresses, which can then trigger the duplicate error on a retry.

title: Hardcoded English tooltip string bypasses i18n
body: The remove-email tooltip uses the literal string "Remove email" instead of `t(...)`, so it is not translated, even though this component already uses `t` for its other labels.

title: Unguarded DB update in catch can abort the whole batch
