body: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the catch block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. Before this PR the catch only logged, so nothing could escape the `for` loop. Now, if this update throws (for example a Prisma P2025 because the reminder was deleted between the fetch and the update, such as by a booking cancellation, or a transient DB error), the exception propagates out of the loop. Every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped for this run and the handler fails instead of finishing. The success-path updates at lines 169 and 179 can throw into this same catch, so the risk is not limited to the new code path.

title: retryCount is incremented with a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` uses the value read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap (each SMS scheduling call is a network round trip, so a run can exceed the schedule interval), both read 0 and both write 1, losing an increment. Reminders then get more attempts than intended before the give-up delete triggers. Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` avoids this. The same pattern is repeated at line 195.

title: Give-up delete clause is not scoped to SMS or unscheduled reminders
body: The `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` branch of the deleteMany OR has no `method` or `scheduled` filter, so it deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP rows and rows that are already scheduled. Today only the SMS path increments retryCount, so this is latent, but the intent described in the PR is SMS-only give-up. Scoping the branch with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and `scheduled: false` would make the delete match that intent and not depend on an invariant elsewhere in the codebase.

title: OR with an unindexed retryCount predicate forces a full table scan each run
body: The deleteMany now runs `OR [method/scheduledDate condition, retryCount > 1]`. The schema has no index on retryCount, and Postgres cannot use the existing (method, scheduled, scheduledDate) index for an OR when one branch is unindexed, so every cron invocation scans the whole WorkflowReminder table. That table grows with every booking step, and this runs on a frequent cron. Either add an index on retryCount or issue the two conditions as separate deletes.

title: Reminders with no message or no sendTo are never counted as failures
body: If `message` is empty or `sendTo` is missing, neither the success branch nor the new else/catch increments retryCount runs. Those reminders stay unscheduled and are re-fetched and skipped on every cron run until scheduledDate passes, never reaching the give-up threshold. The `continue` at lines 68-70 for a missing workflowStep or booking has the same effect. This is a failure to send that the PR's retry-then-delete logic is meant to cover but does not.

title: No tests for the retry and give-up behavior
body: The PR changes the cron's retry semantics (increment on failure, increment on catch, delete when retryCount > 1) but adds no test. Nothing verifies that a failed Twilio schedule increments the counter, that a second failure leads to deletion on the next run, or that the catch path behaves correctly. The regression described in the catch-block finding would also go unnoticed without a test.

title: Generated kysely and zod artifacts were not regenerated (if committed)
body: The schema declares generators for prisma-kysely (output `../kysely`) and zod-prisma (output `./zod`). Adding a column to WorkflowReminder normally requires regenerating those artifacts. The PR does not touch them. If they are checked into the repo, their WorkflowReminder types will lack retryCount and will drift from the database. Please confirm whether these are committed and regenerate them if so.

title: Unscoped deleteMany hard-deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1
body: The new OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` or `scheduled: false` filter. It hard-deletes any WorkflowReminder row with retryCount above 1, whatever its channel (EMAIL/WHATSAPP) and whether it is already scheduled. Only the SMS path writes retryCount today, so the immediate impact is small, but the predicate is broader than the feature described and will silently delete rows for any future channel that uses the counter. There is also an edge case: if Twilio accepts a message but the follow-up update to scheduled:true throws, the row stays scheduled:false, its retryCount can reach 2, and it gets deleted while the Twilio message is still pending. Cancellation via referenceId can then no longer find it. The clause should be scoped to `method: SMS, scheduled: false`.

title: Transient provider errors permanently drop reminders after two attempts
body: Every failure consumes the retry budget equally: a falsy return from twilio.scheduleSMS (lines 178-186) and any exception (lines 189-199). The code does not distinguish permanent errors (e.g. invalid phone number) from transient ones (Twilio outage, rate limiting, network timeout). Two failures in consecutive cron runs cause the deleteMany at line 38 to remove the reminder permanently. The deletion is not logged and the user is not told. A brief provider blip is enough to lose reminders for every booking in the window. Consider backing off, counting only permanent error types, or at least logging each deletion.

title: Unguarded update inside catch can abort the whole batch
body: The catch block now performs a prisma.workflowReminder.update (retryCount) with no try/catch. If that update throws, the exception escapes the for-loop, so the remaining unscheduled reminders in this run are skipped and the handler rejects. One concrete trigger: a reminder deleted between the findMany and this point (for example by a booking cancellation or a concurrent cron run) makes Prisma throw P2025, and that is not handled. A transient DB error has the same effect. Before this PR the catch block only logged, so this is a new failure mode. Guard the update, or make per-reminder error handling non-throwing.

title: retryCount incremented from a stale read instead of atomically
body: The new value is computed as `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value fetched at line 48, not read from the database at write time. If two cron invocations overlap, or the row changes between read and write, increments are lost (both read 0 and both write 1), so the retry limit can be exceeded. The same pattern appears at line 184. Prisma's `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` performs the increment atomically in the database.

title: Empty message or missing recipient is never counted as a failed attempt
body: The retry increments only happen inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)`. When the message resolves to empty, or the recipient is null (an SMS_NUMBER step with no sendTo, or a booking with no smsReminderNumber), nothing is scheduled and retryCount is not incremented. Such a reminder is re-attempted on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes. That unbounded retry is the behaviour this PR is meant to stop, so these cases should count as failures too.

title: Comment no longer describes what the deleteMany does
body: The comment says it deletes scheduled SMS reminders whose date has passed. The query now also deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, regardless of method or date, and it deletes unscheduled rows too. The comment is misleading for anyone maintaining the cleanup logic. It should describe both conditions.

title: No tests for the new retry and deletion behaviour
body: The PR changes deletion semantics and adds retry bookkeeping in three places (the failed-schedule branch, the catch block, and the deleteMany), but adds no tests. Coverage should include: a failed schedule increments retryCount; a reminder with retryCount 2 is deleted on the next run; a successful schedule does not increment retryCount; and the deletion is scoped correctly. Without tests, the off-by-one around `gt: 1` and the scoping problems above are easy to get wrong.

title: Generated Prisma-derived artifacts may not be regenerated
body: Adding a column to WorkflowReminder changes what the generators in this schema emit (the kysely generator writes to ../kysely/types.ts and the zod generator writes to ./zod). The PR touches only schema.prisma and the migration. If those generated files are committed in this repository, they are now stale: typed queries will lack retryCount, and any drift check in CI will fail. Confirm whether the generated outputs need to be regenerated and included.

title: Unguarded DB update inside catch can abort the whole batch
body: The new `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` in the catch block has no try/catch, and it is not inside any outer try. Before this PR the catch only logged, so it could not throw. Now, if this update fails, the exception escapes the `for` loop and the handler rejects. The most plausible trigger is a reminder deleted after `findMany` (for example when its booking is cancelled, which makes Prisma throw P2025), or any transient DB error. The consequence is that every remaining reminder in the batch is skipped for this cron run and the response is an error instead of the normal success response. The increment should be guarded so one bad row does not stop processing of the rest.

title: retryCount delete branch is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The second branch of the `OR` (`retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, unlike the first branch. Any WorkflowReminder of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, or a future channel) with retryCount > 1 is deleted, regardless of its `scheduled` state. Only the SMS path increments the column today, so the practical impact is currently small, but the delete condition is broader than the stated intent and will cause data loss once another channel uses the column. The branch should be scoped as `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` plus `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`.

title: Comment describes only the date-based deletion
body: The comment says this block deletes 'all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date'. After this PR the same `deleteMany` also deletes reminders whose retryCount is greater than 1, including unscheduled ones that failed twice. The comment is now wrong and does not explain the retry threshold either.

title: Reminders with no sendTo or empty message never accrue retries
body: The retry increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)` (the else branch at line 178 and the catch block). If `sendTo` is null (for example an SMS_ATTENDEE step where `booking.smsReminderNumber` is missing) or the message is empty, nothing is scheduled and retryCount is not incremented. Such a reminder stays unscheduled and is reprocessed on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes, with the template/DB work repeated each time. This is the 'keep retrying until the date is reached' behavior the PR is meant to stop, and the PR leaves this path uncovered. Either count these as failed attempts or delete them explicitly.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of retryCount
body: The counter is written as `reminder.retryCount + 1`, using the value read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap (the job makes many external calls and can run long), both can read the same value and write the same increment, so failures are under-counted and a reminder gets an extra attempt. Prisma's `{ increment: 1 }` performs the increment atomically in the database and avoids this. The same pattern appears in the catch block at line 195.

title: OR with an unindexed retryCount predicate forces a full table scan
body: The new `OR` in deleteMany combines a predicate that uses the composite index `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` with `retryCount > 1`, which has no index (schema.prisma line 1000 adds the column without one). Postgres can only use a BitmapOr when every arm is indexable, so this cron query now falls back to a sequential scan of WorkflowReminder on every run. That table grows over time, so the cost increases with it. Consider an index on `retryCount` or splitting the delete into two queries.

title: Retry budget of two attempts is spent within a few cron ticks with no backoff
body: Each cron tick makes one attempt, and the row is deleted on the first tick after the second failure. Two failures can therefore occur only minutes apart, and a Twilio or network outage longer than that permanently drops the reminder with no log beyond a console line and no alert. The magic `gt: 1` also does not state the 'two failures' rule anywhere in code. The threshold or the lack of backoff should be a deliberate, documented choice.

title: No tests for the new retry and deletion behavior
body: The PR changes control flow in three places: failed scheduling increments retryCount, errors increment retryCount, and reminders with retryCount > 1 are deleted. None of this is covered by a test in the diff. A test that drives the handler with a mocked twilio.scheduleSMS returning null or throwing, and checks the retryCount updates and the deletion on the next run, would catch regressions such as the catch-block issue above.

title: Public findMany removed and condition getters now return raw Prisma.Sql
body: The diff deletes the public `findMany` method, which executed the query and returned rows, and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a SQL fragment. `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` also change their return type from Prisma where-input objects to `Prisma.Sql`. The PR changes no file other than this service and its test, so any existing caller of `findMany` or consumer of the old where-input shape will fail type-checking or break at runtime. Callers must now write their own `$queryRaw` and embed the fragment. The PR description frames the change as a test-only update and never mentions removing the public method or changing these return types.

title: Caching tests deleted without mention
body: The entire `describe("Caching")` block, with the tests 'should cache authorization conditions' and 'should cache filter conditions', was removed. The service still memoizes results in `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, so the repeat-call behaviour these tests covered now has no test. The PR description does not mention removing them.

title: Generated SQL is executed against the database only for user scope
body: The new assertions compare hand-written `Prisma.sql` templates by their strings and values. That checks the builder's text against the author's copy of it, not whether the SQL is valid against the `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` view. Only the single `$queryRaw` test runs generated SQL, and it covers only the user scope with one eventTypeId filter. The org-scope and team-scope conditions (`= ANY($n)` array parameters and nested OR/AND groups), the memberUserId filter, and the combined filter path are never executed. A wrong column name or an array-parameter type mismatch would pass these tests. The PR also states the tests were not run.

title: Org-scope expectations depend on unordered query results
body: The expected `teamId = ANY(...)` and `userId = ANY(...)` arrays are asserted in a fixed order, `[org, team, team2, team3]` and `[user, user2, user3]`. The service builds these from `teamRepo.findAllByParentId` and `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`, and neither query has an `orderBy`. Postgres does not guarantee row order without ORDER BY, and the shared test database has rows deleted by earlier tests, so the order can change. Because `toEqual` compares the `values` array in sequence, the test can fail intermittently. Sorting both sides or comparing as sets would make it deterministic.

title: Public findMany() removed and return types changed without updating callers
body: The PR deletes `InsightsBookingService.findMany`, the only method in this class that executed a query, and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a bare `Prisma.Sql` fragment. `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` also change from Prisma where-input objects to `Prisma.Sql`. Only two files are changed in this PR, so any other code in the repo that calls `findMany` or consumes the old where-input shape will fail to compile or behave differently. The description presents this as a test-only update to an already-converted service, so reviewers are not told about this breaking API change. Confirm there are no remaining callers, or update them in this PR.

title: Org/team authorization fragments are top-level ORs without parentheses, unsafe to compose with AND
body: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` reduces to `(A) OR (B)` with no outer parentheses (the team variant does the same at line 206), and `getAuthorizationConditions()` returns that string as-is. A caller that embeds the result in a larger predicate, such as `WHERE ${await service.getAuthorizationConditions()} AND "status" = 'ACCEPTED'`, is parsed as `(A) OR ((B) AND status)`, so every row matching A bypasses the caller's extra constraint. `getBaseConditions()` hides this today only because it wraps the result when a filter is present, and returns the bare OR when no filter is set. The integration tests at lines 296 and 333 of the test file assert the unwrapped text, which locks this shape in. The fragments should be wrapped in parentheses where they are built.

title: Caching tests deleted while the memoization logic remains in the service
body: The whole `describe("Caching")` block ("should cache authorization conditions" and "should cache filter conditions") is removed. The service still memoizes through `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, and this PR changes those cached types to `Prisma.sql`. Nothing in the PR explains the deletion, and no replacement test exists, so a regression in memoization (recomputing every call, or returning stale values) would not be caught.

title: New empty-membership branch in team scope has no test coverage
body: `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` now appends the user-membership branch only when `userIdsFromTeam.length > 0`. This replaces the earlier `userId: {in: []}` behavior with new control flow. No test covers a team with zero memberships, so the `false` branch and the resulting SQL (team-only condition, no trailing OR) are unverified. The same applies to the `userIdsFromOrg.length > 0` branch in the org scope when an org has no sub-teams.

title: getBaseConditions returns unparenthesized SQL that breaks precedence when composed
body: In two of the four branches, getBaseConditions returns authConditions or filterConditions as-is, without wrapping them in parentheses. Org and team auth conditions are top-level `(A) OR (B)` expressions, and the eventTypeId filter is also a top-level OR. Only the combined branch on line 73 wraps its parts. A caller that embeds this result next to other predicates, for example `WHERE ${base} AND status = ...`, gets SQL precedence `A OR (B AND status = ...)`. Rows that the org or team scope should exclude can then be returned. The fix is to wrap the returned fragment in parentheses in every branch so the method always yields one self-contained predicate.

title: Public findMany was removed; scope enforcement is no longer automatic
body: The public `findMany` method was removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a raw SQL fragment. The old method applied the authorization and filter conditions as an AND on every query, so callers could not forget them. Callers now have to write their own `$queryRaw` and interpolate the fragment correctly. Nothing in this diff updates existing callers of `findMany`, so any remaining caller will fail to compile or will silently lose its scope restriction. Either keep a wrapper that always applies the conditions, or update all call sites in this PR.

title: Constructor options type no longer enforces teamId for team scope
body: The constructor's `options` parameter changed from the discriminated-union type `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to the flat `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId` is optional for every scope. Code that passes `scope: 'team'` without `teamId` now type-checks. At runtime safeParse fails, `this.options` becomes null, and the service silently returns NOTHING (`1=0`) with no error. The compile-time check for team scope is lost. The constructor should keep the discriminated-union type.

title: PR description says only tests changed, but the service is rewritten
body: The description says the change only updates the integration tests and that the service was 'previously converted'. The diff rewrites the whole service: it removes findMany, adds getBaseConditions, changes SQL construction for org, team and filter conditions, changes the constructor option type, and changes isOrgOwnerOrAdmin. Reviewers following the description will not look at the service changes, which are the high-risk part. The description should list the service behavior changes.

title: Caching tests were deleted without replacement
body: The `Caching` describe block (cache authorization conditions, cache filter conditions) was removed and not replaced. The memoization in getAuthorizationConditions and getFilterConditions still exists. The filter cache also stores null, which depends on the `=== undefined` check, and nothing covers that path now. The deletion is not mentioned in the PR description. The tests should be restored and adapted to Prisma.sql.

title: Org and team scope SQL is only checked as strings, never executed
body: The org and team scope tests compare the generated SQL template and parameter arrays for equality. Only the user scope is run against BookingTimeStatusDenormalized through $queryRaw. The AND/OR structure of the org and team conditions, which the PR description names as the high-risk part, is never executed. A wrong operator or a missing parenthesis would only show up in a live query. The tests should run org and team scope conditions against the view and assert which bookings are returned, including a booking from another team that must be excluded.

title: Deleting cache does not refresh the cache status shown in the dropdown
body: The dropdown takes cacheUpdatedAt from the viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars query, but the deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess prop. It never invalidates connectedCalendars. After a successful deletion, the 'Cache Status' entry and 'Delete cached data' item keep showing the old timestamp until something else refetches. Some callers do not pass onSuccess at all. The disconnect mutation in the same component invalidates connectedCalendars in onSettled, so the two mutations are inconsistent. Invalidate viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars after the cache delete as well.

title: Cache timestamp is always formatted as en-US, ignoring the user's locale
body: The timestamp is formatted with Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) even though the surrounding label is translated through t() and useLocale() is already in scope. Non-English users see an English date format inside a localized sentence. Format with the user's locale instead.

title: Empty fixed-width actions container is now rendered for cards with no actions
body: The actions prop is now an always-truthy <div className="flex w-32 justify-end"> wrapping CredentialActionsDropdown. CredentialActionsDropdown returns null for delegation-owned credentials when disconnect is not allowed, and for non-Google credentials with no disconnect permission. Before this change, the old conditional expression evaluated to falsy in those cases, so no actions block was rendered. Now every such card reserves an empty 8rem-wide slot, which is a visible layout change. The same applies to the Alert branch at line 123. Only render the wrapper when the dropdown will render, or move the wrapper inside the dropdown.

title: Legacy CalendarCache rows are backfilled with deploy time, so 'Last updated' is wrong
body: Adding the column with DEFAULT NOW() sets updatedAt to the migration time for every existing CalendarCache row. The new status UI reads MAX(updatedAt) per credential and shows it as the last update time. For any cache entry not refreshed since deployment, the displayed time is the deploy time, not the real last write. The upsert sets expiresAt = write time + 30 days, so a better backfill is available: add the column nullable or with a default, then run UPDATE "CalendarCache" SET "updatedAt" = "expiresAt" - interval '30 days' for existing rows, and only then set NOT NULL.

title: Every cache refresh now bumps SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all of the credential's calendars
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now runs an unconditional updateMany on SelectedCalendar for the credential, across all event types, each time the cache is refreshed (webhook, unwatch repopulation, cron). The PR notes say no frontend reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt and that this write may be unnecessary. As written it adds a write per selected calendar on every refresh, and changes the meaning of SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, with no consumer in this change. Remove it unless a real reader is added.

title: Authorization and deletion path for deleteCache has no tests
body: This new mutation has an access check (credential lookup by id AND userId, throwing otherwise) that guards a destructive delete. Nothing in the PR tests that another user's credentialId is rejected or that only the matching calendarCache rows are removed. The new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds repository method and the enrichment in connectedCalendarsHandler are also untested. The PR's checklist confirms only manual verification was done.

title: Comment says CalendarCache has no updatedAt, which this PR now adds
body: The TODO in getCachedAvailability says updatedAt 'doesn't exist yet in CalendarCache table'. This PR adds that column, so the comment is now false and points readers at a non-existent gap. Update or remove it.

title: Script uses BSD-only sed -i '' and a parent-relative .env path
body: sed -i '' is macOS/BSD syntax. On GNU sed (Linux), '' is taken as the script and the GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL update fails. ENV_FILE is also hard-coded to ../.env (line 5), relative to the current directory. Running the script from the repo root writes to a .env outside the repository. The script is also unrelated to the calendar cache feature and is not mentioned in the PR description.

title: Failure paths exit with status 0
body: cleanup() ends with exit 0 unconditionally. It is also called from the rate-limit branch (line 49) and the 'Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL' branch (line 58). Callers and CI cannot tell that the tunnel setup failed. Exit with a non-zero status on the failure paths.

title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx, which is not a declared dependency
body: The change from ts-node to npx tsx is unrelated to the calendar cache feature and is not described in the PR. tsx is not listed in apps/web's dependencies or devDependencies, so npx has to resolve or download it at runtime. That can pick a different version or fail offline. Either declare tsx as a dev dependency or revert this change in this PR.

title: Cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query, so the shown cache status goes stale
body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess prop. It never invalidates trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The disconnect mutation a few lines below does invalidate that query. Since cacheUpdatedAt comes from connectedCalendars, after a successful delete the dropdown keeps showing the old 'Last updated' timestamp and keeps offering 'Delete cached data' unless the parent's onChanged happens to refetch. The PR's test plan explicitly checks that the UI updates after deletion. Invalidate the query in onSuccess or onSettled, as the disconnect path does.

title: Backfilling updatedAt with NOW() makes every legacy cache row report the deploy time as its last update
body: The column is added with DEFAULT NOW(), so every existing CalendarCache row gets updatedAt equal to the migration execution time. The new UI shows 'Last updated: <timestamp>' from this value, so all pre-existing caches will show a fabricated recent timestamp until they are rewritten. There is no real value to backfill from, but the UI should either treat legacy rows as unknown (nullable column or a separate display rule) or the PR should document that the timestamp is not meaningful for them.

title: Migration header warning contradicts the SQL that follows it
body: The header says the required updatedAt column was added 'without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty.' The statement below does add a default (DEFAULT NOW()) precisely so it works on a non-empty table. The comment is misleading for anyone reading the migration history and should be corrected or removed.

title: Cache timestamp is formatted with hardcoded en-US instead of the user's locale
body: Intl.DateTimeFormat is constructed with the fixed locale 'en-US', while the surrounding text is translated through useLocale. Users with other UI languages will see the timestamp in US format next to a localized label. Use the locale from useLocale (or the i18n language) when formatting the date.

title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx, which is unrelated to this feature and relies on an undeclared, unpinned dependency
body: tsx is not listed in apps/web devDependencies (ts-node still is), so 'npx tsx' downloads whatever version the registry serves at run time. That adds network dependence and a non-reproducible toolchain to the dev:cron script. The change has nothing to do with calendar cache management, so it should be separated, or tsx should be added as a pinned devDependency and the behaviour of cron-tester.ts under tsx verified.

title: Every cache refresh now issues an unconditional UPDATE across all SelectedCalendar rows of the credential
body: updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}) runs on every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache call. It touches every selected calendar for the credential, across all event types, to bump updatedAt. The PR notes say nothing in the frontend reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, so this is extra write load on a hot path with no consumer. Either drop it or justify the consumer in code.

title: Unused columns added to the session user query and to UserWithCalendars
body: updatedAt and googleChannelId are added to the selectedCalendars select in findUnlockedUserForSession, which runs on session lookups. Nothing in this diff reads them. The same fields were also made required in the UserWithCalendars type in getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts, so every caller building that type must now supply them, which is an unnecessary type-level break. Remove them unless a concrete consumer is added in this PR.

title: The only authorization guard for cache deletion has no test
body: deleteCacheHandler is the sole check preventing a user from deleting another user's calendar cache: it looks up the credential by id and userId before deleting. No test accompanies the change, and the same is true for getCacheStatusByCredentialIds and the new enrichment in connectedCalendarsHandler. A test for the not-owned and not-found cases is needed before merging.

title: Access-denied case throws a plain Error, which tRPC reports as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
body: When the credential is missing or belongs to another user, the handler throws a generic Error. Through tRPC this becomes an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN, so the client cannot distinguish a bad id from a server fault. Throw a TRPCError with an appropriate code.

title: Actions column is always rendered, leaving blank space for delegated or locked credentials
body: Previously the actions prop was a falsy expression for delegated credentials or when connection modification was disabled, so no actions container was rendered. Now a flex w-32 div is always passed, and CredentialActionsDropdown returns null in those cases. Each card reserves an empty 8rem column where the old UI showed nothing. Pass undefined/false when the dropdown would render nothing, or have the component own its container.

title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only; on Linux the env update silently fails while the script still reports success
body: GNU sed interprets the empty string after -i as the script and then treats the substitution expression as a filename, so the substitution never happens. The script has no set -e or exit check, so it prints 'Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL' regardless. Use a portable approach (e.g. a temp file and mv) and check the result.

title: ENV_FILE is a relative path resolved against the caller's cwd, not the script location
body: ENV_FILE is set to '../.env'. Run from the repo root this writes to the parent directory of the repository, not the repo's .env. The path should be resolved from the script's own directory (e.g. dirname of $0).

title: Failure paths exit with status 0
body: cleanup() ends with 'exit 0', and it is also the failure path when no tunnel URL could be extracted or the rate limit is hit. Callers and CI cannot detect that the webhook setup failed. Propagate a non-zero exit code on the failure paths.

title: Reusing an externally started tmole takes its URL from an unrelated or stale log file
body: When a tmole process is already running, the script extracts the URL from /tmp/tmole.log. That process may have been started by hand or with different output, so the log may be missing or contain a previous, dead tunnel URL. The stale URL is then written into GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in .env with no check that it is live.

title: Cache deletion leaves the 'Last updated' status stale in the UI
body: deleteCacheMutation's onSuccess (lines 42-46) only shows a toast and calls the parent's onSuccess (onChanged). Unlike disconnectMutation, it never invalidates trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, so the cacheUpdatedAt prop is not refreshed. After a successful 'Delete cached data', the dropdown keeps showing the old 'Last updated' timestamp and the delete item stays visible until something else refetches. Whether it refreshes depends on the parent's onChanged, which this component does not control. The PR's own test plan item 'Confirm cache deletion works and UI updates appropriately' would fail as written.

title: Unused SelectedCalendar.updatedAt write on every cache refresh
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) on every refresh, including webhook-driven ones. This bumps updatedAt on every SelectedCalendar row for the credential, across all event types. The PR's own notes say the frontend reads CalendarCache.updatedAt and not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, so this extra UPDATE has no consumer. It also changes the meaning of an existing column that is now selected into UserWithCalendars and the user session selects. Remove it, or justify it with a real consumer.

title: Existing CalendarCache rows are backfilled with the migration time as updatedAt
body: Adding the column with DEFAULT NOW() sets updatedAt for every pre-existing cache row to the deployment time. Immediately after deploy, the 'Last updated' label shows the deploy time for all Google calendars, even when the cached data is weeks old. Nothing in the PR marks these rows as legacy or unknown, so the UI presents a misleading freshness value.

title: Migration header warning contradicts the migration body
body: The Prisma-generated warning block says the required updatedAt column is added 'without a default value' and 'is not possible if the table is not empty'. The statement below adds the column with DEFAULT NOW(), so the warning is wrong for this migration and misleads reviewers about the migration's safety.

title: Stale TODO says CalendarCache has no updatedAt column
body: The comment says updatedAt 'doesn't exist yet in CalendarCache table'. This PR adds that column in schema.prisma and the migration, so the comment is now false. It also misses the point that the new column is what the PR relies on for cacheUpdatedAt.

title: Cache timestamp is hard-coded to en-US instead of the user's locale
body: The label text is translated with t(), but the timestamp is formatted with Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...). Users with other locales see an English-format date inside a localized sentence. The locale from useLocale() should be used for formatting.

title: No tests for the deleteCache ownership check or cache-status grouping
body: The handler's only access control is the findFirst on {id, userId}. This PR adds no test that a user cannot delete another user's credential cache. The new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groupBy/_max mapping and the connectedCalendarsHandler enrichment also have no tests. These are security-relevant and easy to regress.

title: Unrelated dev:cron change swaps ts-node for an unpinned npx tsx call
body: The dev:cron script changes from ts-node to npx tsx. This is unrelated to calendar cache. tsx is not declared in apps/web's dependencies or devDependencies, so npx fetches whatever tsx version the registry serves at run time, outside the lockfile. The change should be justified and the dependency declared, or reverted from this PR.

title: sed -i '' is macOS-only and breaks the update path on Linux
body: The script uses BSD syntax sed -i '' -E ... . With GNU sed, the empty string is taken as the script and the expression as a filename, so the update fails whenever GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists in the env file. The script is not documented as macOS-only, and the failure is not caught.

title: ENV_FILE path is relative to the working directory, not the script
body: ENV_FILE="../.env" resolves against the caller's current directory. It points at the repo's .env only when run from scripts/. Run from the repo root, as the usual `./scripts/...` invocation suggests, it writes GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL into a .env one directory above the repo. It should be resolved from the script's own location.

title: Reschedule still cancels SendGrid sends immediately, reintroducing the 100-cancellation cap failure
body: On reschedule, deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true) is called, which POSTs status:"cancel" to /v3/user/scheduled_sends right away. That is the same mechanism the PR identifies as the root cause: cancelled sends stay in scheduled_sends until their scheduled date, and SendGrid allows at most 100 pending cancellations. Once the cap is reached these cancels fail, the error is only console-logged, and the original reminder emails are still sent. The PR fixes this only for cancellations (deferred via the cancelled flag) and requestReschedule in bookings.tsx now uses the deferred path, so the two reschedule paths now behave differently. The try/catch around the forEach is also ineffective because the helper is async and not awaited.

title: Deleting a workflow cancels emails immediately and then cascade-deletes the rows, so failed cancels are never retried
body: When a workflow is deleted, scheduled email reminders are cancelled with deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true), which issues an immediate SendGrid cancel (same 100-pending-cancel cap problem as the reschedule path). The workflow is then removed with ctx.prisma.workflow.deleteMany, which cascades to the WorkflowReminder rows. If the immediate cancel fails, the error is only logged and the row is gone, so the cron job (which only processes flagged rows) can never retry it, and the emails are sent after the user deleted the workflow. The same pattern appears in the step-deletion path at line 521, where workflowStep.delete cascades the reminders.

title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation batch and loses the DB deletes already queued
body: The loop awaits client.request (the SendGrid cancel) per reminder with no per-item error handling. The first rejected request (for example, a batch SendGrid no longer knows about) throws out of the loop into the outer catch. Consequences: (1) reminders after the failing one are not cancelled in this run, and findMany has no ordering, so emails for other cancelled bookings can still be sent. (2) The prisma.workflowReminder.delete calls are collected as PrismaPromises, which are lazy and only execute when awaited via Promise.all, which is never reached after the throw. Rows for reminders that were already cancelled therefore stay with cancelled=true and are re-cancelled on every run. If SendGrid rejects a repeat cancel, the run aborts at the same item every time until that reminder's scheduledDate passes, blocking every other cancellation in the meantime. Each item needs its own try/catch and the deletes should be awaited per item or via Promise.allSettled.

title: Deferred cancellation misses reminders due within ~15 minutes of the cancel and they are still sent
body: A cancelled booking's reminder is only flagged here; the actual SendGrid cancel happens in the 15-minute cron, and the cron only cancels reminders whose scheduledDate is within the next hour. A reminder whose send time falls before the next cron tick (up to ~15 minutes after the cancellation) is flagged but never cancelled, and SendGrid sends it. This is the same user-visible symptom the PR is meant to fix. Reminders that are due within an hour at cancel time could be cancelled immediately, since the pending-cancellation cap only matters for long lead times.

title: Paid booking cancellations return before workflow reminders are cancelled
body: For paid bookings, the block starting at the bookingToDelete.paid check refunds, sets the booking to REJECTED, and returns at this line. The workflow reminder cancellation (lines 484-493) is after that return, so reminders for paid bookings are never flagged or cancelled in SendGrid or Twilio, and the workflow emails and SMS are still sent for a cancelled booking. This is the exact bug the PR targets, and the new code does not cover it.

title: SMS reminder rows are no longer deleted when the Twilio cancel fails
body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder now deletes the WorkflowReminder row only after twilio.cancelSMS succeeds. Before, callers deleted the rows unconditionally with deleteMany. The PR removed those deletes from handleCancelBooking, requestReschedule and the workflow update path. Twilio cancellation fails for messages already sent or no longer cancellable, which is common close to the send time. In that case the row survives with scheduled=true and a referenceId. The cron cleanup only deletes EMAIL rows, so SMS rows are never cleaned up. Every later cancel or edit re-attempts the Twilio call and logs errors.

title: immediateDelete sends the SendGrid cancel but leaves the WorkflowReminder row untouched
body: In the immediateDelete branch the SendGrid cancel is sent, but the row is neither deleted nor flagged: scheduled stays true, referenceId stays set, and cancelled stays null. The name suggests the row is deleted, which is misleading. The row is never reconciled and lingers until scheduledDate passes. Later operations (workflow or step deletion, event-type removal, step edit) select scheduled=true rows and re-issue cancels for batches that are already cancelled, which feeds the batch-abort problem in the cron job.

title: New deferred-cancellation cron logic and changed helper signatures have no tests
body: The new cron block (flagged reminders, SendGrid cancel, per-row delete) contains error-path behaviour that is subtle, as the batch-abort and lazy-PrismaPromise issues show. The PR also changes the signatures of deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder and their immediate/deferred semantics. No tests cover any of it, and nothing guards the reschedule and workflow-deletion paths against the cap.

title: Paid-booking cancellation returns before workflow reminders are cancelled
body: For a paid booking the handler takes the `bookingToDelete.paid` branch (starts at line 363), refunds, sets status REJECTED, and returns at this line. The workflow reminder cancellation block (lines 484-493) and the zapier `cancelScheduledJobs` call come after this return, so they never run for paid bookings. The booking is cancelled, but its scheduled BEFORE_EVENT email and SMS reminders are still sent, which is the exact bug this PR is meant to fix. The same gap exists at line 437 (`return null` when the payment service is not implemented), and any throw between the status update at line 255 and line 484 leaves reminders uncancelled. Reminder cancellation should happen before the paid branch, or be duplicated into it.

title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation batch and skips all deletes
body: The loop awaits `client.request` for every cancelled reminder inside a single try block. If any call throws (for example SendGrid rejects a batch that was already sent or already cancelled), the catch at lines 75-77 runs and the loop is abandoned, so the remaining reminders in the window are never cancelled. Also, `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` returns a lazy PrismaPromise that only executes when awaited in `Promise.all` at line 74. Because that await is never reached after an error, the deletes for reminders already cancelled earlier in the loop never run either. Those rows keep `cancelled: true`, and the next cron run (about 15 minutes later) hits the same failing reminder first. A single bad batch therefore blocks cancellation of every other reminder in its one-hour window, and emails for cancelled bookings still go out. Each cancel should be isolated (try/catch per reminder), and the delete should be awaited right after its own successful cancel.

title: Immediate cancel path reuses the call that hits SendGrid's 100-pending-cancellation cap
body: The `immediateDelete` branch sends `status: "cancel"` to SendGrid's `/v3/user/scheduled_sends`. The PR description identifies this exact mechanism as the root cause: each cancelled send stays pending until its scheduled date, and once 100 are pending new cancels fail while the emails are still sent. This branch is used for rescheduling (handleNewBooking.ts line 968), workflow deletion (workflows.tsx line 214) and step deletion (workflows.tsx line 521), which can cancel many reminders at once. When the cap is hit, the error is swallowed by the catch at the bottom of the function, so the reminders are silently still sent. The branch also returns without touching the DB row, so the reminder keeps `scheduled: true` and a `referenceId` pointing at a cancelled batch until its scheduled date passes. The name `immediateDelete` is also misleading because the row is not deleted. These paths should use the same deferred `cancelled` flag and cron-based cancellation as the rest of the PR.

title: Cancellation flag write is fire-and-forget, so the reminder's fate is not guaranteed
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is async, but it is called without `await` here (and the same pattern appears in bookings.tsx line 490 and workflows.tsx). The `cancelled: true` UPDATE that now decides whether the reminder is sent may not complete before the handler returns, and on a serverless runtime the process can be frozen after the response. Errors are swallowed inside the helper's try/catch, so a failed write leaves the booking cancelled with no record that its reminder must be stopped, and nothing retries it. The helper's result should be awaited and failures surfaced or retried.

title: SMS reminder row is only deleted if the Twilio cancel succeeds
body: The Prisma `workflowReminder.delete` runs after `twilio.cancelSMS` in the same try block. If Twilio throws (for example because the message is already sent or no longer cancellable), the delete is skipped and the error is only logged. Before this change the callers deleted the row regardless of the Twilio result, so this is a regression: the row keeps `scheduled: true` and its `referenceId`. The row deletion should not depend on the external cancel succeeding.

title: Cron endpoint authorizes everyone when CRON_API_KEY is unset
body: If `CRON_API_KEY` is not configured and the request has neither an `authorization` header nor an `apiKey` query parameter, `apiKey` is `undefined` and the check `process.env.CRON_API_KEY !== apiKey` evaluates to `undefined !== undefined`, which is false, so the request proceeds. This is pre-existing, but the endpoint now also cancels SendGrid sends and deletes reminder rows, so an unauthenticated caller on a misconfigured deployment can trigger those side effects. The handler should reject when the key is missing.

title: Unrelated UI restructuring bundled into a reminder-cancellation fix
body: The condition changes from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to `isPhoneNumberNeeded` and the phone block is unwrapped. This changes rendering for SMS_ATTENDEE steps, which no longer get an empty padded container. Nothing in the PR description or title mentions this UI change, and it is unrelated to cancelling reminders. It should be split into its own PR or described explicitly.

title: New cancel-and-delete cron logic and cancelled flag have no tests
body: The PR changes cancellation semantics across handleCancelBooking, bookings.tsx, handleNewBooking and workflows.tsx, adds a `cancelled` column with a migration, and adds a cron branch that calls SendGrid and deletes rows. None of this is covered by a test in the diff. The previous fix shipped broken with the failure silently swallowed. At minimum, tests should cover: a cancelled reminder inside the one-hour window being cancelled and deleted; a SendGrid failure for one reminder not blocking the others; and a paid booking's reminders being cancelled.

title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole batch and discards all DB progress
body: The loop at lines 56-73 awaits client.request for each cancelled reminder, but the prisma.workflowReminder.delete calls are only pushed into an array and executed later by Promise.all (line 74). If any SendGrid call throws (rate limit, a batch id SendGrid rejects, network error), the catch at line 75 only logs, the loop stops, and no later reminder is cancelled. The reminders that were already cancelled in SendGrid are not deleted either (the Prisma promises never run), so they keep cancelled=true and are re-cancelled on every 15-minute run. A persistent failure on one reminder therefore blocks cancellation of every reminder after it until that reminder's scheduled time passes, so those emails are still sent, which is the bug this PR is meant to fix. The same deferred deletion means a function timeout part-way through a large batch loses all progress, so the cron can never get past the first N reminders. Cancel and delete each reminder inside its own try/catch, and delete the row right after its successful cancel.

title: Cancelling a paid booking returns before any workflow reminder is cancelled
body: The paid branch (lines 363-465) sets the booking to REJECTED and returns at line 464. The reminder cancellation block at lines 484-493 comes after that return, so for paid bookings no EMAIL or SMS workflow reminder is cancelled. Those reminders are still sent for a cancelled and refunded booking, which is the exact bug this PR claims to fix. cancelScheduledJobs is skipped for the same reason. Move the reminder cancellation above the paid branch, or call it from both paths.

title: Immediate SendGrid cancel reintroduces the 100-pending-cancellation limit with no fallback
body: The immediateDelete branch issues the same POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends status=cancel call that the PR description says is capped at 100 pending cancellations. It is used for bulk operations: deleting a workflow (workflows.tsx line 214) or a step (workflows.tsx line 521) with many scheduled reminders, and rescheduling (handleNewBooking.ts line 968). Once the cap is hit the call throws, the error is only logged in the catch, and nothing marks the row cancelled, so the cron never retries. For workflow and step deletion the rows are then removed by cascade, so the emails are sent. These calls are also fired from forEach without await, so the handler can return before the cancellations finish. The branch also returns without updating the row, so rows remain scheduled=true even though the batch was cancelled. Rows already flagged cancelled by requestReschedule (bookings.tsx line 490) are cancelled again here and later re-cancelled by the cron. Set cancelled=true for all email reminders and let the cron perform the cancellation, or otherwise make the cancellation bounded, awaited and retryable.

title: SMS reminder row is kept forever when Twilio cancel fails
body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder now deletes the DB row only if twilio.cancelSMS succeeds (line 180 throws, the catch at line 187 skips the delete at line 182). Previously handleCancelBooking deleted all reminder rows regardless of the Twilio result, and that deleteMany was removed in this PR. Nothing else removes SMS rows: the cron's deleteMany at scheduleEmailReminders.ts lines 34-41 is EMAIL-only. So rows whose Twilio cancel fails (for example messages already sent) accumulate indefinitely, and a message that is still pending is sent with no cancelled flag or retry, unlike the email path. Decouple the row deletion from the Twilio result, or record the failure so it can be retried.

title: Cron endpoint accepts unauthenticated requests when CRON_API_KEY is unset
body: The check compares process.env.CRON_API_KEY to req.headers.authorization || req.query.apiKey. If CRON_API_KEY is not set and the request carries neither an authorization header nor an apiKey query parameter, both sides are undefined, the !== comparison is false, and the request is accepted. Anyone can then trigger this job, which sends and cancels SendGrid batches and deletes WorkflowReminder rows. The pre-existing check is now the gate for the new cancellation and deletion logic. Reject the request when CRON_API_KEY is missing or empty, and only accept a match against a defined value.

title: Cancellation only runs in the final hour, so late cancellations can still be sent
body: Cancelled reminders are only picked up when scheduledDate is within the next hour (lines 44-51), and the job runs every 15 minutes. A booking cancelled less than about 15 minutes before a reminder's scheduled time may not be processed by any run before that time, so SendGrid sends the email anyway. The PR description presents the fix as ensuring cancelled reminders are not sent. Either document this limit or cancel immediately when a reminder is already inside the one-hour window at cancellation time.

title: Helper's row delete races with cascade deletes and logs spurious P2025 errors
body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder now deletes the WorkflowReminder row, but callers that remove rows through cascade do not await it. The workflow delete (workflows.tsx line 216) and the step delete (workflows.tsx line 523) call it without await right before the cascade removes the row. The delete at line 182 then throws 'record not found' and is logged as 'Error canceling reminder' for every SMS reminder, even though the Twilio cancel succeeded. Either skip the row delete when the caller already deletes the row, or make the caller await the helper before deleting the parent.

title: Changed cancellation semantics and helper signatures have no tests
body: This PR changes deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder to take a reminder id, adds a cancelled flag that the cron must honour, adds a new cron cancellation loop, and changes which paths run immediate versus deferred cancellation. No tests are added or updated. The failure modes that caused the original bug (SendGrid cancel errors, the pending-cancellation cap, reminders cancelled with or without a referenceId) are untested. Also confirm that no caller outside the ten files in this diff still uses the old single-argument signatures.

title: forEach(async) detaches calendar/video cancellation and disables the try/catch
body: The callback passed to bookingRefsFiltered.forEach is now async and awaits getCalendar, but Array.prototype.forEach ignores the returned promise. Consequences: (1) the try/catch at lines 124-139 can no longer catch anything. getCalendar, deleteEvent and deleteMeeting failures become unhandled promise rejections, which crash Node by default on v15+. (2) Reschedule returns true before the calendar and video cancellations have run, so the booking is marked cancelled while the old calendar slot may still be held. Fix by using a for...of loop with await inside the existing try block.

title: forEach(async) detaches calendar/video cancellation and disables the try/catch
body: Same defect as the vital reschedule: the forEach callback is async and awaits getCalendar, but forEach does not await it. The surrounding try/catch no longer sees errors from getCalendar or deleteEvent/deleteMeeting, which become unhandled rejections. The function also returns true before the cancellations finish. Use for...of with await so the existing try/catch and ordering actually apply.

title: Unawaited async forEach in requestReschedule drops errors and races the response
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach now takes an async callback that awaits getCalendar and then calls deleteEvent/deleteMeeting. forEach does not await these promises, and this block has no try/catch. The mutation proceeds to sendRequestRescheduleEmail and returns while calendar and video deletions are still in flight. Any rejection (credential failure, network error) becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of a handled error. Replace with for...of and await each deletion, or collect the promises and Promise.allSettled them.

title: Calendar deletions in an unawaited forEach(async) are never awaited and their errors are lost
body: The recurring-cancel branch calls bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... await getCalendar(credential) ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) }). This PR adds an await ahead of the loop, so every push happens later. The handler snapshots apiDeletes at line 652 (prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) and awaits only that copy, so these deletions are neither awaited nor reflected in the response. Cancellation can return success before calendar events are removed, and any rejection is an unhandled rejection. Use for...of with await and push into apiDeletes before the final Promise.all.

title: import() calls are evaluated eagerly, so the modules are not actually deferred
body: Each entry is written as a direct import("./x") call inside the object literal. Those calls run when index.ts is evaluated, so every app module still starts loading on the first import of @calcom/app-store, just without blocking. The only change is that the module evaluation no longer blocks synchronously. If the goal is lazy loading, each entry should be a function such as () => import("./x") that consumers invoke only when needed. As written, the PR does not reduce load work or startup cost.

title: getCalendarCredentials stores un-awaited getCalendar promises in a sync function
body: getCalendarCredentials is still synchronous, but getCalendar is now async, so the calendar field of each returned entry is a Promise<Calendar | null>. Only getConnectedCalendars awaits it (line 48). Any other consumer that uses the field as a Calendar will fail to typecheck, and any rejection from getCalendar (for example a CalendarService constructor throw) in an entry that is never awaited becomes an unhandled rejection. The return type should make the Promise explicit, or the function should become async and its callers should await it.

title: Sync-to-async signature changes have no test updates
body: getCalendar changes from a synchronous return to Promise<Calendar | null>, and deleteMeeting, deleteEvent, getVideoAdapters and about 12 call sites across 10 files gain awaits. The PR touches no test files. Existing unit tests that stub getCalendar, deleteMeeting or appStore synchronously will break or silently pass against the wrong shape. The unhandled-rejection problems in the forEach call sites would also go undetected because no test exercises the failure paths of these functions.

title: Async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch dead and leaves calendar cancellations unawaited
body: The callback passed to bookingRefsFiltered.forEach is now async and awaits getCalendar(). forEach ignores the promises its callback returns, so the try/catch at lines 124-139 can no longer catch anything. Before this change, a synchronous throw from getCalendar (for example a CalendarService constructor error) was caught and logged. Now every throw becomes a rejected promise nobody handles, so it surfaces as an unhandledRejection and the logger.error branch never runs. The function also returns true at line 151 before the calendar and video cancellations have run. The identical change in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 has the same problem. Use a for...of loop with await inside the try so failures are caught and ordering is preserved.

title: requestReschedule fires async callbacks through forEach with no awaiting or error handling
body: The forEach callback is now async and awaits getCalendar() before calendar.deleteEvent(). forEach does not await these promises, so the mutation finishes and responds while calendar and video cancellations may still be in flight. Any failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Before this change, a synchronous throw from getCalendar would propagate out of the mutation and fail it visibly; now that error is silently swallowed as an unhandled rejection. Use for...of with await, or Promise.allSettled with explicit logging, so the outcome of the cancellations is observed.

title: Recurring-cancel calendar deletions are no longer awaited before the response
body: The outer .forEach(async (credential) => {...}) pushes deletion results into apiDeletes from inside an async callback that nothing awaits. apiDeletes is snapshotted by prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes) in the later Promise.all, so these pushes arrive too late to be awaited, and their errors are unhandled. This PR adds another await before deleteEvent is called, so the calendar deletions are now issued a microtask later, after the handler has already moved on toward the response. The same PR converts the non-recurring 'old behaviour' branch just below to a for...of loop with await (lines 477-484), so the recurring branch is inconsistent with the intended pattern. On serverless runtimes, work still pending after the response can be frozen and never complete. Convert this to for...of with await and push into apiDeletes before the Promise.all.

title: Import failure in getVideoAdapters escapes the Cal Video fallback in createMeeting
body: getVideoAdapters now awaits a dynamic import from appStore. Line 52 calls it outside the try block that starts at line 70, and the catch at line 86 is where createMeeting falls back to Cal Video. If the dynamic import rejects (module evaluation error, missing dependency, or a chunk load failure), createMeeting rejects immediately instead of falling back, so the whole booking or reschedule that uses the video location fails. updateMeeting has the same shape at line 111, where the await is also outside its .catch. Before this change, appStore lookups were synchronous and could not reject. Move the adapter resolution inside the try, or catch the import failure and return the fallback.

title: Eagerly created import() promises can produce unhandled rejections
body: Each entry in the appStore object is an import() promise created at module evaluation. Only the keys that a caller actually awaits get a rejection handler. If any app module throws while evaluating, its promise rejects and nothing handles it, which Node reports as an unhandledRejection (process termination under default settings on modern Node). With the previous static imports, the same failure surfaced deterministically at startup. Consider storing factories (() => import(...)) and awaiting only the requested app, or attaching a handler to each promise.

title: import() in an object literal still loads every app eagerly
body: The object literal calls import() for all 28 apps as soon as the module is evaluated, so every app module still loads at startup, just asynchronously. The PR does not make app loading lazy, and the extra awaits at every call site add complexity without a corresponding saving. If the goal is lazy loading, the entries need to be functions such as () => import('./vital') that are invoked only when needed.

title: Default export values changed from modules to Promises; unconverted callers fail silently
body: appStore's values changed from module namespaces to Promise<module>. Any call site that still indexes appStore synchronously, including code outside the 12 changed files, now receives a Promise. The guard pattern used throughout, `if (!(app && 'lib' in app && 'CalendarService' in app.lib))`, evaluates `'lib' in promise` as false and takes the 'not implemented' branch, returning null with only a warning. Calendar events, video meetings, or payments would then be skipped silently rather than erroring. TypeScript does not flag this because `in` accepts any object type. Every consumer of the default export needs to be checked for a missing await.

title: Commented-out example import points at a path that does not exist
body: The old file used `// import * as example from "./_example";`. The new comment refers to `import("./example")`, which drops the leading underscore and so points to the wrong module if someone uncomments it.

title: getCalendarCredentials returns an unawaited Promise in the calendar field
body: getCalendarCredentials stays synchronous, but getCalendar is now async, so each returned entry's `calendar` field is a Promise<Calendar | null> that is never awaited here. The exported return shape changed silently. Callers that read `.calendar` as a Calendar would fail type-checking, and any rejection (for example an import failure) is unhandled if the entry is never consumed. Making this function async and awaiting each calendar, or documenting the Promise field, would make the contract explicit.

title: Object-literal import() calls still load every app eagerly, so nothing is lazy
body: Each `import("./...")` is a property initializer in the object literal, so every app module is requested as soon as this file is evaluated. Awaiting at the call sites only defers the wait; it does not avoid loading the apps. Deferred loading needs thunks (e.g. `googlecalendar: () => import("./googlecalendar")`) with callers invoking them. The PR description gives no goal, so it is unclear whether the intent was laziness. Also, a module whose import rejects produces an unhandled rejection at load time unless that key is awaited, rather than an error at the lookup site.

title: forEach(async) makes the surrounding try/catch ineffective for calendar errors
body: Before this PR getCalendar was synchronous, so a throw from the CalendarService constructor inside this sync forEach callback reached the try/catch and was logged. Now getCalendar is async: the throw becomes a rejected promise returned by the async callback, which forEach discards. The catch never sees it and it surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection. The deletions are also not awaited, so the function returns true and sends the reschedule email while the old calendar event/meeting is still being deleted. Use for...of with await inside the try.

title: forEach(async) makes the surrounding try/catch ineffective for calendar errors
body: Same change as in the vital reschedule: getCalendar is now async, so errors thrown while creating the calendar service escape the try/catch on line 124-139 and become unhandled rejections. The deleteEvent/deleteMeeting calls are not awaited before the function returns true and sends the reschedule email. Use for...of with await inside the try so failures are logged and ordering is preserved.

title: Async forEach in requestReschedule turns calendar failures into unhandled rejections
body: Previously a synchronous throw from getCalendar inside this forEach propagated and failed the mutation. Now getCalendar is async, so the error is returned from the discarded async callback and becomes an unhandled promise rejection while the mutation reports success. The calendar deleteEvent calls are also not awaited before sendRequestRescheduleEmail runs. Use for...of with await so errors are handled and deletions finish before the email is sent.

title: Recurring-cancel calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes after it has already been awaited
body: The outer `.forEach(async (credential) => ...)` does not return its promise, so the handler continues without waiting for it. The final `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` copies apiDeletes before these callbacks reach their `apiDeletes.push(...)` calls, so these per-occurrence calendar deletions are never awaited. Their results and errors are dropped and failures become unhandled rejections. The PR rewrote the sibling non-recurring loop in the else branch to for...of with await but left this one as forEach(async); it should be converted the same way.

title: `await apiDeletes` awaits an array, not the pending deletions
body: On the paid-cancellation path, `await apiDeletes;` does not wait for the promises inside the array. The handler returns 'Booking successfully cancelled' before calendar and video deletions settle, and their rejections are unhandled. This is pre-existing, but the PR touches these calls and the async change makes the difference observable. Use `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)` if the deletions are meant to complete before responding.

title: getCalendarCredentials still calls the now-async getCalendar without await
body: getCalendarCredentials stays synchronous and stores `getCalendar(credential)` directly, so each returned `calendar` field is a Promise<Calendar | null>, not a Calendar. Only getConnectedCalendars currently remembers to await `item.calendar`; any other consumer that uses the field as a Calendar will get undefined methods or a Promise where a value is expected. Make this function async and await the calendar, or document that the field is a Promise.

title: Async conversion changes error propagation in cancel and reschedule paths with no test updates
body: getCalendar, getVideoAdapters, deleteMeeting, deleteEvent and payment app lookup all changed from synchronous to async, and several callers moved from sync forEach to async callbacks. The PR adds no tests or test updates covering what happens when credential or app lookup or CalendarService construction throws during cancel, reschedule, or video deletion. Those error paths are exactly what changed, so they should have coverage.

title: Slots inside a date override skip the busy-time check entirely
body: When a slot falls inside a same-day date override, none of the early-return branches in the find callback fire, so find returns undefined but dateOverrideExist is already true. The following `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` then returns before the `busy.every(...)` check at the end of the function. Calendar events and existing bookings overlapping the slot are therefore ignored for any host (fixed or round-robin) who has a date override on that day. A round-robin host with a conflict inside their override window stays eligible and can be double-booked. Overrides should narrow availability, not bypass conflict checks; this branch should fall through to the busy check instead of returning true. No test covers a busy time inside an override.

title: Days with more than one date override row reject every slot
body: dateOverrides.find returns the first override for which the callback returns truthy, and the callback returns true whenever the slot is outside that particular override (lines 118-124). With two override rows on the same day, for example 09:00-10:00 and 14:00-15:00 (the UI stores each range as its own row), a 09:00 slot is inside the first but the second callback returns true, so find returns it and line 130 returns false. The same happens for a 14:00 slot. Every slot on that day is rejected even though slots in both windows are valid. The intended logic is 'available if inside any override on that day', which needs some() with the correct polarity, not find with inverted returns.

title: Split working hours on one weekday remove all slots for that day
body: workingHours.find returns the first entry on the slot's weekday whose range does not contain the slot (the callback returns true when start < startTime or end > endTime). If a host has two ranges on the same weekday, such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 (a lunch break, stored as two availability rows), a 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the 13:00-17:00 entry, and a 14:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the 09:00-12:00 entry. The host gets no slots on that day. getSlots already restricts slots to working hours, so this block is either redundant or, as written, breaks split schedules. The existing tests only use one contiguous range per day, so this is not caught.

title: Fixed host's days off are not enforced for round-robin slots
body: The working-hours check only rejects a slot when an entry for the same weekday exists and does not contain it. If a fixed host has no working-hours entry for the slot's weekday (for example a Monday-Friday host and a Saturday slot), find returns undefined and nothing rejects the slot. The slot is generated from the round-robin host's hours, and the fixed host's check then only looks at busy times, so the slot passes. A round-robin event with a fixed host who does not work Saturdays still offers and books Saturday slots with that fixed host. This is the exact problem the PR says it fixes. A fixed host should be treated as unavailable when the slot is not on one of their working days.

title: Shifted override minutes wrap past midnight and land on the wrong day
body: startTime and endTime take only .hour()*60 + .minute() of the offset-shifted instant, which drops the date. The day an override is assigned to comes from the unshifted override.start in the activeOverrides filter, so when the offset pushes the time across midnight the result is attributed to the wrong day. Example: organizer America/New_York, invitee Europe/London, override starting 23:00 UTC on day D. The filter assigns it to London day D. offset = 0 - (-300) = +300, so the shifted time is 04:00 on day D+1, but the code yields 240 and shows 04:00 on day D. Day D+1 loses the override entirely. Evening overrides viewed from zones ahead of the organizer will be misplaced like this. The shifted timestamp should be kept as a full datetime and the day derived from it, not reduced to minutes-of-day.

title: Comparing dayjs objects with === is always false
body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares object references, so it is always false. The intended zero-length override check never fires. It should use isSame, or the zero-length case should be handled explicitly.

title: Override day match mixes server-local and UTC formatting
body: dayjs(date.start).add(...).format(...) is in local mode, so it formats in the process timezone, while slotStartTime.format(...) is in UTC (time.utc()). The two strings are compared to decide whether an override applies to the slot's day. On any process not running in UTC, near midnight an override can be matched to the wrong day or not matched at all, which then sends the slot to the working-hours check instead. Both sides should be formatted in UTC.

title: End time is computed from the slot start
body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` uses slotStartTime, so `end` equals `start` and the `end > workingHour.endTime` comparison tests the slot start rather than the slot end. A slot that starts inside the working window and runs past its end is not rejected here. The variable should use slotEndTime.

title: Optional override timeZone is passed to tz() with no fallback
body: TimeRange.timeZone was just made optional, but getSlots passes override.timeZone straight into .tz() without a fallback, even though organizerTimeZone is already in scope in this function. When timeZone is undefined, dayjs falls back to the default or the process local zone, so the organizer offset is computed against the wrong zone without any error. The fallback should be organizerTimeZone, or the code should fail loudly.

title: toHaveTimeSlots passes when fewer slots than expected are returned
body: The matcher iterates over the actual slots only (.every over schedule.slots[date]) and compares each to expectedSlots[index]. Missing trailing expected slots are never detected, so an assertion expecting four override slots passes if only one matching slot is returned. Every new override assertion depends on this matcher, so regressions that remove slots (multiple override rows on one day, fixed host days off, split working hours) would go unnoticed. The matcher should also assert the lengths match.

title: Headline scenarios of the PR have no test coverage
body: The PR's main change, fixed-host date overrides in round-robin events, has no test. The only new test is an extra assertion in the single-host override test, which has no hosts, no busy times, and one override row. None of the regressions in this change are exercised: a busy time inside an override, two override rows on the same day, a split working-hours day, or a fixed host without working hours on the slot's weekday. Tests should cover each of these, and the round-robin plus fixed-host override case the PR describes.

title: New timeZone field on TimeRange is undocumented and its semantics are load-bearing
body: The new optional timeZone is added without a comment. The code relies on an undocumented convention: override start and end are treated as organizer wall-clock time carried in their UTC fields, and the organizer's offset is applied in both lib/slots.ts and checkIfIsAvailable. Nothing in this type says which timezone the field refers to or how start and end should be interpreted, so a future change to getUserAvailability could break the override logic silently.

title: Slots inside a date override skip the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, once a slot falls inside a date override, the function returns true at line 134 before reaching the busy.every(...) check at line 153. The busy array holds the host's existing Cal bookings and calendar events. For any fixed or round-robin host with a date override covering the slot, a booking or external calendar event at that time is ignored and the slot is still offered. Before this PR the busy check always ran for fixed hosts, so this is a regression that can produce double bookings on exactly the days that have date overrides. The override should only decide the working-hours question; the slot should still fall through to the busy check.

title: Working-hours check rejects slots that fall in a second same-day range
body: workingHours.find(...) returns truthy as soon as any entry for the weekday does not contain the slot (the if at line 143 returns true for any entry where the slot is before its start or after its end). Users commonly have several availability rows for one weekday (split shifts such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, or a lunch break). A 14:00 slot is then rejected because the 09:00-12:00 entry does not contain it.
