This affects fixed hosts in individual events and fixed/round-robin hosts in team events, and removes roughly half of a split-shift user's slots. The logic should be: reject only if no entry for that day contains the slot. Also, a weekday with no entries (a day off) passes this check unchecked because find never matches, so the check does not enforce the intent stated in its comment.

title: Working-hours end bound is computed from the slot start, not the slot end
body: Line 142 computes `end` from slotStartTime, so `end` always equals `start`. The end-of-day comparison therefore tests the slot start against workingHour.endTime, not the slot end. A slot starting at 16:30 that runs to 17:15 with working hours ending at 17:00 passes. For a round-robin event this means a fixed host can be offered slots that run past their working hours, which is the availability problem this PR is meant to fix. The end should be computed from slotEndTime.

title: Two date-override ranges on the same day make every slot on that day unavailable
body: dateOverrides.find(...) returns true for the first same-day override that does not contain the slot (the returns at lines 115, 121 and 124). The outer check then treats this as 'slot is outside the override' and returns false at line 130. The predicate never asks whether some other override on that day contains the slot. With two override rows for one date, for example 14:00-15:00 and 16:00-17:00 (the data model allows multiple date-override rows per date), a 14:00 slot is rejected because the 16:00 override does not contain it, and a 16:00 slot is rejected because the 14:00 override does not contain it. All slots on that day disappear for that host. The check should be whether some same-day override contains the slot (some, not find-with-rejection).

title: Zero-length override check compares Dayjs objects with === and never fires
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct Dayjs object references, so it is always false. The branch meant to handle zero-length (start equals end) overrides is dead code. Such an override then falls through to the overlap comparisons, where a slot starting exactly at the override start is treated as inside the override and returned as available (line 133). Use .isSame(...) instead.

title: Override day matching mixes server-local and UTC dates and can attach an override to the wrong day
body: The override's day is computed as dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD'). dayjs(date.start) is in the server process's local timezone, while the slot side, slotStartTime.format(...), is in UTC (time.utc()). On a server whose TZ is not UTC the two sides use different calendars, so the override may match the wrong day or none. Separately, the day is taken from the UTC date of the shifted instant rather than the organizer's local date. An override at 02:00 on 22 Jan in Asia/Kolkata becomes 20:30Z on 21 Jan, so it also rejects the organizer's daytime 21 Jan slots (for example 09:30 IST), which have no override. Day matching should be done on organizer-local dates for both the override and the slot.

title: Override UTC offset is taken at the wall-clock-as-UTC instant, so it is off by an hour on DST-change days
body: Overrides are stored as organizer wall-clock time encoded as UTC. The offset is computed with dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone) at that encoded instant, which can differ from the real instant by up to 14 hours. When the encoded instant and the real instant fall on opposite sides of a DST transition, the wrong offset is used. Example: America/New_York override at 03:30 on 2023-03-12 (already on EDT). The encoded instant 03:30Z is before the 07:00Z switch, so offset -5 is used, and the bound becomes 08:30Z instead of 07:30Z. The same pattern is used in packages/lib/slots.ts lines 212-213, so the lib and the trpc check share the error.

title: timeZone on date overrides is optional in the type but dereferenced without a fallback
body: packages/types/schedule.d.ts now declares TimeRange.timeZone as optional, and this code passes override.timeZone straight into .tz(...) with no guard. If a caller omits it, dayjs falls back to the process's local timezone with no error. Offsets are then computed for the server's zone rather than the organizer's, and slots are shifted silently. The caller contract should be made explicit (required parameter, or an explicit guard and fallback).

title: Tests do not cover the scenarios this PR changes in checkIfIsAvailable
body: The only new test is a second timezone assertion on a single-user event with hosts: []. Nothing covers the headline fix, a round-robin event where a fixed host has a date override, so the fixed-host path in getSchedule is never exercised with overrides. Nothing covers busy bookings or calendar events that fall inside a date override (which would catch the busy-check bypass). Nothing covers two override rows on the same date, or split same-day working hours, or a slot that runs past the end of working hours. The existing suite therefore passes with all of these defects present. Tests for each of these should be added.

title: Slots inside a date override skip the busy-time check
body: When a same-day date override exists and the slot lies inside it, execution reaches `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` and returns before the `busy.every(...)` check at the end of the function. Existing bookings and calendar busy times are therefore ignored for every slot inside a date override window. Personal events are treated as fixed-host events (isFixed is true when there is no schedulingType), so this affects ordinary personal bookings too: a host with an override 14:00-18:00 who already has a 15:00 booking is still offered 15:00 and can be double-booked. The override should only replace the working-hours check; busy times must still be evaluated.

title: Split working hours on one weekday reject every slot
body: `workingHours.find(...)` returns the first entry for which the callback returns true, and the callback returns true when the slot is outside that entry. Working hours come one entry per availability row, so a host with two ranges on the same weekday (for example 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) has every slot outside at least one of those entries. Every slot on that day then hits `return false` at line 150. This check now runs for every fixed host, including personal events, so users with split days get no slots at all. The intended test is 'reject only if no entry contains the slot'. The test suite only uses single-row schedules, so this is not caught.

title: Working-hours end check compares the slot start, not the slot end
body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime`, the same value as `start`, so `end > workingHour.endTime` never checks the slot's end. A slot that starts inside working hours but runs past the end is accepted. With working hours ending at 17:00 and a 60-minute event, the 16:30 slot passes this check. The fixed host's own end boundary is only enforced here, so a fixed host can be booked beyond their hours in round-robin events, which is the scenario this PR is meant to fix.

title: Override end check ignores slots that start inside the override but run past it
body: The override boundary test compares `slotStartTime` with the override end instead of `slotEndTime`. A slot that starts inside an override and extends beyond its end (override ends 18:00, 60-minute slot at 17:30) fails all three checks and falls through to `return true` at line 133. The fixed host is then treated as available for time after the override ends. The earlier check at line 119 does use the slot end, so the two checks are inconsistent.

title: Multiple date overrides on one day make every slot on that day unavailable
body: `dateOverrides.find` returns the first override whose callback returns truthy, and the callback returns true when the slot lies outside that override. With two overrides on the same date (for example 09:00-10:00 and 14:00-15:00, which the availability UI supports as multiple ranges per date), a slot inside the first range is rejected because the second range reports it as outside, and the converse holds for the second range. Every slot on that day is therefore rejected. The correct semantics is 'available if inside at least one override on that day'. The flag `dateOverrideExist` is also mutated as a side effect inside the predicate, which relies on `find` short-circuiting and is fragile.

title: Same-day override check depends on the server process timezone
body: `dayjs(date.start)` is created in local mode, so `.add(...).format('YYYY MM DD')` formats in the server's process timezone. `slotStartTime` is converted with `.utc()` and formats in UTC. On any server whose TZ is not UTC (developer machines, self-hosted deployments), the same-day comparison fails for overrides whose local date differs from the UTC date. The override is then not detected, and the slot falls through to the working-hours/busy logic, so date-override behaviour depends on where the process runs. The shifted value should be put in UTC mode before formatting.

title: Zero-length override check compares object references
body: `dayjs(...) === dayjs(...)` compares object identity, which is always false for two distinct dayjs instances. The zero-length override early return is therefore dead code. It should use `.isSame(...)` or compare timestamps.

title: Availability checks use eventType.length instead of the requested duration
body: `availabilityCheckProps.eventLength` is `eventType.length`, but slot generation at line 451 uses `input.duration || eventType.length`. For events with multiple duration options, the new working-hours and date-override checks compute the slot end from the wrong length, so a 60-minute booking is validated as a 30-minute one. This matters more now that these checks depend on the slot end.

title: Timezone conversions run inside the per-slot override loop
body: `dayjs.tz(...)` (which formats through Intl) is evaluated inside the `find` predicate for every override, for every slot, for every fixed host, although the offset depends only on the override. Over a long date range with many overrides this multiplies into a very large number of timezone conversions per getSchedule call. The override windows should be computed once per call.

title: Timezone-shifted override minutes drop the date and land on the wrong day across midnight
body: The converted override time is reduced to minute-of-day with `.hour() * 60 + .minute()` after adding the timezone offset, which discards the date. When the shifted time crosses midnight, the slot is attributed to the wrong day. Example: an override 15:00-17:00 on Jan 10 for an organizer in America/New_York (stored as 15:00Z-17:00Z) and an invitee in Asia/Kolkata. The real slots are Jan 11 01:30-03:30 IST. The day filter at line 207 selects the override using the unshifted instant, which falls on Jan 10 IST, and line 219 yields 01:30. The slot is therefore offered (or later dropped by checkIfIsAvailable) on Jan 10, and the override never appears on Jan 11. The full converted timestamp should be computed and bucketed by its own date.

title: No tests for the round-robin fixed-host override fix or for busy times on override days
body: The PR's headline fix (fixed-host date overrides constraining round-robin slots, and busy times on override days) has no test. The only added assertion is an invitee-timezone variant of an existing single-override scenario. Missing coverage: a round-robin event where a fixed host's override limits availability; an existing booking inside an override still blocking the slot (this would catch the busy-skip bug); split working hours on one weekday; two overrides on one date; and an override that shifts across midnight for an invitee timezone. The new checkIfIsAvailable logic is subtle and currently untested beyond the single happy path.

title: Migration crashes when no embed_category row matches
body: The category lookup indexes the query result with [0] and then calls ['id'] on it. When no site_settings row named embed_category has a value equal to a category name, the result is empty, [0] is nil, and ['id'] raises, aborting the migration. This is the normal state on most installs, because settings only appear in site_settings once changed. The same unguarded [0]['value'] on line 15 fails when the uncategorized_category_id row is absent, so the intended fallback can never run. Guard for empty results before indexing.

title: Migrated hosts keep scheme, path and whitespace and silently stop matching
body: Each entry from the old embeddable_hosts setting is inserted verbatim, bypassing the EmbeddableHost before_validation that strips http(s):// and paths. The old setting explicitly supported entries with a scheme (allows_embeddable_host? and its spec 'works with a http host'). record_for_host matches lower(host) against the bare hostname, so a migrated 'http://eviltrout.com' row never matches and embedding for that site stops working after upgrade. Lines split on \n also keep a trailing \r for CRLF-stored values. Normalize hostnames in the migration.

title: Host values interpolated into SQL
body: The host string is interpolated directly into an INSERT with single quotes. A stored value containing an apostrophe aborts the migration, and the value is admin-controlled input being spliced into SQL. Use bound parameters or connection.quote.

title: Irreversible data deletion with no down path
body: The DELETE of the old settings is an execute inside change, which cannot be reversed. Rolling back raises IrreversibleMigration and the deleted embeddable_hosts and embed_category values cannot be restored. Also, create_table with force: true silently drops an existing embeddable_hosts table and its rows if one exists. Move the data step into up/down and drop force: true.

title: Host regex rejects valid hosts the old setting accepted
body: The regex requires a dotted name ending in a 2-5 letter TLD. That rejects hosts on longer TLDs such as .museum, .community or .technology, and also localhost:3000 and IP addresses. The old free-text embeddable_hosts setting accepted all of these, so admins can no longer register them and local development against localhost breaks. Relax the validation or document the restriction.

title: Nil host raises NoMethodError before validation
body: If host is nil (for example a JSON request without the key, so params[:embeddable_host][:host] is nil), self.host.sub! raises NoMethodError in before_validation. The request returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard the callback with a nil check.

title: record_for_host cannot match mixed-case or port-bearing hosts
body: The query compares lower(host) in the database against the raw argument, which is never downcased. The validation regex is case-insensitive, so a host saved as 'EvilTrout.com' can never match, and an uppercase host in an embed_url or referer is rejected even for a stored lowercase host. The validation also accepts an optional :port, but uri.host never includes a port, so a host saved with a port can never match. Downcase the argument and make the port handling consistent.

title: No uniqueness on host; duplicates make category assignment arbitrary
body: Nothing prevents two rows for the same host, either at validation or in the schema. record_for_host calls .first with no ordering, so when duplicates exist with different categories, TopicEmbed.import assigns a category nondeterministically. Add a uniqueness validation and a unique index on host.

title: category_id is never checked to reference an existing category
body: category_id comes straight from request params and is only defaulted when blank. Nothing verifies that a Category with that id exists, and the model's belongs_to has no existence validation. A bogus id is saved, and TopicEmbed.import then creates topics pointing at a nonexistent category.

title: Update and destroy return 500 for an unknown id
body: EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil for an unknown id. update then calls save_host(nil), and destroy calls host.destroy, both raising NoMethodError and producing a 500 instead of a 404. save_host also fails if params[:embeddable_host] is absent.

title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding reports success but saves nothing
body: update renders the current embedding without reading any params or persisting anything. The client saveChanges action in admin-embedding.js.es6 calls embedding.update({}) against this endpoint, but no template binds it, so the code is dead and suggests edits persist when they do not. Implement the update or remove the route and action.

title: Admin controller specs only check class inheritance
body: This spec only asserts that the controller subclasses Admin::AdminController. Nothing exercises create, update or destroy, the uncategorized defaulting, validation failures, or the staff gate. The same applies to spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb. The new admin write path has no behavioral coverage.

title: 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' does not test a blank host
body: This test sets nothing up. SiteSetting.embed_truncate defaults to false and has_topic_embed? is not stubbed, so expandable_first_post? returns false whatever the host state. It passes without exercising the condition its name describes. Set embed_truncate and has_topic_embed? to true and assert false with no EmbeddableHost present.

title: Test for fruit 2 actually exercises apple
body: store.find('fruit', 2) hits the /fruits/:id fixture in create-pretender, which always returns fruits[0] (apple) and ignores the id. The assertions (two colors with ids 1 and 2) describe apple, whereas fruit 2 has color_ids [3]. The test passes but is misleading and would not catch an id-based lookup bug. Make the fixture honor the id or use id 1.

title: Unresolved ids become undefined entries; '|| []' is dead code
body: map always returns an array, so hydrated || [] never applies. Ids that cannot be resolved in the sideloaded root collection produce undefined entries in the pluralized property, which the embedding template renders as broken rows. Filter out falsy results before assigning.

title: Fabricator contents swapped with embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
body: This file now holds the :embeddable_host fabricator, while the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Fabrication loads by definition so tests still run, but the file names no longer describe their contents and someone looking for :category will open the wrong file.

title: Failed host delete is unhandled
body: destroyRecord().then(...) has no catch. A failed DELETE (permissions, 404, network) gives no feedback and leaves an unhandled promise rejection, unlike save(), which routes errors through popupAjaxError.

title: Migration crashes when no embed_category row matches
body: The query at lines 9-11 returns a PG::Result. When no row matches, `[0]` is nil and `['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the upgrade. This is the common case: embed_category only exists in site_settings if an admin set it (default ''), and the join requires it to equal an existing category name. The uncategorized fallback at lines 14-16 is only reached when the id is 0, which never happens for a real category, so the intended default is never applied. The empty result needs explicit handling, and the uncategorized_category_id lookup needs a guard too, since that setting may not be stored.

title: Legacy host entries are copied without normalization, so existing embeds silently stop matching
body: Entries from the old 'embeddable_hosts' setting are split on newlines and inserted verbatim. This bypasses EmbeddableHost's before_validation that strips http(s):// and paths. The removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? explicitly accepted entries like 'https://eviltrout.com' (its spec covered that). Such sites get rows like 'https://eviltrout.com', but record_for_host compares against the URI host, so those rows can never match and embedding breaks for them after upgrade. Blank lines and trailing carriage returns from textarea input also become bogus rows. Each entry should be normalized, or invalid ones skipped, before insert.

title: Host values interpolated into SQL without quoting
body: The host string is interpolated directly into the INSERT statement. A value containing a single quote aborts the migration with a SQL syntax error. The pattern is also an injection vector if the setting value ever becomes less trusted. Use bound parameters or connection.quote.

title: Migration is irreversible and create_table uses force: true
body: `def change` contains raw `execute` calls, which Rails cannot invert, so rolling this migration back raises ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration. Separately, `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` (line 3) silently drops an existing embeddable_hosts table and its rows if one exists. Use explicit up/down methods and drop force: true.

title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `self.host.sub!` is called unconditionally. When host is nil (for example a create/update request without the host field, or a direct API call), this raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500 instead of a validation error. The callback should guard against nil.

title: Stored hosts with a port can never match a lookup
body: The format validator explicitly allows an optional port, e.g. 'eviltrout.com:8080'. But record_for_host (line 14) looks up by URI#host, which drops the port, so a host saved with a port never matches and embedding silently fails for it. Either reject ports in validation or compare including the port.

title: Host lookup lowercases the column but not the parameter
body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the parameter. The parameter is `uri.host` taken directly from the referer or embed_url, so a request from 'http://EvilTrout.com/...' is rejected even though the host is allowed. The parameter should be downcased.

title: Duplicate hosts allowed and lookup returns an arbitrary row
body: There is no uniqueness validation or unique index on host, and the admin UI can add the same host twice. `.first` has no ORDER BY, so record_for_host returns an arbitrary row, and TopicEmbed.import will use an arbitrary category for that site. Add a case-insensitive uniqueness validation and a unique index.

title: TLD length limit rejects valid domains
body: The TLD pattern `[a-z]{2,5}` rejects valid hosts with longer TLDs such as example.community or example.technology. The setting this replaces accepted any string, so admins with such sites can no longer configure them.

title: update and destroy crash with a 500 on unknown id
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown or already-deleted id. `save_host(nil)` then raises on `nil.host=`, and destroy (line 16) raises on `nil.destroy`. A double-click on delete or a stale client gets a 500 instead of a 404. Use find or check for nil.

title: category_id is never checked against existing categories
body: The submitted category_id is only defaulted when blank. It is never checked against Category, and the column has no foreign key. A nonexistent id is stored, and TopicEmbed.import then passes it to PostCreator, creating topics in a missing category. The same happens after a category is deleted. Validate that the category exists.

title: Admin hosts controller has no behavioral tests
body: The only spec asserts that the class inherits from Admin::AdminController. Nothing exercises create, update, destroy, the uncategorized default in save_host, validation failures, the not-found path, or non-admin access. The core of the new write endpoint is untested.

title: Fabricator contents are swapped between the two files
body: category_fabricator.rb now contains only the :embeddable_host fabricator, while the category, diff_category, happy_category and private_category fabricators were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Fabrication still loads both files, but the names mislead anyone looking for the category fabricators and make the diff read as a deletion.

title: _hydrateEmbedded now rewrites every *_ids key and can leave undefined entries
body: The regex now matches every `*_ids` key in REST-serialized payloads, and the original key is deleted. When the referenced collection is not in the root payload, _lookupSubType returns undefined for each id, so the result is an array of undefined values. The `hydrated || []` fallback never runs because map always returns an array. Previously such keys were left intact, and now the id list is lost and consumers get undefined items. This matters for the new feature: EmbeddingSerializer uses `embed: :ids` without `include: true`, so the root may have no embeddable_hosts collection and the admin list would iterate undefined hosts. Unresolved ids should be filtered out, and conversion should only happen when the collection is present.

title: find embedded test passes for the wrong record
body: The test calls store.find('fruit', 2) but asserts apple's data. The /fruits/:id pretender in create-pretender.js.es6 (line 227) always returns fruits[0] regardless of the id, so the change from id 1 to 2 has no effect and the test would still pass if lookup by id were broken. The fixture should use request.params.id.

title: Stale test named for a host check that no longer exists
body: The test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' sets up no host. expandable_first_post? no longer checks hosts, and embed_truncate defaults to false, so the test passes trivially and no longer tests what its name says. It should be removed or rewritten to test the behavior that actually matters.

title: Delete has no error handling
body: delete() calls destroyRecord().then(...) with no failure handler, unlike save() which uses popupAjaxError. On a server error the row silently stays with no feedback, and the promise rejection is unhandled. A .catch(popupAjaxError) is needed.

title: Migration aborts when no embed_category row matches, which is the common case
body: The category lookup `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes at least one row. The query only matches when site_settings.embed_category holds the name of an existing category. Most installs never set that setting (its default is empty), so the result is empty, `[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The migration fails on upgrade. The intended fallback to the uncategorized category (`if category_id == 0`, line 14) can never run: it would need a matched row with id 0, and the crash happens first. The uncategorized lookup on line 15 also indexes `[0]['value']` without checking for rows.

title: Legacy host values are copied without normalization or SQL escaping
body: Values from the old embeddable_hosts setting are inserted verbatim. EmbeddableHost's before_validation strips the scheme and path, and the old allows_embeddable_host? accepted entries like 'https://example.com/1234' (it parsed them with URI). Migrated rows keep those prefixes, so EmbeddableHost.record_for_host, which compares lower(host) to a bare hostname, never matches them. Embeds for those sites silently stop working after upgrade. The value is also interpolated into SQL without escaping, so a host containing an apostrophe aborts the migration. Trailing '\r' from CRLF input is also kept. Normalize each entry (strip scheme, path, whitespace, and '\r') and use bound parameters.

title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `self.host.sub!` is called before validations run. If host is nil (for example, the admin create or update request omits embeddable_host[host]), this raises NoMethodError instead of producing a validation error. The admin controller then returns a 500 rather than a 422. The format validator on line 2 would have rejected nil cleanly, but it never runs. Guard the nil case or add a presence check before normalizing.

title: No uniqueness validation or unique index on host
body: Nothing prevents two rows with the same host, case-insensitively or otherwise. The migration adds no unique index and the model has no validates_uniqueness_of. record_for_host (line 17) calls .first with no ORDER, so if duplicates exist with different categories, the category assigned to imported topics is arbitrary. Add a case-insensitive uniqueness validation and a unique index on lower(host).

title: category_id is never checked against an existing category
body: `belongs_to :category` does not verify that category_id points to a real category, and the table has no foreign key. The admin controller passes through any integer (app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb line 24). Deleting a category, or saving a bad id, leaves a host pointing at nothing. TopicEmbed.import then passes that id to PostCreator, so new embed topics get a dangling category. Validate that the category exists.

title: _ids sideloading yields undefined entries and throws on null
body: _hydrateEmbedded now maps every *_ids array through _lookupSubType. If the referenced collection is absent from the payload, _lookupSubType returns undefined for each id, and the result is an array of undefined entries. The `hydrated || []` fallback on line 200 never applies because map always returns an array, so the undefined entries survive. The embedding template then renders a row per entry. Separately, `obj[k].map` throws when the _ids value is null. Previously *_ids keys were ignored entirely, so a single null field now breaks hydration of the whole record. Filter out missing entries and guard null before mapping.

title: Admin CRUD endpoints have no behavioral tests
body: The only spec asserts that the controller subclasses Admin::AdminController. Nothing covers create, update, or destroy; the category default to uncategorized (controller line 25); the response for an unknown id; validation failures; or the staff-only filter. embedding_controller_spec.rb has the same single inheritance assertion. A regression in the endpoints the admin UI depends on would pass CI. Add request specs for each action, including the failure paths.

title: update and destroy crash with 500 for unknown ids
body: `update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without a nil check. For a nonexistent or already-deleted id, `host.host =` (line 23) or `host.destroy` (line 16) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404. Use find (which raises RecordNotFound) or check for nil and return not_found.

title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a silent no-op
body: `update` renders the current embedding without reading params or saving anything, so the endpoint returns success while changing nothing. The client saveChanges action (admin-embedding controller) calls it with update({}), but the template has no save button, so the action is dead and the endpoint is misleading. Either implement the update or remove the route and the client action.

title: record_for_host does not downcase the input before comparing to lower(host)
body: The query is `lower(host) = ?` against the URI host, but the input is never downcased. Any mixed-case host fails to match a stored host. Callers include TopicRetriever#invalid_host?, which passes the raw embed_url param (only TopicEmbed normalizes URLs), so an embed_url with an uppercase host is treated as not embeddable and never retrieved. Downcase the host before the lookup.

title: Hosts saved with a port can never match
body: The format validator on line 2 explicitly allows an optional :port, and before_validation keeps it. But record_for_host compares against uri.host, which never includes a port. An entry like example.com:8080 is accepted by validation and can never match a referer or embed_url. Either reject ports in validation or compare host and port together.

title: Host validation rejects TLDs longer than five letters
body: The regex requires the TLD to be `[a-z]{2,5}`. That rejects valid hosts such as example.technology, example.community, or example.international, and any host without a dotted TLD such as localhost. This is a new validator on a new table, so it blocks legitimate entries that the old free-text setting accepted.

title: Feed-imported topics lose their category, with no default left to configure
body: Previously every imported post was placed in SiteSetting.embed_category. That setting is removed here (site_settings.yml, server.en.yml, and the migration's DELETE). TopicEmbed.import now takes the category only from a matching EmbeddableHost. import is also reached from feed polling and import_remote, which do no host check. Feed-imported topics whose URL host is not registered silently land in the uncategorized category, and no admin setting remains to define a default. This is a behavior regression that should be called out or handled.

title: Failed host deletion gives no feedback
body: delete() calls destroyRecord().then(...) with no catch. Every other request in this component uses popupAjaxError (see save on line 40). If the delete fails (for example a 403 or 500), the promise rejection is unhandled, the user sees nothing, and the row stays in the list. Add .catch(popupAjaxError).

title: Test named for embeddable host checks behavior that no longer exists
body: expandable_first_post? no longer reads embeddable hosts, so the test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' passes only because the built topic has no TopicEmbed row (has_topic_embed? is false for an unsaved topic). It does not exercise host presence at all, and no test replaces the old 'hosts disabled' coverage. The nested describe on the following lines is also misspelled ('emeddable').

title: find embedded test changed to id 2, but the fixture always returns fruit 1
body: The test now calls store.find('fruit', 2), but the /fruits/:id pretender route in create-pretender always returns fruits[0] (apple, id 1), ignoring the id. The assertions therefore check apple's colors. Changing the id suggests coverage of the banana record (color_ids [3]) that does not exist. Either make the fixture honor the id or revert the id to 1.

title: Fabricator definitions are swapped between the two files
body: category_fabricator.rb now defines :embeddable_host, and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb holds the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category, and :private_category fabricators. Fabrication loads every file, so specs still run. But the names are wrong: anyone looking for the category fabricators, or for the host fabricator, will open the wrong file, and the history of category_fabricator.rb is muddled. Swap the contents back so each file matches its name.

title: Second `downsize` definition silently overrides the width/height overload
body: The file now defines `self.downsize` twice: line 145 `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and line 149 `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the later definition replaces the earlier one, so the 5-argument form is dead code and calls that pass width and height break. A call like `downsize(from, to, 100, 100)` now binds `dimensions=100` and `opts=100`, and `opts[:allow_animation]` in `optimize` raises TypeError. A call with options raises ArgumentError because the arity is now 3..4. The removal of the `dimensions` helper is a further change to the public surface. Any existing caller using the old signature breaks. Keep one overload that accepts both forms, or update all callers and document the change.

title: Animated GIFs over the limit are flattened to their first frame when animation is disabled
body: The downsize call passes `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`. When that setting is off, `optimize` uses `downsize_instructions`, which reads `#{from}[0]` (optimized_image.rb line 129) and writes a single frame back over the uploaded file. An animated GIF larger than max_image_size_kb is therefore silently replaced with a static image. The setting governs thumbnails, not the user's original upload, so this destroys user content.

title: Animated downsize passes a percentage to gifsicle, which rejects it
body: `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which emits `--resize-fit 80%`. gifsicle's `--resize-fit` accepts only a WxH geometry, not a percentage. For GIFs with animation enabled, the conversion exits non-zero, `convert_with` returns false, and the GIF is never reduced. The controller loop then retries five times with no effect.

title: Return value of downsize is ignored; failures are silent and the loop retries blindly
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false when convert fails (`convert_with` returns false on a non-zero exit without logging). The loop ignores that result and decrements `attempt` regardless. A persistently failing conversion runs five times and then falls through to `Upload.create_for` with the original oversized file, with no log entry or error for the user. The comment 'automatically reduced to allowed size' is also inaccurate: a fixed 80% step over five attempts does not guarantee the file ends under max_image_size_kb.

title: Up to five full ImageMagick and ImageOptim passes run inline in the request
body: Each loop iteration runs a full `convert` and then `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` on the file. For a large photo that is several heavy external process runs. The synchronous API path (`render json: data.as_json` after `create_upload`) performs all of them inside the web request, which risks timeouts and ties up a worker. The reduction could instead be computed from the size ratio and done in one pass, or moved into the deferred job.

title: Remote download cap hard-coded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
body: The URL download limit changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb to a fixed 10.megabytes. Non-image attachments fetched by URL through the API can now be up to 10MB regardless of max_attachment_size_kb, and the admin-configured image limit no longer applies to downloads. Conversely, images over 10MB cannot be fetched by URL at all, which undercuts the stated goal of accepting large images. A failed download is still swallowed by `rescue nil`, so the user gets no clear error.

title: Client-side size check ignores per-type site settings and always uses 10MB
body: `validateUploadedFile` previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. It now hard-codes 10MB for every upload type, so max_attachment_size_kb is ignored client-side. Attachments above the configured limit pass validation, upload, and only fail on the server, and the user sees a message claiming a 10MB limit. The same hard-coded value at line 246 in `displayErrorForUpload` makes the 413 message show 10MB whatever the server actually accepts.

title: SVG files that exceed the limit are run through the raster downsize path
body: The condition uses FileHelper.is_image?, which covers svg (the client's isAnImage does too). `create_for` in optimized_image.rb special-cases .svg because it cannot be resized, but this loop has no such exclusion. An oversized SVG would be rewritten by ImageMagick, which rasterizes or corrupts the vector data, rather than being left alone or rejected.

title: No specs for the new downsizing path or the changed OptimizedImage signatures
body: The PR adds a downsize loop to the upload path, changes the OptimizedImage.downsize/optimize signatures, removes the dimensions helper, and changes limits in the client and the download path. No spec covers any of it. A single spec calling OptimizedImage.downsize with width and height would have exposed the duplicate method definition, and a spec on an animated GIF would have exposed the flattening and gifsicle issues.

title: Second `downsize` definition silently replaces the (from, to, max_width, max_height) version
body: The PR adds `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` but leaves the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 in place. Ruby does not overload by arity, so the later definition replaces the earlier one and the 4-argument form becomes dead. Any caller that passes width and height separately now fails: `downsize(src, dst, 500, 500, force_aspect_ratio: true)` raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), and `downsize(src, dst, 500, 500)` passes 500 as `opts`, so `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` fails with a TypeError. Either remove the old method and migrate its callers, or keep a single definition that accepts both forms.

title: Downsize loop ignores failures and never verifies the final size before uploading
body: The loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize at most five times and then continues to Upload.create_for with whatever is in tempfile. Two problems. First, nothing re-checks tempfile.size against max_image_size_kb after the loop, so an image that is still over the limit is stored. Each pass scales both dimensions by 0.8 (pixel count by 0.64), so five passes leave about 11% of the original pixels, which is not enough for a large original. Second, downsize returns false when convert exits non-zero (convert_with does not log that case), and the return value is discarded. A failing conversion is retried five times on an unchanged file and the failure is invisible. On this path nothing enforces max_image_size_kb for uploaded images any more.

title: API URL downloads are now capped at a hardcoded 10 MB instead of max_image_size_kb
body: The download cap changes from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a hardcoded 10.megabytes. Consequences: (a) a site that sets max_image_size_kb above 10 MB can no longer fetch images between 10 MB and its own limit through the API URL path, which contradicts the setting; (b) the new downsizing cannot help images above 10 MB fetched by URL, which is the case the feature is for; (c) when FileHelper.download fails or exceeds the cap, the `rescue nil` leaves tempfile nil, and line 72 then calls `tempfile.size` on nil and raises NoMethodError, giving a 500 rather than a validation error. The 10 MB value is also duplicated in utilities.js with no shared source.

title: Client-side size limit replaced with hardcoded 10 MB for images and attachments, ignoring site settings
body: The `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` lookup is replaced by a hardcoded 10 MB for every upload type. Consequences: images larger than max_image_size_kb now pass client validation up to 10 MB, and an admin who sets max_image_size_kb above 10 MB can never upload between 10 MB and that limit from the UI, so the setting above 10 MB has no effect. Attachments are now checked against 10 MB instead of max_attachment_size_kb, so attachments the admin has forbidden pass client validation. The 413 branch (line 246) also now always reports '10 MB' regardless of configuration. If the goal is to let large images through for server-side shrinking, only the image limit should change, and attachments should keep using their setting.

title: Up to five ImageMagick and ImageOptim passes per oversized upload, run inline on the synchronous API path
body: Each loop iteration runs a full convert pass, and convert_with also runs ImageOptim.new.optimize_image! on the output, so an oversized upload can cost five decode/encode cycles plus five optimizer runs. On the synchronous API path (`synchronous` param) this runs inline in the request and blocks the web worker for the duration. This code does not bound the input size: the client-side check is browser-only, the URL path cap is 10 MB, and the multipart path has no size check in this diff. A very large image makes every pass expensive.

title: Downsizing writes in place to the uploaded file, so a failed pass can corrupt the only copy
body: OptimizedImage.downsize is called with the same path as input and output, so ImageMagick overwrites the uploaded file in place. If a pass fails partway (disk full, process killed, ImageMagick error during write), the file is left truncated or corrupt. Because the return value is ignored (see the loop above), the damaged file is then passed to Upload.create_for. Writing to a separate temp file and replacing the original only on success would avoid this.

title: Oversized animated GIFs are flattened to their first frame when allow_animated_thumbnails is off
body: The loop reuses the thumbnail setting `allow_animated_thumbnails` for the user's original upload. When that setting is off, OptimizedImage.optimize uses downsize_instructions, which reads `#{from}[0]`, so an oversized animated GIF is replaced by a static first frame. The animation is lost permanently in the stored upload, and the user is not told. This may be intended, but it is not documented or surfaced anywhere in the PR.

title: No specs for the changed downsize/optimize signatures or the new upload downsizing path
body: The PR changes the signatures of optimize, resize and downsize, removes the public OptimizedImage.dimensions helper, and adds a loop in UploadsController#create_upload. No spec changes accompany any of this. A single spec calling downsize with width and height would have caught the duplicate-definition bug, and nothing covers the '80%' percentage path, the loop's termination, or the behaviour when convert fails.

title: Second downsize definition silently replaces the width/height overload and breaks its callers
body: This adds a second 'def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})' directly after the existing 'downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})'. In Ruby the later definition replaces the earlier one, so the width/height form no longer exists. Any caller passing five arguments now gets ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). The diff also deletes the public 'OptimizedImage.dimensions(width, height)' helper and changes the positional signature of 'optimize'; any caller of those breaks too. Keep a single 'downsize' that accepts both forms, or update the existing callers and make the change explicit.

title: Request-controlled 'type' ends up unquoted in a shell command via the tempfile name
body: For API URL uploads, the tempfile is created at line 55 with the name prefix 'discourse-upload-#{type}', where 'type' is the unvalidated params.require(:type) value. The new code passes tempfile.path to OptimizedImage.downsize, and convert_with (optimized_image.rb, around line 161) joins the instructions and runs them through backticks with the path unquoted. A 'type' containing shell metacharacters such as $(...), backticks, or ';' therefore becomes executed shell code. This is reached when an API caller uploads an image by URL that is larger than max_image_size_kb. It needs an API key, but it is still command execution that did not exist before this PR. Validate 'type', and pass arguments to the external process as an argv array (system, Open3) instead of a shell string.

title: Oversized images are uploaded anyway when downsizing fails or stalls
body: The loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize up to five times and ignores its return value. convert_with returns false (and swallows exceptions) on any failure, such as a missing binary, an unsupported format, or a corrupt file. After the loop there is no re-check of the size, so an image that is still above max_image_size_kb is passed to Upload.create_for as-is. The site's hard limit is therefore no longer enforced on the server. The input and output are also the same path, so a failed or partially written conversion overwrites the user's file with truncated data, and the next pass works on that damaged file. Check the result of each pass, stop on failure, and reject the upload if it is still over the limit.

title: Client size limit hard-coded to 10 MB, ignoring the per-type site settings
body: The size check used to read Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. It now uses a constant 10 MB for every upload type, so admin-configured limits for attachments and images are ignored in the browser. Users can attempt uploads the site was configured to reject, and the 'file too large' message reports 10240 KB even when the configured limit is lower. The 413 handler at line 246 has the same problem: it replaced the max_image_size_kb setting with the constant. The 'type' argument is no longer used for the size check at all.

title: URL download cap is now a fixed 10 MB, decoupled from max_image_size_kb
body: The download limit for API URL uploads changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to 10.megabytes. Two consequences. First, non-image files fetched by URL can now be up to 10 MB regardless of the admin's limit. Second, if an admin raises max_image_size_kb above 10 MB, images between 10 MB and the new limit are rejected at download time (the rescue nil turns the failure into a nil tempfile), which is the opposite of what the feature is meant to allow. Derive the download cap from the setting, or justify the constant.

title: Animated-GIF detection depends on the tempfile path, so animated GIFs get flattened
body: The animated branch in optimize is chosen by matching the GIF extension against 'from', which is the request tempfile path. Rack multipart tempfiles are typically created without the original extension, so the check fails for uploaded GIFs even when allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled. downsize_instructions then uses '#{from}[0]', which keeps only the first frame. The result is that an oversized animated GIF is silently reduced to a still image on upload. Determine animation from the original filename or from the file contents, and pass that decision explicitly.

title: New downsizing behavior and changed limits have no tests, and the PR description is a placeholder
body: The PR adds a server-side loop that rewrites uploaded files, changes the public OptimizedImage downsize/optimize API, and replaces the download and client size limits with constants. No specs were added or updated. The description is just 'Test 1'. Nothing covers an image above the limit being reduced below it, the loop giving up after five attempts, a failed convert, the GIF branch, or the duplicate downsize signature (which a spec calling the width/height form would have caught).

title: Synchronous API uploads run up to five full convert and optimize passes in the request
body: For synchronous API uploads, the request thread now performs up to five ImageMagick conversions, each followed by ImageOptim.optimize_image! (which runs several external optimizers), on an image up to the 10 MB download cap, before responding. Each pass rewrites the whole file. A single pass with a scale factor computed from the size ratio, or moving the reduction into the deferred job, would avoid this cost.

title: track_visit! stores the topic id as user_id when given a plain user id
body: In `track_visit!(topic, user)`, the fallback is `user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic`, which uses `topic` where `user` is meant. The caller in TopicsController#track_visit_to_topic passes an integer (`TopicUser.track_visit! topic_id, user_id`), so `user_id` silently becomes the topic id. The visit timestamp is then written to whichever TopicUser row has user_id equal to the topic id (another user's row), or a bogus TopicUser row is inserted for that wrong user. The real visitor's last_visited_at is never updated. This is pre-existing, but the method is touched by this PR and the bug directly affects the visit tracking the feature relies on.

title: Unsubscribe writes notification_level directly, so the mute is reverted on the next read
body: `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which normally sets `notifications_reason_id` to `user_changed` and `notifications_changed_at`, and publishes the MessageBus `notification_level_change`. Because the reason stays nil, `TopicUser.update_last_read` (its CASE clause checks `tu.notifications_reason_id is null` and total_msecs_viewed over the auto-track threshold) will set notification_level back to tracking the next time the user reads the topic. The unsubscribe is therefore undone silently for most rows. Using `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)` would avoid this and keep open browser sessions in sync.

title: Unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row
body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id:, topic_id:)` can return nil, for example when a logged-in user opens the unsubscribe URL for a public topic they can see but never read or were never notified about. The next line dereferences `tu.notification_level`, producing a 500 instead of a sensible response. Nil should be handled, for example by creating the record through `TopicUser.change` or by redirecting.

title: Unsubscribe changes state on a GET request
body: The action mutates the user's notification level but is routed as GET (routes.rb `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`). Email link scanners and link-preview prefetchers that follow URLs in mail will silently mute topics for recipients. Because Rails forgery protection does not cover GET, any page that can embed the URL can also mute topics for a logged-in user. A POST (or a confirmation step) is the usual safeguard for state-changing unsubscribe links.

title: Unsubscribe lowers watching/tracking topics only to regular, contradicting the message shown
body: For a topic at tracking or watching, the code sets notification_level to regular rather than muted. Regular still notifies on replies and mentions, yet the page (client.en.yml `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications`) says "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>". For a watching topic the user keeps receiving reply and mention notifications after clicking. The toggle-like branching (regular goes to muted, anything above goes to regular) is also undocumented and hard to reason about. Either the behaviour should always mute, or the message should describe the actual new level.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires an unsubscribe_url interpolation argument
body: The `unsubscribe_link` string now contains `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will make `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` in MessageBuilder#body and #html_part raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument, which fails sending the email. The only in-repo caller (send_notification_email) now passes the value, but plugins or other code paths using the existing `add_unsubscribe_link` option break. The option needs a default, or the template should be guarded.

title: New unsubscribe endpoint has no specs
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe adds login enforcement, slug redirects, notification-level toggling, a persistence call and a new render path, but no controller or request spec covers any of it. The notification-level branching, the 301 redirect for mismatched slugs, the behaviour for a missing TopicUser, and the persisted state after the call are all untested. Given the bugs above, a spec would have caught at least the nil-record and reverted-mute problems.

title: Spec passes unsubscribe_url but never checks that the topic unsubscribe link is rendered
body: The `add_unsubscribe_link: true` context now passes `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"`, but the only body assertion checks for the user preferences URL. Nothing verifies that the per-topic unsubscribe link appears in the body or html_part, so a regression that drops `%{unsubscribe_url}` from the template or the interpolation would go unnoticed.

title: Unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when the user has no topic_users row
body: Line 105 does `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])`, which returns nil when the logged-in user has no row for this topic (they never visited or read it, or the link was opened while logged in as an account with no relation to the topic). Line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level` and raises NoMethodError, producing a 500. Use `TopicUser.change` (which creates the row when missing) or handle the nil case explicitly.

title: tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change and can be silently undone by auto-tracking
body: The notification level is written with a direct `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change(...)`. `change` sets `notifications_reason_id` (user_changed) and `notifications_changed_at`; this path sets neither and publishes no MessageBus `notification_level_change`. Consequence: when `notifications_reason_id` is NULL (common for rows created by reading, via the INSERT in `update_last_read`), `TopicUser.update_last_read` sets the level back to tracking once enough reading time accumulates, and `TopicUser.auto_track` does the same on new posts. The user's unsubscribe is silently reverted. Fix by calling `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)`.

title: Unsubscribe leaves watching/tracking users at 'regular', which still sends reply and mention emails
body: The toggle sets watching/tracking topics to `regular` and only sets `muted` when the level is already `regular` or lower. `regular` still generates reply, quote and mention notifications and emails, so a user who clicks the one-click unsubscribe link on a watched or tracked topic keeps receiving email for that topic. The new page text (`topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications`: 'You will stop receiving notifications for ...') is therefore false for those users, and they need a second click. The action should mute the topic from any level, or the copy must change.

title: State-changing action exposed over GET and authenticated only by session cookie
body: `unsubscribe` changes the user's notification level on a GET request (routes.rb lines 440-441). Rails CSRF protection does not cover GET, so any cross-site GET to `/t/:id/unsubscribe` (for example an `` or link) performs the change for a logged-in visitor, and link prefetchers that carry the session do the same. Use a POST from a confirmation page, or a signed per-user token like the existing `email/unsubscribe/:key` flow.

title: Email unsubscribe link carries no recipient identity; it acts on whichever session is logged in
body: The per-topic unsubscribe link in the email contains only the topic path, with no token identifying the recipient. The action uses `current_user` only. Consequences: (a) a recipient who is not logged in is redirected to login by `ensure_logged_in`, and the unsubscribe intent is lost, which is the common case for email clicks; (b) if the browser is logged in as a different account, that account's topic setting is changed while the actual recipient stays subscribed. The existing `email/unsubscribe/:key` route avoids this with a signed key; the topic link should do the same.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires :unsubscribe_url; other callers with add_unsubscribe_link will raise
body: `server.en.yml` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}` in `unsubscribe_link`. This line (and the same key in `body`, line 90) passes `template_args`, which only contains `unsubscribe_url` if the caller supplied it. Any caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` (only `send_notification_email` is updated in this PR; plugins or other mailers may call it too) will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` while building the email. Either default the value in `MessageBuilder` or guard the interpolation.

title: No specs for the new unsubscribe action, Topic#unsubscribe_url, or the topic link in emails
body: The new `unsubscribe` action has no controller spec. Untested paths include: the nil TopicUser case, the level transitions (regular to muted, tracking to regular), the login requirement, the slug-mismatch 301 redirect, and the rendered page. `Topic#unsubscribe_url` is untested. The only spec change adds an `unsubscribe_url:` argument to an existing test that checks only that the List-Unsubscribe header is present; no test checks that the email body contains the topic-specific link.

title: Unrelated route reordering and removed constraints bundled into the feature
body: The diff reorders the `moderator-liked` and `summary` routes and removes `post_number: /\d+/` from both `summary` routes. None of this is needed for the unsubscribe feature and the PR does not explain it. Dropping constraints from existing routes can change which requests match, so it should be split out or justified.

title: Top-level topicUnsubscribe route paired with a nested-style template path
body: The route is declared at top level as `topicUnsubscribe`, but its template is `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, the name a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route would use. Ember resolves a route's template from its route name, so this template may not be picked up and the page could render without its content. Worth verifying in the browser, or setting `templateName` explicitly.

title: Unsubscribe writes notification_level directly, so auto-tracking can silently undo it
body: `tu.save!` changes notification_level without going through `TopicUser.change`. `TopicUser.change` also sets `notifications_reason_id` (user_changed) and `notifications_changed_at`, and publishes the change on MessageBus. Here the reason stays NULL for any topic whose level the user never explicitly set. `TopicUser.update_last_read` (the CASE expression in topic_user.rb) and `TopicUser.auto_track` both switch a topic to tracking when `notifications_reason_id IS NULL` and the user's viewing time passes the auto-track threshold. So after a user clicks the unsubscribe link and the topic is muted, the next read can flip it back to tracking, and the promise in the email to stop notifications is silently broken. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)` instead.

title: State-changing unsubscribe is exposed on GET with no CSRF protection
body: The action mutates notification_level, but it is reachable via GET (config/routes.rb: `get 't/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe'` and `get 't/:topic_id/unsubscribe'`). Rails' forgery protection does not cover GET, so any page that embeds the URL (for example an img tag on another site) will mute a logged-in user's topic. Mail link scanners and prefetchers will also trigger the mutation without the user clicking. A state change like this should be a POST (with a GET confirmation page), or should use a signed token like the existing email/unsubscribe/:key flow.

title: Nil TopicUser dereference when no membership row exists
body: `TopicUser.find_by` can return nil (for example if the row was never created or was removed), and `tu.notification_level` is then called without a guard, which raises NoMethodError and returns a 500. Using `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row when it is missing, would avoid this and also fix the persistence problem noted for the save! call.

title: Unsubscribe only steps watching/tracking down to regular, contradicting the email text
body: The email copy says 'You will stop receiving notifications for <title>', but for users at tracking or watching the action sets notification_level to regular. Regular still sends notifications for replies and mentions, so those users keep getting notified. Only users already at regular are muted. Either mute for every level or change the wording.

title: track_visit! uses the topic id as the user id when given an integer user id
body: `user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic` falls back to `topic`, which is the topic id, instead of `user`. TopicsController calls `TopicUser.track_visit! topic_id, user_id` with integer ids, so `user_id` becomes the topic id. The update then hits (or creates) the topic_users row for whichever user has the same id as the topic, and the real user's last_visited_at is never recorded. This predates the PR, but the PR edits this same method (line 125), so the fix belongs in this change.

title: add_unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url or email building raises
body: The unsubscribe_link string now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}. html_part (line 67) and body (line 90) call I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args), and template_args only contains unsubscribe_url if the caller passed it. Any caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without unsubscribe_url, including plugins that use this public builder, will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument while building the email. Either default the URL in the builder or render the topic line only when the URL is present.

title: Unrelated summary route constraint silently removed
body: The diff rewrites the summary routes and drops `post_number: /<digits>/` from their constraints (both `t/:slug/:topic_id/summary` and `t/:topic_id/summary`). The unsubscribe feature has nothing to do with summary URLs, and the change is not mentioned. Either revert it or explain why it is safe, since the constraint's effect on a route with no post_number segment is not obvious.

title: Route name and template path do not match, so the unsubscribe template may never render
body: The route is declared as a top-level `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', ...)`. Ember derives the default template name from the route name (topicUnsubscribe, or topic-unsubscribe), not from the path topic/unsubscribe, so the new templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs is likely not the template used for this route. The page could render blank or fall back to the application template. Either rename the template to match the route or nest the route under the topic resource as this.route('unsubscribe'). I have not verified the resolver behavior in the running app.

title: New unsubscribe action has no specs
body: Nothing covers the new action: the logged-out redirect, the 301 slug redirect that must happen before any state change, the notification_level transitions (tracking or watching to regular, regular to muted), or a missing TopicUser row. The message_builder_spec change only passes an extra argument and does not assert that the link appears in the body or HTML. A spec that re-reads the topic_user row after unsubscribe would have caught the auto-track persistence bug.

title: Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive, so a case variant of a blocked address gets through
body: `should_block?` looks up `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` using the raw value. Nothing normalizes the address before the lookup: `User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` as typed and `User` has no downcasing callback. An entry for `spammer@spamclub.com` therefore does not match a signup with `Spammer@SpamClub.com`, and the spammer can register anyway. The existing domain restrictions in the same validator use a case-insensitive regex, so they are not affected. The uniqueness validation on `BlockedEmail#email` is also case-sensitive, so case-variant duplicate entries can be created. Normalize with `Email.downcase` on both the stored value and the lookup input, or match case-insensitively.

title: Validation has a side effect that inflates match_count on every valid? call
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` increments `match_count` and saves the record each time it runs. It runs on every validation of a changed email. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` (line 168) and then `user.save` (line 172), which validates again, so one blocked signup attempt is counted twice. The statistic is wrong, and any other `valid?` call also inflates it. Record matches in an explicit step outside the validator, and keep the validator read-only.

title: Whitelist regex is unanchored, so suffix-extended domains pass the whitelist
body: The whitelist check builds `/@(gmail\.com)/i` with no end anchor. An address such as `attacker@gmail.com.evil.example` matches and passes a `gmail.com` whitelist. The code was carried over from `User#email_in_restriction_setting?`, but it now lives in a new validator and the whitelist is an access-control policy. Anchor the domain (for example `/@(domain)$/i` after escaping) and compare the domain part exactly. The domain strings are also interpolated into the regex without `Regexp.escape`.

title: match_count is a non-atomic read-modify-write that loses concurrent increments
body: `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save` reads the count, adds one in Ruby, and writes it back. Two concurrent signups matching the same entry can both write the same value, so the count is undercounted. The full `save` also re-runs validations, including a uniqueness query, for what is a counter bump. Use an atomic database update such as `BlockedEmail.update_counters` or `update_all` with `match_count = match_count + 1`.

title: Client caches server email rejections for the session and never re-checks them
body: Any server error on `email` pushes the address into `rejectedEmails`, which is a controller-lifetime array. Later the client treats that address as invalid without asking the server. If an admin later removes the block or changes the whitelist, the user is still blocked in the browser until a reload. The client also overrides the server's specific message with the generic `user.email.invalid` text. The server should stay the only authority on blocked addresses, so keep the rejection only for the current form submission or drop the client-side check.

title: Specs stub out the blocklist lookup, so the real behavior is untested
body: Both examples stub `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, so the tests never touch the database or the normalization path. Nothing covers case variants of a blocked address, which is the bypass above. Nothing checks that a blocked signup through `User`/`UsersController` is rejected, or that a single attempt increments `match_count` only once, which is the double-count above. The uniqueness and case behavior of `BlockedEmail` are also untested. Add an integration-level spec that creates a blocked entry, attempts signup with a case-variant address, and asserts the rejection and the count.

title: Blocklist match counter is inflated because the check writes from inside validation
body: `should_block?` increments `match_count` and saves the row, but it is called from `EmailValidator#validate_each`, which runs on every `valid?` or `save` of a User whose email changed. In `UsersController#create` the code calls `user.valid?` (line ~168) and then `user.save` (line ~172), so one blocked signup attempt increments `match_count` twice, and any other validation call adds more. The statistic therefore does not reflect the number of blocked attempts. Also, a validator that mutates blocklist state couples every model using `validates :email, email: true` to that side effect. Record the match once in the controller or a single save path, and keep validation read-only.

title: Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive, so case variants bypass a blocked address
body: `should_block?` does `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`, an exact, case-sensitive match. Nothing normalizes the address first: `User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` verbatim, and the domain restriction in the same validator is case-insensitive (`Regexp.new(..., true)`). If 'spam@example.com' is blocked, a signup with 'Spam@Example.com' passes validation and is stored. The unique index on blocked_emails is also case-sensitive, so case variants can coexist as separate entries. Normalize both the stored value and the lookup key (for example with Email.downcase, which the codebase already uses for lookups).

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write loses match_count increments under concurrency
body: `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save` reads the count into Ruby, increments it, and writes it back. Two concurrent signup attempts that read the same value both write value+1, so an increment is lost. `save` also reruns validations, including the uniqueness query, just to bump a counter. Use an atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])` or `update_counters`.

title: rejectedEmails is never cleared, so any server email error blocks that address until reload
body: Every response with `errors.email` pushes the address into `rejectedEmails`, and `emailValidation` then fails that exact address (line 69) for the controller's lifetime. That includes errors that are not about the blocklist, such as 'has already been taken'. The field then shows the generic `user.email.invalid` reason for an address that is well-formed but registered, and submit stays disabled for it even if the server-side condition changes (for example, an admin removes the blocklist entry). Consider clearing the list when the email changes or limiting it to the blocked-email error.

title: New errors and values keys in the failed-signup response have no spec
body: The failed-create JSON now includes `errors` and `values`, and the new client code depends on that shape (`result.errors.email && result.values`). No request or controller spec in this PR checks these keys, so renaming or dropping them would silently break the rejected-email handling in the frontend.

title: Moved domain whitelist/blacklist logic and the real blocklist path are untested here
body: The whitelist and blacklist checks were moved from User into EmailValidator in this PR, but this spec only covers the blocked-email branch, and it stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, so the real lookup is never exercised. Nothing in this PR checks the domain restrictions through the new validator, the short-circuit (no blocklist lookup once a domain error is added), or case-insensitive matching. Regressions in the moved logic or the case-sensitivity issue would not be caught by these specs.

title: Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive, so changing the case of an address bypasses it
body: should_block? does BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with no normalization, and EmailValidator passes the raw submitted value. A blocked entry 'bad@spamclub.com' does not match 'Bad@spamclub.com', and the unique index on blocked_emails.email is also case-sensitive, so rows differing only by case can coexist and .first picks one arbitrarily. Anyone blocked can register again by changing the case of any letter. The codebase already has Email.downcase (used in users_controller#change_email and User.find_by_username_or_email), so both the stored value and the lookup should be normalized the same way.

title: Validation side effect increments match_count on every valid? call, so one signup counts twice
body: should_block? writes to the database (match_count += 1, last_match_at, save) and it runs inside the User email validator. Every valid? call counts as a match. UsersController#create calls user.valid? (line 168) and then user.save (line 172), which runs validations again, so one blocked signup attempt increments match_count by 2 and the statistics the spec describes as 'whether those emails have ever been blocked' are inflated. Any other valid? call, such as a form or preview check, also counts. The counter should be incremented once per blocked attempt (for example in the controller or a dedicated check), not as a side effect of validation.

title: match_count is updated with a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: record.match_count += 1 followed by record.save reads the current value and writes back the incremented one. Two concurrent signups for the same blocked address can both read N and both write N+1, losing an increment. Use an atomic update (for example BlockedEmail.update_counters(record.id, match_count: 1) or a SQL increment) together with the last_match_at update.

title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored, so it matches addresses where the domain is only a substring
body: Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) matches the domain anywhere after an '@'. With a whitelist containing gmail.com, an address like x@gmail.com.attacker.net satisfies the check and passes, which defeats the whitelist. With a blacklist containing spamclub.com, a@spamclub.com.example.org is also rejected. This logic was moved here verbatim from User, but this PR rewrites it into a new validator and it is a security control, so the pattern should be anchored to the end of the address (for example matching '@domain' followed by end of string, case-insensitively).

title: Any server email error marks the address as rejected and then shows a generic 'is invalid' reason
body: The new branch adds result.values.email to rejectedEmails for any result.errors.email, including 'has already been taken' and 'is not allowed from that email provider'. emailValidation then returns the fixed reason I18n 'user.email.invalid' (lines 69-73) for that address, so the field says 'is invalid' even when the address is valid and was rejected for another reason. The flash message shows the server reason, but the field and the form state contradict it, which is misleading to the user.

title: Validator spec stubs the blocklist, so no test exercises the real blocking path or the moved domain rules
body: Both examples stub BlockedEmail.should_block?, so the table, the case-sensitivity behavior, and the match_count side effect are never exercised here. Nothing verifies that a User with a blocked address fails validation, that a case variant is blocked, or that the whitelist/blacklist branches, which this file now owns, still behave as before. The double-counting issue would also go unnoticed. Add a spec that creates a BlockedEmail record and checks User validity end to end, including a case variant and a count-after-valid? expectation.

title: Unescaped embed URL interpolated into stored raw HTML footer enables stored XSS
body: The footer is built as `#{url}` with the URL unescaped, and the result is saved as a raw_html post. `Post#cook` returns raw for raw_html posts and nothing sanitizes it, so any quote in the URL breaks out of the attribute. The URL reaches this code from the `embed_url` query parameter of `/embed/best` via TopicRetriever, which only checks the host. A URL such as `http:///?x='onmouseover='alert(1)` passes URI parsing (apostrophes and `=` are legal in the query), and the remote returns 200 for any existing path. An anonymous visitor can therefore plant an event handler in a topic that every reader, including forum users on the Discourse origin, will execute. Escape the URL (e.g. CGI.escapeHTML / ERB::Util.html_escape) in both the attribute and the text, or build the link with Nokogiri.

title: raw_html cook method permanently disables sanitization for every later edit
body: `cook` returns the raw string whenever cook_method is raw_html, and before_save re-cooks on every update. Nothing resets cook_method, so any edit to an imported post, by any editor, is stored as cooked HTML with no PrettyText sanitization and with the `after_post_cook` plugin filters skipped. The flag was meant for trusted feed/readability imports but is not scoped to the import path. Restrict raw_html to creation by the importer, or re-cook through PrettyText on updates.

title: Retrieval throttle keyed on the full URL can be bypassed to amplify remote fetches
body: The 60-second throttle key is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`, which includes the query string. Anonymous visitors can vary the query on each request and get a fresh key every time, so each request triggers an outbound fetch of the embeddable host. With feed polling enabled, each job also runs a full RSS poll and re-imports every feed item. EmbedController enqueues `retrieve_topic` for any embed_url before the host is validated (embed_controller.rb line 15), so garbage URLs also create jobs. Validate the host in the controller before enqueueing, and throttle per host or per normalized URL.

title: Post-commit jobs and publishes run inside the outer Topic.transaction
body: TopicEmbed.import wraps PostCreator.create in Topic.transaction.
