PostCreator#create calls enqueue_jobs (process_post, feature_topic_users) and publishes to MessageBus and TopicTrackingState before the outer transaction commits. PostCreator's own comment says jobs must be enqueued after commit. A Sidekiq worker can therefore run process_post before the post is visible. Separately, the check-then-create (`TopicEmbed.where(...).first` then `create!`) races with a concurrent import of the same URL (feed poll vs. retrieve_topic). The unique index blocks the duplicate row, but the RecordNotUnique error is unhandled and the rolled-back topic has already been announced. Move the import outside the enclosing transaction or defer enqueues with after_commit, and rescue the unique violation.

title: Scheme check uses ^ which matches at any line start
body: `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` passes if any line of the string starts with http(s)://, so `"javascript:alert(1)\nhttp://x"` is accepted. The value is then written into the footer href and stored as embed_url. Use `\A` (and the same change in PollFeed's `url !~` check, poll_feed.rb line 33).

title: Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten into broken same-site paths
body: `href.start_with?('/')` is true for protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png`. The `sub(/^\/+/, '')` then strips both slashes, producing `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png`. The same applies to img src (line 71). The comment says relative URLs are converted, but only root-relative paths are handled. Protocol-relative URLs should get only the scheme prefixed.

title: Remote fetch has no timeout and reads the whole body into memory
body: `open(url).read` uses open-uri defaults with no open or read timeout and no size cap. A slow or hanging embeddable host blocks the Sidekiq worker indefinitely, and a very large response is loaded entirely into memory. Set open_timeout and read_timeout and limit the body size.

title: A feed item without content aborts the whole poll; String#scrub needs Ruby 2.1+
body: `i.content` is nil when an RSS item has no content element, so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError. The loop stops, so the remaining items are never imported. PollFeed sets `retry: false`, so the hourly job just fails until the feed changes. TopicRetriever calls the same code, so one bad item also fails an unrelated visitor's retrieval. In addition, String#scrub only exists on Ruby 2.1+, so on older Rubies this line fails for every item. Guard nil content (and nil title) and skip or fall back per item.

title: Kernel#open used on an unvalidated admin-set URL
body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` calls Kernel#open. feed_polling_url has no URL validation. On Ruby versions before 3.0, a value beginning with `|` is run as a shell command, and an arbitrary path is read as a local file. Use `URI.parse(url).open` (or validate the scheme first) so only http(s) is fetched.

title: Stray `end if` in template is malformed and breaks the embed view
body: `<%- end if %>` closes the if/else but then starts a modifier `if` that applies to the next emitted output statement. Depending on how the ERB handler terminates the statement, this either fails to compile (every /embed/best render then errors) or reorders the output so the logo link is evaluated as a condition. The intended terminator is `<%- end %>`.

title: X-Frame-Options value ALLOWALL is not a defined value
body: The only defined X-Frame-Options values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN and ALLOW-FROM. Browsers ignore ALLOWALL, so this header has no effect whatever the comment or the intent suggests. If framing from any origin is intended, remove the header and use CSP frame-ancestors. If the goal is to override a stricter app-wide default, this does not do that either.

title: 'is 404 without an embed_url' does not test the missing parameter
body: embeddable_host defaults to '', so the before_filter ensure_embeddable raises InvalidAccess before `params.require(:embed_url)` runs. The example passes because of the host check, not the missing parameter, and its name is wrong (the response is a 403-style access error, not 404). Stub a valid host and referer, then call `get :best` without embed_url to test what the name claims.

title: create_table with force: true drops an existing topic_embeds table
body: If topic_embeds already exists when this migration runs (partly migrated database, or a table created by an earlier revision of this branch), `force: true` drops it along with every embed-to-topic mapping. Once the mappings are gone, the next retrieval of each embedded article creates a duplicate topic. Remove `force: true`.

title: Existing migration changed to force-drop top_topics
body: This edits an already-merged migration to add `force: true`. For any database where top_topics exists when the migration runs, the table and its counters are dropped and then rebuilt. Migrations should not drop tables. Revert to the original, or guard with `table_exists?`.

title: NOT NULL column with default rewrites the posts table
body: On PostgreSQL before 11, `add_column ... default: 1, null: false` rewrites the whole posts table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, blocking reads and writes for the duration on a large forum. Add the column nullable, backfill in batches, then add the default and NOT NULL constraint.

title: Disqus importer silently changes behaviour and drops --category
body: This change is outside the stated embed scope and is not documented. The `--category` option is removed, so `-c` no longer works. The first post's created_at is no longer set. Each thread is now fetched live via TopicEmbed.import_remote instead of an offline import, so an unreachable page, a 404, or a nil t[:link] (open(nil) raises TypeError) now breaks or skips the import. Split this into its own change with a documented migration path.

title: embed_url is varchar(255) with no length guard; longer URLs fail at insert
body: `t.string :embed_url` becomes varchar(255) on PostgreSQL. The URL comes straight from the request query string, and TopicRetriever and TopicEmbed only check the host and presence. A URL over 255 characters makes TopicEmbed.create! raise StatementInvalid after the topic and post were created inside the transaction. The job fails, and the embed page keeps showing 'Loading' and re-enqueuing. Validate length in the model or the controller, or use a text column.

title: cook_method option honoured with no permission check
body: Setting cook_method to raw_html disables PrettyText sanitization for the post. Nothing in this diff restricts who may set it. If any controller passes request params or a user-supplied hash into PostCreator, any user can store unsanitized HTML. Confirm callers only pass server-chosen values, or restrict this option to the import path.

title: Origin check is a substring match, not an origin comparison
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` passes whenever e.origin is a textual prefix of the forum URL. For discourseUrl `https://forum.example.com/`, an origin of `https://forum.example.co` passes. A page on such a domain can post discourse-resize messages and control the iframe height. Compare e.origin for equality with the origin parsed from discourseUrl.

title: setnx followed by expire is not atomic; a crash leaves a permanent throttle key
body: If the process dies or expire fails between `setnx` and `expire`, the key has no TTL. retrieved_recently? then returns true forever for that URL, so the embed can never be retrieved again without manual Redis cleanup. Use a single atomic SET with NX and EX options.

title: Missing embed_by_username silently skips import, leaving visitors on a loading page
body: If embed_by_username is unset or names no user, fetch_http returns without logging or raising. The embedding visitor sees 'Loading Discussion...' and the page reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely with no error for the admin. Validate the setting, or log the failure.

title: poll_feed itself is untested; spec only covers the execute gating
body: All examples only check whether execute delegates to poll_feed. Feed parsing, item-to-topic import, and the URL fallback are not exercised, which is why the nil-content crash in poll_feed.rb goes unnoticed. The file also requires an unrelated job (jobs/regular/process_post).

title: Feed content is double-unescaped and stored as raw HTML, giving stored XSS on the forum
body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` decodes entities that SimpleRSS has already decoded from the XML, so text meant to be shown literally (for example `&lt;img onerror=...&gt;` in the feed) becomes live markup. `TopicEmbed.import` then creates the post with `cook_method: raw_html` (topic_embed.rb:22). `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (app/models/post.rb:133), which skips the Sanitize/PrettyText pipeline and the `after_post_cook` plugin filters. The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked` unescaped (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19), and the same cooked HTML appears in the forum topic. A feed item containing a script or event-handler payload therefore runs on the forum origin for every visitor, including staff. Feed content is third-party data, so this crosses a trust boundary. Run imported content through the normal sanitizer before storing raw HTML, and remove the extra unescape.

title: Dangling `if` modifier in `<%- end if %>` makes the embed template invalid
body: `<%- end if %>` closes the `if` opened on line 2 but leaves a stray `if` modifier with no condition. Once ERB compiles this, the result is not valid Ruby (the modifier is followed by the compiler's statement separator), so the `best` template fails whenever it is rendered. The intent is clearly `<%- end %>`. This breaks the main embed page for every request that finds an existing topic. The controller specs do not catch it because they never render views (no `render_views`), so a view or request spec is needed.

title: PostCreator enqueues jobs inside an outer transaction that has not committed
body: `TopicEmbed.import` wraps `PostCreator#create` in `Topic.transaction`. `PostCreator#create` calls `enqueue_jobs` (which triggers `process_post` and `feature_topic_users`) before the outer transaction commits. PostCreator's own comment says jobs must be enqueued after the transaction because workers may start on uncommitted data. With Sidekiq, a `process_post` job can run before the post and the TopicEmbed row are visible, find nothing, or fail, so the post is never processed (oneboxes, image sizes, and so on). Enqueue after the outermost commit, or do not wrap the creator in an outer transaction.

title: Anonymous requests can force unlimited outbound fetches and full feed polls
body: For any unknown `embed_url`, each request enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job without checking the host (the controller only checks the referer). The only throttle is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` in topic_retriever.rb:26-28, which runs inside the worker and is keyed on the exact URL string. An attacker can vary a query string to get a fresh key every time. Each new key causes an outbound HTTP fetch of the embeddable host, and when feed polling is enabled it runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (topic_retriever.rb:41), which downloads and re-imports the entire feed. Nothing rate-limits the endpoint, so this is a cheap way to exhaust outbound bandwidth and Sidekiq capacity. Validate the host in the controller before enqueueing, throttle per normalized URL in the request path, and do not run a full feed poll from a request-driven job.

title: `force: true` on a new table migration drops any existing topic_embeds table
body: `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` drops an existing `topic_embeds` table before creating it. A migration that creates a new table gains nothing from this option and makes it destructive: running it in an environment where the table already exists (a partially migrated database, or another branch that created the table) silently deletes every embed-to-topic mapping. The importer depends on those mappings to avoid duplicate topics. Remove `force: true`.

title: Unrelated migration gains `force: true`, which drops existing top_topics data if rerun
body: This change adds `force: true` to the `top_topics` table creation. It is unrelated to embedding. If the migration runs in an environment where `top_topics` already exists with data, the table and all its counters are dropped. If the schema needs changing, add a new migration instead of editing one that may already have run.

title: One bad feed item aborts the whole poll, and nil content raises NoMethodError
body: The `rss.items.each` loop has no per-item error handling. `i.content` can be nil for feed items that only supply a description, so `i.content.scrub` on line 35 raises NoMethodError. `i.title` can also be nil. `TopicEmbed.import` can raise too, for example when the URL exceeds 255 characters, or when the embed's post has been deleted. Any of these aborts the loop, and the job has `retry: false`, so nothing retries. The next hourly run reaches the same item and fails again, so every item after it is never imported. Guard nil content and title, and rescue and log errors per item.

title: Origin check uses substring matching, so a prefix origin is accepted
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, not an origin comparison. Any sender whose origin is a prefix of the forum URL passes. With `discourseUrl = "https://community.example.com/"`, a page served from the registrable domain `https://community.example.co` has an origin that is a prefix, so `indexOf` returns 0 and the message is accepted. The handler also never checks `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`. The practical effect is that a lookalike site can resize the iframe, but the check is wrong. Compare the exact origin (scheme, host, port) of `discourseUrl` with `e.origin`.

title: X-Frame-Options 'ALLOWALL' is not a valid value and is ignored by browsers
body: Valid X-Frame-Options values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN, and ALLOW-FROM. Browsers ignore unknown values, so this header does nothing; framing is permitted only because the browser ignores it. It also overwrites any X-Frame-Options set earlier in the request. If the intent is to allow framing from the configured host, use `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors` with the embeddable host and remove this header.

title: setnx followed by a separate expire can leave a throttle key with no TTL
body: `$redis.setnx` and `$redis.expire` are two separate commands. If the process dies or the connection drops between them, `retrieved:<url>` persists with no TTL. Non-staff users are then permanently throttled for that URL and it is never retried. Use one atomic command, `SET key 1 NX EX 60`.

title: Missing post for an existing embed causes NoMethodError on update
body: `post = embed.post` can be nil if the post was deleted. When the content hash differs, `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError on `@post.raw`. The stale embed row is never repaired, and in PollFeed this exception aborts the whole loop (poll_feed.rb:31), so every later item is skipped. Handle a missing post explicitly, for example by recreating the post or removing the stale embed.

title: Readability attribute whitelist does not restrict URL schemes
body: `attributes: %w[href src]` limits which attribute names survive, but it does not check URL schemes. A `<a href="javascript:...">` from the fetched page can survive into the body. That body is stored as raw_html (cook_method), so the link runs script on the forum when clicked. The source is the configured embeddable host, so exploiting this needs that site to be compromised or malicious, but the forum should not accept unsanitized HTML from it. Pass the output through the normal sanitizer with an allowed-scheme list.

title: Imported-from footer interpolates the URL into HTML without escaping
body: The footer is built as `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")`. The URL comes from the feed link or id and is inserted unescaped into a body stored as raw HTML. A link such as `http://x.test/'>` injects markup. The URL check on line 11 uses `^`, which matches after any newline, so the scheme check is also weaker than intended. Escape the URL before interpolating it, and anchor the scheme check at the start of the string.

title: embed_url is varchar(255) with no length check, so long URLs fail at insert
body: `t.string :embed_url` creates varchar(255) in PostgreSQL. The value comes from unauthenticated request params (embed_controller.rb:9) and from feed links, and nothing checks its length. A longer URL makes `TopicEmbed.create!` raise StatementInvalid after the page has been fetched and the post built. The transaction rolls back, and every retry fails the same way. Validate the length at the controller and model, or use a text column.

title: Adding a NOT NULL column with a default rewrites the entire posts table
body: On PostgreSQL releases before 11, `add_column` with a default and `null: false` rewrites the whole posts table while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. On a large forum, reads and writes to posts are blocked for the duration. Add the column nullable, backfill in batches, then add the default and NOT NULL constraint, or schedule the downtime explicitly.

title: The --category option is silently removed from the Disqus import CLI
body: Removing `method_option :category` means `thor disqus:import --category X` now fails with an unknown-option error, and imported topics no longer get a category. This is a breaking change to the command-line interface that the PR description does not mention. Restore the option or document the removal.

title: Disqus import now fetches every thread live with no error handling and duplicates comments on re-run
body: Replacing PostCreator with `TopicEmbed.import_remote` makes the import fetch each thread's live URL with `open(url).read`. There is no timeout, no rescue, and no per-thread handling, so one 404 or network error aborts the import midway. The `ensure` block restores settings, but earlier threads are already imported. Re-running the import also appends every comment again: `import` returns the existing post, and the loop keeps creating posts for it. Rescue per thread, and skip comment creation when the topic already existed.

title: New gems are added for both Rails modes, but only the Rails 4 lockfile is updated
body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` are added unconditionally, and Rails 3 mode uses the same Gemfile with the default `Gemfile.lock`. Only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` is updated in this PR. In Rails 3 mode, `bundle install --deployment` or `--frozen` will fail because the lockfile is missing these gems. Update the Rails 3 lockfile too, or gate the gems by mode.

title: Test named 'is 404' asserts only failure, and no test renders the view
body: The example is titled 'is 404 without an embed_url' but only checks `should_not be_success`. It passes because the `ensure_embeddable` filter raises first when embeddable_host is unset, so `params.require` is never exercised. No spec renders the `best` or `loading` templates (no `render_views`), so a broken template like the one in best.html.erb:6 goes undetected. Add a request spec that checks the status code and renders the templates.

title: Every TopicRetriever example stubs the method under test, leaving the throttle and feed logic untested
body: Each example in the 'with a valid host' context stubs `retrieved_recently?` or `perform_retrieve`. The Redis throttle, the feed-first branch in `perform_retrieve` (topic_retriever.rb:40-43), the existing-embed early return, and `fetch_http` are never exercised. The most important behavior, that a second request within 60 seconds does not fetch again, has no coverage. Add examples that use a real or mock Redis and exercise `perform_retrieve` directly.

title: PollFeed import logic has no test coverage, only the gating conditions
body: The spec only checks when `poll_feed` is called and stubs `poll_feed` in the delegation example. The actual import path, including URL filtering, nil title or content handling, the `TopicEmbed.import` call per item, and the error behavior, is untested. That is the riskiest code in the feature (see the XSS and per-item abort findings above). Add examples that feed a sample RSS document through `poll_feed`.

title: Kernel#open is used on an admin-supplied URL
body: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Kernel#open. In Ruby 2.x, a string beginning with `|` is executed as a shell command rather than fetched. The setting is admin-only, so the exposure is limited, but the call should be explicit. Use `URI.parse(url).open` (open-uri) so only HTTP(S) fetches are possible.

title: String#scrub requires Ruby 2.1 or later
body: `String#scrub` was added in Ruby 2.1. If this application still targets Ruby 2.0 (as Discourse did in late 2013), every poll that reaches this line raises NoMethodError. Confirm the supported Ruby version, or use an encoding-safe alternative.

title: cook_method is accepted from any opts hash and can bypass sanitization
body: `setup_post` now copies `opts[:cook_method]` onto the post. Setting it to raw_html stores the body unsanitized, because `Post#cook` returns raw HTML directly. If any controller forwards request parameters into PostCreator, an API or web user could create raw_html posts. Check that user-facing controllers whitelist their params and never pass `cook_method`, or only honor it from trusted server-side callers.

title: Documented options list omits the new cook_method option
body: The header comment lists the accepted PostCreator options, but `cook_method`, which this PR adds and which changes how the body is rendered and sanitized, is not documented. Add it, with its accepted values and the fact that raw_html skips the sanitizer.

title: raw_html posts are stored and rendered without any sanitization
body: When cook_method is raw_html, cook returns the raw text unchanged, skipping the markdown pipeline, any sanitizer and the after_post_cook plugin filters. Imported content (RSS items via PollFeed, scraped pages via TopicEmbed.import_remote) is stored this way (topic_embed.rb:22), and PostCreator accepts cook_method from any caller's options with no whitelist (post_creator.rb:216). The cooked value is then emitted unescaped: embed/best.html.erb:19 uses 'raw post.cooked', and normal topic views render cooked as HTML. Any markup that reaches a raw_html post, such as a script tag in a feed item, runs as stored XSS on the forum's own origin for every visitor. Remote HTML needs sanitizing before it is stored as cooked.

title: CGI.unescapeHTML turns escaped feed markup into live HTML
body: RSS and Atom descriptions are almost always entity-escaped (a script tag appears as <script>). After CGI.unescapeHTML those entities become real markup. The result is saved with cook_method raw_html (topic_embed.rb:22) and rendered unescaped (see post.rb:133 and embed/best.html.erb:19), so any feed item can inject script into the forum for all visitors. Escaped content should stay escaped, or be sanitized, never unescaped.

title: Article URL interpolated unescaped into stored HTML footer
body: The URL is placed unescaped into an href attribute and a text node of the footer, which is then stored as raw HTML. The only check is that the URL starts with http(s):// (line 11). Characters such as single quote, equals and parentheses are legal in URL paths and can pass URI parsing, so a feed link like http://example.com/'onmouseover='alert(1) produces an anchor with an injected event handler. The URL should be HTML-escaped before interpolation.

title: '<%- end if %>' is a syntax error; the best view cannot render
body: The block opened on line 2 is closed with 'end if', which is not valid ERB/Ruby for closing a conditional. It compiles to 'end if ;', where the modifier 'if' has no condition, so the template raises SyntaxError whenever it is rendered. Every request for an existing embedded topic (the @topic_view branch) fails. It should be '<%- end %>'.

title: Unauthenticated requests can trigger a full feed download and reimport each time
body: The throttle is keyed on the full embed_url (lines 26-28). Only the host must match embeddable_host, so a client can vary the path or query string to get a fresh key every time. Each new key then calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute here, which downloads the entire feed and re-imports every item (poll_feed.rb:29, 31-36). The feed fetch and the readability fetch (topic_embed.rb:48) use open() with no timeout. An attacker can therefore keep Sidekiq workers busy with unbounded outbound fetches and DB writes. The feed poll needs its own global throttle or should not run inline per URL.

title: A retrieve job is enqueued on every request; the throttle only runs inside the job
body: When no topic exists, every request enqueues a retrieve_topic job, and the 60-second throttle is checked only when the job runs (topic_retriever.rb:27-28). Anonymous requests, and the loading page that reloads every 30 seconds, therefore create unbounded queue entries even when the URL was retrieved moments ago. The throttle check should happen before enqueueing, or duplicate jobs should be deduplicated.

title: PostCreator enqueues jobs inside an open transaction
body: PostCreator.create is called inside the outer Topic.transaction (line 21). PostCreator.create calls enqueue_jobs before returning, which queues process_post and feature_topic_users. Its own comment (post_creator.rb around line 290) says jobs must be enqueued after commit. With Sidekiq, a worker can start before this transaction commits and find no post, so the job silently does nothing. The TopicEmbed row is also created after those jobs are queued.

title: ALLOWALL is not a valid X-Frame-Options value
body: The only valid values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN and ALLOW-FROM. Browsers ignore unrecognized values, so this line only appears to allow framing by accident, and it overwrites any app-wide frame policy with a meaningless string. To allow framing, the header should be removed (for example response.headers.delete('X-Frame-Options')), not set to an invalid value.

title: Origin check uses substring match, so look-alike origins are accepted
body: discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 checks whether the sender origin is a substring of discourseUrl, not whether it equals it. If discourseUrl is 'https://forum.example.com/', a page at 'https://forum.example.co' passes the check and can send 'discourse-resize' messages. The impact is limited to setting the iframe height, but this is the only origin validation in the embed script and it is wrong. The comparison should parse discourseUrl and compare origins for equality.

title: One bad feed item aborts the whole poll; nil content is not guarded
body: The loop has no per-item rescue. If any item raises (for example i.content is nil, which is possible for entries with only a summary, so nil.scrub raises; or TopicEmbed.import raises on a PostCreator or permission error), the remaining items are never imported. The job is also scheduled with retry: false, so the failure is dropped until the next hourly run hits the same item again.

title: Shipped migration now uses force: true, which drops an existing table
body: This changes an existing migration to create_table with force: true. If top_topics already exists with data in any environment where the migration version is not recorded (for example a database built from another branch), this migration drops the table and all its rows without warning. The flag is not needed for a table this migration is supposed to create for the first time and should be removed.

title: --category option removed with no replacement and no documentation
body: The method_option :category and its only use are deleted. Existing invocations that pass --category or -c now fail with an unknown-option error. The import also changes behaviour: the topic is now built by scraping the article with readability (TopicEmbed.import_remote) instead of a permalink post, and created_at is no longer set on the topic. The PR description is only 'Test 4', so none of this is documented.

title: Gate tests pass for the wrong reason; poll_feed itself is untested
body: feed_polling_enabled defaults to false (site_settings.yml). The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' examples never enable feed_polling_enabled, so execute returns early at the first gate and the expectation holds regardless of the gate under test. Only the 'delegates' example enables all three, and it mocks poll_feed. The actual import loop, nil handling and failure behaviour have no coverage.

title: Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten to a wrong absolute URL
body: An href like //cdn.example.com/a.png starts with '/', so the sub(/^\/+/, '') strips both slashes and the result is prefix + '/cdn.example.com/a.png', i.e. http://host/cdn.example.com/a.png. The same problem exists for img src (line 71). Protocol-relative links should keep their host, or be resolved with URI.join against the article URL.

title: Adding a NOT NULL column with a default rewrites the posts table under lock
body: On PostgreSQL releases before 11, add_column with default: 1 and null: false rewrites the entire posts table while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. On a large forum this blocks all reads and writes to posts for the duration. The safer pattern is to add the column nullable, backfill in batches, then set the default and NOT NULL constraint.

title: setnx and expire are not atomic; a crash leaves the throttle key without a TTL
body: The key is set with setnx and then given a 60-second expiry in a separate command. If the process dies between the two, the key never expires and that embed URL is throttled permanently for non-staff users. A single atomic SET with NX and EX options would avoid this.

title: URL validation uses ^ instead of \A, so it matches any line
body: In Ruby, ^ matches at the start of any line. A value such as 'javascript:alert(1)' followed by a newline and 'http://x' passes this check. The later URI() call in absolutize_urls currently rejects it, so no harm follows, but the validation is ineffective and relies on an unrelated exception. The regex should be anchored with \A.

title: Test name says 404 but asserts only non-success; referer mismatch is untested
body: The example 'is 404 without an embed_url' does not set a host, so it fails on the host check and never exercises the missing-parameter path. It only asserts not-success, so it does not verify a 404. There is also no example for a referer whose host differs from embeddable_host, which is the main access check in ensure_embeddable.

title: Spec asserts raw HTML is stored and rendered verbatim
body: The assertion post.cooked.should == post.raw locks in the behaviour that imported content is stored as-is with no sanitization. Nothing tests escaping of the article URL in the footer, sanitization of feed or scraped HTML, the unchanged-content update path, or import_remote. The security-relevant paths of this feature are not covered.

title: Floated button inside the new flex container loses its right alignment
body: `.small-action` is converted to `display: flex` in this PR, but the `button` rule inside it still relies on `float: right`. Floats are ignored on flex items, so if the button is a direct child of `.small-action`, it stops being pushed to the right edge and sits right after `.small-action-desc`. `.small-action-desc` has no `flex-grow`, so nothing fills the remaining space to keep the button at the end. The button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the float should be removed and the placement set through flex properties). Otherwise the action button in small-action posts visibly moves.

title: `align-items` mixin emits a bogus `-ms-align-items` property
body: `-ms-align-items` is not a real CSS property. The correct IE10 prefixed property is `-ms-flex-align`, which the same mixin already emits on line 120. The line is dead and misleading: it suggests IE support is covered by a property name that browsers never recognise. It should be removed.

title: `order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` has no effect unless its parent is a flex container
body: `order` only applies to flex or box items. This PR does not make the parent of `.extra-info-wrapper` (`#topic-title`) a flex container, and no changed file does. Unless another stylesheet establishes flex layout there, the `@include order(2)` is a no-op. The same change also adds `line-height: 1.5`, which is unrelated to ordering. The author should confirm the flex parent exists or drop the ordering.

title: Bullet badge top margin inside `.extra-info-wrapper` removed without replacement
body: The `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule under `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper` is deleted, and nothing replaces it. Bullet badges in the topic title lose their 5px top offset, which changes their vertical alignment. The PR does not mention this and the title only refers to performance, so it looks like an unintended visual regression.

title: PR description is a placeholder and does not explain the many visual changes
body: The description reads only "Test 5", and the title claims a performance optimization. The diff is a layout refactor from floats to flexbox across header, topic title, post, small-action and badge styles. It also changes spacing: `.small-action-desc` loses its vertical padding and 4em left padding, `margin-top` is removed, and `.title` and `.panel` float rules are replaced. None of this is justified, and no performance measurement is offered. Reviewers cannot tell which changes are intentional or how they were verified, so the description should explain the intent and the visual impact.

title: Bullet badges in topic title lose their top offset and inherit a new line-height
body: The diff deletes the `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule and adds `line-height: 1.5` to `.extra-info-wrapper`. Bullet badges have no line-height of their own, so they now inherit 1.5 and lose the 5px top margin. Both changes shift where bullet category badges sit in the topic title. The PR does not mention either change, and nothing in this diff makes `.extra-info-wrapper` a flex container that would justify a vertical-alignment change. This is an unexplained visual regression.

title: small-action becomes a flex row without sizing the description, and floats stop working
body: `.small-action` is now `display:flex`, but `.small-action-desc` gets no `flex-grow`/`flex: 1`. It therefore sizes to its content rather than filling the row. The old `padding-left: 4em` that reserved room for the avatar is replaced by `0 1.5%`. Floats are ignored on flex items, so `.topic-avatar { float: left }` is a no-op and, if the `button` is a direct child (the `button` selector at this nesting level suggests it is), `button { float: right }` at line 309 no longer pushes it to the right edge. The message box will not fill the post width and the button placement will change. This needs a visual check; as written it looks like an unverified layout change.

title: align-items mixin emits a non-existent -ms-align-items property
body: `-ms-align-items` is not a property in any browser's CSS. The declaration is silently dropped, so it does nothing, and it misleads readers into thinking an IE-specific alignment declaration is being emitted. The IE10 equivalent is `-ms-flex-align`, which is already on line 120. The line should be removed.

title: order(2) has no effect unless an ancestor of .extra-info-wrapper is a flex container
body: `order` only affects children of a flex or box container. This PR does not turn any ancestor of `.extra-info-wrapper` into a flex container, so the new `@include order(2)` is dead CSS unless an ancestor is already flex in the base stylesheet or markup. The author should confirm that the rule does something or drop it.

title: Title claims a performance optimization; description is placeholder and scope is undocumented
body: The PR title says it optimizes header layout performance, but a float-to-flexbox layout change makes no performance measurement and the diff does not explain any performance gain. The description is only 'Test 5'. The diff also changes topic posts (`.small-action`), topic titles (`.extra-info-wrapper`, the removed bullet margin, the new line-height) and category badges, none of which are part of the header. Reviewers have no rationale for these visual changes and no before/after evidence. The description should state the scope, the intended visual changes and how they were verified.

title: Removed the .title float rule from the header without replacement
body: The diff deletes the `.title { float: left; }` rule inside `.d-header`. Nothing in the PR restores positioning for the title element, and the PR does not mention the removal. The `.contents` container is switched from block flow to flexbox in the same hunk, so the title becomes a content-sized flex item instead of a floated block. If the title/logo markup depends on that float, the left side of the header will shift. The removal needs to be justified or replaced with an explicit flex rule, and checked visually.

title: float: right on the small-action button is ignored now that .small-action is a flex container
body: `.small-action` now gets `@include flexbox()` (added in this PR), and the `button` inside it still relies on `float: right`. Floats do not apply to flex items, so the button is no longer pushed to the right edge. Its position becomes the next slot after `.small-action-desc`, which has no flex-grow. For short messages the button will sit right next to the text instead of at the right side of the notice. Either the button needs `margin-left: auto` or similar, or the float should be dropped as intentional. As written, the rendering change is unaddressed.

title: Bullet badge margin-top rule removed from the extra-info wrapper with no replacement
body: The `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule under `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper` is deleted. The bullet badge in this area was previously offset by that margin. The same PR changes the bullet badge's display model (inline-flex with baseline alignment in badges.css.scss), so vertical alignment of the bullet is changed in two places at once with no stated intent and no replacement offset. This is likely to misalign the bullet relative to the category text.

title: Unrelated spacing changes in .small-action-desc and its children
body: Beyond adding flexbox, the PR changes `.small-action-desc` padding from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`, drops `margin-top: 5px`, changes the `.custom-message p` margin from `5px 0` to `0`, and removes `padding-top: 4px` from `> p`. None of these follow from switching to flexbox, and the PR gives no reason for them. They change the visible spacing of every small-action notice and should be split out or justified.

title: order(2) and line-height on .extra-info-wrapper are unexplained and may be no-ops
body: `order` only affects flex or grid items. Nothing in this change makes the parent of `.extra-info-wrapper` a flex container, so `@include order(2)` on line 30 may have no effect. The added `line-height: 1.5` on line 32 applies to every descendant of the wrapper and changes line box heights in the topic title area, which is not mentioned. Both should be confirmed against the markup or removed.

title: align-items mixin emits a nonexistent -ms-align-items property
body: `-ms-align-items` is not a real CSS property. No browser ever supported it, and the correct IE10 prefixed property (`-ms-flex-align`) is already emitted on line 120. The declaration is dead output that will be silently dropped, and it suggests the mixin was not written against real property names. It should be removed.

title: PR description is a placeholder and the performance claim is unsupported
body: The description reads only 'Test 5', and the title says the change optimizes header layout performance. The PR contains no measurement, benchmark, or before/after evidence. Switching from floats to flexbox is a layout-model change, not a performance optimization by itself. The diff also changes header, topic title, small-action notices, and badges, and gives no visual verification. The description should explain the purpose, the expected visual outcome, and how it was checked, and the title should match what the change actually does.

title: website_name bypasses the TL0 restriction and exposes a hidden website to anonymous viewers
body: `website` is gated by `untrusted_attributes`, so for a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous or restricted scope it is omitted. The new `website_name` attribute is added to the plain `attributes` list (line 43), not to `untrusted_attributes`, and `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?` without calling `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. The result is that the website's domain (and now its path, via the new same-domain branch) is still serialized and rendered by user.hbs line 66 for restricted users. This defeats the intentional hiding of TL0 website data. Adding `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (around line 105) would apply the existing gate, and the custom `include_` method would be unnecessary.

title: include_website_name is missing the '?' and is never called
body: The serializer's include hooks follow the `include_<attr>?` convention (see `include_email?`, `include_card_image_badge_id?`, `include_suspend_reason?`). This method is named `include_website_name` with no question mark, so ActiveModel Serializer will not find it when deciding whether to emit the attribute. The intended `website.present?` condition therefore never runs, and `website_name` is emitted as `null` for every user with no website. Renaming it to `include_website_name?` would fix the contract, though the leak above still needs the untrusted gating.

title: Domain comparison is case-sensitive, so mixed-case website hosts lose the path
body: `URI(...).host` preserves the case typed by the user, but `Discourse.current_hostname` is compared with `==` here and with `ends_with?` and `split` below. A website such as `http://Example.com/user` on an instance at `example.com` does not match the first branch, falls through to the parent-domain check, and returns just `Example.com` with the path dropped. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so the host should be downcased before comparing.

title: Homepage URLs with a trailing slash render as 'example.com/'
body: For a website like `https://example.com/`, `URI(...).path` returns `"/"`, so the first branch returns `"example.com/"`. This is a very common way to enter a homepage and produces an awkward trailing slash in the profile. The path should be ignored when it is empty or `"/"`.

title: Untrusted attribute list was not updated for the new website_name attribute
body: The TL0-anonymous spec asserts that `bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background` are not serialized, but it does not include `website_name`. Because `website_name` is ungated, this spec gives false confidence: it would still pass while the domain leaks for restricted users. Adding `website_name` here and setting a website on the TL0 fixture would catch the regression.

title: Missing coverage for the www/forum sibling-subdomain branch and for a blank website
body: The `website_name` examples cover the exact-match branch and the parent-domain branch, but not the middle branch in the serializer (same label count, same parent domain, e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forums.example.com`). That branch has its own path-appending logic and is untested. There is also no example for a user with no website, which is where `website_name` should return nil and the attribute should be omitted (the `include_` logic that is currently broken).

title: website_name bypasses the untrusted-attribute restriction for TL0 users
body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), so for a TL0 user seen by an anonymous viewer (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`) the raw website URL is omitted. The new `website_name` attribute is not in that list, and `include_website_name?` only checks `website.present?`, so it is serialized for those users. It contains the host and, when the host matches the forum, the full path, so the restricted URL is effectively exposed again. This defeats the anti-spam restriction the `untrusted_attributes` mechanism exists to enforce. Fix: add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list, or gate `include_website_name?` on `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

title: Untrusted-attribute spec does not cover website_name
body: The 'TL0 user seen as anonymous' spec checks that bio, location, website and profile/card background are not serialized. The new `website_name` attribute is not in this list, so the spec does not catch the leak where a TL0 user's website host and path are serialized to anonymous viewers. Add `website_name` to this list and make the untrusted check cover it.

title: Trailing slash on same-domain website is shown as 'example.com/'
body: For a website such as `http://example.com/` on a forum at `example.com`, `URI(...).path` returns `"/"`, so `website_name` becomes `"example.com/"`. Users who type a bare domain with a trailing slash will see a stray slash that the previous client-side `split('/')[2]` logic did not produce. Consider stripping a bare `/` path, for example by treating a path of `/` as empty.

title: Domain comparison is case-sensitive
body: `URI(...).host` preserves the case typed by the user, while `Discourse.current_hostname` is normally lowercase. A website entered as `http://Example.com/user` on a forum at `example.com` fails the `==` test on line 141 and falls through to the else branch. The result is `Example.com` with no path, so the feature silently does not apply. Downcase both hosts before comparing, including in the `ends_with?` and sibling comparisons.

title: Sibling-domain heuristic treats different registrable domains as the same site
body: The branch on line 146 compares everything after the first label. For a forum at `y.co.uk` and a website at `x.co.uk/page`, both have three labels and the comparison yields `co.uk == co.uk`, so the full path is shown as if the website belonged to the forum's site. The heuristic does not account for public suffixes such as `co.uk` or `github.io`. The result is misleading display text for unrelated sites, not a security issue, but it does not match the stated intent of the feature.

title: website_name leaks the website domain and path for TL0 users that anonymous viewers should not see
body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), so for a TL0 user seen by an anonymous viewer the raw website URL is omitted on purpose. The new `website_name` attribute is added to the public attribute list (line 43) but not to that untrusted list. `include_website_name` (lines 153-155) only checks `website.present?`, so for the same user the serializer now emits `website_name`, which contains the host and, with this PR, the full URL path (e.g. `example.com/user`). The untrusted-attributes spec (spec line 11) also omits `website_name`, and the TL0 fixture sets no website, so the existing test cannot catch this. Result: the anti-spam hiding of new users' websites for anonymous visitors is bypassed, and the domain and path are exposed in public user JSON and the profile header.

title: Same-parent-domain check matches unrelated sites that share a multi-label public suffix
body: The branch at lines 144-146 treats two hosts as the same site when they have the same label count and everything after the first label matches. Take an instance at `mysite.github.io` and a profile website `other.github.io/about`. Both hosts have 3 labels and `github.io == github.io`, so the full path is shown for an unrelated site (`other.github.io/about` instead of `other.github.io`). The same happens for `mysite.co.uk` vs `other.co.uk`. The intent was www./forum. siblings under one registrable domain, but the check does not account for public suffixes, so it shows paths for other sites on shared hosting domains.

title: Hostname comparison is case-sensitive, so the same-domain path rule can miss
body: `URI#host` returns the host as written and does not lowercase it. A website such as `http://Example.com/user` on an instance whose hostname is `example.com` fails `website_host == discourse_host` at line 141. It then falls through to the else branch, which returns plain `Example.com` with no path, even though the domain matches. Both sides should be normalized (e.g. with `downcase`) before comparing.

title: website_name is not refreshed after the user saves a new website, so the header can show the old domain
body: The template now renders `model.website_name` (user.hbs line 66), which is computed only on the server. Previously the controller derived the name from `model.website`, which updated reactively. `save()` only copies `bio_excerpt` from the response (line 210), so after a user changes their website in preferences, `website_name` on the shared model stays stale. The profile header keeps showing the old domain until the user record is refetched, which a sibling-route transition may not do.

title: Branches and edge cases of website_name are untested
body: The new specs only cover one website (`example.com/user`) against three hostnames. Not covered: the equal-label-count branch for `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` (serializer lines 144-146), a blank website where `website_name` should be nil, an unparseable website, and mixed-case hosts. The untrusted-attribute spec (line 11) also does not include `website_name`, so the TL0 anonymous visibility problem is not checked. Regressions in the branch logic or visibility rules would go unnoticed.

title: Light-theme color for embedded post author links flipped from 30% to 70% lightness
body: In the .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a rule the light-theme branch was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The change only needed to add the dark-theme branch (secondary-based), but the primary lightness flipped. In the light theme the bold author link goes from dark gray to roughly #b3b3b3 on white (about 2:1 contrast), a visible regression on every light-theme embed. The first argument should stay at 30% with the dark branch at secondary 70%.

title: custom-message-length light-theme lightness changed from 70% to 30%
body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The new value passes scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) as the light-theme branch, which makes the character-count hint in the light theme much darker than before. The dark branch is the only part that should change. The fix is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)).

title: Group member name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: The original .group-member-info .name color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement uses 50% for the primary branch, so the light-theme name text gets lighter with no stated reason. The diff only intended to add the dark-theme branch. The primary value should remain 30%, with the secondary branch at 70% to mirror it.

title: Mobile group member name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: The original .group-member-info .name color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement changes the primary branch to 50%, an unrequested light-theme change. The same mistake appears in the desktop user.scss. The primary value should stay 30%, with the secondary branch at 70%.

title: Topic map h3 light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
body: The original .topic-map h3 color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). The replacement uses 50% for the primary branch, so the light-theme heading becomes a mid-gray instead of near-black. The intended change was only to add the dark-theme branch. The fix is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)), matching the desktop topic-post.scss h3 pairing.

title: Sibling topic-list color left unconverted, so it stays wrong in dark themes
body: The rule .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification still uses a bare scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%). In a dark theme $primary is light, so the badge text stays near-white. The same file converts the th, td, and topic-excerpt colors to dark-light-choose, so this one is an inconsistent miss within the same PR's goal.

title: #file-uploading color uses only $secondary, which is inverted for light themes
body: The color is scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%) with no dark-light-choose. In the light theme $secondary is white and lightening white leaves it white, so the upload-progress text is white on a light-gray background and barely visible. This is the reverse of the bug class this PR fixes. It is unchanged here but sits in a file the PR edits, so it should be converted to dark-light-choose with a primary-based light value.

title: Comment still states the topic-list default is a bare scale-color
body: The comment says the default color for topic list table cells is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%). This PR changes that color to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 50%), scale-color($secondary, 50%)), so the comment is now stale and misleading for anyone tuning the coldmap colors.

title: PR description is a placeholder with no rationale or verification notes
body: The description reads only 'Test 7'. For a 32-file stylesheet change that pairs primary and secondary lightness values, there is no explanation of the pairing rule, no before/after screenshots for either theme, and no note on which values were intentionally changed. That is why five light-theme lightness regressions in this diff went unnoticed. The description should state the pairing rule and how it was verified in both themes.

title: Embedded post meta link light-theme color flipped from 30% to 70% lightness
body: The `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The PR is meant to change only the $secondary-based branch, but here the primary-based (light theme) value was changed from 30% to 70% and the two values were swapped. In the light theme the bold link text becomes a 70%-lightness gray on a white background, which is close to unreadable. The conversion should keep the first argument at 30% and use 70% for $secondary.

title: Custom message length light-theme color changed from 70% to 30% lightness
body: The original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme value is now 30% lightness, far darker than before, and the dark-theme value is 70%, so both sides are swapped. The desktop equivalent in desktop/modal.scss (`.custom-message-length`) uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 70%), scale-color($secondary, 30%))`, so the mobile and desktop modals now render this text differently in the light theme. The first argument should stay at 70% and the second should be 30%.

title: Group member name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme name text becomes noticeably lighter. The dark-theme branch is also not the mirror of 30% (which would be 70% for $secondary). The 50/50 values look copied from the sibling `.title` rule directly below, which was originally 50%. Every other hunk in this PR keeps the original value as the first argument, so this one breaks the pattern. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Mobile group member name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This changes the light-theme name color to a lighter gray, which the PR's stated goal (dark themes only) does not call for. The same selector in desktop/user.scss was changed the same way, so the bug is duplicated. The intended conversion is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Mobile topic map heading light-theme color changed from 20% to 50% lightness
body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme heading becomes much lighter than before. The desktop rule for the same `.topic-map h3` selector in desktop/topic-post.scss uses the mirrored pair 20%/80%, so the mobile and desktop headings now diverge. The correct value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

title: Comment still describes the topic-list default color as a plain scale-color
body: The comment says the default table cell color in the topic list is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. After this PR that default is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 50%), scale-color($secondary, 50%))`, and the coldmap rules below it use that form. The comment is now misleading for anyone maintaining these colors.

title: Category badge-notification color left unconverted in a file this PR otherwise converts
body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses plain `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. The rest of this file (lines 48, 51, 55, 69, 246, 301) was converted to the theme-aware form. In dark themes this element keeps the primary-derived color the PR is meant to replace, so the conversion is incomplete.

title: Uploading indicator uses scale-color on $secondary with no theme branch
body: `#file-uploading` uses `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)`. In the light theme $secondary is white, and scale-color cannot lighten white, so the text stays white on the light composer background (`dark-light-diff(...)`). This is the same family of color rule the PR converts, and it sits in a file the PR touches, but it was left unconverted. It should use dark-light-choose with a primary-based light-theme value.

title: Mobile topic-map h3 light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
body: The mobile `.topic-map h3` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and the diff rewrites it as `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`. The primary-side lightness was silently changed from 20% to 50%, while the PR only intended to add the $secondary branch. In the default light theme, every mobile topic-map heading becomes much lighter than before. The desktop equivalent correctly keeps 20% and pairs it with 80% for $secondary, so the two platforms now also disagree.

title: Mobile .custom-message-length light-theme color flipped from 70% to 30% lightness
body: `.custom-message-length` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, a faded light gray. The new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, so the light-theme branch now uses 30%. That is a much darker color than before for the character-count hint in mobile modals. The dark-theme pairing (70% of $secondary) was copied from the desktop file, but the primary-side value should have stayed at 70%. The desktop version of this rule is correct (70% / 30%).

title: Embedded-post author link light-theme color changed from 30% to 70% lightness
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, which is a dark, bold link color. The diff replaces it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so the light-theme link color jumps to 70% lightness. Links in embedded post headers become faint and lose contrast against the background in the default theme. The primary value should have remained 30%, with 70% as the $secondary counterpart.

title: Desktop group-member .name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: `.group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The diff changes the light-theme branch to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` while also adding the $secondary branch. This is an unintended change to the light-theme value that the PR description does not mention. The name is noticeably lighter in the default theme and now differs from the 30% value used for the same name elsewhere.

title: Mobile group-member .name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: Same problem as the desktop file: `.group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new `dark-light-choose` call uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` for the light theme, so the light-theme color changes without being intended. The $secondary branch should have been `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` to mirror the original 30%, and the primary branch should have kept 30%.

title: Comment says the topic-list cell default is a plain scale-color, which is no longer true
body: The comment says the default color for table cells in the topic list is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. This PR changes the `td` and `th` defaults in `_topic-list.scss` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The comment now documents a value that is no longer the effective default, and it will mislead anyone tuning the coldmap colors.

title: Public member list silently capped at 50 with no paging UI
body: The members action now applies a default limit of 50 to every group. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members. The public members route (group-members.js.es6) calls findMembers() once with the defaults, and the template group/members.hbs has no next/previous controls. In any group with more than 50 members, the public page shows only the first 50 and gives users no way to reach the rest. Either add paging to the public page or keep returning the full list there.

title: GET /groups/:name/members.json response shape changed from array to object
body: The endpoint used to return a bare JSON array of serialized members. It now returns {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}. Any existing consumer that treats the response as an array (API clients, plugins, other frontend code) will break. The change is not versioned or called out, and only the consumers in this PR were updated.

title: Negative limit or offset causes a database error (500)
body: limit and offset come straight from params through to_i with no validation. A negative value (for example offset=-1) is passed into LIMIT/OFFSET, which PostgreSQL rejects, so the request returns a 500 instead of a client error. Previously only automatic groups reached this code path with user-supplied limit/offset; now every group's member endpoint does.

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. With 100 members and limit 50 this yields 3 pages, not 2. Page 2 shows Next as enabled, and clicking it requests offset 100, which returns an empty page labelled 3/3. Math.ceil(user_count / limit) gives the correct count for all values.

title: create ignores alias_level, which the admin UI sends for new groups
body: The admin form shows the alias_level combo box for new groups too, and Group#asJSON sends alias_level on POST. create only reads name and visible, so the chosen alias level is silently dropped and the group is created with the default. The save action does not call save() again after create, so the value is never persisted. The spec suite has no create test that checks alias_level.

title: PATCH incremental membership API removed; PATCH now silently succeeds without changes
body: The old update_patch handled PATCH with a changes payload (add/delete usernames). That branch is removed, but resources :groups still routes PATCH to update. update now ignores the changes key, saves name/visible/alias_level, and returns success. Existing API clients get HTTP 200 and no membership change, which is a silent no-op instead of an error. Either keep the behaviour or reject PATCH explicitly.

title: Removing a non-member raises RecordNotFound instead of succeeding
body: group.users.delete(user_id) is called with an integer id. In Rails 4.x, CollectionProxy#delete with ids first calls find on the association, so a user who is not in the group raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound and returns a 404. The removed spec explicitly tested that removing non-members succeeds silently, and the admin JS removeMember has no error handler, so a stale list just fails with no feedback.

title: remove_member spec sends PUT although the route is DELETE
body: The route for remove_member is delete "members" in config/routes.rb, but this spec issues xhr :put. Controller specs do not check the HTTP verb against the routes, so the test passes regardless of which verb is mapped. It should use :delete so it exercises the real endpoint.

title: Behaviour changes are untested: pagination endpoint, unknown usernames, non-members, alias_level on create
body: The PR changes the public members endpoint (paginated, new response shape) but adds no test for it in the groups controller spec. It also removes the specs for adding unknown users and removing non-members without replacing them. There is no create test covering alias_level, which is why the dropped value above goes unnoticed. The JS pagination arithmetic (totalPages) has no test either.

title: Remove control shown for automatic groups because the template checks the wrong object
body: This template is rendered once per member, so its context is the member User object. {{#unless automatic}} therefore looks up automatic on the user, which is undefined, and the remove link renders for every member, including automatic groups. Clicking it sends a DELETE that the server rejects with a 422, and the UI has no error handler, so nothing visible happens. The flag should be passed in from the group controller.

title: Offset is clamped to a stale user_count, leaving an empty page after removing the last member
body: findMembers clamps the requested offset to the current user_count. removeMember calls findMembers right after the DELETE returns, before user_count has been refreshed. If the last member on the final page is removed, the request uses the old count, so the page is re-fetched at an offset beyond the new total. The result is an empty table with currentPage past the last page, and the offset is never pulled back to the new last page.

title: Overlapping findMembers responses can leave a stale page displayed
body: Each findMembers call writes members, offset and user_count from its own response. When next or previous is clicked quickly, two requests can be in flight and responses can arrive out of order. The last response to arrive wins, which can be the older page, and nothing discards stale responses. The displayed page and the pager state can then disagree with what the user last requested.

title: Selector for the old user-selector id no longer matches
body: The user-selector input was renamed from id group-users to user-selector in group.hbs, but this rule still targets input#group-users, so its width no longer applies. The enclosing .row.groups rule is also unused now. The selector should be updated or removed.

title: Public group members page silently truncated to 50 members
body: The members endpoint now defaults to a page size of 50 for every group (previously non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups were capped at 200). The public members page (`group/members.hbs`) renders `members` with `{{#each}}` and has no pagination controls, and the shared `Discourse.Group` model also defaults `limit: 50`. For any non-automatic group with more than 50 members, users see only the first 50 and have no way to reach the rest. This is a functional regression on the public group page.

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which should be `Math.ceil`. With 50 members and limit 50 it reports 2 pages (header shows "1/2") when only one exists. `next` then sets offset to min(offset+limit, user_count) = 50, which requests an empty page, so the admin sees an empty member list. With 100 members it reports 3 pages.

title: Remove link is rendered for automatic groups because `automatic` is looked up on the member
body: Inside `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` the item context is the member User object, not the group, so `{{#unless automatic}}` resolves `automatic` against the user and is always falsy. The remove link therefore appears for automatic groups too. The server rejects those removals with a 422, and `removeMember` in the admin controller and model has no failure handler, so the click appears to do nothing. The flag needs to come from the controller or be passed into the item view.

title: create ignores alias_level even though the client now sends it
body: `Discourse.Group#asJSON` now includes `alias_level`, and the new-group form shows the alias-level selector. `create` assigns only name and visible, so the chosen alias_level is silently dropped and the group gets the default. The PR rewrote `create` but left this gap in place.

title: Removing a non-member raises RecordNotFound instead of succeeding
body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` with an integer id makes Rails 4 look the record up with `find` on the association, which raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound when that user is not a member. The old PATCH path tolerated removing non-members, and the deleted spec ('succeeds silently when removing non-members') asserted that. A double-click or a stale member list now produces a 404 that the Ember client does not handle.

title: limit/offset are unvalidated: negative values cause a 500, and limit has no cap
body: `limit` and `offset` come straight from `params.to_i`. A negative `limit` produces `LIMIT -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects, so the request fails with a 500; a negative offset fails the same way. There is also no upper bound on limit, so a single request can pull the full membership of any visible group. Clamp limit to a sane range and floor offset at 0.

title: GET /groups/:name/members.json response shape changed from an array to an object
body: The endpoint now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}` instead of a bare array of users, and the default page size changed. Any other consumer of this public JSON endpoint (plugins, API clients) will break silently. The PR description does not mention the contract change.

title: Admin update silently resets visible for clients using the old nested params
body: `update` now reads flat top-level params and no longer reads `group[...]`, and the PATCH membership path is removed. A client still sending the old nested payload (`group[name]`, `group[visible]`) gets `params[:visible]` nil, so `group.visible` is set to false without any error. The name change is also silently skipped.

title: remove_member spec uses PUT although the route is DELETE
body: The route added in config/routes.rb is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, but this spec sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`. Controller specs do not enforce the HTTP verb, so the test passes while production would never reach the action with PUT. The verb mismatch goes untested. The other remove test (line 125) correctly uses :delete.

title: No positive test for updating a non-automatic group
body: The `.update` context only checks that renaming an automatic group is ignored. The rename, visible, and alias_level paths for normal groups, which are the main behavior of the rewritten `update` action, have no test. The old test covering name changes for regular groups was removed.

title: New public members endpoint and its pagination have no spec
body: The `members` action changed its response shape, default limit, and query logic, and the group members UI now depends on the meta fields. No spec in this PR exercises pagination, meta values, the 50-member default, or access to hidden groups through `find_group`.

title: Stale selector targets the user-selector id that this PR renamed
body: `input#group-users` still sets a 600px width, but group.hbs now passes `id="user-selector"`, so this rule no longer matches anything. The layout rule is dead and the input falls back to the generic width.

title: totalPages overcounts by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
body: totalPages is computed as floor(user_count / limit) + 1. With 50 members and limit 50 it reports 2 pages, and with 100 members it reports 3, but only 2 pages of data exist. The extra page is empty: the server returns no rows for offset 50 when total is 50. The next action clamps offset to user_count rather than to the start of the last page, so from page 1 of a 50-member group, Next moves to offset 50 and shows an empty '2/2' page. Every group whose size is a multiple of the page size gets a phantom empty last page. The fix is ceil(user_count / limit) or the equivalent.

title: Remove link is shown for members of automatic groups
body: The '{{#unless automatic}}' guard is evaluated against the item being rendered (a Discourse.User inside the {{each}} item view), not against the admin group controller where 'automatic' is defined. The property is therefore undefined and the remove '×' link is rendered for every member, including automatic groups where removal is forbidden. Clicking it runs the confirm dialog, then the server returns 422 (can_not_modify_automatic in add/remove_member). The removeMember promise in group.js has no error handler, so the admin gets no feedback. The flag needs to be read from the controller explicitly, or the control hidden from group.hbs.

title: Public members list silently truncated to 50 with no pagination controls
body: The public members route now calls findMembers() with the default limit of 50 (groups_controller.rb defaults limit to 50 for every group, not only automatic ones). This template has no next/previous controls, so for any group with more than 50 members the members beyond the first 50 cannot be seen. Before this change, non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups returned up to 200. This is a functional regression for larger groups. Either add pagination to this page or request the full list here.

title: members endpoint response changed from an array to an object, breaking existing clients
body: GET /groups/:name/members.json previously returned a bare JSON array. It now returns {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}. This is a public endpoint, so any existing API client or script that iterates the top-level array will break. The default page size of 50 also silently truncates results for clients that previously received every member of a non-automatic group. Nothing in this PR versions the endpoint or documents the change.

title: create ignores alias_level even though the form lets the admin set it
body: The rewritten create action sets name and visible but never reads params[:alias_level]. The admin group form shows the alias_level combo-box for new groups too (it is not inside {{#if id}}), and asJSON sends alias_level. An admin who picks a value for a new group has it silently discarded and the group is saved with the default. The update action handles this with 'group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?', and create should do the same. No spec covers it.

title: Changed members endpoint contract has no test coverage in this PR
body: The members action's response shape, default limit, limit/offset handling and total count were all changed, and automatic groups now paginate like others. No spec change in this PR covers any of this (the groups controller spec is not touched). Tests should assert the {members, meta} shape, that total reflects the full membership, and that limit/offset select the right page for both automatic and non-automatic groups.

title: Offset clamp uses the stale user_count, leaving an empty page after removing the last member
body: findMembers clamps offset to the user_count from before the request. Take a group with 51 members on page 2 (offset 50) and remove the one member on that page. removeMember then calls findMembers, which clamps to the old user_count of 51 and keeps offset 50. The server returns an empty page with total 50, so the admin sees an empty page and a page counter past the last page. The clamp should use the new total from the response or the server should clamp.

title: Negative limit or offset query params cause a 500 from Postgres
body: limit and offset come straight from params with to_i and go into .limit() and .offset(). A request with offset=-1 produces a negative OFFSET, which Postgres rejects with an error, so the request fails with a 500. This path now runs for every group rather than only automatic ones. limit has no upper bound either. Both should be validated, for example limit clamped to 1..N and offset to >= 0.

title: Pressing Enter in the name field triggers the Add members button instead of Save
body: The new <form> wrapper has no submit handler. The Add members <button> has no type attribute, so it is a submit button and is the first submit button in the form. Browsers implicitly submit a form on Enter using its first submit button, so Enter in the Name field of an existing group clicks Add (addMembers) rather than Save. The name change is not saved. Giving the Add button type='button' would make Save the default button again.

title: CSS rule targets an element id that no longer exists
body: The rule input#group-users is still in the stylesheet, but group.hbs now renders the user selector with id='user-selector', so this 600px width rule never applies. The selector falls back to the 350px rule added in this PR. Update the selector or remove the dead rule.

title: Renaming a non-automatic group via update is no longer tested
body: The removed 'is able to update group members' test was the only spec that renamed a non-automatic group through update and checked that name and membership persisted. The new .update context only covers the automatic-group no-op. The non-automatic rename path (group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic), alias_level updates and visible updates now have no coverage.

title: Fallback target locales are only loaded in set_locale, so non-request code gets inconsistent fallbacks
body: The fallback chain built in config/initializers/i18n.rb is [locale, default_locale, :en], but translate() here only calls load_locale(config.locale). The fallback locales (site default and :en) are loaded only by I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! in ApplicationController#set_locale. Code that sets I18n.locale outside a controller request (Sidekiq jobs such as email, mailers, rake tasks) never loads :en or the site default.
