The file header only names Red Hat copyright and @author rmartinc, which does not reflect the provenance. The author should confirm provenance and add attribution.

title: No test covers the new provider selection (order precedence and ties)
body: The change replaces a fail-fast policy with order-based selection and tie behavior, but no test exercises detectProvider with multiple providers, different orders, or equal orders. A unit test for precedence and tie handling would catch regressions such as the FIPS/default tie described above.

title: Providers with equal order() are picked by classpath order, silently
body: detectProvider no longer rejects multiple providers. It stable-sorts by order() and takes the first entry. DefaultCryptoProvider (line 84), WildFlyElytronProvider (line 77) and FIPS1402Provider (line 115) all return 200. When two of them are on the same classpath, the winner is whichever ServiceLoader discovered first. Before this PR that case threw IllegalStateException; now it only logs at debug level. In a FIPS deployment that also has the non-FIPS BouncyCastle provider on the classpath, the non-FIPS provider can be chosen with no error. Ties need a deterministic rule (for example, FIPS ranked above default) or should still fail. No test covers this selection logic.

title: Non-selected providers are constructed, and their constructors mutate global JVM security state
body: The ServiceLoader stream is collected into a list before sorting, so every discovered CryptoProvider constructor runs, including those that will not be selected. FIPS1402Provider's constructor (FIPS1402Provider.java line 94) inserts a KeycloakFipsSecurityProvider at JVM security slot 1. When BCFIPS is absent it also inserts BCFIPS and BCJSSE and rewrites the ssl.KeyManagerFactory/TrustManagerFactory properties. DefaultCryptoProvider's constructor registers a non-FIPS BouncyCastle provider with Security.addProvider. Previously these side effects were followed by a hard failure when more than one provider was present. Now the multi-provider case succeeds, so the side effects persist in a JVM that runs a different provider. Discovery should avoid constructing unselected providers, for example by ranking on metadata before instantiation.

title: AuthzClient.create() can pin the process-wide crypto provider to the minimal one
body: CryptoIntegration.init is process-global and effectively runs once, using the class loader of AuthzClient. If that loader cannot see the full crypto provider (for example, when the real crypto jar is in another class loader, such as an application server module), or if an application creates an AuthzClient before anything else initializes crypto, the global provider becomes AuthzClientCryptoProvider. Because init is a no-op afterwards, later code that needs the real provider keeps getting AuthzClientCryptoProvider, and most of its methods throw UnsupportedOperationException. Before this change AuthzClient did not touch the global provider. Consider not installing a placeholder provider globally from this entry point.

title: Most provider methods throw a 'Not supported yet.' placeholder
body: About 17 methods, including getAlgorithmProvider, getCertificateUtils, getPemUtils, getKeyFactory, getSignature, getSecretKeyFact, getX509CertFactory and wrapFactoryForTruststore, throw UnsupportedOperationException('Not supported yet.'). That is leftover IDE template text, and it suggests the feature is planned. Because this provider is now a global ServiceLoader entry, callers that reach it through CryptoIntegration.getProvider() get an opaque failure. The message should say the provider is limited to ECDSA conversion, or the methods should be implemented.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JDK keystore provider, not BouncyCastle
body: The method builds a new, uninitialized KeyStore of the default type and returns its Provider, which is normally the JDK's SUN provider. Callers of getBouncyCastleProvider() that expect BouncyCastle, for example to look up algorithms by provider name, get the JDK provider silently. The method also allocates a throwaway KeyStore on every call. It should either return a real BC provider or throw UnsupportedOperationException like the other unimplemented methods.

title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER does not validate signature length
body: The method copies signature[len..2*len) without checking signature.length. A short or malformed signature triggers an unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException rather than an IOException or a clean verification failure. The method is copied from the BC implementation but is new code here, so it should check that signature.length equals signLength.

title: Dead ASN1Encoder calls whose results are discarded
body: Lines 114 and 115 create ASN1Encoder instances and discard the result. The returned DER sequence on lines 117-121 recomputes the same encodings. The dead calls look like a leftover and make the method harder to read.

title: New abstract order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: order() is added to the public CryptoProvider interface without a default implementation. Any existing implementation that does not override it, including out-of-tree providers, is not broken at compile time but throws AbstractMethodError. CryptoIntegration.detectProvider calls order() on every discovered provider, so such a provider fails during crypto initialization. A default method, for example returning 0, would keep existing implementations working.

title: Test only checks the module's own encoder and decoder round-trip
body: The assertion compares the concatenated R||S produced by asn1derToConcatenatedRS with the value obtained after encoding and decoding it again, using the same class. If both directions share a defect, or if the produced DER is not accepted by a standard verifier, the test still passes. The test should verify the DER output from concatenatedRSToASN1DER with java.security.Signature.verify, or check it against a known test vector.

title: ES384 and ES512 are tested with a P-256 key, so the real component sizes are not exercised
body: A single default EC key pair is used for ES256, ES384 and ES512, so ES384 and ES512 sign with P-256 keys. The 48-byte and 66-byte component paths are not tested with matching curves. The P-521 case matters most: R can be 66 bytes plus a sign byte, which hits the truncation branch in integerToBytes, and that path is never exercised. The test therefore gives false confidence for ES384 and ES512. Each algorithm should be tested with its own curve, P-384 and P-521.

title: Providers with equal order() are picked arbitrarily, silently bypassing the old single-provider guard
body: The old code threw when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath. The new code sorts by order() and takes the first element. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200 in this PR, so a tie is possible. Ties are then resolved by ServiceLoader/classpath order, which is not a defined contract. If a FIPS deployment has both the FIPS and the default (or elytron) provider jar on the classpath, the non-FIPS provider can be selected with no error. The only trace is a debug log line. The removed guard existed to prevent exactly this. Equal top-order providers should still fail fast, or the FIPS provider should be given a strictly higher order.

title: AuthzClient.create() installs a process-wide, one-shot crypto provider visible only to its own classloader
body: CryptoIntegration.init() is global and idempotent: it only runs detection while cryptoProvider is null, and later calls are no-ops. Here it is called with AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader(), so only providers visible from that loader are considered. If the real provider (Default, Elytron or FIPS) is only visible through another classloader, or is initialized later with a different loader, the AuthzClientCryptoProvider stub becomes the provider for the whole JVM and stays there. Every later crypto call then fails with UnsupportedOperationException. Before this PR, authz-client did not touch global crypto state at all. Consider not initializing global state from client construction, or only doing so when no provider has been set.

title: Most CryptoProvider methods are placeholder stubs throwing 'Not supported yet.'
body: getAlgorithmProvider, getCertificateUtils, getPemUtils, getOCSPProver, getIdentityExtractorProvider, createECParams, getKeyPairGen, getKeyFactory, getAesCbcCipher, getAesGcmCipher, getSecretKeyFact, getX509CertFactory, getCertStore, getCertPathBuilder, getSignature, wrapFactoryForTruststore and ECDSACryptoProvider.getPublicFromPrivate all throw UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet."). This provider is registered through the service file and is selected whenever it is the only provider present. Any code path that reaches one of these methods then fails with a message that names nothing useful. The class Javadoc ("Simple crypto provider to be used with the authz-client") does not mention these gaps. Document the supported operations, and make each unsupported operation name itself in the exception, or remove stubs that cannot be reached.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the provider of a default KeyStore, not a BouncyCastle provider
body: The method creates a KeyStore of the default type and returns its provider (typically a JDK SUN/SunJSSE provider). The method name and the CryptoProvider contract say it returns the BouncyCastle provider. Callers that use it for Signature, Cipher or other lookups will silently get a non-BC provider, which may lack the required algorithms. A new KeyStore object is also allocated on every call just to read its provider. Return the real BC provider, or throw UnsupportedOperationException like the other unsupported methods in this class.

title: New abstract order() method on the public CryptoProvider SPI breaks existing implementations
body: order() is added as an abstract interface method with no default. Any CryptoProvider implementation outside the three in-repo providers, including third-party or downstream ones, will stop compiling. If it is compiled against an older interface, it fails at runtime with AbstractMethodError when order() is called during provider sorting. A default implementation would keep existing providers loading, while the in-repo providers keep their explicit overrides.

title: ECDSA conversion test is only a self round-trip, and uses a P-256 key for ES384/ES512
body: The test asserts asn1derToConcatenatedRS(concatenatedRSToASN1DER(x)) == x. It checks the two conversions only against each other, so a shared encoding mistake (wrong DER SEQUENCE or INTEGER layout, for example) passes unnoticed. The produced DER is never checked with the JDK's Signature.verify. The key is also always generated as P-256 (KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")), so the ES384 and ES512 cases run with 32-byte R/S values padded to 48 and 66 bytes, not the real curve sizes. Verify each DER signature with the JDK verifier, and use P-384 and P-521 keys for ES384 and ES512. The 33-byte leading-zero INTEGER case should also be covered deterministically.

title: integerToBytes silently truncates over-long DER integers instead of rejecting them
body: When the decoded INTEGER has more bytes than the field length (qLength < bytes.length), the code keeps only the trailing bytes and discards the high-order ones. A malformed or non-canonical DER integer, for example r with an extra leading 0x01 byte, is turned into a different, valid-looking concatenated signature instead of an IOException. Verification then depends on the JDK rejecting the altered value. The conversion should check that the value fits in qLength bytes, allowing only a single leading zero.

title: Indefinite-length marker reaches new byte[-1] and throws an unchecked exception
body: readLength() returns -1 for the indefinite-length marker 0x80. readInteger() passes that value straight to read(), where new byte[length] throws NegativeArraySizeException. The decoder's contract reports malformed DER through IOException, which the callers declare, so malformed input to asn1derToConcatenatedRS escapes as a RuntimeException. readNext() has the same problem. readLength should reject negative lengths with an IOException.

title: Dead ASN1Encoder statements in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 build two ASN1Encoder instances, encode rBigInteger and sBigInteger, and discard the results. The returned DER comes only from the writeDerSeq call below. The dead statements suggest the values feed into the output when they do not, and they should be removed.

title: Client deletion fails under V2 because the removal listener calls an unimplemented V2 method
body: The ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, and this PR makes clients() return ClientPermissionsV2. Its setPermissionsEnabled (ClientPermissionsV2.java:193) throws UnsupportedOperationException. The exception propagates out of event publishing, so deleting any client fails when the V1 flag is also enabled. The V1 flag gate on the listener (line 77) hides this for V2-only deployments instead of fixing it. No test in the PR deletes a client under V2, so the regression is not caught.

title: Removal cleanup is gated on the V1 feature flag, disabling it entirely for V2-only deployments
body: The whole listener is now wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), the V1 flag. The base code had no guard, so under V2-only the role, group and client removal handlers ran through management(), which selects V2. With this change they never run when only V2 is enabled. Permission state for deleted roles, groups and clients is then left behind. The guard appears to be a workaround for the exception in the ClientRemovedEvent branch, not a fix. The guard should check the feature actually in use, and the V2 client cleanup should be implemented or explicitly made a no-op.

title: All-clients grants are ignored for any client that has its own resource
body: hasPermission(client, scope) only consults the 'Clients' type resource when no per-client resource exists. If a per-client permission exists for client A (for example CONFIGURE), then canManage(A), canConfigure(A), canMapRoles(A), canMapCompositeRoles(A) and canMapClientScopeRoles(A) evaluate only A's resource. An all-clients MANAGE or MAP_ROLES grant is therefore silently ignored for A but honored for every other client. This contradicts the Javadoc added in ClientPermissionEvaluator ('For V2 only: Also if the caller has a permission to ... all clients'). It is also inconsistent with canView(client), which checks the all-clients VIEW grant unconditionally via canView(). No test combines a per-client permission with an all-clients permission for clients, so this is not covered.

title: Null dereference when the 'Clients' type resource does not exist
body: getResourceTypeResource(...) returns null when the 'Clients' resource type resource is absent from the store, or when the schema does not apply. That null is passed straight to getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a check. The absence is realistic for realms whose admin permissions were initialized before this change, because init() never adds the Clients resource (see AdminPermissionsSchema.java:226). Any per-client permission check for a client without its own resource then fails with an NPE instead of returning false.

title: No upgrade path for realms already initialized before the Clients type and scopes existed
body: init() returns early when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, so realms initialized before this change never receive the new Clients resource type or the new scopes configure, map-roles-client-scope and map-roles-composite. Creating a client permission in such a realm then fails in getOrCreateResource (line 108) with ModelException 'No scopes found.', and read paths hit the null type resource in ClientPermissionsV2 line 219. The PR needs a sync step for missing resource types and scopes, or it must explain why existing realms are unsupported.

title: Authorization queries throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning a decision
body: canExchangeTo is an authorization decision, yet it throws. The same is true of isPermissionsEnabled (line 188), getPermissions (line 203) and the mapRoles/manage/configure/view Policy factories. MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns this class, so callers that previously received the inherited V1 behaviour now get a server error on these paths. The PR does not show that these callers are unreachable under V2. Returning false, or implementing the method, would be safer than a 500.

title: getResourceName has no mapping for Clients resources
body: For the USERS type, getResourceName maps the internal id to a readable username. For the CLIENTS type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is not derived from the client. Resources for clients are named with the client's internal UUID, so the result will not identify the client by clientId. The USERS branch shows the intended behaviour and the CLIENTS case is missing.

title: requireView() Javadoc describes a boolean return for a void method
body: The Javadoc for requireView() says 'Returns true if canView() returns true', but the method is void and should throw ForbiddenException when canView() is false. The same mistake appears in the Javadoc for requireViewClientScopes() (line 101). Both were added in this PR and should describe the throw behaviour, as the requireX methods above them do.

title: Dead getEvaluationContext method and unused imports copied from V1
body: getEvaluationContext is private and never called, since canExchangeTo throws. Its supporting imports (ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, EvaluationContext) exist only for it. The logger field (line 51), the TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import (line 46) and the Scope import (line 27) are also unused. This is leftover copy-paste that will confuse maintainers about what V2 actually supports.

title: canView(client) ignores per-client policies when the caller has type-level VIEW
body: canView(ClientModel) returns true as soon as canView() is true, and canView() is true for any caller holding VIEW on the all-'Clients' resource. In that case the per-client resource is never evaluated, so a negative or otherwise non-matching per-client VIEW permission is silently ignored and the client stays visible and listable. canManage(client) and hasPermission(client, ...) treat an existing per-client resource as overriding the type-level grant, and the users tests (testViewUserPermission) establish that per-object deny overrides the all-users VIEW grant. This method is inconsistent with that and lets an explicit deny be bypassed. No test covers a per-client deny on top of an all-clients VIEW grant.

title: setPermissionsEnabled throws, so the ClientRemovedEvent listener fails client deletion under V2
body: Before this PR MgmtPermissionsV2 inherited clients() from MgmtPermissions, so setPermissionsEnabled worked. Now clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled (and isPermissionsEnabled) throw UnsupportedOperationException. AdminPermissions.registerListener calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every ClientRemovedEvent, and management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 when the V2 flag is on. When the listener is active (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled alongside V2), deleting any client throws during event dispatch and the deletion request fails.

title: Removal listener gated on the V1 flag; V2-only deployments lose cleanup silently
body: The whole listener (role, client and group removal cleanup) is now wrapped in Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, the V1 flag, while the calls it makes dispatch to MgmtPermissionsV2 when the V2 flag is on. With only V2 enabled, deleting a client, group or role no longer runs any cleanup. Nothing replaces it: ClientPermissionsV2 has no removal path, so the per-client admin-permissions resource (named by the client UUID) and its attached policies stay behind. The gate is not mentioned in the PR description. The gate should follow the flag that governs the active evaluator, and V2 cleanup should be implemented rather than suppressed.

title: V2 branch of the 4-arg evaluator() drops the target realm
body: In the V2 branch, evaluator(session, realm, adminsRealm, admin) calls new MgmtPermissionsV2(session, adminsRealm, admin) and never passes realm, although MgmtPermissionsV2 has a 4-argument constructor (session, realm, adminsRealm, admin) that carries it. The V1 branch passes realm. This PR makes MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() build ClientPermissionsV2 from the realm field. Client permission checks made through this factory may therefore be evaluated against the admin's realm rather than the target realm, depending on what the 3-argument constructor assigns to realm.

title: init() never backfills the Clients resource type or new scopes for existing realms
body: init() returns early when the realm already has an admin-permissions client. Realms set up with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 before this change never receive the new 'configure', 'map-roles-client-scope' and 'map-roles-composite' scopes or the 'Clients' all-resource, and nothing else backfills them. For such realms, creating a CLIENTS permission hits 'No scopes found.' (line 108), and ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(client, ...) passes a null resource into findByResource (ClientPermissionsV2 line 219) whenever no per-client resource exists. That will fail with an NPE or wrong result on client checks. No migration or test covers this path.

title: Type-level grant is ignored when a per-client resource exists, contradicting the documented 'also if' contract
body: hasPermission(client, scope) consults the all-'Clients' resource only when no per-client resource exists. If a per-client resource exists (for example because some other client-specific permission was created), only that resource's policies are evaluated. A caller with MANAGE on all clients is then denied canManage(X) for such a client. The interface Javadoc added in this PR (ClientPermissionEvaluator) says canManage, canView, canConfigure and canMap* are also true for the 'all clients' permission, which this does not honor. Either the documentation or the precedence rule must change. canView(client) applies the opposite precedence, so the two methods disagree.

title: Inherited permission methods now throw UnsupportedOperationException on reachable paths
body: canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, the mapRoles/manage/configure/view permission factories, resource(), getPermissions(), isPermissionsEnabled() and setPermissionsEnabled() all throw UnsupportedOperationException. Previously clients() under V2 returned the inherited V1 implementation. These are methods of the public evaluator interface that existing code calls (for example the legacy token-exchange check calls canExchangeTo, and client management-permission endpoints call getPermissions/resource). A request that reaches them now fails with HTTP 500 instead of a denial or a valid response. Nothing in the PR shows that callers are guarded.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns the literal 'Clients' and omits type-level grants
body: findByType(server, 'Clients', ...) also returns the all-clients resource itself, since its name and type are both 'Clients' (created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init). If the caller holds the scope on it, the string 'Clients' is added to the result as if it were a client id. Clients covered only by a type-level grant are never added, because only per-client resources are inspected, whereas hasPermission(client, ...) falls back to the type-level resource. The result therefore disagrees with canView/canManage for the same caller.

title: getResourceName has no CLIENTS branch, so client permission resources get no readable name
body: getResourceName special-cases USERS to return the username. There is no CLIENTS branch, so client resources fall back to resource.getDisplayName(). getOrCreateResource never sets a display name for client resources, so the name shown for a client permission would be null or the internal UUID rather than the clientId. The PR adds no mapping and no test for it.

title: void require* methods documented as 'Returns true'
body: requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() are void methods, but their Javadoc says 'Returns {@code true} if ...'. They should say they throw ForbiddenException when the corresponding can* method returns false, as the other require* methods in this interface do.

title: canView(client) repeats full policy evaluations for every client in a listing
body: canView(client) first calls canView(), which evaluates the all-clients resource, then canConfigure(client), which evaluates canManage(client) and hasPermission(client, CONFIGURE), and finally hasPermission(client, VIEW). Each hasPermission call does a resource lookup and a full evaluatePermission. Checking each client in a list therefore costs several policy evaluations per client, and the type-level evaluation is repeated N times. Nothing caches the type-level result.

title: getClientsWithPermission never returns individual clients and can return the literal 'Clients'
body: getClientsWithPermission enumerates resources with resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...). Per-client resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (line 104) via resourceStore.create(...) without setting a type, so they never match the type filter. Only the all-clients resource matches, because init() sets its type. Consequence: when the scope is granted on all clients, the method adds the resource name "Clients" to the result as if it were a client id, and no individual client id is ever returned. Set the type when per-client resources are created, or look them up another way.

title: Negative per-client VIEW policy cannot hide a client from an admin with all-clients VIEW
body: canView(ClientModel) returns true as soon as canView() (the all-clients VIEW check) succeeds, before evaluating the client's own resource. Every other per-client check goes through hasPermission(client, ...), which uses the per-client resource when it exists and so honours negative policies. The user resource tests (testViewUserPermission) expect a per-object negative policy to override an all-objects positive permission. Here, an admin with all-clients VIEW and a NEGATIVE VIEW policy on a specific client still sees and can GET that client, and it still appears in listings. The short-circuit should be removed or the per-client result should take precedence.

title: Existing FGAP v2 realms never receive the new Clients resource type or scopes
body: init() returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists. Realms created before this change therefore never get the 'Clients' resource type resource or the new scopes configure, map-roles-client-scope and map-roles-composite. No migration is in this diff. Consequences: creating a client permission fails with ModelException("No scopes found.") (line 108), and getScope() throws 'Scope [...] does not exist'. Also, in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, ...) (services ClientPermissionsV2.java line 219), a missing 'Clients' resource makes getResourceTypeResource return null, and that null is passed to getPolicyStore().findByResource, which will likely throw an NPE. The String-based hasPermission on line 244 null-checks the same lookup, so the two paths behave inconsistently. Add an upgrade step or null-check the resource.

title: Client-removal cleanup is skipped in V2-only deployments, leaving stale per-client resources
body: The whole listener body is now gated on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1). Deployments that enable only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 (the mode management()/evaluator() select V2 for) therefore skip ClientRemovedEvent handling entirely. Per-client resources named by the deleted client's UUID, and scope permissions referencing them, persist after the client is deleted. The guard should check the feature that actually selects the implementation, or V2 should implement the cleanup.

title: Deleting any client fails when both fine-grained feature flags are enabled
body: The ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2. Its setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException (ClientPermissionsV2.java line 193). The listener is gated only on the V1 flag, but evaluator()/management() prefer V2 whenever the V2 flag is set, so the two flags can coexist. In that configuration every client deletion propagates the exception and fails. The V2 implementation should be a no-op here, or the event handler should skip V2.

title: Many ClientPermissionEvaluator methods throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2 mode
body: MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2, which throws UnsupportedOperationException from canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, the *Permission(...) factories, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource and getPermissions. Before this PR, V2 mode used the V1 ClientPermissions implementation for these calls, which returned values instead of throwing. Any caller that reaches these methods in V2 mode now gets an uncaught exception, which surfaces as a 500 rather than a denial. canExchangeTo is the most exposed: it is part of the evaluator contract and is used by client-to-client token-exchange logic. getEvaluationContext (line 262) is an unused private helper that looks intended for canExchangeTo, so the method seems to have been left unfinished.

title: getResourceName has no CLIENTS branch, so client permissions get a null display name
body: getResourceName special-cases only USERS. For CLIENTS it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). That value is never set for per-client resources, which are named by the client UUID (line 104), and it is also unset for the all-clients 'Clients' resource. The result is null for client permissions. The USERS branch returns 'All users' for the type resource and the username for a user resource. The CLIENTS equivalents (an 'All clients' label and the client's clientId) are missing.

title: Javadoc for requireView() says it returns a boolean, but it is a void method that throws
body: The Javadoc for requireView() reads 'Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.' The method is void and is meant to throw ForbiddenException when canView() returns false. The same mistake appears on requireViewClientScopes() (line 101). Implementers reading this doc, including the V2 class, could easily get the contract backwards.

title: New client tests omit client-scope checks, getClientsWithPermission and per-client negative policies
body: The added tests cover per-client and all-clients MANAGE, VIEW, CONFIGURE, MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE. Nothing exercises canManage/canView(ClientScopeModel), MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, getClientsWithPermission, or a NEGATIVE per-client policy overriding an all-clients permission. The getClientsWithPermission type-filter bug and the canView short-circuit would both have been caught by tests of these paths.

title: Feature-disabled and recreate exit codes are never asserted
body: The PR changes the exit-code contract that the docs tell automation to rely on: RECREATE becomes 3 and FEATURE_DISABLED becomes 4. testFeatureNotEnabled only calls assertError on the message and never checks the exit code, so a regression to 0 or 1 would pass. Likewise testWrongVersions (lines 97 and 106) asserts only error text and never checks that the recreate result exits with 3. No test covers the recreate exit code at all, even though the docs present it as the signal for CI/CD pipelines.

title: Feature gate for the 'check' subcommand is untested
body: The new feature gate was added to both UpdateCompatibilityMetadata and UpdateCompatibilityCheck, but testFeatureNotEnabled only launches the 'metadata' subcommand. The 'check' gate, which returns FEATURE_DISABLED before reading the file, has no test. Its early return is the only path that skips validateConfig and file reading for check, so a regression there would go unnoticed.

title: Null-strategy test path runs without rolling-updates, contradicting the docs
body: createInitialDeployment returns early when updateStrategy is null, so the rolling-updates feature is only enabled for non-null strategies. The docs added in advanced-configuration.adoc say the feature 'must be enabled. Otherwise, the Operator will fail.' Either that doc statement is overstated (the operator only fails when update settings are present), or the null-strategy variants of testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount run in a configuration the docs say is invalid. The PR should make the doc precise or enable the feature for the null case too.

title: Null-strategy variants run without the rolling-updates feature that the docs say is required
body: createInitialDeployment returns early when updateStrategy is null, so the rolling-updates feature is only enabled for the RECREATE variant. The operator docs changed in this PR state that while the feature is in preview 'the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the Operator will fail.' Under that statement, the testImageChange-null and testCacheMaxCount-null cases exercise a configuration the docs call invalid, and they still expect rolling/recreate upgrade status. Either the early return should also enable the feature, or the docs claim is wrong and should say the requirement applies only when an update strategy is set.

title: setEnabledFeatures replaces the whole enabled-features list with an immutable List.of
body: The call overwrites any enabled features already set on the FeatureSpec returned by getTestKeycloakDeployment, rather than adding rolling-updates to them, so any feature the base deployment enables is silently dropped for these test cases. Because List.of is immutable, any later code that appends to getEnabledFeatures() on this spec would throw UnsupportedOperationException. Merging into a mutable list would avoid both problems.

title: Changed and new exit codes (3 and 4) are a documented contract but no test asserts them
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3 and FEATURE_DISABLED = 4 is added. The update-compatibility guide presents these exit codes as the interface for CI/DevOps automation. However, UpdateCommandDistTest only checks exit code 0 (testCompatible), and testWrongVersions, which produces the recreate outcome, never asserts the exit code is 3. testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert 4 either. A regression in either code would not be caught, and the renumbering from 4 to 3 is a behavior change that the PR description does not call out.

title: Feature-disabled path is only tested for the metadata subcommand
body: testFeatureNotEnabled launches only UpdateCompatibility and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata. The equivalent feature gate added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck has no test, so a regression there (for example, the check command running without the feature) would not be caught. The test also asserts only the message, not the exit code 4 that the docs promise.

title: Exit code 4 is documented as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible', which misdescribes a precondition failure
body: Exit code 4 is returned when the rolling-updates feature is disabled and the tool never evaluates the upgrade at all. Describing it as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible' tells automation that the upgrade was assessed and found incompatible. A script that branches on 3 versus 4 could then misread a misconfigured invocation as a real compatibility result. The row should say the command could not run because the feature is disabled.

title: Feature-disabled test does not verify the documented exit code 4
body: The new FEATURE_DISABLED path exits with code 4, and the update-compatibility guide documents that code as part of the scripting contract. testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error text, so a regression that exits with 0 or 1 would still pass. The `check` subcommand's disabled path (UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run) has no test at all. The PR also renumbers RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3, and no test pins that value either.

title: Exit code 4 changes meaning: recreate moved to 3 and 4 now means feature disabled
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changes from 4 to 3 and FEATURE_DISABLED is introduced with the value 4. Any automation written against the code's previous behavior, which treated exit 4 as 'shut down before upgrade', will now read 'feature disabled' and react incorrectly. The PR does not mention this renumbering as a behavior change. The docs already listed 3 for recreate, so doc-following scripts are unaffected. Still, the change should be called out, since it alters an externally visible exit-code contract.

title: CAUTION claims the Operator always fails without rolling-updates, which is overbroad
body: The CAUTION says that without the rolling-updates feature 'the Operator will fail', without qualification. UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment(null) builds a CR with no update strategy and no rolling-updates feature, and the image-change tests expect it to work normally. The NOTE in the same section also says the default strategy mimics 26.1 behavior. The requirement should be scoped to CRs that set spec.update, otherwise users will think every CR needs the preview feature.

title: setEnabledFeatures overwrites any features already set on the CR
body: The code guards `getFeatureSpec() == null` before creating a FeatureSpec, which implies the FeatureSpec may already be populated by getTestKeycloakDeployment(true). Line 115 then replaces the whole enabled-features list with an immutable List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES) rather than adding to it. Any other features the base deployment enables are silently dropped for the RECREATE and rolling-strategy variants. Merging into the existing list would avoid this.

title: canManage() on V2 grants manage when the caller only has VIEW on groups
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). Because VIEW is in the accepted scope list, a caller whose only grant on the all-groups resource is VIEW passes canManage(). The no-argument requireManage() is what GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (POST /groups) calls, so a VIEW-only admin can create top-level groups. canView() correctly accepts VIEW and MANAGE; canManage() should accept MANAGE only. The GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() javadoc (lines 75-76) repeats the wrong 'VIEW or MANAGE' semantics. No test checks that a VIEW-only admin is denied group creation.

title: Deleting any group fails when V2 admin permissions are enabled
body: The GroupRemovedEvent listener calls management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) for every group removal. In V2 mode management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, which now returns GroupPermissionsV2. Its setPermissionsEnabled (GroupPermissionsV2 lines 173-175) throws UnsupportedOperationException. The listener runs on every group deletion, whether or not the realm uses fine-grained admin permissions. Before this PR, V2 used the V1 GroupPermissions, where this call was a no-op for realms without permissions. With both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, group deletion will likely fail with an exception propagating out of event publishing. The test cleanup in GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest (realm.cleanup().add(r -> r.groups().group(...).remove())) would hit the same path.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns internal resource UUIDs instead of group IDs
body: Callers treat the returned set as group IDs: it is set as the UserModel.GROUPS session filter in UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource, and passed to getUsersCount. Here, granted.add(groupResource.getId()) adds the internal UUID of the authz Resource record, not the group ID. The resource name is the group ID (see AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource/resolveGroup). The V1 implementation correctly uses getName() with the prefix stripped. Line 122 has the same problem: hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) looks up the resource by name, so the UUID never matches, and the code silently falls back to the all-groups resource. The all-groups 'Groups' resource is itself returned by findByType and can add its own UUID to the set. Result: user search and count are filtered by IDs that match no group, so admins with per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS lose results, and the all-groups case adds garbage IDs.

title: Group management-permissions endpoints now throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2 realms
body: MgmtPermissionsV2 did not override groups() before this PR, so V2 realms used the V1 GroupPermissions for group management permissions. The PR replaces that with GroupPermissionsV2, where isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource and the *Permission accessors all throw UnsupportedOperationException. GroupResource.getManagementPermissions and setManagementPermissionsEnabled reach these, so the endpoints return HTTP 500 in V2 mode. This is a regression for groups, and the PR does not document it or gate the endpoints with a clear error.

title: IMPERSONATE is evaluated against the target user's identity when a requester client is given
body: When requester != null, the evaluation context is built with new UserModelIdentity(root.realm, user), i.e. the impersonated target user. The IMPERSONATE scope is an admin-side permission, and the requester==null path (line 70) evaluates with the admin's identity. The two paths therefore disagree. The target-identity context was copied from V1 isImpersonatable(), which uses it for the USER_IMPERSONATED scope, where it is correct. Here, user or role policies that should match the admin (or the requesting client via kc.client.id) are checked against the victim user, so canClientImpersonate/canImpersonate(user, client) can deny legitimate impersonation or match on the wrong identity.

title: Existing FGAP v2 realms never get the Groups resource type; null is dereferenced
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists (line 250). Realms that enabled FGAP v2 before this PR therefore never receive the Groups resource or the manage-members, view-members and manage-membership scopes. getResourceTypeResource(GROUPS) then returns null. Line 147 passes that null to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource), which will likely NPE on every group check that falls back to the type-level resource. Creating a group permission in such a realm also fails in getOrCreateResource with 'No scopes found.'. This is an upgrade break unless a migration exists elsewhere, and none is in this diff.

title: init() does not add the Groups type to realms that already have admin permissions
body: The early return when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is non-null means the new GROUPS resource type, its resource and its scopes are only created for newly enabled realms. This is the upgrade gap described in the GroupPermissionsV2 finding: existing realms have no 'Groups' resource and no group scopes, and nothing in the diff backfills them.

title: Removed global canView short-circuit makes the list path evaluate policies per group
body: The previous code computed canView() once and skipped per-group checks when it was true. Now filter(groupsEvaluator::canView) calls canView(group) for every group. In V2, canView(group) runs hasPermission, which resolves the per-group resource and evaluates the authorization policy engine each time, or falls back to the all-groups resource. For admins with global view, listing N groups costs N policy evaluations instead of one. GroupResource.getSubGroups has the same change.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc references the wrong method
body: The javadoc for requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says it throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false. It should reference canManageMembers(GroupModel), which is the method it actually calls.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission javadoc says Stream but the method returns Set
body: The @return tag says 'Stream of IDs of groups with view permission', but the method returns Set<String>. The javadoc also says it returns an empty set only when canView() is true, but the implementation also returns an empty set when the caller is not in the same realm or the server is missing.

title: switch on resourceType throws NPE for null, where the old code was null-safe
body: The previous code compared with USERS.getType().equals(resourceType), which is null-safe. The new switch (resourceType) throws NullPointerException when resourceType is null, instead of the intended error path. Callers must guarantee a non-null type or the failure becomes an NPE rather than a clear validation error.

title: No test checks that a VIEW-only all-groups admin is denied group creation
body: testViewGroups grants VIEW on all groups and only checks listing. The VIEW-only canManage() bug in GroupPermissionsV2 allows POST /groups for such an admin, and nothing in this test class catches it. A negative assertion (create top-level group with only all-groups VIEW gets FORBIDDEN) is needed. Similarly, nothing checks that group user-search or count results are correct when the admin has per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS, which the group-ID bug would break.

title: Lithuanian account TOTP step text replaced with Italian
body: The `totpStep1` value is replaced with an Italian sentence ("Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:"). Lithuanian users will see Italian text on the account TOTP setup page. The value should be a Lithuanian translation of the English source ("Install one of the following applications on your mobile:"). The same copy-paste error appears in the login messages_lt.properties file.

title: Lithuanian login TOTP step text replaced with Italian
body: `loginTotpStep1` is changed to the Italian sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". Lithuanian users get Italian text on the login TOTP setup screen, and the adjacent Lithuanian lines (loginTotpStep2/3) show the file is meant to be Lithuanian. This should be a Lithuanian translation of the English source.

title: Traditional Chinese text in the Simplified Chinese bundle
body: The new `totpStep1` value uses Traditional characters and a full-width colon ("在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一："). The other lines in this zh_CN file are Simplified (e.g. totpStep2 "打开应用扫描二维码输入验证码"), so this should be Simplified Chinese ("在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：").

title: Placeholder syntax changed to Java MessageFormat in an i18next bundle
body: The key is rewritten from `{{0}}`-style to `{0}` and gets an ICU `{2,choice,...}` plural segment. Every other interpolated error key in this account UI bundle uses i18next's double-brace syntax (e.g. line 140 `'{{0}}' must have a length between {{1}} and {{2}}.`), and the UI renders messages with i18next. Single-brace placeholders will not be substituted, and unless an ICU plugin is configured the choice segment is shown literally, e.g. 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|...}.' Keep the `{{n}}` syntax and use plain plural wording here.

title: Admin UI message switched to Java MessageFormat placeholders
body: The admin console bundle is rendered by the i18next-based React UI, which uses double-brace placeholders. This change to `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` plus an ICU `{2,choice,...}` segment will leave the placeholders unsubstituted and may show the choice syntax verbatim. The same key in the server-side admin theme (themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/admin/messages/messages_en.properties) is a different bundle, and this JS-side bundle should not be changed to match it.

title: Missing English counterpart throws RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException
body: verifySafeHtml() wraps read failures in RuntimeException, and verify() only catches IOException and rethrows MojoExecutionException. Any locale file whose derived `_en` counterpart is missing (for example, `duplicate_keys.properties` maps to a nonexistent `duplicate_en.properties`, which is why the test fixture had to be renamed) escapes the Mojo as an unhandled runtime exception with a stack trace rather than a Maven plugin error. Report this through MojoExecutionException, or record it as a message.

title: Diff-offset computation can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body: start (common prefix) and end (common suffix) are each computed independently and capped only by the individual string lengths, so they can overlap. When the sanitized output is shorter than the input and the matching prefix and suffix together cover all of sanitized, `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` receives a reversed range and throws. Instead of reporting the illegal HTML, the verifier crashes. Clamp end so that start + end <= sanitized.length() (and the same for value).

title: Anchor regex also matches unrelated tags such as <abbr> and <address>
body: The pattern `</?a[^>]*>` has no word boundary after `a`, so it matches any tag starting with the letter a (<abbr>, <address>, <article>, etc.). Such tags are then handled by the anchor-matching logic and reported as "Didn't find anchor tag <abbr>..." rather than as illegal HTML, which gives a misleading message. Use `</?a(\\s[^>]*)?>` or equivalent.

title: Duplicate-key assertion weakened from exact match to hasItem
body: The original test asserted that the result contains exactly the duplicate-key message (Matchers.contains). It now uses hasItem, which still passes if extra messages appear. The rename to duplicateKeys_en.properties did not require this loosening, so the test loses its ability to catch new spurious messages for this fixture.

title: No test that a valid translation produces no messages
body:
All four tests only assert that a specific error message is present. Nothing checks the negative path: a correct translation (matching anchors, allowed tags, `
`, choice/templateHelp placeholders normalized) should produce an empty result. Without that, false positives in the verifier, like the ones the PR's bundle edits were made to work around, would go unnoticed.

title: Stray 'n' typo left in the HTML email body on the line being edited
body:
identityProviderLinkBodyHtml is edited to add the missing `

`, but the paragraph still begins with a stray character (`

nHvis du ikke vil forbinde ...`). The literal 'n' will be visible at the start of that paragraph in the rendered email. Since this line is already being changed, the typo should be fixed in the same edit.

title: Account UI error message switched to single braces and ICU choice syntax, which i18next will not render
body: The account console is a React app rendered through i18next, whose interpolation syntax is double braces. Other keys in this same file use it (e.g. `error-invalid-length-too-short='{{0}}' must have minimal length of {{1}}.`). This line changes `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` to `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` and adds the Java MessageFormat plural `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`, which i18next does not understand. Users will see literal `{0}` and `{2,choice,...}` in the validation error. The double braces were not a verifier problem, since the verifier strips the `<!-- -->` the sanitizer inserts around them, so the change is unnecessary. Restore the `{{n}}` placeholders and use wording that does not depend on ICU choice.

title: Admin UI error message switched to single braces and ICU choice syntax, which i18next will not render
body: The admin console uses i18next, whose interpolation syntax is `{{name}}`. This line changes the existing `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` placeholders to single braces and adds the Java MessageFormat `{2,choice,...}` plural, which i18next does not support. The admin UI will display literal `{0}` and `{2,choice,...}` to users for this validation message. The original double-brace form was already accepted by the verifier, so this change is a regression. Keep the `{{n}}` placeholders in this js-app file; the ICU plural only belongs in the Java-side theme message files.

title: Lithuanian login translation replaced with an Italian sentence
body: The new `loginTotpStep1` value, 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', is Italian. The file is the Lithuanian login bundle, so Lithuanian users will see Italian text on the OTP setup page. The previous Lithuanian text should be translated to match the new English wording, or the key left out so it falls back to English.

title: Lithuanian account translation replaced with an Italian sentence
body: `totpStep1` is set to 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian, in the Lithuanian account bundle. Lithuanian users will see Italian on the account console's OTP setup page. Provide a Lithuanian translation or omit the key so the English text is used.

title: Simplified Chinese account message written in Traditional Chinese
body: The new `totpStep1` value '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：' uses Traditional characters (手機, 應用程式) and a full-width colon in the Simplified Chinese bundle. Simplified-Chinese users would expect 手机 and 应用程序. The text appears copied from the zh_TW login bundle, so it should be rewritten in Simplified characters.

title: Stray 'n' typo left in the Danish HTML email body on a line this PR edits
body:
The `identityProviderLinkBodyHtml` value contains `

nHvis du ikke vil forbinde disse konti...`. The leading 'n' is a leftover from a `\n` escape and will appear in the rendered email. This line is already being modified in this PR (the closing `

` is added), so the typo should be fixed in the same edit.

title: Anchor check compares anchors by position, so reordered translations are falsely rejected
body: santizeAnchors walks the translation's anchor tags and the English anchor tags in lockstep (`englishMatcher.find()` is called once per translation anchor). Translations often reorder clauses. For English `Click here or there` and German `Oder dort oder hier`, the first translation anchor (`href="y"`) is compared with the first English anchor (`href="x"`). That reports 'Didn't find anchor tag' for a valid translation and the loop breaks, so the remaining anchors are never checked. Matching should look up each translation anchor among the English anchors (e.g. as a multiset) instead of by position.

title: Diff reporting can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when common prefix and suffix overlap
body: The start/end scan for the error message is computed independently, so the common prefix and suffix can overlap. Example: value `aXa` sanitized to `a`. start becomes 1, end becomes 1, and `sanitized.substring(1, 1 - 1)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The exception aborts verification of the whole file instead of reporting the illegal HTML. Clamp the end index so that start <= sanitized.length() - end, or compute the difference with a proper diff.

title: Missing English counterpart or I/O failure is thrown as RuntimeException, bypassing the Mojo's error contract
body: verify() is declared to throw MojoExecutionException and wraps I/O errors that way, but verifySafeHtml() throws RuntimeException on both the translation read (line 70) and the English read (line 79). A translation without a matching `_en` file, or any read failure, therefore escapes as an unhandled RuntimeException with a stack trace, aborting the whole verification run instead of producing a MojoExecutionException with the file name. Propagate these as MojoExecutionException, or record them as messages.

title: No test checks that a valid translation produces no messages
body:
All four new tests only assert that a specific violation is reported. Nothing verifies the accept path: a translation that uses allowed ``/`
` when English has HTML, a matching anchor, or a correct `{2,choice,...}` plural should yield zero messages. Without a negative fixture, false positives in the sanitizer (which the reordering and positional issues show are plausible) can regress without any test failing.

title: Duplicate-key assertion weakened from exact match to hasItem
body: The previous assertion `Matchers.contains(...)` required exactly the duplicate-key message. It was changed to `Matchers.hasItem(...)`, which also passes if extra unexpected messages are produced (for example from the new HTML checks running on the same fixture). If the extra checks should not fire for this fixture, the test should keep asserting the exact result; otherwise, the fixture should be made HTML-clean so the exact assertion still holds.

title: Lithuanian account string replaced with Italian text
body: totpStep1 was changed to the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. Lithuanian users will see this in the account console's authenticator setup. The PR only needed to drop the FreeOTP/Google Play anchors that the verifier rejects, so the value should be Lithuanian text without the anchors. The verifier cannot catch a wrong-language string because it only checks markup.

title: Lithuanian login string replaced with Italian text
body: loginTotpStep1 was changed to the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. Lithuanian users will see Italian on the OTP setup page. The change only needed to remove the anchors the verifier rejects, so the value should be Lithuanian text. The verifier cannot detect this kind of error since it only checks markup.

title: Simplified Chinese account string now contains Traditional Chinese
body: totpStep1 in the zh_CN file was replaced with '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', which uses Traditional characters (手機, 安裝, 應用程式, 之一) copied from the zh_TW bundle. Simplified Chinese users will see the wrong script. It should be Simplified Chinese, e.g. 在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：

title: error-invalid-multivalued-size uses placeholders the UI bundle will not interpolate
body: The English source was changed from double-brace placeholders to single braces plus an ICU choice: 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.' Every other error-* key in this file uses i18next-style {{n}} placeholders (see lines 14, 27, 29), so this bundle appears to be consumed through i18next. In that case {0} and {1} are not substituted and the choice expression is shown literally. The same change in js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties (line 3139) has the same problem. Keep the {{n}} form in these React-consumed bundles, or confirm the consumer really uses MessageFormat.

title: Missing English sibling aborts verification with an unchecked exception
body: If the English sibling file cannot be opened, verifySafeHtml throws a RuntimeException. verify() only catches IOException, so the exception escapes and aborts the whole plugin run with a stack trace, rather than reporting a message for the offending file. The rename of duplicate_keys.properties to duplicateKeys_en.properties in this PR is a symptom: the regex maps duplicate_keys.properties to duplicate_en.properties, which does not exist. Missing English counterparts should be reported as messages, not thrown.

title:
Valid markup such as
is reported as illegal HTML
body:
The check compares the sanitizer output byte-for-byte with the input. OWASP serializes void elements as '
', so semantically valid markup like '
' or '
' is flagged as 'Illegal HTML'. This is why the PR rewrites '
' to '
' in about 40 translation files with no content change. Any translator who writes '
' will get a false failure. Compare normalized output (for example after parsing both sides) or normalize void-element syntax before comparing.

title: Anchor pattern also matches unrelated tags starting with 'a'
body: The pattern '</?a[^>]*>' matches any tag whose name starts with 'a', such as <abbr>, <address>, <article> or <audio>. santizeAnchors then treats these as anchors, which produces misleading 'Didn't find anchor tag' messages and can pair an unrelated tag with a real anchor in the English source. The pattern should require the tag name to end at a word boundary, for example '</?a(\s[^>]*)?>'.

title: Anchor error message omits the key and file
body: The message 'Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string' does not include the message key or the file name. Every other message in this class ('Illegal HTML in key ... for file ...', 'Duplicate keys in file ...') does. A maintainer reading CI output across hundreds of translation files cannot tell which key to fix. Include the key and file path in the message.

title: Tests cover only failure cases and the duplicate-key assertion was weakened
body:
The duplicate-key assertion changed from an exact match to hasItem, and none of the new tests check the passing path. There is no fixture that should produce zero messages: allowed

/
, a matching anchor, or a choice-format placeholder in error-invalid-multivalued-size or templateHelp. Without such a fixture, false positives like the
problem and regressions in normalizeValue will not be caught.

title: isAccessTokenId never checks the grant shortcut and can throw on short prefixes
body: The new matcher has three defects. (1) The slice `substring(3, 5)` is wrong: in a token ID like `onrtac:<uuid>` the grant shortcut occupies characters 4-5 (`substring(4, 6)`), so `substring(3, 5)` yields `ta` and never equals a real grant shortcut. (2) The condition is inverted: `if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the token exactly when the grant matches. (3) `items[0]` is not length-checked, so a prefix shorter than 5 characters throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of failing the matcher. As written, the four new grant-specific assertions (CODE_TO_TOKEN, DEVICE_CODE_TO_TOKEN, REFRESH_TOKEN, AUTHREQID_TO_TOKEN) only verify the UUID suffix and never the grant. Fixing only the offset would make the matcher reject correct tokens, so the logic must be fixed together with the offset.

title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice and never checks rawTokenId
body: The second `Objects.requireNonNull` call tests `grantType` again (copy-paste error) and its message says 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'. The `rawTokenId` parameter is therefore never validated. A null raw ID would be accepted and `encodeTokenId` would produce a token ID ending in `:null`, which is then written into the access token `jti` claim and event details. The check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of an NPE, not the intended validation
body: The test sets up the factory with `init()` only and never calls `postInit()`, so `sessionFactory` is null. For the unknown grant shortcut `ac`, `getGrantTypeByShortcut` falls through to `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory and throws NullPointerException. The test catches any RuntimeException, so it passes even if the decoder's 'Unknown value ... for grant type' IllegalArgumentException path were broken or removed. The test should set up a session factory stub (or assert the specific IllegalArgumentException type and message) so it verifies the intended behaviour.

title: Shortcut doc says 3 letters, but the encoder hard-codes 2-character slots and nothing validates it
body: The Javadoc suggests 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId requires exactly 6 characters for the context (2 per slot) and encodeTokenId concatenates the shortcut as-is. A grant factory that follows this doc and returns a 3-character shortcut will get tokens minted with a 7-character prefix that the decoder rejects ('Expected length of 6'). Also, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit passes `getShortcut()` straight into a ConcurrentHashMap, so a null return causes a NullPointerException and fails server startup with no clear message. postInit should validate that each shortcut is non-null and exactly 2 characters, and the Javadoc should state that requirement.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract interface method with no default. Every existing implementation of OAuth2GrantTypeFactory outside the bundled grants (custom or downstream grant types) will fail to compile, and if the method is not implemented it will fail at runtime during postInit. A default implementation, or a documented migration note, would avoid breaking third-party SPI implementors.

title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed without replacement
body: The diff deletes the public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor from OAuth2GrantType.Context. This is an unexplained removal from a public SPI type. Any caller in the codebase or downstream that copies a context will no longer compile. The description does not mention the removal, and the new `grantType` field is not carried over by any copy path. If the removal is intentional it should be called out, or the constructor should be kept (and updated to copy `grantType`).

title: Access token jti is no longer a UUID; this externally visible change is undocumented
body: The access token `jti` claim, and the `TOKEN_ID` value written to event details, change from a plain UUID to `<6 chars>:<uuid>`. RFC 7519 allows this, but clients and log/analytics pipelines that parse `jti` as a UUID (for example into a UUID-typed column) will break. The PR does not mention this in its description, release notes, or any migration guidance. This should be documented as a visible behaviour change, and existing consumers should be checked.

title: Production encoding path (getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext) has no test coverage
body: The only unit tests exercise decode/encode round-trips from a hand-written string. Nothing tests `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext`, which is the code that actually runs in TokenManager.initToken for every access token. It has no coverage for the TRANSIENT vs ONLINE vs OFFLINE session-type selection, the lightweight vs regular token-type selection, or the fallback to 'na' when the GRANT_TYPE attribute is absent. Combined with the broken AssertEvents matcher, no test verifies the token ID that is actually issued. Tests for these cases should be added.

title: rawTokenId null check is wrong: it re-checks grantType and the message names rawTokenId
body: The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, 'Null rawTokenId not allowed') on line 73, so rawTokenId is never validated and the grantType check is duplicated. A null rawTokenId is accepted, and encodeTokenId() would then build an ID ending in ':null' that is not the generated token id. The check should be on rawTokenId.

title: isAccessTokenId grant-shortcut check is inverted and reads the wrong characters
body: In isAccessTokenId, line 483 returns false when items[0].substring(3, 5) equals the expected grant shortcut. Two things are wrong. The condition is inverted, so a match is rejected. The offsets are also wrong: the token id layout is 2 chars session type, 2 chars token type, then the 2-char grant shortcut at indices 4-5, so the code should read substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5). For 'onrtac' the code reads 'ta'. The net effect is that the grant assertion in expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh and expectAuthReqIdToToken never fails for a well-formed id, so a regression that issues tokens with the wrong grant shortcut will not be caught. For an id whose prefix is shorter than 5 characters, substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of failing the match. The comment saying the shortcut starts at the '4th char' also does not match the code.

title: Javadoc asks for 3-letter grant shortcuts, but the encoding requires exactly 2 characters
body: The getShortcut() Javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut'. The encoder does not work that way: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId reads the grant shortcut as substring(4, 6) and requires the encoded prefix to be exactly 6 characters. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit only checks uniqueness, not length. A grant implementer who follows this Javadoc returns a 3-character shortcut. encodeTokenId then succeeds and issues a token with a 7-character prefix, but that token id can never be decoded ('Expected length of 6'). The Javadoc should say 2 characters, and postInit (or encodeTokenId) should reject shortcuts of any other length.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks every existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation
body: getShortcut() is added as an abstract method with no default, so every existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation (in extensions, or test-only grant types) stops compiling until it adds the method. The PR does not mention this as a breaking change. The new postInit in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory (around line 72) also casts every OAuth2GrantType factory to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory. A grant registered as a plain ProviderFactory<OAuth2GrantType> (which the token endpoint dispatch accepts) therefore causes a ClassCastException at server startup. A default method, plus skipping or handling factories that do not provide a shortcut, would avoid both problems.

title: testIncorrectGrantType passes on any RuntimeException, including the NPE from a null sessionFactory
body: The test catches RuntimeException and does not check its type. The test factory never sets sessionFactory, so for shortcut 'ac' getGrantTypeByShortcut falls through to sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...) and throws NullPointerException. The test therefore passes without exercising the intended IllegalArgumentException for an unknown grant shortcut, and it would also pass for any other bug. It should assert IllegalArgumentException, with a stubbed session factory if needed.

title: Production path getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext and factory validation are untested
body: The tests only cover string decode/encode round-trips. They do not cover getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext, which TokenManager.initToken calls for every access token. That method decides session type (TRANSIENT/OFFLINE/ONLINE), the lightweight-vs-regular decision, and the fallback to 'na' when the grant attribute is missing. Also untested: the postInit duplicate-shortcut validation, and the refresh branches of getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut. A bug in the code path that fills every issued token id would not be caught by these tests.

title: Access token jti is no longer a UUID for every access token, with no compatibility note
body: initToken now sets the access token jti to a value like 'onrtac:<uuid>' instead of a plain UUID. Any consumer, event listener or client that validates or parses jti as a UUID will break. The PR does not document this as a change to the token format or mention a compatibility impact, and the only test updates are in AssertEvents. This should be called out in the PR description or release notes.

title: Only the standard token-exchange provider records the grant type, so other token-exchange paths encode 'na'
body: Constants.GRANT_TYPE is set only in StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient. Other token-exchange providers that issue access tokens through the same TokenManager responseBuilder path do not set the attribute. Their token ids encode the grant as 'na' (UNKNOWN), even though the grant being served is token-exchange. That undermines the grant-type purpose the PR states for the token-exchange use case. Either set the attribute in every provider that issues tokens, or document the limitation.

title: Public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) removed without deprecation
body: The public copy constructor Context(Context) is deleted in this PR. The change is unrelated to the feature and is not mentioned in the description. Any external grant implementation that calls it will fail to compile. If the removal is intentional, it should be called out, or the constructor should be kept and deprecated.

title: isAccessTokenId checks the wrong characters with an inverted condition, so the grant shortcut is never verified
body: The grant shortcut sits at index 4-5 of the encoded context (e.g. 'onrtac' -> 'ac' at 4-5), but this reads `substring(3, 5)`, which is 'ta' for that example. The check is also inverted: `if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the case where the grant matches and accepts the case where it does not. Since index 3-4 can never equal a two-letter grant shortcut in practice, the grant check is effectively a no-op. The expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken and expectAuthReqIdToToken assertions therefore only verify the 'x:UUID' shape and would accept a token minted with the wrong grant. Fixing only the negation would make every correct token fail, so both the offset and the condition need correcting.

title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice and never checks rawTokenId
body: The third `Objects.requireNonNull` call tests `grantType` again, and its message says 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'. The actual `rawTokenId` parameter is never validated, so a null raw token id is accepted silently and would later produce a token ID such as 'onrtac:null' via encodeTokenId. The check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

title: Javadoc asks for a 3-letter grant shortcut, but the encoder requires exactly 2 characters
body: The javadoc says the shortcut is 'usually like 3-letters'. The encoder (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId) requires the encoded context to be exactly 6 characters and slices the grant shortcut as two fixed characters. A grant factory that follows this doc and returns a 3-letter shortcut gets encoded into a 7-character context, and every token carrying it then fails to decode with IllegalArgumentException. The doc should state the 2-character requirement.

title: Grant shortcut is not validated for length, non-null, or character set
body: postInit takes `gtf.getShortcut()` and uses it directly as a map key. Nothing checks that it is two characters long, which the decoder depends on (length 6 check and fixed 2-char slices in getTokenContextFromTokenId), nor that it is non-null or free of ':'. A null shortcut makes ConcurrentHashMap.put throw NPE and aborts server startup. A shortcut of the wrong length is accepted silently at startup but yields token IDs that cannot be decoded. The only check is the duplicate-size comparison at line 82.

title: New abstract getShortcut() on a public SPI interface breaks existing implementations
body: `String getShortcut();` is added as an abstract method with no default. Any existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation outside the files updated in this PR (third-party extensions or any in-tree factory not listed) will fail to compile. Even compiled implementations that return null will crash server startup (see the ConcurrentHashMap NPE in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory). A default implementation or a clear upgrade note would avoid this.

title: testIncorrectGrantType passes only because of an NPE, not the intended validation
body: The test never calls postInit, so `sessionFactory` is null. The shortcut 'ac' is not in the test's map, so getGrantTypeByShortcut dereferences the null sessionFactory and throws NullPointerException. The test catches any RuntimeException and passes. It therefore does not exercise the intended 'unknown grant shortcut' path (IllegalArgumentException) and would pass even if validation were broken. It should assert the specific exception type and stub the lookup so the failure path is actually tested.

title: Only standard token exchange records the grant type; legacy token exchange tokens fall back to 'na'
body: The grant type is set on the client session context only in StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient. TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory is still registered under the legacy TOKEN_EXCHANGE feature with shortcut 'te', and this diff does not touch the legacy exchange path. Access tokens issued through the legacy path therefore get the 'na' fallback in the token ID, so the grant information this PR is meant to provide is missing for that flow. The legacy provider should set Constants.GRANT_TYPE as well, or the gap should be documented.

title: Recovery codes are written to user storage in plaintext, unlike the local DB path
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generatedCodes list (JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)) and passes that JSON to user storage via updateCredential. The local fallback in the same method persists the credentialModel built by RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...), which stores hashed codes (the codebase verifies codes by hashing input with RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode and comparing hashes). So the two storage paths hold different representations of the same secret. With this change, every recovery code is persisted in clear text in an external user store such as LDAP or a custom backend, where anyone with read access to that store can use them to log in. The method also takes both credentialModel and generatedCodes, which lets the two representations diverge. The user-storage path should store the same hashed representation as the local path.

title: Recovery codes validated in user storage are never consumed and can be replayed
body: The recovery-code branch of isValid returns true when the submitted code matches any stored code, but it never marks that code as used or updates the stored credential. The authenticator (RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator) relies on credential.allCodesUsed() to trigger regeneration and to clean up exhausted codes. For a user-storage credential that state never changes, so allCodesUsed() stays false and the same recovery code can be used indefinitely. Single-use semantics are lost for user-storage codes. This is the reference provider for the user-storage contract, so it should consume the matched code, and a test should assert that a used code is rejected.

title: Exhausted user-storage recovery codes are not removed, leaving a broken configured credential
body: The credential is now looked up with RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, which prefers the federated credential. Cleanup still calls removeStoredCredentialById, which only operates on the local credential store, so an exhausted federated credential is never removed. The credential therefore still reports configuredFor = true, and RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean then calls getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() on a credential with no unused codes, which throws NoSuchElementException on later logins. The test provider also rebuilds the credential in getCredentials without propagating the stored id (myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()), so the id passed here may not match the stored credential. Removal for federated credentials needs to go through the storage provider, or the exhausted state needs to be handled explicitly.

title: New recovery-code test only covers the happy path
