The docstring says the function 'should be called when the allowlist configuration changes', but no call site exists.

title: Docstrings contradict each other and the performance rationale is unsupported
body: The function docstring (lines 23-25) says the 60 second cache avoids expensive repeated option lookups. The NOTE in _are_all_projects_error_upsampled (lines 50-53) says the allowlist is read fresh on every call and that this is intentional. The cache at lines 30-38 contradicts the second claim. The performance rationale is asserted without measurement, and the cache adds its own round trip on every request.

title: Comments claim caching and consistency that the code does not provide
body: The comments say 'this cached result ensures consistent behavior across query execution' and describe a performance optimization. Nothing is cached in this function. The eligibility is recomputed on every _get_event_stats call, which can be up to four times per request in the split path. The transform is also applied in three separate places (lines 232-233, 276-277, 295-296). The comments mislead the next maintainer about what is cached and why.

title: Equations and orderby still use the unweighted count()
body: The rewrite is applied only to the timeseries columns. Equations from get_equation_list (line 256 in the top-events branch, and in the RPC branch) and the orderby still refer to raw count(). A request mixing count() with an equation over count() returns a weighted count column next to an unweighted equation, which is inconsistent within one response.

title: Unrelated change to a public API error message
body: The topEvents validation message changes from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This is a wording change to a public API response that the PR description does not mention and that no test update in this diff accompanies. Clients or tests matching the old string will break.

title: Bare except swallows errors and the helper changes every store_event call
body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling wraps both the lookup and the float conversion in bare 'except Exception: pass'. A malformed contexts value is silently dropped, and the test sees no sample rate with no signal. The helper is invoked unconditionally from store_event (line 1049), so it affects every test that stores an event, not just the upsampling tests. Narrow the exception handling and make the side effect explicit.

title: toInt64 truncates a float sum and can undercount by one
body: sample_weight is a non-integer float (1/sample_rate), and toInt64 truncates toward zero. A float sum that lands just below an integer, for example 9.9999999999, becomes 9. Round before casting, e.g. round(sum(...)), so the integer result is not systematically low.

title: Stray submodule-pointer file committed to the repository
body: The PR adds a file named 'sentry-repo' whose only content is 'Subproject commit a5d29095...'. This looks like a submodule pointer written as a plain file, with no .gitmodules entry. It adds a meaningless file to the tree and looks like a leftover from a local submodule operation. It should be dropped from the PR.

title: Error events are duplicated across pages and tail errors are appended to every page
body: gen_request_data is called once per paginated page with the full, time-sorted error_events list, but error_idx restarts at 0 on every call. Errors that were already emitted on earlier pages are emitted again on later pages. The trailing loop at lines 164-168 also appends every error not yet yielded, including errors that occur long after the page's segments, so each page carries the entire future error tail. For any replay that spans more than one page, the Seer summarize request receives duplicated and out-of-range error lines. The new test only covers a single segment, so this is not exercised.

title: Snuba query and nodestore fetch run on every page request, even when error context is disabled
body: The Snuba query via query_replay_instance and the nodestore fetch in fetch_error_details now run before self.paginate on every request, so each page of segment metadata re-runs them. Error IDs are also computed before the enable_error_context flag is checked (lines 87-89), so the replay query still runs when error context is turned off and its result is then discarded.

title: Error IDs are positionally zipped with a dict returned by get_multi
body: zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes get_multi returns values in the same order as error_ids and includes an entry for every ID. nodestore returns a dict keyed by node ID, which may be ordered differently or omit missing nodes. Event IDs can then be attached to another event's title/message/timestamp, and the if data is not None filter never catches a missing node. Iterate error_ids and look each node up by key instead.

title: Strict report-type enum plus batch-wide 422 drops valid reports
body: The type field is now a ChoiceField restricted to eight types, and any report that fails validation makes the handler return 422 for the whole array (lines 110-118). Browsers send batches and do not retry 4xx responses. One report of an unlisted type, such as the NEL network-error type or any future Reporting API type, causes every report in that batch to be discarded, and no metrics are recorded for them. Previously unknown types were processed. Consider skipping invalid entries and still returning 200, or at least not rejecting the whole batch.

title: Feature-flagged table path renders hardcoded empty data instead of query results
body: When organization.features includes 'use-table-widget-visualization', every table widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and a literal tableData of data: [] with empty fields and units. The actual result.data and result.meta are ignored, so enabled orgs see empty tables for every table widget. This looks like a placeholder left in the production render path.

title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is entered
body: The early return at lines 61-63 returns the sorted list untouched when the search box is empty, so is_segment, project_id and received are displayed by default. The HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES exclusion is only in the filter branch below, so those attributes disappear as soon as the user types something. The exclusion should apply in both cases.

title: Every generated repository token is the same hardcoded constant
body: FULL_TOKEN (and the truncated form) is a fixed UUID literal marked 'HARDCODED VALUES FOR TESTING'. Generate and Regenerate always display this same value, and the UI tells users to store it as their repository secret. Users get a non-random credential that is visible in the shipped bundle, and it is presented as a freshly generated token.

title: Attribute-keys query key omits the organization
body: The key is ['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions], and queryOptions contains no organization slug, although the request is org-scoped. The previous useApiQuery key included the org path. With an empty project selection (project: undefined), two organizations produce the same key, and while refetching the hook returns previous data (isFetching ? previous : data), so one org can briefly show another org's attribute keys. The retry and staleTime settings also changed from the previous hook.

title: Saved-search conversion migrations gutted and pointing to a file outside this change
body: Both 0917 and 0920 now just return, with a comment pointing to 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py. That file is not in this changeset. If it does not already exist on the base branch, org saved searches are never converted to GroupSearchView rows in any environment. The 0917 data test was also deleted, so nothing verifies the conversion. The same comment appears at 0920 line 14.

title: Owner is not checked for organization membership in this validator
body: The new owner ActorField accepts any actor, and nothing added here checks that the owner belongs to the detector's organization. test_owner_not_in_organization in test_organization_detector_index.py expects a 400 for a user from another org. Unless ActorField enforces membership (verify), detectors can be assigned owners outside the org.

title: Null max_segment_id branch in delete.py is not exercised
body: The fixture changed max_segment_id to None, but delete_matched_rows is patched out, so _make_recording_filenames and its new None early return in src/sentry/replays/usecases/delete.py never run. Nothing tests that a row with max_segment_id None yields no filenames and does not raise during deletion.

title: Analytics event recorded before the feature gate and body validation
body: analytics.record('preprod_artifact.api.assemble') runs before the features.has check and before schema validation. Requests that get a 404 (feature disabled) or 400 are still counted as assemble events, which skews adoption metrics. Move the record call after the feature check, or after successful validation.

title: Default autofix tuning silently changes from low to off for all projects
body: Projects that never set sentry:autofix_automation_tuning now resolve to off instead of low, and constants.py line 724 makes the same change. Existing customers lose automatic autofix with no opt-in or migration, and the PR description gives no rationale.

title: Removes registration of an experiment option that may still be read
body: The grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent option is unregistered. Any remaining options.get call with that key, including any code that builds option names from the parameterization pattern names, will raise for an unknown option. Confirm there are no remaining readers.

title: Unescaped issue title and environment inside PR comment markdown
body: The title is placed in the link label [**{title}**] and the environment in backticks, with no escaping. Titles containing ], newlines or markdown break the link or bullet structure of the posted comment. Titles are derived from user event data. Previously the title was outside a link, so the new wrapper makes ] a real breakage case. Sanitize newlines and brackets.

title: Per-issue event load during comment build, with broad exception swallowing
body: get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() for each of the top issues while building the PR comment, which loads an event from nodestore each time. The surrounding except Exception logs at info and returns an empty string, so real failures such as nodestore errors are effectively invisible. Narrow the exception and log at warning or above.

title: DB query injection detector now suppressed until five occurrences
body: NoiseConfig(ignore_limit=5) delays reporting of DBQueryInjectionVulnerability issues until five occurrences are seen. This is a security-relevant detector and the PR gives no rationale for the trade-off. Confirm the intent.

title: Typo 'the the' in story copy
body: The introductory paragraph reads 'Below is the the most basic example'. The duplicated word should be removed.

title: Every paginated page's Seer summary includes all error events of the replay
body: The endpoint paginates over recording segments and calls analyze_recording_segments once per page, passing the replay-wide error_events list each time. gen_request_data restarts error_idx at 0 for every page, and this trailing loop yields every error not yet consumed. Each page's Seer request therefore contains every error in the replay, including errors whose timestamps fall in other pages, so the same errors are repeated across page summaries. The new tests only exercise a single page with one error, so they pass despite this.

title: Error IDs are paired with nodestore results by position, not by key
body: nodestore.backend.get_multi returns a mapping keyed by node id that omits missing nodes, and its order is not guaranteed to match error_ids. zip(error_ids, events.values()) pairs each error id with whatever value comes next in the mapping. When any error's nodestore entry is missing (for example after retention expiry), every later error gets the title, message and timestamp of a different event. The 'data is not None' filter runs after the misalignment, so it does not prevent this. Each id should be looked up in the returned mapping.

title: Exceptions from blob deletes are silently discarded
body: pool.map returns a lazy iterator and its result is never consumed, so any exception raised by storage_kv.delete other than NotFound is never re-raised. The with-block only waits for completion. A failed blob delete (permissions, network error) produces no log or metric, and delete_replays then archives the replay anyway, leaving orphaned recording blobs with no trace. Consume the results (for example list(pool.map(...))) or submit futures and check their exceptions. This is pre-existing, but it is in a file this PR touches.

title: Feature-flagged table path renders hard-coded empty data and ignores query results
body: When the use-table-widget-visualization flag is enabled, each table widget is replaced by TableWidgetVisualization with columns set to an empty array and tableData hard-coded to empty data. This ignores tableResults, loading, result.meta, the custom field renderer and minTableColumnWidth. Any organization with the flag sees empty tables for every table widget. This looks like scaffolding and should not ship in this form.

title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is only applied when a search query is entered
body: The early return when searchQuery is empty returns the sorted list without applying the HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter. The filter only runs when the user types a search. With the default empty search, is_segment, project_id and received are shown, but they disappear as soon as any search is typed. The hidden-attribute rule should apply in both cases.

title: Comment points to a replacement migration that is not part of this change
body: The no-op body says the correct migration is 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py, but no such file appears in the changed files. 0917 and 0920 are both replaced with no-ops, and the 0917 test is deleted. If the replacement is not in this PR, org-level saved searches will never be converted into GroupSearchView rows, and the comment misleads readers. Either add the replacement or correct the reference.

title: Summary card renders with empty content when the API returns no summary
body: useFeedbackSummary returns summary as string or null. tooFewFeedbacks is only true when numFeedbacksUsed is 0 and success is false. If feedbacks were used but the LLM call failed (success false, summary null), this component still renders the 'Feedback Summary' header with an empty paragraph. The component should return null when summary is null.

title: Unescaped issue title is placed inside a markdown link in PR comments
body: The template renders '[**{title}**]({url})' with the raw issue title. Titles derive from error messages, which can be influenced by application input. A title containing ']' followed by '(' closes the link text early and lets the remaining text form an arbitrary link destination in a comment the Sentry bot posts on the PR. The environment name is also interpolated raw inside backticks. The title should be escaped or sanitized before interpolation.

title: Recommended event is loaded from nodestore for every issue in every PR comment
body: get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() and then get_environment() for each of up to five issues per comment. Each call does a nodestore fetch and a DB lookup, and this runs on every PR comment build. The environment could be fetched in a batch, or cached per issue.

title: Title truncation and environment formatting have no test coverage
body: The new _truncate_title path (titles longer than 50 characters get an ellipsis) and the non-empty environment suffix in get_environment_info are not exercised by the GitHub or GitLab PR comment tests. The existing tests use short titles and only check the happy path. A regression in truncation or the environment suffix would not be caught.

title: Validation no longer requires timestamp or age; truthiness checks skip 0 values
body: The previous dataclass required timestamp, but both age and timestamp are now optional, so a report with neither field validates. The mutual-exclusion validators use truthiness on initial_data, so age 0 or timestamp 0 combined with the other field is accepted. The checks should test for key presence and the presence of one field should be required.

title: Assemble analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag gate
body: analytics.record runs before features.has(...). Requests from organizations without the preprod-artifact-assemble feature, which receive a 404, still emit preprod_artifact.api.assemble events. This pollutes the metric with traffic from non-enrolled orgs. The record call should move below the feature check.

title: Default autofix tuning changed from low to off for every project without an explicit setting
body: Changing DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT (and the matching projectoptions default) to off changes live behavior for every project that never set sentry:autofix_automation_tuning, with no migration, backfill or release note. The tests were only updated to match the new default. This should be called out explicitly or handled with a data migration.

title: Environment filter silently dropped from the attribute keys request
body: The previous useTraceItemAttributeKeys sent environment: selection.environments to the trace-items attributes endpoint. The new makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions omits it and says it is intentionally unsupported, which contradicts the prior behavior. Attribute keys from every environment are now returned, which is a silent behavior change.

title: Analytics event name changed, breaking continuity of the View HTML metric
body: The trackAnalytics call for the View HTML click was renamed from replay.view_html to replay.view-html. Existing dashboards and queries keyed on the old name will stop receiving data for this action. The rename should be noted, or the old name kept for continuity.

title: Snuba query and nodestore fetch run on every page request, even when error context is disabled
body: The endpoint runs query_replay_instance and fetch_error_details before paginate, so both run on every paginated request, not once per replay. The Snuba query also runs when enable_error_context=false, where its result is discarded except for error_ids that are then ignored. Error details should be fetched once per replay or skipped when disabled.

title: Feature-flagged table path renders an empty hardcoded table
body: When the 'use-table-widget-visualization' flag is on, every table result is rendered through TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and a hardcoded tableData of {data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}. result.data, result.meta, the fields list, fieldHeaderMap and getCustomFieldRenderer are all ignored, so every table widget in an org with the flag shows no rows. This is placeholder wiring that should not ship; the flagged branch needs to pass result.data, result.meta and the real column config, or the branch should be removed from this PR.

title: Org saved-search conversion migrations gutted; referenced replacement migration is not in the PR
body: The conversion body of 0920 (and of 0917) is replaced with an early return. The comment points to 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py, which is not among the changed files, so no migration in this PR converts org-level SavedSearch rows into GroupSearchView. Org saved searches will silently never become views for any environment where this lands. The 0917 migration test is also deleted. Either include the replacement migration and its test, or do not remove the conversion logic here.

title: Default autofix automation tuning silently changed from 'low' to 'off' for all projects
body: DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT changes from 'low' to 'off' here, and the same change is made to the project option default in src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py line 205. Because the option default applies to every project that never set sentry:autofix_automation_tuning, this disables automatic autofix on new issues for existing projects without any explicit opt-in. Nothing in the PR description or diff justifies the behavior change; if intended it needs a rollout note, otherwise it should be reverted.

title: Strict report-type enum rejects the whole batch for any unlisted Reporting API type
body: Previously each item was only type-hinted, so any report was accepted and counted. Now type is a ChoiceField limited to 8 values, and post() returns 422 for the entire request if any single item fails. The Reporting API defines other report types (for example 'network-error' from NEL), and this endpoint exists to collect what browsers actually send. Valid reports, including ones of supported types sent in the same batch, are now dropped with a 422.

title: Snuba query and nodestore fetch run on every paginated request
body: get() now runs query_replay_instance (a Snuba query) and fetch_error_details (a nodestore multi-get over all error ids) before self.paginate. The paginator calls get() once per page, so each page request repeats both lookups even though the error list does not depend on the page. The number of error ids is also unbounded. The error context should be computed once per summary or cached, not per page request.

title: Unescaped issue title lets markdown link injection into PR comments
body: MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE interpolates issue.title raw into [**{title}**]({url}). Issue titles derive from event messages, which anyone holding a project DSN can send. A title containing '**](https://evil.example) **' closes the link text early and injects an arbitrary link into the bot comment posted on a PR. The title (and the environment name placed in backticks) should be escaped before formatting.

title: 60s processing deadline can cut check_auth_identities mid-batch and skip the reschedule
body: check_auth_identities now has processing_deadline_duration=60, but it processes up to chunk_size (100) identities sequentially, each doing an external provider.refresh_identity call. If the batch exceeds 60s the task is killed mid-loop. The trailing check_auth.apply_async reschedule never runs, and the identities after the cut-off have already had last_synced bumped by check_auth, so they are skipped until the next cycle. The deadline should be sized to the worst case or chunk_size reduced.

title: Error ids are paired with nodestore results by position, not by key
body: nodestore.backend.get_multi returns a dict keyed by node id. Its .values() order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, and missing ids are dropped, so zip(error_ids, events.values()) assigns each error id to whichever event data happens to be next. The ErrorEvent.id field is therefore wrong for some entries. Iterate node_ids and look up events.get(node_id) instead.

title: Per-issue recommended-event load added to PR comment generation just to show an environment
body: get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() for every issue (up to five per PR) while building the comment, which loads a full event per issue inside the PR-comment task. The only output is an environment name. This adds per-issue I/O on every comment refresh. Consider using environment data already available or caching it.

title: Truthiness checks let age and timestamp coexist when one is 0
body: validate_timestamp and validate_age test self.initial_data.get(...) for truthiness, so a value of 0 counts as absent. A payload with age=1 and timestamp=0 passes validation even though the spec says only one may be present, and timestamp=0 is explicitly allowed (min_value=0). Use an explicit presence check (key in initial_data / is not None).

title: New None max_segment_id branch has no test that exercises it
body: The early return for max_segment_id is None is not reached by any test. test_delete_replays_bulk.py changes a fixture row to None, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so _make_recording_filenames never sees that row. Nothing asserts that a None max_segment_id yields no filenames instead of failing on range(None + 1).

title: Empty 'Feedback Summary' box rendered when summary is null
body: The component guards only on isError and tooFewFeedbacks. useFeedbackSummary types summary as string | null and returns data.summary unchanged. When the API returns success false with feedbacks used, or summary null, the component renders the 'Feedback Summary' header with an empty paragraph. The guard should also check that summary is non-empty.

title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only filtered while a search query is active
body: The early return when searchQuery is empty returns the sorted list without applying the HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter. The filter (is_segment, project_id, received) therefore applies only when the user is typing a search, which is the inverse of the intent. By default these attributes are shown, and they disappear only once a search is entered.

title: Typo 'the the' in story text
body: The Getting Started story reads 'Below is the the most basic example of the table'. The duplicated word should be removed.

title: Authorized-user check is skipped entirely when no Integration row exists
body: When no Integration matches the installation_id, the code hits `except Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()` and never compares `github_authenticated_user` against anyone. The sender comparison (lines 501-505) runs only when a row already exists, and that row is normally written by the installation webhook. For a fresh install where the webhook has not yet been processed, any request carrying that installation_id passes without the user check. The PR describes this check as the protection against a mismatched installer, so this is fail-open in exactly the first-install case. Consider failing closed, or obtaining the installer identity from the GitHub API instead of relying on a DB row that may not exist yet.

title: KeyError on integration.metadata['sender'] for integrations without sender metadata
body: `integration.metadata['sender']['login']` assumes the key exists. Integrations created by the pipeline without a sender in state do not have it: test_basic_flow asserts the exact metadata dict, which has no 'sender' key. If such a row exists without an OrganizationIntegration (the only branch that reaches this line), reinstalling the app raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the failure page. Use a safe lookup such as `.get('sender', {}).get('login')` and treat a missing value as a mismatch.

title: Installer lookup is not scoped to the GitHub provider
body: `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` does not filter by `provider=GitHubIntegrationProvider.key`. Integration uniqueness is per (provider, external_id), so a non-GitHub integration sharing the same external_id can be returned, and its metadata then drives the GitHub authorization decision. If several rows match, `get` raises MultipleObjectsReturned, which is uncaught and produces a 500. The earlier lookup at line 478 has the same omission, but this new lookup is the one feeding the authorization check.

title: Error strings are no longer extracted for translation
body: `error()` wraps the non-literal `error_short` in `_()` at call time, and the callers pass plain English strings (for example 'Github installed on another Sentry organization.' and 'GitHub installation pending deletion.'). Message extraction only picks up literal arguments to `_()`, so these strings are no longer in the message catalogs and will never be translated. The previous code had literal `_(...)` calls at these sites, so this is a regression. Mark the strings with `_()` at the call sites instead.

title: Network failure during token exchange escapes the error handling
body: `safe_urlopen` at line 423 is outside the try block that guards response parsing, and `get_user_info` at line 434 is not guarded either. A connection error or timeout talking to github.com raises an unhandled exception, so the user gets a 500 instead of the rendered failure page. Every other failure in this view returns `error(...)`, so these calls should be guarded too.

title: installation_id is persisted to pipeline state before the state parameter is verified
body: `pipeline.bind_state('installation_id', installation_id)` runs before the `state` check at lines 412-413. A request with a wrong or forged state still overwrites the stored installation_id and then gets the error page. PipelineAdvancer sets `csrf_protect = False`, so a cross-site request can mutate an in-progress pipeline. Bind the value only after the state has been validated.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests installation-not-found
body: The test now sends a wrong `state` and asserts the generic 'Invalid installation request.' page. The 404 mock on the installation endpoint is never reached, and the 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' IntegrationError path in build_integration is no longer exercised by any test. The test name no longer matches what it asserts. Restore a test that drives the pipeline through build_integration with a 404, or rename this test and add a separate case.

title: No test covers successful verification or the new token and user-info failure branches
body: test_github_user_mismatch covers only the negative case. Nothing verifies that the pipeline completes when the webhook sender matches the authenticated login (octocat). The new failure branches in OAuthLoginView (missing access_token, missing login from get_user_info, and state mismatch aside from the one in test_installation_not_found) are also untested. These are the security-relevant paths this PR adds, so the positive case and each failure branch should have a test.

title: GitHub user check is skipped entirely when no Integration row exists yet
body: When no Integration row exists for `installation_id`, the `except Integration.DoesNotExist` branch returns `pipeline.next_step()` before the new authenticated-user check (lines 501-505) runs. That check only executes when an Integration already exists with `metadata["sender"]`, which the installation webhook normally creates. The webhook is delivered asynchronously while the browser is redirected back to Sentry, so if the browser returns first, or the webhook is delayed or dropped, the pipeline completes without verifying that the authenticated GitHub user is the one who installed the app. This fail-open path defeats the guarantee the PR describes. The check should fail closed when there is no installer record to compare against, or the installer identity should be obtained another way.

title: KeyError when an existing Integration has no sender metadata
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError if the Integration row has no `sender` key. `build_integration` only writes `sender` when the pipeline state contains one (lines 376-377), and integrations created by the pipeline without a webhook do not have it (test_basic_flow asserts metadata with no sender). This line is reached for any Integration row that exists without an OrganizationIntegration, so the install flow returns a 500 instead of the error page. Use `.get()` and return `error(...)` when the sender is missing.

title: Installer check compares mutable GitHub logins instead of immutable user IDs
body: The check compares `login` strings. GitHub usernames can be renamed, and the old name then becomes claimable by another account. The webhook `sender` payload and the `/user` response both include the numeric `id`, which is immutable. If the installer renames their account and another user claims the old login, that second account would pass this check. Comparing `id` values would close this gap.

title: Integration lookups for the security check are not scoped by provider
body: The lookups at lines 478 and 494-496 filter only on `external_id` and not on `provider`. `external_id` is unique only per provider, so `get` can raise an unhandled MultipleObjectsReturned (500), or it can return a non-GitHub row whose metadata is then used for the sender comparison at line 503. The lookup used for the security decision should include `provider=GitHubIntegrationProvider.key`.

title: Network and API failures during token exchange and user lookup are not handled
body: `safe_urlopen` at line 423 and `get_user_info` at line 434 are not wrapped in error handling, unlike the body parsing at lines 425-429. A connection failure, timeout, or non-2xx response from GitHub propagates out of the view and produces a 500 instead of the failure page that the rest of this view renders. These calls should be wrapped so the view returns `error(request, self.active_organization)`.

title: Installation now hard-requires GitHub OAuth client credentials
body: The new step reads the GitHub OAuth client ID and secret (lines 394-395) and places the client ID into the authorize URL without checking that it is set. On deployments that have the GitHub App configured but not GitHub login OAuth credentials, the authorize URL contains `client_id=None`, so users are sent to a GitHub error page and cannot install the integration. This new requirement is not mentioned in the PR description.

title: No test for the success path of the new installer check or for the skipped-check path
body: The only test exercising the new check (`test_github_user_mismatch`) covers the failure case. Nothing verifies that a webhook-created Integration whose `sender` matches the OAuth user completes the pipeline. Nothing covers an installation with no Integration row yet, which is the path where the check is skipped entirely (see the fail-open finding in integration.py). Both cases need tests.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the not-found path
body: The original assertion for 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' was removed. The test now sends a mismatched state, which fails at the state check before `build_integration` runs. The `IntegrationError` raised on a GitHub API 404 (integration.py lines 352-357) is therefore untested, and the `responses.replace(... status=404)` mock is never hit. Restore coverage by sending a matching state, or keep the original test.

title: Installer check is skipped when no Integration record exists yet
body: The new sender check (lines 501-505) runs only after the `except Integration.DoesNotExist` branch above has returned. When no Integration row exists for the installation_id (the installation webhook has not been processed, or never reaches Sentry, e.g. a self-hosted instance without webhook delivery), this line returns pipeline.next_step() immediately. The OAuth-authenticated GitHub user is never compared with the user who installed the app, and build_integration then links the installation to the org. test_basic_flow exercises exactly this path (no webhook posted, authenticated user 'octocat', no check), so the PR's main guarantee does not hold in the default path. Someone handed an installation_id belonging to another GitHub account can complete the install whenever the webhook record has not landed yet. The installer must be verified on this path too, or the pipeline must fail closed.

title: KeyError when an existing Integration has no sender metadata
body: integration.metadata['sender']['login'] assumes every existing Integration has a 'sender' entry. build_integration only writes sender when state.get('sender') is truthy (lines 376-377), so Integrations created by the pipeline without a webhook-provided sender, or created before this metadata existed, lack the key. For such a row that is ACTIVE but has no OrganizationIntegration, this line raises KeyError and the request returns a 500 instead of the error template. Use a safe lookup and treat a missing sender as a failed verification that renders the error page.

title: Integration lookup is not scoped to the GitHub provider
body: Both lookups by external_id=installation_id (this one and the one at line 478) omit provider=GitHubIntegrationProvider.key. external_id is only unique per provider, so the row found may belong to another provider and has no GitHub 'sender' in its metadata. The new check then indexes metadata['sender'] on a non-GitHub integration. Before this PR that case fell through to next_step. Add the provider filter to the lookup.

title: Network and HTTP failures in the OAuth exchange escape as 500s
body: safe_urlopen (line 423) is outside the try block, so a connection error or timeout raises out of the view instead of rendering the failure template; the try only guards reading the body. get_user_info (line 434) is also unguarded, so if it raises on a non-2xx response or on undecodable JSON, the user gets a 500 rather than the 'could not verify' page. Wrap the token exchange and user lookup and route failures to error(...).

title: No test covers a successful install through the sender check or the new OAuth failure branches
body: test_basic_flow never posts an installation webhook, so it never reaches the Integration-exists branch with a matching sender. The only test of that branch (test_github_user_mismatch) covers rejection. Nothing verifies that the matching installer is accepted with the check active. The new OAuth failure branches (state mismatch at integration.py line 412, missing access_token at line 431, missing login at line 435) have no tests either. Add a case that posts the installation event with sender 'octocat' (the stubbed /user login) and expects success, plus cases for a bad state and a failed token exchange.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the not-found path
body: The test now sends a wrong state (ddd023...), so it fails at OAuthLoginView's state check and returns 'Invalid installation request.'. The original assertion for 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' (the 404 branch in build_integration, integration.py line 356) is no longer exercised anywhere in this file, despite the test name. Restore that assertion using the valid state, and keep the bad-state case as a separate test.

title: Mismatch test asserts only a generic error that every failure path shares
body: The mismatch test asserts only 'Invalid installation request.', which is the message for every failure in this pipeline: state mismatch, failed token exchange, missing login, missing Integration, and sender mismatch. It would still pass if the OAuth exchange broke, so it does not prove the sender check fired. It also does not assert that no OrganizationIntegration was created for org_2, which is the security-relevant outcome. Assert the absence of the OrganizationIntegration and/or give the sender mismatch its own error text.

title: `queued` default timestamp is fixed at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, not per instance. Every AssignmentSource created in a process therefore carries the same import-time timestamp, so `queued` is wrong for all real assignments. It is also serialized into `assignment_source_dict` and passed as Celery task kwargs, where every other value is a primitive. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` or drop the field if nothing reads it.

title: New keyword is passed unconditionally to every integration's sync_assignee_outbound
body: The task now always calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue, user, assign=assign, assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`, even when there is no source (None). Previously integrations only received `external_issue`, `user`, and `assign`. Any integration implementation that does not accept `**kwargs` will now raise TypeError on every outbound assignee sync, including ones unrelated to loop prevention. The only tests touching this path mock `sync_assignee_outbound`, so real implementation signatures are never exercised. Either verify that all implementations accept the kwarg, or pass it only when a source is present.

title: Abstract sync_status_outbound gains an assignment_source parameter nothing uses
body: The `assignment_source` parameter is added to the abstract `sync_status_outbound` contract, but no caller in this PR passes it and no implementation consumes it. Integrations reading this signature will assume the source is meaningful for status sync. The parameter is dead API surface and should be removed unless status sync is meant to honour the source in this change.

title: from_dict silently returns None, which drops the loop guard
body: `from_dict` swallows ValueError/TypeError and returns None without logging. Callers treat None as 'no assignment source', so the outbound sync propagates to every integration, including the one that originated the change, which is the exact loop this PR is meant to stop. An extra or renamed key in the dict (for example from a future schema change during a rolling deploy) would silently disable the guard. Log the failure or fail loudly.

title: No test that other integrations still receive outbound updates when the source is a different integration
body: The new test only checks that an assignment whose source matches the target integration is not propagated. The guard in `should_sync` is meant to block only the origin integration, with the comment saying 'This should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward'. Nothing asserts that an assignment sourced from integration A still reaches a different linked integration B. An over-broad guard, such as one that skips all integrations whenever a source is set, would pass the current tests.

title: Deassign path with a matching assignment source is not tested
body: Unassignment from an inbound webhook also generates an outbound update, and the description names unassign as part of the loop. `sync_group_assignee_inbound` passes `assignment_source` to `deassign`, but no test checks that deassigning with a source matching the linked integration skips the outbound `sync_assignee_outbound` call. The only deassign test passes no source, so a regression in the deassign wiring would go unnoticed.

title: queued default is evaluated once at import, not per instance
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created in the process carries the same process-start timestamp instead of the time the assignment was queued. The value is serialized into the Celery task payload via to_dict(), so the recorded time is wrong for every event. It should use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

title: from_dict silently fails open, disabling the loop guard with no log
body: from_dict() swallows TypeError and returns None. `cls(**input_dict)` raises TypeError for any unknown key, so a payload written by a newer producer that added a field (or any malformed payload) yields None. The sync_assignee_outbound task then treats the assignment as having no source, should_sync() stops blocking the originating integration, and the Jira -> Sentry -> Jira cycle this PR is meant to stop comes back. Nothing is logged, so the regression is invisible. The safety check fails open silently; at minimum the parse failure should be logged.

title: New task kwarg breaks mixed-version workers during deploy
body: sync_group_assignee_outbound now always sends an `assignment_source_dict` key in apply_async kwargs (None when there is no source). Messages enqueued by the new code during a rolling deploy will be consumed by workers still running the old sync_assignee_outbound signature, which has no such parameter, so they fail with an unexpected-keyword TypeError. That exception is not in the retry exclude list, so the messages retry and are then dropped. The rollout ordering or signature compatibility should be addressed and called out.

title: No test that a different source integration still propagates outbound
body: The new test only covers the case where the assignment source is the same integration as the linked external issue. Nothing verifies the other half of the contract stated in the code comment: a source from a different integration must still propagate outward. A bug that suppresses all outbound sync whenever assignment_source is set would pass the whole suite. A case with a second integration as the source, asserting that the outbound call happens, is needed.

title: to_dict test cannot detect the queued timestamp bug and no round-trip test exists
body: test_to_dict only asserts `queued is not None`, which passes even with the import-time default. There is no test that `AssignmentSource.from_dict(source.to_dict())` round-trips, although that is the exact path the Celery task uses to rebuild the source from the payload. A round-trip test and a check that queued reflects creation time are missing.

title: New assignment_source parameter on sync_status_outbound is never passed or used
body: The abstract sync_status_outbound gains an `assignment_source` parameter, but nothing in this PR passes it and no implementation reads it. Status sync is not gated on the source at all, so the parameter suggests protection that does not exist while changing an abstract contract that implementers must now consider. It should either be wired through and used or removed.

title: Task now passes new positional and keyword args to every installation
body: The task calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` positionally and `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)` unconditionally. Any installation whose should_sync override still takes one argument, or whose sync_assignee_outbound does not accept **kwargs, will raise TypeError on every assignment. The new tests mock ExampleIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound with a MagicMock that accepts anything, so they cannot catch this. The concrete integration implementations are not in this diff and should be checked.

title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import, so every instance gets the same timestamp
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass default, so `timezone.now()` runs once when the module is imported. Every AssignmentSource created in that process then carries the process-start time, not the time the assignment was queued. The value is serialized by `to_dict()` into the task payload. It should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. The existing `test_to_dict` only asserts `queued is not None`, so it would not catch this.

title: The actual inbound-webhook loop path and the deassign path are untested
body: The new test calls `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` directly with a hand-built `AssignmentSource`. Nothing verifies that `sync_group_assignee_inbound` (the entry point used by the Jira webhook) passes `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` through to `assign`/`deassign`. The `deassign` path with a matching source, which this PR also changes, has no test. The `assignment_source_dict` parsing in `sync_assignee_outbound` and the `should_sync` source-exclusion logic have no direct tests either. Without these, a regression that drops the source on the inbound path would reintroduce the loop with a green test suite.

title: Loop check excludes the whole integration, not the originating external issue
body: The check `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` suppresses outbound assignee sync to every external issue of that integration linked to the group. A group linked to two Jira issues on the same Jira site would no longer receive assignee updates to issue B when issue A's assignee is changed by an inbound webhook. The description only mentions preventing the echo back to the triggering issue. This suppression of legitimate updates to other linked issues is not mentioned or tested.

title: New positional argument to `should_sync` and new kwarg to `sync_assignee_outbound` break existing overrides
body: The task now calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` and `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)` on every installation. Any installation subclass that still overrides `should_sync(self, attribute)` or a concrete `sync_assignee_outbound` without `**kwargs` will now raise TypeError, even when no assignment source is involved. The PR does not show a check that all overrides were updated.

title: Unused `assignment_source` parameter added to the abstract `sync_status_outbound` contract
body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature gains an `assignment_source` parameter, but no caller in this PR passes it and no implementation is required to use it. The docstring still describes only the status propagation. This is a misleading contract change for implementers, unrelated to the assignee fix.

title: `to_dict()` puts a raw datetime into a dict passed as a Celery task argument
body: `asdict(self)` keeps `queued` as a `datetime`. This dict is passed as `assignment_source_dict` in `apply_async` kwargs (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py, around line 141). A datetime is not JSON-native, so the type does not survive a JSON-serialized task round trip, and the consumer receives a string instead. Serializing `queued` to an ISO string, or excluding it, would make the payload type-stable.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with only `pass` as its body. StatefulDetectorHandler declares several abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`), so this class raises TypeError on instantiation. `Detector.detector_handler` calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)` with no guard, so any detector whose type is `metric_alert_fire` will crash in `process_detectors`. Before this PR the class was instantiable and returned an empty result list. Either keep it as a non-stateful handler or implement the abstract members. The PR description also says the new hook 'can be implemented', but it is declared `@abc.abstractmethod`, which forces every stateful handler to implement it, including ones that never emit occurrences. Making the hook optional with a default would avoid this.

title: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe expects a fingerprint for the wrong group key
body: The expected occurrence is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...)`, so its fingerprint is `["<detector_id>:val1"]`. The assertion then calls `evaluate_group_key_value("group_key", 10, ...)`, and the hook builds the occurrence with fingerprint `["<detector_id>:group_key"]`. IssueOccurrence is a dataclass, so the equality check on `DetectorEvaluationResult` compares the fingerprint and fails. The fixture should be built with `"group_key"`.

title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: The docstring says evaluate 'returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`', but the signature and implementation now return a dict keyed by group key. The docstring should describe the dict return shape, since callers such as process_detectors now rely on it.

title: Stale TODO says the handler will become stateful
body: The comment 'This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction' is now wrong. The class already subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler in this same change, so the comment misleads readers about its current state.

title: New abstract hook has no contract documentation
body: build_occurrence_and_event_data is a new abstract extension point that every stateful detector must implement, but it has no docstring. It does not say when it is called (only on state changes to a non-OK priority), what event_data should contain (it is passed through to produce_occurrence_to_kafka), or whether the occurrence's fingerprint must match build_fingerprint(group_key). The resolve path uses build_fingerprint, so a mismatch would split issues. Subclass authors have no way to learn these rules from the code.

title: Expected occurrences are built with values that do not match the evaluated values
body: In test_results_on_change and test_dedupe the expected occurrence is built with value 6, but the evaluated values are 100 and 8. The helper ignores `value`, so the tests pass, but no test verifies that the hook receives the correct value and new_status from evaluate_group_key_value. A regression that drops or swaps those arguments would go undetected.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: The stub body was reduced to `pass`, but the class subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler`, which declares `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and (newly in this PR) `build_occurrence_and_event_data` as abstract. The class therefore remains abstract. `Detector.detector_handler` calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, which now raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. Previously the handler was concrete and returned `[]`. `process_detectors` does not guard this call, so any detector whose type resolves to `metric_alert_fire` would abort processing for the whole data packet. The handler needs concrete implementations of the abstract members, or a test should cover instantiation so this is caught.

title: test_dedupe builds the expected occurrence with the wrong group key
body: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` the expected occurrence is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...)`, but `evaluate_group_key_value` is called with group key `"group_key"`. The mock occurrence's fingerprint is derived from the group key (`[f"{detector.id}:{group_key}"]`), so the expected `IssueOccurrence` has fingerprint `...:val1` while the actual one has `...:group_key`. The other tests in this file compare occurrences by value, so the first `assert ... == expected_result` fails. The expected occurrence should be built with `"group_key"`.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: The docstring of `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` says it 'returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`', but the signature and implementation now return a dict keyed by group key. Subclass authors read this docstring as the contract, so it should describe the dict return value.

title: Stale TODO says the handler will become stateful later
body: The comment says this will be a stateful detector once that abstraction is built, but this same change makes `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` a `StatefulDetectorHandler` subclass. The TODO is now misleading and should be removed or reworded.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with only `pass` in its body. StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and (new in this PR) `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, none of which are implemented. Instantiating the class raises TypeError. The class is registered as the `detector_handler` of the `metric_alert_fire` GroupType, and `Detector.detector_handler` calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, so any detector of that type now raises inside `process_detectors` instead of being a no-op as before. The previous `evaluate` stub returned [] and worked. Either implement the abstract methods or keep this handler non-stateful. The TODO on line 10 ('This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction') is also now stale.

title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: The docstring says evaluate 'returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`', but the signature and implementation now return a dict keyed by group key. Callers relying on the docstring would expect list semantics and the wrong container type.

title: test_dedupe in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue expects an occurrence whose fingerprint does not match the evaluated group key
body: The expected occurrence is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...)`, so its fingerprint is `["<id>:val1"]`. The test then calls `evaluate_group_key_value("group_key", ...)`, and the real code builds the occurrence with fingerprint `["<id>:group_key"]`. IssueOccurrence is a dataclass, so the `== expected_result` assertion compares unequal fingerprints and fails. The group key in the expected occurrence needs to be "group_key".

title: Test helper ignores its `value` argument, so the hook's value propagation is untested
body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts `value` but never uses it. Tests also pass unrelated values (6 in tests where the evaluated value is 100, 8, or 10), so the tests cannot catch a bug where the hook uses the wrong value to build the occurrence or event data. The helper should include the value in the occurrence (e.g. evidence or subtitle) and the tests should pass the actual evaluated value.

title: Occurrences are produced to Kafka before detector state is committed
body: `process_detectors` now calls `create_issue_occurrence_from_result` for every result (line 62) before `handler.commit_state_updates()` (line 68). Previously this path was effectively dead for stateful detectors, so this PR enables real production. If the state or dedupe commit fails after the Kafka produce succeeds, the dedupe value and state are not advanced. The same data packet is then reprocessed, the status is still OK or the old state, and a new occurrence with a new id is emitted again. Consider committing state first, or documenting and accepting at-least-once duplicate occurrences.

title: Schedule-type conversion is computed into `config` but the original config is returned
body: In `get_monitor_environment_context`, `config` is a copy of `monitor.config` and the code rewrites `config["schedule_type"]` to the display string. The returned dict then uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the uncopied original), so the rewritten value is discarded and the monitor context on the incident event carries the raw schedule_type value. The copy-and-rewrite is dead code. This bug was carried over verbatim from mark_failed.py, but since the function is being relocated it should either return `config` or drop the unused rewrite.

title: get_failure_reason docstring examples do not match what the function returns
body: The docstring (and the typo 'humam readible' on line 132) gives example outputs the function cannot produce. For two missed, one timeout and one error check-in, the code returns "2 missed, 1 timeout and 1 error check-ins detected", not "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected". The "A failed check-in was detected" example (line 136) also never occurs: single failures yield "An error check-in was detected", "A missed check-in was detected" or "A timeout check-in was detected" from SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP. Since the function is being moved into a new module, the docstring should be corrected to match actual output.

title: Renamed and relocated symbols have no compatibility shim and no test updates in this PR
body: This PR renames `mark_failed_threshold` to `try_incident_threshold` and `create_issue_platform_occurrence` to `create_incident_occurrence`, and removes `SimpleCheckIn`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context` and `HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP` from `mark_failed.py` without re-exporting them. Any test or module that does `mock.patch("sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence")` or imports one of these names from `mark_failed` will now fail with AttributeError or ImportError. The PR changes no test files, so the monitors test suite needs to be checked and updated to the new module paths before merge.

title: Monitor context ignores the schedule_type translation it computes
body: In get_monitor_environment_context, `config` is a copy of monitor.config with `schedule_type` replaced by the display string (lines 160-162), but the returned dict uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original, untranslated object) on line 168. The computed `config` is dead code, so the event's `contexts.monitor.config.schedule_type` carries the raw stored value instead of the intended display text. The bug was carried over unchanged from mark_failed.py, but this PR is the point where the function gets a new home, so it should be fixed here or tracked explicitly.

title: get_failure_reason docstring examples do not match what the function returns
body: The docstring says the output is "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected" and "A failed check-in was detected". The code actually produces "2 missed, 1 timeout and 1 error check-ins detected" (the per-status text from HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP is joined and followed by " check-ins detected"). The singular case returns one of "An error check-in was detected", "A missed check-in was detected", or "A timeout check-in was detected"; there is no generic "A failed check-in" string. The docstring also has the typo "humam readible". Anyone maintaining the message text will be misled by these examples.

title: Module-level names removed from mark_failed without updating any importers or mocks
body: This change removes `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `SimpleCheckIn`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, and the status maps from mark_failed.py, and renames two of them (`create_issue_platform_occurrence` -> `create_incident_occurrence`, `mark_failed_threshold` -> `try_incident_threshold`). The diff touches only four files, so any remaining `from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed import ...` or `mock.patch("sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence")` (for example in tests) will fail with ImportError or AttributeError. The author should confirm with a repo-wide grep that no references remain, and call out the rename in the PR description.

title: Moved and renamed symbols removed from mark_failed with no re-exports or test updates
body: This PR deletes `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `SimpleCheckIn`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, and `HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP` from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`, and renames two of them (`mark_failed_threshold` to `try_incident_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence` to `create_incident_occurrence`). Nothing is re-exported. Any remaining `from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed import ...` will fail with ImportError, and any `mock.patch("sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence")` or similar will fail with AttributeError. The changed-file list contains no test files. Either no references exist anywhere in the repo, which should be confirmed with a grep, or the test suite is left broken by this change.

title: get_failure_reason docstring has a typo and examples that do not match the actual output
body: The docstring says "humam readible" (typo). Its examples are also wrong. The two-category example at line 135 says "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected", but the code produces "2 missed, 1 timeout and 1 error check-ins detected", since the per-status count is inside get_text_list and the suffix is applied once. The single-failure example at line 136 says "A failed check-in was detected", but no code path produces that string. The single-failure path returns "A missed check-in was detected", "An error check-in was detected", or "A timeout check-in was detected". The docstring was copied over unchanged during the move, so it now misdescribes the function that lives in its new module.

title: Restart path no longer kills hung spawn-context flusher processes
body: The restart path only calls `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Processes created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process` are `SpawnProcess` instances, which derive from `BaseProcess` and are not subclasses of `multiprocessing.Process`. So the check is False in production and the old process is never killed. The pre-change code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally (catching only ValueError), so this is a regression. Consequence: when a flusher is detected as hung (stale `healthy_since`), it keeps running while a replacement is started on the same shards. If the old process recovers, two flushers run concurrently against the same Redis shards, which can produce duplicate or fragmented segments to buffered-segments. Each restart also leaks a live process. Fix by killing any process that supports kill (e.g. check against `multiprocessing.context.BaseProcess`), and add a test that exercises the restart path.

title: join() never terminates spawn-context flusher processes
body: The `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check is False for `SpawnProcess` objects (the type returned by the spawn context used at line 53), so `process.terminate()` is never called in `join()`. The loop was rewritten in this PR, but the check is still wrong. If a flusher is still alive after the join timeout, it is left running until the parent exits. The check should use `BaseProcess` or a duck-typed check.

title: Unused `_create_process_for_shard` would orphan a live process if called
body: `_create_process_for_shard` is added but never called in this PR. If it is called, it invokes `_create_process_for_shards`, which starts a new process and overwrites `self.processes[process_index]` without killing or joining the existing process. The old process is then unreferenced and keeps flushing its shards. Either remove the dead method or make it kill the existing process first.

title: The added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op, so the test is still racy
body: The test patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at line 15 via monkeypatch. The `time.sleep(0.1)` added here therefore does nothing, despite the comment saying it gives flusher threads time to run. `step.join()` then sets `stopped` while the flusher thread may not yet have called `flush_segments` after the drift change. The `(msg,) = messages` assertion can then fail intermittently. The wait should be a real deadline loop that polls `messages`, or the sleep reference should be captured before patching.

title: Inconsistent metric tag keys: "shards" vs "shard" with comma-joined values
body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses the tag key "shards" (line 199), while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` (line 185), `segment_size_bytes` (line 195), and `flusher_unhealthy` (line 244) use "shard". For multi-shard processes, the "shard" value is a comma-joined list, while `flusher_unhealthy` uses a single integer shard id under the same key. Dashboards and alerts that group by `shard` will not line up across these metrics, and the `wait_produce` series changes identity from untagged to tagged. Use one tag key and one value format across all flusher metrics.

title: Docstring says one process per shard, but the default is a single process
body: The class docstring says the flusher "Creates one process per shard". The code actually creates `min(max_processes, len(shards))` processes, and the consumer's `--flusher-processes` option defaults to 1. With default settings, all shards are handled by one process. The docstring and the help text should say this accurately.

title: Unrelated guideline added to a span flusher PR
body: The new "Use hasattr() for unions" anti-pattern section has nothing to do with the multiprocessed span flusher change. It should be split into its own PR so the change history stays reviewable and the guidance can be discussed separately.

title: isinstance check makes kill() a no-op for real flusher processes
body: `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is never true for the processes this class creates. `self.mp_context` is the 'spawn' context, whose `Process` is `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. That class derives from `BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.context.Process`, so the check is False and `process.kill()` is skipped. Before this PR the code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally (catching only ValueError), so this is a regression. Consequence: when a flusher is hung (alive but `process_healthy_since` is stale), it is never killed. `_create_process_for_shards` then starts a second process for the same shards while the hung one keeps flushing the same Redis segments. That can produce duplicate segments to buffered-segments and leaks a live process on every restart. Only the thread path (used in tests) reaches the guarded code, so the tests do not catch this. Fix by testing against `BaseProcess` or by checking `hasattr(process, 'kill')`.

title: join() never terminates spawned flusher processes on timeout
body: The termination in `join` uses `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, which is False for `SpawnProcess` objects (see the same check in `_ensure_processes_alive`). So after the deadline passes, no flusher process is terminated. They are daemon processes, so they keep running until interpreter exit, possibly still flushing to Redis and producing to Kafka after the consumer has shut down and its shards may have been reassigned. This code was already broken before this PR. The PR rewrote this loop to cover all processes and kept the broken check, so it should be fixed in the same change.

title: Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op, so the test still races
body: The test starts with `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, which patches `time.sleep` for the whole process. The `time.sleep(0.1)` added at line 62 therefore does nothing, although the comment says it gives flusher threads time to observe the drift change. The test still depends on the flusher thread running a flush iteration with drift 9000 before `step.join()` sets `stopped`. If it doesn't, `messages` is empty and `(msg,) = messages` fails. The test is flaky as written. Wait for the message to appear (e.g. poll with a deadline), or capture a real sleep before patching.

title: wait_produce metric uses tag key 'shards' while all other flusher metrics use 'shard'
body: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses the tag key `shards`. The produce timer and segment_size metric in the same function, and flusher_unhealthy, all use `shard`. Dashboards or monitors that group by `shard` will not match this series, and the naming is inconsistent within a single change.

title: Docstring says one process per shard, but the defaults do not
body: The class docstring says the flusher 'Creates one process per shard'. The consumer's `--flusher-processes` option defaults to 1, so production runs one flusher for all shards. The factory default of None gives one process per shard. The `max_processes` cap also limits the count. The documentation does not describe these defaults, and the consumer default contradicts the PR description's 'a process per redis shard'.

title: Unused _create_process_for_shard duplicates a similarly named method
body: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is never called. The code calls `_create_process_for_shards` (plural) instead. Two near-identical method names that do different things are a maintenance hazard. Remove the dead method.

title: Negative --flusher-processes crashes startup with KeyError
body: `flusher_processes` is passed through with no validation. A negative value makes `self.num_processes = min(max_processes, len(shards))` negative, so `process_to_shards_map` is empty. The loop then does `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index]`, which raises KeyError during consumer startup with an unhelpful message. A value of 0 silently falls back to one process per shard. Validate the option (minimum of 1) in the CLI definition or in the constructor.

title: --flusher-processes defaults to 1, so the per-shard flusher is not enabled by default
body: The PR's stated goal and the SpanFlusher docstring (flusher.py lines 31-32) say the flusher runs one process per redis shard. But the new CLI option defaults to `1`, and SpanFlusher caps process count at `min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))`. With the default, all shards in the consumer are flushed by one process, so the deployed behavior is essentially unchanged unless the flag is set explicitly. The factory default (`flusher_processes=None` in factory.py line 41, which becomes `len(shards)`) is per-shard, so direct construction and the CLI disagree. Either the CLI default should match the stated design, or the description and docstring should make clear that the flag must be raised to get the new behavior.

title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op here, so the flusher-thread wait is a race
body: `test_basic` monkeypatches the global `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at line 15. `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 therefore returns immediately, and the comment 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' is not true. `step.join()` then sets `stopped`, and the flusher thread may exit without running a flush iteration that sees drift=9000. The test then fails at `(msg,) = messages`, or passes only by scheduling luck. The extra `step.poll()` at line 60 also does nothing useful, since SpanFlusher.poll only forwards to next_step. The test should wait on the expected output (for example, poll with a real timeout until messages appear) instead of relying on a sleep that the test itself disabled.

title: join() breaks out of the loop without terminating the remaining flusher processes
body: In the new join loop, once `remaining_time <= 0` the `break` at line 341 exits the loop before the `terminate()` at line 347 for every remaining process. In the old single-process code, the deadline only ended the wait and the process was still terminated. Now, if the deadline is hit during process i, process i is terminated, but processes i+1..n are neither waited on nor terminated. They keep running and can be mid-flush or mid-produce after join() returns. The termination should happen for every process that is still alive, independent of the deadline.

title: Inconsistent metric tag key: 'shards' here vs 'shard' on the sibling timers
body: The `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer uses the tag key `"shards"` (plural), while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` (line 185) and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` (line 194) use `"shard"`. Dashboards or monitors filtering on `shard` will not see wait_produce data, and it cannot be grouped with the other flusher metrics. The `shard` tag values are also comma-joined shard lists here, while `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` (line 244) emits one integer shard per series, so per-shard breakdowns are not consistent across these metrics.

title: _create_process_for_shard is dead code and nearly duplicates _create_process_for_shards
body: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is added but never called. `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards` directly. The two near-identical names make it easy to call the wrong one, and the unused method suggests a restart-by-shard path that does not exist. It should be removed or wired in.

title: New parameter inserted before produce_to_pipe changes the positional signature
body: `flusher_processes` is inserted before `produce_to_pipe`, so any caller that passes `produce_to_pipe` positionally (the 7th argument) now binds it to `flusher_processes`. If a callable reaches `SpanFlusher`, `min(self.max_processes, ...)` in flusher.py raises TypeError when the consumer starts. The new parameter should be added after `produce_to_pipe`, or the call sites should be confirmed to use keyword arguments.

title: New test only checks counts; per-process restart and shard flushing are untested
body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` asserts only the number of processes, `max_processes`, `num_processes`, and that the shard map sums to 4. The new logic that matters most is not exercised: each process flushing exactly its own shards, `_ensure_processes_alive` restarting a single multi-shard process (including the per-process MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS accounting), per-process backpressure in `submit`, and the case where `flusher_processes` exceeds the number of shards. A regression in the shard-to-process mapping or restart path would not be caught.

title: Unrelated documentation change bundled into a span flusher PR
body: The added 'Use hasattr() for unions' anti-pattern has nothing to do with the multiprocessed span flusher. It should be split into its own change so the reviewed PR stays scoped to the flusher and its consumer option.

title: close() shuts down the factory-owned queue pool, so the next rebalance silently drops every message
body: FixedQueuePool is created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__, and the same instance is passed to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy that create_with_partitions builds. Arroyo closes the strategy and builds a new one on each partition revoke/assign. close() (and join(), which calls close(), and terminate()) calls self.queue_pool.shutdown(), which shuts down every queue and stops every worker permanently. The next strategy's submit() then calls work_queue.put() on a shut-down queue, which raises queue.ShutDown. submit()'s generic except (lines 317-325) logs and marks the offset complete, so the message is never processed but its offset is committed. Every message after the first rebalance is skipped this way. Items still queued at shutdown never complete their offsets, so the shared OffsetTracker also stops committing for those partitions for the rest of the consumer's lifetime. No test creates a second strategy from the same factory, so this is not caught.

title: Arroyo commit callback is invoked from a background thread while the processor loop runs
body: _commit_loop calls commit_function every second from a separate daemon thread. commit_function forwards to the Arroyo Commit callable that create_with_partitions received. Other commit paths in this codebase (CommitOffsets, the batch paths) call Commit from the StreamProcessor's own thread. Arroyo's commit path updates consumer staging and commit state that the processor loop also owns, so this unsynchronized cross-thread call can race with the poll/commit cycle. The consequence could be lost or duplicated offsets or exceptions from the Kafka consumer. Nothing in the PR synchronizes these calls. The unit and integration tests replace commit with a plain dict update, so they cannot surface this.

title: Shutdown stops the commit thread before draining queues and abandons queued work
body: close() joins the commit thread (line 337) and only afterwards calls queue_pool.shutdown() (line 338). Workers then finish processing whatever is still queued, but no commit is ever issued for those completions. The next owner of the partition reprocesses them, producing duplicate uptime results. Separately, FixedQueuePool.shutdown() sets worker.shutdown = True (line 234) before shutting the queues down. Workers check that flag after each item (loop at line 129) and exit, so items still sitting in the queue are never processed and their offsets never complete. This contradicts the 'graceful shutdown' docstring and leaves outstanding offsets that block later commits.

title: Docstring promises backpressure, but the queues are unbounded
body: The docstring claims 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', but the queues are created with queue.Queue() and no maxsize (line 185), and submit() never blocks.
