body: `getClient` fetches a new access token and stores it in the DB, but then constructs `new jsforce.Connection({ ..., accessToken: credentialKey.access_token })` using the *old* token from the credential instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` (and `instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url` instead of the refreshed `instance_url`). The refresh is therefore pointless: all subsequent API calls still use the expired token and will fail with 401/INVALID_SESSION_ID.

title: Salesforce refreshes the token and writes the credential on every service instantiation
body: The new refresh_token request and `prisma.credential.update` run unconditionally inside `getClient`, which is called from the constructor. There is no expiry check (unlike every other app, which only refreshes when the stored token is expired). Every Salesforce CalendarService creation — including availability lookups — now issues a token request to `login.salesforce.com` plus a DB write, which wastes requests, risks hitting Salesforce's OAuth rate limits, and adds latency to the booking path. Gate the refresh on the stored expiry.

title: Refresh success is checked via `response.statusText !== "OK"`
body: `statusText` is not guaranteed to be populated (HTTP/2 and several fetch implementations return an empty string for a 200 response), so this check can throw `HttpError` with an empty message on a perfectly successful token refresh, and it also treats any non-200 2xx as success. Use `response.ok` / `response.status` instead.

title: zoho-bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(fn, "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` — the third parameter of `refreshOAuthTokens` is the Cal.com `userId`, which is sent to the external sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. Passing the credential's id means that, with credential sharing enabled, the self-hosted endpoint is queried for the wrong user, so either the request fails or (worse) another user's tokens are fetched and stored on this credential. `refreshAccessToken` should receive and forward `credential.userId`.

title: Zoom sends appSlug "zoomvideo" while the app's slug is "zoom"
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoomvideo", credential.userId)` sends `appSlug=zoomvideo` to the credential sync endpoint, but the Zoom app's slug everywhere else in the codebase (and in the `App` table / the new `/api/webhook/app-credential` lookup) is `zoom` — see `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` which creates the credential with `appId: "zoom"`. The self-hoster therefore receives an identifier that does not match the slug it must post back, so Zoom credential syncing cannot work without a special case.

title: Credential sync request carries no authentication and its status is never checked
body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no shared secret/signature (contrast with the inbound webhook, which requires `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). The remote endpoint therefore cannot distinguish a request from Cal.com from any other caller, so an endpoint implemented as documented hands out user access tokens to anyone who can reach it. The response status is also never checked, so an error page/HTML body is passed on to the caller as if it were a token response. A signed header (or reuse of `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) and an `response.ok` check are needed, and the expected request/response contract should be documented.

title: Unvalidated request body and decryption failures produce unhandled 500s; no HTTP method guard
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a `ZodError` on a malformed payload, and `symmetricDecrypt(...)` / `JSON.parse(...)` throw on a bad key or non-JSON plaintext. None of these are caught, so the handler returns an unhandled 500 (with a stack trace in the logs/response depending on config) instead of a 400 with a useful message. There is also no method check, so a `GET`/`DELETE` to this route reaches the body parse and 500s. Use `safeParse` + explicit 400s and restrict the handler to POST.

title: Synced credential update does not clear the `invalid` flag
body: When a credential already exists the handler only updates `key`. Credentials that were previously marked `invalid: true` (e.g. by `invalidateCredential` in the Zoom/Webex adapters, or the `invalid_grant` path in Google Calendar) stay flagged after fresh working keys are pushed in, so Cal.com keeps treating the app as broken and shows the "reconnect" state even though the parent application has supplied valid tokens. The update should also set `invalid: false`.

title: Webhook secret compared with `!==` (non constant-time) and header lookup is case-sensitive
body: The shared secret check uses a plain string comparison, which is vulnerable to timing analysis; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. Additionally, `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME]` relies on the operator configuring a lowercase header name (Node lowercases incoming header keys); if they configure `Calcom-Webhook-Secret` every request silently 403s. Lowercase the configured name before the lookup instead of only documenting the requirement in `.env.example`.

title: No tests for the new credential-sync webhook or token parsing helper
body: This PR adds a new unauthenticated-by-default HTTP surface that writes OAuth credentials into the database (`/api/webhook/app-credential`) plus two shared helpers (`parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens`) that are now on the refresh path of ~10 apps, and ships with no unit/integration tests (the PR description confirms this). Given that the helpers change the stored credential shape for Google, Office365, Salesforce and others, regressions here silently break every user's calendar/video integrations. At minimum, tests covering secret rejection, create vs update behaviour, and the enabled/disabled branches of the two helpers should be added.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService
body: `prisma.credential.update(...)` is called inside `getClient()` but the file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` (imports are only getLocation, WEBAPP_URL, HttpError, logger, types, getAppKeysFromSlug, parseRefreshTokenResponse). This will fail type-check/build, and at runtime throws `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` on every Salesforce calendar operation, making the Salesforce app completely unusable.

title: Google Calendar credential key is overwritten with a zod SafeParse result object
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns the whole `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed object, yet the result is stored directly: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the credential object. After the first token refresh the DB row becomes `{"success":true,"data":{...}}`, so the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in the constructor throws and the user's Google Calendar integration breaks permanently (requires reconnect). Either return `.data` from the helper or use `...data` here.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys that evaluate to "[object Object]"
body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are computed property names; a Zod schema object has no meaningful `toString()`, so both evaluate to the same literal key `"[object Object]"` and the second declaration overwrites the first. The effective schema is therefore `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`. Because Zod strips unknown keys by default, parsing a sync-endpoint response drops `expiry_date`/`expires_in`/`refresh_token` and everything else. Consumers (office365calendar, zoomvideo, salesforce) then persist a credential key containing only `access_token`, so the token is treated as permanently expired (or fails later schema validation) and a refresh is triggered on every call. The intent ("allow any extra properties, assume a numeric property is the expiry") needs `z.object({access_token: z.string()}).passthrough()` or `.catchall()`.

title: Credential-sync branch returns a raw fetch Response while callers expect app-specific shapes
body: When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the `Response` of the POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, but several callers pass a `refreshFunction` whose return type is not a `Response`: hubspot's `tokensApi.createToken()` returns a token object and the caller reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` / `.accessToken`; zoho-bigin and zohocrm use axios and read `tokenInfo.data`; googlecalendar reads `res?.data`. With sync enabled these all read `undefined` off a `Response`, producing `NaN` expiry dates, `setAccessToken(undefined)` and corrupted credential rows instead of a working token. The helper needs to normalise the sync response to the same shape each caller expects (or each caller must branch explicitly).

title: zoho-bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects a userId
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(fn, "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` – the third argument of the helper is `userId` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. Passing the credential id means the self-hosted endpoint is asked to refresh tokens for an unrelated (or non-existent) user, which at best fails and at worst returns another user's access token. `refreshAccessToken` only receives `credentialId`/`credentialKey`, so the credential's `userId` must be threaded through.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token"
body: When the refreshed-token response has no `refresh_token`, the code sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. This placeholder is then persisted into the credential key by callers (e.g. office365calendar, zoomvideo, salesforce). On the next refresh the provider is called with the bogus value `"refresh_token"`, which fails with invalid_grant and can mark the credential invalid — overwriting a previously valid refresh token with garbage. If the intent is "keep the existing refresh token", it must copy the old value from the stored credential instead of inventing a string.

title: Salesforce now performs an unconditional token refresh on every service instantiation, and discards the new token
body: `getClient()` unconditionally POSTs to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` with `grant_type=refresh_token` each time a `SalesforceCalendarService` is constructed — there is no expiry check as in the other apps. This burns Salesforce OAuth rate limits (and adds latency) on every booking operation. Worse, the refreshed token is written to the DB but the `jsforce.Connection` below is still created with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token` (the old token), so the refresh has no effect on the current request and an expired credential still fails.

title: Salesforce refresh failure check relies on `response.statusText === "OK"`
body: `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: response.statusText })`. `statusText` is not guaranteed: HTTP/2 responses (which Salesforce serves) have an empty `statusText`, so a perfectly successful 200 response is rejected with an empty error message, and conversely error bodies are reported without any detail. Use `response.ok` / `response.status` and include the response body in the error.

title: Webhook does not restrict HTTP method and crashes with 500 on malformed input
body: The handler accepts any HTTP method (GET included) and calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` plus `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` without try/catch. A bad body, a wrong encryption key, or non-JSON plaintext throws out of the handler, returning an unhandled 500 with a stack trace instead of a 400 with a useful message. Validate the method (POST only) and wrap parse/decrypt in error handling that returns 400.

title: Updating a synced credential does not clear the `invalid` flag
body: When an existing credential is found, only `key` is updated. If the credential had previously been marked `invalid: true` (which Cal.com does on invalid_grant, e.g. in googlecalendar/zoom/webex), pushing fresh working keys leaves `invalid` set, so the credential continues to be treated as broken and the app stays unusable for the user. The update should also reset `invalid: false`.

title: Webhook secret compared with `!==` (timing-unsafe) and header lookup is case-sensitive
body: The shared secret is compared with a plain string inequality, which leaks information through timing; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. Additionally `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME]` relies on the operator setting the header name in lowercase (Node lowercases incoming header keys); if an uppercase name is configured the lookup silently returns `undefined` and every request is rejected with "Invalid webhook secret". Lowercase the configured name before the lookup.

title: Request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication and its status is not checked
body: The POST to the self-hoster's credential sync endpoint sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no shared secret, signature or bearer token, so the endpoint handing out OAuth access tokens cannot verify that the caller is Cal.com and effectively has to be an unauthenticated public endpoint. (The inbound webhook does verify `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; the outbound call should do the equivalent.) The response status is also never checked, so a 4xx/5xx body is passed downstream and parsed as if it were a token.

title: Zoom sends appSlug "zoomvideo" which is not the app's slug
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoomvideo", credential.userId)` sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, but the Zoom app's slug (used for `appId` in `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` and looked up by the new `/api/webhook/app-credential` endpoint) is `zoom`. A self-hoster keying their sync endpoint off the slug they receive from the webhook will not match the slug sent on refresh, so Zoom token refresh via credential sync silently fails. Other apps in this PR pass real slugs (e.g. `msteams`, `google-calendar`), so this is an inconsistency, not a convention.

title: Webex refresh still validates with the strict schema, so credential sync responses are rejected
body: Webex was switched to `refreshOAuthTokens` but still parses the result with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse(responseBody)`, which requires `scope` to equal the exact literal `"spark:kms meeting:schedules_read meeting:schedules_write"`, plus `token_type`, `refresh_token` and `refresh_token_expires_in`. The documented sync-endpoint contract is "only the access token and expiry date", so with credential sharing enabled every Webex refresh rejects with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". It should go through `parseRefreshTokenResponse` like zoom/office365/salesforce.

title: No tests for the new credential-sync webhook or token-parsing helpers
body: The PR adds a publicly reachable endpoint that writes third-party OAuth credentials into the database plus two shared helpers (`parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens`) used by ~10 app integrations, with no unit or integration tests. Given the defects that are easy to introduce here (secret verification, decryption, schema shape, which branch of the helper is taken), tests covering: disabled sharing → 403, wrong secret → 403, unknown user/app → 404, create vs. update path, and the minimum-token-response parsing would prevent regressions in all app refresh flows.

title: Team permission check uses AND instead of OR
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. A user is either an admin or an owner, never usually both in the sense these helpers test, so the expression is almost always false for a team admin and, despite the variable name, this does not grant admins access. The result is that team admins (and in many membership models owners too, if `isTeamAdmin` returns false for role OWNER) cannot add guests to their team's bookings even though the name/intent says they should. This should be `||`.

title: EventManager built from the caller's credentials, not the booking organizer's
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` fetches the credentials of the logged-in caller, and the EventManager is constructed with `{...user, credentials}`. Since this endpoint is reachable by attendees and team admins (not just the organizer), the calendar/video update in `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will be attempted with credentials that do not own the external calendar event, so the attendee update silently fails (or targets the wrong account). The credentials and destination calendar should come from the booking's organizer (`booking.user`).

title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw input list instead of the actually-added guests
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered input array. In `email-manager.ts` this list decides who receives the "you were invited" (`AttendeeScheduledEmail`) vs the "guests added" notice. Any email the caller submitted that was already an attendee (filtered out into `uniqueGuests`) will therefore receive a brand-new booking confirmation email again instead of the add-guests notification. `uniqueGuests` should be passed instead.

title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, allowing bypass and duplicate attendees
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lower-cased but the incoming `guest` string is not, so `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` can be trivially bypassed by submitting a different case (e.g. `Spam@Example.com`). The same case-sensitivity applies to the existing-attendee comparison `guest === attendee.email`, so the same address in a different case is inserted again, producing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails. Both comparisons should normalize case.

title: No limit or de-duplication on the guests array server-side
body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no max length and no uniqueness constraint; the uniqueness/validity checks only exist client-side in `AddGuestsDialog`. Any authenticated user who is an attendee of a booking can POST hundreds of arbitrary addresses and the handler will create an attendee row and send a booking email to each one, turning the endpoint into an email-sending relay (spam/abuse vector) and bloating the booking's attendee list. Add a `.max(...)` bound and de-duplicate (case-insensitively) in the schema/handler.

title: No validation of booking status or time before adding guests
body: The handler accepts any `bookingId` and never checks `booking.status` or whether the booking is in the past. The UI only exposes the action for upcoming/confirmed bookings, but the tRPC mutation is directly callable, so guests can be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED or long-past bookings, which then triggers confirmation/ics emails for an event that no longer exists. It also does not account for `seatsPerTimeSlot`: adding attendees to a seated event bypasses the seat limit and creates attendees with no seat reference.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event type disableStandardEmails settings
body: Unlike every other sender in this file (e.g. `sendLocationChangeEmails`), `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no `eventTypeMetadata` and never calls `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`. Event types configured with `disableStandardEmails.all.host`/`.attendee` will still send host and attendee emails when guests are added, violating the user's explicit email-suppression setting.

title: Team hosts never notified because the CalendarEvent has no team data
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` loops over `calendarEvent.team?.members` to notify co-hosts, but the `evt` built in `addGuests.handler.ts` never populates `team` (the booking query selects `eventType` without team/hosts). For team events, only the primary organizer is emailed and the branch is dead code.

title: Subject line dereferences attendees[0] without a guard
body: `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` will throw a TypeError if `calEvent.attendees` is empty, which would reject the whole `sendAddGuestsEmails` promise chain. Other organizer templates guard this; use optional access or fall back to the organizer/team name.

title: Email failure swallowed without the error details
body: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards `err`, so a mail delivery or template failure leaves no diagnosable trace. Use the project `logger` and include `safeStringify(err)` plus the booking id.

title: Invalid-email banner is never cleared and empty submit is a silent no-op
body: `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` is only called by the Cancel button; on a successful mutation (or when the user corrects the input) the flag stays true, so the red "Emails must be unique and valid" message is still displayed the next time the dialog is opened via the dropdown. Additionally, when the user removes all email rows, `handleAdd` returns early with no toast or message, so clicking "Add" appears to do nothing.

title: New UI component imports from its own package barrel, creating a cycle
body: `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui`, while `packages/ui/index.tsx` re-exports this very module (via `MultiEmailLazy`). This self-referential cycle can resolve to `undefined` components at runtime depending on module evaluation order/bundler, producing "Element type is invalid" render errors. Import the components by relative path (as the sibling form components do) instead of through the package barrel.

title: No tests for the new addGuests mutation
body: The PR adds a new authenticated mutation that writes attendees and sends emails, with non-trivial authorization logic (organizer / attendee / team admin), blacklist filtering and duplicate filtering, but no unit or integration tests were added. Regressions in the permission branches would silently allow or deny guest additions; the AND/OR bug in the team check is exactly the kind of defect a test would have caught.

title: Team permission check uses AND instead of OR
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. A user can be either an admin or the owner, not normally both as reported by these two helpers, so this expression is effectively always false and team admins/owners who are neither the booking organizer nor an attendee will always get a FORBIDDEN error. It should be `||`. (Also note `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` queries membership for team id 0 for personal bookings, which is a misleading fallback.)

title: Guest list is not de-duplicated or case-normalized before insert
body: `uniqueGuests` only filters guests that exactly match an existing attendee email and non-lowercased blacklist entries; it does not de-duplicate the incoming array itself. The tRPC input schema (`addGuests.schema.ts`) also allows duplicates. A direct API call with `guests: ["a@a.com", "a@a.com"]` (or `A@a.com` for an existing attendee) will create duplicate attendee rows for the same booking, producing duplicate emails and corrupt attendee lists. Dedupe case-insensitively server-side and compare existing attendee emails case-insensitively.

title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive against a lowercased list
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased when parsed from `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, but the incoming guest email is compared raw (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Any blacklisted address submitted with different casing (e.g. `Spam@example.com`) bypasses the blacklist and is added as an attendee, defeating the purpose of the environment variable. Lowercase the guest before comparison.

title: Emails are keyed off the unfiltered input list, not the actually-added guests
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input array instead of `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, membership in this list decides whether an attendee gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` ("you were invited") or the "guests added" notification. If a submitted email was filtered out because it is already an attendee, that existing attendee incorrectly receives a brand-new booking confirmation email instead of the guests-added notice.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email-disable metadata
body: Every other sender in this file (e.g. `sendLocationChangeEmails`) guards with `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` and accepts an `eventTypeMetadata` argument. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and always sends to both host and attendees, so event types configured with `disableStandardEmails` will still send organizer and attendee emails, violating that setting.

title: CalendarEvent is built without team info, so team hosts are never notified
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` loops over `calendarEvent.team?.members` to notify co-hosts, but the `evt` constructed here never sets `team` (the booking query doesn't load the event type's hosts/users either). For team or round-robin bookings, no team member other than the booking owner receives the guests-added email, unlike the location-change flow which populates team members.

title: ICS attachment lacks iCalUID/sequence, likely creating duplicate calendar entries
body: The `evt` passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails` sets only `uid` and omits `iCalUID` / `iCalSequence` (both stored on the booking). The generated ICS is sent with `method: "REQUEST"`, so recipients' calendar clients will treat it as a new invite with a different UID rather than an update to the existing event, resulting in duplicate calendar entries for the attendees who already had the booking.

title: findFirstOrThrow with `booking.userId || 0` throws an opaque 500 for bookings without a user
body: `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` will throw a Prisma `NotFoundError` (surfacing as an untranslated INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR to the client) for any booking whose `userId` is null, e.g. dynamic group bookings. Handle the null case explicitly with a proper TRPCError, or derive the organizer from the already-included `booking.user` relation.

title: No guard against adding guests to seated, cancelled or past bookings
body: The handler adds attendees to any booking regardless of `status` or `seatsPerTimeSlot`. For seated event types, remaining seats are derived from the attendee count and each real seat has a `BookingSeat` reference; inserting plain attendees here silently consumes seats without seat references, corrupting seat availability. For past or cancelled bookings (the "Edit" actions menu is also rendered for past confirmed bookings in BookingListItem), new guests receive a confirmation email and ICS for an event that already happened. Validate booking status and reject seated event types.

title: MultiEmail imports its own package barrel, creating a circular dependency
body: `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui`, while `packages/ui/index.tsx` re-exports `MultiEmailLazy` -> `MultiEmail`. This import cycle can yield `undefined` components at runtime depending on module evaluation order, and it pulls the entire UI barrel into the dynamically imported chunk, defeating the purpose of the lazy wrapper. Import the components from their concrete module paths (e.g. `../components/button`, `../components/form`) as the other `form/*` components do.

title: Error toast shows raw tRPC error code and the fallback message is dead code
body: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` is always a non-empty string, so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` can never fall back to the friendly message. Users will see strings like `FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission` (and `undefined: ...` when `err.data` is missing). Build the message from the translated key only, falling back to `unable_to_add_guests`.

title: Invalid-email error never clears and empty list silently does nothing
body: `handleAdd` sets `isInvalidEmail` to true on failure but never resets it to false on a subsequent successful validation or on dialog reopen, so the "Emails must be unique and valid" warning stays visible after the user fixes the input. Additionally, when the user removes all email rows (`multiEmailValue.length === 0`), clicking Add returns silently with no user feedback.

title: Subject line dereferences attendees[0] without a guard
body: `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` will throw a TypeError if `attendees` is empty, and renders an empty name when the first attendee has no name (newly added guests are created with `name: ""`). Other organizer templates guard this (e.g. fall back to the organizer/team name). Since the email send is wrapped in a bare `catch` in the handler, such a failure would be silently swallowed and no organizer email sent.

title: Email failure is swallowed without logging the error
body: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards `err` entirely, so any failure to notify guests/organizers is undiagnosable in production. Use the project `logger` and include the error and bookingId.

title: Copy-pasted comment claims a 40kb payload
body: The comment "These are like 40kb that not every user needs" was copied from the PhoneInput/AddressInput lazy wrappers. `MultiEmail` is a small component with no heavy third-party dependency, so the comment misstates the reason for the dynamic import and will mislead future maintainers.

title: New mutation has no tests
body: `addGuestsHandler` contains non-trivial authorization logic, guest filtering/blacklisting and email fan-out, but no unit or e2e test is added in this PR. At minimum the permission matrix (organizer / attendee / team admin / unrelated user) and the duplicate/blacklisted-guest filtering should be covered, since the authorization expression is currently inverted and would have been caught by a test.

title: Team permission check uses AND of isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both an admin *and* the owner. Despite the variable name, a team ADMIN who is not the owner will be denied, and the combined condition is effectively "is owner" only. This should be an OR (or a single role check). Consequence: team admins who are legitimately allowed to manage team bookings cannot add guests. It also issues two extra DB queries with `teamId ?? 0` for personal bookings.

title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, allowing bypass and duplicate attendees
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lower-cased, but the incoming `guest` string is never normalized, so `Blocked@Example.com` passes the blacklist filter while `blocked@example.com` would be blocked. The duplicate check `attendee.email === guest` is likewise case-sensitive, so an existing attendee can be added again with different casing, creating a second attendee row and duplicate emails for the same person. Normalize (trim + lowercase) guest emails before both checks and before persisting.

title: Input guest list is not de-duplicated server-side
body: The filter only removes guests that already exist as attendees or are blacklisted; it does not de-duplicate the `guests` array itself. The client dialog enforces uniqueness, but the tRPC endpoint is callable directly, so `guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"]` creates two attendee rows for the same email on the booking, which then receive duplicate emails and show up twice in the booking UI and calendar event. De-duplicate (e.g. via a Set) before `createMany`.

title: Calendar/video update uses the acting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` build the EventManager from the session user, while `evt.destinationCalendar` is derived from the booking's organizer/destination calendar. When a team admin/owner or an attendee (both allowed by the permission check above) adds guests, the handler will try to update the organizer's calendar event with the wrong account's credentials, so `updateCalendarAttendees` silently fails or targets an unrelated calendar and the external event is never updated with the new guests. The organizer's credentials (`booking.user.credentials`, already fetched) should be used.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw input instead of the actually-added guests
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered input array. In `email-manager.sendAddGuestsEmails`, membership in this array decides whether an attendee gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (new-booking style) or the `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` notification. Any email the caller submitted that was filtered out because it is already an attendee therefore receives a brand-new "booking confirmed" email instead of the "guests added" notification. `uniqueGuests` should be passed instead.

title: Email failure is swallowed without logging the error
body: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards `err` entirely and uses `console.log` rather than the project `logger`. If sending fails (bad SMTP config, template error) there is no stack trace or context (bookingId, guests) to debug with, and the mutation still reports success to the user.

title: No validation of booking status; guests can be added to cancelled, rejected or past bookings
body: The handler only checks existence and permissions. It never inspects `booking.status` or `booking.endTime`, so a caller can add guests to a CANCELLED/REJECTED booking or to one that already ended; in each case new attendee rows are created and "guests added" emails with a CONFIRMED ICS (`status: "CONFIRMED"`, `method: "REQUEST"`) are sent out, which can re-create a cancelled event on recipients' calendars. The UI also surfaces this action for past bookings (editBookingActions is rendered for past/confirmed bookings), so the server must reject these cases.

title: Attendees are created without seat references for seated event types
body: For event types with `seatsPerTimeSlot`, every attendee is normally paired with a `BookingSeat` record (seatsReferences). This handler inserts attendees directly via `attendees.createMany` with no seat reference and without checking remaining seat capacity, so seated bookings end up with attendees that have no seat uid. Those guests cannot cancel/reschedule via the seat flow and the booking can exceed its configured seat count.

title: No upper bound on the number of guests accepted
body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()` constraint. Any authenticated user who is an attendee or organizer of a booking can submit an arbitrarily long list of arbitrary email addresses; each one is persisted as an attendee and receives an email from the Cal.com mail server. This is a mail-amplification/spam vector and an unbounded DB write. Add a reasonable maximum (and a minimum of 1) to the schema.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings
body: Every other sender in this file (e.g. `sendLocationChangeEmails`) takes an `eventTypeMetadata` argument and guards with `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` accepts no metadata and unconditionally emails the organizer, all team members and all attendees, so event types configured with standard host/attendee emails disabled will still send mail, breaking that setting.

title: Component inside packages/ui imports from its own barrel (@calcom/ui), creating a circular dependency
body: `import { Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip } from "@calcom/ui";` imports the package's own entry point (`packages/ui/index.tsx`), which in turn re-exports this very module via `./form/MultiEmailLazy`. Sibling components in this folder import their dependencies by relative path for this reason. The cycle can produce undefined imports at runtime (especially combined with the `next/dynamic` lazy wrapper) and pulls the whole UI barrel into the lazily-loaded chunk, defeating the purpose of `MultiEmailLazy`. Use relative imports (`../components/button`, `../components/form`, etc.).

title: Hardcoded English tooltip text in shared UI component
body: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` uses a hardcoded English string in a shared, user-facing component while the rest of the component uses `t(...)`. Non-English users will see untranslated text; the string should come from the locale files.

title: Error toast exposes raw tRPC code and the fallback message is dead code
body: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`` is always a non-empty string, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` can never fall back; when `err.data` is missing the user sees `undefined: ...`. The toast also surfaces an internal error code plus an un-translated server message key to end users. Prefer translating the known message keys and falling back to `t("unable_to_add_guests")` when the key is unknown.

title: Validation error state is never cleared except via Cancel
body: `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is only reset in the Cancel button handler. If the user fixes the invalid/duplicate emails and submits successfully, or closes the dialog with the X/overlay and reopens it, the red "Emails must be unique and valid" message remains visible. Reset the flag at the start of `handleAdd` and when the dialog opens/closes.

title: New mutation with non-trivial authorization logic has no tests
body: `addGuestsHandler` introduces an authorization matrix (organizer / team admin-owner / attendee), blacklist filtering, duplicate filtering, attendee persistence, calendar update and email dispatch, but the PR adds no unit or integration tests. Given the permission bug (AND instead of OR), the case-sensitivity bypass and the credential mix-up noted elsewhere in this review, tests covering at least the authorization branches and the filtering of duplicates/blacklisted emails are needed before merge.

title: retryCount delete branch is not scoped to SMS reminders or to unscheduled rows
body: The new `OR` branch in the `deleteMany` matches **any** `WorkflowReminder` whose `retryCount > 1`, with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and no `scheduled: false` constraint. Consequences: (1) the SMS cron will delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders as soon as some other code path (e.g. a future whatsapp/email cron reusing the same column) increments their retryCount, destroying reminders this endpoint is not responsible for; (2) a row that already has `scheduled: true` and a `referenceId` (a message really scheduled in Twilio) would also be deleted if its retryCount ever reached 2, leaving an orphaned scheduled Twilio message that can no longer be cancelled when the booking is cancelled/rescheduled. The branch should at minimum be `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduled: false, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

title: Unguarded prisma.update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
body: In the `catch` block the `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` call is not itself wrapped in a try/catch. If the original error was caused by database unavailability (or the row was deleted concurrently, producing a Prisma P2025 record-not-found error), this update throws from inside the catch, the exception propagates out of the `for` loop and the handler, so every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped and the request fails with a 500 instead of a partial success. Wrap the bookkeeping update in its own try/catch (or use `updateMany`) so one bad reminder cannot abort the batch.

title: retryCount is not incremented when message or sendTo is missing
body: The retry bookkeeping only happens inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)`. A reminder whose resolved `sendTo` is null/empty (e.g. attendee never provided `smsReminderNumber`) or whose template renders to an empty string silently falls through: nothing is scheduled, `scheduled` stays false and `retryCount` stays 0, so the cron keeps re-picking this row on every invocation until `scheduledDate` passes — exactly the unbounded-retry behaviour this PR aims to stop. These cases should also increment retryCount (or the row should be deleted).

title: OR'ed deleteMany on unindexed retryCount forces a full table scan each cron run
body: `retryCount` has no index (see schema: only `[bookingUid]`, `[workflowStepId]`, `[seatReferenceId]`, `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]`, `[cancelled, scheduledDate]`). Wrapping the previous predicate in an `OR` with `retryCount > 1` means Postgres can no longer satisfy the delete with the `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` index alone and will likely sequentially scan `WorkflowReminder`, which is one of the largest tables, on every run of this cron. Either add an index covering the new predicate or keep the retry cleanup as a second, method-scoped `deleteMany` that can use the existing index.

title: No tests for the new retry/delete behaviour
body: The PR introduces a destructive rule (reminders are permanently deleted after two failed scheduling attempts) with no accompanying test. There is no coverage for: incrementing retryCount when `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns falsy, incrementing on thrown errors, and the deleteMany removing only rows that should be removed. Given that a wrong predicate silently deletes customer reminders, at least a unit test around the delete/where clause and the increment paths is warranted.

title: deleteMany retryCount clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` in the `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` call has no `method` filter, so this SMS-only cron will delete *any* WorkflowReminder row (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, mandatory reminders, etc.) whose retryCount exceeds 1, including rows that were already successfully scheduled. Any future code path that increments retryCount for a non-SMS method will silently have its reminders purged by this endpoint. The branch should be combined with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and ideally `scheduled: false`).

title: retryCount is never incremented when sendTo/message is missing, so reminders are retried forever
body: The retryCount increment only happens inside the `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` block (else branch) or in the `catch`. When `sendTo` is null/empty (e.g. a booking with no `smsReminderNumber`, which is one of the main failure modes this PR targets) or the rendered message is empty, the loop silently does nothing: the reminder stays `scheduled: false` with retryCount 0 and will be re-processed on every cron run until the scheduled date passes. The same applies to the `continue` at line 69 when `workflowStep`/`booking` is missing. These cases should also bump retryCount (or delete the reminder).

title: Non-atomic retryCount update can lose increments
body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` computes the new value from the value read earlier in the request. If two cron invocations overlap (or the job is retried while a previous run is still processing), both read the same value and write the same result, losing an increment and allowing more retries than intended. Use Prisma's atomic update `{ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` instead. Same issue at line 195.

title: Prisma update inside catch block can throw and abort the whole cron run
body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` added at the top of the `catch` block is itself unawaited-by-try: if it rejects (e.g. the reminder row was deleted concurrently → Prisma P2025 record-not-found), the rejection escapes the catch, aborts the remaining reminders in the loop and returns a 500 instead of the intended per-reminder error handling. Wrap it in its own try/catch (or use `updateMany`, which does not throw on no match).

title: retryCount filter in deleteMany has no supporting index
body: The new `retryCount` column is used in a `deleteMany` predicate (`retryCount > 1`) that runs on every cron invocation, but no index covers it and the existing indexes (`[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]`, `[cancelled, scheduledDate]`) do not help because the predicate is an unscoped OR branch. On a large WorkflowReminder table this forces a sequential scan each run. Scoping the branch to method/scheduled (so an existing index can be used) or adding an index would avoid the repeated full-table scan.

title: deleteMany retryCount branch is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The new OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` in the `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` call has no `method` (or `scheduled: false`) constraint, while the other branch is correctly scoped to `WorkflowMethods.SMS`. `retryCount` is a column on every WorkflowReminder row (EMAIL, SMS, WHATSAPP), so the SMS cron will permanently delete email/WhatsApp reminders as soon as anything else increments their retry counter, and it will also delete rows that have already been successfully scheduled (referenceId set) but happened to accumulate retries, losing the ability to later cancel the external job. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and ideally `scheduled: false`) to that branch.

title: retryCount updated with a read-modify-write instead of an atomic increment
body: Both update calls set `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read earlier in the request. If two cron invocations overlap (cron overrun, manual trigger, or a retrying scheduler), both read the same `retryCount` and write the same value, so failures are undercounted and the reminder can be retried indefinitely — exactly the loop this PR is trying to stop. Use Prisma's atomic `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`.

title: No retry counting when message or sendTo is missing, so those reminders still loop forever
body: `retryCount` is only incremented inside the `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` block or in the catch. Reminders that have no `sendTo` (e.g. missing/blank attendee phone number) or an empty rendered message silently fall through every cron run with `scheduled: false` and `retryCount: 0`, and are re-processed on every invocation until `scheduledDate` passes. The same applies to the `continue` at line 68-70 when `workflowStep`/`booking` is null. The stated goal of the PR (stop endlessly reprocessing unschedulable reminders) is therefore only partially achieved.

title: Prisma update inside catch can throw and abort processing of remaining reminders
body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` added at the top of the catch block is not itself guarded. If that write fails (connection error, row deleted concurrently by the deleteMany above — P2025 record not found), the exception propagates out of the `for` loop and out of `handler`, so all remaining unscheduled reminders in this run are skipped and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the `{ message: "SMS scheduled" }` response. Wrap the update in its own try/catch (or `.catch()`).

title: OR-ed delete predicate on unindexed retryCount forces a full scan of WorkflowReminder
body: The delete condition is now `(method = SMS AND scheduledDate <= now) OR retryCount > 1`. `retryCount` has no index and the OR prevents the existing `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` index from satisfying the whole predicate, so Postgres will likely sequentially scan the entire WorkflowReminder table on every cron run. On a large table this makes the cron noticeably slower and takes row locks broadly; consider issuing two separate scoped deletes or adding an index covering the retry condition.

title: No tests for the new retry/delete behaviour
body: The PR introduces new deletion semantics (drop reminders once retryCount > 1) and new increment paths (scheduleSMS returning falsy, and thrown errors), but no unit/integration test is added. Regressions such as deleting reminders of the wrong method or never incrementing the counter would not be caught; a test asserting retryCount increments on failure, that a reminder is removed after the second failure, and that non-SMS reminders are untouched would protect this logic.

title: getBaseConditions can return an un-parenthesized top-level OR, breaking AND-composition by callers
body: `getBaseConditions()` returns the authorization SQL verbatim when there are no filters (line 75), and for `org`/`team` scope that SQL is a top-level `OR` expression such as `("teamId" = ANY($1)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true) OR (("userId" = ANY($2)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false))` with no surrounding parentheses (see the reduce at lines 171-174 and 204-207). Any consumer that interpolates the result into a larger predicate, e.g. ``WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" >= ${from}``, gets `A AND B OR (C AND D AND startTime>=...)` because `AND` binds tighter than `OR`. That silently returns bookings outside the requested date range and, worse, rows that should have been excluded by the additional predicate — an authorization-scope leak. The same applies to the public `getFilterConditions()`, which returns `("eventTypeId" = $1) OR ("eventParentId" = $1)` unwrapped when it is the only filter. All returned fragments should be wrapped in outer parentheses (e.g. `Prisma.sql`(${expr})`).

title: Public findMany() removed without updating any callers
body: The `findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)` method was deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment instead of executing a query. No other file in the repository is touched by this PR, so any existing consumer of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` (e.g. insights tRPC routers/handlers) will fail to compile or, if dynamically typed, fail at runtime. Either keep `findMany` as a thin wrapper that runs `$queryRaw` with the base conditions, or update all call sites in the same change.

title: Loosened constructor option type lets invalid scopes compile and silently degrade to 1=0
body: The constructor now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (`scope: "user" | "org" | "team"`, `teamId?: number`) instead of the discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`. Previously, passing `scope: "team"` without a `teamId` was a compile error; now it type-checks, zod validation fails in the constructor, `this.options` becomes `null`, and every query silently gets the `1=0` condition with no error or log. A caller mis-wiring the options will see an empty insights result set rather than a failure, which is very hard to diagnose. Keep the discriminated union in the constructor signature, or at minimum throw/log when `safeParse` fails.

title: Caching tests for auth/filter conditions were deleted while the caching logic remains
body: The entire `describe("Caching")` block (tests for `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`) was removed, but `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` in the service still memoize via `this.cachedAuthConditions`/`this.cachedFilterConditions` (insightsBooking.ts lines 83-95). Notably the `null` case for filter conditions is a subtle memoization branch (`undefined` vs `null`) that is now completely untested, so a regression that re-queries the DB on every call, or that caches `null` incorrectly, would go unnoticed. The tests should be ported to the new SQL expectations rather than dropped.

title: Only the user-scope SQL is actually executed against the database; ANY() array binding is untested
body: The only test that runs real SQL (`$queryRaw` on `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized`) uses `scope: "user"`, whose condition contains no arrays. The org and team scope conditions rely on `"teamId" = ANY(${array})` / `"userId" = ANY(${array})` parameter binding (insightsBooking.ts lines 164, 168, 201), which is only asserted by structural `toEqual` comparison of `Prisma.Sql` objects — that cannot catch a failure of the driver to bind a JS array as a Postgres array, nor a column-type mismatch. Add integration tests that execute the org- and team-scope base conditions via `$queryRaw` and assert the returned rows.

title: Org-scope assertion depends on unordered query results, making the test flaky
body: The expectation compares the exact bound-parameter arrays `[org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` and `[user.id, user2.id, user3.id]` against the SQL built from `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId` and `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`. Those repository calls have no `orderBy`, so PostgreSQL may return rows in any order; since `toEqual` on a `Prisma.Sql` compares the `values` array element-by-element, the test can fail non-deterministically. Either sort the ids in the service before building the condition or compare order-insensitively (e.g. assert on sorted copies of `conditions.values`).

title: getBaseConditions() can return an un-parenthesized OR expression
body: `getBaseConditions()` returns the raw SQL fragment as-is when there are no filters, and for `org`/`team` scope that fragment is `(A AND B) OR (C AND D)` with no surrounding parentheses (see the reducers at lines 171-174 and 204-207). Any caller that composes it, e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" > $x`, gets `(A AND B) OR ((C AND D) AND "startTime" > $x)` because `AND` binds tighter than `OR`. The first OR branch then bypasses the extra predicate entirely, which silently returns rows that should have been filtered out (a correctness and potential data-exposure problem, since the OR branches are the authorization clauses). The fragment returned by `getBaseConditions()` (and by `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()`, which are public) should always be wrapped in parentheses, e.g. `return Prisma.sql`(${conditions})``.

title: Public findMany() removed without updating consumers
body: The public method `findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)` is deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a SQL fragment and performs no query. Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` (tRPC insights routers, etc.) will fail to compile/run, and no such callers are updated in this PR (only the service and its test are touched). Either keep a `findMany`-equivalent that executes the query using the new SQL conditions, or update all call sites in the same change.

title: Constructor options type widened, losing discriminated-union safety
body: The constructor parameter type was changed from the discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to the new flat `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (`scope: "user" | "org" | "team"`, `teamId?: number`). With this signature, `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` (no `teamId`) type-checks, then fails `safeParse`, sets `this.options = null`, and silently yields `1=0` — i.e. insights pages render empty data instead of surfacing a compile-time or runtime error. Keep the discriminated union as the public input type, or throw when validation fails so misuse is visible.

title: Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions
body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always resolves to a `Prisma.Sql` instance (never null/undefined — it returns `NOTHING_CONDITION` on failure), so `authConditions` is always truthy and the `else if (filterConditions)` / final `else { return NOTHING_CONDITION; }` branches at lines 76-80 can never execute. This dead code hides the fact that the "no authorization" case is already represented by `1=0`; it should be simplified to avoid future readers assuming a null-auth path exists.

title: SQL expectations depend on unordered DB row order
body: The org-scope and team-scope assertions compare the generated `Prisma.Sql` (including its bound `values`) against literal arrays such as `[testData.user.id, user2.id, user3.id]` and `[testData.org.id, testData.team.id, team2.id, team3.id]`. Those arrays come from `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds` / `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId`, which are issued without an `ORDER BY`, so Postgres may return rows in any order and the test will fail intermittently. Sort the actual/expected ID arrays before comparing, or assert on membership rather than exact array ordering.

title: Caching tests deleted without replacement
body: The `describe("Caching")` block covering `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` memoization was removed entirely. The caching behaviour still exists in the service (lines 84-95 of insightsBooking.ts) and is now untested, so a regression (e.g. the `=== undefined` check for the nullable filter cache) would go unnoticed. The tests could have been ported to the new `Prisma.sql` expectations like the others.

title: Public `findMany()` removed without updating any callers
body: `InsightsBookingService.findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)` was deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>`. This is a breaking change to the service's public surface: any consumer that previously did `service.findMany({ select: ... })` (the old integration test did exactly that) will now fail to compile/run. This PR only touches the service and its test, so if any production code path (insights routers/handlers) calls `findMany`, the build breaks. Either keep a `findMany` wrapper that executes `$queryRaw` with `getBaseConditions()`, or update all call sites in this PR.

title: Public condition getters return unparenthesized composite SQL (operator-precedence hazard)
body: `buildFilterConditions` returns the single-condition case verbatim, e.g. `"eventTypeId" = $1 OR "eventParentId" = $1`, and `buildAuthorizationConditions`/`buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` similarly return top-level `AND`/`OR` expressions with no surrounding parentheses (see also lines 135, 164, 197). `getBaseConditions` happens to wrap them, but these are public async methods (`getAuthorizationConditions`, `getFilterConditions`) and any caller doing `WHERE ${auth} AND ${filters}` or `WHERE ${base} AND "startTime" > $x` will get silently wrong results because `OR` binds looser than `AND` — in the authorization case that means returning bookings the user is not allowed to see. Wrap each produced fragment in parentheses at construction time.

title: New `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` loses discriminated-union type safety and silently denies access
body: The constructor now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (`scope: "user" | "org" | "team"`, `teamId?: number`) instead of the discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`. A caller can now pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` with no `teamId` and it compiles; at runtime `safeParse` fails, `this.options` becomes `null`, and every query silently returns `1=0` (no rows) with no error or log. Previously this was a compile-time error. Keep the discriminated union in the constructor signature, or at least surface the validation failure (throw/log) instead of degrading to an empty result set.

title: Only user-scope SQL is ever executed against the database; team/org raw SQL is untested
body: The only test that runs real SQL (`$queryRaw ... WHERE ${baseConditions}`) uses `scope: "user"`, which exercises only `"userId"`, `"teamId"`, `"eventTypeId"` and `"eventParentId"`. The team/org conditions, which are the newly hand-written SQL most likely to be wrong (quoted column `"isTeamBooking"`, and `= ANY(${array})` array-parameter binding), are only compared string-wise against hand-copied `Prisma.sql` literals. A misspelled/renamed view column or an array binding the driver rejects would pass all tests and fail in production. Add at least one `$queryRaw` execution for team scope and one for org scope asserting the expected booking ids.

title: Caching tests deleted while the memoization code remains
body: The `describe("Caching")` block covering `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` was removed, but the service still memoizes both (`getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions`, insightsBooking.ts lines 83-95). The memoization has a subtle contract (`undefined` means "not computed", `null` is a valid cached filter result); with the tests gone, a regression such as recomputing on every call or treating a cached `null` as uncached would go unnoticed. Port the caching assertions to the new `Prisma.sql` expectations instead of dropping them.

title: Org/team scope expectations depend on undefined DB row ordering
body: The expected SQL parameters are arrays in a fixed order (`[org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` and `[user.id, user2.id, user3.id]`), but these come from `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId` and `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`, which issue no `ORDER BY`. `toEqual` on arrays is order-sensitive, so this test can fail intermittently depending on Postgres row ordering. Sort the ids before comparing (or compare as sets).

title: deleteCache throws a plain Error instead of TRPCError
body: When the credential is not found or does not belong to the caller, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC converts unknown errors into `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (HTTP 500) and reports them to error logging/monitoring as server faults, instead of a 404/403. Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN", message: ... })` so the client gets a correct status and the condition is not reported as a server crash. The UI currently only shows a generic toast, so the mis-typed error also hides the real cause from the user.

title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired cache rows are shown as current
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` aggregates `MAX(updatedAt)` over all `CalendarCache` rows for a credential with no `expiresAt` filter. Rows stay in the table after expiry (expiry is enforced at read time via `expiresAt: { gte: now }` in `getCachedAvailability`), so the UI will display a "Last updated" timestamp and a "Delete cached data" action for credentials whose cache is expired and no longer served. The displayed status is therefore misleading. Filter by `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (or surface expiry explicitly).

title: Cache status query bypasses the calendar-cache feature gate
body: The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly rather than going through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, which is the factory that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the calendar-cache feature is disabled. As a result, users/teams without the `calendar-cache` feature enabled will still get cache status and the "Delete cached data" action in the UI, and every `connectedCalendars` request pays an extra `groupBy` query even when the feature is off.

title: deleteCache success does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
body: The `deleteCache` mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop, while the disconnect mutation explicitly invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`. In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` the `onSuccess` prop is wired to `props.onChanged`, which is optional and undefined on the installed-apps page; the `connectedCalendars` query is also configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. Consequently, after deleting the cache the dropdown keeps showing the old "Last updated" timestamp and the delete action until a full reload. Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in the mutation's `onSettled`/`onSuccess`.

title: Cache timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale and browser timezone
body: The timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` regardless of the user's locale (available via `useLocale()`) or the user's configured timezone/time format. Non-English users will see a US-formatted date inside an otherwise localized string, and the time is rendered in the browser timezone which may differ from the profile timezone used elsewhere in the app.

title: updateMany with empty data relies on implicit @updatedAt and writes on every cache refresh
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is called at the end of every `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` run (including each Google webhook delivery and cron refresh). It passes an empty `data` object and depends entirely on Prisma implicitly adding `updatedAt` to the SET clause; if that behaviour changes or the field is not `@updatedAt`, the call becomes a no-op UPDATE on every selected calendar row for the credential with no visible error. It also performs an extra write over all rows of the credential on a hot path, and per the PR description the resulting `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not consumed anywhere in the UI (the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache`). Either set the timestamp explicitly (`{ updatedAt: new Date() }`) or drop the call.

title: updateManyByCredentialId typed with SelectedCalendarUpdateInput instead of the updateMany input type
body: `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany` accepts `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`, but the method signature declares `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`, which additionally permits nested relation operations (`user: { connect: ... }`, etc.). Such payloads type-check at compile time but fail at runtime when passed to `updateMany`. Narrow the parameter type to `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId that the function never uses
body: `UserWithCalendars` was widened so `allSelectedCalendars`/`userLevelSelectedCalendars` must include `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, but nothing in this file (or in the new cache-status code, which reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt`) consumes those fields. This is an exported type used by other callers (platform libraries / API v2 / other handlers) that build the user object with only `externalId | integration | eventTypeId`; those call sites now fail to type-check and require a matching `select` change. Either revert the widening or update all construction sites.

title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` without declaring tsx as a dependency
body: `dev:cron` now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not in `dependencies`/`devDependencies` (while the now-unused `ts-node` remains). `npx` will silently download an arbitrary latest version of `tsx` from the network on each developer machine/CI run, which is non-deterministic and fails in offline/locked-down environments. Add `tsx` as a devDependency and invoke it via the local binary.

title: `sed -i ''` is macOS-only and breaks on Linux
body: The in-place edit uses BSD/macOS syntax `sed -i '' -E ...`. With GNU sed (Linux, CI containers) `-i ''` is parsed as an empty suffix argument followed by the empty string being treated as the script/file, so the command errors out or edits the wrong file, leaving `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` unchanged while the script still prints the success message. Use a portable approach (e.g. write to a temp file and move it, or branch on `uname`).

title: Migration warning comment contradicts the SQL it documents
body: The auto-generated warning block states the column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the SQL actually adds `updatedAt` with `DEFAULT NOW()`, which is safe for non-empty tables. Leaving the stale warning in place is misleading for anyone reviewing or replaying migrations; remove or correct it.

title: No tests for the new cache deletion authorization or cache-status mapping
body: The PR adds a destructive mutation (`deleteCache`) whose only protection is an ownership check on `Credential.userId`, plus a new repository aggregation (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`) and the credential→cache mapping in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`. None of these have unit tests: there is no test asserting that another user's credentialId is rejected, that cache rows of other credentials are not deleted, or that the `credentialId → updatedAt` map is built correctly (including credentials without cache). Given the authorization-sensitive and data-deleting nature of the handler, tests should accompany it.

title: deleteCache handler throws plain Error instead of TRPCError
body: When the credential isn't found or doesn't belong to the caller, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps unknown errors to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (HTTP 500) and, depending on error formatting, can surface the raw message. This conflates an authorization/not-found condition with a server failure, breaks client error handling (which only shows a generic toast), and pollutes error monitoring with false 500s. Use `TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN" })` as the other handlers in this router do.

title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates the connectedCalendars query
body: `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop, unlike `disconnectMutation` which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`. In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` the `onSuccess`/`onChanged` prop is optional and is not passed on the installed-calendars page, so after a successful cache deletion the dropdown keeps displaying the old "Last updated" timestamp and still offers "Delete cached data" until a manual reload (the query is also configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`). Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` to the mutation's settled/success handler.

title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired cache is reported as fresh
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `calendarCache` rows for the credential and returns `max(updatedAt)` without filtering on `expiresAt >= now()`. Cache rows that are already expired (and therefore never served by `getCachedAvailability`) still produce a `cacheUpdatedAt` value, so the UI reports a cache as present/"last updated" when there is effectively no usable cache. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to match the read path.

title: UserWithCalendars widened to require updatedAt/googleChannelId without need
body: `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` in their `Pick<SelectedCalendar, ...>` types, but neither field is read anywhere in this module. This is an exported public type consumed by other callers (platform libraries, API handlers, tests) that build the user object with only `externalId`/`integration`/`eventTypeId` selected; they will now fail type-checking and must all add the two selections (only `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated here). Either revert the widening or update all construction sites.

title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data to bump updatedAt
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is issued after every cache refresh with an empty `data` object, relying on Prisma implicitly setting the `@updatedAt` field. This is undocumented behavior (an empty `updateMany` can be a no-op), so the intended timestamp bump may silently never happen, while every cache refresh still pays for an extra write/row lock across all SelectedCalendar rows of the credential. The PR description itself notes this value isn't consumed by the frontend (the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`); either set the field explicitly (`{ updatedAt: new Date() }`) or drop the call.

title: updateManyByCredentialId accepts the wrong Prisma input type
body: The `data` parameter is typed `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`, but `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany` expects `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`. `UpdateInput` permits nested relation writes (e.g. `credential: { connect: ... }`) which `updateMany` cannot execute, so such a call type-checks but fails at runtime. Use `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.

title: Cache timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale and browser timezone
body: The timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, so non-English users see an American date/time format inside an otherwise localized string, and the user's configured timezone/time format preference (12h/24h) is ignored. Use the user's locale (available from `useLocale()`) and the existing date-formatting helpers.

title: Cache status query bypasses the calendar-cache feature gate
body: The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through the `CalendarCache.init()` factory that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the calendar-cache feature is disabled. As a result, cache status (and therefore the "Cache Status"/"Delete cached data" UI) is reported from leftover DB rows even for users/teams where calendar cache is turned off, and an extra DB groupBy runs on every connectedCalendars request regardless of the flag.

title: No tests for the new destructive deleteCache mutation or cache-status repository method
body: `deleteCacheHandler` performs a destructive `calendarCache.deleteMany` gated only by an ownership lookup, and `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` is new query logic, yet neither has unit tests. In particular there is no test asserting that a user cannot delete the cache of another user's credential (the main security property of this endpoint) nor that the credential-id-to-timestamp mapping is correct.

title: Dev script uses macOS-only `sed -i ''` and a CWD-relative .env path
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax; with GNU sed (Linux/CI) the empty string is parsed as the input filename and the command fails with "can't read : No such file or directory", leaving GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL unchanged. Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the current working directory, so running the script from the repository root creates/edits a `.env` in the repo's parent directory instead of the intended file. Use a path derived from the script location and a portable in-place edit.

title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` without declaring tsx as a dependency
body: `dev:cron` now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` but `tsx` is not listed in this package's dependencies/devDependencies, so `npx` will attempt to download it from the network on every run (failing in offline/locked-down environments and ignoring the yarn lockfile), while the now-unused `ts-node` devDependency remains. Add `tsx` as a devDependency and invoke it via the local binary.

title: Migration header warning contradicts the statement it documents
body: The generated warning block states the column is "Added the required column `updatedAt` ... without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the actual ALTER TABLE adds the column with `DEFAULT NOW()`. Leaving the stale warning in place misleads reviewers/operators into thinking the migration will fail on a non-empty CalendarCache table. Remove or correct the comment.

title: deleteCache throws plain Error instead of TRPCError
body: The handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps unknown errors to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) and, in production, replaces the message, so the client cannot distinguish "not yours" from a server failure, and the failure is logged/reported as a server bug. Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN", message: ... })` as the other handlers in this router do.

title: Cache deletion only supports personal credentials, not team/delegation credentials
body: Access is validated with `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`. Calendar credentials installed on a team have `userId = null`, and delegation credentials are in-memory with negative ids, so for those connected calendars the lookup fails and the mutation errors out. The new dropdown in SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper renders the "Delete cached data" entry for any credential that has a cache row (including team/delegation-backed ones), so users will get an "Error deleting cache" toast with no way to clear the cache. Either extend the authorization check (team membership / delegation ownership) or hide the action for those credentials.

title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
body: The disconnect mutation invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`, but `deleteCacheMutation` only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback. `onSuccess` is wired to `props.onChanged`, which is optional and undefined on several call sites of SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper. In that case the success toast is shown but the UI keeps displaying the old "Cache Status / Last updated" entry until a manual refresh, making it look like deletion failed. Add `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in the mutation's onSettled/onSuccess.

title: Cache timestamp is hard-coded to en-US formatting
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })` ignores the user's locale and 12h/24h time preference, so a non-US user sees MM/DD/YY and AM/PM dates inside an otherwise translated string. Use the user's locale (e.g. from `useLocale()`) / the existing date-formatting helpers instead of a literal "en-US".

title: Unnecessary blanket UPDATE of all SelectedCalendars on every cache fill
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` issues an `UPDATE "SelectedCalendar" SET "updatedAt" = now() WHERE credentialId = ?` for every credential each time availability is cached (including on every Google webhook). The PR description itself states `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not consumed anywhere in the UI (the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache), so this is a write with no reader that adds row churn and lock contention on a hot path. For delegation credentials (negative in-memory id) it also matches nothing. Remove it or document a concrete consumer.

title: Cache status query bypasses the calendar-cache feature check
body: The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through the `CalendarCache` factory that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the feature is disabled. As a result every `connectedCalendars` request performs an extra `groupBy` on CalendarCache even for users/teams without calendar cache enabled, and stale rows left over from a previously enabled feature are surfaced in the UI as an active cache (with a delete action) even though caching is off.

title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt
body: The query filters only on `credentialId in (...)`, so expired cache rows (`expiresAt < now()`) are reported with their `_max(updatedAt)`. The UI then shows "Cache Status – Last updated: …" for a cache that will never be served, misleading the user about whether the credential is actually cached. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (or expose expiry so the UI can label stale caches).

title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId that the function never uses
body: `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` were widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, but neither field is read anywhere in this file. Because `UserWithCalendars` is the public input type of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` (also re-exported as `getConnectedDestinationCalendars` for `@calcom/platform-libraries`), every external caller that selects only `externalId/integration/eventTypeId` now fails type-checking and must be updated (only `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated in this PR). Revert the widening unless the fields are actually needed.

title: Migration backfills updatedAt with NOW(), making stale caches look fresh
