body: All pre-existing CalendarCache rows get `updatedAt = <migration time>`. The new UI reads this value and renders "Last updated: <timestamp>", so immediately after deploy every existing cache — including ones written weeks ago — appears to have been refreshed at deploy time. Consider backfilling from a better proxy (e.g. `expiresAt - CACHING_TIME`) or making the column nullable so "unknown" can be shown. Also the auto-generated warning block ("Added the required column `updatedAt` ... without a default value") contradicts the statement actually executed, which does specify a default.

title: Dev script is macOS-only and writes to a path outside the repo
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax; on Linux (GNU sed) the empty string is interpreted as the script argument and the command fails with "unknown command", leaving GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL unchanged while the script still prints the success message. Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory, so running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root creates/edits a `.env` in the repo's parent directory rather than the project one. Resolve the path relative to the script location and use a portable in-place edit.

title: dev:cron depends on tsx which is not a declared dependency
body: `dev:cron` was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`. `tsx` is not in dependencies/devDependencies, so `npx` will attempt an interactive network install on each fresh environment (and fail in offline/CI contexts), while the now-unused `ts-node` devDependency remains. Add `tsx` as a devDependency and invoke it without `npx`.

title: No tests for the new deleteCache handler or getCacheStatusByCredentialIds
body: This PR adds a destructive mutation (`viewer.calendars.deleteCache`) with hand-rolled authorization and a new repository read (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), but no unit tests. At minimum there should be tests asserting that (a) a credential belonging to another user cannot have its cache deleted, (b) the matching CalendarCache rows are removed for an owned credential, and (c) the status aggregation returns the max updatedAt per credentialId and an empty result for unknown ids.

title: One failing SendGrid cancellation aborts the whole cancellation loop permanently
body: The `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop is wrapped in a single outer `try`/`catch`. If the `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` request throws for one reminder (invalid/expired batch id, already-cancelled batch, transient 4xx/5xx), the catch is hit, the loop aborts, and none of the remaining reminders in the batch are cancelled; the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` promises collected so far are never awaited either (Prisma promises are lazy), so nothing is removed from the DB. Because the next cron run re-selects the same rows ordered the same way, a single permanently-failing reminder blocks every other cancellation forever and reminder emails for cancelled/rescheduled bookings keep going out — exactly the bug this PR is meant to fix. The try/catch (and the delete) should be inside the loop, per reminder.

title: immediateDelete path re-introduces the SendGrid pending-cancellation limit and leaks DB rows
body: When `immediateDelete` is true, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` issues the SendGrid `status: "cancel"` request straight away and returns early, without deleting or flagging the `workflowReminder` row. Two consequences: (1) every reschedule (`handleNewBooking.ts`, which passes `true`) and every workflow/step deletion still consumes one of SendGrid's max-100 pending cancellation slots — the root cause described in the PR body — so the limit can still be exhausted and subsequent cancellations silently fail; (2) for the reschedule path (where the old booking row is not deleted and therefore nothing cascades) the stale reminder row survives with `scheduled: true` and a `referenceId`, and `cancelled` left null, so it is only cleaned up when the scheduledDate finally passes. Either route the reschedule case through the deferred `cancelled` flag like cancellation, or delete the row when cancelling immediately.

title: Reminder cancellation is now fire-and-forget; the `cancelled` flag may never be persisted
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but are invoked inside `forEach` without `await`, and their results are no longer collected into `prismaPromises` (as the previous `remindersToDelete` array was). The handler can therefore return its HTTP response before the `workflowReminder.update({ cancelled: true })` / `delete` queries have executed. On a serverless runtime the function can be frozen/terminated right after the response, so the flag is never written and the cron job will never cancel the scheduled SendGrid email — the reminder for a cancelled booking is still delivered. The same unawaited pattern was introduced in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (requestReschedule) and `handleNewBooking.ts`. These calls should be awaited (e.g. `await Promise.all(...)`).

title: Deferred cancellation can miss SendGrid's cancellation deadline for near-term reminders
body: Cancellation is deferred to a cron that runs every ~15 minutes and only picks up reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour. A booking cancelled shortly before its reminder's send time (e.g. 12 minutes before) will only have the SendGrid cancel request issued on the next cron tick, which can be less than SendGrid's required 10-minute lead time before `sendAt` — in that case the cancel is rejected/ignored and the reminder email is still sent. Worse, the `deleteMany` at line 34 removes EMAIL reminders whose `scheduledDate` is already in the past before the cancellation block runs, so such rows are dropped without any cancellation attempt and without any log. Consider cancelling immediately when `scheduledDate` is near (while keeping the deferred path for far-future reminders) so the pending-cancellation quota is still protected.

title: Unused `Prisma` import left behind after removing BatchPayload usage
body: The import block was changed from `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise }` to a value import that still includes `Prisma`, but all `Prisma.BatchPayload` usages were removed in this diff, so `Prisma` is now unused in this file. With the repo's no-unused-vars/consistent-type-imports lint rules this fails CI; the formatting of the new import block (no trailing comma on the last specifier) will also be flagged by the prettier check.

title: Cancellation query does not restrict to EMAIL reminders with a reference id
body: `remindersToCancel` selects every `workflowReminder` with `cancelled: true`, without filtering on `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`, `scheduled: true` or `referenceId: { not: null }`. Today only email reminders are ever flagged, but any future/manual row with another method (or a null `referenceId`) would be POSTed to SendGrid as a `batch_id`, producing an error that — given the shared try/catch — aborts the whole cancellation loop. Add the explicit filters so this endpoint only ever handles rows it can act on.

title: No automated coverage for the cancelled-reminder flow
body: This is the second attempt at fixing reminders being sent for cancelled/rescheduled bookings (the previous fix in #6991 silently stopped working in production). The PR adds a new `cancelled` field plus a new cron branch but no test asserting that cancelling or rescheduling a booking marks the reminder `cancelled: true`, that the cron issues the SendGrid cancel and removes the row, and that a failing cancellation does not block the others. Without a test the regression can recur unnoticed, as it already did.

title: remindersToCancel query is not filtered by method/scheduled/referenceId
body: The query that collects reminders to cancel only filters on `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate`. It does not filter `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`, `scheduled: true`, or `referenceId: { not: null }`. Consequences: (a) a reminder whose `referenceId` is still null (never handed to SendGrid) will produce a `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` with `batch_id: null`, which SendGrid rejects with a 4xx; (b) any non-EMAIL (SMS/Twilio) reminder that ever ends up with `cancelled = true` would be sent to SendGrid with a Twilio SID as batch_id. Both cases turn into request errors inside the loop, which (see the surrounding try/catch) aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders.

title: One failed SendGrid cancellation aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders
body: The `try { for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request(...) ... } }` block wraps the entire loop in a single try/catch. If the SendGrid request for one reminder throws (invalid batch_id, rate limit, transient 5xx, auth error), the loop exits immediately, the already-queued `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` promises are never awaited, and every remaining cancelled reminder in the batch is skipped for this run. Since the cron only looks at reminders scheduled within the next hour, those skipped reminders may never be retried in time and their emails will still be delivered — exactly the failure mode this PR is meant to fix. The try/catch should be per-reminder inside the loop.

title: SendGrid API key is never set on the @sendgrid/client singleton used for cancellation
body: This module only calls `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)`. `@sendgrid/mail` holds its own internal `Client` instance, while the default export of `@sendgrid/client` imported here as `client` is a separate singleton whose API key is never set (contrast `emailReminderManager.ts`, which calls both `sgMail.setApiKey` and `client.setApiKey`). As a result every `client.request(...)` in this file — including the new cancellation calls — is sent unauthenticated and fails with 401; the error is swallowed by the catch, so cancellations silently never happen and the reminder emails are still sent. Add `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)`.

title: immediateDelete path cancels the SendGrid send but never removes the WorkflowReminder row
body: When `immediateDelete` is true the function issues the SendGrid cancel request and returns early, without deleting the `workflowReminder` row or setting `cancelled = true`. Callers no longer delete the row themselves (the previous `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` calls were removed from handleCancelBooking/bookings.tsx/handleNewBooking). For the reschedule path in handleNewBooking the row therefore stays in the DB with `scheduled: true` and a live `referenceId` until the cron's `deleteMany` for past `scheduledDate` eventually removes it, and if the SendGrid call fails there is no record that the cancellation is still pending (no retry by the cron, since `cancelled` is not set). Either delete the row or mark it cancelled on this path.

title: Reschedule path still cancels SendGrid sends immediately, re-exposing the 100 pending-cancellation limit
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` is called with `immediateDelete = true` for reminders of the original booking when a booking is rescheduled. That issues the `scheduled_sends` cancel straight away, and each cancellation occupies a slot in SendGrid's pending-cancellation list until the scheduled send date — which is the exact quota (max 100 pending cancellations) the PR description identifies as the root cause of reminders still being delivered. Rescheduled bookings (one of the two cases named in the PR title/issue) therefore still hit the original failure, while cancelled bookings go through the new deferred path. This should use the deferred `cancelled` flag like the cancellation path.

title: Workflow reminder cancellation promises are not awaited before the handler returns
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but are invoked inside `forEach` without `await` and are no longer accompanied by awaited prisma promises (the `remindersToDelete` array that used to be awaited was removed). The handler can return (and in a serverless environment the function instance can be frozen/terminated) before the `workflowReminder.update({ cancelled: true })` / `delete` writes are issued, leaving the reminder un-cancelled so the reminder email/SMS is still sent. Collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)` before returning.

title: WorkflowReminder row is leaked when Twilio cancellation throws
body: `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` awaits `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` before deleting the DB row, and the whole body is wrapped in a try/catch that only logs. If Twilio rejects the cancellation (e.g. the message already left the queue or the SID is no longer cancellable) the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` is skipped, so the row stays forever: the cron's cleanup `deleteMany` only targets `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`. Previously the caller deleted the row independently of the Twilio result. Delete the row even when the provider call fails.

title: Unused `Prisma` import and non-prettier-formatted import list
body: `Prisma` was moved into the value import but all of its uses (`PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>`) were removed in this diff, so the binding is now unused, and it is added without a trailing comma, which violates the repo's prettier config. Both will fail the lint/format checks in CI.

title: SendGrid client used for cancellation without an API key
body: The new cancellation block calls `client.request({url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends", method: "POST", ...})` using the singleton exported by `@sendgrid/client`, but this module only calls `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` (line 19). `@sendgrid/mail` holds its own internal `Client` instance, so `setApiKey` on it does not configure the imported `client` singleton (compare `emailReminderManager.ts`, which explicitly calls `client.setApiKey(...)`). As a result every cancellation request here is sent unauthenticated and will fail with 401, the error is swallowed by the surrounding catch, and the "cancelled" reminders will still be delivered by SendGrid – i.e. the bug this PR is supposed to fix is not actually fixed in the CRON path. Add `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` in this file.

title: One failing cancellation aborts the whole cancellation batch and leaves DB rows untouched forever
body: The whole `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop is wrapped in a single try/catch. If any single `client.request(...)` throws (invalid/expired batch id, SendGrid already has the batch in `cancel` status, transient 5xx), the loop is abandoned: all remaining reminders in the batch are never cancelled and their emails get sent. In addition, the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` objects are Prisma lazy promises that only execute when awaited in `Promise.all` at line 74; because the throw happens before that await, none of the already-processed reminders are deleted. On the next CRON run the same reminders are selected again, the same request fails again, and the cancellation pass is permanently stuck. Each reminder needs its own try/catch (and its delete should be awaited/committed per item).

title: remindersToCancel query is missing method/referenceId filters
body: `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } } })` does not filter on `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` nor on `referenceId: { not: null }`, unlike every other query in this file. Any row that is flagged `cancelled` but has no `referenceId`, or that belongs to a non-email method, is posted to the SendGrid scheduled_sends endpoint with `batch_id: null`/a Twilio SID, which produces an error that (per the single try/catch above) aborts the whole cancellation pass. Restrict the query to email reminders with a non-null `referenceId`.

title: immediateDelete path re-introduces the pending-cancellation accumulation and leaks reminder rows
body: When `immediateDelete` is true the function issues the SendGrid `scheduled_sends` cancel immediately and returns without touching the `workflowReminder` row. Two problems: (1) the row stays in the DB with `scheduled: true` and its `referenceId`, so it is neither deleted nor flagged – it lingers until the generic `deleteMany` in the CRON removes it after `scheduledDate` passes, and it can be "cancelled" again by later code paths; (2) this path is used for the two most common operations – rescheduling (`handleNewBooking.ts` line 968) and workflow/step deletion (`workflows.tsx` lines 214 and 521) – which means those cancellations still pile up as pending cancellations in SendGrid (the 100-pending limit described in the PR description) and will again start failing silently, so cancelled emails will still be delivered. These paths should use the same deferred `cancelled` flag mechanism as booking cancellation.

title: Reminder cancellation promises are no longer awaited
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but are invoked fire-and-forget inside `forEach`. Previously the DB work for reminders was part of `prismaPromises` and therefore awaited before the handler returned. Now the handler can return (and in a serverless/edge deployment the invocation can be frozen or torn down) before the `workflowReminder.update({ cancelled: true })` / Twilio cancel + row delete have completed, in which case the reminder is never marked cancelled and the workflow email/SMS is still sent – exactly the bug being fixed. Rejections are also unobserved (unhandled promise rejections). Collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)`. The same pattern exists in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (line 488) and `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts` (line 966).

title: try/catch around the reminder cancellation cannot catch anything
body: The `try { originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...) } catch (error) { log.error(...) }` block wraps synchronous `forEach` calls over async functions. Since the returned promises are not awaited, any rejection from `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` escapes this catch as an unhandled rejection, and the log message is never produced. Await the calls (e.g. `await Promise.all(originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.map(...))`) so the error handling actually works and the cancellations complete before the reschedule continues.

title: Cancellation window can be too late for SendGrid's cancellation deadline
body: Cancellation is deferred to this CRON, which (per the PR description) runs every 15 minutes and only picks up reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour. SendGrid only honours a cancel request if it arrives sufficiently ahead of the send time (documented as at least 10 minutes). If a booking is cancelled shortly after a CRON run and its reminder is due in ~15–25 minutes, the next run can reach SendGrid with less than 10 minutes to spare and the cancellation is rejected, so the reminder for the cancelled booking is still delivered. Consider cancelling immediately (or on a much tighter schedule) for reminders due within the next hour, or widening/short-circuiting the window.

title: Type-only imports moved into a value import, and formatting will fail lint
body: `PrismaPromise` is a type-only export of `@prisma/client` but is now pulled in through a value import, and the import list `  Prisma\n} from "@prisma/client";` is missing the trailing comma required by the repo's prettier config, so `yarn lint`/format checks will fail on this file. Keep `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise } from "@prisma/client";` for the type-only names and run prettier (the large commented-out `testAction` block was also re-indented by this change, adding unrelated diff noise).

title: import() calls are evaluated eagerly, so nothing is actually lazy-loaded
body: The object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")`, `import("./caldavcalendar")`, … directly, which means every dynamic import is *started* the moment `packages/app-store/index.ts` is evaluated. The resulting object holds already-pending/resolved module promises, so all ~28 app packages (and their transitive deps such as googleapis, @microsoft/..., stripe, etc.) are still pulled into the bundle and executed at startup; the only thing that changed is that the consumer now has to `await` them. To get the intended benefit the map must hold thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and call sites must invoke them (`await appStore[key]()`). As written the PR adds async plumbing across the codebase without delivering the stated code-splitting/startup win.

title: Eagerly created module promises can produce unhandled rejections and crash the process
body: Because each `import(...)` promise is created at module-evaluation time and no `.catch()` is attached until (and unless) some code awaits that specific key, a module that throws while being evaluated (missing env var, bad app key parsing, native dep failure) produces a rejected promise with no handler. On Node >= 15 an unhandled rejection terminates the process by default, so one broken app package can take down the whole server even for requests that never touch that app. Previously a failing app module threw synchronously at import time of a single entry point and was at least deterministic/attributable. Storing lazy thunks (`() => import(...)`) avoids creating rejected promises nobody is listening to.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in its `calendar` field (silent contract change + floating promise)
body: `getCalendarCredentials` stays synchronous but `getCalendar(credential)` is now async, so each returned item's `calendar` property is a `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of a `Calendar | null`. `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to `await item.calendar`, but any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` (it is a public export of @calcom/core) that reads `.calendar` now receives a promise and will silently misbehave (e.g. truthiness checks always pass, method calls throw). Additionally, these promises are created and left unhandled inside `flatMap`: if a credential's app module fails to load, the rejection has no handler attached, giving an unhandled rejection. Consider making `getCalendarCredentials` async and resolving the calendars (with per-item error handling) before returning.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions are pushed into apiDeletes after it is already awaited
body: In the recurring branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })` uses an async callback inside `forEach`, so the callbacks return immediately and the `apiDeletes.push(...)` happens on later microtasks. By the time `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs at the end of the handler, `apiDeletes` is still empty, so the remote calendar events for the remaining recurring occurrences are deleted fire-and-forget (and their failures surface as unhandled rejections rather than being reported). The sibling non-credentialId branch in this same diff was correctly converted to a `for...of` loop; this branch should be too (e.g. `for (const credential of ...)` with awaited deletes pushed as promises).

title: requestReschedule fires calendar/video cancellations without awaiting them
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` makes every iteration an un-awaited async task. The tRPC mutation then proceeds to send the reschedule email and returns while the external calendar `deleteEvent` / `deleteMeeting` calls may not have started (they now need at least one extra microtask to resolve the dynamic app import). In a serverless/edge deployment the function can be frozen or torn down before the deletions run, leaving stale events on the user's calendar, and any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => ...))` so the work completes (and errors are caught) before responding.

title: try/catch around forEach(async ...) cannot catch anything and deletions are not awaited
body: Converting the `forEach` callback to `async` means `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })` returns before any deletion happens, so the surrounding `try { ... } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }` can never observe a failure — rejections escape as unhandled promise rejections instead of being logged. The function also proceeds to send the reschedule email and `return true` while the external calendar/video cancellations may not have executed. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => ...))` inside the try block.

title: try/catch around forEach(async ...) cannot catch anything and deletions are not awaited
body: Same defect as in the vital app: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { await getCalendar(...) ... })` returns immediately, so the enclosing `try/catch` that logs errors is dead code and any failure of `calendar.deleteEvent` / `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled rejection. The reschedule email is sent and `true` returned before the external cancellations are known to have completed, which can leave orphaned calendar/video events. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` so the awaited work is covered by the try/catch.

title: Dynamic imports are invoked eagerly, so nothing is actually lazy and rejections are unhandled
body: The object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")`, `import("./caldavcalendar")`, … at module-evaluation time. Dynamic `import()` starts loading as soon as the expression is evaluated, so every app module is still fetched and evaluated the moment `@calcom/app-store` is imported — the PR's stated goal (async/lazy loading of app packages) is not achieved, and bundlers still have to include every app in the graph. Worse, the 28 promises are created with no attached handlers at module scope: if any app module throws while being evaluated (bad env/config, side-effectful module), the resulting rejection is unhandled and can crash the Node process (unhandled rejections are fatal by default on modern Node) even when that app is never used. To get real laziness and safe error handling the values should be thunks/getters, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, with call sites doing `await appStore[key]()`.

title: Commented example import points to a non-existent path
body: The placeholder comment was changed from `// import * as example from "./_example"` to `// example: import("./example")`. The directory in the repo is `_example`, so anyone uncommenting this line (its only purpose) gets a module-not-found error. The comment should read `example: import("./_example")`.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions use an async forEach and are never awaited
body: In the recurring branch the code does `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)) })`. `forEach` ignores the returned promises, so the callbacks only run after the synchronous part of `handler` finishes; `apiDeletes` is still empty when `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs at line 652 and when the 200 response is returned. The external calendar events for all remaining recurring instances are therefore deleted fire-and-forget (and any failure surfaces as an unhandled rejection instead of being reported). Now that `getCalendar` is async this gap is larger than before. The same block in the `else` branch was correctly converted to a `for ... of` loop in this PR; this branch should use `for ... of` (or `await Promise.all(map(...))`) too.

title: requestReschedule: async callback in forEach means cancellations are not awaited
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` discards the promises returned by the async callback. Because `getCalendar` is now asynchronous, the mutation proceeds to send the reschedule-request email, fire webhooks and return while the calendar/video event deletions are still pending, and any error (e.g. expired credentials) becomes an unhandled promise rejection with no logging. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => ...))` so failures are observable and the work completes before the request ends.

title: try/catch no longer protects the now-async forEach callback
body: The callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` was made `async`, so the enclosing `try { ... } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }` can never catch anything thrown inside it: rejections from `await getCalendar(...)` or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` escape as unhandled promise rejections instead of being logged, and `Reschedule` returns `true` and sends the reschedule email before the calendar/video events are actually cancelled. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => ...))` inside the try block.

title: try/catch no longer protects the now-async forEach callback
body: Same problem as in the vital app: making the `forEach` callback `async` means the surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections from `await getCalendar(...)`, `calendar.deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting`; they become unhandled promise rejections, and the function returns `true` / sends the reschedule email before the external events are cancelled. Await the work explicitly, e.g. `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => ...))` inside the try block.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns pending promises in its `calendar` field
body: `getCalendarCredentials` is still synchronous but `getCalendar(credential)` now returns `Promise<Calendar | null>`, so each returned item's `calendar` property is a promise rather than a `Calendar`. This silently changes the public shape of `ReturnType<typeof getCalendarCredentials>` for every consumer (only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated here); any other caller that uses `item.calendar` directly will get a promise object at runtime. Additionally the promises are created without handlers, so if a CalendarService constructor/import rejects for a credential that is never awaited, the rejection goes unhandled. Consider making the function `async` and resolving the calendars (e.g. with `Promise.all`) before returning, so the contract stays `Calendar | null`.

title: Dynamic imports are started eagerly at module load, so nothing is actually lazy
body: The object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")`, `import("./caldavcalendar")`, … at module evaluation time, which immediately kicks off loading of every app package the moment `@calcom/app-store` is imported. The promises are merely stored, so consumers `await` an already-running import. The net effect is that all ~28 app modules (and their transitive deps such as Stripe/Google/Exchange SDKs) are still evaluated on every request path that touches the app store — the stated goal of async/lazy loading is not achieved, and webpack will still fetch every generated chunk. To get real laziness the entries must be thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, with call sites invoking the thunk.

title: Module-level import promises can produce unhandled rejections and crash the process
body: Each `import("./x")` promise is created at module scope with no attached handler. If any single app module throws while being evaluated (bad/missing app key, failing SDK init, missing optional dependency), the resulting rejection is unhandled because nothing awaits that specific entry unless the app happens to be used. Under Node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` this terminates the process, so one broken app takes down the whole server even though no booking uses it. Previously a failing module was at least surfaced synchronously at import time of the specific consumer. Lazily created promises (thunks) or `.catch()` handling is needed.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in its `calendar` field, changing its public contract
body: `getCalendarCredentials` still looks synchronous, but `calendar: getCalendar(credential)` is now a `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` in this file was updated to `await item.calendar`; any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` (it is exported and used outside this module, e.g. destination-calendar/connected-calendar flows and the API app) that calls `item.calendar.listCalendars()` or checks `if (!item.calendar)` will now silently see a truthy Promise and break at runtime. Additionally, promises stored on entries that a caller never awaits can reject unobserved. The function should either be made `async` and resolve the calendars with `Promise.all`, or keep the credential list free of promises.

title: Async callback in forEach: calendar/video cancellations are no longer initiated before the mutation completes
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` returns immediately; the deleteEvent/deleteMeeting calls now only start after the `await getCalendar` microtask resolves, i.e. after `requestReschedule` has already sent the reschedule email and possibly returned. Nothing awaits the resulting promises, so failures to delete the old calendar event / video room are swallowed as unhandled rejections and the old events can be left dangling. Use `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { ... }` with `await`, or collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)`.

title: try/catch around forEach with async callback cannot catch failures anymore
body: Changing the callback to `async` means the surrounding `try { ... } catch { logger.error(...) }` block can never observe an error: the callback returns a promise that is discarded, so any rejection from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` escapes as an unhandled promise rejection (process-level crash on modern Node) instead of being logged. The deletions are also not awaited before the reschedule email is sent. Replace with a `for...of` loop using `await` inside the try block.

title: try/catch around forEach with async callback cannot catch failures anymore
body: Same problem as in the vital reschedule helper: the callback passed to `forEach` is now `async`, so the enclosing `try/catch` will never see errors thrown inside it; rejections from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` become unhandled promise rejections rather than being logged, and the cancellations are not awaited before the function returns. Use a `for...of` loop with `await` inside the try block.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes after it is already awaited
body: In the recurring branch the credentials are still iterated with `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })`. Because the callback is async, `apiDeletes.push` runs only after the awaits resolve — long after `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at the end of the handler has captured the (still empty) array. So for "cancel all remaining recurring bookings" the external calendar deletions are neither awaited nor error-checked, and failures surface as unhandled rejections. The sibling non-credentialId branch in the same block was correctly converted to a `for...of` loop; this branch should be too.

title: Commented-out example entry points at a non-existent directory
body: The placeholder comment was changed from `// import * as example from "./_example";` to `// example: import("./example"),`. The directory in the repo is `_example`, so a developer who uncomments this line to register a new app gets a module-not-found error. It should read `// example: import("./_example"),`.

title: Busy times are ignored for any slot on a day that has a date override
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, after the date-override block, `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` returns early and completely skips the `busy.every(...)` check below. Consequence: on any day for which the host has a date override, existing bookings and external calendar busy times are no longer taken into account, so already-booked slots are offered again and can be double booked. The early return should only mean "working-hours check is superseded by the override"; the busy-time check must still run.

title: Working-hours check is inverted: any non-matching range marks the slot unavailable
body: The new check uses `workingHours.find(wh => slot is OUTSIDE wh)` and returns `false` (unavailable) if such an entry is found. A user whose schedule has more than one availability block on the same weekday (e.g. 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, the normal "lunch break" setup) will always have at least one block that does not contain the slot, so *every* slot on that day is rejected. Fixed hosts / collective events with split availability will show no slots at all. The logic must be "available if the slot fits inside at least one working-hour range for that day" (e.g. `!workingHours.some(covers)`).

title: `end` computed from slot start instead of slot end in working-hours check
body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates the `start` expression; it should be derived from `slotEndTime`. As written the event length is ignored, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after them passes the `end > workingHour.endTime` test. The variable is dead/duplicated code that makes the guard weaker than intended.

title: Multiple date overrides on the same day make all slots unavailable
body: `dateOverrides.find(...)` returns truthy as soon as *one* override on the slot's day does not contain the slot, and the code then returns `false` (unavailable). Users can define several override ranges for the same date (e.g. 09:00–10:00 and 14:00–15:00). With two ranges, a slot inside the first range is still rejected by the second, so no slot on that date is bookable. The check must be "unavailable only if the slot fits none of the day's overrides".

title: Dayjs objects compared with `===`, condition never true
body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly created Dayjs objects by reference, so it is always false. The intended case (zero-length override, i.e. a date marked fully unavailable) is therefore never detected and the code falls through to the range comparisons, where a slot starting exactly at the override instant is reported as available. Use `.isSame(...)`.

title: Date-override day comparison is done in the server's local timezone
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` builds a Dayjs in the *server's local* timezone, while `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()` and formats in UTC. On any deployment whose process timezone is not UTC, the two date strings can differ by a day, so the override silently does not match the slot and `dateOverrideExist` stays false, falling back to normal working hours and ignoring the override entirely. Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` for the comparison. The same conversion also shifts overrides whose local time is near midnight onto the neighbouring UTC day, where they will never match a slot.

title: `override.timeZone` is optional; undefined falls back to the server timezone
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` relies on `TimeRange.timeZone`, which was added as optional in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts`. When a caller of `getSlots` passes date overrides without `timeZone` (every call site other than the tRPC `getSchedule` that was updated in this PR), `.tz(undefined)` silently uses the process default timezone, producing a wrong `organizerUtcOffset` and therefore slots shifted by an arbitrary amount. Either make the field required on the type used by `GetSlots` or fall back explicitly to the organizer timezone.

title: Override converted to minutes-of-day wraps across midnight and lands on the wrong day
body: `startTime`/`endTime` are computed as `hour()*60 + minute()` after shifting the override by `offset`. When the shift crosses midnight (e.g. an override at 22:00–23:00 organizer time viewed from a timezone 2 hours ahead becomes 00:00–01:00 of the next day), the minute-of-day values wrap: the override is then applied to the *current* invitee day at the wrong clock time, or produces `startTime > endTime` which `buildSlots` discards, dropping the availability completely. Overrides must be attributed to the invitee day they actually fall on rather than being collapsed to minutes-of-day of the day being iterated.

title: No test for the main fix (date overrides of fixed hosts in round-robin)
body: The PR's primary claim is that date overrides of fixed hosts are now honoured for ROUND_ROBIN events, but the only new test asserts that the existing single-user override case returns the same UTC slots for a second invitee timezone. There is no scenario with a ROUND_ROBIN event type, a fixed host with a date override and an available non-fixed host, so the new `checkIfIsAvailable` override/working-hours code path (and the regression it can cause for split availability or for days with both an override and an existing booking) is untested.

title: Date-override days bypass the busy-time check entirely
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, after the date-override block, `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` returns early, before `busy.every(...)` is evaluated. This means that for any slot on a day that has a date override, existing Cal bookings and external-calendar busy times for that host are completely ignored, so already-booked slots are reported as available. Since every non-round-robin host is treated as `isFixed`, this applies to personal and collective events too, and leads to double bookings on any day with a date override. The override result must be combined with the busy check instead of short-circuiting it.

title: Working-hours check rejects slots when a host has multiple availability windows on the same day
body: The new check uses `workingHours.find((workingHour) => { ... if (start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime) return true; })` and treats a truthy result as "slot is outside of working hours" -> unavailable. `getUserAvailability` returns one working-hours entry per availability row, so a user with a split schedule (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 on the same weekday) has two entries for that day. A 10:00 slot is inside the first entry but outside the second, so `find` matches the second entry and the slot is dropped. The logic must be `!workingHours.some(entry => slot is inside entry)` (i.e. unavailable only if no entry contains the slot). As written, availability is silently broken for every user with more than one availability window per day.

title: `end` is computed from the slot start, not the slot end
body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates the `start` computation on the previous line; it was clearly meant to be derived from `slotEndTime`. As a result the `end > workingHour.endTime` condition never considers the event length, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after them is not detected by this check.

title: Date-override check rejects slots when a host has several ranges on the same date
body: `dateOverrides.find((date) => { ... })` returns truthy as soon as *one* override range on the slot's date does not contain the slot, and the code then returns `false` ("slot is not within the date override"). A date override may legitimately contain multiple time ranges for the same date (e.g. 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00). A slot inside the first range is outside the second, so it is incorrectly marked unavailable. The predicate must be inverted to "no range on that date contains the slot".

title: Dayjs objects compared with `===`, condition is dead code
body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly created Dayjs objects by reference, which is never true. The intended check (a zero-length override, i.e. the organizer marked the day unavailable) therefore never executes. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `valueOf()`.

title: Override date compared in server-local time against a UTC slot time
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` formats in the process's local timezone, while `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` is UTC (`time.utc()`). On a deployment whose system timezone is not UTC, the two date strings can differ for the same instant, so overrides are matched to the wrong day (or not matched at all), making the whole override branch behave differently per server timezone. Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` for the comparison.

title: Override end check ignores event length, allowing bookings that overrun the override
body: `if (slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")))` only tests the slot's *start* against the override end. For an override of 14:00-15:00 and a 60-minute event, a slot starting at 14:30 ends at 15:30 but is still considered inside the override and returned as available. Since for fixed hosts in round-robin events this is the only check against that host's override window, the fixed host can be booked outside their declared override. The comparison should use `slotEndTime`.

title: Override timeZone is optional; dayjs .tz(undefined) silently falls back to the default timezone
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` is called with `override.timeZone` typed as optional (`timeZone?: string` in packages/types/schedule.d.ts). Any caller of `getSlots` that passes date overrides without a `timeZone` (the field is newly added, so existing callers do not set it) will have `.tz(undefined)` resolve to dayjs's default/guessed timezone, producing a wrong `organizerUtcOffset` and shifting the override by an arbitrary amount. Either make the field required on this code path or explicitly fall back to a known timezone (e.g. UTC) when it is missing.

title: Timezone-shifted override wraps around midnight and lands on the wrong day
body: `startTime`/`endTime` are computed as `hour() * 60 + minute()` of the offset-shifted override time, i.e. minutes since the invitee's midnight. When the shift pushes the override across a day boundary the day information is lost: e.g. an organizer override 09:00-11:00 in UTC+5:30 viewed by an invitee in UTC-8 shifts to 19:30-21:30 of the *previous* day, but is emitted as minutes 1170-1290 of the invitee's current day, so slots are offered at a completely wrong time. Negative/over-1440 minute offsets need to be handled (clip to the day or split across days), as `buildSlots` only understands minutes within the invitee day.

title: No test for the PR's main fix (fixed-host date overrides in round-robin)
body: The PR's primary change is that date overrides of fixed hosts are now honoured for ROUND_ROBIN events (via the new `dateOverrides`/`workingHours` handling in `checkIfIsAvailable`), but the only test added covers invitee-timezone handling for a single personal event. There is no test with a round-robin event type where a fixed host has a date override and the round-robin host does not, which is exactly the regression-prone path (and the path where the `dateOverrideExist -> return true` short-circuit and the split-working-hours bug manifest). Please add a getSchedule test for that scenario, including a host with multiple availability windows on the override day.

title: toHaveTimeSlots matcher cannot detect missing slots
body: The matcher iterates with `.every()` over the *actual* slots and compares them index-wise to `expectedSlots`, without comparing array lengths. If the implementation returns fewer slots than expected (e.g. the first N are correct but trailing slots are dropped), the assertion still passes. The newly added timezone assertion relies on this matcher, so a partial regression in override handling would go unnoticed; the matcher should also assert `schedule.slots[dateString].length === expectedSlots.length`.

title: Date override day short-circuits the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls inside the override window, the `dateOverrides.find(...)` callback returns `undefined` for that override, so the outer `if` is false and execution reaches `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` (line 133-135). This returns early and completely skips the `busy.every(...)` loop below, meaning existing bookings, calendar busy times and buffers are ignored for any day that has a date override. Users can therefore be double-booked on date-override days. The override check should only decide whether the slot is inside the override window; the busy check must still run afterwards.

title: Working-hours check computes `end` from the slot start instead of the slot end
body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates the `start` computation on the previous line; `slotEndTime` is never used. As a result the check `end > workingHour.endTime` can never detect a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after them, so slots that overrun the end of the organizer's availability (e.g. a 60-minute slot starting 15 minutes before the schedule ends) are still reported as available.

title: Working-hours predicate marks a slot unavailable if ANY working-hour range does not contain it
body: The new check uses `workingHours.find(workingHour => ... if (start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime) return true)` and then treats a match as "slot is outside of working hours" -> unavailable. Because `find` succeeds as soon as one range does not contain the slot, any schedule with more than one availability range applicable to the same weekday (split days such as 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00, or ranges split across UTC midnight by `getWorkingHours`) will cause every slot to be rejected, producing an empty schedule. The predicate must instead require that *no* range contains the slot (e.g. `!workingHours.some(wh => wh.days.includes(day) && start >= wh.startTime && end <= wh.endTime)`).

title: Dayjs objects compared with `===`, condition is always false
body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly constructed Dayjs objects by reference, which is never true. The intended check (a zero-length override, i.e. a day marked unavailable) is therefore dead code; such overrides are only handled accidentally by the later `slotStartTime.isAfter(date.end)` branch, and a slot exactly at the override instant would be treated as available. Use `.isSame()` on the two values.

title: Timezone-shifted date override wraps around midnight and silently loses availability
body: The override start/end are converted to minutes-of-day with `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...minute()`. When the invitee/organizer offset difference pushes the override across a day boundary (e.g. organizer 22:00-23:00 with a +8h invitee, or 02:00 with a -5h invitee), `hour()` wraps to the other day, so `startTime` can become greater than `endTime`. `buildSlots` then drops such a range via its `if (start >= end) continue` guard (or produces slots at completely wrong times), so the override silently yields no availability for invitees in far-away timezones.

title: Override offset depends on an optional `timeZone` that falls back to the server timezone
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` is used to compute the organizer offset, but `TimeRange.timeZone` is declared optional in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts`. If any caller of `getSlots` passes date overrides without `timeZone` (only the slots router was updated to attach it), `dayjs.tz(undefined)` resolves to the dayjs default/system timezone, producing a wrong organizer offset and silently shifted override slots instead of an error. Either make `timeZone` required for the overrides consumed here or explicitly fall back to the organizer timezone already passed into `getSlots`.

title: No test covers the main fix (date overrides of fixed hosts in round-robin) and the new timezone test is not sensitive to the organizer timezone
body: The PR's primary change is that fixed-host date overrides are honoured for ROUND_ROBIN events (via the new `dateOverrides`/`workingHours` arguments to `checkIfIsAvailable`), but no test creates a round-robin event with a fixed host that has a date override, so that code path is unverified. The added test only re-requests the same personal event with a different invitee timezone and asserts identical UTC slots; it does not exercise an organizer whose schedule timezone differs from the invitee's, and it does not cover a day that has both a date override and an existing booking (where the current implementation returns the slot as available).

title: Migration crashes when embed_category / uncategorized_category_id rows are absent
body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. Site settings rows only exist in the `site_settings` table once an admin has changed them, so on the vast majority of installs there is no `embed_category` row (and/or no category whose name matches), the result set is empty, `[0]` is nil and the migration dies with NoMethodError on `nil['id']`, aborting the deploy. The same pattern is repeated on line 15 for `uncategorized_category_id`, which is a hidden setting that is frequently absent as well. Both queries need an empty-result guard.

title: Migrated hosts are inserted unnormalized (and interpolated unescaped), breaking embedding after upgrade
body: Existing `embeddable_hosts` values could legitimately contain a scheme (the old setting accepted `http://discourse.org`, as the removed SiteSetting spec showed). The migration inserts the raw lines verbatim, so rows like `http://discourse.org` land in `embeddable_hosts.host`. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against `URI(referer).host`, i.e. `discourse.org`, so these migrated rows never match and embedding silently stops working for those sites until an admin re-saves each host. The values should be normalized (strip scheme/path/whitespace, including a trailing `\r` from CRLF splits) before insert. Additionally the value is interpolated directly into the SQL string (`'#{h}'`), so a host containing a quote breaks the migration; use a bind/quoted insert.

title: record_for_host compares lower(host) against a non-downcased host
body: `record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but `host` comes straight from `uri.host` and is never downcased. A referer such as `http://EvilTrout.com/post` yields `EvilTrout.com`, which can never equal the lowercased column value, so a legitimately configured host is rejected and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` raises InvalidAccess (and TopicRetriever refuses to retrieve). The comparison value must be `host.downcase`.

title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `before_validation { self.host.sub!(...) }` assumes `host` is a string. `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly, so a create/update request that omits `host` (or sends null) leaves `host` nil and validation blows up with `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil` — a 500 instead of the intended validation error that the client's `popupAjaxError` expects. Guard with `return if host.blank?` (and prefer non-mutating `sub` so a frozen input string isn't mutated in place).

title: update/destroy 500 when the id does not exist
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown or already-deleted id; `save_host(nil)` then calls `nil.host =` and `destroy` (line 16) calls `nil.destroy`, producing a NoMethodError / 500 response. Two admins editing the list concurrently, or a stale browser tab, will hit this. Use `find_by` plus `raise Discourse::NotFound` (or `find`) so the client gets a proper 404.

title: has_many with embed: :ids does not side-load the hosts the client needs
body: The client hydrates embedded records in `store._hydrateEmbedded`: it sees `embeddable_host_ids` and looks the objects up in `root['embeddable_hosts']`. With ActiveModel::Serializers `embed: :ids` and no `include: true`, only the id array is rendered and no root-level `embeddable_hosts` collection is produced, so `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for every id and `embedding.embeddable_hosts` becomes an array of `undefined`, which the `embedding.hbs`/`embeddable-host` component then renders/mutates. This needs `embed: :ids, include: true` (or `embed: :objects`), and a JS/controller test that actually renders a non-empty host list would catch it.

title: New `_ids` hydration silently drops ids and can throw on non-array values
body: The widened regex `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` now captures every key ending in `_ids`. In the plural branch the original key is deleted unconditionally, even when `root[pluralize(subType)]` is missing: `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined` for each id, so the model ends up with e.g. `groups: [undefined, undefined]` and the original `group_ids` data is gone — a silent data loss for any REST-serialized payload (`__rest_serializer === "1"`) that sends id arrays without side-loaded objects. Also `obj[k].map(...)` throws a TypeError if the serializer sends `foo_ids: null`, and the `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code because `map` always returns an array. Only delete the `_ids` key when the side-loaded collection was actually found, and guard against non-array values.

title: String.replace without /g only converts the first underscore in the type name
body: `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces a single occurrence, so a model type with more than one underscore (e.g. `embeddable_host_group`) will not be matched against `ADMIN_MODELS` and its requests will be sent to `/` instead of `/admin/`, failing with 404/403. Use `type.replace(/_/g, '-')`.

title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a no-op that reports success
body: `update` only re-renders the freshly-fetched `@embedding` OpenStruct; it ignores the request body entirely. The admin controller's `saveChanges` action (`admin-embedding.js.es6`) calls `embedding.update({})` against this route, so the endpoint advertises a write operation and returns 200 while persisting nothing. Either implement the update or drop the route and the client action so no one builds on a fake write API.

title: Host validation rejects valid TLDs and ports can never match
body: The format regex caps the TLD at `[a-z]{2,5}`, so legitimate hosts such as `blog.technology`, `example.travel` or `foo.museum` cannot be saved, and `localhost`/bare IPs are rejected too — admins migrating from the old free-form `embeddable_hosts` setting may be unable to re-save their hosts. The regex also permits a `:port` suffix, but `record_for_host` matches against `URI(...).host`, which never includes the port, so a stored `example.com:3000` can never match a referer. There is also no uniqueness validation on `host`, allowing duplicate rows for the same domain.

title: No request specs for the new embeddable host CRUD endpoints
body: The only assertion is that the class inherits from Admin::AdminController. None of create/update/destroy are exercised, so the nil-record 500s in `update`/`destroy`, the nil-host NoMethodError in the model callback, the uncategorized-category fallback, and the serializer shape are all untested. The same applies to `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`. Please add specs that POST/PUT/DELETE as an admin, including the missing-id and missing-host cases.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`). It happens to work because Fabrication loads every file in the directory, but the naming is inverted and anyone looking for or editing the category fabricators will not find them where expected. Swap the file contents.

title: Stale test name: expandable_first_post? no longer depends on embeddable hosts
body: `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` no longer asserts what it claims — `Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` and ignores hosts entirely, so this example passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and the topic has no embed. Either delete the example or rename it to describe what it actually covers, otherwise it gives false confidence that host configuration is still checked.

title: Migration raises NoMethodError when `embed_category` site setting row is absent
body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes the query returns at least one row. Site settings are only persisted when changed from their default, so on the vast majority of installs there is no `embed_category` row (and even when there is, the join on category *name* may not match). `PG::Result#[]` returns nil for a missing row, so `[0]['id']` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil`, aborting the migration and leaving the deployment half-migrated. The same problem exists on line 15 for the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup. Both queries need nil guards.

title: Migrated hosts keep their scheme/path, so embedding silently breaks after upgrade
body: Existing values of the `embeddable_hosts` setting could contain entries like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` (the old spec and docs explicitly supported this). The migration inserts those raw strings directly with `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, bypassing the model's `before_validation` callback that strips `https?://` and paths. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares the stored value with `URI(referer).host`, which never contains a scheme or path, so every migrated row with a scheme/path will stop matching and embedding will start returning `Discourse::InvalidAccess` for those sites. The migration should normalize each value (strip scheme and path) before inserting.

title: Unescaped string interpolation into INSERT statement
body: The host value from the old site setting is interpolated directly into SQL: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. Any value containing a single quote (or stray whitespace/CR from splitting on "\n" only) will produce invalid SQL and abort the migration; it is also an injection vector from stored data. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` or a parameterized insert, and strip each entry.

title: `create_table ... force: true` can drop an existing table and its data
body: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` first. If this migration is ever re-run (or a table of that name already exists, e.g. created by a plugin or a partially applied deploy) all existing rows are silently destroyed. Migrations should not use `force: true`.

title: Host comparison lowercases the column but not the incoming value
body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` compares the lowercased column against the raw value extracted from the referer. `URI#host` preserves the case the browser sent (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com`), so a referer with any uppercase characters will not match a stored host and the embed request will be rejected with `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. The parameter must be downcased (`host.downcase`).

title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called before validation runs. If `host` is nil — which happens whenever the admin endpoint is posted without a host value (`host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` can assign nil) — this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil`, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `return if host.blank?` and use the non-destructive `sub` (the destructive `sub!` also mutates the caller's string in place).

title: Hosts with a port pass validation but can never match a referer
body: The validation regex permits an optional `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` port and the `before_validation` callback only strips the scheme and path, so `example.com:3000` is stored as-is. However `record_for_host` matches against `URI(referer).host`, which never includes the port, so any host saved with a port will never be allowed and embedding from that origin always fails. Either strip the port on save or compare against host+port.

title: Host format regex rejects valid hosts that previously worked
body: `\.[a-z]{2,5}` restricts the TLD to 2–5 characters and requires at least one dot, so hosts such as `blog.technology`, `foo.website`, `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or an intranet hostname are rejected. The replaced `embeddable_hosts` site setting (a `host_list`) accepted these, so admins migrating from it cannot re-add such hosts through the new UI.

title: No uniqueness validation or index on host
body: Nothing prevents two rows with the same host (possibly pointing at different categories), which makes `record_for_host`'s `.first` result arbitrary and therefore the category used for new embedded topics non-deterministic. There is also no index on `host`, while `host_allowed?` runs on every embed request with `lower(host) = ?`, which cannot use a plain index. Consider a uniqueness validation plus a unique index on `lower(host)`.

title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError on unknown id
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil when the id does not exist (stale admin tab, double-delete, guessed id). `host.destroy` on line 16 and `save_host(nil)` from `update` then raise `NoMethodError` and return a 500 instead of a 404/error JSON. Use `find_by` plus an explicit not-found response (or `find`, which raises RecordNotFound and is handled).

title: Missing `embeddable_host` params cause a 500
body: `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises `NoMethodError` if the `embeddable_host` key is absent from the request. The controller should require the parameter (e.g. `params.require(:embeddable_host)`) so a malformed request yields a 400 rather than an exception.

title: `embed: :ids` without `include: true` does not side-load the host records
body: The serializer declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids`, which emits only `embeddable_host_ids` and does not put an `embeddable_hosts` array in the JSON root. The client's `_hydrateEmbedded` resolves `*_ids` by looking up `root['embeddable_hosts']`; when that collection is missing, `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for every id, so `embedding.embeddable_hosts` becomes an array of `undefined` and the admin table renders empty/broken rows. `embed: :ids, include: true` (side-loading) is required.

title: `embedding#update` is a no-op that reports success
body: The `update` action persists nothing — it only re-renders the freshly fetched `@embedding` OpenStruct. The client's `saveChanges` action (`admin-embedding.js.es6`) calls `embedding.update({})` and will report success without any change having been made. Either implement the update or remove the route, action and the unused client-side `saveChanges`.

title: Plural embedded hydration crashes on null and silently produces undefined entries
body: In the new `*_ids` branch, `obj[k].map(...)` throws a TypeError if the serialized value is `null` rather than an array, and `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` can never fall back to `[]` because `hydrated` is always an array — if the side-loaded collection is missing, the result is an array of `undefined` values while the original `*_ids` key is unconditionally deleted, so the data is lost rather than left intact. The singular branch correctly only deletes the key when a lookup succeeded; the plural branch should behave the same and guard against non-array values.

title: `type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore
body: `String.prototype.replace` with a string pattern replaces only the first occurrence, so a type with more than one underscore (e.g. `some_admin_model`) will never match an entry in `ADMIN_MODELS` and would be routed to `/` instead of `/admin/`. Use a global regex (`type.replace(/_/g, '-')`).

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` now contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators, while `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` contains the `:embeddable_host` fabricator. The two file bodies were clearly exchanged; this makes the fabricators impossible to locate by filename and will confuse every future change to either model's fixtures.

title: No tests for the new embeddable host CRUD endpoints
body: The only assertion is that the class inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. The new `create`, `update` and `destroy` actions control the embedding whitelist (a security boundary: which external sites may embed the forum) and contain non-trivial logic (category fallback to `uncategorized_category_id`, nil-record handling, error rendering), none of which is exercised. The same applies to `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`. At minimum add tests that a host can be created/updated/deleted, that validation errors are returned, and that a non-admin is refused.

title: Test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests that
body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` and no longer looks at embeddable hosts at all. This example passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false for an unsaved topic, so the name is misleading and the assertion no longer covers anything related to hosts. Rename or remove it.

title: Migration crashes when the `embed_category` site setting row does not exist
body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. `embed_category` defaulted to '' and is only persisted in `site_settings` if an admin changed it, so on the vast majority of installs this query returns zero rows and `result[0]` is nil/out of range, raising before the data migration can run. The whole `rake db:migrate` then fails and the deploy is blocked. The row lookup needs to be guarded (e.g. fetch into a variable and check for presence) before dereferencing.

title: Fallback query also dereferences a possibly-missing site_settings row
body: `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value']` assumes the `uncategorized_category_id` setting is stored in the database. It is a hidden setting with default -1 and is frequently absent from `site_settings`, so this raises in the same way as the `embed_category` lookup. Even when present it can be -1, which would be inserted into `embeddable_hosts.category_id` (declared NOT NULL but with no FK), producing rows that point at a non-existent category.

title: Migrated hosts keep their scheme and are interpolated unescaped into SQL
body: Existing values of the `embeddable_hosts` setting were allowed to be of the form `http://discourse.org` (the old `allows_embeddable_host?` stripped the scheme at comparison time). This INSERT stores the raw line, so after upgrading, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` — which compares `lower(host)` with `URI(referer).host` (`discourse.org`) — will never match those rows and embedding silently breaks for previously-working sites. The value is also interpolated directly into the SQL string, so a stray apostrophe or trailing \r in the setting breaks or corrupts the statement. Normalize each host (strip scheme/path/whitespace, downcase) and bind/quote the value.

title: `create_table ... force: true` can silently drop an existing table
body: `force: true` issues a DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating `embeddable_hosts`. If the migration is ever re-run, or if a table with that name already exists (e.g. created by a plugin or a partially applied migration), all existing embeddable host configuration is destroyed without warning. `force: true` should not be used in a schema migration.

title: No index or uniqueness constraint on embeddable_hosts.host
body: `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` on every `embed/comments` and `embed/count` request as well as in TopicRetriever, but the table has no index on `host` (and `lower(host)` would need a functional index anyway), so every embed request does a sequential scan. There is also no unique index or model-level uniqueness validation, so the admin UI happily creates duplicate rows for the same host, after which `record_for_host` returns an arbitrary one and the "post to category" mapping becomes non-deterministic.

title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally in `before_validation`. `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly, so a create/update request with a missing or null `host` (trivially reachable from the new admin UI or any API client) raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil` and returns a 500 instead of the intended validation error. Guard the callback with `return if host.blank?`.

title: Host lookup compares lower(host) against a non-downcased value
body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the value extracted from the URI. `URI#host` preserves the case of the referer/embed URL, so a referer like `http://EvilTrout.com/post` (or a host saved with any uppercase letters) will not match an existing record and embedding is rejected with 'invalid referer host'. Hostnames are case-insensitive; the parameter must be downcased (`host.downcase`).

title: update/destroy blow up with 500 when the id does not exist
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil; `update` then passes nil into `save_host` (which calls `host.host = ...`) and `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on nil. Both raise NoMethodError and return a 500 for a request referencing an already-deleted or bogus id — for example two admins deleting the same host, or a stale browser tab. Use `find_by` plus an explicit 404/`raise Discourse::NotFound`.

title: has_many uses `embed: :ids` without `include: true`, so hosts are never sent
body: With ActiveModel::Serializers `embed: :ids` and no `include: true`, the payload contains only `embeddable_host_ids` and no top-level `embeddable_hosts` collection. The client's `store._hydrateEmbedded` resolves `*_ids` by looking up `root['embeddable_hosts']`; when that collection is absent `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for each id, so `embedding.embeddable_hosts` becomes an array of `undefined` and the admin Embedding page renders empty rows. Either sideload the objects (`embed: :ids, include: true`) or embed objects directly.

title: `*_ids` hydration crashes on null and silently produces undefined entries
body: In `_hydrateEmbedded` the new plural branch calls `obj[k].map(...)` without checking that the value is an array, so a serializer sending `"foo_ids": null` throws a TypeError and the whole hydration (and therefore the find/findAll promise) fails. Additionally, when `_lookupSubType` cannot resolve an id (collection not sideloaded) it returns `undefined`, and those `undefined` values are pushed into the resulting array instead of being filtered out; the `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code since `map` always returns an array. Guard for non-array values and compact the results.

title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding ignores its payload and saves nothing
body: `update` only re-renders the freshly built OpenStruct; it never reads `params` or persists anything. The matching client code (`admin-embedding.js.es6` `saveChanges` calling `embedding.update({})`) therefore does nothing either. Either implement the update or remove the route/action and the dead `saveChanges` action so callers aren't misled into believing changes were saved.

title: Fabricator file contents were swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines the `:embeddable_host` fabricator while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category`. This inverts the file-name convention Fabrication (and every other fabricator in the suite) relies on, breaks name-based lookup/lazy loading, and makes the definitions impossible to find. The two file bodies should be exchanged.

title: New write endpoints have no behavioural or authorization tests
body: The only assertion is that the class inherits from Admin::AdminController. There is no coverage for create/update/destroy (including the uncategorized-category fallback, invalid host validation errors, and missing-id handling, which currently 500s), nor for the fact that non-staff/non-admin users must be rejected from these new state-changing admin routes. Given this PR introduces a new writable admin resource, request specs for success, validation failure and access control are needed.

title: Test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests that condition
body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer consults embeddable hosts at all, so this example passes merely because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false for an unsaved topic. The name is now misleading and the example asserts nothing about hosts; it should be renamed/removed so future readers aren't misled about what behaviour is covered.

title: Underscore-to-dash conversion only replaces the first underscore
body: `type.replace('_', '-')` with a string pattern replaces a single occurrence, so a type such as `some_embeddable_host` would become `some-embeddable_host` and fail the ADMIN_MODELS lookup, silently routing the request to the non-admin base path. Use `/_/g` (or `Ember.String.dasherize`) so all underscores are converted.

title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently removes the (width, height) variant
body: `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) is immediately redefined by `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149). Ruby has no method overloading, so only the 3/4-argument version survives and any existing caller that passes `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height)` (4 positional args + opts) now raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments`. Either keep one signature or give the dimension-string variant a different name (e.g. `downsize_to`).

title: Removal of `self.dimensions` and change of `optimize` signature breaks external callers
body: `self.dimensions(width, height)` was deleted and `self.optimize` changed from `(operation, from, to, width, height, opts)` to `(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts)`. These are public class methods used by plugins/specs and other call sites; existing calls will now raise `NoMethodError` / `ArgumentError`.
