If the change is intended, the old entry points should be kept as deprecated shims or all call sites and specs updated in the same PR.

title: Animated-GIF downsize path passes a percentage to gifsicle, which it does not accept
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` ends up in `downsize_instructions_animated` -> `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80% ...`. gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects explicit `WxH` dimensions (percentages are only supported by `--scale`), so the command fails, `convert_with` returns false, and the while loop spins through all 5 attempts without shrinking the file. Large animated GIFs will then be rejected by the size validation even though the feature claims to downsize them.

title: In-place downsize can leave a stale file handle, causing a wrong filesize and corrupt upload
body: The loop runs `convert` with the same path as both source and destination and then re-reads `tempfile.size` / passes `tempfile` to `Upload.create_for`. ImageMagick may replace the file (new inode) rather than truncate it, in which case the still-open Tempfile descriptor refers to the old, unlinked inode: `tempfile.size` keeps reporting the pre-resize size (loop burns all 5 attempts) and `Upload.create_for` stores the original, un-resized bytes. The tempfile is also never rewound after the external process writes to it. Reopen/stat the path (e.g. `File.size(tempfile.path)`) and rewind/reopen the handle before creating the upload, or write to a fresh temp file.

title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` with a hardcoded constant. Admins who lowered the limit can no longer restrict API URL uploads, and admins who raised it above 10MB will have downloads truncated/rejected. The cap should be derived from the relevant site setting (and from the attachment limit when the upload is not an image, since this path handles both).

title: Client-side size check hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types
body: `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024;` replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. Non-image attachments are not auto-downsized by the new server code, so an attachment between `max_attachment_size_kb` and 10MB now passes client validation and is only rejected by the server, producing a confusing late failure. Conversely, sites configured with a limit above 10MB will have valid uploads blocked in the browser. The limit should stay driven by the per-type site setting (images can be allowed to exceed it since they get downsized).

title: 413 error message reports a hardcoded 10MB limit that may not match the server
body: In `displayErrorForUpload`, the 413 branch now shows `max_size_kb: 10240` instead of the configured `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. A 413 usually comes from the web server's own body-size limit, so the user is shown a number unrelated to the actual limit, which is misleading when the site is configured differently.

title: No tests for the new automatic downsizing path
body: The new downsize loop in `create_upload` (retry count, interaction with `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, animated GIF handling, images that still exceed the limit after 5 attempts) and the changed `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` signatures are not covered by any test in this PR, so the duplicate-method and gifsicle problems went unnoticed. Add controller/model specs covering an oversized image upload and a still-too-large image.

title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently breaks the 4-argument form
body: `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is defined at line 145 and then immediately redefined at line 149 as `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the second definition wins, so the width/height variant is unreachable. Any existing caller doing `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, w, h)` (or with opts) now binds `h` to `dimensions` and the opts hash/height to `opts`, producing either a bogus `-resize` argument or a `TypeError` when `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` is evaluated on an Integer. Use a single method that accepts either a dimension string or width/height instead of two same-named methods.

title: Client upload size limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
body: `maxSizeKB` was read from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024`. Sites that configure a smaller limit will let users upload files the server will reject (bad UX, wasted bandwidth), and sites configured above 10MB will see valid uploads blocked client-side. The error message also now always says 10240 kb regardless of the actual configured limit. This looks like leftover debug code (PR description is "Test 1") and should read the setting again.

title: 413 error message hardcodes 10MB instead of configured max image size
body: In `displayErrorForUpload`, the 413 branch no longer uses `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` and instead reports `10 * 1024` kb. The user is therefore told a limit that may have nothing to do with the real configured/web-server limit, which is misleading.

title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB instead of the site setting
body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. Administrators can no longer restrict the amount of remote data an API upload will pull down; a site configured for e.g. 1MB images now fetches up to 10MB per request (resource/DoS exposure), and sites configured above 10MB silently lose functionality. Derive the cap from the setting.

title: Downsize loop uses a possibly stale `tempfile.size` and converts a file in place while its handle is open
body: The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` (source == destination) and then re-reads `tempfile.size`. `Tempfile#size` stats the still-open file descriptor; ImageMagick/ImageOptim may replace the file (new inode) rather than truncate it in place, in which case the loop keeps seeing the original size, burns all 5 attempts re-shrinking the image, and then passes a wrong filesize to `Upload.create_for`. Re-open/stat the path (e.g. `File.size(tempfile.path)`) after each conversion and pass that size to `create_for`.

title: Percentage dimension and extension-less temp path break animated GIF handling
body: `downsize` is called with the dimension string `"80%"`. For animated images `OptimizedImage.optimize` would dispatch to the gifsicle path, but (a) that branch only triggers when the source path matches `/\.GIF$/i` and the upload tempfile has no `.gif` extension, so it never triggers, and (b) gifsicle's `--resize-fit` does not accept a percentage (`--scale` is the percentage option), so it would fail if it did. Consequently large animated GIFs are run through `convert #{from}[0]`, which keeps only the first frame and silently destroys the animation.

title: Downsize loop ignores conversion failure
body: The return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is discarded. `convert_with` returns false (and only logs) when ImageMagick or ImageOptim fails, so on failure the loop spins through all 5 attempts invoking an external process each time with no effect, before creating an upload that will be rejected for size. Break out of the loop when the downsize returns false.

title: No tests for the new downsize API or auto-downsizing path
body: The change alters the public signature of `OptimizedImage.optimize`/`downsize` (dimension string instead of width/height), removes `self.dimensions`, and adds a new auto-downsize loop in `UploadsController#create_upload`, but no specs are added or updated. Existing specs that stub/call `optimize(op, from, to, width, height, opts)` or `dimensions` would break, and the new loop (including the size-reread and failure behaviour) is untested.

title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently removes the 4-argument signature
body: `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is defined at line 145 and then immediately redefined at line 149 as `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the second definition wins, so the width/height form is dead code and any existing caller doing `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height)` now raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (4 for 2..3)`. Either rename the new entry point (e.g. `downsize_to`) or make a single method that accepts both forms.

title: Downsize loop writes to the source file and ignores failures, risking a corrupted upload
body: The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` with the same path as input and output and never inspects the return value. If `convert`/`ImageOptim` fails (which `convert_with` reports by returning false after swallowing the exception), the destination file — i.e. the user's original upload — may have already been truncated or left partially written, and the loop then runs up to 5 more times on the broken file before the (now corrupt) data is stored via `Upload.create_for`. Convert into a separate temp file and `break` out of the loop as soon as `downsize` returns false, keeping the original intact.

title: Animated GIF uploads are silently flattened to their first frame
body: The downsize call passes `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`. When that setting is false (the default), `OptimizedImage.optimize` uses `downsize_instructions`, which runs `convert #{from}[0] ...` — only the first frame. Because the output path is the uploaded file itself, a large animated GIF uploaded by a user is permanently converted to a single-frame image, losing content the user intended to post. The thumbnail setting is also the wrong switch for deciding how to re-encode an original upload; animation should be preserved regardless (use `allow_animation: true` or a dedicated setting).

title: Downsizing may still exceed the limit, leaving the user with a generic failure
body: The loop gives up after 5 iterations of 80% scaling. If the image is still over `max_image_size_kb` (very likely for e.g. a 40 MB photo with a 1 MB limit, since 5 iterations only reduce area to ~33%), `Upload.create_for` rejects it and the user sees a validation error even though the feature claims uploads are "automatically reduced to allowed size". Either loop until the size target is met (with a sane iteration/dimension floor) or compute the required scale factor up front.

title: Client-side size limit hardcoded to 10 MB, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb / max_image_size_kb
body: `maxSizeKB` was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. This now applies to attachments as well as images, so a site configured with e.g. `max_attachment_size_kb = 2048` will let the browser upload a 9 MB attachment that the server then rejects (attachments are not downsized at all), and the error dialog quotes a bogus 10240 KB limit. Conversely a site with a limit above 10 MB can no longer upload files it is configured to accept. The client limit should remain driven by the site setting for attachments (and only be relaxed for images that the server will downsize).

title: 413 error message reports a hardcoded 10 MB limit
body: The HTTP 413 handler now shows `max_size_kb: 10240` instead of the configured `max_image_size_kb`. A 413 comes from the web server's own body-size limit, which is unrelated to this constant, so the dialog will state a limit that is wrong for most installations and misleads users about what size is acceptable.

title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10 MB for all upload types
body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the previous `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` cap and is used for every `type`, including non-image attachments which are never downsized afterwards. Sites that configure smaller limits now fetch (and buffer) up to 10 MB from a remote URL before rejecting it, and sites with larger configured limits can no longer use the API URL path for bigger files.

title: No tests for the new automatic downsizing path
body: The PR adds a non-trivial in-place image re-encoding loop to `create_upload` and changes `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` signatures, but no specs are added or updated. There is no coverage for: an oversized image being reduced below `max_image_size_kb`, the `downsize` failure path, animated GIF handling, or the fact that the old 4-argument `downsize` signature is now unusable (which existing callers/specs would catch).

title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists
body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (a user may have no topic_users row for the topic — e.g. notifications driven by category/mailing-list settings, a row that was never created because of the `rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` swallow in `TopicUser.change`, or simply a user who types/visits the unsubscribe URL for a topic they never opened). The very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, raising `NoMethodError: undefined method for nil`, which surfaces as a 500 for a link that users click directly from email. The action needs to create/handle the missing record (e.g. via `TopicUser.change`) instead of assuming one exists.

title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping, so the mute can be silently undone
body: The new action mutates `notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly instead of going through `TopicUser.change`. Two consequences: (1) `notifications_changed_at` / `notifications_reason_id` are not set, and `TopicUser#update_last_read` only auto-tracks a topic `when tu.notifications_reason_id is null` — so after unsubscribing, the next visit to the topic will auto-bump the user back to `tracking`, undoing the unsubscribe; (2) no `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", notification_level_change: ...)` is sent, so other open browser tabs keep showing the stale notification level.

title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed as an unauthenticated-looking GET (CSRF / link prefetch)
body: `unsubscribe` is reachable via `GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and changes the user's notification level, while `check_xhr` is skipped. Rails CSRF protection does not apply to GET, so any third-party page can mute a logged-in user's topics with ``, and mail clients / corporate link scanners / prefetchers that fetch links in email bodies will mute topics without the user ever clicking. A mutating endpoint should require a POST/PUT (or a one-time signed key as the digest unsubscribe does), with the GET URL only rendering a confirmation page.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking other callers
body: The `unsubscribe_link` string gained a mandatory `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, but it is rendered from `Email::MessageBuilder#body` / `#html_part` for every caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to supply `unsubscribe_url`; any other core mailer, job or plugin that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without it will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to send the email (the spec change in `message_builder_spec.rb` had to add the param for exactly this reason). Give `unsubscribe_url` a default in `MessageBuilder#initialize` (or guard the per-topic sentence) so the option stays backwards compatible.

title: Client route shows the unsubscribe confirmation without performing any unsubscribe
body: The Ember `topicUnsubscribe` route only loads the topic view; the actual notification-level change happens server-side in `TopicsController#unsubscribe` during the initial HTML request. Any client-side transition to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` (an in-app link, or browser back/forward handled by the SPA without a full page load) will render "You will stop receiving notifications for …" while nothing was changed on the server, misleading the user. The route should issue the unsubscribe request itself (or the page should reflect the level returned by the server).

title: Confirmation text claims notifications stop even when the level is only lowered to 'regular'
body: `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` always says "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>", but the server toggles: a user at `watching`/`tracking` is moved to `regular` (which still emails on replies to their posts, mentions and quotes) and only a second click sets `muted`. So the majority of users who click the email link are told notifications have stopped while they will still receive some. The message should reflect the resulting notification level.

title: No specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint
body: The PR adds a new state-changing controller action, route and `Topic#unsubscribe_url`, but no controller/request spec was added. The untested branches include: missing `TopicUser` row (currently a 500), the watching→regular vs regular→muted toggle, the slug-mismatch 301 redirect, the not-logged-in path, and that the JSON/HTML responses render. Without tests the toggle semantics and the nil case can regress silently.

title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (e.g. the user never visited/read the topic, the row was removed, or the topic was merged/moved), and line 107 immediately calls `tu.notification_level` on it. Any such request raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 to a user who just clicked an unsubscribe link in an email. The action needs to handle the nil case (create the record or go through `TopicUser.change`, which upserts).

title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed as a GET with no CSRF protection
body: `unsubscribe` is routed as `GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and mutates `TopicUser.notification_level`, and `check_xhr` is skipped for it. Because Rails does not verify CSRF tokens for GET requests, any third-party page can trigger it for a logged-in user with e.g. ``, silently muting topics. Link-prefetching/scanning agents that carry the user's session (browser prefetch, some security proxies) can also fire it unintentionally. The mutation should happen on a POST/PUT (or be protected by a signed one-time key, like the existing digest unsubscribe key flow).

title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping and MessageBus notification
body: The new action writes `notification_level` directly on the record instead of using `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`. As a result `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not updated (the level stays attributed to the old reason, e.g. `auto_watch_category`) and no `/topic/:id` MessageBus `notification_level_change` message is published, so other open tabs/clients keep showing the stale notification level and auto-tracking logic sees an inconsistent reason id.

title: Unsubscribe link requires an active session
body: `:unsubscribe` was added to the `ensure_logged_in` before_filter, so a recipient who clicks the per-topic unsubscribe link from an email while not logged in (the common case for mail clients in a different browser/profile) gets a not-logged-in error/login redirect instead of unsubscribing. Email unsubscribe flows in this codebase otherwise use a token (see `email/unsubscribe/:key`); the new link should either use such a key or at least redirect back to this URL after login.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url} and will raise for callers that don't pass it
body: The `unsubscribe_link` string gained a `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, but `Email::MessageBuilder` provides no default for it (only `site_name`, `base_url`, `user_preferences_url` are defaulted). Any `build_email` call that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` in `MessageBuilder#body`/`#html_part`, breaking email delivery. The need to update `message_builder_spec.rb` to add `unsubscribe_url` demonstrates this. Add a fallback in `MessageBuilder` (e.g. default `unsubscribe_url` to the user preferences URL) so existing/plugin callers keep working.

title: Unsubscribe page text claims notifications stop even when level is only lowered to regular
body: `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` reads "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>", but the server action lowers a watching/tracking user to `regular` (not `muted`) on the first click. At `regular` the user still receives notifications/emails for replies, mentions and quotes, so the message is wrong for the most common case and users will believe they are unsubscribed when they are not. Either mute on the first click or make the text reflect the actual resulting level.

title: No specs for the new unsubscribe action
body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` endpoint has no request/controller spec. Untested behaviours that are easy to get wrong and are currently broken or risky: missing `TopicUser` row (raises NoMethodError), the watching/tracking -> regular vs regular/muted -> muted transition, the 301 redirect when the slug is absent or mismatched, and the anonymous-user path. Please add specs covering these.

title: Route name topicUnsubscribe may not resolve the template at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs
body: The route is registered as `topicUnsubscribe`, while the template was added at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` (i.e. template name `topic/unsubscribe`) and the view at `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` (name `topic-unsubscribe`). The resolver decamelizes/dasherizes route names, so `topicUnsubscribe` looks for `topic_unsubscribe`/`topic-unsubscribe`; the template and view names are therefore inconsistent with each other, and the unsubscribe page risks rendering blank. Please make the names consistent (e.g. put the template at `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`) or add an explicit `renderTemplate`.

title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser record exists
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` (e.g. a user who was notified via mailing-list mode, a group PM, or whose topic_users row was never created / was removed), and the next line immediately calls `tu.notification_level`. The result is a 500 error for the user who clicked the "stop receiving notifications about this topic" link in an email — the worst possible place to raise an exception. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` (which upserts) or guard for nil.

title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed as a plain GET without CSRF protection
body: `unsubscribe` is routed as `GET` (config/routes.rb lines 440-441) and `check_xhr` is skipped, yet it mutates the user's `topic_users.notification_level`. Rails CSRF verification does not apply to GET, so any third-party page can embed `` and silently mute/down-level topics for any logged-in visitor. Link scanners/prefetchers in a logged-in browser session have the same effect. Either require a signed/one-time unsubscribe key in the URL and have the GET only render a confirmation page, or perform the mutation via a POST/PUT from the client.

title: Unsubscribe action is a non-idempotent toggle, so a page refresh changes notification level again
body: The handler flips `watching/tracking -> regular` and `regular/muted -> muted`. Because the HTML request performs the mutation, simply reloading the unsubscribe page (or pressing back/forward, or clicking the emailed link twice) applies the change a second time: a watching user who refreshes ends up muted without ever asking for it, and the Ember route for the same URL (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6) only fetches `/t/:id.json`, so client-side navigation to the URL changes nothing at all — the two paths behave inconsistently. Make the operation idempotent (always set one explicit target level) and drive it from an explicit action rather than from rendering the page.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}; callers that omit it will raise
body: config/locales/server.en.yml's `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but `html_part`/`body` call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is set, without guaranteeing the key is present. Any caller (other mailers, plugins, future call sites) that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but no `unsubscribe_url` will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to send the email — the spec change in spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb (adding `unsubscribe_url`) is evidence the old call shape no longer works. Provide a default `unsubscribe_url` in `@template_args` (e.g. fall back to the preferences URL) or only append the per-topic sentence when the URL is supplied.

title: No specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint
body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action (notification-level toggle, slug redirect, nil TopicUser path, anonymous access) has no request/controller spec, and `Topic#unsubscribe_url` has no model spec. The nil-TopicUser crash and the non-idempotent toggle would both have been caught by a basic spec. Please add coverage for: missing TopicUser row, each starting notification level, missing-slug 301 redirect, and not-logged-in access.

title: Unsubscribe route refetches the topic view that the server already preloaded
body: The server-rendered unsubscribe page stores the serialized topic via `store_preloaded("topic_#{id}", ...)` in `perform_show_response`, but this route ignores the preload store and issues a fresh `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` request on boot, duplicating a full topic-view query/serialization for every unsubscribe click. Read from `PreloadStore` first (as the regular topic route does) and fall back to the request.

title: Confirmation text claims notifications stop even when level is only lowered to "regular"
body: `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` ("You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}.") is shown unconditionally, but the server may have only lowered the level from watching/tracking to `regular`, in which case the user still gets notifications for replies to them and mentions. The page should reflect the level actually applied (the response already carries the topic details) so the message is not misleading.

title: Match statistics written from inside a validation get rolled back / double-counted
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` performs a DB write (increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`) and it is invoked from `validate_each`, i.e. from the record's validation chain. Two consequences: (1) ActiveRecord runs validations inside the save transaction, so when the user save ultimately fails (which is exactly what happens when the email is blocked) the counter update is rolled back and the match is never recorded for any code path that calls `user.save` directly (e.g. `User.create_for_email`, invite redemption); (2) `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` (for the Discourse Hub check) and then `user.save`, so the validator runs twice and a single signup attempt can increment `match_count` twice. Statistics should be updated outside validation (e.g. in the controller/creation flow) or with an atomic `update_column`/`increment!` executed outside the transaction.

title: Blocked-email lookup is exact and case-sensitive, trivially bypassed
body: `should_block?` does `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` with no normalization, and neither the model nor the migration downcases/strips the stored value. Since user-supplied emails are not normalized before reaching the validator, blocking `spammer@example.com` does not block `Spammer@Example.com` (Postgres string comparison is case-sensitive), so the block is defeated by changing capitalization. Normalize on write (`before_validation { self.email = Email.downcase(email).strip }`) and on lookup, and make the unique index operate on the normalized value.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of match_count loses updates
body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` reads the current value in Ruby and writes it back. Concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email (the common case for a spam wave) will read the same value and overwrite each other, under-counting matches. Use an atomic SQL increment (e.g. `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')`) instead. Also note `record.save` here silently ignores failures (its return value is discarded), so a validation/DB error leaves the counter silently unupdated.

title: rejectedEmails array is defined on the prototype and shared/never reset
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is a mutable array literal on the class definition, so it is shared by every instance of `CreateAccountController` and is never cleared. Because `pushObject` mutates this shared array, emails rejected during one modal session stay rejected for the lifetime of the page (and are visible to any other instance), e.g. after an admin unblocks an address or after the user fixes an unrelated server-side error, the email field keeps showing "invalid". Initialize it per instance (in `init`/`setupController`) and reset it when the modal is opened.

title: Blocked-email check is skipped when another email error exists
body: The `record.errors[attribute].blank?` guard means that if the whitelist/blacklist rule already added an error (or any earlier validator added an email error, e.g. uniqueness), `BlockedEmail.should_block?` is never called and the match is neither detected nor counted. The blocked-email statistics therefore silently miss attempts that also trip another email rule, which undermines the `match_count`/`last_match_at` data this feature is built on.

title: Extracted whitelist/blacklist logic is untested in the new validator spec
body: The whitelist/blacklist email-domain logic was moved out of `User#email_validator` into `EmailValidator`, but the new spec only exercises the blocked-email branch with `should_block?` stubbed. There is no coverage for `email_domains_whitelist`/`email_domains_blacklist` behaviour in its new location, nor an integration test proving that `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` on `User` actually rejects a blocked email on save. A regression in the moved code would go unnoticed.

title: match_count increment is a read-modify-write race
body: `should_block?` loads the record, computes `record.match_count += 1` in Ruby and then saves. Two concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked address will both read the same `match_count` and write the same value back, so matches are silently lost. Use an atomic update (e.g. `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')` or `increment!`) instead of a full object save.

title: Validation has a DB side effect, so match statistics are double-counted
body: `validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which writes to the database (increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`). Validation is not idempotent and is run multiple times per request: `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` (line 168) and then `user.save` (line 172), each of which runs the email validator, so a single signup attempt bumps `match_count` twice. Any other code that calls `valid?` on a user will also inflate the counters. The statistics gathering should be moved out of the validator (or made explicitly once-per-attempt).

title: Blocked-email lookup is case sensitive and not normalized
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` compares the raw value passed in by the validator against the stored string. Email local parts/domains are commonly entered with different casing (e.g. `Block@SpamFromHome.org`), and the `users.email` column is not guaranteed to be downcased at validation time, so a blocked address can be bypassed just by changing capitalization. Normalize (downcase/strip) both on write and on lookup, or compare with `lower(email)`.

title: Failed save of match statistics is silently swallowed
body: `record.save` is used without checking the return value. Because the model also runs presence/uniqueness validations on save, a failure (or a validation error introduced later) silently discards the `match_count`/`last_match_at` update with no log, making the statistics quietly unreliable.

title: Mutable array declared on the controller class is shared between instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` puts a single array on the class prototype; `pushObject` in `createAccount` mutates that shared array. Any second instance of `CreateAccountController` (or the same instance reused across modal open/close) sees another instance's rejected emails, and the state is never reset. Initialize it per instance (e.g. in `init`) instead of as a class-level literal.

title: Server-side email error reason is replaced by generic "invalid" message
body: When the server rejects an email (blocked address, domain not allowed, already taken, …) the controller pushes the value into `rejectedEmails` and the validation then shows `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')`. The specific reason returned in `result.errors.email` (including the new `user.email.blocked` string added to server.en.yml) is discarded, so users get a misleading "Email is invalid" message for an address that is syntactically valid. Use the server-supplied error text keyed by email instead of a generic constant.

title: No coverage for the whitelist/blacklist logic moved into EmailValidator
body: The `email_domains_whitelist` / `email_domains_blacklist` behaviour was removed from `User#email_validator` and re-implemented here (including the `elsif` precedence and the `errors[attribute].blank?` short-circuit that skips the blocked-email check). The new spec only exercises the blocked-email branch, so the relocated domain restriction code and the interaction between the two branches are untested after the refactor.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case sensitive, trivially bypassed
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` does an exact match (`where(email: email).first`) against the value supplied by the signup form. Email addresses are not normalized/downcased before User validation (`User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` verbatim and there is no downcasing callback), so a user whose address `bad@spamclub.com` is blocked can sign up with `Bad@Spamclub.com` and pass validation. The stored block rows are also inserted verbatim, so a mixed-case row would never match a lowercase signup. The lookup should normalize both sides (e.g. `Email.downcase`) and the column/index should store normalized values.

title: Validator performs DB writes, so match statistics are double-counted
body: `validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which mutates and saves the BlockedEmail row (increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`). Because this happens inside validation, every call to `valid?`/`save` writes. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, so a single signup attempt runs the validation twice and inflates `match_count` by 2; any other code path that validates a user with a changed email also silently bumps the counter. Side-effect-free validation plus an explicit statistics update (or an idempotent guard) is needed, otherwise the match statistics are unreliable.

title: Non-atomic increment of match_count loses updates
body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` is a read-modify-write across two statements. Concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked address (the common case for spam waves) will read the same value and overwrite each other, so `match_count` under-reports. Use an atomic update (`increment!`/`update_all("match_count = match_count + 1")`). Additionally `record.save` re-runs the uniqueness validation (extra query) and silently returns false if the record is invalid, so a failed statistics update goes unnoticed.

title: action_type is NOT NULL with no database default
body: `action_type` is declared `null: false` but has no default; the only default comes from the model's `before_validation :set_defaults`. Any insert that bypasses the model (bulk import of blocked addresses via SQL/COPY, which the spec comments explicitly anticipate, or `insert_all`-style code) will fail with a not-null violation. Add `default: 0` (block) to the column so the DB and model agree.

title: rejectedEmails array is defined on the prototype and shared across instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` creates a single array on the class prototype; every instance of CreateAccountController mutates the same array via `pushObject`. If the controller is ever instantiated more than once (or the app is reset in tests), rejected emails leak between instances and are never cleared, so a previously rejected address stays permanently marked invalid for the page lifetime. Initialize it per-instance in `init` (or reset it when the modal is shown).

title: `<%- end if %>` is a Ruby syntax error, breaking the main embed view
body: The header block is closed with `<%- end if %>`. The ERB compiler emits the literal Ruby `end if`, which closes the `if`/`else` and then starts a *new*, never-closed `if` statement (Ruby allows a newline between `if` and its condition, so the following buffer append becomes the condition). The template therefore raises a SyntaxError (`unexpected end-of-input`) whenever it is compiled, so `GET /embed/best` will 500 for every topic that already has an embed. It should simply be `<%- end %>`. Note the specs never render this template with posts present (TopicView is mocked), so the failure is not caught by tests.

title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript (XSS)
body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` injects the raw Referer header into a single-quoted JS string literal with no escaping. Only the *host* part of the referer is validated in EmbedController#ensure_embeddable; the path and query are arbitrary, so a URL on the embeddable host such as `http://host/page?x='+alert(document.cookie)+'` (or one containing `</script>`) breaks out of the string and executes attacker-controlled script in the context of the Discourse origin, with the visitor's session. Escape it, e.g. `<%= j request.referer %>` / `json_escape`, and preferably send only the origin (scheme://host:port) rather than the full URL.

title: raw_html cook method stores unsanitized remote HTML as `cooked` (stored XSS)
body: `cook` now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == raw_html`, bypassing PrettyText/sanitization entirely. TopicEmbed.import creates posts with this cook method from content fetched from a third party (Jobs::PollFeed passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` straight through with no tag/attribute filtering), and the embed view and normal topic view render `cooked` with `raw`. A hostile or compromised feed can therefore inject `<script>`, `onerror=`, iframes, etc. into forum pages for all users. The HTML needs to be run through a sanitizer (e.g. Sanitize with a whitelist, as ruby-readability does for the import_remote path) before being stored as cooked.

title: `i.content.scrub` breaks for RSS feeds and on Ruby < 2.1
body: The job claims to support "RSS or ATOM", but SimpleRSS only exposes `content` for Atom `<content>` / `content:encoded`; a plain RSS 2.0 item only has `description`. For such feeds `i.content` is nil and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, and because the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` the import silently never happens. Additionally `String#scrub` only exists in Ruby >= 2.1, so on Ruby 2.0 (still supported per the Gemfile/platform notes) even Atom feeds raise NoMethodError. Fall back to `i.description`/`content_encoded` and guard the encoding scrub.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching and can be bypassed
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any origin that is a *substring* of the configured Discourse URL rather than comparing the actual origin. For example with `discourseUrl = 'http://evil.com.discourse.example.com/'` the origin `http://evil.com` passes the test, letting a third-party frame drive the resize handler. Compare against a precomputed origin with strict equality instead (and note the message payload is otherwise trusted).

title: Update path crashes when the embedded post no longer exists
body: In the `else` branch, `post = embed.post` is passed straight to `PostRevisor.new(post)`. If the original post (or its topic) was deleted/trashed, `embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor#revise!` immediately raises NoMethodError on `@post.raw`, so the poll_feed job (retry: false) or the embed retrieval job dies for that URL and the embed stays permanently broken. Guard for a missing post and either recreate the topic or skip the row.

title: `contents <<` mutates the caller's string argument
body: `contents << "\n<hr>\n<small>..."` appends in place to the string the caller passed in. Any caller that reuses or caches that string (or passes a frozen/literal string, which raises RuntimeError: can't modify frozen String) is affected, and the mutation is invisible from the call site. Build a new string instead (`contents = contents + ...`).

title: Adding `force: true` to an already-shipped migration can drop a populated table
body: This migration already exists in the repository history, so installs have run it. Changing `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` means that anyone who re-runs it (rebuilt schema_migrations, re-run of the migration during a repair/rollback, or a fresh checkout on an existing database) will silently `DROP TABLE top_topics` and lose its contents instead of failing loudly. Edits to released migrations should not introduce destructive `force: true`; put schema changes in a new migration.

title: New `embed` CSS/JS assets are not added to the precompile list
body: The layout references `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` and the new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` is a standalone file, but neither is required from an existing manifest (application.js / application.css) nor added to `config.assets.precompile` in config/application.rb. With `config.assets.compile = false` in production this raises `Sprockets::Rails::Helper::AssetNotPrecompiled` (or serves a 404 for embed.js), so the embed page is unusable in production even though it works in development.

title: Kernel#open on a site-setting URL allows command execution and SSRF
body: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open`, which executes a shell command when the argument starts with `|` (e.g. `|curl evil.com`) and will happily fetch internal addresses (127.0.0.1, link-local metadata endpoints). The setting is admin-controlled, which limits exposure, but it is a needless escalation from "change a site setting" to "run code as the sidekiq user". Use `URI.parse(...).open` / an HTTP client and validate the scheme/host.

title: Loading placeholder is cached for longer than its own reload interval
body: `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied to both branches, including the `loading` template, whose inline script reloads the page after 30 seconds. The reload will usually be served from cache, showing the placeholder again without re-checking for the imported topic, so the user waits at least twice as long as intended. Skip the cache headers (or use a much shorter TTL) on the loading response.

title: `<%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby and will raise a SyntaxError when the view renders
body: The closing tag of the if/else block is written as `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. The compiled template becomes `... end if <buffer append>`, i.e. the stray `if` starts a new, never-closed conditional, so rendering `embed#best` raises a SyntaxError and every embed request for an already-imported topic returns a 500. Controller specs don't render views, so this is not caught by the added tests.

title: Unescaped `request.referer` interpolated into inline JavaScript (reflected XSS)
body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` injects the raw Referer header into a single-quoted JS string. `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` only validates the *host* of the referer, so an attacker-controlled path/query such as `http://<embeddable_host>/x'+alert(document.cookie)+'` passes validation and breaks out of the string literal, executing arbitrary JS in the Discourse origin. Use `escape_javascript`/`j` and preferably pass only the scheme+host origin (which is all postMessage uses anyway).

title: raw_html cook method stores unsanitized remote HTML as `cooked`
body: `cook` returns `raw` verbatim for `cook_method == :raw_html`, bypassing the markdown/sanitization pipeline and the `after_post_cook` plugin filters. `Jobs::PollFeed` feeds `i.content` from an arbitrary remote RSS/Atom feed straight into `TopicEmbed.import` with this cook method, so anything the feed publisher puts in the item body (`<script>`, event handlers, iframes) is rendered verbatim to every forum visitor — a stored XSS vector. Feed/imported HTML should be run through the existing sanitizer (as `import_remote` does with its tag/attribute whitelist) before being stored as cooked.

title: Feed items without `content` raise NoMethodError and abort the whole poll
body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every item exposes `content`. Many RSS 2.0 feeds only provide `description` (SimpleRSS returns nil for `content`), so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError. Because the items are processed in a single `each` loop with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, one such item aborts the entire polling run and all remaining items are silently skipped. Fall back to `description`/`summary` and wrap per-item processing so one bad item cannot kill the job.

title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
body: The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. Those are rewritten to `http://embedhost//cdn.example.com/img.png` (the `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips the leading slashes), producing broken links and broken images for any feed that uses protocol-relative references. Exclude hrefs/srcs starting with `//` before prefixing.

title: Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE can permanently block retrieval of a URL
body: `$redis.setnx(key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(key, 60)` is not atomic. If the process dies or the Redis connection fails between the two calls, the throttle key exists with no TTL and `retrieved_recently?` returns true forever, so that embed URL can never be imported again (the embed page will loop on the loading template indefinitely). Use `SET key 1 EX 60 NX` (or `setex` guarded by existence) instead.

title: `force: true` added to an already-released migration can drop an existing table
body: This migration was already shipped; editing it to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` means that on any database where the migration is re-run (re-seeded schema, repaired schema_migrations, `db:migrate:redo`) the existing `top_topics` table is dropped along with its data instead of failing loudly. The change is also unrelated to the embedding feature in this PR and should be reverted.

title: No test renders the embed views; assertions hidden in an `after` hook
body: The specs never render the views (controller specs don't by default), which is why the syntax error in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` (`<%- end if %>`) goes undetected — the only new user-facing templates are completely untested. Additionally, `response.should be_success` and the X-Frame-Options assertion live in an `after` block: hook failures are reported detached from the example and run even when the example already failed, making diagnosis hard. Add a `render_views` request/controller spec for `embed#best` (both the loading and the topic-found paths).

title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any origin that happens to be a substring of the configured Discourse URL. For `discourseUrl = "http://forum.example.com/"`, an attacker-controlled frame on `http://forum.example.co` passes the check. Compare the origin for exact equality against the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` instead, and ignore messages whose `source` is not the created iframe.

title: Kernel#open used with externally supplied URLs (SSRF / command execution)
body: `open(url).read` in `import_remote` and `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `Jobs::PollFeed` use `Kernel#open`, which executes a shell command when the argument starts with `|` and happily fetches `file://` and internal addresses. The feed URL is a per-site setting (a site admin on a multisite install should not be able to run commands on the host), and `import_remote` is also invoked from the Disqus importer with URLs taken from the dump. Use `URI.parse(...).open`/`Net::HTTP` restricted to http(s), with a timeout.

title: Existing embed with a deleted post crashes the import
body: When a `TopicEmbed` row already exists, `post = embed.post` can be nil (post hard-deleted or the association pointing at a missing row). The code then calls `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!`, raising NoMethodError inside the retrieval job/feed poll. Guard on `post.blank?` and either recreate the topic or skip.

title: `import` mutates the caller's `contents` string
body: `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends in place to the argument supplied by the caller rather than building a new string. Callers that reuse or cache the content (and any frozen string passed in, which would raise) get surprising behaviour, and repeated calls with the same object accumulate multiple "Imported from" footers. Use `contents + ...` / `dup` instead.

title: `feed_key` is dead code
body: `feed_key` builds a `feed-modified:` Redis key but nothing in the class (or anywhere else in the PR) reads or writes it, so there is no conditional-GET/If-Modified-Since handling as the name implies. Either implement the caching it was intended for or remove the method so future readers don't assume polling is throttled.

title: Loading page is cached for 1 minute while the page reloads every 30 seconds
body: `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied to both branches, including the `loading` template, whose inline script reloads after 30s. The browser/proxy will serve the cached loading page for the first reload, so the user waits at least a minute even when the topic was imported quickly. Skip caching (or use a much shorter max-age) on the loading response.

title: "ALLOWALL" is not a valid X-Frame-Options value
body: `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` sets a non-standard token. Browsers that don't recognise it are entitled to fall back to denying framing, which would break embedding entirely. The reliable way to permit framing is to delete the header (`response.headers.delete('X-Frame-Options')`), optionally alongside a CSP `frame-ancestors` entry for the embeddable host.

title: embed_url limited to 255 characters with a unique index
body: `t.string :embed_url` creates a varchar(255). Article URLs with query strings/UTM parameters routinely exceed 255 characters, so those imports will fail with a value-too-long error (and the unique index on the column limits how long an indexable value can be). Consider `t.text` with an index on a hash/prefix, or document the limit and truncate/normalise the URL before insert.

title: raw_html cook method stores and renders unsanitized remote HTML
body: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so posts created by `TopicEmbed.import` keep whatever HTML came from the remote source as their `cooked` value. The RSS path (`Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` -> `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`) passes the feed body through with no tag/attribute whitelist at all (only `import_remote` filters tags via ruby-readability), and the resulting `cooked` is emitted with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb as well as in normal topic rendering. A hostile or compromised feed (or an XSS-laden page scraped from the embeddable host) can therefore inject `<script>`/`onerror` payloads that execute for every visitor of the forum. The imported HTML should be run through the existing sanitizer (e.g. Sanitize with a whitelist) before being stored as cooked.

title: Stray `if` in `<%- end if %>` breaks template compilation/output order
body: Line 6 is `<%- end if %>`, which compiles to the Ruby fragment `end if` with no condition. Ruby then continues the modifier-`if` onto the next generated statement, so the logo `link_to` on line 8 becomes the *condition* of the conditional block: the logo is appended to the buffer before the button, and the whole if/else is executed only if that append returns truthy. Depending on the ERB engine this is either a SyntaxError (500 on every embed request) or silently wrong markup ordering. The `if` is a typo and should be removed, leaving `<%- end %>`.

title: `post.present?` does not detect a failed PostCreator run
body: `PostCreator#create` returns the (unsaved) Post object even when creation fails — it raises `ActiveRecord::Rollback` internally, which is swallowed, and the returned post has errors and a nil `id`/`topic_id`. `post.present?` is therefore true for failed creations, and the following `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: nil, post_id: nil, ...)` blows up with a NOT NULL/validation error, masking the real failure (e.g. a title that is too long or a rate limit). Check `post.persisted?` (or `post.errors.blank?`) instead, and bail out gracefully otherwise.

title: `open(url)` used without requiring 'open-uri'
body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` but topic_embed.rb only requires 'nokogiri'. `open-uri` is only required in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, which is not loaded on the `retrieve_topic` -> `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` path (that path only requires 'topic_retriever'/'topic_embed') unless feed polling happens to be enabled. Without open-uri loaded, `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a file name and raises `Errno::ENOENT`, so on-demand embed retrieval (and the disqus thor task) fails. Add `require 'open-uri'` to this file.

title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
body: The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. After the substitution `src.sub(/^\/+/, '')` the result becomes `http://host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, i.e. a broken link/image for any feed that uses protocol-relative references (common for CDN-hosted assets). Protocol-relative URLs should be left alone or prefixed with the scheme only.

title: Existing embed with a deleted post raises NoMethodError
body: In the update branch `post = embed.post` can be nil (post hard-deleted, or a previous import that stored a bogus post_id). `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then fails with a NoMethodError inside a Sidekiq job, and the embed row is never repaired. Guard for a missing post and either recreate the topic or skip.

title: `i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds, aborting the whole poll
body: SimpleRSS exposes RSS 2.0 item bodies as `description` (and `content_encoded` for content:encoded); `item.content` is only populated for Atom feeds. For a plain RSS 2.0 feed `i.content` is nil and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError. Because the job is declared `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the exception kills the entire poll and no items are ever imported; the same exception on a single malformed item also aborts the remaining items in the loop. Fall back to `i.description`/`i.content_encoded` and skip (rather than abort on) items with no body.

title: Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE can permanently block retrieval of a URL
body: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` is not atomic. If the process dies, the Redis connection fails, or the job is killed between the two calls, the key stays forever with no TTL, so `retrieved_recently?` returns true for that embed_url for the rest of the Redis instance's life and that page's discussion can never be retrieved (the embed iframe is stuck on the loading page). Use `$redis.set(key, "1", nx: true, ex: 60)` (or SETEX) instead.

title: Full feed poll executed inline during embed retrieval
body: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs the complete RSS/Atom poll synchronously (HTTP fetch of the feed plus creation/revision of a topic for every item) inside the `retrieve_topic` job each time an unknown embed_url is requested and feed polling is enabled. One cold embed view can therefore trigger a multi-second-to-minute import, and many concurrent unknown URLs will import the feed repeatedly in parallel (no locking), duplicating work and hammering the feed source. Enqueue the poll instead, or guard it with the same throttle used for HTTP retrieval.

title: `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid header value
body: `ALLOWALL` is not a defined X-Frame-Options directive. Per the HTML spec/most current browsers an unrecognized value is treated as `DENY` (some older browsers ignored it), so setting this can actively prevent the page from being framed — exactly the opposite of the intent — and makes embedding fail on the browsers that follow the spec. To allow framing, delete the header that the default Rails/Discourse middleware set (`response.headers.delete('X-Frame-Options')`) and, if restriction is wanted, use a CSP `frame-ancestors` directive with the embeddable host.

title: Loading page is cached for 1 minute but reloads itself after 30 seconds
body: `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied to both branches, including the `render 'loading'` branch. The loading template reloads the iframe after 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), so the reload is served from the browser cache and shows the same "Loading Discussion..." page even after the topic has been retrieved; the user waits at least two cycles. Either skip caching (or use a much shorter max-age) when rendering the loading page, or make the reload cache-busting.

title: Spec stubs TopicView.new to return nil, so the rendered template raises
body: `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` has no `returns`, so `@topic_view` is nil. The default `best` template then evaluates `@topic_view.posts.present?`, raising NoMethodError on nil during render, which makes the example (and the assertions in the `after` block) fail rather than verify the success path. The mock needs to return a double exposing `posts`/`topic`, or the spec should use `render_views false` with an explicit template stub.

title: `force: true` added to an already-released migration can drop a populated table
body: Editing the existing CreateTopTopics migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` means that any environment which re-runs this migration (schema reload, `db:migrate:redo`, re-running from a reset schema_migrations) will silently `DROP TABLE top_topics` and all its rows instead of failing loudly. The same pattern is used in the new 20131217174004_create_topic_embeds migration. `force: true` has no benefit in a forward migration and should be removed.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any origin that is a substring of the configured `discourseUrl` rather than comparing origins for equality (and would also accept a message whose origin happens to be a prefix such as `http://discourse.example.co`). It also throws if `discourseUrl` is undefined. Compare `e.origin` against the origin parsed out of `discourseUrl` exactly.

title: request.referer interpolated into a JS string with HTML escaping
body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` applies HTML escaping inside a `<script>` block, where entities are not decoded. A referer containing `'` produces the literal `'` in the JS string (wrong targetOrigin), and a referer ending in a backslash escapes the closing quote, producing a JavaScript syntax error that kills the resize script. Use `escape_javascript` (`j`) and, better, pass only the scheme+host of the referer since postMessage expects an origin, not a full URL.

title: Disqus import loses created_at and the --category option
body: The thread import was switched to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which drops the previous `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, so imported topics are now dated at import time instead of the original Disqus thread date, and the removed `--category` option means imported topics can no longer be placed in a category. If these behaviours are intentionally dropped, the option removal should at least be reflected in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (accepting `created_at`/`category`) so existing import workflows are not silently degraded.

title: `float: right` on button is ignored now that `.small-action` is a flex container
body: `.small-action` now sets `display: flex` (via `@include flexbox()` at line 264), which makes `float` a no-op on its children. The `button { float: right; }` rule inside `.small-action` therefore no longer pushes the action button to the right edge; it will be laid out inline right after `.small-action-desc`. The same applies to `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` (line 270), which is now dead. To keep the button right-aligned the desc should get `flex: 1` (or the button `margin-left: auto`) instead of relying on floats.

title: Percentage padding on a flex item replaces the fixed offset that cleared the avatar
body: `.small-action-desc` padding changed from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`. The old left padding of 4em reserved space for the floated 45px avatar; the new value is a percentage of the flex container's width, so on narrow containers the gap between avatar and text collapses to a couple of pixels, and on wide ones it grows arbitrarily. A fixed-length padding/margin (or `flex` sizing) would give stable spacing.

title: align-items mixin emits legacy properties that reject modern values and omits -moz-box-align
body: `@mixin align-items($alignment)` forwards the standard value verbatim to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, but those legacy specs only accept `start|end|center|baseline|stretch`. Any future call such as `@include align-items(flex-start)` will emit invalid declarations for the old box model / IE10, silently falling back to the default alignment. It also emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a real property, while omitting `-moz-box-align` even though `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box` for old Gecko — so in exactly the engine the prefix was added for, alignment is never applied. Either map the values (`flex-start` -> `start`, etc.) or drop the legacy prefixes.

title: order mixin does not translate to the 1-based legacy box-ordinal-group
body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based (minimum value 1, default 1), whereas standard `order` is 0-based (default 0). Passing the same number to both means `@include order(0)` produces an invalid ordinal group, and siblings without an explicit order default to group 1 in the legacy model but 0 in the standard one, so the relative ordering can differ between old prefixed engines and modern ones. The mixin should offset the legacy value (e.g. `$val + 1`) or omit the legacy box prefixes.

title: Header panel right-alignment has no fallback for the legacy box model the mixin claims to support
body: `.panel` lost `float: right` and now relies on `margin-left: auto` inside the flex `.contents`. Auto margins are not honoured by the old `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` model that `flexbox()` explicitly emits, so in those engines the panel (user menu, search, hamburger icons) will sit immediately after the title instead of at the right edge, with no float fallback remaining. Either drop the legacy `display` prefixes or keep a fallback alignment.

title: `.valign-helper` rule is dead code after the flex conversion
body: `.valign-helper` relies on `height: 100%` plus `vertical-align: middle` to vertically centre header content. Now that `.contents` is a flex container with `align-items: center`, `vertical-align` has no effect on its children and `height: 100%` resolves against an auto-height flex line, so this rule no longer does anything and should be removed to avoid confusion.

title: `float: right` on .small-action button no longer works now that .small-action is a flex container
body: `.small-action` was turned into a flex container (`@include flexbox()` at line 264), which makes `float` a no-op on all of its direct children. The `button { ... float: right; }` rule at line 306-310 (used for the small-action action buttons, e.g. undo/delete) will therefore no longer be pushed to the right edge; it will sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` in normal flex order. The same applies to `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` (line 270), which is now dead code. To keep the button right-aligned, use `margin-left: auto` on the button (or `flex: 1` on `.small-action-desc`) instead of a float.

title: order() mixin maps modern `order` values directly onto 1-based legacy ordinal-group properties
body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group` (old 2009 flexbox spec) are 1-based and default to 1, while the modern `order` property is 0-based and defaults to 0. Emitting the same raw `$val` for both means legacy WebKit/Gecko engines see an ordering that is shifted by one relative to modern engines, and `@include order(0)` would emit the invalid `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 0`. If the legacy prefixes are intended to work, the mixin should emit `$val + 1` for the ordinal-group properties.

title: align-items() mixin is inconsistent with flexbox() and will emit invalid legacy values for flex-start/flex-end/stretch
body: `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box` for legacy Gecko, but `align-items()` has no `-moz-box-align`, so legacy Gecko gets the old box display with no alignment. Additionally, `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` only accept the old keywords (`start`, `end`, `center`, `baseline`, `stretch`); calling `@include align-items(flex-start)` or `align-items(flex-end)` — the normal modern values — would produce invalid legacy declarations that are silently dropped, making the prefixed fallbacks useless for those values. Either translate the values inside the mixin or drop the legacy prefixes.

title: Header .panel right-alignment relies on `margin-left: auto`, unsupported by the legacy box fallbacks added in the same PR
body: `.panel` lost `float: right` and now relies on `margin-left: auto` plus `order: 3` to be pushed to the right of `.contents`. Auto margins for free-space distribution are a modern flexbox feature; in the legacy `-webkit-box` / `-moz-box` modes that `flexbox()` deliberately emits as fallbacks, `margin-left: auto` does not consume free space, so in those engines the header panel (user/notifications/search icons) will no longer be right-aligned — it will sit directly after the title. If those fallbacks are meant to be functional, use `-webkit-box-flex`/spacer handling or drop the legacy display values.

title: Percentage padding on .small-action-desc makes text indentation viewport-dependent
body: `.small-action-desc` changed from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `padding: 0 1.5%`. Percentage padding resolves against the containing block's width, so the horizontal inset now varies with the topic/viewport width instead of being a fixed, font-relative amount; combined with the fact that `.small-action-desc` is a flex item with no `flex` value (so it only takes its content width), the text position and wrapping of small-action messages will be inconsistent across widths. A fixed em/px padding plus `flex: 1` would be more predictable.

title: `float: right` on small-action button no longer works now that `.small-action` is a flex container
body: `.small-action` was turned into a flex container (`@include flexbox()` at line 264). Float is ignored on flex items, so the `button { float: right; }` rule at line 309 has no effect anymore and the action button (e.g. undo/delete on small post actions) will sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of being pushed to the right edge. To keep the previous layout the button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the container needs `justify-content: space-between`). The same applies to `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` (line 270), which is now dead.

title: Right-alignment of header `.panel` breaks in browsers that only support the legacy box model
body: `.contents` is now laid out with the `flexbox()` mixin, which also emits the legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` fallbacks. Those old box-model implementations do not honour `margin-left: auto` for pushing an item to the end of the line, and the previous `float: right` on `.panel` (plus `float: left` on `.title`) was removed in this diff. In any engine that falls back to `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` (old Android/iOS WebKit, Firefox < 22) the header panel with the user icons/search will be rendered left-aligned next to the title instead of right-aligned, i.e. a visibly broken header. Either keep a float fallback or drop the legacy `box` fallbacks from the mixin.

title: `align-items` mixin emits legacy properties that reject the modern keyword values
body: The mixin blindly maps the argument onto `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy properties accept `start`/`end`/`center`/`baseline`/`stretch`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`. So `@include align-items(flex-start)` silently produces invalid legacy declarations and the legacy-only engines fall back to the default `stretch`, producing a different layout than intended. Also `-ms-align-items` is not a real property (IE10 uses only `-ms-flex-align`), and `-moz-box-align` is missing even though `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box`, so Firefox's legacy box path gets no alignment at all.

title: `order` mixin mixes 1-based legacy ordinal groups with 0-based `order`
body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based (default 1) while the standard `order` property is 0-based (default 0), and `box-ordinal-group: 0` is invalid. As a result `@include order(0)` emits an invalid legacy declaration, and `@include order(1)` makes the element tie with siblings that have no order set in legacy engines, while in modern engines it is placed after them. Any mixin consumer therefore gets different sibling ordering depending on the engine; the legacy value should be `$val + 1`.

title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so the conditional never applies
body: ActiveModel::Serializers only honours conditional inclusion methods named `include_<attr>?`. The method is defined as `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never invoked and `website_name` is unconditionally serialized. Consequences: the key is emitted (with a `null` value) even when the user has no website, and, more importantly, the intended "only when a website exists" gate is dead code. Rename to `include_website_name?`.

title: website_name bypasses the untrusted_attributes restriction and leaks TL0 websites to anonymous users
body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), so for a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor it is withheld (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`). The new `website_name` attribute derives directly from `object.user_profile.website` but has no such guard (and its `include_website_name` helper is misnamed, see other finding), so the host — and the full path when the domain matches the instance domain — is serialized to anonymous visitors for restricted users. This re-opens the spam/privacy hole that hiding `website` was meant to close. Add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (or return nil when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`).

title: untrusted attribute spec not updated for website_name
body: The "with a TL0 user seen as anonymous" context asserts that bio/location/website etc. are absent, but `website_name` was not added to `untrusted_attributes`. Because the new attribute is derived from the website and is currently serialized unconditionally, this spec passes while the website information still leaks. Add `website_name` to the list so the regression is caught.

title: `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal and will raise under frozen_string_literal
body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses the destructive `<<` on a literal receiver. It works today only because the literal is re-allocated on each evaluation; if `# frozen_string_literal: true` is ever added to this file (common in this codebase) it raises `FrozenError` on every profile serialization. Use non-mutating concatenation, e.g. `".#{website_host}"`.

title: Hostname comparison is case-sensitive and path-only (query/fragment dropped, bare `/` shown)
body: `URI(...).host` preserves the case the user typed, so a profile website of `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` will not match `Discourse.current_hostname` (`example.com`) and the full path will not be shown; comparisons should downcase both hosts. Additionally `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` yields a trailing `example.com/` for root URLs and silently drops any query string, so the displayed text can differ from the actual link target.

title: Websites stored without a scheme now render no label at all
body: `URI('example.com/user').host` is nil, so `website_name` returns nil and the template's `{{#if model.website_name}}` hides the link entirely. The previous client-side implementation (`website.split('/')[2]`) also mis-handled such values, but it at least produced a truthy string in some cases; now a stored scheme-less website makes the globe/link disappear from the profile. Consider falling back to the raw website string (or normalizing by prefixing `http://`) when no host can be parsed.

title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so it is never used
body: ActiveModel::Serializers only consults predicate methods named `include_<attribute>?`. The method is defined as `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is dead code and `website_name` is unconditionally serialized — e.g. it is emitted as `"website_name": null` for every user with no website, and, more importantly, it bypasses the intended guard entirely. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (and ideally base it on `website_name.present?`).

title: `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking TL0 websites to anonymous users
body: `:website` is declared in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109) so that a trust-level-0 user's website is hidden from anonymous visitors (anti-spam / SEO protection). The new `:website_name` attribute was added to `attributes` but not to `untrusted_attributes` and has no working inclusion guard, so the host (and now even the full path) of a TL0 user's website is serialized for anonymous requests, and `user.hbs` renders it (`{{#if model.website_name}}`). This re-exposes exactly the spam vector the untrusted_attributes list exists to block. Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list.

title: TL0/anonymous spec not updated for the new `website_name` attribute
body: The `untrusted_attributes` list in the 'TL0 user seen as anonymous' context still only contains `bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background`. The newly added `website_name` attribute is not asserted to be absent, which is why the regression that leaks a TL0 user's website host/path to anonymous visitors is not caught. Add `website_name` to that list (and a case asserting `website_name` is omitted when the profile website is blank).

title: `"" << website_host` mutates a string literal instead of concatenating
body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on the literal `"."`. It happens to work today because each evaluation allocates a fresh literal, but it will raise `FrozenError` the moment the file gets a `# frozen_string_literal: true` magic comment (or runs under `--enable-frozen-string-literal`), breaking user serialization site-wide. Use `"." + website_host` or `".#{website_host}"`.

title: Same-suffix heuristic treats unrelated hosts on shared domains as the same site
body: The second branch considers two hosts related whenever they have the same number of labels (>2) and match after dropping the first label. For shared hosting suffixes this is wrong: with an instance on `forum.github.io`, an arbitrary user website `spammer.github.io` is judged to belong to the same organisation and the full URL path is rendered instead of only the host. Since the whole purpose of showing only the host is to avoid displaying attacker-controlled path text, this heuristic should use a public-suffix check or be restricted to an exact/parent-domain match.

title: Only `path` is appended; query/fragment are dropped and `URI()` is re-parsed repeatedly
body: `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` drops any query string or fragment, so `http://example.com/u?id=1` is displayed as `example.com/u`, which does not match the href the user clicks. It also re-parses the URI on every branch (up to twice per call) outside the `rescue nil` guard of line 138. Parse once into a local variable and build the display string from `path`, `query` and `fragment`.

title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so it never guards the attribute
body: ActiveModel::Serializers only honours conditional methods named `include_<attr>?`. The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is dead code and `website_name` is unconditionally serialized — including as `null` for every user who has no website. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (and note that it then also needs to respect the untrusted-attribute rules, see the separate finding).

title: `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking a TL0 user's website to anonymous viewers
body: `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) deliberately hides `website` (among others) when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true — i.e. a trust-level-0 user's profile seen by an anonymous visitor — as a spam mitigation. The new `website_name` attribute is declared as a plain attribute and is therefore always serialized, exposing the host (and, for same-domain cases, the full path) of a TL0 user's website to anonymous visitors. The template renders `model.website_name` as the visible text, so the spam URL becomes visible again even though `model.website` is suppressed. Add `website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (or gate it on the same condition).

title: `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal in place
body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on the literal `"."`. It happens to work today because the literal is a fresh unfrozen object on each evaluation, but it will raise `FrozenError` the moment `# frozen_string_literal: true` is added to this file (or the global frozen-literal option is enabled). Use `"." + website_host` or `".#{website_host}"`.

title: Host comparison is case-sensitive, so mixed-case websites fall through to the host-only branch
body: `URI("http://Example.com/user").host` returns `"Example.com"` with the original casing, while `Discourse.current_hostname` is normally lowercase. The equality check on line 141 and the sibling-subdomain comparison on line 146 therefore fail for a user who typed their own domain with capitals, and the full path is not shown even though the domains match.
