Downcase both hosts before comparing.

title: Only `URI#path` is appended, dropping query and fragment from the displayed URL
body: For same-domain websites the display string is `host + URI(...).path`, which silently discards any query string or fragment (e.g. `http://example.com/u?id=1` is shown as `example.com/u`). Since the whole point of this change is to show the complete URL when the domain matches the instance domain, the link text can now differ from the actual `href`. Consider using the request-URI (path + query) or the full URL minus the scheme.

title: No test coverage for the sibling-subdomain branch, for non-parsable websites, or for the TL0/anonymous case
body: The three new examples only cover the `==` branch and the `ends_with?` branch. Uncovered behaviours that the implementation makes non-trivial claims about: (1) the `elsif` sibling-subdomain branch (`www.example.com` website with a `forum.example.com` instance) which the inline comment advertises; (2) a website stored without a scheme or otherwise unparsable, where `URI(...).host` is nil and `website_name` becomes nil so the website disappears from the profile entirely; (3) the "TL0 user seen as anonymous" context at the top of this file, which asserts `website` is hidden but does not assert anything about `website_name` — exactly the attribute that currently leaks.

title: Light-theme color for embedded-post author link changed from 30% to 70% lightness
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so the light-theme value silently jumped from 30% to 70% lightness. Since `dark-light-choose`'s first argument is the light-theme value, the author name in expanded reply/in-reply-to blocks becomes a very washed-out grey on light themes (a visible contrast regression), whereas every other conversion in this PR keeps the light value and only adds the complementary dark value. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: `.custom-message-length` light-theme lightness inverted (70% -> 30%)
body: The previous value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`; the change produces `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, i.e. the light-theme value was changed from 70% to 30%, making this hint text much darker than before on light themes and inconsistent with the desktop counterpart (`desktop/modal.scss` line 94 uses 70% / 30%). The two arguments look like they were swapped; it should read `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

title: `.topic-map h3` light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
body: The topic-map heading was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme color is therefore 30 percentage points lighter than before, so the mobile topic-map heading loses contrast and no longer matches the desktop rule (`desktop/topic-post.scss` line 321 keeps 20% / 80%). The intended conversion is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

title: `.group-member-info .name` light-theme color lightened from 30% to 50%
body: The rule previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` for the member name while the sibling `.title` used 50%, giving the name visually stronger emphasis. The change sets the name to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, so on light themes the name is now the same washed-out grey as the title and the intended hierarchy is lost. Only the dark variant should have been added: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: `.group-member-info .name` light-theme color lightened from 30% to 50% (mobile)
body: Same regression as in the desktop stylesheet: the member name was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and now resolves to 50% lightness on light themes, making it identical to the adjacent `.title` (50%) and removing the emphasis difference. The light-theme argument of `dark-light-choose` should stay at 30%, with 70% used for the dark variant.

title: Stale comment referencing the old topic-list default color
body: The comment "the default for table cells in topic list is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)" no longer matches the code: `common/base/_topic-list.scss` now sets table cells with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. Leaving the old expression documented here is misleading for anyone later adjusting the coldmap colors for dark schemes.

title: Light-theme color for embedded post author link changed from 30% to 70% lightness
body: `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` previously resolved to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so on light themes the author link is now scaled 70% toward white instead of 30%. Every other conversion in this PR preserves the original light value and uses its complement for the dark branch (e.g. 30%/70%). This silently reduces contrast of the author name in embedded/in-reply-to expansions on all existing light themes; the arguments appear to be swapped and should be `(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Mobile topic-map h3 light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 20% to 50% lightness, noticeably washing out the topic-map heading on mobile light themes, and it no longer matches the desktop rule which keeps 20%/80% (`desktop/topic-post.scss` line 321). The light branch should stay at 20% with an 80% dark complement.

title: mobile .custom-message-length light/dark arguments are inverted
body: `.custom-message-length` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and becomes `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme value flipped from 70% to 30%, making the hint text much darker than before on mobile light themes, and it contradicts the desktop rule for the same class (`desktop/modal.scss` line 94) which uses 70%/30%. The arguments look swapped.

title: group-member-info .name light value changed from 30% to 50%
body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 30% to 50%, so the member name becomes lighter/lower-contrast than before and now renders identically to the adjacent `.title` (previously the name was intentionally darker than the title). Preserve 30% for the light branch with a 70% dark complement.

title: mobile group-member-info .name light value changed from 30% to 50%
body: Same regression as the desktop file: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme rendering changes (lighter text, no longer distinguishable from `.title` just below it, which uses the same 50%/50% pair). The light branch should remain 30%.

title: #file-uploading color left as scale-color($secondary) and is invisible on light themes
body: `#reply-control #file-uploading { color: scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%); }` was not converted. On a light theme `$secondary` is the (near-white) background color, so scaling it 50% toward white yields text that is effectively invisible against the composer background. Since this PR is specifically normalizing `scale-color()` usages for dark/light themes, this one should also become a `dark-light-choose(...)` pair based on `$primary` for light themes.

title: Comment still documents the old scale-color($primary) default
body: The comment above the coldmap rules states "the default for table cells in topic list is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)", but the topic-list cell color was changed in this PR (`common/base/_topic-list.scss`) to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The comment is now misleading for anyone tuning these heat/cold map colors.

title: Light-theme value for embedded-post username changed from 30% to 70% lightness
body: `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The conversion wrote `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, i.e. the light-theme branch was changed from 30% to 70%. On a normal light scheme the bolded username in expanded/in-reply-to posts goes from a dark gray to a very light gray on a white background, badly reducing contrast/readability. title: Topic-map heading light-theme color changed from 20% to 50% lightness
body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value jumps from 20% to 50%, so on mobile the topic-map heading becomes noticeably lighter than before and no longer matches the desktop rule (which keeps 20%/80%). title: custom-message-length light-theme lightness inverted (70% -> 30%)
body: `.custom-message-length` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The two arguments look swapped: the light-theme value went from 70% to 30%, making the hint text much darker on mobile, and it no longer matches `desktop/modal.scss` which uses 70%/30%. Use 70% for light and 30% for dark.

title: group-member-info .name light value changed 30% -> 50%, now identical to .title
body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`. Besides lightening the name in light themes, it makes `.name` and `.title` exactly the same color, removing the intended visual distinction between the member name and their title. The light branch should remain 30% (with 70% for dark).

title: group-member-info .name light value changed 30% -> 50% (mobile)
body: Same regression as in `desktop/user.scss`: `.group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and now resolves to 50% in light themes, identical to the adjacent `.title` rule, so member name and title are no longer visually distinguishable and the name is lighter than before. Light branch should stay at 30%, dark branch 70%.

title: Missed conversion: category badge-notification still uses scale-color($primary)
body: Every other dim-text rule in this file was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, ...), scale-color($secondary, ...))`, but `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. On dark schemes `$primary` is light, so lightening it by 50% produces near-white text instead of the intended dimmed color, leaving this element inconsistent with the rest of the list after this PR.

title: #file-uploading uses lightened $secondary unconditionally
body: `#reply-control #file-uploading { color: scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%); }` lightens the background color for all schemes. In a light scheme `$secondary` is near-white, so the uploading text is nearly invisible against the composer background. Given the adjacent rules in this hunk were converted to `dark-light-choose(...)`, this one should be converted too (primary-based value for light, secondary-based for dark).

title: Stale comment referencing the old topic-list default color
body: The comment above the coldmap rules still says "the default for table cells in topic list is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)", but after this PR the topic-list cell color is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The comment now documents a value that no longer exists and will mislead anyone tuning these colors.

title: remove_member bypasses GroupUser callbacks and 404s for non-members
body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` on a `has_many :through` association deletes the join rows with `delete_all`, so no `GroupUser` callbacks run. Consequences: the cached `groups.user_count` column is never decremented (the admin UI shows a stale member count and pagination computed from it), and other per-membership side effects (clearing `primary_group`, notification-level/title cleanup) are skipped. Note the opposite path (`add_members` → `group.add(user)`) does create the join record through the model, so counts drift only on removal. Additionally, `CollectionProxy#delete` with an integer id calls `find` internally, so deleting a user that is not a member raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` (rendered as 404) instead of a graceful response. Use the model API (`group.remove(user)` / destroy the `GroupUser` record) instead.

title: Unvalidated limit/offset on public members endpoint
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to `.limit()/.offset()` with no clamping. An anonymous caller can request `?limit=1000000` and force the server to load and serialize the whole membership of a large group (cheap DoS), and `?limit=-1` or `?offset=-1` produces a negative LIMIT/OFFSET which PostgreSQL rejects, turning into a 500 error. Clamp limit to a sane maximum (e.g. 50..100) and floor offset at 0.

title: Breaking response-shape change for GET /groups/:name/members
body: The endpoint previously returned a bare JSON array of serialized users (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`); it now returns `{members: [...], meta: {...}}`. Any external API consumer, plugin or cached front-end asset that expects the array form will break with no versioning or deprecation path. If the change is intentional it should at least be called out in the PR/release notes and covered by a spec (none exists for this endpoint in this PR).

title: Public group member list is silently truncated to 50 with no pagination UI
body: Previously non-automatic groups returned all members (only automatic groups were limited, default 200). Now every request is limited to 50 by default, but the public group page template (`discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`) renders `members` with no next/previous controls, so a group with more than 50 members shows only the first 50 and users have no way to see the rest. Either add pagination to the public template or keep returning the full list there.

title: totalPages off-by-one produces an extra empty page
body: `totalPages` is computed in admin-group.js.es6 as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which over-counts whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100 members / 50 per page → 3 pages instead of 2). Combined with `next`, which clamps `offset` to `user_count` (`Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), the admin can page to an offset equal to the total and see an empty member list labelled e.g. "3/3". Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` and advance offset in whole pages.

title: update unconditionally resets `visible` when the param is absent
body: `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` runs on every update, so any PUT to /admin/groups/:id that omits `visible` (now a flat-param API, so partial updates are natural, e.g. sending only `alias_level`) silently makes the group invisible. Only assign when the parameter is present (`group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" if params.key?(:visible)`).

title: create silently drops alias_level
body: The client's `asJSON()` (discourse/models/group.js) sends `name`, `alias_level` and `visible` for both create and update, but `create` only reads `name` and `visible`. A group created with a non-default alias level in the admin UI is persisted with the default alias level, and the admin gets no indication the setting was ignored. Assign `alias_level` here as `update` does.

title: add_members raises on array usernames param and silently ignores unknown users
body: `usernames.split(",")` assumes a String; if a client posts `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` (a natural form for this parameter) `params.require(:usernames)` yields an Array and `split` raises NoMethodError → 500. Also, usernames that don't resolve to a user are skipped without any report, so the admin sees "success" while some members were not added. Accept both forms (`Array(usernames).flat_map { |u| u.split(",") }`) and return the list of names that could not be added.

title: addMembers/removeMember swallow errors and resolve before the reload completes
body: Both methods call `self.findMembers()` inside `then` without returning its promise, so callers' `then` fires before the member list is refreshed, and neither has a rejection handler. If the server responds 422 (e.g. automatic group) or 404, the admin UI shows nothing at all — the click appears to do nothing. Return the inner promise and surface failures (e.g. bootbox.alert with the server error), as `save`/`create` do.

title: Member add/remove specs use the wrong verb and don't assert counter integrity
body: `xhr :put, :remove_member` exercises the action with PUT even though the only route to `remove_member` is DELETE, so a verb/route mismatch would not be caught. More importantly, no spec asserts that removing a member updates `group.user_count` (the current implementation using `group.users.delete` leaves it stale), that removing a non-member behaves gracefully, or that `add_members` ignores unknown usernames (a case that had explicit coverage before this PR and was deleted). There is also no spec at all for the reshaped `GET /groups/:name/members` response (`members` + `meta`) or its limit/offset handling.

title: remove_member bypasses Group#remove, leaving user_count counter cache and primary_group stale
body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` on a `has_many :through` association removes the join rows with a `delete_all`, which skips ActiveRecord callbacks. `GroupUser` maintains `groups.user_count` through a counter cache / callbacks, and `Group#remove` additionally clears `users.primary_group_id` when the removed group was the user's primary group. By deleting the join rows directly, the group's `user_count` column is never decremented (so the admin group list and the new `{{user_count}}`/pagination UI show wrong totals forever) and a removed member can keep the deleted group as their primary group. The symmetric add path correctly uses `group.add(user)`; removal should use `group.remove(user)` (after looking the user up) so the same bookkeeping runs.

title: create silently drops alias_level
body: `create` only reads `params[:name]` and `params[:visible]`, but the client's `Discourse.Group#asJSON()` (used by both `create` and `save`) always sends `alias_level`, and the admin form lets you pick an alias level before the first save. As a result a newly created group is always persisted with the default alias level and the user's selection is lost without any error; it only takes effect if they save a second time (where `update` does honour `alias_level`). `create` should assign `alias_level` the same way `update` does.

title: Unvalidated limit/offset in public members endpoint
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to `.limit()/.offset()` on this unauthenticated-reachable endpoint. A negative value (e.g. `/groups/foo/members.json?offset=-1` or `limit=-1`) makes PostgreSQL raise "OFFSET must not be negative" / "LIMIT must not be negative", turning user input into a 500, and an arbitrarily large `limit` (e.g. `limit=1000000`) forces the server to load and serialize every member of a large group, which is an easy resource-exhaustion vector. Clamp both values (e.g. offset >= 0, limit between 1 and a sane maximum).

title: Breaking change to /groups/:name/members.json response shape and default truncation
body: The endpoint previously returned a bare JSON array of serialized members (and only paginated automatic groups). It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}` and applies a default `limit` of 50 to every group. Any existing consumer (plugins, mobile clients, scripts) that iterates the top-level array will break, and callers that relied on getting the whole membership now silently receive at most 50 users. This needs at least a changelog/version note, and ideally the pagination default should be documented; consider whether the old array shape must be preserved for compatibility.

title: findMembers returns undefined for unnamed groups instead of a promise
body: The early return was changed from `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` to a bare `return;`, so `findMembers()` now returns `undefined` when the group has no name (the "new group" case in the admin UI). Any caller that chains on the result — e.g. `group.findMembers().then(...)`, or the controller's `next`/`previous` actions whose return value is used by the Ember action/promise machinery — will throw `TypeError: Cannot read property 'then' of undefined`. Return a resolved promise instead.

title: totalPages off by one produces an extra empty page
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 150 members with limit 50) this yields 4 instead of 3. Because `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to `totalPages`, the "next" arrow stays enabled on the real last page, advancing `offset` to 150 and rendering an empty member list labelled page 4/4. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead.

title: addMembers/removeMember ignore server errors
body: `addMembers` and `removeMember` fire `model.addMembers(...)` / `model.removeMember(...)` without attaching a rejection handler. The server returns 422 for automatic groups and can also fail for other reasons, and unknown usernames are silently skipped by `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`. The admin therefore gets no feedback at all: the input keeps its content (see the "TODO: should clear the input"), the list is not refreshed, and nothing indicates the operation failed. Add a failure handler that surfaces the error message (as the `save` action already does).

title: add_members raises NoMethodError when usernames is sent as an array
body: `usernames.split(",")` assumes the parameter is a String. An API client (or a nested form encoding such as `usernames[]=bob`) yields an Array, and `Array#split` does not exist, producing an unhandled NoMethodError / 500 instead of a 400-class response. Coerce with `Array(params[:usernames]).join(',').split(',')` or validate the type explicitly.

title: remove_member spec uses PUT while the route only accepts DELETE
body: The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" example issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but `config/routes.rb` maps only `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. Controller specs bypass verb-based route recognition, so the test passes while exercising a request that cannot actually be made against the app; a regression in the route verb would go unnoticed. Use `xhr :delete` as the other remove_member example does.

title: Lost coverage for unknown/non-member usernames and no coverage for the new members pagination
body: The old specs asserted that adding a non-existent username and removing a non-member succeed silently; those cases are dropped here even though `add_members` still swallows unknown usernames, so that behaviour is now untested. Additionally, `GroupsController#members` was rewritten (new `{members:, meta:}` envelope, new default limit, new offset handling) without any spec update, so the response shape and the limit/offset edge cases are entirely uncovered.

title: remove_member bypasses GroupUser callbacks and the user_count counter cache
body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` deletes the join rows of a `has_many :through` association, whose default deletion strategy is `delete_all` (raw SQL on `group_users`). This skips all `GroupUser` callbacks and the `counter_cache: "user_count"` on `GroupUser#group`, so `groups.user_count` is never decremented and side effects previously performed by `Group#remove` (title / trust-level / primary-group housekeeping) are not run. The result is a permanently wrong member count shown in the admin UI and in the new `members` endpoint's `meta.total`, plus stale user titles. Use `group.remove(user)` with a looked-up `User` record instead. Additionally, `CollectionProxy#delete` with an integer id performs a `find`, so a stale/bogus `user_id` raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` (500) instead of a clean error.

title: create silently drops alias_level
body: `create` only assigns `name` and `visible`, but the client's `Group#asJSON` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js) always posts `alias_level` as well. An admin who picks an alias level while creating a new group has that choice silently discarded; the group is created with the default alias level and the admin must save a second time to apply it. Assign `group.alias_level` in `create` the same way `update` does.

title: update forces visible=false whenever the param is absent
body: `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` is executed unconditionally, so any PUT to `/admin/groups/:id` that does not include `visible` (or sends a JSON boolean `true` rather than the string "true") will set the group to invisible. Since `update` is now the only way to change group attributes, a partial update from any other client silently hides the group. Only assign when the param is present, and accept boolean values.

title: add_members crashes when usernames is sent as an array
body: `usernames.split(",")` assumes a String. If a client posts `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` (a perfectly natural encoding, and the shape the old API accepted via `Array(actions[:add])`), `params.require(:usernames)` returns an Array and `split` raises `NoMethodError`, producing a 500. Normalize with `Array.wrap(...)`/`to_s.split(",")` before iterating.

title: members endpoint accepts unbounded and negative limit/offset
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to the query. Any anonymous visitor can request `?limit=1000000` on a large group and force the server to load and serialize the whole membership (cheap DoS vector), and `?limit=-1` or `?offset=-1` makes PostgreSQL raise "LIMIT must not be negative" / "OFFSET must not be negative", returning a 500. Clamp both values (e.g. limit between 1 and 100, offset >= 0).

title: GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed with no spec coverage
body: The endpoint previously returned a bare JSON array of serialized users; it now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}`. This is a breaking change for any external consumer or plugin hitting the public members endpoint, and no spec was added or updated for the new shape or for the pagination behaviour (spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb is untouched in this PR, so any existing assertion on the array response is now wrong). Add/update specs covering the new payload, the default limit, and the offset handling.

title: totalPages off-by-one creates a phantom empty last page
body: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` over-counts whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`: with 50 members and limit 50 it reports 2 pages, and `next` is enabled (showingLast compares currentPage to totalPages), so the admin can page to an empty member list showing "2/2". Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`. The same off-by-one is reinforced in Group#findMembers, which clamps offset to `user_count` instead of `user_count - 1`, allowing an offset that returns zero rows.

title: Public group members page is now silently truncated to 50 users
body: `GroupsController#members` now applies a default limit of 50 to every group (previously only automatic groups were paginated), but this template has no pagination controls and the group-members route just calls `model.findMembers()` once. For any group with more than 50 members the public page now shows only the first 50 with no indication that members are missing and no way to load the rest. Either add pagination/infinite scroll here or request the full list for this view.

title: remove_member spec uses the wrong HTTP verb and only covers the automatic-group guard
body: `xhr :put, :remove_member` is used while the route is registered as `delete "members"` (config/routes.rb), so the test exercises a verb that does not exist in production routing. More importantly, the only non-automatic test removes an existing member and asserts `group.users.count == 0`; there is no coverage for `group.user_count` staying consistent, nor for a `user_id` that is not a member / does not exist (which currently raises RecordNotFound). Fix the verb and add those cases.

title: findMembers returns undefined for unnamed groups, breaking promise-based callers
body: When `name` is empty `findMembers` now returns `undefined` instead of the previous `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. Callers treat the return value as a promise (`actions.next`/`previous` return it, and `removeMember`/`addMembers` chain off `findMembers`), so for a new, unsaved group any code that calls `.then()` on the result will throw. Return a resolved promise instead.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded in the controller path, so fallbacks silently fail elsewhere
body: Translations are loaded lazily per locale (`load_locale`), and `translate` only guarantees that `config.locale` is loaded. The new fallback chain (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]`) is only pre-loaded by `ApplicationController#set_locale` via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`. Any translation performed outside a web request — Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console, model/service code that sets `I18n.locale` itself — will have the fallback locales' YAML files unloaded, so a missing key in the current locale will not fall back and will return "translation missing" instead. The loading of the fallback chain should happen inside `translate`/`load_locale` (or in `I18n.locale=`) rather than in one before_filter.

title: LRU translation cache key does not account for the fallback chain (multisite/stale results)
body: The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With fallbacks enabled, the resolved value for a key now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which is per-site and mutable. In a multisite process the backend is shared, so a value resolved through site A's default-locale fallback will be served from the cache to site B requesting the same key and locale. Likewise, changing `default_locale` on a site does not invalidate the cache, so previously cached fallback results stay stale until a reload. The cache key must include the fallback chain (or the cache must be flushed when `default_locale` changes).

title: `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` raises if the setting is nil, and `compact` cannot save it
body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `to_sym` on the setting before the array is compacted. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` ever returns nil/blank (unset setting, or SiteSetting not usable yet), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'to_sym' for nil`, from inside every fallback lookup — i.e. from any missing-translation lookup. Guard with something like `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym` so the intended `compact` actually works.

title: Fallback chain is recomputed (with a SiteSetting read) on every lookup and may run before the DB is available
body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` ignores the Hash storage and recomputes the chain on every call, including a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read and a fresh array allocation. `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` normally memoizes the computed chain; here every translation miss hits SiteSetting and allocates. More importantly, this code can be invoked in contexts where SiteSetting/DB is not available (asset precompilation, migrations, boot-time translations), where it will raise instead of returning a usable chain. Consider memoizing per locale and keying/invalidating on `default_locale`, and rescuing to `[locale, :en]` when SiteSetting is unavailable.

title: `@loaded_locales ||= []` in ensure_loaded! runs outside LOAD_MUTEX and can discard loaded-locale state
body: `ensure_loaded!` initializes `@loaded_locales ||= []` without holding `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` mutates the same array under the mutex. Two threads racing after a `reload!`/boot can both observe nil and each assign a fresh array, so one thread's `@loaded_locales << locale` is lost and that locale is considered unloaded (causing redundant reloads) or, worse, a partially loaded array is published. The nil-initialization should be done inside the mutex (or at load time of the patch) so all access to `@loaded_locales` is synchronized.

title: No specs cover the new server-side fallback behaviour
body: This change introduces a custom fallback chain (user locale → site default locale → :en) plus on-demand loading of all fallback locales, replacing the `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` environment settings. There are no tests asserting that a key missing in the user locale resolves from the site default locale and then from English, that the fallback locales get loaded by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, or that changing `SiteSetting.default_locale` takes effect. Given the lazy-loading and LRU caching interactions in `translate_accelerator`, these paths are easy to break silently (missing translations will now be masked rather than raised).

title: Fallback locales are only loaded during web requests, so fallbacks silently fail elsewhere
body: The on-demand locale loader in `I18n.translate` only loads `config.locale` (line 68). The newly added fallback chain is only pre-loaded by `ApplicationController#set_locale` calling `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`. Any translation performed outside a controller request — Sidekiq jobs, mailers/user notifications, rake tasks, rails console, middleware that runs before/without the before_filter — will have only the primary locale's YAML loaded, so `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` will look up the fallback locales (site default locale and `:en`) in an empty translation store and still produce a missing translation. The fallback feature therefore works inconsistently depending on the execution context. The loading of the fallback chain should happen inside `load_locale`/`translate` (i.e. whenever a locale is activated) rather than only in the controller filter.

title: Translation LRU cache key does not account for the fallback chain (stale/cross-site translations)
body: The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With fallbacks enabled, the resolved value for a given (key, locale) pair now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which is computed per request in `FallbackLocaleList#[]`. Two consequences: (1) after an admin changes `default_locale`, previously cached fallback results for other locales remain in the process-level LRU cache and keep returning values resolved through the old fallback locale until a reload; (2) in a multisite deployment the LRU cache is shared across all sites in the process while `SiteSetting.default_locale` is per-site, so a string resolved through site A's fallback locale can be served to site B for the same locale/key. The cache key needs to include the fallback chain (or the current site/default locale), or the cache must be invalidated when `default_locale` changes.

title: `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` can raise, and `.uniq.compact` ordering is wrong
body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `to_sym` on `SiteSetting.default_locale` unguarded. If the setting is nil/not yet available (e.g. during asset precompilation, early boot, or before migrations create the site_settings table) this raises `NoMethodError`/DB errors from inside every `I18n.translate` call, since `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` invokes `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on each lookup. Also, `compact` is applied after `uniq`, so a nil `locale` argument is only removed after being compared — the intent (drop nils, then dedupe) would be `.compact.uniq`. Guard the setting lookup (e.g. `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym`) and reorder.

title: FallbackLocaleList#[] recomputes on every lookup, defeating Hash memoization
body: `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` for every translation lookup. Unlike `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`, which memoizes computed chains in the Hash, this override ignores the Hash storage and rebuilds a new array (plus a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read and a `to_sym`) on each call. On a hot path such as rendering a page with many translations this adds an allocation and a site-setting lookup per translation; consider caching per locale (and invalidating when `default_locale` changes).

title: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` assumes a FallbackLocaleList and will 500 if fallbacks are replaced
body: `ensure_loaded!` is defined only on the custom `FallbackLocaleList` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`. If anything else assigns `I18n.fallbacks` (a plugin, or `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` still present in an environment file such as development.rb/test.rb or a deployment's own copy of production.rb, which installs a plain `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`), this before_filter raises `NoMethodError` on every single request, taking the whole site down. Either define the loading helper in a place that does not depend on the fallbacks object type (e.g. in the translate accelerator, loading `I18n.fallbacks[I18n.locale]`) or guard with `respond_to?`.

title: `@loaded_locales ||= []` in ensure_loaded! runs outside LOAD_MUTEX
body: `ensure_loaded!` lazily initializes and reads `@loaded_locales` without holding `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` mutates the same array under the mutex and `reload!` replaces it. Two threads can both observe nil and each install a fresh array, so a locale recorded as loaded by one thread can be dropped, and `include?` can be executed concurrently with `<<`/reassignment. On non-GVL runtimes this can corrupt the array or cause repeated/missed loads. Initialize `@loaded_locales` eagerly at patch load time or perform the check inside the mutex.

title: No tests for the new fallback behaviour
body: This PR introduces a custom fallback chain (user locale → site default locale → :en), moves pluralization setup, and adds `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, yet no specs are added. There is no coverage asserting that a key missing in a user's locale resolves from `SiteSetting.default_locale` and then `:en`, that `FallbackLocaleList#[]` dedupes, or that `ensure_loaded!` actually loads the fallback locale files. Given that fallbacks are now active in all environments (the per-environment `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` lines were removed), regressions here would silently change every missing-translation lookup, including in the test suite where missing translations will now be masked by the :en fallback.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded in the request cycle, so fallbacks silently fail elsewhere
body: Locale files are loaded lazily: `I18n.translate` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)` for the *current* locale, and the new fallback locales are loaded exclusively by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any translation performed outside a web request (Sidekiq jobs, mailers that set `I18n.locale` per recipient, rake tasks, console, `I18n.t(key, locale: :xx)` calls) will therefore run with the fallback locales' translation data not loaded, so `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` finds nothing in the fallback chain and the user gets a "translation missing" string instead of the English/site-default text — exactly the case this feature is meant to fix. The loading of the fallback chain should happen inside `load_locale`/`translate` (or `ensure_loaded!` should be invoked from a single central place), not in a controller filter.

title: Translation LRU cache key ignores the fallback chain, so results go stale when default_locale changes
body: The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With the new fallbacks, the value returned for a given key/locale also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (the second entry of `FallbackLocaleList#[]`). When an admin changes the `default_locale` site setting, previously cached entries that were resolved through the old fallback locale remain in the LRU cache and keep being served for the lifetime of the process (nothing calls `I18n.reload!` on that setting change). Either include the resolved fallback chain in the cache key or clear `@cache` when `default_locale` changes.

title: Fallback list is recomputed (with a SiteSetting read) on every lookup instead of being memoized
body: `FallbackLocaleList` subclasses `Hash` but overrides `#[]` to always recompute, so every call from `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` (which happens on *every* translation lookup, not just misses) performs a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read, a `to_sym`, and allocates two arrays (`uniq`, `compact`). Translation lookups with interpolation arguments bypass the LRU cache in translate_accelerator, so this runs on a hot path. Since the class is already a Hash, the computed chain should be memoized per locale and invalidated when `default_locale` changes.

title: `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` raises if the setting is nil, and `uniq` before `compact` cannot protect it
body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `to_sym` on the setting value before any nil handling; if `SiteSetting.default_locale` is ever nil/blank (e.g. during early boot, or a site with a cleared setting) this raises `NoMethodError` from inside every translation lookup, which would surface as a 500 on all pages. The trailing `.compact` only removes nils that are already in the array (and `uniq` before `compact` is pointless), it does not guard the `to_sym` call. Use `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym` or a safe default.

title: `@loaded_locales ||= []` in ensure_loaded! runs outside LOAD_MUTEX
body: `ensure_loaded!` lazily initializes `@loaded_locales` and tests `include?` without holding `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` mutates the same ivar inside the mutex. If two threads hit `ensure_loaded!` while the ivar is still nil, both create their own array and one assignment is lost, so the record of already-loaded locales can be dropped and translation files are re-parsed (and the `include?` guard in `translate` can be defeated). Initialize `@loaded_locales` inside the mutex (or at load time) and perform the membership check under the same lock.

title: No tests for the new fallback behaviour
body: The PR changes global I18n behaviour for all environments (fallbacks are now always enabled, with a custom chain user-locale → site default_locale → :en) and adds `I18n.ensure_loaded!`/`FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!`, but no specs are added. There is no coverage asserting that a key missing in a user's locale resolves to the site default locale and then to English, that `default_locale` changes are honoured, or that the lazy locale loader loads every locale in the chain. Given the stale-cache and lazy-loading interactions involved, regressions here would be silent (users just see missing/English text). Note also that `FallbackLocaleList` is defined in an initializer, so it is neither autoloaded nor reloadable, which makes it hard to unit test.

title: Denial cache key can collide across different resources (underscore delimiter)
body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` joins namespace, user UID, action, resource name and parent folder with `_` as the only separator. Resource names and folder UIDs in Grafana may legally contain underscores, so distinct checks produce identical keys, e.g. (name="a_b", parent="c") and (name="a", parent="b_c") both yield `...perm_<uid>_<action>_a_b_c`. Because `Check` now returns an immediate deny on a key hit (service.go:117), a legitimate deny for one resource will spuriously deny access to a different resource for the whole 30s TTL, with no way for the caller to recover. Use a delimiter that cannot appear in UIDs, or hash/length-prefix the components.

title: Denial is cached even when the deny came from a stale folder tree, stacking staleness
body: When the cached permissions do not grant access, the code re-queries permissions from the DB, but `checkInheritedPermissions`/`buildFolderTree` still use the 30s-cached folder tree (service.go:609-635). If the folder tree is stale and does not yet contain a freshly created parent folder, the check denies and that deny is then stored in `permDenialCache` for another full TTL. The staleness windows add up (up to ~2x shortCacheTTL), so a user who just created a nested folder/dashboard can keep being denied even after the permission refresh - exactly the scenario this PR aims to fix. Either bypass/refresh the folder tree on the fallback path, or do not cache denials that were produced by an inherited-permission lookup against a cached tree.

title: Every non-granting cached check now triggers a full DB permission re-query
body: `getUserPermissions`/`getAnonymousPermissions` no longer short-circuit on the permission cache (the cache lookups were removed), and `Check` only returns early when the cached permissions grant access. Consequently every Check for a resource the user is not (yet) known to have access to performs the full store path again (basic role, teams, `GetUserPermissions`) instead of being served from the 30s cache. The denial cache only bounds this per (action, name, folder) tuple, so workloads that check many distinct objects (e.g. per-item authorization over a large dashboard set) will issue one permission query per object per TTL, a large increase in DB load compared to the previous behaviour. Consider limiting the DB fallback (e.g. only when the cached entry is older than a short grace period, or once per user/action per interval).

title: Denial cache has unbounded key cardinality (one entry per user/action/name/folder)
body: The denial cache key includes the requested resource name and parent folder, so the number of entries grows with the number of distinct objects ever denied, per user and action. With a local in-memory cache that has no size limit (see `cache.NewLocalCache` in pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:88), a user or service scanning many resources they cannot access (thousands of dashboards) will populate thousands of entries within each 30s window, which can translate into significant memory pressure on large instances. A bounded/LRU cache or a coarser key is needed.

title: permissionCacheUsage metric is now misleading
body: `permissionCacheUsage` is incremented with "true" on a denial-cache hit (line 118), mixing two different caches into one hit-rate metric, and it is incremented with "false" at line 137 even when the permission cache was actually hit but simply did not grant access. The resulting cache hit-rate dashboards/alerts for the permission cache will report wrong values. Use a separate label/metric for the denial cache and only report "false" on a real permission-cache miss.

title: Denial key uses raw subject UID while permission key uses resolved UID
body: The denial key is built from `checkReq.UserUID` (the raw subject identifier from the request), whereas `userPermCacheKey` is built from `userIdentifiers.UID` resolved via `GetUserIdentifiers` (which treats numeric subjects as internal IDs). For a subject passed as `user:<numeric id>` the two caches are keyed on different identifiers, so the same user gets duplicate/independent denial entries depending on the subject form used by the caller, and denial entries cannot be reasoned about together with the permission entries. Resolve identifiers first and key both caches on the same resolved UID.

title: Denial-cache test does not actually exercise the short-circuit and its comment is wrong
body: In "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" the comment says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked" but the permission cache is seeded with `{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`, i.e. not allowed. Additionally `s.store`/`s.permissionStore` are the default empty `fakeStore`, which returns no permissions. The assertion `resp.Allowed == false` therefore holds even if the denial cache were ignored entirely, so the test gives no coverage of the new early-return path. Seed the permission cache with `true` (and/or a store that grants access) so the test fails if the denial cache is not consulted.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type, allowing cross-identity collisions
body: The new denial cache key is built from `checkReq.Namespace.Value`, `checkReq.UserUID`, action, name and parent folder, but not from `checkReq.IdentityType`. `validateSubject` returns only the raw id portion of the subject, so different identity types can produce the same `UserUID` — e.g. `anonymous:0` and `render:0` both yield `"0"` (both forms are exercised in the tests). A denial recorded for one identity type therefore short-circuits checks for the other identity type within the same namespace, which can deny an access that should be allowed (for instance the render service, whose permissions are synthesized separately in `getRendererPermissions`, for up to the 30s TTL). Note also that the permission cache deliberately uses a distinct key per identity type (`anonymousPermCacheKey` vs `userPermCacheKey`), so the denial cache is inconsistent with it.

title: Ambiguous denial cache key from unescaped concatenation of name and parent
body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` concatenates action, resource name and parent folder with `"_"` separators. Since Grafana UIDs may contain underscores, distinct requests map to the same key: e.g. name="a_b", parent="c" and name="a", parent="b_c" both produce `<ns>.perm_<uid>_<action>_a_b_c`. A cached denial for one resource then wrongly denies a different resource the user may actually be allowed to access, for the lifetime of the entry (30s). Using a separator that cannot appear in UIDs, or hashing/length-prefixing the components, would avoid this.

title: Every non-allowed Check now issues DB queries even with a warm permission cache
body: The cache lookup was removed from `getUserPermissions`/`getAnonymousPermissions`, and `Check` only returns early when the cached permissions grant access. Any check that is not granted by the cached scope map falls through to `getIdentityPermissions`, which re-reads basic roles, teams and permissions from the database (`permissionStore.GetUserPermissions`) even though a fresh cache entry exists. Workloads that check many resources a user cannot see (list/search filtering, authorization probes on many dashboard UIDs) will now generate one full permission query per distinct (name, folder) pair until the denial cache entry is written, which can be a large multiplier on DB load compared to the previous behaviour where the cache served all of them. Consider only re-querying when the cache entry is older than some threshold, or dedup/throttle the refresh.

title: Cached denial short-circuits the DB re-query, so newly granted permissions are invisible for up to 30s
body: `Check` returns immediately on a denial cache hit (line 117) before the permission cache / DB fallback runs, and a denial is cached for every negative result (line 154, shortCacheTTL = 30s). This re-introduces exactly the staleness the PR aims to fix for the case where a Check on a given (name, folder) pair happens before the permission is granted — e.g. a probe for a dashboard/folder UID that is created immediately afterwards, or a permission grant on an existing resource. The subsequent DB re-query cannot correct the result because the denial entry wins. Also, for inherited access the fallback re-reads permissions but still uses the cached `folderTree` (`buildFolderTree`, 30s TTL), so a dashboard placed in a brand-new sub-folder is denied and that denial is then cached, even though fresh folder data would allow it. At minimum the denial cache should be bypassed/invalidated when the underlying folder tree or permissions are refreshed.

title: permissionCacheUsage metric no longer reflects cache hits in Check
body: In `Check`, `permissionCacheUsage` is incremented with `"true"` only when the cached permissions actually allow the request, and the unconditional `"false"` increment at line 137 is reached on every cache hit that did not grant access. The metric therefore measures "allowed from cache" rather than cache hit ratio, and cache hits that end in a denial are reported as misses. Dashboards/alerts built on this metric will show a large, misleading drop in cache hit rate after this change.

title: Denial-cache test does not actually verify the short-circuit
body: In "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" the permission cache is seeded with `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}` under a comment claiming it "allow[s] access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked". A `false` value means not allowed, so `checkPermission` returns false, the code falls through to the DB (empty `fakeStore`, no permissions) and still denies. The assertion `assert.False(resp.Allowed)` passes whether or not the denial cache is consulted, so the new short-circuit path is untested. The value should be `true` (and ideally the fake store should also grant the permission) so that a regression removing the denial-cache lookup makes the test fail.

title: Denial cache can lock in a deny caused by a stale folder tree
body: `Check` now persists a negative result in `permDenialCache` for 30s whenever `checkPermission` returns false. The fallback added above only re-reads *permissions* from the DB; the folder hierarchy used by `checkInheritedPermissions` is still served from `folderCache` (also 30s TTL, see `buildFolderTree`). So for the exact case this PR targets – a resource that was just created in a folder the user only has inherited access to, or a brand-new folder – the folder tree lookup misses, the check is denied even after the fresh DB permission read, and that deny is then cached for the full TTL. The user is blocked for up to 30s even though a re-read of folders would have allowed access. Either skip caching the denial when the decision depended on the folder tree, or invalidate/refresh the folder tree on the fallback path.

title: Every non-cached denial triggers a full permission re-query and an unbounded cache entry
body: The cache read was removed from `getUserPermissions`/`getAnonymousPermissions`, and `Check` now falls through to `getIdentityPermissions` (DB query for basic role, teams and permissions) whenever the cached scope map does not grant the requested resource. Combined with a denial cache keyed by `(namespace, user, action, name, parentFolder)`, any sequence of checks over distinct resource names the user cannot access produces one DB permission query per distinct name, and one new cache entry per distinct name. For bulk authorization (e.g. checking many dashboards during a search) or for a caller passing arbitrary names, this is a significant DB-load amplification versus the previous behaviour (single cached scope map), and the local cache grows without bound until TTL expiry. Consider rate-limiting the re-query (e.g. a short "recently refreshed" marker per user+action) instead of re-querying on every miss.

title: Denial cache key built by naive concatenation can collide between distinct resources
body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` joins `action`, `name` and `parent` with single underscores without escaping. Since Grafana UIDs may contain underscores, distinct requests map to the same key: e.g. name=`a_b`/parent=`c` and name=`a`/parent=`b_c` both produce `...perm_<uid>_<action>_a_b_c`. A cached deny for one resource therefore denies access to a different resource for up to the TTL (and, less harmfully, the key shares the `".perm_"` prefix space with `userPermCacheKey`, so a colliding key makes the permission cache entry undecodable). Use a separator that cannot appear in UIDs/actions, or hash the components; also note the key omits group/resource and relies solely on the derived action string.

title: permissionCacheUsage metric records a miss when the cache was actually hit
body: When `getCachedIdentityPermissions` succeeds but the cached scope map does not grant access, control falls through to line 137 and increments `permissionCacheUsage` with label `"false"` (miss), even though the permission cache was hit. Because the per-function metric increments were removed from `getUserPermissions`, this is now the only accounting point, so cache hit-rate dashboards will systematically under-report hits for denied checks and make the new caching behaviour impossible to evaluate.

title: Denial-cache test does not actually verify the short-circuit
body: In "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" the comment says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked" but the permission cache is seeded with `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`, i.e. *no* permission. With the default `fakeStore` (nil user permissions) the request would be denied even if the denial cache were never consulted, so the test passes whether or not the new short-circuit works. Seed the permission cache with `true` (and/or assert that the store was not called) so a regression that skips `permDenialCache` is detected.

title: Missing `key` prop on GrafanaRuleListItem in the filtered rule list
body: In the `rules.map(...)` loop the `grafana` branch renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` without a `key`, while the other two branches still pass `key={key}`. The previously rendered `GrafanaRuleLoader` had `key={key}`. React will emit "Each child in a list should have a unique key" warnings and, because this list grows incrementally via infinite scrolling, element reuse becomes index-based, which can cause incorrect DOM/state reuse (e.g. open menus or skeletons attached to the wrong rule) when batches are appended.

title: Pause and Delete menu items are still gated on `rulerRule`, so they disappear in the new list view
body: The menu now computes Grafana-Prometheus-based abilities (`grafanaPauseAbility`, `grafanaDeleteAbility`) so actions can work without ruler data, but the render conditions were not updated: line 123 requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` for the pause item and line 165 requires `rulerRule` for the delete item. The new list view (GrafanaRuleListItem -> RuleActionsButtons) only passes `promRule`, never `rulerRule`, so Pause/Resume and Delete silently vanish from the rule menu in the alert list for all Grafana-managed rules. The newly added ability checks have no effect for these two actions.

title: Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer can never open without a ruler rule
body: `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, and `rule` (the ruler rule) is `undefined` when this component is used from the new list view (GrafanaRuleListItem passes only `promRule`). Meanwhile AlertRuleMenu now enables the "Silence notifications" item based on the Grafana Prometheus abilities, so the item is visible but clicking it only toggles `showSilenceDrawer` and nothing is rendered — a dead menu entry for every Grafana rule in the list view.

title: skipToken path returns `Duplicate` as supported and allowed, leaking the action onto non-Grafana rules
body: `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(skipToken, ...)` calls `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)`. With `rule === undefined`, `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` returns `loading: false`, so `MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported` and `duplicateSupported = true`; `Duplicate` therefore evaluates to `[true, ctx.hasPermission(grafana rules create)]`. Because AlertRuleMenu ORs the ruler and Grafana abilities, a user holding Grafana `AlertingRuleCreate` will see the "Duplicate" action on data-source (Mimir/Loki/Prometheus) rules even when the ruler-based ability says it is unsupported/not allowed, and the clone flow will then fail. The skip path should produce all-false abilities. Note the unit tests mock these hooks, so this is not caught by RulesTable.test.tsx.

title: Grafana-managed recording rules lose Pause and Export support in the new ability hook
body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` uses `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` where the ruler-based equivalent used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` (true for both alerting and recording Grafana rules). As a result `Pause`, `Restore`, `DeletePermanently` and `ModifyExport` are reported as unsupported for Grafana-managed *recording* rules, even though these rules can be paused and exported. In the list view (which now relies solely on these abilities) pausing/exporting a Grafana recording rule becomes impossible.

title: Federated rule group detection dropped from useAllRulerRuleAbilities
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and used it to mark Update/Delete/Duplicate/Pause as unsupported for federated (Mimir cross-tenant) rule groups. After merging into `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, `isFederated` is hardcoded to `false` with only a TODO. Users will now be offered Edit/Delete/Duplicate on federated Mimir rules, which cannot be edited through this UI and will fail server-side. If the group information is not available in `RuleGroupIdentifierV2`, this needs another source rather than a silent `false`.

title: `returnTo` query param dropped from the rule view link
body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the href as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new component drops the `returnTo` parameter, so navigating from the rule list into a rule detail page loses the "return to previous" affordance that the rest of the alerting UI relies on.

title: Test asserts exactly 4 menu items, codifying the loss of Delete/Pause actions
body: The test grants `AlertingRuleDelete` and `AlertingRuleUpdate` both globally and on the folder, yet asserts `menuItems.length === 4` and never uses the newly declared `ui.menuItems.delete` selector. Because the menu still requires a ruler rule for Delete and Pause (AlertRuleMenu lines 123/165), those items are absent — and this assertion now locks that regression in, so a future fix restoring Delete/Pause would break the test instead of the test catching the missing actions. The test should explicitly assert the expected presence of Delete and Pause for a user with those permissions.

title: New `provenance` field on GrafanaPromRuleDTO is untested and unverified against the API
body: `provenance?: string` is added to `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` and is now the only signal used by `isProvisionedPromRule` / `GrafanaRuleListItem`'s `isProvisioned` and by the ability hooks to block editing of provisioned rules in the list view. No test (including the new `rulerRuleToPromRule` helper in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx) sets this field, so if the Grafana Prometheus rules endpoint does not return `provenance`, provisioned rules will be rendered as editable/deletable in the list view and nothing will catch it.

title: `logWarning` called from the render phase
body: `getEditableIdentifier` is invoked during render and calls `logWarning(...)` as a side effect when no identifier can be derived. Render-phase side effects run on every re-render (and twice per render under React StrictMode), so a single rule whose identifier cannot be constructed will repeatedly emit the same analytics warning. This should be moved into an effect or deduplicated.

title: Stale comment and variable name after removing the ruler prefetch
body: The ruler `getGrafanaRulerGroup` prefetch was removed, but the surrounding comment still says "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX ... doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded" and the variable is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload`. Both now describe behaviour that no longer exists and will mislead readers about what this block does.

title: Delete menu item can never render for list-view rules (rulerRule is undefined)
body: The Delete item is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule`. After this PR the alert list view intentionally no longer fetches ruler rules, so `rulerRule` is always `undefined` there, which means users can never delete a rule from the new rule list even though `canDelete` is now computed from `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` and the caller (`RuleActionsButtons.V2`) ignores the `rule` argument entirely (`handleDelete={() => showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)}`). The whole point of adding the Grafana-Prom delete ability is defeated. The guard (and the `handleDelete(rule: RulerRuleDTO, ...)` prop signature) should be relaxed so the item renders when `canDelete` is true and the identifier is known. Note that the new GrafanaGroupLoader test asserting exactly 4 menu items (no Delete) hard-codes this regression.

title: Pause menu item still requires a ruler rule, so it is never shown in the list view
body: The pause item is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` is truthy. Since the list view no longer loads ruler rules, `rulerRule` is `undefined` and the pause/unpause action silently disappears from the rule list, despite the newly added `grafanaPauseAbility` computation suggesting it should be available. Either `MenuItemPauseRule` needs to accept a Grafana Prometheus rule / rule identifier, or the computed Grafana pause ability is dead code that gives a false impression that pausing works.

title: Missing React `key` on GrafanaRuleListItem inside mapped list
body: In the `rules.map(...)` body, the `grafana` branch renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` without a `key`, while the previous `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ... />` had one (and the other branches still pass `key={key}`). React will log a key warning for every render and, more importantly, cannot reconcile list items correctly when the filtered result set grows incrementally (items are appended via `setRules`), which can cause wrong item reuse/state and extra re-renders. Pass `key={key}`.

title: Federated rule-group check dropped: federated rules become editable/deletable
body: `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` now hard-codes `const isFederated = false` and the `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` call was removed when `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` was rewritten to delegate here. Previously rules belonging to a Mimir federated rule group (`source_tenants` present) were treated as immutable, so Edit/Delete/Pause were unsupported. With this change the UI will offer edit/delete for federated rules, and those write operations are not supported by the ruler for federated groups, so users will hit failures (or unintentionally modify a federated group). The federated check needs to be preserved, e.g. by passing the group (or a flag) into the hook rather than stubbing it out with a TODO.

title: Grafana-managed recording rules lose Export/Pause/Restore abilities
body: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore` and `DeletePermanently` are gated on `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, whereas the ruler-based equivalent used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` which also matches Grafana recording rules. Since the list view now relies exclusively on this hook (ruler abilities resolve to false with no `rulerRule`), Grafana-managed recording rules can no longer be paused, exported with modifications, or restored from the rule list. If the intent was only to exclude recording rules from silencing, the alerting-only check should be limited to the `Silence` ability.

title: `returnTo` query param dropped from rule view link
body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the rule href as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem` omits `returnTo`, so navigating into a rule from the list and then using the "return to previous" breadcrumb/button will no longer bring the user back to the filtered list page they came from.

title: Test asserts exactly 4 menu items, locking in the missing Delete action
body: The test grants `AlertingRuleDelete` both globally and on the folder, yet asserts `menuItems.length).toBe(4)` and never checks `ui.menuItems.delete()` (the selector is defined but unused). This codifies the current behaviour where Delete (and Pause) are unreachable in the new list view because `AlertRuleMenu` still requires a `rulerRule` for those items. Once the menu is fixed the assertion will break; the test should explicitly assert the presence/absence of Delete and Pause so the regression is visible rather than baked in.

title: Stale ruler-preload naming and comment after removing the ruler prefetch
body: The ruler `getGrafanaRulerGroup` prefetch was removed, but the surrounding comment ("This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules... doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded") and the variable name `cacheAndRulerPreload` still describe ruler preloading. This is misleading for future readers who will look for ruler prefetching that no longer exists; rename/update to reflect that only the Prometheus group cache is populated.

title: Pause and Delete menu items can never render without a ruler rule
body: The menu now computes `canPause`/`canDelete` from the Prometheus-rule abilities as well (so that the list view works without ruler requests), but the render conditions are still `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123) and `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165). In the new rule list view `rulerRule` is `undefined` (GrafanaRuleListItem only passes `promRule`), so Pause/Unpause and Delete can never be shown there. The newly added ability plumbing for those two actions is dead code and users lose the ability to pause or delete a rule from the list, which the GrafanaGroupLoader test now bakes in by asserting exactly 4 menu items.

title: Silence menu item is a no-op when only a Prometheus rule is provided
body: `AlertRuleMenu` now shows the "Silence notifications" item based on the Prometheus-rule abilities, so it appears in the list view where only `promRule` is passed. However the drawer is still rendered conditionally on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` (line 104), and `rule` (the ruler rule) is `undefined` in that path. Clicking "Silence notifications" sets `showSilenceDrawer` but nothing ever renders, so the action silently does nothing for every rule in the new list view.

title: skipToken path returns permissive abilities instead of all-false
body: `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` map `skipToken` to `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)` rather than short-circuiting. With `rule === undefined`, `loading` is false so `MaybeSupported` becomes `AlwaysSupported`, and abilities built with `toAbility` (Duplicate at line 318, View, Explore) come back as `[true, ctx.hasPermission(...)]`. Since `AlertRuleMenu` ORs the ruler-based and prom-based abilities, a data-source (e.g. Mimir) rule — which passes `skipToken` — is reported as duplicatable for anyone holding the global Grafana `alert.rule:create` permission, even when the ruler-based check says the action isn't supported. The skip path should return all-`[false,false]` abilities.

title: OR-ing ruler and prom abilities lets the more permissive source win
body: Every ability is combined as `(rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (promSupported && promAllowed)` (lines 83-100). The ruler-based hook deliberately marks a rule as not supported when it is immutable (provisioned, plugin-provided, federated); the prom-based hook detects provisioning only through the brand-new optional `provenance` field on `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`. Whenever that field is absent from the Prometheus response (it is typed optional and nothing guarantees the backend sends it), the prom branch reports Pause/Delete/Duplicate as allowed and the OR overrides the ruler branch's immutability guard, exposing destructive actions for provisioned rules that the API will reject. Consider selecting one source per call site rather than OR-ing, and/or treating an absent `provenance` conservatively.

title: Missing React `key` on GrafanaRuleListItem in the filtered list
body: The grafana branch of the `rules.map(...)` switch previously rendered `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ... />`; the replacement `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` (lines 157-163) dropped the `key` prop while the datasource and unknown branches still pass it. This produces React key warnings and, because the filter view appends pages incrementally, can cause incorrect element reuse/re-mounting (losing per-item state such as an open menu) as new batches are concatenated.

title: Federated rule-group protection removed for all consumers of useAllAlertRuleAbilities
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, where `isFederated` is hardcoded to `false` (line 245, with only a TODO). Previously it called `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, which made Update/Delete/Pause unsupported for Mimir federated rule groups. With this change the existing (non-list) rule views will offer Edit/Delete on federated groups, leading to user-visible failures or unintended modifications of groups that cannot be edited through this UI.

title: Pause/ModifyExport incorrectly restricted to alerting rules for Grafana prom rules
body: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `AlertRuleAction.Pause` (line 325), `Restore`, `DeletePermanently` and `ModifyExport` (line 324) are gated on `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`. The ruler-based equivalent used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule`, which includes Grafana-managed *recording* rules. Grafana-managed recording rules do support pausing (`is_paused`) and export, so this hook reports those actions as unsupported for them, hiding valid functionality once the list view relies on this hook.

title: Rule view link no longer carries `returnTo`
body: The deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the href as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new component drops the `returnTo` query parameter (line 40), so navigating from the rule list into a rule detail page loses the "return to previous" context and the back affordance in the detail view will no longer point at the filtered list the user came from.

title: Stale comment and variable name after removing ruler prefetch
body: The ruler `getGrafanaRulerGroup` prefetch was removed, but the surrounding comment still says "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX ... doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded" and the array is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload` (lines 81-84). Both now describe behaviour that no longer exists and will mislead future readers about what is being preloaded.

title: Test codifies the loss of Pause/Delete actions and drops provisioned-rule coverage
body: `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)` asserts that only silence/copy-link/duplicate/export exist, locking in the fact that Pause and Delete are no longer reachable from the Grafana rule list (see AlertRuleMenu's `rulerRule` gates). There is also no test covering a provisioned rule (`provenance` set on the prom DTO) to verify that mutating actions stay hidden, which is now the only mechanism preventing destructive actions on provisioned rules in this view.

title: Queries are now interpolated twice (ad hoc filters applied twice) per sub-request
body: `runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` up-front, but the sub-requests built from these targets are still executed with `datasource.runQuery(subRequest)`, and `runQuery` delegates to `DataSourceWithBackend.query()`, which maps every target through `applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` again (the sub-request keeps `scopedVars` and `filters` from the original request). Loki's `applyTemplateVariables` is not idempotent in one respect: it calls `addAdHocFilters(target.expr, adhocFilters)`, so the same ad hoc filters are injected a second time into an expression that already contains them, yielding duplicated matchers/label filters (e.g. `{a="b", env="prod", env="prod"}` or a repeated `| env="prod"`). Variable values are also substituted twice, so any value that itself contains `$name`/`${name}` will be expanded on the second pass. Either strip `filters`/`scopedVars` from the sub-requests, or keep interpolation in a single place.

title: Shard path interpolates each query three times and changes the selector used to fetch shard values
body: `runShardSplitQuery` now interpolates targets with `applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)`; the resulting sharded sub-request is then handed to `runSplitQuery()`, which (after this PR) interpolates again, and finally `datasource.runQuery()` -> `DataSourceWithBackend.query()` interpolates a third time. Since Loki's `applyTemplateVariables` re-runs `addAdHocFilters`, each pass re-inserts the same ad hoc filters into the already sharded expression, producing duplicated matchers. Additionally, the previous code called `interpolateVariablesInQueries(request.targets, request.scopedVars)` without ad hoc filters, whereas the new call passes `request.filters`; the selector derived by `getSelectorForShardValues()` and sent to `fetchLabelValues('__stream_shard__', { streamSelector })` now includes ad hoc filters, which silently changes which shard values are discovered. This behaviour change is untested.

title: Test encodes repeated interpolation (5 calls for 1 target) as expected behaviour
body: The assertion was changed from `interpolateVariablesInQueries` being called once to `applyTemplateVariables` being called 5 times for a single target. Those 5 calls are 1 call in `runShardSplitQuery` plus 1 per shard sub-request from the newly added interpolation inside `runSplitQuery`; i.e. the test now locks in the duplicate interpolation of each sub-request. It only passes because the mock at line 56 mutates the query object and does a plain `replace('$SELECTOR', ...)`, which is a no-op on the second pass; a realistic mock (returning a copy and re-applying ad hoc filters) would show duplicated filters. The mock also mutates its input, unlike the real `applyTemplateVariables`, which returns a new object, so target mutation regressions cannot be caught here.

title: New interpolation test mocks replace() in a way that contradicts real `$__auto` handling
body: The test's `replace` mock substitutes `$__auto` with `5m`, and the test then asserts the executed expr is `count_over_time({a="b"}[5m])`.
