body: `ClientPermissionsV2` contains a private, never-called `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` method (it was only needed for token exchange, which now throws `UnsupportedOperationException`), an unused `logger` field (line 51), and unused imports (`Scope`, `ClientModelIdentity`/`DefaultEvaluationContext` only used by the dead method, and the static import of `AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE`). This dead code suggests an incomplete copy from `ClientPermissions` and should be removed to avoid confusion about whether token exchange is supported here.

title: No test coverage for the map-roles-client-scope scope and client-scope level permissions
body: The PR adds `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` to the Clients resource type and implements `canMapClientScopeRoles()`, `canManage(ClientScopeModel)`/`canView(ClientScopeModel)` and `getClientsWithPermission()` in `ClientPermissionsV2`, but the new tests only exercise `manage`, `configure`, `view`, `map-roles` and `map-roles-composite`. The scope-to-client-scope mapping path and the client-scope evaluators are therefore untested, which is where the issues above (e.g. `getClientsWithPermission` returning the resource-type name) would have been caught.

title: NPE when the "Clients" resource-type resource does not exist
body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when no per-client resource exists the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`, which can legitimately return `null` (it returns null when the realm's `adminPermissionsEnabled` flag is off, or when the `Clients` resource simply does not exist in the resource server, e.g. a realm whose admin-permissions client was initialized before the `Clients` resource type was added). The returned value is immediately passed to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later to `new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server)` without a null check, producing a NullPointerException / HTTP 500 on ordinary admin endpoints such as GET/PUT /clients/{id}. A null check returning `false` is needed.

title: No upgrade path for realms whose admin-permissions client was already initialized
body: `init()` creates the authorization scopes and the per-resource-type "all" resources only once, when the admin permissions client is first created (it returns early if `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null`). Realms that already enabled ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 before this change therefore have neither the new `Clients` resource nor the new scopes `configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, `map-roles-composite`. For those realms, creating a Clients permission fails (`getOrCreateResource` throws `ModelException("No scopes found.")` when a scope is missing) and client permission evaluation hits the missing `Clients` resource. Either a migration that adds missing scopes/resources, or lazy creation on demand, is required.

title: Client/role/group removal breaks when both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and V2 are enabled
body: The removal listener is now guarded by `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`, but `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. With both features enabled (they are independent flags), a `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` now calls `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` -> `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. The event listener runs inside the removal transaction, so deleting a client fails with a server error instead of cleaning up V1 permission policies. The listener should select the V1 management implementation explicitly (or the V2 implementation must tolerate these calls).

title: Overridden methods throwing UnsupportedOperationException turn 403/legacy paths into 500s
body: `canExchangeTo`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions`, `resource` and the `*Permission(ClientModel)` methods all throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. These are still reached at runtime when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled: the token-exchange flow calls `AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(...)` to decide whether an exchange to another client is allowed, and the `/clients/{id}/management/permissions` admin endpoints call `isPermissionsEnabled`/`setPermissionsEnabled` (the latter only requires the V1 feature, which can be enabled simultaneously). The result is an HTTP 500 instead of the previous Forbidden/clean response. These methods should return a safe value (e.g. `false`) or the call sites must be guarded.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns the resource-type resource name and misses per-client resources
body: `getClientsWithPermission` iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...)` and collects `resource.getName()`. Two problems: (1) the "all clients" resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` has both name and type equal to `Clients`, so when an all-clients permission is granted the literal string `"Clients"` is added to the returned set and is then treated by callers as a client id; (2) per-client resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` are created without a type (`setType` is never called), so `findByType` never returns them and clients that have individual permissions are not reported. The method therefore returns wrong data for callers that filter client listings by granted permission.

title: getResourceName not extended for the Clients resource type
body: `getResourceName` only resolves human-readable names for the `Users` resource type. For the newly added `Clients` resource type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is null for resources created by `getOrCreateResource` (only name=clientId-UUID and owner are set). Consequently the admin REST/console representation of a client permission shows a null/empty resource name instead of the client's clientId, and there is no "All clients" label analogous to "All users".

title: Javadoc on require* methods documents a return value for void methods
body: `requireView()` (line 95-98) and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line 100-103) are documented as "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}" / "...if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but both methods are `void` and throw ForbiddenException when the check fails, like the other `require*` methods in this interface. The docs should state the throwing behaviour, otherwise implementers/callers are misled about the contract.

title: New map-roles-client-scope scope and client-scope permissions are untested
body: The PR adds the scopes `configure`, `map-roles`, `map-roles-composite`, `map-roles-client-scope` and the client-scope related evaluations (`canManage(ClientScopeModel)`, `canView(ClientScopeModel)`, `canManageClientScopes()`), but the new tests only cover MANAGE, CONFIGURE, VIEW, MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE. `canMapClientScopeRoles` / `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` and the ClientScopeModel-based checks have no coverage, so regressions in those code paths (including the ones that intentionally differ from V1) would go unnoticed.

title: Exit code 4 silently changes meaning (recreate -> feature disabled)
body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` is changed from 4 to 3 and 4 is reused for the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` result. The exit code is the documented, scriptable contract of `kc.sh update-compatibility check` (see docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc). Any existing automation or operator logic that treats exit code 4 as "recreate upgrade required" will now interpret a "feature disabled" outcome as a recreate request, and will treat the new recreate code 3 as an unknown failure. If the code numbering must change, consider keeping 4 as recreate and using a new free code (e.g. 5) for the disabled-feature case, or at least call this break out explicitly in the release/upgrade notes.

title: Feature-disabled path only covered for `metadata`, exit code not asserted
body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only runs `update-compatibility metadata` without the feature and asserts the console message. The newly introduced exit code `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` (4) is never asserted, and the `check` subcommand's disabled-feature path (the one consumers script against) is not covered at all. Since the whole point of the new code is scriptability, a regression in the returned exit code (or in the `check` guard) would go unnoticed.

title: `rolling-updates` feature is not enabled for the default (null) update strategy cases
body: `createInitialDeployment` returns early when `updateStrategy == null`, so the `ROLLING_UPDATES` feature is only added to the CR for the `RECREATE` parameterization. Both parameterized tests (`testImageChange(null)`, `testCacheMaxCount(null)`) therefore exercise the update logic with the preview feature disabled, while the new documentation states the Operator will fail when `rolling-updates` is not enabled. Either the default-strategy cases should also enable the feature (so they match the documented supported configuration), or the asymmetry deserves an explicit comment/assertion that the legacy path intentionally works without the feature.

title: setEnabledFeatures overwrites any pre-existing enabled features in the test CR
body: The code guards against a null `FeatureSpec` but then calls `setEnabledFeatures(List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES))` unconditionally, replacing whatever list was already present in the deployment produced by `getTestKeycloakDeployment(true)`. If the base test CR ever enables another feature, it will be silently dropped here and the test will run against a different server configuration than intended (and could mismatch the build-time features baked into the custom image). Appending to the existing list would be safer.

title: Exit code 4 description is wrong for the `metadata` command
body: The exit-code table describes 4 as "Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled." but the same code is also returned by `update-compatibility metadata` (see UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run), where nothing about an upgrade was evaluated and no metadata was written. The wording should say the command aborted because the `rolling-updates` feature is disabled, so users don't misread a failed metadata generation as a compatibility verdict.

title: Recreate exit code silently changed from 4 to 3 and 4 reused for a different meaning
body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` is changed from `4` to `3`, and `4` is now reused for the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` result. Any existing consumer (user automation/CI pipelines built on the documented exit code, and the Keycloak Operator logic that inspects the exit code of the `update-compatibility check` run) that interprets `4` as "recreate upgrade required" will now interpret a *feature-disabled* failure as a recreate decision, and will no longer recognize a real recreate decision (`3`). This PR contains no corresponding change on the Operator/consumer side, so if the Operator hardcodes the old value the update strategy decision becomes wrong. At minimum the renumbering should be called out as a breaking change, and the Operator path that reads this code has to be verified/updated.

title: New feature-gate exit code and the renumbered recreate exit code are not asserted
body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error text and never asserts `exitCode() == 4` (`CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED`). There is also no test for `update-compatibility check` with the feature disabled, and no test asserts the new recreate exit code `3` (the `testWrongVersions` test only checks the printed message). Since the exit codes are the documented, script-facing contract of these commands (and were just renumbered in this PR), a regression in any of them would go undetected.

title: Test overwrites any pre-existing enabled features and only enables the flag for non-default strategies
body: `setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))` replaces the whole enabled-features list rather than appending, so if `getTestKeycloakDeployment()` ever sets features in the spec they are silently dropped (the preceding `getFeatureSpec() == null` guard suggests the intent was to preserve existing content). Additionally the feature is only enabled when `updateStrategy != null`, so the default (unset) strategy path runs without the `rolling-updates` feature; if the Operator is supposed to require the feature for the update logic (as the new operator docs claim), that path is untested, and if it is not required, the docs are wrong.

title: CAUTION overstates that rolling-updates must be enabled for all update strategies
body: The new CAUTION block states that while in preview the `rolling-updates` feature "must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail", but the NOTE immediately below describes the default (strategy not set) behaviour which mimics Keycloak 26.1 and does not require the feature — and the operator test only enables the feature for the non-default strategies. As written, users are told to enable a preview feature even when they are relying on the default behaviour. The caution should be scoped to the cases where the feature is actually required (i.e. when `spec.update.strategy` is used).

title: Exit code 4 description is misleading
body: Exit code 4 is documented as "Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled." In reality the command refuses to run at all and produces no compatibility verdict (see `printFeatureDisabled()`/`FEATURE_DISABLED`): no metadata is written and no comparison happens. Describing it as a rolling-upgrade verdict can lead script authors to treat it as a valid "recreate required" answer instead of a configuration error that must be fixed.

title: Exit-code contract changed: 4 no longer means "recreate required"
body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` is changed from 4 to 3 and 4 is reused for the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` result. These constants are the documented, scriptable contract of `kc.sh update-compatibility check` (the guide explicitly tells users to rely only on the exit code). Any existing consumer that hardcodes 4 as "recreate upgrade needed" – including automation pipelines and any operator/job code that inspects the terminated container's exit code – will now silently interpret "the rolling-updates feature is disabled" as "perform a recreate upgrade", and will no longer recognise a real recreate result (3). No non-documentation consumer was updated in this PR; please confirm every reader of these codes uses the constants, and consider picking an unused code (e.g. 5) for the new condition instead of recycling 4.

title: Documented update-compatibility command appends --features, overriding the user's feature set
body: The `updatecompatibility` macro now renders every command in the Update Compatibility guide as `bin/kc.sh update-compatibility <sub> ... --features=rolling-updates`. `--features` is a single, replacing list, not additive, so a user who copies this command loses all other features they have configured (via `KC_FEATURES`, keycloak.conf or the image build). Since the guide simultaneously warns that "omitting any configuration options will result in incomplete metadata", the documented command produces metadata for a different feature set than the running deployment. In addition, `features` is a build-time option, so for an optimized distribution/image passing it on the CLI is rejected or forces re-augmentation. The guide should instruct users to add `rolling-updates` to their existing feature list (or enable it at build time) rather than show a bare `--features=rolling-updates`.

title: New FEATURE_DISABLED exit code is not covered by tests
body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the stderr text and only for the `metadata` subcommand. The newly introduced exit code 4 (`CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED`), which is now part of the documented contract and which also collides with the previous meaning of exit code 4 (recreate upgrade), is never asserted; neither is the feature-disabled path of the `check` subcommand. Also no test asserts the new recreate exit code 3. A future renumbering or a regression in the feature gate would not be caught. Add assertions on `exitCode()` for both subcommands with the feature disabled, and for the recreate result.

title: Operator CAUTION about required feature is overbroad/ambiguous
body: The new CAUTION states unconditionally that "the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail." That contradicts the behaviour exercised by `UpgradeTest`, which enables the feature only when `spec.update.strategy` is set and still runs successfully (default/unset strategy) without the feature. As written, readers will think the feature is mandatory for every Keycloak CR managed by the Operator. The text should state precisely when the feature is required (e.g. only when `spec.update` is used) and what "fail" means (CR in error status, reconciliation error).

title: Test replaces instead of appending the CR's enabled features
body: `setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))` unconditionally overwrites whatever `spec.features.enabled` the base test deployment provides. If the shared test CR template ever enables another feature, it is silently dropped here and the test would exercise a different configuration than intended (or fail for an unrelated reason). The existing list should be read and extended with `rolling-updates`.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs, not group IDs
body:
In `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` the code iterates authz resources of type `Groups` and (a) calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and (b) adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set. For group resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource`, the *resource name* is the group ID; the resource ID is an unrelated UUID. Consequently:

1. `hasPermission(resource.getId(), ...)` does `resourceStore.findByName(server, <resource UUID>)`, which never matches, so evaluation silently falls back to the "all groups" resource instead of evaluating the individual group.
2. The returned set contains resource UUIDs, while the only consumers (`UsersResource.searchForUser`/`getUsersCount` and `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser`, which put the set in `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)` and pass it to `UserProvider.getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)`) expect group IDs.

Result: when an admin's only access to users comes from group `view-members`/`manage-members` permissions, the user search/count is filtered by non-existent group IDs and returns nothing (or, when the set is empty, the DB query is not restricted at all and the admin may see an empty page because filtering happens after pagination). The V1 implementation correctly derived the group ID from the resource name (`resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())`). The set should contain `groupResource.getName()` and the permission check should be done with the resource name/group ID.

title: canManage() grants management rights to admins that only have the view scope
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` (the no-argument variant) returns `true` when the caller has either `AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW` or `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` on the `Groups` resource type. `canManage()` is used by `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` via `auth.groups().requireManage()`, so an administrator who was only granted the `view` scope on all groups can create top-level groups. This is a privilege escalation: the `view` scope must not satisfy a manage check. Only `MANAGE` should be accepted here (as in `canManage(GroupModel)`). Note that the new test `testViewGroups` only grants `VIEW` and never asserts that write operations stay forbidden, so this escalation is untested.

title: NullPointerException when the "Groups" resource-type resource does not exist
body: In `hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes)`, when no resource is found for the group the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and then immediately dereferences the result (`policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and `resource.getScopes()`), without a null check. `getResourceTypeResource` returns `null` whenever `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false (e.g. the realm has an admin-permissions client but `adminPermissionsEnabled` is false) or when the resource named `Groups` simply does not exist. The latter is reachable in practice: `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` returns early if the admin permissions client already exists, so realms that enabled FGAP v2 before the `Groups` resource type was added never get the `Groups` resource or the new `manage-membership`/`manage-members`/`view-members` scopes. Any group permission check in such a realm then fails with a NPE (HTTP 500) instead of a clean deny. Add a null guard (and consider a migration/upgrade path for already-initialized admin permission clients).

title: Scope loop does not verify that the granted permission belongs to the evaluated resource
body: The result loop in `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission` accepts any returned `Permission` whose scope list intersects the expected scopes, without checking `permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId())`. The analogous `UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission` (same file layout, line ~123) explicitly performs that check, which indicates the evaluation result can contain permissions for resources other than the one being evaluated (e.g. resource-type level resources). Without the check, access to one group resource can be granted by a permission evaluated for a different resource. Please align the two implementations.

title: V1 group permission management breaks when both FGAP v1 and v2 features are enabled
body:
`MgmtPermissionsV2` now overrides `groups()` to return `GroupPermissionsV2`, whose `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions` and `*Permission` methods all throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. `AdminPermissions.management(session, realm)` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` as soon as `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled, independently of `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ`. Therefore, with both preview features enabled:

- `AdminPermissions.registerListener` (registered because v1 is enabled) handles `GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent` by calling `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)` → `UnsupportedOperationException`, so deleting any group fails with an internal server error.
- `GroupResource.getManagementPermissions()` / `setManagementPermissionsEnabled()` (guarded only by the v1 feature flag) call `permissions.groups().isPermissionsEnabled(...)` / `setPermissionsEnabled(...)` → HTTP 500 instead of the previous behaviour.

Before this change `MgmtPermissionsV2` inherited the working V1 `GroupPermissions` for these management operations. Either keep returning the V1 management implementation for these paths or make the listener/endpoints v2-aware.

title: getResourceName has no branch for the new Groups resource type
body: `getResourceName` resolves human-readable names only for the `Users` resource type (`All users` or the username) and otherwise falls back to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Group resources are created in `getOrCreateResource` with only a name (the group ID) and no display name, so permissions scoped to a single group will be reported with a `null` name in the policy/permission representation shown in the admin console. A `Groups` branch is needed that returns `All groups` for the resource-type resource and the group name/path for an individual group (and that handles a stale resource whose group no longer exists).

title: switch on resourceType throws NullPointerException for a null resource type
body: `getOrCreateResource` now does `switch (resourceType) { case CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE -> ... default -> throw new IllegalStateException(...) }`. A Java `switch` over a `String` throws `NullPointerException` when the selector is null, so callers that pass a null resource type now get an unhandled NPE (HTTP 500) instead of the previous `IllegalStateException("Could not map resource object ...")`/validation error. Add an explicit null check before the switch so the failure surfaces as a validation error.

title: Javadoc of requireManageMembers and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission is wrong
body: The Javadoc added for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` says it throws `ForbiddenException` if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false, but the implementation checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)` — the copy/pasted reference documents the wrong contract. Likewise, the Javadoc of `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (line 145) says "@return Stream of IDs of groups" while the method returns a `Set<String>`. Both should be corrected since this interface is the contract documentation for the new FGAP evaluators.

title: Removal of the global view short-circuit causes a policy evaluation per group
body: `getGroups` previously computed `boolean canViewGlobal = groupsEvaluator.canView()` once and only fell back to the per-group check when the global check failed; the same pattern was removed from `GroupResource.getSubGroups`. Now `canView(g)` is invoked for every group in the result. With FGAP v2 that means, for an admin without the `view-users`/`manage-users` roles, one `resourceStore.findByName` lookup plus a full authorization policy evaluation per returned group even when a single "all groups" view permission already grants access. For realms with large group lists this multiplies the cost of the group listing endpoints; consider restoring a cheap global short-circuit.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authorization Resource IDs, not group IDs, and evaluates the wrong resource
body:
The method iterates over authorization resources of type "Groups" and (a) calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and (b) adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set.

Both are wrong:
- `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` resolves the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. Group resources are created with the *group id as their name* (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`/`getOrCreateResource`), so passing a Resource *id* never matches; the lookup returns null and the code silently falls back to the schema-wide "Groups" resource. Per-group `view-members`/`manage-members` permissions are therefore never detected here.
- The set returned is contractually a set of *group* ids (it is fed into `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)` in `UsersResource.searchForUser`/`BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` and into `session.users().getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)`). Resource ids do not match any group, so the DB-level restriction matches no users at all.

In addition, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)` for the per-object resources it creates, so `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups")` only returns the single schema-wide "Groups" resource and not the individual group resources at all.

Consequence: user listing/count restricted by group membership is broken under FGAP v2 – either no users are returned for admins whose only access is `view-members` on a group (when the attribute gets set with bogus ids) or the DB query is not restricted at all. The method should use `groupResource.getName()` (the group id) for both the permission check and the returned set, and the resources must be created with the proper type.

title: canManage() grants manage access to admins that only have the 'view' scope on all groups
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` (the no-argument variant) evaluates `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it returns true when the caller merely has the `view` scope on the "Groups" resource type. `canManage()`/`requireManage()` is what guards `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup`, so an admin granted only a read-only all-groups `view` permission can create top-level groups. Only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` should be accepted here (the `canView()` variant above already covers view/manage). Note the new Javadoc in `GroupPermissionEvaluator#canManage()` documents this behaviour, so the doc needs fixing too, and there is no test asserting that a view-only permission cannot create/modify groups.

title: Possible NullPointerException when the schema-wide 'Groups' resource cannot be resolved
body: In `hasPermission`, when no per-group resource is found the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. That method returns `null` when the realm does not support the authorization schema (e.g. `realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled()` is false while the admin-permissions client still exists) or when the resource is simply absent from the store. The returned value is used immediately in `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and `resource.getScopes()` without a null check, which will throw a NullPointerException and surface as a 500 on ordinary admin endpoints (group listing, group update, user search). Add a null check and return `false`.

title: getResourceName() does not resolve names for the new Groups resource type
body: `getResourceName` only special-cases `USERS`; for the newly added `Groups` resource type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Group resources are created by `getOrCreateResource` with the group id as the resource *name* and no display name is ever set, so this returns `null` for every group-scoped permission. Any caller rendering permission resources (e.g. the admin console listing a scope permission's resources) will show `null`/empty instead of the group name or "All groups". A `GROUPS` branch analogous to the `USERS` one (resolving the group by id, returning "All groups" for the type resource) is needed.

title: switch on resourceType throws NullPointerException for a null resource type
body: The new `switch (resourceType)` dereferences `resourceType`, so a null resource type now produces a raw NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of the previous behaviour where `name` stayed null and the explicit `IllegalStateException("Could not map resource object with type [...]")` was thrown. `getOrCreateResource` is reachable from policy/permission creation paths; guard against null (or use the existing validation message) to keep the error actionable.

title: Javadoc of requireManageMembers() references the wrong method
body: The Javadoc on `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` states it throws ForbiddenException if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false, but the implementation checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)` (a different scope: `manage-members` vs `manage-membership`). This is copy-pasted from the method above and will mislead implementers of the interface. Similarly, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` documents "@return Stream of IDs" while it returns a `Set<String>`.

title: Removal of the global-view short circuit causes a policy evaluation per (sub)group under FGAP v2
body: `getSubGroups` previously hoisted `auth.groups().canView()` out of the stream and only fell back to the per-group check when the caller had no global view rights; the same change was made in `GroupsResource.getGroups`. `GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)` does not short-circuit on an all-groups permission, so for an admin whose access comes from an all-groups `view` permission every element now triggers a `findByName` lookup plus a full policy evaluation. For groups with many children (and for group listings) this multiplies the authorization evaluations by the number of groups on the page/stream. Consider caching the all-groups decision per request as before.

title: canManage() grants group-management rights to admins that only have the `view` scope
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns `true` when the caller has either `AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW` **or** `MANAGE` on the all-groups resource. `canManage()` (no argument) is the check behind `GroupPermissionEvaluator.requireManage()`, which `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` uses to authorize group creation. Consequently an admin granted only a read-only `view` permission on `Groups` can create top-level groups, a privilege escalation. The group-scoped variant `canManage(GroupModel)` correctly requires only `MANAGE`, confirming `VIEW` here is a copy/paste mistake. There is also no test asserting that a `view`-only permission is rejected for write operations (`testViewGroups` only exercises reads), so the bug is not caught.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses authorization Resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: Group resources in the FGAP v2 schema are stored with `name == group.getId()` (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`/`getOrCreateResource`), while `Resource.getId()` is a separate generated UUID. This method (a) calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`, and `hasPermission` resolves the argument via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, so the lookup always misses and the evaluation silently falls back to the all-groups resource — per-group `view-members`/`manage-members` permissions are therefore never detected here; and (b) adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set, whereas callers (`UsersResource.searchForUser` via `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)`, and `UsersResource.getUsersCount(..., groupIds)`) expect group IDs and match them against group membership. Result: `GET /users/count` returns 0 (or wrong values) for an admin whose only visibility comes from group `view-members` permissions, inconsistent with `GET /users`, and the group-id filter pushed into the user query can never match. The V1 implementation correctly uses `resource.getName()`. Note also that `findByType(server, "Groups", ...)` returns the all-groups resource itself, whose name is `"Groups"` and is not a group ID, so it would be added to the set as a bogus group ID if an all-groups permission exists.

title: Possible NullPointerException when the all-groups resource cannot be resolved
body: In `hasPermission`, when no per-group resource is found the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`, which returns `null` if the realm does not support the authorization schema (e.g. `realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled() == false`) or if the `Groups` resource does not exist (realms whose admin-permissions client was created before this change). The returned value is used without a null check in `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and `resource.getScopes()`, producing an NPE / HTTP 500 on ordinary admin endpoints (group listing, user search) instead of a clean `false`. Note `MgmtPermissionsV2` is selected purely on the `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` feature flag, so a realm with the feature on but admin permissions turned off (while the admin-permissions client still exists) reaches this path.

title: No cleanup of group authorization resources/permissions when a group is deleted under FGAP v2
body: `AdminPermissions.registerListener` only registers the `GroupRemovedEvent` handler when the v1 `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature is enabled, and `GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` anyway. With the new Groups resource type, deleting a group leaves the authorization `Resource` named with the group id plus every scope permission referencing it orphaned in the admin-permissions client forever. Beyond growing stale data, these orphan entries show up when listing permissions/resources in the admin API (where `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName` cannot resolve them) and must be deleted manually. A removal hook (analogous to the v1 listener) should delete the group resource and its permissions.

title: getResourceName() not extended for the new Groups resource type
body: `getResourceName` resolves friendly names only for `USERS` ("All users" / username). With `GROUPS` now a supported resource type, permissions created for a group resource fall through to `return resource.getDisplayName()`, which is `null` for resources created by `getOrCreateResource` (created with name only). As a result the admin API/console shows `null` instead of the group name (or "All groups") for group-scoped permissions, which is the exact problem the Users branch was added to solve.

title: No migration path: existing admin-permissions clients never get the Groups resource and group scopes
body: `init()` returns early when `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null`, so realms that already enabled FGAP v2 before this change keep an admin-permissions client without the `Groups` resource and without the new `manage-membership`, `manage-members`, `view-members` scopes. In such realms creating a group permission fails in `getOrCreateResource` with `ModelException("No scopes found.")` (the scope lookup at line 125 returns null) and `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission` gets a null all-groups resource. Either a migration that adds the missing resource/scopes or lazy creation is needed.

title: switch on resourceType throws NullPointerException for a null resource type
body: The new `switch (resourceType)` dereferences `resourceType`; a `null` value now produces an NPE (HTTP 500) whereas the previous `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` chain fell through to the explicit `IllegalStateException("Could not map resource object ...")`. `getOrCreateResource` is reachable for policy representations other than `ScopePermissionRepresentation` (which is the only type validated by `throwExceptionIfResourceTypeOrScopesNotProvided`), so a request without `resourceType` can hit this. Guard for null and throw the validation error instead.

title: Removal of the global canView() short-circuit causes per-group policy evaluation under FGAP v2
body: `stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)` (and the same change in `GroupResource.getSubGroups`) no longer computes the realm-wide `canView()` once. With `GroupPermissionsV2`, each group in the page triggers `resourceStore.findByName`, `getResourceTypeResource`, `policyStore.findByResource` and a full policy evaluation — i.e. several DB round trips and an authz evaluation per group even for an admin holding a single all-groups `view` permission. For realms with many groups this is a measurable regression on group listing; the previous code evaluated the global permission once and skipped per-item evaluation.

title: Feature check moved from event time to listener-registration time
body: `registerListener` now evaluates `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` once, when the provider event listener is registered during factory initialization, instead of on each event. If the profile is not yet fully resolved at registration time (or registration happens before feature configuration), the listener is never registered and role/client/group permission cleanup on removal silently stops working for the whole server lifetime, with no error. Keeping the check inside `onEvent` (or asserting profile availability at registration) avoids this ordering dependency.

title: Javadoc on requireManageMembers / getGroupIdsWithViewPermission is wrong
body: The javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` states it throws when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false, but the implementation checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)` — a copy/paste error that misleads implementors of the interface. Additionally `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is documented as returning a "Stream of IDs" while it returns a `Set<String>`.

title: Removal of public static ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes breaks compiled extensions
body: `public static Stream<GroupModel> searchGroupModelsByAttributes(...)` is deleted outright. Although it lives in `server-spi-private`, that module is compiled against by custom providers; any extension calling this helper will fail with `NoSuchMethodError` after upgrade. If removal is intended, deprecate-and-delegate (or at least note the removal in upgrade docs) rather than removing in the same release.

title: Java ChoiceFormat / single-brace placeholders break i18next message in account UI
body: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. This file is consumed by the React/i18next based account console, where interpolation uses the double-brace syntax (see `backTo=Back to {{app}}` on line 3 and `error-invalid-length='{{0}}' must have a length between {{1}} and {{2}}.` on line 140). Single-brace placeholders are not interpolated by i18next, and `{2,choice,...}` is Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax that i18next cannot evaluate, so the user will see the literal text `{0}`, `{1}` and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` instead of the actual limits and pluralized word.

title: Java ChoiceFormat syntax introduced into admin UI i18next bundle
body: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` now uses `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` plus a Java ChoiceFormat expression `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`. The admin console translates these keys with i18next (double-brace interpolation, as used by the other `{{0}}`-style error keys in this bundle), which neither substitutes single-brace placeholders nor understands ChoiceFormat. The message will be rendered verbatim to administrators, including the raw choice expression.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: `totpStep1` was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` which is Italian, not Lithuanian. The same Italian sentence was also introduced into `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` (`loginTotpStep1`). Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction on the OTP setup pages; the previous Lithuanian wording should be kept (minus the hard-coded app links that this PR removes elsewhere).

title: Simplified Chinese file given Traditional Chinese text
body: `totpStep1` was set to `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`, which is Traditional Chinese (手機/應用程式) and belongs in `messages_zh_TW.properties`. This file is the zh_CN (Simplified) bundle; the text should read e.g. `在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：`.

title: Malformed character class makes English-file path derivation match too much
body: `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` contains the class `[a-zA-Z-_]`, where the trailing `-_` is parsed by java.util.regex as the range 0x2D..0x5F. That range covers `-`, `.`, `/`, digits, `:` and all upper-case letters, so the pattern can match far beyond the file name: for an absolute path that contains an underscore in any parent directory (e.g. a CI workspace like `/build_dir/keycloak/themes/.../messages_de.properties`) the greedy match starts at that earlier underscore and the whole path segment chain is replaced, producing a bogus English path and an immediate build failure. Escape the dash (`[a-zA-Z_-]`) and/or derive the sibling file from `File#getName()` only.

title: Missing English counterpart aborts the build with an opaque RuntimeException
body: If the derived `_en.properties` file does not exist (community-only bundles, base `messages.properties` files whose name does not match the locale regex, or any path-derivation mistake), `verifySafeHtml` throws a raw `RuntimeException`. `verify()` only catches `IOException`, so this escapes the Mojo as an unhandled runtime exception instead of a `MojoExecutionException` or a collected verification message, giving maintainers a stack trace rather than an actionable error.

title: Diff substring can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException while reporting a violation
body: The common-prefix (`start`) and common-suffix (`end`) counters are computed independently and can overlap when the sanitized string differs in length from the input (the sanitizer regularly adds characters, e.g. missing close tags). For example value="aba" and sanitized="abba" yields start=2 and end=2, so `value.substring(2, 3-2)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The verifier then crashes with an index error instead of reporting the illegal HTML it just detected. Clamp the indices so that `start + end <= min(value.length(), sanitized.length())`.

title: Anchor-mismatch message does not identify the file or key
body: The message `"Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string"` omits both the properties file and the message key, unlike the HTML violation message a few lines above which includes `key` and `file`. Since the plugin runs over hundreds of bundles, a contributor seeing only this line cannot tell which translation needs fixing.

title: No test asserts that valid translations produce no findings
body: All four tests only assert that a violation message is present. There is no test feeding a legitimate translation (e.g. a `_de` file containing the same `<b>`/`<a href="...">` markup as its `_en` counterpart, or a message with a `{n,choice,...}` pattern) and asserting the result list is empty. Without such a case, false positives introduced by the normalization logic (unescaping, `<!-- -->` stripping, choice-format whitelist) would go unnoticed and break the whole build.

title: Java MessageFormat/choice syntax used in an i18next resource bundle
body: This bundle is consumed by the account console through i18next, where placeholders must be written as `{{0}}` (see every other entry in this file, e.g. `error-username-invalid-character='{{0}}' contains invalid character.`). The key was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. i18next does not interpolate single braces and has no support for MessageFormat `choice`, so the user will now see the raw text including `{0}` and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` whenever a multivalued attribute fails size validation. The Java MessageFormat form is only correct for the server-side `themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/**` bundles.

title: Java MessageFormat/choice syntax used in an i18next resource bundle
body: Same problem as in the account-ui bundle: this file is loaded by the admin console via i18next, which interpolates `{{n}}` and does not understand MessageFormat `choice`. Replacing `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` with `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` makes the message render literally (placeholders and the choice expression visible to the admin) instead of being substituted.

title: Diff computation can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of reporting the problem
body:
The common-prefix length (`start`) and common-suffix length (`end`) are computed independently, so for strings that differ by a repeated substring they can overlap and `start > length - end`. Example: value `

x

` sanitizes to `

x

`; the prefix loop yields start=3 and the suffix loop yields end=8, so `sanitized.substring(3, 8 - 8)` = `substring(3, 0)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The Maven plugin then fails with an opaque runtime exception rather than emitting the intended "Illegal HTML in key ..." message. Clamp the indices (e.g. `end = Math.min(end, Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start)`).

title: Missing English counterpart aborts the build with a bare RuntimeException
body: `verifySafeHtml()` derives the English bundle path by string replacement and then opens it unconditionally; if the file does not exist (community-only theme/message directory with no `messages_en.properties` under `resources`, a bundle without a locale suffix where the regex does not match, or a newly added community locale) a `FileNotFoundException` is wrapped into a plain `RuntimeException`. The surrounding `verify()` already declares `MojoExecutionException` and wraps IO errors of the main file properly, so this path produces an inconsistent, hard build failure with no actionable message. Either skip the HTML check (or report a verification message) when the English bundle is absent, and throw `MojoExecutionException` otherwise.

title: Anchor verification is order-sensitive and mutates the string it is iterating
body: `santizeAnchors` pairs the n-th anchor tag of the translation with the n-th anchor tag of the English source and requires exact equality. A translation that legitimately reorders two links (English `... .. ... ..`, translation with the links swapped) is reported as "Didn't find anchor tag" even though it contains exactly the same tags, i.e. a false build failure. In addition, `value` is reassigned inside the loop while `matcher` keeps iterating the original snapshot, and the removal is done with `replaceFirst` on the *English* group, so the occurrence that is removed is not necessarily the one just matched. Compare the multiset of anchor tags instead of their positions.

title: Anchor failure message does not say which key or file is affected
body: The message added here is only "Didn't find anchor tag <a ...> in original string", while all other messages produced by this class include the key and the file name. With hundreds of message bundles being verified, a build failure with this text gives the contributor no way to locate the offending entry. Include `key` (already passed into the method but unused) and `file`.

title: Properties are read as ISO-8859-1 while Keycloak theme bundles are UTF-8
body: `new PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream)` is specified to decode the stream as ISO-8859-1. The theme bundles checked here (Arabic, Chinese, Greek, Ukrainian, ...) are stored as UTF-8, and the server reads them as UTF-8, so every non-ASCII value is mojibake inside the verifier. The consequence is that the "Illegal HTML in key ... : '<x>' vs '<y>'" diagnostics printed for those locales are garbled and hard to act on, and any future check that depends on the real characters would be wrong. Use `new PropertyResourceBundle(new InputStreamReader(fis, StandardCharsets.UTF_8))` (same for the English bundle) to match how the files are actually encoded.

title: Purely cosmetic serialization differences are reported as "Illegal HTML"
body:
The check compares the translation byte-for-byte with the sanitizer's re-serialized output, so differences that are not security relevant (the sanitizer emits `
`, so every `
` in a bundle fails; likewise attribute quoting/order or added whitespace) are reported with the message "Illegal HTML in key ... for file ...". This is why ~20 unrelated locale files in this PR had to be rewritten from `
` to `
`, and future contributors will get a misleading "Illegal HTML" error for valid markup. Either normalize both sides before comparing, or reword the message so it distinguishes "tag not allowed" from "formatting differs from canonical form".

title: containsHtml only detects lower-case tag names
body:
`HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` is case sensitive, so an English source value written with upper/mixed case markup (e.g. `
` or ``) is classified as containing no HTML. The translation is then validated with POLICY_NO_HTML and every tag it contains is reported as illegal, producing a false failure. Compile the pattern with `CASE_INSENSITIVE`.

title: No test asserts that a valid bundle produces no findings
body:
All four tests only assert `hasItem(...)` on the returned list, so nothing verifies the absence of false positives: there is no fixture where a translation legitimately keeps the HTML of an English source that contains HTML (e.g. ``/`
`/an unchanged ``), nor a case with MessageFormat `choice` or `{{...}}` placeholders, and no assertion that `verify()` returns an empty list for such a file. Given that the new sanitizer compares the exact serialized form, a regression that starts flagging every valid bundle would not be caught by this suite. Also note the assertions were relaxed from `Matchers.contains` to `Matchers.hasItem`, so additional unexpected messages are now silently accepted.

title: Lithuanian bundle now contains Italian text
body: `totpStep1` was replaced with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users of the account console will see an Italian sentence on the OTP setup page. The same wrong-language string was introduced in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` (`loginTotpStep1`). If the old value had to be changed because it contained links, it should be translated to Lithuanian (or left to the translators) rather than copied from the Italian bundle.

title: Traditional Chinese text added to the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) bundle
body: `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese characters and Taiwanese terminology (手機/應用程式) and appears to be copied from the zh_TW bundle. In a zh_CN bundle it should read something like `在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`; as it stands, Simplified Chinese users get a Traditional Chinese sentence.

title: Java MessageFormat choice/placeholder syntax introduced into an i18next-consumed message bundle
body: This file is consumed by the account console (i18next), where parameters are interpolated with the `{{n}}` syntax – every other parameterized key in this file uses it (e.g. `error-invalid-length='{{0}}' must have a length between {{1}} and {{2}}.`). The new value `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` uses Java `MessageFormat` single-brace placeholders plus a `choice` format, neither of which i18next understands. As a result the user will see the literal text `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` instead of actual values. The previous `{{0}} ... value(s)` form worked; only the server-side (Java) bundles should use choice formats.

title: Admin console message switched to Java MessageFormat syntax that i18next cannot render
body: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. This bundle is rendered by the admin console through i18next, which interpolates `{{n}}` (see neighbouring keys such as `error-invalid-length` in the same file) and has no support for `MessageFormat` choice formats. The message will be displayed with raw `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` and the whole `{2,choice,...}` block visible to administrators.

title: Diff trimming can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException while reporting a violation
body:
The common-prefix (`start`) and common-suffix (`end`) scans are independent, so the two regions can overlap and `start + end` can exceed the length of `value` or `sanitized`. `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` then fails with StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. A concrete example: value `x

y` sanitized to `x
y` gives start=5, end=5, so `sanitized.substring(5, 1)` throws. Instead of a readable "Illegal HTML in key ..." message the plugin crashes with an unrelated runtime exception, hiding the actual problem. Clamp `end` to `min(len) - start` before building the substrings.

title: Missing English reference bundle aborts the build with an opaque RuntimeException
body: The English counterpart path is derived purely by string replacement (`resources-community` -> `resources`, `_<locale>.properties` -> `_en.properties`). If that file does not exist (community-only theme/locale layout, a bundle whose name does not follow the `_xx.properties` convention, or a locale containing digits which the `[a-zA-Z-_]*` class does not match), the constructor throws an unchecked RuntimeException out of `verify()`, which declares `MojoExecutionException`. The Maven run then fails with a raw stack trace rather than a diagnosable plugin error, and the file is not verified. Either skip verification when no reference bundle exists or wrap the failure in MojoExecutionException with the computed path.

title: Anchor-mismatch error message does not identify the file or key
body: `messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string")` omits both the properties file and the message key, unlike the HTML message a few lines below which includes them. With hundreds of bundles verified in one build, a contributor cannot tell which translation to fix. The already-passed `key` parameter is unused; include it and `file` in the message.

title: Unescaping HTML entities turns safe escaped markup into reported violations
body: `normalizeValue` runs `unescapeHtml4` on the raw property value, so a translation that deliberately contains escaped markup (e.g. `<div>`) becomes real markup before sanitization. The sanitizer strips it and the key is then reported as "Illegal HTML" even though the original value is harmless literal text. This produces false positives that contributors can only work around by rewording the message.

title: Verification compares sanitizer output verbatim, flagging harmless HTML formatting as illegal
body:
The check requires the message to be byte-identical to the OWASP sanitizer's re-serialized output. Semantically identical markup that the sanitizer normalizes differently (for example `
` vs `
`, attribute quoting/order, or whitespace inside tags) is reported as "Illegal HTML", which is both misleading and brittle – this is why ~20 translation files in this PR had to be rewritten from `
` to `
`. Any future contribution using the other spelling will fail CI with a security-sounding error. Consider comparing the set of allowed elements/attributes, or normalizing both sides through the sanitizer before comparison.

title: Italian text inserted into the Lithuanian bundle
body: `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, not Lithuanian. The previous Lithuanian sentence was replaced (presumably copied from the Italian bundle while removing the `<a href=...>` links). Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction on the OTP setup page. The same problem was introduced in `theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` (`loginTotpStep1`).

title: Italian text inserted into the Lithuanian login bundle
body: `loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian text in the Lithuanian login messages. It replaces the former Lithuanian sentence, so the OTP setup screen for the `lt` locale now shows Italian.

title: Traditional Chinese text placed in the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) bundle
body: `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese wording/characters (手機, 應用程式) and appears to have been copied from the zh_TW bundle, while this file is zh_CN (Simplified). Simplified-Chinese users will see Traditional characters on the OTP setup page; the Simplified equivalent is e.g. `在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：`.

title: No test asserting that valid messages produce no findings
body: All four tests only assert that a violation is reported. Nothing verifies the negative case: that a bundle whose translation legitimately contains the allowed elements (`br`, `p`, `strong`, `b`), the same anchor as the English source, placeholders such as `{0}`/`{{0}}`, or a `{n,choice,...}` block yields an empty message list. Given how much special-casing `normalizeValue`/`santizeAnchors` contain, false positives (which would break the whole themes build) are the most likely regression and are currently untested.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher never checks the grant shortcut (inverted condition + wrong indices)
body: The new matcher is supposed to verify that an access-token ID looks like `<sessionType><tokenType><grantType>:<uuid>` and that the grant part equals `expectedGrantShortcut`. Two defects make it a no-op: (1) the condition is inverted – `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` fails when the shortcut matches and passes when it does not; (2) the offsets are wrong – the encoded prefix is 6 chars with the grant shortcut at indices 4-6 (`substring(4, 6)`), while `substring(3, 5)` reads one char of the token-type and one of the grant-type. For the real value "onrtac" the extracted text is "ta", never equal to e.g. "ac", so the check always falls through to the UUID assertion. As a result all the converted assertions (`expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectAuthReqIdToToken`) silently accept any grant shortcut and the feature introduced by this PR is effectively untested.

title: New abstract method getShortcut() on public SPI interface breaks existing grant-type providers
body: `getShortcut()` is added to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` without a `default` implementation. Any third-party/custom OAuth2 grant type provider compiled against a previous version will no longer compile, and an already-deployed jar will fail at runtime with `AbstractMethodError` as soon as `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` iterates all grant factories and calls `getShortcut()`, which happens during server startup. Consider providing a `default` implementation (e.g. derived from the id, or returning null handled gracefully) to keep the SPI backwards compatible.

title: postInit() can fail with NPE and silently accepts colliding shortcuts registered later
body: In `postInit()` the shortcut returned by a grant factory is put directly into a `ConcurrentHashMap`. A custom (or future) factory returning `null` from `getShortcut()` makes `grantsByShortcuts.put(null, grantName)` throw a `NullPointerException`, aborting server startup with an obscure error instead of a meaningful validation message. In addition, the duplicate-shortcut validation (size comparison) runs only in `postInit()`; the lazy refresh paths `getShortcutByGrantType()`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut()` (lines 106-137) overwrite existing entries without any duplicate check, so a dynamically deployed grant reusing an existing shortcut would silently corrupt the mapping and make token IDs decode to the wrong grant type. The two maps are also updated with two independent `put` calls, so a concurrent reader can observe one map updated and the other not.

title: Null check for rawTokenId actually re-checks grantType
body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` twice and never validates `rawTokenId`. A null `rawTokenId` therefore passes construction and later produces an encoded token id ending in the literal string "null" (`onrtac:null`), i.e. a corrupt `jti`, instead of failing fast at the point of the programming error. Should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

title: Access tokens issued for offline_access are encoded with session type "on" (online)
body: `createTokenResponse()` creates the access token (and thus the encoded session type) before `responseBuilder.generateRefreshToken()` converts/creates the offline session, and before the online user session is removed a few lines below (`session.sessions().removeUserSession(realm, userSession)` when the refresh token is of type offline). At the time `initToken()` runs, `userSession.isOffline()` is still false, so an access token obtained together with an offline refresh token gets the `on` (online) session-type prefix even though no online session exists afterwards. The same ordering exists in `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType`. Since the stated purpose of the encoding is to let endpoints look up only the session type recorded in the token, this will lead to failed/incorrect session lookups for offline tokens once consumers rely on the value.

title: Removal of Context copy constructor and new hard dependency on non-null formParams
body: The public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` is removed from this server-spi-private class; any subclass or extension code that used it (e.g. to wrap/derive a grant context) will no longer compile. At the same time the remaining constructor now dereferences `formParams` (`formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`), so callers that previously could pass `null` form params now get a `NullPointerException`. If the copy constructor must go, the change should be noted as a breaking SPI change, and the constructor should tolerate a null `formParams`.

title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of an unrelated NullPointerException
body: The test feeds the id "ofrtac:5678" whose shortcut "ac" is not in the hand-built map, so `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut()` falls into the lazy-refresh branch and dereferences `sessionFactory`, which is `null` because `postInit()` was never called in the test. The thrown `NullPointerException` is swallowed by `catch (RuntimeException iae)`, so the test is green while the intended `IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value ... for grant type")` path is never exercised. The assertion should be narrowed to `IllegalArgumentException` (and the factory properly initialised), otherwise a regression in the error handling would go unnoticed.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher reads the wrong characters and inverts the comparison
body: The new matcher is supposed to assert that the event's TOKEN_ID encodes the expected grant shortcut. The encoded prefix is 6 chars (2 for session type, 2 for token type, 2 for grant type), so the grant shortcut lives at indexes 4..6, but the code reads `items[0].substring(3, 5)` (e.g. for "onrtac" it extracts "ta" instead of "ac"). In addition the condition is inverted: `if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` fails the match when the grant shortcut *does* match and passes when it does not. The net effect is that all the converted assertions (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) silently validate nothing about the grant encoding, so a regression in the encoding would go unnoticed; and if the extracted substring ever happens to equal the expected shortcut the tests would fail for a correct token.

title: Null check for rawTokenId actually re-checks grantType
body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` duplicates the grantType check instead of validating `rawTokenId`. Consequently an `AccessTokenContext` can be built with a null raw token id, and `encodeTokenId()` will then produce an id like `onrtac:null` (string concatenation of null) which is silently written into the token's `jti`, instead of failing fast with a clear error at construction time.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI interface. Any existing third-party/deployed grant type factory that does not implement it will no longer compile, and pre-compiled providers will throw `AbstractMethodError` at server startup, because `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` invokes `getShortcut()` on every registered grant factory. Providing a `default` implementation (e.g. returning null / a derived value) and handling the null case in the encoder would avoid breaking existing extensions.

title: Public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) removed
body: The copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` is deleted from the `OAuth2GrantType.Context` class in server-spi-private. Custom grant type implementations (or any code outside this repository) that create a derived context by copying an existing one will fail to compile / throw NoSuchMethodError after upgrade. If the removal is intentional it should at least be called out as a breaking SPI change; otherwise keep it and copy the new `grantType` field as well.

title: Lazy grant/shortcut registration bypasses the duplicate-shortcut validation
body: `getShortcutByGrantType()` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut()` lazily add entries to `grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts` without re-running the duplicate detection performed in `postInit()`. If a grant type registered later (e.g. a dynamically deployed provider) reuses an existing shortcut, the mapping is silently overwritten, so `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` will decode previously issued tokens to the wrong grant type. The duplicate check should also be applied on the lazy path (or the collision logged/rejected).

title: Session type derived from clientSession.getUserSession() instead of the user session already available
body: `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` dereferences `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession()` without a null check. `TokenManager.initToken` already has the authoritative `UserSessionModel` as a parameter but does not pass it; for client sessions that are not (yet) attached to a user session this will NPE while building the access token, turning a token request into a 500. Passing the user session explicitly (or null-guarding and falling back to SessionType.UNKNOWN) would be safer.

title: Access token jti format change is not documented / no upgrade note
body: Access token ids (`jti`, and the `token_id` event detail) change from a plain UUID to `<6-char context>:<uuid>` (e.g. `onrtac:1f65761e-...`). This is an externally visible format change: clients, log pipelines or custom extensions that assume `jti` is a UUID (or that it contains no ':' character, e.g. when used in URLs or as a cache key) will break. The PR contains no documentation or upgrade/release note describing the new format and its stability guarantees.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring bounds
body: In `isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut)` the check is `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Two defects: (1) the grant shortcut occupies characters at index 4 and 5 of the encoded prefix (sessionType=0-1, tokenType=2-3, grantType=4-5), so the bounds must be `substring(4, 6)`, not `(3, 5)`; (2) the condition is inverted - the matcher should fail when the shortcut does NOT equal the expected one, i.e. `!equals(...)`. As written, the two bugs cancel out and every event with a well-formed token id passes regardless of the grant shortcut, so all the new `expectCodeToToken`/`expectRefresh`/`expectDeviceCodeToToken`/`expectAuthReqIdToToken` assertions verify nothing about the grant type (and would start failing with false negatives as soon as either half is fixed).

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method on the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI interface. Any third-party/custom grant type factory compiled against a previous release no longer satisfies the interface and will fail with `AbstractMethodError` (or not compile) once deployed - and because `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` iterates all grant factories and calls `getShortcut()`, the failure happens at server start. Providing a `default` implementation (e.g. deriving a shortcut or returning null and handling it) would keep the SPI backwards compatible.

title: Removal of Context copy constructor is a breaking change
body: The `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor was deleted from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. Subclasses outside this repository (and any code that wrapped a Context, e.g. token-exchange contexts) use it; after this change they can no longer compile/link, and there is no replacement that copies an existing Context. If the copy semantics are no longer needed internally, the constructor should still be kept (deprecated) or an equivalent copy path provided.

title: Context constructor now NPEs on null formParams
body: The constructor now dereferences `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`. Previously `formParams` was only stored, so a null value was tolerated by this constructor. Any caller constructing a Context without form parameters now gets a NullPointerException at construction time instead of later (or never). A null-guard (`formParams == null ? null : formParams.getFirst(...)`) would preserve the previous contract.

title: Null check validates grantType twice; rawTokenId is never validated
body: In the constructor, the fourth `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId`. Consequence: a null `rawTokenId` is accepted and the failure surfaces much later (e.g. a token id literally ending in "null" produced by `encodeTokenId`), and if `grantType` were null the thrown message would be misleading.

title: testIncorrectGrantType asserts nothing and masks a NullPointerException
body: The test decodes "ofrtac:5678" and only catches `RuntimeException`. Because the test factory is never `postInit`-ed, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.sessionFactory` is null, so `getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac")` throws a NullPointerException rather than the intended `IllegalArgumentException`. The test therefore passes for the wrong reason and does not verify the documented error behaviour; it also hides that the production lookup path dereferences `sessionFactory` unconditionally. Catch/assert `IllegalArgumentException` explicitly (and initialize `sessionFactory`).

title: Decoding throws IllegalArgumentException for any token id containing ':' in an unexpected format
body: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` treats any id containing ':' as encoded and then throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the prefix is not exactly 6 characters or if a shortcut is unknown. Token ids produced by a different/older encoder, by a custom `TokenContextEncoderProvider`, or by a federated/externally issued token could legitimately contain ':' and would cause an unhandled runtime exception (HTTP 500) in whatever endpoint decodes the id, instead of degrading to an UNKNOWN context like the no-colon case does. Also the message "Expected length of 6" refers to the prefix, not the token id that is printed, which is confusing.

title: Lazy shortcut cache refresh can NPE and bypasses duplicate-shortcut validation
body: `getShortcutByGrantType`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut` lazily insert into the `ConcurrentHashMap`s for grant types discovered after `postInit`. If a (custom) `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` returns null, `grantsByShortcuts.put(null, grantType)` throws NullPointerException; the same happens in `postInit`, failing server startup with an opaque error instead of a message naming the offending factory. In addition, the duplicate-shortcut consistency check performed in `postInit` is not applied on these lazy inserts, so a newly deployed grant with a colliding shortcut silently overwrites an existing mapping, making decoded grant types wrong.

title: Session type derived from clientSession.getUserSession() instead of the user session already available
body: `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` resolves the user session via `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession()` and immediately dereferences it. `TokenManager.initToken`, the only caller, already has a non-null `userSession` parameter it uses for exactly the same persistence-state check. For client session contexts whose client session is not (yet) attached to a user session this call yields a NullPointerException during access token creation. Passing/using the known `userSession` removes the risk and the redundant lookup.

title: Externally visible jti format change without upgrade documentation
body: Access token `jti` values change from a bare UUID to `<6-char prefix>:<uuid>` (and the same value is reported in the `token_id` event detail). Relying parties, log pipelines and tests that assume `jti` is a UUID (or validate its length/charset) will break. The PR contains no upgrading-guide/release-note entry describing this behaviour change or the new `tokenContextEncoder` SPI.

title: Recovery codes stored in user storage are never consumed / exhaustion is never detected
body: After a successful validation the authenticator now resolves the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(), which prefers the credential returned by the user-storage provider (getFederatedCredentialsStream). A federated credential model is rebuilt on every request from the raw code list, so its "next code" index and remaining-code counter are always reset: allCodesUsed() can never become true, the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action is never re-added, and the login form always asks for code #0 again. In addition, removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()) is called with an id that belongs to (or is null for) the user-storage credential, so it cannot delete anything from local storage. Practically this means a single recovery code can be replayed indefinitely for federated users, defeating the one-time-use property of recovery codes. Either the consumption must be delegated to the storage provider through a defined contract, or the codes must be kept (and marked used) in local storage.

title: Mock user storage validates recovery codes without consuming them
body: isValid() for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE matches the submitted code against the stored list and returns true, but never removes/marks the code as used and never updates the stored credential. The same code (and every other code) therefore stays valid forever. Since this provider is the reference implementation used by the new test, it encodes the wrong semantics for recovery codes (which must be single-use) and makes the test pass even though replay is possible.

title: getCredentials() can NPE and drops the credential id
body: `var myUser = getMyUser(user);` is dereferenced at line 235 without the null check used by every other method in this class (isConfiguredFor, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream), so a lookup for a user that is no longer present in the in-memory map throws a NullPointerException instead of returning an empty stream. Furthermore, the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel built by createFromValues() does not carry the stored credential id (myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()), so callers such as RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator (which calls removeStoredCredentialById(model.getId())) and the account/admin credential listing receive a credential with a null id and cannot reference or delete it.

title: User label and generation time are lost when codes are stored in user storage
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential() only passes type + JSON of raw codes to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(new UserCredentialModel("", type, json)). The fully populated RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel (user label entered in the required-action form, generatedAt timestamp, remaining code counter) is used only on the local-storage fallback path. For federated users this metadata is silently dropped, so the stored credential has no label/creation date and the account console cannot display the information the user supplied. The storage provider also has no way to know how many codes remain.

title: No verification or cleanup after delegating recovery-code creation to user storage
body: The method treats a `true` return from updateCredential() as success and then skips local creation entirely, without verifying that the credential is actually usable (unlike createOTPCredential, which calls isValid afterwards) and without removing any pre-existing local recovery-codes credential.
