When that happens a non-allowlisted project set will reuse the cached `True` of an allowlisted set (or vice versa), silently multiplying counts by the sample weight for projects that are not configured for upsampling. Use the actual sorted ids (or a cryptographic digest) in the key instead of `hash()`.

title: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is dead code and cannot actually invalidate the cache
body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere in the PR, although its docstring states it "should be called when the allowlist configuration changes to ensure cache consistency". It also cannot fulfil that promise: the cache key depends on an arbitrary project-id subset, so invalidating after an allowlist change would require enumerating every org/project-id combination that was ever queried. This leaves the misleading impression that stale cache entries are handled, when in practice they are not.

title: `upsampled_count` is exposed as a public discover function with no project gating
body: The new `SnQLFunction("upsampled_count", ...)` is registered without `private=True` (unlike the neighbouring internal functions), so any API consumer can now request `upsampled_count()` as a field/yAxis on arbitrary discover queries. The aggregate is `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`, which is only meaningful for error rows in allowlisted projects; for transactions or non-upsampled errors it will either error out on the missing/unset `sample_weight` column or return meaningless values, bypassing the allowlist checks in `error_upsampling.py` entirely. Mark it private so only the internal transformation can use it.

title: `upsampled_count` declares result type `number` although it returns an integer
body: The aggregate is wrapped in `toInt64`, and the function replaces `count()` (declared `default_result_type="integer"` elsewhere in this file), but it declares `default_result_type="number"`. The response `meta` will advertise a different field type than `count()` does, which changes client-side formatting/axis handling for the very charts this feature rewrites.

title: `upsampled_count` only registered for the discover dataset while the errors dataset path returns True
body: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` unconditionally returns True for `dataset == errors`, so `count()` will be rewritten to `upsampled_count() as count` for errors-dataset queries. However the function is only added to `DiscoverDatasetConfig.function_converter` in this file; the errors dataset uses its own dataset config/function converter. Unless `upsampled_count` is resolvable there, every errors-dataset timeseries query from an allowlisted project will fail with an "unknown function" validation error. No test in this PR exercises `dataset=errors`, so this path is unverified.

title: No test covers the new caching entry point `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`
body: The unit tests only exercise the private helpers (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) and the column transform. The public function added by this PR - including the cache key construction, cache hit/miss behaviour, and the interaction between a cached `False`/`True` and the dataset gate - is completely untested, which is exactly where the risky logic (stale cache, hash-based key) lives. Tests should at minimum cover a cache hit returning the stale decision and the empty-project-ids case.

title: Test comments contradict the asserted values
body: `assert data[0][1][0]["count"] == 10  # First bucket has 1 event` (and the following line) claim the bucket contains 1 event while asserting 10. The 10 comes from the 0.1 client sample rate being upsampled; the comments should state that, otherwise a future reader will assume the assertion is wrong and "fix" it.

title: Accidental git submodule/gitlink `sentry-repo` committed
body: The PR adds a gitlink entry `sentry-repo` pointing at `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This is an accidentally committed nested checkout of the repository itself; `git submodule update --init` will fail for anyone cloning, and tooling that walks the tree (mypy `files = ["."]`, pytest collection) can behave unpredictably. It should be removed from the commit.

title: Blanket `except Exception: pass` hides malformed error_sampling fixtures
body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps both the context lookup and the `float()` conversion in bare `except Exception: pass`. If a test supplies a malformed `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` (e.g. a string, or `contexts` not being a mapping), `sample_rate` is silently not set and the test will then assert on non-upsampled counts, masking the real problem instead of failing loudly. Since this only runs in test fixtures, the errors should propagate (or at least be narrowed to `TypeError/ValueError` with an assertion).

title: Upsampling eligibility uses outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` as its first argument and runs the query against it, but the upsampling decision is computed with the outer, request-level `dataset`: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)`. In the dashboard-widget split path (`get_event_stats_factory`), `_get_event_stats` is deliberately invoked with other datasets (`discover`, `split_dataset`) and with rewritten queries (`"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` / `"... AND event.type:transaction"`). Consequently (a) a transactions-only sub-query can be transformed to `upsampled_count()` when the request-level dataset is `errors`, producing a query over a dataset where `sample_weight` is not meaningful/absent, and (b) an errors-only sub-query run against `discover` will not be upsampled unless the *raw* request query string happens to contain `event.type:error`, since `_is_error_focused_query` inspects `request.GET["query"]` rather than the effective `query` passed in. The decision should be based on `scoped_dataset` and the effective query string.

title: 60s cache of allowlist eligibility is unkeyed on option state and effectively uninvalidatable
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the result of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` for 60 seconds under a key built only from the organization id and a hash of the project id set. `options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist")` is already a cheap, locally cached option read, so the added cache buys little while introducing a window in which counts flip between raw `count()` and upsampled `upsampled_count()` for the same dashboard/alert, i.e. visibly inconsistent numbers after an allowlist change. Worse, invalidation is impossible in practice: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (line 67) requires the exact project-id tuple that was queried, so a single allowlist change cannot be propagated to the unbounded set of cached project-set combinations, and the function is never called anywhere in this PR. Either drop the cache or key it on the allowlist value/version.

title: Cache key uses Python `hash()` of project ids, allowing silent collisions
body: The cache key is `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`. Different project-id sets within the same organization that collide under `hash()` will share a cache entry, so a non-allowlisted project set can be served an `is_eligible=True` verdict and have its `count()` silently multiplied by sample weights (or vice versa). Use a deterministic, collision-free key such as the sorted ids joined by a separator (or a cryptographic digest of it).

title: Docstring claims fresh config reads while the caller caches for 60s
body: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`'s docstring states it "reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time... This is intentional to ensure we always have the latest configuration state." The only caller caches its result for 60 seconds (line 38), so the documented behavior is the opposite of the actual behavior. A future reader relying on this comment will assume allowlist changes take effect immediately.

title: `upsampled_count` sums `sample_weight` with no null/zero fallback and declares a mismatched result type
body: The new SnQLFunction emits `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. Any error event stored without a populated `sample_weight` (events ingested before the field was written, or non-upsampled events in an allowlisted project) contributes 0 instead of 1, so `count()` queries silently under-report after the transform is applied; a `coalesce(sample_weight, 1)`-style fallback is needed, or the allowlist guarantee must be enforced elsewhere. Additionally `default_result_type="number"` contradicts the `toInt64` cast and the `"integer"` type used by the sibling count functions, so the response meta will advertise the wrong field type to clients formatting the value.

title: Accidental git submodule/gitlink `sentry-repo` committed
body: This PR adds a gitlink entry `sentry-repo` ("Subproject commit a5d2909...") with no corresponding `.gitmodules` definition. Clones and CI checkouts of such a dangling gitlink produce an empty directory and `git submodule` operations fail with "No url found for submodule path 'sentry-repo'". This is clearly unrelated to the upsampling feature and should be removed from the branch.

title: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` swallows all exceptions, hiding bad test fixtures
body: Both `try/except Exception: pass` blocks silently discard failures: a non-numeric `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` in a test fixture will simply not set `sample_rate`, so upsampling tests will quietly assert on un-upsampled counts instead of failing loudly on malformed input. Since `normalized_data.get("contexts", {}).get(...)` cannot realistically raise for dict data, the first `except` is dead and the second should either validate explicitly or let the error surface.

title: No coverage for the `errors` dataset path or for the cached public eligibility function
body: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True unconditionally for the `errors` snuba dataset, but every new endpoint test here goes through the default/`discover` dataset; there is no test issuing `dataset=errors` with `yAxis=count()`, so it is unverified that `upsampled_count()` (registered only in `discover.py`'s function converter) actually resolves for the errors query builder — if it does not, those requests would fail with an unknown-function error in production. Likewise, the unit test file only exercises the private helpers; the public `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, including its new 60-second cache and the cache-hit branch at line 32 of `error_upsampling.py`, is entirely untested (e.g. that a cached `False` is honored and that stale entries behave as documented).

title: Trailing whitespace and duplicated transform blocks will fail lint/black
body: Several added lines contain trailing whitespace (e.g. after `)` on line 223, line 234, line 278 here and in the docstrings of `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`), which `black --check` / pre-commit in this repo will reject, breaking CI. Additionally `should_upsample` is immediately aliased to `upsampling_enabled` and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` is repeated in three branches; computing `final_columns` once before the branching would remove the duplication and the misleading "late transformation"/"caching" comments, which do not describe anything the code actually does.

title: Error and replay-event timestamps are compared in different units
body: `gen_request_data` interleaves error messages with replay breadcrumbs by comparing `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"]` against `event.get("timestamp", 0)`. The error timestamp comes from the nodestore event payload and is epoch **seconds** (~1.7e9), while rrweb replay events carry epoch **milliseconds** (~1.75e12). Every error therefore compares as smaller than every replay event, so in production all errors will be flushed to the front of the log list instead of being placed chronologically, which is the whole point of the merge. The new unit test (`test_get_request_data`) uses second-scale timestamps for the replay events too, so it cannot catch this; a test with realistic millisecond rrweb timestamps is needed.

title: fetch_error_details pairs error ids with nodestore values by dict ordering
body: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `nodestore.backend.get_multi()` returns a dict whose iteration order exactly matches the order of the `node_ids` passed in and contains an entry for every id. That is an implementation detail of the backend; if any backend omits missing keys or returns a differently ordered mapping, each `ErrorEvent.id` will be attached to another error's title/message/timestamp. Build the list by iterating the input ids and looking up `events[Event.generate_node_id(project_id, id)]` instead of relying on value ordering.

title: New table widget renders hardcoded empty data when feature flag is on
body: In `tableResultComponent`, when `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` instead of the actual `result`/`fields`/`meta` computed just above. Any organization that gets this flag will see completely blank dashboard tables instead of their widget data. The real result must be mapped into `TabularData`/`TabularColumn` before this branch can be enabled.

title: `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is always true, so the guard is dead
body: `normalizeDateTimeParams(selection.datetime)` always returns an object (possibly empty), so `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` can never be false and the `enabled` condition reduces to the feature check alone. If the intent was to avoid firing the request before page filters are ready (e.g. checking for a statsPeriod/start+end), the condition needs to inspect the actual fields; as written it provides no protection and will issue a request with no date range.

title: 60s processing deadline may be too short for a 100-identity batch and breaks the task chain
body: `check_auth_identities` iterates up to `chunk_size` (default 100) identities and calls `provider.refresh_identity()` for each, which performs an external HTTP round trip per identity. With `processing_deadline_duration=60` the worker will kill the task once the deadline passes; because `check_auth.apply_async(...)` is only executed at the very end of the function, a deadline kill also drops the self-rescheduling call, halting the chained scan of remaining identities until the next scheduled run. Either reduce the chunk size or set a deadline that bounds 100 sequential network calls.

title: get_environment_info issues an extra event lookup per issue and swallows errors as 'no-environment'
body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` (a Snuba/eventstore lookup) plus `get_environment()` for every issue included in a merged-PR comment, i.e. up to 5 extra queries per comment on top of the existing top-issues query. In addition, the blanket `except Exception` logs `get_environment_info.no-environment` with `extra={"error": e}`, which both mislabels real failures (timeouts, Snuba errors) as 'no environment' and loses the traceback (no `exc_info`/`logger.exception`), making such failures effectively invisible.

title: Analytics event recorded before the feature-flag check
body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble")` gate and before any payload validation, so every request — including ones that are immediately rejected with 404 because the feature is disabled — is counted as an assemble event. This inflates the metric and makes it useless for measuring actual usage; move the call after the feature check.

title: Serializer accepts reports with neither `timestamp` nor `age`
body: `age` and `timestamp` are both declared `required=False` and the `validate_age`/`validate_timestamp` hooks only reject the case where *both* are present. A report containing neither field passes validation even though both the Working Draft and Editor's Draft require one of them, so malformed payloads are silently accepted and counted. A `validate()` method asserting exactly one of the two is present would close the gap (and there is no test covering this case).

title: TabularColumn.name is typed as the field-key generic instead of string
body: `TabularColumn<TFields>` declares `name: TFields`, the same type as `key`. `name` is a human-readable display label (the new table explicitly supports custom names such as 'Count of Span Duration'), so once a caller instantiates `TabularColumn<'http.request_method' | 'count(span.duration)'>` the display name becomes impossible to set without a cast. `name` should be `string`.

title: Error IDs are paired with nodestore data by dict ordering
body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `get_multi` returns a mapping keyed by node id; its iteration order is not guaranteed to match the order of the input list (and backends may omit/reorder keys, e.g. when some come from cache). As a result an `ErrorEvent` can be built with the id of one error and the title/message/timestamp of a different one, and if any node is missing the remaining pairings shift by one. The ids/messages that end up in the Seer prompt and in the summary can therefore be wrong. Iterate over `node_ids` and look up `events[node_id]` instead of relying on dict order.

title: Error/replay timestamps compared in different units, so errors are never interleaved
body: `gen_request_data` compares `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"]` with `event.get("timestamp", 0)`. Error timestamps come from nodestore event data, which is Unix time in **seconds**, while rrweb replay event timestamps are Unix time in **milliseconds**. Every error timestamp is therefore smaller than every replay event timestamp, so all error log lines are flushed before the first breadcrumb instead of being interleaved chronologically — defeating the purpose of this change. The unit tests hide this because the fixture segment uses second-scale timestamps (1.5, 2.0). Normalize both to the same unit (e.g. multiply error timestamps by 1000) before comparing.

title: error_ids silently dropped when caller passes `field` query params
body: `process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist("field"))` filters the replay payload down to the requested fields, and then `error_ids` is read from the filtered response. Any caller that supplies `?field=...` without `error_ids` (a legal request for this endpoint signature) will get `error_ids = []` and lose all error context with no indication why. Read `error_ids` from the unfiltered snuba response, or hardcode the field list used for this internal lookup.

title: Feature-flagged table path renders an empty table, discarding widget data
body: When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, the widget renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` — the actual `result`/`fields`/`meta` for the widget are ignored. Any organization with the flag enabled will see every dashboard table widget render with no headers and no rows. Either pass the real `result` data/columns or don't wire the flag up until the mapping exists.

title: Inconsistent optional chaining will throw when meta is absent
body: `Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields)` guards `tableData` but not `meta`, so if `tableData` is supplied without `meta` (the type requires it, but callers pass loosely-typed API data) this throws `Cannot read properties of undefined`. Elsewhere in the same component `tableData?.data ?? []` is defensive, so the intent was clearly to tolerate missing data. Use `tableData?.meta?.fields ?? {}`.

title: Header alignment computed from display name instead of column key
body: `fieldAlignment(column.name, column.type)` uses the human-readable column name. When callers override `name` (the documented use case, e.g. `name: 'Count of Span Duration'` for key `count(span.duration)`), `fieldAlignment` can no longer recognize the aggregate/field and will align numeric columns as if they were strings. Pass `column.key` to `fieldAlignment` and keep `column.name` only for the rendered label.

title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness, so 0 values bypass validation
body: `validate_timestamp` rejects a report when `self.initial_data.get("age")` is truthy and `validate_age` when `timestamp` is truthy. `age: 0` (a report generated just now, which is the common case for freshly queued reports) and `timestamp: 0` are falsy, so a report containing both fields is accepted when one of them is 0, and conversely the validation message is never triggered for the most frequent values. Compare against `None` (`is not None`) instead of truthiness.

title: One invalid report in a batch discards the entire batch
body: The loop returns HTTP 422 as soon as any single report in the posted array fails validation, so none of the valid reports in that batch are counted by the `browser_reporting.raw_report_received` metric. Browsers batch multiple reports per request and will keep re-sending the same batch, so a single malformed/unsupported report (e.g. a non-RFC URL, or a type outside `BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES`) permanently blinds the collector for that client. Prefer skipping+logging invalid entries and still processing the valid ones.

title: get_environment_info issues a Snuba/nodestore fetch per issue in PR comments
body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue included in a merged-PR comment (up to 5 per comment, for both GitHub and GitLab workflows). `get_recommended_event` runs a Snuba query plus a nodestore fetch, so each PR comment now performs several extra round trips in the comment task that previously only used the already-loaded `Group` rows. Consider fetching the latest/recommended events in bulk, or deriving the environment from data already available on the group.

title: Issue template embeds a trailing newline while callers also join with newlines
body: `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE` ends with `\n`, but both `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` and `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` join the rendered lines with `"\n"`. The posted comment therefore contains a blank line between every issue and an extra blank line before the footer (visible in the updated test expectations). If the double spacing is not intended, drop the trailing newline from the template.

title: Analytics event recorded before the feature flag / validation checks
body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before any schema validation, so every request from orgs without the feature (and every malformed request) is counted as an assemble call. This inflates the metric and makes it useless for measuring real usage; move the record after the feature gate, or add a flag/result attribute.

title: 60s processing deadline may be too short for a 100-identity auth refresh chunk
body: `check_auth_identities` iterates over up to `chunk_size=100` identities, each performing a network `provider.refresh_identity(...)`, and then re-schedules `check_auth` to continue the chain. With a 60s processing deadline the task can be killed mid-batch; because `check_auth` already bumped `last_synced` for the whole chunk before enqueuing, those identities are skipped for ~a day and, more importantly, the follow-up `check_auth.apply_async` at the end of the function never runs, so the batching chain stops. Size the deadline to the worst case (chunk_size × per-identity refresh latency) or make the reschedule happen before the refresh loop.

title: attributes can now be undefined and query defaults changed
body: The rewritten hook returns `attributes: isFetching ? previous : data`, where `data` is `TagCollection | undefined`; previously the hook always returned an object (`{}` at minimum), so consumers that spread/iterate the result (e.g. building filter key sections) can now receive `undefined` on error or before the first fetch. Additionally, the move from `useApiQuery` (which set `retry: false`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`) to a bare `useQuery` reinstates the default retry/refetch-on-focus behaviour, and the `environment` parameter that was previously sent is now dropped. Default `data` to `{}` and re-apply the query options if the previous behaviour was intended.

title: No-op migrations point at a replacement migration that is not in this change
body: Both 0917 and 0920 are gutted with the comment "See 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py for the correct migration", but no such file is added in this PR. If 0921 does not exist, the org saved-search → view backfill is now silently never performed and the comment misleads the next reader. Add the replacement migration (or fix the reference).

title: Error IDs are paired with the wrong nodestore payloads
body: `fetch_error_details()` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` (which returns a mapping keyed by node id and may omit/reorder missing keys), and then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. Any missing or re-ordered entry shifts the pairing, so an `ErrorEvent` can be created with the id of one error and the title/message/timestamp of another, producing wrong error text and wrong chronological placement in the Seer prompt. Iterate `events.items()` and map the node id back to the original event id instead of zipping the raw `values()`. The surrounding `except Exception: return []` also means this silently degrades to "no errors" rather than surfacing the problem.

title: get_environment_info triggers a per-issue recommended-event lookup during PR comment generation
body: `get_environment_info()` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue included in a merged-PR comment. That helper performs a search/snuba query plus a nodestore fetch per issue, so generating a comment for the top 5 issues now issues up to 5 extra remote queries inside the webhook/task path that previously only read `issue.culprit` from the already-loaded model. This adds latency and external load to every PR comment, and the broad `except Exception` means failures are invisible apart from an info log. Consider batching the environment lookup (or deriving it from data already fetched for the issue list).

title: New table widget path renders hardcoded empty data instead of query results
body: When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}` while the actual `result` (fields, meta, data) is ignored. Any organization with that flag enabled will see completely blank dashboard tables instead of their widget data. The real `result`/`fields`/`datasetConfig` values need to be mapped into `TabularData`/`TabularColumn` before this branch is usable.

title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter only applies while searching
body: `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` early when `searchQuery` is empty, so the newly added `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` exclusion (`is_segment`, `project_id`, `received`) is only applied once the user types something. In the default (no search) state those attributes are still shown, which is the opposite of the intent and makes the list inconsistent as soon as a user starts/clears a search. The hidden-attribute filter should be applied to the base list, independently of the search term.

title: Hook can now return undefined attributes where it previously always returned a TagCollection
body: The hook was rewritten to return `attributes: isFetching ? previous : data` from `useQuery`. `data` is `undefined` whenever the query errors, is disabled (`enabled` false), or has not run, and `previous` is also `undefined` on the first render — whereas the old implementation always derived a concrete `TagCollection` object (`result.data ?? []` reduced into `{}`). Consumers that do `Object.keys(attributes)` or spread the value (e.g. the filter-key sections / search query builder tag collections) will throw on error or while the hook is disabled. Default to `{}` (or make the undefined case explicit for all callers).

title: Attribute-keys query key omits the organization
body: `queryKey` is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`, and `makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions` only contains item type, attribute type, project ids and the datetime range — the organization slug used to build the request URL is not part of the key. Two organizations with the same project ids/date range would share a cache entry, so attribute keys from one org can be served for another after an org switch within the same session. Include the organization slug (or the full URL) in the query key.

title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness, so age=0 bypasses it
body: `validate_timestamp` checks `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and `validate_age` checks `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. A report containing `age: 0` (a legitimate value for a report generated right now) together with a `timestamp` passes both validators, defeating the intended "exactly one of age/timestamp" rule; conversely `timestamp: 0` also slips through. Use `is not None`/`in self.initial_data` instead of truthiness.

title: One invalid report rejects the entire batch
body: The POST handler returns 422 for the whole request as soon as any single report in the array fails validation, discarding the valid reports in the same batch. Browsers send reports in batches and will keep retrying the same (permanently invalid) payload, so a single malformed report from one page permanently blocks collection of the rest of that batch. Consider skipping/counting invalid reports and still returning 200 for the valid ones.

title: Coverage for the application/reports+json content type was removed
body: The previous test posted with `content_type="application/reports+json"` (the content type browsers actually use for the Reporting API) and asserted the request body was logged. After the refactor every success-path test posts with the default content type, so `BrowserReportsJSONParser` — the only reason the custom parser class exists — is no longer exercised by any test. A regression in the parser media type would silently break real browser reports while the suite stays green.

title: Analytics event recorded before feature check and request validation
body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` is executed as the first statement of `post()`, before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before schema validation. Every request from orgs without the feature, and every malformed/polling request, is counted as an assemble event, so the metric does not reflect actual assemble attempts. Move the `record()` call after the feature gate (and ideally after validation).

title: Custom cell renderers fall back on any falsy return, not just undefined
body: Both `renderDefaultHeadCell` and `renderDefaultBodyCell` do `const cell = render...(); if (cell) return cell;`. The documented contract (see tableWidgetVisualization.stories.tsx and the prop JSDoc) is that returning `undefined` triggers the fallback renderer. With a truthiness check, a custom renderer that legitimately returns `null` (render nothing), `''`, or `0` will be silently replaced by the default renderer, which is not what the docs promise and is hard to debug. Compare against `undefined` explicitly.

title: Unguarded `metadata["sender"]["login"]` access raises KeyError/TypeError
body: `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` compares the pipeline state against `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` with direct subscript access. `sender` is only present in an Integration's metadata when the row was written by the `installation` webhook handler; `GitHubIntegrationProvider.build_integration` only adds it when `state.get("sender")` is set (it never is in this pipeline), and the pipeline's `update_or_create` overwrites the metadata on every successful install (see `test_basic_flow`, where the stored metadata has no `sender` key). So any Integration that was last written by the pipeline, and reaches this branch (Integration row exists and is ACTIVE but has no OrganizationIntegration rows, e.g. after the org integration was removed), will raise an unhandled `KeyError` here and return a 500 instead of the intended error page. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and decide explicitly whether a missing sender should fail closed.

title: OAuth `state` is a constant pipeline signature, not a per-request nonce
body: The OAuth2 authorize request is sent with `state = pipeline.signature`, and the callback validates `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature`. `Pipeline.signature` is a deterministic hash of the pipeline's view classes: it is identical for every user, every org and every installation attempt (the tests hard-code `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3` and reuse it across different users/orgs), and it is exposed in plaintext in every authorize redirect URL. A constant, publicly known value provides no CSRF/code-injection protection, contrary to the PR description's claim that a `state` mismatch is a security check: an attacker can craft `/extensions/github/setup/?code=<attacker code>&state=9cae...` and have the victim's pipeline exchange the attacker's code and bind the attacker's GitHub login into `github_authenticated_user`. Follow the pattern in `OAuth2LoginView`/`OAuth2CallbackView`: generate a random nonce (`secrets.token_hex()`), `pipeline.bind_state("state", nonce)`, and compare the callback value against the stored nonce.

title: GitHub user validation is skipped entirely when no Integration row exists yet
body: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, when `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist` the view immediately calls `pipeline.next_step()`, so the new `github_authenticated_user` vs. installation-sender check is never performed and `build_integration` will happily claim the installation. This is the common case for any installation whose `installation` webhook has not been processed yet (the browser redirect and the webhook race each other on every fresh install) and for installations that still exist on GitHub after the Sentry-side Integration row was deleted. Since GitHub installation ids are small sequential integers, an attacker can supply someone else's `installation_id` and, if no Integration row is present, bind that installation (and its repository access) to their own Sentry org — exactly the attack this PR aims to prevent. The sender/owner should be verified against data fetched from GitHub (e.g. the installation's account/owner via `get_installation_info`) rather than only against a pre-existing local row.

title: `get_user_info` failures propagate as a 500 instead of the installation-failed page
body: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is called without a try/except. It performs an HTTP request to `/user` and raises `ApiError` on non-2xx responses (revoked token, GitHub 5xx, rate limiting), and may also return a non-dict payload, which would make the following `"login" not in authenticated_user_info` check raise `TypeError`. Any of these cases yields an unhandled exception and a generic 500 in the middle of the install pipeline rather than the `error(...)` page the rest of this view uses. Wrap the call and fall back to `error(request, self.active_organization)`.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the installation-not-found path
body: The test still stubs `/app/installations/{id}` as 404, but the request it now makes supplies `state="ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"`, which does not match the pipeline signature used everywhere else in this file (`9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`). The request therefore short-circuits in `OAuthLoginView`'s state check and the assertion only verifies the generic "Invalid installation request." page. The previously covered behaviour — `build_integration` raising `IntegrationError("The GitHub installation could not be found.")` on a 404 from GitHub — is now untested, and the test name/intent is misleading. Use the correct state so the pipeline reaches `build_integration`, and assert the installation-not-found message (or add a separate test for the state-mismatch case).

title: No coverage for the matching-sender branch or for metadata without a sender
body: `test_github_user_mismatch` only covers the negative branch (authenticated login != `metadata["sender"]["login"]`). There is no test where an Integration row exists with a `sender` whose login matches the authenticated user (the branch that must let the install continue), and none where the existing Integration's metadata has no `sender` key — the latter currently crashes with a `KeyError` in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`. Both branches are reachable in production and should be asserted.

title: KeyError when integration metadata has no "sender" entry
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes every existing `Integration` row carries a `sender` key in its metadata. `build_integration()` (line 376) only stores `sender` when the pipeline state contains it, and the pipeline itself never binds a `sender` key, so any Integration created/updated by the installation pipeline (as opposed to the GitHub `installation` webhook) has metadata without `sender`. If such an Integration exists while the OrganizationIntegration does not (e.g. the org integration was deleted and the user re-runs the install), this line raises `KeyError` and the user gets an unhandled 500 instead of the intended error page. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and decide explicitly what to do when the sender is unknown.

title: GitHub user validation is skipped when the Integration row does not exist yet
body: The new ownership check only runs on the code path where an `Integration` row for `installation_id` already exists. When `Integration.DoesNotExist` is raised (line 481) the pipeline advances immediately and `build_integration()` resolves the installation purely with the app JWT, which does not prove the current user owns that installation. Since the `Integration` row is created asynchronously by the GitHub `installation` webhook, a user who supplies someone else's `installation_id` before the webhook is processed (or if the webhook never arrives) can still attach that installation to their own Sentry org — the exact scenario this PR intends to block. Consider validating the authenticated GitHub login against the installation account/sender fetched from `get_installation_info()` instead of relying solely on previously stored metadata.

title: Network failures during token exchange and user lookup produce a 500 instead of the error page
body: `safe_urlopen(...)` on line 423 is outside the `try` block, and `get_user_info(...)` on line 434 calls `resp.raise_for_status()` internally. Any transport error, timeout, or non-2xx response from GitHub therefore propagates out of `dispatch()` and results in an unhandled exception/500 for the user, instead of the `error(request, self.active_organization)` page used for every other failure in this view. Wrap both calls and return the standard error response.

title: Authorize URL built by string interpolation without URL-encoding parameters
body: The GitHub authorize URL is assembled with an f-string, so `state` and especially `redirect_uri` (built from `absolute_uri`, which depends on the deployment's URL prefix) are inserted into the query string unencoded. If the URL prefix ever contains characters that must be percent-encoded (`?`, `&`, `#`, non-ASCII, a path with a query), the resulting authorize request is malformed and the OAuth step will fail or redirect somewhere unexpected. Build the query with `urlencode({...})`.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer covers the 404 installation error
body: The assertion was changed from `b"The GitHub installation could not be found."` to the generic `b"Invalid installation request."`, which is the message emitted by the new OAuth/state failure branch (`error()` default), not by `build_integration()`'s `IntegrationError` for a missing installation. Combined with the hand-written `state` value (`ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`, different from every other test), the test now passes without ever reaching `get_installation_info()`, so the 404-installation path that the test is named for is no longer exercised. Either keep asserting the specific message after a valid OAuth step, or add a separate test for the state-mismatch branch.

title: Brittle positional assertion on responses.calls index
body: `responses.calls[2].request.headers["Authorization"]` hard-codes the position of the app-installations request in the recorded call list, which now depends on the exact number and ordering of the new OAuth calls (`/login/oauth/access_token`, `/user`). Any future change in the pipeline's request order silently asserts the wrong request (or raises IndexError). Match on the request URL instead of the index.

title: KeyError on integration.metadata["sender"] when metadata has no sender
body: `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` reaches `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` whenever an `Integration` row exists for the `installation_id` but no `OrganizationIntegration` rows exist. `metadata["sender"]` is only populated by `build_integration` when the pipeline/webhook state contains `sender` (see `build_integration`: `if state.get("sender")`), and integrations created through the normal pipeline do not have it — `tests/.../test_integration.py::test_basic_flow` asserts the saved metadata contains only access_token/expires_at/icon/domain_name/account_type. So for any integration whose OrganizationIntegration was hard-deleted (e.g. org deletion) or that was created without a sender, a re-install attempt raises `KeyError: 'sender'` and the user gets a 500 instead of the intended error page. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and decide explicitly what to do when the sender is unknown.

title: OAuth `state` is the deterministic pipeline signature, so the state check gives no CSRF protection
body: The authorize redirect uses `state = pipeline.signature` and the callback only checks `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature`. The pipeline signature is deterministic and not user/session specific — the new tests hardcode the same value `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3` for different users and organizations (`test_github_installed_on_another_org`, `test_github_user_mismatch`, `test_github_prevent_install_until_pending_deletion_is_complete`). An attacker can therefore construct a callback URL with a valid `state` plus their own `code`, and if a victim with an in-flight pipeline loads it, the attacker's GitHub identity gets bound into the victim's pipeline via `github_authenticated_user` — exactly the class of attack this PR is meant to prevent. The state should be a per-pipeline random nonce stored in pipeline state and compared on return.

title: Authenticated GitHub user is not verified when the Integration row does not yet exist
body: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, if `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist` the pipeline advances immediately (`return pipeline.next_step()`) without any comparison of `github_authenticated_user` against the account that installed the app. The sender information this check relies on is written by the asynchronous `installation` webhook, so whether the validation runs at all depends on webhook delivery timing: an attacker who knows a victim's `installation_id` and completes the redirect before the webhook is processed bypasses the new check entirely. The installation ownership should be verified against the authenticated user's own token (e.g. `GET /user/installations`) rather than relying on a pre-existing Integration row.

title: Unhandled exceptions from token exchange / get_user_info produce a 500 instead of the error page
body: `safe_urlopen(...)` (line 423) and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` (line 434) are called without exception handling. `get_user_info` performs an HTTP request and raises `ApiError`/`ApiHostError` on non-2xx or network failures (e.g. revoked token, GitHub outage, rate limiting), and `safe_urlopen` raises on connection errors. Only the JSON/body parse is wrapped in `try/except`. The result is an unhandled 500 in the install popup rather than the intended `github-integration-failed.html` page, with no log line to diagnose it. Wrap both calls and fall back to `error(request, self.active_organization)` (plus a log).

title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the 404 installation path
body: This test previously asserted `b"The GitHub installation could not be found."`, covering the `ApiError(404) -> IntegrationError` branch in `GitHubIntegrationProvider.build_integration`. It now passes `state="ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"`, a different value from the `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3` signature used by every other test in this file, and asserts only the generic `b"Invalid installation request."`. The request therefore short-circuits in `OAuthLoginView` on the state mismatch and the 404 handling in `build_integration` is no longer covered by any test. Either restore the correct state so the flow reaches `build_integration`, or add a separate test for the invalid-state branch and keep a real installation-not-found test.

title: gettext applied to a runtime variable breaks string extraction for the short error messages
body: `error()` wraps its `error_short` argument at call time with `_(error_short)`. Because the argument is a variable rather than a literal inside the `_()` call, `makemessages` cannot extract strings like "GitHub installation pending deletion." or "Github installed on another Sentry organization." anymore (previously they were literals inside `_()`), so these user-facing strings will silently stop being translated. Pass already-lazy/translated values from the call sites instead of translating the variable.

title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field default, which is evaluated exactly once when the module is imported, not when an `AssignmentSource` is created. Every instance created in a worker/web process therefore carries the process start-up timestamp, so the field is useless for reasoning about when the assignment was queued (and will drift arbitrarily far from reality in long-lived processes). Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

title: AssignmentSource does not round-trip through task kwargs (datetime `queued`)
body: `to_dict()` uses `dataclasses.asdict`, which leaves `queued` as a raw `datetime`. This dict is passed as a Celery kwarg in `sync_group_assignee_outbound` (`assignment_source_dict=assignment_source.to_dict()`). With a JSON task serializer this either fails to serialize or is serialized as an ISO string; `from_dict` then does `cls(**input_dict)` with no coercion, producing an `AssignmentSource` whose `queued` is a `str` despite the declared `datetime` type. Either serialize/deserialize `queued` explicitly (e.g. `isoformat()` / `fromisoformat`) or drop the field from the wire format.

title: from_dict silently returns None on malformed payload, disabling loop protection
body: `from_dict` swallows `ValueError`/`TypeError` and returns `None`. In `sync_assignee_outbound` a `None` source means `should_sync("outbound_assignee", None)` passes, so a malformed/renamed payload silently re-enables the sync cycle this PR is meant to break, with no log or metric to detect it. Log a warning (or raise) when a non-empty `assignment_source_dict` fails to parse.

title: `assignment_source` added to abstract `sync_status_outbound` but never used
body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature now declares `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`, but no caller in this PR passes it and the concrete provider implementations (Jira/VSTS/etc.) were not updated to accept or honor it. The parameter is dead and only reaches implementations through `**kwargs`, so the signature change implies status-sync loop protection that does not actually exist. Either wire it through (status inbound -> outbound) or drop it from the abstract signature.

title: No test for the actual to_dict -> task kwargs -> from_dict round trip
body: The tests only call `from_dict` with hand-written dicts that omit `queued`, and `to_dict` is asserted only to contain a non-None `queued`. The real production path is `to_dict()` -> Celery kwargs -> `from_dict()`, which is exactly where the `datetime`/string mismatch (and possible serializer failure) occurs. Add a test asserting `AssignmentSource.from_dict(source.to_dict()) == source`, including after JSON round-tripping, so the serialization contract used by `sync_assignee_outbound` is covered.

title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` makes the default value a single `datetime` computed when the module is first imported, not when an `AssignmentSource` is created. Every instance built via `from_integration()` (or any constructor call that omits `queued`) will therefore carry the process-start timestamp, so the field is useless for measuring how long the assignment context has been in flight and will look increasingly stale in long-running workers. Use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

title: from_dict does no validation and silently drops the cycle-protection context
body: `from_dict` constructs the dataclass with `cls(**input_dict)` and returns `None` on any `TypeError`/`ValueError`. Two problems: (1) failures are silent — if the payload shape ever changes (e.g. a field is renamed or an extra key is added by a producer on a different deploy), the loop-prevention context is dropped with no log/metric and the sync cycle this PR is meant to fix reappears; (2) no type coercion is done, so after the dict round-trips through the celery broker the `queued` value comes back as an ISO string, not a `datetime`, violating the field's annotation for any future consumer that does date arithmetic on it. Consider logging when parsing fails and explicitly parsing `queued`.

title: New task kwarg breaks mixed-version workers during rollout
body: `sync_assignee_outbound` is an `@instrumented_task` whose signature now accepts `assignment_source_dict`, and `sync_group_assignee_outbound` always includes that key in `apply_async(kwargs=...)`. During a rolling deploy, tasks enqueued by new web/region code can be picked up by workers still running the old signature, which will raise `TypeError: sync_assignee_outbound() got an unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source_dict'` and burn the task's retries, dropping assignee syncs for those messages. Only send the new kwarg when it is non-None, or guard the task with `**kwargs`.

title: `assignment_source` added to sync_status_outbound but never used or implemented
body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` now declares a 4th parameter `assignment_source`, but no caller passes it and no concrete integration implementation was updated to accept it (they rely on `**kwargs`). The result is a parameter in the published ABC signature that is dead code, misleadingly named for a status (not assignment) sync, and implies status-sync cycles are also guarded when they are not. Either wire it through the status-sync path (task + implementations) or drop it from this PR.

title: New `assignment_source` kwarg forwarded to all sync_assignee_outbound implementations
body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`, but no concrete integration implementation was updated in this PR. Any provider implementation of `sync_assignee_outbound` that does not declare `**kwargs` (or an explicit `assignment_source` parameter) will raise `TypeError` at runtime for every outbound assignee sync. Please confirm every implementation (Jira, Jira Server, VSTS, and any third-party/plugin installation returning `should_sync`) tolerates the extra keyword, or pass it only when it is not None.

title: No test that a different source integration still propagates outbound
body: The added coverage only asserts the suppression case (`AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` matching the target integration blocks the outbound call). There is no test that an assignment originating from a *different* integration still produces an outbound sync, which is the main over-blocking regression risk of the new `should_sync` short-circuit, nor a test covering the celery boundary (`assignment_source_dict` serialized in `sync_group_assignee_outbound` and re-parsed in the task). Add a case with a second integration whose id differs, and a case asserting the dict round-trip yields a usable `AssignmentSource`.

title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field default, so `timezone.now()` is called exactly once when the module is imported. Every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` value therefore carries the process/module import timestamp, not the time the assignment was actually queued. This makes the field useless (and actively misleading) for debugging or any future staleness/TTL logic built on it. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

title: Datetime in to_dict() is passed as Celery task kwargs and is not round-tripped by from_dict()
body: `to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)`, which keeps `queued` as a `datetime`. That dict is handed to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={... 'assignment_source_dict': ...})` (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:141), so a raw `datetime` ends up in the broker payload. Depending on the configured serializer this either fails to encode (the task is never enqueued and assignee sync silently stops) or arrives as an ISO string, in which case `from_dict` happily constructs an `AssignmentSource` whose `queued` attribute is a `str` despite the declared `datetime` type. Serialize/deserialize the timestamp explicitly (e.g., `isoformat()` / `fromisoformat()`) so the dataclass invariants hold across the task boundary.

title: from_dict silently swallows malformed payloads, disabling cycle protection without any signal
body: `from_dict` returns `None` for any payload that doesn't exactly match the constructor (missing key, extra key, renamed field) and performs no type validation on `integration_id`. Because `sync_assignee_outbound` treats `None` as "no source", a malformed/renamed payload means the loop-prevention check in `should_sync` is skipped and the sync cycle this PR is meant to fix silently returns, with nothing logged or metered to indicate it happened. Add a log/metric on the failure path (and validate `integration_id` is an int) so this failure mode is observable.

title: New `assignment_source` kwarg passed to sync_assignee_outbound without updating the abstract signature
body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue, user, assign=assign, assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`, but the abstract declaration in `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound` (src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:397) was not updated to accept `assignment_source`; it only tolerates it via `**kwargs`. Any current or future implementation (including third-party/provider installations) that defines `sync_assignee_outbound(self, external_issue, user, assign=True)` without `**kwargs` will raise `TypeError` at runtime, and the retry decorator will retry it 5 times before failing. Declare `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None` on the abstract method so the contract is explicit.

title: `assignment_source` added to abstract sync_status_outbound but never passed or used
body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature gains an `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None` parameter, but no caller in this PR passes it and no concrete implementation consumes it. The signature now advertises cycle protection for status sync that does not exist; worse, subclasses still declare `(self, external_issue, is_resolved, project_id, **kwargs)`, so a caller following the abstract contract and passing the source positionally would bind it to an unrelated kwarg position. Either wire the parameter through the status-sync path or drop it from the abstract signature.

title: No test that a non-matching assignment source still propagates outbound
body: The new test only covers the case where the assignment source integration matches the target integration (sync suppressed). There is no test asserting the complementary behaviour that this PR explicitly promises: when the `AssignmentSource` comes from a *different* integration, the outbound sync must still fire. Without it, a regression that over-suppresses sync (e.g., comparing the wrong id field in `should_sync`) would go undetected and silently break cross-integration issue sync.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`, but `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares the abstract members `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and (newly added in this PR) `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Because the class implements none of them it remains abstract, so `Detector.detector_handler` (`group_type.detector_handler(self)` in src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...` for any detector of type `metric_alert_fire`. Previously the handler was concrete (it implemented `evaluate` returning `[]`), so this is a runtime regression for metric alert detector processing. Either keep a concrete stub implementation or don't register the handler until it is implemented.

title: evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list
body: The docstring for `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` says "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`", but the return type was changed in this PR to `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. Misleading documentation for implementers of the new handler contract.

title: Multi-group test passes the wrong value for group_2 and still passes
body: In `test_state_results_multi_group`, `group_vals` contains `{"group_1": 6, "group_2": 10}` but the expected occurrence for group_2 is built with `value=6`. The test only passes because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores the `value` argument, meaning the test does not actually verify that the detector passes the correct per-group value into `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Use the real value (10) and have the mock incorporate `value` (e.g. in `evidence_data`) so the hook's arguments are actually asserted.

title: No test covers producing a StatusChangeMessage through process_detectors
body: `process_detectors`/`create_issue_occurrence_from_result` has two branches: `PayloadType.OCCURRENCE` and `PayloadType.STATUS_CHANGE`. Only the occurrence branch is exercised (`test_state_results`, `test_state_results_multi_group`). The resolve path, which sends `payload_type=PayloadType.STATUS_CHANGE` with `occurrence=None`, is never asserted end-to-end, so a regression in the status-change produce call would go unnoticed. The previously existing duplicate-group-key test was also removed without an equivalent assertion that duplicate keys are now impossible by construction.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and will raise TypeError when instantiated
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with just `pass`, but `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares four abstract members: `counter_names` (abstract property), `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. None of them are implemented here, so the class remains abstract and `group_type.detector_handler(self)` in `Detector.detector_handler` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...` for any detector of type `metric_alert_fire`. Previously the handler had a concrete `evaluate` returning `[]` and was safely instantiable. This turns a no-op into an unhandled exception in `process_detectors`. Either keep a concrete stub implementation or don't register the abstract class as `detector_handler`.

title: PriorityLevel(new_status) can raise ValueError for condition results outside PriorityLevel
body: `new_status` is derived from `condition.evaluate_value(value)` results via `max(new_status, evaluation)`, and `DataCondition.condition_result` is user/DB-provided data, so it is not guaranteed to be one of the `PriorityLevel` members (25/50/75). `PriorityLevel(new_status)` will raise `ValueError: <n> is not a valid PriorityLevel` for any other non-zero value (e.g. a condition result of `1` or `True`), crashing detector evaluation for the whole data packet rather than skipping/logging. Consider validating the value or coercing to the nearest valid priority before constructing `PriorityLevel`.

title: evaluate() docstring still describes a list return value
body: The docstring of `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`", but the signature and implementation now return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. Update the wording so implementers of the abstract handler aren't misled about the contract.

title: Mock occurrence builder ignores `value`, so tests can't detect a wrong value passed to the hook
body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` never uses its `value` argument, and the tests exploit this by passing values that don't match the data packet (e.g. `test_state_results_multi_group` builds the expected occurrence for `group_2` with `6` while the packet has `10`; `test_results_on_change`/`TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` pass `6` while the evaluated values are 100 and 10). As a result, a regression where `evaluate_group_key_value` forwards the wrong `value` (or the wrong group key's value) to `build_occurrence_and_event_data` would not be caught. Incorporate `value` (and `group_key`) into the generated occurrence so equality assertions actually verify the arguments.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`, but `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares four abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`) and inherits `abc.ABC`. Because none of them are implemented, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(detector)` raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...`. This is reached from `Detector.detector_handler` for any detector of type `metric_alert_fire`, so `process_detectors` will blow up at runtime instead of returning no results (previously the handler returned `[]` safely). Either implement the abstract hooks or keep the class non-registered/abstract until they exist.

title: New abstract hook breaks existing StatefulDetectorHandler subclasses
body: `build_occurrence_and_event_data` was added as an `@abc.abstractmethod` on `StatefulDetectorHandler`. Any existing subclass (e.g. `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` in `src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py`) that does not define it can no longer be instantiated, producing a `TypeError` at handler construction time rather than a clear failure at import/registration. If subclasses are expected to be rolled out incrementally, consider providing a default implementation that raises `NotImplementedError` only when a non-OK status actually needs an occurrence, so that detectors without an occurrence builder degrade gracefully.

title: get_state_data raises KeyError when counter_names is empty
body: In `get_state_data`, `counter_updates` is only populated inside `if self.counter_names:`; otherwise it stays `{}`. The loop below then unconditionally does `counter_updates[gk]`, which raises `KeyError` for a handler that legitimately tracks no counters (an empty `counter_names` list is a valid implementation of the abstract property). Use `counter_updates.get(gk, {})` or initialize the dict for all group keys.

title: Multi-group test asserts occurrence built with the wrong value
body: `test_state_results_multi_group` sends `group_2` with value 10 but builds the expected occurrence with `value=6`. The test only passes because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores the `value` argument, so the test cannot detect if the wrong value is forwarded from `evaluate_group_key_value` to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Make the mock occurrence depend on `value` (e.g. put it in `evidence_data`) and pass the real value, so the plumbing of `value` and `new_status` is actually verified.

title: Stale TODO comment about stateful detector
body: The comment `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction` sits directly above a class that now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler`, so it is misleading to future readers. It should be removed or replaced with the actual remaining work (implementing the required abstract hooks).

title: get_monitor_environment_context discards the mutated config copy
body: `get_monitor_environment_context` builds `config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy()` and replaces the numeric `schedule_type` with its human-readable display value, but the returned dict uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original, unmodified dict) for the `"config"` key. As a result the monitor context attached to the issue occurrence event still carries the raw integer `schedule_type` and the copy/display-name work is dead code. Since this code was just moved into a new module it is a good moment to fix it: return `config` instead of `monitor_environment.monitor.config`.

title: Docstring example cannot be produced by get_failure_reason
body: The docstring for `get_failure_reason` lists `"A failed check-in was detected"` as an example output, but the function can only return the strings from `SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP` (error/missed/timeout) or the pluralized `"... check-ins detected"` form. The example is misleading for anyone relying on the docstring to know the possible outputs. Also note that when `failed_checkins` contains no statuses in `HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP`, `status_counts` is empty and the function returns the bare string "check-ins detected" with an empty prefix, which the docstring does not describe.

title: Public helpers renamed/relocated without updating any callers or tests
body: `mark_failed_threshold` -> `try_incident_threshold` and `create_issue_platform_occurrence` -> `create_incident_occurrence` were moved out of `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` into new modules, and `SimpleCheckIn` moved to `sentry.monitors.types`. No other file in this PR was updated. Any remaining import or `mock.patch("sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence")` style reference (tests commonly patch these paths) will now raise `AttributeError`/`ImportError` at runtime, or worse, silently stop patching the real code path. Worth grepping for the old names/paths and updating them (or re-exporting from `mark_failed`) before merge.

title: get_monitor_environment_context discards the mutated config copy
body: `get_monitor_environment_context()` copies `monitor.config` into a local `config` and replaces `config["schedule_type"]` with its human-readable display value, but the returned dict sets `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original object), so the local `config` variable is dead code. The occurrence's monitor context therefore carries the raw integer `schedule_type` instead of the display string, which is almost certainly not the intent and affects what is rendered on the issue. Return `config` instead.

title: Public helpers removed from mark_failed without updating importers/tests
body: This change deletes the module-level names `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, `SimpleCheckIn`, `HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP` and `SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP` from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`, but no test or other call-site files are touched in this PR. Any code or test that imports these from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` (or that monkeypatches/mocks `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence`) will now fail with ImportError or silently patch nothing. The importers and mock targets need to be updated to the new `logic.incidents` / `logic.incident_occurrence` modules as part of this move.

title: get_failure_reason docstring example does not match behavior
body: The docstring claims an example output of "A failed check-in was detected", but the singular map only contains error/missed/timeout phrasings, so that string can never be produced. The docstring also contains typos ("humam readible"). Minor, but misleading for future callers reasoning about the user-visible failure reason text.

title: get_monitor_environment_context discards the modified config copy
body: `get_monitor_environment_context` makes a copy of `monitor.config`, replaces `schedule_type` with its human-readable display value, but then returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original, unmodified dict) under the `"config"` key. The `config` local is never used, so the monitor context attached to the issue occurrence still carries the raw integer `schedule_type` instead of the display string. This defect is being carried into the new module unchanged; since the code is being relocated anyway it is a good time to return `config` instead of `monitor_environment.monitor.config`.

title: Public symbols removed from mark_failed without re-export shims
body: `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, `HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP`, `SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP` and `SimpleCheckIn` were all module-level names in `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` and are now gone (moved and partially renamed). Any other module or test that imports them from this path, or that patches e.g. `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence` / `mark_failed_threshold` with `mock.patch`, will now fail at import/patch time (mock.patch raises AttributeError for a missing attribute). No test files are updated in this PR, so please verify (grep for these names across src/ and tests/) and either update call sites/patch targets or keep thin re-export aliases in `mark_failed.py`.

title: Unhealthy flusher process is never killed (isinstance check is always False for spawn processes)
body: `_ensure_processes_alive()` only kills the old process if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. The processes here are created with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, i.e. `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`, which is **not** a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process` (`multiprocessing.context.Process`) — both derive separately from `BaseProcess`. So the check is always False and `process.kill()` never runs, whereas the previous code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. Consequences: a hung-but-alive flusher process is left running while a replacement is spawned for the same shards, so two processes flush the same Redis shards concurrently (duplicate segments produced to `buffered-segments`, racing `done_flush_segments`), and the zombie keeps writing to the shared `process_healthy_since` Value, permanently masking hang detection and leaking a process on every restart. The same wrong check also makes `process.terminate()` in `join()` (line 346) a no-op. Use `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` (or `self.mp_context.Process`) in the isinstance check.

title: max_processes=None/0 silently means one process per shard
body: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means that any caller that does not pass `max_processes` (the default, used by every direct construction such as `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py`) spawns one OS process per assigned shard, while the CLI option `--flusher-processes` defaults to 1. A consumer assigned 32 partitions constructed without the option would fork 32 flusher processes, each with its own Redis connections — a large, unintended resource jump compared to the previous single-process behaviour. Additionally, because of `or`, an explicit `--flusher-processes 0` is silently reinterpreted as "one per shard" instead of being rejected. Make the default explicit (e.g. 1) and validate that the value is >= 1.

title: join() can skip terminating remaining processes and computes an unused variable
body: In `join()`, `remaining_time` is computed but never used, and when the deadline has passed the loop `break`s, so the remaining processes in `self.processes` are never waited for nor terminated (they are only daemonic, so they are killed when the parent exits, possibly mid-flush). Combined with the broken `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check on line 346, no spawn process is ever terminated at shutdown. Either drop the unused variable and terminate all processes regardless of deadline, or document why skipping is acceptable.

title: Dead method `_create_process_for_shard`
body: `_create_process_for_shard(shard)` is not called anywhere after the refactor (restarts go through `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`). Leaving it in is confusing because it looks like the per-shard restart path but would silently do nothing if `shard` is not in any mapping. Remove it.

title: Inconsistent metric tag key: "shards" vs "shard"
body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged `{"shards": shard_tag}` while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use `{"shard": shard_tag}`. Queries/dashboards grouping on a single tag name will silently miss one of these metrics. Pick one key.

title: Comma-joined shard list used as metric tag value creates unbounded cardinality
body: `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` is used as the `shard` tag on `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and the per-segment `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` timing. The value is a *set* of shards that changes with every Kafka rebalance and with the `--flusher-processes` setting, so the tag value space is combinatorial rather than bounded by the number of shards, and `segment_size_bytes` is emitted per segment. This can blow up metric cardinality and makes per-shard aggregation impossible. Consider tagging with the process index or omitting the tag on high-volume metrics.

title: Class docstring contradicts actual process allocation and omits max_processes
body: The docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing", but shards are actually bucketed round-robin into `min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))` processes, and the CLI default is a single process for all shards. The docstring also still documents a `:param topic:` that does not exist while the newly added `max_processes` parameter is undocumented.

title: Added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
body: Line 15 does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, so the `time.sleep(0.1)` added at line 62 ("Give flusher threads time to process after drift change") returns immediately and provides no synchronization at all. The test still relies on the flusher thread happening to flush before `step.join()` sets the stop flag, so it remains racy/flaky and the comment is misleading. Use a real wait (e.g. `monkeypatch`-free sleep, or poll `messages` with a timeout) instead.

title: Shard-distribution assertion cannot detect duplicated or missing shards
body: `total_shards = sum(len(shards) for shards in flusher.process_to_shards_map.values()); assert total_shards == 4` would also pass if the same shard were assigned to two processes while another shard was dropped entirely — exactly the kind of bug that would cause duplicate or lost segments. Assert on the union instead, e.g. that the concatenation of all lists equals `{0,1,2,3}` with no duplicates, and that the buckets are balanced.

title: No test exercises the multiprocess flusher path
body: Both new/updated tests pass `produce_to_pipe`, which makes `SpanFlusher` use `threading.Thread` instead of `mp_context.Process`. The core change of this PR — spawning a real process per shard group, pickling a per-shard `SpansBuffer` into it, restarting a dead/hung process, and the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` kill/terminate paths — is therefore completely untested (and indeed broken, see the isinstance finding). Add at least one test that drives the actual spawn-process path, or a unit test of `_ensure_processes_alive` with a fake spawn process.

title: Unhealthy flusher processes are never killed (isinstance check never matches SpawnProcess)
body: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the kill is guarded by `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Processes here are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, i.e. `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`, which is *not* a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process` (that name resolves to `multiprocessing.context.Process` of the default context; `SpawnProcess` derives directly from `BaseProcess`). The guard is therefore always False in production, so `process.kill()` is never called. Previously `self.process.kill()` was invoked unconditionally. Consequence: when a flusher process is detected as hung (`cause = "hang"`), the old process keeps running while `_create_process_for_shards` starts a second process for the same shards. Two processes then flush and produce the same Redis shards concurrently, which can duplicate/fragment segments on the `buffered-segments` topic, and each restart leaks another process and Redis connection set. Use `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` (or the concrete `SpawnProcess`) in the isinstance check (the same mistake exists in `join()` at line 346, where `terminate()` is likewise dead code).

title: Added `time.sleep(0.1)` in test is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
body: The test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to a no-op at line 15 (`monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`), so the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 does nothing. The comment "Give flusher threads time to process after drift change" is misleading, and the intended synchronization does not happen — the test still relies on timing between `step.poll()` and the background flusher thread, so `(msg,) = messages` can fail intermittently. If a real wait is needed, capture the unpatched sleep (e.g. `from time import sleep` at module import, as test_flusher.py does) or poll for the condition with a timeout.

title: Metric tag key inconsistency and high-cardinality shard tag values
