body: This PR adds a new mutation that mutates booking attendees, updates external calendars and sends emails, with non-trivial authorization and filtering logic (team admin/owner check, blacklist, dedupe). No unit or e2e tests are included, so regressions in the permission check or the filtering cannot be caught.

title: Team admin/owner permission check uses AND instead of OR
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, which is only true for a user who is both admin and owner. Despite the name, a team admin (or the owner, depending on how the helpers classify roles) will be denied. The check should be `||`. Consequence: legitimate team admins/owners who are neither the booking organizer nor an attendee get FORBIDDEN.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw input instead of the filtered new guests
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered request input. In email-manager, membership in this array decides whether an attendee receives the "scheduled" email (treated as a newly added guest) or the "guests added" notice. Emails that were filtered out (already-existing attendees, blacklisted addresses) are still in `guests`, so pre-existing attendees will receive a full booking-confirmation email as if they were just invited. `uniqueGuests` should be passed instead.

title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive against lowercased list
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased when parsed, but the guest email is compared as-is (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). A blacklisted address submitted with any uppercase character (e.g. `Spam@x.com`) bypasses the filter. Lowercase the guest before comparison. The same case-sensitivity also lets duplicate attendees be created with differing case.

title: Email failure swallowed without logging the error
body: The catch block logs a fixed string via `console.log` and discards `err`, making email delivery failures impossible to diagnose. Use the project logger and include the error and bookingId.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores eventType disableStandardEmails settings
body: Every other sender in this file accepts `eventTypeMetadata` and skips host/attendee mail when `disableStandardEmails.all.host/attendee` is set. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and unconditionally sends to organizer, team members and all attendees, so event types that have standard emails disabled will still emit mail, violating the configured behaviour.

title: Organizer subject dereferences attendees[0] and uses an empty guest name
body: `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` will throw if the attendee list is empty, and newly added guests are created with `name: ""`, so the subject can render as "Guests Added:  with  at ..." when the first attendee is a name-less guest. Guard the access and fall back to the attendee email.

title: Initial empty email row always fails validation
body: `multiEmailValue` is initialised to `[""]`, and `handleAdd` only early-returns on a zero-length array. If the user clicks Add without typing, the `""` entry fails `z.string().email()` and the generic "Emails must be unique and valid" error is shown instead of a prompt to enter an email; similarly an extra blank row added via "Add another" blocks submission with a confusing message. Filter out empty strings before validating.

title: Error toast fallback is dead code and shows raw tRPC code
body: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`` is always a non-empty string, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never falls back. Users see strings like "FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission" (and `undefined: ...` when `err.data` is missing) rather than a localized message.

title: MultiEmail imports from the @calcom/ui barrel that re-exports it, creating a cycle
body: `packages/ui/index.tsx` now exports `MultiEmail` from `./form/MultiEmailLazy`, while `MultiEmail.tsx` imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui` — the same barrel. This circular dependency can cause undefined components at module-init time in some bundling/SSR orders. Import directly from the component paths like other files in `packages/ui/form` do.

title: No tests for the new addGuests handler
body: The handler contains non-trivial authorization, dedup/blacklist filtering and calendar/email side effects, but no unit tests were added. At minimum the permission branches (organizer / attendee / team role) and the duplicate-and-blacklist filtering should be covered to prevent regressions in an endpoint that writes attendees and sends mail.

title: Team permission check uses AND of isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, which requires the user to be both admin and owner simultaneously. Since these are typically mutually exclusive role checks, team admins (and likely owners too) are denied, contradicting the variable name and intent. Should be `||`. Additionally `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` queries membership for team id 0 for personal bookings, which is a meaningless query.

title: Calendar update uses the requesting user's credentials, not the organizer's
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` plus `new EventManager({...user, credentials})` builds the EventManager from the logged-in caller. But the handler also allows attendees and team admins/owners to add guests, in which case the calendar/video integration update is attempted with credentials of someone who does not own the booking's calendar entry, so `updateCalendarAttendees` will fail or silently not update the real event. The organizer (`booking.user`) credentials should be used instead.

title: Any attendee can add arbitrary guests to a booking
body: Permission is granted if the caller's email appears among booking attendees (`isAttendee`). Combined with the broken team check, this means any invited guest can add unlimited external email addresses to someone else's booking, triggering emails/ICS updates and leaking booking details (title, description, meeting URL/password) to arbitrary addresses. Consider restricting to organizer/team admins, or gating on event type settings.

title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive on the guest side
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased, but the incoming `guest` string is not normalized before `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. A blacklisted address submitted with any uppercase characters (e.g. `Foo@Bar.com`) bypasses the filter. Lowercase the guest email before comparison (and ideally before persisting/dedup against existing attendees, which is also case-sensitive today).

title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives unfiltered guest list and errors are swallowed
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input rather than `uniqueGuests`; guests that were filtered out (already attendees or blacklisted) are then classified as "new" in email-manager and receive a full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the add-guests notification. Also the catch block logs only a static string via `console.log`, discarding `err`, making email failures undiagnosable.

title: No booking status/time validation before adding guests
body: The handler adds attendees to any booking found by id, including CANCELLED/REJECTED/PENDING bookings and past bookings. This sends confirmation emails and ICS REQUEST invites for events that are cancelled or already over. Validate `booking.status === ACCEPTED` (and probably that the booking is upcoming) before mutating.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event type disableStandardEmails settings
body: Every other send* helper in this file checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail`/`eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` and accepts an `eventTypeMetadata` parameter. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and unconditionally emails organizer, team members and all attendees, breaking the documented ability to disable standard emails for an event type.

title: MultiEmail imports from its own package barrel, creating a circular import
body: `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui`, while `packages/ui/index.tsx` re-exports this module (`./form/MultiEmailLazy`). This self-referencing cycle can yield undefined components at runtime depending on module evaluation order/bundler. Import the components from their relative paths (e.g. `../components/button`) as the sibling form components do.

title: Initial empty email row makes the Add button always fail validation on first click
body: `multiEmailValue` defaults to `[""]`, so if the user presses "Add" without typing, `z.string().email()` fails on the empty string and the generic "Emails must be unique and valid" error is shown rather than the field being treated as empty. Also the `multiEmailValue.length === 0` guard never triggers for this default. Filter out blank entries before validating/submitting.

title: Add-guests action is offered for bookings where it cannot work
body: The new `add_members` entry is added unconditionally to `editBookingActions`, which is also rendered for past bookings (`isBookingInPast && isConfirmed`) and for pending bookings. Users can open the dialog and submit for bookings where adding guests is meaningless or will fail server-side. Gate the action on upcoming/confirmed (and non-seated) bookings.

title: retryCount delete branch is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The new OR branch in `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` matches any WorkflowReminder with `retryCount > 1` regardless of `method`. Since this SMS cron runs globally, it will delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP workflow reminders as soon as some other code path increments their retryCount (and any future retry logic added for those methods), silently dropping pending reminders. The branch should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`.

title: Retry count not incremented when message/sendTo is missing
body: If `message` is empty or `sendTo` is null, the reminder is neither scheduled nor its retryCount incremented, so it will be re-picked by every cron run until its scheduledDate passes — exactly the infinite-rescheduling problem this PR intends to fix (e.g. missing smsReminderNumber). Consider incrementing retryCount (or marking the reminder) in this case too.

title: deleteMany on retryCount has no supporting index
body: The new delete condition filters on `retryCount` alone (OR branch), which cannot use the existing `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` index and will force a full table scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron invocation. Scoping the condition to method/scheduled or adding an appropriate composite index would avoid this.

title: deleteMany OR branch deletes reminders of all methods, not just SMS
body: The new OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` constraint, so this SMS-only cron will delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder rows whenever their retryCount exceeds 1. Since retryCount is a shared column that other schedulers may also increment in the future (and the field is generic), this can silently destroy pending email/WhatsApp reminders. Add the method filter inside the OR branch.

title: Failure paths that never increment retryCount keep retrying forever
body: retryCount is only incremented when `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns falsy or throws. If `message` is empty/null or `sendTo` is missing (e.g. attendee without a phone number), the `if (message?.length ... && sendTo)` block is skipped entirely, the reminder stays `scheduled: false`, and the cron will keep picking it up every run until the scheduledDate passes — exactly the behaviour this PR intends to stop. Increment retryCount (or mark it) in that else case too.

title: deleteMany on retryCount has no supporting index
body: The new delete condition filters on `retryCount > 1` with no method/scheduledDate constraint and there is no index covering retryCount, so each cron run forces a full scan of WorkflowReminder (a high-volume table). Consider restricting the predicate to SMS + existing indexed columns or adding an appropriate index.

title: deleteMany OR branch deletes reminders of any method
body: The second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` filter, so this SMS cron will delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP workflow reminders too as soon as any other job/code path increments their retryCount past 1. Since the column is shared across all reminder methods, this risks silently destroying pending email/WhatsApp reminders. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to that branch.

title: Prisma update inside catch can throw and abort the whole cron run
body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` added at the start of the catch block is awaited outside of any try/catch. If the record was deleted concurrently (P2025) or the DB call fails, the rejection propagates out of the loop, the remaining unscheduled reminders are never processed and the endpoint returns a 500 with no response body written. Wrap this update in its own try/catch (and do it after logging).

title: Use atomic increment instead of read-modify-write for retryCount
body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` uses the value read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap (common with slow Twilio calls), both write the same value and one failure is lost, so a reminder can retry indefinitely. Use `{ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`.

title: No retry accounting when message or sendTo is missing
body: If `message` is empty or `sendTo` is null, the reminder is skipped without incrementing retryCount and without marking it scheduled, so it will be re-fetched every cron run until its scheduledDate passes — the exact loop this PR intends to stop. Increment retryCount (or mark it unschedulable) in this branch too.

title: Public `findMany` removed without updating callers
body: `InsightsBookingService.findMany()` was the only data-fetching entry point and has been replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which merely returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. No other files in this PR were updated, so any existing consumer calling `service.findMany({...})` will now fail to compile / throw at runtime. Either keep a `findMany` implemented on top of `$queryRaw`, or update all call sites in the same change.

title: Widened constructor options type loses discriminated-union safety
body: The constructor now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` where `scope` is a plain union and `teamId` is optional. Previously the discriminated union forced `teamId` to be present for `scope: "team"`. Now `{scope: "team", userId, orgId}` type-checks, zod parsing fails silently, `this.options` becomes null, and every query degrades to `1=0` (empty results) with no error surfaced — a hard-to-diagnose data bug.

title: Returned SQL fragments are not self-parenthesized, risking operator-precedence bugs
body: `buildFilterConditions`, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` can return top-level `OR`/`AND` expressions without surrounding parentheses (e.g. `"eventTypeId" = $1 OR "eventParentId" = $1`, or `(...) OR (...)` for team/org scope). `getBaseConditions` happens to wrap them, but `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` are public and documented as usable directly (the test interpolates conditions into `WHERE ${...}`). Any caller combining them with `AND` will get wrong, potentially authorization-bypassing results. Wrap each returned fragment in parentheses.

title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions mask an unreachable fallback
body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object (never null/undefined, and objects are always truthy), so the `else if (filterConditions)` and `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` branches are unreachable. This hides the intent: if auth conditions were ever intended to be optional, the fail-closed fallback would never trigger. Simplify to `authConditions` + optional filter, or make the types reflect reality.

title: Caching tests deleted without replacement
body: The `describe("Caching")` block covering `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` memoization was removed entirely. The caching logic still exists in the service (including the subtle `=== undefined` check that allows caching a `null` filter result), so this behaviour is now untested and regressions (e.g. re-querying memberships on every call) would go unnoticed.

title: Raw-query test asserts exact row shape that may not match driver output
body: `prisma.$queryRaw<{id:number}[]>` returns values with runtime types from the driver; if `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized.id` maps to a 64-bit integer the value comes back as `BigInt`, and `toEqual([{ id: userBooking.id }])` (a `number`) would fail. The PR description states the tests were never executed, so this assertion needs to be verified against an actual run.

title: Public `findMany` removed without updating callers
body: `findMany(findManyArgs)` was the only query-executing method of `InsightsBookingService` and has been replaced by `getBaseConditions()` returning a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. No other files in this PR are updated, so any existing consumer calling `insightsBookingService.findMany(...)` will fail to compile / break at runtime. Either keep a `findMany` wrapper that executes `$queryRaw` against "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized", or update all call sites in the same PR.

title: Constructor option type widened, losing discriminated-union safety
body: The constructor parameter type changed from the zod-derived discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to the loose `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` where `teamId` is optional for every scope. Callers can now pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without a `teamId` and it compiles; at runtime the zod validation fails silently and `options` becomes `null`, so the service returns `1=0` and the caller sees zero rows instead of a type error or explicit failure. Keep the union type (or at least surface the validation error).

title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions
body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always resolves to a `Prisma.Sql` (never null/undefined), so the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `return NOTHING_CONDITION` branches are unreachable. This hides the intent and could mask a future regression where auth conditions legitimately become empty — an empty auth condition would then fall through to returning only filter conditions, which would be an authorization bypass. Simplify to `authConditions` + optional filter, and assert auth is always present.

title: Caching tests deleted without replacement
body: The `describe("Caching")` block covering `cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` memoization was removed entirely, but the caching logic in `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` still exists (including the subtle `=== undefined` check needed because filter conditions may legitimately be `null`). Regressions that cause the conditions to be rebuilt on every call, or that break the null-caching case, are now untested.

title: Tests assert exact SQL string equality, making them brittle and weak
body: Comparing the returned `Prisma.Sql` with `toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)` asserts both the exact text fragments and parameter values. Any harmless reformatting/parenthesization change in the service breaks the suite, while semantic correctness (does the SQL actually restrict rows correctly?) is still untested for the team/org scopes. Consider asserting behaviour via `$queryRaw` for at least the team and org authorization scopes, as is done in the `getBaseConditions` test.

title: Public `findMany` removed without updating callers
body: `InsightsBookingService.findMany()` was deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment instead of executing a query. Any existing consumer of `findMany` (e.g. insights tRPC handlers) will fail to compile / break at runtime. The PR contains no updates to callers, so either they exist and are broken, or the method is dead code; either way this needs to be verified and the call sites migrated in the same change.

title: Constructor options type widened, losing discriminated-union safety
body: The constructor now takes `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` where `teamId?: number` is optional for all scopes, instead of the discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`. A caller can now pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` with no `teamId` and it type-checks; zod validation then fails silently and `this.options` becomes null, so authorization conditions degrade to `1=0` and insights return empty results with no error surfaced. Keep the union type (or at least require teamId for team scope).

title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions
body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always resolves to a non-null `Prisma.Sql` (it returns `NOTHING_CONDITION` in the fallback cases), so the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `return NOTHING_CONDITION` branches are unreachable. This is misleading: a reader may assume auth conditions can be absent and that filters alone can be used, which would be a security hole if the auth path ever returned null. Simplify to `authConditions` + optional filter.

title: toEqual against freshly-built Prisma.sql likely fails for composed SQL
body: The service builds multi-part conditions by nesting templates (`Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR (${condition})``), which produces a `Prisma.Sql` whose internal `strings`/`values` layout comes from flattening nested fragments. The test compares with `toEqual` against a single flat template literal containing the same final text. These objects are only deep-equal if the flattened `strings` array matches exactly; nesting typically yields different `strings` segmentation (and extra empty strings), so these assertions (team scope line 295, org scope line 332, combined filters line 429) will very likely fail. Compare `conditions.sql`/`text` and `conditions.values` instead, or run the SQL. The PR description itself admits the tests were never executed.

title: Caching behaviour is no longer covered
body: The two tests verifying that `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` memoize results were deleted, but the caching fields (`cachedAuthConditions`, `cachedFilterConditions`, including the `undefined` vs `null` distinction for filters) still exist in the service. A regression where a `null` filter result is recomputed on every call, or where cached SQL is reused incorrectly, would now go undetected.

title: deleteCache rejects team/delegation credentials and throws generic Error
body: The handler only accepts credentials whose `userId` equals the session user, so calendar credentials owned by a team (userId null, teamId set) or delegation-derived credentials can never have their cache cleared, even though the UI renders the "Delete cached data" item for them (the dropdown only checks `delegationCredentialId` for the disconnect action, not for cache deletion). It also throws a plain `Error` instead of a `TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN"/"NOT_FOUND" })`, which surfaces as a 500 internal error and leaks the message as an unexpected server failure instead of a proper authorization response.

title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data object
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` issues a Prisma `updateMany` with an empty `data` payload. Prisma does not guarantee that an empty update bumps `@updatedAt` (and for some providers it is a no-op / can error), so the stated intent ("Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt") is not reliably achieved. Pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` explicitly. Additionally, for in-memory delegation credentials `this.credential.id` can be negative/non-existent, making this an unnecessary write on every cache refresh. The PR description itself notes this field isn't consumed anywhere in the UI, so it may be dead work.

title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired cache shown as valid
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` aggregates `MAX(updatedAt)` for all `CalendarCache` rows of a credential with no filter on `expiresAt`. Rows that have already expired (and are therefore never served) still produce a `cacheUpdatedAt` value, so the UI reports an active cache and a "Last updated" time for credentials whose cache is effectively dead. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (or surface expiry separately).

title: Repository instantiated directly, bypassing calendar-cache feature gating
body: The handler constructs `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, which is the path that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the calendar-cache feature is disabled. This adds an unconditional DB `groupBy` on every connectedCalendars request even for installations/teams where calendar cache is off, and bypasses the mock abstraction the interface was designed for.

title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
body: The disconnect mutation invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations`, but `deleteCacheMutation` only calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. When `onSuccess`/`onChanged` isn't supplied (it is optional and is undefined in some call sites), the UI keeps showing the old `cacheUpdatedAt` after a successful delete, suggesting the cache still exists. Invalidate `connectedCalendars` in the mutation's `onSettled`.

title: Timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale and browser timezone
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's selected locale and time format preference, so non-English users see a US-formatted date inside otherwise translated text. Use the app locale (available via `useLocale`) and the user's `timeFormat`/timezone settings.

title: Script uses macOS-only sed syntax and a fragile relative .env path
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax; on GNU/Linux `sed -i ''` interprets the empty string as the script argument and fails, so the GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL rewrite silently errors for Linux contributors. Also `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the invocation directory, so running the script from the repo root writes/creates a `.env` one level above the repository.

title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx without adding tsx dependency
body: `dev:cron` now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not listed in dependencies/devDependencies (while the now-unused `ts-node` remains). `npx` will attempt an unpinned network install at run time, which fails offline/CI and gives a non-reproducible version. Add `tsx` as a devDependency (and drop `ts-node` if no longer used).

title: Migration warning comment contradicts the statement
body: The generated warning block says "Added the required column `updatedAt` ... without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the actual statement does add `DEFAULT NOW()`. Leaving the stale warning is misleading to anyone reviewing migration history; remove or correct it.

title: deleteCache throws plain Error instead of TRPCError
body: Throwing `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` from a tRPC handler surfaces as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) rather than a 403/404, and the message may be scrubbed in production. Use `TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN" })` so the client can distinguish an authorization failure from a server fault.

title: Credential ownership check misses team/delegation credentials
body: The handler only matches `credential.userId === user.id`. Credentials attached to a team (userId null, teamId set) or delegation-derived credentials will never match, so deleting their cache always fails; conversely there is no check that the user is allowed to act on team credentials at all. Consider mirroring the authorization logic used by `viewer.credentials.delete` (user OR team admin/owner) so behaviour is consistent and complete.

title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired caches are reported as fresh
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all CalendarCache rows for the credential with no `expiresAt` filter. The UI then shows "Cache Status / Last updated: …" for credentials whose cache entries are already expired and will no longer be served, which misleads users into believing caching is active. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (or surface expiry explicitly).

title: deleteCache success does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
body: The disconnect mutation invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, but the deleteCache mutation only calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. In the Alert branch of SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper (and anywhere `onChanged` is not passed) nothing invalidates the query, so the dropdown keeps showing a stale "Last updated" timestamp for a cache that was just deleted. Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in the mutation's onSettled.

title: Timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` formats the cache timestamp with US month/day ordering and 12-hour clock regardless of the user's locale/time format preference, producing confusing dates for non-US users. Use the user's locale (e.g. from `useLocale()`) or the existing date formatting helpers.

title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data relies on implicit @updatedAt and adds a write per cache refresh
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is intended to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, but it passes an empty data object, so it only has an effect if the model declares `@updatedAt`; otherwise it is a silent no-op while still issuing an UPDATE over every selected calendar of the credential on each cache population. The PR notes also state this value is never consumed by the frontend. Either set the field explicitly (`updatedAt: new Date()`) and document the consumer, or drop the call.

title: sed -i '' is macOS-only and ENV_FILE path is cwd-dependent
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` fails on GNU sed (Linux), where `-i ''` is interpreted as an empty script file name, so the script cannot update .env on Linux/CI. Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the current working directory, so running the script from the repo root writes/creates a `.env` outside the repository.

title: Migration header comment contradicts the statement
body: The generated warning says the column was added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", yet the statement adds `DEFAULT NOW()`. Leaving the stale warning in place is confusing for anyone auditing migrations; remove or correct it.

title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx without adding tsx as a dependency
body: `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` relies on npx fetching `tsx` from the network at run time (and may prompt for install), while `ts-node` remains a devDependency. Add `tsx` to devDependencies and invoke it via the local binary for reproducible, offline-capable runs.

title: No tests for new cache-status enrichment or deleteCache handler
body: The new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` repository method, the enrichment in connectedCalendarsHandler, and the deleteCache handler (including its authorization branch) have no unit tests. Given the authorization check in deleteCache guards data deletion, at least a test covering a credential owned by another user should be added.

title: deleteCache throws plain Error instead of TRPCError and ignores non-user credentials
body: The handler looks up the credential with `userId: user.id` only and throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` when not found. A plain Error surfaces to tRPC as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, so the client cannot distinguish auth failure from a real server error and the error is logged as an unexpected exception. It should throw `TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN" })`. Additionally, credentials owned by a team/organization or delegation credentials (userId null or different owner) can never be cleared through this endpoint even though the UI shows the action.

title: Cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
body: On successful `deleteCache`, only the optional `onSuccess` callback is invoked; unlike the disconnect mutation (which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in onSettled), no query invalidation happens. Since `connectedCalendars` is fetched with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, the dropdown continues to show the old "Last updated" timestamp and the delete option after the cache was deleted, until a full reload. Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` on settle.

title: Cache status never resolves for delegation credentials
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` queries CalendarCache by `credentialId`, but in-memory delegation credentials have synthetic negative ids and their cache rows are looked up by `userId` only (see getCachedAvailability's isInMemoryDelegationCredential branch). For delegation-based connections `cacheUpdatedAt` will therefore always be null and the UI will claim there is no cache even when one exists.

title: updateManyByCredentialId with empty data on every cache refresh
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` issues an UPDATE on every selected calendar of the credential each time availability is cached, solely to bump `updatedAt`. This value is not consumed anywhere in the UI (the UI uses CalendarCache.updatedAt), so it is a write amplification on a hot path (webhook handling / cron cache refresh) with no consumer. It also touches rows for calendars not involved in the refresh, and is a no-op for delegation credentials with negative ids. Either remove it or restrict it to the calendars actually refreshed.

title: Cache timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale/time format preference, so the "Last updated" timestamp is always rendered in US format (and 12h clock) regardless of the user's selected language or timeFormat setting. Use the locale from `useLocale()` / the user's timeFormat.

title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only and ENV_FILE path is relative to cwd
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` fails on Linux with GNU sed, which interprets the empty string as the input filename ("can't read : No such file or directory"), so the GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated for Linux contributors. Also `ENV_FILE="../.env"` resolves relative to the caller's working directory, so running the script from the repo root writes/creates a `.env` outside the repository.

title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx without adding tsx as a dependency
body: `"dev:cron": "npx tsx cron-tester.ts"` relies on `npx` fetching `tsx` from the network at runtime since `tsx` is not listed in dependencies/devDependencies (while the now-unused `ts-node` remains). This breaks offline/CI usage and pins no version. Add `tsx` as a devDependency (and drop ts-node if unused).

title: Migration warning comment contradicts the actual statement
body: The generated warning says the column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the statement does add `DEFAULT NOW()`. Leaving the stale warning is misleading to reviewers/operators evaluating migration safety; it should be removed or corrected.

title: No tests for new deleteCache handler or cache status enrichment
body: The new mutation performs a destructive `calendarCache.deleteMany` based on a user-supplied credentialId, and `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` feeds UI state, yet neither has unit tests covering authorization rejection (credential belonging to another user), deletion scope, or the credentialId→updatedAt mapping. Given the authorization-sensitive nature of the endpoint, tests should be added.

title: immediateDelete path leaves the WorkflowReminder row in the DB
body: In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, when `immediateDelete` is true the function cancels the scheduled send at SendGrid and returns without deleting (or updating) the `workflowReminder` row. Callers that use this path (handleNewBooking reschedule, workflows.tsx workflow/step deletion) therefore leave orphaned reminder rows with `scheduled: true` and a now-unusable `referenceId`. The row lingers until the cron's `deleteMany(scheduledDate <= now)` eventually removes it, and because `referenceId` is `@unique` a stale row can also block reuse. The non-immediate path at least marks `cancelled: true`; the immediate path should delete the row.

title: Reschedule path still uses immediate SendGrid cancellation, so the bug being fixed persists for reschedules
body: The PR's stated fix is to avoid SendGrid's 100-pending-cancellation limit by deferring cancellation to the cron (`cancelled: true`). However the reschedule path calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` with `immediateDelete = true`, which issues the `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` cancel immediately. Reschedules will therefore keep accumulating pending cancellations and can still fail once the limit is reached, meaning reminders for rescheduled bookings are still sent — exactly the reported issue (#7225) for the reschedule case. The same applies to workflow/step deletion in workflows.tsx.

title: Single SendGrid failure aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders
body: The cancellation loop is wrapped in one `try/catch` and `await`s the SendGrid request inside the loop. If any single `client.request` throws (e.g. invalid/expired batch_id, rate limit), the catch is hit and all remaining `remindersToCancel` in this run are skipped. Since the cancellation window is only 1 hour and the cron runs every 15 minutes, repeated failures on the same bad reminder will permanently prevent later reminders in the list from being cancelled, and their emails will be sent. The try/catch should be per-reminder inside the loop.

title: Cancellation query is not restricted to EMAIL reminders or non-null referenceId
body: `remindersToCancel` selects every `workflowReminder` with `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now+1h`, without filtering `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` or `referenceId: { not: null }`. Any non-email or reference-less row that ends up with `cancelled: true` would be sent to the SendGrid scheduled_sends endpoint with a null/foreign batch_id, which errors and (per the finding above) aborts the whole batch.

title: Unscheduled-reminder query does not exclude cancelled reminders
body: The `unscheduledReminders` query filters on `method: EMAIL, scheduled: false` but not `cancelled`. A reminder that was scheduled far in the future (stored with `scheduled: false`) and then cancelled on booking cancellation/reschedule will still be picked up by this cron and scheduled with SendGrid, so a reminder for a cancelled booking gets sent. Add `cancelled: null` / `not: true` to the where clause (or delete such rows).

title: PrismaPromise imported as a runtime value
body: The import was changed from `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise }` to a value import that includes `PrismaPromise`. `PrismaPromise` (and `Prisma` as used here) are type-only exports of @prisma/client; importing them in a value import can fail at build/runtime with isolatedModules/SWC transpilation ("PrismaPromise is not exported"). Keep these as `import type`.

title: Reminder cancellation promises are not awaited
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but invoked inside `forEach` without awaiting; the handler returns a 200 "Booking successfully cancelled" before the `cancelled: true` DB updates complete. In a serverless environment the function may be frozen/terminated before the updates are persisted, leaving reminders uncancelled. Collect the promises and `await Promise.all`.

title: try/catch cannot catch failures of the un-awaited async calls
body: The `try { originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)) } catch` block cannot catch errors from these promises since they are not awaited; a rejection would surface as an unhandled rejection rather than the intended `log.error`. Await the promises inside the try.

title: immediateDelete path cancels at SendGrid but never removes the WorkflowReminder row
body: When `immediateDelete` is true the function POSTs the cancel to SendGrid and returns early without deleting (or flagging) the `workflowReminder` row. Callers that previously deleted the row themselves no longer do (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts` for the original rescheduled booking). The result is rows left behind with `scheduled: true` and a referenceId that has already been cancelled; they linger until the cron's `deleteMany(scheduledDate <= now)` cleanup, and the cron's `cancelled` sweep will never touch them. At minimum this is stale data for reporting/queries; it also makes the semantics of the function inconsistent with the `!referenceId` branch, which does delete the row.

title: Cancellation sweep does not filter by method and aborts all remaining cancellations on first error
body: `remindersToCancel` queries only `cancelled: true` without `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`, so any non-email reminder that ever gets flagged cancelled will have its Twilio SID posted to the SendGrid `scheduled_sends` endpoint. More importantly the whole `for` loop is inside a single try/catch: if one SendGrid request fails (invalid/expired batch id, rate limit), the loop exits and every remaining reminder in this run is left uncancelled, so their emails may be sent before the next cron tick (the window is only 1 hour while the cron runs every 15 min, so a couple of failed runs is enough to leak reminders). Each reminder should be cancelled/deleted in its own try/catch and the query should be scoped to EMAIL.

title: SendGrid client API key is never set in this handler
body: `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` is called at module load, but `client` (`@sendgrid/client`) has no `client.setApiKey(...)` call in this file, unlike `emailReminderManager.ts` which does both. The new cancellation requests (and the existing `/v3/mail/batch` call) therefore go out unauthenticated and will fail with 401, meaning cancelled reminders are never actually cancelled — the exact bug this PR is meant to fix.

title: try/catch cannot catch failures from async reminder deletions
body: `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` invokes `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` without awaiting; the returned promises escape the surrounding try/catch. Although both helpers swallow their own errors internally today, any throw outside their try (or a future change) becomes an unhandled rejection rather than the logged error the code intends. The same pattern exists in `handleCancelBooking.ts` and `bookings.tsx`; consider `await Promise.all(...)`.

title: SMS reminder row is not deleted if twilio.cancelSMS throws
body: `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` share one try block. If cancelling fails (e.g. the message already left the queue, or a transient Twilio error), the DB row is never deleted and the reminder stays in the table indefinitely with `scheduled: true`. Deleting the row should be done regardless of the cancel result.

title: Malformed import (missing trailing comma) and type-only imports converted to value imports
body: The import block now reads `  TimeUnit,\n  Prisma\n} from "@prisma/client";` with no trailing comma and inconsistent formatting, which will fail the repo's prettier/lint check. Additionally `Prisma` and `PrismaPromise` were switched from `import type` to value imports here (and `App`/`Credential`/`EventTypeCustomInput`/`Prisma` in `handleNewBooking.ts`), which pulls type-only symbols into the runtime import graph unnecessarily.

title: Cron still schedules emails for reminders marked cancelled
body: The `unscheduledReminders` query filters only on `method: EMAIL`, `scheduled: false` and `scheduledDate <= now+72h`, but not on `cancelled`. Reminders for bookings that were cancelled/rescheduled before they were ever handed to SendGrid (i.e. created with `scheduled: false`, `referenceId: null`, then flagged `cancelled: true` by `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`) will therefore be picked up here, sent to SendGrid with a future `sendAt`, and the reminder email will be delivered for a cancelled booking — exactly the bug this PR aims to fix. Add `cancelled: { not: true }` (or delete such rows at cancel time when `referenceId` is null).

title: Cancellation loop aborts on first failure and does not filter method/referenceId
body: `remindersToCancel` is not filtered by `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` nor by `referenceId != null`. A row with `referenceId: null` (never scheduled) or an SMS row will produce a SendGrid POST with `batch_id: null`/a Twilio SID, which throws. Because the whole `for` loop is inside a single `try`, one such failure aborts cancellation of every remaining reminder in the batch, so other scheduled emails for cancelled bookings are still sent. Filter the query and wrap each request in its own try/catch.

title: immediateDelete path leaves orphan WorkflowReminder rows
body: When `immediateDelete` is true the SendGrid send is cancelled and the function returns early without deleting (or flagging) the `workflowReminder` row. Callers using this path (handleNewBooking reschedule, workflow/step deletion in workflows.tsx) therefore leave rows pointing at steps/bookings whose reminders no longer exist. For workflow/step deletion the cascade cleans up, but for the reschedule path the old booking is only cancelled, so stale reminder rows accumulate until their `scheduledDate` passes. Delete the row after the successful cancel request.

title: PrismaPromise imported as a value from @prisma/client
body: `PrismaPromise` (and in part `Prisma`) was changed from `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise }` to a value import. `PrismaPromise` is a type-only export of @prisma/client; importing it in a value import statement makes the bundler/runtime try to resolve a non-existent runtime binding, which can break the build or throw at module load. Keep it as a type-only import.

title: Reminder cancellation promises are not awaited
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but called without `await` inside `forEach`, and their results are no longer added to `prismaPromises`. The handler can return (and the serverless function can be frozen/terminated) before the `workflowReminder` update/delete or the Twilio cancel completes, so reminders may silently stay active. Collect the promises and await them. The same pattern exists in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (requestReschedule) and `handleNewBooking.ts`, where the surrounding try/catch also cannot catch rejections of un-awaited promises.

title: appStore map invokes import() eagerly, so nothing is actually lazy-loaded
body: Each property is initialized with `import("./app")` evaluated at module-evaluation time, so importing `@calcom/app-store` immediately starts loading every app package (and bundlers will include them all in the graph). The only change versus the previous static imports is that consumers must now `await`; there is no deferral and no bundle-size/cold-start win. To get the intended async behaviour the values must be thunks (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) resolved on demand.

title: Eagerly created import promises can produce unhandled rejections
body: Because all ~28 dynamic import promises are created at module load, a failure in any single app module (missing dependency, throwing top-level code) results in a rejected promise that nobody awaits unless that specific app is used. In Node this surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection and can terminate the process, even for apps the request never touches. Deferring the import until the app is requested avoids this.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in the `calendar` field, breaking external consumers
body: `getCalendar` is now async, so `getCalendarCredentials()[n].calendar` is a `Promise<Calendar | null>` rather than `Calendar | null`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated (it awaits `item.calendar`). Any other caller of `getCalendarCredentials` that uses `.calendar` directly (e.g. API/trpc handlers for connected calendars, availability code) will now silently operate on a Promise object, producing runtime errors or truthy-but-useless values. All call sites need auditing/updating.

title: apiDeletes is populated inside an async forEach callback and is never awaited for recurring cancellations
body: In the recurring-booking branch, `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })` returns immediately; the awaits inside resolve after `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` has already run with an empty/partial array. Calendar deletions for remaining recurring instances are therefore unobserved: failures are swallowed as unhandled rejections and the response can be returned before any event is deleted. Use a `for...of` loop with `await`, or push the promises (not awaited results) synchronously.

title: forEach with async callback escapes the surrounding try/catch and is not awaited
body: Changing the callback to `async` means `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` fires off floating promises: the enclosing try/catch can no longer catch errors from `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` (they become unhandled rejections), and the function returns/sends the reschedule email before the calendar/video events are deleted. Replace with `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { await ... }` or `await Promise.all(map(...))`.

title: forEach with async callback escapes the surrounding try/catch and is not awaited
body: Same problem as the vital variant: the async callback passed to `forEach` is not awaited, so errors from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting` bypass the enclosing try/catch (becoming unhandled rejections) and cancellation of the external calendar/video events may not have happened by the time the function returns true and the email is sent.

title: requestReschedule fires un-awaited async forEach for calendar/video deletion
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { await getCalendar(...) ... })` creates floating promises. The mutation continues to send the reschedule email and webhooks and returns to the client while the deleteEvent/deleteMeeting calls may still be pending, and any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection with no logging. Await the deletions (for...of or Promise.all) before proceeding.

title: Commented example path is wrong
body: The placeholder comment reads `// example: import("./example")`, but the example app lives in `_example` (the previous code commented `import * as example from "./_example"`). Anyone uncommenting it will get a module-not-found error.

title: Dynamic imports are invoked eagerly, defeating the lazy-loading goal
body: The appStore object calls `import("./applecalendar")` etc. at module-evaluation time, so every app package is loaded as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported. The only difference from the previous static imports is that consumers now have to `await` the values; nothing is actually deferred (bundle size and startup cost are unchanged, and in webpack all chunks are requested immediately). To get real async loading the values must be thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, with call sites doing `await appStore[key]()`.

title: Eagerly created import promises can produce unhandled rejections
body: Because each `import(...)` promise is created at module load, any app module that throws during initialization (e.g. missing env/app keys) produces a rejected promise that nobody is awaiting at that moment. In Node this surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection and can crash the process (or at minimum log a fatal warning), even for apps the request never touches. With lazy thunks the rejection would only occur where it is awaited and handled.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in the `calendar` field, breaking external consumers
body: `getCalendar` became async, but `getCalendarCredentials` still stores its result synchronously, so `item.calendar` is now a `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`. `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to await it, but any other caller of `getCalendarCredentials` that uses `.calendar` directly (e.g. to call `listCalendars()`/`getAvailability()`) will now be operating on a Promise and fail at runtime. Either make `getCalendarCredentials` async and resolve the calendars, or audit/update all consumers.

title: async forEach pushes deletions into apiDeletes after they are awaited
body: In the recurring-cancellation branch the callback is `async` and now awaits `getCalendar(credential)` before pushing into `apiDeletes`. The surrounding `forEach` does not wait, so execution continues to `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) while `apiDeletes` is still empty; the calendar deletions are fired after the response is computed and their errors become unhandled rejections. Replace with a `for ... of` loop and await, or collect the promises synchronously.

title: Unused awaited calendar in recurring branch
body: `const calendar = await getCalendar(calendarCredential)` is computed before the branch, but in the recurring path a new `calendar` is fetched inside the loop, so the outer one is unused. This performs an unnecessary credential/calendar instantiation (and now an extra module load) on every recurring cancellation.

title: async callback inside forEach escapes the try/catch and is never awaited
body: Changing the `forEach` callback to `async` means the returned promises are discarded: the enclosing `try/catch` can no longer catch failures of `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` (they become unhandled rejections), and the function returns/sends the reschedule email before the calendar/video events are actually deleted. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => ...))` instead.

title: async callback inside forEach escapes the try/catch and is never awaited
body: Same issue as the vital reschedule: making the `forEach` callback `async` means its promise is dropped, so errors from `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` bypass the surrounding `try/catch` and become unhandled rejections, and the function continues (sending emails, returning true) before the external events are deleted. Use `Promise.all` over `map` and await it.

title: requestReschedule fires calendar/video deletions without awaiting them
body: The `forEach` callback is now `async` and awaits `getCalendar`, but the loop does not await the resulting promises. The mutation proceeds to send the reschedule email and webhooks and returns while deletions are still pending; in a serverless environment the function may terminate before they run, leaving stale calendar/video events, and any error becomes an unhandled rejection. Collect the promises with `map` and `await Promise.all`.

title: Noisy info log of CalendarService on every getCalendar call
body: `log.info("calendarApp", calendarApp.lib.CalendarService)` logs the service class on every calendar resolution, which now happens on every booking/cancel/availability path. This is debug-level noise in production logs and should be removed or downgraded.

title: import() invoked eagerly at module load defeats lazy loading
body: The object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")` etc. immediately when `packages/app-store/index.ts` is evaluated, so every app module is still loaded (and its side effects run) on first access to the app store. The only change versus static imports is that consumers must now `await`; there is no code-splitting or startup-time benefit. To actually defer loading, the values must be thunks (`applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and call sites must invoke them. Additionally, if any of these module evaluations rejects, the stored promise has no attached handler at creation time, producing an unhandled promise rejection that can crash the Node process even if no code ever reads that app.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in `calendar`, breaking other consumers
body: `getCalendar` is now async, so `getCalendarCredentials()` returns items whose `calendar` field is a `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` in this file was updated to `await item.calendar`. Any other caller of `getCalendarCredentials` that uses `.calendar` directly (e.g. truthiness checks or method calls) will now silently treat a promise as a calendar object, and a rejected promise that is never awaited becomes an unhandled rejection. All consumers of this return shape need auditing/updating.

title: async callback in forEach: deletions not awaited and errors escape try/catch
body: Changing the `forEach` callback to `async` means the loop returns immediately; the calendar/video deletions are fire-and-forget. The surrounding `try/catch` can no longer catch failures (rejections happen after the catch block has been left), so errors become unhandled promise rejections instead of being logged, and the function proceeds to send the reschedule email (and returns) before the external events are actually deleted. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` instead.

title: async callback in forEach: deletions not awaited and errors escape try/catch
body: The `forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` callback returns a promise that nobody awaits, so the external calendar/video deletions run detached. The enclosing `try/catch` no longer captures their failures (they surface as unhandled rejections), and the email is sent and the function returns before deletion completes. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`.

title: requestReschedule deletions are fire-and-forget after making callback async
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` is not awaited, so calendar event deletion / meeting deletion now happen after the tRPC mutation has already responded. Failures become unhandled rejections with no logging, and in serverless environments the process may be frozen before the deletes complete, leaving orphaned calendar events. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletes pushed into apiDeletes after it is already awaited
body: In the recurring branch the callback passed to `forEach` is `async` and awaits `getCalendar(credential)` plus `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` before `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)`. Because `forEach` does not await, control returns immediately and `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) runs with an `apiDeletes` array that is still empty for these entries. The recurring calendar deletions are therefore neither awaited nor error-handled; with the extra `await getCalendar` introduced here the race is now guaranteed rather than incidental. Collect the promises synchronously (e.g. `for ... of` with awaited getCalendar, pushing the unawaited deleteEvent promise).

title: Noisy log.info of CalendarService constructor on every calendar resolution
body: `log.info("calendarApp", calendarApp.lib.CalendarService)` runs on every call to `getCalendar`, which is on the hot path for availability, booking creation and cancellation. It serializes a class constructor into logs on every request, adding noise and overhead with no diagnostic value. This looks like leftover debug output and should be removed or downgraded to debug.

title: Working-hours check computes `end` from the slot start, not the slot end
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start`. The intent is clearly to compare the slot's end time (`start + eventLength`) against `workingHour.endTime`. As written, a slot that begins inside working hours but ends after them is treated as available, so bookings can overrun the host's availability. (The condition is also an OR of two checks inside a `.find()` whose truthiness means "outside working hours", so the duplicated value silently disables the end-boundary check.)

title: Date override short-circuits the busy/booking check, so booked slots become available
body: When any date override matches the slot's date, `dateOverrideExist` is set and the function returns `true` immediately (line 133-135), skipping the `busy.every(...)` loop below. Consequently, on a day that has a date override, existing bookings, calendar busy times and reserved slots are ignored and already-occupied slots are offered as available, leading to double bookings. The busy check must still run after override-boundary validation.

title: Dayjs objects compared with `===`, condition is always false
body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two distinct Dayjs object references, which is never true. The intended "unavailable/zero-length override" case (start equals end, i.e. the whole day marked unavailable) is therefore never detected, so slots on a fully-blocked override day are not rejected here. Use `.isSame(...)`.

title: Date overrides of all users are applied to every host's availability check
body: `checkIfIsAvailable` receives the per-user `schedule` spread (`...schedule`) for fixed hosts, but the `dateOverrides` list built at line 410 is the flattened list of overrides for *all* users (it carries `userId`), and the override matching at line 106 never filters by `userId`. An override belonging to one host therefore sets `dateOverrideExist`/rejects slots for a different host, producing wrong availability for team events.

title: Override start/end converted with hour()*60+minute() loses day rollover
body: After applying `offset`, the start/end are reduced to minutes-since-midnight via `hour() * 60 + minute()`. If the timezone offset pushes the override across midnight (common for large offsets, e.g. an organizer override near the end of the day viewed from a far-west/east invitee timezone), the resulting `startTime` can exceed `endTime`, and `buildSlots` skips such ranges (`if (start >= end) continue`). The override day then shows no slots at all instead of the shifted window.

title: `override.timeZone` is optional; undefined falls back to server local timezone
body: `TimeRange.timeZone` was added as optional in packages/types/schedule.d.ts, and `dayjs(...).tz(undefined)` resolves to the process-local timezone. Any caller of `getSlots` that does not populate `timeZone` on date overrides (all callers other than the trpc slots router) will compute `organizerUtcOffset` from the server timezone, silently shifting overrides by an arbitrary amount. Either make `timeZone` required for overrides or fall back to an explicit organizer timezone.

title: No test for the PR's main fix (fixed-host date overrides in round-robin)
body: The PR claims to fix that date overrides of fixed hosts are honoured for ROUND_ROBIN events (issue #8207/#8329), but the only added test re-runs the existing single-user date-override scenario with a different invitee timezone and expects identical UTC slots. There is no scenario with a ROUND_ROBIN event type, a fixed host with a date override and an available round-robin host, so the new `checkIfIsAvailable` date-override/working-hours logic for fixed hosts is untested and regressions would go unnoticed.

title: Any date override on the slot's day short-circuits the busy-time check
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, after the date-override loop, `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` returns availability immediately whenever a date override exists for the slot's day. This skips the `busy.every(...)` check below, so existing bookings, calendar busy times and buffers are completely ignored on days that have a date override, allowing double bookings on those days.

title: Working-hours end boundary computed from slot start, ignoring event length
body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates the `start` computation instead of using `slotEndTime`. The check `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore never accounts for the event duration, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after them is treated as available.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === (always false)
body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset,'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset,'minutes'))` compares two freshly created Dayjs object references, which is never true. The intent (detecting a zero-length override, i.e. a day marked unavailable) is never reached, so days blocked out via a start==end override are still offered as bookable.

title: Date-override day comparison uses local-time formatting and a hand-rolled offset
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset,'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD')` parses the stored UTC override date in the server's local timezone and then shifts it by `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1`, which reinterprets the UTC instant as organizer wall time. The resulting day string can be off by one day depending on the server TZ, causing overrides to be matched to the wrong date (slots wrongly allowed/blocked). Use explicit `dayjs.utc(...)`/`.tz(organizerTimeZone)` conversions instead.

title: Override timezone may be undefined and minute-of-day conversion drops day wrap
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` is called with `timeZone` typed optional (`TimeRange.timeZone?`); when it is undefined dayjs falls back to the local/system timezone, silently producing a wrong organizer offset. Additionally start/end are reduced to `hour()*60 + minute()` after applying the offset, so when the offset pushes the range across midnight (e.g. organizer 22:00-23:00 viewed from a +6h invitee tz) the computed endTime becomes smaller than startTime and the override yields no slots at all instead of the correct range.

title: Spread order can overwrite the injected userId on date overrides
body: `{ userId: availability.user.id, timeZone: availability.timeZone, ...override }` spreads the override last, so if an override object carries its own `userId` (the `TimeRange` type declares `userId?: number | null`) it overwrites the intended user id, breaking the per-user override matching in `getSlots`. Put the explicit fields after the spread.

title: New test does not exercise the behaviour the PR fixes
body: The added assertion calls getSchedule with `Asia/Dhaka` and expects exactly the same UTC slots as the `Asia/Kolkata` call, so it would also pass with the old (broken) override handling — it asserts nothing timezone-specific. Also, the PR's main claim (date overrides of fixed hosts being respected for ROUND_ROBIN events) has no test at all; a round-robin scenario with a fixed host override should be added.

title: Working-hours check uses slot start twice, ignoring event length
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` computes `end` from the slot *start* instead of `slotEndTime`. As a result the check `end > workingHour.endTime` can never detect a slot whose end extends past the end of working hours, so bookings that overrun the organizer's availability are still offered. It should be derived from `slotEndTime`.

title: Working-hours filter rejects slot if any single working-hours entry doesn't contain it
body: The `workingHours.find(...)` predicate returns true for the first entry that does not contain the slot (different day or different time block), and any truthy result makes the function return `false` (unavailable). With multiple availability rows (e.g. split hours 9-12 and 14-18, or several day groups) virtually every slot matches some non-containing entry and is wrongly marked unavailable. The logic must be inverted: the slot is unavailable only if *no* working-hours entry contains it.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === (always false)
body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two distinct Dayjs object references, which is never true. The intended "full-day unavailable override (start == end)" branch is therefore dead code, so zero-length overrides marking a day unavailable are not handled as designed; use `.isSame()`.

title: Override day comparison mixes server-local and UTC formatting
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` formats in the server's local timezone while `slotStartTime.format(...)` is UTC (`time.utc()`). On any server not running in UTC the day strings can differ, so overrides are matched to the wrong day (or not matched), making slots wrongly available/unavailable depending on deployment timezone. Both sides should be computed in the same, explicit timezone.

title: Override timeZone may be undefined, silently falling back to server local time
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` is called with `override.timeZone` typed as optional (`TimeRange.timeZone?: string`). When undefined, dayjs falls back to the server's local zone, producing an incorrect `organizerUtcOffset` and therefore shifting date-override slots by an arbitrary amount. Guard with a required timezone or an explicit UTC default.

title: Override start/end converted to minutes-of-day loses day boundary crossings
body: `startTime`/`endTime` are computed as `hour()*60 + minute()` after applying the invitee/organizer offset. If the offset pushes the override past midnight (common for large timezone differences) the resulting minute-of-day wraps, so endTime can become smaller than startTime (or 0 for midnight) and the override yields no slots or a bogus range. The conversion needs to account for day overflow (e.g. add 1440 when the date shifts).

title: New timezone override assertion can pass with missing slots
body: The `toHaveTimeSlots` matcher only iterates the *actual* slots with `.every` and never compares array lengths, so a result containing a subset (or zero) of the expected slots for that date passes. The newly added `+6:00` timezone assertion therefore does not actually guarantee the date-override timezone fix; add a length/exact-array comparison.

title: Migration crashes when `embed_category` site setting row is absent
body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes at least one row. On the vast majority of sites the `embed_category` setting was never set (no row in site_settings) or doesn't match a category name, so the result set is empty and `[0]` is nil, raising NoMethodError and aborting the migration (and the whole deploy). Same risk on line 15 if `uncategorized_category_id` has no row. Use `.first` with a nil check / COALESCE instead.

title: Un-escaped interpolation of site setting value into INSERT
body: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` interpolates the old `embeddable_hosts` setting value straight into SQL. A host containing a single quote (data entered by an admin, or garbage left in the settings table) breaks the statement or allows arbitrary SQL execution during migration. Use `quote()`/bind parameters.

title: `create_table ... force: true` can silently drop an existing table
body: `force: true` issues DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating. If this migration is ever re-run, or a table named embeddable_hosts already exists, existing data is destroyed without warning. Drop the `force: true` option for a forward migration.

title: Migrated host values are not normalized, so embedding breaks after upgrade
body: Old `embeddable_hosts` values could be of the form `http://example.com` or `https://example.com/1234` (the old code explicitly stripped schemes). The migration inserts the raw lines, bypassing the model's before_validation that strips scheme and path. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against `URI(referer).host`, so rows like `http://example.com` will never match and previously-working embeds will start raising InvalidAccess after the upgrade.

title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally. Creating/validating an EmbeddableHost with a nil host (e.g. `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?`, or the admin controller when `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is missing) raises NoMethodError on nil instead of producing a validation error / 400. Guard with `return if host.blank?`. `sub!` also mutates the caller's string in place, which can raise on frozen string literals.

title: record_for_host does not downcase the incoming host
body: The query is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but `host` comes from `URI(x).host` without `.downcase`. A referer such as `http://EvilTrout.com/page` yields `EvilTrout.com`, which never equals the lower-cased column value, so a legitimately configured host is rejected (embedding returns InvalidAccess). Downcase the parameter.

title: Unknown id causes a 500 instead of 404 in update/destroy
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil; `save_host(nil)` then calls `nil.host =` and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 error. Use `find_by` plus `raise Discourse::NotFound` (or `find`) so a deleted/invalid id yields a proper 404.

title: `update` is a no-op but is presented as a save action
body: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` ignores the request body entirely and just re-serializes the current state. The client's `saveChanges` action (`admin-embedding.js.es6`) calls `embedding.update({})` and will appear to succeed while persisting nothing. Either implement the update or remove the route/action so admins aren't misled.

title: `*_ids` hydration crashes on null or non-array values
body: The new branch does `obj[k].map(...)` whenever a key matches `/(.+)_id(s?)$/` with a plural suffix. If a serializer emits `foo_ids: null` (common for empty/absent associations) or a scalar, this throws TypeError and breaks hydration of the whole payload. Guard with `Array.isArray(obj[k])` / a null check; note `hydrated || []` after the map never helps because map always returns an array.

title: No presence validation on category_id while the column is NOT NULL
body: The migration declares `category_id` NOT NULL but the model has no `validates_presence_of :category_id`. Only the admin controller patches in `uncategorized_category_id`; any other code path (fabricators, console, future callers) that saves without a category raises a raw ActiveRecord::NotNullViolation instead of a validation error.

title: Fabricator file contents swapped between files
body: `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` now contains the category fabricators and `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` contains the embeddable_host fabricator. It works because all fabricator files are loaded, but it makes the definitions unfindable by name and will confuse anyone editing category fabricators. Swap the contents back.

title: New host with no chosen category shows no category badge
body: When adding a host without picking a category, `categoryId` stays null; the server defaults to uncategorized, but the client sets `host.category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(null)` (undefined), so the row renders an empty category cell until a reload. Use the category_id returned by the server response instead of the local `categoryId`.

title: Migration crashes when no category matches embed_category
body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes at least one row is returned. On the overwhelming majority of sites the `embed_category` site setting row does not exist (it is never saved unless changed), so the result set is empty and `[0]` is `nil`, raising `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil`. Every such site fails to migrate. Use a nil-safe fetch (e.g. `rows.first && rows.first['id'].to_i`) before falling back to uncategorized.

title: Unescaped host value interpolated into INSERT statement
body: The host string comes from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting and is interpolated directly into SQL: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. A host containing a single quote (or any SQL metacharacter) breaks the statement or allows SQL injection during migration. Use `quote(h)` / a parameterized insert. Additionally the raw value is not stripped of `http://`/paths like `EmbeddableHost`'s before_validation does, so migrated rows will not match `record_for_host` lookups and embedding will silently break after upgrade.

title: create_table force: true in migration can drop an existing table
body: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` issues a DROP TABLE IF EXISTS first. If the migration is re-run or the table already exists for any reason, existing embeddable host rows are destroyed without warning. Also, because the migration uses `execute` inside `change` (including a destructive `DELETE FROM site_settings`), it is not reversible; it should be split into `up`/`down`.

title: has_many with embed: :ids does not include the host objects, admin page will show no hosts
body: `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids` serializes only `embeddable_host_ids` and does not sideload the actual `embeddable_hosts` array. The Ember store's `_hydrateEmbedded` looks up the ids in `root['embeddable_hosts']`, which is absent, so hydration yields `undefined` entries and the embedding admin template renders empty/broken rows. Use `embed: :ids, include: true` (or sideload the collection explicitly).

title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError on unknown id
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a missing/deleted record; `save_host(nil)` then calls `host.host =` and `destroy` on nil, producing a 500 instead of a 404. Use `find_by` plus `raise Discourse::NotFound` (or `find`).

title: before_validation raises on nil host instead of failing validation
body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally in `before_validation`. Creating/saving an `EmbeddableHost` with a nil host (e.g. an admin submitting a blank host — the controller assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly) raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil`, returning a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if host.present?` and add `validates_presence_of :host`.

title: Host lookup is not case-insensitive on the input side
body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the value derived from the referer/URL. A referer such as `http://EvilTrout.com/page` yields `uri.host == "EvilTrout.com"`, which never matches the lowercased column, so legitimate embeds are rejected with 'invalid referer host'. Pass `host.downcase`.

title: No uniqueness constraint or index on host
body: Nothing prevents two `embeddable_hosts` rows with the same host (the model has no uniqueness validation and the migration adds no unique index). `record_for_host` then silently picks an arbitrary row, making the category used for embedded topics nondeterministic. Add a uniqueness validation and a unique index on `lower(host)`.

title: PostCreator `category:` option now receives an id instead of a name
body: The previous code passed `category: SiteSetting.embed_category`, a category name string; the new code passes `eh.try(:category_id)`, an integer.
