If PostCreator's `category` option is resolved by name, the embedded topic will land in no/uncategorized category instead of the configured one. Verify PostCreator's contract and pass `category_id` (or the name) accordingly — the added spec only asserts equality when the fabricated host's category happens to resolve.

title: Plural embedded hydration assumes array and keeps undefined entries
body: `obj[k].map(...)` is called without checking that `obj[k]` is an array; any attribute whose name matches `(.+)_ids$` but holds null/a scalar throws a TypeError during hydration. Additionally, unlike the singular branch, the plural branch deletes the original `_ids` key unconditionally and stores entries that may be `undefined` when a sub-object is not sideloaded, silently producing a collection of undefined models (which is exactly what happens with the embedding payload).

title: replace('_','-') only converts the first underscore
body: `type.replace('_', '-')` without the `g` flag replaces only the first underscore, so a future admin model type with two or more underscores (e.g. `site_customization_thing`) would not match an entry in ADMIN_MODELS and would be requested from the non-admin path. Use `.replace(/_/g, '-')`.

title: Embedding#update is a no-op
body: `update` performs no state change but returns 200 with the serialized embedding, and the client's `saveChanges` calls `embedding.update({})`. Any future/implied 'save settings' action on this page silently does nothing, which is misleading to callers. Either implement the update or drop the route and the client action.

title: Fabricator file contents swapped between category and embeddable_host files
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators. The file names no longer describe their contents, which will confuse anyone looking for `Fabricate(:category)` or `Fabricate(:private_category)`. Swap the contents.

title: No request specs for the new embeddable hosts endpoints
body: The only assertion is that the controller subclasses Admin::AdminController. The new create/update/destroy actions (including the nil-record paths and the uncategorized-category fallback) and the embedding show/update endpoints are untested, so regressions such as the 500 on a missing id would not be caught.

title: Migration crashes when no `embed_category` site setting row exists
body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes at least one row. On the vast majority of sites the `embed_category` setting is unset (no row in site_settings) or doesn't match a category name, so the result set is empty and `[0]` is nil, raising NoMethodError and aborting the migration/deploy. Guard with a presence check before dereferencing. The same applies to the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup, which also returns no row when the setting was never persisted.

title: `create_table ... force: true` and raw string interpolation in migration
body: `force: true` issues a DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating, so re-running the migration (or running it on a DB where the table already has rows) silently destroys existing embeddable_hosts data. Additionally line 25 interpolates `#{h}` (a value taken from the old site setting) directly into an INSERT string without quoting/escaping, so a host value containing a single quote breaks the SQL (and is an injection vector in a migration). Use `force: false`/no force and bind/quote the value (e.g. `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)`).

title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally in before_validation. Saving an EmbeddableHost with a nil host (e.g. admin submits an empty host, or `EmbeddableHost.new.save`) raises NoMethodError on nil instead of producing a validation error, resulting in a 500 from the admin controller. Guard with `return if host.blank?`.

title: Case-sensitive host lookup and inconsistent return value
body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` compares the lowercased stored host against the raw `uri.host`, which is not downcased. A referer like `https://EvilTrout.com` yields host `EvilTrout.com` and never matches the stored `eviltrout.com`, so legitimate embeds are rejected. Downcase the argument. Also `record_for_host` returns `false` on parse failure but `nil`/record otherwise, which is an inconsistent contract for callers such as `TopicEmbed.import`.

title: update/destroy raise 500 on unknown id
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil; `save_host(nil)` then calls `host.host =` and `destroy` on nil, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of a 404/400. Use `find_by` plus an explicit not-found response, or `find`.

title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding does nothing
body: `update` only re-serializes the freshly fetched state and ignores the request body, so the client's `saveChanges` action (admin-embedding controller `embedding.update({})`) is a silent no-op. Either implement the update or remove the route/UI action so administrators are not misled into thinking changes were saved.

title: `*_ids` hydration crashes / produces undefined entries
body: The new branch assumes `obj[k]` is an array for any key matching `_ids` and calls `.map` on it; a scalar or null value (common for server payloads) throws a TypeError. Also, when `_lookupSubType` cannot resolve an id (sub-collection missing from the payload), `map` yields `undefined` entries and the original `_ids` key is deleted regardless, so the caller loses the ids and gets a list of undefineds. Guard with `Ember.isArray` and filter out unresolved entries (or keep the ids when nothing resolves, as the singular branch does).

title: Only the first underscore is converted when matching admin models
body: `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the first occurrence (no /g, no regex), so a multi-word admin type such as `embeddable_host_thing` or any future `a_b_c` type will not match the dash-separated entries in ADMIN_MODELS and will be routed to `/` instead of `/admin/`. Use `replace(/_/g, '-')`.

title: No uniqueness validation on host
body: Nothing prevents creating two EmbeddableHost rows with the same host but different categories; `record_for_host` then arbitrarily returns whichever `.first` the DB yields, making the category assignment for imported topics nondeterministic. Add a uniqueness validation (and ideally a unique index).

title: Fabricator file contents swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines the category fabricators. The file names no longer match their contents, which will confuse anyone looking for these definitions; swap the contents back.

title: Second `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the 4-arg version
body: Two `def self.downsize` methods are defined: the 4-argument `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` at line 145 and the 3-argument `(from, to, dimensions, opts)` at line 149. In Ruby the later definition wins, so the 4-arg form no longer exists. Any existing caller doing `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100)` now raises ArgumentError (or silently passes `100` as dimensions and `100` as opts). Keep one method, e.g. accept a dimensions string only, and update all callers.

title: Removal of public helper `self.dimensions` and signature change of `optimize`
body: `self.dimensions(width, height)` was removed and `self.optimize` changed from `(operation, from, to, width, height, opts)` to `(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts)`. These are public class methods that plugins/other code may call; the change breaks them without deprecation.

title: Downsizing in place (from == to) can corrupt or truncate the tempfile
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` reads and writes the same path. ImageMagick's `convert` reading and writing the same file is unreliable, and the Ruby `Tempfile` object still has an open handle whose position/metadata is stale after the external process rewrites the file; `tempfile.size` and subsequent `Upload.create_for(... tempfile ...)` may see stale/incorrect data. Convert to a separate temp path and then replace/reopen the tempfile.

title: Downsize loop ignores failures and can spin without progress
body: The while loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to 5 times but never checks its boolean return value. If convert fails (missing binary, unsupported file), the file size never changes and the loop just burns 5 shell invocations per upload, then proceeds to create an upload that will be rejected for size. Check the return value and break/report an error on failure.

title: Animated-GIF detection fails for tempfile paths
body: `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects the animated (gifsicle) code path via `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. A Rails uploaded `tempfile.path` normally ends in a random suffix (e.g. `RackMultipart2014...`), not `.gif`, so animated GIFs will be processed with `convert ...[0]`, flattening animation to the first frame even when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is on. Detect the type from the original filename/content type instead.

title: Hardcoded 10.megabytes download limit replaces configurable setting
body: `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` was replaced by a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. Sites configured to allow larger images (or intentionally smaller limits) no longer have their setting respected for API URL uploads; this also bypasses an administrator-configured resource limit. Use a setting (e.g. a new max upload size setting) instead of a magic constant.

title: Client-side size validation hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
body: `maxSizeKB` was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. Non-image attachments and sites with a different configured max size now get wrong client-side validation: files between the configured limit and 10MB are uploaded and then rejected by the server, and sites allowing >10MB attachments are blocked in the browser. The error message also reports a wrong limit to users.

title: 413 error message reports a hardcoded, possibly wrong size limit
body: In `displayErrorForUpload`, the 413 branch now shows a hardcoded 10MB limit instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. If the web server or site setting limit differs, the user is told an incorrect maximum size.

title: No tests for the new auto-downsize path
body: The new downsizing loop in `create_upload` (retry count, size threshold, non-image skip, failure handling) has no accompanying spec. Given it mutates the user's uploaded file in place, regressions would silently corrupt uploads.

title: Duplicate self.downsize definition silently overrides 4-arg version
body: Two `self.downsize` methods are defined (lines 145-147 with `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` and lines 149-151 with `(from, to, dimensions, opts)`). In Ruby the second definition replaces the first, so any existing caller using `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height)` will now pass `height` as the `opts` hash position and raise ArgumentError or build wrong instructions. Use a single method with an optional/flexible signature.

title: Downsize loop can spin without shrinking and ignores failures
body: The loop repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%")` while `tempfile.size` exceeds the limit. `tempfile.size` on an already-opened Tempfile may be cached/stale after the external `convert` rewrites the file on disk (the Ruby File object's size is read via fstat, but the file position/content is replaced out of band), so the check may not reflect the new size. Also the return value of `downsize` is ignored: if `convert` fails, the loop still runs 5 times and the oversized file is then passed to `Upload.create_for`, producing no useful error. Should check the return value and break on failure, and re-stat the path (e.g. `File.size(tempfile.path)`).

title: Downsizing in-place with same source and destination path
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` uses the same file as ImageMagick input and output. Converting in place is unreliable (and gifsicle's `--output` to the same file as input is explicitly unsafe), risking a truncated/corrupt upload. Write to a new temp file and swap.

title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb settings
body: `maxSizeKB` was replaced with a hardcoded `10 * 1024`, discarding the per-type site settings. Attachments (which are not downsized server-side) can now be submitted far above the configured `max_attachment_size_kb` and will be rejected only by the server, and admins who lowered/raised the limits get an inconsistent client-side check and a misleading error message. The same hardcoding at line 246 shows the wrong size in the 413 message.

title: API URL download size cap hardcoded to 10MB
body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` no longer respects `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, so API-provided URLs can always pull up to 10MB regardless of site configuration; for non-image files there is no downsizing fallback, so the admin-configured limit is effectively bypassed at download time.

title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the 4-arg version
body: `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) is immediately redefined by `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149). In Ruby the second definition wins, so any existing caller passing width and height separately (e.g. `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, w, h, opts)`) now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 5 for 3..4), and `downsize(from, to, 100, 100)` would be interpreted as dimensions=100, opts=100. Keep a single method with an unambiguous signature (e.g. accept a dimensions string only, and update all callers).

title: Downsize loop can spin without progress and still upload an oversized image
body: The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to 5 times but ignores its return value. If the ImageMagick/gifsicle invocation fails (`convert_with` returns false), the tempfile is unchanged and the loop simply burns 5 iterations before passing an image that still exceeds `max_image_size_kb` to `Upload.create_for`. Likewise, 5 × 80% reductions may not be enough for a very large upload, so an oversized image is still accepted. Check the return value, break on failure, and handle the still-too-large case explicitly (error to the user).

title: Animated GIF detection fails because tempfile paths have no .gif extension
body: `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects the animated (gifsicle) code path only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Here `from` is `tempfile.path`, which for uploaded files is a generic Tempfile path with no image extension, so animated GIFs are processed with `convert #{from}[0]`, which keeps only the first frame and destroys the animation of the user's upload. Pass the original filename/extension or create the tempfile with the proper extension.

title: Client-side max upload size hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
body: `validateUploadedFile` now uses a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. Sites configured with a lower (or higher) `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` will have client validation disagree with the server: attachments larger than the configured limit pass client validation and then fail server-side, and the error message shows the wrong limit. The same hardcoding in the 413 handler (line 246) reports a misleading size to users.

title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB
body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the configurable `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` cap. Sites that intentionally restrict upload size can now have up to 10MB fetched from arbitrary API-supplied URLs regardless of their setting, increasing disk/bandwidth exposure. Derive the cap from a setting instead.

title: unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser record exists
body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil for a user who has no topic_users row (e.g. notified via category watching, or a PM invite where the row was never created). The very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, raising NoMethodError (500) for a plain link click from an email. Use `TopicUser.change(...)`/`find_or_initialize` and handle the nil case.

title: Unsubscribe writes notification level directly, bypassing TopicUser.change
body: The action mutates `tu.notification_level` and saves the record directly instead of going through `TopicUser.change`, so `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id` are not updated and no MessageBus `notification_level_change` is published. Any open browser tab or other client keeps showing the stale notification level. Also note the toggle semantics: a user already at `regular` gets muted, so a second click on the same email link silently mutes the topic — repeated/prefetched requests are not idempotent.

title: State-changing operation performed on a GET request
body: `unsubscribe` changes the user's notification level on a GET (route `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`). Mail clients, link scanners and browser prefetchers routinely fetch links in emails, which will silently mute topics without the user's intent. The mutation should happen on a POST/PUT (e.g. the landing page confirms, then posts), or be guarded by a one-time key.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url} for every caller
body: The `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to pass it. Any other `build_email` call with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` (and all plugins/mailers doing so) will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` in `MessageBuilder#body`/`#html_part`, breaking those emails. Either make the second sentence conditional or default `unsubscribe_url` in `template_args`.

title: topicUnsubscribe route is shadowed by topic.fromParamsNear
body: The `topic` resource (declared earlier, path `/t/:slug/:id`) contains `fromParamsNear` with path `/:nearPost`, which matches `/t/slug/123/unsubscribe` with nearPost="unsubscribe" before the later `topicUnsubscribe` route is considered. In-app transitions / client-side handling of the unsubscribe URL will therefore land on the topic route with a bogus post number instead of the unsubscribe page.

title: unsubscribe does not guard topic visibility explicitly and ignores JSON slug check
body: `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` is relied on for access control, but unlike `show` there is no `rescue Discourse::NotFound` / redirect-by-slug handling, so a stale or wrong-slug link produces a raw 404/500 instead of a redirect. Additionally, no spec covers this new endpoint (nil TopicUser, muted/watching transitions, slug mismatch redirect), so the above bugs are untested.

title: unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser record exists
body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (a user can receive a notification email for a topic without a topic_users row, e.g. mailing-list mode or a record cleaned up), and `notification_level` can also be NULL. The subsequent `tu.notification_level > ...` then raises NoMethodError on nil, giving a 500 to anyone following the unsubscribe link. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` or create the record if missing.

title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed over GET
body: `unsubscribe` mutates the user's notification level on a plain GET request (routes.rb line 440/441) with `check_xhr` skipped and no token. Email clients, link prefetchers, antivirus scanners and third-party sites embedding the URL can silently mute topics for the user (CSRF-by-GET). The link should land on a confirmation page and perform the change via a POST/PUT with a signed key, as the existing `email/unsubscribe/:key` flow does.

title: Repeat visits to unsubscribe URL mute the topic unexpectedly
body: The toggle logic lowers watching/tracking to :regular on the first visit, but any subsequent hit of the same URL (back button, re-opening the email, prefetch) falls into the else branch and sets :muted. Combined with the email text/UI claiming 'You will stop receiving notifications', the resulting state is non-deterministic from the user's point of view. Make the endpoint idempotent (always target one level) or require an explicit confirmation action.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url and will raise for other callers
body: server.en.yml's `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but `unsubscribe_url` is only supplied by `UserNotifications#send_notification_email`. Any other build_email call that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will make `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` in both `body` and `html_part`, breaking those emails. Either default `unsubscribe_url` in `@template_args` or guard the interpolation.

title: topicUnsubscribe route shadowed by topic fromParamsNear
body: The `topic` resource declared above defines `fromParamsNear` with path `/:nearPost` under `/t/:slug/:id`, so `/t/slug/123/unsubscribe` is matched first with nearPost='unsubscribe' and never reaches the new `topicUnsubscribe` route. The unsubscribe page will not render client-side (and the post stream request with a non-numeric nearPost will fail). The new route must be declared before the topic resource or nested with a numeric constraint.

title: Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText
body: The computed property is spelled `stopNotificiationsText` ('Notificiations') here and in templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs. While consistent today, the typo is part of the public controller API and will break silently if anyone fixes one side; rename both to `stopNotificationsText`.

title: No specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint
body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action (auth requirement, slug redirect, nil TopicUser, level toggling) and `Topic#unsubscribe_url` have no request/model specs. Given the nil-dereference and toggle semantics above, these paths are untested and regressions will ship silently.

title: unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser record exists
body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (a user can receive a notification email for a topic without an existing topic_users row, e.g. after record cleanup, or simply never having visited). Line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level` on nil, producing a 500 for anyone clicking the unsubscribe link in an email. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` or handle the nil case.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking callers that don't supply it
body: `unsubscribe_link` gained a `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, but `Email::MessageBuilder#body`/`#html_part` interpolate it for every email with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` without passing `unsubscribe_url` (plugins, other mailers, and any email not going through `send_notification_email`) will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to send. A default/fallback or a separate key is needed.

title: State-changing action exposed over GET without CSRF protection
body: `unsubscribe` mutates the user's notification level but is registered as a GET route (config/routes.rb:440-441) and `check_xhr` is skipped. Mail clients, link scanners, image/link prefetchers, and any third-party page embedding `` can silently mute topics for logged-in users. The unsubscribe should either require a POST/PUT confirmation or be gated by a signed one-time key (like the existing `email/unsubscribe/:key` flow).

title: 301 permanent redirect used for a mutating endpoint
body: The slug-less `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` route redirects with `status: 301`. Browsers and intermediaries cache 301s permanently, so if the topic title (and therefore slug) later changes, clients will keep hitting the stale cached URL. Use 302 here, especially since the target performs a state change.

title: Email text promises unsubscribe but action only downgrades to regular
body: The new server locale text says "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here", but the controller only lowers watching/tracking to `regular` on the first click and requires a second visit to mute. A user clicking once will still receive notifications (e.g. for replies to their posts), contradicting the email and the client-side message "You will stop receiving notifications for <topic>".

title: New unsubscribe route may be shadowed by topic.fromParamsNear
body: `topic` resource declares child route `fromParamsNear` with path `/:nearPost` under `/t/:slug/:id`, so `/t/slug/123/unsubscribe` can be matched as a topic with nearPost="unsubscribe" depending on route definition order/dynamic-segment matching. Declaring the more specific `topicUnsubscribe` route after the `topic` resource risks the unsubscribe page never rendering (and a bogus post-stream request for post "unsubscribe").

title: No specs for the new unsubscribe controller action
body: The new `unsubscribe` action contains non-trivial branching (slug redirect, level toggle, missing TopicUser) and is reachable by any logged-in user via a GET link in emails, yet no request/controller spec was added. Regressions such as the nil TopicUser crash or wrong notification level transitions would go undetected.

title: Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText
body: The computed property is spelled `stopNotificiationsText` (extra 'i') in both the controller and templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs. It works but is an API typo that will confuse future maintenance and theme overrides; rename to `stopNotificationsText` in both places.

title: rejectedEmails array is shared between controller instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` puts a single mutable array on the class prototype, so every CreateAccountController instance (and any re-instantiation of the modal) shares the same array. Emails rejected in one session/modal will keep being flagged as invalid afterwards, and the list is never reset. Initialize it per-instance (e.g. in `init`, or via a computed/`Em.A()` created on first use).

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` compares the raw submitted email. Emails stored in the table with different casing (or a user signing up with `Bad@Spamclub.com` when `bad@spamclub.com` is blocked) will not match, so the block is trivially bypassed. Normalize with `Email.downcase` on both write (before_validation) and lookup.

title: match_count increment is non-atomic and written inside a validation
body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` performs a read-modify-write, so concurrent signups with the same blocked email lose increments. Worse, this write happens from `EmailValidator#validate_each`, i.e. inside the enclosing `User` save transaction; if that transaction rolls back the statistics update is discarded. Use `update_all`/`increment_counter` outside the caller's transaction.

title: Validator performs a DB write on every email validation, including valid?/preview calls
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` mutates and saves the matched row. Since `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` runs on every `valid?` call (e.g. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` before `user.save`), match_count can be incremented multiple times per signup attempt, making the statistic unreliable.

title: Signup failure response now echoes submitted attributes without restricting fields
body: `user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")` plus `user.errors.to_hash` are returned in the failure JSON. This is fine for the three listed fields, but note the response now exposes the raw internal error keys; if more attributes are ever added to the slice (or the model gains sensitive attributes) they would leak to an unauthenticated endpoint. Consider returning only the explicitly needed values and documenting the contract, since the JS only uses `result.values.email`.

title: No tests for whitelist/blacklist paths moved into the new validator
body: The whitelist/blacklist logic was deleted from `User#email_validator` and moved to `EmailValidator`, but the new spec only covers the blocked-email branch. Any regression in the domain whitelist/blacklist behaviour (including the interaction where a whitelist/blacklist error suppresses the blocked check) would go undetected unless equivalent specs were moved too.

title: rejectedEmails array is shared across all controller instances
body: Declaring `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` directly on the class body puts a single array on the prototype, shared by every instance of CreateAccountController (and never reset when the modal is reopened). Because the code mutates it with `pushObject`, emails rejected in one session stay rejected forever for the page lifetime, and any other instance sees them too. Initialize it per-instance (e.g. in `init`, `this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A([]))`) and clear it when the modal is shown.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case sensitive and not normalized
body: `should_block?` does an exact `where(email: email)` match. Emails in the users table are stored/compared downcased elsewhere (see `Email.downcase` usage), but blocked entries are stored verbatim from the migration/fabricator with no normalization callback. A blocked address such as `bad@spam.com` is trivially bypassed by signing up as `Bad@Spam.com`. Downcase/strip the email both before persisting a BlockedEmail and in the lookup.

title: match_count update uses non-atomic save and ignores failures
body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` reads-modifies-writes outside a transaction, so concurrent signups with the same blocked email lose counts, and a failed `save` (e.g. validation) is silently swallowed while the block decision still proceeds. Prefer an atomic `update_all`/`increment!`-style SQL update.

title: Signup failure response now echoes full error hash and submitted values
body: The create response now includes `user.errors.to_hash` and the submitted name/username/email. This makes account enumeration easier programmatically (e.g. distinguishing "email already taken" from other failures) and reflects user input back into JSON. If only the email rejection flag is needed by the client, return a minimal, specific field instead of the whole error hash.

title: No specs cover whitelist/blacklist behaviour after move out of User
body: The domain whitelist/blacklist logic was removed from `User#email_validator` and moved here, but the new spec only stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?`. If the existing user specs referenced the removed private methods they would break, and either way the whitelist/blacklist branches of the new validator are untested, so a regression in the regex construction would go unnoticed.

title: rejectedEmails array is shared across all controller instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` creates a single array on the class prototype, so every instance of CreateAccountController (and any re-opened modal) mutates and reads the same array. Emails rejected in one session will persist/leak into later ones, and the array never resets. It should be initialized per-instance (e.g. in `init`, `this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A([]))`).

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` does an exact match. User emails are not guaranteed to be stored/submitted in the same case as the blocked record, so `Bad@Spam.com` bypasses a block entry for `bad@spam.com`. Downcase both on write (before_validation) and on lookup.

title: Non-atomic match_count increment and silent save failure
body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` reads-modifies-writes outside a transaction, so concurrent signup attempts lose increments. Also `save` return value is ignored, so a validation/DB failure silently drops the statistic. Prefer `increment!`/`update_columns` with a SQL increment.

title: should_block? side effect runs on every validation, inflating match_count
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` mutates state (match_count/last_match_at). `validate_each` can be invoked multiple times per request (e.g. `user.valid?` in UsersController#create followed by `user.save`), so a single signup attempt can bump the counter several times, making the statistic unreliable.

title: `<%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby and will raise on render
body: The if/else block is terminated with `<%- end if %>`. `end if` is a syntax error in Ruby (`if` used as a modifier with no condition), so compiling this template raises a SyntaxError and the `embed#best` action will 500 whenever a topic exists. It should be `<%- end %>`.

title: request.referer interpolated unescaped into inline JavaScript
body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` injects an attacker-controlled HTTP header directly into a JS string literal with no escaping. A referer containing a single quote (e.g. `http://x'+alert(1)+'`) breaks out of the string and executes arbitrary script in the Discourse origin, which also has the session cookie available. Escape with `j`/`javascript_escape` (or build the target origin from scheme+host only).

title: Raw rendering of posts whose cooked HTML is unsanitized remote content
body: `raw post.cooked` is emitted in the embed view, while `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim for `cook_method == :raw_html` (posts imported from RSS/readability). That means arbitrary HTML/JS pulled from a third-party feed is stored as `cooked` and rendered unsanitized inside a page on the forum's own origin. The imported HTML should be sanitized (whitelist tags/attributes) before being stored or rendered.

title: `force: true` in create_table will silently drop an existing table
body: `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` first. If the migration is ever re-run (or the table exists for any reason), all topic_embeds rows are destroyed without warning. Remove `force: true` from migrations.

title: Editing an already-released migration to add `force: true` risks dropping top_topics
body: This changes an existing migration (which may already have run on deployed sites) to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, i.e. drop-then-create. Any environment that re-runs or re-plays migrations loses the table and its data. Migrations should be immutable once shipped, and `force: true` should not be used here.

title: poll_feed crashes when feed items have no `content`
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every RSS/Atom item exposes `content`. Many RSS 2.0 feeds only provide `description`, in which case SimpleRSS returns nil and the job raises NoMethodError; with `sidekiq_options retry: false` the whole polling run is lost. Also `String#scrub` requires Ruby >= 2.1. Fall back to `description`/`content_encoded` and guard against nil.

title: `open` used without requiring open-uri in topic_embed.rb
body: `import_remote` calls `open(url)` but this file only requires nokogiri and ruby-readability. open-uri is only required in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, so when `import_remote` is reached via TopicRetriever/RetrieveTopic without PollFeed having been loaded, `open` falls back to Kernel#open and will fail (or behave unexpectedly) on an http URL. Add `require 'open-uri'` here.

title: open-uri `open` on a URL permits pipe/file access and unbounded fetch
body: `open(url)` with Kernel#open semantics treats a string starting with `|` as a shell command and non-http strings as local file paths. Although TopicRetriever checks the host, `import_remote` is also called directly (disqus.thor, and `poll_feed` uses `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`), so a crafted feed URL setting can read local files or run commands. Use an explicit HTTP fetch (e.g. `URI.parse(url).open` after validating scheme) and bound the response size.

title: Weak postMessage origin check on the host page
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any origin that is a *substring* of the configured discourse URL (e.g. `http://disc` or a prefix match), and it does not anchor at position 0. Any page able to postMessage can then resize the iframe. Compare the origin exactly against the origin component of discourseUrl.

title: `import` mutates the caller's contents string
body: `contents << "...imported from..."` appends in place to the string passed in by the caller. Callers that reuse or cache that string (and frozen-literal strings) will see corruption / RuntimeError. Build a new string instead (`contents = contents + ...`).

title: Missing embed_url raises ParameterMissing producing a 500 rather than a 400/404
body: `params.require(:embed_url)` raises ActionController::ParameterMissing, which is not rescued here; unless the app has a global handler this surfaces as a 500 error with a backtrace rather than a clean 400. The accompanying spec only asserts `should_not be_success`, so it passes either way.

title: Dead code: feed_key is computed but never used
body: `feed_key` builds a redis key for feed modification tracking but nothing reads or writes it, so the feed is re-parsed and re-imported in full every hour with no conditional-GET/ETag handling. Either implement the caching or drop the method.

title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript (XSS)
body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` injects the raw Referer header into a single-quoted JS string with no escaping. EmbedController#ensure_embeddable only validates the referer's *host*, so an attacker on the embeddable host (or anyone who can set an arbitrary Referer, e.g. a crafted request) can supply a referer like `http://host/x');alert(1);//` and execute arbitrary script in the context of the Discourse origin. Escape with `j`/`to_json` or build the target origin from scheme+host only.

title: Invalid ERB/Ruby `<%- end if %>` breaks the view
body: Line 6 contains `<%- end if %>`. `end if` with a bare `if` modifier and no condition is a Ruby syntax error, so rendering embed/best will raise instead of producing the page. It should simply be `<% end %>`.

title: raw_html cook method stores unsanitized HTML, enabling XSS from feeds
body: `cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == :raw_html`, bypassing the sanitizing render pipeline. TopicEmbed.import (used by Jobs::PollFeed on arbitrary RSS/ATOM content) passes feed HTML straight through with this cook method, and the embed view renders it with `raw post.cooked`. Any `<script>`/event-handler markup in a polled feed (or any content the feed author controls) becomes executable script on the forum. The HTML should be sanitized/whitelisted before being stored as cooked.

title: import mutates the caller's contents string
body: `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends in place to the string passed in by the caller. Callers that reuse or cache the string (e.g. retrying the import, or passing a frozen/literal string) will see the footer appended repeatedly, or get a RuntimeError on a frozen string. Build a new string instead (`contents = contents + ...`).

title: create_table with force: true in migrations can drop existing tables
body: `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` (and the same change made to 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) issues a DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating. If the table already exists on an installation, running the migration silently destroys its data. Migrations should not use `force: true`.

title: poll_feed assumes every feed item has `content`
body: `i.content.scrub` will raise NoMethodError on nil for RSS 2.0 feeds that only provide `description` (SimpleRSS only populates `content`/`content_encoded` for Atom-style feeds). Since the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a single such feed permanently breaks polling. Fall back to `i.description`/`content_encoded` and skip blank items.

title: Weak postMessage origin check using substring match
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of the configured Discourse URL (e.g. `http://disc` prefixes, or `https://x` if present inside the URL), and conversely rejects nothing reliably. Compare the event origin for exact equality with the Discourse origin instead.

title: content_sha1 updated even when revise! fails
body: `revisor.revise!` can return false (e.g. `should_revise?` false) or `@post.save` can fail validation silently, yet `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` runs unconditionally. The embed then records the new checksum while the post still holds the old content, so the update will never be retried on subsequent imports. Only update the sha when the revision actually succeeded.

title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JS (XSS) and used as postMessage targetOrigin
body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` injects an attacker-controlled header directly inside a JavaScript single-quoted string without escaping. A referer containing `'` (e.g. `http://x/'+alert(1)+'`) breaks out of the string and executes arbitrary JS in the Discourse origin. Additionally, postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin, not a full URL with path/query; derive the scheme+host (e.g. from SiteSetting.embeddable_host) and escape it with `j`/`to_json`.

title: raw_html cook method stores unsanitized HTML as cooked output
body: When `cook_method == raw_html`, `cook` returns `raw` verbatim, bypassing the sanitizing render pipeline. Content fed through TopicEmbed/PollFeed comes from remote RSS feeds or Readability-scraped pages, so any `<script>`/`onerror=` in the feed is persisted as `cooked` and later rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and in normal topic views, giving stored XSS. The HTML must be sanitized (whitelist tags/attrs) before storing.

title: Invalid ERB/Ruby `<%- end if %>` breaks the template
body: `<%- end if %>` compiles to `end if` which is a Ruby syntax error (a bare `if` with no condition following `end`). Rendering embed/best will raise at template compile time, so the whole embed feature fails. It should be just `<%- end %>`.

title: `force: true` on create_table drops an existing table and its data
body: Changing `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` means the migration issues DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating. On any installation where this migration already ran (or is re-run), existing top_topics data is silently destroyed. The same pattern is used in the new 20131217174004_create_topic_embeds migration, where re-running would drop all embed mappings. Remove `force: true`.

title: Weak postMessage origin check using indexOf
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of the configured Discourse URL (e.g. origin `http://d` matches `http://discourse.example.com/`), and an empty origin also passes. Compare the message origin against the exact iframe origin instead.

title: poll_feed crashes when a feed item has no `content`
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item exposes `content`. For plain RSS 2.0 feeds SimpleRSS exposes `description` and `content` is nil, raising NoMethodError and aborting the whole scheduled job (retry is disabled, so all items are skipped). Fall back to `i.description`/guard against nil. Also `feed_key` is defined but never used, so the HTTP modified-check it implies does not happen.

title: import mutates the caller's contents string
body: `contents << "...imported from..."` appends in place to the string passed in by the caller (PollFeed item content, Readability doc content). This mutates caller state, raises RuntimeError on frozen strings, and causes the footer to be appended repeatedly if the same string is passed to import more than once (changing the content_sha1 and triggering spurious revisions). Build a new string instead.

title: Rails 3 lockfile not updated for new gems
body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` were added to the Gemfile and to Gemfile_rails4.lock, but Gemfile_rails3.lock was not updated. Booting/bundling in RAILS3 mode (still supported per the Gemfile) will fail with an out-of-date lockfile in deployment/frozen bundles.

title: Full feed poll executed synchronously inside the retrieve path
body: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` downloads and imports the entire RSS feed inline whenever a single embed URL is missed. For large feeds this makes the retrieve job long-running and can duplicate work across concurrent retrievals (the redis throttle is per embed_url, not per feed).

title: Embed view renders post.cooked with `raw` for imported HTML posts
body: `<%= raw post.cooked %>` outputs post HTML unescaped. Combined with the new raw_html cook method (which stores remote feed HTML unsanitized), scripts from third-party feeds execute inside the Discourse-origin iframe. Sanitize cooked content for raw_html posts before output.

title: Floats inside new flex container are ignored in .small-action
body: `.small-action` now uses `@include flexbox()`, which makes its children flex items. `float` has no effect on flex items, so `.topic-avatar { float: left }` (line 270) and `button { float: right }` (line 309) no longer position as before — the button will no longer be right-aligned. Use `margin-left: auto` on the button (and remove the floats) to preserve the layout.

title: Header panel loses right alignment without flexbox support
body: `.panel`'s `float: right` was replaced by `margin-left: auto` + `@include order(3)`, which only work when the parent is a flex container. In browsers that don't support modern flexbox (where the `display: flex` fallbacks in the mixin resolve to the legacy `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` models that ignore `margin: auto`), the panel will be rendered left-aligned in normal flow, breaking the header. Also `.icons`/`.login-button` still use `float: left`, which is ignored on flex items, so those rules are now dead.

title: align-items mixin emits invalid legacy values for flex-* keywords
body: The mixin blindly forwards `$alignment` to legacy properties. `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` do not accept the modern `flex-start`/`flex-end` keywords (they expect `start`/`end`), so any future `@include align-items(flex-start)` will silently emit invalid declarations in the legacy prefixes while looking correct. Map values explicitly or drop the obsolete `-webkit-box-align`/`-ms-flex-align` lines.

title: order mixin mixes 0-based and 1-based ordinal values
body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based (default 1) while the standard `order` is 0-based (default 0). Passing the same `$val` to both means legacy box-model browsers compute a different relative ordering than standard-flexbox browsers (e.g. `order(2)` is one step from default in old syntax vs two in new). Either emit `$val + 1` for the ordinal-group properties or drop them.

title: inline-flex fallback ordering can override the better prefix
body: In `inline-flex()`, `-moz-inline-box` is declared after `-webkit-inline-flex`. If a UA understood both (and generally for cascade correctness), the older legacy value wins because it comes last. Legacy/box-model fallbacks should be listed before the newer prefixed and standard values, as done in `flexbox()`.

title: float: right on a flex item is ignored after making .small-action a flex container
body: .small-action is now `display: flex` (line 264), so `float` on its direct children has no effect. The `button { float: right; }` rule (line 309) and `clear: both` (line 312) are now dead, meaning the small-action action button will no longer be pushed to the right edge but will sit immediately after the description. Use `margin-left: auto` on the button instead (as was done for .d-header .panel).

title: order(3) on .panel without explicit order on siblings relies on default order 0
body: .d-header .panel gets `@include order(3)` while .title has no order and .extra-info-wrapper (topic.scss) gets order(2). For the legacy `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` prefix the initial value is 1, not 0, so under old WebKit the un-ordered .title (group 1) and the explicitly ordered items still work, but any sibling relying on default ordering is fragile; also `order(3)` is redundant given `margin-left: auto` already pushes .panel right. Consider setting explicit orders on all header flex children or dropping the order include.

title: align-items mixin emits invalid values for legacy prefixes
body: The mixin blindly forwards the argument to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, which only accept start/end/center/baseline/stretch. Calling `align-items(flex-start)` or `align-items(flex-end)` (likely in future use) emits invalid declarations for those legacy properties, silently losing alignment in old WebKit/IE10. Either map values or drop the obsolete box-model prefixes.

title: .d-header .contents previously relied on floats for layout; floated non-flex descendants may need review
body: Converting .contents to flex removes the effect of float on its direct children (the old `.title { float: left }` and `.panel { float: right }` were deleted). `.icons`/`.login-button` still use `float: left` but are inside .panel, which is not a flex container, so they still work; however there is no `flex-wrap`/`min-width: 0` on the flex items, so long titles can overflow instead of shrinking as they did with the float layout. Worth verifying narrow-viewport header rendering.

title: order() mixin emits wrong value for legacy box-ordinal-group
body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based (first item = 1), while the modern `order` property is 0-based (default 0). Passing the same `$val` to both means items using `@include order(2)`/`order(3)` (topic.scss `.extra-info-wrapper`, header.scss `.panel`) are ordered differently in old WebKit/Gecko box-model browsers than in modern flexbox, and elements with implicit order 0 cannot be expressed at all. Compute the legacy value as `$val + 1`.

title: align-items() passes modern keywords to -webkit-box-align/-ms-flex-align
body: The legacy properties accept only `start|center|end|baseline|stretch`, not the modern `flex-start|flex-end`. Any future call such as `@include align-items(flex-start)` will emit invalid declarations for `-webkit-box-align`, `-ms-flex-align`, silently producing no legacy fallback. Map the values (or drop the legacy properties).

title: .small-action now a flex container, but children still rely on float/clear
body: `.small-action` gained `@include flexbox()`, which makes `float: left` on `.topic-avatar`/`.avatar` and `float: right` on `button` no-ops (floats do not apply to flex items), and the trailing `clear: both` on the flex container itself is also meaningless here. The button will no longer be pushed to the right edge; use `margin-left: auto` instead, and remove the dead float/clear rules.

title: Floats inside the new flex .contents are ignored
body: `.d-header .contents` is now a flex container, so `float: left` on `.icons`, `.login-button`, `button.sign-up-button` (direct/indirect children that became flex items) no longer has any effect. The removed `.title { float: left; }` was replaced by flex ordering, but these remaining float rules are dead and the resulting spacing/alignment of the icon row and login buttons may differ from before; they should be converted to flex properties.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing `?`
body: ActiveModel::Serializers looks for a predicate named `include_website_name?`. The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never called and `website_name` is unconditionally serialized — including when `website` is blank (serialized as `null`). Rename to `include_website_name?`.

title: website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, leaking website for TL0 users to anonymous
body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` so it is hidden when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` (TL0 user seen by anonymous). The new `website_name` attribute is not in that list, so the host (and possibly full path) of a TL0 user's website is still exposed to anonymous visitors, defeating the spam-protection intent. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`.

title: No test that website_name is hidden for untrusted users
body: The TL0/anonymous context asserts only the previously-listed untrusted attributes. Since `website_name` now derives from `website`, a spec asserting `json` has no `website_name` key for a restricted user is needed to lock in the privacy behaviour.

title: String literal mutation with `<<` in ends_with? comparison
body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on a string literal. It works today, but under frozen string literals (`# frozen_string_literal: true` or Ruby 3.x with the magic comment/`--enable-frozen-string-literal`) this raises FrozenError. Use `".#{website_host}"` instead.

title: URI parsed up to three times per call; website without scheme yields no name
body: `URI(website.to_s)` is re-evaluated in each branch (wasteful, and the second/third calls are not inside the rescue, so a malformed URI that raised once could raise unrescued later). Also, for a website stored without a scheme (e.g. `example.com/user`), `URI#host` is nil and the method returns nil, so no website is shown at all even though `website` is present. Parse once into a local and handle the scheme-less case.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing `?` so it never gates serialization
body: ActiveModel::Serializers looks for a predicate named `include_<attr>?`. The method is defined as `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never called and `website_name` is always included in the payload, even when the website is blank (serialized as `null`). Rename to `include_website_name?`.

title: website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, leaking TL0 website to anonymous users
body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` so it is hidden when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` (TL0 user seen by anonymous). The new `website_name` attribute is not added to that list, so the website host (and now possibly the full path) is still exposed for TL0 users to anonymous visitors, defeating the existing spam-prevention restriction. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and extend the TL0 spec's `untrusted_attributes` list accordingly.

title: Host comparison is case-sensitive and parses the URI repeatedly
body: `website_host` and `Discourse.current_hostname` are compared with `==`/`ends_with?` without downcasing. A profile URL such as `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` yields host `EXAMPLE.com` which will not match hostname `example.com`, so the full-path behaviour this PR adds silently fails. Downcase both hosts before comparing. (`URI(website.to_s)` is also built three times; parse once.)

title: Subdomain match only works when label counts are equal
body: The second branch requires `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` and >2 labels, so cases like website `www.example.com` with instance `forum.eu.example.com`, or website `example.co.uk` with instance `forum.example.co.uk` (handled only by the `ends_with?` branch, which works) are inconsistent: sibling subdomains with different depths fall back to host-only. Consider comparing registrable suffixes instead of label counts.

title: Use `+` instead of `<<` for string concatenation here
body: `"." << website_host` mutates the receiver string in place; while the literal is a fresh object today, this breaks if `# frozen_string_literal: true` is ever added to the file and is needlessly surprising. Use `"." + website_host`.

title: No test for sibling-subdomain and blank-website cases
body: The new specs cover only equal host, different host, and parent-domain host. Missing: website blank/invalid (verifying `website_name` is omitted, which currently fails because `include_website_name?` is misnamed), and the sibling subdomain branch (`www.example.com` website with `forum.example.com` instance) which is the most fragile piece of the new logic.

title: `include_website_name` is missing the `?` suffix, so the inclusion guard never runs
body: ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_<attr>?` (with a question mark) to decide whether to include an attribute. The method defined here is `include_website_name`, so it is never called and `website_name` is always serialized (as `null` when the user has no website). Rename to `include_website_name?` so the guard actually takes effect.

title: website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, leaking website for TL0 users seen by anonymous
body: `website` is listed under `untrusted_attributes` and is suppressed when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` (TL0 user viewed anonymously). `website_name` is a plain attribute and is derived from the same value, so the site/host (and path) is still exposed to anonymous visitors, defeating the restriction. The existing spec 'doesn't serialize untrusted attributes' does not cover `website_name`. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and to the spec list.

title: String mutation with `<<` on a literal can raise under frozen string literals
body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` mutates the `"."` literal in place. If frozen string literals are ever enabled (magic comment or newer Ruby default), this raises FrozenError. Use `".#{website_host}"` or `"." + website_host` instead.

title: URL is parsed repeatedly and only the first parse is guarded; query/fragment dropped
body: `URI(website.to_s)` is evaluated up to three times per call and only the first is protected by `rescue nil`. Parse once into a local variable. Also only `.host + .path` is used, so any query string or fragment in the user's website URL is silently dropped from the displayed name, which can be misleading when the full path is intentionally shown.

title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic shows full path for unrelated domains of equal label count
body: The `elsif` branch only requires that the hostnames have the same number of labels (>2) and share all labels after the first. So e.g. website `evil.example.com` with instance `forum.example.com` is treated as 'same site' and the full path is rendered, and conversely `forum.example.com` with instance `example.com` (reverse of the documented case) only yields the host. The matching rules should be based on the registrable domain, and the asymmetry deserves a test.

title: Light-theme color for embedded post author link changed from 30% to 70% lightness
body: The embedded-post `.topic-meta-data h5 a` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The light-theme branch should keep 30% to preserve existing appearance; using 70% makes the author name much lighter/lower contrast on light themes, which is an unintended visual/accessibility regression unrelated to the dark-theme fix.

title: Light-theme value for .custom-message-length changed from 70% to 30%
body: Previously `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`; now the light branch is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` while the dark branch is 70% of $secondary. This darkens the hint text on light themes (and is inconsistent with desktop/modal.scss, which kept 70%/30%). Light-theme behavior should be unchanged.

title: Group member .name light-theme lightness changed 30% -> 50%
body: `.group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now the 50%/50% pair, lightening the member name on light themes. Only the dark branch should have been added; keep 30% for the light value to avoid an unintended contrast change.

title: Mobile group member .name light-theme lightness changed 30% -> 50%
body: Same regression as desktop: the light-theme color for `.group-member-info .name` moved from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to 50%, lightening the text on light themes rather than only adding a dark-theme fallback.

title: topic-map h3 light-theme lightness changed 20% -> 50%
body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`; the light branch is now 50%, noticeably lightening the heading on light mobile themes. Desktop kept 20%/80%, so mobile and desktop are now inconsistent too.

title: Light-theme color changed for embedded post author link
body: `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` passes 70% as the light-theme value instead of 30%, so author links in embedded posts become noticeably lighter/lower-contrast on light themes. The PR's stated intent is only to add a dark-theme branch; the light value should stay 30%.

title: group-member-info .name light value changed from 30% to 50%
body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`; the new first argument to `dark-light-choose` is 50%, lightening the name text on light themes and also removing the previous visual distinction between `.name` (30%) and `.title` (50%). The light-theme value should remain 30%.

title: Mobile group-member-info .name light value changed from 30% to 50%
body: Same regression as the desktop file: `.group-member-info .name` used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and now passes 50% as the light-theme argument, changing the light theme rendering and collapsing the contrast difference with `.title`.

title: custom-message-length light/dark values swapped relative to original
body: `.custom-message-length` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`; the change passes 30% for the light theme and 70% for `$secondary` in the dark theme. This makes the mobile hint text much darker on light themes and inconsistent with the equivalent desktop rule (`70%` light / `30%` dark). The light argument should be 70%.

title: topic-map h3 light value changed from 20% to 50%
body: The mobile `.topic-map h3` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and now passes 50% for the light theme, lightening the topic map heading on light themes (desktop keeps 20%). The light-theme argument should stay 20% to preserve existing appearance and desktop/mobile parity.

title: Light-theme color changed for embedded post author link
body: The original value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the new light branch of `dark-light-choose` uses 70% (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`). This PR is supposed to only add a dark-theme variant, yet it silently lightens the embedded-post author name in light themes by 40 percentage points, likely producing a near-invisible, low-contrast link. The light branch should remain 30% (dark branch 70%).

title: custom-message-length light color inverted
body: Original: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. New: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` — the light-theme lightness was changed from 70% to 30%, making the hint text much darker than before on light themes (and inconsistent with desktop/modal.scss which kept 70%/30%). Swap the arguments to preserve existing light-theme appearance.

title: topic-map h3 light color changed from 20% to 50%
body: `.topic-map h3` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`; the new light branch uses 50%, lightening the heading noticeably on light themes. The desktop equivalent kept 20%/80%, so mobile and desktop now diverge. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

title: group-member-info .name light color changed from 30% to 50%
body: The `.name` rule previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and now uses 50% in the light branch, reducing contrast on light themes and making `.name` indistinguishable from `.title`. The same regression exists in app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss (`.group-member-info .name`). Keep 30% for the light branch (70% for dark).

title: totalPages/currentPage off by one when count is a multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With user_count=50 and limit=50 it returns 2 pages although only one page of members exists; the 'next' button becomes enabled and fetches an empty page. The same `+1` logic in `currentPage` means when offset == user_count the displayed page number exceeds the real last page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (and clamp currentPage accordingly).

title: Unbounded/unvalidated limit and offset on public members endpoint
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are taken straight from user input with no upper bound or non-negative check. An anonymous caller can request `limit=1000000` on a large group and serialize the whole membership (memory/CPU DoS), and a negative `limit`/`offset` produces an invalid SQL LIMIT/OFFSET which raises and returns a 500. Clamp limit to a maximum (e.g. 50..100) and force offset >= 0.

title: create ignores alias_level sent by the client
body: `Group#asJSON` in the JS model now sends `name`, `alias_level` and `visible` for both create and update, but `create` only reads `name` and `visible`. A new group created from the admin UI with a non-default alias level silently gets the default alias_level, and the client never issues a follow-up save, so the admin's choice is lost.

title: update forces visible=false when the visible param is absent
body: `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally assigns, so any PUT that omits `visible` (e.g. an API client sending only `name` or `alias_level`) silently makes the group invisible. Only assign when `params.key?(:visible)`.

title: remove_member automatic-group test uses PUT, but the route is DELETE
body: The spec issues `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` while config/routes.rb only maps `delete "members" => groups#remove_member` (PUT maps to add_members). Controller specs generate the URL from routes, so this raises ActionController::UrlGenerationError / exercises the wrong verb, leaving the automatic-group guard for removal effectively untested.

title: Tests rely on hard-coded group id 1 being an automatic group
body: `add_members`/`remove_member`/`update` specs pass `group_id: 1` / `id: 1` and assert 422 or 'name unchanged', implicitly assuming the seeded group with id 1 exists and is automatic. If seed order or ids change these tests break or pass for the wrong reason (e.g. Group.find(1) raising RecordNotFound). Fabricate an automatic group explicitly.

title: findMembers no longer always returns a promise
body: When `name` is empty the method returns `undefined` instead of the previous `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. Any caller doing `group.findMembers().then(...)` (routes/controllers outside this diff, or future callers) will throw a TypeError. Return a resolved promise instead of bare `return;`.

title: Non-block {{each}} with itemView has no closing tag and may not render
body: `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` is used as an inline (non-block) helper with no `{{/each}}`. If the Ember version in use does not support the legacy non-block `{{each}}` form with the `member in` binding, the template will either fail to compile or render nothing, so the member list and the remove buttons will not appear. Use the block form `{{#each member in members itemView="group-member"}}{{/each}}` (or a component).

title: group.users.delete(user_id) passes an integer to an AR collection
body: `remove_member` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id` is an Integer. ActiveRecord collection `delete` expects record objects (or at least responds unpredictably to raw ids, raising NoMethodError on `id`/`destroyed?` in many versions). The member will not be removed, or the request will 500. It should look up the user (`user = User.find_by(id: user_id)`) and call `group.remove(user)` / `group.users.delete(user)`, and return a 404/422 if the user isn't found.

title: update silently clears `visible` and never persists alias_level on create
body: In `update`, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally, so any PUT that omits `visible` (e.g. a partial update from a future client or an API caller) flips the group to not-visible. Additionally `create` only reads `name` and `visible`, so the `alias_level` the client sends in `asJSON()` on group creation is dropped, and new groups always get the default alias level. Use `params.key?(:visible)` guards and handle `alias_level` in `create`.

title: totalPages off-by-one for exact multiples of limit
body: `totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With user_count=50 and limit=50 this yields 2 pages, the second of which is empty; the 'next' arrow stays enabled and `showingLast` never matches on the real last page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead.

title: Offset clamped to user_count yields an empty last page
body: `offset = Math.min(user_count, Math.max(offset, 0))` allows offset == user_count, which requests a range past the last member and returns zero members. The upper clamp should be `Math.max(user_count - limit, 0)`.

title: `{{each}}` used with block-param syntax but no closing tag
body: `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` mixes the keyword (`x in y`) form, which requires a block and `{{/each}}`, with the inline `itemView` form. As written the template will either fail to compile or render nothing, so the member list never appears on the admin group page.

title: Unbounded `limit` param on public members endpoint
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is not capped, and this endpoint is public (only subject to group visibility). A caller can pass `limit=1000000` and force serialization of every group member, a cheap way to generate heavy DB/CPU load. Clamp limit to a sane maximum (e.g. 50–200) and reject negative values.

title: remove_member test uses PUT while the route only accepts DELETE, and relies on hardcoded group id 1
body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but config/routes.rb maps only `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. Controller specs bypass routing, so this passes while the real verb mapping is untested. Both this test and the add_members/update tests also assume group id 1 exists and is automatic, which depends on seed data rather than fabricated fixtures. Fabricate an automatic group and use the correct verb.

title: addMembers/removeMember failures are silently swallowed
body: `addMembers` and `removeMember` call into the model without attaching a rejection handler, so a server error (e.g. 422 for an automatic group, or an unknown username) produces no user feedback and the input is never cleared (per the TODO). Add an error handler that surfaces the response errors via bootbox like `save` does.

title: totalPages off by one for exact multiples of limit
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members with limit 50) it reports 2 pages instead of 1, so `showingLast` is false and the 'next' control is enabled, paging to an empty member list. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

title: create ignores alias_level sent by client
body: Group#asJSON in the JS model posts `name`, `alias_level` and `visible` to POST /admin/groups, but the `create` action only reads `name` and `visible`. A newly created group silently loses the chosen alias level (it stays at the default) until the user saves again, which is confusing and inconsistent with `update`.

title: visible forced to false when param absent
body: `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` in both create and update sets visible to false whenever the param is missing (e.g. a partial update or an API client that omits it), silently hiding the group. Only assign when `params.key?(:visible)`.

title: members endpoint accepts unbounded limit
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is used directly in the query with no upper bound, so any user can request e.g. `?limit=1000000` and force serialization of every group member in one request. Clamp the limit (e.g. `[limit, 100].min`) and guard against negative values.

title: remove_member always reports success even if user is not a member
body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` relies on passing a raw id to the has_many collection and gives no indication whether anything was removed; a bogus or non-member user_id returns 200 success. Consider looking the user up / deleting the GroupUser record explicitly and returning a 404/422 when no membership existed, so the UI doesn't show a false success.

title: remove_member test uses wrong HTTP verb and hardcoded automatic group id
body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the only route for that action is DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members, so the test does not exercise the real routing. It also assumes group id 1 is automatic, which is fragile; fabricate an automatic group instead. Same hardcoded-id issue in the add_members example.

title: No spec for new paginated GroupsController#members response
body: The members endpoint changed from a bare serialized array to `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}` with pagination applied to all groups (previously only automatic ones). There is no spec covering the new payload shape, limit/offset behaviour, or the total count, so regressions in the contract consumed by the JS model would go unnoticed.

title: Non-block {{each}} with keyword binding and no closing tag
body: `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` mixes the `x in y` keyword form (which requires a block, `{{#each}}...{{/each}}`) with the legacy non-block itemView form. In Ember 1.x this either throws a compile error or renders nothing, so the member list would not display. Use `{{each members itemView="group-member"}}` (and reference `this` in the item template) or a proper block form.

title: `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` raises if default_locale is nil
body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `to_sym` on the site setting before compacting. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` ever returns nil (e.g. during early boot, before site settings are provisioned, or a blank setting), this raises NoMethodError inside every I18n lookup's fallback resolution, breaking all translation. The `.compact` is also ineffective for this case since the exception happens earlier. Guard with `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym`.

title: Translation cache key ignores fallback chain / default locale
body: With fallbacks enabled, the result of `translate(key)` now depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (the second entry of the fallback chain), but the LRU cache key is only `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`. In multisite (or after an admin changes the default locale) the same process can serve sites with different default locales, so a cached value resolved via site A's fallback locale will be returned for site B, producing wrong-language strings. Include the fallback chain (or default_locale) in the cache key, or clear the cache when default_locale changes.

title: Fallback locales only loaded in web requests
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is called only from ApplicationController#set_locale. Because the translate_accelerator only lazily loads the yml for `config.locale`, any code path outside controllers (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console) that sets a locale will never load the fallback locale files, so fallback lookups return 'translation missing' instead of the default-locale/English string. The ensure_loaded! call should happen wherever the locale is set (e.g. in I18n.locale= or in the backend/translate path).

title: ensure_loaded! initializes @loaded_locales outside the mutex
body: `@loaded_locales ||= []` and the `include?` check run outside LOAD_MUTEX, while load_locale mutates `@loaded_locales` under the mutex. Concurrent requests can race, re-initializing the array to [] and discarding already-loaded locale bookkeeping (triggering redundant reloads) or reading a partially-updated array. Move initialization/check inside the mutex (or initialize eagerly at load time).

title: SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym can raise NoMethodError
body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` calls `to_sym` on the setting value before any nil check. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` is nil or blank (e.g. during early boot, before site settings are provisioned, or in a DB-less/migration context), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'to_sym' for nil`. Since this method is invoked on every I18n fallback lookup and from `ensure_loaded!` in a before_filter, a single nil setting breaks all translation. The trailing `.compact` cannot help because the exception happens while building the array; guard with `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym` instead.

title: Translation LRU cache key ignores fallback locales
body: The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With the new Fallbacks backend, the resolved value for a given key/locale also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (the second entry of FallbackLocaleList). After an admin changes the site default locale, previously cached entries resolved through the old fallback remain in the LRU cache and are served, producing stale/incorrect translations until a process restart or `I18n.reload!`. The fallback chain (or default_locale) should be part of the cache key, or the cache must be invalidated when default_locale changes.

title: Fallback locales only loaded in web requests; jobs/mailers get missing translations
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only called from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Because `translate` lazily loads only `config.locale`, any code path outside a controller request (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console, console-driven digests) performing a lookup in a locale with a missing key will have the fallback locale's YAML not loaded, so the Fallbacks backend finds nothing and raises/returns a missing-translation instead of the fallback string. The loading should be hooked into the lookup path (e.g. inside `translate`/`load_locale`) or into the job/mailer locale setup as well.

title: translate can NoMethodError on nil @loaded_locales
body: `translate` does `@loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)` without initializing `@loaded_locales`, while the newly added `ensure_loaded!` defensively does `@loaded_locales ||= []`. If any translation happens before `reload!` has run (the only place that initializes the ivar), `translate` raises `NoMethodError` on nil. Initialize the ivar consistently (e.g. `@loaded_locales ||= []` in `translate` too) rather than relying on call ordering.

title: ensure_loaded!/@loaded_locales initialization is not thread-safe
body: `I18n.ensure_loaded!` reads and lazily initializes `@loaded_locales` outside `LOAD_MUTEX` (only `load_locale` takes the lock).
