It is used at line 115 (`authenticate`) and line 137 (`challenge(context, error, field)`), replacing the previous conditions which called `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `context.getUser() == null`. The polarity is inverted: for the normal first-time login (no user yet in the context) the WebAuthn attributes (challenge, rpId, conditional-UI flag) are no longer set on the form, so passkey conditional UI / discoverable-key autologin is broken on the plain login and on error re-renders. The condition likely should be `user == null || <re-auth case>` rather than `user != null`.

title: Always-false shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators skips the "no credential registered" short-circuit
body: By overriding `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` to always return `false`, `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm` never enters the branch that returns `null` when the identified user has no WebAuthn credential of the required type. During re-authentication (user already set in context) the passkey/WebAuthn form elements will therefore be rendered even for users who have no passkey registered, offering an authentication option that cannot succeed. Consider keeping the credential-existence check while suppressing only the allowCredentials list. Also, the method is missing `@Override`, so a future rename in the superclass would silently break this.

title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only method defined in the parent UsernamePasswordForm is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. Unless a no-arg overload exists elsewhere, this does not compile. If an overload is intended, add it explicitly; otherwise pass `context.getUser()` (though note that would make the condition always false here since the branch only runs when user != null).

title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires non-null user, disabling passkeys on the initial login form
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. In `authenticate()` the webauthn form data is now filled only if this returns true, so for a normal (non re-authentication) login where `context.getUser() == null`, `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never invoked and the conditional-UI/passkeys attributes are absent from the login page. Previously fillContextForm was called exactly in the user==null path. This breaks passwordless/conditional passkey login on the first login screen (and contradicts the tests asserting the `webauth` form is present on the initial login page). The same inverted condition also affects the error challenge path at line 137.

title: Missing @Override on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators
body: `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(AuthenticationFlowContext)` overrides the newly added hook in WebAuthnAuthenticator but lacks the @Override annotation, so a future signature change in the base class would silently stop overriding and re-enable showing authenticators during conditional passkey login.

title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` without arguments, but the only method defined in the superclass UsernamePasswordForm is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. There is no no-arg overload, so this does not compile. Either add a no-arg variant (e.g. `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`) or pass `context.getUser()`.

title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires a non-null user, disabling conditional passkeys on normal (first) login
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. It is used in authenticate() (line 115) and challenge() (line 137) to decide whether to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)`. Previously the form was filled when the user was NOT yet identified (`context.getUser() == null`), which is exactly the conditional-UI/passkey autofill case for a fresh login. With this change, a regular login (no user in the context) no longer gets the WebAuthn conditional-UI attributes, so passkey autofill/login from the username+password page is broken for the primary use case, while it is only enabled during re-authentication. The user!=null condition appears inverted / should not gate passkey setup at all.

title: Cleanup registers the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP alias
body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` uses the literal string "alias" rather than the actual alias (`idp-alias-<i>` / `idp-alias-20`). The 21 identity providers created by testCacheIDPForLogin are therefore never removed (and the cleanup call will fail with 404), leaving leftover IDPs in the realm that can make other tests in the class or run order flaky. Same problem at lines 381 and 425 (and the pre-existing line 303).

title: remove() now always issues a DB lookup by alias
body: Previously `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` was only executed on the invalidated-cache path; now it is executed unconditionally before deciding, adding an extra database query to every IDP removal even when the entry is cached. It also means the cached-path branch computes `storedIdp` it doesn't use. Consider reusing the cached model for the login-invalidation check.

title: getLoginPredicate can NPE on IDPs with null config
body: The new predicate calls `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` whenever `getOrganizationId() != null`. `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` is not guaranteed non-null (e.g. models built from partial representations or imports), so a NullPointerException can be thrown from create/update/remove paths that call `registerIDPLoginInvalidation`, breaking the IDP write operation. Use a null-safe access on the config map.

title: getForLogin cache not invalidated/bypassed when the organization changes
body: Unlike `getByOrganization`, which checks `isInvalid(orgId)` in addition to its own cache key, `getForLogin` only checks `isInvalid(cacheKey)`. If an organization is disabled or removed in the same transaction (or its invalidation is registered under the org id), the ORG_ONLY/ALL login lists remain served from cache and still contain the organization's IDPs. Callers that don't re-check `isEnabled()` on the returned wrapped models (only OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean does) will show IDPs of a disabled/removed organization on the login page. Consider also bypassing the cache when `organizationId` is invalidated, and registering login-cache invalidation on organization updates/removal.

title: getForLogin cache is not invalidated on organization changes
body: Unlike getByOrganization (line 173), which checks `isInvalid(orgId)` in addition to its own cache key, getForLogin only checks `isInvalid(cacheKey)`. Removing/disabling an organization, or changing an organization's identity-provider membership through the organization provider (which invalidates the organization id, not the `.idp.login.*` keys), will leave the ORG_ONLY/ALL login caches populated with stale IDP id sets. Consumers that call getForLogin and don't re-check `isEnabled()` (the wrapper only hides disabled orgs, not removed org links) will see providers that should no longer be offered for login. Consider also checking `isInvalid(organizationId)` and registering login-cache invalidations in the organization provider.

title: getLoginPredicate semantics changed for org-linked IDPs
body: `getLoginPredicate()` now additionally rejects any IDP that has an organizationId unless its config has BROKER_PUBLIC=true. This is a public SPI helper that may be used by callers other than the new invalidation logic (e.g. bean/federated-provider filtering); for them, non-public organization brokers will silently disappear from results. If the restriction is only needed for cache invalidation, it should be a separate predicate, or the behavior change should be documented in the method javadoc.

title: remove() always issues an extra DB lookup by alias
body: `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is now executed unconditionally in `remove()`, even when the entry is present (and valid) in the cache, where previously the cached model was used. This adds a database round-trip to every IDP removal. The stored model could be obtained from the cached entry in the else-branch instead.

title: Test cleanup registers the literal alias "alias" so created IDPs are never removed
body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` uses the hard-coded string "alias" rather than the created provider's alias (`idp-alias-N`). None of the 21 identity providers created by testCacheIDPForLogin are deleted after the test, and the cleanup call itself will fail/404. This leaks state into other tests in the realm (same bug is repeated at lines 303 and 425).

title: Cleanup registers removal of a provider named literally "alias"
body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` uses the literal string "alias" instead of the actual alias ("idp-alias-" + i / "idp-alias-20"). Consequently none of the 21 identity providers created by testCacheIDPForLogin are removed after the test (the cleanup targets a non-existent provider and will either no-op or throw), leaking state into other tests in the class/realm and making counts in subsequent tests flaky. Same mistake appears at lines 303 and 425.

title: getLoginPredicate semantics changed for all callers
body: getLoginPredicate() now additionally requires that org-linked IDPs have `organization.broker.public=true`. This public static predicate is used by callers outside the new invalidation logic (e.g. identity provider beans/filters); any caller that previously accepted org-linked, non-public IDPs will now silently drop them. This behavioural change is not documented in the enum's javadoc and could change which brokers are shown/accepted in flows unrelated to the login page.

title: getForLogin cache is not invalidated on organization changes
body: Unlike getByOrganization(), which checks `isInvalid(orgId)`, getForLogin() only checks the login cache key. If an organization is disabled, removed, or its IDP links change outside IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update() (e.g. OrganizationProvider operations that only invalidate the organization entry), the cached ID sets for ORG_ONLY/ALL remain stale. The PR compensates only in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean by re-checking isEnabled() on the wrapped model; other consumers of getForLogin() get IDPs of disabled/removed organizations. Consider also checking isInvalid(organizationId) and registering login invalidation on organization updates/removal.

title: remove() now always performs a DB lookup by alias
body: `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is now executed unconditionally at the start of remove(), even when the alias is present in the cache (previously the DB lookup only happened on the invalidated path). This adds an extra query to every IDP removal. The cached CachedIdentityProvider could be reused to build the model needed for registerIDPLoginInvalidation.

title: New abstract `order()` method breaks external CryptoProvider implementations
body: `int order();` is added as an abstract method to the public `CryptoProvider` interface. Any third-party or downstream implementation (e.g. in the keycloak-client repo, adapters, custom FIPS providers) will fail to compile and will throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime when loaded via ServiceLoader. Give it a `default` implementation (e.g. `return 100;` or 0) to keep the interface backward compatible.

title: Ambiguous provider selection no longer fails fast and is logged only at debug
body: Previously having multiple `CryptoProvider`s on the classpath threw `IllegalStateException`. Now the highest `order()` wins, but `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider` and `WildFlyElytronProvider` all return 200, so if two of them are on the classpath (a real misconfiguration, e.g. default + fips) the choice is arbitrary/ServiceLoader-order dependent and silently proceeds, only noted via `debug` logging. Consider distinct orders and/or a warn-level message when two providers share the top order.

title: logger.debugf called with a dynamic string as format
body: `logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes a runtime-built string as the format template. If any class name or future content contains a '%' character this throws/misformats (java.util.IllegalFormatException). Use `logger.debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", ...)` with the value as an argument.

title: getKeyStore uses enum name() instead of toString() unlike other providers
body: All other CryptoProvider implementations call `KeyStore.getInstance(format.toString())`. `KeystoreFormat` overrides `toString()` (the JCA type string may differ from the enum constant name, e.g. for PKCS12/BCFKS variants), so using `format.name()` here can request a nonexistent keystore type and make `getSupportedKeyStoreTypes()` report wrong results. Use `format.toString()` for consistency.

title: Indefinite-length sequence silently decodes as empty list
body: `readLength()` returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (0x80). In `readSequence()` the loop `while (length > 0)` is then never entered, so an indefinite-length SEQUENCE returns an empty list instead of an error, and callers then throw a confusing "Invalid sequence with size different to 2" or mis-handle it. Reject length < 0 explicitly in readSequence/readInteger.

title: Dead ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls
body: Lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder instances, write the integers and discard the results; they have no effect since the DER sequence is built on lines 117-121. Remove them to avoid confusion (and wasted allocations).

title: Test only round-trips its own encoder and uses a wrong-size key for ES384/ES512
body: The key pair is generated with the JDK default EC curve (typically P-256) yet the test runs with `ECDSAAlgorithm.ES384`/`ES512` signature lengths, so the signatures are not representative of those algorithms. Additionally the assertion only compares the decoder's output with itself after re-encoding, so a systematically incorrect DER encoding (e.g. missing padding or wrong tags) would still pass. The test should use the proper curve per algorithm and verify interoperability, e.g. compare against the BouncyCastle-based `BCECDSACryptoProvider` output and/or verify the re-encoded DER with `Signature.verify()`.

title: New abstract method order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: `int order()` is added to the public `CryptoProvider` interface without a `default` implementation. Any third-party or downstream (e.g. keycloak-client repo, custom FIPS integrations) implementation of this interface will fail to compile / throw AbstractMethodError at runtime after upgrade. Give it a `default int order() { return 100; }` (or similar) to keep binary/source compatibility.

title: Ties in provider order are resolved non-deterministically instead of failing
body: Previously, finding more than one CryptoProvider on the classpath threw IllegalStateException. Now providers are only sorted by `order()`, and DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider and WildFlyElytronProvider all return 200. If two of these end up on the classpath (a realistic misconfiguration, e.g. FIPS + default BC), the selection depends on ServiceLoader/sort stability and the server may silently run with the wrong crypto provider (e.g. non-FIPS BC in FIPS mode) instead of failing fast. Consider throwing when the top two providers have equal order, or at least logging at WARN.

title: logger.debugf called with dynamic string as format
body: `logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes a runtime-built message as a format string with no arguments. Any '%' character in a provider class name (or future message content) would cause an UnknownFormatConversionException inside logging. Use `logger.debug(builder.toString())` or `logger.debugf("%s", ...)`.

title: Dead/duplicated ASN1 encoding calls
body: Lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder instances, write r and s, and discard the results; the actual DER is built again on lines 117-121. These two statements are dead code (wasted allocation and confusing); they should be removed.

title: Test uses a default (P-256) EC key for ES384/ES512, so it does not verify real conversions
body: `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` uses the default curve (usually secp256r1) for all three tests. For ES384/ES512 the signature produced is a P-256 signature, while `algorithm.getSignatureLength()` is 96/132, so `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` silently zero-pads and the round-trip assertion passes without exercising correct ES384/ES512 behaviour. Generate the matching curve per algorithm (secp256r1/secp384r1/secp521r1) and also assert that the re-derived DER signature verifies with `Signature.verify`, so a real encoding bug would be caught.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default KeyStore provider
body: The method is documented to return a BouncyCastle (FIPS or non-FIPS) security provider, but here it returns whatever JCA provider supplies the default KeyStore type. Callers such as `BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` will then pass e.g. "SUN" as a provider name to algorithm lookups, which can fail with NoSuchProviderException for algorithms that provider doesn't implement. Returning null or throwing UnsupportedOperationException (consistent with the other unsupported methods) would be clearer than returning an unrelated provider.

title: New abstract order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: `int order()` is added as an abstract method to the public `CryptoProvider` interface. Any third-party or out-of-tree implementation (e.g. custom crypto providers shipped by adapters or downstream projects) will fail to compile and will throw AbstractMethodError at runtime after upgrade. Since a sensible fallback exists, this should be a `default int order() { return 100; }` (or similar) to preserve binary/source compatibility.

title: Ambiguous provider selection when orders are equal is now silent
body: Previously multiple CryptoProviders on the classpath caused an IllegalStateException. Now providers are sorted by order and the first is chosen; if two providers share the same order (all in-tree providers use 200, e.g. DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider, WildFlyElytronProvider), the selection depends on ServiceLoader iteration order and is effectively non-deterministic, with only a debug log. A conflicting FIPS/non-FIPS selection would be a silent, hard-to-diagnose misconfiguration; consider logging a warning (or failing) when the top two providers have equal order.

title: logger.debugf called with a dynamically built string as format
body: `logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes a runtime-constructed string as the format argument with no parameters. If any class name (or future content) contains a `%` sequence, formatting will fail/produce garbage. Use `logger.debug(builder.toString())` instead.

title: Indefinite length (-1) leads to NegativeArraySizeException instead of IOException
body: `readLength()` returns -1 for the indefinite-length encoding (0x80). In `readInteger()` (line 71-72) and `readNext()` that value is passed straight to `read(int length)`, which does `new byte[length]` and will throw an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException on malformed/attacker-supplied DER instead of the declared IOException. Callers parsing untrusted signatures (asn1derToConcatenatedRS) would get an unexpected runtime exception. Reject indefinite length explicitly with an IOException.

title: Dead code: two ASN1Encoder instances created and discarded
body: Lines 114-115 create `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` / `...write(sBigInteger)` and discard the results; the actual DER sequence is built again on lines 117-121. These two statements have no effect and should be removed to avoid confusing readers into thinking state is accumulated.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns an unrelated provider
body: The method returns the provider of the default KeyStore type (e.g. SUN), which is not a BouncyCastle provider. Code paths such as BouncyIntegration/Provider-name based `getInstance(alg, provider)` lookups will silently use a provider that does not implement the expected algorithms, producing confusing NoSuchAlgorithmException errors far from the cause. Returning null or throwing UnsupportedOperationException (consistent with the other unimplemented methods) would be clearer.

title: Test uses a default (P-256) EC key for ES384/ES512 cases
body: `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` uses the JDK default curve (typically secp256r1) for all three tests, so testES384/testES512 never exercise real P-384/P-521 signatures; r/s are just zero-padded to the larger length. Initialize the generator with the matching `ECGenParameterSpec` per algorithm so the conversion is validated for real ES384/ES512 signature sizes.

title: Possible NPE when the 'Clients' resource-type resource cannot be resolved
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no resource exists for the client, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...). That method returns null when the realm's authorization schema is not supported/enabled or the resource was not found. The returned value is passed straight into policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and then dereferenced via resource.getScopes(), so a null result causes a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of simply denying access. Add a null check returning false.

title: getClientsWithPermission includes the aggregate 'Clients' resource in the result set
body: resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) matches every resource whose type is "Clients", which includes the schema-created aggregate resource named "Clients" (created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init with name == type == "Clients"). If a permission is granted on the aggregate resource, the literal string "Clients" is added to the returned set of client ids. Callers interpret these entries as client identifiers, so this yields a bogus id (and, conversely, granting an all-clients permission does not expand into the actual client ids). Filter out the resource whose name equals the resource type and handle the all-clients case explicitly.

title: getResourceName has no branch for the new Clients resource type
body: getResourceName only resolves friendly names for the Users resource type. For permissions with resourceType "Clients" it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is not set for resources created by getOrCreateResource (only name == client internal id is stored). As a result the admin API/UI will show null (or no name) for client-scoped permissions, instead of the clientId or "All clients". Add a Clients branch resolving the client by id, mirroring the Users handling.

title: Removal cleanup listener now skipped when neither FGAP v1 nor v2 flag matches
body: registerListener's body is now wrapped in `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`. Previously the role/client/group removal handlers always ran, cleaning up leftover authorization policies for deleted roles, clients and groups created while v1 was enabled. After this change, if an installation disables the v1 feature (e.g. switches to v2) any pre-existing v1 permission policies for removed roles/clients/groups are left orphaned in the database. If the gating is only meant to avoid the UnsupportedOperationException thrown by the new V2 classes, gate on "v2 not enabled" or make the V2 setPermissionsEnabled a no-op instead.

title: Dead code and unused imports in new class
body: getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is private and never called, and the `logger` field, the static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE and the imports of Scope/ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/EvaluationContext are unused. This dead code was presumably copied from ClientPermissions (token exchange) and should be removed to avoid suggesting token-exchange evaluation is supported here (canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException).

title: Possible NPE when the 'Clients' resource-type resource is missing
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no per-client resource exists the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...), which can return null (it returns null when the realm doesn't support the authz schema, when the type is unknown, or when the named resource simply isn't found). The returned value is passed directly to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and then dereferenced via resource.getScopes(), so a null fallback causes a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of a clean 'deny'. Add a null check returning false.

title: getClientsWithPermission can return the resource-type resource name
body: resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) also matches the generic 'Clients' resource created by the schema for all-clients permissions (its type equals the resource type). Its name ('Clients') is not a client id, so the returned set may contain a bogus entry that callers use to filter/lookup clients, leading to incorrect client listings. Skip the resource whose name equals CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE (or expand it to all clients).

title: getResourceName not implemented for the new Clients resource type
body: getResourceName() only handles the USERS resource type; for policies with resourceType 'Clients' it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is not set for resources created by getOrCreateResource(). As a result the admin API/console will show null/empty names for client-scoped permissions instead of the clientId (and 'All clients' for the type resource). Add a CLIENTS branch resolving the client by id.

title: Cleanup listener now skipped when only V2 is enabled
body: The removal listener (role/client/group removal -> setPermissionsEnabled(false)) is now guarded by Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ. If a deployment previously created V1 permission resources and then runs with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ disabled (e.g. only V2 enabled), orphan authorization resources/policies for removed roles, clients and groups will no longer be cleaned up, leaving stale data. Consider still cleaning up V1 data regardless of the flag, or document the migration.

title: Dead code and unused imports in new class
body: getEvaluationContext(...) is private and never used, and the imports for TOKEN_EXCHANGE, Scope, ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, EvaluationContext and the unused `logger` field are dead. Removing them avoids confusion about token-exchange evaluation being supported in V2 (canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException).

title: Possible NPE when the 'Clients' resource-type resource is missing
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String) when no per-client resource exists, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...), which can return null (it returns null when the realm does not support the authorization schema, when the resource type is unknown, or when the resource was never created/was deleted). The returned value is immediately passed to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later to new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server), causing a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of a clean 403. A null check returning false is needed.

title: Listener throws UnsupportedOperationException when both FGAP v1 and v2 are enabled
body: registerListener now only runs when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (v1) is enabled, but management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. If both features are enabled simultaneously, removing a client triggers clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...) on ClientPermissionsV2, which throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"), breaking client/role/group deletion. The guard should also exclude the case where v2 is active (or the v1 implementation should be used explicitly here).

title: getResourceName not implemented for the new Clients resource type
body: getResourceName handles only USERS: for a policy with resourceType 'Clients' it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is not set for resources created by getOrCreateResource (resources are created with name=client UUID and no display name). As a result admin/UI consumers get null instead of the client's clientId, or 'Clients' instead of a readable 'All clients' label. Add a Clients branch resolving the client by id.

title: Dead code: unused getEvaluationContext and unused imports/constants
body: getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is private and never referenced (canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException), as are the logger field, the static TOKEN_EXCHANGE import and the Scope/ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext imports. Dead code copied from V1 misleads readers into thinking token-exchange evaluation is wired up; it should be removed.

title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 (breaking scripted contract)
body: The exit code signalling "recreate upgrade required" was changed from 4 to 3, and 4 now means "feature disabled". Since the documented purpose of this command is to be consumed by scripts/CI pipelines via the exit code, any existing automation keyed on exit code 4 will now interpret a disabled-feature error as "recreate needed" (or miss recreate signals entirely). This should at least be called out in release/upgrade notes, and any other consumers of the constant (e.g. the operator's update logic) verified.

title: No assertion on the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the stderr text and does not assert the process exit code is 4 (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED). Since the exit-code contract is the documented machine-readable interface (and codes were just renumbered), a regression in the exit code would go undetected. Also no test covers the `check` subcommand with the feature disabled.

title: Exit code 4 changed meaning: was 'recreate required', now 'feature disabled'
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3 and 4 is now reused for FEATURE_DISABLED. Any existing automation/pipeline written against the previously released behaviour that treats exit code 4 as 'recreate upgrade required' will now silently interpret a 'feature not enabled' failure as a recreate signal (and vice versa, a real recreate requirement returns 3 which such scripts likely treat as unexpected). If backwards compatibility matters, pick an unused code (e.g. 5) for FEATURE_DISABLED instead of recycling 4, and call out the change in the release notes.

title: Feature-disabled path only tested for 'metadata', exit code not asserted
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only exercises the `metadata` subcommand and asserts the error text; it does not assert the new exit code (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) nor cover the `check` subcommand, which has the same new guard. Since the documented contract is the exit code (docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc lists code 4), a regression in the exit code or in the `check` guard would go unnoticed.

title: Exit code semantics swapped: 4 changes meaning from 'recreate needed' to 'feature disabled'
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moved from 4 to 3 and 4 is now reused for FEATURE_DISABLED. Any existing automation/script (or operator logic) that treats exit code 4 as "recreate upgrade required" will now silently interpret a feature-disabled run (where no compatibility check happened at all) as "recreate required", and will not recognize the new code 3. Since both meanings are mutually inconsistent, this is a breaking contract change that should be called out in release/upgrade notes, and ideally the feature-disabled code should be a fresh value rather than the previously used 4.

title: No assertion on exit code for feature-disabled path, and check subcommand not covered
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message for the `metadata` subcommand. The newly introduced exit code (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4) is the documented contract for scripting, but no test verifies it; likewise the `check` subcommand's feature-disabled behaviour is untested. A regression in the exit code (e.g. the recent 3/4 renumbering) would go unnoticed.

title: canManage() grants manage on groups to admins holding only the view scope
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` evaluates `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it returns true if the caller only has the `view` scope on the `Groups` resource type. `canManage()` backs `requireManage()` used by `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup`, so an admin granted only all-groups `view` can create top-level groups. The scope list should contain only `MANAGE` (compare `canManage(GroupModel)` at line 79, which correctly uses only `MANAGE`).

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In V2, the authz resource created for a group is named with the group id (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`, which returns `group.getId()` as the resource name), while `resource.getId()` is an unrelated resource UUID. `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set, and that set is stored as the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute in `UsersResource.searchForUser`/`BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` and passed to `session.users().getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)`. With wrong ids, the store-level filtering/count matches no groups, so user counts are reported as 0 and group-scoped user queries return nothing. Use `groupResource.getName()`.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes a resource id into hasPermission(groupId, ...)
body: `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` resolves the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, but here it is called with `groupResource.getId()` (a resource UUID), not the resource name/group id. The lookup therefore always returns null and the code falls back to the `Groups` resource-type ("all groups") resource, so per-group view-members permissions are never detected and the method returns an empty or incorrect set. Pass `groupResource.getName()` (or refactor to evaluate the already-loaded resource).

title: Possible NPE when the Groups resource-type resource cannot be resolved
body: If `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` returns null (it returns null when the authorization schema is not supported for the resource server, or when the resource type resource is missing), `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` is called with a null resource and `resource.getScopes()` is dereferenced at line 152, causing a NullPointerException instead of a clean deny. Add a null check and return false.

title: getResourceName does not handle the new Groups resource type
body: `getResourceName` only resolves human-readable names for the `Users` resource type. Group permissions store the group id as the resource name, so for `Groups` permissions this now falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is not set for these resources and will typically be null — the admin console will show no/blank resource name for group permissions. Add a `Groups` branch resolving the group path/name (and "All groups" for the type resource).

title: Javadoc on requireManageMembers refers to the wrong method
body: The javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` says it throws ForbiddenException if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false; the implementation checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. Also `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` is documented as returning a "Stream of IDs" while its return type is `Set<String>`.

title: Removal of public ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes breaks extensions
body: `searchGroupModelsByAttributes` was a public static method on `ModelToRepresentation` in server-spi-private; deleting it is a source/binary incompatible change for any provider or downstream code calling it. Consider deprecating and delegating instead of removing outright, or note the removal in upgrade docs.

title: canManage() for all groups is granted by the VIEW scope
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (the no-argument variant used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup via requireManage()) evaluates `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`. This means an admin who only has the `view` scope on the `Groups` resource type is allowed to create top-level groups (and anything else gated by canManage()). The scope list should only contain MANAGE, as canManage(GroupModel) correctly does.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs and evaluates permissions with the wrong key
body: For FGAP v2 the group resource is created with `name` = group id (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup) and a separate generated resource `id`. Here the code (a) calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`, but hasPermission looks the resource up with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, so it never finds the per-group resource and always falls back to the "all groups" resource; and (b) adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set, while callers (UsersResource.searchForUser via session attribute UserModel.GROUPS, and UsersResource.getUsersCount) expect group IDs. Consequently per-group view-members permissions are ignored by this method and, when a result is returned, user searches/counts are filtered by non-existent group IDs. Use `groupResource.getName()` for both the permission lookup and the returned set.

title: Possible NPE when the "Groups" resource-type resource is absent
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource` returns null if the schema is not supported for the resource server or the resource is not found. The returned value is used immediately in `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and `resource.getScopes()` without a null check, which would throw a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of simply denying access. Add a null guard returning false.

title: Group removal listener will fail with UnsupportedOperationException when FGAP v2 is enabled
body: AdminPermissions.registerListener (registered when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled) handles GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent by calling `management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)`. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 also enabled, `management()` returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose new `groups()` override returns GroupPermissionsV2, which throws UnsupportedOperationException from setPermissionsEnabled. Deleting any group (and GroupResource#getManagementPermissions / setManagementPermissionsEnabled, which call isPermissionsEnabled/getPermissions) will therefore fail with a 500 when both features are on.

title: getResourceName does not resolve group names for the new Groups resource type
body: Now that GROUPS is part of the schema, policies of resource type `Groups` store the group id as the resource name. getResourceName only special-cases USERS, so for group permissions it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is null for these generated resources. The admin console/REST representation will show no (or a raw) name for group permissions. A branch resolving the group (including the "All groups" case for the resource named `Groups`) is needed.

title: Javadoc on requireManageMembers refers to the wrong method
body: The Javadoc of `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` states it throws ForbiddenException if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false; it actually checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. This is misleading for implementers of the interface. Also, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` is documented as returning a "Stream of IDs" while it returns a Set.

title: canManage() grants manage on all groups to holders of only the VIEW scope
body: The no-arg `canManage()` evaluates `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it returns true if the admin only has the `view` scope on the Groups resource type. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` calls `auth.groups().requireManage()`, so an admin granted only all-groups `view` can create top-level groups (and any other check routed through `canManage()`), which is a privilege escalation. It should only check `MANAGE`.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs, and permission lookup by resource id fails
body: In the `findByType` callback, `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` is called, but `hasPermission` resolves the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` and the Groups resources are named by the *group id* (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`, which returns `group.getId()` as the resource name). Passing the authz resource UUID therefore never matches, so the method silently falls back to the all-groups resource evaluation and the per-group `view-members`/`manage-members` grants are ignored. Likewise the IDs added to `granted` are authz resource IDs, but the returned set is used as `UserModel.GROUPS` in `UsersResource.searchForUser`/`getUsersCount` and `BruteForceUsersResource`, where group IDs are expected, so user searches/counts scoped by group membership return wrong results. Use `groupResource.getName()` in both places.

title: Possible NullPointerException when the Groups resource-type resource is absent
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...)` returns null when admin permissions are not enabled for the resource server, when the resource type is unknown, or when the 'Groups' resource is missing from the store. The returned value is used immediately in `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and `resource.getScopes()` without a null check, causing an NPE instead of a clean deny. Add a null guard returning false.

title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers references the wrong method
body: The Javadoc above `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` states it throws if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false; it actually delegates to `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. The duplicated doc is misleading for implementors of the interface.

title: getResourceName does not resolve names for the new Groups resource type
body: `getResourceName` only special-cases `USERS`; for the newly added `GROUPS` resource type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Since group resources are stored with the raw group id as name and no display name, the admin UI/REST representation of a group-scoped permission will show an empty/raw id instead of the group path or name. Add a Groups branch resolving the group (and 'All groups' for the type resource).

title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax introduced into i18next-based JS message bundles
body: The admin-ui (and account-ui, line 188 of js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3/account/messages/messages_en.properties) bundles are consumed by the React apps through i18next, which interpolates `{{0}}` placeholders, not Java MessageFormat `{0}`/`{0,choice,...}`. Replacing `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` with `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` means the placeholders are no longer substituted and the raw choice expression is rendered to end users. The sanitizer requirement (avoiding a bare `<`) should be solved differently for the JS bundles, e.g. by keeping `{{n}}` placeholders and avoiding the choice construct.

title: Diff reporting can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body: The prefix/suffix trimming computes `start` and `end` independently, so for overlapping cases the subsequent substring calls are invalid. Example: value="aa", sanitized="a" gives start=1 and end=1, then `sanitized.substring(1, 1-1=0)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. Instead of reporting the offending message, the Maven plugin crashes with an unrelated exception. Clamp `end` to `Math.min(end, len-start)` for each string before substring.

title: santizeAnchors removes the wrong anchor occurrence / uses stale matcher
body: `value = value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` always strips the *first* textual occurrence of the tag in the (already modified) value, not the occurrence the matcher is currently positioned at, while `matcher` still iterates the original string. For messages with several identical anchor tags (e.g. two ``), tags are removed out of order and positions no longer line up, so legitimate strings can be flagged or malicious extra anchors can slip through unnoticed. Use the matcher's start/end offsets (or build the result with Matcher.appendReplacement) instead of replaceFirst.

title: Missing English counterpart aborts verification with RuntimeException
body: The English baseline path is derived purely by string replacement (`resources-community` -> `resources`, locale suffix -> `_en`). If that file does not exist (community-only themes/locales, or any bundle whose English base lives elsewhere), a RuntimeException is thrown and the whole build fails with "unable to read file ..." rather than the verifier reporting a usable message or skipping the HTML check. Handle FileNotFoundException explicitly (skip or add a descriptive message).

title: Lithuanian translations replaced with Italian text
body: `loginTotpStep1` was replaced with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` (Italian) in the Lithuanian bundle; the same wrong-language string was inserted in themes/.../account/messages/messages_lt.properties line 101. Lithuanian users will see Italian text. Use a Lithuanian wording (or leave the key out so the English fallback applies).

title: Simplified Chinese bundle given Traditional Chinese text
body: `loginTotpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機/應用程式) in the zh_CN (Simplified) bundle, which is inconsistent with the rest of the file. Should be e.g. `在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：`.

title: i18next bundle changed to Java MessageFormat syntax; placeholders will not interpolate
body: The admin-ui (and account-ui) message bundles are consumed by the React apps through i18next, which uses double-brace interpolation (`{{0}}`, `{{name}}`) — see all other keys in these files. Changing `error-invalid-multivalued-size` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` means the single braces are not interpolated by i18next and the ChoiceFormat expression is not understood at all, so the user will literally see `{0}`, `{1}` and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` in the UI. The same change was made in js/apps/account-ui/.../messages_en.properties (line 188) and the admin-ui zh_CN bundle. These JS bundles should keep `{{0}}`-style placeholders; only the Freemarker/Java themes under themes/src/main/resources support MessageFormat choice syntax.

title: Missing English counterpart file aborts the build with an unchecked exception
body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file path by string replacement and then throws a RuntimeException if it cannot be opened. Any community/locale properties file that has no matching `_en.properties` in the corresponding `resources` tree (a common situation, e.g. a locale file that exists only in resources-community, or a path where the `resources-community`→`resources` substitution does not yield a real file) will crash the plugin with an unchecked exception instead of producing a verification message or being skipped. Prefer treating a missing English file as "no English reference" (empty bundle) and, where a real I/O error occurs, wrapping it in MojoExecutionException like the rest of the code does.

title: Anchor sanitization removes the wrong occurrence and can misreport
body: santizeAnchors() iterates matches of the translated value with `matcher`, but then does `value = value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` — it mutates `value` while `matcher` still iterates over the original string, and replaceFirst always removes the *first* occurrence rather than the one just matched. For a value with several identical anchors (e.g. two ``), the wrong occurrences get stripped and the loop indices no longer line up with the mutated string, so legitimate values can be reported as illegal HTML, or illegal anchors can be silently stripped and missed. Iterate with a StringBuilder/Matcher.appendReplacement, or remove at the known match offsets.

title: Anchor-mismatch message lacks file and key, making failures hard to locate
body: The message "Didn't find anchor tag <a ...> in original string" contains neither the file path nor the message key (the `key` parameter is passed in but never used), unlike the duplicate-key and illegal-HTML messages. When the plugin runs over hundreds of properties files, a maintainer cannot tell which translation failed. Include `key` and `file` in the message.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: `loginTotpStep1` was replaced with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` — Italian text in a Lithuanian bundle. The same wrong-language string was introduced in themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties. Users with locale `lt` will see Italian on the OTP setup page; the string should be Lithuanian (or left to fall back to the base bundle).

title: Simplified Chinese bundle given Traditional Chinese text
body: `totpStep1` was set to `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`, which is Traditional Chinese (手機/應用程式), in the zh_CN (Simplified) bundle. It should use Simplified Chinese wording (e.g. 在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：).

title: i18next message converted to Java MessageFormat/choice syntax
body: The account-ui (and admin-ui) message bundles are consumed by the React apps through i18next, which interpolates `{{0}}`-style placeholders and has no support for Java MessageFormat `{0}` or `{2,choice,...}`. Changing `error-invalid-multivalued-size` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` means the end user will see the literal text `{0}`, `{1}` and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` instead of substituted values. The same applies to js/apps/admin-ui/.../messages_en.properties:3138. Only the server-side themes/ bundles (Freemarker/MessageFormat) can use the choice syntax.

title: Common-prefix/suffix trimming can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body: The two loops computing `start` and `end` are independent, so `start + end` can exceed the string length when the differing part is a repetition of surrounding characters (e.g. value="aa", sanitized="aaa" yields start=2, end=2). The subsequent `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` then gets end index < begin index and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the build with an opaque error instead of reporting the illegal HTML. Clamp `end` to `min(end, length - start)` for both strings.

title: Missing English reference bundle aborts verification with RuntimeException
body: `verifySafeHtml()` derives the English file path by string replacement and throws an unchecked RuntimeException if it cannot be opened. Any bundle whose English counterpart does not exist at the derived path (community-only message directories, bundles without a locale suffix, or paths where the `resources-community`→`resources` substitution does not yield a real file) will fail the build with a raw RuntimeException instead of a MojoExecutionException/skippable warning. Handle the missing-file case explicitly (skip or report a message).

title: santizeAnchors removes the wrong anchor occurrence and reports without file context
body: Inside the loop, `value.replaceFirst(...)` always strips the *first* occurrence of the English anchor tag in the (already modified) value, while `matcher` still iterates the original string. With more than one identical anchor tag per message the positions get out of sync, so a mismatched/injected anchor can be silently removed (false negative) or a valid one flagged. Also the message added at line 157 contains neither the key nor the file name, making the failure hard to locate; all other messages include them.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: `loginTotpStep1` was replaced with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian sentence. The same wrong text was introduced in themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties (totpStep1).

title: Simplified-Chinese bundle given Traditional Chinese text
body: `totpStep1` was set to `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`, which is Traditional Chinese (zh_TW) wording/characters, in the zh_CN (Simplified) bundle. Should use Simplified characters, e.g. `在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`.

title: No positive test that a clean bundle yields no findings
body: All new tests assert that a violation is reported; none asserts the opposite (e.g. verifying `noHtml_en.properties` or a file with allowed `<b>`/anchor identical to English returns an empty message list). Without such a test, a regression that makes the sanitizer report false positives for legitimate messages (a likely outcome given the unescaping/`<!-- -->` hacks) would go undetected.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring offsets
body: In `isAccessTokenId`, the grant shortcut is extracted with `items[0].substring(3, 5)` but the encoded prefix is `<2 chars sessionType><2 chars tokenType><2 chars grantType>`, so the grant shortcut is at indices 4..6. Additionally the check is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when the shortcut matches. Combined, the matcher accepts tokens with the wrong grant and can reject correct ones, so all event assertions using it (code-to-token, refresh, device, CIBA) do not actually verify the encoded grant type — the new feature is effectively untested.

title: Null check for rawTokenId checks grantType instead
body: The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` — it validates `grantType` twice and never validates `rawTokenId`. A null `rawTokenId` passes validation and later produces a token id ending in "null" or an NPE far from the source.

title: Removal of public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) breaks SPI consumers
body: The `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor was deleted from the `OAuth2GrantType.Context` class in server-spi-private. Any custom grant-type provider or extension (this is a published SPI type) that subclasses or copies the context via this constructor will no longer compile/link. If the removal is intended, it should be deprecated first or at least noted as a breaking change in upgrade notes.

title: Decoding an access token id with unknown shortcuts throws IllegalArgumentException
body: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` throws `IllegalArgumentException` whenever the part before ':' is not exactly 6 chars or contains an unrecognized shortcut. Token ids are attacker/third-party controllable in endpoints that accept tokens (introspection, userinfo, revocation, logout, tokens issued by a differently configured/older cluster node or custom encoder). An unchecked exception there will surface as a 500 instead of an "invalid token" response. Decoding should fall back to the UNKNOWN context (as done for ids without ':') rather than throwing.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring offsets
body: In the new `isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut)` matcher the grant shortcut is extracted with `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, but the encoded prefix is 6 chars (2 session type + 2 token type + 2 grant type), so the grant shortcut lives at indices 4..6, not 3..5. Additionally the check is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false exactly when the grant matches. The combined effect is that the matcher accepts tokens with any grant type except (incorrectly offset) the expected one, so all the converted assertions (`expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectAuthReqIdToToken`) do not actually verify the encoded grant and may pass/fail for the wrong reason. Should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` (with a length check on items[0]).

title: Null check validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` again; `rawTokenId` is never validated. A null rawTokenId will silently pass and produce a token ID ending in "...:null" when encoded. Should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

title: New abstract getShortcut() on public SPI interface breaks existing custom grant implementations
body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` lives in server-spi-private and is implemented by third-party extensions. Adding `String getShortcut();` without a default implementation makes all existing custom grant-type factories fail to compile/load (AbstractMethodError at runtime for pre-compiled providers). Consider providing a default implementation (e.g. derived/unknown shortcut) or documenting the breaking change in upgrade notes.

title: Removal of OAuth2GrantType.Context copy constructor is a breaking SPI change
body: The public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` was deleted from this server-spi-private class. Any extension (or downstream code) that subclasses/copies the grant context will no longer compile or will fail at runtime. If removal is intended it should be noted as a breaking change; otherwise keep the constructor (copying the new `grantType` field as well).

title: Possible NPE when client session has no user session
body: `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession()` is dereferenced without a null check. `initToken` in TokenManager already receives a `UserSessionModel` parameter and some flows (e.g. token exchange with transient/detached sessions, or contexts built from a client session only) can have a null user session on the client session, which would throw an NPE while issuing a token. Either pass the user session explicitly into the encoder or guard for null and fall back to SessionType.UNKNOWN/TRANSIENT.

title: Duplicate-shortcut validation can be bypassed by lazy map refresh
body: The size-comparison check for duplicate grant shortcuts only runs in `postInit`. `getShortcutByGrantType`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut` later insert entries lazily without re-validating, so a newly deployed grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one will silently overwrite the shortcut→grant mapping, causing token IDs to decode to the wrong grant type. Consider validating on insert (e.g. `putIfAbsent` and logging/erroring on conflict).

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring offsets
body: The matcher extracts the grant shortcut with `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, but the encoded prefix is sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grantType(2), so the grant shortcut lives at indices 4..6; indices 3..5 straddle the token-type and grant-type shortcuts. In addition the comparison is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` fails the match when the shortcut *does* equal the expected value. As written the matcher accepts any token id whose prefix differs from the expectation and rejects correct ones, so all the new assertions on Details.TOKEN_ID verify nothing (or the wrong thing). Should be `substring(4, 6)` and `if (!...equals(...)) return false;`.

title: Null check for rawTokenId checks grantType instead
body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` duplicates the previous grantType check, so a null `rawTokenId` is never rejected. A null raw token id then silently produces a token id like "onrtac:null" during encoding instead of failing fast.

title: Removal of public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) breaks SPI compatibility
body: The copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` was deleted from the public SPI class `OAuth2GrantType.Context` in server-spi-private. Any custom grant-type provider (or internal code built against previous versions) using it will no longer compile/link. If it is no longer needed internally, this should at least be noted as a breaking SPI change, or kept and made to copy the new `grantType` field.

title: Lazy shortcut registration bypasses duplicate-shortcut validation
body: `getShortcutByGrantType`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut` add entries to both maps at runtime without checking whether the shortcut is already mapped to a different grant type (the only duplicate validation happens once in postInit). A newly deployed grant with a colliding shortcut will silently overwrite `grantsByShortcuts`, so token ids encoded with that shortcut will decode to the wrong grant type.

title: Unused import added
body: `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory` is imported but not referenced; the grant type is set via `OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE`. Remove the import.

title: Used recovery codes are never invalidated when credential lives in user storage
body: After a successful recovery-code login the authenticator now looks the credential up via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(), which may return a credential coming from getFederatedCredentialsStream() (i.e. built on the fly by the user-storage provider). For such a credential nothing is written back: the code is not marked as used and only removeStoredCredentialById() is attempted when all codes are used — that call operates on local (Keycloak DB) credentials and the federated model may even have a null id, so it is a no-op. Consequently a single recovery code stored in user storage can be reused indefinitely, and the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action is never triggered after exhaustion. Some write-back path (e.g. updateCredential with the consumed code removed) is needed.

title: Login form always asks for recovery code #0 for federated credentials / unchecked Optional.get()
body: codeNumber is derived from getNextRecoveryAuthnCode() of a credential model that, for user-storage backed users, is reconstructed fresh from the provider on every request with no usage state. The form therefore always prompts for the first code, which combined with the missing invalidation makes the flow effectively single-code. Additionally credentialModelOpt.get() is called without isPresent() check, so if RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential returns empty the page rendering fails with NoSuchElementException instead of a meaningful error.

title: getCredentials() can NPE when user is not in the in-memory map
body: getMyUser(user) returns null for any user whose username is not present in the `users` map (e.g. a local-storage user or a stale cached federated reference), and the very next line dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes without a null check. Other methods in this class (isConfiguredFor, isValid, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream) all guard against null. This will throw a NullPointerException from credential enumeration paths (account console / admin REST) and break tests.

title: Recovery-codes credential returned from getCredentials() has no id
body: RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) does not carry over myUser.recoveryCodes.getId(), so the returned CredentialModel has a null id. Callers such as RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator use getId() for removeStoredCredentialById and the account REST API exposes credential ids, so a null id leads to silent no-ops or confusing responses.

title: Raw recovery codes are handed to user storage as plaintext JSON with no documented contract
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the full list of raw (unhashed) recovery codes into UserCredentialModel.challengeResponse and passes it to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). Any user-storage provider implementing CredentialInputUpdater now receives all recovery codes in clear text, whereas local storage stores only hashes (the test provider in this PR indeed stores and compares them in plaintext). At minimum the hashing/storage expectation must be documented on this public helper, and ideally hashed values (RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode) should be passed instead.

title: Raw recovery codes are serialized and passed to the user storage provider in plaintext
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential() serializes the full list of freshly generated recovery codes as JSON and passes them as the challenge response of a UserCredentialModel to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). Unlike the local credential provider, which stores only salted/hashed codes (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel hashes each code), this hands the clear-text codes to arbitrary third-party UserStorageProviders, which will typically persist them as-is (the testsuite provider in this PR does exactly that, see BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential). This turns a hashed-at-rest credential into a plaintext secret store and may also log/expose codes through provider implementations. At minimum the codes should be hashed before being handed out, or the contract documented explicitly.

title: Recovery codes stored in user storage are never marked as used, so a single code can be replayed indefinitely
body: After a successful validation the authenticator obtains the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(), which may now return a credential built on the fly from the federated/user-storage provider (see BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials, which reconstructs the model from all codes each call). Because the authenticator only reads the model and never writes back the updated "used codes" state for the federated case (and cannot, since there is no update path), every code remains valid forever and allCodesUsed() never becomes true, so CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES is never re-triggered. Recovery codes are intended to be single-use; this allows unlimited replay of one captured code.

title: Unchecked Optional.get() can throw NoSuchElementException rendering the login form
body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) returns an Optional, and credentialModelOpt.get() is called without checking isPresent(). If neither the user storage nor local storage holds a recovery-codes credential (e.g. the provider returned nothing or deserialization failed, in which case BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials silently drops the credential), the login page rendering fails with an unhandled NoSuchElementException / 500 instead of a proper error.

title: getCredentials() NPEs for users not present in the in-memory map
body: getCredentials() calls getMyUser(user) and immediately dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes without a null check, while every other method in this class (isConfiguredFor, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream, isValid) explicitly guards against a null MyUser. For any UserModel whose username is not in the map (e.g. stale cache entry or local user mapped to this provider) this throws a NullPointerException during credential enumeration, breaking login/account pages rather than returning an empty stream.

title: Test user storage never consumes a used recovery code
body: isValid() for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE returns true whenever the submitted code matches any stored code, and never removes/marks it used. The provider therefore accepts the same code an unlimited number of times, which does not model single-use recovery codes and means the new test testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin cannot detect the missing code-consumption behaviour in the production path.

title: Recovery-codes credential cannot be disabled/removed from the test user storage
body: supportsCredentialType and isConfiguredFor were extended for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE, but disableCredentialType() and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() still handle only OTP. As a consequence an admin/account action to delete the recovery-codes credential stored in this provider is silently ignored (disableCredentialType logs "Unsupported"), and the test suite has no coverage for removing user-storage recovery codes.

title: getCredentials builds credential model from raw codes, double-hashing and discarding the stored id
body: RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues() hashes the values it is given, but here it is fed the plaintext codes stored in credentialData and the resulting model keeps no id (the generated recoveryCodes.getId() is not propagated). Code paths such as RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator, which call removeStoredCredentialById(model.getId()), therefore operate on a null id, and the hashes in the returned model are inconsistent with what isValid() compares against.

title: Federated recovery-code credential cannot track used codes, enabling code reuse
body: getCredential() now prefers the credential returned from the federated (user storage) credentials stream. Callers treat the result as a stateful RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean uses getNextRecoveryAuthnCode() to decide which code to ask for, and RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator calls removeStoredCredentialById() when all codes are used. For a federated credential there is no local row, so removeStoredCredentialById() is a no-op and the provider is never told that a code was consumed (e.g. BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials() always rebuilds the model from the raw list with no 'used' state). Consequence: the login form always requests code #0 and the same recovery code remains valid indefinitely — one-time codes become reusable, which defeats their security purpose.

title: Raw recovery codes are sent to user storage as plaintext JSON
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the full list of generated raw (unhashed) recovery codes into JSON and passes it as the UserCredentialModel value to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). Any user storage provider that supports the recovery-authn-codes type will receive and most likely persist the codes in clear text (as the test provider does). Local storage stores only salted hashes, so this is a significant weakening of the credential handling contract and should at least be documented/hashed before being handed off.

title: No feedback when neither user storage nor local creation succeeds / credential ID lost
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential returns void and swallows the outcome: if updateCredential() returns false, it unconditionally creates the credential locally, but it never reports whether the operation actually succeeded, and the caller (RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.processAction) calls reqActionContext.success() regardless. A failing provider (e.g. it accepted the type but discarded the value) would leave the user without usable recovery codes while the required action is marked complete.

title: getCredentials() dereferences possibly null MyUser
body: getMyUser(user) returns users.get(...) which can be null (other methods in this class explicitly null-check it, e.g. isConfiguredFor and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream). Accessing myUser.recoveryCodes immediately afterwards will throw NullPointerException for any user not present in the in-memory map (e.g. a stale cached federated user), breaking credential listing.

title: Optional.get() without presence check can throw NoSuchElementException
body: credentialModelOpt.get() is invoked unconditionally. If neither the federated nor the local store holds a recovery-codes credential (e.g. the credential was removed between authentication steps), this throws NoSuchElementException during form rendering, producing a 500 error instead of a graceful login failure. Handle the empty Optional explicitly.

title: Test does not verify code consumption or exhaustion behaviour
body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only logs in once with code #0. It does not assert that a used code is rejected on a subsequent login, nor that the prompted code number advances, which is exactly the behaviour that is broken for federated credentials. Adding a second login attempt with the same code would catch the reuse problem.

title: Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion can run before exceptions are recorded
body: The test spawns a reader thread that polls `groups(...)` and records exceptions into `caughtExceptions`, then sets `deletedAll` and immediately asserts the list is empty. Because the thread is never joined, an exception thrown by the in-flight request (exactly the NPE this PR fixes) can be added after the assertion has already run, making the test pass even when the bug is present. Join the thread (with a timeout) before asserting. Additionally, if the thread hangs, it is left running as a non-daemon thread after the test.

title: Created groups are not registered for cleanup
body: The 100 groups created in `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` are only removed by the explicit delete loop. If `fail(...)` triggers or a delete throws, the remaining groups leak into the shared `managedRealm`, which can break other tests in the class (e.g. ones asserting group counts or names). Register each created group with `managedRealm.cleanup()` as other tests in this file do.

title: getSubGroupsCount() may now return null, moving the NPE to callers
body: `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns `null` when the group no longer exists in the store instead of throwing an NPE. Callers such as `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` pass the value straight to `GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount(...)`, and other callers may unbox it to a primitive `long`, which would NPE again. The `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` contract does not document a nullable result. Returning `0L` (or delegating to the invalidation path via `getDelegateForUpdate()`) would be safer and keeps the API contract non-null.

title: Race in new concurrency test: reader thread is never joined
body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a reader thread but never joins it. The assertion on caughtExceptions runs immediately after deletedAll.set(true), so exceptions thrown by the last in-flight read (exactly the NPE window the fix targets) can be recorded after the assertion and silently ignored, making the test both flaky and able to pass even when the bug is present. The thread also leaks beyond the test and busy-loops calling the admin API without any sleep, consuming CPU. Join the thread (with a timeout) before asserting.

title: Remaining NPE paths via modelSupplier.get() not guarded
body: Only getSubGroupsCount() was hardened against a null delegate. getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults), getSubGroupsStream(firstResult, maxResults) and getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, firstResult, maxResults) (lines 256, 262, 268) still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) directly, so when the group is concurrently removed from the database the supplier returns null and the same NullPointerException reported in #40368 is thrown from those paths. They should handle a null model consistently (e.g. return Stream.empty() or throw a meaningful model exception).

title: getSubGroupsCount() may now return null
body: getSubGroupsCount() returns null when the backing group has been removed. GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() previously never returned null, and callers that unbox the Long (e.g. arithmetic or long assignment) will now throw NullPointerException instead of the previous NPE location; GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount will also produce a representation with a null subGroupCount. Consider returning 0L or documenting the nullability on the interface.

title: Concurrency test never joins reader thread, so assertion can race
body: The test starts a bare reader thread and then asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty immediately after setting `deletedAll`. There is no `join()` (nor a timeout) on the thread, so an exception thrown in the last iterations of the reader loop may be recorded after the assertion runs, making the test pass even when the regression is present. The thread is also never interrupted/stopped if the test fails early, leaking a thread that keeps hitting the admin API. Join the thread (with timeout) before asserting.

title: Created groups are not registered for cleanup
body: The 100 groups created in `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` are only removed by the explicit delete loop; if `fail()` or an exception occurs earlier (e.g. during creation or removal), the groups remain in the shared realm and can affect other tests in the class, which use the same injected realm. Register them via `managedRealm.cleanup()` as the other tests do.

title: getSubGroupsCount() can now return null, propagating null into representations
body: `getSubGroupsCount()` returns `null` when the group has been removed concurrently (model supplier yields null). Callers such as `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` do `representation.setSubGroupCount(group.getSubGroupsCount())` without a null check, so a null subGroupCount is serialized/returned to clients, and any caller unboxing the Long will still NPE. Consider returning 0L, or handling the removed-group case explicitly (e.g. skipping the group) instead of leaking null through the GroupModel contract.

title: has_global_access used as admin authorization gate
body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` treats any member with global/open-membership access as an "authorized administrator" and unlocks the OptimizedCursorPaginator's unchecked negative-offset path. `has_global_access` only means the member can see all teams in the org; it is not an admin/privilege flag. This grants ordinary members a non-standard pagination code path that deliberately bypasses offset bounds checks. The gate should be an explicit permission check (or the feature removed).

title: organization_context.member can be None -> AttributeError
body: For a superuser or staff user who is not a member of the organization, `organization_context.member` is None, so `organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises AttributeError and returns a 500. Because Python evaluates `or` left-to-right the superuser case short-circuits, but any non-member non-superuser request reaching this line (e.g. via org-level permission grants or token auth where member is None) crashes. Guard with `organization_context.member and ...`.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with the datetime sort key
body: The endpoint orders by `-datetime` and uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, whose `get_item_key` does `math.floor(getattr(item, 'datetime'))` and whose `value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value. `math.floor()` on a `datetime` raises TypeError, and the raw int cursor value cannot be compared against a datetime column in `build_queryset`. Any request with `?optimized_pagination=true` from an eligible user will 500 (or produce a bad SQL comparison). A DateTimePaginator-style key conversion is required.

title: Negative slice start on a QuerySet raises ValueError
body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, `start_offset` is negative and `queryset[start_offset:stop]` is evaluated.
