Django QuerySets explicitly reject negative indexing (`ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`), so a client-supplied negative cursor offset produces an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. The comment claiming "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is factually wrong.

title: Silently clamping offset hides invalid cursors and breaks drop-extra logic
body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` silently clamps a negative forward offset to 0 instead of surfacing an error, so a malformed/attacker-supplied cursor now returns page 1 data rather than being rejected. Worse, the subsequent check at line 192 still uses the unclamped `offset` (`len(results) == offset + limit + extra`), so when offset is clamped the extra-row trimming comparison is computed against a different window size than was fetched, producing wrong has-more/trimming behavior. For `is_prev` the negative offset is still passed through to the slice and will raise ValueError from Django.

title: Duplicate trimming logic uses unclamped offset
body: `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra:` in OptimizedCursorPaginator compares the result count against a window computed from the raw `cursor.offset`, while the slice actually used `start_offset` (clamped, or negative). When these differ the extra prev-row is not dropped (or is dropped incorrectly), yielding duplicated/missing rows across pages. This whole method is a copy-paste of BasePaginator.get_result and should delegate instead of duplicating the logic.

title: No tests for new OptimizedCursorPaginator or clamping behavior
body: A new public paginator class plus a behavioral change to BasePaginator.get_result offset handling are added with no accompanying tests. There is no coverage for negative offsets, the clamping branch, or the new endpoint query parameter, so the ValueError/TypeError crashes described above would not be caught by CI.

title: Negative slice start raises ValueError in Django QuerySet
body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices the queryset with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`). Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` (the comment claiming the ORM handles it is false). Any request with a negative cursor offset against this endpoint will produce an unhandled 500. The same applies in `BasePaginator.get_result` line 182 where negative offsets are still passed through when `cursor.is_prev` is true.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key cannot handle datetime keys
body: `get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to `getattr(item, self.key)`. The audit log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so the value is a `datetime`, and `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError`. Likewise `value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric cursor value, which is then compared against a datetime column in `build_queryset`, producing invalid SQL/incorrect filtering. Requests with `optimized_pagination=true` will fail or return wrong pages; a DateTime-aware key implementation (like `DateTimePaginator`) is required.

title: Offset clamping made inconsistent with later length check
body: `BasePaginator.get_result` now slices from `start_offset = max(0, offset)` but the subsequent prev-page trimming still compares `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` using the unclamped `offset`. When `offset` differs from `start_offset` (negative offsets) the trim condition can never match, so the extra fetched row is returned to the client, producing an over-sized page and wrong next/prev cursors. The clamping logic should be applied consistently, or negative offsets rejected as before.

title: Client-controlled query param selects paginator that bypasses offset bounds
body: `optimized_pagination=true` is a user-supplied query parameter that switches to `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`, which explicitly permits offsets outside normal pagination bounds (negative OFFSET/cursor values). The in-code justification that "permissions are checked at the queryset level" is only true for the organization filter; arbitrary offsets are not a permission boundary and expose unvalidated, error-prone query paths to any superuser or member with global access. Either remove the parameter or validate offsets server-side.

title: organization_context.member may be None, causing AttributeError
body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated whenever `request.user.is_superuser` is false. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is `None` for requests that are not made by an organization member (e.g. token/sentry-app auth or a staff user outside the org), so this will raise `AttributeError` and return a 500 on an endpoint that previously worked. Guard with `organization_context.member and ...`.

title: Misleading comment about negative offsets in Cursor
body: The added comment states that negative offsets are allowed as a "performance optimization" enabling reverse pagination, but `Cursor` performs no validation at all and downstream paginators cannot actually use negative offsets (Django queryset slicing rejects them). The comment misdocuments behaviour and encourages callers to construct invalid cursors.

title: New paginator and endpoint branch have no tests
body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and the new `optimized_pagination` branch of the audit log endpoint are added without any unit or API tests. The datetime key bug and negative-offset ValueError would both have been caught by a basic test exercising the new branch.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator key handling is incompatible with datetime ordering used by the audit log endpoint
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does `math.floor(getattr(item, self.key))` and value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value. The audit log endpoint uses it with order_by="-datetime", where the key value is a datetime. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError, and feeding an integer cursor value into the `extra(where="datetime <= %s")` clause compares a timestamp column to an integer, producing a DB error. Any request with ?optimized_pagination=true will 500 as soon as results/cursors are produced. DateTimePaginator-style conversion (multiplier + fromtimestamp) is required.

title: Negative queryset slicing raises in Django; comment claiming ORM handles it is false
body: When enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, the code performs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySets explicitly do not support negative indexing/slicing and raise `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`, so a client-supplied negative cursor offset yields an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 BadPaginationError. The inline comment asserting the ORM handles negative slicing automatically is incorrect.

title: Client-controlled query param gates a different paginator for any org member with global access
body: `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` combined with `has_global_access` lets any ordinary org owner/manager (not just superusers) opt into the unvalidated OptimizedCursorPaginator path, which intentionally skips offset bounds checking ("access to data beyond normal pagination bounds"). Gating behaviour on an undocumented, client-supplied flag with a weak authorization check is an untested access-control surface; it should either be removed or guarded by a proper permission/feature flag with validated offsets.

title: organization_context.member can be None, causing AttributeError
body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated whenever `request.user.is_superuser` is False. For requests where the actor is not a member of the organization (e.g. token/integration auth, or staff access without membership), RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is None, so this raises AttributeError and returns a 500. Needs a None check before accessing has_global_access.

title: BasePaginator now silently clamps negative offsets and leaves inconsistent offset in later arithmetic
body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` changes the shared BasePaginator behaviour for all endpoints: a negative forward offset is now silently clamped to 0 (previously it propagated, surfacing as an error) which can return a duplicate first page instead of an error, while for is_prev cursors the negative offset is still passed into the slice and will raise Django's negative-indexing ValueError. Additionally, the subsequent check `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` still uses the unclamped `offset`, so the extra-row trimming is wrong whenever clamping occurred.

title: New paginator and endpoint branch have no tests
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator and the new conditional branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint add substantial new behaviour (negative offsets, advanced-feature gating, duplicated cursor logic) with no accompanying unit or API tests. Given the code paths crash with the datetime key and negative slicing, tests would have caught these before merge.

title: Misleading comment about negative offsets in Cursor
body: The added comment states that Cursor "allows negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios", but `self.offset = int(offset)` performs no validation and negative offsets are not actually supported downstream (Django raises on negative slicing). The comment documents a non-existent feature and will mislead future maintainers into assuming negative offsets are safe.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator allows negative offsets, enabling unbounded/invalid queryset slicing
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError/AssertionError` ("Negative indexing is not supported"), so any user-supplied cursor with a negative offset on the audit-log endpoint causes a 500. The inline comments claiming "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" and "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level" are factually wrong. There is also no validation rejecting negative offsets as other paginators do (`BadPaginationError("Pagination offset cannot be negative")`).

title: Possible AttributeError on organization_context.member and anonymous users
body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally; `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is `None` for users who are not members of the organization (e.g. a superuser accessing another org), which raises `AttributeError` and returns a 500 for every GET request in that case. Also `request.user.is_superuser` is accessed before confirming the user is authenticated. The check should be short-circuited/guarded (e.g. `getattr(organization_context.member, 'has_global_access', False)`).

title: Undocumented query flag switches paginator and breaks cursor semantics for audit logs
body: `optimized_pagination=true` swaps `DateTimePaginator` for `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, whose `get_item_key`/`value_from_cursor` treat the ordering key as a numeric value, not a datetime. Ordering is by `-datetime`, so `int(math.floor(value))` on a `datetime` raises `TypeError`, and cursors issued by one paginator are not interpretable by the other. This path appears untested and will 500 as soon as it is exercised.

title: BasePaginator offset clamping changes pagination behavior inconsistently
body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` clamps forward offsets to 0 but leaves prev-cursor offsets unclamped, so a negative offset on a prev cursor still reaches the queryset slice and crashes. Additionally the later check `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` still uses the unclamped `offset`, so when clamping occurred the extra-row trimming is computed against the wrong expected length and an extra row may be returned on a page.

title: Span eviction limit hardcoded to 1000 and silently drops spans, ignoring max_segment_spans config
body: The eviction threshold `1000` is hardcoded in Lua while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` (default 1001) is now unused in Python, so the configured limit has no effect and the two can diverge. More importantly `zpopmin` removes the spans with the lowest `end_timestamp_precise`, silently discarding span data from oversized segments without any metric/log (the previous code incremented `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` and skipped the segment). Oversized segments will now be emitted partially, and the dropped span may be the root/segment span, producing a segment with the wrong `is_segment` marking.

title: span_count can be stale/incorrect when both unions execute
body: `span_count` is assigned from the first `zunionstore` and then possibly overwritten by the second, which is fine, but if only the first union runs and the parent merge is skipped, `span_count` reflects the cardinality *before* the current span's own zadd in some orderings; and if neither union runs `zcard` is queried. The net effect is that when a union happened, the count used for the `> 1000` eviction check can be lower than the actual set size (the new span payload is added by a separate pipeline step), so segments can exceed the intended cap or evict the wrong amount. Prefer always calling `zcard set_key` right before the eviction check.

title: Redirect-chain limit silently reduced from 10000 to 1000, removing explanatory comment
body: The loop bound was lowered from 10000 to 1000 and the comment documenting the consequence ("segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly") was deleted. Traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 will now fail to be joined into a single segment, producing split segments, and the behavioral trade-off is no longer documented anywhere.

title: max_segment_spans is now dead config and missing from __reduce__
body: The span-count guard in `_load_segment_data` was removed, so `max_segment_spans` is no longer used anywhere; callers configuring it get no effect. Relatedly `__reduce__` still only passes `assigned_shards`, the two timeouts and `redis_ttl`, so `segment_page_size`, `max_segment_bytes` and `max_segment_spans` are reset to defaults when the buffer is pickled for multiprocessing — any non-default tuning is silently lost in the multiprocess consumer path.

title: No test for the new in-insert eviction behavior
body: The PR's headline change (zset-based buffer with eviction of the oldest spans once a segment exceeds 1000 spans) has no test. Tests were only mechanically updated with `end_timestamp_precise`. A test asserting that a segment with >1000 spans keeps the newest 1000 (and what happens to the root span) is needed, since this path silently drops customer data if it misbehaves.

title: Client-controlled query param enables negative-offset pagination path
body: `optimized_pagination=true` plus `enable_advanced_features=True` lets a request opt into `OptimizedCursorPaginator`'s branch that passes an unvalidated, possibly negative `cursor.offset` directly into a queryset slice. Cursor offsets come from the user-supplied `cursor` query param (`Cursor.from_string` accepts negative integers and no validation was added). This is an unaudited, user-reachable code path that bypasses the offset sanity checks every other paginator enforces (`BadPaginationError('Pagination offset cannot be negative')`), and the whole feature is unrelated to the stated purpose of this PR (spans buffer). It should be removed or gated behind a real permission check plus validation.

title: `organization_context.member` may be None -> AttributeError 500
body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally. For a superuser or staff user who is not a member of the organization, `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is `None`, so this raises `AttributeError` and returns a 500 for every GET of the audit log endpoint, not just when `optimized_pagination` is passed (Python evaluates the right operand of `or` whenever `is_superuser` is False, and `is_superuser` is False for non-superuser members too — in that case `member` is set, but non-member staff/non-member superuser-less tokens will crash). Reorder/short-circuit with `organization_context.member and ...` and only compute it when needed.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key cannot handle datetime keys used by the audit log endpoint
body: `get_item_key` does `math.floor(getattr(item, self.key))`, which works only for numeric keys. The audit log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by='-datetime'`, where the attribute is a `datetime`; `math.floor()` on a datetime raises `TypeError`. Any request hitting the optimized branch will 500. The paginator either needs DateTimePaginator-style key conversion or must not be used for datetime ordering.

title: Negative queryset slice raises, contrary to the comment
body: The comment claims 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', but Django QuerySets explicitly reject negative indices/slices (`ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`). So with `enable_advanced_features` and a negative cursor offset the request fails with an unhandled exception (500) instead of a 400. Additionally `stop` can become negative, producing a nonsensical slice.

title: BasePaginator silently clamps negative offsets for next-page, still passes them through for prev
body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` changes long-standing behavior: a negative offset is now silently clamped on forward pages (masking bad cursors rather than failing), while negative offsets are still forwarded unchanged when `cursor.is_prev`, where they will hit Django's negative-slice error. Also the later `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check still uses the raw `offset`, so it no longer matches the actual slice when clamping occurred, which can drop or keep the wrong extra row on prev pages.

title: Span eviction limit hardcoded to 1000 and not aligned with max_segment_spans
body: The new `zpopmin` eviction uses the literal 1000, while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` defaults to 1001 and is now unused (the span-count guard was removed from `_load_segment_data`). The cap is no longer configurable and silently drops spans with the lowest `end_timestamp_precise` with no metric/log, so oversized segments lose data invisibly. Pass the limit in as an ARGV from `max_segment_spans` and emit a metric when spans are evicted.

title: Redirect-chain depth limit lowered from 10000 to 1000 without justification
body: The loop bound was reduced from 10000 to 1000 and the explanatory comment about segment trees deeper than the limit not being joined correctly was deleted. Traces with redirect chains between 1000 and 10000 that previously merged correctly will now be split into separate segments. If the reduction is intentional (to bound script runtime), keep a comment stating the consequence; otherwise restore the previous bound.

title: max_segment_spans is now dead configuration
body: `_load_segment_data` no longer checks `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`, and the `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` metric is gone, yet `max_segment_spans` remains a constructor parameter. Operators setting it get no effect; the enforcement now lives as a hardcoded 1000 in Lua. Either wire the attribute through to the script or remove the parameter.

title: Module docstring still describes Redis sets, not sorted sets
body: The storage was changed from SET (`sadd`/`sscan`/`sunionstore`) to ZSET (`zadd`/`zscan`/`zunionstore`) with score = `end_timestamp_precise`, but the docstring still says 'Add the ingested span's payload to the set under set_key' and 'span-buf:s:* -- the actual set keys'. It also doesn't mention the new per-segment span eviction, which is the key behavioral change of this PR.

title: No test covers the new span eviction path
body: The core change of this PR is evicting spans once a segment exceeds the size cap (`zpopmin` in add-buffer.lua), plus the switch to score-ordered storage. No test inserts more than the cap to assert that the oldest-by-`end_timestamp_precise` spans are dropped and the newest retained, nor that `redirect_depth`/`span_count` accounting stays correct when both the span_key and parent_key union branches run. Add a test that exceeds the limit.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator allows negative offsets, exposing data outside pagination bounds / 500s
body: The `enable_advanced_features` branch passes `cursor.offset` (negative) directly into a Django queryset slice: `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` for negative slice bounds, so any user-supplied cursor with a negative offset yields an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. The accompanying comments ("underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically", "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level") are factually wrong; there is no permission check in this code path. Previously negative offsets were effectively bounded; this change removes that safety. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`.

title: Unvetted `optimized_pagination` query flag switches audit logs to an unsafe paginator
body: A client-controlled query parameter (`optimized_pagination=true`) selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`, enabling the negative-offset code path. Any org member with `has_global_access` (not just admins, contrary to the comment) can trigger it. Additionally `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` does `int(math.floor(getattr(item, 'datetime')))` on a datetime field, which raises TypeError — so the optimized branch is broken for the `-datetime` ordering used here and will 500. This feature flag should not be user-selectable and the paginator must handle datetime keys.

title: Potential AttributeError on `organization_context.member`
body: `organization_context.member` can be `None` (e.g. for superusers or non-member access via RpcUserOrganizationContext), so `organization_context.member.has_global_access` will raise AttributeError and 500 the endpoint. Short-circuiting is unreliable because `request.user.is_superuser` may be False for non-member staff/token access.

title: BasePaginator offset clamping changes prev-page semantics inconsistently
body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` clamps only for next-page cursors, while `is_prev` cursors still pass a possibly negative offset into the queryset slice (AssertionError in Django). Also, later code still compares `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` using the unclamped `offset`, so when clamping occurs the extra-row trim check no longer matches and an extra row can leak into the page. Either clamp uniformly and use the clamped value in the comparison, or raise on negative offsets.

title: Hardcoded 1000-span cap silently drops spans and ignores max_segment_spans config
body: Eviction uses a literal `1000` instead of the configurable `max_segment_spans` (1001 in SpansBuffer), and `zpopmin` silently discards the oldest spans with no metric or log. The previous behavior (dropping the whole oversized segment with `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` + error log) was observable; now data loss is invisible. Pass the limit in as an ARGV and emit a metric/return the number evicted.

title: span_count may be stale, causing over- or under-eviction
body: `span_count` is set from the result of `zunionstore` calls, but when both unions run the second overwrites the first, and in either case the count reflects the set state before the Python-side `zadd` of new payloads in this batch happens relative to other pipeline commands. Only when `span_count == 0` is `zcard` consulted. If a union ran, the count can be lower than the actual cardinality, so a segment can exceed the cap, or (if a union inflated the count) spans can be evicted unnecessarily. Always read `zcard set_key` right before the cap check.

title: Redirect-chain loop limit reduced 10000 -> 1000 without justification, and explanatory comment removed
body: The loop bound was lowered from 10000 to 1000 and the comment warning that chains deeper than the bound may not be joined correctly was deleted. Segment trees deeper than 1000 redirects will now silently fail to merge, producing split segments. This is unrelated to the eviction change; if intentional it needs a metric/alert and a comment, otherwise restore 10000.

title: max_segment_spans is now dead config while enforcement moved to a Lua literal
body: `self.max_segment_spans` is still a constructor parameter but no longer used anywhere after the span-count check was removed from `_load_segment_data`; the limit is hardcoded as 1000 in add-buffer.lua. Operators tuning `max_segment_spans` will have no effect, and the two values (1001 vs 1000) disagree. Wire the parameter through to the script or remove it.

title: zadd keyed on payload: duplicate payloads collapse and score is overwritten
body: Switching from `sadd` to `zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise})` makes the payload the sorted-set member. Two spans with byte-identical payloads still collapse to one entry (same as the set), but now re-ingesting a span also rewrites its score, which changes its eviction priority. More importantly, eviction by `zpopmin` on `end_timestamp_precise` drops the *earliest-ending* spans — typically the root/parent spans of a segment — rather than the least useful ones, which can destroy segment structure. Worth documenting/justifying, and the module docstring (lines 39-44, 58) still describes these keys as "sets" with `sadd` semantics.

title: __reduce__ omits new/existing fields, so pickled buffers lose configuration
body: `__reduce__` only passes `assigned_shards`, the two timeouts and `redis_ttl`, dropping `segment_page_size`, `max_segment_bytes` and `max_segment_spans`. In multiprocessing mode the buffer is pickled to subprocesses, so any non-default values for those limits are silently reset to defaults in workers.

title: No test for the new eviction-during-insert behavior
body: The PR's stated purpose is eviction during insert, but tests only add the now-required `end_timestamp_precise` field. There is no test that inserts more than the cap into one segment and asserts which spans are retained/evicted, nor a test that the removed `max_segment_spans` read-path behavior is covered by the new Lua cap. Regressions in the eviction arithmetic (stale `span_count`, off-by-one in `span_count - 1000`) would go undetected.

title: New OptimizedCursorPaginator has no tests
body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is a new public paginator wired into a production endpoint but has no unit tests covering next/prev cursors, negative offsets, or the datetime key path. Given it duplicates ~60 lines of `BasePaginator.get_result` with subtle differences, untested divergence is likely.

title: Upsampling eligibility uses outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` as a parameter but passes the outer-scope `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. In the dashboard-widget split path, `_get_event_stats` is intentionally called with a different dataset (e.g. `discover` for the errors-only query, or `split_dataset`), so the eligibility decision will be computed for the wrong dataset. Consequence: count() can be rewritten to `upsampled_count()` for a transactions-like query (where `sample_weight` is not meaningful/absent), or conversely skipped for a genuine errors query, producing wrong numbers or Snuba errors.

title: Caching option-based allowlist in shared cache creates stale/incorrect results and cross-test pollution
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the allowlist eligibility in the global cache for 60s, keyed by org id and `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Problems: (1) the option `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` change takes up to 60s to take effect, and the only invalidation helper (`invalidate_upsampling_cache`) is never called anywhere, so there is no real invalidation path; (2) `hash()` of a tuple is not a stable or collision-free key — different project sets can collide, giving a wrong eligibility answer for an unrelated project list; (3) the docstring of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` claims the config is read fresh every time, which the cache contradicts. Also the option lookup is already cheap/cached in Sentry, so the cache adds risk for no real gain. This also makes the new endpoint tests order-dependent/flaky, since tests mocking different allowlists for the same org+project set share the cache entry.

title: Cached value type not validated; truthy-return instead of bool
body: `cached_result` is returned as `cached_result and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(...)`, which returns the cached object (not a bool) when it is falsy — e.g. returns `False`/`0` from the cache but with declared return type `bool`. More importantly the function is typed `-> bool` while potentially returning a non-bool cache payload. Callers compare it truthily today, but any `is True` check or typed consumer would break.

title: upsampled_count relies on `sample_weight` column existing in discover/errors tables
body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction aggregates `sum(sample_weight)` with no guard. If the underlying Snuba table (discover/errors) does not have a `sample_weight` column, or it is NULL for non-sampled events, queries will either fail with a Snuba error or return 0/NULL counts for allowlisted projects. The code comment asserts the schema guarantees this, but nothing in this PR enforces it (the only place setting sampling data is the test factory, which writes `sample_rate`, not `sample_weight`). Consider a fallback such as `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))` and declaring `default_result_type="integer"` to match the `toInt64` result.

title: Error-focused query detection by substring is unreliable
body: `_is_error_focused_query` does a raw substring check for `event.type:error` on the lowercased query string. This matches negated filters like `!event.type:error` and free-text/message content containing that string, and misses equivalent forms (`event.type:[error, default]`, `event.type: error`). For the discover dataset that means count() can be silently rewritten to `upsampled_count()` on queries that explicitly exclude errors, returning inflated counts. Use the parsed search query/filters instead of a substring match.

title: Unused `organization` parameter and dead invalidation helper
body: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` takes `organization` but never uses it, and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called from anywhere in the codebase, so the cache added in this PR has no invalidation path. Either wire the invalidation into the option-change path or drop both.

title: Blanket `except Exception: pass` silently drops invalid sample rates in test factory
body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps both the context read and the float conversion in bare `except Exception: pass`. A malformed `client_sample_rate` (e.g. a string, or contexts not being a dict) will silently leave `sample_rate` unset, making upsampling tests pass with regular counts and masking real bugs. At minimum narrow the exceptions (`AttributeError`/`TypeError`/`ValueError`) and/or assert in tests.

title: Accidental git submodule/gitlink `sentry-repo` committed
body: The PR adds a gitlink entry `sentry-repo` pointing at `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This is clearly an accidental nested clone of the repository itself; it will break `git submodule` operations and clones for other developers/CI. Remove it before merge.

title: New endpoint tests mock `options` module-wide but do not clear the upsampling cache
body: These tests patch `sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options`, but `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches eligibility in the shared cache for 60s under a key derived from org id + project ids. Because all tests in the class use the same org and project pair, whichever test runs first seeds the cache and the subsequent tests (partial allowlist, no allowlist) can read the stale eligibility value, making the assertions order-dependent and flaky. The tests need to flush the cache in `setUp`, or the caching should be removed.

title: Duplicated upsampling transform logic invites divergence
body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` is invoked in three separate branches (top_events, use_rpc, default) guarded by the same `upsampling_enabled` flag, each re-deriving `final_columns` from `query_columns`. The `should_upsample`/`upsampling_enabled` aliasing adds no value. Computing `final_columns` once right after the eligibility check would remove the risk of a future branch forgetting the transform.

title: Cache key uses Python's randomized hash(), making the cache unstable and collision-prone
body: The cache key is built with `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Python's `hash()` for tuples of ints is deterministic per-process but string/salted hashing and, more importantly, inter-process agreement is not guaranteed across versions/configurations; worse, collisions on the truncated hash mean two different project sets can share one cache entry and get the wrong upsampling decision. The invalidation helper (`invalidate_upsampling_cache`) computes the key the same way, so a key produced in one worker can be unreachable from another. Use a stable, explicit representation (e.g. sorted ids joined by ",", or a md5/sha of it).

title: 60s caching of allowlist eligibility silently serves stale upsampling decisions
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the allowlist eligibility for 60 seconds keyed by org+project set. Because the result drives whether `count()` is replaced by `sum(sample_weight)`, a stale cache entry means the same query returns counts off by the sample-rate factor (e.g. 10x) for up to a minute after an allowlist change, and users will see charts flip between upsampled and raw values. There is no invalidation hook wired to the option change (the provided `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere in this PR). The option lookup is already an in-memory/cached option read, so the added cache gives little benefit for a real correctness risk; consider dropping it or wiring invalidation to the option update signal.

title: Naive substring match treats negated error queries as error-focused
body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the lowercased query string contains `event.type:error`. Queries like `!event.type:error`, `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, or a message search containing that literal text will be classified as error-only, so `count()` is rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` over rows that include transactions (where `sample_weight` is absent/0), producing wrong counts. Parse the query (or require the dataset to be `errors`) rather than substring matching.

title: Allowlist membership test is O(n*m) on a list
body: `allowlist` comes from `options.get(...)` as a list and is then used with `project_id in allowlist` for every project. For large allowlists and multi-project queries this is quadratic on a hot API path. Convert to a `set` once before the `all(...)` check.

title: Unused `organization` parameter in _are_all_projects_error_upsampled
body: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled(project_ids, organization)` never uses `organization`; the allowlist is purely project-id based. The parameter misleads callers into thinking the check is org-scoped (it isn't, so project ids from other orgs would pass). Either remove it or validate project ownership.

title: Accidental git submodule 'sentry-repo' committed
body: A gitlink entry `sentry-repo` pointing at commit a5d2909 was added, with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This will break `git submodule` operations and clones/CI for anyone checking out the branch. It is unrelated to the feature and should be removed.

title: Test factory derives sample_rate from error_sampling context, diverging from production ingestion
body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` injects `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` from `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` only inside the test factory. If production relay/event-manager does not do the same, the new snuba tests (asserting count == 10 for a 0.1 sample rate) will pass while the real pipeline never populates `sample_weight`, giving false confidence. The derivation belongs in the real normalization path, or the tests should assert against data produced the production way.

title: Bare `except Exception: pass` hides malformed sample-rate data
body: Both try/except blocks swallow all exceptions silently. A non-numeric or malformed `client_sample_rate` will silently leave `sample_rate` unset, so an upsampling test would fail with a confusing count mismatch rather than the real cause. Narrow to `(TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError)` and/or avoid the try entirely by using `.get()` chains on known dict types.

title: New `upsampled_count` function is publicly exposed in discover
body: `SnQLFunction("upsampled_count", ...)` is registered without `private=True`, unlike the neighbouring internal functions. That means any API consumer can request `upsampled_count()` on any project, bypassing the allowlist gating in `error_upsampling.py` and getting `sum(sample_weight)` values for non-upsampled projects (where sample_weight may be null/0, producing misleading numbers). Mark it private if it is only meant to be injected by the server-side transform.

title: upsampled_count declares default_result_type "number" while returning Int64
body: The aggregate is wrapped in `toInt64` but `default_result_type` is `"number"` rather than `"integer"` as used by the other count functions. The response meta will advertise a float-ish type for an integer count, which can affect client formatting/axis rendering.

title: No test covers the new caching path; cached values can leak between tests
body: The unit tests only exercise the private helpers (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) and never call `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, so the newly added cache read/write and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` are untested. The endpoint tests in test_organization_events_stats.py mock `options` but do not clear the cache between tests; since the cache key only depends on org id + project ids, an entry written by `test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects` can make a later test with a different mocked allowlist return the stale eligibility, producing order-dependent flakes.

title: Upsampling eligibility recomputed on every _get_event_stats invocation
body: `_get_event_stats` is called up to four times per request by the dashboard-split logic, and each call re-runs `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (option read + cache get/set). The comment claims the result is cached for consistency, but nothing is memoized per-request. Compute it once outside the closure (it depends only on snuba_params/organization/dataset/request) to avoid repeated work and guarantee a consistent decision across the split queries.

title: Column transform duplicated in three branches instead of once
body: `if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` is repeated in the top-events, rpc, and default branches. Besides the duplication, the upsampling decision is computed from the outer `dataset` while the query may actually run against `split_dataset`/`discover` passed in as `scoped_dataset` (see get_event_stats_factory), so an errors-dataset decision can be applied to a discover query and vice versa. Pass `scoped_dataset` to the eligibility check and transform once.

title: Caching allowlist eligibility makes upsampling decisions stale and never invalidated
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the allowlist eligibility result in the shared cache for 60s keyed by org + project set. The `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option lookup it is 'optimizing' is already an in-process/option-store cached read, so the added cache buys little while introducing up to 60s of wrong aggregations (count() silently becoming sum(sample_weight) or vice versa) after the allowlist changes. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called anywhere, so there is no invalidation path. Recommend dropping the cache layer entirely.

title: Shared cache makes the new endpoint tests order-dependent/flaky
body: Because eligibility is stored in the process-wide cache, the new tests in tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py that patch `options` (allowlisted / partial / empty) can read a value cached by a previously run test for the same org+project key, producing wrong counts and intermittent failures. Tests would need explicit cache clearing, or the cache should be removed.

title: Eligibility check uses the outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` but passes the enclosing `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. In the dashboard-widget split path the function is deliberately called with `discover` or other split datasets; the decision will therefore be computed for the originally requested dataset, so an errors-only split query can skip upsampling (or a transactions-like split query can wrongly upsample). Pass `scoped_dataset`.

title: Substring match on 'event.type:error' matches negated filters
body: `_is_error_focused_query` does `"event.type:error" in query`, which is also true for `!event.type:error` (exclude errors) and for `event.type:error_something`. A discover query that explicitly excludes errors would then be transformed to sum(sample_weight), returning inflated/incorrect counts for non-error rows. Parse the query or at least require the term not be negated.

title: Error-focus detection ignores the query actually executed
body: `_is_error_focused_query` reads `request.GET['query']`, but the discover-split code path in organization_events_stats mutates the query (e.g. `({query}) AND !event.type:transaction` / `AND event.type:transaction`). The upsampling decision is therefore made from the original user query and can disagree with the query that is run. The effective query string should be passed into the helper.

title: upsampled_count declares result type 'number' but returns an integer and has no null handling
body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction wraps `sum(sample_weight)` in `toInt64` yet declares `default_result_type="number"`, inconsistent with the sibling count aggregations that use "integer"; clients/meta will report a float type for an integer column. Additionally, events without `sample_weight` (non-upsampled events that may still be in an allowlisted project, or historical data) sum as 0/NULL, silently under-counting; a `sum(coalesce(sample_weight, 1))`-style fallback would be safer than relying on the schema assumption stated in the comment.

title: Stray git submodule/gitlink `sentry-repo` committed
body: The PR adds a gitlink entry `sentry-repo` pointing at commit a5d2909 with no corresponding .gitmodules entry. This leaves the repository with a broken/uninitializable submodule and is clearly accidental; it should be removed before merge.

title: Broad silent excepts hide malformed error_sampling context in test factory
body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps both the context lookup and the float conversion in bare `except Exception: pass`. A test that supplies an invalid `client_sample_rate` will silently produce an event without `sample_rate`, making upsampling tests pass/fail for non-obvious reasons. Validate explicitly (e.g. check types / numeric range) and let unexpected input fail loudly.

title: No test coverage for errors dataset or top-events upsampling paths
body: The new endpoint tests only exercise the default/discover timeseries path. The code adds upsampling transforms in three places (top_events_timeseries, run_timeseries_query/RPC, timeseries_query); none of the top-events or `dataset=errors` paths, nor the dashboard-widget split path, are covered, so regressions in the alias `upsampled_count() as count` handling for top events would go undetected.

title: Flagged TableWidgetVisualization branch renders a hard-coded empty table
body: When the organization has the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature, the table branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` instead of passing the actual `result`/`fields`/`result.meta`. Any org with the flag enabled will see completely blank table widgets (no headers, no rows) rather than their data. The real query results must be mapped into `TabularData`/`TabularColumn` before this can be enabled.

title: Error/breadcrumb timestamps compared in different units
body: In `gen_request_data`, error timestamps come from nodestore event data (`data.get("timestamp")`, seconds since epoch) while rrweb replay events use millisecond epoch timestamps. The merge loop compares `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)` directly, so every error will always compare as earlier than every replay event and all error log lines will be emitted before any breadcrumb, destroying the chronological interleaving the function is meant to produce. One side needs unit normalization.

title: fetch_error_details pairs error ids with node values by position
body: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict whose value ordering matches the order of `error_ids`. That is an implementation detail of the backend (and of how it builds its result dict); if the ordering differs, each `ErrorEvent.id` will be attached to a different event's title/message/timestamp, producing silently wrong summaries. Index by node id instead: build `node_id -> error_id` and look up `events[node_id]`.

title: get_environment_info fetches a recommended event per issue
body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` and then `get_environment()` for each of the up-to-5 issues while building a PR comment. Each call is an additional snuba/nodestore + DB round trip inside a task that previously only used fields already loaded on the Group. This noticeably increases latency/cost for every merged-PR comment; consider batching or caching the environment lookup.

title: One invalid report rejects an entire browser report batch
body: Browsers send batches of reports to the Reporting API endpoint. The new loop returns 422 as soon as any single report fails validation, discarding the valid reports in the same request. Since the browser will retry the whole batch, one malformed/unknown report type permanently blocks collection of the others. Prefer validating per report and skipping (with a metric/log) the invalid ones while returning 200.

title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness
body: `validate_timestamp` checks `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `validate_age` checks `self.initial_data.get("timestamp")` for truthiness. A report with `age: 0` (very common — a report generated just now) plus a `timestamp` will not be flagged, and `timestamp: 0` likewise. Use `is not None` / `in self.initial_data`. Also, neither field is required, so a report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` passes validation entirely.

title: Analytics recorded before feature gate and schema validation
body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `features.has(...)` check and before request validation, so the event is emitted even for orgs without the feature (404 responses) and for malformed requests. This inflates the metric and makes it unusable for measuring real assembles. Move the call after the feature check.

title: useTraceItemAttributeKeys can now return undefined attributes
body: Previously `attributes` was always a `TagCollection` (built with `useMemo` from `result.data ?? []`). It is now `isFetching ? previous : data`, where both `previous` and `data` can be `undefined` (first load, or when `enabled` is false / query errors). Callers doing `Object.keys(attributes)` or spreading it will throw at runtime. Default to `{}` or update the return type and all consumers.

title: dcg_to_slow_conditions now keyed only by dcg_ids, risking KeyError
body: `get_condition_query_groups` previously computed slow conditions from `event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys()`, and `get_groups_to_fire` from `event_data.dcg_ids`. Both now receive a single map built from `event_data.dcg_ids`, and both still index it with `dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id]`. If `dcg_to_groups` contains any group id not present in `dcg_ids` (or `get_slow_conditions_for_groups` omits ids with no slow conditions rather than returning a defaultdict), this raises KeyError and the whole delayed-workflow batch fails. Use `.get(dcg.id, [])` or assert the key sets are identical.

title: Comment points at a migration that does not exist in this change
body: Both 0917 and 0920 now say "See 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py for the correct migration", but no 0921 migration is added in this PR. Readers (and anyone auditing why the data migration was neutered) will look for a file that isn't there; either land the replacement migration in the same change or reword the comment.

title: enabled guard `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is always true
body: `normalizeDateTimeParams` returns an object, so `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is unconditionally `true` and contributes nothing to the `enabled` condition. If the intent was to wait until page filters are ready, check `usePageFilters().isReady` or a specific field instead; as written the query may fire with default/unready filters.

title: Error IDs may be paired with the wrong nodestore payload
body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. The returned mapping is keyed by node id, and nothing guarantees its iteration order matches the input list (backends may batch/dedupe, and missing entries are filtered out *after* the zip pairing, so one missing/reordered node shifts every subsequent pair). The result is `ErrorEvent.id` values attached to a different event's title/message/timestamp, producing incorrect summaries. Iterate `node_ids` explicitly and look up `events[node_id]` keyed by its corresponding error id.

title: New table visualization path renders a permanently empty table
body: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature is enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and hard-coded empty `tableData` (`data: []`, `meta.fields: {}`), completely ignoring the `result`/`fields`/`result.meta` that `StyledSimpleTableChart` receives in the non-flagged branch. Any org with the flag on will see blank table widgets instead of their data. The real result/meta must be mapped into `TabularData`.

title: get_environment_info fetches a recommended event per issue
body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` and then `get_environment()` for each of the top issues while building a PR comment. This performs a Snuba/nodestore lookup plus an environment query per issue inside a loop in the comment workflow, adding several round trips to every merged-PR comment task and silently swallowing all failures. Consider resolving environments in bulk or reusing data already fetched for the top-issues query.

title: Shared slow-condition map is keyed only by dcg_ids, risking KeyError
body: `dcg_to_slow_conditions` is now computed once from `event_data.dcg_ids` and passed to both `get_condition_query_groups` and `get_groups_to_fire`. Previously `get_condition_query_groups` built its map from `event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys()`. If those two sets ever differ (a DCG present in `dcg_to_groups` but not in `dcg_ids`), `dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id]` raises KeyError and the whole delayed-workflow batch fails. Use a `defaultdict(list)`/`.get(dcg.id, [])` or compute the map from the union of both id sources.

title: Reports with neither `age` nor `timestamp` are accepted
body: Both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False`, and DRF only runs `validate_age`/`validate_timestamp` when the field is present. A report containing neither field therefore validates successfully, even though the spec requires exactly one. Add an object-level `validate()` that rejects the both-absent case so the metric isn't recorded for unusable payloads.

title: Analytics recorded before feature/permission gate
body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble")` check, so every rejected (404) request is counted as an assemble event. This inflates the metric with requests that never assemble anything; move the record call after the feature check.

title: TabularColumn.name typed as the field-key union prevents custom display names
body: `TabularColumn<TFields>` declares `name: TFields`, the same union as `key`. Since a documented purpose of the prop is "custom display names for columns" (see tableWidgetVisualization docs/stories), arbitrary labels like `'Count of Span Duration'` will not type-check against a constrained `TFields`. `name` should be `string`.

title: fetch_error_details mis-associates error ids with event data
body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by node id, and entries for missing events may be `None`. Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` relies on the dict preserving the exact order of `node_ids` and on every id being present; the `if data is not None` filter is applied *after* zipping, so as soon as one event is missing (or the backend returns keys in a different order) every subsequent report gets the wrong `id` attached to the wrong title/message/timestamp. Iterate over `node_ids` paired with `error_ids` and look up `events.get(node_id)` instead.

title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check is defeated by falsy values and both-absent case
body: `validate_timestamp` uses `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and `validate_age` uses `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. A report with `age: 0` (a legitimate value meaning "just now") plus a `timestamp` passes validation, because `0` is falsy. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` instead. Additionally, since both fields are `required=False` and the checks only fire inside the respective field validators, a report containing *neither* `age` nor `timestamp` is accepted, although the spec requires one of them; a `validate()` level check is needed. `age` also lacks a `min_value`, unlike `timestamp`.

title: get_environment_info issues a per-issue event fetch inside comment generation
body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` and then `get_environment()` for every issue included in a PR comment. `get_recommended_event` performs a Snuba/eventstore query, so building a comment for 5 issues now triggers 5 extra event lookups plus environment lookups per PR comment task, on a path that previously only read fields already loaded on the Group. Consider batching or using cached group metadata (e.g. `GroupEnvironment`) instead.

title: New table widget path renders hardcoded empty data
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}` instead of the actual `result`/`fields`/`result.meta`. Any organization with the flag on will see every dashboard table widget render completely empty. Either wire the real data through or keep this behind code that is not reachable.

title: Analytics recorded before feature gate and may use anonymous user id
body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble")` check, so the event is emitted even for orgs without the feature (which get a 404), inflating the metric. Also, for org-auth-token authenticated requests `request.user` is an anonymous user, so `request.user.id` will be `None`; consider guarding with `getattr(request.user, "id", None)` and moving the record after the feature check.

title: dcg_to_slow_conditions may be missing keys used by get_condition_query_groups
body: `get_slow_conditions_for_groups` is now computed once from `event_data.dcg_ids`, but `get_condition_query_groups` previously computed it from `event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys()` and indexes `dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id]` directly. If the two id sets ever diverge, this raises a `KeyError` and fails the whole delayed-workflow batch rather than skipping one group. Use `.get(dcg.id, [])` or assert the sets are equal.

title: KeyError when integration metadata has no 'sender'
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes the `sender` key always exists. `build_integration` only sets `metadata["sender"]` when the pipeline state contains `sender` (i.e. when the installation webhook was processed), so pre-existing Integration rows and installs where the webhook didn't populate sender will raise KeyError/TypeError, producing a 500 error instead of the intended friendly failure page. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and treat a missing value explicitly.

title: get_user_info failure is unhandled
body: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is called outside any try/except. If GitHub returns a non-200 (revoked token, rate limit, outage) this raises (e.g. ApiError) and the installation flow returns an unhandled 500 rather than rendering the github-integration-failed page like the other failure branches. It also assumes the return value is a dict supporting `in`.

title: Non constant-time comparison of pipeline signature
body: `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature` compares a user-supplied value against a secret-derived signature with `!=`, which short-circuits on the first differing byte. Use `django.utils.crypto.constant_time_compare` to avoid leaking information about the signature through timing.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the 404 installation path
body: The test now sends `state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`, which does not match the pipeline signature, so the request fails at the new state check in OAuthLoginView and asserts the generic "Invalid installation request." message. The original assertion ("The GitHub installation could not be found." from `build_integration` on a 404 from /app/installations) is therefore no longer exercised at all; that error path is now untested. Use the correct state so the flow actually reaches the installation lookup, and add a separate test for state mismatch.

title: No test for missing/failed access_token exchange or missing sender metadata
body: The new failure branches in OAuthLoginView (token exchange returning no `access_token`, `get_user_info` returning no `login`) and the GitHubInstallation branch where `integration.metadata` lacks `sender` are untested. Given these are the security-critical paths this PR adds, tests covering a failed/reused `code` and a metadata-without-sender integration should be added.

title: Unguarded access to integration.metadata['sender']['login'] can raise KeyError
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is indexed directly. The `sender` key is only populated in `build_integration` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy (i.e. set by the installation webhook); for integrations created before this change, or when the webhook has not been received/processed yet, the key is absent and this raises KeyError, producing a 500 instead of the intended error page. Use `.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and treat a missing value as a verification failure.

title: safe_urlopen call for token exchange is not error-handled
body: `safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` is outside the try/except that only wraps `safe_urlread`/parsing. A network failure, timeout, or non-2xx handling inside safe_urlopen raises, so a transient GitHub outage during installation yields an unhandled 500 rather than the intended user-facing "invalid installation request" page. Wrap the request in the same try/except.

title: get_user_info result assumed to be a dict
body: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` result is immediately checked with `"login" not in authenticated_user_info`. If the call raises (ApiError on 401/5xx from GitHub) or returns None, this either propagates an exception or raises TypeError, resulting in a 500 during installation instead of the graceful error page. Guard the call with try/except and a None check.

title: State comparison is not constant-time
body: `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature` compares a user-supplied value against the pipeline signature (a secret-derived HMAC) with a non-constant-time `!=`. Since this value is now the sole CSRF/authenticity guard for the OAuth callback, prefer `hmac.compare_digest` to avoid timing-based signature discovery.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the 404 installation path
body: The test passes `state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`, which does not match the pipeline signature used elsewhere (`9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`), so the request now fails at the new state-mismatch check in `OAuthLoginView` and the assertion `b"Invalid installation request."` passes without ever reaching `get_installation_info`. The previously covered behaviour ("The GitHub installation could not be found." when GitHub returns 404 for the installation) is now untested; the 404 branch in `build_integration` has no coverage.

title: KeyError when integration metadata lacks 'sender'
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is indexed unconditionally. `build_integration` only sets `metadata["sender"]` when the pipeline state contains `sender` (i.e. when the installation webhook was processed), so pre-existing or webhook-less Integration rows have no `sender` key. In that path the pipeline raises KeyError → HTTP 500 instead of the intended friendly error page, and the user is blocked from re-installing. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and treat a missing value as a verification failure.

title: get_user_info exceptions not handled
body: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` performs an HTTP request to GitHub; if it fails (non-200 / network error) it raises (ApiError or similar) rather than returning a dict, so the `"login" not in ...` guard never runs and the installation flow blows up with an unhandled 500. Wrap the call in try/except and return the standard `error(...)` response on failure.

title: State compared with non-constant-time equality
body: `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature` compares the pipeline signature (a secret-derived value) using `!=`, which is not constant time. Since this is now the anti-forgery check for the installation flow, prefer `django.utils.crypto.constant_time_compare` to avoid leaking timing information about the signature.

title: Lost coverage for 'GitHub installation could not be found' error
body: test_installation_not_found previously asserted the specific message `The GitHub installation could not be found.` raised by `build_integration` on a 404 from `/app/installations/{id}`. The test now only asserts the generic `Invalid installation request.` produced earlier in the new OAuth step, so the 404/IntegrationError path in `build_integration` is no longer exercised and regressions there would go unnoticed.

title: `queued` default evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a class-level default evaluated when the module is first imported, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` shares the process start time instead of the actual creation time. This makes the field useless for diagnosing/ordering sync events (and misleading in logs). Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

title: Non-JSON-serializable datetime passed in Celery task kwargs
body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` (via `dataclasses.asdict`) includes the `queued` datetime object, which is placed into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)`. With a JSON task serializer this raises a serialization error and the outbound assignee sync task is never queued, silently breaking all outbound assignee syncs whenever an assignment_source is present. Serialize `queued` to an ISO string (and parse it back in `from_dict`).

title: from_dict does not validate/convert field types
body: `from_dict` simply splats the dict into the constructor, so a round-tripped `queued` string stays a `str` and `integration_id` could be any type (e.g. a string from JSON), with no error. Downstream comparisons like `sync_source.integration_id == org_integration.integration_id` would then fail silently (string vs int), defeating the cycle-breaking logic. Coerce/validate types explicitly.

title: New `assignment_source` kwarg may break existing sync_assignee_outbound implementations
body: The task now always passes `assignment_source=...` to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound`. Concrete implementations (Jira, Jira Server, VSTS, GitHub Enterprise, etc.) whose signatures are `(self, external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs)` are fine, but any implementation without `**kwargs` will raise TypeError at runtime. The abstract signature in `mixins/issues.py` was not updated to include `assignment_source` either, so implementers get no signal. Add the parameter to the abstract signature and verify every override accepts it.

title: Mutable/eager default for `queued` evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates `timezone.now()` a single time when the module is imported, so every `AssignmentSource` instance created during the process lifetime shares the same (stale) timestamp instead of the time it was actually created. This makes the field useless for any staleness/dedup logic later on and is misleading in logs. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

title: AssignmentSource.to_dict() puts a datetime into Celery task kwargs
body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` returns a dict containing a `datetime` under `queued`, and this dict is passed as a Celery task kwarg via `apply_async`. With a JSON task serializer this will fail to serialize (or be coerced to a string), which would either drop the whole outbound sync task or, on the consumer side, make `AssignmentSource.from_dict` construct an object whose `queued` is a `str` rather than a `datetime` with no type error raised. Serialize `queued` explicitly (e.g. isoformat) and parse it back in `from_dict`.

title: from_dict does not validate/convert field types
body: `from_dict` just forwards the dict into the dataclass constructor, so it will happily produce an `AssignmentSource` with `integration_id` as a string or `queued` as a string (dataclasses do not enforce annotations). A string `integration_id` coming back from a serialized task payload would never equal `org_integration.integration_id` in `should_sync`, silently defeating the loop-prevention this PR adds. Coerce/validate types here.

title: New `assignment_source` kwarg passed to all sync_assignee_outbound implementations
body: The task now always calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`. Any existing integration implementation of `sync_assignee_outbound` that does not accept `**kwargs` (or this keyword) will raise `TypeError` at runtime, breaking outbound assignee sync for that provider. This path is only covered by the ExampleIntegration in tests, so a non-conforming provider would not be caught. Verify/update every implementation, or pass the kwarg defensively.

title: where_should_sync still calls should_sync without a sync source
body: `where_should_sync` invokes `installation.should_sync(key)` with no `sync_source`, so inbound-status sync paths (`sync_status_inbound`) and the inbound-assignee lookup can still fan out to the originating integration. The new cycle-prevention only covers the outbound-assignee task; if status sync is also triggered by the same webhook, the loop remains possible. Consider threading the assignment source through here as well.

title: `queued` default evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field default evaluated when the module is imported, so every `AssignmentSource` created in the process gets the same timestamp (the process start time), not the creation time. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

title: to_dict/from_dict round-trip breaks across Celery JSON serialization
body: `to_dict()` returns a `datetime` for `queued`, which is passed as a Celery task kwarg (`assignment_source_dict` in sync_group_assignee_outbound). With a JSON serializer this either raises a serialization error or, if coerced, arrives in the worker as a string, so `from_dict` will construct an `AssignmentSource` whose `queued` is a `str` (no validation catches it since `cls(**input_dict)` accepts any type). Serialize `queued` to ISO format in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`.

title: New `assignment_source` kwarg may break existing sync_assignee_outbound implementations
body: The task now always passes `assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source` to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound`. Any integration implementation whose signature does not accept `**kwargs`/`assignment_source` (e.g. third-party or plugin-based installations, and `IssueBasicIntegration` subclasses) will raise TypeError at runtime, silently failing assignee syncs after retries. Verify all implementations accept the kwarg or pass it only when present.

title: where_should_sync does not forward assignment source
body: `where_should_sync` calls `should_sync(key)` without a `sync_source`, so inbound paths that use it (e.g. `sync_status_inbound`, `sync_group_assignee_inbound`'s org filtering) cannot suppress cycles for status syncs. The newly added `assignment_source` parameter on `sync_status_outbound` is therefore never populated anywhere, leaving the status-sync cycle unaddressed despite the API change.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and will raise TypeError on instantiation
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`, but `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares abstract members `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Since none are implemented, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` remains abstract and `Detector.detector_handler` (which does `group_type.detector_handler(self)`) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...` whenever a metric alert detector is processed. Previously the handler returned an empty list and was harmless. Either keep a concrete stub implementation or don't register the handler yet.

title: PriorityLevel(new_status) can raise ValueError for unmapped DetectorPriorityLevel values
body: `PriorityLevel(new_status)` converts a `DetectorPriorityLevel` into a `PriorityLevel` purely by numeric value. If the two enums ever diverge (e.g. a DetectorPriorityLevel value with no corresponding PriorityLevel member), this raises ValueError inside detector evaluation and aborts processing of the data packet. An explicit mapping (or a validated helper) would make the coupling safe and explicit.

title: Multi-group test builds expected occurrence with the wrong value
body: In `test_state_results_multi_group`, group_2's data value is 10 but the expected occurrence is built with `value=6`. The assertion only passes because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores `value`, so the test would not catch a handler that mixes up group values. Pass the real value (10) so the expectation is meaningful.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with only `pass`, but StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). Since the class is an ABC with unimplemented abstract methods, `Detector.detector_handler` calling `group_type.detector_handler(self)` will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` whenever a metric_alert_fire detector is processed, breaking process_detectors for this type at runtime rather than being caught at import/type-check time.

title: Unchecked DetectorPriorityLevel -> PriorityLevel conversion can raise ValueError
body: `PriorityLevel(new_status)` converts a DetectorPriorityLevel into PriorityLevel by raw value. Any DetectorPriorityLevel value that does not have an exact numeric counterpart in PriorityLevel (e.g. future/extra levels) will raise ValueError inside evaluate_group_key_value, aborting evaluation of the data packet. The conversion should be an explicit mapping or guarded, and should be covered by a test for each possible priority level (current tests only exercise HIGH).

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is no longer instantiable
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with only `pass`, but StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). Since the class leaves them unimplemented, `Detector.detector_handler` -> `group_type.detector_handler(self)` will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...` at runtime for metric alert detectors, where previously evaluate() returned an empty list harmlessly. Either keep a concrete stub implementation or register no handler until implemented.

title: PriorityLevel(new_status) can raise ValueError
body: `PriorityLevel(new_status)` casts a DetectorPriorityLevel into the unrelated PriorityLevel enum. Any DetectorPriorityLevel value that doesn't have a numerically identical PriorityLevel member will raise ValueError during evaluation, crashing detector processing. The conversion should go through an explicit mapping with a safe fallback rather than relying on the two enums' numeric values staying in sync.

title: Multi-group test builds expected occurrence with the wrong value
body: For `group_2` the data packet value is 10, but the expected occurrence is built with `value=6`. The assertion only passes because the mock occurrence ignores `value`; if build_occurrence_and_event_data ever incorporates the value the test would silently be asserting the wrong thing. Pass 10 to keep the expectation faithful.

title: Removed public names from mark_failed may break other importers/tests
body: `SimpleCheckIn`, `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context` and the HUMAN_FAILURE maps were removed from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` and moved to new modules without re-exports. Any other code or tests importing these from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` (including tests that `mock.patch("sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence")`) will now fail with ImportError/AttributeError. The PR does not update any test or call-site files, so either those references need updating or shims/re-exports should be added.

title: get_monitor_environment_context builds a config copy it never uses
body: The function copies `monitor.config` and rewrites `schedule_type` to its display value, but the returned dict uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original), so the human-readable schedule_type substitution is silently dropped and the raw numeric schedule_type is emitted in the monitor context. Should return `config`.

title: Removed public symbols from mark_failed may break existing importers/tests
body: `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context` and `SimpleCheckIn` were removed from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` and renamed/moved (e.g. `create_issue_platform_occurrence` -> `incident_occurrence.create_incident_occurrence`). Any other module, task, or test that imports these from the old path (or monkeypatches `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence`) will fail at import time or silently stop being patched. No re-exports or shims are provided, and the PR touches no call sites/tests, so this should be verified across the repo.

title: get_monitor_environment_context ignores the modified config copy
body: The function copies `monitor.config` and rewrites `schedule_type` to its display value, but the returned dict sets `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original), so the human-readable schedule_type is never emitted and the `config` local is dead. Since this code is being moved into a new module, it's a good opportunity to return `config` instead.

title: Removed public names from mark_failed without re-exports
body: `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context` and `SimpleCheckIn` were all removed from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` and moved/renamed into new modules, with no backwards-compatible aliases. Any existing imports (e.g. tests patching `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence`, or code importing `SimpleCheckIn` from here) will fail at import time or silently stop patching the real code path. Either keep re-export aliases or update all call sites/tests in this PR.

title: get_monitor_environment_context computes `config` copy but returns the raw config
body: Lines 160-162 copy the monitor config and replace `schedule_type` with its display value, but the returned dict at line 168 uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the modified `config`. The resulting occurrence context therefore reports the numeric schedule_type rather than the human-readable one, and the copy is dead code. (Carried over from the moved code, but easy to fix while relocating.)

title: Unhealthy spawn processes are never killed due to isinstance check
body: In `_ensure_processes_alive` the kill is now guarded by `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Processes are created with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which produces a `SpawnProcess` that derives from `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.Process` (the default-context class). The guard therefore evaluates False and hung flusher processes are never killed before a replacement is started, leaking processes that still hold Redis connections and keep flushing the same shards concurrently with the new process (duplicate/fragmented segment production). The same problem applies to `process.terminate()` in `join()` (line 346). Use `BaseProcess` or check for `threading.Thread` instead.

title: join() breaks out of shutdown loop leaving remaining processes untouched
body: In `join()`, when the deadline is exceeded the loop `break`s, so processes with higher indices are never waited on nor terminated.
