With multiple flusher processes, a timed-out shutdown can leave daemon processes alive that continue flushing segments while the consumer rebalances. `remaining_time` is also computed but unused. Terminate all processes unconditionally after the wait loop instead of breaking out.

title: Dead/incorrect helper `_create_process_for_shard`
body: `_create_process_for_shard(shard)` is never called anywhere after the refactor (health checking now restarts by process index). Dead code that duplicates restart logic and has no restart-counter accounting; it should be removed to avoid future misuse that bypasses the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS guard.

title: Inconsistent metric tag name "shards" vs "shard"
body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `shards=` while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use `shard=`. This breaks dashboards/queries grouping on a single tag key. Also note the tag value is now a comma-joined list of shards, which changes cardinality and the meaning of existing `shard` tags on these metrics.

title: time.sleep is monkeypatched to a no-op, so the added sleep does not wait
body: `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at the top of the test makes the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` (and its comment about giving flusher threads time) a no-op. The test therefore still races against the flusher thread producing into `messages`, and the following `(msg,) = messages` can fail intermittently. Use a real wait/poll loop (e.g. a saved reference to the original sleep or polling until messages is non-empty).

title: Multi-process flusher test only asserts bookkeeping, not behaviour
body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` checks `len(flusher.processes)`, `max_processes` and the shard count, but never submits spans nor verifies that segments from all 4 shards are actually flushed by the 2 workers. The core new behaviour (shard partitioning across processes, per-process backpressure/health, no duplicate or missing segments) is untested.

title: time.sleep(0.1) in test is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
body: The test patches `time.sleep` to a no-op at line 15 (`monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`), so the `time.sleep(0.1)` added at line 62 to "give flusher threads time to process after drift change" does nothing. The intended synchronization doesn't happen, so the test relies on timing luck and can be flaky (the single expected message may not have been produced before `step.join()`). Use a real sleep reference captured before patching, or poll for the expected condition with a timeout.

title: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False for spawn-context processes
body: `self.mp_context.Process` with the "spawn" context creates `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`, which derives from `BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.Process` (= `multiprocessing.context.Process`). Therefore `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is False and neither `process.kill()` in `_ensure_processes_alive` nor `process.terminate()` in `join` is ever executed. Hung flusher processes are never killed before a replacement is spawned, so two processes can flush the same shards concurrently (duplicate segment production), and processes are not terminated on shutdown. Check `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)` instead.

title: Dead method `_create_process_for_shard`
body: `_create_process_for_shard(shard)` is never called anywhere after the refactor (restart now goes through `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`). Dead code that duplicates restart logic and will silently rot / be misused; remove it.

title: Inconsistent metric tag name: 'shards' vs 'shard'
body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `shards=shard_tag` while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use `shard=shard_tag`, and `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` uses `shard=<single shard>`. Mixed tag keys/semantics for the same dimension make dashboards and queries inconsistent; pick one key name (and note the value is now a comma-joined list, which also changes tag cardinality/semantics vs. before).

title: Parent process creates one extra SpansBuffer (and Redis connections) per flusher process
body: `_create_process_for_shards` constructs a `SpansBuffer` in the parent and keeps it in `self.buffers`, in addition to the one pickled into the child. On every process restart a new buffer replaces the old entry without closing it, leaking Redis connections in the long-running consumer. Also `submit()` now calls `get_memory_info()` on every buffer, issuing N duplicate INFO calls against the same Redis cluster each submit.

title: New flusher test asserts only counts, and leaks the strategy factory pool
body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` checks process counts and that the total number of mapped shards is 4, but never asserts the shard->process mapping is a disjoint partition of the assigned shards (the real correctness property: no shard flushed by two processes, none dropped). It also never calls `fac.shutdown()`, leaving flusher threads/buffers around after the test.

title: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is never true for spawn processes, so unhealthy flushers are never killed
body: In `_ensure_processes_alive` the kill is now guarded by `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Processes here are created with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which produces `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` instances; `SpawnProcess` is a subclass of `BaseProcess`, not of `multiprocessing.Process` (= `context.Process`). So the isinstance check is False and `process.kill()` is never invoked. A hung (but still alive) flusher process will not be killed before `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement, leaking live processes that keep flushing the same shards concurrently — duplicate segment production and growing process count up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS. The same flaw makes `process.terminate()` in `join()` a no-op.

title: join() breaks out of loop leaving remaining processes unterminated
body: In `join`, when the deadline is exceeded the loop `break`s, so any processes after the current index are never waited on nor terminated. On shutdown/rebalance with multiple flusher processes, some child processes are left running (they are daemons, so they die with the parent, but during arroyo rebalances the parent keeps running) and may keep flushing shards that have been reassigned. Also `remaining_time` is computed and unused. Terminate all processes unconditionally before returning.

title: num_processes becomes 0 when no shards are assigned, silently disabling the flusher
body: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` plus `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` yields 0 when `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty (possible when a consumer is assigned no partitions). No flusher processes are started and no health check ever fires, so the strategy silently never flushes; additionally `max_processes` passed as 0 from the CLI would behave as "one process per shard" rather than an error. Validate the input and handle the empty-shard case explicitly.

title: Dead method _create_process_for_shard
body: `_create_process_for_shard(shard)` is not called from anywhere after the refactor (restarts go through `_create_process_for_shards`). Dead code that duplicates restart logic and will rot; remove it.

title: Inconsistent metric tag name: 'shards' vs 'shard'
body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged `shards=shard_tag` while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use `shard=shard_tag`. Inconsistent tag keys break dashboards/queries that group by one key. Pick one key name for all flusher metrics.

title: Per-shard unhealthy metric increases cardinality and double-counts a single process failure
body: `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` is now emitted once per shard owned by the failing process, with a `shard` tag. One process failure produces N increments, so the metric no longer counts failures and the `shard` tag adds cardinality proportional to total shards. Consider emitting once per process (e.g. tagged with process index or the joined shard tag).

title: New test asserts only process counts, not shard distribution or flushing correctness
body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` checks `len(flusher.processes) == 2` and that the total shard count is 4, but never asserts that shards are evenly distributed (2 per process) nor that segments from all four shards actually get produced through the multiple processes. The core behaviour this PR introduces (parallel flushing across processes, restart handling) is untested.

title: queue_pool is created once per factory but destroyed on strategy close, breaking processing after a rebalance
body: `FixedQueuePool` is constructed once in `__init__` and reused by every `create_with_partitions` call. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()`/`terminate()` calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, which permanently stops the worker threads and shuts down the queues. Arroyo calls `create_with_partitions` again after every partition revoke/assign (rebalance), so the second strategy will be handed a pool whose workers are dead and whose queues raise `ShutDown` on put. From then on the consumer silently accepts messages that are never processed and never commits, i.e. it stalls permanently until the process is restarted. The pool needs to be created per strategy (or recreated when it has been shut down).

title: Arroyo commit callback invoked from a background thread
body: `_commit_loop` runs in its own thread and calls `self.commit_function(...)` (ultimately arroyo's `commit` passed to `create_with_partitions`). Arroyo's commit callback and the underlying Kafka consumer are not thread-safe and are expected to be called from the strategy/processing thread (the same thread that calls `poll`/`submit`). Calling it concurrently with the StreamProcessor's own consumer operations can corrupt consumer state or crash librdkafka. Offsets should instead be accumulated and committed from `poll()`.

title: No final commit on close(), and offset state survives rebalances
body: `close()` sets `shutdown_event` (ending `_commit_loop` without a last pass) and then shuts the pool down after workers drain remaining queued items. Offsets for everything processed since the last 1-second tick, plus everything drained during shutdown, are therefore never committed, so those messages are reprocessed after restart. Additionally `OffsetTracker` state (`all_offsets`, `outstanding`, `last_committed`) is never reset on partition revocation; because the pool/tracker is shared across `create_with_partitions` calls, a new strategy can commit offsets for partitions the consumer no longer owns. A final `get_committable_offsets()`/commit after draining, plus per-assignment tracker reset, is needed.

title: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure despite docstring claim
body: `queue.Queue()` is created with no maxsize and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` never raises `MessageRejected`. The class docstring claims "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", but in practice a slow group can accumulate unbounded work items (each holding the decoded result and the original Kafka `Message`), growing memory without limit and making the uncommitted offset window unbounded. Set a maxsize and raise `MessageRejected` when full so arroyo throttles consumption.

title: Decode/submit failures are silently acked instead of DLQ'd
body: In `submit`, any exception (including the `assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)` and the `assert not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload)` inside `decode_payload`) is swallowed and the offset is immediately marked added+complete, so the message is committed as if processed. This drops messages without routing them to the DLQ and will also silently discard every `FilteredPayload` while logging an exception for each. Filtered payloads should be handled explicitly and genuine failures should be surfaced/DLQ'd rather than acked.

title: queue.ShutDown / Queue.shutdown require Python 3.13
body: `queue.ShutDown` and `Queue.shutdown(immediate=...)` were added in Python 3.13. On an older interpreter the module-level reference raises `AttributeError` at worker runtime and `q.shutdown()` is swallowed by the broad `except Exception` in `FixedQueuePool.shutdown`, leaving workers blocked forever in `work_queue.get()` and making shutdown hang for 5s per worker. If the project must support <3.13, use a sentinel item to stop workers instead.

title: Transaction name hardcodes "monitors" prefix for generic remote-subscription consumer
body: The sentry_sdk transaction is named `f"monitors.{self.identifier}.worker_{self.worker_id}"`, but this strategy is generic to remote subscriptions (uptime being the first user). Uptime traffic will be reported under a `monitors.*` transaction name, making performance data misleading.

title: Queues are unbounded, so there is no backpressure despite the docstring
body: `FixedQueuePool.__init__` creates `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize`, and `submit()` never raises `MessageRejected`. The class docstring for `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` claims "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", but nothing ever blocks or rejects: if a worker is slow, the consumer keeps reading from Kafka and buffering decoded results in memory without bound, which can OOM the consumer and also inflates offset-tracking state. A bounded queue plus raising `MessageRejected` (or blocking put) is needed to get the advertised backpressure.

title: queue_pool is created once per factory and destroyed by strategy close(), breaking rebalances
body: The `FixedQueuePool` (and its worker threads and `OffsetTracker`) is created once in `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__`, but `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()`/`terminate()` call `queue_pool.shutdown()`, which stops all worker threads and shuts down the queues. Arroyo calls `create_with_partitions` again after every rebalance/partition revocation. On the second call, `assert self.queue_pool is not None` still passes (the attribute isn't cleared by the strategy), so a new strategy is built on top of dead workers and already-shutdown queues: submitted work is never processed and offsets are never committed, stalling the consumer silently. Additionally the `OffsetTracker`'s `last_committed`/`all_offsets` are carried across assignments, so stale per-partition state can suppress commits (or commit offsets for partitions no longer owned) after a rebalance. The pool should be created per `create_with_partitions` call (or reset on revocation).

title: Arroyo commit callback invoked from a background thread
body: `_commit_loop` runs in its own thread and calls `self.commit_function(committable)`, which is arroyo's `commit` callback passed to `create_with_partitions`. That callback (and the underlying consumer offset staging) is expected to be invoked from the main processing thread; calling it concurrently with the StreamProcessor's `poll`/`submit`/commit handling is not thread-safe and can corrupt or lose staged offsets. Offsets should be collected by the worker threads and flushed from `poll()` on the main thread instead.

title: close() does not flush remaining committable offsets or drain queues
body: `close()` sets `shutdown_event`, joins the commit thread and shuts the pool down. The commit loop exits as soon as the event is set, so any work completed in the last interval (and any work the workers finish during their 5s join) is never committed. Queued-but-unprocessed items are also dropped by `queue.shutdown(immediate=False)`? they are drained only if workers keep up within the join timeout. On every consumer shutdown/rebalance this causes re-delivery (duplicate processing) of up to a second's worth of already-processed results, and silently dropped work if workers don't finish. A final `get_committable_offsets()`/commit after draining is needed.

title: queue.ShutDown / Queue.shutdown require Python 3.13+
body: `queue.ShutDown` and `queue.Queue.shutdown(immediate=...)` were only added in Python 3.13. On any older interpreter this module raises `AttributeError` at worker-exception handling time and `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` logs "Error shutting down queue" for every queue while workers stay blocked in `get()` forever, so the consumer can never shut down. If the runtime is not guaranteed to be 3.13+, this needs a compatibility path (e.g. sentinel items).

title: Decode/grouping failures mark the offset complete and are silently dropped
body: In `submit()`, any exception from the decoder or `grouping_fn` is caught, logged, and the offset is immediately added+completed, i.e. the message is committed as if processed. There is no DLQ handling and no metric, so malformed or unexpected payloads are permanently lost with only a log line. Consider routing these to the DLQ (raise `InvalidMessage`) or at least emitting a counter.

title: Per-partition lock map and defaultdicts mutated without a global lock
body: `_get_partition_lock` and the `defaultdict` accesses in `add_offset`/`get_committable_offsets` mutate `self.partition_locks`, `self.all_offsets` and `self.outstanding` from multiple worker threads plus the commit thread with no guarding lock (the per-partition lock is acquired only after the dict lookup/creation). This relies entirely on CPython dict/`setdefault` atomicity and will break under free-threaded builds or if the implementation changes. A single mutex guarding the maps (or a lock around lock-creation) would make the invariants explicit.

title: hash() of group key is not stable across processes
body: `get_queue_for_group` uses builtin `hash(group_key)`, which for `str` is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED). The docstring claims "consistent hashing", but assignment differs between consumer processes and across restarts. This is tolerable since each process owns distinct partitions, but if ordering guarantees are ever expected to hold across processes/restarts this is wrong; use a stable hash (e.g. md5/crc32) instead.

title: WorkItem retains full Kafka message for no reason
body: `WorkItem.message` stores the entire arroyo `Message` (including the raw payload bytes) but is never read anywhere; partition/offset are tracked separately. With unbounded queues this doubles the memory held per queued item. Drop the field.

title: Flaky assertion that 20 groups hit all 3 queues
body: `test_different_groups_distributed` asserts `len(queue_indices) == 3` based on `hash()` of 20 group keys, which is randomized per process. It is likely but not guaranteed that all three queues are hit, so this test can fail intermittently. Assert `>= 2` or seed a deterministic hash.

title: join() ignores its timeout argument
body: `join(timeout)` discards `timeout` and calls `close()`, which uses hard-coded 5s joins for the commit thread and each worker. With N queues this can block for N*5s during shutdown, exceeding arroyo's join timeout and triggering a forced kill mid-processing. The timeout should be honoured/budgeted across the threads.

title: strategy.close() destroys the factory-shared queue pool, breaking rebalances
body: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()`/`terminate()` call `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, but the `FixedQueuePool` is created once in `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__` and shared across every `create_with_partitions()` call. Arroyo closes/recreates the strategy on every partition rebalance, so after the first revoke the pool's worker threads are dead and its queues are shut down, while `factory.queue_pool` is still non-None. The next `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker()` will happily build a strategy over the dead pool and every submitted message will be silently dropped (or raise on `put` into a shut-down queue), stalling the consumer until the process is restarted.

title: commit function invoked from a background thread
body: `_commit_loop` runs in its own thread and calls `self.commit_function(committable)`, which ends up in arroyo's `Commit` callback and ultimately the Kafka consumer. Arroyo strategies are documented as being driven from the single processing thread; the underlying consumer and the processor's offset bookkeeping are not thread-safe. Concurrent `commit()` from this thread while the main loop polls/commits can corrupt offset state or raise from librdkafka, risking duplicate or lost processing.

title: OffsetTracker state is never reset on partition revocation
body: `OffsetTracker` lives on the long-lived `FixedQueuePool`, and there is no API to drop state for revoked partitions. After a rebalance, `last_committed`, `all_offsets` and `outstanding` still contain entries for partitions this consumer no longer owns, so the commit thread can emit commits for partitions owned by another member, and stale `last_committed` values for a re-assigned partition can suppress legitimate commits (the loop only commits offsets greater than `last_committed`, which may now be far ahead of the new fetch position).

title: queue.ShutDown / Queue.shutdown require Python 3.13
body: `queue.ShutDown` and `Queue.shutdown(immediate=...)` were added in Python 3.13. On any earlier interpreter, `except queue.ShutDown` in `OrderedQueueWorker.run` raises `AttributeError` when an exception propagates, and `q.shutdown(...)` in `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` raises `AttributeError` which is swallowed by the bare `except Exception`. The result is that workers block forever in `work_queue.get()` (the `self.shutdown` flag is only checked between items), so shutdown takes 5s per worker and in-flight work is abandoned. If 3.13 is a hard requirement it should be stated; otherwise use a sentinel item plus `get(timeout=...)`.

title: Unbounded queues: no backpressure despite docstring claim
body: The docstrings for `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` and `FixedQueuePool` claim "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", but the queues are created as unbounded `queue.Queue()` and `submit()` never raises `MessageRejected`. A slow `result_processor` therefore causes unbounded growth of queued `WorkItem`s (each holding the full Kafka `Message`), leading to OOM rather than backpressure, and the comment is misleading. Give the queues a maxsize and raise `MessageRejected` when full.

title: Lock creation relies on CPython dict atomicity
body: `_get_partition_lock` does an unsynchronized `get` followed by `setdefault` on a plain dict. This happens to be safe only because of CPython's GIL making `setdefault` atomic; it is not guaranteed by the language and would break under a free-threaded build. Prefer a single module-level lock guarding lock creation, or a `defaultdict(threading.Lock)` created once under a lock.

title: Transaction name hardcodes 'monitors' prefix for remote subscriptions worker
body: The sentry transaction name is `f"monitors.{self.identifier}.worker_{self.worker_id}"`, but this is generic remote-subscription/uptime code. Including `worker_id` also produces high-cardinality transaction names (one per queue). This will make the uptime consumer's traces show up under misleading `monitors.*` names.

title: Error-handling test asserts nothing meaningful about offsets
body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` ends with `assert len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`, which is a tautology (both branches assert the same thing) and, more importantly, contradicts the test's stated intent that "errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages" — the implementation does commit offsets after a failure (the worker completes the offset in `finally`). The assertion will pass even if commits are completely broken; it should assert the expected committed offset (102).

title: Kafka integration test drives StreamProcessor via private APIs and sleeps
body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_kafka_offset_commit` calls `processor._run_once()` / `processor._shutdown()` (private arroyo APIs that can change without notice) and busy-loops for a fixed 5 seconds, which makes the test both brittle against arroyo upgrades and slow/flaky under load. The `commits_made` assertions are also guarded by `if commits_made:` so they silently no-op if no commit was recorded.

title: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, allowing reuse
body: The backup-code login path decrypts the whole `backupCodes` JSON array, sets the matching entry to `null`, and writes the entire re-encrypted array back with `prisma.user.update`. Because the read and write are not atomic (no transaction, no conditional update), two concurrent authorize() calls that both present the *same* code will both find it at a non-(-1) index and both succeed, defeating the single-use guarantee of a backup code. Two concurrent logins with *different* codes will also clobber each other, re-validating an already consumed code. Consider consuming the code inside a transaction or with an update guarded on the previous `backupCodes` value.

title: Backup codes cannot be used by Google/SAML users with 2FA
body: `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode) throw new Error(ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled)` (and the analogous check on the next line) only allows the second-factor flow to proceed when a TOTP code is present. Users who authenticate via Google/SAML and have 2FA enabled are redirected to `/auth/login?totp=<jwt>` with no password; if they submit a backup code (totpCode empty) they get `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` / `IncorrectEmailPassword` instead of being logged in. The login page also hides the "Lost access" button in that flow (`ExternalTotpFooter`), so for these accounts backup codes are generated and stored but can never be redeemed — exactly the lock-out case the feature is meant to solve. The condition should also accept `credentials.backupCode`.

title: onEnable() is only called from the Close button, so dismissing the dialog leaves stale UI and loses codes
body: Previously `onEnable()` fired as soon as the enable API returned 200. Now the success path only calls `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` and `onEnable()` is invoked exclusively by the "Close" button handler. If the user dismisses the dialog with ESC, the X, or an overlay click (which triggers `onOpenChange`), 2FA is already enabled server-side but the parent settings view is never notified, so the two-factor switch stays in the "off" state until a manual reload. The user also loses the only display of their backup codes, with no way to regenerate them. `onEnable()` should be called when the code is accepted (or on `onOpenChange` while on the backup-codes step).

title: "missing_backup_codes" tells users to generate codes in settings, but no such feature exists
body: `"missing_backup_codes": "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings."` is shown when `user.backupCodes` is null — which is the case for every account that enabled 2FA before this change, and for anyone who already spent all ten codes. There is no regenerate/backup-codes screen in settings: codes are only created by `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup`, which rejects accounts that already have 2FA enabled (`TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled`). The only actual remedy is to disable and re-enable 2FA, so the message sends users on an impossible errand. Either add a regeneration path or change the text to describe the real recovery procedure.

title: Backup codes stored with reversible encryption instead of hashed
body: `backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` persists the plaintext codes under a single application-wide key, and both the login and disable paths decrypt them to compare. Unlike `twoFactorSecret`, backup codes never need to be recovered in cleartext — verification only requires an equality check — so they should be stored as hashes (e.g. bcrypt/sha-256 per code). As written, anyone who obtains the database plus `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (one secret shared by every other encrypted field) gets a usable 2FA bypass for every user.

title: Submitting an empty/short backup code silently does nothing
body: The login form is rendered with `noValidate`, so the `required`/`minLength` attributes on the backup-code input (apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx) are never enforced, and the zod schema `passthrough()`es `backupCode` without validation. Submitting the backup-code step with an empty field sends `backupCode: ""`, the server falls through to the TOTP branch and throws `SecondFactorRequired`, which this handler maps to `setTwoFactorRequired(true)` — a no-op since it is already true — leaving no error message and no visible feedback. Add client-side validation for `backupCode` (or surface `SecondFactorRequired` as an error while in the lost-access state).

title: Unvalidated request body can crash the disable endpoint with a 500
body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes the field is a string. A client that posts `{"backupCode": 123}` or `{"backupCode": {}}` passes the truthiness check and then throws `TypeError: replaceAll is not a function`, producing an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. Likewise `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` on line 58 throws if the stored value cannot be decrypted/parsed (e.g. after an encryption-key rotation). Validate/coerce the body (zod or `typeof === "string"`) and wrap the decrypt/parse in a try/catch returning a defined ErrorCode.

title: Passing type="password" to PasswordField disables the show/hide toggle
body: `PasswordField` computes `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` and then spreads `{...props}` *after* it (packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx), so the explicit `type="password"` kept from the old `TextField` usage overrides the computed value. Clicking the eye icon toggles `isPasswordVisible` but the input stays `type="password"`, i.e. the reveal button does nothing. Drop the `type` prop here.

title: tabIndex={-1} makes the password reveal button keyboard-inaccessible
body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the show/hide-password button removes it from the tab order for all `PasswordField` consumers across the app (login, signup, 2FA modals). Keyboard-only and screen-reader users can no longer reach this control even though it has an `sr-only` label, which is an accessibility regression affecting every password input, not just the 2FA dialogs. If the goal was to stop the button from stealing focus during the 2FA flow, make it opt-in via a prop instead of changing global behaviour.

title: resetState leaves stale form/backup-code state and leaks the blob URL
body: `resetState()` clears only `password`, `errorMessage` and `step`. The component is not unmounted when the dialog closes (state lives above the Radix `Dialog`), so `form`'s `totpCode`, `backupCodes`, `secret`, `dataUri` and `backupCodesUrl` persist. Consequences: (1) the previously entered 6-digit `totpCode` is still in the form on a subsequent setup, so pressing "Enable" immediately submits the stale code; (2) the object URL created with `URL.createObjectURL` is only revoked on the next successful setup, so it (and the plaintext backup codes it contains) is retained for the lifetime of the document. Reset the form (`form.reset()`) and clear/revoke the backup-code state too.

title: No test covers the core new behaviour: authenticating with a backup code
body: The added test steps only exercise the download/copy/close buttons on the new backup-codes screen; the primary feature paths — logging in through "Lost access" with a backup code (including that a code is consumed and cannot be reused) and disabling 2FA with a backup code — are left as a TODO comment. Given the security sensitivity (single-use enforcement, re-encryption of the remaining codes, dash stripping), at least one end-to-end or unit test for a successful and a repeated backup-code redemption should be part of this PR.

title: Assertion on the 2FA switch is a no-op and was documented rather than fixed
body: `expect(page.locator(`[data-testid=two-factor-switch]`).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on the Promise returned by `isChecked()`, which is always truthy, so this step can never fail — as the newly added FIXME admits. Since the enable flow now ends on the backup-codes dialog (the switch is not updated until `onEnable` runs), this test would not catch a regression where 2FA is never actually enabled. Replace it with `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch][data-state="checked"]')).toBeVisible()` as the second test already does.

title: Backup-code component is exported under the name TwoFactor
body: The new component in `BackupCode.tsx` is declared as `export default function TwoFactor({ center = true })`. The copy-pasted name makes React DevTools, error stacks and future greps report this backup-code input as "TwoFactor", which is confusing next to the real `TwoFactor` component it is rendered alongside in login.tsx and DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

title: Backup code alone can authenticate without the account password
body: The password is only verified by the block at lines 121-129, which is guarded by `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`. The new backup-code branch is entered whenever `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` is set, regardless of `totpCode`. An attacker who obtains a single backup code (e.g. the downloaded `cal-backup-codes.txt`) but does not know the password can POST to the credentials endpoint with `email`, an arbitrary `password`, any non-empty `totpCode` (e.g. "000000") and the valid `backupCode`: the password check is skipped because `totpCode` is truthy, and only the backup code is validated, so the login succeeds. Backup codes are intended to replace the second factor, not the password, so this turns them into full single-factor credentials. The backup-code branch must verify the password (or the branch selection must not depend on `totpCode` being absent).

title: Backup codes stored with reversible encryption instead of hashed
body: Backup codes are persisted as `symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)`, i.e. recoverable plaintext. The server never needs to display the codes again after setup (they are only shown from the setup response), so they can and should be stored as one-way hashes like passwords. As implemented, anyone who gains read access to the users table together with the (single, global, long-lived) encryption key — which is also present in every app instance's environment — can recover every user's 2FA backup codes and bypass two-factor auth for all accounts.

title: onEnable() is no longer called unless the user clicks "Close", leaving stale UI after enabling 2FA
body: Previously `onEnable()` was invoked as soon as the enable request succeeded. Now it is only called by the "Close" button on the backup-codes step. If the user dismisses the dialog with the X / overlay / Esc (which goes through `onOpenChange`), 2FA is already enabled server-side but the parent is never notified, so the settings page never invalidates its query and the two-factor switch keeps showing "off" until a manual reload. Additionally `resetState()` is not run on that path, so `step` stays at `DisplayBackupCodes` and re-opening the modal shows the previous (now stale) backup codes screen instead of the password step. Either call `onEnable()` when the enable request succeeds, or handle `onOpenChange` to invoke `onEnable()`/`resetState()`.

title: First 2FA test asserts nothing and is not updated for the new backup-codes step
body: `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on the returned Promise, which is always truthy, so the step verifies nothing — the PR documents this with a FIXME instead of fixing it. This matters now: with the new flow the backup-codes dialog stays open after OTP entry and `onEnable()` is never fired, so the switch would legitimately not be checked; the test only passes because the assertion is a no-op. Use `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch][data-state="checked"]')).toBeVisible()` after dismissing the backup-codes dialog, as the second test does.

title: "missing_backup_codes" message points users to a settings feature that does not exist
body: The string is "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." but there is no UI anywhere in this PR to generate or regenerate backup codes — codes are only created inside the 2FA setup flow (`totp/setup`). Every user who enabled 2FA before this migration has `backupCodes = null` and will hit this message with no actionable path; the only way to obtain codes is to disable and re-enable 2FA. Either add a regenerate action or change the message to tell users to disable and re-enable two-factor authentication.

title: Backup code comparison is case-sensitive while the input is not normalized
body: `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` compares the user input literally against lowercase hex codes generated by `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`. The input field in `apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx` sets no `autoCapitalize="off"`/`autoCorrect="off"`, so mobile keyboards commonly capitalize the first character and users who type the code in upper case will be rejected with "Backup code is incorrect" even though they supplied a valid code. The same applies to `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`. Normalize with `.toLowerCase().trim()` server-side and/or disable auto-capitalization on the input.

title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: The code decrypts the whole array, nulls one entry and writes the re-encrypted blob back with a plain `user.update`. Two concurrent logins using the same backup code both read the un-consumed array and both succeed, so a one-time code can be used more than once; two concurrent logins using different codes will clobber each other's update, resurrecting an already-used code. Consider a transaction with a row-level check (e.g. conditional update on the previous value) or storing individual code rows that can be deleted atomically.

title: Submitting an empty backup code silently does nothing
body: The login form is rendered with `noValidate`, and the zod schema only validates `email`/`password` (`.passthrough()`), so the `required`/`minLength` attributes on the backup-code input are not enforced. Submitting the backup-code screen with an empty field sends `backupCode: ""`, the server falls through to the TOTP branch and returns `SecondFactorRequired`, which this handler maps to `setTwoFactorRequired(true)` — a no-op since the user is already on that screen — while `errorMessage` was cleared at the start of submit. The user gets no feedback at all. Validate the backup code client-side or surface an error for this case.

title: Unvalidated request body can crash the disable endpoint
body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes the field is a string; a client sending `{"backupCode": 123}` or an object causes an uncaught `TypeError` and an opaque 500 instead of a 400. Likewise `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` on line 58 is unguarded, so a corrupted/re-keyed `backupCodes` column throws an unhandled exception rather than returning a meaningful error. Validate/parse the body (e.g. with zod) and wrap the decrypt/parse in a try/catch.

title: Backup code state and object URL are never cleaned up
body: `resetState()` only clears password, error and step; `backupCodes` and `backupCodesUrl` keep holding the generated codes in component state after the dialog closes (the modal is kept mounted by the settings page). The blob URL created in `handleSetup` is only revoked when a new one is created, never on unmount or close, so each setup leaks a blob for the lifetime of the page. Clear both in `resetState()` and revoke the URL (e.g. in a cleanup effect).

title: Clipboard write rejection is unhandled and success toast is shown unconditionally
body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a promise that is neither awaited nor caught, and `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` runs immediately. In contexts where the Clipboard API is unavailable or permission is denied (non-HTTPS deployments, some browsers), the user is told the codes were copied while nothing was copied, and the rejection surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection. Await the call and only show success on resolve, with an error toast/fallback otherwise.

title: Password visibility toggle made unreachable by keyboard
body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the show/hide password button removes it from tab order, so keyboard-only and screen-reader users can no longer toggle password visibility. This change affects every `PasswordField` in the app, not just the 2FA dialogs. If the intent was to keep tab order flowing to the next form field, consider other means (e.g. ordering/`aria` handling) rather than making the control unfocusable.

title: Backup codes are unusable for Google/SAML users with 2FA
body: For users who reach the login page via the external TOTP flow (`totpEmail` set, i.e. Google/SAML accounts with 2FA), `ExternalTotpFooter` is rendered and the new "Lost access" button is never shown, so those users cannot use their backup codes. Even if a `backupCode` were submitted, `authorize()` in next-auth-options.ts throws `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` at the `user.identityProvider !== CAL && !credentials.totpCode` check before reaching the backup-code branch. These users have no recovery path if they lose their authenticator, which is the main purpose of the feature.

title: Backup code login can bypass the password check entirely
body: In `authorize()` the password is only verified when `user.password && !credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new backup-code branch is evaluated afterwards and takes precedence over the TOTP branch whenever `credentials.backupCode` is non-empty. An attacker who posts `email` + any non-empty `totpCode` (e.g. "000000") + a valid `backupCode` therefore skips password verification completely and is logged in on the strength of the backup code alone. Backup codes are long-lived static strings that users are encouraged to download to a text file (`cal-backup-codes.txt`), so this turns a comparatively weakly-protected artefact into a full single-factor account takeover. The backup-code branch must require a successful password verification for CAL-identity users (or the password check must not be skippable by merely supplying a totpCode).

title: Backup code invalidation is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: The code decrypts the whole `backupCodes` array, nulls out the used index and writes the whole array back with `prisma.user.update`. Two requests presenting the *same* backup code concurrently can both pass the `indexOf` check before either update lands, so a single backup code can be consumed more than once (defeating the "each code can be used exactly once" guarantee stated in `backup_code_instructions`). Likewise, two concurrent logins using *different* codes will each write a snapshot taken before the other's update, so one consumption is silently lost and that code becomes reusable. This needs to be done in a transaction with a conditional update (or by storing codes as individual rows / hashed values that can be deleted atomically).

title: Backup codes are stored reversibly encrypted instead of hashed
body: `setup.ts` stores the backup codes with `symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` and the login path decrypts them to compare. Unlike `twoFactorSecret`, backup codes never need to be recovered in plaintext after they are shown once, so they should be hashed (e.g. bcrypt/argon2, as passwords are) and compared by hash. As written, anyone with read access to the `users` table plus the encryption key (a single env var shared across the deployment) obtains working second factors for every 2FA user, and combined with the password-bypass issue in this same function that is sufficient for account takeover.

title: onEnable() is now only called from the Close button, leaving UI state stale if the dialog is dismissed
body: Previously `onEnable()` fired immediately after the enable API returned 200. Now it is only invoked by the `backup-codes-close` button. If the user dismisses the dialog any other way (X button, Escape, overlay click → `onOpenChange`), 2FA is already enabled server-side but the parent never learns about it, so the two-factor switch keeps showing "off" until a page reload. Worse, `resetState()` is also skipped in that path, so `step` stays at `DisplayBackupCodes` and `backupCodes` keeps the old values: reopening the modal immediately shows the previous user's/previous run's backup codes instead of starting at the password step. Reset state and notify the parent from `onOpenChange` as well.

title: Submitting an empty backup code gives the user no feedback
body: The login form is rendered with `noValidate`, so the `required`/`minLength` attributes on the backup-code input are not enforced, and the zod schema only validates `email`/`password` (everything else is `passthrough`). Submitting the backup-code step with an empty field sends `backupCode: ""`, the server falls through to the TOTP branch and returns `SecondFactorRequired`, which this handler maps to `setTwoFactorRequired(true)` without setting an error message. The result is a submit that appears to do nothing. Validate the backup-code field client-side (or surface an error for `SecondFactorRequired` while in backup-code mode).

title: Unvalidated request body can crash the disable endpoint
body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes the field is a string; posting `{"backupCode": 1}` or `{"backupCode": []}` throws `replaceAll is not a function`, and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on any corrupt/legacy ciphertext. Both throw out of the handler and surface as an unhandled 500 (with a stack trace in logs) instead of a controlled 400. Validate the body (e.g. with zod) and wrap the decrypt/parse in a try/catch returning `ErrorCode.InternalServerError`.

title: missing_backup_codes message points users to a settings page that cannot generate codes
body: "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." is shown to any user whose `backupCodes` column is null — which is every user who enabled 2FA before this migration, since there is no backfill. There is no UI anywhere in this PR that generates backup codes for an already-enabled 2FA account; the only way to obtain codes is to disable and re-enable 2FA. The message therefore instructs users to perform an action that does not exist. Either add a regenerate action or change the text to describe the actual recovery path.

title: No test covers the security-critical backup code verification paths
body: The only new coverage is the download/copy/close buttons of the backup-code dialog. The actual new logic — logging in with a backup code, rejecting an incorrect code, the single-use invalidation in `next-auth-options.ts`, and disabling 2FA with a backup code in `totp/disable.ts` — is completely untested (the PR itself notes this as a TODO). Given that these paths grant account access and mutate the stored code list, at least a happy-path login-with-backup-code test plus a replay test (same code rejected the second time) should be added before merge.

title: Assertion on isChecked() always passes, FIXME left in place
body: `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on the returned Promise object, which is always truthy, so this step can never fail — exactly as the newly added FIXME comment says. Since the correct form is already used in the sibling test (`[data-state="checked"]` locator) or `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()`, fix the assertion rather than documenting it; as-is the first test silently stops verifying that 2FA was actually enabled.

title: tabIndex={-1} makes the password show/hide toggle keyboard-inaccessible
body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the reveal button removes it from the tab order for every `PasswordField` in the app, not just the 2FA modals. Keyboard-only and switch-device users can no longer toggle password visibility at all (the `sr-only` label does not help because the control cannot be focused). If the goal was to keep Enter on the password field from activating the button, note the button is already `type="button"`, so removing focusability is not needed.

title: Backup-code blob URL is never revoked when the modal closes
body: `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` is only revoked when a new setup run creates another URL (line 98). `resetState()` and unmounting do not revoke it, so the blob containing the plaintext backup codes stays alive for the lifetime of the document and remains fetchable from its `blob:` URL after the dialog is closed. Revoke the URL in `resetState()` and in a cleanup effect on unmount.

title: Google Meet fallback dereferences undefined destination calendar
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` whenever the event has no destination calendar (empty array or null), and the next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. This expression is evaluated exactly in the case the check exists for – a booking whose location is Google Meet while the organizer has no Google Calendar/destination calendar – so instead of falling back to Cal Video the booking creation throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`. The previous code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` and was null-safe. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

title: Video booking references no longer store credentialId
body: In `create()`, `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the credentialId for every non-calendar (i.e. video) result; the previous code stored `result.credentialId` for those. Downstream code relies on it: `handleCancelBooking` only deletes the meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, and seat cancellation only calls `updateMeeting` for references with a credentialId. With this change Zoom/Teams/etc. meetings will silently never be deleted or updated on cancellation for newly created bookings. Keep `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results.

title: updateLocation references lose externalCalendarId/credentialId
body: `referencesToCreate` in `updateLocation()` now takes `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent()` (the source of these results) returns an object that contains neither `externalId` nor `credentialId`. Since `editLocation.handler` persists these references (`references: { create: updatedResult.referencesToCreate }`), every reference created after a location edit will have `externalCalendarId = null` and `credentialId = null`, which makes later reschedules/cancellations fall back to the "primary" calendar instead of the real destination calendar. Previously the values were taken from `evt.destinationCalendar`.

title: updateEvent fallback lookup can never match (calendarId becomes undefined)
body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` – the `find` branch is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares `cal.externalId === undefined` and always returns `undefined`. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. As a result, whenever a booking reference has no `externalCalendarId`, `calendar.events.update()` is called with `calendarId: undefined` instead of the destination calendar, so the update targets the wrong calendar or fails.

title: deleteEvent fallback lookup can never match, silently deletes from primary
body: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the comparison is always `=== undefined` and yields `undefined`. The code then falls back to `defaultCalendarId = "primary"`, so for bookings without a stored `externalCalendarId` the delete is issued against the user's primary calendar rather than the configured destination calendar. Google answers 404, which this service resolves silently, leaving the real event in the calendar forever.

title: events.patch called with possibly undefined calendarId
body: `selectedCalendar` is now `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and can legitimately be `undefined`; the insert call compensates with `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar, ... })` that writes the hangout link into the description uses the raw value. When no destination calendar matches the credential, this patch request is made with `calendarId: undefined` and fails, so Google Meet links are missing from the event description.

title: createEvent now ignores destination calendars without a credentialId
body: The calendar to write to is selected with `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`. Destination calendar rows whose `credentialId` is null (legacy rows, and the branch in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` that calls `createEvent(c, event)` for destinations without a credentialId) will not match, so `calendarId` silently defaults to `"primary"`. Previously the first destination calendar's `externalId` was used. Users with a non-primary destination calendar and a credential-less destination row will get their bookings written into the wrong calendar, and the booking reference stores no `externalCalendarId` (nothing is passed to `createEvent`), breaking later updates/deletes.

title: Collective host destination calendars dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null
body: `destinationCalendar` is now built as `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [...] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [...] : null`, and the collective hosts are appended with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar the value is `null`, the optional-chained `push` is a no-op, and all co-hosts' destination calendars are silently discarded – exactly the multi-host case this PR is meant to fix. Initialize the array (e.g. `[]`) and assign/concat instead of relying on `?.push`.

title: loadUsers for dynamic bookings no longer selects organization slug
body: The rewritten `loadUsers()` dropped `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the Prisma select used for dynamic (no eventTypeId) bookings, while the host-based branch still returns users that carry organization data. Any downstream use of `user.organization` (booker URL / org-domain link building) now gets `undefined` for dynamic group bookings, and the union of the two return shapes also loses the property from the inferred `users` type. Re-add the `organization` selection.

title: Recurring cancellation duplicates deletes and misses extra calendar references
body: The recurring-event deletion block now lives inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. For a booking with N calendar references (the multi-host case this PR introduces) the same "delete all credentials × all updated bookings" work is executed N times, issuing N duplicate delete requests per event. At the same time the inner lookup is still `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`, i.e. only the first calendar reference of each recurring booking is ever deleted, so the second host's calendar events are left behind. The loop should be entered once and should iterate over all calendar references of each updated booking.

title: Organization slug assignment logic inverted
body: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` was changed to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which inverts the condition. With team billing enabled the slug is now claimed immediately (it was intentionally only stored as `metadata.requestedSlug` until payment), and with billing disabled (self-hosted / dev) the organization is created with a `null` slug, breaking org subdomain resolution and the org URL for every newly created organization. This change is also unrelated to the destinationCalendar refactor in this PR.

title: updateAllCalendarEvents error message is built but never logged
body: The catch block still composes the diagnostic `message` (including credential type, userId and bookingId) but the `console.error(message)` call was removed, so calendar update failures now return the generic failure results with no trace in the logs. Either log it again or drop the dead string construction.

title: No tests for multi destination calendar creation/update paths
body: This PR changes the core contract (`CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` becomes an array) and rewrites `createAllCalendarEvents`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` to loop over several destinations and to look credentials up from the DB, plus it changes how `referencesToCreate` is derived. No unit test covers: (a) several destination calendars producing one reference each with the right `externalCalendarId`/`credentialId`, (b) an empty/null `destinationCalendar`, (c) a destination whose credential is not owned by the organizer. Given the regressions these paths feed (cancellation/reschedule rely on the stored references), at least handler-level tests for the collective case should accompany the change.

title: createEvent credentialId made a required parameter
body: `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` now declares a mandatory second argument on the public `Calendar` interface. Every caller that still invokes `calendar.createEvent(event)` (including third-party/app-store code built against this interface) fails to compile, even though all implementations except Google ignore the parameter. Making it optional (`credentialId?: number`) would keep the interface backwards compatible.

title: Organization slug logic inverted (unrelated change)
body: The condition for setting the team `slug` was flipped from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. Now, when team billing is disabled (the default for self-hosted instances), the organization is created with no `slug` at all, so the org has no resolvable subdomain/URL; and when billing is enabled both `slug` and `metadata.requestedSlug` are written, which contradicts the "requested slug until paid" flow. This change is also unrelated to the destinationCalendar refactor and should be reverted.

title: TypeError when Google Meet is selected and there is no destination calendar
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` can yield `undefined` (handleNewBooking explicitly sets `destinationCalendar: null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one). The next line dereferences it unconditionally: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. For any booking with location `integrations:google:meet` and no destination calendar, this throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` and the whole booking creation fails. Use optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`).

title: Video booking references lose their credentialId
body: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` replaces the previous `isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`. For video results (non-calendar) the credentialId coming from `createMeeting` is now discarded, so `BookingReference` rows for `*_video` are stored with `credentialId: null`. handleCancelBooking only deletes the meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so cancelling a booking will no longer delete the video meeting; other code paths that resolve the video credential from the reference are affected too. Keep `result.credentialId` for the non-calendar branch.

title: updateEvent fallback calendar lookup is a no-op, yielding undefined calendarId
body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — the `find` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, and it compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e. against undefined/null), so it can never match. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Result: for any booking reference without `externalCalendarId` (legacy bookings, or references created by the new fallback paths that no longer set it), `calendar.events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined`, so reschedules/updates fail. The fallback should be the first/matching destination calendar's `externalId`.

title: deleteEvent fallback silently targets "primary" instead of the destination calendar
body: Same broken lookup as in updateEvent: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so `calendarId` becomes undefined and the code falls back to `"primary"`. Previously the destination calendar's `externalId` was used. When cancelling a booking whose reference lacks `externalCalendarId`, Google will return 404 for the event in `primary` (which the handler swallows), leaving the real event in the user's destination calendar undeleted and the slot blocked.

title: hangoutLink patch uses possibly-undefined calendarId while insert used "primary"
body: The insert call now uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` (used to rewrite the description with the Meet hangout link) still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. When no destination calendar matches the credential, `selectedCalendar` is undefined, the event was created in `primary`, and the patch request is made with an undefined calendarId — the description never gets the meeting link and the error is unhandled (fire-and-forget promise rejection).

title: Destination calendars with a null credentialId now fall back to "primary"
body: `selectedCalendar` is resolved only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable, and EventManager's new else-branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` (no externalId) for exactly those rows, so the find never matches and the event is created in `primary` instead of the configured destination calendar. Combined with `createEvent` being called without `externalId`, the resulting booking reference also has `externalCalendarId: undefined`, which then breaks subsequent update/delete (see the broken fallbacks in updateEvent/deleteEvent). Keep a fallback to the destination calendar's `externalId` when no credentialId match exists.

title: Team hosts' destination calendars are dropped when there is no primary destination calendar
body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` is a no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, which is exactly the case when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that situation a COLLECTIVE event with co-hosts who do have destination calendars will create no host calendar events at all (EventManager then falls into the `cred.type === "calendar"` legacy fallback, which never matches) — i.e. the bug this PR intends to fix is still present for that configuration. Build the array unconditionally (e.g. start from `[]` and push) instead of relying on optional chaining. Note also that when `eventType.destinationCalendar` is set, the organizer's personal calendar is intentionally excluded while every other host's personal calendar is added, which is an inconsistent semantic worth confirming.

title: destinationCalendar payload shape is inconsistent (null vs [])
body: handleNewBooking emits `destinationCalendar: null` when no calendar is configured, while every other producer changed in this PR (confirm.handler, handleCancelBooking, webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, bookingReminder.ts, requestReschedule) emits `[]`. The field is forwarded verbatim to webhook subscribers (see apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts, which now expects `[]` for BOOKING_REJECTED but `null` for BOOKING_CREATED/BOOKING_REQUESTED). This is a breaking payload change for existing webhook/API consumers (object -> array) and it is not even internally consistent; pick one representation and document the breaking change.

title: Dynamic-booking user query no longer selects `organization.slug`
body: The rewritten `loadUsers` drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-group `prisma.user.findMany` select that existed before. Any downstream use of `user.organization?.slug` (e.g. computing booker/organization URLs) will now see `undefined` for dynamic bookings, and the two branches of `loadUsers` now return structurally different shapes, which also weakens/breaks the type inference the comment "loadUsers allows type inferring" relies on. Restore the selection or justify its removal.

title: Stale `credential` reused across calendar references in updateAllCalendarEvents
body: `credential` is declared once outside the new `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop. If a reference has a `credentialId` that is neither in `this.calendarCredentials` nor resolvable from the DB (e.g. the credential row has no linked app slug), `credential` keeps the value from the previous iteration and `updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId)` is executed against the wrong account/credential — potentially writing one host's event into another host's calendar. On the first iteration it is `undefined`, which makes `updateEvent` throw. Declare `credential` inside the loop and skip the reference when it cannot be resolved.

title: Error message in updateAllCalendarEvents is computed but never logged
body: The catch block still builds the diagnostic `message` (including credential type, userId and bookingId) but the `console.error(message)` call was removed in this diff. Failures while updating calendar events now return `success: false` results with no trace in the logs, making reschedule/update failures undiagnosable.

title: Recurring-event deletion is repeated once per calendar reference
body: The recurring branch (iterating every user calendar credential × every updated booking reference) is now nested inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With N calendar references on the booking, the same set of deleteEvent calls is issued N times, producing N× API calls to every calendar provider and repeated 404/410 responses. The recurring-cancellation block does not depend on `reference` at all and should be hoisted out of the per-reference loop.

title: Non-Google calendar services still only read destinationCalendar[0], so secondary hosts get the wrong calendar
body: EventManager now calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` once per destination with the *full* destinationCalendar array, but only GoogleCalendarService resolves the entry matching the credential. CalDAV/Apple (this file), Office365 (`createEvent`, line 73) and Lark (lines 128/164) destructure `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and therefore target the *first* host's external calendar id while authenticated as another host. In CalDAV this filters the calendar list down to zero entries, `Promise.all([])` resolves, `responses.some(r => !r.ok)` is false, and the method reports success although no event was created; Office365 builds `/me/calendars/<other host's id>/events` and 404s. These services receive the `credentialId` argument now and should use it (or the passed `externalId`) to pick the right destination entry.

title: Calendar.createEvent second parameter made required
body: `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` makes `credentialId` mandatory on the public `Calendar` interface. Any caller outside `CalendarManager.createEvent` (including app-store calendar apps or external/consumer code implementing or invoking this interface) now fails type-checking, and most in-repo implementations ignore the parameter. Declaring it optional (`credentialId?: number`) would keep the contract backwards compatible.

title: No tests for the new multi-destination-calendar behaviour
body: This PR changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array across ~20 files and adds non-trivial branching (per-destination credential resolution with DB fallback, per-reference update/delete loops, collective host calendar aggregation) yet adds no unit/integration tests. The only test change is flipping one e2e expectation from `null` to `[]`, which leaves the other two webhook expectations asserting the old shape. Please add coverage for: collective event with two hosts each having a destination calendar, destination calendar rows with a null credentialId, and cancel/reschedule of a booking with multiple calendar references.

title: Crash when Google Meet is selected and no destination calendar exists
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the event has no destination calendars (e.g. `handleNewBooking` now sets `destinationCalendar: null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one). The next line then dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`, throwing a TypeError. This is exactly the code path the check was written for (Google Meet selected without a Google Calendar), so instead of falling back to Cal Video the whole booking request now fails with a 500. Needs optional access (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`).

title: Video booking references lose credentialId, breaking meeting deletion/updates
body: In `create()`, `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` replaces the previous `isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`. For non-calendar (video) results the credentialId is now always `undefined`, so `BookingReference` rows of type `*_video` are persisted without a credentialId. `handleCancelBooking` only deletes the meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set (`if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)`), and seat cancellation/update paths also key off `reference.credentialId`. Result: video meetings created after this change are never cancelled or updated on the provider.

title: updateLocation writes references with an always-undefined externalCalendarId
body: `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` is used for the references created by `updateLocation()`, but `updateEvent()` in `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts` never sets `externalId` on its returned `EventResult` (only `createEvent` does). So `result.externalId` is always `undefined` here and the new `BookingReference` rows lose the external calendar id that was previously taken from `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Later cancel/reschedule flows that rely on `reference.externalCalendarId` will then fall back to the provider's primary calendar and fail to find the event.

title: Destination calendars without credentialId lose their externalId in references and events
body: In `createAllCalendarEvents`, the branch for a destination without `credentialId` calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing `destination.externalId`. Because `EventResult.externalId` is what now populates `referencesToCreate.externalCalendarId` (see line 169), those bookings get references with no external calendar id. Combined with the Google service now resolving the target calendar by `credentialId` match only, such events are also created in `"primary"` instead of the configured destination calendar. Previously `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId` was used for both the reference and the target calendar.

title: updateAllCalendarEvents failures are now silently swallowed
body: The `console.error(message)` call was removed from the catch block, but `message` is still built from the error. Any failure while updating calendar events (including an `undefined` credential being passed to `updateEvent`) now returns fake failed results with no log line at all, making production diagnosis of calendar update failures impossible.

title: updateEvent fallback calendar lookup can never match
body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — the `find` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares `cal.externalId === undefined` and always returns `undefined`. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Consequently `calendar.events.update({ calendarId: undefined })` is issued whenever no external calendar id is stored on the booking reference, so updates/reschedules of events living in a non-primary destination calendar fail.

title: deleteEvent always falls back to 'primary' calendar
body: Same dead-condition as in `updateEvent`: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it always yields `undefined` and `calendarId` becomes `defaultCalendarId` (`"primary"`). Previously the destination calendar's `externalId` was used. Cancellations for bookings stored in a non-primary Google calendar will now hit the primary calendar, return 404 (swallowed as success) and leave the real event in place.

title: events.patch is called with a possibly undefined calendarId
body: `selectedCalendar` can now be `undefined` (the `|| "primary"` default was only applied inline at the `events.insert` call). The follow-up `calendar.events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar, ... })` that writes the hangout link into the description still uses the raw value, producing a malformed request URL when no destination calendar matches the credential. The promise is not awaited or caught, so this fails silently and the Meet link is missing from the event description.

title: createEvent target calendar now resolved only by credentialId match
body: `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` replaces the former `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable, and `EventManager` reaches this service via the no-credentialId branch for such rows (passing no credential match), so for every destination calendar with a null `credentialId` the event is now created in `"primary"` instead of the user-selected calendar — a silent regression for existing single-host setups.

title: CalDAV createEvent reports success while creating nothing for secondary hosts
body: `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates every destination calendar and calls `createEvent` with that host's credential, but this service still filters the account's calendars against `destinationCalendar[0]` (the main host). When invoked with a second host's credential, no calendar URL matches, `responses` is an empty array, `responses.some((r) => !r.ok)` is false, and the method returns a success result with a fresh uid even though no event was created on any calendar. The booking reference is stored and the host never gets the event, with no error surfaced.

title: Office365 createEvent always uses the first host's calendar id
body: Only `destinationCalendar[0]` is honoured. With the new multi-destination flow, `EventManager` calls `createEvent` once per destination using that destination's owner credential; for the second host this builds `/me/calendars/<first host's calendar id>/events` while authenticating as the second host, which 404s (or writes to the wrong calendar if ids happen to collide). The service should select the destination matching the credential it was constructed with (as the Google service now does via the new `credentialId` argument).

title: Lark createEvent/createAttendees always use the first host's calendar
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` is used for the calendar id in `createEvent`, `createAttendees`, `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`. Since `EventManager` now invokes these once per destination calendar with the corresponding host's credential, every host's run targets the first host's calendar id, producing duplicate events on the main host's calendar (or API errors) and no event on the other hosts' calendars.

title: Collective team destination calendars are dropped when no primary destination exists
body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining, but `destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists. In that case the collected co-host destination calendars are silently discarded and the very bug this PR targets (collective hosts not getting calendar events) remains for teams whose organizer has no destination calendar. Initialise the array (e.g. `[]`) before pushing.

title: organization relation dropped from the dynamic-booking user select
body: The rewritten `loadUsers` removes `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the `prisma.user.findMany` select used for dynamic (no eventTypeId) bookings, while the host-based branch keeps whatever the event type query selected. Any downstream use of `user.organization` for dynamic group bookings now sees `undefined` (and the two branches no longer return the same shape, so the inferred union type changes). This change is unrelated to the destinationCalendar fix and should be reverted unless the field is provably unused.

title: Recurring cancellation deletes every event once per calendar reference
body: The recurring/`allRemainingBookings` block, which already loops over all of the user's calendar credentials and all updated bookings, is now nested inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With N calendar references the same delete calls are issued N times (N × credentials × bookings), multiplying provider API calls and rate-limit risk; the outer `calendar` instance created from `calendarCredential` is also unused in that branch. The recurring branch should run once, outside the per-reference loop.

title: Organization slug assignment logic inverted
body: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` was changed to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. This inverts the intent: with team billing enabled the slug is now set immediately *and* duplicated into `metadata.requestedSlug` (the slug is supposed to be claimed only after payment), while with billing disabled the organization is created with no slug at all, leaving it unreachable by its subdomain. This change is also unrelated to the destinationCalendar fix in this PR.

title: Webhook/CalendarEvent payload shape changed from object to array without versioning
body: `destinationCalendar` changes from `DestinationCalendar | null` to `DestinationCalendar[] | null`. This field is forwarded verbatim to webhook subscribers via `sendPayload` (see the e2e expectations, which now mix `destinationCalendar: null` for BOOKING_CREATED/REQUESTED and `[]` for BOOKING_REJECTED).
