External consumers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` will break, and the payload is now inconsistent (`null` vs `[]` vs array) depending on the code path. The shape should be normalised and the breaking payload change documented.

title: No tests for the new multi-destination calendar fan-out
body: `createAllCalendarEvents`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` now loop over an array of destination calendars, fetch foreign credentials from the DB and build one reference per created event, and every provider service was touched. The only test change in the PR is flipping one e2e expectation from `null` to `[]`. There is no unit/integration coverage asserting that a collective event with two hosts creates exactly one event per host calendar, that references carry the right `credentialId`/`externalCalendarId`, or that the single-host fallback is unchanged — all of which the findings above show are currently broken for several providers.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService
body: `getClient()` now calls `prisma.credential.update({...})`, but the file imports no Prisma client (only `getLocation`, `WEBAPP_URL`, `HttpError`, `logger`, types, `getAppKeysFromSlug`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`). `prisma` is therefore an undefined identifier: TypeScript type-check/build will fail, and at runtime every instantiation of `SalesforceCalendarService` throws a `ReferenceError`, breaking all Salesforce bookings. Add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`.

title: Google credential key is overwritten with a Zod safeParse result wrapper
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns the raw `safeParse` result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed object, yet the return value is written straight into the DB: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); await prisma.credential.update({ ..., data: { key } })`. Previously the code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`. After this change the stored credential key becomes `{"success":true,"data":{...}}`, so the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails and the user's Google Calendar credential is permanently broken. The value should be `...data` (and the helper should return the parsed data, not the wrapper).

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema is not a valid schema and silently strips all token fields
body: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both stringify a ZodType object to the same literal key (`"[object Object]"`), so the schema is effectively `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown }`. It therefore (a) never validates that an expiry field exists, despite the comment, and (b) because Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, the returned `data` contains only `access_token` — `refresh_token`, `expires_in`/`expiry_date`, `scope`, `instance_url`, `api_domain`, etc. are discarded. Any caller that persists this data (Google, Office365, Zoom) loses the fields it needs: e.g. Zoom computes `expiry_date = Date.now() + undefined * 1000` → `NaN`, after which `isTokenValid` never triggers a refresh again. Use an explicit schema such as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), expires_in: z.number().optional(), expiry_date: z.number().optional() }).passthrough()`.

title: Placeholder string overwrites a valid refresh token
body: `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token";` injects the literal string `"refresh_token"` whenever the provider response omits a refresh token — and it does this unconditionally, even when credential sharing is disabled. In `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the result is merged into the stored key (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`) and `refresh_token` is optional in `refreshTokenResponseSchema`, so a refresh response without a new refresh token will replace the user's real Microsoft refresh token with the garbage value, permanently breaking that credential. Only fill in a placeholder when the credential-sync path is active, and never let it clobber an existing refresh token.

title: Sync endpoint returns a fetch Response where callers expect axios/SDK response shapes
body: When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, this helper always returns a `fetch` `Response`, but several call sites expect the shape their original client returned: `zoho-bigin` and `zohocrm` read `tokenInfo.data.error` / `tokenInfo.data.access_token` (axios), `hubspot` expects a `HubspotToken` object with `accessToken`/`expiresIn`, and `googlecalendar` reads `res?.data`. With sync enabled these all dereference `undefined` (TypeError, or `NaN` expiry and `setAccessToken(undefined)`), so token refresh fails exactly in the mode this PR adds. The helper needs to normalise the response per app (e.g. return parsed JSON and have each caller adapt) rather than leaking two different return types.

title: Credential sync request carries no authentication and its status is never checked
body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no shared secret, signature, or auth header, so the self-hoster's endpoint has no way to verify the caller; anyone who learns the URL can request access tokens for arbitrary Cal.com user ids. The inbound direction (`/api/webhook/app-credential`) does use `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, so the asymmetry is clearly unintended. Additionally, `response.ok` is never checked, so a 4xx/5xx HTML error body is passed on to the per-app parsing code, producing confusing downstream failures instead of a clear error.

title: Credential id passed where the user id is expected in Zoho Bigin refresh
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(fn, "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument, but that parameter is `userId` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. With credential sharing enabled the self-hoster's endpoint will be asked for the tokens of whatever user happens to have id == credential id, i.e. the wrong user's credentials get fetched and stored (potential cross-account token leak). `refreshAccessToken` must receive and forward `credential.userId`.

title: Wrong app slug ("zoomvideo") sent to the credential sync endpoint
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoomvideo", credential.userId)` uses the app's directory name, not its slug. The Zoom app's slug is `zoom` (see `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts`, which creates the credential with `appId: "zoom"`, and the `App.slug` row used by the new `/api/webhook/app-credential` endpoint). A self-hoster's endpoint keyed on the Cal.com app slug will not recognise `zoomvideo`, so Zoom token sync silently fails.

title: appStoreMetadata is indexed by slug, but it is keyed by app dirName
body: `appStoreMetadata[app.slug as keyof typeof appStoreMetadata]` casts the slug to a key of the generated metadata map, which is keyed by app directory name. For every app whose dirName differs from its slug — `googlecalendar`/`google-calendar`, `office365calendar`/`office365-calendar`, `zoomvideo`/`zoom`, `office365video`/`msteams` — the lookup returns `undefined` and the handler responds 404 "App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug". Those are precisely the apps this feature targets, so the webhook is unusable for them. Resolve the metadata via a slug lookup (e.g. `getAppFromSlug`) or by the app's `dirName`.

title: Unvalidated input and decryption errors surface as unhandled 500s
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a `ZodError` for a malformed payload, and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...))` throws when the key is wrong or the ciphertext/JSON is invalid. Neither is caught, so callers get an opaque 500 (with a stack trace in the server logs and, in dev, the response) instead of a 400 with an actionable message, making integration debugging hard for self-hosters. Use `safeParse` plus a try/catch around decryption and return 400.

title: No HTTP method restriction and non-constant-time secret comparison
body: The handler accepts any HTTP method (GET, DELETE, …) and compares the webhook secret with `!==` on the raw header value. A method guard (`POST` only) prevents accidental credential writes from GET/prefetch traffic, and `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers avoids leaking the secret through response-time differences on a write-capable, unauthenticated-by-default endpoint.

title: Custom webhook header name is case-sensitive
body: `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]` relies on the operator configuring the name in lowercase, because Node lowercases incoming header names. If a self-hoster sets `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME="Calcom-Webhook-Secret"` the lookup yields `undefined` and every request is rejected with "Invalid webhook secret" with no hint why. Apply `.toLowerCase()` to the configured name instead of relying on the .env comment.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED evaluates to the encryption key, not a boolean
body: `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` returns the value of `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` when both are set, so this exported "flag" is actually the secret string. `packages/lib/constants.ts` is imported broadly (including from client-reachable modules), so any place that logs or serialises this constant leaks the AES key. Wrap it in `!!(...)` so only a boolean is exported.

title: Salesforce token is refreshed on every instantiation and the stale token is still used
body: `getClient()` is called from the constructor and now unconditionally POSTs to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` with `grant_type=refresh_token`, regardless of whether the stored access token is still valid — an extra Salesforce round trip (and API-limit consumption) for every service construction, e.g. on each availability/booking path. Worse, after refreshing and persisting the new token the returned `jsforce.Connection` is still built with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token` and `instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url` from the old key, so the freshly obtained token is discarded and requests may run with an expired token. Gate the refresh on expiry and build the connection from the refreshed values. (Note the `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` branch below is dead code, since `parseRefreshTokenResponse` already throws on failure.)

title: Token refresh success detected via `statusText === "OK"`
body: `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)` is unreliable: `statusText` is an empty string for HTTP/2 responses (undici) and may carry other reason phrases for 2xx responses, so a successful refresh can be rejected with an empty error message while a non-2xx body could slip through. Check `response.ok` / `response.status` instead.

title: Apps wired to refreshOAuthTokens still validate with provider-specific strict schemas
body: Webex (and likewise `larkcalendar` via `handleLarkError`, `office365video`, `hubspot`, `zohocrm`, `zoho-bigin`) now call `refreshOAuthTokens`, but still parse the result with the provider's own strict contract — here `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` requires `refresh_token`, a literal `scope` of `"spark:kms meeting:schedules_read meeting:schedules_write"` and `token_type: "Bearer"`. The documented sync-endpoint contract ("The response should only contain the access token and expiry date") cannot satisfy these schemas, so with credential sharing enabled refresh fails ("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned") or yields `NaN` expiry dates. These call sites need to go through `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (once it is fixed) or the feature should be documented as unsupported for them.

title: Webhook silently overwrites one of several credentials for the same user and app
body: The upsert uses `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })`. Users can legitimately have more than one credential for the same app (e.g. two Google Calendar accounts); the webhook will overwrite whichever row is returned first and leave the others stale, with no indication to the caller. The payload has no way to target a specific credential, so consider including an external identifier/account email in the schema or documenting the single-credential-per-app assumption.

title: No tests for the new credential-sync webhook or token parsing helper
body: The PR adds an unauthenticated-by-default write endpoint that creates/updates OAuth credentials plus a shared `parseRefreshTokenResponse`/`refreshOAuthTokens` layer used by ~10 apps, with no unit or integration tests. Given that the helpers currently mis-handle schemas and return types (see other findings), at minimum there should be tests covering: rejected requests when sharing is disabled / secret mismatch, slug→metadata resolution for apps whose dirName differs from the slug, credential create vs update, and that `parseRefreshTokenResponse` preserves `refresh_token`/expiry in both sharing modes.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService
body: The newly added block calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` at line 96, but this module has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` (see the import list at lines 1-20). This is a TypeScript compile error and, at runtime, a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` that will be thrown on every `getClient()` call, i.e. on every Salesforce event create/update/delete. The Salesforce app is completely broken by this change.

title: Google Calendar credential key is overwritten with the zod safeParse wrapper object
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns the result of `schema.safeParse(...)`, i.e. `{ success: true, data: {...} }`, not the parsed data. Here `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` is passed straight into `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so after the first token refresh the stored credential key becomes `{"success":true,"data":{...}}` instead of the token object. `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` will then fail for that credential forever, breaking Google Calendar for every user whose token refreshes. Previously the code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (the data). Either return `.data` from the helper or use `key.data` here.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token"
body: When the refreshed token response has no `refresh_token`, the helper sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Callers merge this data into the stored credential, e.g. office365calendar does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }` and persists it, and zoomvideo does `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token`. Providers that legitimately omit `refresh_token` on refresh (Microsoft, and any provider in credential-sync mode) will therefore have their valid stored refresh token overwritten with the garbage value `"refresh_token"`, permanently breaking the integration for that user. The old code kept the previous refresh token because the field was optional.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys are a no-op and expiry is never validated
body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` do not create dynamic keys: `toString()` on a Zod schema yields `"[object Object]"`, so the object literal ends up being `{ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() }` (the second computed key overwrites the first). The documented intent ("assume that any property with a number is the expiry") is not implemented, so in credential-sharing mode nothing but `access_token` is validated. Concretely, zoomvideo then computes `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000)` with `expires_in` undefined → `NaN`, and because `isTokenValid` compares `NaN < Date.now()` (false), the adapter will keep returning the stale access token and never refresh again.

title: Credential-sync branch returns a raw fetch Response while callers expect provider-specific shapes
body: In the sync branch the helper returns the `Response` object from `fetch(CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT)`, but the non-sync branch returns whatever the provider client returns, and callers rely on those shapes: googlecalendar reads `res?.data` (gaxios response), zoho-bigin and zohocrm read `tokenInfo.data.error` / `tokenInfo.data.access_token` (axios response), hubspot casts the result directly to `HubspotToken` and reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`, and larkcalendar passes it to `handleLarkError` expecting `{code, data}`. With credential sharing enabled these paths will throw `TypeError`s or persist nonsense (e.g. hubspot writes a `Response` object as the credential key and an `NaN` expiryDate). The helper should normalise the sync response into the same shape each caller expects, and should also check `response.ok` before returning.

title: Zoho Bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects a userId
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFn, "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` — the third parameter of `refreshOAuthTokens` is `userId` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. Passing the credential's primary key means the self-hosted endpoint is asked for the tokens of an unrelated user id (credential ids and user ids are different sequences), so the wrong user's access token can be fetched and stored on this credential, leaking access to a third party's Bigin account. `refreshAccessToken` must receive and forward `credential.userId`.

title: appStoreMetadata is keyed by app directory name, not slug, so most apps resolve to 404
body: `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` assumes the metadata map is keyed by slug, but `@calcom/app-store/appStoreMetaData` is keyed by the app's directory name (e.g. `googlecalendar`, `office365calendar`, `zoomvideo`), which differs from the DB slug (`google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `zoom`). For every app whose dirName != slug the lookup returns `undefined` and the webhook responds 404 "App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug", making credential sync unusable for exactly the apps this PR wires up. Look the app up by iterating the metadata values and matching `slug`, or select `dirName` from the `app` row.

title: Salesforce refreshes the token on every call but then connects with the old access token
body: `getClient()` now unconditionally POSTs a `refresh_token` grant to Salesforce on every instantiation (i.e. for every createEvent/updateEvent/deleteEvent), ignoring whether the stored token is still valid, and then builds the `jsforce.Connection` with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token` — the *old* token from the credential — instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`. So the refresh achieves nothing for the current request while adding a network round trip and burning Salesforce refresh-grant rate limits on every booking operation. Gate the refresh on expiry and use the newly obtained access token/instance URL for the connection.

title: Zoom passes "zoomvideo" as the app slug to the sync endpoint
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoomvideo", credential.userId)` sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, but the Zoom app's slug (and the `appId` stored on the credential, see `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` which creates `{ appId: "zoom" }`) is `zoom`. A self-hoster's sync endpoint keyed on the Cal.com app slug will not recognise `zoomvideo`, so Zoom token sync silently fails or returns the wrong app's credentials. The slug argument should match the app slug used everywhere else (`zoom`).

title: Unvalidated input paths throw unhandled exceptions (500 + stack traces)
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` (line 31), `symmetricDecrypt(...)` (line 57) and `JSON.parse(...)` (line 57) all throw on malformed input, and nothing wraps them in try/catch, so a bad body, a wrong encryption key, or non-JSON plaintext produces an unhandled rejection and a generic 500 instead of a 400 with a useful message. There is also no HTTP method check, so a plain GET to this route (no body) hits the same crash path. Use `safeParse`, wrap the decrypt/parse in try/catch, and reject non-POST requests.

title: findFirst ignores users with multiple credentials for the same app
body: A user can legitimately have several credentials for one app (e.g. two Google Calendar accounts, multiple Zoom accounts). `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` picks an arbitrary one and overwrites its `key` with the synced tokens, silently corrupting the other account's credential (its calendar/video calls will then act on the wrong external account) and never creating a second credential when one is genuinely needed. The payload has no way to identify which credential is meant; consider including an external account identifier or the credential id in the webhook payload.

title: Synced credential update does not clear the `invalid` flag
body: When a credential was previously marked `invalid: true` (e.g. Google Calendar's `invalid_grant` handling, or `invalidateCredential` in the Zoom/Webex adapters), the update at lines 73-80 only writes `key`. The credential stays flagged invalid, so Cal.com keeps showing the app as broken and keeps skipping it even though fresh, working tokens were just synced in. The update should also set `invalid: false`.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED evaluates to the encryption key string instead of a boolean
body: `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` returns the value of `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` when both are set, so this exported "flag" actually holds a secret. Any place that logs, serialises, or returns this constant (it is a general-purpose constants module imported widely) would disclose the credential encryption key. Wrap it in `!!(...)` so the exported value is a boolean.

title: Webex wraps refreshOAuthTokens but still validates with the strict provider schema
body: The refresh call now goes through `refreshOAuthTokens` (so it can hit the credential-sync endpoint), but the response is still validated with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse`, which requires `refresh_token`, `refresh_token_expires_in` and a literal `scope`/`token_type`. The sync endpoint is documented in `refreshOAuthTokens` to return "only the access token and expiry date", so in credential-sharing mode this parse always fails and the refresh rejects with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" — Webex can never be synced. Either use `parseRefreshTokenResponse` here as the other adapters do, or don't route Webex through the sync helper.

title: Salesforce refresh uses statusText equality and a hardcoded login host
body: `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` is an unreliable success check: fetch implementations return an empty `statusText` for HTTP/2 responses, which would make a successful refresh throw `HttpError` with an empty message. Use `!response.ok` instead. Additionally the token endpoint is hardcoded to `https://login.salesforce.com`, which fails for sandbox/My Domain orgs (`test.salesforce.com` / instance URL); the stored `credentialKey.instance_url` or a configurable host should be used.

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality
body: The shared secret check uses `!==` on the raw header value. For a secret-equality check on an unauthenticated endpoint, a constant-time comparison (`crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers) is preferable to avoid leaking information about the secret through response timing. Also note the header lookup relies on the configured name being lowercase (Node lowercases incoming header keys); normalising with `.toLowerCase()` would avoid a silent 403 if a self-hoster configures `Calcom-Webhook-Secret`.

title: Outlook token-refresh error diagnostics were removed
body: The previous code logged the zod error and the raw Microsoft response when the refresh response failed validation. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` now throws a generic `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` with no provider payload, and the surrounding code no longer logs anything, making Outlook refresh failures (a common support issue) effectively undebuggable. Include the validation error / response body in the thrown error or log it before throwing.

title: No tests for the new credential-sync webhook or the token-parsing helpers
body: This PR adds a new unauthenticated-by-default HTTP endpoint that writes third-party OAuth credentials into the database, plus two shared helpers (`parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens`) that every OAuth app now depends on, with no unit or integration tests. Given the bugs reachable in these code paths (wrong metadata key lookup, safeParse wrapper persisted as a credential key, `refresh_token` defaulting to a literal string), tests covering secret rejection, disabled-feature rejection, create vs. update behaviour, and the sync/non-sync branches of the helpers should accompany the change.

title: Google credential key is overwritten with a zod safeParse result object
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns a zod `safeParse` result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed credential. The old code was `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`, which returned the keys themselves. Now `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` persists `{"success":true,"data":{...}}` as the credential key. After the first access-token refresh, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in `googleAuth()` will fail and the user's Google Calendar integration is permanently broken until they reconnect. Either return `.data` from the helper or use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` here.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema is built from invalid computed keys and strips all other fields
body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` do not produce dynamic key matchers: `ZodString.toString()` yields the string "[object Object]", so both computed properties collapse into a single literal key `"[object Object]"` (the second definition overwriting the first). The schema therefore only validates `{ access_token: string }`, the intended "any numeric property is the expiry" rule is never applied, and — because zod objects strip unknown keys — every other field of the sync-endpoint response (expiry/expiry_date, refresh_token, instance_url, api_domain, scope, token_type) is dropped from `data`. Downstream this corrupts stored credentials, e.g. zoomvideo sets `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000)` → `NaN`, office365 never updates its expiry, and salesforce persists a key without `instance_url`. Use `.passthrough()` plus an explicit expiry field, or validate per-app.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token"
body: When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the helper injects the literal string `"refresh_token"`. This value is then written to the DB by callers that merge the parse result into the stored key — e.g. `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` does `{...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data}` and `zoomvideo` does `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token`. Microsoft's refresh response legitimately may omit `refresh_token` (the schema marks it `optional()`), in which case the previously valid refresh token is destroyed and the credential can never be refreshed again — the user must re-install the app. The dummy value should never be persisted; preserve the existing refresh token instead.

title: Sync path returns a raw fetch Response while several callers expect axios/googleapis shapes
body: In the credential-sharing branch the helper returns the `Response` object from `fetch`. Callers do not all consume a `Response`: `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` reads `res?.data` (googleapis style), `zoho-bigin` and `zohocrm` read `tokenInfo.data.error` / `tokenInfo.data.access_token` (axios style), `hubspot` reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` (already-parsed object), and `larkcalendar` passes it to `handleLarkError` which expects the Lark `{code, data}` envelope. With syncing enabled these paths throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` or silently compute `NaN` expiries, i.e. credential sync simply cannot work for those apps. The helper needs a single, documented return contract (e.g. always return parsed JSON) and the call sites must be adapted.

title: Request to the credential sync endpoint is unauthenticated and its status is never checked
body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` carries only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no shared secret, signature, or auth header, so the self-hoster's token-vending endpoint cannot verify that the caller is Cal.com — anyone who can reach that URL can request a user's access token. The inbound direction (`/api/webhook/app-credential`) does require `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; the outbound direction should be authenticated the same way. Additionally the response status is never checked (`response.ok`), so an error page/JSON from the endpoint flows into the token parsing and can be written to the credential.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService
body: `await prisma.credential.update(...)` is added in `getClient()` but the file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This is a type-check failure and, at runtime, a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` on every Salesforce calendar operation (the constructor calls `getClient`), breaking the Salesforce app entirely.

title: Salesforce refreshes the token on every request but then connects with the old access token
body: `getClient()` now unconditionally performs a `refresh_token` exchange on every instantiation of the service (no expiry check), yet the `jsforce.Connection` is still built with `credentialKey.access_token` / `credentialKey.instance_url` from the stale credential rather than the freshly obtained `accessTokenParsed.data`. The refresh therefore adds a blocking round trip (and Salesforce token-request rate-limit pressure) on every booking while not actually fixing an expired token. Use the newly returned `access_token`/`instance_url`, and only refresh when the stored token is expired.

title: Zoho Bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(fn, "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` — the third parameter of `refreshOAuthTokens` is `userId` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. Here the credential's primary key is passed instead of `credential.userId`, so with credential sharing enabled Cal.com asks the self-hosted endpoint for the tokens of a completely different (or non-existent) user, which at best fails and at worst installs another user's tokens on this credential. `refreshAccessToken` needs the userId plumbed through.

title: Zoom sends appSlug "zoomvideo" which is not the app's slug
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoomvideo", credential.userId)` sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, but the Zoom app's slug in the app store / `Credential.appId` is `zoom` (see `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts`, which creates the credential with `appId: "zoom"`), and the inbound webhook resolves apps by `prisma.app.slug`. The self-hoster therefore receives a slug that does not correspond to any Cal.com app id, so token sync for Zoom is keyed on the wrong identifier.

title: Webex wires refreshOAuthTokens but still validates with the strict provider schema
body: Webex now fetches tokens through `refreshOAuthTokens` (so a sync endpoint may answer with just an access token and expiry) yet still validates with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse`, which requires an exact `scope` literal, `token_type: "Bearer"`, `refresh_token` and `refresh_token_expires_in`. Any sync response will fail parsing and reject with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned", so Webex credential sharing cannot work. Either use `parseRefreshTokenResponse` here (as zoom/office365 do) or don't route Webex through the sync helper.

title: Webhook handler has no method guard and throws unhandled errors on bad input
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a `ZodError` for a malformed/absent body (e.g. any GET to this route), and `symmetricDecrypt` / `JSON.parse` throw for a wrong key or non-JSON plaintext. None of these are caught, so callers get a 500 with a Next.js error instead of a 4xx, and decryption stack traces end up in the logs. Add a `req.method !== "POST"` guard, use `safeParse`, and wrap the decrypt/parse in try/catch returning 400.

title: Webhook secret compared with `!==` and header name not lowercased
body: The shared secret is compared with a plain string comparison, which is not constant-time; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. Also, `req.headers` keys in Node are always lowercase, so if an operator sets `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` with any uppercase character the lookup silently returns `undefined` and every request is rejected with "Invalid webhook secret" — apply `.toLowerCase()` to the configured header name rather than relying on the comment in `.env.example`.

title: findFirst + create is ambiguous for multi-credential apps and racy
body: Credentials are not unique per (userId, appId): a user can legitimately have several credentials for the same app (e.g. two Google Calendar accounts, and `larkcalendar`/`zoomvideo` callbacks explicitly deal with duplicates). `findFirst` picks an arbitrary one and overwrites its key, and the payload has no way to identify which credential to update. Two concurrent webhook deliveries will also both miss the `findFirst` and create duplicate credentials. Consider requiring a credential identifier in the payload and/or performing the read-modify-write in a transaction.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED holds the encryption key value instead of a boolean
body: `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` evaluates to the value of `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (a secret) rather than `true`. The export is typed `string | undefined` and lives in a constants module that is imported broadly; any place that logs, serializes into props, or returns this constant would leak the AES key. Wrap it in `!!(...)` so only a boolean is ever exported.

title: Token refresh failure detected via `response.statusText !== "OK"`
body: Checking `statusText` is unreliable (it is empty for HTTP/2 responses and may differ per server), so a successful refresh can be rejected while the error message surfaced to the user is an empty string. Use `if (!response.ok)` and include the response body in the thrown error for diagnosability.

title: No tests for the new OAuth sync helpers or webhook endpoint
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens` and `/api/webhook/app-credential` are new shared primitives that touch every OAuth app's stored credentials, yet the PR adds no unit tests. The schema bug (computed `[z.string().toString()]` keys), the dummy `refresh_token` write, and the mismatched return shapes between call sites are exactly the kind of regressions a few table-driven tests on these two helpers (sharing enabled/disabled, response with and without refresh_token/expiry) plus a handler test for the webhook (bad secret, bad body, create vs update) would have caught.

title: Team permission check uses AND instead of OR, so team admins are denied
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. Since `isTeamAdmin` already matches ADMIN or OWNER roles and `isTeamOwner` matches only OWNER, the conjunction effectively requires the user to be the team OWNER. Team admins — who the variable name and the rest of the codebase say should be allowed — will get `FORBIDDEN`. It should be `||` (or just `isTeamAdmin`). Additionally, for personal bookings (`booking.eventType?.teamId` is null) this issues two pointless membership queries against `teamId = 0` on every call.

title: EventManager is built from the session user's credentials, not the booking organizer's
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` use the *caller's* credentials/destination calendar, but the handler explicitly allows team admins/owners and plain attendees to add guests. In those cases the calendar/video integration update (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`) runs with credentials that have no access to the organizer's calendar event, so the external calendar invite is silently not updated (or errors out) and the new guests never appear on the real event. The query at line 35-40 already fetches `booking.user.credentials` but never uses them; the organizer's credentials should be used instead.

title: Emails are dispatched using the raw input list instead of the filtered guest list
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered input, while only `uniqueGuests` were actually inserted. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` any attendee whose email appears in that list receives `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a brand-new-booking confirmation). So re-submitting an email that already belongs to an existing attendee (or a blacklisted address that was filtered out) makes that existing attendee receive a duplicate 'your booking is confirmed' email instead of the 'guests added' notification. It should pass `uniqueGuests`, normalized the same way as the comparison.

title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, allowing bypass and duplicate attendees
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lower-cased when parsed from the env var, but the incoming `guest` string is compared as-is (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), so `Blocked@Example.com` passes a blacklist containing `blocked@example.com`. The same case-sensitivity applies to the existing-attendee comparison (`guest === attendee.email`), so the same person can be added again with different casing, creating duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails. Both comparisons should normalize to lower case.

title: No server-side deduplication or size limit on the guest list
body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `z.array(z.string().email())` — no `.max()` and no uniqueness refinement (the uniqueness check exists only in the dialog component). The handler's filter removes guests already on the booking but never dedupes within the request, so a direct tRPC call with `["a@b.com", "a@b.com"]` inserts two identical attendee rows via `createMany`. With no upper bound, a single authenticated caller (including a mere attendee of the booking, per the permission check above) can insert thousands of attendees and trigger an email to each arbitrary address containing the booking details and meeting link — an email-amplification/abuse vector. Add a max length and dedupe server-side.

title: findFirstOrThrow on `booking.userId || 0` yields an unhandled 500 for bookings without a user
body: If `booking.userId` is null (possible for dynamic/managed or orphaned bookings), the lookup becomes `where: { id: 0 }` and `findFirstOrThrow` raises a Prisma `NotFoundError`, surfacing as an opaque INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR to the client instead of a meaningful tRPC error. Handle the null case explicitly (e.g. NOT_FOUND / BAD_REQUEST) rather than coercing to id 0.

title: CalendarEvent is built without `team`, so team hosts never receive the guests-added email
body: The `evt` object omits a `team` property (and `bookingId`/`eventTypeId`). In `sendAddGuestsEmails` the block `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) { ... OrganizerAddGuestsEmail({ teamMember }) }` is therefore dead code for this flow: for collective/round-robin team bookings only the single organizer is notified and the other hosts are not told that new guests were added, even though they are on the calendar event.

title: Email failure is swallowed with a message that discards the error
body: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards `err` entirely and uses `console.log` instead of the project's `logger`. When guest notification fails there is no stack trace, no error code and no booking id in the logs, making the failure undiagnosable in production. Log the error object (and ideally the booking id) via `@calcom/lib/logger`.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings
body: Every other sender in this file takes an `eventTypeMetadata` argument and short-circuits on `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and sends unconditionally, so event types configured with `metadata.disableStandardEmails.all.host`/`.attendee` will still blast organizer and attendee emails when guests are added, violating the user's configuration.

title: Subject line dereferences attendees[0] and can render an empty name
body: `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` throws a TypeError if the attendee list is empty, and newly added guests are created with `name: ""` in the handler, so if the ordering ever puts a new guest first the subject becomes `Guests Added: <eventType> with  at <date>`. Guard the access and fall back to the attendee email or organizer name.

title: Validation error state is never reset, leaving a stale error on reopen
body: `isInvalidEmail` is only cleared by the Cancel button. It is not reset in `onSuccess`, nor when the dialog is dismissed via Escape/overlay click (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`), nor when the user edits the emails. As a result the red 'Emails must be unique and valid' message stays visible after a successful submit and reappears the next time the dialog is opened. Reset it when the dialog opens/closes and when `multiEmailValue` changes.

title: Component inside packages/ui imports from its own package barrel, creating a cycle
body: `import { Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip } from "@calcom/ui"` is a self-referential import: `packages/ui/index.tsx` now exports `MultiEmailLazy` → `MultiEmail` → `@calcom/ui`. Other components in this package import siblings relatively (e.g. `./components/form`). Such cycles can resolve to `undefined` components at module-evaluation time depending on bundler/SSR ordering. Use relative imports to the concrete modules instead.

title: No tests for the new addGuests handler
body: The PR adds a mutation that writes attendees to a booking, performs permission checks (organizer / team admin-owner / attendee), filters blacklisted and duplicate emails, updates external calendars and sends emails — with no unit or integration test. The permission expression bug (`&&` instead of `||`) and the raw-vs-filtered guest list bug would both have been caught by a basic handler test. Add tests covering: unauthorized caller rejected, team admin allowed, duplicate/blacklisted emails filtered, and the email payload containing only newly added guests.

title: No guard for cancelled/past bookings or seated event types
body: The handler accepts any `bookingId` regardless of `booking.status` or start time, so a direct call can append attendees to a CANCELLED/REJECTED booking and send them a CONFIRMED ICS REQUEST for an event that no longer exists. It also ignores `eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot`: attendees are inserted with `createMany` without any corresponding `BookingSeat` record, which bypasses seat accounting for seated event types. Reject non-accepted/past bookings and either reject or correctly handle seated events.

title: Team permission check uses AND instead of OR, locking out team admins
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Since `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for ADMIN *and* OWNER roles, requiring both predicates means only team OWNERS pass; team ADMINs are rejected with FORBIDDEN even though the variable name and intent say otherwise. It should be `||` (or just `isTeamAdmin`). Consequence: team admins cannot add guests to team bookings they manage.

title: Calendar/video update uses the requester's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` build the EventManager from the *logged-in* user, but `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` must operate on the organizer's calendar/video integration (the references belong to `booking.user`). When an attendee or a team admin/owner adds guests, the requester has no credentials for the organizer's Google/Outlook calendar or video app, so the external calendar invite is never updated (or the wrong account is targeted) while the DB and emails say it succeeded. The handler already fetches `booking.user.credentials` (line 38) but never uses it.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the unfiltered input list, not the actually-added guests
body: `uniqueGuests` is the filtered list (existing attendees and blacklisted addresses removed), but `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, membership in that array decides whether an attendee gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (new-booking confirmation) or the `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` update. So if the caller re-submits an email that is already an attendee, that existing attendee receives a brand-new booking-confirmation email instead of the "guests added" notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

title: Server does not de-duplicate emails within the submitted guest list
body: `uniqueGuests` only filters guests against existing `booking.attendees` and the blacklist; duplicates *within* the `guests` array pass through and are inserted via `createMany`. The uniqueness check only exists client-side in `AddGuestsDialog`, so any direct tRPC call (or a race between two calls) creates multiple Attendee rows with the same email for one booking, which then produces duplicate emails and duplicate entries in the attendee list/ICS. De-duplicate (e.g. `new Set`, case-normalized) on the server.

title: No upper bound on the number of guests allows mass-mail abuse
body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` accepts an unbounded array. Any authenticated user is the organizer of their own bookings, so they can call `bookings.addGuests` with thousands of arbitrary addresses; the handler then creates an Attendee row per address and `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends a Cal.com-branded confirmation email with an ICS invite to each one. This turns the endpoint into an email relay/spam vector from Cal.com's sending domain and can also blow up the single DB write and the email queue. Add a `.max(...)` limit (and ideally rate limiting).

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings
body: Every other sender in this file guards with `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)`, but `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no `eventTypeMetadata` and sends unconditionally. Event types that have explicitly disabled standard host/attendee emails (e.g. because the organizer sends their own via workflows) will still blast organizer and attendee emails when guests are added, violating that configuration.

title: Newly added guests receive the full attendee list even when seatsShowAttendees is false
body: `new AttendeeScheduledEmail(calendarEvent, attendee)` is called without the `showAttendees` argument (compare `sendScheduledSeatsEmails`, which passes it). For seated event types with `seatsShowAttendees: false`, the email/ICS sent to a newly added guest will disclose the names and email addresses of all other attendees, leaking personal data that the event type is configured to hide.

title: Guests added to seated bookings get no BookingSeat record and bypass seatsPerTimeSlot
body: Attendees are inserted directly with `attendees.createMany` without creating the corresponding `BookingSeat` row and without checking `eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot`. For seated events the rest of the product (seat-reference based cancel/reschedule links, seat availability counting, success page) keys off `BookingSeat`; attendees created here will have no seat reference, so they cannot cancel/reschedule their seat and the seat capacity can be exceeded. Either reject seated bookings in this handler or create the seat references.

title: CalendarEvent is built without `team`, so team hosts are never notified
body: The `evt` object omits `team`, yet `sendAddGuestsEmails` loops over `calendarEvent.team?.members` to notify co-hosts. Because `team` is always undefined here, that loop is dead code and additional hosts of team/round-robin events never learn that guests were added. Populate `evt.team` (as `editLocation`/booking flows do) or drop the loop.

title: No validation of booking status; guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/past bookings
body: The handler only checks existence and permissions. A cancelled, rejected or already-finished booking will still get new attendees, a calendar-attendee update and "your event" confirmation emails to the new guests. The UI hides the action for cancelled bookings, but the tRPC mutation is reachable directly. Reject bookings whose status is not ACCEPTED/PENDING (and optionally bookings in the past).

title: Email failures are swallowed with console.log and the error is discarded
body: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` drops `err` entirely and uses `console.log` instead of the shared `logger` used elsewhere in the codebase. If guest notification emails fail there is no actionable signal (no stack, no bookingId), making production incidents undebuggable while the mutation still reports success.

title: findFirstOrThrow with `booking.userId || 0` yields an opaque 500 for bookings without a user
body: When `booking.userId` is null (e.g. dynamic group bookings or bookings whose user was deleted), the query looks up user id 0 and `findFirstOrThrow` raises a Prisma error that surfaces as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a meaningful tRPC error. Handle the null-userId case explicitly (or use the already-included `booking.user` relation).

title: New mutation that mutates bookings and sends email has no tests
body: `addGuestsHandler` contains non-trivial authorization logic (organizer / attendee / team admin), filtering/blacklisting, attendee creation and email+calendar side effects, but no unit or integration test is added in this PR. The permission bug on line 46 (AND vs OR) and the unfiltered `guests` passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails` are exactly the kind of regressions a handler test would catch.

title: Stale "emails must be unique and valid" error persists after a successful add
body: `onSuccess` resets `multiEmailValue` and closes the dialog but never clears `isInvalidEmail`. If the user first submits an invalid entry and then a valid one, the error banner stays in state and is displayed again the next time the dialog is opened, even though the input is empty. Reset `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` in `onSuccess` (and on successful validation in `handleAdd`).

title: Error toast shows raw tRPC error codes and the fallback message is unreachable
body: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`` is always a non-empty string, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` can never fall back to the friendly copy, and users are shown technical strings such as "FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission" or "undefined: ..." when `err.data` is missing. Translate known message keys and fall back to `t("unable_to_add_guests")` when the code/message is not user-facing.

title: Component inside packages/ui imports the package's own barrel, creating a circular dependency
body: `import { Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip } from "@calcom/ui";` is a self-import of the package root, which `packages/ui/index.tsx` in turn re-exports (`export { default as MultiEmail } from "./form/MultiEmailLazy"`). Circular barrel imports can resolve to `undefined` component references depending on module evaluation order and bloat the lazy chunk this file is meant to keep small. Import from the relative component paths (`../components/button`, `../components/form`, `../components/icon/Icon`, `../components/tooltip`) as other internal files do.

title: Label `htmlFor="emails"` points at a non-existent input id
body: The `<label htmlFor="emails">` has no matching element with `id="emails"` (the rendered `EmailField`s get generated ids and are passed `label={<></>}`), so clicking the label does nothing and screen readers announce the inputs without a label. Either give the first input that id or associate labels per field.

title: Team permission check uses AND instead of OR, blocking team admins
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Since `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for both ADMIN and OWNER roles, requiring both predicates means only team *owners* can pass this branch, and team admins are rejected with FORBIDDEN even though the variable name and the UI (`booking.isUserTeamAdminOrOwner`) imply admins should be allowed. It should be `||` (or just `isTeamAdmin`). Additionally, for non-team bookings `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` performs two pointless membership queries against team id 0 on every call.

title: Blacklist and duplicate filtering are case-sensitive, allowing bypass and duplicate attendees
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lower-cased when parsed from `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, but the incoming `guest` string is compared as-is (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). A caller can therefore bypass the blacklist entirely by sending `Blocked@Example.com` instead of `blocked@example.com`, and that address will be inserted as an attendee and emailed. The duplicate check `guest === attendee.email` has the same problem: an email that differs only in letter case from an existing attendee passes the filter and a second attendee row with the same mailbox is created. Normalize both sides with `toLowerCase()` (and trim) before comparing/inserting.

title: Input schema allows duplicate and unbounded guest lists
body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no uniqueness refinement and no `.max()` limit. The uniqueness check only exists client-side in `AddGuestsDialog` (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema` with the Set refinement), so a direct tRPC call with `["a@b.com", "a@b.com"]` creates two identical attendee rows for the booking, and a call with thousands of addresses creates thousands of attendees and sends that many emails from the Cal instance (spam/abuse amplification). The server should de-duplicate and cap the list.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` build the EventManager from the *logged-in* user, but this endpoint is explicitly reachable by attendees and team admins/owners (see the permission check above). When a non-organizer adds guests, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is executed with credentials that do not include the calendar/video credential referenced by `booking.references`, so the external calendar event is not updated (or the update fails silently) and the newly added guests never appear on the organizer's calendar invite. The organizer (`booking.user`, already fetched with `credentials`) should be used to build the EventManager.

title: No booking status check: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/past bookings
body: The handler loads the booking by id only and never inspects `booking.status` or `booking.endTime`. A caller can therefore add guests to a CANCELLED or REJECTED booking, which inserts attendees and sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` with an ICS of `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` — i.e. new guests receive an invite for a meeting that no longer exists. The UI also exposes the action through `editBookingActions`, which is rendered for past bookings (`isBookingInPast && isConfirmed` branch in BookingListItem), so guests can be invited to meetings that already happened. Reject non-ACCEPTED/past bookings server-side.

title: Raw input is passed to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of the filtered guest list
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered request input. `sendAddGuestsEmails` treats every address in that list as a *new* guest and sends it the full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a "your booking is confirmed" email). Any address that was in the request but filtered out as an already-existing attendee therefore receives a duplicate booking-confirmation email instead of the intended "guests added" notification. `uniqueGuests` (the list actually inserted) should be passed instead.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type disableStandardEmails settings
body: Every other sender in this file gates host/attendee mail on `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` (see `sendLocationChangeEmails` directly above). `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no `eventTypeMetadata` argument and performs no such check, so event types configured with `metadata.disableStandardEmails.all.host/attendee` will still send organizer and attendee emails when guests are added, violating that setting. The handler should pass `booking.eventType?.metadata` and the sender should honour it.

title: Booking `responses.guests` is not updated and no webhooks/workflows are triggered
body: Guests are inserted only into the `Attendee` table; the booking's `responses` JSON (which holds the `guests` booking field and is the source of truth used when the booking is rescheduled or re-rendered from booking fields) is left untouched, so added guests silently disappear on reschedule and are inconsistent with what the booking form shows. The handler also fires no webhook (`BOOKING_*`) and no workflow reminders for the new attendees, unlike other mutation handlers in this router, so integrations will not see the change.

title: Seated events: attendees added without BookingSeat records break seat accounting
body: For event types with `seatsPerTimeSlot`, each attendee of a booking represents a booked seat and has an associated `BookingSeat` row (used for per-seat cancel/reschedule links and for computing remaining seats). This handler inserts plain `Attendee` rows with no `bookingSeat`, so added guests consume seats without being counted/limited, cannot cancel or reschedule their seat, and the attendee list of a seated booking can exceed `seatsPerTimeSlot`. Seated bookings should either be rejected or handled explicitly.

title: findFirstOrThrow on `booking.userId || 0` yields an opaque 500 for userless bookings
body: `booking.userId` is nullable (e.g. dynamic group bookings or bookings whose user was deleted). In that case the query runs with `id: 0`, `findFirstOrThrow` raises a Prisma NotFound error that is not caught, and the client receives an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a meaningful message. Handle the null `userId` explicitly (the booking's `user` relation is already included in the first query and could be reused instead of this second round-trip).

title: Organizer email subject can be empty or crash on attendees[0]
body: The subject interpolates `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. New guests are created with `name: ""` in `addGuests.handler.ts`, and the attendee list passed into the event is built from `prisma.booking.update(... include: { attendees: true })` with no `orderBy`, so the first element is not guaranteed to be the original booker — the subject can render as "Guests Added:  with  at ...". If `attendees` were ever empty this line throws while building the mail payload. Use a defensive fallback (e.g. `attendees[0]?.name || organizer.name`) and order attendees deterministically.

title: MultiEmail imports the @calcom/ui barrel from inside packages/ui, creating a cycle
body: `MultiEmail.tsx` lives in `packages/ui` but imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui`, which is the package's own `index.tsx` — and that index now re-exports `./form/MultiEmailLazy` → `./MultiEmail`. This circular import can produce undefined components at module-init time depending on bundler evaluation order, and it also pulls the entire UI barrel into the dynamically imported chunk, defeating the purpose of the `MultiEmailLazy` code split documented in that file. Import the components from their relative paths (`../components/button`, `../components/form`, etc.) as the other files in `packages/ui/form` do.

title: Validation error state is never reset on success or dialog close
body: `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is set in `handleAdd` but is only cleared by the Cancel button. On a successful mutation (`onSuccess`) and when the dialog is dismissed via the overlay/escape (`onOpenChange` → `setIsOpenDialog`), `isInvalidEmail` stays `true`, so the next time the dialog is opened the red "Emails must be unique and valid" message is displayed before the user has typed anything. Reset the flag in `onSuccess` and at the start of `handleAdd`.

title: Clicking Add with no email rows does nothing and gives no feedback
body: When the user removes all email rows, `multiEmailValue.length === 0` and `handleAdd` returns silently: no toast, no inline error, no mutation. The button looks functional but is a no-op, which reads as a broken dialog. Either disable the Add button when the list is empty or surface the validation message.

title: Email failure is swallowed with a bare console.log
body: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards the actual error object, so an SMTP/template failure produces no actionable information in logs (the rest of the codebase uses `@calcom/lib/logger` with `safeStringify`). Log the error itself via the logger so these failures are diagnosable.

title: No tests for the new addGuests handler
body: This PR adds a new authenticated mutation that writes attendees, mutates external calendars and sends mail, with non-trivial authorization logic (organizer / attendee / team admin-owner), blacklist filtering and de-duplication — but no unit or integration test is included. At minimum there should be tests covering: rejection for an unrelated user, acceptance for organizer/attendee/team admin, duplicate and blacklisted emails being filtered, and the emails being sent only for newly added guests.

title: deleteMany OR branch has no method filter and deletes non-SMS reminders
body: The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` in `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. The SMS cron therefore deletes *any* WorkflowReminder row (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, mandatory reminders, etc.) whose retryCount exceeded 1, including rows with future scheduledDate. Today only this handler increments retryCount, but as soon as the email/WhatsApp schedulers (or any other code) reuse the same column, this cron will silently destroy their pending reminders. Add the method filter inside the OR branch (or combine it as `AND` with method/scheduled conditions).

title: prisma.update inside catch block can throw and abort the whole cron run
body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` added at the top of the `catch` block is itself unprotected. If this update fails (record removed concurrently, connection error, etc.) the exception propagates out of the `for` loop, so every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the previous behaviour where a single failing reminder was only logged. Wrap the retry-count update in its own try/catch (or move it after logging and guard it).

title: retryCount predicate is unindexed, forcing a full scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron tick
body: `retryCount` has no index (see `WorkflowReminder` indexes in schema.prisma), and because it is an `OR` branch Postgres can no longer satisfy the whole delete from the existing `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` index — it must sequentially scan WorkflowReminder. WorkflowReminder is one of the largest tables in this schema and this cron runs frequently, so this adds a repeated full-table scan plus row locks. Either add an index covering retryCount (e.g. `@@index([method, retryCount])`) or fold the retry condition into the existing method/scheduledDate-filtered predicate.

title: retryCount is not incremented when sendTo or message is missing, so those reminders still loop forever
body: The retry increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` (else-branch) or in the catch. When `sendTo` is null (e.g. no smsReminderNumber on the booking / no sendTo on the step) or the template produced an empty message, the loop body does nothing: the reminder stays `scheduled: false`, keeps being picked up by the 7-day query on every cron run and is never cleaned up until scheduledDate passes. This is exactly the "keep scheduling it in our cron job until the date is reached" problem the PR claims to fix, so the fix is incomplete for that class of rows.

title: Reminders skipped for non-transient reasons (e.g. SMS sending locked) are permanently deleted
body: `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value not only on send failures but also when sending is suppressed for the user/team (SMS lock state checks inside the provider). With this change such a skip increments `retryCount`, and after two cron runs the reminder row is deleted by the new `deleteMany` branch. Consequence: once a lock/review is lifted the reminder no longer exists and the customer never gets the SMS. Distinguish genuine scheduling errors from intentional skips before counting a retry.

title: Read-modify-write on retryCount instead of atomic increment
body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` uses the value read at the start of the handler. If two cron invocations overlap (cron overlap, manual POST, retried request), both read the same value and one increment is lost, so a reminder can keep retrying beyond the intended limit. Use Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` instead.

title: No test covering the new retry/delete behaviour
body: The PR introduces a retry-and-delete policy (increment on failure, delete when retryCount > 1) with no accompanying test. A regression here either leaks reminders forever or deletes reminders that should still be sent, both of which are silent in production. A unit/integration test asserting (a) retryCount increments when scheduleSMS fails or returns falsy, (b) rows with retryCount > 1 are deleted, and (c) non-SMS reminders are untouched, would lock the behaviour in.

title: deleteMany `retryCount > 1` arm is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The new OR branch in the `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany()` call matches `retryCount > 1` for *every* row in `WorkflowReminder`, with no `method` filter. This SMS cron therefore deletes EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders too as soon as anything starts incrementing `retryCount` for them (e.g. when the same retry logic is added to `scheduleEmailReminders`/`scheduleWhatsappReminders`, or if a future writer sets the field). It also deletes rows that are already `scheduled: true` with a `referenceId`, losing the record needed to cancel the scheduled message later. The branch should be scoped with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and arguably `scheduled: false`).

title: retryCount update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update()` added at the top of the `catch` block is not itself protected. Before this change the catch only called `console.log`, so any error for one reminder was swallowed and the loop continued. Now, if this update throws (row deleted concurrently by the `deleteMany` of a parallel invocation → Prisma P2025 "record not found", or a DB connection error, which is exactly the kind of failure likely to have caused the original exception), the rejection propagates out of the `for` loop, every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped, and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the expected response. Wrap the update in its own try/catch (or `.catch()`) so a bookkeeping failure cannot abort the batch.

title: Transient failures cause permanent deletion of pending SMS reminders
body: `retryCount` is incremented for every failure path without distinguishing permanent errors (invalid phone number, which is the motivating case) from transient ones (Twilio outage/5xx, network timeout, DB hiccup, rate limiting). Since the cron processes all reminders due within the next 7 days on every run, two consecutive bad runs are enough to push `retryCount` to 2 for the entire backlog, and the next run's `deleteMany` silently deletes all of them — reminders that would have sent fine are lost permanently with no notification. Consider only counting non-retryable Twilio errors, or using a time-based backoff/last-attempt timestamp so retries are spread out rather than consumed within minutes/hours of each other.

title: No retry accounting when message is empty or sendTo is missing
body: The retryCount increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)`. When `sendTo` is null (e.g. `booking.smsReminderNumber` not set for an SMS_ATTENDEE step) or the rendered `message` is empty, the loop body falls through without touching the row: `scheduled` stays `false` and `retryCount` stays unchanged, so this reminder is re-selected and re-processed (including the `prisma.profile.findFirst` and `getBookerBaseUrl` queries) on every cron invocation until `scheduledDate` passes. That is precisely the endless-rescheduling behaviour this PR is meant to eliminate, and it remains unfixed for these cases.

title: OR on unindexed retryCount forces a full scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron run
body: The rewritten `deleteMany` produces `WHERE (method = 'SMS' AND scheduledDate <= now) OR retryCount > 1`. There is no index on `retryCount` (the schema only has `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` and `[cancelled, scheduledDate]`), so the OR prevents an index-only plan and Postgres will sequentially scan the whole `WorkflowReminder` table each time this cron runs. On a table of this size (one row per reminder per booking) that is a noticeable repeated cost. Splitting into two `deleteMany` calls (one per condition, with the retry one scoped to `method: SMS`) and/or indexing the retry predicate would keep the existing index usable.

title: Comment no longer describes what the delete query does
body: The comment `//delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date` now sits above a query that also deletes any reminder (of any method) whose `retryCount` exceeds 1. A reader relying on the comment will not realise rows are being removed for retry exhaustion, which is the main new behaviour here. Update the comment to mention the retry-count deletion.

title: No tests for the new retry/delete behaviour
body: The PR introduces behaviour that permanently deletes user-facing reminders (increment on failure, delete when `retryCount > 1`) and no test covers it: there is no assertion that a failed `twilio.scheduleSMS` increments `retryCount`, that a falsy (non-throwing) return also increments it, that a successful schedule leaves the row intact, or that the delete threshold yields exactly two attempts. Given the data-loss consequence of an off-by-one here (threshold `gt: 1` vs `gte: 1`), a unit test around the handler with a mocked twilio provider would be worth adding.

title: deleteMany `retryCount > 1` branch is not scoped to SMS or to unscheduled reminders
body: The new OR branch in the `deleteMany` only filters on `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`. Unlike the first branch it does not constrain `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, so this SMS-only cron will permanently delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder rows as soon as any other code path starts incrementing `retryCount` for them (the column is shared by all methods). It also does not constrain `scheduled: false` / `referenceId: null`, so a reminder that eventually succeeded after failures (scheduled = true, referenceId = Twilio SID) can be deleted; once the row is gone the SID is lost and the queued Twilio message can no longer be cancelled if the booking is cancelled or rescheduled, meaning reminders get sent for dead bookings. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and `scheduled: false` to this branch.

title: retryCount is incremented for failures unrelated to SMS delivery
body: The `catch` wraps the whole per-reminder body, which includes `getCalEventResponses`, `prisma.profile.findFirst`, `getBookerBaseUrl`, `bookingMetadataSchema.parse` and template rendering — not just `twilio.scheduleSMS`. Any transient failure there (DB hiccup, Twilio-wide outage, a bad metadata blob) now bumps `retryCount`, and after two cron runs the reminder is deleted for good even though its scheduled date may be days away. A short outage spanning two cron invocations would wipe out all pending SMS reminders instead of retrying them later. The counter should only be bumped for an actual send/schedule failure (or the deletion threshold should account for transient errors).

title: Falsy return from scheduleSMS (e.g. SMS sending locked) is treated as a permanent failure
body: `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns without a value in non-error cases such as the user/team being locked for SMS sending (`SMSLockState` / isLockedForSMSSending). The new `else` branch treats that undefined return as a failed attempt and increments `retryCount`, so after two cron runs the reminder row is deleted. Once the account is unlocked or reviewed, those reminders are gone and will never be sent. Locked/suppressed states should be distinguished from real scheduling failures and should not consume retries.

title: Unguarded prisma.update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` added in the `catch` block is awaited without its own error handling. If it throws (e.g. Prisma P2025 because the row was deleted concurrently, or a connection error — likely exactly when the original error was a DB problem), the rejection propagates out of the `for` loop and out of the handler, so every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the previous behaviour of logging and continuing. Wrap it in its own try/catch.

title: retryCount updated with a read-modify-write instead of an atomic increment
body: Both update calls set `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` based on the value read earlier in the request. If two cron invocations overlap (or the job is retried by the scheduler), both read the same value and both write the same result, so failures are undercounted and the reminder keeps being retried indefinitely. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`.

title: OR on unindexed retryCount defeats the existing WorkflowReminder index
body: WorkflowReminder has `@@index([method, scheduled, scheduledDate])`, which the previous delete predicate could use. The new top-level `OR` adds a branch on `retryCount`, which has no index; Postgres will typically fall back to a sequential scan of the whole WorkflowReminder table on every run of this cron. On a table of this size that is an expensive repeated scan. Consider running the retry-exhausted cleanup as a separate narrowly-filtered delete (e.g. `method: SMS, scheduled: false, retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) and/or adding an index covering it.

title: Reminders with no message or no recipient still loop forever
body: `retryCount` is only touched inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` or in the catch. A reminder whose `sendTo` resolves to null (e.g. SMS_ATTENDEE with no `booking.smsReminderNumber`) or whose template produces an empty body falls through silently: it stays `scheduled: false` with `retryCount: 0` and is re-fetched by every cron run until its scheduled date passes — the exact repeated-rescheduling problem this PR is meant to fix. These cases should also consume a retry (or be deleted/marked immediately).

title: Returned SQL fragments contain un-parenthesized top-level OR, enabling authorization bypass when callers append conditions
body: `getBaseConditions()` returns `authConditions` verbatim when there are no filters (line 75), and `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` are public. For org and team scope, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`/`buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` produce a fragment whose top-level operator is `OR` (e.g. `("teamId" = ANY($1)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true) OR (("userId" = ANY($2)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false))` after the reduce), and `buildFilterConditions` likewise returns a bare `OR` fragment when only `eventTypeId` is set. Since the service no longer executes any query, every consumer must interpolate these fragments into their own raw SQL, and the natural `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" > ${x}` becomes `A OR (B AND x)` because SQL `AND` binds tighter than `OR`. That silently widens the authorized row set (bookings of users/teams the caller is not entitled to see). The service should wrap its final result in parentheses (e.g. `Prisma.sql`(${combined})`) before returning it from `getBaseConditions`/`getFilterConditions`/`getAuthorizationConditions`.

title: Public `findMany` removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions` without updating consumers
body: The only query-executing method on `InsightsBookingService` (`findMany(findManyArgs)`) is deleted and replaced with `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>`. Nothing else in the repository is updated in this PR, so any existing caller of `service.findMany(...)` will fail to compile (or, if typed loosely, fail at runtime). It also pushes raw-SQL assembly onto every consumer, which is where the parenthesization hazard above becomes dangerous. Either keep an execution helper on the service (e.g. a `findMany`/`query` that wraps `$queryRaw` with the base conditions correctly parenthesized) or update all call sites in the same change.

title: Constructor option type widened so `scope: "team"` without `teamId` type-checks and silently returns no rows
body: The constructor now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (`scope: "user" | "org" | "team"`, `teamId?: number`) instead of the zod-inferred discriminated union. A caller passing `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` with `teamId` undefined (a very likely shape when `teamId` comes from an optional request field) now compiles, but `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema.safeParse` fails, `this.options` becomes `null`, and `buildAuthorizationConditions` returns `1=0`. The user sees an empty insights result with no error and no log, instead of a compile-time error as before. Keep the exact union type for the public options, or surface the validation failure (throw / log) rather than degrading to an empty result set.

title: Only the user-scope SQL is ever executed; team/org `= ANY(...)` fragments are never run against Postgres
body: After this conversion the correctness of the generated SQL (column quoting, `= ANY($n)` parameter binding for integer arrays, `1=0`) can only be verified by executing it. The single `$queryRaw` test at line 481 exercises the user-scope condition plus an `eventTypeId` filter; the team-scope, org-scope and NOTHING conditions are asserted only by comparing `Prisma.sql` template objects, which would pass even if the SQL is syntactically invalid or the driver cannot infer the array parameter type for `= ANY($1)`. Add `$queryRaw` assertions for at least the org and team scopes (and the NOTHING condition) so a broken raw query is caught by CI rather than in production.

title: Caching tests for auth/filter conditions were deleted with no replacement
