body: The `describe("Caching")` block covering `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` memoization was removed. That behaviour still exists in the service (`cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` with the `=== undefined` sentinel check, which is specifically needed because `getFilterConditions()` legitimately caches `null`). With the tests gone, a regression such as switching the check to `if (!this.cachedFilterConditions)` — which would recompute and re-query on every call — would go unnoticed. Port the caching assertions to the new SQL expectations instead of dropping them.

title: Returned SQL fragments contain top-level OR without enclosing parentheses
body: `getBaseConditions()` returns the authorization fragment verbatim when no filters are set (line 75), and for `org`/`team` scope that fragment is built by the reduce as `(A AND "isTeamBooking" = true) OR (B AND "isTeamBooking" = false)` with no enclosing parentheses (lines 171-174 and 204-207). The same is true for `getFilterConditions()` when only `eventTypeId` is set (`("eventTypeId" = x) OR ("eventParentId" = x)`). Because `AND` binds tighter than `OR` in SQL, any consumer that composes the fragment with extra predicates — e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" >= ${from}` — produces `A OR (B AND startTime >= ...)`, so the additional predicate constrains only one branch of the OR. The result is silently widened row sets, i.e. a potential authorization/scope bypass and wrong insights numbers. The fragments should be wrapped (`Prisma.sql`(${cond})`) before being returned. Note the only test uses `WHERE ${baseConditions}` standalone, so this failure mode is not covered.

title: Public findMany() removed without updating any callers
body: The public method `findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)`, which ran `prisma.bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany` with the authorization and filter where-clauses applied, is deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()` returning a raw `Prisma.Sql`. No other file in the repository is touched by this PR, so any existing consumer of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` will no longer compile, and consumers must now hand-write raw SQL (taking on responsibility for parenthesization, column quoting and result typing). Either keep a `findMany`-style convenience wrapper or update the call sites in this PR. The PR description also states that only the tests changed and that the service was already converted, which hides this breaking change from reviewers.

title: New InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions weakens compile-time validation of options
body: The constructor parameter type changed from the zod discriminated union (`InsightsBookingServiceOptions`, which requires `teamId` when `scope === "team"`) to the hand-written `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` with `scope: "user" | "org" | "team"` and optional `teamId`. A caller can now pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without `teamId` and it type-checks; at runtime `safeParse` fails, `this.options` becomes `null`, and the service silently returns `1=0`, i.e. an empty result set with no error or log. The previous typing made this a compile error. Keep the discriminated union as the constructor type (or at least log/throw when validation fails) so misuse is caught instead of producing silently empty insights.

title: Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions
body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always resolves to a `Prisma.Sql` object (at minimum `NOTHING_CONDITION`), and objects are always truthy, so the `else if (filterConditions)` branch (line 76) and the final `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` (line 79) can never execute. The dead code suggests the author expected auth conditions to possibly be null/absent; if a future change makes auth conditions optional the fallback would silently drop authorization. Either drop the dead branches or make the nullability explicit.

title: Caching tests deleted although the caching logic still exists
body: The `describe("Caching")` block (previously asserting that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return the same cached value on repeated calls) was removed, but the service still implements `cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` memoization, including the `undefined`-vs-`null` distinction in `getFilterConditions()` (a cached `null` must not trigger a rebuild). That memoization path is now untested, so a regression such as caching `null` incorrectly or rebuilding conditions on every call would go unnoticed. The tests could simply be ported to the new `Prisma.sql` expectations instead of deleted.

title: Org/team scope assertions depend on unspecified DB row ordering
body: The org-scope expectation hard-codes the parameter arrays as `[org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` and `[user.id, user2.id, user3.id]`. These come from `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId` and `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`, which issue queries without an `ORDER BY`, so PostgreSQL does not guarantee the returned order. With `toEqual` on the `Prisma.Sql` object the `values` arrays are compared element-by-element, so any reordering (e.g. after a vacuum, index-only scan or parallel plan) fails the test even though the generated SQL is semantically equivalent. Sort the ids in the service (or sort before comparison in the test) to make the assertion deterministic.

title: Public `findMany` removed with no callers updated
body: `findMany(findManyArgs)` was the only query-executing method on `InsightsBookingService` and has been replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which merely returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. The PR touches only this file and its test, so any existing consumer that calls `insightsBookingService.findMany(...)` (e.g. insights tRPC routers) will fail to compile / break at runtime. Beyond the compile break, the enforcement point for authorization has moved out of the service into every caller: previously the auth conditions were guaranteed to be ANDed into the Prisma `where`; now a caller that forgets to interpolate `getBaseConditions()` into its raw query silently returns unfiltered booking data. Either keep a query helper on the service (e.g. `findAll`/`getRows` that builds the full SQL) or update and audit all call sites in this PR.

title: Authorization/filter SQL fragments are returned without outer parentheses
body: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` (line 171-174), `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` (line 204-207) and `buildFilterConditions` (line 119-122) return top-level `A OR B` / `A OR B` expressions with no enclosing parentheses, and these fragments are exposed through the public `getAuthorizationConditions()` / `getFilterConditions()` methods. Any caller that composes them as `WHERE "createdAt" > ${x} AND ${authConditions}` gets `("createdAt" > x AND A) OR B` because `AND` binds tighter than `OR`, i.e. rows matching only `B` are returned regardless of the other predicates — an authorization bypass. Only `getBaseConditions()` currently wraps them. Wrap each composed fragment in parentheses at construction time (`Prisma.sql`((${acc}) OR (${condition}))``) so the returned SQL is safe in any context.

title: Fail-open fallback branch in getBaseConditions
body: In `getBaseConditions()` the branch `else if (filterConditions) { return filterConditions; }` returns the user-supplied filter conditions with no authorization predicate at all. It is unreachable today only because `getAuthorizationConditions()` always resolves to a non-null `Prisma.Sql` (worst case `1=0`), but the typing (`Promise<Prisma.Sql>`) makes the `authConditions &&` checks pointless dead code, and if the auth builder is ever changed to return `null`/empty the query silently becomes unauthenticated. Drop the dead branches or make the no-auth case return `NOTHING_CONDITION`.

title: Constructor option type loosened, team scope without teamId now silently returns nothing
body: The constructor parameter type changed from the validated discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to the new flat `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (`scope: "user" | "org" | "team"`, `teamId?: number`). Passing `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without `teamId` now type-checks, fails the runtime zod parse, sets `this.options = null`, and the service silently produces `1=0`, i.e. insights show zero bookings instead of surfacing a programming error. Either keep the discriminated union in the public signature or throw / log when `safeParse` fails so misuse is detectable.

title: Caching tests deleted while the caching logic still exists
body: The whole `describe("Caching")` block (previously asserting that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return the memoized value on the second call) was removed, but `cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` are still implemented in the service (insightsBooking.ts lines 83-95). The `cachedFilterConditions` memoization relies on an `=== undefined` check to distinguish "not computed" from a cached `null`; that subtle logic is now completely untested. The caching tests should be ported to the new `Prisma.sql` expectations rather than deleted.

title: Only user-scope SQL is executed against the database; ANY() array bindings untested
body: The single test that actually runs SQL (`prisma.$queryRaw` with `getBaseConditions()`) uses `scope: "user"`, whose condition contains no array parameters. The newly introduced `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` / `"userId" = ANY(${userIds})` constructs for team and org scope are only compared as `Prisma.Sql` objects via `toEqual`, which validates the template strings but never that Postgres accepts the generated query or that Prisma binds a JS number array to a PG array correctly. A broken array binding, a wrong column name, or an invalid boolean comparison in those branches would pass CI. Add an integration test that executes `$queryRaw` with team- and org-scope base conditions and asserts the returned booking ids.

title: deleteCache handler throws a plain Error and only authorizes user-owned credentials
body: The handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` instead of a `TRPCError`. tRPC maps unknown errors to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, so an authorization failure is reported to the client as a 500 and logged/alerted as a server bug rather than a 403/404. Additionally, the authorization check is `where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id }`, so credentials owned by a team (`userId` is null, `teamId` set) can never be matched; the UI will still render the "Delete cached data" action for such a credential and the user gets an opaque server error. Use `TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN" | "NOT_FOUND" })` and include the team-admin case in the access check (or hide the action for team credentials).

title: Cache deletion never invalidates the connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in the UI
body: `deleteCacheMutation`'s `onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation (which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`), nothing invalidates the query that provides `cacheUpdatedAt`. In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` the prop is wired to `props.onChanged`, which is optional and not supplied on the installed-apps page, and the query is configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. Consequence: after a successful delete the dropdown keeps showing the old "Last updated: …" timestamp and the "Delete cached data" entry until a full reload, making it look as if the deletion failed. Add `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` to the mutation's settled/success handler.

title: Cache timestamp is hard-coded to the en-US locale and ignores the user's time format
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })` formats the cache timestamp with a fixed US locale, so non-US users see MM/DD/YY and a 12-hour clock regardless of their configured locale/`timeFormat` (24h) preference. The surrounding string is translated via `t("cache_last_updated")`, which makes the mix of translated label and US-formatted date inconsistent. Use the active i18n locale (e.g. `i18n.language`) and the user's time-format preference, or the existing dayjs/date formatting helpers used elsewhere in the app.

title: Confirm buttons are not disabled while mutations are in flight and errors lose server detail
body: `onConfirm` fires `deleteCacheMutation.mutate` / `disconnectMutation.mutate` and immediately closes the dialog without any pending/disabled state, so a user can re-open and re-trigger the mutation while the first request is still running. Also both `onError` handlers discard `error.message` and show a generic toast, so real failures (e.g. the "Credential not found or access denied" case from `deleteCache.handler.ts`) are indistinguishable from transient errors, making support/debugging harder. Wire `isPending` to the dialog's confirm button and surface the server message in the error toast.

title: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache relies on an empty updateMany payload to bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object and depends entirely on Prisma implicitly injecting the `@updatedAt` field into the generated UPDATE. That is non-obvious and fragile (if Prisma treats the empty payload as a no-op the intended timestamp bump silently never happens), and the intent is not verifiable from the code. It also runs on every cache fill — an extra write per credential in the cache-warming cron path — for a field that nothing in this PR reads (the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache`). Either pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` explicitly or drop the call. Note that for in-memory delegation credentials `this.credential.id` is negative, so the update matches no rows at all.

title: updateManyByCredentialId is typed with UpdateInput but calls updateMany
body: The new method accepts `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` but forwards it to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany`, which requires `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`. `UpdateInput` permits nested relation operations (e.g. `user: { connect: { id } }`, `credential: { disconnect: true }`) that `updateMany` cannot execute, so such a call type-checks but fails at runtime with a Prisma validation error. Change the parameter type to `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId that nothing in this PR consumes
body: `UserWithCalendars.allSelectedCalendars` / `userLevelSelectedCalendars` were widened from `Pick<SelectedCalendar, "externalId" | "integration" | "eventTypeId">` to also require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. This is a breaking contract change for every caller that builds this object from a narrower Prisma `select` (platform API v2 / `@calcom/platform-libraries` consumers of `getConnectedDestinationCalendars`), which will now fail type-check and need matching select changes. Neither field is used by the cache-status feature added here (the handler reads `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache`), and adding them to `findUnlockedUserForSession`'s select also enlarges the session payload for no benefit. Revert the type widening unless there is a consumer.

title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt and reports expired cache as present
body: The `groupBy` only filters on `credentialId`, so rows whose `expiresAt` is already in the past are included in the max-`updatedAt` result. `getCachedAvailability` refuses to serve those rows (`expiresAt: { gte: now }`), so the UI will show a "Cache Status / Last updated …" entry and offer "Delete cached data" for a credential whose cache can no longer be used — a misleading status for a diagnostics feature. Filter by `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (or surface expiry separately).

title: connectedCalendars always runs an extra cache groupBy and bypasses the CalendarCache feature-flag factory
body: The handler instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init`, so the `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` (used when calendar-cache is disabled) is bypassed and an additional `calendarCache.groupBy` query is executed on every call to this frequently-used endpoint, even for users/teams that have the calendar-cache feature off. Either skip the query when the feature is disabled or short-circuit when `credentialIds` is empty, and go through the existing factory so the enabled/disabled behaviour is consistent with the rest of the calendar-cache code.

title: Migration header warning contradicts the SQL it documents
body: The generated warning block states "Added the required column `updatedAt` to the `CalendarCache` table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty.", but the statement below adds the column `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`, which is safe for a non-empty table. Leaving the stale warning in place makes reviewers/operators believe this migration will fail or needs a manual backfill. Remove or correct the comment block.

title: ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's CWD and can write a .env outside the repo
body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the current working directory, not to the script location. Running the script the obvious way from the repository root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) resolves to `<parent-of-checkout>/.env`: the script happily creates that file (`touch "$ENV_FILE"`) and writes `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` into it, polluting a directory outside the repo while the developer's real `.env` is never updated — so the webhook test silently does not work. Resolve the path from the script directory (e.g. `ENV_FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/.env"`).

title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only and breaks on Linux
body: `sed -i '' -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD form where `-i` takes a separate (empty) backup suffix. With GNU sed (Linux, CI containers) `-i` does not consume the next argument, so `''` is parsed as the sed script and the substitution expression is treated as a filename, causing the command to fail and the env file to be left unmodified. Use a portable approach (e.g. write to a temp file and `mv`, or detect the sed flavour).

title: cleanup() always exits 0, so failures report success
body: `cleanup()` ends with `exit 0` and is used both as the SIGINT/SIGTERM trap and as the failure path for "Rate limit hit" (line 49) and "Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL" (line 58). The script therefore terminates with status 0 even when it never obtained a tunnel URL and never configured `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL`, so any wrapper script or CI step cannot detect the failure. Use a non-zero exit code for the error paths.

title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` without adding tsx as a dependency
body: `"dev:cron": "npx tsx cron-tester.ts"` relies on `npx` fetching `tsx` from the network at run time; the package is not in `dependencies`/`devDependencies`, so the version is unpinned and unaffected by the lockfile, and the command fails in offline/sandboxed environments. Meanwhile `ts-node` is still a devDependency and is still used by the sibling scripts (`check-changed-files`, `translate-locales`), so the toolchain is now inconsistent. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it directly, or revert to `ts-node`.

title: No tests for the new deleteCache authorization or cache-status aggregation
body: This PR adds a destructive mutation (`viewer.calendars.deleteCache`) whose only protection is an ownership lookup, plus a new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` aggregation and the credential→cache mapping in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, and none of them have unit tests. At minimum there should be tests asserting that (a) deleting cache for a credential belonging to another user is rejected, (b) a successful call removes only the rows for that credentialId, and (c) `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` returns the latest `updatedAt` per credential and maps correctly to `cacheUpdatedAt` (including the no-cache case).

title: deleteCache throws a plain Error instead of TRPCError
body: When the credential does not exist or does not belong to the caller the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps non-TRPCError exceptions to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (HTTP 500), so an authorization failure is reported as a server fault, gets logged/reported to error tracking as a crash, and the client cannot distinguish it from a real failure. Use `throw new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN", message: ... })` as the other handlers in this router do.

title: Cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
body: `deleteCacheMutation.onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation (which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`), nothing invalidates the query that produced `cacheUpdatedAt`. In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` the `onChanged` prop is optional and is not always supplied, and the query is configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, so after deleting the cache the dropdown keeps showing the old "Last updated" timestamp and the "Delete cached data" entry until a full page reload, making it look like the deletion failed.

title: Cache timestamp is hard-coded to en-US formatting
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })` ignores the user's locale and 12h/24h `timeFormat` preference stored on the user, so non-US users see MM/DD/YYYY and AM/PM dates inside an otherwise localized UI (the surrounding string is translated via `cache_last_updated`). Use the user's locale/time-format (e.g. the existing dayjs/`useTimePreferences` helpers) instead of a literal "en-US".

title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt
body: The groupBy query selects `MAX(updatedAt)` for the given credentialIds without filtering on `expiresAt >= now()`, while `getCachedAvailability` only serves non-expired rows. As a result the UI will report a credential as having a cache ("Cache Status / Last updated …") and offer "Delete cached data" even when every cached row is expired and no availability request can be served from it, giving users a misleading view of cache health.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId that are never used
body: `UserWithCalendars` (an exported type consumed outside this file, e.g. by the platform API v2 calendars service and other callers of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb`) was widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars`, but neither field is read anywhere in this module. Any caller that selects only `externalId`/`integration`/`eventTypeId` will now fail type-check, and `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` had to be changed to fetch two extra columns per selected calendar into the session payload purely to satisfy the type. Revert the type tightening unless the fields are actually needed.

title: updateManyByCredentialId called with an empty data object to bump updatedAt
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` relies on Prisma implicitly writing the `@updatedAt` column when `data` is empty. This is implicit/undocumented behaviour — if Prisma emits no SET clause the call is a pure no-op write — and even when it works it issues an extra UPDATE over every SelectedCalendar row of the credential on every cache refresh (including rows that were not refreshed), which runs on the cache cron for every watched credential. The PR description itself notes `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not consumed by the frontend (the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt`), so this write appears unnecessary; if it is needed, pass an explicit `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`.

title: updateManyByCredentialId types data as SelectedCalendarUpdateInput
body: `updateMany` accepts `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`, not `SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`. Using the single-record update type lets callers pass nested relation operations (e.g. `{ user: { connect: { id } } }`) which type-check but fail at runtime with a Prisma validation error. Change the parameter type to `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.

title: Dev script writes .env outside the repository
body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory, not to the script location. The documented way of running repo scripts is from the repository root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`), which makes the script create/modify a `.env` file in the parent directory of the checkout (and print "Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL" as if it had succeeded), while the app's real `.env` is left untouched. Resolve the path from `$(dirname "$0")/..` instead.

title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only and breaks on Linux
body: `sed -i '' -E "s|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD syntax where `-i` takes a separate (empty) suffix argument. With GNU sed (Linux CI/dev containers) the empty string is parsed as the script/first file operand and the command fails with "can't read : No such file or directory", leaving `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` un-updated while the script still reports success. Use `sed -i.bak`/a temp-file approach, or branch on the platform.

title: dev:cron uses npx tsx but tsx is not a dependency
body: `"dev:cron": "npx tsx cron-tester.ts"` invokes a binary that is not declared in `devDependencies` (only `ts-node` is, and it is still used by the `check-changed-files` and `translate-locales` scripts). `npx` will download an unpinned `tsx` from the network on each run (or prompt), which fails in offline/CI environments and is inconsistent with the yarn-workspace setup. Add `tsx` to devDependencies and call it via `yarn tsx`, or leave the script on `ts-node`. This change is also unrelated to the feature in this PR.

title: Cache status lookup bypasses the calendar-cache feature flag
body: The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, so the `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` added in this PR is never used and an extra `calendarCache.groupBy` query is executed on every `connectedCalendars` request even for deployments/teams where calendar cache is disabled (and also when `credentialIds` is empty, producing a pointless `IN ()` query). Route through the feature-flag aware factory, or skip the query when there are no credentialIds / the feature is off.

title: Migration comment contradicts the statement and backfill produces misleading timestamps
body: The generated warning block says the required column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the statement does supply `DEFAULT NOW()`; the stale comment will mislead reviewers/operators about the migration's safety. In addition, all pre-existing rows are backfilled with the migration time, so immediately after deploy the new UI will report long-stale caches as "Last updated: <deploy time>". Consider removing/correcting the comment and documenting (or backfilling from `expiresAt - CACHING_TIME`) the known inaccuracy.

title: No tests for the new deleteCache authorization or cache-status query
body: `deleteCacheHandler` performs an ownership check that gates a destructive `calendarCache.deleteMany`, and `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` is new behaviour surfaced in the UI, yet neither has a unit test. A regression in the `userId` predicate would let a user delete another user's calendar cache, and nothing would catch it. Add tests covering: deletion for an owned credential, rejection for a credential owned by another user, and the credential→updatedAt mapping returned by the repository.

title: Authorization failure throws plain Error → 500 instead of a tRPC error
body: When the credential does not exist or belongs to another user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC turns non-`TRPCError` throws into `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (HTTP 500) and reports them as unexpected server errors (noise in Sentry/logs), while the client only sees a generic failure. This should be `throw new TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN" | "NOT_FOUND", message: ... })` so the status code and client handling are correct.

title: CalendarCacheRepository instantiated directly, bypassing the calendar-cache feature gate
body: The handler does `new CalendarCacheRepository()` instead of going through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, which is the factory that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the `calendar-cache` feature is disabled. As a result every `connectedCalendars` query now issues an extra `calendarCache.groupBy` query (this endpoint is called on the installed-apps and event-type calendar screens), and the UI will advertise "Cache Status"/"Delete cached data" for deployments or users where calendar cache is turned off. Use the existing factory so the feature flag is respected and the mock short-circuits the DB call.

title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates the connectedCalendars query
body: The disconnect mutation invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`, but `deleteCacheMutation` only calls the optional `onSuccess?.()` callback (the `onChanged` prop, which is undefined in several call sites of `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`). Since `cacheUpdatedAt` comes from that query and `connectedCalendars` is configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, after a successful deletion the dropdown keeps showing the old "Last updated" timestamp and the now-meaningless "Delete cached data" entry until a full page reload. Add `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` to the mutation's onSuccess/onSettled.

title: Cache timestamp is hard-coded to en-US formatting
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })` formats the cache timestamp with US date order and 12-hour clock for every user, ignoring the user's locale (available via `useLocale()`) and their 12/24h `timeFormat` preference. Non-US users will see a date like `7/15/25, 4:06 PM`, which is confusing/ambiguous. Pass the active locale (and ideally the user's time format) instead of a literal.

title: Cache status/delete is unavailable for Delegation Credential connections
body: `hasCache` is derived from `cacheUpdatedAt`, which the handler resolves by matching `connectedCalendar.credentialId` against `CalendarCache.credentialId`. Delegation (domain-wide) connections surface in-memory credentials with negative ids, and their cache rows are looked up by `userId` (see `getCachedAvailability`'s `isInMemoryDelegationCredential` branch), so the map lookup never matches: for exactly the org users who most rely on calendar cache the dropdown is rendered as `null` (no cache status, no way to purge a bad cache). Either resolve cache status by userId for delegation credentials or document that the feature intentionally excludes them.

title: Unused updateMany with empty data on every cache refresh
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is executed after every `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` run (triggered by every Google webhook notification and by the watch cron) solely to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. It (a) relies on the implicit Prisma behaviour of emitting `SET updatedAt = now()` for an empty `data` object, which is fragile and non-obvious, (b) touches *all* selected calendars of the credential, including ones whose cache was not refreshed in this run, and (c) writes a value the PR itself states is not consumed anywhere (the UI reads `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache`). It also silently no-ops for in-memory delegation credentials whose id is negative. Remove it or make the intent explicit with an actual `updatedAt: new Date()` payload scoped to the refreshed calendars.

title: updateManyByCredentialId types data as SelectedCalendarUpdateInput but calls updateMany
body: `updateMany` accepts `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`, not `SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`. Because the parameter is typed with the latter, nested relation writes (e.g. `user: { connect: { id } }`, `eventType: { disconnect: true }`) type-check at the call site but are rejected by Prisma at runtime. Type the parameter as `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId that this module never reads
body: `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` in the exported `UserWithCalendars` type were widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, but nothing in `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` (or the new cache-status code, which keys off `CalendarCache`) uses those fields. Every caller that builds this object from a narrower Prisma `select` (API v2 / platform-libraries call sites, onboarding handlers) now fails type-checking; the PR only updated one select (`UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession`). Either revert the type widening or update all the selects that feed this type.

title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired cache is reported as present
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows for the credential with no `expiresAt` filter. Rows stay in the table after they expire (lookups filter on `expiresAt >= now()`), so the UI will show a "Last updated" timestamp and offer "Delete cached data" for a credential whose cache is no longer usable, giving a misleading picture of cache health. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (or surface expiry separately).

title: No tests for the new cache status/delete paths
body: The PR adds a new mutation (`deleteCacheHandler`, including its ownership check), a new repository method (`CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), the credential→cache mapping in `connectedCalendarsHandler`, and a new UI component, with no unit or integration tests. At minimum the authorization branch of `deleteCacheHandler` (another user's credentialId must be rejected and must not delete rows) and the credentialId→updatedAt mapping should be covered, since a mapping bug would silently show one credential's cache state under another credential.

title: Migration warning comment contradicts the actual SQL
body: The header says "Added the required column `updatedAt` to the `CalendarCache` table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty." while the statement below actually adds the column with `DEFAULT NOW()`. A reviewer or operator reading the migration will believe it is a destructive/blocking change on a non-empty table. Remove or correct the stale auto-generated warning.

title: dev:cron now runs an undeclared dependency via npx
body: `dev:cron` was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`. `tsx` is not in this package's (or the repo's) dependencies, so `npx` will download it from the registry at run time — the script fails offline/in restricted CI and pulls an unpinned package version (supply-chain risk). `ts-node` is still listed in devDependencies but unused by this script. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it directly, or keep `ts-node`.

title: Dev script uses macOS-only sed syntax and masks failures
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax; on Linux (GNU sed) the empty argument is parsed as the input filename and the command fails with "can't read : No such file or directory", leaving `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` un-updated. In addition `ENV_FILE="../.env"` only resolves correctly when the script is invoked from inside `scripts/`, and `cleanup()` always `exit 0`, so the "Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL" path returns a success exit status to the caller.

title: One failing SendGrid cancellation permanently blocks all future cancellations
body: The whole cancellation loop is wrapped in a single try/catch and the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` calls are collected as lazy Prisma promises that are only executed by `await Promise.all(...)` after the loop finishes. If any `client.request` call throws (SendGrid rejects a cancellation that is less than ~10 minutes before `sendAt`, or returns 400 because the batch already has a `cancel` status), the loop aborts and *none* of the already-cancelled reminders are deleted from the DB. On the next cron run the same rows are re-processed; the previously-cancelled batches now return an error themselves, so the run aborts again. The result is a poisoned queue in which no reminder is ever cancelled or removed — exactly the failure mode this PR is meant to fix. The failure is also only `console.log`ged and the endpoint still returns HTTP 200, so it is invisible to monitoring. Each reminder should be cancelled and deleted independently with its own try/catch.

title: Reschedule path still cancels at SendGrid immediately, so rescheduled bookings are not fixed
body: For rescheduled bookings the old reminders are cancelled with `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`, i.e. `immediateDelete = true`, which performs the direct `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` call. That is precisely the call that silently fails once SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation limit is reached (the root cause described in the PR). Because the `cancelled` flag is not set and the reminder row is not deleted in that branch, the CRON job will never retry the cancellation, so the reminder email for the old (rescheduled-away) booking is still delivered. The PR title claims to fix rescheduled bookings, but this path bypasses the new deferred-cancellation mechanism entirely.

title: immediateDelete branch cancels at SendGrid but never deletes the reminder row
body: In the `immediateDelete` branch the function returns right after the SendGrid cancel request, without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row and without setting `cancelled`. Callers that rely on the function to clean up (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts`, where the original booking is kept) leave behind rows with `scheduled: true` and a stale `referenceId` pointing at a cancelled batch. These rows only disappear when the CRON's `deleteMany` eventually removes reminders whose `scheduledDate` has passed, and in the meantime there is no record that the cancellation needs retrying if the SendGrid request failed. The function name (`delete...`) and the other two branches (delete row / flag row) make this inconsistency a correctness problem, not just cosmetics.

title: Reminder cancellation promises are no longer awaited
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async and are invoked inside `forEach` without `await` (the previous code collected the Prisma promises and awaited them in `Promise.all`). Nothing in the handler guarantees these DB writes (setting `cancelled: true`, deleting SMS reminder rows, Twilio cancellations) complete before the request returns. In a serverless deployment the execution context can be frozen as soon as the handler resolves, so the reminder may never be flagged as cancelled and the workflow email will still be sent — the exact bug being fixed. The same pattern was introduced in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (requestReschedule) and `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts`; in the latter the surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch anything either because the promise is not awaited.

title: Workflow/step deletion still relies on immediate SendGrid cancellation with no retry possible
body: When a workflow is deleted (line 214) or a step is removed (line 521), reminders are cancelled with `immediateDelete = true` and immediately afterwards the workflow/step is deleted, which cascade-deletes the `WorkflowReminder` rows. If the direct `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` call fails — the failure mode this PR addresses, and failures are only `console.log`ged — the scheduled emails are still delivered and the DB record needed to retry the cancellation is gone. Deleting a workflow with many upcoming reminders can also exceed SendGrid's pending-cancellation limit in one burst, reintroducing the original bug for this path.

title: remindersToCancel query is not restricted to EMAIL reminders with a referenceId
body: The query selects every `WorkflowReminder` with `cancelled: true`, without filtering on `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` or on a non-null `referenceId`, and then posts `reminder.referenceId` as a SendGrid `batch_id`. Today only email reminders ever get the flag, but any row that is flagged with a Twilio SID or a null reference (now or after a future change) will produce a SendGrid 400 which, given the shared try/catch, aborts the whole cancellation batch (see the loop issue). Add the method/referenceId filters to make the query match the intent stated in the comment.

title: Unused `Prisma` import and malformed import formatting
body: The import list was changed to a value import that now includes `Prisma`, but after removing the `Prisma.BatchPayload` usages `Prisma` is no longer referenced anywhere in the file, so this is an unused import that will trip `no-unused-vars` in CI. The entry also lacks the trailing comma (`TimeUnit,\n  Prisma\n}`), which prettier will flag. Both will fail the lint/format check.

title: New cron query on `cancelled`/`scheduledDate` has no supporting index
body: The migration adds `cancelled BOOLEAN` with no default and no index, while the cron now runs `findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } } })` every 15 minutes against `WorkflowReminder`, a table that grows with every booking. With no index on (`cancelled`, `scheduledDate`) this is a full table scan on each run. Making the column `BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false` (and the Prisma field `Boolean @default(false)`) would also avoid the three-state null/false/true semantics that every future query has to account for.

title: No test coverage for the new deferred cancellation flow
body: The fix introduces a new state machine (flag `cancelled` on cancel/reschedule → cron cancels at SendGrid within one hour → delete row) spread across the cancel handler, the reschedule handler, the workflow router and this cron endpoint, but no test is added. Given that the previous attempt at this fix (#6991) shipped broken and silently stopped cancelling emails, at least a unit test for `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (each of the three branches) and for the cron's cancellation loop (including a failing SendGrid request not blocking the remaining reminders) would prevent another silent regression.

title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation loop and prevents all row deletions
body: The cancellation loop (`for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)`) is wrapped in a single try/catch. The `await client.request(...)` call is the first statement in the loop body, so any failure for one reminder (invalid/expired `batch_id`, a batch that is already in `cancel` status, a 401, or SendGrid's 100-pending-cancellation cap being reached) throws out of the loop. Consequences: (a) every remaining reminder in `remindersToCancel` is skipped for this run, (b) `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` on line 74 is never reached, so even the reminders that *were* successfully cancelled keep `cancelled = true` in the DB, and (c) on the next run the same poison record is fetched again and fails again, so cancellation is permanently broken for every reminder behind it. Since the batch row is never deleted after a successful cancel in this scenario, re-cancelling an already-cancelled batch on the next run is itself likely to error, making the deadlock self-sustaining. Each iteration needs its own try/catch (and the delete should happen per-item), so one bad record cannot block the rest.

title: remindersToCancel query is not restricted to EMAIL reminders or to rows with a referenceId
body: `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } } })` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` filter and no `referenceId: { not: null }` filter, unlike the `deleteMany` above it. Any non-email row (or any row with a null `referenceId`) that ever ends up with `cancelled = true` will be POSTed to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` with a Twilio SID or `null` as `batch_id`. SendGrid will reject it, and because of the single try/catch around the loop that aborts all remaining cancellations (see the loop issue), one such row permanently breaks email cancellation. There is also no `take` limit, so a large backlog is processed sequentially with one HTTP request each, risking a serverless timeout mid-loop.

title: Deferring cancellation to a 15-minute cron leaves reminders that are due soon uncancellable
body: Cancellation is now only performed by this cron for reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour, and the `deleteMany` at line 34 unconditionally removes every EMAIL reminder with `scheduledDate <= now` (including rows with `cancelled = true`) before the cancellation block runs. If a booking is cancelled or rescheduled less than one cron interval before the reminder's send time (e.g. 10 minutes before), the next run happens after `scheduledDate` has passed: the row is deleted by `deleteMany` and the reminder email is delivered. Even when the run lands a few minutes before the send time, SendGrid only honours cancellation of a scheduled send up to ~10 minutes before `send_at`, so the cancel request is rejected. This is a regression versus cancelling immediately and reintroduces exactly the symptom this PR is meant to fix for short-notice cancellations.

title: client.setApiKey() is never called in this handler, so the new cancel requests may be unauthenticated
body: This file only calls `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)`. `@sendgrid/mail` keeps its own internal client instance, whereas the `client` default export from `@sendgrid/client` used on line 57 (and line 188) is a separate singleton; `emailReminderManager.ts` explicitly calls `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` for this reason. Unless the key is set on that singleton by some other imported module, every `client.request()` here runs without an Authorization header and returns 401 — which, combined with the loop-wide try/catch, means no scheduled email is ever cancelled and the entire fix silently does nothing (only a `console.log`). Add `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` next to `sgMail.setApiKey`.

title: immediateDelete path has no fallback and leaves the WorkflowReminder row behind
body: In the `immediateDelete` branch the SendGrid cancel request is issued and the function returns without deleting the reminder row and without setting `cancelled = true`. Two problems: (1) if the request fails — which is precisely what happens when SendGrid's limit of 100 pending cancellations is hit, the scenario this PR describes — the error is swallowed by the outer `catch` and nothing records the intent to cancel, so the new cron fallback will never pick the reminder up and the reminder email is still delivered; (2) on success the row stays in the DB with `scheduled = true` and a dead `referenceId` until the cron's `deleteMany` eventually removes it, whereas the previous code deleted it. At minimum this branch should also mark/delete the row so there is a retry path.

title: Reschedules still use the immediate SendGrid cancel, so rescheduled-booking reminders remain broken
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` passes `immediateDelete = true` for the reschedule path. The PR's own diagnosis is that immediate `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends { status: "cancel" }` calls accumulate as pending cancellations and start failing once 100 are pending. Rescheduling is one of the two cases named in the PR title, and it is a high-volume path, so it keeps filling that quota and keeps failing silently (the error is only `console.log`ged in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`), which both leaves the old reminder scheduled and can push the quota over the limit so that other cancellations (including the cron's) fail too. Reschedules should use the same deferred `cancelled = true` mechanism as cancellations.

title: Reminder cancellation promises are not awaited, so the cancelled flag may never be persisted
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` are async but are invoked inside a `forEach` without awaiting, and the promises are no longer collected into `prismaPromises` as the deleted `remindersToDelete` array was. The whole fix now depends on a DB write (`cancelled = true`) performed in a floating promise; in a serverless deployment the function can be frozen/terminated once the handler returns, so the update can be lost and the reminder email will still be sent. The same pattern exists in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (requestReschedule) and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`. In `handleNewBooking.ts` the surrounding `try/catch` (lines 964-975) is additionally dead code: because the calls are not awaited, it can never catch their failures. These calls should be awaited (e.g. `await Promise.all(reminders.map(...))`).

title: cancelled column is nullable with no default and no index for the cron query
body: `cancelled Boolean?` (and the matching migration `ADD COLUMN "cancelled" BOOLEAN` with no default) gives the column three states (null/false/true) where only a boolean flag is needed, so consumers must remember that `cancelled: false` and `cancelled: null` both mean "not cancelled". In addition, `WorkflowReminder` has no index covering `(cancelled, scheduledDate)` or `scheduledDate`, and the cron now runs `findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } } })` every 15 minutes over a table that grows with every booking/workflow step, forcing a sequential scan each run. Consider `Boolean @default(false)` plus an index on the fields the cron filters on.

title: Import block is not prettier-formatted and an unrelated commented-out block was re-indented
body: `Prisma` is added to the import list without a trailing comma (line 9), and the previously type-only `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise }` is turned into a value import even though both are only used in type positions. The same diff also re-indents the large commented-out `testAction` block (lines ~900-1010), which is unrelated to this change. The file is otherwise prettier-formatted, so the formatting check in CI will fail, and the comment reflow makes the diff hard to review.

title: No test covers the new cancellation flow
body: The new two-phase cancellation (mark `cancelled = true` on booking cancel/reschedule, then have the cron cancel at SendGrid and delete the row) is untested. The previous attempt at this fix (#6991) used the SendGrid API incorrectly and regressed silently in production; a test asserting that (a) cancelling a booking sets `cancelled = true` on its email reminders instead of deleting them and (b) the cron picks up only EMAIL reminders due within the window, cancels each and deletes the row even when one of them fails, would catch the loop-abort and filter problems noted above and prevent a repeat regression.

title: immediateDelete path keeps the old failure mode and leaves the reminder row behind
body:
When `immediateDelete` is true (used by the reschedule path in `handleNewBooking.ts:968`, the workflow-delete path and the deleted-step path in `workflows.tsx:214/521`) the function still performs a synchronous `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends { status: "cancel" }` and then returns.

Two problems:
1. This is exactly the call the PR description identifies as unreliable (SendGrid keeps cancelled batches in `scheduled_sends` and caps pending cancellations at 100). Any failure is swallowed by the surrounding `catch` that only `console.log`s, and because the row is neither marked `cancelled` nor deleted, the new CRON-based retry mechanism will never pick it up. The reminder email for the rescheduled booking is therefore still sent – the exact bug this PR claims to fix for rescheduled bookings.
2. Unlike the `!referenceId` branch (which deletes the row) and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` (which deletes the row), this branch leaves the `WorkflowReminder` row in the DB pointing at the old/cancelled booking until the cron's `deleteMany` eventually removes it when `scheduledDate` has passed.

For reschedules it would be safer to use the same deferred mechanism (set `cancelled: true`) instead of the one-shot immediate cancel.

title: Reminder cancellation is now fire-and-forget and may never be committed
body:
The previous code pushed `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany(...)` into `prismaPromises` and awaited them before returning. Now `deleteScheduledEmailReminder()` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder()` are async functions invoked inside `forEach` without `await` and their promises are never collected, so the handler can return its 200 response while the `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true } })` (or the Twilio cancel + row delete) is still in flight. In a serverless deployment the function can be frozen/terminated right after the response, so the `cancelled` flag is never persisted and the reminder email is still delivered for the cancelled booking. Errors are also swallowed inside the helpers, so this fails silently.

The same pattern was introduced at `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:488` (where `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` was removed) and `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966`. These calls should be collected and awaited.

title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation batch and skips all DB deletes
body: The `for` loop over `remindersToCancel` is wrapped in a single `try/catch`. If `client.request` throws for one reminder (invalid/expired batch id, rate limit, SendGrid 4xx/5xx), the loop is abandoned: every remaining reminder in this run is not cancelled, and – because `prisma.workflowReminder.delete()` returns a lazy `PrismaPromise` that is only executed when awaited at line 74 – none of the already-cancelled reminders are deleted either. A single permanently failing `referenceId` therefore blocks cancellation of every other reminder on every subsequent cron run, which reproduces the "reminders still sent" bug this PR fixes. Each iteration should have its own try/catch (and the delete should be awaited per reminder). The query also has no `take` limit, so a large backlog can exceed the function timeout.

title: Deferred cancellation can miss SendGrid's cancellation deadline for imminent reminders
body: Cancelling/rescheduling now never cancels the SendGrid send immediately; it only sets `cancelled: true` and relies on the `scheduleEmailReminders` cron (runs every 15 min, cancels reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour). SendGrid only honours a cancellation submitted sufficiently far ahead of the scheduled send (documented as at least 10 minutes). If a booking is cancelled, say, 12 minutes before the reminder's `sendAt`, the next cron tick can be up to 15 minutes later – i.e. after the send time – so the reminder email is still delivered for a cancelled/rescheduled booking. Consider cancelling immediately (and still marking `cancelled: true` so the cron can retry) when `scheduledDate` is close to now.

title: Cancellation query is not restricted to scheduled SendGrid email reminders
body: `remindersToCancel` selects every `WorkflowReminder` with `cancelled: true`, without filtering `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` or `referenceId: { not: null }`. The `cancelled` column is on the shared model, so any SMS row (or a row with a null `referenceId`) that ever gets `cancelled: true` would be sent to SendGrid as `batch_id: <twilio sid|null>`; the request fails and, per the single shared try/catch around the loop, aborts all remaining cancellations. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` and `referenceId: { not: null }` to the where clause.

title: Unused `Prisma` import and type-only identifiers moved into a value import
body: `Prisma` is added to the `@prisma/client` value import but is no longer used anywhere in the file (the only remaining use, `PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>[]`, was deleted in this diff), which will fail `no-unused-vars` in CI. The same import also converts the previous `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise }` into a value import of type-only identifiers (also done in `handleNewBooking.ts:1-10` for `App`, `Credential`, `EventTypeCustomInput`, `Prisma`), which conflicts with the `import type` convention used throughout the repo/`consistent-type-imports`. Additionally the new member is added without a trailing comma (`Prisma\n} from "@prisma/client";`), so the prettier check will fail. The unrelated re-indentation of the large commented-out `testAction` block (lines ~901-1009) suggests this file was taken from an older branch; please rebase.

title: New `cancelled` flag is nullable with no index backing the cron query
body: `cancelled Boolean?` (and the migration `ADD COLUMN "cancelled" BOOLEAN`) has no default, so every existing and newly created row stores NULL and all call sites must use `cancelled: true` rather than a boolean comparison (easy to get wrong later – `@default(false)` would be safer). More importantly, `WorkflowReminder` has no index on `cancelled`/`scheduledDate`, yet the new cron query `findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } } })` – plus the existing `deleteMany` and unscheduled-reminder scan – runs every 15 minutes over a table that grows with every booking, resulting in repeated full table scans.

title: Dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly, so nothing is actually loaded lazily
body: The object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")`, `import("./caldavcalendar")`, … directly as property values. `import()` is invoked at module-evaluation time, so the moment anything imports `@calcom/app-store` all 28 app modules are requested and evaluated — exactly as before, only now asynchronously. The server/serverless bundle still contains every app and cold start still pays for loading all of them, so the PR's stated goal (async/lazy import of app packages) is not achieved while every call site has been forced to become `async`. To get real laziness the values need to be thunks (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) resolved on demand, ideally with memoization.

title: Rejected app-module imports become unhandled rejections at module load
body: All 28 `import()` promises are created when the module is evaluated, but most are never awaited (only the one app matching a credential/dirName is). If any app module throws while being evaluated (missing env var, bad top-level code, transitive import error), its promise rejects with no handler attached. In Node >= 15 an unhandled rejection terminates the process by default, so a single broken app module can take down the whole web/API server, and the failure is reported at module-init time with no connection to the call site that would have needed that app. Previously a failing app module produced a synchronous error on import of `@calcom/app-store`, which was at least attributable and contained.

title: getCalendarCredentials creates floating promises and changes the type of `calendar`
body: `getCalendar(credential)` is now async, but it is still invoked unconditionally inside the `flatMap` before the `app.variant === "calendar"` check. For every non-`calendar` variant credential the returned promise is created and immediately discarded; if it rejects (e.g. the app module fails to load) it becomes an unhandled rejection, which can crash the Node process. In addition, the `calendar` property of the returned items is now `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`; this is a silent contract change for any consumer of `getCalendarCredentials()` other than `getConnectedCalendars` (which was updated), and such a consumer would call methods on a Promise at runtime. Move the `getCalendar` call behind the variant check and audit/convert all consumers.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions are fire-and-forget and never awaited
body: In the recurring/`allRemainingBookings` branch the credentials are iterated with `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); … apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })`. The callback's promise is discarded, so the `await getCalendar(...)` and the subsequent `calendar.deleteEvent(...)` calls run after `forEach` returns. By the time `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) copies `apiDeletes`, the array is still empty, so the handler returns "Booking successfully cancelled" without waiting for any external calendar event to be removed — in a serverless runtime the function can be frozen/torn down first, leaving cancelled recurring bookings still present on users' calendars. Errors from these calls also escape as unhandled rejections. The sibling non-recurring branch in this same diff was correctly converted to `for (const credential of …)`; this branch needs the same treatment (and should push the promise, not the awaited result).

title: requestReschedule: calendar/video cancellation is now an un-awaited async forEach
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) … })` discards every callback promise. The mutation continues to send the reschedule-request email and webhooks and returns while the `getCalendar` import and the `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls are still pending, so in a serverless environment the previous calendar entries and video meetings may never be deleted. Any error thrown inside the callback is now an unhandled rejection (it can terminate the process) rather than something the caller can observe. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => …))` instead.

title: try/catch around the cancellation loop is dead code after converting the callback to async
body: The callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` was made `async` so it can `await getCalendar(...)`, but the callback's promise is thrown away. The enclosing `try { … } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }` can therefore never observe a failure from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting`: those rejections surface as unhandled promise rejections (process-level crash risk in modern Node) and are silently lost from the logs. The function also returns `true` and sends the reschedule email before the deletions have completed, so the stale calendar/video entries may never be removed. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => …))` inside the try block.

title: try/catch around the cancellation loop is dead code after converting the callback to async
body: Same defect as in `vital/lib/reschedule.ts`: `forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); … })` discards the callback promises, so the surrounding `try/catch` that logs errors can never fire, failures from `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` become unhandled rejections, and the function proceeds to send the reschedule email and return `true` before the external calendar/video entries have actually been deleted. Await the work explicitly (e.g. `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => …))`) inside the try block.

title: Commented template entry points at a non-existent path
body: The commented-out example was changed from `./_example` to `// example: import("./example")`. The app template directory is `_example`, so a developer copying this line as a guide for registering a new app will reference a path that does not exist. Keep the directory name accurate (`import("./_example")`).

title: Dynamic imports are started eagerly, so nothing is actually lazy-loaded (and 28 floating promises are created)
body:
Every value in `appStore` is the *result* of calling `import(...)` during module evaluation, not a thunk. As soon as anything imports `@calcom/app-store`, all 28 app packages begin loading exactly as before – the only difference is that the caller now has to `await`. The stated goal (deferring app loading) requires storing factories, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and invoking them on demand (optionally memoising).

Second, this creates 28 promises with no handler attached. If any single app module throws while being evaluated (missing env var, broken transitive dep, etc.), the resulting rejection stays unhandled until some code happens to `await` that specific key. Under Node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` (Node >= 15) that terminates the server process, even though the failing app may never be used by the request. With the previous static imports a broken app failed loudly and synchronously at import time; now it can crash an unrelated request path at an arbitrary later moment.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions remain fire-and-forget while the sibling branch was fixed
body: In the recurring branch, deletions are still issued inside `credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... })`. Because `forEach` ignores the returned promise, nothing ever awaits these callbacks: `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)` (line 467) runs long after `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 has already resolved with an empty/partial `apiDeletes`. The handler therefore returns `{ message: "Booking successfully cancelled." }` before the external calendar events are deleted; in a serverless/edge runtime the function is frozen or torn down and the remote events are orphaned, and any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection. The PR converted the equivalent non-credentialId branch just below (lines 480-483) to a `for ... of` loop with `await`, so this branch is now inconsistent; it needs the same treatment (collect the `deleteEvent` promises synchronously into `apiDeletes` or `await` them in a `for ... of`).

title: `forEach(async ...)` makes the surrounding try/catch dead and turns errors into unhandled rejections
body: The callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` was made `async` so it can `await getCalendar(...)`. `forEach` discards the returned promise, so the enclosing `try { ... } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }` can no longer observe anything that happens inside: previously a synchronous throw from `getCalendar` was caught and logged, now it (and any `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` rejection) escapes as an unhandled promise rejection, which under Node's default unhandled-rejection handling can kill the process. In addition, the remote delete calls are no longer even *issued* before `Reschedule` returns, because they are now behind an `await`, so the calendar/video events may never be cancelled. Use `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { ... await ... }` inside the existing try/catch, or `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.

title: `forEach(async ...)` makes the surrounding try/catch dead and turns errors into unhandled rejections
body: Same problem as in `vital/lib/reschedule.ts`: the `forEach` callback is now `async`, so the `try/catch` wrapping it (lines 124-139) can never catch a failure of `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` – those rejections now surface as unhandled promise rejections instead of being logged. The deletions are also no longer started synchronously, so `Reschedule` can resolve and the request finish before the external calendar/video events are cancelled. Replace with a `for ... of` loop and `await` (or `await Promise.all(map(...))`) inside the try block.

title: requestReschedule awaits inside `forEach`, so calendar/video cancellations are unawaited and errors are unhandled
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })` is fire-and-forget: the mutation continues to send the reschedule email, fire webhooks and return while the `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls have not even been issued yet (they are now gated behind the awaited `getCalendar`). There is no try/catch here at all, so a failing credential or app import becomes an unhandled promise rejection in the tRPC server process. Iterate with `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered)` and `await`, or collect promises and `await Promise.all(...)` with a `.catch` so failures are logged.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in `calendar`, changing the contract for all consumers
body: `getCalendar` became async but line 28 still calls it without awaiting, so each item returned by the exported `getCalendarCredentials` now carries `calendar: Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` in this file was updated to `await item.calendar`; every other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` (it is a public export of `@calcom/core`) that touches `.calendar` directly will now operate on a Promise and fail at runtime (`item.calendar.listCalendars is not a function`) unless TypeScript happens to flag it. All call sites need to be audited, or `getCalendarCredentials` should itself become async and resolve the calendars before returning. Related risk: the promises created here are left floating; if a dynamic app import rejects and nobody awaits that item, the rejection is unhandled and can terminate the process.

title: Template comment points at a non-existent path
body: The example comment was changed from `// import * as example from "./_example";` to `// example: import("./example"),`. The directory in the repo is `_example`, so a contributor copying this template line will add an import for a path that does not exist and get a build failure. It should read `example: import("./_example")` (matching whatever shape the final map uses).

title: Dynamic imports are started eagerly, so nothing is actually lazily loaded
body: `appStore` is now an object literal whose values are the *results* of calling `import("./app")` at module-evaluation time. Calling `import()` immediately starts loading the module, so every single app package (applecalendar, googlecalendar, stripepayment, …) is still pulled in as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported — the only thing that changed is that consumers now have to `await` the already in-flight promise. The PR's goal of async/lazy app loading is not achieved, while the extra `async`/`await` plumbing added across CalendarManager, videoClient, handleCancelBooking, bookings.tsx etc. buys nothing. To actually defer loading, the map must hold thunks (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and call sites must invoke them, e.g. `await appStore[key]()`.

title: Rejected app-import promises are created with no handler attached (unhandled rejection at startup)
body: Each value in `appStore` is a promise created at module load and stored for an indefinite amount of time before any consumer awaits it. If any one app module fails to evaluate (missing/incorrect peer dependency, module-scope code that throws, bad env configuration), the corresponding promise rejects with no `.catch()` attached, producing an unhandled promise rejection at process start — which terminates the Node process on Node >= 15. Previously a broken app module failed loudly and synchronously at import time with a clear stack trace; now it can either kill the server or silently surface later as a generic "Could not get connected calendars" error from `getConnectedCalendars`'s catch block. Promises for apps that are never used are never awaited at all, so their rejections are always unhandled.

title: Example comment points at a non-existent path
body: The template comment was changed from `// import * as example from "./_example";` to `// example: import("./example"),`. The example app lives in the `_example` directory, so anyone uncommenting/copying this line will get a module-not-found error. The commented path should be `./_example`.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in the `calendar` field, changing its public contract
body: `getCalendarCredentials` is exported and returns `{ integration, credential, calendar }`. Because `getCalendar` became async, `calendar` is now `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` in this file was updated to `await item.calendar`; any other caller that reads `.calendar` keeps a promise, which is always truthy, so guards like `if (!calendar)` silently pass and subsequent `calendar.listCalendars()` style calls fail at runtime. Additionally, these promises are created eagerly for every credential inside a non-async function, so if a caller only needs `integration`/`credential`, a rejected `getCalendar` promise is never handled. Either make the function async and await the calendars, or keep the field lazy (a thunk) and update all consumers.

title: Recurring-cancellation branch still uses forEach(async) so calendar deletions are never awaited
body: In the recurring/allRemainingBookings branch the code iterates credentials with `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); … apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })`. `forEach` does not await the async callbacks, so the handler continues immediately and `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at the end of the handler runs while `apiDeletes` is still empty for this path. Consequently, for recurring bookings the external calendar events are deleted fire-and-forget (and in a serverless runtime may never be deleted at all, since the response is returned before the awaited dynamic app import resolves), and any `deleteEvent` failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of being surfaced. The adjacent legacy branch in this same PR was correctly converted to `for (const credential of calendarCredentials)`; the same conversion is needed here.

title: requestReschedule deletes calendar/video events in an unawaited forEach(async) callback
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` is not awaited, so the mutation proceeds to send the reschedule-request email, fire webhooks and return before the deletions are even initiated. Previously `getCalendar` was synchronous, so the `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` requests were at least started before the handler continued; now the first thing the callback does is await a dynamic module import, meaning in a serverless/edge runtime the function can be frozen or torn down after the response and the stale calendar entries / video meetings will never be removed. Rejections are also unobserved (unhandled promise rejection). Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => …))` or a `for … of` loop.

title: forEach(async) makes the surrounding try/catch dead and leaves deletions unawaited
body: The loop was changed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); … })`. The enclosing `try { … } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }` can never observe errors thrown inside an async callback, so the explicit error logging is dead code and failures surface as unhandled promise rejections. The function also continues to send the reschedule email and return `true` before the awaited dynamic app import resolves, so the calendar/video cancellations are fire-and-forget and may not run to completion in a short-lived (serverless) process. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => …))` so the try/catch works and the work is actually awaited.

title: forEach(async) makes the surrounding try/catch dead and leaves deletions unawaited
body: Same problem as in the vital app: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); … })` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that can no longer catch anything, because errors raised inside the async callbacks reject the (discarded) returned promises instead of propagating synchronously — they become unhandled promise rejections. Additionally the booking is marked cancelled and the reschedule email is sent before the awaited dynamic app import resolves, so the external calendar/video cancellation requests may never be issued. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => …))`.

title: Date override on a day makes every slot available, skipping busy-time checks
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new block sets `dateOverrideExist = true` for any date override whose date matches the slot's date, and then `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` returns early. This return happens *before* the `busy.every(...)` loop, so on any day that has a date override the function reports every slot as available and completely ignores existing bookings, external calendar busy times, event buffers and reserved (`selectedSlots`) entries. Any host with a date override can therefore be double-booked. The override check should only narrow availability, not short-circuit the busy evaluation.

title: working-hours check rejects slots when a user has more than one availability block per day
body: `workingHours.find((workingHour) => ...)` returns truthy as soon as *one* working-hours entry does not contain the slot, and the result is interpreted as "slot is outside of working hours" -> unavailable. A user whose schedule has several blocks on the same weekday (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00) produces two `WorkingHours` entries with the same `days`, so a 10:00 slot is inside the first and outside the second and gets dropped — all slots vanish for split schedules. The same happens for schedules that cross UTC midnight, where `getWorkingHours` emits two normalized entries covering the same days. The predicate must be "no entry contains the slot" (`!workingHours.some(contains)`), not "some entry does not contain it". Note this path applies to personal events too, because single-user events are treated as fixed hosts.

title: Date-override check rejects slots when a date has multiple override ranges
body: `dateOverrides.find((date) => ...)` returns truthy for the first override that does *not* contain the slot, and that result is treated as "slot is not within the date override" -> unavailable. Cal.com allows several time ranges for the same override date (and several hosts' overrides are flattened into the same array when a team event is evaluated per host). With two ranges on one date (e.g. 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00), a slot inside the first range is outside the second, so the slot is rejected and every slot on that date disappears. The condition should be "none of the overrides for this date contain the slot".

title: `end` is computed from the slot start, so the working-hours end boundary is never enforced
body: `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(); const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` — both variables are identical; `end` was clearly meant to be the slot end (`start + eventLength`, or derived from `slotEndTime`). As written, the `end > workingHour.endTime` test only ever compares the slot *start* against the end boundary, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after them (e.g. a 60-minute slot starting 30 minutes before the day's end time) is accepted, allowing bookings that run past the host's availability.

title: Slots that only partially overlap a date override are treated as inside it
body: The override containment test marks a slot as outside the override only when `slotEndTime <= override.start` or `slotStartTime > override.end`.
