A slot that starts before the override start but ends inside it (slot 13:30-14:30 vs override 14:00-18:00) or starts inside but ends after the end (slot 17:30-18:30 vs 14:00-18:00) satisfies neither condition, so it is considered available. Combined with the early `return true` for `dateOverrideExist`, such partially overlapping slots are offered for booking outside the host's overridden availability. The correct test is `slotStartTime < override.start || slotEndTime > override.end`.

title: Override date comparison mixes server-local and UTC dates
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` formats in the *server's* local timezone (plain `dayjs(...)`, no `.utc()`), while it is compared against `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`, which is in UTC (`slotStartTime = time.utc()`). On any deployment whose process timezone is not UTC the two dates can differ by a day, so date overrides are matched to the wrong day: overrides are either ignored (making unavailable time bookable) or applied to the neighbouring day. Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` for the comparison. Tests run with TZ=UTC will not catch this.

title: Dayjs objects compared with `===`, so the zero-length (whole-day unavailable) override branch is dead code
body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly created Dayjs objects by reference, which is always false. The intent (treat an override whose start equals its end as "unavailable all day") is never executed, so the handling of whole-day "mark unavailable" overrides depends on the later, unrelated comparisons. Use `.isSame(...)` (or compare `valueOf()`).

title: Override timezone shift loses the day when it crosses midnight
body: The new override conversion reduces the shifted instant to minutes-since-midnight via `hour() * 60 + minute()`. When `offset` (invitee offset minus organizer offset) pushes the override across a day boundary — e.g. an override 22:00-23:00 in the organizer's timezone viewed by an invitee 5 hours ahead — the computed `startTime`/`endTime` wrap around to small values and are applied to the invitee's *same* day, so the override's slots are generated on the wrong day. If only one of the two endpoints wraps, `endTime < startTime` and `buildSlots` silently discards the range (`if (start >= end) continue`), so the override yields no slots at all. The day offset produced by the shift has to be carried, not discarded.

title: Missing `override.timeZone` silently falls back to the process/default timezone
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` is called with `timeZone` typed as optional (`timeZone?: string` in packages/types/schedule.d.ts). When a caller of `getSlots` passes date overrides without a `timeZone` (the type permits it, and only the slots tRPC router was updated to populate it), the dayjs timezone plugin falls back to the default/local timezone, so `organizerUtcOffset` is computed for the wrong zone and the override is shifted by an arbitrary amount instead of being treated as organizer-local. Either make `timeZone` required for date overrides or explicitly fall back to `organizerTimeZone` which is already passed into `getSlots`.

title: No test for the PR's main fix: date overrides of fixed hosts in round-robin events
body: The PR's primary claim is that date overrides of fixed hosts are now honoured for ROUND_ROBIN events (so slots where the fixed host is unavailable are no longer offered). The only new test added covers a single-user event with a different invitee timezone. There is no scenario with a ROUND_ROBIN event type, a fixed host carrying a date override and a non-fixed host available all day, which is exactly the behaviour added in `checkIfIsAvailable` and the riskiest part of the change (it currently also bypasses busy-time checks). Without such a test the regression this PR fixes can silently come back.

title: toHaveTimeSlots matcher does not compare lengths, so the new assertion can pass with missing slots
body: The matcher iterates `schedule.slots[dateString].map(...).every((actualSlotTime, index) => ...)` over the *actual* slots only and never checks that the number of returned slots equals `expectedSlots.length`. The new assertion for the Asia/Dhaka invitee would therefore still pass if the implementation returned only `08:30:00.000Z` (or any prefix of the expected list), which is precisely the kind of over-filtering the new date-override/working-hours code can cause. Add a length check to the matcher so the new timezone test actually guards against dropped slots.

title: Working-hours check uses `find` with inverted logic, rejecting valid slots for users with more than one availability block
body: `checkIfIsAvailable` rejects a slot if `workingHours.find(...)` locates *any* working-hours entry for the slot's weekday that does not contain the slot (`start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` → `return false` for the slot). `WorkingHours` is a list, and a single user routinely has several entries for the same day: a split schedule (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 UTC) yields two entries, and `getWorkingHours` additionally splits any schedule that crosses UTC midnight into two entries. With a 09:00-12:00 / 13:00-17:00 schedule, the 10:00 slot is inside the first entry but outside the second, so the second entry makes the function return `false` and the slot disappears. Because every user of a personal event is treated as a fixed host (`isFixed: !eventType.schedulingType`), this silently removes all slots for any user with a lunch break or a schedule spanning UTC midnight. The condition must be "no entry contains the slot" (`!workingHours.some(containsSlot)`), not "some entry does not contain the slot".

title: `end` is computed from slotStartTime, so the slot end is never validated against working hours
body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates the `start` expression instead of using `slotEndTime`. As a result the `end > workingHour.endTime` comparison can never detect a slot that overruns the end of a host's working hours. For a round-robin event where the fixed host works 09:00-12:00 and a round-robin host works 09:00-17:00, the aggregate working hours produce an 11:30 slot; for a 60-minute event it ends at 12:30, outside the fixed host's availability, yet this check passes it — exactly the over-booking of fixed hosts this PR is meant to prevent.

title: Date-override check rejects slots when a date has multiple override ranges
body: The `dateOverrides.find(...)` predicate returns `true` as soon as *one* override entry for the slot's date does not contain the slot, and the outer `if` then returns `false` (slot unavailable). Cal.com allows several time ranges for a single date override day, and `getUserAvailability` returns one `{start,end}` entry per range. With overrides 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00 on the same date, a 09:30 slot is inside the first range but `slotEndTime.isBefore(14:00)` is true for the second range, so the slot is dropped; symmetrically the 14:30 slot is dropped by the first range. The net effect is that no slots at all are offered on days with more than one override range. The check must be "the slot is contained in none of the ranges for that date" rather than "some range does not contain the slot".

title: Override containment check ignores the slot end, allowing bookings that overrun the override window
body: Within the matched date override only two rejections exist: the slot ends before/at the override start, or the slot *start* is strictly after the override end. A slot that starts inside the override but finishes after it is therefore accepted: with an override of 09:00-11:00 and a 60-minute event, the 10:30 slot (ending 11:30) is reported as available. Likewise a slot starting exactly at the override end (11:00) passes because `isAfter` is not inclusive. For round-robin events this re-introduces the problem the PR fixes — the fixed host gets booked outside their date override. The condition should require `slotEndTime` to be ≤ override end (and use `isSameOrAfter` for the start comparison).

title: Override date comparison mixes server-local and UTC formatting
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` builds a dayjs in the *server's local* timezone, while `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` is UTC (`slotStartTime = time.utc()`). On any deployment whose process timezone is not UTC the two date strings disagree near midnight, so `dateOverrideExist` is not set for the correct day: overrides are silently ignored (host booked when unavailable) or applied to the wrong day (all slots of a normal day dropped). Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` so both sides are evaluated in the same zone.

title: Dead branch: dayjs instances compared with `===`
body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly-created objects by reference, which is always false, so this branch never executes. It was presumably meant to handle a zero-length override (a date marked completely unavailable) via `isSame()`/`valueOf()`. As written the "whole day blocked" case falls through to the generic range checks, making the behaviour accidental and hard to reason about; it also means the intent of the code is not actually implemented.

title: Timezone-shifted override wraps across midnight and lands on the wrong day
body: `startTime`/`endTime` are derived as `hour()*60 + minute()` after shifting the override by `inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset`, and are then applied relative to `startOfInviteeDay`. When the shift pushes the override past midnight the minute-of-day silently wraps and the override is applied to the wrong date. Example: organizer in UTC with an override 22:00-23:30 on day D, invitee in Asia/Kolkata (offset +330). The shifted time is 03:30-05:00 on D+1, giving startTime=210, which is added to the invitee's start of day D (18:30 UTC on D-1) producing slots at 22:00 UTC on D-1 — a full day earlier than the real override. In the opposite direction (negative offset crossing back over midnight) the wrap can make `endTime < startTime`, in which case `buildSlots` drops the range (`if (start >= end) continue;`) and the override produces no slots at all.

title: `override.timeZone` is optional; a missing value silently uses dayjs' default timezone
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` relies on the new optional `timeZone` field added to `TimeRange` in packages/types/schedule.d.ts. When a caller of `getSlots` passes date overrides without `timeZone` (the field is `timeZone?: string`), `.tz(undefined)` falls back to dayjs' default/guessed timezone (the machine's zone), so `organizerUtcOffset` is computed from an unrelated zone and the override is shifted by an arbitrary amount instead of keeping the previous UTC interpretation. Either make `timeZone` required for date overrides in this code path or default explicitly to `"UTC"`/the organizer timezone already passed into `getSlots`.

title: Expensive per-slot timezone offset computation in the hot slot-filtering loop
body: `checkIfIsAvailable` is invoked once per candidate slot per host (hundreds to thousands of times per `getSchedule` call on this public endpoint). For every invocation and every date override it calls `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()` (Intl-backed, comparatively slow) and constructs ~5 additional dayjs objects, even though `utcOffset` and the converted override start/end are independent of the slot being tested. These values should be computed once per host/override before the slot loop (e.g. precomputed alongside `userAvailability`) rather than inside the predicate.

title: No test covers the main fix (fixed-host date overrides in round-robin) or the new edge cases
body: The only test added exercises a single-range date override for a personal event viewed from a second timezone. The headline behaviour of the PR — a fixed host's date override limiting the slots of a ROUND_ROBIN event (new `dateOverrides`/`workingHours` handling inside `checkIfIsAvailable`) — has no coverage, so the fixed-host filtering path is unverified. The new code paths that are most likely to regress are also untested: a schedule with two availability blocks on the same day (currently removes all slots, see the `workingHours.find` logic), a date with multiple override ranges, and a slot that overruns the end of an override. Adding a scenario with `hosts: [{isFixed: true,...},{isFixed: false,...}]`, `schedulingType: "ROUND_ROBIN"` and an override on the fixed host would catch these.

title: Date override day short-circuits the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls inside the override range, the function does `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` (line 133-135) and returns before ever evaluating `busy.every(...)`. This means that on any day that has a date override, existing bookings and external calendar busy times are completely ignored, so already-booked slots are offered again and can be double booked. The override check should only narrow availability (continue to the busy check) rather than grant it unconditionally.

title: Working-hours check rejects a slot if ANY working-hours range does not contain it
body: The new block uses `workingHours.find(workingHour => ... slot outside this range ... return true)` and treats a truthy result as "slot is outside of working hours" (lines 138-151). `getUserAvailability`/`getWorkingHours` returns one entry per availability row, so a user with a split schedule (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 on the same days) has two entries for that weekday. A 10:00 slot is inside the first range but outside the second, so `find` returns the second entry and the slot is discarded. Because fixed hosts include the single user of personal event types, every user with more than one availability range per day will lose all of their slots. The condition needs to be "no range contains the slot" (`!workingHours.some(contains)`), not "some range does not contain it".

title: `end` is computed from the slot start, so the slot end is never validated
body: At lines 141-142 both `start` and `end` are computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`; `end` should be derived from `slotEndTime` (slot start + eventLength). As written the `end > workingHour.endTime` comparison is equivalent to the `start` comparison, so a slot that begins inside working hours but runs past the end of the working-hours window is never rejected (e.g. a 60-minute event starting at 16:45 for a 09:00-17:00 schedule).

title: Multiple date-override ranges on the same day make all slots unavailable
body: The `dateOverrides.find(...)` callback (lines 106-127) returns `true` when the slot is *outside* a given override range, and any truthy result makes the whole function return `false` (unavailable). Cal.com allows several time ranges for the same override date (e.g. 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00); a 09:30 slot is inside the first range but outside the second, so `find` matches the second range and the slot is dropped. The logic must consider the union of all override ranges for the day (slot is unavailable only if it is outside *every* range for that date).

title: Override/slot day comparison mixes server-local time with UTC
body: Line 110 compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` with `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`. `slotStartTime` is a UTC dayjs object, but `dayjs(date.start)` is in the process-local timezone, so `.format()` renders the override date in whatever `TZ` the server runs with. On a server that is not UTC, overrides whose converted instant lies near midnight UTC will be compared against a different calendar day, so the override is silently not detected (falling through to the normal working-hours path) or matched on the wrong day. Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` so both sides are formatted in the same zone.

title: Dayjs instances compared with `===`, condition is always false
body: Line 114 compares two freshly created Dayjs objects with `===` (`dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)`), which compares object references and is therefore always false. The intended case — a zero-length override marking the whole day unavailable — is never detected by this branch; use `.isSame()` (or compare `valueOf()`). As written the branch is dead code and gives a false impression of handling that case.

title: Override time conversion loses the day component, producing slots on the wrong day/time
body: The new override conversion (lines 216-224) computes minutes-since-midnight as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...minute()`. When the timezone shift moves the override across midnight (e.g. organizer 10:00-11:00 in Asia/Kolkata viewed by an America/Los_Angeles invitee, offset = -750 min), the converted instant lands on the previous day but only hour/minute are kept, so the override is interpreted as 21:30-22:30 of the invitee's current day — roughly 24 hours away from the real time. For eastward shifts the same truncation can also yield `startTime > endTime`, producing no slots at all. The conversion needs to account for the day rollover (e.g. compute the diff in minutes from `startOfInviteeDay`) instead of truncating to hour/minute.

title: Override timezone is optional but used unguarded in `dayjs().tz()`
body: `override.timeZone` is declared optional in `TimeRange` (packages/types/schedule.d.ts) and is only populated by the new code in the slots tRPC router. Line 212 calls `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)`; with `undefined` dayjs silently falls back to the default/guessed timezone, so `organizerUtcOffset` becomes the server's offset and the computed `offset` shifts override slots by an arbitrary amount for any other caller of `getSlots` that passes `dateOverrides` without `timeZone`. Either make `timeZone` required for overrides reaching this code path or fall back explicitly to `organizerTimeZone`. Also note `override.start.toString()` relies on parsing a non-ISO `Date#toString()` value; passing the Date directly would be safer.

title: No test for the fixed-host (round-robin) override fix, and only an eastward timezone is covered
body: The PR's primary claim is that date overrides of fixed hosts are now honoured for ROUND_ROBIN events, but the only new assertion (lines 788-804) re-queries a single-user event type with Asia/Dhaka. There is no scenario with a round-robin event type having a fixed host with a date override plus an available round-robin host, so the new `checkIfIsAvailable` override/working-hours path is untested for the case it was written for. In addition, both tested timezones are east of the organizer's (+5:30 and +6:00, a 30-minute shift), so the day-rollover case (an invitee timezone west of the organizer, e.g. America/Los_Angeles) — which is where the override conversion in packages/lib/slots.ts breaks — is not covered.

title: Migration raises NoMethodError when `embed_category` setting row is absent
body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. `site_settings` only contains rows for settings that have been explicitly changed, and the join additionally requires the stored value to still match a category *name*. For the overwhelming majority of installs (default `embed_category` of `''`, or a renamed/deleted category) the query returns zero rows, so `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration and therefore any upgrade. The same unguarded `[0]['value']` pattern is used on line 15 for `uncategorized_category_id`. Both lookups need to handle the empty-result case.

title: Migrated hosts are inserted unnormalized, so embedding silently stops working after upgrade
body: Host values are copied straight from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting with raw SQL, bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` which strips the scheme and path. The old setting legitimately contained values such as `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234` (see the removed specs in spec/models/site_setting_spec.rb). `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `URI(referer).host` (e.g. `discourse.org`) against the stored `host` column, so rows containing `http://discourse.org` will never match and previously-working embeds start raising `Discourse::InvalidAccess` after the upgrade. The migration must normalize each value (strip scheme/path) before inserting.

title: Host value interpolated directly into INSERT statement
body: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` interpolates a value taken from the database (the old `embeddable_hosts` setting, which was free-form admin input) into SQL without quoting. A value containing a single quote breaks the migration (and could execute arbitrary SQL). Use `quote(h)` / a parameterized insert.

title: `create_table ... force: true` can drop an existing table, and the migration is not reversible
body: `force: true` issues a DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating, so re-running this migration (or running it on a database that already has an `embeddable_hosts` table, e.g. created by a plugin) silently destroys existing rows. In addition, the body is defined in `change` but contains `execute` statements (data copy and `DELETE FROM site_settings`), which Rails cannot reverse: `rake db:rollback` will drop the table without restoring the deleted site settings. Use `def up` (plus an explicit `down`) and drop `force: true`.

title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is executed unconditionally in `before_validation`. If `host` is nil — e.g. `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` which may be missing — validation blows up with `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil`, returning a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `return if host.blank?` (and add a presence validation). Note also that `sub!` mutates the string in place, which mutates the caller's/params' string object; `sub` with assignment would be safer.

title: Case-insensitive host lookup compares against a non-downcased value
body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the column but not the argument. Host names in a `Referer` header are case-insensitive and browsers/servers may send mixed case (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com/page`), in which case `lower(host) = 'EvilTrout.com'` never matches and a legitimately allowed host is rejected with `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. Pass `host.downcase`.

title: Host validation regex rejects valid hosts and allows unmatchable ones
body: The format regex requires `\.[a-z]{2,5}` at the end, which rejects hosts admins can legitimately want to embed from: single-label hosts (`localhost`), TLDs longer than 5 characters (`example.engineering`, `example.technology`), and IP addresses. Conversely the regex permits an optional `:port`, but `record_for_host` compares against `URI(...).host`, which never contains a port, so a saved host like `example.com:3000` can never match a referer and silently never allows anything. The old `host_list` site setting had no such restrictions, so this is a functional regression.

title: update/destroy crash with 500 when the id does not exist
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil. `update` then calls `save_host(nil)` which does `nil.host = ...` and `destroy` (line 16) calls `nil.destroy`; both raise `NoMethodError` and produce a 500 response. These endpoints should respond 404 (e.g. `find_by!`/`raise Discourse::NotFound`) for unknown ids.

title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a no-op that pretends to save
body: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` ignores the request body entirely and just re-renders the current state, so the route registered in config/routes.rb (`put "customize/embedding"`) silently discards any submitted data while returning 200. The admin controller's `saveChanges` action (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6 line 6) calls `embedding.update({})` against it, though nothing in embedding.hbs triggers that action. Either implement the update or remove the route/action so the API does not advertise behaviour it does not have.

title: `*_ids` hydration deletes the ids even when the sideloaded collection is missing
body: In `_hydrateEmbedded`, any key matching `(.+)_ids` is now replaced: `obj[pluralize(subType)] = obj[k].map(id => _lookupSubType(...))` and `delete obj[k]` is executed unconditionally. Unlike the singular branch (which only deletes the key when hydration succeeded), this means that for any REST-serialized payload containing an `*_ids` array that is not sideloaded in the root, the original ids are lost and the model gets an array full of `undefined`. Also, if the server sends `null` for such a key, `obj[k].map` throws `TypeError: Cannot read property 'map' of null`. (`hydrated || []` on the next line is dead code since `map` always returns an array.) Only replace the key when every lookup resolves, and guard against non-array values.

title: `type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore
body: `String.prototype.replace` with a string pattern replaces a single occurrence, so `basePath` normalizes `embeddable_host` correctly but a type with more than one underscore (e.g. `some_admin_model`) still fails the `ADMIN_MODELS` lookup and would be routed to `/` instead of `/admin/`. Use `/_/g` (or `Ember.String.dasherize`).

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. The two file bodies were clearly pasted into the wrong files; this makes the fabricators undiscoverable by filename and will confuse anyone touching category fabrication.

title: New mutating admin endpoints have no behavioural tests
body: The only assertion is that the class inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. There is no coverage for `create`/`update`/`destroy` (including the default-to-uncategorized behaviour, the 500-on-missing-record paths noted above, invalid host handling) nor for access control (non-admin/anonymous requests). The same applies to spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb, which does not exercise `show`/`update` at all. Given these endpoints create the data that gates framing/embedding (a security-relevant allowlist), they should be tested.

title: Test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests that
body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer consults embeddable hosts at all (the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` check was removed), so this example passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false for a fabricated topic — not because no host exists. The name is now misleading and the example asserts nothing about hosts; it should be renamed/removed.

title: No uniqueness validation on host
body: Nothing prevents two `EmbeddableHost` rows with the same host (the migration creates no unique index either, and `before_validation` normalizes `http://example.com` and `example.com` to the same value). `record_for_host` then arbitrarily takes `.first`, so an admin editing the category of a duplicated host can see no effect on which category embedded topics are created in. Add a uniqueness validation (case-insensitive) and/or a unique index.

title: Migration raises NoMethodError when the old settings rows are absent
body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes the query always returns at least one row. On any site where `embed_category` was never set (the default was `''`, so no `site_settings` row exists at all) or where its value no longer matches a category name, the result set is empty and `[0]` is `nil`, so `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError and the whole migration aborts. The same problem exists on line 15: `uncategorized_category_id` defaults to `-1` and is normally not persisted in `site_settings`, so that fallback query also returns zero rows and crashes. Both lookups need to handle an empty result (and the resulting `category_id` must be a real category, since the column is `null: false` and `-1` points at nothing).

title: Migration copies host values verbatim, so hosts that included a scheme stop matching
body: The old `embeddable_hosts` site setting explicitly allowed entries such as `http://discourse.org` (the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped the scheme at comparison time, and the removed specs covered exactly that). This migration inserts each line directly with `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, bypassing the model's `before_validation` that strips `https?://` and paths. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` then compares `lower(host)` against `URI(...).host` (a bare hostname), so a migrated row `http://discourse.org` can never match and embedding/topic retrieval silently breaks for those sites. Because line 31 deletes the `embeddable_hosts` setting, the original data is also gone and cannot be re-migrated. Normalize the value (strip scheme/path, downcase) before inserting.

title: Host value interpolated into SQL without quoting
body: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` interpolates an admin-supplied site-setting value straight into SQL. A value containing a single quote (or any SQL metacharacter) produces a syntax error and aborts the migration mid-way — after the table was created and before the old settings are deleted — leaving the site in an inconsistent state. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` or a parameterized `execute`/model insert.

title: has_many embed: :ids does not side-load the hosts the client needs
body: With ActiveModel::Serializers 0.8 (the version this codebase uses), `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids` emits only `embeddable_host_ids`; the host objects are side-loaded into the root payload only when `include: true`/`embed_in_root: true` is also given. The Ember store resolves plural foreign keys in `_hydrateEmbedded` by looking up `root[pluralize(subType)]` (i.e. a root-level `embeddable_hosts` array) — see the matching test fixture that returns `{__rest_serializer: "1", fruits, farmers, colors}`. Without the side-loaded array every id resolves to `undefined`, so `embedding.embeddable_hosts` becomes an array of `undefined` and the admin table renders empty/broken rows. Add `include: true` (or `embed: :objects`) and a controller spec asserting the JSON contains the hosts.

title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` is executed in a `before_validation` callback without a nil check. `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, which is `nil` when the client omits/blanks the field, and `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?` is also legitimate. In that case `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500 instead of the intended `validates_format_of` validation error. Guard the callback (e.g. `return if host.blank?`) and add `validates_presence_of :host`.

title: Host lookup is case-sensitive on the parameter side
body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the value extracted from the request: `URI("http://Example.com").host` returns `Example.com` with its original case. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so a referer such as `http://Example.com/page` (or a stored host entered with capitals) will not match any row, and `host_allowed?` returns false — `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` then raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` and `TopicRetriever` refuses to fetch, silently breaking embedding. Downcase the argument: `where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase)`.

title: update/destroy dereference nil when the id does not exist
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns `nil` for an unknown or already-deleted id. `update` then calls `save_host(nil)` which hits `nil.host=` and `destroy` (line 16) calls `nil.destroy`, both raising NoMethodError and producing a 500 instead of a 404. This is easy to trigger from the admin UI by deleting the same host twice (or from two browser tabs). Use `find_by`/`find` with an explicit `raise Discourse::NotFound` or `render json: ... , status: 404`.

title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a no-op that reports success
body: `update` only re-renders the freshly fetched `@embedding` OpenStruct; it never reads params or persists anything, yet it returns 200 with the serialized object. The admin controller action `saveChanges` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6) calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` against this endpoint, so any future caller believes a save succeeded when nothing was written. Either implement the update or remove the route, the action and the controller method so no caller depends on a fake success.

title: Plural embedded ids are dropped even when they cannot be resolved
body: The new `m[2]` branch unconditionally does `obj[pluralize(subType)] = obj[k].map(id => this._lookupSubType(...))` and then `delete obj[k]`. Unlike the singular branch (which keeps the `_id` key when hydration fails), this destroys the original ids: if the sub-collection is not side-loaded in the payload, the model ends up with an array of `undefined` values and the `*_ids` property is gone, so callers can neither use the objects nor fall back to the ids. It also assumes the value is an array — any REST-serialized attribute whose name happens to end in `_ids` but holds a string/number will throw `obj[k].map is not a function` and break hydration of the whole record. Only replace the key when every lookup succeeded (and guard with `Array.isArray`).

title: New admin endpoints have no behavioural tests
body: The only assertion in this spec (and in spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb) is that the class inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. Nothing exercises `create`, `update`, `destroy`, the uncategorized-category fallback, the staff/admin constraint, or the JSON shape of `GET /admin/customize/embedding`. As a result none of the new code paths are covered — including the serialization of the `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` (a non-ActiveModel object handed to `EmbeddingSerializer`) and the nil-record handling in update/destroy. Add request specs that create/update/delete a host and assert the rendered payload.

title: Fabricator file contents swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. The two file bodies were clearly exchanged; this works only because Fabrication loads every file in the directory, and it makes the category fabricators impossible to find by filename. Swap the contents back.

title: /fruits/:id handler ignores the requested id, making the new assertions vacuous
body: The handler always returns `fruits[0]` (apple, `color_ids: [1,2]`) regardless of `request.params.id`. The updated store test now calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` and asserts `colors` are ids 1 and 2, but fruit 2 (banana) has `color_ids: [3]` — the test passes only because the wrong record is served. The test therefore does not verify that the right record's `*_ids` are hydrated. Make the handler look the fruit up by id (`fruits.findBy('id', parseInt(request.params.id))`) so the assertions mean what they claim.

title: Only the first underscore is dasherized when matching ADMIN_MODELS
body: `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces a single occurrence, so a type with two or more underscores (e.g. `site_customization_thing`) becomes `site-customization_thing` and will not match its dasherized entry in `ADMIN_MODELS`, silently routing the request to `/` instead of `/admin/` and returning 404/403. Use a global replacement (`type.replace(/_/g, '-')`) or `Ember.String.dasherize(type)`.

title: No uniqueness validation or index on host
body: Nothing prevents two rows with the same `host` (the migration creates no unique index and the model has no `validates_uniqueness_of :host`). `record_for_host` takes `.first` of the match, so when duplicates exist the category used for newly imported embedded topics is whichever row the database happens to return — a non-deterministic result that is confusing to debug. The column is also queried on every embed request with `lower(host) = ?` and has no index. Add a (case-insensitive) unique index plus a model validation.

title: create_table with force: true in a migration can drop an existing table
body: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` first. If the table already exists (e.g. this migration is re-run after a partial failure, or a multisite tenant already has the table), all existing embeddable host rows are destroyed without warning. Additionally, because `change` contains `execute` statements, the migration is not reversible and `rake db:rollback` will fail; use explicit `up`/`down` methods and drop `force: true`.

title: Test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests that
body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer consults embeddable hosts at all (the check was removed from app/models/topic.rb), so this example passes merely because `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false for a built topic. The name claims coverage that does not exist and will mislead anyone debugging embedding. Either delete it or rename it to describe what it actually asserts.

title: Migration raises NoMethodError when no `embed_category` setting row matches
body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. `embed_category` is a non-default, rarely-set setting, so on virtually every existing site (and on every fresh install, where the `site_settings` row does not exist at all) the query returns zero rows, `[0]` is `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`. This aborts `rake db:migrate` and blocks deploys/installs entirely. The result must be checked for emptiness (e.g. `rows = execute(...); category_id = rows.first ? rows.first['id'].to_i : 0`).

title: Fallback category lookup also dereferences a possibly-empty result set
body: `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i` assumes a row always exists. `uncategorized_category_id` is a hidden setting with a default of `-1`; if it was never persisted to the `site_settings` table (the default is only in YAML), `[0]` is `nil` and the migration crashes with `NoMethodError`. Guard the result, and fall back to a sane value.

title: Migrated host values are not normalized (and not SQL-escaped), breaking embedding after upgrade
body: Hosts are copied verbatim from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting via raw `INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. The old setting legitimately contained values like `http://example.com` or `https://example.com/1234` (see the removed specs in `spec/models/site_setting_spec.rb`), but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` matches with `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, i.e. bare hostnames only. Because the raw INSERT bypasses the model's `before_validation` scheme/path stripping, rows such as `http://example.com` will never match a referer and embedding silently stops working for those sites after the upgrade. Values should be normalized (strip scheme/path, strip whitespace/CR) before insert. Additionally, interpolating `h` directly into SQL without quoting will produce a syntax error (or injection) if a host value contains a quote; use `quote()` / a prepared statement.

title: `create_table ... force: true` can drop an existing table and the migration is irreversible
body: `force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS embeddable_hosts` before creating it, so re-running the migration (or running it on a database where the table already exists) silently destroys all existing embeddable host rows. In addition, the migration is declared with `change` but contains `execute` statements (including `DELETE FROM site_settings`), which cannot be reversed, so `db:rollback` will fail. Drop `force: true` and implement explicit `up`/`down`.

title: `before_validation` raises NoMethodError when host is nil; no presence validation
body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally in `before_validation`. If `host` is `nil` (e.g. `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?`, or `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigning `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` when the key is absent) this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil`, producing a 500 instead of a validation error — and the DB column is `null: false`. Add `validates_presence_of :host` and guard the callback (`return if host.blank?`). Note also that `sub!` mutates the assigned string in place, so it mutates the caller's/params' string object; using non-destructive `sub` is safer.

title: update/destroy crash with 500 when the id does not exist
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns `nil` for an unknown or already-deleted id; `update` then calls `save_host(nil)` and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, both raising `NoMethodError` and returning a 500. This is reachable from the admin UI whenever two admins edit concurrently or a stale page is used. Use `find_by` plus `raise Discourse::NotFound` (or `render_json_error`) when the record is missing.

title: Parsed referer host is not downcased before the case-insensitive comparison
body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the value extracted from the URL. `URI('http://EvilTrout.com').host` returns `EvilTrout.com`, so any referer or embed URL containing an upper-case hostname fails the match and embedding/topic retrieval is rejected even though the host is registered. Use `host.downcase` in the query.

title: No uniqueness validation or index on host
body: Nothing prevents two `EmbeddableHost` rows for the same host (the admin UI makes this trivial). `record_for_host` returns `.first` of an unordered query, so which category an imported topic lands in becomes non-deterministic for duplicated hosts. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (case-insensitive) and a unique index in the migration.

title: `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` is a no-op that reports success
body: `update` only re-renders the freshly fetched `@embedding` OpenStruct; it never reads or persists any params. The client's `admin-embedding` controller `saveChanges()` calls `embedding.update({})` against this endpoint, so a user clicking save would get a success response with nothing saved. (The embedding template also has no save button, so `saveChanges` is currently dead code.) Either implement the update or remove the route/action and the unused client action.

title: Plural embedded hydration discards ids even when the lookup fails
body: In the new `_ids` branch, `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` is followed by an unconditional `delete obj[k]`. `hydrated` is always a truthy array, so `|| []` is dead, and when `_lookupSubType` cannot resolve an id (no side-loaded collection in the payload for that type) the resulting array contains `undefined` entries while the original `*_ids` attribute is deleted. Callers then iterate a collection of `undefined` with no way to recover the ids. The singular branch correctly only deletes when hydration succeeded; the plural branch should likewise filter out unresolved ids and keep the raw ids when nothing could be hydrated.

title: `String.replace('_','-')` only replaces the first underscore
body: `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-'))` uses a string (not regex/global) argument, so only the first underscore is converted. Any admin model type with more than one underscore (e.g. `some_embeddable_host`) will not be matched and will be requested from `/` instead of `/admin/`, yielding a 404/403. Use `type.replace(/_/g, '-')`.

title: Fabricator definitions were swapped between files
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`). This is clearly an accidental swap: the file names no longer describe their contents, which breaks Fabrication's `<name>_fabricator.rb` naming convention and makes the definitions impossible to locate by name. Move each definition into the correspondingly named file.

title: New admin endpoints have no behavioural tests
body: Both new controller specs only assert `Controller < Admin::AdminController`. There is no coverage for `create`/`update`/`destroy` of embeddable hosts (success, validation failure, missing id — which currently 500s, see `embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`), for the default-to-uncategorized behaviour, or for the `embedding#show`/`#update` payload shape that the new Ember store/serializer rely on. Given that this PR changes who can embed the forum (a security-relevant allow-list), at least request-level specs for create/update/destroy and non-admin access should be added.

title: `expandable_first_post?` spec no longer tests what its description says
body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` and no longer consults embeddable hosts at all, yet the spec still has `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` (which now only passes because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false) and a `describe 'with an emeddable host'` block whose `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` has no effect on the method under test. The descriptions are misleading (and contain a typo, "emeddable"); either drop the host references or restore a real host dependency.

title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently discards the 4-argument version
body: `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is defined at line 145 and then immediately redefined at line 149 as `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the width/height form is dead code (it also emits a "method redefined; discarding old definition" warning). Any existing caller using `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 200)` now binds `dimensions = 100` and `opts = 200`, so `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` in `downsize_instructions` is called on an Integer and raises (`Integer#[]` with a Symbol), or silently produces the geometry `100` instead of `100x200`. The two call conventions must be merged into one method (e.g. accept either a geometry string or width/height).

title: `optimize` arity change and removal of `dimensions` break external callers
body: `self.optimize` was changed from `(operation, from, to, width, height, opts)` to `(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts)`, and the public helper `self.dimensions(width, height)` was deleted. Both are class methods on a model that plugins and other code can call; existing calls with five positional args will now raise `ArgumentError`, and calls to `OptimizedImage.dimensions` will raise `NoMethodError`. If the change is intended, the old signatures should be kept as thin wrappers (or all internal/plugin call sites updated).

title: Downsize loop ignores conversion failures and overwrites the original file in place
body: The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, i.e. the ImageMagick/gifsicle input and output are the same path, and the boolean return value (false on non-zero exit or exception, see `OptimizedImage.convert_with`) is discarded. Consequences: (a) if `convert` fails part-way, the user's uploaded file is already truncated/corrupted on disk and is then stored as the upload; (b) if conversion simply fails every time, the loop spins 5 times doing nothing and the oversized file is handed to `Upload.create_for`, which rejects it with a size error the client never predicted. The loop should check the return value, break on failure, and convert into a separate temp file that replaces the original only on success.

title: Animated GIFs lose animation because the animated code path can never trigger
body: `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects the gifsicle (animation-preserving) instructions only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. The path passed here is `tempfile.path` of a Rack multipart / download temp file, which has no `.gif` extension (e.g. `/tmp/RackMultipart2015...`), so the regex never matches and every oversized animated GIF is run through `convert input[0]`, which keeps only the first frame. Animation is silently destroyed for any GIF above `max_image_size_kb`. Additionally, gating on `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is the wrong setting here: this is the original upload, not a thumbnail.

title: SVG uploads are passed to `convert` and cannot be shrunk by resizing
body: `FileHelper.is_image?` returns true for `.svg`, so an oversized SVG enters the downsize loop. Resizing a vector/text file by 80% does not reduce its byte size, so all 5 attempts run pointlessly, and running `convert` on it either rasterizes it or produces a file whose content no longer matches the `.svg` filename/extension stored with the upload. SVG (and other non-raster image types) should be excluded from this loop, as `OptimizedImage.create_for` already does for `.svg`.

title: Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick + ImageOptim passes per upload run in the web process
body: For each oversized image the loop may invoke `convert` plus `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` (inside `convert_with`) five times, synchronously, on the request/`Scheduler::Defer` thread of the web process. With the upload ceiling now hard-coded at 10 MB, a single user can tie up a defer thread for many seconds of CPU-heavy work per upload, and a handful of concurrent uploads can starve that pool. This work belongs in a background job, or the number of passes should be computed from the size ratio in a single resize rather than iterating.

title: Hard-coded 10 MB download cap replaces the configurable limit
body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. Sites that configured a larger `max_image_size_kb` can no longer pull images of that size through the API URL path, and sites that deliberately set a small limit now have a 10 MB server-side download/disk/bandwidth exposure that no setting can lower. The cap should be a site setting (e.g. a new `max_upload_size_kb`) rather than a magic constant.

title: Client-side size validation hard-codes 10 MB and ignores attachment/image size settings
body: `maxSizeKB` was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a literal `10 * 1024`, so the `type` argument no longer affects the size check. Attachments are not downsized by the new server code and are still validated against `max_attachment_size_kb` in `Upload.create_for`, so a 9 MB attachment now passes client validation, is fully uploaded, and then fails server-side with an error the user was told would not happen. Sites with a `max_image_size_kb` above 10 MB are also newly blocked client-side. The limit should remain derived from the site settings (with the image case using whatever new upload ceiling the server enforces).

title: 413 error message reports a hard-coded 10 MB limit
body: The HTTP 413 handler now shows `max_size_kb: 10240` instead of the configured `max_image_size_kb`. A 413 comes from the web server (nginx `client_max_body_size`), which is independent of this constant, so the message will state a limit that is wrong for any deployment whose proxy limit or image setting differs from 10 MB, confusing users and support.

title: No tests for the new automatic downsizing path or the changed OptimizedImage API
body: The PR adds a new in-place downsizing loop in `create_upload` and changes/duplicates `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` signatures, but no specs were added or updated. A single spec for `OptimizedImage.downsize` arity would have caught the duplicate method definition, and a controller/unit spec would cover the oversized-image, conversion-failure and non-raster (SVG/GIF) cases that are currently unverified.

title: Second `self.downsize` definition silently overwrites the 4-argument one
body: `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) is immediately redefined by `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149). In Ruby the later definition wins, so the 4-arg form is dead code and every existing caller that passes width and height separately (e.g. `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, w, h)`) now either raises `ArgumentError` (5 args) or passes the height Integer as `opts`, which then blows up with `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` inside `downsize_instructions` when evaluating `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]`. If both forms are needed, use a single method that accepts either a dimension string or width/height, and update all call sites.

title: In-place downsize can destroy the uploaded file and the failure result is ignored
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` uses the same path for input and output, so ImageMagick/gifsicle truncates and rewrites the only copy of the user's upload. `convert_with` swallows errors (`rescue` -> `false`) and this return value is not checked, so a failed or partially written conversion leaves a truncated/empty file that is then handed to `Upload.create_for`, producing a corrupt upload instead of an error. Write to a separate temp file and only swap it in when the conversion reports success; abort the loop as soon as `downsize` returns false.

title: Loop re-reads size from a Tempfile handle whose file was rewritten by an external process
body: The loop condition and the later `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` read size through the still-open `Tempfile` object after an external binary rewrote `tempfile.path`. If the tool writes a new file and renames it over the path (gifsicle does this, and some ImageMagick delegates do too), the open descriptor still refers to the unlinked original inode, so `tempfile.size` returns the stale (large) size: the loop keeps re-converting for all 5 attempts and the recorded filesize can disagree with the stored bytes. Re-open/stat the path (`File.size(tempfile.path)`) after each conversion instead of trusting the cached handle.

title: Percentage dimension is invalid for the animated-GIF (gifsicle) code path
body: With `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled and a `.gif` upload, `optimize` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which builds `gifsicle <from> --colors=256 --resize-fit 80% --optimize=3 --output <to>`. `--resize-fit` only accepts pixel geometry (`WxH`, `_xH`, ...), not a percentage, so gifsicle exits with an error; because input and output are the same path the GIF may also be clobbered. Use `--scale 0.8` for gifsicle, or compute explicit pixel dimensions before calling downsize.

title: Client-side size limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb / max_image_size_kb
body: `validateUploadedFile` previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`; it now hardcodes 10240 KB for every type. Non-image attachments are not downsized server-side, so a site configured with a smaller `max_attachment_size_kb` will let users pick files that the server then rejects (and the `file_too_large` alert quotes 10240 KB, a number the admin never configured). Conversely, sites with a larger configured limit now have uploads blocked in the browser. The `type` argument is also no longer used for the size check. Keep using the site setting for attachments, and only bypass it for images that the server will downsize.

title: 413 error message hardcodes 10MB instead of the configured limit
body: In `displayErrorForUpload`, the HTTP 413 branch now reports `10 * 1024` KB regardless of the site's `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` or the web server's `client_max_body_size`. Users on sites with a different limit get a misleading maximum size in the alert.

title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types
body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`-derived limit. This applies to every `type`, including attachments which are never downsized afterwards, so an API user can make the server fetch and buffer up to 10MB per request even when the administrator configured a much smaller maximum. Derive the cap from the relevant site setting (with an explicit, bounded allowance for images that will be downsized).

title: Up to five full ImageMagick + ImageOptim passes run inline per upload
body: Each loop iteration shells out to `convert` and then `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` (inside `convert_with`), so a single large upload can trigger five full re-encodes plus five lossless-optimizer runs while occupying a request/Defer worker. For multi-megabyte images this is seconds to minutes of CPU per upload and is trivially triggerable by any logged-in user. Compute the target scale from the current/desired byte ratio so one or two passes suffice, and skip the ImageOptim pass for intermediate iterations.

title: No tests for the new auto-downsize behaviour or the changed downsize signature
body: The PR adds a size-reduction loop in `create_upload` and changes `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` signatures, but no specs are added or updated. There is no coverage for: an oversized image being reduced below `max_image_size_kb`, an image still too large after 5 attempts, a non-image skipping the loop, or the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions)` form. Existing specs calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, w, h)` or `OptimizedImage.dimensions` (now removed) would also fail silently unnoticed without updates.

title: Second `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the (width, height) variant
body: `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) is immediately redefined by `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149). In Ruby the later definition wins, so the 4-positional-argument form is gone. Any existing caller/plugin doing `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, 500, 500)` now binds `dimensions = 500` and `opts = 500`, so `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` in `downsize_instructions` raises `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` (or produces a bogus geometry). Either keep a single method that accepts both forms (e.g. `downsize(from, to, dimensions_or_width, height_or_opts = nil, opts = {})`) or rename the new one (e.g. `downsize_to`) and update callers.

title: In-place downsize ignores failure and can corrupt/truncate the uploaded file
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` reads and writes the same path, and its boolean return value is discarded. `OptimizedImage.convert_with` swallows all failures (returns false after logging), so if `convert`/`gifsicle` fails after having already opened the destination for writing, the tempfile is left truncated or partially written and the code unconditionally continues to `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile, ..., tempfile.size, ...)`, storing a corrupt image as the user's upload. Additionally, the still-open Ruby `Tempfile` handle is reused afterwards: if the external tool replaces the inode rather than truncating it, `tempfile.size` reports the stale size, which both makes the loop spin pointlessly and records a `filesize` on the `uploads` row that does not match the stored bytes. Convert to a distinct temp file, check the return value, and only swap in / re-stat the result on success.

title: Percentage geometry is invalid for the animated (gifsicle) downsize path
body: When `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is true and the temp path ends in `.gif`, `OptimizedImage.optimize` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which delegates to `resize_instructions_animated` and emits `gifsicle <in> --colors=256 --resize-fit 80% --optimize=3 --output <out>`. `gifsicle --resize-fit` only accepts a WxH geometry (e.g. `_x300`); a percentage is rejected, so every one of the 5 attempts fails, the file size never changes, and the upload then fails the server-side size validation with no useful diagnostic. Use `--scale 0.8` for the animated path, or compute an explicit pixel geometry before calling downsize.

title: Downsizing the original strips GIF animation and depends on the temp file extension
body: When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false (the default), an oversized animated GIF is passed to `downsize_instructions`, which uses `convert #{from}[0]` – only the first frame. Because the conversion is written back over `tempfile.path`, the user's *original* animated GIF is irreversibly replaced by a single static frame. Worse, the animation branch is selected with `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` against the temp path: files obtained via the API URL branch come from `FileHelper.download(url, ..., "discourse-upload-#{type}")`, whose tempfile has no `.gif` extension, so animated GIFs downloaded by URL are always flattened regardless of the setting. Pass the real `filename` through to `optimize` for format detection, and do not use `[0]`/first-frame conversion on the original upload.

title: Client-side upload size check hardcodes 10MB and ignores max_attachment_size_kb
body: `validateUploadedFile` previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`; it now always compares against a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB, and the `type` parameter is unused for sizing. The server still validates attachments against `SiteSetting.max_attachment_size_kb` (only images are auto-downsized), so a site with, say, a 2MB attachment limit will let the browser accept a 9MB .zip, upload it, and only fail asynchronously server-side with a confusing error. Conversely, sites configured with a limit above 10MB can no longer upload files they are allowed to. The image limit may legitimately be relaxed now, but the attachment limit must still come from the site setting (and the hardcoded ceiling should be a setting shared with the server's `10.megabytes`).

title: 413 error message reports a hardcoded 10MB that may not be the real limit
body: In `displayErrorForUpload`, the HTTP 413 branch now tells the user `file_too_large` with `max_size_kb = 10 * 1024`. A 413 comes from the front-end web server (nginx `client_max_body_size`) or the attachment/image site settings, which are independent of this constant, so the message can state a limit that is neither the configured nor the enforced one, misleading users about what they can upload.

title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site configuration
body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` with a magic constant. Sites configured to allow images/attachments larger than 10MB can no longer ingest them through the API `url` parameter, and the limit is now unconfigurable and duplicated in three places (here, and twice in `utilities.js`). Introduce a site setting (or a shared constant) for the absolute upload ceiling instead of hardcoding it.

title: Up to five convert + ImageOptim passes per upload on the upload path
body: The loop runs `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to 5 times, and `OptimizedImage.convert_with` invokes `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` after every successful conversion. ImageOptim (pngcrush/jpegoptim/advpng...) is very CPU- and time-expensive, so a single large upload can occupy a `Scheduler::Defer` worker for tens of seconds, five sequential ImageMagick runs plus five ImageOptim runs, and this happens for every oversized image. Also, if a conversion fails the loop still burns all 5 iterations because the result is never checked. Consider computing the target geometry once (so a single resize suffices), breaking out on failure/no size change, and skipping ImageOptim for intermediate passes or moving the work to a background job.

title: Public `self.dimensions` removed and `self.optimize` signature changed without deprecation
body: `self.dimensions(width, height)` was deleted and `self.optimize` changed from `(operation, from, to, width, height, opts)` to `(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts)`. These are public class methods on a model that plugins and existing specs call directly; the change will raise `NoMethodError`/`ArgumentError` for any such caller. If the signature change is intentional, it should be called out and the in-tree callers/specs updated, otherwise keep backwards-compatible wrappers.

title: No tests for the new auto-downsize behaviour or the redefined downsize API
body: The PR adds a new in-place downsize loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` and changes/duplicates `OptimizedImage.downsize` / `OptimizedImage.optimize` signatures, but no specs are added or updated. There is no coverage for: an oversized image being reduced below `max_image_size_kb`, the case where 5 attempts are not enough, an oversized non-image skipping the loop, the animated-GIF path, or the new string-geometry `downsize` form (which currently breaks the old width/height form). Given the data-loss risk of writing over the user's tempfile, these paths need tests before merge.

title: Unsubscribe GET endpoint toggles notification level, so a reload/prefetch mutes the topic
body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is reached by a plain GET from an email link, but the body is a toggle: if the current level is above `regular` it is lowered to `regular`, otherwise it is set to `muted`. The request is therefore not idempotent. A user who clicks the email link and then refreshes the page (or whose browser/email client fetches the URL twice, or who clicks the link in two different notification emails for the same topic) ends up fully muted even though they only intended one downgrade. The 301 redirect added at line 102 also makes it easy for the URL to be re-requested. The action should set a single, deterministic target level instead of toggling (and preferably be a POST/PUT with an explicit confirmation).

title: State-changing GET action with CSRF protection effectively disabled
body: `unsubscribe` changes persistent user state (`topic_users.notification_level`) on a GET request, and `check_xhr` is skipped for it (line 32). Rails' `protect_from_forgery` does not apply to GET, so any third-party page can embed `` (or a link/prefetch) and silently mute or downgrade the notification level of any logged-in visitor for an arbitrary topic. Email scanners and link prefetchers in mail clients will also trigger it without the user ever clicking. The unsubscribe should either be performed through a non-GET request with CSRF token, or be gated by a one-time signed key embedded in the email link (as is done for the digest unsubscribe key).

title: Nil TopicUser causes 500 in unsubscribe action
body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (no `topic_users` row exists for this user/topic — e.g. the row was never created, was removed, or a different logged-in user than the email recipient opens the link). The next line calls `tu.notification_level`, raising `NoMethodError` and producing a 500 error page for anyone clicking the unsubscribe link in that situation. The action needs to handle the missing row (e.g. create it via `TopicUser.change`) or respond gracefully.

title: Unsubscribe writes notification_level directly, bypassing TopicUser.change bookkeeping
body: Setting `tu.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` skips everything `TopicUser.change` does: it does not set `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id` and does not publish the `/topic/:id` `notification_level_change` MessageBus message. Two concrete consequences: (1) any open client tab keeps showing the stale notification level, and (2) because `notifications_reason_id` stays `nil` (its common value when the level was never user-set), `TopicUser.update_last_read` will auto-track the topic again the next time the user views it, silently undoing the unsubscribe. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` instead.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, which will break other mailers
body: `Email::MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` interpolate `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` for every email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Adding the mandatory `%{unsubscribe_url}` placeholder means any such caller that does not supply `unsubscribe_url` raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and the email fails to send; only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to pass it (and the message_builder spec had to be changed for exactly this reason). Either make the topic link conditional (e.g. a separate key only appended when `unsubscribe_url` is present) or audit/update every mailer that sets `add_unsubscribe_link`.

title: Unsubscribe page text claims notifications are stopped even when the level was only downgraded to regular
body: `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` reads "You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}." and is rendered unconditionally, but the server only moves watching/tracking down to `regular` on the first visit. At `regular` the user still receives notifications for replies to their posts and mentions in that topic, so the page tells the user something that is not true. The message should reflect the resulting notification level (or the server should actually mute when the message says notifications stop).

title: Unsubscribe link from email silently fails for users who are not logged in
body: `unsubscribe` is added to the `ensure_logged_in` filter list, but the link is delivered by email and will frequently be opened in a browser/webview where the user has no Discourse session. In that case `Discourse::NotLoggedIn` is raised and the HTML request is bounced (to the homepage/login) without performing the unsubscribe and without telling the recipient why, so the email's promise "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here" does not hold. Consider a signed key in the URL so the action works without a session, or at least redirect back to the unsubscribe URL after login with an explanatory message.

title: No specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint or Topic#unsubscribe_url
body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action (slug redirect, missing-`TopicUser` path, which notification level results, access control for topics the user cannot see) and `Topic#unsubscribe_url` have no controller/model specs. The only test change is passing `unsubscribe_url` into `Email::MessageBuilder` so the existing unsubscribe-link spec keeps passing; nothing asserts that the per-topic unsubscribe URL actually appears in the email body or that the new endpoint behaves correctly, so the regressions noted above (nil TopicUser 500, toggle-on-refresh) would not be caught.

title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists
body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately dereferences `tu.notification_level` without a nil check. A `topic_users` row is not guaranteed to exist for the current user and topic (e.g. the link is shared/forwarded and opened by a different logged-in user, the row was removed, or the user simply visits `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` for a topic they have never interacted with). In those cases the request raises `NoMethodError` on nil and returns a 500 instead of a useful page. The action should create/fetch the record (e.g. via `TopicUser.change`) or handle nil gracefully.

title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed over GET with no CSRF protection
body: The new `unsubscribe` action mutates the user's `topic_users.notification_level` and is wired to GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`, `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) with `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`. Rails does not CSRF-protect GET requests, so any third-party page can silently change a logged-in user's notification level for an arbitrary topic with ``, and repeated loads will escalate the level to `muted` (see the toggle logic). Browser prefetching/link scanners and a plain page refresh have the same effect. Side effects should be performed behind a POST/PUT (or a signed unsubscribe key, like `email/unsubscribe/:key`) rather than a plain GET.

title: Writing notification_level directly bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
body: The action assigns `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` instead of going through `TopicUser.change`. As a result `notifications_reason_id` and `notifications_changed_at` are never set, and no MessageBus `/topic/<id>` `notification_level_change` message is published. Two concrete consequences: (1) other open tabs/clients keep showing the stale notification level; (2) `TopicUser.update_last_read` only auto-bumps the level to `tracking` when `notifications_reason_id IS NULL`, so after this unsubscribe the next time the user reads the topic long enough their level is silently raised back to `tracking`, undoing the unsubscribe.

title: Unsubscribe is not idempotent: reloading the page escalates to muted
body: The logic is `if tu.notification_level > regular then regular else muted`. A watching/tracking user who opens the unsubscribe link gets `regular`; if the same URL is hit again (page refresh, back/forward navigation, browser or mail-client prefetch, or the user clicking the link in a second email) the level is now equal to `regular`, so the else branch sets `muted`. A single user action ("unsubscribe from this topic") can therefore silently escalate to full muting of the topic without any further confirmation. The endpoint should be idempotent, i.e. set a single deterministic target level.

title: Unsubscribe page claims notifications will stop even when level is only lowered to 'regular'
body: The page always renders `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` ("You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}."), but the server only sets the level to `regular` when the user was watching/tracking. At `regular` the user still receives notifications for replies to their posts, quotes and mentions in that topic, so the message is factually wrong for the most common case. The same applies to the new `unsubscribe_link` server string ("To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here"). The text should reflect the level that was actually applied.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url} with no fallback
body: The `unsubscribe_link` string gained a `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, but `Email::MessageBuilder` adds no default for `unsubscribe_url` in `@template_args`. Any caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` (other mailers, forks, plugins) will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` in `MessageBuilder#body`/`#html_part`, i.e. the email fails to send. The fact that `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb` had to be changed to add `unsubscribe_url` confirms the hard dependency. Add a default (e.g. fall back to `user_preferences_url`) or only append the per-topic sentence when the option is present.

title: No tests for the new unsubscribe endpoint or unsubscribe_url rendering
body: The only test change is adding `unsubscribe_url` to an existing builder so the suite keeps passing. There is no spec asserting that the per-topic unsubscribe URL actually appears in the email body/HTML, no spec for `Topic#unsubscribe_url`, and no controller spec for `TopicsController#unsubscribe`. Given the nil-`TopicUser` crash, the non-idempotent toggle and the GET-based mutation, a controller spec covering (a) no existing topic_users row, (b) repeated requests, and (c) the slug redirect is needed to prevent regressions.

title: Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText
body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` ("Notificiations") in both the controller and `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`. It works today because the typo is consistent, but it is a trap for future edits/overrides (a correctly spelled reference in a plugin or theme will silently render nothing). Rename to `stopNotificationsText` in both places.

title: Class attribute contains a stray leading dot
body: `<h4 class='.previous-discussion'>` sets the literal class name `.previous-discussion`, so any email stylesheet rule targeting `.previous-discussion` will never match. Since this line is being reformatted in this PR anyway, drop the leading dot.

title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can legitimately return `nil` (a logged-in user who has never visited/been emailed about the topic, or whose topic_users row was removed), and the next line immediately calls `tu.notification_level`, raising `NoMethodError` and returning a 500 to a user who just clicked a link in an email. The action should create the record (e.g. via `TopicUser.change`) or bail out gracefully when the row is missing.

title: Writing notification_level directly instead of TopicUser.change leaves stale metadata and lets the mute be auto-reverted
body: The action assigns `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!`, bypassing `TopicUser.change`. Consequences: (1) `notifications_reason_id` and `notifications_changed_at` are not set, so the row still looks like an auto-assigned level. `TopicUser.update_last_read` re-promotes a topic to `tracking` precisely when `notifications_reason_id IS NULL` and the view-time threshold is exceeded, so the user's unsubscribe can be silently undone the next time they read the topic. (2) No `MessageBus.publish("/topic/<id>", notification_level_change: ...)` is sent, so other open clients/tabs keep showing the old notification level. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: level)` instead.

title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed over GET (CSRF-able)
body: `unsubscribe` is routed as a GET (see config/routes.rb) and mutates the user's notification level. Rails' CSRF token verification only applies to non-GET verbs, and `check_xhr` is explicitly skipped for this action, so any third-party page can mute arbitrary topics for a logged-in Discourse user simply by embedding ``. Browser/extension link prefetching can also trigger it unintentionally. Either make the mutation happen on a POST/PUT from a confirmation page, or require a signed, single-use unsubscribe key in the URL.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking callers that don't pass it
body: `unsubscribe_link` gained a `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, but `Email::MessageBuilder#body`/`#html_part` render it for every caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true`.
