The desktop equivalent in `desktop/topic-post.scss` was converted correctly as `20%` / `80%`; the mobile rule should match.

title: custom-message-length light-theme lightness inverted (70% -> 30%), diverging from desktop
body: `.custom-message-length` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`; the new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, i.e. the light-theme color is now much darker (30% instead of 70%). `desktop/modal.scss` for the same class was converted as `70%` / `30%`, so mobile and desktop now render this hint text differently on light themes. One of the two is wrong; the light branch should keep the original 70%.

title: Missed conversion: category badge-notification still uses scale-color($primary) only
body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` while every comparable rule in this file was converted to `dark-light-choose(...)`. On dark color schemes `$primary` is the light text color, so scaling its lightness up by 50% yields a near-white value, making this badge brighter than normal text instead of dimmer — exactly the defect this PR is fixing elsewhere.

title: Comment describing the topic-list default color is now stale
body: The comment above the coldmap rules states "the default for table cells in topic list is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)". After this PR the topic-list cell default is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` (see `common/base/_topic-list.scss`), so the comment no longer matches the code and will mislead anyone tuning these heat/cold map colors.

title: remove_member uses group.users.delete, bypassing GroupUser callbacks and the user_count counter cache
body: `remove_member` deletes the membership with `group.users.delete(user_id)`. For a `has_many :through` association with no `:dependent` option, Rails deletes the join rows with `delete_all`, so no `GroupUser` destroy callbacks run and the `counter_cache: "user_count"` on `GroupUser#group` is never decremented. Consequences: the `user_count` column (rendered by `BasicGroupSerializer` and shown in the admin group list and `userCountDisplay`) stays stale/too high forever, and the per-membership cleanup normally done on destroy (e.g. clearing a granted group title / primary group) is skipped. The existing `Group#remove(user)` helper (which destroys the `GroupUser` record) should be used instead.

title: remove_member raises RecordNotFound (500) when user_id is not a member of the group
body: `group.users.delete(params.require(:user_id).to_i)` passes an Integer to the collection proxy, which internally calls `find` scoped to the association. If the id does not belong to the group (already removed, bogus id, double-click on the remove button, or `to_i` turning a non-numeric value into 0), `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` is raised and the admin gets an unhandled error instead of a graceful response. The action should look the user up explicitly and no-op / return a proper error when the user is not a member.

title: create silently drops alias_level sent by the client
body: `Discourse.Group#asJSON` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js) always includes `alias_level`, and `create` POSTs that payload, but `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `name` and `visible`. An admin who picks an alias level while creating a new group has that choice silently discarded (the server keeps the default), while the client model still shows the chosen value, so the UI and database disagree until the next save. `update` handles `alias_level`; `create` should too.

title: members endpoint does not validate limit/offset, allowing 500s and unbounded queries
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are used directly in `limit(limit).offset(offset)` on a publicly reachable endpoint. A negative value (`?offset=-1` or `?limit=-1`) produces `OFFSET -1` / `LIMIT -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects ("OFFSET must not be negative"), turning user input into a 500 error. A huge value (`?limit=1000000`) makes the server load and serialize every group member in one request, an easy resource-exhaustion vector. Both parameters should be clamped (e.g. limit between 1 and some max, offset >= 0).

title: Breaking change to the public /groups/:name/members.json response shape
body: The endpoint previously returned a bare JSON array of serialized group users; it now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}`. This is a public, unversioned endpoint used by third-party clients and plugins (and previously returned all members for non-automatic groups, now a default page of 50). Any existing consumer iterating the array will break with no deprecation path. If this change is intended, it should be called out in the PR description/release notes so integrators can adapt.

title: No spec coverage for the rewritten members endpoint
body: `GroupsController#members` changed both its response format (array -> `{members:, meta:}`) and its paging semantics (always paginated, default limit 50), yet only `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` was updated in this PR. `spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb` is untouched, so existing assertions about the old array response are likely broken, and the new behaviour (meta.total, limit/offset handling, ordering) has no test at all.

title: totalPages off-by-one produces an extra empty page
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` this returns one page too many: with 100 members and limit 50 it reports 3 pages, and clicking "next" twice lands on offset 100 where the server returns no members, so the admin sees an empty member list and a bogus "3/3" indicator. It should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the 0 case handled), and the `next` action should clamp offset to `(totalPages - 1) * limit` rather than to `user_count`.

title: addMembers/removeMember swallow server errors with no user feedback
body: `addMembers` and `removeMember` only attach a success handler (`.then(function(){ self.findMembers(); })`) and the calling controller actions (`addMembers`, `removeMember` in admin-group.js.es6) ignore the returned promise. If the request fails - e.g. the 422 `can_not_modify_automatic` response, a validation error, or any 500 - nothing is displayed and the member list is not refreshed, so the admin believes the operation succeeded. Note the server also silently ignores unknown usernames in `add_members`, which compounds the lack of feedback. A failure handler showing `bootbox.alert` (as `save`/`destroy` do) is needed.

title: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when the group has no name
body: The early return was changed from `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` to a bare `return;`. `findMembers` is otherwise promise-returning and is chained by callers (`actions.next`/`actions.previous` return its value, and plugins/other code may call `.then` on it). For a group without a name the function now returns `undefined`, so any `.then()` on the result throws a TypeError. Return a resolved promise to keep the contract consistent.

title: Public group members page is now silently capped at 50 members with no pagination
body: The public group page iterates `members`, which `group-members.js.es6` populates via `model.findMembers()` using the model's default `limit: 50` / `offset: 0`. Previously the endpoint returned all members for non-automatic groups, so the full list was shown. There is no next/previous control in this template (only the admin template got one), so for any group with more than 50 members the page now shows a truncated list with no indication that members are missing, while the counts endpoint still reports the real total.

title: remove_member spec issues a PUT while the route only accepts DELETE
body: The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" example calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, but `config/routes.rb` maps only `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. Controller specs dispatch directly to the action and ignore the HTTP verb, so the test passes while never exercising the real routing; a verb regression in routes.rb would go undetected. Use `:delete` as the other removal example does.

title: Removal spec asserts association count but not the cached user_count
body: "is able to remove a member" only checks `group.users.count == 0`, which is a live SQL count and therefore passes even though `group.users.delete(user_id)` skips the `GroupUser` destroy callbacks and leaves the cached `user_count` column at 1. Asserting `group.user_count` (the value exposed by `BasicGroupSerializer` and shown in the admin UI) would catch the stale-counter bug introduced by the new `remove_member` implementation.

title: add_members assumes the usernames param is a String
body: `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` followed by `usernames.split(",")` raises `NoMethodError` (500) if a client sends `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`, which is a natural way to call this endpoint and is what Rails produces for an array parameter. Accept both forms (e.g. `Array(usernames).flat_map { |u| u.to_s.split(',') }`) or validate the type and return a 400.

title: remove_member deletes join rows with delete_all, skipping callbacks and user_count maintenance
body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` goes through the `has_many :users, through: :group_users` association. For a `has_many :through` association without a `:dependent` option, `delete` removes the join rows with `delete_all`, so no `GroupUser` is instantiated and no ActiveRecord callbacks / counter-cache updates run. Consequences: the cached `groups.user_count` column (exposed by `BasicGroupSerializer` and used by the admin group list and group index) is never decremented and drifts permanently, and any `GroupUser` destroy-time bookkeeping (e.g. clearing `primary_group`/badge title that was granted by the group) is skipped. The removal should go through the model API that destroys the join record, e.g. `group.remove(user)` or `group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).destroy_all`. Additionally, passing an id that is not a member makes the association call `find(id)` and raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`, turning a no-op removal into a 404 instead of a clean response.

title: create ignores alias_level sent by the client
body: `create` only assigns `name` and `visible`, but the client (`Discourse.Group#asJSON`, used by `create()`) always sends `alias_level` as well. A group created with a non-default alias level in the admin UI is silently saved with the default level, and the UI then shows the value the admin picked, so the discrepancy is invisible until a page reload. `update` does assign `alias_level`; `create` should do the same. Note also that this change switches the create/update payload from nested `group[...]` params to flat params and drops support for `usernames`, which breaks any existing API client of `POST/PUT /admin/groups`.

title: Removal of the PATCH membership endpoint makes old PATCH requests silently destructive
body: The `update_patch` branch (incremental `changes: {add:, delete:}` membership edits) was deleted, but `resources :groups` still routes PATCH to `update`. A client still issuing `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes` now gets HTTP 200 while the membership changes are silently discarded, and because `update` unconditionally executes `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`, the absent `visible` param flips the group to not visible. Old callers therefore both lose their intended effect and mutate unrelated state while being told everything succeeded. Either keep handling `changes` (or reject PATCH explicitly) and only assign `visible` when the param is present.

title: members endpoint does not validate limit/offset
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to `.limit()/.offset()`. A request with `?offset=-1` or `?limit=-1` produces `OFFSET -1` / `LIMIT -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects (`ERROR: OFFSET must not be negative`), turning a bad query string into a 500. There is also no upper bound on `limit`, so `?limit=1000000` on a large automatic group (e.g. trust_level_0) will serialize every member in one unauthenticated-reachable request, an easy way to burn server CPU/memory. Clamp both values (e.g. `limit` to 1..100, `offset` to >= 0) server-side; the JS clamping in `Discourse.Group#findMembers` protects nothing against direct requests.

title: GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed from array to object
body: The endpoint previously rendered a bare JSON array of serialized users (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`); it now returns `{"members": [...], "meta": {...}}`. This is an unversioned, breaking change for any external API consumer or plugin that reads `/groups/:name/members.json` as an array (they will now see an object and silently iterate nothing). If the break is intentional it should at least be called out in the PR description/changelog; otherwise consider keeping the array for non-paginated requests.

title: Public group members page now silently truncated to 50 members
body: `model.findMembers()` requests the default page (limit 50, offset 0) and `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` renders only `members` with no pagination controls. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members from this endpoint, so a group with more than 50 members now shows only the first 50 with no way for a user to reach the rest. Either add next/previous controls (as done in the admin template) or load all pages for this route.

title: totalPages off by one produces a reachable empty page
body: `totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which over-counts whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`: with 100 members and limit 50 it reports 3 pages even though only 2 contain data. Combined with `next`, which sets `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, an admin can page to `offset == user_count` and see "3/3" with an empty member list (and `previous` then lands on a non page-aligned offset). Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` and advance the offset in whole pages.

title: Add/remove member failures are swallowed with no user feedback
body: `addMembers` and `removeMember` call into `Discourse.Group#addMembers` / `#removeMember`, neither of which attach a rejection handler. If the server responds 422 (e.g. `can_not_modify_automatic`) or 404/500 (see the RecordNotFound path in `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`), the promise rejects silently: the member list is not refreshed and the admin gets no indication the operation failed. Add an error handler that surfaces the message (as `save`/`destroy` in this controller already do). The `// TODO: should clear the input` note is related: because `usernames` is never reset, clicking Add again re-sends the same list.

title: add_members assumes usernames is a String and silently ignores unknown users
body: `usernames.split(",")` raises `NoMethodError` (HTTP 500) if the parameter arrives as an array (`usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), which is a natural shape for API clients. Also, usernames that do not resolve to a `User` are skipped and the action still returns `success_json`, so an admin who mistypes a username sees a successful save and no member added, with no error reported. Normalize the parameter (`Array(usernames).join(",").split(",")` or similar) and report unknown usernames back to the caller.

title: No spec for the rewritten members endpoint
body: `GroupsController#members` changed substantially in this PR (new `{members:, meta:}` envelope, new default limit of 50 applied to all groups instead of automatic groups only, `total` computed with a separate count query), but the only spec touched is `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`. There is no test asserting the new response structure, that `limit`/`offset` are honoured and echoed in `meta`, or that `total` reflects the full member count — so the response-shape break and any future regression in pagination would go unnoticed.

title: remove_member spec uses a verb the route does not support
body: The test issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but `config/routes.rb` only declares `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. Controller specs dispatch directly to the action, so the test passes even though a real PUT to `/admin/groups/:group_id/members` would be handled by `add_members`, not `remove_member`. The automatic-group guard for the DELETE path is therefore not actually covered; use `xhr :delete, :remove_member` as the other spec in the same context does.

title: Specs depend on hardcoded group id 1 being an automatic group
body: The new `.update` spec (`id: 1`) and the `.add_members` / `.remove_member` automatic-group specs (`group_id: 1`) rely on seeded data where group id 1 happens to exist and be automatic, and `.update` then calls `Group.find(1)`. If seeds change or the test database is built differently, these raise `RecordNotFound` rather than fail meaningfully, and nothing in the spec documents the assumption. Fabricate an automatic group explicitly (`Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)`) as the `.destroy` spec does.

title: totalPages uses floor+1, producing a phantom empty last page
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100 members with limit 50) this returns 3 instead of 2, so `showingLast` never becomes true for the real last page, the pager shows "2/3", and clicking next sets `offset` to `user_count` (see `next`, which clamps with `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), causing `findMembers` to request an offset equal to the total and render an empty member list. The correct formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

title: Unvalidated limit/offset on public members endpoint
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no bounds. A request with `?limit=1000000` to this unauthenticated endpoint will serialize an arbitrary number of users (expensive JSON + N queries for avatars etc.), and a negative value such as `?offset=-1` or `?limit=-1` makes PostgreSQL raise "OFFSET/LIMIT must not be negative", returning a 500. Clamp limit to a sane maximum and force offset to be non-negative.

title: remove_member bypasses GroupUser callbacks and 404s for non-members
body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` operates on a `has_many :through` association, whose default deletion strategy is `delete_all`: the join row is removed with raw SQL, so `GroupUser`'s `counter_cache` on `user_count` and its `after_destroy` hooks (clearing the user's primary group / granted title) never run. The result is a stale `Group#user_count` and users keeping a primary group/title from a group they no longer belong to. The previous code path used `group.remove(user)` / destroyed the `GroupUser` record, which ran those callbacks. Additionally, `CollectionProxy#delete` with an integer id calls `find` on the scoped association, so removing a user who is not a member raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` (404 instead of a JSON error). Use `group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).destroy_all` (or `group.remove(user)`).

title: PATCH /admin/groups/:id now silently hides groups and drops 'changes'
body: The `update_patch` branch was removed, but `resources :groups` still routes PATCH to `update`. Any existing client (plugin, script, or a browser still running the old JS during a deploy) that sends `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `{changes: {add: ...}}` now hits the new `update`, which ignores `changes` entirely, sets `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` (i.e. false because `visible` is absent) and responds with `success_json`. Membership changes are silently lost and the group is silently made invisible. The same unconditional `visible` assignment makes every partial update (any PUT without an explicit `visible`) flip the group to hidden; it should only be assigned when the parameter is present.

title: create silently drops alias_level sent by the client
body: `Discourse.Group#asJSON` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js) includes `alias_level`, and admin/templates/group.hbs renders the alias-level combo box for a brand-new group, but `create` only reads `name` and `visible`. An admin who picks an alias level while creating a group gets a group with the default alias level and no indication that the setting was ignored; they must save a second time. Read `params[:alias_level]` in `create` as `update` does.

title: Members endpoint response shape changed without spec coverage
body: `GET /groups/:group_id/members` previously returned a bare JSON array of serialized users; it now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}` and is paginated (default 50) for all groups, not just automatic ones. This is a breaking change for any external consumer/plugin reading the array form and for non-automatic groups that previously received every member. No spec was added or updated for the new payload or for the pagination behaviour (`spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb` is untouched in this PR), so neither the contract change nor the limit/offset handling is tested.

title: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise for unnamed groups
body: `findMembers` now does `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }` where it previously returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. Any caller that chains (`group.findMembers().then(...)`) will throw `TypeError: Cannot read property 'then' of undefined` for a group without a name (e.g. an unsaved new group). Keep returning a resolved promise so the method's contract stays uniform.

title: No error feedback when adding/removing members fails
body: `addMembers` and `removeMember` call into the model and ignore the returned promise's rejection. The server can legitimately fail these calls (422 `can_not_modify_automatic`, `render_json_error(group)`), and `add_members` silently skips usernames that don't resolve to a user. In all those cases the UI just re-renders the unchanged list with no message, and the rejected promise surfaces only as an unhandled rejection in the console. Add a failure handler that shows the server error (as the `save` action does).

title: destroy() returns undefined for unsaved groups while caller chains .then()
body: `destroy` returns `undefined` when the group has no `id`, but admin-group.js.es6's `destroy` action does `group.destroy().then(...)`. admin/templates/group.hbs renders the Delete button for every non-automatic group, including the unsaved new-group form, so clicking Delete before saving throws `TypeError: Cannot read property 'then' of undefined` and leaves `disableSave` stuck at true. Either return a resolved/rejected promise or hide the button when `id` is absent (the members section already uses `{{#if id}}`).

title: remove_member spec uses the wrong HTTP verb and a hardcoded group id
body: The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" example issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but config/routes.rb only exposes `remove_member` via DELETE. Controller specs don't verify the verb, so this test passes while never exercising the route the client actually uses, and a future routing mistake on the DELETE path would go unnoticed. It also assumes the seeded group with `id: 1` is automatic (same for the add_members and update examples); fabricating an automatic group would make the expectation explicit and robust.

title: Rename path does not strip whitespace like create does
body: `create` does `group.name = (params[:name] || '').strip` (and there is a spec for it), but `update` assigns `params[:name]` verbatim. Renaming a group to " bob " therefore stores the untrimmed name, producing group names that no longer match the username-style rule enforced at creation time and that will not match lookups such as `Group.find_by("lower(name) = ?", name.downcase)` for the trimmed value. Strip the name in `update` as well.

title: Translation LRU cache key does not include the fallback chain (multisite cross-site leakage)
body: The memoized translation cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With this PR the fallback chain is no longer a static `[locale, :en]`; it is `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` (config/initializers/i18n.rb), i.e. it now depends on a per-site setting. Because the cache key does not contain `SiteSetting.default_locale`, a value resolved through the fallback chain on one site is served to every other site in the same process. Example: site A has `default_locale = de`, a user with locale `fr` triggers a lookup of a key missing in `fr`; the German string is resolved and cached under key `"...fr<backend_id>"`. A subsequent request on site B (`default_locale = en`) for the same key in `fr` gets a cache hit and is shown the German string. The same staleness occurs on a single site whenever an admin changes `default_locale` without an `I18n.reload!`/cache flush. Previously the chain fell back to the global `I18n.default_locale`, so the cache was site-independent and this could not happen.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests; missing translations get cached permanently
body: Because of the lazy-loading freedom patch, `I18n.translate` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)` for the *current* locale; translations for the other locales in the fallback chain are loaded exclusively by `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!`, which is only invoked from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any code path that is not an HTTP request through ApplicationController - Sidekiq jobs, mailers rendered from jobs, rake tasks, the console, `I18n.with_locale` blocks - will have an unloaded fallback locale, so `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` finds nothing and the lookup resolves to the "translation missing" string instead of the site default/English text. Worse, `I18n.translate` caches that result in the LRU cache (`@cache.getset(k) { translate_no_cache(key).freeze }`) and `ensure_loaded!` does not clear the cache, so once a key is resolved while the fallback locale was unloaded, the "translation missing" text keeps being returned for web requests too until the entry is evicted or the process restarts. Loading should be hooked into `load_locale`/`translate` (or the cache invalidated when a new locale is loaded) rather than relying on a controller filter.

title: Fallback chain calls SiteSetting on every lookup and raises if default_locale is nil / DB unavailable
body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` executes `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` on every fallback resolution. Two concrete problems: (1) if `SiteSetting.default_locale` is nil or site settings are not usable yet, `nil.to_sym` raises `NoMethodError` from deep inside an `I18n.t` call - this happens in contexts where I18n is used but the database/site_settings are not available (e.g. `rake assets:precompile` on a machine without a DB, early boot, migrations), turning a harmless missing translation into a crash. The trailing `.compact` does not protect against this because `to_sym` is evaluated first; it only guards a nil `locale` argument. (2) `[]` is on the hot path of every missing-translation lookup and allocates a new array plus performs a site-setting read each time, even though `FallbackLocaleList` inherits from `Hash` and never memoizes (unlike `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`, which caches the computed chain). Consider rescuing/guarding the setting lookup and memoizing per locale+default_locale.

title: No tests for the new fallback behaviour, which is now enabled in all environments
body: This PR moves fallbacks from `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` (previously only production/profile) to an initializer that is loaded in every environment, including test and development, and introduces a custom three-step chain (user locale -> site default -> :en) plus a new `I18n.ensure_loaded!`. No spec is added for any of it: there is no coverage that a key missing in the user locale resolves to the site default and then to English, that `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` actually loads the locale files it returns, or that `I18n::Backend::Pluralization` is still applied after `config/initializers/pluralization.rb` was deleted. Since fallbacks now also apply in the test environment, existing specs that rely on missing-translation behaviour can silently change meaning without any new test asserting the intended semantics.

title: `ensure_loaded!` initializes and reads @loaded_locales outside LOAD_MUTEX
body: `ensure_loaded!` does `@loaded_locales ||= []` and `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` without holding `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` appends to the same array under the mutex and `reload!` replaces it. Two request threads entering `ensure_loaded!` concurrently when `@loaded_locales` is nil can each create a separate array, so one thread's bookkeeping is discarded and locale files are parsed again (and, combined with `reload!`, a thread can observe a partially replaced list). The consequence is redundant, expensive YAML loading rather than corruption, but the initialization belongs inside the mutex (or `@loaded_locales` should be initialized eagerly at load time).

title: Fallback locales are never loaded outside of HTTP requests, so fallbacks silently fail in jobs/mailers
body: The translate accelerator only loads the YAML for `config.locale` (`load_locale(config.locale)` in `translate`), and the patched `I18n::Backend::Base#load_translations` deliberately does nothing when called without filenames, so `Simple#init_translations` will not autoload anything either. With `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` now mixed in, a lookup that misses falls back to `SiteSetting.default_locale` and `:en`, but those locales' translations are only in memory if something explicitly called `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for them. The only caller added in this PR is `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any translation performed outside a controller request — Sidekiq jobs (e.g. digest/notification emails rendered with the recipient's locale via `I18n.with_locale`), rake tasks, console, console-driven exports — will therefore still produce “translation missing” for keys absent from the user's locale, which is exactly the case fallbacks are supposed to fix. The ensure-loaded logic should be hooked into `load_locale`/`translate` (or into `I18n.locale=`) rather than into a single before_filter.

title: Every request depends on I18n.fallbacks being the custom FallbackLocaleList
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` assumes `I18n.fallbacks` is the `FallbackLocaleList` defined in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`. `ensure_loaded!` does not exist on the stock `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`. Rails' I18n railtie configures fallbacks from `config.i18n.fallbacks` inside `config.after_initialize`, i.e. *after* `config/initializers/*` have run, and assigns `I18n.fallbacks = I18n::Locale::Fallbacks.new(...)`. This PR removed `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from production/profile/cloud66 only; if it is still set in any other environment file (development/test) or by any plugin/host config, the custom list is replaced at boot and then *every* request raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'ensure_loaded!'` in a before_filter — a complete outage. Either guard the call (`respond_to?`) or install the fallback list from an `after_initialize`/railtie hook that runs after Rails' own i18n setup.

title: `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` can raise and `.compact` cannot protect against it
body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `to_sym` on the site setting before the array is built, so a nil/blank `default_locale` raises `NoMethodError` instead of being removed by `compact` (`compact` after `uniq` only removes a nil `locale`). More importantly, this method is invoked by `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` on every missed translation, including during boot, migrations and `rake assets:precompile`, where `SiteSetting` may be unavailable (no DB / missing table) — turning a harmless missing-translation lookup into an exception. Resolve the default locale defensively (e.g. `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym` inside a rescue) and build the list as `[locale, default, :en].compact.uniq`.

title: LRU translation cache key ignores the fallback chain (stale strings after default_locale change)
body: The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. Now that a lookup result can come from `SiteSetting.default_locale` via the new fallback chain, the cached value depends on the site default locale, which is not part of the key and does not change the backend object. After an admin changes `default_locale`, every already-cached fallback translation for other locales keeps serving strings from the old default locale until the process is restarted or `I18n.reload!` is called. Include the fallback chain (or the default locale) in the cache key, or clear the LRU cache when `default_locale` changes.

title: No tests for the new fallback behaviour
body: This PR changes how every translation is resolved (custom fallback chain, on-demand loading of fallback locales, removal of `config.i18n.fallbacks`) but adds no specs. There is nothing verifying that (a) the fallback order is user locale → `SiteSetting.default_locale` → `:en`, (b) `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` actually loads the fallback locales' YAML so a key missing from the user locale resolves instead of returning “translation missing”, and (c) the chain is recomputed when `SiteSetting.default_locale` changes. Regressions here degrade silently into missing-translation strings, so at minimum a spec exercising a key present only in `en` while `I18n.locale` is a partial locale is needed.

title: `@loaded_locales ||= []` in ensure_loaded! runs outside LOAD_MUTEX
body: `ensure_loaded!` lazily initialises the shared `@loaded_locales` array outside the `LOAD_MUTEX` that `load_locale` uses. Two threads calling `ensure_loaded!` concurrently on a fresh process can each create a separate array; one of them is then discarded together with the locales it recorded, so locales get re-loaded (and the `@loaded_locales.include?` fast path in `translate` can be defeated) under load. Initialise the array inside the mutex (or at module load time) to keep the bookkeeping consistent.

title: translate() only lazy-loads the current locale, not the new fallback locales
body: Translations are loaded lazily per locale (`load_locale`). `translate` still only guarantees `config.locale` is loaded. Now that `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` is enabled and `FallbackLocaleList#[]` returns `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]`, a lookup that misses in the current locale will consult locales whose YAML may never have been loaded, so the fallback silently fails and `I18n.t` returns "translation missing". The only place that pre-loads the fallback chain is `ApplicationController#set_locale`, so every non-request code path is broken: Sidekiq jobs, mailers/notification emails rendered with the recipient's locale, rake tasks, the console, and any `I18n.with_locale` block. Worse, because `translate` memoizes no-arg lookups in the process-wide LRU cache, the bogus "translation missing" value is cached under that key and keeps being returned even after the fallback locale is eventually loaded. `translate` should ensure the whole `I18n.fallbacks[config.locale]` chain is loaded (or `ensure_loaded!` should be called from a lower-level hook than the controller filter).

title: LRU translation cache key does not include the fallback chain / SiteSetting.default_locale
body: The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`, but with the new fallbacks the resolved value for a given (key, locale) pair now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which is per-site and mutable. `@cache` is an ivar on the `I18n` module singleton, i.e. shared by every site served by the process. In a multisite install, site A (default_locale `fr`) looking up a key that is missing in `de` will cache the French string under `key+de`, and site B (default_locale `en`) will then serve that French string to its German users — cross-tenant content leakage. Even single-site, changing the `default_locale` setting does not invalidate these entries, so stale fallback translations persist until the process is restarted. The key must incorporate the fallback chain (or the cache must be reset when `default_locale` changes / be per-site).

title: Fallback lookup hits SiteSetting and allocates on every translation
body: `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on every single translation. The stock `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` memoizes the computed chain in the Hash; this override replaces `Hash#[]` and never stores anything, so each call performs a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read plus `to_sym`, `uniq`, `compact` and a fresh Array allocation. Every interpolated/pluralized lookup (`args.length > 0` bypasses the LRU cache in translate_accelerator) therefore pays this cost, which defeats part of the purpose of the translation accelerator. Memoize per locale and invalidate when `default_locale` changes.

title: Every request depends on a method that only exists on the custom fallbacks object
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only defined on `FallbackLocaleList`, the object assigned in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`. Rails' `I18n::Railtie.initialize_i18n` runs in `after_initialize` (i.e. after config/initializers) and, if `config.i18n.fallbacks` is truthy anywhere, executes `I18n.fallbacks = I18n::Locale::Fallbacks.new(...)`, silently replacing the custom object. Any plugin, environment file, or someone re-adding the line this PR just deleted from production.rb/profile.rb would then make this `before_filter` raise `NoMethodError` on every request — a full site outage, and only in that environment. Either define `ensure_loaded!` on `I18n` itself (next to `I18n.ensure_loaded!`) or guard with `respond_to?`.

title: New fallback behaviour has no tests and silently enables fallbacks in dev/test
body: Fallbacks were previously enabled only in production/profile/cloud66 via `config.i18n.fallbacks = true`; moving the setup into `config/initializers/i18n.rb` enables them in development and test too. That changes existing behaviour: specs (and developers) that previously saw "translation missing" for keys absent from a non-English locale will now silently get English text, so missing-translation regressions stop being detectable. No spec is added for the new `FallbackLocaleList` ordering (user locale → site default → :en), for `ensure_loaded!`, or for the lazy-loading interaction with fallbacks, which is where the real risk is (see the unloaded-fallback-locale problem in translate_accelerator).

title: @loaded_locales initialized outside LOAD_MUTEX in ensure_loaded!
body: `ensure_loaded!` does `@loaded_locales ||= []` outside `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` mutates and reads the same array inside the mutex and `translate` reads it without the mutex. Two threads entering `ensure_loaded!` concurrently when the ivar is nil can each assign a different array, so one thread's `@loaded_locales << locale` is lost; the subsequent `@loaded_locales.empty?` check in `load_locale` can then re-load all `.rb` locale files and re-load an already loaded locale. Initialize the array inside the mutex (or at boot) to keep the bookkeeping consistent.

title: `uniq.compact` cannot protect against a nil default_locale, and the chain depends on the DB
body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `to_sym` on the setting before `compact` can run, so if `SiteSetting.default_locale` ever returns nil this raises `NoMethodError` from inside an `I18n.t` call rather than falling back — the `compact` is dead code for that case. More generally, every translation now requires a readable `site_settings` state; in contexts where the DB/SiteSetting is unavailable (asset precompile without a DB, very early boot, error pages rendered while the DB is down) an `I18n.t` call will now blow up instead of returning a translation. Guard the setting read (`SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym` plus a rescue).

title: Denial cache can persist a deny caused by a stale folder tree, doubling the staleness window
body: After a DB re-query the result is cached as a denial for `shortCacheTTL` (30s). The re-query only refreshes the *permission* map; `checkInheritedPermissions`/`buildFolderTree` still use `folderCache` (also 30s), which is not refreshed. Concrete failure: a user with a grant on folder A creates subfolder B and a dashboard D inside B. `Check(dashboards:read, name=D, folder=B)` fails the direct `folders:uid:B` lookup and then walks `tree.Ancestors("B")`, which is empty because B is not in the cached folder tree, so the request is denied — and that denial is now written to `permDenialCache` with its own independent 30s TTL. If the deny happens just before the folder tree entry expires, the user keeps being denied for up to ~60s even though the refreshed tree would allow it. This is exactly the "creator cannot access the resource they just created" case the PR intends to fix. Consider also invalidating/refetching the folder tree before caching a denial, or not caching denials that depend on folder inheritance.

title: Permission-denial cache key omits identity type (and group/resource) that the decision depends on
body: `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)` is built in `Check` from the raw `checkReq.UserUID` returned by `types.ParseTypeID`, without the identity type. Different identity types share the same identifier space: `anonymous:0` and `render:0` both yield userUID "0", so a denial cached for the render service is returned for the anonymous user (and vice versa) for the same namespace/action/name/folder. The key also omits group and resource, while the decision does depend on them (`checkPermission` uses `mapper.translation(req.Group, req.Resource)` to derive the scope prefix and the `folderSupport` flag); any two group/resource pairs that map to the same action string would therefore share denial entries and produce false denials. Finally, because the raw subject identifier is used (numeric user ID for `user:1`, UID for `user:abc`), the same user gets separate denial entries depending on how the caller addressed them. Include the identity type, group and resource (or the resolved internal UID) in the key.

title: Every denied Check now performs a full permission re-query against the database
body: The permission-cache read was removed from `getUserPermissions`/`getAnonymousPermissions`, and `Check` now only short-circuits on a cached *allow*. Any cached-but-denied result falls through to `getIdentityPermissions`, which executes `GetUserPermissions` (plus basic-role/team lookups on their own cache misses) against the DB. The new denial cache only suppresses repeats of the exact same (user, action, name, folder) tuple, so a workload that checks many distinct resource names the subject cannot access (per-object checks from the resource server, UI pre-flight checks) issues one permission query per check. `singleflight` only dedupes concurrent calls, not sequential ones, so this is a significant increase in DB load compared with the previous behaviour where the 30s permission cache absorbed denies as well.

title: "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" test is vacuous and its comment is wrong
body: The comment says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but the permission cache is seeded with `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`. A `false` value means the scope lookup in `checkPermission` fails, so the request would be denied even if the denial cache were never consulted (the fallback DB query uses the default `fakeStore` with no permissions and also denies). The assertion therefore passes regardless of whether the new `permDenialCache` short-circuit works; the value must be `true` for the test to actually prove the denial cache takes precedence. There is also no test covering the write side of the new behaviour (that a DB-confirmed deny stores an entry under `userPermDenialCacheKey`), so the whole denial-cache feature is effectively untested.

title: permissionCacheUsage metric is misreported in Check
body: `s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", ...)` at line 137 is reached whenever the cached permissions did not yield an allow — including the case where the permission cache *did* hit but the decision was deny. Conversely, a hit in the new `permDenialCache` (line 118) is reported as a `permissionCacheUsage` hit even though it is a different cache. The resulting hit-rate metric no longer measures permission-cache effectiveness and will look much worse than it is, making it useless for tuning TTLs; use a distinct label/metric for the denial cache and only count a permission-cache miss when the cache actually missed.

title: Disabling the in-proc client cache moves per-request cost onto the server path
body: In-proc mode now passes `&NoopCache{}` to `authzlib.NewClient`, so no Check/List response is cached on the client side any more. Every authorization decision now goes through the in-proc channel into `Service.Check`, which reads the permission map out of the byte cache via `cacheWrap` and JSON-unmarshals it on every call. For users/service accounts with large permission sets (thousands of scopes) this adds a JSON decode of the whole scope map to every API request, where previously identical checks were served from the 30s client cache. Worth measuring before merge, or caching the decoded map in memory instead of re-decoding bytes per request.

title: Denial cache has unbounded key cardinality in a shared in-memory cache
body: Denial entries are keyed per (namespace, subject, action, resource name, parent folder), so their cardinality grows with the number of distinct resources any subject is denied on. They are stored in the same unbounded `cache.NewLocalCache` instance as the identity/permission/folder caches (configured in-proc with `CleanupInterval: 10 * time.Minute`), so although entries expire after 30s they are only reclaimed every 10 minutes. A burst of denied checks across many resource names can therefore retain a large amount of memory in the Grafana process; consider a bounded cache or a shorter cleanup interval for this cache.

title: Denial cache key is ambiguous: name/parent concatenation can collide
body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` builds the key as `namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent`. Because `_` is a legal character in Grafana resource/folder UIDs, different (name, parent) pairs map to the same key: e.g. name="a_b", parent="c" and name="a", parent="b_c" both yield `...action_a_b_c`. Since `Check` now short-circuits to `Allowed: false` on any hit in this cache (service.go:117), a denial recorded for one resource can silently deny access to a completely different resource the user is actually permitted to see, for up to the 30s TTL. Use an unambiguous encoding (e.g. length-prefixed or a separator that cannot appear in UIDs/actions, or hash the tuple).

title: Every denied Check now triggers a full permission re-query from the DB
body: The cache read was removed from `getUserPermissions`/`getAnonymousPermissions` and `Check` now only returns early from the cache when the cached scope map *allows* the request. Any request that is not allowed by the cached permissions falls through to `getIdentityPermissions`, which always queries the permission store. Combined with a denial cache that is keyed per (action, name, parentFolder), this means every distinct resource a user is denied on causes a fresh DB round-trip (user permissions, and on a cold cache basic roles and teams) once per 30s TTL window. Deny-heavy workloads (UI browsing/filtering that issues many per-resource Checks) will see a large increase in authz DB queries compared to before this change. Consider bounding the re-query (e.g. only re-query if the permission cache entry is older than some threshold, or a short negative-result TTL on the permission fetch itself).

title: Denial is cached even when it is caused by a stale folder tree
body: The fallback path re-queries permissions from the database, but `checkPermission` -> `checkInheritedPermissions` -> `buildFolderTree` still uses `folderCache` (30s TTL). If a folder was just created/moved and is missing from the cached tree, the inherited-permission check fails and the resulting denial is then written into `permDenialCache` for another 30s. So a denial caused purely by a stale folder tree gets pinned for up to ~2x the folder cache TTL, and the problem this PR is meant to fix (access to just-created folders/dashboards) still reproduces for resources whose access is inherited through a newly created folder. Either skip caching the denial when the decision depended on the (possibly stale) folder tree, or refresh/bypass the folder cache on the fallback path.

title: permissionCacheUsage metric no longer measures cache hit rate
body: `permissionCacheUsage` is incremented with "true" only when the cached permissions allow the request, and the unconditional `WithLabelValues("false", ...)` at this line is also reached when `getCachedIdentityPermissions` *succeeded* but the decision was deny. A permission-cache hit that results in a deny is therefore reported as a cache miss. In addition, a hit in the new `permDenialCache` (line 118) is reported as a `permissionCacheUsage` hit, conflating two different caches. The metric no longer reflects the permission cache hit rate, which makes it useless for tuning TTLs and for detecting cache regressions; it should either count hits/misses of the permission cache independently of the decision, or use a separate label/metric for the denial cache.

title: Denial-cache test does not actually prove the short-circuit
body: The subtest "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" comments "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked" but seeds the permission cache with `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`, i.e. the scope map does *not* grant access. With or without the `permDenialCache` entry the request would be denied (the default fake store returns no permissions), so the test passes even if the denial-cache short-circuit is removed. Set the scope to `true` so the test fails if the denial cache is not consulted, and additionally assert that the store was not queried (e.g. `fakeStore.calls == 0`).

title: In-proc authz client loses all client-side result caching
body: Replacing the authlib local cache with `NoopCache` for the in-proc client means every `Check` and every `Compile`/List performed by API handlers now goes through the in-proc gRPC channel and is fully re-evaluated server-side on every request; previously results were cached for 30s on the client. Server-side caching only covers the raw permission/identity lookups, not the per-request work: building the allowed folder/item sets in `listPermission` walks the whole scope map and folder subtree on every call, and (per the server change) any denied Check falls through to a DB query. For instances with many permissions/folders this is a noticeable per-request CPU and DB cost increase. If the goal is only freshness for newly created resources, consider a very short client TTL rather than disabling the cache entirely.

title: Denial-cache test does not actually prove the short-circuit
body: The new sub-test "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" seeds the permission cache with `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}` while the comment claims "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked". A value of `false` means `checkPermission` would deny anyway, and the fallback path uses the default `fakeStore` (no permissions), which also denies. The assertion `assert.False(t, resp.Allowed)` therefore passes whether or not the new `permDenialCache` short-circuit at the top of `Check` works. To actually cover the new behaviour the scope map must grant access (`"dashboards:uid:dash1": true`) so that the test fails if the denial cache is ignored. Additionally there is no test asserting that `permDenialCache` is written after a DB-confirmed denial (service.go:153-155), so that half of the new logic is untested.

title: Every non-allowed Check now hits the database; denial cache is per (name, folder) and unbounded
body: The cache lookups were removed from `getUserPermissions`/`getAnonymousPermissions`, and `Check` now falls through to `getIdentityPermissions` (a real `permissionStore.GetUserPermissions` query) whenever the cached scope map does not already allow the request. The only protection against repeated queries is `permDenialCache`, whose key includes the resource name and parent folder (cache.go:30) and whose TTL is only 30s. Consequently a caller that checks many distinct resource names the subject cannot access (object-by-object checks, or a client enumerating names) produces one uncached DB permission query per unique (action, name, folder) tuple, and fills the shared local cache with one entry per tuple (the authlib local cache has no size bound), so both DB load and memory are driven by caller-controlled input. This amplification is worse in-proc because the client-side cache was also disabled (rbac.go:103). Consider keeping a bounded/short-lived "permissions were just fetched" marker per (user, action) so the full re-query happens at most once per short interval rather than once per resource.

title: Denial cache key built from unescaped '_'-joined fields can collide
body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` concatenates `action`, `name` and `parent` with `_` separators and no escaping, so distinct requests can produce the same key: e.g. name="a_b", parent="" and name="a", parent="b_" both yield `...<action>_a_b_`. Dashboard/folder UIDs may legally contain underscores and are user-chosen, so a crafted (or merely unlucky) pair of UIDs makes a cached denial for one resource deny access to an unrelated resource for up to the 30s TTL (availability/incorrect-deny, not escalation, since only denials are stored). The key also omits group/resource, relying on `action` to encode them. Use a separator that cannot appear in UIDs/actions or include explicit length/field delimiters.

title: Stale folder tree still causes denials, and those denials are now cached
body: `Check` now re-queries permissions from the DB when the cached scope map does not allow the request, but `checkInheritedPermissions` -> `buildFolderTree` still returns the cached folder tree (30s TTL) and is never refreshed when the requested parent folder is absent from it. So for a resource whose access is granted only through inheritance from an ancestor (e.g. a dashboard created in a brand-new subfolder of a folder the user has permissions on), the tree does not yet contain the new folder, the check denies, and the denial is then stored in `permDenialCache` (line 154), extending the window during which the user cannot see the newly created object. The stated goal of the PR (immediate access to newly created folders/dashboards) is therefore only met for directly-granted scopes. Consider re-fetching the folder tree (or at least not caching the denial) when `req.ParentFolder` is not present in the cached tree.

title: permissionCacheUsage metric is mislabelled on the new Check paths
body: In `Check`, a denial-cache hit increments `permissionCacheUsage{hit="true"}` (line 118) even though the permission cache was not consulted at all, conflating two different caches in one metric. Conversely, when the permission cache *is* hit but the result is "not allowed", execution continues and line 137 increments `permissionCacheUsage{hit="false"}`, reporting a cache miss for a request that was served from the cache. Cache hit-rate dashboards/alerts built on this metric will be wrong after this change; the denial cache should get its own metric and the hit label should reflect whether `getCachedIdentityPermissions` succeeded.

title: Denial cache keyed on raw subject UID instead of the resolved user UID
body: `permDenialKey` uses `checkReq.UserUID`, the raw value parsed from the subject, while `permCache` keys use the resolved `userIdentifiers.UID` (see `getCachedIdentityPermissions`/`getUserPermissions`). Because `GetUserIdentifiers` treats a numeric subject as a user ID, the same identity addressed as `user:1` and as `user:<uid>` gets two independent denial entries (wasted lookups/queries), and a user whose UID is literally a decimal number shares denial entries with the user whose internal ID equals that number, which can deny the wrong identity for the TTL. Resolve the identifiers first and build the denial key from `userIdentifiers.UID` for consistency.

title: Missing `key` prop on GrafanaRuleListItem inside rules.map()
body: In `FilterViewResults`, the `grafana` branch of `rules.map(...)` now renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` without a `key`, while the `datasource` and `default` branches still pass `key={key}`. The pre-computed `key` (from `getRuleKey`) is destructured but unused for Grafana rules. This produces a React "Each child in a list should have a unique key" warning and makes reconciliation index-based; because this list grows by appending pages during infinite scroll, items can be re-created/re-ordered incorrectly and transient component state (e.g. an open action menu or drawer) can be attached to the wrong row.

title: Delete and Pause menu items can never render in the ruler-less list view
body: `AlertRuleMenu` now computes Grafana abilities from `promRule` (so Pause/Delete can be "allowed" without a ruler rule), but the rendering conditions were not updated: the Delete item is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165) and the Pause item on `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123). In the new rule list (`GrafanaRuleListItem` -> `RuleActionsButtons.V2` with only `promRule`), `rulerRule` is always undefined, so users can no longer pause or delete a rule from the list view even when they have permission. Note the delete handler itself only needs the identifier (`showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)`), so the gate is unnecessary. The new assertion `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)` in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx bakes this regression into the tests, and the `ui.menuItems.delete` selector added there is never used.

title: "Silence notifications" menu item is a no-op when only a Prometheus rule is available
body: The silence drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, where `rule` is the ruler rule. In the new list view only `promRule` is passed, so `rule` is undefined and `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` is never mounted. Meanwhile `AlertRuleMenu` now derives the Silence ability from the Prometheus rule (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`), so the "Silence notifications" item is shown (the new GrafanaGroupLoader test even asserts it exists). Clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer` to true and nothing happens — a visible, clickable action with no effect and no feedback.

title: Grafana-managed recording rules lose Pause/Export/Restore abilities in the Prometheus ability path
body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` uses `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` as the gate for `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore` and `DeletePermanently` (lines 324-330). The ruler-based equivalent used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which includes Grafana recording rules. Since Grafana-managed recording rules can be paused and exported, routing the list view through this hook silently removes the Pause, Export, Restore and Delete-permanently actions for every Grafana recording rule. Only `Silence` legitimately requires an alerting rule.

title: skipToken path grants Duplicate ability for non-Grafana rules
body: `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(skipToken, ...)` calls `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)`, which does not short-circuit: with `rule === undefined`, `loading` is false so `MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported`, `isPluginProvided` is false so `duplicateSupported = true`, and `Duplicate` becomes `[true, ctx.hasPermission(AlertingRuleCreate)]`. `AlertRuleMenu` ORs this with the ruler ability (`canDuplicate = ruler || grafana`), so for data-source (Mimir/Loki/Prometheus) rules — which always pass `skipToken` — the "Duplicate" item is shown to any user holding the Grafana `alert.rules:create` permission, even when the data source has no ruler or the user lacks external-write permission. The hook should return an all-false ability map when no rule is supplied.

title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable in the existing rule views
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` from the `CombinedRule`, which disabled Update/Delete/Pause for Mimir federated rule groups. It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, where `isFederated` is hardcoded to `false` (the `isFederatedRuleGroup` import was dropped). As a result, every consumer of `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (RulesTable, rule details, etc.) will now offer Edit/Delete on federated rules, which the backend rejects. The group information is no longer plumbed into the hook, so this needs an explicit fix (or at least the group's `source_tenants` passed through) rather than a TODO.

title: Provisioned-rule protection in the new list view is untested and depends on a newly declared optional field
body: `provenance?: string` is added to `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` and `isProvisionedPromRule` / `GrafanaRuleListItem` (`isProvisioned: Boolean(provenance)`) now rely exclusively on it to mark Grafana rules as provisioned in the ruler-less list view. No mock, fixture or test sets `provenance` on a Prometheus rule (e.g. `rulerRuleToPromRule` in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx omits it), and no test asserts that a provisioned rule hides Edit/Delete through this path. If the Grafana Prometheus rules endpoint does not return `provenance`, provisioned rules will silently become editable/deletable in the list, so this behaviour needs a test that pins it down.

title: Rule view link lost the returnTo parameter
body: The deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the rule href as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The replacement omits `returnTo`, so navigating from the rule list into a rule detail page no longer provides the "return to previous" target and the user loses the back-navigation affordance to their filtered list.

title: logWarning is emitted during render for every affected row
body: `getEditableIdentifier` is called directly in the component body and calls `logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier')` whenever neither a ruler rule nor a Grafana Prometheus rule is supplied. Because this runs on every render — and the rule list polls Prometheus every 20s, re-rendering all rows — a single unsupported row will emit the same warning repeatedly, spamming the analytics backend. Move the reporting into an effect (or dedupe it) so it fires once per occurrence.

title: Stale comment and variable name after removing ruler prefetching
body: The ruler prefetch (`alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)`) was removed, but the surrounding comment still says "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules ... but doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded" and the variable is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload`. Both now describe behaviour that no longer exists and will mislead future readers into thinking ruler data is still warmed up here.

title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered in a list without a `key`
body: In the `rules.map(...)` loop the `'grafana'` branch now returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` without passing `key={key}`, while the `'datasource'` and `default` branches still pass it. The component previously rendered (`GrafanaRuleLoader`) did receive the key. This produces React "Each child in a list should have a unique key" warnings and, because FilterView appends pages of results to the same array as the user scrolls, React will reconcile list items by index instead of identity – causing unnecessary unmounts/remounts and potentially showing stale rule content in the wrong row.

title: Delete and Pause menu items can never render without a ruler rule, so they disappear from the ruler-less list view
body: The menu still gates Delete on `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165) and Pause on `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123). After this change the Grafana rule list renders `RuleActionsButtons` with only `promRule` (see `GrafanaRuleListItem`), so `rulerRule` is always `undefined` there and both items are unconditionally hidden. The newly computed `grafanaDeleteAbility` / `grafanaPauseAbility` therefore have no effect (dead code), and users lose the ability to delete or pause a rule from the rule list – functionality that existed before this PR. The new test in `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` even asserts exactly 4 menu items with full permissions granted, codifying the loss of Delete/Pause.

title: "Silence notifications" menu item is visible but does nothing when only a Prometheus rule is available
body: `canSilence` in `AlertRuleMenu` is now also satisfied via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, so the "Silence notifications" item renders for rules in the list view where only `promRule` is passed. Clicking it calls `handleSilence`, which sets `showSilenceDrawer`, but the drawer is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true – `rule` (the ruler rule) is `undefined` in the list view. The result is a menu entry that silently does nothing. The silence drawer needs to be able to work from the Prometheus rule (uid/folder) or the item must be hidden.

title: skipToken path still computes permissive abilities for a non-existent rule
body: `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` map `skipToken` to `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)`, which does not short-circuit: with `rule === undefined`, `loading` is `false` (see `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`'s early return) and `isPluginProvided(undefined)` is `false`, so `MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported` and `[AlertRuleAction.Duplicate] = [true, hasPermission(AlertingRuleCreate)]` (same for View/Explore). Since `AlertRuleMenu` OR-combines ruler and Grafana-prom abilities, a data-source (Mimir/Prometheus/Loki) rule – which always passes `skipToken` – will show "Duplicate" even when the ruler-based check says duplication is unsupported (e.g. ruler API unavailable, federated, plugin-provided rule), leading the user into a clone flow that cannot succeed. The skipToken/undefined case should return an all-`[false, false]` ability map.

title: Federated rule-group immutability check dropped for CombinedRule abilities
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `isFederated = false` (the `isFederatedRuleGroup` import was removed). Previously the CombinedRule path computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, which marked rules in Mimir federated groups (`source_tenants` set) as immutable and hid Edit/Delete/Duplicate. With this change the existing rule list/detail pages will offer Edit and Delete for federated rule groups; saving such a group through the UI editor can drop `source_tenants` and silently break cross-tenant federation. The federated check needs to be preserved (or re-derived from the group identifier) before merging.

title: Grafana-managed recording rules lose Pause/Export/DeletePermanently support in the new ability hook
body: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` the supported flags for `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore` and `DeletePermanently` are derived from `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, i.e. alerting rules only. The ruler-based equivalent uses `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which is true for Grafana-managed recording rules as well – those rules do support pausing and modify-export. Since the list view now relies exclusively on this hook, Export (and Pause, once the menu gating is fixed) will be missing for Grafana recording rules, a regression from the current list.

title: OR-combining ruler and Prometheus abilities can override a deny, e.g. for provisioned rules
body: All abilities are now computed as `(rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (promSupported && promAllowed)`. Because a deny from the ruler-based check is ignored when the Prometheus-based check allows, any immutability signal that exists only in the ruler DTO is lost. Concretely, provisioning is detected in the prom path via `isProvisionedPromRule`, which reads the `provenance` field that is only now being added as an *optional* property on `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` (no backend change in this PR). If `/api/prometheus/grafana/api/v1/rules` does not return `provenance`, provisioned (file-provisioned/Terraform) rules will show Edit/Delete/Duplicate everywhere `promRule` is available – including the rule detail page where the ruler rule correctly reports the rule as immutable – and the subsequent write will be rejected by the API. Please confirm the API actually returns `provenance` and add a test with a provisioned rule; alternatively prefer the ruler result when it is available instead of OR-ing.

title: Analytics `logWarning` is invoked from render and can be emitted repeatedly
body: `getEditableIdentifier` is called during render and calls `logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier')` whenever neither a ruler rule nor a Grafana prom rule is supplied (e.g. a data-source Prometheus rule whose ruler rule has not loaded yet). Because this is a side effect in the render body it fires on every re-render of every such row, which can flood the analytics backend when a page contains many rules. Move the logging into an effect, or log once per identifier.

title: `returnTo` query param dropped from rule view links
body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the href as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem` omits it, so navigating from the (filtered) rule list into a rule detail page loses the "return to previous" context and the user is no longer sent back to the list they came from.

title: New Grafana-Prometheus ability logic has no unit tests
body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`, the `skipToken` handling and the OR-combination in `AlertRuleMenu`/`RuleActionsButtons` introduce ~130 lines of new permission logic, but there are no tests for them: `RulesTable.test.tsx` mocks the whole `useAbilities` module (so the real logic never runs) and `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` only covers the happy path with all permissions granted plus a single "no update permission" case. Important cases are untested: provisioned rules (`provenance`), plugin-provided rules, recording rules, and `skipToken` (data-source rules) returning permissive abilities.

title: Misleading test comment about skipToken behaviour
body: The repeated comment "Cloud rules only need useRulerRuleAbilities mock (useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gets skipToken)" is incorrect: `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` is still invoked with `skipToken` and, in production, still returns non-false abilities for some actions (see `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` with an undefined rule). The default `[false, false]` mock hides that behaviour, so the comment both misdescribes the code and conceals a gap in coverage for cloud rules.

title: Stale comment and variable name after removing the ruler prefetch
body: The ruler `prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)` dispatch was removed, but the surrounding comment still says "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX ... doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded" and the variable is still called `cacheAndRulerPreload`. Both now describe behaviour that no longer exists and will mislead the next reader into thinking ruler data is still being warmed up here.

title: Delete and Pause menu items can never render in the ruler-free list view
body: The menu now computes Delete/Pause abilities from the Prometheus rule (`grafanaDeleteAbility`, `grafanaPauseAbility`), but the rendering of those items is still gated on the ruler rule being present: `{canDelete && rulerRule && ...}` (line 165) and `{canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && ...}` (line 123). Since the new rule list (GrafanaRuleListItem -> RuleActionsButtons with only `promRule`) no longer loads ruler rules, `rulerRule` is always `undefined` there, so Delete and Pause disappear from the alert rule list menu even for users with permission. This is a user-visible regression: rules can no longer be deleted or paused from the list view. Either the gates must be relaxed to work from `promRule` (deriving the identifier/pause mutation from the Prometheus rule) or the actions must be hidden consistently with the computed abilities.

title: "Silence notifications" menu item is a no-op when only a Prometheus rule is available
body: `canSilence` in AlertRuleMenu is now satisfied by the Prometheus-rule abilities (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`), so the "Silence notifications" item is rendered in the new list view. However the drawer is still rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true (line 104), and `rule` (the ruler rule) is `undefined` for list-view items that only pass `promRule`. Clicking the menu item therefore sets `showSilenceDrawer` but nothing ever opens — a dead menu entry. The GrafanaGroupLoader test asserts the item exists but never clicks it, so this is not caught. The drawer needs a path that works from the Prometheus rule (e.g. lazily fetch the ruler rule when opening) or the item must be hidden when no ruler rule is available.

title: Missing React `key` on GrafanaRuleListItem in the filtered list
body: In the `case 'grafana'` branch the newly used `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` is rendered without the `key={key}` prop that the previous `<GrafanaRuleLoader>` had (the other branches still pass `key`). The surrounding `rules.map(...)` produces a list, so React will log the "Each child in a list should have a unique key" warning and fall back to index-based reconciliation. Because this list is appended to incrementally during infinite scrolling, index-based reconciliation can reuse the wrong component instances (stale internal state such as open menus/drawers) for the wrong rule.

title: Federated rule group check dropped from useAllAlertRuleAbilities
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and treated federated groups as immutable, hiding Update/Delete/Pause. It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false` with a TODO. As a result every consumer of `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (rules table, rule details, rule viewer) will now offer Edit/Delete for Mimir/Cortex federated rule groups (groups with `source_tenants`). Editing such a group through the UI, which has no notion of `source_tenants`, can silently drop the federation configuration on save. The federated check should be preserved (the group/`source_tenants` information is available on the CombinedRule) before merging.

title: Grafana-managed recording rules lose Pause and Export abilities in the Prometheus ability hook
body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` uses `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` as the "is Grafana managed" flag for `Pause`, `ModifyExport`, `Restore` and `DeletePermanently`. The ruler-based equivalent used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which is true for both Grafana alerting *and* Grafana recording rules. Grafana-managed recording rules support pausing and export, so after this change the list view will report Pause/ModifyExport as unsupported for them and the corresponding actions disappear. The flag should be `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` for these abilities, with `alertingRule` reserved for alerting-only concerns such as Silence.

title: Rule view link no longer carries the `returnTo` parameter
body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader.GrafanaRuleListItem` built the href as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new component drops the `returnTo` query parameter entirely. Consequently navigating from the rule list into a rule detail page loses the "return to previous" context, so the back/return affordance on the rule view will not bring the user back to the filtered list they came from. If this is intentional it should be stated; otherwise `createReturnTo()` should be re-added.

title: Test codifies the missing Delete/Pause actions and never exercises Silence
body: The new test asserts `menuItems.length).toBe(4)` (silence, copy link, duplicate, export) while the user has been granted `AlertingRuleDelete`/`AlertingRuleUpdate` both globally and on the folder. Delete and Pause are missing purely because AlertRuleMenu still requires a ruler rule to render them, so this assertion locks in the regression instead of detecting it. In addition, the `delete` selector added to `ui.menuItems` is never used, and the silence item is only asserted to exist — it is never clicked, which is why the non-functional silence drawer (it requires a ruler rule) goes unnoticed. The test should assert the full expected action set, including a click-through for Silence/Delete.

title: Provisioned-rule protection in the new list depends on an untested optional `provenance` field
body: `provenance` is added as an optional field on `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` and is the only signal used by `isProvisionedPromRule` (utils/rules.ts) and `GrafanaRuleListItem`'s `isProvisioned` flag now that the ruler response is no longer fetched in the list view. If the Grafana Prometheus rules endpoint does not populate `provenance` (it is optional, so a missing value is silently falsy), provisioned/file-provisioned rules will be rendered as editable and expose Edit/Delete actions that the API will later reject. There is no test in this PR covering a provisioned Grafana rule in the list view; one should be added (and the API response confirmed to include `provenance`).

title: logWarning is called from the render body on every render
body: `getEditableIdentifier` is invoked directly during render and calls `logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier')` when neither a ruler rule nor a Grafana Prometheus rule is available (e.g. a data-source Prometheus rule with no ruler counterpart). Because this is a side effect inside render, the warning is emitted on every re-render (and twice per render under StrictMode) for each affected row, which can flood the analytics/log backend on a list page with many such rules. The logging should be moved into an effect or deduplicated.

title: Queries are now interpolated twice (ad hoc filters applied twice)
body: `runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on every target, but the sub-requests it builds (`{ ...request, targets }`) still carry the original `scopedVars`/`filters` and are executed through `datasource.runQuery()` -> `DataSourceWithBackend.query()`, which calls `applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` again for each target.
