body: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, i.e. typically `SUN`/`SunJSSE`, which is not a BouncyCastle provider as the interface documents ("BouncyCastle security provider. Can be either non-FIPS or FIPS based provider"). `BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` is derived from this value and is used throughout keycloak-core as the provider name for `Signature.getInstance(alg, PROVIDER)`, `KeyStore.getInstance("BCFKS", PROVIDER)`, `Cipher.getInstance("AES/CBC/PKCS7Padding", PROVIDER)`, etc. With this provider selected, those calls will silently be routed to the JDK provider and fail with a confusing `NoSuchAlgorithmException` for BC-only algorithms. If no BC provider is available, either return `null` (as `WildFlyElytronProvider` does) or throw a descriptive `UnsupportedOperationException` explaining that BouncyCastle is not on the classpath.

title: NPE when the aggregate "Clients" resource does not exist
body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when no per-client resource exists the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and immediately passes the result to `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)` without a null check. `getResourceTypeResource()` returns `null` in two reachable situations: (a) `supportsAuthorizationSchema()` is false, i.e. the realm still has an admin-permissions client (so `root.realmResourceServer()` is non-null) but `realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled()` was turned off, and (b) the realm's resource server has no resource named `Clients` (e.g. a realm whose FGAP client was created before this PR, see the missing migration). The policy store dereferences `resource.getId()`, so this throws a NullPointerException, and because `canManage/canConfigure/canView/canMapRoles` all go through this method, every admin REST call touching a client would fail with HTTP 500. Add a null check and return `false`.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns the literal "Clients" and never a real client id
body: `getClientsWithPermission()` iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and adds `resource.getName()` to the result. Only the aggregate resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` has its type set to `Clients` (`resource.setType(type)`); per-client resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` are created with `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner)` and never get a type. Consequently this method (1) can only ever return the string `"Clients"`, which is not a client id, and (2) never returns the ids of clients that actually have a permission granted. Any caller using this set to decide which clients an admin may act on will both miss all legitimately permitted clients and receive a bogus entry. Either set the resource type when creating per-client resources, or resolve the granted clients differently (and exclude the aggregate resource name).

title: canView() ignores the manage scope, breaking "manage implies view" for client scopes/listing
body: `canView()` is implemented as `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(VIEW)`. Unlike every other place in this class (`canView(ClientModel)` falls back to `canManage(client)`, `canView(ClientScopeModel)` checks VIEW *or* MANAGE) and unlike V1 where the `manage-clients` role implies view, the global `manage` permission does not imply `canView()`. Since `canList()`, `canListClientScopes()`, `canViewClientScopes()` and `requireView()` (not overridden) are all derived from `canView()`, an admin granted only the all-clients `manage` permission is denied listing/viewing realm client scopes (`requireListClientScopes()` → 403) while `canManageClientScopes()` returns true, so the same admin may create and modify client scopes but cannot list them. `canView()` should also consider the `manage` scope.

title: canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException on a runtime (non-admin) code path
body: `canExchangeTo(...)` now throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. This method is not only an admin-console concern: the legacy token-exchange flow calls `AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(...)` to authorize exchanging to a target client, and `AdminPermissions.management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever the `admin-fine-grained-authz:v2` feature is enabled — independently of whether the legacy FGAP feature is enabled. With both the (legacy) token-exchange feature and FGAP v2 enabled, token-exchange requests will produce an HTTP 500 from the unchecked exception instead of a clean 403 denial. The V1 implementation returned `false` when no resource server/permission existed; this override should do the same (or the caller must be made V2-aware).

title: Listener guard does not protect against V1+V2 both enabled; client removal will fail with 500
body: The removal listener is now only executed when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1) is enabled, presumably because `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled()` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. But `management()` (line 67) prefers `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled, and the two preview features are not mutually exclusive. When both are enabled, a `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` reaches `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`, which now throws `UnsupportedOperationException` and aborts the client deletion transaction (HTTP 500). The same applies to the `/clients/{id}/management/permissions` admin endpoints, which call `clients().isPermissionsEnabled()`/`getPermissions()` after the V1 feature check passes. The guard should select the V1 implementation explicitly (or V2 should no-op instead of throwing) for these legacy operations.

title: No migration for realms whose admin-permissions client already exists
body: `init()` returns early when `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null`, so realms where FGAP v2 was already enabled before this change never receive the newly added `Clients` resource nor the new scopes (`configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, `map-roles-composite`). In such realms: creating a Clients permission reaches `getOrCreateResource()` and hits `throw new ModelException("No scopes found.")` (line 108) for the missing scopes, all-clients evaluation silently returns `false` because `resourceStore.findByName(server, "Clients", ...)` is null, and per-client evaluation NPEs on the null aggregate resource (ClientPermissionsV2 line 219). The PR adds no upgrade/migration step to create the missing scopes and resource for existing admin-permissions clients.

title: getResourceName has no handling for the Clients resource type
body: `getResourceName()` translates resource names to human-readable values only for the `Users` resource type ("All users" for the aggregate resource, the username for per-user resources) and otherwise returns `resource.getDisplayName()`. Per-client resources are created in `getOrCreateResource()` without a display name, and the aggregate `Clients` resource has none either, so every Clients permission exposed through the admin REST API/console will report a `null` resource name instead of the client id/clientId or an "All clients" label. The new resource type needs a branch here (resolving the client via `session.clients().getClientById()`), consistent with the Users handling.

title: resolveClient allows permissions to target the admin-permissions client itself
body: `resolveClient()` resolves any client in the realm, including the realm's own admin-permissions (FGAP policy) client and `realm-management`, even though the class already provides `throwExceptionIfAdminPermissionClient()` for exactly this kind of guard and it is not used here. As a result an administrator can create a Clients permission whose resource is the admin-permissions client and grant `manage`/`configure` on it; since the client authorization admin endpoints are gated on being able to manage the owning client, the grantee can then modify or delete all fine-grained admin permission policies — a privilege escalation out of the restricted scope they were given. Target clients that back the FGAP/admin infrastructure should be rejected when resolving the resource.

title: Javadoc for void require* methods says they return true
body: `requireView()` (line 98) and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line 103) are `void`, but the new Javadoc states "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}" / "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}". These should follow the convention used for the other require* methods in this file: "Throws ForbiddenException if ... returns {@code false}". As written the contract documented for implementors/callers is wrong.

title: Dead code and unused imports copied from the V1 implementation
body: `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` (line 262) is private and never called, the `logger` field (line 51) is unused, and the imports `org.keycloak.authorization.model.Scope`, `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `EvaluationContext` and the static import of `AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE` are unused. This dead code (apparently copied from `ClientPermissions`) suggests token-exchange support was intended but is not implemented, and it will mislead future readers. Remove it (or implement the missing behaviour).

title: New Clients scopes and all-clients fallback combinations are untested
body: The added tests cover `manage`, `configure`, `view`, `map-roles` and `map-roles-composite`, but there is no test for the newly introduced `map-roles-client-scope` scope (`canMapClientScopeRoles`), none for `getClientsWithPermission()` (which, as implemented, cannot return any client id), and none for the combination of an all-clients permission with an unrelated per-client permission — a case where `hasPermission(ClientModel, scope)` stops consulting the aggregate `Clients` resource as soon as a per-client resource exists, so a previously granted all-clients permission silently stops applying to that client. These are exactly the paths most likely to regress.

title: Feature guard stops cleanup of legacy fine-grained permission policies
body: Previously the role/client/group removal listener ran unconditionally and invoked `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)`, which deletes the V1 fine-grained permission policies/resources associated with the removed object. With the new `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` guard, deployments that created V1 FGAP data and later disabled the preview feature will leak orphan policies and resources into the authorization store when the corresponding roles/clients/groups are deleted, leaving the data inconsistent if the feature is re-enabled. If the intent was only to avoid the V2 `UnsupportedOperationException`, the guard should select the V1 management implementation rather than skipping cleanup entirely.

title: NPE when the 'Clients' resource-type resource does not exist
body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when no per-client resource is found the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and immediately passes the result to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` without a null check. `getResourceTypeResource` returns `null` in several reachable cases: the realm has an admin-permissions client but `realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled()` is false (so `supportsAuthorizationSchema` returns false), or the `Clients` resource simply does not exist (e.g. a realm whose admin-permissions client was created before this schema change, see the `init()` early-return). Also, if `findByResource` happens to be non-empty while `resource` is null, `new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server)` dereferences null. The result is a NullPointerException in authorization checks, i.e. HTTP 500 on ordinary admin client endpoints instead of a clean allow/deny. Add a null check that returns `false` when the fallback resource is missing.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns the resource-type name and misses per-client grants
body: `getClientsWithPermission` iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and adds `resource.getName()` to the result. Per-client resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner)` without ever setting a resource type, so they are never returned by `findByType`. The only resource with type `Clients` is the "all clients" resource created in `init()`, whose name is the literal string `"Clients"`. Consequently this method returns either an empty set or `{"Clients"}` — never real client ids — while callers of `ClientPermissionEvaluator.getClientsWithPermission(scope)` expect a set of client ids (the V1 implementation strips the `client.resource.` prefix and returns ids). Grants on individual clients are invisible to those callers and the bogus `"Clients"` entry can be mistaken for a client id.

title: canExchangeTo now throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking legacy token exchange when V2 is enabled
body: `ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo(...)` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. Because `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns `ClientPermissionsV2` (previously it returned the V1 `ClientPermissions`), the legacy token-exchange flow, which calls `AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(client, targetClient, token)`, will now blow up with an unchecked exception and return HTTP 500 whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled together with the token-exchange feature. Either keep delegating to the V1 behaviour or make the caller aware that token exchange permissions are not available in V2 and return a proper deny/400 instead of an unhandled runtime exception.

title: Management-permissions admin endpoints return 500 with V2 enabled
body: `isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel)`, `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)`, `getPermissions(ClientModel)` and `resource(ClientModel)` all throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. These are invoked directly by the admin REST endpoints `GET`/`PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management/permissions` (`ClientResource.getManagementPermissions`/`setManagementPermissionsEnabled`). Since `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns this class, enabling `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` turns those endpoints from working (V1) responses into unhandled runtime exceptions, i.e. HTTP 500. A deliberate 400/404 (e.g. `ModelValidationException`/`NotFoundException`) would be the appropriate contract for "not supported in V2".

title: Listener guard checks the V1 feature, so client removal still hits V2 code paths
body: The provider-event listener body is now guarded by `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`, but the code inside calls `management(session, realm)` which dispatches to `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled. If both preview features are enabled at the same time (nothing prevents this), removing a client executes `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)`, which now throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (ClientPermissionsV2), aborting client deletion with an internal error. The guard should also exclude the V2 feature (or the listener should explicitly use the V1 `MgmtPermissions`). Additionally, gating cleanup on the V1 feature means that when the feature is turned off, previously created V1 permission policies for removed roles/clients/groups are left behind as orphans.

title: No migration of new scopes/resource for already initialized admin-permissions clients
body: `init()` returns early when `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null`, so realms that already had admin permissions enabled before this change never get the newly introduced scopes (`configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, `map-roles-composite`) nor the `Clients` resource-type resource. On such realms, creating a Clients permission fails: `getScope()` throws `ModelValidationException("Scope [configure] does not exist.")`, and `getOrCreateResource()` throws `ModelException("No scopes found.")` when building the per-client resource (HTTP 500), and `hasPermission()` in ClientPermissionsV2 cannot find the fallback `Clients` resource. Some upgrade/initialization path is needed to add missing schema scopes and resource-type resources to existing admin-permissions clients.

title: getResourceName not extended for the Clients resource type
body: `getResourceName` resolves friendly names only for the `Users` resource type ("All users" / username). For the newly added `Clients` resource type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is null for resources created by `getOrCreateResource` (only name and owner are set). As a result, permissions created for clients will be reported without a resolvable name in representations, unlike user permissions, and there is no "All clients" label for the resource-type resource.

title: Javadoc on require* methods describes a return value for void methods
body: `requireView()` (line 98) is documented as "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}." and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line 103) as "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}." Both methods are `void` and, consistently with the other `require*` methods in this interface, throw `ForbiddenException` when the corresponding `can*` check fails. The Javadoc therefore documents behaviour that does not exist and should read "Throws ForbiddenException if ... returns {@code false}".

title: Dead code and unused imports left from copy/paste
body: The class contains a private, never-called `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` method (line 262), an unused `logger` field (line 51) and unused imports/static imports (`Scope`, `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `EvaluationContext`, `AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE`). This is leftover from copying the V1 implementation; it produces compiler warnings and suggests an evaluation-context customization that is not actually applied. It should be removed.

title: New map-roles-client-scope scope is untested
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` is added to the Clients resource type and `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles` is implemented, but no test exercises it (tests only cover `manage`, `configure`, `view`, `map-roles` and `map-roles-composite`). Likewise there is no test for the all-clients `configure` permission or for a negative-logic (deny) client permission. Without coverage, regressions in the client-scope role mapping evaluation would go unnoticed.

title: testManageOnlyOneClient mutates shared realm state without cleanup
body: `testManageOnlyOneClient` renames `myclient` (`setName("somethingNew")`), removes one of its default client scopes and adds it as an optional scope, but registers no `realm.cleanup()` task to restore it. The realm/client are shared by the other tests in this class (only scope permissions are cleaned in `@AfterEach`), so the mutated client-scope assignment and name leak into subsequent tests, making the suite order-dependent and potentially flaky (e.g. other tests index into `getDefaultClientScopes()`).

title: Possible NPE when the "Clients" resource-type resource does not exist
body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` the fallback path assigns `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and immediately passes it to `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)` without a null check. `getResourceTypeResource()` returns `null` in two reachable situations: (a) `supportsAuthorizationSchema()` is false (admin-permissions client exists but `realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled()` is false), and (b) the realm's admin-permissions client was created before the `Clients` resource type was added to the schema, so no resource named "Clients" exists (there is no migration adding it). In both cases the policy store is queried with a null resource, which will throw a NullPointerException and turn every client-related admin REST call (view/manage/list clients) into an HTTP 500. The method should return `false` when the resource-type resource is missing.

title: getClientsWithPermission() returns the aggregate resource name instead of client ids
body: `getClientsWithPermission(scope)` iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and collects `resource.getName()`. Two problems: (1) per-client resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` are created with `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner)` and never get a `type` set, so `findByType("Clients", ...)` never returns them — clients that have an individual permission are never reported; (2) the only resource actually typed "Clients" is the aggregate resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()`, whose name is the literal string "Clients", so the returned set can contain "Clients" as if it were a client id. Callers of `ClientPermissionEvaluator#getClientsWithPermission` (which in V1 returns internal client ids) therefore get either an empty set or a bogus id, so the permission-based filtering this method implements is broken.

title: getResourceName() not extended for the new Clients resource type
body: `getResourceName()` only resolves names for the `Users` resource type. Now that `Clients` permissions can be created, policies with `resourceType=Clients` fall through to `return resource.getDisplayName()`, which is `null` for resources created by `getOrCreateResource()` (created with name + owner only, no display name) and for the aggregate "Clients" resource. As a result, representations of client permissions returned to the admin REST API/console will show a null resource name, whereas user permissions show the username or "All users". The Clients branch (client id/clientId and "All clients") is missing.

title: No migration for realms whose admin-permissions client already exists
body: `init()` returns early when `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null`, so the new scopes (`configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, `map-roles-composite`) and the new aggregate `Clients` resource are only created for realms where admin permissions are enabled for the first time after this change. For any realm that already had the admin-permissions client created with the previous schema, these scopes/resources never get created, which means: `getOrCreateResource()` throws `ModelException("No scopes found.")` when creating a Clients permission, `getScope()` throws `ModelValidationException` for the new scope names, and `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission()` hits the null `Clients` resource (see the NPE issue). Either an upgrade path that adds missing scopes/resource-type resources, or at least graceful handling, is needed.

title: UnsupportedOperationException on reachable runtime/admin paths yields HTTP 500
body: `canExchangeTo(...)`, `isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel)` and `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, but these are invoked from paths that are reachable while the V2 feature is enabled: the legacy token-exchange flow calls `AdminPermissions.management(...).clients().canExchangeTo(...)` (producing a 500 on a token endpoint instead of a denial), and `ClientResource` exposes `GET /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management/permissions`, which calls `isPermissionsEnabled(client)` and is invoked by the admin console (again a 500 instead of a well-formed error). These should either deny/return a defined response for V2 or the calling endpoints should be guarded by the feature flag.

title: Javadoc for void require* methods says they return true
body: `requireView()` (line 95-98) and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line 100-103) are documented as "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}" / "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but both methods are `void` and, consistently with the other `require*` methods, throw `ForbiddenException` when the corresponding `can*` check fails. The Javadoc is misleading for anyone implementing or calling the interface and should read "Throws ForbiddenException if ... returns false".

title: New map-roles-client-scope scope is not covered by any test
body: The PR adds three new scopes to the schema (`configure`, `map-roles-composite`, `map-roles-client-scope`) and the corresponding evaluation methods in `ClientPermissionsV2` (`canMapClientScopeRoles`). The new tests cover `manage`, `view`, `configure`, `map-roles` and `map-roles-composite`, but there is no test exercising `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` / `canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` (e.g. adding a client role to a client scope's scope mappings), so that scope's evaluation path is completely untested.

title: Tests mutate shared realm state without cleanup, making them order-dependent
body: `testManageOnlyOneClient` permanently renames `myclient` (`myclient.setName("somethingNew"); clientResource.update(myclient)`), removes a default client scope and re-adds it as an optional scope, and `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` creates the roles `myclient-role`/`myclient-subRole` on `myclient`. Unlike the policies created via `createUserPolicy(...)` (which register a `realm.cleanup()` hook) and unlike `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest` (which deletes the users it creates in `@AfterEach`), none of this state is reverted; only scope permissions are removed in `onAfter()`. Since the managed realm is shared by all tests in the class, later tests observe a changed default-client-scope list (e.g. `defaultClientScopes.get(1)` / `get(0)` indices) and left-over roles, which makes the suite order-dependent and prone to flaky failures.

title: Dead code and unused imports in the new class
body: `ClientPermissionsV2` contains a private, never-called `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` method (copied from the V1 token-exchange logic, which this class explicitly does not support), an unused `logger` field, and unused imports (`org.keycloak.authorization.model.Scope`, `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `EvaluationContext`, and the static `AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE`). This dead code suggests token-exchange support that does not exist here and should be removed.

title: Exit-code contract changed: 4 now means "feature disabled" instead of "recreate required"
body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` was changed from 4 to 3 and 4 is reused for the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` result. Any consumer written against the previously released behaviour of the `update-compatibility check` command (automation/DevOps pipelines, as explicitly encouraged by the guide, and the Operator's auto-update logic that inspects the Job's exit code) will now mis-interpret results: a check that tested `exit == 4` for "recreate needed" will now trigger a downtime upgrade when the only problem is that the preview feature is not enabled, and will not recognise exit code 3 at all. The reverse mapping is just as harmful: code expecting 3 to be unused will now receive it for the common recreate case. Since both codes are swapped in the same release, consumers must be updated in lockstep (operator source is not touched in this PR) and the change should be called out in release notes / upgrade notes.

title: New/changed exit codes are not asserted by any test
body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the stderr message and only for the `metadata` sub-command; it never asserts that the process exits with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` (4), and the `check` sub-command is not covered at all. Likewise `testWrongVersions` asserts only the error text, not the new `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` (3). Because the exit codes are the documented, scriptable contract of this command (and were just renumbered from 4 to 3), a regression in either value would pass CI unnoticed. Add assertions on `result.exitCode()` for the feature-disabled case (both sub-commands) and for the incompatible-version case.

title: Documented command appends --features=rolling-updates, silently replacing the user's feature set
body: The `updatecompatibility` macro now renders `bin/kc.[sh|bat] update-compatibility <params> --features=rolling-updates`. `--features` is a list option that replaces, not extends, the configured feature set, so a deployment that runs with e.g. `--features=admin-fine-grained-authz` will be analysed with a different feature configuration than the running server. This directly contradicts the warning in update-compatibility.adoc ("Ensure that all configuration options ... are included ... Omitting any configuration options will result in incomplete metadata") and can yield a wrong rolling/recreate verdict. The docs should instead instruct the user to add `rolling-updates` to their existing `--features` value. The same rendered command also breaks for pre-built/optimized distributions, where passing the build-time `--features` option together with `--optimized` is rejected.

title: CR-only instructions for enabling rolling-updates are incomplete for custom/optimized images
body: The new CAUTION and the example tell users to enable the preview feature only via `spec.features.enabled: [rolling-updates]`. For deployments using a custom image (`spec.image`), the Operator starts the server with `--optimized`, so build-time options such as `features` must already be baked into the image - exactly what this PR does for the test image in `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image` (`kc.sh build ... --features=rolling-updates`). Without mentioning this, users of custom images will either see the server reject the build-time option or run without the feature while believing it is enabled. The CAUTION also does not say how the Operator "will fail", which makes it hard to diagnose.

title: New feature enum requires regenerating CLI help/doc snapshots
body: `ROLLING_UPDATES` is added to `Profile.Feature`, which feeds the `--features` option's enumerated "Possible values" text in the CLI help and the generated configuration documentation. The approved help output files under `quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/resources/help/` (compared verbatim by the help dist tests) are not updated in this PR, so those tests will fail or the documented feature list will be stale. Regenerate the approved help output after adding the feature.

title: setEnabledFeatures overwrites any features already configured in the test deployment
body: `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))` replaces the whole list. The preceding null check on `getFeatureSpec()` implies the base deployment produced by `getTestKeycloakDeployment(true)` may already carry a FeatureSpec with enabled features; those would be silently dropped, changing what the test actually exercises (and potentially breaking the test if a required feature is removed). Append to the existing list instead of overwriting it.

title: Feature `rolling-updates` is only enabled for the non-null update strategy in UpgradeTest
body: `createInitialDeployment()` returns early (`return kc;`) when `updateStrategy == null`, so the `spec.features.enabled: [rolling-updates]` block is only added for the `RECREATE` parameter. Both parameterized tests (`testImageChange`, `testCacheMaxCount`) therefore run the default/unset-strategy case with the preview feature disabled in the CR, which directly contradicts the new documentation added in this PR ("While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail."). Either the default strategy path is being tested in an unsupported configuration (and may pass only by accident, e.g. because the test image happens to have the feature built in), or the documented requirement is wrong. In addition, the null and RECREATE runs now differ in two dimensions (strategy *and* feature set), making any failure ambiguous.

title: No test covers the changed/added exit codes (3 for recreate, 4 for feature disabled)
body: This PR changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`, and the documentation explicitly tells users to script against these exit codes. However, `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the stderr text and never asserts `exitCode() == 4`, and `testWrongVersions` never asserts `exitCode() == 3`. Note also that `@Launch`-based tests in this suite do not validate the exit code (see the pre-existing `testMissingSubCommand` which really exits with 2). As a result, a regression in the documented exit-code contract — the only thing automation is supposed to rely on — would go unnoticed. The feature gate is also only exercised for the `metadata` subcommand; the identical gate added to `check` is untested.

title: Exit code 4 is re-used with a different meaning while recreate moves to 3
body: Before this change, exit code 4 meant "recreate upgrade required"; after this change 4 means "the rolling-updates feature is disabled" and recreate is signalled with 3. Any existing automation or operator logic that was written against the implemented behaviour (4 == recreate) will now silently interpret "feature disabled" as "recreate required", and will not react to the new code 3 at all. Since the value is being recycled rather than a fresh code allocated, consider using an unused code (e.g. 5) for the new condition, or at minimum call out the incompatible exit-code change in the release notes / upgrade guide for this preview tool.

title: Documented command passes the build-time option `--features` at runtime
body: The `updatecompatibility` macro now renders every documented invocation as `bin/kc.[sh|bat] update-compatibility <args> --features=rolling-updates`. `features` is a build-time option: on a distribution/container that was already built (`kc.sh build`, or any optimized image) specifying it on a runtime command either forces a re-augmentation on every invocation (slow, and impossible on a read-only container filesystem) or is rejected when `--optimized` is in effect. The guide should instead instruct users to enable `rolling-updates` at build time (as this PR does for `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image`), otherwise the copy-pasteable commands in the guide will not work in the main production deployment style. There is also a correctness trap: the guide elsewhere insists the metadata/check commands be run with exactly the deployment's configuration, yet here it tells users to add a feature the running deployment does not have.

title: Operator preview note does not cover custom images and is vague about the failure
body: The new CAUTION states only that "the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail", and the example enables it via `spec.features.enabled`. For users running a custom/optimized image the Operator cannot change build-time options such as `features`, so the CR snippet will not have any effect — the feature has to be baked into the image at build time (exactly what this PR does in `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image`). The doc should say this. The sentence is also inconsistent with the NOTE a few lines below, which says that during preview the default strategy just mimics 26.1 behaviour, leaving the reader unsure whether the feature is required even when `spec.update.strategy` is unset, and "will fail" gives no observable symptom (condition, event, job failure) to look for.

title: Exit code 4 is only documented for the `check` command although `metadata` returns it too
body: The exit-code table (including the newly added `4` = "the feature rolling-updates is disabled") sits in the "Checking the Metadata" section and is introduced as "the command's exit code". `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` also exits with 4 when the feature is disabled, so scripts wrapping the `metadata` step get an undocumented exit code. The "Generating the Metadata" section should state the same behaviour, or the table should be moved/annotated as applying to both subcommands.

title: Recreate exit code silently renumbered from 4 to 3 and 4 reused for a new meaning
body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` is changed from 4 to 3 and the value 4 is now reused for `FEATURE_DISABLED`. The exit code of `kc.sh update-compatibility check` is explicitly documented as the stable contract for automation (see update-compatibility.adoc: "they should rely only on the exit code of the `check` command"). Any script or operator logic written against the previously shipped behaviour that treats 4 as "recreate required" will now see 4 for a completely different condition (feature not enabled) and will see an undefined 3 when a recreate is actually required, so the branch selecting recreate vs. rolling can be taken wrongly or the pipeline will abort with an "unknown exit code". If this renumbering is intentional, it should at least be called out as a breaking change in the release notes/migration docs, and all consumers (including the operator code that interprets the command's exit status) must be verified to use the constant rather than a literal.

title: No test asserts the new/changed exit codes (3 for recreate, 4 for feature disabled)
body: The PR changes the recreate exit code from 4 to 3 and introduces 4 for "feature disabled", yet no test verifies either value. `testFeatureNotEnabled` (line 48-50) only asserts the stderr message and never checks that the process exits with 4, and `testWrongVersions` (lines 96-106) only asserts the error message and never checks that the incompatible case exits with 3. Only the success path asserts an exit code (`assertEquals(0, result.exitCode())`). Since the exit code is the documented, scriptable contract of this command, a regression in the numbering would pass CI unnoticed. Additionally, the feature-disabled path is only exercised for the `metadata` subcommand; the `check` subcommand's new guard is untested.

title: CAUTION about required feature contradicts the documented default behaviour
body: The new CAUTION states "While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail." but the same section documents `<not set>` (default) as a supported value that "Mimics Keycloak 26.1 or older behavior", and the operator upgrade test in this PR (UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment) deliberately does NOT enable the feature for the default-strategy case and still expects normal reconciliation. As written, users will believe their existing CRs without `spec.features.enabled: [rolling-updates]` are broken. The text should state precisely when the feature is required (e.g., only when `spec.update.strategy` is set) and what "fail" means (CR rejected, status condition, pod not started).

title: Exit code 4 is documented only for `check` but is also returned by `metadata`, with a misleading description
body: `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` now also exits with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` (4) when the feature is off, but the exit-code table is placed under the "Checking the Metadata" section and describes 4 as "Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled." For the `metadata` command no upgrade decision is made at all, so a script reading that table will interpret a failed metadata generation as a recreate decision. The description should state that the feature is disabled and the command did not run, and the "Generating the Metadata" section should mention its possible exit codes.

title: Shared macro appends the build-time option --features to a runtime command line
body: The `updatecompatibility` macro now emits `bin/kc.[sh|bat] update-compatibility ${parameters} --features=rolling-updates` for every example in the guides. `features` is a build-time option: on an optimized/pre-built distribution (the common container case, and whenever `--optimized` is used, which this command supports via OptimizedMixin) specifying it on the command line fails instead of enabling the feature, and on a non-optimized distribution it forces a re-augmentation on every invocation. The guide should instead tell users to enable the feature at build time (`kc.sh build --features=rolling-updates` / `KC_FEATURES`) and keep the example command free of build-time options.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs, not group IDs
body:
In the V2 implementation the authorization `Resource` created for a group uses the *group id as the resource name* (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`/`getOrCreateResource`), while `Resource#getId()` is the unrelated internal UUID of the authz resource. This method adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set and also passes `groupResource.getId()` into `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)`, which resolves the group via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`.

Consequences:
1. `hasPermission` never finds the per-group resource for the id it is given, so it always falls through to the "all groups" resource-type resource - the per-group evaluation intended here does not happen.
2. The returned set is consumed as a set of *group ids*: `UsersResource.searchForUser` puts it in `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` (restricting the user query to members of those groups) and `UsersResource.getUsersCount` passes it to `session.users().getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)`. Because the ids are authz resource ids, they match no group, so an admin holding an all-groups `view-members`/`manage-members` permission gets zero users and a count of 0 from `/users` and `/users/count`.

The V1 implementation deliberately strips the resource-name prefix (`resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())`) to produce group ids; V2 should use `groupResource.getName()`. Note also that resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never get `setType(...)`, so `findByType(server, "Groups", ...)` only returns the single "Groups" resource-type resource, never the per-group resources - the loop can therefore never enumerate individual groups. No test covers this code path (the existing tests pass via the per-user `canView(user)` filter).

title: canManage() grants manage when only the VIEW scope is permitted
body: `canManage()` evaluates `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` - i.e. it returns `true` when the caller only has the `view` scope on the "all groups" resource (looks like a copy/paste from `canView()` two methods above). `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` calls `auth.groups().requireManage()`, so an administrator who was granted only a read-only all-groups permission can create top-level groups. This is a privilege escalation; the check must only accept `MANAGE`. The new Javadoc added to `GroupPermissionEvaluator#canManage()` documents the same wrong semantics and should be fixed as well.

title: NPE when the "Groups" resource-type resource does not exist
body: When no per-group resource is found, the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and immediately dereferences the result via `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later `resource.getScopes()`, without a null check. `getResourceTypeResource` returns `null` whenever the resource named "Groups" is absent for the admin-permissions client. This is reachable for any realm where admin permissions were enabled before this change: `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` returns early when the admin permissions client already exists, and there is no migration that adds the newly introduced "Groups" resource/scopes to existing resource servers. Any group-related permission check in such a realm will then fail with a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of simply denying access.

title: Group deletion breaks when both FGAP v1 and v2 features are enabled
body: `MgmtPermissionsV2` now overrides `groups()` to return `GroupPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled(...)`/`isPermissionsEnabled(...)` throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. `AdminPermissions.registerListener` (registered whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled) handles `GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent` by calling `management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)`, and `management(...)` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` as soon as `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled. With both features enabled, deleting any group in any realm therefore throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, failing the delete request (500) and aborting the transaction. The same override also makes `GET/PUT /groups/{id}/management/permissions` fail with 500 instead of operating on the v1 permission model. Either the listener/endpoints must be gated to the v1 implementation, or these methods must degrade gracefully (no-op/false) in v2.

title: All-groups permissions are silently ignored for any group that has its own permission
body: `hasPermission` only falls back to the "all groups" resource when no resource exists for the specific group. A per-group resource is created as soon as *any* group-scoped permission references that group (`AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource`). Because per-group resources are created without a resource type, type-based policy evaluation does not apply either. Result: once an admin creates, say, a `manage-membership` permission for group G, all broader all-groups permissions (e.g. `view`, `view-members`) stop applying to G, so an administrator who could previously view G loses that access as a side effect of an unrelated permission being created for G. The scopes granted at the resource-type level should be evaluated in addition to, not instead of, the group-specific resource.

title: getResourceName does not handle the new Groups resource type
body: `getResourceName` only special-cases `USERS` (returning "All users" or the username). For the newly added `Groups` resource type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is `null` for resources created by `getOrCreateResource` (they are created with name = group id and no display name). Admin API/console responses that list the resources of a group scope permission will therefore show `null`/empty instead of the group name or "All groups", unlike the Users resource type. The method needs a `GROUPS` branch resolving the group by id (and a name for the all-groups resource).

title: switch over resourceType throws NPE for a null resource type
body: The previous implementation used `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` chains, which tolerated a `null` `resourceType` and ended up throwing the descriptive `IllegalStateException("Could not map resource object ...")`. `switch (resourceType)` on a `String` throws `NullPointerException` when the argument is null, which surfaces as an opaque HTTP 500 for any caller that reaches `getOrCreateResource` without a resource type. Add an explicit null check that raises `ModelValidationException` (consistent with `throwExceptionIfResourceTypeOrScopesNotProvided`).

title: Incorrect Javadoc on new GroupPermissionEvaluator methods
body: Two of the newly added Javadoc blocks are wrong: `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` is documented as "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns false" (it actually checks `canManageMembers`), and `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` documents "@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission" although the method returns a `Set<String>`. Since these interfaces are the contract used by other modules (admin-ui-ext, services), the wrong text is likely to be copied into new implementations.

title: No negative test that a view-only group permission does not grant manage
body: `testViewGroups` creates an all-groups `VIEW` permission and only asserts that groups become visible. There is no assertion that this read-only permission does not allow write operations (creating a top-level group, updating a group, adding a child). Such an assertion would have caught that `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns `true` for the `view` scope, which currently lets a view-only admin create top-level groups. Similarly, no test exercises `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (all-groups `view-members` permission combined with `GET /users` and `GET /users/count`), which is why the id/name mix-up in that method goes unnoticed.

title: canManage() grants manage rights to admins that only have the 'view' scope on all groups
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` (the no-argument variant) returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it treats the `view` scope on the aggregate "Groups" resource as sufficient for manage. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` calls `auth.groups().requireManage()`, so an admin who was only granted an all-groups *view* permission can create top-level groups. Compare with the group-scoped variant `canManage(GroupModel)` (line 79) which correctly checks only `MANAGE`, and with `UserPermissionsV2`, where manage never falls back to view. The javadoc added in `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` documents the same wrong behaviour. The VIEW scope should be removed from this check.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization Resource IDs, not group IDs, and never finds per-group resources
body:
The V2 implementation collects `groupResource.getId()` (the internal authz `Resource` id) into the returned set, but all callers treat the returned values as group IDs: `UsersResource.searchForUser()`/`BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser()` put them into `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` and `UsersResource.getUsersCount()` passes them to `session.users().getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)`. In FGAP V2 the per-object resource *name* is the group id (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`), so the ids returned here never match any group and the user query is restricted to a non-existent group – an admin that has `view-members`/`manage-members` on all groups gets an empty user list. The same wrong value is also passed back into `hasPermission(groupId, ...)` on line 122, which resolves resources via `resourceStore.findByName()`, so the per-resource lookup always misses and silently falls back to evaluating the aggregate "Groups" resource.
In addition, `resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` can only return the aggregate "Groups" resource, because `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` creates per-object resources without calling `setType()`. Consequently per-group view-members permissions are never reported, which makes `UsersResource.getUsersCount()` return 0 for such admins while the user list endpoint still returns users (count and list disagree). V1 (`GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`) does this correctly by using `resource.getName()`.

title: NPE when the aggregate "Groups" resource cannot be resolved
body: In `hasPermission()`, when no per-group resource is found the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` and immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` without a null check. `getResourceTypeResource()` returns `null` in two reachable situations: (a) the resource server exists but `supportsAuthorizationSchema()` is false, e.g. a realm where the admin-permissions client was created once and `adminPermissionsEnabled` was later turned off, and (b) the "Groups" resource does not exist in the resource server (realms whose admin-permissions client was created before this resource type was added – `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` only runs when the client is first created). In both cases any group/user listing by an admin without `view-users`/`query-groups` roles ends in a NullPointerException and a 500 response instead of a plain "denied".

title: No upgrade path for realms whose admin-permissions client already exists
body: `init()` returns early when `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null`, so the newly added "Groups" aggregate resource and the new scopes (`manage-membership`, `manage-members`, `view-members`) are only created for realms that enable admin permissions after this change. For a realm that already enabled FGAP V2 with an earlier build: creating any Groups scope permission fails because `getOrCreateResource()` (line 125) throws `ModelException("No scopes found.")` when a schema scope is missing from the resource server, and group permission evaluation hits the missing aggregate resource (see `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission`). Either a migration that adds missing scopes/resource-type resources to existing admin-permissions clients or an idempotent re-initialisation is needed.

title: Evaluated permissions are not filtered to the requested resource (inconsistent with UserPermissionsV2)
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission()` iterates all `Permission` objects returned by `root.evaluatePermission(...)` and grants access as soon as any of them carries one of the expected scopes. `UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission()` (line 123 of that file) deliberately guards this with `permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId())`. Without that guard, any permission the policy engine returns for a resource other than the one being evaluated (e.g. scope-only or resource-type expanded permissions) would grant access on the wrong group. The two implementations should use the same rule.

title: Javadoc of requireManageMembers refers to canManageMembership
body: The javadoc added for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` states "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns false" – it is a copy of the javadoc of `requireManageMembership` and documents the wrong predicate; the method actually delegates to `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. Since these two scopes (`manage-membership` vs `manage-members`) grant very different privileges, wrong documentation on this security API is misleading for implementors. Also note that the javadoc of `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` says "@return Stream of IDs" while the method returns a `Set`, and the permission it actually checks is view-members/manage-members, not `view`.

title: No coverage for all-groups view-members, for the users count endpoint, or for the group members endpoint
body: The new test class only exercises per-group `view-members`/`manage-members` through `users().search(...)`, which happens to work even when `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns nothing (the search then runs unrestricted and is filtered per user). Missing cases that would have caught the broken `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`: (1) an *all-groups* `view-members`/`manage-members` permission followed by `users().search(...)` (currently returns nothing because an authz resource id is used as a group id filter), (2) `users().count()` for an admin whose only visibility comes from group member permissions (currently returns 0 while `search` returns users), and (3) `groups().group(id).members()` which is guarded by the new `requireViewMembers` path.

title: Removal of the global view short-circuit makes group listing evaluate policies per group
body: `getGroups()` previously computed `boolean canViewGlobal = groupsEvaluator.canView()` once and only evaluated `canView(group)` per group when the global check failed; the same hoisting was removed in `GroupResource.getSubGroups()`. With FGAP V2, `GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group)` performs a resource lookup by name plus a full policy evaluation for every group in the stream (and in `getSubGroups` the filter is applied over all subgroups before pagination). For a policy-based admin holding an all-groups view permission this turns one evaluation into one per listed group, which is the main use case of the new feature. Consider keeping the single global check as a short-circuit.

title: canManage() grants manage rights to principals that only have the `view` scope
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` (the no-argument variant) evaluates `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it returns `true` when the caller only holds the `view` scope on the all-groups resource. `canManage()` is what backs `GroupPermissionEvaluator.requireManage()`, which guards `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` (POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups). Consequently an admin who was granted only `view` on the `Groups` resource type can create top-level groups. The check should only accept `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (compare `canManage(GroupModel)` on line 79, which correctly uses MANAGE only). The javadoc added in `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` documents this same incorrect behaviour and should be corrected too. There is also no test asserting that an all-groups `view` permission does not allow group creation/modification, which is why the new `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` does not catch this.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authorization resource IDs, not group IDs
body:
In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` the set is populated with `groupResource.getId()` – the UUID of the authorization *resource* – while callers treat the returned values as group IDs: `UsersResource.searchForUser` puts them into `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` to restrict the user search to members of those groups, and `UsersResource.getUsersCount(...)`/`BruteForceUsersResource` pass them to `UserProvider.getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)`. In FGAP v2 the resource *name* is the group id (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`), so `getName()` is what must be collected (the v1 implementation correctly derives the id from the resource name).

The same method is also wrong in what it iterates over: `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups", ...)` only matches resources whose type is set, and `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never calls `setType(...)` for per-group resources, so the only match is the schema-level all-groups resource named `Groups`. Net effect: when an admin is granted `view-members`/`manage-members` on all groups, the method returns a single bogus id, `UserModel.GROUPS` is set to a group that does not exist, and the user search/count returns zero users instead of all users; per-group `view-members` grants never contribute to the set at all. Neither case is covered by the new tests (they only exercise the per-user fallback via `canViewByGroup`).

title: NPE when the schema-level "Groups" resource is absent
body: `hasPermission(...)` falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` without a null check. `getResourceTypeResource` returns `null` in two reachable situations: (a) the realm still has an admin-permissions client but `adminPermissionsEnabled` was turned off (`supportsAuthorizationSchema` returns false), and (b) the admin-permissions client was created by an earlier version whose schema did not yet contain the `Groups` resource type – this PR adds the type but provides no migration for existing admin-permission clients, so no resource named `Groups` exists. In both cases `findByResource(server, null)` dereferences the resource and throws an NPE, turning every group permission check (e.g. GET /admin/realms/{realm}/groups) into a 500. A null guard returning `false` (and/or a migration that creates the missing resource type) is needed.

title: switch on resourceType throws NPE instead of a validation error for null type
body: `getOrCreateResource` now does `switch (resourceType) { case CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE -> ... }`. A `switch` on a `String` throws `NullPointerException` when the selector is null, whereas the previous `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` chain tolerated null and ended in the descriptive `IllegalStateException("Could not map resource object with type [...]")`. Any caller that reaches this method with a null resource type (policy representations without `resourceType`) now produces an unhandled NPE / HTTP 500 instead of a meaningful error. Guard for null explicitly, or keep the default branch reachable for null.

title: getResourceName() has no branch for the new Groups resource type
body: `getResourceName(session, policy, resource)` special-cases only `USERS` (returning "All users" or the username) and otherwise falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Resources created by `getOrCreateResource` are created without a display name, so for permissions scoped to a single group (resource name = group id) this method returns `null`, and the admin REST/UI representation of a group-scoped permission will show no resource name instead of the group name/path. A `GROUPS` branch resolving the group (and "All groups" for the type resource) should be added together with the new resource type.

title: Javadoc of requireManageMembers() refers to the wrong method
body: The javadoc above `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` states "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}" – it is a copy of the javadoc of `requireManageMembership` one method above. The method actually delegates to `canManageMembers(GroupModel)` (see `GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers`). As written the contract documentation is wrong and misleads implementors about which scope (`manage-members` vs `manage-membership`) is enforced.

title: Javadoc of getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() describes a Stream return type
body: The new javadoc for `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` says "@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission", but the method returns `Set<String>`. It also describes the empty-set shortcut in terms of `UserPermissionEvaluator#canView()` only, while implementations additionally return an empty set when the admin is not in the same realm. The documentation should match the actual signature and behaviour so callers do not assume lazy/stream semantics.

title: i18next placeholders replaced with Java MessageFormat syntax breaks the account console message
body: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. This bundle is consumed by the React account console through i18next, whose interpolation syntax is double braces (see every other entry in this file, e.g. `error-invalid-length-too-short='{{0}}' must have minimal length of {{1}}.`). With single braces none of the arguments are substituted and the ICU/MessageFormat choice construct is not supported by i18next either, so the user will literally see `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` instead of the attribute name and the allowed bounds. If pluralization is desired here it has to be done with i18next plural keys (`_one`/`_other`), as already done for `resourceSharedWith_one`/`_other`.

title: i18next placeholders replaced with Java MessageFormat syntax breaks the admin console message
body: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The `maven-resources` admin bundle is loaded by the admin console via i18next, which only interpolates `{{...}}` placeholders and does not understand MessageFormat `choice` constructs. The rendered error will therefore show the raw format string instead of the attribute name and the min/max limits, making the validation error useless for the administrator. Only the server-side bundles (`themes/.../theme/base/*/messages/*`) are formatted with `java.text.MessageFormat` and may use single braces/choice.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: `totpStep1` is now `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` which is Italian, not Lithuanian. The same wrong string was introduced in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` (`loginTotpStep1`, line 71). Lithuanian users will see an Italian sentence in the OTP setup screens. Either translate the new wording or drop the key so the English fallback is used.

title: Traditional Chinese text added to the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) bundle
body: `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese characters/terminology (手機, 應用程式) and appears to be copied from the zh_TW bundle. All other entries in this zh_CN file are Simplified Chinese (手机, 应用). Simplified-Chinese users will see mixed script on the OTP setup page.

title: Missing English counterpart aborts the build with a bare RuntimeException
body: The English reference bundle is derived purely by string surgery on the absolute path (`replaceAll("resources-community", "resources")` plus `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`). If the derived file does not exist – e.g. a community-only theme/message directory that has no counterpart under `resources`, a bundle whose file name does not follow the `_<locale>.properties` convention, or a future directory rename – the code throws an unchecked `RuntimeException("unable to read file ...")` from inside the `forEach`/verify path. That bypasses the `MojoExecutionException` contract of `verify()` and fails the whole build with a raw stack trace instead of a readable validation message. The missing-English case should either be skipped (treat as "no HTML allowed", as `getEnglishValue` already does for missing keys) or reported via `MojoExecutionException` with guidance.

title: Diff trimming can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException while building the error message
body: The two while-loops compute a common prefix length (`start`) and a common suffix length (`end`) independently, so `start + end` can exceed the length of the shorter string. Example: value `abb`, sanitized `ab` gives start=2 and end=2, and `value.substring(2, 3 - 2)` → `substring(2, 1)` throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` (the same happens on the `sanitized.substring(...)` call for value `aa`/sanitized `a`). This happens exactly when a violation has been detected, so instead of reporting the offending key the plugin aborts the build with an unrelated exception and the real problem is hidden. Clamp with e.g. `end = Math.min(end, Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start)`.

title: Anchor-mismatch message omits file and key, and the `key` parameter is unused
body: `messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string")` gives no indication of which properties file or which message key failed, unlike the HTML message a few lines above which includes both. Since the plugin is run over hundreds of bundles, a failure produces an unactionable message. The method already receives `key` but never uses it; include `key` and `file` in the text (and reword "original string" to something like "in the English source value").

title: Byte-exact comparison against the sanitizer output rejects semantically identical HTML
body:
The check is `!Objects.equals(sanitized, value)`, i.e. the translation must match the sanitizer's *serialization* exactly, not just be free of disallowed markup. The OWASP sanitizer always emits void elements as `
`, so a perfectly safe `
` is flagged as "Illegal HTML" – which is why this PR has to rewrite `
` to `
` in ~20 translation files. Every future translation contribution (including machine/Weblate imports) that writes `
`, `
`, extra whitespace inside a tag, etc. will fail the build with a confusing "Illegal HTML" diff even though nothing unsafe is present. Consider comparing a canonicalized form of both sides (e.g. sanitize the value twice and compare the two sanitizer outputs) so only real policy violations are reported.

title: Property bundles are read as ISO-8859-1 while the files are UTF-8
body: `new PropertyResourceBundle(FileInputStream)` loads the file with `Properties.load(InputStream)`, which decodes ISO-8859-1, whereas `verifyNoDuplicateKeys` reads the same file with `Files.readString` (UTF-8). Keycloak theme message bundles are UTF-8, so every non-ASCII value is mojibake inside the sanitizer check and, more importantly, in the reported "Illegal HTML in key ..." messages, which makes failures for Arabic/Chinese/Cyrillic bundles very hard to read. Use `new PropertyResourceBundle(new InputStreamReader(fis, StandardCharsets.UTF_8))`.

title: No negative test and weakened assertions hide false positives
body:
The assertions were relaxed from `Matchers.contains` to `Matchers.hasItem`, so a test now passes even if the verifier emits additional, unexpected messages. Combined with the fact that there is no test asserting an *empty* result for a legitimate file (e.g. a `_de` bundle whose English source contains ``/`

`/`
` and whose translation uses the same allowed tags, or a bundle containing `{{0}}` placeholders and `{N,choice,...}` constructs), the suite cannot detect the false positives this checker is most likely to produce – which is exactly the risk that forced the large number of cosmetic edits in this PR. Add a test asserting `verify()` returns an empty list for a valid translation.

title: Java MessageFormat/choice syntax put into an i18next message bundle
body: This bundle is served to the Account Console SPA and resolved with i18next, which interpolates `{{0}}`-style placeholders only (see line 27 `error-invalid-length-too-short='{{0}}' must have minimal length of {{1}}.` and line 3 `backTo=Back to {{app}}`), and has no support for Java MessageFormat `choice` sub-formats. After this change the value is `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`, so nothing will be substituted and the user will literally see `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and the whole `{2,choice,...}` expression in the error message. The previous `{{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}}` form worked. If pluralization is wanted here, it must be expressed with i18next's `_one`/`_other` key suffixes while keeping `{{n}}` placeholders.

title: Admin console message switched from i18next `{{n}}` to Java MessageFormat choice syntax
body: The removed line in this same file used `{{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}}`, i.e. this bundle is interpolated by i18next in the Admin Console SPA. The new value `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` uses Java MessageFormat argument syntax plus a `choice` sub-format, neither of which i18next understands, so the administrator will see the raw placeholders and the raw choice expression instead of the min/max values. Keep `{{0}}`-style placeholders here (and use i18next plural key suffixes if plural forms are required).

title: Diff trimming can produce substring(begin > end) and crash the verifier
body:
The common-prefix (`start`) and common-suffix (`end`) counters are computed independently, so `start + end` can exceed `sanitized.length()`. Example: a translation with a stray closing tag, `value = "

text

"` sanitizes to `"

text

"`; then `start = 11` and `end = 4`, and `sanitized.substring(11, 11 - 4)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. Instead of reporting the illegal HTML, the plugin aborts with an opaque exception — and mismatched/duplicated closing tags are exactly the kind of defect this check is meant to find (several such files are fixed in this PR). Clamp `end` to `Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`.

title: English counterpart path is guessed by regex and a miss aborts the build with a raw RuntimeException
body: The English bundle is located by `replaceAll("resources-community", "resources")` plus `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` on the absolute path. Any properties file without a locale suffix (e.g. `messages.properties`) does not match the second regex, so the lookup resolves to a path that need not exist, and any theme whose base directory has no `messages_en.properties` behaves the same. In that case `verifySafeHtml` throws an unchecked `RuntimeException("unable to read file ...")` (lines 70 and 79) which escapes `verify()`, failing the whole build with a stack trace instead of the `MojoExecutionException`/validation message the rest of the class produces. Handle a missing English bundle explicitly (skip the HTML check or add a readable message) and throw `MojoExecutionException` for genuine I/O errors.

title: Anchor mismatch message does not say which key or file is wrong
body: `messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string")` omits both the message key and the file name, while the sibling message on line 111 includes them. With hundreds of locale files, a build failure containing only the anchor tag gives no way to locate the offending entry. The `key` parameter of `santizeAnchors` is already passed in but unused — include it and `file` in the message (the method name is also misspelled, `santizeAnchors`).

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: `loginTotpStep1` was replaced with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, in the Lithuanian bundle; Lithuanian users will see Italian text on the OTP setup page. The same Italian string was also inserted into `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties` (`totpStep1`, line 101). When dropping the HTML from these strings, the replacement should be Lithuanian (or the key should be removed so the English fallback is used).

title: Traditional Chinese text inserted into the zh_CN (Simplified) bundle
body: `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese characters/wording (手機, 應用程式), apparently copied from the zh_TW bundle, while the rest of this file is Simplified Chinese (e.g. 手机, 应用). Use the Simplified form, e.g. `在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：`.

title: No test asserting a valid bundle produces no findings
body: All four tests assert that a message *is* reported; none asserts that `verify()` returns an empty list for a legitimate file (e.g. a translation that keeps the same allowed tags/anchors as its English source, or `noHtml_en.properties`). Given that the check unescapes HTML entities, strips `<!-- -->`, and special-cases keys such as `templateHelp` and `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`, false positives are the most likely regression and are currently untested. A test for the missing-English-bundle path (which today throws an unchecked RuntimeException) is also missing.

title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax put into an i18next bundle breaks the message
body: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. Every other parameterised key in this bundle (e.g. `error-invalid-length-too-short='{{0}}' must have minimal length of {{1}}.`) uses i18next double-brace interpolation, because the account console resolves these messages with i18next, not with java.text.MessageFormat. With single braces the placeholders are no longer interpolated and the `{2,choice,...}` block is not understood at all, so the end user will see the literal string `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The change is also not needed for the sanitizer, since the old text contained no `<` character.

title: Choice format in admin console i18next bundle will be rendered literally
body: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was switched from the i18next form `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to the Java MessageFormat form `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. This bundle is consumed by the admin console through i18next, which only interpolates `{{n}}` and has no support for `choice` patterns, so the admin will see the raw pattern text including `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` instead of a formatted message. Note the equivalent server-side bundle (themes/base/admin) is formatted with MessageFormat and may keep the choice form, but the keycloak.v2 bundle must not.

title: Diff-trimming can compute an invalid substring range and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body: The common-prefix (`start`) and common-suffix (`end`) counters are computed independently, so for values where the removed fragment shares a prefix with the following text (or a suffix with the preceding text) `start + end` can exceed the length of `sanitized`, and `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` is called with begin > end. Concrete example: English contains `<b>`, translation value is `x<div><b>y`; the sanitizer returns `x<b>y`, giving start=2 and end=4 while `sanitized.length()` is 5, so `sanitized.substring(2, 1)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. Instead of reporting the offending key, the build then aborts with an unrelated stack trace. The indices need to be clamped (e.g. `end = Math.min(end, Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start)`).

title: Missing English source bundle aborts the build with a raw RuntimeException
body: The English counterpart path is derived purely by string replacement (`resources-community` -> `resources`, locale suffix -> `_en`). If no such file exists (a theme that only lives in the community resources, a message directory without an English bundle, or a bundle name without a locale suffix) `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` fails and the IOException is rethrown as a plain `RuntimeException`, killing the whole build with a stack trace instead of producing a verification message. The same applies to reading the file under verification a few lines above. Both should either be reported through the `messages` list or be wrapped in `MojoExecutionException` like the rest of `verify()`, and a missing English bundle should be handled gracefully (e.g. treat all English values as empty).

title: Anchor mismatch message does not say which file or key failed
body: `messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string")` omits both the file name and the message key, unlike the HTML message produced a few lines above which includes `key` and `file`. With hundreds of bundles a maintainer cannot locate the offending translation from this output. The `key` parameter of `santizeAnchors` is accepted but never used, so the information is already available. Additionally, after reporting the mismatch the method `break`s and leaves the remaining `<a>` tags in the value, so the subsequent policy check emits a second, redundant "Illegal HTML" message for the same key.

title: HTML detection in the English source only recognises lower-case tags
body:
`HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` is case sensitive, so an English source value written with an upper-case tag (e.g. `` or `
`) is classified as containing no HTML. The translation is then verified with `POLICY_NO_HTML` and every markup element it legitimately mirrors from the source is reported as "Illegal HTML", producing a false build failure that a translator cannot fix without changing the English source. Use `Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE` (or normalise before matching).

title: Unescaping the raw value turns escaped entities into markup and can cause false positives
