The commit thread runs independently every second and commits whatever contiguous prefix is complete at that moment, so a tick that happens after only some offsets have been processed sets `commit_event` with a lower offset (e.g. 100 or 102); the subsequent `commit_event.wait()` returns immediately because the event is never cleared again and the equality assertion fails. The tests should poll until the expected offset is observed (or clear/re-wait) instead of asserting on the first commit.

title: FilteredPayload messages are handled through the exception path, producing an error log per message
body: `decode_payload` in the result consumer starts with `assert not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload)`, which is outside its own try/except, so for every filtered message the `AssertionError` propagates into `submit()`'s broad `except Exception` and is reported via `logger.exception("Error submitting message to queue")`. Filtered payloads are a normal part of arroyo pipelines (e.g. when the stale-message DLQ wrapper is enabled), so this turns routine filtering into a flood of error-level exceptions with stack traces and relies on exceptions for ordinary control flow. `submit()` should check for `FilteredPayload` explicitly and complete the offset without logging.

title: A gauge is emitted for every processed item on the hot path
body: `OrderedQueueWorker.run` calls `metrics.gauge("remote_subscriptions.queue_worker.queue_depth", ...)` in the `finally` block of every single work item, with only an `identifier` tag so all 20 workers overwrite the same series. This adds per-message statsd overhead for a value that is already exported once per `poll()` by `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.poll` (`total_queued`), and the per-worker value is meaningless after aggregation. Emit it periodically rather than per item.

title: Queue pool is permanently shut down on the first rebalance, then reused
body: `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` hands the single, factory-owned `self.queue_pool` to every `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` it creates. Arroyo closes the strategy on every partition revocation/rebalance, and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()`/`terminate()` call `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, which stops all worker threads and calls `queue.shutdown()` on every queue. The factory still holds a non-None reference, so the next `create_with_partitions()` after the rebalance returns a strategy backed by a dead pool: `work_queue.put()` raises `queue.ShutDown`, which is swallowed by the `except Exception` in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()`, where the offset is immediately marked added+complete and therefore committed. The result is that after the first rebalance the consumer silently drops every message while advancing offsets, i.e. permanent data loss. The pool needs to be created per strategy (or recreated on assignment) rather than shared across the factory lifetime.

title: Arroyo commit callback invoked from a background thread
body: `_commit_loop` runs in its own thread and calls `self.commit_function(committable)`, which is arroyo's `Commit` callback (`StreamProcessor.__commit` -> `consumer.stage_offsets`/`commit_offsets`). That callback and the underlying consumer state are only safe to touch from the thread running the processor loop; calling it concurrently with `poll()`/`submit()`/rebalance handling can corrupt the staged-offset bookkeeping or raise (e.g. staging an offset for a partition that was just revoked). Because the exception is caught and only logged in the loop, such failures would be invisible and offsets would silently stop advancing. Offsets should be handed back to the main thread (e.g. collected in `poll()`) instead of committed from the commit thread.

title: Shutdown drops all queued work instead of draining it; join() ignores timeout
body: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` sets `worker.shutdown = True` *before* calling `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`. Each worker checks `self.shutdown` at the top of its loop, so after finishing its current item it exits immediately and never drains the remaining queued items, defeating the point of `immediate=False`. Combined with `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join(timeout)` which just delegates to `close()` and ignores the timeout entirely, a normal shutdown or rebalance discards everything still queued. Those offsets stay uncommitted so the messages are re-delivered, but arroyo's `join(timeout)` contract (flush outstanding work within the timeout) is broken and every restart/rebalance causes a burst of duplicate processing proportional to the queue depth.

title: Queues are unbounded, so there is no backpressure despite the docstring claim
body: Each queue is created as `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize`, and `submit()` never raises `MessageRejected`. The class docstring of `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` claims "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", but nothing ever fills up: if a result processor is slower than the Kafka consumption rate, the strategy will keep accepting messages and grow memory without bound. Each `WorkItem` also retains the full `Message[KafkaPayload]` (field `message`, which is never read anywhere), so the retained payload bytes are kept alive as well, plus one entry per offset in `OffsetTracker.all_offsets`. A bounded queue plus `MessageRejected` (or an explicit limit) is needed to get real backpressure.

title: OffsetTracker state is never reset across partition assignments
body: `OffsetTracker` lives on the long-lived `FixedQueuePool` and keeps `last_committed`/`all_offsets` forever; `create_with_partitions()` never resets it for the newly assigned partition set. If a partition is revoked and later re-assigned to this consumer at a lower offset (rewind, other consumer committed less far, offset reset), `get_committable_offsets()` computes `start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)` from the stale `last_committed`, finds no offsets at or above it, and therefore never produces a committable offset for that partition again - the consumer processes messages but silently stops committing, so the lag grows without bound and everything is reprocessed on restart. The tracker should be reset (or scoped per assignment) when partitions are assigned/revoked.

title: Error-handling test asserts the opposite of the implemented behaviour and passes only by timing
body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` is documented as "errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages" but then asserts `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`, i.e. that nothing is committed. In the implementation the worker catches the exception and still calls `complete_offset()` in its `finally` block, so offsets 100 and 101 become committable and the 1-second commit loop will commit them. The test only passes because its wait loop exits after ~0.3s, before the first commit tick. So it asserts behaviour the code does not have, is timing-dependent (will fail whenever the commit thread ticks early / CI is slow), and provides no real coverage of failure handling.

title: Offset-gap test does not actually verify gap blocking and is timing-dependent
body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_gaps` submits offsets 100, 102, 103 and asserts that no commit ever exceeds 101. The tracker blocks at the gap only for the first commit tick: after `mark_committed(100)` removes offsets <= 100, the next call to `get_committable_offsets()` uses `start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset) = 102` and will therefore commit 103 (reported as 104). The test passes only because the wait loop breaks ~0.2s after the first commit, before the next 1-second tick, making it flaky; and the `for commit in all_commits: assert <= 101` loop gives a false sense that committing past gaps is prevented. Either the skip-the-gap behaviour should be asserted explicitly, or the loop should keep observing commits for more than one tick.

title: Strategy docstring guarantees do not match behaviour
body: The `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` docstring claims "No item is lost or processed out of order", "Natural backpressure when queues fill up" and "Only commits offsets after successful processing". None of those hold: queues are unbounded (no backpressure), items still queued at close are discarded, and the worker marks an offset complete in its `finally` block even when `result_processor` raised, so failed items are committed and never retried. Leaving these claims in place will mislead operators about the delivery semantics of the new mode.

title: FilteredPayload messages are funneled through the generic exception handler
body: `ResultsStrategyFactory.decode_payload` starts with `assert not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload)`, and that assert is outside its try/except. When this strategy is wrapped by something that emits `FilteredPayload` (e.g. the stale-message DLQ wrapper used via `--stale-threshold-sec`), every filtered message raises an AssertionError that lands in `submit()`'s `except Exception`, logging "Error submitting message to queue" at exception level for each one. Offsets are still advanced, so this is noise rather than data loss, but it will flood error logs/Sentry. `submit()` should handle `FilteredPayload` explicitly (track and complete the offset) instead of relying on the catch-all.

title: Shared FixedQueuePool is permanently shut down on the first rebalance, then silently drops all messages
body: `self.queue_pool` is created once in `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__` (line 133) and handed to every `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` created by `create_with_partitions`. Arroyo destroys and recreates the processing strategy on every partition revocation/assignment, and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()`/`join()` calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, which sets `worker.shutdown = True` on all workers and calls `queue.shutdown()` on every work queue. After the first rebalance a new strategy is created around the now-dead pool: every `work_queue.put()` raises `queue.ShutDown` and every worker thread has exited. Because `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()` wraps everything in `except Exception` and then marks the offset as added+completed, those messages are never processed but their offsets are committed — i.e. total, silent data loss for the rest of the process lifetime. The pool must be owned by the strategy (recreated per assignment) or `shutdown()` must not be called from the strategy's close path.

title: submit() swallows every exception and marks the offset as completed, committing unprocessed messages
body: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`, any exception raised by the decoder, the grouping function, or `queue.put()` is caught by the blanket `except Exception`, logged, and then the offset is added and immediately completed so the commit loop will commit it. That means transient or structural failures (closed queue, grouping bug, OOM-adjacent errors, a `FilteredPayload` hitting the `assert not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload)` in `decode_payload`) result in the message being permanently skipped and its offset committed, with no DLQ and no retry. Only genuinely undecodable payloads should be fast-forwarded; everything else should propagate so arroyo can DLQ or crash the consumer.

title: Work queues are unbounded, so there is no backpressure and unbounded memory growth
body: `FixedQueuePool.__init__` creates `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize`, and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()` never raises `MessageRejected`. The class docstring claims "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", but nothing ever fills up: if one group's processing is slow (the exact scenario this PR targets), arroyo will keep polling Kafka and the corresponding queue will grow without limit until the process OOMs. The problem is amplified because `WorkItem` also retains the whole `Message[KafkaPayload]` (line 31) even though only `partition`/`offset` are used, so each queued item holds the full Kafka payload alive. Give the queues a bounded size and raise `MessageRejected` (or otherwise block) when full.

title: Offsets are committed from a background thread, outside arroyo's single-threaded contract
body: `_commit_loop` runs in its own thread and calls `self.commit_function(...)`, which is arroyo's `StreamProcessor` commit callback. That callback mutates the `KafkaConsumer`'s staged-offset state and may call `commit_offsets()` while the main processor thread is concurrently polling and running rebalance callbacks (which also stage/commit offsets). This state is not lock-protected, and staging offsets for a partition that was just revoked raises `ConsumerError("cannot stage offsets for unassigned partitions")`. That error is swallowed by the loop's broad `except Exception`, so commits can silently stop working after a rebalance while processing continues. Commits should be driven from `poll()`/the main thread instead of a separate thread.

title: close()/join() stop the commit thread before draining work, so completed work is never committed
body: `close()` sets `shutdown_event`, joins the commit thread, and only then calls `queue_pool.shutdown()` (which drains/stops workers). Any item processed after the last 1-second commit tick therefore has its offset marked complete but never committed, so it is reprocessed after restart. For uptime results this means duplicate processing of check results (duplicate status transitions/incidents) on every deploy. `join(timeout)` (line 344) also ignores its `timeout` argument and delegates to `close()`, which can block for up to ~5s per worker plus 5s for the commit thread, violating arroyo's shutdown deadline. A final `get_committable_offsets()` + `commit_function(..., force=True)` should run after the queues are drained.

title: FixedQueuePool.shutdown() sets worker.shutdown before draining, so queued items are discarded despite immediate=False
body: `shutdown()` first sets `worker.shutdown = True` for every worker and then calls `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` with the intent of letting workers drain remaining items. But `OrderedQueueWorker.run` re-checks `while not self.shutdown` at the top of each iteration, so each worker processes at most one more item and exits; everything still queued is dropped. This makes the "gracefully shutdown" docstring wrong and means a shutdown under load discards all buffered work (it will be reprocessed, since those offsets stay outstanding, but the drain the code appears to implement never happens). Either drain first and set the flag afterwards, or use `shutdown(immediate=True)` and don't pretend to drain.

title: Worker marks offsets complete even when result processing raised, so failed messages are committed
body: `OrderedQueueWorker.run` calls `self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)` in a `finally` block, so a message whose `result_processor` raised an unexpected exception is logged and then its offset is committed. This silently converts processing failures into permanent message loss and diverges from the serial/batched modes, where an unhandled exception propagates to arroyo and can be DLQ'd or crash the consumer rather than being committed away. If skip-on-error is intended it should be explicit (and metered), not a side effect of `finally`.

title: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling asserts the opposite of its docstring and only passes because of commit timing
body: The test is documented as "errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages" but asserts `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`, i.e. that nothing was committed. It passes only because the test breaks out of its wait loop after ~0.3s while the commit thread's first tick is at 1.0s; the implementation marks offsets complete in the worker's `finally` even on failure, so offset 102 *would* be committed a moment later. The test therefore verifies nothing about error handling and will flip to failing on any timing change. It should wait for the commit tick and assert the intended behaviour explicitly.

title: OffsetTracker never cleans up revoked partitions and keeps stale last_committed values
body: `all_offsets`, `outstanding`, `last_committed` and `partition_locks` grow per partition and are never pruned when partitions are revoked. Because the tracker lives on the long-lived `FixedQueuePool`, a partition that is revoked and later reassigned keeps its old `last_committed` value; if the consumer re-reads from a lower offset (normal after a rebalance), `get_committable_offsets` will refuse to commit anything for that partition until the stream passes the stale high-water mark, and the offsets below it are reprocessed without ever being committed. Add a way to drop per-partition state on revocation.

title: Per-item queue_depth gauge is emitted by all workers with identical tags, making the metric meaningless
body: Every worker emits `remote_subscriptions.queue_worker.queue_depth` with only `{"identifier": ...}` as tags, once per processed item. With N workers the samples overwrite each other (last writer wins) so the gauge reflects a random worker's queue rather than anything interpretable, while paying statsd overhead on every message. Either tag by `worker_id`/queue index or emit aggregate depth from `poll()` only (which already publishes `queue_pool.total_queued`).

title: Kafka integration test relies on private arroyo APIs and a fixed 5-second wall-clock loop
body: `ProcessResultThreadQueueParallelKafkaTest.test_thread_queue_parallel_kafka_offset_commit` drives the consumer by calling `processor._run_once()` and `processor._shutdown()` (private arroyo internals that can change without notice), busy-loops for a hard-coded 5 seconds, and then asserts exact committed offsets. This makes the test slow and timing-dependent (a slow CI run that produces/consumes late will fail), and the `verify_consumer` is left unclosed if any assertion fails. Prefer the public `StreamProcessor.run()`/shutdown path or a condition-based wait with a generous timeout.

title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so one code can be used twice
body:
`authorize` reads `user.backupCodes` at the start of the request, decrypts it, nulls the matched entry and writes the whole blob back. There is no transaction, no optimistic check that the stored ciphertext is unchanged, and no row lock.

Two concurrent sign-ins with the same backup code both see it as valid and both succeed, which breaks the 'usable exactly once' guarantee. Two concurrent sign-ins with different codes can also overwrite each other's update, so one consumed code comes back to life.

Fix: wrap the read and write in a transaction with a conditional update, e.g. `updateMany where { id, backupCodes: <old ciphertext> }` and fail the login if 0 rows are affected.

title: Backup code match is case- and whitespace-sensitive while the UI hints uppercase
body:
Codes are generated as lowercase hex (`randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`). The input only has dashes stripped before an exact `indexOf` match.

The BackupCode input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`, which invites uppercase entry. Uppercase input, or a pasted code with surrounding whitespace or a newline, is rejected as `IncorrectBackupCode`.

The same exact-match logic is in `disable.ts` (line 61). Normalize with `.trim().toLowerCase()` in both places.

title: 2FA is already enabled when the backup-codes step shows, but `onEnable` only runs from the Close button
body:
After a successful `/totp/enable`, the modal now moves to `DisplayBackupCodes` instead of calling `onEnable()`. `onEnable()` and `resetState()` are only invoked by the 'Close' button.

If the user dismisses the dialog any other way (Escape, overlay click, i.e. through `onOpenChange`), the parent never learns that 2FA was enabled. The settings switch keeps showing 2FA as disabled even though it is active server-side. The modal also stays stuck on the backup-codes step for the next open.

Fix: call `onEnable` as soon as the enable succeeds (and only defer closing), or handle dismissal in `onOpenChange` while on that step.

title: `missing_backup_codes` message points to a regeneration feature that does not exist
body:
Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have `backupCodes = null` and get "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings."

There is no UI to generate or regenerate backup codes. The only path is to disable 2FA (which needs a working TOTP code) and enable it again. The message should describe that path, or a regeneration feature should be added.

title: Non-string `backupCode` in the request body causes an unhandled 500
body:
`req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` is called on any truthy value. A JSON body with a numeric or object `backupCode` throws a TypeError and produces a 500 instead of a 400.

The endpoint also throws raw `Error`s instead of returning JSON for the missing-key case, which the client maps to a generic error. Validate the body type before use.

title: No tests cover logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
Backup code plus any non-empty totpCode bypasses the password check
body: `authorize` only verifies the password when `credentials.totpCode` is empty (line 121). The new branch at line 131 runs whenever `backupCode` is present and never looks at `totpCode`. So an attacker can POST `email`, a valid `backupCode` and an arbitrary non-empty `totpCode` such as "x": the password check is skipped and the bogus TOTP is never validated. The result is a login with only the email address and one backup code. Fix this by always requiring a valid password for CAL-identity users when a backup code is used (or by rejecting requests that send both fields), instead of tying the password check to the absence of `totpCode`.

title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: The encrypted code list is read with the user (line 73), checked in memory, then written back with the used entry set to null. Nothing guards against concurrent requests. Two simultaneous logins with the same code both read the old list, both pass, and both write. A single-use backup code can therefore be redeemed more than once. One request can also overwrite another's consumption of a different code, resurrecting it. Use a transaction or an optimistic check, e.g. `updateMany` with `where: { id, backupCodes: <old ciphertext> }` and treat a zero row count as failure.

title: MissingBackupCodes is not reported once codes run out, and the message points to a feature that doesn't exist
body: Used codes are replaced with `null`, so after all ten are consumed `user.backupCodes` is still a non-empty ciphertext. The user then gets `IncorrectBackupCode` rather than `MissingBackupCodes`. Separately, the `missing_backup_codes` text says "Please generate them in your settings", but there is no regeneration UI. Users who enabled 2FA before this feature, or who used every code, can only get new codes by disabling and re-enabling 2FA.

title: Closing the dialog on the backup-codes step skips onEnable and resetState
body: Once `/totp/enable` succeeds, 2FA is active on the server and the modal switches to `DisplayBackupCodes`. Only the explicit Close button calls `onEnable()` and `resetState()`. Dismissing the dialog with Escape or a click outside goes through `onOpenChange` and calls neither. The parent then still shows 2FA as disabled. Reopening the modal lands back on the backup-codes step with stale codes. The blob URL is also never revoked.

title: Backup code matching is case- and whitespace-sensitive
body: Codes are lowercase hex, and the input is compared after stripping only dashes. A user who types the code in uppercase, or pastes it with surrounding whitespace or a trailing newline from the downloaded file, gets `IncorrectBackupCode`. Normalize the input with `trim()` and `toLowerCase()` here and in `disable.ts`.

title: Non-string backupCode in the body causes an unhandled 500
body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` is called on unvalidated JSON input. A truthy non-string value such as a number or an object throws a TypeError and returns a 500 instead of a 400. Validate the body, for example with zod, before using it.

title: No tests exercise backup-code login or disabling 2FA with a backup code
body: None of the new authentication paths are tested: login with a backup code, single-use enforcement, and disabling 2FA with a backup code. The first test also no longer closes the new backup-codes screen, and its switch assertion is acknowledged (FIXME) to pass even when the switch is not checked. These gaps let security regressions in the new code go undetected.

title: Backup code consumption is not atomic, so one code can be used more than once
body: Login decrypts `user.backupCodes`, finds the matching index, nulls it, and writes the re-encrypted blob back. Nothing guards this read-modify-write: there is no transaction and no optimistic check against the previously read value. Two concurrent sign-in requests with the same backup code (or two different codes) can both pass the `indexOf` check. As a result a supposedly single-use code can grant multiple sessions, and one request's update can overwrite the other's, un-consuming a code that was already used. Make the consumption conditional, e.g. `updateMany` with `where: { id, backupCodes: <old ciphertext> }` and fail if the count is 0, or run it in a serializable transaction.

title: Backup code comparison is case-sensitive although the UI suggests uppercase
body: Codes are generated as lowercase hex (`randomBytes(5).toString('hex')`) and compared with an exact `indexOf`. The input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`, which invites uppercase entry, and mobile keyboards often auto-capitalize. A valid code typed in uppercase is rejected as `IncorrectBackupCode`. The input is also not trimmed, so surrounding whitespace causes the same rejection. Normalize with `.trim().toLowerCase()` before comparing, both here and in `totp/disable.ts`.

title: Non-string backupCode in request body causes an unhandled 500
body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes a string. A JSON body with a numeric or object `backupCode` throws a TypeError, which surfaces as an internal server error instead of a 400. Validate the type, e.g. with zod or a `typeof` check, before use.

title: Dismissing the dialog on the backup-codes step skips onEnable and leaves stale state
body: After a successful enable, `onEnable()` is no longer called immediately. It now runs only when the user clicks the new Close button. If the user dismisses the dialog any other way (Escape, overlay click, via `onOpenChange`), 2FA is already enabled server-side but the parent never learns about it, so the settings switch keeps showing 2FA as disabled. `resetState()` also never runs, so the modal reopens on the DisplayBackupCodes step with stale codes. Handle dismissal on this step the same way as Close, or call `onEnable` when entering the step.

title: Error message tells users to generate backup codes in settings, but no such feature exists
body: `missing_backup_codes` reads "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." Codes are only created during initial 2FA setup, and this PR adds no regenerate option. Every user who enabled 2FA before this change has no codes and cannot follow the instruction except by disabling and re-enabling 2FA. Either add a regeneration flow or reword the message.

title: Backup codes stored with reversible encryption instead of hashes
body: Backup codes are single-use bearer credentials that only ever need to be verified. They are stored via `symmetricEncrypt` with the global `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, so anyone with database and key access can recover every user's valid codes. Storing per-code hashes (e.g. SHA-256 of the high-entropy code, or bcrypt) and comparing against those would limit the impact of a compromise.

title: No test covers logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
body: The e2e changes only click the download, copy and close buttons. There is no test that a backup code authenticates, that a used code is rejected on reuse, or that disable works with a backup code; the TODO acknowledges this. Separately, the first test now leaves the backup-codes dialog open and relies on an `isChecked()` assertion that is admitted (FIXME) to always pass, so it no longer verifies that enabling succeeded.

title: Google Meet fallback crashes when there is no destination calendar
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined` when the event has no destination calendar, which is common. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining. Whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType`, this throws a TypeError and the booking creation path fails. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`; use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` here.

title: Video references no longer store credentialId
body: This line was changed from `isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId` to `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Video results now get `credentialId: undefined` in the booking references they create. `handleCancelBooking` only deletes the video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so newly created video meetings (Zoom, Daily, etc.) will never be deleted on cancel. Updates that look up video credentials by reference will break too.

title: Org slug assignment logic inverted (unrelated change)
body: The original code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, which sets the slug immediately only when billing is disabled. The new code `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` does the reverse. With billing enabled, the slug is now reserved before payment. Without billing, organizations are created with no slug at all. This change has nothing to do with the PR's purpose and silently breaks organization creation.

title: Collective hosts' calendars dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
body: When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null`. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then does nothing. In that case the other collective hosts' destination calendars are silently discarded, which is exactly the multi-host scenario this PR is meant to fix. Initialize the array (e.g. to `[]`) before pushing.

title: Hangout-link patch uses an undefined calendarId
body: `selectedCalendar` is now `undefined` whenever no destination calendar matches the credential, and the insert falls back to `"primary"`. The follow-up `calendar.events.patch` still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which is `undefined` in that case. The patch request fails, so the Meet link is never added to the event description. Use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` value in both calls.

title: Non-Google calendars always target the main host's calendar id for every host
body: `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now calls `createEvent` once per destination, each time with a different host's credential. Office365 (and Lark and CalDAV) still pick `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, which is the main host's calendar. For other hosts this either posts to a calendar id that does not exist in their account and fails, or ignores the host's chosen calendar. Only Google uses the `credentialId` to choose the right destination.

title: Fallback lookup for the calendar id can never match
body: In both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`, the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. A real `externalId` will never equal a falsy value, so the lookup always returns `undefined`. In `updateEvent`, `calendarId` is then undefined and the update fails. The old behavior of falling back to the destination calendar's externalId (or `"primary"`) is lost.

title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar event
body: `updateAllCalendarEvents` now handles multiple calendar references, one per host. However, when merging into `newBookingId`, it still uses `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes only the first old calendar event. The other hosts' old calendar events remain on their calendars after a reschedule.

title: Recurring cancellation repeats deletes per reference and misses other hosts
body: The recurring branch now runs inside the per-reference loop, but its body does not depend on the reference. It iterates all of the organizer's credentials and deletes the first calendar reference of every updated booking. With N references, the same deletes run N times. Because it only uses `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and `.find` (one reference per booking), the other collective hosts' recurring events are never deleted.

title: loadUsers dropped the organization select and changed error semantics
body: The rewritten `loadUsers` no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` for dynamic users. Code that relies on the user's organization slug, such as building org booker URLs, will get undefined for dynamic group bookings. The new try/catch also converts every error, including the intentional `dynamicUserList` validation error, into a generic 500 "Unable to load users" response. This refactor is unrelated to the destination-calendar fix.

title: Null dereference on empty destinationCalendar when location is Google Meet
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` is `undefined` when the event has no destination calendar. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. Any booking with location Google Meet whose organizer and event type have no destination calendar now throws a TypeError in `EventManager.create`, so the booking fails instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

title: Video references no longer store credentialId
body: `credentialId` is now `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so references created for video results are saved without a credentialId. `handleCancelBooking` only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set. Video meetings (Zoom, Daily, etc.) for new bookings will therefore not be deleted on cancellation. Keep `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results.

title: Fallback calendar lookup is dead code; update falls back to undefined calendarId
body: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only evaluates the `find` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then compares against that falsy value, so it never matches. Previously the code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. For references without `externalCalendarId` (older bookings or the non-credential path), `calendars.events.update` is now called with `calendarId: undefined` and fails. The same dead lookup exists in `deleteEvent` (line ~317); that path still defaults to "primary", but the destination calendar is lost.

title: Hangout-link patch uses possibly undefined calendarId
body: `selectedCalendar` can now be `undefined`. Insert uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly. When no destination calendar matches the credential, the patch that adds the Meet link to the description fails silently.

title: Non-Google calendars always use the main host's calendar id for every host
body: `createEvent` now runs once per host's destination calendar, but Office365 (and similarly Lark and CalDAV) always reads `destinationCalendar[0]`, which is the main host's calendar. For a second host it posts to `/me/calendars/<main host calendar id>/events` using the second host's token, and that request fails. The credentialId passed to `createEvent` is ignored. The multi-host fix therefore only works for Google Calendar.

title: CalDAV createEvent silently creates nothing for non-main hosts
body: For a collective host whose CalDAV credential is not the main host's, the filter `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` matches none of that host's calendars. `Promise.all([])` resolves, so the method returns success while no event is created in the host's calendar.

title: Lark createEvent ignores the target credential's destination calendar
body: `createEvent` always uses `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, which is the main host's calendar. When a collective host with Lark is not the main host, the event and its attendees are created against another user's calendar id and the request fails.

title: Team host calendars dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing, so the collective hosts' calendars are discarded. This is the exact multi-host scenario the PR is meant to fix. Initialize to `[]` or assign the team calendars when the base is null.

title: loadUsers refactor drops organization select and changes error behavior
body: The dynamic-user query no longer selects `organization: { slug }`, so downstream code that reads the organizer's organization slug (e.g. building the org booker URL) gets undefined for dynamic group bookings. The refactor also throws on an empty `dynamicUserList`. Every non-HttpError/Prisma error is converted into a generic 500 "Unable to load users", which replaces the previous behavior. These changes are unrelated to the PR's purpose.

title: Inverted slug condition for org creation
body: The original code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, which sets the slug immediately only when billing is disabled. The new code sets it only when billing IS enabled. With billing enabled the org gets its slug before payment, bypassing the requestedSlug flow. With billing disabled (self-hosted) the org is created without a slug. This unrelated change inverts behavior.

title: Only the first old calendar event is deleted when merging on reschedule
body: With multiple calendar references per booking (one per collective host), the `newBookingId` path still uses `booking.references.find(...)`, so only the first host's old calendar event is deleted. The other hosts keep stale events in their calendars.

title: Recurring cancellation repeated per reference and ignores other hosts
body: The recurring branch now runs inside the per-reference loop, so the full deletion pass over all of the organizer's calendar credentials repeats once per calendar reference. Each pass uses only the organizer's credentials and only the first `_calendar` reference of each booking. Other collective hosts' recurring events are never deleted, while the organizer's events receive redundant delete calls.

title: Webhook payload shape of destinationCalendar changed to array
body: `CalendarEvent` is spread directly into webhook payloads, so `destinationCalendar` changes from an object (or null) to an array, or `[]`. External webhook consumers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` will break. The e2e test was updated to expect `[]` without any documentation or migration note for this public contract change.

title: Crash when Google Meet is selected and no destination calendar exists
body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array. Several call sites in this PR now pass `[]`. The code then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. For any Google Meet booking where the organizer has no destination calendar, this throws a TypeError. Before this change the access used `?.` and the event fell back to Cal Video; now booking creation fails instead.

title: Video references no longer get a credentialId
body: The reference `credentialId` is now `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so video results (Zoom, Daily, etc.) are stored with no credentialId. Previously they received `result.credentialId`. `handleCancelBooking` only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so cancelling these bookings will leave the external video meetings in place. Credential-based lookup for video updates breaks the same way.

title: Org slug assignment condition inverted (unrelated change)
body: The old code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, which set the slug only when team billing was disabled. The new code is `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, which reverses that. With billing enabled, the slug is now claimed before payment. With billing disabled, organizations are created with no slug at all. This change has nothing to do with destination calendars.

title: Collective hosts' Outlook events go to the first host's calendar id
body: `createEvent` now always uses `destinationCalendar[0]`, the main host's calendar. In a collective event it is called once per host credential. For every other host, it calls `/me/calendars/{mainHostCalendarId}/events` with their own token, which returns 404 or writes to the wrong calendar. It should pick the entry whose `credentialId` matches the credential being used, as the Google service does. Lark (lines 128/164) and the CalDAV `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (line 156) have the same problem. In the CalDAV case, filtering by the main host's externalId matches none of the other host's calendars, so no event is created and no error is reported.

title: Fallback calendar lookup is dead code; update/delete lose the destination-calendar fallback
body: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only reaches `find` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. In that case it compares against null/undefined and always returns undefined. References with no `externalCalendarId`, such as older bookings, previously fell back to `destinationCalendar.externalId`. Now `updateEvent` passes `calendarId: undefined` and the update fails, while `deleteEvent` targets `primary` and may hit the wrong calendar. The same pattern appears at line 315.

title: Hangout patch uses undefined calendarId when insert used 'primary'
body: The insert call uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `events.patch` passes `selectedCalendar` directly. When no destination calendar matches the credential, that value is undefined. The patch then fails, and the Meet link is never added to the event description.

title: Team members' destination calendars dropped when organizer has none
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing. The other collective hosts' calendars are silently discarded, which is the exact scenario this PR is meant to fix. Initialise the array (for example to `[]`) before pushing.

title: loadUsers drops organization select and masks errors as 500
body: The dynamic-user query no longer selects `organization: { slug }`. Any downstream code that reads `user.organization` for org-aware booker URLs will now see it as undefined. Separately, the new try/catch rethrows every non-Prisma error as a generic 500 "Unable to load users". That includes the explicit dynamicUserList validation error, so what is really a 400 client error comes back as a 500 and its message is lost.

title: Recurring cancellation deletion repeated per reference and misses non-first refs
body: The recurring branch is now inside the loop over calendar references. For each reference with a credential, it again deletes events across all of the organizer's calendar credentials and all updated bookings. With N calendar references this runs N times, sending duplicate delete calls. It also only deletes `updBooking.references.find(...)`, the first calendar reference of each occurrence. Collective hosts' events in later references are never removed, and they are deleted with the organizer's credentials rather than the matching ones.

title: Only first old calendar event deleted when merging on reschedule
body: `updateAllCalendarEvents` now handles multiple calendar references. However, the `newBookingId` merge path still deletes only `booking.references.find(...)`, the first calendar reference. For collective bookings, the other hosts' old calendar events are left behind, producing duplicate events after a seated reschedule.

title: Webhook payload shape of destinationCalendar changed
body: Webhook payloads spread `evt`, so `destinationCalendar` changes from a single object or null to an array. Depending on the trigger it is now `null` or `[]`, as the inconsistent test expectations show. This breaks existing webhook consumers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId`. The change is undocumented and should be called out or versioned.

title: Google credential key is overwritten with the safeParse result wrapper
body:
`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed token. Before this change the code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which is the token itself. Now `key` is the wrapper object and is written to the DB as `{ key }`.

After the first refresh, every Google Calendar credential is stored as `{success:true,data:{...}}`. The next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in the constructor then fails, breaking the integration for all users, including those who never enabled sync.

Store `key.data` instead.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys do not do what the comments claim
body:
`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key "[object Object]". Because the keys are duplicates, the second one wins, so the schema is effectively `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`.

Zod strips unknown keys by default. In sync mode every other field is dropped: `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, `scope`, `token_type` and so on.

Consequences:
- Zoom computes `Date.now() + undefined*1000` = NaN for the expiry.
- Office365 loses its expiry.
- Nothing actually validates that an expiry is present.

Use `.passthrough()` or `z.record`/`catchall` instead.

title: Placeholder refresh_token overwrites the real stored refresh token
body:
When the provider response has no `refresh_token`, the function sets it to the literal string "refresh_token". Office365 then spreads this over the stored credential (`{...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data}`), which replaces the real refresh token with "refresh_token".

Microsoft does not always return a new refresh token. This happens even when sync is disabled, so later refreshes fail and the credential is permanently broken.

title: Sync path returns a raw fetch Response, incompatible with most callers
body:
When sync is enabled, the function returns a `fetch` `Response`. Several callers expect a different shape:
- Google reads `res?.data`, which is undefined, so `token.access_token` throws.
- HubSpot expects a `HubspotToken` object and reads `expiresIn`/`accessToken`.
- Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `tokenInfo.data.error` (axios shape).

With sync enabled, token refresh crashes for all of these apps. The helper needs to normalize the sync response, or callers need to handle both shapes.

title: Outbound credential-sync request carries no authentication
body:
The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`. There is no secret, signature or auth header.

The self-hoster's endpoint returns live access tokens, but it has no way to verify the caller is Cal.com. Anyone who can reach that endpoint can obtain any user's third-party tokens by enumerating user IDs.

Include the webhook secret (or an HMAC) in a header.

title: Credential id passed where user id is expected
body:
`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's id as the `userId` argument. The sync endpoint therefore receives the wrong `calcomUserId`, which either fails or returns another user's tokens.

Pass `credential.userId` instead.

title: Wrong app slug sent for Zoom
body: The slug "zoomvideo" is passed to `refreshOAuthTokens`, but Zoom's app slug/appId is "zoom". The callback uses `appId: "zoom"`, and the webhook stores credentials by `appMetadata.slug`. The sync endpoint will receive a slug that does not match the one used everywhere else.

title: prisma used without import in Salesforce CalendarService
body: `prisma.credential.update` is called, but `prisma` is never imported in this file. Every Salesforce service instantiation will throw a ReferenceError (or fail type-check), breaking the Salesforce integration entirely.

title: Salesforce refreshes on every instantiation but uses the stale access token
body:
A refresh-token request is now made unconditionally each time the service is constructed. The refreshed token is saved to the DB, but the returned `jsforce.Connection` still uses the old `credentialKey.access_token` (and `instance_url`), so the refresh has no effect for the current request.

Two further problems:
- The refresh does not go through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so sync is never used for Salesforce.
- `response.statusText !== "OK"` fails on HTTP/2, where `statusText` is empty.

title: Webhook lacks method check and returns 500 on bad input
body:
The handler accepts any HTTP method. `schema.parse` and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throw on invalid bodies or a wrong key, producing unhandled 500s instead of 400s.

In addition, the secret is compared with `!==` rather than a constant-time comparison.

title: Credential key overwritten with a zod SafeParse result object
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `safeParse` result, i.e. `{ success, data }`, not the token itself. That whole object is then written as `key` in `prisma.credential.update`. After the first refresh, every Google Calendar credential is stored as `{success:true,data:{...}}`. On the next load `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails, which breaks the integration for all users, including installs where sync is disabled. Store `key.data` instead.

title: Sync path returns a raw fetch Response that callers don't expect
body:
When sync is enabled, the function returns a WHATWG `Response`. Several callers expect a different shape:
- Google reads `res?.data`, which is undefined on a fetch Response, so `token.access_token` throws.
- Hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object; it reads `.expiresIn` and `.accessToken` and persists the Response object as the key.
- Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin expect an axios response and read `.data.error` / `.data.access_token`.

With sync enabled, refresh is broken for all of these apps. The helper should normalize its return value, or callers should handle both shapes.

title: Minimum token schema uses bogus computed keys and strips the expiry
body:
`z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]". The schema therefore has a single key named "[object Object]" (the second overrides the first), not a wildcard for numeric expiry fields.

Because `z.object` strips unknown keys, the parsed data only keeps `access_token`; `expires_in`, `expiry_date` and similar fields are dropped. For example, in sync mode Zoom computes `Date.now() + undefined*1000`, which gives NaN, so the stored expiry is corrupt and refresh loops. Use `.passthrough()` or `z.record`, and validate the expiry field explicitly.

title: Placeholder "refresh_token" overwrites real refresh tokens
body: If the provider response lacks a `refresh_token`, the helper sets it to the literal string "refresh_token". Office 365 merges this into the stored credentials with `{...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data}`. Microsoft frequently omits `refresh_token` on refresh, so the user's valid refresh token is replaced with the string "refresh_token". The next refresh then fails permanently. This happens even when sync is disabled.

title: `prisma` used without being imported
body: `prisma.credential.update` is called, but `@calcom/prisma` is never imported in this file. This is a compile error, or at runtime a ReferenceError that rejects `getClient`, so every Salesforce operation fails.

title: Salesforce refreshes on every instantiation and keeps using the old access token
body:
`getClient` now calls the Salesforce token endpoint unconditionally on every service construction, with no expiry check. This adds a network round trip and rate-limit pressure on every booking.

The freshly obtained access token is also discarded: the connection is built with `credentialKey.access_token` (the old value) and `credentialKey.instance_url`. On top of that, the `statusText !== "OK"` check fails over HTTP/2, where `statusText` is empty. The refresh also bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so it ignores the sync feature entirely.

title: Credential id passed where user id is expected
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` takes a `userId` as its third argument, but Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId`. In sync mode the self-hosted endpoint receives `calcomUserId` set to a credential id, so it returns the wrong user's tokens or none. Pass `credential.userId` instead.

title: appStoreMetadata looked up by slug instead of directory name
body: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by app directory name, e.g. `googlecalendar`, `office365calendar`, `zoomvideo`. The handler indexes it with the DB slug, e.g. `google-calendar`, `zoom`. For most apps the lookup returns undefined and the webhook responds 404 "App not found". Look up by matching `slug` across the values instead.

title: Webhook secret compared non-constant-time; no method check; parse errors give 500s
body:
- The shared secret is compared with `!==`, which is not timing-safe; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.
- The handler accepts any HTTP method.
- `schema.parse` throws on a bad body, and `symmetricDecrypt` / `JSON.parse` throw on a bad payload or wrong key. These surface as unhandled 500s instead of 400s.

title: Inconsistent app slug sent to sync endpoint
body: Zoom sends `appSlug: "zoomvideo"`, but the app's slug is `zoom`, which is what the credential uses as `appId` and what the webhook expects. A self-hosted sync endpoint keyed by slug will not recognise the Zoom request.

title: Outbound token-sync request carries no authentication
body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no secret, signature or header. The self-hoster's endpoint cannot verify that the caller is Cal.com, yet it is expected to return live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user ids. The request should include the webhook secret header or an equivalent signature.

title: Google credential overwritten with the zod SafeParse result object
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed data. Before this change `key` was `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, i.e. the token object. Now `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` stores `{ success: true, data: {...} }` as the credential key. On the next load, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails, so every Google Calendar credential breaks after its first token refresh.

title: `prisma` used without being imported
body: The new code calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file never imports `@calcom/prisma`. This either fails type-check or throws a ReferenceError at runtime, so the Salesforce integration cannot be constructed at all.

title: Salesforce refreshes the token on every instantiation and then ignores the new token
body: `getClient` now POSTs to the Salesforce token endpoint every time the service is constructed, whether or not the token is expired. That adds latency and rate-limit pressure to every booking. The new `access_token` is written to the DB, but the returned `jsforce.Connection` is still built from the old `credentialKey.access_token`/`instance_url`. The refresh also bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so sync mode never applies here. Separately, `response.statusText !== "OK"` is a fragile success check: statusText is empty over HTTP/2. Use `response.ok` instead.

title: Minimum token schema uses bogus computed keys and strips expiry fields
body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key "[object Object]". The second one overwrites the first. The resulting schema is effectively `{ access_token, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`, and `z.object` strips all unknown keys. In sync mode every refreshed response therefore loses its expiry field (`expires_in`/`expiry_date`/etc.). For example, Zoom computes `expiry_date` from `undefined` and gets NaN, and Office365 stores no expiry. Tokens are then treated as perpetually expired or invalid. Use `.passthrough()` or an explicit schema.

title: Placeholder refresh_token overwrites the real refresh token
body: When the provider response has no `refresh_token`, the helper sets it to the literal string "refresh_token". This also runs when syncing is disabled. Office365 spreads `tokenResponse.data` over the stored credentials, so a refresh response without a refresh_token replaces the user's real refresh token with "refresh_token". All future refreshes then fail. Google also receives this value via `googleCredentials`. The placeholder should only apply in sync mode, and should not clobber an existing stored token.

title: Sync path returns a fetch Response while callers expect SDK/axios result shapes
body:
In sync mode the helper returns a raw `fetch` Response. Several callers expect a different shape:
- Google reads `res?.data` (a gaxios response).
- Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `tokenInfo.data` (axios).
- HubSpot expects a `HubspotToken` object.

With a Response, `.data` is undefined, so Google/Zoho throw on `token.access_token` or `tokenInfo.data.error`. HubSpot stores a Response object as the credential key with NaN `expiryDate`. The sync feature is broken for these apps. Normalize to parsed JSON, or have each caller handle both shapes.

title: Outgoing credential-sync request carries no authentication
body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no shared secret or signature. The self-hoster's endpoint, which returns live third-party access tokens, cannot verify that the caller is Cal.com. Anyone who can reach it can enumerate user IDs and harvest tokens. Include the webhook secret header or an HMAC signature.

title: Credential ID passed where user ID is expected
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential id as the third argument, which is `userId`. In sync mode the self-hosted endpoint is asked for tokens of an unrelated user whose id happens to equal the credential id. This can attach another user's tokens to this credential. It also forces the sync path even for team credentials. Pass `credential.userId`.

title: Wrong app slug "zoomvideo" sent to the sync endpoint
body: The Zoom app's slug/appId is "zoom" (see `createOAuthAppCredential({ appId: "zoom", ... })`). The refresh call sends `appSlug: "zoomvideo"`, which differs from the slug the webhook endpoint uses. A self-hoster's sync endpoint keyed by app slug won't recognize it.

title: Webhook secret compared non-constant-time; malformed input yields 500s
body:
The secret header is compared with `!==`, which is vulnerable to timing attacks; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. Also:
- There is no HTTP method check.
- `schema.parse` throws on a bad body.
- `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on a bad ciphertext or key.

All of these surface as unhandled 500s instead of 400s on an endpoint that writes credentials.

title: Team admin/owner check uses && so only users who pass both checks qualify
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. The variable name says either role should be enough, but the `&&` means a team admin who is not an owner fails the check. Such admins are rejected with FORBIDDEN unless they are the organizer or an attendee. Use `||`, or a single admin-or-owner query.

title: Any attendee can add unlimited arbitrary guests and trigger emails sent in the organizer's name
body: Authorization lets any booking attendee call this mutation. Nothing checks booking status (cancelled, past, rejected), and the input schema has no max length on `guests`. So any attendee can insert arbitrary attendee rows and make the system send emails to any addresses, with the organizer's name and reply-to. This is a spam/abuse vector. It also ignores seat limits on seated events. Restrict who can add guests, cap the list size, and validate booking state.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the organizer's
body: The EventManager is built from `ctx.user`'s credentials. When the caller is an attendee or a team admin rather than the organizer, `updateCalendarAttendees` runs with credentials that do not own the booking's calendar references. The external calendar event then is not updated, or the call throws. The booking user's credentials are already loaded (`booking.user.credentials`) and should be used instead.

title: DB write happens before an unguarded calendar update; a failure leaves inconsistent state
body: Attendees are written to the DB first. `updateCalendarAttendees` is then awaited without try/catch. If it throws, the client gets an error even though the guests were persisted. No emails are sent, and a retry fails with `emails_must_be_unique_valid` because the guests now exist. Wrap the external update and emails so a failure there cannot leave this half-done state, or roll back.

title: Emails use the raw `guests` list instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the original input. Any submitted email that was already an attendee, or was dropped by the blacklist filter, is still in the list. Existing attendees whose emails were resubmitted are treated as new and get a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notification. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

title: Duplicate and blacklist checks are case-sensitive
body: The blacklist entries are lowercased, but the incoming guest emails are not. An address like `Foo@x.com` therefore bypasses a blacklisted `foo@x.com`. The comparison against existing attendees is also exact-case, so an existing attendee can be added again with different casing. Normalize guest emails to lowercase before both comparisons.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disabled standard emails and seated-event attendee privacy
body: Unlike the other senders in this file, `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no `eventTypeMetadata` and never checks `disableStandardEmails`. Hosts and attendees therefore get emails even when the event type disables them. It also sends every attendee the full calEvent, attendee list included, without honoring `seatsShowAttendees`. On seated events that leaks other attendees' emails.

title: Error toast fallback is unreachable and can show 'undefined:'
body: `message` is a template string, so it is always a non-empty string and the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback never runs. When `err.data?.code` is undefined, for example on a network error, the toast reads 'undefined: ...'.

title: Emails use raw `guests` instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the original input list, not `uniqueGuests`. If the input includes someone who is already an attendee, that person is treated as a brand-new guest and gets a fresh `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the 'guests added' update. The intended split between new and existing attendees is therefore wrong whenever the input overlaps the current attendee list.

title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive
body: The blacklist entries are lowercased, but each `guest` is compared as-is. A blacklisted address written with any uppercase letter (e.g. `Bad@x.com`) passes the filter. The attendee check `guest === attendee.email` is also case-sensitive, so an existing attendee can be added again as a duplicate by changing the casing. Normalize guest emails to lowercase before both comparisons.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the organizer's
body: The `EventManager` is built from `ctx.user` and that user's credentials. When a team admin or an attendee (both allowed by the permission check) adds guests, the booking's calendar and video references belong to the organizer. `updateCalendarAttendees` will either fail or touch the wrong account. The organizer's credentials (`booking.user.credentials`) should be used instead.

title: Calendar update failure after DB write leaves inconsistent state
body: Attendees are inserted with `prisma.booking.update` before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs, and that call is not wrapped in error handling. If the calendar update throws, the client sees an error, yet the guests are already saved and no emails are sent. A retry then fails with `emails_must_be_unique_valid` because the guests now exist. Wrap the call in error handling or order the operations so the result stays consistent.

title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, so it is only true when both checks pass. The name and intent call for OR. Depending on how `isTeamAdmin` is implemented, plain team admins are denied permission they are meant to have.

title: Any attendee can add unlimited arbitrary emails, enabling spam
body: Any attendee of a booking may call this endpoint. The schema puts no limit on the number of guests, and the handler does not check booking status (cancelled, past, etc.). Each call sends emails from the platform to arbitrary addresses, so the endpoint can be abused to send spam. Add a maximum list size and a status check, and reconsider whether attendees should have this permission.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email-disable settings
body: Every other booking email sender checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` against the event type metadata. `sendAddGuestsEmails` accepts no metadata and always emails organizers, team members and attendees. This sends mail even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

title: Error fallback message is unreachable
body: `message` is a template string such as `"undefined: ..."`, which is always truthy. As a result, `t("unable_to_add_guests")` is never shown, and users can see text like 'undefined: ...'.

title: Validation error is never cleared after a successful submit
body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on a failed validation. It is only reset by the Cancel button, not when the input is corrected, when a submit succeeds, or when the dialog is closed via `onOpenChange`. A stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' warning therefore stays visible after the problem is fixed.

title: Team admin/owner check uses && so admins are rejected
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. `isTeamAdmin` already covers ADMIN and OWNER roles, so the `&&` effectively requires the user to be an owner. Team admins who are neither organizer nor attendee get FORBIDDEN, contradicting the variable name. This should be `||`, or just `isTeamAdmin`.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
body: The EventManager is built from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The caller can be an attendee or a team admin/owner rather than the organizer. In that case `updateCalendarAttendees` runs against the wrong user's calendar credentials, so the organizer's external calendar event and its references are not updated or the call fails. The organizer's credentials (`booking.user`) should be used.

title: Calendar update failure after DB write leaves inconsistent state
body: The attendees are committed to the database first via `prisma.booking.update`. Only afterwards is `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` awaited, without a try/catch. If the calendar update throws, the client gets an error and no emails are sent, but the guests are already persisted. A retry then fails with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' because the guests already exist.

title: Emails are sent based on raw input instead of the newly added guests
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the full input list rather than `uniqueGuests`. Input emails that were already attendees (filtered out of the insert) are treated as new guests. They get a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notification.

title: Case-sensitive comparisons let the blacklist and duplicate checks be bypassed
body: The blacklist entries are lowercased but the guest emails are not, so `Foo@blocked.com` passes `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. The existing-attendee check is also case-sensitive, so a differently cased address is inserted as a duplicate attendee. The server schema does not dedupe input either, so `createMany` can insert duplicates within one request.

title: Unbounded guest list lets any attendee trigger mass emails
body: Any attendee of a booking can call this mutation, and `guests` has no max length or dedupe. The handler also does not check booking status (cancelled or past bookings are accepted). The result is arbitrarily many cal.com emails, carrying calendar invites, to arbitrary addresses. That is a spam/abuse vector. Limit the array size, dedupe on the server, and reject cancelled or past bookings.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails event-type settings
body: Every other booking email sender respects `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` from the event-type metadata. The new function takes no metadata and always sends host, team-member and attendee emails. Event types that disabled standard emails will still send them.

title: Error toast fallback never used and the invalid-email flag is never cleared
body: `message` is a template string such as `undefined: ...`, so it is always truthy and the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback is dead code. Users may see 'undefined: <raw message>'. Separately, `isInvalidEmail` is only reset by the Cancel button. After fixing the input and submitting successfully, or closing the dialog via overlay/Escape, the error banner persists the next time the dialog opens.

title: Bookings without userId cause an unhandled 500
body: `findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` throws a Prisma NotFound error when the booking has no user. The client receives an internal server error instead of a meaningful TRPCError.

title: retryCount deletion branch is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter. This SMS cron will therefore delete any WorkflowReminder (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) whose retryCount exceeds 1. Today only this handler increments the field, but retryCount is a shared column on WorkflowReminder. Once the email or WhatsApp schedulers start using it with their own retry policy, this job will silently delete their reminders. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to that branch.

title: Unguarded DB update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the `catch` block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. It can throw, for example if the record was deleted concurrently because the booking was cancelled or rescheduled, or on a transient DB error. If it does, the exception escapes the for-loop and the handler. All remaining reminders in that batch go unprocessed and the cron returns an error. The same applies to the retry-increment update in the `else` branch. Wrap the increment so a failure there only logs.

title: Reminders with no sendTo or empty message are never counted as failures
body: retryCount is only incremented when `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns falsy or throws. If `sendTo` is missing (e.g. no smsReminderNumber) or the generated message is empty, the reminder is skipped without incrementing. The same happens for reminders skipped by the `!reminder.workflowStep || !reminder.booking` check. These reminders keep being re-fetched every cron run until their scheduled date, which is the exact behaviour this PR is meant to stop.

title: Non-atomic retryCount increment
body: The new count is computed as `reminder.retryCount + 1` from the value read at fetch time. If two cron invocations overlap, increments can be lost. Use Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` instead.

title: Retry-count delete branch is not restricted to SMS reminders
body: The second `OR` branch of `deleteMany` is `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter. This SMS cron will delete any `WorkflowReminder` whose `retryCount` exceeds 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders. Today only this handler increments the column, but the column is generic on the model. As soon as another scheduler uses `retryCount`, this job will silently wipe that scheduler's reminders. Move the method filter outside the `OR`, or add it to the retry branch.

title: Unguarded DB update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
body: The `catch` block now awaits `prisma.workflowReminder.update` before logging. If this update fails (DB error, or the reminder was deleted concurrently, e.g. booking cancelled), the error escapes the `for` loop. The request returns a 500 and all remaining reminders in the batch are skipped. The original error is also never logged because the `console.log` comes after the update. Wrap the update in its own try/catch, or log first and swallow the update error.

title: Reminders with no message or recipient are never counted as retries
body: When `message` is empty or `sendTo` is null (e.g. missing `smsReminderNumber`), neither branch of the new retry logic runs. These permanently unschedulable reminders are re-fetched and reprocessed on every cron run until their scheduled date passes, which is the behaviour this PR is meant to stop. Increment `retryCount`, or delete the reminder, in this case too.

title: OR on unindexed retryCount likely forces a full table scan each cron run
body: Adding `OR retryCount > 1` with no method filter means Postgres cannot use only the existing `(method, scheduled, scheduledDate)` index. With no index on `retryCount`, this `deleteMany` will probably scan the entire `WorkflowReminder` table on every cron invocation. The cost grows with the table, which holds email and WhatsApp reminders as well as SMS ones.

title: Retry-count delete branch is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The second `OR` branch (`retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) omits `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. This SMS cron therefore deletes every WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP rows. Today only this handler increments the column, but `retryCount` is a generic field on the shared model. Once any other scheduler (email/WhatsApp crons) starts using it, this job will silently delete those reminders. Put the `method: SMS` filter outside the `OR`, or add it to both branches.

title: DB update inside catch can throw and abort the whole cron run
body: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the `catch` block is not guarded. If it throws, the exception escapes the loop and the handler fails. Possible causes are a DB hiccup or the reminder being deleted concurrently, e.g. by booking cancellation, which makes the update raise P2025. All remaining unscheduled reminders in this run are then skipped, and the original error is never logged because the log line comes after the update. Log first and wrap the update in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany`, which does not throw on missing rows.

title: Reminders with no recipient or empty message still retry forever
body: `retryCount` is only incremented when `scheduleSMS` returns falsy or throws. When `sendTo` is null/empty or `message` is empty, nothing is updated. Such reminders are re-fetched and reprocessed on every cron run until their scheduledDate passes, which is the behaviour this PR set out to stop. Increment retryCount (or delete the reminder) in that branch too.

title: OR on unindexed retryCount defeats the existing index for the delete query
body: The existing composite index is `(method, scheduled, scheduledDate)`, and `retryCount` has no index. An `OR` between an indexed predicate and an unindexed `retryCount > 1` predicate will typically force a sequential scan of the entire WorkflowReminder table on every cron invocation. Consider scoping the branch to `method = SMS, scheduled = false` so the index can be used, or running a separate targeted delete.

title: Public `findMany` removed and condition types changed without migrating callers
body: `InsightsBookingService.findMany(findManyArgs)` was removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. The return types of `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` also changed from `BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` to `Prisma.Sql`. The PR touches no other file. Any existing code that calls `findMany`, or that spreads these conditions into a Prisma `where`/`AND` clause, will fail to compile. If it is cast loosely, it will silently pass a `Sql` object as a where input at runtime. Either keep a compatible method or update every call site (insights tRPC handlers, etc.) in the same change.

title: Caching tests deleted rather than ported
body: The whole "Caching" describe block was removed, which verified that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return memoized results. The caching logic is still in the service (`cachedAuthConditions`, `cachedFilterConditions`) and was retyped in this PR. Nothing now checks that the memoization still works, for example that a `null` filter result is cached and not rebuilt on each call. These tests could have been ported to `Prisma.sql` expectations instead.

title: Public findMany() removed and replaced by getBaseConditions(), breaking existing callers
body: The public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method is deleted. In its place is `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment instead of rows. Any caller that does `service.findMany({ select, where, ... })` (for example the insights routers) will no longer compile. Those call sites would also need rewriting to use `$queryRaw`, and the PR does not update any of them. Either keep a compatibility path or update every consumer in the same PR.

title: Authorization fragments are top-level ORs without outer parentheses
body: For org and team scope, `getAuthorizationConditions()` returns `(A) OR (B)` with no wrapping parentheses. A single eventTypeId filter likewise returns `(x) OR (y)` unwrapped. `getBaseConditions()` adds parentheses, but both getters are public. A consumer that writes `WHERE ${auth} AND "createdAt" > ...` or `WHERE ${filter} AND ${auth}` gets `A OR (B AND ...)` because of SQL operator precedence. That silently widens results and can bypass the authorization restriction. Return self-contained, parenthesized fragments, e.g. ``Prisma.sql`((${acc}) OR (${condition}))` ``.

title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions
body: `authConditions` is always a `Prisma.Sql` object and therefore always truthy, including NOTHING_CONDITION. The `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches can never run.
