This misleadingly suggests the filter-only path could skip authorization. Simplify to: return auth alone when there is no filter, otherwise return auth AND filter.

title: Constructor type weakened so invalid options compile and silently yield no data
body: The constructor now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId` is optional for every scope. Passing `scope: "team"` without `teamId` now type-checks. It then fails zod validation at runtime and silently becomes NOTHING_CONDITION (empty results) instead of being a compile-time error. The discriminated union type would catch this at compile time.

title: Caching tests removed and authorization not verified end-to-end
body: The caching tests for `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` were deleted rather than ported, so the caching behavior is now untested. The only test that runs SQL against the database uses user scope. The org and team scope fragments, which use `ANY()` array parameters and OR composition, are only compared structurally and never executed. Type or precedence errors in those fragments would therefore go unnoticed.

title: Public `findMany` method removed without migrating callers
body: `InsightsBookingService.findMany(findManyArgs)` was replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. The return types of `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` also changed from Prisma where-input objects to `Prisma.Sql`. Only the service and its test are modified in this PR. Any existing caller (for example the insights tRPC handlers) that calls `findMany`, or spreads these conditions into a Prisma `where`, will fail to compile. A raw `Sql` object passed into a `where` clause would be invalid. Please verify no other usages exist, or update them to use `$queryRaw` with `getBaseConditions()`.

title: Loosened constructor type lets invalid team scope compile and silently return no data
body: The constructor now takes `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId` is optional for every scope, instead of the discriminated union. A caller can now pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without `teamId` and it type-checks. The zod `safeParse` then fails, so `this.options` becomes null and the service returns `1=0`. That caller gets an empty result set with no error, and the mistake can no longer be caught at compile time.

title: Org-scope assertion depends on unordered DB result order
body: The test compares the generated SQL, including array parameter values, with exact ordering: team IDs `[org, team, team2, team3]` and user IDs `[user, user2, user3]`. Those arrays come from `findAllByParentId` and `findAllByTeamIds` queries that have no ORDER BY. Postgres does not guarantee row order without one, so the test can fail intermittently even though the authorization logic is correct.

title: Caching tests removed and SQL execution only covered for user scope
body: The caching tests for `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` were deleted, although the caching logic still exists in the service. The only test that runs the generated SQL against the database uses user scope. The org and team scope SQL, which is the security-sensitive part and uses `= ANY(array)` parameter binding, is only compared structurally and never executed. A SQL syntax or type error in those paths would not be caught by these tests.

title: Cache status not refreshed after deleting cache
body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. It never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. The disconnect mutation does invalidate it, and that query is configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. So after a successful delete, the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated" and the delete action for data that no longer exists, until a manual reload.

title: Timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
body: The date is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`. The surrounding string is localized through `t()`, but the timestamp ignores the user's locale and time-format preference. Non-US users see month/day ordering and a 12h clock regardless of their settings. Use the user's locale (e.g. `i18n.language`) or the existing dayjs/time-format helpers.

title: Empty-data updateMany adds a write per cache refresh and may be a no-op
body:
`SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is called after every cache refresh, which includes every Google webhook notification. That adds an UPDATE across all SelectedCalendar rows of the credential each time.

With empty `data`, Prisma may skip the query entirely or not bump `@updatedAt`, so the stated goal may not even be achieved. The PR notes also say this value isn't displayed anywhere. Remove the call, or set an explicit field if a timestamp is actually needed.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId from all callers
body:
`allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. The function is also re-exported for `@calcom/platform-libraries` as `getConnectedDestinationCalendars`. Any caller that selects only externalId/integration/eventTypeId will now fail type-checking, which includes platform API v2 and other repositories that build this user shape. Only `findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated.

These fields aren't used inside this function, so the type widening looks unnecessary.

title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError
body: A plain `Error` is thrown when the credential is not found or not owned by the user. tRPC maps it to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500), and the failure is logged as a server error instead of a client authorization/not-found condition. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or FORBIDDEN) instead.

title: Migration warning comment contradicts the SQL
body: The header warns that the required `updatedAt` column was added "without a default value" and that this is "not possible if the table is not empty". The statement actually adds the column with `DEFAULT NOW()`, so it is safe on populated tables. The stale auto-generated warning will mislead anyone reviewing migrations and should be removed.

title: BSD-only `sed -i ''` breaks on Linux
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is macOS/BSD syntax. On GNU sed (Linux, most CI and dev containers), the `''` is parsed as the sed script and the real expression as a filename, so the env file update fails. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is also resolved relative to the caller's cwd rather than the script location, so running the script from the repo root writes outside the repo.

title: dev:cron depends on tsx which is not a declared dependency
body: The script now runs `npx tsx`, but `tsx` isn't listed in devDependencies (`ts-node` still is). npx will download tsx at run time, which needs network access and uses an unpinned version, so the command is non-reproducible and fails offline. Add `tsx` as a devDependency, or keep `ts-node`.

title: No tests for new deleteCache handler or getCacheStatusByCredentialIds
body: The new mutation includes an authorization check: it must only delete cache for credentials owned by the caller. The new repository aggregation feeds the UI. Neither has unit tests, so regressions in the ownership check or the credential-to-status mapping would go unnoticed.

title: Cache status stays stale after a successful cache delete
body: The `deleteCache` mutation's `onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. It never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike the disconnect mutation, which does so in `onSettled`. `onChanged` is often undefined, and the query uses `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. As a result, after deleting the cache the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated" and the delete option until a full reload, so it looks like the delete did nothing.

title: Plain Error instead of TRPCError for not-found/forbidden
body: Throwing a generic `Error` when the credential doesn't belong to the user makes tRPC return an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500). It also gets logged as a server fault. Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN" })` so clients get a proper 4xx response and logs aren't polluted.

title: Extra no-op updateMany on every cache refresh
body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` runs on every `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`, which fires on each Google webhook. With empty `data`, whether Prisma bumps `updatedAt` at all is unreliable. Per the PR notes, `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not consumed anywhere; the UI reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt`. This adds a write across all selected calendars of the credential on a hot path for no functional benefit and should be removed.

title: Timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale even though the surrounding string is translated. Non-US users will see US-style dates (MM/DD/YY, 12h clock) inside localized text. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (i18n.language) instead.

title: Cache status includes expired entries
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups over all CalendarCache rows regardless of `expiresAt`. `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows with `expiresAt >= now`. The UI can therefore show a cache as present and "last updated" when every entry is expired and nothing would actually be served from cache. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }`.

title: Migration warning contradicts the SQL; legacy rows get misleading timestamp
body: The header warns that the column is added "without a default value", but the statement does use `DEFAULT NOW()`. That stale autogenerated comment should be removed. Also, every existing cache row gets the migration time as `updatedAt`, so the UI will report legacy caches as freshly updated at deploy time.

title: sed -i '' is macOS-only; ENV_FILE path depends on cwd
body: `sed -i ''` only works with BSD sed. On Linux, GNU sed treats `''` as a filename and the update fails. In addition, `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory rather than the script's location, so running it from the repo root writes to the wrong file.

title: dev:cron depends on undeclared tsx via npx
body: `npx tsx` relies on `tsx`, which is not declared in dependencies. npx will download it on demand, which can prompt or fail in offline or CI environments and leaves the version unpinned. `ts-node` is still in devDependencies. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency or keep `ts-node`.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId
body: `getConnectedDestinationCalendars` is re-exported for `@calcom/platform-libraries`. Widening the required Pick fields on the input type forces every external caller (e.g. API v2) to select `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on selected calendars. Otherwise their type check breaks, yet these fields are never used by this function.

title: No tests for new handler or repository method
body: There are no unit tests for `deleteCacheHandler`, including its ownership check and the case of a credential belonging to another user. There are also none for `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` or for the cache enrichment in `connectedCalendarsHandler`. The PR itself notes it was never tested end-to-end.

title: Cache status stays stale in the UI after deleting the cache
body: The `deleteCache` mutation's `onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. It never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component. The connected-calendars query also runs with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. As a result, after a successful delete the dropdown keeps showing the old "Last updated" timestamp and the delete option until the page is reloaded.

title: updateMany with empty data is unreliable for bumping updatedAt
body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is meant to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, but it relies on Prisma injecting `@updatedAt` into an `updateMany` whose data is empty, which is fragile. The repository method is also typed with `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`, which allows relation inputs, but `updateMany` only accepts `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`, so the signature is wrong. Pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` explicitly and use the UpdateManyMutationInput type. This also adds an extra write on every cache refresh, and the PR description itself says the frontend does not use this value.

title: Widening UserWithCalendars breaks other callers
body: `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. This function is exported for `@calcom/platform-libraries` (`getConnectedDestinationCalendars`) and used by other code paths. Only `findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated to select these fields, so any other caller that builds a user with the old select will fail type-checking. Nothing inside this function reads the new fields, so the widening is unnecessary.

title: Plain Error returns 500 instead of a proper tRPC error
body: When the credential is not found or not owned by the user, the handler throws `new Error(...)`. tRPC surfaces this as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500), which logs a server error and gives clients the wrong status. Use `TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` or `FORBIDDEN` instead.

title: Cache status counts expired cache entries
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups over all `CalendarCache` rows without filtering on `expiresAt >= now`. A credential whose only cache rows have expired, and are therefore never served, is still shown as having a cache with a last-updated time. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the where clause.

title: Existing rows get the migration time as updatedAt, and the header comment is wrong
body: Every pre-existing cache row gets `updatedAt = NOW()` at migration time. The UI will therefore show a misleading "Last updated" time for legacy caches until they are refreshed. Separately, the auto-generated warning says the column is added "without a default value", which contradicts the actual `DEFAULT NOW()` statement below it.

title: Timestamp is always formatted in en-US
body: The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded `"en-US"` locale, so non-English users see US date formatting inside an otherwise translated string. Use the user's locale from `useLocale` (`i18n.language`) instead.

title: macOS-only `sed -i ''` and cwd-relative env path
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` only works with BSD sed. With GNU sed on Linux, the empty `''` is parsed as the script, so the command fails and the .env file is not updated. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved against the current working directory rather than the script's location, so running the script from elsewhere edits or creates the wrong file. `cleanup` also exits with status 0 on failure paths.

title: dev:cron depends on tsx, which is not a declared dependency
body: `npx tsx` is not in the package's dependencies, so npx downloads an unpinned version at runtime. This breaks offline or locked-down setups and makes runs non-reproducible. Add `tsx` as a devDependency.

title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole batch and can block cancellations permanently
body:
All cancellations run sequentially inside a single try. If any `client.request` throws, the loop stops and `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is never reached. Prisma queries are lazy, so none of the queued deletes run, including those for batches SendGrid already cancelled successfully.

On the next cron run the same reminders are returned again. SendGrid rejects a second cancel for a batch that already has a status, so the same first reminder throws on every run. Every cancelled reminder after it in the list then never gets cancelled, and those emails go out until the stale row ages past `scheduledDate`.

Fix: wrap each reminder in its own try/catch, delete the row right after a successful cancel, and treat an 'already cancelled' response as success.

title: Reschedule uses immediate SendGrid cancellation, reintroducing the 100-pending-cancellation limit
body:
Rescheduling calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)`, which immediately POSTs a cancel to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends`. That is the call the PR description says fails once 100 cancellations are pending.

Reschedules are frequent. They will fill the pending-cancellation quota again, after which these cancels fail silently (errors are only logged) and the old booking's reminders are still sent. Workflow deletion and step deletion in `workflows.tsx` use the same immediate path, so they have the same problem.

The immediate path also never deletes the DB row or sets `cancelled`. On reschedule this leaves stale reminder rows attached to the old booking.

title: Deferred cancellation misses reminders scheduled shortly after the booking is cancelled
body:
Cancelling a booking now only sets `cancelled: true`. The real SendGrid cancel happens in the cron, which runs every 15 minutes.

If the booking is cancelled when its reminder is less than about 15 minutes from `sendAt`, the next cron run may come too late. SendGrid needs the cancel some minutes before send time, or the run may come after the send. The email is then delivered for a cancelled booking. Before this change the cancel was sent immediately.

Fix: cancel immediately when `scheduledDate` is already inside the cron's one-hour window, and defer only reminders scheduled further out.

title: Cancellation flag update is not awaited
body:
`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called inside `forEach` and never awaited. The DB write that sets `cancelled: true` is now the only thing that stops the email from being sent.

In a serverless or API-route environment the handler can return before these promises settle, and the update can be lost. Errors are also swallowed. The same fire-and-forget pattern is used in `bookings.tsx` `requestReschedule` and in `workflows.tsx`.

Fix: collect the promises and await `Promise.all` before returning.

title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts all remaining cancellations in the cron run
body:
The loop awaits `client.request` for each cancelled reminder inside a single try/catch. If one request throws (invalid batch id, rate limit, or the 100 pending-cancellation cap), the loop stops. Every remaining reminder in that run is left uncancelled.

The delete operations already collected are lazy Prisma promises that only run at `Promise.all`, which is never reached. So even reminders that were cancelled successfully stay in the DB. The failing reminder is likely to break subsequent runs the same way until its scheduledDate passes, and the affected emails go out.

Fix: wrap each reminder in its own try/catch and delete each row right after its cancel succeeds.

title: Deferred cancellation can miss reminders that are close to their send time
body:
Cancellation only marks `cancelled: true`. The real SendGrid cancel waits for the next cron run, which happens every 15 minutes.

Suppose a booking is cancelled or rescheduled shortly before a reminder's send time, for example right after a cron tick and less than about 15–25 minutes before sendAt. The next cron run may come too late, either after the send or inside SendGrid's minimum lead time for cancelling a scheduled send. The email for the cancelled booking is still delivered, which is the bug this PR is meant to fix.

Fix: cancel immediately when scheduledDate is within the cron window (for example under 1h15m away), and defer only reminders further in the future.

title: Reschedule path still uses immediate SendGrid cancellation and leaves stale rows
body:
When a booking is rescheduled, its reminders are cancelled with `immediateDelete = true`. That calls the SendGrid scheduled_sends cancel right away, and those pending cancellations count against the 100-cancellation cap. Reschedules are frequent, so this brings back the failure mode the PR describes.

In the immediate branch, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` also neither deletes nor marks the WorkflowReminder row, so stale `scheduled: true` rows remain for the old booking.

The same reminders may already have been marked cancelled by `requestReschedule`, in which case they are cancelled twice. Use the deferred `cancelled` flag here as well.

title: immediateDelete branch never removes the DB record
body:
When `immediateDelete` is true, the function cancels the SendGrid batch and returns. It never deletes or flags the WorkflowReminder row.

For workflow or step deletion, the row is removed later by cascade. Other callers, such as the reschedule path in handleNewBooking, are left with a row that still says `scheduled: true` and has no `cancelled` flag. That row is inconsistent with reality and is only cleaned up after its scheduledDate passes.

title: Reminder cancellation calls are fire-and-forget
body:
`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but are called inside `forEach` without being awaited. The handler can return before the `cancelled` flag update or the Twilio cancel and DB delete finish.

In serverless deployments, work still pending after the response may be dropped. A dropped flag update means the cron never cancels the email. Previously the DB deletes were at least awaited through `Promise.all`, and the same regression applies in bookings.tsx `requestReschedule` and in workflows.tsx.

Fix: collect the promises and await them.

title: Deferred cancellation misses reminders due before the next cron run
body: Cancelling now only sets `cancelled: true`. The actual SendGrid cancel waits for the `scheduleEmailReminders` cron, which runs every 15 minutes. If a booking is cancelled or rescheduled shortly before a reminder's `scheduledDate` (e.g. due in 5 minutes), SendGrid sends the email before the cron gets to it. The old code cancelled immediately, so this is a regression for near-term reminders. Reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the cron window should be cancelled immediately.

title: Reschedule and workflow/step deletion still cancel immediately, hitting the 100 pending-cancellation limit
body: The PR says the root cause is SendGrid's cap of 100 pending scheduled_send cancellations. Yet several paths pass `immediateDelete=true`, which issues the `scheduled_sends` cancel right away: rescheduling here, plus workflow deletion and step deletion in workflows.tsx. Deleting a workflow with many future reminders, or many reschedules, still fills the cancellation quota. Further cancellations then fail silently (only logged) and emails go out anyway, so the bug is only partially fixed.

title: One failing SendGrid cancel blocks all later cancellations on every run
body: All cancellations run sequentially inside a single try/catch. If `client.request` throws for one reminder (invalid/expired batch id, quota error, etc.), the loop aborts. The remaining reminders are not cancelled, and the already-queued deletes are never awaited. The failing reminder stays `cancelled: true` and is retried first on every run, so it can block the others until their emails are sent. Each reminder needs its own try/catch.

title: Reminder cancellation promises are fire-and-forget
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but called inside `forEach` without awaiting. The handler returns before the DB update (`cancelled: true`), the row delete, or the Twilio cancel completes. In a serverless environment the function can be frozen before these finish, so reminders stay un-cancelled and are still sent. The old code at least awaited the DB deletes. The same pattern appears in bookings.tsx, handleNewBooking.ts and workflows.tsx.

title: Unawaited reminder deletion races with step deletion cascade
body: For a deleted step, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` start without being awaited, and then `workflowStep.delete` runs. Step deletion cascades to the reminders, so the concurrent `workflowReminder.delete` / `update` calls can hit already-deleted rows and throw (only logged). The Twilio and SendGrid cancel may also not complete before the response is returned.

title: Dynamic imports run eagerly at module load, so nothing is lazy
body:
Each entry in the `appStore` object is `import("./x")` evaluated directly in the object literal. Importing `@calcom/app-store` therefore starts loading all ~28 app packages immediately, as it did before. The stated goal of async, on-demand loading is not achieved.

It also creates a new risk. If any app module throws during initialization (e.g. missing env, bad dependency), its rejected promise has no handler until some code happens to `await` that key. That causes unhandled-rejection warnings, or a process crash under `--unhandled-rejections=strict`, even when that app is never used.

Fix: make the entries thunks such as `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and have callers invoke them.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns `calendar` as a Promise
body:
`getCalendar` is now async, so every item from `getCalendarCredentials` has `calendar: Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`. That changes the public return type of this exported function.

`getConnectedCalendars` was updated to await it. Any other consumer that reads `item.calendar` and calls methods on it, or checks it for truthiness, will silently break. A Promise is always truthy, so `if (!calendar)` checks no longer detect missing calendars.

The promise is also created eagerly and only awaited later. A rejection in `getCalendar` can go unhandled if a consumer never awaits it.

Suggestion: resolve the calendars inside an async `getCalendarCredentials`, or rename the field and audit all callers.

title: forEach(async) escapes the surrounding try/catch and is never awaited
body:
The callback is now `async` and awaits `getCalendar`. Any error from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` becomes a rejected promise that `forEach` discards. The enclosing try/catch no longer catches it, which previously worked for synchronous `getCalendar` errors, so the error surfaces as an unhandled rejection.

The deletions are also not awaited before emails are sent and the function returns `true`.

Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` instead. The same pattern appears in `wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts` and in `requestReschedule` in `trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletes are pushed to apiDeletes after it has already been awaited
body:
In the recurring branch, `forEach(async (credential) => { await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })` only pushes into `apiDeletes` after asynchronous awaits. By then `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` has already run, so these deletions are neither awaited nor have their errors handled.

This PR adds `await getCalendar` before the first push, which guarantees the problem. Also, `deletedEvent` is an already-awaited value rather than a promise.

Collect the promises with `map`, then `await Promise.all` them.

title: Dynamic imports run eagerly at module load, so nothing is lazy-loaded
body:
Each entry is written as `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`. That calls `import()` immediately when `@calcom/app-store` is first evaluated, so all ~28 app packages still load up front, just asynchronously. The PR's goal (only loading an app when it is used) is not achieved. Meanwhile every consumer had to become async, which adds the problems listed in the other findings.

There is a second risk: if any single app module fails to import, its promise rejects at load time with no handler attached. That produces an unhandled rejection, which can crash the Node process depending on configuration.

Fix: use thunks such as `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")` and have callers invoke the thunk.

title: Async forEach callback escapes the surrounding try/catch
body:
The callback was changed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })`. Any error from `getCalendar` (for example a CalendarService constructor throwing on a bad credential key) is now a rejected promise. The enclosing `try/catch` never sees it, so it becomes an unhandled rejection.

Before this change `getCalendar` was synchronous, so a throw was caught and logged. The deletions are also fire-and-forget, so the function returns before they complete.

Fix: use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try block.

title: Async forEach callback escapes the surrounding try/catch
body:
This has the same problem as the vital reschedule. The `forEach(async ...)` callback awaits `getCalendar`, so a failure while loading or constructing the calendar becomes an unhandled promise rejection. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch it, although it could catch the previously synchronous throw.

Fix: use `await Promise.all(...map(async ...))` inside the try block.

title: requestReschedule fires un-awaited async callbacks; getCalendar failures become unhandled rejections
body:
`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })` is not awaited. If `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` rejects, nothing handles the rejection, and it can crash or log noise in the API process.

The mutation also returns before the old calendar and video events are deleted. Previously a synchronous `getCalendar` throw would have surfaced as a proper TRPC error.

Fix: use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` with error handling.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns `calendar` as a Promise, silently changing its contract
body:
`getCalendarCredentials` still calls `getCalendar(credential)` without awaiting it. The `calendar` field of each returned item is therefore now `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`.

Only `getConnectedCalendars` in this file was updated to `await item.calendar`. Any other caller that uses `item.calendar` directly will now operate on a Promise. That includes truthiness checks like `if (!calendar)`, which are always truthy for a Promise, and calls like `calendar.listCalendars()`.

Also, a rejection of a promise created here before `getConnectedCalendars` attaches a handler can surface as an unhandled rejection.

title: Recurring-cancel deletes are pushed into apiDeletes after it is awaited
body:
In the recurring branch, `forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(...) })` pushes into `apiDeletes` only after an await. By that point `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 has already captured the array.

As a result, these calendar deletions are never awaited, and any errors they throw are unhandled rejections. The new `await getCalendar` makes this race certain rather than incidental.

Fix: use a `for...of` loop like the non-recurring branch below.

title: `import()` calls run eagerly at module load, so no app is actually lazy-loaded
body:
Each property of the `appStore` object literal is initialised with `import("./x")`. That call starts the import as soon as `index.ts` is evaluated. Importing `@calcom/app-store` therefore still loads all ~28 app packages up front, which defeats the PR's goal of async/lazy imports.

The cost is that every caller now pays for an `await` and has an async signature, with no reduction in load cost.

There is a second problem: if any single app module fails to load, its promise rejects whether or not anyone ever reads that key. Nothing handles that rejection, so it surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection at startup.

Fix: store thunks instead, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and call them on demand in `getCalendar`, `getVideoAdapters` and the payment helpers.

title: `forEach(async ...)` escapes the surrounding try/catch, causing unhandled rejections
body:
The callback is now `async` and awaits `getCalendar`. The returned promises are discarded by `forEach`.

Any error from `getCalendar` (app import failure, a `CalendarService` constructor throwing) or from `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` becomes a rejected promise. The surrounding try/catch, which is meant to log these errors, never sees it.

Previously a synchronous `getCalendar` error was caught there. Now it is an unhandled rejection, which can terminate the Node process under default settings. The deletions are also not awaited before the reschedule email is sent.

Fix: use `await Promise.allSettled(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a `for...of` loop.

title: `forEach(async ...)` escapes try/catch, causing unhandled rejections
body:
This is the same problem as in `vital/lib/reschedule.ts`.

The async `forEach` callback's promises are dropped. Failures in `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` are no longer caught by the enclosing try/catch and become unhandled promise rejections. The deletes are also not awaited before the reschedule email is sent.

Fix: replace with `Promise.allSettled` over `map`, or with a `for...of` loop.

title: `requestReschedule` fires async calendar/video deletes without awaiting or handling errors
body:
`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` now awaits `getCalendar` inside each callback. The resulting promises are discarded.

Any rejection from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` is unhandled, with a risk of process crash on Node 15+. The mutation also returns, and sends emails and webhooks, before the external events are actually removed.

Fix: collect the promises with `map` and `await Promise.allSettled(...)`.

title: Working-hours check rejects slots that fall outside any one of several working-hour ranges
body:
The `workingHours.find(...)` returns true, meaning unavailable, as soon as any single working-hour entry for that weekday does not contain the slot.

Users with more than one range on the same day therefore lose slots. Examples:
- A split day such as 9–12 and 13–17.
- A schedule crossing UTC midnight, which `getWorkingHours` splits into two entries (e.g. 1020–1439 on day N and 0–60 on day N+1).

A slot inside one range is always outside the other, so it is rejected. The check must instead verify that the slot lies within at least one matching range. Otherwise US-timezone organizers, and anyone with split hours, can lose most or all slots.

title: Working-hours end check uses slot start instead of slot end
body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`), so it is identical to `start`. The `end > workingHour.endTime` comparison never detects a slot that starts inside working hours but runs past their end. It should use `slotEndTime`.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === (always false)
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct object references, so it is always false. The intended 'override with zero length = unavailable all day' branch never runs. For such an override, a slot starting exactly at the override instant passes the remaining before/after checks and is treated as available. Use `.isSame()` instead.

title: Slots overlapping the end of a date override are accepted
body:
The only end-side rejection is `slotStartTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`. Two cases slip through:
- A slot starting exactly at the override end.
- A slot that starts inside the override but ends after it, e.g. a 60-min slot starting 30 minutes before the end.

Both are considered available, so fixed hosts can still be booked outside their override window. The check should reject when `slotEndTime` is after the override end, or when `slotStartTime` is the same as or after it.

title: Override date matching mixes server-local and UTC calendar days
body:
Two problems in matching an override to a slot's day:
- The override day is computed with `dayjs(date.start)...format("YYYY MM DD")`, which uses the server's local timezone, while `slotStartTime` is UTC. On non-UTC servers the dates can mismatch.
- Matching is by UTC calendar day, not by the organizer's local day the override applies to. For organizers far from UTC (e.g. PST), regular-hours slots from the previous local day that share the UTC date get evaluated against the override and wrongly rejected. Conversely, override hours on the other UTC date are not matched.

title: Shifted override minutes wrap around midnight and get dropped
body: After adding the invitee/organizer offset, start and end are converted to minute-of-day via `hour()*60+minute()`. If the shift moves an override across the invitee's midnight (e.g. 22:00–02:00 in invitee time), endTime becomes smaller than startTime and `buildSlots` discards the range. `activeOverrides` is also still filtered on the unshifted `dayjs.utc(override.start)` date, so for large offsets the override can land on the wrong invitee day. Slots on the adjacent day are then missing or incorrect.

title: Parsing Date.toString() output with dayjs is non-standard
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` relies on `new Date()` parsing the locale-style string from `Date.toString()` (e.g. "Tue Mar 21 2023 ... GMT+0000 (Coordinated Universal Time)"). This format is implementation-defined and drops milliseconds. Passing the Date directly, `dayjs(override.start)`, is reliable.

title: No test for the round-robin fixed-host date override fix
body:
The PR's main fix is that fixed hosts' date overrides restrict round-robin availability, and it adds new override and working-hours logic to `checkIfIsAvailable`. Only a single-user timezone case is tested. Nothing covers:
- A round-robin event with fixed and loose hosts.
- Users with working hours crossing UTC midnight or split ranges.
- Slots overlapping override boundaries.

These are exactly the scenarios where the bugs above occur.

title: Working-hours check uses the slot start time as its end time
body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime`, exactly like `start`. The check therefore never compares the slot's real end (`slotEndTime`) against `workingHour.endTime`. A slot that starts inside working hours but runs past their end is treated as available, so meetings can be booked that overrun a fixed host's working hours.

title: Split working hours reject valid slots
body: `workingHours.find` returns true as soon as any working-hour entry for that weekday does not contain the slot, and that makes the slot unavailable. If a host has several ranges on the same day (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17, or ranges split at the UTC day boundary), a slot inside 9-12 lies outside 13-17 and gets rejected. The fix is to reject only when the slot falls outside all applicable ranges (use `some`/`every` correctly). As written, fixed and round-robin hosts with multiple ranges lose valid slots.

title: Multiple date-override ranges on one day reject slots inside later ranges
body: `dateOverrides.find` returns true, meaning 'not available', for the first same-day override whose range does not contain the slot. If a user has two override ranges on the same day (e.g. 9-10 and 14-16), a slot at 14:00 is rejected because it falls outside 9-10, even though it fits the second range. The slot should be accepted if any override range for that day contains it.

title: Override end boundary compares slot start instead of slot end
body: The slot is rejected only when `slotStartTime` is after the override end. A slot that starts before the override ends but runs past it (e.g. a 60-minute slot at 10:30 with an override ending at 11:00) passes the check. The fixed host is then booked outside their overridden availability. The check should compare `slotEndTime` against the override end.

title: Dayjs objects compared with `===` (always false)
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct object references, so the condition is never true. Zero-length overrides, which mark the user unavailable all day, are not handled by this branch. A slot that straddles the zero-length point then passes the later checks. Use `.isSame()` here.

title: Override day matching mixes shifted organizer time with UTC slot date
body: The override start is shifted by the negated organizer offset and formatted as a date. That date is then compared with the slot's UTC calendar date (`slotStartTime` is `.utc()`). For organizers far from UTC, the organizer's local override day and the slot's UTC day differ near midnight. As a result, overrides can be ignored for slots on the override day, or applied to slots on an adjacent day.

title: Offset-shifted override can wrap past midnight and produce an invalid range
body: Start and end are computed as hour*60+minute after adding the timezone offset. When the shift crosses midnight (e.g. an override ending 22:00 shifted by +3h becomes 01:00), `endTime` ends up smaller than `startTime`. `buildSlots` skips such ranges (`start >= end`), so the override silently yields no slots. Meanwhile it has still removed the user's working hours for that day. The `activeOverrides` filter also uses the unshifted UTC start, so it can choose the wrong invitee day.

title: Parsing Date.toString() output with dayjs is non-standard
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` parses the locale-style `Date.prototype.toString()` string, which is not ISO 8601. That depends on engine-specific `Date` parsing and drops milliseconds. `override.start` is already a `Date` and should be passed directly.

title: Round-robin fixed-host override fix is not tested
body: The PR's main fix is that fixed hosts' date overrides restrict round-robin availability, but no test creates a round-robin event with a fixed host that has an override. The added test only covers a personal event in a second timezone. The existing `toHaveTimeSlots` matcher also does not check the slot count, so missing expected slots go undetected. None of the new `checkIfIsAvailable` paths are covered: multiple ranges, slots running past the override end, and zero-length overrides.

title: Working-hours check rejects slots when a day has more than one working-hour range
body: The new check uses `workingHours.find(...)` and returns false as soon as any range for the slot's weekday does not contain the slot. That requires the slot to fall inside every range for that day, not just one of them. Split schedules (e.g. 9–12 and 13–17) produce several ranges per day. So do schedules that cross UTC midnight, which `getWorkingHours` splits into separate ranges. In all these cases every slot fails at least one range, so valid slots are hidden for fixed and round-robin hosts. The check should pass when the slot lies within at least one range.

title: Slot end is computed from the slot start time
body: `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, which is the same value as `start`. The test `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore never considers the event length. A slot that starts just before the end of working hours and runs past it is treated as available. It should use `slotEndTime`.

title: Multiple date overrides on the same day mark every slot unavailable
body: The override check also uses `dateOverrides.find(...)` and returns true (meaning unavailable) when the slot is outside any single override on that day. If a host has two override ranges on one date (e.g. 9–11 and 14–16), a slot inside the first range is outside the second, so `find` succeeds and the slot is rejected. The host ends up with no availability on that day. The slot should be accepted if it falls within any override for the date.

title: Dayjs objects compared with ===, so the zero-length override check never matches
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct object references, so it is always false. The intended detection of a zero-length ("unavailable all day") override never fires. Such days then go through the before/after checks, and a slot starting exactly at the override instant can be treated as available. Use `.isSame()` or compare `valueOf()`.

title: Timezone-shifted override minutes wrap around midnight
body: After adding the invitee/organizer offset, start and end are reduced to `hour()*60+minute()` of the shifted time. Any override that crosses midnight once shifted wraps to the wrong part of the day. Example: 17:00–20:00 UTC with a +5:30 shift becomes 22:30–01:30, giving endTime < startTime, and `buildSlots` drops the range as invalid. Shifts that push the whole range into the next or previous day are placed on the wrong day. In addition, `activeOverrides` still selects overrides by the unshifted UTC start, which is inconsistent with the shifted values. Overrides near day boundaries will show missing or incorrect slots for attendees in other timezones.

title: Override day matching compares the shifted start against the slot's UTC calendar date
body: An override is applied only when its shifted start formats to the same `YYYY MM DD` as `slotStartTime` in UTC. For organizers far from UTC, an override's local day spans two UTC dates. Slots on the other UTC date then neither count as part of the override nor get rejected by it. They fall through to normal working hours or busy checks, so the override is only partially enforced for fixed hosts.

title: New tests do not cover the round-robin fixed-host fix or a real timezone change
body: The added assertion reuses the IST day window (18:30Z boundaries) with the Dhaka timezone. It only checks that the same UTC slots come back, which does not exercise overrides shifting across day boundaries. No test covers the headline fix, a round-robin event whose fixed host has a date override. No test covers multiple overrides or working-hour ranges per day either, which is where the new checks fail.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset or doesn't match a category
body: The query joins `site_settings` to `categories` on the `embed_category` setting value and then calls `[0]['id']` on the result. If no `embed_category` row exists (the default case, since it defaulted to ''), or its value matches no category name, the result set is empty. `[0]` then returns nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The migration aborts on most installs, and the `category_id == 0` fallback is never reached. Check `cmd_tuples` or `ntuples` before indexing.

title: Migrated hosts are not normalized and the raw value is interpolated into SQL
body: The old `embeddable_hosts` values are inserted verbatim, e.g. `http://eviltrout.com`, `https://example.com/1234`, or values with a trailing `\r` or whitespace. The old matcher stripped schemes and parsed URIs. The new `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` to the bare `uri.host`, so these rows never match and embedding silently breaks for existing sites after upgrade. The value is also string-interpolated into the INSERT, so any quote in it breaks the migration. Strip scheme, path and whitespace, skip blank lines, and use `quote`.

title: before_validation raises on nil host
body: `self.host.sub!` is called unconditionally. When the host is nil, e.g. a POST or PUT to the admin endpoint without `embeddable_host[:host]`, this raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if host.present?` or use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`.

title: Host lookup is not truly case-insensitive and ignores ports
body: The column is lowercased with `lower(host)`, but the parameter is passed as-is from `uri.host`. Ruby's URI does not downcase hosts, so a referer like `http://EvilTrout.com` won't match. The validation regex also allows a `:port` suffix, but `uri.host` excludes the port, so a host saved with a port can never match. Downcase the parameter and either reject ports or compare them.

title: update/destroy with unknown id raise NoMethodError
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: ...).first` returns nil for a missing id. `host.destroy` and `save_host(nil)` then raise NoMethodError and return a 500 instead of a 404. Use `find` or `raise Discourse::NotFound`.

title: Delete failures are silently swallowed
body: `destroyRecord()` has no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. If the server delete fails, the admin gets no feedback and the promise rejection is unhandled. The save action does handle errors, so delete is inconsistent with it.

title: type.replace('_','-') only replaces the first underscore
body: `String#replace` with a string pattern replaces only the first occurrence. Any admin model type with two or more underscores won't be normalized and will be routed to `/` instead of `/admin/`. Use `/_/g`.

title: Test requests fruit 2 but the fixture always returns fruit 1
body: The pretender handler for `/fruits/:id` always returns `fruits[0]`, the apple with `color_ids [1,2]`. The test asks for fruit 2, the banana with `color_ids [3]`, yet asserts two colors with ids 1 and 2. It passes only because the id is ignored, so it misrepresents what is being tested and would fail if the fixture honored the id.

title: "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests what it says
body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer depends on embeddable hosts. This test passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false. The test name is misleading, and the outer `before` block that `Fabricate`s a host has no effect on the behavior under test.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category (or uncategorized_category_id) row is absent
body: The migration does `execute(...)[0]['id']` without checking that any row came back. Site settings only get a row in `site_settings` when they differ from the default, so on most installs, including every fresh install, `embed_category` has no row. `[0]` then returns nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, which aborts the migration. Line 15 has the same problem for `uncategorized_category_id`. Check `cmd_tuples`/`ntuples` before indexing.

title: Legacy host values inserted raw: unescaped and not normalized
body:
Each line of the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is interpolated straight into SQL as `'#{h}'`. A value containing a quote breaks the migration; the value should be passed through `quote`/`PG::Connection.escape_string`.

The values are also never normalized. The old setting accepted entries like `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://example.com/1234`, and old code stripped the scheme at lookup time. The migration skips the model's `before_validation` stripping, so those rows keep the scheme/path. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares against `uri.host`, so they never match, and existing embeds stop working after upgrade.

Trailing `\r`/whitespace and blank lines are not stripped either.

title: Hosts with a port can never match; lookup isn't truly case-insensitive
body:
The validation explicitly allows a port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), and `before_validation` keeps it. `record_for_host` compares against `uri.host`, which never includes the port, so a saved host like `example.com:8080` can never be allowed.

Also, `lower(host) = ?` lowercases only the stored column, not the argument. Ruby's URI does not downcase the host, so a referer such as `http://EvilTrout.com/...` is rejected. Downcase `host` before querying.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host
body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when `host` is nil. That happens with `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?` or when the admin controller receives a request without `embeddable_host[:host]`. The result is a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if host.present?`.

title: update/destroy raise 500 for unknown id
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil. `host.destroy` and `save_host(host)` then raise NoMethodError instead of returning 404. Use `find` or raise `Discourse::NotFound`.

title: Embedded `_ids` hydration crashes on null and keeps unresolved entries
body: `obj[k].map` throws if a serialized `*_ids` key is null or not an array. `hydrated || []` is dead code because `map` always returns an array. Ids that cannot be resolved become `undefined` entries in the array instead of being filtered out.

title: type.replace only replaces the first underscore
body: `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the first occurrence. Any admin model type with more than one underscore will not be recognized and will be routed to `/` instead of `/admin/`. Use a global regex such as `/_/g`.

title: Test name no longer matches behavior
body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks for embeddable hosts. This test, "is false if embeddable_host is blank", now passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false, so it does not test what its name claims. The `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` in the nested before block is likewise irrelevant to the outcome.

title: Fabricator file contents swapped
body: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines the `embeddable_host` fabricator, and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators. It works because all fabricators get loaded, but it is clearly a mistake and will confuse anyone looking for the category fabricator.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category is not set or matches no category
body: The category lookup does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i`. If no `embed_category` row exists in site_settings, or its value matches no category name (the common case, since the default was ''), the result set is empty. `[0]` then returns nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The migration aborts on most installs and blocks deploys. The fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` on line 14 is never reached. The same nil-indexing problem applies on line 15 if `uncategorized_category_id` was never persisted to site_settings.

title: Unescaped, unnormalized host values interpolated into INSERT
body:
Each legacy host string is interpolated directly into SQL as `'#{h}'` without quoting. A value containing a quote breaks the migration and is a SQL-injection vector.

The values are also inserted without the model's normalization. Strings split on "\n" keep trailing "\r" or whitespace, and the old setting allowed `http://` prefixes, which the old lookup stripped. Rows like `http://example.com` or `example.com\r` never match `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, so previously working embeds silently stop working after upgrade.

Fix: strip whitespace and the scheme/path from each value, skip blanks, and use `connection.quote` for the insert.

title: Irreversible data deletion inside a `change` migration
body: The migration deletes the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings in `change`. On rollback, `create_table` is reversed (the table is dropped) but the deleted settings are not restored. Rolling back permanently loses the embedding configuration. Use explicit `up`/`down` methods, or raise `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration` in `down`.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host
body: `self.host.sub!` is called unconditionally. If host is nil, for example when the request params omit `embeddable_host[host]`, this raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if host.present?`, or use non-mutating `sub` on `host.to_s`.

title: Hosts with ports or uppercase referers never match
body: Matching is done with `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, but the query value is not lowercased, so a referer with uppercase letters in its hostname is rejected. In addition, the validation explicitly allows a `:port` suffix, and the before_validation keeps it. `uri.host` never includes the port, so a stored `example.com:8080` can never match. Lowercase the input, and either strip ports on save or compare against host plus port.

title: Host validation rejects valid hostnames
body: The regex requires a final label matching `\.[a-z]{2,5}`. This rejects valid hosts such as `localhost` and TLDs longer than 5 characters (e.g. `.museum`, `.technology`, `.photography`). Admins cannot add these hosts through the new UI, even though the migration can insert such values unvalidated.

title: Update/destroy of a missing id raises NoMethodError
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown or already-deleted id. The next call (`host.host=` in save_host, or `host.destroy`) then raises a 500. Use `find` or `find_by!` so the request returns a proper 404.

title: `_ids` hydration crashes on null and keeps unresolved ids as undefined
body:
Any key ending in `_ids` is assumed to be an array. If the server sends `foo_ids: null`, `obj[k].map` throws and the whole find fails.

Also, `hydrated || []` is dead code because `map` always returns an array. Ids that are not found in the side-loaded collection become `undefined` entries, and the original ids are deleted. Guard against non-arrays and filter out unresolved entries (or keep the ids).

title: find embedded test requests fruit 2 but stub always returns fruit 1
body: The test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)`, but the pretender handler for `/fruits/:id` always returns `fruits[0]` (apple, `color_ids [1,2]`). The assertions on two colors with ids 1 and 2 only pass because of that stub. Fruit 2 (banana) has a single color, id 3. The test is misleading and does not check that the requested record is the one hydrated.

title: Spec name no longer matches behavior under test
body: The spec "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false. `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks embeddable hosts at all, and `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` in the nested context has no effect on the result. The test name describes behavior that does not exist and gives false coverage.

title: Fabricator file contents swapped
body: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, and the new `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators. It works because all fabricators are loaded, but the contents of the two files are swapped and will confuse future maintainers. Swap them back.

title: String replace only converts the first underscore
body: `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the first occurrence. Any admin model type with more than one underscore (e.g. `site_customization_foo`) will not match ADMIN_MODELS and will be routed to the non-admin path. Use `replace(/_/g, '-')` or `Ember.String.dasherize`.

title: Second `self.downsize` definition silently replaces the width/height variant
body:
`OptimizedImage.downsize` is defined twice: `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 and `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the width/height signature no longer exists.

Every existing caller using `downsize(from, to, w, h, opts)` now fails:
- With five arguments it raises `ArgumentError`.
- With four arguments, `max_height` (an Integer) is bound to `opts`, and `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` raises a `TypeError`.

This breaks existing downsizing (e.g. avatar and thumbnail code paths). Give the new method a distinct name, or have a single method that accepts both forms.

title: Animated GIF downsizing passes a percentage to gifsicle, which it cannot use
body:
When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is on and the file is a `.gif`, `optimize` routes to `resize_instructions_animated`, which runs `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. `--resize-fit` expects WxH dimensions, not a percentage.

As a result:
- gifsicle exits non-zero.
- `downsize` returns false, and the result is ignored.
- The loop burns all 5 attempts doing nothing.
- The oversized GIF is passed on unchanged and then rejected.

Animated GIFs, often the largest images, are never reduced.

title: In-place rewrite of tempfile path may leave the open Tempfile handle stale
body:
The loop rewrites the file at `tempfile.path` in place. `convert` writes there, and `ImageOptim#optimize_image!` replaces the file, typically by writing a new file and renaming it over the path. The open `Tempfile` IO can still refer to the original inode.

If so:
- `tempfile.size` keeps reporting the original size, so the loop always runs the full 5 iterations of expensive conversions.
- `Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, ..., tempfile.size)` may read the original, unreduced content and size.

Also, the return value of `downsize` is ignored, so a failed conversion keeps looping. Re-open the file or use `File.size(tempfile.path)`, and stop when `downsize` returns false.

title: Client-side size limit hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types, ignoring site settings
body:
`validateUploadedFile` now uses a fixed 10MB limit instead of `max_<type>_size_kb`. That limit is only meant to let oversized images through for server-side downsizing, but it also applies to attachments.

Consequences:
- Attachments larger than `max_attachment_size_kb` pass client validation, upload fully, and are only rejected by the server.
- Sites configured with limits above 10MB can no longer upload files the server would accept.

The same hardcoding at line 246 makes the 413 error message report 10MB regardless of the real limit. Keep the setting-based limit for attachments, and only relax it for images.

title: URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB regardless of upload type or settings
body:
API URL uploads are now capped at a fixed 10MB instead of following site settings. Two effects:
- Admins who raised `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB can no longer upload such files by URL.
- Attachments up to 10MB are downloaded even when the configured attachment limit is far smaller, wasting bandwidth before the inevitable rejection.

title: No tests for the new automatic downsizing path or the `downsize` signature change
body: The PR adds the server-side downsize loop and changes the `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` signatures without adding any specs. A spec covering the old `downsize(from, to, w, h)` callers would have caught the method-redefinition breakage. A spec for oversized image uploads, including GIFs, would have caught the gifsicle issue.

title: Second `downsize` definition silently replaces the 4-arg `(max_width, max_height)` version
body: Ruby has no method overloading, so `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined just above it. Existing callers that pass width and height (e.g. post-processing or avatar downsizing) now bind `max_height` to `opts` and pass a bare width as `dimensions`. `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` then runs on an Integer and raises a TypeError, or the `-resize` arguments come out wrong. Use a distinct method name, or detect a string dimension argument inside a single method.

title: Percentage resize fails for animated GIFs (gifsicle) and failures are ignored
body: When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is on and the file is a GIF, `downsize` goes through `resize_instructions_animated`, which runs `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. gifsicle does not accept percentage geometry, so the command fails. The loop ignores the boolean result of `OptimizedImage.downsize` and just repeats the same failing call up to 5 times. The oversized file then goes to `Upload.create_for` and is rejected anyway. Large animated GIFs are never downsized, and CPU is wasted on futile shell-outs. Check the return value and break on failure, and build an absolute size for gifsicle.

title: Loop relies on `tempfile.size` of the open descriptor after an external in-place rewrite
body: The file is rewritten in place by an external `convert` and then by ImageOptim, which may write a new file and rename it over the path. `tempfile.size` stats the already-open descriptor, so it can keep reporting the old inode's size. The loop would then keep shrinking needlessly, and the size passed to `Upload.create_for` would be stale. Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` instead.

title: Client size check hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb
body: The client limit used to come from `max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb`; it is now 10MB for every type. Downsizing only applies to images, so attachments larger than the configured `max_attachment_size_kb` now pass client validation and fail on the server after the whole upload. Sites that configured a limit above 10MB can no longer upload files they are allowed to upload. The error text also reports 10MB, not the real attachment limit. Keep using the site setting for attachments.

title: Hardcoded 10MB download limit for API URL uploads
body: The download limit is now a hardcoded `10.megabytes` for every upload type. For attachments this no longer matches `max_attachment_size_kb`: sites configured above 10MB can't import larger files via URL. Files above the limit are downloaded unnecessarily before being rejected. The 10MB magic number is also duplicated across client and server instead of coming from a setting.

title: No tests for automatic downsizing or the new `downsize` signature
body: The new downsize loop and the changed `OptimizedImage.downsize` / `optimize` signatures have no specs. A spec exercising the existing `(max_width, max_height)` callers would have caught the method being overwritten.

title: Second `self.downsize` definition silently replaces the width/height version
body:
Ruby has no method overloading. The new `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined just above it at line 145.

Existing callers that pass width and height separately now break:
- A call like `downsize(path, path, w, h, opts)` raises ArgumentError because it passes 5 arguments to a method that accepts 3–4.
- A call like `downsize(path, path, w, h)` binds `h` (an Integer) to `opts`, and `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` then raises a TypeError.

This breaks avatar and emoji downsizing done in `Upload.create_for`. The two variants need distinct names, or one method that accepts either form.

title: Downsize result ignored; animated GIFs get an invalid gifsicle argument
body:
The return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored. If ImageMagick or gifsicle fails, the loop keeps retrying a no-op up to 5 times and then uploads the oversized file anyway.

With `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled and a .gif file, `optimize` routes to `resize_instructions_animated`. That produces `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`, which is not a valid gifsicle geometry. Every attempt therefore fails, and large animated GIFs are never reduced.

The loop should stop on failure, and it should pass a geometry gifsicle understands, such as concrete pixel dimensions.

title: In-place conversion may leave `tempfile.size` and the open handle stale
body:
The image is rewritten in place at `tempfile.path` by `convert` and then by ImageOptim. ImageOptim, and possibly convert, write a new file and rename it over the path, which gives the path a new inode.

`Tempfile#size` stats the already-open file descriptor, which still points at the old, now-unlinked inode. In that case:
- the `while` condition never sees the reduced size, so all 5 iterations run, each shrinking the image by another 80%;
- `tempfile.size` passed to `Upload.create_for` reports the original size rather than the stored file's size.

Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` for the size checks and the size argument.

title: SVG uploads are run through ImageMagick raster resize
body:
`FileHelper.is_image?` matches .svg files. An SVG larger than `max_image_size_kb` will be passed to `convert ... -resize 80%` with an .svg output path. That rasterizes or mangles the vector file, or fails, instead of leaving it alone.

Elsewhere SVGs are explicitly copied rather than resized (see `OptimizedImage.create_for`). SVGs should be excluded here too.

title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores the attachment size setting
body:
The client check previously used `max_<type>_size_kb`. It is now hardcoded to 10MB for both images and attachments.

This has two effects:
- Sites that set `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB can no longer upload larger attachments, because the client rejects them.
- Attachments between the site limit and 10MB are no longer rejected client-side, so users wait for the upload and then get a server error.

Only the image limit should be relaxed, since only images are auto-downsized. The 413 message at line 246 likewise reports 10MB regardless of the actual server limit.

title: API URL downloads now capped at 10MB regardless of type
body:
The download limit for API-provided URLs is now hardcoded to 10MB for every upload type.

Attachments allowed by `max_attachment_size_kb` beyond 10MB can no longer be fetched. When a download exceeds the cap, the `rescue nil` swallows the error and leaves `tempfile` nil. `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` at line 72 then raises NoMethodError instead of returning a proper size error.

title: No tests for automatic downsizing or the changed downsize API
body:
The PR adds a downsizing loop and changes the `OptimizedImage.resize`/`downsize`/`optimize` signatures, but includes no specs.

A spec exercising `downsize` with width/height arguments, or the upload controller with an oversized image, would have caught the method redefinition that breaks existing callers.

title: Unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists
body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id:, topic_id:)` returns nil when the user has no topic_users row for the topic. That happens, for example, to a user who was mentioned or quoted in a topic they never visited. The next line calls `tu.notification_level` on nil, so clicking the email unsubscribe link raises NoMethodError and returns a 500. Use `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row if needed, or handle the nil case explicitly.

title: save! bypasses TopicUser.change, so the level can be silently reverted and clients are not notified
body: The level is written with `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`. As a result `notifications_reason_id` and `notifications_changed_at` are not set, and no MessageBus `notification_level_change` is published to the user's open clients. When `notifications_reason_id` is still NULL, `update_last_read` auto-promotes the row back to `tracking` once read time exceeds the auto-track threshold. A user who unsubscribed can therefore be re-subscribed just by reading the topic. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`.

title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed as a GET with no CSRF protection, and it toggles on repeat
body: The unsubscribe action changes the user's notification level on a plain GET. Any third-party page can embed `` and change a logged-in user's settings. Email link scanners, prefetchers and page reloads also trigger it. The action is not idempotent: the first hit drops watching/tracking to regular, and a second hit (a refresh or revisit) drops regular to muted. The user ends up muted without intending it. Have the GET render a confirmation page and perform the change via POST/PUT, or use a signed per-user token.

title: unsubscribe_link now needs %{unsubscribe_url}; senders that don't pass it break
body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` render it for every email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Only `send_notification_email` was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`. Any other sender that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` without it will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument or render a broken link. Even when the URL is present, the per-topic sentence is wrong for emails that are not about a single topic. Use a separate translation key, or only add the topic sentence when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

title: No tests for the new unsubscribe endpoint
body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action has no controller specs. Untested cases include the level transitions (watching/tracking to regular, regular to muted), the missing-TopicUser case, the slug redirect, and the logged-out behavior. The only spec change adds an `unsubscribe_url` argument to an existing MessageBuilder test and does not assert that the link appears.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil when the user has no topic_users record for the topic. This happens for a different logged-in user opening a forwarded link, or for a topic the user never interacted with. The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises NoMethodError and the user gets a 500 instead of being unsubscribed. Use `TopicUser.change` (which creates the row when missing) or handle nil explicitly.

title: State-changing GET toggles level on every visit and can be triggered by prefetchers
body: The unsubscribe endpoint is a GET that changes the notification level each time it is hit. The first visit from watching or tracking drops the user to regular; a reload or second click then drops them to muted. Email link scanners and prefetchers, which commonly fetch every link in a message, will silently change or mute users' subscriptions. The action should be idempotent (always set a fixed target level) or require an explicit confirmation POST.

title: Direct save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
body: The level is updated with `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`, so `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (user_changed) are not set and no MessageBus `notification_level_change` is published. If `notifications_reason_id` is still nil, `TopicUser.update_last_read` will auto-promote the topic back to tracking once the user's read time passes the threshold, silently undoing the unsubscribe. Open clients also show a stale notification state.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}
body: The `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, and MessageBuilder renders it for every email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Callers that do not pass `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument or render a broken link. Examples are other mailers, plugins, or any non-topic emails that use this flag. The spec had to be changed to pass `unsubscribe_url`, which confirms the new requirement. Either make the per-topic sentence conditional or default the argument.

title: No tests for the new unsubscribe action
body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action has no controller specs. Untested behaviour includes the level transitions (watching/tracking → regular, regular → muted), the slug redirect, the logged-out case, and the missing-TopicUser case. These are exactly the paths that currently misbehave.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
body: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when the user has no row for the topic. That happens, for example, when they were notified by a mention or a watched category but never visited the topic. The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises NoMethodError and the user gets a 500 from the unsubscribe link in their email. Use `TopicUser.change` (which creates the row when missing) or handle the nil case.

title: Notification level saved directly, so auto-tracking can undo the unsubscribe
body: `tu.save!` writes `notification_level` without setting `notifications_reason_id` or `notifications_changed_at`, and without publishing the MessageBus change. `TopicUser.change` normally does all three. `auto_track` and the SQL in `update_last_read` both re-track a topic when `notifications_reason_id IS NULL`. So a user who never changed this topic manually can be silently moved back to tracking after reading or posting, which reverses the unsubscribe. Open clients also never learn about the new level. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` instead.

title: State-changing GET endpoint that lowers the level again on every visit
body: `unsubscribe` is a GET route and changes notification state on each request, with no confirmation and no CSRF protection. Link prefetchers, email security scanners, browser reloads or a cross-site `` tag can trigger it. Because each call drops the level one step (watching/tracking -> regular, regular -> muted), a second hit silently mutes a topic the user only meant to stop watching. Make the change idempotent, for example by recording the target level, or require a POST/confirmation step.

title: Client-side navigation to the unsubscribe page does not unsubscribe
body: The Ember route loads the topic with `PostStream.loadTopicView`, which calls `/t/:id.json` (topics#show), not the `unsubscribe` endpoint. Only a full server page load of `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` changes the notification level. If the user reaches this route through an in-app transition, the page still says "You will stop receiving notifications" but nothing changes on the server.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url} from every caller
body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` use it for any email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Only `send_notification_email` passes `unsubscribe_url`. Any other caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` without it will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument or render a broken link; the spec had to be patched to pass the argument for exactly this reason. Use a separate key for the per-topic sentence, or include it only when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

title: Message says notifications stop even when the user was only moved to regular
body: The page always shows "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>". A user who was watching or tracking is only moved to `regular`, which still notifies them on mentions and replies. The text overstates what the action did.

title: No tests for the new unsubscribe action
body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action has no controller specs. Untested cases include the slug redirect, logged-out access, a missing TopicUser row, and the level transitions (watching -> regular, regular -> muted).

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and trivially bypassed
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` does an exact, case-sensitive match on PostgreSQL, and neither the stored value nor the incoming value is normalized (e.g. with `Email.downcase`/strip). If `bad@spammers.org` is blocked, signing up as `Bad@Spammers.org` passes the block check. Both sides should be normalized to lowercase before comparing or storing. The uniqueness validation and the unique index on `blocked_emails.email` have the same case gap, so duplicates differing only by case can be inserted.

title: match_count update is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: `should_block?` loads the record, does `match_count += 1` in Ruby, and saves. Concurrent signup attempts with the same email read the same value and overwrite each other, so increments are lost. Use an atomic SQL update instead, e.g. `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])`.

title: Validation side effect counts each signup attempt twice
body: `EmailValidator` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which writes to the database (match_count, last_match_at) on every validation. `UsersController#create` runs `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which validates again. Every signup attempt with a matching email therefore increments match_count by 2, making the statistics wrong. More generally, any extra `valid?` call anywhere inflates the counts. Recording the match should be moved out of the validator, or done only once per attempt.

title: Match statistics recorded inside the user save transaction are rolled back on failure
