body: Because `should_block?` saves the BlockedEmail record during the User's validation, the write happens inside the User save transaction. In `save!`/`create_for_email`, a blocked email raises RecordInvalid and the transaction rolls back, losing the match_count/last_match_at update. Statistics are then inconsistent depending on the call path (`save` vs `save!`).

title: rejectedEmails array is defined on the prototype and shared/persistent
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` in `extend()` creates one array shared by every instance of the controller, and it is never cleared. If an email is rejected for a transient reason (for example 'has already been taken' because of a race), it stays rejected client-side for the rest of the page session. The array should be initialized per instance in `init` and reset when the modal is reopened.

title: should_block? side effects run on every validation, double-counting matches on signup
body: `should_block?` increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at` and saves the record every time it is called. It is called from `EmailValidator`, which runs on every `valid?`/`save`. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` (when `call_discourse_hub?` is on) and then `user.save`, so one signup attempt bumps the counter twice. Any other code path that validates repeatedly inflates the statistics the same way. Validation should be a pure check; record the match once, explicitly, at the point of rejection.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of match_count
body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` loads the value, increments it in Ruby and writes it back. Concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked address can lose increments. Use an atomic SQL update instead, e.g. `update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')` or `increment_counter`.

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and easily bypassed
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` does an exact, case-sensitive match. The unique index and uniqueness validation are also case-sensitive. Email addresses are effectively case-insensitive, so a blocked `bad@spam.org` can register as `Bad@Spam.org`. Normalize the address (e.g. `Email.downcase`) on both storage and lookup, or compare with `lower(email)`.

title: Rejected email compared against server-returned value, which may differ from the typed input
body: The client stores `result.values.email`, the server-side model attribute, in `rejectedEmails`. It then checks `rejectedEmails.contains(accountEmail)` against the raw input. If the server normalizes the email (case, whitespace), the stored value will not equal what the user typed. The field will then not be marked invalid, and the user can resubmit the same rejected address. Store the locally submitted `email` instead.

title: rejectedEmails array defined on prototype is shared across instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` inside `extend` creates one array on the class prototype. Every instance of `CreateAccountController` mutates the same array via `pushObject`. Rejected emails therefore persist across modal openings and instances. Initialize it in `init` instead.

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and trivially bypassed
body: `should_block?` looks up the record with `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)`, an exact, case-sensitive comparison. Neither the stored value nor the incoming value is normalized with `Email.downcase`/strip, and the unique index is also case-sensitive. If `bad@spammers.org` is blocked, a user can register as `Bad@Spammers.org` and the block does not fire. Normalize emails on save and before the lookup.

title: Non-atomic match_count increment loses updates under concurrent signups
body: The counter is updated by read-modify-write: load the record, do `match_count += 1` in Ruby, then `save`. Concurrent validations for the same email read the same value and overwrite each other, so increments are lost. Use an atomic SQL update instead, e.g. `update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', now])` or `increment_counter`.

title: Validator writes to the DB on every validation, inflating match statistics
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` updates match_count and last_match_at every time validation runs. `UsersController#create` validates twice: once via `user.valid?` (outside any transaction, before the DiscourseHub call) and again via `user.save`. For `:do_nothing` entries both writes commit, so each signup is counted twice. Any other `valid?` call also inflates the counts. A validator should not have persistent side effects; record the match once at the point of an actual signup attempt.

title: rejectedEmails array is defined on the prototype and shared/persistent
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined in `extend`, so a single array lives on the class prototype. Every instance shares it, and it is never reset when the modal is reopened. An email rejected once, for any email error including transient ones, stays marked invalid on the client for the rest of the page session, even if the admin later unblocks it. Initialize the array in `init` and clear it when the modal is shown.

title: New error/values fields in create response are untested
body: The client now depends on `errors` and `values.email` being present in the failure response from `create`. No controller spec covers these fields or the blocked-email signup path end to end, so a regression would silently break the client-side rejected-email handling.

title: Unsanitized feed/remote HTML stored as raw_html post (stored XSS)
body: Content from the RSS/Atom feed (`PollFeed`) or from a remote page (`import_remote`) is saved with `cook_method: raw_html`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` as-is, with no sanitizer. The embed view outputs it with `raw post.cooked`, and the normal Discourse topic view renders it too. Any `<script>`, `onerror=` or `javascript:` content in the feed therefore runs on the forum origin. A compromised or malicious feed, or a hijacked page on the embeddable host, gets full XSS against forum users, including admins. The HTML should be sanitized with a whitelist before it is stored.

title: URL interpolated unescaped into HTML attribute
body: `#{url}` builds raw HTML from the feed item's link/id without escaping. That HTML is then rendered unsanitized via the raw_html cook method. A URL containing a `'` breaks out of the href attribute and lets an attacker inject arbitrary markup or event handlers. `url` should be HTML-escaped (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape`).

title: Protocol-relative URLs are mangled by absolutize_urls
body: Any href or src starting with '/' is treated as host-relative, including protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. The leading slashes are stripped and the embed host is prepended, producing `http://host/cdn.example.com/img.png`. This breaks every protocol-relative link and image in imported content. Values starting with '//' should be skipped or resolved properly, e.g. with `URI.join`.

title: Crash on feed items without content / on Ruby < 2.1
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item has a `content` element. Many RSS feeds only provide `description`, so `content` is nil and the call raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole poll. Because `retry: false` is set, nothing after that item is imported. `String#scrub` also only exists in Ruby 2.1+, so on Ruby 2.0 this raises for every item. A fallback to `description` and a nil guard are needed.

title: Every new embed URL triggers a full synchronous feed poll
body: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline whenever an embed URL is unknown. That fetches the whole feed over HTTP and runs import, including SHA comparisons and possible revisions, for every item. The only throttle is per URL. Any visitor hitting distinct article URLs (or the same URL with different query strings) on the embeddable host forces repeated full feed downloads and imports. There is no caching of the feed fetch (`feed_key` is defined but never used).

title: `end if` typo turns following template output into the if-modifier condition
body: `<%- end if %>` compiles to `end if` followed by the next generated `@output_buffer.safe_append=...` statement. Ruby parses that statement as the modifier condition, so the template only works by accident because the append is truthy and evaluated first, which reorders output. It should be `<%- end %>`.

title: Nil post when embed's post was deleted
body: `post = embed.post` can be nil if the post was hard-deleted, or not found because it was trashed via the default scope. `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then raises NoMethodError on every feed poll for that URL, breaking the import of all subsequent items.

title: Substring-based origin check for postMessage
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl. For example, `https://forum.example.co` passes the check for `https://forum.example.com/`. The origin should be compared exactly against the parsed origin of discourseUrl.

title: Editing an existing migration to add force: true
body: Adding `force: true` to an already-shipped migration does nothing on installs that have already run it. On re-runs it silently drops the existing `top_topics` table. Changing historical migrations is unrelated to this feature and risky.

title: Unescaped URL interpolated into raw-HTML post (stored XSS)
body: The URL is interpolated directly into `#{url}` and appended to the post contents. These posts use the `raw_html` cook method, so the HTML is never sanitized. It is later rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and also in the main forum. The URL can come from the unauthenticated `embed_url` query parameter (controller → RetrieveTopic → import_remote). The only check is that the host matches `embeddable_host`, and URI accepts `'` in the path. A crafted URL such as `http://host/x'onmouseover='...` therefore lands as attacker-controlled attributes in a stored post. Escape the URL (ERB::Util.h) before building the link.

title: raw_html cook method bypasses all sanitization
body:
`cook` returns `raw` verbatim for `raw_html` posts. Content pulled from RSS feeds or remote pages via Readability is then stored and served as trusted HTML; Readability is not a security sanitizer.

Any script, iframe or event-handler attributes in the source page or feed are rendered on the forum. The same applies to anyone who later edits such a post, since `cook_method` persists. Run the HTML through a sanitizer (e.g. Sanitize with a whitelist) before storing or rendering it.

title: Failed post creation still creates TopicEmbed with nil ids
body:
`PostCreator#create` returns the unsaved `@post` even when it rolled back (spam detection, topic creation errors such as a duplicate title). `post.present?` is true for that object, so `TopicEmbed.create!` runs with `post_id`/`topic_id` nil.

The columns are NOT NULL, so this raises a DB error and the job or import crashes. Check `post.persisted?` / `creator.errors` instead.

title: Protocol-relative URLs are mangled by absolutize_urls
body:
`href`/`src` values starting with `//` (protocol-relative, e.g. `//cdn.example.com/img.png`) pass the `start_with?('/')` check. After the leading slashes are stripped they become `http://embedhost/cdn.example.com/img.png`, which breaks every protocol-relative link and image in imported content.

The port check is also scheme-agnostic. `http` on 443 or `https` on 80 would drop a required port.

title: Feed items without content / String#scrub crash the poller
body:
SimpleRSS exposes `content` only for Atom `<content>` (or `content:encoded`). Typical RSS items use `description`, so `i.content` is nil and `.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole poll.

In addition, `String#scrub` only exists in Ruby 2.1+, while this codebase still targets 1.9/2.0. Fall back to `description` and avoid `scrub` or polyfill it.

title: Every unseen embed URL triggers a full synchronous feed poll and remote fetch
body:
Any visitor's request for a new `embed_url` enqueues a job. When feed polling is enabled, that job fetches and re-imports the entire RSS feed, then may fetch the remote page as well.

The throttle is keyed per URL. An attacker on (or spoofing a referer for) the embeddable host can vary the path to force unlimited feed polls, outbound fetches and topic creation for arbitrary pages on that host. Each distinct path also creates a new Redis key. The loading page also re-requests every 30s, re-enqueueing jobs.

title: Non-atomic setnx + expire can leave throttle key permanently set
body: If the process dies between `setnx` and `expire`, the key never expires. Retrieval for that URL is then throttled forever. Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` atomically.

title: Stray `end if` turns following output into an if-modifier condition
body: `<%- end if %>` compiles to `end if` followed by the next buffer append. The entire preceding if/else block then becomes conditional on that append expression. It happens to evaluate truthy, but this is a typo that silently changes control flow and could break with template changes. It should be `<%- end %>`.

title: Editing an existing migration to add force: true
body: This migration has already been released. Adding `force: true` changes it after the fact: re-running it (e.g. rollback/redo, or environments that replay migrations) now silently drops and recreates `top_topics`. Already-migrated databases don't pick up any change. The new `create_topic_embeds` migration also uses `force: true` without need.

title: Disqus import drops --category option and original created_at; remote fetch failure aborts import
body: The `--category` option was removed, and the topic's original `created_at` is no longer applied, which is a behavior regression for existing users of the task. Also, `import_remote` performs an HTTP fetch per thread with no rescue. One unreachable or 404 link raises and aborts the whole import midway.

title: Unauthenticated requests can create unlimited topics and outbound fetches
Imported HTML stored and rendered unsanitized (stored XSS)
body:
Posts imported from RSS/Atom (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)`) or via readability are created with `cook_method: raw_html`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` verbatim, with no sanitization. The rendered post is output with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and on the forum.

Risks:
- Any script, event handler, or `javascript:` href in the feed or remote page runs in the forum's origin.
- Readability keeps `href`, so `javascript:` URLs survive that path too.
- Any later edit to such a post (by a moderator or the author) also bypasses cooking and sanitization.
- The 'imported from' footer interpolates `url` into an HTML attribute without escaping.

The content should be sanitized before storage or rendering.

title: `<%- end if %>` typo breaks template compilation/logic
body: The header conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. In compiled ERB, `end if` turns the next generated statement into an `if` modifier condition, or produces a syntax error, depending on how the buffer append is emitted. Either way the template is broken or the logo link output becomes conditional unexpectedly.

title: Feed items without `content` crash the whole poll
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item has a `content` element. Plain RSS feeds normally use `description`, and Atom entries may only have a summary. For such items `i.content` is nil, which raises NoMethodError and aborts the import of all remaining items. Retries are disabled, so the poll simply fails every hour. `i.title` may also be nil. The code should fall back to description/summary and skip items with no content.

title: Kernel#open on a setting allows command execution
body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Kernel#open, which spawns a shell command when the string starts with `|`. An admin setting can therefore be escalated to arbitrary command execution on the server. `import_remote` uses the same `open(url)` pattern, including in the disqus importer on file-provided links. Use `URI.parse(url).open` or an HTTP client restricted to http/https instead.

title: Re-import crashes if the embedded post or topic was deleted
body:
When an embed already exists, `post = embed.post` is passed straight to `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!`. If moderators deleted the post, the `belongs_to` lookup returns nil and `revise!` raises NoMethodError. Each hourly feed poll for that item would then fail.

Similarly, `topic_id_for_embed` still returns the id of a deleted topic, so the embed endpoint builds a `TopicView` for it and errors instead of showing the page.

title: Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE throttle
body: The throttle calls `setnx` and then `expire` as two separate commands. If the process dies between them, the key never expires and that URL is permanently throttled. Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` atomically.

title: import_remote relies on open-uri being loaded elsewhere
body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url)` with an http URL but never requires 'open-uri'. It only works if poll_feed.rb (or something else) has already been loaded. Otherwise `open` treats the URL as a local file path and raises ENOENT, for example in the disqus thor task or in TopicRetriever when feed polling is disabled.

title: "404 without an embed_url" test passes for the wrong reason
body: No `embeddable_host` is stubbed in this test, so `ensure_embeddable` raises InvalidAccess before `params.require(:embed_url)` is ever reached. The test passes regardless of how a missing embed_url is handled. The same pattern affects poll_feed_spec: the url/username tests pass only because `feed_polling_enabled` defaults to false.

title: small-action button no longer floats right after container became flex
body: This PR makes `.small-action` a flex container (`@include flexbox()`). In a flex container, `float` on children is ignored, so `float: right` on the `button` rule no longer works. Nothing replaces it: there is no `margin-left: auto` and no `justify-content`. As a result, the edit/delete button in small-action posts now sits immediately after the description text instead of at the right edge. Add `margin-left: auto` to the button. `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` and `clear: both` are also dead code now.

title: Header panel alignment relies on auto margins unsupported by the legacy -webkit-box fallback
body: `float: right` on `.panel` was replaced by `margin-left: auto`. The new `flexbox()` mixin deliberately emits `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` for old browsers. The 2009 box model does not distribute auto margins, so in those browsers the panel (search, hamburger, user icons) is no longer pushed to the right. It ends up packed next to the title, which is a regression from the previous float layout. Either drop the legacy fallbacks or add a legacy-compatible way to push the panel right, such as `-webkit-box-flex` on the title or `-webkit-box-pack: justify`.

title: align-items mixin emits a nonexistent property and passes unmapped values to the old syntax
body: `-ms-align-items` is not a real property; IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`. The mixin also passes `$alignment` unchanged to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those properties only accept `start`/`end`/`center`/`baseline`/`stretch`, so any future call with `flex-start` or `flex-end` silently fails on the prefixed syntaxes. Remove the bogus property and map `flex-start`/`flex-end` to `start`/`end`.

title: Making .small-action a flex container breaks the floated button and avatar
body: `.small-action` now gets `display: flex` (line 264), but its children are still positioned with floats. `button { float: right; }` (line 309) and `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` (line 270) stop working, because `float` has no effect on flex items. The action button (e.g. undo/delete on small action posts) will no longer sit at the right edge; it will appear right after the description text. The trailing `clear: both` (line 312) is also a leftover from the float layout. Fix: give the button `margin-left: auto` (or put `flex: 1` on `.small-action-desc`) and drop the dead float rules.

title: Header panel right-alignment relies on auto margins, which the old -webkit-box/-moz-box fallbacks ignore
body: The `flexbox()` mixin emits the legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` values as fallbacks. The panel is now pushed right only by `margin-left: auto` (line 37), since its `float: right` was removed. The 2009 box model does not distribute auto margins, so any browser that falls back to the legacy box display shows the panel (notifications, user menu) next to the logo instead of at the right. Either drop the legacy prefixes or keep a fallback such as `-webkit-box-pack: justify` or a flexible spacer.

title: align-items mixin emits a non-existent -ms-align-items property
body: `-ms-align-items` (line 121) was never a real property; IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, which is already emitted on the line above. The extra declaration is dead output repeated everywhere the mixin is used and should be removed.

title: PR title/description do not match the change
body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance" but its description is only "Test 5". The change is a layout refactor from floats to flexbox across the header, small-action posts and category badges, with visual side effects. There is no performance work and no explanation or screenshots for reviewers. The description should state what layouts change and how they were verified.

title: float: right on .small-action button no longer applies once .small-action is a flex container
body: This PR makes `.small-action` a flex container via `@include flexbox()`. Browsers ignore `float` on flex items, so the `button { float: right; }` rule (and `float: left` on `.topic-avatar`) has no effect anymore. The button will sit directly after `.small-action-desc` instead of being pushed to the right edge, which is a visible layout regression. Add `margin-left: auto` (or a high `order` plus auto margin) to the button to keep the right alignment.

title: align-items mixin passes modern values to legacy properties that use a different value set
body: The mixin emits the same `$alignment` for `-webkit-box-align`, `-ms-flex-align` and `align-items`. The legacy properties use `start`/`end` where the modern syntax uses `flex-start`/`flex-end`. The two current callers pass `center` and `baseline`, which work everywhere. Any future `@include align-items(flex-start)` will silently produce invalid declarations in the legacy-prefixed browsers this mixin exists to support. The values should be mapped before being written to the legacy properties.

title: `-ms-align-items` is not a real property
body: IE10 only supports `-ms-flex-align`; no `-ms-align-items` property exists. This line is dead output in every compiled rule that uses the mixin and should be removed.

title: include_website_name lacks `?`, so website_name leaks for TL0 users seen by anonymous viewers
body:
ActiveModel::Serializers only honours filter methods named `include_<attr>?`. The method here is `include_website_name` with no question mark, so it is never consulted and `website_name` is always serialized.

On top of that, `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`. For a TL0 user viewed anonymously, `website` is hidden by `restrict_user_fields?`, but `website_name` still exposes the website host and, for same-domain sites, the full path. That defeats the anti-spam restriction on untrusted profile fields.

Fix: rename the method to `include_website_name?` and make it apply the same `restrict_user_fields?` check, e.g. by adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`.

title: Untrusted-attribute spec does not cover the new website_name field
body:
The TL0/anonymous spec checks that untrusted attributes are absent, but its list does not include `website_name`. As a result, the leak of the website host and path to anonymous viewers goes untested.

The new specs also never exercise the sibling-subdomain branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com) or the `website_host.nil?` path.

title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic treats unrelated domains under multi-part TLDs as the same site
body:
The sibling branch decides two hosts belong to the same site by stripping only the first label from each and comparing the rest. Unrelated sites under multi-part public suffixes therefore match: `foo.co.uk` vs `bar.co.uk` compares `co.uk == co.uk` and shows the full URL path. Likewise `a.github.io` vs `b.github.io` would match.

The display is then inconsistent with the intent of only showing the full path for the instance's own domain.

title: website_name bypasses the TL0 untrusted-attribute restriction
body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is hidden when an anonymous viewer looks at a TL0 user (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`). The new `website_name` attribute is not in that list, so it is still serialized and leaks the host and path of the same website. The profile template now renders whenever `model.website_name` is present, so TL0 spam-account websites become visible to anonymous visitors again. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`, or have its include check honor `restrict_user_fields?`.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?', so it is never used
body: ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_<attr>?` methods. `include_website_name` has no `?`, so it is dead code and `website_name` is always included, as nil when there is no website. It should be `include_website_name?`. Even then it should also apply the untrusted-user restriction that the other website fields use.

title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic treats unrelated domains on multi-part TLDs as same site
body: The equal-label-count branch drops only the first label and compares the rest. For a forum at `forum.co.uk` and a website `http://evil.co.uk/path`, both reduce to `co.uk` and are treated as the same domain, so the full path is shown for an unrelated site. The same thing happens for any two hosts that share only a public suffix, such as `a.github.io` and `b.github.io`. The 'same domain' check needs a public-suffix-aware comparison, or should be limited to exact host and parent-domain matches.

title: Untrusted-attributes spec does not cover website_name
body: The TL0 anonymous spec only checks `bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background`. It passes even though `website_name` now exposes the website for TL0 users. The TL0 fixture also has no website set, so the leak is never exercised. Set a website in that fixture and add `website_name` to the checked list.

title: `include_website_name` lacks `?`, so `website_name` is always serialized and bypasses TL0 hiding
body:
ActiveModel::Serializers only looks for `include_<attr>?` methods. `include_website_name` has no trailing `?`, so it is never called and `website_name` is serialized for every user.

The raw `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is hidden for TL0 users seen by anonymous visitors (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`). `website_name` is not in that list and has no working filter. Anonymous visitors therefore receive the website host, and now also its path, for TL0 users. This defeats the spam-mitigation intent of hiding untrusted fields.

In the template, `{{#if model.website_name}}` will also render a globe and a link with an empty href for these users.

Fix: add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`, or define `include_website_name?` with the same restriction check.

title: Untrusted-attributes spec doesn't cover new `website_name` field
body: The TL0/anonymous spec still checks only the old untrusted attribute list. Because `website_name` is missing from it, the spec does not catch that `website_name` is exposed to anonymous visitors for TL0 users. Add `website_name` to the list.

title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic treats unrelated domains under public suffixes as the same site
body: The same-length branch compares everything after the first label. A forum at `forum.co.uk` would treat any `anything.co.uk` website as the same site. A forum at `forum.github.io` would do the same for any `x.github.io`. In those cases the full URL path of an unrelated external site is shown as if it were on the instance's own domain. Comparing registrable domains (public-suffix aware) would avoid this.

title: Embedded post author link colour flipped from 30% to 70% lightness in light themes
body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original value for light themes and uses the complement for dark ones. Here the arguments are swapped: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. As a result, `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` becomes much paler in light themes. It should be `(…$primary 30%, …$secondary 70%)`.

title: custom-message-length colour inverted for light themes
body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new rule uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` for light themes and `$secondary 70%` for dark. The values were swapped, so this hint text becomes much darker on mobile light themes. The desktop version keeps 70%/30%. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

title: Topic map h3 light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
body: The original `.topic-map h3` colour was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The conversion uses 50%/50%, which changes the existing light-theme appearance. The PR is only meant to add a dark variant. It should be `(…$primary 20%, …$secondary 80%)`, matching the desktop file.

title: group-member-info .name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses 50%/50%, which lightens member names in light themes. This is an unintended visual regression. It should be `(…$primary 30%, …$secondary 70%)`.

title: group-member-info .name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: This has the same error as in the desktop user.scss file. The original value of 30% was replaced with `dark-light-choose(…50%, …50%)`, which changes the light-theme colour. It should be `(…$primary 30%, …$secondary 70%)`.

title: Missed conversion: categories badge-notification still uses $primary only
body: The rule `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification { color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) }` was left unconverted. In dark themes this produces the low-contrast colour this PR is trying to fix. It should be wrapped in `dark-light-choose` like the identical rules elsewhere in the PR.

title: Light-theme color for embedded post author links changed from 30% to 70%
body: `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. It is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so the two values were swapped. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original percentage as the light value and uses its complement for the dark value. Here light themes now render these author names much paler (70% instead of 30%). The intended value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Light-theme `.custom-message-length` color changed from 70% to 30%
body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, so the percentages were inverted. On light mobile themes the flag-message length hint becomes much darker than before, which is an unintended regression. Desktop `modal.scss` correctly uses 70%/30% for the same selector. The mobile value should match: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

title: Mobile topic-map h3 light color changed from 20% to 50%
body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This changes the appearance on light themes, which this PR should not affect; the heading becomes noticeably lighter. The desktop counterpart correctly uses 20%/80%. The mobile value should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

title: group-member-info .name light color changed from 30% to 50%
body: `.group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This silently lightens member names on light themes and removes the visual distinction from `.title`, which also uses 50%. To preserve the light-theme look it should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Mobile group-member-info .name light color changed from 30% to 50%
body: This has the same issue as the desktop file. The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, and the new light-theme value is 50% with a 50% dark value. Light-theme rendering changes and member names now look the same as titles. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Light-theme color for embedded post author links changed from 30% to 70% lightness
body: The original rule for `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. It now uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original value as the light branch and uses the complement (100-X) on `$secondary` for the dark branch. Here the light-theme value changed from 30% to 70%, so these bold author names become much paler on light themes. The expected form is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: group-member-info .name light value changed from 30% to 50%
body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses 50% on `$primary` and 50% on `$secondary`, which looks copy-pasted from the adjacent `.title` rule. On light themes the member name is now lighter and no longer visually distinct from the title. The expected form is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Mobile group-member-info .name light value changed from 30% to 50%
body: This is the same copy-paste issue as in the desktop stylesheet. The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` but the new light branch uses 50%. On light themes the name now renders the same as the title instead of darker. The expected form is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Mobile custom-message-length light/dark values inverted
body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which looks like the arguments were swapped. On light themes the hint text becomes much darker than before, which is a regression unrelated to dark-theme support. It also disagrees with the desktop version of the same rule, which uses 70%/30%.

title: Mobile topic-map h3 light value changed from 20% to 50%
body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The replacement uses 50% on `$primary` and 50% on `$secondary`, so on light themes the topic-map headings become noticeably lighter. The desktop counterpart keeps 20%/80%. The expected form is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

title: totalPages off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When the count divides evenly by the limit, this reports one page too many. For example, 50 members with limit 50 shows "1/2", and 100 members shows "1/3". Clicking next then requests offset=user_count, which renders an empty member list, and `showingLast` never matches on the last real page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

title: Public members endpoint accepts unbounded/negative limit and offset
body: `limit` and `offset` come straight from params with no clamping on this non-admin endpoint. Anyone who can see a group can pass `limit=10000000` and force loading and serializing every member of a huge automatic group (e.g. trust_level_0). A negative `limit` or `offset` reaches Postgres, which rejects a negative OFFSET or LIMIT and returns a 500. Clamp `limit` to a sane maximum (e.g. 1..200) and `offset` to >= 0.

title: remove_member bypasses Group#remove and model callbacks
body: The previous code removed members via `group.remove(user)`. The new code uses `group.users.delete(user_id)`, and on a has_many :through association this defaults to a delete_all strategy that skips GroupUser destroy callbacks. Any cleanup tied to leaving a group can be silently skipped, such as clearing the user's primary_group or title, or keeping user_count in sync. If the user is not a member, `find` raises RecordNotFound, producing a 404 rather than a clean error. Use `group.remove(user)` with an explicit user lookup.

title: Breaking change to admin groups API without compatibility
body: `create` and `update` now read flat params (`params[:name]`) instead of the nested `params[:group][...]`. Membership via `usernames` on create/update and the PATCH `changes: {add:, delete:}` interface were removed. Existing API consumers will silently lose updates: nested params are ignored, `visible` is reset to false because `params[:visible]` is nil, and their membership changes no longer apply. The removed `get "users"` route also breaks any caller using it. This should be documented or kept backward compatible.

title: create ignores alias_level sent by the form
body: The new form shows the alias level combo-box when creating a group, and `asJSON` sends `alias_level`, but `create` only sets `name` and `visible`. Any alias level chosen at creation is silently discarded until the group is saved again.

title: remove_member spec uses wrong HTTP verb and relies on id 1 being automatic
body: The test "cannot remove members from automatic groups" issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route is `delete "members"`, so it does not exercise the real request. Several new specs (`update` with id: 1, `add_members`/`remove_member` with group_id: 1) also depend implicitly on group id 1 existing and being automatic. That makes them fragile across fixture or seed changes. Fabricate an automatic group explicitly and use the correct verb.

title: addMembers/removeMember have no error handling
body: Neither the model nor the controller actions handle rejection. If the server returns 422, for example for an automatic group, the error is swallowed and the admin gets no feedback. The added usernames also stay in the input; the TODO acknowledges this.

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
body:
`totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When the count divides evenly, this reports one page too many. For example, 50 members with limit 50 gives 2 pages, and 100 members gives 3.

As a result, `showingLast` is false on the real last page and the UI shows '1/2'. Clicking next moves `offset` to `user_count` and loads an empty member list.

Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead.

title: Unbounded, unvalidated limit/offset on public members endpoint
body:
`limit` and `offset` are taken straight from user params, with no cap and no lower bound. This endpoint is reachable by any user who can see the group, not just admins.

- A request with `limit=10000000` serializes every member of a huge automatic group such as trust_level_0. That is an easy way to load the database and app server.
- A negative `limit` or `offset` is passed to Postgres. Postgres rejects negative LIMIT/OFFSET, so the request fails with a 500.

Clamp `limit` to a sane maximum (e.g. 1..200) and clamp `offset` to >= 0.

title: Breaking change to /groups/:id/members response shape
body:
The endpoint used to return a bare JSON array of users. It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {...}}`, and non-automatic groups are now paginated to 50 by default where previously the full list was returned.

Any other client of this endpoint will silently break or receive truncated data. That includes external API consumers, plugins, and other front-end code that calls `/groups/:name/members` and expects an array.

The change and default limit should be documented, or existing consumers audited.

title: Admin create/update no longer accept nested `group[...]` params or usernames
body:
`create` and `update` now read top-level `params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`, and so on instead of `params[:group][...]`. The `usernames` and PATCH `changes` interfaces were removed.

API clients that still send nested `group` params will create groups with an empty name, which fails validation. On update they will silently reset `visible` to false, because `params[:visible]` is nil.

This is an unannounced breaking change to the admin API.

title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
body:
The route for `remove_member` is `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members`, but the 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' spec sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`. Controller specs don't enforce the verb, so the spec passes without exercising the request as the client actually sends it.

Use `xhr :delete` to match the route.

title: No error handling for addMembers/removeMember failures
body:
`addMembers` and `removeMember` only handle success. The controller actions `addMembers` and `removeMember` never attach a rejection handler either.

If the server returns 422 (e.g. for an automatic group) or a save error, the admin gets no feedback and the promise rejection goes unhandled. In addition, the username input is never cleared after a successful add, as the TODO acknowledges, so pressing Add again re-submits the same users.

title: totalPages off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
body:
`totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, this reports one page too many. For example, 50 members with limit 50 shows "1/2".

Because `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to `totalPages`, the next button stays enabled. Clicking it sets `offset = min(offset+limit, user_count) = 50` and loads an empty page.

The fix is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

title: Public members endpoint accepts unbounded/negative limit and offset
body:
`/groups/:id/members` is a public, non-admin endpoint. It now takes `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` with no clamping, and applies them to every group.

- Any visitor can pass `limit=10000000` and force serialization of every member of a huge group such as trust_level_0. The old code capped automatic groups at a default of 200.
- A negative `limit` or `offset` makes PostgreSQL raise "LIMIT/OFFSET must not be negative", which returns a 500.

Clamp `limit` to a sane maximum and floor both values at 0.

title: Members endpoint response shape changed from array to object
body:
`GET /groups/:name/members.json` used to return a JSON array of users. It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {...}}`.

This breaks any existing API consumers, plugins, or other client code that iterate the response as an array. The change is made without versioning or a compatibility path.

title: Public group members page silently truncated to first 50 members
body:
The public group route now calls `model.findMembers()`, which requests only `limit: 50` from offset 0. Previously, non-automatic groups returned all members.

The public `group/members.hbs` template has no pagination controls (next/previous exist only in the admin template). Any group with more than 50 members now shows just the first 50, with no way to see the rest.

title: remove_member automatic-group test uses PUT instead of DELETE
body:
The route for `remove_member` is `delete "members"`, but this spec calls `xhr :put, :remove_member`. Controller specs bypass verb routing, so the test does not reflect the real request.

It should use `:delete`, consistent with the other `remove_member` test.

title: create ignores alias_level sent by the client
body:
The admin form lets the admin choose an alias level, and `asJSON` sends `alias_level` on create. However, `create` only sets `name` and `visible`, so the chosen alias level is dropped for new groups.

The value only takes effect after a second save, which goes through `update`.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded in the web request path, not in jobs or mailers
body: With the accelerator patch, translations load on demand. `I18n.translate` only loads `config.locale`, and the fallback locales (site default and `:en`) are loaded only by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`. That call happens solely in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks and other non-controller code never call it. In those contexts the Fallbacks backend looks up keys in locales that were never loaded and gets nil, so fallbacks silently do not work and users see 'translation missing' text. The fallback locales should be loaded inside `I18n.translate`/`load_locale`, not in a controller filter.

title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain, so stale or missing results stay cached
body: Results now depend on the fallback chain: `SiteSetting.default_locale`, plus which fallback locales happen to be loaded. The LRU cache key is still only key + `config.locale` + backend id. Two problems follow. (1) If the site's default locale changes, cached fallback strings from the old default locale keep being served until the process restarts or the entry is evicted. (2) If a key is translated before the fallback locales are loaded (e.g. outside a controller), the 'translation missing' result is frozen into the cache. It is then returned even after the fallback locales are loaded. The cache key should include the fallback chain, or the cache should be cleared when the default locale changes.

title: SiteSetting lookup on every fallback resolution
body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` builds a new array and reads `SiteSetting.default_locale` on every call. The Fallbacks backend calls it on every uncached translate, which includes every translate call that has interpolation or count arguments, since those bypass the LRU cache. This allocates a new array on every one of those calls and adds avoidable overhead to a very hot path.

title: No tests for new fallback behavior
body: The PR changes translation resolution for every locale but adds no specs. Untested cases include: fallback to the site locale then to English, loading of the fallback locales, and behavior in non-request contexts. Regressions such as the missing-load issue in jobs would go unnoticed.

title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain (site default locale)
body:
With fallbacks enabled, the result of `I18n.t(key)` now depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, not only on `config.locale`. The LRU cache key is still only `key + locale + backend.object_id`.

After an admin changes the default locale, keys that fell back are still served from the old fallback locale until the cache evicts them.

In a multisite deployment the cache is process-wide, so one site's fallback translations are returned to other sites that have a different default locale.

Fix: include the fallback chain (or the site default locale) in the cache key.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded in the controller filter; jobs/mailers miss them and cache the miss
body:
`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is called only from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. `I18n.translate` itself only loads `config.locale`.

Code that translates outside a controller request, such as Sidekiq jobs, mailers and rake tasks, gets a fallback chain that points at locales that may never have been loaded. Fallback then quietly fails and returns 'translation missing'.

Worse, the no-args path caches that result in the LRU cache and freezes it. The missing string keeps being served even after the fallback locale is loaded later in the same process.

Fix: load the fallback locales inside `translate` (or `load_locale`) rather than relying on a controller filter.

title: No tests for the new fallback behavior
Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain, so stale or cross-site translations are served
body:
The LRU cache key is built only from `key`, `config.locale` and the backend's `object_id`. With this PR, the value returned for a missing key depends on the fallback chain `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]`. The site's default locale is not part of the key.

In multisite, one process serves sites with different `default_locale` values. A string resolved through site A's default locale gets cached and is then returned to site B, which should have fallen back to its own default.

The same happens on a single site: after an admin changes `default_locale`, cached fallback strings keep the old language until the LRU entry is evicted.

Fix: include the default locale (or the whole fallback chain) in the cache key, or clear the cache when the setting changes.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded in ApplicationController, not in jobs or other entry points
body:
`translate` lazily loads only `config.locale`. The fallback locales (site default and :en) are loaded only by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` inside `ApplicationController#set_locale`.

Code that sets `I18n.locale` and translates outside a controller never loads them. That includes Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, and controllers or middleware that skip `set_locale`.

In those paths a key missing from the user's locale finds no data in the fallback locales and returns a 'translation missing' string, even though fallbacks are configured.

Fix: load the fallback locales from inside `translate`/`load_locale` instead of relying on the controller hook.

title: SiteSetting is read and a new array allocated on every fallback lookup
body:
`FallbackLocaleList#[]` runs `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym`, builds a new array and calls `uniq`/`compact` each time it is invoked. The Fallbacks backend calls it on every uncached translation, i.e. any `I18n.t` call with interpolation or options.

This overrides Hash's memoizing behaviour and puts a SiteSetting lookup plus several allocations on a very hot path.

title: No tests for the new fallback behaviour
Denials are cached for 30s and checked before any requery, reintroducing the stale-access problem
body: A denied Check stores a denial entry for shortCacheTTL (30s). That entry is read at the top of Check, before the cached permissions and before the DB fallback. If a check runs in the window before a newly created dashboard/folder's permission rows are visible, the denial is cached. The same happens when an admin grants access to a resource the user was just denied. In both cases every later Check for that resource returns denied for up to 30s without consulting the DB. The DB requery, which this PR adds specifically to fix creator access, is skipped. Nothing invalidates denial entries when permissions change.

title: DB fallback still uses the cached folder tree, so access via a newly created parent folder is denied and the denial cached
body: On a cache miss or stale-cache deny, Check re-fetches permissions from the DB. checkPermission then calls checkInheritedPermissions, which uses buildFolderTree, served from folderCache (30s TTL). A folder created after the tree was cached has no ancestors in that tree. If the user's grant is on an ancestor of the new folder, the check fails even with fresh permissions, and the result is written to the denial cache. Newly created folder hierarchies therefore still yield false denials for up to 30s, which is the scenario this PR is meant to fix.

title: Denial cache key is ambiguous because '_' can appear inside names and folder UIDs
body: userPermDenialCacheKey joins name and parent with '_', and resource names and folder UIDs may contain underscores. For example, (name="a_b", parent="") and (name="a", parent="b_") both produce "..._a_b_". A denial recorded for one resource/folder pair is then returned for a different one, giving a false deny for up to 30s. Use a separator that cannot occur in these values, or encode the components.

title: Every deny on cached permissions now triggers a full DB permission query
body: Previously a warm permCache answered Check entirely from cache. Now any check that is denied from cached permissions falls through to getIdentityPermissions. That path issues team, basic-role and permission queries; getUserPermissions no longer consults the cache. Singleflight only collapses concurrent identical requests, and the denial cache is per resource. A user checked against many resources they cannot access, such as filtering a dashboard list with per-item Check, now causes one DB round trip per denied resource every 30s. This can substantially increase DB load.

title: List still serves stale cached permissions, so newly created resources are missing from listings
body: List returns the cached permission map whenever one exists and never requeries. A dashboard or folder the user just created (and only has a direct grant on) will not appear in List results for up to 30s. This is inconsistent with Check, which now falls back to the DB, and leaves part of the described problem unfixed.

title: Denial-cache test does not prove the denial cache short-circuits
body: The comment says the permCache entry grants access, but it sets {"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}. checkPermission treats that as not allowed. The DB fallback also returns no permissions, because the default fakeStore has none. The test would therefore pass with the denial cache removed entirely. The cache entry should be true, and the store should grant access, so the test actually verifies the short-circuit.

title: Every new denied resource now bypasses the permission cache and queries the DB
body:
When cached permissions exist but do not grant access, `Check` falls through to `getIdentityPermissions`. That function no longer consults `permCache`, so it always runs the basic-role, team and permission queries against the DB.

The denial cache only short-circuits repeats of the exact (user, action, name, folder) tuple. A user checked against many distinct resources they cannot access triggers a full permission query per resource, for example when filtering a search result set dashboard by dashboard. Singleflight only dedups concurrent identical calls.

Before this change those checks were served from `permCache`. This can multiply DB load substantially for users with restricted access.

title: Requery does not refresh the stale folder tree, so newly created folders still deny and the denial gets cached
body:
The DB fallback only refreshes the permission scope map. `checkInheritedPermissions` still uses `buildFolderTree`, which is served from `folderCache` (30s TTL).

Scenario: a dashboard sits in a newly created folder whose ancestor grants access. The new folder is missing from the cached tree, so `Ancestors(req.ParentFolder)` yields nothing and the check is denied. That denial is then written to `permDenialCache`, extending the wrong answer.

This is part of the scenario the PR claims to fix (newly created folders) and it remains broken. On a miss, the folder tree should also be refreshed, or the denial should not be cached when the parent folder is absent from the tree.

title: Denial cache pins stale denials for 30s, undermining the 'requery on miss' fix
body:
Any denial is cached for `shortCacheTTL` (30s), and the denial cache is checked before anything else.

If a check for a resource happens before its permissions are written, the denial sticks. This can occur during a create flow or right before a share or grant. Every subsequent check for that resource then returns denied for 30s without consulting the DB, even after the permission exists.

This reintroduces the delay the PR is trying to eliminate for newly created dashboards and folders. Nothing invalidates the entry when permissions are granted.

title: Ambiguous denial cache key can deny unrelated resources
body:
`userPermDenialCacheKey` joins name and parent with `_` and no escaping. Resource names and folder UIDs may legitimately contain underscores.

For example, (name="a_b", parent="") and (name="a", parent="b") produce the same key. A cached denial for one resource then wrongly denies access to the other.

The key also shares the `.perm_` prefix with `userPermCacheKey` in the same cache backend, which increases collision risk with differently typed entries. Use a distinct prefix and an unambiguous separator or encoding.

title: Denial-cache test does not prove the cache short-circuits
body:
The test claims to "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but it seeds `permCache` with `{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`. A false value is not a grant in `checkPermission`.

The default fake store also returns no permissions. So the request would be denied even if the denial cache were ignored, and the test passes regardless of whether `permDenialCache` works.

The cached value should be `true`, and ideally the test should assert the store was not called.

title: Denial cache short-circuits the DB re-query, so stale denials persist after permissions are granted
body:
Check now consults `permDenialCache` before anything else and returns `Allowed:false` on a hit, without re-querying the database. Any deny is stored for `shortCacheTTL` (30s) and never invalidated.

If a check runs before a permission exists, that user/resource pair stays denied for 30s even after the grant is written. Examples: a dashboard creator whose managed permission is written just after the first check, or an admin granting access. The 'requery permissions from DB on miss' fallback, which is the stated goal of the PR, never runs during that window.

Consider not caching denials for resources newly seen in the request, using a much shorter TTL, or invalidating denials when permissions change.

title: Denial cache key is ambiguous because '_' can appear in UIDs
body:
`userPermDenialCacheKey` joins userUID, action, name and parent with "_". Grafana UIDs may contain underscores, so different (name, parent) pairs can produce the same key. For example, name="a_b", parent="" and name="a", parent="b_" both end in "_a_b_". A denial for one resource can then wrongly deny another.

The key also shares the ".perm_<uid>_<action>" prefix with `userPermCacheKey` in the same underlying cache, which risks cross-type collisions that only surface as unmarshal warnings.

Use a distinct prefix (e.g. ".perm_denial_") and a separator that cannot appear in UIDs, or escape/encode the components.

title: Denial-cache test does not prove the denial short-circuits evaluation
body:
The test comments that it seeds an allowing permission to prove the cached permissions are not checked. It actually sets `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`, which `checkPermission` treats as no permission.

The store is the default empty fakeStore, so the DB fallback would also deny. The assertion therefore passes even if the denial cache were never consulted.

Seed `true` (and/or DB permissions that would allow), and assert the store was not called.

title: Federated rule group check dropped for legacy CombinedRule abilities
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` used to mark rules as immutable when `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` was true. It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `isFederated = false`. In the legacy list and detail views, Mimir federated rule groups will now show Update/Delete/Pause actions as supported, letting users try to edit or delete rules that should be read-only.

title: Delete and Pause are never shown in the new list view
body: The new list view no longer passes `rulerRule`. `canDelete` and `canPause` can be true from the prom-rule abilities, but the menu items are still gated on `rulerRule` existing (`canDelete && rulerRule`, and `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` for pause). Users with delete or edit permission therefore lose the Delete and Pause actions in the list view. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test asserts exactly 4 menu items while delete permissions are granted, which hides this regression.

title: Silence menu item does nothing when only promRule is available
body: In the list view `canSilence` is computed from the prom rule, so the 'Silence notifications' item is shown. Clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer`, but the drawer only renders when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true. `rule` is now undefined in the list view, so clicking the item silently does nothing.

title: Missing React key on GrafanaRuleListItem in rules.map
body: The previous `GrafanaRuleLoader` was rendered with `key={key}`, but the replacement `GrafanaRuleListItem` has no key. This causes React key warnings. It can also make React reconcile list items incorrectly as results are appended, for example reusing the wrong component state such as an open menu, drawer or modal for a different rule.

title: Export and Pause disabled for Grafana recording rules in prom-based abilities
body: The ruler-based abilities use `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule`, which is true for any Grafana rule including recording rules. The new prom-based abilities use `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` for ModifyExport, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently. As a result, Grafana-managed recording rules in the new list view can no longer be exported or paused, which is a behavioural regression.

title: Rule view link no longer includes returnTo
body: The old item built the href with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`. The new one omits `returnTo`. After opening a rule from a filtered or searched list, the back navigation in the rule viewer no longer returns the user to their filtered list.

title: Missing `key` prop on GrafanaRuleListItem in rule list map
body: `GrafanaRuleLoader` was replaced with `GrafanaRuleListItem`, but the `key={key}` prop was dropped. The other branches in this `rules.map` still pass a key. React will warn about missing keys. Worse, items are reconciled by index while new pages are concatenated, so per-item state such as open menus, the silence drawer, and the delete modal can attach to the wrong rule.

title: Delete and Pause never shown in list view despite prom-based permission checks
body: `canDelete` and `canPause` now OR in the promRule-based abilities. However, the Delete item still requires `rulerRule` to be present (line 165), and the Pause item requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123). The list view no longer passes `rulerRule`, so users with full permissions lose the Delete and Pause actions there. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test asserts exactly 4 menu items, which locks this regression in.

title: Silence menu item shown but does nothing when only promRule is provided
body: In the list view, AlertRuleMenu shows 'Silence notifications' based on the promRule abilities. Clicking it only sets `showSilenceDrawer`. The drawer renders only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, and `rule` (the ruler rule) is now undefined in the list view. The button is therefore a silent no-op for users.

title: Federated rule group detection removed from legacy ability hook
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(CombinedRule)` previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`. It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `isFederated = false`. Federated Mimir rule groups in the existing (V1) list and detail views are no longer treated as immutable. Update, Delete and Pause become supported for them.

title: Export/Pause/Restore restricted to alerting rules for Grafana prom rules
body: The ruler-based hook gates ModifyExport, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently on `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule`, which is true for any Grafana rule, including recording rules. The new prom-based hook uses `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` instead. As a result, Grafana-managed recording rules can no longer be exported or paused from the list view. The variable name suggests 'Grafana-managed' was intended.

title: Rule view link lost `returnTo` parameter
body: The removed implementation built the href with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`. The new component drops `returnTo`, so navigating back from the rule detail page no longer returns users to their filtered or scrolled list position.

title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered in a list without a key
body: The `grafana` branch of `rules.map` returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` without `key={key}`. The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` had one, and the `datasource` and default branches still pass one. The list grows incrementally through infinite scroll, so React falls back to index-based reconciliation. This causes key warnings and can attach component state (open menus, the silence drawer, the delete modal) to the wrong rule as items are appended.

title: Delete and Pause are never shown in the list view even when the prom abilities allow them
body: `canDelete`/`canPause` can now be true from `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`. However, the Delete item is still gated by `rulerRule &&` and the Pause item by `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123). The list view now passes only `promRule`, so users with delete or update permission can no longer delete or pause rules from the list. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test grants AlertingRuleDelete yet asserts exactly 4 menu items, which locks this regression in.

title: Silence menu item does nothing when only promRule is available
body: The menu shows 'Silence notifications' based on prom abilities, and clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer`. The drawer itself only renders when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true. In the list view `rule` (the ruler rule) is now always undefined, so clicking Silence silently does nothing.

title: Federated rule check dropped from legacy useAllAlertRuleAbilities
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(CombinedRule)` previously used `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` to mark rules immutable. It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `isFederated = false`. Federated Mimir rules shown in the legacy list and detail views now report Update, Delete and Pause as supported, allowing edits that shouldn't be offered.

title: Prom-based abilities exclude Grafana recording rules from Export/Pause/Restore
body: The ruler-based version gated ModifyExport, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently on `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule`, which covers recording rules too. The prom version uses `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, which is false for Grafana recording rules. In the new list view, recording rules lose the Export (and Pause) actions. The comment above says 'All GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed', which suggests `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule` was intended.

title: returnTo parameter dropped from rule view link
body: The removed implementation built the href with `createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo: createReturnTo() })`. The new item omits `returnTo`, so after opening a rule from a filtered or grouped list, the view page's back navigation no longer returns to the user's previous list state.

title: Stale doc comments still reference Ruler loading
body: The doc comment still says the group is loaded 'from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints', but the Ruler query was removed. Similarly, the comment in prometheusGroupsGenerator.ts about preloading ruler rules (and the variable name `cacheAndRulerPreload`) no longer reflects the code, since the ruler prefetch was deleted.

title: $__range detection runs on interpolated expr, so range-variable queries are now split
body: `runSplitQuery` now calls `applyTemplateVariables` on every query before partitioning. `querySupportsSplitting()` then calls `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` on the result. That function looks for the literal `$__range` text, which `templateSrv.replace` has already substituted, so the check no longer matches. Queries using `$__range`/`$__range_s`/`$__range_ms` will be split into daily chunks. As the code comment explains, those queries must not be split. Each chunk then evaluates a range-sized window and the merged result is wrong (e.g. `count_over_time(...[$__range])` summed over chunks). Run the splitting check on the raw target expression before interpolation, or keep the original expr around for it.

title: Queries are interpolated and ad-hoc filters applied multiple times
body:
The splitter now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)`. The sub-requests then go through `datasource.runQuery` (DataSourceWithBackend.query), which calls `applyTemplateVariables` again on each target with the same `filters`. In the sharding path it happens three times: `runShardSplitQuery`, then `runSplitQuery`, then the backend query. The test now asserts 5 calls.

Re-applying ad-hoc filters can add duplicate label matchers or filter stages. Re-interpolating an already interpolated expression can expand `$`-sequences that came from variable values, and can double-escape regex-escaped values. Interpolate once, or strip `filters`/scopedVars from the sub-request so later stages don't re-apply them.

title: Empty-expr filter now runs before interpolation
body: Previously `interpolateVariablesInQueries` ran first and the `query.expr` filter ran on the interpolated result. Now the filter runs on the raw expr and interpolation happens afterwards. A query whose expr is just a variable that resolves to an empty string is no longer dropped and gets sent for execution and sharding. The same ordering applies in `runSplitQuery`. Filter on the interpolated expr instead.

title: Shard splitting interpolates queries again downstream, so ad hoc filters can be added more than once
body:
`runShardSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on each target. It then passes each sub-request to `runSplitQuery`, which calls `applyTemplateVariables` again with the same `request.filters` (querySplitting.ts:299). After that, `datasource.runQuery`, which goes through the backend `query` path, normally applies template variables a third time.

The old code used `interpolateVariablesInQueries(targets, scopedVars)` and did not pass `filters`. The new call does pass `request.filters`. Loki's `applyTemplateVariables` appends ad hoc filters to the expression, so running it repeatedly can add the same label matchers or label filters more than once (e.g. `| key="v"` repeated) unless every path is idempotent.

Re-interpolation also means a substituted variable value that itself contains `$name` or `${...}` text gets interpolated a second time.

The test 'Interpolates queries before running' asserts `applyTemplateVariables` is called 5 times (1 + 4 sub-requests), which bakes in this double interpolation instead of catching it.

Fix: interpolate once at the entry point, for example by letting `runSplitQuery` skip interpolation when called from the shard path or via an option, and drop `filters` from the pre-interpolation if the backend path already applies them.

title: Front-loaded interpolation passes ad hoc filters that the backend query path likely applies again
body:
`runSplitQuery` now runs `applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on every target before splitting. The resulting sub-requests keep `filters` (`{ ...request, targets }`) and are sent through `datasource.runQuery`. That backend `query` path normally calls `applyTemplateVariables` per target again with the request's filters.

As a result, ad hoc filters and variable substitution run twice on the already-interpolated expressions. Depending on how ad hoc filters are merged, this can duplicate filters in the final LogQL. It also re-processes values that were already substituted.

Only `$__auto`/`$step` need to be resolved before splitting. Consider interpolating without `filters`, or stripping `filters`/`scopedVars` from the sub-requests, so the backend path does not apply them again.

title: Template variables and ad hoc filters are now applied twice per query
body:
`runSplitQuery` now runs `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on every target. The sub-requests then go to `datasource.runQuery`, whose backend query path runs `applyTemplateVariables` on each target again.

Interpolation is therefore not a single pass:
- The ad hoc filters in `request.filters` are injected twice, for example `{a="b", k="v", k="v"}` or a duplicated `| k="v"` stage.
- Variable values that contain `$...` text are re-interpolated after the first pass.

The result is altered or bloated LogQL that differs from what the user configured. Either interpolate once and skip it downstream, or interpolate a copy only for classification (log vs. metric, step, selector) and send the original targets.

title: Shard splitting interpolates again before delegating to runSplitQuery, which interpolates again
body:
`runShardSplitQuery` calls `applyTemplateVariables` with `request.filters` and passes the result to `splitQueriesByStreamShard`. That function calls `runSplitQuery(datasource, subRequest)`, which now calls `applyTemplateVariables` again with the same `subRequest.filters`. Finally `datasource.runQuery` applies it a third time.

The previous code used `interpolateVariablesInQueries` without filters, so ad hoc filters were added only once. Now the same filters can be injected two or three times into each sharded query, and variable output gets re-interpolated.

The updated test even locks this in by expecting `applyTemplateVariables` to be called 5 times for a single target (line 112). Its mock is idempotent, so the repeated application is hidden.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so logs written through it are never recorded
body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, a new instance unrelated to the receiver. `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. When a test injects a `*TestLogger` and then checks `InfoLogs.Calls` or `InfoLogs.Ctx` on it, the log entries go to the throwaway instance and the test sees zero calls. That makes `TestLogger` unusable for verifying `LoggerMiddleware`, or anything else that logs through `FromContext`. Returning `f` (or a logger that shares the same `Logs` storage) would keep the recordings.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware and the changed LoggerMiddleware fields have no tests
body: The plugin/request log fields (pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, uname) used to be added explicitly in `LoggerMiddleware`. They now depend on `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` setting contextual attributes, and on that middleware sitting before `LoggerMiddleware` in the chain. No test checks that `instrumentContext` sets these attributes or that the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line still carries them and the traceID. A reordering or a regression in `FromContext` would silently strip these fields from the data-egress logs.

title: Adding FromContext to the exported Logger interface breaks other implementations
body: `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` is now a required method on the exported `plog.Logger` interface. Any other implementation of `plog.Logger` stops compiling until it adds this method. That includes fakes and wrappers in other packages and in enterprise or external code. The change goes beyond the rename the PR title describes.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so log calls through it are lost
body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver `f`. `LoggerMiddleware` now always logs through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. As a result, any test that injects a `TestLogger` and asserts on `InfoLogs.Calls`, `Message` or `Ctx` will always see zero calls, because the call was recorded on a throwaway instance. Return `f`, or a logger that shares its recorded state, so the fake keeps recording when used through `FromContext`.

title: Adding FromContext to the exported Logger interface breaks other implementations
body: `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` is a new method on the widely used `plugins/log.Logger` interface. Every implementation outside the two updated here must now implement it or fail to compile. That includes other fakes and test loggers in the repo, enterprise code and external consumers. Check all implementers, or use a separate optional interface with a type assertion.

title: No tests for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware or the FromContext wiring
body: The pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID and uname fields used to be added explicitly by `LoggerMiddleware`. They now depend on two things: `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` setting contextual attributes, and `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` picking them up. The traceID field likewise now relies only on the contextual log provider. Nothing tests this path. If the middleware is reordered, or the type assertion in `FromContext` falls back to `d.New()`, the 'Plugin Request Completed' log lines would silently lose these fields. Add a test that checks the contextual attributes are present on the logged request.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so recorded calls are lost
body: `LoggerMiddleware` now logs through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. `TestLogger.FromContext` returns a brand-new `TestLogger`, so those calls are recorded on a throwaway instance. The `InfoLogs`/`ErrorLogs` counters on the logger a test injected are never updated. Any test that asserts the middleware logged "Plugin Request Completed" with a `TestLogger` will silently see zero calls. Returning `f` (the receiver) would keep the fake useful.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware and the new FromContext behavior have no tests
body: This PR moves pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID and uname from explicit log parameters into context attributes. These are now set by a new middleware and read back through the new `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext`. No test checks that the attributes reach the "Plugin Request Completed" log line. The fields now depend on middleware ordering: `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` must come before `LoggerMiddleware`. A future reordering would drop these fields from the data-egress log with nothing to catch it.

title: Device limit only enforced on first request; cache entry lets rejected devices in afterwards
body: `tagDeviceUI` writes the device key to the local cache before calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, and it does not remove the key when that call fails. When the limit is hit, the first request returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and `Authenticate` rejects it. Every later request from the same device in the next ~29 minutes hits the cache and returns nil, so `Authenticate` succeeds.
