- When an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS permission exists, the returned set contains a non-group id. `UsersResource.searchForUser` and `getUsersCount` pass it as the `UserModel.GROUPS` filter, so searches and counts return zero users.

title: Possible NPE when the all-groups resource is not resolved
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource` returns null when the schema is not supported, for example when `realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled()` is false while the admin-permissions client still exists. The result is passed straight to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later dereferenced via `resource.getScopes()`. In that state any group permission check that falls back to all-groups throws a NullPointerException, which surfaces as a 500. The code should return false when `resource` is null.

title: Group removal listener calls a V2 method that throws UnsupportedOperationException
body: When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, the listener calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)` on GroupRemovedEvent. If ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is also enabled, `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`, whose new `GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws UnsupportedOperationException. Deleting any group then fails. Separately, V2 has no cleanup of per-group resources (named by group id) on group deletion, so orphaned resources remain.

title: Wrong javadoc reference for requireManageMembers
body: The javadoc for `requireManageMembers` says it throws if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false. The implementation actually checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`, so the reference is wrong.

title: canManage() javadoc documents VIEW as granting manage
body: The javadoc for `canManage()` says that in V2, having VIEW or MANAGE on groups grants manage. This documents the incorrect behaviour described above. Only MANAGE should grant manage.

title: canManage() is granted to callers who only have VIEW on all groups
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` evaluates `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`. Because any matching scope grants access, an admin with only an all-groups VIEW permission passes `requireManage()`. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` relies on that check, so a view-only admin can create top-level groups or move existing groups to the top level. This is a privilege escalation. Only `MANAGE` should be accepted here. The interface javadoc for `canManage()` repeats the same error ("VIEW or MANAGE") and should also be corrected.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs and misses per-group resources
body:
There are three problems in this method.

1. Per-group resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never get a type set. Only the schema's all-groups resource has type "Groups", so `findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` will not return per-group resources.
2. The callback passes `groupResource.getId()` (the authz resource id) into `hasPermission`. That method treats the value as a group id and calls `findByName`, so the lookup always falls back to the all-groups resource.
3. The callback adds `groupResource.getId()` to the result set. Group resources are named by group id, so the set holds resource ids rather than group ids.

Callers use this set as group ids: `UserModel.GROUPS` for user search and `getUsersCount(..., groupIds)`. As a result, user counts for group-scoped admins are wrong, and user search filtering by group either matches nothing or matches incorrectly. The new tests only pass because per-user `canView` filtering is applied afterwards on an unfiltered stream, which also breaks pagination. The method should use `resource.getName()` (the group id) and find per-group resources by a means that does not depend on their type.

title: V1 group-removal listener now hits UnsupportedOperationException under V2
body:
Before this change, `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` was inherited and returned the V1 `GroupPermissions`. It now returns `GroupPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`.

`AdminPermissions.registerListener` (active when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled) calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)` on every `GroupRemovedEvent`. When V2 is also enabled, `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`. In that configuration, deleting any group would fail with a 500.

V2 management should either no-op here or the listener should skip V2.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc references the wrong method
body: The javadoc for `requireManageMembers` says it throws if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false. The implementations actually check `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. Readers will be misled about which permission is enforced.

title: canManage() grants global group manage to holders of VIEW-only all-groups permission
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` evaluates `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so it returns true for an admin whose all-groups permission only grants the `view` scope. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` calls `requireManage()`, so a view-only admin can create top-level groups and move existing groups to top level. The check should require only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE`. The interface javadoc for `canManage()` repeats the same wrong "VIEW or MANAGE" statement and should be corrected too.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs, not group IDs, and resolves the wrong resource
body:
In V2, per-group resources are created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` with the group ID as the resource name and no type set. Only the 'Groups' all-resource has type `Groups`. As a result:
- `findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` does not enumerate the per-group resources.
- `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` passes a resource ID where a group ID (resource name) is expected, so `findByName` misses and evaluation falls back to the all-groups resource.
- `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` adds an authz resource ID instead of a group ID.

The returned set is used as `UserModel.GROUPS` in user search and in `getUsersCount`. Users counts and DB-level group filtering for admins with group-based view-members permissions will therefore be wrong: wrong counts, and pagination applied before the in-memory `canView` filter.

title: Possible NPE when the all-groups resource cannot be resolved
body: When no per-group resource exists, `getResourceTypeResource(...)` can return null. This happens if the realm does not have admin permissions enabled, or if the `Groups` resource is missing, for example in a realm whose admin-permissions client was initialized before the Groups type was added to the schema. The null is then passed to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later dereferenced via `resource.getScopes()`. Existing realms initialized with only the Users/Clients schema would hit this on any group permission check. Return false when `resource` is null.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc references the wrong method
body: The javadoc for `requireManageMembers` says it throws if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false. The implementation actually checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. The `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` javadoc also says it returns a "Stream" while the method returns a `Set`.

title: Java MessageFormat syntax in an i18next-rendered bundle breaks interpolation
body:
The account UI (keycloak.v3) renders these messages with i18next, which interpolates `{{0}}`-style placeholders. Every other error message in this file still uses `{{0}}`.

The new value `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` uses Java MessageFormat placeholders and a `choice` format. i18next does not understand either. Users will see the literal text `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` instead of the attribute name and limits.

The change appears to have been made only to satisfy the new HTML verifier, since the `<` inside the choice is whitelisted for this key. It should be reverted to the `{{0}}` form, or use i18next pluralization.

title: Admin UI message switched to Java MessageFormat, which i18next won't interpolate
body:
The admin UI (keycloak.v2) is a React app that uses i18next with `{{n}}` placeholders. `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` to `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` plus `{2,choice,...}`.

When the admin console shows this validation error, it will display raw placeholders and the choice pattern instead of the substituted values.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body:
`loginTotpStep1` in the Lithuanian (lt) bundle is now `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian. Lithuanian users setting up OTP will see a sentence in the wrong language.

It needs a proper Lithuanian translation. Alternatively, drop the key so it falls back to English.

title: Lithuanian account translation replaced with Italian text
body: `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian account bundle was replaced with the Italian sentence `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. Lithuanian users will see Italian text in the account console.

title: Traditional Chinese text placed in Simplified Chinese bundle
body:
`totpStep1` in `messages_zh_CN` (Simplified Chinese) is now `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`. That is Traditional Chinese (手機, 應用程式), which is inconsistent with the rest of the file.

The Simplified form would be something like `在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：`.

title: Missing English counterpart crashes the plugin with an unchecked RuntimeException
body:
`verifySafeHtml` derives the English file path with string replacements. If that file does not exist, it throws a `RuntimeException`.

The path can be missing in several cases:
- a custom or community-only theme with no `_en` file;
- a locale name that the `_[a-zA-Z-_]*` regex does not rewrite as expected.

The exception escapes `verify()`, which only converts `IOException` into `MojoExecutionException`. The build therefore aborts with a stack trace instead of a clean mojo error or a reported message.

The same applies to the read failure of the file itself at line 70.

title: Anchor mismatch message omits key and file
body:
The message `Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string` does not include the property key or the file path. Every other message from this class includes both.

When the verifier runs over hundreds of files, the reported error cannot be traced to its source.

title: No test that legitimate HTML/anchors pass without errors
Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian `totpStep1` value was replaced with "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian. Lithuanian users of the account theme will see an Italian sentence. It should be a Lithuanian translation, or the key should be removed so it falls back to English.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: `loginTotpStep1` in the Lithuanian login bundle now reads "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction on the OTP setup page. Use a Lithuanian string, or drop the key so the English fallback is used.

title: Simplified Chinese bundle gets Traditional Chinese text
body: The new zh_CN `totpStep1` value "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：" is written in Traditional Chinese characters (zh_TW style). The rest of the file uses Simplified Chinese, so users will see mixed scripts. It should be something like "在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：".

title: Java MessageFormat syntax introduced into i18next-based bundle
body: This bundle uses i18next interpolation (`{{0}}`, `{{name}}`), as every other key in the file does. The new `error-invalid-multivalued-size` value uses Java MessageFormat placeholders (`{0}`) and a ChoiceFormat expression (`{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`). i18next will not substitute these, so the account console will show the raw placeholder text to users. Keep the `{{n}}` syntax and use i18next pluralization instead. The same problem applies to the identical change in `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties`.

title: Anchor mismatch message lacks key and file
body: The "Didn't find anchor tag ..." message does not say which key or file is affected, unlike the duplicate-key and Illegal HTML messages. When the verifier runs over hundreds of bundles, maintainers cannot locate the offending translation. Include `key` and `file` in the message.

title: ANCHOR_PATTERN matches any tag starting with 'a'
body: `</?a[^>]*>` also matches tags such as `<abbr>`, `<address>` or `<area>`, not only `<a ...>`. Those tags would be treated as anchors and compared against the English anchors, producing misleading "Didn't find anchor tag" errors. Require a word boundary, e.g. `</?a(\s[^>]*)?>`.

title: Missing English bundle throws RuntimeException instead of a reported failure
body: If the derived English file does not exist, `verifySafeHtml` throws a bare RuntimeException. This happens for files without a locale suffix, or when the path regex derives the wrong name. The exception bypasses the `MojoExecutionException` handling in `verify()`, so the build fails with an unclear stack trace instead of a reported verification error. Throw a `MojoExecutionException`, or report the problem as a message.

title: No positive test and weakened duplicate-key assertion
body: Every test only checks that some error is reported. None verifies that a valid bundle, such as an allowed `<b>` in a translation whose English source also contains `<b>`, produces no messages, so false positives would go unnoticed. The duplicate-key assertion was also loosened from `contains` to `hasItem`, so unexpected extra errors for that fixture are no longer caught.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: `loginTotpStep1` in the Lithuanian login bundle is now "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian. The previous Lithuanian text only needed its anchor tags removed. Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction on the OTP setup page.

title: Lithuanian account translation replaced with Italian text
body: `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian account bundle is now the Italian sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". This replaces a valid Lithuanian translation with a wrong-language string, so Lithuanian users get Italian text.

title: Traditional Chinese text inserted into Simplified Chinese bundle
body: `totpStep1` in `messages_zh_CN` is now "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：". That is Traditional Chinese (手機, 應用程式), while every other entry in the file is Simplified Chinese. It should be a Simplified form such as "在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：".

title: Java MessageFormat syntax put into i18next-based UI bundle
body: The account UI (and admin UI v2) translate with i18next, which interpolates `{{0}}`; the other error-* keys in this file use that style. The new value uses Java MessageFormat `{0}` placeholders and a `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` construct, which i18next does not understand. If the UI renders this key client-side, the placeholders and the raw choice pattern will appear literally instead of the attribute name and counts. The same change was made in `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties`.

title: Diff snippet computation can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body: The `start` and `end` common-prefix and common-suffix scans are computed independently and can overlap when the strings contain repeated characters. Example: value "aaa", sanitized "aa" gives start=2 and end=2. Then `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` becomes `substring(2, 0)` and throws. The verifier would crash the build with an unhelpful exception instead of reporting the illegal HTML. Clamp `end` to `min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`.

title: Anchor mismatch message omits key and file
body: "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string" does not include the property key or the file path, although the method receives `key`. When the plugin runs across dozens of bundles, maintainers cannot tell which entry failed. Include `key` and `file` in the message, as the other messages do.

title: Missing English counterpart aborts with RuntimeException
body: If the derived `_en.properties` file does not exist, `verifySafeHtml` throws a bare RuntimeException instead of a MojoExecutionException or a reported message. Any localized bundle without an English sibling at the computed path will fail the Maven build with a stack trace. The path rewriting is a fragile regex over the full absolute path, which makes such a missing sibling more likely.

title: No negative test that valid bundles produce no findings
body: Every test only asserts that some error is reported. No test checks that a clean file, or an allowed case such as `<b>` in a translation whose English source also has `<b>`, or an identical anchor, produces an empty result. False positives from the sanitizer or the unescape logic would go undetected.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant type factories
body:
`OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` gains a new abstract method `getShortcut()` with no default implementation. Third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations will no longer compile.

Already-compiled extensions are worse off. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `getShortcut()` on every grant factory, so they will throw `AbstractMethodError` and server startup will fail.

Fix: provide a default implementation (for example, a derived or unknown shortcut) or handle a missing shortcut gracefully.

title: Javadoc says shortcut is ~3 letters, but encoding requires exactly 2
body:
The Javadoc says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", and nothing validates its length.

The default encoder concatenates the shortcut into the token ID prefix. The decoder then rejects any prefix that is not exactly 6 characters and splits it at fixed 2-character offsets.

A custom grant following the documented guidance (3 letters) will produce token IDs that `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects with `IllegalArgumentException`. Fix: document that the shortcut must be exactly 2 characters and validate this in postInit.

title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed from SPI class
body:
The public `Context(Context)` copy constructor was deleted from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. This class is part of the grant-type SPI, so any extension that uses it will break at compile or link time.

If the copy constructor is kept, it must also copy the new `grantType` field.

title: Null check for rawTokenId actually checks grantType again
body:
`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` a second time. `rawTokenId` is never validated.

A null raw ID is therefore accepted silently. It later produces token IDs like `onrtac:null` instead of failing fast. The call should be `requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong offset and inverted condition, so it never checks grant type
body:
The grant shortcut sits at indices 4-6 of the prefix, but the matcher uses `substring(3, 5)`, which yields e.g. "ta" for "onrtac". It also returns false when that substring *equals* the expected shortcut, which is the inverse of the intended check.

The wrong substring never equals a real shortcut, so the matcher accepts any `xxx:UUID` value. None of the integration tests actually verify that the expected grant type is encoded. The check should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of an NPE, not the intended validation
body:
The test factory never calls `postInit`, so `sessionFactory` is null. For an unknown shortcut, `getGrantTypeByShortcut` calls `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` and throws `NullPointerException`.

The test catches any `RuntimeException`, so it passes without ever exercising the "Unknown value for grant type" `IllegalArgumentException` path. It should catch `IllegalArgumentException` specifically and stub the session factory.

title: Lazy grant-map refresh bypasses duplicate-shortcut validation
body:
`postInit` validates that grant shortcuts are unique. The lazy refresh paths in `getShortcutByGrantType` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut` do not: they blindly `put` into both maps.

A hot-deployed grant with a shortcut that collides with an existing one silently overwrites `grantsByShortcuts`. Tokens issued under the original grant would then decode to the wrong grant type.

title: rawTokenId null check validates grantType instead
body: The fourth `Objects.requireNonNull` call checks `grantType` again but uses the message "Null rawTokenId not allowed". `rawTokenId` is never validated. A null raw ID is therefore accepted silently, and `encodeTokenId` would produce an ID like `onrtac:null` instead of failing fast. The call should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong offset and inverted condition
body: The grant shortcut occupies characters 4..6 of the prefix (e.g. `ac` in `onrtac`), but the matcher reads `substring(3, 5)`, which is the `ta` in `onrtac`. It also returns false when the substring *equals* the expected shortcut, so the check is inverted. In practice the extracted value almost never equals the shortcut, so the matcher accepts any grant type. The new event assertions in expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken and expectAuthReqIdToToken therefore do not verify the encoded grant type at all. The check should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, ideally with a length check on `items[0]` first.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks custom grant type providers; javadoc contradicts required length
body:
`getShortcut()` is added as an abstract interface method. Every existing third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation will fail to compile, or throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls it. A default implementation would avoid this.

The javadoc also says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", but the decoder requires exactly a 6-character prefix, i.e. a 2-character grant shortcut. A custom grant following the docs would issue tokens whose IDs cannot be decoded: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` throws "Expected length of 6". Shortcut length is not validated anywhere.

title: Offline-token flows encode session type as online
body:
The session type comes from `userSession.isOffline()` at the time the access token is created. In `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` and the ROPC grant, the access token is created before `generateRefreshToken()`. That call creates the offline session, and the online session is then removed when FIRST_OFFLINE_ACCESS is set or for direct grants.

As a result, the access token issued with an offline token is encoded `on`, while the online session it refers to is deleted. The stated goal of using the session type to look up only one session type (#37662) would then fail to find the session for these tokens.

title: Public copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context removed
body: The public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor is removed without replacement. Extensions or custom grant types that wrap or copy the context will break. Removing it is unrelated to the feature. If it is kept, it should also copy the new `grantType` field.

title: Lazy refresh of grant shortcuts skips duplicate validation and can fail token issuance
body:
`postInit` validates that grant shortcuts are unique. The runtime refresh paths in `getShortcutByGrantType` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut` do not. A hot-deployed grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one silently overwrites the `grantsByShortcuts` entry, so existing tokens decode to the wrong grant type.

Separately, any code path that sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` to a value with no registered factory now makes `initToken` throw `IllegalStateException`. Token issuance fails outright instead of degrading to the unknown (`na`) value.

title: rawTokenId null check validates grantType instead
body: The fourth `Objects.requireNonNull` call checks `grantType` a second time but uses the message "Null rawTokenId not allowed". As a result `rawTokenId` is never validated. A null raw id is silently accepted, and `encodeTokenId` would then produce an id such as `onrtac:null` instead of failing fast. It should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong indices and inverted condition
body: The grant shortcut sits at characters 4-6 of the prefix, so it should be read with `substring(4, 6)`. The matcher reads `substring(3, 5)` instead; for `onrtac` that yields `ta`. The condition is also inverted: it returns false when the value equals the expected shortcut. With both errors the check effectively never rejects anything, so the matcher only verifies the `prefix:UUID` shape. The integration tests therefore do not verify that the correct grant type is encoded in the token id. Use `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant type providers
body: `getShortcut()` is added to a public SPI interface without a default implementation. Existing custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations will no longer compile. Already-built extension jars will hit `AbstractMethodError` in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`, and that failure aborts server startup. A shortcut that returns null would also throw an NPE when inserted into the `ConcurrentHashMap`. Consider adding a default implementation, or handling missing or null shortcuts gracefully.

title: Javadoc says '3-letters' shortcut but encoder requires exactly 2 characters
body: The Javadoc tells implementors the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters". However, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` decodes the context by assuming exactly 2 characters per segment and rejects any prefix whose length is not 6. A custom grant following the doc with a 3-character shortcut would get tokens issued successfully (encoding does not validate length), and those tokens could never be decoded by `getTokenContextFromTokenId`. Fix the documentation to require exactly 2 characters, and validate the shortcut length at registration time.

title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed
body: The public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor was deleted from the server-spi-private `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. Any extension or subclass using it will break. The removal is unrelated to the feature. It could instead have been kept and extended to copy the new `grantType` field.

title: testIncorrectGrantType passes due to NPE rather than validation
body: In this test the factory's `sessionFactory` is never set, so it is null. For the unknown shortcut `ac`, `getGrantTypeByShortcut` falls back to `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` and throws a `NullPointerException`. The test catches any `RuntimeException`, so it passes because of that NPE rather than because of the intended `IllegalArgumentException` for an unknown grant type. Assert the specific exception type, or mock the session factory.

title: Federated recovery-code credential cannot be removed via removeStoredCredentialById
body:
`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` can now return a credential from user storage. When all its codes are used, the authenticator calls `credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(id)`, which only works on credentials stored in the Keycloak DB.

For a federated credential this call does nothing. It also may receive a null or foreign id: the test provider's `createFromValues` model never sets an id. The exhausted credential therefore stays in user storage.

As a result, `isConfiguredFor` keeps returning true and the user keeps being sent to the recovery-code form with no usable codes. The federated case needs its own handling, for example `disableCredentialType` or an update through the user storage.

title: Federated providers must expose recovery codes in Keycloak's internal JSON format or login breaks
body:
`getCredential` prefers `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`. Callers such as `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` (`.get()` without a check) and the authenticator then pass the result to `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel`, which parses the credentialData as Keycloak's internal hashed-codes JSON.

A user storage provider can accept recovery codes through `updateCredential` and report `isConfiguredFor` true without returning a compatible model from `getCredentials`. In that case login throws `NoSuchElementException` or a parse error and fails with a 500.

This new contract for user storage providers is implicit and undocumented. The code should handle a missing or malformed credential gracefully, or the contract should be documented.

title: Test provider never consumes codes; test does not cover code consumption
body:
The provider's `isValid` accepts any stored code, regardless of which code number was requested, and never marks a code as used.

As a result, `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode` always returns the same code, and the exhausted-codes path in the authenticator is never reached. The new test only logs in once.

Code consumption and the all-codes-used flow for federated credentials are left untested. That flow is broken (see the `removeStoredCredentialById` finding).

title: getCredentials NPE when user not in map
body: `getMyUser(user)` can return null. Other methods in this provider guard against that (`if (myUser == null) return false`), but `getCredentials` dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` directly. It throws a NullPointerException for users not present in the in-memory map.

title: Exhausted federated recovery-codes credential is removed from the wrong store
body: `getCredential(user)` now returns the federated credential first. When `allCodesUsed()` is true, the authenticator still calls `removeStoredCredentialById(id)`, which only works on local (Keycloak DB) credentials. A credential that lives in user storage is never removed; its id may even be null because the model was rebuilt via `createFromValues`. The exhausted federated codes stay configured, so `configuredFor` keeps returning true while the user is also sent to the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action. Removal should go through the credential manager or federation path, e.g. `disableCredentialType` or `removeCredential`, according to where the credential came from.

title: Raw recovery codes are sent to user storage in plaintext, and label/date are dropped
body: Locally, recovery codes are persisted only as hashes inside `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`. The federated path instead serializes the raw `generatedCodes` list to JSON and hands it to the storage provider as the challenge response. External stores therefore receive and may persist plaintext codes. The user label and generatedAt timestamp from `credentialModel` are also lost on this path. Consider passing the hashed credential data, or at least document this contract clearly for provider implementers.

title: getCredentials NPEs when the user is not in the in-memory map
body: `getMyUser(user)` can return null, and every other method in this provider null-checks it. The new `getCredentials` dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` directly. Any credential listing for a user unknown to this storage, for example via the account or admin REST API, throws a NullPointerException.

title: Test storage accepts any recovery code repeatedly, so the test can't detect consumption or ordering bugs
body: `isValid` returns true if the input matches any stored code, and it never marks the code as used. The new test therefore only checks a single login with code 0. It does not verify that codes are consumed, that the expected next code is required, or how the flow behaves once all codes are used. That last case is where the authenticator's removal logic is broken for federated credentials.

title: Recovery code consumption/removal only works for local credentials; codes in user storage are never invalidated
body:
`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` now returns the user-storage (federated) credential first. The code that follows still assumes a local credential.

- When `allCodesUsed()` is true, it calls `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. That only touches the local DB, so the federated credential is never removed. The id of a model built via `createFromValues` may also be null or meaningless.
- When validation succeeds through the user storage, `isValid` short-circuits in the storage provider. The local provider's code-consumption logic never runs, and nothing tells the storage that the code was used.

The result is that a recovery code kept in user storage can be reused indefinitely. The login bean keeps asking for the same code number, and the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES regeneration path never triggers.

The SPI needs an explicit way to consume or remove codes in user storage, or the authenticator must handle federated credentials separately.

title: getCredentials NPE when user is not in the in-memory map
body:
`getMyUser(user)` can return null; other methods such as `isConfiguredFor` and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` guard against this. The new `getCredentials` dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` without a null check.

Any credential listing for a user unknown to the map throws a NullPointerException. That includes the account console, the admin REST API, and `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`.

title: getCredentials now exposes OTP credentials too, changing existing OTP test behaviour
body:
`getCredentials` now also returns the stored OTP `CredentialModel`, which carries a newly generated id. Previously the federated OTP was represented only by the dummy `createUserStorageCredentialRepresentation`. This changes what the account REST endpoint returns for the existing OTP tests, including the credential id used for deletion in `testOTPSetupAndRemoveThroughAccountMgmtAndLogin`.

The raw OTP secret is also exposed as the credential value. These side effects on existing OTP behaviour are untested and unrelated to the recovery-codes change.

title: Test does not verify recovery code consumption or reuse rejection
body:
`testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` performs only one login with code 0. A second login is the scenario where a federated recovery code should be consumed. The test never checks that a used code is rejected afterwards or that the next code number is requested.

The test provider's `isValid` also never removes used codes. The consumption bug for user-storage codes is therefore neither caught nor documented.

title: Same NPE remains in the paginated getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: The PR adds a null check to `getSubGroupsCount()` for the case where the group was deleted concurrently and `modelSupplier.get()` returns null. The three paginated `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads (lines 256, 262, 268) still dereference `modelSupplier.get()` without any check. They hit the same race, for example when a group is deleted while the admin console lists subgroups, and still throw a NullPointerException. The fix is therefore incomplete. These overloads should handle a null model the same way, for example by returning `Stream.empty()`.

title: Test asserts before the reader thread finishes, so failures can be missed
body: The reader thread is started but never joined. Right after the deletes, `deletedAll` is set and `caughtExceptions` is asserted to be empty immediately. A request still in flight in the reader thread may fail and add its exception after the assertion has already passed. Exceptions are also only recorded if the thread happened to run during the deletes. The regression test can therefore pass even when the bug is present. The test should keep a reference to the thread and `join()` it (with a timeout) before asserting. Ideally it should also confirm that at least one read actually ran concurrently with the deletes.

title: Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion can miss exceptions
body: The reader thread is started but never joined. Right after `deletedAll.set(true)`, the test calls `assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty())` while the reader may still be inside a `groups(...)` request that overlaps the last deletions. An exception from that request is added to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion has already passed. The thread can also outlive the test and keep calling the admin client during cleanup or the next test. Keep a reference to the thread, `join()` it (with a timeout) before asserting, and consider asserting that at least one read actually ran.

title: Same NPE remains in the paginated getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: The fix null-guards only `getSubGroupsCount()`. The three paginated `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads (lines 256, 262, 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` directly. When the group is deleted concurrently, the delegate lookup returns null and these methods throw a NullPointerException. These methods back the sub-group listing endpoints, so concurrent reads plus deletes can still produce 500s. Apply the same null handling, for example return `Stream.empty()`.

title: Created groups are not registered for cleanup
body: The 100 created groups are only removed by the test's own deletion loop. If group creation or deletion fails partway through, the remaining groups are left in the shared managed realm. They can then break other tests, for example name-conflict or group-count assertions. Register each created id with `managedRealm.cleanup()`, or delete them in a finally block.

title: Reader thread is never joined before asserting on caught exceptions
body:
The test sets `deletedAll` to true and immediately asserts that `caughtExceptions` is empty. It never joins the reader thread. A request still in flight (often the one most likely to hit a just-deleted group) can fail and append its exception after the assertion has already passed, so regressions can go undetected.

The test also never checks that the reader completed at least one request while deletions were running. If the thread starts late, the test passes without exercising the race.

If any `remove()` call throws, `deletedAll` is never set and the non-daemon thread keeps hammering the server forever. Keep a reference to the thread, set the flag in a `finally` block, `join()` it with a timeout before asserting, and ideally count the reads that overlapped the deletions.

title: Same NPE remains in the other delegate-backed sub-group methods
body:
The fix null-guards only `getSubGroupsCount()`. Three sibling methods still dereference `modelSupplier.get()` without a check:
- `getSubGroupsStream(search, first, max)` (line 256)
- `getSubGroupsStream(first, max)` (line 262)
- `getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, first, max)` (line 268)

When another request deletes the group between the cache lookup and these calls, the supplier returns null and these methods throw the same NPE described in #40368. That can happen when listing subgroups or searching groups. They should be guarded consistently, for example by returning `Stream.empty()` when the model is null.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator applies math.floor/ceil to datetime keys and crashes the audit log endpoint
body:
`OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` copies the integer `Paginator` implementation and runs `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `getattr(item, self.key)`.

The only caller, `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint`, uses `order_by="-datetime"`, so the value is a `datetime`. `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError`.

`build_cursor` calls `key(results[0])` whenever the page has results. So every `optimized_pagination=true` request that returns at least one row fails with a 500.

title: Raw numeric cursor value used to filter a datetime column
body:
`value_from_cursor` returns `cursor.value` unchanged. `build_queryset` then emits `WHERE datetime <= %s` with that integer or float.

`DateTimePaginator` instead converts the millisecond value back into a timezone-aware `datetime`. Here the integer is compared against a timestamp column, which either raises a database error or filters incorrectly.

Any cursor-based navigation of audit logs through the optimized path is therefore broken. The paginator should extend `DateTimePaginator` (or reuse its key/value conversion) when ordering by a datetime.

title: Negative QuerySet slicing is unsupported in Django and raises an error
body:
The "advanced" branch slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. The comment claims the ORM handles negative slicing automatically, but it does not: Django raises `ValueError`/`AssertionError` ("Negative indexing is not supported").

A user-supplied cursor like `0:-5:0` therefore produces a 500 instead of a clean 400 `BadPaginationError`.

The comments also say this "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds" and is "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level". That rationale is misleading. Negative offsets should be rejected, as `OffsetPaginator` does.

title: BasePaginator change silently clamps negative next offsets but passes negative prev offsets to the QuerySet
body:
This change affects every `BasePaginator` subclass (`DateTimePaginator`, `Paginator`, etc.) used across the API.

- For forward cursors, a negative offset is now silently clamped to 0. But `build_cursor` still computes the next cursor from the original negative `cursor.offset`, so the returned next/prev cursors can be wrong (e.g. `offset + limit` stays negative or small).
- For `is_prev` cursors, the negative offset is still passed straight into `queryset[offset:stop]`, which errors.

The comment calling this "safe" is incorrect. Malformed cursors should be rejected with `BadPaginationError` rather than half-handled.

title: Gate uses is_superuser rather than active superuser, and member may be None
body:
`request.user.is_superuser` is true for superuser accounts even without an active superuser session. Sentry normally gates superuser-only behavior with `is_active_superuser(request)`, so this bypasses that convention.

Separately, for a non-superuser accessing via staff or other paths, `organization_context.member` can be `None`. In that case `.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError` and the request returns a 500.

title: New paginator and endpoint branch have no tests
body:
The PR adds a new paginator, a new query parameter (`optimized_pagination`), and changes the core `BasePaginator.get_result` offset handling, all without tests.

A basic test of `optimized_pagination=true` for an org owner returning audit rows would have exposed the `TypeError` on datetime keys. A test with a negative-offset cursor would have exposed the unsupported negative slice.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor on a datetime and crashes
body: The audit log endpoint uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `getattr(item, self.key)` returns a `datetime`. `get_item_key` then calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on it, which raises `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls this key for every non-empty result set, so any `optimized_pagination=true` request that returns rows fails with a 500. The paginator needs datetime handling like `DateTimePaginator` (or should subclass it).

title: value_from_cursor returns a raw number for a datetime column
body: `value_from_cursor` returns `cursor.value` (an int of milliseconds) unchanged. `build_queryset` then adds `WHERE datetime <= %s` with that integer. Comparing a timestamp column to an integer either raises a database error or filters wrongly. Paging past the first page with the optimized paginator is therefore broken.

title: Negative queryset slicing is unsupported in Django and raises errors
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySets reject negative indexing with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`. Any user can send a cursor like `0:-5:0` with `optimized_pagination=true` and trigger an unhandled 500. The comment saying "Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`, as the other paginators do.

title: BasePaginator still passes negative offsets through for prev cursors
body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` clamps only forward cursors. A client-supplied prev cursor with a negative offset (e.g. `123:-10:1`) still reaches `queryset[negative:...]` and raises an unhandled exception, giving a 500 on every endpoint that uses `Paginator`/`DateTimePaginator`. Separately, silently clamping forward cursors hides malformed input. Negative offsets should raise `BadPaginationError` for both directions.

title: Uses request.user.is_superuser instead of an active-superuser check
body: The gate checks `request.user.is_superuser`, which is true even when the superuser session is not active (no sudo/active-superuser cookie). Sentry normally uses `is_active_superuser(request)` for these checks. As written, a superuser account without an elevated session gets the privileged paginator path, bypassing the standard superuser activation controls.

title: organization_context.member may be None
body: For a non-superuser request, `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` can be `None`, for example for staff or API-token access paths that pass `OrganizationAuditPermission` without membership. In that case this line raises `AttributeError`, so the endpoint returns a 500 even when `optimized_pagination` is not requested.

title: Misleading security/safety comments about negative offsets
body: The comments claim negative offsets "enable access to data beyond normal pagination bounds" and are "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level". They also claim the ORM handles negative slicing. None of this is accurate. The `cursors.py` comment likewise says negative offsets are now allowed, but no behavior changed there. These comments mislead future maintainers about both safety and behavior.

title: No tests for new paginator or endpoint branch
body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, the `optimized_pagination` branch in the audit log endpoint, and the changed offset handling in `BasePaginator` have no tests. A basic test would have caught that the optimized path crashes on datetime keys and on negative offsets.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor on a datetime and raises TypeError
body: The audit log endpoint uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `getattr(item, self.key)` returns a `datetime`. `get_item_key` then calls `math.floor()` or `math.ceil()` on it, which raises `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls this key function on every non-empty result set. As a result, any request with `optimized_pagination=true` that returns at least one row fails with a 500. The method copies `Paginator`'s integer logic instead of `DateTimePaginator`'s timestamp conversion.

title: value_from_cursor returns a raw integer for a datetime column
body: `value_from_cursor` returns `cursor.value` unchanged, which is an integer of milliseconds. `build_queryset` then emits `WHERE sentry_auditlogentry.datetime <= %s` with that integer as the parameter. Comparing a timestamp column to an integer either errors in Postgres or filters incorrectly. Any request that sends a cursor with a value breaks. It should convert the value back to a datetime the way `DateTimePaginator` does.

title: Negative QuerySet slicing raises instead of 'efficiently paginating'
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices with `queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `start_offset` is negative. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing; they raise `ValueError` ("Negative indexing is not supported."). A user-supplied cursor such as `0:-5:0` therefore produces a 500 error. The comments claiming 'the Django ORM properly handles negative slicing' and that this 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' are false and misleading. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`, as `OffsetPaginator` does.

title: BasePaginator change silently clamps or still crashes on negative offsets, with a misleading comment
body: This shared code path is used by `DateTimePaginator`, `Paginator` and others. With the change, a negative offset on a next cursor is silently clamped to 0, returning the first page instead of an error. A negative offset on a prev cursor is still passed straight to the QuerySet slice, which raises `ValueError` and returns a 500. The comment claims 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions', which is not true. Malformed cursors should be rejected explicitly with `BadPaginationError` rather than half-handled across every paginated endpoint.

title: Advanced-pagination gate uses raw is_superuser and can dereference a None member
body: The gate checks `request.user.is_superuser`, which ignores Sentry's active superuser session check (`is_active_superuser(request)`). A superuser without an active superuser session can therefore enable the 'advanced' path. In addition, when the user is not a superuser, `organization_context.member` can be `None` (for example for staff or non-member access paths permitted by `OrganizationAuditPermission`). In that case `.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError` and the request returns a 500, even for requests that never asked for optimized pagination, because the expression is evaluated unconditionally.

title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported but nothing changed
body: The added comment says `Cursor` allows negative offsets to enable 'efficient reverse pagination'. No code changed here, and negative offsets taken from user-supplied cursor strings lead to crashes in the QuerySet-based paginators. The comment misdocuments the cursor contract.

title: New paginator and endpoint branch have no tests
body: This PR adds `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, changes `BasePaginator` offset handling, and adds a new branch in the audit log endpoint, with no accompanying tests. A basic endpoint test with `optimized_pagination=true` would have caught that the datetime key handling fails on every non-empty page.

title: Negative queryset slicing raises in Django, so the 'advanced' path always errors
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`. Any request with a cursor such as `0:-10:0` and `optimized_pagination=true` therefore returns a 500 instead of results. The surrounding comments claiming the ORM 'properly handles negative slicing' and that this 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' are false. The intent described there is also a security smell. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`, as `OffsetPaginator` does.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator key handling breaks on the datetime ordering it is used with
body: The audit log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`. `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on the datetime value, which raises `TypeError` as soon as `build_cursor` computes next/prev cursors on any non-empty page. `value_from_cursor` returns the raw integer cursor value, so `build_queryset` compares the `datetime` column against an integer. The optimized path is unusable even without negative offsets. It needs `DateTimePaginator`'s key/value conversion, or should subclass `DateTimePaginator`.

title: Gate uses raw is_superuser and member may be None
body: `request.user.is_superuser` is true for superuser accounts even without an active superuser session; Sentry normally checks `is_active_superuser(request)`. `has_global_access` is not an admin-only privilege either: in open-membership orgs every member has it. So this 'admin-only' feature is available far more broadly than intended. In addition, `organization_context.member` can be None (for example staff or token access without membership), in which case `.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError` and the request returns a 500.

title: Comment claims negative offsets are safe for prev cursors in BasePaginator
body: For `is_prev` cursors the offset is passed through unclamped to queryset slicing. A user-supplied cursor with a negative offset (`Cursor.from_string` accepts one) makes Django raise `ValueError` and the request returns a 500. The comment says 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions', which is incorrect. Negative offsets should be rejected or clamped for both directions.

title: Eviction silently drops earliest-ending spans, including possibly the root span
body: `zpopmin` removes the spans with the lowest `end_timestamp_precise`. Root/segment spans and other important spans can be discarded without any metric or log. Previously an oversized segment was logged and counted (`segment_span_count_exceeded`). The limit of 1000 is also hardcoded and no longer tied to `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` (default 1001). That setting is now dead config and the two values disagree.

title: Switching span-buf:s keys from SET to ZSET breaks in-flight data during deploy
body: Keys written by the old code are Redis sets. After deploy, `ZADD`, `ZCARD`, `ZUNIONSTORE` and `ZSCAN` against those keys fail with `WRONGTYPE`. This aborts the whole pipeline or Lua call for the batch and leaves segments unflushable until their TTL (up to an hour) expires. A migration or key-prefix change is needed to roll this out safely.

title: Redirect depth limit reduced 10x and its warning comment removed
body: The redirect-following loop limit went from 10000 to 1000. Segment trees deeper than 1000 levels will now be split incorrectly. The comment documenting this limitation was deleted, and the PR does not say why the change was made.

title: No test for the new insert-time eviction
body: The PR's main behavior change is capping segments at 1000 spans by popping the lowest-scored entries in Lua. No test covers it: nothing exercises a segment exceeding the cap, checks which spans survive, or checks interaction with merges via `zunionstore`.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime keys used by audit logs
body:
`get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on `getattr(item, self.key)`. The audit log endpoint orders by `-datetime`, so this raises `TypeError` on a datetime for any non-empty page.

`value_from_cursor` has a matching problem: it returns the raw integer cursor value, which `build_queryset` then compares against a timestamp column (`datetime <= 1700000000000`). That comparison is a type error at the database level.

Every request with `optimized_pagination=true` will therefore return a 500. The class should reuse `DateTimePaginator`'s key and value conversion.

title: Negative offset slicing on a Django QuerySet raises, and the intent is unsafe
body:
The 'advanced' branch passes `cursor.offset < 0` straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets reject negative indexing with `ValueError`/`AssertionError`, so any client-supplied cursor like `0:-5:0` crashes the request with a 500.

The stated purpose, "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds", is not a legitimate feature either. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`, as the other paginators do.

title: BasePaginator forwards negative offsets for prev cursors to the queryset
body:
`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` clamps offsets only for next cursors. A user-crafted prev cursor with a negative offset (`Cursor.from_string` accepts it) is passed to `queryset[...]`, which raises a ValueError and produces a 500.

The later check `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` also still uses the unclamped `offset`. This change touches every `Paginator`/`DateTimePaginator` user. Negative offsets should be rejected uniformly.

title: Wrong authorization check for 'admin-only' paginator
body:
The gate uses `request.user.is_superuser` rather than an active-superuser check such as `is_active_superuser(request)`. A user with the superuser flag but no active superuser session passes.

The other half of the gate is `organization_context.member.has_global_access`. That flag is true for any member of an org with open membership, not only administrators.

In addition, `organization_context.member` can be None (for example, staff or non-member access). In that case the attribute access raises `AttributeError` and the request returns a 500.

title: Switching span buffer keys from SET to ZSET breaks in-flight data on deploy
body:
Existing `span-buf:s:*` keys in Redis are SETs written by the old code. After deploy, several operations hit those keys:
- `zadd` here
- `zcard`/`zunionstore` in `add-buffer.lua`
- `zscan` in `_load_segment_data`

All of these fail with WRONGTYPE errors against SET keys. The consumer and flusher will crash or loop until those keys expire, which can take up to `redis_ttl`, i.e. one hour.

A migration path is needed: new key prefix, a type check, or draining before rollout.

title: Silent hardcoded eviction replaces configurable span-count limit
body:
The script hardcodes a limit of 1000 and silently `zpopmin`s the excess spans, with no metric and no log.

Meanwhile `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` (default 1001) is now unused, and the `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric and log were removed. The configuration is dead and inconsistent with the actual limit, and data loss is unobservable.

A related problem: `zunionstore` uses the default SUM aggregation, so a payload present in both sets gets a doubled score. That distorts which spans are evicted. The limit should be passed as an ARGV and the eviction counted in a metric.

title: Redirect depth limit reduced 10x without justification
body: The redirect-following loop limit was lowered from 10000 to 1000, and the comment explaining its consequence was removed. Segment trees with redirect chains deeper than 1000 will now be split into separate segments instead of joined correctly.

title: No tests for eviction or the new paginator
body:
The PR's headline behavior has no tests:
- trimming segments over 1000 spans via `zpopmin`, and which spans survive
- `OptimizedCursorPaginator`
- the new audit-log branch

A basic test of the paginator would have revealed its datetime and negative-offset crashes.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator applies math.floor to a datetime key
body: The audit-log endpoint uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`. Its `get_item_key` copies the integer `Paginator` logic and calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `getattr(item, 'datetime')`. That raises `TypeError` for a datetime object, so any non-empty page served through the optimized path returns a 500. `value_from_cursor` has the same mismatch: it returns the raw integer cursor value, which is then compared against the datetime column in the WHERE clause, giving wrong results or a DB error. This class needs `DateTimePaginator`'s key and cursor conversion, for example by subclassing it.

title: Negative cursor offsets are sliced directly into the Django queryset
body: With `enable_advanced_features`, a negative `cursor.offset` taken from the user-supplied cursor string is used as `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise an error, so a crafted cursor such as `0:-10:0` causes a 500 instead of a `BadPaginationError`. The comments say this is meant to 'access data beyond normal pagination bounds'. That is the wrong goal for a pagination primitive, and the claim that permissions are checked at the queryset level does not justify it. Negative offsets should be rejected, as `OffsetPaginator` already does.

title: BasePaginator still passes negative offsets through for prev cursors
body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` clamps only next cursors. A prev cursor with a negative offset from user input still reaches the queryset slice and raises an unhandled error, giving a 500. Meanwhile the clamping on next cursors silently hides invalid input. All paginators built on `BasePaginator` are affected. Negative offsets should raise `BadPaginationError` consistently.

title: Possible AttributeError when organization_context.member is None
body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated for every non-superuser request, even when `optimized_pagination` was not requested. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` can be None, for example for staff or token-based access that passes `OrganizationAuditPermission` without a membership. In that case the whole audit log endpoint fails with a 500. The member check should be guarded and evaluated only when `use_optimized` is true.

title: Switching segment keys from sets to sorted sets breaks on keys left by the old code
body: Segment keys `span-buf:s:*` are now written with ZADD and read with ZCARD/ZSCAN. During a deploy, keys created by the old code are still Redis SETs and live up to `redis_ttl` (one hour). ZADD/ZCARD on those keys raises WRONGTYPE, which fails the whole pipeline in `process_spans`. ZSCAN in `_load_segment_data` fails the same way, crashing the consumer and flusher. A migration step, new key prefix, or type-tolerant handling is needed.

title: Spans are evicted silently with a hardcoded limit and no metric
body: When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, `zpopmin` drops the spans with the earliest end timestamps, and nothing records it. The old code emitted `segment_span_count_exceeded` and logged an error. The limit is hardcoded in Lua, while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` (default 1001) is still accepted but no longer used, which is misleading configuration. The data loss is now invisible to operators. The limit should be passed in as an argument, and the eviction count returned so it can be reported as a metric.

title: Redirect depth limit cut from 10000 to 1000 and the caveat comment removed
body: The redirect-following loop now stops after 1000 hops, and the comment explaining that deeper trees will not be joined correctly was removed. Segments with redirect chains deeper than 1000 will now be split into separate segments without any indication. The PR does not explain this behaviour change.

title: New span eviction logic has no tests
body: The PR adds eviction of the oldest spans when a segment exceeds 1000, but no test covers it. Nothing checks which spans are kept, that the count is capped correctly when sets are merged through `zunionstore`, or that the root span survives eviction. The removed `max_segment_spans` behaviour also had no replacement test.

title: Substring match for event.type:error also matches negated and mixed queries
body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the lowercased query contains the substring `event.type:error`. That also matches `!event.type:error`, which excludes errors, and mixed queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. For the discover dataset this applies `upsampled_count()` (sum of sample_weight) to queries that return transactions or other non-error events. Those rows have no sample_weight, so the reported counts are wrong. The query should be parsed properly instead of substring-matched.

title: Upsampling eligibility checks the outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
body: `_get_event_stats` passes the closed-over request-level `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, not the `scoped_dataset` actually being queried. In the dashboard split path, `scoped_dataset` is `discover` with an `!event.type:transaction` errors query while the outer `dataset` is a metrics dataset. The check then never upsamples the errors split. The opposite mismatch is also possible: the decision is made for one dataset and the transformed columns run against another.

title: Allowlist cache makes changes stale and is never invalidated
body: Eligibility is cached for 60s in the shared cache. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but nothing calls it, so allowlist changes take up to 60s to apply. The `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` docstring says it 'reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time', which is false once this cache is in front of it. In tests that mock `options`, a value cached by one test can leak into the next test when the same project IDs recur, giving order-dependent results.

title: Cache round-trip runs before the cheap dataset check and may cost more than it saves
body: `options.get` is already locally cached, so replacing it with a remote cache get/set (memcached/redis) on every `_get_event_stats` call likely adds latency rather than removing it. The lookup also runs before `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, so requests for spans, transactions or metrics datasets pay for the cache round-trip even though they can never be upsampled.

title: upsampled_count silently undercounts events without sample_weight
body: `sum(sample_weight)` ignores NULLs, so any event in an allowlisted project that lacks sample_weight counts as 0 instead of 1. Examples are events ingested before the rollout or without client sampling context. The comment assumes the schema guarantees the column is populated, which is not enforced anywhere. Use something like `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))` so missing weights count as one event.

title: Top-events ordering and selected fields are not transformed
body: For top events only `timeseries_columns` is rewritten to `upsampled_count()`. `selected_columns` (from `get_field_list`) and `orderby` still use raw `count()`. The top-N groups are therefore chosen by raw count while the plotted values are upsampled, so the two can disagree.

title: Accidental submodule gitlink committed
body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink (a subproject pointing at the base commit). It has no `.gitmodules` entry and is unrelated to the feature, so it looks like it was committed by mistake. It will confuse checkouts and tooling and should be removed.

title: No tests for the cached entry point or negated queries
body: The unit tests never exercise `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, so the caching behaviour and cache-key logic are untested. They also do not cover negated or mixed queries such as `!event.type:error` for `_is_error_focused_query`, which is exactly where the substring heuristic fails.

title: Accidental git submodule (gitlink) committed
body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink pointing at the base commit (a5d29095…). It is unrelated to the feature and looks like a local checkout of the repo that got staged by mistake. Merging it adds a broken or recursive submodule entry to the repository, with no `.gitmodules` entry to back it. Remove it from the PR.

title: Substring check treats negated or other error-type filters as error-focused
body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever `"event.type:error"` appears anywhere in the lowercased query string. A query like `!event.type:error` (which excludes errors) contains that substring, so it is treated as error-focused. So is `event.type:errors_foo`. For allowlisted projects on the discover dataset, `count()` is then rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` for non-error events, which have no sample_weight. The result is wrong counts, usually 0. Parse the query, or at least reject negated filters.

title: Upsampling decision ignores the dataset and query actually being executed
Eligibility cache is never invalidated and contradicts its own documentation
body: Eligibility is cached for 60s per org and project set. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called, even though its docstring says it should run when the allowlist changes. As a result, allowlist changes take up to 60s to apply, and different hosts can return different counts for the same query in that window. The docstring on `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` also claims the configuration is read fresh each time, which the cache makes false. Either wire up invalidation or drop the cache.

title: Cache adds a remote round-trip in front of an already-cached option lookup
body: The code claims `options.get` is an expensive lookup. In practice options are cached in-process, so `options.get` is cheap. Putting `cache.get` / `cache.set` in front of it adds a memcached or redis round-trip to every `_get_event_stats` call, which makes the request slower rather than faster. The key is also built from Python `hash()` of the project tuple, so two different project sets can collide and share an eligibility result.

title: upsampled_count silently drops events without sample_weight
body: `upsampled_count` is defined as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no fallback. Events that have no sample_weight contribute nothing to the sum. That includes events ingested before a project was allowlisted, or events whose SDK sent no client sample rate. Once a project is allowlisted, historical or unsampled error counts drop toward 0 instead of counting as 1 each. Use something like `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))`. The result type is also declared `number` while `count()` is `integer`, which changes the response meta for the same yAxis.

title: Missing tests for caching path and negated filters
Substring check for event.type:error also matches negated and mixed queries
body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the lowercased query contains the substring `event.type:error`. That includes negated queries such as `!event.type:error` and mixed ones such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. For these the discover dataset will swap `count()` for `sum(sample_weight)`. Transactions have no sample_weight, so counts come out wrong, and a negated query counts the opposite set of events with the wrong aggregation. The check should parse the query, or at least reject negation and OR'd transaction filters.

title: Upsampling decision uses outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` but passes the closed-over request `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. In the dashboard-split path, `_get_event_stats` is called with `discover`, using an errors-only query (`!event.type:transaction`), while the outer dataset is metrics_enhanced_performance. The decision is then made against the wrong dataset, so error counts in the split path are never upsampled. The reverse mismatch is also possible. The check should use `scoped_dataset` and the actual query being executed rather than `request.GET['query']`.

title: Cache key built from hash() of project ids can collide; invalidation is ineffective
body:
The cache key embeds `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))` instead of the ids themselves. Distinct project sets can collide on this hash, and a colliding request would get another project set's eligibility result. Projects that are not allowlisted could then be upsampled, or the reverse.

The cache is also keyed by org, while the allowlist is a global option. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called and can only clear one exact project set, so it cannot keep the cache consistent when the option changes.

The cache also adds a network roundtrip in front of `options.get`, which is already cached in-process. The claimed performance gain is doubtful, and the cache adds up to 60s of staleness.

title: Docstring claims fresh reads, contradicting the caching layer
body: The NOTE says `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` reads the allowlist fresh each time to always reflect the latest configuration. Its only caller wraps it in a 60-second cache, so the note is misleading. The `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` docstring also describes `sum(sample_weight)` while the code emits `upsampled_count()`.

title: upsampled_count silently undercounts events without sample_weight
body: `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` assumes every event has a populated sample_weight. Events ingested before sampling was enabled, or sent without client sampling context, will have null or zero weight. Those events contribute nothing, so counts drop instead of falling back to 1 per event. A safer expression is `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))` or similar.

title: Accidental gitlink/submodule committed
body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink that points at the base commit. There is no matching .gitmodules entry and it is unrelated to the feature. It looks like a local checkout committed by mistake, and it will break clones and tooling that process submodules. Remove it.

title: No tests for the cached entrypoint or negated queries
body: The tests cover the private helpers but never call `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. Its caching behaviour, including stale results when the option changes, is untested. `_is_error_focused_query` is not tested with `!event.type:error` or OR'd queries, which hides the substring-match bug. `self.snuba_params` is built in setUp but never used.

title: Error events zipped against nodestore result dict values by position
body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids` and calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi`. It then pairs the results with `zip(error_ids, events.values())`, which assumes the returned dict has one entry per requested id, in request order. `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node_id, and backends do not guarantee that order or that missing keys are present. When they differ, error titles and messages get attached to the wrong event IDs, or entries are silently dropped. Look up each result with `events.get(node_id)` instead of relying on position.

title: Error timestamps (seconds) compared with rrweb event timestamps (milliseconds)
body: `gen_request_data` interleaves errors with recording events by comparing `error['timestamp']` to `event.get('timestamp')`. The error timestamp comes from nodestore event data and is in seconds since epoch. Top-level rrweb recording-segment event timestamps are in milliseconds. In real data every error therefore sorts before every breadcrumb, so the chronological ordering sent to Seer is wrong. The tests use seconds for both values and do not catch this. Normalize both values to the same unit before comparing.

title: Migrations turned into no-ops that point to a migration not in this PR
body: Both 0917 and 0920 now just return, with comments directing readers to `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`. That migration is not added in this change. If it does not already exist, organization saved searches are never converted to GroupSearchViews. Environments that already ran the original 0917 also keep its (allegedly erroneous) results with no corrective migration. The comment that the migration 'was never run' may also be inaccurate, since 0917 shipped with a test and was post-deployment. Add 0921 in this PR or fix the reference.

title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness
body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` use `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `.get("timestamp")` as truthy checks. A report with `age: 0` (common for fresh reports) and a timestamp therefore passes validation even though both fields are present. A report with neither field is also accepted, because both are `required=False`. Use `'age' in self.initial_data` and add an object-level `validate()` that requires exactly one of the two fields.

title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only filtered when a search query is present
body: When `searchQuery` is empty, the memo returns `sorted` before the filter runs. As a result `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` stay visible in the default view and disappear only once the user types a search. Apply the hidden-attribute filter in both branches.

title: Feature-flagged table widget renders hardcoded empty data
body: With `use-table-widget-visualization` enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` is given `columns={[]}` and empty `tableData`, and `result.data`/`result.meta` are ignored. Every table widget for flagged orgs will render as an empty table. Pass the actual table results, or keep the flag off until the wiring is complete.

title: 60s deadline for a batch of up to 100 external identity refreshes may break the reschedule chain
body: `check_auth_identities` refreshes up to `chunk_size=100` identities, and each refresh makes a network call to the SSO provider. It reschedules `check_auth` only at the end of the task. With the new 60s processing deadline, a slow provider can get the task killed before that point. The self-rescheduling chain then stops, and further auth checks depend on the periodic trigger. Raise the deadline or reschedule before processing the batch.

title: Per-issue recommended-event lookup when building PR comments
body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` once per issue in the comment. Each call issues a Snuba query plus a nodestore fetch, so every comment build adds N sequential round trips. It also swallows all exceptions with only an info log. Consider fetching environments in bulk, or from group tag values.

title: Error IDs zipped against nodestore results by position rather than by key
body: `fetch_error_details` pairs `error_ids` with `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids).values()` by position. `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node_id, and nothing guarantees it preserves request order. Some backends return results in storage order, and duplicate IDs collapse into one key. When the order differs, error titles and messages get attached to the wrong event IDs. Look each result up with `events.get(node_id)` for its corresponding error_id instead.

title: Error timestamps (seconds) compared against rrweb event timestamps (milliseconds)
body: Nodestore event `timestamp` is epoch seconds, while recording-segment (rrweb) events carry `timestamp` in epoch milliseconds. The merge loop compares the two directly, so every error looks earlier than every breadcrumb. All errors are emitted at the start of the log instead of in chronological order. The tests only pass because the fixtures use second-based breadcrumb timestamps. Normalize both values to the same unit before comparing.

title: Full error list is injected into every paginated page
body: `analyze_recording_segments` receives the complete `error_events` list through `functools.partial` and runs once per page of segments. Each page drains any errors not yet emitted onto the end of its logs. As a result, every page's Seer request contains all of the replay's errors, including ones that belong to other segment ranges. Summaries for later pages are polluted with duplicated, out-of-range errors. Filter errors to the time range of the current page's segments.

title: Migrations turned into no-ops that point to a 0921 migration not included in the PR
body: Both 0917 and 0920 now do nothing and tell readers to see `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`, but this PR does not add that migration. If it does not land alongside this change, org-visibility saved searches are never converted to GroupSearchView. The comments also reference a file that does not exist.
