The 0917 migration test was deleted and nothing replaces it.

title: Feature-flagged table widget renders with hardcoded empty data
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` is passed `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}`. The real `result.data` and `result.meta` are ignored. Every table widget for orgs with the flag will render blank. Pass the actual query results through, or keep the flag off until that wiring is done.

title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only applied when a search query is entered
body: The memo returns the unfiltered sorted list early when `searchQuery` is empty. The `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(...)` filter therefore only runs during a search. In the default view, `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are still shown. Apply the hidden filter before the early return.

title: Per-issue recommended-event lookup when building PR comments
body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue in the comment. That is a separate Snuba/nodestore query per issue, done serially inside the comment task. It adds N extra queries per PR comment. Any failure is swallowed silently at info level, so the environment just disappears from the comment without notice.

title: Mutual-exclusion validation of age/timestamp uses truthiness
body: The age/timestamp checks use `self.initial_data.get(...)` as a truthy test, so a value of `0` counts as absent. For example, `age: 0` together with a `timestamp` passes validation. A report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` is also accepted, even though both specs require one of them. Use `'age' in self.initial_data` and add an object-level `validate` that requires exactly one of the two fields.

title: Header alignment computed from display name instead of field key
body: `fieldAlignment(column.name, ...)` uses the column's display name. When custom names are supplied, such as 'Count of Span Duration', alignment detection for aggregate fields fails. The header then aligns differently from the body cells, which are rendered by `column.key`. Use `column.key` instead.

title: Error IDs zipped positionally against nodestore get_multi values
body: `fetch_error_details` pairs `error_ids` with `events.values()` by position. `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id, and some backends only include found entries or return them in a different order. When that happens, error ids get attached to the wrong event payloads, or the list silently shifts. The data should be looked up by the generated node id, e.g. `events.get(node_id)` for each `(event_id, node_id)` pair.

title: Error timestamps (seconds) compared with rrweb event timestamps (likely milliseconds)
body: Error `timestamp` comes from nodestore event data, which is in float seconds. It is compared directly against the top-level `event["timestamp"]` of replay recording events. rrweb recording events normally carry millisecond timestamps. If so, every error compares as earlier than the first recording event and is emitted at the start of the log, so the interleaving is wrong. The tests use seconds for both values, which hides the mismatch. The units should be normalized before comparing.

title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only filtered when a search query is present
body: When `searchQuery` is empty, the memo returns the full sorted list before the `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` filter runs. As a result `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are still shown in the default view and are hidden only while the user is searching. The hidden-attribute filter should apply unconditionally.

title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hardcoded empty columns and data
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the widget renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and empty `tableData`. It ignores `result.data` and `result.meta`, so every table widget for flagged orgs shows an empty table. The actual results should be converted into `TabularData` and columns.

title: No-op migrations reference a 0921 migration not present in this change
body: Both 0917 and 0920 were turned into no-ops with a comment pointing to `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py` as the correct migration. That migration is not part of this PR. If it does not exist, the org saved-search to view conversion is silently dropped and the comment is misleading. The comment's claim that 0920 "was never run" should also be verified for environments that may already have applied it.

title: Mutual-exclusion check on age/timestamp uses truthiness
body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` check `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `.get("timestamp")` by truthiness. A report with `age: 0` (valid per spec) plus `timestamp`, or `timestamp: 0` plus `age`, therefore passes even though it mixes both specs. Reports with neither field are also accepted, despite the docstrings saying one must be present. The check should use `"age" in self.initial_data` and enforce that exactly one of the two fields is provided.

title: Container lost align-items/gap when replaced by Flex
body: The old `Container` extended `FlexBox`, which set `align-items: center` and `gap: space(1)`. The replacement `<Flex ref={setRef} justify="space-between">` drops both, so the tabs and vitals are no longer vertically centered or spaced. A similar regression is in `traceWaterfall.tsx`, where the removed `FlexBox` set `height: 100%` and the new `Flex` does not.

title: Query options dropped (retry/refetchOnWindowFocus) on attribute keys query
body: The previous `useApiQuery` call set `staleTime: 0`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and `retry: false`. The new `useQuery` uses the defaults instead, so failing attribute-key requests are retried several times and the query refetches on every window focus. This is a behavioral and load change that appears unintended.

title: KeyError when Integration metadata has no `sender`
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes every existing GitHub Integration row has a `sender` entry. `build_integration` only sets `sender` when it is present in state. Integrations created by older code or by other paths will lack it. For those, reaching this branch (an Integration exists without an OrganizationIntegration) raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the intended error page. Use `.get()` and fail closed with `error(...)`.

title: User/installation match is skipped when the Integration row doesn't exist yet
body: The new sender-vs-authenticated-user check runs only on the path where an Integration already exists (created by the installation webhook). If no Integration exists, `pipeline.next_step()` is called with no validation. That happens when the webhook is delayed, failed, or hasn't been processed yet. In that case a user can still finish the pipeline with an arbitrary `installation_id` they did not install and bind it to their own Sentry org. The check should also run here, e.g. by comparing against the installation's account or sender fetched from the GitHub API.

title: Network/API failures in the OAuth exchange produce 500s
body: `safe_urlopen(...)` is called outside the try block, and `get_user_info(...)` is not wrapped either. A connection error, timeout, or a non-JSON or error response from GitHub raises an unhandled exception. The user then gets a 500 rather than the 'Invalid installation request' page described in the PR.

title: OAuth authorize URL parameters are not URL-encoded
body: The authorize URL is built with an f-string, so `redirect_uri` (which contains `:` and `/`) and the other parameters are not percent-encoded. A redirect URI containing `?` or `&` would corrupt the query string. Use `urlencode` for the parameters.

title: Non-active existing Integrations now always fail installation
body: Before this change, an existing Integration with no OrganizationIntegration proceeded to the next step regardless of status. Now, if the Integration is not ACTIVE (e.g. disabled), the lookup with `status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE` raises DoesNotExist. The user then sees a generic 'Invalid installation request' error, which blocks reinstalling such integrations and gives a misleading message.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the 404 path
body: The test now sends a deliberately wrong `state` (`ddd023...`), so it fails at the state-signature check. It asserts the generic 'Invalid installation request.' message. The original assertion for 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' was removed, so nothing covers the 404 branch in `build_integration` any more. The test name is now misleading. Add separate tests for the state-mismatch case and the installation-404 case.

title: GitHub user check is skipped when the Integration row does not exist yet
body: When `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist`, the view returns `pipeline.next_step()` without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to anyone. That happens whenever the installation webhook has not arrived or been processed yet. `build_integration` then fetches the installation with the app JWT and creates the integration for whatever `installation_id` was supplied in the query string. Someone who knows another account's installation_id can win this race and bind that GitHub installation to their own Sentry org, which is the attack this PR is meant to stop. The installer identity should be checked in this branch too, for example by comparing against the installation's sender or account from the GitHub API, or the step should fail closed.

title: KeyError when integration metadata has no `sender`
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes every existing Integration has a `sender` entry. `build_integration` only sets it when `state.get("sender")` is present, and older integrations or ones created through other paths may not have it. In those cases this line raises an uncaught KeyError, and the user gets a 500 instead of the error page. Use `.get()` and treat a missing sender as a failed check.

title: Unhandled exceptions in the OAuth token exchange and user lookup
body: `safe_urlopen(...)` on line 423 is outside the try block, so network or connection errors propagate. The HTTP status of the response is never checked. `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` raises an API error when GitHub returns a non-2xx response, for example a revoked token or rate limiting. All of these escape `dispatch` as a 500 instead of rendering the 'Invalid installation request' error page that the PR says users will see in these cases.

title: OAuth authorize URL is built without URL-encoding parameters
body: `redirect_uri` is an absolute URL containing `:` and `/` characters, and `client_id` and `state` are interpolated raw into the query string. If the configured URL prefix ever contains `?`, `&`, `#` or similar characters, the query string to GitHub will be malformed. Build it with `urlencode({...})`.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests a missing installation
body: The test now sends a `state` (`ddd023...`) that does not match the pipeline signature. It therefore fails at the state check in OAuthLoginView and never reaches `build_integration`. The 404 branch ('The GitHub installation could not be found.') is no longer covered. Use the correct state value and restore the original assertion. Add a separate test for the state-mismatch case.

title: User verification skipped when the Integration row doesn't exist yet
body: When `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises DoesNotExist, the view calls `pipeline.next_step()` without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to the installer. The Integration row only exists once the installation webhook has been processed. So if an attacker finishes the pipeline with someone else's `installation_id` before that webhook lands (or if it is delayed or dropped), no ownership check runs at all. `build_integration` then binds that installation to the attacker's Sentry org. The sender check needs to apply on this path too, for example by verifying installer ownership via the GitHub API.

title: KeyError when integration metadata lacks `sender`
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes every Integration has a `sender` entry. `build_integration` only sets it when `state.get("sender")` is present, and older or otherwise-created integrations won't have it. For an orphaned Integration without `sender` (no OrganizationIntegration), this raises KeyError and the user gets a 500 instead of the error page. Use `.get()` and render the error page when the key is missing.

title: Unhandled exceptions from token exchange / user lookup
body: `get_user_info` raises `GitHubApiError` on a non-2xx response from `/user`, for example a revoked token or a rate limit. `safe_urlopen` can also raise on network errors, and it is called outside the try block. None of these are caught, so the user gets a 500 instead of the documented 'Invalid installation request' page. Wrap both calls and return `error(...)` on failure.

title: OAuth authorize URL query parameters not URL-encoded
body: `redirect_uri` is an absolute URL containing `:` and `/` characters, and `client_id` and `state` are interpolated directly into the query string without encoding. If any value contains `&`, `#` or `?`, the authorize URL is malformed. Build the query with `urlencode`.

title: Reinstall of a non-ACTIVE existing Integration now always fails
body: Before this change, an Integration with no OrganizationIntegration was allowed to proceed whatever its status. Now the lookup filters on `status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE`, so a disabled or pending-deletion Integration row hits the generic 'Invalid installation request' error. Users can then no longer re-install that GitHub installation, and the error message is misleading.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the 404 path
body: The test now sends a deliberately wrong `state` (`ddd023...`), so it fails at the state-mismatch check and asserts 'Invalid installation request.'. The `/app/installations/{id}` 404 handling in `build_integration` ('The GitHub installation could not be found.') is never reached. That behaviour has lost its coverage, and the state-mismatch case is tested only by accident.

title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a plain default value, so `timezone.now()` runs once when the module is imported. Every `AssignmentSource` created afterwards gets that same stale timestamp, so `queued` never reflects when the assignment was actually queued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

title: Task kwargs carry a raw datetime that may not serialize or round-trip
body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` uses `dataclasses.asdict`, which keeps `queued` as a `datetime` object, and that dict is passed straight into the Celery `apply_async` kwargs. With a JSON task serializer this raises at enqueue time. If it does serialize, the value arrives as a string, and `from_dict` does not parse it back into a datetime. The result is either a failed outbound sync or an `AssignmentSource` with a wrongly typed `queued`. Serialize `queued` explicitly (e.g. isoformat) and parse it in `from_dict`.

title: New `assignment_source` kwarg is passed to every integration's `sync_assignee_outbound`
body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` on every integration. Any concrete implementation (Jira, Jira Server, GitHub, GitLab, VSTS, etc.) whose signature lacks `**kwargs` or an explicit `assignment_source` parameter will raise TypeError, and outbound assignee sync will break for that provider. The PR does not update or check those implementations. The value is also already consumed by `should_sync`, so passing it on is unnecessary.

title: New task kwarg breaks old workers during rolling deploy
body: `sync_assignee_outbound` tasks are now enqueued with an `assignment_source_dict` kwarg. Workers still running the previous code will reject these tasks with TypeError (unexpected keyword argument) until the deploy completes. Normally the task signature change is shipped before producers start sending the new kwarg.

title: Cycle is only broken for the originating integration; multi-integration loops remain
body: Outbound sync is suppressed only when the target integration is the source integration. If a group is linked to issues in two sync-enabled integrations (e.g. Jira and GitHub), an inbound change from A is still pushed to B. B's webhook then reassigns in Sentry with source B, which is pushed back to A, and so on. Rapid successive edits can therefore still ping-pong between integrations.

title: Unused `assignment_source` parameter added to abstract `sync_status_outbound`
body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature gains an `assignment_source` parameter, but no caller passes it and no status-sync logic uses it. This changes the documented contract for implementers without any effect and suggests status-sync cycles are handled when they are not.

title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a plain default value, so Python evaluates it once when the class is defined. Every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` (including every one from `from_integration`) gets the timestamp of process startup, not of the assignment. Any later use of `queued` for ordering, staleness or debouncing would be wrong. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

title: Raw datetime placed in Celery task kwargs; deserialized type is not validated
body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` uses `dataclasses.asdict`, which leaves `queued` as a `datetime` object, and that dict is passed as a Celery task kwarg. With a JSON task serializer this either fails to serialize or arrives on the worker as a string. `AssignmentSource.from_dict` then does `cls(**input_dict)` with no type conversion, so `queued` silently becomes a `str` despite being typed as `datetime`. Serialize `queued` explicitly (e.g. ISO string or epoch) in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`.

title: New task kwarg is not safe during a rolling deploy
body: Producers now always send `assignment_source_dict` to `sync_assignee_outbound` (even when its value is None). During a rolling deploy, workers still running the old task signature will receive the unexpected kwarg and raise `TypeError`, so assignee syncs fail until every worker is updated. The usual pattern is to deploy the task parameter first and start sending it in a follow-up change.

title: New `assignment_source` kwarg passed to every integration's `sync_assignee_outbound`
body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)` on every provider. Any concrete implementation (Jira, Jira Server, VSTS, GitHub, example, etc.) whose override lacks `**kwargs` will raise `TypeError`, and outbound assignee sync will break for that provider. Confirm that all overrides accept the kwarg, or add it to their signatures.

title: `sync_status_outbound` gains `assignment_source` but nothing passes it
body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature now accepts `assignment_source`, but no caller provides it and status sync does not go through `should_sync` with a source. The same inbound-to-outbound cycle for status changes is therefore not prevented, while the signature implies it is. Either wire the source through the status sync path or drop the unused parameter.

title: No end-to-end test that inbound sync suppresses outbound to the same integration
body: The new test calls `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` directly with an `AssignmentSource`. Nothing exercises `sync_group_assignee_inbound` (assign or deassign) to check that it no longer triggers `sync_assignee_outbound` for the originating integration, which is the cycle this PR is meant to break. There is also no `to_dict`/`from_dict` round-trip test through the task, which would have exposed the datetime serialization problem.

title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a plain default value, so `timezone.now()` runs once when the module is imported. Every `AssignmentSource` created in that process shares the same timestamp, which can be hours or days old. Any later use of `queued` (ordering, staleness checks, debugging) will be wrong. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

title: Task kwargs carry a raw datetime that may not survive serialization
body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` uses `asdict`, so the `queued` value passed to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` is a `datetime` object. If the Celery broker uses a JSON serializer, the enqueue call can fail; this is the inbound webhook path, so the assignment sync would break. If serialization succeeds, `queued` likely comes back as a string, and `from_dict` silently builds an object whose `queued` is not a datetime. Serialize `queued` explicitly (for example as an ISO string or timestamp) and parse it back in `from_dict`. The tests run tasks eagerly via `self.tasks()`, so they may not catch this.

title: New `assignment_source` parameter on abstract `sync_status_outbound` is never used
body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` gains an `assignment_source` parameter, but no caller passes it and status-sync cycles are not addressed anywhere in this PR. Concrete implementations do not declare the parameter either. This changes the abstract contract without effect and suggests status sync is protected against cycles when it is not.

title: No test covers the inbound path that this fix targets
body: The new test calls `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` with a hand-built `AssignmentSource`. Nothing verifies that `sync_group_assignee_inbound` (assign or deassign) skips the outbound sync back to the originating integration. Nothing checks that other integrations linked to the same group still receive the sync. Nothing tests the `to_dict`/`from_dict` round trip through task serialization. The real cycle scenario therefore has no regression coverage.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`. It does not implement the abstract members `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` or the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` points to this class. For any detector of type `metric_alert_fire`, `Detector.detector_handler` will call `group_type.detector_handler(self)` and raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`, which crashes `process_detectors`. Before this change the handler was concrete and returned an empty result. Either keep a concrete stub implementing the abstract methods, or don't wire the handler until it is implemented.

title: Expected occurrence built for wrong group key in test_dedupe
body: `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` builds the expected occurrence with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...)`. It then evaluates group key `"group_key"`. The fingerprint of the expected occurrence (`<id>:val1`) therefore differs from the actual result (`<id>:group_key`). With dataclass equality on `IssueOccurrence`, the equality assertion should fail. If it passes, the test is not checking what it claims. Build the expected occurrence with the same group key that is evaluated.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` now returns a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". This misleads implementers about the new return contract.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated
body:
`MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`. That leaves several abstract members unimplemented: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`.

`Detector.detector_handler` calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`. For any detector of type `metric_alert_fire` that call will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. As a result, `process_detectors` crashes for these detectors instead of returning no results, which is what the previous stub did.

Fix: either implement the methods (stubbed for now) or keep the old non-stateful stub until the real implementation lands.

title: Expected occurrence built for wrong group key in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe
body:
The expected occurrence is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...)`, so its fingerprint is `["<id>:val1"]`. However, `evaluate_group_key_value` is called with group key `"group_key"`, so the handler builds the fingerprint `["<id>:group_key"]`.

`IssueOccurrence` is a dataclass compared field by field, so the equality assertion should fail. If it somehow passes, the test is not actually checking the occurrence produced for that group key.

Fix: build the expected occurrence with `"group_key"`.

title: Mock occurrence ignores value and uses identical ids, so tests can't catch wrong-value or cross-group mixups
body:
`build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores its `value` argument, and every occurrence uses the same hard-coded `id` and `event_id`. Several tests depend on this, for example `group_2` is built with value 6 while the packet value is 10, and `test_results_on_change` uses 6 while the evaluated value is 100.

Because of this, the tests never check that the correct value is passed to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. They also cannot distinguish occurrences from different groups except by fingerprint.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: The `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` docstring still says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". The method now returns a dict keyed by `DetectorGroupKey`.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed from a concrete `DetectorHandler` with an `evaluate` stub to a `StatefulDetectorHandler` subclass whose body is just `pass`. `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares several abstract members: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. As a result, `Detector.detector_handler` does `group_type.detector_handler(self)` for any detector of type `metric_alert_fire`, which raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. That exception propagates out of `process_detectors` and stops processing of every other detector in the batch. Keep a concrete stub implementation until the real one exists.

title: Tests never check the value passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data
body: Expected occurrences are always built with `value=6` even when the evaluated value is 10, 100 or 8, e.g. `group_2` here and in `test_results_on_change`/`test_dedupe`. The tests still pass only because the mock builder ignores `value`. Nothing verifies that `evaluate_group_key_value` passes the correct value or status into the new hook, so a regression in the arguments would go undetected. Use the actual values, or assert on the hook call arguments.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: The `evaluate` docstring still reads "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`", but the return type is now a dict keyed by group key. Update the docstring to describe the new contract for implementers.

title: Monitor context returns raw config, not the copy with the humanized schedule_type
body: `get_monitor_environment_context` copies `monitor.config` into `config` and replaces `schedule_type` with `get_schedule_type_display()`. It then returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of `config`, so the conversion is discarded. The occurrence's monitor context therefore carries the raw integer schedule_type rather than the display label. This was carried over unchanged from `mark_failed.py`, but the move into a new module is a good time to fix it by returning `config`.

title: Renamed/moved helpers drop the old import paths with no compatibility aliases
body:
These names are no longer available from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`:
- `mark_failed_threshold` is now `incidents.try_incident_threshold`.
- `create_issue_platform_occurrence` is now `incident_occurrence.create_incident_occurrence`.
- `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context` and `SimpleCheckIn` have moved to other modules.

No re-exports or aliases are left behind, and no test files were updated in this PR. Any test that patches `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.<name>` or imports these helpers from `mark_failed` will fail with AttributeError or ImportError, and so will other modules or getsentry code that do the same. Either update those references or keep temporary re-exports in `mark_failed.py`.

title: Moved/renamed helpers removed from mark_failed with no compatibility re-exports
body: This PR deletes `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, `SimpleCheckIn` and the `HUMAN_FAILURE_*` maps from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`. Two of the functions are also renamed (`try_incident_threshold`, `create_incident_occurrence`). No test files or other callers are updated in this PR. Any existing `from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed import get_failure_reason` (or `mock.patch` targets on these names) will now fail with ImportError/AttributeError. Callers and tests should be updated to the new modules, or the old names re-exported from `mark_failed`.

title: Computed config copy with readable schedule_type is discarded
body: `get_monitor_environment_context` copies the monitor config and replaces `schedule_type` with its display value. It then returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the raw original) instead of the modified `config`. As a result, the occurrence's monitor context carries the raw integer schedule_type, and the transformation is dead code. This bug predates the PR but is carried into the new module.

title: Functions renamed and moved with no compatibility re-exports
body: `mark_failed_threshold` was renamed to `try_incident_threshold` in `logic/incidents.py`. `create_issue_platform_occurrence` was renamed to `create_incident_occurrence` in `logic/incident_occurrence.py`. `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context` and `SimpleCheckIn` were also moved out of `mark_failed.py`. Nothing is re-exported from the old module, and the PR changes no other callers or tests. Any existing import or `mock.patch` target of `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.<name>` (for example in the mark_failed tests) will now fail with ImportError or AttributeError. Either update those references in this PR or keep aliases in `mark_failed.py`.

title: Copied config with readable schedule_type is computed but never used
body: `get_monitor_environment_context` copies the monitor config and replaces `schedule_type` with its human-readable label. It then returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config`, the original unmodified dict, instead of the local `config`. As a result the monitor context on the issue event shows the raw `schedule_type` value rather than the display label. The bug predates this PR but is carried into the new module; returning `config` would fix it.

title: Hung flusher processes are never killed before a replacement is spawned
body:
In production the flusher creates processes with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which yields `SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is False and `process.kill()` is never called.

The old code called `kill()` unconditionally. Now, when a process is detected as hung (`cause = "hang"`), a new process is started for the same shards while the old one keeps running. Two flushers then work the same Redis shards concurrently, which can produce duplicate or fragmented segments and leaks a process on every restart.

Fix: check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, or test for `threading.Thread` instead.

title: join() never terminates spawned processes
body:
`join()` has the same `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check as the restart path. It is always False for `SpawnProcess`, so `terminate()` is never called on flusher processes that are still alive after the deadline. With N processes per consumer, any that do not exit in time keep running and flushing until the parent process exits.

Fix: check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`.

title: join() stops handling remaining processes once the deadline passes
body: When the deadline is exceeded, the loop `break`s. Every process after that point is neither waited on nor terminated, so on a slow shutdown some flusher processes are left running. Only the waiting should be skipped after the deadline; termination of each remaining process should still happen.

title: Test sleep is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
body: The test patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at the start. The later `time.sleep(0.1)`, meant to "give flusher threads time to process after drift change", therefore does nothing. The test relies on the flusher thread winning a race before `join()` sets the stopped flag, which makes it flaky. Fix: capture the original sleep before patching, or poll for the expected message with a timeout.

title: CLI default contradicts the factory/flusher default of one process per shard
body: `SpanFlusher` treats `max_processes=None` as "one process per shard", and the PR description says the flusher should spawn a process per shard. However, the `--flusher-processes` CLI option defaults to 1. Every consumer started through the CLI will therefore keep a single flusher process unless the flag is passed explicitly, so the advertised scaling is not enabled by default.

title: Inconsistent metric tag name ("shards" vs "shard")
body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `shards`, while the neighbouring `produce` and `segment_size_bytes` metrics use `shard`. Dashboards that filter or group by one tag name will miss the other metric.

title: Unhealthy flusher processes are never killed because the isinstance check misses SpawnProcess
body: Processes are created with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, so each one is a `SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False in production. The old code called `kill()` unconditionally; with the new guard, a hung flusher is never killed. A replacement process is still spawned for the same shards, so two processes flush the same shards at once. That can produce duplicate or fragmented segments, and leaked processes pile up with each restart. Check for `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` instead, or check `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`. The same wrong check in `join()` (line 346) means `terminate()` is never called either.

title: join() stops early and skips terminating the remaining processes once the deadline passes
body: When the deadline is exceeded, the loop does `break`. Every process after that point is left without `terminate()` being called. This happens often, because `next_step.join(timeout)` runs first and can use up most of the timeout. Those flusher processes keep running past consumer shutdown or rebalance and may still touch Redis and Kafka for shards that are no longer assigned. The loop should skip the waiting but still terminate every remaining process.

title: Restart limit is now counted per process, so total allowed restarts scales with process count
body: `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` used to cap the total number of flusher restarts before the consumer is failed. It is now tracked separately for each process index. With N processes, the consumer tolerates up to N*(MAX+1) crashes before raising, which weakens the crash-loop safeguard.

title: Inconsistent metric tag key: 'shards' here vs 'shard' elsewhere
body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `shards`, while `flusher.produce`, `segment_size_bytes` and `flusher_unhealthy` use `shard`. Dashboards and queries that filter or group by `shard` will miss this metric. In addition, the tag value is a comma-joined list of shards (e.g. "0,4,8") on some metrics and a single shard elsewhere, which adds tag cardinality and makes the values inconsistent.

title: Docstring claims one process per shard, but the CLI default is a single process
body: The class docstring says it "Creates one process per shard". The `--flusher-processes` CLI option defaults to 1, so in production all shards share a single process unless the option is set explicitly. One process per shard only happens when `max_processes` is None or 0.

title: Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
body: The test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so the new `time.sleep(0.1)`, meant to "give flusher threads time to process", does nothing. The test still relies on the flusher thread happening to flush before it sees `stopped` in `join()`. It therefore stays timing-dependent and potentially flaky, despite the comment suggesting otherwise.

title: Unhealthy flusher processes are never killed before a replacement starts
body:
Processes are created from the 'spawn' context, so they are `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. That class subclasses `BaseProcess` directly, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False and `process.kill()` is skipped. The old code called `kill()` unconditionally.

Now, when a process is detected as hung, a new process is spawned for the same shards while the old one keeps running. Both flush the same Redis shards, which can produce duplicate or fragmented segments to Kafka. Hung processes also accumulate with every restart.

Fix: check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, or check `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`.

title: join() never terminates flusher processes
body:
The same broken `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check is used here, and it is always False for `SpawnProcess`. As a result, `terminate()` is never called on processes that are still running after the timeout.

In addition, when the deadline is exceeded, the `break` at line 341 exits the loop. Every remaining process is skipped and gets neither a wait nor a terminate.

With N processes, a slow shutdown can leave several orphaned flushers still writing to Kafka and Redis during rebalance or exit.

title: Inconsistent metric tag name 'shards' vs 'shard'
body:
`spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `shards`, while `flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use `shard`. Dashboards or queries that group by one tag name will silently miss the other metric.

Also, `flusher_unhealthy` tags `shard` with an individual int, whereas the other metrics tag it with a comma-joined list. The same tag key therefore carries different value semantics.

title: Dead method _create_process_for_shard
body: `_create_process_for_shard` is never called anywhere. It duplicates the restart logic and could confuse future maintainers, so it should be removed.

title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
body:
The test does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at the top. That makes the added `time.sleep(0.1)`, meant to give flusher threads time to process, do nothing.

The test only passes because `join()` happens to wait for the threads. The comment is misleading, and the assertion on `messages` is potentially racy.

title: CLI default of 1 contradicts the 'process per shard' default in SpanFlusher
body:
`SpanFlusher` and the factory treat `max_processes=None` as "one process per shard". However, the `--flusher-processes` CLI option defaults to 1, so production consumers keep a single flusher process unless the flag is explicitly passed.

The class docstring states "Creates one process per shard", which is inaccurate for the default deployment. Either the default or the documentation should be aligned.

title: Shared FixedQueuePool is permanently shut down on first rebalance, silently dropping messages afterwards
body:
The `FixedQueuePool` is created once in the factory `__init__`. Every strategy from `create_with_partitions` reuses it, but `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()`/`join()` call `queue_pool.shutdown()`, which shuts down all queues and stops the workers.

Arroyo closes the strategy on every partition revocation, so after the first rebalance the next strategy gets a dead pool. `work_queue.put` then raises `queue.ShutDown`. `submit` catches it and marks the offset as completed. As a result every subsequent message is skipped without being processed, yet its offset is committed. This is silent data loss.

The pool should be owned by the strategy (created per `create_with_partitions`), or the strategy should not shut down a factory-owned pool.

title: Arroyo commit callback invoked from a background thread
body:
`_commit_loop` runs in its own daemon thread and calls `commit_function` there, which invokes the Arroyo `Commit` callable. That callable stages offsets on the `StreamProcessor`/`KafkaConsumer`, which are single-threaded and not thread-safe. This races with `poll`/`stage_offsets` on the main thread.

It can also commit offsets for partitions that were already revoked, because the commit thread and workers keep running during a rebalance. Offsets should be collected in the background but committed from the strategy's `poll()`/`submit()` on the consumer thread.

title: Unbounded queues: no backpressure despite docstring claim
body:
Each `queue.Queue()` is created without a `maxsize`, and `submit` never raises `MessageRejected`. A slow group therefore lets its queue grow without limit while the consumer keeps polling Kafka, so memory grows unbounded.

The class docstring promises "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", which is false. Bound the queues and reject or pause when they are full.

title: Commits stall permanently on natural Kafka offset gaps
body:
`get_committable_offsets` stops at the first offset that is not in `all_offsets`. Kafka offsets are not guaranteed to be contiguous: transactional control markers and compacted topics both leave gaps. Any such gap means the committed offset never advances past it, even though every received message is processed.

The result is ever-growing reported lag and full reprocessing on restart. The contiguity check should only consider offsets that were actually received, for example by advancing to the minimum outstanding offset minus 1, or to the max seen when nothing is outstanding.

title: close() stops committing before workers drain, so processed work is never committed
body:
`close()` first sets `shutdown_event` and joins the commit thread. Only after that does it shut down the pool, which lets workers finish their remaining queued items. There is no final commit.

Items completed during that drain, plus anything completed in the last second before shutdown, are never committed. They get reprocessed after every rebalance or restart. Drain the workers first, then perform one final commit.

title: Failed processing still marks offset complete; docstring claims commit only after success
body:
The `finally` block calls `complete_offset` even when `result_processor` raised, so failed messages are committed. That contradicts the class guarantee "Only commits offsets after successful processing".

Either the behavior or the documentation should change.

title: Error-handling test asserts no commit, contradicting implementation; passes only by timing
body:
In `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling`, the worker completes offsets in `finally` even on exceptions. Offsets 100 and 101 therefore become committable and are committed on the next 1s tick of the commit loop.

The test asserts that no commit happened, and it only passes because it checks before the commit loop fires. That makes it flaky. It also contradicts its own docstring, which says errors should not block commits.

title: Shared queue pool is shut down on rebalance, so later messages are silently dropped and committed
body:
The `FixedQueuePool` is created once in `__init__`, but every `create_with_partitions` call wraps that same pool in a new `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy`. On a partition revocation or rebalance, arroyo calls `close()`/`join()` on the old strategy. That calls `queue_pool.shutdown()`, which shuts down every queue and stops every worker permanently.

The next strategy built after reassignment reuses the dead pool:
- `work_queue.put` raises `queue.ShutDown`.
- `submit` catches it in its generic `except`, then calls `add_offset` and `complete_offset` for that message.
- The commit loop commits those offsets.

After the first rebalance, every uptime result is dropped but its offset is still committed. Either build the pool per strategy, or don't shut down the shared pool in the strategy's `close()`.

title: Arroyo commit callback invoked from a background thread
body:
`_commit_loop` runs on its own daemon thread and calls `self.commit_function`, which calls arroyo's `Commit`, roughly once per second. Arroyo's commit callback is not thread-safe and is meant to be called from the strategy's `submit`/`poll` on the consumer thread.

Calling it concurrently with the `StreamProcessor` run loop can corrupt its staged-offset state. It can also commit after the processor has started revoking partitions or shutting down, because `terminate()` doesn't join this thread. Collect committable offsets here, but perform the commit inside `poll()` on the main thread.

title: Shutdown discards queued work and never commits work that finished after the last tick
body:
`shutdown()` sets `worker.shutdown = True` before shutting down the queues. Each worker exits after its current item, so items still waiting in the queues are never processed. `queue.shutdown(immediate=False)` would normally drain them, but the flag defeats that.

In `close()`, the commit thread is also stopped before the pool shuts down. Offsets for items that finished in the final window are never committed, so they are reprocessed after reassignment.

`join(timeout)` ignores its timeout and does no draining either. On rebalance this produces both skipped items (in-memory loss, recovered only by redelivery) and duplicates. Drain the queues, wait for workers, then do a final commit before returning from `join`.

title: Unbounded queues give no backpressure, despite the docstring
body: Each queue is `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize`, and `submit` never raises `MessageRejected`. A single slow subscription will therefore let its queue grow without limit while the consumer keeps polling Kafka, risking OOM. The strategy docstring promises "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", which is false. Bound the queues and raise `MessageRejected` when one is full.

title: Commits stall permanently when partition offsets are not contiguous
body:
`get_committable_offsets` only advances while every integer offset between `start` and `max_offset` has been seen in `all_offsets`. Kafka offsets are not guaranteed to be contiguous: transactional control records, compacted topics, and aborted transactions all leave gaps that the consumer never receives.

Any such gap blocks commits for that partition forever, while `all_offsets` keeps growing. Track contiguity only among the offsets actually received (for example, commit up to just below the lowest outstanding offset), not across absolute integer ranges.

title: Failed items are committed, contradicting "only commits after successful processing"
body: The worker's `finally` block calls `complete_offset` even when `result_processor` raises. Decode and submit failures are also completed immediately. Offsets are therefore committed regardless of processing outcome, which is at-most-once delivery. The class docstring says "Only commits offsets after successful processing" and "No item is lost", which is misleading for anyone relying on it.

title: Error-handling test asserts no commit, contrary to implementation, and passes only by timing
body:
`test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` asserts that the partition is not committed after one processing failure. The implementation does mark failed offsets complete, so both 100 and 101 become committable and are committed on the next one-second commit tick.

The test passes only because it exits roughly 0.2s after processing finishes, before the commit thread wakes up. It is flaky on slow CI, and it documents behavior the code doesn't have. Assert the real semantics deterministically instead.

title: Shared queue pool is shut down on rebalance, then reused, so messages are silently dropped and committed
body:
`FixedQueuePool` is created once in the factory `__init__`, and every `create_with_partitions` call hands that same `self.queue_pool` to a new `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy`. When arroyo revokes partitions it calls `close()`/`join()` on the old strategy, and that calls `queue_pool.shutdown()`: every queue is shut down and every worker thread exits.

On the next assignment the new strategy reuses the dead pool. `work_queue.put()` then raises `queue.ShutDown`. `submit()` catches it in its generic `except`, and that handler adds and immediately completes the offset. The commit loop then commits it.

After the first rebalance, every message is acknowledged without being processed. The `OffsetTracker` state (`last_committed`, revoked partitions) also carries over between assignments, so a new commit loop can commit partitions it no longer owns. Create a fresh pool/tracker per strategy, or don't shut the shared pool down in `close()`.

title: Arroyo commit callback invoked from a background thread
body:
`_commit_loop` runs on its own daemon thread and calls `commit_function`, which calls arroyo's `Commit` callable. Arroyo's StreamProcessor expects strategies to call commit from the consumer thread, during `submit`/`poll`/`join`. Calling it concurrently with the processor's own commit/poll handling races on the processor's internal offset bookkeeping and on the Kafka consumer.

It can also commit during or after a revocation, for partitions no longer assigned. Commits should instead be staged by the background thread and flushed from `poll()`.

title: Contiguous-offset requirement stalls commits on natural Kafka offset gaps
body:
`get_committable_offsets` only advances while every integer offset in `[start, max]` has been seen and completed. If an offset never arrives, the loop breaks there and nothing past it is ever committed.

Kafka offsets are not guaranteed to be contiguous. Transactional control records, compacted topics, and an initial position that differs from `min_offset` after a prior commit can all leave gaps. One such gap permanently blocks commits for that partition. The consumer keeps processing, but committed lag grows without bound and a restart reprocesses everything.

The committable point should be derived from the offsets actually seen, e.g. the lowest outstanding offset minus one, or the max seen offset when nothing is outstanding.

title: Unbounded queues: no backpressure despite docstring claim
body:
Queues are created with `queue.Queue()` (unbounded), and `submit()` never raises `MessageRejected`. The strategy docstring nonetheless says "Natural backpressure when queues fill up".

If a worker is slow, as with the slow items this PR is meant to address, the consumer keeps pulling from Kafka and buffering in memory without limit. That can lead to OOM and a very large redelivery window on crash. Use a bounded queue and raise `MessageRejected` when it is full.

title: close/join don't drain and commit in-flight work; join ignores timeout
body:
`close()` stops the commit thread first and only then shuts down the queues. Any items the workers finish during shutdown are never committed.

Workers also check `self.shutdown`, which is set to True before the queues are shut down, so they exit after their current item instead of draining. That makes the graceful `immediate=False` shutdown ineffective.

`join(timeout)` ignores its timeout and does not wait for outstanding work before a final commit. On every rebalance or shutdown, all queued and processed-but-uncommitted messages are redelivered.

title: Error-handling test asserts no commit, which only holds due to timing
body:
In `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling`, the worker's `finally` block marks offset 100 complete even when processing raises, and offset 101 completes normally. The commit loop will therefore commit offset 102.

The test asserts that nothing has been committed for the partition. That passes only because the wait loop exits after about 0.2s, before the commit thread's first 1s tick. The test contradicts the implemented behaviour (failed items are committed) and is timing-dependent and flaky.

title: Backup code consumption is not atomic (replay race)
body: In the credentials `authorize` handler, the backup code is checked against a value read earlier and then the whole re-encrypted array is written back with a plain update. There is no compare-and-set or transaction. Two concurrent logins using the same backup code both pass the check and both succeed, so a single-use code can be used more than once. A concurrent use of two different codes also loses one of the deletions, leaving a used code valid.

title: Backup code compared with non-constant-time indexOf and no normalization
body: `indexOf` performs a plain string comparison against the stored codes. The input is also not lowercased or trimmed, so a code typed in uppercase (the placeholder shows `XXXXX-XXXXX`) is rejected even though it is valid. A timing-safe comparison would also be preferable.

title: Rate-limit error not mapped to a message
body: Backup codes are 40-bit secrets, and their brute-force protection depends on the rate limit enforced in `authorize`. The login page has no specific mapping for the RateLimitExceeded error, so a rate-limited user only sees the generic "something went wrong" fallback instead of being told they have been rate limited.

title: Non-string backupCode crashes handler
body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` is called without checking the type. Any truthy non-string value (for example a number) throws a TypeError, which results in a 500 response instead of a 400.

title: Plaintext backup codes remain in component state after close
body: `resetState` clears the password, error and step, but not `backupCodes`, the secret, the QR data URI, or the blob URL. The codes and secret stay in memory, and the object URL is never revoked when the modal closes.

title: formatBackupCode used before its declaration
body: `handleSetup` calls `formatBackupCode`, which is a `const` arrow function declared later in the component body. This works only because `handleSetup` runs after render, so the code is fragile. Separately, `useState([])` infers the type `never[]`, so `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` and the mapping over codes are poorly typed.

title: Backup code path skips password check for external-TOTP flow
body: The password check runs only when `!credentials.totpCode`, but the backup-code branch is selected by `credentials.backupCode`. A client can send a valid backup code together with any non-empty `totpCode`, which skips the password verification. Because the backupCode branch is taken first, the totpCode is never validated. A backup code alone then grants login without the password, making it a single factor.

title: Backup code consumption is not atomic
body: The code reads the backup codes, checks them in memory, and then writes the re-encrypted list back with no transaction or compare-and-set. Concurrent login requests can all validate the same code before any of them writes, so a single-use code can be used several times. A concurrent write can also overwrite another request's update.

title: Unvalidated backupCode type crashes handler
body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` assumes the value is a string. A non-string value, such as a number or an array, throws and returns a 500. The client also always sends `backupCode` (possibly an empty string) alongside `code`, and the request is routed only by truthiness. Nothing validates the format or type of the value.

title: Lost-access option unavailable in external TOTP flow
body: When `totpEmail` is set (Google/SAML users with 2FA), the page shows ExternalTotpFooter, which has no 'Lost access' button. Those users cannot use their backup codes. This is also the only flow where the password check is legitimately skipped.

title: formatBackupCode used before its const declaration
body: `handleSetup` calls `formatBackupCode`, which is declared later with `const`. This works only because the call happens at runtime, after render. The blob object URL is also never revoked when the modal closes, so it leaks for the life of the page.

title: Backup code consumption is non-atomic (race allows reuse)
body: The backup code check reads user.backupCodes, nulls the matching entry in memory, then writes the array back with no compare-and-swap or transaction. Two concurrent logins with the same code both pass the check before either update lands, so one 'single-use' code can open multiple sessions. A concurrent use of a different code can also be overwritten by the last write, which revives a code that was already consumed.

title: Unvalidated backupCode string can match nulled entries or throw
body: `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll` is called on raw input. Used codes are stored as `null`, so the check relies on indexOf of a string never matching null. That holds today, but the input is never validated for length or format. `replaceAll` also needs ES2021; on older runtimes this throws, and the user sees a generic error instead of a proper message.

title: Backup codes screen can be dismissed without onEnable
body: On the DisplayBackupCodes step, 2FA is already enabled on the server. If the dialog is closed through onOpenChange (Escape key or overlay click) instead of the Close button, onEnable and resetState never run. The parent UI then shows 2FA as disabled while it is actually on. The step also stays at DisplayBackupCodes the next time the modal opens.

title: Non-string backupCode in request body causes 500
body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` assumes a string. Any other truthy value (a number, an array) throws an unhandled exception and returns a 500 instead of a 400 validation error.

title: formatBackupCode used before its const declaration
body: handleSetup calls `formatBackupCode`, which is declared later in the component body as a `const`. This only works because handleSetup runs asynchronously after render. It is fragile: an early call would throw a temporal dead zone error.

title: No tests for logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
body: The new authentication paths are untested: backup-code login, single-use enforcement, incorrect code, and disabling 2FA with a backup code. The PR leaves only a TODO comment for these cases.

title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields undefined when the event has no destination calendar, which happens often since many callers now pass `[]` or null. The code then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining, so any booking with a Google Meet location and no destination calendar throws a TypeError and booking creation fails. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

title: Video references lose credentialId
body: In `create`, `credentialId` is now set to `undefined` for every non-calendar result, where it previously was `result.credentialId`. Video booking references are therefore stored without a credentialId. The cancel and update flows (for example `handleCancelBooking`, which requires `bookingVideoReference.credentialId`) then skip deleting the video meeting.

title: Fallback lookup compares against a falsy externalCalendarId
body: The fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, yet it searches for a destination calendar whose `externalId === externalCalendarId`. That search can never match, so `selectedCalendar` is undefined in update. The old behaviour of falling back to the event's destination calendar is lost. The same broken lookup appears in deleteEvent at line 317.

title: Hangout patch uses undefined calendarId
body: After insert, the patch call uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which can be undefined, while the insert itself used `selectedCalendar || "primary"`. When there is no matching destination calendar, the patch that adds the Meet link to the description fails.

title: Calendar events created from the un-processed event
body: `createAllCalendarEvents` receives `cloneDeep(event)` rather than `evt`. As a result, the video call data, the Cal Video location fallback and the iCalUID set on `evt` are not reflected in the created calendar events.

title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar event
body: Multiple calendar references per booking are now supported, but when `newBookingId` is set only `booking.references.find(...)` (the first calendar reference) is deleted. Calendar events belonging to the other collective hosts stay orphaned in their calendars.

title: Collective host calendars dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
body: When neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, `destinationCalendar` is set to null. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so the other hosts never get calendar events. Initialize it to `[]` instead of null.

title: Slug condition inverted
body: This change was previously `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`. It is now `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, which inverts the logic. With billing enabled the slug is set directly (bypassing payment), and without billing the org gets no slug. This is unrelated to the PR's purpose and is a regression.

title: Recurring deletions repeated per reference and miss other hosts
body: For recurring bookings, the inner block loops over all of the organizer's calendar credentials and deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking. That whole block now runs once per calendar reference, so deletes are duplicated. The other hosts' events are never deleted, because their credentials are not among the organizer's credentials.

title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` gives undefined when the array is empty or null, and the next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. This throws a TypeError for any Google Meet booking without a destination calendar. Previously the code used `?.`. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

title: Team member calendars dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing. Collective hosts' calendars are silently ignored, which is exactly the scenario this PR is meant to fix.

title: Reschedule merge only deletes the first host's old calendar event
body: When `newBookingId` is set, only the first `_calendar` reference (`find`) is deleted. With multiple hosts there are several references, so the other hosts keep stale events on their calendars after a reschedule.

title: Recurring cancel repeats the full delete for every reference and ignores other hosts' credentials
body: Inside the per-reference loop, the recurring branch iterates over all of the organizer's calendar credentials and all updated bookings. It does this once for each reference, so the same deletes run multiple times. It also only uses the first `_calendar` ref and the organizer's credentials, so other hosts' recurring events are never deleted.

title: Fallback lookup can never match
body: The `find` that compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it can never match anything. The previous fallback to the destination calendar's externalId is lost. Update and delete then go to undefined in update, or to `primary` in delete, instead of the configured calendar. The same issue appears in deleteEvent at line 317.

title: Inverted slug condition for org creation
body: The original code set `slug` when billing was disabled (`!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`). The new code sets it when billing is enabled, which bypasses the paid slug request flow. When billing is disabled, organizations are now created without a slug. This change is unrelated to the PR and is a regression.

title: E2E expectations inconsistent with new array type
body: BOOKING_CREATED (line 119) and BOOKING_REQUESTED (line 373) still expect `destinationCalendar: null`. The payload is now an array or null, depending on the code path. BOOKING_REJECTED was changed to `[]`, so these expectations should be checked for consistency.

title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` comes from destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so it is undefined whenever there is no destination calendar. The code then reads `.integration` on it without optional chaining. Any booking with Google Meet as location and no destination calendar throws a TypeError, which breaks booking creation. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

title: Inverted slug condition for organization creation
body: The original code set `slug` only when team billing was disabled (`!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`). The new code sets it only when billing is enabled. Self-hosted instances without billing now create orgs with no slug. Billing instances get a slug set immediately, even though they are meant to store it as `requestedSlug` until payment. This unrelated change reverses the intended behavior.

title: Recurring cancellation deletes are repeated per reference and only use the first calendar reference
body: The recurring-cancel branch now runs inside the loop over every calendar reference. Each iteration iterates all of the organizer's credentials and deletes only the first `_calendar` reference of each updated booking. With several hosts, the same deletes run N times and the other hosts' events are never deleted. In addition, those deleted results are pushed into `apiDeletes` after they have already been awaited.

title: Only the first old calendar event is deleted when merging on reschedule
body: `updateAllCalendarEvents` now updates all calendar references. When `newBookingId` is set, however, it still deletes only `booking.references.find(...)`, i.e. the first old calendar event. The other hosts' old events are left orphaned in their calendars.

title: updateEvent called with possibly undefined credential
body: If the credential is neither in memory nor found in the DB (or has no app slug), `credential` is undefined and is still passed to `updateEvent`. `updateEvent` then reads `credential.appName` and throws, and the catch block marks every reference as failed. References whose credential is missing should be skipped instead.

title: Organizer email taken from first destination calendar for every host's event
body: The organizer attendee email is always the first (main host's) destination calendar `externalId`. When the event is created in another host's calendar, the organizer email shown is the main host's calendar ID, not the organizer of that copy. This is inconsistent with the per-credential `selectedCalendar` used for the insert.

title: Hangout patch uses undefined calendarId
body: `selectedCalendar` can now be undefined, in which case the insert falls back to "primary". The follow-up `events.patch` that adds the hangout link still passes `selectedCalendar` without that fallback, so the patch request fails. The patch should use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` value.

title: Fallback lookup compares against falsy externalCalendarId
body: This lookup only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then searches for a calendar whose `externalId` equals that falsy value, which never matches. The fallback therefore always yields undefined, which is a regression from using the destination calendar. The same problem exists in `deleteEvent`.

title: Credential saved as the SafeParseReturn wrapper instead of the token data
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result object ({success, data}), not the parsed token. Before this change `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the token itself. Now `key` is the wrapper, so prisma writes {success:true,data:{...}} into the credential. On the next load, googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) fails and Google Calendar breaks for every user whose token was refreshed.

title: prisma used without import; refresh runs on every instantiation
body: `prisma` is never imported in this file, so the new prisma.credential.update call throws a ReferenceError (or fails type-check). In addition, the refresh request is sent on every service construction, the refreshed access token is never passed to the jsforce Connection (it still uses the old credentialKey.access_token), and the sync endpoint path (refreshOAuthTokens) is not used at all.

title: credentialId passed where userId is expected
body: refreshOAuthTokens takes a userId as its third argument, but this call passes credentialId. When sync is enabled, the sync endpoint is asked for tokens for the wrong Cal.com user, which can hand out another user's credentials.

title: Sync path returns a fetch Response, which callers do not expect
body: When sync is enabled this function returns a raw fetch Response. Several callers expect a different shape: Google reads `res.data`, Zoho and Bigin read `tokenInfo.data`, and HubSpot uses the result directly as a token object. All of these break when sync is enabled. The request also sends no auth header or secret to the sync endpoint.

title: Bogus zod schema keys
body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the literal key "[object Object]". Both computed keys collapse to that same key, and the first one requires a number, so validation of real token responses fails. Separately, the function injects the fake refresh_token "refresh_token" when none is returned, and that value is then persisted; Zoom and Webex would store it and use it for later refreshes.

title: Non-constant-time secret comparison; no method check
body: The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time and leaks timing information. The handler accepts any HTTP method. Invalid input causes zod parse and JSON/decrypt errors to throw as 500s. Use timingSafeEqual, restrict to POST, and return 400 on invalid input.

title: Wrong app slug 'zoomvideo'
body: The Zoom app slug is "zoom", not "zoomvideo". The sync endpoint will receive a slug that does not match what the webhook handler and the app store use, so the parent application cannot resolve the right app.

title: Google credential key stored as safeParse result wrapper
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParseReturnType of the form {success, data}. Here it is used directly as `key` and saved to the DB. Previously the code saved googleCredentialSchema.parse output, i.e. the token object itself. After the first refresh the stored key becomes {success, data}, which breaks googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) on the next load and disables the calendar.

title: Sync endpoint Response has no .data
body: When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response. This code reads `res?.data` as if it were a gaxios response. A fetch Response has no `.data`, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws. Google token refresh is always broken in sync mode. The same mismatch affects hubspot (expects a token object), zoho-bigin and zohocrm (expect an axios `.data`).

title: prisma used without import; refresh on every construction
body: `prisma` is referenced but never imported in this file, so it is undefined and getClient throws a ReferenceError at runtime. Separately, the token is refreshed on every service instantiation. Even after refreshing, the jsforce Connection is still built with the old credentialKey.access_token rather than the new one.

title: credentialId passed as userId
body: refreshOAuthTokens expects a userId, but this call passes credentialId. The sync endpoint is therefore asked for tokens belonging to the wrong user, which can leak another user's tokens or return the wrong account's tokens.

title: Wrong app slug 'zoomvideo'
body: The app slug for Zoom is "zoom", as used in callback.ts and on credential.appId. Sending "zoomvideo" to the sync endpoint means the self-hosted side will not match the app.

title: Non-constant-time secret compare; unhandled parse errors
body: The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time and is open to timing attacks; use timingSafeEqual. There is also no HTTP method check. zod `.parse` and JSON.parse/decrypt failures are not caught, so bad input produces 500 errors instead of 400s.

title: Bogus zod schema keys and fake refresh_token
body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the literal key "[object Object]", so the schema actually requires a property literally named that. With both computed keys collapsing to that one name, the last entry wins and it ends up optional unknown, so the expiry check is not enforced at all. Also, a missing refresh_token is replaced with the placeholder string "refresh_token" and persisted, which corrupts stored credentials outside sync mode.

title: Refresh failures now throw instead of logging
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on an invalid response. The previous code merged what it could and logged the zod error and the Microsoft response. That diagnostic logging has been removed, and the `tokenResponse.success &&` check on the next line is now dead code.

title: Hardcoded redirect slug mismatches callback
body: add.ts now hardcodes "zoho-bigin" in the redirect URI, while callback.ts still builds it from appConfig.slug. If the two values ever differ, the OAuth token exchange fails because the redirect_uri does not match.

title: Credential key saved as safeParse result wrapper
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseReturn object `{success, data}`, not the parsed data. Before this change the code stored the output of `googleCredentialSchema.parse`. Now the whole wrapper is written to credential.key, so the stored credential becomes `{success: true, data: {...}}`. The next googleCredentialSchema.parse of that key fails and Google Calendar breaks after the first token refresh.

title: Sync endpoint fetch Response has no .data
body: When syncing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this code reads `res?.data` (the gaxios shape). `token` is undefined, so `token.access_token` throws. Hubspot, zoho-bigin and zohocrm have the same problem: they read `.data` or token fields directly from the return value instead of calling `.json()`.

title: prisma used without import
body: `prisma.credential.update` is called, but this file never imports prisma. The call throws a ReferenceError at runtime, which breaks every Salesforce client creation.

title: Token refreshed on every client construction; new token unused
body: getClient refreshes the token unconditionally on every instantiation. It also bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, so sync mode is ignored here. It then builds the connection with the old `credentialKey.access_token` instead of the freshly fetched one.

title: Bogus zod schema keys
body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the literal key "[object Object]". Both computed keys collapse to that same string, so the schema actually requires a property named "[object Object]". The intent was to accept any numeric expiry field, but in sync mode valid responses fail validation.

title: Overwrites missing refresh_token with literal placeholder
body: When the response has no refresh_token, it is set to the string "refresh_token". That placeholder gets persisted to the DB as the credential's refresh token, so later refreshes against the real provider fail. Separately, office365 previously tolerated parse failures, but the function now throws on them.

title: credentialId passed as userId
body: refreshOAuthTokens expects a userId, but this call passes credentialId. The sync endpoint is therefore asked for tokens belonging to whatever user happens to have that id, which can fetch the wrong user's credentials.

title: Wrong app slug 'zoomvideo'
body: The app slug is "zoom" (the credential is created with appId "zoom"), but the sync request sends "zoomvideo". The self-hoster's endpoint won't recognize this slug.

title: Non-constant-time secret compare; parse errors return 500
body: The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time and leaks timing information about the secret. Separately, zod `parse` and `JSON.parse` of the decrypted keys throw on bad input, so malformed requests return 500 instead of 400.

title: Sync endpoint call unauthenticated, unchecked
body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no secret header, so the self-hoster's endpoint cannot verify the caller and anyone can request user tokens from it. The response status is also never checked, so error responses are treated as token payloads.

title: Team admin check requires both admin AND owner
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner. A team admin who is not also the owner fails the check and cannot add guests. It should use ||.

title: New-guest emails use the unfiltered guests list
body: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`. An existing attendee who is resubmitted in the list is matched as a 'new guest' and gets a scheduled-booking email instead of the update email. Pass uniqueGuests.

title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive
body: Blacklisted emails are lowercased but the guest emails are not, so a mixed-case address such as Foo@x.com bypasses the blacklist. Comparison against existing attendees is also case-sensitive, so the same person can be added again with different casing.

title: Any attendee can add unlimited guests, triggering emails to arbitrary addresses
body: Any attendee is authorized, there is no cap on the length of the guests array, and the event type's guest settings are not checked. This lets anyone who booked a meeting send calendar invites/emails from the platform to arbitrary addresses (spam vector).

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the organizer's
body: EventManager is built from ctx.user and that user's credentials. When an attendee or team admin calls the endpoint, the organizer's calendar event is updated with the wrong credentials, so it fails or is skipped. The organizer's credentials (booking.user) should be used.

title: Calendar update failure aborts after the DB write
