body: The attendees are already persisted when updateCalendarAttendees runs, and its errors are not caught. If it throws, the client sees an error even though the guests were saved, and no emails are sent.

title: Error toast fallback never used
body: `message` is always a non-empty template string, possibly 'undefined: ...'. Because of that, the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback in the toast is never reached.

title: Invalid-email error never clears
body: isInvalidEmail is set to true on a failed validation but is never reset when validation later succeeds or after a successful add. A stale error message stays visible in the dialog.

title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner. A team admin who is not the owner, or an owner who is not reported as an admin, fails the check. Unless they are also the organizer or an attendee, they get FORBIDDEN, even though the variable name says either role should be enough. Use || instead of &&.

title: Scheduled emails sent to all input guests rather than only newly added ones
body: sendAddGuestsEmails is passed `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`. If a submitted email was already an attendee, that existing attendee receives a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notification. Pass uniqueGuests.

title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive
body: The blacklist entries are lowercased, but guest emails are compared as typed. Duplicate detection against existing attendees is also an exact-case comparison. A mixed-case variant of a blacklisted or existing email therefore bypasses both checks and gets added. Lowercase the guest emails before comparing.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the organizer's
body: EventManager is built from ctx.user and ctx.user's credentials. When an attendee or a team admin adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with credentials that do not own the booking's calendar references. The update fails or throws, and because it is not caught, the request errors even though the attendee rows are already saved. Use the booking user's credentials (booking.user.credentials) instead.

title: No restriction on cancelled or past bookings, and no limit on number of guests
body: The handler does not check booking status. Any attendee can add an unbounded list of guests to any booking they belong to, including cancelled ones. Each added guest triggers outbound email, so this can be abused to spam arbitrary addresses.

title: Error message fallback never applies
body: The message is built with a template string that always produces a non-empty value, even when err.data is missing (e.g. 'undefined: ...'). As a result, the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never be used.

title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. A team admin who is not the owner, or an owner who fails the admin check, is rejected. The two checks should be combined with `||`.

title: Any attendee can add arbitrary guests and trigger emails
body: Any authenticated user whose email matches an attendee can add unlimited new guests. Each addition sends emails from the organizer's name to arbitrary addresses and adds them to the organizer's calendar event. The guest list size is also unbounded, so this can be abused for spam.

title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive
body: Blacklisted emails are lowercased but guest emails are not. Mixed-case input therefore bypasses the blacklist. The comparison against existing attendees is also case-sensitive, so the same email in different case is added again as a duplicate attendee.

title: Emails sent based on the unfiltered guests list
body: sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`. If a submitted email already belonged to an existing attendee, that attendee receives a full 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' update. The same applies to filtered (blacklisted or duplicate) entries.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the organizer's
body: The EventManager is built from ctx.user's credentials. When the caller is an attendee or a team admin, the organizer's calendar event is not updated with their credentials and the update fails or is skipped. The call is also not wrapped in error handling, so the mutation errors after the DB write has already committed.

title: Guest added despite disabled host/attendee email settings
body: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the eventType metadata flags disableStandardEmails, unlike the other booking email senders, so these emails are sent even when standard emails are disabled.

title: Fallback error message is unreachable
body: `message` is a template string, so it is always truthy and the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback is never used. When `err.data?.code` is missing, users see 'undefined: ...'.

title: Invalid-email error never clears
body: isInvalidEmail is set to true on a failed validation but is never reset on a later successful validation or on a successful submit. The error stays visible until the dialog is cancelled.

title: retryCount delete clause not scoped to SMS method
body: The new OR branch `retryCount > 1` has no `method: SMS` filter. This cron will therefore delete any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders, if other jobs ever increment retryCount. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the second OR branch.

title: Scheduled reminders with retryCount>1 also deleted, losing cancel reference
body: The retryCount condition has no `scheduled: false` filter, so it can also match reminders that were already scheduled at Twilio. A reminder can reach that state by failing once and later succeeding, since success does not reset retryCount. Deleting such a row drops its referenceId (the Twilio sid). The SMS can then no longer be cancelled when the booking is cancelled, so the attendee may still get it.

title: Update in catch block can throw and abort the whole cron loop
body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the catch block is not itself guarded. If it throws (for example a DB error, or the row was removed concurrently), the exception escapes the for loop. All remaining reminders in this run are then skipped and the handler errors out.

title: retryCount delete condition not scoped to SMS method
body: The second branch of the OR in deleteMany (`retryCount > 1`) has no `method: SMS` filter. This SMS cron will delete any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP ones. If other code paths increment retryCount for those methods, the SMS cron will delete their reminders. The condition should be scoped with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and probably `scheduled: false`).

title: Update in catch block can throw and abort the whole cron run
body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the catch block is not guarded. If it fails (for example, the reminder was deleted concurrently, or a DB error occurs), the exception propagates out of the loop. The remaining reminders are not processed and the handler returns an error.

title: retryCount deletion not scoped to SMS method
body: The second OR branch (`retryCount > 1`) has no `method: SMS` filter. This SMS cron job will therefore delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP workflow reminders whose retryCount exceeds 1, even if the email/WhatsApp crons use or later start using this column. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to that branch so other channels' reminders are not removed.

title: Already-scheduled reminders can be deleted by retryCount condition
body: The retryCount branch also has no `scheduled: false` filter. A reminder that failed once or twice and then scheduled successfully keeps its incremented retryCount and could match this delete. The DB row then disappears while the Twilio message is still queued, so it can no longer be cancelled when the booking is cancelled or rescheduled. Restrict the deletion to unscheduled reminders.

title: findMany removed without replacement for existing callers
body: The public `findMany` method was removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions` returning raw SQL. Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` (e.g. insights tRPC routers) will break at compile time, or need rewriting to `$queryRaw`. The PR does not update any callers.

title: Caching tests deleted
body: The tests that verified authorization and filter conditions are cached were removed instead of being ported to the Prisma.sql format. The caching behavior is still present in the service but is now untested.

title: Loosened constructor type allows invalid options silently
body: The constructor now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, in which `teamId` is optional for every scope. A caller passing `scope: "team"` without `teamId` now compiles. Validation then fails silently and the service returns `1=0` (no data), where this mistake used to be a type error.

title: Constructor accepts loose public options type, losing compile-time validation
body: The constructor now takes `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId` is optional for every scope. Previously the discriminated union type required `teamId` when scope is "team". Callers can now pass `scope: "team"` without a `teamId` and the code still compiles. At runtime, safeParse then fails and the service silently returns `1=0`, so callers get empty results with no error to point at the bad call.

title: findMany removed without migrating callers
body: The public `findMany` method is replaced by `getBaseConditions`, which returns a raw SQL fragment. Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany`, such as insights routers, will break. Each caller now has to hand-write a raw query, and the PR does not update any of them.

title: Integration test relies on denormalized view and dropped caching tests
body: The caching tests were deleted even though the caching logic is still in the service, so that behaviour is no longer covered. The PR author also admits the tests were never run. The new `$queryRaw` test assumes the `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` view exposes exactly these columns. Because nothing was executed, the SQL fragments' compatibility with the view (column quoting, `ANY` with int arrays) has not been verified.

title: findMany removed without migrating callers
body: The public `findMany` method was replaced by `getBaseConditions`. Any existing callers of `InsightsBookingService.findMany`, such as insights tRPC routers, will break at compile time or at runtime. Nothing in this diff updates those callers.

title: Caching tests deleted
body: The tests that verified caching of authorization and filter conditions were removed, even though the caching logic still exists in the service. That behavior is now untested.

title: Org scope user IDs skipped when org has no child teams
body: `userIdsFromOrg` is only computed when `teamsFromOrg.length > 0`, even though `teamIds` always includes `orgId`. In an org with no sub-teams, the org members' personal bookings are excluded from org-scope results. This logic predates the PR but was carried over unchanged.

title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError
body: When the credential is not found or belongs to another user, the handler throws a plain Error. tRPC turns this into a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN response, so an ordinary access-denied case is reported as a server failure. Throw a TRPCError with an appropriate code instead.

title: updateMany with empty data likely does not bump updatedAt
body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` sends empty update data. Prisma may skip the query or never set `@updatedAt`, so SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is not reliably refreshed. This adds a write on every cache refresh while the UI never reads that field. Either drop the call or set `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly.

title: connectedCalendars not invalidated after cache deletion
body: The delete-cache mutation does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, and the query uses `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. After a successful delete, the dropdown keeps showing the stale 'Last updated' timestamp and the delete action until the page is reloaded.

title: Hardcoded en-US date formatting
body: The cache timestamp is formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US")` even though the surrounding string is localized. Non-English users therefore see US-style dates. Use the user's locale from `useLocale`.

title: BSD-only sed -i syntax
body: `sed -i ''` is macOS/BSD syntax. On GNU/Linux sed the empty string is read as a script or file argument and the command fails, so the env file is never updated.

title: Error alert now hides remove action when connection modification is disabled
body: Previously the error Alert showed the disconnect button whenever the credential was not delegated, regardless of `disableConnectionModification`. It now passes `disableConnectionModification`, so in that mode users with a broken calendar can no longer remove it. This is a behavior change the PR does not mention.

title: updateMany with empty data does not bump updatedAt
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is called with an empty data object. Prisma's `updateMany` with no fields to set does not reliably issue an update, so `@updatedAt` is not refreshed. The stated goal of touching `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is therefore not met, and the call costs an extra query on every cache refresh.

title: Cache deletion doesn't invalidate connectedCalendars query
body: The deleteCache mutation's `onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. It never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. As a result the dropdown keeps showing the old "Last updated" cache status until a manual refetch, which this page disables on window focus. The disconnect mutation does invalidate this query; deleteCache should do the same.

title: Timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
body: The cache timestamp is formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` instead of the user's locale. The surrounding text is translated, but non-English users will still see a US-format date.

title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError
body: A missing or unauthorized credential throws a plain `Error`. tRPC reports this as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN, so a client-side access error is surfaced as a server failure.

title: sed -i '' is macOS-only
body: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed (Linux), the empty string is treated as the script and the command fails, so the env file is never updated. The relative path `ENV_FILE` also means the script only works when run from a specific directory.

title: Cache status shown even when calendar-cache feature disabled
body: The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly and queries the DB, bypassing the feature-flag mock used elsewhere. Stale cache rows can therefore be shown, and can be deleted from the UI, even when calendar-cache is disabled for the user.

title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError
body: When the credential is not found or belongs to another user, the handler throws a generic Error. tRPC turns this into a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR rather than a NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN response, so clients cannot tell an access denial from a server failure. It should throw a TRPCError with an appropriate code.

title: connectedCalendars query not invalidated after cache deletion
body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback. Unlike the disconnect mutation, it never invalidates utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. As a result the UI keeps showing the stale 'Last updated' status and the 'Delete cached data' option even after the cache rows have been removed.

title: Date formatting hardcoded to en-US
body: The cache timestamp is formatted with Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US') while the surrounding label is localized. Non-US users will see a US-style date and time regardless of their locale. It should use the user's locale or the app's date formatting helpers.

title: updateMany with empty data likely doesn't bump updatedAt
body: updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object. Prisma may skip the update or not apply @updatedAt when no fields are set, so the timestamp may never change. This also adds an extra database write to every cache fill for a value the PR description says the frontend does not use.

title: Cache status includes expired rows and runs even when caching is disabled
body: The groupBy query does not filter on expiresAt, so a credential whose cache has fully expired is still reported as having a cache. The connectedCalendars handler also always uses the real CalendarCacheRepository rather than the feature-flagged mock, so this extra query runs for every user, including those without the calendar-cache feature.

title: `sed -i ''` only works on macOS
body: The script uses BSD sed syntax (`sed -i ''`), which fails on GNU/Linux sed, so updating GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in the env file breaks there. Separately, ENV_FILE is set to a path relative to the current working directory ('../.env'), so running the script from anywhere other than the expected directory edits or creates the wrong file.

title: Immediate-cancel path leaves the WorkflowReminder row in place
body: When `immediateDelete` is true, the function cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting the DB row or setting `cancelled`. This path is used on reschedule in handleNewBooking and on step deletion in workflows.tsx. On reschedule the row stays tied to the old booking with `scheduled: true`. Because cancellations go straight to SendGrid again, this path still counts toward the 100 pending-cancellation limit that this PR is meant to avoid.

title: One failed cancel aborts the batch and leaves rows undeleted
body: Each SendGrid cancel is awaited inside a single try block. If any request throws, the loop stops and the queued delete promises are never awaited, so later reminders in the list are never cancelled. Those emails are then sent. Already-cancelled reminders stay in the DB and are retried on every run. Each reminder should get its own try/catch.

title: Cancelled reminders inside the 1-hour window can be deleted before they are cancelled
body: The `deleteMany` for past-due reminders runs before the cancel step. The cron runs every 15 minutes, and SendGrid only accepts cancellations ahead of send time. A reminder flagged `cancelled` close to its send time can therefore be deleted without its batch ever being cancelled. Reminders cancelled less than about an hour before send time may also be past SendGrid's cancellation cutoff, so those emails still go out.

title: Cancel query does not filter on method or referenceId
body: The cancel query matches any reminder with `cancelled: true`. It does not restrict to `method: EMAIL` or require a non-null `referenceId`. A null `referenceId` would send an invalid `batch_id` to SendGrid. That error is thrown inside the shared try block and aborts all remaining cancellations.

title: Scheduling query does not exclude cancelled reminders
body: The query for unscheduled reminders does not filter out `cancelled: true`. Separately, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` only deletes rows when `referenceId` is null, but a row can have a `referenceId` while still `scheduled: false`; such a row is only marked cancelled. If that happens, the cron can still schedule and send an email for a cancelled booking.

title: Reminder cancellation promises are not awaited
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called inside `forEach` without `await`. In a serverless environment the handler can return before the DB updates or Twilio cancels finish, so cancellations may be lost silently.

title: immediateDelete path cancels at SendGrid but never deletes the DB reminder
body: With immediateDelete=true (used for rescheduled bookings), the function cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting or flagging the WorkflowReminder row. The row stays with scheduled=true and cancelled=null, so it is orphaned. On reschedule, the old booking's reminders remain attached to the old booking in the DB. Each immediate cancel also counts toward SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation limit, which is the failure this PR sets out to avoid.

title: Cancelled reminders whose time passed between cron runs are deleted without being cancelled
body: The cron first deletes every email reminder with scheduledDate <= now, and only afterwards looks up cancelled reminders due within the next hour. Suppose a booking is cancelled less than about 15 minutes before its reminder time, so the reminder was never picked up by the previous cron run. That reminder is deleted by the first query before the cancellation step reaches it. Its SendGrid batch is never cancelled, and the email goes out for the cancelled booking.

title: Cancelled but never-scheduled reminders can still be sent
body: If a reminder has no referenceId yet (scheduled=false), deleteScheduledEmailReminder deletes it, which is fine. However, a reminder can be marked cancelled after this function runs but before the cron's unscheduled-reminders query. The unscheduled query does not filter out cancelled=true, so cancelled reminders can be scheduled and sent. The cancellation query also lacks a method: EMAIL filter.

title: One SendGrid failure aborts the entire cancellation batch
body: The whole cancellation loop sits inside a single try block. If any client.request call throws, for example because of a null referenceId or a rate limit, the loop stops. The remaining cancellations are skipped and the deletes already queued are never awaited. Error handling should happen per reminder.

title: Async reminder deletions are not awaited, so try/catch never catches their errors
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called inside forEach without await. The surrounding try/catch therefore never sees their failures. The same fire-and-forget pattern appears in handleCancelBooking and the trpc routers. In serverless environments these promises may be dropped when the response returns.

title: immediateDelete path never deletes the DB reminder row
body: When immediateDelete is true, the function cancels the batch at SendGrid and returns without deleting the workflowReminder row. On reschedule, the old reminders therefore stay in the database. Unscheduled reminders (scheduled=false) will later be picked up by the cron and sent for the old booking time. Each cancellation also adds a pending entry to SendGrid's scheduled_sends, which is capped at 100, so this path brings back the limit the PR is meant to avoid.

title: Cron still schedules reminders already marked cancelled
body: The query for unscheduled reminders does not filter out cancelled=true. A reminder for a cancelled booking that has no referenceId yet will be scheduled with SendGrid and sent. The cancel step only handles reminders scheduled within the next hour, and by then the email has already been queued.

title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole batch
body: The loop over cancelled reminders sits inside a single try/catch. If any SendGrid request throws (for example because referenceId is null or the 100-pending limit is hit), the remaining reminders are skipped. The delete promises collected so far are also never awaited, so those rows stay in the database.

title: Cancelled reminders already past their date are deleted before cancellation runs
body: The deleteMany at the top runs first and removes rows whose scheduledDate is already past. A cancelled reminder whose date fell between cron runs (the cron runs every 15 minutes) is deleted without ever being cancelled at SendGrid. The email is then sent.

title: Workflow delete skips unscheduled reminders and leaves SendGrid cancels pending
body: Reminders are queried with scheduled=true only, and the email path uses immediateDelete, which does not remove the row. The cascade delete of the workflow cleans up the rows, but every scheduled email still triggers an immediate SendGrid cancel. Deleting a large workflow can therefore exhaust the 100 pending-cancellation limit the PR set out to avoid.

title: All app modules still load eagerly at import time
body: Each `import()` call in the object literal runs as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported, so all 28 app packages are still loaded at module evaluation. Nothing is deferred, so the stated goal of the PR is not achieved. An import failure in any one app also becomes an unhandled promise rejection, or makes every lookup fail. Wrap each entry in a thunk instead, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and call it at the use sites.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a calendar Promise to other callers
body: `calendar` in the returned objects is now `Promise<Calendar | null>`. `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to await it, but other consumers of `getCalendarCredentials` (the tRPC/API routes) still treat `calendar` as an instance. They would call methods on a Promise, or treat the always-truthy Promise as a valid calendar. In addition, the promise is created even when `app.variant !== "calendar"` and is never awaited, so a rejection there is unhandled.

title: forEach(async) pushes to apiDeletes after it has been awaited
body: For recurring bookings, the callback now awaits `getCalendar` before pushing deletions into `apiDeletes`. `forEach` does not wait for async callbacks, so `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs before anything is pushed. Calendar event deletions for recurring bookings are therefore not awaited, and any errors from them become unhandled rejections.

title: Async forEach makes calendar and video deletions fire-and-forget
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` returns promises that nobody awaits. Rejections from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` are unhandled and can crash or log noisily. The same pattern in `vital/lib/reschedule.ts` and `wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts` makes their surrounding try/catch ineffective. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` instead.

title: All app modules are still imported eagerly at module load
body:
Each property is written as `import("./x")`, and that call runs as soon as the object literal is evaluated. So every app package is still loaded when `@calcom/app-store` is first imported, and nothing is lazy. The PR's goal of deferring app loading is not met.

It also adds a risk: if any app module throws during load, its promise rejects with no handler attached. That surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection at startup.

The entries should be thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and call sites should invoke them.

title: async forEach pushes to apiDeletes after it is awaited
body:
The recurring-cancel branch uses `forEach(async ...)` and awaits `getCalendar` before pushing into `apiDeletes`. Those pushes happen after the synchronous code has moved on, so `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` has already captured the array and misses them.

As a result, calendar deletions for recurring bookings are not awaited, and their errors become unhandled rejections. Use `for...of` or `Promise.all` instead.

title: forEach(async) in requestReschedule leaves deletions unawaited
body:
`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` now awaits `getCalendar` inside each callback. The returned promises are discarded, so the calendar and video deletions are fire-and-forget.

Any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection. The mutation may also return before the events are actually deleted.

title: try/catch cannot catch errors from forEach(async)
body:
The callback is now async and the promises it returns are discarded. Errors from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` are therefore never caught by the surrounding try/catch.

Those errors become unhandled rejections, and deletions may still be pending when the function returns. The same problem exists in `wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts`.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns calendar as a Promise
body:
`calendar` in each returned item is now a `Promise<Calendar|null>`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to await it.

Any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` that reads `.calendar` directly will get a Promise. Because a Promise is always truthy, those callers will either break or wrongly treat a missing calendar as present.

title: All app modules still eagerly imported at module load
body: Each entry is `import("./x")`, which starts loading every app module as soon as the appStore module is evaluated. Nothing is lazy, so startup and bundle cost are not reduced and the PR's goal is not met. The entries should be thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, called on demand by consumers.

title: A failing app import becomes an unhandled rejection at load time
body: The import promises are created eagerly and nothing awaits most of them. If any single app module fails to load (missing env var, syntax error, etc.), its promise rejects with no handler. That produces an unhandled rejection, which can crash the Node process, even if that app is never used.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in `calendar` field
body: `getCalendar` is now async, so `calendar` in each returned item is a Promise rather than a Calendar or null. `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to await it, but other callers of `getCalendarCredentials` that use `item.calendar` directly are not. Those callers will receive a Promise, which is always truthy, so null checks pass and method calls on it fail.

title: forEach(async) pushes to apiDeletes after it has been awaited
body: The async forEach callback now awaits `getCalendar` before reaching `apiDeletes.push`. By the time it pushes, `Promise.all(apiDeletes)` has already run, so these deletions for recurring bookings are never awaited. Any errors from them become unhandled rejections.

title: forEach(async) makes calendar deletions fire-and-forget
body: Calendar and video deletions now run inside an async forEach callback whose promise is ignored. Failures surface as unhandled rejections rather than being reported to the caller. The same pattern in vital and wipemycalother reschedule.ts also makes their surrounding try/catch ineffective. Use `await Promise.all(map(...))` instead.

title: Dayjs objects compared with ===, always false
body: The check for a zero-length override (start equals end) compares two freshly created Dayjs instances with `===`. That is reference equality, so it is never true. As a result, an override that marks the whole day unavailable is not caught by this branch. It should use `.isSame()`.

title: Working-hours check uses slot start for end
body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime`, the same value as `start`. So a slot that starts inside working hours but runs past their end is still accepted. It should use `slotEndTime`. Also, comparing raw UTC hour/minute against minutes-since-midnight working hours does not handle ranges that span midnight. Such ranges can wrongly reject valid slots.

title: Override day skips busy-time check entirely
body: When a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls inside it, the function returns true immediately. It never evaluates `busy`, so existing bookings and calendar events on override days are ignored. That allows double booking. It should fall through to the busy check instead of returning.

title: Multiple overrides on same day reject valid slots
body: `find` returns true as soon as any same-day override excludes the slot. If a user has several override ranges on one day, e.g. 9-10 and 14-15, a slot inside the second range is rejected because it falls outside the first.

title: Slot end not checked against override end
body: Only `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` is checked. A slot that starts before the override ends but extends past it is accepted, which allows bookings outside the override window.

title: Override minute-of-day may wrap across midnight
body: Start and end are computed as UTC hour*60+minute after adding the offset. When the shifted time crosses midnight, the end becomes smaller than the start, or lands on a different day. buildSlots then discards the range as invalid, so the override silently yields no slots or the wrong ones. The tests only cover small offsets (+5:30 and +6:00 with an IST organizer).

title: Dayjs objects compared with === always false
body: The check that a date override marks the whole day unavailable compares two freshly created Dayjs instances with `===`. This is reference equality, so it is never true. Overrides where start equals end (a day marked unavailable) are not caught by this branch. They only behave correctly by accident through the later isBefore/isSame checks. Compare with `.isSame()` or `.valueOf()` instead.

title: Working hours end check uses slot start instead of slot end
body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime`, the same value as `start`. A slot that begins inside working hours but ends after them passes the check. The intended end-of-slot validation never happens. `end` should be derived from `slotEndTime`.

title: Any single non-matching working-hours entry rejects the slot
body: `workingHours.find` returns true as soon as any entry covering that weekday does not contain the slot. Users commonly have several availability ranges on the same day (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17). A slot at 14:00 falls outside the 9-12 entry, so it is wrongly rejected. The logic should reject a slot only when no working-hours entry contains it (use `some` and negate).

title: Date override day comparison uses incorrectly shifted time
body: `date.start` is already an absolute UTC instant, yet the code adds the negated organizer offset to it before formatting the day. The result is then compared with the UTC slot date. For organizers far from UTC, the shift moves the override onto the wrong UTC calendar day. The start and end bounds are shifted the same way, so slots are wrongly accepted or rejected. Overrides near midnight UTC may never match, or may match the adjacent day.

title: Override minutes wrap across midnight
body: The override start and end are converted to minutes using `hour()*60+minute()` after applying the offset. If the shifted time crosses midnight, the value wraps. A shifted end at 00:30 the next day becomes 30, which is less than the start, and the slot range is silently dropped. Overrides near day boundaries in the invitee timezone are therefore lost.

title: Timezone test doesn't exercise the fixed-host round-robin fix
body: The new test only re-queries a single-user event in another invitee timezone. The headline fix, that date overrides of fixed hosts apply in round-robin events, has no test. The organizer/override timezone mismatch case is also not covered.

title: Dayjs objects compared with ===, zero-length override check never matches
body: `dayjs(...) === dayjs(...)` compares two distinct object references, so it is always false. A date override where start equals end (a day marked unavailable) is therefore not caught by this branch. Use `.isSame()` instead.

title: Working hours end check uses slot start instead of slot end
body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime`, so it is identical to `start`. The `end > workingHour.endTime` check never accounts for the event length, and slots that run past the end of working hours are accepted. It should be computed from `slotEndTime`.

title: Any non-matching working-hours entry marks the slot unavailable
body: `workingHours.find` returns true as soon as one working-hours entry covering that weekday excludes the slot. Users with several ranges on the same day (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17) will have every slot rejected, because each slot falls outside at least one of the ranges. The check should be "not inside any entry" rather than "outside some entry".

title: Slot that ends past the override end is still allowed
body: Only `slotStartTime.isAfter(override end)` is rejected. A slot that starts inside the override but ends after the override end passes this check. Combined with the early `return true` when an override exists, this skips the busy-time checks and can produce bookable slots that overrun the override window.

title: Override existence skips busy/booking checks
body: When a slot falls on a day with a date override and inside it, the function returns true before evaluating `busy`. As a result, existing bookings and calendar events on override days are ignored, which allows double bookings.

title: Date-override day matching shifts by the negated offset and compares in UTC
body: The override start is shifted by the negative organizer UTC offset, but the slot's day is compared in UTC. Overrides near midnight in non-UTC zones are matched to the wrong day, so they can be applied to, or missed on, adjacent days.

title: Host lookup is not case-insensitive
body: `record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but never downcases the `host` argument. `URI#host` keeps the original case, so a referer or URL with uppercase letters (e.g. Eviltrout.com) is rejected even though the stored host matches. The fix is to compare against `host.downcase`.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host
body: The callback calls `self.host.sub!` without checking for nil. Saving a record whose host is nil raises NoMethodError, so the admin API returns a 500 instead of a validation error. The `sub!` calls also mutate the attribute string in place, which can bypass ActiveRecord dirty tracking.

title: Host format regex rejects ports, localhost and long TLDs
body: The pattern requires a dot and a TLD of 2–5 letters, so hosts like `localhost`, IP addresses and newer long TLDs (e.g. `.community`) cannot be saved. Separately, `record_for_host` compares only `uri.host`, so a stored host with a port (which the regex allows) can never match a referer.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting is absent
body: The query uses `execute(...)[0]['id']`. When no `embed_category` site setting exists (the common case), `[0]` returns nil and `['id']` raises NoMethodError, so the migration fails. The same pattern on line 15 fails when `uncategorized_category_id` is not stored in site_settings, which happens whenever it was left at its default.

title: Unescaped interpolation and unnormalized hosts in migration INSERT
body: Host values are interpolated directly into the INSERT SQL, so a quote in the stored setting breaks the migration (SQL injection risk). The values are also inserted raw, without stripping `http://`/`https://` or `\r`. Migrated rows such as `http://example.com` therefore never match `uri.host`, and embedding silently stops working for those sites.

title: Missing record causes 500
body: `update` and `destroy` use `where(...).first` and then call methods on the result without checking for nil. A request for a nonexistent id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404.

title: embeddable_hosts list not hydrated from embedded ids
body: The serializer sends `embeddable_host_ids`, but `_lookupSubType` resolves them against `root['embeddable_hosts']`. Unless that root key is sideloaded, the lookups return undefined, so `embedding.embeddable_hosts` contains undefined entries. `pushObject` then operates on a plain array of undefined values, which breaks the admin list.

title: replace only swaps first underscore
body: `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the first underscore. Any model type with more than one underscore is not normalized and will not match ADMIN_MODELS, so it is routed to the non-admin path.

title: Test name no longer matches behavior
body: The test "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false. `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks for embeddable hosts at all, so the test does not verify what its name claims.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting is absent
body: The migration reads `execute(...)[0]['id']` without checking that a row came back. On sites that never set embed_category, which is the default, the query returns no rows. `[0]` is then nil and `['id']` raises NoMethodError, so the migration fails. The uncategorized fallback lookup on line 15 has the same problem.

title: Unescaped interpolation of host values into SQL
body: Host strings from the old setting are interpolated straight into the INSERT. A value containing a quote breaks the migration and allows SQL injection. Values are also not stripped or normalized: `\r`, `http://` prefixes and blank lines are inserted as-is. Hosts stored with an `http://` prefix will never match the lowercased URI host, so embedding silently stops working for those sites after the upgrade.

title: Case-insensitive lookup compares against non-lowercased input
body: The query is `lower(host) = ?` but it is passed `uri.host` as-is. A Referer such as `http://EvilTrout.com` will therefore never match a stored host. The parameter should be downcased before the comparison.

title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when host is nil, for example when the admin submits without a host. The user gets a 500 error instead of a validation error.

title: Missing record causes NoMethodError
body: `destroy` (and `update` via `save_host`) look up the host with `where(id:).first` and use the result without checking it. An unknown id yields nil and the call raises a 500 instead of returning a 404.

title: Category passed as id where creator previously received a category name
body: The old code passed `SiteSetting.embed_category`, a category name, as the `category` option to PostCreator. The new code passes a category id from `eh.try(:category_id)`. Whether this works depends on how PostCreator resolves the option. Separately, when `record_for_host` returns false (an invalid URL), `try` on false returns nil, so the topic is created with no category.

title: Fabricator file contents swapped
body: category_fabricator.rb now holds the embeddable_host fabricator, and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb holds the category fabricators. The file names no longer match their contents, which is confusing for maintainers.

title: Host lookup lowercases the column but not the input
body: `record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against `uri.host` without downcasing the input. The model does not normalize case on save, so a stored host like 'Example.com' only matches a referer if the referer's hostname is already lowercase. A mixed-case referer or embed URL is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive. Downcase the input value before querying.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host
body: The callback calls `self.host.sub!` with no nil check. If `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is missing, or a record is built without a host, this raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500 instead of a validation error.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category is not set
body: `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the join query returns a row. On sites with no `embed_category` setting, or one that names no existing category, `[0]` is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError, which blocks the deploy. The same problem exists at line 15 when `uncategorized_category_id` has no row in site_settings.

title: Unescaped interpolation of host values into SQL
body: Each old host value is interpolated directly into an INSERT statement without quoting. A value containing a quote breaks the migration and can inject SQL. The values are also not stripped or normalized, so entries with http://, a path, or trailing whitespace/CR are migrated as-is and will never match `host_allowed?`. Existing embeds would silently stop working after the upgrade.

title: Unknown id causes NoMethodError instead of 404
body: `update` and `destroy` use `where(...).first`, which returns nil for an unknown id. They then call methods on that nil, producing a 500 error. Use `find` (or an equivalent) so a missing record returns a 404.

title: Validation rejects localhost and long TLDs
body: The format regex requires a TLD of 2–5 letters. It rejects hosts such as `localhost`, IP addresses, and longer TLDs (e.g. .museum, .technology). Values the old setting allowed, possibly brought over by the migration, can no longer be saved.

title: Displayed category is wrong when none is selected
body: If no category is chosen, `categoryId` is null and the server saves the uncategorized category. The client instead sets `host.category` from `findById(null)`, so the row shows a blank category badge rather than the category the server actually stored.

title: Fabricator file contents swapped
body: category_fabricator.rb now defines `:embeddable_host`, while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the category fabricators. The tests still work, but the file names are misleading for anyone looking for either fabricator.

title: Second `downsize` definition overrides the 4-dimension variant
body:
Ruby has no method overloading. `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently replaces the earlier `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`.

Existing callers that pass a width and a height (for example `downsize(from, to, 800, 600, opts)`) will now bind `max_height` to `opts`. Depending on the arguments this either raises ArgumentError or treats an integer as the opts hash and produces a wrong dimensions string.

title: Downsize result ignored; loop can't detect failure and file metadata is stale
body:
The return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored. If convert fails (unsupported format, or an svg that can't be resized), the loop still burns all 5 attempts on the full-size file.

After the loop, the oversized file is still passed on with no clear error. Upload validation will reject it, but only after up to 5 expensive convert runs.

Convert also writes to `tempfile.path` while the Ruby Tempfile handle stays open. Its cached state and `size` may not reflect the rewritten file.

title: Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick+ImageOptim runs per upload
body:
Each iteration runs convert and then a full ImageOptim pass on files up to 10MB. In synchronous API mode this happens inside the request, and in deferred mode it ties up the defer thread.

This is a denial-of-service vector: any user can upload large images and force heavy CPU work.

title: Client size limit hardcoded to 10MB for all types, including attachments
body:
The check previously used `max_<type>_size_kb`. It now uses a fixed 10MB for every file type.

Attachments are not downsized on the server, so oversized attachments now pass client validation and fail later on the server. Attachments smaller than a configured limit above 10MB are wrongly rejected.

The 413 handler (line 246) has the same problem: it reports 10MB regardless of the actual server limit.

title: Download limit hardcoded to 10MB for non-image URLs
body:
API URL downloads now use a fixed 10MB cap for every file. Previously the cap followed the configured setting.

The same 10MB number is also duplicated across the client and server instead of coming from a single setting, so the limits can drift apart.

title: Second `downsize` definition silently replaces the 4-dimension variant
body: Ruby has no method overloading. The new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` defined at line 149 replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Existing callers that pass width and height separately will now treat `max_height` as `opts`. That either raises when `opts[:...]` is called on an Integer, or produces wrong dimensions like "800" instead of "800x600".

title: Downsize failures are ignored and the loop wastes work
body: The return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is never checked. If `convert` fails, for example on an unsupported format or SVG, the loop still runs up to 5 times and spawns a process each time. The upload then proceeds at its original size and is later rejected by the size validation.

title: Stale tempfile size after in-place conversion
body: `convert` rewrites the file at `tempfile.path` from a separate process while the Tempfile handle stays open. `tempfile.size` can report a stale or buffered size, so the loop condition may not reflect the new file. The same stale size is then passed to `Upload.create_for` at line 72.

title: Client hardcodes 10MB limit for every file type, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb
body: The client size check now uses a fixed 10MB for both images and attachments. Before, it read the per-type site setting. The server only downsizes images, so attachments larger than the configured attachment limit now pass the client check and fail on the server. Sites that allow more than 10MB are also capped incorrectly.

title: API download limit hardcoded to 10MB
body: URL downloads are now capped at a fixed 10MB for all types, regardless of settings. This should be configurable, or at least derived from the larger of the configured limits.

title: Second `downsize` definition overrides the 4-arg version
body: Ruby has no method overloading. The new `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Existing callers that pass a width and a height will now have `max_height` treated as `opts`. That either raises (`opts[:allow_animation]` called on an Integer) or produces a wrong dimensions string. Avatar and thumbnail downsizing elsewhere breaks as a result.

title: Downsize loop ignores failure and may not shrink file
body: The return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored. If convert fails, the loop simply retries. After 5 attempts the file can still be over the limit, and the upload proceeds anyway. Resizing to 80% of dimensions also does not guarantee the byte size drops, for example with PNG or with quality changes. Running convert on the same path as both input and output can also corrupt the file on failure.

title: Downsizing uses the tempfile path, whose extension may not match
body: The animated-GIF check uses `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` on the tempfile path. Rack and download tempfiles usually lack the original extension, so animated GIFs are processed by convert using only frame `[0]`. This silently destroys the animation even when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is enabled.

title: Client hardcodes a 10MB limit for all uploads, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb
body: The client-side check previously used `max_<type>_size_kb`. It is now hardcoded to 10MB for attachments as well, so the attachment size setting is no longer enforced or reported on the client. Users get wrong error messages, and the limit mismatches the configured server limit.

title: Hardcoded 10MB download limit for API URL uploads
body: Downloads by URL are now capped at a hardcoded 10MB instead of a setting. Attachments fetched this way bypass the configured limits until `Upload.create_for` runs, and admins cannot tune the cap.

title: Nil TopicUser crashes unsubscribe
body: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic, for example a user notified by a mention or a watched category without ever visiting. The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500. Use `TopicUser.change` or create the record first.

title: GET request mutates state; repeated visits toggle to muted
body: The unsubscribe action changes notification state on a GET. A second visit (refresh, email prefetchers, link scanners) downgrades regular to muted. The Ember client route also fetches the topic JSON on transition. As a result, users can be muted without intent.

title: Direct save bypasses TopicUser.change side effects
body: `tu.save!` does not set `notifications_reason_id` or `notifications_changed_at`, and does not publish the MessageBus `notification_level_change`. Open clients therefore keep showing the stale state. Auto-tracking via `update_last_read` (which applies when `notifications_reason_id` is null) can also re-raise the level later.

title: Other emails using unsubscribe_link lack unsubscribe_url
body: `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Every other email that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` without passing `unsubscribe_url` will render a missing-interpolation error or a broken 'click here' link. The 'this particular topic' text is also wrong outside topic notifications.

title: Message claims notifications stop even when only downgraded
body: When the user was watching or tracking, the server only downgrades them to regular, so they still get notifications for replies and mentions. The page nevertheless says 'You will stop receiving notifications', which is misleading.

title: Nil TopicUser crashes unsubscribe
body: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the user has no topic_users row for this topic, for example a user who was only mentioned or is watching via category. The next line then calls `tu.notification_level` on nil, raises NoMethodError, and the request fails with a 500. The code should create the row (e.g. via `TopicUser.change`) or handle the nil case.

title: GET unsubscribe toggles state; repeat visits mute topic
body: The unsubscribe action changes state on a GET request. A watching or tracking user is downgraded to regular on the first visit. Any later visit (a reload, an email link prefetcher, or a JSON refetch from the Ember route) drops them further to muted. That is unexpected data mutation and is also CSRF-able through an image tag. The level should be set idempotently, and the change should ideally require a POST or a token.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for all emails
body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Other mailers that use `add_unsubscribe_link`, such as the digest, do not pass that value. They will hit I18n MissingInterpolationArgument errors or render a broken "click here" link to a non-existent topic.

title: Client route performs a second unsubscribe
body: `loadTopicView` fetches `/t/:id.json`, not the unsubscribe endpoint. So the page shown is the topic view and the server unsubscribe happened only on the initial HTML load. The preloaded JSON is also stored under `topic_<id>`, so behavior depends on whether that preload is consumed. When the user navigates client-side to this route, no unsubscribe happens at all, even though the page says notifications will stop.

title: Unescaped title rendering
body: `stopNotificiationsText` is rendered with triple-stash `{{{ }}}`. Its content is built by interpolating `fancyTitle` into the translation. `fancyTitle` is escaped server-side, so this is safe only if every producer of that title escapes it. Translations are also injected raw.

title: Nil TopicUser causes 500 on unsubscribe
body: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the user has no topic_users row, for example a user notified through a mention or a category watch who never visited the topic. The next line calls `tu.notification_level` on nil and raises NoMethodError. Create the record if it is missing, or use `TopicUser.change`.

title: Repeated GET toggles state and mutates on GET
body: The unsubscribe action changes state on a GET request. A user whose level is already regular gets set to muted. Every revisit of the link, a link prefetch, or an email scanner fetching the URL lowers the level further or changes it unexpectedly. A state-changing GET is also CSRF-able: any third-party page can embed the URL and change a logged-in user's notification level.

title: Direct save bypasses TopicUser.change side effects
body: `tu.save!` skips what `TopicUser.change` normally does. It does not set `notifications_reason_id` or `notifications_changed_at`, and it does not publish the MessageBus notification_level_change. As a result, open clients do not update, and later auto-tracking can override the user's explicit choice because the reason stays nil.

title: No visibility check before modifying TopicUser
body: `TopicView.new` in the unsubscribe action is called without the slug-redirect handling used in `show`. The action then creates or modifies state for the topic, so the guard enforced by TopicView is the only protection. There is also no handling for a missing topic: `@topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url` is used when the slug is blank.

title: Added explicit render :show may double-render
body: This change adds `render :show` inside `format.html` in `perform_show_response`. `show` then calls `canonical_url` after `perform_show_response`. Other callers may already rely on implicit rendering, so the change risks a DoubleRenderError. It also alters existing `show` behavior even though only `unsubscribe` needed it.

title: Client route fetches normal topic view, not unsubscribe endpoint
body: The client route loads the topic through `PostStream.loadTopicView`, which calls the normal topic JSON endpoint and never hits `/unsubscribe`. When a user navigates to this route inside the app, no unsubscribe happens, yet the page still says "You will stop receiving notifications".

title: No tests for the unsubscribe controller action
body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action has no specs. Untested paths include the regular-to-muted transition, the redirect when the slug does not match, and the case where no TopicUser row exists, which currently crashes.

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive
body: `should_block?` uses an exact `where(email: email)` lookup and nothing normalizes the stored or incoming address. A blocked address can therefore be bypassed by changing its case, for example 'Bad@Spam.org' instead of 'bad@spam.org'. Both the stored and queried values should be downcased (e.g. with Email.downcase).

title: Non-atomic match_count increment as a side effect of validation
body: The method does a read, then `+= 1`, then `save`. Concurrent signups attempting the same email lose increments. It also writes to the DB on every `valid?` call: the users controller calls `valid?` and then `save`, so each signup attempt is counted twice. Use an atomic `update_all('match_count = match_count + 1')`, or `increment_counter`.

title: rejectedEmails array shared across all controller instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined on the prototype in `extend`, so every instance shares one array. Rejected emails persist across modal instances. It should be initialized in `init`.

title: Rejected email recorded for any email error, including uniqueness
body: The client adds the email to `rejectedEmails` whenever `errors.email` is present. That includes an email-taken uniqueness error and transient whitelist errors. The user is then permanently told the email is 'invalid', which is a misleading message.

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and exact-match
body: `should_block?` uses `where(email: email)` with the raw input. A user can get past a block by changing letter case (e.g. `Bad@spammers.org`), because the check runs before the email is normalized. Normalize both the stored and the checked email (downcase and strip) before comparing.

title: Non-atomic match_count increment loses updates
body: `should_block?` reads the record, adds 1 in Ruby, then saves. Concurrent signups can overwrite each other's increments. It also runs a full save with validations, including a uniqueness query, on every validation. Use `update_all` or `increment_counter` instead.

title: Validation has side effects that inflate statistics
body: `should_block?` writes match statistics every time the validator runs. The users controller calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, so validation runs twice per signup and each blocked match is counted twice. Every `valid?` call anywhere also mutates the database.

title: rejectedEmails array shared across controller instances
body: `Em.A([])` is defined on the prototype in `extend`, so every instance of the controller shares the same array. Initialize it in `init` instead.

title: Any email error permanently rejects the address client-side
body: Any email error is treated as a permanent rejection, including transient ones such as 'already taken'. The address is then marked invalid with no way to retry it without reloading the page.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and can be bypassed
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` runs `where(email: value)` on the raw value. At validation time the user's email has not been downcased or normalized, so `Bad@Spammers.org` will not match a stored `bad@spammers.org`. A blocked address can register just by changing the letter case.

title: Match counter updated with racy read-modify-write during validation
body: `should_block?` loads the record, increments `match_count` in Ruby and saves it. Concurrent requests for the same address lose increments. It also writes to the database on every `valid?` call, so the count is inflated: `UsersController#create` validates twice (once in `user.valid?`, once in `save`). An atomic `update_all('match_count = match_count + 1')` would avoid the race.

title: rejectedEmails array is shared across controller instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is declared in the prototype passed to `extend`, so every instance shares the same array. Rejected emails therefore persist across modal reopenings and across controller instances instead of being per-instance state. It should be initialized in `init`.

title: Any email error permanently rejects the address client-side
body: The client records the email as rejected on any email error, including a transient one such as a uniqueness conflict. That address then can never be resubmitted from the form. The reason shown is also the generic "invalid" message, not the server's actual error.

title: Whitelist/blacklist behavior moved without tests
body: The domain whitelist/blacklist logic was moved out of `User` into `EmailValidator`, but the new spec only covers the blocked-email path. The moved logic has no coverage. There is also no test that a whitelist or blacklist failure skips the blocked-email check.

title: Remote/RSS HTML stored and rendered raw without sanitization (stored XSS)
body: Imported content is saved with cook_method raw_html. Post#cook then returns raw unchanged, so this HTML is never sanitized. The embed view and normal topic views output it with `raw post.cooked`. Any script or event-handler attributes in the feed or fetched page run on the forum origin. Readability only partially filters the import_remote path, and the RSS path in poll_feed is not filtered at all.

title: URL interpolated unescaped into HTML attribute
body: The embed URL is inserted unescaped into `<a href='#{url}'>`. A URL containing a single quote can break out of the attribute and inject markup. That markup is then rendered raw because of the raw_html cook method.

title: Mutates caller's string in place
body: `contents <<` appends to the string the caller passed in. If that string is frozen (for example a literal under frozen_string_literal), this raises an error. Otherwise it silently modifies the caller's object.

title: Embed URL host not validated before enqueueing; spec expects synchronous retriever
body: The controller only checks the referer, then enqueues a job for any embed_url, so any visitor can trigger repeated job enqueues. The spec expects `TopicRetriever.new` and `retrieve` to be called directly from the controller. Because the controller enqueues a job instead, that test will fail when jobs are queued.

title: Every uncached embed request triggers a full feed poll
body: Each embed URL that is missing from the database runs a full PollFeed synchronously. That fetches the feed and reimports every item. A new topic is created for each embed URL, and the throttle is keyed on the URL, so an attacker can force repeated full feed fetches by sending distinct URLs.

title: Referer injected into script without JS escaping
body: `request.referer` is written into a JS string literal with only HTML escaping. That does not reliably prevent breaking out of the string. Passing the full referer URL as targetOrigin is also fragile.

title: Nil content crash
body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element, which is common in RSS feeds that only provide a description. The exception aborts the whole poll, so remaining items are not imported.

title: `end if` is a syntax/logic error
body: `<%- end if %>` combines `end` with a dangling `if` modifier whose condition is whatever ERB code follows. It is likely a parse error or, at best, unintended behavior; it should be a plain `end`.

title: Raw HTML from remote/feed stored and rendered unsanitized (stored XSS)
body: TopicEmbed.import stores the HTML it fetches as the post body with cook_method raw_html, so Post#cook returns it as-is. That HTML comes from Readability output or RSS item content. The feed path in particular unescapes HTML entities and keeps every tag, including script. Nothing sanitizes it before it is rendered on the forum and in the embed view via `raw post.cooked`. Anyone who controls the feed or the remote page can inject script into the Discourse origin.

title: URL interpolated unescaped into HTML attribute
body: The imported_from footer builds `#{url}` without escaping. A URL containing a quote or angle bracket can inject markup or script. Because the post is rendered as raw HTML, this is exploitable.

title: Mutates caller's string; SHA computed before absolutize
body: `contents <<` modifies the caller's string in place, and it raises on a frozen string. The SHA1 is computed on the content before URLs are absolutized; that part is fine, but repeated calls with the same string object keep appending the footer, so the hash changes on every call and the post is revised again each time.

title: Port check ignores scheme
body: The prefix omits the port whenever it is 80 or 443, regardless of scheme. For example, `https://host:80` would wrongly drop the explicit port and produce incorrect absolute URLs.

title: Referer injected into inline script
body: `request.referer` is interpolated into a JavaScript string literal with only HTML escaping, which does not escape for a JS context. The referer is attacker-influenced, and its host is checked only loosely. Using it as the postMessage target origin is also fragile. It should be JS-escaped (j/escape_javascript) or derived from the embeddable_host setting.

title: Unauthenticated requests enqueue jobs that fetch arbitrary URLs
body: Every cache miss enqueues a retrieve job carrying an arbitrary embed_url. The host check only happens later, in the job, against an exact host match. Throttling is per URL, so varying the query string bypasses it and lets anyone flood Sidekiq with jobs.

title: Start-discussion branch unreachable
body: The topic's first post always exists, so the 'start_discussion' branch never renders. It is also suspect that `end if` is used here; it is valid Ruby but confusing.

title: open-uri resource leak and per-item failures abort the whole poll
body: `open(url)` is never closed. If one item has nil content, `scrub` raises NoMethodError and the rest of the feed is skipped. The job also has retry disabled. In addition, `feed_key` is never used.

title: Polling entire feed synchronously per retrieval
body: Each topic retrieval re-polls and re-imports the entire feed inline. This happens for every distinct embed URL that is not yet known, which causes heavy repeated work.

title: Spec expects TopicRetriever but controller enqueues job
body: The controller calls Jobs.enqueue rather than TopicRetriever.new directly. The test passes only because jobs run inline when queue_jobs is false in the test environment, which makes it brittle. It also never asserts the 'loading' render.

title: Revision not saved when import updates a raw_html post
body: Post#save's before_save re-cooks the post. For raw_html posts the content changes only as raw, but the PostRevisor return value and save result are ignored in TopicEmbed. A failed save is silent, yet content_sha1 is still updated, so later changes are never retried.

title: Spec expects TopicRetriever but controller enqueues a job
body: In the test environment queue_jobs is false, so `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic)` runs the job inline. That job calls `TopicRetriever.new(url, no_throttle: ...)` and the stub returns a bare mock. The spec only works through this indirect path. It does not check that the job is enqueued with the right args.

title: Referer interpolated unescaped into inline JS
body: Line 11 writes `request.referer` into a JS string literal with `<%= %>`. That helper HTML-escapes but does not JS-escape, so a backslash or other JS-significant character in an attacker-chosen referer can break out of the literal. The host check only validates the host part, and the path and query of the referer are still attacker-controlled. The target origin should be built from the configured embeddable_host instead.

title: Unescaped URL injected into raw HTML post
body: The feed or remote URL is interpolated directly into `<a href='#{url}'>` without escaping. Posts using cook_method raw_html skip sanitization, so a URL containing `'` or `<` produces stored XSS. Imported feed content as a whole is also rendered with `raw post.cooked` and never sanitized, so a compromised feed source can inject scripts.

title: Mutates caller's string; fails on frozen strings
body: `contents <<` modifies the argument in place. Callers passing literals or frozen strings, such as `doc.content`, may get errors. The caller's data is also silently altered.

title: open(url) with untrusted input allows command execution/SSRF
body: Kernel#open from open-uri is called on the URL. A value starting with '|' executes a shell command. The disqus import passes thread links straight from the XML file, and the URL is not validated as http before this call. Use URI.parse(url).open or an HTTP client, and validate the scheme first.

title: Race creating duplicate embeds
body: Two concurrent imports of the same URL can both see no existing embed. Both then create a topic, and the second `TopicEmbed.create!` raises on the unique index. Because creator.create runs inside the transaction, this rolls back with an exception that is not handled.

title: Nil content crashes feed poll
body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError for RSS items that have no content (only a description), which aborts the whole poll. `scrub` also requires Ruby 2.1.

title: Every embed miss triggers a full feed poll
body: Each retrieve for an unknown URL synchronously polls and imports the entire feed. Staff requests bypass throttling, so this can cause repeated heavy fetches.

title: Start discussion branch unreachable
body: @topic_view is only set when a topic exists, and that topic always has at least the imported post. The 'start_discussion' branch therefore never shows, even when a topic has no replies.

title: align-items mixin passes modern values to legacy box properties
body: The `align-items` mixin writes the modern value straight into `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. The 2009 box spec and the IE10 spec use different keywords (`start`/`end` instead of `flex-start`/`flex-end`). Values like `flex-start` are therefore ignored or misapplied in those legacy engines. Separately, `-ms-align-items` is not a real property.

title: order mixin ordinal-group mismatch across specs
body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` is 1-based and defaults to 1, while `order` is 0-based and defaults to 0. Using the same value for both shifts the relative ordering of items in legacy browsers. With the `.panel` set to 3 and `.extra-info-wrapper` set to 2, any unordered items get order 0 in modern browsers but ordinal 1 in legacy ones, so the computed layouts differ between engines.

title: Floats ignored inside new flex container
body: `.small-action` is now a flex container, so the `float: right` on its button and `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` no longer apply. As a result, the button will sit immediately after the description instead of being pushed to the right edge.

title: align-items mixin passes modern values to legacy box-align properties
body: The `align-items` mixin writes the argument straight into `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy properties use different keywords: `start`/`end` instead of `flex-start`/`flex-end`, and they have no `baseline` in some engines. With the `baseline` and `flex-*` values used here, the legacy declarations are invalid and silently ignored. `-ms-align-items` is not a real property. Map the values to their legacy equivalents, or drop these prefixes.

title: order mixin values differ between legacy and modern syntax
body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` starts at 1, while modern `order` defaults to 0. Elements that are not given an order use 0 in modern browsers but 1 in legacy box layout. As a result, `.extra-info-wrapper` (order 2) and `.panel` (order 3) do not keep the same relative ordering against unordered siblings across implementations.

title: float inside flex container is ignored; button alignment lost
body: `.small-action` is now a flex container, so `float: right` on the button and `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` have no effect. The button that used to sit on the right will now follow the description directly. Use `margin-left: auto` on the button to keep it right-aligned.

title: align-items mixin emits invalid legacy values for old-box syntax
body: The align-items mixin passes values like `flex-start`, `flex-end` and `baseline` straight to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy properties expect `start`, `end`, `center`, `baseline` and `stretch`, so `flex-start`/`flex-end` produce invalid declarations. The mixin also emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a real property.

title: Legacy box-ordinal-group ordering inconsistent across flex items
body: `.panel` gets `order(3)` and `.extra-info-wrapper` gets `order(2)`, but the other flex children (title/logo) have no order set. In the old -webkit-box/-moz-box model, `box-ordinal-group` defaults to 1, while modern `order` defaults to 0. The two models therefore lay the items out differently. Also, the `.panel` children (`.login-button`, `.icons`) still use floats inside the now-flex row, which is fragile.

title: Removing .title float may break header layout in other stylesheets
body: The `.title { float: left; }` rule was removed, and `.contents` now relies on flexbox. In browsers that only support the legacy box model, `margin-left: auto` on `.panel` does not push it right. The panel would then render adjacent to the title instead of right-aligned, with no float fallback left in place.

title: Floats inside the new flex container are ignored
body: `.small-action` is now a flex container, but its children still use `float: left` (`.topic-avatar`) and `float: right` (the button). Floats are ignored on flex items, so the button no longer goes to the right and instead sits right after the description. `clear: both` is also meaningless here.

title: include_website_name missing '?' so website_name leaks for restricted TL0 users
body: The method is named `include_website_name` without the trailing `?`, so ActiveModel::Serializers never calls it as a filter. `website_name` is also not listed in `untrusted_attributes`. As a result, `website_name` is serialized even when `website` is hidden by `restrict_user_fields?`, for example a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor. This exposes the hidden website and partly defeats the anti-spam restriction. The method should be renamed to `include_website_name?` and apply the same restriction check, or `website_name` should be added to `untrusted_attributes`.

title: Subdomain check uses naive suffix matching on short hosts
body: The fallback branch treats any website host that is a dot-suffix of the forum host as the 'same' site. If the website host is a public suffix such as `co.uk` and the forum is `forum.example.co.uk`, the check matches and the full path is shown. The same-length branch has a similar flaw: hosts like `a.co.uk` and `b.co.uk` are treated as the same domain because they share the `co.uk` suffix. The domain comparison is unreliable for multi-part TLDs.

title: No test for TL0/anonymous hiding website_name or for sibling subdomains
body: The TL0 context's `untrusted_attributes` list was not extended with `website_name`, so the leak of `website_name` for restricted users is not caught by the specs. The `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` branch of `website_name` is also untested.

title: include_website_name lacks '?' so the untrusted-user restriction is bypassed
body: Active Model Serializers looks for a method named `include_website_name?`, with a question mark. The method here is named `include_website_name`, so it is never called and `website_name` is always serialized. `website_name` is also not listed in `untrusted_attributes`. As a result, TL0 users seen by anonymous visitors expose their website domain and path, even though `website` itself is deliberately hidden for them. Rename the method to `include_website_name?` and apply the same `restrict_user_fields?` check, for example by adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`.

title: Sibling-subdomain match compares only the suffix, so unrelated domains match
body: When both hosts have the same number of labels (more than two), the code drops the first label of each and compares the rest. With an instance at `forum.co.uk`, a website on `evil.co.uk` would match and show its full path. Likewise `a.example.com` vs `b.example.com` match even though they may be unrelated sites. The heuristic ignores public suffixes and can produce misleading display names.

title: Unparseable website can still raise on later URI parse
body: Only the first `URI(website.to_s)` call is protected by `rescue nil`. The later `URI(website.to_s).path` calls are unprotected, so they re-parse the URL redundantly. The method also mutates the string literal with `"" << website_host`. Parse the URI once and reuse the result, and avoid in-place string mutation.

title: TL0 spec doesn't check website_name is hidden
body: The list of untrusted attributes checked by the TL0 spec does not include `website_name`. The tests therefore miss that the new field leaks for restricted users.

title: include_website_name missing `?` so website_name leaks for restricted TL0 users
body: ActiveModel::Serializers only checks filter methods that end in `?`, so `include_website_name` is never called and `website_name` is always serialized. The field is also not listed in `untrusted_attributes`. As a result, the website host and path of a TL0 user is exposed to anonymous viewers, even though `website` itself is hidden from them. The method should be renamed to `include_website_name?` and apply the same `restrict_user_fields?` check (or `website_name` added to `untrusted_attributes`). The TL0 spec's attribute list should also cover `website_name`.

title: Same-level subdomain comparison treats unrelated domains as same site
body: When both hosts have the same number of labels (more than 2), the code compares everything after the first label. For a two-part public suffix this goes wrong: with discourse host `forum.co.uk` and website `evil.co.uk`, both reduce to `co.uk` and are judged to be the same site. The full path of a third-party site is then shown. The logic has no notion of the registrable domain.
