body: findByType for CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE also returns the all-clients resource, whose name is "Clients" rather than a client id. That bogus id is added to the result set. In addition, per-client resources created via getOrCreateResource are never given a type, so findByType may not find them at all.

title: Possible NPE when type resource is missing
body: getResourceTypeResource can return null, for example in older realms initialized before the Clients type was added. That null is passed to findByResource and later dereferenced via resource.getScopes(), causing an NPE instead of a deny.

title: getResourceName not updated for Clients type
body: For client permissions the resource name is the client's internal UUID, and getResourceName falls back to the display name. As a result, the admin UI shows raw UUIDs instead of the clientId or an "All clients" label.

title: Recreate exit code changed from 4 to 3, and 4 now means something else
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3, and 4 is reused for FEATURE_DISABLED. Any script or operator already written against the previous behaviour (4 meant recreate) will now handle exit 3 as an unexpected error. Worse, when the feature is disabled, exit 4 will be read as 'recreate required'. This silent change of a documented scripting contract should be called out or avoided.

title: Docs say the operator fails without the feature, but no operator-side check is added
body: The new CAUTION says the Operator will fail unless `rolling-updates` is enabled. This PR adds no operator code that gates the update strategy on the feature, so the statement may be inaccurate. The test changes only add the feature to the CR, which suggests the gating lives elsewhere or does not exist.

title: Feature-disabled test doesn't check exit code or cover `check`
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message. It does not verify the new exit code 4. It also does not exercise the `check` subcommand, which is the scripted path that depends on the exit code.

title: Recreate exit code changed from 4 to 3, and 4 now means feature disabled
body:
RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was 4 and is now 3. Code 4 is reused for FEATURE_DISABLED.

Existing scripts, and the operator if it consumes this code, that treat exit code 4 as "recreate needed" will now get a different meaning for the same value. A disabled feature would be interpreted as a recreate decision, and real recreate results (3) would be treated as unknown errors.

Any consumer in the operator should be checked and updated together with this change.

title: Feature-disabled test does not check exit code or the check subcommand
body:
testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message for the metadata subcommand. It does not verify the new exit code 4.

It also does not cover the check subcommand. That leaves the new FEATURE_DISABLED contract untested.

title: Recreate exit code changed from 4 to 3, and 4 now means 'feature disabled'
body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` changes from 4 to 3, and exit code 4 is reassigned to `FEATURE_DISABLED`. Scripts written against the previous behavior treat exit code 4 as 'recreate needed'. After this change they will misread the result: a real recreate requirement (now 3) may be treated as an unexpected error, and a disabled feature (now 4) may be read as 'recreate needed'. This is a silent change to a documented, scriptable contract. It needs at least a release or migration note.

title: New exit codes are not asserted
body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only checks the error message. It never asserts that the exit code is 4 (`FEATURE_DISABLED`). It also covers only the `metadata` subcommand, not `check`. `testWrongVersions` never asserts the new recreate exit code of 3. A regression in the exit-code contract, which is what scripts depend on, would therefore go unnoticed.

title: canManage() grants global group manage with only VIEW scope
body: In GroupPermissionsV2, canManage() calls hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an admin who holds only the all-groups VIEW permission passes requireManage(). That check guards creating and moving top-level groups in GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup. The result is privilege escalation from view to manage. It should check MANAGE only.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission looks up resources by id and returns resource ids, not group ids
body: Inside findByType, the method passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission, which calls findByName. V2 resources are named by group id, so the lookup by resource id fails and evaluation falls back to the all-groups resource. It then adds the resource id, not the group id (getName), to the result set. Filtering users by group membership therefore uses the wrong ids. Also, the V2 schema resources are created via resourceStore.create without setType, so findByType('Groups') may return nothing except the type resource itself.

title: Group filter applied even when admin can view users
body: The previous `!auth.users().canView()` guard was removed before setting the UserModel.GROUPS attribute. In V1 this is masked because the method returns an empty set when the admin can view users. However, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission only short-circuits on users().canView(), so this is fragile, and the same change is duplicated in BruteForceUsersResource.

title: canManage() grants manage on VIEW permission
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). An admin who holds only the 'view' scope on all groups is therefore treated as able to manage groups, for example creating top-level groups via addTopLevelGroup. This is a privilege escalation. The check should require only the MANAGE scope.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs, not group IDs
body: In V2, group resources are named by the group ID, but the code passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission (which looks the resource up by name) and adds groupResource.getId() to the result set. The returned set therefore holds authz resource IDs instead of group IDs. The users search and count group filters will match nothing, or fall back to the all-groups resource. Use groupResource.getName() in both places.

title: Possible NPE when all-groups resource is missing
body: getResourceTypeResource can return null, for example when the schema is unsupported or the 'Groups' resource is absent. hasPermission then passes that null to policyStore.findByResource and later calls resource.getScopes(), which throws a NullPointerException. A null check is needed before using the resource.

title: Permission results not filtered by resource ID
body: Unlike UserPermissionsV2, this loop accepts a matching scope from any permission returned by the evaluation, without checking permission.getResourceId() against the evaluated resource. Scopes granted on other resources could therefore satisfy the check for this group. Filter the permissions by resource ID, as UserPermissionsV2 does.

title: Group permission scan now runs on every user search
body: searchForUser now always calls getGroupIdsWithViewPermission. That method calls users().canView(), which can itself trigger a policy evaluation, and it then evaluates permissions for every group resource. Previously this work was skipped when users().canView() was already true. The cost is duplicated or extra evaluation on every user search.

title: canManage() grants on VIEW scope
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an admin holding only an all-groups VIEW permission passes requireManage(). That lets a view-only admin create top-level groups via addTopLevelGroup. The check should accept only the MANAGE scope.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource id instead of group id
body: In V2 the resource name is the group id, but the code passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission and adds it to the result. hasPermission looks the resource up by name, so the id lookup fails and falls back to the all-groups resource. The returned set then holds authz resource ids rather than group ids, so user search and count filtering by group (UserModel.GROUPS) will not match the intended groups. Use groupResource.getName() in both places.

title: Possible NPE when the all-groups resource is missing
body: getResourceTypeResource can return null, for example when the schema is unsupported or the realm was initialized before the Groups type existed. That null is passed straight to policyStore.findByResource and resource.getScopes(). Realms whose admin-permissions client was created before this change will not have a Groups resource, so every group permission check can throw.

title: Permissions not filtered by resource id
body: Unlike UserPermissionsV2, this loop does not check that permission.getResourceId() equals the evaluated resource's id. Permissions granted on other resources could therefore satisfy the scope check.

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian translation of totpStep1 was replaced with Italian ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'). Lithuanian users will see Italian. The same mistake is in login/messages_lt.properties loginTotpStep1 (line 71).

title: Simplified Chinese file gets Traditional Chinese text
body: The new totpStep1 value '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：' is Traditional Chinese, placed in the zh_CN (Simplified) bundle. Simplified Chinese users get inconsistent script.

title: ICU/MessageFormat syntax used in i18next bundle
body: The account-ui uses i18next with {{0}} interpolation, as every other key in this file does. Changing error-invalid-multivalued-size to Java MessageFormat '{0}' and '{2,choice,...}' means the placeholders will no longer be substituted and the raw choice syntax will be shown to users. The same problem applies to the admin-ui messages_en.properties.

title: Anchor check leaves unmatched English anchors and compares by position only
body: santizeAnchors removes the first textual occurrence of the English anchor instead of the matched position. It only checks that translated anchors appear in order. If the translation drops a closing , the remaining tags are passed to the sanitizer, which removes and reports a confusing result. There is also no check for href-only differences in attribute order or quoting.

title: Missing English file throws RuntimeException and breaks build
body: The English file path is derived by regex. If no matching _en file exists, for example for a file without a locale suffix or a theme with no English base, a RuntimeException is thrown. This bypasses the MojoExecutionException handling. The replaceAll on 'resources-community' also rewrites any path segment that contains that substring.

title: Java MessageFormat syntax used in i18next-based account UI
body: The account UI uses i18next interpolation with double braces ({{0}}), as the other keys in this file do. Changing error-invalid-multivalued-size to single-brace Java ChoiceFormat syntax ({0}, {2,choice,...}) means the React UI will not substitute the values. Users will see the raw '{0} ... {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' text. The same problem applies to the admin-ui messages_en.properties change.

title: Italian text placed into Lithuanian translation
body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian bundle was replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'). Lithuanian users will see Italian. The same mistake was made for loginTotpStep1 in login/messages_lt.properties.

title: Traditional Chinese text in Simplified Chinese bundle
body: The new totpStep1 value ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一') is Traditional Chinese, but this is the zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) bundle. It should use Simplified characters, e.g. 在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一.

title: Anchor check skips leftover English anchors and is order-sensitive
body: The loop advances the English matcher once per translated anchor and compares the tags pairwise. However, replaceFirst removes the first occurrence of that tag anywhere in the value, not necessarily the one just matched, so for repeated tags it may strip the wrong instance. Also, href attributes are compared verbatim, which is acceptable, but the anchors removed here are never passed through the sanitizer at all, so attribute content is never validated beyond the equality check.

title: English file path derivation is fragile
body: The path to the English file is built with replaceAll on the whole absolute path. The 'resources-community' replacement and the '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties' pattern operate on the full string; for example, '_en.properties' itself maps to itself. Any directory component containing these patterns would be altered. If the English file does not exist, a RuntimeException is thrown instead of a reported message, which aborts verification of the file.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian account bundle was replaced with an Italian sentence ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), so Lithuanian users will see Italian. The same mistake is in login/messages_lt.properties loginTotpStep1 (line 71).

title: Traditional Chinese text in Simplified Chinese bundle
body: totpStep1 was set to Traditional Chinese ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：') in the zh_CN (Simplified) file, so the string does not match the rest of the locale.

title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax used in i18next bundle
body: The account UI uses i18next interpolation ({{0}}), but error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed to Java MessageFormat syntax ({0}, {2,choice,...}). It will render literally as '{0} ... {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' in the React UI. The admin-ui messages_en.properties has the same problem.

title: English file path derivation breaks on paths and throws for missing file
body: The English path is built with a global replaceAll of 'resources-community'→'resources'. Any file without a locale suffix, or with no English counterpart, makes the code throw a RuntimeException. That fails the whole build instead of reporting a message. The regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` can also match the first underscore in the file name, not just the locale suffix.

title: Anchor removal uses replaceFirst on the whole string, not the matched position
body: After an anchor matches the English one, the code removes the first occurrence of that text anywhere in the value. It does this while the matcher is still iterating over the original string, so later positions are evaluated against stale offsets. Anchors are also stripped before sanitizing, so any attributes they carry (for example javascript: hrefs that equal the English source) are never checked by the sanitizer.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has wrong substring index and inverted check
body: The grant shortcut sits at characters 4-6 of the prefix (substring(4,6)), but the matcher reads substring(3,5). It also returns false when the values are equal, which inverts the check. A wrong grant type passes as long as the UUID part is valid, so the matcher never verifies the grant and these integration assertions cannot catch encoding regressions. Use `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

title: rawTokenId null check validates grantType instead
body: The fourth `requireNonNull` passes `grantType` with the message for rawTokenId, so a null `rawTokenId` is accepted silently. Tokens could then be encoded with the literal suffix "null".

title: Token creation fails for grant types that are not registered OAuth2GrantType providers
body: `initToken` always calls `encodeTokenId`, which throws IllegalStateException when the grant type has no registered OAuth2GrantType factory. One example is the pre-authorized code grant when OID4VC_VCI is disabled. Another is any custom code path that sets an unregistered string in `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`. Token issuance would then fail with a 500 error. The legacy TokenExchangeProvider path also never sets GRANT_TYPE, so it falls back to "na" and silently loses the grant information.

title: Duplicate shortcut detection via map sizes is unreliable
body: If two grants share a shortcut, grantsByShortcuts has one fewer entry than grantsToShortcuts, so that case is detected. A custom grant whose shortcut is "na" collides with the UNKNOWN entry. Both maps can also shrink by the same amount in other collision cases. Separately, OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() is a new abstract method, which breaks third-party grant factories at compile time or with AbstractMethodError. It also has no length validation, while the decoder assumes exactly 2 characters. Consider a default implementation plus explicit validation.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher checks wrong substring with inverted logic
body: The grant shortcut occupies characters 4-6 of the prefix, i.e. `substring(4, 6)`. The matcher uses `substring(3, 5)`, which straddles the token-type and grant shortcuts. It also returns false when that substring EQUALS the expected shortcut, which is the opposite of the intended check. Because the wrong substring almost never equals the shortcut, the matcher passes for any grant type. The integration tests therefore do not verify that the correct grant is encoded in the token ID.

title: rawTokenId null check validates grantType instead
body: The constructor calls `requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`, so it checks grantType twice and never checks rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is accepted silently and later encoded as the literal string "null" in the token ID.

title: Token issuance fails for grant types without a registered factory
body: `encodeTokenId` throws IllegalStateException when the grant type stored in the client session context has no known shortcut. That attribute is set from the raw `grant_type` form parameter. Any flow that sets an unrecognized grant type will now fail access-token creation with a 500 error. Examples are custom grants whose factory id differs from the grant_type value, or the legacy token exchange path. Consider falling back to UNKNOWN instead of throwing.

title: New abstract method breaks existing custom grant type providers
body: `getShortcut()` is added to the public SPI interface without a default implementation, so existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations no longer compile. The PR also removes the public `Context(Context)` copy constructor, which breaks callers that use it. Separately, the javadoc says shortcuts are "usually like 3-letters", but the decoder hard-requires exactly 2 characters. A custom grant with a 3-letter shortcut will produce token IDs that cannot be parsed.

title: Duplicate-shortcut detection ineffective
body: If two grants share a shortcut, `grantsByShortcuts` loses an entry while `grantsToShortcuts` keeps both, so the sizes differ and an error is thrown. However, the lazy refresh methods can later overwrite mappings without any validation. Duplicates introduced by grants deployed at runtime are therefore not detected, and decoding becomes ambiguous.

title: isAccessTokenId uses wrong substring and inverted check
body: The grant shortcut occupies characters 4-6 of the encoded prefix, so it is `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`. On top of that, the matcher returns false when the extracted value equals the expected shortcut. Taken together, the matcher accepts token IDs whose grant type is wrong and would reject a correctly encoded one. The grant-type assertions in the event tests are therefore meaningless.

title: rawTokenId null check validates grantType instead
body: The second `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...)` was meant to check `rawTokenId`, as its message says. A null rawTokenId is accepted, and encoding then produces IDs like `onrtac:null`.

title: Duplicate-shortcut validation is incomplete; custom grants can break token issuance
body: The size comparison misses collisions, for example two grants sharing a shortcut while another pair collides on ID. Shortcuts are also never checked to be exactly 2 characters, yet the decoder requires a 6-character prefix. A custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` returning a 3-letter shortcut (the interface javadoc even suggests 3 letters) yields token IDs that `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects. A factory returning null from `getShortcut` makes ConcurrentHashMap throw an NPE at startup. Adding `getShortcut()` as an abstract method also breaks every existing third-party grant factory at compile time; a default implementation would avoid that.

title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed
body: The public copy constructor of `OAuth2GrantType.Context` was deleted. Extensions or subclasses that use it will no longer compile. It should be kept, with the new `grantType` field also copied.

title: Unregistered grant type string makes token creation throw
body: A flow can set `GRANT_TYPE` to a value with no registered factory. Examples are a disabled feature or a custom provider such as PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType when its feature toggles at runtime. In that case `encodeTokenId` throws `IllegalStateException` and access token issuance fails. Falling back to the unknown (`na`) shortcut would avoid the outage.

title: Raw recovery codes sent to user storage in plaintext
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generated codes to JSON and passes them to the user storage provider through updateCredential. Local storage only keeps hashed codes, so this changes the security contract: every federated provider that accepts this credential type receives, and probably persists, cleartext recovery codes. Consider sending hashed codes instead, or documenting this behaviour explicitly.

title: Federated recovery codes are never consumed or removed
body: When the credential comes from federated storage, createFromCredentialModel rebuilds the model from the provider's data. Nothing marks the used code as consumed, so the same code stays valid and allCodesUsed() never becomes true. Separately, removeStoredCredentialById only touches local storage, so a federated credential would never be removed even if it were used up. The result is that codes stay reusable indefinitely and the user is never prompted to regenerate them.

title: Federated credential data format may not match the expected model format
body: getCredential returns whatever CredentialModel the federated provider exposes. The authenticator and the login bean then call RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel on it, which expects Keycloak's internal JSON format with hashed codes and numbers. A provider that stores raw data in the shape this PR's own updateCredential input implies (a JSON list of raw codes) will make parsing fail. It will also make getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() throw, which surfaces as a 500 on the login page.

title: getCredentials can throw NPE for unknown user
body: getCredentials dereferences myUser without a null check. If the user is not in the map, accessing myUser.recoveryCodes throws a NullPointerException. Other methods in this class, such as isConfiguredFor and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream, guard against a null user.

title: Raw plaintext recovery codes sent to user storage
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the generatedCodes list as JSON and passes it to user.credentialManager().updateCredential, which hands it to every federated user storage provider supporting the type. These are the raw recovery codes, not hashed. External storages will therefore receive and likely persist plaintext recovery codes. The local provider stores only hashes, so this weakens the security model. The codes should be hashed before being sent, or the contract with providers should be documented explicitly.

title: Removing a federated credential via removeStoredCredentialById is a no-op
body: getCredential may now return a credential that lives in federated user storage. After a code is used, removeStoredCredentialById is called with that credential's ID, but that method only removes credentials from local storage. For federated credentials the removal does nothing. Also, nothing marks the used code as consumed in the federated store.

title: Federated recovery codes never consumed, so the same code is reusable
body: The bean builds a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel from the credential returned by getCredential and takes the next unused code number from it. For federated credentials, nothing in the PR updates the 'used' state after a successful login, so the same code index is always requested. In the test storage, isValid also accepts any listed code, so a single code can be reused indefinitely.

title: Plaintext recovery codes sent to user storage providers
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw plaintext recovery codes to JSON and passes them to the user storage provider through updateCredential. Locally created recovery codes are stored hashed, so any federated provider now receives and may persist the codes in cleartext. A leak of the external store would directly expose usable second-factor codes.

title: Used recovery codes are never consumed in user storage
body: When the credential comes from the federated provider, removeStoredCredentialById only deletes local DB credentials. Nothing else in the flow marks a used code as consumed in the federated store. As a result the same recovery code stays valid indefinitely, and the 'next code' number in the login bean never advances. Recovery codes are meant to be single-use, so this defeats that guarantee for user-storage users.

title: Federated credential always preferred over local, even if stale
body: getCredential prefers federated credentials and only falls back to local storage if none are found. If a user has both a local credential and a federated one, the local credential is ignored. That can show the wrong code number to the user or skip the all-codes-used handling for the credential that is actually being validated.

title: Unchecked Optional.get on recovery code credential
body: credentialModelOpt.get() is called without checking the Optional. If neither user storage nor the local DB returns a recovery-codes credential, for example when the provider's isConfiguredFor and getCredentials disagree, this throws NoSuchElementException and the login page fails to render.

title: Reader thread not joined before asserting; test can pass despite failures
body:
The test sets `deletedAll` and asserts on `caughtExceptions` right away, without joining the reader thread. Exceptions from an in-flight request can arrive after the assertion, so the test can miss failures.

The reader may also not have started or completed a single request before the deletes finish, so the race may never be exercised. If a delete throws, `deletedAll` is never set and the thread loops forever. Keep a handle to the thread, set the flag in a finally block, and join the thread before asserting.

title: Other subgroup methods still NPE when group deleted concurrently
body: `getSubGroupsCount` now null-checks `modelSupplier.get()`. The three `getSubGroupsStream` overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 still dereference `modelSupplier.get()` directly. A group removed concurrently can therefore still cause the same NPE through those paths.

title: Reader thread not joined before asserting exceptions
body: The test sets `deletedAll` and immediately asserts that `caughtExceptions` is empty. The reader thread is never joined, so a request that is still in flight, or an exception raised during the last iterations, is not observed. The test can pass even when the NPE still occurs. It can also leave a live thread running into later tests. Keep a reference to the thread and `join()` it before the assertion.

title: Other subgroup methods still NPE when group is deleted concurrently
body: The fix null-guards only `getSubGroupsCount`. The `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 still dereference `modelSupplier.get()` without a check. If the group is deleted concurrently, these overloads hit the same NPE this PR is meant to fix.

title: getSubGroupsCount may now return null
body: Callers such as `populateSubGroupCount` now receive a null count for a deleted group. Any caller that unboxes the `Long` (for example, comparing it with 0) will throw an NPE instead. Returning 0 would be safer, as would documenting that the method can return null.

title: Reader thread not joined before asserting; exceptions can be missed
body: The test sets `deletedAll` and immediately asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty. It never joins the reader thread, so a request still in flight when the flag flips can fail after the assertion has already passed. If the reader thread never got scheduled before deletion finished, the test also verifies nothing. The thread is never stopped on failure and may outlive the test, hitting the realm during cleanup. Fix: join the thread (with a timeout) before asserting, and ensure at least one read actually ran concurrently with the deletes.

title: Sibling subgroup methods still NPE when group was deleted concurrently
body: `getSubGroupsCount` now null-checks `modelSupplier.get()`. The three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads (lines 256, 262, 268) still call `modelSupplier.get()` directly. If the group was deleted concurrently, the supplier returns null and these throw the same NPE this PR is meant to fix.

title: getSubGroupsCount returns null for deleted group
body: When the group has been removed, `getSubGroupsCount` now returns `null` as a `Long`. Any caller that unboxes the result to `long`, or does arithmetic or comparison on it, will throw an NPE instead. `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` is safe because it stores the value, but other callers may not be. Consider returning 0, or documenting the nullable return.

title: Negative queryset slicing raises in Django
body: When advanced features are enabled and the cursor offset is negative, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise ValueError/AssertionError. A client-supplied cursor like `0:-5:0` therefore causes a 500 error rather than the advertised 'reverse pagination'. The negative-offset branch should be removed and the offset validated as non-negative.

title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets for prev cursors
body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` lets a user-controlled negative offset on a prev cursor (e.g. `123:-10:1`) reach `queryset[offset:stop]`. Django querysets reject negative slicing, so every BasePaginator endpoint in Sentry can be made to return a 500 with a crafted cursor. Clamp the offset with `max(0, offset)` in all cases, or reject negative offsets in Cursor parsing.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime keys
body: `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on the attribute, and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw number. The endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by='-datetime'`, so `math.floor(datetime)` raises TypeError on any non-empty page. Cursor values are also compared against the datetime column as plain integers. The optimized path is broken whenever there are results; it should reuse DateTimePaginator's key and cursor-value conversion.

title: organization_context.member may be None
body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated even for superusers who are not members, and `or` only short-circuits when `is_superuser` is true. Any other request whose context has no member, such as API tokens or staff, raises AttributeError. Use a None-safe check on `member` before reading `has_global_access`.

title: Comments claim unsafe behavior is safe
body: The comments at lines 878-879 say negative offsets 'enable access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' and are 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level'. No validation bounds the cursor offset at all. The feature is driven entirely by a client-controlled query param and cursor, so these comments misrepresent the risk. There are also no tests for the new paginator or the endpoint branch.

title: Negative queryset slicing raises in Django
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices the queryset with `queryset[start_offset:stop]` using a negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError` ("Negative indexing is not supported"). Any request with a cursor such as `0:-5:0` will crash with a 500 error. The comment claiming the ORM "properly handles negative slicing" is wrong.

title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets for prev cursors
body: For prev cursors, `start_offset` is set to the raw `offset`, so a user-supplied negative offset (e.g. `123:-10:1`) reaches the queryset slice and raises `ValueError`. Previously this was also unvalidated, but the new code explicitly keeps negative offsets on the prev path. This affects every DateTimePaginator/Paginator endpoint, letting callers trigger 500s at will. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime key
body: The endpoint orders by `-datetime`, but `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on the raw attribute. Those calls fail on datetime objects with a TypeError. `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw integer instead of converting it to a datetime, so cursor filtering compares a datetime column against a number. The optimized path therefore errors on any non-empty result set.

title: organization_context.member may be None
body: For superusers or staff who are not members of the organization, `organization_context.member` can be None. The `or` only short-circuits when `is_superuser` is true. Any other user without a membership row, such as staff, raises AttributeError and gets a 500.

title: Feature intent is to read data "beyond normal pagination bounds"
body: The code comments describe negative offsets as giving access to data beyond normal pagination bounds, justified by permissions being checked at the queryset level. Exposing an undocumented, user-controlled offset bypass behind a query flag is unsafe. It should be removed rather than shipped.

title: No tests for new paginator or endpoint branch
body: The PR adds `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and a new endpoint code path with no tests. Basic coverage would have caught the datetime and negative-slice failures.

title: Negative offset slicing on Django QuerySet raises error
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the paginator slices the queryset with a negative start index (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`). Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError` ("Negative indexing is not supported"). Any request whose cursor has a negative offset therefore gets an unhandled exception and a 500 response. The code comment saying the ORM "properly handles negative slicing automatically" is wrong.

title: BasePaginator passes negative offsets through for prev cursors
body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` clamps only next cursors. A user-supplied prev cursor such as `1:-5:1` slices the queryset with a negative index, which raises an error and returns a 500. This affects every BasePaginator subclass across the API, not only the new audit-log path.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime keys
body: `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on the raw attribute value, and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw number. The audit-log endpoint orders this paginator by `-datetime`, so `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError` whenever there are results. Cursor values would also be compared against the datetime column as plain numbers, which is wrong. The optimized path fails for any non-empty result set; it should use the DateTimePaginator conversion logic.

title: Possible AttributeError when member is None
body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated even when the requester has no membership, for example a superuser or staff user accessing the org, in which case `member` can be None. The `or` short-circuits only when `is_superuser` is true, so other non-member users with audit access (such as staff) crash with `AttributeError` before the check completes.

title: Comments claim negative offsets reach data beyond pagination bounds
body: The feature is described as allowing "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds", with a claim that this is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level. Offsets come straight from an untrusted cursor and the bounds checks are deliberately removed. Even though the queryset is org-filtered, this is an unvalidated input path with no tests. The offset should be validated, and a BadPaginationError raised for negative values, as other paginators already do.

title: No tests for new paginator or endpoint branch
body: The PR adds OptimizedCursorPaginator, a new endpoint branch, and changes BasePaginator offset handling, but includes no tests. The datetime-key crash and the negative-slice errors would have been caught by basic tests.

title: Negative offsets are passed straight into a Django queryset slice
body: When advanced features are enabled, a client-controlled negative `cursor.offset` is used directly as `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django querysets raise `ValueError` ("Negative indexing is not supported") for negative slice bounds, so any such cursor produces a 500 error. The comment claiming the ORM "properly handles negative slicing" is wrong, and the stated purpose of reaching data "beyond normal pagination bounds" is a red flag for this feature.

title: BasePaginator still slices with a negative offset for prev cursors
body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` clamps the offset only for forward cursors. A user-supplied prev cursor with a negative offset (e.g. `0:-5:1`) still reaches `queryset[-5:...]`, which makes Django raise and the request return a 500. This path is shared by every endpoint that uses Paginator or DateTimePaginator. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError` instead.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime keys
body: `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on the attribute, and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw number. The audit log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `math.floor(datetime)` raises a `TypeError`. The cursor value would also be compared as a raw integer against a datetime column. The optimized path is therefore broken for its only caller.

title: organization_context.member may be None
body: For a superuser who is not a member of the organization, `organization_context.member` can be None. Because `or` short-circuits, superusers happen to be safe. However, a non-superuser request reaching this line with no membership would raise `AttributeError` on `.has_global_access`. Guard the member lookup explicitly instead of relying on evaluation order.

title: Span eviction is silent and the cap is hardcoded
body: Segments larger than 1000 spans are now trimmed with `zpopmin`, which drops the spans with the earliest end timestamps, possibly including the root span. No metric or log records this, whereas the removed Python check emitted `segment_span_count_exceeded`. The limit is also hardcoded in the script, so `max_segment_spans` in `SpansBuffer` is now unused. No test covers the eviction behaviour.

title: Redirect depth limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 without explanation
body: The loop bound for following redirects drops from 10000 to 1000, and the comment noting that deeper segment trees may not be joined correctly was removed. Segment trees deeper than 1000 levels will now be split incorrectly, and the PR gives no justification for the change.

title: __reduce__ passes redis_ttl into the wrong positional slot
body: `__reduce__` passes `redis_ttl` as the fourth positional argument, which the constructor binds to `segment_page_size`. After pickling to multiprocessing workers, the buffer ends up with the wrong page size and the default TTL. This bug predates the PR, but the PR is touching the related segment configuration.

title: Negative offsets passed to Django queryset slicing raise errors / expose data
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with a negative start offset whenever the cursor offset is negative and advanced features are on. The cursor offset is fully client-controlled. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise ValueError/AssertionError, so these requests fail with a 500. The comment that the ORM 'properly handles negative slicing' is false, and the stated intent of reaching data 'beyond normal pagination bounds' is a security smell.

title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets for prev cursors
body: BasePaginator previously sliced the queryset with the raw offset. It now uses an unclamped offset when `is_prev` is set. A client-supplied cursor such as `0:-5:1` sends a negative slice to the Django queryset, which raises an exception (500) on every endpoint that uses Paginator or DateTimePaginator. Clamping only for non-prev cursors gives no protection where negative offsets are actually reachable.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator breaks on datetime keys
body: The audit log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by=-datetime`. Its `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on a datetime value, which raises TypeError. Its `value_from_cursor` returns the raw number instead of a datetime, so the generated SQL compares a timestamp column against an integer. The optimized pagination path therefore fails for every request that uses it.

title: organization_context.member may be None
body: For superusers or staff who are not members of the organization, `organization_context.member` is None. Because `or` short-circuits, superusers are fine. A non-superuser with no membership, for example access through other permissions, gets an AttributeError when the code reads `member.has_global_access`, and the request returns a 500.

title: span_count can be stale after second zunionstore is skipped
body: When only the first zunionstore runs, `span_count` is taken from it, which is fine. The eviction step uses `zpopmin`, which removes the spans with the lowest scores (the earliest end timestamps). This can evict the root/segment span, so the flushed segment loses its root and `is_segment` detection breaks. Separately, the hardcoded 1000 limit ignores the configurable `max_segment_spans`.

title: __reduce__ passes redis_ttl as segment_page_size
body: `__reduce__` passes its arguments positionally, so the 4th argument (`redis_ttl`) lands in the `segment_page_size` parameter. In the multiprocessing path, which pickles the buffer, worker processes therefore get a page size of 3600 and the default TTL. This bug predates the PR but becomes more relevant now that the PR changes the buffer constructor's parameters.

title: No test for new eviction behavior
body: The PR adds span-count eviction in Lua and removes the `max_segment_spans` check in Python. No test covers a segment that exceeds 1000 spans, so it is unverified which spans are evicted or that the root span is preserved.

title: Negative offsets passed to Django queryset slicing raise errors
body: When advanced features are enabled and cursor.offset < 0, the code calls queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise ValueError/AssertionError, so a crafted cursor turns into a 500. The comment saying "the ORM handles negative slicing automatically" is false.

title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets through for prev cursors
body: For prev cursors, start_offset is set to the raw offset with no clamping. Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets, so a user-supplied cursor like '123:-5:1' leads to negative queryset slicing on every endpoint that uses BasePaginator. That raises an exception and returns a 500. The previous behaviour also passed the offset through, but the new comment claims this is safe, which it is not; the offset should be clamped or rejected.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime keys
body: get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on the key value, and value_from_cursor returns the raw number. The audit log endpoint orders this paginator by `datetime`, so math.floor on a datetime raises TypeError and the cursor number is compared against a datetime column. The optimized path fails on any non-empty result.

title: organization_context.member may be None
body: For superusers or staff who are not members of the organization, organization_context.member is None. Because `or` is evaluated left to right, superusers short-circuit and are fine. However, any non-superuser request without a membership raises AttributeError on `.has_global_access`, and that happens even when optimized_pagination was not requested.

title: span_count can be stale after the second zunionstore is skipped
body: span_count is set from the first union. If the second union is skipped, the count is correct. If the parent union runs, the count is overwritten, which is fine. However, when neither union runs, the count falls back to zcard, so this path is okay. The real problem is that the eviction cap is a hardcoded 1000 spans, while max_segment_spans=1001 in Python is now unused. Eviction with zpopmin removes the spans with the earliest end timestamps, which can include the root span, so segments silently lose data with no metric or log.

title: __reduce__ passes redis_ttl positionally into segment_page_size
body: The pickled SpansBuffer is rebuilt with (shards, timeout, root_timeout, redis_ttl). The fourth positional parameter of __init__ is segment_page_size, so after unpickling in multiprocessing workers, redis_ttl lands in segment_page_size and the real TTL resets to its default.

title: No test for eviction behavior
body: The new 1000-span eviction in add-buffer.lua is not covered by any test, so there is nothing verifying the cap or which spans are dropped.

title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is passed the outer `dataset`, not the `scoped_dataset` that is actually queried. In the dashboard split path, the outer dataset is metrics_enhanced while the query runs against discover with `!event.type:transaction`. The upsampling decision is then wrong for the query being run. Upsampled_count may also be applied to RPC or other datasets where the function does not exist, causing query failures.

title: Cache key uses Python hash(), invalidation is unreliable and keys can collide
body: Python `hash()` of a tuple is not guaranteed stable across processes or versions. More importantly, a hash can collide, so two different project sets can share one cache key and return the wrong eligibility. Combined with the 60s cache, this also makes the mocked-options tests order-dependent: one test's cached result can leak into the next. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called when the option changes, so stale results persist.

title: Substring match on event.type:error misfires on negations
body: `"event.type:error" in query` also matches `!event.type:error` and queries that OR in transactions. Upsampling would then be applied to non-error or mixed queries, where `sample_weight` is absent or meaningless.

title: upsampled_count has no null handling for sample_weight
body: `sum(sample_weight)` gives undercounted results when `sample_weight` is null or 0 for events. Examples are events ingested before the field existed, or events without client sampling. The comment simply assumes these cases never occur. A fallback such as `ifNull(sample_weight, 1)` would be safer.

title: Accidental submodule committed
body: A gitlink `sentry-repo` pointing at the base commit was added. This is an accidental artifact and breaks clones and CI that fetch submodules.

title: Eligibility check repeated per _get_event_stats call
body: The eligibility check runs on every `_get_event_stats` invocation, which can be up to three times per request in the split flow. Each run does a cache round-trip, so the claimed performance optimization adds overhead instead.

title: Cache key uses process-randomized hash(), invalidation won't work across processes
body: The cache key embeds Python's `hash()` of a tuple of project IDs. Tuples of ints hash deterministically, so key collisions are possible but rare. The bigger problem is the invalidation design: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` must be called with exactly the same project set that was queried. Nothing in this PR calls it when the allowlist option changes. As a result, allowlist changes take up to 60s to apply for every project combination, which contradicts the 'always latest configuration' note at line 50. The tests that patch `options` can also be affected by stale cache entries left from earlier tests.

title: Substring check for event.type:error matches negated queries
body: `_is_error_focused_query` does a substring search for `event.type:error`. A query like `!event.type:error` or `event.type:error_foo` also matches. Negated queries (e.g. `!event.type:error`, which selects transactions) would get the `sum(sample_weight)` transform. That produces wrong counts, or a query failure on the transactions storage.

title: Upsampling decision uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset/split query
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is passed the outer `dataset` and reads the query from `request.GET`. It ignores the `scoped_dataset` and `query` actually being executed. In the dashboard split paths, the discover sub-queries for errors-only and transactions-only can therefore get an inconsistent decision. For example, the transactions-only query can be upsampled when the original request contained `event.type:error`.

title: upsampled_count sums nullable sample_weight without fallback
body: `sum(sample_weight)` assumes every event has `sample_weight`. Events ingested before the feature, or without a client sample rate, will have null weight and be dropped from the count. Using something like `ifNull(sample_weight, 1)` would avoid undercounting errors.

title: Accidental submodule commit added
body: A `sentry-repo` gitlink pointing at the base commit was added to the repository. This looks accidental and will break clones and CI that try to resolve the submodule.

title: Linear allowlist membership per project
body: `project_id in allowlist` scans the list once for each project, which is O(n*m). Converting the allowlist to a set first would make each lookup constant time.

title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is passed the outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`. During the dashboard split flow, `_get_event_stats` is called with `discover` for errors-only queries and with the original dataset for other queries. The upsampling decision is still made from the request's top-level dataset. As a result, upsampling can be applied to the wrong dataset, or skipped for the error split queries.

title: Eligibility cache defeats allowlist changes, and the invalidation helper is never called
body: The allowlist result is cached for 60 seconds. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere, so allowlist changes take up to 60 seconds to apply. The docstring of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` says the configuration is read fresh each time, which the cache contradicts. Separately, the comment justifies the cache as avoiding an expensive option lookup, but `options.get` is already cached locally, so the extra cache round-trip likely makes things slower, not faster.

title: Python hash() in shared cache key
body: The cache key embeds `hash(tuple(...))` and is stored in a shared cache. Hashing a tuple of ints is stable across processes today, but it can collide, and two different project sets that collide would read each other's eligibility result. Use a deterministic join of the sorted IDs or a digest such as md5 instead.

title: Substring match for event.type:error is unreliable
body: `_is_error_focused_query` checks whether `event.type:error` appears anywhere in the lowercased query string. It therefore matches negated queries such as `!event.type:error`, and queries with OR clauses that also include transactions. In those cases `sum(sample_weight)` runs over transaction rows, where the column doesn't exist or is null, producing wrong counts or query failures.

title: sum(sample_weight) undercounts events lacking a weight
body: `upsampled_count` sums `sample_weight` and assumes every event in an allowlisted project has one. Events with a null weight, such as those ingested before sampling was enabled, contribute 0 instead of 1. Wrapping the column as `ifNull(sample_weight, 1)` would count them correctly.

title: Accidental submodule committed
body: A gitlink named `sentry-repo` pointing at the base commit has been added to the repository. It appears to be an accidental commit with no purpose in this change, and it will break clones and CI for anyone who initializes submodules. Remove it.

title: Trailing whitespace and misleading comments
body: Lines 223, 234 and 278 contain trailing whitespace, which lint will flag. The comments describing the check as a "cached result" and a "late transformation" for "query optimization" are inaccurate: the check simply runs on every call, and the transformation is the same in every branch.

title: zip of error_ids with get_multi values misaligns IDs and data
body: nodestore get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id; zipping error_ids against events.values() assumes ordering and completeness. If ids are deduplicated or missing, events get attributed to the wrong error id. Iterate node_ids and look up events[node_id] instead.

title: request.user.id may fail for org auth tokens / anonymous users
body: This endpoint accepts org auth tokens (is_org_auth_token_auth), where request.user is AnonymousUser with id None. Analytics are also recorded before the feature check, so events are emitted even for orgs without the feature.

title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with empty columns and data
body: When the use-table-widget-visualization flag is on, the widget is passed hardcoded empty columns/tableData instead of the query results, so flagged orgs see empty tables.

title: Logging whole WorkflowEventData object in extra
body: workflow_event_data contains the GroupEvent; putting the dataclass into log extra may be non-serializable/huge.

title: Hidden attributes only filtered when searching
body: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only in the search branch; with an empty query the sorted list is returned unfiltered, so hidden attributes still show by default.

title: PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title referenced but defined on CommitContextIntegration
body: _truncate_title is added to CommitContextIntegration, yet get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, which will raise AttributeError unless PRCommentWorkflow defines it.

title: zip of error_ids with get_multi values mis-associates IDs
body: fetch_error_details zips error_ids with events.values(). nodestore get_multi returns a dict keyed by node id; any missing or reordered entries pair the wrong event_id with the wrong event data. Iterate over node_ids and look each one up with events.get(node_id) instead.

title: Reference to PRCommentWorkflow inside CommitContextIntegration staticmethod
body: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template is defined on CommitContextIntegration, but it calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, and _truncate_title is also defined on CommitContextIntegration. The github/gitlab workflows call self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template on a PRCommentWorkflow subclass. Either the method is unreachable on that class (AttributeError), or the truncate helper is missing on PRCommentWorkflow. The methods look like they were placed in the wrong class.

title: request.user.id may fail for org auth token requests
body: The analytics event is recorded before the feature check using request.user.id. With org auth token authentication, request.user is AnonymousUser, whose id is None, so the event is emitted with a missing user. The event is also emitted for orgs that don't have the feature enabled. Record it after the feature check and handle the case where there is no authenticated user.

title: TableWidgetVisualization renders with empty data
body: When the feature flag is enabled, the table is passed hardcoded empty columns and data instead of tableResults. Users with the flag will see empty tables.

title: age/timestamp exclusivity check is truthy-based
body: The validators use initial_data.get(...) as a truthiness test, so age=0 or timestamp=0 is not detected as present. A report that includes both fields with one of them equal to 0 passes validation even though it should be rejected.

title: Disabled query reports pending forever
body: When the feature is disabled, the useApiQuery is not enabled and isPending stays true. The hook then reports pending indefinitely, so any consumer that checks pending before checking the feature flag will show a loading state that never resolves.

title: Error IDs zipped with nodestore results by position, can misattribute events
body: fetch_error_details zips `error_ids` with `events.values()` from nodestore get_multi. get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id, and ordering or missing keys are not guaranteed to match the input list. Error details can therefore be attached to the wrong event id, or shifted when some ids are missing. Look up each result by its generated node_id instead of relying on position.

title: Analytics recorded before feature check, and user id may be None
body: The assemble analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check, so requests that are rejected with 404 are still counted. Under org-auth-token auth, request.user is anonymous and `request.user.id` is None.

title: Feature-flagged table renders empty data
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, TableWidgetVisualization is passed hardcoded empty columns and empty data instead of `result`. Every table widget then renders blank for orgs with the flag on.

title: Static method on CommitContextIntegration references PRCommentWorkflow
body: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template is defined on CommitContextIntegration but calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title`. The helper is in the wrong class: the GitHub/GitLab PR comment workflows call `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` and `self.get_environment_info`. If these methods don't resolve on the workflow class, that call raises AttributeError.

title: Replay query 'field' params passed to process_raw_response may drop error_ids
body: If the client sends `field` params, process_raw_response restricts the output to those fields. `error_ids` may then be missing, which silently disables error context.

title: User verification skipped when Integration row doesn't exist yet
body: The authenticated-user check only runs when an Integration row already exists for the installation_id. If the installation webhook hasn't arrived yet, `Integration.DoesNotExist` makes the view call `pipeline.next_step()` without any user check. An attacker can supply someone else's installation_id before the webhook lands and take over the installation. The same applies to any installation that has no Integration row.

title: KeyError if integration metadata lacks sender
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes the webhook stored a sender. Integrations created through `build_integration` without a sender in state, and older records, have no such key. Those cases raise a KeyError and produce a 500 instead of the error page. Use `.get()` and treat a missing sender as an explicit failure.

title: redirect_uri not URL-encoded in authorize URL
body: The authorize URL is built with an f-string, so `redirect_uri` (and the other parameters) are not URL-encoded. A redirect URI containing `?`, `&` or `:` can be misparsed by GitHub. Build the query string with `urlencode`.

title: Token exchange and get_user_info errors not handled
body: `safe_urlopen` is called outside the try block, so a network error raises unhandled. `get_user_info` can also raise on an invalid token or an API error. Either failure surfaces as a 500 instead of the intended error page.

title: User verification skipped when Integration does not yet exist
body: When no Integration row exists for the installation_id, the view returns next_step() before the github_authenticated_user check runs. An attacker can supply any installation_id that has no webhook-created row yet and complete the pipeline without proving they installed it. build_integration fetches installation info and creates the integration anyway. The sender check is only enforced when a webhook-created row already exists, so the protection is bypassable.

title: KeyError when integration metadata lacks sender
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes the key exists. Integrations created through the pipeline, or older ones created before sender was stored, have no sender key. This raises a 500 instead of rendering the error page.

title: OAuth redirect URL parameters not URL-encoded
body: The redirect_uri and state are interpolated into the authorize URL without urlencode. The redirect_uri contains ':' and '/' characters and may contain query characters, which can corrupt the request to GitHub. Use urlencode to build the query string.

title: get_user_info failures not handled
body: get_user_info makes an HTTP call to GitHub. If GitHub returns an error or the call raises, the exception is not caught and the user sees a 500 instead of the friendly error page. safe_urlopen at line 423 is also outside the try block, so network errors there are unhandled too.

title: User check skipped when Integration row doesn't exist yet
body: When no Integration exists for the installation_id, the view calls pipeline.next_step() without comparing github_authenticated_user to the installer. An attacker who supplies a victim's installation_id before the installation webhook creates the Integration can bypass the new validation. The installation info and sender are then fetched in build_integration without any verification against the authenticated user.

title: KeyError if integration metadata lacks sender
body: The check reads integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] directly. Older integrations, and integrations created by build_integration when state has no sender, have no "sender" key. Reinstalling in those cases raises a 500 error instead of showing the error page. Use .get() and fail closed with error().

title: OAuth redirect URL query not URL-encoded
body: redirect_uri and the other parameters are inserted into the authorize URL by f-string, without urlencode. A redirect_uri with special characters, such as a query string or ports with paths, can be parsed incorrectly by GitHub. Build the query with urlencode.

title: Network errors from token exchange are unhandled
body: safe_urlopen sits outside the try block. A connection error or timeout reaching GitHub raises an unhandled exception and returns a 500 instead of the friendly error page. get_user_info is also called without error handling.

title: Default `queued` timestamp is evaluated once at import time
body: The field default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` runs once, when the module is imported. Every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` therefore carries the process start time, not the time it was queued, which makes the field meaningless. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

title: datetime in Celery task kwargs breaks JSON serialization
body: `asdict()` keeps `queued` as a `datetime` object, and that dict is passed as `assignment_source_dict` in the task kwargs. Sentry's Celery uses JSON serialization, which either cannot serialize the datetime or turns it into a string. In the string case, `from_dict` silently accepts a str for `queued`. In the failure case, enqueueing the task raises and the outbound sync is lost. Tests run under `self.tasks()`, which executes eagerly, so they do not catch this. Serialize `queued` explicitly (for example as ISO format or a timestamp) and parse it back in `from_dict`.

title: New `assignment_source` kwarg passed to integrations that may not accept it
body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)` on every integration. Any provider whose `sync_assignee_outbound` override (Jira, GitHub, VSTS, etc.) lacks `**kwargs` or an `assignment_source` parameter will raise TypeError, which breaks all outbound assignee sync for that provider. This PR does not update any of those implementations.

title: Inbound status sync path does not use AssignmentSource
body: Only assignee sync passes a source. Status changes coming in from an integration can still trigger outbound status sync back to the same integration, so the same cycle problem remains for status. Meanwhile the new `assignment_source` parameter on `sync_status_outbound` is never supplied by any caller.

title: queued default evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once, when the module is imported. Every AssignmentSource created afterwards gets the same stale timestamp instead of its own creation time. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance records when it was actually queued.

title: datetime in task kwargs is not JSON-serializable
body: `asdict()` keeps `queued` as a datetime object, and the result is passed as Celery task kwargs. With JSON serialization this either fails to serialize, or arrives at the worker as a string. If it arrives as a string, `from_dict` still accepts it, because the frozen dataclass does no type checking. If serialization fails, the outbound sync task cannot be enqueued at all. Serialize `queued` explicitly, for example as an ISO string, and parse it back in `from_dict`.

title: New assignment_source kwarg passed to all sync_assignee_outbound implementations
body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)` for every provider. The abstract signature accepts `**kwargs`, but concrete implementations (Jira, Jira Server, VSTS, GitHub, etc.) that don't declare `**kwargs` will raise TypeError on every outbound assignee sync. None of those implementations are updated in this PR.

title: assignment_source added to sync_status_outbound but never passed
body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature gains an `assignment_source` parameter, but no caller passes it. Status sync cycles are therefore not addressed, and the signature change is misleading to implementers.

title: Default `queued` timestamp is evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once, when the module is imported. Every AssignmentSource then shares the same stale timestamp. The fix is `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

title: datetime in task kwargs breaks JSON serialization and the cycle check
body: `to_dict()` uses `asdict`, so the payload contains a raw `datetime` in `queued`. Celery's JSON serializer either rejects it or turns it into a string. If it becomes a string, the frozen dataclass still accepts it at the worker, so the type is silently wrong. If serialization fails, the outbound task is never enqueued. The datetime should be converted to an ISO string or timestamp before enqueuing and parsed back in `from_dict`.

title: New `assignment_source` kwarg passed to integrations that don't accept it
body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`. Concrete implementations (Jira, VSTS, GitHub, etc.) were not updated in this PR. Any implementation whose signature lacks `**kwargs` will raise TypeError, breaking outbound assignee sync for that provider.

title: Abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature changed but never used
body: `assignment_source` was added to the abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature, but no caller passes it. Status-sync cycles are therefore not addressed, and the signature now disagrees with the subclasses.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with only `pass`. It leaves counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values and build_occurrence_and_event_data unimplemented, so they all remain abstract. When Detector.detector_handler calls group_type.detector_handler(self) for a metric_alert_fire detector, it raises TypeError. That breaks process_detectors for these detectors. Before this change the handler was a concrete no-op.

title: PriorityLevel(new_status) can raise for DetectorPriorityLevel values
body: The code converts DetectorPriorityLevel to PriorityLevel by integer value. If any non-OK DetectorPriorityLevel value has no matching PriorityLevel member, this raises ValueError during evaluation and aborts processing of the whole packet.

title: Test passes wrong value for group_2; value argument never verified
body: The expected occurrence for group_2 is built with value 6, but the packet's value for group_2 is 10. The test only passes because the mock builder ignores `value`. As a result, the tests never check that the correct value is forwarded to build_occurrence_and_event_data. Several other tests make the same mismatch, e.g. evaluating with 100 or 8 while building the expectation with 6.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with only `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler leaves several abstract members unimplemented: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values and build_occurrence_and_event_data. Any call to `detector.detector_handler` for a metric_alert_fire detector will therefore raise TypeError when it tries to instantiate the abstract class. Before this change the handler was a concrete no-op.

title: PriorityLevel(new_status) fails for detector levels with no PriorityLevel equivalent
body: The code converts a DetectorPriorityLevel to PriorityLevel by value. If DetectorPriorityLevel defines any non-OK value that PriorityLevel does not have, this raises ValueError and aborts evaluation for the whole packet. The surrounding state updates have already been enqueued at that point, so the enqueued state is left inconsistent with what was actually processed.

title: Test builds expected occurrences with wrong values, hiding mismatches
body: Several tests build the expected occurrence with value=6 even though the evaluated value is 10, 100 or 8. In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue the expected occurrence also uses group key 'val1' while the code evaluates 'group_key'. These tests only pass because the mock ignores both the value and, effectively, the fingerprint in a way that coincidentally matches. As a result the assertions do not verify that the correct value and group key are passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`. That leaves the abstract members unimplemented: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. When `Detector.detector_handler` calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)` for a `metric_alert_fire` detector, Python raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. Before this change the class was a concrete no-op handler, so this is a crash that did not exist previously.

title: DetectorPriorityLevel converted to PriorityLevel without validation
body: `PriorityLevel(new_status)` assumes every `DetectorPriorityLevel` value has a matching value in `PriorityLevel`. Any non-OK detector level that does not map (for example a level added only to `DetectorPriorityLevel`) raises `ValueError` mid-evaluation. Because the dedupe update has already been enqueued at that point, the failure leaves enqueued state for that packet that is not consistent with what was actually processed. There is no explicit mapping or check before the conversion.

title: Test builds expected occurrence with wrong value for group_2
body: The expected occurrence for group_2 is built with value 6, but the data packet supplies 10 for group_2. The tests pass only because the mock `build_occurrence_and_event_data` ignores `value`. As a result, nothing verifies that the hook receives the correct per-group value. The same pattern appears in other tests that use 6 for inputs of 8, 100 and 10.

title: Removed/renamed functions break existing imports and test mocks
body:
Before this change, `mark_failed.py` exported several names:
- `mark_failed_threshold`
- `create_issue_platform_occurrence`
- `get_failure_reason`
- `get_monitor_environment_context`
- `SimpleCheckIn`

They have been moved and renamed: `try_incident_threshold` and `create_incident_occurrence` now live in new modules. Any existing callers will fail with ImportError or AttributeError. Examples are tests that patch `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.produce_occurrence_to_kafka` or import `get_failure_reason` from `mark_failed`.

Patches targeting the old module path will also silently stop intercepting the calls, so Kafka production would not be mocked. No test updates are included in this PR. Either update those callers and mocks, or re-export the old names from `mark_failed.py`.

title: Removed symbols may break existing imports and test mocks
body: `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `mark_failed_threshold` and `SimpleCheckIn` were removed from `mark_failed.py` and moved elsewhere. `create_issue_platform_occurrence` was also renamed to `create_incident_occurrence`. No compatibility re-exports were left behind, and no test files were updated in this PR. Existing tests that patch `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.produce_occurrence_to_kafka` will stop intercepting the call, because the import now happens in `incident_occurrence.py`. Tests or other modules that import these names from `mark_failed` will fail with ImportError.

title: Removed names from mark_failed module break existing imports/mocks
body:
Three names were removed from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`: `mark_failed_threshold` and `create_issue_platform_occurrence` were renamed and moved, and `get_failure_reason` was moved without a rename.

None of them are re-exported from the old module. Any code or test that imports them or patches them with `mock.patch("sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.<name>")` will now fail, and the PR updates no tests. This most likely includes the existing mark_failed tests and the get_failure_reason tests.

Patches on `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.produce_occurrence_to_kafka`-style paths will also stop intercepting calls, because that logic now lives in `incident_occurrence`.

Either update the callers and patch targets, or keep backward-compatible aliases in `mark_failed`.

title: join() breaks out early leaving remaining processes un-terminated
body: When the deadline expires partway through the loop, `break` skips `process.terminate()` for all remaining processes. Those flusher processes keep running and keep producing after the consumer has shut down or rebalanced. Shards can then be flushed twice by the old and new owners. The loop should still terminate every process after the deadline passes.

title: Zero assigned shards causes modulo/empty process map issues
body: If a rebalance assigns no partitions, `assigned_shards` is empty and `num_processes` becomes 0. No flusher runs, and every per-process loop is a no-op. More importantly, `self.max_processes` is set from `max_processes or len(...)`, so passing 0 falls back silently. The previous single-process behaviour always ran a flusher. This needs at least a guard or an explicit decision about the zero-shard case.

title: isinstance check against multiprocessing.Process misses SpawnProcess
body: Processes are created from the spawn context (`SpawnProcess`), which is a subclass of `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`. As a result, `kill()` in `_ensure_processes_alive` is never called on hung processes. The same applies to `terminate()` in `join()`. A hung flusher is therefore left running alongside its replacement, and both flush the same shards. Check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` instead.

title: Inconsistent metric tag name 'shards' vs 'shard'
body: The `wait_produce` timer uses the tag key `shards`, while the other flusher metrics use `shard`. This breaks dashboards and queries that filter by a single key.

title: join breaks early on deadline and skips terminating remaining processes
body: In join(), the loop over processes uses `break` once the deadline has passed. Every process not yet visited is then never terminated. Those processes are daemon processes and keep running, flushing Redis and producing to Kafka after shutdown or across rebalances. With many shards, they can pile up as orphaned flushers.

title: isinstance check against multiprocessing.Process misses SpawnProcess
body: The processes are created through `get_context('spawn').Process`, so they are `SpawnProcess` instances. That class derives from `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.Process`. The checks `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` are therefore always False. As a result, hung processes are never killed before a replacement is spawned, and join never terminates processes. This differs from the old code, which called kill unconditionally.

title: Zero assigned shards causes modulo-by-zero / empty map
body: If a consumer is assigned no partitions, `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty. `max_processes` then falls back to 0 and `num_processes` is 0. No flusher runs, and the loop is empty, so the modulo-by-zero is never hit. However, passing `--flusher-processes 0` while shards are assigned makes `num_processes` 0 and raises ZeroDivisionError in `i % self.num_processes`.

title: Default flusher_processes=1 contradicts per-shard intent
body: The CLI default of 1 is always passed to the factory, so the `max_processes or len(shards)` fallback (one process per shard) is never reached in production. The PR description says the flusher spawns a process per shard, and the class docstring says it creates one process per shard. Both are wrong for the default configuration, which still runs a single flusher process.

title: Inconsistent metric tag key 'shards' vs 'shard'
body: The `wait_produce` timer uses the tag key `shards`, while the neighbouring metrics use `shard`. This inconsistency breaks dashboards and queries that group by the shard tag.

title: isinstance check against multiprocessing.Process misses SpawnProcess
body:
Processes are created with `mp_context.Process`, which produces `SpawnProcess` objects. `SpawnProcess` is a subclass of `BaseProcess`, not of `multiprocessing.Process`, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is False.

In `_ensure_processes_alive`, hung flusher processes are therefore never killed. A replacement is spawned alongside them, leaving duplicate flushers on the same shards.

The same check in `join()` (line 346) means processes are never terminated on shutdown. Check against `multiprocessing.context.BaseProcess` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)` instead.
