title: join breaks early on deadline, skipping termination of remaining processes
body: When the deadline is reached, the loop does `break` instead of continuing. Every remaining process is then left running without `terminate()` being called. These can keep flushing after the consumer is torn down or rebalanced, so the processes leak.

title: Zero assigned shards causes modulo/zero-process issues
body:
If `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty (for example, an empty partition assignment during a rebalance), `num_processes` becomes 0. No flusher process is created, and `i % self.num_processes` would raise ZeroDivisionError.

A negative `--flusher-processes` value produces the same failure. Guard with `max(1, ...)` and validate the option.

title: Inconsistent metric tag name 'shards' vs 'shard'
body:
The `wait_produce` timer is tagged `shards`, while the other new metrics use `shard`. Dashboards that filter by one tag name will miss this metric.

Separately, a comma-joined list of shards as a tag value increases cardinality and makes per-shard aggregation awkward.

title: Dead code: _create_process_for_shard unused
body: `_create_process_for_shard` is never called anywhere, so it is dead code.

title: Arroyo commit callback invoked from background thread
body: `_commit_loop` calls `commit_function` from a separate daemon thread. That function wraps Arroyo's `commit`. Arroyo's StreamProcessor commit and the consumer's stage_offsets are not thread-safe and are meant to be called from the main poll loop, typically from `poll()`. Calling them from another thread can race with rebalances and consumer operations, which risks corrupted or lost commits. Collect the committable offsets in the background if needed, but perform the commit inside `poll()`.

title: Strategy close shuts down the shared factory-level queue pool
body: The queue pool is created once in the factory `__init__` and shared by every strategy that `create_with_partitions` returns. On a rebalance, Arroyo closes the old strategy, and `close()`/`terminate()` call `queue_pool.shutdown()`, which stops all worker threads and shuts down the queues. The next strategy then reuses the dead pool, so `submit` puts into a shut-down queue, the exception is logged, and the offset is marked complete without processing. Results are silently dropped after the first rebalance.

title: No backpressure; unbounded queues and no MessageRejected
body: The queues are created unbounded and `submit` never raises MessageRejected, even though the docstring claims there is natural backpressure. A slow worker therefore lets memory grow without bound. Separately, `join()`/`close()` do not drain pending work before shutting down, and stale offsets from revoked partitions remain in the tracker and can be committed after a rebalance.

title: hash() of str is randomized per process
body: `hash(group_key)` is salted per process via PYTHONHASHSEED. Ordering within a single process still holds, but the docstring calls this "consistent hashing", which is misleading. Group-to-queue assignment will differ across restarts and processes.

title: Iterating defaultdict while other threads insert
body: `list(self.all_offsets.keys())` runs in the commit thread while `add_offset` can insert new partitions from the main thread without a global lock. Similarly, `_get_partition_lock` runs a check-then-setdefault. Because of this, the dicts are mutated concurrently with no single protecting lock.

title: Error-handling test asserts nothing meaningful
body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` ends with `assert len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`. This assertion does not verify that errors leave later offsets committable, which is the behavior the test claims to check. The real behavior commits both offsets, so the assertion contradicts the test's stated intent.

title: Arroyo commit callback invoked from background thread
body: `_commit_loop` calls `commit_function` from a separate daemon thread. That function wraps arroyo's `Commit` callback, which is not thread-safe and is meant to be called from the consumer's poll/submit thread. Calling it concurrently with the StreamProcessor run loop can race with stage/commit logic or the rebalance path. Commits should instead be gathered and issued from `poll()`.

title: close/join shut down the shared queue pool, breaking strategy after rebalance
body: On rebalance, arroyo calls `close()`/`join()` on the strategy. This shuts down `self.queue_pool`, which belongs to the factory and is shared across strategies. The next `create_with_partitions` call then reuses a pool whose queues are shut down and whose workers have exited, so every `put` raises `ShutDown`. The failure is swallowed by `submit`'s except block, which also marks the offset complete, so messages are silently dropped and their offsets committed. In addition, `join` does not wait for the in-flight work to drain before the final commit, so processed offsets are lost and get reprocessed.

title: Unbounded queues give no backpressure
body: The queues are created with `queue.Queue()` and no maxsize, and `submit` never blocks or raises `MessageRejected`. The docstring claims 'natural backpressure', but in practice a slow consumer will buffer unbounded messages in memory, which can lead to OOM.

title: Offsets skipped by compaction or transaction markers block commits forever
body: `get_committable_offsets` requires every integer between the last committed offset and the target to have been seen. Kafka offsets are not guaranteed to be contiguous; transactional control records and compaction both create gaps. When a gap occurs, commits stall permanently for that partition. The tracker also never removes state for revoked partitions.

title: Race between snapshot and mark_committed; dict iteration unsynchronized
body: `all_offsets.keys()` is iterated in the commit thread while the consumer thread may be inserting into the defaultdict at the same time. Separately, the per-partition lock creation done with `get` followed by `setdefault` is racy.

title: hash() on str is randomized per process
body: Python's `hash()` on strings is salted per process, so queue assignment is not stable across processes or restarts. This contradicts the docstring's claim of 'consistent hashing'. It is harmless within a single process, but the documentation is misleading.

title: Arroyo commit callback invoked from background thread
body: `_commit_loop` calls `commit_function` from a separate daemon thread. Arroyo's `Commit` callable is not thread-safe and is meant to be called from the main thread, typically inside `poll()`/`submit()`. Calling it concurrently with the StreamProcessor's own loop can race on its internal state. Committable offsets should be computed and committed inside `poll()` instead.

title: Shared queue pool shut down on partition revocation
body: The `FixedQueuePool` is created once per factory and shared by every strategy that `create_with_partitions` returns. On a rebalance, arroyo calls `close()`/`join()` on the old strategy, which shuts down the shared pool's queues and workers. The next strategy then reuses that dead pool, and any `put` on it raises `ShutDown`. The consumer stops processing after the first rebalance.

title: join() drops in-flight work and its final commit
body: `join()` sets the shutdown event and stops the commit thread before the queues are drained. Each worker's `shutdown` flag is also set, so the `while not self.shutdown` loop exits after the current item even though `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` alone would let it drain. As a result, queued items may never be processed, and offsets that were completed are never committed. After a rebalance this causes reprocessing, and work can be lost if another consumer has already committed past those offsets. The `timeout` argument is also ignored.

title: Unbounded queues, no backpressure
body: Each `queue.Queue()` is created without a `maxsize`, and `submit` never raises `MessageRejected`. The docstring claims natural backpressure, but a slow worker lets memory grow without limit while the consumer keeps polling.

title: Offset tracker state leaks across revoked partitions
body: Offsets for revoked partitions are never cleared from the tracker. If a partition is reassigned later, the stale `last_committed`/`all_offsets` state remains. A rewind to a lower offset would then never be committed, and stale entries for other partitions can still be committed after they are revoked.

title: queue.ShutDown requires Python 3.13
body: `queue.ShutDown` and `Queue.shutdown()` only exist in Python 3.13 and later. On older interpreters the `except queue.ShutDown` clause raises `AttributeError` when it is evaluated, and `shutdown()` fails; the exception is caught and only logged. Workers then block in `get()` forever.

title: Backup-code login skips password verification when any totpCode is also sent
body:
The password is only checked when `user.password && !credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new backup-code branch is evaluated before the TOTP branch and only needs `credentials.backupCode` to be truthy.

An attacker can POST to the credentials callback with `email`, any `password`, any non-empty `totpCode` (e.g. "1") and a valid `backupCode`. Because a totpCode is present, the password check is skipped. The backup-code branch then accepts the request without ever looking at the TOTP value.

The result is that a single leaked backup code plus the user's email is enough to take over the account. The codes are typically saved in the downloaded `cal-backup-codes.txt` or on the clipboard. This defeats the purpose of a *second* factor.

Fix: always verify the password when a backup code is used, or check the password based on identity provider rather than on whether `totpCode` is present.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write lets a backup code be reused and can resurrect consumed codes
body:
The code consumes a backup code by:
1. reading `user.backupCodes`,
2. decrypting and finding the index in memory,
3. writing back the re-encrypted array.

There is no transaction, optimistic version check or conditional update.

Two concurrent login requests with the same code will both pass validation and both succeed, which breaks the documented "each backup code can be used exactly once" guarantee. Two concurrent logins with *different* codes will each write their own snapshot. The later write overwrites the earlier one, so a consumed code becomes valid again (lost update).

Use an atomic conditional update (e.g. `updateMany` where `backupCodes` equals the value read, retrying on 0 rows) or a row lock inside a transaction.

title: Backup code match is case- and whitespace-sensitive while UI suggests uppercase
body:
Codes are generated as lowercase hex (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`). The comparison only strips dashes (`replaceAll("-", "")`) and then does an exact `indexOf`. The input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`, which implies uppercase entry.

A user who types the code in uppercase, or pastes it with surrounding whitespace, gets `IncorrectBackupCode` even though the code is valid. The same issue exists in `disable.ts` line 61.

Normalize with `.trim().toLowerCase()` before comparing.

title: Dismissing the backup-codes step via ESC/overlay leaves UI showing 2FA as disabled
body:
After a successful `enable` call, the modal now switches to `DisplayBackupCodes` instead of calling `onEnable()`. `onEnable` is only invoked from the "Close" button.

If the user dismisses the dialog with ESC or by clicking outside, `onOpenChange` fires instead. The parent just toggles `open`, so its `enabled` state is never set and `viewer.me` is never invalidated. The settings switch therefore shows 2FA as off even though it is enabled server-side.

The component's `step` state also stays at `DisplayBackupCodes`. Clicking the switch again reopens the modal on the backup-codes screen instead of the enable flow.

Call `onEnable` (or equivalent state sync) when the modal is closed from this step, or handle it in `onOpenChange`.

title: Copy button reports success unconditionally and crashes when Clipboard API is unavailable
body:
The result of `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` is neither awaited nor caught, and the success toast is shown immediately. If the write is rejected (for example, no permission), the user is told the codes were copied when they were not, and they may close the only screen that ever shows the codes.

On self-hosted instances served over plain HTTP (non-localhost), `navigator.clipboard` is `undefined`. The handler then throws a TypeError and nothing is copied.

Await the promise and show an error toast on failure.

title: "missing_backup_codes" tells users to generate codes in settings, but no such feature exists
body:
The message reads "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." This PR adds no way to generate or regenerate backup codes. They are only created in `setup.ts`, which refuses to run when 2FA is already enabled.

This matters in two cases:
- Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have `backupCodes = null`. They get this message and cannot follow it except by disabling and re-enabling 2FA.
- Users who exhaust all 10 codes have an array of `null`s. They get `incorrect_backup_code` rather than any guidance.

Either add a regenerate flow or reword the message to the actual remedy.

title: tabIndex=-1 on shared PasswordField toggle removes keyboard access to show/hide password
body:
Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the visibility toggle button in the shared `PasswordField` makes the show/hide control unreachable by keyboard. This applies to every password field in the app, not just the 2FA modals.

This is an accessibility regression for keyboard and screen-reader users, and it is unrelated to the backup-code feature.

title: Backup codes stored reversibly encrypted rather than hashed
body:
Backup codes are only ever compared for equality and never need to be shown again after setup. Even so, they are stored with `symmetricEncrypt` using the app-wide `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

Anyone who obtains a DB dump plus that key can recover every user's unused backup codes in plaintext. Hashing each code (as is done for passwords) would avoid this. The TOTP secret has to be reversible, but backup codes do not.

title: No tests for logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code; enable test asserts nothing
body:
The new authentication paths have no tests:
- backup-code login in `next-auth-options.ts`;
- backup-code disable in `disable.ts`;
- one-time consumption of a code.

The PR leaves a TODO for these instead.

In the first test, `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` passes a Promise to `expect`, so it always passes, as the added FIXME admits. The test also navigates to logout without waiting for the enable request or the new backup-codes screen, so it can race.

The copy test only waits for the toast, which is shown regardless of whether the clipboard write succeeded.

title: Valid backup code plus any dummy totpCode logs in without a password
body:
The password check at line 121 runs only when `credentials.totpCode` is empty (`if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`). The new branch at line 131 then takes priority over TOTP whenever `credentials.backupCode` is set, and the TOTP code is never checked.

So an attacker can POST to the credentials callback with the victim's email, `totpCode=000000` and one valid backup code. The password check is skipped, the junk TOTP is never validated, and the backup code alone grants a session. Backup codes are offered as a plaintext download (`cal-backup-codes.txt`) and via the clipboard, so leaking one is realistic. This reduces 2FA to a single factor that is easier to steal than the password.

Fix: always verify the password for CAL users when a backup code is used. Better still, reject requests that carry both `totpCode` and `backupCode`, and stop tying password verification to the absence of `totpCode`.

title: Backup code consumption is non-atomic read-check-write (single-use not guaranteed)
body:
The handler reads `user.backupCodes`, decrypts it, finds the index, nulls that entry, then writes the whole re-encrypted blob back with a plain `update`. Nothing checks that the stored value is still the one that was read.

Two concurrent login requests with the same backup code can both pass `indexOf` before either write lands, so a code meant to be used "exactly once" can open several sessions.

A concurrent use of a different code can also be lost (last write wins), which leaves an already-used code valid.

Fix: do a conditional update, e.g. `updateMany` with `where: { id, backupCodes: <original ciphertext> }`, and fail if `count === 0`. Alternatively, store codes in a separate table and delete the row atomically.

title: Dismissing the backup-codes step via Escape/overlay never calls onEnable, leaving stale UI state
body:
After a successful enable, the modal now moves to `DisplayBackupCodes` instead of calling `onEnable()`. Only the custom "Close" button calls `onEnable()`.

The Dialog can also be closed through `onOpenChange` (Escape key, overlay click, the X). That path just toggles `open` in the parent, so `onEnable` never runs. 2FA is already enabled on the server, yet the settings switch keeps showing it as disabled: the `me` query is not invalidated and the success toast never fires.

The component's `step` also stays at `DisplayBackupCodes`. Reopening the modal shows the old codes with no Cancel button. If the user instead retries enabling, `setup` returns `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled`, which the modal shows as "something went wrong".

Fix: handle `onOpenChange` while on the backup-codes step (call `onEnable` and `resetState`), or block dismissal on that step.

title: Existing 2FA users get a 'Lost access' option with no codes and are pointed to a settings feature that doesn't exist
body:
Backup codes are only generated in `setup.ts` during a new 2FA setup. Every user who already has 2FA enabled has `backupCodes = NULL`.

The login page and the disable modal still show them the "Lost access" button. Using it returns `MissingBackupCodes`, whose message reads "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." This PR adds no way to generate or regenerate backup codes in settings. The only route is to disable and re-enable 2FA, which the locked-out user cannot do.

Once all 10 codes are used, the stored array holds only nulls, so the user gets `IncorrectBackupCode` rather than any hint that the codes are exhausted.

Fix: either add a regenerate-codes feature, or reword the message and hide "Lost access" when no codes exist.

title: No test covers logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code, or single-use consumption
Backup codes stored reversibly encrypted instead of hashed
body:
Backup codes are stored as `symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(codes), CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)`. Unlike the TOTP secret, the server never needs the plaintext codes back; it only has to check that a submitted code matches.

With reversible encryption, anyone who obtains a DB dump plus the encryption key (one env var, shared with other secrets) gets every user's usable bypass codes.

Store a salted hash per code (e.g. bcrypt/argon2 or HMAC) and compare hashes on use.

title: Uppercase placeholder suggests uppercase codes, but matching is case-sensitive against lowercase hex
body:
Codes are generated with `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, so they are lowercase. Both `next-auth-options.ts` and `disable.ts` compare with `indexOf(code.replaceAll("-", ""))`, which is an exact, case-sensitive match with no trimming.

The input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`. A user who types a code from paper in uppercase, or pastes one with surrounding whitespace, is rejected as "Backup code is incorrect."

Normalize input with `.trim().toLowerCase()` before comparing.

title: Copy shows a success toast without awaiting the clipboard, and crashes where the Clipboard API is unavailable
body:
The `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` promise is not awaited, so "Backup codes copied!" appears even when the write is rejected (permission denied).

On self-hosted instances served over plain HTTP on a non-localhost host, `navigator.clipboard` is `undefined`. The click handler then throws a TypeError and nothing is copied.

Await the promise, show an error toast on failure, and guard for a missing `navigator.clipboard`.

title: Password visibility toggle removed from keyboard tab order app-wide
body:
Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the show/hide password button in the shared `PasswordField` makes it unreachable by keyboard. This affects every password field in the app, not just the 2FA modals.

Keyboard-only and assistive-technology users can no longer reveal their password. This is an accessibility regression unrelated to backup codes.

title: Backup code alone logs in without a password when any totpCode is sent
body:
Line 121 only checks the password when `credentials.totpCode` is falsy (`if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`). The new backup-code branch at line 131 runs before the TOTP branch and never looks at `totpCode`.

So a request to the credentials provider with `email`, any non-empty `totpCode` (e.g. "1"), and one valid `backupCode` skips the password check, passes the backup-code check, and returns an authenticated user. A leaked backup code (they are offered as a downloadable txt file) is then enough to take over a CAL-password account, which defeats the purpose of a second factor.

Fix: always verify the password for CAL users regardless of `totpCode`, or at least reject requests that carry a backupCode with a totpCode and require password verification on the backup-code path.

title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body:
The code reads the encrypted backup-code array, finds the index in memory, nulls it, and writes the whole re-encrypted blob back. Nothing makes this atomic: no transaction, no conditional update, no version check.

- Two concurrent logins with the same code both pass the `indexOf` check and both succeed, so a single-use code can be used twice.
- Two concurrent logins with different codes each null their own index on the same stale copy. The last writer wins and restores the other, already-used code to valid.

Use a conditional update (e.g. `updateMany` where `backupCodes` equals the value that was read, then fail if count is 0) or a serializable transaction.

title: Dismissing the dialog on the backup-codes step leaves UI out of sync and step stale
body:
After a successful enable, `onEnable()` is no longer called. It now only runs when the user clicks "Close" on the new DisplayBackupCodes step. 2FA is already enabled on the server at this point.

If the user dismisses the dialog any other way (Escape or overlay click, both handled by `onOpenChange`), then:
- `onEnable` never fires, so the parent never refreshes and the 2FA switch keeps showing "disabled".
- `resetState` never runs, so `step` stays `DisplayBackupCodes`. Reopening the modal from the (wrong) unchecked switch lands directly on the old backup codes screen.

Either call `onEnable` (or a refresh) as soon as enable succeeds, or handle `onOpenChange` on this step the same way as Close.

title: Backup code input not normalized for case/whitespace
body:
Codes are generated as lowercase hex (`randomBytes(5).toString('hex')`). The input only strips dashes before an exact `indexOf` match. The same applies in disable.ts line 61.

The input placeholder is "XXXXX-XXXXX" (uppercase), and users commonly paste with leading or trailing whitespace. Either case makes a valid code fail with "Backup code is incorrect."

Apply `.trim().toLowerCase()` (and drop all non-hex characters) before comparing.

title: missing_backup_codes message points to a settings feature that doesn't exist
body:
The message reads "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." This PR adds no UI or endpoint to generate or regenerate backup codes. `setup.ts` refuses to run when 2FA is already enabled, so the only path is to disable and re-enable 2FA.

This error is mainly hit on the login page by users who enabled 2FA before this change. They cannot reach settings at all, so the message gives instructions they cannot follow.

Separately, once all codes are consumed the stored array is all nulls and still truthy. Those users get "incorrect backup code" instead of this message.

title: Assertion on un-awaited promise always passes; backup-code login/disable untested
body:
`expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on a Promise object, which is always truthy. The PR adds a FIXME acknowledging this instead of fixing it (e.g. `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()`).

With the new flow, the dialog in this test stays open on the backup-codes screen and `onEnable` is never triggered. The broken assertion hides that.

The core new behavior (logging in with a backup code, single-use consumption, disabling 2FA with a backup code) also has no test; it is left as a TODO at line 12.

title: Backup codes stored reversibly encrypted instead of hashed
body:
Backup codes only ever need to be verified, never displayed again. Yet they are stored with `symmetricEncrypt` under the shared `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, so anyone with DB access plus that key can recover every user's plaintext codes.

Storing a salted hash per code (and deleting the matching hash on use) is the standard approach. It would also remove the decrypt/re-encrypt round-trip on every login.

title: tabIndex=-1 removes keyboard access to password visibility toggle
body:
This shared `PasswordField` is used across the app. Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the show/hide password button means keyboard-only and screen-reader users can no longer reach the toggle.

This is an accessibility regression unrelated to the backup-code feature.

title: Copy button throws or falsely reports success when clipboard API unavailable
body:
`navigator.clipboard` is undefined in non-secure contexts, e.g. a self-hosted instance served over plain http. There, `navigator.clipboard.writeText` throws a TypeError synchronously.

When the API does exist, the returned promise is not awaited, so the "Backup codes copied!" toast is shown even if the write is rejected.

Await the promise, catch errors, and only show the success toast when the write actually succeeded.

title: TypeError when Google Meet is the location and there is no destination calendar
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined` when `destinationCalendar` is null or `[]`. Many callers in this PR now pass `[]`, and handleNewBooking passes `null`. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. Any booking whose location is Google Meet and whose user has no destination calendar now throws inside `EventManager.create`. Previously this case fell back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

title: Video booking references no longer store credentialId
body: Before: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`. After: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Video results from `createMeeting` carry a `credentialId`, which is now dropped. handleCancelBooking only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set. As a result, Zoom/Teams/etc. meetings for new bookings are orphaned on cancellation. Keep `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results too.

title: Destinations without credentialId: externalCalendarId lost and team members' calendars resolved against the organizer's credentials
body:
For a destination with no `credentialId` (legacy rows), the code calls `createEvent(c, event)` without `destination.externalId`. The resulting reference therefore stores no `externalCalendarId`; previously it stored `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Later updates and deletes then can't target the right calendar.

The credentials are also taken from `this.calendarCredentials`, which holds only the organizer's credentials. If a collective team member's destination calendar lacks a credentialId, an extra event is created in every organizer calendar of that integration type. The organizer gets duplicates and the team member gets nothing.

title: updateLocation references lose externalCalendarId and credentialId
body: The references now use `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. For calendar results these come from `CalendarManager.updateEvent`, which returns neither field. editLocation persists these as new booking references with null `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId`. Previously both fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar`. Later cancellation or reschedule then falls into the legacy path or targets the wrong calendar.

title: Missing credential for one host's reference makes the whole reschedule throw
body: When a reference's credential is in neither `this.calendarCredentials` nor the DB (for example, a team member removed their calendar app), `credential` is `undefined`. It is still passed to `updateEvent`, which dereferences `credential.appName` and rejects. `return Promise.all(result)` is not awaited inside the `try`, so the `catch` never sees the rejection and the whole reschedule fails. Now that every host's reference is processed, this is much easier to hit. Skip references without a resolved credential.

title: Rescheduling with newBookingId deletes only the first old calendar event
body: The update loop now handles one calendar reference per host. The old-event cleanup still uses `booking.references.find(...)`, so it deletes only the first old calendar reference. For collective bookings, every other host keeps a stale event at the old time in their calendar.

title: Error message built but no longer logged in updateAllCalendarEvents
body: `console.error(message)` was removed. `message` is still computed and then unused. Failures updating calendar events are now swallowed silently and only appear as generic `success: false` results, which makes production issues hard to diagnose.

title: Google createEvent ignores destination calendars without credentialId
body: The calendar is now chosen only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`, with fallback to "primary". Legacy destination calendars with a null `credentialId` used to have their `externalId` respected. They now silently get events written to the primary calendar instead of the user's configured destination calendar.

title: Hangout-link patch uses a possibly undefined calendarId
body: `selectedCalendar` used to be guaranteed to be a string (`"primary"` fallback). It is now `undefined` whenever no destination matches the credential, and only the insert call applies `|| "primary"`. The follow-up `calendar.events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar, ... })` then gets `undefined` and fails, so the Meet link is never written into the description. The patch promise is not awaited or caught, so the failure is an unhandled rejection.

title: Google updateEvent fallback can never match, so calendarId becomes undefined
body: The fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`. It runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it can never match and always yields `undefined`. Before, it fell back to the destination calendar's externalId. Updating bookings whose reference has no `externalCalendarId` (older bookings, or the paths above that now drop it) sends `calendarId: undefined` to Google and fails.

title: Google deleteEvent fallback is dead code; events in non-primary calendars aren't deleted
body: The same impossible `find(cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is used when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it always falls through to "primary". If the event lives in a non-primary destination calendar, Google returns 404. The code resolves 404 silently, so the cancelled booking's event stays on the user's calendar.

title: Non-Google services always use the main host's calendar id, so multi-host only works for Google
body: EventManager calls `createEvent` once per host's credential, but Office365 (and Lark in the same way) always uses `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, the main host's calendar. For a second host with Outlook, the request goes to `/me/calendars/<main host calendar id>/events` with the second host's token and fails. The PR's stated goal that every host with any calendar app gets the event is not met for these providers. Pick the destination matching the credential, as the Google service does.

title: CalDAV createEvent silently creates nothing for secondary hosts
body: The calendars are filtered by the main host's destination `externalId`. A secondary host's CalDAV account never contains that URL, so the filter yields zero calendars. `Promise.all([])` succeeds, and `createEvent` returns success with a uid. A booking reference is stored for an event that was never created, and the host gets nothing in their calendar.

title: Collective hosts' calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then does nothing, so every other host's destination calendar is discarded. Initialize to `[]`, or assign `teamDestinationCalendars` when the value is null.

title: Unrelated loadUsers rewrite drops organization select and changes error semantics
body: The dynamic-user query no longer selects `organization: { slug }`, so dynamic group bookings lose the organizer's org data that was previously loaded. The rewrite also turns an empty or invalid `dynamicUserList` into a generic 500 "Unable to load users" and re-wraps any HttpError as 400, discarding its original status code. These behavior changes are outside the PR's scope and untested.

title: Recurring cancellation repeats per reference and misses other hosts' events
body: The recurring-series deletion block now sits inside the `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With N calendar references it runs N times. Each run iterates all organizer credentials and deletes the first calendar reference of each updated booking, sending redundant API calls. It still uses only the organizer's credentials and only the first reference per booking. For collective recurring bookings, the other hosts' events are never deleted.

title: Confirmation and payment flows build evt with only one destination calendar
body: Only handleNewBooking adds the collective hosts' destination calendars. Paths that create calendar events later rebuild `evt` with only the booking's or organizer's destination calendar: confirm.handler → handleConfirmation, and the Stripe/PayPal webhooks → `EventManager.create`. Collective events that require confirmation or payment still create the event only on the main host's calendar, so issue #7754 remains for those flows.

title: Webhook payload `destinationCalendar` changes from object to array (breaking)
body: `CalendarEvent` is spread directly into webhook payloads (BOOKING_CREATED, CANCELLED, REJECTED, etc.). `destinationCalendar` changes from an object or null to an array. It is also inconsistent across triggers: `null` from handleNewBooking but `[]` from other paths, as the e2e test now expects. This breaks third-party webhook consumers, contradicting the PR's 'non-breaking' claim, and needs a migration note or payload compatibility shim.

title: Organization slug logic inverted
body: The original code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, which sets the slug directly only when billing is disabled. The new code is `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which inverts it. Without team billing (for example, self-hosted), organizations are now created with no slug at all. With billing enabled, the slug is claimed immediately alongside `requestedSlug`, bypassing the payment flow. This unrelated change should be reverted.

title: Multi-destination create/update/delete paths have no tests
body: The PR changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and rewrites `createAllCalendarEvents`, `updateAllCalendarEvents` and the cancel-booking deletion loop to iterate multiple references and credentials. The PR states no tests were added. The regressions above (Meet crash on empty array, dead fallback lookups, dropped credentialId on references) would be caught by basic unit tests of these paths.

title: Crash when Google Meet is selected and there is no destination calendar
body:
`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the event has no destination calendar (`handleNewBooking` sets it to `null`; other callers pass `[]`). The next line then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining.

Whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType` and the organizer or event type has no destination calendar, this throws a TypeError. Before this change, that case fell back to Cal Video. Now `eventManager.create` fails and the booking flow errors out after the booking row already exists.

Fix: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

title: Video booking references no longer store credentialId
body:
The old code was `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`, so video results kept their own credentialId. The new code is `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, which drops it for every video (Zoom, Teams, Daily, etc.) reference.

`handleCancelBooking` only deletes the video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set. As a result, cancelling any new booking leaves orphaned meetings at the video provider. Other code that relies on the video reference's credential is affected the same way.

Fix: keep `result.credentialId` for all result types.

title: Organization slug condition was inverted
body:
The original code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`: the slug is set directly only when team billing is disabled, and with billing on it is stored as `requestedSlug` until payment. The new code is `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which flips this.

- Self-hosted / no-billing instances now create organizations with no slug, which breaks org subdomain routing.
- Billing-enabled instances get the slug immediately and bypass the payment-gated slug assignment.

This change is unrelated to the PR's purpose and looks like an accidental logic flip.

title: Google update/delete fallback to the destination calendar can never match
body:
In both `updateEvent` (line 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (line 315-317), the fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then searches `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, comparing against that same falsy value, so it never matches and always yields `undefined`.

Before this change, the fallback was the event's destination calendar externalId. Consequences for references with a null `externalCalendarId` (legacy bookings, and references created by the new no-credentialId and updateLocation paths):
- `events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined` and fails, so reschedules and location changes are not reflected.
- `deleteEvent` silently targets `primary`, which returns 404 (resolved as success) when the event lives in a secondary calendar, leaving it undeleted.

title: Google createEvent ignores destination calendars that lack a credentialId
body:
`selectedCalendar` is now found only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable, and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` has a dedicated path for destinations without a credentialId. For those, no match is found and the event is inserted into `primary` instead of the user's chosen calendar. Previously `destinationCalendar.externalId` was used regardless.

In the same case, the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` (line 168) receives `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which is `undefined`. That patch is an un-awaited promise, so it rejects as an unhandled rejection and the Meet link is never written into the description.

Fix: fall back to the matching-integration destination's externalId, and use the same resolved id (including the `primary` fallback) for the patch.

title: Office365 always writes to the main host's calendar id, breaking other collective hosts
body:
`createEvent` takes `event.destinationCalendar[0]`, the main host's calendar, and posts to `/me/calendars/${externalId}/events` using the current credential. With this PR, `EventManager` calls `createEvent` once per host's destination calendar, using each host's own credential.

For any non-main host on Office365, that means requesting the main host's calendar id (which may even be a Google address) with the member's token. The request fails and the member gets no event, which is the exact scenario this PR claims to fix.

The `credentialId` parameter added to the `Calendar` interface is ignored here. The service should select the destination matching its credential.

Lark (`larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` lines 128-129, 164-165) has the same problem.

title: CalDAV hosts other than the main host get no event, yet creation reports success
body:
`createEvent` filters the user's calendars with `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`, where that externalId belongs to the first (main host's) destination calendar. When called with another collective host's CalDAV credential, none of that user's calendar URLs match.

`Promise.all([])` resolves, `responses.some(r => !r.ok)` is false, and the method returns a successful result with a uid. The booking reference is stored, but no event exists on the member's calendar, so the failure is silent.

Fix: select the destination calendar that matches this credential (via the credentialId parameter) instead of index 0.

title: Team members' destination calendars dropped when organizer has none
body:
`evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (line 1067). The collective merge then does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a no-op on `null`.

In that case every other collective host's destination calendar is silently discarded, and no events are created in their calendars.

Fix: initialise to `[]`, or assign `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

title: updateLocation references lose externalCalendarId and credentialId
body:
`referencesToCreate` in `updateLocation` now uses `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. Calendar results come from `CalendarManager.updateEvent`, whose return object contains neither field. Before this change, they came from `evt.destinationCalendar`.

New calendar references created by `editLocation.handler` are therefore persisted with null `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId`. On a later cancel this has two effects:
- `handleCancelBooking` takes the legacy path, iterating every organizer calendar credential.
- Google `deleteEvent`, given a null externalCalendarId, targets `primary` (see the dead-fallback issue), so events on secondary calendars are not removed.

title: No-credentialId destination path no longer stores externalCalendarId on references
body:
For destination calendars without a credentialId, `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the `externalId` argument. The resulting reference (line 169, `result.externalId`) is stored with `externalCalendarId` undefined, whereas previously it was `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId`.

Later updates and deletes for these bookings then hit the Google null-externalCalendarId paths, which now fail (update) or target `primary` (delete).

Fix: pass `destination.externalId` here as well.

title: Webhook payload shape of destinationCalendar changes from object to array/null inconsistently
body:
`CalendarEvent` is spread directly into webhook payloads (`sendPayload(..., {...evt, ...})`). Changing `destinationCalendar` from a single object to `DestinationCalendar[]` silently breaks existing webhook subscribers, Zapier templates and payload templates that read `destinationCalendar.externalId` or `.integration`.

The value is also inconsistent across paths, as the updated e2e expectations show:
- `handleNewBooking` sends `null` when empty.
- confirm, cancel and payment handlers send `[]`.

This external contract change is not documented, and a single representation should be used.

title: Recurring cancellation repeats deletes per reference and never deletes other hosts' events
body:
The recurring branch (organizer credentials × all updated bookings) now sits inside a `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. For a collective booking with N calendar references, the same set of delete calls is issued N times.

The inner logic still uses only `updBooking.references.find(ref => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`, the first reference, and only the organizer's credentials. Team members' events for the remaining occurrences are never deleted, leaving orphaned events in their calendars.

title: updateAllCalendarEvents error is now silently swallowed
body:
The catch block still builds a descriptive `message`, but the `console.error(message)` call was removed. Any failure, such as a missing credential causing `updateEvent(undefined, ...)` to throw, now returns `success: false` results with no log at all. That makes reschedule and location-update failures very hard to diagnose.

Fix: restore the logging, using the module logger.

title: loadUsers refactor drops organization select and turns client errors into 500s
body:
Two unrelated changes were bundled into this refactor:

1. The dynamic-user query no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`. Any downstream use of `user.organization` for dynamic group bookings, such as building org booker URLs, now sees undefined.
2. An empty or invalid `dynamicUserList` now throws a plain `Error` (line 728). The catch block maps any non-HttpError to `HttpError 500 "Unable to load users"`, so malformed client input becomes a server error.

Separately, the `!Array.isArray(hosts)` check after `|| []` is dead code.

title: Crash when Google Meet is the location and there is no destination calendar
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when `destinationCalendar` is null or `[]`, which is the normal case for users with no destination calendar set. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining (the old code used `?.integration`). When `evt.location === MeetLocationType` and no destination calendar exists, this throws a TypeError and `EventManager.create` fails. Previously this case fell back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

title: Video references are no longer stored with a credentialId
body: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` sets the credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result. The old code stored `result.credentialId` for video results. `handleCancelBooking` only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is truthy. As a result, Zoom, Daily, Teams and other meetings created after this change are never deleted when the booking is cancelled. Keep `result.credentialId` for video results.

title: Hangout-link patch is sent with an undefined calendarId
body: `selectedCalendar` is now `undefined` whenever no destination calendar matches the credentialId. The insert call guards this with `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. Before this change `selectedCalendar` always fell back to "primary". In this case the patch fails (its promise is not awaited or handled), so the event description is never updated with the Meet link. Apply the same `|| "primary"` fallback here.

title: Fallback lookup in update/delete can never match, so destination calendar is ignored
body:
In `updateEvent`, the fallback runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, and it then does `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`. That compares each calendar against a falsy value, so it effectively always returns undefined. The old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. For references without `externalCalendarId` (older bookings, or references created by the paths changed in this PR), consequences are:
- `events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined` and fails.
- `deleteEvent` (line 317, same pattern) targets "primary" instead of the destination calendar. It gets a 404, which is silently resolved, and the event is never deleted.

title: Destination calendars without credentialId lose their externalId
body: In the branch for destinations without a `credentialId`, `createEvent(c, event)` is called without `destination.externalId`. The stored reference therefore gets `externalCalendarId: undefined`; previously `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId` was stored. In addition, Google's `createEvent` now picks its calendar by `credentialId`, finds no match, and creates the event in "primary" instead of the configured destination calendar. Pass `destination.externalId`, and make the Google service honour it.

title: updateLocation references lose externalCalendarId and credentialId
body: `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined` are taken from `updateEvent` results. `CalendarManager.updateEvent` never sets `externalId` or `credentialId`, so both are always undefined; previously they came from `evt.destinationCalendar`. `editLocationHandler` persists these as new booking references. Later cancel and update calls then fall into the legacy no-credential paths and the broken Google fallback, so events can end up on the wrong calendar or fail to update or delete.

title: Other hosts' calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so for a collective event the other hosts' destination calendars are silently discarded. Those hosts never get a calendar event, which is exactly the scenario this PR aims to fix. Initialise to `[]` (or create the array before pushing) for collective events.

title: CalDAV createEvent filters by the main host's calendar, silently creating nothing for other hosts
body: `createEvent` filters the credential's calendars to `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`. For a collective event, `EventManager` now calls `createEvent` with each additional host's credential, but the filter still uses the first (main host's) calendar. The second host's CalDAV calendars never match, so `Promise.all([])` creates no object. The method still returns a success result with a uid, so the failure is invisible and the host gets no event. Select the destination by the credential being used, as the Google service does.

title: Office365 createEvent uses the main host's calendar id with another host's credential
body: For collective events, `createEvent` is now invoked once per host destination with that host's credential. This service still builds the URL from `event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, which is the main host's calendar id (possibly not even an Outlook calendar). The request to `/me/calendars/{otherId}/events` fails, so additional Office365 hosts never get the event. The service should pick the destination calendar matching the credential.

title: Lark createEvent ignores which host's credential is used
body: `createEvent` and `createAttendees` always use the first destination calendar's externalId. When `EventManager` creates the event for a second collective host with their Lark credential, the main host's calendar id is used with the wrong account, so creation fails. The same applies to `createAttendees` at line 164. Select the destination matching the current credential.

title: Recurring cancellation runs once per reference and still deletes only one host's events
body: The recurring-series deletion block is now inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. For a collective booking with N calendar references, it iterates all organizer calendar credentials over all `updatedBookings` N times, causing duplicate delete calls. Each pass still uses `updBooking.references.find(...)` (the first calendar reference only) and only the organizer's credentials. The other hosts' recurring events are therefore never deleted from their calendars. Move the recurring logic out of the loop and iterate every calendar reference, using each reference's own credential.

title: Only the first old calendar event is deleted when merging bookings
body: When `newBookingId` is given, the code does `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes a single calendar event. With multiple per-host calendar references now possible, the other hosts' old events are left behind as orphaned duplicates in their calendars.

title: Each collective host gets a separate Google Meet conference
body: Each host's Google calendar now receives its own `events.insert` with `conferenceData.createRequest` and `conferenceDataVersion: 1`. Google creates a new Meet conference for every inserted event, so hosts on different Google accounts see different Meet links in their calendars. Attendees receive only one link through cal.com emails, so participants can join different meetings. Only the main host's event should create the conference, and the others should reuse its link.

title: Organization slug condition inverted by unrelated change
body: The original code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, which sets the real slug only when billing is disabled; with billing on, only `requestedSlug` is stored until payment. The new `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` inverts this. With billing enabled, the slug is claimed immediately, bypassing the payment flow. With billing disabled, organizations are created with no slug at all, breaking subdomain routing. It should be `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? {} : { slug }`.

title: Webhook payload shape of destinationCalendar changes from object to array
body: `CalendarEvent` objects are spread directly into webhook payloads (cancel, reject, reschedule-request, etc.). Changing `destinationCalendar` from an object to an array is a breaking change for external webhook consumers such as Zapier and custom integrations, which read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId`. The value is also now inconsistent: `null` for BOOKING_CREATED/REQUESTED and `[]` for BOOKING_REJECTED, as the e2e test shows. Consider keeping the external payload shape stable, or document and version the change.

title: No tests for multi-host destination calendar behavior
body: The PR reworks event creation, update and cancellation for multiple calendar references, adds DB credential lookups, and changes the `Calendar.createEvent` signature. The only test change is updating one webhook expectation to `[]`. Nothing covers the collective multi-host path or the regressions above, such as the Meet-without-destination crash or missing video credentialId. Unit tests for `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` and the cancel flow with multiple references are needed.

title: Google credential key is overwritten with a `{success, data}` wrapper on every token refresh
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod `safeParse` result object, not the parsed data. Before this change, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the token itself. Now `key` is `{ success: true, data: {...} }`, and that object is written to `credential.key`. This happens in the default (non-sync) path too, so it affects every Google Calendar user. After the first refresh, the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in the constructor throws, and the Google Calendar integration stops working for that user. Store `key.data`, or have the helper return the data.

title: Minimum token schema strips every field except access_token
body: `[z.string().toString()]` is not a pattern key. `ZodString.toString()` returns "[object Object]", so both computed keys are the same literal property "[object Object]" and the second overwrites the first. The effective schema is `{access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown}` in zod's default strip mode. In sync mode every other property is therefore dropped: expiry_date, expires_in, scope, token_type, instance_url, etc. The consequences differ per app. Zoom computes `expiry_date` from an undefined `expires_in` (NaN, stored as null), so the next `zoomTokenSchema.parse` fails. Salesforce loses `instance_url`. Google loses `expiry_date`, `scope` and `token_type`. Use `.passthrough()` or `z.record`/`.catchall` with an explicit expiry field.

title: Placeholder "refresh_token" overwrites the real refresh token in the default path
body: The fallback `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` also runs when sync is disabled. Office365's `refreshTokenResponseSchema` makes `refresh_token` optional, and the caller spreads `tokenResponse.data` over the stored credentials. Previously, if Microsoft omitted a refresh_token, the existing one was kept. Now it is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token", and every later refresh fails permanently. Only inject the placeholder in sync mode, or don't inject it at all.

title: Sync path returns a raw fetch Response that callers expecting provider-specific objects can't use
body:
In sync mode the helper returns a WHATWG `Response`. In native mode it returns whatever `refreshFunction` returns, so callers get a different type depending on the mode. Several callers break in sync mode:
- Google Calendar reads `res?.data`, which is undefined on a Response, so `token.access_token` throws. The error is swallowed and the expired token keeps being used.
- Zoho Bigin and ZohoCRM read `tokenInfo.data.error`, the axios shape, and throw a TypeError.
- HubSpot treats the result as a token object (`expiresIn`, `accessToken`), computes a NaN expiry and stores the Response object as the credential key.

The helper should normalize the result, e.g. parse JSON and return a common token shape, or the callers must branch on mode.

title: Credential id passed as the Cal.com user id to the sync endpoint
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credential.id` where the helper expects `userId`. The sync endpoint receives `calcomUserId=<credential id>`. It will return tokens for whichever user happens to have that id, or for nobody. In the first case one user's Zoho tokens get written into another user's credential. Team credentials (userId null) are also sent to the sync endpoint, against the helper's stated intent. Pass `credential.userId` here.

title: appStoreMetadata is indexed by slug, but it is keyed by app directory name
body: `appStoreMetadata` is generated keyed by app directory name (e.g. `googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`, `office365calendar`), not by slug. Looking it up with `app.slug` (`google-calendar`, `zoom`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`) returns undefined, so the webhook answers 404 for most of the OAuth apps this PR targets. It only works by accident where slug equals dirName. Select `dirName` from the App row and index by that.

title: `prisma` used without being imported
body: The new `prisma.credential.update(...)` call references `prisma`, but this file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. At best it resolves to the dev-only `globalThis.prisma`. In production that global is not set, so this throws a ReferenceError/TypeError. Since `getClient` runs in the constructor, every Salesforce booking/CRM operation fails.

title: Salesforce refreshes the token on every instantiation, then ignores the new token
body: `getClient` now unconditionally POSTs to the Salesforce token endpoint every time the service is constructed, with no expiry check. That adds latency and rate-limit pressure on every booking. Afterwards the `jsforce.Connection` is still built with the old `credentialKey.access_token` and `instance_url` instead of the freshly refreshed values, so the extra request achieves nothing for the current call. The URL is also hardcoded to `login.salesforce.com`, which breaks sandbox orgs. This refresh also bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens` while still using the sync-mode schema, which corrupts the stored key (see the schema stripping issue).

title: Success is detected via `statusText === "OK"`
body: `statusText` is empty for HTTP/2 responses and is not guaranteed to be "OK" for a 200, so a successful refresh can be reported as a 400 error. Use `response.ok`. Also, the `!accessTokenParsed.success` branch below is dead, because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure instead of returning success=false.

title: Zoom sends app slug "zoomvideo" instead of "zoom"
body: Zoom's app slug and appId is "zoom" (see `createOAuthAppCredential({ appId: "zoom" ...})` in the callback). The webhook also identifies apps by slug. The refresh call sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, the directory name, so the self-hoster's sync endpoint gets an identifier that doesn't match what it uses for the webhook. Zoom refreshes will fail or return the wrong app's tokens.

title: Webex, Lark and MS Teams still require the provider-native response shape in sync mode
body: Webex validates the response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` directly, which requires a scope literal, token_type, refresh_token and refresh_token_expires_in. Lark runs it through `handleLarkError`, which expects `{code:0,data:{...}}`. MS Teams overwrites the entire stored key with the response. All three are routed to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, whose documented contract is "only the access token and expiry date". With a conforming endpoint, Webex rejects every refresh, Lark throws, and Teams loses its refresh_token. The endpoint contract is not consistent across the integrations this PR switches over.

title: Outbound sync request carries no authentication
body: Cal.com POSTs only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` to the sync endpoint, with no shared secret, signature or encryption. The inbound webhook, by contrast, requires a secret and AES-encrypted keys. The self-hoster's endpoint therefore has no way to verify that the caller is Cal.com. Anyone who can reach it can enumerate user ids and obtain live third-party access tokens. Send the webhook secret or an HMAC header, and ideally encrypt the response with the shared key. Also check `response.ok` before returning.

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==`
body: The secret is compared with `!==`, which leaks timing information. If the header is sent more than once it becomes a `string[]` and never matches. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on the buffers after checking the lengths. The endpoint also accepts any HTTP method.

title: Malformed body or bad ciphertext returns an unhandled 500
body: `schema.parse`, `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` all throw on bad input, and nothing catches them. The caller gets a generic 500 instead of a 400 explaining what was wrong. The decrypted keys are also stored without any validation against the app's credential schema.

title: Updating a credential via the webhook doesn't clear `invalid`
body: Google, Zoom and Webex set `invalid: true` on invalid_grant. When the parent app later pushes fresh keys through this webhook, only `key` is updated. The credential stays flagged invalid and is still treated as broken. Reset `invalid: false` on update.

title: Removed diagnostic logging of the Microsoft refresh error
body: The old code logged the zod error and the raw Microsoft response when parsing failed. Now `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" and the MS error body is lost. That makes Outlook token problems much harder to debug. The behavior also changed from "keep the old token and continue" to "throw".

title: No tests for the new refresh/sync helpers or the webhook
body: The PR changes token refresh for about ten integrations and adds a credential-writing webhook, and it states that no tests were added or run. Unit tests for `parseRefreshTokenResponse` would have caught several of the issues above: the returned wrapper object, the fields stripped by the broken schema, and the placeholder refresh_token. The same goes for `refreshOAuthTokens` (sync vs native return types) and the webhook (slug→metadata lookup).

title: Google credential key is overwritten with the zod SafeParse wrapper object
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a zod SafeParseReturnType (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed token. The old code `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the token itself. This result is now written straight to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so after the first token refresh the DB holds `{ success: true, data: {...} }`. On the next instantiation, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in `googleAuth` throws. Every Google Calendar credential breaks after its first refresh, in both normal and sync mode. Use `key.data` (or `.parse`).

title: Sync mode returns a fetch Response, which callers expecting SDK/axios shapes cannot use
body:
In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response`. In normal mode it returns whatever the provider-specific function returns, and several callers depend on that shape:
- Google reads `res?.data`. A fetch Response has no `.data`, so `token.access_token` throws.
- HubSpot treats the result as a `TokenResponseIF`. It computes `expiryDate` from `undefined * 1000` (NaN) and persists the Response object as the credential key.
- Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM read `tokenInfo.data.error` (axios shape) and throw a TypeError.
- Lark goes through `handleLarkError`, which expects `{code:0,data:{...}}`.
- Webex validates with a strict schema that requires `scope`, `refresh_token_expires_in`, etc.

None of these work with the documented sync response ("only the access token and expiry date"). Credential sync is effectively broken for most of the apps this PR wires up.

title: Computed schema keys evaluate to "[object Object]", so expiry fields are stripped in sync mode
body:
`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key "[object Object]". The second overwrites the first, so the schema is effectively `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`. `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, so `expires_in`, `expiry_date` and every other field from the sync endpoint is dropped.

Consequences in sync mode:
- Zoom computes `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined*1000)` = NaN. The stored key then fails `zoomTokenSchema` on next use.
- Office365 never updates expiry, so it refreshes on every call.
- Salesforce loses `instance_url`.

Use `.passthrough()`, or an explicit schema with the expected expiry field.

title: Placeholder "refresh_token" string overwrites real stored refresh tokens
body:
When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the helper injects the literal string "refresh_token". Office365 then does `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }` and persists the result, replacing the user's real refresh token with the string "refresh_token". This happens whenever Microsoft omits a refresh token (the schema marks it optional) and always in sync mode.

Zoom in sync mode likewise sets `key.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Before this change, a missing refresh token left the existing one intact. Now the credential becomes unrefreshable once the sync endpoint is turned off. Don't inject a fake value; let callers keep the existing refresh token.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported
body: The new code calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file imports nothing from `@calcom/prisma`. This is a type error at build time and a ReferenceError at runtime. `getClient` therefore always rejects, which breaks every Salesforce operation (create, update, delete event and contact search).

title: Salesforce refreshes on every instantiation but builds the connection with the stale token
body:
`getClient` now requests a new access token from login.salesforce.com every time the service is constructed, with no expiry check. That costs an extra network round trip and adds rate-limit pressure on every booking.

The freshly obtained `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` is saved to the DB, but `jsforce.Connection` is still built from `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` (the old values). The refresh therefore has no effect on the current request.

This path also bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so it never uses the sync endpoint. Yet `parseRefreshTokenResponse` applies the minimal schema in sync mode, which drops `instance_url` from the persisted key.

title: Success check relies on `statusText === "OK"` instead of `response.ok`
body: HTTP/2 and some proxies return an empty or different reason phrase. A successful 200 response can then be treated as an error, and the HttpError message is empty. Use `response.ok` or check the status code.

title: Credential ID is passed as the user ID to the credential sync endpoint
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's primary key where the other callers pass `credential.userId`. The sync endpoint receives `calcomUserId=<credentialId>`, so it returns tokens for whichever user happens to have that ID. Those tokens are then written into this credential, giving the wrong Cal.com user access to another user's Zoho Bigin account. `credential.userId` needs to be threaded into `refreshAccessToken`.

title: Wrong app slug "zoomvideo" sent to the sync endpoint
body: The Zoom app slug, used as `appId` when the credential is created, is "zoom"; "zoomvideo" is only the directory name. The self-hosted sync endpoint receives `appSlug=zoomvideo`, which won't match the slug used everywhere else, including the inbound webhook that looks apps up by slug. Token refresh for Zoom fails in sync mode.

title: `appStoreMetadata` is indexed by slug, but its keys are directory names
body: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by app directory name (e.g. `googlecalendar`, `office365calendar`, `zoomvideo`, `office365video`). The handler indexes it with `app.slug` (e.g. `google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `zoom`, `msteams`). For every app whose slug differs from its dirName, the lookup returns undefined and the webhook responds 404 "App not found". Most of the apps this feature targets therefore can't be synced. Select `dirName` from the `App` row and index by that.

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==`
body: The shared secret that authorizes writing arbitrary OAuth credentials for any user is compared with plain string inequality, which leaks timing information. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. Also reject requests where the header is missing or is an array.

title: Invalid body or undecryptable keys cause unhandled 500s; no method check
body: `schema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError, and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on a bad ciphertext or key. Neither is caught, so the caller gets a generic 500 instead of a 400. The handler also accepts any HTTP method, not just POST. Use `safeParse`, wrap decryption in try/catch, and return 400/405 as appropriate.

title: Updating synced keys does not clear the credential's `invalid` flag
body: Credentials get marked `invalid: true` on `invalid_grant` (Google, Zoom, Webex). When the parent platform pushes fresh keys through this webhook, only `key` is updated. The credential stays flagged invalid and is still treated as broken. Set `invalid: false` alongside the new key.

title: Outbound token-sync request carries no authentication
body:
Cal.com POSTs `{calcomUserId, appSlug}` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with no secret header and no signature. The endpoint is expected to answer with plaintext access tokens. The self-hosted endpoint has no way to verify the caller is Cal.com, so anyone who can reach it can enumerate user IDs and harvest third-party access tokens.

The inbound direction requires a webhook secret and encrypted payloads, so this is asymmetric. At minimum, send `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in the configured header.

title: Feature flag constant holds the encryption key itself rather than a boolean
body: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` evaluates to the value of `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` when both env vars are set. It is exported from a widely imported constants module. Any place that logs, serializes or returns this "flag" would leak the AES key. Coerce it with `!!(...)`.

title: No tests for the new webhook or the refresh/parse helpers
body: The PR adds an authenticated credential-write webhook and changes token-refresh persistence for about ten integrations, with no unit or integration tests. The description states tests were not added or run. Basic tests would have caught several of the bugs above: the SafeParse wrapper persisted as the Google key, the "[object Object]" schema keys, the missing prisma import, and the slug/dirName mismatch.

title: Google credential key is overwritten with the safeParse wrapper object
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed data. Before this change the code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which returned the data itself. Now `key` is the wrapper, and `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` persists `{ success, data }` as the credential key. On the next instantiation, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in `googleAuth` throws. Every Google Calendar credential therefore breaks on its first token refresh, including on instances that never enable credential sync. Store `key.data`, or make the helper return the data.

title: Computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` produce a single bogus "[object Object]" field
body: `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the string "[object Object]". Both computed keys collapse into one property named "[object Object]", and the second definition (`z.unknown().optional()`) overwrites the first. The effective schema is `{ access_token: string }`, and zod's default strip mode then drops every other field, including expiry_date, expires_in, instance_url and scope. In sync mode the output is always just `{access_token, refresh_token: "refresh_token"}`. Consequences: Zoom computes `expiry_date = Date.now() + undefined*1000 = NaN`, which is stored as null and fails `zoomTokenSchema` next time. Office365 never updates expiry and refreshes on every call. Salesforce loses `instance_url`. Use `.passthrough()` or `.catchall()` and validate the expiry field explicitly.

title: Placeholder "refresh_token" overwrites real refresh tokens when the provider omits one
body: When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the helper injects the literal string "refresh_token". This also runs outside sync mode. Office365's `refreshTokenResponseSchema` marks `refresh_token` optional, and the caller spreads the result over the stored credentials (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`). If Microsoft does not return a new refresh token, the user's real refresh token is replaced with "refresh_token" and every later refresh fails. Previously the missing key was simply absent and the old token survived. In sync mode the same placeholder is written into Zoom's stored `refresh_token`.

title: Choice of schema doesn't match where the tokens actually came from
body:
`refreshOAuthTokens` only calls the sync endpoint when `userId` is non-null. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` switches to the minimal schema whenever sync is enabled, regardless of where the tokens came from. Two cases get a genuine provider response parsed (and stripped) with the minimal schema:
- Team credentials (userId null), whose refresh went to the real provider.
- Salesforce, which calls the provider directly and never goes through `refreshOAuthTokens`.

Those stored credentials lose required fields. The two helpers need a shared decision, for example by passing a flag or returning the source along with the response.

title: Sync path returns a raw fetch Response, which callers don't expect
body:
Callers' refresh functions return different shapes:
- Google returns a GaxiosResponse and reads `res.data`.
- HubSpot returns a `TokenResponseIF` and reads `.expiresIn` / `.accessToken`.
- Zoho CRM and Bigin return axios responses and read `.data.error`.
- Lark expects the `{code:0, data:{...}}` envelope.

In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` always returns a fetch `Response`, so these paths break:
- Google throws a TypeError on `token.access_token`, which is swallowed, and continues with an expired token.
- HubSpot writes a serialized Response object (with NaN expiry) as the credential key.
- Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM throw on `tokenInfo.data.error`.
- Lark's `handleLarkError` rejects the response.

The sync response must be normalized to each adapter's expected shape, or each adapter must handle it explicitly.

title: Outbound token-sync request carries no authentication
body: The request to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no shared secret, signature or auth header. The self-hoster's endpoint returns live third-party access tokens. To work with Cal.com it has to accept unauthenticated requests keyed by a sequential integer user ID, so anyone who can reach it can enumerate IDs and harvest every user's OAuth tokens. The inbound webhook uses a secret and encryption, but the outbound direction has neither. Send the webhook secret (or an HMAC) and expect the response to be encrypted with `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

title: `prisma` used without being imported
body: The new `prisma.credential.update(...)` call references `prisma`, but this file never imports `@calcom/prisma`. It can only resolve through the dev-only `globalThis.prisma` cache, which is typed `PrismaClient | undefined` and is not set in production. In production `getClient` throws a ReferenceError, so the Salesforce integration fails for every operation.

title: Salesforce refreshes on every instantiation, then ignores the new token
body: `getClient` now unconditionally POSTs a refresh_token grant every time the service is constructed, which happens on every booking create/update/delete. It does not check expiry, adding latency and risking Salesforce rate limits. After refreshing and saving the new token, the `jsforce.Connection` is still built from `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url`, the stale values loaded before the refresh. Pass `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` and `instance_url` instead, and refresh only when needed.

title: Success check relies on `statusText === "OK"`
body: `statusText` is an empty string for HTTP/2 responses and can differ between proxies and runtimes. In those cases a successful 200 response is treated as an error and throws `HttpError` with an empty message. Use `response.ok` instead.

title: Credential ID is passed where the user ID is expected
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credential.id` as the third argument, which is the Cal.com user ID.
