The sync endpoint therefore receives `calcomUserId=<credential id>` and may return tokens for the wrong user. Because a credential ID is never null, the `userId` guard meant to skip team credentials is also bypassed. Pass `credential.userId`; this requires threading it into `refreshAccessToken`.

title: Zoom sync uses slug "zoomvideo" instead of the app slug "zoom"
body: The Zoom app's slug/appId is "zoom", which is what `createOAuthAppCredential` uses and what the webhook matches against `prisma.app.slug`. The refresh call sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, the directory name. A self-hoster implementing the sync endpoint therefore sees a slug that doesn't match the one they must send to `/api/webhook/app-credential`.

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==`
body: The secret header is checked with a plain string inequality. That leaks timing information an attacker can use to guess the secret, and this endpoint can write arbitrary credentials for any user. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. The handler also accepts any HTTP method; restrict it to POST.

title: Invalid body or undecryptable keys surface as 500s
body: `schema.parse(req.body)` and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` both throw on bad input, such as a malformed payload, a wrong encryption key or non-JSON plaintext. There is no try/catch, so the caller gets an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 with a useful message. That makes integration failures hard to diagnose for self-hosters. Use `safeParse` and catch decryption errors.

title: Synced credential update doesn't clear the `invalid` flag
body: Adapters such as Google, Zoom and Webex mark credentials `invalid: true` on `invalid_grant`. When the parent app pushes fresh keys through this webhook, only `key` is updated, so the credential stays flagged invalid even though it now holds valid tokens. Set `invalid: false` on update.

title: No tests for the new sync helpers or the webhook
body: The PR changes token refresh for about ten integrations and adds a credential-writing webhook, but includes no unit tests. The PR description says as much. Simple tests would have caught several of the bugs above: the `[object Object]` schema key, the safeParse wrapper being persisted as Google's key, and the Response shape mismatch in sync mode.

title: Team admin/owner check uses && so team admins are rejected
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. `isTeamAdmin` already matches both the ADMIN and OWNER roles, so AND-ing it with `isTeamOwner` lets only OWNERs through. A team ADMIN who is not the organizer or an attendee gets FORBIDDEN, which contradicts the variable name and the intent. The two checks should be combined with `||`, or `isTeamAdmin` alone should be used.

title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive and can be bypassed with mixed-case emails
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased, but each guest is compared as-is with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Submitting `Spam@Blocked.com` for a blacklisted `spam@blocked.com` passes the filter, so the guest is added to the booking and receives emails. The guest should be lowercased before the comparison, as the regular booking flow does.

title: Server-side deduplication is case-sensitive and ignores duplicates inside the request
body: Existing attendees are excluded with a strict `guest === attendee.email` comparison. The input array itself is never deduplicated, and uniqueness is enforced only in the client dialog. A direct API call with `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]`, or with `A@x.com` when `a@x.com` already attends, inserts duplicate Attendee rows through `createMany`. Those duplicates then appear in calendar invites and get extra emails. Guests should be normalized to lowercase and deduplicated on the server.

title: No upper bound on guests; any attendee can make Cal.com email arbitrary addresses
body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()`. The handler also authorizes any logged-in user whose email matches an attendee (`isAttendee`), and there is no rate limiting. An attendee can therefore add an unbounded list of arbitrary addresses. Each address receives an AttendeeScheduledEmail sent under the organizer's name, and every existing attendee and host is re-emailed. This also bypasses event-type settings such as a disabled or hidden guests booking field. The array size should be capped, and whether attendees (as opposed to the organizer or team admins) may do this should be reconsidered.

title: Guests can be added to seated events, bypassing seat limits and seat records
body: The handler never checks `booking.eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot`. For a seated booking, each Attendee row represents a seat holder with a matching BookingSeat reference. `createMany` here inserts attendees with no BookingSeat, which can push the booking past `seatsPerTimeSlot` and leaves seat data inconsistent for later cancel and reschedule flows. Seated events should be rejected or handled explicitly.

title: No booking status or time validation before adding guests
body: After the booking is fetched, the handler never checks its status or end time. A direct call can add guests to CANCELLED, REJECTED or past bookings. That sends 'scheduled' emails and calendar REQUEST invites for meetings that will not happen. The UI hides the action for cancelled bookings, but the server should enforce this too.

title: Calendar update failure after DB write leaves partial state and blocks retry
body: The attendees are committed to the DB first, and then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` is awaited with no error handling. If the calendar provider call throws, the client gets an error and no emails are sent, but the guests are already persisted. A retry then fails with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', because the guests now count as existing attendees. The external calendar and emails stay out of sync with the DB.

title: Emails are keyed on raw `guests` instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the unfiltered input list. A submitted email that was already an attendee, and so was skipped for insertion, is still treated as 'new'. That attendee gets a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the 'guests added' notification. `uniqueGuests` should be passed instead.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event type disableStandardEmails settings
body: Other booking email senders, such as `sendLocationChangeEmails` and `sendRescheduledEmails`, take `eventTypeMetadata` and skip host or attendee emails when `disableStandardEmails.all.host/attendee` is set. `sendAddGuestsEmails` has no metadata parameter and always emails the organizer, all team members and all attendees. Event types configured to suppress standard emails (for example, those using workflows instead) will still send these.

title: Validation error state is never cleared on success or on outside close
body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on a failed validation and reset only by the Cancel button. A successful submit resets the email list but not `isInvalidEmail`. Closing via overlay or Escape (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`) resets neither. The next time the dialog opens, it shows a stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' error and leftover input.

title: Error toast fallback is unreachable and can show 'undefined: ...'
body: `message` is a template string such as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, so it is always truthy and the `t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is never used. When `err.data` is absent, for example on a network error, users see 'undefined: <message>'. Raw tRPC codes such as 'FORBIDDEN:' are also shown to end users.

title: Team admin/owner check uses && so team admins are rejected
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for both ADMIN and OWNER roles, so ANDing it with `isTeamOwner` reduces the check to "is owner". A team ADMIN who is not the organizer or an attendee gets FORBIDDEN, even though the variable name and intent say admins are allowed. Use `||`, or call `isTeamAdmin` alone.

title: Calendar update runs with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
body: The `EventManager` is built from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The handler explicitly allows team owners and booking attendees, who are not the organizer, to call it. In those cases the booking's calendar and video references, which belong to the organizer's credentials, are updated with the wrong user's credentials. The update then fails, or touches the wrong account. The handler already loads `booking.user` with `credentials`, but never uses them. The EventManager should be built from the booking organizer's user and credentials.

title: Calendar update failure after DB write leaves state inconsistent and blocks retry
body: New attendees are committed with `prisma.booking.update` before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs, and that call is not wrapped in try/catch. If the calendar or video provider call throws, the client gets an error, but the guests are already saved. Because of the throw, no emails are sent and the external calendar is not updated. If the user retries, the existing-attendee filter removes those guests and the handler throws "emails_must_be_unique_valid". The guests stay in the DB and are never notified.

title: Case-sensitive comparisons bypass blacklist and allow duplicate attendees
body: `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` entries are lowercased, but `guest` is compared without lowercasing. `Bad@Example.com` therefore passes the blacklist check. The existing-attendee check `guest === attendee.email` is also case-sensitive, so `Foo@x.com` can be added next to an existing `foo@x.com`. Normalize guest emails (trim and lowercase) before both comparisons.

title: Unbounded, non-unique guest array accepted server-side
body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()` and no uniqueness refinement. Uniqueness is only checked in the client dialog. Any authenticated attendee or organizer can call the endpoint directly with thousands of addresses, or with the same address repeated. That creates many or duplicate Attendee rows via `createMany` and makes the server send an email to each address in the organizer's name, which is a spam vector. Add a reasonable max and dedupe or reject duplicates on the server.

title: Any attendee can add arbitrary guests regardless of event-type guest settings or booking status
body: Any logged-in user whose email matches an attendee is allowed to add guests. The handler does not check whether the event type disables or hides the guests booking field. It also does not check booking status, so cancelled, rejected or past bookings are accepted. This lets attendees bypass host-configured restrictions and trigger organizer-branded emails and calendar invites to arbitrary addresses.

title: Emails classified using raw input instead of filtered new guests
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the unfiltered input list. If the input contains an email that was already an attendee (filtered out of `uniqueGuests`), that existing attendee is treated as a new guest. They get a fresh "booking scheduled" email instead of the "guests added" notice. Pass `uniqueGuests`. The catch block also discards `err`, so failures are hard to diagnose.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails event-type settings
body: Every other booking email sender takes `eventTypeMetadata` and skips host or attendee emails when `disableStandardEmails.all.host` or `.attendee` is set. `sendAddGuestsEmails` has no such parameter or check, and the handler does not pass metadata. Organizations that turned off standard emails, for example to use their own workflows, will still get organizer and attendee emails whenever guests are added.

title: Error toast fallback is unreachable and can show 'undefined: ...'
body: `message` is a template string and is always truthy, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never uses the fallback. When `err.data?.code` is undefined, for example on network or non-TRPC errors, the toast reads "undefined: <message>".

title: Validation error state is not reset on success or on dismiss
body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on a failed validation, but nothing resets it after a successful add, after the user fixes the input, or when the dialog is closed via overlay or Escape (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`). Only the Cancel button resets it. On reopening, the dialog still shows "Emails must be unique and valid" and may also keep stale email values.

title: New mutation has no tests
body: The new handler covers permission checks, filtering, DB writes, calendar updates and email sending, but the PR adds no unit or e2e tests. Several of the bugs above (admin check, case handling, credentials used) would have been caught by basic coverage of these paths.

title: Team admin/owner check uses && so team admins are denied
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. `isTeamAdmin` already matches ADMIN or OWNER memberships, so the conjunction is only true for team OWNERs. Team ADMINs who are neither organizer nor attendee get FORBIDDEN, which contradicts the variable name and the intent. The operator should be `||`, or `isTeamAdmin` alone should be used.

title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive and can be bypassed
body: The `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` entries are lowercased, but the incoming `guest` is compared as-is with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Submitting `Blocked@Example.com` instead of `blocked@example.com` gets past the blacklist, so the address is added as an attendee and emailed. Normalize the guest (e.g. `guest.toLowerCase()`) before comparing.

title: Server-side dedup misses in-request duplicates and differing case
body: `uniqueGuests` only drops guests that exactly (case-sensitively) match an existing attendee. Duplicates inside the request itself are not removed, and the server schema has no uniqueness refinement; the dialog's check is client-only and also case-sensitive. A direct API call with `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]`, or `A@x.com` when `a@x.com` already attends, creates duplicate attendee rows via `createMany` and duplicate emails. Dedupe case-insensitively on the server.

title: Raw `guests` passed to email sender instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the unfiltered input. If the request includes an email that already belongs to an attendee, that existing attendee is treated as new. They then get a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a fresh booking confirmation) instead of the add-guests notification. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

title: EventManager built with the acting user's identity/credentials instead of the organizer's
body: The handler explicitly allows attendees and team admins/owners, not just the organizer, to add guests. But it builds `EventManager` from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The booking's calendar references belong to the organizer's credentials. When a non-organizer performs the action, the calendar update may fail or not reach the organizer's calendar, so the external event never gets the new attendees. `booking.user.credentials` is fetched in the query but never used. Build the EventManager from the booking organizer.

title: Attendees persisted before calendar update with no rollback; failure leaves inconsistent state
body: The new attendees are committed via `prisma.booking.update` before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs. That call is not wrapped in try/catch. If the calendar update throws, the request returns an error and no emails are sent, yet the guests are already saved in the DB. A retry then fails with `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, because the guests now count as existing attendees. The guests are never notified and the calendar is out of sync.

title: No booking status / time check before adding guests
body: The handler never checks booking status or end time. Through the API, guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED or already-finished bookings, and each new guest gets an `AttendeeScheduledEmail` booking confirmation with a CONFIRMED ICS invite for an event that will not happen. The UI also exposes the action on past bookings, because `bookedActions` is rendered for past confirmed bookings. Reject non-active or past bookings.

title: Unbounded guest list enables mass email sending
body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()` and no `.min(1)`. Any attendee of a booking (not just the organizer) may call this mutation. A user can submit an arbitrarily large list, which creates that many attendee rows and sends that many emails from the organizer's name and reply-to. This is a spam/abuse vector and can also be costly for the mail provider. Add a reasonable upper bound and dedupe on the server.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event type's disableStandardEmails settings
body: Every other booking email helper (location change, reschedule, cancel, etc.) accepts `eventTypeMetadata` and skips host or attendee emails when `disableStandardEmails.all.host/attendee` is set. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and always emails the organizer, team members and all attendees. Event types configured to suppress standard emails (e.g. because workflows send custom ones) will still send these.

title: CalendarEvent lacks `team`, so team hosts are never notified
body: `evt` is built without a `team` property. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the `calendarEvent.team?.members` loop is therefore dead code. For collective or round-robin team events, co-hosts get no notification that guests were added, unlike the other organizer email flows that populate `team.members`.

title: Recurring rule included in invite although guest is added to a single occurrence
body: `recurringEvent` is taken from the event type, so for a recurring event type the ICS sent to new guests carries an RRULE for the whole series. The guest is only added as an attendee to the single `bookingId` occurrence. This happens when the action is used from the Upcoming tab, where per-occurrence edit actions are shown. The guest's calendar then shows a full series they are not booked into.

title: Error toast fallback is unreachable and can render "undefined: ..."
body: `message` is a template literal and is always a non-empty string, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never uses the fallback. When `err.data` is absent (e.g. a network error), the toast reads `undefined: <message>`.

title: Validation error state is never cleared on success, edit or dismiss
body: `isInvalidEmail` is only reset by the Cancel button. It stays set after a successful add (`onSuccess` doesn't reset it), while the user edits the fields, and when the dialog is closed via overlay or Esc (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` doesn't reset state). The "Emails must be unique and valid" error therefore persists and reappears the next time the dialog is opened.

title: Hardcoded untranslated tooltip text
body: The tooltip text `"Remove email"` is hardcoded English in a shared UI component that otherwise uses `t(...)`. Non-English users will see English text.

title: retryCount delete branch is not scoped to SMS and cannot use the existing index
body:
The `deleteMany` OR has a second branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter. The SMS cron will therefore delete EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders with `retryCount > 1`. Today only this handler increments the counter, but any other reminder cron that adopts the new column would have its reminders deleted by the SMS cron, which is surprising cross-method data loss.

The branch is also unindexed. `retryCount` has no index, and the OR stops Postgres from relying on `@@index([method, scheduled, scheduledDate])`. This is likely to become a sequential scan of the whole WorkflowReminder table (all methods, all history) on every cron run.

Fix: add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and probably `scheduled: false`) to the second branch.

title: Transient failures permanently delete reminders after two cron runs
body:
The catch block increments `retryCount` for any exception in the try body. That includes transient errors such as Twilio 5xx or 429 rate limits, network timeouts, the `prisma.profile.findFirst` or `getBookerBaseUrl` calls, and template rendering. It also includes the `scheduled: true` update failing after Twilio already accepted the message.

After two failures the row is deleted on the next run. Previously the reminder would be retried until its scheduled date (up to 7 days out). Now a short Twilio or DB outage spanning two cron invocations silently and permanently drops every SMS reminder processed during it.

If the post-schedule update is what failed, the reminder is retried and deleted while a Twilio message is already queued. That causes duplicate sends, and the `referenceId` needed to cancel the queued message is lost.

Only known-permanent errors (e.g. Twilio invalid-number error codes) should count toward deletion, or the retry budget should be larger or time-based.

title: SMS-locked users/teams have their reminders deleted
body:
`twilio.scheduleSMS` returns `undefined`, not an error, when the user or team has `smsLockState === LOCKED`. This new `else` branch treats that as a failed attempt and increments `retryCount`, so after two cron runs every pending SMS reminder for that account is deleted.

Previously these reminders stayed unscheduled and would be sent if an admin unlocked the account, for example after a false-positive abuse lock. Now unlocking does not restore them and attendees silently get no reminders.

The locked case should be distinguished from a real scheduling failure.

title: Failure inside the catch handler aborts the whole cron run
body:
The catch block now awaits `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` before logging. If that update throws, the exception escapes the `for` loop and the handler. This happens for example when the original error was a DB connectivity problem, or when the row was deleted concurrently (e.g. a booking cancellation), which makes Prisma throw `P2025`.

All remaining reminders in the batch are then skipped, the endpoint returns 500, and the original error is never logged. Before this PR the catch only logged, so one bad reminder could not stop the rest.

Wrap the counter update in its own try/catch, or log first and ignore update failures.

title: Reminders with no recipient or empty message are still retried indefinitely
body: The PR's goal is to stop endlessly re-processing reminders that can never be sent. However, when `sendTo` is null (e.g. `smsReminderNumber` missing) or the rendered message is empty, the `if` at this line is skipped. Neither branch increments `retryCount`, so these reminders are still re-fetched and fully re-processed on every cron run until their scheduled date. That includes the profile lookup, booker-URL resolution and template rendering. These permanently unsendable cases are arguably the ones that most need the retry cap.

title: No tests for the new retry/deletion behavior
body: The PR adds behavior that deletes user-facing reminders, but no tests cover it. Cases worth testing: incrementing `retryCount` on a falsy `scheduleSMS` result and on thrown errors, deleting reminders with `retryCount > 1`, leaving reminders of other methods untouched, and not deleting on success. Given the data-loss risk if the conditions are wrong, these should be covered.

title: Retry-count delete branch is not limited to SMS reminders
body: The second `OR` branch of the `deleteMany` is just `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`, with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and no `scheduled: false`. `retryCount` lives on the shared `WorkflowReminder` table, so this SMS cron deletes any EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminder whose `retryCount` exceeds 1. As soon as the email or WhatsApp crons reuse this column for their own retry logic, their reminders will be silently removed by the SMS job. The branch should be scoped to `method: SMS` (and ideally `scheduled: false`).

title: Falsy scheduleSMS result is counted as a failure, so reminders of SMS-locked accounts get deleted
body: The new `else` branch increments `retryCount` whenever `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value. In the Twilio provider, that function returns `undefined` on purpose when the user or team is locked for SMS sending (`smsLockState` LOCKED or REVIEW_NEEDED). That is a deliberate skip, not a delivery failure. Previously these reminders stayed in the table and could still be scheduled once an admin unlocked the account. Now they are permanently deleted after two cron runs, so a user under temporary review loses all upcoming SMS reminders. A deliberate skip should be told apart from a real scheduling error.

title: DB update inside catch can throw and abort the whole cron batch
body: The `catch` block used to only log. It now runs `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` first, which is not protected by its own try/catch. If that update fails (DB/connection error, or the row was deleted concurrently, which makes Prisma throw P2025), the exception escapes the `for` loop. The handler then returns a 500 and every remaining reminder in `unscheduledReminders` is skipped for this run. One bad reminder can stall SMS scheduling for everyone. Wrap the update in its own try/catch, or log first and swallow update errors.

title: Transient errors are treated like permanent ones; two failures permanently drop the reminder
body: Every exception in the try block increments `retryCount`, and after two increments the reminder is hard-deleted. That includes a Twilio outage or rate-limit response, and failures in unrelated code before sending such as `prisma.profile.findFirst`, `getBookerBaseUrl` or `customTemplate`. Two consecutive cron runs can be minutes apart, so a short provider outage now silently and permanently loses SMS reminders that would previously have been retried until the send date. The deletion is also not logged anywhere. Consider counting only non-retryable errors (e.g. invalid number) toward deletion, or allowing more attempts with logging.

title: OR on unindexed retryCount forces a full scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron run
body: Before this change, the `deleteMany` predicate (`method = SMS AND scheduledDate <= now`) could use the `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` index. Adding an `OR` branch on `retryCount`, which has no index and no `method` restriction, generally forces Postgres into a sequential scan of the entire `WorkflowReminder` table. That table includes all email and WhatsApp reminders and runs on every cron invocation. Scoping the second branch to `method = SMS` (or adding an index) would avoid this.

title: No tests for the new retry/deletion behavior
body: The PR adds logic that permanently deletes user reminders based on a failure counter, but no tests cover it. Cases worth covering: the increment on a falsy `scheduleSMS` result, the increment on a thrown error, deletion once `retryCount > 1`, and confirming that non-SMS reminders are untouched. Regressions here mean SMS reminders are silently lost.

title: Intentional skip (locked SMS sending) is counted as a failure, so reminders are permanently deleted
body:
`twilio.scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` on purpose when the user or team is LOCKED for SMS sending. Before this PR the reminder stayed unscheduled and would go out once the account was unlocked, as long as the scheduled date had not passed.

The new `else` branch treats that falsy return as a failed attempt and increments `retryCount`. After two cron runs, which can be well under an hour, the next run's `deleteMany` removes the reminder. An admin unlocking the account later cannot recover those reminders.

The same applies to transient Twilio or network errors in the `catch`. Reminders scheduled up to 7 days ahead get only two closely spaced attempts before permanent deletion.

Only genuine send failures should count toward the limit. Consider a backoff, or a separate state for locked accounts.

title: Prisma update inside catch can throw and abort the whole cron loop
body:
Previously the `catch` only logged, so one bad reminder could not stop processing of the others. Now the catch block calls `prisma.workflowReminder.update`, which is not itself guarded.

If the reminder row no longer exists, `update` throws P2025 (record not found). That happens, for example, when the booking was cancelled or rescheduled and its reminders were deleted between `findMany` and this point.

This also covers the case where the `else`-branch update inside the `try` is what threw: the catch retries the same failing update. The exception then escapes the `for` loop and the handler. All remaining reminders in that run are skipped and the cron returns an error.

Wrap the retry-count update in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany` (which does not throw on 0 rows).

title: retryCount deletion branch is not scoped to SMS and forces an unindexed full-table scan
body:
The second `OR` branch is `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method` filter. This SMS cron will delete any EMAIL or WHATSAPP `WorkflowReminder` whose `retryCount` exceeds 1. That breaks as soon as the email or WhatsApp crons start using the newly added shared column.

The filter is also not restricted to `scheduled: false`. On top of that, `retryCount` has no index and is OR'ed with the indexed predicate. Postgres therefore has to sequentially scan the entire `WorkflowReminder` table (all methods, all history) on every cron run.

Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and `scheduled: false`) to this branch. That fixes the scoping and lets the existing `(method, scheduled, scheduledDate)` index narrow the scan.

title: Read-modify-write of retryCount instead of atomic increment
body:
`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` writes a value computed from the row as it was read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap, both read 0 and both write 1, losing an increment and allowing extra attempts. A stale value can also overwrite a newer one.

Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` in both the `else` branch and the `catch` block.

title: Reminders with no recipient/message or missing step/booking are still re-queried forever
body:
The PR aims to stop reminders that can never be scheduled from being retried every cron run, but several such paths never increment `retryCount`:
- `sendTo` is null (e.g. a booking without `smsReminderNumber`).
- The computed `message` is empty (e.g. a non-REMINDER template with no body).
- The early `continue` when `workflowStep` or `booking` is null (line 68).

These reminders are fetched and skipped on every run until their scheduled date passes, which is the behaviour the PR set out to fix.

title: Top-level OR fragments are returned without outer parentheses, so composing them gives wrong results
body:
`Prisma.sql` inlines nested fragments verbatim; it does not wrap them in parentheses. Several public methods return a fragment whose top level is an unparenthesized OR:
- `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` / `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` return `(A AND B) OR (C AND D)`.
- `buildFilterConditions` returns `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` when only one filter is set.
- `getBaseConditions` returns the auth fragment bare when there are no filters.

These methods are the replacement for `findMany`, so callers must embed the fragments in their own queries. A natural pattern is `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ${start}`. That parses as `(team branch) OR ((user branch) AND createdAt >= start)`, so date, status or any other extra predicate applies to only one branch. The result is wrong counts and leaked rows outside the requested range.

It is worse with `getFilterConditions()`: `WHERE ${auth} AND ${filter}` becomes `... OR "eventParentId" = X`, which returns rows with that eventParentId regardless of authorization.

The old Prisma where-object API could not be mis-composed this way. Each returned fragment should be wrapped in parentheses, e.g. `Prisma.sql\`(${...})\``, so it is safe to combine.

title: Public `findMany` method removed and constructor contract changed
body:
The public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method is deleted and replaced with `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a raw SQL fragment. All getters now return `Prisma.Sql` instead of `BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput`.

Existing callers of `findMany` or of `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` would break. That includes any code passing the conditions into a Prisma `where`. Those callers would get type errors or, if typed loosely, runtime query failures.

Only the test file is updated in this PR. The PR also says the type-check and test runner were not run successfully. Either confirm there are no other consumers or migrate them in this PR.

title: Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions
body:
`getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object, which is always truthy. Even the NOTHING case is a non-null Sql instance.

As a result, the `else if (filterConditions)` branch and the final `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` can never run. This is harmless today, but it suggests a fallback that does not exist.

If auth were ever made nullable, the `filterConditions`-only branch would silently drop authorization. Simplify to `filterConditions ? (auth) AND (filter) : auth`.

title: Caching tests deleted although caching logic remains
body:
The entire `Caching` describe block was removed, covering both authorization and filter condition caching. The service still caches through `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`.

The cache uses an `=== undefined` sentinel, and `null` is a valid cached filter value. Without these tests, a regression in that logic would go unnoticed. The tests only needed their expectations updated to `Prisma.sql` values, not removal.

title: getBaseConditions returns an un-parenthesized OR expression when there are no filters
body:
When both auth and filter conditions exist, `getBaseConditions` wraps each one: `(auth) AND (filter)`. When there are no filters, it returns `authConditions` unwrapped. For org and team scope that is `(teamBranch) OR (userBranch)`.

The old `findMany` let Prisma's `AND` array handle grouping. Raw-SQL callers will now write things like `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ${start}`. Because SQL `AND` binds tighter than `OR`, that becomes `teamBranch OR (userBranch AND createdAt >= ...)`. Every caller-supplied predicate (date range, status, etc.) is then silently ignored for all team bookings.

The same problem affects the public `getFilterConditions`, which returns the bare `"eventTypeId" = X OR "eventParentId" = X`. Combining it as `${auth} AND ${filter}` would match any row with `eventParentId = X`, including rows outside the authorized set.

Fix: wrap every returned fragment in parentheses, e.g. `Prisma.sql\`(${authConditions})\``, or build each OR fragment already wrapped.

title: Dead fallback branch would return filter conditions without any authorization
body:
`getAuthorizationConditions()` always resolves to a `Prisma.Sql` object, which is always truthy. So the `else if (filterConditions) return filterConditions` and `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` branches can never run.

The branch is also dangerous as written. If auth conditions ever become nullable or empty in a refactor, the method would return only the user-supplied filters with no authorization restriction, exposing bookings across tenants.

The fallback for a missing auth condition should be `NOTHING_CONDITION`, never the filter alone, or the dead branches should be removed.

title: Public findMany method removed without a replacement query method
body:
`findMany(findManyArgs)` was the service's public query entry point. It is deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a SQL fragment.

Any existing or in-flight caller of `insightsBookingService.findMany(...)` will stop compiling. Each caller now has to hand-write `$queryRaw` against `"BookingTimeStatusDenormalized"` and get operator precedence right itself (see the parenthesization issue).

The PR description presents this as a test-only update and does not mention the API removal.

title: Org/team SQL fragments are never executed against the database
body:
The only test that runs a generated condition against Postgres uses user scope (`"userId" = X AND "teamId" IS NULL`).

The org and team fragments use hand-written raw SQL: `"teamId" = ANY(${array})` with JS arrays as parameters, and the `"isTeamBooking"` column. Tests only compare them structurally against identical template literals. A wrong column name, an array/type mismatch in `ANY(...)`, or a precedence bug (e.g. appending `AND ...` to an OR expression) would pass these tests.

The PR description also says the tests could not be run locally. A `$queryRaw` assertion for org and team scope would actually validate the new SQL.

title: Caching tests deleted although caching logic remains
body:
The `Caching` describe block, which covered `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` caching, was removed outright instead of being ported to the `Prisma.sql` format.

The service still caches via `cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions`, including the `null`-vs-`undefined` distinction for filters. A regression there (e.g. re-querying memberships on every call, or treating a cached `null` as uncached) is now untested.

title: getBaseConditions returns an unparenthesized OR fragment, so appended predicates change meaning
body:
When there are no filters, `getBaseConditions()` returns the authorization fragment as-is. For org and team scopes that fragment is `(A) OR (B)` (built by the reduce at lines 171-174 and 204-207) with no outer parentheses.

The natural way to use it is `WHERE ${base} AND "createdAt" >= ${start}`. That renders as `(A) OR (B) AND createdAt...`, which Postgres parses as `A OR (B AND createdAt...)`. Every extra predicate (date range, status, etc.) then silently skips the team-booking branch, so insights counts come out wrong.

The old Prisma object API could not have this problem. The service should wrap every fragment it returns, e.g. `Prisma.sql\`(${authConditions})\``, so callers can compose it safely.

title: Public filter fragment `(eventTypeId = X) OR (eventParentId = X)` has no outer parentheses; naive AND-combination bypasses authorization
body:
With a single eventTypeId filter, `getFilterConditions()` (a public method) returns `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` with no outer parentheses.

`getBaseConditions` wraps it correctly. But any caller that combines the public fragments itself, e.g. `WHERE ${auth} AND ${filter}`, gets `auth AND (eventTypeId = X) OR (eventParentId = X)`. Postgres evaluates that as `(auth AND eventTypeId = X) OR eventParentId = X`. Every booking whose eventParentId matches is then returned regardless of the authorization condition, leaking other users' and teams' bookings.

The service should return self-contained, parenthesized fragments. The new tests lock in the unwrapped form.

title: Public `findMany` removed without a replacement query method
body:
The public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method is deleted and replaced with `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a SQL fragment.

Any existing consumer of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` will stop compiling. Each caller now has to hand-write raw SQL against `"BookingTimeStatusDenormalized"`, which multiplies the composition and precedence risks above.

The PR does not update any callers and does not say whether any exist. Either keep a query method that applies the conditions internally, or confirm and update all call sites.

title: Unreachable fail-open fallback returns filter conditions without authorization
body:
`getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object, which is always truthy. So the `else if (filterConditions) return filterConditions;` and `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` branches can never run.

The structure is also dangerous: if the auth builder is ever changed to return null or undefined, this code fails open and returns filter-only conditions with no authorization restriction. Remove the dead branches, or make the missing-auth case return NOTHING_CONDITION.

title: Caching tests deleted although caching logic is unchanged
body:
The whole "Caching" describe block was removed. `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` still memoize via `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, but nothing tests that behavior any more.

The tests could have been converted to the Prisma.sql format like the others. The single DB-backed test only covers user scope; org and team scope SQL is never executed against the database. Malformed SQL in those branches, such as the `= ANY(...)` array binding or the `isTeamBooking` column, would go undetected. The author also notes the tests were not run.

title: updateMany with empty data is a no-op, so SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is never bumped
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object. Prisma only fills in `@updatedAt` when there are other fields to write. With no write arguments the query engine skips the UPDATE, so `updatedAt` on SelectedCalendar is never refreshed. The stated purpose ("Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars under this credential") is not achieved. The call still adds a DB round-trip on every webhook-driven cache refresh. Either set `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly or remove the call; the PR notes already say the frontend doesn't use this field.

title: Deleting the cache doesn't invalidate connectedCalendars, so the UI keeps showing stale cache status
body: `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. It never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. In contrast, `disconnectMutation` invalidates it in `onSettled`. On pages where `onChanged` isn't provided (e.g. /apps/installed/calendar), and because the query uses `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated …" and the "Delete cached data" action after a successful deletion. Users get no feedback that the cache is gone. Add an `onSettled` that invalidates `connectedCalendars`.

title: Authorization failure thrown as plain Error, surfaces as 500
body: When the credential doesn't belong to the user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps plain errors to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR. A legitimate not-found/forbidden case is therefore reported and logged as a server crash, and the client can't tell the two apart. Throw a `TRPCError` with code `NOT_FOUND` or `FORBIDDEN` instead.

title: Backfilled updatedAt = migration time makes existing caches appear freshly updated
body: `ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" ... DEFAULT NOW()` stamps every existing CalendarCache row with the migration timestamp. The new UI shows "Last updated: <timestamp>" from this column. Right after deploy, every user with an existing cache will see it as freshly updated, even if the data is up to a month old (CACHING_TIME). That is misleading in a feature meant to show cache freshness. A better backfill would be something like `expiresAt - interval '30 days'`.

title: Migration warning comment contradicts the SQL
body: The auto-generated header says the column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty." The statement below does add `DEFAULT NOW()`, so the warning is false and will confuse anyone auditing migrations. Remove or correct it.

title: Cache status counts expired entries that are never served
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups over all CalendarCache rows for the credential with no `expiresAt >= now` filter. `getCachedAvailability` only returns non-expired rows. A credential whose cache has fully expired, and is therefore never used, will still show a cache status and a "Last updated" timestamp in the UI. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` so the status reflects cache that is actually in effect.

title: Handler bypasses calendar-cache feature gating by instantiating the real repository directly
body: The handler does `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init`, which selects `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the feature is disabled. As a result, the mock's new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` is never used. Users whose team has calendar-cache disabled, but who still have leftover rows, will see cache status and delete actions. The handler also adds an unconditional groupBy query to every connectedCalendars request.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires unused updatedAt/googleChannelId fields
body: The `Pick` for `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now requires `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. Neither field is read anywhere in this module. The type is part of the public `getConnectedDestinationCalendars` export (legacy export for @calcom/platform-libraries), so every caller must now select these columns or fail type-checking. To satisfy it, `findUnlockedUserForSession` in user.ts now loads these columns for every session. Revert the type widening unless something actually consumes the fields.

title: Cache timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale and time format preference (12h/24h). Non-US users see a US-style date like 7/15/25, 4:06 PM inside an otherwise translated string. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (i18n.language) or the app's existing date formatting helpers.

title: `sed -i ''` is macOS-only; script fails on Linux and exits 0 on errors
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD sed syntax. On GNU sed, `''` is parsed as the (empty) script and the substitution expression as a filename, so updating an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` fails on Linux. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the caller's cwd rather than the script location. `cleanup` always does `exit 0`, so rate-limit and URL-extraction failures report success.

title: dev:cron depends on undeclared tsx via npx
body: `dev:cron` now runs `npx tsx`, but `tsx` isn't a declared dependency while `ts-node` still is. npx will download an unpinned tsx at runtime, or fail offline. The change is also unrelated to this feature. Add `tsx` as a devDependency or keep ts-node.

title: No tests for new deleteCache authorization or cache status query
body: The PR adds a mutation that deletes data scoped by an ownership check, plus a new groupBy repository method. There are no unit or integration tests for either. Cases worth covering: deleting another user's credential cache must be rejected, and `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` must return the max `updatedAt` per credential. The PR description itself notes end-to-end testing was not possible.

title: Deleting cache does not refresh connectedCalendars, so the UI keeps showing the old cache status
body:
On success, `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop (`onChanged` from the wrapper, which is often undefined). It never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. The disconnect mutation in the same component does invalidate it in `onSettled`.

After a successful delete, the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated: …" and the "Delete cached data" action. That stale state lasts until something else refetches the query, and `refetchOnWindowFocus` is false for this query. This contradicts the test plan's "UI updates appropriately".

Fix: invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSuccess`/`onSettled`.

title: updateMany with empty data does not bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
body:
`SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is meant to touch `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` after each cache refresh. Prisma only injects `@updatedAt` when the update has at least one field; with `data: {}` the update is a no-op. So `updatedAt` never changes, and the call is a wasted DB round trip on every webhook-driven cache refresh.

The PR description's claim that SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is updated via the webhook handler is therefore false.

Either set `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly or remove the call. The PR notes the field is unused in the frontend anyway. Also note that `updateManyByCredentialId` is typed with `SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` rather than `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.

title: Cache status includes expired cache rows
body:
`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups over all CalendarCache rows for the credential and takes the max `updatedAt`, without filtering on `expiresAt >= now`. `getCachedAvailability` ignores expired rows, so a credential whose cache has fully expired is still reported as having cache data with a "Last updated" timestamp. The dropdown then shows a status for cache that is never served.

Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the `where` clause.

title: Plain Error used for access denial yields 500 instead of NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN
body:
When the credential does not belong to the user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps a plain Error to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500). As a result, authorization failures show up as server errors in monitoring and clients cannot distinguish them.

Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or FORBIDDEN), consistent with other handlers.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId that nothing consumes
body:
`allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. Nothing in this PR reads these fields; the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache.

`getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` is also exported for `@calcom/platform-libraries` and has other callers. Any caller that builds the user with only `externalId/integration/eventTypeId` now fails type-checking.

The change also widens the session user select (`findUnlockedUserForSession`) for no functional benefit. Revert these type and select changes unless they are needed.

title: Cache timestamp formatted with hard-coded en-US locale
body:
The "Last updated" timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)`, while the surrounding string is translated via `t()`. Users with other locales see US-style dates (MM/DD/YY, 12h clock) inside localized text.

Use the user's locale from `useLocale()` (e.g. `i18n.language`), or the app's date formatting helpers, together with the user's time format preference.

title: Migration warning comment contradicts the SQL and legacy rows get a misleading timestamp
body:
The header warns that the required column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty." The statement actually adds the column with `DEFAULT NOW()`, so the warning is stale and misleading.

Also, every existing CalendarCache row gets the migration time as `updatedAt`. Right after deploy, the new UI reports all legacy caches as "Last updated" at migration time, regardless of when they were actually written.

title: BSD-only `sed -i ''` breaks on Linux; relative ENV_FILE depends on cwd
body:
`sed -i '' -E ...` is macOS/BSD syntax. With GNU sed, the empty string is parsed as the sed script and the `s|...|` expression as a filename, so updating an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` fails on Linux.

Separately, `ENV_FILE="../.env"` (line 5) is resolved relative to the caller's cwd. Running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root creates or edits a `.env` outside the repository.

Resolve the path relative to the script directory, and use a portable in-place edit (e.g. `sed -i.bak` or a temp file).

title: dev:cron relies on unpinned `npx tsx` not declared as a dependency
body:
`tsx` is not listed in devDependencies, so `npx tsx` downloads whatever version is latest at run time. That requires network access and gives non-reproducible behavior. `ts-node` is still kept as a devDependency.

Add `tsx` as a pinned devDependency and invoke it directly, or keep `ts-node`. This change is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature.

title: No tests for new deleteCache handler, cache status repository method, or dropdown
body:
The PR adds a mutation that deletes data, guarded by an ownership check (`deleteCacheHandler`). It also adds `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` and new conditional rendering logic in `CredentialActionsDropdown`, but none of these have tests.

At minimum, cover these cases:
- The handler rejects credentials owned by another user.
- The handler deletes only rows for the given credential.
- The status query returns the max `updatedAt` per credential.

title: Deleting the cache does not invalidate connectedCalendars, so the UI keeps showing the deleted cache
body:
The `deleteCache` mutation's `onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop (`onChanged` from the wrapper). It never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. That query is the source of `cacheUpdatedAt`, and it runs with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`.

Wherever `onChanged` is not passed, or does not refetch that query, the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated: …" and the "Delete cached data" action after a successful deletion.

The disconnect mutation in the same component does invalidate this query in `onSettled`. `deleteCacheMutation` should invalidate it the same way.

title: updateMany with empty data likely doesn't touch updatedAt and adds an unused write on every cache refresh
body:
`SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is meant to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. As far as I know, Prisma only applies `@updatedAt` when at least one field is being set; with `data: {}` the update is a no-op, so the timestamp probably never changes.

Even if it did work, nothing reads this value: the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, and the PR notes themselves question it.

The call also adds an extra DB round-trip to every webhook-driven `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` and to the unwatch path. If it throws, it fails the webhook after the cache was already written. Either pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` explicitly or remove the call.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires unused updatedAt/googleChannelId fields, widening the public input contract
body:
`allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. This function is also exported as `getConnectedDestinationCalendars` for `@calcom/platform-libraries`. Any caller that builds the user with a narrower selectedCalendars select will stop type-checking.

No code in this PR reads these fields. To satisfy the type, `findUnlockedUserForSession` in `user.ts` (lines 899-900) now selects them on every session load. This puts `googleChannelId` (the webhook channel identifier) into `ctx.user` for no functional reason.

Drop these additions unless they are actually consumed.

title: Authorization failure thrown as plain Error surfaces as 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
body:
When the credential doesn't exist or belongs to another user, the handler throws a plain `new Error(...)`. tRPC maps this to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, so an expected access-denied or not-found case gets logged and reported as a server fault.

Other handlers use `TRPCError` with `code: "NOT_FOUND"` or `"FORBIDDEN"` so clients and monitoring can tell these cases apart. The same should be done here.

title: Cache status includes expired entries that are never served
body:
`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups over all `CalendarCache` rows for the credential, with no `expiresAt` filter. `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows with `expiresAt >= now`.

A credential whose cache rows have all expired therefore still shows "Last updated: …" and a delete option, which suggests a usable cache exists. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the where clause if the status is meant to reflect the active cache.

title: Stale migration warning and misleading backfilled timestamps
body:
The header comment says the column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty". The SQL actually adds `DEFAULT NOW()`, so the leftover warning is wrong and will confuse anyone reviewing migrations.

The default also stamps every pre-existing cache row with the migration time. After deploy, the new UI will report "Last updated" as the deploy time for legacy caches that may be weeks old, until each row is next upserted.

title: Timestamp formatting hardcodes en-US locale
body: The cache timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)`. All users therefore see US date order and 12h time, regardless of their locale (`useLocale`) or their 12/24h `timeFormat` setting. The surrounding label is translated, but the date inside it is not. Use the user's locale, or the existing dayjs/time-format helpers.

title: BSD-only `sed -i ''` breaks the script on Linux
body: `sed -i '' -E "s|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses macOS/BSD syntax. On GNU sed, `''` is taken as the (empty) script and the substitution expression is taken as a filename. The command fails with "can't read s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=...", so on Linux an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` entry is never updated. The script still prints "✅ Updated" afterwards.

title: ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's cwd, and failure paths exit 0
body:
`ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved against the current working directory, not the script's location. Running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root (the usual way) touches or creates a `.env` in the parent directory of the repository instead of the repo's own `.env`. It should resolve relative to `$(dirname "$0")`.

Separately, `cleanup` always ends with `exit 0`. The rate-limit and "failed to extract URL" paths therefore report success to callers.

title: dev:cron now relies on an undeclared, unpinned tsx fetched via npx
body:
`dev:cron` was changed to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` isn't in this package's dependencies. `npx` will download whatever version is current from the registry at run time. That is non-reproducible and fails offline.

The change is also unrelated to this feature, and the other scripts in this file still use the declared `ts-node`.

title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation batch on every cron run
body:
One `try` wraps the entire `for` loop of `client.request` calls, and the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` promises run only at the end via `Promise.all`. Prisma promises are lazy, so if any cancel request throws, the loop stops and none of the queued deletes execute.

This includes reminders that SendGrid already cancelled earlier in the same run. They keep `cancelled: true`, so the next run re-POSTs a cancel for those batch ids. SendGrid can reject a cancel for a batch that is already cancelled, and that failure aborts the loop again.

Concrete triggers:
- the 100 pending-cancellation limit;
- a batch already cancelled through the `immediateDelete` path (e.g. organizer `requestReschedule` sets `cancelled=true`, then the attendee reschedules and `handleNewBooking` cancels the same batch immediately);
- a null `referenceId`.

One bad row therefore blocks every other cancellation until its `scheduledDate` passes, and those other emails are sent. Handle each reminder in its own try/catch and delete or mark each row right after its own request succeeds.

title: Reschedule still uses immediate SendGrid cancel and leaves the reminder row behind
body:
For rescheduled bookings, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` POSTs to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` immediately. That is the exact behaviour the PR identifies as broken: it consumes SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation quota, and once the quota is full these cancels fail and rescheduled-booking reminders are still sent.

The `immediateDelete` branch in `emailReminderManager.ts` also returns without deleting the row or marking it cancelled. The row stays with `scheduled: true` and its `referenceId`. If it was already `cancelled: true` (from `requestReschedule`), or is later marked cancelled by a workflow edit, the cron sends a second cancel for the same batch.

The old booking is not deleted here, so the deferred path (no `immediateDelete`) works and should be used. Otherwise the immediate path should at least delete the row.

title: Workflow/step deletion still cancels immediately and is subject to the 100-cancellation limit
body:
When a workflow is deleted (and when a step is deleted, line 521), every scheduled email reminder is cancelled with `immediateDelete=true`. That issues one SendGrid scheduled_sends cancel per reminder right away.

A workflow active on many event types can easily have more than 100 scheduled reminders in the 72h window. Past the account-wide limit, the remaining cancels fail. The failures are only logged inside `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, and the rows are then cascade-deleted with the workflow or step, so nothing retries. Those reminders are still delivered after the user deleted the workflow.

This path needs its own deferred mechanism, for example detaching or keeping cancelled rows instead of cascade-deleting them before the cron processes them.

title: Reminder cancellation DB writes are fire-and-forget (previously awaited)
body:
`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but are called inside `forEach` without being awaited or added to `prismaPromises`. Before this PR, the `workflowReminder.deleteMany` promises were awaited.

Now the handler can return before the `cancelled: true` update, the row delete or the Twilio cancel completes. In serverless deployments, work after the response may be frozen or dropped. The flag is then never set, the cron never cancels the email, and the reminder for the cancelled booking is sent: the bug this PR is meant to fix.

The same pattern appears in `bookings.tsx` `requestReschedule` (line 490), `handleNewBooking.ts`, and the `workflows.tsx` update paths. Collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)` them.

title: Deferring cancellation for imminent reminders can miss SendGrid's cancel cutoff
body:
Every cancellation with a `referenceId` is now deferred to the cron by setting `cancelled: true`, whatever the reminder's `scheduledDate`. The cron runs every 15 minutes, and SendGrid only honours a scheduled-send cancel made at least ~10 minutes before send time.

If a booking is cancelled or rescheduled roughly 10–25 minutes before its reminder is due, the cron may not run before the cutoff, so the email goes out. The previous immediate cancel would have stopped it.

Cancel immediately when `scheduledDate` is already inside the cron's 1-hour window; only reminders further out need to be deferred.

title: Unused `Prisma` import after removing batch-delete code
body:
`Prisma` is still imported from `@prisma/client`, but its only use was in the removed `PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>[]` arrays, so it is now unused. The import also lost its trailing comma.

This will trip lint (no-unused-vars) and formatting checks.

title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cron cancellation pass, and the failure repeats every run
body:
The cancellation loop has a single try/catch around all reminders. Each reminder awaits `client.request(...)`, and its DB delete is only queued as a lazy PrismaPromise in `workflowRemindersToDelete`. That array is executed by `Promise.all` only after the loop finishes.

If any SendGrid call throws (transient error, invalid or already-cancelled batch_id), three things go wrong:
1. Every remaining reminder in this run is skipped.
2. None of the queued deletes run, including those whose SendGrid cancel already succeeded.
3. On the next run (15 min later) those already-cancelled batch_ids are POSTed again. SendGrid rejects a second POST for a batch that already has a status, so the loop throws again at the same point.

The result is a persistent failure loop. Every other cancelled reminder in the 1-hour window is never cancelled and its email is sent, which is the bug this PR is meant to fix.

Fix: handle errors per reminder, delete or mark each row right after its cancel succeeds, and treat an "already cancelled" response as success.

title: immediateDelete path cancels at SendGrid but leaves the row (possibly already `cancelled: true`) for the cron to cancel again
body:
With `immediateDelete`, the function POSTs a cancel to SendGrid and returns. It does not delete or update the WorkflowReminder row.

A common sequence leads to a double cancel:
1. A booking is cancelled (handleCancelBooking) or the host uses requestReschedule. Its email reminders get `cancelled: true` and the rows stay.
2. The booker then reschedules. `getOriginalRescheduledBooking` includes CANCELLED bookings, so handleNewBooking calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(id, referenceId, true)` on those same rows, and SendGrid cancels the batch immediately.
3. The rows still have `cancelled: true`, so the cron later POSTs a cancel for the same batch_id. SendGrid rejects it, which triggers the loop-abort problem in scheduleEmailReminders.ts.

Fix: after a successful immediate cancel, delete the row, or at least clear `cancelled` / set `scheduled: false`.

title: Reschedules and workflow/step deletions still cancel immediately, so the 100 pending-cancellation cap can still be exhausted
body:
The PR says cancellations fail once SendGrid has 100 pending `scheduled_sends` cancellations. It fixes this by deferring cancellation to the cron within 1 hour of send time.

However, rescheduling (this line) still passes `immediateDelete = true`. So do workflow deletion (workflows.tsx line 214) and step deletion (workflows.tsx line 521).

Each immediate cancel stays pending in `scheduled_sends` until the original send time, which can be up to 72h away. A handful of reschedules, or deleting one workflow with 100+ scheduled reminders, fills the account-wide quota. After that every cancellation fails, including the cron's deferred ones, and emails go out for cancelled and rescheduled bookings. Rescheduled bookings are explicitly in scope of this fix.

Fix: reschedule should use the deferred `cancelled` flag like cancel does. For workflow/step deletion, avoid the cascade removing rows before the cron runs, for example by detaching or flagging the reminders instead of cancelling immediately.

title: Deferring every cancellation to the 15-minute cron misses reminders that are about to be sent
body:
Cancellation is always deferred by setting `cancelled: true`, even when the reminder's `scheduledDate` is already inside or near the cron's 1-hour window. The cron runs only every 15 minutes, and SendGrid does not guarantee cancellation of a scheduled send less than about 10 minutes before `send_at`.

So if a booking is cancelled or rescheduled roughly 25 minutes or less before a reminder fires, the cancel may happen too late or not at all, and the email is sent. Before this PR the cancellation was attempted immediately.

Fix: cancel immediately when `scheduledDate` is within the cron look-ahead window, and defer only reminders further out.

title: One SendGrid failure aborts every remaining cancellation and skips all DB deletes
body:
A single try/catch wraps the whole `for` loop over `remindersToCancel`. If `client.request` throws for any one reminder (transient error, the 100-cancellation cap, or a batch that already has a cancel status), the loop exits. No later reminders in that run are cancelled, so their emails go out.

The deletes are also lost. They are collected as lazy `PrismaPromise`s and only run at `Promise.all` after the loop, so none of them execute when the catch fires, including deletes for reminders that SendGrid did cancel. On the next run those reminders are retried. Re-cancelling an already-cancelled batch fails again, so the same reminder can block the whole loop every 15 minutes until its date passes.

There is a concrete trigger. `requestReschedule` flags a reminder `cancelled: true`. `handleNewBooking` then cancels the same batch immediately on reschedule but leaves the row. The cron later re-POSTs that batch.

Fix: wrap each reminder in its own try/catch and run (await) its delete right after its own cancel succeeds.

title: Deferred cancellation misses bookings cancelled shortly before the reminder fires
body:
Cancellation now only happens in the cron, which runs every 15 minutes. Each run first deletes all EMAIL reminders whose `scheduledDate <= now`, and only then cancels flagged reminders.

If a booking is cancelled or rescheduled after the last cron run but before the reminder's send time, the next run deletes the row without ever calling SendGrid's cancel. The email is sent. Example: cron runs at :45, reminder at :50, booking cancelled at :46.

Even when the cron does catch it, it may only be a few minutes before the send. SendGrid does not guarantee cancellations made less than about 10 minutes before the send time.

The old code cancelled immediately, so this is a regression for late cancellations. `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` should cancel right away when `scheduledDate` is near (e.g. within the next hour + cron interval), and only defer far-future reminders.

title: Reschedule path still cancels in SendGrid immediately, reintroducing the pending-cancellation cap
body:
The PR says cancelled and rescheduled bookings are deferred to the cron to stay under SendGrid's limit of 100 pending cancellations. Here, though, every reschedule calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)`. That POSTs a cancel to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` right away for reminders that may be up to 72h out.

Reschedules are common, so these still pile up in `scheduled_sends` and can hit the cap. Once the cap is reached the call fails, the error is only logged, and the email is still sent.

This path also re-cancels reminders that `requestReschedule` already flagged `cancelled: true`, which leads to the duplicate cancel described for the cron. Use the deferred (flag) path here, as `bookings.tsx` and `handleCancelBooking` do.

title: immediateDelete cancels in SendGrid but leaves the DB row in an inconsistent state
body:
With `immediateDelete`, the function POSTs the cancel and returns. It neither deletes the `WorkflowReminder` row nor updates it.

For workflow or step deletion the row is cascade-deleted afterwards, so that case is fine. In the reschedule path, the original booking's rows stay with `scheduled: true` and a valid `referenceId`.

- If the row was already flagged `cancelled: true` (e.g. by `requestReschedule`), the cron will try to cancel the same batch again. That can fail and abort the cron loop.
- If the immediate POST fails (e.g. the cancellation cap), nothing records the failure and nothing retries, so the email is sent.

Fix: after a successful immediate cancel, delete the row. On failure, set `cancelled: true` so the cron retries.

title: Reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget; the try/catch around it in handleNewBooking does nothing
body:
The only thing that now stops a cancelled booking's email is the `cancelled: true` DB update (or the delete/SMS cancel). These calls are no longer awaited:

- `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` here
- the same calls in `bookings.tsx` `requestReschedule` (line 490)
- the same calls in `handleNewBooking`

Before this PR, the DB deletes were awaited via `Promise.all`. Now the handler can respond before the flag is written. Under serverless execution the update can be dropped, and any failure is only logged.

In `handleNewBooking` (lines 965-975), the surrounding try/catch is ineffective because the async calls are never awaited.

Fix: collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)` before returning.

title: Every app's import() runs eagerly when the module loads, so nothing is lazy-loaded
body:
Each value in the `appStore` object is a call like `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`. These calls run as soon as the object literal is evaluated, which happens the first time anything imports `@calcom/app-store`.

As a result, all 28 app packages are still loaded on startup, even in requests that never touch them. The PR's goal of async/lazy loading is not achieved; the only effect is that every consumer now has to `await`.

There is also a reliability cost. If any one app module throws while it is being evaluated, its promise rejects with nobody awaiting it. Node then reports an `unhandledRejection` (which crashes the process by default on Node 15+), even if that app is never used.

To get real lazy loading, store thunks such as `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")` and call them at the lookup sites (`await appStore[key]?.()`).

title: async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch dead and leaves errors unhandled
body:
The callback was changed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })`.

`forEach` throws away the promises the callback returns, which has three consequences:
- The `try/catch` around it (lines 124-139) can no longer catch anything. Before this change it at least caught synchronous `getCalendar` / CalendarService constructor errors.
- A rejection from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection, which can crash the Node process.
- The function returns `true` and sends emails without waiting for the calendar or video deletions.

Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try block instead.

title: async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch dead and leaves errors unhandled
body:
This has the same problem as vital/lib/reschedule.ts. `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })` discards the promises it creates.

The enclosing `try/catch` (lines 124-139) therefore never catches anything. Errors from `getCalendar` or from the calendar/video deletion become unhandled rejections, which can crash the process. The deletions are also never awaited before the function returns.

Replace this with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try block.

title: requestReschedule fires async forEach without awaiting; getCalendar failures become unhandled rejections
body:
`requestReschedule` now uses `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })`. Because the promises are discarded, the mutation goes on to send emails and webhooks and then resolves without knowing whether any calendar or video event was deleted.

Any rejection from `getCalendar` (for example a CalendarService constructor failing to parse or decrypt the key) or from `deleteEvent` / `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection. It does not become a tRPC error.

Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`, optionally with per-item `.catch` and logging.

title: getCalendar promise is created and dropped for non-"calendar" variants, risking unhandled rejection
body:
In `getCalendarCredentials`, `getCalendar(credential)` is called for every credential of every `_calendar` app. That includes `*_other_calendar` CRM apps whose `variant` is not `"calendar"`, and for those the result is thrown away (`return app.variant === "calendar" ? [...] : []`).

`getCalendar` is now async, so a failure while constructing the service becomes a rejected promise that nobody awaits. Examples are `symmetricDecrypt` failing in the CloseCom/Salesforce services, or a schema parse error. That surfaces as an unhandled rejection instead of an error the caller can handle.

It also needlessly loads and instantiates services for credentials that are never used. Only call `getCalendar` when `app.variant === "calendar"`.

title: Recurring-cancel branch still uses forEach(async) so calendar deletions are never awaited
body:
The non-credentialId branch was correctly converted to a `for...of` loop with `await getCalendar`. The recurring branch was only patched to `const calendar = await getCalendar(credential)` inside `.forEach(async (credential) => ...)`.

In that branch, `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)` runs only after the awaits. By then `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 has usually already run, and `sendCancelledEmails` and the response go out first. Deletion failures there are unhandled rejections.

The extra `await getCalendar` adds one more async hop before anything is recorded. Convert this to a `for...of` loop that pushes the `deleteEvent` promises, as was done for the sibling branch.

title: Dynamic imports run eagerly at module load, so nothing is lazily loaded
body:
Each property is assigned `import("./x")`, and that call runs immediately when the `appStore` object literal is evaluated. Importing `@calcom/app-store` (which `getCalendar`, `videoClient`, the payment helpers and others do) therefore starts loading all 28 app modules at once, just as the old static imports did.

The PR's goal of async/lazy loading is not met. Cold start and memory cost are unchanged, and every call site now pays an extra `await`.

There is also a new failure mode. If any app module throws during evaluation (for example a missing env var at import time), its promise rejects with no handler attached until some caller awaits that key. That produces an `unhandledRejection` at startup even for apps that are never used.

Fix: store thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and call them at the use sites (`await appStore[key]?.()`).

title: async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch dead and leaves rejections unhandled
body:
The callback was changed to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })`. `forEach` ignores the returned promises.

Before this change, a synchronous failure in `getCalendar` (for example a `CalendarService` constructor throwing on a bad or undecryptable key) was caught by the enclosing `try { ... } catch` at lines 124-139 and logged.

Now every failure from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection that the try/catch can never see. Under Node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` that can take down the process; at best the error is lost. The calendar/video deletions also run detached from `Reschedule`'s control flow.

Use `await Promise.allSettled(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (or a `for...of` with `await`) inside the try block.

title: async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch dead and leaves rejections unhandled
body:
This file has the same change as the vital app: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...) ... })`. `forEach` discards the promises.

Errors from `getCalendar` were previously thrown synchronously and caught by the try/catch at lines 124-139. They now become unhandled rejections that bypass the catch entirely. This can crash the process under Node's default unhandled-rejection mode, or the errors are silently lost. The deletions are also no longer tied to the function's execution.

Replace it with `await Promise.allSettled(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try.

title: requestReschedule now fires calendar deletions as detached async callbacks with unhandled rejections
body:
