That call returns null in two cases: `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false (for example, realm admin permissions were disabled but the admin-permissions client still exists), or the 'Clients' resource was never created (realms initialized before this change, since `init()` returns early when the client exists).

The null is then passed directly to `getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)` and later to `resource.getScopes()`, which throws a NullPointerException. Every client admin endpoint called by an admin without manage-clients would return 500.

The sibling `hasPermission(String)` null-checks the resource; this branch should do the same and return false.

title: Per-client deny on VIEW is bypassed by the all-clients VIEW check
body:
`canView(ClientModel)` first calls `canView()`. That evaluates only the all-clients 'Clients' resource and returns true as soon as an all-clients VIEW permission grants. The client-specific resource is never consulted.

As a result, a negative per-client VIEW permission (all clients viewable except X) has no effect. `requireView(X)` succeeds, and `ClientsResource.getClients` (which computes `canView()` once) lists every client.

The user resource type tests (`testViewUserPermission`, `testImpersonatePermission`) establish that a resource-specific permission overrides the all-resource one, so client semantics are inconsistent. This is also untested.

title: Any per-client permission suppresses all-clients grants for every other scope
body:
If a resource exists for the client, only that resource is evaluated. Per-client resources are created without a type, and all-clients permissions are attached to the 'Clients' resource, so the policy evaluator never picks up the all-clients permissions for that client.

Example: an admin has an all-clients MANAGE permission and a per-client permission granting only MAP_ROLES on client X. `canManage(X)` then returns false, even though the admin can manage every other client.

The fallback should be per scope: when the specific resource yields no decision for the requested scope, also evaluate the all-clients resource. Otherwise only deny on the same scope should override.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns the string 'Clients' instead of client ids
body:
`resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...)` only matches resources whose type is 'Clients'. In the V2 schema that is just the all-clients resource created by `init()`; per-client resources are created by `getOrCreateResource` without a type.

The method therefore never returns real client ids. When an all-clients permission grants the scope, it returns `{"Clients"}` (the resource name), which callers will treat as a client id. Per-client grants are ignored entirely.

It should iterate per-client resources (or the policies attached to them) and return the client ids those resource names represent.

title: canExchangeTo now throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking token exchange under V2
body:
Before this PR, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returned the V1 `ClientPermissions`. It now returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, whose `canExchangeTo` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`.

The token exchange provider calls `AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(...)` when exchanging to another client. With the V2 feature enabled, such requests will fail with a 500 instead of an access-denied response.

The unused `getEvaluationContext` helper and `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` import suggest this was meant to be implemented. At minimum it should return false or delegate rather than throw.

Similarly, `isPermissionsEnabled`/`setPermissionsEnabled` now throw. Those are reached from the `/clients/{id}/management/permissions` endpoints, which will return 500.

title: canView() ignores all-clients MANAGE, inconsistent with canView(ClientScopeModel)
Repeated full policy evaluations per client in listings
body:
Each `hasPermission` call evaluates the resource with all of its scopes and then checks a single scope. In the fallback path it also loads all policies of the 'Clients' resource just to test emptiness.

`canView(c)` alone triggers up to 4 evaluations: `canView()`, MANAGE via `canConfigure`, CONFIGURE, and VIEW. `getAccess(c)` repeats `canView`, `canManage` and `canConfigure`. Listing N clients therefore performs roughly 10+ evaluations and extra policy queries per client.

The granted scopes from one evaluation could be computed once per client (and the all-clients result once per request) and reused.

title: getResourceName has no CLIENTS branch, so client permission resources render with null names
body:
`getResourceName` maps USERS resources to "All users" or the username. For the new CLIENTS type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Neither per-client resources (created via `resourceStore.create(...)`) nor the 'Clients' all-resource (created in `init()`) have a display name, so this returns null.

Permission resource listings for client permissions will show empty names instead of "All clients" or the client's clientId.

title: Realms already initialized never receive the new Clients resource and scopes
body:
`init()` returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled admin permissions before this change never get:
- the 'Clients' all-resource;
- the new `configure`, `map-roles-client-scope` and `map-roles-composite` scopes.

For those realms, creating a client permission fails ("Scope [configure] does not exist" / "No scopes found."). Evaluation also hits the null all-clients resource path in `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission`.

The schema should be reconciled for existing clients, adding missing scopes and resource-type resources.

title: Javadoc for void require* methods says 'Returns true'
body:
The new Javadoc on `requireView()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}", and `requireViewClientScopes()` has the same wording. Both methods are void and throw ForbiddenException on failure.

The docs should match the other require* methods: "Throws ForbiddenException if canView()/canViewClientScopes() returns false".

title: Client removal no longer cleans up permission data; V2 has no replacement
body:
The removal listener now runs only when V1 `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled. Previously it always cleaned up V1 client/role/group permission objects. If V1 permissions were created and the feature later disabled, deleting clients, roles or groups now leaves orphaned resources and policies.

Under V2, nothing removes the per-client resource and permissions created by `getOrCreateResource` when a client is deleted. Stale permissions referencing non-existent clients accumulate in the admin-permissions resource server.

title: Test rotates the secret of the client used by the injected admin client and leaves other mutations unrestored
body:
`testConfigureOnlyOneClient` calls `generateNewSecret()` and `invalidateRotatedSecret()` on `myclient`. That is the confidential client (secret "mysecret") the `realmAdminClient` authenticates with, and nothing restores the secret. Any later re-authentication or token refresh by `realmAdminClient` in this class will fail with 401, making results order-dependent.

Other tests have the same problem with no cleanup registered:
- `testManageOnlyOneClient` renames `myclient` and moves a default client scope to optional;
- `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` creates client roles and maps one to `myadmin`.

These changes should be registered via `realm.cleanup()` or done on a dedicated client.

title: Docs say the Operator fails without `rolling-updates`, but no Operator check is added
body:
The new CAUTION block says that during preview the `rolling-updates` feature must be enabled, "Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail." This PR adds no Operator code that reads `spec.features` or gates `spec.update.strategy` on that feature. The only Operator-side changes are the test CR and the test Dockerfile.

As a result, a CR with `update.strategy: Recreate` and no `rolling-updates` feature behaves exactly as before, and nothing fails. Either the enforcement is missing (for example, a status error when an update strategy is set without the feature) or the documentation is wrong.

The `UpgradeTest` change only enables the feature on the happy path. No test checks that the Operator rejects or flags a strategy when the feature is disabled, so the documented behavior is not verified.

title: Appended `--features=rolling-updates` overrides the user's own features configuration
body:
The `updatecompatibility` macro now always appends `--features=rolling-updates` after the user's parameters. The guide tells users to run `metadata`/`check` with exactly the same configuration options as their deployment, including env vars and CLI args.

If a deployment sets features via `KC_FEATURES`, `keycloak.conf`, or its own `--features=...`, this appended CLI option either takes precedence and replaces that list, or duplicates the option. In both cases the metadata is generated for a feature set that differs from the deployment's. Once metadata includes configuration, this can produce a wrong rolling/recreate verdict.

The guide should tell users to add `rolling-updates` to their existing feature list (or use `--profile=preview`) instead of appending a separate `--features` option.

title: New feature changes `--features` help output; approval files not updated
body:
Adding `ROLLING_UPDATES` adds `rolling-updates` to the possible values of the `--features` / `--features-disabled` options, which are generated from `Profile.Feature`. That list is printed in the CLI help, and the help approval files in the quarkus integration tests capture it for `start`, `start-dev`, `build`, `export`, `import`, `update-compatibility`, etc.

None of those approved files are updated in this PR. The help approval tests are expected to fail until they are regenerated.

title: New exit codes (3 = recreate, 4 = feature disabled) are not asserted
body:
The PR renumbers `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and gives 4 to the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` result. The docs present these exit codes as the scripting contract.

However:
- `testFeatureNotEnabled` only checks the error message, and only for the `metadata` subcommand. The `check` subcommand's feature gate is untested, and exit code 4 is never asserted.
- `testWrongVersions` only checks the error text, not that the exit code is now 3.

A regression in either mapping, such as recreate and feature-disabled colliding again, would go unnoticed.

title: New feature added without updating the approved help-output snapshots
body: Adding `ROLLING_UPDATES` changes the list of possible values printed by `--features` and `--features-disabled` in every command's help. The Quarkus `HelpCommandDistTest` compares that output against static `*.approved.txt` snapshot files, and none of them are updated in this PR. Adding `rolling-updates:v1` to the feature list should make those approval tests fail. Regenerate and commit the approved help files, along with any other test that hard-codes the preview feature list.

title: Docs say the Operator fails without `rolling-updates`, but nothing enforces it
body: The new CAUTION says the `rolling-updates` feature must be enabled or the Operator will fail. This PR adds no Operator validation that inspects the CR's enabled features. The `ROLLING_UPDATES` enum constant is new here, so no earlier check could reference it. The Operator also does not run the `update-compatibility` commands in this version; the only update strategy is Recreate (or unset). So setting `spec.update.strategy: Recreate` without the feature still works, and the documented failure never happens. `UpgradeTest` enables the feature only when a strategy is set and never covers the claimed failure. Either add a reconcile-time validation that reports an error status when `spec.update` is used without the feature, or correct the documentation.

title: Appending `--features=rolling-updates` to every documented command overrides the user's feature configuration
body:
The `updatecompatibility` macro now hard-codes `--features=rolling-updates` on every documented invocation. A CLI option takes precedence over keycloak.conf and env, so any features the user already enables (e.g. `features=token-exchange` in the config file) are replaced for that run. That contradicts the guide's warning that the command must be run with exactly the same configuration as the deployment. A user who also passes their own `--features` gets a duplicate option.

`features` is also a build-time option. With an optimized/pre-built image (`--optimized`, which these commands support via `OptimizedMixin`), a runtime `--features` value is not applied. The check then reads the build-time profile and exits with "feature disabled" unless the image was built with the feature, as the PR itself does in `Dockerfile-custom-image`.

The docs should tell users to add `rolling-updates` to their existing feature list and to include it at build time for optimized images.

title: Feature-gate and new exit codes are not asserted
body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only exercises the `metadata` subcommand and only checks the error text. It never asserts the documented exit code 4 (`CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED`), and the `check` subcommand's gate is not tested at all. The PR also changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and gives 4 a new meaning, yet `testWrongVersions` never asserts the exit code. A regression mixing up these two values, which callers rely on to choose a rolling vs. recreate strategy, would go unnoticed. Add `assertEquals(...exitCode())` checks for the disabled-feature case on both subcommands and for the incompatible-version case.

title: New feature changes `--features` help output but approved help snapshots are not updated
body: Adding `ROLLING_UPDATES` adds `rolling-updates[:v1]` to the 'Possible values' list that the `--features` option prints in CLI help. That list is checked by the approval-based help tests (`HelpCommandDistTest.*.approved.txt` for start, start-dev, build, export, import, update-compatibility, etc.). None of those snapshot files are part of this PR, so the help tests are likely to fail once this merges. Regenerate and commit the approved help files together with the new feature.

title: Operator doc says the Operator will fail without `rolling-updates`, but nothing enforces this
body:
The new CAUTION block says the `rolling-updates` feature must be enabled or 'the Keycloak Operator will fail'. This PR adds no Operator code that checks the feature. The existing `Recreate` strategy behaves the same whether or not the feature is on.

The default `<not set>` strategy also clearly works without the feature: `UpgradeTest` runs the `null` strategy case without enabling it. The statement is therefore inaccurate at this commit. Readers will also be confused about whether the feature is needed when they don't set `update.strategy`.

Either add Operator-side validation that reports a clear status error, or reword the doc to say exactly when the feature is needed and what happens without it.

title: Hard-coded `--features=rolling-updates` in the command template can clobber the user's real feature set
body:
The `updatecompatibility` macro now appends `--features=rolling-updates` to every documented `update-compatibility` invocation. The same guide tells users to pass exactly the options used by `start`.

Users who already run with `--features=<their list>` will now pass a second `--features` value that replaces their list. The metadata/check then runs with a different feature set than the real deployment, or the duplicate option causes a CLI error. Users need to add `rolling-updates` to their existing list, not override it.

Separately, `features` is a build-time option. With an optimized (`--optimized`) image, passing it at runtime does not take effect. The commands will then exit with code 4 unless the image was rebuilt with the feature, which is why `Dockerfile-custom-image` had to be changed. Neither point is documented.

title: Feature-disabled test checks neither the new exit code nor the `check` subcommand
body:
`testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error text for the `metadata` subcommand. The PR's main contract change is the new exit code `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (and the move of `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3), and scripts are told to rely on these exit codes.

No test asserts that a disabled feature yields exit code 4, that `check` is also gated, or that an incompatible result now returns 3. A regression in the exit codes would go unnoticed. Add `assertEquals(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED, result.exitCode())` for both subcommands, and assert 3 in `testWrongVersions`.

title: V2 canManage() grants global group management to callers with only VIEW permission
body:
`GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Any admin with only an all-groups `view` permission therefore passes `groups().requireManage()`.

That check is what guards `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup`. As a result, a view-only admin can:
- create arbitrary top-level groups;
- send an existing group id and move any group in the realm to top level, changing the hierarchy and any role or attribute inheritance that depends on it.

The per-group `canManage(GroupModel)` correctly uses only `MANAGE`. The no-arg variant should do the same.

The interface Javadoc for `canManage()` in `GroupPermissionEvaluator` ("Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") documents the same wrong behavior and should be fixed too. No test checks that an all-groups VIEW permission does not allow creating groups.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs
body:
In V2, per-group resources are named by the group id (`resolveGroup` returns `group.getId()` and the resource is created with that name). The method instead passes `groupResource.getId()`, the authorization resource UUID, both to `hasPermission` (which calls `findByName`) and to the result set.

Consequences:
1. `findByName(server, resourceId)` never finds the per-group resource, so a per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grant is never recognized here. It silently falls back to the all-groups resource.
2. The all-groups `Groups` resource has type `Groups` (set in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init`), so `findByType` returns it. With an all-groups `view-members`/`manage-members` permission, its resource UUID is added to the set.

The IDs that end up in the set are not group IDs. `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` then put them into the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute, and the user query is restricted to members of a non-existent group, so the search returns nothing. `getUsersCount` computes counts against the same bogus IDs.

In the per-group case the set stays empty, so no DB-level pre-filtering happens. Results are filtered after pagination, and pages can come back empty or incomplete in realms with more than `max` users.

Use `groupResource.getName()` for both the lookup and the collected ID, and skip the type-level `Groups` resource. Add a test with an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS permission and a user search.

title: NPE / ModelException for realms whose admin-permissions schema predates the Groups type
body:
`AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists, so nothing migrates existing data. Realms that enabled FGAP v2 before this change have no `Groups` type resource and no `manage-membership`, `manage-members` or `view-members` scopes.

For those realms, `getResourceTypeResource(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` returns null. That null is passed unchecked to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later dereferenced via `resource.getScopes()`. The result is an NPE, i.e. HTTP 500, on every group endpoint and on user view/manage-by-group checks for any admin without MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS.

Creating a group permission in such a realm also fails: `getOrCreateResource` throws `ModelException("No scopes found.")` because the new scopes are missing.

Add a null guard (treat as no permission) and either migrate or lazily create the new type resource and scopes.

title: getResourceName has no handling for the new Groups resource type
body:
`getResourceName` only maps the `Users` type to a human-readable name. For `Groups` it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`.

Per-group resources are created by `getOrCreateResource` with the group id as the name and no display name. Permission representations for groups will therefore show null or a raw UUID instead of the group name, and the all-groups resource will not be shown as "All groups" the way users get "All users".

title: requireManageMembers Javadoc references the wrong method
body:
The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` says it throws if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false. The implementation actually checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`, and the two have different semantics, so the doc is misleading.

In the same file, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` documents `@return Stream of IDs` although it returns a `Set`.

title: canManage() is granted by the VIEW scope on all-groups
body:
`GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Holding only the `view` scope on the all-groups resource therefore makes `canManage()` true.

`GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` gates on `auth.groups().requireManage()`. An admin who was only granted read access to groups can then:
- create new top-level groups, and
- move any existing group (by id) to the top level.

This is a privilege escalation. The check should be `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, matching `canManage(GroupModel)`.

The interface javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` ("For V2 only: Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") documents the same wrong behavior and should be fixed too.

No test checks that a view-only all-groups permission cannot create groups; one should be added.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses the authz resource ID instead of the group ID
body:
The callback passes `groupResource.getId()` (the authz resource UUID) to `hasPermission(...)` and adds the same value to `granted`. V2 resources are named after the group ID, and `hasPermission` looks them up with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. Two things go wrong:
- The lookup by resource UUID always misses, so evaluation silently falls back to the all-groups resource and the group-specific permission is never evaluated.
- The returned set contains resource UUIDs, not group IDs.

The all-groups resource is the only one created with type `Groups` (`getOrCreateResource` never sets a type). So an admin with an all-groups `view-members`/`manage-members` permission gets a set holding just that resource's UUID.

`UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` put this set into `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)`, and `getUsersCount` passes it to the store. User search is then restricted to members of a non-existent group and returns nothing, and counts are wrong. The fix is to pass and collect `groupResource.getName()`, and to find per-group resources correctly. A test covering all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS with user search/count is missing.

title: Group checks fail for realms whose admin-permissions client was initialized before this change
body:
`AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns early when the admin permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled admin permissions before this change therefore never get:
- the `Groups` all-resource, or
- the new `manage-membership`, `manage-members` and `view-members` scopes.

In such a realm, `getResourceTypeResource(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` returns null. `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)` then dereferences the null resource, so every group permission check for a non-role admin (listing groups, viewing a group, user search via `canViewByGroup`) can fail with a 500.

Creating a group permission also fails in `getOrCreateResource` with `ModelException("No scopes found.")`.

The code should guard against a null type resource, and `init` (or a migration) should add missing resource types and scopes to existing admin-permission clients.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc references the wrong method
body: The javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` says it throws ForbiddenException if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false. It actually delegates to `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`, which checks the `manage-members` scope, not `manage-membership`. The text is a copy of the `requireManageMembership` doc and misdescribes which permission is enforced.

title: canManage() is granted by the VIEW scope on all groups
body:
`GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. This looks copied from `canView()`. The effect is that an admin with only a read-only "view all groups" permission passes `requireManage()`.

`GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` uses `requireManage()`, so such an admin can create top-level groups and move existing groups to the top level. This is a privilege escalation.

The interface Javadoc for `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` ("V2 only: Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") documents the same wrong behavior and should also be fixed. Only `MANAGE` should be checked.

No test covers this: `testManageAllGroups` only grants MANAGE. There is no test that VIEW alone does not allow creating groups.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs and looks up resources by the wrong key
body:
The callback passes `groupResource.getId()` (the authz resource UUID) to `hasPermission`. That method calls `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, so a resource ID is used as a name and never matches. Evaluation always falls back to the all-groups resource.

The callback then adds `groupResource.getId()` to the result. Callers treat the result as group IDs: `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource` put it in the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute, and `getUsersCount(realm, groupIds)` uses it.

In addition, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never calls `setType`, so `findByType(server, "Groups")` only returns the all-groups resource named "Groups". Per-group resources are never iterated.

Consequences:
- With an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS permission, the set contains the "Groups" resource UUID. The user query is restricted to a non-existent group and returns no users.
- With only per-group permissions, the set is empty. The DB query is unfiltered and users are filtered in memory after pagination, so pages come back short or incomplete.
- `/users/count` returns wrong counts in both cases.

The method should iterate per-group resources and return `resource.getName()` (the group id). The all-groups case needs its own handling.

title: NPE when the all-groups "Groups" resource does not exist
body:
`AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...)` can return null. This happens when the schema is not supported for the current context, or when the "Groups" resource was never created. The result is passed straight into `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later `resource.getScopes()` with no null check.

`AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns early if the admin-permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled admin permissions before this change therefore have no "Groups" resource and none of the new `manage-members`/`view-members`/`manage-membership` scopes.

For such realms, any admin without the `view-users`/`manage-users` roles who lists or reads groups goes through `canView(group)` and hits this path, which fails with a 500. Creating group permissions there also fails with "No scopes found".

Add a null guard here, and either add a migration or create the missing schema resources and scopes for existing admin-permissions clients.

title: Any per-group permission hides all-groups grants for other scopes on that group
body:
`hasPermission` falls back to the all-groups resource only when no per-group resource exists. Once any permission references a group (for example VIEW_MEMBERS on `topGroup`), that group's resource exists and only it is evaluated.

Per-group resources are created without a type, so the "Groups"-typed all-groups permissions are not included in that evaluation. As a result, an admin with "manage all groups" who is also given "view-members on topGroup" can no longer manage, view, or map roles on `topGroup`.

This also makes `canView()`/`canManage()` (all-groups) and `canView(group)`/`canManage(group)` disagree for the same group. The evaluation should combine the per-group result with the all-groups resource for scopes the per-group permissions do not decide.

title: requireManageMembers Javadoc references the wrong method
body:
The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` says it throws ForbiddenException if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false. The implementations actually check `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`, which is a different scope (MANAGE_MEMBERS vs MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP). It looks copy-pasted from `requireManageMembership` and will mislead callers.

Separately, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` documents its return as a "Stream" while it returns a Set.

title: Public evaluator interface methods renamed/removed without deprecation
body:
`GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupsWithViewPermission()` is renamed to `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, and `getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel)` is removed. `ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes` is also removed.

`GroupPermissionEvaluator` is reachable from `AdminPermissionEvaluator`, which custom admin REST extensions (`AdminRealmResourceProvider`) receive. Those extensions will fail to compile or link after upgrade.

Consider keeping the old method as a deprecated default that delegates to the new one.

title: Groups resource type not handled in getResourceName
body:
The new GROUPS resource type is added, but `getResourceName` still only maps USERS resources to human-readable names ("All users" or the username).

Per-group resources are created by `getOrCreateResource` with the group id as name and no display name. The "Groups" type resource also has no display name. For group permissions this method therefore returns `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is null.

Resource names shown for group permissions in the admin API/UI will be null or meaningless instead of "All groups" or the group name/path.

title: testManageGroupMembership does not verify that the group-level permission is required
body:
The test grants all-users MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP and per-group MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP together, then only asserts that the join succeeds.

The initial negative check uses the non-existent group "no-such", so it only exercises the user-level check. Nothing asserts that the join to `topGroup` is forbidden when the group's MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP permission is absent, so a regression in `GroupPermissionsV2.canManageMembership` would go unnoticed.

The suite also has no case for all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on user listing or count, which would expose the `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` bug.

title: Java MessageFormat syntax used in an i18next bundle breaks interpolation in the Account Console
body:
The v3 Account Console is a React app that translates with i18next, whose default interpolation is `{{name}}`. The rest of this file follows that convention (e.g. `error-invalid-length='{{0}}' must have ...`).

User-profile server errors are translated client-side: `t(errorMessage, {0: ..., 1: ..., 2: ...})` in `setUserProfileServerError`. With the value changed to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`, i18next performs no substitution. Users would see the literal placeholders and the raw `{2,choice,...}` pattern.

The previous `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` form should be kept for the JS bundles. If the verifier needs this key, extend its normalization rather than switching the bundle to MessageFormat syntax.

title: Admin Console bundle switched to MessageFormat placeholders/choice, which i18next cannot render
body:
The admin console (keycloak.v2) also translates with i18next using `{{...}}` interpolation. User-profile validation errors returned by the admin REST API are translated client-side with numeric params.

The new value `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` will not be interpolated. Admins creating or editing users with a multivalued-size violation would see raw `{0}` and `{2,choice,...}` text.

The `{{0}}`-style placeholders should be restored for this JS bundle.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian bundle is now `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian sentence in the OTP setup page. It should be a Lithuanian phrase, e.g. `Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame telefone:`.

title: Lithuanian login translation replaced with Italian text
body: `loginTotpStep1` in the Lithuanian login bundle was changed to the Italian `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. Lithuanian users configuring OTP at login will see Italian. A Lithuanian translation should be used instead.

title: Simplified Chinese bundle now contains Traditional Chinese text
body: `totpStep1` in `messages_zh_CN` was set to `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`. That is Traditional Chinese (手機/安裝/應用程式), apparently copied from zh_TW. The rest of the zh_CN file uses Simplified characters. It should read e.g. `在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`.

title: Diff-trimming logic can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of reporting the error
body: The `start` and `end` loops that trim common prefix and suffix are computed independently. Neither is bounded by `length - start`, so they can overlap. Example 1: value `y` sanitizes to `y`. That gives start=1 and end=8, and `sanitized.substring(1, 0)` throws. Example 2: value `x` sanitizes to `x`. That gives start=11 and end=4, and `value.substring(11, 7)` throws. The unchecked exception escapes `verify()`, which only catches IOException. The Maven build then fails with a stack trace instead of the intended `Illegal HTML in key ...` message. The end loop should be bounded, e.g. `end < Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`.

title: Anchor mismatch message omits key and file, making failures hard to locate
body:
`santizeAnchors` receives `key` but never uses it. It reports only `Didn't find anchor tag <a ...> in original string`.

When the verifier runs across dozens of message files, a failing build gives no indication of which file or key is at fault. By contrast, the `Illegal HTML` message includes both. The key and `file` should be included in this message.

title: ANCHOR_PATTERN matches any tag starting with 'a', not just anchors
body:
`</?a[^>]*>` also matches `<abbr>`, `<area ...>`, `<audio ...>`, `<article>`, `<aside>`, etc. Any such tag in the English source string is treated as an "anchor" and stripped before sanitization. An identical tag in a translation is therefore accepted without going through the OWASP policy, including any attributes such as event handlers. Non-anchor tags in translations are also misreported as anchor mismatches.

The pattern should be restricted to real anchors, e.g. `</?a(?:\s[^>]*)?>`.

title: Java MessageFormat syntax in an i18next bundle breaks interpolation in the account console
body:
The account console renders this bundle with i18next. Its placeholders use `{{0}}`, as every other `error-*` key in this file still does, and server errors are passed as `t(errorMessage, {0:..,1:..,2:..})`.

The new value uses `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`. i18next interpolates none of these, so users will see the literal text "Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}."

The old `{{0}}` value already passed the new verifier, because the `<!-- -->` stripping handles it, so the change was not required. Keep `{{n}}` placeholders here and use i18next pluralization instead of ChoiceFormat.

title: Admin console message switched to MessageFormat syntax that i18next won't interpolate
body: The admin console (keycloak.v2) also uses i18next with `{{param}}` interpolation. Replacing `{{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} value(s)` with `{0} ... {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` means the user-profile multivalued-size validation error appears with raw `{0}` placeholders and the choice pattern visible. Revert to `{{n}}` placeholders or use i18next plural keys.

title: Prefix/suffix trimming can overlap and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body: The `end` loop is bounded only by the string lengths, not by `length - start`. When the common prefix and common suffix overlap in the shorter string, `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` (or the `value` substring) is called with begin > end and throws. Example: a translation containing a duplicated closing tag such as `{0}`. The sanitizer drops the orphan ``, so start=10 and end=4 on a 10-char string, giving substring(10, 6). The consequence is that the maven plugin crashes with a stack trace instead of reporting "Illegal HTML in key ..." for exactly the kind of broken markup it is meant to catch. Bound the suffix loop with `end < sanitized.length() - start && end < value.length() - start`.

title: Anchor mismatch message omits key and file
body:
`messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string")` does not include the file or the key. The `key` parameter is passed into `santizeAnchors` but never used.

The verifier runs over hundreds of property files, so a build failure with this message gives no way to find the offending translation. Include `key` and `file` the same way the "Illegal HTML" message does.

title: Missing English counterpart crashes the plugin with a RuntimeException
body:
The English file path is guessed with two regex replacements. The `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` pattern also swallows any earlier underscore-separated segment of the file name, so `my_messages_de.properties` resolves to `my_en.properties`.

If the guessed file does not exist, a `RuntimeException` is thrown. `verify()` only catches `IOException`, so this escapes as an unhandled exception rather than a `MojoExecutionException` or a reported message. Any community bundle without an exactly mirrored `_en` file in `resources` aborts the build with an unclear stack trace.

Fall back to an empty English bundle and add a message, or wrap the error in `MojoExecutionException`.

title: Anchors are stripped before sanitizing, so unbalanced or reordered anchors are mishandled
body: `santizeAnchors` removes each translated `` or `` that matches the next English anchor, and only the remainder is sanitized. Two problems follow. 1. A translation that keeps `` but drops the closing `` passes silently. The page or email then renders an unclosed link that swallows the following content. The sanitizer would normally detect this imbalance, but it never sees the anchor. 2. Matching is strictly positional, so a translation that legitimately reorders two links relative to English is reported as an error. Also, `]*>` matches any tag starting with `a` (``, `

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian translation of `totpStep1` was replaced with "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian. Lithuanian users of the account theme will see an Italian sentence on the OTP setup page. It should be Lithuanian, for example "Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame telefone:".

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian `loginTotpStep1` is now "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian, apparently copied from the Italian bundle. Lithuanian users will see Italian text on the login OTP configuration page. Provide a Lithuanian translation, or remove the key so it falls back to English.

title: Traditional Chinese text added to the Simplified Chinese bundle
body: The new `totpStep1` value "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：" uses Traditional characters (手機, 安裝, 應用程式) in the zh_CN (Simplified) file. It should be Simplified, for example "在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：", consistent with the zh_CN login bundle.

title: No tests confirm valid translations produce no messages
body:
All new tests only assert that some error is reported. There is no fixture where a translation has allowed tags (``, `
`, `

`) or the same anchors as English, with an assertion that `verify()` returns an empty list. The verifier relies on fragile normalization: entity unescaping, `` stripping, choice-format and RTL-style special cases. False positives that would break the theme build are therefore not covered. Add positive fixtures, and a case with a duplicated closing tag, which currently crashes the diff code.

title: Java MessageFormat syntax breaks i18next interpolation in the account console
body: The account console (keycloak.v3, React) translates messages with i18next. Every other key in this file uses `{{0}}`, `{{1}}` placeholders. The user-profile error handler passes server params as `{0: ..., 1: ..., 2: ...}` and calls `t(key, params)`. This change switches `error-invalid-multivalued-size` to Java MessageFormat (`{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}`) and adds a ChoiceFormat sub-pattern, which i18next supports in neither case. Users who violate a multivalued attribute's size constraint will see the raw string `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` instead of a formatted message. Keep `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` here, or use i18next pluralization.

title: Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax breaks i18next interpolation in the admin console
body: The admin console (keycloak.v2) renders server-side user-profile validation errors client-side via i18next (`setUserProfileServerError` → `t(errorMessage, {0:..,1:..,2:..})`), which expects `{{n}}` placeholders. The previous value used `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}`. The new value uses `{0}` and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`, so i18next leaves them unreplaced. Admins will see the literal pattern text when a multivalued attribute size validation fails.

title: Lithuanian file now contains an Italian sentence
body: `totpStep1` was replaced with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is the Italian translation (apparently copied from messages_it). Lithuanian users will see Italian text in the OTP setup step. It should be a Lithuanian sentence such as `Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame telefone:`.

title: Lithuanian login file now contains an Italian sentence
body: `loginTotpStep1` was replaced with the Italian text `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. Lithuanian users configuring OTP on the login page will see an Italian instruction. The original Lithuanian content should have been rewritten in Lithuanian rather than replaced by another locale's string.

title: Traditional Chinese text placed in the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) bundle
body: The new `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional characters (手機, 安裝, 應用程式) and was likely copied from zh_TW. The rest of this zh_CN file uses Simplified Chinese, e.g. `mobile=手机` on the line above. It should be the Simplified form, e.g. `在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`.

title: Common prefix/suffix computation can overlap and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body:
The suffix loop only bounds `end` by the string lengths, not by `length - start`. So the common prefix and suffix can overlap in the shorter string. Example: value `

a

`, sanitizer output `

a

`. Here `start` = 8 and `end` = 4, so `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` becomes `substring(8, 4)` and throws. Duplicated closing tags are exactly the kind of malformed input this verifier should report. Instead the plugin crashes with an unhandled runtime exception and no useful message. Bound the suffix loop with `end < Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`.

title: ChoiceFormat contents are removed before sanitizing, so HTML inside them is never checked
body: For `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*` and `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, every `{n,choice,...}` block is replaced with `...` before the sanitizer runs, for both the translation and the English value. A translation such as `{0,choice,0#|1#x}` would pass verification untouched. These are server-rendered messages in email and login themes, so this defeats the purpose of the check for those keys. Split each choice alternative and sanitize it individually, or only strip the `n<`/`n#` selector syntax, instead of discarding the whole block.

title: Anchor-mismatch message omits file and key
body: `Didn't find anchor tag <a ...> in original string` contains neither the key nor the file path, unlike the duplicate-key and illegal-HTML messages. When the plugin runs over hundreds of property files in the build, a maintainer cannot tell which file or key to fix. Include `key` and `file` in the message; `key` is already passed into `santizeAnchors` but unused.

title: Missing English counterpart aborts the build with a raw RuntimeException
body: The English file path is derived by string replacement on the absolute path. If that file does not exist (a new theme/locale layout, a path whose naming doesn't match the regex, or a file outside the expected directories), `verifySafeHtml` throws an unchecked `RuntimeException`. `verify()` only catches `IOException`, so the exception is not converted to a `MojoExecutionException`. The Maven build fails with a stack trace instead of a reported verification problem.

title: No test that a valid translation produces no findings
body:
All new tests only assert that some error message is present (`hasItem(...)`). Nothing verifies that a legitimate translation passes cleanly: identical anchors, allowed `/

/
` tags when the English source has HTML, `{{0}}` placeholders, choice formats, or `<0>` numeric tags. A verifier that flags everything would pass this suite, and false positives that break the build on valid translations would go unnoticed.

title: Session type is wrong for the first access token issued with offline_access
body:
The session type is taken from `userSession.isOffline()`. In the code-to-token and password grants with `scope=offline_access`, the access token is created from the online user session before `generateRefreshToken()` creates the offline session.

As a result, that access token is encoded as `on` (online). Right afterwards the online session is removed: always in `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType`, and when `FIRST_OFFLINE_ACCESS` is set in `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`. The token then advertises an online session that no longer exists; the session survives only as offline.

The stated purpose is to look up only the encoded session type (#37662). Any such consumer would fail to find the session and reject a valid token. Use `clientSessionContext.isOfflineTokenRequested()` (or equivalent) to decide between offline and online.

title: Grant type only recorded for grants that go through createTokenResponse; client_credentials (and UMA) end up as 'na'
body:
`Constants.GRANT_TYPE` is set on the client session context only in `createTokenResponse`, plus explicitly in ROPC, pre-authorized code, refresh and standard token exchange.

`ClientCredentialsGrantType` builds its response via `tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` without calling `createTokenResponse`, and this PR does not change it. The permission (UMA) grant also does not use `createTokenResponse`.

Tokens from these grants are therefore encoded with the unknown grant `na`, even though shortcuts `cc` and `pg` were added to their factories. This silently defeats the feature for the client-credentials case. No test catches it, because `expectClientLogin` does not check `TOKEN_ID`.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher never verifies the grant type (inverted condition and wrong offset)
body:
The encoded prefix is 2 chars of session type, 2 of token type and 2 of grant type, so the grant is at indices 4-6. The matcher reads `substring(3, 5)` instead (e.g. `"ta"` for `onrtac`), which can never equal a grant shortcut.

On top of that, the condition is inverted: it returns `false` when the shortcut *matches*. The net effect is that the matcher accepts any grant type as long as the suffix is a UUID.

All updated `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` assertions are therefore vacuous with respect to grant type. The check should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` plus a length check on `items[0]`.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant type factories at startup
body:
`getShortcut()` is added to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` without a default implementation.

Any custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` compiled against the previous SPI will throw `AbstractMethodError` when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `gtf.getShortcut()`, which prevents server startup. A custom implementation returning `null` would instead cause an NPE from `ConcurrentHashMap.put`.

Consider a default implementation (or a fallback to `na`) and handling of null shortcuts instead of failing boot.

title: Javadoc recommends 3-letter shortcuts, but encoding/decoding requires exactly 2 characters with no validation
body:
The Javadoc says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters". However, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` hard-codes a 6-character prefix and takes characters 4-6 as the grant shortcut.

A custom grant that follows the doc and returns a 3-letter shortcut will produce token ids (e.g. `onrtabc:...`) that the same provider cannot decode; it throws "Expected length of 6".

Neither `postInit` nor the lazy refresh paths in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` validate shortcut length. The doc should say exactly 2 characters, and the factory should reject other lengths.

title: Copy-paste: null check for rawTokenId validates grantType instead
body:
The line meant to enforce non-null `rawTokenId` is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`. It re-checks `grantType`, so a null `rawTokenId` is accepted silently.

`encodeTokenId` would then produce an id ending in `:null`. It should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of an NPE, not the intended validation
body:
In this test the factory's `sessionFactory` is null. For the unknown shortcut `ac`, `getGrantTypeByShortcut` falls into the refresh branch and calls `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)`, which throws `NullPointerException`.

The test catches any `RuntimeException`, so it passes without ever reaching the `IllegalArgumentException("... Unknown value 'ac' for grant type")` path. It should assert on `IllegalArgumentException` and set up a (mock) session factory.

title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed from SPI class
body:
The public `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context)` copy constructor is deleted rather than updated to copy the new `grantType` field.

Custom grant implementations or wrappers that used it to derive or modify a context will fail to compile or link. This removal is unrelated to the feature, which only needed the new field copied. Keep the constructor and copy `grantType` in it.

title: Lazy map refresh can silently overwrite existing shortcut mappings
body:
`postInit` detects duplicate shortcuts by comparing map sizes. The lazy refresh in `getShortcutByGrantType` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut` instead blindly `put`s into both maps.

A newly deployed grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one would overwrite the mapping in `grantsByShortcuts`. Previously issued tokens would then decode to the wrong grant type, and the two maps would become inconsistent. The two maps are also updated non-atomically.

The refresh paths should apply the same collision and length validation, e.g. via `putIfAbsent` and rejecting conflicts.

title: Access token jti is no longer a UUID
body:
The access token `jti` changes from a 36-char UUID to a prefixed form, e.g. `onrtac:<uuid>`, 43 chars containing `:`.

Resource servers or integrations that parse or validate `jti` as a UUID, or store it in fixed-length/UUID-typed columns for replay detection, will break after upgrade. This externally visible format change is not documented in upgrade/migration notes in this PR.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher never checks the grant type (wrong offsets and inverted condition)
body:
The grant shortcut sits at characters 4–5 of the prefix (e.g. `onrtac`), but `items[0].substring(3, 5)` takes characters 3–4. For `onrtac` that yields `ta`.

The condition is also inverted: it returns `false` when the extracted value equals the expected shortcut.

The two bugs cancel out. `substring(3,5)` never equals a real grant shortcut, so the early return never fires and the matcher only checks that the suffix is a UUID. `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` therefore pass for any grant shortcut, including `na`.

If only the offsets were fixed, every correct token would fail. A prefix shorter than 5 characters also throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of a clean mismatch.

Fix: `return items[0].length() == 6 && items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut) && isUUID().matches(items[1]);`

title: rawTokenId null check validates grantType instead
body:
The fourth check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`. It re-checks `grantType`, so a null `rawTokenId` is never rejected.

An `AccessTokenContext` with a null raw ID can be built. `encodeTokenId` would then silently produce an ID like `onrtac:null` instead of failing fast. It should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant type factories and can block server startup
body:
`getShortcut()` is added to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` as an abstract method with no default. The OAuth2GrantType SPI exists so that custom grants can be deployed.

Custom factories compiled against the previous SPI will fail when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on every registered grant factory. They will throw `AbstractMethodError` during server startup, preventing Keycloak from booting.

A custom factory that returns `null` causes a `NullPointerException` from `ConcurrentHashMap.put` in the same `postInit`.

Provide a default implementation (or a fallback when the shortcut is missing or invalid). Encoding should degrade to the unknown grant (`na`) instead of failing startup or token issuance.

title: Javadoc says shortcut is ~3 letters, but the encoding requires exactly 2 characters and nothing validates it
body:
The javadoc tells implementers the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters". `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires the encoded prefix to be exactly 6 characters, 2 per field, and throws `IllegalArgumentException` otherwise.

Neither `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` nor the lazy refresh in `getShortcutByGrantType` validates shortcut length. A custom grant that follows the documentation will issue access tokens whose IDs cannot be decoded. Any later consumer of `getTokenContextFromTokenId` (introspection, userinfo, token exchange, as planned) would then fail for those tokens.

Fix the javadoc to require exactly 2 characters and validate length (and non-null) when registering shortcuts.

title: Client credentials (and other flows) never set the GRANT_TYPE attribute, so their tokens encode grant as 'na'
body:
The grant type is only put into the `ClientSessionContext` in these places:
- `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`
- ROPC
- refresh
- PreAuthorizedCode
- `StandardTokenExchangeProvider`

`ClientCredentialsGrantType` builds its response with `tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` directly and does not call `createTokenResponse`. Its access tokens are therefore encoded as `...na:<uuid>` rather than `...cc:<uuid>`, even though the `cc` shortcut is registered here. The unit test's `trltcc` example implies `cc` is expected.

The same applies to UMA/permission grant tokens (`pg`) and the legacy V1 token-exchange providers. This undermines the stated purpose of letting endpoints rely on the encoded grant type.

Set `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` in these code paths too.

title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of a NullPointerException, not the intended validation
body:
The factory is built without `postInit`, so `sessionFactory` is null. When `ac` is not found in `grantsByShortcuts`, `getGrantTypeByShortcut` falls into the refresh branch and calls `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)`, which throws `NullPointerException`.

The test catches any `RuntimeException`, so it passes without ever reaching the `IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value ... for grant type")` path it is meant to verify.

Catch `IllegalArgumentException` specifically, and stub or mock the session factory so the unknown-shortcut path is actually exercised.

title: Public Context copy constructor removed from SPI class
body:
`public Context(Context context)` was deleted from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. This change is unrelated to the feature. Any extension that wraps or copies the grant context (e.g. custom grant types delegating to another grant) will no longer compile or link.

If removal is intended, it should be called out as a breaking change. Otherwise keep the constructor and copy the new `grantType` field in it.

title: grantType derived once in constructor and not updated by setFormParams
body:
`grantType` is computed from `formParams` only in the constructor. `setFormParams(...)` replaces `formParams` but leaves `grantType` unchanged.

Any caller that swaps the form parameters gets a `getGrantType()` value that no longer matches them. That stale value is what `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` and ROPC write into the client session context and encode into the token ID.

Either update `grantType` in `setFormParams` or derive it lazily from the current `formParams`.

title: Lazy refresh can silently overwrite an existing shortcut mapping
body:
The duplicate-shortcut validation runs only in `postInit`. When a grant type is hot-deployed later, `getShortcutByGrantType` (and `getGrantTypeByShortcut`) does `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` without checking whether that shortcut already belongs to another grant.

A colliding shortcut replaces the existing mapping. Tokens previously issued for the original grant would then decode to the wrong grant type.

Use `putIfAbsent` and reject or log the conflict, applying the same uniqueness check as in `postInit`.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher never checks the grant shortcut (inverted condition, wrong offset)
body:
The grant shortcut is the last 2 characters of the 6-character prefix, at `substring(4, 6)`. The matcher reads `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, which for `onrtac` is `ta`. It also returns `false` when the value *equals* the expected shortcut, so the condition is inverted.

With the current offset the comparison never matches, so the check is a no-op and the matcher passes any `xxxxxx:<uuid>` ID. If someone fixes only the offset, every correct token will fail.

As a result, `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` do not verify that the right grant type is encoded. A grant that wrongly encodes `na` would go unnoticed. A prefix shorter than 5 characters would also throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of failing the match.

Fix: use `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` and also check the prefix length. The comment about the "4th char" is wrong as well.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant type factories and can block server startup
body:
`getShortcut()` is added to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with no default implementation. Custom grant types built on this SPI will no longer compile.

The runtime impact is worse. A custom factory compiled against the old SPI will throw `AbstractMethodError` when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `gtf.getShortcut()` for every registered grant factory. That exception aborts `postInit` and prevents Keycloak from starting.

A factory that returns `null` causes `ConcurrentHashMap.put(null, ...)` to throw NPE in the same place.

Fix: provide a default method, e.g. one returning `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.UNKNOWN`. Alternatively, have the encoder tolerate missing or null shortcuts by mapping them to unknown instead of failing startup.

title: Javadoc says 'usually 3-letter' shortcut, but the default encoder requires exactly 2 characters
body:
The contract tells implementers the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters". `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` assumes every shortcut is exactly 2 characters: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects any prefix whose length is not 6 and slices fixed 2-character segments.

Nothing validates shortcut length at registration in `postInit`, and `encodeTokenId` does not check it either. A custom grant that follows the Javadoc and returns a 3-letter shortcut will issue access tokens (`onrtabc:...`) that the same provider cannot decode; it throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

Fix: document that the shortcut must be exactly 2 characters, and validate the length in `postInit` and in the refresh paths.

title: Client credentials (and UMA) grants never set the GRANT_TYPE attribute, so their tokens are encoded as 'na'
body:
The grant type is put into the `ClientSessionContext` in only a few places: `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`, ROPC, PreAuthorizedCode, refresh and standard token exchange.

`ClientCredentialsGrantType` is not modified. It builds its response directly with `tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` rather than through `createTokenResponse`, so `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` is never set. Every client-credentials access token is therefore encoded with grant shortcut `na`, even though the `cc` shortcut is defined here and the unit test uses `trltcc` as an example.

The UMA permission grant (`pg`) and legacy/V1 token exchange flows have the same problem.

Future consumers (#37117, introspection optimizations) will get wrong context for these tokens. The broken `isAccessTokenId` matcher, and the fact that `expectClientLogin` does not assert `TOKEN_ID`, mean no test catches this.

Fix: set `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())` in `ClientCredentialsGrantType`, and likewise for the other flows that bypass `createTokenResponse`.

title: Copy-paste error: rawTokenId null-check validates grantType instead
body:
`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` checks `grantType` a second time. `rawTokenId` is never validated, so a null raw ID is accepted silently, and `encodeTokenId` then produces an ID like `onrtac:null`.

Fix: it should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

title: testIncorrectGrantType passes only because of an NPE from the null sessionFactory
body:
The test factory never calls `postInit`, so `sessionFactory` is null. Decoding `ofrtac:5678` misses `ac` in `grantsByShortcuts`, and `getGrantTypeByShortcut` then calls `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)`, which throws `NullPointerException`.

The test catches any `RuntimeException`, so it passes without ever reaching the intended `IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value 'ac' for grant type")` branch.

Fix: supply a stub `KeycloakSessionFactory` that returns no factories, and assert specifically on `IllegalArgumentException`.

title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed; grantType captured once and not refreshed by setFormParams
body:
The public `Context(Context)` copy constructor is deleted from this public SPI class without any mention in the description. Extensions that wrap or clone a grant context will no longer compile.

Separately, `grantType` is read from `formParams` only in the constructor. `setFormParams(...)` replaces the form parameters but leaves `grantType` stale, so `getGrantType()` can disagree with `getFormParams()`.

Fix: either keep the copy constructor (copying `grantType`), or document the removal. Also either derive `grantType` lazily or update it in `setFormParams`.

title: Access token `jti` format change is user-visible but undocumented
body:
The access token `jti`, and the `token_id` detail on events such as `CODE_TO_TOKEN` and `REFRESH_TOKEN`, change from a plain UUID to `xxxxxx:<uuid>`, which is 43 characters and contains a colon.

Resource servers, event listeners and audit pipelines that validate or store `jti` as a UUID, or in a 36-character column, will break after upgrade.

The PR adds no upgrade or release note for this observable contract change. One should be added.

title: Exhausted user-storage recovery codes are 'removed' from the wrong store; null id can crash the login
body:
`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` can now return a credential that came from the user storage provider (`getFederatedCredentialsStream`). When that credential reports `allCodesUsed()`, the authenticator still calls `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. For a non-local user this targets Keycloak's federated JPA credential store, not the user storage provider, so the exhausted credential is never removed where it actually lives.

It can also fail outright. The reference provider in this PR returns a model built with `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)`, which has no id, and `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials` does not copy the stored id. The result is `removeStoredCredentialById(null)`, which reaches `em.find(FederatedUserCredentialEntity.class, null, ...)` and throws `IllegalArgumentException`. The user would get an error page when signing in with their last recovery code.

Fix: when the credential is federated, remove or disable it through the storage provider (e.g. `disableCredentialType`), or skip the local removal and rely only on the required action.

title: Login page throws NoSuchElementException for storages that validate recovery codes but don't override getCredentials
body:
With this PR a user storage provider can own the recovery-codes credential: it gets `updateCredential`, and `isConfiguredFor`/`isValid` are routed to it. The login page bean still calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` unconditionally.

`CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials` defaults to `Stream.empty()`. A provider that implements `supportsCredentialType`/`isConfiguredFor`/`isValid`/`updateCredential` for `recovery-authn-codes` but not `getCredentials` therefore gets an empty Optional here (there is no local credential either). The recovery-code form then fails with `NoSuchElementException` (HTTP 500) every time it is rendered.

Even when `getCredentials` is implemented, the provider must return a credential in Keycloak's internal hashed `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` JSON format, while it receives the codes as a raw JSON array of strings. This contract is undocumented.

Fix: handle the absent case gracefully, and document the contract or derive the next code number differently.

title: Regenerating codes into user storage leaves previously stored local recovery codes valid
body:
The previous code called `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential`, which deletes any existing recovery-codes credential before storing the new one. When the user storage accepts the new codes (`userStorageCreated == true`), this branch only logs and never removes an existing locally stored credential.

Before this change, federated users' recovery codes were always kept in Keycloak's local/federated credential store. After upgrading to a storage provider that supports `recovery-authn-codes`, a user who regenerates codes will still have the old local credential. `UserCredentialManager.isValid` falls back to the local `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider` when the storage rejects an input, so the old, supposedly replaced codes can still be used to authenticate.

Fix: remove any stored `recovery-authn-codes` credential when the codes are successfully saved in user storage.

title: getCredentials dereferences myUser without null check
body:
`getCredentials` calls `getMyUser(user)` and immediately accesses `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp`. Every other method in this provider (`isConfiguredFor`, `isValid`, `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`) guards against `myUser == null`.

`getCredentials` is now reached via `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` from the recovery-code login bean and authenticator. A user unknown to the in-memory map (e.g. removed from the map but still cached) would cause an NPE instead of an empty stream.

title: New test only covers the happy path; single-use and wrong-code behaviour are untested
Old local recovery codes stay valid after regenerating into user storage
body:
Before this change, regenerating recovery codes went through `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential`, which deletes any existing recovery-codes credential before storing the new one. Regeneration therefore revoked the old codes.

Now, when `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` returns true because the user storage accepted the codes, the local path is skipped. Any recovery-codes credential already stored locally for that user is left in place. This happens for users who set up codes before their provider supported the type, or while it was disabled.

`UserCredentialManager.isValid` falls back to local `CredentialInputValidator` providers when the user storage rejects an input. So the stale local codes are still accepted at login. A user who regenerates codes because the old ones leaked would still be able to log in with the leaked codes.

Fix: remove any locally stored `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` credentials when the user storage takes ownership.

title: Exhausted federated recovery codes are never removed
body:
`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` can now return a credential that lives in the user storage provider. When that credential reports `allCodesUsed()`, the code calls `removeStoredCredentialById(id)`. That method only deletes from Keycloak's own DB (local or federated-storage tables), so it cannot remove the credential held by the user storage provider.

The call is a silent no-op, or it fails if the provider-built model has a null id. For example, `createFromValues` does not set an id, and `em.find(..., null)` throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

The exhausted credential then stays in the user storage, and `isConfiguredFor` keeps returning true. If the user does not finish the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action, the next login shows the recovery-code form again. `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` then calls `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()` on an empty Optional and the page errors out.

Fix: use `disableCredentialType` or similar for federated credentials, and guard against a null id.

title: Unchecked Optional.get() crashes the login form when the federated provider does not expose credentials
body:
Previously, `configuredFor` returning true implied a locally stored credential existed. Now `configuredFor` and `isValid` can be satisfied by a user storage provider through `supportsCredentialType`, `updateCredential`, `isValid` and `isConfiguredFor`.

The credential is read back only via `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials`. That is a default method returning an empty stream, and the classic credential SPI does not require providers to override it. For such a provider, `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` returns an empty Optional.

`credentialModelOpt.get()` then throws `NoSuchElementException` while rendering the recovery-code login page, so the user cannot log in with recovery codes. Separately, the authenticator sees `recoveryCodeCredentialModel == null` and adds CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES after every successful recovery-code login.

Fix: handle the empty case explicitly, or document and enforce the requirement to implement `getCredentials`.

title: Undocumented, asymmetric storage format for federated recovery codes
body:
The read and write sides of the new user-storage contract use different formats, and neither is documented.

Write side: the user storage receives a `UserCredentialModel` whose challenge response is a JSON array of plaintext codes. The user label and generatedAt timestamp are dropped.

Read side: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` feeds whatever `getCredentials` returns into `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel`. That method requires Keycloak's internal credentialData/secretData layout with hashed codes and used flags, and throws a `RuntimeException` on parse failure.

A provider that returns the credential it was given, as the test provider does for OTP, breaks the authenticator and login form. The test provider only works because it manually rebuilds the internal model via `createFromValues`. This contract should be documented, or the read side should tolerate the format that was written.

title: Test storage never consumes codes, leaving federated single-use and exhaustion paths untested
body:
The test provider's `isValid` accepts any code in the stored list, whichever code number the form asked for. It also never marks codes as used, and `getCredentials` rebuilds a fresh model every time, so the next code is always #0.

As a result, `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` only checks one happy-path login. It would still pass if the wrong code were accepted or codes could be reused.

The new federated-specific paths in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` have no coverage:
- the all-codes-used removal
- required-action re-adding
- fallback when the provider exposes no credential
- regenerating when local codes already exist

title: Old local recovery codes stay valid when new codes are stored in user storage
body:
Before this change, `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential` always ran, and it deletes the user's existing stored recovery-codes credential before creating the new one. Now, when `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` returns true (the codes went to user storage), the local provider is skipped, so any previously stored local recovery-codes credential is never deleted.

`UserCredentialManager.isValid` checks the user-storage validator first and then falls through to the local `CredentialInputValidator`s. So a code the user entered that fails in user storage is then checked against the stale local codes and is accepted.

Result: after a user regenerates recovery codes (for example after an upgrade where the provider starts accepting this type, or after a provider config change), the old codes that were supposed to be replaced can still be used to log in. The user-storage branch should also remove any existing local recovery-codes credential.

title: All-codes-used cleanup targets the local store even when the credential came from user storage
body:
`optUserCredentialFound` now comes from `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`, which prefers credentials returned by the user storage provider (`getFederatedCredentialsStream`). When `allCodesUsed()` is true, the code still calls `credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(id)`. That only touches Keycloak's local/federated JPA credential store, never the user storage provider.

For a provider-supplied credential this has two failure modes:
- If the id belongs to the provider, the call is a silent no-op. The exhausted credential stays, and `isConfiguredFor` keeps returning true.
- If the provider returns a model without an id, the call receives null. `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues` leaves the id unset, and the test provider's `getCredentials` does exactly this. With a null id, `em.find(..., null)` in the JPA store throws `IllegalArgumentException`, so the login fails with a 500.

For federated credentials the code should take a different path, such as `disableCredentialType(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)` or no removal at all.

title: Test provider accepts any of the codes and never consumes them, so single-use is untested
body:
`isValid` for recovery codes returns true if the input matches any stored code. It never marks the code as used and does not check that it is the code the login form asked for (`getNextRecoveryAuthnCode`).

The new `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` therefore only checks that some valid code is accepted once. It would still pass if:
- the wrong code number were entered,
- a code could be reused,
- the next login asked for the same code again.

The core recovery-code contract (single-use, sequential) is not exercised at all for the user-storage path.

title: Changing the "4.8.3-compatible" provider alters what existing OTP backward-compat tests cover
body:
The class Javadoc says this provider mimics a Keycloak 4.8.3 implementation and should not need changes for newer versions. This PR adds the newer `getCredentials` API and gives OTP credentials a generated id (`newOTP.setId(...)`).

As a result, the existing OTP tests no longer run against an old-style provider. For example, `testOTPSetupAndRemoveThroughAccountMgmtAndLogin` (issue 19575) used to get the placeholder `otp-id` from the account REST endpoint (`CredentialHelper.createUserStorageCredentialRepresentation`). It will now receive the real OTP credential with a UUID from `getFederatedCredentialsStream`.

The legacy placeholder path that these tests were written to protect loses coverage. The recovery-code support would be better placed in a separate, modern test provider.

title: Paginated getSubGroupsStream overloads still NPE when the group is deleted concurrently
body:
The PR null-guards `modelSupplier.get()` in `getSubGroupsCount()`, but three sibling methods do the same unguarded dereference:

- `getSubGroupsStream(search, first, max)` at line 256
- `getSubGroupsStream(first, max)` at line 262
- `getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, first, max)` at line 268

Each calls `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)`. In the same race the PR fixes (cached group still visible, row already deleted in the DB), `getGroupById` returns null. These methods then throw an NPE, which surfaces as a 500 on the admin subgroup and group-hierarchy endpoints. The fix should cover these paths too, e.g. by returning `Stream.empty()` when the delegate is null.

title: Reader thread is never joined, so exceptions can be missed and the thread leaks
body:
After `deletedAll.set(true)` the test asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty right away, without joining the reader thread.

- A request that was in flight during the final deletions can fail and append to the list after the assertion has run. That is exactly the window where the NPE race occurs, so the regression can go undetected and the test can pass while the bug is present.
