Unlike passwords, which are hashed one-way, backup codes act as long-lived authentication secrets (similar to passwords) and should be hashed (e.g. bcrypt/argon2) rather than symmetrically encrypted. If the encryption key and database are both compromised, all users' backup codes can be recovered in plaintext, allowing full account takeover bypassing 2FA. This is a weaker security posture than expected for a credential of this type.

title: Dismissing the dialog on the backup-codes screen leaves UI state out of sync with the server
body: After the TOTP is verified, the server has already enabled 2FA (handleEnable sets step to SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes without calling onEnable()). The onEnable() callback that informs the parent component that 2FA is enabled is now only invoked when the user explicitly clicks the 'Close' button (data-testid="backup-codes-close", lines 261-272). If the user dismisses the dialog any other way (Escape key, clicking the overlay, navigating away and back, etc. via the Dialog's onOpenChange), onEnable() is never called and resetState() never runs, so the parent's UI (e.g. the two-factor switch) can remain stale/unchecked even though 2FA is actually enabled server-side. Previously, onEnable() fired immediately on successful verification, so this inconsistency window did not exist.

title: No e2e coverage for logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
body: The PR's stated purpose is to enable backup codes for 2FA login and disable flows, but the added test only exercises the download/copy/close UI actions on the backup-codes screen during setup (lines 110-125). There is no test that actually submits a backup code via the 'Lost access' flow on the login page or the disable-2FA modal, which is the core new functionality described in the PR (and explicitly called out as missing via the 'TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup' comment at line 12). This leaves the primary new feature (backup code authentication) completely untested.

title: backupCodes state is implicitly typed as never[], losing type safety
body: `const [backupCodes, setBackupCodes] = useState([]);` has no generic type argument, so TypeScript infers backupCodes as `never[]`. Although `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` compiles because `body` comes from an untyped `response.json()` (effectively `any`), subsequent usages such as `backupCodes.map((code) => ...)` and `formatBackupCode(code)` lose type checking on `code`, which should be `string`. This removes compile-time protection against passing the wrong shape and can mask bugs if the API response shape changes.

title: Backup codes Blob URL is never revoked when the modal is closed/unmounted
body: `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` is only revoked the next time `handleSetup` succeeds (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);`, line 98). If the user never re-runs setup (e.g., completes 2FA setup once and later reopens/cancels the modal, or navigates away), the created object URL is never revoked, causing a memory leak that persists until the page is reloaded.

title: Unsafe destructure of destinationCalendar causes TypeError when array is empty
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` on the next line. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is an empty array (no connected calendar for any host, which is a common and valid scenario), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`, and accessing `.integration` on it throws a TypeError whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. The previous code used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`) which safely handled the missing-calendar case and fell back to Cal Video. This regression will crash booking creation for any user who selects Google Meet as location but has no destination calendar connected.

title: updateEvent/deleteEvent calendarId resolution is broken when externalCalendarId is falsy
body: In `updateEvent` (and the identical pattern in `deleteEvent` at line ~315), the fallback is: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (undefined/null), this predicate compares each `cal.externalId` to the same falsy `externalCalendarId` value, which will basically never be true for any real calendar entry, so `.find()` returns `undefined` and `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` end up `undefined`. The previous code simply fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, which correctly picked a default calendar. Now, any update or delete call made without an externalCalendarId (e.g. legacy bookings or calendar references lacking it) will be issued with `calendarId: undefined`, which will fail against the Google Calendar API or silently target the wrong calendar. This affects reschedule and cancellation flows broadly, not just the multi-host scenario the PR targets.

title: Lark/Office365/CalDAV calendar services always use the first destinationCalendar entry regardless of the credential being processed
body: `createEvent`, `createAttendees`, `updateEvent`, and `deleteEvent` all do `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and use that single entry as the calendar id, ignoring which specific host/credential each CalendarService instance represents. Unlike GoogleCalendarService (which was updated to match `destinationCalendar` entries by `credentialId`), Lark, Office365 (`packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, line 73) and the generic CalDAV `BaseCalendarService` (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts`, lines 156 and 509) were not updated the same way. In a collective event with multiple hosts using these calendar providers, the event will always be created/updated/deleted against the first host's calendar, even when processing the second (or later) host's credential — defeating the stated purpose of this PR for every non-Google calendar integration.

title: destinationCalendar defaults to null, silently dropping team members' calendars for collective events
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized as `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [...] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [...] : null` — note the `null` fallback instead of `[]`. Immediately after, for collective events the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If the organizer has no personal destination calendar and the event type has none either, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, so the optional-chained `.push(...)` becomes a no-op and all team members' destination calendars collected in `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded. This directly undermines the PR's goal of inviting every host with a calendar app to the event, specifically in the case where the organizer (first host) has no destination calendar configured but other hosts do.

title: Inconsistent destinationCalendar fallback values (null vs []) across the codebase
body: `handleNewBooking.ts` falls back to `null` when no destination calendar is available, whereas essentially every other call site touched by this PR (`handleCancelBooking.ts`, `confirm.handler.ts`, `editLocation.handler.ts`, `webhook.ts`, `paypal-webhook.ts`, `requestReschedule.handler.ts`, `deleteCredential.handler.ts`) falls back to `[]`. Since `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` is typed as `DestinationCalendar[] | null`, both are technically valid, but the inconsistency means downstream code and tests must handle two different 'empty' representations for the same conceptual state, increasing the risk of bugs like the `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` no-op described separately, and making behavior harder to reason about/test consistently.

title: No automated tests added for the core multi-destinationCalendar feature
body: The PR description explicitly checks 'I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works'. The only test changes are a cosmetic update to `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts` changing an expected payload field from `null` to `[]`, which does not exercise the actual multi-host/multi-destinationCalendar logic (array iteration in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`/`updateAllCalendarEvents`, per-credential calendar matching in `GoogleCalendarService`, or the collective-event team calendar collection in `handleNewBooking.ts`). Given the extent and risk of the refactor (converting a singular field to an array across ~20 files), the lack of unit/integration coverage for the new array-handling paths is a significant gap that should block merging until at least basic coverage is added.

title: Unguarded access to destructured destinationCalendar causes TypeError
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` (no optional chaining) will throw a TypeError whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is empty/undefined (a very common case – e.g. no connected calendar) and the location is Google Meet. The previous code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which was safe. This regression will crash booking creation whenever Google Meet is selected as the location and there is no destination calendar set, instead of correctly falling back to Cal Video.

title: Broken calendarId fallback logic in updateEvent
body: `selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` – the fallback branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, yet it still searches `destinationCalendar` for an entry whose `externalId` equals that same falsy value, which will essentially never match. Previously the fallback correctly used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (the main calendar). Now `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` whenever no externalCalendarId is supplied (e.g. legacy bookings without a stored externalCalendarId), and `calendar.events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined`, which will fail against the Google API.

title: Broken calendarId fallback logic in deleteEvent defaults to 'primary'
body: Same faulty pattern as updateEvent: `calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` always resolves to `undefined` when `externalCalendarId` isn't supplied, so `calendarId ? calendarId : defaultCalendarId` falls back to `"primary"` instead of the correct destination calendar. This can cause deleteEvent to delete (or attempt to delete) an event from the wrong calendar (the user's primary calendar) instead of the actual destination calendar, leaving the real event un-cancelled – a data-integrity risk for cancellations/reschedules of bookings lacking a stored externalCalendarId.

title: Team destination calendars silently dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null
body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` is a no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (which happens whenever neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set). In that scenario, for a COLLECTIVE event, the collected `teamDestinationCalendars` for the other hosts are silently discarded and never pushed into `evt.destinationCalendar`, meaning other hosts' calendars will not receive the event — defeating the primary purpose of this PR (handling collective events with multiple hosts).

title: Office365/Lark/CalDAV calendar services ignore credentialId and always use first destinationCalendar entry
body: Unlike googlecalendar's createEvent, which now selects the correct calendar via `destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`, Office365 (and similarly Lark and the base CalDAV service) continue to use only `[mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` (the first array entry) regardless of which credential/host is currently being processed by EventManager's per-destination loop. As a result, when a collective event has hosts using Office365/Lark/CalDAV calendars, the event will be repeatedly created against the *same* (first) host's calendar instead of each host's own calendar, so the multi-host destination-calendar fix only actually works for Google Calendar.

title: Inverted conditional logic for organization slug assignment, unrelated to stated PR scope
body: The condition for setting `slug` on org creation was flipped: originally `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` (slug set when team billing is disabled) is now `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` (slug set when team billing is enabled). This behavior change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (destinationCalendar array handling) and appears to be an accidental regression that changes when an organization's slug is persisted at creation time.

title: Dynamic-user lookup no longer selects organization slug
body: In the refactored `loadUsers`, the `prisma.user.findMany` query for the dynamic-booking (`!eventTypeId`) branch no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`, which was present before this change. If any downstream code (e.g. building dynamic group booking URLs, org-aware redirects) relies on `user.organization.slug` for these users, it will now be `undefined`, silently breaking organization-aware behavior for dynamic group bookings.

title: Inconsistent and incomplete test coverage for destinationCalendar shape change
body: Only the BOOKING_REJECTED test was updated to expect `destinationCalendar: []` while BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED tests (lines 119 and 373) still assert `destinationCalendar: null`. This reflects a real inconsistency in the codebase (some code paths emit `null`, others emit `[]`) but no test actually exercises the PR's stated goal — a collective event with multiple hosts receiving correctly populated destinationCalendar arrays. The PR explicitly acknowledges no tests were added for the core fix.

title: References built from result.externalId/credentialId lose fallback to evt.destinationCalendar for video-only results
body: `referencesToCreate` now uses `isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined` and `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` instead of previously falling back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`/`credentialId` for non-calendar (video) results. Since `destinationCalendar` is now an array, the previous single-value fallback was removed entirely rather than adapted (e.g. to the first entry), silently dropping any externalCalendarId/credentialId info for video event references which previously could inherit it from the destination calendar.

title: Unguarded access to mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration can throw when destinationCalendar is empty
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null/undefined/empty. The very next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining: `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. Any booking using Google Meet location where the organizer/eventType has no destination calendar configured (a legitimate, common case) will throw a TypeError ("Cannot read properties of undefined") and crash booking creation. Previously this used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`), so this is a regression introduced by the array migration.

title: Broken calendarId fallback logic in updateEvent after destinationCalendar array migration
body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined/empty string, which is a common case when the stored booking reference has no externalCalendarId), the fallback branch searches destinationCalendar entries for one whose `externalId` equals that same falsy value, which will essentially never match a real calendar id. As a result `selectedCalendar` resolves to `undefined` and is passed as `calendarId` to `calendar.events.update(...)`, which will fail or behave unexpectedly. Previously this simply used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` as a sane fallback; the new logic is a functional regression for all update calls lacking an explicit externalCalendarId.

title: Same broken calendarId fallback logic in deleteEvent
body: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` has the identical defect as in updateEvent: when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, it searches for a destinationCalendar whose externalId equals that same falsy value, which will not match. The code happens to fall back to `defaultCalendarId` ("primary") afterward, but this means any destination calendar other than primary will not be targeted for deletion when no explicit externalCalendarId is passed, silently deleting from the wrong calendar (or failing to delete the actual event).

title: Team members' destination calendars are silently dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` uses optional chaining. If neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` are set, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, so the `?.push` call is a no-op and all collected `teamDestinationCalendars` (the whole point of this PR — inviting other hosts' calendars) are discarded. For a COLLECTIVE event where the organizer doesn't have a destination calendar configured but team members do, none of the hosts will get calendar invites, defeating the stated purpose of the PR.

title: Dynamic user lookup lost `organization.slug` selection during loadUsers refactor
body: The refactored `loadUsers` function for the dynamic-booking branch (`!eventTypeId`) selects `{...userSelect.select, credentials: true, metadata: true}` but drops the previously-selected `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` field that existed before this PR. Any downstream code relying on `user.organization.slug` for dynamic/organization-aware bookings will now receive `undefined`, which can cause incorrect behavior or runtime errors later in the booking flow.

title: Silent failure when calendar credential cannot be resolved for a destination calendar
body: In `createAllCalendarEvents`, when a `destination.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found in `this.calendarCredentials` nor in the DB (e.g. deleted/invalid credential), the code falls through without logging an error or recording any failed result — `createdEvent` is simply never pushed. This means a host configured with a destination calendar that has a bad credential silently never gets invited, with no visibility into why, making this hard to diagnose in production.

title: Potential crash passing an unresolved credential to updateEvent
body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, when `reference.credentialId` is set but not found locally, the code attempts to fetch it from the DB; if `credentialFromDB` exists but `credentialFromDB.app?.slug` is falsy, `credential` remains `undefined`, yet `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId))` is still called unconditionally with the undefined credential. `updateEvent` (via `getCalendar`) expects a valid `CredentialWithAppName` and will likely throw when given `undefined`, crashing the whole reschedule/update Promise.all batch instead of failing gracefully for just that one reference.

title: No test coverage added for the core multi-host destinationCalendar feature
body: Only a pre-existing e2e assertion (`destinationCalendar: null` → `destinationCalendar: []`) was adjusted to match the new array type; no new test was added to verify that a COLLECTIVE event with multiple hosts, each with their own destination calendar, actually results in calendar events being created/updated/deleted on all hosts' calendars. The PR description itself acknowledges 'I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works.' Given this PR changes a widely-used type (`CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar`) across ~20 files, lack of coverage for the primary multi-host scenario is a significant gap.

title: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw, unparsed fetch Response while the normal refresh path returns an already-parsed SDK/axios response, breaking callers when credential sync is enabled
body: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, refreshOAuthTokens() returns the raw `fetch()` Response object from hitting CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. However, several callers assume the shape returned by their normal (non-sync) refresh function, which is NOT a raw fetch Response (e.g. googlecalendar's googleapis client returns `fetchTokens.res` with a `.data` property, hubspot's SDK returns a parsed token object with `.expiresIn`/`.accessToken`, and zoho-bigin/zohocrm use axios which returns `{ data: ... }`). When sync is enabled the function instead returns a bare fetch Response, which has no `.data` property and is not the SDK's parsed object. Any code path that reads `res.data`, `.expiresIn`, etc. on the sync-enabled branch will get `undefined` and throw a TypeError (or silently produce NaN/garbage values), meaning the credential-sync feature is broken for every app except those whose non-sync refresh function itself performs a raw `fetch()` (office365calendar, office365video, webex, zoomvideo, lark). This is a core correctness bug in the feature this PR implements.

title: Google Calendar token refresh breaks when credential sync is enabled: `res?.data` is undefined for the sync branch
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` is called with a refresh function that returns `fetchTokens.res` (an object with `.data`) in the non-sync case. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, refreshOAuthTokens instead returns a raw `fetch()` Response, which has no `.data` property. The subsequent line `const token = res?.data;` followed by `token.access_token` will throw a TypeError at runtime, so enabling app credential sync for Google Calendar will crash token refresh entirely instead of working as advertised in the PR.

title: HubSpot token refresh breaks when credential sync is enabled due to response shape mismatch
body: In the non-sync branch, `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...)` resolves directly to a parsed HubspotToken object (with `.expiresIn`, `.accessToken`, etc.). When credential sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` instead returns the raw `fetch()` Response from the sync endpoint. The code immediately does `hubspotRefreshToken.expiryDate = Math.round(Date.now() + hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn * 1000)` and `hubspotClient.setAccessToken(hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken)`, both of which will be `undefined`/`NaN` on a raw Response object, since Response has no `.expiresIn`/`.accessToken` fields. The same shape-mismatch pattern also affects `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts` and `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, which read `tokenInfo.data...` / `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data...` assuming an axios-style response, but get a raw fetch Response when sync is enabled.

title: Missing `prisma` import causes compile/runtime failure in Salesforce CalendarService
body: The new `getClient` method calls `await prisma.credential.update({...})`, but the file never imports `prisma` (e.g. `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`). This is a plain reference error that should fail TypeScript type-checking and will throw `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime, breaking every Salesforce calendar operation (create/update/delete event, availability) since `getClient` is invoked unconditionally from the constructor.

title: Salesforce access token is refreshed on every CalendarService instantiation with no expiry check
body: Unlike other providers (hubspot, zoho-bigin, zohocrm, office365, zoomvideo, webex), the new Salesforce `getClient` unconditionally POSTs to Salesforce's OAuth token endpoint every time a `SalesforceCalendarService` is constructed, regardless of whether the current access token is still valid. There is no `isTokenValid`/expiry check guarding the refresh call. This causes unnecessary refresh-token round trips on every booking operation, risking rate limiting and unnecessary rotation of refresh tokens (some OAuth providers invalidate the previous refresh token on each refresh, which under concurrent requests could cause race conditions where one request's refresh token becomes stale before it is persisted). Additionally, this refresh call does not go through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce credential syncing (the stated purpose of this PR) is not actually wired up for this app despite other apps being updated.

title: Computed property keys using `.toString()` do not implement the intended catch-all schema
body: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` attempts to define a dynamic/catch-all schema using `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. Calling `.toString()` on a Zod schema instance does not return a dynamic field name pattern; it returns the default `Object.prototype.toString()` value (e.g. "[object Object]") for both expressions. As both computed keys evaluate to the identical literal string, the second definition silently overwrites the first in the object literal, so the resulting schema is effectively just `{ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() }`. The intended behavior (treat any numeric property as an expiry field and accept arbitrary other properties) is never implemented, meaning the 'minimum' schema used when credential sync is enabled does not actually validate token expiry fields are present at all; it's dead code that would pass validation for payloads completely missing any expiry information.

title: parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws unconditionally on invalid tokens, changing previously tolerant error handling in Office365
body: Previously, office365calendar's refresh flow used `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` directly and, on failure, logged the Zod error plus the raw MS response and continued gracefully (merging only successfully-parsed fields, keeping the stale credentials). The new shared `parseRefreshTokenResponse` helper throws an `Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` whenever parsing fails, and the office365 diagnostic `console.error` logging of the zod error / MS response was removed. This changes office365's refresh behavior from a soft, loggable failure to a hard throw, and removes debugging visibility into why Microsoft's token response failed validation — a regression for an existing, unrelated code path incidental to this feature.

title: Webhook secret comparison is not constant-time and HTTP method is not validated
body: The webhook secret check at line 24-29 uses a plain `!==` string comparison between the incoming header and `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, which is vulnerable to timing attacks that could let an attacker incrementally guess the secret. Additionally, the handler never checks `req.method`, so GET/PUT/DELETE requests are processed the same as POST; combined with no `defaultHandler`/`defaultResponder` wrapper used elsewhere in the codebase, malformed non-POST requests will hit `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` with an undefined body and throw an unhandled exception instead of a clean 400 response.

title: symmetricDecrypt call is not wrapped in try/catch
body: `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...)` followed by `JSON.parse(...)` can throw if the payload is malformed or was encrypted with a different key. There is no try/catch around this, so a bad request results in an unhandled exception / generic 500 instead of a clear validation error, making it harder for self-hosters to diagnose integration issues with their own sync service.

title: Hardcoded redirect URI slug diverges from callback.ts which still uses appConfig.slug
body: This PR changes `add.ts`'s redirect_uri from the templated `` `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback` `` to a hardcoded `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback`, while `callback.ts` in the same app still builds its redirect_uri dynamically from `appConfig.slug`. Although the value happens to be identical today, this inconsistency is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose and makes the two files diverge silently if the app slug ever changes, risking a redirect_uri mismatch between the authorization request and the token exchange.

title: No automated tests for the new credential-sync webhook or OAuth refresh/credential utilities
body: The PR adds a new, security-sensitive webhook endpoint (`app-credential.ts`) plus shared helpers (`refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) that affect token refresh for ~10 apps, but ships with no unit or integration tests (the author explicitly checked 'I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective'). Given the response-shape bugs identified in refreshOAuthTokens consumers, tests covering both the sync-enabled and sync-disabled code paths would have caught these regressions before merge.

title: Missing `prisma` import causes ReferenceError / compile failure
body: The new refresh-token logic added to `getClient` calls `prisma.credential.update({...})` (around line 96-99), but the file never imports `prisma` (compare with other CalendarService files that do `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`). This will fail TypeScript compilation (no symbol `prisma` in scope) or throw a ReferenceError at runtime, breaking Salesforce OAuth token refresh entirely.

title: Credential key saved as the whole safeParse result instead of the parsed token data
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full `z.SafeParseReturnType` object (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed data itself (see packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). Here the code does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists `data: { key }` directly to `prisma.credential.update`. This stores `{ success: true, data: {...} }` as the credential's `key` JSON instead of the actual token fields (access_token, refresh_token, expiry_date, etc.), corrupting the stored Google Calendar credential and breaking any subsequent code that reads `credential.key.access_token` etc. Other call sites of this helper (office365, salesforce, zoom) correctly destructure `.data`; this one does not.

title: refreshOAuthTokens return type mismatch breaks token refresh when credential sync is enabled
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, but the non-sync branch here returns `fetchTokens.res` (the googleapis client's internal response object which exposes `.data`). The caller unconditionally does `const token = res?.data;` then `token.access_token` — a bare `fetch` Response has no `.data` property, so when credential syncing is enabled this will throw a TypeError (`Cannot read properties of undefined`), breaking Google Calendar token refresh for any self-hoster who enables the very feature this PR introduces.

title: refreshOAuthTokens result treated as a parsed HubspotToken when sync is enabled, but it is a raw fetch Response
body: When credential sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response`, but the normal path returns the already-parsed object from `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...)`. The code immediately treats the result as a `HubspotToken` (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`, `.accessToken`, `.tokenType`), which are undefined on a raw Response object. This produces `NaN` expiry dates and `undefined` access tokens being persisted to the DB and passed to `hubspotClient.setAccessToken(undefined)` when the sync feature is enabled.

title: Dynamic schema keys using `.toString()` do not do what the comments claim
body: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` tries to build dynamic keys with `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. Calling `.toString()` on a Zod schema instance does not return a property name derived from the response data; it returns the default `Object.prototype.toString` value (effectively the same literal string, e.g. `"[object Object]"`) for both expressions, and the second object-literal key overwrites the first. The net effect is that the "assume any numeric property is the expiry" validation described in the comment never happens — the schema ends up only requiring `access_token` with an unrelated optional unknown field under a bogus key name. This silently weakens validation of credential-sync responses without the dead code being obviously non-functional.

title: Unhandled exceptions from zod `.parse()` and `symmetricDecrypt` return raw 500s
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` (line 31) and `symmetricDecrypt(...)` (lines 57-59) are called without try/catch. A malformed request body or malformed/incorrectly-keyed ciphertext will throw an uncaught exception instead of a clean 400 response, resulting in an unhandled Next.js API error (500) and potentially leaking internal error details/stack traces to the caller. These should be wrapped and translated into controlled error responses (e.g. using `safeParse` and a try/catch around decryption).

title: Webhook secret compared with non constant-time string inequality
body: The webhook secret validation uses a plain `!==` comparison between the incoming header and `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. This is vulnerable to timing attacks that could help an attacker incrementally guess the secret. A constant-time comparison (e.g. `crypto.timingSafeEqual`) should be used for secret validation on an endpoint explicitly designed to create/update user credentials.

title: redirect_uri hardcoded, now inconsistent with callback.ts which still uses appConfig.slug
body: This PR changes `add.ts` to build the redirect URI with a hardcoded string `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback` instead of `` `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback` ``, while `zoho-bigin/api/callback.ts` in this same PR still builds its redirect URI using `appConfig.slug`. If `appConfig.slug` ever changes, these two files will silently diverge and the OAuth redirect URI will stop matching between the authorize and callback steps, breaking the integration. This change also appears unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (credential syncing).

title: No automated tests for the new credential-sync webhook or OAuth refresh changes
body: The PR explicitly notes no tests were added, and this review found multiple concrete runtime bugs introduced by the OAuth refresh/credential-sync changes (e.g., response-shape mismatches in googlecalendar/hubspot CalendarService, a missing import in salesforce CalendarService, and a broken dynamic zod schema). None of the new files (`app-credential.ts`, `refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) nor the modified `CalendarService`/`VideoApiAdapter` refresh logic have unit or integration tests, so these regressions would not be caught by CI.

title: Wrong value stored as credential key breaks Google Calendar token refresh
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the whole `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed token data itself. Here the return value is assigned directly to `key` and persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. This means the stored credential.key becomes `{ success: true, data: { access_token, ... } }` instead of the flat token object the rest of the code (and `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on the next load) expects. Every time a Google Calendar token is refreshed (which happens regardless of whether app-credential-sync is enabled), the credential record is corrupted and subsequent calendar operations for that user will fail to parse the stored key. Other call sites of this helper (office365calendar, zoomvideo, salesforce) correctly destructure `.data`, but this one does not.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema's dynamic keys don't implement a catch-all and strip/corrupt token data
body: The schema uses computed property keys `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. `z.string().toString()` evaluates to a fixed literal string (e.g. "ZodString"), not a wildcard match for arbitrary keys, so this does not create a pass-through/catch-all schema. Since the zod object schema has no `.passthrough()`, any field in the actual refreshed-token response that isn't `access_token` (e.g. `expiry_date`, `refresh_token`, `instance_url`) is silently stripped from `.data` when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true. Combined with the fallback below (`refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`), this causes the stored credential's refresh_token to be overwritten with the literal placeholder string `"refresh_token"` and other required fields (expiry_date, instance_url, etc.) to disappear, corrupting every synced credential's stored key (affects google-calendar, office365calendar, salesforce, zoomvideo refresh flows).

title: Sync-mode response shape mismatches callers' expectations across multiple apps
body: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, this helper resolves to a raw, un-parsed `fetch` `Response` object. Several call sites assume the resolved value is already a parsed object: e.g. packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts does `tokenInfo.data.error` and packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts does `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` (expecting an axios-like `.data` wrapper), and packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts assigns the result directly to a `HubspotToken` and reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`/`.accessToken` directly. A raw fetch `Response` has none of these properties, so when credential syncing is enabled, token refresh for hubspot, zoho-bigin, and zohocrm will throw (`Cannot read properties of undefined`) or silently store `undefined`/`NaN` values, breaking those integrations entirely under the very feature this PR is adding.

title: Salesforce access token is unconditionally refreshed on every CalendarService instantiation
body: Unlike every other provider in this PR, `getClient` performs an OAuth refresh-token request unconditionally, with no check of whether the current access token is still valid (there is no `isTokenValid`/expiry check before calling the Salesforce token endpoint). Since `getClient` runs in the constructor and a new `SalesforceCalendarService` is created per operation, this triggers an extra network round-trip and a token refresh call to Salesforce on every single booking/calendar action, which is wasteful and can hit Salesforce's rate limits. It also introduces a concurrency risk: concurrent requests using the same credential will each attempt to refresh the token independently, risking invalidation/race conditions if Salesforce invalidates the previous access token on refresh.

title: Fragile success check using statusText === 'OK'
body: `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw ...` is unreliable: `statusText` is not guaranteed to be the literal string "OK" across all environments/HTTP versions (e.g., HTTP/2 responses commonly have an empty statusText), and conversely a non-200 response could still have statusText "OK" in rare cases. This should check `response.ok` or `response.status === 200` instead, otherwise valid refresh responses can be incorrectly treated as failures (or vice versa).

title: Non constant-time secret comparison and no HTTP method restriction
body: The webhook secret check (`req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) uses a plain string inequality comparison, which is vulnerable to timing attacks that could help an attacker brute-force the secret. Additionally, the handler never checks `req.method`, so it will process the body on any HTTP verb that reaches it (not just POST), and malformed/invalid encrypted payloads (`symmetricDecrypt` / `JSON.parse` failures) are not caught, resulting in an unhandled exception and a generic 500 instead of a controlled error response.

title: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME is not normalized to lowercase
body: `.env.example` documents that `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` 'should be in lowercase', but the code never lowercases the configured value before using it as a key into `req.headers`. Node/Next.js always lowercases incoming header names, so if an operator sets this env var with any uppercase character, the lookup will always miss and the webhook will always return 403, with no indication of why. The code should normalize the header name itself (e.g. `.toLowerCase()`) instead of relying on operator discipline.

title: No automated tests for new credential-sync logic
body: The PR adds several new, trust-sensitive pieces of logic (the `/api/webhook/app-credential` endpoint, `refreshOAuthTokens`, and `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) that directly affect how OAuth credentials are persisted, but no unit or integration tests were added for any of them (the author's own checklist states tests were not added). Given the data-corruption risks identified in the token-refresh code paths, this is an area that should have had test coverage before merging.

title: Incorrect boolean logic grants/denies permission incorrectly for team admins/owners
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. Since `isTeamOwner` is a stricter check than `isTeamAdmin` (an owner typically already satisfies the admin check), ANDing the two collapses the condition to effectively 'is team owner only'. A plain team admin (non-owner) who is neither the organizer nor an attendee will be denied access to add guests even though the intent (variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner`) is clearly to allow either role. This should be `||`, not `&&`.

title: EventManager built with the calling user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` use `ctx.user` (the caller). The authorization check above explicitly allows non-organizers (team admins/owners and attendees) to call this endpoint. When such a non-organizer calls it, the calendar/video update is attempted using their own personal credentials rather than the booking organizer's, which can silently fail to update the organizer's actual calendar event or incorrectly touch the caller's own calendar/integration. The EventManager should be built from the booking's organizer (`booking.user`), not from `ctx.user`.

title: Wrong guest list passed to sendAddGuestsEmails causes incorrect email content
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw, unfiltered `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests` (the actually-added subset). In `email-manager.ts`'s `sendAddGuestsEmails`, every current attendee whose email is in `newGuests` receives the full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` while others receive `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. If a caller resubmits an email that already belongs to an existing attendee (filtered out by the `uniqueGuests` dedupe), that pre-existing attendee will incorrectly be classified as a 'new guest' and receive a full scheduling/invite email instead of the appropriate add-guests notification.

title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive while blacklist entries are normalized to lowercase
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased, but the `guests` array from user input is compared against it as-is (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), without lowercasing `guest`. A blacklisted email submitted with different casing (e.g. `Blocked@Example.com` vs `blocked@example.com`) will bypass the blacklist filter entirely, defeating its purpose.

title: No deduplication of repeated emails within the same request
body: `uniqueGuests` only filters guests against existing attendees and the blacklist; it does not deduplicate the `guests` input array against itself. If the same email appears twice in the submitted list (e.g. by bypassing client-side validation or via a different API caller), `createMany` will create two attendee rows with the identical email for the same booking, causing duplicate attendee records and duplicate notification emails.

title: Email sending failures are silently swallowed with a bare console.log
body: The catch block only logs a static string `"Error sending AddGuestsEmails"` and discards the actual error object (`err`), and does not use the project's `logger` (already imported pattern elsewhere in the codebase). This makes diagnosing production email failures (e.g. SMTP errors, template rendering issues) effectively impossible from logs.

title: Dead fallback in error toast message always skipped
body: `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` uses a template string `` `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` `` for `message`, which is always a non-empty, truthy string even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined` (producing the literal text "undefined: ..."). The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can therefore never execute, and users may see a confusing "undefined:" prefix instead of a clean fallback message.

title: Any existing attendee can unilaterally add arbitrary new guests
body: The authorization check allows any current attendee (`isAttendee`) of the booking to add arbitrary new guest emails, with no organizer approval step. This lets any invitee silently expose meeting details (video link, location, calendar invite) to third parties the organizer never intended to invite, which may be unexpected/undesirable default behavior for an organizer-managed scheduling event.

title: No automated tests for the new addGuests feature
body: This PR introduces a new tRPC mutation (`addGuests.handler.ts`/`addGuests.schema.ts`), a new dialog (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx`), a new reusable form component (`MultiEmail.tsx`), and two new email templates, but no unit/integration tests are included for any of them. Given the permission logic bugs identified (admin/owner `&&` vs `||`, credential source, email list used) this feature is especially test-worthy and currently has zero coverage.

title: Array index used as React key for removable list items
body: Each email input's `key={index}` is based on array position. When an item is removed via `onClickAddon` (which does `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`), all subsequent items shift index, so React will reuse DOM nodes/input state incorrectly (e.g., focus state, cursor position) for the wrong email field. This can cause subtle UI glitches when removing a non-last email from the list.

title: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses AND instead of OR, excluding legitimate team admins
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, meaning a user must be BOTH a team admin AND the team owner simultaneously to pass this check. In practice a user is either an admin or the owner, so this condition is almost always false for team members who are 'only' an admin, contradicting the variable's name and intended semantics ('admin OR owner'). As a result, team admins who are not also the literal owner will be denied permission to add guests unless they happen to also be the booking organizer or an attendee, breaking the intended authorization model for team bookings.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw/unfiltered guest list instead of the deduplicated uniqueGuests
body: After filtering out guests that are already attendees or blacklisted into `uniqueGuests` (used to actually create new attendees), the original unfiltered `guests` array is passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` instead of `uniqueGuests`. Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts), attendees are classified as 'new' vs 'existing' by checking membership in this list. If `guests` contains emails that were filtered out (already an attendee, blacklisted, or duplicate), those existing attendees will incorrectly be treated as newly added and sent the full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` invite again instead of the intended `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` notification, producing confusing/duplicate invite emails.

title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive on the guest side, allowing bypass via case variation
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lower-cased, but the incoming `guest` values from `guests` are compared as-is (`guest === attendee.email` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`) without lower-casing `guest` first. A blacklisted address submitted with different letter casing (e.g. 'Admin@Example.com' vs 'admin@example.com') will not be filtered out, defeating the blacklist mechanism.

title: Email send failure logged via console.log instead of the project logger
body: On failure to send the add-guests emails, the error is only logged with `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")`, swallowing the actual error object and not using the standard `@calcom/lib/logger` used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. in email-manager.ts). This makes failures hard to diagnose in production and is inconsistent with the rest of the handler's error-handling conventions.

title: Error toast fallback message is unreachable dead code
body: `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`;` always produces a non-empty string, so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` never falls back to the friendlier localized message; it always shows the raw error code and message key concatenation to the end user, which can be confusing/unlocalized if `err.message` isn't a translation key that resolves properly.

title: Dialog state (emails, invalid flag) is not reset when closed via outside click or Escape
body: The `multiEmailValue` and `isInvalidEmail` state are only reset inside the explicit Cancel button's onClick handler. When the dialog is dismissed via the Dialog's `onOpenChange` (e.g. clicking outside or pressing Escape), `setIsOpenDialog` is called directly without clearing `multiEmailValue`/`isInvalidEmail`, so reopening the dialog later will show the previously entered (possibly invalid) email values and error state.

title: No transaction/locking between read and write when adding attendees, risking duplicate attendee creation under concurrent requests
body: The handler reads the booking's current attendees, computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering against that in-memory list, and then performs a separate `prisma.booking.update` with `createMany` to insert them. If two add-guest requests for the same booking run concurrently (e.g. two different users clicking 'Add' at the same time with overlapping emails), both could compute the same 'unique' guest as not-yet-present and both insert it, resulting in duplicate attendee rows for the same email on the same booking, since there is no visible transaction or unique constraint enforcing (bookingId, email) uniqueness in this flow.

title: No automated tests added for the new addGuests flow
body: This PR introduces a new tRPC mutation (`addGuestsHandler`), a new client dialog (`AddGuestsDialog`), and a new reusable `MultiEmail` form component, but ships no unit or integration tests covering permission checks (organizer/attendee/team admin), duplicate/blacklist filtering, calendar update behavior, or the email dispatch logic (`sendAddGuestsEmails`). Given the authorization bug identified above, test coverage would likely have caught the issue before merge.

title: Incorrect boolean logic makes team-admin/owner permission check nearly always false
body:
The permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`:
```
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
    (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
    (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
Since a membership typically has exactly one role (MEMBER, ADMIN, or OWNER), a user can almost never satisfy both `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` simultaneously. This means the variable named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is effectively always `false`, so team admins and owners who are not themselves the booking organizer or an attendee will be rejected with FORBIDDEN when trying to add guests, defeating the intent of granting admins/owners this permission.

title: Team members never notified because evt.team is never populated
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` in email-manager.ts iterates `calendarEvent.team?.members` to notify all team members with `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail`, but the `CalendarEvent` object (`evt`) constructed in `addGuestsHandler` never sets a `team` property. As a result, `calendarEvent.team` is always `undefined` for this flow, so the team-member notification loop is dead code and only the single organizer email (from `booking.userId`) ever receives the organizer notification for team-based bookings, even though other team members may need to be informed guests were added.

title: No check that booking is not cancelled before adding guests
body: The handler fetches the booking and performs permission checks but never verifies the booking's status (e.g. `CANCELLED`/`REJECTED`). This allows adding guests to cancelled or rejected bookings, which doesn't make logical sense and could trigger calendar/video updates and emails for events that no longer exist.

title: Guest emails deduped against existing attendees but not against each other, and comparison is case-sensitive
body: `uniqueGuests` is filtered only against `booking.attendees` (`!booking.attendees.some(...)`) and does not remove duplicate entries within the submitted `guests` array itself, nor normalize case. If duplicates (or case-variant duplicates, e.g. `a@b.com` vs `A@B.com`) are submitted in a single call -- which bypasses the client-side `AddGuestsDialog` uniqueness check if called directly via API -- multiple attendee rows with effectively the same email can be created via `createMany`, leading to duplicate attendee records on the booking.

title: Email send failures are silently swallowed with console.log instead of being logged with context
Dead fallback branch in error toast message
No upper bound on number of guests that can be added in a single request
body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no maximum length constraint. A caller could submit an arbitrarily large array of guest emails in one request, causing a large number of attendee rows to be created and a large number of emails to be queued/sent in one `addGuestsHandler` invocation, which is a potential performance/abuse concern for a mutation exposed to any authenticated attendee/organizer.

title: No automated tests for the new addGuests feature
body: This PR introduces a brand-new mutation (`addGuestsHandler`), a new dialog (`AddGuestsDialog`), and a new reusable form component (`MultiEmail`), none of which have accompanying unit or integration tests. Given the handler contains non-trivial permission logic (which is already buggy, see other findings) and mutates booking/attendee data plus triggers calendar updates and emails, the lack of tests is a significant gap for verifying correct behavior and preventing regressions.

title: retryCount deletion branch not scoped to SMS method
body: The new OR clause `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` in the deleteMany call has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, unlike the first clause. Since `retryCount` is a shared column on the `WorkflowReminder` model used for all methods (EMAIL, SMS, WHATSAPP), any non-SMS reminder that somehow ends up with retryCount > 1 (e.g. via future code reuse of this field, or a bug elsewhere) would be silently deleted regardless of method. This widens the deletion scope beyond what the PR intends (deleting failed SMS reminders) and can cause data loss for unrelated reminder types.

title: Non-atomic retryCount increment is racy
body: retryCount is incremented by reading the in-memory `reminder.retryCount` value fetched at the start of the loop and writing `reminder.retryCount + 1` back. This is not atomic: if this cron job overlaps with another run (or is retried concurrently), both executions could read the same stale value and write the same incremented result, losing an increment. Using Prisma's atomic `{ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` would avoid this race and ensure the failure count is accurate, which matters since after retryCount > 1 the reminder is permanently deleted.

title: Non-atomic retryCount increment is racy (catch block)
body: Same issue as the success-path update: `data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }` computes the new value from a value read earlier in this request rather than using an atomic increment. Concurrent executions of this cron handler could under-count failures, delaying or preventing the intended deletion of permanently-failing SMS reminders after two failures.

title: retryCount never incremented when message/sendTo is missing
body: If `message` ends up empty/null or `sendTo` is falsy, the `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` branch is skipped entirely and neither the success path nor the new retryCount-increment path executes. Such a reminder will be re-fetched by every subsequent cron run (scheduled remains false) but its retryCount will never increase, so it will never hit the new retryCount>1 deletion condition. This defeats the purpose of the fix for this class of failure (e.g. workflowStep with no body and no recognized template, or missing sendTo), leaving the reminder stuck forever instead of being retried/deleted.

title: Stale comment not updated for new deletion logic
body: The comment above the deleteMany call still reads "delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date", but the query was changed to also delete any reminder (not necessarily SMS, not necessarily past its scheduled date) that has retryCount > 1. The comment should be updated to describe the new OR condition so maintainers understand the full deletion criteria.

title: No automated test coverage for new retry logic
body: This PR introduces new behavior (incrementing retryCount on failure, and deleting reminders once retryCount > 1) but no tests were added or updated to verify: (1) that retryCount increments on a twilio.scheduleSMS failure/exception, (2) that reminders with retryCount > 1 are deleted on the next run, and (3) that successful scheduling does not affect retryCount. Given this directly affects whether customer SMS reminders are silently dropped, test coverage would help prevent regressions.

title: Non-atomic retryCount increment can lose updates
body: The retryCount is updated via `data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }`, using the value read earlier in the same request rather than Prisma's atomic `increment` operator. If the cron endpoint is ever invoked concurrently (e.g. overlapping schedules, retried HTTP calls, or multiple workers), two requests reading the same reminder's retryCount at the same time will both write retryCount+1 based on the stale value, causing one increment to be lost. Since the cleanup logic in this same PR deletes reminders once retryCount > 1, undercounting means a persistently-failing reminder (e.g., due to an invalid phone number) may never reach the deletion threshold and keep being retried indefinitely, defeating the purpose of this fix. Use `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } }` instead.

title: Broad delete condition not scoped to SMS method
body: The deleteMany OR clause's second branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` constraint, unlike the first branch. retryCount is a generic column on WorkflowReminder used for all methods (EMAIL, SMS, WHATSAPP), and currently only this SMS cron sets it, but that is an implicit assumption, not enforced by the schema or query. If any other code path (now or in the future) increments retryCount on an EMAIL or WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder, this query will silently delete those reminders as well, even though they were never scheduled for SMS. This is a landmine that could cause silent loss of unrelated workflow reminders. The retryCount branch should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to match intent.

title: Outdated comment does not describe new deletion criteria
body: The comment above the deleteMany call still reads "delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date", but the query was extended to also delete any WorkflowReminder (regardless of method/scheduled state) once retryCount > 1. The comment should be updated to mention the retry-based deletion so future maintainers understand both deletion conditions.

title: No automated tests added for new retry/delete behavior
body: This PR introduces new business logic (retryCount increments on failure, and deletion once retryCount exceeds 1) but adds no unit or integration tests verifying: that retryCount increments correctly on scheduling failure and on thrown errors, that reminders are deleted after the threshold is reached, and that the scoping of the delete query behaves as expected. Given this handles data deletion, lack of test coverage increases risk of regressions going unnoticed.

title: deleteMany retryCount condition is not scoped to SMS method
body: The second branch of the OR clause in the deleteMany call (`retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` restriction, unlike the first branch. Since `retryCount` is a generic field on the shared `WorkflowReminder` model (also used, e.g., by `WebhookScheduledTriggers`-like retry concepts, or potentially by future email/WhatsApp retry logic), any WorkflowReminder row of any method that ends up with retryCount > 1 will be permanently deleted by this SMS-specific cron endpoint, even if it is an EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminder unrelated to SMS sending. This can cause unintended data loss for non-SMS reminders if retryCount is ever incremented elsewhere, and is inconsistent with the stated intent of only cleaning up failed SMS reminders.

title: Catch block treats all errors as SMS send failures, risking premature deletion
body: The try block spans many operations beyond the actual SMS send: fetching the organizer's profile, resolving the booker URL, parsing booking metadata, rendering templates, etc. Any exception from these unrelated operations (e.g., a transient DB query failure, a template rendering bug, or a metadata parsing error) is caught by the same catch block and increments `retryCount` exactly like a genuine SMS delivery failure (e.g., invalid phone number). Combined with the new deletion logic (retryCount > 1 triggers deletion), two unrelated/transient errors on a reminder are enough to have it permanently deleted, even though the actual SMS send may never have been attempted or may have been perfectly deliverable. This conflates infrastructure/transient errors with the specific 'invalid phone number'-type failures the PR intends to handle, risking silent loss of valid reminders.

title: No retry/cleanup path when message or sendTo is empty
body: When `message` is falsy/empty or `sendTo` is missing, the code silently does nothing (no retryCount increment, no scheduling, no logging). Such reminders remain `scheduled: false` indefinitely and are only ever cleaned up once their `scheduledDate` passes (via the first deleteMany branch), meaning they can linger unprocessed for up to 7 days without any retryCount-based accounting or visibility, unlike the newly added failure paths. This inconsistency was not addressed by this PR despite being a closely related failure mode (e.g., a booking never had a phone number set).

title: Missing test coverage for new retryCount/deletion behavior
body: This PR introduces non-trivial new behavior (incrementing retryCount on failure, and deleting reminders once retryCount exceeds 1) but no tests were added or updated to verify: (1) retryCount increments correctly on both the 'no scheduledSMS result' path and the exception path, (2) the deleteMany call actually removes reminders with retryCount > 1, and (3) it does not inadvertently remove unrelated reminders. Given this logic directly affects whether customer-facing SMS reminders get silently dropped, the lack of test coverage is a notable gap for a bug-fix PR.

title: Public findMany() method removed without updating/checking callers
body: The `findMany(findManyArgs)` method that previously returned fully-typed Prisma results has been removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. This PR only touches `insightsBooking.ts` and its test file, but `InsightsBookingService.findMany` is a public API that is very likely consumed elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. insights trpc routers/handlers). Removing this method without updating or even searching for its call sites will break compilation or runtime behavior for any consumer still calling `.findMany(...)`. The PR should either keep a `findMany`-equivalent wrapper around the new raw-SQL conditions, or update all call sites in the same change.

title: Caching behavior tests removed with no replacement
body: The previous `describe("Caching", ...)` block, which verified that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return cached (identical) results on repeated calls, was deleted entirely in this PR. The service still implements `cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` caching logic (lines 49-50, 84-95 of insightsBooking.ts), but after this change there is no test coverage verifying that caching still works correctly with the new `Prisma.sql` return type, leaving a regression risk undetected if caching logic breaks (e.g., due to object identity issues with `Prisma.Sql` instances).

title: PR description misrepresents scope of change
body: The PR description states the production code conversion to `Prisma.sql` was "previously converted in the service implementation" and that this PR "updates ... tests to work with the new Prisma.sql format", implying `insightsBooking.ts` is unchanged context. However, the diff shows substantial production logic changes in `insightsBooking.ts` itself (converting Prisma object-filter WHERE clauses to raw SQL, removing `findMany`, renaming types, changing return types of `buildAuthorizationConditions`/`buildFilterConditions`/`getBaseConditions`). Mischaracterizing this as a test-only fix could cause reviewers to under-scrutinize an actually risky production change to authorization-critical SQL generation.

title: Public `findMany` method removed without replacement call-sites update
body: The previous public method `InsightsBookingService.findMany(...)` (which executed a Prisma `findMany` using the combined conditions) has been removed entirely and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment and does not execute any query. Any existing caller of `service.findMany(...)` elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. insights routers/analytics endpoints) will now fail to compile/run since the method no longer exists. The PR only touches the service and its integration test; no other files were updated to use `getBaseConditions()` instead. This is a breaking API change that is not called out or verified against other consumers.

title: Constructor option type loosened, losing compile-time scope validation
body: The constructor parameter type was changed from the strict discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (`zod.infer`) to a new loosely-typed `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` with `scope: "user" | "org" | "team"` and an optional `teamId`. This removes compile-time enforcement that `teamId` must be supplied when `scope === "team"`. Previously the discriminated union would catch such mistakes at compile time; now a caller can omit `teamId` for `scope: "team"` and only discover the problem at runtime (silently falling back to `NOTHING_CONDITION`), making bugs harder to catch during development.

title: Org-scope authorization test asserts exact array order from unordered DB query, risking flaky failures
body: The test for org-scope conditions asserts `Prisma.sql` equality with an exact ordering of `teamId`/`userId` arrays: `[testData.org.id, testData.team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` and `[testData.user.id, user2.id, user3.id]`. These arrays are built from `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId` and `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`, neither of which appear to specify an explicit `orderBy`. Postgres does not guarantee row order without `ORDER BY`, so the resulting arrays may be returned in a different order than expected (especially under parallel test execution or query planner changes), causing this `toEqual` deep-equality assertion on the `Prisma.Sql` object (which also compares the `values` array) to fail intermittently even though the underlying SQL semantics (ANY(...)) are order-independent.

title: Caching behavior tests removed without replacement
body: The previous `describe("Caching", ...)` block, which verified that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` memoize their results via `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions`, was deleted in this PR and not replaced with an equivalent test using the new `Prisma.sql` comparisons. The service still implements this caching logic (`insightsBooking.ts` lines 83-95), but there is no longer any integration test asserting that repeated calls return the cached value instead of rebuilding (e.g., re-querying membership/team tables), so a regression in the caching logic would go undetected.

title: Raw SQL fragments reference bare, unqualified column names
body: The SQL fragments built in `buildFilterConditions`, `buildAuthorizationConditions`, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` reference unqualified column names such as `"userId"`, `"teamId"`, `"eventTypeId"`, `"eventParentId"`, and `"isTeamBooking"` with no table alias/qualifier. These fragments are intended to be composed into larger raw queries (as shown by the `getBaseConditions()` usage in `$queryRaw`). If the final query joins the `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` table with any other table that also has columns with these same names (common for `userId`/`teamId`), Postgres will raise an ambiguous-column error, or worse, silently resolve to the wrong table depending on query structure. Previously, using Prisma's object-based `where` clause scoped these fields unambiguously to the `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` model.

title: Public findMany() method removed and replaced with getBaseConditions(), breaking the service's contract
body: The previous implementation exposed `findMany(findManyArgs)` which executed the query against `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized` and returned rows. This PR removes that method entirely and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment and requires the caller to manually construct and execute a raw `$queryRaw` query (as the test now does). Any production code that calls `InsightsBookingService.findMany(...)` (e.g. insights routes/UI data fetchers) will fail to compile/run after this change, since the method no longer exists. The PR description claims this is only a test update to match an already-converted implementation, but the diff shows the public API of the service itself is being changed in the same PR, which is a contract break that isn't validated against other call sites in the diff.

title: Array-based ANY(...) SQL conditions for team/org scope are never executed against the real database in tests
body: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` build SQL like `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) AND (...)` where `teamIds`/`userIdsFromTeam` are JS number arrays interpolated via Prisma.sql. Passing arrays as parameters to `ANY()` in raw Postgres queries can require explicit type casts (e.g. `ANY($1::int[])`) depending on the driver/parameter binding, otherwise Postgres may fail with a parameter type inference error at execution time. The only integration test that actually executes a query via `prisma.$queryRaw` (the renamed `getBaseConditions` test) exercises the 'user' scope, which does not use `ANY()`. The 'team' and 'org' scope tests only assert structural equality of the constructed `Prisma.Sql` object and never actually run the query against the database, so a runtime failure in the ANY()-array binding for team/org scopes (explicitly called out as a risk in the PR's own review checklist) would not be caught by these tests.

title: Caching behavior tests were removed even though the caching logic still exists in the service
body: The previous test suite had a `describe("Caching", ...)` block verifying that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return cached results on subsequent calls (backed by `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` fields). This PR deletes those tests entirely without replacing them, while the service implementation (`insightsBooking.ts`) still contains and relies on this same caching mechanism (fields `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions`, lines 49-50 and 83-95). Removing these tests silently drops coverage for an existing, still-present feature, so a regression in caching (e.g., accidentally rebuilding the Prisma.Sql object on each call, or caching stale/incorrect conditions) would go undetected.

title: PR description scope does not match actual diff contents
body: The PR description states this change only updates the integration test file to match a service implementation that was 'previously converted' to Prisma.sql, implying `insightsBooking.ts` itself was not modified by this PR. However the diff shows substantial changes to `insightsBooking.ts` (import change from `import type { Prisma }` to `import { Prisma }`, removal of `findMany`, new `getBaseConditions` method, rewritten condition-building logic). This mismatch between the stated scope and the actual change makes it harder for reviewers to know which parts of the service logic are newly introduced in this PR versus pre-existing, and increases risk that the 'HIGH RISK' authorization/SQL logic in the service itself did not receive a dedicated, scoped review.

title: Credential ownership check fails for team/delegation-owned credentials
body: The authorization check `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })` only matches credentials whose `userId` column equals the current user's id. Credentials belonging to a team (where `userId` is null, e.g. delegation/shared calendar credentials) will never satisfy this condition, so legitimate users managing such credentials will always get an 'access denied' error even though they should be allowed to delete the cache. This makes the feature unusable for any non-personal credential and is inconsistent with how other credential-related handlers in the codebase resolve ownership (typically via a repository helper that also considers team membership/delegation).

title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError loses proper error code
body: `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` produces a generic INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR on the tRPC client instead of a semantically correct code (e.g. NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN via TRPCError). This is inconsistent with tRPC error-handling conventions used elsewhere in the codebase and prevents clients from distinguishing between 'not found' and 'server error' cases, which can also affect logging/alerting noise since legitimate client errors get reported as 500s.

title: deleteCacheMutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query, causing stale cache status in UI
body: Unlike `disconnectMutation`, which has an `onSettled` handler that invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `utils.viewer.apps.integrations`, `deleteCacheMutation`'s `onSuccess` only calls the optional `onSuccess` prop (`onChanged`). If the parent component doesn't pass `onChanged` (it is optional on `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapperProps`), the `cacheUpdatedAt` value shown in the dropdown will not be refreshed after a successful cache deletion, leaving the UI showing a stale 'Cache Status' timestamp even though the cache was actually deleted.

title: Cache timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
body: The cache-updated timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {...})`, ignoring the user's configured locale/time format settings used elsewhere in the app. For non-English locales this will render dates in an inconsistent format compared to the rest of the UI.

title: updateManyByCredentialId updates ALL selected calendars for a credential regardless of which ones were actually refreshed
body: In `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`, after looping over only the `selectedCalendars` passed into the method (which can be a subset, e.g. the 'remainingCalendars' passed from `unwatchCalendar`), the code calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`, which updates `updatedAt` for every `SelectedCalendar` row tied to the credential — not just the ones that were actually processed in this call. This produces an inaccurate 'last synced' signal for calendars that weren't touched, and also issues an extra DB write on every cache refresh even when it is a no-op from a data perspective. The PR description itself flags uncertainty about whether this update is even needed.

title: No tests for new deleteCache mutation, cache-status repository method, or CredentialActionsDropdown
body: This PR introduces a new destructive mutation (`deleteCache`), a new repository method (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), and a new UI component (`CredentialActionsDropdown`) with confirmation-dialog flows, but no unit or integration tests are added for any of them. Given the PR's own review checklist calls out multiple untested behaviors (authorization, cache status mapping, conditional rendering), this is a significant test gap for a feature that deletes user data.

title: updatedAt field combines @default(now()) and @updatedAt; migration uses NOW() instead of Prisma's usual CURRENT_TIMESTAMP default
body: The new `updatedAt DateTime @default(now()) @updatedAt` field combines a static default with the auto-managed `@updatedAt` directive, which is redundant since `@updatedAt` fields are already set to the current time on create. Additionally, the hand-written migration sets the column default as `DEFAULT NOW()` while Prisma's generated migrations for `@default(now())` on Postgres typically emit `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3)`. This textual mismatch between the schema-declared default and the actual DB default can cause `prisma migrate dev`/schema-drift detection to flag an unexpected diff in a future migration.

title: Removed `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` type check in findMany
body: The diff removes the `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` assertion that previously validated the shape of the args object passed to `prisma.selectedCalendar.findMany`, replacing it with an inline object literal. This is unrelated to the calendar-cache feature and reduces compile-time type safety for this method without any stated reason.

title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in UI
