body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only calls `onSuccess?.()` on success, whereas the sibling `disconnectMutation` explicitly invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `utils.viewer.apps.integrations` in its `onSettled`. After successfully deleting the calendar cache, the `cacheUpdatedAt`/`hasCache` state shown in the dropdown (and the 'Delete cached data' menu item) will not refresh unless the parent's `onChanged` callback happens to invalidate the same queries. This can leave the UI showing a stale 'Last updated' timestamp and a cache-deletion option that no longer corresponds to actual cache state.

title: deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error instead of TRPCError, losing proper error codes
body: When the credential isn't found or doesn't belong to the user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC will wrap this as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than a meaningful NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN code, which both misrepresents the failure to clients and can be confusing when monitoring/alerting on 500s for what is really an authorization/validation failure. It should use `TRPCError` with an appropriate code (e.g. `NOT_FOUND` or `FORBIDDEN`).

title: Cache deletion authorization only checks direct credential ownership, not delegation/team-based credentials
body: The handler verifies access via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`. This does not account for delegation credentials or team-managed credentials that this codebase otherwise supports (e.g. via `enrichUserWithDelegationCredentialsIncludeServiceAccountKey`). For users accessing a Google Calendar through a delegation/organization-managed credential, this check will always fail, making the 'Delete cached data' action non-functional for those connections even though the UI may present it as available (see CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx `hasCache`, which does not exclude delegation credentials).

title: hasCache does not exclude delegation credentials, so a non-functional 'Delete cached data' action can be shown
body: `hasCache` is computed as `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` without checking `delegationCredentialId`. For delegation-based Google Calendar connections that have cache entries, the dropdown will render the 'Delete cached data' menu item and allow the user to attempt deletion, but the backend `deleteCacheHandler` (which keys off `credential.userId === user.id`) will reject it for delegation credentials, resulting in a confusing failure for an action the UI implied was valid.

title: Unconditional extra DB write on every cache refresh with no consumer of the updated field
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now unconditionally calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` after every cache refresh loop, updating `updatedAt` for all SelectedCalendar rows under the credential (across all event types). The PR's own notes acknowledge this value is 'currently only updated in backend... but not displayed in frontend' and question whether it should be removed. As written, this adds an unconditional, potentially frequent extra UPDATE statement (fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache can run per watched-calendar-batch/webhook) with no current UI consumer, adding unnecessary DB load/lock contention without a corresponding feature use.

title: Regression: broken/errored calendar connections can no longer be disconnected when disableConnectionModification is true
body: In the previous code, the Alert (error-state) branch rendered `DisconnectIntegration` guarded only by `!connectedCalendar.delegationCredentialId`, ignoring `disableConnectionModification`. The new code passes `disableConnectionModification` into `CredentialActionsDropdown`, whose internal `canDisconnect` check now also requires `!disableConnectionModification`. This means a user who previously could remove a broken/errored calendar connection even in a 'modification disabled' context (e.g. event-type scoped view) can no longer do so, which could trap users with unrecoverable broken calendar integrations in that scope.

title: No tests added for new deleteCache handler, getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, or CredentialActionsDropdown component
body: This PR introduces new backend logic (deleteCacheHandler, CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, enrichment of connectedCalendars with cacheUpdatedAt) and a new UI component (CredentialActionsDropdown) with non-trivial conditional rendering and multiple confirmation flows, but no unit/integration tests are included for any of them. Given these touch authorization logic (deleteCache ownership check) and data correctness (cache status mapping), lack of tests increases the risk of undetected regressions.

title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
body: The deleteCacheMutation only calls the optional `onSuccess` prop on success, whereas the disconnectMutation right below it explicitly invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `utils.viewer.apps.integrations` in its `onSettled` callback. If the parent component does not pass an `onChanged`/`onSuccess` handler that performs the same invalidation, the dropdown will keep showing the stale 'Cache Status'/'Last updated' timestamp after the cache has actually been deleted, because the `connectedCalendars` query (which supplies `cacheUpdatedAt`) is never refetched.

title: Cache timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {...}).format(new Date(cacheUpdatedAt))` hardcodes the locale to en-US instead of using the user's active locale (available via `useLocale()`/`i18n.language`). In a multi-locale product like cal.com, this means the cache-updated timestamp will always render in US date/time format regardless of the user's configured language/region settings.

title: Cache deletion bypasses CalendarCacheRepository abstraction
body: deleteCacheHandler calls `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` directly instead of going through `CalendarCacheRepository`/`CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` (which already exposes a `deleteManyByCredential` method used elsewhere in the codebase to gate behavior behind the calendar-cache feature flag). Bypassing the repository abstraction is inconsistent with the rest of the calendar-cache feature and could allow cache deletion even when calendar caching is supposed to be disabled for a tenant via the mock repository.

title: updateManyByCredentialId updates all SelectedCalendars, not just the ones refreshed
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` after processing only the `selectedCalendars` passed into the function. However `updateManyByCredentialId` updates every SelectedCalendar row for that credentialId, including rows that were not part of the batch being refreshed (e.g. in `unwatchCalendar`, `remainingCalendars` excludes the calendar being unwatched, yet its `updatedAt` would still be bumped by this call). This makes the 'last updated' timestamp inaccurate for calendars whose availability was not actually re-fetched in this call.

title: dev:cron now relies on npx tsx without adding tsx as a dependency
body: The `dev:cron` script was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not added to `devDependencies` (only `ts-node` remains, still used by other scripts). This forces `npx` to resolve/download `tsx` on every invocation (network dependency, non-pinned version), which can fail in offline/CI environments and introduces inconsistent tooling between scripts.

title: sed -i '' syntax is BSD-only and breaks on Linux
body: `sed -i '' -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD/macOS sed syntax for in-place editing (`-i ''`). On GNU/Linux sed (common in CI and most dev containers), this will either error out or incorrectly treat `''` as the script, breaking the script for non-macOS contributors.

title: No tests added for the destructive deleteCache feature
body: This PR introduces a new destructive mutation (`deleteCacheHandler`), a new UI component (`CredentialActionsDropdown`) with confirmation dialogs, and a new repository method (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), but no unit or integration tests were added for any of them. Given that deleteCache permanently removes cached calendar availability data and the PR's own review checklist flags end-to-end verification as still outstanding, lack of automated test coverage for authorization (credential ownership check) and the delete logic itself is a notable gap.

title: Single SendGrid failure aborts cancellation of entire batch and loses already-cancelled reminders
body: The for-loop that cancels pending email reminders (lines 56-73) is wrapped in a single try/catch around the whole loop. If `client.request` throws for any one reminder (e.g. an invalid/expired batch_id), the loop stops immediately: (1) all subsequent reminders in `remindersToCancel` are skipped for this cron run even though their scheduledDate may be within the next hour, meaning their emails can still be sent — the exact bug this PR is meant to fix; (2) `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` calls created for reminders that WERE successfully cancelled earlier in the loop are Prisma 'thenable' lazy promises that only execute when awaited via `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`. Since the exception short-circuits execution before that `await Promise.all(...)` line is ever reached, those delete operations never actually run, so already-cancelled reminders are never removed from the DB and will be retried (and the SendGrid cancel re-sent) on every subsequent cron run indefinitely. The loop should catch/log errors per-reminder and continue, and each delete should be executed immediately rather than deferred to a batched Promise.all after the loop.

title: immediateDelete branch cancels in SendGrid but never deletes the WorkflowReminder row
body: When `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is called with `immediateDelete=true` (lines 213-223), it issues the SendGrid 'cancel' request but returns without deleting or updating the corresponding `workflowReminder` row. Unlike the other two branches (no referenceId -> delete immediately; deferred -> set `cancelled: true`), this path leaves the row in the database indefinitely with `scheduled: true` and `cancelled` unset. The row will only be purged later by the unrelated 'delete all scheduled reminders whose scheduledDate is in the past' cleanup in scheduleEmailReminders.ts, meaning stale WorkflowReminder rows linger in the table (potentially for days) referencing an event that has already been cancelled/replaced, polluting any UI or reporting that reads this table.

title: Reschedule flow bypasses the new batched-cancellation mechanism, risking the original SendGrid pending-cancellation cap bug
body: When rescheduling, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` is called with `immediateDelete=true`, which synchronously calls SendGrid's cancel endpoint right away instead of marking the reminder `cancelled: true` for the throttled CRON-based cancellation introduced by this PR. The PR's stated rationale is that direct/immediate SendGrid cancellations build up against SendGrid's max of 100 pending cancellations and start failing silently, causing reminders to still be sent. By using `immediateDelete=true` here, bulk/rapid rescheduling (e.g. for recurring events or round-robin events) can reintroduce exactly that failure mode for the reschedule flow, even though the booking-cancellation flow (handleCancelBooking.ts) was fixed to defer via the `cancelled` flag.

title: Workflow deletion also bypasses batched cancellation via immediateDelete=true
body: In the `delete` mutation, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` is called for every scheduled reminder belonging to a deleted workflow. As with the reschedule path, this issues a direct SendGrid cancel call per reminder instead of deferring to the new CRON-based cancellation (`cancelled: true`) that this PR introduces specifically to avoid hitting SendGrid's max-100-pending-cancellations limit. Deleting a workflow that has many scheduled reminders can trigger many simultaneous direct cancel calls, risking the same silent-failure scenario the PR is fixing elsewhere, and leaves the corresponding rows undeleted in the DB (see emailReminderManager.ts immediateDelete branch) for every immediate call that doesn't fail.

title: SMS reminder DB row is only deleted if twilio.cancelSMS succeeds, unlike previous unconditional deletion
body: Previously, callers (e.g. handleCancelBooking.ts) unconditionally ran `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` for every reminder regardless of whether the external cancellation call succeeded. Now `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` performs `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` inside the same try block; if `twilio.cancelSMS` throws (e.g. invalid/expired SID, Twilio API error), the subsequent delete is skipped and the error is swallowed by the catch block (just logged). This leaves an orphaned WorkflowReminder row in the database for a cancelled/rescheduled booking, with no retry mechanism, which is a regression in data cleanliness compared to the prior behavior.

title: Cancellation query does not scope to EMAIL method despite being EMAIL/SendGrid-specific logic
body: The query for `remindersToCancel` (lines 44-51) filters only on `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate`, without restricting to `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`. The subsequent code unconditionally treats every matched row as a SendGrid batch (calling the `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` cancel endpoint with `batch_id: reminder.referenceId`). Currently the `cancelled` flag is only ever set for EMAIL reminders, so this works, but the coupling is implicit and fragile — if any future code path sets `cancelled: true` on an SMS reminder, this cron job would incorrectly attempt a SendGrid cancel call against a Twilio reference id.

title: Missing test coverage for the new cancellation/cron logic fixing the reported bug
body: This PR adds a materially new and fairly intricate cancellation flow (cancelled flag set at cancel/reschedule time, consumed by this CRON job up to 1 hour before scheduledDate, interacting with SendGrid's scheduled_sends API) specifically to fix a production bug where reminders for cancelled/rescheduled bookings were still sent. No automated tests were added to validate that cancelled bookings no longer produce sent reminders, that the new `cancelled` flag is correctly set/consumed, or that the batch cancellation endpoint is called with the right parameters, leaving the exact scenario this PR fixes unverified by CI.

title: Cancellation of workflow reminders is fire-and-forget and not awaited before the handler returns
body: The forEach loop calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without awaiting the returned promises, and these calls are not included in the subsequent `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`. Previously, the actual DB deletion of the WorkflowReminder was performed via an awaited `Promise.all` so it was guaranteed to complete before the API response was sent. Now, the deferred-cancellation path relies on an async DB update (`cancelled: true`) inside `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` that is never awaited. In a serverless/Next.js API route, the function execution can be frozen or terminated right after the response is returned, meaning this update may never actually run. If it doesn't run, the reminder keeps `cancelled: null/false` and will still be sent out by the `scheduleEmailReminders` cron, which is exactly the regression this PR is supposed to fix.

title: Rescheduling still uses immediate SendGrid cancellation instead of the new deferred-cancellation mechanism
body: When rescheduling, previous workflow reminders are cancelled via `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` with `immediateDelete=true`, which performs an immediate SendGrid 'scheduled_sends' cancel POST request synchronously (same mechanism described as the root cause of the original bug: too many pending cancellations accumulating and failing once the 100-pending-cancellation quota is hit). Unlike `handleCancelBooking.ts`, which now defers cancellation (sets `cancelled: true` and lets the cron job cancel close to send time), the reschedule flow does not benefit from this fix. Since the PR title explicitly claims to fix reminders for both cancelled AND rescheduled bookings, this inconsistency means the rescheduled-booking scenario can still hit the same SendGrid pending-cancellation limit and fail to cancel stale reminders.

title: A single failed SendGrid cancellation aborts cleanup of the entire cancellation batch
body: The for-loop over `remindersToCancel` performs the SendGrid cancel request and queues a DB delete for each reminder, but the whole loop (and the trailing `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`) is wrapped in one try/catch. If the SendGrid request throws for any single reminder (e.g. transient network error, invalid/expired batch id), the exception propagates out of the loop immediately: remaining reminders in the batch are never processed in this run, and even reminders successfully cancelled with SendGrid earlier in the loop never get their DB delete executed (since `Promise.all` is never reached). This can cause workflow reminders to remain in a 'cancelled but not cleaned-up' state indefinitely if the failure recurs, and prevents other, unrelated reminders scheduled in the same cron tick from being cancelled at all this cycle.

title: remindersToCancel query lacks a method filter for EMAIL reminders
body: The query `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: {...} } })` does not filter by `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`. This endpoint (scheduleEmailReminders) subsequently treats every returned reminder's `referenceId` as a SendGrid `batch_id` and issues a SendGrid cancel request. If an SMS reminder (or any future reminder type) is ever marked `cancelled: true`, this cron job would incorrectly attempt to SendGrid-cancel it using a non-SendGrid reference id (e.g. a Twilio SID), causing an API error and, per the adjacent bug, potentially blocking cancellation of other legitimate email reminders in the same batch.

title: Unrelated UI refactor bundled into a backend bug-fix PR
body: This file's changes (merging the phone-number/sender-id blocks and removing the outer `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` wrapper) are a UI refactor unrelated to the stated purpose of the PR (fixing workflow reminders for cancelled/rescheduled bookings). While the change itself appears benign (it removes an effectively-empty wrapper div when only `isSenderIdNeeded` is true), bundling unrelated UI changes into a critical bug-fix PR makes the change harder to review and increases the risk of unintentionally introducing a UI regression that isn't covered by this PR's testing focus.

title: No automated tests cover the new deferred-cancellation / cron cancellation logic
body: This PR fixes a previously-reported production bug (workflow reminders still sent after cancellation/reschedule) by introducing a new `cancelled` flag and a batch cancellation step inside the `scheduleEmailReminders` cron job. No tests were added to verify that: (1) reminders marked `cancelled` within the 1-hour window are actually cancelled and removed, (2) a failure in one cancellation does not silently prevent cancellation of other reminders in the same run, or (3) the end-to-end flow (cancel booking -> cancelled flag set -> cron cancels in SendGrid) behaves as expected. Given this is explicitly fixing a reported bug, lack of regression tests risks the same issue resurfacing undetected.

title: Reschedule flow still immediately cancels SendGrid-scheduled email reminders, reintroducing the exact bug this PR fixes
body: In the reschedule branch, deleteScheduledEmailReminder is called with immediateDelete=true (`deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`), which calls the SendGrid '/v3/user/scheduled_sends' cancel endpoint synchronously instead of deferring to the new `cancelled` flag + CRON mechanism. The whole point of this PR is that immediate SendGrid cancellation can fail once the account hits the 100-pending-cancellations limit, silently letting the old reminder email go out. By keeping immediateDelete=true specifically for rescheduled bookings (the scenario explicitly named in the PR title), this path is not actually fixed: under load, rescheduled-booking reminder emails can still be sent even though they were supposed to be cancelled. Other call sites (handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings.tsx requestReschedule) correctly omit the third argument so cancellation is deferred.

title: Immediate-delete branch never deletes or updates the WorkflowReminder DB row, leaking orphan records
body: When deleteScheduledEmailReminder is called with immediateDelete=true and a referenceId, the function calls SendGrid to cancel the batch and then returns, without deleting the WorkflowReminder row or marking it cancelled. For call sites where the parent record isn't deleted via cascade afterwards (e.g. handleNewBooking.ts's reschedule flow, which does not delete the original booking or its reminders), this leaves a permanently 'scheduled: true' WorkflowReminder row in the database that is never updated. It will only eventually get swept up by scheduleEmailReminders.ts's blanket 'scheduledDate <= now' deleteMany once its date has passed, meaning stale/incorrect reminder records persist for potentially days.

title: remindersToCancel query lacks a method filter, risking SendGrid API misuse on non-email reminders
body: The `remindersToCancel` query filters only by `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate`, without restricting `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` (unlike the deleteMany cleanup query above it and the unscheduledReminders query below it, both of which filter by method). The subsequent loop unconditionally sends every matched reminder's `referenceId` to the SendGrid `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` cancel endpoint as a `batch_id`. If an SMS WorkflowReminder is ever marked `cancelled: true` (currently not done by the SMS manager, but nothing in the schema or type system prevents it), its Twilio SID would be sent to SendGrid, which would fail or behave unpredictably, and the record would still be deleted from the DB as if it had been properly cancelled via Twilio.

title: A single failed cancellation aborts the whole cancellation batch, leaving earlier successes undeleted
body: The entire cancel loop (SendGrid request + collecting delete promises) is wrapped in one try/catch, and the collected `workflowRemindersToDelete` are only awaited after the for-loop completes. If the SendGrid cancel request throws for any single reminder mid-loop, the exception propagates out of the loop before `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is reached, so none of the already-successfully-cancelled reminders processed earlier in the same run get their DB rows deleted. This causes redundant repeat cancellation calls on the next CRON run and delays cleanup, and masks partial failures since only one generic console.log is emitted for the whole batch.

title: Workflow deletion still cancels all scheduled email reminders immediately instead of deferring
body: In the `delete` mutation, scheduled EMAIL reminders are cancelled with `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` (immediateDelete=true), issuing an immediate SendGrid cancel call for every reminder instead of using the new deferred `cancelled` flag mechanism this PR introduces to avoid the SendGrid pending-cancellations limit. For a popular workflow with many active bookings and scheduled reminders, deleting it could still trigger the same 100-pending-cancellation failure mode described in the PR, silently letting some reminder emails go out despite the workflow being deleted.

title: No automated tests cover the new deferred-cancellation CRON logic
body: This PR introduces the core fix (the `cancelled` flag on WorkflowReminder plus new logic in scheduleEmailReminders.ts to batch-cancel reminders within the next hour), but no tests were added to verify that reminders marked cancelled are correctly filtered by method/date, that the SendGrid cancel call is made with the right batch id, or that DB rows are cleaned up appropriately. Given the bug this PR fixes was itself a silent failure mode (reminders sent despite being 'cancelled'), lack of test coverage for this exact mechanism increases the risk of a future regression going unnoticed.

title: Dynamic imports are invoked eagerly, defeating the purpose of async/lazy loading
body: Each app module is loaded with `import("./appname")` directly inside the object literal (e.g. `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`). These `import()` calls execute immediately when the `appStore` module is evaluated, not lazily when a given app key is actually accessed. This means all app chunks begin loading as soon as anyone imports `appStore`, exactly like the previous static-import approach, except now every consumer must `await` the property access. The PR title/description implies on-demand/code-split loading of apps, but this implementation provides no such benefit while adding overhead (every lookup becomes async) to every call site across the codebase (getCalendar, videoClient, payment helpers, etc.).

title: getCalendarCredentials not updated for async getCalendar, silently changes contract
body: `getCalendar` was changed to be async and return `Promise<Calendar | null>`, but `getCalendarCredentials` (line 28) still calls it without `await`: `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);`. The returned `calendar` field in each credential entry is now a `Promise` instead of a resolved `Calendar` instance. Only the call site inside this same file (`getConnectedCalendars`) was updated to `await item.calendar`. Any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` elsewhere in the codebase that expects a synchronously-resolved `Calendar` object (not shown in this diff) will silently receive an unresolved Promise and break at runtime, since this is a breaking API/contract change that was not fully propagated.

title: getVideoAdapters resolves credentials sequentially instead of in parallel
body: The rewritten `getVideoAdapters` uses a `for...of` loop with `await appStore[appName]` inside, resolving each credential's app module one at a time. Previously this was a synchronous `reduce`. With multiple credentials (e.g. several video integrations configured for a booking), each dynamic import lookup is awaited sequentially rather than concurrently (e.g. via `Promise.all`), unnecessarily serializing what could be parallel async work and adding latency to booking creation/cancellation/update flows that call this function.

title: Async forEach callback races with downstream Promise.all, dropping calendar deletions for recurring bookings
body: In the recurring-event branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => {...})` pushes results into `apiDeletes` inside an async callback that `forEach` does not wait for. Later in the function, `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` is executed, but because the async forEach callbacks (which now also `await getCalendar(credential)`) may not have completed and pushed into `apiDeletes` by that point, some calendar deletion promises can be missing from the awaited list. This can result in calendar events for recurring bookings not being reliably deleted, and the function may return success ('Booking successfully cancelled.') before (or without ever) actually deleting those calendar entries. Note the sibling branch just below (lines ~475-484) was correctly rewritten using a `for...of` loop with `await`, but this branch was left using the broken `.forEach(async...)` pattern.

title: try/catch around forEach(async) cannot catch errors from the awaited getCalendar call
body: The code wraps `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` in a `try { } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }` block. Since `forEach` does not await its async callback, and the callback now does `await getCalendar(...)` (previously synchronous), any rejection thrown inside the callback (e.g. a rejected getCalendar promise or a failing deleteEvent/deleteMeeting call) becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of being caught by the surrounding try/catch. This silently swallows/loses errors that the code intends to log, and can also leave the process with unhandled rejections.

title: Same try/catch-around-forEach(async) issue as in vital/lib/reschedule.ts
body: Identical pattern: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` inside a try/catch that cannot catch rejections thrown inside the async callback. Making `getCalendar` async and awaiting it inside this unawaited forEach callback means calendar/video deletion errors during reschedule are not actually caught or logged as the surrounding try/catch intends, risking silent failures and unhandled promise rejections.

title: requestReschedule mutation does not wait for calendar/video cancellation before resolving
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` is not awaited by the surrounding `requestReschedule` mutation handler. The mutation proceeds (sending webhooks, returning to the client) without waiting for the calendar/video event deletions inside this now-async callback to complete. Since `getCalendar` is now async, each iteration performs an additional await before deleting the event, further increasing the window during which the mutation can complete and respond to the client before cancellation of the old calendar/video events has actually finished, which can cause rescheduled bookings to temporarily (or permanently, if an error occurs) leave stale calendar entries.

title: No tests added for the behavioral change to async app lookups
body: This PR changes `appStore` lookups from synchronous to asynchronous across many critical flows (calendar CRUD, video meeting creation, payment processing, booking cancellation/reschedule). No new or updated tests accompany these changes to verify that awaiting resolves correctly, that errors from unresolved/missing app keys are still handled the same way, or that the various forEach/async patterns behave as expected. Given the breadth of files touched (12 files across core booking/payment/calendar logic), this is a meaningful test gap for a change with this level of risk.

title: forEach callback made async but errors no longer caught by surrounding try/catch
body: The callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(...)` was converted to an `async` function so that `getCalendar` can be awaited. However, `Array.prototype.forEach` never awaits the promises returned by its callback and does not propagate rejections to the caller. Previously the callback was synchronous, so any exception thrown inside it (e.g. from `getCalendar`) was thrown synchronously and caught by the surrounding `try { ... } catch (error) { ... }` block. Now that the callback is async, any error (including a *synchronous* throw now wrapped into a rejected promise) becomes an unhandled promise rejection that bypasses the try/catch entirely. This both silently swallows/escapes expected error handling and means `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`/`deleteMeeting(...)` are fire-and-forget — the function can return before calendar/video cleanup actually completes.

title: forEach callback made async but errors no longer caught by surrounding try/catch
body: Same issue as in vital/lib/reschedule.ts: the `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` callback is now async but forEach does not await it or propagate its rejections. The enclosing `try/catch` can no longer catch errors raised inside the callback (including from the now-async `getCalendar` call), and the calendar/video deletion promises are not awaited, so cleanup may not complete before the function proceeds and errors are silently turned into unhandled promise rejections instead of being logged.

title: Async forEach callback not awaited, deletion races with subsequent email send
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => {...})` was changed to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` so the newly-async `getCalendar` call can be awaited inside it, but `forEach` does not wait for the returned promises. As a result the calendar/video deletion work (`calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`, `deleteMeeting(...)`) is fire-and-forget: the code immediately proceeds to `await sendRequestRescheduleEmail(...)` and webhook dispatch without waiting for cleanup to finish, and any rejection from this async callback becomes an unhandled promise rejection with no error handling (there is no try/catch around this block), unlike the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase.

title: Dynamic app imports resolved sequentially instead of in parallel
body: `getVideoAdapters` was rewritten from a synchronous `reduce` into a `for...of` loop that does `await appStore[appName...]` for each credential one at a time. Since `appStore[appName]` is now a dynamic import `Promise`, awaiting them sequentially in a loop serializes the resolution of all needed app modules instead of resolving them concurrently (e.g. via `Promise.all`). For bookings with multiple video credentials this adds unnecessary latency compared to resolving all needed app chunks in parallel.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise-valued 'calendar' field without updating its own signature
body: `getCalendar` was changed to return `Promise<Calendar | null>`, but `getCalendarCredentials` (still a synchronous function) stores this directly as `calendar` in the objects it returns: `{ integration: app, credential, calendar }`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` in this file was updated to `await item.calendar`. `getCalendarCredentials` is exported from this module and may be consumed elsewhere in the codebase (not part of this diff) expecting a resolved `Calendar | null` value as before; such call sites would now silently receive an unresolved Promise instead of a calendar instance, a breaking change that isn't reflected in the function's own type signature (still implicitly synchronous).

title: All app-store dynamic imports are started eagerly on module load, not on demand
body: The appStore object stores the results of calling `import("./x")` directly as object values, e.g. `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`. Because `import()` is invoked immediately when the object literal is evaluated, every one of the 29 app packages begins loading as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is first imported anywhere (e.g. from `CalendarManager`, `EventManager`, `videoClient`, or any tRPC router), regardless of whether a given request only needs a single app. This does not provide true lazy/on-demand loading per app; it only defers resolution behind a Promise while still eagerly kicking off every import at module-initialization time, which may add unnecessary module loading overhead especially in short-lived serverless/edge invocations.

title: No test coverage added for the sync-to-async conversion of core calendar/video/payment functions
body: This PR changes the public async contract of many widely used, previously-synchronous functions (`getCalendar`, `CalendarManager.deleteEvent/createEvent/updateEvent`, `videoClient.getVideoAdapters/deleteMeeting/createMeeting/updateMeeting`, `handlePayment`/`deletePayment`'s appStore lookup, etc.) across the booking cancellation, rescheduling, and payment refund flows. No new or updated unit/integration tests are included to verify that callers correctly await these functions and that behavior (ordering of calendar deletion vs. email/webhook sending, error propagation) is preserved after the conversion, despite several call sites exhibiting the forEach/async anti-pattern that silently changes error-handling and ordering semantics.

title: Dynamic imports are triggered eagerly, defeating the purpose of async/lazy loading
body: Every property in the appStore object literal calls `import("./appName")` directly as part of module evaluation. Because these import() calls are not wrapped in a function/getter, they execute as soon as `packages/app-store/index.ts` is first required, i.e. all 29 app packages begin loading immediately, exactly like the previous eager `import * as` style, just now wrapped in Promises. Any code path that imports `appStore` (which includes almost all booking/calendar/payment code) will kick off every app's dynamic import regardless of which app is actually needed, so there is no genuine code-splitting/lazy-loading benefit, while every consumer now pays the extra cost of awaiting a Promise. To actually get on-demand loading, each entry would need to be a function (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) invoked only when a specific app key is accessed.

title: forEach(async ...) inside try/catch cannot catch async errors — unhandled rejections and lost error logging
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` is wrapped in a try/catch intended to log errors via `logger.error`, but `Array.prototype.forEach` ignores the promise returned by its async callback and never awaits it. Since `getCalendar` is now async and awaited inside this callback, any rejection (e.g. from `getCalendar` or `calendar.deleteEvent`) happens asynchronously after `forEach` has already returned, so the surrounding try/catch never sees it — the error is silently swallowed as an unhandled promise rejection instead of being logged, and the function can return `true` before the calendar/video cleanup has actually completed or even been attempted successfully.

title: Same forEach(async ...) try/catch defect as vital/lib/reschedule.ts
body: Identical to the vital/lib/reschedule.ts issue: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` is inside a try/catch block that cannot catch rejections thrown by the async callback because forEach doesn't await it. Errors from the now-async `getCalendar` call (or deleteEvent/deleteMeeting) are not logged and the function can resolve before cleanup finishes.

title: Recurring-event calendar deletion still uses unfixed forEach(async ...), unlike the sibling block fixed a few lines below
body: In the recurring-events branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => {...})` pushes results into `apiDeletes` asynchronously, but nothing awaits the promise returned by each forEach callback. Meanwhile the `else` branch directly below (lines ~476-484) was converted in this same PR to a proper `for...of` loop with `await`, showing the author was aware of the pattern but didn't apply the same fix here. As a result, `apiDeletes` may not contain all pending deletions by the time it is passed into `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` later in the function, so some calendar-deletion calls run detached from the request's awaited work and their completion/errors are not guaranteed to be captured before the handler responds.

title: forEach(async ...) with no awaiting or error handling for calendar/video cleanup during reschedule
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` now performs an `await getCalendar(...)` inside an async callback that forEach never awaits and that has no surrounding try/catch. Any failure in `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection, and the subsequent code (sending the reschedule email, firing webhooks) proceeds without waiting for these calendar/video cleanup operations to finish or succeed.

title: No tests added/updated for the new async appStore contract
body: This PR changes the fundamental contract of `appStore` from a synchronous object of modules to an object of Promises, requiring every consumer to `await appStore[key]` (and `getCalendar`, `getVideoAdapters`, etc. to become async). Several call sites across the codebase needed manual fixes in this very PR (some still incomplete, e.g. forEach(async...) patterns). No tests were added to verify that all current and future consumers correctly await these values, leaving the change prone to silent regressions where a missed `await` returns a Promise where a `Calendar`/`VideoApiAdapter` instance was expected.

title: Dayjs objects compared with `===`, condition never true
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two freshly created Dayjs instances by reference. Even when the override's start and end represent the exact same instant (a zero-duration override, typically used to mark a day fully unavailable), this comparison is always false because `===` never compares object/instant equality for Dayjs. The intended branch (treating a zero-length override as blocking) can never execute, silently falling through to the subsequent range checks instead.

title: Working-hours bound check computes identical start/end from slotStartTime, never checking slot end
body: In the new workingHours validation added to `checkIfIsAvailable`, both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime` (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`), so `end` never reflects the actual end of the slot (`slotEndTime`). As written, the check only verifies that the slot's start time is within working hours, but can never detect a slot whose end extends past the working-hours end boundary. Since this check is part of the core fix enforcing fixed-host availability (including date overrides) for round-robin bookings, this bug can let slots that run past a fixed host's working hours be shown as bookable.

title: Date-override matching with Array.find() stops at first same-day override entry, breaking multi-range date overrides
body: The new date override check iterates `dateOverrides.find(...)` to find a day match. If a given day has multiple override time ranges (a common pattern for split-day overrides, e.g. 9-12 and 14-17), the callback sets `dateOverrideExist = true` on the first matching entry and returns `true`/`false` based on only that single range. If the checked slot falls inside a *different* range for the same day, `find` will have already evaluated (and possibly returned true for) the first range, incorrectly marking the slot unavailable even though a later range on the same date would have allowed it. This can incorrectly block valid slots when a date has more than one override interval.

title: Fixed-hosts list recomputed on every slot during filter instead of once
body: `const fixedHosts = userAvailability.filter((availability) => availability.user.isFixed);` is placed inside the `timeSlots.filter` callback, so it is recomputed for every single time slot even though `userAvailability` and the fixed/non-fixed partition do not change across slots. For event types with many slots and many hosts this results in unnecessary repeated filtering work; it should be computed once before the loop.

title: No test added for the primary PR fix: round-robin events respecting fixed hosts' date overrides
body: The PR description states the main bug being fixed is that round-robin events could be booked outside a fixed host's date-override availability. The only new test added ("Check for Date overrides") covers timezone handling for a single-user personal event; there is no test with `schedulingType: "ROUND_ROBIN"` combined with a fixed host (`isFixed: true`) having a date override, which is the scenario explicitly called out in the PR's manual test plan. Without this test, a regression in the round-robin/fixed-host override interaction (e.g. the bugs noted in the workingHours/dateOverrides matching logic in slots.ts) would not be caught by CI.

title: Busy/booked time check is skipped entirely for days with a date override
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, once a date override is detected for the slot's day and the slot falls inside the override's time window, the function returns `true` immediately (`if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }`) before ever reaching the `return busy.every(...)` check at the bottom of the function. This means that for any day on which a host has a date override, existing bookings/busy times for that host on that day are no longer checked at all when determining slot availability. Previously (before this PR) `checkIfIsAvailable` always ran the busy-time check unconditionally. Now, on override days, a user can be shown as available and double-booked into a slot that is already occupied by an existing booking, because the override branch short-circuits before the busy check runs. This directly undermines the booking integrity this function exists to enforce.

title: dayjs instances compared by reference (always false) when detecting all-day/zero-duration overrides
body: The check `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two freshly created dayjs objects with `===`. Since dayjs instances are objects, this reference comparison will always evaluate to false even when the two represent the same instant (e.g. a zero-duration override meant to mark the entire day unavailable). As a result, the intended 'whole day blocked' override case never triggers this branch, and such overrides are silently treated as a regular time range or ignored, which can show slots as available when the organizer explicitly blocked the day. This should use `.isSame()` instead of `===`.

title: Working-hours end check uses slot start time twice instead of slot end time
body: In the new working-hours validation inside checkIfIsAvailable, both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime` (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`), so the comparison `end > workingHour.endTime` never accounts for how long the slot actually runs (eventLength). A slot that starts within working hours but whose end (slotEndTime) extends past the working-hours end time will incorrectly pass this check and be considered available, allowing bookings that run past the end of the organizer's working hours.

title: override.timeZone is optional but used unguarded for offset calculation
body: `TimeRange.timeZone` (packages/types/schedule.d.ts) was added as an optional field, yet getSlots unconditionally does `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. If any caller of getSlots builds dateOverrides without populating `timeZone` (the field is optional and not enforced anywhere in the type system), `.tz(undefined)` will fall back to ambiguous/system-default behavior, producing an incorrect offset and therefore an incorrect override time window silently, rather than failing loudly or falling back to a sane default (e.g. the schedule's own timeZone).

title: No test covers the primary fix: fixed-host date overrides for round-robin events
body: The PR description states its main fix is that date overrides of fixed hosts are now respected for round-robin event types (so round-robin events aren't bookable when a fixed host is unavailable due to an override). However, the only test added in this PR covers date-override timezone conversion for a single-user personal event; there is no round-robin + fixed-host + date-override scenario test. This leaves the headline bug fix of the PR without automated regression coverage.

title: No test exercises date overrides together with existing busy/booked time
body: The 'Check for Date overrides' test only verifies slot generation against working hours/override boundaries with no bookings present. There is no test combining a date override day with an existing booking (busy time) on that same day, which is exactly the scenario affected by the checkIfIsAvailable early-return bug (dateOverrideExist causing the busy-time check to be skipped). Such a test would have caught the double-booking risk introduced by this change.

title: Working-hours end-time check uses slot start time instead of end time
body: In checkIfIsAvailable's new working-hours validation, both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime` (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`). This means the check never actually validates whether the slot's end time exceeds the organizer's working hours — it only ever compares the start time against both boundaries. As a result, bookings that start within working hours but extend past the end of the working window will incorrectly be treated as 'within working hours' and remain bookable, defeating the purpose of this new safeguard.

title: Dayjs objects compared with strict equality always evaluate false
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two freshly constructed Dayjs object instances by reference. Since dayjs() always returns a new object, this condition can never be true, even when start and end actually represent the same instant. The intended special-case handling for zero-duration (point-in-time) date overrides is therefore dead code and will never trigger.

title: Date override lookup only inspects the first matching override per day
body: `dateOverrides.find(...)` stops at the first override entry whose date matches the slot's date and makes the availability decision based solely on that entry, setting `dateOverrideExist = true` as a side effect inside the callback. If a schedule has multiple override time ranges for the same date (which Cal.com's UI allows, e.g. split availability on one date), only the first range in array order is evaluated; subsequent ranges for that date are silently ignored, which can incorrectly mark a slot as unavailable (or available) when a later override entry for the same date would have produced a different result.

title: Timezone offset calculation depends on server's local timezone via Date.toString()
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` and the analogous invitee line convert the Date to a string via `Date.prototype.toString()` before re-parsing with dayjs. `toString()` renders the date using the host process's system timezone, so the resulting calendar date fed into `.tz()` can shift depending on where the Node process runs (and can roll over to an adjacent day near local midnight). This makes the organizer/invitee UTC-offset difference used for date-override conversion non-deterministic across deployment environments, instead of being based purely on the override's actual UTC instant.

title: Duplicated, divergently-implemented date-override timezone logic
body: Date-override timezone adjustment is now implemented twice with different math: once here (DST-diff based, using `dayjs().tz(...).utcOffset() - startOfInviteeDay.tz(...).utcOffset()`), and separately in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts's checkIfIsAvailable (plain `utcOffset()` diff with no DST adjustment). Because both paths independently decide whether an override applies/at what time, and they can diverge (e.g., around DST transitions), the two filters can disagree on the same slot, making the overall availability result inconsistent and harder to reason about or fix in only one place.

title: No test coverage for the headline round-robin fixed-host date-override fix
body: The PR description states its main purpose is fixing that fixed-host date overrides are respected for round-robin events (Fixes #8207), with explicit manual test steps involving a round-robin event with a fixed host and a round-robin host. However, the only test added in this file extends the existing single-user 'Check for Date overrides' test with a different invitee timezone; there is no new test exercising a ROUND_ROBIN event type with a fixed host plus override, nor verifying that round-robin host overrides don't block availability while fixed-host overrides do. This leaves the primary bug fix unverified by automated tests.

title: Migration crashes when no category matches the embed_category setting (the common/default case)
body: `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` assumes the query returns at least one row. Since `embed_category` previously defaulted to an empty string and most installs never set a category whose name equals the setting's raw value, this query will typically return zero rows. Indexing an empty PG::Result with `[0]` yields `nil`, and calling `['id']` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration for essentially every existing installation that hasn't explicitly matched a category name to the `embed_category` setting value. This blocks upgrades rather than falling through to the `uncategorized_category_id` fallback that follows.

title: before_validation callback crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and the following `sub!` are called unconditionally in `before_validation`, without checking whether `host` is nil. If `host` is nil (e.g. the `embeddable_host` param key is missing in the admin controller, or `EmbeddableHost.new` is used without setting host first), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` instead of producing a normal validation error, resulting in an unhandled 500 error rather than a controlled validation failure.

title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError (500) instead of 404 for unknown host id
body: `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns `nil` when the id doesn't exist. In `update`, `save_host(nil)` then calls `host.host = ...` on nil, raising NoMethodError. In `destroy` (line 15-16), `host.destroy` is called on a potentially nil object with the same result. Both actions will produce an unhandled 500 error instead of a proper 404/`render_json_error` response for a missing record.

title: Unescaped string interpolation into raw SQL INSERT during migration
body: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"` interpolates the `h` value (parsed from the pre-existing `embeddable_hosts` site setting) directly into SQL without escaping. If any historical host value contains a single quote or other SQL metacharacter, this migration will fail or behave unexpectedly. The migration should use parameterized execution (e.g., `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`) instead of raw interpolation.

title: No behavioral test coverage for create/update/destroy of embeddable hosts
body: This spec only asserts that `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`. There is no test exercising `create`, `update`, or `destroy`, no test for validation failures, no test for the not-found path (which, per the controller bug, currently 500s), and no test confirming staff-only access is enforced in practice. Given this controller manages the whitelist of hosts allowed to embed content (a security-sensitive feature), the lack of functional test coverage is a significant gap.

title: No behavioral test coverage for the embedding show/update actions
body: This spec, like the embeddable_hosts_controller spec, only checks the class hierarchy. There's no test verifying `show` or `update` actually renders the expected serialized `embedding` payload containing `embeddable_hosts`, nor any check of the `fetch_embedding` before_filter behavior.

title: Plural `_ids` hydration doesn't guard against failed subtype lookups
body: In the new pluralized branch of `_hydrateEmbedded`, `obj[k].map(id => self._lookupSubType(subType, type, id, root))` is assigned directly to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]` without filtering out `undefined` results, unlike the singular branch which only assigns when `hydrated` is truthy. If any id in the `_ids` array doesn't resolve to an object in the root payload's corresponding collection (e.g. a `color_ids` entry not present in the sideloaded `colors` array), the resulting array will contain `undefined` entries, which can cause runtime errors when templates/components call `.get()` on those entries.

title: Client-side category badge can diverge from server-assigned category when none is chosen
body: After `host.save(props)` succeeds, the component does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`. If no category was selected (`categoryId` is null), this sets `category` to `undefined`, while the server (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`) falls back to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` for blank category_id. This leaves the UI showing no/blank category badge even though the host was actually persisted with the uncategorized category, until a full page reload re-fetches the correct data.

title: No pretender mocks added for the new admin embedding endpoints
body: This PR adds new client-side adapters/controllers/routes/components for managing embeddable hosts (`GET/PUT /admin/customize/embedding`, `POST/PUT/DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts`), but no corresponding mock endpoints were added to the test pretender, and no new JS test files were added to exercise the admin-embedding route/controller/component. This leaves the entire new admin UI feature without JS test coverage.

title: Migration crashes with NoMethodError on nil when no matching site_settings row exists
body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` assumes the query returns at least one row. Discourse only persists a `site_settings` row when a setting has been explicitly changed from its default; most installs never set `embed_category`, so this query returns zero rows. `result[0]` is then `nil`, and calling `['id']` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`, crashing the migration for the vast majority of existing installations that never customized `embed_category`. The same pattern is repeated on the fallback query for `uncategorized_category_id`, which also may not have a persisted row.

title: Unsanitized string interpolation into raw SQL INSERT
body: The migration builds an INSERT statement by directly interpolating `h` (a value parsed from the pre-existing `embeddable_hosts` site setting) into the SQL string: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If the stored host value contains a single quote or other SQL metacharacters, this breaks the statement or allows SQL injection into the running migration. Values should be escaped (e.g. via `connection.quote` / parameterized execution) rather than interpolated raw.

title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
body: The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice without checking for nil. If `host` is not supplied (e.g. a direct API POST to `/admin/embeddable_hosts` without the `host` param, or any caller that leaves it blank), `self.host` is `nil` and `nil.sub!` raises `NoMethodError`, causing an unhandled 500 error instead of a normal validation failure. The code should guard with something like `self.host = self.host.to_s` before calling `sub!`, or skip the block entirely when host is blank.

title: destroy action crashes if the record does not exist
body: `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first; host.destroy` will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil` if no record matches `params[:id]` (e.g. the host was already deleted in another browser tab/session, or an invalid id is supplied). This should use `find` with rescue/404 handling or check for `host.present?` before calling `destroy`, otherwise a routine double-delete causes an unhandled 500 instead of a clean 404.

title: update action crashes if the record does not exist
body: In the `update` action, `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return `nil` for an invalid/missing id, and `save_host(host)` then calls `host.host = ...` on `nil`, raising `NoMethodError` and returning an unhandled 500 instead of a proper error response.

title: Fabricator file content no longer matches its filename
body: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines the `:embeddable_host` fabricator (host/category) instead of category fabricators, while the newly added `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators. The file names and their contents are swapped, which will confuse future maintainers looking for category fabricators in `category_fabricator.rb` or the host fabricator in a file literally named for it.

title: File named embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains category fabricators, not the host fabricator
body: This newly added file is named for the embeddable host fabricator but its content is the category/diff_category/happy_category/private_category fabricators (previously in category_fabricator.rb). This is the counterpart of the mismatch in category_fabricator.rb and should be corrected so file names reflect their contents.

title: No functional tests for create/update/destroy actions
body: The spec for `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` only asserts that it is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`. There are no tests covering `create`, `update`, or `destroy`, including no coverage for validation failures, missing-record scenarios (which currently crash with NoMethodError, see other findings), or successful serialization output. This leaves the new admin endpoints essentially untested.

title: No functional tests for show/update actions
body: The spec for `Admin::EmbeddingController` only asserts the controller's superclass. There is no test verifying that `show`/`update` return the expected serialized `embeddable_hosts` list, or that staff-only access is enforced, leaving the new endpoint's actual behavior unverified.

title: "find embedded" test does not actually validate fetching by the requested id
body: The test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` but then asserts properties (2 colors with ids 1 and 2) that belong to fruit id 1 in the fixture data, not fruit id 2 (which only has one color, id 3). This passes only because the pretender stub for `/fruits/:id` (in create-pretender.js.es6) ignores the requested id and always returns `fruits[0]`. The test name and the id passed to `find` suggest it is testing per-id embedded hydration, but it is not actually exercising that path correctly, and would silently pass even if id-based lookup were broken.

title: No tests added for new admin embedding UI components/controllers/routes
body: This PR introduces a nontrivial new admin UI (embeddable-host component with inline edit/save/cancel/delete, admin-embedding controller/route, adapter) but adds no JS unit or acceptance tests exercising add/edit/delete host flows, category selection, or error handling (e.g. popupAjaxError on save failure). Given the backend bugs identified elsewhere (nil-record crashes), tests here would likely have caught them before merge.

title: Migration crashes when 'embed_category' site_setting was never customized
body: The migration does `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. Site settings are normally only persisted in the `site_settings` table when an admin has explicitly changed them from their default value. Since `embed_category` defaulted to `''`, the vast majority of installations will have no row with `name = 'embed_category'`, so the query returns zero rows and `execute(...)[0]` is `nil`. Calling `['id']` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration for essentially every typical install (and for test/CI databases that never touched this setting). The fallback for `category_id == 0` is never reached because the exception happens before it.

title: Unescaped string interpolation in raw SQL INSERT
body: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"` interpolates the `host` value (pulled from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting, which could contain arbitrary characters such as single quotes) directly into the SQL string without using `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote` or parameter binding. A host value containing a single quote will break the INSERT (syntax error, migration failure) or corrupt the migration's intent; this is a data-integrity risk in the migration path.

title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `before_validation { self.host.sub!(...); self.host.sub!(...) }` assumes `host` is always a String. If `host` is nil (e.g. the admin submits the form with no host value, or `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is missing as set in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`), `self.host.sub!` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` instead of surfacing a normal `validates_format_of`/presence validation error. This turns a user input mistake into an unhandled 500 error.

title: update/destroy do not handle a missing EmbeddableHost record
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns `nil` when no matching record exists. In `update`, the subsequent `save_host(host)` call will do `host.host = ...` on `nil`, raising `NoMethodError`. In `destroy` (line 15-16), `host.destroy` is called directly on a possibly-nil object, also raising `NoMethodError`. Neither action returns a proper 404/error response for an invalid id; both will surface as unhandled 500 errors instead.

title: Fabricator file content doesn't match its filename (content appears swapped)
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now only defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the newly-added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines `Fabricator(:category)`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category`. The contents of the two files appear to have been swapped: the category fabricators ended up in the file named for embeddable hosts, and vice versa. Fabrication doesn't care about filenames so tests still pass, but this is confusing and will mislead future maintainers looking for category or embeddable-host fabricators by filename.

title: New controller spec only checks class inheritance, not actual behavior
body: The spec for `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` only asserts `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`. None of the new `create`, `update`, or `destroy` actions (including the error paths discussed above, such as missing-id handling or invalid host validation) are exercised, leaving the new admin endpoints for managing embeddable hosts essentially untested.

title: New controller spec only checks class inheritance, not actual behavior
body: Similar to the embeddable_hosts controller spec, this spec for `Admin::EmbeddingController` only checks that it is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`. The `show`/`update` actions and the `fetch_embedding` before_filter are not tested at all, so regressions in the embedding admin endpoint would not be caught.

title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the 4-argument version
body: Two class methods named `downsize` are defined: one with signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (lines 145-147) and immediately after another with signature `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (lines 149-151). In Ruby the second definition completely replaces the first, so the 4-positional-argument form is dead code and no longer callable. Any existing caller elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. thumbnail generation code) that still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height, opts)` will now raise an ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments) because the method only accepts 2 positional args plus opts. This is a breaking API change that is easy to miss since Ruby only emits a silent 'method redefined' warning.

title: Hardcoded 10MB upload size replaces configurable site settings
body: `validateUploadedFile` used to read `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, allowing admins to configure separate size limits for images vs. attachments. It is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` KB for all upload types, so the `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` site settings are silently ignored on the client side. This creates an inconsistency with the server, which still reads `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` in `uploads_controller.rb` for the new downsizing feature, meaning client-side validation no longer matches server-side behavior for sites that configure a limit different from 10MB.

title: Hardcoded 10MB value in displayErrorForUpload loses configured max_image_size_kb
body: `displayErrorForUpload` previously read `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to show the correct configured limit in the 413 error message. It is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` KB, so the error message shown to users will be wrong whenever an admin configures a different `max_image_size_kb` value, misleading users about the actual upload limit.

title: Hardcoded 10MB download cap for API URL uploads ignores max_image_size_kb setting
body: `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` was changed to `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`. This removes respect for the admin-configured `max_image_size_kb` setting when downloading images via API URL, allowing files up to 10MB regardless of the configured limit. While the new downsizing logic will later try to shrink the file, this silently changes the download-time cap for all sites, including those that intentionally set a stricter limit, and is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase which still references `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` elsewhere (e.g. `migrate_to_new_scheme`).

title: In-place downsizing writes output over the same file being read, risking corruption
body: The downsizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, using the same path for both source and destination. Image tools such as ImageMagick's `convert` and `gifsicle` are not guaranteed to be safe when input and output paths are identical — depending on how they open/truncate the output file, this can corrupt or truncate the file mid-read, especially for multi-frame/animated GIFs processed via gifsicle. This can result in a corrupted or zero-byte image being uploaded instead of a properly downsized one, with no validation afterward to catch this failure mode.

title: Return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored, allowing silent failures and oversized uploads
body: The loop `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but never checks its boolean return value (it returns false on failure, e.g. ImageMagick exits non-zero). If downsizing fails, the loop will burn through all 5 attempts without reducing size and the code falls through to `Upload.create_for` and uploads a file that still exceeds `max_image_size_kb`, with no error reported to the user or logged specifically for this scenario, defeating the purpose of the size limit.

title: No tests added for new automatic downsizing behavior
body: The PR introduces non-trivial new logic (retry loop with a hardcoded attempt limit, size comparisons, and reliance on `OptimizedImage.downsize`) in `create_upload`, as well as a signature change in `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize`. No spec changes are included to cover the new downsizing loop (e.g., verifying it stops after reaching the limit, after exhausting attempts, or that it is skipped for non-image uploads), leaving this feature and the related method signature change unverified by automated tests.

title: Duplicate `self.downsize` method definition overrides the 4-argument version
body: Two class methods named `downsize` are defined: one at line 145 taking `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and another at line 149 taking `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby, the second definition completely replaces the first. Any existing caller elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. thumbnail-generation jobs) that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height, opts)` with four positional arguments will now raise an ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments) because only the 3-arg version is reachable. This silently removes the old API contract and will break any code outside this diff that still uses the old signature.

title: Downsize loop does not verify success and can silently exceed configured max size
body: The new loop (lines 64-70) calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` up to 5 times while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, but it never checks the boolean return value of `downsize` (which returns false on failure, e.g. ImageMagick error). If a downsize attempt fails, the loop just burns an attempt without actually shrinking the file, and after 5 failed/insufficient attempts the code proceeds to create the upload anyway, silently allowing an image larger than `max_image_size_kb` to be stored — defeating the purpose of the limit without any error being surfaced to the user or logs.

title: In-place downsize uses identical path for source and destination
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` passes the same path as both `from` and `to`. For animated GIFs this dispatches to `gifsicle ... --output #{to}` with `from == to`, and for static images to ImageMagick `convert`. Overwriting the same file that is simultaneously used as input is risky (depending on tool buffering behavior) and can produce a truncated/corrupted file if the external process fails partway or does not fully buffer input before writing output, resulting in a corrupted upload being stored for the user.

title: API URL download size limit hardcoded, ignoring site setting
body: The download size cap for API-provided URLs was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. This removes administrator control over the maximum allowed download size for API uploads; sites configured with a smaller `max_image_size_kb` will now allow downloads up to 10MB regardless, and sites that intentionally allowed larger downloads via the setting are now capped at 10MB. This is a behavior/API contract change that isn't mentioned in the PR description and isn't configurable.

title: Client-side upload size validation hardcoded, ignoring per-type site settings
body: `validateUploadedFile` previously computed `maxSizeKB` from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, honoring separate configured limits for images vs. attachments. It is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` (10MB) for all upload types, so admin-configured limits (e.g. a smaller max_attachment_size_kb, or any limit different from 10MB) are no longer enforced client-side. This creates inconsistent behavior between client-side pre-validation and actual server-side limits, confusing users with incorrect error messages or allowing oversized attachments to be submitted before failing server-side.

title: 413 error handler hardcodes max size instead of using the image-specific site setting
body: `displayErrorForUpload` previously read `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to report the correct max size in the 413 (entity too large) error message. It is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024`, so the error message shown to the user may not match the actual configured (or newly auto-downsized) limit, producing a misleading error message when the real limit differs from 10MB.

title: No test coverage for new automatic image downsizing behavior
body: The PR adds a non-trivial feature (automatically downsizing oversized images on upload, with a retry loop and in-place file modification) but includes no new or updated tests for `UploadsController#create_upload` covering: successful downsizing under the limit, downsizing failing to converge within 5 attempts, or the interaction with `allow_animated_thumbnails`. This is a user-facing behavioral change with no verification that it works as intended.

title: Duplicate `self.downsize` method definition silently overrides the width/height variant
body: Two class methods named `downsize` are defined: one accepting `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) and a second accepting `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149). Ruby allows method redefinition, so the second definition completely replaces the first — the width/height variant becomes dead code and unreachable. Any existing caller elsewhere in the codebase that still invokes `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height, opts)` with 5 positional arguments will now raise an ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments) because the active method only accepts 3 positional args plus an options hash. This is an undocumented, breaking change to the public API of `OptimizedImage.downsize` and the first definition should be removed or the overload properly consolidated.

title: Hardcoded 10MB download cap ignores SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb
body: The API URL-download path now uses a hardcoded `10.megabytes` limit instead of the configurable `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` that was previously used. This removes admin control over the maximum download size for API-sourced uploads (both images and non-image attachments go through this code path), and is inconsistent with the newly-added downsizing logic a few lines below that still reads `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` to decide when to shrink an image. Admins who configure a smaller max image/attachment size will no longer have that limit enforced for URL-based uploads.

title: Hardcoded 10MB client-side file size limit ignores per-type SiteSettings
body: `validateUploadedFile` previously computed `maxSizeKB` from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, allowing separate configurable limits for images vs attachments. It now hardcodes `10 * 1024` KB for all upload types, so admin-configured `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` settings are no longer respected client-side. This creates an inconsistency with server-side logic (uploads_controller.rb) which still consults `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, and silently changes the enforced limit for attachments regardless of what the admin configured.

title: 413 error handler reports a hardcoded 10MB limit instead of the configured value
body: In `displayErrorForUpload`, the 413 (entity too large) handler now hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. The error message shown to the user will state an incorrect maximum size whenever the site is configured with a different `max_image_size_kb` value, misleading users about the actual upload limit.

title: No test coverage for the new automatic image downsizing feature
