body: The PR adds a non-trivial feature — automatically downsizing images larger than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` by iteratively calling `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to 5 times — but no tests were added or updated for `uploads_controller.rb` or `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` to verify this logic (e.g., that it stops once the file is small enough, that it gives up after 5 attempts, that it uses the correct dimensions string, or that non-image uploads/API-only cases work as expected). Given the signature changes to `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` and the new retry loop, this is a risky area to leave untested.

title: In-place downsizing with identical from/to path risks data corruption and silent oversized uploads
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` uses the same path for both source and destination. For animated GIFs this is routed to `gifsicle --output <path>` with the same input and output path (see `resize_instructions_animated`/`downsize_instructions_animated` in optimized_image.rb); depending on how gifsicle buffers input before writing, this can truncate/corrupt the source file while it is still being read. Additionally, if `OptimizedImage.downsize` fails (returns false, e.g., ImageMagick/gifsicle missing or erroring) the loop still decrements `attempt` without any error reported to the user, and if the file is still over the limit after 5 attempts, the upload proceeds silently with the oversized file instead of surfacing an error to the caller.

title: Unhandled nil TopicUser causes 500 error in unsubscribe action
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (e.g. a user who navigates directly to the unsubscribe URL for a topic they were never notified about or that never created a topic_user row). The following lines immediately call `tu.notification_level` and `tu.save!` without a nil check, which will raise `NoMethodError` and produce an unhandled 500 error instead of a graceful response.

title: State-changing action exposed via GET request (CSRF exposure)
body: The `unsubscribe` action mutates persistent state (changes `TopicUser#notification_level`) but is routed as a GET endpoint (`config/routes.rb`: `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`). Rails' CSRF protection by default only guards unsafe (non-GET) verbs, so this endpoint is not covered by CSRF tokens. Any third party page can trigger this mutation for a logged-in user simply by causing their browser to issue a GET to this URL (e.g. via an `` tag, link prefetching, or crawler), silently changing/muting their topic notification settings without consent.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url but is not validated
body: `config/locales/server.en.yml`'s `unsubscribe_link` string was changed to embed `%{unsubscribe_url}`, and `MessageBuilder#html_part`/`#body` render it via `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true. There is no guard ensuring `unsubscribe_url` is present in `template_args` for every caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Any current or future caller (mailer or plugin) that enables `add_unsubscribe_link` without supplying `unsubscribe_url` will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` at email-build time, breaking that notification entirely.

title: Template path inconsistent with flat route/controller naming, may fail to resolve
body: The new route is registered with a flat name `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', ...)` in app-route-map.js.es6, and its controller/view are placed using the matching flat naming convention (`controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`). However the template was placed in a nested path `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` instead of the flat `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`. Under the classic Ember resolver conventions used elsewhere in this codebase, a flat route name resolves to a flat (dasherized) template name, not a nested directory path. This mismatch risks the template not being found/resolved for the `topicUnsubscribe` route, resulting in a blank or broken unsubscribe page.

title: Misspelled property name 'stopNotificiationsText'
body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (missing an 'a', should be `stopNotificationsText`). It's used consistently in the matching template (`{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`) so it functions, but the typo will confuse future maintainers and complicate searching/refactoring this code.

title: No test coverage verifying the unsubscribe_url is actually rendered in the email
body: The test fixture `message_with_unsubscribe` now passes `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"`, but none of the existing assertions check that this URL is actually interpolated into the rendered `unsubscribe_link` text/body/html_part. The only assertion reused (`has the user preferences url in the body`) predates this change and does not exercise the new per-topic unsubscribe link behavior, so a regression in the `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation (e.g. missing argument errors, or the URL simply not appearing) would not be caught by this spec.

title: No controller specs added for the new unsubscribe action
body: The PR introduces a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action with non-trivial branching logic (slug mismatch redirect, notification level toggling between muted/regular/tracking/watching, nil-handling risk noted separately), and a new `Topic#unsubscribe_url` helper, but no new or updated controller/model specs were added to verify this behavior (e.g. correct notification level transitions, redirect behavior on slug mismatch, response format handling).

title: State-changing unsubscribe action exposed via unauthenticated-safe GET with no CSRF protection
body: The new `unsubscribe` action mutates a user's notification_level (a persisted side effect) but is only reachable via GET requests (see config/routes.rb: `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`). Rails' CSRF protection only guards unsafe HTTP verbs (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE); GET requests are exempt. Because the action relies on the logged-in session (`current_user`) rather than a signed token (unlike the existing `email/unsubscribe/:key` flow which uses a token), any third-party page can trigger this state change for a logged-in user simply by loading an `` tag or link pointing at this URL, silently muting/changing their topic notification preference without consent (CSRF).

title: unsubscribe action can crash with NoMethodError if no TopicUser record exists
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (e.g. if the TopicUser row was never created, got deleted, or the user visits the unsubscribe link without a prior TopicUser record). The subsequent code immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and `tu.notification_level =`, which will raise NoMethodError on nil, causing a 500 error instead of gracefully creating/updating the record (as `TopicUser.change` would do).

title: Unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change, losing audit fields and realtime notification
body: The notification_level is updated directly on the `TopicUser` record and saved with `tu.save!`, bypassing the `TopicUser.change` class method used everywhere else in the codebase for this purpose. This means `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not updated, and the MessageBus publish of `notification_level_change` (used to keep other open tabs/clients in sync) is skipped. Because `notifications_reason_id` is left unset, later logic such as `TopicUser.auto_track` (which checks `notifications_reason_id: nil` to decide whether to auto-upgrade tracking level) may silently override the user's explicit unsubscribe choice the next time they interact with the topic.

title: Template placed at wrong path for the new top-level 'topicUnsubscribe' route
body: The route is registered as a flat, non-nested route: `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' });` in app-route-map.js.es6, which (per the naming convention used throughout this codebase, e.g. the matching controller `controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` and view `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`) should resolve to a template at `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`. Instead the template was added at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which is the path convention for a nested route like `topic.unsubscribe` under the `topic` resource — a route that does not exist. This mismatch means the dedicated unsubscribe route likely renders without its intended template (blank page) or errors, defeating the purpose of the feature.

title: New route path may be shadowed by existing dynamic segment route
body: `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' });` is declared after the `topic` resource, which already defines `fromParamsNear` with path `/t/:slug/:id/:nearPost`. Both patterns can match a URL like `/t/some-slug/123/unsubscribe`, with `:nearPost` capturing the literal string "unsubscribe". Depending on router/route-recognizer resolution order and specificity rules, requests to the unsubscribe URL risk being routed to `topic.fromParamsNear` instead of the new `topicUnsubscribe` route, breaking the feature or throwing an error when `nearPost="unsubscribe"` is used as a post number in `postStream.closestPostForPostNumber`.

title: No tests added for the new unsubscribe controller action or Topic#unsubscribe_url
body: This PR adds a new controller action (`TopicsController#unsubscribe`) that mutates notification state, a new model method (`Topic#unsubscribe_url`), and new routes, but no controller or model specs were added to cover the happy path, the nil-TopicUser edge case, the slug-mismatch redirect, or the toggle logic between regular/muted/tracking/watching. Only an unrelated mailer spec (`message_builder_spec.rb`) was minimally updated to pass an `unsubscribe_url` option.

title: Misspelled property name 'stopNotificiationsText'
body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (missing an 'a', should be `stopNotificationsText`). It still works because the template references the same misspelled name, but the typo will confuse future maintainers and makes the code harder to search/grep for related functionality.

title: State-mutating action performed via GET request
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe is only reachable via GET routes (config/routes.rb: `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) yet it mutates `TopicUser#notification_level` and persists it with `tu.save!`. GET requests are expected to be idempotent/safe; browsers/email clients routinely prefetch or re-request GET URLs (link previews, safe-link scanners, page refresh), and because the user must already be logged in (added to `ensure_logged_in`), a logged-in user who simply reloads the unsubscribe page, or who is tricked into navigating to this URL from a third-party page (GET requests are not blocked by SameSite=Lax on top-level navigation), will have their notification level silently changed again. Worse, the toggle logic is not actually idempotent: on the second invocation it moves the state from `regular` to `muted`, progressively down-grading notifications on every reload instead of leaving state unchanged. This should require POST/PUT with explicit CSRF protection, or be made properly idempotent.

title: Possible NoMethodError when TopicUser record does not exist
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (e.g. if the TopicUser row for this user/topic was never created or was deleted), and the following code immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and `tu.notification_level =`, which will raise NoMethodError on nil and return a 500 error instead of gracefully handling the case. There is no `TopicUser.find_or_initialize_by` fallback or nil guard.

title: Template placed at wrong path for the new top-level 'topicUnsubscribe' route
body: The route is registered as a top-level, non-nested route: `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' });` in app-route-map.js.es6, and its matching controller/view files are dasherized at the top level (`controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`). However the template is placed in a nested folder as `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which is the convention used for routes nested under the `topic` resource (e.g. topic.fromParams), not for a standalone dasherized route name. This mismatch is likely to cause the Ember resolver to fail to find the template for the `topicUnsubscribe` route, breaking the newly added feature entirely.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url, breaking other callers of build_email
body: The `unsubscribe_link` i18n string (config/locales/server.en.yml) now contains a new interpolation placeholder `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `html_part` and `body` both call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true, without ensuring `unsubscribe_url` is present in `template_args`. Any existing caller of `build_email`/`MessageBuilder` that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but does not also pass `unsubscribe_url` (for example other mailers not touched by this PR, or future/plugin code) will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` instead of rendering the email. This is confirmed by the fact that the existing spec in message_builder_spec.rb had to be updated to add `unsubscribe_url` just to keep passing.

title: unsubscribe_link changed to multiline block scalar without stripping trailing newline
body: `unsubscribe_link` was changed from a single-line scalar to a `|` block scalar, which by default preserves a trailing newline. Since `body` appends this string with `body << "\n"; body << I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', ...)`, the resulting plain-text email body will contain extra trailing whitespace/newlines that weren't present before. Using `|-` (strip) would avoid the extra blank line.

title: Misspelled method/translation key name 'stopNotificiationsText'
body: The computed property and its backing translation key use the misspelling 'Notificiations' instead of 'Notifications' (also mirrored in client.en.yml's `stop_notifications` key use and the template). While internally consistent, this typo will persist in the codebase and confuse future maintainers who search for 'notifications'.

title: No controller spec added for the new unsubscribe action
body: The PR adds a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action with non-trivial branching logic (slug mismatch redirect, notification level toggling, nil TopicUser handling) but no request/controller spec was added to cover it. Only an unrelated small change to message_builder_spec.rb was made. The new behavior (including the non-idempotent toggle noted above) is untested.

title: Blocked email matching is case-sensitive, allowing trivial bypass
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` using the raw email string exactly as submitted by the user, with no downcasing/normalization. Since the User model does not appear to normalize/downcase the email before validation runs (normalization such as Email.downcase is only used elsewhere, e.g. find_by_username_or_email), an attacker can trivially bypass a block entry such as 'spam@evil.com' by signing up with 'Spam@Evil.com' or any different casing. This defeats the entire purpose of the blocked-email feature.

title: Non-atomic counter update is subject to lost updates under concurrency
body: should_block? loads the record, then does `record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save` as separate read-then-write steps. If two signup/validation requests hit the same blocked email concurrently, both will read the same match_count, increment it independently, and the last writer wins, silently losing one of the increments. For a feature meant to produce accurate abuse statistics, this is a legitimate data-integrity concern that should use an atomic UPDATE (e.g. `update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', ...])`).

title: Email validation (and its side effects) runs twice per signup, double-counting blocked-email statistics
body: In `create`, `user.valid?` is called first (left operand of `&&`, so it always executes regardless of `call_discourse_hub?`), and later `user.save` triggers the full validation chain again. Because `EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which has the side effect of incrementing `match_count` and updating `last_match_at` on every invocation, a single signup attempt against a blocked email will increment the counter twice instead of once, corrupting the abuse statistics the feature is meant to produce.

title: No test coverage for the migrated whitelist/blacklist domain validation logic
body: The whitelist/blacklist domain-restriction logic (`email_domains_whitelist`/`email_domains_blacklist`) was moved out of User#email_validator into this new EmailValidator class, but spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb only exercises the new 'blocked email' branch (lines 9-21) via stubbed BlockedEmail.should_block?. There is no test verifying that the whitelist/blacklist branches still add the `not_allowed` error correctly after being refactored into this class, so a regression in that previously-tested behavior would go unnoticed.

title: Structured per-field errors and submitted values now exposed on signup failure, enabling account/field enumeration
body: The `create` action's failure response now includes `errors: user.errors.to_hash` and `values: user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")` in addition to the message. Previously only a combined message string was returned. Returning a machine-readable mapping of which specific field failed (e.g. `errors: {email: ["has already been taken"]}`) makes it trivial for an automated script to enumerate which emails/usernames are already registered or blocked, which is a stronger enumeration primitive than the prior free-text message.

title: rejectedEmails permanently blacklists an email for any email-related server error, not just blocked/invalid emails
body: In createAccount's failure handler, any response where `result.errors.email` is present causes `result.values.email` to be pushed into `rejectedEmails` forever (for the life of the controller instance), regardless of the actual reason for the email error (blocked email, domain restriction, transient server/DiscourseHub failure, etc.). Once added, `emailValidation` will always report that email as failed even if the underlying condition was transient or already resolved (e.g. a temporary DiscourseHub timeout), preventing the user from ever resubmitting that same email in the same session without reloading the page.

title: Non-atomic match_count update causes lost updates under concurrent requests
body: `should_block?` reads the record, increments `match_count` in Ruby, and then calls `save`. If multiple requests for the same blocked email arrive concurrently (a very plausible scenario since this is specifically meant to catch repeated spam signups), the read-modify-write is not atomic: two processes can read the same `match_count`, each increment it locally, and the last `save` wins, silently losing one of the increments. This makes the match_count/last_match_at statistics unreliable exactly in the high-traffic/spam scenario this feature is designed for. Should use an atomic increment, e.g. `update_counters` or a raw SQL `UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1`.

title: Validation (and thus BlockedEmail.should_block?) runs twice per signup, double-counting match stats
body: `create` calls `user.valid?` explicitly (to decide whether to call `DiscourseHub.register_nickname`) and then calls `user.save`, which runs full validations again internally. Because `EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` as a side effect on every validation pass, a single signup attempt against a blocked email will increment `match_count` and update `last_match_at` twice instead of once, corrupting the statistics the feature is meant to track.

title: Blocked-email matching is case-sensitive, allowing trivial bypass
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` looks up `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` with an exact (case-sensitive) match, and the migration (`db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb`) creates a case-sensitive unique index on `email`. Nothing in the signup path downcases the submitted email before it reaches this check (unlike `change_email`, which explicitly does `Email.downcase`). A blocked user can bypass the block entirely by altering the case of their email address (e.g. `Spammer@Example.com` instead of `spammer@example.com`), and the uniqueness validation on `BlockedEmail` would also allow two rows that are the same address but differ only in case.

title: Error payload lets clients distinguish 'blocked' from other validation failures, enabling email-blocklist enumeration
body: The `create` action now returns `errors: user.errors.to_hash` plus the submitted `values`, and the new `user.email.blocked` message ("is not allowed.") is textually distinct from the existing `user.email.not_allowed` message ("is not allowed from that email provider..."). Combined with the JS controller surfacing per-field validation state immediately, this lets an attacker probe arbitrary email addresses against the signup endpoint and determine, based on the returned message, which addresses are present in the `blocked_emails` table versus merely domain-restricted. This creates an oracle for enumerating or testing the blocklist.

title: rejectedEmails array is a shared instance across all controller instances/sessions
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is declared directly on the Ember object literal passed to `extend`, so the array is created once when the class is defined rather than per-instance in `init`. If `CreateAccountController` is ever instantiated more than once (e.g., re-created on route transition, tests, or any code path that doesn't reuse a true singleton), all instances will share and mutate the same array, so rejected emails from one session/user can leak into another and the list is never actually reset. Even for a singleton controller, there is no code path that clears `rejectedEmails`, so once an email is rejected it is permanently flagged invalid client-side for the remainder of the page's life, even if the server-side condition causing the rejection (e.g., a temporarily blocked email) is later resolved.

title: No tests for the migrated domain whitelist/blacklist validation logic
body: This file now contains the domain whitelist/blacklist logic that used to live in `User#email_validator` (removed from `app/models/user.rb`), but `spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb` only tests the new `BlockedEmail.should_block?` branch. There is no test coverage in this PR for `email_domains_whitelist`/`email_domains_blacklist` behavior in its new location, so a regression in that migrated logic (e.g., broken regex construction, broken short-circuit ordering with the new blocked-email check) would go undetected.

title: Blocked-email matching is case sensitive, allowing trivial bypass
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` does `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` using the raw email string passed in from the validator (which in turn comes from `user.email`, which is never normalized/downcased before this check). Since the comparison is a case-sensitive SQL match (and the unique index on `blocked_emails.email` is also case sensitive), an email that was blocked as `bad@spammers.org` can be bypassed simply by registering as `Bad@Spammers.org` or `BAD@SPAMMERS.ORG`. This defeats the entire purpose of the blocked-email feature.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write race condition on match_count/last_match_at
body: `should_block?` loads the record, increments `match_count` in Ruby, sets `last_match_at`, and calls `save`. Under concurrent signup attempts for the same blocked email, two requests can both read the same `match_count`, increment it independently, and save, causing lost updates (the counter under-reports actual match attempts). This should use an atomic update (e.g. `update_counters`/`UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1`) instead of load-then-save.

title: should_block? side-effects run multiple times per signup attempt, inflating match_count
body: `should_block?` is called from the `email` EachValidator, which runs every time `valid?`/`save` triggers validations. In `UsersController#create` (app/controllers/users_controller.rb), `user.valid?` is called once (to decide whether to call DiscourseHub), and then `user.save` triggers validations again internally. This means a single signup attempt against a blocked email can increment `match_count` by 2 (or more, if other code paths call `valid?`), making the recorded match statistics inaccurate and misleading for any analysis or reporting based on `match_count`/`last_match_at`.

title: Account-creation failure response now leaks raw validation errors and submitted email
body: The `create` action's failure branch now returns `errors: user.errors.to_hash` and `values: user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")` to the client. This echoes back the submitted email (even when rejected for being blocked, already taken, or disallowed by whitelist/blacklist) along with the specific validation error keys. This allows an attacker to probe arbitrary email addresses and learn whether they are already registered, blocked, or restricted by domain policy without ever creating an account — a user/email-enumeration vector that did not exist before (previously only a combined message string was exposed).

title: No test coverage for whitelist/blacklist branches moved out of User model
body: `app/models/user.rb` previously had `email_validator`/`email_in_restriction_setting?` methods handling `SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist` and `email_domains_blacklist`, and this logic has been moved into `lib/validators/email_validator.rb`. The new spec file only tests the `BlockedEmail` branch (lines 9-21); it does not exercise the whitelist or blacklist branches (lines 4-12 of email_validator.rb) at all, so a regression in that moved logic (e.g. regex construction, which setting takes precedence) would go undetected. Any prior tests for this logic that existed against `User` should be confirmed as migrated here, otherwise this behavior now has no automated coverage.

title: Validator always invokes should_block? even with no record errors check limited to one attribute, could run against blank/invalid values
body: `validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` whenever the whitelist/blacklist checks pass, without guarding against `value` being blank or malformed. Although presence is validated elsewhere on `User`, this validator can be reused on other models/attributes where blank or nil values might reach `should_block?`, causing an unnecessary `BlockedEmail.where(email: nil)` query and wasted BlockedEmail record lookups. A `return if value.blank?` guard would make this validator more robust and reusable.

title: rejectedEmails array literal shared at prototype definition time
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined directly on the controller's prototype as a shared array literal rather than being created fresh per instance (e.g. in an `init` hook). If more than one instance of `CreateAccountController` is ever created (tests, multiple modal opens without a full page reload, etc.), all instances share and mutate the same array, so rejected emails from one session/instance can leak into another, causing emails to be incorrectly reported as previously rejected.

title: raw_html cook_method bypasses all sanitization for externally sourced content
body: Post#cook now returns `raw` unmodified when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, completely skipping PrettyText/post_analyzer rendering and sanitization. This path is used by TopicEmbed.import for content retrieved from RSS feeds and third-party web pages via Readability (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Since the content originates from an untrusted external source (a feed the admin configured, or any page fetched via the embed flow), and the resulting `cooked` HTML is rendered unescaped (`<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb and in normal topic views), a malicious or compromised feed/page can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript that executes in the context of the forum for every visitor who views that topic, not just inside the embed iframe. This is a stored XSS vector that defeats the forum's normal sanitization guarantees.

title: Protocol-relative URLs are mangled by absolutize_urls
body: `absolutize_urls` treats any href/src starting with '/' as a site-relative URL and rewrites it by stripping all leading slashes and prefixing with the embed site's scheme+host. Protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/x.jpg` also start with '/', so this code strips both leading slashes and produces `http://<embedhost>/cdn.example.com/x.jpg` instead of leaving the external URL `http://cdn.example.com/x.jpg` untouched. This breaks images/links that use protocol-relative URLs, which are common on syndicated content.

title: postMessage origin check uses unsafe substring match
body: `postMessageReceived` validates the sender using `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, i.e. it checks whether the message's origin string appears anywhere inside `discourseUrl`, rather than checking that `e.origin` equals (or is a prefix match of) the trusted Discourse origin. This is a well-known postMessage anti-pattern: a crafted or coincidental origin that happens to be a substring of `discourseUrl` (e.g. a shared domain fragment) could pass this check and have its `discourse-resize` messages accepted, allowing an untrusted page to manipulate the iframe height from outside the embed context.

title: Referer host comparison is case-sensitive
body: `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` compares hostnames with case-sensitive string equality. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so a referer like `Example.com` would fail to match a configured `embeddable_host` of `example.com` (or vice versa), causing legitimate embed requests to be incorrectly rejected with InvalidAccess.

title: Potential NoMethodError when RSS/Atom item has no content
body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes `i.content` is always present. Many RSS 2.0 feeds use `description` rather than `content`, and SimpleRSS will return `nil` for a missing `content` field, causing `.scrub` to raise `NoMethodError` on `nil` and aborting the whole feed-polling job (and since `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the failure is silently dropped) for every item that lacks a `content` element, not just the problematic one.

title: feed_key is defined but never used
body: `feed_key` computes a Redis cache key presumably meant to track the feed's last-modified state (to avoid reprocessing/refetching unchanged feeds), but it is never referenced anywhere in `poll_feed`. As written, the job always re-downloads and re-parses the entire feed and iterates every item on every run, with no last-modified/ETag based short-circuiting, making this dead code and a missed optimization opportunity.

title: Full feed poll executed synchronously per missing embed request
body: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline whenever an embed_url isn't found and feed polling is enabled, which downloads and parses the entire configured RSS/Atom feed and imports every item just to possibly locate the single requested embed_url. Because the throttle in `retrieved_recently?` is keyed per `embed_url`, concurrent requests for different not-yet-imported embed URLs each trigger their own full feed fetch/parse/import cycle with no global throttle, which can hammer the external feed URL and do redundant work under load (e.g. many visitors loading many different not-yet-cached embed pages at once).

title: Core poll_feed RSS parsing/import logic is untested
body: The spec only verifies that `execute` delegates to `poll_feed` under the right site-setting conditions, but it never exercises `poll_feed` itself: there is no coverage for RSS/Atom item iteration, URL fallback to `i.id`, HTML unescaping, or the call to `TopicEmbed.import`. Given this is the main new behavior introduced by this PR (feed-based topic creation/import), the lack of a test for `poll_feed`'s actual body is a significant gap.

title: New gems only reflected in the Rails 4 lockfile
body: The Gemfile adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` unconditionally (outside the rails3/rails4 branch), but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` is updated in this diff to include them. The repository supports dual-booting Rails 3 via a separate default `Gemfile.lock` (per the monkey-patching at the top of the Gemfile); if that lockfile isn't also updated, `bundle install`/`bundle exec` in Rails 3 mode will fail or be inconsistent with the new dependencies required by the embed/feed-import feature.

title: Untrusted RSS feed content is stored and rendered as raw HTML (stored XSS)
body: poll_feed.rb takes `i.content` straight from an externally-controlled RSS/Atom feed, only unescapes HTML entities, and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (see app/models/topic_embed.rb line 22). In `Post#cook` (app/models/post.rb line 133), raw_html posts skip the normal `PrettyText`/sanitization pipeline entirely (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), so whatever HTML comes from the feed ends up verbatim in `post.cooked`. The embed view then outputs it unescaped (`<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb), and the normal topic page presumably does the same since `cooked` is generally trusted. A malicious or compromised feed can inject `<script>` tags or other active content that will execute in every visitor's browser (both on the embed page and on the main forum topic page). There is no sanitizer anywhere in this import path (Nokogiri's `absolutize_urls` only rewrites href/src, it doesn't strip scripts/attributes).

title: Use of Kernel#open (open-uri) on externally supplied URLs risks command/file injection
body: `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` (Kernel#open via `open-uri`) directly on a URL that is not scheme-validated before this point (the `^https?://` check only happens later, inside `TopicEmbed.import`, which `import_remote` never calls before opening the URL). `Kernel#open` is well known to treat strings beginning with a pipe character (e.g. `|some-shell-command`) as a command to execute, and can also open local files via `file://` or bare paths. `import_remote` is invoked directly with attacker/feed-influenced strings in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, line 148) where `t[:link]` comes from parsing an externally supplied Disqus XML export, and in `lib/topic_retriever.rb#fetch_http` with the user-supplied `embed_url`. While `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` provides some protection for the web-triggered path, the thor task has no such guard, and the scheme check inside `import_remote`→`import` happens too late (after `open` has already run). This should use a strict allow-list of schemes (http/https only) and/or `URI.open`/`Net::HTTP` instead of bare `Kernel#open` before performing the request.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring containment instead of exact match
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` only verifies that `e.origin` is a substring of `discourseUrl`, rather than verifying the message truly originated from the Discourse host. This is a loose, non-standard way to validate postMessage origins and is fragile: e.g. it does not account for scheme/port differences and can be confused by crafted `discourseUrl` values that happen to contain unrelated but overlapping substrings. The check should parse both values and perform an exact origin comparison (e.g. compare `new URL(discourseUrl).origin === e.origin`).

title: Race condition on first-time embed import can raise unhandled RecordNotUnique
body: `TopicEmbed.import` checks `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` to decide whether to create a new topic/post or update an existing one. If two requests for the same new `embed_url` run concurrently (e.g. a user request and the hourly feed poller, or two near-simultaneous visitors before the Redis throttle key in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is set), both can see `embed.blank?` as true and both attempt `TopicEmbed.create!(...)` with the same `embed_url`. Since `embed_url` has a unique DB index (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb), the second `create!` raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, which is not rescued anywhere in this path, causing the background job (or request) to fail with an unhandled exception instead of gracefully falling back to the update path.

title: No timeout on blocking HTTP fetch for feed polling (open-uri)
body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `open-uri` with no read/open timeout configured. If the configured feed URL is slow, unresponsive, or the connection hangs, this call can block the Sidekiq worker thread indefinitely (or for a very long time), since `sidekiq_options retry: false` won't help here and there is no `Timeout` wrapper. The same issue applies to `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed#import_remote` (app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48). This can starve the scheduled-job queue of workers.

title: feed_key method is defined but never used (dead/incomplete code)
body: `feed_key` computes a Redis key based on a SHA1 of the feed URL (`"feed-modified:#{...}"`), presumably intended to support conditional GETs / tracking last-modified state to avoid re-downloading/re-parsing the whole feed on every run, but it is never referenced anywhere in `poll_feed` or elsewhere in the class. This indicates either dead code that should be removed, or an incomplete feature (feed modification tracking) that was never wired up, which could be confusing for future maintainers and leaves `require 'digest/sha1'` as an otherwise-unused dependency for this half-implemented feature.

title: Third-party gem loaded via require_dependency instead of require
body: `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` loads the Nokogiri gem through Rails' autoload/dependency-tracking mechanism, which is meant for application code that should be reloaded between requests in development, not for third-party native-extension gems. Using `require_dependency` for a gem like Nokogiri is non-idiomatic and can cause Rails to attempt to track/reload it as part of the app's dependency graph, which is unnecessary overhead and can lead to subtle reload issues with native extensions. This should simply be `require 'nokogiri'` (or omitted entirely since Nokogiri is already a Bundler dependency loaded at boot).

title: Unused require_dependency for email/sender
body: `require_dependency 'email/sender'` at the top of this job is never used anywhere in the file (there is no reference to `Email::Sender`). This looks like leftover/copy-paste code and should be removed to avoid confusion about the job's actual dependencies.

title: No test coverage for the actual feed-parsing/import logic in poll_feed
body: The spec for `Jobs::PollFeed` only verifies the guard conditions in `execute` (that `poll_feed` is or isn't called based on site settings) by stubbing out `poll_feed` itself. There is no test exercising the real `poll_feed` method: parsing the RSS/Atom feed with SimpleRSS, falling back from `i.link` to `i.id`, unescaping HTML, or calling `TopicEmbed.import` with the right arguments. Given the security-sensitive nature of this import path (raw HTML is stored and rendered unescaped), and the fact that `open(...)` has no error handling, this is a significant gap — bugs in URL selection, content extraction, or error handling for malformed feeds would not be caught by this test suite.

title: Invalid ERB/Ruby code `end if` breaks template compilation
body: Line 6 contains `<%- end if %>` which compiles to the Ruby statement `end if` with no preceding expression for the `if` modifier. This is a syntax error and will raise a SyntaxError at template-compile time whenever the `embed/best` view is actually rendered (both when posts are present and when they are not). The controller spec for this action mocks `TopicView.new` and doesn't render views, so this bug is not caught by the included tests. This should simply be `<%- end %>`.

title: NoMethodError when feed item has no content
body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes `i.content` is always present. Many plain RSS 2.0 feeds only populate `<description>`, not `content:encoded`/Atom `<content>`, so `i.content` can be `nil`, raising `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil`. Since `sidekiq_options retry: false` is set on this scheduled job, such an exception will cause polling to silently fail (without retry) for any feed item lacking a content field, and potentially abort processing of all subsequent items in that run since the exception propagates out of the `each` loop.

title: cook_method :raw_html bypasses sanitization entirely for imported content
body: `cook` returns `raw` unmodified when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, skipping the normal PrettyText rendering/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` (used both by `PollFeed` and by `TopicRetriever`/`import_remote`) creates posts with this cook_method, and the resulting `cooked` value is rendered unescaped via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `embed/best.html.erb` as well as in the normal topic view used throughout the rest of the application. Content coming from `PollFeed` (`TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`) is taken directly from the RSS/Atom feed with no tag allow-list (unlike `import_remote`, which at least constrains tags via Readability's `tags:`/`attributes:` options). A malicious or compromised feed can therefore inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript that is stored verbatim and rendered without sanitization to every visitor of the topic, constituting a stored XSS vector.

title: Backwards/weak origin check for postMessage listener
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` checks whether `e.origin` is a substring of `discourseUrl`, rather than verifying that `e.origin` strictly equals (or is a prefix of) the Discourse origin. This is the wrong direction for an origin check: a message is accepted as long as `e.origin` happens to appear anywhere inside the `discourseUrl` string, which is a fragile comparison that can behave unexpectedly depending on how `discourseUrl` is configured (e.g. if it contains query params, paths, or other substrings). The check should compare the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` against `e.origin` with strict equality instead of using substring containment.

title: Disqus import loses category assignment and original post timestamps
body: The previous implementation created the first post with `category: category_id` (derived from the removed `--category`/`-c` option) and `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, preserving the thread's original category and creation date during import. The new call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` does not accept or forward either a category or a created_at value, so imported Disqus threads are now always created with no category and with the current time as their creation date instead of the original Disqus post date. This is both a feature removal (the `--category` CLI option still exists in `method_option` metadata removed from the diff but no longer has any effect) and a data-fidelity regression for anyone running this migration tool expecting historical dates/categories to be preserved.

title: Unguarded race condition on `embed_url` uniqueness in TopicEmbed.import
body: `self.import` does a plain `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` check and, if blank, proceeds to create a new Topic/Post and then `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a `Topic.transaction` block. There is no locking (e.g. `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) around the blank-check, so two concurrent callers for the same `embed_url` (e.g. the hourly `PollFeed` job and a simultaneous `TopicRetriever`-triggered import from a visitor request) can both see `embed.blank? == true` and both attempt to create a topic/post and a `TopicEmbed` row. The unique index on `embed_url` (added in the accompanying migration) will cause the second `TopicEmbed.create!` to raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, which is not rescued here, potentially leaving an orphaned Topic/Post with no corresponding `TopicEmbed` record if the surrounding nested transaction semantics don't fully roll back the already-created post (PostCreator#create uses its own internal `Post.transaction`).

title: Full RSS feed re-poll triggered per unknown embed URL
body: `perform_retrieve` runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`, which downloads and parses the entire configured feed, every time a never-before-seen `embed_url` is requested and feed polling is enabled — even though the hourly scheduled `PollFeed` job already performs this work independently. The only throttle (`retrieved_recently?`) is keyed per `embed_url`, not per feed, so many distinct unseen embed URLs arriving in a short window (e.g. several different articles being embedded concurrently) can each trigger a full, redundant feed fetch/parse, which is wasteful and could amplify load against the external feed host.

title: Controller spec never renders views, hiding template errors
body: The success-path examples stub `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed`/`TopicView.new`/`TopicRetriever` and never actually render `embed/best.html.erb` or `embed/loading.html.erb` (the spec is not configured with `render_views: true`, and `TopicView.new` is merely expected to be called, not exercised). As a result, a real rendering error in the view (such as the invalid `<%- end if %>` in `best.html.erb`) is not caught by this test suite, even though this is the primary new user-facing code path added by the PR.

title: Mixing float with flexbox children breaks layout of .small-action
body: `.small-action` was converted to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`), but its direct children `.topic-avatar` (line ~270, `float: left;`) and `button` (line ~309, `float: right;`) still rely on `float`. In CSS, `float` is ignored on flex items (direct children of a `display:flex` container). As a result the avatar will no longer be positioned via float but will simply become the first flex item (which happens to look similar), while the `button`'s `float: right` will have no effect at all — it will just be laid out as the last flex item in normal flow instead of being pushed to the right edge of the container. This silently breaks the right-alignment of the action button (e.g. undo/dismiss controls on small-action notices) without any compensating `margin-left: auto` or `justify-content` change. The trailing `clear: both;` on `.small-action` is also now vestigial since there are no floated children to clear within the flex container.

title: Removed `.title { float: left; }` rule without replacement when converting `.contents` to flexbox
body: The diff removes the `.title { float: left; }` rule nested inside `.d-header .contents` while turning `.contents` into a flex container. No `order` or other flex-specific rule was added for `.title` to replace the old floating behavior, unlike `.panel` which received `margin-left: auto; @include order(3);`. If `.title` is one of the flex items inside `.contents`, its layout now depends entirely on flex default behavior (order 0, normal flex-basis) with no explicit styling, which may differ from the previous floated layout and could shift or resize the site title/logo area unexpectedly.

title: `@include order(2)` added to `.extra-info-wrapper` with no visible flex container context
body: `.extra-info-wrapper` now has `@include order(2)` applied, but the CSS `order` property only has an effect on elements that are direct children of a flex (or grid) container. Nothing in this file establishes `.extra-info-wrapper`'s parent as `display: flex`. If the parent element isn't a flex container (and no such change is visible in this PR), this `order` declaration is a no-op and the intended re-ordering will silently fail to take effect, leaving dead/misleading CSS in the stylesheet.

title: Removed `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` inside `.extra-info-wrapper` without equivalent replacement
body: The previous rule gave bullet-style badge wrappers inside `.extra-info-wrapper` a 5px top margin for vertical alignment. This specific rule was deleted and replaced only with a `line-height: 1.5` on the parent `.extra-info-wrapper`. Line-height alone does not reproduce a per-element top margin; depending on surrounding content this can cause the bullet badge to misalign vertically relative to the rest of the extra-info row, since the compensating offset for the bullet variant is gone.

title: Removed margin-top for .badge-wrapper.bullet with no replacement
body: The previous rule `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` inside `.extra-info-wrapper` was deleted and not replaced by any equivalent spacing (e.g. via the new `order`/`line-height` properties). This is an unrelated styling regression bundled into a 'flexbox mixin' refactor: bullet-style category badges inside `.extra-info-wrapper` will now lose their 5px top offset and may visually misalign relative to sibling badge/box styles, which still retain their own margin-top rules elsewhere.

title: order() mixin applied without a confirmed flex parent
body: `@include order(2);` is added to `.extra-info-wrapper`, but nothing in this file (or diff) establishes `display: flex` on the parent container of `.extra-info-wrapper`. The `order` CSS property only has an effect on flex (or grid) items; if the parent isn't a flex container, this rule is a silent no-op, and if it relies on flex context defined elsewhere, that dependency is undocumented and fragile — a later refactor of the parent's display property could silently break the intended item ordering.

title: Removed .title float rule has no explicit flex-order replacement
body: The diff removes `.contents .title { float: left; }` while converting `.contents` into a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) and giving `.panel` an explicit `order(3)`. `.title` (and other now-unordered children of `.contents`) will fall back to default flex order (0) based on source order, which may not match the previous float-based visual arrangement of logo/title/icons. There is no verification in the PR that this reordering preserves the original header layout, risking a visual regression that wasn't covered by any added test or screenshot.

title: Removed spacing reservation for floated .topic-avatar icon may cause text overlap
body: `.small-action-desc` padding was changed from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` (reserving ~64px on the left to clear the 45px-wide floated `.topic-avatar` icon) to `0 1.5%`, and the compensating `margin-top: 5px` and `> p { padding-top: 4px; }` were also dropped. `.topic-avatar` still uses `float: left`, but floats have no effect on flex items now that `.small-action` is a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`). Since no `flex-basis`/width/margin is set to reserve space for the icon, the description text in `.small-action-desc` risks overlapping or crowding the icon, a visual regression not covered by any test.

title: Non-standard vendor-prefixed property in align-items mixin
body: The `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, which is not a real IE vendor-prefixed CSS property (the correct IE10 flexbox alignment property is `-ms-flex-align`, which is already emitted on the preceding line). The `-ms-align-items` declaration is dead code that will simply be ignored by browsers, but it's misleading and should be removed to avoid confusion about actual IE10 support.

title: PR description is uninformative
body: The PR description is just 'Test 5', which gives no explanation of the intended visual/behavioral changes (header flex layout, small-action spacing changes, badge spacing removal). For a change touching multiple visual components and removing/altering CSS rules with real layout implications, reviewers and future maintainers have no context to assess whether the behavioral changes (e.g., removed badge margin-top, changed small-action-desc padding) were intentional or regressions.

title: `.title { float: left; }` rule removed without replacement
body: The previous `.title { float: left; }` rule inside `.contents` was deleted and not replaced by any flex-related property (no explicit `order`, `flex`, or alignment rule for `.title`). Since `.contents` is now `display:flex`, the `.title` element becomes a flex item relying entirely on default flex behavior, which can change its sizing/position compared to the previous floated layout (e.g. width calculation, wrapping behavior). This looks like an accidental omission rather than an intentional simplification and risks visually breaking the header title/logo layout.

title: Float-based child layout left in place after converting `.small-action` to flexbox
body: `.small-action` was converted to `display: flex` (lines 264-265), but its children `.topic-avatar` (line 270, `float: left`) and `button` (line 309, `float: right`) still rely on `float` for positioning. The CSS flexbox spec explicitly makes `float` a no-op on flex items, so these floats no longer have any effect. As a result the avatar is no longer guaranteed to sit to the left and the trailing button is no longer pushed to the right — the three children (`.topic-avatar`, `.small-action-desc`, `button`) will instead lay out in normal flex row order with no explicit `order`/`margin-left:auto` compensation, which changes the visual layout from what was previously intended.

title: `.small-action-desc` left padding drastically reduced, likely causing overlap with the icon
body: `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em;` was changed to `padding: 0 1.5%;`. The original 4em left padding was almost certainly reserved to make room for the floated `.topic-avatar` icon (45px wide, set via `.topic-avatar i { width: 45px; }`). With the new padding of only 1.5%, combined with floats no longer applying inside the new flex container (see related finding), the description text/icon are likely to overlap or be misaligned, which is a visible regression.

title: Removed `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` without a compensating rule
body: The previous nested rule setting `margin-top: 5px` on `.badge-wrapper.bullet` inside `.extra-info-wrapper` was deleted with no replacement. This was presumably used to vertically align the bullet badge within the line; removing it without adding any corresponding alignment (e.g. via flex `align-items`) risks a vertical misalignment regression for bullet-style category badges in the extra-info area.

title: `@include order(2)` added to `.extra-info-wrapper` with no verified flex parent
body: The CSS `order` property only has an effect when the element is a direct child of a `display:flex` (or similar) container. From the shown file there is no indication that the parent of `.extra-info-wrapper` is a flex container; if it isn't, this `order` declaration is dead code that has no visual effect, and if it is intended to be meaningful, the PR should verify/establish the flex container on the parent to avoid silently non-functional CSS.

title: Removed `padding-top: 4px` from `.small-action-desc > p` without explanation
body: The `padding-top: 4px` previously applied to the first-level paragraph inside `.small-action-desc` was removed. Combined with the other spacing changes in this same selector block, this reduces vertical spacing that may have been needed for readability/alignment of the small-action description text, and there is no indication this was deliberate given the PR description does not explain the rationale.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' required by the serializer convention
body: All other conditional inclusion methods in this file (e.g. include_card_image_badge_id?, include_user_fields?) follow the ActiveModel::Serializer convention of defining `include_<attr>?`. The newly added method is named `include_website_name` without the question mark, so the serializer framework will not recognize it as the inclusion guard for `website_name`. As a result the guard (`website.present?`) is effectively dead code, and `website_name` will be serialized unconditionally (e.g. as nil) instead of being conditionally included only when a website is set.

title: website_name leaks website info even when website attribute is restricted for untrusted viewers
body: The `untrusted_attributes` list (lines 105-111) hides `:website` from anonymous viewers of TL0 users via `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. However the new `:website_name` attribute, which is derived directly from the same underlying `website` value, is not added to this list. Because the underlying `website` method still returns the actual profile website regardless of serializer-level restriction, an anonymous viewer of a restricted TL0 user can still see the hostname (and sometimes full path) of that user's website via `website_name`, defeating the purpose of the existing restriction.

title: No test verifies website_name is hidden for untrusted/restricted users
body: The 'with a TL0 user seen as anonymous' spec only checks that `website`, `bio_raw`, `bio_cooked`, `bio_excerpt`, `location`, `profile_background`, and `card_background` are hidden, but does not verify that the newly introduced `website_name` attribute is also hidden in this scenario. Given that `website_name` derives from the same restricted data, this gap allowed the privacy leak (website_name not added to untrusted_attributes) to go unnoticed.

title: website_name bypasses untrusted_attributes restriction, leaking domain for restricted users
body: The new `website_name` attribute is added to the `attributes` list (line 43) but is not included in the `untrusted_attributes :bio_raw, :bio_cooked, :bio_excerpt, :location, :website, :profile_background, :card_background` list (lines 105-111). That list is what hides sensitive profile fields (including `website`) from anonymous viewers when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (e.g. TL0 user viewed anonymously). Because `website_name` is derived from the same `website` data but is not covered by this restriction, an anonymous viewer who should not be able to see a TL0 user's website will still see the host/path derived from it via `website_name`. This defeats the existing privacy restriction and leaks information that `website` itself is meant to hide. The existing spec (`spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb` untrusted_attributes list) doesn't check `website_name`, so this leak is not caught by tests.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' required by the serializer convention
body: Every other conditional-inclusion method in this file follows the pattern `include_<attr>?` (e.g. `include_card_image_badge?`, `include_edit_history_public?`, `include_email?`). The new method is defined as `include_website_name` without the trailing `?` (line 153). ActiveModel::Serializer looks for `include_<attr>?` to decide whether to include an attribute; since this predicate name doesn't match, it's never invoked, and `website_name` falls back to the default (always included because it is listed in `attributes`). This means the intended guard (`website.present?`) silently has no effect, and in combination with the issue above, there is no server-side control at all over when `website_name` is exposed.

title: No test verifies website_name is hidden for TL0/anonymous restricted users
body: The `untrusted_attributes` array used in the "with a TL0 user seen as anonymous" test (line 11) was not updated to include `:website_name`, even though this PR introduces that derived attribute from the same restricted `website` data. As a result, there is no test coverage asserting that `website_name` is also suppressed when `scope.restrict_user_fields?` is true, which would have caught the leak described above.

title: include_website_name is missing the '?' suffix required by the serializer convention
body: The serializer uses the `include_#{attr}?` naming convention everywhere else (e.g. `include_card_image_badge_id?`, `include_card_image_badge?`, `include_user_fields?`). The newly added guard method is named `include_website_name` without the trailing `?`, so ActiveModel::Serializer will never find/call it to decide inclusion. As a result the `website_name` attribute is always serialized regardless of whether `website` is present, defeating the intended `website.present?` guard and potentially emitting `website_name: null` when there is no website.

title: website_name bypasses the untrusted_attributes privacy restriction applied to website
body: `website` is listed under `untrusted_attributes`, which hides it from anonymous users when the owning user is TL0 (via `scope.restrict_user_fields?`), presumably to prevent spam-link exposure. The new `website_name` attribute computes its value directly from `object.user_profile.website` and is only declared in the plain `attributes` list (with the broken `include_website_name` guard, see other finding), completely bypassing the untrusted-attribute restriction. This means a TL0 user's website host/path is still leaked to anonymous viewers via `website_name` even though `website` itself is correctly suppressed, undermining the existing privacy/anti-spam protection.

title: Test for untrusted attributes was not updated to cover the new website_name attribute
body: The `untrusted_attributes` array used in the 'with a TL0 user seen as anonymous' context still only lists `%i{bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background}` and was not updated to include `:website_name`. Since `website_name` is derived from the same `website` data that this test is meant to protect, the missing entry means the test suite would not catch the regression where `website_name` leaks website information for TL0 users viewed anonymously (see related serializer finding).

title: Missed conversion of scale-color($primary) in categories badge-notification
body: In `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification`, the color is still `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` and was not converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` like every other identical `$lightness: 50%` usage in this same file (lines 48, 51, 55, 69, 246, 301). This PR's whole purpose is to fix dark-theme contrast for scale-color($primary) usages; this spot was overlooked, so the badge-notification text color on category topic lists will remain unreadable/low-contrast on dark themes.

title: Lightness values swapped when converting .topic-meta-data h5 a color
body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. Following the pattern used everywhere else in this PR, the correct conversion should preserve 30% for the primary branch and use the complementary 70% for secondary, i.e. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. Instead the primary branch lightness was changed to 70% (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`), which produces a much lighter color than before for the default/light theme, likely reducing readability of this anchor text against the light background. This is inconsistent with the symmetric X/(100-X) pattern used consistently elsewhere in the diff.

title: Lost original lightness value when converting .group-member-info .name color
body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The converted rule became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, i.e. identical to the sibling `.title` rule a few lines below instead of preserving the original 30%/70% pair. This changes the visual appearance of usernames in the group-member-info block (now lighter/less contrasted than before) and appears to be a copy-paste mistake rather than an intentional change.

title: Same incorrect lightness substitution as desktop/user.scss for .group-member-info .name
body: Mirroring the desktop version, the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` instead of the expected 30%/70% complementary pair, duplicating the same mistake across the mobile stylesheet and causing an unintended contrast change for usernames in group listings on mobile.

title: Incorrect lightness mapping for .topic-map h3 color
body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` (a fairly dark color). It was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` rather than preserving the 20%/80% complementary pair used by the sibling `.number, i` rule a few lines below (which correctly became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`). This makes the topic-map header text noticeably lighter than intended on the default theme.

title: Primary/secondary lightness values swapped for .custom-message-length
body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The converted rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which changes the primary-branch lightness from 70% to 30% instead of keeping 70%/30% as the complementary pair (consistent with the desktop version of this same rule in desktop/modal.scss, which correctly produced `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`). This introduces a noticeably darker text color for `.custom-message-length` on the default/light theme than existed before this PR.

title: Light-theme lightness value changed unintentionally (30% -> 70%) while adding dark variant
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. The PR's goal is only to add a dark-theme counterpart via `dark-light-choose()`, but the light-theme value itself was changed to 70% instead of being preserved as 30%: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`. This is inconsistent with every other conversion in the PR (which keeps the original percentage as the first argument and mirrors it as `100-X` for the second argument), and it silently alters the light-theme appearance of this text (now much lighter/lower-contrast than before), which is an unintended visual regression unrelated to the stated purpose of the PR.

title: Arguments to dark-light-choose swapped/incorrect for .custom-message-length
body: Original rule: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);`. Expected conversion (per the pattern used everywhere else in this PR) would be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, preserving the light-theme value and mirroring for dark. Instead the diff produces `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` — the two percentages are swapped relative to the expected mapping. This both changes the light-theme color unintentionally (from 70% to 30% lightness) and produces an incorrect (also swapped) value for the dark theme.

title: group-member-info .name lightness value changed unintentionally (30% -> 50%)
body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` (note: the sibling `.title` rule a few lines below correctly preserves its 50% value). In this conversion, the value was changed to 50%/50% instead of preserving 30% and mirroring to 70% as done consistently elsewhere in the PR: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. This silently changes the light-theme text color for group member names, an unintended regression.

title: group-member-info .name lightness value changed unintentionally (30% -> 50%), same bug as desktop/user.scss
body: Same issue as in desktop/user.scss: the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` but the conversion produced `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`, changing the light-theme value from 30% to 50% instead of preserving it and mirroring to 70% for the dark variant. This is an unintended visual regression for the light theme on mobile user pages.

title: topic-map h3 lightness value changed unintentionally (20% -> 50%)
body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);`. The equivalent desktop rule (desktop/topic-post.scss h3 inside .topic-map) was correctly converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`, preserving 20%. However the mobile version here was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`, changing the light-theme lightness from 20% to 50%. This creates an unintended, inconsistent visual regression between desktop and mobile for the same heading style.

title: Lightness value changed for light theme in .topic-meta-data h5 a color
body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. The PR's intent is to only add a dark-theme fallback via `dark-light-choose`, preserving the existing light-theme value as the first argument. Here the first argument was changed from 30% to 70% (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`), so the light theme's rendered color for this link changes unintentionally (much lighter/washed-out), while 30% ended up assigned to the dark-theme branch instead. This is a visual regression for light theme users, inconsistent with every other conversion in this PR which keeps the original lightness value as the primary-theme argument.

title: Lightness value changed for light theme in .group-member-info .name color
body: Original rule: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. After conversion it became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme lightness from 30% to 50%. This alters the appearance for existing light-theme deployments instead of simply adding a dark-theme-safe fallback, unlike the sibling `.title` rule a few lines below which correctly preserves 50%->50%/50%. The 30% value appears to have been dropped/lost during the refactor.

title: Lightness value changed for light theme in .group-member-info .name color (mobile)
body: Same issue as the desktop counterpart: original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%, an unintended visual change rather than a pure dark-theme-compatibility fix.

title: Lightness value changed for light theme in .topic-map h3 color
body: Original rule: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);`. After the change it became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, i.e. the light-theme lightness moved from 20% to 50%. This is inconsistent with the rest of the PR's pattern (which keeps A and uses 100-A for the dark branch) and visibly changes heading color in light theme.

title: Lightness value swapped between light/dark branches in .custom-message-length color
body: Original rule: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);`. It was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The 70% value, which should remain the light-theme (first) argument per the pattern used throughout this PR, was instead moved to the dark-theme (second) argument, and 30% was substituted for light theme. This changes the light-theme appearance of this element unintentionally.

title: Public group members endpoint now truncates membership lists with no pagination UI
body: The `members` action previously only paginated automatic groups (default limit 200) and returned the FULL member list for regular (non-automatic) groups. The new code unconditionally applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` / `offset` to every group, so any group (automatic or not) with more than 50 members will only return the first 50. However, the public-facing template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` and its route `group-members.js.es6` were not updated with any next/previous pagination controls (only the admin group page got pagination UI in group.hbs). Consequently, visitors to a public group's members page for any group with >50 members will silently see only the first 50 members with no way to view the rest — a visible functional regression.

title: Breaking response shape change for GET /groups/:name/members.json
body: The members endpoint previously returned a bare JSON array (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`). It now returns `{ members: [...], meta: { total, limit, offset } }`. This is a backward-incompatible change to a public API endpoint; any external client, script, or integration that consumed the old array response will break. This change isn't mentioned/versioned in the PR description.

title: Unbounded client-supplied limit on members endpoint
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` has no upper bound/clamp, and this unbounded limit is now applied to ALL groups (previously only automatic groups allowed an uncapped client-supplied limit, defaulting to 200). A client can request an arbitrarily large `limit` (e.g. `?limit=1000000`) forcing the server to query and serialize an unbounded number of rows, which is a resource-exhaustion/perf risk now exposed more broadly than before.

title: Off-by-one bug in totalPages computation
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 users with limit 50), this yields totalPages = 2 instead of the correct 1 (should be `Math.ceil(user_count/limit)`). This causes `showingLast` (`currentPage === totalPages`) to be false on what is actually the last real page, so the 'next' arrow stays enabled, and clicking it loads a phantom empty page (offset clamped to user_count returns zero members) while the pager displays e.g. '2/2' with no content.

title: No error handling for addMembers/removeMember AJAX failures
body: `removeMember` and `addMembers` only chain a `.then` success callback that reloads the member list; there is no failure/catch handler. Unlike `save`/`destroy` (which show a `bootbox.alert` on failure), if the request fails (e.g., 422 for an automatic group, validation error, or network failure) the promise rejection is silently swallowed and the admin controller (admin-group.js.es6 `removeMember`/`addMembers` actions) also does not attach any failure handler. Users get no feedback when adding/removing a member fails.

title: No tests added for GroupsController#members behavior/response-shape change
body: The PR substantially changes `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members` (new paginated response shape `{members, meta}` applied to all groups instead of only automatic groups, plus a new default/unbounded `limit`). No spec file for `GroupsController` is included or updated in this PR to cover the new pagination defaults, the new JSON shape, or the regression for non-automatic groups with many members.

title: Add-members input is not cleared after submission (acknowledged TODO)
body: The `addMembers` action contains `// TODO: should clear the input` and indeed never resets `usernames` after a successful add. This leaves stale usernames in the input field after members are added, which is confusing UX and was merged as a known-incomplete feature.

title: Route param name mismatch breaks add_members / remove_member endpoints
body: `add_members` (line 66) and `remove_member` (line 85) call `params.require(:group_id)`, but the routes added in `config/routes.rb` (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` / `put "members" => "groups#add_members"`) are declared directly inside the `resources :groups do ... end` block without a `member do` wrapper or a custom `param:` option. Rails treats such bare routes as member routes using the resource's default id parameter, i.e. `:id` (same as `/admin/groups/:id`), not `:group_id`. As a result the real request path produces `params[:id]`, and `params.require(:group_id)` will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` for every real HTTP request made by the JS model's `addMembers`/`removeMember` calls (`Discourse.ajax('/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json', ...)`), making the core feature of this PR (adding/removing group members from the admin UI) non-functional in production.

title: Controller specs bypass routing and hide the group_id/id param mismatch
body: The `.add_members` and `.remove_member` specs invoke the controller actions directly with `group_id: ...` (e.g. `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, usernames: "l77t"`). Rails' `ActionController::TestCase` dispatch bypasses real route recognition and just merges the given params, so these tests pass even though the actual routes (declared without a `member do` wrapper) would supply `:id` instead of `:group_id`. There is no request/integration spec exercising the real route, so the runtime `ParameterMissing` bug described separately is not caught by this test suite.

title: Off-by-one in totalPages causes a phantom empty last page
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100 users with limit 50), this yields 3 instead of the correct 2 pages. Combined with the `next` action's offset calculation (`Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), clicking "next" from the last real page (offset 50) will set offset to 100 and reload, returning zero members (since indices 0-99 are exhausted) while `currentPage`/`totalPages` both report page 3 of 3, presenting a bogus empty page to the admin instead of correctly computing `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

title: `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` likely uses wrong option name
body: The each-helper option for specifying a custom per-item view class in this version of Ember/Handlebars is `itemViewClass`, not `itemView` (as used consistently elsewhere in Discourse, e.g. `itemViewClass="..."`).
