Using `itemView` means the newly added `group-member` view/template (which renders the avatar, username and the remove-member link) will likely never be applied, so the admin group members list will not render as intended and the "remove member" UI added by this PR may simply not appear.

title: `{{#unless automatic}}` resolves against the wrong context, always showing remove link
body: This template is rendered as the item view for each member inside `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`. Inside that per-item context, `automatic` is looked up on the member (a User) object, not on the outer group/controller, so it will always be undefined/false. Consequently `{{#unless automatic}}` always evaluates true and the "remove member" link is shown even for automatic groups, whose members cannot actually be removed (the server rejects such requests with a 422). This creates a confusing dead-end UI action instead of correctly hiding the control for automatic groups.

title: Public group members page silently truncates to 50 members with no pagination UI
body: `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members` now always paginates with a default `limit` of 50 for every group (previously only automatic groups were capped, at 200, and regular groups returned the full member list). The public-facing `group/members.hbs` template has no next/previous controls (unlike the admin `group.hbs` template, which does), so any group with more than 50 members will silently show only the first 50 with no way to view the rest — a functional regression for larger groups.

title: Controller model changed from members array to Group object without visible controller update
body: Previously `setupController` assigned the resolved members array itself as the controller's `model` (`controller.set('model', this.get('_members'))`), implying the group-members controller is array-oriented, and the template iterated `{{#each m in model}}`. The route now assigns the raw `Group` model object instead (`controller.set("model", model)`) and the template was changed to `{{#each m in members}}`. No controller file for group-members is included in this change set; if the existing controller is an `ArrayController` (as the prior code's usage suggests), assigning a non-array `Group` object as its content/model is likely to break member rendering on the public group page.

title: addMembers/removeMember actions swallow errors silently
body: The `addMembers` action (line 61-65) calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))` and `removeMember` (line 51-59) calls `self.get("model").removeMember(member)` without attaching a `.catch`/error handler on the returned promise, unlike `save` and `destroy` which do handle rejection with `bootbox.alert`. The backend (`Admin::GroupsController#add_members`/`#remove_member`) returns a 422 with an error message when the group is automatic, or can fail for other reasons (e.g. unknown usernames silently skipped, group save validation failure). Because there is no error handler, any such failure is silently swallowed in the UI and the user gets no feedback that the add/remove operation did not succeed.

title: `automatic` lookup in item view template resolves against the member, not the group
body: `group_member.hbs` is rendered as the template for the `group-member` itemView used via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` in `group.hbs`. Since this is the non-block `{{each}}` form with an `itemView`, the rendering context for each item's template is the member object itself, not the outer group/controller context. The bare `{{#unless automatic}}` check in this template therefore resolves `automatic` against the `member` (a user object, which has no `automatic` property) rather than against the group's `automatic` flag, so it will always be falsy and the remove link will be rendered for members of automatic groups too, even though removal is disallowed server-side. This produces a UI affordance that always fails (compounded by the missing error handling noted elsewhere), misleading admins into thinking they can remove members from automatic groups.

title: Membership mutation is persisted before validation/save, causing misleading error responses
body: In `remove_member`, `group.users.delete(user_id)` (line 90) immediately executes a DELETE against the join table for a persisted `group`/association, and in `add_members`, `group.add(user)` (line 73) similarly persists membership immediately via the association. Only afterwards is `group.save` called to determine the HTTP response. If `group.save` fails for any unrelated reason (e.g. stale validation state), the controller renders `render_json_error(group)` even though the membership change has already been committed to the database. Clients receiving an error response will believe the operation failed and may retry, potentially causing duplicate adds or confusing inconsistent state, since the actual membership mutation already succeeded independent of the `save` result.

title: Unhandled RecordNotFound possible when removing a non-member/invalid user_id
body: `remove_member` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` with a raw integer id and no rescue. Depending on how the has_many association's `delete` resolves an id that is not currently part of the group's collection (e.g. stale client state, concurrent removal, or a malicious/incorrect user_id), this can raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`, which is not rescued here and would bubble up as an unhandled 500 error instead of a clean validation error response. There is also no spec covering this scenario (see spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb), so this regression path is untested.

title: Default member page size silently reduced for automatic groups
body: The previous implementation gave automatic groups a larger default limit (200) specifically to work around truncation for groups with many members, while non-automatic groups were unpaginated/unlimited. The new code applies a flat default `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` to all groups regardless of the `automatic` flag. This is a behavior change for the public `/groups/:group_id/members` endpoint: large automatic groups (e.g. trust-level groups) that used to return up to 200 members by default now only return 50, which can break any existing API consumers or UI relying on the previous default page size, without any changelog/doc update reflecting this change.

title: Misleading singular placeholder text for a multi-username input
body: `admin.groups.selector_placeholder` was changed from "add users" to "enter username" (singular). However, the `user-selector` field it labels (used in `admin/templates/group.hbs`) accepts a comma-separated list of usernames that are split and processed as multiple users in `addMembers`/`Admin::GroupsController#add_members`. The new singular wording suggests only one username can be entered, which is misleading to admins trying to add multiple members at once.

title: Usernames input is not cleared after successfully adding members
body: The `addMembers` action contains a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment acknowledging that `this.get("usernames")` is never reset after a successful add. This means the previously entered usernames remain in the input field after the members are added, and clicking "Add" again (or forgetting the field still has old content) will re-submit the same usernames, causing redundant/no-op requests and a confusing UX for admins managing group membership.

title: Fallback locale translation files are only force-loaded within web requests
body: I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! (added in set_locale) is the only place that forces the whole fallback chain (current locale, site default locale, :en) to be loaded via I18n.ensure_loaded!. The lazy-loading patch in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb only loads the currently-active I18n.locale on a translate() call (load_locale(config.locale)), not the fallback locales. Any code path that calls I18n.t outside of ApplicationController#set_locale — background jobs, Sidekiq workers, ActionMailer deliveries, rake tasks, console sessions — will never call ensure_loaded!, so when a translation is missing for the active locale, the fallback lookup for e.g. :en can silently fail (return nil / raise MissingTranslationData) even though the English translation file exists on disk, because that locale's YAML was never actually loaded into the backend. This can produce missing/blank translations specifically in background contexts where fallback behavior is most needed.

title: FallbackLocaleList#[] recomputes and hits SiteSetting on every call instead of memoizing
body: FallbackLocaleList overrides Hash#[] to always compute [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact on every invocation rather than storing/memoizing the result in the underlying Hash. Since I18n's Fallbacks backend module calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] on essentially every translate() call (not just on a miss), this means SiteSetting.default_locale is invoked repeatedly on the hot translation path instead of once per locale, adding avoidable overhead compared to the stock I18n::Locale::Fallbacks implementation, which memoizes per-locale fallback chains in the hash itself.

title: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but never populates the underlying hash store
body: FallbackLocaleList < Hash entirely overrides [] without ever calling super or storing values via []=/store, so the object itself remains an empty Hash. Any code that treats I18n.fallbacks as an actual Hash (e.g. enumerating via each/keys/to_a, or gems/tools that introspect configured fallback mappings) will see an empty collection instead of real data, even though direct [] lookups work correctly. This is fragile and can break downstream code that reasonably assumes I18n.fallbacks is a real, iterable Hash.

title: No tests added for new fallback locale behavior
body: This PR introduces non-trivial new behavior (FallbackLocaleList, I18n.ensure_loaded!, and the controller's forced pre-loading of the fallback chain) but adds no specs verifying that translations correctly fall back to the site default locale or to :en, nor that ensure_loaded! actually loads the required locale files. Given the subtlety of the lazy-loading/fallback interaction (see related finding about non-web contexts), this feature needs direct test coverage to avoid silent regressions.

title: I18n fallbacks now enabled globally instead of only in production/profile/cloud66 environments
body: Previously config.i18n.fallbacks = true was only set in config/environments/production.rb, profile.rb, and config/cloud/cloud66/files/production.rb. This PR removes those settings and instead enables fallbacks unconditionally for every environment via config/initializers/i18n.rb, including development and test. This is a behavior change beyond what the removed lines implied: specs or development workflows that previously relied on missing translations raising/being visibly flagged (rather than silently falling back to English) will now behave differently, which could mask incomplete translation work until it reaches a real fallback path in production anyway.

title: Fallback locale translations are only pre-loaded inside ApplicationController requests, not in jobs/console/mailers
body: FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded! is only invoked from ApplicationController#set_locale (app/controllers/application_controller.rb line ~159). The actual lookup used by I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate calls `super(fallback, key, ...)` directly on the backend instance, bypassing the patched `I18n.translate` in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb that performs lazy `load_locale`. That means a fallback locale's YAML translations are only guaranteed to be loaded in memory when a web request goes through ApplicationController#set_locale beforehand. Any translation performed outside of a controller request lifecycle (Sidekiq jobs, mailers triggered from jobs, rake tasks, console) for a user whose locale differs from the default will not have the fallback locale(s) loaded, so a missing key in the user's locale will not actually fall back to the site default or English — it will just be reported as missing. This defeats the purpose of the fallback feature in exactly the contexts (async notifications/digests in minority locales) where it matters most.

title: No tests for the new fallback locale chain or load-triggering logic
body: This PR introduces a new FallbackLocaleList class that computes a fallback chain (user locale -> site default -> :en) and a new ensure_loaded! helper, plus a corresponding before_filter in ApplicationController. No specs were added to verify the fallback order, the dedup/compact behavior, that ensure_loaded! actually causes the expected locale files to load, or that end-to-end translation lookups correctly fall back when a key is missing in the primary locale. Given this is a behavior-changing feature (removing config.i18n.fallbacks = true and replacing it with custom logic), lack of test coverage risks silent regressions.

title: PR description provides no explanation of the change
body: The PR description is just "Test 9", with no explanation of why config.i18n.fallbacks was removed from three environment files in favor of a hand-rolled FallbackLocaleList, what the fallback chain semantics are, or what testing was performed. For a feature that changes global I18n fallback behavior and touches a performance-sensitive translation cache, reviewers and future maintainers have no context to evaluate correctness or intended behavior.

title: Custom FallbackLocaleList replaces full-featured I18n::Locale::Fallbacks with a minimal stand-in
body: Previously `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` assigned a standard `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` instance, which implements the full fallback API (`map`, `default`, `defaults`, locale-tag decomposition such as `pt-BR -> pt -> en`, etc.). The new `FallbackLocaleList` only overrides `[]` and `ensure_loaded!`; all other Hash/Fallbacks methods are either absent or behave as an empty Hash. Any code (core, plugin, or gem) that calls other methods on `I18n.fallbacks` besides `[]` will now silently misbehave or raise NoMethodError, and locale-tag-based fallback behavior (e.g. regional variants) is lost without an equivalent compatibility shim.

title: Required initializer ordering is enforced only by a comment, not by code
body: The file relies on `02-freedom_patches.rb` having already patched `I18n::Backend::Simple`/`I18n::Backend::Base` (translate_accelerator) before this initializer runs, but the only indication of that dependency is the comment `# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb`. Rails initializer load order is driven by filename sort order; there is no explicit `require` or `config.before_initialize`/`after_initialize` hook enforcing the sequence. If the freedom-patch filename or load mechanism changes, this file could load before the patches are applied, causing `I18n::Backend::Simple` to not have the LRU-cache/explicit-load behavior when `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` is mixed in, or vice versa, leading to subtle load-order bugs.

title: Fallback behavior is now enabled globally instead of per-environment, silently changing dev/test behavior
body: `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` was previously set only in production.rb, profile.rb and the cloud66 production.rb — i.e. selectively per environment. By moving the equivalent logic into `config/initializers/i18n.rb` (which loads for all environments including development and test), locale fallbacks are now always active everywhere. This is a behavior change that isn't called out in the PR description, and it means missing-translation issues that previously surfaced in development/test (because fallback wasn't enabled there) will now be silently masked by falling back to the default locale/English, potentially hiding real translation bugs until they reach users of other locales in production.

title: ensure_loaded! recomputes fallback chain (including a SiteSetting lookup) on every request
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is invoked unconditionally in `set_locale`, a before_filter run on every request. Internally this calls `FallbackLocaleList#[]`, which reads `SiteSetting.default_locale` on every single request just to build the (mostly already-loaded) fallback chain. While the actual file loading is memoized via `@loaded_locales`, the SiteSetting lookup and array construction happen on every request regardless, adding avoidable per-request overhead that the translate_accelerator patch was specifically designed to minimize.

title: No tests added for the new fallback resolution logic
body: The PR introduces new runtime logic (`FallbackLocaleList#[]`, `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!`, `I18n.ensure_loaded!` in translate_accelerator.rb, and the new call in `ApplicationController#set_locale`) but adds no specs verifying that: (1) translations correctly fall back from user locale -> site default locale -> English, (2) `ensure_loaded!` actually loads the right locale files, or (3) `set_locale` behaves correctly when a translation is missing in the user's locale. Given this is a user-facing localization feature, lacking any automated coverage is a significant gap.

title: PR description is a non-descriptive placeholder
body: The PR description is simply "Test 9", which provides no information about the rationale, scope, or testing performed for this localization fallback feature. This makes it difficult for reviewers or future maintainers to understand why the change was made or what edge cases were considered.

title: Denial-cache key can collide across distinct (name, parentFolder) pairs
body: userPermDenialCacheKey builds the cache key by naively concatenating userUID, action, name and parent with '_' as separator: namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent. Because resource UIDs (name/parentFolder) can themselves legally contain underscores, two different requests can produce the same concatenated string, e.g. name="ab_cd", parent="ef" and name="ab", parent="cd_ef" both yield "..._ab_cd_ef". When this happens, a denial cached for one (name, parent) pair will be served for an unrelated resource, causing an incorrect 'denied' result to be returned for a resource the caller actually has access to (or, if the collision is reversed, the opposite type of mistake could occur with other callers sharing the key space). This is a correctness/security risk introduced by the new denial cache, since the previous caches never combined multiple variable-length, potentially-overlapping fields into one key this way.

title: permDenialCache keyed on raw subject UID instead of canonical resolved UID
body: The denial-cache key uses checkReq.UserUID directly (the raw identifier parsed from the Subject string), whereas every other cache in this service (idCache, permCache, teamCache, basicRoleCache) is keyed on the canonical identifier returned by GetUserIdentifiers (userIdentifiers.UID), which can resolve either a numeric ID or a UID to the same canonical value. If different callers pass the subject using different formats (numeric internal ID vs. UID) for the same user, the denial cache will never be shared between them, defeating the purpose of the cache and creating inconsistent caching behavior between the positive permission cache and the new denial cache.

title: New denial cache can reintroduce the staleness problem this PR is meant to fix
body: After a Check() call determines (via a fresh DB query) that a user is not allowed to access a resource, the result is cached for shortCacheTTL (30s) via permDenialCache.Set. If the user is subsequently granted access to that exact resource (e.g., permission is shared, or role changed) within that 30s window, Check() will short-circuit on the denial cache (lines 117-121) and return Allowed=false without consulting the DB, even though the user now has permission. This is the same category of staleness bug the PR is trying to fix for newly-created resources (stale positive cache), but now reintroduced via the new negative cache for recently-denied lookups.

title: Permission-cache usage metric mislabeled when cache is hit but check is denied
body: In Check(), when getCachedIdentityPermissions returns a cache hit but checkPermission on the cached permissions evaluates to false, execution falls through past the `if err == nil { ... }` block and records `s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", ...)` (line 137), labeling this as a cache miss even though the cache was actually hit (just didn't contain the requested permission). This produces misleading cache-hit-ratio metrics for operators monitoring cache effectiveness.

title: Denial-cache short-circuit test doesn't verify the cache path was actually used
body: The subtest 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' sets s.permDenialCache and expects resp.Allowed == false, but it never asserts that the fallback store/identity lookups were skipped (e.g. via store.calls == 0). Since the default fakeStore used by setupService() returns no permissions anyway, the test would still pass with the same expected result even if the denial-cache short-circuit logic in Check() were removed entirely. This test therefore does not actually validate the new denial-cache behavior and would not catch a regression.

title: Removing client-side cache for in-proc AuthZ client increases per-call overhead
body: ProvideAuthZClient now wires the in-proc client with a NoopCache instead of a local cache, meaning every single Check/List call goes through the full inprocgrpc channel (including proto marshal/unmarshal through the gRPC interceptor chain) rather than being served from a short-lived client-side cache. For code paths that perform many individual Check calls in a loop (e.g., per-item authorization checks), this removes a previously-available fast path and could noticeably increase per-request latency/CPU, even though the server now has its own cache, because the gRPC call overhead itself is no longer avoided on repeated checks within the same request.

title: Permission denial cache can mask newly granted permissions for up to the full TTL
body: In Check(), the permDenialCache lookup happens unconditionally before any attempt to re-check real permissions. Once a (user, action, name, parent) combination is cached as denied (line 154, s.permDenialCache.Set), subsequent Check calls return Allowed=false immediately for shortCacheTTL (30s) regardless of whether the user's permissions have since been updated (e.g. an admin granted access, or a role change). Unlike the main permCache fallback added in this PR for Check (which re-queries the DB when the cached permission map doesn't contain the resource), there is no equivalent re-validation path for the denial cache - a hit always short-circuits to deny without consulting the DB. This means that after a legitimate denial, a user who is subsequently granted access can still be denied access for up to 30 seconds, which is a new correctness/UX regression introduced by this feature; there is no cache invalidation hook tied to permission changes.

title: permissionCacheUsage metric mislabels cache-hit-but-insufficient results as cache misses
body: When getCachedIdentityPermissions returns a cached permission map (cache hit, err == nil) but checkPermission determines the cached map does not grant access for the specific resource, execution falls through past the if-block to line 137, which unconditionally records permissionCacheUsage with label "false" (cache miss). This mislabels a scenario where the cache was actually hit (just insufficient for this specific resource) as a full cache miss, understating the real cache hit rate in metrics/dashboards used to monitor cache effectiveness.

title: List() does not get the same stale-cache fallback that Check() received, so newly created resources may still be missing from list results
body: The PR's stated goal is to let dashboard/folder creators immediately access resources they just created. Check() was updated to fall back to a fresh DB query when the cached permission map does not satisfy the specific resource being checked (lines 123-137). List(), however, only distinguishes cache-hit vs cache-miss at the whole-permission-map level (lines 180-192): if getCachedIdentityPermissions returns any cached map at all, it is used as-is with no verification that it contains a newly created resource. As a result, a user who just created a dashboard/folder may be able to Check access to it directly, but it can still be absent from List() results (e.g. for a folder/dashboard browser) until the permission cache naturally expires (shortCacheTTL, 30s). This is an incomplete fix relative to the PR's described motivation and is not covered by any new test.

title: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates variable-length fields with a non-unique delimiter, risking key collisions
body: userPermDenialCacheKey builds the cache key as namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent, using plain underscore concatenation. Because userUID, name, and parent are externally supplied identifiers (resource UIDs, folder UIDs) that are not guaranteed to be free of underscores, two different (action, name, parent) combinations could produce the identical concatenated string (e.g. action="a_b", name="c" vs action="a", name="b_c"), causing an unrelated resource's permission check to incorrectly hit another resource's cached denial entry. This would surface as a user being denied access to a resource they actually have permission to, due to an unrelated cached denial colliding on the same key.

title: Permission-denial cache can reintroduce the exact staleness bug the PR is meant to fix
body: In Check(), after the early permDenialCache short-circuit (lines 116-121), a negative Check() result (resource not found in the cached permission map) causes a fresh DB query and, if still denied, a new entry is written to permDenialCache with shortCacheTTL (30s) (lines 153-155). If any Check() call is evaluated for a given (user, action, name, parentFolder) tuple shortly before the underlying resource becomes visible/granted (e.g. a speculative/early access check, or a check issued immediately after creation but before permissions/propagation settle), that negative result is now cached explicitly for up to 30s and will short-circuit all subsequent checks for that exact resource during that window — even though the resource now exists and the user should be allowed. This can resurrect, in a narrower but still real window, the exact 'user can't access the item they just created' problem this PR is meant to solve, because the explicit denial cache is not invalidated when the underlying permission/permCache is refreshed.

title: permissionCacheUsage metric mislabels cache hits that end up denied as cache misses
body: When getCachedIdentityPermissions returns a cached permission map (err == nil) but checkPermission on it returns false, the code does not record a cache hit; it falls through to line 137 which unconditionally increments permissionCacheUsage with label "false" (cache miss), even though the cache was actually consulted and hit. This understates the true cache hit rate for any action whose cached permission set does not include the requested resource, which will skew cache-hit-rate dashboards/alerts used to tune cache TTLs or diagnose cache effectiveness.

title: Negative results no longer short-circuited by the main permission cache, risking repeated DB round-trips per distinct resource
body: Previously, a cached permission map that didn't grant access to a specific resource was enough to return 'denied' without hitting the DB. Now, any cache hit that evaluates to 'not allowed' triggers an unconditional DB refetch of full identity permissions (getIdentityPermissions) before the result can be cached per-resource in permDenialCache. For a legitimately-denied identity, every distinct (name, parentFolder) combination requested during the permDenialCache TTL window (30s) incurs one full DB permission query (basic role + teams + permissions) the first time it's seen, since the per-resource denial cache has not yet been populated for that specific resource/folder pair. A client enumerating many resource names (or polling many different items the user has no access to) can therefore generate significant extra DB load compared to before this change.

title: Unescaped delimiter concatenation in userPermDenialCacheKey risks ambiguous cache keys
body: userPermDenialCacheKey builds the cache key by joining namespace, userUID, action, name, and parent with plain "_" separators without escaping or using a fixed-width/length-prefixed encoding. Because four variable-length segments (action, name, parent) are concatenated with the same separator, different combinations of these values that happen to contain "_" (or produce the same concatenated string through different splits) can collide into the same cache key, returning a cached allow/deny decision for the wrong resource. While action strings and most Kubernetes names are unlikely to contain underscores today, this is a fragile key-construction pattern that silently depends on that external invariant holding.

title: Silence drawer never renders when only promRule is available (new ruler-less list view)
body: The Silence menu item's visibility is now computed in AlertRuleMenu using the Grafana Prometheus rule ability (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`), which does not require a `rulerRule`. This means the 'Silence notifications' menu item is shown even when `rule` (the RulerRuleDTO) is undefined, which is exactly the case for the new ruler-less list view (GrafanaRuleListItem only passes `promRule`). However, in RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx the drawer itself is gated by `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`, which requires a truthy `rule` (rulerRule). When `rule` is undefined, clicking 'Silence notifications' sets `showSilenceDrawer` to true but the `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` never mounts, so the action silently does nothing. This breaks the silence feature for any consumer that only supplies `promRule` (i.e. the entire point of this PR).

title: Missing key prop for Grafana rule items rendered in a list
body: In the `rules.map()` call, the 'grafana' branch returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} namespaceName={ruleWithOrigin.namespaceName} showLocation={true} />` without a `key` prop, even though a `key` variable is destructured from `ruleWithOrigin` and used by the other two branches ('datasource' and default). Rendering a list without unique keys produces a React warning and can cause incorrect reconciliation/identity issues (lost component state, unnecessary re-mounts) especially since this list is updated incrementally via infinite scroll (`setRules((rules) => rules.concat(...))`).

title: Rule view link no longer includes returnTo parameter
body: The previous implementation (GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx, now removed) built the view URL with `createRelativeUrl(\`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view\`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`, allowing the rule detail page to show a 'back to list' link that returns to the exact filtered/paginated list state. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` builds the href as `createRelativeUrl(\`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view\`)` with no `returnTo` param, and no longer imports `createReturnTo`. This silently drops the 'go back to previous view' UX for every rule rendered through this component (used by both FilterView and GrafanaGroupLoader), which is a behavior regression not mentioned in the PR description.

title: Federated rule-group immutability check lost for the deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities hook
body: Previously `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` using the rule's actual group data, so rules in federated groups were correctly treated as immutable (Update/Delete/Pause/etc. disabled). After this refactor, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` (with a TODO comment to re-add support later). Since `useAllAlertRuleAbilities`/`useAlertRuleAbility` are still actively used elsewhere (e.g. by `RuleActionsButtons.tsx`/`RulesTable`, per the test file comments), this change silently removes the safeguard that disabled mutating actions on rules belonging to federated rule groups.

title: Both ruler-based and Grafana-prom-based ability hooks are always evaluated
body: `useRulerRuleAbilities` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` are both called unconditionally regardless of whether `rulerRule` or `promRule` is actually provided to the component. Each of these hooks performs its own folder lookups/permission computations (via `useIsRuleEditable` and `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`/`useFolder` respectively). For the common case where a full `rulerRule` is available (non-list views), the Grafana-prom ability path still runs (as long as promRule satisfies `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule`), duplicating folder permission computation/requests that are already covered by the ruler-based path, and vice versa for the ruler-less list view. This adds unnecessary hook/query overhead on every render of the menu for Grafana-managed rules.

title: Silence action is broken when only a promRule is supplied (new Grafana alert list view)
body: RuleActionsButtons now accepts either `rule` (RulerRuleDTO) or `promRule` (Rule), but the Silence drawer is only mounted when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true: `{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && (<SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} .../>)}`. GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx (used by GrafanaGroupLoader and FilterView, i.e. the whole new alert list) only passes `promRule`, never `rule`. Meanwhile AlertRuleMenu's `canSilence` is computed from the Grafana-prom-based ability check and can be true for these promRule-only invocations, so the 'Silence notifications' menu item is rendered and clickable (confirmed by GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx which asserts the silence menu item is present). Clicking it calls `handleSilence` → `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`, but because `rule` is always undefined in this flow, the guard `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is always false and the drawer never renders. Users will see a Silence option that does nothing when clicked, with no error or feedback.

title: Missing `key` prop when rendering GrafanaRuleListItem in a list
body: In the `rules.map(...)` loop, the previous `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../>` is replaced with `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} namespaceName={...} showLocation={true} />` without a `key` prop. The other two branches of the same switch (`DataSourceRuleLoader` and `UnknownRuleListItem`) still pass `key={key}`. Rendering a list item without a stable key causes React reconciliation issues (console warnings, and potential incorrect DOM/component reuse) especially problematic here since this view implements infinite scroll where the `rules` array grows incrementally.

title: Rule view link no longer carries the `returnTo` parameter
body: The previous implementation (removed GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx) built the rule link with `createRelativeUrl(\`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view\`, { returnTo })` where `returnTo` was computed via `createReturnTo()`. The new GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx drops this entirely: `href: createRelativeUrl(\`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view\`)`. This removes the 'return to previous page' functionality when a user clicks a rule from the alert list (e.g. from a filtered search), so after viewing/editing the rule, the user can no longer be navigated back to the exact list/filter state they came from.

title: New `provenance` field on GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase has no accompanying backend change in this PR
body: `isProvisionedPromRule()` (utils/rules.ts) and the new `GrafanaRuleListItem`/`useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` logic rely on `promRule.provenance` to gate Edit/Delete/Pause abilities for provisioned (locked) rules. This PR adds `provenance?: string` to `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` but contains no Go backend changes (no files under the Go backend are part of this PR). If the Grafana Prometheus rules API (`/api/prometheus/grafana/api/v1/rules`) does not already populate this field, `provenance` will always be `undefined` for promRule-only consumers, causing `isProvisionedPromRule` to always return false — meaning provisioned/locked Grafana rules could incorrectly appear editable/deletable from the new alert list view.

title: Pause and Delete actions silently become unreachable for promRule-only consumers, with no documentation of the limitation
body: `MenuItemPauseRule` (line ~123) is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` is true, and the Delete menu item (line ~165) requires `rulerRule` truthy. Since the new alert list view flow (GrafanaRuleListItem → RuleActionsButtons.V2 → AlertRuleMenu) never supplies a `rulerRule`, Pause and Delete are now permanently absent from the dropdown menu for rules shown in that view, even though the corresponding `canPause`/`canDelete` abilities can be computed as true via the Grafana-prom-based ability checks. This is a real functional regression/limitation (confirmed by GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx asserting exactly 4 menu items with no mention of Pause/Delete), but it is not called out anywhere in the PR description or code comments, risking confusion for future maintainers or being perceived as an unintentional regression.

title: Menu item presence tests don't verify the actual Silence action functionality
body: The test 'should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked' only checks that the Silence, Copy link, Duplicate and Export menu items are present (`ui.menuItems.silence().get()`, etc.) but never clicks the Silence item to assert that the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer actually opens. This test gap allowed the regression where the Silence menu item renders but produces no visible effect (see RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx finding) to go undetected.

title: Pause and Delete menu items are unreachable when only a Grafana Prometheus rule is available
body: The Pause menu item is gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and the Delete menu item is gated on `rulerRule` truthiness (lines 123 and 165). In the new 'no ruler calls in list view' flow (GrafanaRuleListItem -> RuleActionsButtons.V2 -> AlertRuleMenu), only `promRule` is passed and `rulerRule` is always `undefined`. The new Grafana-prom-based ability checks (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) correctly compute `canPause`/`canDelete` as true when the user has permission, but because the render conditions additionally require a non-null `rulerRule`, the Pause and Delete menu items never render in this code path even for fully permitted users. This silently removes the ability to pause or delete alert rules from the alert list view, which directly contradicts the goal of keeping these actions working while removing ruler API calls. This is confirmed by GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx asserting the menu contains exactly 4 items (silence, copy-link, duplicate, export) even though delete permission was granted in that test's setup.

title: Missing `key` prop when rendering GrafanaRuleListItem in FilterView
body: When switching from the removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` (which had `key={key}`) to the new `GrafanaRuleListItem`, the `key` prop was dropped: `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} namespaceName={ruleWithOrigin.namespaceName} showLocation={true} />`. The sibling branches (`DataSourceRuleLoader`, `UnknownRuleListItem`) still pass `key={key}`. Since this is rendered inside an array (`rules.map(...)`), React will emit 'missing key' warnings and may misidentify/incorrectly reconcile list items (e.g. during incremental loading via infinite scroll), causing stale DOM state or unnecessary re-mounts for Grafana rule items in the filtered list.

title: View link no longer includes `returnTo` query param
body: The previous implementation (deleted `GrafanaRuleListItem` in `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`) built the rule view URL with a `returnTo` parameter via `createReturnTo()`: `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })`. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` builds the href as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view')` without `returnTo`. This drops the 'navigate back to the list' context that was previously passed when a user clicked into a rule's detail view from the list, degrading back-navigation UX for all Grafana rules rendered through this component (used by both FilterView and GrafanaGroupLoader).

title: Stray leftover comment '// duplicate' in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities
body: The line `const { isEditable, isRemovable, loading } = useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule); // duplicate` contains a leftover inline comment that doesn't explain anything meaningful and appears to be a stray note from development (possibly meant to flag duplicated logic with `useIsRuleEditable`). It should either be removed or replaced with a clear explanation, since as written it is confusing to future maintainers.

title: No test coverage for Pause or Delete menu items in the new ruler-free rule list flow
body: The test 'should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked' grants `AccessControlAction.AlertingRuleDelete` (and others) but asserts only 4 menu items exist (silence, copy-link, duplicate, export) and never checks for Pause or Delete. Given that `AlertRuleMenu`'s Pause/Delete rendering depends on a `rulerRule` which is never supplied in this flow (see AlertRuleMenu.tsx finding), this test effectively documents the regression but does not call it out or assert that it is expected/intentional behavior, so a future reader could easily overlook that Delete/Pause silently never appear in this view.

title: Interpolating queries before the $__range exclusion check breaks splitting-safety for $__range queries
body: runSplitQuery() now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() on every target (lines 296-299) before partitioning them with querySupportsSplitting()/isQueryWithRangeVariable() (lines 282-287, 300). isQueryWithRangeVariable() is meant to detect the literal `$__range` token in the raw expr and exclude such queries from splitting, because (per the existing comment) the interpolated $__range value would be wrong once the query is split into sub-ranges. After this change, the expr passed to isQueryWithRangeVariable() has already had `$__range` substituted with the actual duration computed from the *original, unsplit* request range. The literal token is gone, so the check can no longer detect these queries, and they will now incorrectly be treated as splittable. Each split sub-request will then execute with a baked-in range window from the full request instead of the correct per-chunk window, producing wrong/duplicated aggregation results for any query using $__range. This directly contradicts the rationale documented in the adjacent comment and is a data-correctness regression introduced by moving interpolation to the top of the pipeline.

title: Queries are interpolated twice when shard splitting delegates to runSplitQuery
body: runShardSplitQuery() interpolates every target via datasource.applyTemplateVariables() (lines 49-53) before sharding. Later, splitQueriesByStreamShard()'s runNextRequest() builds subRequest.targets from these already-interpolated targets (via interpolateShardingSelector) and passes them into runSplitQuery() (line 163 in the full file). runSplitQuery() itself unconditionally calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() again on every incoming target (querySplitting.ts, the new .map() at the start of runSplitQuery). This means each query is run through template-variable interpolation twice per shard group. Besides being wasted work (tested in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts as 5 calls to applyTemplateVariables for a single logical query across 4 shard groups), this is risky if applyTemplateVariables is not fully idempotent (e.g. if it unconditionally injects ad-hoc filters/label matchers into the selector), since a second pass could duplicate filters already baked into the expr by the first pass. The test suite only exercises this with a trivial mock replace() that happens to be idempotent, so it does not actually validate correctness of double interpolation against the real datasource implementation.

title: No test covers that $__range queries remain excluded from splitting after the interpolation reorder
body: The PR adds a test only for interpolation of $__auto/$step before execution, but does not add or update any test exercising a query containing the $__range variable to verify it is still excluded from splitting (querySupportsSplitting/isQueryWithRangeVariable). Given that interpolation now happens before this exclusion check (see querySplitting.ts), and the check relies on finding the literal `$__range` token in the expr, this is exactly the scenario most likely to regress from this change, yet it is untested.

title: Interpolating queries before the $__range split-eligibility check defeats that check
body: `runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` on every query *before* `querySupportsSplitting()` is evaluated (line 300), and `querySupportsSplitting()` relies on `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` (lines 285-287) to detect the literal `$__range` token and exclude such queries from time-range splitting, because `$__range` is normally resolved to the whole request's range and would be wrong if baked into a split sub-range. Since `$__range` is a Grafana built-in template variable that gets resolved by `templateSrv.replace` (invoked via `applyTemplateVariables`) using `request.scopedVars`, by the time `isQueryWithRangeVariable` runs, the literal `$__range` text has already been substituted with the resolved value for the *whole* request range. The detection therefore never matches, so queries using `$__range` are now incorrectly classified as splittable and get partitioned into sub-time-ranges, each sub-query still carrying the stale, whole-range `$__range` value baked in — producing incorrect results for every sub-range chunk. This is exactly the scenario the existing check was designed to prevent.

title: Queries are interpolated twice: once in runShardSplitQuery and again inside runSplitQuery for every sub-request
body: `runShardSplitQuery` now maps over targets and calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` up front (line 52). The resulting already-interpolated queries are later passed (via `splitQueriesByStreamShard` -> `runSplitQuery`) to `runSplitQuery` in querySplitting.ts, which independently calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` again on every sub-request target (querySplitting.ts line 299). This means interpolation runs redundantly for every shard group/cycle of the same query (confirmed by the updated test expecting `applyTemplateVariables` to be called 5 times for what is effectively a single logical query across 4 sharded sub-requests plus the initial call). This wastes CPU cycles on every retry/cycle and risks subtle correctness issues if the interpolation function is not perfectly idempotent (e.g. values containing '$' that could be mistaken for variable syntax on a second pass).

title: No test covers interaction between early interpolation and the $__range split-exclusion check
body: The new 'Interpolates queries before execution' test only verifies that `$__auto` and `$step` placeholders get replaced before the sub-request is run. It does not add a regression test for a query containing `$__range`, which is the specific case `querySupportsSplitting`/`isQueryWithRangeVariable` is meant to protect (queries with `$__range` should never be split). Because interpolation now happens before that check, such a test would have caught that these queries are no longer correctly excluded from splitting after this change.

title: Queries are interpolated twice when sharding is combined with query splitting
body: runShardSplitQuery() now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on every target before sharding (line 52), exactly as before. However, splitQueriesByStreamShard() still delegates execution of each shard group to `runSplitQuery()` (imported from './querySplitting', used at line 163), and that function has been changed in this PR to also call `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on its targets (querySplitting.ts, line 299) before doing its own time-based splitting. Because the sub-request passed into the nested `runSplitQuery()` call still carries the same `request.scopedVars`/`request.filters` and an already-interpolated, shard-labeled `expr`, template-variable interpolation (including ad-hoc filter injection via `request.filters`) now runs a second time on an expression that has already been fully interpolated and had the `__stream_shard__` selector injected. If `applyTemplateVariables` unconditionally appends ad-hoc filters to the expression (a common implementation pattern), this will duplicate label matchers in the final query sent to the backend whenever ad-hoc filters are configured on the dashboard, silently breaking filtering for sharded+split Loki queries. Even if duplication is harmless in the specific implementation, the double interpolation is wasted work and a correctness risk that should be either avoided (skip re-interpolation for already-interpolated sub-requests) or explicitly verified not to double-apply filters/macros.

title: New tests don't verify that filters/macros are not double-applied when sharding delegates to runSplitQuery
body: The new 'Interpolates queries before execution' test (and the updated 'Interpolates queries before running' test, which now simply asserts `applyTemplateVariables` was called 5 times) mock `datasource.applyTemplateVariables`/`replace` with simple, idempotent string substitutions and never exercise `request.filters` (ad-hoc filters). Because the production code now calls `applyTemplateVariables` twice for every shard group (once in `runShardSplitQuery`, once inside the nested `runSplitQuery` call), a scenario where ad-hoc filters are present is never tested, so a regression that duplicates ad-hoc filter label matchers in the final sharded query would not be caught by this test suite.

title: traceID field dropped from 'Plugin Request Completed' log entries
body: The previous logRequest implementation explicitly added a "traceID" field (via tracing.TraceIDFromContext) to the log params for the 'Plugin Request Completed' message. This PR removes that code (and the tracing import) entirely, and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware/instrumentContext function that replaces part of the old logic does not add traceID to the context either. As a result, the completed-request log line permanently loses the trace correlation ID, which is a real observability regression: operators will no longer be able to correlate these log lines with distributed traces using the traceID field they previously relied on.

title: Logger middleware silently depends on being placed after ContextualLoggerMiddleware
body: LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx) to retrieve pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname fields that are only populated if ContextualLoggerMiddleware ran earlier in the chain and called log.WithContextualAttributes. This creates an implicit ordering dependency between NewContextualLoggerMiddleware and NewLoggerMiddleware that is not enforced anywhere (no assertion, no doc comment on either struct). If someone reorders CreateMiddlewares in the future (e.g. moving the logger middleware up, or adding another middleware in between that forks/clears the context), the 'Plugin Request Completed' log lines would silently drop these fields with no compile-time or runtime warning, making a difficult-to-detect regression.

title: Test function still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware after rename to MetricsMiddleware
body: The file was renamed to metrics_middleware_test.go and the production type/constructors were renamed from InstrumentationMiddleware to MetricsMiddleware, but the test function name 'TestInstrumentationMiddleware' (line 21) was left unchanged. This is inconsistent with the stated goal of the PR ('Better naming and consistency') and will confuse anyone searching for tests related to MetricsMiddleware.

title: No dedicated tests for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware/instrumentContext logic
body: This PR extracts instrumentContext and introduces a new exported middleware, ContextualLoggerMiddleware, as a standalone component responsible for attaching plugin/request metadata (pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, uname) to the context for downstream consumers (including LoggerMiddleware, which now critically depends on it). No test file was added to verify this behavior (e.g. that the attributes end up in the context and are retrievable via FromContext, or that CollectMetrics/QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth correctly instrument the context while SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream do not). Given that LoggerMiddleware now relies entirely on this middleware for several previously-explicit log fields, the lack of coverage is a meaningful gap.

title: Logger name still references 'instrumentation' after the rename
body: NewLoggerMiddleware is now constructed with log.New("plugin.instrumentation") even though the PR's stated purpose is to rename InstrumentationMiddleware to MetricsMiddleware for clarity and the contextual logger has been split out into its own middleware. Leaving the logger name as 'plugin.instrumentation' is inconsistent with the renaming effort and will make log filtering/searching by this name misleading now that it specifically backs the request-completion logger rather than instrumentation/metrics.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards state and the context, breaking log-call assertions
body: TestLogger.FromContext always returns a brand-new TestLogger (`NewTestLogger()`), ignoring the input context and discarding any reference to the original TestLogger instance. Now that LoggerMiddleware calls `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` instead of `m.logger.Info(...)`, any test that passes a TestLogger into NewLoggerMiddleware and later asserts on that same TestLogger's InfoLogs/DebugLogs/etc. fields will never see the call recorded, because the actual Info() call happens on a disposable logger returned by FromContext. This silently makes such test assertions pass/fail incorrectly (false negatives), hiding real logging bugs rather than catching them.

title: Logger interface extended with FromContext — breaking change for other implementers
body: A new method FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger was added to the plugins/log.Logger interface. Any type implementing this interface outside of the two updated implementations (grafanaInfraLogWrapper and TestLogger) will fail to compile or satisfy the interface. This is an interface-breaking change that should be called out explicitly and verified against all implementers/consumers in the codebase (and potentially downstream plugin SDK usages) before merging.

title: No unit tests for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware
body: The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware (and its instrumentContext helper moved from the metrics middleware) has no dedicated test file added in this PR, even though it contains non-trivial logic for building contextual log attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) per RPC method. Since LoggerMiddleware now depends entirely on this middleware having run earlier in the chain to produce correct log output, lack of coverage for this middleware (e.g., verifying attributes added/omitted for datasource vs non-datasource contexts, or for user-less contexts) is a meaningful test gap.

title: LoggerMiddleware silently loses pluginId/endpoint/user/datasource log fields if middleware ordering changes
body: logRequest no longer receives pluginCtx or endpoint; it now solely relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` picking up contextual attributes that were injected earlier in the chain by ContextualLoggerMiddleware (via log.WithContextualAttributes). This couples LoggerMiddleware's correctness to being registered strictly after ContextualLoggerMiddleware in CreateMiddlewares (pkg/services/pluginsintegration/pluginsintegration.go). There is no compile-time or runtime check enforcing this ordering — if the middleware list is ever reordered or ContextualLoggerMiddleware is removed/disabled, the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line will silently stop containing pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, and uname fields with no error or warning, degrading observability without any obvious failure signal.

title: Test function name not updated after middleware rename
body: The test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware even though the file was renamed to metrics_middleware_test.go and the type under test is now MetricsMiddleware. This is inconsistent with the stated purpose of the PR (renaming Instrumentation->Metrics for clarity) and will confuse future readers/searchers looking for tests of MetricsMiddleware.

title: Stale logger name 'plugin.instrumentation' used for the renamed LoggerMiddleware
body: NewLoggerMiddleware(cfg, log.New("plugin.instrumentation")) still uses the old 'instrumentation' terminology for the logger name, even though this PR's whole purpose is to rename Instrumentation to Metrics for clarity and this logger name is now used by LoggerMiddleware (not MetricsMiddleware). This leaves a misleading log channel name in log output that no longer corresponds to any component called 'instrumentation'.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new logger, discarding recorded calls
body: TestLogger.FromContext always returns NewTestLogger(), a fresh instance unrelated to the receiver `f`. Production code (LoggerMiddleware.logRequest) now calls `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` instead of `m.logger.Info(...)`. Any test that constructs a TestLogger, passes it into NewLoggerMiddleware, and later asserts on the original TestLogger's InfoLogs/ErrorLogs/etc. fields will never see the recorded call, because the Info call lands on the discarded, newly-created instance instead of the original. This silently breaks the ability of TestLogger to verify logging behavior through code paths that use FromContext, which is now the primary logging path in LoggerMiddleware, and can make pre-existing or future tests pass vacuously without exercising real assertions.

title: traceID field dropped from 'Plugin Request Completed' log line
body: The previous logRequest implementation explicitly added a 'traceID' field to logParams via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false). This logic (and the tracing import) has been removed, and the new instrumentContext helper in contextual_logger_middleware.go (which supplies the contextual attributes now used by m.logger.FromContext(ctx)) only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName/dsUID and uname -- it never adds traceID. As a result, the 'Plugin Request Completed' log entries emitted by LoggerMiddleware no longer contain a traceID field, removing the ability to correlate these logs with distributed traces. This appears to be an unintended regression rather than part of the stated rename/refactor.

title: Test function name not updated after renaming middleware to MetricsMiddleware
body: The file was renamed from instrumentation_middleware_test.go to metrics_middleware_test.go and the middleware type/constructor were renamed to MetricsMiddleware/newMetricsMiddleware, but the test function itself is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware. This leaves a naming inconsistency that defeats the purpose of the rename-for-consistency chore and will confuse future readers searching for tests related to MetricsMiddleware.

title: Logger name 'plugin.instrumentation' left over after renaming to metrics middleware
body: NewLoggerMiddleware is now instantiated with log.New("plugin.instrumentation"), but 'instrumentation' terminology was intentionally renamed away to 'metrics' in this PR for the MetricsMiddleware. The logger name still implies this is the metrics/instrumentation path even though it is unrelated to MetricsMiddleware (it backs LoggerMiddleware). This stale name is misleading for anyone searching logs or metrics by this logger name and should be updated to match the new naming scheme.

title: Device tagging is now synchronous on the anonymous auth hot path
body: Previously TagDevice was invoked asynchronously in a goroutine with its own timeout/panic-recovery, decoupled from the request. Now `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, httpReqCopy, anonymous.AnonDeviceUI)` is called synchronously inside Authenticate, which runs on every anonymous request. This adds a DB round trip (CountDevices + Insert/Update) to the critical path of every anonymous page load/request, and removes the panic-recovery wrapper that previously protected the request from an unexpected panic inside the tagging logic. This is a meaningful latency/availability regression for a feature that is on the hot path for all anonymous traffic.

title: Device-limit check is a non-atomic read-then-write, allowing the limit to be exceeded under concurrency
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice first runs CountDevices and then, based on that count, decides whether to INSERT a new device or fall back to UPDATE-only. There is no transaction or locking between the count and the subsequent insert, so multiple concurrent requests for different new devices can all observe a count below the limit and all proceed to insert, allowing the actual number of active devices to exceed deviceLimit. This undermines the guarantee the feature is supposed to provide.

title: No test coverage for the new error-propagation behavior when the device limit is reached
body: Authenticate now returns an error (failing anonymous authentication entirely) when TagDevice returns anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached, whereas other TagDevice errors are only logged. This is a behavior change with user-facing impact (anonymous users get denied once the device limit is hit), but no test in the shown diff (e.g. client_test.go) exercises this new code path to confirm Authenticate returns the expected error and identity is nil.

title: anonymousDeviceLimit default assignment yields an incorrectly narrow inferred type
body: `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` has no explicit type annotation, so TypeScript infers the field's type as the literal `undefined`, not `number | undefined` as declared in the `GrafanaConfig` interface. Although assignable for the `implements` check, any code that accesses this property through the concrete `GrafanaBootConfig` type (e.g. the exported `config` singleton) will see the type as always `undefined`, even though at runtime it can hold a numeric device limit merged in from boot data. This can break type-safe usage of the field (e.g. numeric comparisons) and should instead be declared as `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;`.

title: New `device_limit` anonymous auth setting is undocumented
body: A new `device_limit` key under `[auth.anonymous]` is introduced and read via `anonSection.Key("device_limit").MustInt64(0)`, but there is no corresponding update to the configuration documentation or sample/defaults ini shown in this change set. Operators have no way to discover this setting or its default/behavior without reading the Go source.

title: 30-day expiration window constant is now duplicated across three packages
body: The 30-day device expiration window is now independently defined three times: `thirtyDays` in impl.go, `anonymousDeviceExpiration` in anonstore/database.go, and `anonymousDeviceExpiration` in api/api.go. If one of these is changed in the future (e.g. to tune the retention window), the others can silently drift out of sync, causing inconsistent behavior between device counting, device listing, and device-limit enforcement.

title: Device-limit check is a non-atomic check-then-act, allowing the limit to be exceeded under concurrent load
body: In CreateOrUpdateDevice, the code first calls CountDevices to read the current count, then decides whether to insert a new device or fall back to updateDevice. There is no transaction, row lock, or unique-constraint-based enforcement tying the count check to the subsequent insert. Under concurrent anonymous requests (which is the normal case for this feature), multiple goroutines can simultaneously read a count that is below the limit and all proceed to insert new devices, allowing the configured anonymousDeviceLimit to be exceeded by an arbitrary margin. This defeats the purpose of the feature under real traffic.

title: Anonymous device tagging changed from async fire-and-forget to a synchronous, blocking call inside Authenticate, adding DB latency/risk to every anonymous request
body: Previously TagDevice was invoked in a separate goroutine with its own timeout context and panic recovery, so DB latency or panics in the tagging path could not affect the anonymous authentication request. This PR removes that goroutine and panic-recovery wrapper and calls a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...) synchronously in Authenticate. This is required to make ErrDeviceLimitReached able to block authentication, but it also means every anonymous request (at least until the device is cached) now blocks on a DB round-trip (and, when the device limit is enabled, an additional CountDevices query) as part of the authentication hot path, and any panic inside TagDevice is no longer isolated from the request. This is a potential latency/availability regression for installs with many anonymous users.

title: New auth.anonymous device_limit setting is not documented anywhere
body: setting.go adds a new ini key `device_limit` under the `[auth.anonymous]` section (cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit = anonSection.Key("device_limit").MustInt64(0)), but no changes were made to conf/defaults.ini, conf/sample.ini, or the configuration documentation pages describing this new option, its default value (0 = unlimited), or its effect. Administrators have no way to discover this new, user-facing configuration knob.

title: No test covers that Authenticate rejects anonymous login once the device limit is exceeded
body: The new behavior in Authenticate propagates anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached from TagDevice back to the authn broker, effectively denying anonymous authentication once the device limit is reached. Only anonstore/database_test.go (TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit) tests the lower-level store behavior; there is no test exercising Anonymous.Authenticate or the end-to-end AnonDeviceService.TagDevice flow to confirm the error is correctly surfaced/handled (vs. other, non-limit errors which should be swallowed). This leaves the primary new user-facing behavior of the feature (anonymous users get rejected beyond the device limit) without direct test coverage.

title: Device-activity window constant duplicated across packages risks silent drift
body: anonymousDeviceExpiration (30 days) is now defined independently in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go and pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/api/api.go, while pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go already has its own separate `thirtyDays` constant with the same value used for usage-stat counting. These three constants must be kept in sync by hand across files/packages; if one is changed (e.g., to adjust the retention/activity window) without updating the others, the device-limit count, the /api/anonymous/devices listing window, and the usage-stat count will become inconsistent with each other.

title: Anonymous device limit value is exposed to unauthenticated users via frontend settings
body: AnonymousDeviceLimit is added to FrontendSettingsDTO and populated unconditionally from hs.Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit in getFrontendSettings, which is served by GetFrontendSettings without requiring authentication (it is accessible to anonymous users since this endpoint powers anonymous access itself). This leaks an operational/security-relevant configuration value (the device cap) to any unauthenticated caller, which could help an attacker determine how close the deployment is to its device limit or tune an attack to exhaust it.

title: Device tagging changed from async best-effort to synchronous blocking call on auth hot path
body: Previously TagDevice was called in a background goroutine with its own timeout context and a `recover()` to protect against panics, decoupling device bookkeeping from the request path. The new code calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, httpReqCopy, anonymous.AnonDeviceUI)` synchronously inside `Authenticate`, using the request's own context. Every anonymous request (which can be very high volume, e.g. for public dashboards) now performs a blocking DB round trip (CountDevices + insert/update) as part of authentication, adding latency to all anonymous traffic and removing the panic-safety net that previously prevented a tagging failure/panic from affecting the authenticated request.

title: Reaching the device limit now fails anonymous authentication entirely instead of only skipping tagging
body: When `TagDevice` returns `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached`, `Authenticate` now returns `nil, err`, causing the entire anonymous authentication attempt to fail. Previously, any tagging error (including this one, since it ran async) was only logged and never affected the resulting Identity. Since anonymous access is often the sole/last-resort auth client for public dashboards or orgs with anonymous access enabled, once the global device limit is reached, all subsequent anonymous requests may fail to authenticate at all (not just fail to be tracked), effectively locking out anonymous users instance-wide instead of degrading gracefully.

title: Check-then-act race condition in device limit enforcement
body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` first calls `CountDevices` to check whether the limit is reached, then performs either an insert or an update, as two separate, unsynchronized DB operations with no transaction or locking between them. Multiple concurrent requests for different new device IDs can all read a count below the limit before any of them commits its insert, allowing the number of distinct devices to exceed `deviceLimit`. There is no unique constraint or atomic counter preventing this overshoot.

title: TagDevice now propagates tagging errors (including device-limit errors) up the call stack
body: `TagDevice` previously only logged a tagging failure and always returned `nil`. The change adds `return err` after logging, so any failure from `tagDeviceUI` (e.g. `ErrDeviceLimitReached`) is now returned to callers. Combined with the change in client.go that treats this error specially, this converts an internal bookkeeping failure into a hard authentication failure, which is a behavioral change not called out in the PR description and lacks test coverage for the new failure path through the full `AnonDeviceService`/`Anonymous` client stack.

title: Device limit is enforced globally across all organizations, not per anonymous org
body: `CountDevices` queries `anon_device` without any organization filter, so the single global `AnonymousDeviceLimit` config value is applied across the entire Grafana instance. If multiple orgs have anonymous access enabled, devices from one org count against the limit for all other orgs, which may not match the intended per-deployment or per-org licensing semantics implied by a configurable 'device limit' feature.

title: New `device_limit` configuration option is undocumented
body: A new ini setting `auth.anonymous.device_limit` is introduced (`cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit = anonSection.Key("device_limit").MustInt64(0)`), but no corresponding entries were added to `conf/sample.ini`/`conf/defaults.ini` or the configuration documentation. Admins have no discoverable way to learn about or configure this new feature flag.

title: No test exercises device-limit enforcement through the full service/client stack
body: The updated tests only call `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` with a default `setting.NewCfg()` (device limit 0, i.e. unlimited), so the new device-limit behavior is only verified at the `anonstore` layer (`database_test.go`). There is no integration test confirming that `AnonDeviceService.TagDevice` or `Anonymous.Authenticate` correctly surfaces `ErrDeviceLimitReached` once the configured limit is exceeded, despite this being a user-facing behavior change in `client.go`/`impl.go`.

title: Unrelated and unexplained change of cleanup ticker interval from 10 to 1 minute
body: The periodic ticker that drives srv.clean() (which runs all cleanup jobs: temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, user invites, short URLs, query history) was changed from `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` to `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)`. This is unrelated to the stated purpose of the PR (splitting annotation cleanup queries to avoid MySQL deadlocks) and is not mentioned anywhere in the PR description. Running every cleanup job 10x more frequently increases database load across every cleanup job, not just annotations, and could even make the targeted deadlock problem worse by increasing contention frequency. This looks like a leftover debugging change that should be reverted or, if intentional, needs to be called out and justified in the PR description.

title: Misuse of Error log level for routine, successful batch cleanup logging
body: In CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags, every batch iteration logs via r.log.Error (e.g. lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579) even when there is no error (err is nil and is logged as a field). This mislabels routine, expected operational information as an error, which will pollute error-level logs/alerting dashboards that filter or page on Error severity, and may trigger false alerts in production for normal cleanup activity. These should be logged at Debug or Info level, consistent with how the rest of the cleanup service (cleanup.go) logs routine completion at Debug level.

title: Inefficient O(n^2) string building for SQLite large-batch delete
body: In deleteByIDs, when running on SQLite with a batch size exceeding the parameter limit, the code builds the IN-clause value list by repeatedly calling fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) inside a loop over all ids. Each call reallocates and copies the growing `values` string, making this O(n^2) in the number of ids. With batch sizes in the tens of thousands (the added test uses 32767), this can be noticeably slow and allocate excessive memory compared to using a strings.Builder or strconv.AppendInt into a byte slice (as is already done elsewhere in this same file, e.g. in getAccessControlFilter).

title: Cleanup job ticker interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute without explanation
body: The ticker driving ALL cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, user invites, short URLs, query history) was changed from `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` to `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)`. This is a 10x increase in the frequency of every cleanup job, not just the annotation cleanup job this PR is meant to fix. The PR description only discusses splitting annotation cleanup queries to avoid MySQL deadlocks and says nothing about changing the cleanup cadence. This looks like an unrelated/unintentional change that will significantly increase database load for all cleanup jobs and could itself contribute to lock contention (the very problem this PR tries to solve), and should be reverted or explicitly justified.

title: Normal, successful cleanup operations logged at Error level
body: In CleanAnnotations (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags (lines 576, 579), `r.log.Error(...)` is called on every batch iteration regardless of whether an error actually occurred (the `err` value logged is often nil, and these calls happen on the success path). Since this cleanup job runs continuously in the background, this will flood logs with Error-level entries during completely normal operation, which can trigger false alerts in monitoring/alerting systems that key off error-level logs and makes it harder to spot genuine failures. These should be logged at Debug/Info level, with only real failures logged as errors.

title: Full ID list logged on every batch, which can be very large
body: The log calls on lines 534, 554, and 576 include the full `ids` slice as a log field. Since the batch size (`AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize`) can be configured very large (the new test uses 32767), each cleanup iteration will serialize and emit a potentially huge list of integers into the logs on every batch, which adds unnecessary overhead and can bloat log storage, especially since (per the previous finding) these are logged unconditionally at Error level.

title: fetch-then-delete split introduces a TOCTOU window not present with the previous atomic subquery DELETE
body: CleanAnnotations/CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags now call fetchIDs and deleteByIDs as two separate WithDbSession calls (not wrapped in a shared transaction), whereas previously a single DELETE ... WHERE id IN (subquery) statement was atomic. Between the SELECT and subsequent DELETE, concurrently running cleanup instances (e.g. in a multi-instance Grafana deployment without a server lock around this specific call) or other writers could change which rows match, causing deleteByIDs to delete fewer/different rows than counted, so the reported 'affected' counts from CleanAnnotations/CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags can diverge from what was actually intended to be deleted. This behavior change is only partially acknowledged in a code comment ('may under-delete') but is not covered by any new test demonstrating the acceptable failure mode under concurrent access.

title: Cleanup ticker interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute, unrelated to stated PR scope
body: The background cleanup ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This change is not mentioned anywhere in the PR description (which is only about splitting the annotation cleanup query to avoid MySQL deadlocks) and affects *all* cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, user invites, short URLs, query history), not just annotation cleanup. Running all of these jobs 10x more frequently significantly increases database load and lock contention, which directly works against the stated goal of reducing deadlocks/contention on the annotation tables. This looks like an accidental leftover from debugging/testing and should be reverted to the original 10 minute interval (or justified explicitly) before merge.

title: Misuse of Error log level for routine, successful cleanup progress
body: Lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576 and 579 all call `r.log.Error(...)` to log normal, successful progress of the batched cleanup loop (e.g. "Annotations to clean by time", "cleaned annotations by time"), even when `err`/`y` is nil. These calls execute on every batch iteration (potentially thousands of times per cleanup cycle, especially combined with a now much more frequent 1-minute ticker in cleanup.go).
