title: Email send errors only logged to console, not properly reported
body: If `sendAddGuestsEmails` throws, the error is swallowed with just `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without using the project's logger or including the actual error details (`err` not logged), making failures to notify attendees/organizers hard to debug in production.

title: Zod schema re-created on every render
body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is constructed inside the component body on every render instead of being defined once at module scope. This is wasteful and inconsistent with best practice for schema definitions used only for validation logic.

title: Empty string in multiEmailValue passes validation incorrectly
body: The default state is `[""]` and `handleAdd` only checks `multiEmailValue.length === 0`, not whether entries are empty strings. An empty string fails `z.string().email()`, so submitting without touching the field would show a validation error, but if a user adds then removes focus without filling it could still submit empty placeholder entries along with valid ones, potentially sending blank guest strings to the backend when validation briefly passes due to array mutations.

title: Duplicate default export name context with form/Select's UnstyledSelect unaffected but no type export for MultiEmail
body: `MultiEmail` is exported but no corresponding prop types (e.g., `MultiEmailProps`) are exported from the package index, unlike other similar form components (e.g., TimezoneSelectProps). Consumers outside the package cannot type-check props without reaching into internal paths.

title: Permission check uses AND instead of OR, breaking team admin/owner authorization
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. A user can be an admin OR an owner, but these two role checks are typically mutually exclusive (owner is a separate role from admin), so logically ANDing them means this will almost always evaluate false, denying legitimate team admins/owners the ability to add guests unless they happen to satisfy both roles. This should be `||`.

title: Guest emails leak into console log on error, and errors swallowed silently
body: On failure to send add-guest emails, the catch block just does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging the actual error or using the project's logger (`@calcom/lib/logger` used elsewhere). This hides failures from monitoring and makes debugging email delivery issues difficult; it should use the structured logger and include the error object.

title: No input sanitization/limit on number of guests added
body: The schema (addGuests.schema.ts) only validates each guest is a valid email but places no limit on the number of guests that can be added in one call. A malicious or buggy client could pass thousands of emails, causing a large bulk createMany and spamming hundreds of emails per booking with no rate limiting, unlike other similar endpoints that usually cap list sizes.

title: Guests added to calendar/video event but no error handling around eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees
body: The call to `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is unguarded; if the underlying calendar/video provider call throws, the whole mutation fails even though the DB has already been updated with the new attendees (see the `prisma.booking.update` call above). This creates a data inconsistency where guests exist in the DB as attendees but the calendar event/invite was never updated, with no rollback or compensation logic, and no user-facing distinction between a DB failure and a calendar sync failure.

title: Error toast interpolates raw backend message key without translation fallback safety
body: `t(err.message)}` passes `err.message` directly to the translation function; if the backend throws a message that isn't a translation key (e.g. a raw error string, Prisma error, or unexpected exception message), `t()` will just return the untranslated string, which is fine, but combined with `err.data?.code` prefix this could show raw/confusing text (e.g. 'undefined: NOT_FOUND') to users for errors not explicitly mapped to i18n keys, as there's no safe default handling for the generic case.

title: Guest email case-sensitivity not normalized when deduping / blacklist check
body: `uniqueGuests` compares `guest === attendee.email` directly without lowercasing, while blacklist check lowercases only the blacklist entries but not the incoming guest emails (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). This means mixed-case guest emails can bypass both the duplicate-attendee check and the blacklist filter, allowing duplicate or blacklisted guests to be added via case variation.

title: Overly broad delete condition removes all reminders with retryCount > 1 regardless of method
body: The deleteMany OR clause `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` is not scoped to `method: SMS` like the first clause. Since retryCount is a shared field on WorkflowReminder (also potentially used by EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders in the future, or any reminder with a non-SMS method that incidentally has retryCount > 1), this condition could delete non-SMS workflow reminders too. Given this is the SMS-specific scheduling cron, it should scope by method: SMS as well, otherwise it silently deletes unrelated reminders that happen to exceed the threshold.

title: Reminder deleted before scheduledSMS actually succeeds confirmed, and retryCount increments may still allow unlimited retries within a single run due to delete running once at top
body: The deleteMany for retryCount > 1 only runs once at the start of the handler. If a reminder fails scheduling in this same cron run (incrementing retryCount from 1 to 2), it will not be deleted until the next cron invocation, meaning it stays in an invalid state for up to the next run's cadence. This is a minor behavioral inefficiency rather than a hard bug, but combined with the lack of method scoping it increases risk of unexpected reminder loss or persistence.

title: Delete condition for retryCount is global, not scoped to SMS method
body: The OR clause `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, regardless of method (EMAIL, SMS, WHATSAPP). Since retryCount is only incremented in this SMS-specific handler, this may be fine today, but it is a latent bug: if retryCount is ever reused by other reminder types, this unscoped condition will delete unrelated reminders. It should be scoped with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` as well to avoid unintended data loss.

title: Reminders with empty/missing message or sendTo are retried indefinitely
body: When `message` is falsy or `sendTo` is missing, the code silently skips both the success and retry-increment branches (lines 158-188). Such reminders remain `scheduled: false` forever and are picked up again every cron run without ever incrementing retryCount or being cleaned up, unlike failures caught by try/catch or the twilio.scheduleSMS failure path. This creates reminders that loop indefinitely rather than being retried-and-deleted per the stated intent of the PR.

title: No test coverage added for new retry/delete logic
body: This PR changes core scheduling/deletion behavior (adding retryCount increments and deletion when retryCount > 1) but includes no new or updated tests verifying that reminders are retried, incremented, and eventually deleted as expected. This is a behavioral change with data-deletion consequences and should have test coverage.

title: deleteMany OR clause deletes unrelated reminders with retryCount > 1
body: The deleteMany query ORs `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` with the SMS-method/scheduledDate condition, but this second clause has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter. This means any WorkflowReminder (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, etc.) that happens to have retryCount > 1 would be deleted too, even though retryCount is only ever incremented for SMS reminders in this file. If retryCount is reused/incremented elsewhere for other methods, this causes unintended data loss across unrelated reminder types.

title: Reminders are only deleted on next cron run after reaching retryCount 2, allowing one extra retry/duplication window
body: After a reminder fails twice, retryCount becomes 2, but the current run's deleteMany query runs before the update loop and only deletes rows with retryCount > 1 (i.e. existing reminders from a prior run). This means a reminder that just hit retryCount=2 in this run will still be re-processed in the next cron invocation before being deleted, since the delete step always runs first and would only catch it on the *following* run - meaning the reminder could be retried indefinitely if continually caught right at the boundary and twilio.scheduleSMS is retried for the same booking without respecting the already-incremented retry count the same cycle. This is a minor logic/ordering issue, not fatal, but means a reminder is attempted at least 3 times (0,1,2) not 2 as intended by the PR description ("failed twice" implies deletion after exactly 2 failures).

title: No retryCount increment when message/sendTo is empty
body: If `message` or `sendTo` ends up falsy, the if-block at line 158 is skipped entirely with no retryCount increment and no logging, so these reminders remain in scheduled=false, retryCount=0 state forever, retried every cron run without ever being cleaned up or flagged as failing.

title: No test coverage added for new retry logic
body: This PR introduces new retryCount increment/deletion behavior (on scheduling failure, exception, and cleanup query) but includes no unit or integration tests verifying that: (1) retryCount increments correctly on failure, (2) reminders are deleted once retryCount exceeds the threshold, (3) the OR condition in deleteMany doesn't wrongly delete non-SMS reminders. This is a meaningful behavior change without regression protection.

title: findMany method removed, breaking callers
body: The service previously exposed a `findMany` method used by consumers of InsightsBookingService to query bookings via Prisma's typed API. This PR removes `findMany` entirely and only exposes `getBaseConditions`, which returns a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment that callers must manually interpolate into `$queryRaw`. Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` (e.g. API routes or other services) will now fail to compile/run. The PR description and diff do not show any check or migration of callers of this now-removed method, which is a breaking API change not reflected in the integration tests update.

title: Caching tests removed without replacement
body: The previous test suite included a 'Caching' describe block verifying that getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions results are cached across calls. This block was deleted entirely in the PR, removing coverage of the caching behavior (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions) that still exists in the service implementation. No equivalent test was added to validate caching still works correctly with the new Prisma.sql return type.

title: Potential SQL fragment growth with large ID lists via ANY(array)
body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition now use `ANY(${ids})` with parameter arrays passed directly into Prisma.sql. For orgs/teams with very large membership, this creates a single large array parameter; while likely fine, it changes from Prisma's `in` operator semantics to raw SQL ANY, and should be verified for correct parameter binding/escaping especially given these ids come from DB-generated integers (likely safe) but any assumption on this being type-checked by Prisma is weakened since this is now a raw SQL path.

title: Team scope condition always includes OR branch even with no users
body: buildTeamAuthorizationCondition only pushes the userId OR condition when userIdsFromTeam.length > 0, but previously the WHERE-based implementation always included a userId IN [] clause (effectively false). The Prisma.sql version silently omits the userId clause entirely when it's empty, resulting in only the team booking condition applying—functionally fine here, but note that if usersFromTeam is empty while teamId condition is also false, there is no NOTHING fallback, which is still consistent. However, the subtle risk is that this branch previously using findAllByTeamIds for all orgs can return huge arrays bound as ANY($1) parameters—confirm Prisma supports array binding for ANY() cleanly across drivers (postgres only); this breaks compatibility if any other DB target is used.

title: Potential unbounded growth of ANY() array for large orgs
body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition fetches all teams and all users of an org and inlines them into an ANY($ids) SQL array. For large organizations this could produce very large parameter arrays in raw SQL queries, which may hit Postgres parameter limits or cause performance degradation compared to a JOIN/subquery based condition in the previous Prisma object query.

title: Removed caching tests not replaced
body: The PR removes the previous 'Caching' describe block tests (that verified getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions caching behavior) without adding equivalent coverage for the new Prisma.sql-based caching. Since cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions are still implemented in the service, this leaves caching behavior untested.

title: findMany API no longer tested
body: The original test exercised service.findMany(...), the public querying API consumers would use. The rewritten test only calls getBaseConditions() and performs a manual $queryRaw, meaning the actual integration of baseConditions into a real repository/service query method (if such method still exists elsewhere) is no longer verified by this test file.

title: Removed public findMany() method breaks callers
body: The previous InsightsBookingService exposed a findMany(findManyArgs) method that combined conditions and queried via Prisma's typed API. This PR removes it in favor of getBaseConditions(), but any existing callers of service.findMany(...) elsewhere in the codebase (e.g., insights routers/handlers) will fail to compile or break at runtime. There's no deprecation shim or migration of callers shown in this diff; if callers still invoke findMany, this is a breaking API change not covered by the test updates.

title: Caching behavior tests removed
body: The previous test suite included a 'Caching' describe block verifying that getAuthorizationConditions() and getFilterConditions() cache their results across repeated calls. This PR deletes those tests entirely without replacement, reducing coverage of the memoization logic (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions) that still exists in insightsBooking.ts. Regressions in caching (e.g., accidentally rebuilding conditions) would no longer be caught by tests.

title: Loss of findMany integration test coverage
body: The final integration test previously exercised the public findMany() API end-to-end with typed Prisma where-clauses. It was replaced with a raw $queryRaw test against getBaseConditions(). If findMany is still used elsewhere, there is no integration test left verifying it works correctly with the new Prisma.sql-based conditions.

title: deleteCache does not check delegation credential ownership
body: The handler only looks up prisma.credential with userId filter. For delegation credentials (which may not have a direct userId or are shared), this check could incorrectly allow or deny access, or miss validating that the credential actually belongs to the acting user in multi-tenant/org scenarios. Other handlers in this codebase use more thorough credential ownership checks (including org/team credentials). This bypass could allow deleting cache for credentials not truly owned by the user if credential.userId semantics differ (e.g., shared/team credentials).

title: N+1 free pattern but new repository instance ignores credential type correctness
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is called with all credentialIds including non-Google-calendar integrations (Office365, etc.) and in-memory delegation credentials whose credentialId may be negative (per isInMemoryDelegationCredential checks elsewhere in CalendarCacheRepository). Passing negative/in-memory credential IDs into the groupBy query is harmless but wasteful, and more importantly it does not filter by integration type, so the resulting cacheUpdatedAt map is computed for all credential types though it's only meaningful for Google Calendar. This doesn't match the pattern elsewhere in the code (e.g. assertCalendarHasDbCredential) which explicitly guards against invalid credential ids being used in cache lookups.

title: updatedAt added as @updatedAt but migration lacks backfill/default consistency check
body: The Prisma field uses @default(now()) @updatedAt, meaning Prisma manages it automatically on every write (including raw upsert calls in calendar-cache.repository.ts that don't explicitly set updatedAt). This is fine for Prisma Client writes, but any raw SQL inserts/updates to CalendarCache (e.g. via migrations or external scripts) that don't go through Prisma Client will not get updatedAt refreshed automatically, since @updatedAt is implemented at Prisma Client/query level, not DB level. If any other code path writes to CalendarCache via raw queries, cache status reporting will be stale/incorrect.

title: Hardcoded locale in date formatting ignores user's language settings
body: new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) hardcodes the locale instead of using the user's configured locale from useLocale(). This will show reversed/incorrect-looking date formats for non-English users, inconsistent with the rest of the app's localization support that was added in this PR (new i18n strings).

title: interpolation option improperly placed inside t() call
body: The `interpolation: { escapeValue: false }` option is passed inside the same object as the `timestamp` interpolation value for `t("cache_last_updated", {...})`. react-i18next expects interpolation options to be passed separately (as part of i18next options), not mixed with variables; here it will be treated as an extra named variable, not as an actual interpolation config, so it has no effect and could show up unexpectedly if the translation string references it.

title: Unconditional updateManyByCredentialId call after every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache regardless of cache miss/hit
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now unconditionally calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId for all selected calendars under the credential, bumping SelectedCalendar.updatedAt even when this method is invoked as part of routine operations (e.g., unwatchCalendar's call to repopulate cache for remaining calendars). This adds an extra DB write on every fetch cycle, which, combined with CalendarCache being queried heavily, could add non-trivial write load, and the PR description itself notes this field isn't actually surfaced in the UI (cacheUpdatedAt from CalendarCache is used instead), making this update likely unnecessary overhead.

title: No credential type/ownership scoping to calendar credentials only
body: The handler validates the credential belongs to the user but doesn't restrict deletion to calendar-type credentials or verify it is actually a Google Calendar credential with cache data. Any credential ID owned by the user could trigger a (harmless but unintended) calendarCache.deleteMany call. More importantly, it does not check team/organization-owned credentials (e.g. via delegation) possibly leaving admins unable to delete cache for team-managed accounts, or conversely silently no-op without feedback since deleteMany on non-matching credentialId succeeds with 0 rows deleted, giving a false success response to the UI even if no cache existed.

title: Unconditional updateManyByCredentialId call on every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache
body: After looping through all event-type groups, the code unconditionally calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` to bump `updatedAt` for all calendars under the credential. This runs an extra UPDATE query on every call to fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache (used extensively in webhook/cron and cache refresh flows), with an empty `data` object relying on Prisma's `@updatedAt` auto-timestamp behavior. Doing this for every invocation adds additional DB load, and the empty `data: {}` pattern is fragile — if the `updatedAt` field were ever changed to not use `@updatedAt`, this call would silently do nothing useful while still issuing a query to all rows matching credentialId regardless of eventTypeId scoping, potentially touching more rows than intended within a single credential across multiple event types.

title: updatedAt added with @updatedAt plus a migration-time default; comment is contradictory/misleading
body: The field is declared `updatedAt DateTime @default(now()) @updatedAt` with a comment saying "Provide an initial value for legacy rows and future raw inserts." However `@updatedAt` automatically manages the timestamp on every Prisma update, so the explicit `@default(now())` is only relevant for raw SQL inserts bypassing Prisma — but the migration itself already backfills existing rows with `DEFAULT NOW()`. This dual mechanism is redundant/confusing and could cause confusion for future maintainers about whether `updatedAt` reflects "row created" vs "cache value last updated", especially since cache entries are upserted via Prisma `upsert` (update branch) which already triggers `@updatedAt`.

title: Hardcoded locale/date formatting ignores user locale and i18n
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` is hardcoded, ignoring the app's `t`/i18n locale setting used elsewhere in the component. This causes an inconsistent experience for non-English users, showing dates in US format regardless of their chosen locale.

title: Component return null leaves user without any affordance when disableConnectionModification and no cache
body: When `canDisconnect` is false (delegation credential or disableConnectionModification) and there's no cache (`hasCache` false, e.g. non-Google calendar or Google with no cache yet), the component renders `null`. This silently removes any actions/ellipsis menu for that credential row with no visual indication, which is a behavior change versus the previous `DisconnectIntegration` component that likely rendered a disabled/absent state more predictably; combined with the PR replacing `DisconnectIntegration` entirely, non-Google calendar integrations (e.g., Outlook, Office365) lose any action affordance since `hasCache` is always false for them and disconnect may still be legitimately desired.

title: Added fields to UserWithCalendars type not used/validated for all callers
body: `allSelectedCalendars`/`userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` fields to be selected, but this type is consumed by multiple callers constructing `UserWithCalendars` from various Prisma selects (e.g. withSelectedCalendars, platform libraries). If any caller doesn't select these new fields, this is a type-level breaking change that could cause runtime undefined errors or TypeScript failures outside the files shown in this diff that weren't updated to add the new select fields.

title: No authorization check for team/org delegated credentials
body: The deleteCache handler only checks `credential.userId === user.id`, but credentials can be delegated or team-owned (as seen elsewhere with delegationCredentialId handling). This check doesn't account for delegated credentials or admin-managed credentials, potentially blocking legitimate admin deletions or allowing inconsistent authorization behavior compared to other credential-related handlers (e.g. disconnect) that may use a shared permission check.

title: Generic Error thrown instead of TRPCError
body: Throwing a plain `Error` instead of `TRPCError` with a proper code (e.g. `NOT_FOUND` or `UNAUTHORIZED`) means the client will receive a generic 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a meaningful error code, making it harder for clients to distinguish between 'not found' and other failures, and this is inconsistent with other handlers in the codebase using TRPCError.

title: updatedAt default violates @updatedAt semantics / inconsistent with schema default
body: The migration sets `updatedAt` with `DEFAULT NOW()` but the Prisma schema marks the field `@default(now()) @updatedAt`. Prisma's @updatedAt expects the column to auto-update on every write via Prisma Client, but any direct SQL writes/upserts bypassing Prisma (e.g. raw queries) will not update this field automatically, and existing rows retroactively get 'NOW()' as updatedAt at migration time which is misleading since it doesn't reflect actual last-cache-update time, undermining the newly added cache-status UI feature.

title: cacheUpdatedAt may already be a Date, double wrapping with new Date()
body: `cacheUpdatedAt` is typed `Date | null` but comes over tRPC (serialized via superjson, so likely fine) — however calling `new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)` when cacheUpdatedAt is already a Date object is redundant but not harmful. More importantly, `hasCache` check `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` doesn't account for `cacheUpdatedAt` being `undefined` vs `null`, and the dropdown won't render if cache does not yet exist even though 'isGoogleCalendar' is true, which may be the intended early return but should be verified against the full feature matrix (e.g. integrations other than Google Calendar relying on cache).

title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds called on every connectedCalendars query without caching
body: `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` on every request to `connectedCalendars`, adding an additional groupBy query per request. For users/orgs with many credentials this could add noticeable DB load; there's no memoization or batching optimization, and this new query runs regardless of whether the UI actually needs cache status (e.g., non-Google calendar integrations).

title: cacheUpdatedAt uses || null, converting falsy-but-valid timestamps incorrectly
body: `cacheStatusMap.get(calendar.credentialId) || null` will treat a valid Date object as falsy only if it's literally falsy, which Date objects never are, so this isn't actually buggy for Date values — but it silently swallows the distinction between 'no cache status found' and 'found but value is null', which could mask bugs if getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ever returns `{credentialId, updatedAt: undefined}`. Low risk but worth tightening to explicit undefined check for clarity and correctness guarantees.

title: Scheduled sends cancellation uses sendgrid batch cancel without checking previous cancel limit, no error handling for individual failures
body: The cron now cancels reminders marked 'cancelled' within the next hour via SendGrid's scheduled_sends cancel API, then deletes the DB record. If the SendGrid request throws (e.g. due to the same 100-pending-cancellation limit mentioned in the PR description, or any transient API error), the entire loop's try/catch wraps all iterations, so a single failure aborts the whole batch (workflowRemindersToDelete never gets Promise.all'd for remaining items, and already-cancelled-in-SendGrid items that failed DB delete won't retry correctly). This can still result in silently stuck 'cancelled' reminders whose emails are sent anyway if they fall outside the next cron run's time window overlap assumptions, or lead to duplicate cancel calls on subsequent runs that may error out and block the rest of the batch again.

title: immediateDelete bypasses cancellation-limit issue the PR intends to fix
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder still supports an 'immediateDelete' path (used in handleNewBooking.ts reschedule flow and workflows.tsx step-delete flow) that directly calls the SendGrid cancel endpoint synchronously, which is exactly the behavior that caused the original bug (exceeding the 100 pending cancellations limit documented in the PR description). Since this path is still used for immediate deletes (e.g., on reschedule of previous booking, step deletion, workflow deletion), those cases are not protected by the new 'cancelled' flag + cron batching mechanism, and could still experience the same silent failure once more than 100 cancellations are pending at once.

title: Removed deleteMany of to-be-removed reminders when event types deactivated
body: Previously the code also called ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany for reminders being removed when event types are deactivated. The new code only calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder (which, for EMAIL, now just sets the 'cancelled' flag rather than deleting), but never deletes the row from the DB in this update() flow for the 'removedEventTypes' case. Since these reminders are tied to bookings that remain in the activeOn relation state after this update, this may leave orphaned WorkflowReminder rows that are only cleaned up by the cron if 'scheduledDate' is within the next hour — otherwise they persist indefinitely, and if the event type is later reactivated, the booking may not get a new reminder since the old row still exists with cancelled=true, scheduled=true referencing an old obsolete batch, blocking the new unscheduled-reminder path from re-creating one for that booking given no uniqueness check here on bookingUid/workflowStepId pair but risk of leftover stale cancelled reminders never purged in time to free email sends is still present.

title: SMS reminder deletion remains synchronous but no cancelled-flag batching like email
body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the WorkflowReminder row immediately after calling twilio.cancelSMS, unlike the new two-phase (cancelled flag + cron deletion) approach for email. If twilio.cancelSMS throws for some reason (e.g., rate limiting or already-passed cancellation window), the whole function throws before prisma.workflowReminder.delete runs, by design in the try/catch it's swallowed, but the reminder row then still exists in a scheduled state and will still attempt to send via Twilio since nothing marks it cancelled; there's no retry or cron-based cleanup path for SMS now, meaning the original cancellation reliability issue described in the PR for emails is not fully addressed for SMS reminders.

title: Cancellation and new scheduling race within same cron run
body: The cron job first cancels reminders flagged `cancelled: true` scheduled within the next hour, then later finds unscheduled reminders and schedules new emails. There's no check that excludes already-cancelled bookingUids/workflowStepIds from this unscheduled-reminders query, so if a reminder was cancelled (cancelled=true) but not yet caught by the 1-hour window pass, it could still be picked up and sent since the `unscheduledReminders` query filters only on `scheduled: false` without excluding `cancelled: true` reminders. This re-introduces a path for cancelled reminders to be sent.

title: deleteScheduledEmailReminder swallows errors silently affecting data integrity
body: The function wraps all branches in a single try/catch that only logs to console on failure. If the prisma update to set `cancelled: true` fails (e.g. transient DB issue), the reminder remains scheduled with no retry or alerting, meaning the workflow reminder could still fire for a cancelled/rescheduled booking undetected, since callers of this function don't check/await its result for error handling (it's called without awaiting in handleCancelBooking.ts and others).

title: deleteScheduledEmailReminder/SMS calls not awaited
body: The forEach loop calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` without awaiting the promises. Since the cancel API handler returns right after, and these calls perform async DB writes (setting `cancelled: true`), the response may complete before the cancellation flag is actually persisted, increasing the race window where the cron job's query (within the same cron tick) might miss marking it cancelled before the response is used by the client to assume cancellation succeeded fully. It also means errors are not propagated to the caller for retries/logging context tied to the specific booking cancellation flow.

title: Deleted reminders no longer deleted from DB in update handler
body: Previously, after cancelling scheduled reminders when event types are removed from a workflow, the code also deleted the WorkflowReminder DB rows (`deleteReminderPromise`/`ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany`). This deletion was removed; now only `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called, which for EMAIL just sets `cancelled: true` (not deleted) unless `immediateDelete` is passed (it is not passed here). This leaves orphaned/stale WorkflowReminder rows relying entirely on the cron job to clean them up and relies on the cron window logic working correctly; if an eventType is removed well before the one-hour cutoff, the reminder would remain unresolved for a long time and SMS reminders are deleted immediately via `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` (which does prisma.delete) causing inconsistent behavior between EMAIL and SMS method cleanups.

title: SMS reminder deleted immediately while email reminder is only soft-cancelled
body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder immediately deletes the WorkflowReminder DB row and cancels the Twilio SMS synchronously, whereas deleteScheduledEmailReminder (non-immediate) only sets `cancelled: true` and defers actual cancellation to the cron job. This asymmetry means the fix described in the PR (relying on cron-based batched cancellation to avoid hitting the SendGrid 100-pending-cancellation limit) does not apply to SMS cancellation at all, and the SMS path still directly calls the provider's cancel endpoint synchronously on every cancellation/reschedule, which could reintroduce the same kind of rate/pending-limit issue for Twilio if it exists, with no explanation on why this discrepancy exists or is safe.

title: forEach with async callback is not awaited, breaking error handling and ordering
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...}) is used inside a try/catch block. Array.prototype.forEach does not wait for async callbacks, so any error thrown inside the async callback (including from the newly-async getCalendar call) becomes an unhandled promise rejection rather than being caught by the surrounding try/catch. Additionally, the outer function can proceed (e.g. to sending emails) before calendar/video deletions actually complete, since forEach doesn't return a promise. This should use Promise.all with .map instead of forEach.

title: Same forEach(async ...) issue as vital/reschedule.ts
body: Identical to the vital reschedule.ts issue: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...}) inside try/catch does not propagate errors into the catch block and does not block execution until the async deleteEvent/deleteMeeting calls resolve, since getCalendar is now async. This can silently swallow calendar/video deletion failures and proceed to send reschedule emails before cleanup finishes.

title: forEach(async ...) means booking cancellation side effects are not awaited
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... }) is not awaited by the caller. Since getCalendar is now async, the loop fires off promises that are not tracked, so sendRequestRescheduleEmail and the webhook dispatch further down can run before the calendar/video deletions complete, and any errors from these async calls become unhandled rejections instead of being surfaced.

title: Dynamic import() at module top-level still eagerly loads every app at startup
body: The appStore object's values are the results of calling import("./appX") directly as object literal properties. These import() calls execute immediately when the appStore module is evaluated (object literals evaluate all their values eagerly), so every app package is still loaded eagerly at process startup, exactly as before, just now wrapped in Promises. This defeats the stated purpose of the PR (async/lazy imports) while adding await overhead at every call site (getCalendar, getVideoAdapters, payment app lookups, etc.) without actually deferring any loading or enabling code splitting benefits. A lazy factory, e.g. appStore[app] as a function returning import(...), would be needed to truly delay loading until first use.

title: Dynamic imports still execute eagerly at module load, defeating async/code-splitting goal
body: The appStore object stores `import("./x")` expressions directly as object values. Since `import()` calls are evaluated immediately when the object literal is constructed (i.e., as soon as this module is loaded), all app packages are still being imported eagerly at module-load time, exactly as before. Wrapping access sites in `await appStore[key]` only defers *resolution* of already-started imports, not the import itself. This means the PR's stated purpose (async/lazy-loading of app packages to reduce bundle size) is not actually achieved — it only adds async overhead (promises, awaits) throughout the codebase without any lazy-loading benefit. To truly lazy-load, the import should occur inside a function/getter invoked only when the app is actually needed.

title: Sequential awaits in for-loop serialize dynamic imports
body: getVideoAdapters now loops over credentials with a `for...of` and `await appStore[appName]` inside the loop body. Each dynamic import is awaited one at a time instead of being kicked off in parallel (e.g., via Promise.all), so for multiple credentials the imports/resolutions are serialized, adding unnecessary latency compared to the previous synchronous array reduce. This is a performance regression for calls with multiple credentials (e.g., getBusyVideoTimes with many video credentials).

title: forEach with async callback silently swallows errors and runs unawaited
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` was changed to await `getCalendar` inside the callback, but `forEach` does not wait for the returned promises nor propagate rejections to the enclosing try/catch. Any error thrown inside the async callback (e.g., from `getCalendar` or `calendar.deleteEvent`) becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of being caught by the surrounding `try/catch`, and the subsequent code (sending reschedule emails) does not wait for calendar/video deletions to complete before proceeding. This existed before but is now more clearly broken since `getCalendar` is async and genuinely needs awaiting across multiple iterations.

title: Same forEach-async unhandled-rejection issue as vital/reschedule.ts
body: Identical pattern: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` with an awaited `getCalendar` call inside. Errors are not caught by the surrounding try/catch, and the loop's async work is not awaited before the function proceeds to send emails and return, risking race conditions and silently dropped failures when deleting calendar/video references during reschedule.

title: requestReschedule forEach(async) not awaited, errors unhandled
body: In `requestReschedule`, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` now awaits `getCalendar` inside, but the surrounding code does not await the forEach's async work at all (no Promise.all), and there is no try/catch around it (unlike the vital/wipemycalother examples). This can lead to unhandled promise rejections and the reschedule email being sent before calendar/video deletions actually complete, since nothing waits for them.

title: forEach(async) inside calendar deletion loop not awaited
body: In the recurring-event cancellation branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => {...})` performs awaited `getCalendar` calls and pushes to `apiDeletes` from within an async callback that forEach does not wait on. Although `apiDeletes` is later awaited via Promise.all, the push itself happens asynchronously after forEach has already returned, so there's a window where `apiDeletes` may not yet contain all the deletion promises before the outer code proceeds to use the array (e.g., `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`), risking some deletions being missed from the final await.

title: async forEach callback breaks error handling and ordering
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...}) is wrapped in a try/catch, but forEach does not await the async callbacks. Previously (sync code) a thrown error inside the callback would propagate synchronously and be caught by the surrounding try/catch. Now that the callback is async and awaits getCalendar(), any error thrown inside becomes a rejected Promise that is never awaited, so it escapes the try/catch entirely and becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of being logged via logger.error. The function also returns before all deletions settle, so callers relying on completion (e.g. before sending reschedule emails) might run concurrently with/ahead of the pending deletions.

title: Same unhandled-rejection issue as vital/reschedule.ts
body: Identical pattern: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...}) inside a try/catch. Making the callback async while using forEach means thrown/rejected errors from getCalendar()/deleteEvent() bypass the try/catch, resulting in silent/unhandled promise rejections rather than being logged.

title: forEach with async callback not awaited for calendar/video cleanup before sending reschedule emails
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... }) is fire-and-forget: the surrounding code (sendRequestRescheduleEmail, webhook dispatch) proceeds without waiting for these calendar/video deletions to finish or to catch their failures. Converting getCalendar to async made this race more pronounced, since previously the deletion happened synchronously or near-synchronously; now it's an unawaited microtask chain and any failures are swallowed as unhandled rejections.

title: Dynamic import() calls are still evaluated eagerly, not actually lazy
body: Each `import("./app")` call in the object literal executes immediately when this module is evaluated (as soon as `appStore` is imported anywhere), regardless of whether a given app is ever used. Simply storing the resulting Promise instead of awaiting it does not defer the module loading/bundling — bundlers like webpack will still create and request each chunk at the time this file runs. This negates the stated goal of the PR (async/lazy imports of app-store packages) while adding async/await overhead to every call site that previously did synchronous property access, with no actual reduction in initial load work for consumers who only need one app.

title: getCalendarCredentials still treats getCalendar as returning a value directly used downstream without documenting it's now a Promise
body: `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` now stores a Promise<Calendar|null> in the `calendar` field of the returned structure (relying on later code awaiting `item.calendar`). This is a subtle API shape change (every consumer of getCalendarCredentials() must know to await `.calendar`) that is not documented via types/comments, making it easy for a future caller to accidentally treat it as a resolved Calendar object.

title: Nested async forEach for recurring-event calendar deletions remains unawaited
body: `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` pushes into apiDeletes asynchronously inside a forEach that isn't awaited by the enclosing code before `apiDeletes` is used in `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`. If the outer `if (bookingCalendarReference)` block finishes and the function moves on before these async pushes complete, some deletions could be missed from apiDeletes, resulting in orphaned calendar events in that recurring-event + allRemainingBookings branch.

title: workingHours check compares start==end, always false condition
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates the computation of `start` instead of using slotEndTime. This makes the working-hours boundary check (`end > workingHour.endTime`) effectively check the slot start time twice instead of validating the slot's end time against working hours, so slots that end after working hours but start within them will incorrectly be considered available.

title: Dayjs object comparison with === never true
body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two different Dayjs object instances with strict equality, which is always false since Dayjs objects are not primitives. This dead code branch (meant to detect override start===end, i.e. an all-day-unavailable override) never triggers, so overrides representing a fully blocked day won't be handled as intended.

title: Override's own date may shift when offset computed relative to invitee tz with DST mismatch
body: The override startTime/endTime are computed as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset,'minute')` where offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset. However `organizerUtcOffset` is derived from `override.start` parsed with `dayjs(override.start.toString())` rather than from the already-known override.timeZone-based organizer time directly; if `override.start` lacks timezone info (just a date string), `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` may misinterpret the local wall time, causing an incorrect offset and shifted slot times for overrides near DST transitions.

title: No test coverage for round-robin + date override interaction
body: The PR's primary claimed fix is that fixed-host date overrides are respected in round-robin events, but no test in this file exercises a round-robin event type combined with a date override for a fixed host. Only the plain date-override timezone case and existing round-robin busy-time tests are covered, leaving the main bug fix for issue #8207 unverified by tests.

title: Dead-code comparison on dayjs objects with ===
body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two newly created dayjs object references with `===`, which will always be false since dayjs() returns new objects. The intended check for a zero-length override (start === end) never triggers, so this branch is unreachable dead code.

title: Working-hours bound check uses start time for both start and end
body: In the fallback check for whether a slot is within normal working hours: `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(); const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime`, ignoring the slot's actual end time (which should use `slotEndTime`). This makes the `end > workingHour.endTime` check meaningless (since start==end), so slots that end after working hours (e.g. due to eventLength) will incorrectly be considered within bounds, causing availability to be computed incorrectly for slots overlapping the end of working hours.

title: organizerTimeZone omitted from dateOverrides path for currentSeats busy check
body: The last `checkIfIsAvailable` call (used when checking selectedSlots/currentSeats-based busy times) does pass `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone` but does not pass `dateOverrides` or `workingHours`, unlike other call sites. Since `checkIfIsAvailable` defaults these to `[]`, this invocation will skip the date-override/working-hours logic entirely for this code path, meaning date overrides for a specific user are not respected here, potentially allowing booking of a slot that is actually blocked (or vice versa) when selected/seat slots are involved.

title: override.timeZone may be undefined causing wrong offset
body: `override.timeZone` is typed optional (`TimeRange.timeZone?: string`), but `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` is called without a fallback. If `timeZone` is undefined for an override (e.g. constructed elsewhere without setting it), `dayjs().tz(undefined)` behavior is implementation-dependent and could silently produce an incorrect offset, defeating the timezone-adjustment fix this PR intends to add.

title: New timezone test does not actually exercise different invitee timezone behavior meaningfully
body: The new test asserts that querying with timezone +6:00 yields the exact same UTC slot list as +5:30, which trivially passes since results are always converted to UTC Z notation and compared by UTC string regardless of input tz; it doesn't verify that slots shift according to the override's organizer timezone when the invitee timezone differs from organizer's, so the actual bug (date overrides not adjusting per attendee timezone) is only weakly covered.

title: Dayjs objects compared via === always evaluate to false
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset,'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset,'minutes')` compares two distinct Dayjs object instances by reference, so it is always false regardless of whether start and end actually represent the same instant. This branch intended to detect zero-length overrides never triggers, so that special case is not handled as intended.

title: workingHour end computed from start time (copy-paste bug)
body: In the new working-hours check inside checkIfIsAvailable, both `start` and `end` are computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` — `end` should instead be based on `slotEndTime`. As written, `end` always equals `start`, so the `end > workingHour.endTime` check can never correctly flag a slot that starts within working hours but ends after them, causing slots that extend past working hours to incorrectly be treated as available.

title: DST/offset adjustment uses override.start for both organizer and invitee offsets, applied uniformly to start and end
body: The same `offset` (computed solely from `override.start`) is applied to both `override.start` and `override.end`. If the override spans a DST transition boundary in either the organizer's or invitee's timezone, using a single offset for both the start and end instants can produce incorrect start/end minutes, silently shifting or shrinking the override window by an hour in those edge cases. This is a narrow edge case but was not covered by any test (only non-DST-transition dates are exercised in the added test).

title: New timezone test doesn't actually test a different organizer/invitee offset scenario thoroughly
body: The new 'different timezone' test only changes the invitee timeZone between two zones that are both ahead of UTC (+5:30 and +6:00) and expects identical UTC output, which only confirms the override is stored/read in UTC-correct form; it does not cover timezones on opposite sides of UTC (e.g., negative offset) or a case where the organizer's and invitee's day boundaries diverge, which is exactly the scenario this PR claims to fix (slots not adjusting across different timezones for overrides near day boundaries).

title: Migration raw SQL interpolation vulnerable to SQL injection and crashes on special characters
body: The migration inserts site_settings values for embeddable_hosts via string interpolation into raw SQL (`execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`). If a host string contains a single quote or other SQL metacharacters, this will break the migration or allow SQL injection. Existing data from the deprecated `embeddable_hosts` site setting is untrusted/arbitrary and should be inserted using parameterized values (e.g. via ActiveRecord model creation or quoted values) instead of raw interpolation.

title: category_id lookup query is fragile/broken
body: The query `SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'` joins on an exact string match between category name and the embed_category setting value, which can easily fail to match (whitespace, case, slug vs name mismatches) and silently falls back to uncategorized without any error/log. This could silently assign the wrong category when migrating existing installations, losing user configuration state. No test covers this migration behavior.

title: Host validation regex requires TLD of 2-5 chars, rejecting valid hosts like localhost or newer TLDs
body: The regex `\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z` requires a dot and a 2-5 letter TLD. This rejects valid use cases such as `localhost`, single-label hostnames, or longer TLDs (e.g. `.technology`, `.photography`), which is a regression from the previous embeddable_hosts setting which did not enforce a strict host validation. This could block valid admin configurations without clear explanation (dev/testing with localhost is explicitly supported elsewhere in embed_controller.rb).

title: update/destroy do not handle missing records
body: In `update` and `destroy`, `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil if the id doesn't exist (e.g., already deleted by another admin). `save_host(nil)` would raise a NoMethodError on `host.host =`, and `destroy` would raise NoMethodError on `host.destroy`, resulting in an unhandled 500 error instead of a clean 404/error response.

title: basePath type.replace only replaces first underscore occurrence
body: `type.replace('_', '-')` (without a global regex flag) only replaces the first underscore in the type string. If a model type name contains multiple underscores, matching against ADMIN_MODELS (which uses hyphens) will fail for all but the first underscore, potentially misrouting those types to the non-admin basePath.

title: No negative/missing-host test for TopicEmbed category assignment
body: The import spec only verifies that the post's category equals the embeddable_host's category when a matching host exists. There's no test verifying behavior when `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` returns nil (e.g., falls back to default/uncategorized category), which is a meaningful behavior change introduced by this PR (previously used SiteSetting.embed_category directly).

title: before_validation callback can crash on nil host
body: `self.host.sub!(...)` will raise NoMethodError if `host` is nil (e.g. creating a record without host param). The controller sets host from params but doesn't guard against missing/blank input before calling save, so a malformed request to the admin controller could 500 instead of returning a validation error.

title: No existence check for update/destroy
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil if the id doesn't exist, and `save_host(nil)` or `host.destroy` will then raise NoMethodError on nil, producing a 500 instead of a 404/error response.

title: Host regex rejects hosts with port but description allows paths/ports loosely
body: The validation regex requires a TLD segment of 2-5 chars, which will reject valid TLDs longer than 5 characters (e.g. .london, .company) and some edge-case valid hostnames, limiting legitimate host entries without an easy way to override.

title: SQL injection risk in migration via string interpolation
body: The migration builds raw SQL using string interpolation of untrusted site_setting values (`h`) without escaping/quoting: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. If an existing embeddable_hosts setting value contains a single quote or malicious SQL, this could break the migration or allow SQL injection during upgrade.

title: Dropped explicit 'embeddable hosts not set' check changes behavior silently
body: Previously there was an explicit error for blank embeddable_hosts setting; now that check is removed and only `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` is used. If no EmbeddableHost records exist, `host_allowed?` will simply return false, giving the same generic 'invalid referer host' error for both 'not configured' and 'wrong host' cases, which is less informative for admins debugging configuration issues.

title: Fragile string replace for underscore model names
body: `type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore occurrence, not all occurrences (no global flag). If a model type name contains multiple underscores, this basePath check would fail to properly normalize the type and could incorrectly treat it as a non-admin model or vice versa.

title: Host validation regex rejects localhost/single-label hosts used in dev
body: The regex `\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z` requires at least one dot, so hosts like `localhost` or single-word internal hostnames cannot be saved as embeddable hosts. This could block legitimate dev/staging use cases that the old free-text site setting allowed.

title: before_validation mutates host destructively using sub! without nil guard
body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called without checking if `host` is nil. If `host` is nil (e.g., a bad request or if `category_id` validation runs before `host` presence is set), this raises a NoMethodError instead of producing a clean validation error. There's no `validates_presence_of :host` either, so an empty/nil host could raise an unhandled exception in `EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` rather than a user-facing validation error.

title: Migration does not sanitize host values before SQL interpolation
body: The migration inserts `h` (read from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting) directly into a SQL string without escaping: `"INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. If an admin previously stored a host value containing a single quote or other SQL-significant characters, this migration will fail or behave unexpectedly. Should use `quote` or parameterized execution.

title: No nil-check before setting attributes on host potentially nil from DB lookup
body: In `update`, `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil if the id doesn't exist, and `save_host` then calls `host.host = ...` on nil, raising a NoMethodError (500) instead of a clean 404/error response.

title: Pluralized hydration key collision risk
body: The new `_hydrateEmbedded` code for pluralized keys (`m[2]` truthy, e.g. `color_ids`) always writes to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]`, overwriting any pre-existing property with that pluralized name without checking if it already exists, differing from the singular case which only assigns `obj[subType]` if `hydrated` is truthy. This asymmetry could silently overwrite existing data with an empty array if `obj[k]` is empty/falsy, and no test covers that an existing colors array isn't improperly overwritten.

title: Removed site setting descriptions without migration note / leftover orphan descriptions
body: The description for `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings were removed, matching removal of the settings themselves, but there is no check that other locale files (if any) or documentation referencing these settings were also updated, risking stale references elsewhere in the codebase.

title: Duplicate method definition `downsize` silently overrides original signature
body: Two `self.downsize` methods are defined (lines 145 and 149), the second overriding the first. Any caller using the old 4-arg signature `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` (e.g. existing callers elsewhere in the codebase) will now get wrong behavior since `max_height` is silently dropped and `opts` is misassigned, or will raise ArgumentError due to mismatched arity. This is a backward-incompatible API break hidden behind a redefinition rather than an explicit rename/removal.

title: Downsize loop ignores failure and risks corrupting original upload file
body: The while loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` in-place up to 5 times without checking the boolean return value of `downsize`/`convert_with`. If the conversion fails (returns false), the loop still decrements `attempt` and continues, and `tempfile.size` is reread assuming the file was modified; on failure the original tempfile could be left in a bad/truncated state (since `to` == `from`, a failed convert may truncate the destination file) and the subsequent `Upload.create_for` would ingest a corrupted file without any error being surfaced to the user.

title: download size cap decoupled from max_image_size_kb, now hardcoded then downsized after full download
body: Previously `FileHelper.download` capped the download at `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`; now it's hardcoded to `10.megabytes`. For non-image attachments this silently increases the max download size regardless of site configuration, and for images the full (now up to 10MB) file is downloaded before any downsizing attempt, increasing bandwidth/memory usage compared to before even though the final image size enforcement still happens via the new downsize loop. This changes documented/configured size limit behavior without being mentioned in the PR description.

title: Hardcoded max upload size removes site-setting-based validation
body: `maxSizeKB` is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (and similarly `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` at line 246). This breaks the ability for admins to configure max upload size per type via site settings; client-side validation will always allow uploads up to 10MB regardless of the actual configured `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb`, which could mismatch the server-side limits and confuse users with incorrect error messages or allow oversized uploads to be attempted unnecessarily.

title: Duplicate method definition `downsize` silently overrides first
body: Two `def self.downsize` methods are defined with different signatures (one taking max_width, max_height, the other taking dimensions). Ruby allows redefinition, so the second definition (`downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`) silently overwrites the first. Any existing caller using `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` (two numeric args) will now break because the new method only accepts a single `dimensions` string argument, causing an ArgumentError or wrong behavior at runtime.

title: Repeated downsizing can degrade image quality without guarantee of success
body: The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` up to 5 times, each time overwriting the file with a lossy re-encode of the previous resize output. This compounds quality loss unnecessarily, and if `max_image_size_kb` is set very low or the image can't be reduced further (e.g. already minimal size), the loop just exhausts attempts without any error reporting to the user — the oversized file is still uploaded afterward silently exceeding the configured limit.

title: Download size limit changed from configurable setting to hardcoded value
body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the previous `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` limit with a hardcoded 10MB. This decouples the enforced download size cap from the site's configured max_image_size_kb setting, meaning admins can no longer control the API download size limit via settings.

title: File size validation hardcoded instead of using site setting
body: `maxSizeKB` is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. This breaks the configurability of max upload size per type (image vs attachment) and is inconsistent with the backend which still uses `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, causing client-side validation to diverge from server-side limits.

title: Error message hardcodes max size instead of using site setting
body: `maxSizeKB` in the 413 error handler is hardcoded to `10 * 1024` rather than `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`, so the error message shown to users may not reflect the actual configured limit.

title: Duplicate method definition of self.downsize silently overrides the first
body: Two `def self.downsize` methods are defined with different signatures (one taking max_width/max_height, one taking dimensions string). Ruby allows this but the second definition completely overrides the first, meaning the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` signature is dead code and any caller using that 4-arg form will get a wrong number of arguments error or silently broken behavior. This is likely unintentional leftover code that should be removed.

title: Hardcoded 10MB download limit ignores SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb
body: The download size limit was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. Since the PR introduces automatic downsizing specifically to allow larger uploads beyond max_image_size_kb, this works for the resize feature, but it silently changes behavior for admins who configured a smaller or larger value for max_image_size_kb-based downloads unrelated to the resize retry loop, and removes configurability. If this is intentional it should be documented, but currently it's an undocumented behavior change with no corresponding site setting.

title: Downsize loop can silently fail or infinite small-step reduce without catching errors
body: The resize loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to 5 times reducing to 80% each time, but if `OptimizedImage.downsize` fails (returns false, e.g. ImageMagick error) the loop doesn't check the return value, it just decrements attempt and tries again overwriting the same file. If the tool fails on the first iteration, the tempfile could become corrupted or zero-byte, and the code would still proceed to use it in `Upload.create_for`, with `content_type` possibly stale/mismatched to the now-corrupted file, producing invalid or broken uploads without any error being surfaced to the user.

title: Hardcoded max upload size removes site-setting-driven configurability
body: Both `validateUploadedFile` and `displayErrorForUpload` previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` / `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to determine file size limits, but now hardcode 10MB. This breaks the API/contract for admins who have configured different max_image_size_kb or max_attachment_size_kb values — client-side validation will now be inconsistent with server-side settings, giving users misleading error messages (e.g., showing 10MB limit when server actually allows uploads up to a different size via the new downsizing feature, or rejects differently).

title: mailing_list_notify bypasses unsubscribe link
body: mailing_list_notify calls send_notification_email without going through notification_email, and send_notification_email now unconditionally sets unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url; this is fine, but notification emails for notification_type outside replied/mentioned/quoted/posted (e.g. invited) still get add_unsubscribe_link true even though per-topic unsubscribe semantics (mute/regular) may not make sense for PM invites, since unsubscribe_url always points to topic unsubscribe regardless of context.

title: unsubscribe action lacks guardian/nil checks
body: The unsubscribe action does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` and then calls `tu.notification_level` without checking if tu is nil (e.g., user never visited topic) or whether current_user is present (if not logged in, current_user.id raises NoMethodError). This will raise a 500 error for logged-out users or users with no existing TopicUser record, rather than gracefully handling the unsubscribe request.

title: unsubscribe not permission-checked
body: Unlike other actions (e.g., status, autoclose) that call guardian.ensure_can_X!, unsubscribe never verifies guardian.ensure_can_see!(topic) before mutating the TopicUser record for current_user. Although it only mutates current_user's own record, there's no check that the topic is visible to them, allowing probing of private/restricted topics' existence via this unauthenticated-looking endpoint.

title: Duplicate respond_instructions placeholder
body: `%{respond_instructions}` appears twice (lines 6 and 19) but message_builder's html_part only replaces the first occurrence it finds via gsub! on the whole string — actually gsub! replaces all occurrences, but respond_instructions is only computed once from template_args, so both placeholders get the same text, which may be redundant/confusing for recipients since the same instructions appear twice in rendered email with no content between except the previous discussion section somtimes missing causing duplicate instruction text directly adjacent.

title: unsubscribe_url interpolation may be undefined for non-topic emails
body: The unsubscribe_link translation now references %{unsubscribe_url}, but this key is only populated for topic-related notification emails (send_notification_email). Other emails using add_unsubscribe_link (e.g., digest emails via @unsubscribe_key) do not set unsubscribe_url in template_args, so I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) would raise a MissingInterpolationArgument error or render a broken link for those templates.

title: unsubscribe action lacks authentication/authorization guard
body: The `unsubscribe` action calls `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)` without checking that `current_user` is present (there's no `ensure_logged_in` filter applied for anonymous email-link visits since this route is meant to be visited from an email link, often without session). If `current_user` is nil, `current_user.id` raises NoMethodError. Also no `guardian.ensure_can_see!` check is performed on the topic before mutating notification state, and `tu` may be nil if no TopicUser record exists yet (e.g., user never visited the topic), causing `tu.notification_level` to raise NoMethodError on nil.

title: TopicUser record may not exist, causing crash
body: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic (e.g. has never visited/posted). The subsequent `tu.notification_level` call will raise a NoMethodError instead of gracefully creating/updating via `TopicUser.change`, which is the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g., `set_notifications` action uses `TopicUser.change`).

title: mailing_list_notify omits unsubscribe_url
body: `send_notification_email` now relies on `post.topic.unsubscribe_url` being referenced via `email_opts[:unsubscribe_url]`, which is fine since it's inside `send_notification_email`. However, the `add_unsubscribe_link: true` passed from `mailing_list_notify` and other callers always triggers template substitution of `%{unsubscribe_url}` in `unsubscribe_link` locale string; if `unsubscribe_url` isn't present in template_args (e.g., for `digest` mailer, which still sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but does NOT set `unsubscribe_url`), the `%{unsubscribe_url}` placeholder in the i18n string will be left unresolved or raise a missing interpolation argument error, since `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` requires the key but `digest` mailer never supplies `unsubscribe_url`.

title: unsubscribe_link requires unsubscribe_url interpolation but not all callers supply it
body: The `unsubscribe_link` translation now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but it's used by `digest` (via `build_email`) and other mailers that set `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without passing `unsubscribe_url` in opts/template_args. This will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` for those emails (e.g., digest emails), breaking all digest email delivery.

title: render :show explicitly added but may conflict with implicit render for unsubscribe action
body: `perform_show_response`'s html format block now explicitly calls `render :show`, but this method is shared by `unsubscribe` action, which presumably wants its own `show` template context (fine) but no distinct unsubscribe view/template was added for non-JS (non-Ember) rendering; the front-end relies on a new `topic/unsubscribe` Ember route/template, but the server-rendered `show.html.erb` for GET requests to `/t/.../unsubscribe` will render as if it were a normal topic page, not an unsubscribe-specific page, potentially confusing users who load the link without JS enabled.

title: unsubscribe action does not check current_user presence
body: The `unsubscribe` action calls `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)` without checking that `current_user` is present. While `ensure_logged_in` before_filter is applied, the find_by can return nil if a TopicUser record doesn't exist yet (e.g. a user who has never visited the topic), causing a NoMethodError on `tu.notification_level` for nil. This will 500 for users unsubscribing from topics they haven't interacted with before (no existing topic_user row), which is a plausible scenario when clicking an unsubscribe link in a digest/mailing email.

title: unsubscribe action lacks ownership verification of topic_user record
body: The code fetches `TopicUser` by `user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]` which is fine for ownership, but there's no `guardian.ensure_can_see!` check as in `show`. A logged-in user could unsubscribe from a topic they otherwise could not see (information disclosure via side channel is minor, but behavior is inconsistent with `show`'s access control).

title: Duplicate respond_instructions placeholder emitted twice
body: The template outputs `%{respond_instructions}` twice (once inside the context_posts block at line 6, and unconditionally again at line 19). Since `html_part` in message_builder.rb does a global `gsub!` for `%{respond_instructions}`, both placeholders get replaced with the same text, resulting in duplicated response instructions in the rendered email when context_posts are present. This existed before but combined with the new unsubscribe_url change, it's worth flagging since the diff touches this file extensively without fixing the duplication issue.

title: unsubscribe_url not guaranteed present in template_args when rendering unsubscribe_link i18n string
body: The new `unsubscribe_link` i18n string references `%{unsubscribe_url}` (per server.en.yml diff), but `MessageBuilder#html_part`/`#body` call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` unconditionally when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true. If `unsubscribe_url` is not passed in `@opts` (e.g. digest emails, which still just use `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url`), I18n translation will raise a missing interpolation argument error, since digest doesn't set `unsubscribe_url`. This breaks the digest email flow since `digest` method in user_notifications.rb was not updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`.

title: Non-atomic match_count increment causes race condition
body: should_block? reads the record, increments match_count in Ruby, then saves. Under concurrent requests for the same blocked email (e.g. a spam signup burst), multiple processes/threads can read the same match_count value before any save completes, causing lost updates. Should use an atomic SQL update (e.g. update_all with `match_count = match_count + 1`) instead.

title: should_block? mutates state on every validation call, including failed saves/dry runs
body: should_block? is called from EmailValidator.validate_each, which can run multiple times per request (e.g. valid? called twice as in UsersController#create: `user.valid? && SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` then save). This causes match_count to be incremented more than once per actual signup attempt, inflating statistics inaccurately.

title: Exposing full error hash and raw submitted values in JSON response
body: The create action now returns `errors: user.errors.to_hash` and `values: user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")` to the client. This leaks server-side validation error structure and echoes back submitted values (including email) in all failure cases, which was not previously exposed. While used by the JS to populate rejectedEmails, this changes the API contract and could leak more information than intended (e.g. internal error keys for other attributes beyond email).

title: Email validator order allows email_domains validation to run even when blocked
body: The new EmailValidator (lib/validators/email_validator.rb) always evaluates email_domains_whitelist/blacklist and only checks BlockedEmail.should_block? when no prior error exists, meaning should_block? (and its side-effecting match_count update) is skipped if the domain whitelist/blacklist already rejects the email. This means blocked-email statistics won't be collected for already-blacklisted domains, which may be surprising/inconsistent with the intent of tracking all block attempts.

title: Missing newline at end of file
body: The file lacks a trailing newline, which is a minor style/lint issue but can cause warnings in some Ruby tooling/CI configured to enforce file-ending newlines.

title: rejectedEmails is a shared singleton array across controller instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([]),` is defined as a literal array on the prototype/mixin level. In Ember/Discourse's object model, if CreateAccountController is reused as a shared instance (typical for Ember controllers), this is fine, but if multiple instances are created this literal array will be shared across all instances since it's evaluated once at class definition. This can cause rejected emails from one modal session to leak into another, so emails rejected in a previous attempt may incorrectly block valid emails in a new session unless the controller object is a true singleton that gets reset elsewhere.

title: should_block? has race condition / non-atomic increment
body: self.should_block? reads a record, increments match_count in Ruby, then saves. Under concurrent signups with the same blocked email, this read-modify-write is not atomic and can lose updates (lost increments). Should use update_counters or an atomic SQL UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1.

title: BlockedEmail.should_block? called on every validation and mutates state as a side effect
body: should_block? is invoked from validate_each, which can run multiple times per request (e.g. once for user.valid? check in UsersController#create and again on user.save). This causes match_count to be incremented and last_match_at updated multiple times for a single signup attempt, inflating statistics and causing extra DB writes during validation, which is also a surprising side effect for a validator to perform directly against the DB on every validation pass.

title: Exposing full errors hash and attribute values to client without filtering
body: The create action now exposes user.errors.to_hash and user.attributes.slice(name, username, email) in the JSON response. While email/username/name are already visible to the user, returning the full errors hash changes the API contract for any consumer and could leak more validation detail than before (e.g. internal error keys) without the previous explicit review of what's exposed.

title: rejectedEmails never cleared, causing valid emails to be permanently rejected within the modal session
body: Once an email is pushed into rejectedEmails (e.g., due to being blocked), it stays rejected forever within that modal session even if the underlying blocked status changes or the user corrects something else.
