There's no mechanism to clear previously rejected but now-fixed emails, and because rejectedEmails is a prototype-level array (Em.A([]) at the class level), it may also be inadvertently shared across controller instances if not properly reset per instantiation, leading to stale rejection state across signups in the same page session.

title: Race condition in match_count increment
body: should_block? reads the record then increments match_count and saves without locking or atomic update. Under concurrent requests for the same blocked email, increments can be lost due to read-modify-write races (two requests load the same match_count, both increment and save, one update is overwritten). Should use update_all/increment! with SQL-level atomicity.

title: BlockedEmail check only runs when email changes, but every create changes email
body: This is mostly fine for new users, but on existing user update() flows where email doesn't change, the email: true validator (and BlockedEmail.should_block?) won't run — that's expected. However the bigger issue is validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed? combined with EmailValidator calling BlockedEmail.should_block?(value) means every save that changes email (e.g. change_email flow in users_controller) will increment match_count/last_match_at on the BlockedEmail table even for validation-only checks that may be re-run multiple times per request (e.g. due to uniqueness validation combined with email validation both triggering saves on the user, or multiple validate! calls), causing inflated match_count statistics not reflecting actual distinct block attempts.

title: should_block? mutates state as a side effect of a query-named method
body: should_block? looks like a predicate/query method but has side effects (increments match_count, updates last_match_at, saves to DB) on every call. This violates the principle of least surprise: validations or other code paths calling should_block? multiple times (e.g. validated twice during a single form submission, or re-validated via valid? before save in users_controller#create) will record multiple matches for a single actual attempt, corrupting match statistics. Also no error handling if save fails silently (return value of save ignored).

title: Full error hash and submitted attribute values exposed to client on failed signup
body: The create action now returns errors: user.errors.to_hash and values: user.attributes.slice("name","username","email") in the JSON response. While limited to name/username/email, returning raw error hashes could leak additional validation messages (e.g., any new validator added later) not intended for display, and echoes back the submitted email, which combined with the blocked email check could allow an attacker to probe which emails are in the blocked list by observing error type (not_allowed vs blocked) in response text — enumerating blocklist membership.

title: Missing trailing newline / file-level validator not covering nil values
body: value could be nil if email is nil; email_in_restriction_setting? and BlockedEmail.should_block? call regexp/match on nil, which could raise NoMethodError for a blank email during validation, instead of simply skipping (presence validator should catch this, but order of validators execution isn't guaranteed, so a nil email could raise an unhandled error here).

title: Referer-based host check is spoofable and uses blank URI check incorrectly
body: `ensure_embeddable` relies solely on `request.referer` to validate the embedding host, comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. The HTTP Referer header is client-controlled and can be spoofed or omitted by proxies/browsers, so this is a weak access control mechanism for an endpoint that creates topics indirectly via jobs. There is no additional check (e.g. a signed token, Origin header validation with stricter rules, or CORS) protecting this. Also, when `embed_url` differs in scheme/case from `embeddable_host`, no normalization occurs, which could lead to false negatives/positives.

title: import silently mutates and discards invalid url contents, with inconsistent return and side effects
body: `self.import` mutates the caller-supplied `contents` string in place via `contents << "..."` before checking url validity is already done above via early return, but note the mutation happens only after the regex check passes. More importantly, if `url` doesn't match the regex, the method returns `nil` without any error indication, silently swallowing bad data from feeds (e.g., in `poll_feed.rb` loop, a bad `url` for one item just skips that topic with no logging), making debugging feed import issues difficult.

title: Unrescued exceptions in per-item processing abort the whole feed poll
body: Inside `poll_feed`, `rss.items.each` calls `TopicEmbed.import` for every item without any per-item rescue. Since `sidekiq_options retry: false` is set, if any single feed item causes an exception (e.g., malformed content causing a Nokogiri parse error, or absolutize_urls raising on an invalid url), the entire job aborts, and no retry occurs, leaving all remaining feed items for that run unprocessed and silently dropped until the next hourly poll's items happen to still be present in the feed.

title: feed_key method is defined but never used
body: `feed_key` builds a redis key intended presumably to track feed modification/caching (likely meant to avoid refetching unchanged feeds), but it is never referenced anywhere in `poll_feed` or elsewhere in the codebase. This indicates incomplete work: the feed is always fully re-fetched and all items reprocessed every hour, which is wasteful and was presumably meant to be optimized by this key but isn't.

title: No feedback given to user if embed_url is same-origin spam risk / repeated hits enqueue duplicate jobs
body: Every request with no matching topic_id enqueues a `:retrieve_topic` job regardless of how recently the same `embed_url` was requested from this controller action (throttling is only applied inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, which is bypassed for staff and only limited to 60 seconds otherwise). Since the controller returns the 'loading' view which polls every 30 seconds and reloads, multiple concurrent viewers of the same not-yet-imported embed URL will each enqueue a new `RetrieveTopic` job on every reload within the throttle window boundary, potentially causing bursts of duplicate job enqueues under load before the redis throttle key is set the first time (race condition between concurrent requests both checking `retrieved_recently?` before either sets the key).

title: SSRF-adjacent host validation using referer header is unreliable
body: The ensure_embeddable check compares request.referer host against SiteSetting.embeddable_host, but relies entirely on the Referer header which is attacker-controllable (can be omitted or spoofed by many clients) and doesn't validate the embed_url param itself against embeddable_host. An attacker could craft requests without a Referer or spoof it, then supply any embed_url to trigger retrieval of arbitrary external URLs via the retrieve_topic job (TopicRetriever eventually checks embed_url host too, but only after enqueuing the job, consuming resources and running an HTTP fetch of attacker-chosen URLs limited by one host check in topic_retriever). This is weak defense-in-depth and should also validate embed_url's host explicitly in the controller.

title: Open redirect / SSRF via import_remote fetching arbitrary URLs
body: fetch_http calls TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url) which does `open(url).read` (open-uri). Although invalid_host? restricts @embed_url's host to embeddable_host, open-uri can still follow redirects to internal addresses (SSRF) since Ruby's open-uri by default does not restrict redirect targets. This can be used to probe internal network resources if embeddable_host's server redirects to internal IPs. No protection against redirects to non-http(s) schemes or internal addresses is implemented.

title: No validation of PostCreator result before use in revisor path
body: In TopicEmbed.import, when embed already exists, post = embed.post. If embed.post has been deleted/trashed independently (post_id orphaned), the subsequent revisor.revise!(user, ...) will raise against nil, with no guard. This should check post presence before attempting revision.

title: skip_validations changes save behavior silently for existing revise! callers
body: update_post now calls `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` instead of plain `@post.save`. This changes behavior for all existing callers of PostRevisor#revise! that don't pass skip_validations (defaults to validating, same as before), but any caller relying on validate: true default behavior combined with other opts could be affected if skip_validations is inadvertently truthy from merged opts hashes elsewhere. Worth confirming no other code paths pass skip_validations unintentionally given it's a now-functional flag change.

title: Potential nil content causes crash when RSS content missing
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes i.content is always present; if an RSS/Atom item lacks a content/description field, i.content will be nil and `.scrub` raises NoMethodError, crashing the whole feed polling for all items (no per-item rescue), potentially breaking poll_feed job for the entire batch due to one malformed item.

title: Referer-based host check is spoofable and breaks when referer is absent (e.g. HTTPS->HTTP, privacy extensions)
body: ensure_embeddable relies entirely on request.referer to validate the embedding host. The Referer header is client-controlled and often stripped by browsers/proxies for privacy reasons, so legitimate embeds can be blocked (DoS on themselves) while an attacker that can control/spoof the Referer header (e.g. via a crafted request from a page that sets referrer policy, or environments where referer leaks) could pass this check. A more robust mechanism (e.g. signed state, or Origin header combined with Referer, with graceful fallback) should be used instead of trusting Referer alone for access control.

title: import silently returns nil on invalid URL without raising/logging
body: self.import returns unless url matches http(s) scheme, silently discarding content/title and not informing callers (PollFeed, disqus.thor) that an item was skipped. In PollFeed#poll_feed, rss.items.each calls TopicEmbed.import without checking the return value, so malformed feed URLs are silently dropped with no logging, making debugging feed import failures hard.

title: mutates shared content string before computing checksum, and unescapes untrusted HTML without sanitization
body: TopicEmbed.import mutates its `contents` argument in place via `contents << ...` to append the import footer (topic_embed.rb line 13), and poll_feed passes `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` built fresh each iteration, so this isn't a major issue here, but combined with `absolutize_urls`, raw remote HTML content from an RSS feed is directly rendered with cook_method raw_html and never sanitized (no `sanitize` gem usage), meaning any HTML/JS in the feed content is stored and rendered as-is in the post. This creates a stored-XSS-like risk since posts imported this way bypass the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline entirely (Post#cook returns raw for cook_method raw_html).

title: Raw HTML cook_method bypasses all sanitization for embedded/imported content
body: Post#cook returns `raw` unmodified when cook_method is raw_html, skipping PrettyText/Plugin::Filter sanitization entirely. Since this path is used for RSS-imported and readability-imported content (see TopicEmbed.import / import_remote), any malicious markup in third-party feeds or scraped pages will be stored and served as-is to viewers, enabling XSS through the embed feature if the imported site/feed is compromised or malicious.

title: No rate limiting/validation on embed_url triggering background job for arbitrary URLs
body: The `best` action enqueues a RetrieveTopic job for any embed_url supplied by the client as long as referer host matches embeddable_host, but the embed_url itself can be any value (TopicRetriever later checks host, but only after the job runs). This means arbitrary users can trigger outbound HTTP fetches (potential SSRF-ish behavior / resource exhaustion) merely by hitting this endpoint many times with different query strings, since the per-URL throttle key is only enforced inside TopicRetriever and not before enqueueing the job each time `best` is hit for a brand new distinct URL.

title: Removed .title float causes layout regression
body: The `.title { float: left; }` rule inside `.contents` was deleted and not replaced by any flex-related ordering/positioning for `.title`. Since `.panel` now uses `@include order(3)` and `margin-left: auto` within a flex container, but `.title` and other direct children have no explicit `order`, the relative ordering/layout of title vs panel/icons is unspecified and likely breaks the previous visual layout (title no longer floats, and no flex item properties are set for it).

title: Removed bullet margin-top regression
body: The `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule was removed from `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper` without replacement. This was presumably compensating for vertical alignment of the bullet badge; removing it may cause misalignment in the topic header area, especially since `.extra-info-wrapper` is now also assigned `@include order(2)` implying it participates in a flex layout where vertical centering may differ from before.

title: .small-action-desc padding/margin changes not justified by flexbox need
body: `.small-action-desc` padding was changed from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`, `margin-top: 5px` was dropped, and `> p { padding-top: 4px; }` was removed. These are unrelated to the stated purpose of 'optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins' and change visual spacing in small-action messages (used for topic status changes), likely causing a regression in that area with no clear flex-related reasoning tying these changes together, and no test or visual verification is referenced.

title: Switching plain CSS flex properties to vendor-prefixed mixins has no functional benefit here
body: `display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline;` were replaced with `@include inline-flex(); @include align-items(baseline);`, adding vendor prefixes for very old browsers (e.g., `-moz-inline-box`, `-ms-inline-flexbox`) that are no longer relevant for modern browser support. This increases CSS output size without any stated benefit, and conflicts with the PR's framing as a 'performance optimization' since it actually increases the compiled CSS payload.

title: Removed .title float causes header layout to break
body: The `.contents .title { float: left; }` rule was removed but `.contents` is now a flex container without any explicit order/flex properties on `.title`. Combined with `.panel` now using `margin-left: auto` and `@include order(3)`, the title element's layout behavior inside the flex container is undefined/relies on default flex item behavior, which may not preserve the previous left-aligned layout, especially since other children like `.icons`, `.login-button` still use `float: left`/`float: right` which have no effect inside flex containers. This can break header alignment across themes.

title: Floats mixed with flexbox parent are ineffective
body: .icons, .login-button, button.sign-up-button still use float: left/float: right as children of .contents, which is now display:flex. Float has no effect on flex items, so their positioning logic effectively changes silently, potentially causing visual regressions that aren't covered by any test or visual review in this PR.

title: .small-action children still use float with flex parent
body: .small-action is now a flex container (@include flexbox()), but .topic-avatar and the button inside still use float: left/float: right, which are ignored for flex items. This silently changes the layout from what was presumably tested before, and there's no mention of adjusting these children to use order or flex properties instead.

title: extra-info-wrapper uses order() without being a flex item of a confirmed flex container
body: `.extra-info-wrapper` now includes `@include order(2)`, but order only takes effect if its parent is a flex/inline-flex container. There's no diff indicating the parent (#topic-title or similar) is a flex container, so this new order declaration may be a no-op, suggesting incomplete understanding of the flex hierarchy and potentially masking a real layout bug it was meant to fix.

title: Removed bullet margin-top may affect vertical alignment
body: The removal of `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` from `.title-wrapper` changes existing vertical alignment of bullet badges without an equivalent replacement, which could introduce a visual regression for category bullet badges in topic titles.

title: Removed `.title { float: left; }` rule without replacement
body: The `.title` selector inside `.contents` that previously set `float: left;` was deleted entirely as part of converting `.contents` to flexbox, but no equivalent flex-based styling (e.g. explicit flex-grow/order) was added for `.title`. Since `.contents` is now `display: flex`, the title element will behave as a flex item with default properties, which may differ visually from the previous floated layout (e.g. losing its intended width/positioning relative to the logo and panel). This is a visible regression with no replacement styling.

title: Dropped `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule
body: The nested `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule under `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper` was removed while adding flexbox ordering to `.extra-info-wrapper`. This silently changes the vertical alignment of bullet-style badges in the extra-info-wrapper with no equivalent replacement, likely causing a misalignment regression for topic badges.

title: `.small-action-desc` padding change may cause overlap with icon
body: The padding was changed from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` (which reserved space for the 45px-wide `.topic-avatar` icon floated to the left) to `0 1.5%`. Since `.topic-avatar i` has a fixed `width: 45px`, a percentage-based padding of 1.5% will be smaller than 45px on most viewport widths, causing the icon and the description text to overlap instead of being properly spaced, especially combined with switching `.small-action` to flexbox (which no longer relies on float clearing the same way).

title: Inconsistent mixin usage for already-cross-browser properties
body: `.bullet` previously used plain `display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline;` (modern syntax, acceptable since other code already uses unprefixed flex properties elsewhere). Swapping to the `@include inline-flex()` / `@include align-items()` mixins adds back vendor-prefixed, mostly obsolete `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` flexbox syntax (2009 spec) which is unnecessary for current browser support and increases generated CSS size without functional benefit.

title: include_website_name missing question mark
body: Method is named `include_website_name` instead of `include_website_name?`. Active Model Serializers' `include_<attr>?` convention requires the trailing question mark to be recognized; without it, this method is never called and `website_name` will likely always be serialized (or behave inconsistently), unlike `website` which uses `untrusted_attributes` for conditional inclusion. This can leak website_name for untrusted/TL0 users even though `website` itself is hidden, defeating the privacy guard in `untrusted_attributes`.

title: Fragile domain parent/child matching logic
body: The branch comparing `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` to detect sibling subdomains (e.g. www.example.com vs forum.example.com) is brittle: it only matches when both hosts have the same number of labels and more than 2 labels on the host side, and does not handle multi-level TLDs (e.g. co.uk) or mismatched label counts for legitimate sibling domains, potentially producing incorrect short names or exposing full paths unintentionally.

title: Missing test for include_website_name behavior
body: No test verifies that `website_name` is excluded for untrusted/TL0 users (via `include_website_name?`), unlike other untrusted attributes like `website`. Given the suspected missing `?` bug in the include method, this test gap means the regression would not be caught.

title: include_website_name missing question mark breaks AMS inclusion check
body: The method is defined as `include_website_name` instead of `include_website_name?`. ActiveModel::Serializer's attribute inclusion mechanism relies on `include_<attr>?` methods; without the trailing `?`, this method will not be recognized as the inclusion predicate for `website_name` and the attribute's visibility logic (returning nil when website is blank) won't be honored consistently with the rest of the codebase's pattern (e.g. `include_card_image_badge_id?`, `include_user_fields?`). This could cause `website_name` to always be serialized (relying only on the method returning nil) or inconsistent behavior across serializer versions.

title: website_name logic duplicated from removed JS computed property without shared tests for edge cases
body: The three-branch domain comparison logic (exact match, same TLD+1 generic check requiring >2 segments, suffix check) is intricate and only exercised by 3 happy-path specs. Edge cases such as discourse_host having exactly 2 segments (e.g. 'example.com') combined with a website_host with more subdomains, or malformed URIs, are not covered, risking incorrect display or exceptions in production for malformed website values (though `rescue nil` guards URI parsing, but note it swallows all errors including unrelated ones).

title: Leftover incorrect doc comment reference
body: The doc comment for `profileBackground` was changed from `@property websiteName` to `@property profileBackground`, but this diff is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (website path display) and is just incidental cleanup; not a functional issue, but indicates the `websiteName` computed property removal in user.js.es6 controller was not matched with equivalent removal/rename everywhere, e.g., model computed `profileBackground` naming confusion suggests leftover artifacts from a copy-paste of the old `websiteName` property.

title: include_website_name missing '?' breaks ActiveModelSerializers convention
body: The predicate method is defined as `include_website_name` instead of `include_website_name?`. AMS conventions require a trailing `?` for conditional attribute inclusion methods (as seen with all other include_* methods, e.g. `include_email?`, `include_suspend_reason?`). Without the `?`, AMS will not recognize this method as the inclusion guard for `website_name`, so the attribute will likely always be serialized (or behave inconsistently) regardless of whether `website` is present, defeating the purpose of this check and potentially leaking an unwanted empty/nil website_name attribute.

title: website_name not covered by untrusted_attributes guard
body: `untrusted_attributes` lists `:website` but not `:website_name`. Since website_name is derived from website and may contain more revealing info (the full path), TL0 users viewed anonymously will still have website_name present in the serialized output even though website itself is hidden, inconsistent with the intent of the untrusted_attributes restriction and the first spec in the test file which doesn't check for website_name.

title: Fragile domain-matching heuristic for website_name
body: The logic in website_name uses split('.').length comparisons and ends_with? checks to decide whether website and instance share a domain. This can produce incorrect results for cases like 'notexample.com' matching 'example.com' via ends_with?("." + host) only partially guards against false positives, but subdomain-length-based matching (elsif branch) can mismatch for domains with different numbers of labels (e.g., co.uk-style TLDs), producing wrong website_name values silently rather than erring safely to just the host name.

title: Lightness value changed unintentionally, not just converted to dark-light-choose
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The diff changes this to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` — the light-theme lightness value was changed from 30% to 70%, not just paired with a dark-theme fallback. This changes the light-theme appearance (lighter/dimmer text instead of darker), inconsistent with the stated goal of only adding dark-theme support.

title: Light-theme lightness value changed instead of preserved
body: In the mobile `.topic-map h3` color rule, the original light-theme value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The converted rule uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which changes the light-theme lightness from 20% to 50%, altering the original light-theme color rather than only adding dark-theme support.

title: Light-theme lightness value changed instead of preserved
body: The `.topic-map .map .number, i` rule originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` for both mobile files but was converted inconsistently: here it correctly keeps 20% but elsewhere (e.g., topic-post desktop map .number) the lightness was changed. Cross-check with desktop/topic-post.scss `.number, i` where lightness: 20% → still 20% but secondary 80%, in some other instances values were altered. This specific instance appears fine, but should be checked against similar occurrences for consistency since the PR introduces inconsistent treatment of the same selector/property across similar files.

title: Light-theme lightness value changed instead of preserved (group-member-info .name)

After conversion it became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme lightness from 30% to 50%. This is an unintended visual change to the light theme beyond the PR's stated purpose of fixing dark theme support, and is inconsistent with the same selector in desktop/user.scss which also made this same change — indicating a systematic but unintended modification rather than a straightforward find-and-wrap conversion.

title: Light-theme lightness value changed instead of preserved (group-member-info .name)
body: Same issue as in mobile/user.scss: `.group-member-info .name` originally was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, silently changing the light-theme color value from 30% to 50% lightness instead of simply adding a dark-theme fallback.

title: Light-theme lightness changed from 70% to 30% in custom-message-length

The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which changes the light-theme value from 70% to 30% lightness — a much darker color than before, not merely adding dark-mode support.

title: Lightness value changed inconsistently with surrounding pattern, inverting intended effect
body: The diff changes `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` color from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. title: remove_member uses delete without permission/membership validation and no auth-check for cross-group misuse
body: group.users.delete(user_id) directly removes a user from a group association without verifying the user_id actually belongs to that group or sanitizing it beyond to_i. While not strictly a security hole given admin-only access, the removed code path previously went through group.remove(user) which may trigger model callbacks (e.g., updating is_default_mod_role, etc.) that this new direct ActiveRecord association delete bypasses, potentially leaving related state inconsistent.

title: Route changed from member-scoped id to flat params, breaking existing API consumers
body: The admin groups routes changed from nested resource member actions (which used :id) to collection-level 'members' routes requiring group_id and user_id/usernames params. Any external integrations or other code paths calling the old route structure (e.g. PATCH update for incremental membership changes) will break since update_patch/incremental logic was entirely removed from the controller. This is a breaking API change without any deprecation path mentioned in the PR description.

title: members endpoint always paginates now, changing behavior for non-automatic groups
body: Previously, pagination (limit/offset) was only applied for automatic groups; now all groups are always limited to 50 by default. Clients that previously fetched the full member list for small, non-automatic groups in one call now get only 50 members silently unless they also pass offset/limit, which could silently truncate data for existing callers not updated to use pagination.

title: findMembers no longer returns a value usable by old callers expecting a members array
body: findMembers() used to resolve with the array of User objects; now it resolves to undefined and instead mutates the model's own properties (members, user_count, limit, offset) as a side effect. Any remaining caller expecting the promise to resolve with the member list (per the previous contract) will now get undefined, which is a backward-incompatible contract change that could silently break usages outside the files touched in this PR.

title: Template iterates over 'members' but route exposes raw group model without computed property guarantee at render time
body: The route no longer waits for findMembers() to resolve before transitioning (setupController fires model.findMembers() without returning/chaining the promise), so the template may render with 'members' still undefined on first paint, resulting in an empty list rendering before members load asynchronously. This differs from previous behavior where afterModel waited for the promise to resolve before the controller/template were set up, so there's a transient UI flash/empty state regression.

title: Member routes for add/remove not scoped to a specific group id
body: The new routes `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` are declared inside `resources :groups do ... end` as collection-level routes (not `member do ... end`), producing paths like `/admin/groups/members` instead of `/admin/groups/:group_id/members`. The controller actions rely on `params.require(:group_id)` passed in the body/query instead of the URL, which works but is inconsistent with REST conventions used elsewhere in this file (e.g., `/users/:username/groups/:group_id`), and means the group id is not validated as part of the route, making CSRF-style/method confusion or missing-param errors less obvious. This is a design inconsistency rather than a crash, but it diverges from the rest of the routes file and could confuse future API consumers expecting `/admin/groups/:id/members`.

title: members endpoint always issues two queries, no caching, breaking automatic/large group handling
body: The previous implementation had special-case handling for automatic groups (limiting/offsetting large automatic groups to avoid timeouts/truncation issues) with a TODO about more than 200 groups truncating. The rewritten `members` action removes that special case and always does `group.users.count` plus a paginated query for every group type with a default limit of 50. For very large automatic groups (e.g. trust_level groups with tens of thousands of members) this now always executes a full COUNT(*) on every request, which can be an expensive query under load, especially since this is a public user-facing endpoint (`GroupsController`), not admin-only. There's no caching of the total count, which was presumably one of the reasons the former code treated automatic groups specially.

title: findMembers silently returns undefined instead of a resolved promise when name is empty
body: `findMembers` early-returns `undefined` (via bare `return ;`) when `name` is empty, whereas the previous code returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. Any caller doing `.then()` on the result of `findMembers()` (e.g. route hooks that previously chained promises) will now throw a TypeError if name happens to be empty, since `undefined` has no `.then` method. Although current call sites in this PR don't chain on this specific case, this is a behavior regression that silently breaks the promise contract of the function.

title: addMembers never clears the input field after adding, acknowledged by stale TODO
body: The `addMembers` action contains a TODO: "should clear the input" but it's left unaddressed. After adding members, the `usernames` property is not reset, so the user-selector field keeps showing the previously entered usernames, which is confusing when the admin wants to add another batch of members.

title: members iterated in group.hbs but never defined for the new group (create) flow
body: The template references `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` and `user_count`, which are populated only after `model.findMembers()` succeeds (triggered from the route). For a new group (no `id` yet), `{{#if id}}` guards the whole members+add-members block so this is fine, but once a group is saved for the first time via `create()`, `members`/`user_count`/`offset`/`limit` are never populated (findMembers is only called from the route's `setupController`, not after `create()`). This means immediately after creating a group and transitioning to `showGroup`, the newly created group's member section will render with stale/undefined pagination data until the admin navigates away and back, since `admin_group_route.js`'s `model` hook just looks up the already-cached group object rather than re-fetching it with members.

title: add_members/remove_member routes don't include group id in path
body: The new routes `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` are nested under `resources :groups` collection-style without a member block, so they map to `/admin/groups/members` instead of `/admin/groups/:group_id/members`. The controller actions rely on `params.require(:group_id)`, which must then be passed as a query/body param instead of a path segment, inconsistent with the group.js model which calls `/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json'`. This mismatch means the JS-generated URLs (e.g. `/admin/groups/5/members.json`) will not match this route definition at all, causing 404s for add/remove member actions from the admin UI.

title: findMembers silently returns undefined for group with no name, breaking promise chains
body: `findMembers` returns `undefined` (via bare `return;`) when name is empty, but callers like `admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6` call `model.findMembers()` without checking the return value, and other callers (`removeMember`, `addMembers`) chain `.then()` on it. If `findMembers` is ever called in that state (e.g. a group being created, with no name yet) any subsequent chained `.then()` would throw since `undefined.then` is not a function. The previous code safely returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`; this behavior was removed without updating all callers to tolerate it.

title: members action performs an extra count query without an existing index verified
body: The new `members` action calls `group.users.count` for `total` and a separate paginated query, resulting in two queries instead of one previously. For large automatic groups (previously limited to 200), this adds overhead on every page load. Not necessarily wrong, but a potential performance regression worth confirming is acceptable given removal of the previous automatic-group-only limit comment about truncation bugs with >200 groups, which is no longer mentioned or addressed here as a known limitation goes unverified for all group types now (always paginated with limit 50).

title: add_members/remove_member endpoints lack explicit automatic-group checks consistency with destroy/update
body: Both `add_members` and `remove_member` guard against automatic groups via `return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic`, which is good, but there is no spec covering case where `group_id` doesn't exist (invalid id leads to ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound, unhandled -> 500 instead of a clean 404). This isn't newly introduced but the PR adds these actions without addressing error handling for missing groups, which could leak 500 errors instead of friendly 404s in production for malformed requests.

title: FallbackLocaleList#[] uses SiteSetting during early boot/non-request context
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale, which requires DB access. This initializer runs at boot before the DB may be ready (e.g. during asset precompilation or rake tasks with no DB), potentially raising errors. Previously config.i18n.fallbacks = true used Rails' built-in fallback mechanism without a DB dependency. This change introduces a hard runtime dependency on SiteSetting (and thus DB connectivity) wherever I18n.fallbacks is used, which could break any management task running without an available database.

title: ensure_loaded! accesses @loaded_locales without synchronization
body: ensure_loaded! reads/initializes @loaded_locales outside of LOAD_MUTEX before calling load_locale (which does synchronize internally). This creates a race: @loaded_locales ||= [] can race with the mutex-protected block in load_locale set up by a different thread, potentially overwriting the array concurrently or causing an inconsistent state. All other access points to @loaded_locales are guarded by LOAD_MUTEX; this new entry point bypasses that protection for its own initialization step.

title: Fallback locale loading walks a list and triggers DB SiteSetting lookup on every request
body: set_locale now calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!, which internally calls self[I18n.locale] (triggering SiteSetting.default_locale lookup, and array building each time) before iterating to call I18n.ensure_loaded! for each locale in the fallback chain, on every request. Although ensure_loaded! short-circuits once locales are loaded, the SiteSetting.default_locale access and array allocation happen every request, adding needless overhead per request compared to the previous static config.i18n.fallbacks = true approach.

title: FallbackLocaleList calls SiteSetting before DB may be ready
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale during I18n fallback resolution, which can be invoked very early in boot (e.g. during other initializers, rake tasks, migrations) before the database/connection is available. This risks raising ActiveRecord::NoDatabaseError or similar during tasks like db:create, assets:precompile, or any I18n.t call executed prior to DB readiness, unlike the previous config.i18n.fallbacks = true approach which used static fallback rules.

title: ensure_loaded! reads/mutates @loaded_locales without synchronization
body: ensure_loaded! checks and lazily initializes @loaded_locales outside of LOAD_MUTEX before calling load_locale (which itself synchronizes). The initial `@loaded_locales ||= []` is a race: under concurrent requests, two threads could both see @loaded_locales as nil and reassign it, potentially losing already-loaded-locale tracking or causing redundant loads. This should be done inside the mutex or guarded consistently with the rest of the class to avoid the known race in multi-threaded Rails deployments.

title: ensure_loaded! triggers repeated SiteSetting lookups and fallback list per request
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] is called every time set_locale runs (every request) and queries SiteSetting.default_locale each time, building a new array. Since this replaces a previously built-in Rails i18n fallback resolution (config.i18n.fallbacks = true), the cost of SiteSetting lookups on every request could add overhead unless SiteSetting itself is cached; worth confirming caching behavior is adequate.

title: ensure_loaded! runs under global LOAD_MUTEX for every fallback locale on every request
body: set_locale now calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! on every controller request, which iterates up to 3 locales (user, site default, en) and calls I18n.ensure_loaded! for each, acquiring LOAD_MUTEX each time. Although load_locale returns early if already loaded, this still means every request now runs the mutex-synchronized membership check 2-3x instead of once, adding unnecessary contention/overhead especially under multi-threaded Puma/Unicorn with many concurrent requests.

title: translate still only loads config.locale, not fallback locales
body: The patched translate method only ensures config.locale is loaded (load_locale(config.locale)), but with fallbacks now enabled via I18n::Backend::Fallbacks, a translation lookup for the current locale may need to fall through to SiteSetting.default_locale or :en translations which are never explicitly loaded by this accelerator. Since Base#load_translations is overridden to require explicit loading of files, translations for fallback locales other than config.locale may never actually be loaded into the backend unless something else triggers it (e.g. the controller's set_locale calling ensure_loaded! for all fallbacks). This creates a fragile coupling: translate() depends on an external before_filter to pre-load fallback locales, so any I18n.t call made before set_locale runs (e.g. during console/rake tasks, background jobs, or early boot) can silently return missing-translation results instead of falling back correctly.

title: SiteSetting access during initializer load order risk
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale at lookup time, which is fine lazily, but note this initializer unconditionally overwrites I18n.fallbacks for all environments (removed previously environment-specific config.i18n.fallbacks = true toggles). There's no longer any way to disable fallbacks per-environment as previously supported in production/profile configs, which were removed. If fallbacks are undesired in some environment (e.g. test, to catch missing translation keys precisely), this is now a global behavior change with no opt-out, differing from previous per-environment configurability.

title: Denial cache never invalidated on permission changes, risking stale denies
body: permDenialCache entries are set with a TTL (shortCacheTTL=30s) but are never explicitly invalidated when a user's permissions change (e.g. after a grant). Although the TTL will eventually expire the entry, during that window a user who is just granted access to a resource (e.g. the folder/dashboard they just created) could still be denied if a prior Check attempt cached a denial for the exact same name/action/parent combination before the permission was granted. This can reintroduce the very bug this PR aims to fix (can't access just-created resources) in edge cases where Check is called before creation completes and then re-checked within the TTL window.

title: Permission cache not invalidated/refreshed consistently between Check cache-hit and re-fetch paths
body: When getCachedIdentityPermissions returns a cache hit but checkPermission returns false (not allowed), the code falls through to re-fetch permissions via getIdentityPermissions and overwrite the perm cache with fresh data (service.go line ~139-155). This means every 'miss' on a stale/incomplete cached scope map triggers a full DB fetch, which is the intended fix, but combined with permDenialCache being set afterward, a legitimate but just-granted permission that arrives between the cached-permission check and the DB fetch could still get cached as a denial if the DB read is also stale (e.g. read replica lag). There's no documentation or handling of eventual consistency behind permissionStore.GetUserPermissions, so denial caching on top of potentially stale reads compounds the staleness window instead of resolving it reliably.

title: In-proc server still uses a 5 minute local cache for all cache wraps including the new denial cache
body: In ProvideAuthZClient, the Service is constructed with a single shared cache.NewLocalCache(cache.Config{Expiry: 5 * time.Minute, ...}) used for all cacheWrap types in rbac.NewService, but each cacheWrap sets its own TTL per Set call (e.g. shortCacheTTL=30s for permDenialCache). This works correctly since TTL is passed per Set, but the underlying LocalCache's global Expiry (5m) could override/compete with per-entry TTLs for cleanup semantics depending on the authlib cache implementation; worth verifying that the authlib LocalCache correctly honors the TTL argument passed to Set rather than relying on the Config.Expiry, since misconfiguration here was not covered by any test added in this PR.

title: Denial cache never invalidated on permission grants, can cause stale denies
body: The denial cache entry (permDenialCache) is set with shortCacheTTL but there is no invalidation when a user's permissions change (e.g. after being granted access to a resource). Although TTL is short (30s), during that window a user who was just granted access to a resource they were previously denied will continue to be denied, which directly works against the stated goal of this PR (allowing users to access resources they just created/were granted). Since permission grants aren't necessarily reflected until the next TTL expiry, this cache can mask legitimate permission updates for up to 30s with no proactive invalidation path.

title: Cached permission check short-circuits only when allowed=true, hiding stale denies from cache but not reducing DB calls on deny
body: In Check(), when getCachedIdentityPermissions succeeds but checkPermission returns allowed=false, the code falls through and re-fetches permissions from the DB and performs the full check again. This means cache hits for a user who lacks the permission always double the work (cached check + DB fetch + check again) instead of simply trusting the fresh DB fetch result, which could be returned directly from the second check without doing both. This is a performance regression for all 'denied' or missing permission cases, somewhat defeating the purpose of the permission cache for negative outcomes aside from the explicit denial cache for exact name/folder lookups since the denial cache key depends on exact Name/ParentFolder which won't match for other requested names and thus won't prevent repeated DB round trips for the same user+action+different resource names that are also denied.

title: Metric mislabeling: permissionCacheUsage recorded 'false' even on cache hit when permission denied
body: When the cached permission check at line 123 returns allowed=false (cache hit occurred but resource not allowed), the code proceeds to line 137 and records permissionCacheUsage with 'false', incorrectly implying there was no cache hit. This produces misleading metrics about actual cache utilization, since a cache hit did occur yet is counted as a miss when the cached result happened to be a denial for this specific resource.

title: Denial cache can mask newly granted permissions until TTL expiry
body: The new permDenialCache stores a 'denied' result for `shortCacheTTL` (30s) keyed by namespace/user/action/name/parent. If a user is denied access and then permissions change (e.g. they are granted access, or create the resource) within that 30s window, the Check() call will short-circuit to a cached denial at line 117-121 without re-querying the DB, returning Allowed=false even though the user now has access. This directly undermines the stated goal of the PR (allowing users to access resources they just created), since any earlier failed check for the same name/action will keep denying access for up to 30 seconds afterward.

title: Redundant lookups when cached permissions exist but check fails
body: When getCachedIdentityPermissions returns permissions but checkPermission(ctx, cachedPerms, checkReq) returns false (stale/incomplete cache), the code falls through to call getIdentityPermissions, which for TypeUser/TypeServiceAccount calls GetUserIdentifiers (and getUserBasicRole/getUserTeams) again. GetUserIdentifiers was already resolved inside getCachedIdentityPermissions just moments earlier, so the same cache lookups/sql queries for identifiers are effectively repeated. Not incorrect, but adds avoidable overhead on every cache-miss request.

title: Render service identity never benefits from permission caching
body: getCachedIdentityPermissions always returns cache.ErrNotFound for types.TypeRenderService (line 353-355), forcing getIdentityPermissions -> getRendererPermissions to be computed on every single Check/List call for renderer identities, even though the result is static and cheap to cache. While getRendererPermissions is cheap, this inconsistency with other identity types means the renderer path bypasses the whole caching/denial mechanism introduced in this PR.

title: In-proc authz client caching disabled entirely
body: ProvideAuthZClient now passes `authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{})` for the in-proc client instead of a real cache (previously a `cache.NewLocalCache` was used). This means every Check/List call made in-proc now always crosses the gRPC channel without any client-side caching, relying solely on the server-side permission cache added in rbac/service.go. If the server-side cache has a cache miss or needs singleflight dedup under load, this adds overhead for every single authorization check in-proc that was previously avoided by the client cache; the PR description claims this is intentional for resolving stale-cache resource-creation issues, but it removes a layer of caching for all other read-heavy authz checks that aren't related to freshly-created resources.

title: Delete menu item hidden when rulerRule is absent for Grafana-managed rules from list view
body: `canDelete` is now computed from either rulerRuleAbility or grafanaPromRuleAbility, but the actual menu rendering condition at `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}` still requires `rulerRule` to be truthy. Since the whole point of this PR is to support the case where only `promRule` is available (ruler API removed from list view), delete action will never render for rules coming from the alert list view even when `canDelete` is true via `grafanaDeleteAbility`. `handleDelete` also requires a `RulerRuleDTO` parameter, so the API is inconsistent with the new partial-data flow.

title: Pause menu item still gated on rulerRule only
body: The pause menu item condition `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana'` requires rulerRule to be a grafana rule, but canPause can now become true purely from grafanaPauseAbility (based on promRule) without rulerRule being present. This means pause will never show in the alert-list-view context even though canPause is true, since MenuItemPauseRule requires a RulerRuleDTO rule prop that isn't present.

title: Removed ruler rule matching no longer differentiates creating/deleting rule states
body: The previous implementation fetched both ruler and Prometheus data and used matchRules to render 'Creating' (ruler-only) and 'Deleting' (prom-only) states via RuleOperation. This PR removes the ruler fetch and the matching logic entirely, rendering only Prometheus-sourced rules. As a result the UI will not show rules that exist only in ruler but haven't propagated to Prometheus yet (creating state), nor rules that still appear in Prometheus but were deleted from ruler (deleting state), effectively silently dropping these transitional states without a replacement implementation or test coverage for the removed behavior described by matchRules tests that were deleted.

title: useRulerRuleAbility called with possibly undefined rule but still used for canEditRule logic unconditionally
body: useRulerRuleAbility(rule, groupIdentifier, AlertRuleAction.Update) is called even when `rule` is undefined (RuleProps now allows either rule or promRule). While useAllRulerRuleAbilities tolerates undefined rule, mixing this with the new useGrafanaPromRuleAbility fallback obscures intent and risks returning stale/incorrect ability tuples (e.g., when both rule and promRule happen to be present but inconsistent, the OR logic could incorrectly grant edit permission based on whichever path returns true first).

title: Comment above useAllAlertRuleAbilities refers to its own deprecated usage incorrectly
body: The comment '// This hook is being called a lot...' was moved under useAllAlertRuleAbilities but it originally described performance concerns for that specific (now deprecated) hook. Since the hook now simply delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, the comment is misleading as placed - it implies the memoization optimization lives directly in this wrapper, but the actual heavy useMemo lives in useAllRulerRuleAbilities, called via delegation on every re-render of groupIdentifierV2 memo dependency on rule, which recomputes a new object identity whenever rule changes, potentially duplicating the concern rather than fixing it.

title: Removed handling of rules deleted from ruler but still in Prometheus (and vice versa) causes inconsistent/stale UI
body: The previous implementation fetched both ruler and Prometheus groups and reconciled them (matchRules), showing 'Creating'/'Deleting' operation states for rules that are out of sync between the two APIs. This PR removes the ruler fetch entirely and only renders based on the Prometheus response. As a result, rules that have just been created (visible in ruler but not yet in Prometheus) or deleted (removed from ruler but still present in Prometheus due to eventual consistency) will not show any transitional state, or will show rules as fully loaded/normal when they're actually deleting/creating, since there's no mechanism to detect this discrepancy anymore. This changes user-visible behavior and removes test coverage (GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx removed tests for 'Creating'/'Deleting' states) without an equivalent replacement, which could confuse users during rule creation/deletion.

title: isPaused and provenance now derived from Prometheus data instead of ruler, potentially stale due to eventual consistency
body: GrafanaRuleListItem now solely relies on `rule.isPaused` and `rule.provenance` from the GrafanaPromRuleDTO (Prometheus) rather than the ruler response (`grafana_alert.is_paused`/`provenance`). Since Prometheus endpoints are eventually consistent (per comments elsewhere in the codebase, e.g. the removed matchRules logWarning), pause state and provenance status shown in the UI may lag behind recent ruler-side changes (e.g. right after pausing/unpausing a rule), leading to incorrect state being displayed temporarily, with no mechanism to reconcile this discrepancy.

title: Missing key prop on GrafanaRuleListItem elements in list
body: In the switch statement, the 'grafana' case renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` without a `key` prop, while the other cases (`datasource`, `default`) correctly pass `key={key}`. Since this is inside `.map()`, React will warn about missing keys and reconciliation may behave incorrectly (e.g., unnecessary remounts) for Grafana-origin rules in the filtered list.

title: Delete menu item unavailable when only promRule is provided (list view)
body: The Delete menu item is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule`, requiring a rulerRule to be present. However, per the new doc comment, consumers coming from the alert list view only pass `promRule` (ruler API calls have been removed from that view), meaning `rulerRule` will be undefined and the Delete action will never render for Grafana rules in the list view, even though `canDelete` may be derived correctly from the Grafana Prometheus rule abilities. This silently breaks the delete workflow from the new list view for users who otherwise have permission.

title: Silence drawer gated on rulerRule, won't trigger for promRule-only consumers
body: `showSilenceDrawer` rendering is conditioned on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`, requiring the ruler rule. Since the component now also supports promRule-only usage (per RuleProps using RequireAtLeastOne and the new grafana prom ability checks), when only `promRule` is supplied (as in the new list view), the Silence button triggered via AlertRuleMenu's `handleSilence` sets `showSilenceDrawer` to true but the drawer will never actually render because `rule` (rulerRule) is undefined, silently breaking the silence action for list-view-only consumers.

title: Removed 'creating'/'deleting' rule states handling causes loss of UX feedback
body: The old code compared ruler rules against prom rules to detect rules that are being created (present in ruler but not yet in Prometheus) or deleted (present in Prometheus but removed from ruler) and rendered RuleOperationListItem/operation=Creating/Deleting accordingly. The new implementation only renders from the Prometheus response and no longer fetches/compares the ruler group, so rules in the process of being created or deleted will simply not appear or appear with no special indication, changing user-visible behavior during rule creation/deletion.

title: Edit/view URL no longer includes returnTo parameter
body: The removed GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx built the view href with `createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`, preserving navigation context. The new GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx builds the href with `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view')` without passing returnTo, so users navigating from the rule list to the detail view and back may lose their previous location/filter state.

title: isPaused no longer falls back to rulerRule.is_paused
body: Previously isPaused used `rule?.isPaused ?? is_paused` combining both prom and ruler sources. Now it's just `rule?.isPaused` from the GrafanaPromRuleDTO. Since the ruler lookup is removed entirely, this is likely fine, but if the Prometheus rule briefly lacks the isPaused field (e.g. stale response), the pause state indicator could be incorrect with no fallback.

title: Deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities still exported without migration path enforced
body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities is marked @deprecated but is still used elsewhere (e.g. RulesTable via useAlertRuleAbility) and now internally forwards to useAllRulerRuleAbilities with a derived groupIdentifier. This dual-path (rulerRule vs promRule abilities) risks diverging behavior between RuleActionsButtons (old table) and the new RuleActionsButtons.V2/AlertRuleMenu, since permissions can now be computed via two independent paths that must be kept consistent manually.

title: Double interpolation risk when runSplitQuery is called from shardQuerySplitting
body: runSplitQuery now applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables to each query. However, shardQuerySplitting.ts also calls applyTemplateVariables on queries before invoking runSplitQuery (via runSplitQuery -> runSplitGroupedQueries). This means queries get interpolated twice: once in runShardSplitQuery and again inside runSplitQuery. If applyTemplateVariables is not idempotent (e.g. for variables with special characters, regex escaping, or variables that get consumed/removed on first pass), this could produce corrupted queries or double-escaping, and is wasteful. This also changes order relative to shard selector interpolation (interpolateShardingSelector happens before the second applyTemplateVariables call), which may re-process the shard selector unexpectedly.

title: Loss of per-query metadata/order from applyTemplateVariables map
body: The new `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))` is applied to all non-hidden, non-empty queries uniformly, but applyTemplateVariables for sharded/interpolated selector queries previously happened in a different place with different context. No test covers interaction with scopedVars per-query differences (e.g., when `request.filters` is combined with sharding-specific values), so there's a test gap for the combined sharding + ad hoc filter + split scenario.

title: Interpolated queries passed into runSplitQuery for re-interpolation
body: runShardSplitQuery interpolates queries via applyTemplateVariables and passes them to splitQueriesByStreamShard, which eventually calls runSplitQuery with already-interpolated expressions (including shard selector interpolation via interpolateShardingSelector). Since runSplitQuery itself now calls applyTemplateVariables again on its targets, the shard-selector-modified expr (containing __stream_shard__ labels) will be run through applyTemplateVariables a second time. If applyTemplateVariables performs operations that aren't safe to re-apply (e.g., stripping/escaping of variable syntax, or relies on original unmodified expr), this could silently break shard-filtered queries or produce incorrect results that aren't caught by existing tests focused only on happy-path interpolation of $__auto/$step variables.

title: Interpolation now happens twice
body: runSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on each query target before splitting, but runSplitGroupedQueries subsequently constructs subRequest objects that are passed to datasource.runQuery, which internally (per Loki datasource logic) typically also applies template variable interpolation per sub-request (e.g. with per-chunk scopedVars/range). Since runSplitQuery is also called from shardQuerySplitting.ts via runSplitQuery after shardQuerySplitting already applied applyTemplateVariables itself, templates variables may be interpolated twice. If applyTemplateVariables is not idempotent (e.g. replaces $__range or special chars) this can corrupt the final query text, especially for shard splitting flows where interpolation happens for both the sharding step and inside runSplitQuery.

title: scopedVars/range not updated per split sub-request
body: Interpolation is now done once up-front at the full request's range/scopedVars, before time-range splitting occurs. Any template variables that depend on the per-chunk time range (e.g. $__range, $__interval relative to the sub-request's partitioned range) will be resolved using the original, unsplit request range rather than each sub-request's actual range. This changes behavior from before, where (seemingly) interpolation happened closer to execution. This could silently produce incorrect query results for queries using range-dependent variables within split sub-queries, though isQueryWithRangeVariable queries are excluded from splitting, other interval-based vars like $__interval may still be affected per chunk since runQuery normally recomputes them for each subRequest with its own range/intervalMs — but now the interpolation already happened on the original query before this per-chunk recompute could take effect, defeating per-chunk accuracy for $__interval and similar vars.

title: Possible double interpolation across shardQuerySplitting -> runSplitQuery
body: shardQuerySplitting.ts now applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables to each target instead of the previous interpolateVariablesInQueries. Downstream, splitQueriesByStreamShard calls runSplitQuery (querySplitting.ts) with these already-interpolated queries, where runSplitQuery itself calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on request.targets again. If applyTemplateVariables isn't idempotent for all variable types (e.g., special characters introduced by shard selector string manipulation such as __stream_shard__=~"20|10"), the second interpolation pass could mangle the already-built shard selector expression.

title: Double interpolation risk: runSplitQuery now applies template variables, but callers may already have interpolated queries
body: runSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on each target unconditionally. shardQuerySplitting.ts's runShardSplitQuery also independently applies applyTemplateVariables before calling splitQueriesByStreamShard, which internally calls runSplitQuery (via subRequest). If runSplitQuery is reached with already-interpolated queries from the sharding path, applyTemplateVariables will be invoked a second time on an already-interpolated expr/step, which can corrupt expressions containing literal '$' characters or already-substituted template variables (e.g., if a label value itself contains a '$' sequence that happens to match a variable syntax). This also changes the datasource.query() entrypoint behavior if it previously relied on interpolation happening elsewhere exactly once.

title: Non-splitting/instant queries now go through applyTemplateVariables unconditionally, bypassing prior per-call-path interpolation contracts
body: Previously, interpolation timing/ownership was handled by callers (e.g., datasource.query or specific splitting functions). Now querySplitting.ts interpolates every non-hidden, non-empty query up front for all code paths (logs, metric, non-splitting). If any caller already interpolates before invoking runSplitQuery (a plausible existing contract elsewhere in the codebase not shown in this diff), this introduces silent double-interpolation bugs that are hard to detect via type-checking since applyTemplateVariables is idempotent only for already-resolved queries without conflicting variable names docs/tests don't cover this scenario.

title: traceID log attribute silently dropped
body: The old logRequest implementation added a 'traceID' attribute (via tracing.TraceIDFromContext) to each log entry. The rewritten logRequest no longer includes traceID, and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go also doesn't add it. This means plugin request completion logs will no longer be correlatable with trace IDs, a regression in observability that isn't mentioned in the PR description.

title: instrumentContext() duplicated logic now only sets context, not logger message formatting consistency
body: instrumentContext builds contextual attributes using log.WithContextualAttributes, but these attributes are only retrievable through FromContext() calls. Since TestLogger.FromContext (pkg/plugins/log/fake.go) just returns a brand-new empty TestLogger discarding any contextual attributes, any test relying on verifying that contextual attributes (pluginId, dsName, uname, etc.) are correctly logged cannot be validated with the current fake implementation, and no test was added for ContextualLoggerMiddleware or for verifying FromContext() produces the expected attributes end-to-end.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards call context, breaking tests of contextual logging
body: FromContext on TestLogger always returns a fresh NewTestLogger() instance that has no connection to the original TestLogger's recorded calls or the context's attributes. Since LoggerMiddleware now calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) instead of m.logger.Info(...), any test using TestLogger to assert on logged messages/attributes via LoggerMiddleware will not observe anything recorded on the original TestLogger instance, since the Info call happens on the discarded instance. This silently breaks the ability to unit test LoggerMiddleware's logging behavior with TestLogger, and no updated test was included for logger_middleware.go despite the significant behavior change (contextual attributes, dropped pluginId/endpoint/dsName/uname/traceID in logParams).

title: Removed structured log fields (pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, uname) from logParams without equivalent verification
body: logRequest previously added pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID directly into logParams. These are now expected to come via the contextual logger set by ContextualLoggerMiddleware/instrumentContext, but there's no test verifying that the final emitted log record actually contains these fields through the FromContext()-based logger chain. If the contextual-logger wiring order ever changes (e.g., LoggerMiddleware placed before ContextualLoggerMiddleware), these fields would be silently lost from logs with no test coverage to catch such a regression.

title: Stale logger name reflects old middleware name
body: The logger passed to `NewLoggerMiddleware` is still named `log.New("plugin.instrumentation")`. Since the instrumentation/metrics logic has been moved out, and this logger is now used by LoggerMiddleware for request completion logs, the name should reflect that (e.g. `plugin.loggermiddleware`) to avoid confusing log output and future maintainers.

title: FromContext silently drops contextual attributes on type-assertion failure
body: `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` falls back to `d.New()` (a plain new logger with no context) if the underlying `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` result isn't a `*log.ConcreteLogger`. This silently discards all contextual attributes (e.g. pluginId, dsName, uname) added upstream by `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`, meaning log lines from `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` (which relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)`) could lose important plugin/request context without any warning, undermining the stated goal of this PR (moving contextual logging into LoggerMiddleware).

title: No test coverage for new FromContext-based logging behavior
body: `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now depends on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` picking up contextual attributes set by the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`, but there is no test added (in this PR) verifying that log output actually contains the pluginId/endpoint/dsName/uname attributes that used to be asserted when they lived inside the metrics/instrumentation middleware. The removed fields (pluginId, endpoint, uname, traceID, dsName, dsUID) from `logRequest`'s own params are not covered by any new test demonstrating they are now correctly supplied via context.

title: Loss of traceID in log output
body: The previous implementation added a `traceID` field via `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` to the log parameters. This logic was removed in the refactor and not replicated in the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (which only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname). As a result, plugin request logs no longer contain the trace ID, which is a regression in observability/debuggability compared to before.

title: Logger name still references old 'instrumentation' terminology
body: `log.New("plugin.instrumentation")` passed to `NewLoggerMiddleware` still uses the old "instrumentation" name even though the whole point of this PR is to rename instrumentation middleware to metrics middleware and separate out logging concerns. This leaves inconsistent/outdated naming in log output that doesn't reflect the renamed middleware architecture.

title: Missing nil-request guards unlike sibling middlewares
body: Other middlewares (e.g. LoggerMiddleware, MetricsMiddleware) check `if req == nil` before accessing req.PluginContext to avoid potential nil pointer dereference. ContextualLoggerMiddleware.QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics do not perform this check before calling instrumentContext(ctx, endpoint, req.PluginContext), so a nil req would panic here, whereas it would be gracefully handled further down the middleware chain in LoggerMiddleware.

title: Test name not updated to match renamed middleware
body: The test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware even though the file was renamed to metrics_middleware_test.go and the production type/constructor renamed to MetricsMiddleware/newMetricsMiddleware. This is inconsistent with the stated goal of the PR (better naming/consistency) and could confuse future readers correlating test names with implementation names.

title: Race condition in device-limit enforcement
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice first calls CountDevices and only if count < deviceLimit proceeds with the upsert. Between the count check and the insert there is no locking/transaction, so concurrent requests can all pass the check and insert simultaneously, allowing the device count to exceed deviceLimit. The limit is a soft, racy guard rather than a hard limit.

title: Anonymous authentication now fails synchronously when device-tagging fails
body: Previously TagDevice was invoked asynchronously in a goroutine so tagging failures (including DB errors) never blocked authentication. Now Authenticate calls TagDevice synchronously and returns the error directly (not just for ErrDeviceLimitReached but anything propagated from TagDevice/tagDeviceUI/CreateOrUpdateDevice), which will cause Authenticate to fail and reject anonymous access on any device-tagging error, e.g. transient DB issues, not just when the limit is actually reached. This changes behavior for all non-limit errors from 'warn and continue' to 'fail the request'. Also, running TagDevice synchronously now adds a DB round trip to every anonymous request's auth path, which could have a performance impact that wasn't present before (the removed goroutine had a timeout and panic recovery that are no longer present).

title: TagDevice now propagates all tagDeviceUI errors, not just the device-limit error
body: The change added `return err` after `a.tagDeviceUI(...)` fails, so any error returned by tagDeviceUI/CreateOrUpdateDevice (not only ErrDeviceLimitReached) is now returned to the caller (Authenticate), which will cause anonymous authentication to fail on any device creation error (e.g. transient DB failures), whereas previously such errors were only logged and ignored.

title: TagDevice now runs synchronously on request path, blocking auth flow
body: The previous implementation ran anonDeviceService.TagDevice in a background goroutine with a timeout context, decoupling the DB write from the authentication request. The change removed the goroutine and now calls TagDevice synchronously using ctx from the request. Every anonymous request now blocks on a DB write (CreateOrUpdateDevice/updateDevice) before returning the identity, which can meaningfully increase latency and DB load for anonymous auth, especially under high traffic. This also means any DB slowness/timeouts directly affect user-facing anonymous request latency, not just background error logging.

title: Device limit reached blocks ALL anonymous authentication, not just the specific device
body: When ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned from TagDevice, Authenticate now returns (nil, err), causing authentication to fail entirely for the anonymous client. Previously, tagging failures were just logged as warnings and the anonymous identity was still returned. Now, once the device limit is reached, any new anonymous device/session will fail to authenticate at all (since Test() always returns true and there's no fallback), effectively breaking anonymous access for all new devices once the configured limit is hit, rather than just skipping the quota tracking as likely intended.

title: Device limit check has a race condition (count-then-insert without transaction)
body: In CreateOrUpdateDevice, the device limit is enforced by first running a separate CountDevices query and only then performing the insert/upsert in a different statement. Between the count and the insert, concurrent requests can also pass the same check, allowing the device limit to be exceeded under concurrent load. This is a classic TOCTOU race since there is no transaction or locking tying the count and insert together.

title: New device_limit setting not documented
body: A new ini configuration key `device_limit` is added under `[auth.anonymous]` (cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit), but there is no accompanying update to configuration documentation (e.g., conf/defaults.ini, docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana) in the diff. Users have no way to discover this new setting or its default/behavior without reading the source.

title: Race condition in device limit enforcement
body: CountDevices and the subsequent decision to insert vs update are not performed atomically. Multiple concurrent requests can all see count < deviceLimit and proceed to INSERT, resulting in more devices than deviceLimit allows. This defeats the purpose of a hard device limit under concurrent load.

title: Device tagging now synchronous, changing authentication latency and failure semantics
body: Previously TagDevice was invoked in a background goroutine with its own timeout so that tagging failures/slowness never affected the Authenticate call path. The change makes TagDevice synchronous and returns errors (notably ErrDeviceLimitReached) directly from Authenticate, meaning every anonymous authentication now blocks on a DB write and that a client exceeding the device limit is fully denied authentication rather than just not being tracked. This is a significant behavior change (anonymous access can now fail entirely once device limit is reached) that should be explicitly called out, and lacks the previous panic-recovery/timeout safety net for a synchronous DB call occurring on the hot auth path.

title: TagDevice error now propagated up through Authenticate, which was previously only logged
body: a.tagDeviceUI's error is now returned instead of only logged with a.log.Debug. Combined with the synchronous call in client.go, any transient DB error during tagging (not just device-limit) will now cause Authenticate to fail for anonymous users, whereas before failures were swallowed. This broadens the blast radius of DB hiccups to break anonymous access entirely.

title: Device limit check doesn't account for existing device being updated
body: When count >= deviceLimit, the code unconditionally calls updateDevice instead of first checking if the device already exists (e.g., a known device checking in again should always succeed via normal upsert, not just within the expiration window check in updateDevice). This conflates 'at limit, so only allow updates to existing active devices' with potential false negatives if a legitimately active device's updated_at narrowly falls outside the window used in the update condition, causing ErrDeviceLimitReached for an existing device instead of updating it via the normal insert-or-update path.

title: Debug logging uses log.Error level
body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags use r.log.Error(...) for routine informational logging of counts (e.g. 'Annotations to clean by time', 'cleaned annotations by time'). This is not an error condition and will pollute error logs/alerting on every cleanup cycle. Should be Debug or Info level.

title: deleteByIDs loses non-SQLite batch deadlock protection by not splitting large ID lists
body: deleteByIDs builds a single DELETE ... WHERE id IN (...) statement with up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize parameters for non-SQLite databases. For large batch sizes this still issues one large multi-row DELETE statement which can hold locks for an extended period, partially re-introducing the kind of lock contention this PR is trying to avoid, since the fix only addressed the subquery lock scope, not statement size for MySQL under large batch configs.

title: Fetch and delete occur in separate non-transactional statements, allowing race / double counting
body: fetchIDs and deleteByIDs are now executed as two separate WithDbSession calls without a shared transaction.
