Between the SELECT and subsequent DELETE, rows matching the condition could be concurrently modified (e.g. tags change, or org cleanup settings elsewhere), causing deletes of IDs that no longer meet the criteria, or missing newly matching rows. The PR documents accepting under-deletion but doesn't address potential over-deletion by ID when a row's content changed between fetch and delete (e.g. an annotation unexpectedly becoming non-matching no longer matters because deletion is by ID only, so any row with that ID gets deleted regardless of current state).

title: Cleanup job interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute without justification
body: The ticker interval for running all cleanup jobs (including unrelated ones like snapshot/dashboard version/image/query history cleanup) was reduced from every 10 minutes to every 1 minute. This is a 10x increase in frequency for all cleanup jobs, not just annotation cleanup, which could increase load unnecessarily and isn't explained in the PR description, which only discusses deadlock avoidance via query splitting.

title: Logging annotation cleanup counts at Error level
body: In CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags, r.log.Error(...) is used to log routine/successful cleanup progress (e.g. "Annotations to clean by time", "cleaned annotations by time"), not actual errors. This will pollute error logs/alerts with normal operational information and could trigger false error-rate alarms.

title: Fetch-then-delete by ID introduces TOCTOU window per batch
body: CleanAnnotations/CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags now fetch IDs in one query/transaction and delete them in a separate one. Between fetch and delete, the row's state could change (e.g., it stops matching the original criteria, or in rare cases is already deleted by another process), making the delete silently delete fewer or different rows than counted, and the reported 'affected' count can diverge from fetched IDs count without any error surfaced. This is called out as acceptable in the comment for under-deletion, but there's no safeguard or logging distinguishing fetched vs. actually deleted counts (the Error logs intermix len(ids) and x without clarifying whether they match), making root-causing data-mismatch issues difficult in production.

title: SQLite ID interpolation uses unparameterized values but non-SQLite path still bounded by driver parameter limits
body: deleteByIDs falls back to raw string interpolation of IDs only for SQLite over the parameter limit; for other DB types (e.g., MySQL/Postgres) all IDs are passed as query parameters regardless of batch size. If AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize is configured very large for MySQL/Postgres, this could exceed those drivers' parameter count limits (MySQL's limit is typically 65535 placeholders), causing a runtime failure that isn't tested or guarded against for non-SQLite databases.

title: Cleanup job interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute without justification
body: The ticker interval for background cleanup jobs (including snapshot/version/short-url/query-history cleanup, not just annotations) was changed from every 10 minutes to every 1 minute. This 10x increase in cleanup job frequency affects all cleanup jobs system-wide, not just annotation cleanup cited in the PR description, and could increase DB load significantly. There's no mention of this tradeoff in the PR description, and it isn't scoped only to annotation cleanup.

title: Delete-by-time and delete-by-count run outside a single transaction, no longer atomic with tag cleanup
body: CleanAnnotations now issues separate fetchIDs + deleteByIDs calls, each opening its own WithDbSession/transaction instead of sharing one transaction as before. If the process crashes or an error occurs between fetching IDs and deleting, or between deleting annotations and deleting their tags elsewhere, orphaned annotation_tag rows or partially-cleaned state can result. The PR acknowledges under-deletion but doesn't address the broader loss of atomicity between fetch and delete across concurrent writers (an annotation could be deleted concurrently with the DELETE WHERE id IN (...) still succeeding harmlessly, but a concurrently inserted/updated annotation matching the IDs is a non-issue; however, loss of the single-transaction guarantee for correctness during errors/crashes should be called out and tested).

title: Cleanup ticker interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute without justification
body: The ticker driving srv.clean (which runs all cleanup jobs, not just annotations) was changed from every 10 minutes to every 1 minute. This is a 10x increase in frequency for all cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, short URLs, query history, etc.), which seems unrelated to the stated purpose of fixing MySQL deadlocks in annotation cleanup, and may increase load/contention on the database rather than reduce it. This change is not mentioned in the PR description and could have broad unintended performance/concurrency consequences across all cleanup jobs.

title: Raw ID interpolation into SQL for SQLite batch delete
body: In deleteByIDs, when running on SQLite with batch size over 999, IDs are formatted directly into the SQL string via fmt.Sprint/fmt.Sprintf instead of using parameter binding. Although IDs are int64 values fetched from the DB (low injection risk here), this pattern deviates from safe parameterized queries used elsewhere and could become a problem if the code is later reused with less-trusted ID sources upon refactor.

title: Fire-and-forget goroutines use parent context that may be canceled before legacy write completes
body: In Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection, the async goroutine does `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` deriving from the request's ctx. Once the HTTP request completes, the original ctx is typically canceled by the server, which will immediately cancel the derived context too, aborting the legacy write before the 10s timeout is reached. This defeats the purpose of "asynchronously write to legacy as a safe measure" since most async legacy writes will likely be canceled right after the response is sent back to the client, silently dropping legacy writes.

title: Metric mislabeled as legacy duration on storage failure
body: In Create, when d.Storage.Create fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` — but this is a storage failure, not a legacy failure. This mislabels the metric, polluting legacy error-duration metrics with storage errors. The same pattern repeats in Update (line ~129) where a storage failure is recorded via `recordLegacyDuration`.

title: Delete records metric using resource name instead of kind
body: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes `name` (the object's name) where other calls pass `options.Kind`. This produces inconsistent/incorrect metric labels, mixing up object names and resource kinds across metrics, making dashboards for mode3 delete duration unreliable.

title: DeleteCollection records legacy outcome under storage metric
body: In the DeleteCollection async goroutine, after calling d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, the code calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`, mislabeling the legacy write duration/outcome as a storage metric.

title: No test coverage for async legacy writes
body: The new tests for Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection only assert the result returned from Storage; they never assert that the legacy store's Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection mocks were actually called (there's no `AssertExpectations`/`AssertCalled` on the legacy mock, and goroutines are fire-and-forget with no synchronization), so the core new behavior of mode 3 — asynchronously writing to legacy as a safety measure — is effectively untested and could silently regress.

title: Fire-and-forget goroutine with derived context, no error propagation or sync in tests/production
body: Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection spawn goroutines using context.WithTimeoutCause derived from the request ctx. If the parent ctx (request context) is cancelled when the HTTP response is sent, the derived context will also be cancelled before the legacy write completes, causing the asynchronous legacy write to be silently aborted (not after 10s, but immediately on request completion). This defeats the stated goal of 'write to legacy asynchronously as a safe measure' since most of the time the write will be cancelled right after the response is returned.

title: Legacy write errors are silently swallowed
body: In Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection, errors from the asynchronous legacy write are only recorded in a duration metric (recordLegacyDuration) but never logged or surfaced anywhere else. If legacy writes to the fallback store start failing consistently, there is no log signal to catch it, undermining the 'safe measure' purpose of still writing to legacy.

title: Delete ignores constructed log context
body: In Delete, a logger with method/kind/name values is built into `log`, but `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` uses `d.Log` instead of the local `log` variable, so the extra context fields (name, kind, method) are not propagated into the context used by subsequent calls.

title: Incorrect metric call on storage update failure
body: In Update, when d.Storage.Update fails, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...). This mislabels a storage failure as a legacy failure in metrics, making mode3 dashboards/alerts inaccurate.

title: Incorrect metric call on storage create failure
body: In Create, when d.Storage.Create fails, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) rather than d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...), mislabeling the failure source in telemetry.

title: Shadowed metrics registry causes duplicate registration risk
body: In TestMode3_Get a new prometheus.NewRegistry() `p` is created locally shadowing the package-level `p`, inconsistent with other subtests in the same file that reuse the shared `p`. This is unnecessary and can mask registration-collision bugs that would otherwise be caught by reusing a single registry across test cases within the same process.

title: No tests verify asynchronous legacy writes
body: The new DualWriterMode3 implementation performs legacy writes in background goroutines for Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection, but none of the tests assert that the legacy mock's Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection methods are actually invoked (e.g., via m.AssertExpectations or similar with a wait). Since these calls happen asynchronously, the tests may pass even if the goroutine logic is broken, is never triggered, or has a race condition — leaving the core new behavior of mode 3 untested.

title: Fire-and-forget goroutines using request-scoped context without proper detachment
body: In Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection, the async legacy write goroutine does `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` using the original request ctx as parent. If the HTTP request context is cancelled/finishes (as it normally does once the response is returned to the client), the derived context is cancelled immediately, so the legacy write will likely fail with context canceled before the 10s timeout has a chance to elapse. This defeats the purpose of the async legacy write (reliability net) in mode 3, silently causing legacy writes to fail most of the time in production. The context passed to the goroutine should be detached from the parent request context (e.g., using `context.WithoutCancel` or a fresh context with request-scoped values copied) before adding the timeout.

title: Metric label mix-up: name used instead of Kind, and errObjectSt naming inconsistency
body: Line 106 (`d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`) passes the deleted resource `name` where other calls pass `options.Kind` as the metric label; this is inconsistent with every other method in this file and will skew/break metric aggregation by kind for Delete operations.

title: DeleteCollection records legacy result using recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration
body: In the goroutine for DeleteCollection, the legacy call's result is recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`, unlike Create/Delete/Update which correctly call `recordLegacyDuration` for the async legacy write. This mislabels legacy write metrics as storage metrics, corrupting dashboards/alerts based on these metrics.

title: No rollback/compensation when legacy write fails in mode 3 async path
body: Because the legacy write happens asynchronously after the unified storage write succeeds, there's no mechanism (retry, dead-letter, reconciliation) to catch or compensate when the legacy write fails (errObjectSt != nil only gets fed into a metric, nothing else). Given this is explicitly described as a 'safe measure' for keeping legacy in sync, silently dropping failures could lead to drift between legacy and unified storage with no operator-visible signal besides a metric. The PR doesn't address detection/alerting/retry for this gap.

title: No tests verify async legacy write behavior of mode 3
body: All tests for mode3 only verify that the Storage (unified) call result is used/returned; none of the tests assert that the Legacy mock's Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection methods are actually invoked (asynchronously) with correct arguments, nor do they test the new timeout/cancellation behavior. Given mode3's entire purpose is to also write to legacy storage, this is a significant test gap — a regression that stops the async legacy write entirely would not be caught by this suite.

title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, inverted logic also present
body: The function enableSqlExpressions computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (i.e. enabled is true when the flag is NOT enabled), then returns false either way (both branches return false). This makes the function always return false regardless of feature flag state, meaning SQL expressions are unconditionally disabled even when intentionally wanted, and the logic is nonsensical/dead code. While this currently achieves the goal of disabling the vulnerable feature, the naming and logic are backwards and misleading, and if flag intent is ever restored this will silently remain broken. Should be a simple hard return false with a clear comment, or fixed boolean logic tied to the feature flag.

title: TablesList calls RunCommands which always errors, breaking valid SQL expression configs
body: db.go's RunCommands (and QueryFramesInto) stub always returns errors.New("not implemented"). TablesList calls duckDB.RunCommands and will always fail, so even when FlagSqlExpressions were enabled in future, any SQL expression would fail with 'error serializing sql: not implemented'. There's no test covering TablesList/QueryFramesInto behavior change, so broken functionality isn't caught in CI.

title: No tests updated/added for disabled SQL execution path
body: The PR disables the DuckDB-backed SQL engine by stubbing it out, but no tests were added or updated to verify that SQLCommand.Execute now fails gracefully, or that ReadQuery rejects QueryTypeSQL properly in all code paths (e.g., UnmarshalSQLCommand doesn't check the feature flag at all, so legacy/alerting code paths that call UnmarshalSQLCommand directly bypass the ReadQuery-level block and will reach the broken Execute path silently).

title: UnmarshalSQLCommand does not check feature flag / enablement before constructing command
body: UnmarshalSQLCommand (used for legacy raw-node parsing, e.g. in alerting) builds a SQLCommand without any check against enableSqlExpressions or the FlagSqlExpressions toggle, unlike ReadQuery which blocks QueryTypeSQL. This means code paths that use UnmarshalSQLCommand instead of ReadQuery could still attempt to construct and execute SQL commands, which only fail later via the stubbed db.go (and only because of that side effect), rather than being explicitly disabled. This is fragile: if db.go stub is removed/replaced in future without restoring the check here, the vulnerable code path reopens silently.

title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false regardless of flag state
body: The function `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then always returns `false` in both branches (if enabled, return false; otherwise fall through to return false). This means the function is dead/confusing code that always disables SQL expressions no matter the feature flag state. While the net effect (always disabled) achieves the security goal of this PR, the logic is misleading and buggy — if someone later tries to re-enable the feature by flipping the flag, it will silently not work, and the variable `enabled` is unused in a meaningful way. This should be simplified to `return false` directly with a comment, to avoid confusion and dead code since the flag check is a no-op.

title: TablesList still calls RunCommands which always errors
body: TablesList() calls duckDB.RunCommands(...) against the new stub DB in db.go, which unconditionally returns `errors.New("not implemented")`. Combined with reader.go's always-false enable check, SQL expressions are effectively disabled, but this leaves two different disablement mechanisms (feature flag always false, and stub DB always erroring) that could get out of sync if one is fixed without the other, potentially creating confusing behavior or partial re-enablement bugs in the future.

title: Unused parameters in stub methods not referenced, could trigger lint warnings
body: The stub methods in db.go (TablesList, RunCommands, QueryFramesInto) take parameters that are never used in the function bodies. While harmless at runtime, this can trigger unused-parameter lint warnings and signals that this is dead placeholder code; a comment explaining the stub's purpose (and that it intentionally disables SQL expressions) would help future maintainers understand why DB does nothing instead of assuming it's an incomplete implementation.

title: No test coverage asserting SQL expressions are disabled
body: The PR's stated purpose is to disable SQL expressions to prevent an RCE/LFI vulnerability, but no test was added to pkg/expr (e.g., in reader_test.go or sql_command_test.go) that verifies QueryTypeSQL requests are rejected with the expected error, or that NewSQLCommand/Execute paths fail safely when the feature is toggled on. Given the security-critical nature of this change, a regression test ensuring the vulnerability can't be silently reintroduced is important and currently missing.

title: enableSqlExpressions logic bug - always returns false regardless of feature flag state
body: The function negates the feature flag check (`!h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)`) and then both branches return false. This means SQL expressions are now unconditionally disabled no matter what the feature flag value is, which happens to achieve the goal here (disabling the vulnerable feature), but the logic is dead/confusing code with an unreachable branch and inverted naming (checking `!IsEnabledGlobally` but naming the var `enabled`). This is misleading for future maintainers who may try to re-enable the feature by flipping the flag, not realizing the function can never return true.

title: TablesList still composes raw SQL into a command string even though the DB backend is a stub
body: TablesList still builds a SQL command string via fmt.Sprintf with user-controlled rawSQL (only escaping single quotes) and passes it to RunCommands. Although the new DB.RunCommands always returns 'not implemented', this leaves a latent SQL/command-injection-prone pattern in the code; if RunCommands is ever reimplemented without careful review, the vulnerability could be reintroduced. The PR description says this is a stopgap, but the unsafe raw string construction remains a landmine for future implementers.

title: Stub DB methods always return errors, causing SQL expression users to see generic/opaque failures
body: NewInMemoryDB/TablesList/RunCommands/QueryFramesInto are now stub methods that always return 'not implemented' errors. Combined with reader.go's enableSqlExpressions always returning false, the SQL expression type is effectively dead code behind an always-false gate, yet this new stub also runs independently in sql_command.go and parser.go error paths. There's no test coverage verifying these stub behaviors or verifying that SQL expressions are indeed fully disabled end-to-end (e.g., a test that attempts to create an SQL command and asserts the expected 'not implemented' error).

title: Removed go-duck dependency but no corresponding version bump or changelog note
body: The PR removes github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck entirely and the DuckDB-based implementation, replacing it with stub functions, but there's no documentation update explaining to users that SQL Expressions are now completely non-functional (not just feature-flagged) and why. The PR description explicitly says documentation isn't touched, but given this disables a previously working (if vulnerable) feature, users with the feature flag enabled will now get hard failures without any release note added in this diff.

title: NewResourceServer now blocks startup synchronously and can fail hard on index build errors
body: Init(ctx) is now called synchronously inside NewResourceServer, using the long-lived background ctx (claims.WithClaims(context.Background())). Any transient failure during search index build (e.g. slow DB, timeout, or temporary storage issue) now causes NewResourceServer to return an error, which can prevent the whole module/server from starting. Previously, failures were deferred to first gRPC call and could be retried per-request. This is a behavior/API change that could turn transient indexing problems into full startup failures, with no retry mechanism.

title: Init uses sync.Once — a transient failure permanently blocks the server
body: s.once.Do caches the first result in s.initErr; if Init fails once (e.g., due to a transient index/watcher error), every future caller of Init will get the same cached error forever since Once never re-runs. Since Init is now called once at construction and no longer called before every RPC, this effectively means a single early failure can never be recovered without restarting the whole process. Previously, each RPC re-called Init, giving many chances to succeed; now there's exactly one attempt with no retry path at all, since RPC handlers no longer call Init themselves.

title: Removed guard against unitialized server: RPCs no longer check Init before executing
body: All gRPC handlers (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, PutBlob, GetBlob) previously called s.Init(ctx) defensively before executing; this diff removes all of those calls, relying solely on the one-time Init call during NewResourceServer. If NewResourceServer's Init silently failed in a way that returned a server anyway, or if some other code path constructs `server` without going through NewResourceServer (e.g., tests), these methods will now run against a server where backend/watcher weren't properly initialized, with no safety net or explicit error returned.

title: Watch loop ignores context cancellation, can leak goroutine with init's background context
body: s.search.init starts a goroutine using watchctx := context.Background() reading from `events` in an infinite for loop with no select on ctx.Done(). Since init is now called synchronously during server construction with its own context (that is subsequently discarded, since watchctx is a new unrelated background context), there is no way to ever stop this goroutine except for the channel closing. Combined with the search support being created once per ResourceServer and that now being constructed eagerly at startup, any server restart/shutdown path that doesn't close the `events` channel will leak this goroutine indefinitely.

title: Finer-grained locking introduces race for concurrent BuildIndex calls on the same key
body: GetIndex uses cacheMu.RLock to check the cache, and BuildIndex no longer holds a lock for the whole build process (previously the full function was locked). Now, two concurrent calls to getOrCreateIndex for the same NamespacedResource (e.g., during Search or handleEvent when the index doesn't exist yet) can race: both see nil from GetIndex, and both proceed to independently build full indexes for the same key before only one of their results survives in `cache[key]` (last writer wins) — wasting resources and potentially leaving a stale/duplicate bleve.Index handle (and underlying directory bleve.New(dir,...) for file-based ones) open and never closed, leaking file handles/goroutines.

title: Blocking search index build now in NewResourceServer constructor can cause long startup / deadlock risk
body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously, which triggers searchSupport.init() that builds the full index for all namespaces before returning from the constructor. For large installations this can take a very long time, blocking server startup (and anything that constructs ResourceServer, e.g. module server wiring, tests, or other services that expect fast construction). Any caller relying on fast/non-blocking construction (previously relying on lazy init during the first gRPC call) will now be blocked indefinitely or until index build completes, with no timeout or context deadline applied to the Init call.

title: Stop() mutates initErr without synchronization against Init()/once
body: Stop() sets s.initErr directly outside of the sync.Once guarded path used by Init(). If Init() is still running concurrently (e.g., background watcher goroutine) while Stop() executes, there's a race writing/reading s.initErr without synchronization (no mutex, no atomic). This was already present before, but now that Init() runs synchronously at construction and the once can still fire later from other paths, the race window remains and reviewers should flag that initErr access is unguarded.

title: totalBatchesIndexed increment and errgroup closure captures loop variable info unsafely in older style
body: In the init loop, group.Go closures use the loop variable `info` from `for _, info := range stats`. Depending on Go version semantics (pre-1.22) and since the closures run concurrently, capturing `info` without taking a local copy inside the goroutine can lead to data races/incorrect namespace reported if Go version < 1.22. Also totalBatchesIndexed++ is incremented from multiple goroutines without synchronization (concurrent writes to the same int from errgroup goroutines), which is a data race since initWorkers can run several goroutines in parallel.

title: NewResourceServer now returns error on index build failure, changing behavior/contract for existing callers
body: Previously, failures in search index initialization (e.g., transient DB/network issues during index build) only affected the first gRPC call lazily. Now any error returned from s.search.init(ctx) during NewResourceServer causes construction of the ResourceServer to fail entirely, preventing the whole module/server from starting. This is a notable behavior change: any transient issue in index building (e.g., one misbehaving namespace or stats collection failure) will block the entire resource server from being created, with no partial-start fallback.

title: NewResourceServer now blocks on full index build at startup, with no timeout
body: Init(ctx) (which triggers s.search.init -> builds all namespace indexes) is now called synchronously inside NewResourceServer using a background ctx with no deadline. If index building for many namespaces takes a long time (which is exactly the motivation for this PR), the server constructor itself can hang indefinitely or for a very long time, blocking the whole application startup (and anything depending on ResourceServer creation, e.g. module server wiring). This moves the problem from a gRPC call's context cancellation to blocking overall process startup, which can be worse for large/slow deployments and provides no way to bound or observe the delay before serving traffic.

title: Init is no longer idempotently callable per-request, removing safety net for lazy failures
body: Previously every RPC method called s.Init(ctx) defensively, ensuring the server was initialized before serving (and returning init errors to callers). That per-call guard was removed from Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob. If NewResourceServer's Init succeeds partially (sync.Once only runs once) or if some external code path manages to construct a `server` struct without going through NewResourceServer, the server will serve requests referencing unitialized state (e.g. broadcaster not set) causing nil pointer dereferences (e.g. in Watch calling s.broadcaster.Subscribe) rather than a clean error.

title: Non-atomic totalBatchesIndexed increment under concurrent goroutines
body: In searchSupport.init, totalBatchesIndexed++ is executed inside group.Go goroutines that run concurrently (group.SetLimit(s.initWorkers) allows multiple workers), but totalBatchesIndexed is a plain int incremented without synchronization. This is a data race and can produce incorrect/undercounted totals in the emitted span event, and under -race will be flagged as a race condition.

title: ListIterator span context not propagated to child calls
body: ListIterator still uses `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, tracePrefix+"List")` and discards the derived ctx, so trace context is not propagated into listAtRevision/listLatest and their nested spans, unlike the fix applied to GetResourceStats in the same PR. This leaves traces still disconnected for the List path, which the PR claims to fix generally.

title: NPE risk if webauthnAuth is null but passkeys considered enabled
body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) checks webauthnAuth != null before calling webauthnAuth.fillContextForm, but UsernamePasswordForm() (no-arg constructor) sets webauthnAuth=null; since isConditionalPasskeysEnabled already guards with webauthnAuth != null this specific path is safe, but subclasses overriding isConditionalPasskeysEnabled (e.g. in UsernameForm) without updating guard could reintroduce NPE. No test exercises the no-webauthn constructor path with context.getUser() non-null + override, so this is a fragile invariant depending on method ordering across subclasses.

title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without user param causing inconsistent behavior
body: UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() (no-arg), but UsernamePasswordForm only defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user); presumably an overload exists but is not shown in the diff for this file. If no no-arg overload exists in UsernamePasswordForm, this is a compile error; if it does exist elsewhere, its semantics (independent of user) differ from the user-aware check used elsewhere in the same class, risking inconsistent skip-decisions between UsernameForm.authenticate and UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate for the same user context.

title: Behavior change to shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators affects subclasses silently
body: WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm now delegates to shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) instead of a direct null check on user, and WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides it to always return false. This means WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator (parent of WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator) will never show allowed authenticators even in 2FA-style flows where it inherits this authenticator type without the conditional override; verify this is intentional and tested for all subclasses, not only the conditional-UI case covered by new tests.

title: Widened visibility of internal auth note constant
body: USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH was changed from protected to public solely to be referenced from AuthenticatorUtils via static import. This increases the public API surface of an internal implementation detail; consider exposing it through a method rather than a public constant to avoid external code depending on this auth note key.

title: shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators now gates return null, affecting non-passkey subclasses
body: fillContextForm now returns null (causing required-action registration flow) based on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) instead of simply user != null. For WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator this method is overridden to return false, meaning authenticators.getAuthenticators().isEmpty() check and the early `return null` path is skipped entirely for conditional UI, changing behavior silently for any caller relying on the previous `user != null` short-circuit (e.g. second-factor WebAuthnAuthenticator subclasses that don't override the method but have different expectations). This behavioral change isn't covered by any non-webauthn unit tests.

title: fillContextForm only called when context.getUser()==null branch previously, now also for pre-set user with wrong condition ordering
body: The webauthn fillContextForm call was moved outside of the `else` block and is now gated solely by isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which runs regardless of whether formData was already populated with loginHint/rememberMe values. This changes the order/conditions under which fillContextForm executes compared to the original code and may call fillContextForm even when the user was already set via USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH note, which previously used a different helper form.setAttribute block; the two concerns (hiding username field vs showing webauthn fields) are no longer mutually tied, risking inconsistent form state for re-authentication (e.g. passkeys icon shown with username hidden fields in unexpected combos). Needs explicit test coverage for the combination of USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH + conditional passkeys to confirm correct form rendering.

title: Visibility of USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH widened from protected to public
body: The authentication note constant was made public to allow access from AuthenticatorUtils, widening the API surface of this abstract class. This is a minor API contract change; if this field is intended to remain internal to authenticators, consider moving the constant to a shared location instead of exposing it as public API, which could be depended upon by external SPI implementations now that it's public, complicating future refactors.

title: webauthnAuth null check inconsistent with isConditionalPasskeysEnabled usage
body: action() calls `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` directly, but authenticate()/challenge() now use `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` which additionally requires `user != null`. During normal login (no user set yet) with passkeys enabled, action() will still try to route webauthn form submissions via webauthnAuth, but authenticate()/challenge() will no longer call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when user==null, since previously the old code called fillContextForm when user was null (conditional UI case). This reverses the previous conditional-UI behavior: conditional UI (discoverable login with no selected user) must have fillContextForm invoked when user is null, but the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled explicitly requires user != null, which will break conditional UI passkey flows where no user is pre-selected.

title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled called without context/user
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the inherited method signature in UsernamePasswordForm is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. This implies either a missing no-arg overload exists elsewhere undocumented, or this code does not compile. If there is a separate no-arg overload, its semantics (ignoring the user) differ from the single-arg version used elsewhere, causing inconsistent behavior between UsernameForm and UsernamePasswordForm when deciding to skip the form for an already-authenticated user ignoring whether they actually have passkeys registered.

title: Reauthentication form flags not reset on success path first render
body: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError only sets USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED attributes when an error occurs, duplicating logic previously in authenticate(). Because this is now spread across three call sites (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, UsernamePasswordForm, WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator) there's a risk that one path (e.g. WebAuthnAuthenticator.setErrorResponse for 2FA errors) never calls this helper, so hidden-username state could be lost/inconsistent on certain error branches, leading to the username field reappearing unexpectedly during re-authentication errors routed through WebAuthnAuthenticator rather than WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.

title: configureTestRealm method not shown/defined in diff
body: addTestRealms calls `configureTestRealm(realmRepresentation)` but this method isn't defined in the shown diff/content for this file, nor is it inherited visibly in the provided AbstractWebAuthnVirtualTest excerpt. If this method doesn't exist, the test class will fail to compile; this should be verified before merge.

title: remove() invalidates login caches even when IDP is unknown
body: In remove(), storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) can be null if the alias doesn't exist. registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) is then called with a null idp, which calls getLoginPredicate().test(null). The predicate starts with Objects::nonNull so it returns false safely, but this relies on implicit behavior rather than an explicit null check, making the code fragile to future predicate reordering and obscuring intent.

title: getForLogin cache key does not depend on organizationId for ORG_ONLY/ALL modes
body: cacheKeyForLogin only incorporates the FetchMode, not the organizationId, but the underlying IdentityProviderListQuery stores results per searchKey (organizationId) within that single cached entry. This means a single invalidation key is shared across all organizationId values for a given mode, which is fine for invalidation but means the cache entry for FetchMode.ORG_ONLY/ALL grows unbounded as more distinct organizationIds are queried (there is no eviction except full invalidation), since IdentityProviderListQuery accumulates entries per searchKey indefinitely until the whole object is invalidated. This can lead to unbounded memory growth in deployments with many organizations repeatedly queried under FetchMode.ALL/ORG_ONLY.

title: update() invalidation ordering depends on stale idpById before delegate update
body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpById, model) is called using idpById (the pre-update state fetched via getById, potentially from cache) and the new model, before idpDelegate.update(model) is executed. If getById returned a stale cached entry whose login-eligibility differs from the actual DB state, the invalidation decision could be made on outdated data, potentially skipping a needed cache invalidation when organizationId or other login fields have changed outside of this fetch's visibility (e.g., concurrent updates).

title: getLoginPredicate() missing null-safety for idp.getConfig()
body: The predicate added at line 254 calls idp.getConfig().get(...) without checking if getConfig() can return null. If an IdentityProviderModel exists with a null config map, this will throw a NullPointerException when evaluating login eligibility, breaking getForLogin and all cache paths that rely on this predicate (create, remove, update invalidation logic).

title: registerIDPLoginInvalidation called with possibly null idp without null check
body: In remove(), storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) may be null if the IDP doesn't exist (alias not found). registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) then calls getLoginPredicate().test(idp) which internally checks Objects::nonNull first, so it won't NPE, but it silently returns false and skips invalidation — fine functionally. However, registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) at line 103 (in the isInvalid branch) will NPE if storedIdp is null since it directly calls idp.getInternalId() without a null check, unlike before this change there was no such path change but it still exists as a latent bug exposed via removed/invalid aliases.

title: getForLogin cache does not account for 'mode' granularity across ORG_ONLY organizationId variations consistently with getByOrganization caching
body: The IdentityProviderListQuery cache for getForLogin keys on cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode) and the per-organizationId filter result is stored as a sub key, similar to getByOrganization. However, when mode=ORG_ONLY and organizationId is null (fetch all org-linked IDPs), searchKey becomes empty string "", colliding conceptually with REALM_ONLY's empty search key semantics on a different cache key — this is probably fine since cacheKeyForLogin includes mode, but there's no invalidation differentiation per organization: any organization-level IDP change invalidates ALL cached searchKeys for all organizations under ORG_ONLY/ALL modes (via registerIDPLoginInvalidation iterating over all FetchMode and clearing the whole cacheKey), which means caching granularity per organizationId provides no benefit since the entire list query entry is invalidated together, causing cache thrashing for multi-tenant setups with frequent IDP updates in different orgs.

title: getLoginPredicate behavior change may have broader than intended effect
body: getLoginPredicate() now adds an extra condition requiring BROKER_PUBLIC=true for any idp with an organizationId, applied in both getForLogin's default implementation context and the invalidation logic in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider. This predicate is reused for cache invalidation decisions (create/remove/update) but the default getForLogin implementation uses separate search options (not getLoginPredicate directly) for building search criteria, so there's a risk of divergence between the actual query logic (search options) and the invalidation logic (predicate) if the two implementations are not kept in sync, since they must independently encode the same business rules (enabled, not link-only, not hidden, org public check) in two separate places.

title: remove() invalidates login cache using post-removal lookup of storedIdp which may not reflect prior login eligibility correctly
body: In remove(), storedIdp is fetched from idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) before removal, which is correct, but registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) is called with storedIdp possibly null if the alias doesn't exist. getLoginPredicate().test(idp) does handle null via Objects::nonNull check, so this is safe, but note that in the invalid branch (isInvalid(cacheKey)), registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) is also called with potentially null storedIdp passed into registerIDPInvalidation which calls idp.getInternalId() without a null check, causing a NullPointerException if the alias does not match any identity provider.

title: getForLogin cache keyed only by FetchMode, not by organizationId, except via per-searchKey entries growing unbounded
body: The IdentityProviderListQuery cached under cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode) accumulates entries per distinct organizationId searchKey (ORG_ONLY/ALL modes). Since organizationId can vary per request/organization, this list query cache can grow without bound as more organizations are queried over the realm's lifetime, with no eviction of stale per-org entries other than full invalidation. This differs from the by-organization cache which is keyed per org (cacheKeyOrgId), bounding growth to one entry per org; here all orgs share one IdentityProviderListQuery object which may grow large for realms with many organizations, impacting cache memory and lookup cost.

title: create() invalidates login cache using the model before internalId/alias is set by delegate
body: registerIDPLoginInvalidation(model) is called before idpDelegate.create(model), using the model as passed in which may not yet have config fully normalized (e.g., defaults applied) by the delegate. If getLoginPredicate() depends on fields normalized during creation (e.g., default enabled/hideOnLogin values applied by the delegate), the invalidation decision could be based on stale/incomplete data, potentially causing newly created login-eligible IDPs to not invalidate the cache so stale results are served until next change.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider misleadingly returns the default KeyStore provider
body: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is not actually the BouncyCastle provider in most environments (it's whatever the default KeyStore provider is, e.g. SUN). This is semantically wrong for a method whose contract is to return a BouncyCastle-based security provider, and any caller relying on getBouncyCastleProvider() to get BC capabilities will get an unrelated provider, potentially causing subtle failures or wrong algorithm lookups downstream.

title: Dead/wasted ASN1Encoder.create() calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder instances and call write() on them, but the results are discarded and never used (the encoder instance is immediately discarded). This is dead code left over from refactoring, wastes allocations and reads confusingly, though it causes no correctness issue since correct encoders are created again on lines 117-121.

title: Removed safety check allows silent selection among multiple CryptoProviders
body: The previous behavior threw an IllegalStateException when multiple CryptoProvider implementations were found on the classpath, forcing developers to notice and resolve ambiguous crypto configurations. This PR replaces that with silent ordering/sorting by order(), picking the highest order and merely logging (at debug level) which providers were ignored. If a deployment accidentally has two crypto providers on the classpath (e.g. due to a dependency misconfiguration), it will silently pick one based on order value instead of failing fast, which could lead to the wrong crypto provider being used in production without any visible warning (debug logging is typically disabled).

title: CryptoIntegration.init called without checking for pre-existing/conflicting provider
body: AuthzClient.create(Configuration) now unconditionally calls CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()). If the authz-client is used within the main Keycloak server or testsuite (sharing a classloader where both the AuthzClientCryptoProvider and DefaultCryptoProvider service files are visible), detectProvider will pick whichever has higher order (DefaultCryptoProvider order=200 > AuthzClientCryptoProvider order=100), but since CryptoIntegration.init is a once-only init guarded by a null check, if some other code path already initialized CryptoIntegration with a different provider before AuthzClient.create is called, this call becomes a no-op, silently keeping the previous provider. This ordering/initialization-order dependency is fragile and not well documented; combined with the lack of multiple-provider detection warnings, it can result in using the wrong CryptoProvider in mixed classpath scenarios without any error.

title: New crypto provider added to the test-only artifact, not the public authz-client module
body: The artifactId of this module is `keycloak-authz-client-tests`, and its own description explicitly states this module is only for the Keycloak testsuite and that 3rd parties should use `org.keycloak:keycloak-authz-client`. Yet the PR adds the new AuthzClientCryptoProvider implementation, its ASN.1 encoder/decoder, and the META-INF/services registration file into this same test-only module's `src/main`. If the public `keycloak-authz-client` artifact does not pick up this provider (it is a separate module), then the actual fix for issue #32962, which affects 3rd-party users of authz-client, never reaches them — the goal described in the PR (sync to keycloak-client repo for 3rd-party use) will not be met since this code lives in the test-only artifact.

title: Multiple CryptoProvider detection no longer throws, silently picks highest-order one
body: Previously, detecting more than one CryptoProvider on the classpath threw an IllegalStateException to prevent ambiguous/misconfigured deployments. The change now silently selects the provider with the highest `order()` and only logs the others at debug level. This is a behavior change that can mask accidental inclusion of multiple incompatible crypto providers (e.g. both FIPS and non-FIPS, or an unexpected AuthzClientCryptoProvider on the server classpath) which previously would fail fast; now it will silently proceed with whichever provider happens to have the highest order, potentially using the wrong crypto backend without any visible error at normal log levels.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() does not actually return a BouncyCastle provider
body: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` calls `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which returns the provider associated with the JVM's default keystore type — this has nothing to do with BouncyCastle and will typically return the SUN provider, not a BC provider. The method name and interface contract promise a BouncyCastle (FIPS or non-FIPS) provider; returning an unrelated provider is misleading and could break callers that rely on this contract (e.g. code registering/relying on BC algorithms via this provider).

title: Dead code building unused ASN1Encoder instances
body: In `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, the lines `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` create ASN1Encoder objects, write to them, and then discard them without using the result. This is leftover/dead code that does nothing useful, wastes allocations, and is confusing to readers trying to understand the actual encoding logic that follows just below.

title: Dead/wasted ASN1Encoder calls before building actual sequence
body: In concatenatedRSToASN1DER, two throwaway ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls are made (lines 114-115) whose results are discarded entirely before building the real DER sequence a few lines later. This is dead code that does nothing useful, wastes allocations, and is confusing/misleading to maintainers reading the encoding logic — it looks like a leftover from development that should be removed.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider misuses KeyStore provider as 'the' BC provider
body: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the provider backing KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(). This is fragile: the default keystore type's provider is not necessarily BouncyCastle (it could be SUN, PKCS11, etc. depending on JVM/platform configuration), yet CryptoProvider callers elsewhere in the codebase assume this method returns a BC-compatible provider. This can silently return the wrong provider on some platforms, causing unexpected failures or incorrect security provider usage downstream.

title: Silent provider selection replaces previous fail-fast behavior on multiple providers
body: Previously, detecting multiple CryptoProvider implementations on the classpath threw IllegalStateException to force explicit configuration. Now it silently picks the provider with the highest order() and only logs at debug level which providers were ignored. In production deployments where debug logging is disabled, this means a misconfigured classpath with multiple incompatible crypto providers (e.g., accidentally bundling authz-client with the main server) will silently select one without any visible warning, which can hide subtle and hard-to-diagnose cryptographic configuration errors.

title: New abstract method order() breaks binary/source compatibility for third-party CryptoProvider implementations
body: Adding a new non-default abstract method order() to the CryptoProvider interface is a breaking change for any third-party or external implementations of this interface (e.g. keycloak-client repo or other consumers) that are not updated to implement it. Since this is a public SPI interface loaded via ServiceLoader, this will cause compile and runtime failures for existing implementations until they add the method. Consider providing a default implementation to preserve backward compatibility.

title: Inconsistent resource lookup key for all-clients permission check
body: In hasPermission(String scope) the all-clients resource is looked up via resourceStore.findByName(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId()), while hasPermission(ClientModel, String) uses AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) to resolve the same 'all-clients' resource. Using two different lookup paths for what should be the same resource is fragile; if the resource type name differs from the resource name convention used elsewhere, this method will silently return false even when an all-clients permission exists, since it doesn't fall back to resolving via getResourceTypeResource like the other overload does.

title: No fallback when resource.getScopes() doesn't include the needed scope semantics
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), when the specific client resource exists, it is evaluated directly without checking whether an 'all-clients' permission could still grant extra permissions beyond what's modeled for the single resource (e.g. a MANAGE permission on all-clients should also grant VIEW/CONFIGURE even if the specific client resource only has a narrower permission). This differs from canManage()/canView() combos elsewhere that explicitly call multiple canX() methods for transitive scope checks, but hasPermission by itself does not combine both the specific-resource and all-resource evaluations, potentially under-granting access when both exist with different scopes.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns resource names, not client IDs for 'all-clients' pseudo-resource
body: getClientsWithPermission iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) and adds resource.getName() to the granted set. This will also include the pseudo resource named after CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE itself (the 'all-clients' resource), which is not an actual client ID. Callers treating the returned set as a list of real client IDs could get a bogus entry equal to the resource type name, causing invalid downstream behavior (e.g. attempting to look up a client with id 'Clients').

title: resourceStore.findByName uses client.getId() instead of client name consistently with getOrCreateResource
body: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) looks up `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`, relying on the resource name being the client's ID. This matches AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource's resolveClient which stores the client's internal id as resource name, so it's consistent, but there's no safeguard/comment establishing that invariant; if resolveClient's resolution logic changes (e.g., returns clientId string instead of internal id) this lookup silently breaks, always returning false and denying all permissions, which is a hard-to-detect data integrity bug.

title: hasPermission(String scope) does not fallback to resource-type resource consistently
body: In hasPermission(String scope), `resourceStore.findByName(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId())` looks up the 'all clients' resource directly by name equal to the resource type constant ('Clients'), while hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) uses `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` to fetch it. These are two different code paths for retrieving the same conceptual resource; if the two diverge (e.g., schema changes resource naming logic), the all-clients scope checks in canManage()/canManageClientScopes() will silently stop working while per-client checks continue to work, causing inconsistent permission evaluation.

title: Potential NPE if resource-type resource doesn't exist
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, scope), if `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` returns null (e.g., schema not initialized, or admin-permissions client never had init() run), the subsequent call `authz.getStoreFactore().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)` with a null resource may throw an NPE rather than gracefully returning false, causing an unhandled server error instead of a controlled permission denial.

title: getScope performs unchecked map access for unsupported resourceType
body: In getScope(), `SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType)` is called without null-checking the result before calling `.getScopes()`. If resourceType is null or not present (e.g., CLIENTS newly introduced but caller passes mismatched/legacy type), this throws a NullPointerException instead of the intended ModelValidationException, resulting in an unclear 500 error for callers instead of a controlled 400.

title: hasPermission(String) looks up resource with swapped name/id arguments, likely always failing
body: In `hasPermission(String scope)`, `resourceStore.findByName(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId())` passes the resource server's id as the owner argument. Compare with `getOrCreateResource`/`hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` which use `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())` differently, and with `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource` which does a plain `findByName(resourceServer, type.getType())` without an owner. If the `findByName(ResourceServer, String name, String owner)` overload actually requires the resource owner (not server id) to match the stored resource's owner, this lookup can fail to find the all-clients resource (created with `resourceServer.getClientId()` as owner in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource`), causing `canManageClientScopes()`/`canView(ClientScopeModel)` to always return false even when an all-clients permission exists. This diverges from the correct pattern used elsewhere (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource`), and should use the same consistent lookup rather than owner=server.getId().

title: Mismatched resource lookup key in hasPermission(ClientModel, String) vs. resource creation
body: `hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)` looks up `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`, using the client's internal id as resource name. But resources for individual clients are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` using `name = resolveClient(session, id)` which resolves to `client.getId()` as well, so this should match — however the owner parameter passed is `server.getId()` whereas resources are created with owner `resourceServer.getClientId()` (see `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())`). If `server.getId()` differs from `resourceServer.getClientId()` (likely, since one is the resource-server's internal id, the other is the owning client's id), this lookup will never find existing per-client resources, breaking the per-client manage/view/configure checks and effectively relying only on the all-clients fallback path.

title: Potential NPE when all-clients resource type is not yet created
body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when the per-client resource is not found, the code calls `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` which can return null (e.g., if resource type resource was never created, or `supportsAuthorizationSchema` returns false). The result is then passed directly into `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)` without a null check, risking an NPE instead of gracefully returning false.

title: Changing RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE breaks documented/scripted exit codes
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3, and FEATURE_DISABLED now uses 4. This changes the exit code contract documented in update-compatibility.adoc and relied on by external scripts/CI pipelines. Since this is a preview feature it may be acceptable, but it's a breaking behavior change not called out in the PR description, and any existing automation written against the old codes (recreate=4) will silently misinterpret results after upgrade.

title: Exit code table doesn't match actual constant ordering
body: The table lists exit code 3 for 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible' (recreate) and 4 for feature disabled, which matches the new code, but no mention is made of the previous value 4 for recreate in old docs/version compatibility notes, risking confusion for users following older guides or automation across releases during the preview window.

title: Changing RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE breaks documented/established exit code contract
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3, and FEATURE_DISABLED was introduced as 4. This changes the exit code semantics for the `check` command. Any external scripts or CI/CD pipelines built against the previous exit code mapping (4 = recreate required) will now behave incorrectly, interpreting 'feature disabled' as 'recreate needed' or vice versa. Since this tool is explicitly documented for scripting purposes, exit code changes are a backward-incompatible break and should be called out prominently in release notes, not silently remapped during a preview-stage PR.

title: Exit code table lists code 4 for feature disabled but doesn't mention 3 was reused for recreate
body: The doc table now lists exit code 3 for 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible' (recreate) and 4 for feature disabled. This is consistent with the new CompatibilityResult constants, but the PR silently changed the recreate exit code from 4 to 3 without highlighting this as a breaking change to consumers relying on the previous mapping documented in earlier releases.

title: Feature flag only enabled when updateStrategy is non-null
body: In createInitialDeployment, the ROLLING_UPDATES feature is only enabled inside the `if (updateStrategy == null) return kc;` early-return branch skips feature enabling entirely for the null case. Since the operator now requires rolling-updates feature to be enabled for the new update behavior (per docs), the null-strategy test path never enables the feature, meaning testImageChange/testCacheMaxCount with null strategy test the default/disabled-feature behavior only, potentially masking regressions in the new feature-gated behavior for the default case.

title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3, breaking existing contract
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was previously 4 and is now changed to 3, while FEATURE_DISABLED takes the old value 4. Any existing scripts or documentation relying on exit code 4 meaning 'recreate upgrade needed' will now get incorrect behavior (3 now means recreate, 4 means feature disabled). This is a breaking change to a documented exit-code contract for a preview feature; it should be called out explicitly as a behavior change, and existing automation relying on these codes could silently misinterpret results.

title: Exit code 4 documented inconsistently with CompatibilityResult
body: The doc states exit code 4 means 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature rolling-updates is disabled,' which matches the new FEATURE_DISABLED=4, but combined with the exit-code renumbering (RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3) there is a risk of confusion for readers of older docs/version metadata who might have cached the previous exit-code meaning. The PR should clarify this is a breaking change in exit codes for the preview feature.

title: Removed grantIfNoPermission fallback changes semantics for canQuery/canView ordering
body: canQuery() now calls root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.QUERY_USERS) || canView() instead of previously checking canView() first then QUERY_USERS role; order change is harmless for boolean OR, but note canManageDefault/canViewDefault helper methods used by canManageByGroup/canViewByGroup chains across GroupPermissions were removed/inlined without an accompanying check that all V1 fallback call sites (e.g., RolePermissions.canMapRole) still behave identically. Given RolePermissions.canMapRole previously called root.users().canManageDefault() and now calls root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS) directly, any custom logic inside canManageDefault() beyond the role check (if present in other code paths or overridden in subclasses) is now bypassed. This refactor should be verified for all previous callers of the removed canManageDefault/canViewDefault helpers to ensure no behavior regressed, especially for V1 class hierarchies that might have relied on virtual dispatch of these methods.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission only checks root.users().canView(), ignoring canManage()
body: Previously (per the diff), the old getGroupsWithViewPermission() method checked both canView() and canManage() of root.users() before returning empty set. The new getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() only checks root.users().canView(). This means an admin with only manage permission on users (but not explicit view) will now have groups incorrectly filtered/computed, which could result in incorrect scoping or performance overhead from needlessly computing group IDs when the admin should already have full access via manage permission.

title: searchForUser no longer checks canView() before computing/filtering groupIds, double filtering removed
body: The old code wrapped the groupIds lookup in `if (!auth.users().canView())`, avoiding unnecessary computation of group IDs for admins who can already view all users, and separately filtered the stream with `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`. The new code unconditionally computes `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (which internally checks canView() so it's not functionally broken) and removes the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` on the stream from `searchForUserStream`, instead relying solely on `toRepresentation`'s filter. This refactor is likely fine functionally, but removing the direct filtering here is a behavior-sensitive change that should be covered by tests ensuring per-user permission filtering still works correctly when group-based attribute injection (UserModel.GROUPS session attribute) is used with searchForUserStream, since the underlying store query uses the GROUPS session attribute for filtering, and if that store-level filtering has gaps, results could leak un-permitted users without an additional in-memory filter safety net.

title: canManage(UserModel) role check changed from ADMIN+MANAGE_USERS to only MANAGE_USERS
body: The diff removes AdminRoles.ADMIN from the hasOneAdminRole() check in canView(UserModel) and canManage(UserModel). This could change authorization behavior for callers previously granted access via the generic ADMIN role; if ADMIN role holders are expected to always have access, this is a regression that should be confirmed as intentional (schema cleanup) and covered by a test.

title: canQuery no longer grants fallback for group-scoped view access
body: canQuery() now is `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.QUERY_USERS) || canView()`, but canView() only returns true for global view/manage roles or hasPermission at the Users resource level; it does not account for per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions. Previously an admin who can only view users of specific groups (via requireQuery in UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource) might have been allowed to query based on group-scoped access, and is now blocked. This changes the admin's ability to list/search users they otherwise have group-scoped visibility into - search endpoints call requireQuery() before falling back to group-restricted search, so such admins would get a 403 instead of a filtered result set.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource.getId() names inconsistent with resource naming scheme (V1)
body: In V1 GroupPermissions, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() strips the 'group.resource.' prefix off resource.getName() to produce a group id, consistent with getGroupResourceName(). This is fine for V1, but GroupPermissionsV2 (new file) instead adds groupResource.getId() (the resource's internal ID, not the group ID) to the granted set in its getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(). Since resources for V2 groups are created/named by group ID directly (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returning group.getId() as resource name), using resource.getId() instead of resource.getName() will return wrong values (internal resource UUIDs instead of actual group IDs), breaking downstream usages like UsersResource.searchForUser() and getUsersCount() that expect group IDs to filter users by UserModel.GROUPS attribute.

title: Group resource name uses group ID, not stable identifier semantics inconsistent with user resource naming
body: resolveGroup returns group.getId() similarly to resolveUser returning user.getId(), but getResourceName() special-cases USERS to map resource.getName() to username while GROUPS has no equivalent branch, so getResourceName for group resources will just return resource.getDisplayName() (likely the raw group id) instead of a human-readable group name. This leaves the UI/representation showing the group id rather than the group name, inconsistent with the Users resource type behavior added in the same change.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission adds resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, resourceStore.findByType is used to iterate resources of type GROUPS, and granted.add(groupResource.getId()) adds the *resource* ID, not the group's model ID. Unlike GroupPermissions (V1) which strips the RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX off the resource name to recover the group ID, V2 resources are created with resource name == group ID (per AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup), so resource.getId() is the authorization resource's internal ID, not the group ID. This will return a set of resource IDs that callers (e.g. UsersResource, session.users().getUsersCount(realm, groupIds)) expect to be actual group IDs, causing user/group filtering based on group membership to silently fail (return no users or wrong set).

title: canList() role check narrowed, removing VIEW_USERS/MANAGE_USERS short-circuit note
body: canList() was changed to `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.QUERY_GROUPS) || canView()`. canView() internally checks MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS roles so behavior is preserved, but the diff removed explicit AdminRoles.VIEW_USERS/MANAGE_USERS from the role check in canList and now solely relies on canView() which, in GroupPermissionsV2, performs an authorization policy evaluation hitting the store (hasPermission) even for simple admin-role checks. This introduces extra avoidable policy evaluation overhead on every list check versus the previous hasOneAdminRole short-circuit covering more roles directly.

title: grantIfNoPermission logic changed without accounting for group-based filtering correctly
body: toRepresentation() calls usersEvaluator.grantIfNoPermission(session.getAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS) != null) to decide whether canView() should default-grant when there's no explicit permission setup. Previously the group attribute was only set when `!auth.users().canView()`; now it's set whenever groupIds is non-empty regardless of whether the user already has full view permission. This changes grantIfNoPermission's effective semantics subtly (session attribute set even when user canView() is true), which could cause unintended default-grant behavior in edge cases depending on how canView()/grantIfNoPermission interact across requests using the same session.

title: English reference file lookup is fragile and may throw unhandled exceptions
body: `verifySafeHtml` derives the English reference file path by naively doing `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. If a path contains "resources-community" multiple times, or the filename pattern doesn't match (e.g. en file itself, or a locale name containing unexpected characters), this can produce an incorrect path. More importantly, if the computed `englishFile` doesn't exist (e.g. missing en counterpart for a given theme/module), `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` throws FileNotFoundException, which is wrapped as an unchecked `RuntimeException` propagated out of `verify()`, which only declares `MojoExecutionException`. This will crash the whole build for any file without a matching English counterpart rather than reporting a soft validation failure.

title: santizeAnchors uses replaceFirst on whole string potentially matching wrong occurrence
body: `santizeAnchors` iterates anchor tags found via the matcher, but calls `value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` against the *original* `value` string on each loop iteration, not the updated local variable's position context. If the same anchor tag string appears multiple times in `value`, repeated calls to `replaceFirst` with the same pattern will always remove the first occurrence, never advancing past already-processed matches, potentially stripping the wrong occurrence or looping incorrectly relative to `matcher`'s cursor (which continues scanning the original `value`, not the mutated one), causing find/replace to get out of sync and produce incorrect sanitized results or false positive 'anchor mismatch' messages.

title: normalizeValue hardcodes key-specific exceptions reducing maintainability/generality
body: normalizeValue special-cases specific keys ("templateHelp", "optimizeLookupHelp", keys starting with "linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit", or "error-invalid-multivalued-size") directly in the verifier logic instead of deriving these exceptions from data/config. Any new translation key introducing legitimate special syntax (e.g., new choice-format messages or generic placeholders resembling HTML tags) will trigger false-positive 'Illegal HTML' failures until the verifier code itself is updated, creating ongoing maintenance burden tied to translation content changes rather than to code changes.

title: verify() swallows RuntimeExceptions raised deep in verifySafeHtml without proper MojoExecutionException wrapping
body: `verify()` catches only `IOException` around `verifySafeHtml()`, but `verifySafeHtml()` internally throws unchecked `RuntimeException` (for FileNotFoundException-like issues) rather than IOException. These RuntimeExceptions will propagate uncaught out of `verify()`, breaking the stated `throws MojoExecutionException` contract and potentially causing an unhandled build failure with a less helpful stack trace instead of a clean MojoExecutionException.

title: English file path lookup fails for different theme bases (login/account/admin/email)
body: englishFile is computed by regex-replacing the locale suffix in the current file's absolute path, assuming the English file lives in the exact same directory with the same basename structure. For files under resources-community vs resources, and across different theme categories (account/login/admin/email), this heuristic may not reliably resolve to the actual English source file if directory layouts differ, silently falling back to empty string on exception, masking real validation issues since englishValue becomes "" and HTML in translations would then be verified against the strict POLICY_NO_HTML even when the English source legitimately contains HTML.

title: verify() swallows exceptions from verifySafeHtml as RuntimeException, not reported as validation messages
body: verifySafeHtml() throws RuntimeException (not caught) when the matching English file cannot be opened (e.g., FileNotFoundException wrapped), causing the whole verify() call to crash with an unchecked exception instead of being reported as a validation message or at least a graceful failure. This could crash the build in unexpected ways for any properties file whose matching English file path can't be resolved (e.g., for files that don't have a direct English equivalent at the predictable path), rather than failing with a clear verifier message.

title: santizeAnchors mutates matcher position asymmetrically causing potential false positives/negatives
body: santizeAnchors matches anchor tags in value with Matcher.find() in a loop, but calls value.replaceFirst() inside the loop which does not update the matcher's underlying input, so subsequent find() calls continue to scan the original (unmodified) value string, not the updated one. If value contains multiple anchors, this can produce incorrect pairing between value's anchors and englishValue's anchors, leading to incorrect 'Didn't find anchor tag' messages or missed detections.

title: normalizeValue special-casing by key name is fragile and incomplete
body: The sanitizer special-cases specific keys like "templateHelp", "optimizeLookupHelp", and key prefixes like "linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit" or "error-invalid-multivalued-size" to strip out patterns resembling HTML tags (e.g. '<NAME>', '<Extensions>', MessageFormat choice patterns). This is a maintenance burden: any new translation key containing legitimate '<' usage (e.g. other MessageFormat choice patterns, generic placeholders) not in this hardcoded list will trigger false-positive 'Illegal HTML' errors, as seen already needing special handling for multiple distinct keys across different locale files in this PR.

title: English reference file path derivation is fragile and may fail silently
body: englishFile is computed via two regex replaceAll calls on the absolute path ("resources-community"→"resources" and locale suffix→"_en.properties"). This assumes a specific directory naming convention and will break (or silently point to a nonexistent/incorrect file) for any theme file whose path doesn't match these exact substrings, e.g. files already under "resources" (not "resources-community") where the first replaceAll is a no-op but still works, but any renamed/variant theme directories or files with unexpected naming (e.g. containing "resources-community" as part of another word) would silently produce a wrong path. There's no validation that englishFile exists; the FileInputStream will throw a plain IOException wrapped in RuntimeException, which is harder to diagnose than a clear error referencing the actual theme/key being checked.

title: verifySafeHtml does not handle missing or malformed properties files gracefully
body: verifySafeHtml wraps IOExceptions from reading `file` and `englishFile` in unchecked RuntimeException and lets them propagate out of verify(), while verify() itself only declares/catches MojoExecutionException for the Files.readString call. This means the exception types mismatch: verifyNoDuplicateKeys errors are handled via MojoExecutionException while verifySafeHtml errors escape as RuntimeException, producing inconsistent error handling/reporting behavior for the Maven plugin (likely results in a raw stack trace rather than a clean message during the build).
