This skips setting `notifications_changed_at` / `notifications_reason_id`, and skips the `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... })` call that other sessions/tabs rely on to update the UI live. The result is inconsistent bookkeeping and stale notification icons in any other open browser tab/session for the same user.

title: Per-topic unsubscribe mutates state on a plain, login-gated GET request
body: Unlike the existing digest unsubscribe flow (`email/unsubscribe/:key`, backed by `DigestUnsubscribeKey`) which works without an active login session via a signed token, this new `unsubscribe` action requires `ensure_logged_in` and performs the notification-level mutation synchronously on a GET request tied to the user's session cookie. This both breaks the "click unsubscribe from any device/mail client" use case the digest flow supports, and is a state-changing GET endpoint driven purely by session cookies, which is a classic CSRF-prone pattern (an embedded image/link while the victim is logged in elsewhere in the same browser would silently flip their notification level).

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url but builder doesn't guarantee it's present
body: The `unsubscribe_link` locale string was changed to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}` (config/locales/server.en.yml). `html_part` (line 67) and `body` (line 90) call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true, but `unsubscribe_url` is an optional opt with no default/fallback. Only `send_notification_email` in `user_notifications.rb` was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`; any other current or future caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will hit `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to build the email entirely.

title: Template location likely mismatches the route/controller naming convention
body: The route is registered as a top-level route `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', {...})` in app-route-map.js.es6 (not nested inside the `topic` resource), and its controller/view are named `topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` (flat, dasherized). By Ember's naming convention this route resolves its template as `topic-unsubscribe` (flat), not the nested path `topic/unsubscribe` used here. Other nested routes in this codebase (e.g. `topic.fromParams`) use the `topic/...` template path precisely because they are declared inside `this.resource('topic', ...)`. Since `topicUnsubscribe` is not nested, placing the template at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` will likely fail to resolve, leaving the route's outlet blank at runtime.

title: Misspelled computed property name "stopNotificiationsText"
body: The property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (missing an "a", should be "Notifications"). It is functionally consistent with its one use in the template, so it isn't a runtime bug, but the typo will confuse future maintainers searching the codebase and should be fixed before merge.

title: No test coverage added for the new unsubscribe controller/model behavior
body: This PR adds substantial new server-side behavior (`TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `Topic#unsubscribe_url`) but the only test change is adding an `unsubscribe_url` opt to an existing MessageBuilder spec. There is no controller spec exercising `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (including the nil-TopicUser case, the slug-redirect branch, or the notification-level toggle logic), and no spec verifying `Topic#unsubscribe_url`. Given the nil-TopicUser crash risk identified elsewhere in this review, test coverage for this action would have caught the bug before merge.

title: Unsubscribe action crashes when no TopicUser row exists
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil, e.g. if the logged-in user navigates directly to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` for a topic they have never visited/been notified about (no TopicUser record has been created for that pair yet). The very next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass`, producing an unhandled 500 error instead of creating/updating the preference (e.g. via the existing `TopicUser.change` helper, which already handles record creation).

title: Unsubscribe mutates notification state via a GET request with no CSRF protection
body: The `unsubscribe` action calls `tu.save!` to change the user's topic notification level, but it is only reachable via GET (`skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]` and `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in config/routes.rb). Rails' CSRF protection does not cover GET requests, so any authenticated user whose browser loads this URL as a side effect (e.g. an `` embedded on another page, a link preview/prefetch by an email client, or a security scanner following links) will have their topic subscription silently changed without consent. State-mutating actions should not be exposed as unprotected GET endpoints.

title: Unsubscribe copy overstates the effect for watching/tracking users
body: When the user's current notification_level is above `regular` (e.g. `watching` or `tracking`), the action only downgrades them to `regular` rather than muting (lines 107-111), but the user-facing text shown immediately after (`topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` in config/locales/client.en.yml: "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>") and the equivalent copy in the email (`unsubscribe_link` in config/locales/server.en.yml) both unconditionally claim all notifications for the topic will stop. A user who was `watching`/`tracking` and is merely downgraded to `regular` can still receive notifications for direct replies/mentions, contradicting what they were told.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url, risking MissingInterpolationArgument for other callers
body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` i18n string was changed to require a new `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation value. `Email::MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` (lib/email/message_builder.rb) call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is truthy, regardless of whether `unsubscribe_url` was supplied. Only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated in this PR to pass `unsubscribe_url`; any other existing or future caller of `build_email`/`MessageBuilder` with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but without `unsubscribe_url` will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to send, where previously the same call worked fine.

title: No automated test coverage for the new unsubscribe feature
body: The PR introduces a security-sensitive controller action (`TopicsController#unsubscribe`), a new model method (`Topic#unsubscribe_url`), and a breaking change to the `unsubscribe_link` translation contract, but adds no controller or model specs covering: a successful unsubscribe for a `regular`-level user, the downgrade behaviour for `watching`/`tracking` users, the slug-mismatch redirect, or the case where no TopicUser row yet exists. The only spec touched here just adds `unsubscribe_url` to an existing MessageBuilder test's options without asserting that the value is actually rendered into the body/html output, or exercising the case where `add_unsubscribe_link` is true but `unsubscribe_url` is missing.

title: Typo in computed property name stopNotificiationsText
body: The computed property is misspelled `stopNotificiationsText` (should be `stopNotificationsText`). It still works because the template at app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs references the same misspelled name, but the typo makes the binding hard to discover via search and is a latent trap: fixing the spelling in only one of the two files later will silently break the unsubscribe page's message.

title: PR description gives no information about the feature
body: The PR description is just "Test 2", with no explanation of the new unsubscribe feature's behavior (including the watching/tracking-to-regular downgrade semantics), rationale, or what was tested, despite the change spanning 18 files including routes, mailer templates, and a new user-facing flow. This makes it hard for reviewers and future maintainers to understand intent or verify completeness.

title: unsubscribe action crashes when no TopicUser record exists
body: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil for any logged-in user who can see the topic but has never had a TopicUser row created for it (e.g. never visited it and never received an email about it, since TopicUser is normally created lazily). The very next line calls `tu.notification_level` with no nil check, which raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil`, producing a 500 error for any such request (e.g. someone directly navigating to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe for a topic they haven't interacted with).

title: Notification-level mutation performed as a side effect of a plain GET request, with no idempotency or CSRF protection
body: The new `unsubscribe` action (routed via GET in config/routes.rb lines 440-441) mutates `TopicUser#notification_level` directly inside a GET request handler, with no confirmation step and no CSRF protection (GET requests are not covered by Rails' CSRF token checks). Because the action is keyed off the logged-in session (current_user) rather than a signed one-time token (unlike the existing key-based `email/unsubscribe/:key` route), any page that causes the user's browser to issue a GET to this URL while they are logged in (e.g. an tag, link prefetching, or an email security scanner following the link) can silently change their notification settings. Additionally, the mutation is not idempotent: every visit to the same URL re-evaluates `tu.notification_level > regular` using the *current* (already mutated) value, so repeated visits (page refresh, back/forward navigation, duplicate email link clicks, or automated re-fetching) progressively downgrade watching/tracking -> regular -> muted, fully muting the topic after just two visits even though the user only intended a single click.

title: Direct TopicUser save bypasses the canonical TopicUser.change path
body: The new action mutates `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly instead of using `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`, which is the method used everywhere else in the codebase (e.g. TopicsController#set_notifications) for this kind of update. This bypasses: setting `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id`, publishing the `/topic/#{topic_id}` MessageBus event (so any other open tab/browser showing the topic will not reflect the new notification state in real time), and the `observe_after_save_callbacks_for` hook (e.g. UserActionObserver). This creates an inconsistent code path for notification-level changes and a real-time UI sync gap.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now silently requires an unsubscribe_url interpolation value
body: `config/locales/server.en.yml`'s `unsubscribe_link` key now contains `%{unsubscribe_url}`, which `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` (used in both `html_part` at line 67 and `body` at line 90) will try to interpolate. `template_args` only contains `:unsubscribe_url` if the caller of `build_email`/`MessageBuilder.new` passed it in `opts`. Currently only `send_notification_email` in user_notifications.rb supplies it alongside `add_unsubscribe_link: true`, but this is an implicit, unenforced contract: any other current or future caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` at email-build time, breaking that notification email entirely.

title: "stop_notifications" message is inaccurate when the user was watching/tracking the topic
body: The text "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>" is shown unconditionally by the unsubscribe page/controller, but the backend logic in TopicsController#unsubscribe (lines 107-111) only sets notification_level to `muted` when it was already `regular` or below; if the user was `tracking` or `watching`, it is merely downgraded to `regular`, which still generates notifications for mentions/replies. The displayed copy therefore overstates the actual effect for a large class of users (anyone above 'regular'), who will continue to receive some notifications despite being told they will 'stop receiving notifications'.

title: Typo in computed property name 'stopNotificiationsText'
body: The property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (extra 'i', missing proper spelling of 'Notifications') instead of `stopNotificationsText`. It is referenced consistently with the same typo in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs line 3, so it works, but the misspelling makes the code harder to find/search/maintain and looks unprofessional in a user-facing feature.

title: No controller spec coverage for the new unsubscribe action
body: The new TopicsController#unsubscribe action introduces non-trivial logic (slug-mismatch redirect, JSON vs HTML handling, toggling notification_level based on current state, and a dependency on an existing TopicUser row) but no corresponding spec file changes are included in this PR (no updates to spec/controllers/topics_controller_spec.rb). Given the nil-TopicUser crash risk and the notification-level toggling logic described above, this feature ships without any automated regression protection.

title: No assertion that the new unsubscribe_url renders in the email body/html_part
body: The test was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to `Email::MessageBuilder.new`, but none of the existing assertions check that this value actually appears in `message_with_unsubscribe.body` or `html_part` output. The only existing assertion still just checks for `user_preferences_url`. This leaves the new per-topic unsubscribe link functionality (the actual feature of this PR) without direct test coverage, and would not catch the `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` risk described above if `unsubscribe_url` were ever omitted by a caller.

title: No test added for new Topic#unsubscribe_url helper
body: The new `unsubscribe_url` method on Topic (returning `"#{url}/unsubscribe"`) has no accompanying unit test verifying its output format, despite being a new public API used both by the mailer and the controller's redirect logic.

title: Case-sensitive exact-match lookup lets blocked users bypass the block by changing email case
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` does `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`, a case-sensitive exact string match (Postgres `=` is case sensitive by default), and the model's `uniqueness: true` validation on `email` is likewise case-sensitive. Since nothing normalizes/downcases the email before storing a BlockedEmail row or before looking it up, an admin blocking `spammer@example.com` will fail to catch the exact same address submitted as `Spammer@Example.com` or `SPAMMER@EXAMPLE.COM`. This defeats the entire purpose of the feature with a trivial, common bypass (most mail providers treat the local part/domain case-insensitively).

title: Validator persists DB writes as a side effect, and is invoked twice (or more) per signup, inflating block statistics
body: `validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, which increments `match_count` and sets `last_match_at` and saves the row every time it's called. Validations are not guaranteed to run only once: in `UsersController#create` (app/controllers/users_controller.rb) `user.valid?` is called explicitly and then `user.save` runs validations again internally, so for a single signup attempt against a blocked email the counters get incremented twice. Additionally, any other code path that calls `user.valid?` without actually persisting the user (e.g. checks, previews, specs) will silently write to the `blocked_emails` table and skew `match_count`/`last_match_at`, even though no real signup attempt occurred. Validators should not have unconditional persistent side effects like this.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write race on match_count
body: `should_block?` reads `record.match_count`, increments it in Ruby, then calls `record.save`. Concurrent requests that match the same blocked email (a realistic scenario for automated spam signups hitting the same address) can read the same starting value and overwrite each other's increments, silently losing count updates (classic lost-update race). This should use an atomic SQL increment (e.g. `update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?", ...)` or `increment_counter`) instead of read-then-save.

title: No tests added for new `errors`/`values` response fields or blocked-email rejection flow
body: The `create` action now returns `errors: user.errors.to_hash` and `values: user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")` on failed signup, which the JS controller depends on to populate `rejectedEmails`. No controller/request spec is added or updated to verify this new response shape, nor is there an integration test exercising the end-to-end scenario of signing up with a blocked email and getting the expected error payload. This is a meaningful behavior/contract change with no regression coverage.

title: Whitelist/blacklist domain validation logic moved out of User but has no test coverage in the new spec
body: The domain-restriction logic (`email_domains_whitelist`/`email_domains_blacklist`) was moved from `User#email_validator` into `EmailValidator`, but `email_validator_spec.rb` only exercises the new `BlockedEmail.should_block?` branch (lines 9-21). There is no test in this new spec verifying the whitelist/blacklist behavior that was relocated, so a regression in that moved logic (e.g. wrong attribute/value being validated) could go unnoticed if the previous coverage (if any) wasn't preserved elsewhere.

title: rejectedEmails default array literal is a shared prototype property across controller instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined as a plain array literal directly on the `Ember.Controller.extend()` definition rather than created per-instance (e.g. via `init()` or a computed property). In Ember's object model, array/object literal defaults declared this way are shared across all instances of the class unless explicitly reset in `init`. If more than one instance of `CreateAccountController` is ever created (e.g., in tests, or if the controller is not a true singleton), mutations via `pushObject` will leak between instances/sessions, causing stale 'rejected' emails to persist incorrectly across unrelated signup attempts.

title: should_block? mutates and persists match stats as a side effect of validation, causing double counting
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, and saves the record every time it is called. It is invoked from `EmailValidator#validate_each` (lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13), which runs as part of `User` validations. `UsersController#create` (app/controllers/users_controller.rb:168) explicitly calls `user.valid?` before calling `user.save` (line 172), and `save` internally re-runs validations. Because `email_changed?` is true for a brand-new unsaved user both times, validations (and therefore the BlockedEmail side effect) run twice for every single sign-up attempt against a blocked address, so `match_count` is incremented twice (and `last_match_at` recomputed twice) per attempt, corrupting the very statistics this feature is meant to track. The side effect is also persisted outside of the `User` save/transaction (validations run before the AR save transaction begins), so the counters are updated even if the `User` save subsequently fails, or if `valid?` is called anywhere else (forms, specs, console) without ever creating a user.

title: Non-atomic match_count increment risks lost updates under concurrent requests
body: `record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = Time.zone.now; record.save` reads the counter into memory and writes it back without any locking or atomic SQL update. If two sign-up attempts for the same blocked email happen concurrently (a realistic scenario for exactly the kind of repeated spam/bot signups this feature targets), both requests can read the same starting value and each save overwrites the other's increment, silently losing hits/undercounting match_count. This should use an atomic update such as `update_counters`, `increment!`, or a raw SQL `match_count = match_count + 1`.

title: Blocked email lookup and uniqueness are case-sensitive, allowing the block to be bypassed by case variation
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` and the `validates :email, presence: true, uniqueness: true` on line 5 do no case normalization. Elsewhere in the app, email comparisons are explicitly case-normalized (e.g. `UsersController#change_email` uses `Email.downcase`), but `BlockedEmail` does not. As a result, an admin who blocks "Spammer@EXAMPLE.com" will fail to block a sign-up using "spammer@example.com" (or any other casing variant), defeating the purpose of the feature. It also permits multiple rows for the same logical address differing only in case, since the uniqueness check is case-sensitive by default.

title: rejectedEmails default array literal is shared across controller instances and never reset
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` assigns a single array object as the default value directly on the controller definition instead of creating a fresh array per instance (e.g. via `init`). In Ember, object/array literals used as defaults this way are shared by reference across every instance created from the same class/mixin definition rather than instantiated per object — a well known Ember pitfall. Because the array is also never cleared anywhere (no reset on modal open/close or `init`), once an email is pushed into `rejectedEmails` it stays rejected for the lifetime of that shared array object. If the "Create Account" controller is ever recreated (e.g. the modal reopened, or in a shared/kiosk browser session), a previously rejected email — even from an unrelated earlier attempt, or one that the server would no longer reject (e.g. an admin unblocked it) — will continue to be permanently flagged invalid client-side with no way to retry short of a full page reload.

title: Domain whitelist/blacklist validation behavior has no test coverage after being moved into EmailValidator
body: The domain-restriction logic (`email_in_restriction_setting?` plus the whitelist/blacklist branches) was moved out of `User` (previously `email_validator`/`email_in_restriction_setting?`, deleted from app/models/user.rb in this PR) into `lib/validators/email_validator.rb`. The new spec file only covers the new "blocked email" branch via `BlockedEmail.should_block?` and adds no example for `SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist`/`email_domains_blacklist` behavior, so this pre-existing, non-trivial logic is left untested after the refactor. Additionally, any prior spec that exercised the now-removed `User#email_validator`/`User#email_in_restriction_setting?` methods directly would fail since those methods no longer exist on `User`.

title: action_type column has no DB default or range validation, relying only on an app-level callback
body: The `action_type` column is declared `null: false` with no database default, and the only place a default is applied is the `before_validation :set_defaults` callback in app/models/blocked_email.rb (lines 21-23), which only runs through ActiveRecord's validation path. There is also no validation constraining `action_type` to the two defined enum values (`actions[:block]`/`actions[:do_nothing]`). The spec file's own comment ("If we manually load the table with some emails...") suggests bulk/manual loading is an expected use case; such inserts bypassing ActiveRecord callbacks would violate the NOT NULL constraint unless `action_type` is explicitly supplied, and any out-of-range value stored would silently be treated as "do nothing" by `should_block?`'s equality check rather than raising an error.

title: BlockedEmail match_count/last_match_at are double-counted per signup attempt
body: In UsersController#create, `user.valid?` is called explicitly (line 168) and then `user.save` is called again a few lines later (line 172). Rails reruns all validations on every call to valid?/save, so the new EmailValidator (and therefore BlockedEmail.should_block?, which mutates and saves the matched BlockedEmail row) executes twice per request. This means `match_count` is incremented by 2 instead of 1 and `last_match_at`/the extra `BlockedEmail` lookup+save happen twice for every single signup attempt (not just discourse-hub flows, since `user.valid?` is evaluated unconditionally due to `&&` short-circuit order). This corrupts the statistics the feature is meant to produce and doubles the DB load added by this feature on every signup.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, allowing trivial bypass
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` performs an exact, case-sensitive string match against the stored email. Since email addresses are effectively case-insensitive, a spammer whose address was blocked (e.g. `spam@example.com`) can bypass the block entirely simply by submitting `Spam@Example.com` or any other casing variant. This defeats the purpose of the feature. The whitelist/blacklist domain check in lib/validators/email_validator.rb uses a case-insensitive regex, but the new block-list lookup does not normalize case at all.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write race on match_count
body: should_block? loads the BlockedEmail row, increments `match_count` in Ruby, then calls `save`. Two concurrent signup requests for the same blocked email can both read the same `match_count` value before either writes back, so one increment is silently lost (classic lost-update race). The statistic is also not updated atomically with respect to `last_match_at`. This should use an atomic DB update (e.g. `update_counters`, `increment!`, or a raw SQL `UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1`) instead of a load-then-save round trip.

title: rejectedEmails array is a shared mutable default shared across controller instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is declared as a plain property value in `.extend()`, so this exact array object is evaluated once at class-definition time and shared by the prototype. `createAccount` later calls `pushObject` on it (line 275), mutating the shared array in place. Any new instance of CreateAccountController created later (e.g. if the modal controller is re-instantiated) will see emails rejected by a completely unrelated prior session/instance, incorrectly failing emailValidation for emails that were never rejected for that instance. The array should be initialized per-instance in an `init()` hook instead of as a literal default value.

title: No end-to-end test for blocked-email signup rejection or new response fields
body: The create action now returns `errors` and `values` fields on failure specifically to support the new client-side rejectedEmails tracking, and signups are expected to be rejected when the submitted email matches a BlockedEmail record. There is no request/controller spec asserting that POST /users with a blocked email is rejected and that the JSON response includes the `errors`/`values` keys the JS controller depends on. Only the isolated EmailValidator and BlockedEmail model specs exist, so the full integration path (controller -> User#valid? -> EmailValidator -> BlockedEmail) is untested.

title: EmailValidator spec omits whitelist/blacklist coverage removed from User model
body: The domain whitelist/blacklist validation logic previously lived in User#email_validator/email_in_restriction_setting? and is now moved into EmailValidator (lib/validators/email_validator.rb), but this new spec file only exercises the 'blocked email' branch. There is no test verifying `email_domains_whitelist`/`email_domains_blacklist` behavior still works correctly after being relocated out of user.rb, leaving that previously-tested logic without direct validator-level coverage.

title: New rejectedEmails client logic has no test coverage
body: The new rejectedEmails tracking in emailValidation (lines 69-74) and the pushObject call in createAccount (lines 274-276) introduce new client-visible behavior that gates form submission, but no JS unit test was added to verify that a rejected email correctly fails emailValidation/submitDisabled or that successful resubmission with a different email clears the failure.

title: Invalid Ruby `end if` breaks the embed view template
body: Line 6 contains `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. The bare `if` with no condition is a syntax error: counting the if/each blocks in this file, there are 4 opening block keywords (the `if` at line 2, the orphan `if` created by `end if`, the `if` at line 11, and the `each do` at line 12) but only 3 `end` tokens total in the whole file (lines 6, 22, 29). This means the template will fail to compile with a Ruby SyntaxError (missing `end`), so every request to `EmbedController#best` that reaches a found topic will raise an error instead of rendering, breaking the entire embed feature that this PR introduces.

title: cook_method raw_html bypasses all HTML sanitization for RSS-imported content
body: `Post#cook` returns `raw` unmodified when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, skipping `PrettyText`/`post_analyzer.cook` entirely. `TopicEmbed.import` (used directly by `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`) always uses this cook method, but unlike `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (which runs content through Readability's whitelist of tags/attributes), the RSS/feed path passes feed item content straight through (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) with no tag or attribute whitelist at all. Since `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders this with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, any script/markup present in a polled RSS/Atom feed item is stored and rendered verbatim, enabling stored XSS for anyone who can influence the configured feed's content.

title: Unescaped URL interpolated into href attribute enables markup/attribute injection
body: `contents << "...#{url}..."` inserts `url` directly into an HTML attribute without escaping. `url` is only validated with `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` (anchors the start only; arbitrary characters, including single quotes, are allowed afterward) and can originate from end-user input (the `embed_url` controller param is passed through `TopicRetriever`/`TopicEmbed.import_remote` into this method) or from a polled feed item link. A URL containing a single quote (e.g. `http://host/'onmouseover='alert(1)`) breaks out of the `href='...'` attribute and injects an arbitrary attribute/markup. Because the resulting post uses `cook_method: raw_html` (which bypasses sanitization, see Post#cook) and is rendered with `raw`, this is exploitable stored HTML/JS injection.

title: Check-then-create race on embed_url can raise an unhandled unique-constraint error
body: `TopicEmbed.import` reads `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`, and if blank, later calls `TopicEmbed.create!` inside the same `Topic.transaction`. There is a unique index on `embed_url` (see the `create_topic_embeds` migration), so two concurrent calls for the same not-yet-imported URL will race: both see `embed.blank?` as true, both create a Topic/Post, and the second `create!` raises an unhandled DB uniqueness error which rolls back that transaction. This can realistically happen because `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttling is bypassed entirely for staff users (`no_throttle: true` from `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`), and concurrent `PollFeed` runs/imports of the same item are also possible, leaving an unhandled exception surfacing from the job.

title: Full RSS feed poll triggered synchronously for every unresolved embed request
body: When `feed_polling_enabled?` is true, `perform_retrieve` synchronously executes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` — fetching and parsing the entire configured feed and importing every item — any time a user requests an embed for a URL that is not yet in `topic_embeds`, even if that URL has nothing to do with the feed. The per-URL throttle in `retrieved_recently?` only limits repeated requests for the *same* embed_url; many distinct unknown URLs (or bursts of requests) will each trigger a full, redundant feed fetch with no rate limiting on the feed-poll operation itself, creating unnecessary load on both this server and the remote feed source.

title: feed_key is defined but never used
body: `feed_key` builds a Redis-style key based on a SHA1 of the feed URL, presumably intended for tracking feed modification state (e.g. to skip reprocessing an unchanged feed via conditional GET), but it is never referenced anywhere in `Jobs::PollFeed` or elsewhere. As written, every hourly run re-downloads and re-parses the entire feed and re-imports every item from scratch, which is wasted work; this looks like an incomplete feature left behind in the PR.

title: New gems added outside dual-boot conditional, but only one lockfile updated
body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` are added unconditionally in the Gemfile (lines 210-211), outside the `if rails4? ... else ... end` block, meaning they apply to both the Rails 3 and Rails 4 boot modes that this Gemfile's custom Bundler monkeypatch supports (via separate lockfiles, e.g. `Gemfile_rails4.lock` vs the default lockfile). Only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` is updated in this PR; the default (Rails 3) lockfile is not shown as updated. If Rails-3 mode is still used (e.g. CI or deployment with `RAILS3` set), `bundle install`/`bundle check` would fail because the Gemfile and its lockfile are out of sync.

title: Disqus import task silently drops category assignment and original timestamp
body: Previously, importing a Disqus thread created the topic with `category: category_id` (derived from the `-c/--category` option) and `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, preserving the original thread date and allowing categorization. This PR removes the `method_option :category` entirely and replaces the manual `PostCreator` call with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which has no way to specify a category or a custom `created_at`. Anyone invoking this thor task with `-c`/`--category` will now get a Thor "unknown option" error, and all imported Disqus threads will be timestamped at import time rather than their original creation date — an undocumented behavioral regression.

title: Prerequisite-setting tests don't isolate the condition under test
body: In "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username", only the setting under test is stubbed; `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is left at its real default (`false`, per `config/site_settings.yml`). Since `execute` short-circuits on `feed_polling_enabled?` first, both tests pass trivially regardless of whether the url/username checks work correctly — they would still pass even if those specific checks were removed from `execute`. The tests give false confidence and don't actually verify the url/username guard clauses.

title: Weak postMessage origin check using substring containment instead of equality
body: `postMessageReceived` validates the sender using `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, i.e. it checks whether `e.origin` appears anywhere as a substring of `discourseUrl`, rather than comparing the two for equality (or checking that `discourseUrl` starts with `e.origin`). This is a looser check than a proper origin comparison and can behave unexpectedly depending on how `discourseUrl` is configured (e.g. trailing path segments, protocol differences), weakening the intended protection against processing resize messages from untrusted origins.

title: absolutize_urls mishandles protocol-relative URLs
body: `absolutize_urls` treats any `href`/`src` starting with `/` as site-relative and rewrites it to `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`. For a protocol-relative URL like `//cdn.example.com/image.png`, `start_with?('/')` is true, and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both leading slashes, producing `cdn.example.com/image.png`, which then gets rewritten to `http://<originalhost>/cdn.example.com/image.png` — a broken URL pointing at the wrong host/path instead of the intended external resource. Any imported content (RSS or scraped article) using protocol-relative links/images will render broken links/images.

title: Controller spec never enables render_views, so the broken embed template is never exercised
body: This spec (and the rest of the test suite for this feature) never sets `render_views true`. RSpec controller specs default to stubbing out the view-rendering layer, so `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` — which contains an invalid `end if` that breaks compilation (see separate finding) — is never actually rendered by any test in this PR. This allowed a template that cannot compile to be merged without any test catching it.

title: force: true added to an already-existing migration; also added with an earlier timestamp than this PR's new migrations
body: This migration already existed prior to the PR and is modified here to add `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics`, which will silently drop the existing `top_topics` table (and any data in it) if the migration is ever re-applied against an environment where that table already exists. Additionally, the two new migrations added in this PR (`20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` and `20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb`) carry earlier timestamps than this already-existing migration (`20131223171005`), which is unusual ordering for newly added migrations and can cause confusion about intended apply order across environments.

title: Unsanitized raw HTML from imported content rendered directly in embed view
body: Posts imported via TopicEmbed.import use cook_method raw_html (see app/models/post.rb Post#cook), which causes Post#cook to simply `return raw` and skip PrettyText's sanitization pipeline entirely. That raw content (scraped via Readability from arbitrary remote URLs, or pulled from an RSS/Atom feed) is then rendered unescaped here with `raw post.cooked`. Any script tags or event handlers present in the source page/feed will execute inside the embed iframe (and via postMessage/window.parent access can potentially reach the embedding site). Since the content source is an external, non-Discourse-controlled URL/feed, this is a stored XSS vector that bypasses the normal content-safety pipeline used for all other posts.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match instead of exact comparison
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` rejects a message only if `e.origin` cannot be found anywhere inside `discourseUrl`. Because `indexOf` performs a substring search rather than an origin equality check, an attacker-controlled origin that is merely a prefix/substring of the real discourseUrl (e.g. `http://example.co` when discourseUrl is `http://example.com/`) will pass this check and be allowed to send `discourse-resize` messages that control the iframe's height, defeating the intended origin restriction.

title: Access control relies solely on the client-supplied Referer header
body: `ensure_embeddable` authorizes embedding purely by comparing `request.referer`'s host to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. The Referer header is fully attacker-controlled on non-browser requests (curl, scripts, server-to-server calls), so this check can be trivially bypassed to call `/embed/best`, triggering TopicEmbed/TopicRetriever logic (including outbound HTTP fetches) for arbitrary allowed hosts without ever being embedded on the real site. It also doesn't verify scheme, so http and https referers are treated identically.

title: X-Frame-Options value 'ALLOWALL' is not a standard directive
body: The X-Frame-Options header only defines DENY, SAMEORIGIN and ALLOW-FROM <uri> as valid values. 'ALLOWALL' is not part of the spec; some browsers may ignore the unrecognized value (making the header a no-op) while others could treat it conservatively and block framing, which would silently break the embed feature for some users/browsers. Omitting the header (the real intent here) would be the correct way to allow framing by any origin.

title: Outbound fetch of user-controlled embed_url has no scheme/SSRF restriction
body: `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` (Kernel#open from open-uri) on a URL that ultimately originates from the public, unauthenticated `embed_url` query parameter in EmbedController#best. The only restriction applied upstream (TopicRetriever#invalid_host?) checks that the URI's host matches SiteSetting.embeddable_host, but the scheme, port, and full path are attacker-controlled. This allows triggering server-side requests to arbitrary ports/paths on the configured host (SSRF), and relies on the Kernel#open/open-uri pattern which is also known to execute shell commands if the string begins with a pipe character — a defense-in-depth concern given this value flows from request params through two layers before reaching open().

title: Unhandled race condition on unique embed_url constraint
body: `TopicEmbed.import` checks `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and only creates a new TopicEmbed via `create!` if none exists. There's a unique index on embed_url (see db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb), but the check-then-create is not atomic. Two concurrent imports for the same URL (e.g. the hourly PollFeed job and a user-triggered RetrieveTopic job, which can itself invoke PollFeed synchronously — see lib/topic_retriever.rb) can both see `embed.blank?` as true and both attempt `TopicEmbed.create!`, causing one to raise an unhandled ActiveRecord error (RecordNotUnique/RecordInvalid) and crash the job instead of gracefully falling back to the update path.

title: TopicEmbed.import mutates the caller-supplied contents argument
body: `contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the string object passed in by the caller via the `<<` operator rather than creating a new string. This is a surprising side effect for callers that reuse the string afterward, and will raise a FrozenStringError if the caller passes a frozen string literal (e.g. under `# frozen_string_literal: true`), which is increasingly common in Ruby codebases.

title: Full feed poll executed synchronously and redundantly on every embed cache miss
body: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly and synchronously (bypassing Jobs.enqueue) whenever feed polling is enabled and the requested embed isn't found. This means every single unmatched embed request re-fetches and re-processes the *entire* configured RSS/Atom feed inline within the RetrieveTopic job, duplicating the work already done by the hourly scheduled PollFeed job. Under load (many simultaneous first-time embed requests), this can cause repeated, expensive network fetches of the whole feed and increases the window for the race condition described in TopicEmbed.import.

title: poll_feed assumes every feed item has a non-nil content field
body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls `.scrub` directly on `i.content` without checking for nil. Many RSS 2.0 feeds only populate `description` and not a `content`/`content:encoded` element, so SimpleRSS would return nil for `i.content`, causing a NoMethodError that aborts processing of the entire feed for that run (sidekiq_options retry: false means the job silently fails with no retry).

title: feed_key method is defined but never used
body: `feed_key` builds a Redis key intended to track feed modification state (e.g. for conditional GET / Last-Modified caching), but it is never referenced anywhere in poll_feed.rb or elsewhere in the diff. This looks like an incomplete feature: the feed is always fully fetched and fully re-processed on every hourly run with no change-detection short-circuit, which is wasteful for large feeds and puts unnecessary load on the external feed source.

title: Pre-existing migration modified to add force: true
body: This migration (dated 2013-12-23) already existed prior to this PR and is being edited to add `force: true` to `create_table`. Editing an already-committed migration changes its behavior depending on whether an environment has already run it: environments that ran the old version have a table without the force-drop semantics, while fresh environments running the edited version will drop-and-recreate on every migrate (or fail unexpectedly on table already existing in edge cases). The correct approach is a new migration if the table needs to be recreated, to keep migration history reproducible across all environments.

title: disqus.thor loses category assignment and original thread timestamp without replacement
body: The `--category`/`-c` method_option and the category-resolution logic were removed entirely, and the topic-creation call was switched from `PostCreator.new(user, title:, raw:, created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not accept a category or created_at. This silently drops two previously supported behaviors (assigning an imported thread to a category, and preserving the original Disqus thread's creation date for the topic's first post) with no replacement, which will surprise existing users of this import task.

title: No test coverage for referer-host mismatch rejection
body: The spec covers 'missing embeddable_host' and 'missing referer' failure cases, but never exercises the actual host-mismatch branch of `ensure_embeddable` (`URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), which is the core security check of the controller. A regression in that comparison (e.g. the substring/case-sensitivity issues noted elsewhere) would not be caught by this test suite.

title: poll_feed's core RSS-processing logic is untested
body: All tests in this file only verify the guard conditions in `execute` (feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url, embed_by_username) and stub out `poll_feed` itself. The actual `poll_feed` method — RSS/Atom parsing via SimpleRSS, URL fallback logic, and the `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` call that can raise on nil content — has no test coverage at all, so bugs such as the nil-content crash noted elsewhere would not be caught.

title: Transient 'loading' placeholder response is cached for 1 minute like the final content
body: `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied unconditionally regardless of whether the controller rendered the real topic view or the transient 'loading' placeholder (which itself auto-reloads client-side after 30 seconds, per app/views/embed/loading.html.erb). If this response is cached by any intermediary (browser cache, CDN), the client-side reload after 30s can be served the same stale cached 'loading' page for up to 60 seconds, delaying display of the actual content well past when it became available.

title: Invalid Ruby syntax `end if` breaks the embed view
body: The template closes the `if/else` block with `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. `end if` with no condition after `if` is not valid Ruby (the `if` keyword here has nothing to modify/condition on), so this template will raise a SyntaxError (wrapped in ActionView::Template::Error) whenever it is compiled/rendered. Since this view is rendered whenever `EmbedController#best` finds an existing `topic_id`, the core feature of this PR (showing embedded discourse comments) will 500 for every successful request. This should simply be `<%- end %>`.

title: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs
body: `absolutize_urls` treats any `href`/`src` starting with `/` as site-relative and rewrites it by stripping all leading slashes and prepending `prefix + "/"`. Protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/image.png` also start with `/`, so `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both leading slashes, turning the URL into `cdn.example.com/image.png`, which then becomes `prefix/cdn.example.com/image.png` (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/image.png`) — a broken link to the wrong host instead of the intended absolute external resource. This affects both the `a['href']` and `img['src']` rewriting blocks (lines ~62-73).

title: raw_html cook method bypasses sanitization for externally-sourced content
body: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim (skipping `PrettyText`/`post_analyzer.cook`) when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. This mode is used for all posts created via `TopicEmbed.import` (app/models/topic_embed.rb line 22), including content pulled from `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, which feeds raw RSS/Atom `content` (only `CGI.unescapeHTML`'d, never sanitized) directly into `TopicEmbed.import`. The resulting `cooked` value is later rendered unescaped via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb. If the configured feed (or a compromised/hijacked feed source) contains `<script>` or other malicious markup, it will be served verbatim to all visitors of the embed page, bypassing Discourse's normal HTML sanitization pipeline entirely — a stored XSS risk.

title: Race condition can raise unhandled uniqueness violation in TopicEmbed.import
body: When `embed.blank?` is true, a new Topic/Post/TopicEmbed is created. Two concurrent calls to `import` for the same new `embed_url` (e.g. two users hitting the embed controller at the same time before any embed exists) can both see `embed.blank? == true` and both attempt `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)`. The unique index on `embed_url` (migration 20131217174004) will reject the second insert, but there is no rescue for `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`/`StatementInvalid`, so the second caller's `TopicRetriever`/background job will raise an unhandled exception instead of gracefully reusing the already-created embed.

title: Disqus import tool silently drops the --category option
body: The previous implementation accepted `-c/--category` to assign imported Disqus threads to a specific category and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator.new`. The new implementation calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which has no way to specify a category, and the `method_option :category` declaration itself was removed. Any existing script or documentation relying on `thor disqus:import -c <category>` will now silently ignore the option (or error, since the option no longer exists), a backward-incompatible regression with no migration note.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match instead of exact comparison
body: `postMessageReceived` validates the message sender with `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`. This checks whether `e.origin` occurs anywhere inside `discourseUrl` rather than requiring an exact origin match. A malicious page whose origin happens to be a prefix (or other substring) of the configured `discourseUrl` string would pass this check and be able to send fake `discourse-resize` messages (and any future message types added to this handler) to the embedding page. The check should compare `e.origin` against the expected origin with strict equality rather than `indexOf`.

title: Feed item content assumed always present; no test for malformed/short items
body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every RSS/Atom item exposes a non-nil `content` (e.g. `content:encoded`). Plain RSS 2.0 feeds frequently only provide `description`, in which case `i.content` can be `nil`, causing `nil.scrub` to raise `NoMethodError` and fail the whole scheduled job (no items get imported, not just the bad one). There is no test exercising `poll_feed` itself (spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only tests the guard conditions in `execute`), so this failure mode is untested and unguarded.

title: Test does not stub TopicView.new's return value
body: `TopicEmbed.expects(:topic_id_for_embed).returns(123)` and `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` mock `TopicView.new` without a `.returns(...)`, so it returns `nil` by default. The controller then sets `@topic_view = nil` and implicitly renders `best.html.erb`, which calls `@topic_view.posts.present?` — this will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil`, so the subsequent `after` block assertion (`response.should be_success`) can never be reached; the test will error rather than pass/fail meaningfully, meaning the 'creates a topic view when a topic_id is found' path is not actually verified to render correctly.

title: Same cache duration applied to loading and completed states
body: `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is called unconditionally for both the "loading" (topic not yet retrieved) and "found" (topic_view rendered) branches. If any HTTP cache/CDN sits in front of this response, the "loading" page can be cached for up to a minute, so the client-side `document.location.reload()` in `loading.html.erb` (which fires every 30s) may keep receiving the stale cached loading page even after the topic has actually been imported, delaying the user from seeing the real content.

title: feed_key is computed but never used
body: `feed_key` builds a Redis key intended to track feed modification state (likely for conditional GET / avoiding reprocessing unchanged feeds), but it is never referenced anywhere in `poll_feed` or elsewhere in the job. As written, every hourly poll fully fetches and parses the entire feed and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for every item regardless of whether the feed has changed, which is unnecessary load on the external feed source; the dead `feed_key` method suggests this optimization was intended but not wired up.

title: Unused translation key `embed.permalink`
body: The new `embed.permalink: "Permalink"` string is added to the locale file but is never referenced by any of the new embed views or controller (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb`), making it dead i18n content left over from an unfinished feature.

title: `.contents .title { float: left; }` removed with no flex replacement
body: The diff removes the `.title { float: left; }` rule that previously positioned the site title/logo text inside `.d-header .contents`, while simultaneously turning `.contents` into a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`). No equivalent flex property (e.g. flex-basis, flex-shrink, min-width) was added for `.title`. Since `.title` becomes an un-constrained flex item, its sizing/wrapping behavior changes from the previous float-based layout with no verification that the new default flex-item behavior produces the same visual result, especially now that `.panel` is pushed to the far right via `margin-left: auto`. This risks the header title overlapping or being squeezed incorrectly on narrow viewports.

title: Leftover float-era margin-top conflicts with new flex align-items:center
body: `.login-button, button.sign-up-button` still use `float: left; margin-top: 7px;` (lines 42-47), which was presumably hand-tuned to vertically align the buttons when the header items were float-based. Now that the parent `.contents` is a flex container with `align-items: center` (lines 17-18), floats are ignored on flex items and the leftover `margin-top: 7px` will simply add extra space inside the already vertically-centered flex item, pushing the login/sign-up buttons lower than the other centered header elements (logo, icons, panel). This was not reconciled as part of the flexbox migration.

title: Removed `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` alignment fix without replacement
body: The previous `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper { &.bullet { margin-top: 5px; } }` rule provided a vertical-alignment correction specifically for the bullet-style category badge. This diff deletes that nested rule and replaces it only with `@include order(2); line-height: 1.5;` at the `.extra-info-wrapper` level, which does not address the same bullet-specific offset. This removes a previously necessary alignment fix without any compensating change, risking visual misalignment of bullet category badges in topic titles/suggested topics.

title: `order()` added to `.extra-info-wrapper` without confirmed flex parent
body: `@include order(2);` is added to `.extra-info-wrapper`, but the CSS `order` property only has an effect when the element's direct parent is a flex (or grid) container. Nothing in this file (or the diff) establishes that the actual DOM parent of `.extra-info-wrapper` has `display: flex` set. If the parent is not a flex container, this change is a no-op, meaning the ordering intent of the change may silently fail without any indication in the PR of where/if the parent flex context exists.

title: Undocumented spacing changes to `.small-action-desc` bundled into a 'header flexbox' PR
body: Beyond adding `@include flexbox()`/`@include align-items(center)` to `.small-action`, the diff also changes `.small-action-desc` padding from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`, drops its `margin-top: 5px`, changes `.custom-message p` margin from `5px 0` to `0`, and removes `> p { padding-top: 4px; }`. None of these spacing changes are explained in the PR description (which is just 'Test 5'), and they are unrelated to the stated purpose of optimizing header layout. These values directly affect spacing of topic timeline 'small action' notices (e.g. pinned/closed messages) and risk unintended overlap or cramped spacing between the avatar icon and description text, with no visual regression verification included.

title: PR title claims a performance optimization but changes are a layout/mixin refactor
body: The PR title states 'Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins', but the actual diff only introduces reusable flexbox mixins and swaps float-based layout for flexbox in several unrelated stylesheets (header, topic, topic-post, badges). There is no measurement, benchmark, or explanation showing any performance improvement; flexbox vs. float is not inherently a performance optimization for this static layout. Combined with the empty description ('Test 5'), this makes the rationale and scope of the change unclear to reviewers and future maintainers, especially given the changes span files unrelated to the header.

title: Float-based child layout breaks after parent becomes a flex container
body: .small-action is turned into a flex container (@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);) but its direct children .topic-avatar (line 270, float: left) and button (line 309, float: right) still rely on float for positioning. Per the CSS Flexbox spec, float has no effect on flex items (it is computed as none), so these declarations become dead code. In particular the action/dismiss button, which previously relied on float: right to sit at the far right of the row, now has no mechanism (no margin-left:auto, order, or justify-content) to stay right-aligned and will simply follow normal flex document order next to the description text. This is a visible layout regression, not merely a performance optimization.

title: Avatar offset padding replaced with percentage value that is inconsistent across widths
body: .small-action-desc previously used padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em (plus margin-top: 5px) to reserve a fixed left offset matching the floated 45px-wide .topic-avatar icon. It was changed to padding: 0 1.5% with the margin-top and the > p padding-top also removed. Since 1.5% is relative to the container width, the gap between the avatar icon and the description text will shrink or grow depending on viewport/container width instead of staying proportional to the fixed-size icon, and the removed vertical offsets likely alter text alignment versus the icon. No corresponding flex-basis/width was added to .topic-avatar to make this proportional spacing correct.

title: Removed bullet badge vertical-alignment fix without replacement
body: The previous rule `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` inside `.extra-info-wrapper` provided a specific vertical offset so bullet-style category badges aligned correctly with surrounding content. This sub-rule was deleted and replaced only with a generic `line-height: 1.5` on the parent, with no compensating offset for `.bullet` badges specifically. This risks a visual misalignment regression for topics that render bullet-style category badges inside `.extra-info-wrapper` (e.g. suggested topics list), and the PR provides no justification for dropping this targeted fix.

title: order() mixin added without establishing a flex parent
body: `@include order(2);` is added to `.extra-info-wrapper`, but the `order` property only has an effect when the element's parent has `display: flex`. Nothing in this file (or the diff) sets `#topic-title` or any ancestor of `.extra-info-wrapper` to `display: flex`. If the parent isn't a flex container (and none is introduced here), this declaration is dead code that gives a false impression the ordering is being controlled, while the actual rendering order is unaffected.

title: Right-alignment of .panel now depends on unverified DOM nesting under the new flex container
body: `.panel` previously used `float: right;` to self-position within `.d-header`. It was changed to `margin-left: auto;` plus `@include order(3);`, which only right-aligns the element if `.panel` is a direct flex-item child of `.contents` (the element that now has `display: flex`). Likewise `.title { float: left; }` was removed entirely. If the actual template markup does not make `.title` and `.panel` direct children of `.contents` (e.g. if there is an intermediate wrapper), both the left title and the right-aligned panel will lose their positioning entirely, since no float fallback remains. The PR does not demonstrate (via markup reference, screenshot, or test) that this structural assumption holds.

title: Non-existent vendor-prefixed property in align-items mixin
body: The `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` (line 121). This is not a property that Internet Explorer or any browser ever implemented (the correct and already-present IE10 flexbox alignment prefix is `-ms-flex-align`, on the preceding line). The `-ms-align-items` declaration is dead/invalid CSS that will be silently ignored by all browsers, adding no value and indicating the mixin wasn't verified against actual vendor-prefix requirements.

title: Float-based children lose intended layout once `.small-action` becomes a flex container
body: `.small-action` now has `@include flexbox();` (display:flex) added, but its children `.topic-avatar` (line 270, `float: left;`) and `button` (line 309, `float: right;`) still rely on CSS floats. Per the flexbox spec, float/clear have no effect on flex items, so these children become ordinary flex items laid out in document order (avatar, description, button) instead of being pushed to opposite edges as before. The dismiss/undo button that previously sat flush right via `float: right` will now simply follow the description text in the flex row, changing its visual position in every 'small action' post entry (e.g. 'topic closed by...') without any compensating `margin-left: auto` or `order` rule being added.

title: Unrelated spacing changes bundled into a 'flexbox mixin' PR without explanation
body: Alongside the stated goal of introducing flexbox mixins, this file also changes `.small-action-desc` padding from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%` (line 280), removes `margin-top: 5px` on the same rule, changes `.custom-message p` margin from `5px 0` to `0` (around line 292), and removes `padding-top: 4px` from `.small-action-desc > p` (previously present, now removed). These are independent visual/spacing regressions unrelated to adding flexbox mixins, with no rationale given in the PR description, making it hard to verify whether the removal of the left-padding offset (which compensated for the floated avatar icon width) still renders correctly for all 'small action' message variants.

title: Removed bullet-badge vertical offset without replacement, risking misalignment
body: The diff removes `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` from inside `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper` while only adding `@include order(2);` and `line-height: 1.5;` to the parent `.extra-info-wrapper`. This margin-top was presumably tuned to vertically align the bullet-style category badge (rendered with `inline-flex`/`align-items: baseline` in badges.css.scss) with surrounding text. Removing it with no compensating adjustment can reintroduce the vertical misalignment it was originally added to fix, and the change is unrelated to the stated purpose of adding flexbox mixins.

title: `.panel`'s new flex alignment (`margin-left:auto`, `order(3)`) only works if it is a direct child of the flex container `.contents`
body: `.panel` previously used `float: right;` to sit at the right edge of the header regardless of exact DOM nesting depth. It now relies on `margin-left: auto;` plus `@include order(3);` (lines 36-39), both of which only affect direct flex-item children of a flex container — here `.contents` (line 14-19), which is the only selector given `display:flex`. The SCSS itself declares `.panel` as a sibling rule under `.d-header`, not nested inside `.contents`, so whether this works depends entirely on the actual HTML template making `.panel` a direct child of the `.contents` element — something not verifiable from this diff and not covered by any test or screenshot. If that assumption is wrong, the panel (containing search/user menu/hamburger) will fall into normal block flow and break the header layout instead of being right-aligned.

title: PR title/description mischaracterizes the change as a 'performance optimization' with no supporting rationale
body: The PR title claims to 'Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins,' but the actual change only replaces/adds cross-browser vendor-prefixed flexbox declarations (display, align-items, order) and refactors some raw CSS into mixins; no performance measurement, profiling, or reasoning is provided to support a performance claim. Meanwhile, the PR description is just 'Test 5', giving reviewers no information about why several unrelated spacing/margin changes (header .panel/.title, topic small-action spacing, badge margins) were bundled in, nor any confirmation that visual regression/manual testing was performed across browsers for these cross-cutting CSS changes.

title: include_website_name is missing the required '?' suffix, so it is never invoked
body: The method `include_website_name` (lines 153-155) is meant to control whether `website_name` is serialized, based on `website.present?`. Every other conditional-inclusion method in this file follows the `include_<attr>?` naming convention (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_stats?`, `include_card_image_badge?`, `include_user_fields?`), which the serializer framework looks up by that exact name. Because this new method is named `include_website_name` without the trailing `?`, the framework never finds/calls it, so `website_name` is always serialized — even when the user has no website set, in which case it will be emitted as `null`. This silently breaks the intended 'only include when present' behavior and adds a useless field to every user payload.

title: website_name is not covered by the untrusted_attributes restriction that hides website for low-trust/anonymous viewers
body: The raw `website` attribute is passed to `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), which hides it from anonymous visitors viewing a TL0 user via `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. The new derived attribute `website_name` (added to the attributes list and implemented at line 137) is not added to this list, so it has no such restriction and is controlled only by the broken `include_website_name` check (see other finding). As a result, even when `website` is correctly hidden from a restricted viewer, `website_name` — which exposes the domain, and, when domains match, the full path derived from the same website value — is still serialized, leaking information that the `website` restriction was meant to hide.

title: untrusted_attributes test does not cover the new website_name attribute
body: The spec list at line 11 enumerates attributes expected to be hidden from anonymous TL0 viewers, but it was not updated to include `:website_name` even though this PR introduces that attribute as a direct derivative of the restricted `:website` field. Because of this omission, the existing 'doesn't serialize untrusted attributes' test does not catch that `website_name` is unconditionally serialized and bypasses the trust-level restriction applied to `website` (see related serializer findings).

title: Domain comparison in website_name is case-sensitive
body: In `website_name` (lines 137-151), `website_host` (parsed from the user-supplied `website` URL) is compared against `discourse_host` (`Discourse.current_hostname`) using plain string equality and `ends_with?` without normalizing case. Host names are case-insensitive, so a website entered as e.g. 'Example.com' when the instance hostname is 'example.com' (or vice versa) will fail to match even though the domains are effectively identical, causing the UI to show only the bare host instead of the intended full path.

title: `include_website_name` missing the `?` suffix breaks conditional inclusion
body: Every other manually-defined inclusion guard in this file follows the `include_#{attr}?` naming convention (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_card_image_badge_id?`, `include_card_image_badge?`, `include_suspend_reason?`), and the `untrusted_attributes`/`private_attributes` macros generate methods named with the trailing `?` as well. The newly added method is defined as `def include_website_name` (no `?`), so the serializer framework never calls it to decide whether to include the `website_name` attribute. As a result, `website_name` is unconditionally serialized for every user (even when `website` is blank, producing a `website_name: null` entry), instead of being gated by `website.present?` as intended.

title: `website_name` is not covered by the `website` untrusted-attribute restriction, leaking site info to low-trust/anonymous viewers
body: `:website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, which hides it from anonymous viewers of TL0 users via `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. The new derived field `website_name` (added at line 43/137) is computed from the same `website` data but is not included in that `untrusted_attributes` list, and its own gate (`include_website_name`, see separate finding) never checks `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. Consequently, even when the raw `website` value is correctly hidden for a restricted viewer, the derived `website_name` (hostname or hostname+path) is still exposed in the API response, leaking information the attribute list was designed to protect.

title: Untrusted-attribute test does not cover the new `website_name` field
body: The `untrusted_attributes` array used by the "with a TL0 user seen as anonymous" spec (`%i{bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background}`) was not updated to include `:website_name`. Since `website_name` is derived from the restricted `website` field but is not actually hidden for untrusted/anonymous viewers (see related bug in `user_serializer.rb`), this test gives false confidence that sensitive website data is properly hidden; it does not fail despite the leak.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' required by the serializer convention
body: Every other conditional attribute in this file follows the `include_#{attr}?` naming convention (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_card_image_badge_id?`, and the dynamically generated `include_#{attr}?` methods from `staff_attributes`/`private_attributes`/`untrusted_attributes`). The new method is defined as `def include_website_name` (no `?`), so the serializer will never find/call it as the inclusion-guard for the `website_name` attribute. As a result `website_name` is unconditionally included in the serialized output (even as `null` when `website` is blank), ignoring the intended `website.present?` gate. This also means any attempt to hide `website_name` based on trust-level/anonymous rules (see related finding) cannot work even if added, since the guard method itself is never invoked.

title: website_name leaks the restricted website attribute to untrusted/anonymous viewers
body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), which hides it from anonymous viewers when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (e.g. TL0 users). The new derived attribute `website_name` (lines 137-155) is computed directly from `website` via `object.user_profile.website` but is not added to `untrusted_attributes` and has no equivalent restriction check (its `include_website_name` method only checks `website.present?`, not the trust/anonymous restriction). Consequently, a TL0 user's website hostname (and sometimes the full host+path) will still be exposed to anonymous visitors even though the underlying `website` field is correctly hidden for them, defeating the existing privacy control.

title: No test verifying website_name is restricted for TL0/anonymous viewers like website
body: The 'with a TL0 user seen as anonymous' context (lines 6-16) asserts that `website` and other untrusted attributes are hidden, but does not include `website_name` in `untrusted_attributes` nor set a website on the fabricated user to actually exercise the check. This missing coverage allowed the access-control gap (website_name leaking despite website being restricted) and the broken `include_website_name` guard to go unnoticed.

title: Asymmetric subdomain matching logic in website_name
body: The matching logic handles the case where the Discourse host has an extra subdomain relative to the website host (e.g. website 'example.com' vs instance 'forums.example.com', tested in spec), via `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`. However the reverse case — the website host has an extra subdomain relative to a bare instance domain (e.g. website 'http://forum.example.com' vs instance host 'example.com') — is not handled: the `ends_with?` check is only performed in one direction, so this case falls through without expanding to the full path even though it represents the same underlying domain relationship. This asymmetry is untested and likely not intended given the feature's goal of detecting same-domain websites.

title: Mutating string literal with << instead of safe concatenation
body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses the mutating `<<` operator on the string literal `"."` rather than `+` or interpolation. This happens to work today because the file has no `# frozen_string_literal: true` magic comment, but it is fragile: if frozen string literals are enabled for this file in the future (a common Rails convention), this line will raise a `FrozenError` at runtime. It should use `".#{website_host}"` or `"." + website_host` instead.

title: Lightness value changed for light theme instead of just adding a dark-theme fallback
body: In `.topic-meta-data h5 a` (embedded-posts 'in reply to' link), the color was originally `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The refactor changed it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The first argument (used for the default/light theme) should have kept the original 30% lightness value (with 70% used for the $secondary/dark branch), but the values were swapped. This means the default light theme's link color changes unintentionally (becomes much lighter, reducing contrast), which is outside the stated scope of this PR (only adding dark-theme support via $secondary).

title: Group member name color lost its distinct lightness value, now identical to title
body: `.group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, distinguishing it from `.title`'s `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. After the refactor, `.name` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` — identical to `.title`'s new value. The light-theme lightness for `.name` was changed from 30% to 50% instead of being preserved, so the two elements that previously had different visual prominence now render with the same color in the default theme.

title: custom-message-length color values swapped, changing default theme appearance
body: `.custom-message-length` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The refactored line is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The first (light-theme) argument should have stayed at 70% (with 30% applied to $secondary for dark theme), but the values were swapped. As a result, the hint text under the custom-message textarea renders much darker/more prominent in the default light theme than it did before this change, which is an unintended visual regression not described by the PR's stated purpose.

title: topic-map h3 lost its distinct lightness value, collapsing heading hierarchy
body: `.topic-map h3` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` making it visually darker/more prominent than `h4` (`scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`). After the refactor it became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, identical to h4's value, instead of preserving 20% for light theme (and using 80% for $secondary in dark theme). This removes the intended visual hierarchy between the two headings in the default theme.

title: Group member name color lost its distinct lightness value, now identical to title (mobile)
body: Same issue as in desktop/user.scss: `.group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to differentiate it from `.title` (`scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`). The refactor changed `.name` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, matching `.title` exactly, instead of preserving the original 30% value for the light theme. This unintentionally removes the visual distinction between the group member's name and title in the default theme.

title: PR description provides no information about the change
body: The PR description is simply 'Test 7', giving reviewers and future maintainers no explanation of why `scale-color($primary, ...)` calls across 32 stylesheet files are being wrapped in `dark-light-choose(...)`, what visual regression or dark-theme bug this fixes, or how the replacement values were derived/verified. Given the number of files and the subtlety of the values involved (several of which were inconsistently applied, see other findings), a clear description and verification notes are needed to catch mistakes like the swapped lightness values found in this diff.

title: Category badge-notification count color not converted for dark theme
body: In `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification`, the color rule is still `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%);` and was not wrapped in `dark-light-choose(... , scale-color($secondary, ...))` like every other similar rule in this PR (e.g. the `th`, `td`, `.topic-excerpt`, `.top-date-string` and `div.education` rules a few lines above/below were all converted).
