As a result, in a dark theme this badge count text will keep using a lightened shade of the (dark) primary color, producing low-contrast/unreadable text against the dark background on the categories topic list, defeating the purpose of this PR for this specific element.

title: Light-mode lightness value changed unintentionally for .topic-meta-data h5 a
body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. After the change it became `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));` — the light-mode (first) argument's lightness was changed from 30% to 70%, not just extended with a dark-mode fallback. Every other converted rule in this PR preserves the original lightness for the primary/light-mode branch and uses `100 - lightness` for the secondary/dark branch (e.g. the `.arrow` rule right below correctly keeps 60%/40%). This mismatch changes the rendered color of the embedded-post topic title link in the default (light) theme, which is an unintended visual regression.

title: Light-mode lightness value changed unintentionally for .group-member-info .name
body: Originally `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. The PR changed it to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`, altering the light-mode lightness from 30% to 50% instead of preserving it (the pattern used everywhere else in this PR keeps the original value as the first argument and uses `100 - value` for the second). The sibling `.title` rule directly below (already 50%/50% before this PR) was left unchanged, suggesting its value was mistakenly duplicated into `.name`. This causes a visible, unintended color change for the member name text in the notifications panel under the default theme.

title: Light-mode lightness value changed unintentionally for .group-member-info .name (mobile)
body: Same issue as the desktop counterpart: originally `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`, now `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. The light-mode lightness was changed from 30% to 50% rather than being preserved while only adding the dark-theme fallback, producing an unintended color change on mobile for the group member name text in the default theme.

title: Light-mode lightness value swapped for .custom-message-length
body: Originally `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);`. The converted rule is `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));` — the light-mode and dark-mode lightness values appear swapped: the light-mode branch now uses 30% instead of the original 70%, while 70% was moved to the (wrong) secondary/dark branch. The desktop equivalent in `desktop/modal.scss` correctly keeps 70%/30%. This produces a visibly different (much darker) color for the custom-message-length hint text on mobile in the default theme, and also means the dark-theme fallback does not mirror the original value as intended elsewhere in this PR.

title: Light-mode lightness value changed unintentionally for .topic-map h3 (mobile)
body: Originally `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);`. The new rule is `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`, changing the light-mode lightness from 20% to 50%. The desktop equivalent (`desktop/topic-post.scss` `.topic-map h3`) was correctly converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`, preserving the original 20% value. This mobile/desktop inconsistency confirms the mobile value was altered by mistake, causing an unintended, more muted heading color for the topic-map section header on mobile in the default theme.

title: Lightness value swapped introduces unintended color change for light theme
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the color was previously `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Following the pattern used everywhere else in this PR, the first (light-theme) argument should preserve the original 30% lightness value (paired with secondary at 70%), i.e. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 30%), scale-color($secondary, 70%))`. Instead the primary lightness was changed to 70%, which changes the rendered color in the default/light theme (previously a darker 30%-lightness shade, now a much lighter 70%-lightness shade) — an unintended visual regression unrelated to the PR's stated purpose of only adding dark-theme support.

title: Lightness value changed (30% -> 50%) in .group-member-info .name, altering light-theme appearance
body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. To preserve the original light-theme look (consistent with the sibling `.title` rule which kept 50%/50% because it was originally 50%), this should have been `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 30%), scale-color($secondary, 70%))`. As written, the light theme's text color for this element changes from a darker 30%-lightness shade to a lighter 50%-lightness shade, which is an unrelated visual regression.

title: Lightness values swapped for .custom-message-length, darkening text in light theme
body: `.custom-message-length` previously used `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme (first) argument should retain the original 70% lightness (paired with 30% for secondary/dark-theme), i.e. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 70%), scale-color($secondary, 30%))`. As written, the light theme now renders this text with a much darker (30%) shade instead of the original lighter (70%) shade — a visual regression unrelated to dark-theme support.

title: Lightness value changed (20% -> 50%) for .topic-map h3, altering light-theme heading color
body: `.topic-map h3` previously used `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new code is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The sibling `.map .number, i` rule in the same file correctly kept its original 20% value and used 80% for the counterpart (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 20%), scale-color($secondary, 80%))`), showing the intended pattern. This h3 rule instead was changed to 50%/50%, meaning the light theme's heading color shifts from a dark 20%-lightness shade to a medium 50%-lightness shade, an unintended visual regression.

title: Lightness value changed (30% -> 50%) in .group-member-info .name, altering light-theme appearance (duplicate of desktop/user.scss issue)
body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` instead of the expected `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 30%), scale-color($secondary, 70%))`. This duplicates the same regression found in the desktop variant of this stylesheet: the light theme's text color changes from darker 30%-lightness to lighter 50%-lightness, an unintended side effect beyond the PR's stated scope.

title: Missed conversion: .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification color still uses raw scale-color($primary) without a dark-theme fallback
body: In `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification`, `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%);` was left unconverted, while every other occurrence of `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` in this same file (e.g. the `th`, `td`, `.topic-excerpt`, and `div.education` rules a few lines above/below) was updated to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 50%), scale-color($secondary, 50%))`. Because this instance was missed, the badge-notification text color inside category topic lists will still be computed purely from `$primary` and will not adapt for dark themes, defeating the purpose of this PR for this specific element and likely resulting in poor contrast/readability in dark themes.

title: add_members/remove_member require :group_id but the route only supplies :id
body: The routes added in config/routes.rb (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"`, lines 49-50) are declared directly inside the `resources :groups do ... end` block without being wrapped in an explicit `member do ... end` block or `on: :member`. Such bare declarations resolve to member routes using the resource's default id parameter, i.e. the URL becomes `/admin/groups/:id/members` with the captured param named `id`, not `group_id` (this matches the previous `get "users"` route it replaced, and matches the JS which builds the URL as `/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json'`, embedding the id directly in the path). However `add_members` (line 66) and `remove_member` (line 85) both call `params.require(:group_id)`. Since the real request will only populate `params[:id]`, every real HTTP call to these endpoints will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` (400) instead of succeeding, completely breaking the admin 'add members' / 'remove member' feature that this PR is supposed to deliver, even though it looks correct in isolation.

title: Controller specs bypass routing and mask the group_id/:id param mismatch
body: The specs for `.add_members` and `.remove_member` (e.g. `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, usernames: "l77t"` at line 94 and `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: group.id, user_id: user.id` at line 125) inject `group_id` straight into the controller action, bypassing the actual route path/param extraction defined in config/routes.rb. Because of this, the tests pass even though the real route (a bare member-style declaration generating `/admin/groups/:id/members`) would never populate `params[:group_id]` for an actual HTTP request. There is no request-spec/feature-level test that exercises the real route, so the production-breaking parameter mismatch described above is not caught by this test suite.

title: Public group members page now silently truncates to 50 members with no pagination UI
body: `members` previously returned the full, unpaginated list of users for non-automatic groups and only limited automatic groups to 200. This PR unconditionally applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` / `offset = params[:offset].to_i` to every group (lines 22-26), and `Discourse.Group#findMembers` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js) defaults `limit` to 50. The public-facing group members page (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` + `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`) was not given any next/previous controls (unlike the admin template, which did get pagination UI). As a result, any group (automatic or not) with more than 50 members will now show only the first 50 members on the public `/groups/:name/members` page with no way to see the rest, a functional regression compared to the previous behavior for non-automatic groups (which showed all members).

title: findMembers() failures are now silently swallowed
body: Previously `afterModel` returned the promise from `model.findMembers()`, so a failed request (e.g. network/server error) would reject the route's model hook and trigger Ember's normal error substate handling. Now `setupController` just calls `model.findMembers();` without returning or handling the resulting promise (same pattern in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6, lines 8-12). If the members request fails, there is no error feedback to the user and the member list simply stays empty/stale with no indication that something went wrong.

title: Username input is not cleared after adding members, and failures are unhandled
body: The `addMembers` action contains an acknowledged `// TODO: should clear the input` and calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))` without handling the returned promise's rejection. Similarly `removeMember` (lines 51-59) calls `self.get("model").removeMember(member)` without a `.catch`. If the add/remove request fails server-side (e.g. validation error), the admin gets no feedback and, for addMembers, the previously entered usernames remain in the input, which can lead to accidental duplicate submissions or user confusion. This should be resolved before merge rather than left as an open TODO.

title: Public group members endpoint now hard-caps all groups at 50 members with no pagination UI
body: Previously, only automatic groups were paginated (capped at 200), while manually-created groups returned the full member list unpaginated. The new `members` action applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` to every group regardless of type, and the public-facing template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` (and its route `group-members.js.es6`) never passes a custom limit nor offers any 'load more'/pagination controls (unlike the admin group page, which does have next/previous). As a result, any group (automatic or manual) with more than 50 members will silently show only the first 50 members on the public group page with no way for a user to see the rest — a data-completeness regression compared to the previous behavior for manual groups.

title: Off-by-one error in totalPages computation produces a phantom empty last page
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 members with the default limit of 50), this yields `floor(50/50)+1 = 2` instead of the correct value of 1. Combined with `currentPage` using the same `floor(...)+1` formula, clicking 'next' on the last real page will move to a non-existent page 2 of 2 that renders zero members, and `showingLast` will report false until the user is already past the real data. The formula should use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead.

title: removeMember/addMembers promises resolve before the member list refresh actually completes
body: In `removeMember` and `addMembers`, the `.then()` callback calls `self.findMembers();` but does not `return` it: `return Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { self.findMembers(); });`. Because the inner async call isn't returned, the outer promise resolves as soon as the delete/add request finishes, not after the member list reload (`findMembers`) completes. Any caller that chains off `removeMember()`/`addMembers()` to know when the UI data is fresh (current callers don't, but this is a latent bug) will get a false 'done' signal before `members`/`user_count` have actually been updated.

title: Unconditional group.save() after membership mutation can report an error after the change already persisted
body: `add_members` and `remove_member` call `group.add(user)` / `group.users.delete(user_id)` (which persist the membership change immediately via the join table), and then separately call `group.save` to decide the HTTP response. If `group.save` fails for any reason unrelated to membership (e.g. a validation on `name`/`alias_level` that happens to be in a bad state), the controller will return a 422 error even though the membership change already took effect in the database. The old `update_patch` code for incremental membership changes never checked `save` at all for this reason. This inconsistency between the reported result and actual persisted state can confuse the admin UI (which only calls `findMembers()` to refresh on success).

title: Breaking response-format change to /groups/:name/members.json has no accompanying test update
body: The `members` action's response shape changed from a plain serialized array to `{ members: [...], meta: { total, limit, offset } }`. This is a breaking change for any consumer of this JSON endpoint. No spec file for `GroupsController` is included in this PR's diff, so there is no verification that the new shape is correct, and any pre-existing spec asserting the old array format would now fail. The PR should add/update tests covering the new pagination metadata and format for this public endpoint.

title: Username input is not cleared after successfully adding members
body: The `addMembers` action contains `// TODO: should clear the input` and indeed never resets `this.get('usernames')` after a successful add. After adding members, the user-selector field retains the previously entered usernames, which can mislead the admin into re-submitting the same usernames or being confused about the current state of the input.

title: Route no longer waits for member data before rendering, losing loading-state guarantee
body: The previous implementation used `afterModel` to await `model.findMembers()` before `setupController` ran, guaranteeing the member list and pagination metadata (`user_count`, `limit`, `offset`) were populated before the template rendered. The new code calls `model.findMembers()` from `setupController` without returning/awaiting the promise, so navigating directly to (or refreshing) an existing group's admin page will briefly render with stale/default values (`user_count: 0`, `0/0` pagination, no members) before the async fetch resolves, instead of Ember's route loading state being used to mask this.

title: Off-by-one error in totalPages computation causes a phantom empty last page
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100 members with limit 50), this yields 3 instead of the correct 2 pages. Combined with the `next` action's offset calculation (`Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), a user can click 'next' from the real last page and land on an extra page whose offset equals `user_count`, which returns zero members from the server (since valid offsets are `0..user_count-1`). The pager will show e.g. 'Page 3/3' with no members listed, and `showingLast` never becomes true until this phantom page is reached. The correct formula should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

title: Breaking change to /groups/:id/members.json response shape and default page size
body: The `members` action used to return a plain serialized array for non-automatic groups (unbounded) and only paginated automatic groups at a default limit of 200. It now always returns a hash `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}` and defaults to a limit of 50 for every group, automatic or not. Any existing API consumer (mobile apps, external integrations, scripts) that expects the previous array response or expects to receive the full membership list for non-automatic groups will break or silently receive only the first 50 members with no indication that pagination occurred. This is a backward-incompatible API change that is not called out or versioned.

title: No upper bound on client-supplied limit and no validation of offset for /groups/:id/members.json
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are used directly in the query with no maximum cap or minimum validation. A client can request an arbitrarily large `limit` to retrieve an entire (potentially huge, e.g. 'everyone') group's membership in a single request, defeating the purpose of pagination and risking excessive serialization/DB load. A negative `offset` is also not guarded against, which can produce unexpected SQL (Postgres rejects negative OFFSET values), leading to a 500 error for malformed input on this public, non-admin endpoint.

title: Membership mutation is persisted before the subsequent save-based success/failure check
body: In `add_members`, `group.add(user)` is called in a loop (which persists the association immediately via the has_many collection), and only afterward is `group.save` checked to decide whether to render success or `render_json_error`. The same pattern exists in `remove_member` with `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `group.save`. If `group.save` fails for any unrelated reason (e.g. a validation on the group model), the membership change has already been committed to the database, yet the client is told the operation failed via `render_json_error`, producing an inconsistent/misleading response relative to the actual state of the data.

title: No spec coverage added for the rewritten /groups/:id/members pagination behavior
body: The `members` action was substantially rewritten: response shape changed to `{members:, meta:}`, pagination now applies uniformly to automatic and non-automatic groups, and the default limit changed from effectively unlimited (non-automatic) / 200 (automatic) to 50 for all groups. No corresponding spec file (e.g. groups_controller_spec.rb) was added or updated in this PR to verify the new `meta` payload, default/overridden limit and offset behavior, or the total count, leaving this behavior-changing rewrite untested.

title: addMembers/removeMember actions silently swallow AJAX failures
body: Unlike `save` and `destroy`, which attach failure handlers that show a `bootbox.alert` with the server error, the `removeMember` and `addMembers` actions call `this.get('model').removeMember(member)` / `addMembers(usernames)` without attaching any rejection handler. If the request fails (e.g. a 422 for an automatic group, or a network error), the promise rejection is unhandled and the admin receives no feedback that the action did not take effect. Additionally the `addMembers` action leaves a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment, meaning the username input is never cleared after a successful add, which can lead to accidental duplicate submissions.

title: Fallback locale preloading only happens on web requests, not in jobs/mailers/console
body: The new `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` call is only wired into `ApplicationController#set_locale`, which runs as a before_filter on controller actions. Background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, and console sessions that switch `I18n.locale` and translate text never trigger this preload step. Since `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb#translate` only lazily loads the *current* locale (not the fallback chain), and `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` performs lookups against whatever translations happen to already be loaded in memory, any fallback locale (site default locale or `:en`) that hasn't been separately loaded in that process context will simply be treated as having no translations, silently defeating the fallback feature outside of the request/response cycle. This makes the fallback feature incomplete for a large class of use cases (e.g. localized emails, job notifications).

title: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but ignores all Hash mutation semantics
body: `FallbackLocaleList` extends `Hash` yet overrides only `[]` to always recompute `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` on every call, ignoring any entries actually stored in the hash. Any code (current or future, including third-party plugins or admin tooling) that relies on the standard I18n fallback API to customize mappings (e.g. `I18n.fallbacks[:xx] = [:yy]`, `I18n.fallbacks.map(...)`) will silently have no effect, since `[]=`/`store`/`merge!` write into the underlying Hash storage that `[]` never reads from. This is a misleading API surface that can mask configuration bugs.

title: Custom fallback chain drops locale-tag hierarchy fallback (regional variants)
body: The previous Rails-provided `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` (enabled via `config.i18n.fallbacks = true`) resolves fallback chains based on locale tag structure (e.g. `zh-TW` -> `zh` -> default -> `en`). The replacement `FallbackLocaleList#[]` only returns `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`, with no intermediate base-language fallback. The TODO comment in the same file acknowledges this limitation but it represents an actual regression in translation coverage for locale variants that previously could fall back to their base language before hitting the site default or English.

title: No automated tests for the new fallback mechanism
body: This PR introduces a custom `FallbackLocaleList`, a new `I18n.ensure_loaded!`/`ensure_loaded!` preloading path, and changes to `set_locale`, but no specs verify that: (1) translations fall back correctly from user locale to site default locale to English, (2) `ensure_loaded!` actually loads the expected locale files, or (3) removing the environment-specific `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` settings and enabling fallbacks globally (now including development/test environments, where it previously was not enabled) doesn't change existing test expectations around missing/fallback translations. Given this is a behavior change that spans multiple environments and files, the lack of coverage is a notable gap.

title: Fallback-locale loading only wired into the controller request cycle
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only invoked from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any code path that sets `I18n.locale` outside of a web request (Sidekiq jobs, mailers rendering in a user's locale, rake tasks, console usage) never calls this method. Because `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` requires translation files to be explicitly loaded with `I18n.ensure_loaded!`/`load_locale` before lookups work, the fallback locales (site default locale, `:en`) will not be loaded in those contexts, so fallback translations will silently fail to resolve (returning nil/raising `I18n::MissingTranslationData`) even though the feature appears to work for normal page requests.

title: Fallback chain now depends on a DB/cache-backed SiteSetting instead of a static config value
body: The previous `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` approach relied only on `I18n.default_locale`, a static value available at boot. The new `FallbackLocaleList#[]` calls `SiteSetting.default_locale` on every fallback resolution, which requires the `site_settings` table/cache to be available. If any translation lookup occurs before migrations have run (fresh install, `rake db:migrate`, `assets:precompile` on a new deployment, etc.), this will raise a DB error where translation previously worked fine with the static fallback.

title: LRU translation cache is not invalidated when SiteSetting.default_locale changes
body: The cache key `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"` only accounts for the requested locale, not the locale a fallback translation actually came from. Since the fallback chain now depends on the mutable `SiteSetting.default_locale` (added in config/initializers/i18n.rb), changing that setting at runtime does not bust already-cached fallback results. Users/admins can keep seeing translations resolved under the old default locale until the 300-entry LRU naturally evicts those keys or the process restarts, producing stale/incorrect localized content.

title: No tests added for the new fallback behavior
body: This PR introduces a new `FallbackLocaleList` class, a new `I18n.ensure_loaded!`/`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` loading path, and changes `ApplicationController#set_locale`, but no spec files were added or updated to verify fallback ordering, lazy-loading of fallback locale files, or interaction with the LRU translation cache. This is user-facing localization behavior and should have test coverage before merging.

title: Fallback behavior is now enabled unconditionally in every environment
body: Previously `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` was only set in production, profile, and cloud66 production configs; development/test presumably ran without fallbacks. This new initializer enables `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` and the custom `FallbackLocaleList` for all environments, including test and development. This silently changes behavior so that missing translations in those environments now resolve to the default locale or English instead of raising, which can mask genuine missing-translation bugs during development and in the test suite.

title: Fallback chain locales are only pre-loaded in ApplicationController, not everywhere I18n.locale is used
body: `translate` (and `load_locale`) only loads translation files for `config.locale`, the single currently-active locale. Because `I18n::Backend::Base#load_translations` is patched (line ~25-29 of this file) to be a no-op unless called explicitly, any locale whose files were never explicitly loaded has zero translations in memory, even if the YAML file exists on disk. The new feature relies on `ApplicationController#set_locale` calling `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` to pre-load the whole fallback chain (locale, site default locale, :en) before rendering a web request. But any other code path that sets `I18n.locale` directly – Sidekiq jobs, mailers that iterate per-recipient locales, rake tasks, console sessions – never calls `ensure_loaded!`, so the middle fallback locale (the site default locale) is never loaded there. The fallback module will then raise MissingTranslationData for that un-loaded locale regardless of whether a real translation exists, and silently skip straight to `:en`. This defeats the purpose of the feature for exactly the code paths (background jobs, digest emails) where multi-locale translation matters most.

title: LRU translation cache can serve stale fallback results after SiteSetting.default_locale changes
body: The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`, which does not encode which locale a translation was actually resolved through in the fallback chain. With this PR, the fallback chain itself (`FallbackLocaleList#[]` in config/initializers/i18n.rb) depends on the mutable `SiteSetting.default_locale`. If an admin changes the site's default locale at runtime, previously cached entries for keys that were resolved via fallback to the old default locale will continue to be returned from the LRU cache (keyed only by key+locale+backend id) until the backend object changes or the process restarts/`I18n.reload!` is invoked. This produces incorrect, stale fallback translations for an indeterminate period after a site-setting change that used to have no bearing on translation caching before this PR (previously fallback only ever used the fixed `I18n.default_locale` config constant).

title: FallbackLocaleList silently ignores any explicit per-locale fallback configuration
body: `FallbackLocaleList` subclasses `Hash` but only overrides `#[]`, fully computing `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` regardless of hash contents. Standard mutator methods like `[]=`/`store`/`merge!` are still inherited unchanged, so any code (future plugin, console usage, or another part of the app) that tries to customize the fallback chain for a specific locale the normal `I18n.fallbacks` way (e.g. `I18n.fallbacks[:'pt-BR'] = [:pt]`, which works with the standard `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` Hash-like API) will silently write into the backing Hash but the write is never read back by `[]`. This breaks the expected Hash/fallbacks contract without any error or warning, which can be confusing and hard to debug later.

title: New fallback chain drops intermediate language-tag fallback, reducing translation coverage for regional locales
body: Previously, fallback was enabled via `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` (removed from config/environments/production.rb, profile.rb and the cloud66 config in this PR), which engages Rails/I18n's standard `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`, computing fallback through locale-tag decomposition (e.g. `:'zh-CN'` -> `:zh` -> default locale). The new `FallbackLocaleList#[]` only returns `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`, with no intermediate base-language step. For any regional locale where only the base-language YAML exists (e.g. only `client.zh.yml`, no `client.zh-CN.yml`), lookups that previously fell through to `:zh` will now jump straight from `:'zh-CN'` to the site default locale (often `:en`), losing already-translated strings. The code acknowledges this via a TODO comment but it is still a behavioral regression for users on region-specific locale codes.

title: No tests added for the new I18n fallback behavior
body: This PR introduces a new fallback resolution mechanism (`FallbackLocaleList`), a new `I18n.ensure_loaded!`/`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` loading path, and a behavior change in `ApplicationController#set_locale`, all of which materially change how translations resolve across the whole application. No spec covers that the fallback chain is `[locale, site default, :en]`, that `ensure_loaded!` actually loads the needed locale files, or that translations correctly fall back when a key is missing in the primary locale. Given the wide blast radius of i18n changes, the lack of any automated coverage is a notable gap.

title: Denial cache can reintroduce the exact staleness bug this PR is meant to fix
body: The new permission-denial cache (checked at lines 116-121 and populated at line 154) is consulted before the regular permission cache or any DB fallback, and has the same 30s TTL (shortCacheTTL) as the rest of the caches. Once a Check() call for a specific (namespace,user,action,name,parentFolder) combination is denied, every subsequent Check() for that exact resource short-circuits to `Allowed: false` for up to 30 seconds, with no invalidation hook tied to permission grants/role/team changes. If a user is denied access to a resource and is then granted access (e.g. shared a dashboard, added to a team, or the permission write for a just-created resource lands slightly after the first check), the user will continue to be denied for up to 30 seconds even though a fresh DB query would now return 'allowed'. This reproduces, for the negative-cache case, the same 'cannot access what I should now have access to' symptom that this PR is otherwise trying to fix by falling back to the DB on cache misses.

title: userPermDenialCacheKey is vulnerable to key collisions because its fields are joined with '_' without escaping
body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates action, name and parent with a plain '_' delimiter: `namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent`. Grafana dashboard/folder UIDs are allowed to contain underscores (UID validation permits [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+), so two different (action, name, parent) triples can produce the identical cache key string (e.g. action='A', name='B_C', parent='D' vs action='A_B', name='C', parent='D' both yield '..._A_B_C_D'). Because every denial-cache entry stores the same value (`true`), a collision causes a denial cached for one resource/action to be incorrectly served as a cached denial for a completely unrelated resource/action belonging to the same user, wrongly blocking access that was never actually evaluated, for up to the cache TTL.

title: New denial-cache test doesn't actually verify the denial-cache short-circuit
body: In TestService_CacheCheck's 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' subtest, the comment claims 'Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked', but the permCache entry is set to `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}` (an explicit false) rather than `true`. Since reading a missing key or an explicit false both yield `false` from a Go map, and `s.store`/`s.permissionStore`/`s.folderStore` are left as the default empty fakeStore (which returns no permissions and no folders without error), the test would still produce `Allowed: false` via the normal fallback path even if the permDenialCache short-circuit were broken or removed entirely. The test therefore provides no real coverage of the new denial-cache behavior it is supposed to validate.

title: Denial-cache hits and permission-cache hits are reported under the same metric labels
body: In Check(), both a denial-cache hit (line 118) and a positive permission-cache hit (around line 132) increment `s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("true", checkReq.Action)`. These are two distinct caches (permDenialCache vs permCache) with different semantics and TT悠L behavior, but the metric conflates them into a single 'cache hit' counter per action. This makes it impossible to measure the effectiveness/behavior of each cache independently from metrics, reducing the observability value that this feature is supposed to add.

title: List() does not get the same freshness fallback as Check(), so newly created/newly granted resources may still be missing from list results
body: Check() was changed so that when the cached permission map doesn't grant the specific requested resource, it falls back to a fresh DB query (fixing the 'can't access what I just created' bug for single-resource checks). List(), however, only distinguishes cache-hit vs cache-miss as a whole (lines 180-192): if `getCachedIdentityPermissions` returns any cached map at all, that stale map is used as-is to build the list, with no mechanism to detect that it is missing a newly created/newly granted item. As a result, a user who creates a dashboard/folder may be able to directly Check() access to it immediately (via the DB fallback), but the item can still be absent from List() results (e.g. folder/dashboard browse views) for up to shortCacheTTL (30s), partially undermining the stated goal of letting creators see resources they just created.

title: Removing the client-side cache entirely for in-proc mode increases per-check overhead
body: The in-proc AccessClient is now constructed with `authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{})` instead of a real local cache, meaning every single Check/List call from any in-proc caller must always traverse request validation, the in-proc gRPC channel/interceptor, and the server-side cache lookups, instead of being able to short-circuit via a cheap client-side memory lookup as before. For call patterns that issue many repeated/duplicate permission checks in quick succession (e.g. rendering a page that checks access on many individual items), this removes a previously-available fast path and could noticeably increase CPU/allocation overhead, even though the server-side caches still avoid the DB round-trip.

title: Permission-denial cache key collides across identity types sharing the same UID
body: `userPermDenialCacheKey(checkReq.Namespace.Value, checkReq.UserUID, checkReq.Action, checkReq.Name, checkReq.ParentFolder)` (defined in pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go) builds the cache key purely from the parsed subject UID, action, name and parent folder, without including the identity type. Anonymous subjects ("anonymous:0") and the render-service subject ("render:0") both resolve to UserUID=="0" (see the test file's own usage of these literal subjects), so a denial recorded for one identity type (e.g. render service denied on some action) will be returned for the other identity type (e.g. an anonymous user) on the next Check call for the same namespace/action/name/folder, even though their actual permission semantics (getRendererPermissions vs getAnonymousPermissions) are completely different and unrelated. Unlike the existing permCache which deliberately uses separate key schemes per identity type (userPermCacheKey vs anonymousPermCacheKey, and no caching at all for render), this new denial cache does not preserve that separation. The result is an incorrect deny being served to a different identity than the one it was computed for, causing availability/correctness regressions (legitimate requests incorrectly denied) that only clear once the 30s denial TTL expires.

title: "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" test doesn't actually exercise the override behavior it claims to test
body: In TestService_CacheCheck's "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" subtest, the comment says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but the code sets `s.permCache.Set(ctx, userPermCacheKey(...), map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false})` — i.e. it stores `false`, not `true`. Because the stored value is already `false`, `checkPermission` would return `allowed=false` from this cache entry on its own, and the subsequent default fakeStore (unset in this subtest) also returns no permissions, so the test would still pass (assert resp.Allowed == false) even if the new permDenialCache short-circuit logic were removed entirely. The test therefore does not actually validate that the denial cache takes precedence over a cached "allow" entry, which is the behavior it is meant to demonstrate. The permCache value should be set to `true` to make the test meaningful.

title: Per-resource cache miss now forces a full permissions DB requery on every mismatched Check call
body: Previously `getUserPermissions`/`getAnonymousPermissions` returned the cached permission map unconditionally whenever any entry existed for the user+action, regardless of whether it covered the requested resource, so a single cache entry served all Check calls for that action for the whole 30s TTL. Now, `Check` calls `getCachedIdentityPermissions` and, if the cached map doesn't contain the specific requested scope, always falls through to `getIdentityPermissions` which performs a full DB permissions query (deduplicated via singleflight only for truly concurrent calls). For workloads that call Check sequentially for many distinct resource names under the same action (e.g. authorizing each item of a list one at a time), every resource not already present in the cached scope map now triggers its own DB round trip, and is only protected from repeat DB hits via the new per-resource permDenialCache (keyed by name+parent) on subsequent identical calls. This can multiply DB load roughly proportional to the number of distinct resources checked, compared to the previous single-query-per-TTL-window behavior, and is not bounded/debounced beyond the exact (name, parent) tuple.

title: permissionCacheUsage metric mislabels a used-but-denying cache lookup as a cache miss
body: When `getCachedIdentityPermissions` returns a cached permission map (err == nil) but `checkPermission` evaluates it as not allowed, the code falls through to the line `s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", checkReq.Action).Inc()`, recording this as a cache miss even though the cache was actually read and used to make a (negative) decision before falling back to the DB. This mislabels cache effectiveness, making dashboards built on this metric appear to show a lower cache hit rate than what is actually happening, which could mislead capacity planning/alerting based on this metric.

title: Denial cache key can collide for different (action, name, parent) tuples
body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates action, name and parent with a plain '_' delimiter: namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent. Because dashboard/folder UIDs (name, parent) are allowed to contain underscores, two different tuples can produce the exact same string, e.g. (action="dashboards:read", name="a_b", parent="c") and (action="dashboards:read", name="a", parent="b_c") both yield "...perm_<uid>_dashboards:read_a_b_c". Since permDenialCache, permCache, idCache, etc. all share the same underlying cache.Cache instance (only key prefixes differ), this collision causes the cached 'denied' verdict for one resource to be incorrectly applied to a completely different resource/folder combination, producing wrong Check() results for up to the cache TTL.

title: New denial cache can re-introduce the exact bug this PR fixes via a create/permission-grant race
body: After a real (non-cached) permission check returns not-allowed, Check() unconditionally stores a 'deny' entry (s.permDenialCache.Set) keyed by namespace/user/action/name/parent, and this entry is consulted first on every subsequent Check() for up to shortCacheTTL (30s), short-circuiting before any DB lookup. If a user creates a resource and the authorization check races with the commit of the resource's permission grant (the exact scenario this PR intends to fix), the first Check() can observe no permission yet, be denied, and have that denial cached for 30 seconds — meaning the creator would be locked out of their own newly created dashboard/folder for up to 30 seconds even though permission is already correctly granted moments later. Previously (without this denial cache) each subsequent Check() would simply re-evaluate permissions and succeed as soon as the grant was committed.

title: Check() now performs a full permission re-fetch from DB whenever the cached permission map denies a specific resource
body: Previously, getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions checked permCache first and returned the cached scope map unconditionally (whether or not it granted the specific requested resource), so a single cached entry served unlimited Check() calls for any resource until TTL expiry. After this change, that internal cache check was removed from getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions; now, whenever getCachedIdentityPermissions finds a cached map but checkPermission against it returns false (resource not found in the cached scope map), Check() falls through and calls getIdentityPermissions again, which unconditionally re-queries permissionStore.GetUserPermissions from the DB. Only the new per-resource permDenialCache prevents repeating this for the exact same resource later. For workflows that call Check() once per resource across many distinct dashboards/folders a user cannot access, each first encounter with a new resource now triggers a full DB permission listing query instead of being resolved for free from the already-valid cached permission map, multiplying DB load compared to before.

title: Denial cache key uses unresolved subject id, inconsistent with other caches
body: userPermDenialCacheKey is built from checkReq.UserUID, which is the raw identifier parsed directly from the request subject (could be a numeric legacy ID or a UID depending on caller). All other per-user caches (idCache, permCache, teamCache, basicRoleCache) key on the canonical resolved UID obtained via GetUserIdentifiers. If the same user is referenced by different subject formats across calls (e.g. numeric ID in one call, UID in another), the denial cache entries will not be shared between them, reducing the cache's effectiveness and making its behavior inconsistent with the rest of the caching scheme.

title: permissionCacheUsage metric conflates two distinct caches and mislabels cache hits
body: The permissionCacheUsage metric is incremented with "true" both when the new permDenialCache short-circuits (line ~118) and when the permission cache actually grants access (line ~132), even though these are two separate caches with different semantics. Additionally, when getCachedIdentityPermissions returns a cached map but checkPermission determines the specific resource is not granted, the code unconditionally records permissionCacheUsage "false" (line 137) even though the permission cache was in fact consulted (just insufficient for this resource). This makes the metric unreliable for distinguishing actual cache-miss rates from 'cache hit but resource not covered' cases, undermining monitoring/alerting based on this metric.

title: No test exercises the write path of the new denial cache
body: TestService_CacheCheck's "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" test manually seeds s.permDenialCache and verifies that Check() reads it, but no test verifies that Check() actually populates permDenialCache after a genuine denial computed from the store (the new write at service.go's s.permDenialCache.Set call). The existing 'should deny user without permission' test in TestService_Check only checks the response value and never asserts that a subsequent call benefits from (or is affected by) the newly written denial cache entry, leaving this core new behavior without direct coverage.

title: Pause and Delete menu actions become unreachable for Grafana rules rendered by the new ruler-less list view
body: The Pause menu item (line 123) is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` is true, and the Delete menu item (line 165, `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}`) is only rendered when `rulerRule` is truthy. Both require an actual `RulerRuleDTO`. However, the new Grafana-only alert list rendering path (`GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` -> `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`) never supplies `rule`/`rulerRule` to `AlertRuleMenu` — it only passes `promRule` (a `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`), since this PR's goal is to stop fetching ruler data for this view. `canPause`/`canDelete` were updated to also become true from the new prom-based ability checks (`grafanaPauseAbility`/`grafanaDeleteAbility`), but the JSX gating conditions were not updated to match, so Pause and Delete will never render for rules shown in this view even when the user has full permissions. This silently removes two previously available actions from the alert list's dropdown menu. The regression is masked rather than caught by `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`'s 'should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked' test, which grants delete/update permissions yet asserts exactly 4 menu items (Silence, Copy link, Duplicate, Export) with no Delete or Pause entries.

title: Missing `key` prop on GrafanaRuleListItem breaks React list identity in the filtered rule list
body: In the `rules.map()` render loop, the `'datasource'` and `default` cases still pass `key={key}` to their returned elements, but the `'grafana'` case's `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` lost its `key` prop entirely (the previous implementation using `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../>` had it). This produces React 'missing key' warnings and risks incorrect component reuse/state across re-renders for Grafana rule items in this list, which is populated incrementally via infinite scroll (new batches pushed into `rules` state). The pre-computed unique key from `getRuleKey`/`getGrafanaRuleKey` should be applied here just like the sibling cases.

title: Rule view link no longer includes the `returnTo` query parameter
body: The view URL is built as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view')` without a `returnTo` parameter. The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx` built the equivalent link with `createRelativeUrl(path, { returnTo })` where `returnTo` came from `createReturnTo()`. Since this new component is used both by `FilterView.tsx` and `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` to render every Grafana rule link in the alert list, clicking through to a rule's detail/view page from the list now loses the information needed to return back to the originating list/filter, regressing the previous 'go back' navigation behavior.

title: Stale JSDoc still references the Ruler response this component no longer queries
body: The `expectedRulesCount` prop's doc comment states: "Ruler response might contain different number of rules, but in most cases what we get from Prometheus is fine", implying the component still cross-checks against a ruler response. This PR removes the `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` call entirely (the component now exclusively calls `useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery`), so the comment is now inaccurate and should be updated to avoid confusing future maintainers about the component's actual data sources.

title: Ability hooks are now invoked twice per rule regardless of relevance, doubling permission-check overhead
body: `AlertRuleMenu` now unconditionally calls both `useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule, groupIdentifier, [...])` (lines 57-64) and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(... , [...])` (lines 67-79) for every rendered rule, even though in the new ruler-less list view `rulerRule` is always `undefined` and the ruler-based branch is a no-op. Each of these aggregate hooks internally invokes several other hooks (`useIsRuleEditable`/`useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`, `useFolder`, `useCanSilence`/`useCanSilenceInFolder`, `useAlertingAbility`), so this roughly doubles the hook computation performed per rule row. Since existing comments in this codebase already flag that these ability hooks are 'called a lot... for ~80 rules' and this PR's stated purpose is to make the list scale better by removing extra requests, unconditionally evaluating both ability branches for every row works against that goal.

title: Missing `key` prop for Grafana rule items rendered in a list
body: In the `.map()` callback that renders `rules` (line 151), the `'datasource'` and `default` cases pass `key={key}` to the returned element, but the `'grafana'` case (lines 155-163) returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem .../>` without any `key` prop. This was present before this PR (the removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` had `key={key}`) and was dropped when switching to `GrafanaRuleListItem`. Since this list grows via infinite scroll/filtering (`setRules((rules) => rules.concat(...))`), missing keys cause React warnings and make React fall back to index-based reconciliation, which can cause incorrect component reuse/state bleed between rows (e.g. open menus, pause state) when the list changes. Add `key={key}` back to the `GrafanaRuleListItem` element.

title: Pause and Delete menu items never render when only `promRule` is supplied (new ruler-less list view)
body: The Pause item (line 123-125) is gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and the Delete item (lines 165-175) is gated on `rulerRule` being truthy. Both `canPause` and `canDelete` are now computed as an OR between the ruler-based ability and the new Grafana-prom-rule-based ability (lines 81-87), so these booleans can be `true` purely from the `promRule` permission check. However, in the new list view (`GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` -> `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`) only `promRule` is ever passed to this component; `rulerRule` is always `undefined`. As a result, Pause and Delete are computed as allowed but the menu items are unconditionally suppressed because they still require a `rulerRule` reference (`MenuItemPauseRule` needs the full rule body, and `handleDelete` is typed to take a `RulerRuleDTO`). Users browsing the new Grafana-managed alert list therefore lose the ability to pause or delete rules from the row menu, with no indication why, even though the ability checks say it should be allowed. This is also implicitly confirmed by the new test in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx which asserts exactly 4 menu items (silence, copy link, duplicate, export) with no delete/pause.

title: `returnTo` query param dropped from the rule view link
body: The previous `GrafanaRuleListItem` (in the now-deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`) built the view href with `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`, so that navigating to the rule detail page preserved a way back to the originating (possibly filtered) list. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` builds `href: createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view')` with no `returnTo` parameter at all. This removes the 'back to list' behavior for every rule reached via the new list components (`GrafanaGroupLoader` and `FilterView`), which is a UX regression for users navigating from a filtered/sorted list into a rule's detail page.

title: Loss of eventual-consistency handling between Ruler and Prometheus endpoints
body: The previous implementation fetched both the Ruler group and the Prometheus group and used `matchRules` to render 'Creating' items (rule exists only in Ruler, not yet in Prometheus) and 'Deleting' items (rule still returned by Prometheus but already removed from Ruler), plus a warning log on persistent mismatches. This PR removes the Ruler fetch entirely and only renders `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` (line 68). Two consequences: (1) a newly created rule that hasn't yet propagated to the Prometheus rules endpoint will simply not appear in the list at all (no skeleton, no indicator, not even caught by the `!promResponse` check since the overall response is still present, just missing this specific rule/group), and (2) a rule just deleted via the Ruler API may continue to render as a fully interactive item (with Edit/View links) until the Prometheus endpoint catches up, so users can click into a rule that no longer exists. Neither scenario is handled or surfaced to the user anymore.

title: Stale comment and variable name referencing removed ruler-preload logic
body: The comment above `if (hookOptions.populateCache)` still reads "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX... doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded", and the local variable is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload`, even though the actual `alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)` call was removed in this PR. The remaining code only populates the Prometheus RTK Query cache, so the comment and variable name are now inaccurate and misleading for future maintainers.

title: No replacement coverage for removed eventual-consistency scenarios
body: This PR deletes the previous tests that verified 'Creating' state (ruler-only rule) and 'Deleting' state (prom-only rule) behavior, as well as the `matchRules` unit tests, without adding any new tests that cover the corresponding edge cases for the new ruler-less implementation (e.g. what happens when the requested group is not yet present/returned in the Prometheus response, or when a rule was recently deleted from Ruler but is still present in the cached Prometheus response). Given `GrafanaGroupLoader` now relies solely on the Prometheus endpoint, these consistency edge cases are exactly the ones that need new coverage, but none was added.

title: Missing `key` prop for Grafana-origin rule items in FilterView list
body: In the `rules.map((ruleWithOrigin) => {...})` loop, the 'datasource' and default cases pass `key={key}` to their returned elements, but the 'grafana' case's `<GrafanaRuleListItem .../>` (previously `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../>`) no longer has a `key` prop set. Since React requires a stable `key` on elements returned directly from a `.map()` callback, this will produce 'Each child in a list should have a unique key prop' warnings and can cause incorrect DOM reuse/reconciliation when the filtered rule list updates (e.g. on refetch or pagination), potentially showing stale rule data for Grafana rules in the filtered/search view.

title: Delete menu item is unreachable in the new alert-list flow because it still requires `rulerRule`
body: `canDelete` is now computed as `(deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`, so it can become true purely from the new Grafana Prometheus-rule-based ability check (used when only `promRule` is supplied, as is the case for `GrafanaRuleListItem` -> `RuleActionsButtons` in the new alert list view). However the actual render condition is `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}`, and `rulerRule` is never passed in that new flow (GrafanaRuleListItem only passes `promRule`). As a result, even users with Delete permission will never see the Delete menu item for Grafana rules rendered via the new list view, even though the ability computation says they should be able to delete. This is confirmed by the new test in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx ('should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked'), which grants `AlertingRuleDelete` but asserts exactly 4 menu items (no Delete).

title: Pause ability computed via promRule is dead code; can cause a stray empty divider
body: `canPause` can now become true solely via the new `grafanaPauseAbility` (promRule-based) check, but the Pause menu item is still gated by `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, which is always false in the new alert-list flow because `rulerRule` is never supplied there. This means the Pause option can never actually render in that flow despite `canPause` being true, making the promRule-based pause computation effectively dead code. Worse, `canPause` still feeds into `showDivider` (`[canPause, canSilence, ..., canDuplicate].some(Boolean) && [canExport].some(Boolean)`), so when `canPause` is true but nothing else above it renders, an extra/empty `<Menu.Divider />` can appear with nothing above it in the dropdown.

title: Rule view link no longer carries the `returnTo` parameter, breaking back-navigation
body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx` built the rule-detail link with `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })`, where `returnTo` came from `createReturnTo()` so the detail page could navigate back to the originating list/filter view. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` builds the href as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view')` with no `returnTo` and no import of `useReturnTo`/`createReturnTo` at all. Users navigating from the alert list to a rule's detail page will lose the ability to return to their previous filtered/list view context.

title: New `provenance` field on GrafanaPromRuleDTO is not confirmed to be populated by the backend
body: `provenance?: string` was added to `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` and is now the sole mechanism used by `isProvisionedPromRule()` (utils/rules.ts) to flag a rule as provisioned/immutable in the new alert-list flow, replacing the previous Ruler-based provenance check (`rulerRule.grafana_alert.provenance`). This PR contains no backend changes to the Grafana Prometheus rules endpoint that would populate this field. If the backend does not actually return `provenance` in that API response, `isProvisionedPromRule` will always evaluate to false, causing provisioned (e.g. Terraform/API-managed) alert rules to be incorrectly treated as editable/deletable/duplicable from the UI, which is a data-integrity and governance risk.

title: Transient 'Creating'/'Deleting' states for Grafana rules are removed without replacement
body: The previous implementation fetched both the Ruler group and the Prometheus group and used `matchRules()` to show a 'Creating' indicator for rules present in the Ruler but not yet reflected by Prometheus, and a 'Deleting' indicator (via `RuleOperationListItem`) for rules still present in Prometheus after being removed from the Ruler. This PR removes the Ruler fetch and the matching logic entirely (and the corresponding `matchRules` unit tests), so during the eventual-consistency window after creating or deleting a Grafana rule, the list will simply omit or show stale rules with no visual indication of the pending state, which is a UX regression compared to the previous behavior and is not covered by any new test.

title: Queries get interpolated multiple times when shard splitting delegates to runSplitQuery
body: runShardSplitQuery() now interpolates every target with datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) before any splitting happens (lines 49-53). However, splitQueriesByStreamShard()'s runNextRequest() (shardQuerySplitting.ts, ~line 163) calls runSplitQuery(datasource, subRequest, options) once per shard group/cycle, and runSplitQuery() (querySplitting.ts, lines 296-299) now also unconditionally re-interpolates request.targets via datasource.applyTemplateVariables for every call. Because the sub-request built for each shard group still carries the already-interpolated (and shard-selector-modified) targets, those targets get interpolated again on every shard cycle. This is confirmed by the updated test expectation in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts ('Interpolates queries before running') which changed from `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` to `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` for a single logical query split into 4 shard groups. Repeated interpolation is wasteful, and if applyTemplateVariables is not idempotent (e.g. it injects ad hoc filters as extra label matchers into the selector text, as its own test mock does by mutating query.expr), running it multiple times on the same query risks duplicating ad hoc filter clauses or otherwise corrupting the final selector sent to the backend when ad hoc filters (request.filters) are present.

title: Moving interpolation before querySupportsSplitting() defeats the $__range splitting safeguard
body: querySupportsSplitting() (lines 282-289) relies on isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) to detect queries using the $__range family of variables, with the comment explaining that such queries must not be time-split because the interpolated $__range value would otherwise become incorrect. Previously this check ran on the raw (non-interpolated) expr, so the literal '$__range' text was still present and detectable. Now queries are interpolated via datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...) at line 299 before this check runs at line 300, so by the time isQueryWithRangeVariable() executes, any '$__range' reference has already been replaced with its literal value and can no longer be detected in the string. As a result, querySupportsSplitting() can never classify a query as using $__range anymore, so such queries will now flow into the normal time-splitting path (logQueries/metricQueries) instead of being executed as a single non-split request, risking incorrect merged results for queries that depend on $__range spanning the whole original range versus the narrower per-partition sub-ranges. The accompanying comment is now also stale/misleading since the described protection no longer functions as written.

title: No regression test for $__range queries after reordering interpolation and splitting checks
body: The PR reorders interpolation to happen before querySupportsSplitting()/isQueryWithRangeVariable() is evaluated (see querySplitting.ts), which changes whether queries using the $__range variable get excluded from time splitting. No test was added (here or elsewhere in this file) that exercises a query containing $__range to confirm it is still correctly excluded from splitting, or to validate the new intended behavior if inclusion is now considered safe. Given this is exactly the kind of interaction the interpolation-timing change affects, its absence leaves a meaningful regression risk unverified.

title: No test verifies ad hoc filters aren't duplicated due to repeated interpolation
body: The test 'Interpolates queries before running' now asserts datasource.applyTemplateVariables is called 5 times for a single query (previously the batch call interpolateVariablesInQueries was asserted to run once), confirming the query gets interpolated multiple times across the shard-splitting/time-splitting delegation. None of the tests pass a non-empty request.filters (ad hoc filters) to verify that this repeated interpolation does not duplicate ad hoc filter matchers in the final query selector sent to runQuery. Given applyTemplateVariables is the mechanism typically used to inject ad hoc filters into the query text, and it is now invoked multiple times per logical query, this scenario should be covered by a dedicated test.

title: Queries get interpolated twice when shard splitting delegates to time splitting
body: `runShardSplitQuery()` (lines 49-52) now interpolates every target once via `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` before grouping by shard. For each shard group, `splitQueriesByStreamShard()` then builds a `subRequest` from these already-interpolated targets (with the shard selector injected) and passes it to `runSplitQuery()` (line 163). But `runSplitQuery()` was changed in this same PR (querySplitting.ts lines 296-299) to itself call `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on `request.targets` before doing any further work. As a result every outgoing sub-request produced via shard splitting is interpolated twice. This is confirmed by the updated test expectation in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts (`expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` for a single target that produces 4 shard groups: 1 initial call + 4 repeats, one per group). Re-running interpolation (including ad hoc filter application via `request.filters`) on a query that was already interpolated is unsafe unless that operation is perfectly idempotent: if the ad hoc filter insertion logic is additive (locates the stream selector and appends matchers) rather than replace-in-place, filters will be inserted twice into the LogQL selector for every sub-request, producing duplicated/malformed selectors whenever ad hoc filters are combined with shard splitting. Even when harmless, this duplicates work on every single sub-request, multiplying with both shard-group count and further time-based sub-splitting inside each group, adding needless overhead. The sharding path should not feed already-interpolated targets back through a second full interpolation pass (e.g. give `runSplitQuery` an option to skip interpolation when the caller has already applied it, or make interpolation happen exactly once at a single, well-defined entry point).

title: No test exercises the double-interpolation risk with non-idempotent ad hoc filters
body: The updated test 'Interpolates queries before running' only asserts the call count of `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` (now 5 instead of 1), and the new 'Interpolates queries before execution' test mocks `applyTemplateVariables`/`replace` with a plain, idempotent string `.replace()` that leaves no trace once a variable has been substituted. Neither test exercises a scenario where `request.filters` (ad hoc filters) are set and the interpolation/filter-insertion step is additive rather than idempotent. Since `applyTemplateVariables` is now invoked twice per sub-request when shard splitting delegates to `runSplitQuery` (once in `runShardSplitQuery`, once inside the delegated call), there is no coverage proving that ad hoc filters, or any other non-idempotent transformation performed by `applyTemplateVariables`, are not duplicated in the final query sent to the backend.

title: Interpolating queries before the $__range exclusion check breaks splitting-safety for $__range queries
body: In runSplitQuery(), queries are now interpolated via datasource.applyTemplateVariables() (line 299) before being passed to querySupportsSplitting()/isQueryWithRangeVariable() (lines 282-289, used at line 300). isQueryWithRangeVariable() is a textual check for the literal `$__range` placeholder in query.expr. Because interpolation now runs first, any `$__range` usage is already replaced with a concrete value (computed for the original, un-split overall range) before this check executes, so the literal text is gone and isQueryWithRangeVariable() will always return false post-interpolation. As a result, queries that use `$__range` - which the code comment explicitly says must be excluded from time splitting because the backend would otherwise interpolate the range variable using each split sub-range - are no longer routed into `nonSplittingQueries`. Instead they are split normally, and every sub-request ends up reusing the single baked-in value computed for the full original range (e.g. a 3-day range baked into `[3d]`) even though each sub-request only covers a fraction of that range (e.g. 1 day). This silently produces incorrect query results (wrong window/rate calculations) for any metric/log query relying on `$__range`, and effectively makes the exclusion logic in querySupportsSplitting() dead code.

title: applyTemplateVariables is now invoked redundantly multiple times for the same query in the shard-splitting path
body: runShardSplitQuery() interpolates all targets via datasource.applyTemplateVariables() (line 52) before delegating to splitQueriesByStreamShard(), which for every shard group/cycle calls runSplitQuery() (querySplitting.ts line 163-166) - and runSplitQuery() itself now also calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() on its targets (querySplitting.ts line 299). The already-interpolated query is therefore re-interpolated once more for every sub-request that the sharding loop produces. This is confirmed by the updated test in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts (line 112), which now expects applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times for a single input query (1 initial call + 4 sub-request calls) instead of once as before. Besides the unnecessary repeated work, this is risky if applyTemplateVariables is not fully idempotent (e.g. if it injects ad-hoc filters into the expr string), since re-running it on an already-processed query could duplicate ad-hoc filter matchers or otherwise produce different results depending on context (scopedVars/time range) available at each call site.

title: No regression test for $__range queries after moving interpolation earlier
body: The new 'Interpolates queries before execution' test only exercises variable interpolation for `$__auto` and `$step`, which are unrelated to time-range splitting decisions. There is no test verifying that queries containing `$__range` are still excluded from time splitting (routed to nonSplittingQueries) after interpolation now runs before the querySupportsSplitting/isQueryWithRangeVariable check. Given that this reordering can break that exclusion (see related finding), a regression test asserting that `$__range` queries are not split, and that the correct non-split range interpolation is preserved, is missing and would have caught this issue.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards all logger state
body: TestLogger.FromContext(_ context.Context) returns a brand-new NewTestLogger() instance instead of returning the receiver (or a logger that still writes into the same DebugLogs/InfoLogs/WarnLogs/ErrorLogs fields). Since LoggerMiddleware now always logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (see logger_middleware.go), any test using plog.NewTestLogger() to assert on logged messages/calls through code paths that call FromContext will never see those calls recorded on the original TestLogger instance - the call lands on a throwaway logger that is immediately discarded. This makes TestLogger unusable for verifying the new context-aware logging behavior and can mask real bugs in tests that rely on it.

title: traceID field dropped from 'Plugin Request Completed' log line
body: The previous logRequest implementation in logger_middleware.go explicitly added a "traceID" attribute to the log params via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false). That code (and the tracing import) was removed in this PR, and the replacement contextual-attribute builder here (instrumentContext) only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname - traceID is not restored anywhere. As a result, the 'Plugin Request Completed' log entries emitted by LoggerMiddleware no longer contain a traceID, which is a regression for trace/log correlation that isn't mentioned in the PR description.

title: No unit test added for new ContextualLoggerMiddleware
body: This PR introduces a new, independently-registered middleware (ContextualLoggerMiddleware) that carries meaningful logic (building the contextual log attributes from plugin/datasource/user info and depending on being ordered before LoggerMiddleware in the chain). No test file (e.g., contextual_logger_middleware_test.go) was added to verify that the context attributes are correctly set, nor to guard against future middleware-order regressions that would silently break the LoggerMiddleware's enriched logging.

title: Test function name not updated after rename
body: The file was renamed from instrumentation_middleware_test.go to metrics_middleware_test.go and the underlying type/constructor were renamed to MetricsMiddleware/newMetricsMiddleware, but the test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware. This leaves a stale, inconsistent name that no longer matches the renamed type or file, contrary to the stated goal of the PR (better naming/consistency).

title: Adding FromContext to exported Logger interface is a breaking change for other implementers
body: A new required method, FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger, was added to the exported plugins/log.Logger interface. This PR only updates the two known implementations (grafanaInfraLogWrapper in logger.go and TestLogger in fake.go). Any other type in the codebase (or downstream consumer) that implements plugins/log.Logger without this method will fail to compile/satisfy the interface. This should be verified across the codebase before merging, since interface changes like this silently break unrelated implementers.

title: Logger name still references old 'instrumentation' naming
body: clientmiddleware.NewLoggerMiddleware(cfg, log.New("plugin.instrumentation")) still names the logger "plugin.instrumentation" even though this PR's stated purpose is to rename instrumentation-related concepts to metrics-related ones for clarity, and the logger here is purely for request logging (LoggerMiddleware), not metrics. This leaves confusing/incorrect logger naming in production logs after the rename.

title: traceID field dropped from 'Plugin Request Completed' log line
body: The old logRequest implementation explicitly computed `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` and appended a "traceID" key/value to logParams whenever a trace ID was present. That code (and the `tracing` import) was removed in this PR and not replaced anywhere: the new `instrumentContext` helper in contextual_logger_middleware.go only adds `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `uname`, never `traceID`. As a result, the "Plugin Request Completed" log entries emitted by LoggerMiddleware no longer contain the trace ID, making it harder to correlate plugin request logs with distributed traces unless pkg/infra/log's FromContext independently injects trace correlation (which is not evident from the diff). This looks like an unintentional regression rather than a deliberate removal.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards state, breaking assertions on logged calls
body: TestLogger.FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger always returns a brand new `NewTestLogger()` instance instead of returning the receiver (or a logger that still records into the original fields). LoggerMiddleware now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (logger_middleware.go), so any test that supplies a `*TestLogger` to code under test and later inspects `InfoLogs`/`DebugLogs`/etc. on that original instance will always see zero calls, because the actual Info() call lands on a throwaway logger that is discarded immediately afterward. This silently defeats the purpose of the fake logger for any code path that calls FromContext before logging.

title: No unit tests added for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware
body: This PR extracts the previously-embedded `instrumentContext` logic into a new standalone ContextualLoggerMiddleware (and exported constructor NewContextualLoggerMiddleware), but no test file (e.g. contextual_logger_middleware_test.go) was added to verify which fields are placed on the context, that QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics are instrumented while SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream intentionally are not, or that the middleware correctly feeds LoggerMiddleware downstream. Given this logic directly affects what shows up in production logs, lack of coverage is a real gap.

title: Test function name not updated after Instrumentation -> Metrics rename
body: The file was renamed from instrumentation_middleware_test.go to metrics_middleware_test.go and the internal constructor call was updated to `newMetricsMiddleware`, but the top-level test function is still named `TestInstrumentationMiddleware`. This leftover name contradicts the stated goal of the PR (renaming for clarity/consistency) and will confuse anyone searching for tests related to MetricsMiddleware.
