body: In searchSupport.init(), the errgroup loop spawns one goroutine per namespace (group.SetLimit(s.initWorkers) allows real concurrency) and each goroutine does `totalBatchesIndexed++` and `_, _, err = s.build(...); return err`, where both `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` are variables captured from the enclosing scope and written concurrently by multiple goroutines without any mutex/atomic. This is a data race: concurrent non-atomic increments of totalBatchesIndexed can lose updates, and concurrent writes to the shared `err` mean a goroutine's `return err` can read a value written by a different goroutine between assignment and return, causing errgroup to receive an incorrect per-goroutine result (e.g. returning another goroutine's error for a successful build, or masking a real failure with nil from a later successful goroutine). This can cause init() to incorrectly fail startup, or silently swallow a failed index build. Each goroutine should use its own local err variable and totalBatchesIndexed should be an atomic counter or protected by a mutex.

title: Postgres integration test skipped instead of fixed, masking potential regression
body: The test now unconditionally skips when dbType == 'postgres' with the comment 'test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.' This removes CI coverage of the storage-server module startup path for Postgres, one of the supported production databases, right in the same PR that changes resource-server initialization to run synchronously and eagerly at construction time. Skipping rather than diagnosing/fixing risks hiding a real regression introduced by the eager-Init change (e.g., startup taking too long or behaving differently under Postgres in CI) and leaves no coverage to catch future regressions on that backend until the TODO is addressed.

title: Trace-context propagation fix applied inconsistently within the same file
body: The PR fixes span propagation in GetResourceStats by reassigning `ctx, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)` so the span is attached to the context used by the subsequent DB call. However, sibling methods in the same file with the identical bug were left unfixed, e.g. ReadResource (line 353: `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, tracePrefix+".Read")`, followed by `b.db.WithTx(ctx, ...)` using the original, span-less ctx), WriteEvent (line ~158), and ListIterator (line ~388). Since the PR's stated goal is 'fixes trace propagation by passing span contexts down', leaving these other call sites with the same discarded-context pattern means their DB operations still won't appear nested under their respective spans in traces, contradicting the PR's intent and leaving inconsistent tracing behavior in the same backend file.

title: Compile error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called with no arguments
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with zero arguments, but the only method with that name is defined in the superclass UsernamePasswordForm as `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which requires a UserModel parameter. There is no zero-arg overload anywhere in the changed files. This will not compile, breaking the build for the whole module.

title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() requires a non-null user, inverting the intended condition and breaking the primary (non-reauth) passkeys flow
body:
`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. It is used in `authenticate()` (line 115) and in `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137) to decide whether to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)`, which sets up the conditional-UI/passkeys attributes (challenge, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI, allowed authenticators) on the rendered form.

Previously this fill was done specifically when `context.getUser() == null` (the normal, non-reauthentication login scenario, e.g. fresh login page, invalid-username error, or empty-password error before the user object is set on the context). With the new `user != null` requirement, `fillContextForm` is skipped exactly in that common case, since `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.getUser()`/`badPasswordHandler()` never call `context.setUser()` before the failing scenario is rendered back. This means the conditional-UI passkeys form data will not be set up for ordinary (non-reauth) logins or after a username/empty-password validation error, which directly contradicts the PR's own updated test `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey()` (expects the webauthn form present after submitting only a username, i.e. before `context.setUser()` is invoked) as well as the pre-existing `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` tests that expect the webauthn form to render on a fresh login page where no user is yet set.

title: Unused import after replacing assertThrows(NoSuchElementException...) assertions
body: The import `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` is no longer used in this file: both previous usages (`Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` in `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`) were replaced with `MatcherAssert.assertThat(..., Matchers.notNullValue())`. The dangling unused import may trigger checkstyle/unused-import build failures depending on the project's lint configuration.

title: Compile error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called with no arguments
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with zero arguments. The only method with that name visible via the inherited UsernamePasswordForm class is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which requires a `UserModel` parameter. There is no no-arg overload anywhere in the class hierarchy shown in this PR (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator doesn't define one either). This call therefore cannot be resolved and the module will fail to compile ('method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled in class UsernamePasswordForm cannot be applied to given types'). The call was most likely meant to be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, matching the pattern used elsewhere (e.g. UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate()/challenge()).

title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) requires a non-null user, inverting the WebAuthn conditional-UI setup and breaking normal (non-reauthentication) passkey login
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. It gates the call to `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` both in `authenticate()` (line 115) and in the overridden `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137); `fillContextForm` populates the WebAuthn challenge/rpId/conditional-UI attributes that enable the browser's passkey autofill UI on the combined username/password form. Before this change, that call ran precisely when `context.getUser() == null` (the normal/first-time login path, with no pre-selected user) — this is the primary use case for discoverable-credential/passkey autofill login, and was explicitly commented as 'setup webauthn data when the user is not already selected'. After the change, the call only fires when a user is already set (the new re-authentication scenario this PR targets), so for every normal fresh login attempt (no pre-selected user) the WebAuthn attributes are never populated and passkeys conditional UI will not be offered — this removes functionality rather than adding the new re-authentication support, and conflicts with existing/updated tests that still expect the webauthn form/autofill to appear for fresh, non-reauthenticated logins (e.g. PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest#webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest's non-discoverable-key flow). The fix for re-authentication should be additive to, not a replacement for, the existing null-user case.

title: Unused import left after assertions were changed
body: The import `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` is no longer referenced anywhere in the file: both previous usages inside `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` (`Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> ...)`) were replaced with `MatcherAssert.assertThat(..., Matchers.notNullValue())` in this PR. The now-dead import should be removed; in modules where checkstyle enforces 'no unused imports' this would fail the build.

title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not match the only defined method signature
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments: `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) {`. However, the only method with that name introduced in this PR is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` defined in the parent class `UsernamePasswordForm` (which `UsernameForm` extends). There is no zero-argument overload anywhere in the shown diff. This will fail to compile (method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is undefined for the given arguments), breaking the build of the entire services module and blocking any test from running. The call should likely be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requiring user != null breaks anonymous/discoverable-key passkey login
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. This method now gates the calls to `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` in both `authenticate()` (lines 115-117) and `challenge(context, error, field)` (lines 137-140), which are invoked with `context.getUser()` as the argument. Previously, `fillContextForm` was called precisely when `context.getUser() == null` (the normal, anonymous/first-time login case that enables the discoverable-key / conditional UI passkeys flow, e.g. navigator.credentials.get with conditional mediation). With the new `user != null` requirement, `fillContextForm` is now only invoked when a user is already present in the context (the re-authentication case this PR intends to fix), and is skipped entirely for a fresh/anonymous login attempt. This removes the webauthn challenge/rpId/attribute setup needed for the base passkeys login flow, which is exercised by pre-existing tests such as `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey()` and `passwordLoginWithExternalKey()` in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest/PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest, that rely on the webauthn form/attributes being present on the very first page load with no pre-selected user. The fix for re-authentication should not have been conditioned on `user != null`; the flag should simply reflect whether passkeys/webauthn is enabled, independent of whether a user has already been resolved.

title: Unused import added
body: The import `org.keycloak.models.credential.PasswordCredentialModel` was added by this PR but is never referenced anywhere in the file's body. This is dead code left over from the change and should be removed.

title: remove() now unconditionally hits the underlying JPA store even when the IDP is already cached
body: In remove(), `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is now executed unconditionally before the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` check. Previously, `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` was only called inside the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch; when the cache entry was valid, the code used the already-cached `CachedIdentityProvider` (`cached.getIdentityProvider()`) without touching the delegate at all. After this change, every call to remove() performs an extra round-trip to the underlying storage (JPA/DB) even in the common case where the alias is already present in cache, which is pure overhead introduced only to support the new `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` call. The same information could be derived from `cached.getIdentityProvider()` in the else-branch instead of re-fetching from the delegate, avoiding the redundant query.

title: Test cleanup references the literal alias "alias" instead of the actual created IDP alias, leaking test data
body: In the new testCacheIDPForLogin test, cleanup is registered with `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (also repeated at line 425 for the "idp-alias-20" provider). The literal string "alias" is passed instead of the actual alias used when creating the provider (e.g. "idp-alias-" + i). This means the cleanup never removes the 20+ identity providers created by the test; at best the cleanup call fails (no IDP with alias "alias" exists), and the created identity providers remain in the realm after the test finishes. This leftover state can pollute subsequent tests in the same realm (e.g. IDP count assertions, alias uniqueness on re-run, or other cache tests), causing flaky or order-dependent test failures.

title: No test coverage for invalidating warm login caches via create()/remove() of a currently login-eligible IDP
body: testCacheIDPForLogin only exercises the create()/remove() invalidation paths (registerIDPLoginInvalidation) with IDPs that do NOT qualify for login (e.g. `testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-1").remove()` removes a disabled, non-login IDP, and the newly created idp-alias-20 is initially hideOnLogin=true). The 20 initial IDP creations happen before any cache is warmed, so they never actually exercise invalidation of a populated cache either. As a result, the scenario where a currently login-eligible IDP is created or removed after the login caches are already populated (which should trigger registerIDPLoginInvalidation to clear all FetchMode caches) is never verified; only the analogous update() path (registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) is thoroughly tested. A regression in the create()/remove() invalidation logic for this case would not be caught by this test.

title: update() uses the org-aware wrapped model for login-cache invalidation decisions, which can mask real eligibility changes
body: In update(), `idpById` is obtained via `getById(model.getInternalId())`, which is the cache-aware method of this same class and therefore wraps the result with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(...)`. That wrapper overrides `isEnabled()` to also factor in the live state of the linked organization (`org.isEnabled()`), while the underlying `getForLogin()` query that actually populates the cached ID list filters strictly on the IDP's raw, persisted `enabled` column (via `LoginFilter`), independent of the organization's current status. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpById, model)` then calls `getLoginPredicate().test(idpById)`, which invokes the wrapped (live) `isEnabled()`. If the linked organization happens to be disabled at the moment of the update, `idpById.isEnabled()` returns false even though the IDP's raw `enabled` flag (and therefore its actual membership in the cached login ID list) is true. Comparing this masked value against the predicate result for the raw `model` passed to update() can make the method wrongly conclude that login-eligibility 'didn't change' (both evaluate false) when in fact the IDP's raw eligibility did change (e.g. toggling hideOnLogin), causing the login caches to be left stale instead of invalidated. Note that remove() correctly avoids this by using `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` (the raw, unwrapped delegate) rather than the cache/organization-aware getById(); update() should do the same for consistency and correctness.

title: remove() now always performs an extra backend lookup for the IDP by alias, even when not needed
body: Previously, `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` was only invoked inside the `if (isInvalid(cacheKey))` branch when a backend lookup was actually required. The refactor moved this call out to the top of remove(), so `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is now executed unconditionally on every removal, even when the cache entry is still valid and already available via `realmCache.getCache().get(cacheKey, ...)`. This adds an unnecessary delegate/DB round trip to every identity-provider removal purely to support the new login-cache invalidation check, instead of reusing the already-available cached model when present.

title: Login cache sub-key is unnecessarily split by organizationId for FetchMode.REALM_ONLY
body: `getForLogin` computes `searchKey = organizationId != null ? organizationId : ""` and stores results in the per-mode `IdentityProviderListQuery` under that sub-key, regardless of fetch mode. However, for `FetchMode.REALM_ONLY` the default `getForLogin` implementation completely ignores `organizationId` (it forces `ORGANIZATION_ID=null` in the search options), so the result is identical for any organizationId value. If `getForLogin(REALM_ONLY, orgA)` and `getForLogin(REALM_ONLY, orgB)` are both invoked, they will be cached as two separate sub-entries with identical content, causing redundant delegate queries and unnecessary cache growth instead of reusing a single REALM_ONLY entry.

title: Test cleanup removes a non-existent IDP alias instead of the one actually created
body: In the new `testCacheIDPForLogin` test, after creating identity providers with aliases like "idp-alias-" + i (and later "idp-alias-20"), cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` (also repeated at the idp-alias-20 creation point). The literal string "alias" is passed instead of the actual alias that was created, so the cleanup action targets a non-existent identity provider named "alias" rather than the ones actually created by the test. As a result, none of the up-to-21 identity providers created by this test are properly removed during cleanup, leaking realm state across test runs/test methods and risking alias-conflict failures or inflated counts in subsequent tests that rely on a clean realm/IDP set.

title: Unconditional extra backing-store lookup added to remove()
body: In remove(), `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is now called unconditionally before the isInvalid(cacheKey) check. Previously, when the cache entry was valid (`isInvalid(cacheKey)==false`), the method only consulted the local cache (`realmCache.getCache().get(cacheKey, ...)`) and never hit the delegate/JPA store in that branch. Now every remove() call performs an extra delegate lookup even when the cached CachedIdentityProvider already holds the needed model (available via `cached.getIdentityProvider()` in the else branch), adding an avoidable database round-trip to every IDP removal.

title: Inconsistent wrapped vs raw model comparison in login-cache invalidation on update
body: In update(), `idpById = getById(model.getInternalId())` returns an organization-aware wrapped IdentityProviderModel whose isEnabled() also factors in the linked organization's enabled state (see createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel), while `model` (the second argument passed straight through to registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) is the raw, unwrapped model from the caller whose isEnabled() reflects only the stored 'enabled' attribute. Because getLoginPredicate() tests ENABLED via isEnabled(), comparing the wrapped 'original' against the raw 'updated' is inconsistent: when the organization is disabled, idpById.isEnabled() can be false even though the stored attribute is true, causing registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate to conclude 'no login-eligibility change' and skip cache invalidation even though the raw 'enabled' attribute genuinely changed. Since the underlying idpDelegate.getForLogin() query filters by the raw stored attribute (not the wrapped value), the cached ID list for getForLogin can become stale and keep referencing an IDP whose real enabled flag changed, violating the documented getForLogin() contract that only enabled/eligible IDPs are returned for callers that don't re-check isEnabled() themselves.

title: No test covers organization enable/disable or removal affecting the new getForLogin cache
body: testCacheIDPForLogin only exercises create/update/remove on the IdentityProvider itself to verify cache invalidation of the new getForLogin caches. It never tests disabling/enabling the linked Organization or removing the Organization entirely. This matters because OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java was specifically changed in this PR to re-check idp.isEnabled() at render time precisely because toggling an organization's enabled flag does not invalidate the getForLogin ID-list cache. There is no test verifying that disabling an organization correctly excludes its IDPs from login, nor that removing an organization properly invalidates/cleans up the new login caches for its linked IDPs, leaving this behavior unverified.

title: Login-eligibility logic duplicated between getForLogin() search options and getLoginPredicate()
body: The default getForLogin() method (lines 165-184) determines login eligibility by building search-option maps (LoginFilter.getLoginSearchOptions() plus explicit ORGANIZATION_ID/BROKER_PUBLIC handling), while the new getLoginPredicate() (lines 252-256) re-implements the same eligibility rules as a Predicate for use purely in cache-invalidation decisions in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider. These two independent representations of the same business rule must be kept manually in sync; if either is changed in the future without updating the other, the Infinispan cache invalidation logic will silently diverge from the actual query semantics, resulting in stale or incorrect getForLogin() cache results.

title: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Inside `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, the two lines `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` create throwaway ASN1Encoder instances, encode the BigIntegers into them, and then discard the result without ever using it - the method immediately re-creates new encoders a few lines below to build the actual return value. This is leftover/dead code that wastes CPU cycles on every signature conversion and signals the implementation wasn't cleaned up before merging; it should be removed.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() does not return a BouncyCastle provider
body: `CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider()` is documented (in the interface) as returning "BouncyCastle security provider. Can be either non-FIPS or FIPS based provider". This implementation instead returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which on a typical JVM resolves to the JDK's built-in keystore provider (e.g. SUN), not BouncyCastle at all. Unlike every other unimplemented method in this class, which consistently throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, this method silently returns a semantically wrong value, which can mislead any caller that relies on the contract (e.g. comparing/using the provider for BC-specific operations). It should either throw `UnsupportedOperationException` like the rest of the unimplemented methods, or be documented/implemented correctly.

title: New abstract order() method breaks source compatibility for existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: `CryptoProvider` is a public interface loaded via ServiceLoader/SPI and is implemented both inside and (potentially) outside this repository. Adding `int order();` as a new abstract method (no default implementation) means any existing implementation of this interface that is not updated in lock-step will fail to compile/break until it adds an `order()` override. Since this is a published API in the `common` module, this is a source-compatibility break for downstream custom CryptoProvider implementations. A default method (e.g. returning a baseline value) would avoid breaking existing implementors while still allowing providers that need preference to override it.

title: Multiple CryptoProviders on classpath are now silently resolved instead of failing fast, with only debug-level logging
body: Previously, `detectProvider` threw an `IllegalStateException` when more than one `CryptoProvider` was found on the classpath, forcing an explicit fix of classpath/packaging issues. The new code silently picks the provider with the highest `order()` and only logs the ignored providers via `logger.debugf(...)`, which is typically disabled in production. This means a classpath misconfiguration that places two different CryptoProvider implementations on the classpath (e.g. accidentally bundling both FIPS and non-FIPS crypto modules) will no longer fail at startup and will instead silently run with whichever provider happens to have the higher `order()` value, without any visible warning in default logs. This can hide serious security/operational misconfigurations (e.g., running non-FIPS crypto when FIPS mode was intended) that used to be caught immediately.

title: No test coverage for the new multi-provider ordering/selection logic
body: `detectProvider` now sorts discovered `CryptoProvider` instances by `order()` (descending) and picks the first one instead of throwing when multiple are present. This is a meaningful behavioral change (see related finding about silent provider selection), but no unit test was added to verify that, given multiple CryptoProviders with different `order()` values on the classpath, the correct (highest-order) one is selected and the others are merely logged rather than causing failure.

title: Single EC key pair of a default curve reused across ES256/ES384/ES512 tests
body: The constructor generates a single `KeyPair` via `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` without specifying a curve, which will typically produce a P-256 (secp256r1) key pair. This same key pair is then reused for `testES256`, `testES384`, and `testES512`. Signing with SHA-384/SHA-512 using a P-256 key does not produce signatures whose R/S components match the natural lengths expected for ES384/ES512 (which are meant to be used with P-384/P-521 keys respectively). As a result, the tests don't exercise the ASN.1 encode/decode logic with realistically-sized R/S integers for the larger curves (e.g., the extra sign-byte handling that occurs with 66-byte P-521 integers), reducing the value of the ES384/ES512 test cases and potentially masking edge-case bugs that would only manifest with correctly-sized keys.

title: New abstract method order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementors
body: CryptoProvider.order() is added as a plain abstract method (no default implementation). CryptoProvider is a public, SPI-loaded extension point (discovered via META-INF/services and ServiceLoader in CryptoIntegration). Any existing third-party or downstream implementation of this interface that is not updated to implement order() will fail to compile/load. Since this interface is explicitly designed for pluggable crypto backends (FIPS vs non-FIPS, custom providers), this is a breaking API change that should either provide a default method (e.g. `default int order() { return 100; }`) or be clearly called out as a breaking change in release notes.

title: Removed fail-fast check for multiple CryptoProviders now silently resolves ties non-deterministically
body: Previously, detecting more than one CryptoProvider on the classpath threw an IllegalStateException, which protected against misconfiguration (e.g. accidentally shipping both a FIPS and non-FIPS crypto module together). Now, detectProvider() just sorts by order() and silently keeps the first. All of DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider return the same order() value of 200, so if two of them ever end up on the same classpath/classloader, the choice between them depends on the arbitrary ServiceLoader iteration order (not guaranteed to be stable across JVMs/OS), rather than failing loudly. In a FIPS-mandated deployment this could silently select the non-FIPS provider instead of raising an error, which is a meaningful loss of a safety net with potential compliance/security consequences.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() does not return a BouncyCastle provider, violating the documented contract
body: CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() is documented as returning 'BouncyCastle security provider. Can be either non-FIPS or FIPS based provider'. This implementation instead returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is whatever JCA provider backs the JVM's default keystore type (typically the JDK's built-in SUN provider), completely unrelated to BouncyCastle. Other providers that don't rely on BouncyCastle (e.g. WildFlyElytronProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider()) simply return null, which is the established convention for 'no BC provider'. Returning an arbitrary unrelated Provider instance here is inconsistent with that convention and can mislead any code that relies on this method's contract (e.g. diagnostics, provider registration logic) if this CryptoProvider instance is ever the active one.

title: Dead code: throwaway ASN1Encoder instances created and discarded
body: In concatenatedRSToASN1DER(), two ASN1Encoder instances are created and `write()` is called on them, but the results are never used or assigned (lines 114-115); the actual return value is built via separate, freshly-created ASN1Encoder instances a few lines later. This is leftover/dead code from development that performs unnecessary object allocation and encoding work on every signature conversion call, and should be removed before merging.

title: ES384/ES512 tests reuse a single default-curve EC key, never exercising real signature lengths for those algorithms
body: The single EC KeyPair used across all three tests (testES256/testES384/testES512) is generated with `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` without specifying a curve, which defaults to a 256-bit curve (e.g. secp256r1/P-256) regardless of the algorithm under test. For ES384 and ES512 the real R/S components should be ~48 and ~66 bytes respectively, but because the same P-256 key is reused, the actual signature always has ~32-byte components that get zero-padded to the expected length in asn1derToConcatenatedRS/concatenatedRSToASN1DER. As a result, the tests never exercise the encoder/decoder with genuinely large R/S values (e.g. values requiring a leading 0x00 byte near the boundary of a 48- or 66-byte field), reducing their ability to catch boundary bugs specific to the larger curves these algorithms are meant to represent.

title: Silent resolution of multiple CryptoProviders removes a fail-fast safety check
body: Previously, detectProvider() threw an IllegalStateException if more than one CryptoProvider was found on the classloader, forcing operators to fix a misconfigured classpath (e.g. accidentally shipping both DefaultCryptoProvider and FIPS1402Provider together). The new code silently keeps only the highest-order provider and logs the ignored ones at debug level only (logger.debugf), which is typically disabled in production. All three built-in providers (DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, FIPS1402Provider) use the same order()=200, so if two of them end up on the same classpath by mistake, selection among ties depends on ServiceLoader iteration order (jar/classpath ordering), which is not guaranteed to be deterministic across environments. For FIPS-sensitive deployments this can silently select a non-FIPS-compliant provider instead of failing loudly as before, which is a meaningful regression in safety/compliance guarantees without any visible warning.

title: New abstract method order() breaks binary/source compatibility for existing implementers
body: CryptoProvider is a public SPI interface loaded via ServiceLoader; adding a new abstract method order() (without a default implementation) means any existing third-party or external implementation of CryptoProvider will fail to compile/implement the interface until updated. All in-repo implementers were updated in this PR, but any external module implementing this interface (which is exactly the scenario this PR is designed to support, e.g. authz-client) will break unless it also adds order(). A default method (e.g. returning a baseline value) would preserve compatibility while still allowing providers to opt into custom ordering.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() does not return a BouncyCastle provider, violating the interface contract
body: CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() is documented as returning "BouncyCastle security provider. Can be either non-FIPS or FIPS based provider". This implementation instead returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is simply whatever JCA provider backs the JVM's default keystore type (e.g. SUN/SunJSSE for 'pkcs12' or 'jks'), unrelated to BouncyCastle. Any shared keycloak-core code path that calls this method expecting an actual BC(-FIPS) provider (e.g. to perform signature/key operations that require BC-specific algorithm support) will silently get the wrong provider instead of a clear failure, which can cause subtle incorrect behavior rather than an explicit error.

title: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: In concatenatedRSToASN1DER, the lines `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` create two throwaway ASN1Encoder instances, write to them, and discard the result without ever using it. This is leftover/dead code that serves no purpose and should be removed before merge; it suggests the implementation was not fully cleaned up.

title: Inconsistent use of KeystoreFormat.name() instead of toString()
body: getKeyStore() here calls `KeyStore.getInstance(format.name())`, whereas DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all use `format.toString()`. If KeystoreUtil.KeystoreFormat ever overrides toString() to map enum constants to different keystore type strings, this implementation would silently diverge from the other providers and could request the wrong keystore type. Even if currently harmless, it is an inconsistency that should match the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase.

title: No test coverage for the new order()-based provider selection logic
body: This PR's core mechanism change (allowing multiple CryptoProvider instances on the classpath and resolving via order(), replacing the previous exception-on-conflict behavior) has no accompanying unit test. There is no test verifying that the highest-order provider is chosen when multiple providers are present, nor one covering the tie-breaking behavior when providers share the same order value. Given this is a behavior-changing core feature (and a security-relevant one, since it silently resolves what used to be a hard error), it should be covered by dedicated tests in common's test sources.

title: Unconditional CryptoIntegration.init() now exposes a crypto provider with mostly unimplemented operations
body: AuthzClient.create(Configuration) now always calls CryptoIntegration.init(), which, for real consumers of the published org.keycloak:keycloak-authz-client artifact, will typically resolve to AuthzClientCryptoProvider as the only CryptoProvider on the classpath (since it has the lowest order=100 and is meant to be overridden when a full provider like DefaultCryptoProvider is also present, which downstream consumers are unlikely to bundle). That provider throws UnsupportedOperationException for the majority of CryptoProvider methods (getAlgorithmProvider, getCertificateUtils, getPemUtils, getOCSPProver, getIdentityExtractorProvider, createECParams, getKeyPairGen, getKeyFactory, getAesCbcCipher/getAesGcmCipher, getSecretKeyFact, getX509CertFactory, getCertStore, getCertPathBuilder, getSignature, wrapFactoryForTruststore). Any current or future authz-client code path (or shared keycloak-core code invoked by it) that relies on these operations will now fail at runtime with UnsupportedOperationException instead of either working (if it didn't previously touch CryptoIntegration) or failing clearly at startup.

title: Indefinite-length ASN.1 encoding not rejected, silently mis-parses malformed sequences
body: readLength() returns -1 for the BER indefinite-length form (0x80) without raising an error, but DER (which is what ECDSA signatures must use) never permits indefinite length. In readSequence(), the loop condition `while (length > 0)` treats a -1 length as "already done", silently producing an empty element list instead of rejecting the malformed/non-DER input outright. The subsequent `seq.size() != 2` check in AuthzClientCryptoProvider happens to catch this particular case, but the decoder itself does not validate or reject indefinite-length encodings, which is a correctness gap for an ASN.1 DER parser handling externally-supplied signature bytes.

title: canExchangeTo/exchangeToPermission now unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException, breaking standard OAuth2 token exchange
body: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo() (and exchangeToPermission()) unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException. Before this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() was not overridden, so calls to AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(...) fell back to the legacy, functional ClientPermissions implementation even when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 was enabled. Now that MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, any call to canExchangeTo (used by the standard OAuth2 token-exchange grant to check the per-client 'token-exchange' permission) will throw an unchecked RuntimeException instead of evaluating/denying the request. Because AdminPermissions.management(...) dispatches to V2 purely based on the global Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 flag (not a per-realm setting), enabling this preview feature on a server breaks token exchange for every client in every realm on that server, not just realms that opted into the new permission schema.

title: Client/role/group removal cleanup can crash with UnsupportedOperationException when V2 evaluator is selected
body: The ProviderEventListener registered here calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false) (and similarly for roles/groups) when a RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent occurs. The whole block is now gated by Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) (line 77), but the inner call to management() independently decides between V1 and V2 based on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. If both the legacy ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and the new ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 feature flags are enabled at the same time (nothing in this code prevents that, and both are server-wide flags), management() will return MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients().setPermissionsEnabled() (and similarly users()/groups() for the respective events) now throws UnsupportedOperationException unconditionally (see ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled). This exception would propagate out of the event listener during a client/role/group deletion, breaking that admin operation.

title: getClientsWithPermission cannot return real client IDs and can return the bogus literal 'Clients'
body: getClientsWithPermission() iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) and adds resource.getName() to the result for any matching resource with the given scope granted. However, per-client resources created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() (server-spi-private .../AdminPermissionsSchema.java, around line 104) are never given a 'type' attribute (only resource.updateScopes(...) is called, there is no resource.setType(resourceType)), so findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) will never match them - individual per-client granted permissions are silently excluded from the result. Conversely, the catch-all 'all clients' resource created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init() does have its type explicitly set to CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE and its name is literally the string 'Clients'. If an all-clients permission for the requested scope exists, that resource matches findByType and the literal string 'Clients' gets added to the returned Set<String> as if it were an actual client ID. Any caller treating the result as a set of real client identifiers will get incorrect/garbage data.

title: getResourceName() was not updated to handle the new CLIENTS resource type
body: getResourceName() special-cases USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE (returning 'All users' for the catch-all resource and the username for individual user resources) but has no corresponding branch for CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE even though this PR adds Clients as a fully supported resource type. For permissions targeting Clients, this method falls through to 'return resource.getDisplayName();', which, for resources created via getOrCreateResource/resourceStore.create (no display name set), returns the raw resource name - the client's internal UUID rather than a friendly label like 'All clients' or the client's clientId. This produces a poor/incorrect UX anywhere this name is surfaced (e.g. admin console or REST responses listing permissions for the Clients resource type).

title: Possible NullPointerException when the 'all-clients' resource is missing
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), if the per-client resource is not found, the code falls back to resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE), and then immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without checking whether getResourceTypeResource returned null. If the 'Clients' catch-all resource does not exist for the resource server (e.g. schema not initialized for that resource server, or data inconsistency), resource will be null and findByResource(server, null) is likely to throw an NPE (and if it somehow doesn't, resource.getScopes() later in the method would).

title: Missing test coverage for Clients resource-type permission CRUD/resource lifecycle and getClientsWithPermission
body: UserResourceTypePermissionTest provides dedicated coverage for permission/resource representation semantics for the Users resource type (testCreateResourceTypePermission, testCreateResourceObjectPermission, testFindByResourceObject, testDelete - verifying orphan resource cleanup, and testUpdate). PermissionClientTest, added by this PR for the new Clients resource type, only contains behavioral tests (manage/configure/view/mapRoles scenarios) and has no equivalent tests verifying that creating/removing scope permissions for Clients correctly creates/cleans up the underlying Resource records, nor any test exercising ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(). Given the identified bug in getClientsWithPermission (not finding real per-client resources, and potentially returning the literal 'Clients'), this gap means the regression would not be caught by the test suite.

title: init() is a no-op for already-initialized realms, so the new Clients scopes/resource are never backfilled
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately (lines 226-228) if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null, i.e. if the Admin Permissions client/resource-server was already created (which happens the first time Admin Fine-Grained Authorization V2 is enabled for a realm). This PR adds three new scopes (CONFIGURE, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE) and a new 'Clients' all-resource-type Resource to the schema, but there is no migration/backfill logic to add them to resource servers that were initialized before this change. For any realm that already had FGAP V2 enabled prior to upgrading, attempting to create a Client-resource-type permission will fail: getOrCreateResource() looks up each required scope via scopeStore.findByName(resourceServer, scopeName) and explicitly throws new ModelException("No scopes found.") if any of CONFIGURE/MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE is missing, and the 'Clients' all-resource-type Resource itself (used for all-clients permissions) will not exist either. This effectively breaks the new Clients permission feature for all pre-existing FGAP V2 deployments unless an administrator manually recreates the Admin Permissions client.

title: Unconditional UnsupportedOperationException now reachable for every client via MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()
body: MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now always returns ClientPermissionsV2 instead of falling back to the V1 ClientPermissions implementation as it did before this PR (clients() was not previously overridden). ClientPermissionsV2 overrides isPermissionsEnabled(), setPermissionsEnabled(), getPermissions(), resource(), managePermission(), configurePermission(), viewPermission(), mapRolesPermission(), mapRolesClientScopePermission(), mapRolesCompositePermission(), canExchangeTo() and exchangeToPermission() to unconditionally throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2") for ANY client, not only ones related to the new 'Clients' resource-type functionality. Any existing admin REST call that still relies on these methods when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled -- e.g. GET/PUT .../clients/{id}/management/permissions to toggle fine-grained permissions on a client, or a Standard Token Exchange authorization check via canExchangeTo() -- will now throw an unchecked exception where it previously worked by falling back to V1 behavior. There is no guard at the call sites to avoid reaching these methods, so this is a functional regression likely to surface as unhandled exceptions/500 errors for unrelated, pre-existing admin operations.

title: getResourceName() has no branch for the new CLIENTS resource type
body: getResourceName() special-cases USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE to return a friendly label ('All users' for the all-resource Resource, or the username for individual user resources), but after this PR adds CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE to the schema there is no equivalent 'if (CLIENTS.getType().equals(resourceType))' branch. For Client-type permissions the method falls through to 'return resource.getDisplayName()'. Resources for clients are created via getOrCreateResource() (and the all-resource 'Clients' Resource in init()) without ever setting a displayName, so this will return null/blank instead of a friendly client name (e.g. the client's clientId, or 'All clients'), unlike the equivalent Users case. This leaves permission resource names unresolved/blank wherever this API is surfaced (e.g. admin console display of resources tied to a Clients-type scope permission).

title: Possible NullPointerException when the all-clients fallback resource does not exist
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), when no resource exists for the specific client the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without checking whether the returned resource is null. getResourceTypeResource() returns null whenever the 'Clients' all-resource-type Resource cannot be found (e.g. for realms where it was never created, or where supportsAuthorizationSchema() returns false at call time). Passing a null Resource into findByResource() is likely to throw a NullPointerException instead of simply denying the permission, turning an authorization check failure into an unhandled server error.

title: canManageClientScopes() Javadoc is a copy-paste of canManage() and doesn't describe client-scope semantics
body: The Javadoc added for canManageClientScopes() (lines 52-57) is identical, word for word, to the Javadoc of canManage() directly above it (lines 40-45): both state 'Returns true if the caller has MANAGE_CLIENTS role... For V2 only: Also if it has permission to MANAGE'. The comment never mentions client scopes at all, so it fails to document what, if anything, differentiates this method from canManage(), which is misleading for future readers/maintainers trying to understand what permission this method actually checks.

title: No test coverage for the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope / canMapClientScopeRoles()
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS now includes the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles() checks it, but none of the new tests in this file (or elsewhere in the PR) exercise this scope. testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient only grants/tests MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE (plus CONFIGURE). Without a dedicated test, a regression in canMapClientScopeRoles() or the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE evaluation path would go unnoticed.

title: No end-to-end test coverage for the ClientScopeModel-level V2 permission methods
body: ClientPermissionsV2 overrides canManageClientScopes(), canViewClientScopes(), canListClientScopes(), canManage(ClientScopeModel) and canView(ClientScopeModel), which gate the global Client Scopes admin REST API (/admin/realms/{realm}/client-scopes). None of the tests added in this PR exercise that REST API with a caller that only has Clients-resource-type FGAP permissions (e.g. creating/listing/deleting a client scope via the admin client). The existing tests only cover per-client default/optional client-scope assignment on a specific ClientModel, which goes through canManage(ClientModel)/canConfigure(ClientModel), not the ClientScopeModel-specific methods, leaving a meaningful chunk of new behavior untested.

title: No migration path for realms that already have the admin-permissions client provisioned before the Clients resource type was added
body: init() exits immediately with `if (client != null) { return; }` whenever realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. The new CLIENTS resource type and its scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite, etc.) are only created inside this method, which only runs once when the admin-permissions client is first provisioned. Any realm that already had Admin Fine-Grained Authorization V2 enabled before this change is deployed will keep an admin-permissions resource server that lacks these new scopes/resources forever, since init() will never run its resource/scope creation logic again. Subsequent attempts to create a Clients-type permission on such realms will fail deep inside getOrCreateResource with `ModelException("No scopes found.")` because the required scopes were never added to that resource server. There is no migration/upgrade logic in this PR to reconcile already-provisioned resource servers with the updated schema.

title: Provider event listener now gated by ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), silently skipping cleanup when only V2 is enabled
body: The whole body of registerListener's onEvent was wrapped with `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`. However, `management()`/`evaluator()` elsewhere in this same file only check `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`, and `AdminPermissionsSchema.isAdminPermissionsEnabled()` also only checks the V2 feature — V2 can be enabled independently of V1. With this guard, realms that only enable ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 (not the legacy V1 feature) will no longer process RoleRemovedEvent, ClientRemovedEvent, or GroupRemovedEvent at all, whereas before this change they always were. This appears to have been added only to avoid calling the new ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(), which throws UnsupportedOperationException, but the chosen fix disables event handling for roles and groups too (whose management() implementations are not overridden in V2 and would not have thrown). The consequence is that removing a role or group under a V2-only configuration no longer disables the associated permission state, leaving stale permission data behind.

title: Incorrect Javadoc on void methods requireView() and requireViewClientScopes()
body: The Javadoc added for `void requireView()` (line 98) says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}", and the Javadoc for `void requireViewClientScopes()` (line 103) says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}". Both are void methods that throw ForbiddenException, not boolean-returning methods — this is a copy/paste error inconsistent with every other require*() method in the same interface (e.g. requireListClientScopes(), requireManage(), requireConfigure()), which correctly document the throwing behavior. This is misleading documentation for API consumers.

title: getResourceName() was not updated to handle the new CLIENTS resource type
body: getResourceName() only special-cases `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` to resolve a friendly name ("All users" for the blanket resource, or the username for an individual resource). No equivalent branch was added for CLIENTS, even though this PR introduces the Clients resource type and per-client resources (whose stored resource name is the client's internal ID, per resolveClient()). As a result, any permission representation built for a Clients-type policy falls through to `return resource.getDisplayName();`, which will surface the raw internal client ID (or the literal resource type name "Clients" for the blanket resource) instead of a human-readable name such as the client's clientId or "All clients", unlike the parity that exists for Users.

title: getClientsWithPermission() relies on resource type tagging that individually-created client resources never receive
body: getClientsWithPermission() calls `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` to enumerate resources of type "Clients" and check granted scopes on each. However, AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() (lines 101-111) creates per-object resources via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` without ever calling `resource.setType(...)`; only the single blanket/catch-all resource created in init() has its type explicitly set (`resource.setType(type)`). Because of this, individually-created per-client resources (e.g. the resource representing a single client granted MANAGE/VIEW) are not tagged with type "Clients" and will not be returned by findByType, so getClientsWithPermission will under-report clients that only have an individual (non-blanket) permission grant. There is also no test in this PR that exercises getClientsWithPermission with a per-client (non-'all') grant, so this gap would not be caught by CI.

title: No test coverage for the map-roles-client-scope scope and ClientScopeModel-based permission checks added for Clients
body: The PR adds the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope to the CLIENTS resource type and implements `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)`, as well as `canManage(ClientScopeModel)`/`canView(ClientScopeModel)` overrides used for realm-level client-scope management. None of the new tests in PermissionClientTest (or elsewhere in this PR) exercise canMapClientScopeRoles or the ClientScopeModel-based overrides (e.g. via the /client-scopes admin REST endpoints), unlike MANAGE, CONFIGURE, VIEW, MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE which are all covered. This leaves a meaningful part of the new authorization logic unverified by automated tests.

title: CAUTION note overstates when the rolling-updates feature flag is required
body: The newly added CAUTION block states unconditionally: 'While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail.' This is placed directly under the 'Managing Keycloak Operator Updates' heading, before any explanation of the default behavior. However, the immediately following NOTE says that when `update.strategy` is left unset, the Operator defaults to mimicking the pre-existing (26.1 and older) behavior with no mention of needing the feature flag. This is corroborated by operator/src/test/java/.../UpgradeTest.java, where `createInitialDeployment` only enables the `rolling-updates` feature when an explicit `UpdateStrategy` (e.g. RECREATE) is configured, and returns early (without enabling the feature) when `updateStrategy == null`. So the feature flag is only required when explicitly setting `update.strategy`, not for using the Operator's update mechanism in general. As written, the CAUTION note will mislead readers into thinking they must always enable `rolling-updates` or the Operator will fail, even when relying on default behavior.

title: Feature-disabled gating is only tested for the metadata subcommand, and exit code is never asserted
body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only launches `UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME` without the feature flag and checks the error message. The identical feature-gating logic was also added to `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` (quarkus/runtime/.../UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java), but there is no test exercising the `check` subcommand with the feature disabled. Additionally, the test never asserts the actual exit code (`CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` = 4), even though the documentation (docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc) explicitly documents exit code 4 as the contract for 'feature disabled', and this exit code is meant to be relied upon by automation. Without an assertion on the exit code and without coverage of the `check` subcommand, a regression in either path (e.g., wrong exit code, or the check subcommand silently allowing use when the feature is disabled) would not be caught by tests.

title: Silent reassignment of RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 changes the exit-code contract for existing users
body: This change moves `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and reuses 4 for the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` code. Prior to this PR, any scripts/automation built against the previously-released preview `update-compatibility check` command that interpreted exit code 4 as 'recreate upgrade required' will now observe exit code 4 meaning 'feature disabled' and exit code 3 meaning 'recreate required' — a behavior change with no migration note, deprecation warning, or changelog entry in the diff. Even though the tool is labeled preview, this is a backward-incompatible change to a documented, script-facing contract (the exit codes are explicitly called out in docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc as being safe to depend on), and should be called out explicitly (e.g., in release notes) so existing preview adopters are not silently broken.

title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE value changed from 4 to 3, repurposing exit code 4
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was previously 4 and is now changed to 3, with the freed-up value 4 reassigned to the new FEATURE_DISABLED constant. The update-compatibility check/metadata commands already existed before this PR (only +4/+7 line diffs were needed to add the feature-flag gating), meaning this exit code contract was already shipped and could be relied upon by external automation/scripts that branch on exit code 4 meaning 'recreate update required'. After this change, the same scripts will now interpret exit code 4 as 'feature disabled' and exit code 3 as 'recreate required', silently breaking any existing integration built against the previous exit code semantics. This renumbering is not mentioned in the PR description and should be called out as a breaking change (or avoided by picking an unused code for FEATURE_DISABLED).

title: No test for operator failing when update.strategy is set without the rolling-updates feature enabled
body: The updated docs (docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc) explicitly state: 'While on preview stage, the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the Operator will fail.' However, createInitialDeployment() in this test only ever enables the ROLLING_UPDATES feature together with a non-null UpdateStrategy, and only exercises the default (updateStrategy == null, feature not enabled) and explicit-strategy-with-feature-enabled combinations. There is no test exercising the documented failure path where an explicit update.strategy is configured in the Keycloak CR while the rolling-updates feature is left disabled, so the documented 'Operator will fail' behavior is never verified by this test suite.

title: CAUTION about rolling-updates feature requirement is overly broad relative to actual default behavior
body: The new CAUTION block states unconditionally that 'the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail', placed directly under the 'Managing Keycloak Operator Updates' heading before any mention of the optional update.strategy field. This reads as if the feature flag is required any time this section's functionality (including the default/unconfigured behavior) is used. But per the accompanying UpgradeTest.java changes, when updateStrategy is left unset (no 'update' stanza in the CR), the Operator falls back to legacy (pre-rolling-updates) behavior without requiring the feature flag at all. The caution should clarify that the feature is only required when explicitly setting the `update.strategy` field, not for all uses of the Operator's update handling, to avoid confusing users into thinking the flag is always mandatory.

title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the printed error message ('Unable to use this command. The preview feature ...') but never asserts that the process exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4), which is the new behavior introduced by this PR. Since this PR also changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and introduces FEATURE_DISABLED as 4, the actual exit code values are an important, easily-regressed part of the contract and should be explicitly verified by this test (and by the recreate-path tests) rather than relying solely on message text.

title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE value changed from 4 to 3, reusing 4 for FEATURE_DISABLED
body: CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was previously 4 and is now changed to 3, while the newly introduced FEATURE_DISABLED constant takes over the value 4. This silently changes the exit-code contract of the `update-compatibility check`/`metadata` CLI commands, which the accompanying documentation explicitly encourages users to script against ('the command's exit code can be used to determine the upgrade type'). Any existing automation or CI/CD pipeline built against the previously implemented exit code 4 for 'recreate upgrade required' will now receive exit code 3, and any logic checking for exit code 4 will misinterpret a 'feature disabled' result as 'recreate required'. This renumbering was not strictly necessary for the feature-flag work (a different unused exit code could have been chosen for FEATURE_DISABLED) and is not called out anywhere as an intentional breaking change.

title: Feature-disabled guard is only tested for the metadata subcommand, not for check
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only launches UpdateCompatibility.NAME + UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME without the --features=rolling-updates flag, verifying the new 'feature disabled' error message. However, the identical feature-gating logic was also added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() (quarkus/runtime/.../UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java), and there is no corresponding test verifying that running `update-compatibility check` without the rolling-updates feature enabled also prints the error and exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED. This leaves half of the newly added behavior completely untested.

title: CAUTION about mandatory rolling-updates feature contradicts the default-behavior note that follows
body: The CAUTION block placed immediately under '=== Managing Keycloak Operator Updates (Preview)' states unconditionally that 'the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail.' This reads as applying to the whole update-strategy feature area. However, the NOTE a few lines later explains that, by default (no explicit `update.strategy` set), the Operator falls back to mimicking 26.1-or-older behavior without requiring any feature flag — which matches the operator/src/test/java/.../UpgradeTest.java test setup, where the `updateStrategy == null` case never enables the rolling-updates feature and is expected to succeed. The documentation should clarify that the feature is only mandatory when explicitly configuring `spec.update.strategy`, not for the default/unset case, to avoid confusing operators into thinking the flag is always required.

title: No test verifies the Operator fails when update.strategy is set without enabling the rolling-updates feature
body: The documentation (docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc) explicitly states that while the rolling-updates update-strategy feature is in preview, configuring `spec.update.strategy` without enabling the `rolling-updates` feature flag will cause the Operator to fail. createInitialDeployment() in this test only ever enables the feature together with a non-null update strategy, so this exact failure path (update.strategy set, feature not enabled) is never exercised. There is no negative test confirming the documented failure actually occurs, so a regression that silently ignores or mis-handles this combination would not be caught by this test suite.

title: Group-wide canManage() grants manage rights to callers that only have VIEW permission
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (the no-arg, "all groups" variant), the permission check is `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` – i.e. it treats VIEW as sufficient to satisfy a manage check. Compare this with the per-group override `canManage(GroupModel group)` a few lines below, which correctly checks only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE`. Because `requireManage()` (used e.g. by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() to guard creating top-level groups) ultimately calls this no-arg canManage(), any admin who was only granted the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource is incorrectly treated as having manage rights and can create/modify groups. This is a privilege-escalation bug; it should check AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE only, matching canManage(GroupModel).

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() passes the Resource's internal id instead of the group id, breaking the lookup and the returned ids
body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the lambda receives `groupResource` (a Resource found via findByType) and calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())`. Everywhere else in this class (canView(GroupModel), canManage(GroupModel), canViewMembers, canManageMembers, canManageMembership) the lookup key passed to hasPermission is `group.getId()` – the actual GroupModel id, which is also the value AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() uses as the Resource's *name* when the resource is created. Resource.getId() is a separate, internally-generated identifier that does not equal the resource's name. As a result, the internal `hasPermission(groupId, ...)` call does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` with the wrong value, which will not find the correct resource and will instead always fall back to the catch-all "Groups" resource-type resource. In addition, the ids placed into the returned `granted` set are resource ids, not actual group ids, so callers (UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource) that use this set to filter by `UserModel.GROUPS` will never match real group memberships. This breaks per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS based user visibility for V2 admin permissions.

title: getOrCreateResource() never tags per-resource instances with their resource type
body: getOrCreateResource() creates per-instance resources (for Users, Clients, and now Groups) via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` but never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)` on them, unlike the "all-resource" resources created in init() (which do call resource.setType(type)). Because of this, `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` used by the new GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() will not find individual per-group resources created through this method, since they were never tagged with the "Groups" type. This silently undermines any type-based resource queries introduced for the new Groups feature.

title: Undocumented behavior change: canViewMembers(group) now also honors MANAGE_MEMBERS scope
body: In GroupPermissions.canViewMembers(GroupModel), the scope check was widened from `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` to `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)`. This is part of the stable (GA) ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature, not the new V2 feature this PR is adding. The PR description only mentions adding Groups resource type/scopes to the V2 authorization schema, so this silent semantic change to the existing V1 group-members view permission is undocumented and untested for V1 (the new tests target only the V2/KeycloakAdminPermissionsServerConfig path). Existing V1 deployments relying on manage-members not implying view-members will see a behavior change.

title: Missing negative test that VIEW-only all-groups permission does not grant manage capability
body: testManageAllGroups() only verifies that granting MANAGE on the all-groups resource allows creating/updating groups; there is no test asserting that an admin granted only VIEW on the all-groups resource is still forbidden from creating/updating/deleting groups. Such a test would have caught the bug in GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() where hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) incorrectly allows VIEW to satisfy a manage check.

title: canManage() treats VIEW-only group permission as sufficient to manage groups
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-arg, realm-wide check), the method returns true via `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` — i.e. it accepts either VIEW or MANAGE scope. This is identical to canView()'s body except for the admin-role check, and it means an admin who was granted only a read-only 'view' permission on the Groups resource type is treated as if they also have 'manage' permission. Since GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() calls `auth.groups().requireManage()` to authorize creating new top-level groups, a user with only VIEW scope on Groups would be able to create (and, via other requireManage() call sites, modify) groups, which is a privilege escalation. Compare with canManage(GroupModel) and canManageMembership(GroupModel) in the same class, and with UserPermissions.canManage(), none of which accept VIEW as sufficient for MANAGE — confirming this is inconsistent/incorrect. The call should check only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs, and per-group resources are not discoverable
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() calls `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> ...)` to enumerate group-scoped authorization resources, then calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the result set. However: (1) individual per-group resources are created via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(), which never calls resource.setType(...) (unlike the legacy V1 GroupPermissions.initialize(), which explicitly sets `groupResource.setType("Group")`), so findByType(server, "Groups", ...) will not find per-group resources at all — it will only match the single 'all-groups' placeholder resource created during schema init (which does have its type set). (2) Even for that placeholder, `groupResource.getId()` is the authorization resource's own internal ID, not a GroupModel id; hasPermission(String groupId, ...) expects a real GroupModel id (it looks the resource up via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, and resources are named by the group's id per resolveGroup()). As a result this method either returns an empty set (making the group-based DB pre-filter in UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource a no-op, relying solely on slower per-user canView checks) or, when an 'all-groups' VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission exists, returns a bogus id that does not correspond to any real group, which would be used as a UserModel.GROUPS search filter and could incorrectly exclude all users even though the admin should see them via blanket group-membership permission. This should use `groupResource.getName()` (not getId()) and the underlying resources need a type set so findByType can actually locate them.

title: getResourceName() does not resolve a friendly display name for Group resources
body: getResourceName() special-cases USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE to translate the resource's internal name (the user's UUID) into the user's username (or 'All users' for the catch-all resource), but no equivalent branch was added for the newly introduced GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE even though group resources are created the same way (named by the group's UUID via resolveGroup()). As a consequence, any UI or API that calls getResourceName() for a group-scoped scope-permission will fall through to `resource.getDisplayName()` and show the raw group UUID (or whatever default display name is stored) instead of the group's actual name, unlike the symmetric behavior implemented for Users.

title: Removed short-circuit for global group-view permission when listing subgroups
body: getSubGroups() previously computed `canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView()` once and used `.filter(g -> canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g))`, short-circuiting per-subgroup evaluation when the caller already has global view rights. The change replaces this with `.filter(auth.groups()::canView)`, which invokes canView(GroupModel) for every subgroup even when the admin already has global view permission. For FGAP V2, canView(GroupModel) performs a resource lookup and policy evaluation per call, so for groups with many subgroups this reintroduces an evaluation (and potential DB query) per subgroup instead of a single check, which is a performance regression compared to the previous behavior.

title: Removed short-circuit for global group-view permission when listing top-level groups
body: getGroups() previously cached `canViewGlobal = groupsEvaluator.canView()` and used `.filter(g -> canViewGlobal || groupsEvaluator.canView(g))` to avoid a per-group permission evaluation when the caller already has blanket view rights. This was changed to `.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)`, so canView(GroupModel) — which for FGAP V2 can trigger a resource lookup and policy evaluation — now runs once per group returned by the query instead of being short-circuited by a single global check, which can be a notable performance regression for realms with many groups.

title: Admin fine-grained authz event listener registration now gated at registration time instead of per-event
body: registerListener() used to always register the ProviderEventListener and check `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` inside onEvent() for every incoming event. The change moves the feature check outside, so the listener is only registered if the feature is enabled at the moment registerListener() is invoked (typically once, at provider/session-factory initialization). If the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is toggled on after this registration happens (e.g. in test harnesses or deployments that enable the feature dynamically after providers have already been initialized), RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent cleanup of permissions will silently stop firing, whereas previously it would have resumed working as soon as the flag became true. This is a behavior change that is not obviously covered by tests.

title: No negative test that VIEW-only group permission cannot be used to manage groups
body: testManageAllGroups() only verifies that granting MANAGE scope on the all-groups resource allows group creation/update; there is no test asserting that an admin granted only VIEW (or VIEW_MEMBERS) scope on Groups is still forbidden from creating/updating/deleting groups. Such a test would have caught the canManage() bug in GroupPermissionsV2 where VIEW scope is incorrectly treated as sufficient for manage operations. Additionally, there is no test exercising an 'all-groups' level VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission and verifying that user search via group membership actually returns the expected users, which would have revealed the getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() id-mapping bug.

title: Public utility method removed without deprecation
body: The public static method `ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes(session, realm, attributes, first, max)` was removed outright (callers were updated to call `session.groups().searchGroupsByAttributes(...)` directly in GroupsResource). Although this class lives in server-spi-private, it is a public API surface; removing a public method without a deprecation cycle can break any other internal or external module that still references it directly, since there is no compiler-visible deprecation warning period.

title: canManage() for Groups V2 treats VIEW scope as sufficient for MANAGE, enabling privilege escalation
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() passes resource ID where a domain Group ID (resource name) is expected
body: In `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the code iterates resources of type GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE and calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), VIEW_MEMBERS, MANAGE_MEMBERS)`, then adds `groupResource.getId()` to the granted set. Inside `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)`, the value is used as `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` - i.e. it is treated as the resource's *name*, which (per `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`) is the domain Group's own ID, not the Resource entity's internal ID. Everywhere else in this class (e.g. `canView(GroupModel group)`, `canManage(GroupModel group)`) the method is correctly invoked with `group.getId()` (the domain Group ID == resource name). Passing `groupResource.getId()` (the internal Resource PK) instead of `groupResource.getName()` means the by-name lookup will not find the correct resource, causing the method to fall back to only checking the 'all-groups' resource and to add garbage/internal IDs (not real group IDs) to the returned set. This breaks `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` for admins who were granted VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on individual groups (rather than an all-groups permission): such grants will not be detected, and consumers such as `UsersResource.getUsersCount(realm, search, groupIds)` and the `UserModel.GROUPS` session-attribute optimization will receive an incorrect/empty or meaningless set of IDs, under-counting or mis-filtering visible users.

title: hasPermission() omits resource-id filter present in the analogous UserPermissionsV2 implementation
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes)` evaluates permissions with `root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server), server)` and then checks every returned `Permission`'s scopes without verifying `permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId())`. The structurally similar `UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission(...)` does include this check (`if (permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()))`).
