Without this filter, if the evaluation ever returns permissions for a resource other than the one being checked (e.g. due to how the policy engine aggregates results), GroupPermissionsV2 could incorrectly grant access based on an unrelated resource's permission that happens to share a scope name. This inconsistency with the Users implementation suggests a missed safety check.

title: No test exercises the global canManage()/requireManage() path with only VIEW scope granted
body: `testManageAllGroups()` only tests granting the `MANAGE` scope via `createAllGroupsPermission(policy, Set.of(MANAGE))` and verifies group management becomes possible. There is no test that grants only `VIEW` scope on the all-groups resource and then asserts that group-management operations (e.g. `POST /groups`) remain forbidden. Such a test would have caught the bug in `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` where VIEW scope is incorrectly treated as sufficient for management operations (see separate finding), so its absence is a meaningful coverage gap for this new feature.

title: Interface methods renamed/removed without deprecation on a cross-module interface
body: `GroupPermissionEvaluator` previously exposed `boolean getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel group)` and `Set<String> getGroupsWithViewPermission()`. Both were removed/renamed (the group-specific boolean overload was dropped entirely in favor of `canViewMembers(GroupModel)`, and the Set-returning method was renamed to `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` with a changed return value semantics - names vs. IDs). This interface is consumed outside the `services` module (e.g. `rest/admin-ui-ext`'s `BruteForceUsersResource`), so any other out-of-tree code built against the previous method signatures will fail to compile, with no deprecation cycle offered.

title: error-invalid-multivalued-size rewritten with incompatible Java MessageFormat syntax, breaking i18next interpolation
body: The key was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. This file is consumed by the Account Console React app via i18next, which uses double-curly-brace interpolation (`{{0}}`), as confirmed by every other key in the same file (e.g. `backTo=Back to {{app}}`, `setUpNew=Set up {{name}}`). Switching to single braces means `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` will no longer be substituted by i18next, and the Java `MessageFormat` ChoiceFormat fragment `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` is not valid i18next syntax at all, so it will be rendered verbatim to end users instead of the pluralized word. This is a functional regression in the Account Console error message, seemingly caused by blindly applying the Java-properties fix for this key to the JS i18next resource file as well.

title: error-invalid-multivalued-size rewritten with incompatible Java MessageFormat syntax in Admin Console i18next resources
body: Same issue as in the account-ui file: `error-invalid-multivalued-size=Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` was changed to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The surrounding keys in this file use i18next double-brace interpolation, so this change breaks placeholder substitution and introduces a literal, unparsed ChoiceFormat string that will be shown to admins instead of a correctly pluralized message when editing multivalued user/client attributes.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: The key `totpStep1` was changed from the (stale, link-containing) Lithuanian text to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. This is a user-visible content defect: Lithuanian users configuring an authenticator will now see an unrelated Italian sentence instead of a Lithuanian translation. This appears to be a copy/paste mistake made while fixing the illegal anchor tags flagged by the new sanitizer.

title: Lithuanian login translation replaced with Italian text
body: The key `loginTotpStep1` was changed from the Lithuanian text (which previously contained mismatched FreeOTP/Google Play anchor tags) to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian rather than Lithuanian. This is the same mistake as in the account messages file for the same locale and key, and results in Lithuanian users seeing Italian text on the login TOTP setup page.

title: Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) file now uses Traditional Chinese phrasing
body: The key `totpStep1` was changed to `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`, which uses Traditional Chinese characters/terminology (手機, 裝, 應用程式) rather than Simplified Chinese (which would use 手机, 装, 应用). Since this file is the zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) locale resource, this introduces a script/locale inconsistency that should instead read with Simplified characters, e.g. 在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：

title: Property files are read with default ISO-8859-1 decoding although they contain raw UTF-8 text
body: `bundle = new PropertyResourceBundle(fis)` (and the equivalent call for the English counterpart) uses the InputStream-based constructor, which per the Properties/PropertyResourceBundle contract decodes content as ISO-8859-1. The actual theme message files (as shown throughout this PR, e.g. Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, Greek text) are UTF-8 encoded with literal multi-byte characters, not `\uXXXX`-escaped ASCII. Reading them through the InputStream constructor will corrupt all non-ASCII text used for comparisons and for the diff snippets emitted in error messages, making the tool's diagnostic output unreliable/garbled for the vast majority of real locale files. The code should decode explicitly as UTF-8 (e.g. via `InputStreamReader`/`PropertyResourceBundle(Reader)`).

title: Fragile string-substitution derivation of the English source file path
body: The path to the English counterpart file is computed with `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. This blindly rewrites any occurrence of the literal substring "resources-community" anywhere in the absolute path, and assumes the file name's final underscore-delimited segment is exactly the locale suffix. This is fragile: a checkout path containing "resources-community" elsewhere would be mis-rewritten, and file names containing an underscore before the locale code in a different position (e.g. a base name with an embedded underscore) will compute a non-existent English file name. In fact, the accompanying test had to rename `duplicate_keys.properties` to `duplicateKeys_en.properties` specifically to avoid the mid-name underscore being matched by this regex and resolving to a nonexistent `duplicate_en.properties`, which demonstrates the fragility of this approach in production use.

title: Unchecked RuntimeException thrown instead of using the MojoExecutionException error-reporting path
body: `verifySafeHtml()` wraps IOExceptions (e.g. missing/English file not found) in `RuntimeException` rather than propagating through the `MojoExecutionException` used by `verify()`/`verifyNoDuplicateKeys`. Since `verify()`'s try/catch only catches `IOException`, any IO failure inside `verifySafeHtml()` surfaces as an unchecked `RuntimeException` with a raw stack trace rather than being reported through the structured `messages` list or wrapped the same way other failures are, producing an inconsistent and less actionable failure mode for the Maven build.

title: Choice-format normalization is hardcoded to specific key names, which will miss future keys using the same syntax
body: `normalizeValue` only strips MessageFormat ChoiceFormat syntax (which legitimately contains `<`) for keys matching `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, keys starting with `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit`, or exactly `error-invalid-multivalued-size`. Any new or existing message key elsewhere in the codebase that uses `{n,choice,...}` syntax with a `<` character (a common pattern for pluralization) but isn't in this hardcoded list will be incorrectly flagged as illegal HTML by this verifier, producing false positives that block legitimate translations/content unless the hardcoded list is remembered and updated every time such a key is added.

title: Anchor-tag validation assumes identical ordering between translation and English source
body: `santizeAnchors` walks through anchor tags in the translated value and the English value in lockstep using two independent `Matcher.find()` calls, requiring the Nth anchor tag in the translation to exactly equal the Nth anchor tag in English. Legitimate translations frequently reorder embedded markup (e.g. due to different sentence/grammar structure, as is common for RTL or SOV languages), which would cause a correct translation with the same set of anchors (just reordered) to be reported as "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string", a false positive that would block otherwise-valid translations from passing verification.

title: No test coverage for non-ASCII/UTF-8 property content
body: All added test fixtures (`illegalHtmlTag_en.properties`, `noHtml_en.properties`, `noHtml_de.properties`, `changedAnchor_en.properties`, `changedAnchor_de.properties`) use plain ASCII content. None of the tests exercise a file containing multi-byte UTF-8 characters (Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, etc.), even though essentially all real translated message files in this repository contain such content and the tool reads files via an InputStream-based `PropertyResourceBundle` that decodes as ISO-8859-1. This gap means the encoding-corruption problem for non-ASCII translations is not caught by the test suite.

title: Java-style ChoiceFormat syntax injected into a react-i18next resource bundle
body: Line 188 now reads `error-invalid-multivalued-size=Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` This file is consumed by react-i18next, which uses double-curly-brace interpolation (`{{0}}`, see e.g. line 14 `error-username-invalid-character='{{0}}' contains invalid character.` and the `_one/_other/_zero` suffix convention used elsewhere, e.g. `resourceSharedWith_one`/`resourceSharedWith_other`). Single-brace placeholders and Java's `{N,choice,...}` syntax are not understood by i18next, so this key will render literally (e.g. '...at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.') instead of substituting the validator's parameters. This is a regression from the previous (grammatically poor but functionally correct) `value(s)` wording.

title: Same i18next placeholder/ChoiceFormat regression as account-ui
body: The diff changes `error-invalid-multivalued-size=Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. Like account-ui, admin-ui uses the double-curly-brace i18next convention (unchanged lines around it still use `{{...}}`-style placeholders for other validators). Switching this single key to single braces plus Java ChoiceFormat syntax means react-i18next will not interpolate the values and will show the raw '{0}', '{1}', '{2,choice,...}' text to admins editing user profile attributes with a multivalued validator.

title: Italian text committed into Lithuanian translation file
body: The fix for `totpStep1` replaces a correct (if HTML-laden) Lithuanian sentence with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users configuring the mobile authenticator will now see an Italian instruction instead of their own language. The diff explicitly shows this is a new change introduced by this PR (the previous Lithuanian text is removed).

title: Same Italian-text regression repeated in the login theme's Lithuanian file
body: `loginTotpStep1` is changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian rather than Lithuanian, duplicating the mistake also made in the account theme's messages_lt.properties. This is user-facing text shown during OTP setup for Lithuanian-locale users and should be a proper Lithuanian translation.

title: Traditional Chinese characters used in a Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) resource file
body: The fixed `totpStep1` value is `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`, which uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 應用程式) rather than Simplified Chinese (手机, 应用程序/应用). This file is for locale zh_CN (Simplified, mainland China), so Traditional characters are inconsistent with the rest of the file (e.g. line 29 `email=电子邮件` uses Simplified forms) and will look wrong/inauthentic to Simplified-Chinese users.

title: Properties files are read with the wrong character encoding (ISO-8859-1 instead of UTF-8)
body: `verifySafeHtml()` loads both the target file and its English counterpart via `new PropertyResourceBundle(new FileInputStream(...))`. Per the `PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream)` javadoc, this constructor decodes the stream as ISO-8859-1 (same as `Properties.load(InputStream)`), yet the actual theme message files in this repository store non-ASCII characters directly as UTF-8 text (e.g. Korean, Thai, Arabic, Cyrillic, accented Latin letters) rather than as `\uXXXX` escapes. As a result, every non-ASCII character will be mis-decoded, producing corrupted ('mojibake') text inside the tool and in any 'Illegal HTML in key ...' diagnostic messages it prints. This is inconsistent with `Files.readString(file.toPath())` used a few lines above in `verify()`, which defaults to UTF-8.

title: IOException from missing English counterpart file surfaces as an unchecked RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException
body: `verifySafeHtml()` is called from `verify()` inside a try/catch that only catches `IOException` and rethrows as `MojoExecutionException`. However `verifySafeHtml()` itself swallows `IOException` and rethrows it as a plain `RuntimeException` (lines 70 and 79). If the computed `englishFile` path (derived via brittle string substitution of 'resources-community'->'resources' and the locale suffix) does not actually exist for some theme file, the Mojo will fail with an unhandled `RuntimeException` and a raw stack trace rather than the controlled `MojoExecutionException` the rest of the plugin is designed to produce, making build failures harder to diagnose for plugin users.

title: No test exercises the cross-directory English-file resolution logic used in production
body: All new test fixtures (illegalHtmlTag_en.properties, noHtml_de/en.properties, changedAnchor_de/en.properties) live in the same test-resources directory and only exercise the locale-suffix substitution (e.g. '_de.properties' -> '_en.properties'). None of them exercise the 'resources-community' -> 'resources' directory substitution that `verifySafeHtml()` performs via `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources")`, which is exactly the logic used for the real theme files modified in this PR (e.g. themes/src/main/resources-community/... locating themes/src/main/resources/...). There is also no test for the case where the derived English file does not exist, which (per the other finding) throws an unchecked RuntimeException.

title: i18next placeholder syntax broken for error-invalid-multivalued-size
body: The value for error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from the i18next double-curly-brace interpolation format (`Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).`) to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`, which uses single curly braces plus Java's MessageFormat ChoiceFormat syntax. Every other key in this file (backTo=Back to {{app}}, setUpNew=Set up {{name}}, credentialCreatedAt=<0>Created</0> {{date}}., etc.) uses the `{{var}}` convention required by i18next in the React Account Console. Because i18next does not interpret `{0}` or `{2,choice,...}` syntax, this key will no longer be interpolated at all: end users will literally see `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` in the error message instead of the real attribute name/limits. This looks like the Java-side ChoiceFormat fix needed to satisfy the new HTML sanitizer in the Java theme bundles was mistakenly copy-pasted into this unrelated JS/i18next resource file.

title: Same i18next placeholder regression in Admin Console messages
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. As with the Account Console file, this admin-ui properties file is consumed by i18next which requires `{{var}}` double-brace interpolation, not single braces or Java MessageFormat ChoiceFormat syntax. This will show the raw placeholder text to Admin Console users instead of a properly formatted validation error, and is inconsistent with every other key in the surrounding file that still uses double braces.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: The fix for totpStep1 (removing a mismatched anchor href flagged by the new HTML sanitizer) replaced the Lithuanian sentence with Italian text: 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' (Italian for 'Install one of the following applications on your phone'). This is not Lithuanian, so Lithuanian-speaking Account Console users configuring OTP will now see Italian instructions. Compare with the correctly localized equivalent fixes done in the same PR for Finnish ('Asenna jokin seuraavista sovelluksista matkapuhelimeesi:'), Slovak ('Nainštalujte si do mobilu jednu z nasledujúcich aplikácií:') and Swedish ('Installera en av följande applikationer på din mobil:').

title: Lithuanian login translation also replaced with Italian text
body: loginTotpStep1 was changed to 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian, not Lithuanian. The same erroneous text was introduced here and in the account messages_lt.properties file (totpStep1), so Lithuanian users will see Italian setup instructions on both the login flow and the account console when configuring a mobile authenticator.

title: Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) totpStep1 replaced with Traditional Chinese text
body: The new value for totpStep1, '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 安裝, 應用程式), but this file's locale is zh_CN (Simplified Chinese). Every other string in the same file uses Simplified characters (e.g. mobile=手机, totpStep2=打开应用扫描二维码输入验证码, totpStep3=输入应用提供的一次性验证码单击保存). Mixing Traditional characters into a Simplified-Chinese locale file is a localization regression for mainland-China users and suggests the fix for this key accidentally reused the zh_TW translation instead of a Simplified-Chinese one.

title: Property files are read as ISO-8859-1 instead of UTF-8
body: verifySafeHtml() loads both the checked file and the English reference file via `new PropertyResourceBundle(new FileInputStream(...))`. PropertyResourceBundle's InputStream constructor always decodes the stream as ISO-8859-1, but the actual .properties files in this repository contain literal UTF-8 multi-byte characters (Cyrillic, Arabic, Thai, Korean, CJK, etc., as seen throughout this diff) rather than \uXXXX escapes. Reading them with the wrong charset corrupts every non-ASCII character into mojibake. ASCII-only HTML tags are unaffected, but the diagnostic text appended via messages.add(...) (e.g. 'Illegal HTML in key ... for file ...: ...') will show garbled fragments of the surrounding translated sentence, undermining the usefulness of the new sanitizer's error output for the very (non-English) locale files it is meant to help fix.

title: Brittle derivation of the English reference file path can crash the build ungracefully
body: The English reference bundle path is derived purely by string substitution on the absolute path of the checked file (replaceAll("resources-community", "resources") then replacing the locale suffix with "_en.properties"). This assumes every checked file lives under a path containing the literal substring 'resources-community' and is named '..._<locale>.properties'. Any theme/module with a different layout, or any file without that exact suffix pattern, will make `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` throw FileNotFoundException, which is caught and rethrown as an unchecked RuntimeException (line 79). Since verify() (lines 46-56) only catches the checked IOException and wraps it in MojoExecutionException, this RuntimeException propagates out of the Mojo uncaught, producing a raw stack trace instead of the structured Mojo failure used for the other checks in this class.

title: Anchor mismatch leaves partially-stripped HTML, causing duplicate error messages
body: santizeAnchors stops removing matched / tags as soon as it hits a mismatch and breaks out of the loop (line 158), leaving the mismatched tag (and any after it) still embedded in the returned value. verifySafeHtml() subsequently runs the HTML policy sanitizer over that same value, so the still-embedded anchor tag is flagged again as 'Illegal HTML'. A single changed/malicious link therefore produces two separate messages ('Didn't find anchor tag ...' and 'Illegal HTML in key ...') for the same root cause, which can be confusing when triaging a CI failure.

title: Check is sensitive to the sanitizer's own serialization, not just real HTML safety
body:
The sanitized output of policy.sanitize(value) is compared byte-for-byte to the original value. The OWASP sanitizer re-serializes self-closing elements with a space before '/>' (turning '
' into '
'), so a translation using the equally valid '
' form fails the check even though there is no actual markup injection. This PR had to edit dozens of locale files (ar, ca, cs, de, el, es, fa, fi, hr, ka, ko, sk, th, tr, uk, zh_CN, zh_TW, fr, en, etc.) purely to insert a space before '/>' to satisfy the sanitizer's canonical form. Future translation contributions using '
' will fail CI with a misleading 'Illegal HTML' message unrelated to security.

title: Test fixture contains malformed HTML (missing closing bracket)
body:
The fixture value is `key=Some
tag' and the file has no trailing newline. This appears to be an unintentional typo (likely meant to be `
`); the test still happens to fail because of the unmatched `
` opening tag, but the fixture does not actually represent a well-formed-but-disallowed HTML tag as its name implies, reducing confidence that the scenario is tested as intended.

title: No regression test for HTML that legitimately matches between English and translation
body:
All four tests in this file check failure scenarios (disallowed tag, HTML added only in the translation, mismatched anchor href). There is no fixture/test asserting that a translation whose HTML matches the English source exactly (e.g. both containing an identical `...`) passes with zero messages. Given how sensitive the comparison is to exact formatting (the PR had to rewrite `
` to `
` across dozens of locale files to satisfy it), a positive test would help guard against future regressions where legitimately matching, safe HTML starts being flagged as illegal.

title: Copy-paste bug: rawTokenId null-check is never performed
isAccessTokenId() grant-shortcut check is logically inverted and off-by-one, so it never actually validates the grant type
body:
The new helper `isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut)` is supposed to verify that the encoded access-token id contains the expected grant-type shortcut (at positions 4-5 of the 6-character context prefix, per DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider's encoding: sessionType[0-1] + tokenType[2-3] + grantType[4-5]). The implementation has two combined defects:
1. It extracts `items[0].substring(3, 5)` instead of `substring(4, 6)`, so it reads the wrong characters (half of the tokenType shortcut and half of the grantType shortcut) rather than the actual grant-type shortcut.
2. The condition is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns a non-match precisely when the (wrongly extracted) substring equals the expected value, instead of returning a non-match when it does NOT equal the expected value.
Because of the wrong substring range, the extracted characters will essentially never equal `expectedGrantShortcut`, so the `if` branch is effectively never taken and the method degenerates into validating only that the raw id part is a UUID. This means all the call sites that were updated to use this helper (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) do not actually assert that the correct grant-type shortcut was embedded in the token id, silently defeating the purpose of the new assertion and hiding future regressions in the grant-type encoding.

title: New mandatory getShortcut() method breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: A new abstract method `String getShortcut();` was added to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory provider-factory interface with no default implementation. Any existing third-party/custom implementation of this SPI (grant types are a documented extension point) will fail to compile/deploy until it implements this new method, and any already-compiled custom provider will throw AbstractMethodError at runtime when loaded against the new interface. This is a breaking SPI change that should at least be called out as such (or given a default implementation) given it is not accompanied by any deprecation path.

title: Backward-incompatible change to access-token id (jti) format is not documented
body: `initToken()` now prefixes every access-token id with a 6-character encoded context (session type + token type + grant type) before the previously plain UUID, e.g. `onrtac:1f65761e-...` instead of a bare UUID. This changes the format of the `jti` claim for every access token issued by Keycloak going forward. Any external system, log parser, SIEM rule, or client integration that validates/parses the token id as a plain UUID (36 chars, specific dash positions) will break. The PR does not include any upgrade-guide note, migration documentation, or changelog entry describing this change in token id format, even though it affects every issued access token by default with no opt-out configuration (only an SPI override is possible, which requires writing custom provider code).

title: Duplicate-shortcut validation logic in postInit() has no test coverage
body: postInit() contains important validation logic that throws an IllegalStateException if two registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations collide on id or shortcut (`grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()`). This is the only safety net preventing silently incorrect token-id decoding when a new grant type is added with a clashing shortcut. The added DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest only exercises DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider with hand-built maps and never calls postInit() with a real (or fake) KeycloakSessionFactory/provider-factory stream, so this validation path is completely untested.

title: isAccessTokenId() matcher has inverted logic and off-by-one substring indices
Constructor validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId
New abstract method getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` is a provider factory interface that custom/extension grant-type providers can implement. This PR adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut();` with no default implementation. Any existing third-party implementation of this interface (compiled against the previous version, or even recompiled without updating) will fail to compile or throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime, because the interface contract has changed without providing backward compatibility (e.g. a default method returning a fallback shortcut). This is a breaking API/contract change for anyone extending this SPI.

title: Removed public copy constructor from OAuth2GrantType.Context without deprecation
body: The public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` was removed from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. This is a public API that any custom `OAuth2GrantType`/`OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation might rely on to clone/wrap a Context object (e.g. to adjust grant type before delegating). Removing it outright, rather than deprecating first, is a binary/source compatibility break for any external code using this constructor.

title: Potential NullPointerException if cache-miss fallback runs before postInit() populates sessionFactory
body:
`getGrantTypeByShortcut()` (and similarly `getShortcutByGrantType()` at line 110) dereferences `sessionFactory` directly in the fallback branch used when a shortcut/grant type isn't found in the cached maps:
```
sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class) ...
```
`sessionFactory` is only assigned inside `postInit()`. If this provider's methods are invoked (by this factory or any other SPI) before `postInit()` runs, or if `create()`/the provider instance is otherwise used prior to full lifecycle completion, this throws an unguarded NPE instead of gracefully returning null/unknown. There is no null-check or lazy-initialization guard protecting this access.

title: Test catches overly broad RuntimeException, masking an unrelated NPE instead of verifying intended IllegalArgumentException
body: `testIncorrectGrantType()` builds a `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` by calling only `init(null)` and manually populating `grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts`, without ever calling `postInit()`. This leaves the factory's `sessionFactory` field null. The test then calls `provider.getTokenContextFromTokenId("ofrtac:5678")` with grant shortcut `ac` absent from the stub map, which triggers `getGrantTypeByShortcut()`'s fallback branch that dereferences the null `sessionFactory`, throwing a `NullPointerException` rather than the intended `IllegalArgumentException` for an unrecognized grant shortcut. Because the test catches the overly broad `RuntimeException`, it passes regardless of which exception is actually thrown, so it does not verify the intended validation behavior and would silently continue to pass even if the real `IllegalArgumentException` path were broken.

title: Access token id format change (non-UUID prefix) has no migration/compat notes and may break consumers assuming UUID-formatted token ids
body: `initToken()` now sets the access token's `id` (the `jti` claim) to an encoded value like `onrtac:1f65761e-...` rather than a plain UUID produced by `KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()`. This changes the format/contract of the access token id for all tokens going forward. The PR itself had to update `AssertEvents` test matchers (replacing `isUUID()` checks on `TOKEN_ID` details with a new matcher) because of this format change, demonstrating that other code paths, external integrations, logging/analytics tooling, or custom extensions that assume access token ids are plain 36-character UUIDs (e.g. any `UUID.fromString()` parsing, fixed-length storage, or string-length assumptions) could break. No changelog/upgrade-guide note or compatibility discussion is included for this change in token id semantics.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId
isAccessTokenId() matcher has wrong substring offset and inverted boolean logic, making it a no-op check
body:
The new helper `isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut)` is supposed to verify that the grant-type shortcut encoded in the access token id matches the expected grant. Two bugs make this check ineffective:
1. Wrong offset: the encoded context is laid out as sessionType(2 chars) + tokenType(2 chars) + grantType(2 chars), so the grant shortcut occupies index 4-6, but the code extracts `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, which actually reads the last char of the tokenType plus the first char of the grantType – never the real grant shortcut.
2. Inverted logic: even if the offset were correct, the code does `if (... .equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` – i.e. it treats a *matching* shortcut as a failed match, and anything that does NOT match falls through to `return isUUID().matches(items[1])`, which ignores the grant check entirely.
Combined, this matcher effectively never fails on the grant-type portion of the token id (it only checks that the raw-id portion is a UUID), so all the test assertions added in this PR (`expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectAuthReqIdToToken`) do not actually verify that the correct grant-type shortcut was encoded into the token id, defeating the purpose of the new test coverage.

title: Javadoc claims shortcuts are usually 3 characters, but implementation hard-requires exactly 2
body: The Javadoc for `getShortcut()` states: "usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants". However, every built-in implementation in this PR (ac, cc, ci, dg, pc, pg, ro, rt, te) uses exactly 2 characters, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId()` hard-codes the expectation that the encoded prefix is exactly 6 characters (2 for session type + 2 for token type + 2 for grant type), throwing `IllegalArgumentException("Expected length of 6")` otherwise. A third-party implementor following the documented "3-letters" guidance would produce tokens that encode successfully (encodeTokenId has no length check) but fail to decode later, since nothing enforces/validates the 2-character contract. The documentation should state the actual required length (2 chars), and ideally the implementation should validate it.

title: New mandatory getShortcut() method breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: `getShortcut()` is added as a new abstract method on the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface with no default implementation. Any existing custom/third-party implementation of this provider factory (a supported SPI extension point, registered via META-INF/services) will fail to compile/deploy against this version until it implements the new method. Additionally, if such an implementation is updated hastily and returns null for the shortcut, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` will call `grantsByShortcuts.put(null, grantName)` on a `ConcurrentHashMap`, which throws `NullPointerException` at server startup (postInit), bringing down the whole realm/session factory initialization rather than failing gracefully for just that custom provider.

title: Removal of public copy constructor Context(Context) is a binary/source compatibility break
body: The previous version of `OAuth2GrantType.Context` had a public copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` that cloned all fields from another Context instance. This PR removes that constructor entirely (per the diff) in favor of recomputing `grantType` only in the main constructor. Since `Context` is a public nested class in a provider-facing API, removing a public constructor without deprecation is a backward-incompatible change for any code (including third-party extensions of OAuth2GrantType/OAuth2GrantTypeBase) that relied on cloning a Context via this constructor; such code will now fail to compile.

title: No validation that registered grant shortcuts are non-null and exactly 2 characters long
Recovery-code metadata (hash, label, timestamp) is dropped when delegating to a UserStorageProvider
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential() builds a plain UserCredentialModel containing only the raw, unhashed JSON list of generated codes (recoveryCodesJson) and passes that to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). The already-built RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel passed into the method (which contains the hashed codes, the user-chosen label and the generation timestamp) is only used on the local-storage fallback path and is discarded whenever a UserStorageProvider accepts the update. Any UserStorageProvider implementation therefore receives raw codes and no label/timestamp, and must re-implement hashing and reconstruct metadata itself (or lose it entirely, as the shipped reference implementation does). This is a real loss of functionality/metadata for the new 'recovery codes in user storage' feature, not just a theoretical concern, since the included test provider demonstrates exactly this loss.

title: Recovery codes are persisted unhashed in the reference UserStorageProvider implementation
body: In updateCredential(), the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE branch stores input.getChallengeResponse() (the raw, unhashed JSON array of generated recovery codes) directly as credentialData with no hashing, unlike how the local DB-backed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider stores codes (hashed). This is the provider shipped as the reference/test implementation for the new 'store recovery codes in user storage' feature, and it stores backup authentication codes in cleartext, which is an insecure pattern that could be copied by real implementers of UserStorageProvider.

title: Recovery codes validated through the user-storage provider are never marked as consumed, allowing infinite reuse
body: isValid() for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` and never removes/marks the matched code as used, nor persists any updated state back to `myUser.recoveryCodes`. Recovery/backup codes are meant to be single-use; with this implementation the exact same code can be used to authenticate an unlimited number of times when the credential is stored via this UserStorageProvider, defeating the core security property of recovery codes. Because the integration test (testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin) only logs in once, this defect is not caught by the new tests.

title: getCredentials() can throw NullPointerException when the user is unknown to this storage
body: getCredentials(RealmModel, UserModel) calls `getMyUser(user)` and then immediately dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes`/`myUser.otp` without checking `myUser != null`. Every other method in this class that uses getMyUser() (getDisableableCredentialTypesStream, isConfiguredFor) explicitly guards against a null result, but this new method does not, so a call for a user not present in the backing map will throw an NPE instead of returning an empty stream.

title: New recovery-codes-in-user-storage test does not cover code consumption, reuse prevention, or credential removal
body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only sets up recovery codes in the custom user storage and performs a single successful login with one code. It never verifies that a used code cannot be reused, that the credential is removed/required action re-added once all codes are consumed (mirroring RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator's allCodesUsed()/removeStoredCredentialById logic), or that disabling/removing the credential works for the federated case (as is done for OTP in testOTPSetupAndRemoveThroughAccountMgmtAndLogin and testDisableCredentialsInUserStorage). As a result, the actual data-integrity bug in the shipped BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid() (codes never consumed) goes undetected.

title: Hard-coded credential provider id instead of the existing constant
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential() looks up the provider with the literal string "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" instead of RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID, which was previously referenced directly (and imported) in RecoveryAuthnCodesAction before this change removed that import. Using a magic string loses compile-time safety: if the provider id ever changes, this call will silently fail at runtime (NPE from session.getProvider returning null) instead of failing to compile.

title: New getCredentials() override also changes existing OTP credential exposure, outside the scope of the recovery-codes feature
body: To support the new feature, updateCredential() now assigns a real generated id to the OTP CredentialModel (newOTP.setId(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())), and the newly added getCredentials() override unconditionally includes myUser.getOtp() whenever an OTP credential exists. Previously this provider did not implement getCredentials(), so OTP credentials were not exposed through the generic federated-credential discovery path at all. This is a behavior change for OTP handling in this provider that is incidental to the recovery-codes feature and is not covered by any new or existing test specifically validating that OTP account-management flows (e.g. listing/deleting OTP credentials via account REST) still behave the same with this newly real, generated credential id.

title: Recovery codes are passed unhashed to user-storage credential update, enabling plaintext storage
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential() builds a UserCredentialModel from the raw/unhashed `generatedCodes` list (JSON-serialized) and hands it to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(), while the local-DB fallback path uses `credentialModel`, which already contains hashed codes. Nothing in the API/contract requires a UserStorageProvider implementing updateCredential() for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE to hash the raw value before persisting it (unlike the Password case, which explicitly hashes via PasswordHashProvider). The reference implementation shipped in this very PR (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential/isValid) indeed stores and compares the raw codes verbatim with no hashing at all, meaning recovery codes end up persisted in plaintext when backed by user storage, unlike the hashed codes stored for local-DB users. This is a security regression/inconsistency for a feature whose whole purpose is one-time secret codes.

title: getCredentials() loses the stored credential id and userLabel for recovery codes
body: In getCredentials(), the OTP branch returns the actually stored CredentialModel object (myUser.getOtp()), preserving its id. The recovery-codes branch instead builds a brand new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel via createFromValues(...) and never copies over myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() (which was set in updateCredential() via KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()). As a result, the credential model returned to callers (e.g. RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential -> RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator) has a different/undefined id than the one actually stored. Any subsequent operation that references the credential by this id (e.g. authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()) in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.action() when allCodesUsed()) will fail to locate/remove the real stored credential, since the id doesn't match. Additionally, myUser.recoveryCodes.getUserLabel() is read here but userLabel is never set in updateCredential(), so it is always null.

title: Recovery codes stored via user storage are never consumed, breaking single-use guarantee
body: isValid() for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks whether the submitted code exists in the stored list (generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...)); it never removes or flags the matched code as used, nor persists any updated state back into myUser.recoveryCodes. Consequently, a recovery code backed by this user storage provider can be reused an unlimited number of times, unlike the local/DB-backed implementation where recovery codes are intended to be single-use (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.allCodesUsed() logic depends on per-code consumption). This defeats a core security property of recovery/backup codes for any user whose credentials are stored via a UserStorageProvider following this pattern.

title: getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() not updated for recovery codes
body: This PR adds RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE support to supportsCredentialType, updateCredential, isConfiguredFor, isValid and getCredentials, but getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() (lines 255-264) still only ever returns CredentialModel.OTP. As a result, a user whose recovery codes are stored in this user-storage provider can never have that credential listed/disabled through the standard disable-credential API/UI, unlike OTP, leaving the new feature only partially wired up.

title: New test does not verify single-use/exhaustion behaviour of recovery codes in user storage
body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin() only performs a single successful login using one recovery code and then logs out; it never attempts to reuse the same code, nor exhausts all codes to verify that the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action is re-triggered. Given that BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid() never marks codes as consumed (see related finding), this test suite does not catch that regression, so the single-use guarantee for recovery codes stored via user storage is effectively untested.

title: getCredentials() can NPE if user is not present in the backing map
body: getCredentials() calls `var myUser = getMyUser(user);` and immediately dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` / `myUser.otp` without a null check, unlike isConfiguredFor() and isValid() in the same class which explicitly guard with `if (myUser == null) return false;`. If this method is ever invoked for a user no longer present in the in-memory map, it will throw a NullPointerException instead of returning an empty stream.

title: Recovery codes are sent unhashed to the federated/user-storage credential provider
body: In createRecoveryCodesCredential(), the raw, unhashed generatedCodes list (the plaintext codes shown to the user) is JSON-serialized and passed as the challenge response of the UserCredentialModel given to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). For local storage, recovery codes are hashed via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode() before being persisted (as used when building credentialModel). But the user-storage path receives the plaintext codes directly, with no hashing step. Any UserStorageProvider implementing CredentialInputUpdater (and the sample BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage added by this PR) ends up storing recovery codes in plaintext, which is a weaker security posture than the hashed local storage and is inconsistent/undocumented behavior for third parties implementing this SPI.

title: Recovery codes are never consumed, allowing indefinite reuse of the same code
body: In isValid(), the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE branch only checks whether input.getChallengeResponse() exists in the stored generatedKeys list; it never removes/marks the matched code as used nor persists any updated state back to myUser.recoveryCodes. This breaks the fundamental single-use guarantee of recovery/backup codes: once stored in user storage, the exact same code can be used to authenticate repeatedly. The new test (testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin) only performs a single login with a single code and never attempts to reuse a code or exhaust all codes, so this regression is not caught.

title: disableCredentialType() does not support recovery-codes, breaking the "all codes used" cleanup path for federated storage
body: disableCredentialType() only handles OTP types (isOTPType check); RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE falls into the else branch and just logs "Unsupported to disable credential of type". RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.action() calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...) when recoveryCodeCredentialModel.allCodesUsed() is true, to clear the exhausted credential and force CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES again. For a recovery-codes credential now created in user storage (as enabled by this PR), that cleanup relies on the storage provider supporting removal/disabling of this credential type, which this sample implementation does not provide, so the exhausted credential effectively cannot be cleared when stored via user storage. Additionally, getCredentials() rebuilds the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel via createFromValues() without restoring the originally generated credential id (myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()), so even id-based removal would target the wrong id.

title: New recovery-codes-in-user-storage test does not exercise single-use enforcement or code exhaustion
body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin() sets up recovery codes in user storage and logs in exactly once using a single code. It never attempts to reuse the same code (to verify it is rejected) nor exhausts all codes (to verify the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action is re-triggered and the exhausted credential is properly removed). Given that the underlying sample provider has gaps in consumption tracking and credential removal for this type (see isValid()/disableCredentialType()), this is exactly the scenario that needed coverage and is missing.

title: Hardcoded credential provider id string instead of reusing the existing constant
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential() looks up the provider using the literal string "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" instead of RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID (which was used directly in RecoveryAuthnCodesAction before this change and was removed from that file as part of this PR). Duplicating the id as a magic string is fragile: if the provider id constant ever changes, this call site will silently fail to find the provider (returning null) without any compile-time safety net.

title: Logout result not asserted in new recovery-codes test
body: In testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin(), testAppHelper.logout() is called without wrapping it in assertTrue(...), unlike other tests in this file (e.g. loginSuccessAndLogout, testOTPUpdateAndLogin) which assert the boolean result of logout(). As written, a failed logout would go unnoticed by this test.

title: Same concurrent-delete NPE risk remains in sibling getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: getSubGroupsCount() was fixed to null-check the result of modelSupplier.get() before calling getSubGroupsCount() on it (lines 272-276), but the three overloaded getSubGroupsStream methods (lines 254-257, 259-263, 265-269) still do `return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` without any null check. modelSupplier.get() calls getGroupModel() -> cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(realm, cached.getId()), which can legitimately return null if the group is concurrently deleted — exactly the race this PR is meant to fix. Calling getSubGroupsStream(...) on that null result will still NPE, so the reported concurrency bug can still occur through these paths even after this patch, leaving the fix incomplete.

title: getSubGroupsCount() now can return null, a contract change that may just relocate the NPE
body: The fix changes getSubGroupsCount() to return null when the underlying group model can no longer be resolved (concurrently deleted), instead of throwing NPE. This is a behavior/contract change for an interface method that previously always returned a non-null Long in the success case. Callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount (representation.setSubGroupCount(group.getSubGroupsCount())) tolerate null, but other call sites across the codebase that unconditionally unbox or otherwise assume a non-null Long were not audited/updated in this PR, so the underlying race may simply surface as an NPE somewhere else instead of being eliminated.

title: Background reader thread is never joined before asserting on caughtExceptions, creating a race in the regression test
body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, a background Thread is started (line 139) that loops calling groups() until deletedAll is set to true. After deleting all groups and setting deletedAll.set(true) (line 155), the test immediately asserts assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty()) (line 157) without calling Thread.join(). The background thread only checks the flag at the top of its loop, so an exception produced by a request that is in-flight (or about to run) when the flag flips may be recorded into caughtExceptions after the assertion has already executed, letting a real regression pass unnoticed (false negative). Additionally, since the thread is never joined, it can keep running past the end of the test method, continuing to call the admin client/HTTP client after the test's injected resources (managedRealm, adminClient) may be torn down, risking flakiness or interference with subsequent tests.

title: Fix for NPE on concurrent group deletion is incomplete - sibling methods still dereference a possibly-null model
body: getSubGroupsCount() was patched to call `modelSupplier.get()` and check for null before invoking a method on it, but the sibling overloads `getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer)` (line 256), `getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer)` (line 262) and `getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer)` (line 268) still do `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` without any null check. These methods hit exactly the same underlying race described in the issue (the cached group's backing persistent entity being concurrently deleted so `cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(...)` returns null). Since these call paths are not protected, the same NullPointerException can still be thrown from these methods under concurrent group deletion, meaning the reported bug is only partially fixed.

title: getSubGroupsCount() now silently returns null, changing the method's implicit contract
body: `getSubGroupsCount()` previously threw an NPE when the backing group model vanished during concurrent access; the fix now returns `null` in that case (`return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();`). This changes observable behavior for every caller that assumed a non-null Long (e.g. UI/serialization code that expects a count, sorting/comparison logic, or future unboxing to a primitive). Returning null silently swaps a visible failure for a subtly wrong result (e.g. a group with unknown/zero subgroups reported as null) instead of handling the stale/invalidated-cache condition explicitly (e.g. refreshing the cache entry or falling back to a sensible value).

title: New concurrency test leaks a background thread and has a race between thread completion and assertion
body: The new `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` test spawns a raw `Thread` that loops reading groups until `deletedAll` becomes true, but it never calls `thread.join()` before asserting `caughtExceptions` is empty (line 157). The main thread sets `deletedAll.set(true)` (line 155) and immediately asserts, without waiting for the background thread to observe the flag and actually stop; any exception thrown by the background thread's last in-flight call after the assertion has already run is never captured, so the test can report success even when the race condition it is meant to catch actually occurred (flaky false negative). Additionally, if an exception were thrown between starting the thread and `deletedAll.set(true)` (e.g. in the delete loop), the thread would never be stopped (no try/finally around setting the flag), leaking a thread that keeps hammering the admin REST API for the lifetime of the JVM/test run and potentially polluting subsequent tests.

title: Unrelated removal of a helper method not explained by the PR description
body: This PR, whose stated purpose is fixing an NPE on concurrent group cache access, also removes the private method `groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement` from `GroupUtils`. This change is unrelated to group caching/concurrency and is not mentioned in the PR description. If this method was leftover/dead code it's fine to clean up, but bundling an unrelated and unexplained removal into a bugfix PR makes the change harder to review and risks accidentally reverting logic intended for other in-flight work (e.g. a search/filter feature) without anyone noticing.

title: Fix for the concurrent-delete NPE is only applied to getSubGroupsCount(), leaving identical bug in sibling getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: getSubGroupsCount() was changed to null-check the result of modelSupplier.get() before calling getSubGroupsCount() on it, to avoid an NPE when the backing group was concurrently deleted. However getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) (line 256), getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer) (line 262) and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) (line 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` directly without checking for null. If the group is concurrently removed from the DB while one of these methods is invoked (the exact scenario described in issue #40368), modelSupplier.get() will return null and these three methods will throw the same NullPointerException the PR claims to fix. The fix is incomplete and the underlying race condition remains reachable through these code paths.

title: Background reading thread is not joined and can leak or produce false-negative assertions
body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti(), a plain non-daemon Thread is started to repeatedly call groups() while the main thread deletes groups. After the delete loop finishes, deletedAll.set(true) is called and the assertion on caughtExceptions runs immediately with no Thread.join()/wait. There's a race: the main thread can read and assert on caughtExceptions before the background thread has finished its current REST call and recorded a thrown exception, so the test can pass even though the race condition actually occurred (false negative). In addition, if an earlier step throws (e.g. the fail() call in the creation loop, or an exception from groupUuuids.forEach(...).remove()) before deletedAll.set(true) is reached, the background thread's while(!deletedAll.get()) loop will never terminate, leaking a running thread that keeps hitting the admin API indefinitely and can interfere with subsequent tests or prevent clean JVM shutdown. The test should join the thread (with a timeout) and use try/finally to guarantee deletedAll is always set.

title: Unrelated removal of private helper method bundled into the NPE bug-fix PR
body: This PR removes the private method groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement(GroupModel, String) entirely, which has nothing to do with the stated purpose of the PR (fixing an NPE when accessing a group concurrently) and is not mentioned in the PR description. Bundling unrelated dead-code removal into a targeted bug-fix PR makes the change harder to review and bisect, and risks silently reverting functionality that may have been intended for use elsewhere (even though currently unused) without any explanation.

title: Negative-offset 'advanced pagination' branch will crash with ValueError, not optimize anything
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset` (and potentially negative `stop`). Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ explicitly rejects negative slice bounds with `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` - it does NOT translate them into reverse-order SQL. So any request that reaches this branch (e.g. a client supplying a cursor string with a negative offset, such as `0:-5:0`) will raise an unhandled 500 error instead of the claimed 'efficient bidirectional pagination'. The entire advertised performance feature of this PR is non-functional for Django ORM querysets, and the inline comment "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is factually incorrect.

title: Shared BasePaginator.get_result modified for a niche feature, affecting every consumer
body: The change clamps `offset` to `max(0, offset)` only for non-prev cursors inside `BasePaginator.get_result`, which is the base class used by `Paginator` and `DateTimePaginator` across the entire codebase (not just the audit log endpoint being modified). Previously, a cursor with a negative offset (constructible via `Cursor.from_string`, e.g. a malformed/tampered cursor) would propagate the negative start into the queryset slice and raise a Django `ValueError`. Now it silently resets to offset 0, changing behavior for every endpoint using this base paginator. This is a broad, unscoped change to shared infrastructure to support a feature that should have been isolated to the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` subclass, creating unnecessary regression risk across the product.

title: Possible AttributeError/None-access on organization_context.member.has_global_access
body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally. Due to short-circuiting, if `request.user.is_superuser` is False, `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is accessed. If `organization_context.member` can be `None` (e.g. for certain contexts) or the RPC member model does not expose a `has_global_access` attribute, this will raise an `AttributeError`, causing a 500 for any non-superuser authorized org member who passes `optimized_pagination=true`. This should be validated/guarded (e.g. `getattr` with default, or explicit None check) before merging.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates ~90 lines of BasePaginator.get_result instead of reusing it
body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` copy-pastes nearly the entirety of `BasePaginator.get_result` (cursor handling, hits counting, result trimming, cursor building, post-query filtering) and only diverges for the negative-offset branch. This duplication means any future bug fix or behavior change made to `BasePaginator.get_result` (including the clamp logic just added in this same PR) will silently diverge between the two implementations, which is a maintenance and correctness risk. The differing logic should be factored out (e.g. an overridable method for computing `start_offset`/`stop`) rather than duplicating the whole method.

title: Misleading comments claim unsafe/incorrect behavior is 'safe'
body: Comments state "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" and "This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level". Both claims are incorrect: Django raises a `ValueError` for negative slice bounds (it does not support reverse/negative indexing on QuerySets), and permission scoping on the queryset has nothing to do with whether negative offsets are 'safe' to use for slicing. These comments will mislead future maintainers about both the feature's correctness and the reasoning behind it.

title: Undocumented, unvalidated query parameter controls server-side pagination strategy
body: `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` introduces a new, undocumented API query parameter that is not validated through `AuditLogQueryParamSerializer` and silently changes which paginator class (and therefore which code path, including the buggy negative-offset handling) is used. This is an unreviewed/undocumented API surface change: there's no serializer validation, no API documentation update, and the exact-string comparison (`"true"`) means values like `"True"` or `"1"` silently fall back to default pagination with no error, which is confusing behavior for API consumers.

title: Negative offsets handled inconsistently with existing paginator conventions in the same file
body: Elsewhere in this same file, `OffsetPaginator.get_result` and `MergingOffsetPaginator.get_result` explicitly treat negative offsets as invalid input and raise `BadPaginationError("Pagination offset cannot be negative")`. This PR instead attempts to actively support negative offsets in `OptimizedCursorPaginator`/`BasePaginator`, which is inconsistent with the established convention and, combined with the Django slicing restriction, results in an unhandled exception (500) rather than a controlled `BadPaginationError` (400) response.

title: No test coverage added for new OptimizedCursorPaginator
body: The PR adds a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` class with a novel negative-offset code path and an `enable_advanced_features` flag, but no tests are included (or referenced) that exercise this class, including the negative-offset branch that is actually broken. Given this is new pagination logic affecting a security/permission-gated feature, the lack of tests means the crash bug identified above would not be caught by CI.

title: No test coverage for new conditional pagination branch in endpoint
body: The new `if use_optimized and enable_advanced` branch introduces a new execution path (superuser/global-access gated optimized pagination) in `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get`, but no new or updated tests are included to verify this behavior (e.g. that non-privileged users fall back to `DateTimePaginator`, or that the optimized path behaves correctly), despite this being user/permission-facing logic.

title: Comment describes a feature that this diff does not actually implement
body: The added comment claims "Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios" and that this "enables efficient reverse pagination", but the diff makes no functional change to `Cursor.__init__` (`self.offset = int(offset)` is unchanged). The comment is misleading documentation that implies new capability was added here, when in fact the negative-offset handling (and its bug) lives entirely in `paginator.py`.

title: Negative-offset "advanced" pagination path will raise a Django exception, not work as advertised
body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly disallows negative slice bounds and raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` for any negative start/stop. This means the entire "negative offset / bidirectional pagination" feature that this PR is centered on will always throw an unhandled exception (500 error) the moment it is actually exercised, rather than providing the claimed performance benefit. Since a client can control `cursor.offset` via the opaque cursor string (parsed by `Cursor.from_string` without validation), any user granted `enable_advanced_features` (superuser or org member with global access) can trivially trigger this crash.

title: Misleading comment claims Django ORM "properly handles negative slicing automatically"
body: The comment above the negative-offset branch states that "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" and that the operation "is safe". This is factually incorrect — Django's QuerySet slicing explicitly rejects negative indices with a ValueError. The comment will mislead future maintainers into believing this code path is safe/functional when it is not (see the related bug finding), making debugging harder.

title: Shared BasePaginator.get_result modified for an audit-log-only feature, with a comment that contradicts the actual behavior
body: `BasePaginator.get_result` (used by `Paginator`, `DateTimePaginator`, and every other consumer across the codebase, not just the audit log endpoint) was changed to clamp offsets with `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. The accompanying comment claims this change is meant to "allow negative offsets to enable efficient bidirectional pagination," but the code actually does the opposite — it clamps negative offsets to zero when not `cursor.is_prev`, silently discarding/changing behavior that previously would have surfaced as an error for a negative offset. Modifying this widely-shared base class for the sake of one experimental audit-log feature risks unintended regressions in dozens of unrelated paginated endpoints, and no new tests were added to validate the change against existing paginator behavior.

title: Potential AttributeError if organization_context.member is None
body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` directly accesses `organization_context.member.has_global_access` without checking whether `member` is `None`. If a non-superuser request reaches this endpoint with `organization_context.member` unset (e.g., certain staff/service-account flows that don't carry an org membership), this line will raise an `AttributeError` and turn into an unhandled 500 error instead of a graceful permission denial.

title: New query parameter bypasses the endpoint's existing validation serializer
body: `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` reads a raw GET parameter directly instead of going through `AuditLogQueryParamSerializer`, which is used for all other query parameters (`event`, `actor`). This is inconsistent with the endpoint's established validation pattern, is undocumented (the endpoint is marked EXPERIMENTAL but this parameter isn't reflected anywhere), and silently no-ops for any value other than the exact string "true" with no error feedback to the caller.

title: No tests added for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new audit-log pagination branch
body: This PR introduces a new paginator class (`OptimizedCursorPaginator`) with a non-trivial, non-standard code path (negative-offset handling) and wires it into `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` behind a permission+query-param gate, but no unit or integration tests were added for either the paginator's negative-offset behavior or the endpoint's new `optimized_pagination`/advanced-access branch. Given the bug where negative offsets raise an exception (see related finding), basic tests exercising this path would have caught the problem before merge.

title: Comment added without any corresponding behavior change or validation
body: A comment claiming "Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios" was added above `self.offset = int(offset)`, but no actual validation or logic changed here — `Cursor` already stored whatever integer offset was given, positive or negative, with no guard. The comment implies this is where negative-offset support was introduced/enabled, which is misleading since no enforcement exists here either before or after this change, and could confuse future maintainers trying to find where negative-offset handling is implemented.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key is incompatible with datetime fields and crashes on any real use
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() (and value_from_cursor) are copied verbatim from the numeric Paginator implementation: `value = getattr(item, self.key); math.floor(value)`. But the endpoint wires this paginator up with `order_by="-datetime"` (organization_auditlogs.py), so `self.key` is "datetime" and `value` is a `datetime.datetime` instance. `math.floor()`/`math.ceil()` on a `datetime` object raises `TypeError` because datetime defines neither `__floor__` nor `__float__`. `build_cursor()` calls this key function on the first/last result as soon as there is at least one row, so any request to `/organization-audit-logs/?optimized_pagination=true` made by an authorized admin that returns a non-empty result set will raise an unhandled exception (HTTP 500). The entire 'optimized pagination' feature is therefore non-functional for its only real caller.

title: Negative-offset branch passes a negative start index into Django QuerySet slicing, which Django explicitly rejects
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` (negative). Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ explicitly raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` for negative slice bounds; it does not 'properly handle negative slicing automatically' as the adjacent comment claims. As a result, the advertised 'negative offset support for efficient reverse pagination' will throw an unhandled exception any time it is exercised (e.g. a client-supplied cursor like `0:-5:0` combined with `optimized_pagination=true`), rather than providing any pagination benefit. The subsequent `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check also reuses the unclamped, possibly-negative `offset`, compounding the broken logic once/if the slicing issue is fixed.

title: Unrelated behavioral change to shared BasePaginator.get_result() affects every consumer of Paginator/DateTimePaginator
body: `BasePaginator.get_result()` is the shared implementation used by `Paginator` and `DateTimePaginator`, which are used by many unrelated list endpoints across the codebase, not just audit logs. This PR changes `results = list(queryset[offset:stop])` to clamp the offset via `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, silently changing behavior for any caller that (intentionally or via a malformed cursor) passes a negative offset with `is_prev=False`: previously this would raise (Django disallows negative slice bounds), now it silently starts the page at 0. This is a meaningful behavior change to widely-shared pagination code, introduced only to support a feature that is itself broken (see other findings), with no test coverage and no changelog/documentation of the change. Additionally the accompanying comment says this 'allows negative offsets' when the code actually does the opposite (clamps negative offsets to zero in the non-prev branch), which will mislead future maintainers.

title: Possible AttributeError if organization_context.member is None
body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` will raise `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'` if `request.user.is_superuser` is False and `organization_context.member` is None (e.g. a non-superuser path that does not guarantee a member record, such as certain token-based or cross-silo access patterns). Other code in the codebase typically guards this with `organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access`. If this path is reachable, a normal GET request to this endpoint would 500 instead of falling back to standard pagination.

title: No tests added for the new OptimizedCursorPaginator or the audit log endpoint's new pagination branch
body: The PR introduces a new paginator class with a non-trivial negative-offset code path, a new `enable_advanced_features` flag, and a new permission-gated branch in `organization_auditlogs.py`, but no tests are included for any of it. Basic tests exercising `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result()` with real `AuditLogEntry` rows (ordered by `-datetime`) or the `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter against the endpoint would have immediately caught the `TypeError` in `get_item_key` and the `ValueError` from negative slicing described in other findings. Given the feature touches shared pagination infrastructure, the lack of coverage is a significant gap before merge.

title: Misleading comments overstate Django's slicing capabilities and the safety of the feature
body: The comments at lines 876 ('The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically') and 879 ('This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level') are factually incorrect/misleading: Django's QuerySet does not support negative slice bounds and will raise ValueError, and the 'safety' claim conflates authorization (who can call this code) with the actual boundary-condition correctness of slicing negative indices, which it is not. These comments will mislead future maintainers trying to understand or debug this code.

title: Comment claims new 'advanced pagination' capability was added here, but no functional change was made
body: The added comment states 'Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios... This enables efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions in large datasets', but the line below it (`self.offset = int(offset)`) is unchanged from before the PR — `Cursor` already accepted negative integers via `int()`. The comment implies this file implements/enables a feature, when in fact the (broken) negative-offset handling lives entirely in paginator.py and is unrelated to this cast. This is misleading documentation that doesn't reflect any real change.

title: New paginator duplicates ~65 lines of BasePaginator.get_result with no actual performance optimization
body: Despite the PR's title and docstring claiming 'performance optimizations for high-traffic endpoints' and an 'optimized query path for large datasets', `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result()` is a near-verbatim copy-paste of `BasePaginator.get_result()` with one added (and broken, per other findings) branch for negative offsets. It performs the same queries, same hit counting, and same cursor-building as the base class — there is no demonstrated or plausible performance improvement. The duplication also means any future bug fix or improvement made to `BasePaginator.get_result()` will not automatically apply here, creating a maintenance hazard for logic that is already copy-pasted and partially incorrect.

title: Negative-offset pagination crashes because Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing
body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly rejects negative slice bounds (raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`), so this path will always raise at runtime rather than 'enable efficient bidirectional pagination' as the comments claim ('The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false). Any admin/superuser request that hits `organization_auditlogs.py` with `optimized_pagination=true` and a cursor whose offset is negative will 500. There is no test exercising this branch, so the bug would ship undetected.

title: Shared BasePaginator.get_result silently clamps negative offsets instead of erroring, affecting all cursor paginators
body: `BasePaginator.get_result` (used by `Paginator`, `DateTimePaginator`, and now `OptimizedCursorPaginator` — i.e. most cursor-paginated endpoints in the codebase) used to do `results = list(queryset[offset:stop])` directly. The change introduces `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, which silently clamps negative offsets to 0 for non-prev cursors instead of letting the previous (implicit) error surface. This changes pagination semantics for every endpoint built on `BasePaginator`, not just the audit log endpoint this PR is nominally about, and ships with no new/updated tests demonstrating the previous vs. new behavior across those call sites.

title: New admin-gated 'optimized pagination' code path has no test coverage and is unrelated to stated PR scope
body: A new branch is added that switches to `OptimizedCursorPaginator` (with `enable_advanced_features=True`, which enables the broken negative-offset code path) based on a client-supplied query parameter `optimized_pagination=true` combined with `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. This is a brand-new, security-sensitive conditional pagination feature introduced in a PR whose description and other changes are about the spans buffer. No tests were added for this branch, for the permission gating, or for `OptimizedCursorPaginator` itself, so none of this new logic (including the crash described separately) is verified before merge.

title: Redirect-chain loop bound silently reduced from 10000 to 1000, removing the explanatory warning comment
