body: With sync enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch Response. The code then reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`, which is undefined, so a TypeError is thrown and swallowed by the catch. The token is then never refreshed.

title: Bigin passes credentialId instead of userId
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects the Cal.com user id, but `credentialId` is passed here. With sync enabled this sends the wrong id (a credential id) as `calcomUserId`, so the self-hoster's endpoint returns credentials for the wrong user or none. The response shape also differs, as noted for other services.

title: Unrelated change: hardcoded slug in redirect URI
body: The redirect URI was changed from `appConfig.slug` to a hardcoded `zoho-bigin`. The callback still uses `appConfig.slug`, so the two are now inconsistent. This is unrelated to the PR and brittle.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported in the Salesforce service
body: The newly added `prisma.credential.update(...)` call has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` in this file. It will fail type-check and throw a ReferenceError at runtime as soon as a Salesforce client is constructed.

title: Salesforce now refreshes the token on every client construction, bypassing credential sync
body: This adds an unconditional refresh against login.salesforce.com every time the service is instantiated. It does not go through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so with credential sync enabled the app still hits Salesforce directly with local keys. It also adds a network round trip on every use, and the refreshed `accessToken` is stored in the DB but never used. The `jsforce.Connection` below is still built from the stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `instance_url`.

title: Computed zod schema keys are meaningless and break the minimum token schema
body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to a literal string like "[object Object]" or "ZodString", not a wildcard key. The schema therefore requires a property literally named that and accepts nothing as the expiry. In sync mode, `safeParse` on a real token response will always fail, and `access_token` is the only meaningful field. The comment-described behaviour (any numeric property is the expiry, other properties allowed) is not implemented. Use `.passthrough()` or `.catchall()` instead.

title: Unconditionally injects a fake refresh_token and returns the wrong shape
body: When `refresh_token` is missing the code sets it to the literal string "refresh_token", even when sync is off. That string is then persisted and later sent to providers as a real refresh token. The function also returns the safeParse result object `{success, data}`, but callers such as Google (`const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`; `data: { key }`) store that wrapper instead of the token data. The assignment `data.refresh_token = ...` is also a type error on the minimum schema.

title: Google credential is saved as the safeParse wrapper instead of the key
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{ success, data }`. The code writes that whole object into `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so the stored key becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}`. `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` then fails on the next load and breaks the Google Calendar credential. It should use `.data`. When the sync endpoint returns the response, `res?.data` on a fetch `Response` is also undefined.

title: Sync-mode response is a raw fetch Response, incompatible with callers' expectations
body: In sync mode this returns a fetch `Response`. Several callers expect something else. Google reads `res.data`. Hubspot treats the result as a parsed `HubspotToken` and reads `.expiresIn` and `.accessToken`. Zoho and Bigin read `tokenInfo.data`, which is axios-specific. All of these get undefined or throw. The fetch also has no `Content-Type` or auth header and no `response.ok` check.

title: Bigin passes credentialId as userId
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects `userId`, but `BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken` passes `credentialId` (the third argument is `credentialId`, and the `biginAuth` method never captures `credential.userId`). In sync mode the self-hoster endpoint receives the wrong `calcomUserId` and can return another user's tokens or fail.

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==` and may match undefined
body: A plain `!==` comparison leaks timing information about the secret. The header value is also `string | string[] | undefined`. `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is checked first, so the secret is non-empty, but a timing-safe comparison (`crypto.timingSafeEqual`) should be used for a secret that gates credential writes.

title: Unhandled parse/decrypt/JSON errors and no method check
body: `schema.parse` throws on bad bodies, and `symmetricDecrypt` or `JSON.parse` throw on a bad payload or wrong key. All of these surface as unhandled 500s instead of 400s. There is also no HTTP method check, so any method can reach the credential write path. Use `safeParse`, try/catch, and restrict to POST.

title: Credential lookup ignores team credentials and can race to create duplicates
body: The find-then-create flow without a unique constraint can create duplicate credentials when two webhooks arrive concurrently. `findFirst` on `userId` and `appId` also picks an arbitrary credential if the user has several. In addition, `app.slug` is looked up in the DB and then again in `appStoreMetadata`. The `type` is taken from metadata, but there is no check that the app is one that supports sync.

title: Redirect URI hardcoded instead of using appConfig.slug
body: The change replaces `appConfig.slug` with a literal in `add.ts`, but `callback.ts` still builds the redirect URI from `appConfig.slug`. The two can drift out of sync, and the OAuth redirect_uri must match exactly between the authorize and token requests. The change is unrelated to this PR and not needed.

title: Removed error logging and parse failure now throws
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on an invalid response, whereas the old code logged and continued. The previous diagnostic `console.error` with the zod error and MS response was removed, so failures now lose that context. The `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` spread after a throwing parse is dead logic.

title: Computed zod keys from `.toString()` create literal bogus keys, schema does not do what the comments say
body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to a fixed string such as "[object Object]" or "ZodString", not a wildcard key. The schema therefore requires a numeric property with that literal name, and the second computed key is another literal. No real token response will contain that property. When credential sync is enabled, `safeParse` fails for every response and "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" is thrown. A real approach would be `z.object({access_token: z.string()}).passthrough()` plus a custom expiry check.

title: Placeholder refresh_token written into the schema's result data and persisted
body: If `refresh_token` is missing, it is set to the literal string "refresh_token". Callers such as Salesforce and Zoom then store it in the credential. A fake refresh token may later be sent to the provider on non-synced paths and fail with invalid_grant. It also mutates `data` typed as an arbitrary schema output. Further, `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` is accessed on a union type where the property may not exist, which is a type error.

title: parseRefreshTokenResponse result (a SafeParse object) saved as the credential key
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `{success, data}` safeParse result, not the parsed data. The code stores that whole object as `key` in `prisma.credential.update`. This corrupts the Google credential: the stored value becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}`, and subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails. Use `.data`.

title: Sync endpoint response is a fetch Response, but code reads `res.data`
body: When credential sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw fetch `Response`. Here it is read as `res?.data.access_token` (a gaxios shape), so `data` is undefined and this throws. The error is swallowed by the catch, which returns the old auth, so the token is never refreshed. The response body is never `.json()`-parsed.

title: Sync fetch has no auth, no error handling, and returns inconsistent shapes across callers
body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` carries no authentication/secret header, so the endpoint cannot verify the caller. A non-OK response is returned as-is. The helper returns a fetch `Response` on the sync path but whatever `refreshFunction` returns otherwise (axios response, hubspot token object, googleapis res). Callers such as hubspot (expects a token object), zoho (`.data`), and google (`.data`) break on the sync path.

title: Salesforce refresh now unconditionally performed and `prisma` is not imported
body: The new token refresh code calls `prisma.credential.update`, but `prisma` is never imported in this file, so it is a ReferenceError at runtime and fails type-check. The refresh also runs on every client construction (every service instantiation), not just when expired, and does not use `refreshOAuthTokens`, so it never goes through the sync endpoint. Further, the refreshed access token is saved but the Connection is built from the stale `credentialKey.access_token`. `response.statusText !== "OK"` is a fragile success check (HTTP/2 has empty statusText).

title: Failure to parse refreshed tokens no longer logged/handled; parse now throws
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on a parse failure, so the old zodError logging was removed and replaced by an exception. The following `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` check is now dead. In sync mode the minimal schema produces data without the `expires_in` transformation to an absolute timestamp, so the stored expiry is a relative offset.

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==`; undefined header edge cases
body: The secret is compared with `!==` (timing attack). If the header name env var is mis-set, or the secret is an empty string, the check is weak. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` and require method POST (no method check exists).

title: Unhandled zod parse / decrypt / JSON.parse errors yield 500s; no method check
body: `parse` throws on bad bodies and `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` throw on bad payloads, all uncaught and returned as generic 500s instead of 400s. Use safeParse and try/catch. Also, the credential lookup uses `appId` only, so a user with several credentials for the same app gets an arbitrary one updated, and decrypted keys are not validated against any shape before being stored.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string|undefined, not a boolean
body: The constant evaluates to the key string (or undefined/""), not a boolean. This leaks the encryption key value into any module that might serialize/log the constant, and its type is misleading. Use `!!(...)`.

title: Bigin passes credentialId as userId to refreshOAuthTokens
body: `refreshAccessToken(credentialId, credentialKey)` passes `credentialId` as the `userId` argument. With sync enabled, the sync endpoint is asked about calcomUserId = credential id, fetching or syncing the wrong user's tokens. Pass `credential.userId`.

title: Unrelated redirect URI change hardcodes slug
body: The redirect URI was changed from `appConfig.slug` to a hardcoded "zoho-bigin" in add.ts only, while callback.ts still uses `appConfig.slug`. If they differ the OAuth redirect_uri will mismatch. This is unrelated to the PR.

title: Team admin check uses AND of isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. The name and intent call for OR. With AND, only users who are both admin and owner pass, so team admins who are not owners are wrongly denied. Fix by using `||`. Also, for bookings with no team, `teamId ?? 0` queries team id 0, which is pointless.

title: Any attendee can add guests to a booking
body: Authorization allows any existing attendee, matched by `attendee.email === user.email`. This lets a guest add arbitrary new attendees to someone else's booking. Each new attendee triggers confirmation emails sent from the organizer's identity, and the guests are added to the organizer's calendar event, which is a spam and abuse vector. The email match is also not restricted to a verified or case-normalized email. Restrict to the organizer and team admins/owners, or at least tighten the check.

title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive
body: The blacklist entries are lowercased, but `guest` is compared as-is. `Blocked@x.com` bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. The same applies to the dedup check against existing attendees (`guest === attendee.email`), so differently-cased duplicates can be added. Also, duplicates within the input list itself are not removed server-side (the client check is bypassable), so `createMany` can insert duplicate attendees. Normalize case and dedupe on the server.

title: Emails use the raw input `guests` list instead of the filtered unique guests
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the original input, not `uniqueGuests`. Guests that were filtered out as already-attending or blacklisted are treated as new, so existing attendees get a full 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notification. A guest the server rejected can also get the new-guest email. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

title: Calendar update uses the acting user's credentials and identity, not the organizer's
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({...user, credentials})` use the logged-in user. If an attendee or team admin triggers this, the booking's calendar event (owned by the organizer's credentials) cannot be updated correctly, or the update silently fails. The handler also loads `booking.user.credentials` but never uses it. The `updateCalendarAttendees` call is not wrapped in try/catch either. A calendar failure after the DB write has committed leaves the attendees saved but the request failing, and no emails are sent.

title: New guests are created with an empty name and the organizer's locale/timezone
body: Guests are created with `name: ""`, and `timeZone` and `locale` copied from the organizer. The guest's email therefore renders with no name, and the email language and time zone are the organizer's, not the guest's. For organizer emails, `attendees[0].name` is used in the subject, which stays correct only while the first attendee is the original booker. Also, the `catch` at the end logs a static message and discards the error.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email-disable settings and sends full scheduled email to new guests
body: Unlike the other send functions, it takes no `eventTypeMetadata` and never checks `disableStandardEmails` for host or attendee, so emails get sent even when the event type has disabled them. When `calendarEvent.team` is set, the organizer email is sent once without a teamMember and then once per team member. The sequence matches the existing patterns, but the guard checks are missing.

title: Add guests action is offered for all editable bookings, including seated and past bookings
body: The 'add_members' action is added unconditionally to `editBookingActions`. It also appears on past confirmed/pending bookings and on seated events. For seated events, attendees are individual seats and adding guests this way breaks seat accounting (`seatsPerTimeSlot`). There is no gating on seats or on the booking being upcoming.

title: Error message formatting is wrong and the fallback is unreachable
body: `message` is always a non-empty template string like `BAD_REQUEST: ...`, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback never applies. The code prefix is also exposed to users. `isInvalidEmail` is never reset to false after the user edits the field or after a successful add, so the error banner persists. Empty strings in the input array (the initial `[""]`) fail the email validation, but only the generic 'unique and valid' message is shown.

title: Hard-coded English tooltip and index-based React keys
body: The tooltip `"Remove email"` is not translated. The list uses `key={index}`, so removing a middle entry in a controlled list of inputs can misattribute input state. The `label htmlFor="emails"` points to no element id.

title: Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. A user must be both admin and owner, and for team bookings the owner may not count as admin, so legitimate admins and owners are denied. For bookings without a team, `teamId ?? 0` is also queried with a bogus id. It should be `||`.

title: Any attendee can add guests, and email match is case-sensitive
body: Any existing attendee (matched by `user.email`) is allowed to add guests to the booking, and attendees can be arbitrary people who booked. This lets an attendee make Cal.com send emails and calendar invites to arbitrary addresses. Combined with the emails going out under the organizer's name, it is an abuse vector. The comparison is also case-sensitive, so it can reject legitimate matches.

title: Dedup and blacklist comparisons are case-sensitive and ignore duplicate inputs
body: Blacklisted emails are lowercased, but `guest` is compared as-is, so `Foo@X.com` bypasses the blacklist. Comparison with existing attendees is also case-sensitive, so the same address with different casing is added twice. Duplicates within the `guests` input are not removed server-side, because the uniqueness check exists only in client code. This can cause duplicate attendee rows.

title: Emails use the unfiltered `guests` list rather than the guests actually added
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the raw input, not `uniqueGuests`. Blacklisted or already-existing emails are therefore treated as 'new guests'. They receive the scheduled-invitation email instead of the add-guests notification, and blacklisted addresses still get mail. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

title: Calendar update is not error-handled after the DB write
body: Attendees are committed to the DB before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`. If that call throws, the mutation returns an error while the guests are already saved, and no emails are sent. Retrying then fails with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' because the guests already exist. There is no transaction or compensation. The `catch` around the email send only does `console.log` and discards the error.

title: Credentials and EventManager use the acting user, not the organizer
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({...user})` use the logged-in user's credentials. When an attendee or team admin adds guests, the calendar event owned by the organizer is updated with the wrong user's credentials. The update can fail or silently do nothing. The booking's organizer credentials (already included in the query) should be used.

title: New guests take the organizer's locale and timezone
body: Guests are created with the organizer's `timeZone` and `locale`, so guest emails and times are rendered in the organizer's locale and timezone rather than the guest's. New guests also have an empty name.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disable-email settings and sends wrong mails to existing attendees
body: Unlike the sibling functions, it takes no `eventTypeMetadata` and does not check `disableStandardEmails`. Hosts and attendees who opted out still get emails. Organizer emails are also sent unconditionally. Because the `evt.attendees` list comes from the updated booking, every attendee is covered; the 'else' branch correctly uses AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but only for those not in the raw input (see the unfiltered `guests` issue).

title: Error toast shows 'CODE: message' and the fallback is unreachable
body: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`` is always a non-empty string, so `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` never triggers. Users see messages like 'BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid' prefixed with a raw error code. Also, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is recreated on every render inside the component.

title: Empty-string entries and stale error state are not handled
body: The initial value is `[""]`, and `handleAdd` only checks `length === 0`. The empty email is caught only through the zod validation error, so the error message is misleading. `isInvalidEmail` is never reset on a successful add, on a subsequent edit, or when the dialog closes via the overlay, so the error persists the next time the dialog is opened.

title: Add-guests action is shown for every booking in the edit menu, including seated events
body: The 'additional_guests' action is added unconditionally to `editBookingActions`. Its id is 'add_members', which is misleading. It is not restricted to bookings the user may modify (for example, attendee-only views). Seated events are not handled and would get a mix of seat references.

title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR, and denies legitimate admins
body: `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` only passes when the user is both admin and owner. Plain admins are rejected, so the intended permission is wrong. When `teamId` is missing, `?? 0` is passed to the team lookup, which is sloppy. The check should be `isTeamAdmin || isTeamOwner`, and it should be skipped when the event type has no team.

title: Any existing attendee can add guests to a booking
body: `isAttendee` is true for any attendee whose email matches the logged-in user's email, and that alone authorizes adding guests. The UI exposes this action only on the organizer's bookings list, but the tRPC mutation is callable directly. Attendees can then invite arbitrary external emails, which triggers outbound emails and calendar updates sent under the organizer's identity. This is spam and abuse potential. Also, `attendee.email === user.email` is a case-sensitive comparison and ignores secondary or verified emails.

title: Duplicate and blacklist checks are case-sensitive and the input list is not deduplicated
body: The blacklist is lowercased, but `guest` is compared without lowercasing, so `Foo@X.com` bypasses the blacklist. The comparison with existing attendees is also case-sensitive, so the same address in different case is added as a duplicate attendee. Duplicates inside `guests` itself are not removed server-side, because the uniqueness check exists only in the client dialog. Blacklisted or duplicate guests are also silently dropped, and the same raw `guests` list is later passed to the email sender.

title: Emails are sent using the unfiltered `guests` list rather than `uniqueGuests`
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the raw input. A guest that was already an attendee (and was filtered out) or a blacklisted address still counts as a "new guest" in the email logic. Existing attendees therefore get a full "scheduled" email instead of the "guests added" notice. It should be `uniqueGuests`.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials and is unguarded; no guard on booking state
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({...user})` use the logged-in user's credentials. If an attendee or team admin triggers this, the organizer's calendar event is not the one updated. A failure in `updateCalendarAttendees` happens after the DB write and throws after the guests are already persisted, leaving data inconsistent. No check prevents adding guests to cancelled, rejected or past bookings, or to seated events. The `booking.user.credentials` that were loaded are unused. The handler also uses the booking's organizer for the event but the caller's credentials for the calendar.

title: Email failure is swallowed with a bare console.log and no error detail
body: The catch block logs only a constant string and drops the error. The user still sees "Guests added" even if no notifications went out, and debugging is impossible. Use the project logger and include `err`.

title: New guests get the same attendee email, and the logic mis-handles email-disable settings and case
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` metadata, so event types that disabled standard emails still send them. `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` is case-sensitive. The organizer email is sent without any indication of which guests were added. `calEvent.attendees` contains all attendees and the new ones get a scheduled email, so a booking with many attendees triggers a burst of emails.

title: Subject uses attendees[0].name which can be blank
body: The subject uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. Newly added guests are stored with `name: ""`. The attendee list order is whatever the DB returns, so the subject can render as "Guests Added: X with  at ..." with an empty name. `attendees[0]` could also be undefined in theory.

title: Error toast is malformed and the fallback is unreachable
body: The message is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, which always produces a truthy string such as "BAD_REQUEST: ..." or "undefined: ...". The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback therefore never runs, and the raw tRPC code is exposed to users. Also `isInvalidEmail` is never reset on a successful add or when the dialog is closed with the X or Esc.

title: Empty-string emails are not handled before submit
body: The initial state is `[""]`. The `length === 0` check never fires. If the user clicks Add without typing, zod validation fails and the user sees an "unique and valid" message, which is acceptable. But removing every row and clicking Add skips the guard only by accident. The schema is also rebuilt on every render and should live at module scope.

title: Index used as React key and non-localised tooltip text
body: Using `key={index}` for removable inputs causes input state to get mixed up when removing a middle row. The tooltip "Remove email" is hardcoded English instead of using `t()`. The `<label htmlFor="emails">` references no element with that id.

title: Add-guests action shown for all bookings regardless of permission or state
body: The `add_members` action is added to `editBookingActions` unconditionally. It shows for bookings the viewer cannot modify, for past bookings, and for seated events. The label `t("additional_guests")` and id `add_members` are also inconsistent with the feature.

title: Retry-count delete clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The new OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` condition. Because the two branches are OR'd, the cron deletes any WorkflowReminder (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) whose retryCount > 1, not only SMS ones. Today only this SMS job increments retryCount, so the impact is latent. But any other job that starts using the column will have its reminders silently deleted by the SMS cron. Move the method filter outside the OR so it covers both branches.

title: Threshold `gt: 1` deletes after two failures, but the failed reminder is also dropped from this run's remaining logic
body: A reminder is deleted only on the next cron run after retryCount reaches 2. Meanwhile, retried reminders are not backed off at all, so each cron run (possibly every few minutes) counts as a retry. Two transient Twilio errors (rate limit, network blip) in consecutive runs permanently drop the reminder. The retry count therefore does not distinguish permanent failures (invalid number) from transient ones. The `gt: 1` magic number is also undocumented and does not clearly match the 'failed twice' wording in the description.

title: Update inside catch can throw and abort the whole batch
body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the catch block is not itself guarded. If it throws (DB error, or the row was deleted concurrently), the exception escapes the for-loop. The handler then fails with a 500 and every remaining reminder in the batch goes unprocessed. Wrap the update in its own try/catch or use `updateMany`.

title: Reminders with no message or no sendTo never count as a retry
body: The common failure case, such as an invalid or missing phone number (`sendTo` is null) or an empty message, fails the `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)` check. That branch has no else, so retryCount is never incremented and the reminder is retried on every cron run until scheduledDate. This is exactly the problem the PR is meant to fix. Also, `continue` for missing workflowStep/booking has no retry handling.

title: Use atomic increment and consider an index
body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` uses a value read earlier, so concurrent cron runs can lose increments. Use `{ increment: 1 }`. The new `retryCount` delete predicate is also OR'd with the existing indexed condition, so it can force a full table scan on WorkflowReminder, and the migration adds no index for it.

title: Retry-count delete clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The deleteMany `where` is now `OR: [{method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now}, {retryCount > 1}]`. The second branch has no `method` filter. This cron only handles SMS, but the clause deletes any WorkflowReminder (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) with retryCount > 1. Today only this handler increments retryCount, so the risk is latent. But the column is generic, and any future use by another reminder type would cause this SMS cron to delete those rows. It should be `{ method: SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

title: Retry threshold does not match the described behavior
body: The description says the reminder is deleted after scheduling failed twice. The delete runs at the start of the next cron run and removes reminders with `retryCount > 1`, i.e. >= 2. The sequence is: run 1 fails and sets retryCount to 1; run 2 fails and sets it to 2; run 3 deletes the row. That is consistent with two failures, but the delete only happens on a later run. Nothing reads or deletes after the second failure, so the failed reminder lingers until the next cron run. The `gt: 1` magic number is also unexplained.

title: Error-path update is unguarded and can abort the whole batch
body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the `catch` block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If it throws (DB error, or the row was deleted concurrently, giving P2025), the exception escapes the loop. The remaining reminders are then not processed and the handler returns a 500. The original error is also never logged in that case, because `console.log` comes after the update.

title: Reminders skipped before sending never increment retryCount
body: Retry counting only happens when `message` and `sendTo` are both present and scheduling fails, or when an exception is thrown. If `sendTo` is missing (for example an invalid or absent smsReminderNumber, a common failure case) or the message is empty, nothing happens and retryCount is not incremented. Those reminders are re-evaluated on every cron run until the date passes, which is the problem the PR aims to fix. Likewise `!reminder.workflowStep || !reminder.booking` just `continue`s.

title: Read-modify-write increment is not atomic
body: The code writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, using a value read earlier in the run. If two cron invocations overlap, both write the same count and increments are lost. Use `{ increment: 1 }` for an atomic update.

title: No tests for the new retry/delete behavior
body: The PR adds retry counting and a new deletion rule that can remove reminders, but includes no tests for incrementing on failure, for deletion at the threshold, or for method scoping.

title: Retry-count delete clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The deleteMany `OR` has a second branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter. It deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders. Only the SMS cron increments retryCount today, but the column is generic. Any future retry logic in other crons would be silently wiped by this job. The `method: SMS` condition should be applied to both branches, or moved outside the OR.

title: Threshold `gt: 1` does not match the 'failed twice' description
body: The deletion condition is `retryCount > 1`. A reminder is removed in the next cron run after its second failure, when retryCount becomes 2. That matches 'failed twice', but it is an off-by-one-prone magic number with no constant or comment. It also means a single transient Twilio error leaves only one more chance before the reminder is deleted. Define a named constant for the max retries.

title: Catch block update can itself throw and abort the whole cron loop
body: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the `catch` is not guarded. If the update fails (DB error, or the row was deleted concurrently), the exception escapes the loop. The remaining reminders are not processed and the handler returns a 500. It should be wrapped in its own try/catch or use updateMany.

title: Reminders with no sendTo or empty message are never counted as failures
body: The retry increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)`. A reminder with a missing or invalid phone number (`sendTo` null) or an empty message is skipped without incrementing retryCount. It is re-evaluated on every cron run until its date passes, which is the exact behavior the PR aims to stop.

title: Non-atomic retryCount increment
body: The code writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` from a value read earlier. If two cron invocations overlap, both write the same value and an increment is lost. Use `{ increment: 1 }` instead.

title: No tests for new retry/deletion behavior
body: The retry-count increment and the deletion of reminders after repeated failures are new behavior in a cron job and have no test coverage. The comment above the deleteMany is also now inaccurate, since it also deletes by retryCount.

title: Caching tests were deleted although caching behaviour still exists
body: The "Caching" describe block was removed from the tests. The service still caches results in `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` inside `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions`. Nothing in the converted suite now checks that a second call returns the cached value. Those tests only needed their expected values changed to `Prisma.sql`, not removal, so a regression in the cache logic would go unnoticed. Restore them with Sql-based expectations.

title: Public `findMany` removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions` (breaking API change)
body: The public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method is removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. Any caller that used `findMany` (for example tRPC handlers) will fail to compile or break at runtime. The diff does not update any other callers, and the PR description does not mention the removal. Callers must now write their own `$queryRaw` and handle the view's column names and typing themselves. Confirm all usages are migrated, or keep a compatibility wrapper.

title: Caching tests deleted without replacement
body: The "Caching" describe block was removed. The service still has `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, and `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` still rely on that caching. Nothing now verifies that the second call returns the cached value, or that a `null` filter result is cached rather than rebuilt. The tests should have been converted to the Sql format, not dropped.

title: Filter condition returned as an unparenthesized top-level OR
body: For the single-filter case, `getFilterConditions()` returns `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` with no outer parentheses. `getBaseConditions` wraps it, so that path is safe. Any other caller that embeds the public result as `... AND ${filterConditions}` gets wrong operator precedence, which would silently widen the result set. Wrapping the OR in parentheses where it is built would make the fragment safe to compose.

title: Exact-SQL equality tests are brittle and miss the empty-membership branches
body: The tests assert exact Sql structure and parameter order, including the order of user IDs returned by the membership query, which has no `ORDER BY`. A harmless reformat or a different row order will fail them. The new branches that skip the `userId = ANY(...)` clause when the user list is empty, in both the team and org builders, have no test coverage.

title: Caching tests deleted with no replacement
body: The "Caching" describe block was removed. The service still caches in `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` through `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`. Nothing now checks that a second call returns the cached value, or that a cached `null` filter result is not rebuilt. Those tests could easily have been kept by comparing `Prisma.sql` objects. The removal looks like a side effect of the conversion rather than a deliberate decision.

title: Behavior change in team scope and new empty-list branches have no tests
body: The old team-scope condition always included the `userId IN [...]` branch, even when the user list was empty. The new code adds it only when `userIdsFromTeam.length > 0`, and the org scope has the same kind of conditional branch. The tests only cover cases where users exist. They do not cover a team with no members, an org with no child teams, a team that does not belong to the org (which should return `NOTHING_CONDITION`), or `getBaseConditions` when only one side is present. These are the authorization edge cases the PR checklist calls out as risky, and none of them is exercised.

title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError; delegation credentials not handled
body: A plain `Error` becomes an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) in tRPC, so a not-found or unauthorized credential is reported as a server failure and shows up in error monitoring. It should throw `TRPCError` with `NOT_FOUND` or `FORBIDDEN`. The ownership check also only matches credentials in the DB with `userId`. Delegation credentials are in-memory with negative ids and the UI passes them through, so deleting their cache will always fail.

title: deleteCache success does not refresh connectedCalendars query
body: After deleting cache, the mutation only calls `onSuccess?.()`, which is an optional prop. The disconnect mutation invalidates `connectedCalendars`, but deleteCacheMutation does not. If `onChanged` is not provided, or does not refetch, the "Last updated" timestamp and the delete option stay visible after the cache is gone, which contradicts the expected UI update. It needs `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in onSuccess/onSettled.

title: updateMany with empty data does not bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty data object. Prisma `updateMany` does not apply `@updatedAt` when no fields change, so this is likely a no-op while still costing a DB round trip. The comment claims it updates `updatedAt`, but it does not do so reliably. The PR notes also say the frontend does not use this value, so the call looks like dead or misleading code that adds a write on every cache refresh/webhook.

title: Cache timestamp semantics are misleading and the mock is missing from the connected-calendars path
body: `updatedAt` is `@default(now()) @updatedAt`, and the migration backfills existing rows with `NOW()` at migration time. All pre-existing cache rows therefore show a "last updated" of the deploy time, not their real update time. In `connectedCalendarsHandler`, `new CalendarCacheRepository()` is used directly rather than the `CalendarCache.init` factory that returns the mock when calendar-cache is disabled. Cache status is therefore queried and displayed even when the feature is disabled, and the mock's `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` is never used.

title: Hardcoded en-US date formatting ignores user locale
body: The timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, so non-English users see US-style dates. It should use the user's locale (e.g. `i18n.language`). Also `hasCache` is typed as `Date | null | false | undefined`, and `cacheUpdatedAt` is serialized over tRPC (superjson) as a Date, so this works only because of superjson.

title: Extra DB query on every connectedCalendars call
body: Every call to `connectedCalendars`, which is also used in onboarding and event-type settings, now runs an additional `groupBy` on CalendarCache even for non-Google credentials, and negative (in-memory delegation) credential ids are included in the `IN` list. Filter to Google Calendar DB credentials (`credentialId > 0`) before querying.

title: macOS-only sed and unrelated dev script included in feature PR
body: `sed -i ''` works only on BSD/macOS sed and breaks on GNU/Linux, where `''` is interpreted as the script and the real script as a filename. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the cwd, so the script writes to a different path depending on where it is run. The script is unrelated to the cache feature and also hardcodes /tmp paths. The unrelated `dev:cron` change to `npx tsx` is likewise out of scope.

title: Cache status ignores the calendar-cache feature flag and in-memory delegation credentials
body: The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through the `CalendarCache.init` factory that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when caching is disabled. It then queries `calendarCache.groupBy` with `credentialId IN (...)`. `connectedCalendars` can include in-memory delegation credentials with negative ids; these ids are passed straight to the query. The mock added in this PR (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` returning `[]`) is never reachable from here.

title: Ownership check only matches credentials with credential.userId, excluding team/delegation credentials
body: The credential lookup filters on `userId: user.id` only, so credentials the user can legitimately see but which are not directly owned (for example, team credentials) cannot have their cache deleted. The UI still shows the delete option for those credentials, so the user gets a generic error. Failure is also signalled with a plain `Error`, which tRPC maps to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) instead of a `TRPCError` with NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN.

title: Extra unconditional DB write bumps SelectedCalendar.updatedAt on every cache refresh
body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` runs an UPDATE across all selected calendars for the credential after every `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`. Prisma's `@updatedAt` will bump the column. This is a write amplification on a hot webhook path, with locking across every row of the credential. Nothing in the UI uses it (the PR notes admit the frontend uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`). The `{}` payload is also fragile and unclear. This should be removed.

title: Cache actions show only for Google credentials; Cache Status item is a focusable menu item
body: `hasCache` is `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`, which has type `false | Date | null | undefined`. The 'Cache Status' entry is rendered as a `DropdownMenuItem`, so it is interactive/focusable and closes the menu on select even though it is purely informational. The date is formatted with a hard-coded `en-US` locale, ignoring the user's locale. `Intl.DateTimeFormat` also formats in the browser timezone without regard to the user's profile timezone.

title: Delete-cache mutation does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
body: On success the delete-cache mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` (which is `props.onChanged`, possibly undefined). It does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` as the disconnect mutation does. After deletion the UI continues to show a stale 'Last updated' timestamp and the delete option until a manual refetch (`refetchOnWindowFocus` is false).

title: Unrelated dev script is macOS-only and has bugs
body: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS syntax and fails on GNU/Linux. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory, not the script. The script is unrelated to the PR's stated feature. Alongside the unrelated `dev:cron` change to `npx tsx` (which is not a declared dependency), this should be split out of the PR.

title: Migration header comment contradicts the statement
body: The auto-generated warning says the column is added 'without a default value', but the statement adds `DEFAULT NOW()`. All existing cache rows get the migration timestamp as `updatedAt`, so the UI will show a misleading 'last updated' time for rows that were refreshed long ago.

title: Cache status ignores the calendar-cache feature flag; repository always hits the DB
body: The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly. The codebase uses `CalendarCache.init` to choose between the real repository and `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the cache is disabled, and this PR adds `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` to the mock. Because the mock is never used here, that method is dead code. It also means the UI can show cache status for deployments or users where caching is disabled.

title: In-memory delegation credentials have negative IDs and are passed to the DB query
body: `connectedCalendars` can contain in-memory delegation credentials with negative or non-DB `credentialId` values. These are passed to `groupBy ... credentialId IN (...)`. Negative IDs never match, so it is wasteful at best. Check that `credentialId` is always a number for these entries, and filter out in-memory delegation IDs before querying.

title: Cache actions are not gated by disableConnectionModification or delegation
body: `hasCache` depends only on integration type and `cacheUpdatedAt`. The dropdown therefore exposes "Delete cached data" even when `disableConnectionModification` is true (for example when the scope is disabled for the event type) or the credential is a delegation credential. A delegation credential's `credentialId` is negative, so the server rejects the deletion with a generic error. Cache deletion should respect the same permission flags as disconnecting.

title: After cache deletion the status is not refetched; onSuccess is optional and unrelated to the cache query
body: `deleteCacheMutation` has no `onSettled` or `onSuccess` invalidation of `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike the disconnect mutation. It relies on the optional `onSuccess` prop, which is `props.onChanged` and may be undefined. The query uses `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, so after a successful delete the dropdown keeps showing the stale "Last updated" timestamp and the delete action. The user can then delete repeatedly.

title: Generic Error is thrown instead of a TRPCError
body: A plain `Error` becomes an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) and is reported as a server error. A missing or unauthorized credential should throw `TRPCError` with code NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN. The router input is also an inline `z.object` rather than a schema file, which is inconsistent with the sibling procedures.

title: Writes to every SelectedCalendar of the credential for no functional purpose
body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` runs on every cache refresh, which includes webhook-triggered refreshes. With empty data, Prisma's `@updatedAt` bumps `updatedAt` on all selected calendars of the credential, including rows for other integrations or event types. This adds write load. The PR's own notes say the frontend does not use `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, so the extra write has no benefit. It also runs after a loop that may throw, so the semantics are inconsistent.

title: groupBy on credentialId for status is unindexed and runs on every connectedCalendars call
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` aggregates MAX(updatedAt) across all cache rows per credential on every `connectedCalendars` query. This is a hot settings-page query. Each credential can have many cache rows. The `updatedAt` column is not indexed and the aggregate is never cached. The query scans all of a credential's cache rows each time.

title: Migration header comment contradicts the SQL
body: The "Warnings" comment says the column was added without a default and that this is not possible on a non-empty table, but the statement adds it with `DEFAULT NOW()`. Existing rows all get the migration timestamp as `updatedAt`, so the UI will show a misleading "last updated" time for old caches.

title: Unrelated dev script uses macOS-only sed -i '' and is outside the PR scope
body: `sed -i ''` fails on GNU/Linux, where `''` is interpreted as the script argument. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the current working directory, so the script behaves differently depending on where it is run. The script is unrelated to the feature, and the unrelated `package.json` `ts-node` to `npx tsx` change is in the same category.

title: Reschedule path still uses immediate SendGrid cancellation, which hits the 100-pending-cancel limit
body: The PR exists because SendGrid allows at most 100 pending cancellations in `scheduled_sends`. Once that limit is reached, new cancels fail and the emails are still sent. Here `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` takes the immediate branch, which POSTs the cancel straight to SendGrid. The same immediate path is used in workflows.tsx for deleting a workflow and for deleted steps. Those flows can therefore still silently fail once the limit is reached, because the error is only logged. The reschedule flow does not need the immediate path, since the booking row still exists and the cron could cancel it later. Using the deferred `cancelled=true` flag there would avoid the limit.

title: Fire-and-forget callers may drop the `cancelled` flag update
body: Marking the reminder `cancelled: true` is the only thing that now stops the email from being sent. The callers in bookings.tsx, handleCancelBooking.ts and workflows.tsx do not `await` this call. The old code awaited the DB deletes via `Promise.all`. In serverless runtimes, un-awaited work can be frozen or dropped once the response is returned, so the DB write may never happen. The cron would then never cancel that reminder and the email would still go out. These calls should be awaited, for example with `Promise.all`.

title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts all remaining cancellations and deletions
body: The whole cancel loop is inside a single try/catch. If any `client.request` call throws, for example from a rate limit or a bad batch id, the loop exits. Remaining reminders are not cancelled, and none of the queued `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` promises run, because they are lazy and only awaited after the loop. A single bad reminder with an invalid referenceId can therefore block every later cancellation on every cron run. Each reminder should be handled in its own try/catch. Reminders that SendGrid reports as already gone should be deleted rather than retried forever.

title: Cancellation window can be missed for late cancellations and is not limited to EMAIL
body: The cron runs every 15 minutes and only cancels reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour. A booking cancelled shortly before the send time, between two cron runs, may not be picked up in time. In that case the reminder is deleted by the earlier `deleteMany` only after its scheduled time has passed, and the email has already been sent. The query also does not filter on `method: EMAIL`, unlike the other queries in this file.

title: Unused value import and unrelated reformatting of commented code
body: `Prisma` is now imported as a runtime value, but nothing in the file uses it after the removal of the `PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>` code. The list also lacks a trailing comma. The diff additionally strips the indentation of the large commented-out `testAction` block, which adds noise unrelated to the fix.

title: Unrelated UI refactor bundled into the bug-fix PR
body: The phone-number block's wrapper condition changes from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to `isPhoneNumberNeeded`, and the markup is reindented. This has nothing to do with cancelling workflow reminders. It changes rendering behaviour for SMS_ATTENDEE, where an empty gray box is no longer shown. It should be a separate change, or at least be mentioned in the PR description.

title: Reschedule path cancels in SendGrid immediately, so the 100-pending-cancellation cap is still hit
body: The PR exists because SendGrid keeps cancelled sends pending until their scheduled date and allows only 100 of them, after which new cancellations fail and the email goes out anyway. This call passes `immediateDelete=true`, which sends the SendGrid cancel straight away instead of just setting `cancelled=true` for the cron to process within the hour. Rescheduled bookings therefore keep consuming the capped pending-cancellation slots, and the bug is still reachable for reschedules. The same applies to the `true` argument in the workflow-delete and step-delete paths in workflows.tsx. In addition, the immediate path never deletes or marks the DB row. A later call on the same row (for example the `requestReschedule` flow followed by `handleNewBooking` on the already-cancelled booking) re-cancels the same batch_id in SendGrid, because reminders already flagged `cancelled` are not skipped.

title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole batch and leaves reminders stuck
body: The loop awaits a SendGrid cancel for each reminder, and the Prisma `delete` for each row is only executed afterwards by `Promise.all`. The whole loop sits in a single try/catch. If one `client.request` throws (bad batch_id, already-cancelled batch, rate limit), the loop exits and no rows are deleted, including those already cancelled in SendGrid. Every later cron run retries the same failing reminder first and can fail on it again, which blocks the other cancellations until the scheduled date passes. The next run may also re-cancel the batches that already succeeded. Handle each reminder in its own try/catch and delete its row right after a successful cancel.

title: Deletion is fire-and-forget, so the new `cancelled` flag may never be persisted
body: The cancellation flow now depends entirely on a DB write (`cancelled: true`) made inside `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`. Every caller (handleCancelBooking, handleNewBooking, bookings.tsx, workflows.tsx) invokes it without `await`, and the function swallows errors with `console.log`. On serverless deployments the request can finish before the update runs, and a failed update is silent. The email is then sent for a cancelled booking, which is the bug being fixed. The callers should await these calls, or the function should surface failures.

title: No tests for the new cancellation flow
body: The PR adds a DB column, a cron cancellation step and three different behaviours of `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (no referenceId deletes the row, immediate SendGrid cancel, deferred flag). None are covered by tests, and the main conditions are untested: only reminders within the next hour are cancelled, rows are removed after cancel, and SendGrid errors are handled.

title: Deferred cancellation leaves a gap in which cancelled emails are still sent
body: The default path only sets `cancelled = true` in the DB. The cron job cancels at most one hour ahead and runs every 15 minutes. If a booking is cancelled or rescheduled shortly before the reminder's send time, the next cron run may fire after the send time, or the reminder may only enter the 1-hour window after the last run. The row is then deleted by the 'scheduledDate <= now' cleanup and the SendGrid email goes out anyway. When `scheduledDate` is already within the next hour, the code should cancel in SendGrid right away instead of waiting for the cron.

title: One failing SendGrid cancel blocks all remaining cancellations and the DB deletes
body: The loop awaits `client.request` for each reminder inside a single try/catch. If one request throws (for example an invalid or already-sent batch id, or a 4xx), the loop exits. Reminders later in the list are not cancelled in that run. The Prisma `delete` calls collected so far are lazy and are never awaited, so nothing is deleted either. That failing reminder stays `cancelled: true` and is retried first on every run until its `scheduledDate` passes. A permanently failing entry can therefore keep the other cancelled emails from being cancelled, so they get sent. Handle each reminder in its own try/catch and delete each row right after its cancel succeeds.

title: Reschedule uses immediate SendGrid cancel, bringing back the 100-pending-cancellation limit
body: On reschedule, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)` posts a SendGrid cancel immediately. That is the same path the PR says fails once about 100 cancellations are pending, so emails are still sent. This is inconsistent with `requestReschedule` and `handleCancelBooking`, which use the deferred path. The workflow-delete and step-delete paths also pass `true`; they need it because the DB rows are cascade-deleted. After an immediate cancel nothing is recorded on the row. If SendGrid rejects the cancel, the row is not marked `cancelled` and the cron will not retry, so the email is sent. On failure, fall back to marking the row `cancelled: true`.

title: Reminder cancellation promises are not awaited
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` now do the DB writes (set `cancelled` or delete the row) and call Twilio, but they are fire-and-forget. The old code awaited the Prisma deletes via `Promise.all`. In a serverless runtime the invocation can end before the update runs, leaving the reminder uncancelled and the email still sent. The same applies to the loop in `bookings.tsx` `requestReschedule`. Collect these promises and await them, for example in the existing `Promise.all`.

title: Unused `Prisma` import, and type imports changed to value imports
body: `Prisma` is now imported as a value but no longer used, since the `deleteReminderPromise` code was removed, which will fail lint. `PrismaPromise` and `Prisma` were `import type` before and are now regular imports. The same change was made to `App`, `Credential`, `EventTypeCustomInput` and `Prisma` in `handleNewBooking.ts`. Regular imports of type-only symbols can break under `isolatedModules`/SWC. The line also lacks a trailing comma. The diff also re-indents the commented-out `testAction` block, which is unrelated noise.

title: getCalendarCredentials stores un-awaited Promises; other consumers of `.calendar` break
body: `getCalendar` is now async, so `calendar` in the returned objects is a `Promise<Calendar|null>`. `getConnectedCalendars` was patched to `await item.calendar`, but any other caller of `getCalendarCredentials` that reads `.calendar` synchronously (e.g. availability or selected-calendar code) now gets a Promise, which is truthy and has no `.listCalendars` or `.createEvent`. The return type changed silently and the PR does not audit the other call sites.

title: async forEach callback makes calendar/video deletions fire-and-forget; try/catch is ineffective
body: `forEach(async ...)` does not await the callbacks, so the `try/catch` around it can never catch rejections from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting`. Those become unhandled promise rejections, which can crash the Node process in some runtimes. Previously calendar errors thrown synchronously (e.g. in the constructor) were at least caught. The function also returns and sends emails before the deletions finish, and on serverless platforms the work may be killed after the response. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` inside the try.

title: async forEach callback makes deletions fire-and-forget; try/catch is ineffective
body: Same problem as in the vital reschedule: `forEach(async ...)` is not awaited, so errors escape the surrounding try/catch as unhandled rejections and the deletions may not complete before the function returns. Await them with `Promise.all` and `map`.

title: async forEach in requestReschedule: deletions not awaited, errors unhandled
body: Making the `forEach` callback async means calendar and video deletions run detached from the mutation. Rejections become unhandled, and the mutation may return, or the serverless invocation end, before the events are removed from external calendars. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.

title: async forEach pushes to apiDeletes after it has already been awaited, so recurring-event calendar deletions can be lost
body: The recurring-cancellation branch uses `forEach(async (credential) => {...})` and pushes `deletedEvent` into `apiDeletes` only after awaiting `getCalendar` and `deleteEvent`. `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` snapshots the array before those pushes happen, so they are not awaited. Errors go unhandled and the handler can return before the calendar events are deleted. The old code had the same shape but ran mostly synchronously. Now that `getCalendar` is async, the race is real. It also pushes resolved values, not promises. Replace with a `for...of` loop that awaits, or push the promises.

title: Dynamic imports are created eagerly at module load, so nothing is lazy
body: Each entry is `import("./x")` evaluated immediately when the object literal is built. All ~29 app packages start loading as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported, and the promises are kept for the process lifetime. This defeats the purpose of async or lazy imports, since the load cost is paid at startup. A failing import also becomes a rejected promise at module-eval time, with an unhandled rejection if nobody awaits it, and every later `await appStore[x]` rethrows it. Use thunks such as `() => import(...)` or a lazy getter.

title: Unknown app keys give a misleading or noisy result
body: `await appStore[...]` on an undefined key yields undefined and falls through to the warn. Separately, `log.info("calendarApp", calendarApp.lib.CalendarService)` still logs on every call. This is minor, but the awaited module namespace is typed as a union of dynamic-import modules, which makes the `"lib" in calendarApp` narrowing fragile.

title: Dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly at module load, so nothing is lazy
body: Every entry is `import("./x")` placed directly in an object literal. Each call runs the moment `appStore` is first imported, so all ~29 app packages start loading together. This brings none of the lazy-loading benefit that async imports are supposed to provide. Cold start cost and memory stay the same. A failure in any one app module also becomes an unhandled promise rejection at import time. Entries should be thunks (`() => import(...)`) that are called only when an app is needed.

title: async forEach callback escapes the try/catch and is not awaited
body: `forEach(async ...)` returns promises that nothing awaits. The `try/catch` around it cannot catch rejections from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting`. Those rejections become unhandled promise rejections. The function also continues to send emails and return `true` before the calendar and video deletions finish. In a serverless context the work can be cut off. This was already a latent problem, but the PR made the callback async without fixing it. Use `await Promise.all(refs.map(...))` inside the try.

title: async forEach callback escapes the try/catch and is not awaited
body: This is the same issue as in the vital copy. The async `forEach` callbacks are fire-and-forget. Errors are not caught by the surrounding try/catch and become unhandled rejections. The handler returns before the calendar and video deletions complete.

title: Un-awaited async forEach in requestReschedule
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` now awaits `getCalendar` inside a callback that nothing waits for. Calendar and video deletions are not completed before the mutation continues or returns. Any rejection is an unhandled promise rejection and is not reported to the caller. Collect the promises and `await Promise.all`.

title: Recurring-cancel deletes are pushed into apiDeletes after it is awaited
body: The recurring branch uses `forEach(async ...)`, which now awaits `getCalendar` before the loop pushes into `apiDeletes`. The pushes therefore happen after the callback yields, which is after `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` has already snapshotted the array. The calendar deletions for recurring bookings are never awaited, and errors become unhandled rejections. The handler may respond before the events are deleted. Before the change `getCalendar` was synchronous, but `deleteEvent` was still awaited inside the callback. The async forEach is still the problem and should become a `for...of` loop or a `Promise.all` over map.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a promise inside `calendar`, and other consumers may not await it
body: `calendar` in the returned objects is now a `Promise<Calendar|null>`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to await it. Any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` that uses `item.calendar` synchronously will break. TypeScript may not flag a Promise used with optional chaining. In addition, the promise is created eagerly for every credential, so a rejected promise whose consumer never awaits it becomes an unhandled rejection.

title: await getCalendar added where the enclosing callback may not be async
body: The diff adds `await getCalendar(credential)` inside the reschedule integration cleanup. Only a one-line hunk is shown, so it cannot be verified that the enclosing function is `async`. If this code runs inside a non-async `forEach` or callback, it is a syntax or TypeScript error. If it is `forEach(async ...)`, the pushes into `integrationsToDelete` happen after the array is awaited. Confirm that this is a `for...of` loop in an async scope.

title: getCalendarCredentials stores a Promise in `calendar` but its callers are not updated
body: `getCalendar` is now async, so `getCalendarCredentials` returns items whose `calendar` field is a `Promise<Calendar | null>`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to `await item.calendar`. Any other consumer that reads `.calendar` directly will now hold a Promise, so a call like `calendar.listCalendars()` fails at runtime. The return type changed silently. Nothing in the diff checks the other call sites, such as the trpc calendars router, availability code and selected-calendar handling.

title: All app imports are started eagerly at module load
body: The object literal calls `import(...)` for all ~29 apps when `@calcom/app-store` is first loaded. Every app module, with its heavy dependencies (googleapis, stripe, zoom, etc.), is therefore loaded immediately and unconditionally. This defeats the purpose of async or lazy loading. To be lazy, the values should be thunks, such as `() => import(...)`, resolved only on demand. Any app whose import throws or rejects at load time also creates an unhandled rejection at module init, even if that app is never used.

title: async forEach callback makes the try/catch ineffective and the deletes unawaited
body: The `forEach` callback is now `async`, so the returned promises are discarded and the surrounding `try/catch` can no longer catch their errors. A failure in `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection. The code also proceeds to send emails and return before the calendar and video deletions finish, which is risky in serverless environments where the process can end early. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` instead. The same problem is duplicated in `wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts` and in `trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`.

title: Async forEach pushes to apiDeletes after it has already been awaited
body: In the recurring-cancellation branch, `forEach(async ...)` awaits `getCalendar` and then `deleteEvent`. `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)` therefore runs after the outer flow has continued to `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`. Before this PR the callback had no `await` before the first push, so it ran synchronously up to the first `deleteEvent`. The awaited `getCalendar` now guarantees the callback yields first. The calendar deletions are neither awaited nor reliably included in `apiDeletes`, and their errors are unhandled. Recurring cancellations may not delete the calendar events before the response returns. Use `for...of` with `await`, or collect promises with `map` and `Promise.all`.

title: calendar promises are created eagerly and rejections are handled late
body: `getCalendarCredentials` calls `getCalendar` immediately for each credential and keeps the promises. They are only awaited later, inside the `getConnectedCalendars` try/catch. If a promise rejects before it is awaited, or if the caller never calls `getConnectedCalendars`, this is an unhandled rejection.

title: Working-hours check compares the slot start with itself, so `end` is always equal to `start`
body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start`. It should presumably use `slotEndTime`. The check also treats a slot as unavailable if `start < startTime || end > endTime`. That uses the UTC clock of the slot against working hours that may be in other units or timezones, and a slot that ends after `workingHour.endTime` is never rejected. Also, `find` returns true as soon as any single working-hour entry for that day does not contain the slot, so a user with two disjoint ranges on a day (e.g. 9-12 and 14-18) is treated as unavailable for every slot. This will wrongly remove slots.

title: Dead comparison between Dayjs objects using `===`
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct object references, so it is always false. The intended zero-length-override check never fires and the code is misleading. It should use `.isSame()` or be removed.

title: Date override matching in checkIfIsAvailable uses an inverted/ambiguous offset and compares dates in UTC
body: The offset is computed as `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` and added to the UTC override start. That shifts the override into the opposite direction from the organizer's local time. The shifted date is then compared by `YYYY MM DD` string with the slot's UTC date. With an override on a day boundary or non-UTC organizer, this matches the wrong day, so `dateOverrideExist` is set for the wrong slots or not set for the right ones. The `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` check also lets a slot that starts before the override end but runs past it be accepted. Slots that would exceed the override window are not rejected. The override detection ignores the slot's end entirely.

title: Override on the day short-circuits busy-time checks
body: When `dateOverrideExist` is true the function does `return true` and never reaches the `busy.every(...)` check. A fixed host with a date override on that day will therefore be reported as available for every slot inside the override, even when they have a booking or calendar event at that time. This causes double bookings on override days. It should fall through to the busy check.

title: Override offset computed from `override.start.toString()` and may be wrong or undefined timezone
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` parses a locale-formatted Date string, which loses milliseconds and depends on parsing the local-string format; `.toISOString()` or `dayjs(override.start)` is safer. `override.timeZone` is optional in the type; if it is undefined, `.tz(undefined)` falls back to the system/default timezone and gives a wrong offset. The shifted `hour()*60+minute()` of the start/end also wraps around midnight when the offset pushes the time into another day, so an end time of e.g. 23:00 plus offset becomes 04:30 and is less than start, which `buildSlots` drops as invalid.

title: Active overrides are still filtered by the unshifted UTC start while times are shifted afterwards
body: The filter `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, ...)` selects overrides by their raw UTC start, but the new offset adjustment is applied afterwards. An override whose shifted time falls on the invitee's day but whose UTC start falls on the adjacent day is excluded or placed on the wrong day. This is a mismatch between selection and conversion.

title: Timezone test asserts identical slots and does not test the fixed-host round-robin fix
body: The new test for `Asia/Dhaka` expects the same UTC slots as for Kolkata. That passes trivially because the result is in UTC and does not verify that the override is shifted per invitee timezone. The PR's primary fix, date overrides of fixed hosts in round-robin events, has no test at all. The `toHaveTimeSlots` helper also only iterates over actual slots, so extra or missing expected slots are not detected.

title: Working-hours check compares a single point (start==end) and uses the wrong logic
body: `end` is computed identically to `start` (`slotStartTime.hour()*60 + minute()`), so `end > workingHour.endTime` is not checking the slot's end. The `.find` returns true if ANY working-hour entry that includes the day has the slot outside its range. With multiple entries per day (split shifts, or multiple aggregate entries) a slot inside one entry is rejected because it's outside another. The check also ignores the organizer timezone/DST (working hours are in UTC minutes, compared against slot UTC time, so day-of-week and day boundaries can be wrong). This can wrongly remove valid slots, or fail to catch slots whose end exceeds working hours.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === (always false)
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares object references, so it is never true. The intended handling of zero-length overrides (start equals end, meaning unavailable that day) is dead code. The slot may then be treated as inside the override or only partially excluded.

title: Date override matching mixes organizer-local date with invitee-UTC slot date and ignores later overrides
body: The override date is derived by shifting `date.start` by the negative organizer offset (`-utcOffset`), which is the wrong direction for converting UTC to organizer local (it should be adding +offset), and it is then compared to the slot's UTC date. The offset sign and the frame of reference are inconsistent, so an override can be attributed to the wrong day for non-UTC organizers, and slots on adjacent days may be wrongly accepted or rejected. Also `dateOverrideExist` is set on the first matching override but `find` stops at the first returning true; with several overrides on one day (split ranges) a slot inside the second range is rejected because it fails the first range check.

title: Override offset computed with a single timezone-offset difference breaks across DST and day boundaries
body: The shifted start/end times are reduced to minutes-of-day via `.hour()*60+.minute()`, which discards day rollover: when the offset pushes an override past midnight, startTime/endTime wrap (e.g. end becomes smaller than start), and `buildSlots` skips ranges with `start >= end`, so the override disappears. The `activeOverrides` filter at line 207 still uses the unshifted UTC start for picking the invitee day, so overrides shifted into an adjacent invitee day are neither selected nor placed correctly. Also `override.start.toString()` is used to build the dayjs object, which yields a locale-formatted string with truncated precision and is parsed in server-local time, so the offset can be wrong. `override.timeZone` is optional and, if undefined, `.tz(undefined)` falls back to the local zone.

title: New timezone test asserts unchanged behavior and doesn't cover the fix or the fixed-host case
body: The added test expects the identical slots for Asia/Dhaka and Asia/Kolkata, because timeSlots are returned in UTC and the helper compares UTC strings, so it cannot detect whether the override shifted per invitee timezone. The `toHaveTimeSlots` matcher also only uses `.every` over actual slots, so extra or missing expected slots can go unnoticed. No test covers the main fix of the PR (a round-robin event with fixed-host date overrides), nor DST or cross-midnight overrides.

title: Working-hours check is broken: `end` equals `start`, and a single non-matching entry rejects the slot
body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute()` is identical to `start`. It should use the slot end time, so the `end > workingHour.endTime` test only ever checks the slot start. The surrounding `workingHours.find(...)` returns true, meaning the slot is rejected, if ANY working-hour entry for that weekday does not contain the slot. A user with two blocks on one day (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17) therefore has every slot rejected, because it is outside at least one of the blocks. The same happens when multiple per-user entries are passed. The check should reject only if no entry contains the slot. As written it can wrongly remove valid slots, and the working-hours comparison is also done in UTC day/minutes.

title: Date override check rejects slots when there are multiple override ranges on one day
body: `dateOverrides.find(...)` returns true (slot unavailable) as soon as any override on the same date does not contain the slot. Cal.com allows several override ranges on the same day (e.g. 9-11 and 14-16). A slot inside the second range is rejected because it is outside the first. The logic should accept the slot if it fits within any override for that date. It also only compares `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` and `slotEndTime <= start`, so a slot that starts inside the override but ends after the override end is treated as available. The day-matching also compares the slot's UTC date against a start shifted by the negated offset, which is questionable for overrides near midnight.

title: Dead comparison using `===` on dayjs objects
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct object references, so it is always false. The branch is dead code. If the intent was to handle zero-length overrides (a day marked unavailable), it does not work. It should use `.isSame()` or compare timestamps.

title: Parsing `override.start.toString()` is locale-dependent and drops milliseconds
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` formats the Date with the locale-style `Date.toString()` and re-parses it. This is non-ISO and fragile, and it drops milliseconds. `override.timeZone` is optional in the type, so `.tz(undefined)` silently falls back to the default zone for overrides without a timezone. The code should pass `override.start` directly. The offset is also computed twice per override because `.add(offset)` is called separately for hour and minute.

title: Tests do not cover the behaviours the PR claims to fix
body: The new timezone test asserts identical UTC slots for +5:30 and +6:00 organizer/invitee views, so it does not prove that overrides adjust to the attendee timezone. `toHaveTimeSlots` only iterates over actual slots (`every`), so it does not check that the slot count matches. Extra or missing trailing slots can go unnoticed. There is no test for the main fix, date overrides on fixed hosts in round-robin events. There is also no test for multiple blocks or overrides on the same day, which the new availability code mishandles.

title: Migration crashes when the embed_category / uncategorized_category_id rows are missing
