body: `execute(...)[0]['id']` is called on the result of a join between `categories` and the `embed_category` site setting. When that setting was never saved (the default was '', so the row is normally absent) or matches no category, `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The same applies to `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value']` when that row doesn't exist, as on a fresh DB. Most installs have no `embed_category` row, so the migration fails for them. Guard against empty results (`.first`, `cmd_tuples`).

title: Raw string interpolation of host values into INSERT SQL
body: Each host line from the old site setting is interpolated straight into the SQL string. A value containing a single quote breaks the migration and is an injection vector. Lines can also contain `\r` or whitespace and are not stripped. Use `quote`/`connection.quote` or ActiveRecord to insert, and strip each line. Also, the old `type: host_list` values could include `http://` and paths, which are only normalized later by the model callbacks and not here.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host and mutates input in place
body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when `host` is nil. The controller assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, which is nil if the param is omitted, so this causes a 500 instead of a validation error. `sub!` also mutates the string in place, which can alter the caller's or params' string. Use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`, or guard on `host.present?`.

title: Case-insensitive lookup only lowercases the column, not the input
body: The query is `lower(host) = ?` with `uri.host` unmodified. A referer or embed URL with uppercase letters in the host (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com/...`) will not match a stored host, so legitimate embeds are rejected. Downcase the parameter too. The method also returns `false` or a record, which is an inconsistent return type.

title: update/destroy do not handle a missing record
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown id, and `save_host(nil)` / `host.destroy` then raise NoMethodError (500). Use `find` or return a 404. `params[:embeddable_host]` being absent likewise raises in `save_host`.

title: Fabricator file contents swapped
body: `category_fabricator.rb` now contains the `:embeddable_host` fabricator. All the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were moved into `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. They work only because all fabricator files are loaded, but anyone looking for them in the conventional file will not find them, and the diff is misleading. Restore the original category fabricator and put only the embeddable host one in its own file.

title: Category shown after save may not match what the server stored
body: After save, the category is set locally from `this.get('categoryId')`. When the user leaves the chooser empty, the server substitutes the uncategorized category, but the client sets `category` to `findById(null)` (undefined). The row then renders a blank category badge until reload. Use the `category_id` from the server response. In the same save path, the `edit` action seeds `categoryId` from `host.category.id` and the new-host path leaves it null.

title: Hydrated *_ids arrays can contain undefined and `|| []` is dead code
body: `obj[k].map(...)` returns an array that may contain `undefined` entries when a sub-record isn't in the root collection. `hydrated || []` is always truthy, so the fallback never applies, and consumers get undefined elements. Filter out missing entries. The branch also assumes `obj[k]` is an array without checking.

title: Test no longer tests what its name says
body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks embeddable hosts, but the test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' remains. It passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false. The nested `describe` also calls `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` even though the host is irrelevant to the result. The test is misleading and should be removed or rewritten.

title: New admin controllers have no behavioural tests
body: Both new admin controller specs only assert the class inherits from AdminController. Nothing covers create/update/destroy, the default-category fallback, validation errors, non-admin access, or the embedding show endpoint. The nil-record and nil-host failure paths therefore go untested. The migration is untested too.

title: Migration crashes when no `embed_category` setting row exists
body: The `execute(...)[0]['id']` call indexes the first row of a join between `categories` and `site_settings` on `name = 'embed_category'`. On any install where that setting was never saved, the result set is empty, so `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The `category_id == 0` fallback below it is never reached. The same problem applies to the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15, whose `[0]['value']` is also unguarded. The migration needs to handle empty results.

title: Raw string interpolation in INSERT; host values are unquoted, unstripped and unnormalised
body: Each line of the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is interpolated straight into SQL as `'#{h}'`. A value containing a quote breaks or injects into the statement. Lines are also not stripped, so `\r` or whitespace can be inserted. They are not normalised either: old entries like `http://foo.com` are stored with the scheme, and the model's `before_validation` stripping is bypassed. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote` or the model, and strip and normalise each entry.

title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `self.host.sub!` is called unconditionally. `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?` or a controller request with a missing `host` param gives nil, so it raises instead of failing validation. The in-place `sub!` also mutates the attribute string. Guard with `host.present?` or use non-bang `sub` with assignment.

title: update/destroy use `.first` and dereference nil for unknown ids
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a missing or already-deleted id. `save_host(nil)` and `host.destroy` then raise NoMethodError and the client gets a 500. Use `find`, which gives a proper 404, or add an explicit not-found response. `save_host` also dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` without a guard when the param is absent.

title: Host lookup lowercases the column but not the input
body: The query is `lower(host) = ?` with `uri.host` passed through unchanged. If the referer or URL host has uppercase characters (for example `http://EvilTrout.com/`), it will never match and the embed is rejected. Downcase the input (`host.downcase`). `record_for_host` also returns `false` instead of nil on failure, which is inconsistent with the `first` result.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category and embeddable_host files
body: `category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. It works only because both files are loaded, but it is clearly a mix-up. It will confuse anyone looking up a fabricator by filename and invites future conflicts or duplicate definitions.

title: Test no longer verifies host-dependence and its name is misleading
body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks for any embeddable host, so 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false. It no longer tests what its name says. The removed host check is a behaviour change, and the new test does not cover it.

title: `update` action is a no-op that returns the current state
body: `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` ignores all params and just re-serializes. The client `saveChanges` action calls `update({})`, so it implies saving but does nothing. Either remove the route and action, or implement them.

title: New admin CRUD endpoints have no functional tests
body: Both new controller specs only assert inheritance from `AdminController`. Create, update, destroy, validation errors, default category fallback, and non-admin access are all untested. The nil-id and nil-param crash paths would have been caught.

title: `_ids` embedding assumes an array and can leave undefined entries
body: The regex `(.+)\_id(s?)$` now matches any key ending in `_ids`, and `obj[k].map` throws if the value is not an array (null or a string). Entries that `_lookupSubType` cannot resolve become `undefined` inside the hydrated array. The `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code, since `map` always returns an array.

title: Migration crashes when no embed_category setting exists
body: `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` returns no rows when `embed_category` was never set, which is the default state and the case on fresh installs. `[0]` is then nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, so the migration fails. The fallback `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15 has the same unguarded `[0]['value']`. The result must be checked before indexing.

title: Unescaped setting value interpolated into raw INSERT SQL
body: Each line of the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is interpolated directly as `'#{h}'`. A value containing a quote, or stray whitespace or a trailing `\r` from the multi-line setting, breaks the statement or can inject SQL. Values are also inserted without the trimming or normalization that the model's `before_validation` would apply. Use `connection.quote` or the model.

title: before_validation raises on nil host and mutates in place
body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when `host` is nil. The admin controller assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, so a missing host param gives a 500 instead of a validation error. `sub!` also mutates the attribute string in place, which bypasses dirty tracking. Use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`, guarded for nil.

title: Host lookup is case-sensitive on the input side and ignores ports
body: The query compares `lower(host) = ?` against `uri.host`, which is not downcased, so a referer like `http://EviLTrout.com` never matches. The validation regex allows `host:port`, and `before_validation` keeps the port. `uri.host` never includes the port, so a host saved with a port can never match and is silently useless. Downcase the input and decide how ports are handled.

title: update and destroy dereference a nil record for unknown ids
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown or already-deleted id. `save_host(nil)` and `host.destroy` then raise NoMethodError and return a 500 instead of a 404. A double-clicked delete or a stale admin page triggers this. Use `find` or raise a not-found error.

title: No uniqueness validation or DB index on host
body: Duplicate hosts can be created, each possibly with a different category. `record_for_host` then returns an arbitrary one through `.first` with no ordering, so the category a topic is posted to is ambiguous. The migration also adds no index on `host`.

title: Fabricator file contents swapped between category and embeddable_host files
body: `category_fabricator.rb` now holds the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` holds the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. It works only because Fabrication loads every file in the directory. The contents are in the wrong files, so the diff looks like deleted category fabricators and the files are misleading to maintain.

title: Test 'false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests that
body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks for embeddable hosts. This test passes only because `embed_truncate` is false and the topic has no embed. The test name claims a behaviour that no longer exists, so it should be removed or renamed.

title: New admin controllers have no functional tests
body: The specs for both new admin controllers only assert the class hierarchy. Nothing covers create, update, destroy, validation errors, default category fallback, or permission checks, and those are the paths with the nil and error-handling bugs above.

title: Second `downsize` definition overrides the 4-arg version, breaking existing callers
body: `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is defined at line 145 and then redefined as `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. Ruby has no overloading, so the second definition replaces the first. Existing callers that pass `(from, to, width, height, opts)` now bind `height` to `dimensions` and `opts` to the hash. That makes `dimensions` the integer height and drops the width entirely, so the resize target is wrong and ImageMagick gets a malformed geometry. Or it raises ArgumentError for a 5-arg call with opts. The first definition is dead code. Keep one signature and update the callers.

title: Downsize loop ignores failures and may leave the image over the size limit
body: The return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored. If `convert` fails (missing binary, corrupt image), the loop still runs 5 times without changing the file. The oversized file is then passed to `Upload.create_for`, so the user sees a generic size error. Also, `tempfile.size` on a Ruby Tempfile can be stale after an external process rewrites the file, because of buffering and the cached size. The loop may then re-run needlessly or exit early. Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` and check the result.

title: In-place downsize with identical source and destination, and the `[0]` frame selector
body: `downsize` is called with `from == to == tempfile.path`. The downsize instructions use `from[0]`, which keeps only the first frame, so animated GIFs lose animation. The `allow_animation` branch is only taken if the temp path matches `/\.GIF$/i`. Upload tempfiles generally keep the extension, but for URL downloads this is not guaranteed. In the animated case, gifsicle with `--output` equal to the input is also questionable. In-place conversion also overwrites the original with no recovery if the conversion fails midway.

title: Hardcoded 10MB download cap ignores site settings
body: The API download limit is now a hardcoded `10.megabytes` instead of a site setting. The client-side limits in utilities.js are hardcoded to 10MB too. The admin-configured `max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb` no longer drives the client checks. Attachments are now capped at 10MB on the client regardless of `max_attachment_size_kb`, and the 413 error message shows 10MB even for configured limits. Larger configured limits are silently blocked, and smaller ones are no longer enforced client-side.

title: Client validation uses a fixed 10MB limit for all upload types
body: `maxSizeKB` was `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so it was per-type (image or attachment). It is now a constant 10MB for both. Attachments with a smaller configured limit pass client validation and fail only on the server. The server-side enforcement in `Upload.create_for` is unchanged, so the user gets a late, less helpful error.

title: Second `self.downsize` definition overrides the first, breaking existing callers
body: `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is defined at line 145 and then `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` is defined at line 149. Ruby has no overloading, so the second silently replaces the first. Any existing caller using the 4-positional-arg form (`downsize(from, to, 100, 100, opts)`) now passes `max_height` as the `opts` argument. `optimize` then reads `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer, which is a bug, and the dimensions are wrong. The first definition is dead code. Keep one signature and update callers.

title: Downsizing loop can run needlessly and uses the wrong extension/animation handling
body: The loop runs ImageMagick on `tempfile.path` in place, up to 5 times. When `convert` fails, `downsize` returns false and the file is unchanged, but the loop keeps retrying five times, each time spawning a process. The result is never checked. If the image is still too large afterwards, it proceeds to `Upload.create_for`, which presumably rejects it, but only after wasted work. Also, `tempfile.size` may be cached or stale after an external process rewrites the file, because it is a Ruby File/Tempfile object. `File.size(tempfile.path)` would be safer. The animated-GIF path (gifsicle) is chosen by the `.GIF` extension of the temp path. Rails tempfile names often lack the original extension, so animation handling will not trigger as intended. Stop the loop when the downsize returns false.

title: Hardcoded 10MB limit ignores site settings and the 413 message is inaccurate
body: The client-side limit was changed from `max_<type>_size_kb` to a hardcoded 10MB. This applies to attachments as well as images, so the `max_attachment_size_kb` setting is no longer enforced on the client. Attachments over the configured limit but under 10MB now pass the client check. Nothing in this diff shows the server enforcing it. The same hardcoding appears in the 413 handler (line 246). The error message reports a limit that may differ from the actual server limit. The magic number is duplicated in the JS and in the controller (`10.megabytes`).

title: API download limit hardcoded and `tempfile` nil not handled
body: The URL download limit was changed from the site setting to a fixed 10MB, so admins' configured limits are no longer honoured for API URL uploads. If the download fails, `tempfile` is nil because of `rescue nil`. The new guard handles nil, but `tempfile.size` on line 72 will still raise NoMethodError. This pre-existing problem is now more visible, since the new block is guarded for nil while the next line is not.

title: No tests for the new auto-downsize behavior
body: The new automatic downsizing path, the refactored `optimize`/`downsize` signature, and the removed `dimensions` helper have no accompanying tests. This is a behavioral change in upload handling that touches shell-invoked image processing.

title: Second `downsize` definition silently overrides the 5-arg version
body: Ruby has no overloading, so `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Any existing caller using the width/height form now passes `max_height` as `opts`. That either raises (for example when `opts[:allow_animation]` is called on an Integer) or silently drops the options. The earlier definition at line 145 is dead code. Remove one of the two, or have a single method that accepts either form.

title: Downsize loop overwrites the tempfile in place, with no failure check and a wrong extension
body: The result of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored. If convert fails, the loop retries the same unchanged file five times with no feedback. The tempfile is also overwritten in place, so `tempfile.size` may be stale if the File object caches it. The controller does not update `content_type` or `filename` to match the converted output. For animated GIFs, `optimize` only picks the animated path when the path matches `/\.GIF$/i`. Tempfile paths from uploads often lack an extension, so `convert` may fail or choose the wrong output format. The `"80%"` resize also ends up in `downsize_instructions` as `-resize 80%\>`. That form only shrinks if the image is larger than 80% of itself, which is always true, but it behaves oddly with `force_aspect_ratio`.

title: Client-side size limit hard-coded to 10MB and ignores site settings
body: The client now ignores `max_image_size_kb` and `max_attachment_size_kb`, replacing them with a fixed 10MB. Attachments, which are not downsized, can now pass client validation, hit the server limit, and get a generic error. The same applies to the 413 handler. The error message now reports 10MB even when the real limit is different. The server-side `10.megabytes` in the API URL download is likewise a hard-coded value that no longer follows the site setting. A shared constant or the settings should be used instead.

title: API URL download limit no longer tied to site settings
body: `FileHelper.download` was previously limited by `max_image_size_kb`. It is now fixed at 10MB regardless of the setting, and the oversized-image reduction only runs for images. Non-image files fetched through the API are therefore allowed up to 10MB, bypassing the configured attachment limit at this stage.

title: unsubscribe dereferences a possibly-nil TopicUser
body: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil if the user has no topic_users row for this topic. This can happen if the link is opened by a user with no row, for example one who was emailed through mailing list mode or was never tracked. `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError and the user gets a 500 instead of being unsubscribed. Use `TopicUser.change`, or create the record when it is missing.

title: State change on a GET request, with no Guardian check
body: A GET action mutates the user's notification level. Link prefetchers, email scanners and CSRF-style image loads can trigger it. Setting a regular-level user to muted is the more harmful case. The action never calls `guardian.ensure_can_see!`, and `TopicView.new` is built without the guardian. It should be a POST or PUT, or at least be confirmed by the client page. The bundled Ember route already exposes a UI for changing the state.

title: Toggle semantics are surprising and not idempotent
body: The action lowers tracking/watching to regular, and mutes if the level is already regular or lower. Clicking the same email link twice, or a prefetch followed by a click, silently escalates from 'stop watching' to fully muted. The user message says 'You will stop receiving notifications' without saying which level was applied.

title: Redirect loop or wrong target when slug is blank
body: When the slug doesn't match, the action redirects to `topic.unsubscribe_url`. If the topic's slug is empty (title with only non-slug characters), `url` has an empty segment and the redirect can hit `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` again with a blank slug. That loops forever. The redirect also drops query and format handling.

title: Unsubscribe not covered by tests and `render :show` change affects other callers
body: `perform_show_response` now calls `render :show` explicitly in the html branch. This is needed because the `unsubscribe` action has no template. No controller spec for `unsubscribe` was added, so the nil TopicUser case, the redirect case and the toggle behavior are untested. The spec change only adds an option to an existing builder test.

title: unsubscribe_url missing from templates for non-topic emails
body: `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but only `send_notification_email` provides it. Any other caller using `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will make I18n raise or leave the literal `%{unsubscribe_url}`. The body then contains a broken link. The spec had to be changed to pass `unsubscribe_url` to avoid this. Provide a fallback, or use a separate translation key when the URL is absent.

title: Multi-line unsubscribe_link yields trailing newline and text-body inconsistency
body: The block scalar `|` appends a trailing newline. In `body`, the unsubscribe text is appended after `"\n"` and now includes two paragraphs. Other locale files that translate `unsubscribe_link` without `%{unsubscribe_url}` will simply omit the per-topic link.

title: Typo in property name 'stopNotificiationsText'
body: The property name is misspelled ('Notificiations'). It is consistently misspelled in the controller and template, so it works, but it is a public name that will be confusing to maintain. Rename it.

title: Triple-stash rendering of a string containing topic title
body: `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` renders unescaped HTML. The text is built from `model.fancyTitle`, which is server-escaped. But the translation is interpolated client-side, and anything that bypasses fancy_title escaping would become XSS. This is a risky pattern. Escape the title explicitly and keep the `<strong>` in the template.

title: Title interpolated into HTML unescaped
body: Existing behavior, but the new conditional keeps pushing `title` raw into the buffer. Since `longDescription`, `text` and `row.title` are likewise unescaped, this stays an XSS surface if any of these are user-derived.

title: unsubscribe dereferences a possibly nil TopicUser record
body: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when the user has no topic_users row for the topic, for example when they were emailed via mailing list mode or never visited the topic. The next line then raises NoMethodError on `tu.notification_level`, producing a 500. Use `TopicUser.change`, or create the record when it is missing.

title: State-changing action on a GET request, and a bad toggle
body: A GET request changes the user's notification level, which is a CSRF-style side effect. Mail clients and link scanners that prefetch the URL, and anyone embedding it, will mute the topic. The action also toggles: a user at tracking or watching is lowered to regular, and a user already at regular is muted. Reloading the page or clicking the link twice therefore silently escalates to muted. The action should not be this non-idempotent.

title: `render :show` added to the shared perform_show_response
body: `render :show` was added inside the `format.html` block of `perform_show_response`, which `show` also calls. Previously the implicit render happened. `unsubscribe` has no template of its own, so the explicit render is needed there, but the change affects both actions. Check that `show` is not rendered twice or affected when other code paths reach it.

title: Redirect and guardian handling in unsubscribe
body: The redirect to `unsubscribe_url` when the slug is missing or wrong sends a 301, which browsers cache permanently. The redirect target is built from the topic's absolute URL, which is fine. The route `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` carries no slug, so a user who is not logged in gets `ensure_logged_in`'s error rather than a login flow that returns to the unsubscribe action. For an emailed link this gives a poor experience.

title: `unsubscribe_url` is not passed to the other `unsubscribe_link` users
body: The `unsubscribe_link` locale string now contains `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but only `send_notification_email` supplies that argument. The digest, and any other mailer that sets `add_unsubscribe_link`, does not pass it. Interpolation then raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument, or the link is left blank. `MessageBuilder#body` and `html_part` are used by every mail with `add_unsubscribe_link`, so those mails can break.

title: Multi-line unsubscribe_link text body
body: The block scalar ends with a trailing newline, and `body` appends it after a `\n`. The text-email layout changes and the footer is now two paragraphs. For emails where `unsubscribe_url` is unset, such as the digest, the interpolation fails (see the other finding). Other locale files that still hold the old single-sentence string will not show the per-topic link.

title: Typo in property name 'stopNotificiationsText'
body: The property name is misspelled as `stopNotificiationsText`. It is used consistently between the controller and the template, so nothing breaks, but it should be fixed now rather than baked into the API.

title: Triple-stash renders a title interpolated into an HTML translation
body: `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` renders unescaped HTML built from `model.fancyTitle`. `fancy_title` is HTML-escaped on the server, so this is probably safe, but the safety depends on that server-side escaping. Because I18n.t does not escape the interpolated value, any path that sets `fancyTitle` from unescaped data would allow XSS.

title: Template path and route naming mismatch
body: The template is at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which maps to the route `topic.unsubscribe`. The route is registered as the top-level `topicUnsubscribe`, so the matching template would be `topic-unsubscribe` or `topicUnsubscribe`. The page may render blank. The `topic` controller and route naming also need checking.

title: Unrelated route constraint changes
body: The `post_number` constraint was removed from the summary routes, and routes were reordered, with no explanation. The `post_number` constraint was a no-op for those paths, but changes to existing routes in a feature PR add regression risk. The `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` route has to sit before the `t/:slug/:topic_id` catch-alls; this order works but is fragile.

title: No tests for the new unsubscribe controller action or URL
body: The only test change adds an `unsubscribe_url` option in the message builder spec. Nothing covers `TopicsController#unsubscribe`: the nil `TopicUser` case, the toggle between regular and muted, the redirect, or login enforcement. There are also no tests for `Topic#unsubscribe_url` or for the per-topic link in the email body.

title: unsubscribe dereferences a possibly-nil TopicUser record
body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id:, topic_id:)` returns nil when the user has no topic_users row, for example when they were emailed through a category watch or mailing-list mode and never visited the topic. Line 107 then raises NoMethodError, so the user gets a 500 on the unsubscribe link. Use `TopicUser.change`, or create the record, instead of assuming it exists.

title: State-changing action performed on a GET request
body: The unsubscribe action changes the user's notification level on a plain GET route. Mail clients, link scanners and prefetchers will trigger the change just by fetching the URL. Any third-party page can also mute or unwatch a topic through a cross-site request such as an `` tag, because there is no CSRF protection on GET. The change should only happen after an explicit POST or PUT confirmation.

title: No visibility check before showing and modifying the topic
body: `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` raises if the topic is not visible to the user, which is partly protected. However, the redirect branch uses `@topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url` before anything else, and the action then writes to TopicUser and renders the full topic view. The action also falls through to `perform_show_response`, which serialises and preloads the entire topic. A lightweight confirmation page would be safer and cheaper.

title: Toggle semantics make the unsubscribe link non-idempotent
body: If the level is above regular it is set to regular. Otherwise it is set to muted. Clicking the same emailed link twice, or refreshing the page, goes from tracking/watching to regular and then to muted. The user ends up muting the topic when they only meant to stop notifications. The link should set a deterministic target state.

title: Direct save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
body: `tu.save!` does not set `notifications_changed_at` or `notifications_reason_id`. It also does not publish the MessageBus `notification_level_change` that `TopicUser.change` handles. The rest of the code base uses `TopicUser.change` for level changes, so the reason and timestamp can be stale and open clients are not notified.

title: Explicit `render :show` added to shared perform_show_response
body: Adding `render :show` to the HTML branch of `perform_show_response` is needed so `unsubscribe` finds a template. It also changes the shared path used by `show`, `wordpress` and others. It is easy to double-render or change behaviour if a caller has already rendered, and it is not covered by tests.

title: Triple-stash renders unescaped HTML containing the topic title
body: `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` is unescaped. The text is built from `model.fancyTitle` and interpolated into an I18n string. `fancyTitle` is escaped server-side, but this relies on the title being sanitised on every path. If the title is ever not escaped, this is an XSS vector. The property name `stopNotificiationsText` is also misspelled (extra 'i').

title: Route model hook has no error handling
body: `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` has no catch. If the user is not logged in or cannot see the topic, the route fails without graceful handling. `afterModel` also sets `details.notificationReasonText` directly and assumes `details` exists.

title: unsubscribe_link translation needs %{unsubscribe_url} for all callers
body: The `unsubscribe_link` string now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Only `send_notification_email` passes it. Other callers that set `add_unsubscribe_link` and do not pass `unsubscribe_url` will get an I18n missing-interpolation error (raised in tests, rendered as a broken string in production). The spec was patched to pass a fake URL rather than handling the missing-key case in the builder.

title: Multi-line unsubscribe_link is also used in plain-text body
body: The locale string is now a YAML block scalar with a trailing newline and a blank line. It is appended in `body` via `body << I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', ...)` and used as markdown in the HTML part. Other locale files still lack `%{unsubscribe_url}` and the new text, so non-English locales will not show the per-topic link. Spec coverage for the new text is missing.

title: Route ordering and constraint changes lack tests
body: The PR reorders the routes and changes the `summary` constraints by dropping `post_number`. It adds two unsubscribe routes but there are no controller specs for unsubscribe: the redirect, a missing TopicUser, the level toggle, and an unauthenticated user. Mail template output is untested as well.

title: Validator has a side effect: should_block? writes to the DB on every validation
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` increments `match_count` and saves the record. It is called from inside a validator, which runs on every `valid?`, not only on save. In `UsersController#create`, `user.valid?` runs and then `user.save` runs it again, so a single signup attempt bumps `match_count` twice. Any other `valid?` call also inflates the count. Validations should not write to the database. Counting also happens even when the user is never created, and inside a validation context it can be rolled back or can leave the statistics inconsistent. The counting should happen only on an actual rejected save, or be explicit and separate from validation.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of match_count
body: `record.match_count += 1` followed by `save` is a read-modify-write in Ruby. Concurrent signups with the same blocked email load the same count and overwrite each other, so increments are lost. Use an atomic `update_all`/`increment_counter` instead. The `save` return value is also ignored.

title: Email lookup is case-sensitive and not normalized
body: `where(email: email)` is an exact match, and neither the stored value nor the lookup is downcased or stripped. `Bad@Spam.com` therefore bypasses a block on `bad@spam.com`. The rest of the codebase normalizes with `Email.downcase`. Blocklist bypass is trivial.

title: Nil value is not guarded and the blocked check runs on every email change
body: `validates :email, email: true` has no `allow_nil`, so `value` can be nil (presence already fails in that case). `email_in_restriction_setting?` then does `nil =~ regexp`, which works, but `BlockedEmail.should_block?(nil)` runs a pointless query. More importantly, the validator is also triggered by `email_changed?` in flows like `change_email` and `create_for_email`, where the side-effecting counter is bumped in unintended contexts.

title: values hash is built from user.attributes and exposes raw state
body: The failure response now returns `user.attributes.slice(...)` and the full `errors` hash. The client uses `result.errors.email` to add any email-related error (including a plain uniqueness error) to `rejectedEmails`. It is then reported as the generic 'invalid' message, which hides the real server error reason. The client does not distinguish the blocked error from other errors.

title: rejectedEmails array is shared across all controller instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is declared on the prototype in `extend`, so one array instance is shared by all instances and persists across modal opens. Rejected emails are never cleared. Initialize it in `init` instead.

title: Rejected-email message is the generic 'invalid' text
body: A server-rejected email (blocked or domain-not-allowed) is shown as `user.email.invalid`, which misleads the user. A server-provided message should be used. Also, `rejectedEmails.@each` is not a valid dependent key form; use `rejectedEmails.[]`.

title: Validator spec is incomplete
body: The spec stubs `should_block?` and does not cover the whitelist/blacklist branches that were moved here from `User`. The old `user_spec` coverage may now be only indirect. It also does not test that blocking is skipped when a domain error already exists. There is no integration test showing a user with a blocked email fails validation, or that `valid?` repeated does not double count.

title: Validation has a side effect: should_block? writes to the DB on every validation
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` increments match_count and saves the record each time it is called. The validator calls it inside `validate_each`, which runs on every `valid?` or `save`. In `UsersController#create`, `user.valid?` runs and then `user.save` runs again, so a single signup attempt counts twice. Any later save with a changed email also bumps the counter. The validator also writes to the database inside a validation, which should be read-only. Move the stat update out of validation, or only record a match when the block actually happens.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count
body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` loads the value into Ruby, increments it, and writes it back. Concurrent signups with the same blocked email will lose updates. Use `update_all` or `increment_counter` with an atomic SQL increment instead.

title: Case-sensitive exact email lookup
body: `where(email: email)` is an exact, case-sensitive match. The unique index and uniqueness validation are case-sensitive as well. A blocked address `Bad@Spam.com` is bypassed by `bad@spam.com`. The rest of the app normalizes emails with `Email.downcase`. The email should be normalized when stored and when compared.

title: Blocked-email check skipped when domain check fails, and nil value risks
body: The block check only runs when `record.errors[attribute]` is blank. That is a deliberate guard, but it also depends on earlier validators: the presence and uniqueness errors on the same attribute suppress the blocked check and its stats. Separately, `value` can be nil. `email_in_restriction_setting?` would then compute `nil =~ regexp`, which returns nil, so a whitelist would add an error to a nil value. This is harmless when presence already fails, but the code is fragile.

title: Missing newline at end of file
body: The file has no trailing newline, as the diff itself shows with `\ No newline at end of file`.

title: rejectedEmails array is shared across all controller instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined on the class prototype, so one array instance is shared by every instance and persists. `pushObject` mutates that shared array. Initialize it in `init` instead. The property dependency `'rejectedEmails.@each'` is also non-standard; it should be `rejectedEmails.[]`.

title: Failed-create response exposes values and error details to client, enabling blocklist probing
body: The failure response now returns `user.errors.to_hash` and the submitted values. Combined with the `blocked` error message and the client rejecting only that email, this lets anyone probe whether specific addresses are on the block list. The client rejects any email error, including 'has already been taken', not just blocked ones. `user.attributes.slice` is also an unnecessarily broad way to echo input; `params` would do.

title: No test of the validator integration with User
body: The specs stub `should_block?` for the validator and never test that a `User` with a blocked email is invalid. They also don't cover interaction with the whitelist/blacklist domain settings. The refactor moved the domain validation from `User` into a new validator, so the domain restriction behavior now has no test coverage in the new spec files.

title: Validator has a database write side effect and runs on every validation
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at` and saves the record. It is called from inside a validator, which runs on every `valid?` call. In `UsersController#create`, `user.valid?` is called and then `user.save` validates again, so a single signup attempt increments the counter twice. Validation also writes to the DB even when the user is never saved, and the write sits inside the save transaction, so it is rolled back if the save fails. The statistics are therefore unreliable, and validation is no longer free of side effects.

title: Email lookup is case-sensitive and not normalized
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` does an exact-case match, but emails are case-insensitive in practice and elsewhere in the codebase are downcased via `Email.downcase`. A blocked address like `bad@spam.com` can be bypassed by signing up as `Bad@Spam.com`. Neither the stored value nor the lookup value is normalized. A nil email passed to the validator is also not handled.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count
body: `record.match_count += 1` followed by `save` is a lost-update race under concurrent signups. Use `update_all`, or an atomic `match_count = match_count + 1`, instead. The save also ignores its return value.

title: Validator crashes on nil/blank values and the record is not checked for missing attributes
body: `validate_each` runs the whitelist/blacklist regexp and `BlockedEmail.should_block?` on `value` without a nil guard. `value =~ regexp` with a nil value returns nil, so the whitelist branch wrongly adds a "not allowed" error on top of the presence error. Skipping blank values (`allow_blank`) would avoid this.

title: rejectedEmails array is shared across all controller instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined on the prototype in `extend`, so the same array object is shared by every instance, and entries are never cleared. Rejected emails persist for the lifetime of the page and across instances. Initialize it in `init`. The `.property('accountEmail', 'rejectedEmails.@each')` dependency key is also non-standard for this Ember version.

title: Any email error is treated as a rejected email, with a generic message
body: `result.errors.email` is truthy for any email error, including "has already been taken" or a malformed address. The email is then marked locally as invalid with the generic `user.email.invalid` text. The user sees no explanation of why it was blocked. The server's actual reason is not surfaced in the field validation.

title: No tests for whitelist/blacklist behavior or the end-to-end user validation path
body: The whitelist/blacklist logic was moved from User into the validator, but the new spec only covers the blocked-email stub. The existing domain restriction behavior and the skipping of the blocked check when a domain error is already present are not tested. The controller's new `errors`/`values` response fields and the validation counting behavior are also untested.

title: Referer-based embed authorization is weak and sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL
body: `ensure_embeddable` trusts the client-supplied Referer host and then sets `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`. A Referer can be forged or stripped by non-browser clients. When the check passes, the page can be framed by any site. Rendering also runs for logged-in users with their cookies, so clickjacking is possible. Prefer a `frame-ancestors` CSP restricted to `embeddable_host`. The check also ignores scheme and port. Subdomains of the host are not handled, so legitimate embeds there fail.

title: embed_url is not validated against embeddable_host before enqueueing, and the job is enqueued on every miss
body: `embed_url` comes straight from the query string. A Referer check is the only guard, and `TopicRetriever` checks the host only later in the job. Every miss enqueues a Sidekiq job, so an attacker can flood the queue with arbitrary URLs. The `loading` page also auto-reloads every 30s, which enqueues another job each time. Validate the URL's host synchronously in the controller before enqueueing.

title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript
body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` is HTML-escaped by ERB but is placed inside a JS string in a `<script>` block. The Referer header is only checked on its host component. A path or query string containing a quote or backslash, or a newline, can break out of the string or cause JS errors. HTML escaping does not make the value safe in a JS context. Also, the full Referer URL is used as the `postMessage` targetOrigin, which must be an origin only. Use the origin (`scheme://host[:port]`) via `to_json`/`j`.

title: Weak postMessage origin check via indexOf
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test. An empty or short origin string, or an origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`, passes. For example, origin `http://a` matches `http://a.example.com/`. Compare `e.origin` for exact equality with the origin of `discourseUrl`.

title: contents mutated with << and footer is added before the sha1 is computed on each import
body: `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string in place. This can raise FrozenError for frozen strings and has side effects on the caller. The link is also interpolated unescaped into an HTML attribute (`'<a href='#{url}'>`). Separately, `import_remote` and the feed importer pass content straight from remote sources, which then go into a raw_html post with no sanitization (see `Post#cook`). That makes stored XSS possible.

title: raw_html cook method skips all sanitization
body: When `cook_method` is `raw_html`, `cook` returns `raw` untouched. Content fetched from remote sites or RSS feeds is stored and later rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and in the main site. Scripts and event handlers in the feed content run in the forum's origin. ruby-readability sanitizes only to a limited degree, and the RSS path (`CGI.unescapeHTML` of feed content) has no sanitizer at all. The content should be sanitized, for example with Sanitize.

title: Kernel#open on admin-configured URL (and in import_remote)
body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses open-uri's `Kernel#open`. A value beginning with `|` runs a shell command, and a path reads local files. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does the same with `open(url).read`. There the URL is supplied by the embedding page and only its host is checked. Use `URI.parse(...).open` or RestClient with an http(s) scheme check. This is also a possible SSRF vector.

title: Feed item handling not nil-safe and one bad item aborts the whole run
body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no `content`. Many RSS feeds only supply `description`, and `String#scrub` also requires Ruby 2.1+. Any exception in `TopicEmbed.import` aborts the loop for all remaining items. The job has `retry: false`. `feed_key` is defined but never used, so there is no conditional-GET caching and the whole feed is re-fetched hourly.

title: Non-atomic setnx + expire throttle
body: If the process dies between `setnx` and `expire`, the key never expires. That URL is then blocked forever for non-staff users. Use `SET key value EX 60 NX`, or `setex`-style semantics.

title: Spec expects TopicRetriever.new in the request, but the controller enqueues a job
body: The controller calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. The spec expects `TopicRetriever.new` and `retrieve` to be invoked during the request. This only works if jobs execute inline in test. Even then it is an indirect assertion. The test does not verify that the job is enqueued with the right arguments.

title: Revising a raw_html post may re-cook and drop content
body: `Post#before_save` re-cooks via `cook(raw, topic_id: ...)`. For raw_html posts this returns raw, which is fine. `TopicEmbed.import` also calls `absolutize_urls` on update, but computes `content_sha1` from the pre-absolutize contents. The `bypass_rate_limiter` option is respected, but `revise!` returns false when the absolutized raw equals the stored raw. In that case `embed.update_column(:content_sha1)` is still executed, which is fine. A missing post (`embed.post` nil) would raise on `PostRevisor.new(nil)`.

title: Unrelated edit to an existing migration adds force: true
body: `force: true` on `create_table` drops the table if it exists. The edit is made to an already-existing migration, which is unrelated to this PR. It is risky if the migration is ever re-run. The unrelated whitespace changes in `20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` are noise as well.

title: create_table with force: true drops existing table
body: `force: true` will silently drop any existing `topic_embeds` table and its data when the migration is run. It is also not reversible in an obvious way. The `topic_id` and `post_id` columns have no indexes, although `where(topic_id:)` is used.

title: Invalid ERB `<%- end if %>` and posts-present check mislabelled
body: `<%- end if %>` is a syntax error in ERB/Ruby. `end if` requires a condition and is not a valid terminator for the `if/else` block. The template will fail to compile, so the embed page would never render. In addition, the branch logic is inverted from a readable standpoint: 'Discussion Highlights' is shown only when posts exist. A topic with only the first post would show 'Begin the Discussion'.

title: Header text depends on posts but view assumes topic_view is set after TopicView.new with nil topic
body: `TopicView.new` could raise for a deleted or inaccessible topic. `topic_id_for_embed` returns an id even if the topic was trashed, which results in an error page inside the iframe. There is no handling.

title: Referer-based host check is the only guard and sets X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL
body: The embeddable-host check relies solely on the client-supplied Referer header, which is trivial to spoof. Once it passes, the controller sets `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`. The page can also be framed by any site that strips or forges the referer, which opens clickjacking. The check also compares only the host and ignores the scheme and port.

title: Invalid ERB `end if` and nil topic in best view
body: `<%- end if %>` is a syntax error in ERB: `end` is followed by a dangling `if` with no condition. The template will not compile, so `/embed/best` fails whenever a topic exists. Separately, the view uses `@topic_view.topic.url`. The `TopicView.new` call can raise if the topic is not visible to the user.

title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript
body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` is HTML-escaped but not JS-escaped. A referer containing `'`, a backslash, or a newline, or `</script>`-style content, breaks out of the string literal or the script block. The result is an XSS vector, or at minimum a broken postMessage target. It should use `j`/`to_json`. An empty referer also makes postMessage throw.

title: `contents <<` mutates caller's string and the hash changes on every poll
body: `contents <<` mutates the argument in place. It will raise `FrozenError` for frozen strings and has side effects for callers. The appended footer is included in the SHA1, which is acceptable only if it is deterministic. The footer also interpolates the URL into an `href='...'` without escaping.

title: Kernel#open on admin-supplied URL and unsafe feed handling
body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with open-uri's Kernel#open will execute a shell command if the string starts with `|`. It also reads local files. Use `URI.parse(url).open` or RestClient. The same applies to `open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, where the URL comes from the embed_url request param (only host-checked in TopicRetriever).

title: Feed item content handling can crash or import unsanitized HTML
body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no content, aborting the whole poll. `CGI.unescapeHTML` is applied to the content. The result is imported as raw HTML (cook_method raw_html, validations skipped) and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view. No sanitization is applied, so a malicious or compromised feed can inject scripts. The unused `feed_key`, which was meant for modified-tracking, indicates unfinished logic.

title: Non-atomic create can fail on unique index race and orphan data
body: If `creator.create` fails, `post` is a post with errors and `present?` is true. The code then calls `TopicEmbed.create!` with `post.topic_id`, which may be nil, and raises on the NOT NULL column. Concurrent imports of the same URL (poll job plus retrieve job) can also both pass the `embed.blank?` check and violate the unique index, leaving an orphan topic. `PostCreator` has its own inner transaction that does not roll back the topic when the outer `create!` raises unless nested properly.

title: absolutize_urls mishandles protocol-relative URLs and ports
body: `start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.jpg`. These are rewritten into `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.jpg`, which is wrong. Relative paths without a leading slash (e.g. `foo.html`) are not handled at all. The prefix also omits the port for any URL on 80/443 regardless of scheme.

title: Weak origin check in postMessage handler
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring check. An origin like `http://a` or an empty string would match as a substring of the Discourse URL, so an attacker origin that is a substring of discourseUrl is accepted. It should compare for equality against the parsed origin.

title: Controller spec expects TopicRetriever.new in controller but controller enqueues a job
body: The controller calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders 'loading'. The spec 'tells the topic retriever to work' expects `TopicRetriever.new` and `retrieve` to be called synchronously. That only passes if jobs run inline in test. The spec is also loose, since no render assertion is made. Separately, enqueuing a job on every uncached request for an arbitrary `embed_url` (the throttle only applies inside the job) allows queue flooding.

title: Editing an existing migration to add force: true drops table data
body: Modifying an already-shipped migration to add `force: true` makes `create_table` drop an existing `top_topics` table. The change is unrelated to this PR. The same applies to the `topic_embeds` migration, where `force: true` can silently drop data on re-run. Related, the unrelated whitespace edit to `MigrateWordCounts` (and its removed trailing newline) adds noise.

title: Revised raw_html post cook behavior and skip_validations side effects
body: `before_save` re-cooks via `cook`, which returns raw for raw_html posts. That works, but `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` now ignores the failure result as before. The `revise!` method still returns true even if save fails. `TopicEmbed.import` then does `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` regardless of whether the revision succeeded, so a failed revise marks the content as already synced.

title: Reload loop via 30s timer with no retry limit
body: The loading page reloads every 30 seconds forever. Each reload enqueues another retrieve job, hitting the Redis throttle. If the retrieval permanently fails (remote down, invalid user), the iframe loops indefinitely and generates load.

title: Referer-based host check is weak and bypassable; X-Frame-Options set to ALLOWALL
body: Embedding access control relies entirely on the Referer header's host equalling SiteSetting.embeddable_host. The Referer is attacker-controlled outside browsers and may be stripped or spoofed. Once it passes, X-Frame-Options is set to ALLOWALL, so any page that can forge or strip the referer can frame the content. A proper fix would use CSP frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options ALLOW-FROM with the configured host instead of ALLOWALL.

title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript string
body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` is placed inside a JS string. ERB HTML-escapes it, but that does not protect a JS string context in all cases, and the referer is user-controlled. It is also the full referer URL, not an origin, so postMessage's targetOrigin may not match (postMessage requires an origin, and a full URL with a path is reduced or rejected in some browsers). Use `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` with a scheme, or `j`/to_json escaping.

title: Weak origin check uses indexOf on discourseUrl
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring check, not an equality check. An origin such as `http://a` or an empty/short string that is a substring of discourseUrl would pass. Compare origins for equality instead.

title: Unescaped URL and imported HTML are stored and rendered raw (stored XSS)
body: Remote HTML (from feed or readability) is stored as raw and served unsanitized via cook_method raw_html and `raw post.cooked`; the feed-supplied URL is interpolated into an `<a href='...'>` without escaping. Feed or page content containing script or attribute injection is therefore served from the forum origin and embedded in the iframe. The content should be sanitized, and the URL escaped.

title: import mutates the caller's contents string with <<
body: `contents << ...` mutates the argument in place. If the string is frozen it raises, and callers' strings are altered. It also means the sha1 includes the footer, so it will be recomputed identically only if the footer is the same. Use a new string instead.

title: Kernel#open on user-influenced URL (SSRF / command execution)
body: `open(url)` with open-uri's Kernel#open will run a shell command if the string begins with `|`, and fetches arbitrary URLs. `import_remote` is reachable from the retrieve_topic job with the user-supplied embed_url. The host is checked against embeddable_host, but disqus.thor passes arbitrary links. In PollFeed, `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has the same problem. Use `URI.parse(url).open` or Net::HTTP with scheme validation.

title: Race creating duplicate embeds; transaction doesn't prevent duplicate topics
body: The check `embed.blank?` followed by creating the post and TopicEmbed is racy. Concurrent jobs for the same URL create two topics, then TopicEmbed.create! hits the unique index and raises. The raise happens after PostCreator has committed side effects (the rollback is inside the transaction, but job enqueues occur in PostCreator, and the post was created). Handle RecordNotUnique or use a lock.

title: absolutize_urls drops/mishandles ports and protocol-relative URLs
body: `prefix << ...` mutates an interpolated string (fine) but the port rule omits the port for 80 or 443 regardless of scheme, so an http URL on 443 or an https URL on 80 is wrong. Also, `//host/path` protocol-relative hrefs start with '/' and are rewritten into `prefix/host/path`, which is broken.

title: Feed item content may be nil / String#scrub on Ruby <2.1, no error handling
body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError if an item has no content (e.g. only description), aborting the whole poll. `String#scrub` is also unavailable before Ruby 2.1, which this Rails 4.0-era app likely runs on. Any one bad item stops the import of the rest, and sidekiq retry is disabled. The `feed_key` method is unused.

title: Controller spec expects TopicRetriever.new to be called, but controller enqueues a job
body: The controller enqueues Jobs :retrieve_topic, whereas the spec 'tells the topic retriever to work' expects TopicRetriever.new and retrieve to be invoked directly. This only passes if jobs run inline in test, and the expectation is brittle. Additionally, the `loading` render followed by `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` caches the loading page. Also an unauthenticated visitor can enqueue a job for an arbitrary embed_url; the throttle only runs later in the job.

title: Invalid ERB `<%- end if %>` breaks template
body: Line 6 is `<%- end if %>`, which is a syntax error (`end if` with no condition). The template will fail to compile, so the embed best page always errors. It should be `<%- end %>`. Also, when `@topic_view` posts is empty, the view still links via topic.url.

title: skip_validations added silently to revise! affects all callers
body: The new `skip_validations` option makes `@post.save` bypass validations. It is undocumented, and a blank line was removed in revise!. It is only used by TopicEmbed, but the option is exposed to every caller of the revisor. Fine if intentional, but it should be documented and tested.

title: Non-atomic setnx + expire throttle
body: `setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is non-atomic. If the process dies between the two, the key never expires and the URL is permanently throttled. Use `set` with `nx` and `ex` options or `setex`-style atomic operations.

title: Unrelated edit to an existing migration adds force: true (drops table)
body: Modifying an already-existing migration to `force: true` makes `create_table` drop an existing top_topics table if the migration is re-run. The change is unrelated to this feature and is data-destructive. The whitespace change to migrate_word_counts is also unrelated noise.

title: Weak tests: 'is 404' only asserts not success; missing coverage for view/XSS/URL edge cases
body: The first test is named '404' but only asserts `should_not be_success`, and it would pass for the wrong reason (the referer check fails before params.require runs). No tests cover referer host mismatch, invalid-URI referers, rendering best.html.erb (which would have caught the template syntax error), or PollFeed.poll_feed itself.

title: `.small-action` becomes a flex container but its children still rely on `float`
body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex`, but its children still use floats. `.topic-avatar` has `float: left` and `button` has `float: right`; floats are ignored on flex items. The button used to sit at the right edge and now sits immediately after `.small-action-desc`, because `.small-action-desc` has no `flex: 1` and the button has no `margin-left: auto`. The trailing `clear: both` on the same rule is also meaningless for a flex container. The float declarations should be removed and the button should be pushed right with `margin-left: auto` or a flex-grow on the description.

title: `align-items` mixin emits a non-existent `-ms-align-items` property and has trailing whitespace
body: `-ms-align-items` is not a real property, so it just adds dead CSS. The legacy `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` properties also use different keywords (`start`/`end`) than the modern `flex-start`/`flex-end`. The mixin passes `$alignment` through unchanged, so any value other than `center` or `baseline` produces invalid declarations for the old syntaxes. Line 120 also has trailing whitespace after `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;`.

title: Global `order` and `line-height` added to `.extra-info-wrapper`
body: `@include order(2)` and `line-height: 1.5` are applied to `.extra-info-wrapper` globally, not scoped to the header. `order` only matters inside the header's flex `.contents`, which couples this rule to the header layout. `line-height: 1.5` is a visible change to every place the class is used. The removed `.bullet { margin-top: 5px }` compensation also now depends on `align-items: center` in the parent. Any context where this wrapper is not inside that flex container will misalign the bullet badge.

title: `float: right` on the button is ignored now that `.small-action` is a flex container
body: `.small-action` became `display: flex`, and `float` has no effect on flex items. The `button { float: right; }` rule (and `.topic-avatar { float: left }`) therefore no longer does anything. The button, which was pushed to the right edge before, will now sit directly after the description text. The rule needs `margin-left: auto` or an equivalent, or the dead float declarations should be removed.

title: Hard-coded percentage padding replaces the fixed 4em indent
body: `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` became `padding: 0 1.5%`. The description's left offset now depends on container width instead of lining up with the 45px icon column. The description is also no longer given `flex: 1` or a similar sizing rule. Long text or a custom message can therefore push the button or squeeze the avatar, and the alignment will vary across viewports. The removed vertical padding and margins also change the spacing of every small-action post, which the PR title doesn't mention.

title: `align-items` mixin passes the modern value to legacy prefixed properties unchanged
body: The same `$alignment` is written to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy syntaxes use different keywords: `start`/`end` instead of `flex-start`/`flex-end`. `-ms-align-items` is not a real property at all. The mixin only works for `center` and `baseline`. Any other value will produce invalid declarations in older browsers. The line on 120 also has trailing whitespace.

title: `.extra-info-wrapper` styling changes may regress bullet badge alignment
body: The `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px }` compensation is removed and `line-height: 1.5` is added to the wrapper. The bullet badge's vertical position inside the topic header now depends on the flex centering and the new line-height, with no explicit handling. Floated `.badge-wrapper` children inside a flex item are also a fragile combination. Nothing in the PR shows that this was visually verified.

title: PR title and description do not match the change
body: The description is just "Test 5". The change goes beyond header layout: it also reworks `.small-action` post styling, the badges, and the topic title styles. Reviewers cannot tell the intended scope, or why `float` was replaced by flexbox for performance.

title: align-items mixin passes the modern keyword to legacy and non-existent properties
body: The mixin writes the same `$alignment` value into `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy syntaxes use different keywords: `start` and `end` instead of `flex-start` and `flex-end`. Any caller passing `flex-start` or `flex-end` would get an invalid declaration, which is silently dropped, so the prefixed fallback does nothing. `-ms-align-items` is not a real property at all. Current callers use only `center` and `baseline`, so nothing breaks today. The mixin is still unsafe as a general-purpose helper, and line 120 has trailing whitespace.

title: Inconsistent default ordering between legacy and modern flexbox for the header
body: `.panel` gets `order(3)`, which emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 3`. Its siblings in the header, such as the logo/title, have no explicit order. Old `-webkit-box` ordinal groups default to 1, while the modern `order` default is 0. On browsers that use the legacy syntax, the relative order of items with and without an explicit value can therefore differ from modern browsers. This is minor, but the fallback prefixes give a false sense of cross-browser parity.

title: small-action layout rewritten with a percentage padding and removed spacing
body: `.small-action` becomes a flex container. The `.small-action-desc` padding is changed from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`, and `margin-top: 5px` is removed. Inner paragraph margins and padding are also zeroed. This changes the vertical spacing and the avatar-to-text gap of every small-action post (closed, pinned, and similar). The gap now varies with container width instead of being fixed, so it can look wrong on narrow or mobile layouts. Floats on `.topic-avatar`, `.avatar` and `button`, plus the leftover `clear: both`, are now redundant or conflicting inside a flex container. There is no evidence that mobile or other overriding stylesheets were checked.

title: Removed bullet badge margin and added line-height without compensating alignment
body: The `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px }` rule is removed from `.extra-info-wrapper`, and `line-height: 1.5` and `order(2)` are added. `order` only has an effect if `.extra-info-wrapper` is a direct child of the new flex container `.d-header .contents`, which this PR does not show. The bullet badge's vertical alignment now depends on the inline-flex baseline alignment in `badges.css.scss` plus the new line-height. That may shift the badge relative to the title, and nothing verifies it.

title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?`, so it is never called
body: ActiveModel::Serializer only honours `include_<attr>?` methods. `include_website_name` without the `?` is dead code. As a result `website_name` is always serialized, even when website is blank, and for TL0 users seen by anonymous. It is also not listed in `untrusted_attributes`. The website host leaks for restricted users whose `website` is hidden, and it appears as null when there is no website.

title: `website_name` crashes or misbehaves with blank or unusual website values
body: `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` will return nil for blank values, so `website_name` is nil. For a host-less URI like "example.com" without a scheme, the name is nil and the old client behaviour (split('/')[2]) is lost. If `website_host` is present but `Discourse.current_hostname` is nil (e.g. in some contexts), `discourse_host.split` raises NoMethodError. The URI is parsed repeatedly; compute it once. Also `path` may be a trailing '/', yielding names like 'example.com/'.

title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic is wrong for multi-part TLDs and unrelated domains
body: The check compares host label counts and then everything after the first label. For hosts like `a.co.uk` and `b.co.uk` (same length, > 2 labels), the tails `co.uk` match, so unrelated sites are treated as the same domain and the full path is shown. The comment and the PR title say only 'same domain', but the behaviour is broader than intended.

title: Missing tests for sibling-subdomain branch, blank website and anonymous TL0
body: The tests cover only three of the branches. The `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` branch is untested. So are a website with no path, an invalid or blank website, and a restricted TL0 user (where `website_name` should not be exposed). The TL0 spec's untrusted attribute list does not include `website_name`, which would have exposed the `include_website_name` bug.

title: String `<<` mutates discourse_host, corrupting the hostname
body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` is wrong for two reasons. First, `"." << website_host` builds a string that is then used only for the check, so it works, but if the frozen-string literal magic comment is ever enabled it will raise. Second, the logic is fragile: the check relies on the string-building side effect rather than an explicit `".#{website_host}"`. Rewrite it with interpolation so the intent is clear and the code is safe under frozen string literals.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so it is never called
body: ActiveModel::Serializers only honors `include_<attr>?` methods. `include_website_name` without the question mark is dead code. As a result `website_name` is always serialized, including when the website is blank or when `untrusted_attributes` hides `website` for TL0 users viewed by anonymous. That leaks the website host for TL0 users and emits `website_name: nil` when there is no website. Rename it to `include_website_name?`, and also add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`.

title: URI parsing is repeated and the path may be empty or have no scheme
body: `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed up to three times per call. Websites saved without a scheme, e.g. `example.com/user`, have a nil host. That makes `website_name` nil, and since the old client-side `split("/")[2]` also returned nothing for them, the behavior stays the same but is now untested. Also, appending the full path for same-domain sites will include trailing slashes (`example.com/`) and long paths. Parse once into a local variable and handle the empty-path case.

title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic is incorrect
body: The branch compares the label count and everything after the first label. This makes `www.example.com` match `forum.example.com`, but it also matches unrelated multi-part TLDs such as `a.co.uk` and `b.co.uk`, which have the same label count and the same suffix `co.uk`. It also fails when the website host and the instance host have different depths. The branch comment says "www.example.com == forum.example.com", but the spec has no test for it. Add tests and use a more robust domain comparison.

title: Missing tests for sibling-subdomain, blank-website and anonymous TL0 cases
body: The specs cover three branches, but not the sibling-subdomain branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com), not an unparseable or blank website, and not that `website_name` is hidden for the anonymous TL0 user (the untrusted attributes list in the spec does not include it).

title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?`, so it is never called
body: ActiveModel::Serializers only consults `include_<attr>?` methods. `include_website_name` without `?` is dead code, so `website_name` is always serialized. Because `website_name` is not in `untrusted_attributes`, it is also exposed to anonymous viewers of TL0 users, even though `website` itself is hidden for them. This leaks the host of the website and defeats the restriction. The method should be `include_website_name?`, and it should also honour `scope.restrict_user_fields?`.

title: Malformed URL handling and website without scheme
body: `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` swallows all errors. For website values without a scheme, such as `example.com/foo`, `host` is nil, so website_name is nil. The old client-side `split('/')[2]` also returned nothing there, but the template now hides the website entirely because `model.website_name` is empty. `URI(...)` is also parsed three times. Parse once into a local variable. `path` may also be empty or contain a trailing slash, for example `http://example.com/` renders as `example.com/` when the hosts match.

title: Sibling-subdomain comparison treats unrelated domains as the same
body: The branch comparing `website_host.split('.')[1..-1]` to `discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1]` only requires equal label counts and more than 2 labels. For multi-part TLDs, such as `a.co.uk` against `b.co.uk`, it compares `co.uk` with `co.uk` and wrongly shows the full path for an unrelated site. The branch is also only reachable when hosts have equal depth, so cases such as `www.example.com` against `a.b.example.com` are not handled consistently.

title: Client-side website_name is not refreshed after saving preferences
body: The template now reads `model.website_name`, which comes from the server. After the user edits `website` in preferences and saves, `website_name` on the model is not updated, since `save` only sends `website` and updates `bio_excerpt`. The profile therefore shows a stale or missing name until reload. The old computed property updated automatically.

title: Missing test coverage for edge cases
body: The new tests cover only three happy paths. Nothing covers an invalid or schemeless website, an empty website, the sibling-subdomain branch, or the TL0 anonymous case. The anonymous case would have exposed that `website_name` leaks for TL0 users, because `untrusted_attributes` in the spec does not include it.

title: Light-theme value changed from 30% to 70% (typo in dark-light-choose)
body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new light-theme branch is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, paired with `$secondary 30%`. This silently makes `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` much lighter on light themes, a visual regression in an otherwise dark-mode-only change. The light value should remain 30% and the dark value should be 70%, i.e. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: `.group-member-info .name` light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. It was replaced with the 50%/50% pair, which changes the light-theme color and makes the name as dim as the title. The matching pair for 30% should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The same regression is repeated in mobile/user.scss.

title: `.group-member-info .name` light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses 50%/50%, so the light-theme appearance changes unintentionally and the name loses its emphasis over the title. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: `.topic-map h3` light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new value is the 50%/50% pair, which unintentionally lightens the topic-map heading on light themes and weakens the hierarchy against `h4`, which is also 50%. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`, matching the desktop version.

title: `.custom-message-length` light-theme lightness changed from 70% to 30%
body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new light branch is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with the dark branch at `$secondary 70%`, so the pairs are swapped. On light themes the text becomes much darker than before, and on dark themes the lightness is inconsistent with the desktop equivalent, which uses 70%/30%. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

title: `#file-uploading` still uses `$secondary` lightness, unhandled for light themes
body: `#file-uploading` colors the text with `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)` and is not wrapped in `dark-light-choose`. The text is mid-grey derived from `$secondary` and is likely hard to read on dark themes, the very problem this PR targets, and is inconsistent with the rest of the changes. The change is incomplete there.

title: Light-theme color changed from 30% to 70% for embedded-post author links
body: The original value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new light branch is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which is lighter and lower contrast. The dark branch is `$secondary` at 30%, which matches the 70% value instead. The PR is only meant to add a dark-theme variant, so light themes should keep 30% (dark: `$secondary` 70%). As written, `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` regresses on every light theme.

title: group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50% in both branches
body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule uses 50%/50%, which looks copy-pasted from the `.title` rule below it. This changes the light-theme color and removes the intended visual distinction between the name (darker) and the title (lighter). It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: custom-message-length light-theme lightness changed from 70% to 30%
