There is no second check of `entryPointAssetsCache` under the write lock. At startup, or after a failed load, N concurrent requests do N redundant loads while the others block. In Dev mode every call takes the exclusive lock and does file I/O under it, which serializes all requests that need web assets. Add a double-checked `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil` after `Lock()`.

title: Cache overwritten with nil on error, and err may be masked
body: `entryPointAssetsCache = result` runs even when `err != nil`, so a transient read failure (or a Dev-mode reload failure) replaces a previously valid cache with nil. Callers then get `(nil, err)`. This is existing behavior, but the lock now makes it a deliberate write path. Only assign the cache on success. Also, if the `cdn` branch fails, `err` is set and `result` is nil, and the file fallback then reassigns `err`, which is fine. A partial result is never cached, though, so the guard should be explicit.

title: No concurrency test for the race fix
body: The PR fixes a data race but adds no test, for example a `-race` test calling `GetWebAssets` from several goroutines. Nothing guards against a regression. Returning the shared `*dtos.EntryPointAssets` pointer is also still mutable by callers, and the code does not make it immutable.

title: No re-check of cache after acquiring write lock (thundering herd on cold start)
body: After the RLock fast path misses, every concurrent caller takes the write Lock and independently re-reads the manifest from disk. In production mode (non-Dev) the cache only needs to be populated once, so callers that were queued behind the first writer should re-check `entryPointAssetsCache != nil` after `Lock()` and return it. As written, N concurrent requests at startup each redo the file read and JSON parse serially. In Dev mode every request serializes on the write lock, which is intended there, but in production this is redundant work.

title: Cache is overwritten with nil/partial result when loading fails
body: `entryPointAssetsCache = result` is assigned unconditionally, even when `err != nil` and `result` is nil. A transient failure (e.g. a Dev-mode reload hitting a half-written manifest) wipes a previously good cached value. The function also returns `(nil, err)`, so callers that ignore the error get a nil pointer. The cache should only be updated on success. This behavior existed before, but the new lock makes the write path explicit and it is worth fixing here.

title: Returned pointer is shared and mutated in Dev mode without synchronization
body: The lock only protects the pointer variable. The `*dtos.EntryPointAssets` it points to is handed out to many callers and is not guarded. In the non-Dev path the object is created and mutated (via `SetContentDeliveryURL`) before it is stored, so that is fine. However, the data race concern is only partially addressed: any caller that mutates the returned struct still races with other readers. No test (for example one run with `-race` and concurrent callers) was added to verify the fix.

title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false and has confusing, dead logic
body: The function computes `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns false when `enabled` is true, and returns false otherwise. Every path returns false, so the feature flag has no effect. This is probably the intent for a security stopgap, but the code is misleading: the inverted `enabled` variable and the redundant branch suggest the flag is honored when it is not. A future maintainer may 'fix' it and silently re-enable the vulnerable path. It should be a plain `return false` (or removed) with a comment explaining why SQL expressions are disabled.

title: Execute and the SQL command are still reachable via the legacy node-building path
body: The disable check lives only in `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery`. `UnmarshalSQLCommand` (used by the older rawNode path) still calls `NewSQLCommand`, which calls `sql.TablesList`; that now fails with 'not implemented' and surfaces as the generic 'error reading SQL command'. This does not cause a vulnerability, but the two paths return different, misleading errors for the same disabled feature. A user hitting the legacy path is told their SQL is invalid rather than that SQL expressions are disabled. The disable check should be applied at one common place.

title: No tests added for the disabled SQL expression behavior
body: The PR changes SQL expression behavior (always rejected in the reader, stub DB returns 'not implemented'), but adds or updates no tests. Existing tests that rely on SQL expressions working, such as sql_command_test or parser tests that call `TablesList`, will now fail or need updating. Nothing asserts the new error from `ReadQuery` for `QueryTypeSQL`, so a regression that re-enables the path would go unnoticed.

title: Stale DuckDB naming and misleading error text
body: `TablesList` still uses a variable named `duckDB`, builds a DuckDB-specific `json_serialize_sql` command, and logs the raw SQL on error, even though the DuckDB dependency is gone. The stub's `RunCommands` always returns 'not implemented', so every call fails with 'error serializing sql: not implemented'. That message is confusing for operators. The leftover code is dead and misleading and should be removed or the function should return a clear 'SQL expressions are disabled' error.

title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false and its logic is convoluted
body: The helper computes `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false whether `enabled` is true or false. Both branches return false, so the function is a hard-coded kill switch that only looks like a feature-flag check. The dead logic is misleading, and a later change that 'fixes' it could silently re-enable the vulnerable path. It should be a plain `return false`, or the SQL case should return an error directly, with a comment explaining that this is a security disable.

title: Disable guard exists only in the new-style reader; the legacy path is unguarded
body: SQL expressions are blocked only in `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery`. The legacy parse path, `UnmarshalSQLCommand` called from the graph node builder, is not gated. It calls `NewSQLCommand`, which calls `sql.TablesList`, which now hits the stub DB. That path therefore fails with a generic 'error reading SQL command' rather than the explicit 'not implemented' message, and it still depends on the stub being in place. The block should be enforced once, centrally, so that every entry point is covered.

title: No tests cover the disabled behavior
body: The PR changes security-critical behavior: SQL expressions are now rejected, and the stub DB returns 'not implemented'. It adds no test asserting that a QueryTypeSQL query is rejected by the reader, or that the node-building path fails. Existing SQL tests that relied on DuckDB, such as parser and sql_command tests, may now fail or need updating, and none were touched. A regression test is needed so the kill switch can't be accidentally re-enabled.

title: Dead parsing code retained, and TablesList error is logged with the raw SQL
body: `TablesList` now always errors via the stub, so the JSON/AST parsing code and the `flatten` dependency are unreachable. The failure is also logged at Error level with the full user SQL on every attempt, which is noisy. The `jeremywohl/flatten` import is kept, which is fine, but the dead code should be removed or noted.

title: go.work.sum churn unrelated to this change
body: Besides moving lines for the removed dependencies, the diff drops azblob v1.3.2 and go-replayers/grpcreplay and httpreplay entries from go.work.sum. These entries are unrelated to the go-duck removal. The removal could break workspace builds for modules that still need those checksums, and it suggests a `go work sync` or tidy was run with side effects that were not intended.

title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false and has confusing, dead logic
body: The function computes `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)`. It then returns false whether `enabled` is true or false, so the feature flag is never consulted for the result. The name suggests flag-based behavior, but the function is a hard-coded disable. The inverted `enabled` variable and the identical return branches look like a bug and will confuse maintainers. A plain `return false`, or removing the function and returning the error directly, would be clearer. The `h` parameter is also unused in effect.

title: Misleading error message for a deliberately disabled feature
body: A user who has enabled the `sqlExpressions` feature flag gets `sqlExpressions is not implemented`. That wrongly suggests the feature is unfinished rather than disabled for security reasons. The message should say the feature is disabled. The flag is also still documented, so users will be confused.

title: Other entry points to SQL commands are not blocked, only the reader
body: The disable check is added only in `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery`. `UnmarshalSQLCommand` (called from the legacy node-building path) still calls `NewSQLCommand` without any gate. It fails only because the stub `TablesList` errors with 'not implemented', and that error is surfaced as a misleading 'error reading SQL command'. Security therefore depends on a stub rather than an explicit check at the command level. The disabled path also returns a generic invalid-SQL error instead of a clear message.

title: Dead code and no tests for the disabled behavior
body: `TablesList` always fails now because the stubbed DB's `RunCommands` returns 'not implemented'. The JSON AST parsing, `tablesFromAST` and the `jeremywohl/flatten` dependency are unreachable except through existing tests. No test was added to verify that the SQL query type is rejected, so a future regression that re-enables execution would go unnoticed. Existing parser and SQL command tests that depended on DuckDB may now fail or need updating.

title: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without a lock while BuildIndex now writes to it concurrently
body: `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu`. `searchSupport.init` now calls it in the new "search index initialized" log line, right after it starts the watch goroutine. That goroutine's `handleEvent` calls `getOrCreateIndex`, which can call `BuildIndex` and write `b.cache[key] = idx` under the lock. The PR also narrows the lock to cover only that write, so builds from many goroutines now hit the map at the same time. Iterating a Go map while another goroutine writes it can cause a fatal 'concurrent map iteration and map write' crash. `TotalDocs` should take `cacheMu.RLock()`.

title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same index
body: `BuildIndex` no longer holds `cacheMu` while building, and it never checks the cache for an existing entry before creating the index. `getOrCreateIndex` is a check-then-build with no per-key guard, so two callers can both see a miss for the same key. Examples are startup `init` racing with a Search request, or a watch event arriving during startup. Both then run `BuildIndex`. For file-backed indexes the second `bleve.New(dir, ...)` fails because the directory already exists, or both write the same directory. For memory indexes the second build overwrites the cache entry and leaks the first index, and the `IndexTenants` and `IndexedKinds` metrics are double counted. The coarse lock hid the concurrency but did not remove this problem. A per-key single-flight or an existence check under the lock is needed.

title: Failed eager Init leaks the server's context and goroutines
body: `NewResourceServer` now runs `s.Init(ctx)` synchronously, including the full index build. On failure it returns `nil, err` without calling `s.cancel()` or `lifecycle.Stop`. If `search.init` or `initWatcher` already started pollers or goroutines from `WatchWriteEvents` before failing, they keep running. The backend lifecycle is also never stopped. The cancelable context created just above is leaked. Cancel the context and stop the lifecycle on the error path.

title: Eager Init makes construction block for the whole index build and fail hard
body: Index building previously happened lazily on the first gRPC call. It now blocks `NewResourceServer`, so the process cannot serve health checks or `/metrics` until every index is built. Any build error also makes server construction fail rather than surfacing as a per-request error. The PR description itself asks what depends on lazy init, but nothing in the PR shows that this was examined. Callers such as the module server and tests that build the resource server during wire-up are affected, and the Postgres test had to be skipped in the same PR.

title: Test skipped for postgres rather than fixed
body: The test is skipped on Postgres with a TODO because it does not work in Drone. This is the same PR that moves initialization to server construction, so the failure may be caused by the change, for example init failing or taking too long at startup. Skipping removes the only coverage for the storage-server module target on that database and hides any regression.

title: Trace context fix is incomplete; other backend spans still discard ctx
body: The PR is meant to fix trace propagation, but only `GetResourceStats` was changed to `ctx, span :=`. `WriteEvent`, `ReadResource` and `ListIterator` in this file still use `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)`. `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` has the same pattern. Their child spans (create, update, delete and the DB calls) therefore are not nested under these spans and stay detached from the parent trace.

title: Removing per-request Init checks drops the stopped/failed-init guard
body: Every RPC used to call `s.Init(ctx)` and return `s.initErr`. `Stop()` sets `initErr` to "service is stopping" or "service is stopped", so requests arriving after shutdown began were rejected. With the checks gone, nothing reads `initErr` after construction. Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch and Search now run against a stopped server: the lifecycle hooks have stopped, the DB may be closing and the context is cancelled. Callers get arbitrary backend errors or hangs instead of a clear error. The reviewer's question about lazy init is partly answered here: the only post-start use of that state is lost. Keep a cheap state check (for example an atomic stopped flag) in the request paths.

title: Server construction now blocks on a full index build and fails hard on any error
body: `NewResourceServer` now runs `s.Init(ctx)` synchronously. That runs the lifecycle hooks, builds the search index for every namespace and resource above the size threshold, and starts the watcher. Constructing the server, and therefore module startup and wire/DI, blocks for the entire index build. Any error, such as one namespace failing to index or a transient DB failure, makes construction return an error. Before, such an error was cached and returned per request. For large installs, startup latency and liveness probes need consideration, and a single bad index should probably not take the whole server down.

title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding cacheMu
body: `BuildIndex` now takes `cacheMu` only around the map write, and `TotalDocs` reads `b.cache` with no lock. The PR adds a call to `s.search.TotalDocs()` in `searchSupport.init`, right after the goroutine that handles watch events has been started. That goroutine can call `getOrCreateIndex` and then `BuildIndex`, which writes the map concurrently with the read. This is a concurrent map read/write, which Go can turn into a fatal panic. `TotalDocs` should take `cacheMu.RLock()`.

title: Trace context is still dropped in BuildIndex and several SQL backend methods
body: The PR claims to fix trace propagation, but `BuildIndex` still does `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)` and discards the derived context. In `sql/backend.go`, `WriteEvent`, `ReadResource` and `ListIterator` have the same problem. Spans created below these functions therefore do not become children of the span started here. The fix was applied to `GetResourceStats`, `init` and `build`, but not to these.

title: Concurrent BuildIndex for the same key is no longer serialized
body: The whole-function lock is removed, but nothing replaces it as per-key protection. `getOrCreateIndex` does an unlocked get-then-build, so two concurrent callers for the same key (for example a search request and a watch event) can both build. For file-backed indexes, `bleve.New(dir)` then fails because the path already exists. For memory indexes, one index silently overwrites the other in the cache, leaving the first as a leaked orphan whose metrics were already incremented. Finer-grained locking should be per key (singleflight or a per-key mutex), not only around the map write.

title: Data races in the init worker goroutines
body: Inside the errgroup closure, `totalBatchesIndexed++` and the assignment `_, _, err = s.build(...)` write shared variables from several goroutines without synchronization. `err` is the outer variable declared by `GetResourceStats`. This was already racy, but init now always runs at startup with `initWorkers` goroutines. The race can corrupt the counter and also lose or mix errors. Use an atomic counter and a local `err` inside the closure.

title: Postgres integration test skipped, possibly masking a regression from eager init
body: The test is skipped for postgres with a note that it works locally but not in Drone. This PR changes startup so the resource server initializes eagerly, and the test is exactly the one that starts the storage-server target, which is the path affected. Disabling it removes the only coverage for that path on postgres, and the cause is not investigated. Linking a tracking issue, or confirming the failure is unrelated to this change, would make the skip safer.

title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding cacheMu
body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache with no lock. BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu for its whole duration, and writes to the map happen concurrently from watch events and from Search via getOrCreateIndex. The PR also adds a TotalDocs call to the init log line, which runs after the watch goroutine has started. Concurrent map iteration and map write is a fatal runtime error in Go. TotalDocs should take cacheMu.RLock.

title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same key
body: The whole-function lock is gone, and getOrCreateIndex has no per-key guard. Two callers that both miss the cache for the same NamespacedResource (for example a search request and a watch event, or two parallel searches) will now both build the index. For file-backed indexes the second bleve.New on the same directory fails or conflicts. For memory indexes the last writer silently replaces the cached index, and the replaced one is leaked, never closed. The finer-grained locking should also check the cache again under the lock, or use a per-key singleflight, rather than only locking around the map write.

title: Heavy, blocking init in the constructor makes startup fail or hang
body: NewResourceServer now runs lifecycle Init, the full search index build for every namespace, and the watcher synchronously. Any failure, such as a transient DB error while building one index, now makes the constructor return an error and aborts server creation. Previously this failed only the first request. Construction time grows with data size, which can stall Grafana startup, and a wire-injected dependency now does I/O at construction. The PR itself asks whether anything depends on lazy init, and the postgres test being skipped suggests something does. Also, Init is now never re-invoked, so calls after a failed Stop no longer return the initErr and instead proceed against a stopped server.

title: Test skipped for postgres to hide a failure caused by this change
body: The test is skipped for postgres in Drone with only a TODO, apparently because eager initialization breaks it there. This removes coverage for the new startup path and masks a likely real regression instead of fixing it. At minimum it needs a tracking issue.

title: Trace context still discarded in several places despite the PR claiming a fix
body: bleveBackend.BuildIndex still does `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)`, so the span context is not propagated. The same is true in sql/backend.go for WriteEvent, ReadResource and ListIterator, which also discard the returned ctx. Only GetResourceStats was fixed, so the traces stay fragmented.

title: Data race on shared err and counter in init workers
body: The errgroup goroutines all assign to the outer `err` variable (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and increment `totalBatchesIndexed++` without synchronization. Init now runs eagerly with many workers over many namespaces, so the race is exercised at startup. The reported count and returned error can be wrong, and the race detector will flag it. Use a local err and an atomic counter.

title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition, added in `UsernamePasswordForm`, is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. There is no no-arg overload, so the `services` module will not compile. The call should pass `context.getUser()`.

title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, which disables passkeys on the initial login page
body: The helper returns true only when `user != null`. `authenticate()` and `challenge(context, error, field)` use it to decide whether to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm`. On a normal first login the user is null, so the conditional-UI/passkey attributes are no longer set. The old code did the opposite and set them when `context.getUser() == null`. This breaks passkey login for fresh logins, including the discoverable-key and external-key paths that the existing tests cover. Failed-login re-renders also lose the passkey data, because the user is usually cleared after a bad password. The intent is presumably to enable passkeys both for unidentified users and for re-authentication, so the `user != null` condition looks inverted or incomplete.

title: Overriding method lacks @Override
body: `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` overrides `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` but has no `@Override` annotation. A future signature change in the parent would silently turn it into a non-override, and re-authentication would start showing the allowed-authenticator list again.

title: Fragile try/catch(Exception) pattern for asserting element absence
body: The test calls `findElement(...)` inside `try`, asserts `nullValue()`, then `fail(...)`, and catches `Exception`. The expected `NoSuchElementException` is swallowed. A `WebDriverException` from some other cause would also be swallowed, so the test can pass for the wrong reason. `fail` throws `AssertionError`, which is not an `Exception`, so it does propagate, but the check is still imprecise. Use `driver.findElements(...).isEmpty()` or `assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)`.

title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition in `UsernamePasswordForm` is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. The `services` module will not compile, so the PR cannot be built or tested. The call needs `context.getUser()` as its argument, and the intended semantics should be rechecked.

title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, which disables passkeys on the initial login
body: The helper returns true only when `user != null`. Before this change, passkeys were set up when the user was NOT yet identified (`context.getUser() == null`). Now `authenticate()` and `challenge(...)` call `fillContextForm` only if a user is already set, i.e. only during re-authentication. On a fresh login the user is null, so no WebAuthn challenge, RP id or conditional-UI attribute is rendered. Discoverable-key autologin and the external-key link then stop working. The existing tests `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` and `passwordLoginWithExternalKey` would fail. The condition should cover both the user-null case and the re-authentication case, not replace one with the other.

title: Re-authentication shows passkeys without checking that the user has a passkey
body: During re-authentication passkeys are enabled whenever the realm has passkeys on and a user is set. The code never checks whether that user actually has a passwordless credential. A user with no passkey is therefore offered a conditional-UI/WebAuthn form that cannot succeed. The test comment for `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` says passkeys should not be shown for such a user. The test only turns passkeys off for the whole realm, so it does not exercise this case.

title: shouldDisplayAuthenticators is inconsistent with the new shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators override
body: The conditional-UI authenticator now returns false from `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators`, so the allowed-authenticators bean is not set and IS_USER_IDENTIFIED is false. `shouldDisplayAuthenticators` still returns `context.getUser() != null`, so SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS is true during re-authentication. The template is told to display authenticators that were never provided, which may render an empty list or fail on the missing attribute. Override it consistently as well. The new override also lacks `@Override`.

title: Absence checks are written so they can never fail meaningfully
body: The check calls `findElement(...)` inside `assertThat(..., nullValue())` and then `fail(...)`, all in a `try` block with `catch (Exception)`. `findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException` when the element is missing, which is the only path that passes. If the element exists, `assertThat(..., nullValue())` throws an AssertionError instead. The `fail` call is dead code. The check works only by accident and is hard to read. Use `driver.findElements(...).isEmpty()` or `assertThrows`.

title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition, in `UsernamePasswordForm` (line 160), takes a `UserModel` parameter, so the `services` module will not compile. It should pass `context.getUser()`.

title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, so passkeys are lost on the normal login page
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. The old code filled the WebAuthn form data when the user was NOT yet identified (`context.getUser() == null`), and `authenticate()` and `challenge(...)` now rely on this helper instead. On a fresh login the user is null, so the conditional-UI data (challenge, rpId, `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI`) is no longer set. Passkey autofill and the passkey form disappear from the initial login page, and the existing tests `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey`, `passwordLoginWithExternalKey` and `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` would fail. Passkeys should be available both when the user is null and when re-authenticating, so the `user != null` condition is wrong (inverted or unnecessary).

title: Passkey form fill gated by the wrong condition in authenticate()
body: `authenticate()` now fills the passkey form only when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, which requires a non-null user. In the same method the branch for `context.getUser() == null` (loginHint / rememberMe) previously set up WebAuthn. That path no longer does, so anonymous login pages get no passkey support. The same helper has the same problem in `challenge(context, error, field)` at line 137, so passkey data is also not restored after a failed username or password on a fresh login.

title: Test comment does not match what the test configures
body: `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` says passkeys should not appear because 'this user does not have passkey'. The test actually disables passkeys at the realm level (`setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(FALSE)`), so it does not cover the case of a realm with passkeys enabled and a user with no passkey credential. The catch-all `catch (Exception)` around `fail(...)` is also fragile. The scenario in the comment is untested.

title: Cleanup registered for literal alias "alias", not the created IDPs
body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` targets an IDP literally named "alias", not the one just created (`idp-alias-N`). The same bug is on line 425, where `idp-alias-20` is created. None of the 21 IDPs created by `testCacheIDPForLogin` are removed after the test, and cleanup may also fail because "alias" does not exist. Leftover IDPs, including org-linked public ones, leak into later tests in the same realm. This can change login-IDP counts and make other tests order-dependent. The alias variable should be used instead.

title: Login-cache invalidation on update uses the org-aware wrapped model as the original
body: `update()` obtains the original via `getById()`, which returns the wrapper whose `isEnabled()` returns false when the linked organization is disabled. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` evaluates `getLoginPredicate()` on that wrapper. If the org is disabled, the original is treated as non-login. If the update also makes the IDP non-login (for example `hideOnLogin=true`), neither condition triggers and the login caches are not invalidated. The cached ID set still contains the IDP. When the org is re-enabled, the IDP appears on the login page even though it is hidden. The predicate should be evaluated on the raw stored model, not the org-aware wrapper.

title: getLoginPredicate semantics changed without updating the search options or docs
body: `getLoginPredicate()` now also requires that org-linked IDPs have BROKER_PUBLIC=true. `getLoginSearchOptions()` and the `LoginFilter` enum, which the Javadoc describes as the fields considered for login availability, do not reflect this. The REALM_ONLY and ORG_ONLY paths in `getForLogin` add BROKER_PUBLIC separately. The predicate and the search options are now two separately maintained definitions of "login IDP" that can drift apart. Any other caller of `getLoginPredicate()` silently gets stricter behaviour.

title: Update invalidation decision uses the org-aware wrapped model, which can skip a needed login-cache invalidation
body: `update()` takes the original IDP from `getById()`, which returns the org-aware wrapper. For an IDP linked to an org, the wrapper's `isEnabled()` also requires the org and the organization feature to be enabled. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` then calls `getLoginPredicate().test(original)`, so an enabled IDP in a disabled org looks 'not a login IDP'. The cached login lists are built from the stored attributes (JPA query on `enabled=true` etc.) and still contain that IDP. If the IDP is then updated so that the new state is also 'not login' (for example `hideOnLogin=true`), the early return skips invalidation. The stale entry stays in the cache, and when the org is re-enabled the IDP is wrongly shown on the login page. The comparison should use the unwrapped stored model, for example from `idpDelegate.getById`.

title: Cleanup registered with literal "alias" instead of the created alias, leaking IDPs
body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` targets an IDP literally named "alias", not the IDPs created in the loop (`idp-alias-N`). The same bug is at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`. None of the 21 IDPs created by `testCacheIDPForLogin` are cleaned up, and the cleanup itself may fail with 404. Leftover login IDPs can pollute other tests in the same realm, such as the exact counts asserted in this test or `OrganizationCacheTest` reruns. The cleanup should use the actual alias.

title: Cleanup registered for literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP alias
body: Inside the creation loop the cleanup is `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove`, which uses the string literal "alias" rather than the loop's `alias`. The cleanup therefore targets a nonexistent IDP and the 21 IDPs created by this test (`idp-alias-0` to `idp-alias-20`) are never removed. They can leak into other tests and change counts that depend on the realm's IDPs. The same defect appears at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`, and it was copied from the existing `testCacheIDPByOrg`. The cleanup should reference the actual alias.

title: Invalidation on create/remove of a login-eligible IDP is not tested
body: The test only checks that adding or removing an IDP that is NOT available for login leaves the login caches intact. No scenario creates or removes an IDP that IS login-eligible and asserts that the caches are invalidated. That is the main path covered by the new `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` calls in `create()` and `remove()`. A regression there, such as a wrong `null` or predicate handling in `remove`, would go undetected. The test also never exercises a disabled organization with a cached IDP, nor the wrapped `isEnabled` re-check in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`.

title: remove() now always hits the database for the IDP before removal
body: `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is now called unconditionally, whereas it was previously only called when the alias key was already invalidated. When the IDP is cached, a database lookup is added to every remove just to evaluate the login predicate. Using the cached model, or loading it via `getByAlias` through the cache, would avoid the extra query. In addition, a null result is only handled for the new login invalidation; the `isInvalid` branch still passes a possibly null `storedIdp` into `registerIDPInvalidation`.

title: Misconfigured classpaths are no longer detected; same-order providers are picked arbitrarily
body: The old check that threw when several CryptoProviders were present is gone. Default, Elytron and FIPS1402 providers all return order() == 200. If two of them end up on the classpath (for example default and FIPS), the sort leaves them tied and the winner depends on ServiceLoader discovery order, which depends on classpath order. Keycloak could then silently run non-FIPS crypto where FIPS was intended, and the only trace is a debug log line. Either keep failing when the top-ordered providers tie, or give each provider a distinct order.

title: Conflicting crypto providers are now silently picked instead of failing
body: The old check threw "Multiple crypto providers loaded" when more than one provider was on the classpath. It is removed and replaced by sorting on `order()`. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200. A misconfigured classpath, such as default plus FIPS or default plus Elytron, now picks one by `ServiceLoader` order, which depends on classpath order. The rest are only mentioned at debug level. Before, this was a hard failure; now a FIPS deployment could silently run on the non-FIPS provider. Equal-order conflicts should still throw, or at least be logged at warn. Only the authz-client fallback (order 100) should be allowed to lose to another provider.

title: New abstract `order()` method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: `order()` is added as an abstract interface method. Any external or custom `CryptoProvider` implementation, such as third-party or testsuite providers, will no longer compile. Already-compiled ones will fail with `AbstractMethodError` inside the `sorted(Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order))` call in `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider`. A `default int order() { return 0; }` would keep source and binary compatibility.

title: Dead duplicate encoder calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and the same for `sBigInteger` encode the values and discard the result. They have no effect, and the values are encoded again in the `writeDerSeq` call below. Remove them. The method also does not validate that `signature` has at least `signLength` bytes. A short, attacker-supplied JWS signature produces an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of an `IOException`.

title: Indefinite or oversized length leads to unchecked exceptions or unbounded allocation
body: `readLength()` returns -1 for the indefinite-length form (0x80). `readInteger()` then calls `read(length)` with -1, which throws `NegativeArraySizeException` instead of `IOException`. The `length >= limit` bounds check applies only to the long form. Short-form lengths are bounded by 127, but `read(int)` does not otherwise validate against the remaining input. Malformed DER input should be rejected with `IOException`. Reject negative lengths in `readInteger`/`readNext` and check the length against `is.available()`.

title: Round-trip test never validates the DER encoder independently
body: The test only checks that decode(encode(decode(x))) equals decode(x). It never verifies that the DER produced by `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` is accepted by a real JDK `Signature.verify`, and it never covers edge cases. Those edge cases include r/s with the high bit set, r/s shorter than the curve length (leading zeros), and malformed or indefinite-length input. A round trip with a symmetric bug would still pass. Compare the encoder output against the original JDK-produced DER and verify the signature with it.

title: New abstract order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: `int order();` is added as an abstract method on a public SPI interface. Any third-party or custom CryptoProvider compiled against the old interface will fail to compile, and will throw AbstractMethodError at runtime when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` calls `CryptoProvider::order` while sorting. A `default int order() { return 0; }` would keep compatibility. The in-tree providers would then only need to override it with their own values.

title: Providers with equal order are chosen silently, replacing the previous fail-fast error
body: The old 'Multiple crypto providers' IllegalStateException is removed. Providers are now sorted by order() and the first is taken. The in-tree providers (Default, Elytron, FIPS1402) all return 200. If two of them end up on the classpath, for example FIPS and default, the pick depends on ServiceLoader discovery order, because the sort is stable and the order values tie. A misconfigured deployment that used to fail fast now silently runs with the wrong crypto provider, which is a risk in FIPS setups. The 'Ignored crypto providers' message is logged only at debug level. Ties should be detected and rejected or warned about, or the ignored providers should be logged at warn.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK default KeyStore provider, not BouncyCastle
body: The method returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is the JDK's SUN provider and not a BouncyCastle provider. Code that uses `BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` or the provider's name, for example the `Signature.getInstance(..., BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER)` pattern, will resolve to SUN. The javadoc contract says BouncyCastle, so the behaviour is misleading and undocumented. Other methods throw UnsupportedOperationException, so any call path that reaches them fails at runtime.

title: Dead code: result of ASN1Encoder write calls discarded
body: Lines 114-115 create encoders, write r and s, and discard the results. The same encoding is repeated in the return statement. These are leftover no-op lines and should be removed.

title: Test uses one default-size EC key for all algorithms and only checks a self round-trip
body: A single key from `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")` is used for ES256, ES384 and ES512 (a P-256 key in practice). The ES384 and ES512 cases therefore sign with a 256-bit curve, which produces 32-byte r and s. These are then padded to 48 or 66 bytes, so the truncation and padding paths for real P-384 and P-521 signatures are not exercised. The test also only compares round-trip equality of this provider's own encode and decode. It never checks against the JDK-produced DER or verifies the converted signature, and it has no negative cases such as malformed DER. Bugs in the ASN1Decoder, for example a zero-length INTEGER throwing a runtime NumberFormatException instead of IOException, would go undetected.

title: getClientsWithPermission likely returns the type name instead of client IDs
body: `resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` matches resources whose `type` is "Clients". Per-client resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` through `resourceStore.create(server, name, owner)`, and no type is set on them. So the search probably returns only the "all clients" resource, and the code adds `resource.getName()` ("Clients"). The method therefore returns "Clients" instead of client IDs. That makes it useless for filtering clients by granted scope and gives wrong results to any caller. It also has no test coverage.

title: Possible NPE when the Clients type resource is not found
body: `getResourceTypeResource` returns null if the schema isn't supported for the server, or if no "Clients" resource exists. For example, the "all-clients" resource can be missing in a realm whose admin-permissions client was initialised before CLIENTS was added to the schema. The result is passed straight to `findByResource(server, resource)` and then to `resource.getScopes()`. A null result throws a NullPointerException (an HTTP 500) instead of returning false (deny). There is no null check.

title: getResourceName not extended for the Clients resource type
body: `getResourceName` handles only `USERS` and resolves the user's username. For permissions of type `Clients` it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Per-client resources are named by client UUID and have no display name, so the name is null or the raw ID. "All clients" is not mapped to a friendly name either. Resource names shown for client permissions are therefore wrong, and the Clients type is only half-integrated in the schema.

title: ClientRemovedEvent still calls V1-only setPermissionsEnabled, which throws in V2
body: The listener now runs only when V1 `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled. `management()` still returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever V2 is enabled, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. If both features are enabled, deleting a client throws from the removal event listener. The gate hides the problem only when V1 is disabled. The listener should skip V2 explicitly or tolerate the unsupported call. Gating on V1 also silently changes the cleanup behavior of existing listeners.

title: Tests mutate the admin client's own secret and shared client state without cleanup
body: `testConfigureOnlyOneClient` calls `generateNewSecret()` on `myclient`, which is the client `realmAdminClient` authenticates with (the secret is "mysecret"). Token re-acquisition for later calls, or in later tests that share the realm, can then fail with 401. `testManageOnlyOneClient` renames `myclient` and removes a default client scope. `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` creates client roles and composites. `onAfter` removes only permissions, so this state leaks into other tests and can make them order-dependent or flaky.

title: JUnit 4 Assert.fail used in a JUnit 5 test
body: The test imports `org.junit.Assert.fail` (JUnit 4) while the rest of the class and the sibling tests use `org.junit.jupiter.api`. This relies on a transitive JUnit 4 dependency and is inconsistent with the other tests, which use `org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.fail`.

title: Javadoc on void require* methods says 'Returns'
body: `requireView()` and `requireViewClientScopes()` are void methods that throw ForbiddenException. Their new Javadoc says "Returns {@code true} if ...". The wording is wrong and contradicts the other `require*` docs, which say "Throws ForbiddenException".

title: Dead code and unused imports
body: The private `getEvaluationContext` method is never used. The `logger` field is also unused, as are the imports `Scope`, `TOKEN_EXCHANGE`, `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext` and `EvaluationContext`. This looks copy-pasted from V1 and should be removed.

title: Possible NPE when the all-clients resource cannot be resolved
body: When no per-client resource exists, `getResourceTypeResource(...)` is used as the fallback and passed straight to `findByResource(server, resource)`. That method returns null if the schema is not supported for the server, if admin permissions are disabled for the realm, or if the 'Clients' resource is missing. The result is a NullPointerException, which surfaces as a 500 instead of a plain 'no permission' false. A null check should return false.

title: getClientsWithPermission may return the type resource name and evaluates every resource
body: `findByType(server, "Clients", ...)` also matches the all-clients type resource, whose name is the literal "Clients" and not a client id. That string can end up in the returned set of client ids. Each resource is also evaluated separately through `root.evaluatePermission`, so the cost grows with the number of clients that have per-client resources. The type resource should be skipped, and the evaluation cost noted or reduced.

title: Dead code and unused imports
body: `getEvaluationContext` is never called, so `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `EvaluationContext`, `AccessToken` and the helper itself are dead. `logger`, the static import `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` and the `Scope` import are also unused. This is copy-paste residue and should be removed.

title: No cleanup of Clients-type resources when a client is deleted under V2
body: The listener is now gated on `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ`, so under V2 `ClientRemovedEvent` does nothing. A client's per-client resource and any permissions referencing it remain in the admin-permissions resource server after the client is deleted. The orphaned resource is named by the old client id. There is no V2 cleanup path. Also, the gate changes existing V1 behaviour, because the listener previously ran whenever the V1 listener was registered, regardless of the feature flag.

title: Tests mutate shared client state without restoring it
body: `testManageOnlyOneClient` renames `myclient` and removes a default client scope, then re-adds it only as an optional scope. `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` creates client roles. `onAfter` removes only permissions, so this state leaks into other tests on the same realm. `testConfigureOnlyOneClient` indexes `getDefaultClientScopes().get(0)`, so results can depend on test order.

title: JUnit 4 fail() used in a JUnit 5 test
body: `org.junit.Assert.fail` is imported while the rest of the class and sibling tests use `org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions`. Mixing in the JUnit 4 API depends on a transitive dependency and is inconsistent.

title: Possible NPE when falling back to the all-clients resource
body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, if no client-specific resource exists, `getResourceTypeResource(...)` is called. It returns null when the schema is unsupported (admin permissions disabled, or the server is not the admin-permissions client) or when the 'Clients' resource is missing. The result is passed straight into `getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)` and then `resource.getScopes()` with no null check. That produces an NPE, which surfaces as a 500 instead of a plain 'no permission' (false). Add a null check on `resource` before using it.

title: Fallback to all-clients permission happens only when no client-specific resource exists
body: The all-clients ('Clients' type) resource is consulted only when no resource exists for the individual client. Once any permission references that client, a resource is created for it and evaluation runs only against that resource. A broad grant on all clients (for example MANAGE or VIEW) is then ignored for that client unless the per-client evaluation happens to merge it in. The tests only cover per-client and all-clients cases separately, so this mixed scenario is untested. It also differs from how the Users tests expect fallback to 'all-users' to work.

title: Listener now gated on V1 feature flag; behavior change and V2 still throws
body: The cleanup listener is now wrapped in `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`. Previously it ran unconditionally. Role, client and group removal no longer disable and clean up permissions when only V1 is off. If both V1 and V2 features are on, `management(...)` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` and `clients().setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, so deleting a client fails. Selecting the behavior by feature flag this way is fragile. The V2 variant should be a no-op, or the check should be on the evaluator type rather than the flag.

title: Several ClientPermissionEvaluator methods throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2
body: `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions`, `resource`, `canExchangeTo` and others throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. Existing callers, such as the client 'management/permissions' endpoint and token-exchange checks, call these unconditionally. With V2 enabled they will return 500s instead of a clean 'not supported' 4xx or a false result. Callers should be guarded, or these methods should return safe defaults such as `false` or an empty map.

title: Dead code and unused imports
body: `getEvaluationContext(...)` is never used. The `logger` field and the imports `TOKEN_EXCHANGE`, `Scope`, `EvaluationContext`, `ClientModelIdentity` and `DefaultEvaluationContext` exist only for that dead code or are unused. Remove them.

title: Javadoc on require* methods says 'Returns true'
body: `requireView()` and `requireViewClientScopes()` are `void` methods that throw ForbiddenException. Their Javadoc says 'Returns `true` if ...'. It should say they throw ForbiddenException when the corresponding `can*` method returns false.

title: getResourceName does not handle the Clients resource type
body: `getResourceName` special-cases only the Users type (translating ids to usernames and 'All users'). For Clients permissions it falls back to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Client resources are named by internal id, so this likely returns null or an opaque id when permissions are listed. The 'Clients' all-resource has no friendly label either, so Clients permissions will show up inconsistently with Users ones.

title: Mixes JUnit4 fail with JUnit5 tests
body: The test imports `org.junit.Assert.fail` (JUnit 4) in a JUnit 5 class, while the rest of the suite uses `org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.fail`. Tests also do not cover deny scenarios for CONFIGURE/MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, the all-clients plus single-client mix, or the VIEW-all-clients fallback for individual client permissions.

title: Recreate-upgrade exit code changed from 4 to 3 without checking consumers
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3, and the new value 4 is reused for FEATURE_DISABLED. Any script, CI pipeline or operator code that treated exit code 4 as 'recreate required' will now read 4 as 'feature disabled'. Callers that already handle 3 will now take the recreate branch. The operator's handling of these exit codes is not part of this diff, so it is unclear whether it was updated. The docs table already listed 3 as the recreate code, which suggests it was out of sync, but this still silently changes a contract that scripts may rely on.

title: Custom image now always bakes in the preview feature rolling-updates
body: `--features=rolling-updates` is added unconditionally to the custom image build. Every test that uses this image, including those that do not use rolling updates, now runs with a build-time preview feature enabled. This hides cases where the feature is off. If the feature is later renamed or removed, `kc.sh build` fails for all of these tests. A build-time feature also makes the operator CR's `features.enabled` list redundant or conflicting for this image.

title: Feature-disabled check runs before config validation and does not stop the command
body: `picocli.exit(...)` followed by `return` relies on exit() recording the code without terminating execution. The check is also placed before `validateConfig()`, so with the feature disabled, invalid arguments such as a missing `--file` on `check` return exit code 4 instead of the usage error 2. The same logic is duplicated in UpdateCompatibilityCheck. A shared guard in AbstractUpdatesCommand would be safer. The test only asserts the error text for the disabled case, not the exit code 4.

title: Docs macro appends --features after parameters, making the example order inconsistent and hiding the requirement
body: The `updatecompatibility` macro now always appends `--features=rolling-updates` to every rendered example. Readers copy the flag without being told why. It is also not a build-time option, so the example mixes build and runtime semantics. The macro does not produce the same text as the CAUTION block describes, and `--features` is emitted after subcommand options, which is unusual. The guide should explain the flag explicitly.

title: Feature-disabled test does not verify exit code and only covers one subcommand
body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only launches `metadata` and checks the error message. It does not assert the new exit code 4. It does not cover the `check` subcommand, which has the same new guard. The documented contract (exit code 4) is therefore untested.

title: Existing recreate-upgrade exit code silently changed from 4 to 3
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3 and 4 is reused for FEATURE_DISABLED. Any script or pipeline that already treats exit code 4 as "recreate required" will now read 4 as "feature disabled" and 3 as recreate. The documented meaning of the codes changes in place. The guide also still describes this tool as an evolving preview, but anything that already consumed the old code is broken without notice. Consumers inside the repo, such as the Operator code that runs the check, must be audited and updated. This diff does not touch any.

title: Feature check runs before option/config validation and relies on early profile init
body: `Profile.isFeatureEnabled` is called first in run(). `Profile.getInstance()` may be null if the profile is not yet configured, which would throw an NPE. Also, `--features=rolling-updates` is a build-time option. When the server is run with `--optimized` (a mixin is present on these commands), a feature that was not enabled at build time is not picked up. The same applies to the identical check in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata. The only behaviour tested is the non-optimized dist case.

title: Feature-disabled test does not check exit code and covers only the metadata command
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message for the `metadata` subcommand. It does not assert exit code 4, which is the new contract that scripts rely on and is documented. It also never exercises `check` with the feature disabled. A regression in the `check` path, or in the exit code, would go unnoticed.

title: Appended --features flag is placed after user parameters in every generated example
body: The macro appends `--features=rolling-updates` after `${parameters}` in all generated update-compatibility examples. The guide text then tells users to supply the same options as for `start`, but the example hides the fact that the feature is required. Only the CAUTION block mentions it. Users copying only the snippet get the flag, but anyone writing their own command lines or config files has to find the CAUTION block. The `--features` value also replaces rather than adds to the user's feature list when they already pass `--features`, and the docs do not warn about this.

title: Exit code for 'recreate upgrade' changed from 4 to 3 and 4 reused for a different meaning
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3, and 4 now means FEATURE_DISABLED. Any script or the Operator that already treats 4 as 'recreate required' will now read 'feature disabled' as a recreate. The Operator-side code that interprets these exit codes is not updated in this PR, so I cannot confirm it handles the new numbering. Existing docs and clients are affected even though the command is a preview.

title: Custom image always bakes in rolling-updates, also for tests using the default strategy
body: The build step now sets --features=rolling-updates for every use of the custom image. A build-time feature should match what the CR enables, and tests that use the default strategy with no features set may hit a mismatch. This can trigger a non-optimized start or a build-option mismatch with runtime features. The test `createInitialDeployment` sets the feature only when `updateStrategy != null`, and returns early with no feature otherwise. That means the `null` strategy case gets no feature in the CR, even though the Operator is documented to fail without the feature.

title: Feature enabling is skipped for the default (null) strategy case
body: For `updateStrategy == null` the method returns before enabling the `rolling-updates` feature. The docs say the feature must be enabled even for the default strategy (which mimics 26.1 behavior), and that the Operator fails otherwise. The `null` parameterized cases (testImageChange-null, testCacheMaxCount-null) therefore either run without the feature, contradicting the docs, or the Operator does not actually require it. Enable the feature before the early return so both cases are consistent.

title: Feature-disabled path: exit code not tested, and features check relies on runtime Profile
body: The new feature-disabled branch calls `picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED)` and returns. `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error text, and only for the `metadata` subcommand. It never checks exit code 4, and `check` has no such test. The documented exit code 4 is therefore unverified.

title: Doc macro appends --features after user parameters, inconsistent with prior ordering
body: The macro places `--features=rolling-updates` after `${parameters}` for every use. Users who copy it are told to enable the feature, but the generated command line gives no hint that this is a preview-only requirement. It is also appended to the sample output for `check`, which could confuse readers about whether the flag belongs in a real deployment (the build vs. runtime features must match).

title: canManage() grants global group management for VIEW-only permission
body: The no-arg `canManage()` calls `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so any admin with only the `view` scope on the all-groups resource passes. `requireManage()` is used to guard `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup`, and `canManage()` is also reached via `root.groups()`. A view-only admin can therefore create top-level groups. It should check only `MANAGE`. The javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` repeats the error by saying VIEW or MANAGE.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes the resource id, not the group id
body: In the `findByType` callback, `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` looks the resource up with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. For V2 the resource name is the group id, and `getId()` returns the authz resource's own UUID. The lookup misses and falls back to the all-groups resource. The result is evaluated against the wrong resource: specific group permissions are ignored, and groups can be granted or denied based on all-groups policies instead. `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` then returns resource UUIDs instead of group ids, so the `UserModel.GROUPS` filter used by user search and count does not match real group ids. The type query also returns the "Groups" type resource itself. Both uses should be `groupResource.getName()`, and the type resource should be skipped.

title: Possible NPE when the Groups type resource is missing
body: `getResourceTypeResource` returns null when the schema is unsupported or the type resource is not found. The code then calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` with a null resource, which is likely to throw an NPE instead of denying. A null check before the call should return false.

title: Javadoc inaccurate for canManage() and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()
body: The `canManage()` javadoc says it also returns true for VIEW permission on groups. That is wrong for a manage check, and it documents the bug in `GroupPermissionsV2`. The `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` javadoc says it returns a "Stream of IDs" but the method returns `Set<String>`.

title: canManage() on all-groups is granted by the VIEW scope
body: `canManage()` in V2 calls `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. It returns true when the admin has only the `view` scope on the all-groups resource. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` calls `requireManage()`, so an admin with view-only access to all groups could create top-level groups. The Javadoc in `GroupPermissionEvaluator` documents the same wrong behaviour ("VIEW or MANAGE groups"). It should check only `MANAGE`. No test covers this: `testViewGroups` never tries to create a group with view-only permission.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission mixes up the resource id and the group id
body: The callback in `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and then adds `groupResource.getId()` to the result. In `hasPermission`, the first argument is used as a name: `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. Group resources are named by the group id (see `getOrCreateResource`), while `Resource.getId()` is a different generated id. Two consequences follow. The lookup misses the per-group resource and falls back to the all-groups resource, so the wrong resource is evaluated. The returned set contains resource ids rather than group ids, yet callers (`UsersResource` and `BruteForceUsersResource`) use it to filter users by group membership and for the users count. It should use `groupResource.getName()` for both the lookup and the result. Also, `findByType("Groups")` can return the all-groups "Groups" resource itself, whose name is not a group id.

title: Possible NPE when the all-groups resource type resource is missing
body: `getResourceTypeResource` can return null, for example if the schema is not supported or the resource has not been created. The code then calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and `resource.getScopes()` without a null check. `UserPermissionsV2` has the same pattern. Because these methods are now on the hot path for `canView(group)` of every group, a null here would turn an authorization check into a 500 instead of a deny.

title: getResourceName has no handling for the new Groups resource type
body: `getResourceName` resolves a display name only for `Users` resources (id to username). Groups resources are now named by group id, but they fall through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is likely empty for these resources. Listing group permissions would then show no useful name instead of "All groups" or the group name. Add a Groups branch alongside the Users one.

title: switch on a null resourceType throws NPE
body: The old if/else chain tolerated a null `resourceType` and ended in the "Could not map resource object" IllegalStateException. The new `switch (resourceType)` throws a NullPointerException when `resourceType` is null, so the error is less informative and a different exception type.

title: canManage() grants manage-all-groups to admins who only have the VIEW scope
body: `canManage()` falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Any admin holding only an all-groups `view` permission therefore passes `canManage()`. This is a privilege escalation. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` calls `requireManage()`, so a view-only admin can create top-level groups. `canManage(GroupModel)` and `canManageMembership` also depend on it. The check should only accept `MANAGE`. The interface Javadoc for `canManage()` repeats the mistake ("VIEW or MANAGE") and should be fixed too.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission mixes up resource id, resource name and group id
body: In V2 a group's resource is named with the group id (`resolveGroup` returns `group.getId()` and `getOrCreateResource` uses it as the name). Here the lambda passes `groupResource.getId()` (the resource UUID) to `hasPermission`, which looks the resource up with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. That lookup misses, so evaluation silently falls back to the all-groups resource. The method then adds `groupResource.getId()` to the result instead of the group id (resource name), so the returned set does not contain group ids. In addition, resources created by `getOrCreateResource` get no type, so `findByType(..., "Groups")` probably does not return per-group resources at all. Callers pass this set to `searchForUserStream` (via `UserModel.GROUPS`) and to `getUsersCount(..., groupIds)`. They will get wrong or empty group sets, so user counts and queries restricted by group permissions will be wrong. The tests miss this because `canView(user)` filters the result afterwards. Use `groupResource.getName()` for both the lookup and the result, and make sure per-group resources are actually found.

title: Possible NPE when the Groups resource-type resource is missing
body: `getResourceTypeResource` can return null (schema not supported, or the resource was not created). The result is passed straight to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later dereferenced via `resource.getScopes()`. A null here gives an NPE and a 500 instead of a plain deny. Add a null check and return false.

title: V2 group permissions throw UnsupportedOperationException on paths that are still reachable
body: `GroupPermissionsV2` now overrides `groups()` for V2 and makes `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions` and similar methods throw. `GroupResource.getManagementPermissions` and `setManagementPermissionsEnabled` still call these when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled. The `GroupRemovedEvent` listener in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` calls `groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)`. If the V1 feature is enabled alongside V2, those paths now fail with a 500 where before they worked, because `groups()` used to return the V1 implementation.

title: Javadoc for getGroupIdsWithViewPermission and canManage() is inaccurate
body: The Javadoc says it returns a "Stream of IDs" but the method returns a `Set<String>`. The `canManage()` Javadoc (lines 73-77) says V2 also grants it for VIEW permission on groups. That documents the bug in `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` as intended behavior.

title: No negative tests for view-only permission or group-id-based counting
body: No test checks that an all-groups permission with only `VIEW` (or only a per-group `VIEW`) is denied for manage operations such as creating a group. That is the case that exposes the `canManage()` bug. Nothing exercises `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` or the users count endpoint with group permissions. User search tests pass only because results are filtered again afterwards. Tests for those cases would have caught the wrong id and name usage.

title: Lithuanian login TOTP step text replaced with Italian
body: The `loginTotpStep1` value was changed from a Lithuanian sentence to the Italian 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. Lithuanian users will now see Italian text on the OTP setup page. A Lithuanian translation, or removing the key so it falls back to English, would be correct.

title: Lithuanian account TOTP step text replaced with Italian
body: `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian account bundle now reads 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. The user-facing page will show the wrong language. The same copy-paste mistake appears in the Lithuanian login bundle.

title: zh_CN account TOTP step replaced with Traditional Chinese text
body: `totpStep1` in the Simplified Chinese bundle now contains Traditional Chinese ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：'). It was copied from zh_TW. Simplified-Chinese users get mismatched script, and the same file uses Simplified Chinese elsewhere.

title: English-file path derivation is fragile and only covers some layouts
body: The regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` is greedy. It is not anchored to the file name and can match earlier in the path. The mapping `resources-community` to `resources` works for the themes module, but account-ui and admin-ui keep the community files in `maven-resources-community`. That path is rewritten to `maven-resources`, which only works by accident. If the English file is missing, the verifier throws a RuntimeException instead of reporting a message, which makes the build crash on any file whose English counterpart is not found.

title: HTML detection regex misses uppercase and slash-prefixed tags
body:
`HTML_TAGS` is `<[a-z]+[^>]*>`. It is case-sensitive, so an English value containing `` or `
` would not count as HTML. It also matches non-HTML such as `` placeholders, which would wrongly enable the permissive policy for a translation. The 'English has HTML' gate is therefore both over- and under-inclusive.

title: Anchor tag comparison is order-based and removes only the first textual match
body: `santizeAnchors` pairs the Nth anchor tag in the translation with the Nth in the English text. A reordered but otherwise identical set of anchors is reported as invalid. `value.replaceFirst(...)` removes the first occurrence of the string regardless of position, while the matcher keeps iterating over the original `value`. Both can misbehave when the same anchor tag appears several times. The `key` parameter is also unused.

title: Tests only assert that an error appears, not the positive case
body: The new tests use only `hasItem(containsString(...))`. No test verifies that a valid file, or one with legitimate HTML such as `<strong>` or allowed anchors, produces no messages. `noHtml_en.properties` is added but never used as a clean case. The duplicate-keys assertion was also weakened from `contains` to `hasItem`. False positives in the new verifier would go undetected.

title: New dependencies not added to the plugin's managed/compile classpath consistently
body: `owasp-java-html-sanitizer` is added without an explicit scope and `commons-text` with `compile`. Versions are hard-coded rather than taken from the parent's dependency management. The plugin is built standalone, but this risks version drift and pulls in transitive dependencies (guava, commons-lang3) that are not reviewed.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian account bundle was replaced with "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian sentence on the OTP setup page. It should be a Lithuanian translation of "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:", or the key should be removed so the English fallback is used.

title: Lithuanian login bundle gets an Italian string for loginTotpStep1
body: `loginTotpStep1` now reads "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction on the login TOTP setup screen. Use a proper Lithuanian translation or drop the key so it falls back to English.

title: Traditional Chinese text in the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) bundle
body: `totpStep1` was changed to "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：", which is written in Traditional Chinese characters. The rest of the zh_CN file is Simplified, so this entry is inconsistent for zh_CN users. It should be Simplified, for example "在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：". The same wording already exists in the zh_TW bundle.

title: account-ui message switched from {{n}} to {n} placeholders and a MessageFormat choice
body: Every other parameterised message in this account-ui bundle uses i18next-style `{{0}}`, `{{1}}` and `{{2}}`. This entry now uses `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and a Java `{2,choice,...}` pattern. i18next will not interpolate single-brace placeholders or evaluate a `choice` expression. If the UI renders this key through i18next, users will see the literal text "Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,...}". The same concern applies to the matching change in the admin-ui English bundle. The change appears to have been made only to satisfy the new sanitizer.

title: English reference file path derived with fragile global regex replaces
body: The English file path is built with `replaceAll("resources-community", "resources")` and `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", ...)` on the full absolute path. If the English counterpart does not exist (a new locale directory, or `maven-resources-community` mapping to a non-existent `maven-resources` file), the plugin throws a bare RuntimeException instead of a MojoExecutionException or a readable message. Any unusual path layout can also mis-resolve the reference file. Resolve the sibling file in a more robust way and report a proper Mojo error.

title: Anchor error message lacks key and file
body: The message "Didn't find anchor tag X in original string" does not say which key or file it refers to. The `key` parameter is available but unused, unlike the "Illegal HTML" message. With dozens of locale files, maintainers cannot locate the offending translation from the build output. Include the key and file in the message.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The HTML-bearing Lithuanian string was replaced with "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian. Lithuanian users now see an Italian sentence on the OTP setup page. Use a Lithuanian translation of "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:", or drop the key so it falls back to English.

title: Lithuanian account totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian account theme was replaced with the Italian sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". The neighbouring Lithuanian lines are untouched, so the page mixes languages. Provide a proper Lithuanian translation or remove the key so it falls back to English.

title: Simplified Chinese locale given Traditional Chinese text
body: totpStep1 in messages_zh_CN now reads "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：", which is Traditional Chinese (手機, 安裝, 應用程式). The rest of the file is Simplified Chinese, so zh_CN users see the wrong script. Use Simplified wording such as "在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：".

title: JS-app bundle switched from i18next {{n}} placeholders to {n}
body: This key was changed from `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` to `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` plus a Java `choice` format. Every other error-* key in the same file still uses i18next `{{n}}` interpolation, and i18next does not understand `{2,choice,...}`. If the UI renders this key client-side, it will show the literal placeholders and choice pattern instead of the values. The same change was made in the admin-ui bundle. Keep the i18next form for these JS bundles, or confirm the message is only ever formatted server-side.

title: Admin UI bundle error-invalid-multivalued-size no longer uses i18next interpolation
body: The admin-ui bundle is rendered by i18next, which uses `{{0}}` placeholders, but this key now uses `{0}` and a Java `{2,choice,...}` expression. i18next will leave these unresolved, so the message shows raw placeholders and the choice syntax. Either keep i18next-compatible placeholders here or make sure the message is only formatted server-side.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher checks the wrong characters and the condition is inverted
body: The context prefix is 6 chars (session type 0-1, token type 2-3, grant type 4-5), but the matcher reads `substring(3, 5)`, which is the second char of the token type plus the first char of the grant type. The comparison is also negated: it returns false when the substring equals the expected shortcut. A token id with the correct grant shortcut therefore fails to match at the correct position. The only thing the matcher effectively verifies is the `xxx:UUID` shape, so the expectedGrantShortcut argument is not really validated. The fix is `substring(4, 6)` with `!equals` → return false. The comment 'starts at 4th char' also contradicts the 0-based indices used.

title: Null check for rawTokenId validates grantType instead
body: The fourth `Objects.requireNonNull` call passes `grantType` but carries the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'. A null `rawTokenId` is therefore accepted. Later `encodeTokenId` would produce a token id ending in the literal string `:null`, and `getTokenContextFromTokenId` would never produce it. The check must use `rawTokenId`.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method on a public server SPI interface (no default). Every third-party grant type factory fails to compile or throws AbstractMethodError at runtime. Worse, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls it on all grant factories, and a null or duplicate shortcut from a custom grant would either NPE on ConcurrentHashMap.put or abort server startup. A default method, or null-safe handling in the encoder, would avoid this.

title: Context copy constructor removed and grantType captured only once
body: The public `Context(Context)` copy constructor is removed from an SPI class, which breaks any caller or extension that used it. `grantType` is read from `formParams` once in the constructor, while `setFormParams(...)` can replace the form params afterwards without updating `grantType`. The grant type used for the token id could then differ from the actual request parameters.

title: Token type derived from session context client rather than the client the token is issued for
body: `getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)` reads `session.getContext().getClient()`. `TokenManager.initToken` receives an explicit `client` argument, which can differ from the context client (for example token exchange or pre-authorized code, where the context client is changed). The lightweight/regular flag encoded in the id could then be inconsistent with the token actually built. It is better to pass the client explicitly.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring indices
body: The matcher does `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Two things are wrong. First, the condition is inverted: the matcher returns false when the shortcut matches and true when it differs. Second, the grant shortcut sits at indices 4..6 of the 6-char prefix (`onrtac` gives `ac` at `substring(4,6)`), not 3..5. With the current code every event assertion (code-to-token, device, refresh, CIBA) accepts any wrong grant shortcut and would reject a correct one in most cases. The comment ('4th char') also disagrees with the indices used. The integration tests therefore don't validate the encoding.

title: Null check for rawTokenId actually checks grantType
