body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` repeats the grantType check, so rawTokenId is never validated. A null rawTokenId passes the constructor and later produces a token ID like `onrtac:null` in `encodeTokenId`.

title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of an NPE, not the intended validation
body: The test factory is built without `postInit`, so `sessionFactory` is null. For unknown shortcut `ac`, `getGrantTypeByShortcut` falls into the refresh branch and dereferences the null `sessionFactory`. This throws an NPE, which the broad `catch (RuntimeException)` swallows, so the test passes without ever reaching the 'Unknown value for grant type' `IllegalArgumentException`. The test should catch `IllegalArgumentException` and provide a session factory stub or otherwise avoid the refresh path.

title: Session type can be wrong for offline_access token requests
body: The session type is derived from `userSession.isOffline()` at access-token creation time. On an initial `offline_access` login (code-to-token or direct grant) the access token is built from the online user session, and the offline session is created later for the refresh token. The online session may then be removed (see the `FIRST_OFFLINE_ACCESS` handling in `OAuth2GrantTypeBase`). The token ID then says `on` although the online session no longer exists. This defeats the stated purpose of using the ID to choose which session type to look up, and the follow-up optimization #37662 would fail to find the session.

title: Token creation fails hard when the grant type has no registered shortcut
body: `encodeTokenId` throws `IllegalStateException` if `getShortcutByGrantType` returns null. The grant type comes from the request's `grant_type` form parameter via `Context.getGrantType()`. Any grant implementation or code path where the form parameter doesn't equal a registered factory ID would make access-token creation fail with a 500. Falling back to the `na` shortcut would be safer for a purely informational encoding.

title: Public copy constructor of Context removed
body: `Context(Context context)` was a public constructor in the SPI module. It is removed without any replacement or mention in the PR description. Third-party grant types or extensions that used it will break at compile time. The `grantType` field would not have been copied by it anyway.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring indices
body: The token id has the form `ssttgg:uuid`, so the grant shortcut is at chars 4..6, i.e. `substring(4, 6)`. The matcher uses `substring(3, 5)`, which covers the 2nd char of the token type and the 1st char of the grant. It also returns false when the substring EQUALS the expected shortcut, so the condition is inverted. Because indices 3..5 never equal a 2-char shortcut such as `ac`, the check never fires and the grant shortcut is never verified. Every test that uses `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh` and similar helpers passes without validating the grant type, and the wrong code would fail if the check ever matched. It should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

title: Null check for rawTokenId actually checks grantType
body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` repeats the grantType check, so `rawTokenId` is never validated. A null raw id is accepted and later encoded into the string `"xxxxxx:null"`. It should be `requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

title: New abstract method on SPI interface breaks existing custom grant factories
body: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method on the public `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI. Any third-party grant type factory will no longer compile or load. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` also calls it and puts the result into maps, so a null or duplicate shortcut from a custom grant would fail startup or corrupt the mapping. Consider a default implementation, or tolerate missing shortcuts and map them to the unknown value.

title: Token type and session type derived from ambient/early state, not the actual token
body: The lightweight flag comes from `getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)`, which reads `session.getContext().getClient()` rather than the `client` that `initToken` is creating the token for. In flows where the context client differs from the token's client (for example token exchange), the encoded token type can be wrong. The session type is read from the user session at the moment the access token is created. For offline-scope flows the access token is generated before the offline session is created (when the refresh token is generated), so it is encoded as `on` even though the request ends up using an offline session. This defeats the stated purpose of using the type to pick the right session lookup.

title: Parsing throws for any token id containing ':' that is not in the 6-char format
body: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` returns an UNKNOWN context only when there is no ':'. If the id contains ':' but the prefix is not exactly 6 chars with known shortcuts (for example tokens issued by older or custom code, or ids with other prefixes), it throws IllegalArgumentException. Callers that later use this to inspect arbitrary tokens will fail with a 500 instead of falling back to UNKNOWN. Legacy or foreign ids should degrade gracefully.

title: Context grantType is captured once and the copy constructor was removed
body: `grantType` is read from `formParams` in the constructor only. `setFormParams` can later replace the form params, which leaves `grantType` stale. The public copy constructor `Context(Context)` was also removed from this SPI class, which breaks any external code that used it.

title: Unused import added
body: `TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory` is imported but never used in this file.

title: getCredentials dereferences a possibly-null MyUser
body: `getMyUser(user)` returns null when the user is not in the `users` map, for example after removal or for a user from another provider instance. `getCredentials` then calls `myUser.recoveryCodes` without a null check. Every other method (`isConfiguredFor`, `isValid`, `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`) guards against null. A missing user would cause an NPE during credential listing instead of an empty stream.

title: Used-up user-storage codes are never removed, and used codes are not tracked
body:
`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` can now return a credential from user storage. The following lines still call `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` when `allCodesUsed()`. That call only removes credentials in the local DB. The federated credential is not removed, and its id may be null, as it is for the test storage model built via `createFromValues`.

Nothing marks a code as used when it is validated against user storage either. `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider` normally does that on validation, but the user-storage path bypasses it. As a result, the 'next code' shown by `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` never advances, and the used-up/re-configure logic only works for local credentials.

title: Recovery-key test covers only the happy path with code 0
disableCredentialType ignores recovery codes
body: The storage now supports and stores recovery codes. `disableCredentialType` and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` handle only OTP, so recovery codes can never be removed or disabled through the admin API. `isConfiguredFor` keeps returning true after the admin tries to disable them, and the state leaks between tests because the factory map is shared.

title: Used recovery codes in user storage are never consumed or removed
body:
The credential is now resolved from user storage first. But the follow-up logic still assumes local storage. `allCodesUsed()` is evaluated on a model that user storage keeps as a plain list of raw codes. The only cleanup path is `removeStoredCredentialById`, which touches only local credentials, and the federated model may have no id. As a result:
- Nothing records which code was used, so `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()` can keep asking for the same code.
- An exhausted set is never removed.
- `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES` is never re-triggered after exhaustion.

The feature only creates and validates the federated credential. It does not implement the one-time-use semantics that recovery codes require.

title: Test storage accepts any stored code, so the test cannot catch wrong-code or used-code handling
body: `isValid` for recovery codes returns true if the input matches any stored code, and never marks codes as used. The login form asks for a specific code number, and the real provider validates only that code and consumes it. The new test enters only code 0, so it cannot detect reuse of a code or acceptance of the wrong code. This gap also hides the missing consumption logic in the authenticator.

title: getCredentials can throw NPE when the user is unknown to the storage
body: `getMyUser(user)` may return null, for example after the user was removed. `getCredentials` dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp` without a null check. Other methods such as `isConfiguredFor` and `isValid` do check for null. Since `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` now calls `getFederatedCredentialsStream` on every lookup, this NPE becomes reachable in more flows.

title: Raw recovery codes are sent unhashed to user storage and the user label is dropped
body: For user storage, the raw plaintext codes are serialized as JSON and passed via `updateCredential`. The local path stores hashed codes. This differs from the local behaviour, and the storage provider becomes responsible for protecting the secrets. The user label and creation time from `credentialModel` are not passed along, so they are lost for federated credentials. This should be documented, or the metadata should be passed through.

title: getCredentials dereferences myUser without a null check
body: `getMyUser(user)` returns null when the user is not in the map, for example after `removeUser` or for a user imported from elsewhere. `myUser.recoveryCodes` is then dereferenced directly. Other methods such as `isConfiguredFor` and `isValid` guard against null. Because `getCredentials` is now on the path of every `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` call, this can throw an NPE during login or cleanup.

title: Recovery credential returned from getCredentials loses its id and always looks unused
body: `updateCredential` stores a CredentialModel with a generated id. `getCredentials` rebuilds a fresh `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)` and does not copy that id, so the returned model has a null id. It also regenerates the code state on every call, so no code is ever marked used and `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode` always returns code #0. `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` calls `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` and checks `allCodesUsed()` on the credential from `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`. For a federated credential that id is null and the used-code tracking never advances. This is only exercised with code 0, so the test hides it.

title: Federated recovery credentials are never consumed or removed after use
body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` can now return a federated credential. The post-validation logic still assumes a local credential. It calls `removeStoredCredentialById`, which only affects local storage, and relies on `allCodesUsed()`. Nothing in the user-storage path marks a used code. A recovery code accepted by the storage (`isValid`) therefore stays valid forever, and the 'next code to enter' number never advances. This defeats the one-time-use property of recovery codes for user-storage users, and no SPI contract exists to report consumption. The behaviour should at least be handled or documented.

title: Raw recovery codes are handed to user storage and old local credentials are not cleaned up
body: On the local path only hashes of the codes are persisted. This helper serializes the plaintext codes as JSON and passes them to `updateCredential`, so any user storage provider receives and can persist the raw codes. That is acceptable for OTP secrets but is worth documenting for recovery codes. In addition, when the storage accepts the credential, any previously created local recovery-codes credential is not removed. `getCredential` then silently prefers the federated one, leaving a stale local credential.

title: Recovery key test is thin and has sloppy details
body: The test only covers the first-code happy path (code index 0) and never checks that a wrong code fails. It does not cover the local-storage fallback or credential removal, which the new `getCredential` fallback and the form authenticator change affect. The authenticator config alias contains a typo (`delayed-suthenticator-config`). A 'delayed-authenticator' with delay 0 is added without need. `org.wildfly.common.Assert.assertTrue` is used as a test assertion.

title: Concurrent-deletion NPE still possible in the other getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: Only getSubGroupsCount() now null-checks the result of modelSupplier.get(). The three getSubGroupsStream(...) overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) directly. If the group was deleted concurrently, the supplier returns null and these throw the same NPE this PR is meant to fix. Either handle null there (for example return Stream.empty()) or explain why they cannot be reached.

title: getSubGroupsCount() now returns null for a deleted group
body: A vanished group makes getSubGroupsCount() return a null Long instead of throwing. Any caller that unboxes the value, or any other GroupModel consumer, would hit an NPE later and farther from the cause. In GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount the null is passed straight to setSubGroupCount, so the representation silently reports no count for a group that no longer exists. Returning 0L, or skipping groups that no longer exist, would be more predictable. The null-return contract should also be documented.

title: Reader thread is never joined and the test is timing-dependent
body: The background reader thread is started and never joined. After deletedAll.set(true), assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty()) can run before the thread's last iteration finishes, so an exception from that iteration could be missed. The thread also runs a tight loop with no bound, and an uncaught Error would not be reported. The test can pass without exercising the race at all, and it asserts only that the list is empty, not which exception occurred. Use an ExecutorService or Thread.join() before asserting, and consider a failure message. The 100 groups created are also not registered for cleanup if the test fails midway.

title: Same NPE remains in the other getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: The fix null-checks `modelSupplier.get()` only in `getSubGroupsCount()`. The three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads (lines 256, 262, 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` without a null check. If the group is deleted concurrently, `LazyModel` returns null from `getGroupById` and these methods throw the same NPE this PR is meant to fix. Listing a group's subgroups while the group is being removed hits that path. The null handling should be applied consistently, for example by returning `Stream.empty()` when the model is gone.

title: getSubGroupsCount now returns null for a vanished group
body: `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns `null` when the delegate group no longer exists, instead of throwing. Callers may unbox the `Long` or compare it numerically, and `GroupModel` does not document a null contract. Returning null silently hides the deletion and can move the NPE to the caller. Returning 0L, or an explicit documented outcome, would be safer.

title: Reader thread is never joined, so the concurrency test can miss failures and leak a thread
body: The background reader is started with `new Thread(...).start()` and never joined. After `deletedAll.set(true)` the test asserts immediately on `caughtExceptions`. An exception thrown by the reader's last in-flight iteration can be added after the assertion and go unnoticed. The thread may also keep making requests while the test tears down. The thread should be joined before asserting, ideally via an executor or a `Future`. The race is also timing-dependent and only loosely tied to the NPE being fixed.

title: Test does not exercise the changed code path
body: The reader calls `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)`, a brief listing. The fix changed `getSubGroupsCount()` in `GroupAdapter`. That method is only reached when the subgroup count is requested, via `populateSubGroupCount` with `subGroupsCount=true`. If the endpoint call does not request counts, the test does not cover the fix and may pass without it. The query should request subgroup counts, or the test should check that it fails without the fix.

title: Same NPE remains in the other getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: The PR makes getSubGroupsCount() null-safe against `modelSupplier.get()` returning null when the group was concurrently deleted. The three getSubGroupsStream overloads (lines 256, 262, 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` with no null check. The same race (group deleted between cache hit and lazy DB load) still throws an NPE there. The fix is partial. Those overloads should handle null, for example by returning an empty stream or throwing a meaningful exception.

title: getSubGroupsCount now returns null for a vanished group, which callers may not expect
body: When the group no longer exists, getSubGroupsCount() returns null instead of failing. The null flows into GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount and from there into the representation, so the API silently reports a missing count. Any other caller that unboxes the Long will NPE instead. A deleted group probably should be skipped or reported as not found, not given a null count. The null contract is undocumented.

title: Concurrency test is racy, never joins the reader thread, and may not hit the fixed path
body: The reader thread is started but never joined. After `deletedAll.set(true)`, the assertion on caughtExceptions can run while the reader is mid-request. An exception thrown in that last in-flight iteration is then missed, and the thread can outlive the test. The reader also calls `groups(null, 0, MAX, true)` with the brief representation, and it is not clear this reaches GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount(). That method is only called when subGroupsCount is requested. The test therefore may not exercise the changed code and may pass without the fix. The test is also inherently timing-dependent. It should join the thread (or use an executor) and request the sub-group count.

title: Negative offset slicing on a Django queryset raises an error; the gate is also user-controllable
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes a negative `cursor.offset` straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` when `enable_advanced_features` is true. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`. The comment claiming 'the Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is wrong. The offset comes from the user-supplied cursor string (`Cursor.from_string` accepts negative ints). So an admin (or superuser) who sends `optimized_pagination=true` with a negative-offset cursor gets a 500. Any case where it does not error (for example a mixed slice) would bypass the intended pagination bounds, so the claim that this gives 'access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' is a data-exposure risk.

title: Change to the shared BasePaginator lets negative offsets reach the ORM for all prev cursors
body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` now passes an unclamped, user-controlled negative offset to `queryset[...]` whenever `is_prev` is set. This affects every BasePaginator subclass across Sentry, not only the new opt-in path. Previously the offset was passed through as-is, so negative values already failed. The change adds no protection, and the comment ('safe because the queryset handles boundary conditions') is false. A crafted prev cursor such as `0:-5:1` triggers an AssertionError (500) on any paginated endpoint. The stop computation is also inconsistent: `stop = start_offset + limit + extra` can be smaller than the start.

title: Authorization gate for the experimental paginator is weak and can crash
body: `enable_advanced` is `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. `organization_context.member` can be None, for example for superusers who are not org members, which raises AttributeError. The `or` short-circuits only when the user is a superuser, so a non-member non-superuser would hit it, and the check is hard to reason about overall. The feature is also exposed through a plain query parameter. Combined with the negative offset handling, this opens an unsafe code path to a broad set of org members (anyone with global access). Trailing whitespace also appears on lines 71 and 89.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is wrong for datetime ordering and duplicates BasePaginator logic
body: The endpoint uses `order_by="-datetime"` with OptimizedCursorPaginator, whose `get_item_key` does `math.floor(getattr(item, 'datetime'))`. `floor` on a datetime raises TypeError. `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw value instead of converting it back to a datetime, as DateTimePaginator does. So the optimized path fails on the first request that returns results. Beyond that, the class copies about 70 lines of BasePaginator.get_result, which invites drift. It also has no tests.

title: Misleading comment claims negative offsets are supported
body: The added comment says negative offsets are allowed for efficient reverse pagination. The code is unchanged (`int(offset)`) and nothing validates or supports negative values downstream. The comment documents unsupported, unsafe behavior and will mislead maintainers.

title: Prev-cursor trimming uses the raw offset after negative-offset slicing
body: `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` uses `offset`, which may be negative, while the slice used `start_offset`. The condition is meaningless for negative offsets, so an extra row is not trimmed and prev pages return wrong or duplicated rows.

title: Negative offset slicing on Django QuerySet raises or misbehaves
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes `cursor.offset` (user-controlled, parsed from the cursor string, which allows negative ints) straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`. The comment that the ORM "properly handles negative slicing" is false. Where the slice does not assert (e.g. a start of -5 with a positive stop), the result is wrong, so a crafted cursor returns a 500 or inconsistent data. There is no validation that the offset is non-negative.

title: Shared BasePaginator now allows negative offsets for prev cursors
body: The change to `BasePaginator.get_result` uses `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. For any prev cursor, a negative offset from a user-supplied cursor (e.g. `value:-5:1`) now reaches `queryset[negative:stop]`, which raises an AssertionError (500) instead of being clamped. Before this PR the same input would have failed on the negative slice too, but the added comments claim this is a deliberate safe feature. This is a behavior change on a path used by every endpoint using BasePaginator subclasses, and the `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check further down becomes inconsistent with the clamped start.

title: Privilege gating on negative-offset feature, and potential data exposure to org-level admins
body: The `optimized_pagination` path is enabled for any member with `has_global_access` (not just superusers), and it unlocks negative offsets that the code comment says give "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds". The claim that "permissions are checked at the queryset level" is not a real safeguard, since the queryset is only filtered by organization_id. An untested, user-controlled flag that changes slicing semantics on an audit log endpoint is risky. `organization_context.member` can also be None (e.g. for superusers who are not org members), which raises AttributeError, but only after `request.user.is_superuser` is evaluated false.

title: Possible AttributeError when member is None
body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally for every request (even without the `optimized_pagination` param). If `member` is None (e.g. a staff or API-token user who is not an org member), this raises AttributeError and breaks the whole endpoint, a regression for the default path. The evaluation should be short-circuited behind `use_optimized`, and `member` should be null-checked.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key breaks on datetime ordering
body: The audit log endpoint orders by `-datetime`, but the new paginator's `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `getattr(item, 'datetime')`, which is a `datetime` object, so it raises TypeError. The `value_from_cursor` method also returns the raw cursor value rather than converting it to a datetime, unlike `DateTimePaginator`. As a result, the optimized path fails for every request (or produces wrong cursor filtering).

title: Duplicated get_result and unused/misleading design
body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` is a near-verbatim copy of `BasePaginator.get_result`. The only difference is the negative-offset branch, and the `else` branch is identical to the base logic. This creates a maintenance burden and divergence risk. The docstring claims performance optimizations that do not exist, since it performs the same queries.

title: Prev-cursor trimming uses unadjusted offset
body: `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` uses the raw `cursor.offset`, which can be negative in the advanced branch, while the actual slice start differs. The condition will not match the number of rows fetched, so the extra row is not dropped and pages can contain an extra or duplicate item.

title: No tests for new paginator or endpoint branch
body: The PR adds a new paginator, a new query parameter, and negative-offset behavior with no tests. The PR description is just "Test 1", with no explanation of the feature. There is also trailing whitespace on lines 71 and 89.

title: Negative offset slicing on a Django QuerySet raises AssertionError (500)
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The comment claiming the ORM handles this is wrong. A client-supplied cursor such as `0:-5:1` therefore turns into an unhandled 500. Even if the slice were accepted, the PR's stated intent of reading 'data beyond normal pagination bounds' is a bounds bypass, not a feature.

title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets through for prev cursors
body: The change in the shared BasePaginator.get_result sets `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. For prev cursors a negative offset now reaches `queryset[start_offset:stop]` unclamped. Previously, negative offsets were passed directly for all cursors; this change doesn't clamp for prev cursors at all, so a crafted cursor like `123:-1:1` causes an AssertionError (500) on every endpoint that uses DateTimePaginator or Paginator. The misleading comment says negative offsets are safe. Behavior for normal cursors is unchanged, so this edit adds risk with no benefit.

title: Access check is broader than 'administrators' and uses a possibly missing member
body: `enable_advanced` is `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. `has_global_access` is true for ordinary members of open-membership orgs, so any such member can opt in with `?optimized_pagination=true`, and with it the unsafe negative-offset path. `organization_context.member` can also be None, for example for a superuser who is not a member of the org. The `or` short-circuits only when the user is a superuser, but any non-superuser without a membership would raise AttributeError. The gating is neither principled nor safe.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is a near-copy that misuses key types and adds a feature with no tests
body: The class duplicates BasePaginator.get_result and uses the integer-oriented get_item_key and value_from_cursor (`math.floor(getattr(item, key))`) rather than DateTimePaginator's logic. The audit log endpoint orders by `-datetime`, so `math.floor` on a datetime raises TypeError and the optimized path crashes on any non-empty result. Cursor values also aren't converted back to datetimes. No tests were added for the new paginator, the endpoint flag, or negative offsets.

title: Prev-cursor trimming check uses the unclamped offset
body: `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` uses the raw `offset`, which can be negative in the advanced path. The length comparison then no longer matches the number of rows fetched, so the extra row is not dropped correctly and pages can contain wrong or extra items.

title: Comment advertises negative offsets but no code change supports it
body: The added comment says negative offsets are allowed for 'efficient reverse pagination', but `Cursor.__init__` is unchanged and performs no validation. The comment implies a supported feature and may mislead; negative offsets from user cursors are in fact unvalidated and cause errors downstream.

title: Negative offset slicing is unsupported by Django and the 'advanced' path is a client-controlled bypass
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset` taken from the client-supplied cursor. Django querysets raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` for negative slice bounds, so any request with a negative offset becomes a 500. The comments claim the ORM 'properly handles' this and that it 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds', which is wrong and describes a boundary bypass. The path is also enabled by a client-controlled `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter.

title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets through for prev cursors
body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` means that for `is_prev` cursors the raw, possibly negative offset reaches `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Cursor.from_string accepts negative ints, so a user can craft `0:-5:1` and trigger an assertion error (500) on every endpoint using BasePaginator or its subclasses. Before this change the code sliced `[offset:stop]`, which behaved no differently for negative values, but the added comment now claims this is a deliberate, safe feature. The change also affects all callers, not just audit logs.

title: User-controlled flag selects an experimental paginator on a sensitive endpoint
body: The audit-log endpoint switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator when `optimized_pagination=true` and the user is a superuser or has global access. This is an undocumented, unfeatured switch that exposes the unsafe negative-offset path. `request.user.is_superuser` is checked without verifying an active superuser session. The comment 'permissions are checked at the queryset level' does not justify skipping bounds checks. There is also no test coverage for this branch.

title: New paginator duplicates BasePaginator logic and has no tests
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator copy-pastes nearly all of BasePaginator.get_result, and its get_item_key is the plain integer version rather than the datetime version. When used with `order_by="-datetime"` in the audit-log endpoint, `math.floor(datetime)` raises TypeError, so the optimized path crashes on the first page. `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw int, which is then compared against a datetime column. No tests were added.

title: Redirect-depth loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 without justification
body: The loop bound was lowered from 10000 to 1000, and the comment about depth limits was removed. Segment trees deeper than 1000 will no longer have their redirects resolved correctly, so their spans end up in the wrong set. This is unrelated to the eviction change and unexplained.

title: Span count check removed from load path; max_segment_spans now unused
body: The `max_segment_spans` check in `_load_segment_data` was deleted, so the `max_segment_spans` constructor parameter is now dead. The Lua script hardcodes 1000, which is inconsistent with the default of 1001. Eviction in Lua is also not covered by any test (no test inserts more than 1000 spans). The module docstring still says sets, not sorted sets.

title: end_timestamp_precise accessed with hard indexing
body: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises KeyError if a span lacks the field, which crashes the whole batch in the consumer (poison message). Previously, spans without it were processed fine. A fallback or validation is needed. In addition, zadd with the scores gives spans identical payloads the same member, so dedup semantics stay the same, but eviction (zpopmin) drops the oldest spans, which may include the root span.

title: Negative offset slicing on Django querysets is unsupported and exposes an unsafe path
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `start_offset = cursor.offset < 0`). Django raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`. The comment saying the ORM "properly handles negative slicing automatically" is wrong. The cursor offset comes from the user-supplied cursor string (`Cursor.from_string` accepts negative ints). Any admin passing `optimized_pagination=true` with a negative offset will get a 500. The comment about 'data beyond normal pagination bounds' suggests the feature is meant to bypass pagination bounds, which is a risk in itself.

title: Undocumented user-controlled query flag switches the audit-log endpoint onto an experimental paginator
body: `optimized_pagination=true` selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, gated only by `is_superuser or member.has_global_access`. That is a broad gate (every org owner/manager). This is unrelated to the PR title (spans buffer) and it exposes the unsafe negative-offset path on an audit-log API. Also `organization_context.member` can be None (e.g. for superusers not in the org), which would raise AttributeError. The `request.user.is_superuser or ...` evaluation order means non-superusers without a member would crash.

title: Shared BasePaginator now passes negative offsets for prev cursors to every paginator
body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` changes behavior for all BasePaginator subclasses used across Sentry. For `is_prev` cursors with a negative offset (user-controlled via the cursor string), the slice is now negative and raises an AssertionError (500) instead of being clamped. The justification comment is wrong. This is an unrelated, risky change to core pagination.

title: Prev-cursor trim uses raw offset inconsistent with the slice actually used
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator, the condition `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` uses `offset`, while the slice was computed from `start_offset`. With a negative offset the lengths do not match, so the extra row is never trimmed and pages come out with the wrong size. The class also duplicates most of BasePaginator.get_result, and its `get_item_key` lacks datetime handling, so ordering by `-datetime` will fail with `math.floor(datetime)` TypeError.

title: Redirect traversal depth limit reduced from 10000 to 1000
body: The loop bound was lowered from 10000 to 1000 and the explanatory comment removed. Span trees deeper than 1000 will no longer resolve to the correct root set, silently producing split segments. This is not mentioned in the description.

title: Eviction hard-codes 1000 while Python max_segment_spans is 1001; span_count may be stale
body: The Lua script trims to 1000 spans with `zpopmin`, but the `max_segment_spans` config (1001) is still defined in `SpansBuffer`, and the Python-side span-count check was removed from `_load_segment_data`, leaving it unused. Also, `span_count` is only the result of the last zunionstore. The payloads for the current span are zadded in Python before the script, so if neither union happens the zcard fallback is used, but if the first union ran and the second did not, the count reflects only the first union. That is fine, but the limit is not configurable and diverges from the config value.

title: Switching from SET to ZSET without migration breaks in-flight data and dedups by payload only
body: Keys with the same names (`span-buf:s:*`) change type from set to sorted set. During rollout, existing set keys will cause WRONGTYPE errors in `zcard`/`zunionstore`/`zscan`, breaking the consumer. Also, `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` is now required in `process_batch`, so any span lacking it raises KeyError and crashes the batch.

title: No tests for eviction behavior or new paginator
body: The PR adds span eviction at 1000 spans, a new OptimizedCursorPaginator, and negative offset handling, but the tests only add the new `end_timestamp_precise` field. No test covers the eviction ordering (oldest dropped), nor the paginator or audit log changes.

title: Negative offsets allowed in OptimizedCursorPaginator, and Django rejects negative slicing
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django querysets raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`, so a crafted cursor such as `0:-5:0` gives a 500. Even if it worked, the comment claiming this is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level is wrong. Negative offsets are a way around the pagination bounds. The cursor comes from user input, and nothing validates it. Reject negative offsets instead of enabling them.

title: BasePaginator now passes negative offset to queryset slicing for prev cursors
body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` leaves negative offsets unclamped for any prev cursor. This affects every endpoint that uses BasePaginator, not only the new paginator. A user-supplied prev cursor with a negative offset (e.g. `123:-1:1`) now reaches `queryset[-1:stop]`, which raises an AssertionError (500). Before this change the slice was `queryset[offset:stop]`, which also had no clamp, so the change adds nothing and its comment claiming safety is false. The `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check further down also mixes up the offsets.

title: Unreleased experimental pagination path gated on client-controlled flag in an audit-log endpoint
body: The audit log endpoint is unrelated to the spans buffer change in the PR title. It adds an `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter that switches to a paginator accepting negative offsets. This is exposed to superusers and to any member with global access. Giving privileged users a less-validated cursor path on a sensitive audit log is risky, and the paginator has no tests. This should be a separate, reviewed change. `OptimizedCursorPaginator` also duplicates `BasePaginator.get_result` almost entirely. Its `get_item_key` is the plain integer one, which would fail on the datetime `-datetime` ordering used here: `math.floor` on a datetime raises TypeError.

title: Possible AttributeError on organization_context.member
body: `organization_context.member` can be None, for example for a superuser who is not a member of the organization. `request.user.is_superuser or ...` short-circuits for superusers. For non-superusers without a membership, `.has_global_access` raises AttributeError. The expression is also evaluated even when `optimized_pagination` is not requested, so it can break the default path.

title: Trailing whitespace
body: Lines 71 and 89 have trailing whitespace (also in paginator.py docstring lines). This will fail the repo's lint checks.

title: Redirect loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 without justification
body: The loop bound went from 10000 to 1000, and the comment that documented the limit was dropped. Segment trees deeper than 1000 hops will now be joined incorrectly. Nothing in the PR says this is intentional, and it is unrelated to the eviction feature.

title: Eviction trims by score order using hardcoded 1000 and is inconsistent with max_segment_spans
body: Eviction uses a hardcoded 1000 limit, while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` is 1001 (and no longer enforced in `_load_segment_data`). `span_count` is only the zunionstore result from the last merge, or a zcard. Because `zpopmin` removes the lowest-score (earliest end timestamp) spans, a segment's root or early spans can be dropped silently, with no metric or log. The old explicit check and the `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric were removed, so there is no visibility. The `max_segment_spans` parameter is now dead.

title: Switching set to sorted set breaks compatibility with existing keys and drops required field handling
body: Switching from SADD/SSCAN to ZADD/ZSCAN changes the Redis type of `span-buf:s:*` keys. Existing set keys in a live deployment will cause WRONGTYPE errors on `zadd`, `zcard` and `zunionstore`, with no migration or rollout note. Also, `end_timestamp_precise` is read with `val[...]`, which raises KeyError for any span lacking the field, crashing the whole batch. Identical payloads are deduplicated by member, as with sets, so the score of a re-sent span is updated.

title: __reduce__ does not pass the new/reordered constructor args correctly
body: `__reduce__` passes `redis_ttl` positionally as the 4th argument, but the 4th parameter of `__init__` is `segment_page_size`. This is a pre-existing bug, but it matters now because the segment limits are central to this change. Pickled instances in multiprocessing get the wrong `segment_page_size`.

title: Cache key uses Python's per-process randomized hash() of a tuple
body: The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Python's built-in `hash` is not stable across processes for tuples of ints in all cases, and it can collide. That makes it unsafe for a shared cache (memcached/redis). Colliding project sets would share an eligibility result, so a non-allowlisted set could be told it is eligible, or the reverse. Use a stable key such as a joined sorted id list or a real digest.

title: Allowlist eligibility cached for 60s with no invalidation hook
body: Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds, but `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere. After the option changes, stale results are served for up to a minute. The cache is also pointless, since `options.get` is already cached in-process. It adds a cache round-trip and staleness for no gain. The docstring's claim that the lookups are expensive is wrong.

title: Allowlist membership test depends on the option's element types
body: `project_id in allowlist` does a linear scan of the option list for every project. If the option contains strings, or ids of a different type, the check silently fails. Convert the allowlist to a set of ints once, then check membership against that set.

title: Discover eligibility is decided by a substring match on the raw request query
body: `_is_error_focused_query` does a substring match for `event.type:error` on `request.GET['query']`. This misfires on negated queries (`!event.type:error`), on `event.type:error_foo`, and on any query containing that text in a value. The endpoint also rewrites the query internally, for example adding `AND !event.type:transaction` for the dashboard split. In that case the helper reads the original request query rather than the query actually executed. The result is upsampled counts applied to the wrong queries, or missed for the right ones. Parse the query that is actually run instead.

title: Upsampling check uses the outer `dataset`, not `scoped_dataset`
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is called with the closure `dataset`, not the `scoped_dataset` argument. The dashboard-split paths call `_get_event_stats` with `discover` or the scoped dataset, and the eligibility decision ignores that. A transaction query or a split-to-transactions query can therefore be rewritten with `upsampled_count`, which reads `sample_weight`, a column transactions do not have. The query can then fail or return wrong data.

title: Transformed `upsampled_count()` is sent to datasets that don't define it
body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` emits `upsampled_count() as count`. The function is only registered in the discover dataset's `function_converter`. The errors dataset, and the RPC path at line 277, are not given it. Eligibility returns True for `dataset == errors`, so top-events and RPC queries on those datasets may fail with an unknown-function error. Only count() is rewritten, and the alias is hard-coded to 'count', which would break aliasing for top events that use a different yAxis.

title: Trailing whitespace and misleading comments
body: Lines 223, 234 and 278 (and the cache helper file) have trailing whitespace, which will fail lint. The comments claim 'cached result ensures consistent behavior' and 'late transformation ensures we use most current schema assumptions'. The code does neither, and the check re-runs on every `_get_event_stats` call.

title: upsampled_count() sums sample_weight with no null/zero fallback and is not private
body: `sum(sample_weight)` is used directly. Events ingested without `sample_weight` contribute NULL or 0 and are dropped from the count. Events from before the feature, or from non-sampled SDKs in allowlisted projects, are therefore undercounted. A fallback such as `coalesce(sample_weight, 1)` is needed. The function is also publicly exposed (no `private=True`), so users can call it directly. The 'assumes schema guarantees' comments are not backed by anything.

title: Test factory unconditionally rewrites sample_rate on stored events, with swallowed exceptions
body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` is applied to every `store_event` call. It overrides `sample_rate` for all tests that happen to include `contexts.error_sampling`. It also wraps everything in bare `except Exception: pass`, which hides malformed data. The helper lives in shared test infrastructure and changes behavior for unrelated tests, so it should be opt-in or narrower.

title: No unit test for the main entry point or the caching behavior
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and the cache and invalidate logic have no unit tests. Only the private helpers are tested. Nothing exercises cache hits, staleness, or the key function. The test also builds a `SnubaParams` that it never uses.

title: Stray submodule/gitlink file committed
body: A `sentry-repo` entry, a subproject commit pointing at the base commit, is added to the repo. It is unrelated to the feature and looks like an accidental commit. It should be removed.

title: Cache key uses Python's per-process randomized hash() of a tuple
body: The key is `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Python's built-in hash of a tuple of ints is stable, but it is a lossy 64-bit hash with possible collisions, and it makes the key opaque. Two different project sets that collide would share an eligibility result. That can wrongly upsample counts for non-allowlisted projects. Use a deterministic join of the IDs, or a real digest, instead.

title: Cached eligibility is never invalidated, so allowlist changes are delayed up to 60s
body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called anywhere, including when the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes. After an allowlist edit, results stay stale for 60s. That is only an option lookup, which is already cheap and in-process, so the cache adds staleness and a cache round trip with almost no benefit. The tests also mock `options` but not the cache, so a cached value from one test can leak into another via the shared cache. The cache should be removed or properly invalidated.

title: Allowlist membership check on a list of raw option values
body: `project_id in allowlist` is a linear scan per project and relies on the option holding ints. If the option is stored with a different type (e.g. strings), eligibility is silently False. Convert to a set of ints for both correctness and performance.

title: Upsampling check uses outer `dataset`, not `scoped_dataset`
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, which differs from `dataset` in the dashboard-split paths (e.g. `discover` is passed for the errors-only query). The eligibility check passes the closure's `dataset`. In the split path the transformation can be applied or skipped for the wrong dataset. For example, a transaction-only query run against `discover` can get `upsampled_count()` even though the sample_weight column does not apply. Use `scoped_dataset`.

title: Error detection is a naive substring match on the raw request query
body: `_is_error_focused_query` checks `"event.type:error" in query` on the raw request `query` param. This misses `!event.type:error`, so negated queries are treated as error queries. It also misses queries that only get event.type through the split path's appended `AND !event.type:transaction`. For example, `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` is treated as error-only and so would sum sample_weight over transactions. The query actually executed in `_get_event_stats` (the `query` argument) is not used.

title: Upsampling applied to RPC datasets / transformed column not supported there
body: The transformed column `upsampled_count() as count` is passed to `run_timeseries_query` and `run_top_events_timeseries_query` for the RPC path. The RPC resolver has no `upsampled_count` function. `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns False for other datasets, so this is mostly dead code today. It is also unreachable-looking logic that would break if the dataset check changes. The same transform is duplicated in three branches instead of being done once.

title: upsampled_count sums sample_weight, which is NULL/absent for events without sample rate
body: `sum(sample_weight)` ignores events with a NULL sample_weight, so events lacking a sample rate contribute 0 instead of 1. The comment assumes the column exists for every event in allowlisted projects, but nothing enforces that. Counts will be undercounted, or 0 for projects with no sample_weight. It should fall back with something like `ifNull(sample_weight, 1)`. The function also isn't validated against the errors dataset (`sample_weight` may not be a known column in the builder).

title: Test factory silently swallows all exceptions and mutates event data
body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` uses bare `except Exception: pass`. It also sets `sample_rate` on every stored event from the context, changing behavior of unrelated tests. Failures to parse are hidden, and a falsy rate of 0 is ignored.

title: Stray submodule/gitlink file committed
body: A `sentry-repo` gitlink (Subproject commit a5d29095...) was added to the repository. This looks like an accidental artifact and should not be part of the change.

title: Misleading comments and trailing whitespace
body: Comments claim a 'cached result ensures consistent behavior' and 'late transformation ensures most current schema assumptions', which is inaccurate. Lines 223, 234 and 278 contain trailing whitespace (lint failures). The unrelated error message change at line 124 is also bundled in.

title: Tests don't cover top_events path, cache behavior, or discover dataset with errors; fragile cache interplay
body: Tests mock `options` but the real cache is used. Cached eligibility keyed by org and project IDs can leak between tests and give order-dependent results. `self.project`/`project2` are created via `create_project()`, whose IDs vary, so key collisions are unlikely but not controlled. There is no coverage of topEvents or of the dashboard split path, where the dataset mismatch bug lives.

title: Cache key uses Python's randomized hash() of project IDs, which is unstable across processes
body: The cache key is built with `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. For tuples of ints, hash() is deterministic, but it is not collision-free, so two different project sets can share a key and get each other's eligibility result. A collision could upsample a query whose projects are not all allowlisted. The key should use the explicit sorted ids (e.g. a join) or a stable digest instead.

title: Eligibility is cached for 60s but nothing calls invalidate_upsampling_cache
body: Allowlist eligibility is cached for 60 seconds and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called when the option changes. After the allowlist is edited, queries can keep returning upsampled or non-upsampled counts for up to a minute. The docstring says it "should be called" on config change, but no caller exists. The cache also adds almost nothing, because `options.get` is already cheap and in-process cached. It also makes tests flaky: the endpoint tests mock `options` but the shared cache can return a result from a previous test with the same org and project ids.

title: Misleading docstring and comments about cache and schema guarantees
body: The docstring of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` says it reads the config fresh each time to get the latest state, while the caller caches the result for 60s. The comment in `_get_event_stats` says the 'cached result ensures consistent behavior', and the code comments describe a 'late transformation' as using 'current schema assumptions'. None of these match what the code does. Comments also claim sample_weight is guaranteed by the schema, but nothing enforces that.

title: Upsampling check uses outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is passed the closure variable `dataset`, not the `scoped_dataset` argument of `_get_event_stats`. The dashboard-widget split path calls `_get_event_stats(discover, ...)` with a modified query, such as `!event.type:transaction`, and with `transactions_only_query`. The eligibility check ignores that dataset and also reads `request.GET['query']` rather than the `query` argument. For these calls the decision is wrong. The transactions-only discover query can be upsampled based on the original request, which would reference sample_weight on transaction rows. The check should use `scoped_dataset` and the actual query.

title: Error-focused detection is a naive substring match on the raw request query
body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True for any query containing 'event.type:error'. That includes `!event.type:error`, `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and quoted text. Queries that include transactions would be upsampled, and queries using other forms (e.g. `is:unresolved`, or no event.type with discover) are never upsampled. It also reads the raw request rather than the effective query.

title: upsampled_count has no null handling and is a public function with unsafe semantics
body: `upsampled_count` is registered as `sum(sample_weight)` wrapped in `toInt64`, with no guard for rows where sample_weight is NULL or missing. Events stored before this feature, or from SDKs that don't send a sample rate, have no weight, so they contribute 0 and counts are silently under-reported. The function is also not marked `private=True`, so users can call it in any query on any dataset, including transactions, where the column does not exist, which produces Snuba errors.

title: Bare `except Exception: pass` blocks in the test factory hide errors
body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` swallows all exceptions in both the lookup and the float conversion. Malformed fixtures then fail silently and the sample_rate is never set, so tests exercising upsampling may pass or fail for the wrong reason. It also treats a 0 rate as absent. Catching the specific exceptions (AttributeError, TypeError, ValueError) would be more appropriate.

title: Test setup reassigns self.user and has gaps in coverage
body: `setUp` calls `self.login_as(user=self.user)` and then overwrites `self.user` with a new user, which is confusing. The tests only cover the `count()` yAxis on the plain timeseries path. There is no coverage of topEvents, the RPC path, the dashboard-split path, or cache invalidation. The mocked `options` is patched at module level while the cache is not cleared between tests.

title: Stray submodule/gitlink file committed
body: A `sentry-repo` gitlink (Subproject commit a5d29095...) is added to the repo root. It is unrelated to the feature and looks like an accidental commit. It should be removed.

title: Error timestamps likely compared against replay event timestamps in different units
body: gen_request_data compares `error_events[idx]["timestamp"]` (nodestore event timestamp, float seconds) with `event.get("timestamp", 0)` from rrweb segment events, which are normally epoch milliseconds. If the units differ, every error is less than every replay event, so all errors are emitted before the first breadcrumb. The chronological interleaving then fails and the 'at <timestamp>' values mix seconds and milliseconds in the prompt sent to Seer. The tests only pass because they use identical small or second-based values. Normalize one side (for example multiply the error timestamp by 1000) before comparing.

title: Error ids zipped with nodestore results by position
body: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns values in the same order as the requested ids, and that no ids are missing. `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id. Missing nodes or a different ordering misattribute event ids to the wrong data. Iterate the node ids and look up each one in the dict instead.

title: Analytics event recorded before the feature-flag check
body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` check. Requests from organizations without the feature, which get a 404, are still counted as assemble events. This inflates the metric. Record after the feature gate.

title: Truthiness check on age/timestamp lets age=0 coexist with timestamp
body: validate_timestamp and validate_age use `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `.get("timestamp")` as truthiness checks. `age: 0` is a valid value in the Editor's Draft format. A report with `age: 0` plus a `timestamp` passes validation even though the two specs are meant to be mutually exclusive. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` instead.

title: Flagged TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with empty columns and empty data
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the widget renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and an empty `tableData`. The real `result.data` and `result.meta` are ignored, and `columns={[]}` also defeats the fallback to `meta.fields`. Every table widget in an org with the flag on therefore shows an empty table. This is only safe while the flag is off, and the placeholder should be wired to the result data or clearly marked as a TODO.

title: Hook now returns undefined attributes and drops the environment filter
body: The old hook always returned a `TagCollection` (an empty object while loading). It now returns `isFetching ? previous : data`, which is `undefined` until the first fetch resolves, so callers that index or iterate `attributes` can break. The `environment` query param (selection.environments) is also no longer sent, and the `staleTime: 0`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and `retry: false` options were dropped. That changes caching and refetch behavior. Default `attributes` to `{}` and confirm the dropped options are intentional.

title: Error timestamps are compared against replay event timestamps in different units
body: Nodestore error events carry `timestamp` in float seconds (line 115). Replay recording events (rrweb) normally carry their `timestamp` in milliseconds. `gen_request_data` compares `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)` directly. With real data every error looks earlier than the first breadcrumb, so all errors are emitted at the start of the log instead of at their chronological position. The tests hide this because they use seconds for both.

title: All error events are re-sent with every paginated page
body: `on_results=functools.partial(analyze_recording_segments, error_events)` runs once per page of segment metadata. Each call builds a separate Seer request with the full error list. Errors later than the page's last event are appended at the end of every page, so they are duplicated across pages. Errors from outside a page's time range also appear in it, out of order. The error list should be filtered by each page's time range, or the pages should be combined before the Seer request is built.

title: Feature-flagged table widget renders an empty table
body: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` flag is on, `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and `tableData` set to empty `data` and empty `meta`. The real `result.data`, `result.meta` and `loading` are ignored. Every table widget for flagged orgs shows no columns and no rows. If this is deliberate scaffolding, it needs a TODO. Otherwise the result should be mapped into `TabularData`.

title: Query key omits the organization, and the migration dropped the old request settings
body: The key is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`. `queryOptions` has no organization slug, but the fetch URL is org-specific. Two orgs with the same page filters and item type share a cache entry, so one org can be served the other's attributes. The previous `useApiQuery` also set `staleTime: 0`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and `retry: false`, and sent `environment`. The new `useQuery` call uses defaults, so it retries and refetches on window focus.

title: Analytics event recorded before the feature-flag check
body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` check. The event fires for organizations that don't have the feature, and the endpoint then returns 404. Usage metrics are skewed by requests that are rejected. The call should come after the feature check.

title: Per-issue event lookup when building the PR comment
body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for each issue while the comment body is built. That is a separate event fetch per issue (up to 5), and it adds latency to the comment workflow. The catch-all `except Exception` hides failures and logs them only at info level. Fetching the environment in bulk, or from data already loaded, would be cheaper.

title: New PR-comment template drops the culprit/subtitle and truncates titles
body: `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE` no longer includes the issue culprit/subtitle. `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` also truncates titles to 50 chars with `...`. The PR comment now carries less context than before, and nothing in the PR description mentions the change. The template also ends in `\n`, and each item is joined with `\n`, so every entry is followed by a blank line. That produces separate paragraphs instead of a tight list, and trailing blank lines in the GitLab body. The tests were rewritten to match this output.

title: get_environment_info triggers an extra event fetch per issue
body: For every issue in the comment, `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` and then `get_environment()`. That is an extra nodestore/Snuba lookup per issue, up to 5, inside the comment task. The broad `except Exception` swallows failures and logs only at info level. The helper also logs under the key `no-environment` even when the cause is a real error.

title: Static method references PRCommentWorkflow instead of the defining class
body: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` is a `@staticmethod` on `CommitContextIntegration`, but it calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title`. `_truncate_title` is defined on `CommitContextIntegration`, not on `PRCommentWorkflow`. If `PRCommentWorkflow` is a different class, as its name suggests, this raises AttributeError. The call should reference `CommitContextIntegration`.

title: Default autofix automation tuning silently changed from "low" to "off"
body: `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` and the project option default both change from `low` to `off`. Projects that never set this option change behavior: autofix automation stops running for them. The change is not mentioned in the PR description, and it is unrelated to the replay bulk-delete theme.

title: Applied migrations rewritten into no-ops
body: Migrations 0917 and 0920 are replaced with no-ops, and the 0917 test is deleted. The comment claims they never ran. Any environment that already applied the originals, or any self-hosted install, silently loses that conversion. The comment points to a `0921_..._rerevised` migration, but that file is not part of this change, so the data fix may not exist. Rewriting history is also risky for migration state.

title: Unauthenticated endpoint logs full request body and raw invalid payloads
body: The endpoint has `permission_classes = ()`. It logs the entire `request.data` at info level on every request, and logs the raw invalid data at warning level. Anonymous clients can inject arbitrarily large or sensitive content into logs. No batch size or list length limit is enforced either.

title: age/timestamp validators use truthiness, so a value of 0 is accepted alongside the other field
body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` check `self.initial_data.get(...)` for truthiness. `age: 0` or `timestamp: 0` therefore passes the mutual-exclusion check. The two specs can be mixed, and a report with neither field is also accepted. The check should use `is not None` or key presence. If exactly one of the two is required, add that requirement.

title: Error events zipped with nodestore result by position, and timestamp may be a string
body: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `get_multi` returns values in the same order as the requested IDs. The dict is keyed by node ID, and any missing node is dropped from the result, so the IDs and values can misalign. Event IDs get attached to the wrong data. In addition, nodestore `timestamp` is a float in normal events but is not validated. `error_events.sort` and the `<` comparison will raise on bad types.

title: Extra Snuba and nodestore queries on every request, even for pagination
body: Each GET runs `query_replay_instance` against Snuba and a nodestore multi-get. This happens outside the paginator and is repeated for every page request. `error_events` is also sorted in place inside `get_request_data`, which mutates a list shared across the `on_results` call. The error context should be fetched once and the in-place mutation avoided.

title: Analytics recorded before the feature flag check
body: `analytics.record` runs before `features.has(...)`. Orgs without the feature, whose request then returns 404, still emit `preprod_artifact.api.assemble` events. This inflates the metric. It also uses `request.user.id`, which may be None or missing for org-token auth. The event could be recorded after the feature check.

title: Owner field is not validated against the organization
body: `ActorField` is added to the validator, but the validator does not check that the owner belongs to the organization. The new tests (`test_owner_not_in_organization`, `test_invalid_owner`) assert a 400 for an owner from another org. Nothing in this diff enforces that, so those tests may fail, and a cross-org owner may be accepted. Add an explicit `validate_owner`.

title: New hard processing deadlines on webhook delivery tasks
body: The deadlines are 30s for the scheduler, 300s for `drain_mailbox`, and 120s for `drain_mailbox_parallel`. They are new and unexplained. Draining a mailbox with slow or retrying destinations can exceed them, and the task is then killed and retried mid-delivery. This risks duplicate webhook delivery.

title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with empty placeholder data behind feature flag
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and empty `tableData`. The real `result.data` and `meta` are never passed. Every table widget therefore renders blank for orgs with the flag, and the loading state is ignored.

title: Optional chaining on a required prop, then unguarded access
body: `tableData?.meta.fields` is used even though `tableData` is a required prop. If `tableData` were undefined, `.meta` would still throw, so the optional chaining protects nothing. `renderDefaultHeadCell` also passes `column.name` to `fieldAlignment` where a field key is expected. When `columns` supplies a custom display name, alignment is computed from the display name instead.

title: Query key and caching behavior changed: staleTime and refetch settings dropped, key omits org
body: The hook moves from `useApiQuery` to a raw `useQuery`. The query key `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]` does not include the organization slug. Two orgs with identical filters can share a cache entry. The previous `staleTime: 0`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and `retry: false` options are dropped, so defaults now apply (window-focus refetch, retries). `isLoading` is now mapped to `isFetching`, which flickers on background refetches. The environment filter is also removed from the request.

title: isVisualize now requires `yAxis` string, breaking detection of JSON-form visualizes
body: The `isVisualize` check changed from `yAxes` to `yAxis`. Plain `BaseVisualize` objects, such as the output of `toJSON()`, are no longer recognized. The same applies to saved-query data or any caller still passing `{yAxes: [...]}`. The `findAllFieldRefs` fix works around this by switching to `isBaseVisualize`, but other call sites may regress. A multi-yAxes `BaseVisualize` is also now silently expanded into several charts (`fromJSON` now returns an array), which changes saved-query and URL behavior.

title: Analytics event name changed with no registration for the old name
body: `replay.view_html` becomes `replay.view-html` here. This is consistent with `replayAnalyticsEvents`, but the event name change breaks any downstream dashboards or queries on the old name. Mention it, or keep the old name.

title: Unguarded `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` access raises KeyError
body: The sender check does `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` with no guard. `sender` is only stored when the installation webhook (or `build_integration`) supplied it. Integrations created earlier, or created without a sender, will have no `sender` key. In that case the installation view raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the friendly error page. If a missing sender is meant to fail closed, it should be handled explicitly with `.get()` and rendered through `error()`.

title: GitHub user validation is skipped when the Integration row does not exist yet
body: If `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises DoesNotExist, the view calls `pipeline.next_step()` immediately. The `github_authenticated_user` comparison only runs when the Integration row already exists, i.e. after the installation webhook has been processed. If the user returns to Sentry before the webhook arrives, or the webhook is delayed or lost, the check is bypassed. The OAuth step is then pointless, because the authenticated user is never compared with the installer. That fail-open path undermines the security fix.

title: Network and HTTP errors in the OAuth exchange are not handled
body: `safe_urlopen(...)` is called outside the try/except. A connection error, timeout or blocked host will propagate as a 500. `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is also unguarded. It performs a GitHub API call that can raise on HTTP errors (rate limit, 5xx, revoked token), and it can return a body that is not a dict. The PR description says the pipeline should fail with the standard error page, but these paths produce unhandled exceptions.

title: OAuth authorize URL is built without URL-encoding
body: The `state` and `redirect_uri` values are interpolated directly into the query string with an f-string. They should be encoded with `urlencode`. The redirect URI contains `://` and `/`, and the test even asserts the unencoded form. This works only because the current values happen to be safe. It is fragile if the signature format or host ever contains reserved characters.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the installation-not-found path
body: The test now sends a hard-coded `state` of `ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`, which differs from the pipeline signature. The failure therefore comes from the state-mismatch check in `OAuthLoginView`, and the flow never reaches `build_integration`. The assertion changed from 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' to the generic 'Invalid installation request.', so the 404 handling for a missing installation is no longer covered. There is also no dedicated test for state mismatch, a failed token exchange, or missing `login` in the user info response.

title: Brittle assertion on the index of the recorded HTTP call
body: `responses.calls[2]` assumes the exact number and order of outbound calls made by the OAuth step (token exchange, `/user`, then the JWT call). Any change to that sequence silently breaks the test or checks the wrong request. Filtering the calls by URL would be more robust.

title: KeyError when existing Integration has no `sender` in metadata
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes the `sender` key is always present. It is only set by the installation webhook, and `build_integration` only adds a string `state["sender"]` when one exists. An existing Integration created before this change, or one whose webhook has not arrived or lacked a sender, raises KeyError. The result is a 500 in the install pipeline instead of the friendly error. Use `.get()` chaining and treat a missing value as a mismatch.

title: GitHub user is not validated when no Integration row exists yet
body: When `Integration.DoesNotExist` is raised, the code goes straight to `pipeline.next_step()`. The authenticated GitHub user obtained in OAuthLoginView is never compared with anyone. The sender check only runs for an already existing Integration. If the installation webhook has not been processed yet, or the Integration was removed, anyone can attach another account's `installation_id` to their org. This is the attack the PR is meant to stop.

title: Token exchange and user-info calls can raise and cause a 500
body: `safe_urlopen` is outside the try/except, so a network error or timeout propagates as an unhandled exception. `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is also unguarded. A failing GitHub API call, or a response that is not a dict, is not turned into the intended error page. Only the body read and parse are wrapped, so the PR's promise to fail gracefully in these cases is not met.

title: Authorize URL built without URL-encoding parameters
body: `state` and `redirect_uri` are interpolated directly into the query string with no encoding. This works with the current values, but it is fragile. `redirect_uri` is a full URL, so it should go through `urlencode`.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests a missing installation
body: The test now submits a hardcoded, different `state` (`ddd023d8...`) and asserts "Invalid installation request.". That error comes from the state/signature mismatch (or a missing pipeline), not from the 404 installation lookup. The original assertion about "The GitHub installation could not be found." was dropped, so the 404 path in `build_integration` is untested. There are also no tests for a failed token exchange, a missing `login`, or a missing `sender` in metadata.

title: User validation is skipped when no Integration row exists yet
body: The authenticated-user check only runs at the end of `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, after an `Integration` row is found with no `OrganizationIntegration`. If `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist`, the code returns `pipeline.next_step()` at line 482 without comparing the OAuth user to the installer. This happens when the installation webhook hasn't arrived or processed yet. An attacker who knows an installation id can then bind it to their own org, which is the attack the PR is meant to stop. The sender is only available once the webhook has created the Integration, so the check is racy and bypassable. The `github_authenticated_user` state is only used in the narrow already-exists branch.

title: Unguarded integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] can raise KeyError
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes that `sender` and `login` exist. Integrations created before this change, or by a webhook without a sender, have no `sender` key. Those users would get a 500 instead of the friendly error page. Use `.get` and fail closed with `error(...)` when the sender is missing.

title: Network errors in the OAuth token exchange and user lookup are unhandled
body: `safe_urlopen(...)` is called outside the try/except. Only the body read and parse are guarded. A connection error or timeout to github.com raises and produces a 500 rather than the install-failed page. `get_user_info(...)` is also unguarded. The PR says all token failures show the error page, but these paths do not.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the installation-not-found path
body: The assertion changed from "The GitHub installation could not be found." to "Invalid installation request.", and a state-based callback request was added. The test now hits the generic invalid-request error (a state/pipeline mismatch) and never reaches `build_integration`'s 404 handling. The 404 stub is no longer exercised, so the behavior it was written for is untested. The test name is also misleading.

title: No positive test for matching user, wrong state, or failed token exchange
body: New tests cover only the mismatching-user case. There is no test where an existing Integration with a sender matches the OAuth user and the install succeeds. There is no test for a `state` mismatch, for a failed `access_token` exchange, or for a missing `sender` in metadata. In the success flows the Integration doesn't exist yet, so the comparison branch is never exercised. `assert_setup_flow` also relies on the brittle index `responses.calls[2]`.

title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once, when the class is defined. Every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit value gets the same process-start timestamp. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. The `to_dict` test only checks that `queued` is not None, so it does not catch this.

title: `to_dict` puts a raw datetime in the Celery task kwargs, which breaks serialization and the round trip
body: `asdict(self)` leaves `queued` as a `datetime`. `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes this dict as `kwargs` to `apply_async`.
