body: Throwing a generic Error yields an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR response and gets logged as a server fault. A missing or foreign credential should throw TRPCError with code NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN so clients and monitoring get correct semantics.

title: Cache actions shown only for GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TYPE; delegation cache delete impossible
body: hasCache requires integrationType === GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TYPE and a truthy cacheUpdatedAt. For delegation credentials (negative or in-memory ids) the cache is keyed by user rather than credentialId. The status lookup and deleteCache (which looks up the credential in the DB) will not work for them. Also, `hasCache` is typed Date|null|false|undefined, and the date passes through tRPC serialization.

title: Pointless updateMany with empty data on every cache refresh
body: updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}) runs after every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache. With empty data, Prisma's @updatedAt may still bump the timestamps, but the intent is unclear. It adds a write per webhook and the value is never displayed, since the UI uses CalendarCache.updatedAt. The PR notes even admit this is unneeded. It should be removed.

title: Upsert update does not reliably bump updatedAt
body: The cache status shows the max updatedAt of CalendarCache rows, which depends on the upsert update touching the row. Prisma's @updatedAt is set automatically on update, so this works. However, the migration's DEFAULT NOW() makes all existing rows appear 'just updated' at deploy time, so the displayed last-updated time is misleading for legacy rows.

title: macOS-only sed -i '' and unrelated dev script
body: `sed -i ''` fails on GNU/Linux sed, where it treats '' as the file name. The relative ENV_FILE path depends on cwd. The script is also unrelated to this feature and slipped into the PR.

title: Generic Error thrown instead of TRPCError
body: A plain `Error` is thrown when the credential is missing or not owned by the user, so tRPC maps it to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN. This also pollutes error monitoring. Throw `TRPCError` with the appropriate code.

title: Cache deletion does not refresh the connected calendars query
body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. It never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. The cache status entry therefore keeps showing the old `cacheUpdatedAt` and the 'Delete cached data' option stays visible, even though the cache is gone. The disconnect mutation does invalidate; this one should too.

title: Pointless updateMany with empty data
body: `updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {})` relies on Prisma `@updatedAt` behaviour for an empty update. Prisma may skip the write or touch every SelectedCalendar row for the credential, and each cache refresh issues this extra DB write. The UI uses CalendarCache.updatedAt rather than SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, so the extra write has no consumer.

title: macOS-only sed -i syntax and unrelated script
body: `sed -i ''` works only on BSD/macOS sed. On GNU/Linux it treats '' as the script and fails. The script is also unrelated to this feature, and it uses a relative `../.env` path that depends on the working directory.

title: Hardcoded en-US date locale
body: The timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded "en-US" locale instead of the user's locale, so non-English users see US-formatted dates.

title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError
body: A generic `Error` becomes an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500). Not found or access denied should be a `TRPCError` with code NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN. Otherwise the error is logged and reported as a server fault, and clients cannot distinguish it from a real failure.

title: Delegation credentials can get the delete-cache action, but the handler rejects them
body: `hasCache` only checks the Google type and `cacheUpdatedAt`. Delegation credentials have in-memory negative IDs and are not in the Credential table. The server handler looks up `credential.findFirst({ userId })` and will throw for them. The UI can offer an action that always fails with a generic error toast.

title: Cache status ignores the calendar-cache feature flag
body: The handler constructs the real `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of using the `CalendarCache.init` factory. That factory returns the mock when caching is disabled. The status query therefore always hits the DB. It also reports stale cache rows even when the feature is off. Delegation credentials have negative IDs and will never match any rows.

title: updateMany with empty data does not bump updatedAt reliably
body: `updateManyByCredentialId(id, {})` sends an empty data object. Prisma may skip the update, or may not apply `@updatedAt`, so the call can be a no-op. It also touches every SelectedCalendar row for the credential on each cache refresh, which adds write load for no displayed benefit (the PR notes the UI doesn't use it).

title: macOS-only sed -i syntax in a committed script
body: `sed -i ''` works only with BSD/macOS sed. On GNU/Linux it treats `''` as the script and fails, so the env file is not updated. The script is also unrelated to this feature and has no documentation.

title: Hard-coded en-US date formatting
body: The timestamp is formatted with a fixed "en-US" locale instead of the user's locale, so non-English users see US-style dates.

title: Cron deletes past-due reminders before cancelling flagged ones
body: The unconditional deleteMany of reminders with scheduledDate <= now runs before the cancellation lookup, and the cancel step only covers scheduledDate within the next hour. A cancelled reminder is only cancelled in SendGrid once it is inside that 1-hour window. If the cron is missed, or a booking is cancelled less than 15 minutes before the send, the row is deleted without the cancel call and the email still goes out. Cancel flagged rows before the cleanup, and make the cleanup skip them.

title: One failed SendGrid call aborts all remaining cancellations and swallows the error
body: The whole loop sits in a single try/catch. If client.request throws for one reminder, the loop exits and the deletions already queued in workflowRemindersToDelete are never awaited. Later reminders are skipped for this run. The Prisma deletes are also lazy promises that only execute at Promise.all. Handle errors per reminder. Also, remindersToCancel is not filtered by method, so SMS reminders flagged cancelled would be sent to SendGrid (SMS deletion currently deletes the row directly, so this is latent).

title: client.setApiKey is never called in the cron module
body: The cron handler now uses the @sendgrid/client `client`, but the file only calls sgMail.setApiKey. Authentication relies on emailReminderManager having been imported in the same process, which is not guaranteed. If the key is unset, the cancel requests fail with 401, and the error is swallowed by the catch.

title: Reminders with no referenceId are deleted, but unscheduled ones may be sent later
body: When referenceId is null, the row is simply deleted. This is right for unscheduled rows. In the non-immediate path, a reminder that was scheduled and flagged cancelled is only cancelled by the cron. The cron's 1-hour window means reminders flagged less than an hour before send depend on a 15-minute cron running successfully. There is no fallback if SendGrid cancellation fails, since the row is then left flagged until the date passes and gets deleted by the cleanup.

title: Unrelated whitespace changes inside a commented-out block
body: The diff strips indentation across the large commented-out testAction block. It is unrelated to the fix and adds noise to review and blame.

title: Unrelated UI change removes sender ID rendering inside the phone block
body: This change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose. The wrapper condition changes from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded only. The sender section is separately rendered below, so the visible effect should be neutral, but it is an unexplained refactor mixed into a bug fix.

title: Cron deletes reminders whose scheduled date has passed before cancelling them
body: The existing `deleteMany` for all EMAIL reminders with `scheduledDate <= now` runs before the new cancellation query. A cancelled reminder whose date falls within the last cron interval is already gone. The cancellation window is the next hour, but the cron runs every 15 minutes, so for emails scheduled between cron runs it is mostly fine. However, if a cron run is missed or delayed, SendGrid is never told to cancel and the email is sent. Cancellation should run before this delete, or the delete should exclude cancelled rows.

title: One SendGrid failure aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders
body: The loop awaits `client.request` inside a single try/catch. If one request fails (e.g. a bad batch_id or the 100-pending-cancellation limit), the loop exits and every later reminder is skipped until the next run. Nothing is deleted from the DB either, because `Promise.all` is never reached, even for reminders already cancelled at SendGrid. Handle errors per reminder. Also, `remindersToCancel` has no `method: EMAIL` filter and could include SMS reminders that have no valid batch id.

title: SendGrid client API key is never set in the cron handler
body: This file calls `client.request`, but only `sgMail.setApiKey` is called at the top. `client.setApiKey` is called in emailReminderManager, and the cron handler already relies on `client.request` for `/v3/mail/batch`. It works only if that module happens to be imported in the same process. Set the key explicitly here.

title: Reminder with no referenceId is deleted even if scheduled and not yet sent, and unscheduled rows never get a cancel
body: When `referenceId` is null the row is deleted, which is correct for unscheduled reminders. For scheduled reminders that are marked cancelled but later fall inside the 72h cron flow, cancellation relies on the cron only seeing `cancelled: true` rows. Unscheduled cancelled rows are removed immediately, so that case is fine. But `immediateDelete` cancels at SendGrid yet never deletes or marks the DB row. The stale reminder stays and is later removed only by the past-date cleanup.

title: Reminder deletion promises are not awaited
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but called without await or collection into the `Promise.all`. Previously the DB deletes were awaited. Now the handler can return, and a serverless runtime may freeze, before the DB update or delete or the Twilio cancel completes. Reminders may then stay uncancelled and still be sent. The same applies to bookings.tsx, handleNewBooking.ts and workflows.tsx.

title: Workflow delete only handles scheduled reminders with immediateDelete, leaving cascade race
body: On workflow delete, the immediate SendGrid cancel is fired un-awaited and then the workflow is deleted, which cascades to the reminders. The `immediateDelete` path never touches the DB row, which is fine, but errors are only logged and the request is not blocked. This is also what consumes the 100-cancellation limit the PR is trying to avoid.

title: Unrelated reformatting inside commented-out block
body: The diff strips indentation across a large commented-out testAction block. It is noise unrelated to the fix and makes review and blame harder. The `Prisma` and `PrismaPromise` imports were also changed from type imports to value imports without need.

title: Blanket delete of past reminders removes cancelled reminders before they are cancelled in SendGrid
body: The existing `deleteMany` removes every EMAIL reminder whose scheduledDate is in the past. It runs before the new cancel step, so those rows never reach it. The cancel query only picks up cancelled reminders scheduled within the next hour. Cancelled reminders that sit in the 1-72h window and are only picked up later are fine. But a cron run that is skipped or delayed past the send time deletes the row and the email still goes out. The delete also doesn't touch the SendGrid batch. The cancel step should run before this cleanup, or the cleanup should skip rows with cancelled=true.

title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole batch and orphan rows are never cleaned
body: All cancel requests share a single try/catch. If one `client.request` throws (for example the 100 pending-cancellation limit, or a bad batch id), the loop exits. The remaining cancelled reminders are skipped for that run, and the prisma deletes collected in the array are never awaited, so even the already-cancelled rows are not removed. The array of deletes is also built lazily and awaited only at the end, so a failure loses them. The failure is only logged. The cancel and delete should be handled per reminder inside the loop.

title: Cancel query is not limited to EMAIL and null referenceId is not excluded
body: `findMany` filters only on cancelled and scheduledDate. It does not filter on method=EMAIL or on referenceId being non-null. Cancelled rows with a null referenceId would send `batch_id: null` to SendGrid. This cron also never calls `client.setApiKey`. That is done in emailReminderManager, which this file doesn't import, so the request may be unauthenticated depending on module load order.

title: Rescheduled/cancelled reminders scheduled less than an hour out can still be sent
body: Non-immediate deletion only sets cancelled=true. The cron runs every 15 minutes but only cancels reminders within the next hour. The reminder time is not checked here, so a reminder scheduled in under an hour is only cancelled on the next cron run. Because the row is not deleted and the cancel is deferred, a window remains where the email is still sent. Also, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is not awaited by callers, so failures are silent.

title: Fire-and-forget reminder deletion races with attendee/booking deletes
body: The `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` calls are neither awaited nor included in `Promise.all`. The SMS delete removes the row by id with no existing check. The bookings' reminders may also be cascade-deleted concurrently, so the delete can throw and is swallowed by the catch. The process can also end before the calls finish (serverless), leaving the reminders uncancelled.

title: immediateDelete cancels in SendGrid but leaves the DB row
body: With immediateDelete=true the SendGrid cancel is sent but the workflowReminder row is not deleted or marked cancelled. For the workflow-delete path the cascade covers it. For the reschedule path in handleNewBooking the row is left behind, uncancelled, with scheduled=true. The cron later deletes it once its date passes, but the semantics are inconsistent.

title: Unrelated whitespace changes in commented-out code
body: The diff strips indentation inside the commented-out testAction block, which adds noise. The `Prisma` import is also now a value import that is unused.

title: getCalendarCredentials stores un-awaited promises in the result
body: getCalendar is now async, so `calendar` in each returned item is a Promise<Calendar|null>. Only getConnectedCalendars awaits it. Other callers of getCalendarCredentials that use `.calendar` directly (for example the availability code) will now get a Promise and fail or silently misbehave. The inferred type of the `calendar` field changed with no compile-time check at those call sites. The calendar should be resolved before it is returned, or every consumer must be audited.

title: async forEach callback makes errors unhandled and un-awaited
body: Converting the forEach callback to async means the returned promises are never awaited. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from getCalendar or deleteEvent, so a failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Reschedule continues and returns before calendar and video deletions finish, which is risky in serverless runtimes. The same pattern is repeated in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and in trpc bookings.tsx requestReschedule. Use `await Promise.all(refs.map(...))` instead.

title: async forEach pushes to apiDeletes after it has been awaited
body: The recurring-cancel branch uses `forEach(async ...)`. It now awaits getCalendar before it reaches the loop that pushes into apiDeletes. Because forEach does not wait, `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs while apiDeletes is still empty. The calendar deletions for recurring bookings are therefore not awaited, can be dropped, and may reject unhandled. Previously the callback ran synchronously up to the first await. Use a for...of loop.

title: Dynamic imports are started eagerly at module load
body: Every `import(...)` in the appStore object literal runs when the module is first imported. All 29 apps are loaded immediately, so this is not lazy loading. Any failing app import becomes an unhandled rejection at startup. Making each entry a function such as `() => import(...)` would give real lazy loading.

title: getCalendarCredentials stores un-awaited promises and other callers are not updated
body: getCalendar is now async, so `calendar` in getCalendarCredentials is a Promise. Only getConnectedCalendars was updated to await it. The returned type has changed from Calendar|null to Promise<Calendar|null>. Any other consumer that reads `.calendar` directly, such as availability or other routers, will call methods on a Promise or treat it as always truthy. Those callers should be audited, or the function should resolve the promises itself.

title: Dynamic imports are created eagerly, so nothing is lazy
body: Every entry is `import(...)` evaluated at module load. Importing appStore therefore kicks off loading all ~29 app packages immediately, which defeats the purpose of lazy loading. Also, a single failing import produces an unhandled rejection at startup, and rejects every later await of that key. Use functions such as `() => import(...)` to make the loading lazy.

title: async forEach makes the try/catch ineffective and the deletions fire-and-forget
body: The callback is now async, so `forEach` neither awaits it nor propagates its rejections. The surrounding try/catch can never catch errors from getCalendar, deleteEvent or deleteMeeting. Failures become unhandled promise rejections. The emails are sent without waiting for the deletions to complete. The same pattern is duplicated in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and in trpc bookings.tsx. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` instead.

title: async forEach pushes to apiDeletes after it has been awaited
body: The recurring-event branch uses `forEach(async ...)`, which is not awaited. `apiDeletes.push` happens after the awaited getCalendar and deleteEvent calls. Because deleteEvent is awaited inside the callback, the pushed values are already-resolved results, not pending promises. `Promise.all(apiDeletes)` runs before the pushes, so calendar deletions for recurring bookings are not waited on. Errors become unhandled rejections, and the response can return before the deletions finish. This pattern was made more broken by the PR's added await. Replace it with a for...of loop.

title: getCalendarCredentials stores un-awaited promises; other callers use calendar synchronously
body: getCalendar is now async, so `calendar` in getCalendarCredentials is a Promise. getConnectedCalendars was updated to await it, but any other consumer of getCalendarCredentials (e.g. in the app or trpc code, not shown in this diff) that reads `.calendar` synchronously will call methods on a Promise and fail at runtime. The return type changed silently and should be audited or made explicit.

title: async forEach callback: errors escape try/catch and the deletes are not awaited
body: The forEach callback is now async, so rejections from getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting become unhandled promise rejections. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch them. The function proceeds to send emails and return before the calendar and video deletions finish. In serverless environments the work may be cut off. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` inside the try. The same issue exists in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and trpc bookings.tsx requestReschedule.

title: async forEach pushes to apiDeletes after it has already been awaited
body: In the recurring cancellation branch the async forEach callback awaits getCalendar and then pushes into apiDeletes. Previously the getCalendar call was synchronous, so the callback body ran up to the first await. Now the push happens after the await, and the handler's `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` snapshots the array before those pushes. Recurring calendar deletions are never awaited, may silently fail, and may be dropped in serverless runtimes. Replace with a for...of loop or Promise.all over the credentials.

title: Dynamic imports are started eagerly at module load, so nothing is lazy
body: Each entry is `import(...)` evaluated when the object literal is built. Importing appStore therefore starts loading all ~29 apps immediately, with the same total cost as before, and a failing import becomes an unhandled rejection at load time. Real lazy loading needs thunks like `() => import(...)` or a lookup function. This PR changes the API to promises without delivering the intended benefit.

title: Working-hours check compares start to start, so the end bound is never enforced
body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` (same expression as `start`) rather than from the slot end time. The check `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore only tests the slot start, and slots that run past the end of working hours are accepted. Also, `workingHours.find` returns true if any one working-hour entry fails, so a user with several entries on one day (split shifts) is rejected for every slot outside any single entry. Working hours are in the organizer's tz minutes but are compared to UTC slot minutes without any conversion. The check is likely wrong and could wrongly drop valid slots.

title: Dead comparison of Dayjs objects with ===
body: `dayjs(a) === dayjs(b)` compares object references and is always false. The intended zero-length override (unavailable day) case is never handled. A day marked unavailable with start equal to end is therefore not blocked here, since the following isBefore/isAfter checks do not catch it either.

title: Override offset logic is fragile and breaks across day boundaries
body: The offset is derived from tz offsets at `override.start`, then hour/minute are taken after shifting. If the shift crosses midnight, the start or end wraps to a different day and the minutes-of-day value ends up with endTime < startTime (the slot loop skips start >= end). The override then yields no slots. Also `dayjs(override.start.toString())` reparses a locale-dependent Date string; use the Date directly. The `activeOverrides` filter still selects by the unshifted UTC start, so the day matching is inconsistent with the shifted times.

title: Override day comparison done in UTC after shifting by a sign-flipped offset
body: The override date is shifted by `-offset` of the organizer timezone and then compared by UTC calendar date to the slot's UTC date. For invitees in other timezones, or for overrides near midnight, the match can fall on the wrong day. `dateOverrideExist` is also set before the range checks, so a slot on a matching date but outside the override range is rejected. Inconsistent with the invitee-tz handling in getSlots.

title: Working-hours check uses identical start and end values
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, `start` and `end` are both computed as `slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute()`. `end` should use the slot end time. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends past them is therefore never rejected. The check is also in UTC minutes and ignores the organizer timezone, so it can wrongly reject valid slots for hosts whose working hours cross midnight in UTC. Slots can be wrongly dropped or wrongly accepted.

title: Dead comparison between Dayjs objects
body: `dayjs(a) === dayjs(b)` compares object references, so it is always false. The zero-length override case (a day fully blocked) is never handled by this branch. Use `.isSame()`.

title: Date override matching and offset are fragile
body: The offset is computed with `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone)`, which reinterprets the Date as a local time in that zone rather than converting an instant. The sign handling is therefore likely wrong, and DST may be applied incorrectly. The override day is then compared by UTC date string against the slot's UTC date. For invitee timezones far from the organizer, or slots near midnight UTC, the override can be matched to the wrong day, or an override that spans UTC midnight is partly ignored. Only the +5:30 and +6:00 zones are tested.

title: Override offset can wrap across midnight and breaks the day filter
body: The override start and end are shifted by the offset and reduced to hour*60+minute. If the shift crosses midnight, endTime becomes smaller than startTime, or the override moves to the neighbouring day. The result is that the override produces no slots (start >= end is skipped). `activeOverrides` is still filtered using the unshifted UTC start. Also `dayjs(override.start.toString())` goes through a locale string and loses milliseconds and timezone information; use `dayjs(override.start)`.

title: Timezone test does not verify the behaviour it claims to
body: The new test passes a different invitee timezone but expects identical UTC slots, so it would pass even if timezone handling were broken. The fixed-host date override fix for round robin has no test at all.

title: Working-hours check compares the same value twice and uses inverted logic
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, `start` and `end` are both computed as `slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute()`. The slot's end time is never used, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after them passes. The `.find` returns true when the slot is OUTSIDE a single working-hours entry. With several entries for the same day (multiple users or split hours), a slot inside one range but outside another is rejected. Working hours are also compared in UTC minutes against the UTC day, so ranges crossing midnight in UTC are mishandled. Net effect: availability is wrongly rejected or accepted.

title: Object identity comparison is always false
body: `dayjs(a) === dayjs(b)` compares two distinct object references, so it is never true. The intended zero-length override check (start equals end) is dead code. A day blocked by an override with start equal to end would not be treated as unavailable by this branch.

title: Date override matching is by UTC calendar day and the offset sign is questionable
body: The override's start is shifted by minus the organizer's utcOffset (taken at that instant) and its date string is compared to the slot's UTC date. This mixes organizer-local and UTC days. Overrides that span midnight in UTC, or whose UTC date differs from the organizer's local date, will not match the slots they apply to. An override that exists on a day never blocks slots after `date.end` on a neighbouring UTC day. Only the first matching override is considered, because `find` stops at the first true result. With multiple overrides on one day (the same user's several ranges, or different users'), a slot inside one range can be rejected because another range returned true first.

title: Override offset uses the invitee's current-day timezone and wraps minutes modulo 24h
body: The offset is computed from `dayjs(override.start.toString())`. `Date.toString()` is a locale string, so parsing it is non-ISO and can be unreliable and lossy. The shifted start/end are then reduced to hour*60+minute, which wraps at midnight. When the shift crosses a day boundary, endTime can end up smaller than startTime and the override produces no slots. The filter on activeOverrides still compares override.start in UTC to the invitee's day, so it is not timezone-adjusted. Also, `override.timeZone` may be undefined, which makes `.tz(undefined)` use the local timezone.

title: Timezone test expects identical output, so it does not verify the fix
body: The new test requests the +6:00 timezone but expects the same UTC slots as for +5:30, and the comment says so. The PR claims override slots should shift with the invitee timezone. The test only checks that slots are keyed by UTC date, so it passes without exercising the changed offset logic. There is also no test for the fixed-host round-robin date override scenario that the PR targets.

title: Category fabricators deleted and replaced with embeddable_host fabricator
body: The diff replaces the entire contents of category_fabricator.rb (the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators) with the :embeddable_host fabricator. The category fabricators are re-added in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, so the two files look swapped. The :embeddable_host fabricator is defined in this file, which now has the wrong name for its contents. Fabrication loads every file in the directory, so the specs may still pass, but the files no longer match the fabricators they define, which is confusing and fragile.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting is absent
body: The query is `execute(...)[0]['id']`. When no `embed_category` row exists, which is the default because the setting defaulted to '', the result set is empty. `[0]` is then nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, so the migration fails on most installs. The line 15 lookup of `uncategorized_category_id` has the same risk. The fallback `if category_id == 0` is never reached.

title: Unescaped host value interpolated into SQL
body: The host strings from the old site setting are interpolated directly into the INSERT statement. A value containing a quote breaks the migration or allows SQL injection. Hosts are also not stripped of `http://` or whitespace, and `\r` is not handled, so migrated rows may fail the model's format validation.

title: Case-insensitive lookup compares against non-lowercased host
body: The query is `lower(host) = ?` but the bound value `uri.host` is not downcased. URL hosts with uppercase letters, such as `Example.com`, will not match. `URI()` does not normalise the case of the host.

title: before_validation mutates host in place and crashes on nil
body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when host is nil, for example when a request omits the param. `sub!` also mutates the string that was passed in. The format regex accepts a path, but the callback strips it first. `host_allowed?` also ignores the port, so a host saved with a port never matches.

title: Missing record causes nil errors (500) in update/destroy
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: ...).first` returns nil for an unknown id. `save_host(nil)` and `host.destroy` then raise NoMethodError and the response is a 500 instead of a 404. A missing `params[:embeddable_host]` also raises.

title: Save sends the key `host` but the buffered value is wrapped incorrectly
body: On a new record `categoryId` is never initialised because only `edit` sets it. The server falls back to the uncategorized category instead of the chosen one. The `delete` action also calls `sendAction` after the record is destroyed, with no error handling.

title: saveChanges does nothing useful
body: `saveChanges` calls `update({})`, and the server `update` action does nothing but re-render. It is also not referenced from the template.

title: Category fabricators deleted and replaced with embeddable_host fabricator
body: category_fabricator.rb now defines only :embeddable_host, and the real :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. The files appear to have been swapped by mistake. Fabricator load order is fine, but the file naming is wrong and confusing. If the fabricators are loaded by filename convention, or either file is later cleaned up, every spec that uses Fabricate(:category) breaks.

title: Migration crashes when the embed_category setting is absent
body: execute(...)[0]['id'] is called on a query result that is empty when no embed_category site setting exists, which is the default because the value was ''. [0] returns nil, so nil['id'] raises NoMethodError and the migration fails on most installs. The uncategorized fallback is never reached. The same applies to the uncategorized_category_id lookup if that row is missing.

title: Unescaped SQL interpolation of host values
body: Host values taken from site settings are interpolated directly into the INSERT with no quoting, so a host containing a quote breaks the migration or allows SQL injection. Values with an http:// prefix or a path are also inserted unnormalized because model callbacks are bypassed. Use connection.quote. Also, blank lines and \r from the split are not stripped.

title: before_validation raises on nil host and mutates in place
body: self.host.sub! is called with no nil check, so a nil host (for example a missing param) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. In-place sub! on the attribute string also mutates it without dirty tracking.

title: Host lookup is case-sensitive on the URI side and ignores ports
body: The query compares lower(host) to uri.host without downcasing the input. URI#host is not lowercased, so a referer such as http://EvilTrout.com never matches. Also, the validation allows a host with a port or path, but the before_validation strips only the path, while the lookup compares against the host without a port, so host entries with ports never match.

title: update and destroy dereference nil when the id is not found
body: EmbeddableHost.where(id:).first returns nil for an unknown id, and then save_host(nil) or nil.destroy raises NoMethodError, giving a 500 instead of a 404. Use find. Also, params[:embeddable_host] being absent raises.

title: Save does not update the host display from the buffer
body: save sends the buffered props, but after success the host's `host` property is only updated if the store applies the server response. Any server-side normalization, such as http:// stripping, depends on the response being applied. Also, cantSave only checks the host is non-empty, so a new host can be saved with no category.

title: update action is a no-op
body: The update action just re-renders the embedding without changing anything. The route and the JS saveChanges call exist but do nothing.

title: replace only swaps the first underscore
body: type.replace('_', '-') uses a string pattern, so only the first underscore is replaced. Types with multiple underscores will not match ADMIN_MODELS.

title: Category fabricators overwritten by embeddable_host fabricator
body: This file previously defined :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category. The diff replaces all of them with the :embeddable_host fabricator. The same category fabricators are re-added in spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, so the two files look swapped. Fabricator loading may still work, but :embeddable_host is now defined in two places and the file names no longer match their contents. Any load-order or duplicate-definition problem would break most of the test suite.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting row is absent
body: The query `execute(...)[0]['id']` indexes the first row of the result. On a default install there is no `embed_category` row in site_settings (the default was ''), so the result is empty and `[0]` is nil. `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError and the migration fails. The `category_id == 0` fallback below it is never reached. The uncategorized_category_id lookup on line 15 has the same problem if that row is missing.

title: Unescaped SQL interpolation and unnormalized hosts in migration
body: Host values from the old setting are interpolated directly into the INSERT statement with no quoting. A value containing a single quote breaks the migration, and it is also an injection vector. The values are also not stripped of http(s):// or trailing whitespace, so old entries such as 'http://eviltrout.com' are stored as-is. The model normalizes hosts only on validation, so these migrated rows would never match in `host_allowed?`. The migration also uses `change` with irreversible deletes and data work.

title: Host lookup is case-inconsistent and breaks on uri.host being nil
body: The query compares `lower(host)` with the unlowered `uri.host`. URI normally downcases the host, but stored values are not downcased on save and `lower(host)` is only applied to the column. `record_for_host` returns `false` rather than nil on failure, which is inconsistent. Hosts with ports are stored with the port (the validation regex allows it) but are compared against `uri.host`, which has no port, so those entries never match.

title: before_validation mutates nil/frozen host
body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when host is nil, for example when the params key is missing. It also mutates the string in place. The controller reads `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, so a request without a host gives a 500 error instead of a validation error.

title: Nil host record on update/destroy yields 500
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: ...).first` returns nil for an unknown id. `save_host(nil)` and `host.destroy` then raise NoMethodError, producing a 500 where a 404 would be correct. Use `find`, or return a not-found response.

title: update action is a no-op
body: `update` ignores its params and just re-renders the embedding. The client's `saveChanges` calls it with an empty hash, so nothing is persisted.

title: Save sends 'host' key and sets category from client lookup
body: `getProperties('host')` on the buffer returns `{host: ...}`, and `host.save(props)` is then called with it. The component's buffer is also not committed back to the model on success, so the displayed host text stays stale after an edit. The category is set from `Discourse.Category.findById` instead of from the server response.

title: replace only swaps first underscore
body: `type.replace('_', '-')` with a string pattern replaces only the first underscore. A type name with more than one underscore would not match ADMIN_MODELS.

title: Second `downsize` definition overrides the 5-arg version
body: Ruby has no overloading, so the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Existing callers that pass width and height separately will now treat max_height as `opts` (an Integer), and `opts[:allow_animation]` or `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` will raise or be ignored. Dimensions will also be wrong. The first definition is dead code. Keep one signature and update the callers.

title: Downsize loop can corrupt or ignore failures, and mishandles animated GIFs
body: The return value of `downsize` is ignored, so if convert fails the loop repeats 5 times for nothing. The in-place conversion (from == to) on a tempfile can also lose the original. After downsizing, `tempfile.size` may be stale, because `File#size` on a Tempfile can be cached or buffered. The upload then uses the old size. For GIFs the gifsicle path uses `--resize-fit` with "80%", which is not a valid dimension argument, so it fails. If the image is still too big after the loop, the upload goes ahead and is later rejected with a confusing error.

title: Hardcoded 10MB limit ignores the site settings
body: The client-side limit is now hardcoded to 10MB, so the `max_attachment_size_kb` setting is no longer enforced on the client. Admins who set a lower limit get no client-side validation. The 413 error message likewise shows 10MB instead of the real limit. The server-side download limit in the controller is also hardcoded to 10MB.

title: Second `downsize` definition overrides the (from,to,w,h,opts) version
body: Ruby has no overloading, so the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Existing callers that pass width and height separately will now have the height bound to `opts`. That raises errors or gives a wrong dimension string, and `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer or String will fail. The earlier definition is dead code and should be removed, with all callers checked.

title: Downsize loop can silently fail and does not enforce the limit
body: The return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored. If the conversion fails, the loop retries 5 times with no effect. `tempfile.size` may also be stale or buffered, and the loop assumes the file was rewritten in place. After the loop the file may still exceed `max_image_size_kb`, and nothing re-checks it. Each iteration also runs ImageOptim, which is expensive, all inside the request's deferred job. Oversized files rely on a later size check that no longer exists on the client.

title: Downsizing applies to non-image-type uploads and can break GIFs and other formats
body: `downsize` uses `convert from[0]` and writes back to the same path. Animated GIFs are reduced to the first frame unless the gifsicle path is taken. The animated path only triggers when the filename matches `/\.GIF$/i` on the temp path. Temp paths may have no extension, so animation is lost. Converting in place with the same input and output path is also risky.

title: Hardcoded 10MB limit ignores site settings
body: The client now ignores `max_image_size_kb` and `max_attachment_size_kb` and uses 10MB for every type, attachments included. Admins who set a lower attachment limit get no client-side validation. The server only downsizes images, so oversized attachments are no longer caught early. The 413 handler has the same hardcoded value.

title: Second `downsize` definition overrides the 5-arg version
body: Ruby has no overloading, so the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Existing callers that pass width and height separately now fail or misbehave. A call with 5 positional args raises ArgumentError. A call with 4 args treats max_height as `dimensions` and breaks the dimension string. The earlier definition is dead code and should be removed or renamed.

title: Downsizing loop may leave the file oversized and is not checked for failure
body: `downsize` returns false on failure, but the loop ignores it. It then retries up to 5 times on a failing or no-op conversion, which wastes time. Non-image-convertible or corrupt files proceed unchanged. After the loop, `tempfile.size` may be stale or cached, and the file can still exceed the limit. Upload.create_for then has to reject it, while the client-side check no longer matches the server setting. The 80% conversion also rewrites the file in place, so formats such as GIFs or PNGs may shrink very little.

title: Hard-coded 10MB limit replaces the site-setting limits
body: The client now uses a fixed 10MB limit for all types. This ignores `max_attachment_size_kb`, so attachments above the configured limit pass client validation and are rejected only by the server. Server-side limits are also not tied to this constant. The 413 handler is hard-coded the same way, so the error message may show a wrong limit.

title: API download limit hard-coded to 10MB
body: The API URL download limit no longer follows the site settings. Attachments get a 10MB limit regardless of configuration, and `max_attachment_size_kb` is ignored.

title: Unsubscribe crashes with nil TopicUser and changes state on a GET
body: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the user has no topic_users row, for example after watching via category settings or following a link from an old email. `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError and the user gets a 500. The action also mutates notification state on a GET, so link prefetchers or mail scanners can unsubscribe users. Use `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row if missing, or guard against nil.

title: Missing visibility and permission checks and user lookup
body: `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` is not wrapped in the `rescue Discourse::NotFound` handling that `show` has. The `show` action also removes notifications on `InvalidAccess`, which this action does not do. Separately, `ensure_logged_in` is applied, so a logged-out user clicking the email link gets a login error rather than a clear path to unsubscribing.

title: Added `render :show` changes the behaviour of `show`
body: `perform_show_response` is shared by `show`, but `render :show` is now added to its html branch. The branch previously relied on the implicit render. For the `unsubscribe` action this explicit render is needed, but it is a change to shared code and should be verified for `show`.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url} everywhere
body: `unsubscribe_link` is also used by other emails that set `add_unsubscribe_link` but do not pass `unsubscribe_url`. Examples are the digest, signup and other `build_email` callers. I18n raises MissingInterpolationArgument or leaves the placeholder in the body for those emails. The spec was patched to pass `unsubscribe_url` to work around this, which shows it is a real break.

title: Misspelled property name `stopNotificiationsText`
body: The property name `stopNotificiationsText` is misspelled. It is consistent with the template, so it works, but it will confuse maintainers. Rename it to `stopNotificationsText` in both files.

title: unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
body: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil if the user never visited or has no record for the topic. The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500. Use `TopicUser.change` or `find_or_create`, which also handles the unique-index race.

title: State-changing action on a GET request
body: `unsubscribe` is routed as GET and changes the notification level as a side effect. Email link scanners, prefetchers and crawlers will trigger it, and it is exposed to CSRF-style requests. It needs a confirmation step or a POST.

title: Missing topic and guardian handling; level cycles on each hit
body: `TopicView.new` is built with `current_user` before the user is checked, and `ensure_logged_in` only covers logged-in users, so a logged-out visitor to the emailed link gets a login error rather than a redirect back after login. The toggle is also not idempotent: a second hit (a reload, or a scanner) drops the user from regular to muted. The unsubscribe also skips `TopicUser.change`, so `notifications_changed_at`, the reason id and the MessageBus publish are not set.

title: Added `render :show` inside shared perform_show_response
body: This helper is also used by `show`. An explicit `render :show` in `format.html` changes behaviour for `show` and applies to any caller, which could cause double-render conflicts. It is needed here only because the template name differs for `unsubscribe`.

title: Route order, and a dropped constraint without explanation
body: `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` is defined before `t/:topic_id/:post_number`, which is fine. However, the `post_number` constraint was removed from the summary routes without explanation, and the line moves are unrelated churn.

title: Typo in property name, and an unescaped title rendered with triple-stash
body: `stopNotificiationsText` is misspelled, and the template uses it consistently. The template renders it with `{{{ }}}`, which is only safe because `fancyTitle` is escaped server-side. Any change to that would introduce XSS.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, which other callers don't pass
body: `unsubscribe_link` is also used by other emails that set `add_unsubscribe_link` without `unsubscribe_url`, such as digest or other builders. The missing interpolation argument will raise or render a broken link. The spec was patched to pass `unsubscribe_url`, which hides this.

title: unsubscribe dereferences a possibly nil TopicUser
body: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when the user has no topic_users row for this topic, for example a user who received a mailing-list email without ever visiting the topic. `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500. Use `TopicUser.change`, or create the row first, so the unsubscribe still works.

title: State change on a GET request with no CSRF protection
body: The unsubscribe action mutates the notification level on a GET request, so any link or image tag can trigger it. Mail scanners and link prefetchers that follow the link in the email will also mute or unwatch the topic without the user asking. The action also changes the level on every visit, not just once: a second visit flips regular to muted.

title: Guardian access check is missing for the topic
body: `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` is created without `check_and_raise_exceptions`, and the code never calls `guardian.ensure_can_see!`. The code also reads `@topic_view.topic` before any permission check.

title: Misspelled property name `stopNotificiationsText`
body: `stopNotificiationsText` is misspelled, and the template repeats the typo. It works only because the two match. The name should be fixed before it becomes API.

title: Triple-stash renders the topic title unescaped
body: `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` renders unescaped HTML that interpolates `model.fancyTitle`. This is probably safe only because `fancyTitle` is escaped server-side, but `I18n.t` interpolation of user-controlled titles into raw HTML is fragile.

title: Template path does not match the route name
body: The route is `topicUnsubscribe`, but the template is placed at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`. Ember resolves `topicUnsubscribe` to `templates/topicUnsubscribe` or `topic-unsubscribe`, so this template will probably not be found.

title: `unsubscribe_link` now needs `%{unsubscribe_url}` but not all callers pass it
body: The `unsubscribe_link` string now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but only `send_notification_email` passes it. Other users of `add_unsubscribe_link` would raise an I18n missing-interpolation error. The text body also appends the string with `<<` onto what may be a frozen translation.

title: Validator has a write side effect and runs on every validation
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and saves the record each time it is called. The validator runs on every `valid?`, and users_controller#create calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which validates again. A single signup attempt therefore bumps the counter twice, so the statistics are wrong. Validation should not write to the database.

title: Email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized
body: `where(email: email)` is an exact match. A blocked address can be bypassed by changing case (Bad@Spam.com) or adding whitespace. User emails are lowercased elsewhere via Email.downcase, but here neither the stored value nor the lookup is normalized.

title: Racy read-modify-write counter increment
body: `match_count += 1` followed by `save` is a lost-update race under concurrent signups. The save result is also ignored. An atomic `update_all` or `increment_counter` would avoid both problems.

title: Nil value passed to validator and uses `and`
body: The validator is applied with `if: :email_changed?` but a nil or blank email still reaches `value =~ regexp` and the BlockedEmail lookup. Using `and` instead of `&&` is also fragile. Add a blank guard, and note that `should_block?` can return nil, not just true or false.

title: Shared array on controller prototype
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is created once in the class definition, so every controller instance shares the same array. Rejected emails therefore persist across instances, and the array is never reset. It should be initialized in `init`.

title: Failure response echoes user attributes
body: The failure response now returns `errors` and `values` (name, username, email) back to the client. Combined with the client-side rejectedEmails logic, any email error, such as the uniqueness error, marks the email as rejected with the generic 'invalid' message. This hides the specific reason (taken, blocked, not allowed).

title: Validator has a side effect: it updates match_count on every validation
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and saves the record each time it is called. It is called from a validator that runs on every `valid?`/`save`. In UsersController#create, `user.valid?` runs and then `user.save` runs validations again, so each signup attempt counts twice. It also writes to the database from inside validation, which is unexpected and inflates the statistics.

title: Email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact match. A blocked address can be bypassed by changing the case (Spam@x.com vs spam@x.com) or adding whitespace. The email is not downcased on lookup or on storage. Also, `value` can be nil, which would query `email IS NULL`.

title: Racy read-modify-write of match_count
body: `match_count += 1` followed by `save` is a lost-update race under concurrent signups. It also skips the model's own validations and callbacks when saving. Use an atomic `update_all`/`increment_counter` instead.

title: Naming the validator EmailValidator may collide with other validators and does not handle nil values
body: The class name `EmailValidator` can shadow or collide with other email validators (for example, a gem's). `email_in_restriction_setting?` and `should_block?` are called with `value`, which may be nil. The user model's `presence` validation also runs, but the whitelist `=~` on nil silently flags the record as not allowed.

title: Shared mutable array on controller prototype
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined on the class prototype, so all instances of the controller share one array. Rejected emails persist across instances. Initialize it in `init` instead.

title: Validator has a write side effect and runs on every validation
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and saves the record on every call. Because the validator runs on any `valid?` call, one signup can be counted several times. In UsersController#create, `user.valid?` runs and then `user.save` validates again, so each attempt increments the count twice. The statistics are therefore inflated, and a validation step writes to the database even if the surrounding transaction is later rolled back.

title: Case-sensitive email lookup lets blocks be bypassed
body: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) is an exact, case-sensitive match. Email is neither downcased nor normalized when stored or looked up. A blocked address such as bad@spam.com is bypassed by Bad@Spam.com. The same normalization gap affects the uniqueness validation.

title: Racy read-modify-write on match_count
body: match_count += 1 followed by save is a read-modify-write on the Ruby side. Concurrent signups for the same email can lose updates. An atomic `increment_counter` or an SQL `UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1` avoids this.

title: Shared array literal in controller prototype
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is declared on the class prototype. The same array instance is therefore shared by all instances of the controller, and `pushObject` mutates it. Rejected emails persist across instances. It should be initialized in `init`.

title: Every email error marks the email as rejected
body: Any server-side email error, such as 'already taken', is treated as a rejected email. The client then shows the generic 'invalid' message instead of the server's reason. A transient error would also permanently reject that address in the client.

title: Embed access control relies on the spoofable Referer header and ALLOWALL framing
body: ensure_embeddable authorizes only by comparing the host of request.referer to embeddable_host. Referer is trivially forged by any non-browser client. It is also often stripped by privacy settings or Referrer-Policy, so legitimate embeds fail. The response then sets X-Frame-Options to ALLOWALL, which removes clickjacking protection for the page. A logged-in user visiting a malicious page could be framed. Because current_user is used, the framed content can include user-specific data.

title: Embed URL host is never validated in the controller before enqueuing a retrieve job
body: The `embed_url` param is passed to the retrieve_topic job without checking its host. Validation happens only inside the job (TopicRetriever.invalid_host?). Any request carrying the correct Referer can therefore enqueue arbitrary jobs. The controller spec expects TopicRetriever.new to be called synchronously, but the code enqueues a job, so that spec does not match the implementation.

title: Referer interpolated unescaped into inline JS and used as postMessage targetOrigin
body: `request.referer` is written into a JS string literal. ERB HTML-escapes it, but that is not JS escaping. A quote or backslash in the URL could break the literal. The full URL path is also not a valid targetOrigin, which must be an origin, so postMessage silently fails to deliver for any referer containing a path. As a result, the resize message never reaches the parent page.

title: Origin check uses substring indexOf
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test. An origin that happens to be a substring of discourseUrl (e.g. an empty or partial string) passes. It should be an exact origin comparison.

title: import mutates the caller's string and interpolates unescaped URL into raw HTML
body: `contents <<` mutates the argument in place. This also breaks on frozen strings. The sha1 is computed from the mutated content. The url is placed unescaped into an href in raw_html posts, which are not sanitized. Remote feed content is rendered as-is, creating a stored XSS risk.

title: Kernel#open on a URL (SSRF / command execution)
body: `open(url)` (and `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in poll_feed) uses Kernel#open. With open-uri this fetches arbitrary URLs. A value beginning with `|` would execute a shell command. The url ultimately comes from the embed_url request param. TopicRetriever restricts the host to embeddable_host, but Disqus import does not. Use URI.parse(url).open or an HTTP client instead.

title: Feed item content may be nil, and String#scrub is unavailable on older Ruby
body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no content, which aborts the whole poll. Entries that only have a description would fail. `scrub` also requires Ruby 2.1+. The unused feed_key method is dead code.

title: Non-atomic setnx plus expire
body: If the process dies between setnx and expire, the key never expires. That URL is then throttled forever. Use `set` with ex and nx, or setex.

title: Unrelated edit to an existing migration adds force: true
body: Editing a historical migration to add `force: true` makes it drop the existing top_topics table (and its data) if the migration is re-run. Changes unrelated to this feature should not be made to old migrations.

title: skip_validations now applies to all revisions
body: `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` is a sensible extension, but the post_revisor change is untested. Also, update_post does not handle raw_html cook_method specially, so cooked is recomputed in before_save via cook, which depends on cook_method being preserved. This is subtle, and no test covers updating an existing embedded post's cooked.

title: Referer-only host check is spoofable and sets X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL
body: Embedding authorization relies solely on the client-supplied Referer header, which non-browser clients can forge. The response is then marked X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL, so any site can frame it. A page can also be framed with no referer, which is rejected. The check is weak as an access control, and combined with ALLOWALL it is the only gate.

title: Controller spec expects TopicRetriever to be invoked, but the controller enqueues a job
body: The controller calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...), while the spec expects TopicRetriever.new/retrieve to be called directly. Unless jobs run inline in tests, the spec fails. In addition, the controller never calls TopicRetriever itself.

title: Missing topic after embed lookup leaves @topic_view nil or errors
body: TopicView.new raises if the topic was deleted but the embed row remains, giving a 500/404 in the iframe. Also, in the else branch `render 'loading'` is followed by discourse_expires_in, which is fine, but the retrieval is enqueued on every request for an unknown URL, so retries can flood the queue before the throttle applies.

title: Unescaped referer interpolated into inline JavaScript
body: request.referer is attacker-controlled and is written inside a single-quoted JS string. ERB HTML escaping does not stop quote characters from breaking out in a JS context in every case, and the value is a full URL rather than an origin. Use `to_json` on a validated origin. This is an XSS risk and also makes postMessage targetOrigin invalid when the referer includes a path.

title: contents mutated with << and URL interpolated unescaped
body: `contents <<` mutates the caller's string, so it breaks on frozen strings. In poll_feed it also mutates feed item content. The url is inserted into HTML without escaping. The sha1 is computed over the content including the appended footer, which is consistent, but the mutation is fragile.

title: open(url) on user-supplied URL (SSRF / command execution)
body: Kernel#open with open-uri on a URL derived from a request parameter. Hosts are checked against embeddable_host, but a string starting with '|' is not a URL and is rejected only by earlier checks; relying on these is fragile. Redirects can reach internal hosts. Use a dedicated HTTP client with timeouts.

title: Feed item content can be nil and crashes the whole poll
body: i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError when an item has no content (many RSS feeds use description). One bad item aborts the import of all remaining items. Also, `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no timeout.

title: Weak origin check using indexOf
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, so an origin like 'http://a' matches any URL containing it, and an empty origin always matches. Compare for equality against the parsed origin.

title: Editing an old migration with force: true drops existing table
body: Changing an already-released migration to `force: true` is unrelated to this feature and would drop data if re-run. Similarly, the whitespace edit to the word counts migration is unrelated noise.

title: Referer-based embed check is weak, and X-Frame-Options is set to ALLOWALL
body: Access is gated only on the Referer header host, which is spoofable by non-browser clients and is often stripped. The response then sets X-Frame-Options to ALLOWALL, which lets any site frame the page. Use a CSP frame-ancestors restriction on the allowed host instead of ALLOWALL.

title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript string
body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` is ERB-escaped as HTML, not as JS. A referer containing a single quote or a backslash can break out of the string. HTML escaping also turns & in the query string into &, which corrupts the targetOrigin, so postMessage silently fails. The value should be a JS-escaped origin, not the full referer URL.

title: Mutating `contents` in place, and unescaped URL in HTML
body: `contents <<` mutates the caller's string. It raises FrozenError if the string is frozen, and it appends the footer repeatedly if the caller reuses the string. The url is also interpolated into an href without escaping, so a crafted URL containing a quote can inject HTML. Raw HTML posts are not sanitized.

title: Kernel#open on a setting-supplied URL
body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Kernel#open from open-uri. This allows local file paths and, on older Rubies, pipe commands like `| cmd`. Use URI.parse(url).open, or restrict the value to http(s) URLs.

title: Kernel#open on user-influenced embed_url (SSRF)
body: import_remote calls `open(url)` with embed_url taken from a request parameter. The host check passes, but redirects, or the embeddable_host resolving to internal addresses, can lead to SSRF. Using Kernel#open also permits file and pipe access. Use an explicit HTTP client and validate the scheme.

title: Nil content or String#scrub crashes the job
body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element (e.g. summary-only feeds). String#scrub also does not exist on Ruby < 2.1. One bad item aborts the whole poll.

title: Malformed ERB `end if`
body: `<%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby: `end` followed by a dangling `if` modifier is a syntax error. This will break rendering of the template.

title: Missing topic or view yields errors; test and code disagree
body: The spec expects TopicRetriever.new to be called from the request, but the controller enqueues a job instead, so the 'tells the topic retriever' test fails or tests the wrong behavior. In the success path the 'loading' render is followed by discourse_expires_in, and best.html.erb renders the topic_view with a stubbed nil in the spec.

title: Origin check uses indexOf substring match
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl, including an empty or partial origin. Compare for exact origin equality instead.

title: align-items mixin emits invalid legacy-prefixed values
body: The mixin passes the same `$alignment` to every vendor property. The old `-webkit-box-align` accepts `start`, `end`, `center`, `baseline` and `stretch`. `-ms-flex-align` accepts `start`, `end`, `center`, `baseline` and `stretch`. Neither accepts `flex-start` or `flex-end`, so those values would produce invalid declarations on older browsers. The bare `-ms-align-items` is not a real property. For the `center` and `baseline` values used in this PR the output is fine, but the mixin is unsafe for other values.

title: Header children still use float inside the flex container
body: `.contents` becomes a flex container, but the `.title` float rule was removed and `.panel` lost `float: right` in favour of `margin-left: auto`. Flex ordering is only partly applied: `.panel` gets `order(3)` and `.extra-info-wrapper` gets `order(2)`, but the title has no order. Its position depends on the DOM order matching the intended layout. The `.valign-helper` rule, which has `height: 100%`, is now a flex item and may stretch or shift. This layout change is not described in the PR.

title: Floats inside the new flex container are ineffective
body: `.small-action` is now a flex container, but its children (`.topic-avatar`, `.avatar`, `button`) still declare `float`, which has no effect on flex items. The trailing `clear: both` is also irrelevant for the container. The floated button therefore no longer right-aligns, and the layout may regress. The padding and margin changes also alter spacing for all small-action posts.

title: Removed bullet margin-top may misalign badges
body: The `.bullet` `margin-top: 5px` was removed from `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper`, and `line-height: 1.5` was added. This presumably relies on the header's flex centering, but other contexts using `.extra-info-wrapper` could shift vertically. `order(2)` only takes effect if the parent is a flex container.

title: align-items mixin emits invalid legacy values
body: The same $alignment value is written to -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align. Those legacy properties use different keywords (start/end/center/baseline) than modern flexbox, so values such as flex-start or flex-end are invalid there. The mixin is called with center and baseline, which happen to work. Also, -ms-align-items is not a real property, and the line at 120 has trailing whitespace.

title: order mixin maps value to ordinal-group without offset
body: The legacy box-ordinal-group property starts at 1, while the modern `order` property defaults to 0. Passing the same value to both gives different relative ordering in old engines. The mixin does not translate between them.

title: Header flex layout removes .title float and relies on order and auto margin
body: .contents becomes a flex container, but children such as .title lose their float rules. Float is ignored on flex items anyway. The panel now uses margin-left:auto plus order(3), while the extra-info wrapper uses order(2). Other siblings that have no explicit order, such as the logo and the mobile header, default to 0 and are unaffected. Any child that still depends on float or inline layout, for example the .valign-helper with height:100%, will now behave differently as a flex item. This is a risky layout change with no test or visual verification.

title: clear:both on a flex container and floats inside flex items
body: .small-action is now display:flex, but its children (.topic-avatar, button, .avatar) still use float. Floats have no effect on flex items. The `clear: both` on the container is also redundant. The padding and margin changes (padding: 0 1.5% replacing the 4em left indent) alter the visual layout of small actions, and the avatar spacing is now inconsistent.

title: align-items mixin emits invalid legacy values for old flexbox syntaxes
body: The mixin writes the same $alignment into -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align. Those legacy properties use different keywords: `center` is valid, but `baseline` is valid in both while `flex-start` and `flex-end` must be `start` and `end`. Callers passing `flex-start` or `flex-end` get invalid declarations on those engines. `-ms-align-items` is not a real property. Prefer a keyword translation or drop the nonexistent prefix.

title: order mixin uses the same value for box-ordinal-group
body: The `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` properties are 1-based and are not equivalent to the modern `order`, which defaults to 0. In `header.scss`, `.panel` uses order(3) while the unordered siblings have the default order, so the old-box fallback yields different ordering than modern flexbox.

title: Removing .title float and making .contents flex may break header layout
body: The `.title` float rule was removed and `.contents` became a flex container, yet `.panel` relies on `margin-left: auto`. The `.contents` children (logo, extra-info-wrapper, panel) now depend on order values. Only `.extra-info-wrapper` (order 2) and `.panel` (order 3) are given an order, and the title stays at the default 0, which works only if the title is the first child. The `.icons`, `.login-button` floats inside the flex `.panel` are unchanged, so the panel may collapse. Also, other stylesheets, such as mobile or desktop ones, that still set floats on these elements are not updated.

title: Flex on .small-action has float and clear on flex items and container
body: `.small-action` becomes a flex container but children still use `float` (`.topic-avatar`, `.avatar`, `button`). Floats are ignored on flex items, so the `button` float:right no longer pushes the button to the right. The fixed `padding: 0 1.5%` replaces the earlier 4em left offset and the removal of the margins and paddings changes the vertical spacing of small-action posts, which is a visible regression unrelated to the header title.

title: String mutation with `<<` corrupts the hostname and can raise on frozen strings
body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` appends `website_host` into the string literal `"."`. That mutates the literal, which raises FrozenError under frozen-string-literal or on newer Ruby and gives wrong results on older Ruby. It is also easy to misread. Use `discourse_host.ends_with?(".#{website_host}")` instead.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing `?`
body: ActiveModelSerializers looks for `include_website_name?`. The method as written is never called, so `website_name` is always emitted, including for anonymous viewers of TL0 users where `website` is hidden. That leaks the website host. `website_name` is also not added to `untrusted_attributes`, so the restriction is not applied there either. Rename it to `include_website_name?` and also check `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

title: Host comparison is case-sensitive and the same-level subdomain branch is wrong
body: `URI(...).host` is not normalised, so `Example.com` will not match the instance hostname. The sibling-subdomain branch compares everything after the first label for hosts with the same number of labels. For `foo.co.uk` against `bar.co.uk`, or an unrelated site such as `a.example.com` against `b.example.com`, it treats them as the same domain. Beyond that, `URI(...).path` is empty for `http://example.com`, and a trailing slash is kept, so the displayed name can end in `/`. The same URI is also re-parsed several times.

title: Missing coverage for edge cases
body: There are no tests for the sibling-subdomain branch, an unparseable website, a blank website, or the anonymous TL0 case. The untrusted-attributes spec does not include `website_name`, so the leak described above goes unnoticed.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?', so it is never called
body: ActiveModel::Serializers only honors `include_<attr>?` hooks. Without the `?`, this method is dead code and website_name is always emitted, even when the website is blank. It is also not covered by untrusted_attributes, so anonymous viewers of a TL0 user's profile get website_name (the host/path of the hidden website) even though `website` is hidden. That leaks information the restriction was meant to hide.

title: `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal, and the suffix check is wrong
body: `"..." << website_host` appends in place to the literal. With frozen string literals this raises FrozenError, and otherwise it is fragile. The `ends_with?("." + website_host)` logic here also misfires when the website host has a different label count, for example a website of a.example.com on an instance of forum.example.com.

title: Path appended without normalization; invalid URI handling is fragile
body: `URI(website.to_s).path` is appended unchanged. A website like `http://example.com/` yields `example.com/`, and a path-only value with no host returns nil. The URI is parsed repeatedly, and `rescue nil` swallows every error. Parse once and strip trailing slashes. Also, if current_hostname is nil, the `.split` calls raise.

title: Missing test coverage for sibling-subdomain and blank-website cases
body: The tests do not cover the sibling-subdomain branch (www.example.com against forum.example.com), a blank website, or an invalid URL. They also do not verify that website_name is omitted for the anonymous TL0 user. The missing `?` on include_website_name would have been caught by such tests.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?', so it is never called
body: ActiveModel::Serializer only honors `include_<attr>?` methods. `include_website_name` without `?` is dead code, so the intended guard never runs. `website_name` is also not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is serialized for TL0 users seen by anonymous. This leaks the website host that the `website` attribute deliberately hides. Rename to `include_website_name?`, and also hide it for untrusted users (for example by adding `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`).

title: String#<< mutates the literal and the logic is wrong
body: `"." << website_host` appends the website host to the "." literal. `discourse_host.ends_with?` then checks the result, which is correct only when the literal is not frozen. With frozen string literals this raises. Building a new string, as in `".#{website_host}"`, is safer. The same-length-subdomain branch compares everything after the first label. That wrongly treats unrelated domains such as a.example.com and b.example.com as related, and `a.co.uk` against `b.co.uk` is likewise misjudged.

title: URI parsed repeatedly; the path may be empty or have a trailing slash
body: `URI(website.to_s)` is re-parsed several times, and only the first parse is protected by `rescue`. The later calls are not protected by it, and they are redundant. A website such as `http://example.com/` yields `example.com/`, with a trailing slash. A website with a query string loses that query string. Parse the URI once and normalise the path.

title: Missing test coverage for edge cases
body: The specs do not cover sibling subdomains (www.example.com against forum.example.com), an invalid URL, or a TL0 anonymous user. The untrusted-attributes spec does not list website_name, so the leak described above goes undetected.

title: Light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 70% for embedded post author links
body: The diff replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The light-theme branch should stay at 30%, with the dark branch being `$secondary` at 70%. This PR is meant to leave light themes unchanged, but these links become much lighter and less readable there. The dark branch is also inverted: 30% on $secondary is far too dark for a dark theme.

title: group-member-info .name light lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: The original light-theme color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code uses 50%/50% for both light and dark. The light theme therefore changes unintentionally and `.name` is no longer visually distinct from `.title`. The correct pair is 30% for `$primary` and 70% for `$secondary`.

title: Mobile group-member-info .name light lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: This is the same regression as in desktop/user.scss. The light-theme color shifts from 30% to 50% lightness, so the PR changes the light theme's appearance. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: custom-message-length light value changed from 70% to 30%
body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new light branch is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, with `$secondary` at 70%. The light-theme color becomes much darker, which is an unintended regression, and the dark pair is mismatched with the desktop version. The correct pair is 70%/30%, matching desktop/modal.scss.
