A null check is needed before querying, and the method should return false in that case.

title: Fallback to all-clients skips per-client negative permissions only when the resource is missing
body: The per-client resource is looked up by client.getId(). If it exists, evaluation uses only that resource. It does not fall back to the all-clients permission. A client with a per-client permission for a different scope, such as VIEW only, therefore loses an all-clients MANAGE grant. This is inconsistent with the all-clients fallback used when no resource exists. The user-permission flow handles this differently.

title: getClientsWithPermission uses findByType and includes the all-clients resource
body: The resource for the type 'Clients' itself may be returned and its name ('Clients') added to the granted set of client IDs. Also, findByType may not match resources whose type is unset, because per-client resources are created without a type, so per-client grants may be missed. This makes listing unreliable.

title: Dead code and unused imports
body: getEvaluationContext is private and never used. The Logger, the TOKEN_EXCHANGE import, Scope and others are also unused. Remove them.

title: Event listener gated on the V1 feature flag
body: Cleanup of permissions on role, client and group removal is now gated by ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ. Previously it ran unconditionally. When only V2 is enabled, the listener stops cleaning up. When V2 is enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients().setPermissionsEnabled now throws UnsupportedOperationException, which would otherwise break client deletion. The gating is a behavior change that is not explained in the description.

title: canManageClientScopes and canManage() are inconsistent with the Javadoc for V2
body: canView(ClientScopeModel) and canManage(ClientScopeModel) now grant access through the Clients resource type's permissions. The tests do not cover client-scope access. The tests also have no check that a MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE permission is enforced.

title: Exit code for recreate upgrade changed from 4 to 3
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3, and 4 is reassigned to FEATURE_DISABLED. Existing scripts that treat 4 as 'recreate needed' will now read it as 'feature disabled'. The Operator or other tooling that maps these codes also needs checking. The change is justified by the picocli codes but is a breaking contract change that should be called out.

title: Feature-disabled path tested only for the metadata command
body: The new feature check was added to both the metadata and check commands. The new test testFeatureNotEnabled covers only metadata. No test verifies that check prints the error and exits with code 4 when the feature is disabled. The exit code 4 is also not asserted for either command.

title: Feature flag is appended after the user-supplied parameters
body: The macro appends `--features=rolling-updates` to every rendered update-compatibility example. Users who copy the command and add their own `--features` list would end up with two `--features` options, so the examples can mislead users. The docs also never explain that the flag must be merged with the user's existing features.

title: Exit code for recreate upgrade changed from 4 to 3
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3, and 4 is reused for FEATURE_DISABLED. Any script that already treats 4 as "recreate required" will now read a disabled feature as a recreate upgrade, or miss the recreate case. The old code 4 now means something different. The documentation describes the new codes, but the change is breaking and nothing calls it out as a breaking change. The `check` command is still preview, so this is only a moderate risk.

title: Feature-disabled check lacks exit code test
body: The disabled-feature path in `run()` exits with code 4 for both `metadata` and `check`. The new test `testFeatureNotEnabled` covers only `metadata` and only asserts the error text. It does not assert the exit code, and `check` without the feature has no test. A regression in the exit code would go unnoticed.

title: Existing exit code for recreate upgrade changed from 4 to 3
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3, and 4 is reused for FEATURE_DISABLED. Scripts and pipelines that already treat 4 as "recreate required" will now misread "feature disabled" as a recreate result, and will miss real recreate results. The change is intentional (it avoids picocli codes 1 and 2), but any other code that hard-codes 4 or 3 must be updated. The Operator is a likely candidate, because it runs the check and interprets the exit code.

title: Feature-disabled path tested only for the metadata command
body: The new feature-disabled guard is also added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck. The only test, testFeatureNotEnabled, launches just the metadata subcommand and checks only the stderr message. It does not assert exit code 4, and nothing covers the check command. A regression in the check guard, or a wrong exit code, would go unnoticed.

title: canManage() grants manage on groups based on VIEW scope
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() falls back to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). An admin who only holds the VIEW scope on all groups is therefore treated as able to manage groups. requireManage() is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup, so this lets a view-only admin create top-level groups. The fallback should check only MANAGE.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes the resource id where hasPermission expects a group id
body: Inside the findByType callback, hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) is called, and the id is added to the granted set. hasPermission looks the resource up with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). In V2 the resource name is the group id, not the resource UUID, so the lookup finds nothing. It then falls back to the all-groups type resource. The set returned also contains resource UUIDs instead of group ids, which breaks the user-search group filter. The code should use groupResource.getName() for both the permission check and the returned set. The test only passes by accident, since a resource id may equal the group id in some stores.

title: Possible NPE when the Groups type resource is missing
body: getResourceTypeResource can return null, for example if the realm was created before the Groups type existed. policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) is then called with null and resource.getScopes() would also fail, so the permission check throws instead of returning false. There is no null check, unlike the null-safe handling elsewhere. Existing realms with admin permissions enabled will not have a Groups resource, because AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns early when the client already exists.

title: Group view lookup no longer guarded by canView()
body: The `!auth.users().canView()` guard was removed. getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() performs the same check internally for the regular admin-role case. It returns an empty set only if users().canView() is true, so the behaviour is the same for that case. However, session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...) is now set even when the caller can view all users, because the V2 canView depends on hasPermission. When it is set, grantIfNoPermission(true) is also invoked, which widens the grant. This is subtle and needs review and tests.

title: canManage() checks VIEW scope, so view-only admins are treated as managers
body: canManage() falls back to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). A caller with only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource therefore passes canManage(). That grants group creation (GroupsResource.requireManage()) and any other check that relies on canManage(). Only MANAGE should be accepted here. Likely a copy-paste from canView(). The interface javadoc says 'VIEW or MANAGE groups' for canManage(), so the doc has the same mistake.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes a resource ID to hasPermission, which looks up by name
body: hasPermission(groupId, ...) calls resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). Here the code passes groupResource.getId(), which is the resource's internal UUID, not its name (the group id). The lookup returns null and falls back to the all-groups resource, so the result is wrong. The same ID is then added to the granted set. The set should hold group ids, i.e. the resource names. As written, per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants are mishandled when the user search is filtered by group.

title: Possible NPE when the all-groups resource is missing
body: getResourceTypeResource can return null, for example when the schema is not supported or the resource is absent. policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and resource.getScopes() are then called without a null check. This will throw NPE instead of returning false.

title: canViewMembers/getGroupIds use users().canView() but not the group-specific permission path correctly
body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission the early return relies on root.users().canView(). When users().canView() is false the method iterates every Groups resource and evaluates permissions per resource. The all-groups type resource itself is also of type Groups, so it is included in the iteration. Its id is added to the result as if it were a group id.

title: canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership now accept group-level MANAGE_MEMBERS
body: canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership now return true via canManageByGroup(user), which means MANAGE_MEMBERS on any group the user belongs to. Previously these checks required MAP_ROLES or MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP on the user. This is a deliberate-looking widening of privilege, and no test covers it.

title: canManage() on all groups is granted by the VIEW scope
body: canManage() checks hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an admin who holds only the 'view' scope on all groups is treated as able to manage groups. addTopLevelGroup calls requireManage(), so a view-only admin can create top-level groups. Only MANAGE should be checked here. The Javadoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() repeats the mistake by saying 'VIEW or MANAGE'.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes resource id where the group id is expected
body: hasPermission(groupId, ...) looks up the resource with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), because V2 group resources are named by group id. The lambda passes groupResource.getId(), which is the resource UUID and differs from the name. The lookup misses, falls back to the all-groups resource, and yields wrong results. The granted set also holds resource ids instead of group ids, and callers pass it to user searches as group ids. It should use groupResource.getName().

title: Possible NPE when the all-groups resource type resource is missing
body: getResourceTypeResource can return null, for example when the schema is unsupported or the resource is not found. The code then calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and resource.getScopes() on the null value without a check. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2.

title: V1 group view filtering behavior changed
body: UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource now always set UserModel.GROUPS from getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, even for callers who can view all users. In V1 that case returns an empty set and the attribute is skipped, so it is probably fine. However, the old `!auth.users().canView()` guard was dropped. Previously canManage() also short-circuited this path; it is now covered only by canView(), which does include the manage-users role. The behavior is subtle and untested.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian login bundle's loginTotpStep1 now reads "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian sentence. The same wrong string was also put into the Lithuanian account bundle (account/messages_lt.properties line 101). It should be Lithuanian or removed so the English fallback is used.

title: Simplified Chinese totpStep1 replaced with Traditional Chinese
body: totpStep1 in the zh_CN bundle now uses Traditional Chinese (在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：), while the rest of the file is Simplified. It is the wrong script for this locale and should be written in Simplified Chinese.

title: Whitespace left inside <b> tags in identityProviderLinkBodyHtml
body: The fix only corrects `` to ``. The value still has padded text like ` {1} `, which renders with extra spaces. This is a minor cosmetic point.

title: English-file path derivation is fragile and crashes the verifier
body: The English file path is built by regex on the absolute path. The pattern `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` is not anchored, so an earlier `_xx` segment in the path could also match. If the derived English file does not exist, for example a community-only theme, or a _en file in a different directory, a RuntimeException is thrown instead of a clean verifier message. This would fail the whole build, and the exception is not a MojoExecutionException.

title: HTML detection regex only matches lowercase tags and misses closing or self-closing forms
body:
`<[a-z]+[^>]*>` requires a lowercase start and a closing `>`. English values containing `
` or `` are treated as having no HTML. In that case the translation is held to the no-HTML policy and gets false positives. The check also depends on the English file having a well-formed opening tag.

title: replaceFirst with a quoted pattern removes the wrong anchor occurrence
body: `value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(group), "")` removes the first matching text in the whole value, not the match just found. The matcher is also run on the original `value` while `value` is mutated inside the loop. If a translation reorders anchors or the same tag text appears more than once, the wrong occurrence is removed. This can hide or misreport anchor problems.

title: Lithuanian totp step replaced with Italian text
body: loginTotpStep1 was changed from a Lithuanian string to the Italian "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". This looks like a bad copy/paste when removing the links. Lithuanian users will see Italian text. The same wrong text is applied to the Lithuanian account messages_lt.properties totpStep1.

title: Simplified Chinese file given Traditional Chinese text
body: totpStep1 in the zh_CN file now uses Traditional Chinese (在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：), copied from zh_TW. Simplified Chinese users get the wrong script; it should be simplified (在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：).

title: English file derivation is fragile and fails hard
body: The English reference path is derived by regex replacement on the absolute path. `replaceAll("resources-community","resources")` and the `_xx.properties` replacement will also affect directory names containing such patterns. The greedy `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` can match from an earlier underscore in the file name. If the English file is missing (e.g. theme directories with no `_en`, such as the account-ui or admin-ui community files), a RuntimeException aborts the build rather than reporting a verification message. Admin-ui community files live under `maven-resources-community` which is not rewritten to `maven-resources`, so lookups there may fail.

title: Anchor check mutates value and breaks after first mismatch with stale matcher
body: santizeAnchors iterates a matcher over `value` while reassigning `value` via replaceFirst; the matcher still scans the original string, and replaceFirst removes the first textual occurrence, which may not be the one matched. Also, extra English anchors not present in the translation are not detected, and the added message lacks the key and file name, making it hard to locate.

title: Weak tests for sanitizer
body: Tests only assert that some message contains a substring. There is no positive test that valid HTML (e.g. allowed <b>, matching anchors, the choice-format or templateHelp exceptions) passes with no messages, so false positives from the sanitizer normalization would go unnoticed.

title: Lithuanian totp step replaced with Italian text
body: loginTotpStep1 was changed to the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' in the Lithuanian bundle. Lithuanian users will see Italian text. The same wrong string appears in account/messages_lt.properties line 101. A correct Lithuanian translation, or the English fallback, should be used instead.

title: Simplified Chinese bundle gets Traditional Chinese text
body: totpStep1 was replaced with Traditional Chinese text ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：') in the zh_CN file. The surrounding strings use Simplified Chinese, so this is the wrong script for the locale. It should use Simplified characters.

title: Fragile English file derivation, and a missing English file crashes verification
body: The English path is derived with the regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties`. It is not anchored and does not handle every locale name. A file with no locale suffix, or with a path that has an earlier underscore, resolves to the wrong path or to the file itself. If the English file does not exist (new theme types, other directories), the code throws a RuntimeException instead of reporting a verification message. The replaceAll on 'resources-community' also rewrites any such substring elsewhere in the path.

title: Anchor check can match wrong occurrence and mismatch counts
body: The anchor matching walks both matchers in lockstep. Extra English anchors absent from the translation are silently allowed. replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(...)) removes the first textual match, which may not be the one just found. Translations that drop an anchor tag, such as a missing closing tag, are not detected.

title: Non-static, non-private mutable fields for policies and patterns
body: POLICY_SOME_HTML, POLICY_NO_HTML and HTML_TAGS are package-private instance fields that are rebuilt for every verifier instance. They should be private static final.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring offsets
body: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the token when the shortcut matches, so it accepts wrong grants and rejects correct ones. The comment and offsets are also wrong. The context prefix is 6 chars with the grant at indices 4..6, so substring(3,5) takes the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant. Tests using expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh and similar will fail, or if they pass they verify nothing.

title: requireNonNull checks grantType twice, rawTokenId never checked
body: The fourth check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`. It should check rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId is accepted and produces a token id ending in 'null'.

title: Token creation throws for flows that don't set GRANT_TYPE
body: initToken now always calls encodeTokenId. If the GRANT_TYPE attribute is not set on the client session context, the grant falls back to "na". Unknown grant types are mapped ("na" is in the map), so that case still encodes. But a custom grant type factory that is not registered, or a flow that sets a grant id lacking a shortcut, makes encodeTokenId throw IllegalStateException. Other token-creation paths (implicit/hybrid flow, token-exchange legacy providers, admin or account flows) never set GRANT_TYPE and now get an 'na' encoding. That differs from the documented design and may break consumers expecting a UUID.

title: Lightweight detection depends on the session's current client
body: getShouldUseLightweightToken(session) reads session.getContext().getClient(), which may be null or differ from the client the token is issued for, for example during refresh or token exchange. It can throw an NPE or encode the wrong token type.

title: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws on any ID containing ':' that isn't 6-char prefixed
body: Any token id with a ':' whose prefix is not exactly 6 characters throws IllegalArgumentException. This includes old or foreign ids, which would break callers that parse arbitrary tokens.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring offsets
body: The matcher returns false when the extracted shortcut EQUALS the expected one, so it rejects correct IDs and accepts wrong ones. The substring(3,5) is also wrong for the 6-char prefix `sstt gg`, where the grant shortcut is at indexes 4..6. The comment about the '4th char' reflects the old format. The assertion therefore never validates the grant type, and the tests that use it will fail or pass for the wrong reasons.

title: Null check on wrong variable
body: The `rawTokenId` null check is done on `grantType` (`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId...")`), so a null rawTokenId is never rejected. This is a copy-paste bug.

title: Token ID encoding throws for contexts without a registered grant type
body: initToken encodes the ID using the GRANT_TYPE attribute on clientSessionCtx. Any code path creating access tokens that does not set this attribute falls back to "na". That is handled. However, grant types set from `context.getGrantType()` come from the raw form param, which may be null or differ from the factory id (e.g. when the Context is constructed by internal callers). A null grantType makes `clientSessionContext.getAttribute` return null and falls back to "na"; a non-registered string makes encodeTokenId throw IllegalStateException, which turns a token request into a 500.

title: Lightweight detection uses session attribute and context client, not the token being created
body: getShouldUseLightweightToken reads session.getContext().getClient(), which may not be the client the token is issued for (e.g. in token exchange or when the context client is null). That can mislabel the token type or cause an NPE.

title: Shortcut uniqueness validation is ineffective
body: Duplicate shortcuts or ids are detected only by comparing map sizes after puts to ConcurrentHashMaps. A duplicate shortcut overwrites the earlier entry, and the sizes may then still differ or match by coincidence. A grant type's shortcut that collides with "na" is also undetected. The lazy refresh paths also skip duplicate checks.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted and wrong-offset grant check
body: The condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when the shortcut matches, so the matcher rejects correct IDs and accepts wrong ones. The offset is also wrong: the format is `onrtac:`, so the grant shortcut is at chars 4-6, i.e. substring(4, 6). Substring(3,5) reads the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant. As written the matcher can never match a correct ID (it would be 'tac' vs 'ac'), so any test using expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh and similar would fail, or pass only by accident. It should be `!substring(4,6).equals(expected)` and the comment should say chars 5-6.

title: Null check on rawTokenId validates grantType instead
body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks grantType a second time, so rawTokenId is never validated. A null rawTokenId is silently accepted and later encoded as the string "null" in the token ID. It should check rawTokenId.

title: initToken throws if grant type attribute not set
body: initToken now calls encodeTokenId, which throws IllegalStateException if the grant type is unknown ("na" is a valid value in the shortcut map, but a null attribute becomes UNKNOWN and then encodes as 'na'). Even so, several paths create access tokens without setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE (implicit/hybrid flows, other callers of createClientAccessToken, and any token created before the attribute is set). Those produce 'na' IDs silently, which defeats the feature. A custom or unregistered grant would fail token creation outright. Related: the getShouldUseLightweightToken(session) call relies on session.getContext().getClient() being non-null, which may NPE in some flows.

title: Duplicate shortcut validation is weak
body: Duplicates are detected only by comparing map sizes after puts that overwrite silently. If two grants share a shortcut, the later one overwrites the earlier in grantsByShortcuts, so the sizes differ only by accident. The lazy refresh paths also never validate. Collisions should be checked explicitly on each put. Also, a shortcut of 'na' from a grant would collide with UNKNOWN.

title: Used recovery code never marked as used for federated credentials
body: For user-storage users, the credential stored is just a JSON list of raw codes. Validation in the real federated provider path never marks a code as used. In RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator, `allCodesUsed()` and `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()` operate on a model that the storage never updates. As a result, the same code can be reused indefinitely and the prompted code number never advances. The `removeStoredCredentialById` call is also applied to a federated credential ID, which will not work.

title: Raw recovery codes sent to user storage in plaintext
body: For federated storage the raw generated codes are serialized as JSON and passed as the challenge response. Local storage keeps only hashes. The codes are therefore stored unhashed in the external storage, a security downgrade. Metadata such as the user label and creation time are also lost.

title: Unchecked Optional.get() calls
body: `credentialModelOpt.get()` and `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()` throw NoSuchElementException if no credential is found. This is more likely now that lookup spans two sources. Previously the same risk existed, but a clearer error should be produced.

title: getCredentials NPE when user missing, and the credential type is not converted
body: `getMyUser(user)` can return null, for example after the user is removed, and `myUser.recoveryCodes` then throws an NPE. Also, the recovery model is built via createFromValues, which re-hashes the codes. Because of that, the model's credential data differs from what isValid compares against, and the user label is never persisted.

title: Raw recovery codes sent to user storage as credential value
body: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` serializes the plaintext generated codes to JSON and passes them to `updateCredential`. Any user storage provider that supports the recovery-codes type therefore receives the raw, unhashed codes. The local path stores hashed codes via the credential model. This is inconsistent and leaves the secrets in plaintext. The test provider also validates by comparing the plaintext codes.

title: Credential lookup order and removal ignore federated credentials
body: `getCredential` can now return a federated credential. In `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator`, `allCodesUsed()` leads to `removeStoredCredentialById`, which only removes local credentials. A federated credential is never removed or updated when codes are used. Used codes are also never marked used in the federated store, so the next-code number never advances.

title: Test storage returns inconsistent recovery credential model
body: `getCredentials` rebuilds the model with `createFromValues` on the raw codes. That generates a new credential without the stored id, so the id differs from the stored one. The raw codes are hashed into the credential data, which is inconsistent with the storage's `isValid` that compares plaintext. `getCredentials` also does not null-check `myUser`, unlike other methods, so it throws an NPE for an unknown user.

title: Unchecked Optional.get()
body: `credentialModelOpt.get()` throws NoSuchElementException if no credential is found. Before this change the code had the same `.get()` on a stream. With the federated lookup, a storage that reports `isConfiguredFor` but returns no credential from `getFederatedCredentialsStream` triggers the exception. Handle the empty case explicitly.

title: Raw recovery codes sent to user storage instead of hashed codes
body: The user-storage path passes the raw generatedCodes JSON as the credential value (`recoveryCodesJson`). The local path stores hashed codes via the credential model. A federated store therefore receives plaintext one-time recovery codes. The test storage provider compares raw input with the raw stored codes. Any real provider that tries to hash them or treat them like local data gets inconsistent semantics. Also the local provider's `createCredential` may apply side effects, such as removing old credentials, that the user-storage path skips.

title: Federated credential lookup breaks consumption tracking
body: `getCredential` returns the federated credential first. But `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` then calls `removeStoredCredentialById` on it, which only works for local storage. Used codes are never marked used in user storage. The test provider's `getCredentials` rebuilds the model with `createFromValues` on every call, so `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode` always returns code 0 and the same code is requested forever. Federated recovery codes are effectively reusable, and `allCodesUsed` can never become true.

title: Unchecked Optional.get() calls
body: `credentialModelOpt.get()` and `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()` throw NoSuchElementException when no credential exists or no codes remain. The previous code had the same weakness, but the new lookup adds more paths on which the Optional can be empty.

title: getCredentials NPE and lost user label
body: `getMyUser(user)` can return null, for example for a user that has been removed. `myUser.recoveryCodes` then throws an NPE, unlike the null checks elsewhere in this class. The model built from `createFromValues` also has a random id and never sets the stored credential id. It therefore does not match the `recoveryCodesModel` id created in `updateCredential`.

title: getSubGroupsCount returns null when group is concurrently deleted
body: When the group has been deleted concurrently, `modelSupplier.get()` returns null and the method now returns null instead of throwing an NPE. The `Long` return type is documented and used as a count. Callers such as `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` pass the result to `representation.setSubGroupCount(...)`, and other callers may unbox it, so an NPE can resurface further up the stack. Returning 0, or treating the group as gone, would be safer. The other delegating methods (`getSubGroupsStream(...)`) still call `modelSupplier.get()` without a null check, so the same race remains there.

title: Concurrency test thread is not joined and is racy
body: The reader thread is started but never joined, so `caughtExceptions` can be asserted while the thread is still running, or before it has done any reads. The thread is not a daemon and can outlive the test. If the loop is slow, no read may overlap the deletes at all, so the test can pass without exercising the race. It should join the thread before the assertion and ensure that reads happen during the deletes.

title: Test does not exercise the subGroupsCount path that was fixed
body: The test calls `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)`. That is the brief representation and the fifth argument may not request `subGroupsCount`. The fix is in `getSubGroupsCount`, so the test may not cover the changed code path.

title: getSubGroupsCount returns null for a concurrently deleted group, which can still NPE callers
body: When the group is deleted concurrently, modelSupplier.get() returns null and getSubGroupsCount() now returns null. The declared return type is Long and callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount pass it straight to representation.setSubGroupCount(...). If that setter takes a primitive long, the unboxing throws an NPE, so the original failure just moves to another place. Other methods in the class (getSubGroupsStream with search or paging) still call modelSupplier.get().xxx() without a null check, so the same race remains there.

title: Test reader thread is not joined and failures there are racy
body: The background reader thread is started but never joined. After deletedAll is set, the main thread asserts on caughtExceptions immediately, so an exception thrown by the reader's final iteration can be missed. This makes the race test flaky, and it can pass without ever reproducing the bug. The thread is also non-daemon. The test calls groups(...) with brief=true, which may not exercise the getSubGroupsCount path that was fixed. Join the thread before asserting.

title: getSubGroupsCount returns null for a concurrently deleted group
body: When the group is deleted concurrently, modelSupplier.get() returns null and getSubGroupsCount() now returns null instead of throwing. Callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount pass this straight to representation.setSubGroupCount(...), and other callers may unbox the Long. The NPE can then move to those callers, or the API silently reports a null count for a group that no longer exists. The other methods in this adapter (getSubGroupsStream with search/paging, getDelegateForUpdate) either dereference modelSupplier.get() directly or throw IllegalStateException when the group is not found, so this method is also inconsistent with them.

title: Racy test with an unjoined thread and weak assertion
body: The reader thread is started but never joined. After deletedAll is set, the main thread asserts immediately, so an exception thrown by an in-flight request can be missed. The thread is not a daemon and is never awaited, so it can outlive the test and keep calling the server during cleanup. The loop has no pause, which hammers the server. The test also only passes or fails by timing, so it may not reliably reproduce the NPE. Join the thread before asserting.

title: Unrelated dead-code removal bundled in the fix
body: The removal of the unused groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement method (and likely the now-unused StringUtil import) has nothing to do with the NPE fix. It adds noise to the PR. If StringUtil is still imported elsewhere in the file, this is harmless, but it should be a separate cleanup.

title: Negative offset slicing on Django queryset raises an error or is unsafe
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes a user-controlled negative cursor.offset straight into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise AssertionError (a 500). The comment claiming the ORM handles it is wrong. The cursor offset comes from the request cursor string, which Cursor.from_string parses with no sign check. The 'authorization' for this path is only a client-supplied query flag plus a role check, so the feature is an unvalidated attack surface that was never needed.

title: Shared BasePaginator now lets negative offsets through for prev cursors
body: The change in BasePaginator.get_result uses the raw offset when cursor.is_prev. A crafted prev cursor with a negative offset on any paginator that uses BasePaginator (many endpoints) now reaches queryset slicing with a negative start and raises an AssertionError. Previously the slice used offset directly, and a negative offset failed the same way, but the comment claims this is a deliberate feature. The edit is not behavior-preserving in intent and adds no validation. The same pattern is duplicated in the new class, and `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` uses the unclamped offset.

title: Authorization check may fail or be too broad
body: organization_context.member can be None (for example for superusers who are not members), which raises AttributeError. The `or` short-circuits for superusers, but a non-member with other access would crash. Gating a pagination mode on is_superuser or global access is also weak protection for the unsafe negative-offset path. Trailing whitespace on lines 71 and 89 also exists.

title: New paginator is mostly duplicated code and has no tests
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator copies BasePaginator.get_result nearly verbatim, and get_item_key and value_from_cursor duplicate Paginator. It adds no real optimization. No tests cover the new paginator, the negative offset path, or the endpoint flag. Also get_item_key uses math.floor on a datetime, since order_by is -datetime, which raises TypeError. The optimized path therefore breaks on the audit log endpoint it is wired to.

title: Negative offsets passed to Django queryset slicing
body: With enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0, the code runs queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django raises AssertionError('Negative indexing is not supported.') for negative slice bounds, so a user-supplied cursor such as 'x:-5:0' becomes a 500 error. The comment claiming the ORM 'properly handles negative slicing' is wrong. Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets, so this is user-controllable. If a negative-stop slice were somehow accepted it could also expose rows outside the intended page, and the 'permissions checked at queryset level' comment does not make this safe.

title: Base BasePaginator now allows negative offsets for prev cursors
body: The shared BasePaginator.get_result was changed so that for is_prev cursors start_offset = offset without clamping to 0. This affects every endpoint using BasePaginator, not just the audit log. A crafted prev cursor with a negative offset now reaches queryset slicing and raises an AssertionError (500). Previously the negative offset hit the same slice, so the max(0, ...) only helps non-prev cursors, and the change is a pointless, misleading edit to shared code.

title: Authorization check may fail and is loosely gated
body: organization_context.member can be None (e.g. for superusers who are not members), so organization_context.member.has_global_access raises AttributeError. Because `or` short-circuits only when the user is a superuser, non-superuser access with no member could also break. The check is also evaluated eagerly for every request, even without optimized_pagination. The optimized path is opt-in via a query param and unlocks the unsafe negative-offset behavior.

title: New paginator duplicates BasePaginator logic with no tests
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator copies BasePaginator.get_result almost verbatim, and get_item_key does not handle datetimes (it calls math.floor on a datetime value, which raises TypeError). The endpoint orders by -datetime, so the optimized path crashes with a TypeError whenever results exist. No tests were added for it.

title: Negative offset slicing on Django QuerySet is unsupported and bypasses bounds
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes a negative cursor.offset straight into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django raises AssertionError('Negative indexing is not supported') for negative slice bounds, so a user-supplied cursor like 'value:-5:0' causes a 500. The comments claim the ORM handles this and that it exposes data 'beyond normal pagination bounds', which is wrong. Cursor.from_string accepts negative ints from user input, and no validation rejects them.

title: Change to BasePaginator allows negative offset for prev cursors
body: In the shared BasePaginator, start_offset is now `offset` unclamped when cursor.is_prev. Previously the offset was passed through as is, so this adds nothing, but the comment says it deliberately allows negatives. A user-controlled negative offset in a prev cursor now reaches queryset slicing for every paginator that subclasses BasePaginator, causing an assertion error (500). The original behavior should be kept, with negative offsets rejected explicitly (as OffsetPaginator does with BadPaginationError).

title: Undocumented query flag gates an unvalidated code path; access check is fragile
body: The optimized_pagination=true flag routes to a paginator with unvalidated negative-offset behavior. The gate `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` can raise AttributeError if member is None (e.g. superuser not in the org), causing a 500 for requests even when the flag isn't set, since it's evaluated unconditionally. It also changes the audit log endpoint for all requests.

title: Prev-cursor trimming uses unclamped offset and is duplicated code
body: `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` uses the raw offset, which with negative offsets will never match the actual fetched length, so the extra row is not dropped. Also OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates the whole BasePaginator.get_result, and get_item_key uses math.floor on a datetime (order_by is -datetime), which raises TypeError. The optimized path is broken for the audit log endpoint.

title: No tests added for new paginator or endpoint behavior
body: A new paginator, a new query parameter and a modified base paginator are introduced without any tests, including negative-offset and permission-gated paths.

title: Negative offsets passed to Django queryset slicing
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]` where start_offset = cursor.offset < 0). Django raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` on negative slices, so a crafted cursor such as `?cursor=0:-5:0` causes a 500. The comment claiming the ORM handles this is wrong. The cursor is user-controlled via Cursor.from_string, which accepts negative offsets.

title: BasePaginator now permits negative offsets for prev cursors
body: The change `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` lets a prev cursor with a negative offset reach `queryset[negative:stop]`. Before this change it was the same failure mode, but the new code is explicitly intended to allow it, so it affects every paginator subclass. The result is an AssertionError/500 for any endpoint that accepts a crafted `is_prev` cursor. The later `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check also uses the unclamped offset.

title: Undocumented opt-in flag that unlocks a less-validated paginator
body: Any org member with global access, or any superuser, can pass `optimized_pagination=true` to switch to a paginator that is meant to allow negative offsets. This is an unnecessary expansion of the attack surface on the audit-log endpoint. The paginator is also not tested, and a comment about 'permissions checked at the queryset level' does not justify skipping offset validation. The trailing whitespace on lines 71 and 89 is a minor nit.

title: Eviction is based on a stale span_count and the redirect limit was reduced
body: span_count is only set when a zunionstore ran, so a zadd done earlier in Python can leave the count out of date. It is only recomputed with zcard when it is 0. After a merge, span_count is the size of the last union, which is correct, but the first merge's count is overwritten. The redirect loop limit was also silently cut from 10000 to 1000, which means deeper trees are no longer joined correctly. Evicting with zpopmin drops the oldest spans silently, with no metric.

title: Removed max_segment_spans enforcement while the parameter remains
body: The span-count check in _load_segment_data was removed, but `max_segment_spans` is still a constructor parameter and is now unused. The Lua script hardcodes 1000 instead of using the configured value. Configuration therefore has no effect.

title: Hard dependency on end_timestamp_precise
body: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises KeyError for any span payload missing the field, which crashes the whole batch in the consumer. Using `.get` with a fallback would be safer.

title: Negative offsets passed to Django queryset slicing
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes a user-controlled negative cursor.offset straight into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django raises an AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported') for negative slice bounds, so this produces a 500 error. Cursor.from_string accepts negative ints, so any admin sending optimized_pagination=true with a crafted cursor triggers it. The comment that the ORM handles negative slicing is wrong. The 'safe because permissions are checked' claim is also unfounded.

title: BasePaginator now allows negative offsets for prev cursors
body: The change `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` lets a negative offset reach queryset slicing whenever is_prev is true. Previously negative offsets failed in the same way, but this change deliberately keeps them for prev cursors, which affects every endpoint using BasePaginator. A crafted cursor such as `0:-5:1` would cause an assertion error and a 500 response. The change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose.

title: Unrelated feature gated on has_global_access, member may be None
body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is dereferenced without a None check. A superuser who is not an org member has member=None, so evaluating the `or` right-hand side would raise AttributeError whenever is_superuser is False. Also, this audit-log pagination feature is unrelated to the spans buffer PR title, and it exposes the negative-offset path.

title: Redirect depth limit reduced 10x
body: The loop limit drops from 10000 to 1000 without explanation, and the comment explaining the limit was removed. Segment trees deeper than 1000 now fail to join correctly.

title: Span count check removed; max_segment_spans is now unused
body: The max_segment_spans check in _load_segment_data was removed and the Lua script now caps sets at 1000 via zpopmin. The cap is 1000 but max_segment_spans defaults to 1001, and the parameter is now dead code. Eviction also drops the lowest-scored (oldest end timestamp) spans silently, with no metric or log. The zpopmin only runs after the zunionstore merge, and spans zadd'd before the script (the pipeline step) can push the set well over the limit until later calls trim it.

title: end_timestamp_precise accessed as required key
body: val["end_timestamp_precise"] raises KeyError if a span lacks the field, which crashes the whole batch in the consumer. This is a poison-pill risk during rollout or for older Relay versions.

title: Negative offsets bypass pagination bounds in OptimizedCursorPaginator
body: With enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0, the code slices queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django QuerySets raise AssertionError on negative indexing/slicing, so a crafted cursor such as `0:-5:1` gives a 500 error. The comment claiming Django handles this is wrong. The `Cursor.from_string` path accepts negative offsets from user input, and the feature is gated only by a user-controllable query param.

title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets to the queryset for prev cursors
body: Changing the slice to `start_offset = offset if cursor.is_prev` lets negative offsets reach `queryset[...]` for every paginator subclass. Previously a negative offset also failed, but now it is deliberately preserved, and the `stop` computation changes. A user-supplied prev cursor with a negative offset can trigger an assertion error or unexpected results across all endpoints that use BasePaginator. The later `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check also uses the unclamped offset.

title: Unrelated, weakly justified paginator path on audit log endpoint
body: The audit log endpoint adds an opt-in `optimized_pagination` mode that exposes the negative-offset code to superusers and global-access members. This is unrelated to the spans buffer change described in the PR. `organization_context.member` may be None for superusers who are not members, which would raise AttributeError. Trailing whitespace is also present.

title: Redirect depth limit reduced from 10000 to 1000
body: The loop bound dropped from 10000 to 1000 with no explanation. Segment trees deeper than 1000 will no longer be joined correctly, which regresses behavior the old comment documented.

title: Removed max_segment_spans check; the limit is now enforced only in Lua
body: The span-count guard in _load_segment_data was removed, and `max_segment_spans` is now unused. The Lua script hard-codes 1000 and evicts the lowest-scored entries via zpopmin. The two limits are inconsistent (the config default is 1001), and the config is no longer honored. Spans are silently dropped without a metric.

title: end_timestamp_precise accessed as a required key
body: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises KeyError if a span lacks the field. That crashes the whole batch in the consumer. Using `.get` with a fallback, or dropping the span, would be safer.

title: Cache key uses Python hash() of project IDs, which is not stable or collision-free
body: hash(tuple(...)) of ints is deterministic within a process, but a 64-bit hash makes collisions possible. Two different project sets could then share an eligibility result, so a non-allowlisted project could be upsampled, or the reverse. The key is built from the hash instead of the joined IDs, so it is not safe as a cross-process cache key. Build the key from the joined sorted IDs instead.

title: Cache invalidation is never called, so the cache is stale for up to 60s
body: invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but nothing calls it, and it only deletes a single project-set key. Changes to the allowlist option therefore do not take effect until the 60s TTL expires. The docstring claiming consistency is misleading. The caching also saves almost nothing, because options.get is already cheap.

title: Transform only handles an exact 'count()' and always aliases the result as 'count'
body: Other count forms and aggregates are not handled, such as count() with an alias, or equations. Rewriting to 'upsampled_count() as count' can also collide with a user-requested column that is already named count. Events lacking sample_weight (older events, or events without a client sample rate) would sum to 0, so the chart would undercount. The comments claim the schema guarantees the column, but nothing enforces that.

title: Upsampling check uses the outer dataset and request query rather than the scoped dataset and actual query
body: The check passes the closure's `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`, and it inspects request.GET['query'] instead of the `query` parameter. The dashboard-widget split paths call _get_event_stats with discover and a rewritten query such as '!event.type:transaction'. In those paths the decision is wrong, so transaction queries could get upsampled_count (sample_weight does not exist for transactions), or error queries could be missed. The check is also repeated on every call. Also, 'event.type:error' is matched as a substring of the query text, which misses queries like '!event.type:error' and similar forms.

title: Upsampling is applied to RPC datasets, but the transform produces a legacy-only function
body: In the RPC paths (spans_rpc and ourlogs), the transform emits 'upsampled_count() as count'. This is only defined in the discover SnQL function converter. The helper returns False for those datasets, so the path is dead code today, but it would break if the helper changes.

title: upsampled_count is registered as a public function for all discover queries
body: It is not marked private. Users can call it directly against transactions or non-allowlisted projects, where sample_weight is missing, and get errors or wrong results. It also sums sample_weight without the sampling-rate inversion (1/rate), so the semantics are unclear.

title: Tests mock the whole options module and depend on factory behavior, with no cache coverage
body: Mocking `options` makes every options.get return the allowlist, which affects unrelated lookups. The cache is never cleared between tests, and the key is identical for identical project sets, so tests can leak state. The caching, the invalidate function, and the top_events path are untested.

title: Test factory silently swallows all exceptions and rewrites sample_rate for all store_event callers
body: The bare `except Exception: pass` blocks hide errors. The helper also changes sample_rate for any test event that carries the error_sampling context, a global change to fixtures. Also, a client_sample_rate of 0 is ignored because the check is truthiness.

title: Stray submodule/gitlink file added to the PR
body: The 'sentry-repo' file is a subproject commit pointer unrelated to the feature. It should not be committed.

title: Cache key uses Python's per-process randomized hash()
body: The key is built from hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python's hash of ints is stable, but for tuples it depends on the interpreter version, and the key is not collision-safe. Two different project sets can collide and share a cached eligibility result, so one set of projects can wrongly get upsampled counts. Use a deterministic key such as a joined string of project ids or a digest. The same issue is repeated in invalidate_upsampling_cache.

title: Cache invalidation is never called
body: invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but nothing calls it, for example from a change to the allowlist option. The result is stale for 60 seconds, and the docstring's claim of cache consistency is not met. A cache entry also cannot be invalidated for every project combination, because the key depends on the exact project set. Caching an options.get lookup, which is already cheap and cached in-process, adds complexity without a clear benefit.

title: Eligibility check uses outer dataset and request query, not scoped dataset and actual query
body: The check is passed the outer `dataset`, not `scoped_dataset`, and it reads `request.GET['query']`, not the `query` argument. Dashboard split logic calls _get_event_stats with discover and with modified queries such as `!event.type:transaction`. Those calls can wrongly get upsampled, or a real errors query can be skipped. The decision should be based on the arguments actually passed in.

title: Only the exact string count() is transformed
body: The transform handles only the literal `count()` column. Aliased forms and other aggregates are left alone. The rewrite also unconditionally aliases the result as `count`, which changes the response key for callers and can collide with other columns. For top events, the sort or orderby on count() may no longer resolve after the rewrite.

title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public function over a column that may be missing
body: The new function is registered in the discover dataset, so any user query can call it. It sums sample_weight, which does not exist on transactions and may not exist on older error events, so Snuba will error or produce wrong values. The code comment says the column is assumed to exist, but no code guarantees that. It also uses the default result type "number" while returning toInt64. The function should be marked private.

title: Trailing whitespace and misleading comments
body: Several lines contain trailing whitespace, which fails linting. The comments claim 'cached result', 'schema assumptions' and 'query optimization', but none of that is implemented here.

title: Tests don't cover top_events, RPC, or the discover event.type:error path
body: The tests mock options but do not test the cache behavior. They also do not cover top events, or the discover dataset with event.type:error. They rely on the test factory setting sample_rate from the context, which is a test-only shim that production ingestion does not use. As a result, the sample_weight column may not be populated in production.

title: Cache key uses Python hash() of project ids
body: The key is built from hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python's tuple hash is not guaranteed unique, so two different project sets can collide and share a cached eligibility result. A non-allowlisted project set could then be upsampled, or the reverse. The hash is also not a stable cache key. Use the joined project ids instead.

title: Cache invalidation is never called
body: invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but nothing calls it, for example when the allowlist option changes. Allowlist changes are therefore stale for up to 60 seconds. Because the key is per project set, invalidating after an option change is impractical anyway. The 60s cache saves almost nothing, since options.get is already cheap and cached.

title: Transform emits 'upsampled_count() as count', which is only defined in the discover dataset
body: The transform runs for the errors dataset and for the RPC/other paths, but upsampled_count is only registered in the discover dataset function converter. The errors dataset or its builder may not know the function, so such queries can fail. The transform is also applied to the discover queries run in the widget-split paths. The "as count" alias with the string-based parser is unverified.

title: Eligibility check uses the outer `dataset`, not `scoped_dataset`
body: The check passes the closed-over `dataset` instead of the `scoped_dataset` argument. In the dashboard split paths the queried dataset is `discover` or the scoped one, so the decision is made against the wrong dataset. It also reads `event.type:error` from the request query rather than the `query` argument. The split path appends `AND !event.type:transaction`, so the actual query is not what gets checked. The check also runs on every call, including the repeated split queries.

title: upsampled_count assumes a sample_weight column and sums NULLs
body: sum(sample_weight) returns NULL or 0 for events that have no sample_weight, so counts drop to 0 for those events. The code comments assume the column exists for all events, but nothing enforces that. A fallback such as a coalesce to 1 is missing. The function is also registered without the `private` flag, so users can call it directly in discover queries.

title: Test factory silently swallows exceptions and sets sample_rate on every event
body: The helper uses broad `except Exception: pass` blocks. It also changes `sample_rate` for every stored event in the shared test factory. A falsy rate of 0 is ignored. This can affect unrelated tests.

title: Tests don't cover top_events, the RPC path, or the cache
body: The upsampling tests mock `options` and cover only the plain timeseries path. They do not cover topEvents or the cache hit/miss behavior. The sorted-vs-cached eligibility interaction is also untested. The test setUp reassigns self.user after login, which is confusing.

title: Stray submodule/gitlink file added
body: A `sentry-repo` subproject commit entry was added accidentally. It should not be part of this PR.

title: Per-issue event lookup in comment body generation causes N+1 queries
body: get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() (a Snuba/nodestore lookup) and get_environment() for every issue while building the PR comment. With up to 5 issues this adds several extra queries on each comment task. The broad `except Exception` also hides real failures and logs them only at info level.

title: New comment template drops culprit and changes markdown list formatting
body: The template ends in "\n" and is joined with "\n", so each item is followed by a blank line and the list renders as loose paragraphs with extra trailing whitespace. The `culprit` subtitle was also removed. The ISSUE_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH truncation can cut the title mid markdown-token, for example inside backticks or emphasis.

title: Editing already-merged migrations to no-ops
body: Migrations 0917 and 0920 are rewritten to do nothing, and their tests are deleted. Any environment that already ran the original bodies keeps the data they produced. The comment says the migration was never run, but that cannot be guaranteed. The comment also refers to a 0921 migration that is not part of this diff.

title: Default autofix automation tuning changed from low to off
body: This changes the default behaviour for every project without an explicit option value. Autofix automation silently turns off for existing projects that relied on the default. The change is bundled into an unrelated PR with no migration or release note.

title: Truthiness check on initial_data misses age=0 or timestamp=0
body: validate_timestamp and validate_age use `if self.initial_data.get(...)`, which is falsy for 0. A report with age=0 plus a timestamp passes validation even though the specs are meant to be mutually exclusive. Use `in` or `is not None` instead.

title: Error events are paired with the wrong ids and the zero-ts default breaks ordering
body: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes get_multi returns results in the same order as error_ids, which a dict does not guarantee. Events can therefore be mislabeled, and the id field is unreliable. Missing timestamps default to 0.0, which sorts those errors first. The endpoint also now runs a Snuba query before pagination, and request.user.id is passed even for anonymous users.

title: Analytics recorded before the feature flag check
body: analytics.record runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check. Events are therefore emitted for orgs that do not have the feature, and the request is then rejected with 404.

title: Table widget renders empty data under the feature flag
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, TableWidgetVisualization receives hardcoded `columns=[]` and empty `tableData`. Every table widget shows empty, ignoring result.data and result.meta. The `loading` state is also dropped.

title: Per-issue environment lookup issues extra queries on a hot path
body: get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() once per issue while building the PR comment. Each call can hit nodestore or Snuba, so a comment with many issues adds a per-issue query cost. The broad `except Exception` also hides real failures behind an info-level log.

title: Template ends with a trailing newline and the comment layout changes
body: MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE ends with "\n", and the callers then join the items with "\n". This produces blank lines between bullets plus an extra trailing blank line before the footer. The tests encode this spacing, so it is likely unintended. Separately, the subtitle/culprit is dropped from the comment, which is a behaviour change.

title: Static method reaches into a different class
body: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template is a staticmethod, and it calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title by class name. It sits next to code that appears to be in CommitContextIntegration, so it is unclear whether PRCommentWorkflow is the enclosing class. If it is not, this raises NameError or couples the two classes by accident.

title: Editing already-shipped migrations to no-ops
body: The bodies of migrations 0917 and 0920 are replaced with no-ops, on the claim that they "never ran". Any environment that already applied them keeps the converted data, while new environments skip it. The comment points to a 0921 migration that is not in this diff. The 0917 test was also deleted.

title: Default autofix automation tuning changed from "low" to "off"
body: This changes the default behaviour for all projects that have not explicitly set the option, and nothing in the PR description mentions it. The change is silent and unrelated to the stated purpose of the PR.

title: Error fetch and the replay Snuba query add failure paths and mismatch IDs
body: query_replay_instance is now called on every request and is not wrapped in error handling, so a Snuba failure turns a summary request into a 500. In fetch_error_details, `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes get_multi preserves order and returns an entry for every id. A missing or reordered entry attaches the wrong event_id to the data. Also, on_results mutates error_events with an in-place sort.

title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with empty data when the flag is on
body: With the feature flag enabled, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with `columns=[]` and an empty `tableData`. The actual `result.data` and `meta` are ignored, so the table shows no data. This is incomplete code behind a flag.

title: Analytics recorded before the feature check
body: analytics.record runs before the feature-flag check, so events are emitted for organizations without the feature. It also uses request.user.id, which is None for org-auth-token requests. The event declares user_id as optional, so this does not fail, but it is noisy data.

title: Rows without segments skip the delete but are still archived
body: When max_segment_id is None, no recording files are deleted. The replay is still archived via delete_replays. This is probably fine, but any recordings that exist without ClickHouse segment rows are orphaned.

title: Environment lookup issues extra queries per issue and swallows errors
body: get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() and get_environment() for every issue while the comment is built. This adds a Snuba/nodestore query per issue, up to 5 issues per PR comment. The broad `except Exception` only logs at info level, so failures are hidden. The error object is also placed in `extra`, which may not serialize cleanly.

title: Comment template drops the culprit and adds blank lines
body: MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE ends with `\n`, and the callers join items with `\n`. The result is blank lines between bullets and a trailing blank line. The culprit/subtitle that was shown before is also removed. That is a user-visible format change, and the formatting is awkward.

title: Autofix automation default changed from 'low' to 'off'
body: The default for autofix automation tuning changed from 'low' to 'off'. Projects that never set the option will silently stop receiving automated autofix runs. The PR description gives no rationale for this behavior change, and the PR is otherwise unrelated to the change.

title: Editing already-applied historical migrations
body: The migration body is replaced with a no-op, and the comment claims it was never run. If it did run in any environment, the data conversion is now inconsistent with the history. The migration test file for 0917 was also deleted, and the replacement migration 0921 is not shown in this PR.

title: Age/timestamp validation uses truthiness
body: validate_timestamp and validate_age check `initial_data.get(...)` for truthiness. A value of 0 (for example `age: 0`) is treated as absent, so a report with both fields can pass validation. Neither field is required, so a report with neither also passes.

title: Error events matched to IDs by zip over dict values
body: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes get_multi returns results in the same order as error_ids. Dict order does not guarantee that, and missing nodes may be omitted from the result. Events can therefore be paired with the wrong IDs. Keys should be looked up explicitly by node_id.

title: Shared error list is sorted in place, and paginated callbacks can reuse it
body: get_request_data sorts error_events in place, mutating the shared list. Separate error-event log lines are emitted on every page of segments, because the same error_events are passed to every on_results call.

title: Analytics recorded before the feature flag check
body: analytics.record runs before the feature-flag check, so events are emitted even for orgs where the endpoint returns 404. It also uses request.user.id, which can be None for token auth. Recording after the check would be more accurate.

title: Feature-flagged table renders empty data
body: When 'use-table-widget-visualization' is on, TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with columns=[] and empty data, ignoring result.data and result.meta. Enabling the flag shows blank tables on dashboards.

title: Analytics event key renamed
body: trackAnalytics now uses 'replay.view-html' instead of 'replay.view_html'. Any dashboards or consumers keyed on the old event name will lose data. The key does match the event map entry.

title: Possible KeyError and weak sender check when the integration has no sender
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is read directly. `build_integration` only stores `sender` if state has it, and the sender is set from the webhook. If the integration exists but the installation webhook has not populated `sender`, or `sender` has no `login`, this raises KeyError and the user gets a 500 instead of the error page. Use `.get()` and fail closed with `error()`. Also, the new check applies only when an Integration row already exists. On a fresh install (`Integration.DoesNotExist`, line 481-482) the authenticated user is never compared with anything, so the OAuth step adds no protection in that path.

title: Token exchange request has no error handling and the redirect URI is built unsafely
body: `safe_urlopen` is called outside the try block, so a network error or timeout raises and gives a 500. `get_user_info` is also unguarded. Separately, `state` and `redirect_uri` are put into the authorize URL without URL-encoding. The code also does not send `redirect_uri` or `state` in the token exchange, unlike the standard OAuth2 callback.

title: installation_id taken from the request before the state is validated
body: `OAuthLoginView` binds `installation_id` from `request.GET` into pipeline state before verifying `state` or the code. Any request carrying `installation_id` overwrites the stored value. `GitHubInstallation` then prefers `request.GET` over the stored state, so the value can still be replaced after OAuth. An attacker could therefore authenticate as themselves and then supply a different installation_id.

title: Brittle assertion on call index and no tests for the new failure paths
body: `responses.calls[2]` depends on the exact number of HTTP calls made by the new OAuth step. The PR also adds no tests for a state mismatch, a missing `access_token`, or a missing `login`, even though the description lists these as failure modes. The `test_installation_not_found` test now asserts the generic 'Invalid installation request.' message, which hides the original 404 'installation could not be found' behaviour.

title: KeyError when integration metadata lacks sender
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError (a 500) if the Integration exists without a `sender` entry. Integrations created before the webhook stored the sender, or when `state.get("sender")` was falsy, have no such key. Use `.get` chains and fail with the error page instead.

title: User validation only applies when an Integration already exists
body: When no Integration exists (`Integration.DoesNotExist` at line 481), the pipeline proceeds via `next_step()` without comparing the authenticated GitHub user to the installer. The check only runs for an existing Integration with no OrganizationIntegration. A first-time install by someone other than the installing GitHub user is therefore not validated, which weakens the security fix.

title: Token exchange and user lookup lack error handling
body: `safe_urlopen` is outside the try block, so network errors or timeouts raise 500s. `get_user_info` can also raise on an API error. Both should be caught and turned into the error page. The `state` parameter is also interpolated into the redirect URL without URL-encoding.

title: Non-constant-time comparison and OAuth state reuse
body: The `state` comparison uses plain `!=`, and the code is not tied to the pipeline beyond the signature. The OAuth step also runs again whenever `state` is in the query. A later `installation_id`-only request skips it, so the bound `github_authenticated_user` is never re-verified. Consider `constant_time_compare`.

title: Brittle index into responses.calls
body: `responses.calls[2]` depends on the exact number and order of HTTP calls made by the new OAuth step. Any change to those calls will silently check the wrong request. Find the call by URL instead.

title: User check only runs when an Integration row already exists
body: The authenticated-user comparison sits after the `Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()` early return (line 481-482). On a first-time install, where no Integration row exists yet, the check is skipped. A victim can then be tricked into completing OAuth and the pipeline links an installation_id that someone else installed. The validation described in the PR therefore does not cover the main case.

title: Unguarded access to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]
body: `build_integration` only sets `metadata["sender"]` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy. Integrations created before this change, or without a sender from the webhook, have no `sender` key. This line then raises KeyError (or TypeError if sender is not a dict) and returns a 500 instead of the error page. Use `.get` and fail gracefully.

title: Network calls are unguarded and the OAuth request is not validated
body: `safe_urlopen` is outside the try block, so connection errors or timeouts propagate as a 500. `get_user_info` is also unguarded and may raise on a bad token. The request is a POST with an unchecked status, and the `code` may be None. Wrap these calls and route failures to `error()`.

title: Non-constant-time state comparison and unencoded redirect URL
body: The state is compared with `!=` rather than a constant-time comparison. The authorize URL at line 408 is built by f-string without URL-encoding redirect_uri. The test expects the raw, unencoded redirect_uri in the query, so the URL is fragile.

title: Brittle index into responses.calls
body: `responses.calls[2]` depends on the exact number and order of HTTP calls made by the new OAuth step. It will break if any call is added or removed. In addition, the user-mismatch test never exercises the case where no Integration exists yet, which is the unprotected path.

title: Default `queued` timestamp is evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated when the class is defined, so every AssignmentSource that doesn't pass `queued` gets the same process-start timestamp. The field is meant to record when the assignment was queued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

title: to_dict output contains a datetime that is not JSON serializable
body: `asdict(self)` returns `queued` as a datetime. The dict is passed as a kwarg to `apply_async` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound`. Celery with the JSON serializer will fail or convert it to a string. On deserialization `from_dict` then passes `queued` as a str, which is never validated. Serialize the datetime explicitly (isoformat) and parse it back, or drop the field.

title: assignment_source kwarg passed to all integrations' sync_assignee_outbound
body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`. The abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` accepts `**kwargs`, but concrete implementations (Jira, VSTS, GitHub, etc.) are not updated here. Any implementation without `**kwargs` will raise a TypeError. The diff does not show that these were checked.

title: Inbound sync paths are not tested for passing an assignment source
body: The tests verify the outbound skip when `assignment_source` is passed directly to `assign`. They do not check that `sync_group_assignee_inbound` actually passes `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)`. There is also no test for deassign with a matching source, or for the task-level dict round trip. A regression in the cycle-breaking wiring would go unnoticed.

title: Default `queued` evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource shares the same stale timestamp. It should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Also, `asdict` leaves a datetime in the dict. The dict is passed as Celery task kwargs, which may fail JSON serialization or come back as a string.

title: from_dict round trip is unsafe with serialized `queued`
body: `to_dict` produces a datetime for `queued`. After the task serializer round trip it may arrive as a string or be unserializable. `from_dict` passes it straight into the constructor with no parsing. Unexpected extra keys raise TypeError, which is swallowed and returns None. That silently disables the cycle-breaking.

title: Abstract signatures changed and callers not updated
body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`. The abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` only accepts `**kwargs`, so it is fine there. But the `sync_status_outbound` signature was changed without any caller or implementation being updated, which is unrelated to the fix. Implementations that don't accept the new keyword in a compatible way may break.

title: No test that inbound sync passes the assignment source
body: The tests only call assign with a manually built source. Nothing verifies that `sync_group_assignee_inbound` now passes `AssignmentSource.from_integration`, which is the actual cycle fix. Nothing covers the deassign path with a matching source either.

title: Default `queued` is evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated when the class is defined, so every AssignmentSource built without an explicit value gets the same process-start timestamp. The field is meant to record when the assignment was queued, so the value is wrong and misleading. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

title: to_dict leaves a datetime that may not survive task serialization
body: `asdict` returns `queued` as a datetime object. It is passed in the kwargs of `apply_async`, and Celery with a JSON serializer cannot handle a raw datetime. This can fail at enqueue time or arrive as a string. `from_dict` does `cls(**input_dict)` and would then accept a string `queued` without validation. Serialize `queued` to ISO format and parse it back in `from_dict`.

title: assignment_source kwarg passed to all sync_assignee_outbound implementations
body: The task now always calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`. The abstract signature accepts `**kwargs`, but the diff only changes `sync_status_outbound`, and the concrete integrations (Jira, GitHub, etc.) are not updated or checked. Any implementation without `**kwargs` will raise a TypeError on every outbound assignee sync.

title: where_should_sync does not use the assignment source
body: `where_should_sync` calls `should_sync(key)` without a source, so the new cycle check does not apply there. That is acceptable for inbound sync, but the source filtering exists only on the task path, so the protection is incomplete if other outbound paths call `should_sync`.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract class that cannot be instantiated
body: The handler changed from a concrete DetectorHandler to a StatefulDetectorHandler with an empty body. StatefulDetectorHandler has abstract members (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the new build_occurrence_and_event_data). Any Detector of type metric_alert_fire will raise TypeError when `detector_handler` instantiates it, which breaks process_detectors for these detectors. Previously the handler was instantiable and returned an empty result.

title: New abstract method lacks docstring and no test covers resolve vs occurrence contract
body: build_occurrence_and_event_data is a new abstract hook on StatefulDetectorHandler, but it has no docstring describing its contract (for example, what event_data must contain, or that it is only called for non-OK statuses). Implementers have to read evaluate_group_key_value to find out. Adding an abstract method also breaks every existing subclass at instantiation time.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract class that cannot be instantiated
body: It now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with only `pass`. That base class has abstract members: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values and the new build_occurrence_and_event_data.
