Any call to `detector.detector_handler` for a metric_alert_fire detector will raise TypeError on instantiation. Previously it returned an empty list. This breaks process_detectors for that type. Either keep the old stub handler or implement the abstract methods.

title: New abstract hook has no docstring and lacks a contract for event_data
body: build_occurrence_and_event_data is a new abstract method that every subclass must implement. It has no docstring describing the expected contents of the returned event_data or how new_status maps to priority. The hook is a breaking change for existing subclasses and is undocumented.

title: State committed after Kafka produce, with no failure handling
body: Occurrences are produced inside the loop before handler.commit_state_updates() runs. If a produce raises midway, the dedupe and state updates are never committed. Already-produced occurrences will then be re-emitted on retry. The ordering was the same before, but the new hook makes it a real path.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract class that cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but its body is just `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract members: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data. Instantiating the handler therefore raises TypeError. Detector.detector_handler calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, so any detector of type metric_alert_fire will crash in process_detectors. Previously the class had a concrete (stub) evaluate and worked. Either implement the hooks or keep it as a plain DetectorHandler stub.

title: New abstract method breaks existing StatefulDetectorHandler subclasses
body: build_occurrence_and_event_data is added as an abstractmethod, so every existing subclass must implement it or fail at instantiation. This is the cause of the MetricAlertDetectorHandler breakage. A non-abstract default, or a documented contract, would be safer.

title: Exception from hook could skip commit of state updates
body: Occurrences are produced inside the loop before commit_state_updates. If build_occurrence_and_event_data or produce_occurrence_to_kafka raises, dedupe and state updates for that detector are never committed. The packet is then reprocessed and occurrences can be emitted twice. Conversely, state is committed after the produce calls, so a commit failure after a successful produce leaves the same duplicate risk.

title: Public functions removed/renamed without updating other callers or tests
body: The PR deletes `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, `SimpleCheckIn` and the failure-status maps from `mark_failed.py`, and renames two of them. The diff shows no updates to tests or other modules that import them from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`. Any such import will now raise ImportError. Existing tests that patch `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.*` (e.g. `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` or `create_issue_platform_occurrence`) will also break. Update the callers and tests, or re-export the old names.

title: Copied config is computed but the original config is returned
body: `get_monitor_environment_context` builds a copy of the config with `schedule_type` replaced by its display value. It then returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config`, the unmodified original, so the copy is never used. The intended display-friendly `schedule_type` never reaches the event context. This bug was carried over in the move, so this is a good moment to fix it by returning `config`.

title: Public functions renamed/moved without updating other importers or tests
body: `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, `SimpleCheckIn` and the failure-status maps were removed from `mark_failed.py`. The PR changes only four files, so any other importers, such as tests that patch `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence` or import `get_failure_reason`, will hit ImportError or patch the wrong target. Patched mocks would also silently stop intercepting calls, because the function is now resolved in `incidents.py`. Search the repo for remaining references and update them, or re-export the old names.

title: Copied config is never used; context returns the original config
body: `get_monitor_environment_context` builds `config` as a copy with `schedule_type` replaced by its display value, but the returned dict uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config`. The human-readable schedule_type is therefore dropped. This is a pre-existing bug that the move carried over. It should return `config`.

title: Public functions removed/renamed without updating other callers or tests
body: The PR deletes mark_failed_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence, get_failure_reason, get_monitor_environment_context, the HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP constants and SimpleCheckIn from mark_failed.py. It renames them in the new modules (try_incident_threshold, create_incident_occurrence) and does not re-export them. The diff touches no other files, so existing imports from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed (tests, other modules) will raise ImportError, and tests that patch 'sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.*' will fail. Update the callers and tests, or keep compatibility aliases.

title: Copied config is computed but the uncopied config is returned
body: get_monitor_environment_context copies the config and replaces schedule_type with its display value. The returned dict then uses monitor.config (the original) instead of the local copy, so the display conversion is never applied. This bug existed before the move, but the PR carries it over unchanged. It should return `config`.

title: Restarted flusher gets a new SpansBuffer, losing state of the old one
body: Every restart in _create_process_for_shards builds a new SpansBuffer(shards) and overwrites self.buffers[process_index]. Any in-memory state on the old buffer is dropped. Previously the same buffer was reused across restarts. Also, the old thread (in produce_to_pipe/test mode) is never stopped on restart, so two threads can flush the same shards.

title: Hung threads are not killed on restart; isinstance check uses multiprocessing.Process
body: The kill step checks isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), but processes are created from a spawn context (SpawnProcess), which is not guaranteed to subclass the base multiprocessing.Process class. The kill may be silently skipped, leaving a hung old process running next to its replacement. The same check in join() may skip terminate().

title: join() deadline logic skips terminating remaining processes
body: When the deadline expires, the loop breaks and the remaining processes are never terminated. Also, `deadline = time.time() + timeout if timeout else None` treats timeout=0 as no deadline, so join waits forever.

title: Inconsistent metric tag name
body: The `wait_produce` timer uses the tag key "shards", while the other metrics added in this change use "shard". Dashboards will split across two tag keys.

title: Test relies on real sleep after patching time.sleep
body: monkeypatch replaces time.sleep globally with a no-op, so the added `time.sleep(0.1)` does nothing. The test remains racy because the flusher thread may not have flushed before join. The new limit test only checks the process-to-shard mapping, not restarts or any flush behavior.

title: Restarted flusher gets a new SpansBuffer, losing the old buffer's state
body: Every restart of a process (`_create_process_for_shards`) builds a fresh `SpansBuffer(shards)` and overwrites `self.buffers[process_index]`. Any per-buffer state held by the old one (for example `any_shard_at_limit` and the counters read by `record_stored_segments`) is lost. A related problem is that the old thread or process is not stopped when the cause is `hang` and the process is a thread: the `kill` is skipped for non-`multiprocessing.Process` objects. Two flushers can then run on the same shards at once and produce duplicate segments.

title: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) never matches a SpawnProcess
body: Processes are created from the spawn context, so they are `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` instances. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`, which is a different class (`multiprocessing.context.Process`). The isinstance check in `join` and in `_ensure_processes_alive` is therefore always False. Hung flusher processes are never killed on restart, and `terminate()` is never called on shutdown. Leaked processes then run alongside their replacements.

title: Inconsistent metric tag name: `shards` vs `shard`
body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged `shards`, while the other new metrics use `shard`. Dashboards that group by one tag name will miss the other metric's data.

title: join() timeout handling breaks early and skips terminating the remaining processes
body: When the deadline passes, the loop `break`s and never calls `terminate()` on the remaining processes. They are left running (daemon only). `deadline` is also None when `timeout` is 0, which makes `join` wait indefinitely.

title: Test uses a real time.sleep and does not verify multi-process flushing
body: `time.sleep` is monkeypatched to a no-op at the top of the test, so the added `time.sleep(0.1)` does nothing and the wait is racy. `test_flusher_processes_limit` only checks the shard-to-process mapping. Nothing tests the restart path or backpressure across several processes.

title: Restarted process gets a fresh SpansBuffer, losing state and mixing up metrics
body: `_create_process_for_shards` builds a new `SpansBuffer(shards)` on every restart and overwrites `self.buffers[process_index]`. Any in-memory state held by the old buffer is lost, such as the `any_shard_at_limit` flag and the stored-segment metrics used by `record_stored_segments`. The old process is also only killed if it is a `multiprocessing.Process`. In thread mode, a hung thread is left running next to its replacement, so two flushers then flush the same shards.

title: Restart counter never resets and restart limit is off by one
body: `process_restarts` is only ever incremented, so a process that restarts occasionally over a long uptime eventually exceeds MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS and crashes the whole consumer. The check uses `>` before incrementing, so 11 restarts are allowed rather than 10. This was already the behaviour before the PR, but with several processes the chance of reaching the limit is higher.

title: join with a timeout can skip terminating processes
body: In `join()`, when the deadline passes the loop `break`s before reaching `process.terminate()`. The remaining processes, and the current one if it is still alive, are never terminated. They are left running after shutdown or rebalance and hold Redis and Kafka resources until the daemon flag kills them at interpreter exit. The `join` timeout is also used as a single budget across all processes, so later processes get no time.

title: Inconsistent metric tag name
body: The `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` timer and the `segment_size_bytes` metric use the tag `shard`, but `wait_produce` uses `shards`. This splits dashboards and queries for what is the same dimension. The tag values are also comma-joined shard lists, which makes cardinality grow with the shard assignment.

title: Test relies on real sleeps, and the new test only checks the process map
body: `test_basic` calls `time.sleep(0.1)` after `time.sleep` has been monkeypatched to a no-op, so it does not actually wait. It is therefore not a real synchronisation point and can be flaky. `test_flusher_processes_limit` only checks the process-to-shard mapping. It does not test that flushing works with multiple processes, or that unhealthy-process restarts and backpressure behave correctly across them.

title: Python's hash() on str is randomized per process, so group assignment is not stable
body: `hash(group_key)` uses per-process hash randomization (PYTHONHASHSEED). Within one process the mapping is consistent, so in-process ordering holds. But the 'consistent hashing' docstring is misleading, and the assignment changes on every restart or rebalance. Use a stable hash such as crc32 or md5 if per-queue behaviour must be reproducible.

title: Worker uses queue.ShutDown, which exists only in Python 3.13+
body: `queue.ShutDown` and `Queue.shutdown()` were added in Python 3.13. On earlier versions, `except queue.ShutDown` raises AttributeError and `q.shutdown` fails. The shutdown path swallows the failure via `except Exception`, so workers blocked in `get()` never wake. Shutdown then waits out the join timeout and leaves daemon threads behind. Also, `break` inside the `except queue.ShutDown` around `result_processor` skips nothing useful but is misplaced.

title: Commit happens from a background thread, and state is shared across partition assignments
body: The Arroyo `commit` callable is invoked from a separate thread, but Arroyo strategies are expected to call commit from the main consumer thread. The FixedQueuePool and OffsetTracker are created once by the factory and shared across every `create_with_partitions` call. After a rebalance, stale offsets and `last_committed` from revoked partitions persist. Items still queued from the old strategy can later be committed for partitions no longer owned. Also, `close()` on the strategy shuts down the shared pool, so the next strategy created by the factory after a rebalance gets a dead pool with no workers.

title: Unbounded queues give no backpressure; docstring claims otherwise
body: The queues are unbounded and `submit` never blocks or raises `MessageRejected`. The consumer will keep polling Kafka while a slow worker backs up, so memory grows without limit. The class docstring's claim of 'natural backpressure' is false.

title: get_committable_offsets scans a Python range over offsets
body: The loop iterates `range(start, max_offset+1)` under a lock every second. If offsets have large gaps (compacted or filtered topics), this becomes a very long loop. A gap also stops commits permanently, since a missing offset is never in all_offsets. For example, a skipped or non-contiguous offset blocks all further commits for that partition.

title: Error-handling test asserts the opposite of its docstring
body: The docstring says errors don't block offset commits, but the assertion is `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`. The test passes when nothing is committed, which hides the intended behaviour. It also only waits 2s for a 1s commit loop, so it can pass vacuously.

title: Python's hash() on str is randomized per process
body: `hash(group_key) % num_queues` uses Python's salted string hash. Two consumers, or a consumer after restart, map the same subscription to different queues. Per-subscription ordering therefore holds only inside one process. After a rebalance or restart, in-flight work on the old process and new work on the new one can run out of order. A stable hash such as crc32 or md5 should be used.

title: Partition revocation/rebalance not handled; no backpressure
body: Queues are unbounded `queue.Queue()` and `submit` never blocks or raises MessageRejected. The docstring claims 'Natural backpressure', but a slow worker lets queued items grow without limit in memory. Separately, the shared pool and OffsetTracker outlive the strategy. `create_with_partitions` creates a new strategy on every rebalance, and `close()` shuts down the pool owned by the factory. A second strategy then reuses a shut-down pool with dead workers and stale offsets from revoked partitions.

title: queue.ShutDown requires Python 3.13
body: `queue.ShutDown` and `Queue.shutdown()` exist only in Python 3.13+. On older interpreters, evaluating `except queue.ShutDown` raises AttributeError only when an exception actually occurs. `q.shutdown` is also missing, so the workers never wake from the blocking `get()` and the join times out. Sentry's supported Python version should be checked, or a sentinel used instead.

title: Shutdown can drop or hang on queued items; worker break skips remaining work
body: In `run`, `except queue.ShutDown: break` inside the processing block exits without being a normal path. The `finally` still completes the offset, so an item can be marked complete even though it was not processed. The `shutdown` flag is also checked only between items. The commit thread is joined before the pool is drained, so items finished during shutdown never get committed.

title: Unsynchronized shared dict mutation and O(range) commit scan
body: `all_offsets`, `outstanding` and `last_committed` are defaultdicts. They get mutated, with new keys created, under different per-partition locks. The lock creation itself (`get` then `setdefault`) is fine. `get_committable_offsets` iterates over every integer from start to max_offset. After large gaps, for example compacted topics or offsets skipped by filtering, this becomes very slow while holding the lock that workers need.

title: Errors in result processing still commit offsets (data loss)
body: The worker's `finally` always calls `complete_offset`, even when processing raised. Failed messages are therefore committed and lost. The test `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` asserts that no commit happens, which contradicts this behavior. It passes only because the commit loop runs once per second and the test checks sooner.

title: Error-handling test asserts the wrong thing and is timing-dependent
body: The test claims errors do not block commits for other messages but asserts that nothing is committed. This passes only because the commit loop has not yet run (1s interval) within the roughly 0.3s window. It will be flaky, and it does not verify the intended behavior.

title: queue.ShutDown requires Python 3.13
body: `queue.ShutDown` and `Queue.shutdown()` exist only in Python 3.13+. If the runtime is older, the `except queue.ShutDown` clauses raise AttributeError at the point the exception is evaluated. `q.shutdown(...)` also raises AttributeError, which is swallowed with a logged error, so workers blocked in `get()` never wake and shutdown hangs.

title: Dismissing the backup-codes dialog with Esc/overlay leaves the UI saying 2FA is off
body: `onEnable()` is no longer called when the TOTP code is verified. It now runs only from the "Close" button on the new DisplayBackupCodes step. By then 2FA is already enabled server-side. If the user dismisses the dialog with Escape or by clicking outside, only `onOpenChange` fires. As far as I can tell the parent's `onEnable` is what marks 2FA as enabled, and `onOpenChange` just toggles the modal. The settings switch then shows 2FA as disabled while it is active. `step` is never reset either, so reopening the modal lands back on the backup-codes screen. The step needs to be reset and `onEnable` called whenever the dialog closes from that step, not only from the Close button.

title: "missing_backup_codes" tells users to generate codes in settings, but no such feature exists
body: The message says "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." Codes are only generated inside the 2FA setup endpoint, and there is no UI or API to regenerate them. Every user who enabled 2FA before this migration has `backupCodes = null`. Choosing "Lost access" shows them this message with nothing they can do. To disable 2FA and re-enable it they would need their TOTP code, which is what they lost. Either add a regenerate flow or change the message so it does not point to a nonexistent setting.

title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so a code can be used twice
body: The user row is read at the top of `authorize`. The code is nulled in memory and the whole encrypted blob is written back with an unconditional `update`. Two concurrent logins with the same backup code both read the unconsumed list, both pass `indexOf`, and both succeed. This breaks the "each code can be used exactly once" guarantee. The write can also overwrite a concurrent update to `backupCodes`. Use a transaction with a row lock, or an optimistic check that the stored value is unchanged (compare-and-swap).

title: Backup code comparison is case- and whitespace-sensitive, while the UI placeholder suggests uppercase
body: Codes are generated as lowercase hex (`randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`). The input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`, which suggests uppercase. The comparison only strips `-` and does not lowercase or trim. A user who types or pastes the code in uppercase, or with stray whitespace, gets "Backup code is incorrect". This is a usability problem at exactly the moment the user is locked out. The same logic is duplicated in the disable endpoint.

title: Submitting an empty backup code silently does nothing
body: The login form has `noValidate`, so the `required`, `minLength` and `maxLength` attributes on the BackupCode input are not enforced. If the user submits with the field empty, `credentials.backupCode` is falsy and the server falls into the TOTP branch. It throws `SecondFactorRequired`. The client handles that by calling `setTwoFactorRequired(true)`, which is already true, and shows no error. The user sees no feedback. Show an error message, or validate the field in the zod schema when in lost-access mode.

title: Non-string backupCode in the request body causes an unhandled TypeError (500)
body: `req.body.backupCode` is only checked for truthiness. If a client sends a non-string truthy value such as an object, number or array, `.replaceAll` is not a function and the handler throws an unhandled exception that becomes a 500. The input should be validated as a string (for example with zod) and rejected with a 400/`IncorrectBackupCode`.

title: tabIndex={-1} added to the shared PasswordField toggle button
body: This changes the shared `PasswordField` component, so every password input in the app is affected. Keyboard-only and screen-reader users can no longer tab to the show/hide password toggle. It was probably added to make tabbing through the login form smoother, but it removes an accessible control everywhere. It is unrelated to backup codes and should be scoped to the login page, or reverted.

title: Core backup-code flows (login and disable with a backup code) have no tests
body: The new e2e coverage only checks that the download and copy buttons exist and that the dialog closes. Nothing tests logging in with a backup code, a code being invalidated after use, wrong-code errors, or disabling 2FA with a backup code. Those are the security-sensitive paths this PR adds, and the TODO acknowledges the gap. The download and clipboard contents are not checked either. The first test's `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on a Promise and always passes, so it does not verify 2FA is enabled (the FIXME notes this). The PR checklist also admits no tests were added.

title: Copy button shows success toast without awaiting the clipboard write; codes and blob URL linger after close
body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a promise that is neither awaited nor caught. The "Backup codes copied!" toast shows even if the write is rejected (permission denied, insecure context). The user may believe the codes are saved when they are not. Separately, `resetState()` does not clear `backupCodes`, `secret`, `dataUri`, or `backupCodesUrl`. The Blob object URL containing all plaintext codes is never revoked on close or unmount, so the secrets stay in memory until the next setup.

title: Backup-code login can skip password verification by also sending a dummy totpCode
body: The password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121, unchanged). The new branch at line 131 is chosen when `credentials.backupCode` is present, and it never looks at `totpCode`. An attacker can send `email` + any non-empty `totpCode` + a valid `backupCode`. The password check is skipped and the backup-code branch authenticates the request. A single secret (a 40-bit backup code) then replaces both password and second factor. The PR adds a new credential path on top of this guard without tightening it. Fix: always verify the password for CAL-provider users when no external TOTP/JWT flow is in progress, and make the backup-code branch independent of `totpCode`.

title: Closing the dialog on the backup-codes step skips onEnable/resetState
body: 2FA is already enabled server-side once the TOTP code is verified, but `onEnable()` and `resetState()` now run only from the "Close" button on the DisplayBackupCodes step. The Cancel button is hidden there. If the user dismisses the dialog via Escape, the overlay or the X (`onOpenChange`), the parent is never told 2FA was enabled, so the settings UI can still show it as off. The wizard also stays on `DisplayBackupCodes`, so reopening it shows stale codes. The user may never have saved the codes either. The dismiss path should be handled the same way as Close, or dismissal should be blocked on this step.

title: "missing_backup_codes" message points to a settings feature that does not exist
body: Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have `backupCodes = null`. When they click "Lost access" they get "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." There is no UI or endpoint to generate or regenerate backup codes for an already-enabled account. The only way to get codes is to disable 2FA, which requires a TOTP code or backup code they no longer have. The message gives an impossible instruction. Either add a regenerate flow or change the message to something actionable.

title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: The code reads the encrypted blob, finds the index, nulls the entry, re-encrypts and writes the whole blob back, with no lock or compare-and-swap. Two concurrent logins using the same single-use code can both pass the `indexOf` check before either write lands. Both then succeed, violating the "can be used exactly once" guarantee. Concurrent logins using different codes can also overwrite each other's update and resurrect a used code. Use a transaction or optimistic concurrency, for example update where `backupCodes` equals the value that was read.

title: Unvalidated backupCode type can crash the disable endpoint
body: `req.body.backupCode` is only checked for truthiness, then `.replaceAll` is called on it. A non-string truthy value (number, object, array) throws a TypeError and returns a 500 instead of a 400 `IncorrectBackupCode`. Validate that it is a string before use, and ideally trim it.

title: Empty backup code submit silently does nothing on the login form
body: The login form uses `noValidate`, so the `required`/`minLength` attributes on the BackupCode input are not enforced. Submitting an empty backup code sends `backupCode: ""`, which is falsy. The server falls through to the TOTP branch and returns `SecondFactorRequired`. The handler then just calls `setTwoFactorRequired(true)` (already true), with no error shown. The user sees nothing happen. Handle the empty case client-side or show an error.

title: No test coverage for logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
body: The core new behaviour is untested, and the PR checklist admits no tests were added. The e2e changes only click download/copy/close on the new screen, and the file/clipboard contents are TODOs. Nothing exercises backup-code login, one-time consumption of a code, disabling 2FA with a backup code, or the MissingBackupCodes/IncorrectBackupCode paths. The first test ("enable and login") never closes the new backup-codes dialog. Its `isChecked()` assertion is always truthy, as the FIXME admits, so it does not verify the new step. Given that this is authentication code, tests for the login and disable paths should be included.

title: Copy button shows success toast without awaiting the clipboard write
body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a promise that is neither awaited nor caught, and the success toast is shown immediately. If the write is rejected (permission denied, non-secure context, unfocused document), the user is told the codes were copied when they were not. For one-time recovery codes this is risky. Await the promise and show the toast only on success, with an error path otherwise.

title: tabIndex={-1} on the shared password visibility toggle removes it from keyboard navigation
body: This is a shared `PasswordField` used across the whole app, and the change makes the show/hide-password button unreachable by keyboard for every form. It is unrelated to backup codes and is an accessibility regression. If the goal was to improve tab order on the login or disable-2FA forms, apply it locally instead.

title: Backup-code login can skip the password check by sending a dummy totpCode
body: The password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` branch runs before any TOTP validation and never looks at `totpCode`. A request with `email`, a bogus non-empty `totpCode` (e.g. "000000") and a valid `backupCode` skips password verification and then authenticates on the backup code alone. Before this PR a bogus `totpCode` failed the TOTP check. Now it does not, because the backup branch short-circuits it. Backup codes are static, long-lived secrets, so this makes them a standalone credential that replaces the password. The backup branch should verify the password itself, or the password skip should be conditioned on a TOTP code that is actually validated.

title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: The codes are decrypted, the matching entry is set to null, and the whole array is re-encrypted and written back, with no transaction or compare-and-set. Two concurrent logins with the same code can both read it as unused and both succeed, so 'usable exactly once' is not guaranteed. Concurrent consumption of two different codes can also overwrite each other. The second write restores the code the first request just burned. An atomic update guarded on the previous ciphertext value, or a transaction with row locking, would fix this.

title: Dismissing the dialog on the backup-codes step skips onEnable/resetState
body: After a successful enable, the modal moves to `DisplayBackupCodes` and hides the Cancel button. The dialog is still dismissable through `onOpenChange` (Escape or clicking the overlay). That path calls neither `onEnable()` nor `resetState()`. The parent is not told 2FA is now enabled, so the settings switch can stay stale until a reload. When the modal is reopened the component may still be on the backup-codes step with the old codes. Backup codes cannot be shown again, so a user who dismisses by accident can lose them. The close handler should route through the same cleanup as the Close button, or the dialog should not be dismissable on this step.

title: Backup codes and blob URL are never cleared or revoked when the modal closes
body: `resetState` only resets the password, error message and step. The plaintext `backupCodes`, `secret` and `dataUri` stay in component state, and the Blob object URL created in `handleSetup` is only revoked if setup is run again. It is not revoked on close or unmount. The sensitive codes therefore stay in memory and the blob URL leaks for the life of the page. Clear this state in `resetState` and revoke the URL in cleanup.

title: Copy button shows success toast without awaiting clipboard write
body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a promise that rejects on permission denial or in non-secure contexts. It is neither awaited nor caught, and the 'Backup codes copied!' toast is shown unconditionally. A user can believe the codes were copied when they were not, and the codes cannot be retrieved again afterwards.

title: missing_backup_codes message points to a settings feature that does not exist
body: Users who enabled 2FA before this PR have no `backupCodes`. If they click 'Lost access' on login or in the disable modal, they get 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' This PR adds no UI or endpoint to generate backup codes for an already-enabled account. Codes are only created in `setup.ts` when enabling 2FA. The message sends users to a nonexistent action, and for them backup-code recovery is simply unavailable. The text should be accurate, or a regenerate flow should be added.

title: No tests for the actual backup-code behavior; first e2e test left on backup-code screen
body: The new logic is not covered: login with a backup code, single-use enforcement, wrong or missing codes, and disabling 2FA with a backup code. The TODO on line 12 admits this. The 'enable and login' test never closes the new backup-codes dialog, and its `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` assertion is vacuous because it asserts on a Promise (acknowledged by the new FIXME). The security-sensitive server paths in `authorize` and `disable.ts` have no automated coverage.

title: Unrelated change removes the password show/hide toggle from keyboard navigation globally
body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the toggle inside the shared `PasswordField` affects every password field in the app. Keyboard and screen-reader users can no longer tab to the show/hide button, an accessibility regression unrelated to backup codes. Nothing in this feature requires it, so it should be scoped to the places that need it or dropped.

title: Unvalidated backupCode type can crash the endpoint with a 500
body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes a string. A non-string JSON value such as a number or object that is truthy throws a TypeError and returns an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 `IncorrectBackupCode`. The endpoint also has no rate limiting for repeated backup-code guesses, unlike the login path, which calls `checkRateLimitAndThrowError`.

title: TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty/null and location is Google Meet
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the array is empty or null. The next line then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. handleNewBooking can set `destinationCalendar: null` and other handlers set `[]`. This is exactly the case the fallback is meant for: Google Meet selected with no Google calendar. It now throws instead of falling back to Cal Video, so the booking creation fails. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

title: Video references lose their credentialId
body: The old code was `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`, so video results kept `result.credentialId`. The new code is `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. The ternary branches were effectively swapped for non-calendar results. Video BookingReferences are now saved without a credentialId. handleCancelBooking only deletes the video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so cancelling no longer deletes the video meeting for new bookings. Should be `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : result.credentialId` (i.e. `result.credentialId`).

title: Fallback lookup in updateEvent/deleteEvent can never match
body: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only runs the `find` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then looks for a calendar whose externalId equals that falsy value, which never matches. The fallback therefore always returns `undefined`; the old code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. In updateEvent, `calendarId` becomes undefined for any reference without an externalCalendarId (legacy bookings), and the Google API call fails. The same pattern in deleteEvent (line ~315) silently drops the configured destination calendar and falls back to `primary`. Fall back to the main host's destination calendar's externalId instead.

title: createEvent only matches destination calendar by credentialId; legacy destinations go to "primary"
body: `selectedCalendar` is now found only via `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. EventManager still has a branch for destination calendars with no `credentialId`, where it calls `createEvent(c, event)` for every credential of that integration. For those, no destination matches, so the event is inserted into `primary` instead of the configured `destinationCalendar.externalId` as before. This is a behaviour regression for existing users whose DestinationCalendar rows lack a credentialId. Fall back to the matching-integration destination's externalId when no credentialId match exists.

title: Hangout-link patch uses undefined calendarId
body: Previously `selectedCalendar` defaulted to `"primary"`, so the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` had a valid calendarId. Now `selectedCalendar` can be `undefined` (insert uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`), but the patch still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. When no destination matches the credential, the event is inserted into primary, but the patch that adds the Meet link to the description fails or targets nothing. Use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` value for the patch.

title: Non-Google calendar services use the main host's destination for every credential
body: EventManager now calls `createEvent` once per destination calendar, passing the whole event with all hosts' destination calendars. Only Google uses the `credentialId` argument to pick its own destination. Office365 (here), Lark, and CalDAV (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts`) always use the first entry (`mainHostDestinationCalendar`) regardless of whose credential is being used. For a collective event where a team member has Office365/CalDAV/Lark and the main host has a different calendar, the member's service is given the main host's externalId. For Office365 this POSTs to `/me/calendars/<wrong id>/events` and fails. For CalDAV the filter matches no calendar, nothing is created, and the call still reports success. The multi-host fix therefore only works for Google.

title: Recurring-cancel deletion now repeats once per calendar reference
body: The calendar-reference handling was changed from `find` to a `for...of` over all `_calendar` references. The recurring branch (`recurringEvent && recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings`) inside the loop deletes events for every user credential and every updated booking, independent of the current `reference`. With N calendar references (now common with multiple hosts), the full set of deletions runs N times. This causes duplicate delete calls and rate-limit or error noise for providers that don't treat a missing event as success. The recurring deletion should run once outside the per-reference loop.

title: Unrelated change inverts organization slug / requestedSlug logic
body: The old code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })`. The `slug` column was set only when billing is disabled, and deferred via `requestedSlug` when billing is enabled. The new code is `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, which inverts the first condition. With billing disabled (self-hosted), organizations are now created without a slug. With billing enabled, the slug is set before payment while `requestedSlug` is also set. This has nothing to do with destination calendars and should be reverted or split into its own PR.

title: Team members' destination calendars silently dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op. Collective team members who do have destination calendars get no calendar events, and EventManager falls back to the generic path. Initialise the array (e.g. `[]`) and push to it, rather than relying on a possibly-null value. Duplicates are also possible if a member's destination equals the organizer's.

title: Unrelated rewrite of loadUsers changes selection and error behaviour
body: `loadUsers` was rewritten as part of this PR. The dynamic-user query no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug } }`. An empty or undefined `dynamicUserList` now throws, and the catch turns it into an HttpError 500 "Unable to load users". Neither change is described by the PR or needed for the destination-calendar work, and the dropped organization field may be needed by downstream code. This should be reverted or justified and tested separately.

title: Webhook/API payload shape for destinationCalendar changes from object to array
body: `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` is serialized into webhook payloads (see the updated e2e expectation `destinationCalendar: []`). Changing it from a single object to an array is a breaking contract change for webhook subscribers and API consumers. The PR is labelled non-breaking and has no migration note. It is also inconsistent: BOOKING_CREATED/REQUESTED can still emit `null` (handleNewBooking) while other flows emit `[]`.

title: No tests for new multi-destination calendar logic
body: The PR changes the core `CalendarEvent` contract and adds multi-credential create/update/delete flows across EventManager, CalendarManager, handleCancelBooking, and several calendar services. No unit or e2e tests cover multiple destination calendars, the credential DB-lookup fallback, or the empty/null cases. The checklist states no tests were added. The regressions above (Meet fallback crash, video credentialId, Google fallback lookup) would have been caught by basic tests.

title: updateLocation references lose externalCalendarId and credentialId for calendar updates
body: `referencesToCreate` now uses `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. `CalendarManager.updateEvent` results contain neither field, so calendar references created by `updateLocation` (and any update results) have both undefined. Previously they were filled from the event's destinationCalendar. Those references then take the legacy 'run through every credential' path on cancellation instead of using the exact credential and calendar.

title: TypeError when destinationCalendar is null/empty and location is Google Meet
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the event has no destination calendar (handleNewBooking now sets `null` in that case). The next line then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. Any Google Meet booking where neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar will throw. The previous code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` and fell back to Cal Video. It should be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

title: Video references no longer persist credentialId
body: The old code was `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`, so video results kept their own credentialId. The new code is `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, which drops it for video results. handleCancelBooking only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so cancelling a booking will no longer delete the Daily/Zoom/etc. meeting. Update and reschedule lookups that rely on the reference credential are affected too. The ternary should keep `result.credentialId` in the non-calendar branch.

title: Team members' destination calendars silently dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The following `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so collective hosts who do have calendars never get an event. This is exactly the scenario the PR is meant to fix. The array should be initialised to `[]` (not `null`) and the team destination calendars concatenated into it. The in-place `push` onto an array that is also exposed on `evt` is also fragile.

title: Unrelated change inverts organization slug / requestedSlug logic
body: The original code set `slug` only when `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` and `requestedSlug` only when billing was enabled. The new code sets `slug` when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is true, so with billing on the org gets its final slug immediately without payment/verification. With billing off, no slug is set at all. This flips the behaviour and has nothing to do with destination calendars. It looks like an accidental or merge-leftover change and should be reverted.

title: Hangout-link patch uses undefined calendarId when no destination matches
body: `selectedCalendar` is now `undefined` when no destination calendar matches the credentialId. The insert falls back to `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. The patch then targets an undefined calendar and fails, or a required-parameter error is raised, so the description with the Meet link is never updated. Previously `selectedCalendar` defaulted to `"primary"`. The same resolved id should be used for both calls.

title: Destination calendars without credentialId no longer used when creating Google events
body: The target calendar is now chosen only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. EventManager still handles destination calendars that have no credentialId by creating the event with each credential of the matching integration. For those legacy destinations nothing matches, so Google events are always created in `primary` instead of the configured `destination.externalId`. This is a regression for existing single-host users. The code should fall back to the main destination calendar's externalId when no credentialId match exists.

title: Fallback calendar lookup in updateEvent/deleteEvent is dead logic
body: The expression is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. In the else branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the `find` compares against a falsy value and always returns `undefined`. The old fallback to the event's destination calendar externalId is gone. `updateEvent` now calls `events.update` with `calendarId: undefined` for references lacking externalCalendarId, which fails. `deleteEvent` (line 317) silently uses `primary`. The fallback should use the main destination calendar, e.g. `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

title: CalDAV creates no event for second host's credential in collective events
body: `createEvent` filters the account's calendars by the first (main host) destination calendar's externalId. EventManager now calls `createEvent` once per host credential, passing the whole destination list. For a second host's CalDAV credential, none of its calendars match the main host's externalId, so the filtered list is empty, `Promise.all([])` resolves, and `createEvent` returns success without creating anything. That host silently gets no calendar event. The method needs to use the destination calendar belonging to the credential being used (as Google does with `credentialId`).

title: Office365/Lark use the first host's calendar id with every host's credential
body: Both services take `event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId` as the calendar id, regardless of which credential the call is made with. In a collective event with multiple hosts, EventManager invokes `createEvent` per host credential. Office365 then POSTs to `/me/calendars/<host A's calendar id>/events` using host B's token, which gets a 404/403 or lands in the wrong calendar. Lark's `createEvent` and `createAttendees` do the same with `calendarId`. The new `credentialId` argument (added to the interface) is ignored, so multi-host support only works for Google.

title: Unrelated loadUsers rewrite changes behavior and drops the organization select
body: The `loadUsers` refactor is unrelated to destination calendars and alters behavior. For dynamic groups it no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`, so anything downstream reading `user.organization` for dynamic users loses data. It now throws for an empty `dynamicUserList` instead of returning an empty list. The catch block converts every non-Http/Prisma error into a generic 500 "Unable to load users", which hides the real cause. This should be split into its own PR or reverted.

title: Recurring cancellation block now runs once per calendar reference
body: The recurring-cancellation branch (deleting every `updatedBookings` calendar event across all of the organizer's calendar credentials) now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. With N calendar references (the multi-host case) it runs N times, issuing duplicate deletes that can fail on non-Google calendars. It also only iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and `updBooking.references.find(...)` (first calendar ref only), so other hosts' events for the remaining recurring instances are still not removed. The bulk deletion should be hoisted out of the loop and cover all references and credentials.

title: destinationCalendar changes from object to array in webhook payloads and public types
body: Webhook payloads spread the `CalendarEvent` (`...evt`), so the `destinationCalendar` field delivered to subscribers silently changes from an object/null to an array. Within the PR it is also inconsistent: the BOOKING_REJECTED e2e now expects `[]`, while BOOKING_CREATED/REQUESTED still expect `null`. This is a breaking change for webhook consumers and for any other code or templates reading `calEvent.destinationCalendar.<field>`. It should be called out or normalised, and docs updated.

title: No tests for multi-destination calendar create/update/cancel flow
body: The PR rewrites how calendar events are created, updated and deleted across EventManager, CalendarManager, handleNewBooking, handleCancelBooking and several CalendarServices. This includes new DB credential fallbacks and per-credential calendar selection. The author states no tests were added. The regressions above (null destination, video credentialId, legacy destinations without credentialId) would be caught by basic unit tests for `EventManager.create` and `updateAllCalendarEvents`.

title: Null dereference when event has no destinationCalendar and location is Google Meet
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when `destinationCalendar` is null or empty. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. The old code was `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which was safe. Any Google Meet booking where neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar now throws a TypeError in `EventManager.create`, instead of falling back to Cal Video. It should be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

title: Video references lose their credentialId
body: The old code was `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`. The new code is `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so non-calendar (video) results now get `credentialId: undefined`. `BookingReference` rows for video meetings are saved without a credential. `handleCancelBooking` only deletes the meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so cancelling a booking silently skips deleting the Daily/Zoom/etc. meeting. The non-calendar branch should still use `result.credentialId`.

title: Hangout-link patch uses undefined calendarId when falling back to primary
body: `selectedCalendar` is now `undefined` when no destination calendar matches the credentialId. The insert falls back with `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` still passes the raw `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. Previously `selectedCalendar` defaulted to `"primary"`. The patch that writes the Meet link into the description now fails or targets the wrong calendar whenever the fallback is used.

title: Destination calendars without a credentialId no longer route to their externalId
body: The selected calendar is now found only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, destination calendars without a `credentialId` take the else branch and call `createEvent(c, event)`. That is a legacy but still supported path. For those, the destination's `externalId` is never matched, so the event is created on `"primary"`. Before this change the destination's `externalId` was always used. Users who selected a non-primary calendar will now have events land on their primary calendar.

title: Dead/incorrect fallback lookup in updateEvent and deleteEvent
body: The fallback is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. In the else branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the find compares against a falsy value and effectively never matches (it returns `undefined`). The old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Updating or deleting a reference that has no stored `externalCalendarId` now hits an undefined calendar (update) or `primary` (delete) instead of the destination calendar. The same pattern appears in `deleteEvent` (~line 317).

title: Multi-host creation uses the first host's calendar id with every host's credential
body: `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now calls `createEvent(credential, event, ...)` once per destination, using that destination's credential. But the same `event.destinationCalendar` array is passed each time. Office365 (and Lark) always take `[mainHostDestinationCalendar]`, the first entry, and ignore the credential/destination being processed. For the second host's credential, it POSTs to `/me/calendars/<first host's calendar id>/events` with the second host's token. That fails (404) or targets the wrong calendar. Only the Google service was updated to select by `credentialId`, so collective events for non-Google hosts are still not handled.

title: CalDAV/Apple createEvent filters on the first host's calendar for every host's credential
body: `calendars` is listed with the current credential, then filtered to `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` where `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is always the first array entry. When EventManager invokes this service with the second host's credential, none of that account's calendars match the first host's externalId. The filter yields an empty list, `Promise.all([])` resolves, and `createEvent` returns a 'successful' result without creating anything. The second host silently gets no event.

title: Unrelated change inverts the slug condition when creating an organization
body: The original was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`. It is now `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which drops the negation. With team billing enabled, the slug is now written immediately although only `requestedSlug` should be set until payment. With billing disabled, the organization is created with no slug at all. This is unrelated to the PR's purpose and appears to be an accidental regression in organization creation.

title: Team members' destination calendars are dropped when the organizer has none
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so collective hosts' calendars are never added. This is the exact scenario the PR targets (other hosts having calendars). Build the array first (`[...main, ...teamDestinationCalendars]`) instead of pushing into a possibly-null value. Also, only `destinationCalendar[0]` is connected to the Booking row, so any flow that rebuilds the event from the DB later sees at most one calendar.

title: Unrelated loadUsers rewrite changes selected fields and error behavior
body: The `loadUsers` refactor is not related to destination calendars. It removes `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-group user query. Any downstream code reading `user.organization?.slug` for dynamic bookings will now get undefined or a type error. It also now throws for an empty `dynamicUserList`, and the surrounding try/catch turns that into a generic 500 'Unable to load users', where it previously fell through to normal 'no users' handling. It also adds `firstName`/`lastName: ""` to team members, which are not part of the `Person` type. These behavior changes should be separated from this fix or justified.

title: Recurring-cancel branch now runs once per calendar reference and only handles the first ref per booking
body: The code now iterates over every calendar reference. Inside that loop, the recurring branch deletes events for every calendar credential across all `updatedBookings`, using `updBooking.references.find(...)`, which takes only the first calendar reference. With N calendar references per booking (the new multi-host case), the same deletion runs N times, producing duplicate API calls. Meanwhile the other hosts' references are never targeted, because `find` returns only the first and only the user's own credentials are iterated. The recurring branch should be hoisted out of the per-reference loop and iterate all references.

title: Flows that rebuild the event from the DB only get a single destination calendar
body: Only `destinationCalendar[0]` is persisted on the Booking. Confirmation, Stripe/PayPal payment webhooks and similar flows rebuild `evt.destinationCalendar` as a one-element array (booking's or organizer's calendar). For collective events that require confirmation or payment, `EventManager.create` runs later with only the main host's calendar, so the other hosts never receive the calendar event. The multi-host fix therefore only works for immediately-confirmed bookings.

title: Webhook payload shape for destinationCalendar changes from object to array
body: `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` is spread directly into webhook payloads. Changing it from a single object to an array silently changes the public webhook contract (BOOKING_CREATED, CANCELLED, REJECTED, etc.). Existing subscribers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` will break. The e2e test was adjusted to match, and null/`[]` are now used inconsistently across events. The payload should be mapped back to the old shape or the change documented as breaking.

title: No tests for the new multi-destination create/update/cancel logic
body: The PR changes `destinationCalendar` to an array across about 20 files and adds new branching (credential lookup from DB, per-reference updates and deletes, per-credential Google calendar selection). The PR checklist states no tests were added. The regressions listed above (null deref on Meet fallback, lost video credentialId, undefined calendarId) would be caught by basic unit tests of `EventManager.create`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` and `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`.

title: Google credential saved as the zod safeParse result object instead of the key data
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed data. The old code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which returned the key directly. Now `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` followed by `data: { key }` writes `{ success: true, data: {...} }` into `credential.key`. On the next load, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails because access_token, refresh_token and the other fields are no longer at the top level. This happens in the default non-sync path, so every Google Calendar credential is corrupted the first time its token refreshes. The code should store `key.data`.

title: Sync-mode refresh returns a fetch Response but code reads `res.data`
body: With credential sync enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response`. The code then reads `res?.data` and `token.access_token`. A `Response` has no `.data`, so this throws a TypeError. The surrounding catch swallows any error other than `invalid_grant` and returns the stale auth, so Google Calendar silently never refreshes in sync mode. The Response needs `.json()`, and its shape must be mapped to the gaxios `{ data }` form.

title: Hubspot treats the sync endpoint's fetch Response as a HubspotToken and persists it
body: When sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response`, but the result is typed and used as `HubspotToken`. `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` is undefined, so `expiryDate` becomes NaN. `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` is undefined. The `Response` object is then written to `credential.key` (`as any`), which serializes to roughly `{}` and wipes the stored Hubspot token. The body must be parsed and mapped to the token shape before use.

title: Axios-style callers read `.data` from the fetch Response returned in sync mode
body: Zoho CRM here, and Zoho Bigin in its CalendarService, call `refreshOAuthTokens` and then access `.data.error`, `.data.expires_in` and `.data.access_token`. Their normal path returns an axios response, but in sync mode the helper returns a `fetch` `Response`, so `.data` is undefined. This throws a TypeError (swallowed by the catch in Zoho CRM). Credential syncing therefore cannot work for these apps. The helper should return a normalized shape, or each caller must parse the body.

title: Credential ID passed where the Cal.com user ID is expected
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's row id as the third argument, which is `userId`. In sync mode this posts `calcomUserId=<credential id>` to the self-hoster's endpoint. The endpoint will return tokens for a different user, or none, so one user's tokens can be attached to another's credential. The refresh also runs for team credentials, which should have no user id. `credential.userId` has to be passed instead, and `biginAuth`/`refreshAccessToken` must carry it through.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses nonsensical computed keys
body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key `"[object Object]"`, not 'any key'. The second silently overrides the first, so the schema is effectively `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`. Zod strips unknown keys, so the parsed data contains only `access_token`. The expiry and every other field from the sync endpoint are dropped, contrary to the comment about numeric expiry. Callers then compute `expires_in * 1000` as NaN (Zoom) or never update the expiry (Office365). A real catch-all needs `.passthrough()` or `.catchall(...)`.

title: Placeholder refresh_token "refresh_token" overwrites real refresh tokens
body: If the response has no `refresh_token`, the helper sets the literal string `"refresh_token"`. Callers such as Office365 (`{...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data}`; schema marks refresh_token optional) and Zoom (`key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token`) then persist this placeholder over the user's real refresh token. This applies in sync mode, where the minimal schema strips everything but access_token. It can also apply in normal mode when the provider omits a rotated token. Later refreshes without sync will fail permanently. The placeholder should not be merged into stored credentials.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported
body: The new refresh logic calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file does not import `@calcom/prisma`. This fails type-check/build, and at runtime throws a ReferenceError inside `getClient`. That rejects `this.conn`, so every Salesforce operation fails.

title: Salesforce refreshes the token on every instantiation but builds the connection with the stale access token
body: `getClient` (run in every constructor call) now POSTs a refresh request to Salesforce and stores the new token. The `jsforce.Connection` is still built with `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` from the old key, so the connection uses the pre-refresh token rather than `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`. This also adds a network call and DB write on each service creation, regardless of expiry. It bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync does not apply to Salesforce. The check `response.statusText !== "OK"` is unreliable because HTTP/2 responses have an empty statusText, and `response.ok` should be used.

title: Sync endpoint is called unauthenticated, with no error handling or timeout
body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` carries no secret or auth header. Anyone who can reach it could request tokens for any `calcomUserId`, and Cal.com cannot prove who it is. The raw `Response` is returned without checking `response.ok`, so a 4xx/5xx body is passed to callers, which parse it as a token response. There is no timeout. At minimum the webhook secret or an auth header should be sent and non-OK responses rejected.

title: Webhook secret compared with `!==` (not constant-time) and no HTTP method check
body: The shared secret is compared with a plain `!==`, which is not timing-safe. A header sent as an array also fails to match. The handler accepts any HTTP method, not only POST. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers and reject non-POST requests.

title: Invalid body, bad ciphertext or bad JSON produce unhandled 500s
body: `schema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError for malformed input, and `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` throw on a wrong key or bad payload. None are caught, so authenticated callers get an opaque 500 with a stack trace instead of a 400. Use `safeParse` and wrap decryption and parsing in try/catch to return a clear 400. The decrypted `keys` are also stored without any validation of shape.

title: find-then-create is racy and can create duplicate credentials
body: `findFirst` followed by `update` or `create` is not atomic. Two concurrent webhooks for the same user and app both see no credential and both create one, yielding duplicates. Later reads use `findFirst`, so which credential gets refreshed or used is nondeterministic. Use a transaction or a unique constraint.

title: Webex still validates the refresh response with the full schema, so sync mode always fails
body: Zoom, Office365 and Salesforce route the refresh response through `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, but Webex still uses `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse`. That schema requires scope, token_type, refresh_token and refresh_token_expires_in. The documented sync response contains only the access token and expiry, so with sync enabled the parse fails with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" and Webex cannot refresh.

title: No tests for the new sync flow
body: The PR adds a credential-sync webhook, `refreshOAuthTokens` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` across about ten providers without any tests, and the PR checklist says none were added. The bugs above (wrong stored key shape, bad schema keys, wrong user id, `.data` on a Response) would be caught by basic unit tests of the helpers and the webhook handler.

title: Google credential is saved as the zod SafeParse result object instead of the key
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the safeParse result (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed data. The old code was `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`, which returned the plain key. Now `key` is `{ success: true, data: {...} }` and is written to `credential.key` via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. After the first token refresh every Google Calendar credential is corrupted. The next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in `googleAuth` fails, so Google Calendar breaks for any user whose token refreshes. The fix is to pass `key.data` (or unwrap the result) when saving.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys that evaluate to "[object Object]", so expiry and other fields are stripped
body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are computed property keys. A zod type has no custom `toString`, so both evaluate to the literal string `"[object Object]"`. The second entry overwrites the first, so the schema is effectively `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown? }`. `z.object` strips unknown keys by default. In credential-sync mode the parsed data therefore contains only `access_token`: `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, `scope`, `token_type` and the rest are dropped. Callers such as Zoom (`newTokens.expires_in`) then compute `Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)`, which is `NaN`, and store a broken `expiry_date`. Salesforce loses `instance_url` the same way. The comment says "any property with a number is the expiry", but this does not implement that. Use `.passthrough()` or `.catchall(z.unknown())`, and define the expiry field explicitly.

title: Placeholder refresh_token is injected in every mode and can overwrite a real refresh token
body: `if (!data.refresh_token) data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` runs for the normal (non-sync) path too, not only in credential-sync mode. For the Office 365 calendar flow, `refresh_token` is optional in `refreshTokenResponseSchema`. If Microsoft omits it from the refresh response, the merge `{...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data}` replaces the user's real refresh token with the string `"refresh_token"`. Every later refresh then fails and the credential is permanently broken. In sync mode the placeholder also overwrites the stored token in Zoom (`key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token`). The placeholder should only be applied in sync mode, and it should never overwrite an existing value.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported in the Salesforce CalendarService
body: The new refresh block calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but the file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This is a TypeScript error and a runtime `ReferenceError`. `getClient` runs in the constructor, so every Salesforce calendar operation fails.

title: Salesforce refresh is unconditional, bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, and the new token is not used
body: `getClient` now calls `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` on every instantiation, whether or not the token is expired. That adds a network call and a DB write per use, and risks rate limiting. It does not go through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync is never used for Salesforce and the self-hoster's endpoint is ignored. The `jsforce.Connection` is still built with the old `credentialKey.access_token` rather than the freshly fetched one. `response.statusText !== "OK"` is unreliable because HTTP/2 responses have an empty `statusText`, so it would throw 400 even on success. In sync mode the stripped schema also drops `instance_url` from the stored key.

title: credentialId is passed where refreshOAuthTokens expects the Cal.com userId
body: `refreshAccessToken(credentialId, credentialKey)` only has the credential id, and that value is passed as the third argument (`userId`) of `refreshOAuthTokens`. In sync mode the POST sends `calcomUserId=<credentialId>`, so the self-hoster's endpoint returns tokens for the wrong user, or none. When `userId` happens to be falsy the sync is silently skipped. The credential's `userId` must be threaded through to this method.

title: Sync mode returns a raw fetch Response, but several callers expect their SDK/axios result shape
body: In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response`. In non-sync mode it returns whatever each caller's `refreshFunction` returns. Several callers rely on the latter shape and break in sync mode. Google reads `res?.data`, Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `tokenInfo.data` (axios shape), and HubSpot expects a token object with `expiresIn` and `accessToken`. With a `Response` these are all `undefined`: Google throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'access_token')`, and the Zoho and HubSpot flows fail or log errors. The helper needs to normalise the response (check `response.ok`, parse the JSON, and wrap it to match each caller's expected shape). The unauthenticated POST also has no error handling for non-2xx responses.

title: Webex still validates the refresh response with the strict schema, so sync mode always fails
body: Webex was wired to `refreshOAuthTokens` but not to `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. The synced response is documented as containing only the access token and expiry. `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` requires `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token` and `refresh_token_expires_in`, so `safeParse` fails and the code rejects with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Credential sync therefore cannot work for Webex.

title: Behavior change: a bad refresh response now throws, and the diagnostic log was dropped
body: Previously a failed `safeParse` was tolerated: the code logged the zod error and the MS response, then continued with the existing credentials. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` now throws a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned", and the `console.error` with the zod error and MS response was removed. Failures are harder to debug, and the leftover `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` check is now dead code. This change in error semantics for non-sync users is not mentioned in the PR.

title: Unhandled exceptions from body validation, decryption and JSON parsing produce 500s
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on a malformed body, so the caller gets an opaque 500 instead of a 400. `symmetricDecrypt(...)` and `JSON.parse(...)` at lines 57-59 can also throw if the key is wrong or the payload is not valid JSON. Use `safeParse` and try/catch around decrypt and parse, and return 400 with a clear message. Otherwise self-hosters cannot tell a bad payload from a server fault, and a bad or missing `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` shows up only as a 500.

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==`
body: This endpoint writes arbitrary OAuth credentials for any user and is protected only by a shared secret. The secret is compared with `!==`, which is not timing-safe. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. There is also no method check (any HTTP verb is accepted) and no rate limiting.

title: No tests for the new credential webhook or the refresh/sync logic
body: The PR adds a credential-writing webhook and changes token refresh in about ten apps, but ships no tests. The PR checklist says tests were not added. The bugs found above (corrupted Google key, stripped schema fields, wrong user id) would have been caught by basic unit tests of `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens` and the webhook handler.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses `z.string().toString()` as a computed key, so it never validates real token responses
body: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` evaluates `toString()` on a Zod object at module load. That yields a literal key such as "[object Object]", not a wildcard 'any numeric property'. The schema therefore requires a property literally named "[object Object]" to be a number, and no real token response has one. The second computed key on line 10 is just as broken. Whenever credential sync is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), `safeParse` fails and the function throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'. Every app routed through `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (Google, Office365, Zoom, Salesforce) is broken in sync mode. The 'any numeric field is the expiry' rule needs something like `.passthrough().refine(...)`, not computed keys.

title: Google credential key is overwritten with the safeParse result wrapper instead of the parsed data
body: Before this change `key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` returned the credential object. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`). `data: { key }` therefore stores `{ success, data: { ... } }` as the credential key. On the next load `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails, because `access_token`, `refresh_token` and the other fields are now nested under `data`. Every Google Calendar token refresh corrupts the stored credential, even with sync disabled. It should use `.data` from the parse result.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported in the Salesforce CalendarService
body: The new code calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but the file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This fails type-check and throws a ReferenceError at runtime. Because `getClient` runs from the constructor, every Salesforce calendar operation is affected.

title: Salesforce refresh bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, runs on every instantiation and then uses the stale access token
body: The new block calls login.salesforce.com directly instead of going through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync is not honoured for Salesforce. It also runs unconditionally, with no expiry check, so every service construction does a token refresh and a DB write. The `jsforce.Connection` that follows still uses `credentialKey.access_token` (the old token), not the one just fetched and persisted. The `response.statusText !== "OK"` check is fragile: statusText is empty on HTTP/2 responses, so a successful refresh would be treated as failure.

title: Credential id is passed to refreshOAuthTokens where a user id is expected
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's primary key as the `userId` argument. In sync mode this sends `calcomUserId=<credentialId>` to the self-hoster's endpoint, so it returns tokens for the wrong user or none. The credential's `userId` isn't available in `biginAuth`/`refreshAccessToken` as written, so it has to be threaded through. Teams credentials with a null `userId` should also skip sync, but a credential id is always truthy, so they can't.

title: Sync path returns a raw fetch Response, but most callers expect a different shape
body: In sync mode the function returns the raw `fetch` Response. The non-sync callbacks return other shapes, and callers rely on them. Google reads `res?.data` (a gaxios response), so `token.access_token` throws and the error is swallowed, leaving the stale token. Hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object, so it reads `.expiresIn` on a Response, gets NaN, and stores the Response as the credential key. Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `tokenInfo.data.error` (axios), which is undefined on a Response and throws; the Bigin call is not wrapped in try/catch. The sync result needs to be normalised to the shape each caller expects, or each caller needs to parse the Response, and it needs to be exercised in tests.

title: Request to the credential-sync endpoint is unauthenticated and unchecked
body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` carries only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`. There is no shared secret or signature, even though the inbound webhook requires one. Anyone who can reach that endpoint can request OAuth access tokens for any Cal.com user id. The response is also returned without checking `response.ok` or setting a timeout. A 4xx/5xx body then flows into the callers' parsing as if it were token data.

title: Placeholder refresh_token is injected unconditionally, including when sync is off
