body: If the parsed data has no `refresh_token`, the literal string "refresh_token" is set, even without credential sync. Office365 Calendar spreads `tokenResponse.data` over the existing credential, so a response lacking `refresh_token` replaces the real refresh token with the string "refresh_token". Later refreshes then fail permanently. The fallback should apply only in sync mode, and should not overwrite an existing token.

title: Webex still uses the strict refreshed-token schema, so sync mode cannot succeed
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` was added for Webex, but the response is still validated with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse(responseBody)` instead of `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. The schema requires a fixed `scope` literal, `refresh_token` and `refresh_token_expires_in`. A sync endpoint that returns only an access token and expiry fails with 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'. Zoom was migrated to `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, so the apps are handled inconsistently.

title: Unhandled validation and decryption errors return 500; secret compared non-constant-time
body: `schema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on bad input. `symmetricDecrypt(...)` and `JSON.parse(...)` also throw on a wrong key or malformed payload. None of these are caught, so the endpoint returns a 500 instead of a 400 and may leak stack information. The HTTP method is never checked. The webhook secret is compared with `!==` rather than a constant-time comparison such as `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. When updating an existing credential, `invalid` is not reset, so a credential previously marked invalid stays invalid after a successful sync.

title: Token-parse failure now throws and the diagnostic logging was dropped
body: Previously a schema mismatch logged the zod error and the MS response and then continued. Now `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws a generic 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', and the `console.error` with the zod error and MS response body was removed. This is a behaviour change, and the information needed to debug why a refresh failed is lost. The later `tokenResponse.success && ...` is now redundant.

title: redirect_uri hard-coded in add.ts but still derived from appConfig.slug in callback.ts
body: `add.ts` now builds the redirect URI from the literal 'zoho-bigin', while `callback.ts` still uses `appConfig.slug` for the token exchange. OAuth requires both redirect URIs to match exactly. This only works as long as the config slug equals 'zoho-bigin'. The change is unrelated to the feature and creates a silent coupling.

title: No tests for the new webhook, token parsing or sync refresh path
body: The PR adds a credential-writing webhook and changes the token-refresh path of about ten apps, and the PR checklist says no tests were added. The parsing and return-shape bugs elsewhere in this PR (the broken computed keys, the unwrapped safeParse result, the missing prisma import, the credentialId/userId mix-up) would all have been caught by even basic unit tests.

title: Emails are sent with the raw `guests` input instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the unfiltered request list. Any email that was dropped as an existing attendee still matches `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. That existing attendee then gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a new-booking email) instead of the 'guests added' notification. The newly created guests are the ones that should be passed, i.e. `uniqueGuests`.

title: Team admin/owner check uses `&&`, so admins are denied
body: `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` only passes for owners. `isTeamAdmin` is true for ADMIN or OWNER and `isTeamOwner` is true only for OWNER, so the `&&` excludes plain team admins. It should be `||`, or just `isTeamAdmin`. As written, team admins who are neither organizer nor attendee get FORBIDDEN even though the variable name says admin-or-owner is allowed.

title: Calendar update uses the acting user's credentials instead of the organizer's
body: The handler allows attendees and team admins to call it, but it builds the `EventManager` from `ctx.user` (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `...user`). The calendar events being updated belong to the booking organizer (`booking.user`). When the caller is an attendee or admin, the manager holds the wrong user's credentials and destination calendar. The organizer's calendar event is then not updated, or the update fails. In that case the guests are saved in the DB but never added to the calendar event. The organizer's credentials/destination calendar should be used.

title: DB is mutated before the calendar update, with no failure handling
body: Attendees are written to the DB (lines 92-106) before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs, and that call is not wrapped in try/catch. If the calendar update throws, the mutation fails and the user sees an error. The guests are already persisted as attendees and no notification emails go out. A retry then hits the 'existing attendee' filter and fails with `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, leaving the booking in an inconsistent state.

title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive; no server-side dedupe or limit
body: The blacklist is lower-cased, but `guest` is compared as-is (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), so `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. The same applies to the existing-attendee check (`guest === attendee.email`), so case variants of an existing attendee are inserted as duplicates. The server also never dedupes the input list. The uniqueness rule lives only in the client dialog, so a direct tRPC call with repeated emails creates duplicate attendee rows. Neither the schema nor the handler caps the array length. Any attendee can submit an arbitrarily large list, which triggers one email per guest plus extra emails to every attendee.

title: No check on booking status or end time before adding guests
body: The UI only offers the action for confirmed bookings, but the handler enforces nothing. A caller can add guests to a cancelled, rejected, pending or already-ended booking via the API. That writes attendees, pushes calendar updates, and sends 'guests added' / 'scheduled' emails for a booking that no longer exists. The handler should reject non-ACCEPTED bookings and bookings in the past.

title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores `disableStandardEmails` settings and never emails team members
body: Every other email sender takes `eventTypeMetadata` and honors `disableStandardEmails.all.host/attendee`. This one does not, so event types that disabled standard emails still get these emails. In addition, `addGuests.handler.ts` builds `evt` without a `team` field, so the `calendarEvent.team?.members` loop never runs and team hosts are never notified.

title: New guests are created with an empty name and the organizer's locale
body: Guests are stored with `name: ""` and the organizer's `locale`/`timeZone`. The email templates then render ` <email>` recipients and empty-name greetings, and the guest receives emails in the organizer's language rather than their own.

title: Validation error and form state not reset reliably; error fallback unreachable
body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on a failed validation but is never cleared on edit, on successful submit, or when the dialog is closed through the overlay or X (`onOpenChange`). Only the Cancel button resets it, so the red error can show up the next time the dialog opens. The same applies to the email list when the dialog is closed outside Cancel. In `onError`, the string `` `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` `` is always truthy, so the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback is dead code. The user sees an ugly message such as 'BAD_REQUEST: ...', or a raw zod JSON string for validation errors.

title: Hardcoded untranslated tooltip and dangling label association
body: The tooltip text `"Remove email"` is hardcoded English in a component that otherwise uses `t()`, so it will not be localized. The `<label htmlFor="emails">` points to an id that no input has, so the label is not associated with any field.

title: No tests for the new endpoint's authorization, filtering and email behavior
body: The PR adds a new mutation with permission logic (organizer / attendee / team admin), blacklist and duplicate filtering, calendar updates and several email paths, but adds no unit or e2e tests. The bugs above (the `&&` admin check, the wrong `guests` list passed to the emails, case-sensitive filtering) would be caught by even basic handler tests.

title: Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. The intent is admin OR owner. `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for both roles, so the `&&` effectively requires an owner and a plain team ADMIN is denied. Those admins get FORBIDDEN unless they are also the organizer or an attendee. The condition should be `||`, or just `isTeamAdmin`. The route also uses `authedProcedure`, not the `bookingsProcedure` that `editLocation` uses, so this hand-rolled check is the only authorization.

title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, and the input is not deduplicated server-side
body: The blacklist is lower-cased, but each `guest` is compared as-is. `Blocked@Example.com` therefore bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. The existing-attendee check `guest === attendee.email` is also case-sensitive, so the same address in a different case is added as a second attendee. Duplicate entries within `guests` are only rejected by the client dialog. A direct tRPC call with the same email twice creates two attendee rows, because `uniqueGuests` never dedupes the input. Lower-case the emails and dedupe on the server.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw `guests` list instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`
body: The emails are sent with `guests`, the unfiltered request input, not `uniqueGuests`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide between the full 'scheduled' email and the 'guests added' notification. If the request includes an address that is already an attendee, that existing attendee is wrongly sent a fresh 'scheduled' invite instead of the update notice. Pass the list of guests that were actually inserted.

title: Attendees are persisted before the calendar update with no error handling or rollback
body: The DB update that creates the attendees runs first. `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` follows with no try/catch. If the calendar update throws, the client sees an error but the guests are already stored and no emails are sent. A retry then filters those guests out as duplicates and fails with `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, so the user cannot complete the operation. The calendar and DB state are left inconsistent. Handle calendar failures explicitly, or reorder the steps and roll back.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials rather than the organizer's
body: `EventManager` is built from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `...user`. The route also permits attendees and team admins to add guests. For those callers the credentials do not belong to the user whose calendar holds the event, so `updateCalendarAttendees` will fail or silently skip the external event. The organizer's calendar (`booking.user`, which is already loaded with its credentials) is the one that should be updated.

title: Any attendee can add an unbounded number of arbitrary guests, which sends emails to arbitrary addresses
body: Any logged-in user whose email matches an attendee of the booking is authorized. Neither `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` nor the handler limits the array size, and the booking status is not checked. A single call with many addresses triggers organizer, team and per-attendee emails and ICS invites to third parties, which makes it a spam vector. The attendee check is also case-sensitive on `user.email`. Add a max count, tighten who may add guests, and consider rejecting cancelled/rejected bookings.

title: CalendarEvent has no `team`, so the team-member email loop in sendAddGuestsEmails never runs
body: `evt` is built without `team` or any team member info, but `sendAddGuestsEmails` iterates `calendarEvent.team?.members` to notify the other hosts. For collective and round-robin team events that loop is dead code, and the other hosts are never told about the new guests. The subject also falls back to the organizer's name instead of the team name. Other fields such as `responses` and `bookerUrl` are missing too, which can degrade the email content.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings
body: Every other send function takes `eventTypeMetadata` and honors `disableStandardEmails.all.host` and `.attendee`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` has no such parameter and always sends host and attendee emails. Event types that disabled standard emails (e.g. for workflow-only or custom notifications) will still send these messages to hosts, existing attendees and the new guests.

title: Case-sensitive match on new guest email
body: `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` compares strings exactly. The attendee emails come from the DB and the guest list from user input, so a casing difference sends a new guest the 'guests added' notification instead of the full scheduled invite.

title: isInvalidEmail is never cleared on success or on dialog dismiss
body: `isInvalidEmail` is set when validation fails and is only reset by the Cancel button. If the user triggers the error, corrects the emails and submits successfully, `onSuccess` resets the values but not the flag. The error banner then reappears the next time the dialog opens. Closing the dialog via overlay or Esc (`onOpenChange`) also keeps stale emails and error state.

title: Error toast is always prefixed with the code and the fallback message is unreachable
body: `message` is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, which is always a non-empty string. `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` can therefore never run, and users see raw text like `BAD_REQUEST: Emails must be unique and valid` or `undefined: ...`. The new `unable_to_add_guests` string is dead. Also, `handleAdd` silently returns when the email list is empty.

title: Hardcoded English tooltip and a label not bound to an input
body: The tooltip `"Remove email"` is not passed through `t()`, unlike the rest of the component. The `<label htmlFor="emails">` references an id that no input has, so the label is not associated with the fields. Rows use `key={index}`, which is fragile when entries are removed from the middle of the list.

title: Email failures are swallowed without logging the error
body: The catch block only logs a fixed string with `console.log` and drops `err`. If sending fails, the user still gets a 'Guests added' success and operators have nothing to diagnose it. At minimum log the error through the project logger.

title: Blacklisted or duplicate guests are silently dropped and the all-filtered error is misleading
body: If only some of the submitted guests are filtered out (existing attendee or blacklisted), the request still succeeds and the UI shows 'Guests added', with no indication that some were skipped. If all are filtered, the user gets 'Emails must be unique and valid' even when the cause is the blacklist. The response should report what was actually added or skipped.

title: New feature ships without any tests
body: The PR adds a mutation with non-trivial authorization, filtering and email logic, plus new UI and email templates, but no handler unit tests or e2e tests. The `data-testid="add_members"` hook is added but never exercised. Bugs like the `&&` permission check and the wrong `newGuests` list would be caught by basic tests.

title: Emails are keyed off raw `guests`, not the filtered `uniqueGuests`
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the unfiltered input. Emails already on the booking, which were dropped from `uniqueGuests`, are still in `guests`. Those existing attendees get the 'scheduled' email meant for brand-new guests instead of the 'guests added' notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead, and compare emails case-insensitively.

title: Team admin/owner check uses `&&` instead of `||`
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner = isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for admins and owners, and `isTeamOwner` is true only for owners. The `&&` therefore restricts access to owners and wrongly denies team admins. It also runs two redundant membership queries even when the caller is the organizer. The intent is clearly `||`, or just `isTeamAdmin`.

title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased, but `guest` is compared as-is, so `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. The existing-attendee check (`guest === attendee.email`) is also case-sensitive, so `A@x.com` can be added next to `a@x.com`. The server also never dedupes within `guests`, so a direct API call with the same email twice creates duplicate attendee rows. Normalise emails (lowercase/trim) before every comparison and dedupe the input.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, and a failure leaves DB and calendar inconsistent
body: The EventManager is built from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, not the booking owner's credentials. The booking's calendar event lives in the organizer's calendar. When a team admin or an attendee adds guests, the calendar is silently not updated, or the update fails. The attendees are already persisted by `prisma.booking.update` before `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)`, which is outside the try/catch. If it throws, the request returns an error to the user, no emails are sent, and the guests are still saved. Use the organizer's credentials (`booking.user.credentials` is already loaded but unused), and handle calendar failures without losing the notification step.

title: No check on booking status or whether the booking is in the past
body: The handler never checks `booking.status` or `endTime`. A caller can add guests to cancelled, rejected, pending or already-finished bookings, and each guest is sent a 'CONFIRMED' calendar invite (`method: REQUEST`, `status: CONFIRMED` in the new email templates). The UI also adds the action to `editBookingActions`, which is shown for past confirmed and past pending bookings and for seated events. Seated events track attendees via `seatsReferences`, which this flow ignores. The server should reject non-accepted or past bookings, and probably seated events.

title: Unbounded guest list lets any attendee trigger arbitrary email sends
body: `guests` has no `.max()`. The handler lets any attendee, not just the host, add guests. Each added address gets a calendar invite and email sent from the organizer's name, and every existing attendee, the host and team members are also emailed. One request with hundreds of addresses is an easy spam/abuse vector and a load problem. Add a reasonable cap and consider restricting who may add guests.

title: CalendarEvent omits `team`, so team-member emails never fire
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` loops over `calendarEvent.team?.members`, but `evt` never sets `team` (nor `bookingId`, `iCalUID`, `responses`, `hideCalendarNotes`). For team or round-robin bookings the extra hosts are therefore never notified, and the team-member branch is dead code. Populate the missing fields as other booking handlers do.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails and compares emails case-sensitively
body: Every other sender here takes `eventTypeMetadata` and honours `disableStandardEmails` for host/attendee emails. `sendAddGuestsEmails` always emails organizer, team members and all attendees, so event types that disabled standard emails still get notifications. `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` is also case-sensitive, so a differently-cased match sends the wrong template.

title: Email failure is swallowed and the error is not logged
body: The catch block does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without the caught `err`, so the failure reason is lost and ops cannot diagnose it. The request still returns success. At minimum, log the error with the repo logger.

title: Stale validation error is never cleared
body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on a failed validation but is never reset when the user edits the emails, when a valid submission is made, in the mutation `onSuccess`, or when the dialog is closed via the overlay or Escape. Only the Cancel button resets it. After one invalid attempt the 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner stays visible even after fixing the input, and it reappears the next time the dialog opens. Reset it on `handleAdd` success and on input change/close.

title: Error toast shows raw code and untranslated message; fallback is unreachable
body: The message is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, which is always a non-empty string, so `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` never applies. Users see text like 'FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission'. For tRPC input-validation failures `err.message` is a JSON blob of zod issues. Show `t(err.message)` only for known keys, otherwise fall back to `unable_to_add_guests`.

title: Hard-coded English tooltip text
body: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` is not passed through `t()`, unlike the rest of the component, so it is not localised. Add a translation key.

title: No tests for new permission-sensitive mutation
body: The PR adds a mutation with authorization logic, a blacklist filter, DB writes, calendar updates and several email templates, but no unit, integration or e2e tests. The role check, blacklist, dedupe and email-recipient selection would all benefit from tests, and several of the bugs above would likely have been caught by them.

title: retryCount cleanup clause is not limited to SMS reminders
body: The second OR branch, `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`, has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` condition. The first branch is SMS-only, and the comment says this handler deletes SMS reminders. `WorkflowReminder` is shared with EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders. Today only this cron increments `retryCount`, so nothing is wrongly deleted yet. If another cron (email or WhatsApp) later uses the column, this SMS cron will delete its reminders as well. Scope the clause to `method: SMS`, or use `AND` with the method.

title: Unguarded DB update inside catch block can abort the whole cron run
body: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` in the `catch` block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If it throws (DB error, or the reminder was deleted concurrently, giving a Prisma 'record not found'), the exception escapes the `for` loop. The handler then fails with a 500, and every remaining reminder in that run is skipped. Before this change, per-reminder errors were only logged and the loop continued. Wrap the update in its own try/catch, or log first and then update safely.

title: Reminders with no recipient number or empty message are never counted as failures
body: `retryCount` is only incremented when `scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value or throws. If `message` is empty or `sendTo` is missing (for example an attendee with no `smsReminderNumber`), the `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)` block is skipped and nothing is recorded. Those reminders stay `scheduled: false` and are re-processed on every cron run until `scheduledDate` passes. That is the same endless-retry behaviour the PR sets out to remove. An invalid or missing phone number is the PR's own example. Add an `else` that increments `retryCount` for this case too.

title: Two attempts is a very aggressive threshold for transient failures, and the counter is a stale read-modify-write
body: All failures count the same, including transient Twilio or network errors. Because the cron runs often, a short outage can burn both attempts and permanently delete a valid reminder (`retryCount > 1`). The increment is also computed from the value read at the start of the run (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) rather than an atomic `{ increment: 1 }`. If two cron invocations overlap, both write the same value and the counter under-counts. Use `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`, and consider a larger limit or distinguishing permanent errors (such as an invalid number) from transient ones.

title: No tests for the new retry/deletion behaviour
body: The PR changes the cron's deletion criteria and adds retry bookkeeping in both the failure and exception paths. It adds no tests for incrementing on a falsy `scheduleSMS` result or on a thrown error, deleting once `retryCount > 1`, or leaving non-SMS reminders untouched.

title: retryCount cleanup clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The first OR branch is limited to `method: SMS`, but the new `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` branch has no method filter. This SMS cron will delete any WorkflowReminder (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, etc.) whose retryCount exceeds 1. Today only this file increments retryCount. But the column is generic, and any other reminder flow that later uses it would have its rows silently deleted by the SMS job. The clause should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, and ideally `scheduled: false`.

title: Unguarded prisma.update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
body: The catch block now runs `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` without its own try/catch. If that update throws (DB error, or the row was deleted concurrently so Prisma raises P2025), the exception escapes the `for` loop. The handler rejects, the endpoint returns a 500, and every remaining reminder in `unscheduledReminders` is skipped for that run. Previously one bad reminder only logged an error. Wrap the update in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany`, so a bookkeeping failure cannot stop the batch.

title: Reminders with no sendTo or empty message never increment retryCount
body: retryCount is only incremented when `scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value or throws. If `sendTo` is missing (e.g. no `smsReminderNumber` on the booking) or the message is empty, the `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)` check fails and nothing happens. The same applies to the earlier `continue` for a missing workflowStep or booking. Those reminders are never counted as failures, so the cron keeps re-processing them every run until `scheduledDate` passes. That is the exact behaviour the PR sets out to remove. A missing phone number is a common case of the 'invalid phone number' scenario in the description.

title: Read-modify-write retryCount update is not atomic
body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` uses the value read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap, both read the same count and both write count+1, so a failure is undercounted and the cutoff is delayed. Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` avoids this and is the idiomatic form (the same applies to the catch block at line 195).

title: Unindexed retryCount in an OR condition on a large table
body: The delete's WHERE is now `(method AND scheduledDate) OR retryCount > 1`. The existing indexes (`[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]`, etc.) cannot serve the `retryCount` branch, so Postgres will likely fall back to a sequential scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron run. Scoping the second branch to `method = SMS` and `scheduled = false` would let the existing index apply.

title: No tests for the new retry/delete behaviour
body: The PR adds retry counting and a new deletion rule: a failed `scheduleSMS` increments retryCount, and rows with retryCount > 1 are deleted on the next run. None of this is covered by a test, including the off-by-one threshold (`gt: 1` means deletion after the second failure). A regression in the counting or the OR delete filter would go unnoticed.

title: retryCount delete clause is not scoped to SMS or unscheduled reminders
body: The second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter and no `scheduled: false` filter. This is the SMS cron, but the clause deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders. It would also delete reminders that were already successfully scheduled with Twilio. Only this job increments retryCount today, so the damage is latent. But `retryCount` is now a generic column on a shared table, and any other job that starts using it will have its reminders silently deleted by the SMS cron. Scope the clause: `{ method: SMS, scheduled: false, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

title: Unguarded prisma update inside catch can abort the whole cron loop
body: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the `catch` block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If it throws (DB error, or the row was deleted by a concurrent run or cancellation so Prisma raises 'record not found'), the exception escapes the for-loop. The handler then fails with a 500 and every remaining reminder in `unscheduledReminders` goes unprocessed for that run. Before this change a failure on one reminder was logged and the loop continued. Guard the retry-count update so one bad row cannot block the others.

title: Reminders with no recipient or empty message never count as failures
body: The retry counter is only incremented when `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns falsy or throws. If `sendTo` is missing (for example a booking with no `smsReminderNumber`, a common case for a bad phone number) or the message is empty, the `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)` check is false and nothing happens. Those reminders are re-evaluated on every cron run until `scheduledDate` passes, which is the behaviour the PR sets out to remove. Likewise, the early `continue` for a missing workflowStep or booking never increments. The else path of this condition should also bump retryCount.

title: Read-modify-write retry increment is not atomic
body: The code writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read earlier by `findMany`. If two cron invocations overlap, or the run is slow, both write the same stale value and an increment is lost, so a failing reminder gets extra attempts. Use Prisma's atomic update `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` in both places (here and line 195).

title: OR with unindexed retryCount forces a full scan on every cron run
body: Previously the delete was served by the `(method, scheduled, scheduledDate)` index. Adding an OR branch on `retryCount` alone, with no index, makes Postgres unable to use that index for the whole predicate, so each cron execution will likely sequentially scan the large WorkflowReminder table. Scope the clause (method/scheduled) so the index can still be used, or run two separate deleteMany calls.

title: No tests for the new retry/deletion behaviour
body: The PR changes cron control flow (increment on falsy result, increment on exception, delete when retryCount > 1) and adds a destructive delete condition, but includes no tests. Nothing covers the 'fails twice then is deleted' path or confirms that non-SMS reminders are left alone.

title: getBaseConditions returns an unparenthesized OR expression that is unsafe to compose
body: `getBaseConditions()` is meant to be dropped into a larger `WHERE` clause. When only the authorization condition is returned (line 75), it is returned bare. For org and team scope that is `(A) OR (B)`. A caller writing `WHERE ${base} AND "startTime" > ${d}` gets `(A) OR (B) AND startTime > d`. Because AND binds tighter than OR, the date or other filters then apply only to the second branch, so team-booking rows are returned unfiltered. The combined branch wraps both sides in parentheses, but the single-condition branches do not. Always wrap the result, e.g. `Prisma.sql\`(${authConditions})\``, so the returned fragment is safe to compose.

title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions hide the real contract
body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object, which is always truthy. So `authConditions` is never falsy, and the `else if (filterConditions)` and `NOTHING_CONDITION` fallbacks can never run. The apparent "fail closed" fallback is unreachable and misleads readers about the invariants. Simplify to `filter ? sql\`(${auth}) AND (${filter})\` : sql\`(${auth})\``.

title: Public findMany method removed without replacement or caller audit
body: `findMany(args)` was the service's public entry point for fetching bookings. It is deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment. Any existing caller (tRPC handlers or other services) will fail to compile, or will have to build its own raw query. The PR description only talks about updating tests and does not mention this breaking change or confirm that no other callers exist.

title: Constructor options type loosened, allowing scope 'team' without teamId at compile time
body: The constructor now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `scope` is a plain union and `teamId` is optional. `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` therefore type-checks. At runtime the zod discriminated-union validation fails, `this.options` becomes null, and the service silently returns `1=0`, so the caller sees no data and no error. The compile-time guarantee from the discriminated union is lost. Keep the strict type, or surface the validation failure.

title: Caching tests deleted although caching behavior remains
body: The "Caching" describe block was removed. The service still memoizes via `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, so the behavior is now untested. Nothing checks that a second call returns the cached value, or that a `null` filter result is cached rather than rebuilt. The tests should have been updated to the `Prisma.sql` expectations, not dropped.

title: Only the user-scope SQL is executed against the database
body: The conditions that matter most for security are the org and team scopes, with `= ANY(${array})` array binding and the nested `(...) OR (...)` grouping. These are only compared against hand-written `Prisma.sql` strings and never run against Postgres. The single `$queryRaw` test uses user scope with an eventTypeId filter. It never checks that another user's or another team's bookings are excluded, and never exercises array parameter binding or operator precedence. A syntax error or wrong grouping in the org or team SQL would pass the string-equality tests. Add DB-backed tests for team and org scope with a negative case, plus the empty-user-list team case.

title: getBaseConditions can return an unparenthesized OR expression that breaks authorization when callers append AND clauses
body: The org and team authorization conditions are built as `(A) OR (B)` with no outer parentheses. The eventTypeId filter has the same shape: `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)`. `getBaseConditions` only wraps them when both auth and filter conditions exist. In the `else if (authConditions) return authConditions;` path, which is the live path when no filters are set, it returns the bare `A OR B`. A caller writing `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" > ...` gets `A OR B AND C`, which SQL parses as `A OR (B AND C)`. The first branch of the authorization check then matches rows regardless of the extra filter. For an authorization predicate this is easy to get wrong silently. Wrap every returned fragment in parentheses, for example `Prisma.sql\`(${authConditions})\``, or parenthesize inside the `reduce` and in each builder. The final `else if (filterConditions)` and `NOTHING_CONDITION` branches are unreachable, because `authConditions` is always a truthy `Sql` object.

title: Only the user-scope path is tested end to end against the database
body: `getBaseConditions` is executed with `$queryRaw` only for `scope: "user"` plus an eventType filter. The org/team scopes with `OR` combinations, `= ANY($n)` array parameters, and the combined auth-plus-filter case are only compared as SQL objects and never run against Postgres. The exact-equality tests would pass even if the SQL were invalid or had wrong precedence, for example the bare-OR problem when combined with other clauses. Add at least one execution test for org or team scope with a filter.

title: Caching tests removed and new service branches left uncovered
body: The "Caching" describe block was deleted, but `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` still exist in the service. Nothing now verifies that the second call reuses the cached value. The new `userIdsFromTeam.length > 0` and `userIdsFromOrg.length > 0` branches are also never exercised with an empty list. The team test always has a member, and there is no case for a team that is not a child of the org (`NOTHING_CONDITION`) or a team with no members. Restore the caching tests with the new `Prisma.sql` expectations and add cases for the empty-member and non-child-team branches.

title: Auth-only condition returned unparenthesized can leak rows when callers append AND clauses
body: For org and team scope, `buildAuthorizationConditions` returns a top-level OR: `(teamId = ANY(..) AND isTeamBooking = true) OR (userId = ANY(..) AND isTeamBooking = false)`. In `getBaseConditions`, when a filter is also present, the auth part is wrapped in parentheses. When there is no filter, the auth condition is returned bare (line 75). Any caller that composes it as `WHERE ${base} AND "startTime" >= ...` gets the wrong precedence, because AND binds tighter than OR. The date, status or other filter then applies only to the last OR branch, so team bookings escape the extra filters. Because this value is the authorization boundary, `getBaseConditions` (or the reduce helpers) should always wrap the result in parentheses so it is safe to embed.

title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions: auth condition is never falsy
body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object, which is always truthy, falling back to `NOTHING_CONDITION`. So the `else if (filterConditions)` branch and the final `return NOTHING_CONDITION` can never run. The code suggests auth is optional when it is not, and it hides the invariant that authorization is always applied. Simplify to `filterConditions ? sql\`(${auth}) AND (${filter})\` : auth`.

title: Caching tests deleted although caching logic still exists
body: The whole `Caching` describe block (auth and filter condition caching) was removed. `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` and the `=== undefined` checks are still in the service, so the memoization behaviour is now untested. This includes the `null` filter case, where `null` is a valid cached value distinct from `undefined`. The tests should have been converted to the `Prisma.sql` form rather than dropped.

title: New branching in team/org conditions has no test coverage
body: The refactor adds conditional behaviour: the user-clause is omitted when `userIdsFromTeam` is empty (previously always emitted), and in org scope it is omitted when there are no member user IDs. The tests only cover the case where users exist. There is no test for a team scope whose team is not a child of the org (which should yield `NOTHING_CONDITION`), a team with no members, or an org with no child teams. These are the authorization edge cases the PR checklist itself calls out.

title: Delete-cache mutation never refreshes the connectedCalendars query
body: `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. Unlike `disconnectMutation`, it has no `onSettled` that invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. The `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamp and the "Delete cached data" item are rendered from that query, and the query is created with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. If the parent does not pass `onChanged`, the dropdown keeps showing the old "Last updated" time and a delete action for a cache that no longer exists. Invalidate `connectedCalendars` in the mutation itself instead of relying on the caller.

title: Plain Error thrown for not-found or unauthorized credential
body: When the credential is missing or belongs to another user, the handler throws a bare `Error`. tRPC turns that into INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500), which is logged as a server fault. It should throw a `TRPCError` with `NOT_FOUND` or `FORBIDDEN`. The input schema is also defined inline in `_router.tsx` as `z.number()` rather than in a `.schema.ts` file like the sibling procedures. It also does not require an integer.

title: Migration header is wrong, and legacy rows get a misleading timestamp
body: The header comment says the column is added "without a default value", but the statement adds `DEFAULT NOW()`. The comment is stale, auto-generated text and contradicts the migration. Because of the default, every existing CalendarCache row gets the migration time as `updatedAt`. The UI will show "Last updated: <migration time>" for caches that may be much older, so the displayed freshness is inaccurate until each row is next upserted.

title: Extra write to every SelectedCalendar row on each cache refresh, with no consumer
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now runs `updateMany({ where: { credentialId } }, data: {})` after every cache refresh. That function runs from the Google webhook path and from `unwatchCalendar`. This adds a write against all of a credential's SelectedCalendar rows (user-level and event-type-level) on every webhook purely to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. The PR notes say the frontend does not read that field and uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt` instead. The write is wasted load and contention on a hot table. It also relies on Prisma bumping `@updatedAt` for an empty `data` object. Remove it.

title: Cache timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
body: The cache time is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, ignoring the user's locale and time-format preference even though the surrounding string is translated with `t()`. Non-US users see US-style dates, for example M/D/YY. Use the active locale (for example `i18n.language`) or the app's date utilities.

title: Unrelated dev script with macOS-only sed and wrong exit code
body: This tunnel script has nothing to do with the cache feature. `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed (Linux) it treats `''` as the script and fails, so the env file is never updated. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` depends on the current working directory. `cleanup` always `exit 0`, including the failure paths at the rate-limit check and when no URL could be extracted. When reusing an existing tmole, the log file may not exist, so URL extraction silently returns nothing. It should be removed from this PR or fixed.

title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` without declaring tsx as a dependency
body: The `dev:cron` script now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not declared in this package's dependencies or devDependencies. `npx` will download it on demand, so versions are unpinned and offline or CI use can fail. This change is also unrelated to the calendar cache feature.

title: No tests for the new handler, repository method, or dropdown logic
body: The PR adds a destructive mutation with an ownership check (`deleteCacheHandler`), a new `groupBy` query (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), the `cacheUpdatedAt` enrichment in `connectedCalendarsHandler`, and conditional dropdown rendering. None of them has a test. Ownership enforcement (another user's credentialId must be rejected) and the credential-to-cache mapping should be covered.

title: Deleting cache does not refresh connectedCalendars, so the UI keeps showing stale cache status
body: `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls `onSuccess?.()`. It never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. The `disconnectMutation` in the same file does invalidate it in `onSettled`. `onSuccess` is the optional `onChanged` prop, and the wrapper passes whatever the parent gave it, which may be undefined. After a successful delete, `cacheUpdatedAt` stays cached, so the dropdown still shows the old "Last updated" timestamp and still offers "Delete cached data". The test plan expects "UI updates appropriately", which this does not do. Invalidate the query in the delete mutation.

title: Cache timestamp formatted with hard-coded en-US locale
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale and the app's i18n setting. Non-English users see US-style dates (M/D/YY) inside an otherwise translated string. Use the user's locale (for example `i18n.language`) or the existing date-formatting helpers.

title: Authorization failure throws a plain Error instead of TRPCError
body: When the credential is missing or belongs to another user, the handler throws `new Error(...)`. tRPC maps this to a generic 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR and it gets logged as a server error. Use `TRPCError` with `NOT_FOUND` or `FORBIDDEN`, as other handlers do. Negative in-memory delegation credential IDs also fall into this branch and will surface as 500s. The input schema in `_router.tsx` is also an inline `z.number()`, with no `.int()` and no separate schema file like the sibling procedures.

title: Backfill with NOW() makes all legacy cache rows report the migration time as last updated; header comment is wrong
body: Every pre-existing `CalendarCache` row gets `updatedAt = <migration time>`. The new UI will then show "Last updated" as the deploy time for entries that may be weeks old, which is misleading. Backfilling from an existing signal such as `expiresAt - 30 days` would be more accurate. The warning at the top of the file (lines 1-6) says the column was added "without a default value" and "is not possible if the table is not empty". That contradicts the statement below it, which adds a default. It is leftover auto-generated text and should be removed.

title: Extra unconditional updateMany on every cache refresh with empty data
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` now runs after every `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`, which is called from the webhook path. It relies on Prisma implicitly bumping `@updatedAt` for an empty update, and it rewrites every SelectedCalendar row of the credential, including event-type-level rows. It runs even when no calendars were processed. The PR notes admit the UI does not use `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` (it uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`), so this is a pure extra write on a hot path. Drop it, or restrict it to a real requirement.

title: Unrelated change: dev:cron now relies on undeclared tsx via npx
body: Switching `dev:cron` from `ts-node` to `npx tsx` is unrelated to calendar cache. `tsx` is not declared in any dependency list, so `npx` downloads it at run time, unpinned and unreproducible. Other scripts in this file still use `ts-node`. Either keep `ts-node` or add `tsx` as a devDependency, and ideally put the change in a separate PR.

title: Unrelated, macOS-only helper script added; breaks on Linux and exits 0 on failure
body: The script is not wired into anything and is unrelated to this feature. `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax; with GNU sed the empty string is parsed as the script and the real expression as a filename, so the .env update fails on Linux. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` depends on the caller's cwd. `cleanup` always does `exit 0`, so the rate-limit and failed-URL paths report success. It also silently rewrites `.env`. Remove it from this PR or make it portable and correct.

title: Empty fixed-width wrapper rendered when dropdown has nothing to show
body: The old code only rendered the `<div className="flex w-32 justify-end">` when the credential could be disconnected. Now the wrapper is always rendered, but `CredentialActionsDropdown` returns `null` for delegation or read-only credentials with no cache. This leaves an empty 8rem-wide block in the card header and in the Alert's actions area. The same applies to the second usage at line 123. Render the wrapper only when the dropdown has content, or move it inside the component.

title: No tests for new repository method, tRPC handler, or dropdown component
body: The PR adds `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` (a groupBy with `_max`), a new `deleteCache` mutation with an ownership check, the `cacheUpdatedAt` enrichment in `connectedCalendarsHandler`, and a component with conditional rendering. None of these has a unit or integration test. The ownership check in `deleteCacheHandler` and the empty-result and negative-credential-ID cases in the enrichment are the most important to cover.

title: Deleting the cache does not refresh connectedCalendars, so the UI keeps showing the old timestamp
body: `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. It never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike `disconnectMutation`, which does so in `onSettled`. `cacheUpdatedAt` comes from that query, so after a successful delete the dropdown still shows 'Last updated: …' and offers 'Delete cached data' again. Nothing guarantees `onChanged` refetches, because it is optional and is `props.onChanged` from the wrapper. Invalidate `connectedCalendars` in `onSuccess` or `onSettled` of the delete mutation.

title: Authorization failure throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError
body: When the credential is missing or belongs to another user, the handler throws `new Error(...)`. tRPC maps this to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500), so the client and monitoring see a server fault rather than a 403/404. Other tRPC handlers use `TRPCError` with `FORBIDDEN` or `NOT_FOUND`. Use `TRPCError` here so the response code is correct and error tracking is not flooded with false 500s.

title: No tests for the new delete mutation, repository method, or component
body: The PR adds an ownership-checked destructive mutation (`deleteCacheHandler`), a new repository method (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), handler enrichment with `cacheUpdatedAt`, and a new dropdown component with conditional rendering. It adds no tests for any of them. The ownership check that stops a user deleting another user's cache, and the empty-cache and delegation-credential paths, are the logic most worth covering.

title: Unused SelectedCalendar.updatedAt bump adds a DB write to every cache refresh
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now runs `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`, an `updateMany` over all of the credential's SelectedCalendar rows. This runs on every webhook-triggered cache refresh and on `unwatchCalendar`. The new UI reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, not `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, so the write has no consumer. The PR notes already question whether it should be removed. It also depends on Prisma bumping `@updatedAt` for an empty `data: {}`, which is fragile. Remove it, or justify it with a consumer.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId, which nothing uses
body: The `Pick` types for `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, and the select in `user.ts` was extended to match. No code in this PR reads these fields, since the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache. Widening a shared exported type forces every other producer of `UserWithCalendars` (platform libraries, API v2, tests) to supply the fields or fail type-checking, and it loads extra columns for nothing. Revert unless a consumer is added.

title: Cache timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
body: The 'Last updated' text uses `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` regardless of the user's UI locale. Users of other locales see US-style dates (M/D/YY, 12-hour) next to translated strings. Use the locale from `useLocale()`, or the existing dayjs/locale formatting helpers, instead of a fixed locale.

title: Unrelated dev script is macOS-only and exits 0 on failure
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` works only with BSD/macOS sed. On GNU sed (Linux) the empty argument is parsed as the script, so the `.env` update fails. `cleanup` ends with `exit 0`, so the rate-limit and 'Failed to extract URL' paths report success. The script rewrites a relative `../.env` that depends on the caller's working directory. It is also unrelated to cache status and actions and is not wired to any package script. Drop it from this PR or fix these problems.

title: dev:cron switched to unpinned `npx tsx`, an undeclared dependency
body: `dev:cron` changed from `ts-node` (a declared devDependency) to `npx tsx`. `tsx` is not declared in this package, so `npx` downloads whatever version is latest at run time. Behaviour is then unpinned and breaks offline. The change is unrelated to this feature. If tsx is wanted, add it as a devDependency and call it directly, or revert.

title: Migration warning contradicts the SQL
body: The header says the column was added 'without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty', but the statement adds it with `DEFAULT NOW()`. The stale auto-generated warning is misleading. Also, every pre-existing CalendarCache row gets the migration timestamp as `updatedAt`, so legacy rows will show the deploy time as 'Last updated' rather than when they were actually populated.

title: Cron cancel loop aborts on first SendGrid error and defers all DB deletes until the end
body: All SendGrid cancel calls and the `workflowReminder.delete` queries sit inside one try/catch. The delete queries are only awaited via `Promise.all` after the loop finishes. If any `client.request` throws (batch already sent, already cancelled, 4xx or 5xx), the catch swallows it. The remaining reminders are never cancelled, so those emails go out. The reminders already cancelled at SendGrid are never deleted from the DB because `Promise.all` is not reached. On the next run they are re-sent to SendGrid. If SendGrid rejects a cancel for an already-cancelled batch, the same failing reminder aborts the loop again and again. One bad record can therefore block every later cancellation until its `scheduledDate` passes. Handle each reminder in its own try/catch and delete (or flag) each row right after its successful cancel.

title: `immediateDelete` path still uses the limited SendGrid cancel API, with no DB flag and no fallback
body: The PR exists because SendGrid allows at most 100 pending cancellations. Yet `immediateDelete` still POSTs `status: cancel` straight to SendGrid. It is used for rescheduled bookings (handleNewBooking), deleted workflows and deleted steps. Reschedules and large workflow deletions can therefore still hit the 100-cancel cap. When the call fails, the error is only logged and the reminder is neither marked `cancelled` nor deleted. The email is then sent anyway, which is the original bug. On success the row is also left untouched (not flagged, not deleted), so a later cancel or reschedule of the same booking sends a duplicate cancel for the same batch. For the reschedule case the booking and its reminders are retained, so simply setting `cancelled: true` (the deferred path) would avoid the limit. At minimum, fall back to `cancelled: true` when the immediate cancel fails.

title: Reminder cancellation is now fire-and-forget although the DB write is the only cancellation mechanism
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async and are called inside `forEach` without being awaited. Previously the reminder DB deletions were collected and awaited in `Promise.all`. Now the DB update (`cancelled: true`) or delete is the only thing that stops the email, and nothing waits for it. In a serverless environment the work can be dropped once the response is sent, which silently reintroduces the 'reminder still sent for a cancelled booking' bug. The same pattern appears in bookings.tsx (requestReschedule), handleNewBooking.ts and several places in workflows.tsx. Collect the promises and await them (e.g. add them to the `Promise.all`).

title: Reschedule re-cancels reminders already cancelled by requestReschedule and ignores the `cancelled` flag
body: When an organizer uses `requestReschedule`, the old booking's email reminders are only flagged `cancelled: true`. The attendee then books a new slot via handleNewBooking, which loads `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders`, including the already-flagged ones. For each of them it calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)` and sends a second SendGrid cancel for the same batch. That wastes pending-cancel slots and may error. Because the call is not awaited and errors are only logged, a failure leaves things unflagged. The loop should skip reminders where `cancelled` is already true. It should also prefer the deferred path (flag only) over the immediate SendGrid cancel.

title: Cancellations made shortly before send time can be missed by the 15-minute cron
body: A cancelled reminder is only handed to SendGrid when the cron runs within the hour before `scheduledDate`. The cron runs every 15 minutes, and a cancellation made after the last run before the send time is never processed. The first-step `deleteMany` then removes the row after the send time, and the email goes out for a cancelled or rescheduled booking. Likewise, any skipped or failed cron run in that window loses the cancellation. This is an inherent limitation of the deferred design and should at least be documented. A mitigation would be to cancel directly when the reminder is within the last 15 minutes, or to widen the window.

title: Unused `Prisma` import and type-only symbols turned into value imports
body: After removing `PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>[]`, `Prisma` is no longer referenced anywhere in this file but was added as a value import. `PrismaPromise` was also changed from `import type` to a regular value import although it is only used as a type. This produces an unused-import lint error. The same unnecessary `import type` to value-import change was made for `App`, `Credential`, `EventTypeCustomInput` and `Prisma` in handleNewBooking.ts. Restore the `import type` form.

title: No tests for the new cancel flow or cron cancellation step
body: The PR changes the cancellation contract of `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` (new signature, new `cancelled` column, new deferred cron step). It adds no tests for the deferred flag, the immediate path, the null-`referenceId` path, or the cron picking up `cancelled` reminders within the one-hour window. The previous fix (#6991) failed silently for the same lack of coverage.

title: Reschedule path cancels via SendGrid immediately, bringing back the 100-pending-cancellation failure
body: The PR moves normal cancellations to a deferred model: set `cancelled = true`, and let the cron cancel in SendGrid within an hour of the send time. This was meant to avoid SendGrid's cap of about 100 pending cancellations. The reschedule path in handleNewBooking passes `immediateDelete = true`, so each rescheduled booking sends a cancel request to SendGrid right away. Once the cap is reached, the request fails and the error is only logged. The row is neither marked `cancelled` nor deleted, so the cron never retries and the reminder email for the old time is still sent. That is the bug this PR set out to fix. The same reminders are also cancelled a second time when the booking was first cancelled through `requestReschedule` (which already flagged them `cancelled`), which uses up another pending-cancel slot. The reschedule path should use the deferred flag, as `requestReschedule` and `handleCancelBooking` do.

title: immediateDelete branch swallows SendGrid errors and never records the cancellation
body: In the `immediateDelete` branch the function POSTs the cancel to SendGrid and returns. It neither deletes the reminder row nor sets `cancelled`. If the request fails (for example at the 100 pending-cancellation limit), the outer catch only logs, so there is no fallback and the cron cannot retry. If the request succeeds, the row lingers until the scheduled date passes. This only works for callers whose rows are cascade-deleted afterwards (workflow or step deletion). For callers whose rows persist, such as the reschedule path, a failed cancel is lost. The branch should fall back to flagging `cancelled` on failure, or callers whose rows persist should not use it.

title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole batch and blocks later cancellations on every run
body: The cancel loop sits in a single try/catch. The `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` calls are lazy PrismaPromises that only run at `await Promise.all(...)` after the loop. If any `client.request` throws (invalid or expired batch_id, rate limit, transient error), the loop exits and none of the deletes run, including those for reminders already cancelled. Reminders after the failing one are never processed. The failing row is still `cancelled: true` with a date inside the next hour, so it is retried first on every 15-minute run and fails again. All later cancelled reminders then go out as emails. Each reminder should be handled in its own try/catch, and its row deleted right after its own successful cancel.

title: Shared @sendgrid/client is never given the API key in this module, so the new cancel calls may be unauthenticated
body: This file only calls `sgMail.setApiKey(...)`. `@sendgrid/mail` uses its own internal Client instance, so that does not configure the default `@sendgrid/client` singleton used for `client.request`. Nothing in this module calls `client.setApiKey`. The new cancellation loop depends entirely on `client.request`. If the singleton has no key in the cron's process, every cancel returns 401. That error is swallowed by the try/catch (`console.log`), so nothing is cancelled and the emails still go out, silently. Add `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` here, as emailReminderManager does.

title: Unused `Prisma` import and type imports turned into value imports
body: After the `PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>[]` code was removed, `Prisma` is no longer used in this file, so it is an unused import (a lint failure). `PrismaPromise` was also changed from `import type` to a regular value import even though it is only used as a type. The same pattern appears in handleNewBooking.ts, where `App`, `Credential`, `EventTypeCustomInput` and `Prisma` were moved from `import type` to a value import. Restore the type-only imports and drop `Prisma`.

title: No tests for the new deferred-cancellation flow
body: The fix changes the contract of `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` and adds a new cron phase. It also rewires cancel, reschedule, workflow-update and workflow-delete paths. No tests were added for any of it: setting `cancelled`, the one-hour cancellation window, deleting rows after a successful cancel, or behaviour when SendGrid fails. The earlier fix in #6991 had to be redone because it was never exercised against SendGrid's real limits, so regression coverage matters here.

title: immediateDelete branch cancels in SendGrid but leaves the DB row, and still uses the 100-slot cancel quota
body: When `immediateDelete` is true the function POSTs a cancel to SendGrid and returns. It neither deletes the `workflowReminder` row nor sets `cancelled`. Two consequences follow. First, in the reschedule path in handleNewBooking the row survives with `scheduled=true` and a `referenceId` until the cron's generic cleanup removes it once `scheduledDate` has passed. Second, this branch is exactly the immediate cancellation that the PR says is limited to 100 pending cancellations. Every reschedule via handleNewBooking therefore still consumes a SendGrid cancel slot. Once the cap is hit, further cancels fail and the emails are sent anyway, which is the original bug. Either delete the row after cancelling, or use the lazy `cancelled=true` path wherever the row will survive (rescheduled bookings). Reserve immediate cancel for cases where the row is cascade-deleted, such as workflow or step deletion.

title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole batch and blocks later reminders on every run
body: The whole loop is inside a single try/catch, and the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` calls are lazy Prisma promises that only execute at the final `Promise.all`. If one `client.request` throws (invalid or expired batch_id, rate limit, transient error), the loop exits. No row is deleted, including those already cancelled in SendGrid. The next cron run fetches the same rows in the same order and hits the same failing reminder first. That one bad row then stops every reminder after it from being cancelled, so those emails are still sent. Wrap each reminder in its own try/catch, and delete or mark each row right after its own successful cancel.

title: Cancellations made shortly before the send time can still result in the email going out
body: The cancellation is deferred to a cron run every 15 minutes and only covers reminders with `scheduledDate` within the next hour. If a booking is cancelled or rescheduled when the reminder is due in, say, 5–15 minutes, the row is only flagged `cancelled`. The next cron run may come after the send time, or after the cutoff SendGrid allows for cancelling a scheduled send. The email is then sent for a cancelled booking. The earlier step at line 34 also deletes any row whose `scheduledDate` has passed, so the cancel flag is lost. The PR claims to fix the problem, but this window is left open. Cancelling immediately when the reminder is due within about the next hour (the pending-cancel cap is the problem for far-future sends, not near ones) would close it.

title: `client` (@sendgrid/client) is used in the cron but its API key is never set in this file
body: Only `sgMail.setApiKey` is called here. `@sendgrid/mail` keeps its own client instance, whereas the default export of `@sendgrid/client` is a separate singleton. Elsewhere `client.setApiKey` is called in emailReminderManager.ts, but that module is not imported by this API route. The new cancel loop now depends on `client.request` for `/v3/user/scheduled_sends`. If the singleton has no key in this process, every cancel fails with 401. The surrounding try/catch swallows that with a console.log, and nothing is cancelled. Call `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` in this file.

title: Reminder cancellation (now DB-write based) is fire-and-forget instead of awaited
body: Previously the `workflowReminder.deleteMany` calls were included in the awaited `Promise.all`. Now `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called without `await` or collection. The DB update (`cancelled=true`) and the row delete happen only inside these floating promises. In a serverless runtime the invocation can be frozen or terminated once the response is returned, and unhandled work is not guaranteed to finish. If the write is lost, the reminder is never flagged, the cron never cancels it, and the email or SMS is sent for a cancelled booking. The same unawaited pattern is used in `requestReschedule` in bookings.tsx and in handleNewBooking. Collect these promises and await them with the other promises.

title: try/catch around unawaited async calls can never catch anything
body: The `forEach` callbacks call `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` without awaiting them. These functions are async and catch their own errors, so the surrounding try/catch with `log.error("Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders")` is dead code. The cancellations also run un-awaited, so the reschedule can proceed (and the request can finish) before they complete. Await them with `Promise.all` if the error handling is meant to be real.

title: `Prisma` is now an unused value import
body: The import was changed from `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise }` to a value import that also pulls in `Prisma`. After removing the `Prisma.BatchPayload` usage, `Prisma` is no longer referenced anywhere in the file, so it will trigger an unused-import lint warning. The same edit left a missing trailing comma. In the commented-out `testAction` block the diff also strips indentation, which is pure noise.

title: No tests for the new deferred-cancellation flow
body: The PR changes the cancellation contract: `cancelled` flag, lazy vs. immediate delete, and the cron cancelling reminders within the next hour. It adds no tests. Nothing covers `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (null referenceId, immediateDelete, lazy flag) or the cron's selection and cancel logic. Nothing covers the failure mode that motivated the PR, where more than 100 cancellations are pending. These paths are easy to regress and hard to verify manually.

title: import() calls in the object literal run eagerly, so nothing is lazy-loaded
body: Every entry is `import("./x")`, and a dynamic import starts as soon as it is evaluated. All ~29 app modules therefore load when `@calcom/app-store` is first imported, so the cost is the same as the old static `import * as` and the lazy-loading benefit is lost. It also adds a failure mode: each promise is created up front and nobody awaits the ones that aren't used. If any single app module fails to import (missing optional dependency, bad env access at module scope), that promise rejects with no handler. That raises an unhandledRejection at startup (a process crash on Node 15+ defaults) even for code paths that never touch that app. The entries should be thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, awaited per call site, so only the needed app loads and errors surface where it is used.

title: async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch ineffective and leaves deletions un-awaited
body: The callback is now `async` and awaits `getCalendar`. `forEach` ignores the returned promises, so the enclosing `try/catch` can no longer catch anything from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent`. A failure, such as a CalendarService constructor throwing (which the old synchronous code would have caught and logged), becomes an unhandled promise rejection. The function also proceeds to send the reschedule email and `return true` before the calendar/video deletions have run. In a serverless handler the work can be cut off. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` (or a `for...of` loop with await) inside the try.

title: async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch ineffective and leaves deletions un-awaited
body: Same issue as in the vital app. `forEach(async ...)` with `await getCalendar(...)` means errors from `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent` bypass the `try/catch` and become unhandled rejections. The calendar and video deletions are not awaited before the email is sent and `true` is returned. Previously a synchronous throw from `getCalendar` would have been caught and logged. Replace with `await Promise.all(refs.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop.

title: requestReschedule fires un-awaited async deletions with no error handling
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` now awaits `getCalendar` inside a fire-and-forget callback. Nothing awaits the calendar or video deletions, and any rejection from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` is an unhandled rejection that nothing logs. The mutation continues to send emails and webhooks and resolves before the previous calendar/video events are removed. In a serverless runtime the pending work may never finish. Collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)` (with per-item error handling) before continuing.

title: Recurring-cancel branch still uses async forEach, so deletions are neither awaited nor tracked in apiDeletes
body: The PR converted the sibling legacy branch (lines ~477-483) from `forEach` to `for...of` with `await getCalendar`, so its promises land in `apiDeletes` before `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs. The recurring branch keeps `forEach(async ...)`. There, `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)` happens only after `await getCalendar(...)` and `await calendar.deleteEvent(...)`. By then `Promise.all` has already snapshotted `apiDeletes`, and the handler may have returned. The calendar events for the remaining recurring bookings are therefore not awaited and their errors are unhandled. Use a `for...of` loop (or `Promise.all` over `map`) so these deletions are actually part of `apiDeletes`. The `calendar` fetched at line 452 is also unused in this branch.

title: import() calls in the object literal run eagerly, so every app still loads at module evaluation
body: Each entry is `import("./x")` evaluated directly in the object literal. All ~29 dynamic imports start the moment `@calcom/app-store` is first imported, so every app package is still loaded on first use of the store. This gives no lazy loading, and the module graph still pulls in every app. It also adds overhead: the promises are created up front, and call sites must now `await` them. An app whose import fails produces an unhandled rejection at startup. It then rejects on every later lookup instead of being skipped. To get lazy behaviour, store thunks (`() => import("./x")`) and invoke only the one needed.

title: async forEach callback inside try/catch: errors are no longer caught and deletions are not awaited
body: The callback was made `async` so it can `await getCalendar(...)`. `forEach` ignores the returned promise, so the surrounding `try/catch` can no longer catch a `getCalendar` failure or a `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` rejection. Previously a synchronous throw from `getCalendar` was caught and logged. Now the error becomes an unhandled promise rejection. The function also continues to send emails and returns `true` before the calendar and video deletions finish. In serverless environments the work can be cut off. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try block.

title: async forEach callback inside try/catch: errors are no longer caught and deletions are not awaited
body: Same issue as the vital reschedule. `forEach(async ...)` discards the promises, so the `try/catch` around it is now dead for any rejection from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting`; these become unhandled rejections. The reschedule flow does not wait for the external deletions before sending emails and returning. Replace with `await Promise.all(refs.map(async ...))` so errors are logged and the work completes.

title: requestReschedule: async forEach leaves calendar/video deletions unawaited and rejections unhandled
body: Making the `forEach` callback async to `await getCalendar` means the mutation neither awaits nor handles failures of `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting`. There is no `try/catch` here at all. A failing integration produces an unhandled rejection, which can crash the Node process or be silently dropped. The mutation also returns, after sending emails and webhooks, before the external events are actually removed. Collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)`, with error handling.

title: Recurring-cancel path pushes into apiDeletes from an unawaited async forEach, after Promise.all has already run
body: In the `allRemainingBookings` branch, `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })` is not awaited. It also pushes the resolved result rather than the promise. `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs later and sees an `apiDeletes` array that these callbacks have not populated yet. The calendar deletions for recurring bookings are therefore never awaited, and their failures are unhandled rejections. Adding `await getCalendar` inside the callback delays the first `deleteEvent` call further, so a response (or serverless freeze) can happen before any deletion starts. Replace with a `for...of` loop or `Promise.all(map(...))` and push the promises.

title: Dynamic imports run eagerly at module load, so nothing is lazy
body: Every entry is `import("./app")`, evaluated when the `appStore` object literal is created. The first file that imports `@calcom/app-store` therefore starts loading all ~29 app packages, including their heavy SDKs and module-level side effects. This is the same eager loading as the old static imports, now with extra promise overhead and no code-splitting or cold-start benefit. Real lazy loading needs factories such as `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, called only when that app is needed.

title: Eagerly created import promises can become unhandled rejections
body: The promises are created at module load and only awaited much later, if at all. If any app module throws while loading (missing env, bad dependency), its promise rejects with no handler attached. Node's default unhandled-rejection behaviour then fires, which can crash the process or flood logs, even for requests that never use that app. Before, a failing app only broke code that touched it. With per-app lazy factories, the failure would surface only where the app is awaited.

title: async forEach makes the surrounding try/catch ineffective
body: The callback is now `async` because of `await getCalendar(...)`, and `forEach` neither awaits nor handles the returned promises. The `try { ... } catch` around it can no longer catch anything. A rejection from `getCalendar` (failed app import) or from `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled rejection instead of being logged. The function also continues to send emails and return `true` before the calendar and video deletions have finished. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try.

title: async forEach makes the surrounding try/catch ineffective
body: Same issue as in vital/lib/reschedule.ts. The `forEach(async ...)` callback is not awaited, so errors from `await getCalendar(...)`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` bypass the try/catch and surface as unhandled rejections. The reschedule flow then reports success and sends emails without waiting for the deletions. Await `Promise.all` over the references inside the try block.

title: Fire-and-forget async forEach in requestReschedule can leave unhandled rejections and unfinished deletions
body: The callback now awaits `getCalendar`, which loads an app module asynchronously, but `forEach` does not await it. There is no error handling around the calendar/video deletions. If the app import fails, or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` rejects, the result is an unhandled rejection. The mutation also proceeds to send emails and webhooks and returns before the old calendar/video events are removed, which can be cut short in serverless environments. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`, ideally with per-item error handling.

title: Recurring-cancel deletions are pushed into apiDeletes after it has already been awaited
body: The `forEach(async ...)` now does `await getCalendar(credential)` and then `await deleteEvent(...)` before pushing into `apiDeletes`. `forEach` does not wait, so the pushes land after `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` has captured the array (and after the early `await apiDeletes` in the paid path). The calendar deletions for recurring bookings are therefore never awaited. The cancellation emails go out first, and a failure becomes an unhandled rejection. The extra async hop for the app import makes this race more likely. Build the promises with `map` and await them, or use a `for...of` loop as was done in the else branch.

title: Working-hours check rejects any slot that falls outside any one range for that day
body: `workingHours.find(cb)` returns true, and the slot is rejected, as soon as the slot lies outside any single working-hour entry whose `days` includes the slot's weekday. A user with split availability on the same days (for example 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, or a lunch break) has two entries for those days.
