A slot inside the first range is always outside the second, so `find` matches and `checkIfIsAvailable` returns false. Every slot for such a host is then dropped. The check should pass if the slot lies inside at least one range (`!workingHours.some(contains slot)`), and it should apply only when entries exist for that day. Because `...schedule` is spread into every fixed and loose host check, this regresses ordinary non-round-robin events too.

title: `end` is computed from slotStartTime, so the slot end is never checked against working hours
body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start`. The intent was clearly the slot end (`slotEndTime`). As written, `end > workingHour.endTime` is just a check on the start time, so a slot that starts inside working hours but runs past their end passes. The check is effectively broken.

title: Multiple date-override ranges on the same day make every slot unavailable
body: The `dateOverrides.find` callback returns true (slot unavailable) as soon as the slot is outside any single override on that date. A host with two override ranges on one day (for example 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00) has each valid slot fail the other range's checks. A 10:00 slot is before the 14:00 range and so returns true, and the function returns false. The slot has to be rejected only if it fits none of the overrides for that date. Cal.com's date-override UI allows multiple ranges per date, so this makes valid slots disappear for those hosts.

title: Object identity comparison with `===` on dayjs objects is always false
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two freshly created objects by reference, so it never evaluates to true. This branch was meant to handle a zero-length override (the day marked unavailable). It is dead code, so that case relies on the later `isBefore`/`isAfter` checks. Compare with `.isSame()` or `.valueOf()`.

title: Override matched by UTC calendar date of its start only; overrides crossing UTC midnight are skipped
body: After shifting the override start to real UTC, the code matches an override to a slot only if the UTC date of the override start equals the UTC date of the slot start. An override that spans UTC midnight is common for hosts far from UTC, for example 06:00–12:00 in Sydney, which runs from 20:00Z the previous day to 02:00Z. Slots on the later UTC date never match, so `dateOverrideExist` stays false. Those slots fall through to the regular working-hours check and the override is ignored for them. The comparison should use the organizer-local date, or check whether the slot falls inside the [start, end) instant range.

title: Override-to-day filter is not timezone-adjusted, but the time conversion now is
body: `activeOverrides` still selects overrides whose raw `start` (the organizer's wall-clock time encoded as UTC) falls between the invitee's start and end of day. The new code then shifts the minutes by the invitee-vs-organizer offset. The day selection and the time conversion therefore use different frames. For an invitee far ahead of the organizer (for example UTC+10 and an organizer in IST), the override's real instant is on invitee day D, but the raw start falls on D+1. The override is dropped from day D and applied to D+1 at the shifted time. The filter should run on the converted start, using the same offset.

title: Shifted override minutes wrap at midnight, producing inverted or wrongly-placed ranges
body: Start and end are converted to `hour()*60 + minute()` after adding the offset, which discards the day. If the shift pushes an override across the invitee's midnight, start and end wrap to small values. A late-evening override such as 18:00–23:59 in the organizer's timezone, viewed from a timezone further east, can give an end value smaller than the start, which `buildSlots` skips (`start >= end`), so the slots vanish. If only one side wraps, the range is placed on the wrong day. Clamp or split the range at the invitee's day boundaries instead of taking time-of-day modulo 24h.

title: Offset derived from `Date.toString()` and possibly undefined timeZone
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` re-parses a host-locale string such as 'Tue Jul 04 2023 14:00:00 GMT+0000 (...)'. That is implementation-dependent and drops milliseconds; pass `override.start` directly. `override.timeZone` is optional in the updated `TimeRange` type. When it is missing, `.tz(undefined)` silently falls back to the runtime's local timezone, giving a different offset on client and server.

title: No test for the headline fix (fixed-host date overrides in round-robin)
body: The PR's main fix is that fixed hosts' date overrides and working hours are enforced in `checkIfIsAvailable` for round-robin events. The only new test is a personal-event invitee-timezone case. Nothing covers a ROUND_ROBIN event with a fixed host having an override, multiple overrides on one day, split working hours, or an override spanning UTC midnight. Those are the cases where the bugs above show up. Also, `toHaveTimeSlots` only iterates the actual slots, so a result with fewer slots than expected still passes.

title: Multiple date-override ranges on the same day make most slots unavailable
body: `dateOverrides.find(...)` returns true (slot rejected) as soon as ANY override range on that day does not contain the slot. A host with two override intervals on one date (e.g. 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00) is a supported setup. A slot at 14:30 is outside the first interval, so `find` returns true on it and the slot is rejected even though it is inside the second. The check needs to pass when the slot fits in at least one same-day override, and fail only when it fits in none. As written, the new logic wrongly drops valid slots for fixed hosts, and for collective and loose hosts too, since all of them now go through this check.

title: Slots that only partially overlap a date override are treated as available
body: The override test only rejects a slot if `slotEnd <= override.start` or `slotStart > override.end`. A slot that starts before the override and ends inside it is accepted. A slot that starts inside the override and ends after `override.end` is accepted. A slot starting exactly at `override.end` is accepted, because `isAfter` is strict. Example: with a fixed-host override of 10:00-11:00, a 10:30-11:30 or 11:00-12:00 slot generated from another host's availability passes. This is the situation the PR is meant to prevent (RR events booked when the fixed host is unavailable). The condition should be that the whole slot lies in `[override.start, override.end]`, i.e. reject when `slotStart < start` or `slotEnd > end`.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === (always false)
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct object references, so it is never true. The intended "zero-length override means unavailable" branch is dead code. Use `.isSame()` or compare the underlying values.

title: Working-hours check is wrong: `end` equals `start`, and multiple ranges per day reject everything
body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute()` is identical to `start`. It should be based on the slot end time, so a slot that runs past the end of working hours is never caught. The `find` also returns true (slot unavailable) whenever any working-hours entry for that weekday does not contain the slot. Users with split schedules (e.g. 09-12 and 13-17) produce two entries for the same day, and any slot is outside at least one of them, so nearly all slots are rejected. Because this check is now applied to every fixed and loose host, it is a regression for those schedules. It should reject only when no entry contains the slot. Working hours are also compared against the UTC weekday and minutes of the slot, which needs care for schedules that cross UTC midnight.

title: Override-to-slot matching uses the UTC calendar day and breaks for overrides crossing UTC midnight
body: An override is matched to a slot only when the UTC date of the shifted `override.start` equals the UTC date of `slotStartTime`. For organizers far from UTC, an override that begins on one UTC day and ends on the next (e.g. 10:00-18:00 PST is 18:00-02:00 UTC) will not match slots falling on the second UTC day. Those slots are then treated as having no override and fall through to the normal working-hours/busy logic. This can wrongly allow or deny them, which defeats the override.

title: Timezone-shifted overrides can wrap past midnight and land on the wrong invitee day
body: The override is selected for an invitee day by `activeOverrides` using the unshifted (organizer-wall-clock-as-UTC) `override.start`. Only afterwards is the invitee-organizer offset added and reduced to `hour()*60+minute()`. Two problems follow. (1) If the shift pushes the start/end past midnight, the minutes wrap modulo 24h, so start or end becomes a small number and the range is either dropped (`start >= end` is skipped in `buildSlots`) or shown on the wrong day. (2) The day the override is attached to is computed before the shift. With a large timezone gap (e.g. organizer in Kolkata with a 20:00-23:00 override, invitee in Tokyo) the override can be attached to the day after the one it really falls on. The shifted instant, not the raw one, should be used for both the day filter and the minute-of-day computation.

title: Parsing `override.start.toString()` is lossy and environment-dependent
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` goes through `Date.prototype.toString()`, which yields a locale/host-timezone formatted string without milliseconds that is re-parsed by the engine. Pass `override.start` directly. Also `override.timeZone` is optional in `TimeRange`, and `.tz(undefined)` silently falls back to the default zone instead of failing visibly.

title: Fixed-host round-robin date-override fix has no test; new timezone test is weak
body: The headline fix is that fixed hosts' date overrides must be respected in round-robin events, but no test covers it: no scenario with a fixed host that has an override and a round-robin host that does not. None covers multiple override ranges on one day, slots overlapping an override boundary, or overrides crossing midnight or UTC midnight, which are exactly where the new logic is fragile. The added timezone test (Dhaka) only shifts by 30 minutes and expects identical UTC slots. The `toHaveTimeSlots` matcher also passes when the actual list is shorter than the expected list, so missing slots would go unnoticed.

title: Date-override early return skips the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
body: When a slot falls on a day with a date override and is not rejected by the range checks, `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` returns before the `busy.every(...)` block. Bookings, calendar busy times and buffers are therefore never consulted for that host on override days. A fixed host with an override can be offered a slot that overlaps an existing booking or calendar event. This applies to every personal and collective event too, since those hosts are all treated as fixed. The override should only decide whether the slot is inside working time, and the busy check should still run afterwards.

title: Working-hours check rejects slots for any user with several ranges on the same day
body: `workingHours.find(...)` returns true, meaning "outside working hours", as soon as the slot is outside any single working-hour entry that includes today. `getWorkingHours` yields one entry per distinct start/end range, so a user with 9-12 and 13-17 on Mon-Fri has two entries covering the same days. A slot at 10:00 is inside the first entry but outside the second, so the whole slot is rejected. Because personal and collective hosts are `isFixed`, every user with a split schedule, such as a lunch break, would now lose all their slots. The check must pass if the slot is inside at least one entry (`some`/`every` with the logic inverted), not fail if it is outside any one.

title: `end` in the working-hours check is computed from the slot start, not the slot end
body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start`, so `end > workingHour.endTime` only tests the slot's start. A slot that starts inside working hours but runs past the end (for example a 60-minute slot at 16:30 with working hours ending at 17:00) is treated as available. It should use `slotEndTime` (start plus event length).

title: Multiple date overrides on the same day make slots unavailable
body: The override check uses `find`, which returns true ("slot not within override") if the slot is outside any one override whose day matches. A user can have several override ranges on one date, for example 9-12 and 14-17. A slot at 10:00 is inside the first range but before the second, so the second range returns true and the slot is rejected. A slot is only outside the overrides when it is outside all of them for that day. The check should be an `every`/`some` over the day's overrides, not a short-circuit on the first miss.

title: Dayjs objects compared with `===` so the zero-length override branch never fires
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two freshly created object references, which is always false, so this branch is dead code. The intent was to detect a zero-length (fully unavailable) override. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `valueOf()`.

title: Override day compared via server-local formatting against UTC slot day
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD')` formats in the server's local timezone, but it is compared with `slotStartTime.format(...)`, which is UTC. On any server whose TZ is not UTC (local dev, some deployments) the day match can be off by one and silently apply or skip overrides. Even in UTC, matching on the UTC calendar day rather than the organizer's calendar day misassigns overrides near midnight, for example a 02:00-05:00 IST override that lies on the previous UTC day. Both sides should be formatted in the same explicit timezone, normally the organizer's.

title: Override day filter and time-of-day wrap are not adjusted for the new timezone offset
body: The new offset is applied to the override's hour and minute, but `activeOverrides` still picks overrides by comparing the unshifted `override.start` to the invitee's day boundaries. An override can therefore be assigned to the wrong invitee day. Example: organizer wall-clock 20:00 and invitee +6:00. The offset is also applied via `.hour() * 60 + .minute()`, which wraps modulo 24h. An override that shifts across midnight gets a start and end on different days, so `end < start`. `buildSlots` then drops it as invalid or places it on the wrong day. The shifted range needs to be mapped to the correct invitee day and split or clamped at midnight.

title: `override.start.toString()` and optional `timeZone` used for offset calculation
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` goes through `Date.toString()`, which is locale and format dependent and drops milliseconds; pass the `Date` directly. `override.timeZone` is optional in the `TimeRange` type, and `.tz(undefined)` falls back to the server's guessed zone. Any caller that does not set `timeZone` silently gets a wrong offset (or zero) instead of the old behaviour. There should be a fallback to `organizerTimeZone` or an explicit skip when it is missing.

title: Tests do not cover the main fix (fixed-host date overrides) and the new timezone test is weak
body: The PR's headline fix is that a fixed host's date override restricts round-robin slots. No test creates a round-robin event with a fixed host and an override, and none covers split working hours, multiple overrides per day, or an override day with busy bookings. Those are exactly the cases where the new `checkIfIsAvailable` logic breaks. The added Dhaka test only asserts the same UTC slots as the IST case. The custom `toHaveTimeSlots` matcher iterates only over the actual slots and never checks the length, so missing expected slots would still pass.

title: Migration crashes when no `embed_category` row exists in site_settings
body: `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes at least one row. `embed_category` defaulted to `''` and only has a DB row if an admin changed it. On most installs the query returns zero rows, so `[0]` raises (IndexError or NoMethodError on nil) and the whole migration aborts. That also blocks the later `category_id == 0` fallback, which was written to handle exactly this case. The same unguarded `[0]['value']` is used for the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15. Both lookups need nil-safe handling.

title: Migrated hosts are inserted raw and unnormalized, via string-interpolated SQL
body: Each line of the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is interpolated straight into an INSERT: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. This skips the model's `before_validation` that strips `http(s)://` and paths. The old setting explicitly allowed values like `http://eviltrout.com` and `https://example.com/1234`, and the old matcher stripped the scheme. Those rows are now stored verbatim, but `record_for_host` compares `lower(host) = <uri.host>`, so they never match. Existing embeds silently stop working after upgrade. The lines are also not stripped of `\r` or whitespace, and a value containing a single quote would break or inject into the SQL. Normalize each host and use `quote`/sanitization.

title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
body: `self.host.sub!` is called with no nil check. `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly, so a request with a missing or empty host key sets `host = nil`. Validation then raises NoMethodError and the client gets a 500 instead of a validation error from `render_json_error`. The in-place `sub!` also mutates the attribute string. Guard with `host.present?`, or assign a new string.

title: Host lookup lowercases the column but not the input, so mixed-case referers are rejected
body: The query is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, but `host` is `URI(...).host`, which keeps the case of the referer or embed URL (for example `Blog.Example.com`). The column is lowercased and the parameter is not, so a mixed-case referer never matches and embedding is denied. The host should be downcased before comparing. The format validation accepts uppercase (`/i`), and stored hosts are not downcased on save either.

title: No uniqueness validation or index on host
body: Nothing prevents two `embeddable_hosts` rows with the same host, either in the model or as a DB unique index. If duplicates carry different categories, `record_for_host` uses `.first` with no ordering. The category chosen for imported topics is then arbitrary. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (case-insensitive) and a unique index.

title: update/destroy dereference nil when the id does not exist
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown id (for example a record already deleted in another tab). `update` then calls `save_host(nil)` and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, so both raise NoMethodError and return a 500. Use `find`, or check for nil and respond 404.

title: `update` action and JS `saveChanges` are no-ops
body: `update` just re-serializes the unchanged OpenStruct. The `PUT customize/embedding` route and the controller's `saveChanges` action (`embedding.update({})`) persist nothing, and no template references `saveChanges`. This is dead code that suggests a feature that doesn't exist. Remove the route and action, or implement them.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
body: `category_fabricator.rb` now contains only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`. `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. Fabrication loads every file, so tests still run. But anyone looking for the category fabricators, or the embeddable_host one, will look in the wrong file. Git history for the category fabricators is lost. The contents should be in the matching files.

title: Admin controller specs only assert inheritance; create/update/destroy are untested
body: Both new admin controller specs only check that the class is a subclass of `AdminController`. Nothing exercises create, update, destroy, the blank-category fallback to uncategorized, validation-error rendering, staff-only access, or the embedding show endpoint. The nil-host and nil-record failure paths above would have been caught by even basic request specs.

title: "is false if embeddable_host is blank" test no longer tests what it says
body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer looks at embeddable hosts. The test builds a topic with no `has_topic_embed?` stub and `embed_truncate` false by default, so it returns false whatever the hosts are. The test is vacuous and its name is misleading. Either delete it or make it test something real.

title: Plural `_ids` hydration assumes arrays and leaves undefined entries
body: The regex change now matches every `*_ids` key on any REST-serialized payload and calls `obj[k].map(...)` on it. A non-array value there throws and breaks hydration of the whole record. Ids that can't be resolved by `_lookupSubType` yield `undefined` elements in the array. The `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code, because `.map` always returns an array. Templates iterating the collection will then hit undefined items.

title: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when no `embed_category` row exists
body: `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the query returns a row. `site_settings` only stores rows for settings an admin changed. On a fresh install, or any site that never set `embed_category`, the result set is empty, `[0]` is `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. The fallback on line 15 has the same problem: `execute(...)[0]['value']` for `uncategorized_category_id` also breaks if that row is not present yet. Check for an empty result before indexing and default to a safe category id.

title: Migrated hosts are not normalized and are interpolated into SQL unescaped
body: Old `embeddable_hosts` values could be `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://example.com/1234`. The migration inserts each line with raw SQL, so the model's `before_validation` that strips the scheme and path never runs. Rows keep the `http://` prefix (and `\r` or whitespace if the setting had it), and `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares against `uri.host`, so they never match. Every existing site that used the scheme form silently loses embedding after upgrade. The value is also interpolated as `'#{h}'` with no quoting or escaping, so a host containing a single quote breaks the migration, or injects SQL. Strip scheme, path and whitespace in Ruby and use `quote`/sanitization.

title: before_validation calls `sub!` on a possibly-nil host
body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when `host` is nil, for example `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?`, or a POST to the controller without `embeddable_host[host]`. The user gets a 500 instead of a validation error. The `sub!` calls also mutate the caller's string in place. Guard with `host.present?` or use non-destructive `sub`.

title: Hosts with a port (or uppercase) can be saved but never match
body: The validation regex explicitly allows `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`, and the normalizer keeps the port. But `record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against `uri.host`, which never includes the port, so a host like `example.com:8080` is accepted and then never matches any referer. The right-hand side is also not downcased, so a mixed-case referer or embed URL fails against the lowercased column. Either reject ports on save or compare against `host:port`, and downcase the lookup value.

title: update/destroy dereference a nil record for unknown ids
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a missing or already-deleted id. `destroy` then calls `nil.destroy`, and `update` passes nil to `save_host`, which calls `nil.host=`. Both raise NoMethodError and return a 500. Double-clicking delete or a stale admin page hits this. Use `find` and let Discourse's RecordNotFound handling return a 404, or add an explicit not-found check. A missing `params[:embeddable_host]` has the same effect in `save_host`.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category and embeddable_host files
body: `category_fabricator.rb` now contains only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`. All the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were moved into `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. It works only because Fabrication loads every file in the directory, but it looks like an accidental swap. Anyone searching for the category fabricator or the embeddable host one will look in the wrong file, and the diff of both files is misleading. Restore the category fabricators to `category_fabricator.rb` and put only the embeddable_host fabricator in its own file.

title: New admin controllers have no behavioral tests
body: Both new controller specs only assert that the class inherits from `AdminController`. Nothing tests create/update/destroy of hosts, the uncategorized default, validation error rendering, non-staff access being denied, or the embedding show endpoint. The nil-record and nil-host crashes in this PR would have been caught by such tests. `embeddable_host_spec` also lacks cases for nil host, ports, case and duplicates.

title: "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests what it says
body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer checks for any embeddable host. This test passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false for an unsaved topic. It would still pass if host handling were broken. The behavior change (expandable posts no longer require a configured host) is untested, and the test name is misleading. Remove the case or rewrite it to reflect the actual condition.

title: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when `embed_category` (or `uncategorized_category_id`) has no row in site_settings
body: `execute("SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` indexes into a PG::Result. Sites that never changed `embed_category` have no row in `site_settings`, because defaults are not stored. Fresh installs and most upgraded sites are in this case. `[0]` is then nil and `nil['id']` raises, so the whole migration aborts and `embeddable_hosts` is never created. The fallback on line 15 has the same problem: `execute("SELECT value ... 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value']` fails if that row is missing. Use `.first`/`.ntuples` checks and fall back to a default instead of assuming a row exists.

title: Migrated hosts are inserted raw: not normalized, not SQL-escaped, blanks not skipped
body: The old `embeddable_hosts` setting allowed entries like `http://eviltrout.com` and values with surrounding whitespace or blank lines. The migration inserts each line verbatim with string interpolation, so it bypasses the model's `before_validation` that strips the scheme and path. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` with `URI(...).host`, so a row stored as `http://eviltrout.com` can never match. Every site that used the documented scheme-prefixed format silently loses embedding after upgrade. Blank lines become empty-host rows, and a quote in a value breaks the SQL statement. Strip the scheme and path, strip whitespace, skip blanks, and quote with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
body: `category_fabricator.rb` now holds only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`. The `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators were moved into `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. Fabrication loads every file in the directory, so tests still run. But the file names no longer match their contents, so anyone looking for the category fabricators will not find them. It also looks like a copy/rename mistake that will cause confusion or merge conflicts later. Each file should contain its own fabricators.

title: update/destroy dereference nil when the host id doesn't exist
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown or already-deleted id. `save_host(nil)` then calls `host.host=` on nil, and `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on nil. Both raise NoMethodError, so the client gets a 500 instead of a 404. Double-clicking delete or editing a stale list would trigger this. Use `find_by` plus an explicit not-found response, or `find`, so `RecordNotFound` is handled.

title: Missing params cause 500s; nil host blows up in the model's before_validation
body: `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises if the `embeddable_host` key is absent. If `host` is absent or nil, `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!` on nil and raises NoMethodError. Both cases give a 500 instead of a validation error from `render_json_error`. The model callback should guard against nil, and the controller should use `params.require(:embeddable_host)`. The category id is also never checked to exist.

title: Host lookup ignores case of the input and can never match hosts stored with a port
body: The query is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, where `host` is `uri.host` taken straight from the referer or embed URL. Only the column is lowercased, so a referer such as `http://Example.COM/...` never matches a stored `example.com`. The validation regex explicitly allows a `:port` suffix, and `before_validation` only strips from the first `/`, so `example.com:8080` is stored with its port. `uri.host` never includes a port, so such a record can never match any request. Normalize with `host.downcase` and decide consistently whether ports are stored or compared.

title: Host validation is overly restrictive and there is no uniqueness check
body: The regex requires a final label of 2-5 letters. This rejects `localhost`, intranet names, IPs and longer TLDs such as `.photography` or `.technology`. The old free-text setting accepted these, so admins can no longer add or re-save them. There is also no uniqueness validation on `host`, so the same host can be added repeatedly, each with a possibly different category. Which category an imported topic gets is then arbitrary, because `.first` has no ordering.

title: expandable_first_post? specs have a misleading name and a no-op fixture
body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer looks at embeddable hosts. The test "is false if embeddable_host is blank" actually passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and there is no topic embed, so it does not test what its name says. In the `'with an emeddable host'` context (typo included) the `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` has no effect on the result. The specs should be renamed or cleaned up to reflect the new behavior.

title: New admin endpoints have no behavioral tests
body: The new `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and `Admin::EmbeddingController` are covered only by a test that they subclass AdminController. There are no tests for create/update/destroy, validation errors, a missing id, default-category fallback, or non-staff access. The 500 paths in the controller therefore go unnoticed. The migration is also untested.

title: Client assigns a category that may differ from what the server saved
body: When no category is chosen, the server falls back to the uncategorized category id. After saving, the component sets `host.category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`, which is undefined for a blank id. The row then shows an empty category badge until the page is reloaded, even though the server stored Uncategorized. Use the `category_id` from the server response instead of the local `categoryId`.

title: Second `downsize` definition silently overrides the existing 5-argument `downsize`
body: `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` is defined after `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` in the same class. Ruby has no overloading, so the later definition replaces the earlier one and the `max_width, max_height` version (lines 145-147) is dead code. Any existing caller using `downsize(from, to, width, height[, opts])` now binds `height` to `opts`. `optimize` then evaluates `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer or String, which raises TypeError, or it drops the real options. Fix by using a single method that accepts the dimensions string, and update or remove the old callers.

title: Percentage geometry is passed to the animated GIF path, and the downsize result is never checked
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` can route to `downsize_instructions_animated`. That delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which runs `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. `--resize-fit` expects `WxH`, not a percentage, so gifsicle fails. The return value of `downsize` is ignored, so the loop retries the same failing command up to 5 times, and the oversized GIF is then rejected later by `Upload.create_for`. When animation is not allowed, the `[0]` frame selection silently drops the animation. The loop should stop on a `false` return, and the animated path should use a valid scale option such as `--scale`.

title: Client-side size limit hard-coded to 10MB, ignoring site settings for images and attachments
body: `maxSizeKB` used to come from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. It is now a constant 10MB for every type, including `attachment`. Sites that configure `max_attachment_size_kb` below or above 10MB no longer get a correct client-side check. Smaller limits give no early rejection, so the file is uploaded and only then fails on the server. Larger limits are blocked client-side. The error dialog also reports 10240 KB, which can differ from the real limit. The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hard-coded value. Only the image case needed relaxing, to allow server-side downsizing. The attachment setting should still be honoured, and the magic number should be defined in one place.

title: Changed `optimize`/`downsize` signatures and the new automatic downsizing have no tests
body: The `optimize` signature changes from `(operation, from, to, width, height, opts)` to `(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts)`, and `dimensions` is removed. A new overload `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` is added. `UploadsController#create_upload` also gains a retry loop that rewrites the uploaded temp file in place. No specs cover any of this. That includes images over and under `max_image_size_kb`, the 5-attempt cap, failure of the convert step, and animated GIFs. A spec would have caught the duplicate `downsize` definition.

title: Second `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) version
body: Ruby has no method overloading, so `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145. The first definition is dead code, and Ruby emits a 'method redefined' warning. Any existing caller using the width/height form now breaks: with five arguments it raises ArgumentError, and with four arguments the height is bound to `opts`, so `opts[:allow_animation]` raises or misbehaves. Keep a single `downsize` signature and update every caller, or give the new variant a different name.

title: Percentage dimensions break the animated GIF downsize path, so the loop silently fails
body: The call passes `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` with the dimension string "80%". When the setting is on and the filename matches /\.GIF$/i, `optimize` switches to `downsize_instructions_animated`. That delegates to the gifsicle command `--resize-fit 80%`, and gifsicle's `--resize-fit` takes WxH, not a percentage. The command fails and `convert_with` returns false. The return value is ignored, so the loop runs all 5 attempts, spawning a process each time, and the oversized GIF is passed on unchanged. There is also no check or log that downsizing failed.

title: Size check relies on the Tempfile handle after the file is rewritten externally by convert/ImageOptim
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` rewrites the file through its path using external `convert` and ImageOptim. The loop condition and the later `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` depend on `tempfile.size`. If ImageOptim replaces the file (new inode) rather than rewriting it in place, the open Tempfile handle can report a stale size or read stale content. The loop would then keep downsizing needlessly, or the recorded filesize would not match the stored data. Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` and reopen or rewind the file after modifying it.

title: Client-side size limit hard-coded to 10MB, ignoring max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb
body: `maxSizeKB` was `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and is now a constant 10MB for both images and attachments. Attachments are no longer checked against `max_attachment_size_kb` on the client. A site with a smaller limit lets users upload up to 10MB before the server rejects it. A site with a larger limit blocks files between the configured limit and 10MB ... and anything above 10MB, even though the setting allows it. The error dialog also reports 10MB instead of the real limit. The same hard-coded value is repeated in the 413 handler at line 246. A shared constant would at least avoid the duplication.

title: API URL download limit changed from the site setting to a hard-coded 10MB
body: `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` became `10.megabytes`. The download cap no longer follows site configuration. Sites that set `max_image_size_kb` lower now fetch up to 10MB of arbitrary data before it is rejected or downsized. Non-image attachments get the same fixed cap regardless of `max_attachment_size_kb`. This should be a named constant or setting.

title: New auto-downsizing behaviour and signature change have no tests
body: The PR adds a retry loop that rewrites the user's uploaded file, a new `OptimizedImage.downsize` signature, and removes setting-based limits from the JS validators. It adds or updates no specs. Untested cases include an oversized image being shrunk below the limit, the 5-attempt cap, GIF handling, and `max_image_size_kb == 0`. The existing JS utilities tests that exercised the setting-based limits are also not updated. The duplicate `downsize` definition would have been caught by a simple spec.

title: Second `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the 5-argument one
body: Ruby has no method overloading, so the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145. The first definition is dead code. Any existing caller using the width/height form with an options hash (5 arguments) now raises `ArgumentError`. A caller passing 4 arguments binds `max_height` to `opts`, and `opts[:allow_animation]` then fails. Keep one signature and update all callers, or give the percentage form a different name.

title: Client-side size limit hard-coded to 10MB for all upload types
body: `validateUploadedFile` used to read `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` from site settings, depending on `type`. It now uses a constant 10MB for both. The attachment limit is therefore ignored. If an admin sets it below 10MB, the client lets oversized files through and the server rejects them. If an admin sets it above 10MB, legitimate attachments are blocked on the client. The same hard-coded value is used in the 413 handler at line 246, so the error message no longer reports the real limit. Only images should get the 10MB cap, because the server now downsizes them. Attachments should keep using their setting.

title: Downsizing uses the tempfile path, so the animated GIF branch is never taken and its arguments would be wrong
body: `optimize` chooses the animated (gifsicle) variant only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Rack and Tempfile paths have no extension, so an uploaded GIF never takes that branch. The static `convert from[0] -resize 80%>` path runs instead and flattens an animated GIF to its first frame, even with `allow_animation` enabled. If the branch were taken, `resize_instructions_animated` would emit `--resize-fit 80%`, which gifsicle does not accept (it takes `WxH`, or `--scale`). The in-place conversion also writes to an extensionless output path, so the output format is inferred and is not guaranteed for formats such as SVG. The code should work from the real filename or extension and handle GIFs explicitly.

title: Return value of `downsize` ignored; failures retried 5 times and oversized file still used
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false when `convert` fails, for example when the file is corrupt or the format is unsupported. The loop ignores that result and runs the same failing command up to 5 times. It then falls through to `Upload.create_for` with the original file. Break out of the loop when `downsize` returns false. Also note that five passes of 80% only shrink each dimension to about 33%, which may not be enough for very large files. Such files then fail with a generic size error.

title: Hard-coded 10MB download cap and no server-side bound before running ImageMagick up to 5 times
body: The API URL download limit changed from the configured `max_image_size_kb` to a literal `10.megabytes`. This is also used for non-image attachments. The only enforcement of the 10MB limit for direct uploads is the client JS, which is trivially bypassed. The server now runs `convert` up to 5 times, synchronously inside `Scheduler::Defer`, on whatever size and dimensions arrive. A user can upload a very large or decompression-bomb image and consume CPU and memory repeatedly. Enforce a server-side maximum input size (and ideally dimensions) before downsizing.

title: No tests for the new auto-downsize behaviour or the changed OptimizedImage API
body: The PR adds an auto-downsize loop in the uploads controller. It also changes the signatures of `OptimizedImage.resize`, `downsize` and `optimize` and removes `dimensions`. No tests were added or updated for any of it. The duplicate `downsize` definition would have been caught by a basic spec. Add specs for uploading an oversized image, for the setting set to 0, and for the `OptimizedImage` methods.

title: unsubscribe action crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil when the user has no topic_users row. That happens for a user who was emailed through category watching, mailing-list mode or a mention but never visited the topic. The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises NoMethodError and the user gets a 500 on the unsubscribe link from the email. Use `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row if it is missing, or handle the nil case explicitly.

title: Unsubscribe toggle is not idempotent; a reload or link prefetch mutes the topic
body: The action sets the level to `regular` if the user was tracking or watching, otherwise to `muted`. Hitting the same URL a second time therefore escalates from regular to muted. Browser reload, back/forward, a mail client or security scanner prefetching the link, or clicking the email link twice all re-run the GET. The user ends up with the topic fully muted, while the page text still says only 'You will stop receiving notifications'. The action should be deterministic for a given URL, for example always mute or take an explicit target level, and should not depend on the previous state.

title: State-changing operation performed on a GET request
body: `unsubscribe` is routed as a GET and calls `tu.save!`, so it changes the user's notification level with no CSRF token and no confirmation. Any cross-site GET, such as an image or link that targets `/t/:id/unsubscribe` while the victim is logged in, silently downgrades or mutes that topic for them. Email link scanners that auto-follow URLs trigger it too. The GET should only render the page, and the change should be a POST/PUT, which is what the client's notification button already uses (`set_notifications`).

title: Direct save bypasses TopicUser.change and leaves reason/timestamp stale
body: The level is assigned and saved directly on the model instead of going through `TopicUser.change`. As a result `notifications_changed_at` is not updated and `notifications_reason_id` keeps its old value (for example `auto_watch_category`). The user's change is not recorded as `user_changed`, which later auto-tracking logic keys off (`notifications_reason_id` is null). No MessageBus `notification_level_change` is published, so other open tabs and the notification button keep the old level. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking other add_unsubscribe_link callers
body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` for every email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Only `send_notification_email` was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`. Any other caller, including plugins and the existing builder spec that had to be patched, raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and the email fails to send. The builder should only add the per-topic sentence when `unsubscribe_url` is present, or use a separate locale key.

title: New unsubscribe feature has almost no test coverage
body: The only test change adds `unsubscribe_url` to an existing builder spec so it stops raising. Nothing asserts that the generated body or HTML contains the per-topic URL. There is no controller spec for `TopicsController#unsubscribe`: the slug redirect, the tracking/watching to regular and regular to muted transitions, the missing TopicUser row, and the logged-out case. There is no spec for `Topic#unsubscribe_url` or the new routes. The nil-TopicUser crash and the non-idempotent toggle would have been caught by such tests.

title: Logged-out email recipients get a bare 403 instead of a login path
body: `unsubscribe` is added to the `ensure_logged_in` list, but it is the target of a link in an email. Recipients are often not logged in on the device where they open it. For a non-XHR GET the user lands on a generic 403 page with no redirect to login and no way to complete the unsubscribe, so the feature's main entry point fails for them.

title: unsubscribe dereferences a possibly-nil TopicUser
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when the logged-in user has no `topic_users` row for the topic, and the next line calls `tu.notification_level` on it. That raises NoMethodError and the page returns a 500. The URL is a plain GET, so any logged-in user can reach it for a topic they never visited, for example by following a forwarded email link from another account. Handle nil, either with `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row, or by returning a clean error.

title: Unsubscribe toggle is not idempotent: reloading the page mutes the topic
body: The first visit drops a watching or tracking user to regular. Any later hit on the same URL, whether a page reload, a double click, or an email-client or security-scanner prefetch, sees `notification_level <= regular` and mutes the topic. A user who only asked to stop watching can end up with the topic fully muted. The resulting state depends on how many times the URL is requested, not on user intent. The action should be idempotent, or require explicit confirmation before escalating to muted.

title: State-changing action exposed on GET (CSRF / prefetch)
body: `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` map to an action that writes `topic_users.notification_level`. GET requests are not covered by CSRF protection. A post or any third-party page that embeds an image or link pointing at `/t/x/<id>/unsubscribe` will change the notification level for any logged-in viewer. Link prefetchers and scanners trigger it too. The write should be a POST/PUT from the client page (with a CSRF token) after the user confirms, rather than a side effect of loading the page.

title: Direct save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping and MessageBus
body: The notification level is set by assigning the attribute and calling `tu.save!`. Everywhere else it is changed through `TopicUser.change`, which sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (to `user_changed`) and publishes `notification_level_change` on MessageBus. Here the reason stays at its old value, the timestamp is not updated, and other open tabs are not told about the change. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` to keep behaviour consistent.

title: add_unsubscribe_link now silently requires an unsubscribe_url option
body: The English `unsubscribe_link` string now contains `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `html_part` (line 67) and `body` (line 90) interpolate it from `template_args` with no default. Any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url`, including plugins and other mailers, will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` when the email is built. The spec had to be edited to pass `unsubscribe_url` to avoid this. Provide a fallback in `template_args`, or only include the per-topic sentence when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

title: Template name likely does not match the topicUnsubscribe route
body: The route is declared as `topicUnsubscribe` and the controller, view and route files are all named `topic-unsubscribe`, but the template lives at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, so its name is `topic/unsubscribe`. The Discourse resolver looks up `topicUnsubscribe`, `topic_unsubscribe` and `topic-unsubscribe`, not `topic/unsubscribe`. If it does not resolve, the unsubscribe page renders empty and shows neither the message nor the notification dropdown. Rename the file to `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`, or verify that the resolver finds the nested path.

title: New unsubscribe feature has no tests
body: The only spec change is adding `unsubscribe_url` to an existing fixture so it stops raising. Nothing asserts that the per-topic URL appears in the email body or HTML part. There is no controller spec for `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, covering downgrade to regular, escalation to muted, the slug redirect, the missing-TopicUser case and the not-logged-in case. There is no spec for `Topic#unsubscribe_url`. The behaviour problems above (nil TopicUser, non-idempotent toggle) would have been caught by basic controller tests.

title: Explicit `render :show` makes `show` render before `canonical_url` is set
body: `perform_show_response` now calls `render :show` inside the `format.html` block. In `show`, `perform_show_response` is called first and `canonical_url UrlHelper.absolute_without_cdn(...)` is called right after it. Previously the template rendered implicitly after the action returned, so the canonical URL was set before the layout ran. Now the view and layout are rendered immediately inside `perform_show_response`, so the later `canonical_url` call has no effect on the HTML. Topic pages will lose the correct `<link rel="canonical">` and fall back to the request URL, for example `/t/slug/id/5`. That is an SEO regression on every topic page. Fix by calling `canonical_url` before `perform_show_response`, or by rendering only in `unsubscribe`.

title: `TopicUser.find_by` can return nil, causing a 500 in `unsubscribe`
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil when the logged-in user has no `topic_users` row for that topic, which is the case for any other user who opens the URL. The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises NoMethodError and the user gets a 500 error page. The action should create the row, for example via `TopicUser.change`, or handle the nil case.

title: Notification level changed with `save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`
body: The action sets `tu.notification_level` directly and calls `tu.save!`. This bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which also sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (user_changed) and publishes the `notification_level_change` MessageBus message. With `notifications_reason_id` left unchanged (often NULL), `TopicUser.update_last_read` will later auto-promote the topic back to `tracking` once the user has read enough. That silently undoes the mute or unsubscribe. Open clients also never receive the level change. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`.

title: State-changing, non-idempotent toggle behind a GET route
body: `unsubscribe` is routed as a GET and mutates the user's notification level on every request. Each reload or repeat visit steps it down further: watching/tracking becomes regular, regular becomes muted, muted stays muted. A single click followed by a refresh, or the back button, therefore mutes the topic instead of just unsubscribing. Because it is a GET with no CSRF protection, any third-party page that embeds `` can mute topics for a logged-in visitor. The `.json` format variant mutates as well. The action should compute a deterministic target state, or require an explicit POST/PUT from the confirmation page.

title: `unsubscribe_link` string now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`, which breaks callers that omit it
body: The English `unsubscribe_link` string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Both `html_part` (line 67) and `body` (line 90) call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`. Any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` (other mailers, plugins, existing specs) now raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` when the email is built. The spec had to be edited to pass `unsubscribe_url` for exactly this reason. The builder should supply a fallback or only include the per-topic sentence when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

title: No tests for the new unsubscribe action, URL helper, or email content
body: The only spec change adds an `unsubscribe_url` option to an existing message-builder example. There is no controller spec for `TopicsController#unsubscribe`: login required, slug redirect, level transitions, missing `TopicUser` row, JSON vs HTML. There is no spec for `Topic#unsubscribe_url`. There is no spec that the notification email actually contains the per-topic unsubscribe link in both the HTML and text parts. The nil-`TopicUser` crash and the idempotency problem above would have been caught by such tests.

title: should_block? writes to the DB and is called from a validator, so match_count is inflated
body: `should_block?` increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at` and saves the record, yet it is called from `EmailValidator#validate_each`. Validators should be side-effect free and may run many times per request. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which validates again, so one signup attempt bumps the counter twice (and any other `valid?` call adds more). The statistics are therefore wrong. Each validation also costs an extra SELECT, the uniqueness-validation query inside `record.save`, and an UPDATE. The stats update should happen once, at the point where the block is actually enforced, not inside validation.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so blocking is trivially bypassed
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact string match, and `User.new_from_params` stores the email as typed without downcasing. A blocked address such as `bad@spamclub.com` can be bypassed by signing up as `Bad@SpamClub.com`. Elsewhere in the codebase emails are normalised with `Email.downcase`. Both the stored blocked email and the lookup value should be normalised, for example downcased in `before_validation` and in `should_block?`.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count
body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` loads the value into Ruby, increments it and writes it back. Concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email will lose increments. `increment_counter`, or an `update_all` with `match_count = match_count + 1`, would be atomic and skip the validation and uniqueness query on every hit.

title: Invalid Ember dependent key 'rejectedEmails.@each'
body: `@each` is only valid as `rejectedEmails.@each.someProp`, and the array-change key for a plain array is `rejectedEmails.[]`. With `'rejectedEmails.@each'` the `emailValidation` property may not recompute when `pushObject` adds a rejected email. In that case the UI would not flag the rejected address until `accountEmail` changes, which defeats the purpose of the feature.

title: Mutable array declared on the controller prototype is shared
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` in `.extend({...})` creates one array shared by every instance of the class, and it is never reset. Rejected emails therefore persist across any reuse of the controller, and a rejected address stays flagged even after the underlying issue (for example a blocklist change) is resolved. Initialise it per instance in `init`.

title: Validator spec doesn't cover whitelist/blacklist paths or interaction with blocked check
body: The domain whitelist and blacklist logic was moved out of `User` into `EmailValidator`, but the new spec only covers the blocked-email branch with a stubbed `BlockedEmail`. It does not test that whitelist or blacklist violations still add `not_allowed`, or that `should_block?` is skipped (so no stats update happens) when a domain error already exists. A regression in the moved code would go unnoticed.

title: Validator calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which writes to the DB, so stats are counted more than once per signup
body: `should_block?` increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at` and saves the record. It is called from inside a validator, which should be side-effect free. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which validates again, so one signup attempt bumps the counters at least twice. Any other `valid?` call on a user with a changed email does the same. Statistics for `do_nothing` entries are inflated. Entries for `block` can be written outside the save transaction, so they are not rolled back. The lookup-and-record-hit logic should run once at a deliberate point, or the validator should do a read-only check.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count loses updates under concurrency
body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` loads the row, increments in Ruby and writes back the absolute value. Two concurrent signups with the same email both read N and both write N+1, so a hit is lost. It also runs a full save with callbacks and a uniqueness validation query on every check. Use `BlockedEmail.increment_counter(:match_count, record.id)` or `update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])` so the increment happens atomically in SQL.

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and not normalized, so it is trivially bypassed
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact string match, and the unique index on `blocked_emails.email` is case-sensitive too. If `bad@spamclub.com` is blocked, `Bad@SpamClub.com` or ` bad@spamclub.com` passes the check. The rest of the codebase normalizes emails with `Email.downcase` and `strip`. Stored and queried emails should be normalized (for example downcased on save and on lookup), otherwise the blocking feature is easy to evade.

title: Array literal on the controller prototype is shared across instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is declared in `extend({...})`, so the one array lives on the prototype and is shared by every instance. `pushObject` then mutates shared state, so rejected emails persist across all controller instances (and across tests). It should be initialized per instance in `init`, for example `this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A([]))`.

title: Invalid computed-property dependent key 'rejectedEmails.@each'
body: In Ember, `@each` must be followed by a property name (`rejectedEmails.@each.foo`). To observe array membership changes the key should be `rejectedEmails.[]`. With a bare `.@each` the `emailValidation` property may not be invalidated when `pushObject` adds a rejected email. The "rejected email" feedback then wouldn't update until `accountEmail` changes.

title: Client marks any email-error rejection as 'invalid' and hides the real server reason
body: The JS adds the email to `rejectedEmails` whenever `errors.email` is present, and `emailValidation` then shows the generic `user.email.invalid` text. The server-side reasons (`blocked`, `not_allowed`, already taken) are not shown in the field. The new `user.email.blocked` message appears only in the flash, and the inline field gives a misleading "invalid" message. The per-field error from `errors.email` should be used as the validation reason.

title: Tests don't cover validator interaction with whitelist/blacklist or the User model integration
body: The spec only stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?` and checks the error toggles. It does not cover the moved whitelist/blacklist logic, the short-circuit when an earlier error exists, a nil or blank value, or an end-to-end `User` validation. It also does not cover the new `errors`/`values` JSON returned by `UsersController#create`, or the repeated validation calls that inflate `match_count`. Regressions in the refactor out of `User#email_validator` would not be caught here.

title: Validation has a DB-write side effect, so match_count is over-counted
body: `should_block?` increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at` and saves the record. It is called from `EmailValidator#validate_each`, which runs on every validation of a user whose email changed. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which validates again. A single signup attempt with a blocked email therefore bumps the counter twice. Any other `valid?` call on a new or changed user does the same. Statistics collection and validation should be separate. Record the hit only when the block actually rejects a save, or do it explicitly in the controller.

title: Read-modify-write counter update loses concurrent increments
body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` is a read-modify-write on an in-memory copy. Two concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked address can both read N and both write N+1, losing a count. `save` also runs the model validations, including the uniqueness query, on every hit. An atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.increment_counter` or `update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?")` avoids both problems.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so it can be bypassed
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact, case-sensitive match. Email addresses are case-insensitive, and the rest of the app normalizes with `Email.downcase`. A blocked address like `bad@spammers.org` can be bypassed by registering `Bad@Spammers.org`. The `uniqueness: true` validation and the unique index on `blocked_emails.email` are also case-sensitive, so case-variant duplicates can be stored. Normalize to lowercase on save and on lookup, or compare with `lower(email)`.

title: Block check is skipped whenever any earlier error exists on the attribute
body: The blocked-email check only runs if `record.errors[attribute].blank?`. Presence and uniqueness validators run first, so a duplicate email never reaches the check. Hit statistics for a blocked address are skipped whenever another error is present. The condition also depends on validator declaration order, which is fragile. Make the block check independent of other errors, or document that it is intentionally conditional.

title: Every server-side email error is shown as a generic 'invalid' email
body: On any failed signup where `result.errors.email` is present, the submitted email is added to `rejectedEmails`. `emailValidation` then shows `user.email.invalid` for that address. The server error may be that the email is already taken, is not allowed from that provider, or is blocked. All of these now show the same generic message, which can mislead the user. The list is also never cleared and is declared as `Em.A([])` on the controller prototype, so it is shared state.

title: Moved whitelist/blacklist logic and the double-validation side effect are not tested
body: The whitelist/blacklist domain logic moved from `User#email_validator` into `EmailValidator`, but the new validator spec only covers the blocked-email stub. No test covers the whitelist or blacklist branches, or the skip-when-already-errored behavior. Nothing checks that a signup with a blocked email returns the new `errors`/`values` fields from `UsersController#create`. Nothing covers case variants of a blocked address, and no test exposes that validating twice increments `match_count` twice.

title: raw_html posts are served with no sanitization (stored XSS)
body: `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == raw_html`. For imported content this means RSS item bodies (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)`) and `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` output (a Nokogiri round-trip that does not sanitize) are stored as `cooked`. They are then rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and in the regular topic view. `<script>`, `onerror=` handlers and `javascript:` links in a feed or page therefore execute on the forum origin. The `import_remote` path restricts tags, but the RSS path does not. Run the HTML through a whitelist sanitizer (e.g. `Sanitize`) at import or in `cook`.

title: Embed URL interpolated into HTML unescaped; URL check uses `^` instead of `\A`
body: The footer is built as `"#{url}"` with no escaping, and that string goes into a post that is never sanitized (raw_html). The only guard is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` on line 11. `^` matches at any line start, so a value like `"junk\nhttp://x"` passes. A `'` in a feed-supplied link (for example `http://a/' onmouseover='...`) breaks out of the attribute. Anchor the check with `\A`, parse the URL, and escape it with `ERB::Util.h` or `CGI.escapeHTML`.

title: import mutates the caller's contents string in place
body: `contents << "...footer..."` appends to the string passed in. This breaks on frozen strings and has surprising side effects for callers that reuse the string, such as the spec's `let(:contents)` or the Disqus importer. Use `contents = contents + footer` or build a new local string.

title: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs and ignores other relative paths
body: The `start_with?('/')` check also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/a.png`. `sub(/^\/+/, '')` then strips every leading slash and yields `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/a.png`, a broken link or image. The same bug is on line 71 for `src`. Relative paths without a leading slash (`images/x.png`, `../x`) are not resolved at all, even though the method is documented as converting relative URLs to absolute. Use `URI.join(url, href)` for non-absolute values and skip anything that already has a scheme or a `//` prefix.

title: embed.post can be nil (soft-deleted post), crashing the update path
body: `post = embed.post` goes through Post's trashable default scope. If the imported post or topic was deleted, the association returns nil. When the content hash changes, `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then raises NoMethodError on `nil.raw`. In `PollFeed` this aborts the whole `rss.items.each` loop, so one deleted topic blocks all later imports every hour. Guard against a nil post, and either skip it or recreate the topic.

title: Disqus importer silently loses --category option and original topic created_at
body: The `-c/--category` option and its lookup are removed, and `PostCreator` is replaced by `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. All imported topics now land in the default category, and `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` is dropped, so topics get today's date instead of the Disqus thread date. The importer now also does a live HTTP fetch of every thread link via `open(url).read`, with no error handling. A single 404 or timeout raises and aborts the whole import. None of this is mentioned in the PR.

title: Unrelated edit to an existing migration adds destructive `force: true`
body: This PR rewrites an already-existing migration (`create_top_topics`) to use `force: true`, which drops and recreates `top_topics` if the migration is ever re-run. That is unrelated to embedding and destructive. `create_topic_embeds` also uses `force: true` (line 3) and would drop an existing `topic_embeds` table and its data. Editing historical migrations, and the whitespace-only change to `migrate_word_counts`, should be left out of this PR.

title: New gems added without updating the Rails 3 lockfile
body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` are added to the shared Gemfile, but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` is updated. The repo is dual-booted, and `Gemfile.lock` (RAILS3=1 mode) is not touched. Bundler in that mode will have to re-resolve, or fail with a frozen or deployment lockfile, and CI for the Rails 3 boot is likely to break.

title: embed.css / embed.js not added to the asset precompile list
body: The layout calls `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`, and `embed.js` is meant to be loaded by third-party sites. Neither asset is added to `config.assets.precompile` (no change to `config/application.rb` in this PR). With precompiled assets in production the stylesheet raises or 404s, so the embed iframe renders unstyled or errors. `embed.js` will not be served either.

title: Referer interpolated into an inline JS string with HTML escaping only
body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` places a request header inside a JavaScript string using HTML escaping, which is the wrong context. A backslash is not escaped, so a referer ending in `\` breaks the string and the script. Escaped entities such as `'` are not decoded inside `<script>`, so the value is mangled. It should be emitted with `.to_json` or `j()`. It is also better to use the origin derived from the validated `embeddable_host` than the raw header.

title: Origin check is a substring test
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` only checks that the message origin is a substring of the configured URL. A different-origin sender can match, for example `https://example.com` against `https://example.com:8080/`. Compare against the exact origin of `discourseUrl` and also check `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`.

title: Nil item content or one bad item aborts the whole feed poll
body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no `content` (common for RSS items that only have `description`). There is no per-item rescue, so one bad entry stops processing of all remaining items on every hourly run. The same loop also reaches the nil-post crash in `TopicEmbed.import`. Handle nil content (fall back to `description`/`summary`) and rescue per item so one failure doesn't block the rest.

title: Each unknown embed URL can trigger a full synchronous feed poll
body: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline whenever an unknown embed URL is requested. The throttle key is per URL, so requests for many different URLs each fetch and parse the entire feed and import every item in a Sidekiq worker, with no timeout. Since the `embed/best` endpoint enqueues this job for any unseen URL, it is an easy amplification path. Throttle at the feed level (e.g. one key for the feed URL) rather than per embed URL.

title: Embeddability gate relies solely on the Referer header
body: Access is allowed only if `request.referer`'s host equals `embeddable_host`. Referer is client-controlled and trivially spoofed by non-browser clients, and is dropped for legitimate embeds when the embedding page sets a strict Referrer-Policy. Those embeds get an InvalidAccess error. Also, `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid value, and framing is unrestricted once the Referer check passes. Consider CSP `frame-ancestors` for the configured host.

title: Malformed `<%- end if %>` closes the conditional with a modifier
body: `end if` turns the following generated statement into an `if` modifier condition on the whole if/else block. It only works by accident because the next generated expression is a truthy string append. It reads as a typo and is fragile against template changes. It should be `<%- end %>`.

title: "is 404 without an embed_url" passes for the wrong reason
body: With no stubs, `embeddable_host` is blank, so the request fails in `ensure_embeddable` before `params.require(:embed_url)` is ever reached, and the failure is an InvalidAccess response, not a 404. The missing-parameter path is never exercised. There is also no test for a referer whose host differs from `embeddable_host`. The new `PollFeed#poll_feed`, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` and the update branch of `import` also have no meaningful coverage.

title: raw_html posts are stored and rendered with no sanitization (stored XSS)
body: `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == raw_html`, so none of the normal cooking or sanitizing pipeline runs. The content comes from remote sources. In `PollFeed` it is `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)`, which turns escaped entities such as `<script>` back into live markup. In `import_remote` it is the readability output. Nothing in `TopicEmbed.import` or `absolutize_urls` strips scripts, event handlers, or `javascript:` links. The result is written to `posts.cooked`, shown on the main site, and emitted via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in the embed iframe, which is served from the Discourse origin with `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`. A compromised or malicious feed or page can therefore run script in Discourse's origin. The imported HTML should be sanitized with a whitelist before it is saved or served.

title: `<%- end if %>` is invalid ERB/Ruby and breaks the best template
body: The `if/else` opened on line 2 is closed with `end if`, a modifier `if` with no condition. Erubis appends `;` after a statement tag, which yields `end if ;`. That is a syntax error, or at best an `if` conditioned on the next emitted output statement. Either way the template cannot render correctly, so `embed/best` fails whenever a topic already exists. It should be `<%- end %>`. The controller specs do not render views, so nothing catches this.

title: Wrapping PostCreator in Topic.transaction defeats its after-commit job enqueueing
body: `PostCreator#create` deliberately enqueues `process_post` and `feature_topic_users` after its own transaction commits (see the comment in `enqueue_jobs`). Wrapping the call in an outer `Topic.transaction` means those jobs are enqueued before the outer transaction commits, which now also includes `TopicEmbed.create!`. In production a Sidekiq worker can pick up `process_post` before the post row is visible and fail or skip processing. It also makes the rollback semantics unclear, because the `ActiveRecord::Rollback` raised inside PostCreator's nested transaction does not roll back the outer one.

title: Failed post creation is not detected before creating the TopicEmbed
body: `PostCreator#create` returns `@post` even when it failed and rolled back, for example on host-spam detection or a save failure. That post is unsaved, so `post.present?` is still true. `TopicEmbed.create!` then runs with `post_id: nil` and `topic_id: nil`, which raises a NOT NULL violation. This surfaces as a confusing exception in the job instead of a clean failure. The guard should check `post.persisted?` or `post.errors.blank?`. The update branch has a related problem: `embed.post` can be nil if the post was deleted, and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` then blows up.

title: Kernel#open on a URL string allows command execution and unchecked fetches
body: `open(url)` is `Kernel#open` with open-uri loaded, so a string starting with `|` runs a shell command. `import_remote` does not validate its argument itself. Only the `TopicRetriever` path checks the host. The Disqus thor task passes `t[:link]` straight from an XML export, and `PollFeed` does `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` the same way. Use `URI.parse(url).open`, or RestClient, after verifying the scheme is http or https, and set explicit timeouts. `open-uri` is also only required in `poll_feed.rb`, so `import_remote` can fail with ENOENT if that file has not been loaded.

title: import mutates its input and interpolates the URL into HTML unescaped
body: `contents << ...` appends the footer to the caller's string in place. Callers that reuse the string, such as the memoized `let(:contents)` in the spec, see it change. The URL is also placed into `#{url}` without escaping. The only validation is `/^https?:\/\//`, which uses `^` rather than `\A`, so a multi-line value with `http://` on a later line passes. A `'` or `<` in the URL can inject attributes or markup into a post that is never sanitized. Build a new string, escape the URL, and anchor the regex with `\A`.

title: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs and ignores other relative forms
body: `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative links such as `//cdn.example.com/x.jpg`. `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, giving `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.jpg`, which is a broken link. The same happens for `img src` on line 71. Relative paths without a leading slash (`images/a.png`, `../a.png`) are left untouched, and the code resolves against only scheme and host rather than the article URL. The port check (`!= 80 && != 443`) is also wrong for https on 80 or http on 443. `URI.join(url, href)` handles all of these correctly.

title: One bad feed item aborts the whole poll (nil content, no per-item rescue)
body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no `content`, which is common for RSS 2.0 feeds that only carry `description`. The loop has no per-item rescue, so one such item, or an exception from `TopicEmbed.import` (such as `create!` validation or a DB error on a long title), stops the import of every item after it. The job runs with `retry: false`, so the same item blocks the feed on every hourly run. Fall back to `description` when `content` is nil, and rescue and log errors per item.

title: Throttle is keyed on the full URL and non-atomic, so it is trivially bypassed
body: The key is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`, so varying the query string (`?a=1`, `?a=2`, ...) on the allowed host gets a fresh throttle slot each time. Each one triggers a full `Jobs::PollFeed` run (fetch, parse and import of the whole feed) when feed polling is enabled, plus a remote HTTP fetch and a new topic via `import_remote`. This allows request amplification and duplicate topics per URL variant. The embed URL should be canonicalized, and there should be a global limit on retrievals. Separately, `setnx` followed by `expire` is not atomic. A crash between the two leaves a key that never expires and blocks that URL permanently. Use `SET key val NX EX 60`.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test. Any origin that is a substring of the configured URL passes. For example, with `discourseUrl = 'http://forum.example.com/'`, a message from origin `http://forum.example.co` is accepted. Compare `e.origin` for equality against the origin parsed from `discourseUrl`.
