title: Request referer interpolated into an inline JS string as the targetOrigin
body: `request.referer` is attacker-influenced (path and query are free-form) and is only HTML-escaped inside a `<script>` block, where entities are not decoded. A trailing backslash in the referer escapes the closing quote and breaks the script, so the resize message is never sent. HTML-escaping is also the wrong encoding for a JS context, and `&` sequences end up in the string. `postMessage` expects an origin, so emit `scheme://host[:port]` derived server-side and serialize it with `to_json` or `j`.

title: `force: true` in migrations drops an existing table
body: `create_table ..., force: true` runs `DROP TABLE` first if the table exists. Here it is in the new `topic_embeds` migration and in the edited `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`. The latter is an already-applied migration unrelated to this feature, and the edit has no effect except when the migration is re-run, when it silently destroys data. Remove `force: true` from the new migration and leave the old migration untouched.

title: Disqus import silently drops the --category option and original thread dates
body: The `-c/--category` option and its lookup are removed, and topic creation now goes through `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which takes no category or `created_at`. Existing users of the task lose category placement and the original topic timestamps. Each import now also performs a live HTTP fetch of the thread link, so the task fails or produces content from the live site if the link is dead. This is a behaviour change unrelated to the embed feature and is not mentioned in the PR.

title: Controller specs pass for the wrong reason and miss the key access check
body: 'is 404 without an embed_url' does not set `embeddable_host`, so `ensure_embeddable` raises InvalidAccess before `params.require` is reached. The test passes without exercising the missing-parameter path. `should_not be_success` is also too weak to tell the cases apart. There is no test for a referer whose host differs from `embeddable_host`, which is the central security check, and none for a malformed referer. Nothing covers the `loading` branch.

title: New gems added to the Gemfile but only the rails4 lockfile was updated
body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` were added for both Rails 3 and Rails 4 boot modes, but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` was updated. If a separate `Gemfile.lock` exists for the Rails 3 mode, it is now out of sync, and `bundle install --deployment` or frozen installs there will fail.

title: raw_html cook method skips all sanitization, so imported feed HTML is stored and served as-is (stored XSS)
body: `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == :raw_html`, bypassing the cooking pipeline and its sanitizer. `TopicEmbed.import` feeds this path with unsanitized RSS/Atom item content (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` in PollFeed) and with remote page HTML. That content is stored in `posts.cooked` and rendered unescaped with `raw post.cooked` in `embed/best.html.erb` and in the main forum UI. Any `<script>`, `onerror=` or `javascript:` payload in a third-party feed, or injected into a compromised feed, therefore runs in the forum's origin. The cook step also runs on every later save, so editing does not clean it. Sanitize the HTML (for example with the already-bundled `sanitize` gem and a whitelist) before storing or rendering it.

title: URL interpolated unescaped into the HTML footer, and URL check uses multiline `^`
body: `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` uses `^`, which matches at the start of any line, so a value like `"junk\nhttp://x"` passes. The URL is then interpolated unescaped into `#{url}`, and the result is stored with the raw_html cook method, which does no sanitizing. A feed item `` or `` containing `'` or `<` can therefore break out of the attribute and inject markup. Validate with `\A...\z` or `URI.parse`, and HTML-escape the URL (`ERB::Util.h`) before building the footer.

title: Kernel#open on an admin-supplied string allows command execution and local file reads
body: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open` (open-uri patched) on a site-setting string. If the value starts with `|`, `open` runs it as a shell command. A plain path reads local files. Site admins are not normally trusted with shell access on the server. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` and `disqus.thor` use the same pattern. Parse the URL, require an http(s) scheme, and call `URI.parse(url).open`, with explicit timeouts.

title: Feed items without `content` crash the whole poll
body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no `content`. Many RSS 2.0 feeds provide only `<description>`, so `i.content` is nil. One such item aborts the loop, and every later item in the feed is skipped on every run. `String#scrub` also requires Ruby 2.1+, which may not match the supported Ruby versions. Fall back to `description`, skip items with blank content, and rescue per item so one bad entry does not stop the import.

title: Wrapping PostCreator in an outer transaction enqueues jobs before commit
body: `PostCreator#create` deliberately enqueues `process_post` and `feature_topic_users` after its own transaction, so workers cannot see uncommitted rows (see the comment in `enqueue_jobs`). Wrapping it in `Topic.transaction` here defeats that: the jobs and the TopicTrackingState/MessageBus publishes fire before the outer transaction commits. If `TopicEmbed.create!` then fails, for example on the unique `embed_url` index when PollFeed and RetrieveTopic race, the transaction rolls back but the jobs and notifications for the non-existent post have already gone out. Create the embed row outside this wrapping transaction, or handle the failure explicitly.

title: `post.present?` is always true for an unsaved post, so create! can fail on null post_id
body: `PostCreator#create` returns `@post` even when saving failed and it rolled back, in which case the post is unsaved with `errors` populated. An ActiveRecord object is always `present?`, so the code goes on to `TopicEmbed.create!(post_id: post.id ...)` with nil ids. That raises a DB NOT NULL violation (`post_id` is `null: false`) instead of failing cleanly. Check `post.persisted?` or `creator.errors.blank?`.

title: Existing embed whose post was deleted causes NoMethodError on every re-import
body: In the update branch, `post = embed.post` is nil if the post was trashed, because Trashable scopes out deleted posts. When the content hash changes, `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises. In PollFeed that aborts the rest of the feed every hour. The stale `topic_embeds` row also prevents the URL from ever being re-imported. Handle a missing post: skip, or remove the embed and re-create.

title: `open(url)` used without requiring open-uri
body: `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` but this file never requires `open-uri`. It only works if `jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` (which has the require) or some gem happened to load it first. Otherwise `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a filename and raises Errno::ENOENT. This is likely in the thor Disqus import and in a lazily-loaded dev/test environment. Add `require 'open-uri'` here and prefer `URI.parse(url).open`.

title: Protocol-relative URLs are mangled by absolutize_urls
body: Any `href`/`src` beginning with `/` is rewritten as `prefix + '/' + href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/a.jpg` becomes `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/a.jpg`, which is a broken link or image. Skip values starting with `//`, or resolve with `URI.join(url, href)`, which also handles `../x` and `images/x.png`.

title: Embed import paths are barely tested
body: The specs only cover a malformed URL, the happy create path, and a trivial update. Nothing covers `import_remote`, `PollFeed#poll_feed` (nil content, relative links), the unchanged-hash path, the deleted-post path, or the HTML-escaping of the footer URL. Those are exactly where the bugs above live.

title: setnx followed by expire is not atomic
body: If the process dies or Redis errors between `setnx` and `expire`, the `retrieved:<url>` key stays forever and that URL can never be retrieved again by non-staff users. Use a single atomic `SET key value NX EX 60` call (or `setex` semantics) instead.

title: Unauthenticated requests can trigger unbounded fetches and topic creation
body: The only gate is the spoofable Referer header plus a per-URL 60s throttle. Any client can request `/embed/best?embed_url=` with arbitrarily many distinct URLs on the embeddable host (for example, differing query strings). Each distinct URL enqueues a job, and each job polls the entire feed synchronously (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute`) and fetches the page. If it parses, the page is turned into a new topic, so URLs with different query strings each get their own. This allows unlimited topic creation and outbound-request amplification. Add a global rate limit, URL normalization, and possibly an allowed-path/pattern setting.

title: `<%- end if %>` is malformed ERB/Ruby
body: `end if` ends the block and then applies a dangling `if` modifier to whatever expression the ERB compiler emits next (the following output-buffer append). It only works by accident and obscures the template's logic. It should be `<%- end %>`. Separately, the logo links in the header (line 8) and footer (line 26) lack `target: '_blank'`, so clicking the logo loads the entire forum inside the small embed iframe.

title: Substring check on message origin is not a valid origin validation
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`. For `http://forum.example.com/`, a message from `http://forum.example.co` passes. The check also ignores `e.source`, and `e.data.height` is applied unvalidated. Compare `e.origin` for exact equality against the origin of `discourseUrl`, check `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`, and coerce height to a bounded number.

title: Referer emitted into a JS string with HTML escaping
body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` uses HTML escaping inside a `<script>` block. `&` becomes `&` and `'` becomes `'`, and a backslash is not escaped. The value is only coincidentally harmless, because the host was validated and postMessage uses only the origin part. A referer ending in `\` breaks the string literal and the resize message. Use `<%= raw request.referer.to_json %>`, or better the validated `embeddable_host` origin, rather than the raw Referer.

title: Unrelated edit to an existing migration adds `force: true`, which drops the table
body: This PR modifies an already-committed migration to add `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics`. `force: true` drops any existing `top_topics` table before creating it, so re-running or resetting this migration destroys data. The change has nothing to do with embedding. The same file set also includes a whitespace-only edit to `20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` (and it removes the trailing newline). Revert both edits to old migrations, and avoid `force: true` unless it is truly intended.

title: Disqus importer loses `--category` and now requires live HTTP fetches
body: The `-c/--category` option was removed, so existing invocations now fail and imported topics can no longer be placed in a category. The topic's `created_at` from Disqus is also dropped, so topics get the import time. Each thread now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote` on the thread link, which makes a network fetch. A 404 or timeout raises and aborts the whole import. A non-http link makes `import` return nil, so the thread is silently skipped. This changes the tool's behavior without fallback or documentation.

title: Only the Rails 4 lockfile is updated for the new gems
body: The new `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` gems are added to the shared Gemfile and `Gemfile_rails4.lock`. The Rails 3 lock (`Gemfile.lock`, used when `RAILS3` is set, as this Gemfile supports) is not updated. That boot mode will fail under frozen/deployment bundling, or silently re-resolve versions.

title: Negative-condition specs pass vacuously
body: "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" stub only one setting and leave `feed_polling_enabled?` at its default of false. `poll_feed` is therefore never called, whatever those conditions do. Each test should enable the other settings so it actually exercises the condition it names. Similarly, `embed_controller_spec`'s "is 404 without an embed_url" fails earlier at `ensure_embeddable` (no referer), not on the missing parameter, so it does not test what it claims.

title: `.small-action` button's `float: right` is ignored once the container is flex
body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex`, so its children are flex items and `float` has no effect on them. `button { float: right; }` therefore no longer pushes the button to the right edge. It now sits immediately after `.small-action-desc`, because the desc has no `flex: 1` and the button has no `margin-left: auto`. The same applies to `.topic-avatar { float: left }`, which is now a dead rule. The small-action edit/undo buttons used to be right-aligned, and this change moves them next to the text. Right-align the button explicitly, for example with `margin-left: auto` or a growing desc, and drop the dead float rules.

title: Custom message paragraphs lose all spacing
body: The `.custom-message p` margin changed from `5px 0` to `0`, and `.small-action-desc > p` also lost its `padding-top`. A custom message with several paragraphs now renders them with no gap between them. The surrounding vertical rhythm also shifts: the `margin-top: 5px` and the `0.5em` vertical padding on `.small-action-desc` were removed. This reads as a visual regression that is unrelated to the header work.

title: `align-items` mixin emits invalid legacy declarations for flex-start/flex-end
body: The mixin copies the same `$alignment` value into the legacy `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` properties. Those old syntaxes use `start` and `end` rather than `flex-start` and `flex-end`, so any future `@include align-items(flex-start)` produces invalid declarations for the older engines. `-ms-align-items` is not a real property at all, and line 120 has trailing whitespace. This works for the `center` and `baseline` values used in this PR, but the mixin is a trap for the next caller. Map the values for the legacy properties, or document that only `center` and `baseline` are supported.

title: Unrelated small-action restyle bundled under a header-performance PR with no description
body: The PR title claims to 'optimize header layout performance', and the description is just 'Test 5'. The diff also converts `.small-action` to flexbox and rewrites its paddings and margins, and changes the badge, topic and `.extra-info-wrapper` styles. None of this is explained, and no performance rationale is given. This makes review and bisecting harder, and the small-action change introduces the layout regressions noted above. It should be split out or at least described.

title: `float: right` on the button has no effect now that `.small-action` is a flex container
body: `.small-action` becomes a flex container, so its children are flex items and `float` is ignored on them. `.small-action button { float: right }` is still there, but the button is now laid out right after `.small-action-desc` instead of at the right edge. Within the same hunk, `.topic-avatar { float: left }` is also dead. The button needs `margin-left: auto` (or `.small-action-desc` needs `flex: 1`) to keep its old position. As written, the action button on small-action rows (for example the undo or delete button) shifts position.

title: `align-items` mixin applies one value to legacy properties that expect different keywords, and includes a non-existent property
body: The value is passed unchanged to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy properties accept `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so `@include align-items(flex-start)` would emit invalid declarations for old engines. `-ms-align-items` is not a real property and is dead output. The mixin emits `-webkit-box-align` but no `-moz-box-align`, although `flexbox()` and `order()` emit `-moz-box` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group`. Old Firefox would therefore get a `-moz-box` container with no vertical centering. The line at 120 also has trailing whitespace. Current callers only pass `center` and `baseline`, so this is latent, but the mixin is a shared foundation helper.

title: `order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` is a global rule that only works inside the header's flex container
body: `@include order(2)` is added to the global `.extra-info-wrapper` selector, while the flex container that makes it meaningful (`.d-header .contents`) and the `.panel` ordering (`order(3)`) live in header.scss. The header layout now depends on two files staying in sync. Any other place that renders `.extra-info-wrapper` outside that flex container, such as a mobile or desktop override, silently gets a no-op rule. The same change also drops the `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px }` offset and adds `line-height: 1.5`. Bullet-badge alignment in the topic title now depends on `align-items: center` and the new inline-flex bullet rather than an explicit margin, and nothing verifies it.

title: PR title and description do not match the change; no verification of the layout switch
body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance" and the description is just "Test 5". The change replaces floats with flexbox in the header and also rewrites `.small-action` layout, the topic title badge margins and the bullet badge display. None of this is a performance optimization and nothing in the PR shows a measurement. There is no explanation or visual check for the layout-affecting changes, such as removing `.title { float: left }` and `.panel { float: right }`. Reviewers cannot tell the intended scope, and the unrelated `.small-action` regression went unnoticed.

title: align-items mixin passes modern values to legacy box-align properties and emits a nonexistent property
body: The mixin writes `$alignment` unchanged into `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy properties use different keywords (`start`/`end` instead of `flex-start`/`flex-end`). `center` and `baseline`, the only values used today, happen to be valid in both. Any future call such as `align-items(flex-start)` will produce invalid legacy declarations, and old browsers will silently ignore them. `-ms-align-items` (line 121) does not exist in any IE/Edge implementation and is dead output. The mixin looks safe for all inputs when it is not.

title: Panel right-alignment now depends on `margin-left: auto`, which legacy flexbox fallbacks don't support
body: The panel used to be pushed right with `float: right`. That was replaced by `margin-left: auto` on a flex item. The new mixins emit legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` fallbacks. In those 2009-era flexbox implementations, auto margins do not absorb free space the way they do in the modern spec. A browser that takes the legacy path will therefore render the user/search panel directly after the title instead of at the right edge. Floats are also ignored on flex items, so there is no fallback. Either drop the legacy-prefix claim or add a legacy-compatible alignment such as `-webkit-box-flex: 1` on the spacer or title.

title: Custom-message paragraph spacing removed
body: `.small-action-desc .custom-message p` changed from `margin: 5px 0` to `margin: 0`. Custom messages are rendered as cooked HTML and can contain several paragraphs. They now run together with no vertical separation. The spacing was not needed to fix the flex centering, so this is an unrelated visual regression.

title: Float declarations inside the new flex container have no effect, so the button no longer right-aligns
body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex`, but `.topic-avatar { float: left }` and `button { float: right }` are left in place. Floats are ignored on flex items. If the button is a flex item of `.small-action`, the intended right alignment is lost and it sits right after the description text. `.small-action-desc` has no `flex: 1` or auto margin to absorb the free space. The stale float rules are misleading, and the button positioning should be reworked explicitly, for example with `margin-left: auto`.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing `?`, so the guard never runs
body: ActiveModel::Serializers only calls hooks named `include_<attr>?`. The method here is `include_website_name` without the `?`, so it is dead code. `website_name` is therefore always serialized, even when the website is blank (it comes out as `nil`). The intended condition `website.present?` is never applied. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

title: website_name bypasses the untrusted-attribute (TL0/anonymous) restriction
body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is hidden when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (a TL0 user seen by an anonymous viewer). The new `website_name` is derived from the same value but is not in that list and has no equivalent guard. It is serialized unconditionally, so it leaks the host and path of the website of a user whose website is meant to be hidden. The template shows `model.website_name` whenever it is present, so the old behaviour (nothing displayed when `website` is hidden) changes. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`, or make its include check respect `restrict_user_fields?`.

title: Profile website display no longer updates after the website is edited
body: The template used to compute `websiteName` client-side from `model.website`, so it was always current. It now reads the server-supplied `model.website_name`. `User.save` only copies `bio_excerpt` back from the response and never refreshes `website_name`. `preferences` is nested under the `user` route, so the user profile is not re-fetched when the user returns from editing. After changing the website, the profile header can show the old name, or nothing if there was no website before, until a full reload.

title: Path handling gives odd output for trailing slashes and ignores case
body: When the domains match, the result is `website_host + path`. For `http://example.com/` this yields `example.com/` with a stray trailing slash, and the user who typed the bare domain sees a different display. Host comparison is also case-sensitive: `URI` does not lowercase the host, so `http://Example.com/x` will not match `example.com`. Normalize with `downcase` and strip a lone `/`.

title: Spec leaves the sibling-subdomain branch, nil/invalid URL and untrusted cases uncovered
body: The new tests cover only the non-matching, exact-match and parent-domain cases. The middle branch (same-length hosts with a shared parent, e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) is untested. So are a website with no scheme or an unparsable URL (`website_name` is `nil`), a blank website, and the TL0-anonymous case. The existing `untrusted_attributes` list in the spec was not extended with `website_name`, which is why the leak described above goes unnoticed.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing `?`, so the guard never runs
body: ActiveModel::Serializers only honours `include_<attr>?` methods. `include_website_name` is never called, so the `website.present?` check is dead code. `website_name` is always emitted as a key, with a nil value when there is no website. The template's `{{#if model.website_name}}` hides the nil case, but the intended contract (omit the attribute when there is no website) is not enforced. Rename it to `include_website_name?`. Note that `website_name` is also not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, which matters more (see the next finding).

title: website_name leaks the website domain for restricted (TL0, anonymous) users
body: `website` is in `untrusted_attributes` and is hidden when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true. This is anti-spam behaviour for TL0 users seen by anonymous viewers. The new `website_name` is derived from the same website but is not in that list, and its own `include_` hook is misnamed. The serializer therefore still returns the host and path for restricted users, and the profile template renders it as visible text. That defeats the restriction. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`. The spec's `untrusted_attributes` list (spec line 11) also needs `website_name`, otherwise nothing guards against this regression.

title: Client-side website_name goes stale after the website is edited
body: The old `websiteName` was a computed property on `model.website`, so it updated immediately when the website changed. It is now a server-provided static attribute, `website_name`. `User.save()` sends `website` but on success only copies `bio_excerpt` from the response, so `website_name` is never refreshed. After a user edits their website in preferences and returns to the profile, the user route is not re-entered, so `findDetails` is not re-run. The profile then shows the old name next to the new `href`. If the website is cleared, the old name is still shown with an empty link. Update `website_name` from the save response, or keep deriving it on the client.

title: website_name implementation is fragile and has edge-case quirks
body: `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal. It works today only because literals are not frozen, and it will raise FrozenError under `# frozen_string_literal: true`. Use `".#{website_host}"` instead. `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed up to three times per call; parse it once. For `http://example.com/` the result is `example.com/` with a dangling slash, and query strings and fragments are silently dropped. The duplicated ternaries make the three branches hard to follow. Extract a local `path` and a boolean `same_site`.

title: Website-name specs miss the sibling-subdomain branch and edge cases
body: The three specs cover different domain, same domain, and website domain as parent of the instance domain. They do not cover the `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` sibling-subdomain branch. They also skip a website without a scheme or an unparseable URL (the `rescue nil` path), a blank website, a trailing-slash URL, and the untrusted/anonymous TL0 case where `website_name` should be hidden. Because of this, the missing `?` on `include_website_name` and the restricted-user leak go undetected.

title: website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, so it leaks the hidden website for TL0 users
body: `website` is in the `untrusted_attributes` list, so it is omitted for TL0 users when the viewer is anonymous (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`). The new `website_name` attribute is not in that list. It is still serialized, and it carries the host and sometimes the path of the very website that was meant to be hidden. The template now renders `model.website_name` instead of the old controller property derived from `model.website`. Before this change a hidden website produced no name at all, so this is a regression in the spam-protection behaviour. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and to the matching list in the spec.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so it is never called
body: ActiveModel::Serializers only consults `include_<attr>?` methods. The method is defined as `include_website_name` without the `?`, so it is dead code and the attribute is always emitted. When there is no website, `website_name` is serialized as `null` instead of being omitted. The guard also would not have covered the restricted-user case, because it checks `website.present?` and not `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. Rename it to `include_website_name?`, or drop it and use `untrusted_attributes` instead.

title: website_name is now a static server value and goes stale after the user edits their website
body: The old `websiteName` was a client computed property depending on `model.website`, so it updated as soon as the website changed. `website_name` is now a plain attribute that is only set by `findDetails`. `User.save` sends `website` but only copies `bio_excerpt` back from the response. After a user changes their website in preferences and returns to their profile, the same user model is reused. The profile then shows the old `website_name` until a full reload, while the link `href` already uses the new `website`. Refresh `website_name` from the save response, or keep deriving it client-side.

title: Fragile host-matching logic; `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal
body: `"" << website_host` appends to a string literal. This works only while string literals are not frozen; with `frozen_string_literal` or a newer Ruby it raises `FrozenError` and breaks serialization of every user with a website. Use `".#{website_host}"` instead. The same-label-count branch compares everything after the first label. That treats unrelated sites on a shared public suffix as siblings, for example `foo.co.uk` and `forum.co.uk`, and shows the full path. The code also parses the URI up to three times per call; parse it once into a local.

title: Missing tests for the sibling-subdomain branch, blank website, and untrusted users
body: The new tests cover only three of the branches in `website_name`: a different domain, an identical domain, and a parent domain. They do not test the `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` branch (same label count, shared parent), a blank or unparseable website, or the TL0-anonymous case. The `untrusted_attributes` list at line 11 omits `website_name`, so the information leak described above is not caught. Add cases for these paths.

title: Light-theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` silently changed from 30% to 70%
body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new first argument to `dark-light-choose` is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, paired with `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)`. The 70%/30% pair was copied from a neighbouring rule. Light themes now render these embedded-post author links much lighter than before, which reduces contrast and is an unrelated visual regression. The light value should stay at 30%, paired with `$secondary` at 70%.

title: `.group-member-info .name` changes light-theme lightness from 30% to 50%
body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. Both branches of the new `dark-light-choose` use 50%, copied from the `.title` rule below. The light theme therefore gets a lighter, lower-contrast name than before, and this mismatch with the stated intent (only add a dark-theme variant) was not caught. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` to preserve the original look.

title: Mobile `.group-member-info .name` light color altered from 30% to 50%
body: The original light-theme color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The change wraps it as `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which also lightens the light theme. This is a behavioural change outside the scope of the PR. The light value should stay 30%, with the dark counterpart at `$secondary` 70%.

title: `.custom-message-length` light-theme color changed from 70% to 30%
body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, a faint hint color. The new light value is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, with `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` for dark themes. The 30%/70% pair looks copied from another rule. The character-count hint in light themes now becomes much darker and more prominent, and no longer matches the desktop `modal.scss`, which uses 70%/30%. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

title: Mobile `.topic-map h3` light color changed from 20% to 50%
body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new code uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light theme heading becomes noticeably lighter, which reduces contrast, while the desktop equivalent correctly uses 20%/80%. The same file also uses 20%/80% for `.number, i` further down. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

title: Light-theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` changed from 30% to 70% lightness
body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The light-theme branch should keep 30% and the dark branch should use 70%. The PR instead copied the 70/30 pair from the neighbouring `.username.new-user a` rule. Embedded-post author links on light themes become much paler, which is a visible regression and contradicts the PR's purpose of changing only dark-theme behaviour.

title: `.group-member-info .name` light-theme color changed from 30% to 50%
body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light branch moved from 30% to 50%, so group member names lose contrast on light themes. The correct pair is `30%` / `$secondary 70%`. The `.title` rule below uses 50% and the `.name` rule appears to have been copy-pasted from it.

title: `.custom-message-length` light-theme lightness flipped from 70% to 30%
body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, a pale hint color. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light branch is now 30%, which makes the text much darker than before. The dark branch is also inverted. It should be `$primary 70%` / `$secondary 30%`, matching the desktop `.custom-message-length` rule. The values appear to be swapped, which changes the light theme.

title: `.topic-map h3` light-theme color changed from 20% to 50% lightness
body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The mobile topic-map headings become noticeably lighter on light themes. The correct pair is `$primary 20%` / `$secondary 80%`, as used for `.number, i` in the same block and for the desktop `.topic-map h3`.

title: Mobile `.group-member-info .name` light-theme color changed from 30% to 50%
body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This changes the light-theme appearance, which should not happen in a dark-theme fix. It should be `$primary 30%` / `$secondary 70%`. The same copy-paste error appears in `desktop/user.scss`.

title: Remaining `scale-color($primary, $lightness: ...)` not converted
body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. It is not wrapped in `dark-light-choose` like the other 50% greys in this file. On dark themes this text will still be a dim color derived from `$primary`, so the PR's stated goal is not fully met for this file. The same pattern remains in other places the PR did not touch, such as `mobile/compose.scss` `#file-uploading`, which uses `$secondary` unconditionally.

title: Light-theme value for embedded-post link color changed from 30% to 70%
body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The light-theme branch moved from 30% to 70%, so `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` is now much fainter on light themes. This PR is meant to leave light themes unchanged and only fix dark themes. It looks like the dark-theme pair (30%) was copied into the light slot. The correct pair is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`.

title: `.group-member-info .name` light color changed from 30% to 50%
body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule uses 50%/50%. That makes the name text lighter on light themes and drops the visual distinction between `.name` and `.title`, which now share the same color. The light-theme appearance changes unintentionally. The pair should be 30% for `$primary` and 70% for `$secondary`.

title: `.custom-message-length` light-theme color inverted from 70% to 30%
body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light branch now uses 30%, so the hint text is much darker on light themes. The pair is swapped relative to the desktop `.custom-message-length` rule in this same PR, which correctly uses 70%/30%. Mobile and desktop now diverge. It should be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)`.

title: Topic map `h3` color changed from 20% to 50%/50%, altering the light theme
body: The original `.topic-map h3` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value goes from 20% to 50%, so the heading is noticeably lighter and loses contrast against its `h4` sibling. The matching desktop rule in this PR correctly uses 20%/80%. This one should be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)`.

title: Mobile `.group-member-info .name` light color changed from 30% to 50%
body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule uses 50%/50%. This changes the light-theme appearance and makes `.name` identical to `.title`. It repeats the same mistake as in desktop/user.scss. The pair should be 30% for `$primary` and 70% for `$secondary`.

title: Missed conversion: categories badge-notification still uses a bare `scale-color($primary, ...)`
body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still has `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%);` with no `dark-light-choose`. On dark themes `$primary` is light, so scaling it 50% towards white gives poor contrast. That is exactly the bug this PR fixes elsewhere. The same file's other 50% usages were converted, so this one should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` too.

title: totalPages over-counts by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With 50 members and limit 50 it returns 2 although there is only one page. `showingLast` (`currentPage == totalPages`) stays false, so the 'next' arrow is enabled. Clicking it requests offset 50 and shows an empty page labelled 2/2. The same happens in the admin UI after removing the only member on the last page. `findMembers` clamps the offset using the stale `user_count`, so it requests an offset equal to the new total and lands on an empty page. This should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

title: limit/offset are taken from params without bounds or validation
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are used directly in the query. There is no upper cap, so `?limit=1000000` serializes every member of a large group in one request. A negative limit or offset is passed to SQL and raises a Postgres error, giving a 500. The limit should be clamped to a sane range (for example 1..N) and the offset to >= 0.

title: Public group members page now shows only the first 50 members with no pagination
body: `GroupsController#members` now applies limit/offset to every group and defaults to 50. Before, the default limit only applied to automatic groups and non-automatic groups returned all members. `group-members` route and `group/members.hbs` were changed to call `findMembers()` once and render `members`, but only the admin template got next/previous controls. For any group with more than 50 members, the public page silently truncates the list and offers no way to see the rest. The JSON response shape also changed from a bare array to `{members, meta}`, which breaks any other consumer of this endpoint.

title: findMembers returns undefined for nameless groups and no longer resolves to the member list
body: `findMembers` used to always return a promise (`Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` for an empty name) that resolved to the members. Now it returns `undefined` when the name is empty, and otherwise a promise resolving to `undefined` because it writes into the model. Any caller that chains `.then(...)` on the result will throw for nameless groups, and callers expecting the members from the promise get nothing.

title: `usernames` input state is never reset, so it leaks between groups and repeat clicks
body: `usernames` lives on the singleton controller and is neither cleared after `addMembers` (only a TODO) nor reset in the route's `setupController`. Names typed for group A and not submitted stay in the selector after navigating to group B, and clicking Add there adds them to B. Clicking Add twice also resubmits the same names. `addMembers` also has no failure handler, so a server error is swallowed silently.

title: remove_member spec uses PUT while the route is DELETE
body: The route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, but the 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member`. It only passes because Rails 4 controller specs do not enforce the HTTP verb, so the test does not exercise the real request.

title: No spec covers the changed GroupsController#members contract
body: `GroupsController#members` changed its response from a bare array to `{members, meta: {total, limit, offset}}`, and the default limit/offset behaviour changed. No spec was added or updated for this (groups_controller_spec is not in the change). Pagination, the meta values, and the new response shape are untested, and any existing spec asserting an array response would now fail.

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts whenever the member count divides evenly by the page size. With 50 members and limit 50, it reports 2 pages although there is only one. The 'next' arrow stays enabled, so clicking it sets offset=50 and fetches an empty page. Because `showingLast` compares `currentPage` with `totalPages`, the pager also shows '1/2' on the real last page. The same stale count shows up after `removeMember`: deleting the only member on the last page reloads using the old `user_count` and leaves an empty page. This should use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

title: Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination UI
body: `members` now defaults to `limit = 50` for every group, where before only automatic groups were limited, to 200. The public `group/members.hbs` template renders `members` but has no next/previous controls, and `group-members.js.es6` only calls `model.findMembers()` once with the default offset. Any group with more than 50 members now shows only the first 50 on its public page, and users cannot reach the rest. Pagination was added only to the admin UI.

title: GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed from an array to {members, meta} without updating specs
body: The endpoint used to return a JSON array of users. It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}`. Any other consumer of this endpoint, such as plugins, external API clients or existing specs for `GroupsController#members`, will break. The PR adds no spec for the new response format or for limit/offset behaviour. The only spec changes are for the admin controller, so the changed public contract has no test coverage.

title: limit and offset are not validated or capped
body: `limit` and `offset` come straight from `params` via `to_i`. A negative value makes Postgres raise "LIMIT must not be negative" or an equivalent offset error, which returns a 500. A very large `limit` lets any user who can see the group pull the entire member list in one request, so the pagination does not bound the cost. The values should be clamped, for example 1..N for limit and >=0 for offset.

title: add_members silently ignores unknown usernames and assumes a string param
body: Usernames that do not match a user are skipped and the action still returns `success_json`. The admin gets no signal that nothing was added, and the UI just reloads the unchanged list. Usernames are also not stripped, so `"a, b"` silently drops `b`. If `usernames` arrives as an array, `.split` raises NoMethodError and returns a 500. The client also never clears the selector (the code has a `TODO: should clear the input`), so the admin can click Add repeatedly with the same input.

title: Incremental PATCH membership API and usernames on create/update removed outright
body: `update_patch` (PATCH with `changes[add]`/`changes[delete]`) is deleted. `create` and `update` no longer accept `group[usernames]`, and the params are now top-level rather than nested under `group`. Any external script or plugin using the old admin endpoints breaks with no deprecation path. The old specs for these behaviours were deleted rather than ported.

title: remove_member spec uses the wrong HTTP verb and coverage is thin
body: The route is `delete "members"`, but the automatic-group test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member`. It passes only because controller specs do not enforce the verb, and it misrepresents the real request. The remove/add specs also never cover removing a non-member (where `group.users.delete(id)` raises RecordNotFound), adding unknown usernames, or non-admin access.

title: totalPages uses floor()+1, producing a phantom empty last page when user_count is a multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With 50 members and limit 50 it reports 2 pages. `next` (line 33) then moves to offset 50 (`min(offset+limit, user_count)`) and loads an empty page. `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to `totalPages`, so the UI shows "2/2" with no members listed. It should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`, and `next` should not advance past the last real offset. A related stale-state case: removing the only member on the last page re-fetches with the old offset (clamped to the stale `user_count`) and lands on an empty page.

title: limit/offset are taken from params without validation or an upper bound
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to the query. A negative limit or offset makes PostgreSQL raise and returns a 500. `limit=0` returns nothing, and the admin UI then computes `user_count / 0` (Infinity). A very large limit lets any caller who can see the group pull the whole member list in one request, so the pagination does not bound anything. Clamp limit to a sane range (e.g. 1..max) and offset to >= 0.

title: Response shape of /groups/:name/members changed from array to {members, meta} and default is now capped at 50, with no spec coverage
body: `members` used to return a bare array (all members for non-automatic groups, 200 for automatic ones). It now returns `{members:, meta:}` and defaults to 50 rows. Any other client, plugin or existing spec that parses the array breaks, and nothing in the PR adds or updates a spec for the new payload, the `meta` values, or limit/offset behaviour (groups_controller_spec is untouched).

title: Public group members page now shows only the first 50 members with no way to page
body: The public members route calls `model.findMembers()` and renders `members`. The server now caps results at the default limit of 50, and this template and its route have no next/previous controls. Non-automatic groups used to return every member, so any group with more than 50 members now silently shows a truncated list to users with no way to see the rest. Pagination was only added to the admin UI. The `{{#if model}}` guard is also always truthy now that the model is the group itself.

title: remove_member uses group.users.delete(id) instead of Group#remove, bypassing callbacks and failing for non-members
body: The old incremental-delete code called `group.remove(user)`. The new code calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` with a raw integer. On a has_many :through association this deletes the join rows without running GroupUser destroy callbacks, so any cleanup tied to the join model (e.g. primary group or title) is skipped. When given an id, Rails also does a `find` on the association, so a user who is not in the group (stale UI, double click) raises RecordNotFound and returns an error instead of succeeding silently, as the old PATCH delete did.

title: Admin group API contract changed silently: params no longer nested under `group`, usernames and PATCH changes dropped
body: `create` and `update` now read flat `params[:name]` / `params[:visible]` instead of `params[:group][...]`. `usernames` and the PATCH `changes[add/delete]` incremental API are gone, replaced by new `/members` endpoints. External scripts or plugins using the old shape get no error. `update` sends `visible` as absent, so it resets visibility to false, and name changes are ignored. `create` sees an empty name and fails validation. This is a breaking API change that is not documented in the PR description ("Test 8").

title: usernames input is never cleared or reset, so it leaks across groups and repeats on re-add
body: `usernames` is a property on the singleton admin-group controller. It is not cleared after `addMembers` (acknowledged by the TODO) and not reset when the route sets up a different group. Usernames typed or left over for group A are still in the selector when the admin opens group B, and pressing Add adds them to B. `addMembers` and `removeMember` also have no failure handler, so a rejected request gives the admin no feedback.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded in ApplicationController#set_locale, so other paths get missing translations
body: `translate` loads only `config.locale`. The fallback locales (site default and `:en`) are loaded only by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, which is called solely from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any other code that switches locale (jobs, mailers using `I18n.with_locale`, rake tasks, MessageBus or other non-controller paths) can hit a key missing in the user's locale while the fallback locale is not yet loaded. The fallback lookup then finds nothing and returns 'translation missing: ...'. That string is stored in the LRU cache under key+locale, so the wrong text is served until the next `reload!`. Loading the fallback chain should happen inside `translate`/`load_locale`, not only in one controller filter.

title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain, which now depends on SiteSetting.default_locale
body: The cache key is `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`. With the new `FallbackLocaleList`, the result for a key missing in the current locale depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`. If an admin changes the default locale, cached values for a user locale with a missing key keep returning the old fallback (or a cached 'translation missing'). Nothing in this diff clears the cache or reloads when that setting changes. The key should include the fallback chain, or the cache should be invalidated on change.

title: No tests for the new fallback behavior
body: The PR replaces Rails' `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` with a custom fallback list and adds on-demand loading of fallback locales, but adds no specs. Untested cases include the order user locale → site default → en, lazy loading via `ensure_loaded!`, and the LRU cache interaction. Fallbacks were previously enabled only in production-like environments and are now active in dev and test as well. That changes test behavior, because missing translations are now silently masked. Specs should cover a key present only in `en` being resolved for a non-English user.

title: Fallback locales are only preloaded in the controller before_filter
body: Translations are loaded on demand. `translate` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)`, so the fallback locales (site default and :en) are loaded only by this `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` call in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any code path that does not go through this filter has no fallback data loaded. That includes Sidekiq jobs, mailers, `I18n.with_locale` blocks and rake tasks. If a key is missing in the user's locale, the fallback chain [locale, default, :en] finds nothing because :en may not be loaded in that process. The result is a 'translation missing: ...' string, not the English text. A fresh worker process hits this on its first email in a non-English locale. The loading belongs in the accelerator, for example `translate`/`load_locale` loading the whole fallback chain, not in one controller filter.

title: Translation LRU cache key ignores the fallback chain and caches missing-translation results
body: The cache key is `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`. With this PR the result also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (the custom fallback chain) and on which fallback locales are already loaded. Two consequences follow. (1) If an admin changes the default locale, entries cached for other locales still hold text from the old fallback until they are evicted or the process restarts. (2) If a lookup runs before the fallback locales are loaded, the frozen 'translation missing' string is stored under that key. It is then served on every later call, even after :en has been loaded. The key should include the fallback chain, or the cache should be cleared when the default locale changes. Missing-translation results should not be cached.

title: No tests for the new fallback behavior
body: The PR adds a custom `FallbackLocaleList`, `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, and a hook in `set_locale`. It also removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from the production configs, which makes fallbacks active in every environment, including test and development. No spec covers any of this. Missing coverage includes: a key missing in the user locale falling back to the site default and then English, ordering and de-duplication of the chain, loading of fallback locales on demand, and interaction with the translation cache. Regressions in this globally applied behavior would go unnoticed.

title: Every fallback lookup reads SiteSetting and allocates a new array
body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` is called by the I18n Fallbacks backend on every `translate_no_cache` call. Each call evaluates `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` and builds and de-duplicates a new array. This sits on the hot translation path that the accelerator exists to speed up. Because `[]` is overridden to always compute, nothing is memoized. It also makes translation depend on `SiteSetting` being available, which can fail early in boot or in rake tasks before the DB is ready. A `locale` passed as a String is not de-duplicated against the Symbols in the list.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded by the controller filter, not by translate itself
body: `I18n.translate` still lazy-loads only `config.locale`. The new fallback chain is `[locale, site default, :en]`, and `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is called only from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any code outside a web request does not go through that filter. This includes Sidekiq jobs, mailers using `I18n.with_locale`, rake tasks and the console. In those contexts a key missing from the current locale falls back to locales that were never loaded, unless some earlier request in the same process happened to load them. For example, when the site default is `fr`, English is never loaded in a job process. The result is a "translation missing: ..." string instead of the English fallback. The loading should happen inside `translate`/`load_locale` for every locale in the chain, not in one controller filter.

title: LRU cache key ignores the fallback chain, so cached results go stale
body: The cache key is `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`. The result now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which `FallbackLocaleList` puts in the chain. If a key is missing in the current locale, the value served from the site default locale (or the 'translation missing' string) is cached under the current locale only. After an admin changes `default_locale`, or after a fallback locale is loaded later, the process keeps returning the old cached fallback until the cache is evicted or `reload!` runs. The key should include the fallback chain or the default locale, or the cache should be cleared when `default_locale` changes.

title: Fallbacks now enabled in every environment with no tests
body: The PR removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from the production, profile and cloud66 configs. It installs a custom `FallbackLocaleList` unconditionally, so dev and test now have fallbacks too, where they previously did not. No spec covers the new behavior: chain ordering (user, site default, en), lazy loading of the fallback locales, or the 'translation missing' case. Specs that relied on missing-translation behavior in a non-English locale may also silently change. A spec for `FallbackLocaleList#[]`, `ensure_loaded!` and an end-to-end lookup of a key present only in `en` should be added.

title: Fallback lookup reads SiteSetting and allocates an array on every translate call
body: `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on every lookup, not only when a key is missing. Each call now evaluates `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` and builds a new array through `uniq` and `compact`. Calls with arguments bypass the LRU cache in `translate_accelerator`, so they pay this cost every time. It also ties every translation to SiteSetting being readable. If `default_locale` were nil or unavailable, `nil.to_sym` would raise from inside I18n. The chain could be memoized per `(locale, default_locale)` instead.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type, so renderer and anonymous share denials
body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` is built from `checkReq.UserUID` (the raw subject ID), not the identity type. `anonymous:0` and `render:0` both yield UserUID `0` (the tests use exactly these subjects). If an anonymous check on dashboard X is denied, the key `<ns>.perm_0_dashboards:read_X_<folder>` is stored. A `render:0` check on the same dashboard within 30s then hits that entry in `Check` and is denied. The renderer holds a wildcard read grant, so image rendering can fail spuriously. Include the identity type in the key.

title: Underscore-joined denial key is ambiguous and can deny the wrong resource
body: The key joins userUID, action, name and parent with `_`, and these values can contain underscores. `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` both produce `..._a_b_c`. A cached denial for one resource then wrongly denies the other for up to 30s. The key also starts with the same `perm_<uid>_<action>` prefix as `userPermCacheKey`, which makes cross-key clashes possible if values contain underscores. Use an unambiguous separator or encoding, or a distinct prefix such as `perm_denied_`.

title: Every non-allowed check not already in the denial cache hits the permission DB
body: Cached permissions that do not allow the request now fall through to `getIdentityPermissions`. `getUserPermissions` no longer consults `permCache`, so it always runs the permission query, and the denial cache is keyed per (name, folder). A user or client probing many distinct resources the user cannot access triggers one full permission query per resource. Singleflight only dedups concurrent calls for the same user and action. The first denied check for each resource therefore costs a DB round trip, which amplifies load. Consider rate-limiting the refetch, for example a short per-user/action refresh cooldown, instead of re-querying on every miss.

title: Requery path still uses a stale cached folder tree, then caches the resulting denial
body: After a cache miss, permissions are re-fetched from the DB, but `checkPermission` → `checkInheritedPermissions` → `buildFolderTree` still reads the folder tree from `folderCache` (30s TTL). Suppose a user with inherited access via parent folder P creates subfolder C and a dashboard in C. If the cached tree predates C, `tree.Ancestors(C)` is empty, so the check returns denied. This PR then writes a 30s denial entry for it. The newly created nested folder or dashboard stays inaccessible for up to 30s, which is the scenario the PR is meant to fix. The folder tree should be refreshed on the requery path, or denials caused by a possibly stale tree should not be cached.

title: Denial entries are never invalidated and can mask a permission granted shortly after
body: A denial is cached for 30s with no invalidation. It is checked before the cached permissions and before the DB requery. If a check for a resource runs before its permission rows exist, or before a grant takes effect, the user is denied for the full TTL even though the DB now allows it. For example, a check may run between resource creation and permission assignment. That is the same "cannot fetch what I just created" symptom the PR targets. Consider a much shorter TTL for denials, or invalidation on resource creation or permission change.

title: Tests do not cover writing the denial entry, and a dead cacheHit branch remains
body: `TestService_CacheCheck` only checks that a pre-seeded denial entry is honored. No test verifies that a real denied `Check` writes `permDenialCache`, that a repeated denied check skips the DB (via `store.calls`), or that anonymous and renderer identities are handled. List fallback to the DB on a cache miss is untested. Separately, removing the "cached" case from `TestService_getUserPermissions` leaves the `cacheHit` field and its assertions as dead code, because no case sets `cacheHit: true`.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type, so denials leak between anonymous and render subjects
body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` is built from namespace, `checkReq.UserUID`, action, name and parent. The identity type is not part of the key. `Check` reads the denial cache before it looks at `IdentityType`. `anonymous:0` and `render:0` both have UID `0`, so they share a key. The existing permission cache avoids this by using a separate `anonymousPermCacheKey`. If anonymous is denied `dashboards:read` on dash1, a later `render:0` check for the same dashboard hits that entry and is wrongly denied, even though the renderer is granted read on everything. The reverse also happens: a render denial for a write action can deny an anonymous Editor. Include the identity type in the key, or use a separate prefix per type.

title: Denial cache key is ambiguous because fields are joined with '_' and names can contain '_'
body: The key is `ns.perm_<uid>_<action>_<name>_<parent>`, and Grafana dashboard and folder UIDs may contain underscores. `name="a_b", parent="c"` and `name="a", parent="b_c"` produce the same key, so a denial for one resource denies the other for the whole TTL. The key also shares the `.perm_<uid>_<action>` prefix with `userPermCacheKey`, so the two caches are only kept apart by their value types. Use a distinct prefix such as `perm_denial_` and a separator that cannot occur in the fields, or hash the parts.

title: Every distinct denied resource now triggers a full DB permission re-query
body: In `Check`, when the cached scope map does not allow the request, the code always falls through to `getIdentityPermissions`. That runs `GetUserBasicRole`, `ListUserTeams` and `GetUserPermissions` against the DB, and `getUserPermissions` no longer short-circuits on the cache. The denial cache is keyed per (user, action, name, parent), so it only helps for repeats of the exact same resource. A user who is legitimately denied on many different dashboards or folders, for example a UI list of items or a scan, causes one DB permission query per distinct resource within each 30s window. Singleflight only merges concurrent calls. This removes most of the protection the permission cache gave and can amplify load on the DB. Consider rate-limiting the refresh per user/action, or negative-caching at the (user, action) level for a short time after a refresh.

title: Denials computed from a possibly stale folder tree are cached with no invalidation
body: After the DB re-query, `checkPermission` calls `checkInheritedPermissions`, which uses `buildFolderTree`. That tree is itself cached for 30s and is not refreshed by the permission re-query. For a newly created nested folder whose permission comes only from an ancestor, the stale tree does not contain the folder, so the check is denied. That result is then stored in the denial cache for another 30s, with no way to clear it when the folder tree or the user's permissions change. Access to newly created resources can stay denied for up to a minute even though the re-query was meant to fix exactly this case.

title: Denial-cache test passes even if the denial cache is ignored
body: The test comment says it allows access in `permCache` 'to prove this is not checked', but the cached map is `{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`, which also denies. Without the denial-cache lookup, `Check` would see a cached deny, fall back to the default `fakeStore` (no permissions), and still return `Allowed=false`. The test therefore cannot tell whether the denial short-circuit works. It should seed an allowing permission (`true`, or a store that grants access) and assert the store is not called. There is also no test that a DB-confirmed deny populates `permDenialCache`, and none that a later identical check skips the DB.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type, so anonymous and renderer share denials
body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` is built from `checkReq.UserUID`, the ID part of the subject, and does not include the identity type. `anonymous:0` and `render:0` both yield UserUID `0`, so they get the same denial key for the same namespace, action, name and folder. The denial lookup in `Check` runs before any identity-specific logic. If an anonymous check on `dashboards:read` for `dash1` is denied, the denial is cached for 30s. A renderer check for the same dashboard is then denied from the cache, although the renderer is granted read on all dashboards and folders. The result is renders that fail intermittently for up to the TTL. The key should include the identity type, or the resolved internal UID, as the permission cache keys do.

title: Underscore-joined denial key is ambiguous for names and folders that contain underscores
body: The key is `ns.perm_<user>_<action>_<name>_<parent>`, joined with `_`. Dashboard and folder UIDs commonly contain underscores, so different (name, folder) pairs can map to the same key. For example, name `a_b` with folder `c` and name `a` with folder `b_c` both produce `..._a_b_c`. A denial for one resource then wrongly denies the other for the TTL. The key also shares the `perm_<user>_<action>` prefix with the permission-map key, which holds a different value type. Use an unambiguous separator or a distinct prefix such as `perm_denied_`, and consider hashing or escaping the components.

title: Every first-time denial for a distinct resource triggers a DB permission re-query
body: When cached permissions do not allow the request, `Check` always falls through to `getIdentityPermissions`, which queries the DB. The only mitigation is the denial cache, which is keyed per (user, action, name, folder). A user without access to many resources, such as a UI or search path that checks many dashboards individually, therefore causes one permission query per distinct denied resource until each has its own denial entry. Singleflight only deduplicates concurrent calls. This weakens the cache and can amplify load on the SQL permission store, including for unauthorized or probing callers who vary the resource name. Consider rate-limiting the re-query, for example a per-user/action 'recently refreshed' marker, so that a fresh DB fetch is not repeated within a short window.

title: Cached denials are not invalidated when permissions are refreshed
body: A denial entry is written for 30s and consulted before the permission cache. If a user's permissions are refreshed from the DB between the denial and a later check, for example by a check or List on another resource, the permission cache can already grant the resource. The denial entry still takes precedence, so access stays denied until the denial TTL expires. The same applies if a permission is granted after an earlier check on a not-yet-existing resource. This partly defeats the goal of letting a creator access a just-created dashboard or folder. When `getUserPermissions` repopulates the permission cache, the denial entry for the checked resource should be dropped, or the allowed result should be authoritative.

title: Denial-cache test is vacuous: it would pass without the denial short-circuit
body: The test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' comments that it allows access to prove the permission cache is not consulted. It sets the permCache value to `false` (`{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`), which does not grant anything. Without the denial-cache logic, `checkPermission` would see no grant and fall through to the empty fake store, so the result is still `Allowed=false`. The test therefore passes whether or not the denial cache works. It should set the scope to `true` and/or use a store that would grant access, so that only the denial entry can produce the deny.

title: No test that a DB-derived denial is written to the denial cache; removed cache-hit case leaves dead test fields
body: The new tests cover reading a pre-seeded denial entry. None checks that `Check` writes a denial entry after a DB-confirmed deny, which is the behaviour that protects the DB from repeated queries. None checks that an allowed result does not write one. Nothing covers the anonymous or renderer paths through the new cache-then-DB flow, or the case where the identity lookup fails. The 'permissions from cache' case was also deleted from `TestService_getUserPermissions`, so the `cacheHit` field is now always false there and effectively dead code.

title: Missing `key` on GrafanaRuleListItem in the filtered rules list
body: The previous `GrafanaRuleLoader` element had `key={key}`. The new `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` returned from `rules.map` has no key. The other `datasource` and `default` branches still pass `key`. React will warn about missing keys. Reconciliation falls back to index, so as filtered results stream in or get reordered, rows can reuse the wrong component state. That includes each row's delete modal, silence drawer and clone-redirect state, because `RuleActionsButtons` holds `useState`. Pass `key={key}` as before.

title: Delete and Pause menu items can never render in the list view (no rulerRule)
body: The list view now passes only `promRule`, and `rulerRule` is undefined. `canDelete`/`canPause` are computed from the prom-rule abilities, but the items are still gated on a ruler rule. Delete is wrapped in `canDelete && rulerRule`, and Pause requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`. So in the Grafana alert list, Delete and Pause are silently dropped even for users with permission. `showDivider` still counts `canPause`, so a stray divider can appear. The new `GrafanaGroupLoader` test also encodes this: delete permission is granted, yet it asserts exactly 4 menu items with no Delete. The Delete handler and `MenuItemPauseRule` need to work from the prom rule or a rule identifier, not `RulerRuleDTO`.

title: Silence menu item is shown but the drawer never opens in the list view
body: `AlertRuleMenu` shows 'Silence notifications' from the prom-rule ability and calls `handleSilence`, which sets `showSilenceDrawer` to true. The drawer is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`. In the list view `rule` (the ruler rule) is undefined, so the condition is always false. Clicking Silence does nothing, which is a dead menu entry. The drawer needs to be driven by the prom rule, or the item hidden when no ruler rule is available.

title: Export/Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently disabled for Grafana recording rules in the new prom hook
body: The ruler-based hook gates ModifyExport, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently on `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule`, which is true for both alerting and recording Grafana rules. The new `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` gates them on `isAlertingRule` (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule`). The in-code comment says 'All GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed by definition', which contradicts this. Result: recording rules lose Export and Pause in the list view, which they previously had. Only Silence should be restricted to alerting rules. The new tests use only alerting rules, so this is not covered.

title: Federated rule group check dropped for the deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities path
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` used to compute `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, which made federated (Mimir `source_tenants`) groups immutable. It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `isFederated = false` with a TODO. Every existing caller (e.g. `RulesTable`, `RuleDetails`) therefore now offers Edit, Delete and Pause on federated rule groups. This is a silent behaviour regression unrelated to the stated goal of removing the ruler from the list view. Pass the federated flag through, or keep the old check in the deprecated wrapper.

title: returnTo parameter dropped from rule view link
body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader`/`GrafanaRuleListItem` built the href with `createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo: createReturnTo() })`. The new component links to `/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view` with no `returnTo`. The rule view page can therefore no longer send the user back to the filtered list or position they came from. Nothing in the PR says this was intended, and the updated tests only check `stringContaining('/alerting/grafana/<uid>/view')`, so they would not catch it.

title: Stale comment and variable name referring to ruler preload
body: The ruler prefetch dispatch was removed, but the comment ('This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules...') and the variable `cacheAndRulerPreload` still describe ruler preloading. This misleads readers into thinking ruler data is still loaded here. Rename and update the comment.

title: GrafanaGroupLoader docs still say it loads from the Ruler endpoint
body: The component doc ('Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints') and the `expectedRulesCount` comment ('Ruler response might contain different number of rules') are now wrong. The ruler query was removed and the component only uses the Prometheus endpoint.

title: Tests lose coverage of removed behaviours and lock in the missing Delete/Pause actions
body: The tests for creating/deleting operation states and for `matchRules` were removed. The one remaining menu test grants delete and update permissions but asserts exactly four items (silence, copy link, duplicate, export), so it passes even though Delete and Pause are missing. There is no test that clicking Silence opens the drawer, or that Delete or Pause work from the list view. The RulesTable negative tests pass trivially because the default mocks return `[false, false]` for every ability.

title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered in a .map() without a `key`
body: The old `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../>` had a key. The replacement `<GrafanaRuleListItem .../>` in the `'grafana'` case does not. `key` is still destructured and passed in the `datasource` and default branches, so the omission looks accidental. React will warn about missing keys, and reconciliation is unstable when results are appended or filtered. The component holds state (delete modal, silence drawer, clone redirect), so that state can attach to the wrong row. Add `key={key}`.

title: Pause and Delete menu items can never render in the ruler-less list view
body: `canPause` and `canDelete` now include the Grafana Prom-rule ability. The items are still gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (Pause, line 123) and `canDelete && rulerRule` (Delete, line 165). The new list view (`GrafanaRuleListItem` → `RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule}`) passes no `rulerRule`, so these conditions are always false. Users cannot pause or delete Grafana rules from the list view, even though the permission checks pass. The new `GrafanaGroupLoader` test grants delete and update permissions and expects exactly 4 menu items (silence, copy link, duplicate, export), so it locks this regression in. Either make these actions work from the Prom rule, or do not compute and OR in abilities that can never be rendered.

title: 'Silence notifications' menu item does nothing in the list view
body: In the list view only `promRule` is supplied. The Silence menu item is shown based on the Prom-rule ability (`canSilence`), and clicking it calls `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`. The drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`, and `rule` is undefined here. The click therefore silently does nothing. `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` still requires a `rulerRule`. The test only asserts that the item is present, never that clicking it opens the drawer.

title: Prom-rule abilities treat Grafana recording rules differently from the ruler path
body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` derives Pause, Restore, DeletePermanently and ModifyExport from `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`. The ruler equivalent uses `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which includes recording rules. The inline comment even says 'All GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed by definition', which is the semantics of `grafana.rule`. With the new code, Grafana recording rules lose Export (and Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently) wherever the Prom-based abilities are used. Only Silence should be restricted to alerting rules. The new function also has no unit tests covering recording rules.

title: Federated-rule-group check dropped for the legacy CombinedRule abilities
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` used to compute `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`. It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hard-codes `isFederated = false`. The `isFederatedRuleGroup` import was removed. Rules in Mimir federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable. Edit, Delete and Pause (where applicable) can be offered in the legacy list and table views, which are used by `RulesTable`, `RuleActionsButtons` and others. This is a behavior regression outside the new list view, and a TODO is not a substitute for keeping the existing check.

title: returnTo parameter dropped from the rule view link
body: The removed `GrafanaRuleListItem` built the href with `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo: createReturnTo() })`. The new one omits `returnTo`. The rule view page can no longer send the user back to the list with their filter and pagination state. The PR is about removing ruler requests and does not mention this behavior change.
