title: Integration test disabled for postgres instead of fixing it
body: The test is skipped for postgres with 'not working with postgres in Drone'. It is the integration test that starts the storage-server module, which is exactly the path this PR changes by running `Init` (lifecycle, DB init, search index) eagerly in `NewResourceServer`. Skipping it for a whole database backend hides a possible regression from the eager-init change, and nothing tracks it beyond a TODO. The PR also adds no test of its own for eager initialization (init failure propagating from `NewResourceServer`, or no first-request init).

title: NewResourceServer does not clean up when eager Init fails
body: If `s.Init(ctx)` fails, `NewResourceServer` returns `nil, err` without calling `s.cancel()` or `lifecycle.Stop`. The cancelable context, and anything already started in `Init`, stays alive: the SQL backend and its DB handle from `lifecycle.Init`, and any goroutines started by `search.init` or the watcher. Init can partially succeed, for example when the search init starts its event goroutine and the watcher then fails. The caller has no handle to stop it. Cancel the context (and stop the lifecycle) on the error path.

title: Stop() no longer gates requests because the per-RPC Init checks were removed
body: `Stop` sets `s.initErr` to 'service is stopping/stopped'. That error used to reach clients because every RPC called `s.Init(ctx)` and returned `initErr` from the `sync.Once`. With all those calls removed, nothing reads `initErr` after construction. Requests arriving after `Stop` now run against a stopped backend and a cancelled watcher context instead of getting a clear 'service is stopped' error. Either keep a cheap stopped/initErr check in the handlers or drop the dead state.

title: Trace-context propagation fix is incomplete
body: The PR is described as fixing trace propagation by passing span contexts down, but only `GetResourceStats` (plus search `init`/`build`) was changed. `WriteEvent` (`_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)`), `ReadResource` and `ListIterator` here, and `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` in bleve.go, still discard the context returned by `Start`. Child spans created afterwards (`create`, `update`, `listLatest`, and so on) are therefore parented to the caller's span rather than to these spans, which leaves broken trace hierarchies.

title: UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() but only the one-argument overload exists
body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition added to `UsernamePasswordForm` is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. There is no no-arg overload in this class or its parent `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`, so `UsernameForm` does not compile and the `services` module build fails. Either add a no-arg overload, or pass `context.getUser()` here. The no-arg form is probably what was intended, since this branch is only entered when the user is non-null.

title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, which disables passkeys on the initial login page
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. Before this change, `authenticate()` and `challenge(context, error, field)` set up passkeys when the user was not yet identified (`context.getUser() == null`). With the new guard, the normal first-visit login, where no user is in the context, never calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm`. The conditional-UI attribute, challenge and rpId are not set, so passkey login is lost for the standard flow. The patch's own tests expect passkeys on the first page: the "username webauthn" autocomplete, `form#webauth`, and auto-login with a discoverable key. They would fail. The `user != null` condition should be dropped so passkeys are enabled whenever the realm has them enabled, for both fresh login and re-authentication.

title: Passkey setup in authenticate() is skipped for a new login because of the user != null check
body: The passkey setup was moved out of the `else` (user == null) branch so it also covers re-authentication. It is now gated by `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which requires a non-null user. The effect is inverted. Re-authentication gets passkeys, but the first-time login, where `context.getUser()` is null, no longer does. The same inverted check is in the `challenge(context, error, field)` override (line 137). Error re-renders such as a bad username or a failed passkey on the first login page therefore also lose the conditional UI.

title: shouldDisplayAuthenticators is not overridden alongside shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators
body: `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` now returns false for conditional-UI login. `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldDisplayAuthenticators` is not overridden and still returns `context.getUser() != null`. During re-authentication (user set) the form therefore gets `SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS=true` and `IS_USER_IDENTIFIED=false`, but no `ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS` attribute. A template that renders the authenticator list under that flag may fail or render an empty list. The method is also missing `@Override`, so a signature mismatch would not be caught by the compiler.

title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey comment does not match what is tested, and missing-element checks are weak
body: The comment says the user has no passkey and passkeys should be hidden, but the test disables passkeys at the realm level (`setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(FALSE)`). It does not cover the case the name implies: passkeys enabled on the realm, user without a registered passkey. In that case `fillContextForm` still runs with a non-null user. The absence checks use `findElement(...)` inside `try/catch (Exception)`, which only passes because `findElement` throws. The `assertThat(..., nullValue())` can never pass if the element exists, so it is misleading. Use `findElements(...).isEmpty()` or `assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)`.

title: UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, which no longer exists
body: `UsernamePasswordForm` now declares only `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. No such overload exists in `UsernameForm` or `UsernamePasswordForm`, so the `services` module fails to compile. Pass `context.getUser()`, or restore a no-arg method, and make sure the semantics are what you intend for the username-only form.

title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, so passkeys are disabled for normal (non-re-auth) login
body: The helper returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. It guards both `authenticate()` (line 115) and the error `challenge(...)` (line 137). The old code filled the WebAuthn data when `context.getUser() == null`, which is the ordinary login case. The new code fills it only when a user is already set, which is the re-authentication case. For a fresh login, and for the error page after an unknown username, no challenge, RP id or conditional-UI attribute is rendered. Discoverable-key and 'username webauthn' autocomplete login stops working, and the existing tests (`webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey`, `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`, `passwordLoginWithExternalKey`) would fail. The `user != null` condition should be dropped, or the helper should cover both cases.

title: Error challenge no longer keeps passkeys after a failed username lookup
body: `challenge(context, error, field)` used to fill the WebAuthn form data when `context.getUser() == null`. For example, after a failed username lookup, `testInvalidUser` clears the user and the form is re-rendered. It now fills the data only when a user is set, so the error page for an invalid username or password loses the passkey/conditional-UI setup. `PasskeysUsernameFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` still expects 'username webauthn' autocomplete after an invalid-user error, and that assertion would fail.

title: shouldDisplayAuthenticators still keyed on user != null while authenticators are never provided
body: `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` is overridden to return false, so `ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS` is never set for conditional UI. `shouldDisplayAuthenticators` in the base class still returns `context.getUser() != null`. During re-authentication, when a user is set, the form therefore gets `SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS=true` with no authenticator list. This is inconsistent and relies on the template tolerating the missing attribute. Override `shouldDisplayAuthenticators` consistently. The new override also lacks `@Override`, so a signature drift in the parent would go unnoticed.

title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey does not test a user without a passkey
body: The comment and method name say the test covers a user who has no passkey, but the test only disables passkeys at the realm level with `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(FALSE)`. It therefore never exercises the scenario where passkeys are enabled for the realm and the re-authenticating user has no registered passkey. In that case the conditional UI would still be offered, which is the interesting behaviour of this change. The test name and comment are misleading, and the intended case is untested.

title: UsernameForm re-authentication shows a form with no usable input for users without passkeys
body: When passkeys are enabled in the realm, the username-only form no longer skips itself during re-authentication, whether or not the current user has any passkey. `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate` sets `USERNAME_HIDDEN` for the re-authenticating user. A user with no registered passkey is then shown a username page with no visible username field and no passkey to use, and must click through it before reaching the password step. The decision should depend on whether the user actually has a passkey credential, not just on the realm flag.

title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not compile
body: `UsernamePasswordForm` only defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, and no such overload exists in the class or its parents. The `services` module will not compile. The call should pass the user, e.g. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, so passkeys are never set up on the initial login
body: The new helper returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. It is used in `authenticate()` and in `challenge(context, error, field)`. On a normal first login `context.getUser()` is null, so the helper returns false and `fillContextForm` is never called. The old code did call it when the user was null. The login page then has no conditional-UI/passkey form, and the "username webauthn" autocomplete and `//form[@id='webauth']` checks in the existing tests fail. The same happens on the error path after an invalid username, because the user is still null there. The condition should be `user == null || <user has a passkey credential>`. As written, passkeys only work when a user is already set, which is the opposite of the intended behaviour.

title: Passkey UI is enabled for any pre-set user without checking whether the user has a passkey credential
body: For the re-authentication case the helper only checks that realm passkeys are enabled and that a user is present. It never checks that the user has a passwordless/WebAuthn credential. A user with no passkey is therefore shown the conditional-UI passkey form during re-authentication. In `UsernameForm.authenticate`, the shortcut that skips the form for users without linked brokers is disabled for every re-authenticating user once passkeys are enabled in the realm, whether or not they own a passkey. The fix is to enable passkeys only when the user is null or has a passkey credential configured.

title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys for the realm, so it does not cover its stated scenario
body: The test is meant to show that a user without a passkey does not see passkeys during re-authentication. It sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` for the whole realm, so nothing passkey-related would be shown for anyone. The real case, passkeys enabled in the realm but the user has no passkey credential, is untested. That case is the one the missing credential check in `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` would break. The try/`fail()`/`catch (Exception)` pattern also hides the intent. Use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` or check for absence directly.

title: Override of shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators is missing @Override
body: `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` overrides the new protected method in `WebAuthnAuthenticator` but has no `@Override` annotation. A later signature change in the parent would silently turn it into an unrelated method, and conditional-UI would again show or require the allowed authenticators list.

title: Invalidation-on-update decision uses the org-aware wrapped model as the 'original'
body: `update()` takes `idpById = getById(...)`, which returns the anonymous org-aware wrapper. Its `isEnabled()` also depends on whether the organization and the organization feature are enabled. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` evaluates `getLoginPredicate()` on this wrapper, so `test(original)` can be false even though the IDP is stored as enabled and is present in the cached login list (the cache is filled from the DB, where only the IDP's own `enabled` counts). Example: the org is disabled, the IDP is stored enabled, and an admin sets it to disabled. Both `test(original)` and `test(updated)` are false, so the early return skips invalidation. The cached login list still holds the now-disabled IDP, and callers other than the login bean (which re-checks `isEnabled`) see a stale entry. Evaluate the predicate on the raw stored model (for example `idpDelegate.getById`), or always invalidate when the org-aware wrapper is involved.

title: Per-organization search keys bloat and thrash a single cache entry per fetch mode
body: All searches for a fetch mode share one `IdentityProviderListQuery` entry, and `searchKey` is the organizationId. For `REALM_ONLY` the delegate ignores organizationId, so the same result is stored once per org. For `ALL`, every organization's set repeats all realm-level login IDPs. Each first lookup for a new org takes the `cached == null` branch, which calls `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and rebuilds a new query by copying all previous searches. In a realm with many organizations this means O(orgs) growth of one entry, O(n²) copying, and repeated local invalidation/re-adds on the hot login path. Normalise the key (use `""` for `REALM_ONLY`) and/or key the entry by organization instead of piling everything into one query.

title: remove() now always hits the DB even when the IDP is in the cache
body: `storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` runs unconditionally. Before, the DB lookup only happened when the alias key was already invalidated in this transaction; otherwise the cached entry was used. The result is only needed to evaluate the login predicate, so every removal now pays an extra query. Reuse the cached model (`cached.getIdentityProvider()`) when available, and only fall back to the delegate when the entry is missing or invalid.

title: Cleanup removes the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP
body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` targets an IDP named "alias", not the one created in the loop (`idp-alias-N`). The same applies to the cleanup for `idp-alias-20` at line 425. The created providers are never cleaned up, and the cleanup call either fails with a 404 or is silently ignored. Leftover IDPs can leak into other tests that share the realm. Use the actual alias variable.

title: Test checks only cache presence, never the returned results or invalidation on creating/removing an eligible IDP
body: `testCacheIDPForLogin` inspects the `IdentityProviderListQuery` contents but never asserts what `getForLogin` actually returns on a cache hit (including the wrapped, org-aware models and the HashSet reassembly). It only covers creating a non-eligible IDP and removing a non-eligible IDP, so the branches that matter are untested. These are: creating an eligible IDP, removing an eligible IDP (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation` in `create`/`remove`), disabling an eligible IDP, and organization disable/enable. A regression in those invalidation paths would go unnoticed.

title: Update invalidation tests the org-wrapped `original` model, so its `isEnabled()` depends on org state and can skip a needed invalidation
body: `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` receives `original` from `getById()`. With the ORGANIZATION feature on, that is the wrapped model whose `isEnabled()` also requires the organization to exist and be enabled. The cached `getForLogin` ID sets are built from the raw DB state and ignore org enabled-state. If an IDP is linked to a disabled org, is enabled and public in the DB, and is already in the cached set, `test(original)` is false. An update that hides it on login, marks it link-only or disables it makes `test(updated)` false too, so the method returns early and nothing is invalidated. The stale ID set keeps the IDP. When the org is re-enabled, `getForLogin` returns the fresh model through `getById`. The bean in this PR re-checks only `isEnabled()`, not `hideOnLogin` or `linkOnly`, so an IDP that was hidden or link-only appears on the login page. The comparison should use the raw persisted state, for example the delegate's model or one not wrapped by the org-aware `isEnabled`.

title: remove() now always queries the DB for the IDP, even when it is in the cache
body: `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is now called unconditionally at the top of `remove()`. Previously the delegate was queried only when the alias key was invalidated; otherwise the cached entry supplied the internal id. The `else` branch's cache lookup no longer saves a query. The cached or already-loaded model could be used to decide whether login caches need invalidation.

title: Cleanup registers removal of a literal IDP "alias" instead of the created IDPs
body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` binds to an IDP with the literal alias "alias", not the `idp-alias-N` IDPs just created. The same mistake is at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`, and the new test copied it from `testCacheIDPByOrg`. The cleanup never removes the 21 IDPs and will probably hit a 404 for the nonexistent "alias" when it runs. The test asserts exact counts, so leftover IDPs would make it order-dependent if the realm is not re-imported between tests. The variable alias should be captured, for example `testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove`.

title: No test for the positive invalidation paths of create/remove, or for the bean and org-disabled behaviour
body: `testCacheIDPForLogin` covers only creating or removing IDPs that are not login-eligible, which must not invalidate. It never creates or removes an IDP that is login-eligible, though `create()` and `remove()` now call `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` to invalidate in that case. It also does not cover disabled orgs, where the cache holds IDs based on raw DB state but `getById` returns wrapped models. The `isEnabled()` re-check added to `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` has no test either. The cached results are never compared with what `getForLogin` actually returns.

title: Login-cache invalidation on update evaluates the org-wrapped model, so edits made while the org is disabled can leave the cache stale
body: `update()` takes `original` from `getById()`, which returns the organization-aware wrapper. The wrapper's `isEnabled()` also returns false when the linked org, or the organization feature, is disabled. `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` therefore reports 'not a login IDP' for any org-linked IDP while its org is disabled, whatever its stored state. The updated model comes straight from the request and is not wrapped. Example: the org is disabled and an admin sets hideOnLogin=true, linkOnly=true or enabled=false on a previously listed IDP. Both `original` and `updated` test as non-login, so the method returns early and registers no invalidation. The cached id set still contains an IDP that the database query now excludes. Once the org is re-enabled, `getForLogin` returns the stale id set. The bean's added `isEnabled()` re-check only covers the enabled case, so a hidden or link-only IDP would show up on the login page until something else invalidates the entry. The comparison should use the stored (unwrapped) state of the original IDP, for example the cached delegate model.

title: remove() now always queries the database for the IDP, even when it is cached
body: `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is now called unconditionally at the top of `remove()`. Before, it was only called when the alias key was already invalidated in the transaction. In the common case, where the alias entry is cached, this adds an extra DB round trip on every removal. The stored model is needed only for the login-invalidation check. It could be taken from the cached entry that is already looked up, and fetched from the delegate only when that entry is missing or invalidated.

title: Cache search key includes organizationId even for REALM_ONLY mode, where it is ignored
body: `searchKey` is always derived from `organizationId`. For `FetchMode.REALM_ONLY` the delegate ignores the organization id, so each distinct org id produces a separate but identical entry. Every new key also triggers the `invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and re-add path, which bumps the revision for that cache key. The search key should be normalized, for example to "" for REALM_ONLY, so the entry is shared.

title: Cleanup registered with the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP's alias
body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` targets an IDP literally named "alias", not the one just created (`idp-alias-N`). The same bug is on line 425, and the pattern is copied from the existing test. The 21 IDPs created by this test are never removed. Cleanup will either fail with a 404 or silently do nothing, depending on the cleanup implementation. The leftover IDPs can leak into other tests, because several tests assert exact IDP counts. The cleanup should use the actual alias variable.

title: Test does not exercise creating or removing an IDP that is available for login
body: The invalidation tests only create a non-login IDP (hideOnLogin) and remove a non-login IDP (a disabled one), and assert the caches survive. The new `create()` and `remove()` invalidation for IDPs that qualify for login is never tested. A regression there would go unnoticed. The test also only checks the size of the cached id sets, not what `getForLogin` actually returns. It does not cover the org-disabled scenario that the new `isEnabled()` re-check in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` exists for. Add cases that create and remove a login IDP and assert the cache is cleared, and cases that verify the returned content.

title: Duplicate-provider error removed, and equal-order providers are now picked arbitrarily
body: The old code threw IllegalStateException when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath. The new code sorts by order() and takes the first. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200. If two of them are on the classpath, for example FIPS and default through a packaging mistake, the winner depends on the sort being stable over ServiceLoader order, which is classpath order. A FIPS deployment could silently run the non-FIPS BouncyCastle provider, where it used to fail fast. The ignored providers are reported only at debug level. All providers are also instantiated before the choice (the stream is collected eagerly), and the Default and FIPS constructors register global java.security providers as a side effect. Give the real providers distinct orders, or keep failing when the top order is tied, and log ignored providers at a visible level.

title: New abstract method order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public SPI, and `int order()` is added as an abstract method. Any third-party or downstream implementation (custom FIPS/HSM providers and the like) no longer compiles. A binary that was compiled earlier throws AbstractMethodError inside CryptoIntegration.detectProvider when `CryptoProvider::order` is invoked, which fails startup. A `default int order()` returning a neutral value would keep compatibility while still letting the three built-in providers override it.

title: Most CryptoProvider operations throw UnsupportedOperationException, including plain-JCA ones
body: AuthzClient.create now calls CryptoIntegration.init, so this class becomes the active provider whenever no higher-order provider is on the classpath. getSignature, getKeyFactory, getKeyPairGen, getAesCbcCipher, getAesGcmCipher, getSecretKeyFact, getX509CertFactory, getCertStore, getCertPathBuilder, createECParams, getPemUtils and getCertificateUtils all throw UnsupportedOperationException. Most of these have trivial plain-JCA implementations, which WildFlyElytronProvider already shows (Signature.getInstance, KeyFactory.getInstance and so on). keycloak-core code that goes through CryptoIntegration.getProvider() for signing, key parsing, EC parameters or PEM/cert handling will fail at runtime with a bare 'Not supported yet.'. Implement the JCA-based methods, or make the failures descriptive and document the supported subset.

title: Dead code: encoded INTEGERs are computed and discarded
body: `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` create encoders and throw the results away, since the same values are encoded again in the following writeDerSeq call. They look like leftover debugging and should be removed.

title: Test uses a P-256 key for ES384/ES512 and only checks a self-consistent round trip
body: `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` uses the default curve (P-256), and that same key signs for ES256, ES384 and ES512. For ES384/ES512 the real r/s values are about 32 bytes while the test asks for 48 and 66 byte components, so the padding path is exercised but the truncation and matching-curve paths are not. P-521 signatures also produce a DER sequence longer than 127 bytes, which uses the long-form length code in ASN1Decoder/ASN1Encoder, and that path is never run. The assertion is only DER->RS->DER->RS, so a symmetric bug in the encoder and decoder would still pass. The test should use secp256r1, secp384r1 and secp521r1 for the corresponding algorithms. It should also compare against known vectors, or against another implementation, and cover small r/s values and values with the high bit set.

title: Multiple crypto providers no longer fail fast; ties at order 200 are resolved silently by classpath order
body: The old check threw IllegalStateException when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath. It is replaced with a sort by order() descending, taking the first, and logging the ignored ones only at debug level. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200. If, for example, both the default and FIPS providers end up on the classpath, the choice is decided only by ServiceLoader/classpath order. The server can then start in non-FIPS mode (or the reverse) without any warning. The ordering is meant to let the lower-order authz-client provider yield to a real one. Ties between real providers should still be an error, or at least be logged at warn. The ignored-providers message is also passed to debugf as the format string and ends with a dangling ", ".

title: New abstract order() breaks every existing CryptoProvider implementation
body: order() is added to the public SPI interface as an abstract method. Any third-party or custom CryptoProvider compiled against the previous interface now fails to compile. A pre-compiled one throws AbstractMethodError, and CryptoIntegration.detectProvider calls order() during sorting, so startup fails. A default method (for example returning a neutral value) would add the ordering feature without breaking the contract.

title: Dead code: two ASN1Encoder results are computed and discarded
body: `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` build encoders whose results are never used. The same values are encoded again in the `writeDerSeq(...)` call below. These look like leftover debugging lines and should be removed.

title: Provider auto-selected by AuthzClient.create throws UnsupportedOperationException for core JCA operations
body: AuthzClient.create() now calls CryptoIntegration.init, which on a standalone client classpath selects this provider. Most of its methods (getSignature, getKeyFactory, getKeyPairGen, getX509CertFactory, getCertStore, getCertPathBuilder, getAesCbcCipher, getAesGcmCipher, getSecretKeyFact, getPemUtils, wrapFactoryForTruststore, ...) just throw UnsupportedOperationException. They could trivially delegate to the plain JDK (for example `Signature.getInstance(JavaAlgorithm.getJavaAlgorithm(alg))`, `KeyFactory.getInstance`). Keycloak core code paths that go through the CryptoProvider, such as signing client-assertion JWTs with an RSA/EC key or loading certificates and PEM keys, will fail at runtime with an unchecked exception. Only the ECDSA conversion helpers and getKeyStore are implemented.

title: Round-trip-only test cannot catch a symmetric encoder/decoder bug and does not use realistic curve sizes
body: The test only asserts that DER → R||S → DER → R||S returns the same R||S. It never checks that the re-encoded DER (`asn1Des`) equals the original JDK signature (`sign`). It never verifies the converted signature against the public key. A symmetric error in the custom ASN1Encoder/ASN1Decoder (for example non-minimal integer encoding or sign handling) would still pass. The key pair is always the default P-256 curve, even for ES384/ES512, so the 48- and 66-byte component paths are not exercised with matching keys. No negative or malformed-input cases are covered either. Adding `assertArrayEquals(sign, asn1Des)` and per-curve key generation would make the test meaningful.

title: Multiple-provider check removed; equal-order providers are now silently resolved
body: `detectProvider` used to fail fast when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath. It now sorts by `order()` and takes the first. `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider` and `FIPS1402Provider` all return 200, so a misconfigured deployment (for example default and FIPS together) no longer fails. Stable sorting then makes the winner depend on ServiceLoader/classpath order, and the ignored providers are only listed at DEBUG. `ServiceLoader` is also drained eagerly, so every provider is instantiated, including those that are then ignored. The `FIPS1402Provider` and `DefaultCryptoProvider` constructors have global side effects (`Security.insertProviderAt`, `Security.addProvider`). Equal-order ties should still throw, or the fallback should be the only case where multiple providers are tolerated. At minimum, log a WARN when the top two orders are equal.

title: `order()` added as an abstract interface method breaks existing implementations
body: `CryptoProvider` is a public SPI. Adding `int order()` without a default makes every external or third-party implementation, and any test or custom provider elsewhere in the repo not updated here, fail to compile. It also fails at runtime with `AbstractMethodError` against already-built jars. A `default int order() { return 0; }` (or similar) would keep source and binary compatibility and still let the built-in providers override it.

title: Dead code: two ASN1 encodings are computed and discarded
body: `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` build encoders and throw the results away. The real encoding is built again in the `writeDerSeq(...)` call below. These lines do nothing and look like leftover debugging. Remove them.

title: No input validation in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: The method assumes `signature.length >= signLength`. If the input is shorter, `System.arraycopy` throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`, an unchecked exception, although the method contract declares `IOException`. Callers that handle malformed signatures through `IOException` will not catch it. Check the length and throw `IOException`.

title: Signature, KeyFactory, KeyPairGenerator and related operations throw UnsupportedOperationException
body: `getSignature`, `getKeyFactory`, `getKeyPairGen`, `getAesCbcCipher`, `getCertificateUtils`, `getPemUtils` and others all throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. `AuthzClient.create` now calls `CryptoIntegration.init`, which picks this provider whenever it is the only one on the classpath. Any authz-client flow that needs JWS signing, for example `client-jwt`/`signed-jwt` client credentials or ES/RS signature handling in keycloak-core, will then fail at runtime with a bare 'Not supported yet.' None of these methods even use the JDK's default providers, which would be enough for RSA/EC signatures. The limitation is not documented in the class Javadoc.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns an unrelated JDK provider (SUN) via a KeyStore lookup
body: The method returns whatever provider backs the default KeyStore type, normally `SUN`, not BouncyCastle. Code that derives its provider name from this (for example `BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` used in `Signature.getInstance(alg, BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER)`) will look up algorithms in `SUN`, which does not provide RSA/EC signatures or AES ciphers. This produces confusing `NoSuchAlgorithmException`/`NoSuchProviderException` failures. The result also depends on the `keystore.type` security property. Returning `null` (as the Elytron provider does) or documenting the intent would be safer.

title: Indefinite/negative length is not handled and surfaces as NegativeArraySizeException
body: `readLength()` returns -1 for the indefinite-length marker (0x80). `readInteger()` then calls `read(length)` and `readNext()` calls `read(length + header)`. For a malformed or indefinite-length element these reach `new byte[negative]` in `read(int)`, which throws an unchecked `NegativeArraySizeException`. The method signatures promise `IOException`, so callers will not handle it. Reject length < 0 with an `IOException` (DER does not allow indefinite lengths). Also, `readSequence` does not check that the declared length is consumed exactly or that no trailing data follows.

title: Round-trip-only test with a P-256 key for all algorithms; no fixed vectors or edge cases
body: The test generates one default EC key (P-256) and signs with ES256, ES384 and ES512 using that same key. The ES384/ES512 cases therefore only exercise the padding branch of `integerToBytes` with 32-byte r/s, not real P-384/P-521 signatures. The assertion only compares RS→DER→RS with the encoder and decoder from the same class, so a consistent bug in both would pass. It never asserts that `asn1Des` equals the original JDK DER signature, and it never verifies the re-encoded signature with `Signature.verify`. The random key also means the interesting edge cases (r or s with a leading zero byte, or with the high bit set) are not tested deterministically. Nothing tests the new `order()`/provider selection in `CryptoIntegration` either.

title: NPE when the 'Clients' type resource is missing
body: When no resource exists for the client, `getResourceTypeResource(...)` is used as the fallback. That method returns null if the schema is unsupported or no `Clients` resource exists, but the result is passed straight to `getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)`. That call dereferences the resource and throws an NPE. The case is realistic. `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists, so realms initialised before this change never get the new `Clients` resource or the `configure`, `map-roles-client-scope` and `map-roles-composite` scopes. For those realms every non-realm-admin client permission check becomes a 500 instead of a deny. Add a null check and return false.

title: getClientsWithPermission cannot return client ids
body: The method iterates `findByType(server, "Clients", ...)` and adds `resource.getName()` to the result. Only the all-clients resource has type `Clients`, because `init()` sets it. Its name is the literal string `Clients`, not a client id. Per-client resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` via `resourceStore.create(...)` without `setType`, so `findByType` does not return them. The result is therefore either `{"Clients"}` or an empty set, never the ids of the clients the caller can access. Anything relying on this method for filtering gets wrong results. The method is also not covered by any test.

title: getResourceName has no handling for the new Clients resource type
body: `getResourceName` special-cases only `Users`: it returns 'All users' for the type resource and the username otherwise. For `Clients` it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. That is null for both the all-clients resource and per-client resources, whose name is the client UUID. Listing the resources of a Clients permission therefore returns resources with a null name, so the API and UI cannot show 'All clients' or the clientId. It should return something like 'All clients' for the type resource and the clientId for per-client resources.

title: V2 clients() throws UnsupportedOperationException from methods reachable at runtime
body: `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns a `ClientPermissionsV2` whose `canExchangeTo`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions` and the `*Permission` methods all throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. Before this change V2 used the V1 implementation, which simply returned false or an empty result. Code paths that still call these methods now produce a 500 instead of a normal deny or empty answer. Examples are the legacy token-exchange permission check (`canExchangeTo`) and `GET /clients/{id}/management/permissions`, which calls `isPermissionsEnabled`. The V2 implementation should return safe values (false, empty, or a proper 4xx) rather than throwing from request paths.

title: Cleanup listener is skipped under V2, leaving orphan client resources and permissions
body: The removal listener is now wrapped in `isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` (V1). V1 and V2 are mutually exclusive versions of the feature, so the listener does nothing under V2. The wrapper is needed because `setPermissionsEnabled` now throws in V2. However, nothing replaces the cleanup. When a client is deleted, the per-client resource named by its UUID, and any permission that references it, stays in the admin-permissions resource server. Stale resources are left behind and the permissions still refer to a nonexistent client. V2 needs its own removal handler that deletes the resource, or detaches it from the permissions.

title: Javadoc on void require* methods describes a return value
body: `requireView()` and `requireViewClientScopes()` are `void` methods that throw `ForbiddenException`. Their new Javadoc says 'Returns {@code true} if canView() returns true' and 'Returns {@code true} if canViewClientScopes() returns true'. The other `require*` methods correctly say 'Throws ForbiddenException if ...'. The wording is copy-pasted from the `can*` methods and misdescribes the contract.

title: Tests mutate shared client and roles without cleanup, and key paths are untested
body: `testManageOnlyOneClient` renames `myclient` and moves a default client scope to optional. `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` creates client roles, a composite and a role mapping. None of this is restored or registered with `realm.cleanup()`, and `onAfter` removes only the permissions. State leaks between tests in the class, so results depend on test order. There is also no coverage for several paths added in this PR. `getClientsWithPermission` is untested. `map-roles-client-scope` is untested. The view-all-clients case with MANAGE or CONFIGURE implying VIEW is untested. Deleting a client that has permissions is untested. No negative case checks that a per-client permission on client A does not grant access to client B beyond the one 'can't update a different client' assertion.

title: Javadoc for requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() says "Returns true" but they are void and throw
body: `requireView()` (lines 95-98) and `requireViewClientScopes()` (lines 100-103) are documented as "Returns {@code true} if canView()/canViewClientScopes() returns true". Both methods are `void` and throw ForbiddenException when the check fails. Every other `require*` method in this same interface is documented correctly as "Throws ForbiddenException if ...". These two should be fixed to match.

title: getResourceName does not handle the Clients resource type
body: `getResourceName` special-cases only `USERS` ("All users" for the type resource, the username for a per-user resource). For a policy whose resourceType is `Clients`, it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Per-client resources are created in `getOrCreateResource` via `resourceStore.create(server, name, owner)` with no display name, and their name is the client's internal UUID. So the "all clients" resource and each per-client resource resolve to a null or opaque name when permissions are rendered. Clients need the same handling: "All clients" for the type resource and the clientId for a specific client.

title: getClientsWithPermission uses findByType and returns resource names that are not necessarily client ids
body: `getClientsWithPermission` iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...)` and adds `resource.getName()` to the result. In `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource`, per-client resources are created without a type, so they are not returned by `findByType`. The only resource with type `Clients` is the all-clients resource, whose name is the literal string "Clients", not a client id. If an all-clients permission grants the scope, the result is {"Clients"}, which matches no client. Clients granted individually are never returned. Callers that use this set to filter clients will get wrong results. Either the lookup must also cover per-client resources (and resolve names to client ids), or the method needs an all-clients expansion.

title: Up to five full policy evaluations per client in canView(client) when listing
body: `canView(client)` calls `canView()` (one evaluation on the all-clients resource), then `canConfigure(client)`. That calls `canManage(client)` (a second evaluation) and a CONFIGURE `hasPermission` (a third). Finally it calls `hasPermission(client, VIEW)` (a fourth). Each `hasPermission` does a resource lookup, possibly a policy-store lookup, and a full `evaluatePermission` over all of the resource's scopes. Only one scope is inspected afterwards. When listing clients this runs per client, so cost grows quickly with realm size. Evaluating once and checking several scopes, or passing only the requested scope to the evaluation, would avoid the repetition.

title: Possible NPE: getResourceTypeResource can return null and is passed to findByResource
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...)` returns null when the schema is not supported for the server (for example admin permissions disabled on the realm while the client still exists) or when the type resource is not found. The result is passed straight into `findByResource(server, resource)` and later dereferenced via `resource.getScopes()`, with no null check. That would turn a permission check into a 500 instead of a plain "false".

title: canView() ignores an all-clients MANAGE grant while canView(ClientScopeModel) honours it
body: `canView()` is `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(VIEW)`. An admin with only the all-clients MANAGE scope therefore fails `canView()`/`requireView()`. `canView(ClientScopeModel)` explicitly accepts `VIEW || MANAGE`, and `canView(ClientModel)` accepts manage indirectly through `canConfigure`. For users, the tests treat manage as implying view. Endpoints guarded by the no-arg `canView()`/`requireView()` will behave differently from per-client and client-scope checks for the same admin.

title: Dead code and unused imports left in ClientPermissionsV2
body: The private `getEvaluationContext(...)` is never called. The `logger` field and the imports `Scope` and `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` are also unused. This looks like leftover scaffolding copied from the V1 class (including the token-exchange `kc.client.id` attribute), and it is misleading because V2 throws UnsupportedOperationException for token exchange. It should be removed.

title: Event listener is now gated on V1 feature, so V2 gets no cleanup when a client is removed
body: The whole listener body is now wrapped in `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`. This avoids calling the V2 `setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws UnsupportedOperationException. As a side effect, under V2 nothing reacts to `ClientRemovedEvent`. The per-client resource (named after the client UUID) and any scope permissions that reference it remain in the admin-permissions authorization store after the client is deleted. Stale resources and permissions accumulate and show up when permissions are listed. The change also silently drops the previous behaviour in realms where neither feature is enabled. A V2-specific cleanup handler is needed rather than just disabling the listener.

title: Test regenerates the secret of the client used to authenticate the admin client and mutates shared state without restoring it
body: `realmAdminClient` authenticates with client `myclient` and secret `mysecret`. `testConfigureOnlyOneClient` calls `clientResource.generateNewSecret()` on that same client. Once the secret is rotated, any later token acquisition or refresh by this admin client in the class (the token expires, or another test builds a new session) fails with 401 using the old secret. This makes the suite order- and timing-dependent. Other tests also leave persistent changes: they rename `myclient` and `realmClient`, move a default client scope to optional, and create roles on `myclient`. `onAfter` only removes permissions, so these mutations leak into subsequent tests.

title: No coverage for several new V2 client paths
body: The new tests cover manage, configure, view and map-roles(+composite) on clients. There is no test for `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`. Nothing checks that a client with a CONFIGURE or VIEW permission still cannot be managed or modified beyond what is intended. `getClientsWithPermission` and the client-scope management permissions (`canManageClientScopes`, `canView(ClientScopeModel)`) are not exercised either. The `getClientsWithPermission` path is the one with the likely defects noted above, and a test would have exposed them.

title: A broad 'view all clients' grant short-circuits per-client deny permissions in canView(client)
body: `canView(ClientModel)` first returns true if `canView()` is true. `canView()` is true when the caller holds the VIEW scope on the all-clients (type) resource (`hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)`). Only afterwards does it consult the per-client resource. The same applies to `canConfigure(client)`, which is also reached from this short-circuit. A per-client permission with negative logic, or any per-client policy that should deny VIEW for one client, is therefore never evaluated once an all-clients VIEW permission exists. The Users tests (`testViewUserPermission`) treat 'allow all, deny one' as supported behaviour. Here the deny is silently ignored, so the caller can view and list a client they were explicitly denied. No test covers this case for clients.

title: getResourceName has no branch for the new Clients resource type
body: `getResourceName` maps resource names to display names only for `USERS`. The `Users` branch turns the user id into a username and returns 'All users' for the type resource. The new `Clients` type is not handled. A per-client resource is named by the client's internal UUID (see `getOrCreateResource`/`resolveClient`) and has no display name, so it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Clients permissions then show a null or meaningless name for per-client resources, and 'Clients' instead of an 'All clients' label for the type resource. Add a `CLIENTS` branch that resolves the client id to its clientId and returns 'All clients' for the type resource.

title: Possible NPE when the Clients type resource does not exist
body: When no per-client resource exists, `getResourceTypeResource(...)` is called and its result is passed straight to `PolicyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`. That method returns null when the schema is not active (for example admin permissions disabled on the realm while the client remains), or when the 'Clients' resource was never created. The second case applies to any realm whose admin-permissions client was created before this change, because `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` returns early if the client already exists and never adds the new Clients scopes or resource. This path runs for every ordinary client access check, so it would turn those checks into 500s instead of a plain 'false'. Add a null check on `resource` before using it.

title: UnsupportedOperationException is thrown from methods reachable via public admin and token-exchange paths
body: `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns a `ClientPermissionsV2` whose `canExchangeTo`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions`, `resource` and the `*Permission(client)` methods all throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. These are the V1 methods called from existing code. One caller is the client `management/permissions` REST endpoint. Another is the legacy token-exchange check, which calls `canExchangeTo`. With V2 enabled these requests now fail with an uncaught exception, a 500, instead of a 403/404 or a 'permissions disabled' response. Before this change the inherited V1 behaviour returned a normal answer. Either return safe values (false / disabled / empty) or guard those endpoints for V2.

title: Gating the removal listener on V1 leaves orphaned V2 permission resources when clients, roles or groups are deleted
body: The listener that disables permissions on role, client and group removal now runs only when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1) is enabled. This avoids calling the throwing V2 `setPermissionsEnabled`. But nothing replaces it for V2. When a client is deleted, its per-client resource (named by client id) and any scope permissions that reference it stay in the admin-permissions resource server as stale data. Deleting a client that has per-client permissions therefore leaves dangling resources and permissions. V2 needs a cleanup on `ClientRemovedEvent`, or this gap should be called out explicitly.

title: Javadoc of void require* methods describes a boolean return
body: `requireView()` and `requireViewClientScopes()` are void methods that throw `ForbiddenException`. Their new Javadoc says 'Returns {@code true} if canView() returns true' and 'Returns {@code true} if canViewClientScopes() returns true'. Every other require* method in this file says 'Throws ForbiddenException if ...'. The text misleads callers about the contract and should be changed to the 'Throws ForbiddenException if ... returns false' form.

title: Dead code and unused imports left in new class
body: `getEvaluationContext(...)` is private and never called. The `logger` field and the imports `Scope`, `TOKEN_EXCHANGE`, `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `EvaluationContext` and `AccessToken` (used only by the dead method and `canExchangeTo`) are leftovers from the V1 token-exchange code. They add noise and suggest functionality that does not exist in V2. Remove them.

title: Test rotates the secret of the client that the admin client authenticates with
body: `testConfigureOnlyOneClient` calls `clientResource.generateNewSecret()` on `myclient`. The injected `realmAdminClient` authenticates as `myclient` with secret `mysecret`. After rotation, `mysecret` no longer authenticates, because no rotation policy is configured. Any later test in the class that needs a fresh or refreshed token (token expiry, a re-created admin client) would get 401 depending on execution order and timing. The test state is also not restored in cleanup. Use a different client for the secret operations, or restore the secret afterwards.

title: Missing coverage for map-roles-client-scope, deny semantics and the all-clients/per-client interplay
body: The new schema adds `map-roles-client-scope`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` is implemented, but no test exercises it. There is also no test of a negative per-client permission combined with an all-clients VIEW/MANAGE grant, which is where `canView(client)` currently misbehaves. There is no test of `getClientsWithPermission`. The tests only check positive grants on one client, or on all clients, in isolation.

title: Default (null-strategy) test case never enables the rolling-updates feature in the CR
body: `createInitialDeployment` returns early when `updateStrategy == null`, so the `rolling-updates` feature is only added to the Keycloak CR for the RECREATE case. The new docs say the feature must be enabled on the CR ("Otherwise, the Operator will fail") and show `<not set>` together with `features.enabled: rolling-updates`. The null case passes only because `Dockerfile-custom-image` now bakes `--features=rolling-updates` into the image at build time. The tests therefore never exercise the documented configuration for the default strategy, and a missing or disabled feature in the CR is never tested. Enable the feature for both parameterized cases, or add a case that covers the feature being absent.

title: setEnabledFeatures overwrites any features already configured on the test CR
body: `getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES))` replaces the whole enabled-features list. If `getTestKeycloakDeployment` or a future change already sets enabled features on the FeatureSpec, they are silently dropped. Append to the existing list, or build a mutable list that merges the new key in.

title: New exit codes (4 = feature disabled, 3 = recreate) are not asserted
body: The PR changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`. These are documented as the scripting contract for the `check` command. `testFeatureNotEnabled` only checks the stderr message, and `testWrongVersions` only checks the error text. Neither asserts the process exit code, so a regression such as returning 3 for a disabled feature, or 4 for a version mismatch, would pass. `testFeatureNotEnabled` also covers only the `metadata` subcommand, not `check`. Add `assertEquals(4, ...)` for the disabled case on both subcommands and `assertEquals(3, ...)` for the incompatible-version case.

title: Exit code 4 is reused with a different meaning, and no consumers are updated in this PR
body: Exit code 4 used to mean "recreate upgrade required" and now means "feature disabled". Recreate moves to 3. Any consumer that hardcodes the old value will misread the result. The Operator's update logic, which runs this tool, is one candidate; scripts built on the earlier code are another. A missing feature would then be treated as a recreate signal, and a real recreate (3) as an unknown error. This PR changes no Operator main code, and the Operator tests do not cover the exit-code mapping, because the image-change test never runs the job. Confirm that all consumers use the new 3/4 mapping, ideally via shared constants rather than duplicated literals.

title: Default-strategy test path never enables rolling-updates in the CR; the custom image build hides it
body: createInitialDeployment returns early when updateStrategy == null, before FeatureSpec.setEnabledFeatures(rolling-updates) is applied. The `null` case of testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount therefore runs without the feature in the CR. It only works because Dockerfile-custom-image now builds the image with `--features=rolling-updates`. The new operator docs say the feature must be enabled, "Otherwise, the Operator will fail", and that is how the default-strategy case is documented. The test neither verifies this nor matches it, and the image-level flag makes the CR-level setting redundant. A regression in how the feature gets enabled would not be caught. Apply the feature setting to both branches, or add a test that the update fails or reports a clear status when the feature is off.

title: Feature-disabled behaviour only checked for `metadata`, and the new exit code 4 is never asserted
body: The new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4) is a scripting contract documented in update-compatibility.adoc. testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the error text for the `metadata` subcommand and does not assert the exit code. The `check` subcommand has the same guard and no disabled-feature test. A regression that exits with 0 or 1, or drops the early return in `check`, would pass. Add assertions that the exit code is 4 for both subcommands. Also cover the renumbered RECREATE exit code (now 3) in testWrongVersions.

title: Macro hard-codes `--features=rolling-updates`, conflicting with the "use all your start options" instruction
body: The updatecompatibility macro appends a fixed `--features=rolling-updates` to every rendered example. The guide tells users to pass all the options they use with `start`, including `--features=...` in most real deployments. Following both instructions yields two `--features` options. Picocli rejects that or silently overrides one. Either way the metadata is computed against a different feature set than the running server, which is the case the warning in the guide describes. The guide should say that `rolling-updates` must be added to the existing feature list, rather than showing it as an extra standalone flag.

title: Exit code 4 changes meaning from 'recreate upgrade' to 'feature disabled'
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3, and 4 is reused for the new FEATURE_DISABLED code. Any script, pipeline or operator logic that treated exit code 4 as 'rolling upgrade not possible, recreate' now reads a disabled feature as a recreate result. Meanwhile 3 means recreate. Because the old and new meanings overlap on 4, a consumer that was not updated fails silently instead of loudly. The PR should check every consumer of these exit codes (operator code, tests, scripts) and call out the renumbering. The docs already listed 3, so the old code was out of sync with them, but the swap is still a contract change.

title: Disabled-feature path is only tested for 'metadata' and the exit code is never asserted
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only launches `update-compatibility metadata` and checks the error text. The `check` subcommand has the same new guard but no test. Neither test asserts that the process exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4), which is the contract the docs and scripts depend on. A regression that returned 0 or 1 with the same message would pass. Add a `check` case and assert the exit code.

title: Macro hard-codes `--features=rolling-updates` and can clash with the user's own `--features`
body: The guide tells users to pass the same options they use for `start`, but the macro now appends `--features=rolling-updates` to every update-compatibility example. A user who already sets `--features=...` for their deployment will either repeat the option, which may be rejected, or drop their other features from the compatibility run. The guide should say that `rolling-updates` must be added to the existing feature list instead of presenting it as part of the fixed command. Also, `features` is a build-time option, so a custom image must be built with it. The operator docs' new CAUTION says only that the Operator 'will fail' and does not say that.

title: V2 canManage() grants manage access to admins who only have the VIEW scope on all groups
body: `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. VIEW is wrongly accepted as a manage scope, probably copied from `canView()`. `canManage()` guards `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` (`auth.groups().requireManage()`). An admin whose all-groups permission only has `view` can therefore create top-level groups. The interface Javadoc repeats the mistake: `canManage()` is documented as granting access to 'VIEW or MANAGE groups'. It should check only `MANAGE`. `testViewGroups` only lists groups with a VIEW-only permission and never tries a write, so it doesn't catch this.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses the resource UUID instead of the group id (resource name)
body: In V2 a group's authorization resource is named after the group id (`resolveGroup` returns `group.getId()` as the resource name). The callback passes `groupResource.getId()`, the resource's internal UUID, to `hasPermission(...)`, which does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. That lookup never matches, so every iteration falls back to the all-groups `Groups` type resource. Per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are therefore ignored. `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` also puts resource UUIDs into the set instead of group ids. This set is passed to `UserModel.GROUPS` in user search and to the `getUsersCount(..., groupIds)` overloads, which expect group ids. Searches and counts are filtered by ids that match no group, or they return an empty set and fall back to post-filtering, which breaks pagination. Both uses should be `groupResource.getName()`.

title: Possible NPE when the Groups type resource does not exist
body: `getResourceTypeResource(...)` returns null when the `Groups` resource is missing. `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` is then called with null, and `resource.getScopes()` would dereference it too. `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists, so it never creates the new `Groups` resource or the new group scopes in realms that had admin permissions v2 enabled before this change. For those realms every group permission check that falls back to the all-groups resource would throw instead of returning false. Before this PR, `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` used the V1 evaluator and did not have this problem. A null check on `resource` is needed.

title: Javadoc on requireManageMembers references the wrong check; getGroupIdsWithViewPermission doc is inaccurate
body: `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` is documented as throwing 'if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false', but it calls `canManageMembers`. The `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` Javadoc says `@return Stream of IDs` although the method returns `Set<String>`. It also doesn't say that the set holds group ids, the contract the V2 implementation currently violates. The `canManage()` Javadoc (lines 73-77) says V2 grants it for VIEW or MANAGE, which matches the buggy implementation rather than the intended semantics.

title: Tests don't cover VIEW-only admins being denied writes or the group-id based user filtering
body: `testViewGroups` only checks that listing works with VIEW permissions. No test confirms that an admin with only `view` (per-group or all-groups) is denied create/update/delete of groups. This is the case that would have caught the `canManage()` bug. No test covers `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` through the users count endpoint (`/users/count`). The user search tests pass even if the returned group-id set is empty or wrong, because per-user `canView` post-filtering compensates.

title: V2 canManage() grants global group management for the VIEW scope
body: `canManage()` falls back to `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so a view-only permission on the "all groups" resource is enough to pass it. This is the check behind `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` (`auth.groups().requireManage()`). An admin who was granted only `view` on all groups can therefore create top-level groups. The per-group `canManage(GroupModel)` correctly uses only `MANAGE`, and the V1 equivalent requires the manage-users role, so this looks like a copy-paste from `canView()`. The Javadoc in `GroupPermissionEvaluator` repeats the same wrong contract. No test covers a VIEW-only admin attempting a manage operation. Change the call to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource IDs where group IDs (resource names) are needed
body: In V2 the authorization resource for a group is named after the group ID (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`, and `hasPermission` looks it up with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`). The callback here passes `groupResource.getId()`, which is the resource's own UUID, to `hasPermission`. That lookup by name never matches, so evaluation silently falls back to the generic "Groups" type resource and ignores the per-group permission. The method then adds `groupResource.getId()` to the result set, but callers (`UsersResource.searchForUser`, `getUsersCount`, `BruteForceUsersResource`) treat the values as group IDs for `UserModel.GROUPS` and `getUsersCount(..., groupIds)`. The result is wrong or empty sets and wrong user counts. For searches, the group restriction is not applied in the query, so the later per-user `canView` filter runs after `first`/`max` pagination and returns short or empty pages. The new test only checks the unpaginated search, where the post-filter hides the problem. Use `groupResource.getName()` for both the evaluation and the result, and skip the type-level resource whose name is "Groups".

title: Possible NPE when the Groups type resource does not exist
body: `getResourceTypeResource` returns null when the "Groups" resource has not been created. This happens for realms whose admin-permissions client was initialized before this change, because `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns early when the client already exists and never adds the group scopes or resource. It also returns null if the schema is not active. The code passes that null straight into `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`, which throws an NPE and turns every group permission check into a 500. Add a null check and return false.

title: Incorrect Javadoc on requireManageMembers and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission
body: The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers` says it throws when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false, but it actually delegates to `canManageMembers`. The Javadoc for `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` says it returns a "Stream of IDs" while the method returns `Set<String>`. The `canManage()` Javadoc documents VIEW as sufficient for manage, which is wrong behavior (see the canManage finding above). Fix these descriptions.

title: Weak and missing assertions in group permission tests
body: `testManageGroupMembership` only checks that `joinGroup` does not throw. It does not verify that bob became a member, and it has no negative case such as a different group without the permission. The test suite also has no case showing that a VIEW-only permission on all groups cannot create or modify groups, which would have caught the `canManage()` bug. No test covers the users count endpoint or paginated user search, which use `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` and would expose the resource-ID/group-ID mix-up.

title: canManage() grants manage rights when only the VIEW scope is held
body: `canManage()` (no-arg) falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. An admin who has only `view` on the all-groups resource is therefore treated as able to manage groups. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` calls `auth.groups().requireManage()`, so a view-only admin can create top-level groups. The fallback should check only `MANAGE`. The new interface Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` also says VIEW or MANAGE, which documents the wrong behaviour. The new tests do not catch this: none grants VIEW on all groups and then attempts a manage operation.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes and returns the resource UUID instead of the group id
body: In the `findByType` callback, `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` is called and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` is stored. In V2 the resource name is the group id: `getOrCreateResource` creates the resource with `name = group.getId()`, and `hasPermission` looks it up with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. The resource's own UUID never matches a name, so `hasPermission` silently falls back to the all-groups type resource. The returned set also contains resource UUIDs rather than group ids. Consequences: `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource` set `UserModel.GROUPS` to ids that match no group, and `getUsersCount` is given the same wrong ids, so results can be empty or wrong. Per-group `view-members` permissions are never reflected in the id set. The new test only passes because the post-filter `canView(user)` hides the problem. The callback should use `getName()` for both the evaluation and the collected id.

title: Possible NPE when the Groups type resource does not exist
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...)` returns null when the `Groups` resource is missing. The result is passed straight to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and then to `resource.getScopes()`. `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` returns early for realms that already have an admin-permissions client, so those realms never get the new `Groups` resource or the group scopes. For them every non-role-based group check would throw a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of denying. There is no null guard and no migration.

title: Javadoc of requireManageMembers and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission is wrong
body: `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` is documented as throwing when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false, but it delegates to `canManageMembers`. `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` says it returns a "Stream of IDs" but returns `Set<String>`. These are the new Javadocs this PR introduces for the interface, so they should be correct.

title: getResourceName has no handling for the Groups resource type
body: `getResourceName` special-cases only `USERS` ("All users" or the username). A Groups permission now falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Resources created by `getOrCreateResource` have no display name, and their name is the raw group id. Group permissions will therefore show a null or opaque UUID name instead of "All groups" or the group name.

title: Italian text used as the Lithuanian translation of totpStep1
body: The old Lithuanian `totpStep1` (with FreeOTP/Google Play links) was replaced with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. That is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian sentence on the account TOTP setup page. The line should either be a proper Lithuanian translation of "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:" or be removed so it falls back to English.

title: Italian text used as the Lithuanian translation of loginTotpStep1
body: `loginTotpStep1` was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian. The Lithuanian login OTP setup screen will show an Italian instruction. Use a real Lithuanian translation or drop the key so the English default is used.

title: Traditional Chinese text inserted into the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) bundle
body: The new `totpStep1` is `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`, which is Traditional Chinese (手機, 安裝, 應用程式). It is in the zh_CN bundle, where the rest of the file is Simplified. Simplified-Chinese users will see mixed scripts. It should read something like `在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`.

title: i18next {{n}} placeholders replaced with Java MessageFormat {n} and choice syntax in a JS UI bundle
body: This file uses i18next-style `{{0}}`/`{{1}}` placeholders (see the neighbouring `error-invalid-length-too-short='{{0}}' must have minimal length of {{1}}.`). The PR rewrote `error-invalid-multivalued-size` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. i18next does not interpolate single-brace `{0}` and does not support `choice` formatting. The message will probably render literally with raw `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and the choice expression. The old `{{0}}` form worked with the UI's interpolation. Only the server-side bundles under `themes/` should use MessageFormat choice syntax; the JS bundle should keep `{{n}}` and avoid `choice`, for example a plain "value(s)".

title: Admin UI bundle switched from i18next {{n}} to MessageFormat {n} and choice syntax
body: The admin-ui bundle is rendered by i18next, like the account-ui one, and its sibling `error-*` keys use `{{0}}`. `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed to single-brace `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` plus `{2,choice,...}`. i18next will not substitute the parameters or evaluate the choice, so the validation error shown to admins is likely to contain raw placeholders. Keep the `{{n}}` form here and do not use `choice`.

title: Diff-snippet computation can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of reporting the error
body:
The common prefix (`start`) and common suffix (`end`) are computed independently and are not bounded so that `start + end <= min(length)`. If the removed fragment shares boundary characters with its neighbours, the two ranges overlap. Example: `

A

B

` where the disallowed `` sits between a `>` and a `<`. Then `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` has start > end and throws. The verifier would crash with an unchecked exception rather than emit the "Illegal HTML" message, hiding the real problem. Clamp `end` to `min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`.

title: English reference file lookup is fragile: unchecked exception or silent self-comparison
body: The English file is derived by regex on the whole absolute path. If no `_en` counterpart exists, a `RuntimeException` is thrown from `verify()`, which declares `MojoExecutionException`, so the build fails with a raw stack trace. If the file name does not match `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` (for example a locale suffix containing digits, or a file without a locale), the 'English' file resolves to the file being checked. In that case the translation is compared against itself and the check that only the English source's HTML/anchors may appear is silently bypassed. Fail with a clear MojoExecutionException when the English file is missing or cannot be derived.

title: Only negative cases are tested; no test that valid content passes
body:
All new tests assert that a violation is detected (`hasItem(...)`). Nothing checks that valid input produces no findings. Missing cases are `noHtml_en.properties` verifying clean, a translation that keeps the English ``/`
`/`

` markup, `{{`/`<1>`-style placeholders, and the special-cased keys such as `templateHelp` and `error-invalid-multivalued-size`. Because the sanitizer round-trip comparison is brittle (for example `
` vs `
`), false positives would break the build for translators and are not covered. The duplicate-keys test was also weakened from `contains` to `hasItem`.

title: Diff-trimming logic can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of reporting the violation
body:
The common-prefix (`start`) and common-suffix (`end`) are computed independently, so they can overlap. When they do, `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` has start > end and throws. Example: the English source has HTML, and the translation contains an unclosed `

`. The sanitizer outputs `

`, giving start=3 and end=2 on a 3-character value, so `substring(3, 1)` fails. The same happens whenever the sanitizer inserts text that repeats neighbouring characters, such as a closing tag. The unchecked exception escapes the lambda in `verifySafeHtml`, so the build dies with a stack trace instead of the intended 'Illegal HTML in key ...' message. Clamp `end` to `min(len(value), len(sanitized)) - start` before taking the substrings.

title: Anchor-mismatch message identifies neither key nor file
body: The `santizeAnchors` method receives `key` but never uses it. The message is just "Didn't find anchor tag <a ...> in original string". With thousands of message files and keys, a maintainer cannot tell which file or key failed from this message. The 'Illegal HTML' message does include both. Include the key and `file` in this message too.

title: Lithuanian file now contains an Italian string for totpStep1
body: While stripping the anchors, `totpStep1` was replaced with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. That is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian sentence in the OTP setup instructions. It should be a proper Lithuanian translation, or the key should be removed so it falls back to English.

title: Lithuanian login file now contains an Italian string for loginTotpStep1
body: `loginTotpStep1` was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction on the OTP setup page. Provide a Lithuanian translation, or remove the key so the English fallback is used.

title: Simplified Chinese file now contains a Traditional Chinese string
body: `totpStep1` was replaced with `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`, which is Traditional Chinese (zh_TW). The zh_CN locale is Simplified, and every other string in the file uses simplified characters and phrasing. It should read something like `在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`.

title: i18next-style placeholders replaced with MessageFormat syntax in account-ui messages
body: Every other parametrised message in this file uses i18next interpolation (`{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, `{{name}}`). This key was changed to `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` plus `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`. i18next does not interpolate single-brace placeholders and does not support `choice` formats. The account console would then show the literal text `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,...}`. The same conversion was made in the admin-ui resource file (`js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/.../messages_en.properties`). If those UIs render this key through i18next, the message is broken. Keep the i18next syntax there, for example with `{{count}}` plural forms, and only use MessageFormat in the server-side themes.

title: New verifier behaviours are barely covered by tests
body:
The tests only assert that some message containing 'Illegal HTML' or 'anchor' appears. There is no test for the key-specific normalizations (`templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `choice` formats), HTML-entity handling, or `
` normalization. There is also no test for an allowed tag that the sanitizer rewrites, such as an unclosed `

`. The missing unclosed-tag test is why the substring-overlap crash in the diff printing went unnoticed. Add fixtures for these cases.

title: Italian text inserted as the Lithuanian translation of totpStep1
