That callback stages and commits offsets on the `KafkaConsumer`, whose state is owned by the main `StreamProcessor` thread; arroyo does not support calling it concurrently with `poll`/`_run_once`. This can race with the main thread's own consumer calls. It can also commit offsets for partitions that have just been revoked, which makes `stage_offsets` raise. When that raise happens, `mark_committed` is skipped. The tracker never forgets the revoked partition, so the same failing commit is retried and logged every second indefinitely. Commits should be handed back to the main thread, for example by recording the committable offsets and calling `commit` from `poll()`.

title: Queues are unbounded, so there is no backpressure despite the class docstring promising it
body: `queue.Queue()` is created without `maxsize`, and `submit()` never blocks or raises `MessageRejected`. The strategy's docstring claims "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", but there is none. If any worker is slow (the exact scenario this PR targets) or the DB is degraded, the consumer keeps reading from Kafka at full speed. Queue depth, the `WorkItem`s (which hold the full Kafka message) and the offset tracker sets all grow without bound, which risks OOM. Meanwhile no offsets are committed because commits are contiguous. Use a bounded queue and translate a full queue into `MessageRejected` so arroyo applies backpressure, or at least fix the docstring.

title: Commit logic assumes strictly contiguous Kafka offsets and stalls permanently on any gap
body: `get_committable_offsets` walks `range(start, max_offset + 1)` and stops at the first offset that is not in `all_offsets`. Kafka partitions can legitimately have non-consecutive offsets (compaction, transaction control records, messages skipped or filtered upstream). After `mark_committed` trims the set, a single missing offset means `highest_committable` never advances past it. The consumer then stops committing for that partition forever, `all_offsets` grows without bound, and a restart replays everything since the gap. `test_offset_gaps_block_commits` encodes this behavior as desired. A safer approach is to track only the offsets actually submitted, in order, and commit up to the smallest outstanding offset.

title: Shutdown joins workers sequentially with 5s each, never flushes a final commit, and 'graceful' drain is not honored
body: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` joins each worker with a 5s timeout one after another. If several workers are busy, `terminate()` or `close()` can block for up to 5s × num_queues (100s with the default 20), which stalls rebalances and shutdown. `worker.shutdown = True` also makes workers exit after the current item, so `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` never actually drains the remaining queued items. Neither `close()` nor `terminate()` does a final commit of offsets that finished processing since the last 1s tick, so those messages are reprocessed on restart. `join(timeout)` also ignores its timeout argument.

title: Error-handling test asserts no offsets are committed, contradicting its docstring and the actual behavior
body: The docstring says "errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages". The assertion `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets` checks that nothing was committed. In the implementation, a failing item still has its offset completed in the `finally`, so both offsets 100 and 101 become committable and are committed on the next 1s commit tick. The test only passes because it stops waiting about 0.2s after processing, before the commit loop fires. It is timing-dependent and verifies nothing about the intended behavior. It should wait for the commit and assert that offset 102 is committed.

title: Distribution test is flaky because str hash is randomized per process, and the ordering/concurrency tests do not check ordering or concurrency
body: `test_different_groups_distributed` asserts that 20 string group keys cover all 3 queues. `hash(str)` is salted per interpreter run, so there is roughly a 0.1% chance on any run that some queue is never hit, which makes the test flaky. Separately, `test_preserves_order_within_group` and `test_concurrent_processing_different_groups` in the strategy tests only check that the result count equals the number submitted, even though their names and docstrings claim ordering and concurrency are verified. `test_concurrent_processing_across_groups` has the same problem, since it never checks that groups actually run in parallel.

title: Strategy close() shuts down the factory-owned queue pool, so messages are dropped after the first rebalance
body: `FixedQueuePool` is created once in `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__` and the same instance is handed to every `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` from `create_with_partitions`. Arroyo calls `close()`/`join()` on the old strategy at each partition revoke. `close()` and `join()` call `queue_pool.shutdown()`, which sets `worker.shutdown=True`, shuts every queue and joins the workers. The next `create_with_partitions` reuses the dead pool. Its workers have exited and `work_queue.put()` raises `queue.ShutDown`. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` catches that exception, logs it, then calls `add_offset` and `complete_offset`. Every message after the first rebalance is therefore silently dropped and its offset is committed, which is data loss. The shared `OffsetTracker` also keeps stale `last_committed` and `all_offsets` state across assignments. The strategy should not own or shut down the pool (the factory's `shutdown()` should), or the pool must be created per strategy.

title: Arroyo commit callback is invoked from a background thread
body: `_commit_loop` runs in its own daemon thread and calls `self.commit_function(committable)`. In the factory that wraps arroyo's `commit` callback, which stages offsets on the `KafkaConsumer` and may commit. That state is owned by the `StreamProcessor` thread and is not designed for concurrent access while the main thread is polling, pausing or rebalancing. The loop can also commit offsets for partitions that were just revoked, which raises inside the thread; the exception is swallowed and retried every second. Commits should be driven from `poll()`/`submit()` on the consumer thread, using the tracker's committable offsets, rather than from a separate thread.

title: Unbounded queues and no MessageRejected, despite the documented 'natural backpressure'
body: The class docstring promises 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', but each queue is `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize`, and `submit` never raises arroyo's `MessageRejected`. If one worker stalls on a slow item, the consumer keeps polling and enqueueing. Memory grows without bound and the backlog is never limited by the poll loop. The offset tracker's `all_offsets` and `outstanding` sets also grow because the stuck offset blocks all later commits. Either bound the queues and reject when full, or remove the claim.

title: Gap detection only works until the first commit; later gaps are skipped
body: `start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)` skips any gap between `last_committed` and the smallest tracked offset. `mark_committed` prunes `all_offsets` to offsets above the committed one. With offsets 100, 102, 103 tracked, the first pass commits 100. The next pass sees `all_offsets={102,103}`, `start=102`, and commits 103 without 101 ever being tracked or completed. `test_offset_gaps_block_commits` (and the uptime gaps test) do not catch this: the first one passes because it submits 101 before the second commit can matter, and the other only checks the first commit. The documented guarantee ('only commits when all prior offsets are processed') is not enforced. Contiguity should be checked against `last_committed + 1`, or the tracker should rely on in-order submission explicitly.

title: Docstring claims offsets are committed only after successful processing
body: The worker's `finally` block calls `complete_offset` even when `result_processor` raised. Failed items therefore become committable and are committed, so processing errors are skipped rather than retried. The docstring 'Only commits offsets after successful processing' is wrong. Similarly, `terminate()` calls `shutdown()` with `immediate=False`, which does not actually terminate quickly.

title: Error-handling test asserts the opposite of its docstring and passes only by timing
body: The docstring says 'errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages', but the test asserts `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`. With the actual implementation both offsets (the failing one included) are completed in the worker's `finally` and would be committed by the commit loop after its 1s wait. The assertion passes only because the test checks within about 0.3s, before the first commit tick. It verifies nothing about error handling and will fail or flake if timing changes. It should wait for a commit and assert that offsets 100 and 101 are committed (as 102), or assert the intended behavior explicitly.

title: Flaky assertions on queue depth and on hash distribution
body: `test_stats_reporting` asserts `stats['total_items'] > 0` right after submitting 10 items to live worker threads. The workers only append to a list, so they can drain everything before the check. `test_different_groups_distributed` (line 106) asserts that 20 string keys hit all 3 queues. Python string hashes are randomized per process, so this fails for a small fraction of runs (about 0.1%). Both should avoid depending on timing or on the hash seed, for example by blocking the processor on an event or by choosing keys with known assignments.

title: Backup code check and use is not atomic
body: When logging in with a backup code, authorize() reads the decrypted `backupCodes` array, checks `indexOf(credentials.backupCode...)`, and then updates the user row with the consumed code set to null. These are separate non-transactional operations. Two concurrent requests using the same valid backup code can both pass the `index === -1` check before either update runs, so a one-time backup code can authenticate more than once. The code should be consumed atomically, e.g. via a transaction or a conditional update on the current encrypted value.

title: Successful 2FA enable is not reported if dialog is closed by native close
body: `handleEnable` now ends with `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` instead of calling `onEnable`. Only the explicit `backup-codes-close` button calls `onEnable` later. If the dialog is closed with its built-in close control, Escape, or overlay through the `onOpenChange` prop on line 166, the parent never receives `onEnable`, so the settings UI can remain out of sync with the server even though 2FA has already been enabled. Handle dialog close during the backup-codes step or call `onEnable` immediately on successful enable.

title: Core backup-code login/disable paths are untested
body: The PR adds backup-code login and backup-code disabling, but the only added e2e assertions cover showing the backup codes during setup, the download filename, the copy toast, and closing the dialog. It does not test that a generated backup code can be used to complete login when 2FA is required, nor that it can be used to disable 2FA. The TODO at line 12 explicitly acknowledges this. Security-critical one-time-code behavior should have success and rejection e2e coverage.

title: Clipboard write failure is reported as success
body: The copy handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` without awaiting or catching its promise, and immediately calls `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")`. Clipboard access can fail due to permissions or document focus, so users can be told the codes were copied when they were not, and an unhandled promise rejection can appear in the console. Await the write and only show success if it resolves.

title: Backup code login bypasses password when a totpCode is also supplied
body: The password verification block at line 121 only runs when `credentials.totpCode` is falsy. The new backup-code branch at line 131 is chosen whenever `credentials.backupCode` is present, and it never verifies the password itself. A caller can therefore authenticate with `email`, a valid `backupCode`, and any non-empty `totpCode` (for example `000000`): the truthy `totpCode` skips password verification, then the backup code is validated and authorize returns the user. A stolen/leaked backup code alone becomes sufficient to sign in, defeating two-factor protection.

title: Backup code single-use consumption is not atomic
body: The code reads `user.backupCodes`, validates the submitted code with `indexOf`, and then later writes the whole array back with the matched index set to `null`. There is no transaction or conditional update. Two concurrent requests using the same backup code can both pass validation before either write happens, so both sessions are authorized. Requests using different backup codes can also lose updates because each writes a stale array, leaving an already-used code active. The one-time-code guarantee should be enforced with an atomic/conditional update.

title: First 2FA enable test does not close the new backup-code screen before asserting state
body: `handleEnable` now leaves the modal on the new `DisplayBackupCodes` screen and does not call `onEnable` until the `backup-codes-close` button is clicked. This test enters the OTP and immediately asserts the two-factor switch is checked, so it checks state before the parent is notified/refetched. The second test was updated to click `backup-codes-close` and assert `data-state="checked"`; this test should do the same. As written it either fails or passes due to the already-noted unreliable `isChecked()` assertion.

title: Continue from QR screen submits an empty TOTP code
body: The `goto-otp-screen` button has `type="submit"` inside the `Form` whose submit handler is `handleEnable`, and its `onClick` only calls `setStep(SetupStep.EnterTotpCode)` without calling `preventDefault`. Clicking "Continue" on the QR step therefore immediately invokes `handleEnable` before the user has entered a TOTP code, causing an API request with an empty/missing code and an incorrect-code error on the next screen. This should be `type="button"` or the click handler should call `e.preventDefault()`.

title: Closing the backup-code dialog via X/backdrop skips onEnable
body: After 2FA is enabled, `onEnable` is only invoked by the `backup-codes-close` button. The `Dialog` can also be closed with its X button, backdrop, or Escape, which only uses `onOpenChange`. If the user closes the backup-code screen through one of those paths instead of clicking "Close", `onEnable` never runs, so the parent settings page can remain in the pre-enable state even though 2FA is already enabled in the database. Either call `onEnable` immediately after successful enable or ensure every close path from the final screen invokes it.

title: Backup codes are consumed non-atomically
body: The backup code is checked with `backupCodes.indexOf(...)` on the selected array, then a separate Prisma update re-encrypts and stores the modified array. There is no transaction, conditional update, or deletion of the specific code in the database. If the same valid backup code is submitted in concurrent login requests before one request updates the stored codes, both requests can pass the `indexOf` check and both can be authorized, breaking the one-time-use guarantee for backup codes.

title: No e2e coverage for backup-code login or disable
body: The added test only checks download, copy, and close on the backup-code screen after enabling 2FA. The central security-sensitive paths introduced by this PR — logging in with a backup code, disabling 2FA with a backup code, and ensuring a used backup code cannot be reused — are not tested. The TODO at line 12 acknowledges this gap, but these paths are currently where regressions would go unnoticed.

title: Password visibility toggle is no longer keyboard accessible
body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the show/hide password button removes it from the keyboard tab order. Keyboard and assistive-technology users can no longer focus or activate the toggle, while mouse users are unaffected. Unless there is an alternative accessible control for this action, this is an accessibility regression and should be reverted or given an accessible keyboard handler.

title: Unguarded access to first destination calendar crashes when no destination calendar is set
body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so it is `undefined` when the event has no destination calendar. The next line then accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. Previously this used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. Any booking with a Google Meet location and no destination calendar will throw a TypeError and fail event creation instead of falling back to Cal Video.

title: Office365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar for every host
body: `createEvent` now runs once per host/credential through `EventManager`, but this method still selects `event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId`. It ignores the credential whose calendar is being created. With a collective event that has multiple hosts using Office365, every Office365 host will get an event created in the first host's selected calendar rather than in their own. The same first-element-only pattern exists in Lark and BaseCalendarService, so those integrations are also broken for multi-host collective events.

title: updateLocation creates calendar references without externalCalendarId or credentialId
body: `referencesToCreate` now reads `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` does not return either field. For calendar updates (`updateAllCalendarEvents`), the resulting reference is stored with `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId` undefined. Later cancellations/reschedules cannot target the correct calendar credential and may fall back to deleting through every calendar credential or fail.

title: Only the first old calendar reference is deleted when rescheduling multi-host events
body: When `newBookingId` is provided, the cleanup path still does `booking.references.find(...)` instead of `filter(...)`. A collective booking now has multiple `_calendar` references, one for each host. On reschedule, only the first old calendar event is deleted; the other hosts keep the old event on their calendars.

title: Recurring cancellation only deletes the first calendar reference for each occurrence
body: Inside the recurring/all-remaining branch, `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` selects only one calendar reference per updated booking. For a multi-host collective recurring booking, each occurrence has multiple calendar references. Cancelling the series will remove only the first host's event from each future occurrence and leave the other hosts' events in their calendars.

title: Google update/delete fallback no longer resolves the destination calendar when externalCalendarId is absent
body: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it looks for an externalId of null/undefined and returns undefined. Previously the fallback used the single `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Legacy booking references without `externalCalendarId` will therefore update with an undefined calendarId (or delete from primary rather than the selected calendar). The same issue appears in `deleteEvent` below.

title: Team destination calendars are silently discarded when evt.destinationCalendar is null
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op for `null`. In a collective event where the organizer has no destination calendar but the hosts do, none of the host destination calendars are attached to the event, so no calendar events are created for those hosts.

title: Google organizer email uses the first destination calendar for every credential
body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is always the first item in `destinationCalendar`, while `selectedCalendar` is correctly found by `credentialId`. When creating the event for the second/third host credential, the organizer attendee email is still set to the first host's `externalId`. This makes the Google Calendar event organizer incorrect for every host except the first, which can affect ownership, notifications, and invitation behavior.

title: Organization slug/requestedSlug conditions are inverted
body: The previous code set `slug` on the organization when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` was false, and stored `requestedSlug` in metadata when billing was enabled. This change swaps that behavior: billing-enabled environments now set `slug` directly and no longer store `requestedSlug`, while non-billing environments create the organization without a slug. This is an unrelated behavior change that can break organization creation/subdomain handling depending on the deployment configuration.

title: Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty
body: `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` produces an empty array when no destination calendar is set, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined. The next line dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`, throwing a TypeError before the intended fallback to Daily can run. Previously `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` was safely undefined. Use optional chaining, e.g. `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

title: updateLocation creates booking references without externalCalendarId or credentialId
body: `referencesToCreate` now reads `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` does not return either field (unlike `createEvent`). After editing a location, the newly created calendar `BookingReference` rows will have null `externalCalendarId` and null `credentialId`. Later cancellation/reschedule/update logic cannot identify the external calendar or credential, so it may target the wrong calendar or fail to delete/update the right event. Either `updateEvent` should return these fields, or `updateLocation` should derive them from the calendar reference being updated.

title: Google updateEvent fallback calendar lookup always misses
body: When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which compares each calendar's externalId against null/undefined and returns undefined. `calendar.events.update` is then called with an undefined calendarId instead of the previous behavior of using `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. The same broken pattern appears in `deleteEvent` around line 317. Legacy bookings or references without `externalCalendarId` will fail to update/delete Google Calendar events.

title: Google Meet description patch uses undefined calendarId when no selected calendar
body: `calendar.events.insert` uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the subsequent `calendar.events.patch` uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without that fallback. When no destination in the array matches the current credentialId, `selectedCalendar` is undefined; the insert proceeds against primary, but the patch that adds the hangout link fails because the calendarId is undefined. Use the same fallback in both calls.

title: Office365 createEvent always targets the first destination calendar
body: Even though EventManager now iterates all destination calendars and calls `createEvent` once per credential, Office365 still destructures only the first element of `event.destinationCalendar` and ignores the supplied credentialId. For a collective event with multiple hosts, every Office365 invocation targets the same first host calendar, causing duplicate events in that calendar and no event in the other hosts' Office365 calendars. The service must select the destination whose credentialId matches the current credential, similar to GoogleCalendarService. LarkCalendarService and BaseCalendarService have the same first-element-only behavior.

title: Team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destinationCalendar
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer user has a destination calendar. The team calendars are then added with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a no-op on null. If the organizer has no destination calendar but the other collective hosts do, all collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are lost and EventManager falls back to the organizer's first connected calendar rather than creating events in the hosts' selected calendars. Initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` to an array before pushing or assign the combined array explicitly.

title: Confirmed collective bookings only schedule the first destination calendar
body: When a booking requiring confirmation is later confirmed, this handler rebuilds `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar` (a single Prisma relation) or the confirming user's default. The multi-host `teamDestinationCalendars` assembled at initial booking time are not persisted or reconstructed here. `handleConfirmation`/EventManager therefore creates calendar events only for the first destination, not for all hosts of a collective event.

title: Paid collective bookings schedule only the first destination calendar
body: Both `getBooking` and `handlePaymentSuccess` build `evt.destinationCalendar` from the booking's single `destinationCalendar` or the user default. For a paid collective event, the multi-host destination calendars assembled in `handleNewBooking` are not available here and are not stored on the booking. When payment succeeds and `EventManager.create` runs, only the first/primary calendar receives the event; other hosts are not scheduled. The same issue exists in `paypal-webhook.ts`.

title: Recurring cancellation still deletes only one organizer calendar reference
body: Inside the new loop over `bookingCalendarReference`, the recurring/allRemaining branch ignores the current reference's `credentialId` and instead maps over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` (the organizer's own credentials). For each updated booking it then calls `references.find(...)`, which returns only the first calendar reference. For a collective recurring booking with multiple host calendars, this repeats deletion of the first organizer-visible event and never deletes events belonging to the other host references. It should iterate all calendar references and use each reference's credential/externalCalendarId.

title: Organization creation slug condition is inverted
body: The diff changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, and similarly changes `requestedSlug` in the metadata. This is the opposite of the previous logic and is unrelated to the destinationCalendar change. With billing disabled, new organizations no longer receive a slug, likely breaking org creation/URLs; with billing enabled, slug is now set when it was previously withheld in favor of requestedSlug. Revert this condition unless there is a separate intentional billing change.

title: All Google calendar events use the first destination as organizer
body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is always the first element of `event.destinationCalendar`, and its externalId is used as the organizer email for every create/update invocation. When EventManager iterates the other host destination calendars with different credentialIds, the event is inserted into another host's calendar but the organizer attendee is still set to the first host's externalId. This can set the wrong organizer/permissions or cause Google to reject the event. The organizer email should correspond to the destination/credential being processed.

title: Google Meet fallback crashes when there is no destinationCalendar
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` can be `null` or `[]`, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar` becomes `undefined` after destructuring. The following condition dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` unconditionally. Any booking that uses Google Meet but has no destination calendar will throw a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video.

title: Collective host destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op on `null`, so the host calendars collected in `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded. In a collective event where the organizer has no calendar but hosts do, the hosts still do not get calendar invites.

title: Office365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
body: `createEvent` still selects only the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar` and ignores the `credentialId` passed by EventManager. For multiple hosts, EventManager calls this once per destination credential, but each call creates the event in the first host's calendar while the booking reference records another host's `externalCalendarId`. This creates events in the wrong calendar and causes later update/delete operations to target a calendar that does not contain the event.

title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
body: `createEvent` destructures only the first `event.destinationCalendar` entry and uses its `externalId` as the calendar ID. With multiple host destination calendars, every per-host `createEvent` call will attempt to create the event in the first host's calendar, while the resulting booking reference stores the other host's `externalCalendarId`. This breaks multi-host calendar creation and later update/delete for Lark.

title: updateEvent results omit externalId and credentialId required by updateLocation
body: `EventManager.updateLocation` now builds booking references from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent`'s return object does not set either field. Previously those references were populated from `evt.destinationCalendar`. After this change, location updates create booking references with missing `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId`, so later updates/cancellations cannot locate the correct calendar event.

title: Organization slug condition was inverted
body: The old code included `slug` on the organization when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` was false via `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`. The new code uses `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, so the `slug` is set when billing is enabled and omitted when billing is disabled. This reverses the previous behavior and can break organization creation/subdomain setup depending on the billing flag.

title: Google update/delete fallback cannot select a calendar from destinationCalendar array
body: When `externalCalendarId` is null, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` fall back to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Because the predicate compares against `null`, it never matches. `updateEvent` then passes `undefined` as `calendarId`, causing the update to fail; `deleteEvent` silently falls back to `primary`, which can delete from the wrong calendar.

title: Google organizer email uses first host calendar for all created events
body: For a multi-host collective, each Google credential creates an event on that credential's selected calendar, but the organizer attendee email is always set to `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (the first destination calendar). For the second and subsequent hosts, the organizer email belongs to another user's calendar, which can cause Google Calendar API to reject the insert or record the wrong organizer.

title: CalDAV createEvent only filters to the first destination calendar
body: `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` destructures only the first destination calendar and uses its `externalId` to filter `listCalendars` results. With multiple destination calendars/credentials, every per-host creation targets the first host's calendar even though the booking reference records another host's external calendar. Later update/delete can therefore reference a calendar that does not contain the created event.

title: Recurring cancellation branch is duplicated for every calendar reference
body: The new loop over `bookingCalendarReference` still contains the old `allRemainingBookings` recurring deletion block inside it. That block does not use the current `reference`; it iterates all of `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and deletes the first calendar reference of each updated booking. With multiple calendar references, the same deletion operations are scheduled once per reference, and host calendar events that are not in the organizer credentials are not deleted correctly.

title: No test covers multiple host destination calendars
body: Only an existing webhook expectation was changed from `null` to `[]`; there is no automated test that creates a collective event with multiple hosts/calendars and verifies that each host's calendar receives, updates, and cancels the correct event. The core behavior of this PR is currently unverified.

title: SalesforceCalendarService uses prisma without importing it
body: The new token-refresh block calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file does not import `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma` (unlike the other services modified in this PR). This will fail TypeScript type-checking/build or throw a runtime ReferenceError when `getClient` runs. Add the missing import.

title: Google Calendar refresh persists the Zod SafeParse wrapper as the credential key
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `SafeParseReturnType` object such as `{ success: true, data: {...} }`, not the parsed token data. In `refreshAccessToken`, this value is assigned to `key` and then written to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. After the first refresh, the stored credential is the wrapper rather than the Google credential, so the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails and the integration breaks. Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` or change the helper to return the parsed data before persisting.

title: Webhook looks up app metadata by app.slug, but appStoreMetadata is usually keyed by directory name
body: `appStoreMetadata` is generated from app-store directories, and its keys are directory names such as `googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`, and `office365video`; these often differ from `App.slug` values such as `google-calendar`, `zoom`, and `msteams`. Indexing `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` will return undefined for many existing apps and incorrectly return 404 even though the app exists. Look up the metadata by iterating values and matching `metadata.slug === app.slug`, or use a helper like `getAppFromSlug`.

title: Synced-token schema does not validate or preserve expiry fields and inserts a fake refresh_token
body: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses `[z.string().toString()]` as a computed key, which is just a literal string property rather than a record, so it does not validate or preserve expiry-related fields. Because `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, synced responses parse down to only `access_token` (plus the literal keys). The code then sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when missing. Downstream callers such as Zoom and Webex then compute `Date.now() + undefined` and store `NaN` expiry values, or lose the real refresh token, corrupting credentials. Define a real schema for the sync response and preserve the provider-required fields.

title: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, breaking axios-shaped refresh callers
body: When sync is enabled, this helper returns the raw `fetch` `Response` from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` without parsing it. Existing refresh functions return different shapes: Google returns an Axios-like response with `.data`, and Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM return Axios responses with `.data`. Those callers then access `res.data` or `tokenInfo.data` and throw because a `Response` has no `.data`. The helper also does not check `response.ok`. Parse/standardize the response before returning, or change all callers to handle a `Response` consistently.

title: Refreshed Salesforce token is persisted but not used for the current connection
body: After fetching and parsing `accessTokenJson` and updating the database, the returned `jsforce.Connection` is constructed with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token` and `instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url` rather than the newly parsed values. The current calendar/video call still uses the old credential, so the refresh may not prevent failures on this call. This refresh also happens every time `getClient` runs, regardless of whether the token is still valid.

title: Zoho Bigin sends credential ID instead of user ID to credential sync
body: `refreshOAuthTokens`'s third parameter is documented and used as `userId`, and it is sent as `calcomUserId` in the sync request. Here the code passes `credentialId`, which is the database `Credential.id`, not `credential.userId`. When credential sync is enabled, the self-hosted endpoint receives the wrong user identifier and may associate refreshed tokens with the wrong account or fail lookup. Pass the actual user ID through `refreshAccessToken`.

title: Zoom refresh sends appSlug 'zoomvideo' instead of 'zoom'
body: The Zoom app is created and installed with `appId: "zoom"` and installed path slug `"zoom"` elsewhere in this package, but `refreshOAuthTokens` is called with `"zoomvideo"`, which is the directory name. The credential-sync endpoint uses this value to identify the app, so self-hosters may receive or look up an unknown `appSlug`. Pass `"zoom"` instead.

title: Synced credentials remain invalid if previously marked invalid
body: When updating an existing credential, the handler only updates `key`. If that credential was previously flagged `invalid: true` (for example after an `invalid_grant`), it remains invalid and is likely skipped by calendar/video adapters even after receiving valid credentials from the webhook. Set `invalid: false` when syncing a new valid key.

title: Salesforce token refresh bypasses CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT
body: Unlike the other modified app adapters, `getClient` calls `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` directly instead of going through `refreshOAuthTokens`. When app-credential sharing and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are configured, Salesforce still refreshes with local Cal.com app keys, defeating the self-hosted source-of-truth behavior and failing if only synced credentials are available. Route the refresh through `refreshOAuthTokens` like the other integrations.

title: findFirst-then-create can create duplicate credentials under concurrent webhooks
body: The endpoint finds an existing credential and then either updates the first match or creates a new row. This sequence is not atomic. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both see no existing credential and both insert, creating duplicates; later updates will only affect one row. Add a unique constraint on `(userId, appId)` for user credentials and use an upsert or transaction.

title: Webhook endpoint accepts any HTTP method and returns unhandled validation errors
body: The handler does not check `req.method`, and it calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`. A GET or a malformed body reaches Zod and throws, producing a generic 500 instead of a client-facing 400, and non-POST requests can still trigger DB lookups. Restrict the handler to POST and use `safeParse` with an explicit 400 response.

title: Salesforce refresh uses undefined prisma
body: The newly added refresh block calls `prisma.credential.update` but this file never imports `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. When this code runs, it will throw `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined`, and the project should also fail type-checking. Add the missing import.

title: Google refresh stores Zod SafeParse result instead of token data
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the whole `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), but here `key` is that wrapper and is written to the credential directly. After a successful Google refresh, the DB key becomes `{ success: true, data: { ...tokens } }`; subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in the constructor fails, breaking the Google Calendar integration. Use `refreshTokenResponse.data` here.

title: Minimum token schema does not validate or retain expiry fields
body: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` both resolve to the same string (`[object Object]`), so the schema effectively only requires `access_token` and drops or fails to validate all other token fields. When credential sharing is enabled, any caller using this branch parses a token response into essentially `{ access_token }`, losing `expires_in`/`expiry_date`, `instance_url`, and other fields. The intended numeric expiry validation is never performed.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with string "refresh_token"
body: When a parsed refresh response does not include `refresh_token`, this mutates `data.refresh_token` to the literal text `"refresh_token"`. Callers like Office365 and Zoom then persist that value over the user's real refresh token, so later refreshes fail. Do not synthesize a placeholder; preserve the existing credential refresh token in the caller.

title: Sync token refresh returns an unnormalized Response
body: In sync mode this returns the raw `fetch` `Response`. Existing callers expect provider/axios-shaped values: Google reads `res.data.access_token`, HubSpot expects `.expiresIn`, and Zoho/Bigin expect `tokenInfo.data`. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, those code paths get `undefined` or missing properties and fail. Parse the JSON and return a consistent shape such as `{ data }`, or update every caller to consume `Response`.

title: Credential sync endpoint receives no authentication
body: The `fetch` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body. There is no secret, signature, or API key. Anyone who can reach the sync endpoint can request access tokens for arbitrary Cal.com user IDs. Since this endpoint returns third-party credentials, add an authenticated header/shared secret and enforce HTTPS.

title: Zoho Bigin sends credential.id as calcomUserId
body: `refreshOAuthTokens`'s third argument is supposed to be the Cal.com user ID, but this call passes `credentialId` (the credential row ID). When credential sharing is enabled, the parent app receives the DB credential ID as `calcomUserId` and may update the wrong user or fail to find the user. Pass `credential.userId` through to `refreshAccessToken`.

title: Salesforce token parsing switches on global sharing flag despite fetching Salesforce directly
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)` chooses the minimal schema whenever `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is set, even though this method always calls `login.salesforce.com` directly and never uses `refreshOAuthTokens`. Enabling credential sharing therefore makes Salesforce token parsing drop required fields such as `instance_url`, `id`, `issued_at`, `signature`, `scope`, and `token_type`; the stored DB key becomes incomplete and future connections can break.

title: Refreshed Salesforce token is not used for the connection
body: The method fetches and parses a new access token, but `new jsforce.Connection(...)` is created with `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.refresh_token`, not the newly parsed token. The service instance therefore starts with the old/expired access token, causing avoidable 401s or reliance on jsforce's own auto-refresh. Use the new access token and instance URL from the refresh response.

title: Credential sync can create duplicate credentials under concurrent requests
body: The handler does `findFirst` and then either `update` or `create` in separate queries. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both miss the existing row and insert duplicates. There is also no deterministic choice if multiple rows exist. Use a transaction plus a unique constraint/upsert keyed by `(userId, appId, type)`.

title: Sync update does not mark credential valid again
body: When updating an existing credential, only `key` is changed. If that credential was previously marked `invalid: true` (for example after an invalid_grant failure), it remains invalid after syncing fresh credentials and may be skipped by integrations. The update should set `invalid: false` to reflect the new source-of-truth credential.

title: Office 365 video sync refresh can overwrite stored credential with an incomplete token
body: When sync mode returns the documented generic payload (`access_token` plus expiry date), `responseBody.expires_in` is undefined, so `expiry_date` is set to `Date.now()` (immediately expired), and the whole `responseBody` is stored as the key. The existing `refresh_token`, `token_type`, `scope`, and `email` are not preserved, so later refreshes fail. This integration needs to merge the sync response into the existing credential instead of replacing it.

title: Invalid webhook body causes unhandled ZodError
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` is not wrapped in try/catch and no method check is performed. A POST with a malformed body, or a GET where `req.body` is absent, throws a `ZodError`, producing a generic 500 instead of a controlled 400. Use `safeParse` and explicitly reject non-POST methods.

title: AES-256 key generation command yields 24 bytes, not 32
body: The comment says the key must be 32 bytes for AES-256 and suggests `openssl rand -base64 24`. Base64-decoding 24 input bytes yields a 24-byte key, not 32. Users following this instruction will configure an invalid/weak key. Suggest `openssl rand -base64 32` or `openssl rand -hex 32`.

title: No tests for credential sync webhook or token refresh helpers
body: The PR adds a security-sensitive webhook, encryption/decryption path, and shared OAuth refresh/parsing helpers used by many integrations. The checklist explicitly says no tests were added. Given the parser shape mismatches and data-loss issues, tests for success, invalid secret, malformed payload, existing/update, and sync vs local refresh would catch regressions.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token"
body: When a token response omits refresh_token (the credential-sync endpoint is explicitly described as returning only access token and expiry), this line writes the literal string "refresh_token" into the parsed data. Callers then persist that data (e.g. Office365CalendarService and ZoomVideoApiAdapter) and later use it as the OAuth refresh token, so subsequent refreshes fail with an invalid grant. The existing stored refresh token should be preserved, or the field should be required, not fabricated.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema does not validate an expiry field
body: The computed key `[z.string().toString()]` does not create a dynamic schema for arbitrary numeric fields; it evaluates to a single literal property name (for example `[object Object]`). Since Zod object schemas ignore unknown keys by default, the only real requirement is `access_token`. A credential-sync response with no expiry/expires_in passes validation, and downstream code such as ZoomVideoApiAdapter computes `Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)`, storing NaN as the expiry date. The schema must explicitly validate the actual expected expiration field.

title: Credential-sync mode returns a raw fetch Response, breaking callers
body: When sync is enabled this returns the native `fetch` `Response`. Original refresh functions return different shapes across callers: Google expects `res?.data`, HubSpot returns a token object and callers read `.expiresIn`, Zoho Bigin/ZohoCRM use Axios and callers read `.data`, while Office 365/Webex callers expect a Response and parse it. In sync mode Bigin and ZohoCRM crash at `tokenInfo.data`, HubSpot persists a Response instead of token fields, and Google crashes at `token.access_token`. The helper needs a normalized return contract or each caller must handle the sync-response format explicitly.

title: Bigin passes credential id instead of user id to credential-sync endpoint
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` receives `credentialId` as its third argument, but that parameter is `userId` and is sent to the self-hosted sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. The external app store therefore receives the Cal.com database credential id rather than the user id, so it may attach tokens to the wrong user or fail to match an account. The function needs access to `credential.userId` here.

title: Zoom refresh sends wrong appSlug
body: The Zoom app id/slug is `zoom` everywhere else in this package (callback uses `appId: "zoom"` and redirects to `slug: "zoom"`), but credential-sync mode sends `appSlug: "zoomvideo"`. A self-hosted app store keyed by the actual Cal.com app slug will not match the Zoom integration.

title: Salesforce connection is built with the stale pre-refresh access token
body: The newly fetched `accessTokenParsed.data` is persisted, but the returned `jsforce.Connection` is constructed with `credentialKey.access_token` (the old value) and `credentialKey.instance_url`. If the token was refreshed because it had expired, the first API calls made with this connection still use the expired token. The connection should be built from the refreshed token response fields.

title: Salesforce refresh token flow runs on every CalendarService construction
body: `getClient` performs an OAuth refresh request and credential update every time a SalesforceCalendarService instance is created, regardless of whether the stored token is still valid. This adds an external API call and database write for each booking operation and may hit Salesforce rate limits. It should refresh only when the token is near or past expiry, or use jsforce's built-in refresh behavior.

title: Credential find-first then create/update can create duplicates
body: The endpoint looks up an existing credential with `findFirst` and then either updates or creates it. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both observe no existing row and both insert, leaving duplicate credentials. Since credential selection elsewhere may rely on a single row per user/app, this can cause ambiguity. The operation should be serialized under a transaction/unique constraint or the insert should be idempotent.

title: Invalid webhook body returns an unhandled 500
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError for malformed request bodies and there is no try/catch around it. A caller with the correct webhook secret can trigger a 500 and default error page instead of a controlled 400 validation response. Use `safeParse` and return the validation error.

title: Encryption key generation command does not produce a 32-byte key
body: The comment says CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY must be 32 bytes for AES256, but suggests `openssl rand -base64 24`. That command encodes 24 random bytes as a 32-character base64 string; if decoded for use as the AES key it is only 24 bytes, and if used directly as a string the comment is still misleading. Use `openssl rand -base64 32` (which encodes a 32-byte key) instead.

title: Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId))`, so a user must be both an admin and an owner to pass. Users who are only one of those roles are rejected with FORBIDDEN unless they are also the organizer or an attendee. This contradicts the variable name and likely intent, and prevents authorized team members from using the feature.

title: Calendar update is performed with caller's credentials, not the booking organizer's
body: The handler permits attendees and team admins/owners to call this endpoint, but then builds `EventManager` from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. For a non-organizer caller, this uses the caller's credentials to update the calendar event, even though the booking's user credentials were already fetched. External organizer calendar updates can fail or act in the wrong calendar context, leaving external calendars inconsistent.

title: Server-side filtering does not deduplicate or normalize emails
body: `uniqueGuests` filters `guests` with raw, case-sensitive string comparisons and does not deduplicate the input. A direct tRPC client can send duplicate addresses or uppercase variants that bypass existing-attendee and `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` checks because the blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is not. Duplicate emails can be inserted as duplicate attendee rows, or cause a database error if a uniqueness constraint exists.

title: Bookings without a user cause findFirstOrThrow to query user id 0
body: `organizer` is looked up with `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is null, this queries user ID 0 and throws an internal error. The UI adds the action for upcoming bookings and the booking list type models `user` as nullable, so such bookings can reach this handler and fail unexpectedly.

title: Add-guests emails ignore event type email disable settings
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept or check `eventTypeMetadata`, `eventTypeDisableHostEmail`, or `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`, unlike the existing scheduled/location-change email helpers. It unconditionally sends organizer and attendee notification emails, so event types that disabled standard host or attendee emails will still send these emails after guests are added.

title: Error fallback toast is unreachable
body: `message` is a template literal that always contains at least the interpolated values, so when `err.data?.code` is undefined it becomes `"undefined: ..."`, which is truthy. As a result, `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` never uses the fallback and can display a confusing prefix to the user.

title: Any attendee can add guests to a booking
body: The handler grants permission to any user whose email appears in `booking.attendees` via `isAttendee`. This exposes the tRPC mutation to every attendee, allowing them to add arbitrary emails to the booking without organizer approval. New attendees may receive calendar invitations and meeting details. Unless attendee self-service is an explicit requirement, restrict this mutation to the organizer or team admins/owners.

title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This means a team admin who is not an owner, or an owner who is not an admin, is denied. The variable name and intended behavior indicate an OR condition; use `||` or separate the two permission checks.

title: Calendar update uses caller credentials instead of organizer's
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` returns the authenticated caller's credentials, but the event belongs to `booking.user` (the organizer). The `EventManager` is then pointed at the organizer's destination calendar via `evt.destinationCalendar`. If the caller is not the organizer, this mismatch can make `updateCalendarAttendees` fail or attempt to update the wrong account's calendar. Use the booking organizer's credentials (e.g., `booking.user.credentials`) or load credentials for the organizer.

title: Blacklisted email comparison is case-sensitive
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased before comparison, but incoming `guest` values are not normalized. An email such as `Blocked@example.com` can bypass a blacklist entry of `blocked@example.com` and be added to the booking. Normalize incoming guests with `.toLowerCase()` before comparing, or better normalize in the schema/handler before all validation.

title: Incoming duplicate guests are not deduplicated server-side
body: `uniqueGuests` filters incoming guests only against existing `booking.attendees` and the blacklist; it does not deduplicate the incoming `guests` array. The server schema `z.array(z.string().email())` does not enforce uniqueness, so a caller can pass the same email twice with different casing and `createMany` will insert duplicate attendee records for the same booking, causing duplicate calendar invites and inconsistent attendee data. Deduplicate case-insensitively on the server before insertion.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email disable settings
body: Other email helpers in this file respect `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`, but `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends organizer and attendee emails unconditionally. Users who disabled standard host or attendee emails for an event type will still receive these add-guests notifications, violating their email preferences. Pass `eventTypeMetadata` to this function and check the relevant disable flags before sending.

title: No tests cover the new addGuests mutation
body: This new tRPC mutation introduces authorization rules, email blacklisting, deduplication concerns, and external calendar/email side effects, but no tests are added. Missing coverage makes it easy for permission bypasses and duplicate-handling regressions to go unnoticed. Add tests for authorized and unauthorized callers, duplicate/blacklisted emails, and missing bookings.

title: Team admin/owner check requires both admin and owner roles
body: The code computes `isTeamAdminOrOwner` as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. That makes the action available only to users who are both a team admin and a team owner, which is normally impossible. A user who is only an admin or only an owner is denied, despite the variable name and the UI exposing the action to `booking.isUserTeamAdminOrOwner`. This should use `||`.

title: Guest email comparisons are case-sensitive, bypassing blacklist and duplicate checks
body: `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is split and lowercased, but each `guest` is compared as supplied. A guest address such as `User@Example.com` will bypass `user@example.com`. In addition, the comparison against existing `booking.attendees` is case-sensitive, so the same email with different case can be added more than once. Normalize guest emails before filtering and deduplicating.

title: Unbounded and duplicate guest list accepted at API
body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` accepts `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()` and no uniqueness constraint. A direct tRPC caller can submit an arbitrarily large list, causing a large `createMany`, many external calendar API updates, and many invitation emails in one request. Add a sane maximum and reject duplicate entries at the schema or handler level.

title: No status or end-time check: guests can be added to past bookings
body: The handler only checks that the booking exists and that the caller has some role; it never rejects past bookings or disallowed statuses. The UI also includes the add-guests action under edit for past confirmed bookings (`apps/web/components/booking/BookingListItem.tsx` line 554). This allows new invitations and external calendar updates for events that have already ended. Reject bookings whose end time has passed and disallowed statuses.

title: Database commit before external calendar update leaves unretryable partial state
body: The new attendees are written to Postgres at line 92 before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` on line 165. That external call is not covered by a try/catch or transaction, so if it fails the request errors while the new attendees remain. Retrying then sees them as already existing (`uniqueGuests.length === 0`) and returns `BAD_REQUEST`, so the booking can be left permanently out of sync unless rows are manually removed. Add compensation handling or perform/validate the calendar update before committing, and make retries idempotent.

title: External calendar update uses caller credentials instead of booking organizer credentials
body: `EventManager` is constructed with `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. Since attendees and team admins/owners are allowed to call this handler, the credentials belong to the caller, not the owner of the booking/destination calendar. For such callers the calendar event is likely not updated or an update is attempted against the wrong account. The handler even fetches `booking.user.credentials` but never uses them. Use the booking organizer's credentials for `EventManager`.

title: New add-guests emails ignore event-type email suppression settings
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not receive or check `eventTypeMetadata` and always sends organizer, team-member, and attendee emails. Other comparable functions (`sendLocationChangeEmails`, `sendScheduledEmails`) honor `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`. As a result, event types configured to disable host or attendee emails will still emit these notifications when guests are added.

title: DeleteMany retryCount branch is not scoped to SMS
body: This handler is the SMS workflow scheduler, and the first OR branch filters `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, but the second OR branch only requires `retryCount > 1`. Because `WorkflowReminder` is shared by EMAIL/SMS/WHATSAPP methods, any non-SMS reminder whose `retryCount` becomes > 1 (now or in future code paths) will be deleted by this SMS cron. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retryCount branch or otherwise constrain the delete to SMS reminders.

title: Retry count update loses attempts under concurrent cron runs
body: The update writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value loaded by `findMany` earlier in the handler. If two cron invocations process the same reminder simultaneously, both can read the same retryCount and both write the same incremented value, so two failed attempts count as one. This undermines the delete-after-two-failures logic and can allow extra scheduling attempts. Use an atomic Prisma `increment: 1` or an `updateMany` guarded by the expected retryCount.

title: Catch increments retryCount for errors unrelated to SMS scheduling
body: The `try` block wraps message/template building, DB lookups, metadata parsing, and the Twilio call. The `catch` at line 189 increments `retryCount` for any of those failures. A persistent error before `twilio.scheduleSMS` is ever called, such as invalid booking metadata or a failing `bookingMetadataSchema.parse`, therefore counts as an SMS scheduling failure, and after two runs the reminder is deleted even though no SMS was attempted. Scope retry counting to the actual `scheduleSMS` call or handle pre-scheduling errors separately.

title: No tests for retry limit and deletion behavior
body: This PR adds a retry counter, increments it in the false-result and catch paths, and changes `deleteMany` to prune reminders with `retryCount > 1`, but no tests are added. The behavior needs coverage for one failure, two failures, successful scheduling after a failure, and non-SMS reminders so the retry/delete semantics do not regress.

title: Catch block treats every processing error as an SMS scheduling failure
body: The new catch block increments retryCount for any error thrown anywhere in the large try block (lines 74-187), not only for twilio.scheduleSMS. This includes template rendering, getBookerBaseUrl, prisma.profile.findFirst, and bookingMetadataSchema.parse failures. A persistent non-scheduling error will therefore increment retryCount on each run and after retryCount reaches 2 the reminder is deleted by the deleteMany query, even though the SMS was never attempted. Scope the retryCount increment to scheduleSMS failures or otherwise distinguish scheduling failures from message-preparation/DB errors.

title: deleteMany retryCount branch can delete non-SMS workflow reminders
body: The OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` is not constrained by `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` or by `scheduled: false`. This handler is the SMS scheduling cron, but WorkflowReminder is shared by email and WhatsApp workflows, and retryCount is defined on the base model. Once any non-SMS reminder has retryCount > 1, this cron deletes it, causing cross-method data loss. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and likely `scheduled: false` to this branch.

title: retryCount updates are read-modify-write and can lose concurrent failures
body: Both failure updates set `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read when the reminders were loaded. If two cron invocations process the same unscheduled reminder concurrently, both can read the same retryCount and write the same value, so a failure is not recorded. Because deletion uses `retryCount > 1`, the reminder may never reach the deletion threshold and can continue being retried indefinitely. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` in both updates or otherwise serialize the update.

title: No tests for new retry/delete behavior
body: The PR adds a retry count and a deletion threshold but includes no tests. Important cases are untested: scheduleSMS returning false or throwing increments retryCount, non-scheduling errors do not count as scheduling failures, retryCount > 1 deletion is scoped to SMS, and concurrent updates do not lose increments. Add unit/integration tests for this cron handler.

title: Retry-count delete branch can delete non-SMS reminders
body: The new second OR branch only checks `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`, unlike the first branch which filters `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. `WorkflowReminder` is shared by EMAIL, SMS, and WHATSAPP methods, so any non-SMS reminder with `retryCount > 1` would be deleted by this SMS cron job. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and likely `scheduled: false`) to this branch to prevent deleting unrelated workflow reminders.

title: retryCount increments are not atomic
body: Both update sites use `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` based on the value read earlier by `findMany`. If two cron invocations overlap, they can both read the same value and write the same value, losing an increment. This can defeat the delete-after-two-failures logic and may allow more retries or duplicate Twilio schedule calls than intended. Use an atomic `increment: 1` update instead.

title: All errors count as SMS scheduling failures
body: The try block includes reminder preparation work such as `getBookerBaseUrl` (line 119) and `bookingMetadataSchema.parse` (line 134) before Twilio is called. The catch at line 190 increments `retryCount` for any error in that block. As a result, a record with malformed booking metadata can throw during parsing each run, reach retryCount 2, and then be deleted at the start of a later run even though no SMS scheduling was ever attempted and the event is still upcoming. Only `twilio.scheduleSMS` failures should count toward this deletion limit, or preparation errors should be handled separately.

title: Prisma.sql object comparison fails for service-built nested SQL
body: The service builds this team condition with `conditions.reduce((acc, condition) => Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR (${condition})`)`, so the returned `Prisma.Sql` is composed of multiple nested `Prisma.Sql` fragments. `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)` compares the internal `strings` and `values` arrays, not the rendered SQL text, so the actual and expected structures will differ even though the SQL is semantically equivalent. The same issue affects the org-scope expectation near line 332 and the combined-filter expectation near line 429. The test should compare rendered SQL or explicitly flattened/normalized `strings`/`values`, and should be run to confirm.

title: Public findMany method removed without migrating callers
body: The previous class exposed `findMany(findManyArgs)` for querying `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized`; this PR replaces it with `getBaseConditions()` returning raw `Prisma.Sql`. Only the service and its tests are changed in this diff, so any production code still calling `service.findMany(...)` will fail to compile or run when this is merged. If the service is used outside the test file, keep `findMany` as a thin wrapper or migrate all callers in the same PR.

title: Caching tests removed for raw SQL conditions
body: The old `describe("Caching")` tests verified that repeated calls to `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return cached values and do not rebuild. Those tests are deleted, but the caching logic remains in `insightsBooking.ts` (lines 83-94). Losing this coverage makes it easy to break caching with `Prisma.Sql` fragments without a failing test.

title: Removed public `findMany` method breaks existing callers
body: The diff deletes `InsightsBookingService.findMany` and replaces it with `getBaseConditions`. `findMany` was the method that executed the Prisma query on `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized`, allowing callers to pass `select`, additional `where` clauses, etc. Any code importing this exported service and calling `service.findMany(...)` will fail to compile after this PR. If this change is intentional, callers need to be migrated in the same PR; otherwise keep `findMany` implemented in terms of the new raw conditions or provide a compatibility adapter.

title: `teamId` is optional in public options even when scope is `team`
body: `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` types `teamId` as `number | undefined` for all scopes, but `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema` requires `teamId` for `scope: 'team'`. As a result, callers can write `{ scope: 'team', userId, orgId }` without a TypeScript error; the constructor then fails validation, sets `this.options` to `null`, and `getAuthorizationConditions()` returns `NOTHING_CONDITION`. This silently returns no data rather than surfacing the missing required option. Use a discriminated public type or throw a clear validation error.

title: Caching tests removed without replacement
body: The previous `Caching` describe block tested that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return the same cached result on repeated calls. Those tests were deleted in this PR, but the caching fields and `=== undefined` checks remain in the service. Caching can now regress unnoticed. Replace these tests with updated raw-SQL assertions rather than deleting them.

title: Removal of findMany breaks existing callers
body: The previous public method findMany(findManyArgs) was removed and replaced with getBaseConditions(). Only the service and its integration tests are updated in this PR, so any existing consumer of InsightsBookingService.findMany() will fail TypeScript compilation or, if untyped, throw at runtime. If the raw-SQL conversion is intentional, the same PR should either migrate all call sites or keep a findMany wrapper that builds a raw query from getBaseConditions().

title: Org authorization omits user bookings when org has no child teams
body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition only queries userIdsFromOrg when teamsFromOrg.length > 0. An organization can have accepted members via the org membership itself even when it has no child teams, but in that case the isTeamBooking = false branch is omitted entirely. As a result, an org owner/admin cannot see personal/user-scoped bookings of org members for organizations without child teams. The guard should not depend on teamsFromOrg.length, or the membership query should still run with [options.orgId].

title: Public options type makes invalid team scope calls compile
body: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions declares teamId optional for every scope, whereas the zod schema still requires teamId when scope is 'team'. This means new InsightsBookingService({ scope: 'team', userId, orgId }) now compiles, then safeParse fails in the constructor and the service silently returns NOTHING_CONDITION. This moves a real configuration error from compile time to runtime. The public type should remain a discriminated union or otherwise require teamId for scope 'team'.

title: Org/team raw SQL branches are never executed against the database
body: The team and org authorization tests only assert that the generated Prisma.sql object equals an expected Prisma.sql object. They do not run a query using those conditions, so a SQL syntax error, invalid ANY(array) parameter binding, or incorrect column/table mapping in the org/team OR branches would not be caught. The only end-to-end query test uses user scope. Consider adding a $queryRaw execution for at least one team or org branch where the generated SQL is actually sent to the database.

title: Deleting cache does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
body: The deleteCacheMutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback. Unlike disconnectMutation, it never calls utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate(). The connectedCalendars query is what supplied cacheUpdatedAt, so after a successful delete the UI can continue showing the old cache status and timestamp until some unrelated refetch occurs.

title: dev:cron uses npx tsx but tsx is not a declared dependency
body: The script was changed to 'npx tsx cron-tester.ts', but tsx is not listed in dependencies or devDependencies for this package. npx may download tsx on demand or fail in offline/CI/Yarn PnP environments, making 'yarn dev:cron' non-deterministic. Either add tsx as a devDependency or use a command backed by an already-installed dependency.

title: BSD-only sed -i '' syntax breaks on Linux
body: The script uses 'sed -i '' -E ...', which is valid on BSD/macOS sed but not on GNU sed. On Linux, GNU sed does not consume the separate empty string as the backup suffix, so the empty argument is treated as a file operand and the command errors or behaves unexpectedly. Use portable syntax such as 'sed -i -E' or add an OS check.

title: Cache timestamp is always formatted in en-US
body: The timestamp display hardcodes Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...). Users with other locales will see a US-style date/time format even though the rest of the UI is localized. The user's locale or Cal.com time format should be used instead.

title: No tests cover deleteCache authorization or cache status enrichment
body: The PR adds a security-sensitive mutation that checks credential ownership before deleting CalendarCache rows and enriches connectedCalendars with cacheUpdatedAt. The diff includes no automated tests for the unauthorized case (one user targeting another user's credential), successful deletion, or the cacheUpdatedAt mapping. This leaves the ownership boundary and the new UI-visible behavior unverified.

title: Empty data passed to Prisma updateMany
body: The new call `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany`. Prisma requires at least one field in the data argument; an empty object is rejected by validation or performs no update. This runs at the end of `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` after availability has already been cached, so a validation error would fail the webhook cache refresh and cause retries/error handling, while a no-op would not actually refresh `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. Pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` or remove the call if the update is not needed.

title: cacheUpdatedAt may be null/undefined when passed to Date constructor
body: Although this JSX is inside the `hasCache` branch, TypeScript does not narrow the separate `cacheUpdatedAt` prop from the boolean local. The prop is `Date | null | undefined`, so `new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)` is a strict null check type error and will fail type-check/build. Verify the value directly, e.g. use `cacheUpdatedAt && ...`, or format in a helper that accepts `Date | null | undefined`.

title: Delete cache mutation does not invalidate the connected calendars query
body: After `deleteCacheMutation` succeeds, it shows a toast and calls `onSuccess`, but unlike `disconnectMutation` it never calls `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. The calendar list is rendered from a suspense query with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, so after deleting cache the old `cacheUpdatedAt` can remain visible until a manual refresh. Add invalidation to the mutation's `onSuccess` or `onSettled` so the cache status is refetched.

title: ENV_FILE path is relative to cwd and updates the wrong .env from repo root
body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is interpreted relative to the caller's current working directory, not the script location. The likely invocation from the repository root, `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`, resolves to the parent directory of the repository, so the tunnel URL is written to the wrong `.env` or a new file is created there. Compute `SCRIPT_DIR` from `BASH_SOURCE` and derive the path from that, or use a path relative to the repository root consistently.

title: macOS-only sed -i syntax breaks on Linux
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU/Linux, including WSL and many CI runners, the empty argument is treated as a backup extension or an invalid option, so updating an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` line fails. Use a portable form such as `sed -i -E` under GNU sed, `perl -pi -e`, or detect the OS before choosing the syntax.

title: dev:cron now depends on npx fetching an undeclared tsx package
body: The script was changed to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not declared in `dependencies` or `devDependencies` for this package. `npx` can fetch the latest `tsx` from the registry at runtime, which makes the dev script non-deterministic, may fail offline, and may not work correctly under Yarn PnP. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and invoke the local binary, or use the already-declared runner.

title: updateMany with an empty data object cannot bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty data object to Prisma `updateMany`. Prisma rejects empty update data or produces no real update, so it will not update `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` as the comment claims, and it may throw. This runs after availability cache is written in `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`, so a throw here can fail the Google webhook/cache-refresh path after cache was already updated. Pass a concrete field such as `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` if the timestamp bump is intended, or remove the call if it is not needed.

title: deleteCache success does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
body: The delete-cache mutation only calls `onSuccess?.()` and shows a toast. It does not invalidate `trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component which invalidates that query in `onSettled`. As a result, after deleting cached data the `cacheUpdatedAt` already loaded in the UI remains stale, so the cache status and delete action are still shown until a manual refetch. Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in the delete mutation's success or settled handler.
