title: Cache status query includes expired calendar cache entries
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all CalendarCache rows for the given credential IDs without filtering on `expiresAt`. The actual cache lookup in `getCachedAvailability` only uses rows where `expiresAt >= now()`, so the new UI can report that cache exists for a credential whose cached entries are expired and would not be served. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the `where` clause so the status matches effective cache data.

title: Passing optional/null cacheUpdatedAt to Date constructor is not type-safe
body: `cacheUpdatedAt` is declared as `Date | null | undefined`, but `new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)` is called after only checking the separate `hasCache` boolean. TypeScript does not narrow `cacheUpdatedAt` through an aliased boolean check, so with strict null checks this is a compile error; the code is also not type-safe as written. Use a narrowed local value after checking `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` directly, or pass a non-null assertion/cast, before constructing the Date.

title: Reminder cancellation promises are not awaited
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async and perform database writes and external API calls, but they are fired inside nested `forEach` callbacks without collecting or awaiting the returned promises. The handler can return `Booking successfully cancelled` before those operations finish, and in a serverless/Next API route the runtime may freeze after the response, so the `cancelled: true` update at the core of this PR may never be persisted. The same fire-and-forget pattern appears in `handleNewBooking.ts:967`, `bookings.tsx:488`, and several `workflows.tsx` paths. Collect the promises and await them with `Promise.allSettled` before completing the handler.

title: Immediate email cancellation has no retry/fallback on SendGrid failure
body: In the `immediateDelete` branch, the function sends the SendGrid cancel request and then returns without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row or setting `cancelled: true`. If `client.request` throws, the catch logs the error and leaves the reminder with `cancelled` null and `scheduled` true. The cron retry logic only selects reminders where `cancelled: true`, so this reminder will never be cancelled and the scheduled email can still be delivered for a cancelled/rescheduled booking. This branch is used by reschedule and workflow/step deletion paths. On failure it should mark the reminder as canceled (or otherwise make it eligible for cron retry) instead of returning unchanged.

title: Non-immediate cancellation can be too late for near-term scheduled sends
body: For the non-immediate path, the function only sets `cancelled: true`; the actual SendGrid cancel happens later in the 15-minute cron when the scheduled date is within the next hour. If a booking is cancelled close to the reminder's scheduled send time, the next cron run may happen after the send time, so the email will already have been delivered. This reintroduces the reported bug for a last-minute cancellation window. Reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next cron interval should be cancelled immediately, or the cron schedule/cutoff should guarantee cancellation before the send time.

title: One SendGrid cancellation error blocks all other cancellations in the batch
body: The whole `for` loop over `remindersToCancel` is wrapped in a single `try/catch`. If any single `client.request` fails, control jumps to the catch, logs, and skips all remaining selected reminders until the next cron run. Since these reminders are already within the next hour of their scheduled send, one transient error can cause multiple uncancelled emails to be delivered. Each reminder's cancel/delete should be handled independently so one failure does not prevent the rest from being cancelled.

title: No tests were added for the new cancellation behavior
body: The PR changes the cancellation model for workflow email reminders, including the new `cancelled` field, deferred SendGrid cancellation in the cron, immediate-delete call paths, and SMS deletion. No tests cover these paths. A regression here would silently send workflow emails for cancelled or rescheduled bookings, which is the exact user-facing bug being fixed. Add unit/integration tests for marking reminders cancelled, cron retrieval within the one-hour window, SendGrid cancel failures, and SMS cancellation.

title: Workflow reminder cancellation is not awaited in cancel handler
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async, but they are fired inside a `forEach` without being collected into `prismaPromises` or awaited. The previous code collected `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` promises and awaited them before returning. Because this handler returns after `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`, the DB update that sets `cancelled = true` (or the SMS row deletion) may not complete before the serverless function is frozen after the response. A cancelled booking can therefore still have its scheduled email/SMS reminder sent.

title: Reschedule path bypasses deferred cancellation and leaves stale reminder rows
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` calls SendGrid immediately with `status: 'cancel'`. This is the same pattern the PR says caused the 100 pending cancellation limit: it creates a SendGrid pending cancellation until the original send date. For rescheduled bookings, the new `cancelled`/cron mechanism should be used instead. In addition, the `immediateDelete` branch returns without deleting or marking the `WorkflowReminder` DB row, so the original booking retains rows that still appear scheduled and may be retried later. The promise is also not awaited.

title: Request-reschedule workflow reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async and are called in a `forEach` without being awaited. The old code collected and awaited `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` promises. The mutation continues to send the reschedule request and returns; in a serverless environment the process can be frozen before the deferred `cancelled = true` update is written. The old workflow reminders can then still fire after the booking was put into the reschedule path.

title: Workflow update cancels reminders without awaiting DB writes
body: `remindersToDelete.flat().forEach(...)` calls the async managers without awaiting them, and the later `userWorkflow.steps.map(async (oldStep) => ...)` promises are also never awaited. The mutation subsequently updates the workflow and returns, so email/SMS cancellation calls and related DB deletes/updates can still be in flight. A cancelled reminder may be re-created or the old reminder may remain uncancelled, allowing emails/SMS from a disabled or edited workflow to be sent after the update completes.

title: One failed SendGrid cancellation prevents deletion of already-cancelled rows
body: The loop awaits each `client.request` sequentially and only afterwards calls `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`. If any later SendGrid request throws, the `catch` runs before the delete promises are awaited, so rows for which cancellation already succeeded are not deleted. They remain `cancelled = true` and are retried on the next cron run, generating duplicate SendGrid cancellation requests and keeping stale rows until a run with no cancellation failures. The delete should be awaited immediately after a successful cancellation or the final `Promise.all` should run in a `finally`.

title: Paid bookings return before scheduled workflow reminders are cancelled
body: When `bookingToDelete.paid` is true, the handler refunds the payment, marks the booking REJECTED, and returns at this line. This is before the block at lines 484-493 that cancels scheduled workflow reminders. As a result, paid/rejected bookings with scheduled workflow reminders will still have those reminder emails/SMS sent after cancellation. This path is not covered by the PR's cancellation fix.

title: Past reminders are deleted before cancelled reminders are cancelled
body: The handler first deletes all EMAIL workflowReminders with scheduledDate <= now (lines 34-41), then later queries for cancelled reminders to cancel at SendGrid (lines 44-51). A reminder cancelled shortly before its scheduledDate can therefore be removed by the first deleteMany when the next 15-minute cron tick runs after the scheduledDate, and the SendGrid scheduled send is never told to cancel, so the unwanted email can still be sent. Cancel processing should run before the past-date deletion, or near-term cancellations should be sent to SendGrid immediately.

title: Immediate SendGrid cancellation leaves no retry state
body: When immediateDelete is true, the function sends the SendGrid cancellation request and returns without deleting the workflowReminder or setting cancelled=true. If the request fails, the caught error is only logged, the row remains with cancelled null, and the regular CRON cancellation query will never retry it because it is not marked cancelled. For rescheduled bookings this can still allow the old scheduled email to be sent after a transient SendGrid error. Set cancelled=true before attempting the immediate cancellation or delete the row only after success with retry semantics.

title: Old workflow reminders are cancelled before reschedule succeeds
body: The new block cancels/deletes the original booking's workflow reminders before calling eventManager.reschedule and before checking whether it succeeded. If reschedule fails, the original booking remains but its reminders are already gone, so the user no longer receives the reminders they should still get. Only cancel old reminders after a successful reschedule, or recreate them on failure.

title: Workflow reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async, but their promises are not collected or awaited. The previous code at least awaited the Prisma deletes. As a result, the handler can return success before Twilio/SendGrid cancellation and DB cleanup complete, and failures are swallowed with no retry. Collect the promises and await them before returning.

title: Paid bookings return before scheduled workflow reminders are cancelled
body: The paid/refund branch returns at line 464 before the updatedBookings workflow-reminder cancellation block at lines 484-493. Scheduled BEFORE_EVENT/AFTER_EVENT reminders for paid bookings are left untouched and can still be sent after the booking is cancelled/rejected. Move the workflow-reminder cancellation before this early return or restructure the early return.

title: Dynamic imports are still evaluated eagerly
body: The object literal uses `import("./applecalendar")` etc. as property values, so every `import()` call runs as soon as the appStore module is evaluated. This does not provide on-demand/lazy loading of app packages: all app chunks are fetched/parsed immediately. If the goal is to import only the requested app, wrap each import in a function (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) or invoke `import()` at access time. It also creates promises for all apps without individual `.catch`, so a failed chunk for an unused app can become an unhandled rejection.

title: Recurring cancellation calendar deletions are not awaited before final Promise.all
body: In this recurring-bookings branch, the `.forEach(async (credential) => {...})` callback suspends at `await getCalendar(credential)` and at `await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` before `apiDeletes.push(...)`. Because the async callbacks are not awaited, `apiDeletes` is still missing these calendar deletion promises when `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs later, so external calendar events for the remaining recurring occurrences are not cancelled. Use a `for..of` loop and push the promises before the final await, or `await Promise.all(credentials.map(...))`.

title: `await apiDeletes` does not wait for the promises in the array
body: `apiDeletes` is an array of promises returned by `deleteMeeting`/`deleteEvent`. `await apiDeletes` resolves immediately with the array itself, so the paid cancellation path can return before those external integration deletions complete or fail. This should be `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)`.

title: Reschedule deletions are fire-and-forget via `forEach(async)`
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` is not awaited by `forEach`. The calendar/video cancellation promises are ignored, and the function continues to send emails and return before the deletions complete; rejections from the async callbacks also become unhandled. Replace this with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for..of` loop so the cancellations are actually awaited.

title: Reschedule deletions are fire-and-forget via `forEach(async)`
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` is not awaited by `forEach`. The calendar/video cancellation promises are ignored, and the function continues to send emails and return before the deletions complete; rejections from the async callbacks also become unhandled. Replace this with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for..of` loop so the cancellations are actually awaited.

title: Reschedule deletion is fire-and-forget in bookings router
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` is not awaited by `forEach`. The old calendar/video events are deleted in background, but the mutation proceeds to send reschedule emails and webhooks before those cancellations complete, and any rejection is unhandled. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for..of` loop to await the cancellation operations.

title: forEach async callbacks are not awaited, so cancellation errors are lost
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` starts an async callback for each reference but `forEach` discards the returned promise. The surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections after the callback suspends, so a failed `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled rejection and the function returns before external calendar/video cancellation is known to have completed. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop.

title: forEach async callbacks are not awaited, so cancellation errors are lost
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` starts an async callback for each reference but `forEach` discards the returned promise. The surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections after the callback suspends, so a failed `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled rejection and the function returns before external calendar/video cancellation is known to have completed. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop.

title: requestReschedule does not await async calendar/video cancellation callbacks
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` discards the promise returned by each async callback. The mutation continues immediately to send reschedule emails and webhooks, so external calendar/video cancellation for the old booking may still be running, and any rejection from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled rejection. Convert this to `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop.

title: Recurring cancellation starts unawaited async callbacks and `apiDeletes` is captured too early
body: In the recurring cancellation branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` does not await the callbacks. Each callback suspends at `await getCalendar`, so the later `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` captures `apiDeletes` before these callbacks resume and push their calendar deletions. As a result, recurring calendar events are not deleted/cancelled before booking references and attendees are removed and cancellation emails are sent. Use `await Promise.all(credentials.map(async (credential) => { ... }))` instead of `forEach`.

title: Recurring calendar deletions are not awaited and can be missed
body: The recurring cancellation branch uses `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })`. `forEach` ignores the returned promise, so execution reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 before these async callbacks have resumed and populated `apiDeletes`. Recurring booking calendar events may never be deleted before the handler returns, and any rejected `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent` promise is unhandled. This regressed because the callback previously used synchronous `getCalendar` and pushed into `apiDeletes` synchronously. Use `for...of` or `Promise.all` and await the deletions.

title: Reschedule cancellation runs in unawaited async forEach
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` does not await the async callbacks. The mutation continues to send reschedule emails and webhooks and can return before the old calendar/video events are cancelled; rejections from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` also become unhandled. Use an actual `for...of`/`Promise.all` and await before sending the follow-up emails.

title: Unawaited async forEach can leave Vital calendar events uncancelled
body: The async callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` awaits `getCalendar` but `forEach` does not await the returned promise. The surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections from the async callback, and `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` runs before the cancellation work completes. Replace this with a `for...of` loop or collect and `await Promise.all(...)` for the cancellation promises.

title: Unawaited async forEach can leave WipeMyCal calendar events uncancelled
body: Same issue as in the vital reschedule helper: the async callback passed to `forEach` is not awaited, so the function can send reschedule emails and return before `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent` finish. Errors from the async callback are unhandled. Use an `await`-able loop or `Promise.all`.

title: Storing `import()` promises still eagerly loads every app
body: Each property is an executed `import()` call, so when this module is evaluated all app modules start loading/evaluating even if no caller ever accesses that app. That undercuts the intended lazy loading and can cause a large prefetch/cold-start cost; an import failure for an unused app can also become an unhandled rejection. Store thunks (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and invoke them at the lookup sites if on-demand loading is desired.

title: Date-override check allows slots that only partially overlap the override
body: The condition marks a slot as outside an override only when slotEndTime is before or the same as the override start, or slotStartTime is after the override end. A slot that starts before the override and ends inside it, starts inside and ends after it, or starts exactly at the override end is treated as inside the override and allowed. Since fixed-host slots are generated from aggregate availability, this lets a round-robin event be booked while the fixed host is unavailable.

title: Fixed host with no working hours on a day is treated as available
body: This `workingHours.find(...)` only rejects a slot when a working-hour entry for the day exists and the slot start is outside that entry. If no entry has `days` including `slotStartTime.day()`, `find` returns undefined and execution continues to the busy check, which can return true. For a round-robin slot generated by another host on a day the fixed host does not work, this makes the fixed host appear available and allows a booking outside their schedule.

title: Working-hours check ignores slot end time/event length
body: `end` is assigned the same value as `start`, so `end > workingHour.endTime` only checks whether `slotStartTime` is after the working hour end. It never validates that `slotStartTime + eventLength` fits within the working hours. A slot starting inside a fixed host's working hours but ending after them will be accepted, again undermining the fixed-host availability check.

title: Multiple same-day date overrides are not all considered
body: `dateOverrides.find` returns true as soon as one matching-day override is outside the slot, causing `checkIfIsAvailable` to return false immediately. Later same-day overrides that do contain the slot are never checked. If a fixed host has several overrides on one day, for example 10-11 and 14-15, a slot inside the later override can be blocked because the first override did not encompass it.

title: Dayjs objects compared with strict equality
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares object references, not timestamps, so it is always false. This branch was presumably meant to identify equal start/end overrides with `isSame`. As written, that case falls through and can produce the wrong availability result.

title: Round-robin fixed-host date override scenario is not tested
body: The PR title/description says date overrides of fixed hosts should be taken into account for round-robin events, but the added test only covers a personal event date override with a different invitee timezone. The new `checkIfIsAvailable` date-override and working-hours paths for fixed hosts are the most complex part of this change and have no regression test.

title: Date-override slots skip busy checks and can be double-booked
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, once dateOverrideExist is set and the function has not returned false, it returns true immediately at lines 133-135. This happens before the busy array is checked at line 153. Slots are generated by getTimeSlots without considering busy, so a fixed or loose host with a date override is treated as available even when they have an accepted booking or calendar event during that override. Date overrides should replace normal working hours, not suppress busy checks.

title: Working-hours validation uses slot start for both start and end
body: The new working-hours check computes `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` and then `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`, so it never tests slotEndTime. A slot that starts inside the host's work hours but ends after `workingHour.endTime` is not rejected. For round-robin fixed hosts, getTimeSlots can produce such slots from other hosts' longer availability, so fixed hosts can be booked outside their actual working hours.

title: Multiple date overrides on the same day are not all evaluated
body: The date-override validation uses `dateOverrides.find` and returns true as soon as the slot is outside one same-day override, which makes checkIfIsAvailable return false immediately. If a host has multiple same-day date overrides (for example 09:00-10:00 and 14:00-15:00), a slot in the second override is rejected because the first override does not contain it. Only if no same-day override contains the slot should the slot be considered outside the overridden availability.

title: Split working-hours windows are not all evaluated
body: The normal working-hours validation similarly uses `workingHours.find` and returns true when a single same-day working-hour window does not contain the slot. A host with split hours (for example 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00) will be treated as unavailable for slots in the later window because the first window is checked first and the function returns false before checking the second. The check should pass if any working-hours window contains the slot, not fail if the first one does not.

title: Date override day filter still uses unadjusted organizer wall time
body: activeOverrides filters overrides by comparing `dayjs.utc(override.start)` with the invitee day. `override.start` is the organizer-local wall time encoded as a UTC timestamp (for example 14:00 IST is stored as T14:00Z), not the actual UTC instant. The new offset conversion later in the function fixes slot minutes but this filter is still applied before that conversion. For attendee timezones whose UTC day differs from the organizer's encoded day, the override can be applied to the previous or next day, so the correct day shows wrong availability.

title: No test covers fixed-host date overrides in round-robin events
body: The new test only exercises a personal event and checks that the returned UTC slots remain the same for a different attendee timezone. The main round-robin fixed-host date-override behavior is untested. A round-robin event with fixed and loose hosts, where the fixed host has a date override, should be added to verify the fix and would have exposed the busy-time and working-hours issues in checkIfIsAvailable.

title: Date overrides bypass busy checks, allowing double bookings
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot is not excluded by the override, the function returns true at line 133 before running the busy.every conflict check. This means calendar bookings and existing Cal bookings for that host are ignored on any day with a date override, so a slot can be offered even when the host is already busy. This applies to fixed hosts and regular non-team event hosts, leading to double-bookings on override days.

title: Working-hours end time is computed from slot start, not slot end
body: The working-hours validation sets both start and end to slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(). The end value should be derived from slotEndTime or at least start + eventLength. As written, a slot that starts inside the host's working hours but ends after the working-hours end passes the check. If the fixed host has shorter availability than the aggregate availability used to generate slots, bookings can be made outside that host's actual working hours.

title: Zero-length date override check compares Dayjs objects with ===
body: The condition dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes") compares two distinct Dayjs object references, so it is always false. A zero-length date override used to mark a date unavailable does not block a slot that starts exactly at that override time, because the callback returns undefined and dateOverrideExist then returns true.

title: Multiple same-day date overrides are not all considered
body: The dateOverrides.find callback sets dateOverrideExist and returns true immediately when it finds a same-day override that does not contain the slot. If a host has several date-override intervals on the same date, a slot that lies in a later interval is rejected because an earlier same-day interval returned true first. The logic should determine whether the slot is inside any of the same-day overrides rather than stopping at the first one that excludes it.

title: Timezone-adjusted date overrides drop day-crossing information
body: The active-override filter at line 206 still uses dayjs.utc(override.start), and the start/end calculation at lines 219-224 only keeps hour() and minute() after adding the offset. When the organizer/invitee timezone adjustment crosses midnight, this discards the new day. For example, a 23:30-23:45 Honolulu override is 02:30-02:45 next day in Los Angeles, but the current code can attach the override to the previous invitee day and produce 02:30 without carrying into the next day. This makes date overrides near midnight appear on the wrong day in certain timezones.

title: No regression test for fixed-host date overrides in round-robin
body: The PR's main round-robin fix is that fixed-host date overrides are now enforced in availableTimeSlots through checkIfIsAvailable, but the only added test covers a personal event date override with a different timezone. There is no test creating a round-robin event with one fixed host, a date override for that fixed host, and a round-robin host. That is the most complex new path and should have a regression test.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category is not set
body: The query `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the `embed_category` site setting is non-empty and matches a category name. The default for `embed_category` is `''` (removed in this PR), so on a typical site the query returns zero rows, `[0]` is `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. It should handle no result and skip directly to the uncategorized fallback.

title: Migrated embeddable hosts are inserted without normalization, breaking existing allowed hosts
body: Old `embeddable_hosts` accepted values like `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234` (the existing specs even use these), but the new `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares only `URI(...).host` to the stored `host` column. The migration inserts each old line verbatim, so rows containing a scheme or path will never match allowed-host checks after upgrade. Values are also interpolated directly into SQL; a host value containing a quote will break the migration or inject SQL. Normalize before insert and use parameterized queries.

title: Update/destroy with missing record raises 500
body: `update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then pass the result to `save_host` or call `host.destroy` without checking for nil. A request for a non-existent id (stale admin tab, concurrent delete, or malformed request) will raise NoMethodError and return 500 instead of a JSON 404/error response. Use `find` or check `host.present?`.

title: save_host assumes embeddable_host params are present
body: `save_host` immediately accesses `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]`. If `params[:embeddable_host]` is missing or null, this raises NoMethodError and returns 500. It should return a standard JSON validation error for missing parameters instead.

title: before_validation does not handle nil host
body: `self.host.sub!` is called before validation on every save. If `host` is nil (for example from a direct model call or malformed API request), this raises NoMethodError rather than producing a normal validation error. Guard the normalization with `if self.host.present?` or add a presence validation before mutating.

title: Hosts saved with a port can never match
body: The format validation explicitly allows an optional port (`:[0-9]{1,5}`), but `record_for_host` uses `uri.host` only and ignores `uri.port`. A configured host like `example.com:8080` will be compared as `example.com` and never match a referer to `http://example.com:8080/...`. Either reject ports in the validator or include `uri.port` in the comparison.

title: Controller spec only checks inheritance
body: The only test in this spec asserts that `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` subclasses `Admin::AdminController`; create, update, destroy, and `save_host` are untested. The missing-record and missing-param failure paths in this controller are exactly where bugs can land without coverage.

title: Legacy embeddable hosts are inserted without normalization and will not match the new host check
body: The old `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` values could include full URLs and paths, as shown by the removed specs using `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234`. This migration inserts each `h` verbatim into `embeddable_hosts.host`, but `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`/`record_for_host` parses the incoming referer and compares only `uri.host` to the stored `lower(host)`. A migrated value like `http://example.com` will never match `example.com`, so existing full-URL host configurations silently stop allowing embeds after upgrade.

title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
body: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!` before any presence or format validations run. If a request creates or updates an `EmbeddableHost` with a missing/null `host`, this raises `NoMethodError` on nil and returns a 500 instead of a normal validation error. The callback should guard with `self.host.to_s` or a presence validation should be added before mutation.

title: Missing records and malformed params cause 500 errors
body: `update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`, which can be nil for an unknown ID. `update` then passes nil to `save_host` and calls `host.host=`, while `destroy` calls `host.destroy`, both raising `NoMethodError`. Additionally, `save_host` unconditionally dereferences `params[:embeddable_host]`, so malformed input without that root key also raises. These should return 404/JSON errors instead of 500s.

title: Hosts saved with a port can never match
body: The host format validation allows an optional `:port` (line 2), and `before_validation` does not strip it. However `record_for_host` compares only `uri.host` to the stored `lower(host)`, ignoring `uri.port`. A host entered as `example.com:8080` will therefore never match `http://example.com:8080`. Either reject ports in the validation or include the port in the lookup comparison.

title: Category and embeddable host fabricator contents were swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` definitions. This looks like an accidental file-swap. It may work in the full suite if all fabricator files are loaded, but the file named `category_fabricator` no longer defines `:category` and direct requires or future maintenance will be broken. The contents should be moved back.

title: GET /fruits/:id always returns the first fruit, so the id-2 test exercises the wrong record
body: The test changed to `store.find('fruit', 2)` and asserts `fruitCols.length` is 2 with color ids 1 and 2, but this pretender route always sets `const fruit = fruits[0]` regardless of the requested id. The assertion therefore still validates fruit id 1, not fruit id 2's actual single-color array, and would not catch errors in the plural `_ids` hydration for a single element.

title: No action-level tests for embeddable host admin CRUD
body: The new admin controller specs only assert that the controllers inherit from `Admin::AdminController`. They do not exercise `create`, `update`, or `destroy`, staff authorization, invalid host input, missing categories, or missing-record behavior. Since this PR introduces a new admin CRUD API and changes embedding access control, these cases should be covered.

title: Migration crashes when legacy embed_category is missing or blank
body: The migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` without checking for an empty result. `embed_category` is optional and often blank or unset; in that case the INNER JOIN query returns zero rows, `[0]` is nil, and the migration raises `NoMethodError`, blocking deployment. Use a safe fetch such as `first`/`try` before indexing.

title: Legacy embeddable hosts are copied without normalization
body: The migration inserts legacy `embeddable_hosts` values verbatim. The old matcher accepted entries with `http://`, `https://`, or trailing paths, while the new `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares the incoming URL's `URI#host` to the stored host string exactly. Existing site settings that contained scheme/path forms will stop matching after migration, breaking embedding for those hosts.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host
body: `before_validation` calls `sub!` directly on `self.host`. When `host` is nil or blank, possible via the admin create/update API, `nil.sub!` raises `NoMethodError`, returning a 500 instead of a normal validation failure. Guard the callback with `self.host.present?` or coerce with `self.host = self.host.to_s.sub(...)`.

title: No uniqueness constraint on host
body: There is no unique validation or index on `host`. The admin API/UI can create multiple `EmbeddableHost` rows for the same host with different categories, while `record_for_host` returns the first one. Imported topics then use whichever row is returned first, making the host-to-category mapping ambiguous and nondeterministic.

title: Missing record in update/destroy becomes fatal
body: `update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without handling nil. A request with a deleted or unknown id passes nil to `save_host` or calls `destroy` on nil, causing a 500 instead of a 404 or JSON error response.

title: Host entries with ports cannot match
body: The format validation allows a port such as `example.com:8080`, but `record_for_host` compares `URI(host).host`, which drops the port, against the stored host string. A stored host with a port can never match an incoming referer, so such entries appear valid in admin but silently deny embeds. Either strip ports on save and adjust lookup, or disallow them.

title: Fabricator definitions are in the wrong files
body: `category_fabricator.rb` now contains `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the category fabricators. Fabrication may load them regardless, but the file names no longer describe their contents and future maintenance by filename will be misleading.

title: /fruits/:id fixture ignores the requested id
body: The pretender route always returns `fruits[0]` regardless of `:id`. The updated store test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` but still gets fruit 1; the plural `color_ids` assertions happen to pass because fruit 1 also has two colors. This means the test does not actually exercise lookup of a different record and could mask regressions.

title: Client upload validation ignores site size settings
body: validateUploadedFile now uses a hard-coded 10 MB maximum for both image and attachment types instead of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. The 413 handler in displayErrorForUpload (line 246) uses the same hard-coded value. Attachments are not downsized server-side, so this allows users to select and submit files beyond max_attachment_size_kb and gives users an incorrect maximum, while also blocking sites that allow uploads larger than 10 MB.

title: API URL download cap ignores type-specific size settings
body: FileHelper.download is now always capped at 10.megabytes instead of the configured upload size. The new downsize path only applies to images and only when max_image_size_kb > 0, so non-image API uploads can still be downloaded and processed far above max_attachment_size_kb, and image uploads can be accepted beyond the intended limit if downsize fails. Use the type-specific site setting or enforce the limit after download.

title: Loop uses stale Tempfile#size after in-place resize
body: tempfile is normally a Tempfile (Rack uploaded files and FileHelper.download). Tempfile#size caches the file size, so after OptimizedImage.downsize rewrites the same file outside the Tempfile object, tempfile.size at line 66 still returns the original size. The loop can run all five 80% reductions even after the image is below max_image_size_kb, degrading the image, and Upload.create_for is called with the stale original size at line 72. Use File.size(tempfile.path) after each downsize or otherwise refresh/reopen the file.

title: No final size check after downsize loop
body: The return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored and there is no check after the loop that the resulting file is at or below SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. If the ImageMagick/gifsicle command fails, or if five 80% reductions are not enough for a very large file, the code still calls Upload.create_for with an oversized image. This silently bypasses the configured max image size. Check the result and return an upload error if the image cannot be reduced below the limit.

title: Duplicate self.downsize overrides the legacy width/height form
body: Ruby does not support method overloading; this second definition of self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) replaces the first definition at line 145 (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}). Any caller using the existing numeric width/height form now gets an ArgumentError, and the first method is dead code. Either keep only the new method and update callers, or replace both with a single method that accepts both forms.

title: Animated GIF uploads via API are flattened
body: OptimizedImage.optimize chooses the animated gifsicle path by testing the source path for a .GIF extension (optimized_image.rb line 155). Here the source is tempfile.path, but FileHelper.download creates a Tempfile named discourse-upload-<type> without the original extension. An animated GIF fetched from an API URL will therefore go through the ImageMagick non-animated path (from[0]) and be reduced to its first frame, losing animation even though allow_animation is passed. Detect animation from the original filename/content type rather than the temporary path.

title: Automatic downsize ignores conversion failure and final size
body: The loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize and decrements attempt, but ignores the boolean returned by downsize and never checks after the loop whether tempfile.size is still greater than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. If ImageMagick/gifsicle fails (corrupt image, mislabeled non-image, unsupported format) or five 80% reductions are insufficient, create_upload proceeds with the same tempfile. This can reject the upload only later with a generic error, or store an oversized/corrupt image depending on the rest of the model validation. The code should break on successful downsize and return an explicit error if the final file is still over the limit.

title: URL download limit is hardcoded to 10 MB and ignores site settings
body: FileHelper.download now uses 10.megabytes instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. Non-image URL uploads do not go through the later image downsize loop, so this action can fetch up to 10 MB even if the configured max_image_size_kb is much lower. Conversely, sites with max_image_size_kb above 10 MB can no longer fetch such files via URL. Use the configured limit for non-image uploads or enforce it explicitly after download.

title: Client upload validation hardcodes 10 MB instead of per-type site settings
body: validateUploadedFile no longer reads Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so both image and attachment client-side checks now use 10 MB. The 413 handler at line 246 does the same instead of using max_image_size_kb. Sites with a smaller configured limit still allow the browser to submit oversized files, while sites with a larger configured limit have valid uploads blocked by the client. The alert text can also report the wrong maximum size. Keep using the site settings or add a separate consistent cap.

title: Animated GIFs are flattened because downsize sees the tempfile path, not the original filename
body: OptimizedImage.downsize decides whether to use the animated downsize path by testing the source path for a .GIF extension in OptimizedImage.optimize. Here the source path is tempfile.path, which for Rack uploads is typically a generated /tmp/RackMultipart... path without the original .gif extension, while the original filename is available separately. As a result, oversized animated GIF uploads are processed by the normal ImageMagick instructions with from[0], which reads only the first frame and throws away the animation. The original filename/extension must be preserved on the tempfile or passed into the downsize call so the animated branch can be selected.

title: Redefining self.downsize overrides the existing four-argument method
body: Ruby does not support overloading, so the new def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) replaces the previous def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}). Any caller using OptimizedImage.downsize(path, out, width, height) now binds width as dimensions and height as opts. The next downsize call may then evaluate opts[:allow_animation] on an Integer and raise TypeError, or silently ignore the height. Remove one of the duplicate methods and provide a single supported signature.

title: OptimizedImage.optimize signature change breaks positional width/height callers
body: optimize changed from optimize(operation, from, to, width, height, opts={}) to optimize(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts={}). Direct callers that still pass width and height as two arguments will now have height treated as opts, causing TypeError when opts[:allow_animation] is evaluated or otherwise incorrect behavior. If this is meant as an internal API, make that explicit and update all consumers; otherwise keep a backwards-compatible shim.

title: No tests added for auto-downsize behavior
body: The PR adds server-side downsize-on-upload, changes OptimizedImage method signatures, and changes client validation, but no specs are included. Boundaries around max_image_size_kb, downsize failure, insufficient reduction, animated GIFs, and non-image uploads are untested. A test for the previous OptimizedImage.downsize call style would also have caught the duplicate method issue.

title: In-place downsizing can destroy animated GIF originals and ignores conversion failures
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, '80%', allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` uses the original upload as both input and output. If `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false, `OptimizedImage.optimize` picks the non-animated `downsize_instructions`, whose ImageMagick command reads only `#{from}[0]` (the first frame) and writes to `#{to}`. Because `from == to`, a large animated GIF upload is replaced by a static resized first frame and the animation is permanently lost. Also `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` on conversion failure rather than raising, but the return value is ignored; after up to five attempts the code proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with the possibly unchanged, oversized, or partially overwritten file. Downscale to a separate temp file, check the result, and never mutate the original upload path directly.

title: Second `downsize` definition overrides the existing 4-argument method
body: Ruby does not overload class methods by arity. Defining `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 completely replaces the previous `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145. Existing code that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height, opts)` will either raise `ArgumentError` (when five arguments are passed) or bind the height integer to `opts`, causing a later `TypeError` in `optimize` when `opts[:allow_animation]` is accessed. Keep one method and explicitly support both call forms or update all callers.

title: Client upload size validation is hardcoded to 10MB instead of using site settings
body: `validateUploadedFile` now sets `maxSizeKB` to `10 * 1024` for every upload type instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, and the 413 handler at line 246 does the same for `max_image_size_kb`. This disables configured `max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb` limits in the client: sites with a larger limit reject valid files before upload, and sites with a smaller limit do not warn before the upload is rejected server-side. It is especially wrong for attachments because server-side auto-downsizing only applies to images.

title: API URL download limit is hardcoded to 10MB
body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the configured `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` with a constant. API URL uploads are now capped at 10MB even when the site allows larger files (or has no such small cap), and the setting is ignored for this path. If the intent is to download a larger original before downscaling it, the download cap should be derived from the site setting or a separate explicit setting, not fixed to 10MB.

title: Unsubscribe route has no matching Ember template
body: The route is declared as top-level `topicUnsubscribe`, but the template was added at `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which is the path for a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route. A top-level `topicUnsubscribe` route looks for `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`. The route defines no `renderTemplate`, so the client-side unsubscribe page will fail to render or error. Either nest the route inside the existing `topic` resource as `this.route('unsubscribe', ...)`, or move the template to `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`.

title: unsubscribe action crashes when TopicUser record is missing
body: `TopicUser.find_by` can return nil when the logged-in user has no TopicUser record for this topic. Any logged-in user can open `/t/:id/unsubscribe` for a visible topic they have never interacted with; the action is not restricted to users coming from an email. On line 107 it immediately calls `tu.notification_level`, so a missing record raises `NoMethodError` and returns 500. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` or otherwise initialize/handle a missing record.

title: Per-topic unsubscribe mutates state via GET without CSRF or token
body: The new unsubscribe routes are GET and `TopicsController#unsubscribe` mutates the user's `TopicUser#notification_level` on each request. Rails CSRF protection does not cover GET, and the URL contains no per-recipient token. A logged-in user who can be induced to load `https://.../t/123/unsubscribe` (for example through an image on an attacker-controlled page) will have their topic notification setting changed without intent. The same issue means email scanners/prefetchers that carry a session cookie could trigger it. This should be a POST with CSRF protection, or use a non-mutating tokenized flow.

title: Unsubscribe does not stop all topic notifications for watching/tracking users
body: When `notification_level` is `watching` or `tracking`, this action lowers it to `regular`. The link text promises to stop receiving notifications about the topic, but `regular` still permits reply and mention notifications for that topic, which are exactly some of the notification emails this link is attached to. A watching/tracking user can click the unsubscribe link and still continue receiving other notifications for the same topic. To honor the advertised behavior, the action should set `muted` (or explicitly use a different, clearly communicated level).

title: Top-level topicUnsubscribe route will not resolve the nested unsubscribe template
body: The route is declared as a top-level route named `topicUnsubscribe`, so Ember's default template name is `topic-unsubscribe` (or `topicUnsubscribe`), not `topic/unsubscribe`. The added template is at `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which would match a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route. Since the route does not override `renderTemplate`, the unsubscribe page will not render its client-side content. Move the template to `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs` or declare `unsubscribe` as a nested route under `topic`.

title: unsubscribe crashes when the current user has no TopicUser record
body: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil if the current user has never interacted with this topic, which is possible when the URL is visited directly or from a stale email. The next line calls `tu.notification_level`, raising `NoMethodError` and returning a 500 before any notification level is changed. Use `TopicUser.find_or_initialize_by(...)` or `TopicUser.change` so a missing record is created instead of crashing.

title: Per-topic unsubscribe changes state via GET without CSRF or token
body: The new `unsubscribe` action is a GET route that modifies `TopicUser.notification_level`. A logged-in user's browser can be made to request `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` from a third-party page, and because the action is not protected by CSRF or a token, the change will be applied. An attacker can mute or downgrade notification settings for arbitrary topics for a victim. Use a signed/one-time token in the email link or require a CSRF-protected POST.

title: unsubscribe_link interpolation now requires unsubscribe_url but MessageBuilder has no fallback
body: `server.en.yml` changed `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `MessageBuilder` only populates that key if the caller passed `unsubscribe_url` in opts. Any existing `Email::MessageBuilder` use with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but no `unsubscribe_url` will now get an I18n missing interpolation error in both `html_part` (line 67) and `body` (line 90). Since this is a shared builder, provide a safe default/guard or update all callers and fail explicitly before building the mail.

title: Unsubscribe copy promises full stop but controller only lowers to regular
body: The string says "You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}." However the controller sets a watching/tracking user to `regular` on the first click, and `regular` still permits notifications such as replies and mentions. Users may believe they are fully unsubscribed while still receiving some notifications. Either set `muted` for a true unsubscribe or change the copy to describe changing notification state.

title: No tests for new unsubscribe action, route, or per-topic email link
body: The only test change supplies `unsubscribe_url` to an existing builder example but does not assert that the per-topic unsubscribe link appears in the body. There are no controller/request specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (authentication, slug redirects, missing TopicUser, notification-level transitions) or for the Ember route/template. The new behavior can break without detection.

title: unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists
body: TopicUser.find_by(...) can return nil for a logged-in user who opens the unsubscribe URL without having a TopicUser row for that topic, for example by visiting /t/.../unsubscribe directly for a topic they never interacted with. The next line calls tu.notification_level, causing NoMethodError and a 500. Use TopicUser.find_or_initialize_by, TopicUser.change, or handle nil explicitly.

title: unsubscribe_link interpolation now requires unsubscribe_url from every caller
body: The shared unsubscribe_link translation now contains %{unsubscribe_url}, and MessageBuilder interpolates it whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. Only send_notification_email was updated to pass unsubscribe_url. Any other MessageBuilder call with add_unsubscribe_link: true and no unsubscribe_url will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when building the text or HTML body, breaking those emails. Either provide a default value in MessageBuilder or update all callers.

title: State-changing unsubscribe action is exposed via GET without CSRF protection
body: The new route maps GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe to a controller action that mutates TopicUser.notification_level based only on the current session. Because there is no CSRF token or per-message secret, any website visited by a logged-in user can embed an image or request to that URL and silently change their notification level for a topic.

title: No assertion for the new topic unsubscribe URL or controller behavior
body: The spec change adds unsubscribe_url to the MessageBuilder input but still only asserts the existing user_preferences_url appears in the body. It does not check that the topic-specific unsubscribe URL appears in the text or HTML, and there are no specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe or Topic#unsubscribe_url, leaving the new behavior effectively untested.

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and can be bypassed
body: `should_block?` uses `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` with the raw submitted value, and neither `BlockedEmail` nor `User` normalizes the address before validation. Since the domain part of an email is case-insensitive, a block for `spammer@gmail.com` will not match `spammer@Gmail.com`, allowing the same mailbox to sign up by changing the case of the domain or local part. The unique index does not help because it is also case-sensitive. Normalize addresses with `Email.downcase` before saving and querying blocked emails.

title: BlockedEmail side effects run twice per signup
body: `validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which increments `match_count` and writes `last_match_at`. In `UsersController#create`, the same user record is validated first by `user.valid?` and then again by `user.save`, so a single signup attempt against a blocked or do_nothing email increments the counters twice. This makes the new match statistics inaccurate; the write should be removed from the validator or the controller should avoid the duplicate validation call.

title: match_count increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save` loads the current count and writes the whole record. Two concurrent attempts for the same blocked email can both read the same `match_count`, and the last save will discard the other increment. Use `update_counters` or an SQL `match_count = match_count + 1` update if accurate statistics are required.

title: should_block? has DB write side effects and double counts per attempt
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and calls record.save whenever a matching record is found. EmailValidator calls it during User validation; UsersController#create calls user.valid? before user.save, and save runs validations again, so one blocked signup attempt increments and saves the BlockedEmail row twice. The read-modify-write is also not atomic, so concurrent attempts can lose increments. Track match statistics after a real signup attempt (or use an atomic update) and avoid writing in a validation predicate.

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? uses BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with the raw submitted value. Elsewhere the app normalizes email addresses via Email.downcase (and change_email also strips), but this check does not. On PostgreSQL the unique index is case-sensitive, so a block stored as foo@example.com can be bypassed by submitting Foo@example.com, and duplicate case-variant block records can be created. Normalize the address before lookup and before persistence.

title: change_email sends confirmation for blocked email before validation
body: change_email creates an EmailToken for lower_email and enqueues the authorize_email job without checking BlockedEmail.should_block? or otherwise running email validation. Because the new block validator only runs when a User record's email is changed and saved, a blocked email can receive a confirmation/authorization email before any model validation occurs. Add an explicit BlockedEmail check in change_email and reject the request before creating the token or enqueuing mail.

title: rejectedEmails is shared mutable state and never reset
body: Defining rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) on the controller class creates one shared Ember array rather than a per-instance array. Because createAccount only pushes into it and there is no clearing on successful account creation or modal close, an email rejected during one attempt remains rejected for later attempts in the same long-lived controller instance. Define the array in init or clear it when the signup form is reset.

title: Any server email error is cached as rejected, not just block-list failures
body: On a failed create, any presence of result.errors.email causes result.values.email to be pushed into rejectedEmails. Server errors can include uniqueness (already has been taken), domain whitelist/blacklist, blocked-list, or other failures, but the client will later show every such address as user.email.invalid. It also never removes entries. Cache only a machine-readable blocked-email rejection or clear rejectedEmails after the specific issue is resolved.

title: Blocked email matching is case-sensitive and bypassable
body: `should_block?` compares the raw email value against `blocked_emails.email` with no normalization, and the User signup path shown in this diff does not downcase email before validation. Email address routing is case-insensitive, so a mixed-case address such as `Bad@example.com` will not match a blocked record stored as `bad@example.com`. An attacker can bypass the block by changing case. Normalize with `Email.downcase` both when creating BlockedEmail records and before querying/validating.

title: change_email does not enforce the blocked email list
body: The change_email path only checks whether another user already has the requested email and then creates an email token. It never calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?` or otherwise runs the email validator, so an existing user can request a change to a blocked address. This sends a confirmation email to the blocked address and, depending on EmailToken confirmation behavior, may complete the change. The blocked-email control should be applied here before the email token is created.

title: match_count updates are non-atomic and double-count signup attempts
body: `match_count += 1; record.save` is a read-modify-write and can lose increments under concurrent attempts. Additionally, UsersController#create calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, both of which run validations; since EmailValidator invokes `should_block?` during validation, a single signup attempt with a matching BlockedEmail increments match_count twice. This makes the match statistics unreliable and adds extra database writes during validation. Use an atomic counter update and/or avoid running the validator twice for the same attempt.

title: Server-side EmailValidator does not validate email syntax
body: validate_each only checks domain whitelist/blacklist and BlockedEmail. It never verifies that value is a syntactically valid email address. Because this is the validator wired through `validates :email, email: true` in User, a direct POST to /users with a malformed non-blank email (for example `foo` or `a@`) can pass validation if client-side checks are bypassed, resulting in a user record with an invalid email. Add a server-side email format check.

title: Invalid ERB syntax breaks rendering of embed/best
body: The tag `<%- end if %>` expands to invalid Ruby (`end if`) after the if/else block. Rendering `best` when a topic exists raises SyntaxError and returns 500, so the embedded comments view cannot be displayed.

title: Imported URL is interpolated into raw HTML unsafely
body: The imported URL is placed directly into an `<a href='#{url}'>` footer without HTML escaping. Because the post is created with `cook_method: raw_html`, this footer becomes rendered HTML and is emitted with `raw` in the embed view. A URL containing `'`, `">`, or event-handler markup can execute stored XSS when the post is viewed. Escape the URL before interpolation.

title: RSS/Atom feed content is stored and rendered as unsanitized raw HTML
body: `i.content` is unescaped with `CGI.unescapeHTML` and passed to `TopicEmbed.import`, which sets `cook_method: raw_html`; `Post#cook` then returns the raw content unchanged and the embed view renders it with `raw`. A malicious or compromised feed can include `<script>`, event-handler attributes, or `javascript:` URLs, resulting in stored XSS on the Discourse site. Sanitize the feed HTML or use the normal cooking pipeline.

title: RSS `content` may be nil with no fallback
body: Many RSS/Atom feeds provide the entry body in `description`, `summary`, or `content:encoded`, so SimpleRSS may leave `content` as nil. The code calls `i.content.scrub`, which raises `NoMethodError` and aborts the whole poll. Use a fallback such as `i.content || i.description || i.summary`.

title: absolutize_urls drops explicit ports 80/443 incorrectly for the wrong scheme
body: The condition `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` is independent of the URL scheme. For `http://example.com:443/...` the port is omitted, rewriting relative links to port 80; for `https://example.com:80/...` the port is omitted, rewriting them to port 443. Compare against the scheme's default port, for example using `uri.default_port`.

title: import_remote uses HTTP open without requiring open-uri
body: `import_remote` calls `open(url)` on an HTTP URL, but this file does not require `open-uri`. If no other code loaded it, Kernel#open treats the URL as a filesystem path and raises `Errno::ENOENT`. Callers such as `TopicRetriever` and the Disqus import can reach this path. Add `require 'open-uri'`.

title: Update path assumes the associated post still exists
body: In the update branch, `post = embed.post` is used without a nil check. The `belongs_to :post` association has no guarantee that the post still exists, and posts can be deleted. If `embed.post` is nil, `PostRevisor.new(post)` and subsequent calls on nil will raise. The importer should recreate the post or explicitly handle the missing record.

title: Concurrent imports for the same URL race and hit unique index
body: `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` is checked before the create transaction. Two concurrent jobs can both see no existing embed, both create topics/posts, and then the second `TopicEmbed.create!` fails on the unique index on `embed_url`, causing job failure. Re-check inside the transaction or rescue `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and re-fetch the existing embed.

title: request.referer is interpolated into JavaScript without escaping
body: `request.referer` is inserted directly into a JavaScript string. The controller only validates the host part of the referer, so a page on the allowed host whose URL contains a quote can break out of the JS string and execute script in the Discourse iframe's origin. Escape it with `j(request.referer)` or `escape_javascript`.

title: Invalid ERB syntax `<%- end if %>` will break rendering
body: The `if` block is closed as `end if` with no condition, which is not valid ERB/Ruby and will fail the embed page. This template is the success path for `/embed/best`; requests for an existing topic will error instead of rendering comments.

title: Imported raw HTML is rendered unescaped
body: `post.cooked` is emitted with `raw`. Imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` now returns `raw` directly for that method, bypassing Discourse's normal cooking/sanitization. RSS or readability content can therefore contain executable `<script>`/event-handler markup that runs in the Discourse origin for every visitor of the embedded comments.

title: URL is interpolated into HTML without escaping
body: The imported-from footer builds `#{url}` with the raw URL. A URL such as `http://example.com/'>` passes the `https?://` regex and breaks out of the attribute before being stored as raw HTML. This is an independent HTML/script injection vector and should be HTML-escaped or constructed with a safe helper.

title: PollFeed assumes every feed item has `content`
body: `i.content.scrub` raises `NoMethodError` when an RSS item uses the common `<description>` element or has no content instead of `content:encoded`. The importer should fall back to `i.content || i.description` and skip entries where both are blank.

title: fetch_http calls `.downcase` without checking `embed_by_username`
body: `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` can fail with `NoMethodError` when the setting is nil/unset, which the controller and RetrieveTopic do not prevent. PollFeed guards this setting with `present?` before polling, but `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` does not. Add a blank check and return early before querying.

title: Remote reads have no timeout
body: `open(url).read` uses default open/read timeouts, so a slow or stalled source can block a Sidekiq worker indefinitely. PollFeed has the same issue at `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29`. Use explicit `open_timeout` and `read_timeout` values or another HTTP client with timeout support.

title: Throttle key expiry is not atomic with creation
body: `setnx` followed by `expire` has a crash window between the two calls that can leave the `retrieved:<url>` key with no TTL. That URL would then be throttled forever. Use an atomic NX+EX set (or a Lua script/MULTI) so the key is always created with an expiry.

title: Disqus import loses original thread creation time
body: The previous importer passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` when creating the initial topic. The new `TopicEmbed.import_remote` path does not accept or set `created_at`, so imported topics are stamped with the current time while replies still use their original timestamps, breaking chronological ordering.

title: Invalid ERB syntax breaks embed rendering
body: The tag `<%- end if %>` is not valid Ruby/ERB; `end` cannot be followed by a postfix `if` like this. Template compilation raises a SyntaxError whenever this view is rendered, so the embed page will fail once a topic exists.

title: Imported feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered unsanitized
body: `url` is interpolated directly into HTML without escaping and only checked to start with `http(s)://`, so a URL like `http://evil.com/'><script>...` is injectable. The resulting `contents` are stored via PostCreator with `cook_method: raw_html` and then rendered in `embed/best` with `raw post.cooked`, so attacker-controlled feed or imported HTML can execute script in the forum embed context.

title: Missing embed_by_username causes nil.downcase crash
body: `fetch_http` calls `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` without checking the setting is present. If an embed is requested while `embeddable_host` is set but `embed_by_username` is not configured, the background job raises NoMethodError, so the loading page never resolves. This is an easy misconfiguration and should return or fallback instead of crashing.

title: postMessage targetOrigin uses full referer URL instead of origin
body: `request.referer` is the full embedding page URL (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com/2013/...`), but `Window.postMessage` requires the target origin (`http://eviltrout.com`). Passing the full URL with a path prevents the resize message from being delivered to the parent page, so the iframe height is never updated.

title: iframe URL is malformed when discourseUrl has no trailing slash
body: `discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` concatenates the path without a separator. If `discourseUrl` is configured as `http://forum.example.com` (no trailing slash), the iframe src becomes `http://forum.example.comembed/best?...`, which fails to load. Use `discourseUrl + "/embed/best?..."` or normalize the base URL.

title: PollFeed crashes on RSS items without content
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every RSS/Atom item has a `content` member. Many valid feeds only provide `description` or `summary`, so `i.content` is nil and the job raises, and since retry is disabled the entire poll run fails. The parser should use `i.content || i.description || i.summary` or explicitly skip missing content.

title: Throttle key expiration is not atomic with creation
body: `retrieved_recently?` calls `$redis.setnx` and then `$redis.expire` separately. If the process crashes between the two calls, the `retrieved:<url>` key is left without a TTL and the URL is effectively throttled forever. This should be done with an atomic `SET NX EX`-style command or ensure expiration in a Redis transaction.

title: `.small-action` flex container breaks right alignment of the action button
body: `.small-action` is now a flex container, but its button still relies on `float: right` for alignment. Floats have no effect on flex items, so if the button is a direct child it will sit right after `.small-action-desc` instead of at the row's right edge. If the button is nested inside `.small-action-desc`, that desc is now a content-sized flex item rather than full width, so the float no longer reaches the container edge. The small-action button (e.g. undo/dismiss) will no longer be right-aligned. Add `margin-left: auto` to the button and/or allow `.small-action-desc` to grow (`flex: 1`).

title: `align-items` mixin is missing `-moz-box-align` for the `-moz-box` fallback
body: `flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` emit `display: -moz-box` / `-moz-inline-box`, so old Firefox versions use the 2009-spec flexbox. However `align-items()` emits `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, `-ms-align-items`, and `align-items`, but never `-moz-box-align`. In those Firefox versions, `align-items: center` and `align-items: baseline` are ignored, so header contents, `.small-action`, and `.badge-wrapper.bullet` will not be center/baseline aligned when the `-moz-box` fallback is active. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment;` to the mixin.

title: small-action button no longer right-aligned
body: `.small-action` is now a flex container, so its children, including this `button`, are flex items. Floats do not apply to flex items, so `float: right` is ignored. There is also no `margin-left: auto`, `flex-grow`, or `order` on the preceding `.small-action-desc` or the button to push it to the right edge, so the button will sit immediately after the description content instead of being right-aligned. This regresses the existing small-action post layout.

title: Header panel right alignment depends on modern flexbox auto margins
body: `.panel` is no longer floated and is right-aligned only via `margin-left: auto` inside `.contents`, which the new `flexbox()` mixin turns into a flex container. That mixin also emits legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` fallbacks, but 2009 flexbox does not use auto margins for main-axis packing. Since no `box-pack: end` or equivalent fallback is provided, browsers that use those legacy declarations will not keep the panel right-aligned. If the fallbacks are meant to be supported, the header controls will be misplaced there.

title: align-items mixin omits Mozilla 2009 flexbox alignment fallback
body: `flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` emit `display: -moz-box` / `-moz-inline-box` fallbacks, but this `align-items` mixin emits `-webkit-box-align` for the 2009 box model without emitting `-moz-box-align`. As a result, Firefox versions using the `-moz-box` fallback will not get the intended `center` alignment for header `.contents` or `.small-action`, nor the `baseline` alignment for `.badge-wrapper.bullet`.

title: order mixin maps modern order values directly to 2009 box-ordinal-group
body: The 2009 `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group` properties start at 1, while modern `order` starts at 0. Passing the modern value unchanged means `order(1)` would map to ordinal group 1, the same as default siblings, and `order(0)` would be invalid in the old model. The old fallback should add 1 to the value. The current calls use 2 and 3 and happen to work, but the generic mixin is incorrect and will break when reused with 0 or 1.

title: Small-action button no longer right-aligned after flexbox conversion
body: The `.small-action` container is now a flex container via `@include flexbox()`, but the existing `button` rule still has `float: right` (line 309). Floats are ignored on flex items, and there is no `margin-left: auto` on the button or `flex-grow` on `.small-action-desc` to push it to the right edge. As a result, the button is laid out immediately after `.small-action-desc` rather than at the right edge of the row.

title: align-items mixin omits -moz-box-align for old Firefox fallback
body: `flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` emit `display: -moz-box` / `-moz-inline-box`, but `align-items()` does not emit the corresponding old Firefox property `-moz-box-align`. In a Firefox build that relies on the `-moz-box` fallback, the `center` or `baseline` alignment will be ignored. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment;` or remove the `-moz-box` display fallbacks.

title: website_name bypasses untrusted profile field hiding
body: The serializer hides `website` for restricted viewers by including it in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), but the new `website_name` attribute is derived from the same stored website and is not covered by that restriction. The inclusion hook added here also does not call `scope.restrict_user_fields?`, so for a TL0 user viewed anonymously, `website` can be omitted while `website_name` such as `example.com/path` is still serialized, leaking the profile website/path and defeating the existing privacy control.

title: include_website_name is not a predicate method
body: ActiveModel::Serializer decides whether to serialize an attribute by calling `include_<attribute>?`. The method here is named `include_website_name` without the trailing `?`, so it is not used by the serializer. As a result, `website_name` is always serialized even for users with no website, including `website_name: nil`, and the `website.present?` guard is dead code. The method should be renamed `include_website_name?` and covered with a no-website test.

title: Domain comparison treats public-suffix siblings as the same domain
body: The second branch compares all but the first DNS label, which misclassifies unrelated domains sharing a multi-label public suffix. For example, with `website_host = 'evil.co.uk'` and `discourse_host = 'example.co.uk'`, both have the same label count and the comparison drops the first label to match on `co.uk`, so the serializer returns `evil.co.uk/path` even though the website domain is neither the instance domain nor a parent/subdomain of it. A proper registrable-domain/public-suffix comparison is needed to avoid showing paths for unrelated sites.

title: website_name leaks hidden website info for anonymous TL0 users
body: `website_name` was added to the serialized attributes but was not added to `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111). `website_name` is derived from `website`, so even when the existing untrusted-attribute restriction suppresses the `website` key for anonymous visitors viewing a TL0 profile, the serializer still computes and emits `website_name`. This reveals the host and path of a website that is supposed to be hidden. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and make sure any manual `include_website_name?` does not override the generated restriction; the spec's untrusted attributes list should also be updated.

title: include_website_name is missing `?` and has no effect
body: ActiveModel Serializer conditional inclusion methods are named `include_<attribute>?` (see `include_email?` and `include_stats?` in this same file). The new method is `def include_website_name` without the trailing question mark, so it is never consulted during serialization. As a result, `website_name` is always included, producing `website_name: null` for users with no website or an unparsable website value instead of omitting the key. Rename it to `include_website_name?` or remove it in favor of the generated untrusted-attributes include method.

title: Same-domain check misses website subdomains such as www.example.com
body: The `else` branch only treats the user's website domain as a parent/suffix of the Discourse host (`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`). It does not handle the reverse case where the website is a subdomain of the Discourse host.
