For example, with `Discourse.current_hostname == 'example.com'` and `website == 'http://www.example.com/user'`, `website_name` returns `'www.example.com'` and drops `/user`, even though the sibling-subdomain logic indicates subdomains of the same registrable domain should show the path. This makes the new UX fail for the common bare-apex vs `www` configuration.

title: `include_website_name` is misnamed and dead code
body: Serializer inclusion callbacks use `include_website_name?` with a trailing question mark, and `untrusted_attributes` already defines that callback for `:website_name`. Defining `include_website_name` without `?` has no effect. It should be removed; simply renaming it to `include_website_name?` would override the untrusted guard and could expose `website_name` to restricted anonymous TL0 users.

title: TL0 anonymous untrusted attribute list not updated
body: `website_name` was added to the serializer's `untrusted_attributes` list, but the local `untrusted_attributes` array in the TL0 anonymous test still omits `:website_name`. The current test would pass even if `website_name` were exposed because no `website` is set in that context. Add a profile website and assert that `json` does not have `:website_name`.

title: Incorrect dark-theme color transform for embedded topic meta link
body: This replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The first argument should remain `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and the dark alternative should be `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`. As written, light themes get a much lighter link and dark themes get a much darker link, reducing contrast in the embedded-post topic metadata.

title: Dark/light arguments reversed for custom-message-length
body: The old value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The correct theme-aware form is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, but this patch uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` as the light-theme value and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` as the dark-theme value. This reverses the intended contrast and is inconsistent with the desktop modal.

title: Topic map h3 color changed to 50% instead of 20%/80% theme pair
body: The old value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The dark-theme equivalent should be `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)`, giving `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`. This patch uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, making the mobile topic map h3 significantly lighter in light themes and losing the intended contrast and hierarchy against h4.

title: Group member name uses wrong lightness values
body: This was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, so the theme-aware replacement should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. It is currently `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which removes the intended emphasis distinction from the 50%-lightness title and changes the rendered color in both themes.

title: Group member name uses wrong lightness values on mobile
body: This was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, so the theme-aware replacement should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. It is currently `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which removes the intended emphasis distinction from the 50%-lightness title and changes the rendered color in both themes.

title: Badge notification background has low contrast with its text in dark themes
body: `.badge-notification` sets `color: $secondary`. In a dark theme, `dark-light-choose` returns the second argument here: `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)`. Because `$secondary` is the dark background color in such themes, the background remains relatively dark while the text remains `$secondary`, producing dark-on-dark badges with insufficient contrast. The dark-theme background needs to be light, or the text color must be adapted for this base badge.

title: Embedded post author link color uses inverted light/dark lightness values
body: The old rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This changes the light-scheme color from 30% to 70% and gives the dark scheme 30% instead of the complementary 70%. The `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` link becomes washed out in light themes and too dark/low-contrast in dark themes. It should likely be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Custom message length color uses inverted light/dark lightness values
body: The old rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, but the replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light and dark arguments are swapped: the light theme now uses 30% instead of 70%, and the dark theme uses 70% instead of the expected 30%. This reverses the intended contrast for `.custom-message-length`. It should likely be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

title: Topic map h3 color changed from 20% to 50% lightness
body: The old rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but the replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-scheme value should remain 20%, and the dark-scheme value should be 80%, as done for the equivalent desktop rule. The new value reduces light-theme contrast and gives dark themes a less distinct heading color.

title: Group member name color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
body: The old rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-scheme value should remain 30%, and the dark-scheme value should be 70%. The new values reduce contrast for `.group-member-info .name` in both themes.

title: Group member name color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
body: The old rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-scheme value should remain 30%, and the dark-scheme value should be 70%. The new values reduce contrast for `.group-member-info .name` in both themes.

title: Missed dark-light-choose conversion for category badge notification
body: This rule still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` even though the rest of this PR converts equivalent `scale-color($primary, ...)` text/border colors to `dark-light-choose(..., scale-color($secondary, ...))`. As a result, `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still derives its color from `$primary` in dark themes, leaving an inconsistent color in the modified file.

title: Embedded post author link light-theme color changed from 30% to 70%
body: This rule was previously `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so light themes now get a 70% tint instead of the original 30% tint. That makes the embedded-post author link much lighter and lower-contrast in light themes. It should likely be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Group member name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50%
body: This rule was previously `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new value uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` for light themes, which makes group member names noticeably lighter and reduces contrast. The original 30% value should be preserved for light themes, with the dark theme branch using `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`.

title: Custom message length hint color inverted in light theme
body: This rule was previously `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, but the replacement uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` for light themes and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` for dark themes. This makes the hint text much darker in light themes and is inconsistent with the desktop conversion, which uses 70% primary / 30% secondary. It should likely be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

title: Topic map h3 light-theme color changed from 20% to 50%
body: This rule was previously `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The replacement uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` for light themes, weakening the header emphasis. The desktop counterpart was converted to 20% primary / 80% secondary. This should likely be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

title: Group member name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50%
body: This rule was previously `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new value uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` for light themes, making group member names lighter and reducing contrast. The original 30% value should be preserved for light themes, with the dark theme branch using `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`.

title: Missed dark-theme conversion for category badge notification color
body: This selector still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` directly, unlike the nearby th/td/topic-excerpt rules changed in this PR. In dark themes, category badge notification text will still use the primary-only value and remain inconsistent with the rest of the converted topic list. It should use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`.

title: totalPages is off by one for groups with an exact multiple of limit
body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 users with limit 50), this returns one extra page. The pagination controls then show page 1 of 2, leaving 'next' enabled. Clicking next sets offset to user_count, requests an empty page, and displays an empty last page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) and keep the zero-member special case.

title: Public group member pages are silently truncated to 50 users
body: The members action now defaults limit to 50 and always applies limit/offset. The public route group-members.js.es6 calls model.findMembers() with the model's defaults (limit 50, offset 0), and the public group/members.hbs template has no pagination controls. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members. As a result, any public group with more than 50 members will display only the first 50 with no way to reach the rest. Either add public pagination or preserve the old behavior for the public UI.

title: limit and offset are not validated or clamped
body: limit and offset are taken directly from query parameters with .to_i and passed to ActiveRecord's limit/offset. Negative values such as ?limit=-1 or ?offset=-1 can reach PostgreSQL, which rejects negative LIMIT/OFFSET and causes a 500. Very large limit values also allow a client to force a large result set. These values should be validated, clamped to sane bounds, or both.

title: Add members succeeds silently when usernames are not found
body: add_members looks up each username and silently skips users it cannot find, then returns success_json even if no members were added. The admin UI treats this as a successful Add operation, so a typo or whitespace after a comma can make the request report success while no user is added. The dedicated add-members endpoint should report unknown usernames or return validation errors instead of accepting them silently.

title: remove_member spec uses PUT instead of DELETE
body: The route is defined as delete "members" => "groups#remove_member", but this spec uses xhr :put, :remove_member. Controller specs invoke the action directly rather than going through the router, so this test would pass even if the DELETE route were missing or misrouted. It should use xhr :delete, and ideally a request spec should cover the actual route and HTTP method.

title: Pagination computes an extra page for exact multiples
body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is a positive multiple of limit (for example 50 users with limit 50), this returns 2 instead of 1. As a result the first page is not treated as the last page, Next sets offset to user_count, and the UI shows an empty second page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

title: Member list iterates controller property `members` instead of the group's members
body: The group-members route now sets the controller model to the Group object and calls model.findMembers(), which populates model.members. This template iterates `members` directly. The route does not set a controller property named `members`, so with the generated route controller the list will be empty. Iterate `model.members` or expose `members` on the controller.

title: Usernames are split on comma but not stripped
body: The client sends a comma-separated string. If it contains spaces, e.g. 'alice, bob', split(',') yields ' bob' and User.find_by_username(' bob') returns nil. The request then succeeds but silently skips valid users. Strip each username after splitting before lookup.

title: Group create ignores alias_level from the client
body: The client Group#asJSON sends alias_level and the admin form always displays the alias level combo for new groups, but create only sets name and visible. A new group saved with a non-default alias level is persisted with the default alias_level 0; the client model is only updated with the id from the response, so the UI continues showing the unsaved selection. Assign group.alias_level from params if present.

title: Automatic-group removal test uses PUT instead of the DELETE route
body: The routes map remove_member to DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members, but this spec calls xhr :put, :remove_member. Controller specs bypass the router and the action does not check request method, so the test does not verify the actual HTTP method or catch a misrouted DELETE. Use xhr :delete, :remove_member.

title: No spec for the paginated public members JSON contract
body: GroupsController#members changed from rendering a serialized member array to returning a custom {members, meta} object with limit, offset, and meta.total for all groups. This is a public API contract change, but no controller spec in the PR covers the JSON shape, default limit, offset, total, or authorization/visibility behavior.

title: totalPages off by one for exact multiples of limit
body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (for example 50 with the default limit 50), this returns 2 instead of 1. As a result showingLast is false, the next control is enabled, and clicking it sets offset to user_count, loading an empty second page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), preserving the existing zero-member special case.

title: Unbounded public group member query limit
body: GroupsController#members is reachable without authentication for any visible group. limit is taken directly from params[:limit] with no upper bound and no positive-integer validation. A request such as /groups/some-group/members.json?limit=100000000 forces the server to construct and serialize a huge result set, causing database load and memory exhaustion. Cap limit to a small maximum and reject values <= 0.

title: Public members endpoint response shape changed from array to object
body: Previously /groups/:group_id/members returned a JSON array of serialized users. It now returns an object with members and meta. Existing consumers of this public route that expect a top-level array will break. The SPA client was updated, but this is an unversioned contract change to a public API path.

title: PATCH update semantics were removed but PATCH still routes to update
body: The old update distinguished request.patch? and processed params[:changes] for incremental membership changes. The new update ignores changes, so a PATCH request (which resources :groups still routes to this action) will not add or remove members. Worse, because params[:visible] is absent, group.visible is set to false. Existing PATCH clients can silently hide a group and receive a success response.

title: Automatic group check evaluates against member user instead of group
body: group_member.hbs is used as the itemView for each member in {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}, so the template context is the member User object, not the group. User has no automatic property, so automatic is undefined/falsy and {{#unless automatic}} renders the remove link even for automatic groups. The server rejects removal with 422, but the UI exposes a control that fails with no client-side error handling.

title: Automatic remove_member test uses PUT instead of DELETE
body: The route for remove_member is delete "members" => "groups#remove_member" and the client sends DELETE. This spec calls xhr :put, :remove_member. Because controller specs dispatch the given action directly, the test does not verify that the production HTTP verb is routable and could pass even if the DELETE route is broken or removed. It should use xhr :delete, :remove_member.

title: Fallback translation files are only loaded for controller requests
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is invoked only from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` still only loads the current locale before translating and never loads fallback locales itself. In non-controller contexts such as Sidekiq jobs, mailers, or rake tasks, `I18n.translate` can be called with a non-English locale and a key missing from that locale. The site-default and English fallback locale files will not have been loaded, so fallback lookups can return a missing translation even when the key exists in the fallback files. Fallback loading should be triggered from the I18n translate path or wherever I18n.locale is set outside controllers.

title: Runtime default locale changes can serve stale fallback translations
body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` makes fallback results depend on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which can be changed at runtime by an admin. However `I18n.translate` in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` caches translations with a key composed only of the translation key, current locale, and backend object id (line 72). If `SiteSetting.default_locale` changes, cached missing-key translations for a locale will still reflect the old default locale, because the cache is not invalidated by the setting change and the cache key does not include fallback configuration. The cache key should include fallback-relevant information or the cache should be invalidated when the default locale changes.

title: English locale can fall back to a non-English site default
body: The fallback list is always `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`. When `I18n.locale` is `:en` and the site default is not English, this reduces to `[:en, :fr]` (for example). A missing English translation will then be looked up in the site-default language instead of remaining English. For English requests the site-default fallback should not be inserted after `:en`; the chain should stop at `[:en]` or otherwise prefer English last.

title: No tests added for fallback behavior
body: This PR introduces a custom fallback order, eager fallback loading, and removal of environment fallback configuration, but adds no specs. The behavior around missing keys, English vs site default locale, runtime default locale changes, and non-controller translation paths is subtle and can regress silently. Tests should cover `FallbackLocaleList` ordering and ensure fallback locales are loaded in all contexts that call `I18n.translate`.

title: Fallback locales are loaded only for controller requests
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only called from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. `I18n.translate` in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` lazy-loads only the current locale via `load_locale(config.locale)`, so translations performed outside controller actions (for example mailers, background jobs, or rake tasks) with a non-default locale will not have the site-default or `:en` YAML loaded before fallback lookup runs. A missing key in the current locale can then fail or produce an I18n missing-translation error instead of falling back. The fallback preloading must happen wherever `I18n.locale` is set, or `translate` should load the fallback chain itself.

title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain
body: The cached translation key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With the new fallback chain `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`, a translation that is missing in the requested locale can be resolved from a fallback locale and then cached under the requested locale. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` changes at runtime, the same key and locale would need a different fallback resolution, but the old cached value is still returned until `I18n.reload!` clears the cache. This can serve stale translations after an admin changes the default locale. Include the fallback chain in the cache key or invalidate the translation cache when the default locale changes.

title: No tests cover the new fallback behavior
body: This PR introduces a custom fallback order, loads fallbacks and pluralization in a new initializer, removes environment-specific fallback flags, and adds `ensure_loaded!` wiring, but no specs are added. The behavior should be tested: anonymous users use the site default, logged-in users fall back in the expected order, fallback locale YAMLs are actually loaded, and non-controller translation paths do not regress. Without tests, this lazy-loading/fallback interaction is easy to break.

title: Fallback locales are only preloaded for controller requests
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only called from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. The patched `I18n.translate` lazily loads only `config.locale` (`lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68`), so server-side code outside the controller, such as Sidekiq jobs, mailers, and rake tasks, does not load the fallback locale's YAML. When a translation is missing in the current locale, the Fallbacks backend tries `:en`, but `en.yml` may not be loaded, so the lookup raises a missing translation instead of returning the English fallback. Fallback locales should be ensured in the translation path or in a global locale change hook, not just in this before_filter.

title: No tests cover the new fallback order or lazy loading
body: The PR adds custom fallback behavior (`FallbackLocaleList`) and a controller `ensure_loaded!` call, but includes no tests. At minimum, specs should assert the fallback order, that fallback locale files get loaded, and that translations in non-controller contexts such as jobs or mailers fall back correctly; otherwise the lazy-loading bug can regress.

title: Denial cache key uses raw underscore concatenation and can collide
body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` builds the cache key as `namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent`. Because the fields are not length-prefixed or escaped, different tuples containing underscores can map to the same key; for example, `name="a", parent="b_c"` and `name="a_b", parent="c"` both produce a suffix of `a_b_c`. A cached denial for one dashboard/folder can then falsely deny access to a different allowed resource for the same user/action until the TTL expires. Use a collision-resistant key such as a hash of the fields or length-delimited concatenation.

title: Check re-queries permissions for every distinct denied resource
body: After a cached permission map is found but the requested resource is not allowed, `Check` unconditionally falls through to `getIdentityPermissions`, which queries the permission store. The subsequent denial cache only prevents repeats for the exact `name`+`parent` tuple. For a user with a cached empty or stale permission map, each unique `Name` causes a fresh DB permissions query. This allows sequential requests with arbitrary unique resource names to bypass the action-level permission cache and impose significant DB load. Consider rate-limiting or deduplicating these fallbacks, or using a per-action last-refresh/negative TTL instead of a full DB query per denied resource.

title: Remote AuthZ client still caches decisions and bypasses the server-side fix
body: `newRemoteRBACClient` still configures `authzlib.NewClient` with a 30-second local cache. The PR disables the authlib client cache only for the in-process path via `NoopCache`. In remote/standalone deployments, `Check`/`List` results, including false denials, can be served from this client-side cache and never reach the server-side denial-cache and DB requery logic. Users in those modes can therefore still be denied access to newly created dashboards/folders for up to 30 seconds. If the fix is intended for all modes, the remote client cache needs to be disabled, shortened, or invalidated on resource creation.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type, so anonymous denials can deny renderer requests
body: The denial cache key is built from checkReq.UserUID but not checkReq.IdentityType. Both `anonymous:0` and `render:0` parse to the same userUID `0` in validateSubject, so a denied anonymous Check for a dashboard/folder creates the same permDenialCache key that a later renderer Check for the same namespace/action/name/folder will hit. The renderer path would normally return allowed for `dashboards:read` via getRendererPermissions, but the cached denial is returned first. An attacker who can cause repeated anonymous denied checks can keep this entry warm and deny rendering for that resource.

title: Denial cache key concatenation permits collisions between different resource tuples
body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates namespace, userUID, action, name, and parent with underscore separators without escaping or length delimiting. These values are not prevented from containing underscores, and an empty parent adds a trailing separator. For example, name=`a_b`, parent=`` produces the same key as name=`a`, parent=`b` for the same user/action. A cached denial for one dashboard/folder can therefore incorrectly deny another resource. Use length-prefixed or hashed components to make the tuple unambiguous.

title: Denial cache test does not prove denial cache is being used
body: The test `Should deny on explicit cache deny entry` sets the permission cache to `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}` and leaves fakeStore permissions empty. If the denial cache lookup were removed or its key did not match, the cached false permission and empty DB result would still produce `Allowed: false`, so the test passes without exercising the denial cache. It should set the cached permission to `true` or provide a DB permission that would allow the request, so the assertion fails if the denial cache is not consulted.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type, so anonymous denials can deny renderer access
body: The denial cache key is built from `checkReq.UserUID`, action, name, and parent folder only. `validateSubject` returns the same UID `"0"` for both `anonymous:0` and `render:0`. If an anonymous check for a dashboard is denied, `permDenialCache` stores a key such as `org-12.perm_0_dashboards:read_dash1_fold1`. A later renderer check for the same dashboard and folder hits this denial entry at line 117 and returns `Allowed: false` before `getRendererPermissions` can grant the renderer wildcard read access. This causes authorized rendering to fail depending on prior anonymous requests.

title: List treats a cached empty or stale permission map as authoritative and skips DB refresh
body: `List` only falls back to `getIdentityPermissions` when `getCachedIdentityPermissions` returns an error. A cached empty map (`map[string]bool{}`) is a successful cache hit, so `List` passes it directly to `listPermission`. A user who listed dashboards before creating any (or before the new permission was granted) can have an empty/partial `permCache` entry; after creating a dashboard, the next list request will keep returning the stale cached map until the 30s TTL expires. The client-side `NoopCache` change does not help because this is the server-side `permCache`. This undermines the PR goal of letting creators fetch newly created dashboards/folders.

title: Permission denial cache key can collide when name/parent contain underscores
body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` concatenates namespace, UID, action, name, and parent with underscores and no escaping or length delimiter. Dashboard names and folder UIDs can contain underscores, so distinct tuples can produce the same key. For example, `name="a_b", parent="c"` and `name="a", parent="b_c"` both produce a suffix like `dashboards:read_a_b_c`. A cached denial for one resource can therefore be served for a different resource, causing an authorized check to be denied.

title: Federated rule immutability lost for CombinedRule callers
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` is now implemented by delegating to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`, but `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hardcodes `isFederated = false` and has no access to the original rule group. The previous `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` checked `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, which made update and delete abilities unsupported for federated rule groups. As a result, callers using `useAlertRuleAbility`/`useAlertRuleAbilities` with a `CombinedRule` will now treat federated data-source rule groups as mutable, allowing edit/delete actions to be shown and invoked when they should be blocked.

title: skipToken path still evaluates Grafana permissions and can allow Duplicate for cloud rules
body: `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` maps `skipToken` to `undefined` and calls `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)`. For a missing rule, `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` returns `loading: false`, so `MaybeSupported` becomes `AlwaysSupported` and `duplicateSupported` becomes true. The hook then evaluates `getRulesPermissions('grafana')`. In `AlertRuleMenu`, this hook is called with `skipToken` for non-Grafana (cloud) Prom rules, so a user with Grafana rule-create permission but without the data source's create permission can see Duplicate enabled for a cloud rule even though the ruler-based ability would deny it.

title: Delete and pause actions are still gated on rulerRule, so they disappear in the ruler-less list view
body: The new `GrafanaRuleListItem` renders `RuleActionsButtons` with only `promRule`, so `AlertRuleMenu` receives `rulerRule` as undefined. However, Delete is still rendered only when `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165), and Pause is still rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` is true (line 123). The component now computes `canDelete` and `canPause` from Prom-based abilities, but users cannot ever see or use those actions in the list view because the old ruler-based guards remain.

title: Silence menu item is shown in ruler-less list view but the drawer is never rendered
body: `AlertRuleMenu` can show the Silence notifications item based on the new Prom-based `canSilence` ability, and clicking it calls `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`. But `RuleActionsButtons` only renders `<SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer>` when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true. In the new list path `rule` (the ruler rule) is undefined, so the drawer is never rendered. The user sees and can click Silence, but nothing happens.

title: Missing React key on GrafanaRuleListItem in FilterView
body: In `rules.map`, the computed `key` is passed to `DataSourceRuleLoader` and `UnknownRuleListItem`, but the Grafana branch renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` without `key={key}`. React falls back to index keys, so list items can be reconciled incorrectly when rules are appended, reordered, or filtered, and React will emit a key warning.

title: Silence menu item is shown but clicking it does nothing when only promRule is available
body: In the new prom-only rule list, RuleActionsButtons receives no `rule`/rulerRule. AlertRuleMenu shows the Silence item because `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` can report it as supported and allowed, and clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer` to true. However this render condition requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`; with `rule` undefined it is false, so `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` is never rendered and the user-visible action is a dead click. Either hide/disable the Silence item when no ruler rule is available or make the drawer work from the prom rule.

title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable in CombinedRule ability checks
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (still used by `useAlertRuleAbility` and `useAlertRuleAbilities`) now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `isFederated = false`. The previous `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` implementation computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and used it to make Update, Delete, Pause, and Restore unsupported for federated rule groups. After this change, CombinedRule callers can report those actions as supported for federated rules when the user has ordinary permissions, so the UI may expose edit/delete actions that are disallowed for federated rules.

title: Delete action is hidden for prom-only Grafana rules even when canDelete is true
body: The new alert list view passes `promRule` but no `rulerRule`. `canDelete` can be true via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, but the Delete menu item is guarded by both `canDelete` and `rulerRule`. Since `rulerRule` is undefined in the prom-only list, users with delete permission no longer see Delete for Grafana rules. `RuleActionsButtons` already builds a valid identifier from `promRule`, so this guard should be updated or the removal should be intentional and documented.

title: Pause action is never shown for prom-only Grafana rules despite canPause
body: `canPause` is computed using either rulerRule or Grafana prom rule abilities, and can be true in the new prom-only list. However the Pause menu item is additionally guarded by `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`. With no rulerRule, the Pause item never renders, so the newly added `grafanaPauseAbility` is ineffective and pause access disappears from the alert list view.

title: GrafanaRuleListItem is rendered without a React key
body: In `FilterViewResults`, `rules.map` destructures `key` from each `RuleWithOrigin`, and the datasource and unknown branches pass `key={key}` to their list items. The `grafana` branch returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` without a key. React will warn and may reuse or misreconcile component state when Grafana rules are reordered, added, or removed. Add `key={key}` to this branch.

title: Rule view link no longer preserves returnTo navigation
body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` implementation used `createReturnTo()` and passed `{ returnTo }` to `createRelativeUrl` when building the rule view href. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem` builds the same href without `returnTo`, so navigating from the rule list to the rule view no longer carries the return location and in-app back/return behavior can be regressed. If this is intentional, it should be documented; otherwise the `returnTo` query should be retained.

title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities used to check isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) before deciding whether update, delete, pause, etc. were supported. After this change it delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which only receives a RulerRuleDTO and a group identifier, and now hardcodes isFederated = false. As a result, federated rule groups can be reported as editable/removable when datasource/folder permissions allow, breaking the previous immutability guard for federated rules.

title: Missing key prop on GrafanaRuleListItem in filtered rule list
body: In the rules.map branch for origin === 'grafana', the newly rendered GrafanaRuleListItem has no key prop, while the other branches use key={key}. Since this is a React list, the missing key causes index-based reconciliation, which can reuse component state such as open menus or focus for the wrong rule as the list changes and triggers React warnings. Pass key={key} to GrafanaRuleListItem.

title: Silence drawer never opens for prom-only Grafana rules
body: GrafanaRuleListItem now renders RuleActionsButtons with only promRule, so rule is undefined. The AlertRuleMenu can show the Silence notifications item based on the promRule ability, and handleSilence sets showSilenceDrawer to true, but this line only renders SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. With rule undefined, clicking Silence does nothing in the new list view. The condition and drawer data need to support the promRule-only path.

title: Pause action is missing for Grafana rules in the alert list view
body: canPause is now computed from useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities when only promRule is available, but the pause menu item is still gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) and passes rulerRule to MenuItemPauseRule. In the prom-only alert list view rulerRule is undefined, so the pause action never renders even when canPause is true. Use a pause item that accepts GrafanaPromRuleDTO or derive the required data from promRule, or remove the promRule pause ability if pause is intentionally unsupported.

title: Delete action is missing for Grafana rules in the alert list view
body: The Delete Menu.Item is still wrapped in {canDelete && rulerRule && ...}. In the new prom-only alert list view rulerRule is undefined, so Delete never appears even when useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities reports delete as supported and allowed. The actual delete handler passed from RuleActionsButtons already uses only the identifier and groupIdentifier, so the rulerRule guard appears unnecessary and removes delete functionality from the list view.

title: Duplicate action can appear for data source rules based on Grafana create permission
body: For a non-Grafana promRule, AlertRuleMenu passes skipToken to useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities. However, skipToken is mapped to undefined, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) returns Duplicate as supported with getRulesPermissions('grafana').create as the allowed permission. Because canDuplicate ORs that result with the ruler ability, a data source rule can show the Duplicate menu item even if the user lacks the external write permission required for that rule. This is a UI authorization regression; the backend may still reject the action.

title: View link no longer preserves returnTo
body: The removed GrafanaRuleLoader created the rule view URL with { returnTo: createReturnTo() }. The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds the same /alerting/grafana/${uid}/view URL without returnTo, so navigating from the alert list to a rule and then using in-app back/return controls may no longer return to the previous filtered list. Add returnTo back if list navigation should be preserved.

title: Interpolation makes `isQueryWithRangeVariable` guard ineffective
body: `runSplitQuery` now maps targets through `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` before `partition(queries, (query) => !querySupportsSplitting(query))`. `querySupportsSplitting` calls `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to avoid splitting queries containing `$__range` (or similar range variables), but after interpolation those variables have already been replaced with duration literals, so the guard no longer detects them. Queries that were deliberately excluded from time-splitting will now be split, and each subrequest will use an expression interpolated against the full request range rather than the intended unsplit query. This can produce incorrect result semantics. The check should be done against the pre-interpolation expression, or the guard must be intentionally re-evaluated with tests.

title: Shard splitting applies template variables twice
body: `runShardSplitQuery` now applies `applyTemplateVariables` to every target at line 52. Later, `splitQueriesByStreamShard` passes those same targets to `runSplitQuery` (line 163), and the modified `runSplitQuery` applies `applyTemplateVariables` again to its targets (querySplitting.ts line 299). This double interpolation is not guaranteed to be idempotent; in particular, if `request.filters` contains ad hoc filters, `applyTemplateVariables` can insert those filters into the expression on each call, duplicating filter selectors in the final query. The new test expectation that `applyTemplateVariables` is called five times for one target reflects this duplication rather than guarding against it. `runSplitQuery` should support skipping interpolation when the caller has already interpolated, or this path should avoid pre-interpolating before delegating.

title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting bypasses the $__range split guard
body: The new `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` runs before `querySupportsSplitting`. `querySupportsSplitting` is designed to reject queries containing `$__range`/`$__range_ms` via `isQueryWithRangeVariable`, with a comment explaining these queries must not be split because the range variable would be interpreted relative to the split sub-range and produce an incorrect result. Since `applyTemplateVariables` replaces `$__range`/`$__range_ms`, the check on the interpolated expr no longer sees them and will allow time-splitting of those queries. The range-variable check should be performed on the pre-interpolated expression or otherwise preserve the raw expression for this guard.

title: Shard splitting applies template variables twice per query
body: `runShardSplitQuery` now interpolates every target with `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` at line 52. Later, `splitQueriesByStreamShard` sends each shard sub-request through `runSplitQuery` (line 163), which now also applies `applyTemplateVariables` to each target. Each query is interpolated again for every shard/time sub-request; the test change even asserts `applyTemplateVariables` is called five times for a single target. If variable replacement is not idempotent (for example, a variable value contains `$` or template-variable syntax), the second pass can change the query incorrectly. One of the two layers should avoid re-interpolating already-interpolated targets.

title: Queries can become empty after interpolation but are not re-filtered
body: The target pipe filters `query.expr` before `applyTemplateVariables`. When a non-empty template expression such as `$var` resolves to an empty string, the query remains in `queries` and proceeds through partitioning. Since the interpolated empty expr is not a logs query, it is treated as a metric query and sent to Loki with `expr: ''`. Reorder the pipe to interpolate first and then `.filter((query) => query.expr)` so queries whose value is empty are skipped.

title: $__range queries are now split because interpolation happens before the guard
body: runSplitQuery() now maps request.targets through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() in the chain ending at line 299, before the querySupportsSplitting() partition on line 300. querySupportsSplitting() deliberately returns false for expressions containing $__range via !isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) (line 287), but by the time it runs, $__range has already been replaced with a concrete duration such as '3d'. The guard is therefore dead. For example, count_over_time({job="x"}[$__range]) over a 3-day window will now be split into one-day subqueries while each subquery still carries the full original range vector, which is not equivalent to the intended single unsplit query and can produce incorrect/duplicated metric results. The range-variable decision must be made on the pre-interpolation expression, or an explicit flag must be preserved; the now-stale comment should also be updated.

title: Shard splitting interpolates the same queries twice
body: runShardSplitQuery() interpolates every target at line 52, and the resulting splittingTargets are later used to build subRequest (line 154) and passed to runSplitQuery() (line 163). runSplitQuery() now also applies applyTemplateVariables() to each target in its own pipeline (querySplitting.ts lines 296-299). As a result, every sub-query in the shard-splitting path is interpolated twice; the test in this PR now asserts five applyTemplateVariables calls for a single initial target. Plain substitutions may be harmless, but interpolation is not safely idempotent when a substituted value itself contains template syntax such as $... or [[...]], and it is redundant work otherwise. The shard path should avoid re-interpolating already-interpolated targets, or runSplitQuery should support an already-interpolated/internal entry point.

title: Plugin request logs no longer include traceID
body: The previous logRequest appended `traceID` from `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` to the `Plugin Request Completed` log params. This change removes that field entirely, and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName/dsUID, and uname. As a result these plugin request logs lose trace correlation, which is a regression for debugging and tracing. Add `traceID` to `logParams` (or to `instrumentContext`) before logging.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, hiding logs made via FromContext
body: LoggerMiddleware now logs through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. A TestLogger passed to NewLoggerMiddleware will have `FromContext` return a brand-new TestLogger, so the original TestLogger's `InfoLogs` (and other log fields) will not be incremented. Any existing or future logger middleware test using this fake cannot observe the log call. Return `f` (or otherwise share the log fields) so FromContext preserves observability.

title: Logger name still says 'plugin.instrumentation'
body: After renaming InstrumentationMiddleware to MetricsMiddleware and adding ContextualLoggerMiddleware, the logger for LoggerMiddleware is still constructed with `log.New("plugin.instrumentation")`. Log messages emitted by the request logger will continue to appear under the old instrumentation name, which is misleading and inconsistent with the PR's naming goal. Rename it to reflect the actual logger purpose (for example `plugin.requests` or `plugin.logger`).

title: Plugin request logs lose traceID
body: The previous `logRequest` appended `traceID` from `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` to the request completion log. This change removes that field and the `tracing` import. The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname; it does not add a trace ID. Unless some unchanged middleware already injects traceID as a contextual log attribute, `Plugin Request Completed` entries will no longer contain a trace ID, breaking log-to-trace correlation.

title: LoggerMiddleware now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware
body: `LoggerMiddleware` no longer includes pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, or dsUID in its own log params. It now calls `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` and expects those fields to already be present in the context. Production middleware ordering in `CreateMiddlewares` inserts `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware` before it, so the production path gets those fields. However `NewLoggerMiddleware` is exported and can be used independently; any caller that builds a middleware stack without the new contextual middleware will get request logs with those fields silently missing. This hidden ordering dependency should be documented, enforced, or avoided by keeping the fields inside `LoggerMiddleware`.

title: TestLogger.FromContext drops the logger whose logs tests inspect
body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning `f` or a logger that shares `f`'s `Logs` fields. Since `LoggerMiddleware` now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, any test that passes a `*TestLogger` and then asserts on the original logger's `InfoLogs`/`ErrorLogs` will observe zero calls because the actual log is written to a brand-new `TestLogger`. The fake should preserve the same test logger or share its log counters/fields.

title: Adding FromContext to Logger is a source-breaking interface change
body: The exported `log.Logger` interface now requires `FromContext(context.Context) Logger`. Any existing implementation outside this package, including external/enterprise code, will no longer satisfy the interface and will fail to compile until it adds the method. If `pkg/plugins/log` is consumed as an API, this should be introduced as an optional interface or with a compatibility/deprecation path.

title: Exported InstrumentationMiddleware symbols removed without compatibility aliases
body: This renames the exported `InstrumentationMiddleware` type and `NewInstrumentationMiddleware` constructor to `MetricsMiddleware` and `NewMetricsMiddleware`. Because `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware` is not an `internal` package, downstream importers such as enterprise or external code will fail to compile after upgrading. If the package is public API, keep deprecated alias symbols during the transition or coordinate the breaking change explicitly.

title: Plugin request completion logs lose traceID field
body: Previously, logRequest appended traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) to logParams and imported pkg/infra/tracing. That field and import are removed here. The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware/instrumentContext only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname; it does not add traceID, and m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info has no inherent way to recover it. As a result, every "Plugin Request Completed" log loses trace correlation. If this was not intentional, traceID should be added to the contextual attributes or kept in logParams.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards original logger so log assertions are lost
body: LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now logs through m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info. TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger() instead of returning f or a logger sharing f's Logs. Any test that passes a *TestLogger to NewLoggerMiddleware and then inspects InfoLogs/Calls or Message against that original TestLogger will see zero values, because the actual log was recorded on a fresh, inaccessible TestLogger. Returning f, or otherwise sharing the same counters, would preserve the previous assertion behavior.

title: Adding FromContext to Logger is a source-breaking interface change
body: Logger is a public interface in pkg/plugins/log. Adding FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger forces every implementation and mock of Logger to implement the new method. This diff updates TestLogger and grafanaInfraLogWrapper, but any other implementation in the repository or any external consumer of this package will fail to compile. If backward compatibility matters, keep Logger unchanged and define a separate optional interface such as ContextualLogger that LoggerMiddleware can type-assert.

title: No tests cover the new contextual logger behavior
body: The PR adds ContextualLoggerMiddleware and changes LoggerMiddleware to obtain pluginId, endpoint, user and datasource fields from FromContext(ctx) instead of passing them explicitly. The only test change in the diff renames the metrics test to use newMetricsMiddleware; there is no test that verifies QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth or CollectMetrics adds the expected contextual attributes, nor that LoggerMiddleware actually emits those fields in the completion log. A middleware ordering or context-propagation mistake would not be caught.

title: New updateDevice SQL uses `?` placeholders on PostgreSQL
body: The new `updateDevice` query uses `?` placeholders unconditionally (`... WHERE device_id = ? ...`), but PostgreSQL requires `$1`-style placeholders. The same file's `CreateOrUpdateDevice` explicitly uses `$1` for `migrator.Postgres`, so this path will fail when `device_limit` is reached on Postgres. Because `Anonymous.Authenticate` only treats `ErrDeviceLimitReached` as fatal and logs other TagDevice errors, a placeholder error here is swallowed and the device limit is not enforced.

title: Rejected devices are cached before persistence, allowing device-limit bypass
body: `tagDeviceUI` checks and sets the local cache before `CreateOrUpdateDevice`. When a new device ID hits the limit, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, but the device ID is already cached. A retry with the same `X-Grafana-Device-Id` finds the cache entry, skips the device store and limit check, returns nil, and `Anonymous.Authenticate` completes successfully. This makes the configured limit trivially bypassable. Move the cache write to after a successful DB write or invalidate the key on error.

title: Count-then-insert race can exceed anonymous device limit
body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` performs a `CountDevices` check and then inserts when below limit without any transaction, lock, or serializable isolation. Concurrent anonymous sign-ins with different device IDs can all observe a count below `deviceLimit` and then insert, exceeding the configured limit. If the limit is intended to be enforced, the count and insert/update must be made atomic.

title: Device-limit rejection is bypassable by retrying with the same device ID
body: In tagDeviceUI the local cache entry is set before CreateOrUpdateDevice. When CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the cache entry remains. TagDevice propagates the error so the first anonymous authentication request fails, but any subsequent request with the same X-Grafana-Device-Id on the same instance within the 29-minute local-cache TTL sees the cached key and returns nil without touching the store. Anonymous.Authenticate then succeeds, so a client can bypass the configured device limit simply by retrying.

title: Clients can bypass the device limit by omitting the device ID header
body: TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is empty. Since Anonymous.Authenticate now only rejects when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, an anonymous request that omits this header is never counted and always proceeds even when the configured limit has been reached. If the device limit is intended to be enforced, missing or empty device IDs should not silently skip enforcement.

title: Device limit check and insert are not atomic
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice first calls CountDevices and then, if count < deviceLimit, performs an upsert. There is no transaction, lock, or database-enforced cap around these two operations. Concurrent requests from different devices can all observe a count below the limit and then insert, so the configured device limit can be exceeded under normal concurrent anonymous traffic.

title: Anonymous authentication now blocks on synchronous device-store writes
body: Authenticate now calls TagDevice synchronously before returning an identity. On a local-cache miss, TagDevice performs a database count when the limit is enabled and an insert/update upsert for each new device, and again after the 29-minute local-cache TTL. Previously this work ran in a background goroutine with a timeout and did not delay login. This adds database latency and database-availability risk to the anonymous authentication path.

title: RowsAffected == 0 can incorrectly reject existing devices on MySQL
body: updateDevice treats RowsAffected() == 0 as proof that no existing device was updated and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL default behavior, the affected-row count for UPDATE is the number of rows changed, not rows matched. An existing device row whose client_ip, user_agent, and updated_at already equal the supplied values can produce 0 affected rows and be rejected incorrectly. Use CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS, a follow-up existence check, or otherwise distinguish 'updated an existing row' from 'no matching row'.

title: Authn client is coupled to the anonstore storage package for a sentinel error
body: Authenticate imports pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore and uses errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached). This couples the authentication client to a concrete database-store implementation. The sentinel error should be part of the anonymous service contract or a shared service package so alternate anonymous.Service implementations can signal the same condition without importing storage internals.

title: Device limit can be bypassed by retrying after a rejected tag
body: In tagDeviceUI, the device ID is written to localCache before CreateOrUpdateDevice is called. If CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached on the first attempt, the cache entry remains. A retry for the same device within the cache TTL hits the cached entry and returns nil before reaching the store, so Anonymous.Authenticate no longer sees ErrDeviceLimitReached and anonymous authentication succeeds. This makes the configured device limit bypassable after one retry, and the rejected device is never recorded.

title: Device limit enforcement is not atomic
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the limit with a separate CountDevices call followed by an insert/upsert, with no transaction, row lock, or serialization. Two different new devices can concurrently both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert, so the stored number of devices can exceed the configured limit. For example, with deviceLimit=1, two concurrent new device requests can both count 0 and both insert, leaving 2 devices.

title: Anonymous authentication now synchronously writes to the device store
body: Anonymous.Authenticate now calls TagDevice synchronously on the authentication path. Previously this work was fire-and-forget in a background goroutine. With the default anonymousDeviceLimit=0 this feature is not even active, but every cache-missing anonymous request must still wait for a database upsert before authentication completes. This adds database write latency to anonymous login/page-load paths and is a performance regression for all anonymous traffic.

title: updateDevice can falsely report ErrDeviceLimitReached for an existing device
body: updateDevice treats RowsAffected() == 0 as proof that the device is missing or stale and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL, UPDATE RowsAffected is commonly the number of rows changed, not matched. If an existing row already has the same client_ip, user_agent, and updated_at values (for example, requests within the same second when the timestamp column has second precision), the update can affect 0 rows even though the device exists. The existing device is then rejected and anonymous authentication fails unexpectedly. The code should distinguish 'matched but unchanged' from 'not matched', such as by using CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS or checking existence separately.

title: Cleanup ticker reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
body: This change is unrelated to the annotation deadlock fix and makes the entire cleanup suite (old annotations, expired snapshots/dashboard versions/images, temp users, short URLs, query history) run 10x more often. `clean` has a 9-minute timeout, so with a 1-minute ticker a long cleanup can finish and then immediately consume a queued tick, creating sustained high DB/CPU load. More frequent annotation cleanup may also reintroduce the write/lock pressure that the PR is trying to avoid. This appears accidental; revert or explain and justify this scheduling change.

title: Normal cleanup batches logged as errors with full ID lists
body: The new cleanup paths call `r.log.Error` for successful fetch/delete iterations (`Annotations to clean by time`, `cleaned annotations by time`, etc.). The fetch log returns before logging when `fetchIDs` fails, so those logs always have err == nil and represent normal operation. This generates error-level noise/false alerts and logs the full `ids` slice per batch, which is very large for big `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` values. Use debug or info level and avoid dumping all IDs (same pattern at lines 537, 554, 557, 576 and 579).

title: Non-SQLite deletion path can exceed database bind limits
body: `deleteByIDs` builds `id IN (?,?,...)` with one placeholder per ID for every non-SQLite database. The previous subquery-based DELETE did not bind one parameter per row, so very large `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` values were safer. PostgreSQL has a bind-parameter limit of 32767, and MySQL/similar databases have practical packet/query-size limits. If the configured batch size exceeds the database limit, cleanup fails even though the old statement worked. The SQLite branch is special-cased by inlining IDs; the non-SQLite path should also chunk the delete by IDs or otherwise use a dialect-safe limit.

title: Per-subtest cleanup is registered after data is inserted
body: Each table-driven subtest calls `createTestAnnotations` and performs initial count assertions before registering the `t.Cleanup` that deletes `annotation` and `annotation_tag`. If setup or one of these initial `require` assertions fails, `t.Cleanup` is never registered, leaving up to 40k annotations and 80k tags in the shared test DB; subsequent subtests then run against polluted data and produce cascading failures. Register the cleanup before inserting/asserting data, or otherwise guarantee cleanup runs on any setup failure.

title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
body: The ticker interval for the entire cleanup service was changed from time.Minute * 10 to time.Minute * 1. This is unrelated to the annotation deadlock fix and greatly increases how often all cleanup jobs run, including snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, and query history. Since clean() has a 9-minute timeout and cleanup jobs can take a while, a 1-minute ticker can cause cleanup to run nearly continuously or back-to-back. If this was not intentional, it should be reverted or explicitly justified.

title: Cleanup logs successful batch operations at error level
body: The new batch cleanup code calls r.log.Error for every batch even when there is no error: see lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579. For example, after fetchIDs succeeds, line 534 logs 'Annotations to clean by time' with err=nil, and line 537 logs 'cleaned annotations by time' even when deleteByIDs returns nil. These calls happen for no-op batches with zero IDs and can include large 'ids' slices up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize (e.g. 32767). This floods logs with error-level events during normal cleanup, can trigger log-based alerts, and is misleading. Use Debug/Info for successful batch progress and avoid logging full ID slices at Error level.

title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute without related rationale
body: This PR is focused on the annotation cleanup SQL, but this change reduces the top-level cleanup service ticker from every 10 minutes to every 1 minute. That makes all cleanup jobs run ten times as often, which can significantly increase database load and contention, including for the annotation cleanup job this PR is trying to make safer. If this was not intentional, it should be reverted; if it was intentional, it deserves an explicit note in the PR because it is an unrelated behavioral change.

title: Routine annotation cleanup logs full ID batches at error level
body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags call r.log.Error after successfully fetching IDs and include the entire ids slice, for example line 534: r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, "cond", cond, "err", err). The err variable is nil at that point because errors return early, so this logs every successful batch as an error. The ids slice can be as large as AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, which the new test sets to 32767, so this can flood error logs with large ID lists and impose significant log I/O/CPU. Log successful progress at debug level without dumping all IDs, and reserve error-level logging for actual errors.

title: SQLite IN-list construction is quadratic
body: deleteByIDs builds the inline SQLite ID list with repeated fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v). Each iteration copies the entire accumulated string, making this O(n²) in the number of IDs. For configured batch sizes like the test's 32767, this can copy gigabytes of string data per batch and make cleanup slow or CPU-spiky on SQLite. A strings.Builder or strconv.AppendInt-based construction would avoid the repeated full-string copies.

title: Subtest cleanup is registered after data creation and initial assertions
body: In TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp, each subtest calls createTestAnnotations and performs initial count assertions before registering the t.Cleanup function that deletes the rows. If any of those early require calls fail, the cleanup is never installed, leaving data in the shared test database and causing later subtests to fail with confusing cascading assertion errors. The t.Cleanup that deletes annotation and annotation_tag rows should be registered before inserting data for the subtest.

title: Async legacy writes inherit the request context and are canceled after the handler returns
body: `Create` starts a goroutine that derives from the caller's `ctx` (`context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). The same pattern is used in `Delete` (line 110), `Update` (line 135), and `DeleteCollection` (line 163). In the apiserver this `ctx` is the HTTP request context, which is canceled when `ServeHTTP` returns; the dual writer returns immediately after starting the goroutine, so the legacy write races with cancellation and can be canceled before it has completed. Since the legacy write is the safety mechanism for Mode 3, this can silently lose the backup write. Use a request-detached context such as `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` plus an explicit timeout, or a server-owned background context.

title: Unordered goroutines can leave stale data in legacy storage
body: Each successful storage write launches an independent goroutine for the legacy write, with no per-object queue, mutex, version check, or ordering guarantee. Two concurrent updates or deletes for the same object can complete in unified storage in one order but be applied to legacy in the opposite order due to goroutine scheduling. For example, an older `Update` goroutine can run after a newer one, leaving legacy with the older object even though unified storage has the newer one. A per-key worker, resourceVersion precondition, or other ordered writeback mechanism is needed to ensure the legacy backup does not regress.

title: Legacy Update recomputes the update instead of writing the object returned by unified storage
body: `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` passes the original `rest.UpdatedObjectInfo` to legacy storage. `UpdatedObjectInfo` is called again by legacy storage against the legacy old object, so it can produce a different object than `res` returned by `d.Storage.Update`, especially when legacy and unified storage are at different versions. The previous implementation wrapped the already-returned unified object (`updateWrapper{updated: obj}`), ensuring legacy wrote the same object. Reinstate that behavior by passing a wrapper that returns `res`; otherwise the legacy backup may be inconsistent with unified storage or fail update validation.

title: Storage Create failure is recorded as a legacy duration
body: On `d.Storage.Create` error, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` using `startStorage`. This increments the legacy error/duration metric for an operation in which legacy was never called, while the unified-storage error is not recorded as a storage duration. It should call `d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`. The same mistake exists in `Update` at line 129.

title: Delete success records the object name in the `kind` metric label
body: After a successful `Storage.Delete`, the code calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`, passing `name` where every other call passes `options.Kind`. The `kind` label will contain per-object names instead of the resource kind, producing unbounded metric cardinality and destroying aggregation by kind. It should pass `options.Kind`.

title: Legacy DeleteCollection result is recorded as a storage duration
body: In `DeleteCollection`'s legacy goroutine, `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ..., startLegacy)` uses the storage metric for the legacy call and starts from `startLegacy`. This mislabels legacy duration/errors as unified-storage operations and leaves the legacy metric unpopulated. It should call `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`.

title: Mode3 unit tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy write
body: The success tests configure legacy mock expectations (for example, `setupLegacyFn` in `TestMode3_Create`) but return immediately after the synchronous unified-storage call. Because the actual legacy write happens in a goroutine, the test passes even if the legacy mock is never called, and no `m.AssertExpectations` or synchronization verifies it. This makes the core Mode3 behavior (legacy backup write) untested and can also leave background goroutines running after the subtest exits. Add a wait group or injectable async executor and assert the legacy calls.

title: Mode3 integration tests reuse synchronous CRUD assertions and race with legacy writeback
body: The new Mode3 cases call `doPlaylistTests`, which checks the legacy API immediately after k8s create/update/delete (for example `client.Resource.Create` followed by a legacy `/api/playlists` GET, and `client.Resource.Delete` followed by a legacy GET). With Mode3 those legacy writes are asynchronous, so the test assertions are timing-dependent and can fail intermittently if the goroutine has not completed. Mode3 needs a poll/wait mechanism for the legacy side or a separate test suite that accounts for asynchronous propagation.

title: Async legacy writes inherit the request context and are canceled after return
body: The goroutine at this line wraps the incoming request context with a 10s timeout and then performs Legacy.Create. The same pattern is used for Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection (lines 108, 134, 161). In Kubernetes API server storage, the context passed to the storage method is typically canceled when the HTTP handler returns. Since this method returns immediately after launching the goroutine, the legacy backup write frequently starts with an already canceled context and is aborted, so mode 3 does not reliably keep legacy storage as a safe backup. Detach from the request lifecycle, for example with context.WithoutCancel/context.Background, before applying the timeout.

title: Legacy update reuses the original UpdatedObjectInfo instead of the object written to unified storage
body: This line passes the same `objInfo` that was already consumed by `d.Storage.Update` to `d.Legacy.Update`. `rest.UpdatedObjectInfo` may be single-use or may compute the new object against the old object in the target store; because legacy may have a different old object than unified storage, legacy can produce a different object or fail. The previous implementation wrapped the final object returned by storage in `updateWrapper` for the legacy update. The async legacy update should use the object returned by `d.Storage.Update`, or a wrapper that returns that object, rather than the original `objInfo`.

title: Delete records the object name as the metric kind label
body: This line passes `name` as the kind argument to `recordStorageDuration`, while other calls pass `options.Kind`. `name` is a user-controlled object name, so every deleted object creates a new Prometheus label value. This causes unbounded cardinality in the mode 3 storage metrics and can make metrics expensive or unusable. It should pass `options.Kind`.

title: Storage create/update errors are recorded as legacy durations
body: On a `Storage.Create` error, the code records `recordLegacyDuration` with the storage start time even though no legacy call was made. The same mistake is present in `Update` at line 129. These should be `recordStorageDuration`. As written, storage failure metrics are underreported and legacy duration metrics are polluted with storage call durations.

title: Legacy DeleteCollection result is recorded with the storage metric
body: The async legacy `DeleteCollection` result is recorded with `recordStorageDuration` and `startLegacy`. It should use `recordLegacyDuration`. As written, legacy successes and failures are attributed to storage metrics, corrupting both metric sets.

title: Mode 3 integration tests immediately assert legacy consistency despite async legacy writes
body: The new mode 3 subtests run `doPlaylistTests`, which after k8s Create/Update immediately calls the legacy API and asserts that the change is present (for example the legacy list check and `getFromBothAPIs`). Mode 3 now writes to legacy asynchronously after the unified storage write returns, so these checks race with the legacy-write goroutine and can fail intermittently in CI. The tests should poll or wait for legacy convergence, or use a mode-specific expectation for async propagation.

title: Async legacy writes inherit request context and are canceled
body: In Create (and the same pattern in Delete at line 110, Update at line 135, and DeleteCollection at line 163), the goroutine derives context.WithTimeoutCause from the incoming ctx. In the apiserver this ctx is the request context, which is canceled as soon as the handler returns. Since these legacy writes are scheduled asynchronously after the unified-store write and after the handler returns, they generally start with an already canceled context and are aborted before writing. Mode 3 reads only from unified storage, so legacy is the safety copy; missed legacy creates/updates/deletes can mean lost safety data. Use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a fresh background context before adding the timeout.

title: Delete records object name in metric kind label
body: After a successful Storage.Delete, the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage). Every other call passes options.Kind as the third argument. Using the deleted object name as the kind label creates an unbounded Prometheus series per object name, causing high cardinality on delete operations and making the metric impossible to aggregate by resource kind. Pass options.Kind instead of name.

title: Mode3 integration test asserts immediate legacy consistency after async writes
body: The new mode3 cases run doPlaylistTests, where k8s create/update/delete now propagate to legacy asynchronously. The test immediately queries the legacy /api/playlists endpoint at line 523 and uses getFromBothAPIs around lines 535 and 547 without waiting or polling for the async legacy write to finish. This makes the mode3 integration tests racy: they can fail when the goroutine has not completed, or pass while the legacy safety write is actually broken. The test should poll or otherwise await eventual convergence before asserting legacy state.

title: Legacy update reuses the same UpdatedObjectInfo instead of the unified-storage result
body: Update passes the same objInfo to both d.Storage.Update and, asynchronously, d.Legacy.Update. UpdatedObjectInfo.UpdatedObject is invoked independently by each store against its own old object; it is not guaranteed to be idempotent or to produce the same object when legacy is stale. The previous implementation wrapped the object returned from unified storage before sending it to legacy, which ensured both stores wrote the same updated object. Without that, legacy may store a different version from unified storage, defeating the safety copy and potentially causing legacy update failures.

title: Async legacy Create uses original obj rather than the object returned by Storage
body: Create passes the original request obj to d.Legacy.Create instead of the created object returned by d.Storage.Create. If unified storage assigns server-generated fields such as a generated name, UID, or resourceVersion only on the returned object without mutating obj, the legacy write will generate or record a different identity than unified storage. That leaves mode3 with two divergent objects for the same logical create. The legacy writer should receive the object identity returned by unified storage.

title: Storage create/update failures are recorded as legacy duration
body: On a failed Storage.Create, line 45 calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage), and the same occurs for Storage.Update at line 129. No legacy operation was attempted in these paths, and startStorage measures the unified-store call. This records storage failures and latency in the legacy metric while leaving the storage metric missing those failures. These paths should call recordStorageDuration, and recordLegacyDuration should be used only after actual Legacy calls.

title: DeleteCollection records legacy duration in the storage metric
body: In the DeleteCollection goroutine, after d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). This records the legacy operation as a storage operation, corrupting both storage and legacy latency/error metrics and hiding failures in the legacy safety write. It should call d.recordLegacyDuration.

title: Mode3 unit tests do not wait for or assert legacy writes
body: The Mode3 Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection tests launch asynchronous legacy writes but do not wait for the goroutines and do not assert that Legacy.Create, Legacy.Update, Legacy.Delete, or Legacy.DeleteCollection were called. An implementation could skip the legacy write entirely and these tests would still pass, and the current context-cancellation issue would not be detected. Add a wait mechanism and assertions for the expected legacy calls.

title: GetWebAssets does not re-check the cache after acquiring the write lock
body: The fast path reads entryPointAssetsCache under RLock, but once it sees nil it releases and later calls Lock without re-reading the cache. Multiple goroutines that observed nil before the first writer populated the cache will all enter the slow path serially, each opening and parsing the manifest while holding the exclusive lock. If one of those later reloads fails, it can overwrite an already-valid cache with nil, causing subsequent requests to retry and potentially fail. After acquiring Lock, the function should re-check entryPointAssetsCache (and return it when cfg.Env != setting.Dev) before doing any I/O.

title: No concurrent regression test for the data race fix
