body: This change adds synchronization to GetWebAssets but no test exercises concurrent calls. A race-enabled test that calls GetWebAssets from multiple goroutines and accesses the returned assets would help detect a regression back to unsynchronized access of the global entryPointAssetsCache.

title: Missing cache re-check after acquiring write lock causes thundering herd and I/O under exclusive lock
body: After the initial RLock sees entryPointAssetsCache == nil, the function takes the write lock and immediately performs readWebAssetsFromFile/CDN without re-reading entryPointAssetsCache. Multiple goroutines that all observed nil will therefore serialize on the write lock and each recompute and overwrite the cache, while all other GetWebAssets callers are blocked. Add a second check for a non-nil cache after acquiring the write lock (or use singleflight) before doing I/O.

title: No concurrent test for the race fix
body: The PR changes shared-state synchronization but adds no test that exercises GetWebAssets concurrently. A test invoking GetWebAssets from multiple goroutines (run under the race detector) would verify both that the cache assignment is race-free and that the cache population path behaves correctly under contention.

title: Missing recheck after write lock causes cache stampede and can clobber a valid cache
body: After the initial RLock snapshot, the function may see a nil cache and move to the write lock, but it does not re-read entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring that lock. In non-development mode, multiple callers that saw nil on first request can serialize on the write lock and each rebuild the manifest. Worse, if a later rebuild fails, line 69 assigns entryPointAssetsCache = nil, overwriting a valid cache installed by the first caller with nil. Re-check the cache under the write lock in non-dev mode and return the existing value, and avoid replacing an existing valid cache with nil on an error.

title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, making the SQL feature flag dead
body: The helper initializes `enabled` to the negation of `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns false both when `enabled` is true and when it is false. As a result, every QueryTypeSQL is rejected before parsing regardless of whether the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle is on. If the toggle is meant to control the feature, this should return `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)`; if the feature is intentionally unconditional-off, the function should just return false and not consult the toggle. The current code leaves a contradictory, dead toggle.

title: Original DuckDB json_serialize_sql command construction is still present
body: TablesList still interpolates user SQL into `SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')` after only replacing single quotes and passes it to RunCommands. The new stub RunCommands returns not implemented so the command is not executed today, but the DuckDB-specific parsing path that carried the original RCE/LFI vector remains wired into NewSQLCommand. Any future real DB implementation or alternate caller would re-enable the vulnerable path. The fix would be safer if this serialization logic were removed rather than only stubbed.

title: No automated tests cover the SQL-expression disabling
body: This security fix adds a hard rejection for QueryTypeSQL and replaces DuckDB with stubs, but no tests are included. There is no check that ReadQuery rejects SQL expressions with the intended error, that NewSQLCommand and sql.TablesList return not-implemented errors, or that the feature flag behavior is as intended. A future regression could remove or invert this guard without CI noticing.

title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, making the sqlExpressions toggle a no-op
body: The function reads `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, but both control-flow branches return false, so SQL expressions are rejected regardless of whether the feature toggle is enabled. This makes the still-existing `sqlExpressions` feature flag a no-op and leaves the `QueryTypeSQL` parsing branch below unreachable. If disabling is intentional, it should be explicit (for example `return false` with a comment), or the toggle/docs should be updated; otherwise the dead flag and unreachable code create a misleading contract and a future risk of accidental re-enable.

title: No regression test covers that SQL expressions are disabled
body: The PR changes behavior for all SQL expression queries but includes no tests asserting the new rejection behavior. There should be a regression test for `ReadQuery` with `QueryTypeSQL` returning an error, and for `NewSQLCommand`/`UnmarshalSQLCommand` rejecting SQL commands without doing any DuckDB work, so this security fix cannot be accidentally reverted by future refactors.

title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, making the feature flag dead code
body: The function computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` but then returns false both when `enabled` is true and when it is false. As written, `FlagSqlExpressions` has no effect and the SQL expression path can never be re-enabled through the existing feature toggle. If the security fix is intended to hard-disable SQL expressions, this should be an explicit unconditional `return false` with no feature-toggle call; if the flag is meant to remain usable later, the logic is wrong. The current code is misleading and likely to cause an accidental revert or bad future re-enablement.

title: No tests cover the SQL expression disable behavior
body: This PR closes a critical RCE/LFI path by rejecting QueryTypeSQL in the reader and by replacing DuckDB with a not-implemented stub, but no tests are added. There should be regression tests asserting that SQL expression queries are rejected both through ReadQuery and through NewSQLCommand/UnmarshalSQLCommand, so a future change that restores execution or unintentionally weakens the guard is caught. Without such tests, the security fix is only protected by the current stub implementation and not by the test suite.

title: BuildIndex scoped lock allows concurrent builds for the same key
body: The lock was moved from the entire BuildIndex path to only the final cache insertion. However searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex has no per-key synchronization: two callers that both see GetIndex return nil for the same NamespacedResource can now run BuildIndex concurrently. For file-backed indexes this means two calls to bleve.New on the same directory can open/modify the same bleve data files concurrently, causing corruption or an error; for memory indexes one built index is leaked and the cache is last-writer-wins. Use a per-key lock/singleflight or re-check the cache after acquiring the lock.

title: Search init worker goroutines race on shared variables
body: Inside searchSupport.init the errgroup workers are limited but still concurrent. Each goroutine executes `totalBatchesIndexed++` and `_, _, err = s.build(...)` on variables shared with all other workers. These are unsynchronized writes to the same memory, so this is a data race. The `err` capture is also semantically wrong: one goroutine can overwrite the outer `err` before another returns it, causing a build failure to be reported as success or vice versa. Declare `err` locally with `:=` in the closure and use an atomic counter for totalBatchesIndexed.

title: Search watch goroutine panics on closed event channel
body: The goroutine started in searchSupport.init reads from the write-events channel with `v := <-events` and immediately calls `s.handleEvent(watchctx, v)` without checking the channel-open boolean. The SQL watcher closes its stream when the backend stops (`defer close(stream)` in the poller), after which a receive returns a nil *WrittenEvent. `handleEvent` dereferences `evt.Type`, causing a nil-pointer panic that can crash the process during shutdown. Check `v, ok := <-events` and return on `!ok`, and wire the loop to a cancellable context.

title: Resource version returned by build is discarded so watch events can be lost
body: s.build returns the last resource version read while listing that namespace, specifically so a watch can resume after it. searchSupport.init discards that value with `_`. After all indexes are built it calls WatchWriteEvents, which in the SQL backend starts from the latest RV at that moment. Any write that lands after a namespace was listed but before WatchWriteEvents captures the baseline becomes the baseline itself and is never emitted to the search index, leaving the search index missing that update until a later event or rebuild. Keep the per-resource RV and pass it to the watcher, or start watching before the build and buffer events.

title: Postgres storage server integration test is skipped
body: This PR adds a skip for the postgres backend in TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer, with a TODO to fix the test later. Since the PR changes unified storage initialization from lazy to eager, postgres coverage for this startup path is removed exactly when it is most likely to catch startup or indexing regressions. Fix the test or ensure equivalent postgres coverage runs in CI.

title: Eager Init failure returns without cleaning up partial startup
body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) before returning the server. If Init fails, it returns nil and discards s, but Init can have partially succeeded: lifecycle.Init may have opened the backend, and search.init may have already started its watcher goroutine before a later step such as initWatcher fails. Since no server is returned, the caller cannot call Stop, and s.cancel/lifecycle.Stop are not invoked on this error path, leaking the DB lifecycle and background watchers. On Init failure, cancel s.ctx and stop the lifecycle if it was initialized before returning.

title: Fine-grained BuildIndex lock permits concurrent builds for the same key
body: BuildIndex now takes cacheMu only when inserting into b.cache. getOrCreateIndex in resource/search.go is not singleflight: callers can both call GetIndex, see nil, and call build concurrently. For file-backed indexes both goroutines call bleve.New on the same directory at the same time, which can fail or corrupt the index; even for memory indexes, the later insertion can overwrite a fresher index. Re-check the cache after acquiring cacheMu or add per-key singleflight before building.

title: Ignored build resource version causes permanent index gaps
body: s.build returns the last RV consumed from ListIterator, and the call in init discards it. After all builds, init starts WatchWriteEvents, but the SQL implementation starts from the latest RV at that moment and has no since parameter. Writes that land after a resource's ListIterator scan and before WatchWriteEvents starts are neither in the built index nor replayed, so the index can remain stale at least until restart or reindex.

title: Data race in init errgroup goroutines
body: The goroutines launched by group.Go all execute totalBatchesIndexed++ and _, _, err = s.build(...) using variables captured from the enclosing function. These are unsynchronized concurrent writes to the same variables (and err is returned), so this is a data race: increments can be lost and error propagation is undefined. Use local variables in the closure and an atomic counter, or update metrics after group.Wait.

title: Watch goroutine panics on closed channel
body: The search watcher loop reads v := <-events without checking ok or selecting on a done context. When the backend closes the event stream during shutdown, v is a nil *WrittenEvent and handleEvent immediately dereferences evt.Type, causing an unrecovered panic. It also uses context.Background() rather than a cancelable context, so it cannot be stopped cleanly. Check the ok value and return on channel close, and use a cancellable context.

title: Error path leaks the server context and started services
body: NewResourceServer creates a cancelable ctx for the server's background work and then calls s.Init(ctx). If Init fails, it returns nil, err without calling s.cancel() or stopping the lifecycle. Since the server is not returned, the caller cannot call Stop. By that point search.init may already have started its watch goroutine, and Init may have initialized the backend, so these resources leak. Cancel ctx and perform cleanup on this path.

title: Postgres integration test skipped
body: This change disables the storage-server integration test for postgres due to CI failures. That leaves the postgres unified-storage path without this integration coverage and may hide regressions in the new eager-init behavior. Either fix the underlying failure or file and track a concrete issue rather than silently skipping.

title: Events between index build and watch start are dropped
body: `init` builds each index from storage (`s.build` on line 190) but discards the per-resource resource version returned by `s.build`, then starts `WatchWriteEvents` only after all builds complete (line 203). The SQL backend's `WatchWriteEvents` starts from the latest RV at the time it is called. Any write that commits after the list query for a resource but before this watch start is neither included in the built index nor delivered on the new watch channel, leaving the search index permanently stale for that event until a full rebuild. This is especially likely now that init runs as a blocking startup step while other instances may write.

title: Search watch goroutine can panic on closed event channel
body: The watch goroutine receives with `v := <-events` without checking whether the channel is closed. The SQL backend poller closes its event channel when it exits on Stop, so this loop will receive a nil `*WrittenEvent` and call `s.handleEvent(watchctx, v)`, which dereferences `evt.Type` and panics. The goroutine also uses `context.Background()` rather than a cancellable context, so it cannot be stopped by server shutdown. Because `NewResourceServer` now eagerly calls `s.Init`, this goroutine is always started. Use the server/backend context for cancellation and check `v, ok := <-events`.

title: Data race in concurrent index build goroutines
body: The worker goroutines started by `errgroup` concurrently write shared variables: `totalBatchesIndexed++` on line 189 and `_, _, err = s.build(...)` on line 190, where `err` is the outer function variable. These unsynchronized writes race under the Go race detector, can lose increments for the span event count, and make the code's behavior undefined. Use a local error variable inside each closure and update the counter safely (or compute it after `Wait`).

title: Lock change allows duplicate concurrent builds for the same index key
body: `BuildIndex` no longer holds `cacheMu` for the whole build, only when inserting into the cache. However, `searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex` still performs a non-atomic `GetIndex` then `build`. Two callers for the same missing key can therefore enter `BuildIndex` concurrently. For file-backed indexes both can call `bleve.New` on the same directory and build the same index, causing open/create contention; the loser remains open/leaked and whichever finishes last wins the cache. Distinct keys can be built in parallel, but same-key builds need a per-key lock or singleflight.

title: Call to non-existent no-argument `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` breaks compilation
body: `UsernameForm` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only inherited method is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)`. There is no zero-argument overload, so this file cannot compile. Pass `context.getUser()` or add an overload before merge.

title: Passkeys conditional UI no longer rendered when the user is not already set
body: The new guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` requires a non-null user because `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` returns false when `user == null`. Previously this setup ran when `context.getUser() == null` to support first-factor username/password login with discoverable passkeys. The same inverted condition is used in the error challenge at line 137, so after an invalid username or empty-password error, where the context user is still null, the WebAuthn form is also lost. This breaks passkey auto-login and leaves the conditional webauthn form absent on the initial username/password page; tests that assert `//form[@id='webauth']` on that page will fail.

title: Call to missing no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
body: UsernameForm.authenticate invokes isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method with that name in the class hierarchy is UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). Because no no-arg overload exists, this file cannot compile. The call should likely pass context.getUser() or a no-arg overload must be added.

title: Passkeys no longer rendered for initial first-factor login when no user is selected
body: The new condition uses isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), whose implementation requires user != null. This replaces the previous behavior where fillContextForm was called exactly when context.getUser() == null for normal first-factor authentication. On a fresh login without an already selected user, webauthnAuth.fillContextForm is now skipped, so the login page lacks the conditional webauthn/passkey challenge and discoverable-passkey auto-login is broken. The same null-user exclusion also affects challenge(...) at line 137 after failed first-factor submissions. The fill should be based on webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled(), independent of whether context.getUser() is set.

title: Non-existent no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() call breaks compilation
body: The new condition calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments. The only inherited method is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) from UsernamePasswordForm, so this source file will not compile. If the intent was to check the current user, it should likely be isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()).

title: Passkey conditional UI is no longer populated for unidentified users
body: authenticate() now calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) only when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true. That helper returns false when user is null: return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null. In the normal first-factor username/password flow, context.getUser() is null at this point, so the WebAuthn conditional UI attributes are never set, and the initial login page will no longer include the passkey form/autofill. Previously the else branch filled the form for unknown users when passkeys were enabled. This breaks normal discoverable-passkey login from the initial username/password page and contradicts the still-present tests that expect //form[@id='webauth'] after openLoginForm.

title: getForLogin can return identity providers that are not available for login
body: The new getForLogin cache stores only internal IDs and, on both cache miss and cache hit, reconstructs the result by calling session.identityProviders().getById(id) and adding every non-null model to the returned stream without applying IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate(). The delegate search can include organization-linked IDPs whose organization is disabled, because it filters on BROKER_PUBLIC and ORGANIZATION_ID but does not evaluate the organization's enabled state. createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel then intentionally makes isEnabled() false for such IDPs. As a result, getForLogin violates its contract by returning IDPs that are not available for login. The OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean had to add extra isEnabled() filters, but other callers will still receive disabled brokers. Filter the final stream with getLoginPredicate() or otherwise invalidate/refresh the login cache when organization enabled state changes.

title: Test cleanup registers the literal alias "alias" instead of the created provider alias
body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup for each newly created identity provider is registered as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, using the literal string "alias" rather than the variable alias such as "idp-alias-" + i or "idp-alias-20". The same mistake is repeated at line 425. Therefore the actual created providers are not removed after the test, and cleanup may attempt to delete a nonexistent/wrong provider. Use the actual alias variable or the created provider resource in addCleanup.

title: Login cache invalidation misses realm-level IdP BROKER_PUBLIC changes
body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate returns without invalidating when both old and new models pass getLoginPredicate() and have the same organizationId. For a realm-level IdP (organizationId == null), getLoginPredicate() is true regardless of OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC. However getForLogin(ORG_ONLY, null) populates its cache from a delegate query that searches BROKER_PUBLIC=true without requiring an organization link, so a realm-level IdP with BROKER_PUBLIC=true can be part of that cached result. Changing BROKER_PUBLIC on such an already login-eligible realm-level IdP therefore does not invalidate the ORG_ONLY cache, leaving a stale broker list on the login page until some other login-relevant mutation invalidates it.

title: remove() can leave a stale getById cache entry on alias cache miss
body: When isInvalid(cacheKey) is false and the alias cache entry is null, the removal path does not call registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp). If the IdP was previously loaded by internal id (cached under that id) but its alias key was never cached or was evicted, idpDelegate.remove(alias) deletes the entity while the internal-id cache entry remains. A subsequent getById(internalId) then returns the deleted IdP. Since storedIdp is now loaded unconditionally at line 100, it should be invalidated in all removal paths.

title: Cleanup registers the wrong alias for created identity providers
body: Line 381 (and similarly line 425) uses testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove instead of the actual idpRep.getAlias(). As a result, the created idp-alias-* identity providers are not removed during cleanup, and remain in the realm for later tests or reruns. This can cause cross-test pollution or duplicate-alias failures, and may also remove an unrelated IdP that actually has the alias 'alias'.

title: Cleanup action uses literal alias instead of actual IDP alias
body: The cleanup callback is created with `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")` instead of the alias built for the IDP (e.g. `alias` variable or `"idp-alias-20"`). The same mistake appears for idp-alias-20 at line 425. None of the IDPs created in `testCacheIDPForLogin` are removed during cleanup, leaving up to 21 IDPs (and organization links) in the test realm. This can contaminate subsequent tests and cache assertions.

title: Unconditional delegate fetch on IDP removal
body: `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is now invoked before checking whether a valid cached `CachedIdentityProvider` is available. When the alias cache hit path is taken, the code already has the model in `cached.getIdentityProvider()` and uses it for `registerIDPInvalidation`; the extra delegate fetch adds a database read to every IDP removal. This can be avoided by using the cached model and falling back to the delegate only when the cache is invalid or missing.

title: New abstract order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: Adding an abstract order() method to the public CryptoProvider interface is binary and source incompatible for any external implementation compiled against an older Keycloak version. During CryptoIntegration.detectProvider, sorting calls order() on every loaded provider, so an older implementation will fail with AbstractMethodError even if it is the only provider on the classpath. Provide a default implementation such as default int order() { return 0; } or preserve SPI compatibility.

title: Providers with equal order are selected silently and arbitrarily
body: The new logic replaces the previous fail-fast multiple-provider check with sorting by order(). But all built-in providers except AuthzClientCryptoProvider (DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, FIPS1402Provider) return 200. If two of them end up on the classpath, the selection depends on ServiceLoader encounter order and no error is raised. This can silently select the non-FIPS provider in a FIPS-required environment, or vice versa, defeating the old classpath integrity guard. Distinct orders are needed for each real provider, or a tie at the top order should still fail.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default KeyStore provider, not BouncyCastle
body: KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider() returns the JCA provider backing the default keystore type (usually SUN/SunJCE on a stock JDK), not a BouncyCastle provider. Callers of CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() may check for null or use the returned provider to request BC-specific algorithms, so this can lead to NoSuchAlgorithmException or use of an unintended security provider. If this provider intentionally does not use BouncyCastle, it should return null or a provider that actually supplies the algorithms it claims to support, and callers must handle that.

title: Indefinite BER length leaks into DER parser and causes unchecked exception
body: readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (0x80). readInteger() then passes that -1 to read(int), which executes new byte[length] and throws unchecked NegativeArraySizeException rather than the declared IOException. A malformed DER signature can therefore bypass normal error handling. This DER decoder should reject indefinite-length encoding explicitly, and readInteger() should also reject an empty INTEGER before new BigInteger(bytes) to avoid NumberFormatException.

title: Test does not verify the first DER-to-raw conversion against the original signature
body: The test computes rsConcat from the JCA DER signature, converts it back to asn1Des, then only asserts that converting asn1Des back to raw gives the same rsConcat. A paired defect in asn1derToConcatenatedRS and concatenatedRSToASN1DER could pass this roundtrip while still producing the wrong raw signature from the original DER, or the wrong DER from the raw signature. It should also assert that asn1Des equals the original sign, or compare against known DER/raw vectors.

title: Silent arbitrary crypto provider selection when multiple providers have equal order
body: detectProvider now sorts providers by order and always returns the first one instead of throwing when multiple providers are present. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200, so if more than one of them is on the classpath the chosen provider depends on unspecified ServiceLoader enumeration order. Previously this condition failed fast. With this change a non-FIPS provider can be selected on a FIPS-enabled classpath, or the FIPS provider constructor can still run and modify security providers before it is ignored. This can violate FIPS requirements and is very hard to diagnose because other providers are only logged at debug level.

title: Adding abstract order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public interface. Adding an abstract int order() method without a default implementation breaks both source and binary compatibility for any third-party or otherwise out-of-tree implementation of CryptoProvider; such implementations will fail to compile or will throw AbstractMethodError at runtime. The method should have a default implementation, for example returning a neutral order, unless this is a deliberately accepted breaking API change.

title: Registered crypto provider throws UnsupportedOperationException for core crypto operations
body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider is advertised through META-INF/services and will be auto-selected when no higher-order provider is present. Yet getSignature(), getKeyPairGen(), getKeyFactory(), getCertificateUtils(), getPemUtils(), and most other CryptoProvider methods throw UnsupportedOperationException. Standalone authz-client code that uses these SPI methods, such as JWT client authentication or other signature operations via CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getSignature(...), will fail at runtime instead of using the JCA defaults. Either implement the needed methods using standard JCA or do not register a class as a general CryptoProvider until it is complete.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default keystore provider, not BouncyCastle
body: CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() documents that it returns a BouncyCastle security provider. This implementation returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is typically the JDK SUN/SunJSSE provider when BC is not present. Any caller that relies on the returned provider being BC, for BC algorithms or provider-specific registration, gets the wrong provider, which can lead to algorithm lookup failures or inconsistent provider behavior. The provider should return the actual BC provider it uses, or null if it intentionally does not use BC, with callers updated accordingly.

title: ECDSA conversion test uses one default EC key for all curves and only tests round-trip
body: The test generates a single KeyPair with KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() without specifying a curve. For ES384 and ES512 the key is not necessarily on P-384 or P-521, and the test only asserts that DER -> R||S -> DER equals the intermediate R||S. It does not verify the conversions against the JCA signature value or against known test vectors, so an incorrect implementation could pass while producing wrong encodings for the actual algorithm or curve. Use per-algorithm curve parameters and assert the expected raw signature/conversion result.

title: Adding abstract order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public interface. Adding a new abstract method is a binary and source compatibility break for any implementation outside this repository compiled against an older Keycloak version; such providers will fail to compile or can throw AbstractMethodError when ServiceLoader invokes order(). Since this is only used to sort providers, it should have a default implementation (e.g. return 0).

title: Equal-order server crypto providers are silently selected instead of rejected
body: detectProvider previously threw when more than one CryptoProvider was found. It now sorts only by order(), and DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200. If e.g. the default and FIPS provider are accidentally both on the classpath, ServiceLoader iteration order determines which one is used, so a non-FIPS provider may be selected in a FIPS environment instead of failing fast. Tie/conflict detection is still needed for providers with the same order, or the server providers need distinct precedence.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default keystore provider, not a BouncyCastle provider
body: The CryptoProvider contract documents this method as returning a BouncyCastle provider. This implementation returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which on standard JVMs is typically SUN or SunJSSE, not BouncyCastle. Any code that uses the returned provider as a BC provider (for BC algorithms, adding it to Security, or looking up BC services) can get the wrong provider and fail with NoSuchAlgorithmException/NoSuchProviderException or use unintended crypto implementations.

title: ECDSA DER-to-RS conversion silently truncates oversized integers
body: integerToBytes copies only the low qLength bytes when BigInteger.toByteArray() is longer than the field length. For a DER INTEGER that does not fit in signLength/2 bytes, this discards significant high-order bytes instead of rejecting the malformed/non-canonical signature. That can turn an invalid oversized r or s into a different value and should throw an IOException unless the only extra byte is a leading zero sign byte.

title: ECDSA conversion tests only check round-trip symmetry
body: The test signs data, converts DER to concatenated RS, back to DER, then back to concatenated RS, and only asserts the two raw RS arrays are equal. It never compares the reconstructed DER to the original signature or verifies the resulting bytes with Signature.verify. A pair of inverse bugs in the two conversion methods would pass. The test also uses the same default EC key pair for ES256, ES384, and ES512 instead of curve/key sizes matching each algorithm.

title: Existing admin permission clients are not upgraded with the new Clients resource type and scopes
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns early whenever realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already non-null, so realms that already had the admin permissions client created under the previous V2 schema will not get the newly added Clients resource type or its scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite). Later, client permission creation can fail with ModelException "No scopes found." and client permission evaluation can fail or NPE because the all-Clients resource is missing. The init method needs to be idempotent and add missing schema entries for existing admin permission clients.

title: Per-client permission check can dereference a null all-clients resource
body: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) may return null when the all-resource for the Clients type does not exist. The code then immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check, causing a NullPointerException. This is especially likely for an existing admin permissions client that was not upgraded with the new schema. The method should handle resource == null by returning false or ensuring initialization first.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns the synthetic all-clients resource name
body: getClientsWithPermission iterates all resources of type CLIENTS, including the all-clients resource whose name is AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE ("Clients"). If a policy grants the requested scope on that all-resource, hasGrantedPermission returns true and the code adds resource.getName(), i.e. "Clients", to the returned set. Callers expect this set to contain concrete client IDs, so the all-resource grant is not expanded into actual clients and a nonexistent client ID is returned. The all-resource should be skipped or expanded to the corresponding concrete client IDs.

title: getResourceName does not resolve Clients resources
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName has special handling for the USERS resource type but not for the newly added CLIENTS resource type. For client permissions/resources it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), but client resources created by getOrCreateResource use the client's internal id as the resource name and do not set a meaningful display name. Resource name resolution or representation output for client permissions can therefore be null or an internal UUID instead of the client's clientId. A CLIENTS branch should resolve the client and return client.getClientId() or another appropriate display value.

title: Void require methods are documented as returning boolean
body: The Javadoc for requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() says "Returns true if ... returns true", but both methods are void and throw ForbiddenException when the corresponding check fails. This misdocuments the API and should say that it throws ForbiddenException when the check returns false.

title: All-client permission is skipped once a per-client resource exists
body: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) evaluates the all-clients resource only when no resource exists for that client. If any per-client resource exists, for example a VIEW or CONFIGURE permission for that client, the type-level Clients resource is not evaluated. The per-client checks canManage(ClientModel), canConfigure(ClientModel), canMapRoles(ClientModel), canMapCompositeRoles(ClientModel), and canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) all rely on this method, so a caller with a valid MANAGE/CONFIGURE/MAP_ROLES permission for all clients can be denied for any client that also has some individual permission. Conversely, a negative type-level Clients policy is not considered for such clients, which can allow an action that the all-clients policy was intended to deny. The all-clients resource should always be evaluated together with any individual client resource.

title: getClientsWithPermission cannot return per-client resources
body: getClientsWithPermission iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...), but per-client resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource are created with resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId()) and never have their type set to CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE. Only the type-level resource named "Clients" has that type. As a result, the method misses all concrete client resources and may return the pseudo-resource "Clients" when a type-level permission exists. Callers that treat the returned set as client IDs will either see no concrete clients or an invalid ID.

title: Client deletion cleanup is gated on the old FGAP feature and has no V2 path
body: registerListener now wraps role/client/group cleanup in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), but the factory methods in the same class choose MgmtPermissionsV2 based on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. When only V2 is enabled, ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent is ignored, so authorization resources created for a deleted client are never removed. If both flags are enabled, management(...).clients() resolves to ClientPermissionsV2 and setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) throws UnsupportedOperationException, so client deletion breaks. Client cleanup needs a V2 implementation rather than being gated on the V1 feature flag.

title: Test mutates shared client name without cleanup
body: testManageOnlyOneClient changes myclient's clientId/name to "somethingNew" via clientResource.update(myclient) and never restores it. Other tests in the same class, such as testConfigureOnlyOneClient and testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient, look up clients with realm.admin().clients().findByClientId("myclient").get(0). If this test runs before them, those lookups return an empty list and the tests fail. Restore the client in a finally block or @AfterEach, or avoid changing the shared fixture.

title: Client map-role permission checks bypass the manage-clients admin role
body: In ClientPermissionsV2, canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission(client, <scope>). They do not first check root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) or otherwise delegate to canManage(), unlike canManage(client), canConfigure(client), canManageClientScopes(), and the V1 semantics for these operations. As a result, an administrator holding the realm manage-clients role but no explicit fine-grained map-roles/map-roles-composite/map-roles-client-scope permission is denied these client role operations when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. The methods should preserve the admin-role bypass before evaluating fine-grained scopes.

title: V2 authorization cleanup is skipped on role/client/group removal
body: The listener now runs its cleanup only when the legacy ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled. When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled by itself, AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, but this block does not execute, so client/role/group removal does not clean up the corresponding admin-permission resources or policies in V2. Additionally, ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled currently throws UnsupportedOperationException, so if both feature flags are enabled the guard passes and deletion events can hit that exception. The result is stale authorization resources/policies for deleted objects, potentially causing incorrect permission listings and evaluation state.

title: getClientsWithPermission can return the all-clients resource name as a client ID
body: getClientsWithPermission iterates over every resource of type CLIENTS, including the special all-clients resource whose name is AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE ("Clients"). If hasGrantedPermission() is true for that resource, the code adds resource.getName() to a set that callers treat as actual client IDs. With a type-level "all clients" permission the returned set contains "Clients" instead of all real client IDs, so callers filtering clients can end up with no matching clients or a bogus client ID. The all-resource case must be expanded to actual client IDs or otherwise handled explicitly, and the resource-type resource name must not be returned as a client ID.

title: getResourceName does not handle the new Clients resource type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema now registers CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE and creates client resources with name = client.getId() and no display name in getOrCreateResource. However getResourceName still only has a branch for USERS. For a policy with resource type Clients, including the all-clients resource, it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is null for these resources or at best the raw client UUID, and it never returns an "All clients"-style display. This leaves the new client resource type without a proper human-readable resource name in permission representations. A CLIENTS branch symmetric to USERS is needed, resolving client IDs to clientId and mapping the type resource to a display such as "All clients".

title: Exit code 3 is reserved by Picocli for execution errors
body: This change sets RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE to 3 while the preceding comment explicitly refers to picocli.CommandLine.ExitCode. In that interface, 3 is EXECUTION_ERROR. A normal incompatibility result (recreate required) would therefore be indistinguishable from an execution failure if Picocli or any handler returns the standard EXECUTION_ERROR code. The documented contract reserves 1 for unexpected errors, so use a non-picocli-reserved code for recreate (e.g. keep 4 for recreate and move feature-disabled to another value such as 5).

title: Exit-code contract is not asserted by the new tests
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the stderr message and does not assert that the process exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4). Likewise, testWrongVersions checks the error messages for incompatible Keycloak/Infinispan versions but never asserts exit code 3, even though this PR changes the recreate exit code from 4 to 3 and documents it. Since exit codes are the scripting contract for this tool, the tests should assert them to prevent regressions such as the code returning the old exit code while the docs show the new one.

title: Operator feature requirement is stated unconditionally but default update behavior does not enable it
body: The caution says the Operator will fail unless `rolling-updates` is enabled, with no qualification. However, `UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment` only enables the feature when an explicit `UpdateStrategy` is configured; the default/null strategy test cases exercise operator update behavior without it and are expected to succeed. This either overstates the requirement and will lead users to enable a preview feature unnecessarily, or the tests are not covering a real failure in the default path.

title: Feature-disabled exit code and check subcommand are not tested
body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only exercises the `metadata` subcommand and asserts the error text, but does not assert the newly documented exit code 4 for the feature-disabled case. The `check` subcommand has an identical feature gate that is not covered in this test. A regression in the exit code or in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck`'s feature gate would not be caught.

title: Recreate exit code is not asserted
body: The wrong-version tests assert the printed error messages but never assert that the command exits with `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` (now 3). The exit code is the documented contract for automation, and its value was changed in this PR, so the tests should verify it rather than relying only on output text.

title: Public exit code meaning changed from 4 to 3
body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` was changed from 4 to 3, and 4 now means the `rolling-updates` feature is disabled. This is a user-visible contract change for any scripts already written against the previous preview behavior, especially because the accompanying documentation tells users to rely on the exit code. If backward compatibility matters for preview users, this should be called out or a non-conflicting new code should be used.

title: Recreate exit code changed from 4 to 3 breaks the documented CLI contract
body: This changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and assigns 4 to feature-disabled. The update compatibility docs explicitly tell users to script against the exit codes, so existing scripts that check for 4 to detect a required recreate upgrade will now classify recreate upgrades as feature-disabled and may choose the wrong upgrade strategy. If backward compatibility with the previously documented preview behavior matters, leave recreate at 4 and choose a separate code such as 5 for feature-disabled, or call out the break clearly.

title: New CLI exit codes are not asserted
body: `testWrongVersions` only asserts the stderr message and never checks `result.exitCode()`. The PR changes the recreate exit code to 3 and introduces feature-disabled exit code 4, but the tests would still pass if the command printed the expected error and returned the wrong exit code. Since the exit code is the primary scripting contract, assert exit code 3 for the wrong-version cases, exit code 4 for `testFeatureNotEnabled`, and exit code 0 for the successful check path.

title: Caution overstates when the operator will fail without rolling-updates
body: The new caution says the feature must be enabled, otherwise the Operator will fail. However, the default update strategy path (`spec.update` unset) uses legacy behavior and the operator tests in this PR do not enable the feature for that path: `createInitialDeployment(null)` returns before setting a `FeatureSpec`. The documentation should clarify that the feature is required when using the new `spec.update` strategy rather than stating that every Keycloak CR will fail without it.

title: Example contains an invalid CRD value for update strategy
body: The YAML example uses `strategy: Recreate|<not set>`, which is not a valid value for the update strategy field. A user copying this example would get a schema validation error. The listing should use `strategy: Recreate` for the example, with the unset/default behavior described separately in the callout or table.

title: VIEW permission on all groups grants manage rights to all groups
body: canManage() checks hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). A caller who only has the global Groups view scope is therefore treated as having manage rights. requireManage() is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() and group update/delete flows, so this allows users with view-only permission to create or modify groups. The check should require AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE only.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group model IDs and may not enumerate per-group resources
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() iterates resources returned by findByType and passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission(), then adds that ID to the returned set. The returned set is used as GroupModel IDs for the UserModel.GROUPS search attribute in UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource. However, group permission resources are created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() with the group model ID as the resource name and a separate generated authorization resource UUID as the resource ID; getId() is not the group ID. In addition, those per-group resources are not created with type Groups, so findByType may not find them. The result is that user search/count filtering by viewable groups receives invalid or empty group IDs and can return wrong results. The code should use groupResource.getName() and ensure resources are actually typed and enumerable.

title: Existing admin permissions clients are not migrated with the new Groups resource type and scopes
body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already non-null. Realms that already initialized the V2 admin permissions schema before this change will therefore not get the new Groups resource type or the new group scopes. Later, GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() can call getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE), receive null, and then call policyStore.findByResource(server, resource), causing an NPE; alternatively, Groups permissions cannot be configured or enforced for those realms. Initialization should create the missing Groups resource/scopes for existing admin permission clients.

title: Group view permission incorrectly grants manage/create access
body: `canManage()` returns true when the caller has either `VIEW` or `MANAGE` on the all-groups resource (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`). `requireManage()` is used by `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` before creating a top-level group, so a principal granted only view access to all groups can create groups. It should require only `MANAGE`.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authorization resource ID instead of group ID
body: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission(...)`, but `hasPermission` starts with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. In `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` the resource name is the actual group ID, while `groupResource.getId()` is the internal authorization resource UUID. It also adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set. User search puts those IDs into `UserModel.GROUPS`, so the membership filter is wrong and can return no users for group view-members/manage-members permissions. It should use `groupResource.getName()` and add `groupResource.getName()`.

title: Individually created group resources are not assigned the Groups type
body: When `getOrCreateResource` creates a new resource for a group, it calls `resourceStore.create(...)` and updates scopes but never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` discovers group resources with `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`, so these individual group resources will not be found; only the aggregate all-groups resource created in `init` has the type. This breaks group-membership-based user search filtering.

title: Per-group authorization evaluation replaced one global short-circuit
body: The new code filters with `stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)` instead of evaluating `groupsEvaluator.canView()` once and short-circuiting. For callers with fine-grained all-groups view/manage but no legacy admin role, `canView(group)` performs a resource lookup and policy evaluation for every group. On realms with many groups this makes the group listing endpoint significantly more expensive. The same pattern was removed in `GroupResource.getSubGroups`.

title: VIEW all-groups permission grants global group manage
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so a caller who only has the `view` scope on the all-groups resource is treated as having global group manage permission. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() calls auth.groups().requireManage(), meaning a view-only FGAP admin could create top-level groups. This should evaluate only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE for canManage().

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In V2, individual group resources are looked up by name equal to the group id, but this method passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission() and then adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. groupResource.getId() is the generated authorization resource UUID, not the group id, so hasPermission() usually cannot find the group resource and falls back to the all-groups resource. The resulting set is then used as UserModel.GROUPS in UsersResource.searchForUser and getUsersCount, filtering users by IDs that are not actual group IDs. For example, an all-groups view-members permission can produce an invalid group id and return no users in search. It should use groupResource.getName() for both evaluation and grant collection.

title: New group resources are created without a resource type
body: When getOrCreateResource() creates a missing resource for a resource type, it never calls resource.setType(resourceType). The all-resource entries created in init() do set a type, but per-group resources created later do not. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) to discover group resources, so group-specific resources with a null type are skipped. This makes the group-id set incomplete and causes user search pre-filtering and user counts based on group view-members permissions to be wrong.

title: AdminRoles.ADMIN is no longer accepted for per-user V2 evaluations
body: canView(UserModel) at line 48 and canManage(UserModel) at line 57 previously granted access when the caller had AdminRoles.ADMIN, in addition to MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS. This PR removes AdminRoles.ADMIN from both checks. A master realm admin with the admin role but without the target realm's manage-users/view-users management-client role can now be denied per-user operations. Unless AdminRoles.ADMIN is guaranteed to be a composite containing those target-realm roles, this is an authorization regression.

title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers references the wrong method
body: The Javadoc for requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says it throws ForbiddenException when canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false. It should reference canManageMembers(GroupModel).

title: Account UI message switched from i18next to Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax
body: This file uses i18next `{{0}}` interpolation throughout, but the new `error-invalid-multivalued-size` value uses Java MessageFormat `{0}`, `{1}`, and `{2,choice,...}`. The Account UI will not interpret the Java choice format; it will render raw `{0}`/`{1}` and the choice pattern instead of a correctly pluralized validation message.

title: Admin UI message switched from i18next to Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax
body: This admin UI message file uses i18next `{{0}}` interpolation, but the new `error-invalid-multivalued-size` value uses Java MessageFormat `{0}`, `{1}`, and `{2,choice,...}`. The admin UI will not interpret the Java choice format; it will render raw placeholders or the choice pattern instead of a properly pluralized validation message.

title: Choice-format normalization bypasses HTML sanitization
body: `value.replaceAll("\\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}", "...")` removes the entire `{n,choice,...}` block for `error-invalid-multivalued-size` and `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit.*`, not just the `<` comparison characters. This happens before `policy.sanitize`, so any HTML inside a choice alternative is invisible to the sanitizer and is not compared. A malicious translation can hide disallowed HTML such as `` inside one of these choice blocks and the verifier will approve it.

title: PropertyResourceBundle reads UTF-8 properties as ISO-8859-1
body: `new PropertyResourceBundle(new FileInputStream(file))` loads the `.properties` file as ISO-8859-1 via `Properties.load(InputStream)`, while the same file is read as UTF-8 by `Files.readString` elsewhere in this class. The changed message resources contain native non-Latin scripts such as Chinese and Arabic, so their values are read as mojibake and sanitized/compared on mangled strings. Use `new PropertyResourceBundle(Files.newBufferedReader(file.toPath(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8))` (and similarly for the English file).

title: Lithuanian account message `totpStep1` is now Italian
body: The new value is "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see Italian text in the account authenticator setup. The text should be translated into Lithuanian.

title: Lithuanian login message `loginTotpStep1` is now Italian
body: The new value is "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see Italian text on the login authenticator setup page. The text should be translated into Lithuanian.

title: Simplified Chinese file contains Traditional Chinese text
body: `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese characters (`手機`, `應用程式`) in the zh_CN Simplified Chinese resource. Simplified Chinese users will see mixed-script text. It should be written in Simplified Chinese, e.g. `在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：`.

title: Missing or unreadable English file causes unhandled RuntimeException
body: `verifySafeHtml()` catches `IOException` and throws `RuntimeException` when the English counterpart cannot be read or is missing. This bypasses the `MojoExecutionException` contract of `verify()` and causes a raw stack trace in the Maven plugin instead of a normal plugin error. Wrap these failures in `MojoExecutionException` or allow them to be handled by `verify()`.

title: i18next placeholders and ICU choice will render literally in React admin/account UIs
body: This file is consumed by the React account UI, where interpolation uses the i18next syntax {{0}}, {{1}}, etc. (see all other keys in this file such as backTo=Back to {{app}}). The new value uses Java MessageFormat placeholders {0}, {1} and a {2,choice,...} segment. i18next will not interpolate those or evaluate the choice format, so users will see literal braces and format text instead of the actual counted value. The same addition was made in js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties.

title: Lithuanian account message replaced with Italian text
body: The new totpStep1 value is 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian, while this is a Lithuanian resource file. Lithuanian users will see Italian text in the OTP setup instructions instead of the translated instruction.

title: Lithuanian login message replaced with Italian text
body: The new loginTotpStep1 value is 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian, while this is a Lithuanian resource file. Lithuanian users will see Italian text in the OTP setup instructions instead of the translated instruction.

title: Simplified Chinese account message replaced with Traditional Chinese text
body: The new totpStep1 value '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：' uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 應用程式), but this is the Simplified Chinese locale file. Simplified Chinese users will see Traditional Chinese text mixed into the otherwise Simplified Chinese UI.

title: Diff substring can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when prefix and suffix overlap
body: The common-prefix/common-suffix loop computes start and end independently. If the sanitized and original values differ only in a middle region and the common suffix overlaps the common prefix (for example with repeated or symmetric text), end can become greater than length - start, so value.substring(start, value.length() - end) is called with an end index before the start index. This throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and crashes the Maven verifier instead of reporting the actual 'Illegal HTML' difference.

title: PropertyResourceBundle is loaded with ISO-8859-1 instead of UTF-8
body: PropertyResourceBundle created from FileInputStream uses Properties.load(InputStream), which decodes bytes as ISO-8859-1. The Keycloak message properties are UTF-8 and contain raw non-Latin scripts such as Chinese, Arabic, and Cyrillic. Both the target and English bundles are therefore decoded to mojibake before sanitization and before any violation text is generated. Use a Reader with UTF-8 (for example Files.newBufferedReader) for both bundles so verification and error messages operate on the real message text.

title: Account UI validation message switched to Java MessageFormat syntax
body: The value was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The account UI uses i18next/react-i18next, which interpolates `{{0}}` placeholders and does not understand Java `choice` format or single-brace `{0}` placeholders. As a result, users will see raw placeholders and the choice expression instead of a localized validation message.

title: Admin UI validation message switched to Java MessageFormat syntax
body: The value was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The admin UI uses i18next/react-i18next, which interpolates `{{0}}` placeholders and does not understand Java `choice` format or single-brace `{0}` placeholders. As a result, users will see raw placeholders and the choice expression instead of a localized validation message.

title: Choice-pattern removal allows malicious HTML to bypass sanitizer
body: In `normalizeValue`, for keys starting with `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit` or `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, the code replaces the entire `{n,choice,...}` block with `...` before sanitizing. Any HTML inserted inside that choice block is removed before the sanitizer runs, so malicious or unintended HTML in those translation strings will not be reported. These keys are used in email bodies and validation messages, which may be rendered as HTML, so this can allow XSS through translations.

title: Lithuanian account message replaced with Italian text
body: The translation for `totpStep1` was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. This breaks the localized account UI for Lithuanian users.

title: Lithuanian login message replaced with Italian text
body: The translation for `loginTotpStep1` was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. This breaks the localized login screen for Lithuanian users.

title: Property files read with ISO-8859-1 instead of UTF-8
body: `new PropertyResourceBundle(fis)` loads the file using ISO-8859-1 by default, but Keycloak's message properties are UTF-8. This mis-decodes non-ASCII characters (e.g., Lithuanian, Chinese, Cyrillic), which can alter the values before HTML sanitization and produce false positives or false negatives. Use `PropertyResourceBundle(new InputStreamReader(fis, StandardCharsets.UTF_8))`.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: Adding an abstract method to a public SPI interface without a default implementation means any external/custom grant type provider implementing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory will no longer compile, and existing binary providers will throw AbstractMethodError when getShortcut() is invoked during DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(). Add a backward-compatible default method or otherwise handle factories that do not provide a shortcut.

title: Access token jti claim changes from UUID to prefixed ID
body: token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx)) now emits values like onrtac:<uuid> instead of the previous plain UUID. The jti claim is visible in issued access tokens and is often logged or treated as a UUID by clients and tests. This is an intentional format change, but it is a public token contract change that can break existing consumers that expect a 36-character UUID and should be called out as a migration/release-note concern.

title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
body: The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"), duplicating the grantType check and never checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted, and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId() will produce a token ID ending in ":null", violating the expected unique-ID format for jti. The check should requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

title: Decoder assumes 2-char grant shortcut but the SPI permits longer shortcuts
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId() rejects any encoded context whose prefix length is not 6 and splits the prefix into three two-character parts. However OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() is documented as 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' and is never validated to be exactly two characters. A custom grant provider returning a three-character shortcut will be encoded successfully as, for example, onrtabc:<uuid> with a 7-character context prefix, but the same token will later fail to parse here with IllegalArgumentException. Validate shortcut length/format in postInit or encoding, or make the decoder handle the documented contract.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher extracts the wrong characters and has inverted assertion
body: The grant type shortcut is positions 4-5, so it should be substring(4, 6), but the matcher uses substring(3, 5), which captures the second token-type character and the first grant-type character. It also returns false when that value equals the expected shortcut. As a result, the matcher does not actually verify the grant type and returns true for any access token whose suffix is a UUID and whose prefix has at least five characters. Tests using this matcher will not catch incorrect grant-type encoding. Fix the substring, remove the inverted return, and add a prefix-length check.

title: Removed public Context copy constructor breaks custom grant implementations
body: The public OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context) copy constructor was removed. Custom grant type implementations or tests that construct a context from an existing context will no longer compile, and existing binary consumers referencing that constructor will fail. If the constructor is removed intentionally, this is a breaking SPI change that should be documented; otherwise retain a deprecated copy constructor that also copies the new grantType field.

title: Constructor checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
body: At line 73, the constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"), so it validates grantType a second time and never rejects a null rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is then accepted and encodeTokenId can later produce an ID ending with the literal string "null". The argument should be rawTokenId.

title: Access token ID matcher does not validate grant type shortcut
body: In matchesSafely, the encoded token prefix such as "onrtac" has the grant type at indices 4-5 ("ac"), but the code calls substring(3, 5), which returns "ta". It also returns false when the substring equals the expected shortcut, which is inverted. As a result, these event assertions accept any encoded token ID regardless of its grant type and would reject a correct one if the offset were fixed. It should use substring(4, 6), guard the prefix length, and return false when the substring does not equal the expected grant shortcut.

title: Adding abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is a public provider-factory SPI. Adding `String getShortcut()` with no default means every existing third-party or custom grant type factory fails to compile until it implements the new method, and previously compiled factories can fail at runtime with an abstract-method error when loaded. Since this is an extension point, this is a breaking API change. Provide a default implementation, or make the shortcut optional via a separate interface.

title: Public Context copy constructor removed
body: The public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor has been removed from the public nested class `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. Existing custom grant implementations that clone the context using this constructor will no longer compile, or will fail with `NoSuchMethodError` if already compiled. If removing it is intentional, it should at least be called out as a breaking change because this class is part of the OAuth2 grant provider contract.

title: Default encoder assumes all context shortcuts are exactly 2 characters
body: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` hard-codes the encoded prefix length to 6 and splits it into three 2-character shortcuts. However `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` does not enforce a 2-character shortcut and its Javadoc says shortcuts are usually 3 letters. A valid custom grant type with a 3-letter shortcut will be encoded into a 7-character prefix and then later rejected during decoding with `IllegalArgumentException: Expected length of 6`. Shortcut length must be validated and enforced when factories are registered, or the parser must be made resilient to registered non-2-character shortcuts.

title: rawTokenId null check checks grantType twice
body: The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` where it should validate `rawTokenId`. As a result, a null `rawTokenId` is accepted and stored. Later, `encodeTokenId` can produce a token ID ending with `:null`, and multiple tokens built from null raw IDs could collide. The check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher logic is inverted
body: The matcher does `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, so it rejects exactly the token IDs it is supposed to accept: for an expected authorization-code token, actual ID `onrtac:<uuid>` will return false. It also allows IDs with a different shortcut to pass as long as the UUID part matches. The condition should return `true` on the expected shortcut match, and avoid falling through for a mismatched shortcut.

title: Lazy grant shortcut cache update can create inconsistent reverse mappings
body: In `getShortcutByGrantType`, when a grant type is not cached, the factory is looked up and the shortcut is inserted into both `grantsByShortcuts` and `grantsToShortcuts` without the duplicate validation performed in `postInit`. If a newly deployed grant factory uses a shortcut already mapped to another grant type, `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` overwrites the old mapping while `grantsToShortcuts` now has two grant types pointing to the same shortcut. The same encoded shortcut will then decode to the new grant even for tokens issued for the older grant, silently corrupting the grant-type context. The lazy refresh path should validate shortcut uniqueness or update the maps consistently.

title: All-used federated recovery codes are removed through the local credential API
body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential now prefers federated credentials, so when the final recovery code is used, removeStoredCredentialById may be called with a federated credential ID. This API removes only credentials stored in the Keycloak DB, not federated user-storage credentials. If the federated provider returns a CredentialModel without a local DB id, such as the included test provider does, the call can no-op or throw. As a result, the user can keep an all-used credential and may be repeatedly forced to reconfigure recovery codes, or login may fail instead of completing cleanly.

title: Plaintext recovery codes are passed to user storage
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generated recovery codes and passes them as the challengeResponse to user.credentialManager().updateCredential. The local Keycloak provider hashes recovery codes before persisting them, but user-storage providers receive the plaintext codes. The included test provider stores exactly this value in credentialData. A production user-storage provider following the same pattern would store usable recovery codes unhashed, exposing valid recovery credentials if the external user store is compromised. Consider passing only hashed values or explicitly enforcing hashing in the user-storage SPI contract.

title: Recovery code form can throw NoSuchElementException for user-storage credentials
body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential returns an Optional, but this code immediately calls get(). Since recovery codes can now be created in user storage, a provider that implements updateCredential/isValid for recovery codes but does not expose them through getFederatedCredentialsStream/getCredentials (where the default is empty) will cause getCredential to return empty and the login form to throw NoSuchElementException while rendering, instead of showing a proper challenge or error.

title: Federated recovery credential test model loses the stored ID and does not consume codes
body: getCredentials builds a new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel from the raw stored codes but does not copy myUser.recoveryCodes.getId(), so the returned credential id is null. It also validates the raw code list without marking the entered code as used. This is the provider used to cover the new user-storage recovery path, so the test does not exercise final-code consumption or removal and hides the all-codes-used removal problem in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.

title: Federated exhausted recovery credential is removed with local-storage API
body: After switching to RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, optUserCredentialFound can be a federated credential. When allCodesUsed is true, this line calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()). That API removes credentials from Keycloak's local credential store, not from the user-storage provider that owns the federated credential. Federated credential models may also have no local persistent ID (for example the test provider returns a model built via createFromValues without copying the stored ID). As a result, after the last recovery code the exhausted federated credential is not removed, or the call fails for a null ID, leaving the credential lifecycle broken. This path is not covered by the added test because it only uses the first code.

title: Recovery codes are not consumed by the test user storage provider
body: The new recovery-code validation branch only checks whether the submitted code is present in the stored list and returns true. It never removes the matched code or persists a reduced list, so recovery codes remain reusable indefinitely in this test provider. Consequently the added test does not exercise one-time-use behavior or the all-codes-used removal path in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator. The provider should consume/update the verified code, or a test should cover reuse and exhaustion.

title: Federated recovery codes are not consumed after successful use
body: After `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().isValid(...)` succeeds, this code fetches the recovery-code credential only to inspect `allCodesUsed()`. It never marks the submitted code as used or removes it. The built-in local recovery-code provider consumes the code during `isValid`, but the new user-storage path delegates validation to the storage provider. The included `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid` does a raw list comparison and returns true without updating the stored data, so the same backup code remains valid and can be replayed, and `allCodesUsed()` never becomes true so the user is never forced to renew codes. Recovery/backup codes must be single-use.

title: Recovery-code credential returned with an ID that does not match persisted federated credential
body: `updateCredential` persists `recoveryCodesModel` with the ID assigned at line 195 (`KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()`). `getCredentials` ignores that persisted model and builds a new `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` via `createFromValues` from the raw JSON, returning a different (or null) credential ID. `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` later calls `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` when `allCodesUsed()` is true. Because that ID does not identify the stored federated credential, removal fails/no-ops and the used-up recovery-code credential remains in user storage. The provider should preserve the persisted credential ID and update the same model as codes are used.

title: getSubGroupsStream overloads still NPE when group deleted concurrently
body: The same race fixed in getSubGroupsCount remains here: after isUpdated() returns false, the method directly calls modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...). If the group was deleted after this adapter was obtained from the cache, getGroupModel() returns null, so modelSupplier.get() returns null and the call throws NPE. The null check added to getSubGroupsCount should be applied to these overloads as well (see also lines 262 and 268).

title: Concurrency test asserts before reader thread is joined
body: The reader thread is started at line 139 and is never joined or otherwise awaited. The main thread sets deletedAll = true and immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty, so the test can pass before the reader observes the stop flag, before an in-flight request completes, or even when the thread has not run at all. The thread can also continue making admin requests after the test method returns and after realm cleanup begins, causing flaky failures. Join the thread (with a timeout) or use an executor/latch to ensure it has exited before asserting.

title: Regression test does not wait for the reader thread before asserting
body: The test creates a raw reader thread at line 139 but never retains or joins it. After setting deletedAll to true, the main thread immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty at this line. Any in-flight groups() call that began before deletedAll was set can still fail after the assertion and add an exception too late, so the test can pass even if the NPE it is meant to catch occurs. Retain the thread and join it with a timeout before asserting, or use an ExecutorService/Future so the read is complete before the assertion.

title: Other getSubGroupsStream overloads still dereference a null model supplier
body: The PR fixes getSubGroupsCount by checking modelSupplier.get() for null (line 274), but the three getSubGroupsStream overloads at lines 256, 262, and 268 still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. Under the same concurrent group deletion that causes the original NPE, modelSupplier.get() can return null and these methods will still throw NPE. Use the same null-handling strategy, or a shared helper, so all concurrent access paths are covered.

title: NPE on concurrent group deletion still present in subgroup stream methods
