With multiple calendar references (one per collective host), this always resolves to the first reference. Therefore the second and subsequent host events are never deleted; instead the first host's event is deleted repeatedly with different credentials. It should use the current `reference`/credentialId to select the matching booking reference.

title: Destination calendar webhook payload type changes from null/object to array
body: The test now expects `destinationCalendar: []` for BOOKING_REJECTED where it previously was `null`. Because this field is part of the public webhook payload, existing webhook consumers that expect an object or null will break. This should be called out/migrated as a breaking webhook payload change.

title: No tests cover multi-destination collective booking/cancel/reschedule
body: The PR only updates one webhook expectation; the central multi-destination logic in handleNewBooking, EventManager, and handleCancelBooking (including recurring cancellation) has no tests. Given the bug-prone branches, add e2e/unit tests for multiple hosts with different calendar providers and for cancellation/rescheduling.

title: Potential TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty or undefined
body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and can be `undefined` when the array is empty or when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null. The condition then dereferences it with `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without optional chaining. When an event with Google Meet location has no destination calendar, this throws and aborts the booking flow. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` or explicitly guard for undefined.

title: Reschedule cleanup only removes first old calendar event
body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, when `newBookingId` is set for a reschedule and old events need to be removed, the old calendar event is selected with `booking.references.find(...)`. Since this PR now supports multiple calendar references, only the first old calendar event is deleted; events for other hosts remain on their calendars, causing stale or duplicate events after reschedule. Filter all old calendar references and delete each.

title: Recurring cancellation only cancels first calendar reference per booking
body: In the recurring `allRemainingBookings` branch, each updated booking's calendar reference is selected with `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`. With multiple calendar references now possible, this cancels only one calendar event per recurring instance and silently leaves other hosts' calendar events intact. All calendar references for each updated booking should be iterated and scheduled for deletion.

title: Collective team destination calendars not added when organizer has none
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists. Then `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op on `null`, so for collective events where only team members have destination calendars, those calendars are never added and no events are created for them. Initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array before pushing, for example `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

title: Calendar.createEvent contract changed without updating all implementations
body: The `Calendar` interface now requires `credentialId` in `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)`. However LarkCalendarService, Office365CalendarService, and BaseCalendarService still implement `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` with only one parameter. This is a contract break that will cause TypeScript errors and a build failure. Update all implementations to accept and use the credentialId, or make the interface parameter optional.

title: Fallback calendar selection condition is impossible
body: In `updateEvent`, `selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. If `externalCalendarId` is truthy, the else branch never runs; if it is falsy, the predicate compares against a falsy value and never matches, leaving `selectedCalendar` undefined. The same broken pattern appears in `deleteEvent` around line 317. Updating or deleting events with a null/undefined `externalCalendarId` will target an undefined calendarId and fail. Use a fallback that selects the appropriate destination (e.g., first destination or by credential).

title: Organizer email uses first destination calendar for all created events
body: In `createEvent` and `updateEvent`, the organizer attendee email is set to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`, where `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is the first item of `destinationCalendar`. When multiple collective hosts each have their own destination calendar, events created for later credentials still use the first host's calendar externalId as organizer email, resulting in incorrect organizer identity and potentially invalid IDs. The destination matching the credential being used should determine the organizer email.

title: Reversed slug/requestedSlug conditions for organization creation
body: The diff changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})`. This reverses the intended behavior: now when team billing is enabled, both `slug` and `requestedSlug` are set, and when disabled, neither is set. This likely breaks organization slug assignment for non-billing deployments. Restore the original conditions.

title: CalDAV createEvent ignores credentialId and uses only first destination
body: `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` does not accept the new `credentialId` parameter and always uses `mainHostDestinationCalendar` (the first entry in `event.destinationCalendar`) to select the calendar. In multi-host collective events, every credential will create the event on the same first host's CalDAV calendar, causing duplicates on one calendar and missing events on the others. It must select the destination calendar matching the credential being used.

title: Dereferences undefined destination calendar for Google Meet fallback
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` produces `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty. The next line accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`, so any booking with `MeetLocationType` and no destination calendar throws a TypeError during event creation. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` or guard the value.

title: Google update event selects no calendar when externalCalendarId is missing
body: In `updateEvent`, the else branch runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but then executes `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. That compares `cal.externalId` to null/undefined and normally returns undefined, so `calendar.events.update` receives `calendarId: undefined`. Rescheduling or updating a Google event without a stored `externalCalendarId` fails. The selection should look up the destination for the current credential/first destination, with a primary fallback.

title: Google delete event can fall back to primary for secondary calendars
body: In `deleteEvent`, when `externalCalendarId` is null the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since the find predicate compares to null/undefined, it normally returns undefined, so `calendarId` falls back to `"primary"`. For events originally created on a secondary calendar but whose reference has no `externalCalendarId`, this deletes from the wrong calendar or misses the real event. The destination should be resolved by credential or first destination, not by comparing with the missing ID.

title: Google Meet hangout patch uses undefined calendarId on primary fallback
body: `createEvent` inserts with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` that adds the hangout link uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly. When no destination calendar matches the credentialId, `selectedCalendar` is undefined even though the event was created on primary, so the patch is sent with an undefined calendar ID and can fail. The patch should use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` fallback.

title: Team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither the event type nor organizer has one. Later, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op on `null`, so host calendars are silently discarded. For collective events where the organizer lacks a calendar but hosts have configured calendars, no events are created for the hosts. Initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` to `[]` before the push, or assign `[...teamDestinationCalendars]` explicitly.

title: Recurring cancellation only deletes first calendar reference per booking
body: In the recurring cancellation branch, for every updated booking the code uses `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`. With multiple calendar references (the newly supported multi-host case), only the first reference is selected; the loop then tries that same UID against every calendar credential. The remaining host calendar events for each recurring booking are never deleted, leaving ghost events after cancellation. The code should iterate all calendar references and use each reference's own credentialId/type/externalCalendarId.

title: Office 365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
body: `createEvent` destructures only `[mainHostDestinationCalendar]` from the array and does not know which destination the current EventManager loop iteration is targeting. When a collective event has multiple Office 365 host calendars, every Office 365 credential creates the event in the first host's calendar instead of its own. This service needs to select the destination matching the current credential, similar to the Google implementation, or otherwise receive the current destination external ID.

title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
body: `createEvent` only reads `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and uses that calendar ID. EventManager now invokes createEvent for each host destination, but the same full `destinationCalendar` array is passed every time and the service does not select the current credential's destination. For collective events with multiple Lark-calendar hosts, each event is created on the first host's Lark calendar rather than the correct host's calendar.

title: Organization slug condition was inverted
body: The previous logic used `!(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED) && { slug }`, meaning the Team/org got a `slug` when team billing was not enabled. This PR changes it to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, so the slug is only set when billing is enabled and omitted when it is disabled. The `requestedSlug` metadata change at line 153 is similarly inverted. This changes organization creation behavior based on the billing flag and can break subdomain/org provisioning.

title: Zod schema uses an object toString as a property key, so credential sharing validation always fails
body: In minimumTokenResponseSchema, the computed property `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` evaluates to a literal key like "[object Object]" and requires that exact property to exist. Real OAuth refresh responses do not contain such a key, so `safeParse(response)` will fail whenever APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and the sync endpoint is used, causing every affected integration to throw "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` or a proper passthrough schema instead of computed keys.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with a dummy string, corrupting stored credentials
body: The code assigns `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` whenever the token response omits that field. Many OAuth providers, like Microsoft, do not return a refresh token on refresh. Callers that merge `response.data` into their existing credential (for example Office 365) will overwrite the real refresh token with this invalid placeholder, causing subsequent refreshes to fail with invalid_grant. Preserve the existing refresh token instead of injecting a dummy value.

title: Returns raw fetch Response, breaking callers that expect token data objects
body: When credential sharing is enabled, this function returns the raw `Response` from `fetch(CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT)` instead of parsing it into the shape that callers expect. Callers such as Google Calendar (`const token = res?.data;`), HubSpot (`await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` as a token object with `.expiresIn`), and Zoho apps (`tokenInfo.data`) assume either an object with a `.data` property or direct token fields. With a native `Response` those properties are undefined, causing TypeErrors or silently skipped refreshes. Define a single response contract and parse the response accordingly, or update every caller to handle the returned type.

title: Stores Zod safeParse result wrapper instead of parsed credential in the database
body: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` returns the entire `safeParse` result object (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), but that value is then saved as the credential key. This corrupts the persisted Google Calendar credential; the next load will fail when `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` receives this wrapper instead of the expected token object. Use the `.data` property of the parse result for the stored key.

title: prisma is used but not imported
body: The newly added code calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` in `getClient`, but this file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";` at the top. At runtime this will throw `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` whenever Salesforce credentials are refreshed. Add the missing import.

title: Passes credentialId instead of userId to credential sync endpoint
body: In `refreshAccessToken`, the call to `refreshOAuthTokens` passes `credentialId` as the third argument, which is treated as the userId. That value is sent as `calcomUserId` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, so the self-hosted platform receives the internal Cal.com credential ID rather than the owning user's ID and cannot correctly sync the right user's credentials. Pass the actual user ID associated with the credential, such as `credential.userId`.

title: Updating an existing credential does not clear the invalid flag
body: When the webhook updates an existing credential, it only replaces `key` but leaves any previous `invalid: true` value untouched. If a credential was marked invalid (for example after an invalid_grant error) and the self-hosted app store then pushes fresh valid keys, the credential remains invalid and continues to be ignored by the app. The update should set `invalid: false` when synced credentials are meant to reactivate the connection.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys are invalid and strip token fields
body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the string `'[object Object]'`, not a dynamic key. The second computed key at line 10 also evaluates to `'[object Object]'` and overwrites the first. The resulting zod object only allows `access_token` and a property named `'[object Object]'`, so when credential sharing is enabled it strips `refresh_token`, `expiry_date` / `expires_in`, and all other fields from the sync response. The fallback then sets `refresh_token` to the literal string `'refresh_token'`. Affected integrations (Google, Office 365, Zoom, Webex, Salesforce) will persist incomplete or corrupt credentials and token refresh will fail.

title: External refresh path returns a raw fetch Response, but callers expect provider response objects
body: In credential-sharing mode this function returns the raw `Response` from `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`. Several callers treat the return value as an axios/googleapis style object with `.data` (Google Calendar, HubSpot, Zoho Bigin, Zoho CRM) or as a token object (HubSpot). With `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` set, those code paths access undefined properties and throw or save corrupt credentials. The helper should parse the sync response and return a consistent shape, or all callers must be updated to handle `Response`.

title: `token` is undefined when using external credential sync
body: `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;`. When `refreshOAuthTokens` takes the sync branch, it returns a fetch `Response` (see refreshOAuthTokens.ts), whose `.data` property does not exist. `token` is undefined and the next line throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'access_token')`, breaking Google Calendar token refresh for self-hosters with credential sync enabled.

title: Credential key stores the Zod safeParse result instead of the parsed data
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `SafeParseReturnType` object `{ success, data }`, not the parsed credential object. Assigning `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` and then `data: { key }` persists that wrapper as the credential key. Subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` will fail because the key is `{ success: true, data: {...} }`. Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` or make the helper return only the parsed data.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported
body: The newly added `await prisma.credential.update(...)` uses the `prisma` client, but this file has no `import prisma from '@calcom/prisma';` and no other binding. Constructing `SalesforceCalendarService` will throw `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime. Add the missing import.

title: Newly refreshed access token is not used for the jsforce connection
body: The code performs a refresh-token exchange and stores `accessTokenParsed.data` back to the DB, but then creates the connection with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token`, the old token from the original credential. If that token is expired (the reason a refresh is needed), the connection is built with an invalid token and subsequent Salesforce API calls fail. It should use `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

title: `credentialId` is passed where `refreshOAuthTokens` expects a user id
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFn, appSlug, userId)` sends the third argument as `calcomUserId` to the credential sync endpoint. This call passes `credentialId` (the DB credential record id) instead of `credentialKey.userId` or `credential.userId`. The external platform will receive the wrong user identifier and may sync tokens to the wrong account or reject the request.

title: Credential find-then-create/update is racy and can create duplicates
body: The handler does `findFirst` and then either `update` or `create` without a transaction or uniqueness constraint. If two valid webhook requests for the same user/app arrive concurrently, both can observe no existing credential and both insert a new row. Callers may then pick either credential, leading to split or inconsistent state. Use an upsert based on a unique key or wrap the check/update in a transaction with appropriate locking.

title: Missing prisma import in SalesforceCalendarService
body: The code at line 96 calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file does not import `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. This will fail TypeScript compilation/build and makes the Salesforce calendar service unusable.

title: Google Calendar stores Zod SafeParse result instead of token data
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the whole `safeParse` result object (for example `{ success: true, data: { ... } }`), not `refreshTokenResponse.data`. Here `key` is assigned that wrapper and then persisted with `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. On the next instantiation `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` will receive the wrapper rather than the actual Google credentials, so the credential becomes invalid/unusable.

title: Google token refresh crashes when credential sync endpoint is enabled
body: When `refreshOAuthTokens` takes the sync branch, it returns a `fetch` `Response`. This code then does `const token = res?.data;`, but a web `Response` has no `.data` property, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` at line 95 throws. Refreshing Google Calendar tokens fails whenever credential sharing is active.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token"
body: If the parsed response does not contain `refresh_token`, the code writes `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. For providers that intentionally omit the refresh token on a refresh response, this overwrites the real refresh token with a fake literal value, causing all subsequent refresh attempts to fail with `invalid_grant` or equivalent.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys do not work as intended
body: The schema uses `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` as computed property names. `z.string().toString()` evaluates to `"[object Object]"`, so the two declarations target the same key and the later optional-unknown rule overrides the numeric-expiry rule. The resulting schema only requires `access_token`; it does not enforce any expiry field and zod strips fields such as `refresh_token`, `expires_in`, or `expiry_date` from the parsed data.

title: refreshOAuthTokens returns different shapes depending on branch
body: In the sync branch this utility returns a `fetch` `Response`, while in the regular branch it returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns, often an axios response or a provider token object. Callers such as Hubspot, Zoho Bigin, and Zoho CRM access `.data` or token-specific fields on the result. With credential sharing enabled, those callers receive a `Response`, have no `.data`/provider fields, and throw or silently store broken tokens.

title: Hubspot refresh breaks when sync mode returns a fetch Response
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `Response` in sync mode, but `hubspotRefreshToken` is typed and used as a Hubspot token object. Accessing `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` at line 192 yields `undefined`, so `Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` becomes `NaN` and the stored expiry is corrupted.

title: Zoho Bigin refresh breaks when sync mode returns a fetch Response
body: When `refreshOAuthTokens` takes the sync branch it returns a `Response`, but this code reads `tokenInfo.data.error`. A fetch `Response` has no `data` property, so this throws a TypeError and token refresh fails.

title: Zoho CRM refresh breaks when sync mode returns a fetch Response
body: When `refreshOAuthTokens` takes the sync branch it returns a `Response`, but this code reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`. A fetch `Response` has no `data` property, so this throws a TypeError and token refresh fails.

title: Credential lookup and create/update are not atomic
body: The endpoint performs `findFirst` and then either `update` or `create` without a transaction or unique constraint. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both observe no existing credential and both create one, leaving duplicate credentials for the same app.

title: Webhook handler has uncaught parse/decrypt errors and no method check
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` and the later `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` are not wrapped in error handling. A malformed body, invalid encrypted payload, or wrong decryption key will throw an unhandled error and produce a generic 500 response. The handler also does not restrict the HTTP method, so GET/HEAD/etc. can enter this code path.

title: Webhook secret comparison is not constant-time
body: The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time. An attacker who can measure response timing may be able to brute-force the header value byte by byte. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on fixed-length digests instead.

title: No tests for new credential-sync webhook or refresh helpers
body: The PR introduces a security-sensitive webhook endpoint and new shared OAuth refresh/sync utilities, but the checklist explicitly states tests were not added. The endpoint and utilities have multiple mode-dependent branches and would benefit from tests covering malformed payloads, missing env vars, sync vs non-sync refresh paths, and duplicate webhook deliveries.

title: Team admins are denied permission due to && instead of ||
body: The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be both team admin and team owner simultaneously, which effectively excludes team admins who are not owners. As a result, team admins cannot add guests to team event bookings even though they should have permission, causing a 403 FORBIDDEN error on a valid action.

title: Case-sensitive email comparison bypasses blacklist and duplicate detection
body: The blacklist emails are lowercased, but the input guest emails are not normalized before comparison (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Similarly, duplicate detection against existing attendees uses `guest === attendee.email` without lowercasing. An attacker can bypass the blacklist by using mixed-case emails (e.g., `Blocked@example.com`) and may create duplicate attendees when an existing attendee's email differs only by case. This can lead to unwanted calendar invitations and data integrity issues.

title: Calendar update uses acting user's credentials instead of organizer's
body: The handler builds the EventManager with `ctx.user` and credentials fetched from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, ignoring the booking's actual organizer stored in `booking.user` (which includes `credentials` and `destinationCalendar`). If the person adding guests is a team admin or a different attendee, calendar invitations are sent/updated using that user's calendar integration, not the organizer's. This can fail to update the correct calendar, send invites from the wrong email, or expose the acting user's calendar credentials to the event.

title: No seats capacity check before adding guests
body: For bookings with limited seats (`seatsPerTimeSlot`), the handler does not check whether adding new guests would exceed the allowed number of attendees. Users can add unlimited guests beyond the configured seat limit, leading to over-capacity bookings and inconsistent data between the booking and event type capacity.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails uses original input list instead of actually added guests
body: The function receives `newGuests` as the original `guests` array from the input, not the filtered `uniqueGuests` that were actually added. If the input contained an existing attendee's email (duplicate) or a blacklisted email, that email will still appear in `newGuests`. For existing attendees, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` will be true, causing them to receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a new booking confirmation) instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. This can confuse users and duplicate confirmation emails. The function should instead receive the list of emails that were actually added (`uniqueGuests`).

title: Add-guests emails ignore event-type email disable settings
body: Other email sending functions in this file check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` from the event type metadata and skip sending if disabled. `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept or check these flags, so organizer/attendee emails are sent even for event types where standard emails are disabled. This violates user preferences and may send unwanted notifications.

title: Error toast shows raw TRPC code and may not fallback to default message
body: The error handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then does `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. If `err.data?.code` is undefined, the message becomes `undefined: <translation>`, which is truthy, so the fallback is never used. Additionally, `err.data?.code` is a TRPC error code like `BAD_REQUEST` or `FORBIDDEN`, not a user-facing message, and concatenating it with a colon produces output like "BAD_REQUEST: Emails must be unique and valid". The toast should display a friendly error, not the internal code.

title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
body: The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires a user to be both a team admin and a team owner simultaneously to pass. In Cal.com, team admins and team owners are distinct roles; most admins are not owners and vice versa. As a result, authorized team admins (or owners) who are not both will be denied when they are not the organizer or an attendee, breaking the add guests feature for team bookings. The condition should use `||` not `&&`.

title: Uses current user's credentials instead of organizer's for calendar updates
body: The handler creates `EventManager` with `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is the session user and `credentials` come from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. When a team admin, attendee, or anyone other than the booking organizer adds guests, the calendar update will be attempted using the requester's credentials, not the organizer's. This can fail to update the organizer's calendar or update the wrong calendar, leaving invitees without proper calendar invitations. The EventManager should be constructed with the booking organizer's credentials (or team members' credentials), not the current user's.

title: Passes raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests` to email function
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the raw input array `guests`, not the filtered `uniqueGuests`. `guests` may contain emails that were filtered out (already existing attendees or blacklisted). Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the logic decides whether to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` or `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` based on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. If an existing attendee's email was in the raw input but was not actually added, they will incorrectly receive a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (the standard booking confirmation) instead of the 'new guests added' notification. The function should receive the actual newly added email list (`uniqueGuests`).

title: New guest emails ignore event type email disable settings
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept `eventTypeMetadata` and does not call `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` or `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`, unlike other email functions such as `sendScheduledEmails` or `sendLocationChangeEmails`. As a result, even when an event type has host or attendee standard emails disabled, this function will still send organizer and attendee add-guests emails. Users who opted out of email notifications will receive unwanted emails. The function should respect the event type's email disable flags.

title: Does not check booking status before allowing guest additions
body: The handler fetches the booking but never validates `booking.status`. A cancelled or rejected booking can still have new attendees added via the API, leading to emails and calendar updates for a non-active event. The UI hides the action for cancelled bookings, but the API remains open. The handler should reject adding guests to bookings with statuses like CANCELLED, REJECTED, or any terminal status.

title: `booking.userId` may be null for team bookings causing findFirstOrThrow failure
body: `const organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } });` assumes `booking.userId` is always set. For team events (especially collective or round robin where the booking may not be assigned to a single user), `booking.userId` can be null. The fallback `|| 0` queries for a user with id 0, which does not exist and throws an error, causing the entire mutation to fail. The organizer should be determined using `booking.eventType?.userId` or the included `booking.user` relation, with appropriate handling for null.

title: Server-side schema allows duplicate guest emails
body: The schema defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` but does not enforce that the array is non-empty or that emails within the array are unique. Client-side validation in `AddGuestsDialog` prevents duplicates for normal UI usage, but a direct API request can send duplicates. The handler filters against existing attendees only, not within the input, so duplicate attendee records with the same email can be created in the database. The schema should use `.min(1)` and a uniqueness refinement, or the handler should deduplicate the input.

title: Passes stale pre-update booking object to updateCalendarAttendees
body: `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` uses the `booking` object fetched before the attendee update. If `updateCalendarAttendees` relies on `booking.attendees` to determine which attendees are new or removed, it will operate on the old attendee list while `evt.attendees` contains the updated list. This can result in incorrect calendar invitations (e.g., not sending invitations to newly added guests or sending updates to removed ones). The updated booking object (returned by `prisma.booking.update`) should be passed instead, or the method should be verified to only use `evt.attendees`.

title: Error message fallback never used due to template literal always truthy
body: In `onError`, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a string, even if `err.data?.code` and `err.message` are undefined (resulting in "undefined: undefined"). Therefore the later condition `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never uses the fallback translation. The error toast can show a confusing or misleading message. The fallback should be applied before constructing the string, or use a conditional that checks the presence of actual data.

title: Team admin/owner authorization uses AND instead of OR
body: The permission check `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` requires the user to be both admin and owner, which is almost never true. A team admin who is not an owner (or vice versa) will be denied. This should use `||` to allow either role. Consequence: legitimate team administrators cannot add guests to team bookings through this endpoint.

title: Calendar update uses requesting user's credentials instead of organizer's
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` returns the credentials of the user making the request, not the booking organizer. If the caller is an attendee or a team admin who is not the organizer, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will attempt to update the external calendar using the wrong credentials, likely failing to update the organizer's calendar and potentially modifying the caller's calendar with an event they do not own. The handler should always use the booking organizer's credentials, matching the identity in `evt.organizer`.

title: Add guests emails ignore user email preferences
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not check `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` or `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` from `eventTypeMetadata`, nor any host/attendee email disabled flags. Other email-sending functions in this file respect these settings. As a result, users who have disabled standard booking emails for attendees or hosts will still receive these new-guest notifications, violating their configured preferences.

title: Guest de-duplication and blacklist checks are case-sensitive
body: The filter comparing `guest` to existing attendees (`guest === attendee.email`) and to blacklist (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`) is case-sensitive, while the blacklist itself is lowercased. This allows adding the same email with different casing as a duplicate attendee and can bypass the blacklist if the input email is not lowercase. The result is duplicate attendees in the booking and possible emails to addresses that should be blocked.

title: No booking status validation before adding guests
body: The handler does not check `booking.status`. It proceeds even if the booking is cancelled, rejected, or in the past. An API caller can add guests to a cancelled booking, which triggers calendar updates and sends emails about an event that no longer exists. The endpoint should reject modifications for non-active bookings (e.g., status must be ACCEPTED or PENDING).

title: Overriding getNodeMailerPayload may omit cancellation links and other base-class content
body: The new `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` class completely overrides `getNodeMailerPayload` without calling `super`. The base `AttendeeScheduledEmail` may include additional payload elements such as cancellation links, additional notes, or attachments. By not inheriting those, existing attendees receiving this notification may lose important information (e.g., the ability to cancel) that would normally be present in a booking email.

title: Using array index as React key causes focus issues after removal
body: The email input list uses `key={index}`. When an item is removed, React may reuse the DOM node for the wrong item because keys are not stable. This can cause input values to be incorrectly associated and focus loss while editing multiple emails. A stable unique identifier (e.g., a generated id) should be used instead of the index.

title: Error toast prepends error code but translation may be incorrect
body: The `onError` handler builds `message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`. `t(err.message)` assumes `err.message` is always a valid translation key. If the server returns a raw error message (e.g., from Prisma), `t` will likely return the key unchanged, resulting in a confusing toast that includes an internal code and an untranslated string. The fallback `unable_to_add_guests` is only used when `message` is empty, which is unlikely because the code prefix ensures it is non-empty.

title: Retry cleanup is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The new deleteMany OR arm is `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` without `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. Since `retryCount` now exists on every WorkflowReminder row regardless of method, this SMS cron endpoint will delete EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders once their retryCount exceeds 1, either now through other code paths or in the future when those methods adopt retryCount. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and preferably `scheduled: false`) to this arm so only failing SMS reminders are removed.

title: retryCount increment is not atomic
body: The code reads `reminder.retryCount` once in the initial findMany and later writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` in both failure paths. If two cron invocations overlap and process the same unscheduled reminder, both can read the same value (for example 0) and both write 1, so the count never reaches 2 and the reminder may be retried indefinitely or scheduled multiple times. Use Prisma's atomic `increment: 1` or a conditional update instead of client-side arithmetic.

title: No tests for retry/deletion behavior
body: This PR changes workflow reminder deletion behavior and adds a retry limit, but there are no tests covering the two-failure deletion path, the success path, or ensuring non-SMS reminders are not deleted. Given the deleteMany can remove workflow reminders, a regression test is warranted.

title: Non-atomic retryCount increment can lose updates under concurrent cron runs
body: Both the else branch (line 184) and the catch block (line 195) set retryCount to `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value loaded at the start of the loop. If two cron instances run simultaneously (e.g., multiple deployments or a sharded scheduler), both may read the same retryCount and write the same incremented value, causing one increment to be lost. This could allow more than two scheduling attempts or prevent deletion when the limit is exceeded. Use Prisma's atomic `increment: { retryCount: 1 }` instead.

title: Deletion condition for retryCount > 1 lacks method filter
body: The deleteMany at the top of the handler uses an OR condition: one branch deletes SMS reminders with scheduledDate in the past, the other deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of `method`. Currently only this SMS handler increments retryCount, but if the field is later used for email or WhatsApp reminders (or if existing data contains non-SMS rows with retryCount > 1), those unrelated reminders would be silently deleted. The second OR branch should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to restrict deletion to SMS reminders.

title: No tests added for new retry count behavior
body: The PR introduces a new retryCount field and modifies deletion logic, but no tests are added to verify that a reminder is deleted after exactly two scheduling failures, that one failure does not cause deletion, or that successful scheduling does not reset/change retryCount. This is a critical behavior change in a cron job; without tests the risk of regression is high.

title: DeleteMany on retryCount > 1 may cause sequential scan
body: The new deletion condition `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` is not covered by any existing index on WorkflowReminder. In a large deployment with many workflow reminders, this branch can trigger a sequential scan of the entire table on every cron run, degrading performance. An index on `retryCount` (or a partial index where retryCount > 1) should be considered.

title: Post-schedule DB failure is counted as SMS scheduling failure
body: The catch block wraps both `twilio.scheduleSMS` and the subsequent `prisma.workflowReminder.update` that marks the reminder as scheduled. If Twilio successfully schedules the SMS but the DB update fails (transient DB error, unique `referenceId` conflict, etc.), the code increments `retryCount` as if the SMS scheduling failed. The reminder remains `scheduled: false`, so the next cron run will schedule the same SMS again, causing duplicate messages. After two such failures the reminder is deleted even though an SMS is already scheduled on Twilio. The retry count should only be incremented for failures from the actual scheduling call, not for failures while updating the result record.

title: Retry-based deletion is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The new OR branch deletes every `WorkflowReminder` whose `retryCount` is greater than 1, without filtering by `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. Although this PR currently only increments `retryCount` for SMS reminders, `retryCount` is a column on the shared `WorkflowReminder` model, so EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders could be silently deleted if they ever have `retryCount > 1`. The condition should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and probably `scheduled: false` to avoid deleting valid reminders for other methods.

title: Missing sendTo or empty message never increments retry count
body: The retry count is only incremented when `twilio.scheduleSMS` is actually called and fails or throws. If `message` is empty or `sendTo` is missing/falsy, the reminder is skipped entirely, remains `scheduled: false`, and retains the same `retryCount`. Such reminders will be selected forever on every cron run, which is the exact repeated-scheduling problem this PR is meant to fix. Missing or invalid recipient data should also count as a failed attempt or otherwise remove the reminder.

title: retryCount update is not atomic and can lose failures under concurrent runs
body: Both failure paths set `retryCount` to `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value fetched at the start of the handler. If this endpoint is invoked concurrently by overlapping cron runs, two attempts can both read `retryCount: 0` and both write `retryCount: 1`, so two failures are counted as one. The reminder may then be retried indefinitely instead of deleted after two failures. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead of setting it from the stale value.

title: Removing findMany and changing condition return types breaks existing consumers
body: The public `findMany()` method was removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions()`. Because this is an exported service and this PR only updates its tests, any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany({ select, where, ... })` will fail to compile. The return types of `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` also changed from Prisma where inputs to `Prisma.Sql`, which breaks consumers that pass them to Prisma model methods or merge them as objects. Either retain a query method that uses raw SQL internally or update all consumers in the same PR.

title: Public options type makes teamId optional and silently returns no rows when it is missing
body: The new `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` type declares `teamId?` for every scope. The constructor passes that type through to the schema `safeParse`, but if `scope: 'team'` is supplied without `teamId`, validation fails and `this.options` is silently set to `null`; `getAuthorizationConditions` then returns `1=0`, yielding an empty result with no error. The previous discriminated-union type made this a compile-time error. Use the discriminated union or derive the public options type from the schema so missing `teamId` is caught.

title: Org scope drops individual bookings when organization has no child teams
body: `userIdsFromOrg` is populated only when `teamsFromOrg.length > 0`. For an organization with no child teams, `teamsFromOrg` is empty, so the second authorization branch for individual (`isTeamBooking = false`) bookings is omitted. Org owners/admins therefore cannot see non-team bookings for an org without child teams, even though `teamIds` includes `options.orgId` and org memberships should be considered. This path is not covered by the new tests, all of which create at least one child team.

title: Caching behavior is no longer tested after raw SQL conversion
body: The old integration suite had explicit tests for `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` caching, and they were removed rather than converted. The service still has `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` and now caches `Prisma.Sql` objects, so a regression in caching would go undetected. Add tests that call each method twice and assert the cached value is reused.

title: Public findMany method removed without updating consumers
body: The previous InsightsBookingService exposed a public findMany(findManyArgs) method that applied authorization and filter conditions while querying bookingTimeStatusDenormalized. This PR deletes it and only leaves getBaseConditions(); callers must now write $queryRaw manually. No production call site is updated in this diff, so any existing consumer of service.findMany will break at compile time or lose intended filtering. If the API change is intentional, callers must be migrated in the same change or the method retained.

title: Constructor accepts weaker options type with optional teamId
body: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions declares teamId?: number independent of scope, and the constructor now accepts this type instead of the discriminated-union InsightsBookingServiceOptions. A caller can pass { scope: 'team', userId, orgId } and it now compiles; at runtime safeParse rejects it and the service silently returns the 1=0 condition, producing no rows with no error. This removes compile-time validation of required fields and can hide misconfigured call sites. The constructor should accept the discriminated union or a public type whose 'team' branch requires teamId.

title: Caching behavior tests removed while caching code remains
body: The diff deletes the Caching test block that verified getAuthorizationConditions and getFilterConditions are memoized on the service instance. The service still implements caching via cachedAuthConditions and cachedFilterConditions, including the null-vs-undefined handling for filters, but the new test file has no coverage for it. A regression that caches conditions for the wrong options/filters or mishandles a cached null filter result would go unnoticed. Restore equivalent caching tests adapted to Prisma.Sql return values.

title: Removal of public findMany method breaks existing callers
body: The public `findMany` method has been removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions`. Any code that previously called `service.findMany(...)` will now fail to compile or break at runtime. This is an API contract break that will affect any consumers of this service (e.g., API route handlers) that were not updated in this PR. The maintainer should either retain the method or update all callers before merging.

title: Constructor accepts looser public options type leading to silent validation failures
body: The constructor parameter type changed from `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (the strict z.infer type) to `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, which makes `teamId` optional for all scopes. The service then runs `safeParse` and sets `this.options = null` on validation failure. A caller providing `{ scope: 'team', userId, orgId }` without `teamId` will now pass the TypeScript type check but fail validation at runtime, causing the service to silently return `NOTHING_CONDITION` for every query. This is a type safety regression that can hide authorization errors and prevent access without any error message.

title: Integration test relies on unspecified ordering of database query results
body: The org scope test expects the `Prisma.sql` condition to contain the array `[testData.org.id, testData.team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` in that exact order. However, the service builds `teamIds` from `teamRepo.findAllByParentId()` which does not specify an `orderBy`, and the test data is created without any guaranteed ordering. The database may return teams in any order, making the test flaky. The same issue applies to the array of user IDs, which comes from `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds()` without an explicit order. The tests should either sort the expected arrays or the service should sort the results before building the SQL.

title: Integration test may fail due to asynchronous denormalized table updates
body: The `getBaseConditions` test now uses `prisma.$queryRaw` to query the `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` table immediately after creating bookings. If this table is populated asynchronously (e.g., by a background job or materialized view refresh), the newly created `userBooking` may not be present when the query runs, causing the test to fail. The PR description itself notes that the test runner could not be executed, leaving this risk unverified. A more robust test would wait for the denormalized table to be updated or mock the underlying data source.

title: Caching tests were removed, leaving caching behavior untested
body: The PR removes the entire `Caching` describe block that verified authorization and filter conditions are cached. The service still implements caching via `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, so this behavior is no longer covered by tests. If the caching logic is faulty (e.g., stale data or incorrect invalidation), it could go undetected. A low-effort fix is to reintroduce tests that assert the same object is returned on repeated calls.

title: Cache deletion does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
body: `deleteCacheMutation` only calls `onSuccess?.()` and shows a toast on success. Unlike the disconnect mutation below it, it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. The parent query in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` uses `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, and `onChanged` is optional, so after a successful cache deletion the dropdown can continue showing the old `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamp and "Delete cached data" action until some unrelated refetch happens. Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in the mutation's success/settled path.

title: Cache status query includes expired CalendarCache rows
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows for a credential without filtering `expiresAt >= now`, while `getCachedAvailability` only treats non-expired rows as valid cache. If expired rows remain in the table, the UI will still show a cache status and timestamp for a credential whose cache is no longer usable. The query should filter to active rows, e.g. `where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds }, expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } }`, unless showing historical rows is intentional.

title: Cache timestamp is always formatted in en-US
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` is hardcoded even though the component obtains the user's locale via `useLocale()`. Users on non-English locales will see the cache timestamp formatted with US date/time conventions instead of their locale. Use the current locale or a shared date formatting utility.

title: No test covers the cache deletion ownership check
body: The new `deleteCache` endpoint enforces access by requiring the credential to belong to `user.id`, then deletes all `CalendarCache` rows for that credential. There are no added tests covering the key negative case: a user trying to delete cache for another user's credential should get an error and no rows should be deleted. This is the main security boundary of the new endpoint and should be covered by a unit or integration test.

title: Existing cache rows get migration time as their last-updated timestamp
body: The migration adds `updatedAt` with `DEFAULT NOW()`, so all pre-existing `CalendarCache` rows are backfilled with the migration/deploy time rather than the time the cache was actually written. Since `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` surfaces `max(updatedAt)` as the UI's "Last updated" value, users with existing cache entries will initially see a misleadingly recent timestamp. Consider backfilling from another source such as `expiresAt` minus the caching period, or otherwise noting the limitation.

title: TypeScript cannot narrow cacheUpdatedAt through hasCache
body: The prop `cacheUpdatedAt` is typed as `Date | null | undefined`. The variable `hasCache` is computed as `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`, but testing `hasCache` in JSX does not narrow the original `cacheUpdatedAt`. Therefore `new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)` still receives `Date | null | undefined`, which is a type error under strict null checks and will fail the build. Use a direct `cacheUpdatedAt && (...)` check or assign the narrowed value to a separate variable before formatting.

title: Deleting cache does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
body: `deleteCacheMutation` only calls `onSuccess?.()` when deletion succeeds, unlike `disconnectMutation`, which invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`. Since the connected calendars query is not invalidated after a successful cache deletion, the UI can keep showing the old `cacheUpdatedAt` and continue offering the delete-cache action until some other refetch happens. Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in the delete mutation's success or settled handler.

title: Cache status includes expired cache entries
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows by `credentialId` and returns the max `updatedAt` without filtering on `expiresAt`. However `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows where `expiresAt >= now`. As a result, a credential can be shown as having live cache data, with a delete-cache action, even when all of its cache entries are expired and not actually used. Add a filter such as `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the groupBy query.

title: Authorization failure is thrown as a generic 500 error
body: When the credential is missing or does not belong to the current user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. An untyped `Error` from a tRPC procedure is treated as an internal server error, so clients receive a 500 for an authorization failure instead of a 401/403 or 404. Throw `TRPCError` with `UNAUTHORIZED` or `NOT_FOUND` so the API contract is correct and these expected failures are not logged as server crashes.

title: Hardcoded en-US date formatting ignores user locale
body: The component calls `useLocale()` for translated labels but formats the cache timestamp with a hardcoded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`. Non-English users will see US date and time conventions regardless of their locale preference. Use the locale obtained from `useLocale`/i18n when constructing the `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.

title: macOS-only sed syntax fails on Linux
body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E ...`, which is BSD/macOS syntax. GNU sed, the default on Linux, treats the empty string as a file argument and fails with an error such as "can't read '': No such file or directory", so the script cannot update `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` on Linux. Use a portable approach such as GNU `sed -i -E` or a temp-file/`perl -pi` replacement.

title: Deleting cache does not invalidate connected calendars query
body: The deleteCacheMutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls onSuccess. Unlike the disconnectMutation above it, it never invalidates utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. After a successful cache deletion the list item will keep showing the old cacheUpdatedAt until the query is refetched by some other action or remount, so the UI displays stale cache status immediately after the user deletes cached data.

title: Delete cache fails for delegated calendar credentials shown in the UI
body: The handler authorizes the request by requiring a Credential with id equal to credentialId and userId equal to the current user id. However, CredentialActionsDropdown renders the delete-cache action whenever the integration is Google Calendar and cacheUpdatedAt exists, without considering delegationCredentialId. The previous UI explicitly commented that delegation credentials cannot be disconnected by the current user, which indicates those credentials are not owned by them. For such delegated Google Calendar connections the delete action will therefore be shown but the mutation will fail with 'Credential not found or access denied'. Either hide delete for delegated credentials or add an authorization path that allows deleting the corresponding calendar cache.

title: Cache status includes expired CalendarCache rows
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds filters only by credentialId and takes the max updatedAt, but does not filter by expiresAt. getCachedAvailability only serves rows where expiresAt is at least now, so a credential with only expired cache rows will still show a 'Last updated' timestamp and a delete-cache action in the UI even though the cache is no longer used. This gives users a misleading cache status. Filter expired rows here, or otherwise treat the displayed status as valid cached data only.

title: Timestamp is formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
body: The cache timestamp uses new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) regardless of the user's configured locale. Since the rest of the component uses useLocale() for translations, non-English users will see English/US date formatting. Use the active locale from useLocale or omit the explicit locale so Intl uses the user's default.

title: Cancelled reminders are deleted before SendGrid cancellation
body: The first `deleteMany` removes all EMAIL reminders with `scheduledDate <= now`, including those marked `cancelled: true`. The subsequent cancellation query (lines 43-51) looks for reminders with `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. If a cancelled reminder's scheduledDate has already passed (e.g., it was cancelled just before its send time), it is deleted from the database by the first `deleteMany`, so the SendGrid cancellation request is never sent, and the email is still delivered. This defeats the purpose of the PR for reminders that are cancelled after their scheduled time but before SendGrid actually sends. The first `deleteMany` should exclude `cancelled: true`, or the cancellation step should run before any deletion.

title: immediateDelete sends cancellation but leaves stale DB row
body: When `immediateDelete` is true, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` sends the SendGrid cancellation and then `return`s without deleting the `workflowReminder` row or setting the `cancelled` flag. This leaves a row with `scheduled: true` and `referenceId` still pointing to a cancelled batch. In rescheduling (handleNewBooking.ts), this row persists associated with the cancelled booking, potentially for days until its `scheduledDate` passes. It may also be processed again later by `handleCancelBooking` if the same booking is cancelled again, causing duplicate cancellation attempts. The function should either delete the DB row or set `cancelled: true` after successful SendGrid cancellation.

title: Async reminder cancellation calls are not awaited
body: Within the `forEach` over `updatedBookings`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called but their promises are not awaited or collected. These functions perform external API calls (SendGrid, Twilio) and DB updates. The handler proceeds to `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` and then returns, so the API may signal successful cancellation before the reminder cancellations have actually completed. If the process crashes or the client assumes cancellation is fully done, reminders may still be sent. The async calls should be collected and awaited (e.g., using `Promise.all`).

title: Async reminder cancellation in reschedule is not awaited
body: In the reschedule path, the loop over `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders` calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` without awaiting them (the `forEach` callback is not async and no promises are collected). This means the new booking's workflow reminders may be scheduled before the old reminders have been fully cancelled at SendGrid/Twilio, and the function could return before cancellation completes. The calls should be awaited or their promises aggregated.

title: Cancellation loop aborts on first SendGrid error
body: The entire cancellation process is wrapped in a single try/catch. Inside the `for` loop, if `client.request` throws for one reminder, the catch block logs the error and exits, skipping all remaining reminders and also preventing the queued `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` operations from running (since the promises are not awaited before the exception). This can leave many cancelled reminders uncancelled at SendGrid and in the database. Errors should be handled per reminder, or the loop should continue after logging.

title: Immediate email cancellation has no retry or DB state change
body: In the immediateDelete branch, the function posts a SendGrid cancellation but returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder or setting cancelled. If that request fails, the catch only logs and leaves the row unchanged. On reschedule (handleNewBooking.ts:968) this leaves the old reminder with cancelled null, so scheduleEmailReminders will never retry it and the old SendGrid email can still be delivered. On workflow/step deletion (workflows.tsx:214, 521) the related row may then be cascade-deleted, making retry impossible even though the SendGrid cancellation failed. Mark the row cancelled before the API call or delete it only after a successful cancel, and provide a retry path on failure.

title: A single SendGrid cancellation failure prevents deleting already-cancelled reminder rows
body: The loop awaits one SendGrid cancel request at a time and only awaits the collected prisma.workflowReminder.delete promises after the loop. If any client.request throws, control jumps to catch, so the DB deletes for previous successfully cancelled reminders never execute. Those rows remain cancelled: true and will be retried on the next cron run, causing duplicate SendGrid cancellation requests for the same batch IDs and potentially keeping stale rows longer. Move each row delete immediately after its successful SendGrid call or use Promise.allSettled/individual try-catch so one failure doesn't block cleanup of other reminders.

title: No tests cover deferred/immediate cancellation behavior
body: This PR changes the cancellation flow to a deferred cron-based cancel for normal cancellations and an immediate branch for reschedule/deletion, but no tests were added for how rows are updated/deleted when referenceId is null, when immediateDelete succeeds or fails, or how scheduleEmailReminders picks up cancelled rows. Given this fixes a production notification bug, regression tests for these paths would prevent the same failure mode.

title: Non-immediate email cancellation waits for cron and can miss the send window
body: When called without `immediateDelete`, this function only sets `cancelled: true` in the database and returns; it never calls SendGrid to cancel the scheduled send. Callers like `handleCancelBooking` and `requestReschedule` use this path for all email reminders. Because `scheduleEmailReminders` runs only every 15 minutes, a reminder whose `scheduledDate` is before the next cron run will already have been sent by SendGrid before the cron attempts cancellation. Cancelling a booking close to a reminder time can therefore still deliver the reminder. For reminders within the near-term window, SendGrid should be cancelled immediately or the cancellation must be event-driven.

title: Workflow reminder cancellations are not awaited
body: `updatedBookings.forEach` starts `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` but does not `await` them or collect their promises. This API handler returns right after `sendCancelledEmails`, so the process can end before the async Prisma update/delete or provider cancellation completes. An email reminder may never be set to `cancelled: true`, so the cron in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` never cancels it and the reminder can still be sent after cancellation. Use `await Promise.all(...)` over all reminder cancellations before returning.

title: Request-reschedule reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget
body: The `requestReschedule` mutation calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` inside `forEach` without awaiting their promises. In a serverless/TRPC context the mutation can resolve before the DB rows are marked or deleted and before Twilio/SendGrid operations finish, so reminders for the cancelled original booking can survive and still send. Collect and await these promises before the mutation returns.

title: Disabling event types does not await reminder cancellation
body: `remindersToDelete.flat().forEach(...)` invokes cancellation functions without awaiting their promises. Disabling an event type from a workflow can return to the client before the email reminder row is updated to `cancelled: true` or the SMS reminder is deleted. If the runtime shuts down after the response, the cancellation is lost and reminders for disabled workflows can still send. The same fire-and-forget pattern appears below when deleting/editing steps; all cancellation promises should be awaited before returning.

title: Old reminders are cancelled before rescheduling succeeds
body: This block sends cancellation for `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders` before `eventManager.reschedule` runs. If the reschedule fails, for example due to a calendar or video integration error, the original booking remains active but its workflow reminders have already been cancelled. A live booking would then stop receiving reminders. Move this cancellation to after a successful reschedule, or compensate on failure if it must occur before.

title: One SendGrid cancellation failure aborts all remaining cancellations in the cron run
body: The entire `for` loop is inside one `try`/`catch`. If `client.request` throws for one reminder, execution jumps to the catch, skipping every remaining `remindersToCancel` entry and never awaiting the already-created Prisma delete promises. A single persistently bad `referenceId` or transient SendGrid error can block all other due cancellations in that run. Handle each reminder's SendGrid cancellation and delete independently (or continue on error) so one failure cannot prevent the rest.

title: Immediate email cancellation leaves stale scheduled reminders in the database
body: With `immediateDelete` true and a `referenceId`, this function sends the SendGrid cancel and returns without deleting or marking the `WorkflowReminder`. The reschedule path in `handleNewBooking` calls it this way and does not delete the row afterwards, leaving the old reminder as `scheduled: true` with `cancelled` null. Such rows accumulate and can be mistaken for active reminders later by workflow step edit/delete queries. Delete the row or set `cancelled: true` after successful SendGrid cancellation when the caller will not cascade a delete.

title: Dynamic imports are executed eagerly when the appStore module loads
body: The object literal uses `import("./applecalendar")` etc. as property values. Dynamic `import()` expressions are evaluated immediately, so every app chunk starts loading as soon as this index module is imported, even if no app is ever requested. This defeats lazy loading and can significantly increase startup/bundle loading cost. Use lazy accessor functions, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and update consumers to call and await them.

title: Unawaited async forEach leaves calendar deletions unperformed in recurring cancellation
body: In the recurring `allRemainingBookings` branch, `forEach(async (credential) => { ... const deletedEvent = await calendar?.deleteEvent(...); apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` discards the returned promises. Because `forEach` does not await async callbacks, `apiDeletes` is still empty when later `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs, so external calendar events for the remaining recurring bookings are not reliably cancelled/awaited. Replace with a real loop or `await Promise.all(credentials.map(async ...))` and collect the deletion promises.

title: Calendar/video deletion promises are fire-and-forget
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` ignores the async callbacks' returned promises. The function can send the reschedule email and return before the calendar/video deletions complete, and rejections from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` become unhandled. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a `for...of` loop with awaited calls.

title: Calendar/video deletion promises are fire-and-forget
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` ignores the async callbacks' returned promises. The function can send the reschedule email and return before the calendar/video deletions complete, and rejections from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` become unhandled. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a `for...of` loop with awaited calls.

title: Calendar/video deletion promises are fire-and-forget
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` ignores the async callbacks' returned promises. The request can continue and complete before the calendar/video deletions finish, and rejections from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` become unhandled. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a `for...of` loop with awaited calls.

title: Recurring calendar deletions are not awaited after async getCalendar
body: In the recurring cancellation branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` starts an async callback but the surrounding handler does not await it. `apiDeletes` may still be empty when `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs, so external calendar events for recurring bookings may never be deleted. Rejections from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` are also unhandled. Replace this with a `for...of` loop plus `await`, or collect promises and await them explicitly.

title: Reschedule does not await calendar/video deletion promises
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` awaits inside an async callback whose returned promise is ignored by `forEach`. The function continues to send the reschedule email without waiting for calendar or video deletions to complete, and errors from the dynamic import or deletion become unhandled promise rejections. Use `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop with `await`.

title: Reschedule does not await calendar/video deletion promises
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` awaits inside an async callback whose returned promise is ignored by `forEach`. The function continues to send the reschedule email without waiting for calendar or video deletions to complete, and errors from the dynamic import or deletion become unhandled promise rejections. Use `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop with `await`.

title: requestReschedule does not await external calendar/video deletion
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(credentialsMap.get(...)); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` starts an async callback that `forEach` ignores. The mutation proceeds to send the reschedule email before the old calendar/video events are actually deleted, and any rejection from `getCalendar` or the deletion is unhandled. Replace with `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop that awaits each operation.

title: Dynamic import expressions are evaluated eagerly at module load
body: The object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")`, `import("./caldavcalendar")`, etc. directly. These `import()` expressions start loading every listed app as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported, not when an entry is awaited. This does not give per-app lazy loading and can cause all app chunks to be fetched at startup. If lazy loading is intended, wrap each entry in a thunk such as `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")` or use a lazy proxy.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns promise-valued calendar fields
body: `getCalendar` is now async, but `getCalendarCredentials` remains synchronous and assigns `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` without awaiting it. The exported function's effective return type changes from objects containing `Calendar` instances to objects containing `Promise<Calendar | null>`. The in-file consumer was updated to await `item.calendar`, but any other callers of this exported function that treat `calendar` as a `Calendar` will break. Consider making `getCalendarCredentials` async and awaiting each calendar, or explicitly documenting and updating all call sites.

title: forEach(async) does not await deletion operations
body: The change to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` does not cause the loop to wait for the async callbacks. The async operations (calendar event deletion or video meeting deletion) are fire-and-forget, and the surrounding function continues execution and returns `true` before these deletions complete. This can lead to a race condition where the reschedule email is sent and the function returns success while the external calendar/video events are still being deleted (or have failed). Use a `for...of` loop with `await` or collect promises and `await Promise.all`.

title: forEach(async) does not await deletion operations
body: Same issue as in vital/lib/reschedule.ts: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` does not await the async callbacks, so the calendar/video deletion operations are not awaited before the function returns `true`. This can cause incomplete cancellation and inconsistent state.

title: Recurring cancellation forEach is not awaited and pushes resolved values
body: In the recurring booking cancellation branch, the code uses `forEach(async (credential) => { ... const deletedEvent = await calendar?.deleteEvent(...); apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })`. The `forEach` does not wait for these async callbacks, and because `deletedEvent` is the resolved value (not a Promise), `apiDeletes` contains non-promise values that `Promise.all` later will not wait for. The function can proceed to send emails and return success before the external calendar events are actually deleted. Use a `for...of` loop and collect the promises returned by `calendar?.deleteEvent` without awaiting them inside the loop, or use `Promise.all` on an array of promises.

title: Ineffective await on array of promises in paid cancellation path
body: In the paid cancellation branch, the code executes `await apiDeletes;` where `apiDeletes` is an array containing Promises from `deleteMeeting` and `calendar?.deleteEvent`. `await` on an array does not await the individual promises; it simply yields the array. Therefore, the function does not wait for these asynchronous deletion operations to complete before marking the booking as REJECTED and returning. This can lead to inconsistent state (e.g., booking marked rejected while external calendar event still exists). Use `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)` instead.

title: forEach(async) does not await calendar/video deletion before sending email
body: The code at line 553 uses `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })`. Because the callback is async but the `forEach` does not await it, the deletion promises are not collected or awaited. The function immediately proceeds to send the reschedule email, potentially before the external calendar/video events have been cancelled. Use a `for...of` loop with `await` or collect the promises and `await Promise.all`.

title: getCalendarCredentials returns unresolved Promises for calendar
body: `getCalendarCredentials` is a synchronous function that calls the now-async `getCalendar(credential)` without awaiting it. As a result, each returned object's `calendar` property is a Promise, not a Calendar instance. While some consumers (e.g., `getConnectedCalendars`) correctly await this promise, other callers of `getCalendarCredentials` may not, leading to unawaited promises or runtime errors when trying to call calendar methods. The function should either become async and await `getCalendar`, or its return type should be explicitly documented and all consumers updated to await the calendar promise.

title: Double filtering of date overrides can incorrectly remove valid slots
body: getTimeSlots already accounts for date overrides and working hours when generating timeSlots.
