Then in availableTimeSlots.filter for fixed hosts, checkIfIsAvailable is called again with the raw dateOverrides and workingHours. This double-processing, combined with the flawed date override logic in checkIfIsAvailable, can cause valid slots to be rejected. For example, a fixed host with an override that is correctly handled by getTimeSlots may be marked unavailable by checkIfIsAvailable due to offset or comparison errors. This directly undermines the PR's goal of respecting fixed host overrides in round-robin events.

title: Working hours check uses slot start time for both start and end
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, the lines `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` and `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` use the same value for start and end. The end should likely be computed from slotEndTime. As written, the condition `end > workingHour.endTime` will never be true (unless slotStartTime itself is past the end), so slots that start within working hours but extend beyond the working window will not be filtered out. This check is redundant because buildSlots already ensures slots fit, but the incorrect computation may hide logical errors or cause unexpected behavior if working hours are ever used independently.

title: Date override logic fails when multiple overrides exist for the same date
body: The checkIfIsAvailable function uses a `find` on dateOverrides and returns false if the callback returns true for any override. If there are multiple overrides for the same date, the callback may return true for an override where the slot is outside, causing the entire slot to be considered unavailable, even if another override for the same date would have allowed it. This can lead to false negatives in availability for users with more than one override on a given day.

title: Date override conversion ignores day shift when offset crosses midnight
body: The calculation `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...` extracts only the hour and minute from the shifted UTC time, discarding the date component. If the timezone offset difference causes the shifted time to cross midnight (e.g., an override at 23:00 in one timezone appearing as 01:00 the next day in the invitee's timezone), the resulting slot will be placed at 1:00 AM on the same invitee day rather than the next day. This can cause overrides near day boundaries to produce incorrect availability.

title: No test for round-robin fixed host date override scenario
body: The PR's main goal is to ensure date overrides of fixed hosts are respected in round-robin events, but the only new test is for a single-user event. There is no test with a round-robin event containing a fixed host with an override and a non-fixed host available. This leaves the critical double-filtering path untested and could allow regressions in the exact scenario the PR is meant to fix.

title: Working hours check uses start time for both start and end
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the code computes `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` and then `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`, making `end` equal to `start`. The subsequent condition `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` only checks whether the slot start falls outside the working hour window; it fails to verify that the entire event duration (slotStart + eventLength) fits within the working hours. For a fixed host whose working hours end before the slot's end time, a slot starting within working hours but extending beyond them will incorrectly pass as available, leading to bookings outside the host's availability.

title: Working hours day-of-week check uses UTC day instead of organizer local day
body: The condition `workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())` uses `slotStartTime`, which is derived from `time.utc()` (line 100). The `days` array in the schedule's `WorkingHours` represents days of the week in the organizer's local timezone. For slots near midnight, the UTC day may differ from the organizer's local day, causing the check to reject or accept slots incorrectly. This is especially problematic for users in timezones far from UTC.

title: Date override date comparison is unreliable across timezone boundaries
body: The code computes `utcOffset = organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0` and then compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` with `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` where `slotStartTime` is UTC. This attempts to align dates but fails when the slot's UTC date differs from the organizer's local date. For example, a slot at 2023-01-01 23:30 UTC may have a local date of 2023-01-02 in the organizer's timezone, and the override date may be 2023-01-02, but the mismatch causes the override to be ignored, potentially showing unavailable slots.

title: Multiple date overrides on the same day can incorrectly mark slots unavailable
body: The `dateOverrides.find` callback returns `true` (meaning slot outside override) as soon as it finds a date override on the same day that does not contain the slot. If a user has multiple date overrides for the same day (e.g., two separate time ranges), the first override that does not include the slot will cause `checkIfIsAvailable` to return `false` early, even if a later override covers the slot. This results in valid slots being hidden.

title: Date override timezone conversion uses offset from fake 1970 date, not the override date
body: The computation `organizerUtcOffset = dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` and `inviteeUtcOffset = dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(timeZone).utcOffset()` uses `override.start`, which is a Date object representing a time-of-day encoded as 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. The UTC offset for a timezone on 1970-01-01 may differ from the offset on the actual override date (e.g., DST rules or historical changes). This leads to an incorrect offset difference and produces wrong slot times for date overrides in timezones with DST or where the offset has changed since 1970. The test only covers Asia/Kolkata and Asia/Dhaka, which do not have DST, so the bug is not caught.

title: Active override filtering compares UTC timestamp with invitee local day boundaries
body: The code uses `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, startOfInviteeDay.endOf("day"), null, "[)")` to determine if an override applies to the current invitee day. This compares the UTC instant of the override start with the boundaries of the invitee's local day. When the organizer's timezone differs significantly from the invitee's, an override whose date matches the invitee's day may have a UTC start outside the local day boundaries, causing the override to be ignored entirely. This pre-existing issue undermines the PR's timezone fix.

title: Incorrect organizer UTC offset calculation uses Date.toString()
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` first converts the Date to a string in the environment's local timezone, then interprets that string as if it were in `override.timeZone`. This changes the instant. For example, if the server runs in UTC, a Date representing 14:00 IST would be converted to an 08:30 UTC string, and then parsed as 08:30 IST, completely shifting the time. The correct approach is `dayjs(override.start).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. This bug causes date override windows to be placed at wrong times for all users when the server timezone differs from the organizer's timezone.

title: Date override start/end minutes are computed in UTC instead of invitee timezone
body: The code computes `startTime` and `endTime` as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...`. This keeps the time in UTC (after shifting by offset) and extracts hour/minute without converting to the invitee's timezone. The resulting minutes are relative to UTC midnight, not to the invitee's local midnight, which is what `buildSlots` expects. This produces incorrect slot times whenever the invitee timezone is not UTC. The correct implementation is to use `dayjs(override.start).tz(timeZone).hour()*60 + dayjs(override.start).tz(timeZone).minute()` (and similarly for end). This bug affects all events with date overrides and a non-UTC invitee timezone.

title: Date override logic marks partially overlapping slots as available
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the date override check only rejects slots that are entirely before the override start or entirely after the override end (by checking `slotEndTime.isBefore(start)` / `slotEndTime.isSame(start)` and `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)`). A slot that starts before the override start but ends inside the override window will not be rejected and will be considered available. Since a date override replaces normal working hours, any slot not fully contained in the override should be unavailable. This can lead to bookings being offered that begin before the host's available time.

title: Working hours check uses slot start for both start and end and ignores timezone
body: In the working-hours validation added to `checkIfIsAvailable`, `const start` and `const end` are both set to `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`. This means the check never accounts for the event length, and also uses the slot's UTC time directly without converting to the organizer's timezone. Working hours are defined in the organizer's local time. As a result, valid slots may be rejected or invalid slots allowed for any non-UTC timezone. The check should compare the slot's start and end times (in the organizer's timezone) against the working hour boundaries.

title: UTC offset for date override is computed incorrectly
body: `const utcOffset = organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0;` treats `date.start` (an absolute Date object) as if it were a local time string in `organizerTimeZone`. This computes the wrong offset and causes the subsequent day comparison (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")`) to potentially match the wrong day. The correct approach is to directly format `date.start` in the organizer's timezone using `dayjs(date.start).tz(organizerTimeZone).format("YYYY MM DD")` without any manual offset manipulation.

title: Missing test for round-robin fixed host date overrides
body: The PR description states it fixes date overrides for fixed hosts in round-robin events, but the only added test is for a personal event with a different attendee timezone. There is no test covering the round-robin scenario where a fixed host has a date override and a non-fixed host is available. Without such a test, the core bug fix is unverified and could regress silently.

title: Migration fails if embed_category is unset and does not normalize old hosts
body: The query to find category_id from embed_category assumes a matching row exists. If the setting is blank or no category name matches, the result set is empty and `[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError, causing the migration to fail on fresh installs or when embed_category was never configured. Additionally, old host values are inserted directly into the new table via raw SQL without trimming scheme/path. The new model's `before_validation` trims these, but raw insertion bypasses that, so hosts like 'http://example.com' will be stored with scheme and will never match `record_for_host`, breaking embedding for migrated sites.

title: Category and embeddable_host fabricator definitions are swapped
body: The file `category_fabricator.rb` now contains `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the new `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the original `Fabricator(:category)` definitions. This means tests requiring `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator` will load the wrong fabricator, and the `:category` fabricator will be missing, causing many tests to fail with 'No fabricator registered for :category'. The definitions need to be placed in the correct files.

title: Controller does not handle missing record or parameters, causing 500 errors
body: In `update`, if the host ID is not found, `host` is nil and `save_host(host)` will call `host.host = ...`, raising NoMethodError. Similarly, `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on nil. Additionally, `save_host` assumes `params[:embeddable_host]` and its subkeys `:host` and `:category_id` exist; if any are missing, it raises NoMethodError. These should be guarded with 404/422 responses.

title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
body: The callback uses `self.host.sub!(/^https?:///, '')`, which calls `sub!` on nil if `host` is nil. This can happen when creating an EmbeddableHost without a host (e.g., from a form missing the field) and will raise NoMethodError. The callback should guard against nil, for example by using `self.host = self.host.to_s.sub(/^https?:\/\//, '')` or checking presence first.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category has no matching category
body: The expression `execute("SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes at least one row is returned. If the `embed_category` site setting is blank or points to a non-existent category name (common default is empty), the query returns no rows, `[0]` is nil, and calling `['id']` raises NoMethodError. This aborts the migration and prevents deployment.

title: SQL injection in migration from site setting value
body: Old `embeddable_hosts` values are interpolated directly into a raw INSERT statement: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. If a stored host value contains a single quote or other SQL metacharacters, the migration can fail or potentially execute arbitrary SQL. Use parameterized inserts or ActiveRecord create! instead.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host
body: `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` is called in a `before_validation` callback. If `host` is nil (e.g., an admin request omits the host parameter), `sub!` raises NoMethodError instead of allowing validation to fail gracefully. The controller relies on model validation to report errors, so this will result in a 500 error rather than a validation error.

title: Missing 404 handling for update and destroy
body: Both `update` (line 10) and `destroy` (line 15) retrieve `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without checking for nil. If the id does not exist, `save_host(nil)` or `host.destroy` raises NoMethodError, causing a 500 error. The controller should respond with a 404 JSON error for missing records.

title: Missing index for embeddable host lookup causes full table scan
body: `record_for_host` performs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` on every embed request. There is no index on the `host` column, so PostgreSQL must scan the entire `embeddable_hosts` table for each comment embed or topic retrieval. This can become a significant performance bottleneck on high-traffic forums. Add an index on `lower(host)` or store hosts downcased with a normal index.

title: Plural _ids hydration can crash on null values
body: The new plural `_ids` handling calls `obj[k].map(...)` without checking that `obj[k]` is an array. If any REST payload contains a `*_ids` key set to null (rather than an array), this will throw `Cannot read property 'map' of null`, breaking model hydration. The previous code only matched singular `_id` and did not have this risk. Guard with `Array.isArray(obj[k])` or default to an empty array.

title: Pretender /fruits/:id always returns the first fruit
body: The route `/fruits/:id` always returns `fruits[0]`, regardless of the requested id. The test `store-test.js.es6` calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` and then asserts the presence of color_ids [1,2], but those belong to fruit id 1. The test would pass even if the store returned the wrong record by id. The route should return the fruit matching `request.params.id` to make the test meaningful.

title: Serializer produces embeddable_hosts as ids but client store expects embeddable_host_ids
body: The serializer uses `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids`, which outputs a key `embeddable_hosts` containing an array of ids. However, the client store's `_hydrateEmbedded` method looks for keys ending in `_ids` (e.g., `embeddable_host_ids`) to hydrate plural associations. As a result, the embedding model will not have its `embeddable_hosts` property set to a collection of models; instead it will contain a plain array of ids. The template `embedding.hbs` iterates over `embedding.embeddable_hosts` and passes each item to the `embeddable-host` component, which expects a model, leading to runtime errors and an empty/broken admin page. The `embed: :ids` option should be removed so that the default rest serializer includes `embeddable_host_ids`, or the client code must be updated to handle the plural association name.

title: Migration fails if embed_category setting is missing or has no matching category
body: The migration executes `SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'` and immediately calls `[0]['id']`. If the `embed_category` site setting does not exist or its value does not match any category name, the query returns no rows, and `[0]` is nil, causing a `NoMethodError` and aborting the migration. This would break upgrades for any forum that has not configured `embed_category` or has it set to a non-existent category. The code should check for the existence of a result before accessing `[0]`.

title: SQL injection and missing normalization when migrating host values
body: The migration uses raw string interpolation to insert host values: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ..."`. This is vulnerable to SQL injection if the old `embeddable_hosts` setting contained a quote. Additionally, the inserted hosts are not normalized (e.g., stripping `http://` or paths), unlike the model's `before_validation` which does so on save. As a result, migrated hosts will not match when `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against the URI host, breaking embed functionality until each record is manually edited and saved. Parameterized queries and application of the same normalization logic should be used.

title: Update action does not handle missing host record
body: In the `update` action, `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` may return nil if the id is invalid. The code then calls `save_host(host)`, which attempts `host.host = ...` on nil, raising a `NoMethodError` and returning a 500 error. The action should check for nil and return a 404 response with an appropriate error message.

title: Destroy action does not handle missing host record
body: Similar to update, `destroy` fetches `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without checking for nil. If the id does not exist, `host.destroy` raises a `NoMethodError`, causing a 500. The controller should return a 404 when the host is not found.

title: Category and embeddable_host fabricators appear swapped between files
body: The file `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` instead of category fabricators, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the original category fabricators. This is almost certainly an accidental swap during file creation. While it may still work because Fabrication loads all `.rb` files regardless of name, it is confusing and likely unintended. The category fabricators should be in their own file and the embeddable_host fabricator in its own.

title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
body: The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!` and `self.host.sub!` without checking if `host` is nil. If a host record is created or updated with a nil host (e.g., due to missing params), this will raise a `NoMethodError`. The controller always attempts to set `host.host` from `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, but if that param is absent, the value remains nil. The model should handle nil gracefully, either by skipping the callback or adding a presence validation.

title: Update action is a no-op and may mislead the frontend
body: The `update` action in `Admin::EmbeddingController` simply renders the same `@embedding` serialization without processing any incoming parameters. The frontend calls `embedding.update({})` which triggers a PUT to this endpoint, but no data is persisted. This could cause confusion or mask missing functionality. Either implement actual update logic or remove the route/action to avoid a misleading API.

title: Removal of embeddable_hosts check may expose expandable posts when no hosts configured
body: The `expandable_first_post?` method previously required `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` in addition to `embed_truncate?` and `has_topic_embed?`. With the removal of that check, if `embed_truncate` is true and a topic has an embed (perhaps from old data), the expandable feature will be enabled even when no embeddable hosts are configured in the new table. This could lead to unexpected UI behavior for forums that have embed_truncate enabled but no allowed hosts.

title: Client-side max file size hardcoded to 10MB ignores site settings
body: Both validateUploadedFile (line 182) and displayErrorForUpload (line 246) now use a hardcoded 10MB value instead of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. This means administrators' configured max_image_size_kb and max_attachment_size_kb are no longer enforced on the client. Users may be allowed to attempt uploads that the server will reject, or conversely be blocked from uploading images that the new server-side downsize feature would otherwise accept. The error message also shows 10MB regardless of the actual setting.

title: Animated GIFs are flattened during automatic downsizing
body: The call to OptimizedImage.downsize passes tempfile.path as the source. This path does not end in .GIF (it is a system tempfile with no extension), so the animated detection in OptimizedImage.optimize (`from =~ /\.GIF$/i`) never triggers. As a result, even when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, the non-animated downsize instructions are used, which read only the first frame (`#{from}[0]`) and produce a static image. Any animated GIF exceeding max_image_size_kb will be permanently converted to a still image, causing data loss.

title: In-place downsizing does not verify convergence and may leave stale file
body: The while loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%") without checking its return value or confirming that the file size actually decreased. If the conversion fails (e.g., ImageMagick error, unsupported format), the loop runs up to 5 times and then proceeds with a possibly corrupted or still-oversized file. Additionally, because the Tempfile object remains open while the file is overwritten at the same path, the open file descriptor may continue to reference the old inode, so Upload.create_for may read the original oversized file instead of the downsized version. The tempfile should be closed and reopened, or the output written to a separate path and atomically replaced.

title: URL download size limit ignores per-type settings
body: The change from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a fixed 10.megabytes applies to all URL-based uploads, including attachments (type != 'image'). While Upload.create_for may later reject non-images based on max_attachment_size_kb, this allows a download of up to 10MB regardless of configured limits and may consume excessive memory/disk before rejection. The previous behavior was also incorrect for attachments, but the new hardcoded value is not configurable and can be much higher than intended limits.

title: New downsize method overrides existing 4-argument signature, breaking callers
body: The addition of `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 completely overrides the earlier method at line 145 which accepted `max_width`, `max_height`. Any existing code or plugin that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height)` will now pass four positional arguments into a method expecting three, raising ArgumentError. The old method is dead code and the API has silently changed. If the intention was to support both string dimensions and width/height, a different approach (e.g., splat args or a single dimensions keyword) is needed.

title: No tests for automatic image downsizing
body: The new downsizing loop has no corresponding test coverage. Scenarios such as successful reduction, failure to reduce below the limit, animated GIF preservation, in-place overwrite consistency, and interaction with max_image_size_kb = 0 are all untested. Given the potential for data loss and file corruption, automated tests are essential before merging.

title: Redefining self.downsize overwrites the existing width/height API
body: The class defines self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) at line 145 and then immediately defines self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149. Ruby keeps only the second method. Existing callers using the old width/height form will now pass max_height as opts; optimize will then try to use opts[:allow_animation] or opts[:force_aspect_ratio] on an Integer/Fixnum (or use the wrong dimensions), causing downsizing to fail or behave incorrectly. Merge the two forms or update all callers.

title: In-place downsize can leave an open tempfile pointing to the original bytes
body: OptimizedImage.downsize runs an external command reading and writing tempfile.path while the Ruby tempfile object remains open. ImageMagick/gifsicle may replace the output by writing a temporary file and renaming over the destination; in that case the Ruby Tempfile file descriptor still refers to the old unlinked inode. The next tempfile.size call and Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, ...) may then read the original, not the downsized image, defeating the size limit and possibly storing stale content. Write downsize output to a separate Tempfile/path and reopen or pass that file to Upload.create_for.

title: Fixed five-attempt 80% loop does not guarantee the image is under max_image_size_kb
body: The loop reduces the image to 80% of its current size per iteration and only runs attempt=5 times. That leaves the size at best 0.8^5 == 32.77% of the original. An image initially larger than about 3.05 times the configured limit remains above SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes after the loop, but the code proceeds to Upload.create_for without checking downsize success or reporting the failure. Either iterate until the limit is met with a higher/calculated cap and check OptimizedImage.downsize's result, or reject with a clear error when the image cannot be reduced enough.

title: Hardcoded 10 MB URL download cap bypasses configured upload limits for non-images
body: The API URL download path now uses FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...) instead of the configured SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. The subsequent downsize block is only entered when FileHelper.is_image?(filename) is true, so non-image URL uploads can be downloaded at up to 10 MB even if the site's max_attachment_size_kb or max_image_size_kb is smaller. Keep the configured limit for non-images or validate the resulting upload against the site settings before creating it.

title: Client-side upload size validation ignores site settings
body: validateUploadedFile now sets maxSizeKB to a hardcoded 10 * 1024 instead of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. This allows users to select files up to 10 MB regardless of configured max_image_size_kb or max_attachment_size_kb, producing client behavior inconsistent with server policy and likely causing server-side 422/413 errors for normal attachments. The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hardcoded value; both should use the relevant site setting.

title: No tests cover the new automatic downsize behavior
body: This pull request adds a nontrivial server-side image mutation path but no controller/model tests. Cases that need coverage include an image over the limit being reduced below it, an image large enough that five 80% iterations are insufficient, an animated GIF when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, and OptimizedImage.downsize returning false (e.g. ImageMagick/gifsicle missing or unsupported). Without these tests the in-place/stale file and fixed-attempt bugs are likely to regress unnoticed.

title: Duplicate `downsize` method overrides the 4-argument API
body: There are two definitions of `OptimizedImage.downsize` in this file (lines 145 and 149). In Ruby the second definition completely replaces the first, so the 4-argument `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` API no longer exists. Any existing caller passing two numeric dimensions will now invoke the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` method: the third argument is treated as an ImageMagick geometry string and the fourth as an options hash, causing `TypeError` (`Numeric#[]`) or an invalid `-resize` command. The old method should be removed or renamed, and all callers updated.

title: Client-side upload size limit hard-coded to 10MB for all types
body: `maxSizeKB` is hard-coded to `10 * 1024` instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. This applies to both images and attachments. If the site has a lower `max_attachment_size_kb`, users can now upload attachments up to 10MB from the browser, and the server-side change in this PR does not downsize non-image attachments. This bypasses configured upload limits and may allow abuse or disk exhaustion.

title: API URL download limit hard-coded to 10MB for all file types
body: The API URL upload path now downloads up to `10.megabytes` for every file type, instead of respecting `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` or an attachment size limit. The new downsize loop only applies to images, so a non-image URL up to 10MB is passed to `Upload.create_for` even when the site's max attachment size is lower. This bypasses the configured server-side upload limit.

title: Downsize failure is ignored and oversized images may still be saved
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` when ImageMagick/gifsicle fails (see `convert_with`), but this loop ignores the return value and simply retries. After five failed attempts it proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with the still-oversized file. If image processing is unavailable or repeatedly fails, an oversized image is stored, defeating the site's `max_image_size_kb` limit.

title: 413 error message shows hard-coded 10MB limit
body: The 413 error path now displays a hard-coded 10 MB limit regardless of the site's actual `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb`, so the user may see an incorrect accepted size. Use the configured value or a generic message.

title: No tests added for automatic downsize behavior
body: No tests were added for the new automatic downsize behavior, particularly failure paths where `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false`, or for the duplicate `downsize` method in `OptimizedImage`. Without coverage, these regressions are likely to go unnoticed.

title: Emails without unsubscribe_url will raise MissingInterpolationArgument
body: The updated `unsubscribe_link` translation now requires an `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation. In `MessageBuilder#html_part` (line 67) and `MessageBuilder#body` (line 90), `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` is called whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true. If the caller did not provide `unsubscribe_url` in opts, `template_args` lacks that key and Rails raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`, causing the email to fail. Previously only `user_preferences_url` was required, which is always present. Existing mailers that set `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but do not pass `unsubscribe_url` will break. Provide a default or conditionally include the topic-specific line.

title: unsubscribe action crashes when user has no TopicUser record
body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` may return `nil` for users who have never visited the topic or have no explicit topic-user row (e.g., receiving notifications via category watching). The next line (107) calls `tu.notification_level`, raising `NoMethodError` on nil. The unsubscribe link is included in notification emails and may be clicked by such users. Use `TopicUser.get` or create/ensure a record before modifying.

title: Notification level change bypasses TopicUser.change and only downgrades one step
body: The action manually sets `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!`. This skips `TopicUser.change`, which sets `notifications_changed_at`, `notifications_reason_id`, publishes a MessageBus event, and handles creation. As a result, the UI will not reflect the change and tracking metadata is missing. Additionally, the logic sets to regular if current level is above regular, otherwise muted. A user watching/tracking a topic will only be downgraded to regular, still receiving notifications for replies and mentions, not fully unsubscribing as the page claims. Consider using `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted])` directly.

title: Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText
body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (extra 'i' in 'Notificiations'). It is referenced consistently in the template, so functionality is unaffected, but the spelling is incorrect and could cause confusion for future maintenance.

title: Markdown links in text email unsubscribe footer are not rendered
body: The `unsubscribe_link` translation now uses Markdown link syntax (`[text](%{unsubscribe_url})`). In the plain text email body generated by `MessageBuilder#body`, this string is inserted directly without Markdown processing, so recipients see raw Markdown like `[click here](https://...)` instead of a plain URL or formatted link. This degrades the text email experience. Consider using plain URLs for the text version or a separate text-specific translation.

title: No test for missing unsubscribe_url or new controller action
body: The spec was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url` but there is no test verifying that `MessageBuilder` handles the absence of `unsubscribe_url` gracefully (which it currently does not). Additionally, no tests were added for the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, including the nil TopicUser case and the notification level transition. These gaps leave the high-severity bugs in this PR undetected.

title: Global unsubscribe text now requires a per-topic unsubscribe_url from every caller
body: The global `unsubscribe_link` string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`. Any other `Email::MessageBuilder` caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` will render this locale string via `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` without `unsubscribe_url` and raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`, breaking those emails. Either supply `unsubscribe_url` everywhere, provide a default in `MessageBuilder`, or make the per-topic sentence conditional.

title: unsubscribe can 500 when no TopicUser record exists
body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil when the logged-in user has no topic_user row for that topic. The next line calls `tu.notification_level`, raising `NoMethodError` and returning a 500. The route is reachable by any logged-in user for a visible topic and can also be hit from email links in edge cases. Use `TopicUser.get` or `TopicUser.change`, which creates the missing row instead of assuming it exists.

title: Per-topic unsubscribe downgrades watching/tracking to regular instead of muting
body: For a user with tracking or watching level, `notification_level > regular`, so the action sets the level to `regular`. Regular still generates notifications and emails for replies, quotes, and mentions in that topic, so the email's promise to "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic" is not honored for those users. If the intent is to stop all topic notifications, set `muted`; otherwise the email copy and route behavior are contradictory.

title: New per-topic unsubscribe URL is not asserted
body: The test now passes `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"`, but the assertion still only checks that the old `user_preferences_url` appears in the body. There is no test that the rendered text/HTML contains the per-topic unsubscribe URL, nor coverage for the now-required interpolation argument when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true. This allows the new contract introduced by the locale change to regress without failing specs.

title: Unsubscribe template path does not match topicUnsubscribe route name
body: This template is stored at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which Ember resolves for a nested topic.unsubscribe route. However app-route-map.js.es6 registers the route as top-level topicUnsubscribe, so Ember will look for templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs. As a result the unsubscribe route will render without its intended template (empty or missing template), so the new unsubscribe page is broken.

title: unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists
body: TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) may return nil for users who received a notification (for example a mention, reply, or quote) without ever having a topic_users row. The next lines dereference tu.notification_level, causing NoMethodError. Use TopicUser.change(...) or find_or_initialize_by and handle the missing record, otherwise the unsubscribe page 500s for valid users.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url for all add_unsubscribe_link emails
body: The shared unsubscribe_link text now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}. Email::MessageBuilder calls I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) for every message that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true, but only UserNotifications#send_notification_email has been updated in this diff to pass unsubscribe_url. Any other email using add_unsubscribe_link will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument or render a broken link. Either provide a default for unsubscribe_url, make the topic-specific sentence conditional, or update every caller.

title: Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET without CSRF or unique token
body: The new /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe routes are GET and directly change the user's notification_level. GET requests are not CSRF-protected and are treated as safe by clients, so a logged-in user can be unsubscribed by an embedded image, link prefetch, or email scanner following the URL. State changes should be POST/PUT with CSRF protection, or the link should include an unguessable per-user token.

title: Unsubscribe renders stale serialized topic notification state
body: @topic_view is constructed at line 99 before tu.notification_level is changed. perform_show_response then serializes that original @topic_view, so the preloaded JSON/HTML response contains the old notification level. The client's topic-notifications-button can show the pre-unsubscribe state, and another GET may be required to see the change. Rebuild @topic_view or update its topic-user data after saving.

title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
body: Changing notification_level directly and calling save! does not set notifications_reason_id or notifications_changed_at, and does not publish the /topic/:id MessageBus update that TopicUser.change performs. Other live clients won't see the state change, and notification-change history/reasoning can become inconsistent. Use TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...) instead.

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and bypassable
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? queries BlockedEmail.where(email: email) without normalizing the address via Email.downcase/strip, and User creation passes params[:email] directly to User.new_from_params with no email normalization. An attacker can register using a case variant such as Bad@spamclub.com for a blocked bad@spamclub.com, or with surrounding whitespace, and the blocklist is bypassed. The unique validation/index is also case-sensitive, so multiple case variants can coexist. The previous domain restriction check used a case-insensitive regex, indicating normalization/case-insensitivity was expected here.

title: match_count is non-atomic and increments multiple times per signup
body: should_block? performs a read-modify-write on record.match_count and then saves the record. In UsersController#create, user.valid? is called before user.save (lines 168 and 172), and for a new record email_changed? remains true, so the email validator runs twice for a single blocked signup and increments match_count twice. Concurrent signup attempts can also lose increments because the update is not atomic. This corrupts match_count/last_match_at statistics and causes unnecessary DB writes. Use an atomic DB update or move the side effect out of validation.

title: Blocked email matching is case-sensitive, allowing bypass
body: Emails are case-insensitive. The lookup `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` does an exact, case-sensitive comparison. An attacker can bypass a block by using a different case (e.g., if 'bad@spam.com' is blocked, submitting 'Bad@Spam.com' will not match). The uniqueness validation on line 5 is also case-sensitive, allowing duplicate entries with different cases. Normalize emails to lowercase both when storing and when querying.

title: should_block? increments match_count non-atomically and writes on every validation
body: The method loads the record, increments `match_count` in memory, and saves the whole record. Concurrent requests for the same email can race, causing lost increments (both read the same value and write the same incremented value). Additionally, every call to `should_block?` for a matching email performs a database write, which an attacker can trigger repeatedly to amplify write load and potentially cause contention. Use an atomic `update_counters` or `update_all` to increment the counter and avoid saving the whole record.

title: Missing tests for email domain whitelist/blacklist logic
body: The domain restriction logic (whitelist/blacklist) was moved from User#email_validator to EmailValidator, but the new spec only tests the blocked email branch. There are no tests covering the whitelist/blacklist behavior, so regressions in that existing functionality could go unnoticed.

title: Non-atomic match_count increment and DB write inside validator
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and saves the record on every call. This method is invoked from EmailValidator during User validation, which can run multiple times per signup (e.g., user.valid? before save, then again during save). Each validation attempt will increment match_count multiple times, leading to inaccurate statistics. Concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email will also suffer from lost updates because the increment is not atomic (no lock or update_all). This causes race conditions and corrupts match_count data. The method should either be split into a pure predicate and a separate tracking method, or use atomic increments (e.g., increment!(:match_count, touch: :last_match_at) with a transaction).

title: Validation triggers unnecessary database writes for do_nothing action
body: EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block? during validation. Even when the blocked email's action_type is :do_nothing (meaning the email should not be blocked), should_block? still executes a database update (incrementing match_count and saving). This causes writes on every signup attempt for emails that are merely being tracked, which can degrade performance under load and violates the principle that validators should be side-effect-free. The validator should only query for the record's action_type without updating it, or the tracking update should be moved to a separate explicit call after validation.

title: No tests for domain whitelist/blacklist logic in EmailValidator
body: The new EmailValidator replaces the previous email_validator method in User, which handled email domain whitelist and blacklist restrictions. The spec file only tests blocked email behavior, leaving the whitelist/blacklist logic untested. If a regression were introduced in that logic, no test would catch it. Tests should be added to verify that whitelist and blacklist settings correctly add or don't add errors to the email attribute.

title: Invalid ERB syntax renders the embed/best template unusable
body: The tag `<%- end if %>` is not valid Ruby/ERB. ERB compiles the tag body as `end if`, which is a Ruby syntax error. Rendering `EmbedController#best` for an existing topic will raise a SyntaxError or ActionView::Template::Error instead of returning the comments, breaking the embed feature. The tag should be `<%- end %>`.

title: Unsanitized embed_url in imported HTML footer allows stored XSS
body: `embed_url` is interpolated directly into an HTML string using `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")`, with no HTML escaping. `url` is ultimately user-influenced (passed from `EmbedController#best` through the retrieve job, with only a prefix check for http/https) and is later stored and rendered with `cook_method` raw_html and `raw post.cooked` in the embed view. A URL such as `http://eviltrout.com/'>` becomes executable HTML in the post, giving stored XSS for anyone viewing the embedded topic. Escape `url` (e.g. with `ERB::Util.html_escape`) before building the footer.

title: Unescaped referer is injected into JavaScript targetOrigin
body: `request.referer` is interpolated directly into a JavaScript string inside a `<script>` block without `j`/`escape_javascript`/HTML escaping. Although `ensure_embeddable` validates only the referer's host, the rest of the URL can contain quotes or `</script>`. A referer such as `http://eviltrout.com/foo'></script><script>alert(document.cookie)</script>` would break out of the script and execute in the Discourse embed page. Escape the referer or derive the target origin from configuration rather than embedding the raw header.

title: PollFeed assumes every RSS item has a content field
body: `i.content.scrub` calls `String#scrub` on `i.content` unconditionally. RSS/Atom feeds commonly store the body in `description`/`summary` (or omit it for titles-only items); when `content` is nil, this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass`, aborting the entire poll before later items are processed. Use `(i.content || i.description || '')` (or equivalent per feed format) and guard nil.

title: Missing null check for embed container element
body:
`document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` may return `null` if the embedding page omits the expected `
`. The code then calls `comments.appendChild(iframe)` on line 12, throwing a TypeError and preventing the resize message listener from being registered. Guard with `if (comments)` or explicitly document the required element.

title: Raw HTML imported from feeds is rendered without sanitization (stored XSS)
body: TopicEmbed.import creates the post with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] using the caller-supplied contents as raw. PollFeed passes i.content from the RSS feed directly after only unescaping/scrubbing, with no sanitizer. Because Post#cook returns raw for raw_html, embed/best.html.erb then outputs post.cooked with `raw`. Script tags in a feed item are therefore stored and executed in the Discourse-origin embed iframe. This is a stored XSS vector for any untrusted or compromised feed.

title: Invalid ERB tag `<%- end if %>` prevents the template from compiling
body: The first if/else block is closed with `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. ERB treats everything inside the tag as Ruby code, and `end if` is a syntax error. Whenever this template is rendered, ERB compilation raises SyntaxError, so the embedded discussion view is unusable.

title: PollFeed assumes rss.items is always present
body: `rss.items.each` is called without checking whether `rss.items` is nil. SimpleRSS.parse can return nil or an object with nil `items` for empty/malformed feeds, causing NoMethodError and aborting the entire scheduled poll. The job should guard `rss.items.present?` before iteration.

title: Missing `content` field crashes the feed poll
body: `i.content.scrub` is called without checking that `i.content` is present. RSS/Atom items frequently provide only `description` or `summary`, in which case `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError and the entire poll job fails. Use `(i.content || i.description || i.summary).to_s.scrub` or otherwise handle missing content.

title: request.referer is interpolated into JavaScript without escaping
body: The postMessage target origin uses `'<%= request.referer %>'` directly inside a JavaScript string. The Referer header is browser-supplied and the embedding page URL is not necessarily trusted to be JS-safe; a URL path containing a single quote can break out of the string and execute script in the Discourse-origin iframe. Escape it for JavaScript (or otherwise encode it) before inclusion.

title: Race condition can cause duplicate TopicEmbed insert and job failure
body: TopicEmbed.import checks `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` outside the transaction and later relies on a unique index when creating the row. Two concurrent RetrieveTopic/PollFeed jobs for the same missing URL can both see no embed and both attempt the insert; the second will raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique instead of reusing the existing record. Add a unique-index rescue or an atomic insert/check to handle concurrent imports gracefully.

title: Invalid ERB syntax '<%- end if %>' causes template compile error
body: Line 6 contains '<%- end if %>', which is not valid ERB. The 'if' after 'end' is a syntax error; the conditional should be closed with '<%- end %>'. This will cause the view to fail to compile and result in a 500 error whenever the embed/best template is rendered.

title: Unescaped referer in inline JavaScript allows XSS in Discourse origin
body: The line `parent.postMessage({type: 'discourse-resize', height: document['body'].offsetHeight}, '<%= request.referer %>');` inserts the raw request referer directly into a JavaScript string without escaping. An attacker who controls the embedding page's URL (which is allowed by the embeddable_host check) can include a single quote and arbitrary JavaScript payload that will execute in the context of the Discourse-origin iframe. This is a stored/reflected XSS vulnerability. The referer must be escaped using a JavaScript-safe method such as `j(request.referer)` or `escape_javascript`.

title: RSS/Atom feed content imported as raw HTML without sanitization
body: The `poll_feed` method extracts `i.content` from the feed and passes it directly to `TopicEmbed.import`, which stores the post with `cook_method = Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Since raw HTML posts bypass all rendering and sanitization pipelines, any `<script>` or other malicious markup in the feed will be stored and served to users viewing the topic, leading to stored XSS. The feed content must be sanitized (e.g., with Sanitize or by using the regular markdown cooking path) before import.

title: Substring check for message origin allows attacker-controlled origins
body: The condition `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` tests whether the message origin contains the discourseUrl as a substring, rather than exact origin equality. An attacker could host a page on an origin such as `https://discourse.example.com.attacker.com` (which contains the legitimate origin as a substring) and send a postMessage to the embedding page. The check would incorrectly accept the message, allowing the attacker to trigger the resize handler and manipulate the iframe height, bypassing the intended origin restriction. The check should compare `e.origin` to the exact origin of `discourseUrl` using `new URL(discourseUrl).origin`.

title: Race condition in TopicEmbed.import can cause unique constraint violation
body: The `import` method first checks if a TopicEmbed exists for the URL, then creates a new one inside a transaction. If two processes invoke `import` simultaneously for the same URL, both may see no existing record, both create a new topic and post, and then both attempt to create a TopicEmbed with the same `embed_url`. The second `TopicEmbed.create!` will raise an ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique exception due to the unique index on embed_url, causing the entire transaction (including the newly created topic and post) to be rolled back. The job will fail and the URL will remain unimported. A safer approach is to handle the unique violation gracefully (e.g., rescue and re-fetch) or use a database-level upsert/lock.

title: Unbounded open() in import_remote can hang or consume excessive resources
body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `open(url).read` without any timeout or size limit. A slow or unresponsive server could cause the job to hang indefinitely, tying up a worker, or a huge page could consume excessive memory. Consider using a library with timeouts and response size limits, or setting timeouts via open-uri options.

title: Flexbox makes `.small-action` button lose right alignment
body: `.small-action` is now a flex container via `@include flexbox()`, so `float: right` on its direct child `button` is ignored. The button will be laid out immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of being pushed to the right edge of the small-action row. Add `margin-left: auto` to the button, use `justify-content: space-between`, or otherwise reorder the flex items to preserve the previous placement.

title: `align-items` mixin omits `-moz-box-align` for the `-moz-box` fallback
body: The new `flexbox()` mixin emits `display: -moz-box`, but `align-items()` does not emit `-moz-box-align`. In Firefox versions that honor the `-moz-box` fallback, the cross-axis alignment will remain the initial `box-align` value (`stretch`) rather than `center` or `baseline`, so header and badge layout will be wrong on that fallback path. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment;` to the mixin or remove the `-moz-box` display fallback.

title: Flex container makes the small-action button float ineffective, changing right alignment
body: `.small-action` is now a flex container, so its children no longer honor `float`. The existing `button { float: right; }` in this selector therefore no longer moves the button to the right edge; it will be laid out as the next flex item after `.small-action-desc`. No `margin-left: auto` or equivalent flex alignment was added, so the action button shifts left and the existing right-aligned layout regresses. Add `margin-left: auto` (or another flex ordering/alignment rule) to the button.

title: Order on .extra-info-wrapper has no effect because it is not a flex item
body: `order` only applies to direct flex items. The flexbox conversion in this PR targets `.d-header .contents` (`header.scss`), whose direct items are the title/panel elements; `.extra-info-wrapper` is nested inside the title, so this `order(2)` is inert and will not change header ordering. If this was meant to reorder the extra info, put the order on the actual direct flex item or make its parent a flex container.

title: Button loses right alignment after .small-action becomes flex
body: `.small-action` is now a flex container via `@include flexbox()`, so its direct `button` child is a flex item and the `float: right` declaration is ignored. With default `justify-content: flex-start` and no `margin-left: auto` on the button, the button is laid out immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of on the right. Add `margin-left: auto` (or otherwise justify the item) to preserve the previous right alignment.

title: align-items mixin missing -moz-box-align for legacy Firefox
body: The `flexbox()` mixin emits `display: -moz-box`, so old Firefox builds that use it expect alignment through `-moz-box-align`, but `align-items()` only emits `-webkit-box-align`, `-ms-flex-align`, and the modern properties. In those browsers this change silently fails to center/baseline-align flex items. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment` alongside `-webkit-box-align`.

title: website_name leaks TL0 website information to anonymous visitors
body: `website_name` is added to the serializer attributes, but it is not added to `untrusted_attributes` alongside `website` (line 109). The old client derived the displayed name from `model.website`, which was hidden for anonymous visitors viewing TL0 profiles via `include_website?`. Now the server will emit `website_name` even when `website` itself is suppressed, exposing the website host and path to anonymous visitors for users whose website should be restricted. Add `:website_name` to the untrusted attributes list and ensure its include callback honors `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing question mark
body: The serializer conditional-include hook is defined as `def include_website_name` instead of `def include_website_name?`. ActiveModel serializers look for the `include_<attribute>?` form, so this method will not be called. As a result, `website_name` is always emitted as an attribute, including as `nil` for users without a website or with an invalid website URL, rather than being omitted when the condition is false. Rename the method to `def include_website_name?`.

title: Naive label-count domain comparison treats unrelated subdomains as the same domain
body: The `elsif` branch drops the first label and compares the remaining labels whenever both hostnames have more than two labels. This incorrectly treats two unrelated subdomains of a shared public suffix as the same domain. For example, if `Discourse.current_hostname` is `forum.blogspot.com` and the user's website is `http://random.blogspot.com/private`, `website_name` becomes `random.blogspot.com/private` even though the sites are not controlled by the same domain owner. Use a public-suffix-aware comparison or otherwise verify the registrable domain before deciding to append the URL path.

title: website_name bypasses trust-level restrictions and leaks private website info
body: The new `:website_name` attribute is added to the main `attributes` list but is not included in `untrusted_attributes` (unlike `:website`). As a result, when a TL0 user's profile is viewed by an anonymous user and `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` returns true, the `website` attribute is hidden, but `website_name` is still serialized because its inclusion logic only checks `website.present?`. This leaks the user's website host and path to anonymous visitors, violating the privacy controls applied to other profile fields. The `include_website_name` method also lacks a trailing `?`, potentially causing it to be ignored entirely, which would make the attribute always present even when `website` is empty. The spec at line 11 of `spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb` omits `:website_name` from `untrusted_attributes`, so this regression is not caught.

title: Domain comparison treats sibling subdomains as the same domain
body: The condition in the `elsif` branch compares the suffix after the first label: `website_host.split('.')[1..-1] == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1]`. This means any two domains with more than two labels that share the same parent after the first label are considered equivalent. For example, `www.example.com` and `forum.example.com` would both match, causing the full URL path to be shown for any website hosted on a sibling subdomain of the instance domain, even though they are not the same domain nor a parent/child relationship. The PR description and tests only cover exact domain match and parent-child relationships (e.g., `example.com` vs `forums.example.com`), so this behavior is likely unintentional and may expose a misleading display of the website path. Additionally, the conditional uses a ternary inside an `elsif` containing a comparison that returns a boolean, possibly making the intent unclear.

title: Derived website_name bypasses untrusted attribute filtering
body: `website_name` is added as a normal serialized attribute, but `website` is already in the `untrusted_attributes` list (lines 105-111), which suppresses fields for restricted users such as TL0 profiles viewed by anonymous visitors. Because `website_name` is derived from `website` and is not added to that untrusted list, it is still serialized and rendered when `website` itself would be hidden, leaking the user-supplied website host and path. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and add a spec asserting it is omitted alongside `website`.

title: Inclusion predicate is missing the trailing question mark
body: `include_website_name` is defined without the trailing `?`, while serializer inclusion predicates in this file follow the `include_email?` / `include_website_name?` convention. As written, this method is not used as the inclusion check, so `website_name` can be emitted even when `website` is blank (as a null field) instead of being omitted. Rename it to `def include_website_name?`.

title: Sibling-subdomain branch is not tested
body: The new `website_name` serializer logic has distinct branches for exact host match, same-length subdomain siblings (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`), and parent-domain suffix matching. The new examples cover exact host and parent-domain cases but not the sibling-subdomain `elsif` branch, so a regression in that branch would not fail these tests. Add a spec using two different subdomains of the same parent domain.

title: Embedded topic author link color lightness changed in light theme
body: The old rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so the light theme branch changed from 30% to 70% lightness. The first argument should remain `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` (the dark theme branch would then be 70%). As written, the embedded post author link becomes much lighter than intended in light themes.

This changes the light theme from 70% to 30% and gives the dark theme 70% instead of the expected 30%, so the modal hint text renders with the wrong contrast in both themes.

title: Member add/remove routes use :id, but controller requires :group_id
body: The new routes in config/routes.rb (`delete "members"` and `put "members"` inside `resources :groups`) produce paths like `/admin/groups/:id/members`, so the group id arrives in `params[:id]`. However `add_members` (and `remove_member` at line 85) call `params.require(:group_id)`, which raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing` for real HTTP requests. The JS client calls `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json`, so adding or removing members will always return 400 and the feature is broken. The specs pass only because they invoke controller actions directly with `group_id`, bypassing routing. Use `params[:id]` or configure the route with `param: :group_id`.

title: Public members endpoint uses :group_id although route param is :id
body: `GET /groups/:id/members` (from `resources :groups do get 'members' end`) places the group identifier in `params[:id]`, but this action calls `find_group(:group_id)`, which does `params.require(:group_id)`. Real HTTP requests therefore fail with `ActionController::ParameterMissing`. The admin group page now depends on this endpoint through `Discourse.Group#findMembers` (`/groups/<name>/members.json`), so the admin member list will not load. The `show` action correctly uses `find_group(:id)`; this action should do the same, or the route should be changed accordingly.

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` — for example 50 users with limit 50, or 100 with limit 50 — this reports one extra page. That makes `showingLast` false on the last real page, so the Next button can navigate to an empty page before becoming disabled. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the existing zero-user guard).

title: create ignores alias_level sent by the client
body: The admin group form renders the alias level selector even for a new group, and the client sends `alias_level` in `asJSON()`. However `create` only sets `name` and `visible`; it never assigns `group.alias_level` from `params[:alias_level]`. The group is saved with the default alias level instead of the value the admin selected. The client model also only updates `id` after creation, so the UI may continue showing the selected value until a full reload, hiding the mismatch.

title: Usernames are not stripped when splitting comma-separated input
body: `add_members` does `usernames.split(",").each` and looks up each entry with `User.find_by_username`. If the input is `"alice, bob"`, the second entry is `" bob"` and lookup fails, so that member is silently not added even though the request still reports success. The username list should be split on commas and each token stripped before lookup.

title: remove_member auto-group spec uses PUT for a DELETE action
body: This test invokes `xhr :put, :remove_member` directly on the controller, but the actual route is `DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members`. Because controller specs bypass routing, this also fails to detect that real requests send `params[:id]` while the controller requires `:group_id`. The spec should use `xhr :delete, ...` and ideally an integration/request spec should exercise the routes, otherwise the broken endpoint passes tests.

title: Public group members page now shows only first 50 members with no pagination
body: The public group members route (`group-members`) now calls `model.findMembers()` which uses the model's default `limit` of 50. The template iterates over `members` without any pagination controls, so for any group with more than 50 members, only the first 50 are displayed and there is no way to see the rest. Previously, non-automatic groups showed all members. This is a functional regression for public group pages.

title: totalPages calculation is off-by-one when user_count is divisible by limit
body: The `totalPages` computed property uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100 users, limit 50), this returns 3 instead of 2. This causes `showingLast` to remain false on the final page, so the next button stays enabled and clicking it does nothing (offset is clamped to user_count). The UI shows an extra non-existent page.

title: Admin group creation ignores alias_level parameter
body: The `create` action only sets `name` and `visible` from params; it does not set `alias_level`. The frontend form always displays the alias level combo box (even for new groups), but any value selected by the user is silently discarded during creation. The group will be created with the default alias level instead of the chosen one.

title: No upper bound on limit parameter for public members endpoint
body: The `members` action uses `(params[:limit] || 50).to_i` without validating that the provided limit is reasonable. A client could request `limit=1000000` or higher, causing the server to load and serialize a huge number of records, potentially degrading performance or exhausting memory. A maximum value (e.g., 200) should be enforced.

title: Member list rendering broken due to incorrect each helper syntax
body: The template uses `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` without the opening `#`. In Ember, block helpers require `{{#each ...}}`. As written, this is treated as an inline helper returning nothing, and the members are never iterated. Additionally, there is no closing `{{/each}}`. This causes the admin group members list to be empty. The line should be `{{#each member in members itemView="group-member"}} ... {{/each}}`.

title: Spec uses wrong HTTP verb for remove_member automatic group test
body: The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, but the route for remove_member is defined as DELETE (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`). This will raise a RoutingError and cause the spec to fail. It should use `xhr :delete` instead.

title: Remove button appears for automatic groups due to wrong context
body: The template uses `{{#unless automatic}}` to conditionally show the remove link. Inside the itemView, the context is the member (a User), not the group, so `automatic` is undefined and the `#unless` always evaluates true. Therefore the remove icon is shown for members of automatic groups, even though the backend will reject removal with a 422. The group's automatic flag should be passed to the item view or checked from the parent controller.

title: Public group members template may fail if controller does not proxy to model
body: The template now iterates over `members` (`{{#each m in members}}`) instead of `model`. The route's setupController sets `controller.set("model", model)` and calls `model.findMembers()`, which populates `model.members`. If the controller for this route does not proxy properties to the model (e.g., is not an Em.ObjectController), `members` will be undefined and the list will be empty. The controller definition is not included in this diff, so it is unclear if this works. Ensure the controller proxies or explicitly set `members` on the controller.

title: No maximum limit on group members page size
body: The `members` action accepts a `limit` parameter and passes it directly to `.limit(limit)` without enforcing a maximum. A client can request an arbitrarily large limit (e.g., 1000000), causing a large database query and memory consumption. Consider capping the limit to a reasonable value (e.g., 100) to prevent abuse or accidental performance degradation.

title: Fallback locales are not loaded in non-controller code paths
body: The new ensure_loaded! method only loads fallback locales when ApplicationController#set_locale explicitly calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, and other non-controller code call I18n.translate directly; translate_accelerator's translate method only loads config.locale before looking up the key. With the new fallback chain [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en], a job using a non-English locale can therefore miss fallback translations that exist in the site-default or English locale, producing missing translation errors or empty/fallback text in emails and jobs.

title: Translation cache key omits dynamic fallback order
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] now makes fallback resolution depend on mutable SiteSetting.default_locale. translate caches results using only key, config.locale, and backend.object_id, so if the site default locale is changed at runtime, entries cached when a key fell back to the old default or :en will continue to be served for the same locale until LRU eviction, even if the new fallback chain would resolve to a different translation.

title: No tests cover the fallback setup
body: The PR replaces per-environment config.i18n.fallbacks with a custom fallback chain and lazy loading, but adds no tests. There is no coverage that a non-English locale falls back to SiteSetting.default_locale and then :en, that fallback locales are loaded in all relevant entry points, or that runtime changes to default_locale do not leave stale accelerator cache entries.

title: Dynamic fallback chain is not represented in the I18n translation cache key
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] builds the fallback order from SiteSetting.default_locale at lookup time. The translation cache in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb uses the key "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}" (line 72), which does not include the fallback chain or default locale. If an admin changes SiteSetting.default_locale, entries cached for a locale using the old fallback translation (for example fr falling back to es) will still be returned for fr until I18n.reload! or a restart. The cache key should include the fallback order/site default locale or the cache must be invalidated when default_locale changes.

title: Fallback locales are only preloaded for web requests, not background jobs/mailers/rake tasks
body: I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is only called from ApplicationController#set_locale after setting the request locale. Other code paths call I18n.translate directly; translate_accelerator.rb's translate only load_locale(config.locale) and never ensures the fallback locales. With the new global FallbackLocaleList active in all environments, a missing key in a worker/mailer/rake task current locale will fall back to SiteSetting.default_locale or :en, but those locale files may not be loaded in that process, so the lookup can return a missing translation despite valid fallback translations. Preloading fallbacks should happen in the I18n.translate path or in ensure_loaded!, or background codepaths need the same preload.

title: No specs cover the custom fallback order and preloading behavior
body: This PR introduces a custom fallback chain, moves pluralization and fallback setup into a new initializer, and adds request-time ensure_loaded! preloading, but adds no tests. Regressions in fallback order (user locale, site default, English), the migration of pluralization, or loading fallback locales in non-controller contexts would not be caught. Add specs for FallbackLocaleList and for I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! plus fallback translation results outside ApplicationController.

title: No tests added for localization fallback behavior
body: The PR introduces a custom fallback mechanism (FallbackLocaleList) and changes pluralization loading, but no tests are included. Without tests, regressions in translation fallback order, fallback loading via ensure_loaded!, or pluralization integration could go unnoticed. Given that this feature affects every I18n lookup, test coverage should verify that translations fall back through the expected locale chain and that pluralization still works.

title: Denial cache key ignores identity type, causing cross-identity false denials
body: The denial cache key is built from namespace, UserUID, action, name, and parent, but not IdentityType. validateSubject returns UID "0" for both `anonymous:0` and `render:0` (and potentially other identity types). If an anonymous user is denied access to a dashboard, the negative entry is stored under that key; a subsequent renderer check for the same dashboard/action/parent hits the denial cache and returns false before getCachedIdentityPermissions or getRendererPermissions can grant wildcard read access. This can block rendering of dashboards for up to the cache TTL. Include IdentityType (or otherwise namespace the key per identity type) in userPermDenialCacheKey.

title: Denial cache key concatenation is ambiguous and can collide
body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates namespace, userUID, action, name, and parent with "_" separators without escaping or length prefixes. Values may themselves contain underscores (for example resource UIDs/folder UIDs), so different tuples can produce the same key, e.g. userUID "a_b", action "c", name "d", parent "e" collides with userUID "a", action "b_c", name "d", parent "e". A collision in the denial cache can cause a user to be denied access to a resource for which no negative decision was actually made. Use an unambiguous encoding (length-prefixed, structured key, or hashed fields).

title: Denial cache key does not include identity type, causing cross-identity collisions
body: The denial cache key is built without the identity type. For anonymous users the parsed userUID is "0", and for render service the parsed userUID is also "0". Since the key does not differentiate between these identity types, a denial entry cached for an anonymous user can be returned for a render service request for the same action/name/parent, and vice versa. This can cause incorrect authorization decisions (false denials). The key should include checkReq.IdentityType to separate identities.

title: Denial cache key concatenation can cause collisions between different resources
body: The function userPermDenialCacheKey builds a key by concatenating namespace, userUID, action, name, and parent with underscores, with no escaping or delimiter that cannot appear in the values. For example, name="foo_bar" and parent="" produces the same key as name="foo" and parent="bar". Such collisions can cause a denial cached for one resource to be incorrectly applied to a different resource, leading to false access denials. Use a safe encoding (e.g., length-prefixing, hashing, or a non-ambiguous delimiter) or a structured key builder.

title: Denial cache entries are not invalidated when permissions are granted, causing temporary false denials
body: When a check results in a deny, the service stores a denial entry in permDenialCache with TTL 30 seconds. This cache is checked first on subsequent requests and is never invalidated when permissions are added or the resource is created. A user who previously attempted to access a resource that did not exist or for which they lacked permission will have a denial entry for that resource key. If the resource is then created or the user is granted permission, they will continue to be denied for up to 30 seconds because the stale denial entry is returned before checking the permission cache or database. This can cause the very problem the PR aims to fix (immediate access to newly created dashboards/folders) for resources with previously attempted names. The denial cache should be cleared on permission changes or the TTL should be very short, or denials should only be cached when the resource is known to exist.

title: Stale denial cache can keep newly granted access denied until TTL
body: The denial cache entry is consulted before any permission evaluation (lines 116-121), but it is only written when a DB-backed check returns false (lines 153-155). When a later DB check would return true, no code deletes the existing denial entry. Thus a user/resource that was denied once (e.g., before permission propagation completed) will continue to receive Allowed: false for shortCacheTTL (30s), even though fresh permissions now allow access. This undermines the PR's goal of letting creators see newly created resources and can cause support issues. Consider deleting the denial key when a fresh check yields allowed, or not caching denials for resources that may be newly created.

title: Denial cache key is ambiguous and omits identity type
body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates namespace, userUID, action, name, and parent with '_'. Fields are not escaped and the identity type is not included. Different tuples can collide (e.g., action "a_b", name "c" vs action "a", name "b_c"), and anonymous:0 can collide with user:0. Because this key is checked before permission evaluation in Check, a collision can make a legitimate request return Allowed: false. Use a length-prefixed/JSON-encoded key or include identity type and unambiguous delimiters.

title: Real errors from cached permission lookup are ignored and DB is queried twice
body: In Check, getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cache.ErrNotFound on a cache miss, but it can also return real errors (e.g., GetUserIdentifiers DB failure or unsupported identity type).
