body: The method `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is documented and used as an accessor for a BouncyCastle-compatible Provider, but this implementation returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, usually SUN/SunJCE. Any code that expects BC-specific algorithms or casts/uses this provider as BouncyCastle will get the wrong provider and may fail or silently use unintended cryptography.

title: Adding abstract order() breaks binary compatibility for existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public interface that external integrations may implement and compile against older Keycloak versions. Adding an abstract method `int order()` makes existing provider JARs binary-incompatible: ServiceLoader will instantiate them, and the method reference `CryptoProvider::order` used in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider will throw AbstractMethodError because the implementation class lacks that method. Keep binary compatibility by making `order()` a default method, for example `default int order() { return 0; }`.

title: Equal provider order values make provider selection nondeterministic
body: detectProvider now sorts providers only by `order` descending and silently picks the first one. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, and ServiceLoader encounter order for equal priority is not specified. If more than one of these providers is on the classpath, the selected crypto implementation becomes arbitrary and can change between runs or environments, replacing the previous fail-fast behavior. Assign distinct order values or add a deterministic tie-breaker.

title: readSequence can loop forever on a zero-length child element
body: `readSequence` loops while `length > 0` and decrements `length` by `bytes.length`. `readNext()` can return a zero-length byte array when a child TLV has content length 0, which is valid ASN.1 DER for some primitive types. If that happens, `length` is never decremented and this loop spins forever. The decoder is used to parse DER-encoded ECDSA signatures, so a malicious or malformed signature can cause CPU exhaustion or denial of service. Reject zero-length TLV children in this path or decrement by the number of header bytes consumed separately.

title: Registered CryptoProvider throws UnsupportedOperationException for core signing operations
body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider is registered through META-INF/services and becomes the active CryptoProvider when no higher-order provider exists. However `getSignature` and many other required CryptoProvider methods throw UnsupportedOperationException. Keycloak's JWS signing path calls `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getSignature(algorithm)`, so client authentication or token handling that requires signing will fail at runtime when this provider is selected. The added test only exercises ASN.1 conversion directly and does not exercise provider selection or JWS signing, so this regression is not covered. Either implement the needed methods or do not register this class as a general CryptoProvider.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns an unrelated default KeyStore provider
body: The CryptoProvider contract describes `getBouncyCastleProvider()` as returning the BouncyCastle (or FIPS BouncyCastle) provider. This implementation returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is normally a JDK provider such as SunJCE/SunJSSE and has no relation to BouncyCastle. Callers that rely on BC algorithms or provider identity will get incorrect behavior. Returning null, as WildFlyElytronProvider does, or actually loading/registering BouncyCastle would be consistent with the interface.

title: All-clients permission is ignored when an individual client resource exists
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), if resourceStore.findByName finds a resource for the specific client, evaluation proceeds only against that individual resource and never falls back to the 'Clients' resource-type resource. Scope permissions created for the whole Clients resource type with no resources field are associated with the all-resource, not with each client resource. As a result, an admin granted MANAGE, CONFIGURE, or MAP_ROLES for all clients can be denied for a client that happens to have an individual resource (for example because another single-client permission was created). The method must evaluate both the specific client resource and the all-clients resource before deciding.

title: Individual client resources are created without their resource type
body: getOrCreateResource creates the per-client resource with resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId()) but never sets the resource type to resourceType. The new ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission relies on resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...), which will not find these individual resources. The callback therefore sees only the singleton 'Clients' resource created by init, so getClientsWithPermission cannot return the actual client IDs for per-client grants. The resource type must be set on newly created resources before they are returned.

title: Missing all-clients resource leads to null pointer dereference
body: When the individual client resource is not found, hasPermission(ClientModel, String) obtains the all-clients resource via AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...). That method can return null if the 'Clients' resource-type resource does not exist, but the code immediately passes resource to authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource). A missing or not-yet-initialized all-resource then throws a NullPointerException instead of simply denying the check. A null check is needed before querying policies.

title: getClientsWithPermission can return the 'Clients' sentinel instead of client IDs
body: resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) includes the resource-type resource named 'Clients' that represents all clients. If the caller has an all-clients grant for the requested scope, hasGrantedPermission returns true for that resource and the code adds resource.getName(), i.e. 'Clients', to the result set. The method contract returns client IDs, so callers receive a bogus non-client-ID entry and still do not receive the actual clients implied by the all-clients permission. The all-resource must be excluded from this enumeration or expanded into real client IDs.

title: Client removal cleanup is skipped under admin fine-grained authz V2
body: The removal listener is now gated by Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), which is the V1 feature. When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled instead, ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent never reaches the cleanup branch, and there is no alternative V2 cleanup in this change. Since this PR introduces per-client authorization resources under the admin permissions client, deleting a client that has client-specific scope permissions leaves orphaned Clients resources in the authorization store. A V2-aware cleanup path is needed for client removal.

title: getResourceName does not resolve the new Clients resource type
body: getResourceName special-cases USERS to resolve a username, but the newly added Clients resource type falls through to return resource.getDisplayName(). Per-client resources created by getOrCreateResource are named with the internal client id and do not have a display name set, so callers get null or an internal UUID rather than the client's clientId. A Clients branch analogous to the Users branch should resolve the client and return its clientId.

title: NPE when fallback all-clients resource is missing in per-client permission check
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no resource exists for the specific client, the code replaces `resource` with the result of getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) but never checks it for null. If that synthetic 'Clients' resource is absent (for example the admin-permissions realm was enabled/initialized before the new client resource type existed, or the resource was removed), findByResource(server, resource) at this line dereferences null and the request fails with a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of denying the permission. Add a null check and return false.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns the synthetic all-clients resource name 'Clients' as a client ID
body: resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) matches both individual client resources and the synthetic all-clients resource whose name is "Clients" because AdminPermissionsSchema.init creates that resource with type "Clients". If an all-clients scope permission exists, hasGrantedPermission returns true for it and granted.add(resource.getName()) adds "Clients" to the returned Set<String>. Callers expect client IDs, so the set is polluted with a non-existent ID. Exclude resource.getName().equals(AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) or otherwise skip the type-level resource.

title: Role/client/group removal listener can call V2 unsupported methods when both fine-grained authz features are enabled
body: The listener is gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ only, but AdminPermissions.management(...) gives precedence to ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. If both features are enabled, RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent still enter the block and management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2. For clients, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...) throws UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client (and similarly roles/groups if their V2 implementations are unsupported) can fail with an exception. The feature guard should account for V2 being active or the listener should force the V1 management implementation.

title: Javadoc says void requireView() returns boolean
body: The newly added Javadoc for `void requireView()` says 'Returns true if canView() returns true' even though the method returns void and throws ForbiddenException when not permitted. The same wording problem exists for requireViewClientScopes(). This misdocuments the API and can confuse implementers; adjust the Javadoc to describe the throw/require behavior instead of a boolean return.

title: Listener cleanup is gated on the wrong feature flag for V2
body: The event handling block is gated on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), but this PR is for ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. When only V2 is enabled, removal events for roles, clients, and groups are ignored, so associated admin permission resources/policies are not cleaned up. Conversely, if both V1 and V2 are enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and clients().setPermissionsEnabled() throws UnsupportedOperationException, so client removal events can cause a server error. The check should use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2, and the V2 evaluator must implement the cleanup path.

title: getClientsWithPermission filters by a type that per-client resources do not have
body: resourceStore.findByType is called with AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, but per-client resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource are created without calling setType, so they will not be returned by this query. The all-clients type resource itself does match and its name "Clients" is added to the result as if it were a client ID. As a result, the returned set does not contain the actual client IDs needed for admin list filtering, regardless of whether specific-client or all-client permissions are granted.

title: getResourceName does not resolve client resources added in this PR
body: getResourceName only handles the Users resource type. Client-specific resources are named by the client UUID and are created without a display name, so for the newly added Clients resource type this method falls through to resource.getDisplayName() and returns a null or otherwise meaningless value. This breaks human-readable permission/resource descriptions for client resources. A CLIENTS branch should resolve the ClientModel and return its clientId, similar to the existing user branch.

title: Null updateStrategy cases do not enable rolling-updates feature
body: In createInitialDeployment(UpdateStrategy), the early return for updateStrategy == null happens before the ROLLING_UPDATES feature is added to the Keycloak CR. The parameterized tests testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount therefore run with updateStrategy=null and the preview feature disabled. Since this PR introduces a feature gate for rolling-updates, these cases either will fail once enforcement is in place, or they are not exercising the feature-gated path and give false confidence. The null/default strategy path should also enable the feature or explicitly document/test that the feature is not required for that path.

title: Feature-disabled coverage only for metadata subcommand and not checking exit code
body: testFeatureNotEnabled launches only the metadata subcommand and asserts the error message, but does not assert exit code 4 and does not cover UpdateCompatibilityCheck. Both UpdateCompatibilityMetadata and UpdateCompatibilityCheck have duplicated feature-gate logic that exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED; a regression in the check subcommand or in the exit code contract would not be caught.

title: Invalid reference to picocli.exit causes compilation failure
body: The code calls `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED);` but `picocli` is not a class, variable, or static import. The correct call is `CommandLine.exit(...)` (the `CommandLine` class is imported) or `System.exit(...)`. As written, the project will not compile.

title: Invalid reference to picocli.exit causes compilation failure
body: The code calls `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED);` but `picocli` is not a class, variable, or static import. The correct call is `CommandLine.exit(...)` (the `CommandLine` class is imported) or `System.exit(...)`. As written, the project will not compile.

title: Feature-disabled test only covers metadata subcommand
body: The new test `testFeatureNotEnabled` only invokes the `metadata` subcommand without the feature flag, verifying the error and exit code. The `check` subcommand has identical feature-gating logic but is not covered. A similar test for `check` would ensure the behavior is consistent and prevent regressions.

title: Null update strategy case does not enable rolling-updates feature, but a test expects a rolling upgrade
body: `createInitialDeployment` returns at line 106 before enabling `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` when `updateStrategy` is null. `testCacheMaxCount` is parameterized with `null` and then expects `eventuallyRollingUpgradeStatus` for a configuration change. Since this PR introduces rolling-updates as a preview feature and documents that it must be enabled for operator update behavior, the null-strategy configuration-change case either fails if the operator enforces the feature flag, or does not exercise the feature-gated path if the operator still allows legacy rolling updates. The feature should be enabled for the null strategy when a rolling update is expected, or the expectation should be adjusted.

title: New exit codes 3 and 4 are not asserted by the CLI tests
body: The PR documents that recreate upgrades exit with code 3 and feature-disabled invocations exit with code 4, and `CompatibilityResult` now defines `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 3` and `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`. However, `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error text and `testWrongVersions` only asserts error messages; neither asserts `cliResult.exitCode()` equals 3 or 4. Also, the feature-disabled path is only tested for the `metadata` subcommand, not for `check`. A regression changing either exit code would not be detected by these tests.

title: Group resources created without type, breaking findByType lookup
body: When creating a resource for a specific group via getOrCreateResource(), the code does not call resource.setType(resourceType). The all-groups type-level resource created in init() does have its type set, but individual group resources do not. As a result, GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) and will not find these resources, causing the method to always return an empty set. This breaks pre-filtering of users by group membership in UsersResource.searchForUser() and, more importantly, leads to incorrect user counts in UsersResource.getUsersCount(), as the storage query will count all users instead of only those in groups the admin can view.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource UUIDs instead of Keycloak group IDs
body: In the lambda for resourceStore.findByType, the code adds groupResource.getId() to the granted set. However, groupResource.getId() is the internal authorization resource UUID, not the Keycloak group ID. The set is later used as a filter for user search via session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds), which expects actual group IDs. Since the resource name is set to the group ID (in AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup), the correct value is groupResource.getName(). This bug causes user filtering by group membership to fail and, when combined with missing type on group resources, completely breaks group-based user search and count.

title: canManage() incorrectly grants manage permission for VIEW scope
body: The method canManage() returns hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). This means an admin with only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource is considered to have global manage permission for groups. As a result, such an admin could call requireManage() and perform operations like creating top-level groups or other manage-level actions, violating the intended authorization model. The check should only include AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE, not VIEW.

title: Potential NullPointerException when all-groups resource is missing
body: In hasPermission(), if groupId is null and the all-groups resource cannot be found (e.g., admin permissions schema not initialized or resource type resource not created), getResourceTypeResource() returns null. The subsequent call policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) will throw a NullPointerException instead of returning false. This could lead to HTTP 500 errors for unauthorized access attempts. The code should check if resource is null before calling findByResource.

title: canManage() grants manage permission with only view scope
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the method calls hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). The hasPermission method returns true if any of the provided scopes is granted. Therefore, a user with only the VIEW scope on all groups would be considered as having manage permission for all groups. This bypasses authorization checks that rely on requireManage() (e.g., creating groups, updating group management). The correct call should be hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) only.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs instead of group IDs and uses wrong lookup
body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code iterates over group resources and for each groupResource calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), VIEW_MEMBERS, MANAGE_MEMBERS) and then adds groupResource.getId() to the granted set. However, groupResource.getId() is the authorization resource ID, not the group ID. The method is expected to return a set of group IDs (as used by UserModel.GROUPS attribute in user search). Additionally, inside hasPermission, the lookup uses resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), but the group resource name is the group ID (set by AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup which returns group.getId()). Since the passed ID is the resource ID, the lookup will fail and fall back to the all-groups resource for every group, leading to incorrect permission evaluation. The correct approach is to use groupResource.getName() (which is the group ID) for both the permission check and the returned set.

title: VIEW permission on all groups grants manage access
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). This means that a caller with only the VIEW scope on all groups will be considered as having manage permission. As a result, any operation requiring requireManage(), such as creating groups, adding child groups, or updating groups, will be allowed without the MANAGE scope. The method should only check the MANAGE scope. This is a privilege escalation vulnerability.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In the callback of resourceStore.findByType, the method adds groupResource.getId() to the granted set. Resource.getId() is the internal authorization resource UUID, which is not the same as the group ID. The returned set is later used in UsersResource.searchForUser and getUsersCount to filter users by group membership via session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds). Since the IDs are wrong, the filtering will not match any group, causing legitimate users to be hidden or search results to be empty. The method should instead use groupResource.getName(), which contains the group ID.

title: Individual group resources are not assigned the Groups resource type
body: When getOrCreateResource creates a new resource for a specific group (resourceType = GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE), it does not call resource.setType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) after creation. Later, GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) to discover group resources. Because the resources lack the type, they will not be returned, causing group-scoped view-members permissions to be ignored during user search and count queries. This breaks the ability to see users based on group VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions.

title: Missing fallback to all-groups permission when a specific group resource exists
body: In hasPermission, if a specific group resource exists (resource != null), the method evaluates only that resource's permissions. It does not fall back to the all-groups resource when the specific resource has no policy granting the requested scopes. Consequently, once a group-specific resource is created (e.g., via a single permission like MANAGE), a user with an all-groups VIEW or MANAGE permission may be denied access to that group for other scopes, because the all-groups policy is not considered. The fallback should occur not only when the resource is null, but also when the evaluation against the specific resource yields no matching permission.

title: Modifying value while iterating with matcher leads to incorrect anchor validation
body: In sanitizeAnchors, `value.replaceFirst(...)` is called inside a loop driven by `matcher.find()` where `matcher` was created from the original `value` string. The `Matcher` holds a reference to the original `CharSequence`, so the loop continues scanning the unmodified string while the replacement mutates `value`. This can cause anchors to be found multiple times, replacements to miss their intended target, or incorrect error reports. The anchor matching logic must be redesigned to avoid mutating the string during iteration (e.g., collect matches first and process them in reverse order).

title: PropertyResourceBundle reads using ISO-8859-1, not UTF-8
body: The `PropertyResourceBundle` is constructed with a `FileInputStream`, which reads properties using ISO-8859-1 encoding by default. Most Keycloak message property files are encoded in UTF-8 (as evidenced by the use of `Files.readString` elsewhere, which defaults to UTF-8). Non-ASCII characters (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic) will be misinterpreted, leading to incorrect sanitization comparisons and false positives/negatives. Use `new InputStreamReader(new FileInputStream(file), StandardCharsets.UTF_8)` when creating the bundle.

title: RuntimeException escapes instead of MojoExecutionException
body: verifySafeHtml() catches `IOException` and throws an unchecked `RuntimeException`. The public `verify()` method declares `MojoExecutionException`, but a RuntimeException can propagate and crash the Maven build with a less descriptive error. This breaks the expected exception contract and makes error handling harder. Wrap the RuntimeException in a MojoExecutionException (or change verifySafeHtml to throw MojoExecutionException).

title: containsHtml pattern is case-sensitive and may miss uppercase tags
body: The regex `Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` only matches lowercase tag names. HTML tags are case-insensitive, and the OWASP sanitizer normalizes or handles them case-insensitively. If a translation contains `<B>` while the English source contains `<b>`, containsHtml(englishValue) would be true (if English has lowercase), but the comparison against the translation's uppercase tag would still fail because the sanitized output from OWASP likely normalizes to lowercase, producing a mismatch. The pattern should be case-insensitive (`Pattern.compile("<[a-zA-Z]+[^>]*>"` or with `Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE`).

title: PropertyResourceBundle read with default ISO-8859-1 encoding corrupts non-ASCII translations
body: The verifier opens the properties file with FileInputStream and constructs PropertyResourceBundle, which decodes the stream as ISO-8859-1. Message properties files are UTF-8 encoded (as read correctly earlier with Files.readString), so all non-ASCII characters will be misdecoded. This will produce garbled strings, causing false positives in HTML detection and possibly invalid characters, making the verifier unreliable for most translated files. Use an InputStreamReader with UTF-8 or a Reader-based PropertyResourceBundle constructor.

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 contains Italian text
body: The value for totpStep1 was changed to 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian, not Lithuanian. This will display Italian text to Lithuanian users. The original text was Lithuanian. The same issue occurs in the login theme file.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 contains Italian text
body: The value for loginTotpStep1 was changed to 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian, not Lithuanian. This will display Italian text to Lithuanian users during TOTP setup.

title: Simplified Chinese totpStep1 contains Traditional Chinese text
body: The value for totpStep1 was changed to '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', which uses Traditional Chinese characters (您, 機, 應用程式). This is the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) file, so users will see Traditional Chinese characters. Should be Simplified Chinese.

title: Blanket removal of style attribute based on path containing 'email' is fragile
body: The normalization removes any occurrence of ' style="direction: rtl;"' for any file whose absolute path contains the substring 'email'. This is not specific to email message files; it can affect other resources in directories with 'email' in the name, silently removing legitimate style attributes. It also only matches the exact string, so variations like single quotes or no spaces will not be removed, leading to false positives. Replace with a precise check or handle styles in the sanitizer policy.

title: verifySafeHtml throws RuntimeException if English reference file is missing
body: When constructing englishFile and opening it with FileInputStream, any IOException is wrapped in a RuntimeException. If a translation file has no corresponding English file (e.g., some community-only resources), the verifier will abort the entire build. This should be handled gracefully, perhaps by skipping HTML verification or reporting a specific error message, not crashing.

title: RuntimeException bypasses MojoExecutionException error handling
body: In verifySafeHtml(), IOException while reading either the current file or the English file is wrapped in a RuntimeException and thrown. This occurs inside the try block of verify(), which only catches IOException. As a result, any I/O error (missing English file, permission issue, etc.) will propagate as an uncaught RuntimeException instead of the expected MojoExecutionException, causing the Maven plugin to fail with a stack trace that does not conform to standard error handling and may hide the underlying cause.

title: Italian text in Lithuanian translation
body: The value for totpStep1 was replaced with the Italian phrase "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". This is clearly a copy-paste error and produces an incorrect Lithuanian translation. Users with Lithuanian locale will see Italian instructions. The original Lithuanian text should be restored or properly translated.

title: Italian text in Lithuanian translation
body: The value for loginTotpStep1 was replaced with the Italian phrase "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". This is the same copy-paste error as in the account messages file, causing Italian text to appear for Lithuanian users on the login page TOTP setup step.

title: Traditional Chinese text in simplified Chinese translation
body: The value for totpStep1 was changed from simplified Chinese to traditional Chinese ("在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一："). The file is intended for the zh_CN (simplified) locale, so this introduces an incorrect variant. The simplified Chinese text should be used instead.

title: Non-default method added to public grant type SPI
body: Adding `String getShortcut()` to the public `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface without a default implementation is a binary/source incompatible change for existing third-party grant type providers. During `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`, every `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` is fetched and `getShortcut()` is invoked. Existing extension JARs compiled against the old interface will throw `AbstractMethodError` and can prevent server startup. A default implementation, separate capability interface, or migration/validation path is needed.

title: Removed public Context copy constructor breaks extensions
body: The public `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context)` copy constructor was silently removed. External grant type implementations or other code using `new Context(existingContext)` will no longer compile and previously compiled binaries will fail with `NoSuchMethodError`. If this SPI is meant to be extensible, retaining the copy constructor or explicitly documenting the break is necessary.

title: Wrong argument is null-checked for rawTokenId
body: The constructor validates `grantType` twice: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. `rawTokenId` is never checked and can be null, contrary to the constructor's apparent contract. A null raw ID is then accepted and can produce an encoded token ID with the string "null" as the identifier suffix.

title: Encoder assumes exactly two-character grant type shortcuts
body: The SPI contract for `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` does not require a two-character value, and its Javadoc even says shortcuts are usually like three letters. However, `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` requires the encoded prefix to be exactly length 6 and splits it into fixed 2-character chunks, while `encodeTokenId()` performs no length validation. A custom grant type with a three-character shortcut will emit a longer prefix, and decoding that token ID will throw `IllegalArgumentException` because `encodedContext.length() != 6`, making valid providers unusable.

title: Reserved UNKNOWN shortcut can silently mask a custom grant type
body: `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.UNKNOWN` is the string "na", but it is inserted into `grantsByShortcuts` after all provider shortcuts and overwrites any provider using the same shortcut. The duplicate-shortcut validation only compares map sizes; for a grant whose shortcut is "na", the overwrite plus the added UNKNOWN entry can keep both map sizes equal and bypass validation. Such a grant would encode as "na" but decode as UNKNOWN, losing the grant type information.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses inverted condition and wrong substring
body: The matcher extracts `items[0].substring(3, 5)` rather than the grant-type range at indices 4-5, and returns false when that substring equals the expected shortcut instead of returning false when it does not. With the built-in shortcuts this means the condition is essentially never true, so any six-character prefix followed by a UUID passes. The test does not actually verify the grant type encoded in the token ID. It should likely be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

title: Null check validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
body: The constructor uses Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") for the fourth argument, so rawTokenId is never checked. When such a context is encoded, encodeTokenId concatenates null as 'null', which can produce malformed or non-unique token IDs. The intended invariant is that rawTokenId is non-null; the check should use rawTokenId.

title: isAccessTokenId checks wrong substring with inverted condition
body: The grant-type shortcut is at prefix positions 4-5 (e.g. onrtac -> ac), but substring(3, 5) extracts positions 3-4 (the token type), and the method returns false when those characters equal the expected grant shortcut. It never validates the actual grant type, and for refresh-token flows the token type shortcut rt equals the grant shortcut rt, so expectRefresh(...) will always fail for regular tokens. Use items[0].substring(4, 6) and return true on equality (or otherwise verify the correct segment).

title: New abstract interface method breaks existing custom grant type providers
body: getShortcut() is added as an abstract method to the public OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI. Existing compiled third-party grant type provider factories will fail with AbstractMethodError when loaded, and source code will no longer compile. Since this is a public Keycloak SPI, this is a binary/source compatibility break. Consider providing a default implementation (e.g. returning a neutral shortcut) or otherwise versioning the SPI.

title: Removing public Context copy constructor breaks API consumers
body: OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context) was a public constructor on a public nested class in a SPI package and has been removed. Any existing custom grant implementation that clones the context will fail to compile or run. If the constructor is no longer wanted, it should be deprecated before removal or the new grantType field must be made available elsewhere; as-is this is an API contract break.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher rejects matching grant shortcuts and checks the wrong prefix offset
body: In matchesSafely(), `items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` returns false when the grant shortcut matches, so every token with the expected grant shortcut is rejected. In addition, the 6-character prefix is laid out as session[0:2], token[2:4], grant[4:6], but substring(3,5) reads characters 3 and 4. The check should use substring(4,6) and return true when that equals expectedGrantShortcut. As written, the updated expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken assertions will fail for valid issued tokens.

title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
body: The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` for the rawTokenId parameter, so rawTokenId is never validated and the error message is misleading. If a caller supplies a null raw token id, encodeTokenId() will later produce a token id ending with `:null` instead of rejecting it, potentially breaking the expected uniqueness of jti. The second check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

title: Adding abstract getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks existing grant type factories
body: `getShortcut()` is added to the public `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI without a default implementation. Existing third-party grant type factories compiled against the previous interface will not implement this method, causing `AbstractMethodError`/`NoSuchMethodError`, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` calls `getShortcut()` on every factory, so server startup or token issuance can fail after an upgrade. If this SPI is intended for extensions, the new method should be a default method or missing shortcuts should be handled explicitly.

title: Public copy constructor removed from OAuth2GrantType.Context
body: The public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor is deleted from the public nested `OAuth2GrantType.Context` class. Extensions that copy an existing grant context will fail to compile or link after this change. If this removal is not intended as a breaking API change, keep the constructor and copy the newly added `grantType` field (`this.grantType = context.grantType`) as well.

title: Custom grant shortcuts with a length other than two produce unparseable token IDs
body: The default encoder and decoder hard-code a 6-character prefix composed of 2-char session type, 2-char token type, and 2-char grant type. `postInit()` validates only duplicate shortcuts, not their length, and `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` does not specify a 2-character contract. A custom grant type returning, for example, a 3-character shortcut will be accepted here and emitted in access-token IDs, but `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` will later reject those IDs because `encodedContext.length()` is not 6 or because the grant substring is misaligned. Validate exactly two characters at startup or enforce/document the length contract.

title: removeStoredCredentialById does not remove federated recovery codes
body: The credential may now reside in user storage (retrieved via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential which checks federated storage first). removeStoredCredentialById operates only on local stored credentials and will not remove a federated credential, leaving the exhausted credential in user storage. Subsequently, the required action is added, causing duplicate credentials when the user reconfigures. A federated-specific removal method or clearing the credential via updateCredential should be used.

title: getCredentials loses used state for recovery codes
body: The getCredentials method deserializes raw codes and calls RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...), which creates a model with all codes marked unused. Any usage tracking from the provider (if implemented) would be lost, causing RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential to always return a model where allCodesUsed() is false. This prevents the authenticator from detecting exhausted codes and triggering reconfiguration. Additionally, the provider's isValid does not track usage, so codes can be reused indefinitely. The creation path in CredentialHelper only passes raw codes to user storage, not the hashed/stateful model, making it impossible for providers to track used state correctly.

title: Recovery codes cannot be disabled or removed via admin API
body: disableCredentialType only handles OTP types; recovery codes are ignored. Additionally, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream (line 254) does not include recovery codes, so they won't be listed. This means administrators or account management cannot remove recovery codes from federated users, leaving stale credentials and preventing proper lifecycle management. These methods should be extended to support RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE.

title: Optional.get() can throw if no recovery credential
body: credentialModelOpt.get() will throw NoSuchElementException if RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential returns empty. While this bean is likely only used when a credential exists, relying on that implicit precondition is fragile; a missing credential would cause a server error instead of a graceful handling.

title: Non-deterministic selection of federated recovery credential
body: getFederatedCredentialsStream().filter(...).findFirst() returns the first credential from an unordered stream. If multiple federated providers provide recovery codes, the selected credential may vary, leading to inconsistent behavior in checking allCodesUsed or retrieving the next code. A deterministic ordering or a check across all credentials should be considered.

title: Recovery codes are not consumed after use
body: In isValid() for recovery codes, the provided code is only compared against the stored raw codes, but it is not marked as used or removed. As a result, the same recovery code can be reused multiple times, defeating the purpose of recovery codes. This differs from the local storage implementation, which consumes the code after successful validation. The test provider should update its stored credential to remove or mark the used code, and the test should verify that a used code cannot be used again.

title: Recovery codes credential ID not preserved in getCredentials
body: In getCredentials(), the recovery codes credential model is reconstructed from raw codes using RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(), which generates a new ID. The original ID stored in myUser.recoveryCodes is lost. If the authenticator later determines that all codes have been used and attempts to remove the credential via removeStoredCredentialById(), it will use the newly generated ID, which does not match the stored credential ID, causing the removal to fail. This also prevents proper usage tracking because the returned model always appears to have all codes available.

title: Unchecked Optional.get() can crash recovery code login page for user-storage credentials
body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` can now return an empty `Optional` when the user has recovery codes only in a user storage provider that implements `isConfiguredFor`/`isValid` but does not implement `getCredentials` (making `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` empty). The previous local-only lookup also used `.get()`, but this PR newly supports federated-only recovery codes, so this path is newly reachable. The unchecked `credentialModelOpt.get()` throws `NoSuchElementException`, causing a 500 instead of rendering the recovery-code login form.

title: User-storage recovery codes are not consumed, so codes remain reusable and reconfigure is never required
body: After a valid recovery code is submitted, this code relies on `recoveryCodeCredentialModel.allCodesUsed()` from `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` to decide whether to remove the credential and add the `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES` required action. For a credential stored in user storage, `isValid` is dispatched to the user storage provider. The test provider (and any provider that implements `CredentialInputValidator` without mutating stored credentials) only compares the submitted raw code against the stored list and does not remove the used code. The model returned by `getCredential` therefore continues to report that codes remain, so `allCodesUsed()` never becomes true, used codes stay valid indefinitely, and the required action is never added. Recovery codes must be consumed either by the framework or by an enforced provider contract; otherwise the one-time property is lost for federated storage.

title: Null delegate handling still incomplete for subgroup stream methods
body: The PR fixes getSubGroupsCount() by guarding a null result from modelSupplier.get(), but the three getSubGroupsStream overloads at lines 256, 262, and 268 still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. Since getGroupModel() can return null when the group is deleted concurrently, which is the exact scenario this PR addresses, these overloads will still throw NullPointerException. Apply the same null-handling strategy consistently, e.g. return Stream.empty() or delegate for update.

title: Reader thread is not joined before asserting no exceptions
body: The test starts a reader thread and then sets deletedAll to true and immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty without joining the thread. A request that was already in flight when deletedAll was set can fail after the assertion reads the list, so the test can pass even though the NPE it is meant to catch occurred. Additionally, if group removal throws before deletedAll is set, the non-daemon reader thread will loop forever and can outlive the test, interfering with cleanup and other tests. Join the thread before asserting and ensure the stop flag is set in a finally block.

title: Concurrency test asserts without joining the reader thread
body: The test starts a non-daemon reader thread that loops over group reads until deletedAll is set, then immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty after setting deletedAll and deleting groups. There is no thread.join(), so the assertion races with the reader's final HTTP call: an NPE or other exception raised after the assertion is never observed, making the test unable to reliably catch the regression it targets. Also, if deletion throws before deletedAll.set(true), the reader never gets the stop signal and can keep running against the test realm during teardown, leaking a non-daemon thread. Join the reader thread (with a timeout) or otherwise synchronize termination before asserting, and ensure the stop flag is set in a finally block.

title: Null dereference still possible in other methods using modelSupplier.get()
body: The PR fixes getSubGroupsCount() by checking for null, but several other methods in the same class (e.g., getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer) at line 262, getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) at line 268) still directly call modelSupplier.get().<method>() without a null check. If the group is concurrently deleted (the exact scenario this PR addresses), modelSupplier.get() can return null and cause a NullPointerException. The fix is incomplete and the same race can still crash the request.

title: Reader thread is not joined and may outlive the test
body: The test starts a new thread that loops until deletedAll is set to true, but never calls join() on that thread. As a result, the test method can return while the reader thread is still executing, leading to resource leaks, nondeterministic test cleanup, and potential interference with subsequent tests. Additionally, if the test fails before deletedAll is set, the thread will run forever and may hang the test suite. The thread should be joined with a timeout and/or made daemon.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on DateTimeField order_by
body: The new paginator is used by OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint with order_by="-datetime", but `get_item_key` is copied from `Paginator` and does `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` on the raw field value. For `AuditLogEntry.datetime` that value is a `datetime`, and `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime`. `build_cursor` calls this key function for the first page, so any authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true` will return a 500 instead of results. It should convert datetimes to epoch milliseconds like `DateTimePaginator` does.

title: Negative cursor offsets cause Django negative-slicing error/500
body: In the advanced-feature branch, a forged or malformed cursor with negative `offset` sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and then slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet does not support negative offsets/indices and raises an exception rather than the Python list semantics implied by the comment. A client can pass a cursor string such as `-1:-1:0` with `optimized_pagination=true` and trigger an internal server error. Negative offsets should be rejected or clamped, as the base paginator now does for non-prev cursors.

title: No tests for the new paginator or gated endpoint
body: This PR adds a new paginator and an opt-in endpoint path but includes no tests. There is no coverage for `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with datetime ordering, cursor navigation, negative/malformed cursor offsets, or the superuser/global-access gating in `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint`. Tests would have caught the datetime key crash and the negative-slice crash before merge.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator fails on datetime keys
body: The new OptimizedCursorPaginator inherits from BasePaginator and overrides get_item_key to call math.floor/ceil on the attribute value. However, the endpoint uses this paginator with order_by="-datetime", so self.key is "datetime" and getattr(item, self.key) returns a datetime object. math.floor() cannot operate on a datetime, causing a TypeError on the first cursor building or result key computation. The original DateTimePaginator handles datetime fields, but this paginator does not. Any request with optimized_pagination=true will crash.

title: Negative offset slicing on Django QuerySet raises an exception
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, the code executes results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop]) with a negative start_offset. Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError or ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported"). The comment claims the ORM handles negative slicing automatically, which is false. This can be triggered by a client-provided cursor with a negative offset, causing a 500 error and potential denial of service for admins using the feature.

title: Possible AttributeError when organization_context.member is None
body: The expression organization_context.member.has_global_access assumes that member is not None. A superuser who is not a member of the organization may still pass permission checks (OrganizationAuditPermission often allows superusers regardless of membership), but in that case organization_context.member could be None. Accessing has_global_access on None will raise AttributeError and return a 500 instead of a proper response. Add a null check before dereferencing member.

title: No tests for new optimized pagination path
body: The PR adds a new paginator and a conditional code path (optimized_pagination=true) but includes no tests. The new paginator is broken for datetime keys and negative offsets, and the member dereference issue would not be caught without tests. At minimum, tests should cover the new endpoint query parameter, cursor generation, and handling of missing members.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime sort keys and crashes on first page
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime', so self.key is 'datetime' and get_item_key receives a datetime object. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError: must be real number, not datetime. build_cursor always calls the key callable for non-empty results, so any optimized_pagination=true request from an authorized user fails. value_from_cursor also returns cursor.value as a raw number rather than converting it to a datetime like DateTimePaginator does, so even if get_item_key were fixed, the generated SQL would compare a datetime column with a numeric value.

title: Negative cursor offsets reach Django slicing and produce a 500 response
body: Cursor.from_string and Cursor.__init__ accept arbitrary negative offset values without validation. In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, the advanced branch passes a negative cursor.offset directly into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative offsets and will raise ValueError (negative offset is not supported) or produce invalid SQL. An authorized user can trigger this by supplying a crafted cursor such as 0:-1:0 with optimized_pagination=true. The comment claiming the Django ORM handles negative slicing automatically is incorrect.

title: No tests cover the new OptimizedCursorPaginator or its advanced negative-offset path
body: The PR adds a new paginator class and a new endpoint code path but includes no tests. This is especially risky because the class is used with a datetime order_by, which its numeric get_item_key cannot handle, and because the negative-offset branch relies on Django behavior that is incorrectly assumed to be safe. Tests for the paginator and the endpoint conditional would have caught both failure modes.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime fields
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", so self.key is "datetime" and get_item_key is called with a datetime.datetime object. This method does math.floor/ceil on that datetime, which raises TypeError as soon as a non-empty page needs next/prev cursor values. Additionally, value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor int instead of converting it to a UTC datetime for the SQL cursor comparison, so even if get_item_key were fixed, resumed pages would compare a datetime column with an integer. Consequence: optimized_pagination=true requests against audit logs with any results fail with a server error or produce invalid cursor queries.

title: Eviction can silently drop the root span from a buffered segment
body: The new size cap calls zpopmin on the whole sorted set to remove spans with the smallest end_timestamp_precise. The script does not know which member is the root span and has no guard against removing it. If the root span has the oldest timestamp, it gets evicted while the has-root-span flag remains set. The segment then flushes on the root-span timeout but contains no span whose span_id matches the segment key, so downstream receives a segment without its root/segment span and incomplete trace data.

title: zunionstore sums duplicate span scores and corrupts eviction order
body: Redis zunionstore defaults to SUM aggregation, unlike the previous set union which deduplicated members. If the same span payload is present in both source keys (possible with redelivery or reprocessing), its score becomes the sum of the two end_timestamp_precise values instead of the timestamp itself. Since eviction at line 63 uses zpopmin on these scores, duplicate spans can appear artificially new, causing the wrong spans to be evicted and making the 1000-span cap operate on incorrect ordering. Use MAX aggregation or otherwise deduplicate before union.

title: Advanced negative-offset branch slices a QuerySet with a negative start
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, start_offset is set to the negative cursor.offset and then queryset[start_offset:stop] is evaluated. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative start offsets and emits an invalid negative OFFSET or raises, so the advertised advanced reverse pagination path cannot work. A crafted cursor with a negative offset on an endpoint using optimized_pagination=true can therefore cause a server error.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime fields
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime" (organization_auditlogs.py:79). This paginator's get_item_key assumes a numeric key and calls math.floor/math.ceil on the value, but the value is a datetime.datetime for audit logs. math.floor raises TypeError ("must be real number, not datetime") as soon as build_cursor processes the first non-empty page, so the optimized pagination path returns a 500. It should use the timestamp conversion logic from DateTimePaginator, both in get_item_key and value_from_cursor, or not be used with datetime fields.

title: Negative cursor offsets hit unsupported Django negative slicing
body: The advanced branch intentionally sets start_offset = cursor.offset when it is negative and then evaluates queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet does not support negative indexing and raises ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported. The comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing is false. A crafted cursor with a negative offset (for example via Cursor.from_string, which accepts negative offsets) will cause a 500 instead of the advertised reverse pagination. The non-advanced is_prev fallthrough can also pass a negative offset.

title: Redis set-to-zset change breaks existing buffered segments and rolling deploys
body: The span buffer storage is changed from Redis SETs (SADD/SUNIONSTORE/SCARD/SSCAN) to sorted sets (ZADD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZCARD/ZSCAN), but the same span-buf:s:* keys are reused. Keys already buffered by the old code, and keys written by old consumers during a rolling deploy, are still SET type. New code executing ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZADD/ZSCAN on those keys, or old code executing S* commands on zsets, will get WRONGTYPE errors and affected segments will be lost or fail to flush. Use a versioned key namespace, a migration window, or otherwise prevent mixed-version access.

title: Eviction can remove the segment/root span and silently drops spans
body: The new cap calls zpopmin to remove the entries with the lowest end_timestamp_precise scores. Evicted spans are never flushed and there is no metric or log recording that data was dropped. If the segment/root span has the lowest score (possible with clock skew or particular is_segment spans), it can be evicted while has_root_span_key is still set, so the buffer later flushes a segment whose segment_id points to a missing root span and no span is marked is_segment. Eviction should preserve the segment span and at least account for/report evicted spans.

title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or Lua eviction behavior
body: The new OptimizedCursorPaginator is completely untested, and none of the changed span buffer tests exercises the new >1000 span zpopmin eviction branch in add-buffer.lua. This leaves the first-page datetime TypeError, negative-offset crash, and root-span eviction behavior uncaught, despite all being reachable in the newly added optimized endpoint path or normal buffer operation.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime fields
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", so self.key is "datetime" and getattr(item, self.key) returns a datetime.datetime. math.floor and math.ceil do not accept datetime values and raise TypeError, so any use of optimized pagination will fail with a 500. Additionally value_from_cursor returns cursor.value (an int) instead of converting it to a datetime like DateTimePaginator, so even if get_item_key were fixed, second-page cursors would compare a datetime column to an integer.

title: Advanced negative-offset pagination uses unsupported negative QuerySet slicing
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, start_offset is set to the negative cursor.offset and the code evaluates queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet slicing raises ValueError for negative start/stop offsets ("Negative indexing is not supported"). A client can supply a negative cursor offset, causing the endpoint to return 500 instead of paginating.

title: Redirect depth reduced from 10000 to 1000 can split deep span trees
body: The redirect-following loop now stops after ~1000 hops instead of 10000. For span trees deeper than that, the script writes a redirect for the deepest processed span to an intermediate set rather than the true root, so the segment will be flushed in pieces with incorrect or duplicate segment IDs. The previous comment explicitly noted the 10k limit could already fail to join; lowering it to 1k makes that failure much more likely for deep traces.

title: Eviction can drop the root span or other required spans before flush
body: The new zpopmin eviction trims the sorted set to 1000 members by score, but it runs before has_root_span is recorded and does not protect the root span payload. When batch insertion pushes a segment above 1000 members, zpopmin may remove the root span (e.g., when timestamps are equal, as in the tests, or when timestamps are out of order), while the has_root_span flag may still be set. The flushed segment can then be marked as having a root span but contain no segment span, yielding incomplete trace data with no error or metric.

title: Accidental gitlink/submodule added
body: The PR adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing only `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`. This is a gitlink (submodule pointer), not source code, and appears unrelated to the feature. Unless intentionally adding a submodule, this should be removed: it can break fresh clones/CI and will pin or update the parent repository unexpectedly.

title: Naive substring check misclassifies mixed/negated error queries
body: `_is_error_focused_query()` does a raw substring search for `event.type:error`. Queries such as `!event.type:error` or `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` contain that substring, so an allowlisted project on the discover dataset will be treated as error-focused and `count()` will be rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)`. Transactions either lack usable sample_weight or should be counted separately, so counts become wrong or the query fails. The filter must be parsed/validated to ensure the query actually selects only error events (for example, no negation or OR-mixing with transactions).

title: Upsampling decision uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` passes the outer `dataset` from the request, not the `scoped_dataset` that is actually being queried. For dashboard split logic this function is called with `split_dataset=discover` (and modified queries), while the outer dataset can be metrics/performance. The helper then evaluates against the wrong dataset and the original request query, so the split errors-only query can skip upsampling or be misclassified. Pass `scoped_dataset` and the local `query` down so the decision matches the query actually executed.

title: Accidental submodule pointer committed
body: A gitlink entry named `sentry-repo` is added, pointing to subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a, which is the base commit of this PR. This appears to be an accidentally committed git submodule; it will make the repository depend on an external/self-referential submodule, break checkouts/CI for other contributors, and is unrelated to the feature. It should be removed from the PR.

title: Cache key uses process-local hash()
body: The cache key uses Python's built-in `hash()` on sorted project IDs. Tuple hashing is randomized per interpreter process unless PYTHONHASHSEED is fixed, so different web workers/processes generate different keys for the same logical project set. This defeats cross-process caching, and `invalidate_upsampling_cache()` at line 73 deletes a different key than the one workers wrote, so invalidation is ineffective. Use a stable serialization such as `",".join(map(str, sorted(project_ids)))` instead of `hash(tuple(...))`.

title: Upsampling decision ignores the query actually being executed
body: `_get_event_stats` receives a `query` argument, but `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(..., request)` determines whether the query is error-focused from `request.GET["query"]` only. This endpoint calls `_get_event_stats` with different query strings for dashboard discover split logic, such as `errors_only_query = f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` and transaction-only queries. In those cases the actual query can be error-only or transaction-only while the decision is based on the original request query, so `count()` may be left untransformed for an errors-only split query or transformed for a transaction-only query, producing incorrect stats or Snuba errors. Pass the current `query` parameter into the helper and use it for the error-focus check.

title: Substring check misclassifies negated/mixed queries
body: `_is_error_focused_query` only checks whether `"event.type:error"` appears anywhere in the request query. A query like `!event.type:error` contains that substring but selects non-error/transaction events; similarly `event.type:transaction OR event.type:error` includes transactions. For the discover dataset this can enable `upsampled_count()` (`sum(sample_weight)`) on transaction rows where `sample_weight` is not available or meaningful, causing Snuba errors or wrong counts. Parse the actual event.type filter, including negation and OR, rather than doing a raw substring search.

title: toInt64 truncates fractional sample weights
body: The new `upsampled_count` aggregate wraps `sum(sample_weight)` in `toInt64`. Sample weights are floating-point when the sample rate is not a reciprocal integer (for example, client_sample_rate 0.3 gives weight 3.333...). `toInt64` truncates toward zero, so estimated counts are systematically undercounted by up to one per bucket, and small/fractional accumulations can become zero. Use rounding or keep the result as a number/float instead of truncating.

title: New aggregation relies on sample_weight but only sample_rate is populated
body: This PR adds a SnQL aggregate `upsampled_count()` defined as `sum(sample_weight)`, but the only data-population change is in `src/sentry/testutils/factories.py`, which sets `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` from `client_sample_rate`. Nothing in the PR sets or ensures `sample_weight` exists on error events. If `sample_weight` isn't already stored or derived by Snuba ingestion for all allowlisted events, `sum(sample_weight)` will be null/zero and the endpoint will return 0 instead of the upsampled count. Verify the production ingestion path populates `sample_weight`, or compute the weight from `sample_rate` in the aggregate.

title: Negated event.type:error filter is misclassified as error-focused
body: _is_error_focused_query checks `"event.type:error" in query.lower()`. This substring test also matches negated filters such as `!event.type:error` or `NOT event.type:error`, so a discover query that excludes errors can be treated as error-focused. For allowlisted projects the endpoint then replaces `count()` with `upsampled_count()`, which sums `sample_weight` instead of counting rows. For transaction/non-error events this produces wrong counts or fails if sample_weight is absent. Parse the query filter properly or at least reject `!`/`NOT` directly preceding the filter.

title: Upsampling eligibility uses outer dataset instead of actual scoped_dataset
body: In `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is called with the outer closure variable `dataset`, not the `scoped_dataset` argument that the function actually queries. `get_event_stats_factory` intentionally calls `_get_event_stats` with a different `split_dataset` (for example `discover` after a dashboard split or fallback), but the upsampling decision still uses the original dataset. This can apply or skip `upsampled_count()` based on the wrong dataset, returning inconsistent or incorrect counts in split-dashboard paths. The eligibility check should use `scoped_dataset`.

title: Accidental nested submodule/repository reference committed
body: The diff adds a Git gitlink/submodule file named `sentry-repo` pointing at commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a. This appears to be an accidental nested checkout or submodule reference and is unrelated to the feature. It should be removed before merge; committing it pollutes the repository and can confuse cloners, CI, and tooling that encounter the gitlink.

title: upsampled_count() only registered for discover dataset, but errors dataset path is enabled
body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQL function is added only to the discover dataset's function converter. However `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` explicitly returns true for the `errors` dataset, and the endpoint passes the transformed column `upsampled_count() as count` to `errors` query paths. If the errors dataset does not inherit this discover function converter, `errors.timeseries_query` or top-events errors queries will fail with an unknown/unsupported function. There are no tests in this PR for `dataset=errors`. Register the function for the errors query builder or restrict the transformation to datasets that support it, and add coverage.

title: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title but the helper is on CommitContextIntegration
body: The static helper `_truncate_title` is defined on `CommitContextIntegration`, but `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` (also in `CommitContextIntegration`) calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`. `PRCommentWorkflow` is the workflow class hierarchy, not `CommitContextIntegration`, so it does not inherit this helper. The GitHub/GitLab comment workflows call `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)`, which will also not resolve unless the workflow inherits the integration class. Consequence: generating suspect PR/MR comments crashes with AttributeError/NameError, breaking the suspect commit comment feature.

title: Feature-flagged table visualization ignores actual table data and renders an empty table
body: When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, the branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`. It does not pass `result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, or `fieldAliases`, so real query results are discarded. Once this flag is enabled, dashboard table widgets will show no rows or columns. The branch should build `columns` and `tableData` from the current `tableResults` entry and metadata.

title: Zipping error_ids with events.values() misaligns data when nodestore entries are missing
body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` does not guarantee a value for every requested key; missing entries are typically omitted. The list comprehension zips the original `error_ids` with `events.values()`, so if any intermediate event is absent from nodestore, every later event is paired with the wrong id/title/message. The subsequent `if data is not None` filter cannot repair this misalignment. Instead, iterate over `error_ids` and look up each corresponding `node_id` in the returned mapping, or otherwise preserve the key association.

title: Feature-flagged table visualization discards query results
body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the organization has `use-table-widget-visualization`, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`. It ignores `result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, `fieldAliases`, and the custom field renderers already computed for the widget, so every dashboard table widget for such organizations will show an empty table instead of its query results.

title: Mutual exclusion validation uses truthiness and misses zero values
body: `validate_timestamp` checks `if self.initial_data.get("age")`, and `validate_age` checks `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. Because `0` is falsy, a report containing both `age` and `timestamp` will be accepted when one of them is `0` (for example `timestamp: 0` and `age: 1`). The two spec formats are supposed to be mutually exclusive; use key presence (`"age" in self.initial_data`) instead of truthiness.

title: No-op migration references missing replacement migration
body: Both this migration and `0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py` have been changed to no-op functions with comments pointing to `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`, but no `0921` migration is included in this PR. If `0921` is not already present in the target branch, the saved-search-to-`GroupSearchView` conversion will never run while the no-op migrations are recorded as applied, leaving organization saved searches unconverted.

title: Feature-flagged table widgets render an empty table instead of query results
body: When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, this branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and a hard-coded empty `tableData` instead of using the available `fields`, `result.meta`, and `result.data`. Real query results are ignored, so any organization with this flag enabled would see blank table dashboard widgets. Either wire the real result into `TableWidgetVisualization` or remove this branch before enabling the flag.

title: Replay error timestamps and breadcrumb timestamps use incompatible units
body: `error_events` are populated from nodestore event data where `timestamp` is the absolute event timestamp, while replay segment breadcrumb `timestamp` values are relative seconds from the replay start. `gen_request_data` compares these directly with `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`, so real requests will interleave errors at the wrong position in the generated log stream, likely grouping all errors at the beginning or end. The unit test uses small values for both and therefore does not catch the unit mismatch. Normalize error timestamps to replay-relative time before merging.

title: User-controlled issue title is embedded unescaped in a Markdown link
body: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` formats `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE`, which wraps the raw issue title inside a Markdown link label: `[**{title}**]({url})`. `_truncate_title` only truncates and does not escape characters such as `]`, `(`, backticks, or newlines. An issue title from event data can break out of the link or inject Markdown into the bot's PR/merge-request comment. Sanitize or escape the title before placing it inside the link label.

title: Zero value for `age` or `timestamp` bypasses mutual-exclusion validation
body: The mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness: `validate_timestamp` does `if self.initial_data.get("age")`, and `validate_age` does the equivalent for `timestamp`. Since `0` is falsy, a report containing both `timestamp` and `age: 0` (or `timestamp: 0` and an age) passes both validators even though the two spec variants are supposed to be mutually exclusive. Use an explicit presence check such as `if "age" in self.initial_data` and add tests for zero values.

title: OAuth token exchange omits redirect_uri, causing GitHub OAuth to fail.
body: The token exchange request to GitHub's OAuth access token endpoint does not include the `redirect_uri` parameter, even though it was included in the authorization URL (line 407). GitHub requires that if `redirect_uri` was provided in the authorization request, the same value must be sent in the token exchange. Without it, GitHub returns an `error=redirect_uri_mismatch` and no access token, causing the installation pipeline to always fail. The token body will not contain `access_token`, leading to the generic error response. Must add `redirect_uri` to the data dict.

title: User mismatch check crashes when integration metadata lacks sender info.
body: The new check compares `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` but does not guard against missing `sender` key. Integrations created before this change, or created via the Sentry pipeline without receiving the GitHub installation webhook event, will not have `sender` in their metadata. This will raise a `KeyError`, causing a 500 Internal Server Error instead of a handled error response. The code should check for the presence of `sender` (and `sender.get("login")`) before accessing, and either skip validation or return a specific error.

title: get_user_info API call can raise unhandled exceptions.
body: After obtaining an access token, the code calls `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` without catching `ApiError` or other exceptions that may occur if the token is invalid, GitHub API is down, or network issues. This will propagate up and result in a 500 error instead of the intended friendly error page. Wrap the call in a try/except and return the error response on failure.

title: Unhandled exception when get_user_info fails
body: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is called without any try/except. If the GitHub API request fails (network error, rate limit, invalid token, etc.), the exception propagates, resulting in a 500 error instead of the graceful error page returned by the `error` function. This can happen during routine outages or transient failures, breaking the installation flow for users. Wrap this call in a try/except and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure.

title: KeyError when integration metadata lacks 'sender'
body: The code accesses `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` without checking that `"sender"` exists. Existing GitHub integrations created before this change may not have a `sender` field in their metadata, causing a KeyError and a 500 error during reinstallation for those users. Use a safe access like `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` or explicitly handle missing sender metadata (e.g., skip the check or fail with a clear message).

title: Regression: block reinstallation when Integration is not ACTIVE
body: The new query `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` and subsequent error return on DoesNotExist changes prior behavior. Previously, if an Integration existed with this external_id but was not linked to any OrganizationIntegration (e.g., after uninstall), the pipeline proceeded to `next_step()`. Now, if the Integration exists but its status is not ACTIVE (for example, DISABLED), the user receives an error and cannot complete installation. This can block legitimate reinstallation workflows where the Integration was disabled rather than deleted.

title: KeyError when integration metadata lacks sender
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes every active `Integration` has a `sender` object with a `login`. Integrations created before this change, and first-time installs where the installation webhook has not populated `state["sender"]`, do not have `metadata["sender"]` (see `build_integration`, which only adds it when `state.get("sender")` is truthy). When such an `Integration` exists but no `OrganizationIntegration` is attached to the current org, this path raises `KeyError` and returns a 500 instead of the intended GitHub installation failure page, breaking legitimate reinstallation or linking. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and explicitly handle the missing-sender case.

title: GitHub user validation is skipped for first-time installs
body: When `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist`, `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` returns `pipeline.next_step()` immediately, before the `github_authenticated_user` vs `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` comparison at lines 500-505. `build_integration` also only records `sender` if it was already present in pipeline state, so a normal first installation creates an integration with no sender metadata. Consequently, the PR's stated protection against an OAuth-authenticated GitHub user differing from the installing GitHub user is not enforced on the initial installation; it only applies once an `Integration` object already exists (usually via a webhook). An attacker can exploit the race or the normal first-install path where the webhook has not created/populated the integration before pipeline completion.

title: get_user_info errors are not handled and can crash install
