body: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is called outside the surrounding `try`/`except` that handles token-response parsing failures. `get_user_info` makes a GitHub API request and can raise `ApiError` on invalid tokens, rate limits, or network failures; similarly, `safe_urlopen` for the token exchange on line 423 is before the `try` block and can raise on connection failures. These exceptions propagate as a 500 instead of rendering the advertised `github-integration-failed` error page, contradicting the PR's goal of failing gracefully when GitHub authentication cannot be validated.

title: Default `queued` timestamp is evaluated at import time, not per instance
body: The dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, not when each AssignmentSource instance is created. Every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` value (including via `from_integration`) will share the same import-time timestamp, making the field useless for tracking when a source was actually queued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

title: `to_dict()` includes a datetime object that Celery's JSON serializer cannot handle
body: `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` calls `asdict(self)`, which includes the `queued` datetime object. `sync_group_assignee_outbound` then passes this dict to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)`. Celery's default JSON serializer cannot serialize datetime objects, so any inbound assignment/deassignment from an integration (where `assignment_source` is set) will raise a serialization error when enqueuing the outbound sync task, breaking the feature in production. The test suite likely does not catch this because tasks are executed synchronously in tests without going through Celery's serializer. The timestamp must be converted to a string (e.g., ISO format) or removed from the serialized dict.

title: Unconditionally passing `assignment_source` to `sync_assignee_outbound` may break existing integrations
body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` even when `parsed_assignment_source` is `None`. The abstract method signature in `IssueSyncIntegration` includes `**kwargs`, but concrete integration implementations may not accept an `assignment_source` keyword argument. Previously this kwarg was not passed, so adding it unconditionally can raise `TypeError` for integrations that do not define `**kwargs`. This is an API/contract break for third-party or existing integrations. Consider only passing the kwarg when it is not None, or ensuring all implementations accept **kwargs.

title: No test verifies that outbound sync still occurs for a different integration
body: The new test `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` only asserts that `sync_assignee_outbound` is not called when the source integration matches the target. It does not test that a different integration still receives the outbound sync. The PR's stated goal is to prevent cycles while still allowing other integrations to propagate changes, so a test covering the positive case for a non-matching integration would be valuable to prevent regressions where the filter becomes too broad.

title: queued timestamp is evaluated once at import time
body: The `queued` field defaults to `timezone.now()` at class definition time, so every `AssignmentSource` constructed without an explicit `queued` value shares the same module-import timestamp. If `queued` is meant to represent when each assignment source was queued, it will be wrong for all instances. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` or set it in `__post_init__` if a dynamic timestamp is intended.

title: Malformed assignment source disables cycle guard
body: `from_dict` swallows `ValueError` and `TypeError` and returns `None`. In `sync_assignee_outbound`, a non-empty malformed `assignment_source_dict` therefore becomes `None`, and `should_sync` cannot compare integration IDs, so the outbound sync to the originating integration is allowed. The guard should fail closed or retry if an assignment source was supplied but cannot be parsed; otherwise the sync loop this PR fixes can reappear if serialization or schema issues produce an invalid dict.

title: No coverage that non-matching source integrations still sync
body: The new `should_sync` guard is only tested for the matching source integration (`assert_not_called`) and for `assignment_source=None`. The comment in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` says other integrations should still propagate changes outward, but there is no test with an assignment source from integration A and an external issue linked to integration B asserting that `sync_assignee_outbound` is called. An overbroad comparison would pass the current tests and silently stop cross-integration sync.

title: Passing datetime via Celery kwargs may break inbound assignee sync
body: `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` uses `asdict`, which includes `queued` as a `datetime.datetime` object. This dict is passed as `assignment_source_dict` to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async`. With Celery's default JSON serializer (or Sentry's JSON-based task serialization), a raw datetime object cannot be serialized, causing an `EncodeError` at dispatch time. This breaks every inbound assignee sync that carries an `assignment_source` (the new code path), so the fix itself will fail in production.

title: Unconditionally passing `assignment_source` keyword may break existing integrations
body: The task now unconditionally passes `assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source` to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound`, even when `parsed_assignment_source` is `None`. Existing concrete integration implementations that follow the old task interface and do not accept an `**kwargs` or an explicit `assignment_source` keyword will raise `TypeError`, breaking outbound assignee sync for all flows that don't provide a source (e.g., manual assignments). The task should only pass this keyword when it is non-None, or all implementations must be updated to accept it.

title: `queued` default evaluated at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated at module import time, not at instantiation. All `AssignmentSource` instances created without an explicit `queued` share the same timestamp (the import time), which is usually incorrect for audit/logging purposes. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement its abstract methods: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. Because StatefulDetectorHandler is an ABC, MetricAlertDetectorHandler remains abstract. Detector.detector_handler calls group_type.detector_handler(self), and MetricAlertFire.detector_handler is MetricAlertDetectorHandler, so any attempt to use a metric alert detector will raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler. This is a regression from the previous DetectorHandler subclass that had a concrete evaluate method.

title: KeyError when StatefulDetectorHandler has no counter_names
body: In get_state_data, counter_updates is initialized to {} and only populated when self.counter_names is non-empty (lines 196-208). In the results loop, counter_updates=counter_updates[gk] unconditionally indexes that dict. If a concrete StatefulDetectorHandler returns an empty list for counter_names, counter_updates remains {} and this line raises KeyError for every group key, crashing evaluation. Subclasses that do not need counters should still get a default empty dict per group key.

title: Docstring still says evaluate returns a list
body: The StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring says "returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult" but the method now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult] after this PR. The documentation should be updated to avoid misleading future readers.

title: Test expected occurrence built with wrong group key causing test failure
body: In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe, the expected_result uses group_key="group_key" (line 540), but the IssueOccurrence for result is generated by build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...) on line 536. The actual evaluate_group_key_value call uses expected_result.group_key ("group_key"), so build_occurrence_and_event_data will produce an occurrence with fingerprint based on "group_key". DetectorEvaluationResult equality compares the IssueOccurrence fields including fingerprint, so the assertion will fail. The occurrence should be built with the same group_key ("group_key") as expected_result.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler remains abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler, which defines several abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data). The class body is just `pass` and does not implement any of these methods. As a result, the class itself is abstract and attempting to instantiate it will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. Since MetricAlertFire sets `detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler`, any Detector with type 'metric_alert_fire' will crash in `Detector.detector_handler` when `group_type.detector_handler(self)` is called. This will break the workflow engine for that detector type.

title: Test builds expected occurrence with wrong group key, causing assertion failure
body: In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe, the expected_result is constructed with an IssueOccurrence built using group_key "val1" (via build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...)), but evaluate_group_key_value is invoked with group_key "group_key". The handler's build_occurrence_and_event_data hook will produce an occurrence whose fingerprint is based on "group_key", so the actual result's occurrence fingerprint differs from the expected one. IssueOccurrence is a dataclass and equality includes all fields, so the assertion `handler.evaluate_group_key_value(...) == expected_result` will fail. The expected occurrence should be built with the same group_key ("group_key") as used in the evaluation.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler does not implement StatefulDetectorHandler abstract methods
body: The class inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only has `pass`, so it remains abstract and cannot be instantiated. Any Detector whose `type` slug is 'metric_alert_fire' will trigger `group_type.detector_handler(self)` in models/detector.py, which will raise TypeError when trying to instantiate this handler, breaking metric alert detection. The new abstract methods `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` must be implemented, or the class must be explicitly marked as abstract and not assigned as a detector_handler.

title: process_detectors silently overwrites duplicate group keys instead of logging
body: The previous code used a set to detect duplicate group keys and logged an error, skipping subsequent duplicates. After changing to a dict, if `handler.evaluate` returns multiple results with the same group key, the later one overwrites the earlier without any log. This can cause loss of evaluation results and hide bugs in detector implementations. Consider logging a warning when overwriting or retaining explicit duplicate detection.

title: Docstring still says evaluate returns a list
body: The docstring for `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` says "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`" but the return type is now `dict`. Update the docstring to avoid confusion.

title: Breaking change to process_detectors and evaluate return types
body: Changing the return type of `process_detectors` from `list[tuple[Detector, list[DetectorEvaluationResult]]]` to `list[tuple[Detector, dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]]]` and changing the abstract method `DetectorHandler.evaluate` signature from returning a list to a dict is a public API break. Any existing callers of `process_detectors` or subclasses of `DetectorHandler` outside this PR will break. Ensure all consumers are updated or provide backwards compatibility.

title: get_monitor_environment_context returns unmodified monitor config
body: The function copies monitor_environment.monitor.config into the local variable `config` and conditionally updates `schedule_type` to its display value, but then returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original, unmodified dict) instead of `config`. As a result, the occurrence context contains the raw schedule_type value rather than the human-readable display. This appears to be an accidental leftover from the move; the function should return `config`.

title: get_monitor_environment_context returns original config, discarding schedule_type conversion
body: The function copies `monitor_environment.monitor.config` into `config` and conditionally replaces `config["schedule_type"]` with the human-readable display value, but the returned context uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of `config`. The conversion is therefore never applied, so the produced monitor issue occurrence context will contain the raw schedule_type value rather than the display value that the code clearly intends to emit.

title: get_monitor_environment_context returns the raw config instead of the converted copy
body: The function creates a local `config` copy and converts `schedule_type` to its display value, but the returned dictionary uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of `config`. The converted value is therefore discarded, and the occurrence event context contains the raw internal `schedule_type` rather than the human-readable value. Line 168 should return `config`.

title: Plural failure reason repeats "check-ins"
body: `get_failure_reason` builds strings such as "3 missed check-ins" and then formats them with `"%(problem_checkins)s check-ins detected"`, producing "3 missed check-ins check-ins detected". The docstring examples show the intended output without the duplicated "check-ins", and this is user-facing evidence text. The final format string should not append "check-ins" after labels that already contain it.

title: Spawned flusher processes are never killed or terminated because the isinstance check targets the wrong process class
body: SpanFlusher creates workers with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process (line 53). On Linux, that returns SpawnProcess instances, which are not instances of top-level multiprocessing.Process (the default context's process class). Therefore the new guard `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` at line 254 is false for real flusher processes. In `_ensure_processes_alive`, a hung worker is not killed before `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement, so two workers can concurrently own and flush the same shards, creating duplicate or lost segments. The same predicate at line 346 also prevents `join()` from terminating spawned workers on shutdown. Use the spawn context's process class/BaseProcess, or remove the isinstance check as the previous code did.

title: Negative flusher_processes silently starts no flusher workers
body: The `--flusher-processes` CLI option accepts any int and no positive-value validation is performed. If `max_processes` is negative, `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` becomes negative, `process_to_shards_map` and the process/backpressure/healthy dictionaries are all empty, and no flusher processes are created. Backpressure and memory checks then iterate over empty dictionaries, so `submit` never raises and the consumer keeps committing while spans are never flushed. Validate that `flusher_processes` is at least 1 (for example with click.IntRange(min=1)) before constructing SpanFlusher.

title: Spawned flusher processes never match multiprocessing.Process, so hung workers are not killed before restart
body: Processes are created via `self.mp_context.Process` after `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, so they are `SpawnProcess` instances. `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` checks against the default context process and is false for them. Therefore in `_ensure_processes_alive` a process that is stuck/hung is not killed before `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement, leaving two flushers on the same Redis shards; they can concurrently call `flush_segments`/`done_flush_segments` and produce duplicate segments or corrupt the buffer state. The same wrong check at line 346 also means `join()` never terminates a live spawned process on timeout. Use `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` (or the spawn context's process class) or call `kill`/`terminate` unconditionally for processes.

title: New flusher_processes argument inserted before produce_to_pipe breaks positional callers
body: `flusher_processes` was added before the existing `produce_to_pipe` parameter. Existing callers that instantiate `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` with the old positional order (e.g. passing `produce_to_pipe` as the sixth argument) will now pass a callable as `flusher_processes`; `SpanFlusher` will then use it as `max_processes` and fail or misbehave. The default is also `None`, which makes direct construction spawn one flusher per assigned shard instead of the CLI's documented default of 1. Append the new keyword after `produce_to_pipe` (or make it keyword-only) and consider defaulting to 1.

title: join() stops processing the process list when the timeout expires, leaking remaining flusher processes
body: When `timeout` is provided, the loop over `self.processes` breaks as soon as `remaining_time <= 0` is seen for one process. The earlier `self.next_step.join(timeout)` can consume the entire deadline, so the loop may break before calling `terminate` on any spawned flusher or before reaching later processes. A process stuck in `future.result()`, Redis work, or produce can therefore outlive shutdown and keep flushing shards. Iterate over all processes and terminate each after the deadline rather than breaking out.

title: --flusher-processes accepts negative values and disables flushing
body: The option is `type=int` with no lower-bound validation. In `SpanFlusher`, `max_processes=-1` is truthy, so `self.num_processes = min(-1, len(assigned_shards))` is negative and `range(self.num_processes)` is empty; no flusher process is started. Spans are then written into Redis without any worker flushing them or setting backpressure, eventually filling Redis and stalling segment delivery. Validate `min=1` or clamp/raise in `SpanFlusher`.

title: Multiprocess flusher path is not exercised by tests
body: Both flusher tests pass `produce_to_pipe`, which causes `SpanFlusher` to create `threading.Thread` workers instead of the new `spawn` `Process` workers. The production path (`produce_to_pipe=None`) is untested, so issues with spawn pickling and the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` mismatch can pass CI. Add a test that runs `SpanFlusher` without `produce_to_pipe` for more than one process/shards, ideally with a fake Redis buffer and Kafka producer removed/patched.

title: join() can return without waiting for or terminating flusher processes on timeout
body: When join() is called with a finite timeout, that timeout is first consumed by self.next_step.join(timeout). Then the process loop computes remaining_time. If it is <= 0, the loop breaks at line 341 before reaching process.terminate() for that and all later processes. Because stop was signaled but child processes may still be producing or waiting on Kafka futures, join() can return while flusher processes are still alive, overlapping with shutdown/rebalance. The previous code always terminated the single process at the end regardless of deadline. The loop should not break out of the entire process iteration without terminating each process, or remaining timeout should be preserved/reset before processing children.

title: max_processes=0 is treated as one process per shard due to `or`
body: The expression `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats 0 as unset, so `--flusher-processes=0` spawns one process per assigned shard instead of limiting the flusher to zero processes. Since Click accepts any int and there is no validation, an operator intending to disable or zero out the flusher gets the opposite resource-heavy behavior. Use an explicit `is None` check or validate the CLI value. Negative values also pass through and can make `process_to_shards_map` empty, disabling flushing entirely.

title: New parameter inserted before existing `produce_to_pipe` breaks positional callers
body: ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__ previously ended with `produce_to_pipe`; the new `flusher_processes` parameter is inserted before it. Any existing caller that passed the test/produce callback positionally (for example, ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(..., my_pipe)) now binds that callable or list to flusher_processes and leaves produce_to_pipe as None. This can change behavior from the thread-based test path to spawning Kafka-producing processes, or fail later when flusher_processes is used as an int. Preserve positional compatibility by appending new parameters after existing ones, or update all call sites.

title: Added wait is a no-op and leaves test race-prone
body: The test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to a no-op at line 15. The new `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 therefore does not give the flusher thread any time, contrary to the comment. The assertion that the message was produced depends on a race between the background flusher thread seeing `current_drift` and `join()` setting stopped. Use a real wait or explicit synchronization, or do not monkeypatch `time.sleep` before this wait.

title: Strategy close shuts down the shared queue pool, breaking rebalances and losing messages
body: `ResultsStrategyFactory` creates one `FixedQueuePool` in its constructor and passes that same pool to every `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` created by `create_with_partitions`. On Kafka partition revocation/reassignment, Arroyo closes the previous strategy, and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`. This shuts down worker threads and queues that are owned by the long-lived factory. The next strategy created from that factory then submits to a shut-down pool: `work_queue.put()` raises `queue.ShutDown`, which is caught by the broad `except Exception` in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`, and the offset is marked complete without ever invoking `result_processor`. Messages are silently skipped and their offsets are committed. The pool lifecycle should be separated from the per-assignment strategy lifecycle.

title: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure and can exhaust memory
body: Each queue in `FixedQueuePool` is created as `queue.Queue()` with no max size. The strategy docstring claims 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', but these queues never fill up. If one group's worker is slow or processing stalls, that queue can grow without bound, consuming all available memory and allowing consumer lag to grow indefinitely. Use a bounded `Queue(maxsize=...)` and handle `QueueFull`, or otherwise bound pending work so backpressure is actually exerted on the Arroyo submit loop.

title: Failed result processing still completes the offset and allows commit
body: `OrderedQueueWorker.run` catches any exception from `result_processor`, logs it, and then the `finally` block always calls `offset_tracker.complete_offset`. This means an unexpected failure that escapes `ResultProcessor.__call__` is treated as successfully processed; the commit loop later commits past it. The message is never retried and is not routed to a DLQ. The worker should only complete the offset when processing succeeds, or explicitly mark poison messages for the configured DLQ path.

title: Unexpected submit-time failures mark the message complete, silently skipping it
body: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`, any exception from `decoder`, `grouping_fn`, or work-item construction is caught, logged, and then the offset is both added and completed. As a result, a message that cannot be decoded or grouped due to a bug is committed and never processed instead of propagating to Arroyo's error/DLQ handling. This can cause silent loss of subscription results. Only the explicit `decoder` returning `None` case should be skipped; unexpected exceptions should not complete the offset.

title: Invalid or zero max_workers silently creates 20 queues
body: `num_queues=max_workers or 20` means `0`, negative values, and other falsy values all become 20 worker threads. Passing `--max-workers 0` or a negative value unexpectedly starts 20 threads instead of being rejected. `max_workers` should be explicitly validated as a positive integer when `mode` is `thread-queue-parallel`.

title: Message loss when queue submission fails after offset is added
body: In SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit, the broad except block catches any exception, including one raised by queue_pool.submit. FixedQueuePool.submit first records the offset as outstanding via add_offset, then attempts work_queue.put. If put raises (e.g., because the queue has been shut down during consumer shutdown), the exception propagates here, and the handler marks the same offset as completed. Since the item was never enqueued or processed, the offset will later be committed by the commit loop, permanently losing that message. This can happen during graceful shutdown or after queue shutdown is initiated while the producer is still submitting.

title: Offsets are completed even when processing raises an exception
body: In OrderedQueueWorker.run, the finally block unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset after result_processor is invoked. If result_processor raises (e.g., a transient database error not caught internally), the offset is still marked complete and will be committed by the commit loop, causing the message to be skipped without successful processing. The class docstring claims 'Only commits offsets after successful processing', but this implementation commits after any outcome, including failure. While ResultProcessor.__call__ currently swallows exceptions, this strategy may be reused with other result processors that do not, leading to silent data loss.

title: Multiple commit threads share a single OffsetTracker without coordination
body: FixedQueuePool is stored on ResultsStrategyFactory and reused across calls to create_with_partitions, so multiple SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy instances can exist simultaneously (e.g., during rebalancing or assignment changes). Each strategy starts its own commit thread in __init__, and all threads operate on the same queue_pool.offset_tracker. They concurrently call get_committable_offsets and mark_committed. While per-partition locks prevent most corruption, multiple threads may compute the same committable offsets before either marks them committed, leading to duplicate Kafka commits and potential race conditions when one thread updates last_committed while another is still using the old snapshot. This is redundant and can increase commit load; it should be centralized or the tracker should be locked across the entire commit operation.

title: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure
body: FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize, so queues are unbounded. The class docstring claims 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', but there is no fill limit. A slow subscription group can accumulate an unlimited number of work items, leading to unbounded memory growth and potentially crashing the consumer. Consider using a bounded queue with a maximum size and applying backpressure in submit.

title: num_queues can be negative or zero due to unvalidated max_workers
body: In ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ for thread-queue-parallel mode, num_queues=max_workers or 20. If max_workers is a negative integer (e.g., -5), it is truthy, so num_queues becomes -5, resulting in range(-5) producing no queues and no workers. The consumer will accept messages but never process them, and offsets will remain outstanding indefinitely, causing a stall. The CLI option is an arbitrary int with no validation. A positive integer check should be added.

title: get_committable_offsets can be O(n) per commit tick
body: OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets iterates over every integer from last_committed+1 to max_offset for each partition. If there is a large gap (e.g., a stuck message) and many offsets have been accumulated, this range can be very large and the loop executes repeatedly every second in the commit thread. This may cause CPU spikes and delay commits. Consider tracking the next expected offset or using a min-heap of completed offsets to find contiguous runs more efficiently.

title: Queue pool is shut down by the per-assignment strategy and then reused after rebalance
body: `ResultsStrategyFactory` creates one `FixedQueuePool` and stores it on the factory. Arroyo can call `create_with_partitions` again on this same factory after a partition assignment/rebalance. However, `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, which permanently shuts down the queues and worker threads owned by the factory. On the next assignment, `create_with_partitions` reuses the already-shutdown pool. New submits will call `put()` on a shutdown queue, raise `queue.ShutDown`, be caught by the broad `except` in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`, and the offset will still be marked complete. This means messages are dropped and their Kafka offsets are advanced without processing after any rebalance. The queue pool should either be created per assignment or `close()` must not shut down the factory-owned pool.

title: Offsets are completed even when result processing fails
body: In `OrderedQueueWorker.run`, `self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)` is in the `finally` block. If `result_processor` raises, the offset is still marked completed and can be committed by `_commit_loop`. This contradicts the strategy's guarantee that offsets are only committed after successful processing: a transient or programming failure can cause the message to be lost forever once Kafka commits past it. The same commit-on-error behavior exists in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`'s broad exception handler. `complete_offset` should only be called on successful processing, or failed items must be explicitly marked as non-committable.

title: Uses queue.Queue.shutdown / queue.ShutDown, which are Python 3.13+ APIs
body: `Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were added in Python 3.13. On Python 3.11/3.12 runtimes, `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` reaches `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`, which raises `AttributeError`; that is caught and logged, but workers are never unblocked with a `ShutDown` exception. The thread-queue-parallel consumer can then hang on shutdown until each worker join times out. This feature must either avoid these APIs or the runtime baseline and CI matrix must be explicitly upgraded to Python 3.13+.

title: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure and can exhaust memory
body: Each per-group queue is created as `queue.Queue()` with the default `maxsize=0`, meaning it is unbounded. The class docstring claims "natural backpressure when queues fill up," but because the queues never fill, the Kafka polling thread will keep enqueueing items for a slow group without bound. Under sustained slowness or a stalled subscription, this can grow memory until the consumer process is OOM-killed. Use bounded queues or otherwise block/stop polling when queue depth exceeds a configured threshold.

title: Graceful shutdown stops the commit loop before draining and committing queued work
body: `close()` sets `shutdown_event` and joins `commit_thread` before `queue_pool.shutdown()` drains queued work. Messages completed during pool shutdown therefore have no commit loop left to commit them. Additionally, `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` sets each worker's `shutdown` flag before calling `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`, so a worker woken from `get()` processes at most one more item and then exits the `while not self.shutdown` loop, leaving the rest of the queue undrained. The result is that successfully processed messages near shutdown may not be committed, causing duplicate reprocessing after restart (and making `wait_until_empty` unused despite existing for this purpose).

title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so a code can be used twice or resurrected
body: The new backup-code login branch decrypts `user.backupCodes` into an array, nulls the matched entry (`backupCodes[index] = null`) and then writes the whole re-encrypted array back with `prisma.user.update`. This is a read-modify-write with no transaction or conditional update. Two login requests that arrive concurrently with the same code both match it and both return success, so the "each backup code can be used exactly once" guarantee advertised in `backup_code_instructions` is not enforced. Worse, two concurrent requests with *different* codes each write back a list derived from the same original snapshot, so the last write wins and the code consumed by the other request is silently restored and becomes reusable. Because an attacker typically does not need parallelism, this is not trivially exploitable, but the single-use property of a security credential must hold under concurrency. Suggested fix: perform the removal atomically (e.g. a `updateMany` guarded on the exact previous encrypted value, or a transaction with a row lock / `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`), or store codes as individual rows and delete by id/`deleteMany`.

title: onEnable is only fired from the backup-codes Close button, so dismissing the dialog otherwise leaves 2FA state stale
body: Before this change `onEnable()` was called as soon as the enable API returned 200. Now enablement is only reported to the parent from the `backup-codes-close` button (`resetState(); onEnable();`). The dialog is controlled by the parent and Radix closes it on Escape (and on other dismissal paths) via `onOpenChange`, none of which call `onEnable` or `resetState`. Consequence: a user who enables 2FA and closes the dialog with Escape gets a server state where 2FA is enabled, while the settings page still shows the toggle as unchecked; if they retry, `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup` answers `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled` and they get a generic "something went wrong" error. The internal `step` also stays on `DisplayBackupCodes`, so re-opening the modal later shows the old backup-code screen instead of the password step. `onEnable` should be invoked (and state reset) whenever the dialog is dismissed after a successful enable, not only from one button.

title: Backup-code input is not normalized, so auto-capitalized or whitespace-pasted codes are rejected
body: The new backup-code input is a plain `TextField` with no `autoCapitalize="none"`/`autoCorrect="off"`/`spellCheck={false}`. Codes are generated as lowercase hex (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`) and the server-side match is an exact, case-sensitive `array.indexOf(value)` after only stripping `-` (`next-auth-options.ts:144` and `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61`). On mobile (and iOS Safari in particular) a text input auto-capitalizes the first character, so typing the code shown on screen produces a mismatch and "Backup code is incorrect" — precisely in the lost-access recovery path where the user has no other way in. Pasting a code with surrounding whitespace fails for the same reason. Add the input attributes and/or `trim()`/`toLowerCase()` the value before comparing.

title: missing_backup_codes message tells users to generate codes in settings, which is impossible
body: The new `missing_backup_codes` string reads "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." but no such setting exists: backup codes are only produced by `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup`, which returns `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled` for any user who already has 2FA on, and there is no UI to regenerate them. Every user who enabled 2FA before this migration (`backupCodes` is `NULL`) and then clicks "Lost access" will follow the advice, find nothing, and be stuck. Either provide a regenerate-codes entry point in the 2FA settings section or change the text to describe what the user can actually do (e.g. disable and re-enable 2FA).

title: No test covers logging in with a backup code or its single-use behaviour
body: The PR's core security behaviours are untested. The added assertions only verify that the download produces a file named `cal-backup-codes.txt`, that the copy button shows a toast, and that Close works (`// TODO: check file content`, `// TODO: check clipboard content`), and a `// TODO: add more backup code tests` is left behind. Nothing exercises: logging in via "Lost access" with a real code, rejection of a wrong code, the fact that a consumed code cannot be reused (the guarantee the UI copy makes), or disabling 2FA with a backup code. Since the consumption logic lives in `next-auth-options.ts` and is exactly the part that can silently regress (including the concurrency issue above), at least a happy-path login-with-backup-code test and a reuse-rejection test should be added before merge.

title: New `required` on the password field blocks disabling 2FA for accounts with no password
body: `required` was added to the password `PasswordField`. The field is rendered whenever the caller doesn't pass `disablePassword` (the default), and the API deliberately treats the password as optional: `disable.ts` only verifies it `if (user.password && user.identityProvider === IdentityProvider.CAL)`. Accounts that have 2FA enabled but no password (e.g. a user who set up 2FA while using CAL credentials and later signed in with Google, which nulls `password`, or SAML/Google accounts with 2FA) can legitimately disable 2FA server-side, but the browser now refuses to submit the form with an empty required field, so they are blocked in the UI. The client-side constraint should mirror the server rule (e.g. only mark it required when the account actually has a password).

title: Third-party identity-provider guard makes backup codes unusable for OAuth accounts with 2FA
body: The existing guard `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode) throw new Error(ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled)` runs before the new backup-code branch. A user with a GOOGLE/SAML identity provider who has 2FA enabled necessarily submits a backup code with an empty `totpCode`, so they always hit this error and can never use their backup codes, even though `loginWithTotp` routes such users through the 2FA login page. Either the guard should also accept a supplied `backupCode`, or the limitation should be made explicit (and the UI should not offer a path that can never succeed) — as written, the feature silently does not apply to that group of 2FA users.

title: Backup-code login bypasses password and IdP checks when totpCode is supplied
body: The new backup-code branch only checks credentials.backupCode. The existing password guard at line 121 runs only when !credentials.totpCode, and the identity-provider guards at lines 113 and 117 are also skipped when totpCode is truthy. An attacker who obtains a valid backup code can submit email, backupCode, and any non-empty totpCode; the request skips password and IdP validation, takes the backup-code branch, consumes the code, and authenticates the user. A single leaked backup code is therefore enough for account takeover. Require password or an equivalent trusted first-factor proof for the backup-code path and do not let an arbitrary totpCode value disable the earlier checks.

title: Backup-code consumption is racy and permits replay or reinstatement
body: The branch reads the encrypted backup-code list, sets one element to null, and writes the whole list back with no transaction, row lock, or conditional update. Two concurrent requests using the same code can both read the old list and both succeed, so a one-time code can be replayed. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's deletion and reinstate the other code. Use an atomic operation, such as a row lock plus verify-and-update or one row per hashed code with a usedAt conditional update, and add a concurrency test.

title: Closing the backup-codes step by dialog dismissal skips onEnable and leaves UI stale
body: After the enable API succeeds, handleEnable now only moves to SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes and no longer calls onEnable. onOpenChange at line 166 is passed straight through to Dialog, and onEnable is called only from the Close button at line 269. If the user closes with Escape, the X button, or the backdrop, 2FA is already enabled in the database but the parent is never notified; the settings switch can remain off and the user may try to enable 2FA again. Call the success callback when enabling succeeds and/or handle closing from this step explicitly.

title: 2FA enable assertion does not actually validate the switch and ignores the new backup-codes step
body: The added FIXME acknowledges that isChecked() passes even when the switch is not checked. With the new flow, after submitting the TOTP code the modal remains on the backup-codes step and onEnable/switch refresh does not happen until that step is closed. This test never closes the step, so the assertion is either false/flaky or, as the FIXME says, passing for the wrong reason. Use the data-state=checked assertion after closing backup codes, or otherwise explicitly complete the new step.

title: No e2e coverage for backup-code login or one-time-use behavior
body: The only new test interactions are downloading, copying, and closing the backup-code display. The TODO at line 12 explicitly defers backup-code login and disabling tests. The PR adds security-critical branches in next-auth-options and the disable endpoint, including single-use consumption, with no automated coverage. Add tests that log in with a backup code, assert the same code fails the second time, and disable 2FA with a backup code.

title: Missing-backup-codes message is not actionable for existing 2FA users
body: The new missing_backup_codes copy tells users to generate codes in settings, but the only generation path is the TOTP setup endpoint, which returns TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled once 2FA is enabled. Existing 2FA users with a null backupCodes column therefore reach a dead end from this message; they must disable and re-enable 2FA. Add an authenticated regeneration flow or change the message to reflect the actual recovery path.

title: Password visibility toggle is removed from keyboard navigation
body: Adding tabIndex={-1} to the password show/hide button makes the control unreachable by keyboard. Users who rely on keyboard navigation can no longer reveal the password they are typing, and this affects every PasswordField in the app. If the goal was to prevent focus stealing, use a visually hidden alternative or keep the button focusable.

title: Backup-code login can bypass password verification
body: The new backup-code branch is entered whenever `credentials.backupCode` is present, but the password check above only runs when `user.password && !credentials.totpCode`. This branch never validates `credentials.totpCode`, so an attacker who knows a valid backup code can POST credentials containing the victim email, the backup code, and any arbitrary non-empty `totpCode` (for example `000000`) without the password. Password verification is skipped, the backup code is accepted, and the attacker is logged in. A backup code must not replace the password factor; verify the password whenever backupCode is supplied, or explicitly validate only the selected factor while still requiring the password.

title: One-time backup codes can be reused concurrently
body: Consuming a backup code is implemented as a read-modify-write of the encrypted backup-code array: the request reads `user.backupCodes`, finds the matching index, sets that element to null, and writes the entire array back. Two concurrent login requests using the same code can both read the original array and both write their own nulled copy, so both requests succeed and the supposedly single-use code is accepted twice. Use a transaction/row lock or an atomic conditional update keyed on the ciphertext that was read so only one request can consume a given code.

title: Closing backup-codes screen via dialog X skips onEnable and loses codes
body: After `handleEnable` succeeds, 2FA is already enabled on the server and the modal switches to `DisplayBackupCodes`. Only the explicit Close button calls `onEnable()` and `resetState()`. Closing via the dialog's X, Escape, or outside click calls `onOpenChange` directly, so the settings switch is not updated, the component can reopen on the stale backup-codes step, and the user may leave without ever seeing or saving the only copy of the backup codes. Any dismissal while on `DisplayBackupCodes` should either commit the enable state and reset state, or be blocked until the user confirms they have saved the codes.

title: No coverage for actual backup-code login, consumption, or disable flow
body: The added e2e assertions only check that the download has the expected filename and that a copy-success toast appears; the file contents and clipboard contents are explicitly left as TODO. There is no test that logs in with a backup code, rejects an invalid code, verifies a used code cannot be reused, or disables 2FA using a backup code. These are the security-critical paths added by this PR, and a regression in code formatting, one-time consumption, or either server endpoint would currently pass the tests.

title: Copy button shows success toast even when clipboard write fails
body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a promise that can reject when clipboard permission is denied or the API is unavailable, but the promise is neither awaited nor caught and the success toast is shown unconditionally. Users can be told the backup codes were copied when nothing was copied, or an unhandled rejection can be produced. Await the clipboard write and show the success toast only after it resolves, with an error fallback.

title: Password visibility toggle is ineffective after switching to PasswordField
body: `PasswordField` sets its own `type` based on `isPasswordVisible` before spreading `{...props}`, so passing `type="password"` here overrides that dynamic value. Clicking the eye button changes the visibility state but the input remains `type="password"`, making the newly added visibility control non-functional in the enable-2FA modal. Remove the explicit `type` prop when using `PasswordField`, or change `PasswordField` so caller props cannot override its visibility-driven type.

title: Password visibility toggle removed from keyboard navigation
body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the password visibility button removes it from the keyboard tab order. Keyboard-only users can no longer focus the control to reveal or re-hide the password, which is an accessibility regression for every `PasswordField` in the application. Keep the button focusable, or provide an equivalent keyboard-accessible way to toggle visibility.

title: Dereference of undefined destination calendar for Google Meet fallback
body: When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array (now a valid state and produced by several callers), destructuring yields `undefined`, but the next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`. Creating any event with `location === MeetLocationType` and no destination calendar throws before bookings/emails are created. Use optional chaining or check for a destination before reading `.integration`.

title: Video meeting references lose credentialId
body: For non-calendar results (`isCalendarType` false), the new code sets `credentialId: undefined`; previously it preserved `result.credentialId`. Video meeting creation returns a credential id, and downstream cancellation code only deletes a video reference when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so video meetings can be left behind on cancellation/reschedule. Preserve `result.credentialId` for video results.

title: Location updates create calendar references without calendar linkage
body: `updateLocation` now builds references from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` does not populate either field (it returns only appName/type/success/uid/updatedEvent/originalEvent/calError/calWarnings). Every location edit therefore creates calendar references with null `credentialId` and `externalCalendarId`, so later cancellation/reschedule can target the wrong calendar or all credentials. Populate these fields in updateEvent or derive them from the destination calendar.

title: Stale credential reused when a multi-host credential lookup fails
body: Inside the new loop over calendar references, `credential` is declared outside the loop and only overwritten when the in-memory or DB lookup succeeds. If a later reference's credential is missing, `credential` still holds the previous reference's credential and is passed to `updateEvent` with the current reference's uid/externalCalendarId, potentially updating the wrong calendar. Reset/skip when no credential is found.

title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar event
body: The PR now supports multiple calendar references, but the `newBookingId` merge branch still uses `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes only one old calendar event. Collective bookings can have references for several hosts, so old events for all but the first host remain on their calendars after a reschedule/merge. Iterate over all calendar references when deleting old events.

title: Google Calendar fallback compares externalId to a null externalCalendarId
body: In `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`, when `externalCalendarId` is falsy the code does `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, i.e. compares calendar ids to null/undefined. That never matches. `updateEvent` then calls Google with an undefined calendarId and `deleteEvent` falls back to `primary`, so events on a non-primary destination calendar are updated/deleted on the wrong calendar or fail. Use the matching destination for the current credential, or at least the first destination, when no external id is supplied.

title: Google insert patches hangout link with undefined calendarId
body: The insert call uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || 'primary'`, but the subsequent hangout-link patch uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without the fallback. When no destination calendar matches the credential, the event is created on primary but the patch is sent with an undefined calendarId, so the hangout link/description is not patched and the unawaited call can reject. Use the same fallback for both calls.

title: Collective co-host calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor organizer has a destination calendar. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so destination calendars collected from co-hosts are discarded. A collective host with a calendar will not get an event if the organizer has none. Initialize to `[]` before pushing.

title: Office365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
body: EventManager calls createEvent once per destination credential, but Office365's createEvent reads `event.destinationCalendar[0]` and uses that calendar for every call. With two Office365 hosts, both calls create the event on the first host's calendar (or fail for the second credential), so additional hosts never get the event and the first can get duplicates. Select the destination belonging to the current credential (pass credentialId/externalId) instead of index 0.

title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
body: Lark's createEvent derives the calendar id from `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. EventManager invokes the service for each destination credential, so a second Lark host's event is created against the first host's calendar id, likely failing due to permissions or writing into the wrong calendar. Use the destination matching the current credential rather than the first array entry.

title: CalDAV createEvent filters all calendars by the first destination
body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters calendars using only `event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId`. When a collective booking has multiple CalDAV destinations, every invocation filters to that first calendar, so other hosts' calendars never receive an event and the first calendar can receive duplicates. Select the destination for the current credential or pass the target externalId into createEvent.

title: Recurring collective cancellation ignores non-organizer credentials
body: The outer loop now iterates every calendar reference, but the recurring cancellation branch still builds its work from `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and picks the first calendar reference per updated booking. Co-hosts' credentials are not in the organizer's `credentials`, and their per-reference ids are ignored, so recurring collective bookings leave calendar events on co-host calendars. Delete using each reference's own credential/external id.

title: Organization slug logic is inverted
body: This unrelated change flips `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`. With billing disabled (self-hosted), organizations are now created without a slug; with billing enabled, both `slug` and `requestedSlug` are set before domain verification. Restore the original conditions unless this behavior change is intentional and covered.

title: Meet fallback dereferences undefined destination calendar
body: When evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined, but the code reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration unconditionally. Any Google Meet event without a destination calendar now throws a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use optional chaining or check the main host destination before reading integration.

title: Organization slug creation condition is inverted
body: This changes the original !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED slug condition to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED. As a result, non-billing deployments create organizations without a slug, and billing-enabled deployments create a slug immediately instead of only storing requestedSlug. This is unrelated to destinationCalendar and breaks organization creation/routing.

title: Non-Google calendar services still use only the first destination calendar
body: EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now calls createEvent once per destination calendar and passes the full multi-host CalendarEvent. GoogleCalendarService resolves the destination by credentialId, but Office365CalendarService still takes event.destinationCalendar[0] and builds /me/calendars/{first.externalId}/events using whichever credential is being processed. For a collective booking, the second host's Office365 credential can be used with the first host's calendar id, causing a 404 or creation in the wrong calendar. The same first-element logic remains in LarkCalendarService.createEvent and BaseCalendarService.createEvent, so the multi-host fix is incomplete for those integrations.

title: Updated location references lose calendar credential and external id
body: EventManager.updateLocation now builds references from result.externalId and result.credentialId, but CalendarManager.updateEvent's return value does not include either field. editLocation persists these references, so newly created BookingReferences have null credentialId and externalCalendarId. Future cancellation or reschedule then cannot identify the correct calendar credential/event. Add those fields in CalendarManager.updateEvent or derive them from the destination/credential being updated.

title: Collective team destination calendars are dropped when main destination is null
body: For a collective booking where neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is set to null. The following optional push is then skipped, so teamDestinationCalendars collected from other hosts is discarded. If only a non-organizer host has a connected calendar, that host receives no calendar event. Initialize destinationCalendar to [] when collecting team destinations.

title: Google update/delete fallback compares externalId to itself
body: When externalCalendarId is null or empty, this find compares cal.externalId to null/undefined, so selectedCalendar becomes undefined. The previous code fell back to event.destinationCalendar.externalId. Google update now calls events.update with calendarId undefined (error), and deleteEvent at line 317 falls back to primary, leaving the event on its actual non-primary destination calendar. Fall back to the first matching destination or the main host destination instead.

title: Recurring collective cancellation still deletes only one calendar reference per booking
body: The outer loop now iterates every booking calendar reference, but the recurring/allRemainingBookings branch still uses updBooking.references.find(...) and iterates only bookingToDelete.user.credentials. For a recurring collective booking with one calendar reference per host, only the first reference per booking is ever deleted, and the same deletion is repeated once per outer reference. Other hosts' calendar events remain. The inner logic must iterate all references and use each reference's credentialId.

title: Crash when Google Meet has no destination calendar
body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then dereferenced with `.integration`. For a Google Meet event with no destination calendar (null or empty array), it is undefined, so booking creation throws a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use optional chaining/defaulting here.

title: Video meeting references lose credentialId
body: For non-calendar results (the dedicated video meeting), `credentialId` is now hard-coded to `undefined`. The previous code used `result.credentialId`, which is how the video credential was persisted on the booking reference. Since `handleCancelBooking` only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, this regression leaves video meetings behind on cancellation and breaks later video updates.

title: Collective hosts' destination calendars are dropped when no main destination exists
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so other collective hosts' destination calendars are never added and those hosts do not get calendar events. Initializing to `[]` has to be done carefully so the organizer's fallback-calendar path is still preserved.

title: updateLocation creates booking references without externalCalendarId/credentialId
body: `referencesToCreate` reads `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` returns an EventResult without either field. Before this change the code fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` and `evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId`. Now location changes persist new booking references with both values undefined, so later updates/cancellations cannot locate the actual calendar and credential.

title: Stale credential reused when a reference's credential is missing
body: `credential` is declared outside the reference loop. If a reference has a credentialId that is not in `this.calendarCredentials` and the DB lookup fails or yields no app slug, the variable still holds the previous reference's credential and is passed to `updateEvent` with the current reference's uid/externalCalendarId. This can update/delete the wrong host's calendar. Reset `credential` per iteration and skip/report when it cannot be resolved.

title: Legacy destination without credentialId loses externalCalendarId on references
body: When a destination calendar has no credentialId, this branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the destination's externalId. `EventManager.create` now builds `referencesToCreate[].externalCalendarId` from `result.externalId`, so it is undefined even though the destination identifies a specific calendar. Previously the reference used `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, so this can make later update/delete target the primary or wrong calendar. Pass `destination.externalId` here as well.

title: Office365 create ignores credentialId and always uses the first destination
body: `createEvent` always uses `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. EventManager invokes it once per destination credential; for a second collective host, the first host's calendar id is used with the second host's token, usually causing a 404 or writing to the wrong calendar. The same first-only pattern exists in larkcalendar and packages/lib/CalendarService.ts. CalDAV is especially dangerous: filtering the second host's calendars against the first host's externalId can produce an empty list and return success without creating anything.

title: Google update/delete fallback compares externalId to the same falsy value
body: When `externalCalendarId` is not supplied, the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which only matches a destination whose externalId is null/undefined. For legacy references without an externalCalendarId this leaves `calendarId` undefined in `updateEvent` (the update fails) and falls back to primary in `deleteEvent` (line 317), deleting from the wrong calendar. Use a real fallback destination or require the external id.

title: Recurring collective cancellation still only deletes the organizer's calendar events
body: The new outer loop over all calendar references enters the recurring branch, but inside it ignores the current `calendarCredential`/`calendar` and iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` (the organizer's credentials only). It also uses `.find` to pick only the first calendar reference of each updated booking. For a recurring collective booking, other hosts' calendar events are never deleted, and the same deletion work is repeated once per current reference. Use the current reference's credential and iterate all references.

title: Collective confirmation flow does not load all hosts' destination calendars
body: This handler creates calendar events for bookings that required confirmation. It builds `destinationCalendar` from the single booking destination or the confirming user only, and `handleNewBooking` persists only the first destination on the booking. Other collective hosts' destination calendars are never loaded, so confirming a collective booking still creates events for only one host. The same gap exists in the payment webhooks (`features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts` and `paypal-webhook.ts`), which also create calendar events after payment.

title: Unrelated inversion of IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED changes organization slug creation
body: This unrelated change flips the condition: previously `slug` was set when team billing was disabled and `requestedSlug` when enabled; now `slug` is set when billing is enabled, and neither field is set when billing is disabled. That changes organization URL/slug behavior for self-hosted/billing-disabled deployments and is unrelated to the calendar fix. If not intentional, revert it.

title: prisma is used without being imported
body: getClient calls prisma.credential.update(...) at line 96, but this file does not import prisma from @calcom/prisma; the PR only added the z and parseRefreshTokenResponse imports. The package will not type-check/build, so Salesforce calendar and this credential-sync path are unusable.

title: Google credential key is replaced with the SafeParse result object
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the result of safeParse ({ success, data }), not the parsed token data. Assigning that object to key and writing it to credential.key means the stored Google credential no longer matches googleCredentialSchema. The next construction/refresh of this credential will fail schema parsing, breaking Google Calendar for the user. Store parsed.data (or change the helper to return data) instead.

title: Sync-mode refresh returns a raw fetch Response to callers expecting app-specific token objects
body: When credential sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the native Response from the parent endpoint. Several callers treat the return value as their provider client's response: Google reads res.data, HubSpot reads expiresIn/accessToken directly, and ZohoBigin/ZohoCRM read tokenInfo.data. Those values are undefined, so the code writes empty/undefined credentials to the DB and subsequent API calls fail. The helper needs to parse the response and return the shape each caller expects, or the callers must handle the fetch Response explicitly.

title: Sync-mode token schema does not pass through provider token fields and fabricates a refresh token
body: [z.string().toString()] evaluates to the literal key '[object Object]' (and the second computed key overwrites the first), so minimumTokenResponseSchema only validates access_token and strips all other fields because z.object is not passthrough. The code then invents refresh_token: 'refresh_token' when it is absent (lines 25-27). In sync mode this drops expires_in/refresh_token/scope/instance_url from responses and overwrites real refresh tokens with that dummy value in callers such as Office365 and Zoom, causing repeated refreshes and eventual broken credentials. Use a passthrough schema and preserve existing refresh tokens.

title: Zoho Bigin sends the credential ID as the Cal.com user ID during sync refresh
body: refreshOAuthTokens's third parameter is userId, but this caller passes credentialId (the credential row ID). With credential sync enabled, the parent endpoint receives a calcomUserId that is actually a credential ID, so it will look up/return tokens for the wrong user or fail. The method should receive and pass credential.userId.

title: Zoom sync refresh uses the folder name zoomvideo instead of the app slug zoom
body: The rest of the Zoom app identifies itself with appId/slug 'zoom' (e.g. the callback creates appId: 'zoom' and the install path uses slug zoom), and the credential webhook looks up apps by their canonical DB slug. Passing 'zoomvideo' to the parent sync endpoint makes it inconsistent with those identifiers, so the parent cannot reliably resolve the app and token sync fails.

title: Salesforce connection uses the old access token after refreshing
body: getClient fetches and persists a new access_token at lines 96-99, but the returned jsforce.Connection is still created with credentialKey.access_token, the value loaded before the refresh. If the old token is expired, the new connection is immediately unusable; the freshly parsed token should be used.

title: Malformed webhook bodies and invalid ciphertext return 500 instead of 4xx
body: appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) throws a ZodError for invalid payloads, and symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse at lines 57-59 can throw for bad ciphertext or invalid JSON. There is no try/catch, so Next returns a 500 to the caller. Webhook senders will treat malformed requests as server failures and retry them; validate and return 400.

title: Salesforce token refresh references prisma without importing it
body: The new refresh path calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)` at this line, but the file does not import `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. TypeScript will fail to compile with `Cannot find name 'prisma'`, blocking the build.

title: Minimum token schema uses literal computed keys instead of wildcards
body: `[z.string().toString()]` is evaluated once to a fixed property name (for example `ZodString`), not a wildcard for arbitrary token fields. In credential-sharing mode `minimumTokenResponseSchema` therefore requires a numeric property with that literal name and normal OAuth token responses fail validation; because the schema is not a passthrough, valid fields such as `expires_in` and `refresh_token` are also stripped. This breaks token refresh for Google, Office 365, Salesforce, and Zoom whenever sync is enabled.

title: Missing refresh tokens are replaced with the literal string refresh_token
body: When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, this code writes the literal value `refresh_token` into the result. Callers such as Office365Calendar spread the parsed data over the existing credential, so a response without a new refresh token overwrites a valid stored refresh token with that placeholder. A later refresh using the placeholder will fail and disconnect the integration. The old refresh token should be preserved instead.

title: Google refresh reads `.data` from a fetch Response in sync mode
body: With credential sharing enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `Response` from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. This code reads `res?.data` and then `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date`, which are undefined on a Response. The refresh throws, is swallowed by the catch block, and Google API calls continue with expired credentials.

title: Google stores the SafeParseReturnType wrapper as the credential key
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `safeParse` result object `{ success, data }`, not the parsed token object. This line stores that wrapper directly in `prisma.credential.update`, so the credential key becomes `{ success: true, data: ... }` and no longer matches `googleCredentialSchema`. The next initialization of GoogleCalendarService will fail to parse the stored credential.

title: HubSpot treats a fetch Response as a HubspotToken in sync mode
body: In credential-sharing mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch `Response`, but the result is cast to `HubspotToken` and then read as `expiresIn` and `accessToken`. Those fields are undefined, so `expiryDate` becomes `NaN`, the Response object is written as the credential key, and `setAccessToken(undefined)` is called. HubSpot API calls fail and the stored credential is corrupted whenever sync is enabled.

title: Zoho Bigin sends credential id as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint
body: The third argument of `refreshOAuthTokens` is the Cal.com user id and is sent as `calcomUserId` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. This call passes `credentialId` instead of `credential.userId`, so the self-hosted app store is asked to refresh tokens for a credential id as if it were a user id. The wrong user's tokens may be returned or the lookup may fail.

title: Zoho Bigin treats a fetch Response as an axios response
body: In credential-sharing mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch `Response`, which has no `.data` property. This line accesses `tokenInfo.data.error`, so refresh throws a TypeError and no token is stored. The local axios path works only when sharing is disabled.

title: Zoho CRM treats a fetch Response as an axios response
body: In credential-sharing mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch `Response`, not an axios response. `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is undefined here, so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` throws and Zoho CRM token refresh fails whenever credential sync is enabled.

title: Salesforce connection is built with the stale access token after refresh
body: The new refresh code fetches and stores a new access token at lines 75-99, but the returned `jsforce.Connection` still uses `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` from the old credential. If the old access token was expired, the current operation fails even though a valid token was just saved in the database. It should use the refreshed `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED stores the encryption key instead of a boolean
body: `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` returns the encryption key string when both env vars are set. The exported constant is therefore a secret, not an enabled flag. If it is logged, serialized, or imported into code that reaches the client, `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` can leak. Use `Boolean(...)` and keep the key out of exported constants.

title: Credential-mutating webhook accepts any HTTP method
body: The handler never checks `req.method`; it will process GET, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE requests as long as the secret header and body are present. A credential-mutating webhook should accept only POST and return 405 for other methods.

title: Updating synced credentials leaves the invalid flag set
body: When a credential already exists, the update only changes `key`. If that credential was previously marked `invalid` after a refresh failure, it stays invalid and Cal.com will continue ignoring the fresh credentials from the app store. Synced credentials should reset `invalid` to false.

title: Salesforce bypasses the configured credential sync endpoint
body: Unlike the other integrations changed in this PR, Salesforce never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`; it always fetches directly from `login.salesforce.com` using local consumer keys. Consequently, when a self-hoster configures `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and expects their app store to be the source of truth, Salesforce token refreshes still use Cal.com's local app secrets and never contact the app store.

title: No tests cover the new credential webhook or token-sharing helpers
body: This PR adds a security-sensitive endpoint that writes third-party credentials and changes token refresh paths for many integrations, but no automated tests were added. Tests are needed for bad/missing webhook secrets, non-POST methods, malformed encrypted payloads, and the different expected refresh response shapes, since simple tests would catch the response-shape and parsing failures in this change.

title: Google Calendar stores the Zod safeParse wrapper as the credential key
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the whole Zod safeParse result (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed credential object. The code assigns that wrapper to `data.key` when updating the credential. On the next refresh/use, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` receives `{ success: true, data: ... }` instead of the credential and fails. Store `key.data` after checking success instead.

title: Sharing mode returns a fetch Response where callers expect token data
body: When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` Response. Callers expect provider-specific token data: Google does `res?.data` (undefined), Hubspot writes the Response object into the credential and reads `accessToken`/`expiresIn` off it, and Zoho does `tokenInfo.data.error` on a Response. This makes sync fail or store corrupt credentials. The function also never checks `response.ok`, so an error response can be treated as success. Return one consistent parsed-token contract and update all callers.

title: Minimum token schema does not allow the fields it is meant to accept
body: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is built with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]`; both computed properties resolve to the same string and the second overwrites the first, so this is not a catchall. Zod therefore strips every response field except `access_token`, including `refresh_token`, `expires_in`/`expiry_date`, and `instance_url`. The next `if` then sets `refresh_token` to the literal string `'refresh_token'` whenever it was stripped. In sharing mode this drops expiry/refresh/instance fields and writes a fake refresh token, corrupting credentials and breaking later refreshes.

title: Schema choice is based on env, not on whether the sync endpoint was used
body: The parser switches to the minimal sharing schema solely because env vars are set. However `refreshOAuthTokens` falls back to the provider when `userId` is null, and Salesforce always refreshes directly. Those provider responses are still parsed with the minimal schema even though no sync endpoint was involved, stripping required fields such as `instance_url`, `expiry_date`, and scope. The helper should receive a flag indicating the response source, or the caller should choose the schema.

title: Salesforce service uses prisma without importing it
body: `prisma.credential.update` is called here, but this file never imports `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. This is a TypeScript/build error for the Salesforce app. Add the import or remove the DB write.

title: Salesforce bypasses the new sync helper and ignores the refreshed token
body: The new refresh code posts directly to `login.salesforce.com` instead of calling `refreshOAuthTokens`, so `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is never used for Salesforce and the self-hosted app store cannot be the source of truth. Additionally, after updating the DB with the freshly refreshed token, the returned jsforce connection is still built with the old `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url`, so the refreshed token is not used for the current connection.

title: Zoho Bigin sends credential id as calcomUserId
body: `refreshOAuthTokens`' third argument is the Cal.com user id and is sent in the request body as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`. The self-hosted endpoint receives a credential id where it expects a user id, so it cannot identify the user whose credentials should be refreshed. Pass `credential.userId` instead.

title: Zoom sync request uses the wrong app slug
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` sends `appSlug` to the credential sync endpoint. Zoom's app slug is `zoom` (the callback creates credentials with `appId: 'zoom'`), but this call sends `zoomvideo` (the folder name). The self-hosted endpoint will not find or sync the correct app. Use `zoom`.

title: Updated credentials do not clear the invalid flag
body: On the update path only `key` is written. If the existing credential was previously marked `invalid: true` (for example after an `invalid_grant`), it remains invalid after the app store sends fresh credentials, so the synced token is still ignored by the app. Set `invalid: false` (and any other required fields) when applying fresh credentials.

title: Find-then-create is not atomic and can create duplicate credentials
body: `findFirst` followed by `create` is not atomic. Two webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both see no credential and then both create rows, producing duplicate credentials. Later updates only touch the first row via `findFirst`, leaving the other stale. Use a unique constraint plus upsert/transaction, or otherwise serialize this path.

title: New credential sync webhook and refresh paths have no tests
body: This PR adds an authenticated webhook that writes credentials and changes token refresh behavior across many integrations, but no tests cover missing/invalid secret, malformed encrypted payload, update vs create, invalid-flag recovery, fallback when the sync endpoint is absent, or provider-specific response parsing. These paths are high risk and currently unverified.

title: Team admin/owner permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`
