body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, so a user must satisfy both predicates at once. A team member who is only an admin (not the owner) is therefore rejected with FORBIDDEN, even though the UI exposes the "additional_guests" action and other checks in the codebase use `booking.isUserTeamAdminOrOwner` (an OR). In practice only the organizer (or an attendee) can add guests; team admins/owners operating on someone else's team booking get a confusing permission error. The two calls should be combined with `||`.

title: Guest filters are case-sensitive, allowing blacklist bypass and duplicate attendees
body: `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is lowercased when parsed, but `uniqueGuests` compares `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` against the raw user input, and the duplicate check `guest === attendee.email` is also an exact string compare. Zod's `.email()` does not normalize case. As a result `Blocked@Example.com` passes the blacklist, and `John@x.com` creates a second attendee row next to an existing `john@x.com` (who then receives a duplicate invitation). Both comparisons should be done on lowercased values.

title: Emails sent with unfiltered `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw request payload, but the DB write only used `uniqueGuests`. Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails` the check `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` decides whether someone gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (new guest) or the `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (existing attendee). Because already-existing attendees appear in `guests` whenever the caller resubmits them, those attendees get a full duplicate booking confirmation with a `METHOD:REQUEST` ICS instead of the "guests added" notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` here.

title: Calendar sync uses the acting user's credentials, not the booking organizer's
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` builds the EventManager with the credentials of whoever called the mutation. The event being updated belongs to `booking.userId`. When a team admin/owner or an attendee (explicitly allowed by the permission check above) adds guests, the EventManager either has no calendar credentials at all (plain attendees) or only the actor's (admins), so `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` does not update the organizer's calendar event — guests are persisted in the DB and emailed, but never actually added to the calendar invite. Credentials for the booking's organizer/host should be used.

title: Any attendee can add unlimited arbitrary email addresses
body: The authorization check grants access to anyone whose email is in `booking.attendees`, and guests added by this same endpoint become attendees too. There is no cap on the number of addresses in `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (`z.array(z.string().email())`) and no rate limiting, so a booker (or a guest they previously added) can repeatedly POST arbitrary addresses and cause cal.com to send them calendar invites and attendee emails from the organizer's identity — a spam/open-relay vector against arbitrary third parties. If attendees are meant to invite others, this needs at least a per-booking count limit and rate limiting, and probably a config flag.

title: No validation of booking status before mutating attendees
body: The handler loads the booking by id and only checks existence and permissions; it never checks `booking.status`. A direct API call can therefore add guests (and trigger calendar invites and emails) to a CANCELLED or REJECTED booking, resurrecting attendee records and sending invitations for an event that no longer takes place. The booking status should be validated (e.g. ACCEPTED/PENDING) before modifying attendees.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores host/attendee email opt-outs
body: Every other helper in this file consults `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` before enqueuing emails, but `sendAddGuestsEmails` has no `eventTypeMetadata` parameter and unconditionally sends the organizer email (plus team members) and attendee emails. Event types configured with `disableStandardEmails.all.host` or `.attendee` will still send mail when guests are added, violating the organizer's explicit preference. The handler already loads `eventType`; its metadata should be passed through and checked here.

title: No tests for the new addGuests endpoint or dialog
body: The PR adds a new authenticated mutation that mutates attendee records, talks to calendar integrations and sends emails, plus a new dialog and a new form component, but contains no tests. The permission matrix (organizer / team admin / team owner / attendee / unrelated user), the dedupe and blacklist filtering, and the case where `updateCalendarAttendees` throws are exactly the kind of logic that regresses silently; at minimum a unit test for the handler's authorization and filtering would be expected.

title: Error toast always shows raw tRPC code; fallback message is unreachable
body: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`` always evaluates to a non-empty template string (e.g. `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR: <english text>`), so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never falls back and users are shown internal error codes instead of the localized "Unable to add guests" text. Additionally `t(err.message)` only produces a translation when the server message happens to be a key; other messages are leaked verbatim.

title: Hardcoded "Remove email" tooltip is not translated
body: The remove button tooltip uses the literal string `content="Remove email"` instead of `t("remove_email")` / an existing locale key, while every other user-facing string in this component goes through `useLocale()`. In a fully localized product this surfaces English text in all non-English locales.

title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)). A team admin who is not also an owner will be rejected, and depending on isTeamAdmin's role semantics even owners may be rejected. The new UI action then fails with you_do_not_have_permission for intended team administrators. Use an OR/combined membership check.

title: Any attendee can add guests to a booking
body: The same guard also treats any attendee as authorized (isAttendee). The mutation only needs a bookingId and the caller's session, so any booker/guest on a booking can add arbitrary addresses to it, which then triggers calendar updates and emails to every attendee. The new UI is host-facing and does not expose attendee self-service, so this is an unintended write/notification path unless explicitly required.

title: Guest filtering does not deduplicate or normalize email addresses
body: uniqueGuests compares each submitted email against existing attendees and the blacklist, but never deduplicates the submitted array or normalizes case. A direct tRPC call with duplicate addresses can insert duplicate attendee rows (or hit a unique constraint) and send duplicate invites, and an uppercase variant of an existing or blacklisted address bypasses both checks because BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased but guest is not. Normalize/trim/lowercase and dedupe with a Set before writing.

title: No booking status check before adding guests
body: The handler never checks booking.status. A caller with permission can add guests to a cancelled or rejected booking, which then writes attendee rows and attempts calendar/email updates for an event that is no longer active. Reject non-active statuses before the update.

title: Event manager uses the caller's credentials, not the booking owner's
body: booking.user.credentials are loaded by the query but are not used; EventManager is constructed with getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). For a team admin/owner or attendee modifying another host's booking, the calendar operation therefore runs with the caller's credentials instead of the booking owner's, so the organizer's calendar event may not be updated or the wrong calendar may be touched. Use the booking owner's credentials/identity for the event manager.

title: Attendee rows are committed before the calendar update
body: The prisma.booking.update creates attendee rows before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees and before email dispatch. If the calendar update throws, the booking keeps the new attendees but the calendar was not updated; retrying the same guests is then rejected because uniqueGuests sees them as existing. Move the calendar work before the DB write or add rollback/recovery handling.

title: Add-guests emails ignore event-type disableStandardEmails settings
body: sendAddGuestsEmails sends organizer/team and attendee emails unconditionally. Other send helpers in this file accept eventTypeMetadata and honor disableStandardEmails for host/attendee. The handler has booking.eventType loaded and can pass metadata, but it does not, so event types configured to suppress standard emails will still email everyone when a guest is added.

title: Hidden calendar notes can leak in add-guests emails
body: When hideCalendarNotes is true, sendScheduledEmails removes additionalNotes before constructing attendee emails. sendAddGuestsEmails does not do this; it passes the full calendarEvent to AttendeeScheduledEmail/AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. A new guest can therefore receive notes that the event type is configured to hide from attendees.

title: Email dispatch receives raw guests instead of filtered uniqueGuests
body: addGuestsHandler calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the raw request array rather than uniqueGuests. sendAddGuestsEmails treats every email in newGuests as newly added and sends the full scheduled email to matching attendees. If the request included an existing attendee along with at least one valid new guest, that existing attendee is misclassified and receives a scheduled email instead of the add-guests notification. Pass the filtered uniqueGuests.

title: Invalid-email state is not reset on success or close
body: onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but not isInvalidEmail, and closing the dialog through onOpenChange also leaves it set. After one validation error, correcting the input and succeeding leaves isInvalidEmail true, so reopening the dialog immediately shows 'Emails must be unique and valid' even though the field is empty. Reset both state values on success and on close.

title: Error toast fallback is unreachable
body: The expression `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` always produces a non-empty string, so `message || t('unable_to_add_guests')` can never fall back. If err.data is absent users see a message beginning with 'undefined:'. Build the message with an explicit fallback when the code/translation is missing.

title: No tests cover the new addGuests mutation
body: No tests are added for the new addGuests mutation. It changes authorization (organizer/team admin/attendee), duplicate and blacklist filtering, booking status handling, calendar integration, and email recipient selection. Those paths are security/data-integrity sensitive and should be covered by tests to prevent regressions.

title: Team admin/owner permission check uses && instead of ||
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be both a team admin AND a team owner at the same time. A team admin who is not the owner (the exact case the variable name and the `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && ...` guard below are meant to allow) fails this check and is rejected with FORBIDDEN when trying to add guests to a team booking. The two predicates should be OR'd, otherwise team admins (excluding owners) cannot use the feature.

title: No booking status check before adding guests and sending invites
body: The booking is fetched by id only and the handler never inspects `booking.status`. Guests can therefore be added to a CANCELLED (or REJECTED) booking and to bookings whose start/end time is in the past. This inserts new attendee rows, calls `updateCalendarAttendees`, and sends `sendAddGuestsEmails` (with a CONFIRMED ICS REQUEST) for an event that no longer exists/is over, which is misleading to recipients and pollutes data. The handler should reject non-active bookings (e.g. only ACCEPTED/PENDING and upcoming).

title: Email comparison is case-sensitive and duplicates within input are not removed
body: `uniqueGuests` filters with `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`, but the blacklist is lowercased while `guest` is not, and the existing-attendee comparison is case-sensitive. As a result: (a) a guest whose email differs only in casing from an existing attendee is added as a duplicate attendee row, and (b) a blacklisted address can be added by changing its case. Additionally, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only enforces `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint, so duplicate emails within one request are all inserted (the uniqueness check `uniqueEmails.size === emails.length` exists only in the client dialog). Normalize emails (trim + lowercase) before all comparisons and dedupe/validate uniqueness server-side.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails is passed raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`
body: Emails are sent with `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the unfiltered input list. If a submitted email already belongs to an existing attendee (filtered out of `uniqueGuests`), that attendee matches the `newGuests.includes(...)` branch in `sendAddGuestsEmails` and receives a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` booking confirmation instead of the `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` notification, potentially re-sending the event/ICS to someone who was already on the booking. It should use `uniqueGuests` so only genuinely new attendees are treated as new.

title: Calendar update uses the acting user's credentials, not the booking owner's
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` returns the credentials of the user invoking the endpoint, and those are handed to `new EventManager(...)` for `updateCalendarAttendees`. When the caller is a team admin or an attendee (both permitted above) rather than the booking owner, the calendar/video event that must be updated lives on the organizer's connected account, so the update may fail or target the wrong calendar/meeting. The credentials should be resolved for the booking's owner (e.g. `booking.user`) whose calendar holds the event.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails settings
body: Unlike every other send* function in this file, `sendAddGuestsEmails` never checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` (nor the `eventTypeMetadata` argument). Hosts or attendees who configured `disableStandardEmails` will still receive organizer/attendee emails when guests are added, violating their explicit email preferences. The function should accept and honor the event type metadata like `sendLocationChangeEmails` etc. do.

title: Email failures are silently swallowed with console.log
body: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` catch block only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")`, dropping the error entirely. Any failure to notify guests/attendees/hosts (e.g. mailer misconfiguration) is invisible in logs/monitoring, so the feature can silently stop sending notifications. Use the project logger and include the error, consistent with the rest of the emails package.

title: Invalid-email state and input are not reset when the dialog reopens
body: `isOpenDialog`/`isInvalidEmail` and `multiEmailValue` are only reset on success or on the Cancel button. The Dialog's `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` does not clear `isInvalidEmail`, so after an invalid submission the user closes and reopens the dialog, the red `emails_must_be_unique_valid` error is still shown even though they haven't submitted again; stale entered emails likewise persist. Reset these states when the dialog opens/closes.

title: New addGuests handler has no tests
body: The PR introduces a new backend mutation that performs access-control checks, guest deduplication/blacklisting, attendee creation, calendar updates, and email dispatch, plus new email templates, but adds no automated tests. Given the permission check bug and the deduplication/normalization issues above, at minimum unit/integration tests covering authorization (owner, admin, attendee, unrelated user), duplicate/blacklisted/case-variant emails, and cancelled bookings are needed to prevent regressions.

title: retryCount cleanup clause is not scoped to SMS/unscheduled reminders
body: The new deletion branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` inside the `OR` is not restricted by `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` or `scheduled: false`, unlike the pre-existing branch next to it. As written, any WorkflowReminder row (email, WhatsApp, or an already-scheduled reminder) whose retryCount is greater than 1 is hard-deleted on each cron run. Today only this handler increments retryCount, but the column lives on the shared model, so as soon as another scheduler writes retryCount — or a concurrent run manages to schedule a reminder after it has already been bumped twice — unrelated reminders are silently purged, and an already-scheduled reminder is deleted without cancelling its provider-side scheduled message (referenceId), leaving an orphaned SMS/email job that will still fire. The clause should be constrained to the same rows this handler owns, e.g. `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduled: false, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

title: Reminders that cannot be attempted never increment retryCount and are retried forever
body: retryCount is only incremented when `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns falsy or throws. When `sendTo` is missing (e.g. an SMS_ATTENDEE reminder for a booking with no `smsReminderNumber`, or an SMS_NUMBER step with an empty `sendTo`) or the computed `message` is empty, the `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` guard simply skips the reminder. Those rows stay `scheduled: false` forever, are re-fetched on every cron run, and are skipped again — exactly the unbounded-rescheduling behavior this PR is meant to stop. A missing phone number is one of the common failure modes, so this path needs to bump retryCount (or delete the reminder) when the reminder cannot be attempted.

title: Read-modify-write of retryCount loses increments under overlapping cron runs
body: Both increment sites (the `else` branch here and the one at line 195) compute `reminder.retryCount + 1` in application code from the value returned by the earlier `findMany`. If two cron invocations overlap — plausible because the per-reminder loop awaits a `profile.findFirst` and `getBookerBaseUrl` call for every reminder, so a run can exceed the cron interval — both read the same retryCount and write the same value. Failures are then under-counted and a persistently failing reminder may never reach the `> 1` threshold, so it is retried indefinitely and the PR's retry cap never takes effect. Use Prisma's atomic `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` instead.

title: Unguarded update inside catch can abort the whole batch
body: The `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` added inside the catch block is not itself protected. If it throws (row deleted concurrently by the cleanup query, or a transient DB error), the exception escapes the `catch` and the `for` loop, so all remaining unscheduled reminders in the batch are left unprocessed and the endpoint returns a 500. Additionally, this catch also runs when `twilio.scheduleSMS` succeeded but the subsequent `update({ scheduled: true, referenceId })` threw; in that case retryCount is bumped even though a Twilio message is already scheduled, so the reminder is re-sent on the next run (duplicate SMS) and then eventually deleted while the Twilio job remains live. The increment should be guarded with its own try/catch and should not be applied when the failure occurred after a successful provider call.

title: New retryCount predicate has no supporting index
body: The `retryCount > 1` condition has no index, and mixing it in an `OR` with the indexed `(method, scheduledDate)` predicate means Postgres cannot satisfy the whole query from the existing composite index. WorkflowReminder is a high-volume table (one row per reminder per booking), so every cron invocation can fall back to a sequential scan of the whole table. Consider a partial index such as `CREATE INDEX ... ON "WorkflowReminder"(retryCount) WHERE retryCount > 0`, or restructuring the cleanup so the unindexed predicate is not part of the main scan.

title: Comment no longer describes the delete query
body: The comment says "delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date", but the query now also deletes unscheduled SMS (and, due to the unscoped OR branch, non-SMS) reminders that have exceeded the retry limit. The comment should be updated to reflect both deletion conditions so future readers understand that the cleanup is not limited to past-due reminders.

title: Generated Prisma artifacts for retryCount were not regenerated
body: The schema's `zod` and `kysely` generators write committed outputs (`packages/prisma/zod/*`, `packages/prisma/kysely/types.ts`). This PR adds `retryCount` to `WorkflowReminder` and the migration, but does not update those generated files, so the WorkflowReminder zod schema and the Kysely `WorkflowReminder` interface still lack the new column. Any code that validates a reminder via the generated zod schema will silently drop retryCount, and Kysely-typed queries cannot reference it; the repository's prisma-generate check will also fail or produce a dirty diff. Regenerate and commit the zod/kysely outputs alongside the schema change.

title: Retry cleanup deletes reminders of any method and any scheduled state
body: The new OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` is not constrained by `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` or `scheduled: false`. Because `retryCount` lives on the shared `WorkflowReminder` model, this SMS cron can delete email/WhatsApp reminders, and can also delete a reminder whose SMS has already been scheduled if its retry count ever exceeds 1 (for example through interleaved cron runs). Those rows are then permanently lost, so later cancellation logic cannot find the scheduled reminder. Scope the retry branch to SMS unscheduled reminders, e.g. `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduled: false, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

title: Retry count uses a stale read-modify-write instead of an atomic increment
body: Both failure paths write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value fetched once before the loop. If two cron invocations overlap—there is no locking in this endpoint—or the row is updated by another process, one increment is lost, so the reminder can be retried more times than intended and deletion is delayed or skipped. Use an atomic Prisma update such as `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` (ideally with a claim/conditional update so overlapping runs do not both send).

title: Every exception is treated as an SMS send failure and consumes the retry budget
body: The catch wraps the whole per-reminder flow, not just `twilio.scheduleSMS`. Errors from profile lookup, URL generation, template rendering, or the DB update after Twilio has already accepted the SMS all increment `retryCount`. After two such errors the reminder is deleted. This means transient failures such as a database hiccup or Twilio outage can permanently drop reminders, and a DB update failure after a successful Twilio schedule leaves the row unscheduled so the next run can schedule a duplicate SMS. Only increment for confirmed send failures, and handle post-send persistence errors separately.

title: Retry update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
body: The `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` inside `catch` is not itself guarded. If it fails—for example because another cron invocation deleted the row, or the database is unavailable—the error escapes the catch and aborts the handler loop. The remaining unscheduled reminders are then not processed and the endpoint returns an error. The retry bookkeeping should not be able to stop the batch; catch and log failures around it (or use an updateMany and continue).

title: No tests cover the new retry/deletion behavior
body: The PR adds a schema column, retry increments on two failure paths, and deletion after the retry limit, but no tests were added. There is no coverage proving that a reminder is kept after one failure, deleted after two failures, that successful scheduling does not get deleted, or that non-SMS reminders are not removed by this SMS cron. These are exactly the failure-sensitive branches where regressions are likely.

title: Retry cleanup deletes non-SMS workflow reminders
body: The new OR branch matches any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, not just SMS reminders. WorkflowReminder is shared by email, SMS, and WhatsApp, so any non-SMS row that ever reaches retryCount > 1 (including future code paths that use this shared column) will be deleted by this cron. The branch also ignores the scheduled state, so a scheduled row with retryCount > 1 would be deleted while its external scheduled job still exists. Scope the condition to the intended SMS/failed reminders, for example by including method: WorkflowMethods.SMS and the intended scheduled state.

title: Retry count increment is a lost-update race
body: Both new increments use reminder.retryCount + 1 with the value read before the Twilio call. If two cron executions (or a retried request) process the same reminder concurrently, both can read the same retryCount and write the same incremented value, so a failure is lost. The reminder can then keep retrying past the intended two-failure limit and never be deleted. Use an atomic Prisma increment such as { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } or an equivalent SQL update.

title: Catch increments retries even when the SMS was already scheduled
body: The try block includes the prisma.workflowReminder.update at lines 169-177 that records a successful Twilio send. If twilio.scheduleSMS succeeds but that database update throws, the catch block increments retryCount and leaves scheduled false. The next cron run sends the same SMS again, and the new delete logic can eventually remove the row, losing the referenceId of the already-scheduled Twilio message so it cannot be cancelled. Retry increments should only happen for actual twilio.scheduleSMS failures; persistence errors after a successful send need separate handling.

title: Missing sendTo or empty message never increments retryCount
body: If sendTo is missing or message is empty, this condition is false and the loop continues without calling Twilio and without throwing. No retryCount increment occurs, so the reminder remains unscheduled and is picked up again on every cron run forever, which is exactly the infinite-retry behavior this PR is trying to stop. Handle this skip case by incrementing the retry counter, deleting the invalid reminder, or otherwise recording the failure.

title: No index for the retryCount cleanup query
body: The cron now runs deleteMany with a predicate on retryCount > 1, but the migration adds no index for retryCount. On a large WorkflowReminder table this OR predicate can force a full scan on every cron invocation, even though almost all rows have retryCount 0. Add an appropriate index (for example a partial index on retryCount > 0, or a composite index with method) to keep the cleanup query efficient.

title: No tests for the destructive retry cleanup path
body: The PR adds retry accounting and a deleteMany that permanently removes workflow reminder rows, but no test covers the new behavior. Add tests for: SMS scheduling failure incrementing retryCount, success after a retry, deletion at the retry threshold, non-SMS reminders not being deleted, and concurrent increments not losing failures.

title: Removing `findMany` breaks existing consumers
body: This PR deletes the public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, but the diff updates no call sites. `InsightsBookingService` is exported and was previously responsible for executing the denormalized query; any consumer still calling `findMany` will fail TypeScript compilation or runtime. Either migrate every call site in this PR or keep a `findMany` wrapper that executes a raw query using `getBaseConditions()`.

title: Unparenthesized OR authorization condition can be miscombined by callers
body: When scope is `team` or `org` and no filter conditions are supplied, `getBaseConditions()` returns `authConditions` directly. For those scopes `authConditions` is a top-level `OR` such as `(team booking) OR (user booking)`. If a caller appends another predicate, e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" >= ...`, SQL precedence makes it `(team booking) OR ((user booking) AND date filter)`, so the extra predicate is applied only to one branch. The returned fragment should always be wrapped in parentheses, otherwise date/security predicates can be silently skipped for part of the dataset.

title: Composite `Prisma.Sql` expectations are not structurally equal to reduce-built fragments
body: The service builds org/team and combined-filter conditions through `reduce` using nested fragments like `Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR (${condition})` and `Prisma.sql`(${acc}) AND (${condition})`. The expectations at lines 295, 332, and 429 are single flat `Prisma.sql` templates. `Prisma.Sql` equality is structural over its internal `strings` and `values`, not based on the rendered SQL text, so a nested fragment built with `reduce` will not deep-equal a flat template even when the SQL renders identically. These assertions will fail; compare rendered SQL or execute the query instead of using `toEqual` on `Prisma.Sql` objects.

title: Exact SQL array order depends on unordered repository results
body: The expected SQL hard-codes the order of `teamIds` and user IDs inside `ANY([...])`. `teamIds` comes from `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId` and user IDs come from `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`; neither call specifies an `orderBy`. If Postgres returns those rows in a different order, the `ANY` arrays differ even though the authorization semantics are identical, and the exact `Prisma.sql` comparison fails intermittently. Sort the IDs before asserting or compare semantically.

title: No database execution coverage for org/team `ANY` conditions
body: The only test that actually executes the generated conditions against Postgres uses `scope: "user"`. The org/team authorization paths, which are the only places that emit `ANY(${array})`, are only compared as `Prisma.sql` strings and never run against the database. A real parameter-binding/type-inference problem in those paths (for example around array parameters) would therefore pass the test suite while failing in production. Add a `$queryRaw` execution test for at least one org/team scope.

title: Prisma.Sql deep equality fails for reduce-built conditions
body: These expectations compare a whole Prisma.Sql object with a flat template, but the service builds team/org/filter combinations with nested Prisma.sql calls and reduce. Prisma.Sql equality is structural over its strings and values arrays; nested composition leaves different string segmentation even when the SQL text is identical. For example, the service OR condition has five strings while this flat template has three. Therefore the team, org, and combined-filter assertions at lines 296, 332, and 429 will fail. Compare conditions.sql/text plus values instead, or build the expected SQL with the same nested structure.

title: getBaseConditions can return an unparenthesized OR expression
body: When there is no filter, getBaseConditions returns the authorization expression directly. For org/team scopes that expression is an unparenthesized top-level OR, e.g. (A) OR (B). Any caller that composes it as WHERE ${baseConditions} AND ... gets SQL precedence A OR (B AND ...), so the extra predicate is applied only to one branch. This can return rows outside the requested date/status/team range. The returned expression should always be wrapped in parentheses, or callers should use a service method that composes safely.

title: Public findMany API removed without caller migration
body: The public findMany method is removed and replaced by getBaseConditions, which only returns a SQL fragment. No caller updates are included in this PR. Any existing consumer of service.findMany(...) will fail to compile or run, and responsibility for applying authorization moves to every raw-query caller; forgetting to interpolate getBaseConditions would query all rows. Keep a query method that applies the conditions, or migrate all callers in the same PR.

title: Team scope no longer requires teamId at compile time
body: The new public options type makes teamId optional for every scope, whereas the old constructor type was a discriminated union that required teamId for scope "team". Missing teamId now passes TypeScript, fails the runtime schema, and is silently converted to this.options = null, so the service returns 1=0 (empty results) instead of reporting a configuration error. Retain the discriminated union or throw on validation failure.

title: Unwrapped auth OR can bypass appended filters
body: In `getBaseConditions`, when `filterConditions` is null the method returns `authConditions` unchanged. For org/team scope that value is an unwrapped OR chain, e.g. `(team match) OR (user match)`. A caller that appends another predicate (`WHERE ${base} AND startTime > ...`) gets SQL where the appended predicate binds only to the last OR branch; rows from the team-booking branch can bypass the added filter. This differs from the old `findMany`, which combined conditions through Prisma's `AND` array. Wrap the returned auth fragment (and the filter fragment) in parentheses so the base condition is self-contained.

title: Event-type filter fragment is an unparenthesized OR
body: The event-type filter is built as `(eventTypeId = ...) OR (eventParentId = ...)` without outer parentheses. `getFilterConditions` is public and previously returned a grouped Prisma `AND` object, so code that composes it as `WHERE ${auth} AND ${filter}` will evaluate as `auth AND eventTypeId = ... OR eventParentId = ...`; eventParentId rows bypass the auth predicate. Wrap the OR fragment in parentheses at construction.

title: Public findMany API removed without updating consumers
body: The public `findMany` method is removed, and `getAuthorizationConditions` / `getFilterConditions` now return `Prisma.Sql` instead of Prisma `WhereInput`. No caller is updated in this PR. Any existing consumer of `InsightsBookingService.findMany`, or code that passes these conditions to Prisma's `where`, will fail to compile or query incorrectly. Update all consumers or keep a compatibility method.

title: Org-scope test depends on unspecified DB array ordering
body: This expectation compares the `Prisma.sql` values arrays in a fixed order: `[orgId, team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` and `[user.id, user2.id, user3.id]`. The service obtains these arrays from `findAllByParentId` and `findAllByTeamIds` without an `orderBy`, and `ANY(array)` is order-insensitive. PostgreSQL does not guarantee row order, so the test can fail nondeterministically. Sort arrays before binding/comparison or compare as sets.

title: Caching behavior no longer covered
body: The service still caches authorization and filter conditions via `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, but this PR deletes both caching tests and adds no replacement. A regression where conditions are rebuilt on every call, or where a cached `null` filter result is not reused, would no longer be detected. Re-add caching tests using spies/call counts.

title: Team/org ANY conditions never executed against the database
body: The only integration test that actually executes SQL uses user-scope conditions, which contain no `= ANY(${array})` parameters. The team/org tests only compare generated `Prisma.sql` objects. Array parameter binding and SQL validity for the team/org authorization branches are therefore unverified; a broken `ANY` binding or malformed OR composition there would still pass the suite. Add an integration test that executes org/team base conditions against the database.

title: Cache status stays stale after deleting cached data
body: The deleteCacheMutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess prop; it never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. In the apps-installed calendar page `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` is rendered without an `onChanged` prop, so `onSuccess` is undefined. As a result the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated: …" and the "Delete cached data" entry after the rows were already deleted, until a full page reload. The sibling `disconnectMutation` in the same component does invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (and `viewer.apps.integrations`) in `onSettled`, so the omission looks accidental. Add the same invalidation to the deleteCache mutation.

title: Cache deletion always fails for credentials not owned by the session user (delegation/team credentials)
body: The authorization check is `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`, i.e. it only accepts credentials whose `userId` equals the logged in user. Team/service-account delegation credentials are not user-owned (they are stored with `userId = null` and belong to a team / DelegationCredential), and in-memory delegation credentials even have negative ids, so the query never matches and the mutation throws "Credential not found or access denied". The UI does not guard against this: `canDisconnect` is computed from `delegationCredentialId`, but `hasCache` only checks the integration type, so the "Delete cached data" item is rendered for delegation-connected Google calendars and then always fails with the generic "Error deleting cache" toast. Either authorize team/delegation ownership in the handler or hide the action when `delegationCredentialId` is set. Note also that for in-memory delegation credentials, cache lookups are keyed by `userId` (see `getCachedAvailability`), so a delete-by-`credentialId` would not clear those rows even if it succeeded.

title: Cache status reports expired cache rows as a live cache
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups over all CalendarCache rows for a credential without filtering on `expiresAt`. Expired rows are not removed from the table (availability reads just ignore rows with `expiresAt < now` and the row is only replaced on the next upsert), so a user whose Google cache expired weeks ago is shown "Cache Status — Last updated: <old date>" and offered "Delete cached data" even though the cache is effectively dead and the next availability request will miss. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the `where` clause so the indicator reflects a usable cache. Relatedly, the migration backfills `updatedAt = NOW()` for all pre-existing rows, so after deploy every legacy cache row will display the deploy timestamp as its "last updated" time rather than when it was actually written.

title: Unconditional bulk update of all SelectedCalendar rows on every cache refresh
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now ends with `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`, whose only effect is to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` via the Prisma `@updatedAt` attribute (the data object is empty). This runs on every cache population, which is triggered by the Google push webhook — i.e. potentially many times per minute for busy calendars — and issues an UPDATE touching every SelectedCalendar row of the credential, adding write load and row-lock contention. The PR description itself notes that SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is not shown in the frontend (the UI uses CalendarCache.updatedAt), so this write has no consumer. Remove it, or make it conditional on an actual reader existing.

title: Cache-status query bypasses the CalendarCache factory and runs on every connectedCalendars call
body: The handler instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init()` (the factory that returns the mock when calendar-cache is disabled / not enabled for the user's teams). Consequence: every `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` request — including onboarding, apps pages, and users/orgs where the calendar-cache feature is off — performs an extra `groupBy` aggregate over CalendarCache, even though the mock exists specifically to avoid that work when the feature is disabled. Scope the query (e.g. only for Google credentials, and via the repository factory) so non-cache users don't pay for it.

title: `sed -i ''` is macOS-only, so the script silently fails to update .env on Linux
body: `sed -i '' -E "s|...|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD/macOS in-place invocation. With GNU sed (Linux), the empty `''` argument is not consumed as an in-place suffix, so the command errors out and the file is never modified, yet the script still prints "✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in $ENV_FILE to $TUNNEL_URL", leaving developers with a stale webhook URL while believing it was updated. Use a portable form (e.g. `sed -i.bak -E ... && rm -f "$ENV_FILE.bak"` or write to a temp file) and check the command's exit status before printing success. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is also cwd-dependent and only correct when the script is run from `scripts/`.

title: Unrelated dev:cron change introduces an undeclared `tsx` dependency invoked via npx
body: Changing `dev:cron` from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` is unrelated to calendar cache status/actions and means the script depends on `tsx`, which is not declared anywhere in this package's devDependencies. On a clean checkout `npx` will download `tsx` from the network at run time (failing in offline sandboxes/CI) and pins nothing, so different developers may run different versions. Either revert this line or add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it through the package manager (`yarn tsx`).

title: Removal of the `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` assertion drops type-checking of the hand-written where clause
body: `findMany` previously validated the hand-rolled `FindManyArgs` (whose `where` is a narrowed custom shape with e.g. `googleChannelId?: string | null | { not: null }`) against Prisma's generated `SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` via `satisfies`. The new code passes the raw object to `prisma.selectedCalendar.findMany` without that assertion, so a future edit to the custom `FindManyArgs` type can now silently produce a filter Prisma will reject at runtime instead of failing the build. This change is also unrelated to the feature. Restore the `satisfies` assertion (or explain why it had to go) so the type contract keeps being enforced.

title: Cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded en-US locale
body: The "cache_last_updated" value uses `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` while the component already uses `useLocale()` for translations. Non-US users therefore see US-formatted dates (M/D/YY, 12-hour clock) in an otherwise translated UI. Use the active user locale (e.g. from the locale context / `useLocale().i18n.language`) so the timestamp follows the user's locale settings.

title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache UI
body: The `deleteCacheMutation` onSuccess only shows a toast and calls `onSuccess?.()` (the parent `onChanged` callback). It never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, so the `cacheUpdatedAt` value that drives the "Cache Status" row and the "Delete cached data" item is not refetched. After a successful delete the dropdown still shows the old timestamp and offers the delete action again until the query happens to refetch. The sibling `disconnectMutation` correctly calls `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in onSettled; the delete-cache path should do the same.

title: Instantiating CalendarCacheRepository directly bypasses the calendar-cache feature gate
body: Everywhere else the cache layer is obtained via `CalendarCache.init(...)`, which returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the `calendar-cache` feature is disabled. Here `new CalendarCacheRepository()` is constructed directly, so `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` always issues a `groupBy` query against `CalendarCache` on every `connectedCalendars` request, even for users/orgs that do not have calendar cache enabled. It also surfaces "cache status" for stale rows left over from when the feature was enabled. Use `CalendarCache.init(null)` so the feature flag is respected.

title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, reporting expired cache as present
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` aggregates `_max(updatedAt)` over all rows for the credential, including rows whose `expiresAt` is in the past. `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows with `expiresAt >= now()`, so the UI can show a "Cache Status / Last updated" for data that is already expired and no longer used. If the intent is to show usable cache, the `where` clause should include `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }`; otherwise the label is misleading.

title: Cache timestamp hard-codes en-US locale
body: The cache "last updated" timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`. cal.com is localized (the component already uses `useLocale`), so users on other locales will always see a US-formatted date/time. It should use the current user's locale (e.g. from `useLocale`) rather than the literal "en-US".

title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` but tsx is not a declared dependency
body: The `dev:cron` script was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not listed in apps/web devDependencies (only `ts-node` is). `npx` will therefore try to download `tsx` on demand, making the script non-reproducible and liable to fail or prompt in offline/CI/restricted environments. This change is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature and should either be reverted or accompanied by declaring `tsx` as a dependency.

title: Dev script uses macOS-only sed syntax and a CWD-relative env path
body: Two portability/correctness problems in the new helper script: (1) `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax; on GNU sed (Linux/CI) `-i ''` is parsed as an empty backup suffix and the command errors, so updating `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` fails. (2) `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory, not the script location, so running `bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root writes/creates a `.env` in the parent of the repository instead of the repo's `.env`. Use a script-relative path and a portable sed invocation.

title: New destructive mutation and cache-status query have no tests
body: `deleteCacheHandler` performs an access-control check (credential must belong to `ctx.user`) and then deletes rows; `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` is a new query used to drive UI. Neither has any unit/integration test. Given this is a destructive, authorization-sensitive endpoint, at minimum there should be a test that a credentialId belonging to another user is rejected and that a valid delete removes exactly that credential's cache rows.

title: Cache status includes expired cache rows
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` aggregates every `CalendarCache` row for the credential without filtering on `expiresAt`, while `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows with `expiresAt >= now`. Expired rows are not deleted elsewhere, so `cacheUpdatedAt` stays non-null after the cache expires. The UI then shows “Cache Status / Last updated” and “Delete cached data” for a cache that is not actually being served, giving users a misleading view of cache state. Add an `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` predicate or return expiry state explicitly.

title: Migration backfills every cache row with the deployment time
body: Adding `updatedAt ... DEFAULT NOW()` sets all pre-existing `CalendarCache` rows to the time the migration runs. Since the new UI displays `_max(updatedAt)` as “Last updated”, every existing cached credential will appear to have been refreshed at deploy time even though the old rows have no real update timestamp. Existing caches will report a false freshness date until each row is rewritten. Consider making the column nullable for legacy rows, backfilling from a meaningful source, or suppressing the status for backfilled rows.

title: Cache deletion does not invalidate connected calendars query
body: `deleteCacheMutation` only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback. Unlike `disconnectMutation`, it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, and `onSuccess` is optional at this component’s API. In a caller that does not pass an invalidating `onSuccess`, the dropdown continues to render the old `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamp and a delete action for data that no longer exists until the user manually refreshes. Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` after successful deletion.

title: Cache timestamp is hard-coded to en-US
body: The component formats `cacheUpdatedAt` with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, ignoring the active locale from `useLocale`. Users in other locales get U.S.-formatted dates in an otherwise localized UI. Use the current locale or a shared date formatting helper instead of the literal `"en-US"`.

title: Webhook test script uses macOS-only sed syntax
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax. GNU sed on Linux interprets the empty string incorrectly and fails or behaves unpredictably, so the script cannot update `.env` on Linux. Separately, `ENV_FILE` on line 5 is relative to the caller’s current working directory, so running it from the repo root writes to the parent directory’s `.env` rather than the repo `.env`. Use a portable in-place edit and resolve paths relative to the script location.

title: No tests for destructive cache deletion authorization
body: This PR adds a destructive `deleteCache` mutation and an ownership check, but no tests cover the new handler, the unauthorized path (credential id belonging to another user), or the repository’s `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` behavior (empty ids, multiple cache rows, expired rows). A regression in the ownership check would let a user delete another user’s cache. Add unit/integration tests for authorized and unauthorized deletion and the cache-status query.

title: Rescheduled reminders still use immediate SendGrid cancellation
body: This passes `true` for `immediateDelete`, so rescheduling still POSTs cancellations directly to SendGrid instead of marking the reminder `cancelled` and letting `scheduleEmailReminders` cancel it close to the send time. That reintroduces the pending-cancellation limit that this PR is meant to fix: after enough reschedules, SendGrid cancellations fail and the old reminders are still sent. Because this immediate path also does not set `cancelled`, a failed cancellation has no DB marker for the cron to retry. Use the deferred cancellation path for reschedules, or otherwise persist the cancellation for retry.

title: Reminder cancellation calls are fire-and-forget
body: The calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` inside `forEach` are not awaited. For email reminders the actual cancellation work is now the async DB update that sets `cancelled`; if the serverless invocation ends before that update completes, the reminder is never marked and the cron will not cancel the SendGrid email. This is the core regression path for cancelled bookings. Collect these promises and await them before returning. The same fire-and-forget pattern also appears in the reschedule and workflow handlers.

title: One SendGrid cancellation failure aborts all reminder cancellations
body: The whole cancellation loop is inside one `try/catch`, and the collected `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` promises are only awaited after the loop. If a single `client.request` fails (invalid/already-cancelled batch, rate limit, etc.), the code jumps to `catch`, skips every remaining `remindersToCancel`, and never executes the delete promises already collected. Those reminders stay in the DB, and the same failing reminder can block every subsequent cron run, so cancelled emails are still sent. Handle each reminder independently and delete/flag it per reminder.

title: Immediate cancellation does not delete or mark the WorkflowReminder row
body: When `immediateDelete` is true, the function returns after the SendGrid request without deleting the row or setting `cancelled`. In the reschedule path this leaves the old booking's reminder with `scheduled: true` and the old `referenceId` until the cron's past-date cleanup. It also means a failed SendGrid call is invisible to the cron retry mechanism. The immediate path should delete the row or set a persisted state so failed cancellations can be retried.

title: No index supports the new cron cancellation query
body: The cron now repeatedly queries `WorkflowReminder` with `cancelled = true` and a `scheduledDate` range, but the migration only adds the column. On a large `WorkflowReminder` table this is a full scan every 15 minutes. Add an index, preferably a partial index for cancelled reminders, or document why it is intentionally omitted.

title: Cancellations made shortly before a reminder's send time still deliver the email
body: Cancellation is now deferred to this cron, which cancels only reminders that are still in the future when it runs (and it runs every 15 minutes). A reminder marked `cancelled: true` whose `scheduledDate` falls between the cancellation and the next cron run is never cancelled at SendGrid, so the email is still delivered. Worse, the `deleteMany` at the top of the handler (lines 34-41) runs before the cancellation step and silently removes exactly those past-due rows, so the reminder disappears from the DB without ever having been cancelled and there is no trace left to retry. Since the whole point of the PR is that cancelled bookings must not receive reminders, the last ~15 minutes before a reminder fires are a hole that needs closing (e.g. cancel synchronously when the reminder is imminent, or run the canceller more frequently than the minimum remaining lead time).

title: The DB write that records the cancellation is fire-and-forget
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` now performs its side effect (either deleting the row or setting `cancelled: true`) internally, but here it is invoked inside an un-awaited `forEach`, so the handler can return before the Prisma update/delete is committed. Previously this block collected the `workflowReminder.deleteMany` promises and awaited them via `Promise.all`, so the DB state was guaranteed on return. On serverless (Vercel) the runtime may freeze/terminate right after the response, leaving the reminder un-cancelled - which means the workflow email is still sent for the cancelled booking, the exact bug this PR fixes. The same pattern appears in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966` and in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:378/521/576`; in `handleNewBooking` the surrounding `try/catch` is also dead code because the helper swallows its own errors. Collect and `await` these calls.

title: One SendGrid failure aborts cancellation for every other reminder and skips the deletes
body: The whole `for` loop is wrapped in a single `try/catch`. If `client.request` throws for any one reminder (SendGrid error, network hiccup, or the 100-pending-cancellations limit described in the PR description - which is still reachable under load, and is also hit by the synchronous `immediateDelete` path used by reschedule/workflow deletion), the loop is abandoned: all remaining reminders in that run stay scheduled, and `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is never reached, so the rows already POSTed are not deleted either. The error is only `console.log`ged, so nobody is alerted. Each reminder should be wrapped individually (and the delete awaited per item / the failures counted and reported) so one bad batch cannot silently let a whole hour's worth of cancelled reminders go out.

title: immediateDelete path leaves the workflowReminder row behind
body: When `immediateDelete` is true the function cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting or marking the row. That is fine for the workflow/step deletion callers (the row is removed by cascade), but `handleNewBooking` uses `immediateDelete: true` for rescheduled bookings, so the old booking's `WorkflowReminder` rows survive with `scheduled: true` and a `referenceId` pointing at a cancelled batch. They are only cleaned up later by the cron's blanket `deleteMany`. Any future code that inspects `workflowReminders` (or retries cancellation over them) will treat those as live reminders. Either delete the row in the immediate path or document why it must be left to the caller.

title: No test coverage for the new cancellation flow
body: The PR changes the contract of `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` and introduces a new deferred-cancellation lifecycle (`cancelled` flag -> cron -> SendGrid cancel -> row delete), but no tests are added. Nothing verifies the ordering problem with the past-due `deleteMany`, the behaviour for reminders without a `referenceId`, the retry/error behaviour of the cancel loop, or that a reschedule actually cancels the previous booking's reminders. A regression test around `scheduleEmailReminders` with a mocked SendGrid client would catch both the ordering hole and the loop-abort behaviour.

title: New cron query has no supporting index
body: The migration adds `cancelled` with no index, yet the every-15-minutes cron now runs `findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } } })` over the whole `WorkflowReminder` table (which grows with every booking × workflow step). Without a composite index on `(cancelled, scheduledDate)` (or at least `scheduledDate`) this is a full table scan on every run, and `cancelled` is also a nullable column with no default, so the index should be added together with `@default(false)` to keep the flag non-null for existing and future rows.

title: Workflow reminder cancellation is not awaited
body: The new calls to deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...) are made inside a synchronous forEach with no promise collected or awaited. deleteScheduledEmailReminder now performs async work (Prisma update/delete, and sometimes a SendGrid request), so the cancellation endpoint can return before that work finishes; on serverless runtimes the pending work may be terminated entirely. The same fire-and-forget pattern exists in handleNewBooking.ts around line 968, bookings.tsx around line 490, and workflows.tsx around lines 214/378/521/576. Consequence: a cancelled or rescheduled booking can leave its reminder active, so the workflow email is still sent, which is exactly the failure this PR is meant to fix.

title: One SendGrid cancellation error blocks all other cancellations
body: The entire cancellation loop is covered by one try/catch. If client.request fails for one reminder, execution jumps to the catch, so no later reminder in remindersToCancel is processed, and the Prisma delete promises already collected in workflowRemindersToDelete are never awaited. A single stale or failed batch_id can therefore leave many cancelled reminders active and allow their emails to be sent; successfully cancelled rows also remain in the database. Cancellations should be handled per reminder (or with allSettled), and rows should be deleted only after their own cancellation succeeds.

title: Cron window does not guarantee cancellation for imminent reminders
body: The cron only picks up cancelled reminders whose scheduledDate is at or before now + 1 hour, but the job runs every 15 minutes. A reminder cancelled just after a cron run and due in, say, 5-10 minutes will not be visited until the next cron run, after SendGrid has already sent the email. The one-hour lookahead does not fix near-term cancellations by itself; imminent reminders need immediate cancellation or a processing mechanism that can run before their send time.

title: Immediate cancellation path has no retry or DB cleanup
body: When immediateDelete is true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder sends the SendGrid cancel request and returns without setting cancelled = true or deleting the WorkflowReminder row. Errors are caught and only logged. handleNewBooking uses this immediate path when a booking is rescheduled, so a transient SendGrid/network failure leaves the old reminder scheduled with no cron retry, and even on success the old row remains scheduled in the database. A failed immediate cancellation should fall back to marking the reminder cancelled (or otherwise be retried), and successful cancellations should clean up the row where the caller does not cascade-delete it.

title: No test coverage for new cancellation lifecycle
body: No tests were added for the new cancelled flag, the cron cancellation/deletion flow, or the reschedule cancellation path. The previous implementation was wrong without being caught, so regressions here will silently send workflow emails again. Coverage should include: marking a reminder cancelled, the cron cancelling and deleting it, SendGrid failure behavior, reminders without referenceId, and rescheduled bookings cancelling old reminders.

title: Recurring-cancellation calendar deletes are no longer awaited before Promise.all
body: In the `allRemainingBookings` + `credentialId` branch, calendar deletions are collected by pushing into `apiDeletes` from inside `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })`. Because the callback is async and now contains an `await` before the first push, the callback yields immediately and `apiDeletes` is still empty when `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs later in the handler (line 652). The recurring-booking calendar events are therefore never awaited before the request returns, and any rejection from `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent` escapes as an unhandled rejection (which terminates Node by default). The sibling branch just below (lines 476-484) was correctly converted to a `for...of` loop with `await`; this branch needs the same conversion.

title: async forEach makes reschedule cancellations fire-and-forget and defeats the try/catch
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })` is used inside a `try { ... } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }`. `forEach` discards the promises returned by the async callback, so the surrounding try/catch can never observe a failure from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting`, and those failures become unhandled promise rejections (fatal by default in Node >= 15). `Reschedule` also resolves and returns `true` (and sends the reschedule email) before the external calendar/video events are actually deleted; in a serverless handler the process may be frozen at that point, leaving the old event on the organizer's calendar even though the booking is marked CANCELLED. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop inside the try block.

title: async forEach makes reschedule cancellations fire-and-forget and defeats the try/catch
body: Same defect as in the vital reschedule file: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })` returns immediately because `forEach` ignores the promises returned by the async callback. The outer `try/catch` around the loop therefore no longer catches errors from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting`, those errors surface as unhandled rejections, and the function resolves before the calendar/video deletions complete, so the old event may remain on the user's calendar after a reschedule. Replace the `forEach` with `await Promise.all(...map(...))` or a `for...of` loop with `await`.

title: requestReschedule deletions are started asynchronously and never awaited
body: The `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` block in the `requestReschedule` mutation discards every returned promise. Before this change the callback was synchronous, so the `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls were at least initiated synchronously in the handler; now they are deferred until after the surrounding synchronous code runs (i.e. potentially after `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` and after the mutation returns), and no failure from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` is observed or logged (unhandled rejection, fatal by default in Node). The old calendar/video event for the rescheduled booking can silently survive. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop with `await`.

title: `!calendar` early return skips cleanIntegrationKeys and sends raw credentials to the client
body: In `getConnectedCalendars`, when `getCalendar` returns null the function returns `{ integration, credentialId }` with the raw `integration` object. `integration` comes from `getApps(credentials)`, i.e. the app object that carries `credentials` (including the user's OAuth `key`) and `credential` — see how this same object is used at lines 27-30 of this file. The other two return paths correctly call `cleanIntegrationKeys(integration)` precisely to avoid leaking credentials to the client (there is even a comment "Don't leak credentials to the client"), but this path returns them verbatim, so any credential whose calendar implementation is missing/keyless will ship the user's secrets to the browser via the connectedCalendars endpoint. Pre-existing, but it is inside the function this PR modifies; the return should also be `{ integration: cleanIntegrationKeys(integration), credentialId }`.

title: getCalendar is called for non-calendar-variant apps and its promise is dropped
body: In `getCalendarCredentials`, `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` runs for every credential, but the result is only kept when `app.variant === "calendar"`; for other variants the promise is created and discarded. Now that `getCalendar` is async this is (a) a wasted dynamic `import()` of the app's calendar module for every non-calendar-variant app on every call, and (b) a floating promise whose rejection (e.g. the lazy import failing, or `calendarType.split` on a malformed credential type) becomes an unhandled rejection. Move the `getCalendar` call inside the `app.variant === "calendar"` branch.

title: Commented-out example points at a non-existent path
body: The template comment `// example: import("./example"),` references `./example`, but the example app directory in this package is `_example` (the previous comment was `// import * as example from "./_example";`). A developer copying/uncommenting this template will get a module-resolution error. It should read `// example: import("./_example"),`.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns calendar promises but remains synchronous
body: `getCalendar` was made async, but `getCalendarCredentials` still calls it synchronously and returns the promise as `calendar` in each result. `getConnectedCalendars` was patched to `await item.calendar`, but this exported function's contract silently changed: any other caller now receives a Promise where it previously received a Calendar and will call calendar methods on the promise. It also discards the promise entirely when `app.variant !== 'calendar'`, so a rejected dynamic import there becomes an unhandled rejection. Make `getCalendarCredentials` async and await the calendars (or update the type and every caller).

title: Recurring calendar deletions can be omitted from apiDeletes
body: In the recurring-cancellation branch the calendar credentials are processed with `.forEach(async ...)`, and the new `await getCalendar(credential)` is followed by `await calendar.deleteEvent(...)` before `apiDeletes.push(...)`. The `forEach` result is never awaited, so the handler reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` while `apiDeletes` is still empty or partial; recurring calendar events can be left on calendars or deleted only after the response, and rejections become unhandled. Collect the callbacks in a `Promise.all` over `map` and await the delete promises there.

title: Unawaited async forEach skips waiting for calendar event deletion
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` is not awaited. Since `getCalendar` is now awaited inside the callback, the function continues to `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` and returns before `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent` execute, and the surrounding try/catch cannot catch their rejections because they are floating promises. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` and await the deletion calls.

title: Unawaited async forEach skips waiting for calendar event deletion
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` is not awaited. Since `getCalendar` is now awaited inside the callback, the function continues to `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` and returns before `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent` execute, and the surrounding try/catch cannot catch their rejections because they are floating promises. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` and await the deletion calls.

title: requestReschedule does not await async calendar deletions
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` is not awaited. The mutation can return before old calendar/video references are deleted, and rejections from the new `await getCalendar` or the returned `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls are unhandled. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` and await the deletion promises.

title: Async forEach delays calendar deletions until after apiDeletes is awaited
body: This async callback now awaits `getCalendar` before pushing its `deleteEvent` promises into `apiDeletes`. The surrounding function continues synchronously to `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`, so `apiDeletes` is still empty when that array is evaluated. The recurring-cancellation path therefore marks bookings cancelled and returns without awaiting or observing the calendar deletions; failures become unhandled rejections and external calendar events/availability can remain stale. Use a `for...of` loop with `await` or `await Promise.all(credentials.map(async ...))` and collect the deletion promises before awaiting them.

title: Async forEach drops calendar/video deletion promises during reschedule
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` does not await the async callback. Because `getCalendar` is now awaited inside it, the callback suspends before calling `calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting`, so `Reschedule` can return before those integrations have run. The surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections from the callback either, so calendar/video events may remain after a reschedule and errors become unhandled rejections. Use `for...of` with `await` or `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.

title: Async forEach drops calendar/video deletion promises during reschedule
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` does not await the async callback. Because `getCalendar` is now awaited inside it, the callback suspends before calling `calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting`, so `Reschedule` can return before those integrations have run. The surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections from the callback either, so calendar/video events may remain after a reschedule and errors become unhandled rejections. Use `for...of` with `await` or `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.

title: requestReschedule does not await calendar/video deletions
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` is not awaited. With the new `await getCalendar(...)`, the callback suspends before invoking `calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting`, so `requestReschedule` proceeds to send the reschedule email and return while cancellations are still pending. Any rejected calendar/video deletion is also unhandled. This can leave old calendar/video events active after the user has been told the reschedule request succeeded. Await the callbacks via `for...of` or `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`.

title: Date override short-circuits the busy-time check
body: When a slot falls inside a user's date override, `dateOverrideExist` is true and `checkIfIsAvailable` returns true before reaching the `busy.every(...)` check at the bottom. A date override replaces working hours, not existing bookings/calendar busy time, so a fixed host with an override 10:00-14:00 and an existing booking 11:00-12:00 will still make the 11:00 round-robin slot pass. That can lead to double booking the fixed host. Only bypass the normal working-hours check for an override; the busy check must still run.

title: Date override check accepts slots only partially inside the override
body: The containment test rejects a slot only when it ends at/before the override start or when it starts after the override end. It never checks that the slot end is within the override end (or that the slot start is at/after the override start). For an override 10:00-11:00, a 60-minute slot 09:30-10:30 or 10:30-11:30 falls through, sets `dateOverrideExist`, and returns true. In round-robin events, aggregate slots generated from another host can therefore be accepted for a fixed host even though they are only partially within the fixed host's override. Require the whole slot to be inside the override.

title: Working-hours end uses the slot start minute instead of the slot end minute
body: `const end` is computed from `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, exactly the same value as `start`. For a 60-minute slot starting 12:00 when a fixed host's working hours end at 12:30, `end > workingHour.endTime` is `720 > 750`, so the slot is not rejected even though it ends at 13:00. This lets round-robin fixed hosts be booked outside their working hours. Compute `end` from `slotEndTime` (or compare timestamps) and reject slots whose end exceeds the working-hour end.

title: Working-hours check tests only the first matching day and ignores days with no hours
body: `workingHours.find(...)` returns true as soon as it sees the first entry whose `days` includes the slot's UTC day and the slot is outside that one interval. With split availability (09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00), a 13:30 slot is outside the first interval, so the host is marked unavailable even though the second interval contains it. Conversely, if no working-hour entry includes the slot's day, `find` returns undefined and the function falls through to the busy check, treating the fixed host as available on a day they do not work. The check should test whether the slot is inside any matching interval and reject it when no interval matches.

title: Zero-length date override comparison uses object identity
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct Dayjs object references, so it is always false. If a date override with equal start and end is used to represent an unavailable day, that case is never detected; only slots before the override are rejected, and the slot at the override start can be treated as available. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare timestamps.

title: Date override date comparison mixes server-local and UTC dates
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD')` formats in the server's local timezone, while `slotStartTime` is a `.utc()` Dayjs. On self-hosted servers not running in UTC, the shifted override date is compared to a UTC slot date, so date overrides can be missed or matched to the wrong day. Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` (and end) for the date/range calculations so both sides use UTC.

title: Active date overrides are filtered by wall-clock date, not actual UTC/invitee date
body: `activeOverrides` compares `dayjs.utc(override.start)`—where `override.start` is the organizer's wall-clock date/time stored as UTC—against the invitee day boundaries. The new conversion below explicitly treats it as wall time by subtracting the organizer offset, but this filter does not. For example, with an organizer in UTC+14, an override at local D 01:00 is stored as D 01:00Z but actually occurs at D-1 11:00Z; when an invitee in UTC views day D-1, the stored value is outside that invitee day, so the override is ignored and normal working hours are used. Convert the override to actual UTC (or to the invitee timezone) before deciding whether it belongs to the invitee day.

title: No test covers the fixed-host round-robin date override behavior or the new availability branches
body: The only added test changes the invitee timezone for a personal event. It does not exercise the PR's main claim: a round-robin event with a fixed host whose date override should constrain available slots. There are also no tests for a fixed host with busy time inside an override, slots partially overlapping an override, or split working hours. These missing cases would have caught the early return that skips busy checks and the working-hours containment bugs.

title: Date override short-circuits before the busy check, so already-booked slots are reported available
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, once a slot falls inside a date override the function returns `true` at line 134, before the `busy.every(...)` check at the end of the function. A date override is only meant to replace the working-hours check; the host's `busy` entries (Cal bookings plus connected-calendar events) must still make the slot unavailable. Because personal events mark every user as `isFixed`, and this helper is used for both the fixed-host filter and the loose-host filter, any host with a date override will be shown as available during a time they are already booked, producing bookable slots that double-book the host. The new tests place no booking on the override day, so this is not caught.

title: Working-hours check uses the slot start time for both `start` and `end`
body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start`, so the `end > workingHour.endTime` condition only re-tests the start time and can never detect a slot that begins inside the host's working hours but ends after them (e.g. host available until 10:00, 60-minute slot at 09:30). Such slots are then accepted for fixed hosts in round-robin events, allowing a booking outside the fixed host's working hours, which is the situation this change is supposed to prevent. `end` must be derived from the slot end (`slotEndTime`), not the slot start.

title: `workingHours.find` rejects a slot when any same-day range does not contain it and never rejects a non-working day
body: The block rejects the slot whenever `workingHours.find(...)` returns a range whose `days` include the weekday and whose bounds do not contain the slot. This has two wrong consequences: (a) if a host has more than one availability range on the same weekday (the `Availability` model/API permits multiple rows for a date), a slot inside range 2 is still rejected because it is outside range 1; (b) if no range exists for that weekday at all (the host does not work that day), nothing matches and the slot is accepted, so a round-robin event still offers slots on days the fixed host is unavailable.
