The correct test is 'reject unless some range covers the slot', e.g. `workingHours.some(w => w.days.includes(day) && start >= w.startTime && end <= w.endTime)`.

title: Multiple date overrides on the same day: first non-matching override marks the slot unavailable
body: `dateOverrides.find(...)` stops as soon as the callback returns `true`, and the callback returns `true` when the override is on the slot's day but the slot is outside that override's range. If a user has two overrides on the same date (e.g. 10:00-11:00 and 14:00-15:00, which the `Availability` table permits), a slot inside the second range is reported as unavailable because it is outside the first. The day should be classified with `some()` - is the slot covered by at least one override on that date - before deciding availability.

title: Dayjs objects compared with `===`, so the zero-length-override check never fires
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares object references, not times, and `.add()` returns new Dayjs instances, so this is always false. The intended handling of zero-length (unavailable-day) overrides is therefore dead code, and only the following instant comparisons apply. Use `.isSame(...)` instead.

title: Override day match mixes local and UTC dates and only looks at the override start
body: `dayjs(date.start)` is a Dayjs in the server's local timezone, while `slotStartTime` was created with `.utc()`, so the `format("YYYY MM DD")` comparison compares a local date against a UTC date. On servers not running in UTC (and near day boundaries on any server) the override is attached to the wrong date. In addition, the match uses only the converted `start` instant, so an override whose real-UTC window crosses midnight (typical for early-morning overrides in positive-offset organizer timezones, e.g. 05:00-06:30 Asia/Kolkata) is not recognized for the slots after UTC midnight; those slots then fall through to the working-hours check and are wrongly dropped. Build the override window with `dayjs.utc(...)` and test whether the slot overlaps that window instead of string-comparing dates.

title: No coverage for the fixed-host round-robin fix or for a booking inside a date override
body: The added test only asserts the UTC output of `getSlots` for a second invitee timezone. All asserted slots (08:30-12:30 UTC) also lie inside the fixture's normal working hours (04:00-12:30 UTC), so the assertions still pass if the new date-override/working-hours logic in `checkIfIsAvailable` is removed entirely - the test does not exercise the router change. The PR's headline fix (a round-robin event whose fixed host has a date override) has no test, and no test puts an existing booking inside the override window, so the busy-check bypass in `checkIfIsAvailable` is not detected.

title: Test comment gives the wrong reason for the expected result
body: The comment `// it should return the same as this is the utc time` is misleading: the invitee gets the same UTC slots in both cases because the slots are absolute instants and the override is anchored to the organizer's timezone, not because 'this is the utc time'. As written it suggests the second assertion is trivially true, whereas it is precisely the assertion that fails with the old `getUTCHours()` logic (which would yield 08:00/09:00/10:00/11:00 UTC for Asia/Dhaka). The comment should explain that the override must represent the same absolute time regardless of the viewer's timezone.

title: Date override path skips busy-time checks
body: `checkIfIsAvailable` now returns `true` as soon as a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot is not completely outside it, before reaching the `busy.every(...)` check. Existing bookings or calendar busy times that fall inside a date override are therefore ignored when filtering fixed/loose hosts. A host with an override 10:00-11:00 and a booking 10:00-10:30 will still be offered at 10:00, allowing a double booking. The override check should only decide whether the slot is within the override; busy-time filtering must still run afterward.

title: Partially overlapping slots are accepted for date overrides
body: The override containment logic only rejects a slot when it ends at/before the override start or starts strictly after the override end. A slot that starts before the override and ends inside it is treated as available, and a slot starting exactly at the override end is also accepted because the final condition uses `isAfter(end)` instead of also rejecting `isSame(end)`. For example, with a fixed host override 10:00-11:00 and an event slot 09:30-10:30 generated from another host, the fixed host check passes even though the fixed host is only available 10:00-11:00. The slot should be available only when `slotStartTime >= overrideStart` and `slotEndTime <= overrideEnd`.

title: Working-hours check rejects valid split availability
body: The working-hours validation uses `find` with a callback that returns true when the slot is outside that particular working-hour range. If a host has two same-day ranges, e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected because the second range returns true when `start < workingHour.startTime`. Since this check runs for fixed hosts and personal-event users, split availability becomes largely unavailable. The code should use `some`/`every` to reject only when no same-day range contains the slot.

title: Slot end is never checked against working-hour end
body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime.hour()` and `slotStartTime.minute()` instead of `slotEndTime`, so `end > workingHour.endTime` can never detect a slot extending past the working hours when the start is inside the range. In a round-robin event with a fixed host whose availability ends before the event slot's end, a 60-minute slot starting at 10:30 passes a working-hour range ending at 11:00. This should use the slot end time for the upper-bound check.

title: Zero-length date override check compares Dayjs objects by identity
body: The condition `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two separate Dayjs object instances and is always false. A date override with identical start and end, which is the representation this code is trying to treat as a fully unavailable day, is not handled; for a slot starting exactly at the override start, the other boundary checks also fail to reject it, so a slot can leak through. Use `.isSame()` or compare timestamps.

title: Date override day filter ignores converted invitee date
body: `activeOverrides` still filters by comparing the organizer's original `override.start` against `startOfInviteeDay`, without applying the timezone offset computed below. This breaks date overrides when the converted time falls on a different invitee day. Example: 09:30-18:00 Asia/Kolkata on Aug 15 is 21:00 Aug 14-04:30 Aug 15 in America/Los_Angeles, but the override is not active for the invitee Aug 14 day; it is instead applied one day later on Aug 15. The filter needs to use the same converted instant as the minute calculation.

title: No test covers round-robin fixed-host date overrides
body: The only added test checks a personal event with a +30 minute timezone difference, where the override stays on the same invitee day. It does not cover the PR's main behavior: a round-robin event with a fixed host date override, a negative timezone offset/day rollover, or a date override combined with an existing busy booking. The new `checkIfIsAvailable` override/working-hours logic is therefore untested for the cases most likely to regress, including skipping busy times or accepting partially overlapping slots.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category has no matching setting row
body: The migration runs `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` for the `embed_category` lookup. That setting was optional and `site_settings` only stores rows that were changed, so when it is absent (or blank, so the join matches no category) `execute` returns no rows, `[0]` is nil, and `['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. The fallback lookup for `uncategorized_category_id` makes the same nil assumption. Use `first`/`find_by` and guard before dereferencing.

title: Migration copies old host values raw and interpolates them into SQL
body: The old `embeddable_hosts` SiteSetting accepted schemes and paths (the removed code parsed them with URI and old specs used `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234`). The migration puts `h` verbatim into the new column via `INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, bypassing `EmbeddableHost` normalization and also not escaping quotes. Records like `http://eviltrout.com` or `example.com/1234` can never match `record_for_host`'s `URI(referer).host` comparison, so existing embeddings stop working after upgrade; a quote in the old setting also breaks the migration. Normalize and parameterize the insert.

title: Host matching drops the port while validation allows it
body: Validation explicitly allows an optional `:port`, and `before_validation` keeps it (it only strips the scheme and path). But `record_for_host` matches `URI(referer).host`, which omits the port, against the full stored `host`. A saved host such as `example.com:3000` therefore never matches a referer whose host is `example.com`. Either reject ports in validation or compare `host:port` consistently. The bound lookup value is also not downcased, so a mixed-case referer host can miss a lower-cased row.

title: Host validation rejects valid TLDs longer than five characters
body: The regex requires the TLD to be `[a-z]{2,5}`, so valid hostnames such as `example.museum`, `example.travel`, or modern long TLDs cannot be saved as embeddable hosts. Admins cannot configure otherwise valid embedding sources. Use a looser hostname check or rely on URI parsing.

title: No uniqueness constraint on host makes the category mapping ambiguous
body: Neither the model nor the migration enforces a unique host (case-insensitively). The admin UI can create two rows for the same host with different categories, and the migration can copy duplicates from the old newline list. `record_for_host` then returns whichever row the database returns first, making the category used for new embedded topics non-deterministic. Add a case-insensitive uniqueness validation and matching unique index.

title: Missing ids cause 500 instead of a clean not-found response
body: `update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If the id does not exist, `save_host(nil)` calls `nil.host=` and `nil.destroy` raises. A stale admin UI request gets a 500 instead of a clean 404/JSON error. Use `find_by` and return an error when nil.

title: Plural embedded ids are deleted even when hydration fails
body: In the new plural branch, `obj[k].map(...)` can return `undefined` entries when the side-loaded collection is absent or partial, but the code still assigns `obj[plural] = hydrated` and deletes the original `*_ids` key. Unlike the singular branch, it never checks whether lookup succeeded. That silently changes the model shape and loses ids for any rest_serializer payload that sends `foo_ids` without all `foo` objects (or without a `foos` collection). Preserve the original ids unless every reference resolves, and don't create arrays of undefined.

title: Feed imports can lose their configured category after this change
body: The category for every imported embed is now `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url).try(:category_id)`. Feed polling imports arbitrary feed item URLs through `TopicEmbed.import` without going through `TopicRetriever`'s host check; if the feed host was not also in the old `embeddable_hosts` list, the migration creates no record for it and `category_id` becomes nil. Existing feed-polling installs will start creating uncategorized topics (or fail when uncategorized topics are disabled) instead of using the old `embed_category` setting. Migration/fallback needs to cover the feed-polling host.

title: UI clears the category after saving with the uncategorized fallback
body: When saving a host without a selected category, the server assigns `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, but the success handler overwrites `host.category` with `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`, where `categoryId` is null. The table then shows a blank category until reload even though the host was saved to the uncategorized category. Use the category returned/assigned by the server, or map the null id to the uncategorized category.

title: Embedded test requests fruit 2 but only ever checks fruit 1
body: The test now calls `store.find('fruit', 2)`, but the pretender's `/fruits/:id` handler always returns `fruits[0]` (apple, `color_ids: [1,2]`), and the assertions still expect `[1,2]`. The test passes without exercising banana/id 2 (`color_ids: [3]`), so it does not verify id-specific embedded hydration. Update the fixture to return the requested fruit or keep the test on id 1.

title: Admin endpoint specs only assert inheritance
body: The new admin controller specs contain only a subclass assertion. None of the new create/update/destroy behavior is tested: host normalization, category assignment/fallback, missing ids, destroy, or authorization. These endpoints currently contain 500 paths, and the migration behavior is also untested. Add request specs for the happy path and missing-id/error cases.

title: Migration can crash when embed_category is unset or does not match a category
body: The migration reads `execute(...)[0]['id']` without checking that the query returned a row. `embed_category` defaults to an empty string and commonly will not join to any category, so the result is empty and indexing `[0]` returns nil; the migration then raises on `['id']` and aborts the upgrade. The fallback query for `uncategorized_category_id` has the same risk if that setting row is absent. Use a nil-safe first-row lookup and fall back when no category exists.

title: Old host values are interpolated raw into SQL and inserted without normalization
body: The INSERT is built as `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting. A value containing a single quote breaks the migration (and is an injection primitive), and values are inserted directly without going through `EmbeddableHost`'s scheme/path trimming. Existing settings that contain `http://example.com` or `https://example.com/path` will be stored in that raw form, but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` queries `lower(host) = uri.host`, so those hosts can never match after the upgrade and embedding silently stops. Quote the value and normalize each host before insertion, preferably by creating records through the model.

title: Blank host raises NoMethodError instead of adding a validation error
body: The `before_validation` hook calls `self.host.sub!` unconditionally. If `embeddable_host[host]` is missing or nil, `host` is nil and the admin create/update request raises NoMethodError before validations run, returning a 500 instead of a validation response. Guard against a blank host or rely on a presence validation before string manipulation.

title: Hosts with an explicit port can be saved but can never match a request
body: The format validator accepts an optional `:port`, and the before_validation hook does not remove it, so a host such as `example.com:3000` can be stored. `record_for_host` uses `URI(host).host`, which drops the port, and then binds only `example.com` into `lower(host) = ?`; a stored port can therefore never match. Strip the port when saving or include it when matching.

title: Host validation rejects valid TLDs longer than five characters
body: The new format regex uses `[a-z]{2,5}` for the TLD. Valid hosts such as `example.museum`, `example.travel`, and many newer TLDs cannot be added, even though they are valid embeddable hosts and could be used with the old site setting. Allow longer TLDs or use a dedicated hostname validator.

title: Updating or deleting a missing embeddable host returns a 500
body: Both `update` and `destroy` fetch with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and immediately call `save_host(host)` or `host.destroy`. If the id is invalid or the record was deleted concurrently, `host` is nil and the request raises NoMethodError instead of returning a 404/error response. Use `find_by` with a nil check, or `find` with `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` handling.

title: Saving a host without a chosen category overwrites category with undefined
body: After a successful save, the component sets `host.category` from its local `categoryId`, not from the server-returned `category_id`. For a new host, or when the chooser is cleared, `categoryId` is null while the controller has assigned `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`; `Discourse.Category.findById(null)` returns undefined. The row then loses its category badge, and the next click on Edit throws when `edit()` reads `this.get('host.category.id')`. Update `categoryId`/`category` from the saved host response instead.

title: Fruit-by-id fixture ignores the requested id
body: The `/fruits/:id` handler always returns `fruits[0]`, whose id is 1, even though the updated store test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)`. The test therefore does not verify that `find` requests and hydrates the requested record and passes even though the handler returned the wrong fruit. Return the record matching `request.params.id` and assert the fetched id in the test.

title: Category and embeddable-host fabricator files are swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines only `:embeddable_host`, while all category fabricators including `:private_category` were moved into `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. The suite may still pass because Fabrication loads all fabricator files, but this makes file-based loading/tooling and future maintenance confusing; restore the original contents to the matching filenames.

title: expandable_first_post test no longer tests the embeddable-host condition
body: After `Topic#expandable_first_post?` stopped checking `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts`, this test still says 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' but only passes because `has_topic_embed?` is false. The inner block also fabricates a host that the method no longer consults. The test no longer covers the behavior described and can hide regressions around removing hosts; rename/restructure it or explicitly test the current `embed_truncate?`/`has_topic_embed?` conditions.

title: Migration aborts when embed_category is blank/unset
body: `category_id` is computed with `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. The legacy `embed_category` default is an empty string, so for any site that never explicitly set it (or set it to a name that no longer exists) the INNER JOIN returns zero rows, `[0]` is `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration after the table was already created. Crucially, this is exactly the scenario the following `if category_id == 0` fallback is meant to handle, but that fallback is unreachable because the exception fires first. Guard the result before casting (e.g. `(...[0].try(:[], 'id') || 0).to_i`); the same unsafe pattern exists for the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15.

title: Host value interpolated directly into raw SQL
body: The INSERT does `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`, interpolating the legacy host string `h` straight into the statement. If any stored value contains a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) the statement becomes malformed and the migration fails; since the source is admin-controlled setting data, it is also an injection vector. Use a parameterized insert or model creation/`quote` instead of string interpolation.

title: Legacy host entries copied without normalizing scheme/path
body: The old `embeddable_hosts` setting allowed entries with a scheme and path (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com`, `https://example.com/1234`, as used by the old specs), and they are copied verbatim into the new `host` column. But `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against the bare `URI#host` (`eviltrout.com`), so a stored `http://eviltrout.com` never matches. After upgrade, every site that configured hosts with a scheme/path has all embeds rejected with `invalid referer host`. Normalize each value (strip scheme and path, as the model's `before_validation` does) during migration.

title: Host matching is case-sensitive for the caller's host
body: `record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but passes the raw `URI#host`, which preserves case. Because only the column is lowercased, a referer whose hostname contains any uppercase letter (e.g. `Example.com`) will not match the stored `example.com`, so `host_allowed?` returns false and embedding is incorrectly blocked. Downcase the parameter (`host.downcase`) to match the column lowering.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host
body: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` without a nil guard. If a record is saved with a blank/missing `host` (e.g. the admin form posts no host, or `EmbeddableHost.new` is persisted), `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError and the request returns 500 instead of a normal validation failure. Use `self.host = self.host.to_s...` or guard with `if self.host`.

title: update/destroy raise 500 on unknown id instead of 404
body: `update` and `destroy` do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` with no nil check. A request for a non-existent id raises NoMethodError on `nil` and returns 500 rather than 404. `save_host` also assumes `params[:embeddable_host]` is present, so a malformed payload crashes the same way.

title: Embedded hosts missing from response root; UI list will be empty
body: `has_many :embeddable_hosts, ..., embed: :ids` emits only the `embeddable_host_ids` array on the `embedding` object; it does not put the `embeddable_hosts` collection in the response root unless `include: true` is set. The JS store's `_hydrateEmbedded` (mirrored by the `create-pretender` fixtures, which return both `*_ids` fields and root collections) needs `root['embeddable_hosts']` to rebuild the records; without it `embedding.embeddable_hosts` hydrates to an empty (or undefined-filled) array, so the admin Embedding page shows no hosts. Add `include: true`.

title: Fabricator files were swapped
body: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`). It only works because every file under `spec/fabricators` is loaded, but the filenames no longer describe their contents and will confuse future edits. Move each fabricator back into the matching file.

title: New admin controllers only tested for inheritance
body: Both `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and `Admin::EmbeddingController` specs only assert that the class subclasses `Admin::AdminController`; none of `create`/`update`/`destroy` (including not-found ids and blank host input) is exercised. This is why the 500-causing nil handling in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` is not caught. Add request specs for the happy path and the not-found/invalid-input paths.

title: Test name no longer matches what it verifies
body: `topic.rb` removed the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` check from `expandable_first_post?`, but this test still claims to cover the 'embeddable_host is blank' case. It now passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is stubbed false, so it would not catch a regression in the embed gating (there is no longer any such gate). Rename or rewrite the test to assert the actual conditions.

title: New downsize overload silently shadows the 4-argument downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height)
body: `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149) redefines the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` method declared at line 145; in Ruby the later definition wins, so the 4-argument form is unreachable. Any caller passing explicit dimensions (e.g. `OptimizedImage.downsize(src, dst, 1024, 768)`) is now dispatched to the new method with `dimensions = 1024` and `opts = 768`; `optimize` then evaluates `opts[:allow_animation]` and raises `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for 768:Integer` instead of producing a `1024x768` instruction. Even when no exception is raised, `dimensions` is a bare Integer, yielding a broken `-resize` argument. Callers elsewhere in the codebase or scripts that use the width/height form will break silently. Remove the four-argument overload or give the string-dimensions entry point a distinct name.

title: Downsizing an animated GIF keeps only the first frame when allow_animated_thumbnails is off
body: The controller's new resize path calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. When that setting is false (the default), `optimize` selects `downsize_instructions`, whose command contains `#{from}[0]`, i.e. only the first frame of a multi-frame GIF. Because the downsized temp file replaces the upload, an animated GIF larger than `max_image_size_kb` is permanently stored as a static single-frame image, silently destroying the user's animation. The animated instruction set is only used when the setting is explicitly enabled. Animated uploads should either always go through the animated/`gifsicle` path or be exempted from automatic downsizing.

title: Downsize loop with at most five 80% steps cannot bring files more than ~3x the limit under the limit
body: Repeatedly applying `-resize 80%` five times yields only 0.8^5 ≈ 0.33 of the original, so a file more than roughly 3x `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` is still oversized after the loop and `Upload.create_for` then rejects it. The advertised feature (accept large images by shrinking them) therefore still fails for genuinely large uploads, e.g. a 10MB image on a 1MB limit. Each pass is also a separate lossy re-encode (no `-quality` specified), so intermediate steps degrade the image more than necessary. The required scale factor should be computed from `tempfile.size / limit` (or the loop should recompute a percentage from the current size) rather than using fixed 80% steps.

title: Resize loop runs ImageMagick on SVG uploads, which convert cannot faithfully handle
body: The guard only checks `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, and that helper's image list includes SVG, so an SVG larger than `max_image_size_kb` is fed to `OptimizedImage.downsize` → `convert`. `OptimizedImage.create_for` deliberately special-cases `.svg` (it copies the file instead of calling `resize`), showing that `convert` is not suitable for vector files. The result is either a rewritten/rasterized file different from what the user uploaded (data loss) or a failed `convert`; in the failure case the loop still spawns five pointless `convert` processes per upload before giving up. Exclude SVG (and any format that cannot round-trip through `convert`) from the resize loop.

title: Client upload limit hard-coded to 10MB, ignoring max_image_size_kb/max_attachment_size_kb site settings
body: `validateUploadedFile` previously derived the limit from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`; it now always uses `10 * 1024` KB for both images and attachments. Attachments are not auto-downsized on the server, so sites configured with a smaller `max_attachment_size_kb` will now accept up to 10MB in the browser and only fail later with a less clear server error (or the setting is effectively bypassed). The same applies to images where an admin deliberately configured a limit below 10MB. In addition, the 413 handler at line 246 now reports `max_size_kb: 10MB` regardless of the web server's real limit, so the error message can be wrong. The limit should stay driven by the site settings (or a dedicated setting for the resize threshold).

title: No tests for the new automatic downsizing behavior or the OptimizedImage API refactor
body: The PR adds a multi-iteration in-place resize loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` and changes the public signatures of `OptimizedImage.resize/downsize/optimize`, but no specs were added or updated. Tests covering (a) an oversized image that must be shrunk, (b) a file that remains oversized after five attempts, (c) an animated GIF and an SVG upload, and (d) a call to `downsize` with explicit width/height would have caught the shadowed-method bug and the first-frame truncation. Please add model/controller specs for these paths.

title: Second `self.downsize` definition silently replaces the width/height version and breaks existing callers
body: The file now defines `self.downsize` twice: line 145 keeps the old signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts = {})` and line 149 adds `(from, to, dimensions, opts = {})`. In Ruby the later definition wins, so the 5-argument form at line 145 is dead code. Any code that still calls the old signature (e.g. `ImageSizer.downsize(from, to, width, height, opts)`, scripts, or plugins that pass width and height) now raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)` on every invocation, so whatever that path did (avatars/attachment/post image downsizing) stops working at runtime. The old arity should be preserved in a single method that accepts either a dimensions string or width+height (e.g. a splat/branch), with a test for both call forms.

title: Downsize loop ignores failure and never verifies the result, so oversized images are stored silently
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false when ImageMagick/gifsicle fails (corrupt file, unsupported format, missing binaries), and the return value is discarded here. When it fails the temp file is unchanged, so the `while` condition stays true and the identical expensive conversion is executed up to 5 times. When the loop exits, there is no check that the file actually got under `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (5 passes of 80% may be insufficient for a large image and a small limit), and nothing rejects the upload. The result is that `max_image_size_kb` is silently bypassed for images that cannot be reduced, and up to five image-conversion subprocesses are spent on the request/deferred job for nothing. Break out of the loop when `downsize` returns false and return an error to the user if the final size still exceeds the limit. The guard is also only extension based (`FileHelper.is_image?`), so a non-image file named `*.jpg` triggers the same five doomed conversions.

title: In-place downsize destroys the original: animated GIFs lose their animation and JPEGs are re-encoded repeatedly
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` rewrites the upload's temp file in place, i.e. the only copy of the user's file is destructively modified. The non-animated instructions use `convert #{from}[0]`, which selects only the first frame, so with the default `allow_animated_thumbnails` disabled a large animated GIF is replaced by a single static frame and the animation is irrecoverably lost. Iterating the loop also re-encodes the same JPEG up to five times, compounding generation loss. Downsize into a separate temp file, never replace multi-frame GIFs when animation cannot be preserved, and only swap in the result when it is genuinely smaller.

title: Percentage dimensions passed by the new caller are not valid for the gifsicle (`--resize-fit`) path
body: The controller calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`. For animated GIFs with `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled, `optimize` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated` -> `resize_instructions_animated`, which emits `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%`. `--resize-fit` expects a `WIDTHxHEIGHT` pair (or `--scale 0.8x0.8`), not a percentage, so gifsicle exits non-zero, `convert_with` returns false, the GIF is never shrunk, and (combined with the ignored return value above) the loop burns all five attempts and then stores the oversized file. Pass pixel dimensions for the animated path, or use `--scale`.

title: Client-side size limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring the configured site settings
body: `maxSizeKB` is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, and the 413 handler at line 246 similarly reports a fabricated 10240 KB maximum. Consequences: (1) admins can no longer constrain what the client lets users select; (2) the same 10MB cap is applied to attachments, which the new server-side downsize logic does not touch, so a multi-megabyte attachment passes client validation and is only rejected (by the still-configured server limit) after the whole body has been uploaded; (3) the displayed `max_size_kb` in error messages no longer matches the actual server/nginx limit. Read the site settings and only relax the cap for images that the server will downsize.

title: API URL downloads now capped at a hardcoded 10MB instead of `max_image_size_kb`, ignoring configuration in both directions
body: `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` became `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`. An API client can now make the server fetch and process up to 10MB from an arbitrary URL regardless of the admin's configured image limit (followed by up to five ImageMagick runs per request), which is a resource-amplification change not controlled by any setting. Conversely, if an admin configures `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB, API URL uploads that used to be accepted now fail: `FileHelper.download` returns nil (the `rescue nil`) and the following `tempfile.size` raises `NoMethodError`, returning a 500 instead of a meaningful validation error. The download cap should be derived from the configured limits, not a constant.

title: Public `OptimizedImage.optimize` arity changed and `OptimizedImage.dimensions` removed without updating callers
body: `self.optimize` changed from `(operation, from, to, width, height, opts)` to `(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts)`, and the public helper `self.dimensions(width, height)` was deleted. Only three files are touched by this PR, so any other caller (plugins, maintenance scripts, specs) that used either method with the old signature now fails with `ArgumentError`/`NoMethodError`. Either keep backwards-compatible signatures or grep and update every in-repo caller in the same change.

title: No tests for the new automatic-downsize behaviour or the changed `downsize` signature
body: The PR adds an untested upload path and an untested change to `OptimizedImage.downsize`, which is why the broken overload and the ignored-failure loop above were not caught. Add specs covering: uploading an image larger than `max_image_size_kb` results in a stored file at or below the limit; an image that cannot be downsized yields an error rather than a silently oversized upload; an animated GIF with `allow_animated_thumbnails` disabled/enabled; and `OptimizedImage.downsize` called both with a dimensions string and with width/height.

title: Second `downsize` definition silently replaces the width/height overload
body: The file now defines `self.downsize` twice: the pre-existing `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 and the newly added `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the four-argument form quietly disappears. Existing callers using `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height)` will bind `height` to `opts`, and `optimize` later evaluates `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer, raising NoMethodError; callers passing five arguments raise ArgumentError. This is a public class-method contract break and will also break any existing specs. Remove or rename one overload (or dispatch on argument count) and update callers.

title: Downsize loop ignores failures and proceeds with an oversized or corrupt file
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` when the ImageMagick/gifsicle command fails or the output cannot be written, but the loop ignores the return value and merely decrements `attempt`. After five failures it exits and `Upload.create_for` is called with the original tempfile, so an image still larger than `max_image_size_kb` (or a partially written file) can be persisted as an upload, with no error returned to the user. There is also no final size check after the loop. Check the downsize result/final size and reject with a clear error instead of silently storing the oversized file.

title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores per-type site settings
body: Both client-side checks were changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (and `max_image_size_kb` in the 413 handler at line 246) to a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. This raises the client-side limit for attachments to 10MB regardless of `max_attachment_size_kb`, so files the admin disallowed pass validation and are sent to the server. For images, an admin who configures `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB now sees valid uploads rejected, while an unlimited (0) setting is effectively capped at 10MB. The 10MB constant is duplicated in the 413 handler, so the two can drift. Use the site setting, or `max(setting, 10MB)` only for images, and share a single constant.

title: API download cap hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring configured limits
body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the configured limit with a fixed 10MB. If `max_image_size_kb` or the attachment limit is configured higher than 10MB, permitted API uploads now fail; if configured lower, the server will download and store files larger than the site's limit (non-images are never downsized). The same 10MB value is also duplicated in the JavaScript client, so client and server limits can silently diverge. Derive the download limit from the relevant site setting, with the 10MB floor only if that is the intended behavior for images.

title: Animated GIF downsize passes a percentage to gifsicle
body: This call passes dimensions `"80%"` together with `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`. When `optimize` selects the animated path (for a `from` path ending in `.GIF`), `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which builds `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80% ...`. gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects a `WxH` value, not a percentage, so the command fails, the loop burns all five attempts, and the oversized GIF is uploaded unchanged. If the temp path does not end in `.GIF`, the animated branch is not selected at all. Pass pixel dimensions (or use the percentage only with `convert`), and ensure the animated path is actually selected for browser uploads.

title: No tests for the new auto-downsize behavior
body: The PR adds non-trivial branching (image vs non-image, successful downsize, downsize failure, animated GIFs, oversized files, API url uploads) without any specs. Tests exercising these paths would have caught the overridden `downsize` signature and the invalid `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%` command. Add coverage for `create_upload` downsize behavior and the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions)` overload.

title: Explicit render in perform_show_response breaks canonical URL on topic pages
body: Adding `render :show` inside `perform_show_response` causes the normal `show` action to render before it executes `canonical_url` (line 87). `canonical_url` sets `@canonical_url` for the layout, so topic show pages will no longer emit the canonical link (or will use a stale one). Move the canonical URL assignment before `perform_show_response`, or render explicitly only from `unsubscribe`.

title: Unsubscribe crashes on missing TopicUser and bypasses TopicUser.change
body: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil whenever a logged-in user visits the unsubscribe URL without an existing topic_users row (for example a direct visit or a stale email link), and the next `tu.notification_level` call raises NoMethodError, returning a 500. Even when the row exists, assigning the level and calling `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, so `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id` are not updated and the `notification_level_change` MessageBus event is not published, leaving the topic's notification reason stale. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)`, which upserts and goes through the normal path.

title: State-changing unsubscribe action is a GET without a CSRF/token check
body: `unsubscribe` changes the current user's notification level in response to a plain GET and is authorized only by the session cookie. A third-party page can therefore embed `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` as an image/link and mute a logged-in user's topic (and email link scanners can trigger it too). Use a signed per-user/per-topic token in the emailed URL, or require a POST with the normal CSRF protection.

title: Unsubscribe route name does not match the added template path
body: The route is declared at top level as `topicUnsubscribe`, so Ember's default template lookup is `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`. The PR adds `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which is the path for a nested route named `topic.unsubscribe`, not for a top-level `topicUnsubscribe` route. As written the new URL has no template and will render blank or throw a template-not-found error. Either nest the route under the `topic` resource as `this.route('unsubscribe', { path: '/unsubscribe' })` or rename the added template to `topic-unsubscribe.hbs`.

title: Unsubscribe only downgrades watching/tracking users to regular
body: When the user's level is tracking or watching, the action sets it to regular instead of muted. Regular still sends notifications for replies and mentions, so the page text 'You will stop receiving notifications' is false and a mention/reply email can keep arriving after the user clicks the unsubscribe link. Set the level to muted when the intent is to stop notifications, or change the branch and copy to describe a downgrade.

title: No coverage for the new unsubscribe behavior
body: The spec change only adds `unsubscribe_url` to the builder options; it does not assert that the rendered body or HTML actually contains the per-topic unsubscribe URL. There are also no controller/route specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (missing TopicUser, watching/tracking to regular/muted, slug redirect) or for the new Ember route. The nil crash and the notification-level behavior above would pass CI.

title: New locale interpolation makes unsubscribe_url mandatory for all add_unsubscribe_link emails
body: `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder` calls this translation from both `body` and `html_part` whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, and only UserNotifications was updated to pass the new option. Any other mailer or plugin that uses `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send email. Provide a fallback to `user_preferences_url` or make the option explicitly required and update all callers.

title: Unsubscribe can 500 on a missing TopicUser and bypasses notification bookkeeping
body: The new action does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` and then calls `tu.notification_level` and `tu.save!` without a nil check. A logged-in user who can see the topic but has no TopicUser row (for example a forwarded email link, or a record removed by cleanup) will get a 500 instead of being unsubscribed. Even when the row exists, assigning and saving it directly bypasses TopicUser.change, so notifications_changed_at/notifications_reason_id are not updated and no MessageBus notification_level_change is published; other open tabs keep the old notification state. Use TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: target_level), which creates the row and publishes the change.

title: Per-topic unsubscribe is a CSRF-able GET with no token
body: The new `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` / `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` routes perform a state change (notification_level) and rely only on the session cookie. topics_controller skips check_xhr for this action, so non-XHR requests are accepted, and the JSON form `/t/123/unsubscribe.json` bypasses the slug check because `params[:slug].blank?` is only rejected for non-JSON requests. A malicious page can therefore include `` (or many IDs) and silently mute a logged-in victim from topics. Make this a POST with CSRF protection or use a signed per-email token; do not mutate state on an unauthenticated GET.

title: Unsubscribe is not idempotent; reloading the link mutes further
body: The action always computes a new level from the current one: watching/tracking goes to regular, then regular goes to muted. Because the unsubscribe URL is a GET, refreshing the confirmation page or opening the same email link again invokes the action again and keeps lowering the level. A user who unsubscribed once from a watched topic and reloads to read the confirmation will be muted. Set a fixed target level (or no-op when the current level is already at/below it) so the operation is idempotent.

title: Global unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url from every caller
body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` translation now unconditionally interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Email::MessageBuilder calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` for every email with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`, but this PR only supplies the new key in UserNotifications#send_notification_email. Any other mailer or plugin using MessageBuilder with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument at send time. Either keep the existing preferences-only fallback or update all callers/make the per-topic sentence conditional.

title: No test asserts the new per-topic unsubscribe link or controller behavior
body: The spec change only adds `unsubscribe_url` to the builder so the existing translation does not fail; the assertions still check only the user-preferences URL and the List-Unsubscribe header, never the new per-topic link. There is also no controller/request spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe covering a missing TopicUser, notification-level transitions, the slug redirect, or the JSON/CSRF path. Add assertions for the rendered link and controller specs for those branches.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
body: `TopicUser.find_by` can return nil, but the action immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and later `tu.save!`. A logged-in user hitting `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` for a topic they have never visited, or whose TopicUser row has been removed, gets a NoMethodError/500 instead of an unsubscribe. Use `TopicUser.change` (which creates the row and publishes the level change) or handle nil explicitly.

title: Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET with no signed token
body: The new route is a plain GET that calls `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which changes the logged-in user's `topic_users.notification_level`. Because the URL has no signed per-recipient token and GET requests are not CSRF-protected, any third-party page can embed/fetch this URL for a logged-in user and silently mute or downgrade notifications for a topic; mail scanners/link prefetchers can trigger the same effect. Use a signed token and/or a POST/confirmation flow for the mutation.

title: Repeated unsubscribe requests progressively downgrade the topic
body: The new level depends on the current level: watching/tracking becomes regular, while regular/muted becomes muted. A page refresh, double-click, or a fetched-link retry therefore runs the mutation again and can take a user from watching to regular and then to muted. The unsubscribe target should be deterministic/idempotent (or encoded in a signed link), otherwise retries silently over-mute the topic.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for every add_unsubscribe_link email
body: The shared server locale string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder` still treats `unsubscribe_url` as optional and only checks `add_unsubscribe_link` when rendering `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`. Any caller using `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without the new option, or a non-topic/digest mailer that only supplies `user_preferences_url`, will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to build the email. Default `unsubscribe_url` to the preferences URL, guard the interpolation, or keep the per-topic sentence in a separate conditional string.

title: No coverage for the new unsubscribe endpoint or per-topic link
body: The PR adds a destructive controller action and URL but the only spec change adds an unused `unsubscribe_url` to an existing email-builder test. There are no tests that the per-topic URL appears in the email body, that `TopicsController#unsubscribe` updates `notification_level` correctly (including when no TopicUser exists), or that repeated requests do not further downgrade the setting. Add request/controller specs so these behaviors are protected.

title: Validation triggers a DB write and double-counts blocked-email statistics
body: `EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, and `should_block?` (app/models/blocked_email.rb lines 12-17) loads the matching record, increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, and calls `record.save`. This means a simple `valid?`/`save` check now performs a database write. In `UsersController#create` the user is validated twice on the same request: `user.valid?` (line 168) and then `user.save` (line 172), so a single signup attempt against a blocked (or even `do_nothing`) email increments `match_count` by 2 instead of 1. Match counts will be inflated unpredictably, defeating the purpose of these statistics for spotting spam campaigns, and read-only validation paths unexpectedly mutate the DB. The stat update should be decoupled from the pure predicate and triggered once per real block event (e.g., after a confirmed rejection), not on every validation invocation.

title: Non-atomic counter update loses matches under concurrency
body: `should_block?` performs a read-modify-write: `record.match_count += 1; record.save`. Two concurrent requests matching the same blocked email both read count N and write N+1, losing one increment. Since these counters are the signal used to identify spam waves (exactly when many concurrent attempts happen), the undercounting is most severe in the scenario the data is meant to detect. Use an atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(["match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?", Time.zone.now])` (or `increment_counter`) instead.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and bypassable
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` compares the raw submitted email against the stored string with exact case. E-mail addresses are treated case-insensitively in practice, and nothing downcases the user's email when it is set/validated (`User.new_from_params` stores it verbatim). So an entry for `spam@bad.com` will not block a signup using `Spam@Bad.com` or `spam@BAD.com`, and imported/manually-entered records in mixed case won't match either — trivially bypassing the blocklist. Normalize on both sides: downcase/`Email.downcase` the value in `should_block?` (and ideally normalize the stored `email` in a `before_validation`/`before_save` so the unique index also behaves case-insensitively).

title: New validator spec does not cover the ported domain restrictions or the real lookup
body: The only new validator specs stub `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, so they neither exercise the actual database lookup/scoping nor verify the end-to-end behavior (`user.valid?` returning false for a blocked email). More importantly, this PR moves the `email_domains_whitelist`/`email_domains_blacklist` logic out of `User#email_validator` into `EmailValidator`, but no spec covers that moved logic (whitelist pass/fail, blacklist pass/fail). A regression in the relocated domain-restriction behavior would go undetected. Add specs covering the whitelist and blacklist branches (and ideally one integration spec that a blocked email makes a `User` invalid), plus a test for the new `errors`/`values` fields returned by `UsersController#create`.

title: Blocked-email matching is case- and whitespace-sensitive, allowing bypass
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` looks up the address with an exact `where(email: email)` match, and `BlockedEmail` does not normalize email on write; the migration's unique index on `email` also does not enforce case-insensitive uniqueness. The User model/controller do not downcase or strip `params[:email]` before validation, so an address blocked as `bad@spam.com` is not matched when submitted as `Bad@Spam.com` or with surrounding whitespace, and the account can still be created. Normalize email on insert and lookup (e.g. `strip.downcase`), make uniqueness/index case-insensitive, and add a regression spec for mixed-case input.

title: Blocked-email statistics are updated during validation, causing duplicate and racy increments
body: `should_block?` increments `match_count` and saves the record every time it is called, but it is called from `EmailValidator`, so every validation pass mutates the database. In `UsersController#create` the code calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which re-runs validations, so one blocked signup attempt increments `match_count` at least twice; every additional `valid?` call increments it again. The `match_count += 1`/`save` sequence is also a non-atomic read-modify-write, so concurrent attempts can lose increments. Move the statistics update out of the validation path or use an atomic update, and avoid validating the same user twice in the controller.

title: Domain whitelist regex is unanchored and can be bypassed
body: The restriction regex is built as `@(#{domains})` with no end anchor. If `email_domains_whitelist` is `example.com`, the address `user@example.com.attacker.tld` matches because the string contains `@example.com`, even though the actual domain is under `attacker.tld`. Since this validator is the only server-side domain check, an attacker controlling `attacker.tld` can satisfy a whitelist they should not satisfy; blacklist matching can also produce false positives. Anchor the domain pattern at the end (and add specs covering lookalike domains).

title: Blocked-email lookup is case- and whitespace-sensitive, allowing bypass
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` looks up the raw submitted value with `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`, and `set_defaults` never normalizes stored addresses. On the default Postgres setup this comparison is case-sensitive, and surrounding whitespace also matters. A blocked address such as `spammer@example.com` can therefore still register as `Spammer@example.com` or `spammer@example.com ` because the validator finds no record and returns false. Normalize both the stored address and the lookup value (for example with `Email.downcase`/strip), and enforce that normalization on write, including the unique constraint, so the block cannot be bypassed by casing or whitespace.

title: should_block? mutates the record during validation and is not atomic
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` performs `record.match_count += 1` and `record.save` every time it is called, but it is called from `EmailValidator`, so it runs during validation rather than only when a signup actually fails. In `UsersController#create`, `user.valid?` (line 168) is followed by `user.save` (line 172), so a single blocked signup attempt invokes it twice and increments `match_count` twice; any other `valid?` call also increments it. The read/modify/write is also racy, so concurrent checks lose increments. This makes `match_count`/`last_match_at` unreliable and adds database writes to validation. Record the match once at the point of the blocked signup, and use an atomic counter update such as `increment_counter`/`update_counters`.

title: Migration added without updating db/schema.rb
body: The PR creates the `blocked_emails` table in a migration but does not update `db/schema.rb`. Rails test and development databases are normally loaded from `schema.rb`, so the new `BlockedEmail` model and specs will fail with a missing `blocked_emails` table unless the test setup happens to run migrations. Regenerate and commit `db/schema.rb` with the new table and unique email index.

title: Invalid `end if` makes the embed template fail to compile
body: Line 6 closes the header `if` with `end if` and no condition. ERB compiles this to Ruby containing `end if`, which is a SyntaxError, so every request that renders `embed/best` will raise instead of displaying discussion highlights or the start-discussion link. It should just be `<%- end %>`. Controller specs do not render views by default, so this is not caught.

title: Imported feed/readability HTML is stored as raw HTML and rendered without sanitization
body: `TopicEmbed.import` sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns the raw string for that method, bypassing Markdown/sanitization. `Jobs::PollFeed` feeds arbitrary RSS/Atom content here (after `CGI.unescapeHTML`, which can turn escaped `<script>` into a real script tag), and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` emits `raw post.cooked`. The readability path only filters tag/attribute names, not dangerous URL schemes, and line 13 interpolates the feed-provided URL unescaped into the raw post. A malicious or compromised feed can therefore inject script/event-handler HTML and execute it in the forum origin when the embed is viewed. Sanitize the HTML (and URL schemes/attributes) before storing it, or do not use the raw_html cook method for untrusted feed content.

title: postMessage targetOrigin is a full referer URL instead of an origin
body: The resize script sends `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. `targetOrigin` must be a serialized origin (scheme://host[:port]); a referer with a path (and query string, which ERB also HTML-escapes to `&` inside the script) does not match the parent origin. The browser therefore drops the message, so the iframe never receives the height and content is clipped to the initial iframe size. Build the target origin from `URI(request.referer).scheme`, host, and port (or use a controlled site setting), not the full URL.

title: Feed items without `content` raise NoMethodError and abort polling
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every RSS/Atom item has a `content` field. Many valid feeds provide only `description` or `summary`, so `i.content` is nil and `nil.scrub` raises, aborting the entire poll and preventing all later items from importing. Use `i.content || i.description` (and handle nil) before scrubbing/unescaping.

title: Origin check uses substring matching instead of exact origin equality
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) return;` accepts any origin that appears as a substring of the trusted URL, for example `http://forum.example` when `discourseUrl` is `http://forum.example.com`, or the same host on a different port. Such a page can send a `discourse-resize` message and control the iframe height. Compare `e.origin` against the normalized origin of `discourseUrl` exactly.

title: Guard tests pass without exercising the setting under test
body: The `feed_polling_url` test stubs only `feed_polling_url` to nil; it leaves `feed_polling_enabled?` at its default false, so `execute` short-circuits before the URL check. The `embed_by_username` test has the same issue. These tests would still pass if the corresponding condition were deleted. Stub all earlier guards true in each test, and only the condition under test false, to make the assertion meaningful.

title: URL absolutization corrupts protocol-relative URLs and misses path-relative URLs
body: Only root-relative links are rewritten, and protocol-relative URLs are corrupted: `//cdn.example.com/x` satisfies `start_with?('/')`, then `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, producing `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/x` instead of `http://cdn.example.com/x`. Path-relative URLs such as `foo/bar` are not absolutized at all. The same issue exists for `img[src]` below. Treat `//` separately and resolve relative URLs against the article URI.

title: Unvalidated `open(url)` allows command execution/file reads from Disqus links
body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url)` before any URL validation. Ruby's `Kernel#open` treats a string beginning with `|` as a shell command and other strings as local file paths, so a malicious Disqus export can put e.g. `|touch /tmp/pwned` or `/etc/passwd` in a thread link; `lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148` now passes `t[:link]` directly to this method. Running the importer would execute the command or read the file. Validate that the URL is http/https and use an HTTP client (with redirect/size/timeout handling) instead of Kernel#open.

title: Raw HTML imports bypass sanitization and allow stored XSS
body: `TopicEmbed.import` stores external feed/article content with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for raw_html, and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders `post.cooked` with `raw`, so Discourse's normal HTML sanitizer is completely bypassed. `PollFeed` also calls `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, which can turn escaped `<script>` into an active `<script>` before import. Anyone controlling or compromising the configured feed/article can execute JavaScript in the Discourse origin (and inside the embed iframe). Sanitize imported HTML with the existing allowed-tag/attribute sanitizer before saving, or do not use raw_html for untrusted feed content.

title: Imported-from footer interpolates an untrusted URL into raw HTML
body: `url` comes from an RSS/Atom item and is only checked with a loose `^https?://` regex. It is interpolated directly into `href='#{url}'` and appended to the raw HTML body. A URL containing a single quote and attribute text, such as `http://host/'onmouseover='alert(1)`, can produce an extra event-handler attribute in the generated anchor. Because the post is stored as raw HTML, this is another stored XSS vector. Escape the URL with `ERB::Util.html_escape` or build the link with `link_to` and sanitize the final HTML.

title: Referer value is interpolated into JavaScript without escaping
body: `request.referer` is a request header, and the only validation is that its host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Its path/query is interpolated unescaped into a JavaScript string. A referer such as `http://eviltrout.com/';alert(1);//` breaks out of the string and executes in the Discourse iframe, allowing script in the Discourse origin. Escape the value with `escape_javascript`/`to_json` and use a fixed or parsed origin for the `postMessage` target instead of the raw referer.

title: Invalid `end if` makes the best view fail to compile
body: `<%- end if %>` is not valid Ruby: it closes the `if` and then starts an `if` modifier with no condition. Rendering the `best` action after a topic has been found will raise a template syntax error, so existing embeds return 500 instead of displaying the topic. It should be `<%- end %>`.

title: PostCreator is called inside an outer transaction, so jobs are enqueued before commit
body: `PostCreator.create` is invoked inside `Topic.transaction`. `PostCreator` opens its own transaction but it nests inside this one, so its internal block does not commit before it calls `enqueue_jobs` (process_post, feature_topic_users, etc.). Those Sidekiq jobs may run before the topic/post are committed and fail to find them; if the subsequent `TopicEmbed.create!` fails, for example during a duplicate-URL race, the outer transaction rolls back the post/topic but the already-enqueued jobs remain. Use after_commit callbacks or avoid wrapping PostCreator in an outer transaction.

title: Embed endpoint enqueues retrieval jobs for arbitrary embed URLs
body: `best` only checks the request's Referer host; it never checks that `params[:embed_url]` is on the embeddable host before enqueuing `retrieve_topic`. Any non-browser client can forge `Referer: http://<embeddable_host>/` and send unlimited distinct `embed_url`s. The host is rejected later inside `TopicRetriever`, after the Sidekiq job has been accepted, and `invalid_host?` short-circuits before the Redis throttle, so invalid URLs are never throttled. This allows unauthenticated queue flooding, and the loading page reloads every 30 seconds, enqueueing more jobs. Validate the embed URL host and throttle before enqueueing.

title: PollFeed tests for feed URL and username do not enable polling
body: In the 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' examples, `feed_polling_enabled?` is left at its default `false`. The `&&` chain stops at that first condition, so `poll_feed` is never called regardless of the URL or username setting, and these tests still pass even if those checks are removed. Stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true, along with the other required settings, in those examples.

title: Disqus import now depends on remote fetches and drops the category option
body: The import task now creates the initial post through `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which fetches `t[:link]` over the network and returns nil if the fetch fails or the link is not an HTTP URL. In that case the entire thread's comments are skipped, whereas the old code always created a topic from the local XML. The `--category` option was also removed, so existing invocations using it fail and imported threads no longer receive the requested category. Keep a fallback initial post/category or handle the failure explicitly.

title: ERB `end if` is a syntax error and breaks the best view
body: The closing tag is `<%- end if %>` with no condition after `if`. ERB compiles this to invalid Ruby, so any request that renders the `best` template (i.e. whenever a TopicEmbed exists) raises a template error/500 instead of showing the embedded discussion. The closing tag should be `<%- end %>`.

title: raw_html imports bypass sanitization and enable stored XSS
body: `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method` is `raw_html`, and `TopicEmbed.import` sets that for RSS/Readability content while `PollFeed` even calls `CGI.unescapeHTML` on it. `TopicEmbed.import` also interpolates the feed URL directly into an `<a href='...'>` footer. The imported HTML is stored unsanitized and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` renders it with `raw post.cooked`. A feed containing `<script>`, event handlers, or `javascript:` URLs therefore executes in the Discourse origin. Sanitize the HTML before storing/serving it, or keep imported posts on the normal cook path.

title: PollFeed assumes every RSS item has `content`
body: `i.content` is not defined for standard RSS items that only provide `<description>` or `<summary>`. Calling `.scrub` on nil raises NoMethodError, and because PollFeed has retry disabled a single such item aborts the hourly polling run so later items are never imported. Use a fallback such as `i.content || i.description` and guard against nil.

title: Updating a TopicEmbed whose post was deleted raises and stops feed polling
body: When an existing embed is found, `post = embed.post` is used without checking whether the post still exists. If the imported topic/post was deleted, `embed.post` can be nil; on a content change `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!` then dereferences nil and raises, aborting the whole PollFeed run (retry is disabled). Remove or repair stale TopicEmbed rows before revising.

title: Open-uri fetch follows redirects and permits SSRF
body: `open(url).read` performs an unrestricted outbound request. The only host validation, `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, checks the original URI host; `open-uri` follows redirects, so an allowed embeddable host that has an open redirect can make the Discourse server fetch localhost/internal services or cloud metadata and then import the response into a post. Validate redirect targets and block private addresses, and add timeouts/size limits.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring instead of exact origin
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that appears as a substring of the configured Discourse URL. For example, with discourseUrl `http://example.com/`, an origin `http://example.co` passes, so another frame can send `discourse-resize` messages and alter the iframe height. Parse discourseUrl and compare the scheme/host/port exactly.

title: Success spec leaves @topic_view nil and cannot pass
body: `TopicView.expects(:new).with(...)` has no `.returns(...)`, so the controller assigns nil to @topic_view. The rendered `best` view immediately calls `@topic_view.posts` and raises NoMethodError, so the after block expecting a successful response fails. Stub TopicView.new to return a view object with a topic and posts.

title: PollFeed guard tests are vacuous
body: The tests for missing feed_polling_url and missing embed_by_username do not stub feed_polling_enabled? to true, and the default is false. The execute condition therefore short-circuits before reaching the setting under test, so these specs pass even if the URL/username guards are removed. Stub the other required settings to true.

title: Flex layout breaks right-aligned small-action button
body: Adding `@include flexbox()` to `.small-action` changes its children to flex items. The existing `.small-action button { float: right; }` rule (line 309) can no longer right-align a button that is a direct flex child because floats are ignored on flex items. Also, `.small-action-desc` is not given `flex-grow`, so it no longer spans the remaining row width; if the button is nested inside it, the internal float will no longer push the button to the full row’s right edge either. The undo/act action button will therefore sit next to the description instead of at the right side. Add `margin-left: auto` to the button or make `.small-action-desc` grow.

title: align-items mixin omits -moz-box-align fallback
body: The new `align-items()` mixin emits `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, and `align-items`, but omits `-moz-box-align`. Since the new `flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` mixins explicitly fall back to `display: -moz-box`/`display: -moz-inline-box`, old Firefox versions will select the legacy box display but ignore the requested alignment. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment;` for parity; the `-ms-align-items` declaration is not a recognized IE property and can be removed.

title: Flex container ignores the small-action button's float, losing right alignment
body: Making `.small-action` a flex container turns its direct children into flex items. The existing `button { float: right; }` at line 309 is therefore ignored, and the button has no auto margin or other flex rule that allocates the remaining space. The action/undo button will render immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of at the right edge of the row. Add `margin-left: auto` to the button or otherwise distribute the free space explicitly.

title: Legacy order properties need +1 to match standard order semantics
body: The new `order($val)` mixin passes the standard zero-based `order` value directly to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group`. Those legacy flexbox properties are one-based and default to 1, while modern `order` defaults to 0. Calls such as `order(0)` or `order(1)` will place items differently in the old `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` fallback than in modern flex. Emit `$val + 1` for the legacy properties while keeping `$val` for `-ms-flex-order`, `-webkit-order`, and `order`. The current 2/3 calls happen to preserve their relative order, but the reusable mixin is incorrect for common values.

title: align-items mixin omits -moz-box-align and emits an invalid -ms property
body: `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box`, but `align-items()` never emits the corresponding `-moz-box-align`; it also emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a real CSS property. In an old Firefox that falls back to `-moz-box`, requested alignment (`center` in the header and `.small-action`, `baseline` in badges) will not apply, and the non-existent `-ms-align-items` declaration is dead code. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment` and remove `-ms-align-items`.

title: Flex conversion of .small-action breaks right-aligned action button
body: Converting .small-action to a flex container invalidates the existing right-alignment mechanism: floats are ignored on flex items, so the button rule still using float: right no longer pushes the action to the right edge. At the same time .small-action-desc is not given flex: 1, so it shrink-wraps instead of consuming the row width. The result is that the button sits immediately after the description rather than at the far right, regressing the small-action row layout. Give .small-action-desc flex: 1 and/or give the button margin-left: auto.

title: order mixin uses 0-based values for 1-based legacy flexbox property
body: The legacy flexbox properties -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group use a 1-based initial value, while the standard order property uses 0. Emitting the same $val for both means the mixin does not provide equivalent behavior: for example @include order(1) has no effect in browsers using the legacy box syntax, and other values are shifted by one relative to modern flexbox. Since this mixin is intended to abstract ordering for the header layout, emit $val + 1 for the box-ordinal-group properties.

title: website_name bypasses the untrusted-attribute filter and leaks TL0 users' website
body: `website` is in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), so it is hidden from anonymous viewers when `scope.restrict_user_fields?` is true (TL0 users). The new `website_name` attribute is not added to `untrusted_attributes`, and the manual guard `include_website_name` (without `?`) is never executed by the serializer, so anonymous visitors still receive `website_name`. Because `website_name` contains the host and, when it matches the instance domain, the full path, this re-exposes the exact URL that the untrusted restriction is meant to hide. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (which will also define the correct `include_website_name?` predicate) and update the untrusted-attributes spec.

title: include_website_name is missing the `?` suffix and is never called
body: ActiveModel::Serializers decides whether to emit an attribute by calling `include_<attr>?`; every other predicate in this file (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_stats?`, `include_suspend_reason?`) uses the question mark. Because this method is defined as `include_website_name` without `?`, it is dead code: `website_name` is always serialized, including `website_name: null` for users with no website, and any conditional exclusion written here would silently do nothing. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

title: Domain comparison is asymmetric and can treat unrelated domains as equal
body: The path is appended only when the instance host ends with '.'+website_host (else branch) or when both hosts have the same label count > 2 and their labels after the first match (elsif). As a result, instance `example.com` with website `www.example.com` (2 vs 3 labels) falls into the else branch, fails `ends_with?('.www.example.com')`, and returns only `www.example.com`, while the reverse case (`forum.example.com` instance, `example.com` website) shows the path. The feature therefore works inconsistently. In addition, comparing all-but-the-first labels treats unrelated registrable domains under multi-label public suffixes as identical: `foo.co.uk` and `bar.co.uk` both reduce to `co.uk`, so the full path of one is shown as if it belonged to the other. Use a proper registrable-domain/subdomain comparison instead of label counting.

title: New specs miss the untrusted/anonymous leak and the elsif branch
body: The added examples only cover different domains and the equal/parent-domain cases. There is no example for a TL0 user with a website viewed by an anonymous guardian, so the `website_name` privacy leak is not caught, and the `untrusted_attributes` list at line 11 still omits `website_name`. The `elsif` branch (same label count, different subdomain, e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) that the code comment describes is never exercised, nor is a user with a blank website (the `include_website_name` behavior). Add these cases so the serializer's inclusion and matching logic is verified.

title: website_name bypasses TL0 untrusted-field filtering and is always serialized
body: ActiveModel::Serializer only consults `include_<attribute>?` predicates. The new guard is named `include_website_name` (without the question mark), and `website_name` is not added to `untrusted_attributes`. Consequently every user JSON now contains `website_name`, even for a TL0 user viewed anonymously, for whom the existing `website` attribute is intentionally suppressed by `untrusted_attributes :website`. The profile template then renders that field, leaking the host/path of a website that was deliberately hidden. Rename the guard to `include_website_name?` and apply at least the same `scope.restrict_user_fields?`/presence gate as `website`, or add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`.

title: Host comparison treats unrelated hosts under public suffixes as the same domain
body: The equal-label branch strips only the first label before comparing hosts. For an instance host such as `other.co.uk` and a user website of `example.co.uk`, both have three labels and both reduce to `co.uk`, so the code treats them as the same domain and returns `example.co.uk/path`. These are unrelated registrable domains (the same problem occurs for `alice.github.io` versus `bob.github.io`). The path should only be appended when the hosts actually belong to the same registrable domain, which requires public-suffix-aware comparison or a narrower exact/parent check rather than comparing `split('.')[1..-1]`.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so it never runs
body: ActiveModel::Serializer decides whether to emit an attribute by calling `include_<attribute>?`. This guard is named `include_website_name` (no trailing `?`), so it is never invoked and `website_name` is emitted for every serialized user, including users with no website (as `null`). The intended `website.present?` condition has no effect. Rename it to `include_website_name?`, or (better, see the trust-level finding) move `website_name` into `untrusted_attributes`.

title: website_name leaks a website that untrusted_attributes deliberately hides
body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) so that a TL0 user's profile fields are not exposed to anonymous visitors (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`). The new `website_name` attribute is added to the plain `attributes` list and has no such guard: its `include_website_name` method only checks `website.present?` and, being misnamed, is not called anyway. As a result anonymous visitors now receive `website_name` containing the hidden TL0 user's website host and path, defeating the anti-spam restriction. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (and make the include check honour `restrict_user_fields?`).

title: Gating the website block on model.website_name hides websites the serializer cannot parse
body: The block that renders the globe icon and the website link is now guarded by `{{#if model.website_name}}`.
