The serializer returns `nil` whenever `URI(website.to_s)` raises (e.g. a URL containing a space such as `http://example.com/my page`), and it is also absent if an endpoint does not include the new attribute. Previously the display name was derived in JS from `model.website` (`website.split('/')[2]`), so such a user still saw the globe and a link. Now the website silently disappears from the profile even though `model.website` is present. Gate on `model.website` and fall back to a derived name, or make the serializer always return a non-nil name when the website is present.

title: untested: website_name is not added to the untrusted attributes spec
body: The `untrusted_attributes` list still contains only the original attributes. Because `website_name` is not added, there is no test asserting that the new field is omitted for a TL0 user seen as anonymous, so the leak of a hidden website described elsewhere in this review passes the suite. Add `website_name` here; the test should fail until the serializer guards that attribute.

title: The equal-length subdomain branch of website_name is never exercised
body: The three new examples cover `website_host == discourse_host`, the `else` branch, and the parent-domain case. None exercises the `elsif` branch (`website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length && ... > 2`), i.e. the `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` case named in the code comment, which is the most complex branch. The nil/invalid-website case (host cannot be parsed) is also untested.

title: Subdomain comparison treats unrelated domains under multi-label public suffixes as equal
body: The equivalence check removes only the first label of each host and compares the rest. For hosts whose public suffix has more than one label this is wrong: with website `http://foo.co.uk/post` and instance `bar.co.uk`, comparing `['foo','co','uk'][1..-1].join` with `['bar','co','uk'][1..-1].join` yields `co.uk` for both, so it reports the domains as the same and shows the full path `foo.co.uk/post`, even though `foo.co.uk` and `bar.co.uk` are unrelated registrable domains. Use a real registrable-domain/public-suffix comparison, or only treat the website as a subdomain of the instance when it actually ends with `.` + instance host (and vice versa).

title: Wrong lightness pair for embedded post author links
body: The embedded-post author link color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Both arguments are wrong for preserving the original appearance: the light-theme value should stay at 30%, and the dark-theme value should use the complementary 70% of `$secondary` (as done for the equivalent quote-title styling). As written, the light theme gets a much lighter, low-contrast link and the dark theme gets the opposite end of the scale.

title: Custom message length color lightness is reversed
body: `.custom-message-length` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The lightness pair is reversed: the light-theme argument changed from 70% to 30%, and the dark-theme argument from the expected 30% to 70%. The equivalent rule in `desktop/modal.scss` uses `primary 70% / secondary 30%`. This makes the mobile custom-message-length text darker in the light theme and lighter in the dark theme than intended.

title: Topic map heading lost its intended 20% lightness
body: The `.topic-map h3` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. Unlike the desktop topic-map rule, which correctly uses `primary 20% / secondary 80%`, this changes the light-theme color from 20% to 50% and does not derive the dark-theme value correctly. The section heading becomes noticeably lighter and loses the intended emphasis.

title: Group member name color no longer preserves 30% lightness
body: `.group-member-info .name` was originally `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme value from 30% to 50% and not using the complementary 70% for the dark theme. This makes the member name lighter and removes the intentional emphasis relative to the adjacent title.

title: Mobile group member name uses the wrong lightness pair
body: `.group-member-info .name` was originally `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the replacement uses the 50%/50% pair instead of preserving 30% for the light theme and using 70% of `$secondary` for the dark theme. The same mistake exists in the desktop user stylesheet, and it makes the name less emphasized than before.

title: Category badge notification color missed the dark-theme conversion
body: The `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` color is still `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` while every other similar color in this file was wrapped with `dark-light-choose`. In a dark theme `$primary` is the light foreground color, so this produces a very light count color instead of a muted value derived from the dark `$secondary`. This leaves the badge inconsistent with the rest of the dark-theme conversion and can make it stand out too strongly.

title: Embedded post author-link lightness values are inverted
body: The original color for links inside `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so in light theme the link is lightened 70% instead of 30%, and in dark theme it is lightened only 30% from `$secondary` instead of the corresponding 70%. This lowers contrast in both themes, especially against dark backgrounds, making expanded-post author links hard to read. It should preserve 30% for the light branch and use 70% for the dark branch.

title: Custom message length hint uses reversed lightness values on mobile
body: `.custom-message-length` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, a light hint color. The replacement uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` for the light branch and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` for the dark branch, reversing both. This makes the hint much darker than before in light theme and brighter than intended in dark theme, and it is inconsistent with `desktop/modal.scss`, which uses the expected 70/30 mapping. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

title: Mobile topic-map h3 heading lightness was changed accidentally
body: `.topic-map h3` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new expression uses 50% for both branches, so in light theme the heading becomes much lighter than before, and in dark theme it uses 50% from `$secondary` rather than the expected 80% counterpart. This also differs from the desktop topic-map h3 rule, which correctly maps 20% to 80%. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

title: Group member name color no longer preserves the original 30% lightness
body: `.group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which changes the light-theme color from 30% to 50% and uses only 50% from `$secondary` in dark theme instead of the corresponding 70%. The name becomes noticeably less distinct than before. It should preserve the light value and use the 70% dark counterpart.

title: Mobile group member name color no longer preserves the original 30% lightness
body: `.group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme color from 30% to 50% and using 50% from `$secondary` in dark theme instead of the expected 70%. This makes the member name lighter than before and inconsistent with the same selector on desktop. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Category badge-notification still uses $primary in dark themes
body: The PR converts the muted topic-list colors in this file to `dark-light-choose`, but `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. Since `$primary` is light in dark themes, this badge count is lightened further instead of being derived from `$secondary`, so the original dark-theme contrast issue remains for category badge notifications. It should be converted like the surrounding rules, e.g. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`.

title: Embedded post author link uses wrong lightness for dark-light conversion
body: The referenced author link under `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but this PR changes it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The first argument is the light-theme value, so light themes now get a much lighter color than before, and the dark-theme branch uses the non-complementary 30% instead of 70%. This makes the author link visually inconsistent and potentially low-contrast in both themes.

title: Group member name lightness changed instead of preserving original value
body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which changes the light-theme color from 30% to 50% and gives the dark theme a 50% secondary color instead of the corresponding 70%. This makes the member name less distinct from the adjacent title and does not preserve the original design.

title: Custom message length hint lightness reversed
body: `.custom-message-length` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The replacement uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, so the light-theme branch becomes much darker and the dark-theme branch becomes much brighter than intended. The correct complementary conversion would keep the original 70% for `$primary` and use 30% for `$secondary`; this regression affects the flag modal hint text contrast.

title: Topic map section heading lightness changed incorrectly
body: `.topic-map h3` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but the new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This lightens the light-theme heading from 20% to 50% and fails to use the complementary 80% secondary color for dark themes, so the topic-map section headings lose their intended emphasis and contrast.

title: Mobile group member name lightness changed incorrectly
body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new conversion uses 50% for both branches: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. It should preserve 30% for `$primary` and use 70% for `$secondary`; the current value changes the mobile user stream styling and reduces the intended contrast difference from `.title`.

title: Category count badge missed the dark-theme conversion
body: This file was converted in the PR, but `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. On dark themes this continues to derive the badge count color from the text color instead of the background color, leaving the same dark-theme contrast issue that the rest of this PR is fixing.

title: Unconditional visible assignment can hide groups on partial updates
body: `update` always executes `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`. A PATCH or PUT that omits `visible`—including the old PATCH membership-changes API that still routes to `update` because `resources :groups` accepts PATCH—now sets `visible` to false and saves. The old `update_patch` membership add/delete handling was also removed, so such requests no longer update memberships and can silently make the group invisible. Only assign `visible` when the parameter is present, and either support or explicitly reject the old PATCH contract.

title: Total page count is wrong for exact multiples
body: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With 50 members and a 50-member page limit this reports 2 pages instead of 1, so the Next link stays enabled and takes the admin to an empty page. The same happens for 100 members (3 pages instead of 2). Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` for non-zero counts.

title: Public members endpoint accepts unbounded and negative pagination values
body: `limit` and `offset` are taken directly from public query parameters and passed into `.limit(...).offset(...)`. A caller can request a very large limit, causing an unnecessarily large database result and JSON serialization, or pass negative values that can produce SQL errors/500 responses. Clamp `limit` to a sane maximum and enforce `offset >= 0`.

title: Public group member list truncates at 50 with no pagination
body: The backend now returns only one page of members (default limit 50), and the public group-members route never requests another page. This template simply iterates `members` and has no pagination controls. Groups with more than 50 members will silently show only the first 50, whereas non-automatic groups previously returned all members. Either add paging or explicitly fetch all members for the public view.

title: Removing the last member on the last page leaves an invalid offset
body: `removeMember` deletes the user and then calls `findMembers()` with the current offset. If the removed user was the only member on the current page (for example 51 members at offset 50), the new total becomes 50 but the request still uses offset 50, so the reload returns an empty page and the UI stays on an invalid blank page. Adjust the offset when it reaches or exceeds the new `user_count` after deletion.

title: Username input is not cleared after adding members or switching groups
body: `usernames` is state on the singleton admin group controller and is not reset after `addMembers` or when `setupController` switches to another group. After adding users to group A, selecting group B leaves the old usernames in the selector; clicking Add again can add those stale users to group B unintentionally. Clear the property after each add and when the model changes (the existing TODO acknowledges this).

title: Creating a group ignores the selected alias level
body: The client’s `Group.asJSON()` sends `alias_level` when creating a group, and the admin template exposes the alias selector for new groups, but `create` only assigns `name` and `visible`. A newly created group therefore silently loses the selected alias level and falls back to the database default. Assign `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i` when present.

title: Public members endpoint response shape is a breaking change
body: `/groups/:group_id/members.json` previously returned a JSON array of users; it now returns an object of the form `{members: [...], meta: {...}}`. The in-repo JavaScript client was updated, but any plugin, mobile app, or external consumer expecting the old array will break. If this endpoint is part of the public API, either maintain backward compatibility or introduce a versioned/new endpoint.

title: remove_member test uses PUT despite the route being DELETE
body: The actual route for removing a member is `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members`, but the test invokes `xhr :put, :remove_member`. Controller specs bypass routing, so this can pass even if the DELETE route is missing or the PUT route actually maps to `add_members` in production. Use `xhr :delete` to exercise the real contract.

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members and limit 50) this returns 2 instead of 1. The template then renders '1/2', and because showingLast compares currentPage to this wrong totalPages, the 'next' link is not disabled on what is really the last page. Clicking next advances offset to user_count, findMembers requests that offset, the server returns an empty page, and the user is left looking at an empty member list. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (or Math.floor((user_count - 1) / limit) + 1).

title: remove_member deletes the join row directly and leaves groups.user_count stale
body: remove_member removes the membership with group.users.delete(user_id) followed by group.save, instead of using the Group#remove path. The groups.user_count column is a denormalized counter (the .index spec shows it is stored and populated by group.add). Deleting the join record directly bypasses whatever keeps that counter in sync (Group#remove and/or a counter cache / GroupUser callbacks, which delete_all does not trigger), so after removing a member the stored user_count remains too high. The admin groups list and the group header render that stored count, so they will report a wrong member total until it is recomputed. Use Group#remove (or recompute user_count) and cover it with a spec asserting user_count — the current spec only asserts users.count.

title: Group members endpoint now silently truncates to 50 with no pagination on the public page
body: members now always paginates: limit defaults to 50 and the previous behavior (all members for non-automatic groups, up to 200 for automatic groups) is gone. The public group members page (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs) was not given pagination controls and only iterates `members`, so any group with more than 50 members now silently shows just the first 50 with no way to load the rest. In addition the response changed from a bare array to {members, meta}, which breaks any client of the public /groups/:id/members.json route that still expects an array. Either add pagination to that template or keep returning the full list for this endpoint.

title: add_members splits usernames without stripping whitespace
body: add_members does usernames.split(",") and passes each element straight to User.find_by_username without stripping. If the client ever submits a space-separated list such as "alice, bob", the lookup for " bob" fails and that user is silently not added (the old Group#usernames= setter stripped entries). Strip each element and drop blanks before lookup.

title: Unbounded limit parameter on the public members endpoint
body: members reads the caller-supplied limit with no upper bound: (params[:limit] || 50).to_i. This is a public (non-admin) route, so a request with limit=1000000 forces the entire membership set to be loaded and serialized in one response. Clamp limit to a sane maximum (e.g. the page size) before applying it.

title: remove_member test uses PUT although the route is DELETE
body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example issues xhr :put, :remove_member, but config/routes.rb maps remove_member to DELETE. Controller specs bypass routing, so the test passes even though it never exercises the real verb/route the browser uses; a mismatch between the configured route and the action would go undetected. Issue :delete here to match the actual route (the 'is able to remove a member' example already uses :delete).

title: Member list is rendered with an invalid each helper
body: The new member-list block is written as `{{each member in members itemView='group-member'}}` without the leading `#` and there is no closing `{{/each}}`. Handlebars treats this as an inline helper, not a block, so the group-member template is never rendered; the admin group member list and its remove links are missing or rendering fails. Use `{{#each member in members itemView='group-member'}} ... {{/each}}`.

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (for example 50 members with limit 50), it reports 2 pages instead of 1. `showingLast` is then false and the Next action sets offset to user_count, so the admin UI goes to an empty page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (returning 0 when user_count is 0).

title: Removing the last member on the last page leaves an empty member list
body: `findMembers` clamps the requested offset with `Math.min(user_count, ...)`. If an admin removes the only member on the last page, user_count falls to the current offset (for example 50), so the reload requests offset=50 against a 50-member total and receives an empty array. The member list goes blank; clamp to the last valid page start or step back a page when offset >= user_count.

title: Public group members endpoint now silently truncates at 50 with no public pagination
body: The endpoint now defaults to limit 50, but the public group/members route and template have no pagination or load-more control. Public group pages therefore silently show only the first 50 members; before this change manual groups returned all members and automatic groups up to 200. Add pagination to the public page or avoid applying the 50-row default there. The supplied limit is also not capped, so callers can request arbitrarily large pages.

title: Member reload uses the unsaved editable group name
body: `findMembers` builds the URL from `this.get('name')`, but the admin form edits `name` directly. If an admin renames a group and then adds/removes a member or pages before saving, the add/remove request uses the id and succeeds, but the follow-up GET uses the unsaved new name and fails or returns 404, leaving the member list stale. Use the group id for admin member listing or the persisted name.

title: Remove link is shown for automatic groups because automatic is read from the wrong context
body: This template is the itemView for each member, so its context is the member rather than the parent group. `automatic` is a group attribute and is undefined in this scope, making `unless automatic` true; the remove link is shown even for automatic groups. Removing then fails with a 422. Pass the group's automatic flag into the item view or render the link conditionally from the parent template.

title: Creating a group ignores the submitted alias_level
body: `create` only assigns name and visible. `Group#asJSON` includes alias_level, and the form allows choosing it for a new group, so the submitted alias_level is silently ignored and the new group keeps the default until an explicit update. Assign alias_level in create (with the same presence check used in update).

title: Fallback locales are only loaded for controller requests
body: `translate` still only calls `load_locale(config.locale)` for the current locale, and the only place that calls `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is `ApplicationController#set_locale` (application_controller.rb:159). Because the patched `load_translations` forces explicit loading and `load_locale` is the only loader, any translation performed outside a web request (Sidekiq/background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, the console, or `I18n.with_locale` / `I18n.t(key, locale: x)` inside a request) will try the fallback chain (`SiteSetting.default_locale`, `:en`) without those locale files ever having been loaded. When the requested locale lacks a key, the fallback lookup then misses and the caller gets a missing translation/raw key instead of the site-default/English string. For example, a job running under `I18n.locale = 'de'` on a site whose default locale is `'fr'` never loads `fr`, so a missing German key cannot fall back to French. Ensure the whole fallback chain is loaded whenever a locale is loaded (e.g. make `load_locale`/`translate` call `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for each entry of `I18n.fallbacks[locale]`), not only from the controller before_filter.

title: Fallback chain recomputes a SiteSetting lookup on the translation hot path
body: `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on every `I18n.translate`/`I18n.exists?` that reaches the backend (i.e. every translation not served from the translate accelerator's LRU cache), and this `[]` override calls `SiteSetting.default_locale` each time. That turns a previously pure in-memory fallback-list lookup into a site-setting lookup on the hot translation path and, via `set_locale`, once per request. It also means an early `I18n.t` (boot initializers, asset precompilation, rake tasks, console before the DB/Redis are available) now attempts to read site settings and can raise instead of simply returning a translation. Memoize the default locale / compute the chain once per locale and invalidate it on reload.

title: No tests for the new fallback behavior, which is now enabled in every environment
body: The PR changes translation resolution globally (fall back to the site default locale, then English) but adds no specs covering `FallbackLocaleList#[]`, the fallback ordering, or `ensure_loaded!`. Additionally, `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` runs in every environment, while the `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` lines that were removed only existed in production/profile/Cloud66, so fallbacks now also apply in test/development where they were previously unset. Tests that assert a missing key is returned verbatim, or that a given locale has no translation, will now silently receive the site-default/English string. Add tests for the new fallback chain and confirm the intended test-environment behavior.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded in controllers, so fallbacks fail in mailers/background jobs
body: The accelerator's `translate` only lazy-loads the active locale (`load_locale(config.locale)` on line 68); it never loads the fallback locales returned by `I18n.fallbacks[locale]`. The only place that force-loads the fallback chain is `ApplicationController#set_locale` (app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159 → `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`). Any translation performed outside an HTTP request — ActionMailer, Sidekiq/background workers, rake tasks, console — never runs `set_locale`, so `:en` (and the site default) yml is not loaded. When a key is missing in the user's locale the Fallbacks backend tries `:en`, finds no loaded data, and the caller gets a "translation missing" string instead of the English fallback. This defeats the stated 'server-side fallbacks' goal for exactly the server-side paths (emails etc.) that need it most. The fallback locales should be loaded inside the translate/locale-loading path rather than only from the controller.

title: Fallback chain does a DB-backed SiteSetting lookup on every translation
body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` builds its result from `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which is a runtime site setting rather than a boot-time constant. `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` for essentially every `I18n.t` lookup (the accelerator routes all translation through the backend), so this now performs a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read (and allocates a fresh array) on the hot translation path for every request. In addition to the overhead, it makes translation depend on `SiteSetting` being initialized: in contexts without a ready DB/settings (boot, `rake db:migrate`, `rake assets:precompile`, or if the setting is nil so `.to_sym` raises NoMethodError) any `I18n.t` call can raise instead of returning a translation. The fallback list should be computed once/memoized with a safe hard-coded default instead of reading SiteSetting per lookup.

title: No tests for the new fallback behavior
body: This PR changes global i18n behavior (enables Fallbacks in every environment, replaces the default fallbacks object, and adds an `ensure_loaded!` hook) but adds no specs. There is no coverage that a key missing in a non-English locale resolves to the site default and then to English, that `ensure_loaded!` actually loads the fallback locales' yml, or that a missing key still raises/returns the expected result. Given this touches translation resolution for all requests and is easy to regress, at least a request spec exercising a missing translation in a non-English locale and a unit test for `FallbackLocaleList#[]`/`ensure_loaded!` should be added.

title: Translation cache key omits fallback/default locale, so changing default_locale yields stale fallback text
body: The LRU cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`, which only captures the requested locale. With fallbacks now resolving through `SiteSetting.default_locale`, the *value* stored for a given locale can change when an admin changes the default locale, but the key does not, so previously cached fallback-resolved strings keep being served until `I18n.reload!` happens to be called. For locales whose own translations are incomplete, this means users continue to see text from the old default-locale fallback after the setting is changed. The cache key (or a `reload!` on default_locale change) should account for the fallback chain.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded for HTTP requests; translations in jobs/mailers never fall back
body: The new `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` call loads the user locale, the site default locale and `:en`, but it only runs inside `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any translation performed outside a controller request — Sidekiq jobs, mailer/notification rendering, rake tasks, the console, specs — never executes it. In those contexts `I18n.translate` in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` still only calls `load_locale(config.locale)`, and the i18n `Fallbacks` backend invokes `Base#translate` (not `I18n.translate`) for each fallback, so it never triggers loading of the fallback locale files. Consequence: in a separate Sidekiq/mailer process, a key missing from, e.g., `de.yml` will not resolve to `:en` and will emit "translation missing" instead of falling back. The fallback-chain loading should live inside `I18n.translate`/`ensure_loaded!` rather than relying on the controller before_filter.

title: Fallback chain mixes String and Symbol locales, defeating uniq and double-loading the YAML
body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` builds `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`. For anonymous requests `set_locale` assigns `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale`, which is a String, so `locale` is (for example) `"en"` while the site default is `:en`. `uniq` does not treat the String and Symbol as equal, so the chain becomes `["en", :en]`. Both values are then passed to `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, and because `@loaded_locales` stores them as distinct entries, `en.yml` is parsed twice on the first request and the same locale is translated twice inside the Fallbacks backend. Normalize the locale (e.g. `locale.to_sym`) when constructing the array.

title: No tests for the new server-side fallback behavior
body: This change reworks how locale fallbacks are configured (dropping `config.i18n.fallbacks = true`, adding `FallbackLocaleList`, and adding `I18n.ensure_loaded!`) and directly affects user-visible output when translations are missing. No specs were added to verify that a key absent from a non-English locale resolves to the site default and then English, that `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` actually loads the fallback locale files, or that pluralization still works through the fallback chain. Add request/unit coverage for these paths before merging, since a regression here silently produces "translation missing" strings.

title: Denial cache has no invalidation and can override fresh allows
body: `Check` returns immediately from `permDenialCache` before consulting `permCache` or the DB, and `permDenialCache.Set` is called after any DB-backed denial. Nothing invalidates these entries when permissions are granted or when a new dashboard/folder is created. A denied check (for example, before a just-created dashboard's creator permission is visible, or before an admin grants a role) therefore keeps returning Allowed=false for the 30s shortCacheTTL even after the DB grants access. This also means a stale denial overrides a later-refreshed allow in permCache, which directly undermines the PR goal of making newly created resources accessible. Deny entries need invalidation, or must not override a fresh cached allow, and likely deserve a shorter TTL.

title: Denial cache key uses raw subject ID and omits identity type
body: The denial-cache key is built from the raw subject ID (`checkReq.UserUID`) before `GetUserIdentifiers` resolves the canonical UID, and it does not include the identity type. The permission cache, in contrast, is keyed by the resolved `userIdentifiers.UID`. The same user can therefore have separate denial entries for `user:123` and `user:<uid>`, so the denial cache is bypassed when the subject form changes. Conversely, identities such as `user:123`, `service-account:123`, or `anonymous:123` share the same denial key even though they can represent different principals; a denial for one can be served for another until TTL expiry. Resolve the subject first and include the identity type plus canonical UID, and escape or hash the key components.

title: No test that Check populates the denial cache
body: The new test for the denial cache only seeds `permDenialCache` manually; it does not exercise a normal denied `Check` and verify that the denial entry is written. A bug in the key used by `s.permDenialCache.Set` or a missed Set call would pass the current tests. Add a case with a denying fake permission store that asserts a second identical `Check` is served from the denial cache without incrementing `store.calls` and still returns Allowed=false.

title: Per-resource DB fallback allows DB/cache-fill DoS on denied resources
body: When the cached permission map exists but does not contain the requested resource, Check unconditionally calls getIdentityPermissions (line 139), and getUserPermissions now always queries the DB because its own cache check was removed. The denial cache is keyed by resource name and parent, so it only helps repeat checks of the same resource; an attacker can vary dashboard/folder UIDs to force one permission DB query and one new denial-cache entry per request. Anonymous users are especially exposed: an empty anonymous permission map is cached, so every unique denied resource misses the denial cache and hits the permission store. This creates a cache-penetration DoS and unbounded local/remote cache growth (the in-proc cache has a 10m cleanup interval), even though the permission cache already told us the user has no matching permission.

title: Denial cache key is not scoped by identity type and uses ambiguous concatenation
body: userPermDenialCacheKey builds the key from namespace, userUID, action, name, and parent only. The identity type is missing, but anonymous and renderer identities both use UID "0" (e.g. anonymous:0 and render:0), so a denial cached for a renderer on an action/resource will also deny an anonymous user checking the same action/resource, even if anonymous has permission (and vice versa). The fields are also concatenated with unescaped '_' separators, so UIDs containing underscores can make different (name, parent) pairs produce the same key. Use the full subject/identity type in the key and length-prefix or hash the fields.

title: DB fallback still relies on stale folder-tree cache for newly created folders
body: The new fallback requeries only permissions and then calls checkPermission again at line 146. For dashboards, checkPermission calls checkInheritedPermissions -> buildFolderTree, which first returns the cached folder tree. If the dashboard is in a folder that was just created and is not yet in that tree, the fresh permission map cannot resolve the folder's ancestors, so the check still returns false even though the user has permission on an ancestor folder. The result is then written to the denial cache, potentially extending the false denial beyond the folder cache TTL. To actually fix newly created folders/dashboards, the fallback needs to bypass or refresh the folder cache as well. Existing tests prepopulate folderCache, so they do not cover this.

title: Denial-cache test uses a deny value in permCache and cannot detect a regression
body: The test comments that it is allowing access to prove the denial cache is checked, but it populates permCache with map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}. checkPermission treats that as a denial, so the test would still pass if the denial-cache short-circuit were removed; the fallback DB store also has no permissions for dash1. Set the value to true (or use a store that errors/counts calls) so the test fails when the denial cache is not consulted, and add coverage that Check writes a denial-cache entry after a fresh DB denial.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type, causing cross-identity denials
body: The new denial cache key is built only from the subject UID: userPermDenialCacheKey(ns, checkReq.UserUID, action, name, parent). It does not include checkReq.IdentityType nor the resolved user identifiers. Both 'anonymous:0' and 'render:0' carry UID "0", so a denied Check for an anonymous user (e.g. reading a private dashboard) stores a denial under the ..._0_... key, and the next render-service read Check for the same namespace/action/name/parent hits that entry and is incorrectly denied for up to 30s, breaking dashboard image rendering. The same key also collides when a subject is passed as a numeric user id (user:123) versus a user whose actual UID string is "123". The key must include the identity type (and should use the resolved user UID rather than the raw subject).

title: Every resource absent from cached permissions now triggers a DB query
body: Before this change a Check for a resource not present in the user's cached permission map was answered from the cache (deny) without touching the database. Now, whenever the cached permission map exists but does not cover the requested resource, execution falls through to getIdentityPermissions, which always queries the permission store (the in-singleflight cache read was removed). The new denial cache only suppresses repeats of the exact same (user, action, name, parent) tuple, so workloads that check many distinct resources the user cannot access (a user or service account iterating/probing dashboards across an org) issue one DB query per distinct resource per 30s instead of being served from the permission cache. In large orgs this can significantly increase permission-store load.

title: DB requery does not refresh the folder tree, so inherited access to new folders is still denied and cached
body: The new fallback only re-queries the user's permission scopes; it does not refresh the folder tree used by checkInheritedPermissions. buildFolderTree reads folderCache (shortCacheTTL = 30s) and nothing invalidates it when a folder is created. If the tree was cached before a new child folder was created, tree.Ancestors(parent) will not include the new folder, so a user whose access to the new folder/dashboard is inherited from an ancestor is denied even though permissions were re-queried. That false denial is then written to permDenialCache, keeping the user blocked for up to another 30s after the folder tree finally refreshes. This means the PR's stated target case (newly created folders) remains broken in any busy namespace where the folder tree is already cached.

title: Tests do not cover denial-cache writes or identity isolation
body: The new 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' test seeds permDenialCache by hand and only asserts the false result; it never exercises the code path that is supposed to populate the denial cache after a DB-backed denial, and it would still pass if the `s.permDenialCache.Set(...)` call at the end of Check were removed (the default fake store denies too). There is also no test that a denial cached for one identity type does not affect another, which is why the anonymous/"0" vs render/"0" collision above is not caught. Add a test that performs a denied Check and asserts the second call is served from the denial cache without a store call (e.g. via store.calls), and a test that a denial for anonymous:0 does not deny render:0.

title: Delete (and Pause) menu items are gated on rulerRule, so they disappear from the prom-only list view
body: AlertRuleMenu still renders the Delete item only when `canDelete && rulerRule`, and the Pause item only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123). This PR changes the alert list view so that `GrafanaRuleListItem` -> `RuleActionsButtons.V2` passes only `promRule` and never a ruler rule (the ruler API calls were removed on purpose). `canDelete`/`canPause` are now correctly computed from `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, but the extra `rulerRule` guard means they are never used: Delete is no longer available anywhere in the alert list view even for users with delete permission, whereas before this PR the ruler rule was fetched and the action was shown. `handleDelete` only needs the identifier (`RuleActionsButtons.V2` passes `() => showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)`), so requiring a ruler rule is unnecessary. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test actually grants AlertingRuleDelete and asserts exactly 4 menu items (no Delete), codifying the regression.

title: Silence menu item is shown in the list view but clicking it does nothing because the drawer requires a rulerRule
body: AlertRuleMenu now decides whether to show "Silence notifications" from the prom-rule abilities, so in the new prom-only list view (GrafanaGroupLoader / FilterView) the item is rendered when the user has silence permission. However the drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`, where `rule` is the optional rulerRule prop. In the list view that prop is undefined, so `handleSilence` sets `showSilenceDrawer` to true but no drawer ever mounts and the click is a no-op. Either the menu item must be hidden when no ruler rule is available, or `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` must be able to build the silence from the prom rule. The GrafanaGroupLoader test asserts the Silence item is present but never clicks it, so this dead action is not caught.

title: Grafana rule list items are rendered without a key in the .map()
body: In `FilterViewResults`, `rules.map(...)` renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} .../>` for `origin === 'grafana'` without a `key`. The previous `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../>` did pass the computed `key` (and the sibling `DataSourceRuleLoader` / `UnknownRuleListItem` branches still do). React will emit "Each child in a list should have a unique key" and fall back to index keys, so component state in the row (e.g. the open dropdown in `AlertRuleMenu`) can be attached to the wrong rule when results are appended or re-rendered. Add `key={key}` to the `GrafanaRuleListItem` branch.

title: Federation detection is lost: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to a hook that hardcodes isFederated = false
body: Before this change `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, which made Update/Delete/Pause/Restore unsupported for federated Mimir/Metrics Enterprise rule groups (they are immutable from Grafana). It now just delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, where `const isFederated = false;` is hardcoded (with a TODO). As a result `useAlertRuleAbility`/`useAlertRuleAbilities` (still used by the rules table and other rule-based components) will report these actions as supported for federated groups, showing Edit/Delete/Pause controls that the backend rejects. The `CombinedRule` still carries `rule.group`, so federation can still be detected; the delegation loses it.

title: Prom-rule abilities restrict ModifyExport and Pause to alerting rules, dropping them for Grafana recording rules
body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` sets `[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isAlertingRule, exportAllowed]` and gates `Pause`/`Restore`/`DeletePermanently` on `isAlertingRule`, i.e. `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule`. The ruler-based equivalent gates these on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule`, which is also true for Grafana-managed recording rules, and Grafana recording rules can be paused and exported. In the new list view (where only the prom-based ability is available) the Export item therefore disappears for Grafana recording rules, and Pause would be reported unsupported (currently masked by the separate `rulerRule` guard in AlertRuleMenu). Use `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule` for the actions that apply to recording rules, and keep `alertingRule` only for Silence.

title: Rule view links no longer carry returnTo, losing back-navigation from the rule viewer
body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader.GrafanaRuleListItem` built the view link with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`, where `returnTo = createReturnTo()`. The new component uses `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` without the `returnTo` query parameter. The rule view page uses `returnTo` to render its back link to the page the user came from (e.g. a filtered/paginated list); without it users are sent to the default destination instead of the list they navigated from. Restore the `returnTo` parameter (the AlertRuleMenu export item still relies on this mechanism).

title: Comment and variable name still describe ruler-rule preloading that was removed
body: The ruler prefetch (`alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)`) was removed from `useGrafanaGroupsGenerator`, but the surrounding comment still says "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX..." and the local variable is still called `cacheAndRulerPreload`. Both now describe behaviour that no longer exists and will mislead future readers into thinking ruler rules are still fetched here; update the comment and rename the variable (e.g. `cachePreload`).

title: No test covers Delete/Silence in the prom-only list; the new test asserts the broken behaviour
body: The new "should render correct menu actions" test grants AlertingRuleDelete and per-folder delete permissions but then asserts `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)` (Silence, Copy link, Duplicate, Export), i.e. it locks in the fact that Delete is missing from the prom-only list view; it also never clicks Silence even though the drawer cannot render without a ruler rule. Additionally, `RulesTable.test.tsx` mocks `useRulerRuleAbilities`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` wholesale, so the `(ruler ability) || (prom ability)` combination logic is never exercised with real hooks, and the newly added `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`/`useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` have no direct unit tests for provisioned rules or folder-loading states. Add at least one test that grants delete/silence and verifies the actions actually work in the prom-only list.

title: Delete action never renders in the new alert list because it is still gated on rulerRule
body: AlertRuleMenu now computes `canDelete` from both the ruler rule and the new Grafana prom-rule abilities (line 87), and the new list view (`GrafanaRuleListItem` -> `RuleActionsButtons.V2`) passes only `promRule`, never `rulerRule`. But the Delete item is still rendered behind `canDelete && rulerRule && ...`, so with `rulerRule === undefined` the Delete entry is never shown even when the prom-rule ability grants delete. This drops rule deletion from the alert list, which the previous `GrafanaRuleLoader` supported by loading the ruler rule. The `onClick` also passes `rulerRule` to `handleDelete`, so the `(rule: RulerRuleDTO, groupIdentifier)` handler contract has to be relaxed; the delete modal already only needs the `identifier` computed two lines above. Note the updated `GrafanaGroupLoader` test asserts exactly 4 menu items, so it codifies the regression instead of catching it.

title: Silence notifications menu item is a no-op in the new rule list view
body: In the list view `RuleActionsButtons.V2` receives only `promRule`, so `rule` (the `RulerRuleDTO`) is `undefined`. The menu still shows "Silence notifications" because `AlertRuleMenu` derives `canSilence` from the new Grafana prom-rule ability, and `handleSilence` just sets `showSilenceDrawer = true`. However the drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, which is never the case when `rule` is undefined, so clicking the menu item opens nothing. Either `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` must be refactored to accept the prom rule/identifier, or the Silence item must be hidden when no ruler rule is available. The new `GrafanaGroupLoader` test only checks that the item exists and never clicks it, so this is not covered.

title: Grafana rules are rendered without a React key in the filtered list
body: The `grafana` branch returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem ...>` without the `key` that the other branches pass (and that the old `GrafanaRuleLoader` element received from this map). The list is built incrementally with `rules.concat(...)` during infinite scrolling, so React will reconcile all items by position, emit "each child in a list should have a unique key" warnings, and can attach state belonging to one rule (open dropdown, delete modal, clone redirect inside `RuleActionsButtons`) to a different rule as pages are appended. Pass `key={key}` as in the `datasource` and default branches.

title: Prom-rule abilities wrongly treat recording rules as not exportable/pausable
body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` gates `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore` and `DeletePermanently` on `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, whereas the ruler-based implementation that it mirrors used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` (i.e. alerting *and* recording rules). Grafana recording rules can be paused and exported today, so in the new prom-rule-driven list view the Export menu item disappears for Grafana recording rules, and a recording rule in the recently-deleted view would lose `DeletePermanently`/`Restore`. Only `Silence` should be restricted to alerting rules; the remaining actions should use `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`.

title: Federated rule-group detection removed from the shared ruler abilities hook
body: The refactor replaced `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` with `const isFederated = false;` in `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`. That hook is still reached via `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` from `RuleActionsButtons`/`RuleDetails`, whose `CombinedRule` still carries `rule.group.source_tenants`. As a result, Mimir federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable: Edit/Pause/Delete/Permanently-delete actions will be offered for groups the ruler API exposes as read-only, and the requests will fail. The federation flag needs to be threaded through (from the group or an extended group identifier) instead of being hard-coded to false.

title: Delete action is hidden for prom-rule-only list items
body: The Delete menu item is guarded by `canDelete && rulerRule`. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem` passes only a `promRule` to `RuleActionsButtons`/`AlertRuleMenu` (no `rulerRule`), so `rulerRule` is undefined in the new list view and the Delete item never renders even when `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` reports the user has delete permission. The delete modal already receives the identifier, so requiring a ruler DTO here unnecessarily removes delete from the list view. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test expects only four menu items, so it does not catch this regression.

title: Pause action is hidden for prom-rule-only list items
body: The Pause menu item is guarded by `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`. In the new prom-only list path `rulerRule` is undefined, so the Pause/Pause? menu item is never rendered even though `canPause` can be true from the new Grafana prom-rule abilities. Users lose the ability to pause Grafana rules from the list. The condition should also accept the Grafana prom rule for this path.

title: Grafana recording rules lose pause/export/delete-permanently abilities
body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` gates `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore`, and `DeletePermanently` on `isAlertingRule` (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule`). The old ruler-based implementation used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule`, which includes recording rules, so Grafana-managed recording rules now lose these abilities and their menu entries in the prom-only list. Use a predicate covering all Grafana prom rules or explicitly handle recording rules.

title: Federated Mimir rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hard-codes `isFederated = false`. Previously this path called `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, so federated rule groups were included in `immutableRule` and edit/delete/pause/restore/delete-permanently abilities were disabled. Consumers of `useAlertRuleAbility` on federated Mimir groups will now be shown mutation actions that the backend rejects.

title: skipToken still grants the Grafana duplicate ability
body: When `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` receives `skipToken`, they call `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)`, but that function still sets `MaybeSupported` to `AlwaysSupported` (when not loading) and builds abilities from `getRulesPermissions('grafana')`. In particular `Duplicate` becomes `[true, true]` for any user with Grafana `AlertingRuleCreate`. `AlertRuleMenu` calls this with `skipToken` for non-Grafana `promRule`s and ORs `canDuplicate` with the ruler ability, so a user with Grafana create permission but without external-rule write permission can see Duplicate on data source rules. `skipToken` should yield all-false abilities.

title: Grafana rule list items are rendered without a React key
body: In the `origin === 'grafana'` switch branch, the mapped `GrafanaRuleListItem` is returned without the computed `key`. The previous `GrafanaRuleLoader` used `key={key}`. These items contain stateful action components and the list grows while paginating, so missing keys can cause React to reuse the wrong instance/state and emits duplicate-key warnings. Pass the computed key.

title: Grafana rule list links no longer preserve returnTo
body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the view URL with `createReturnTo()`. The new component builds `/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view` without a `returnTo` parameter, so navigating from a filtered list to a rule (and then to edit) no longer preserves the list/filter location as the return target. Add `returnTo` as before.

title: Group loader comment still mentions Ruler loading
body: The component doc comment still says it 'Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints', but this PR removed the Ruler query and the component now only uses Prometheus. Update the comment to avoid misleading future changes.

title: Interpolation before querySupportsSplitting bypasses the $__range guard
body: runSplitQuery applies template variables to every target at line 299 before partitioning with querySupportsSplitting. applyTemplateVariables resolves $__range against the full request range and removes the token, so isQueryWithRangeVariable in querySupportsSplitting no longer detects these queries and they are split. Each time chunk then keeps the full-range duration (for example rate({...}[$__range]) becomes rate({...}[2d]) in every 1-day chunk), producing overlapping or double-counted results; these queries were previously left unsplit specifically to avoid that. Check the range variable on the raw expression before interpolation, or carry the original expression through to the guard.

title: Targets are interpolated twice on the shard-splitting path
body: runShardSplitQuery maps every target through applyTemplateVariables here, and then each shard group calls runSplitQuery, which applies applyTemplateVariables again (querySplitting.ts:299). Template interpolation is not idempotent: a literal escaped dollar such as $$__range becomes $__range after the first pass and is substituted on the second, and variable values containing $ are re-expanded. The new test expecting 5 applyTemplateVariables calls (one initial plus four shard groups) asserts this double interpolation. Pass already-interpolated targets to the nested splitting call or add an option to skip interpolation there.

title: Empty-after-interpolation targets are not filtered out
body: The expr filter runs before applyTemplateVariables. A query whose whole expression is a variable (for example $query) passes the filter even when interpolation produces an empty string, so runSplitQuery can execute datasource.runQuery with an empty expr. On the shard path the same ordering in shardQuerySplitting.ts:50 lets such an empty target reach groupTargetsByQueryType; when it is later passed to runSplitQuery it is filtered out and can leave the grouped request list empty, causing the Math.max/undefined access in runSplitGroupedQueries to fail. Filter again after mapping, as the old shard code did, or map before filtering.

title: Interpolation before partitioning bypasses the `$__range` non-splitting guard
body: At line 299 the targets are interpolated before `querySupportsSplitting` is evaluated at line 300. `querySupportsSplitting` (lines 282-288) explicitly rejects expressions containing `$__range`/`${__range}` because splitting would change the range used for that variable. Once `applyTemplateVariables` has replaced `$__range` with its value, `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` no longer finds it, so such queries are classified as splittable and executed as multiple subqueries. This silently disables the existing guard (and makes its comment false). Either evaluate the guard against the original target before interpolation, or, if pre-interpolation is intended to make `$__range` safe, remove the guard/comment and add a regression test.

title: Shard splitting interpolates each target twice
body: `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates every target here with `applyTemplateVariables(..., request.filters)`, then each shard request is sent through `runSplitQuery`, which interpolates the same targets again at querySplitting.ts:299. The updated test `Interpolates queries before running` now expects five `applyTemplateVariables` calls for a single target, confirming the double pass. Interpolation is not guaranteed idempotent: a variable value that itself contains `$...` will be expanded on the second pass, and ad-hoc filters passed in the third argument can be applied twice, potentially changing the query (and adding repeated work per shard). Interpolate once, or add an option so `runSplitQuery` skips interpolation when called from the shard path.

title: Shard path interpolates every query twice
body: runShardSplitQuery now interpolates each target with applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) and then calls runSplitQuery (line 163), which this PR also changed to interpolate every target again (querySplitting.ts:296-299). A single query is therefore templated once up front and once more for each shard/time sub-request; the updated test at shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112 asserts exactly this (5 calls for one target). applyTemplateVariables is not guaranteed to be idempotent: it applies ad hoc filters from request.filters to the stream selector, so the second pass appends the same filters again (e.g. {a="b", foo="bar", __stream_shard__="1", foo="bar"}), and it re-evaluates any template syntax introduced by a previous substitution. This can silently change the query sent to Loki whenever ad hoc filters or variables whose values contain template text are used. Interpolation should happen once per target; for example, have runShardSplitQuery interpolate and prevent runSplitQuery from re-interpolating already-interpolated targets, or move interpolation to a single shared entry point.

title: querySupportsSplitting's $__range exclusion is now evaluated after interpolation
body: Interpolation now happens before partition(queries, (query) => !querySupportsSplitting(query)) on line 300. querySupportsSplitting excludes queries containing $__range because splitting them makes that variable wrong, but it now checks the already-interpolated query.expr. applyTemplateVariables runs the expression through templateSrv.replace, so wherever a time range is available $__range is substituted and isQueryWithRangeVariable no longer sees it, meaning those queries are now time-split despite the explicit guard. The exclusion should be checked against the raw expression before interpolation (or the raw expression should be carried alongside the interpolated one), and there should be a regression test with $__range.

title: Test locks in double interpolation instead of catching it
body: This expectation was changed from asserting one interpolation (interpolateVariablesInQueries once) to asserting five applyTemplateVariables calls (one initial target plus one for each of the four shard sub-requests). That codifies the redundant/unsafe double interpolation rather than detecting it; after fixing interpolation to run once per target this should assert a single call. There is also no test that ad hoc filters from request.filters are applied exactly once through the shard + time splitting path, which is where the duplication becomes user-visible.

title: traceID dropped from 'Plugin Request Completed' logs
body: The diff removes the explicit trace correlation from logRequest (`traceID := tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` plus its append to logParams) and now relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` to populate the log record. However, the contextual attributes installed by the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext` are only endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname; they do not include a trace ID. Unless `ConcreteLogger.FromContext` independently extracts the trace ID from the OTel span, the 'Plugin Request Completed' lines lose their traceID field, breaking the log/trace correlation these logs had before this PR. Verify traceID still appears and add a test that asserts it.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards the injected logger, making FromContext-based logs unassertable
body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns a brand-new `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver (or a logger sharing the same `Logs`). `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now emits its log via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. When a `TestLogger` is injected into the middleware, the Info call is recorded on the throwaway logger returned by FromContext, so `testLogger.InfoLogs.Calls` stays 0. Any test (existing or newly added) that asserts the middleware logged a request cannot observe it, and the moved contextual-logging behavior is effectively untestable with this fake. `FromContext` should return a logger that records into the same `Logs` as the receiver.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware and moved log fields are untested
body: Responsibility for endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname was moved out of LoggerMiddleware's explicit logParams into the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware, and the middleware ordering in pluginsintegration.go was changed (Metrics -> ContextualLogger -> Logger). There is no test for the new middleware and no test asserting those fields still appear in 'Plugin Request Completed' logs after the move. A regression in the middleware ordering or in `log.WithContextualAttributes`/`FromContext` would silently drop all these fields with no failing test. Add coverage that exercises the full chain and asserts the emitted log record contains the expected fields.

title: FromContext silently drops contextual attributes on type-assertion failure
body: `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` type-asserts the value returned by `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` to `*log.ConcreteLogger`; if the infra logger ever returns a different concrete type (for example a future wrapper around the concrete logger), the assertion fails and the method returns `d.New()`, a plain logger without the contextual attributes. Because this wrapper is now the only path by which pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname reach the backend request logs, a failed assertion would silently drop every one of those fields. Wrap the returned `log.Logger` directly (assign it to an interface-typed field) rather than asserting a concrete type, or at minimum surface the failure.

title: TestLogger.FromContext drops the receiver's recorded logs
body: `FromContext` returns a brand-new `TestLogger` instead of the receiver or a child sharing the same `Logs`. `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now calls `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, so when a test passes a `*TestLogger` into `NewLoggerMiddleware`, the log call is recorded on an unreachable new logger and the original logger's `InfoLogs` stays empty. Existing or new assertions that the middleware logged `Plugin Request Completed` will fail or silently stop covering the logging path. Return `f` (or a child wired to the same `Logs`) and, if needed, store the context attributes on that child.

title: New contextual logger middleware is untested after behavior was moved
body: The contextual logging behavior was moved out of the instrumentation middleware into this new middleware, but no test was added for it. The renamed metrics test only validates Prometheus metrics; it does not verify that `QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics` enrich the context with `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, and `uname`, nor that `LoggerMiddleware` consumes those attributes. Because `LoggerMiddleware` no longer appends these fields itself, a regression in this middleware would silently remove all plugin/request metadata from `Plugin Request Completed` logs. Add a test that captures the contextual attributes observed by the logger.

title: TestLogger.FromContext records logs on an unreachable logger
body: LoggerMiddleware now logs every request through m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...). The new TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger(), i.e. a different TestLogger instance with its own empty Logs. The log call therefore goes to an instance the test cannot access, while the TestLogger passed to NewLoggerMiddleware remains with InfoLogs.Calls == 0. Existing logger-middleware tests that inspect the supplied TestLogger will fail, and the new contextual logging behavior cannot be asserted. The fake should return the receiver or a logger sharing the same Logs sink.

title: No test covers the moved contextual logging and middleware ordering
body: The PR moves pluginId, endpoint, user, data source, and trace attributes out of the metrics/logger middleware and makes LoggerMiddleware depend on the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware plus Logger.FromContext. The only test touched, metrics_middleware_test.go, still asserts metrics only; no test verifies the new middleware or the two-middleware interaction. A wrong middleware ordering or a FromContext implementation that drops the attributes would silently remove all request identifiers from backend plugin logs without failing tests. Add a test that chains ContextualLoggerMiddleware before LoggerMiddleware and asserts the logged InfoLogs contain endpoint, pluginId, dsName/dsUID, uname, and traceID.

title: Device limit is bypassed because the local cache is populated before the DB write succeeds
body: In `tagDeviceUI` the device's cache key is written (`a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})`, line 87) *before* `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs (line 93). With the new `return err` at line 147, `ErrDeviceLimitReached` now propagates through `TagDevice` into `Anonymous.Authenticate`, which returns `nil, err` and fails the request. But the cache entry set on line 87 is never removed on failure. On the next request from the same device (within the 29-minute cache TTL) `tagDeviceUI` hits the cache and returns nil without touching the DB, so `Authenticate` succeeds. Net effect: the limit only fails the very first request per device per 29 minutes and is trivially bypassed by reloading the page; furthermore, an expired device that `updateDevice` refuses to update still reaches the app on retry without ever being recorded, so it never counts toward the limit. The cache must only be populated after a successful write, and `ErrDeviceLimitReached` must not be masked by a cache hit.

title: Count-then-insert device limiting is not atomic and allows exceeding the limit
body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` first calls `CountDevices` and, only if `count < deviceLimit`, runs a separate INSERT ... ON CONFLICT. The count and the insert are independent statements with no transaction, lock, or conditional insert. Under concurrency, two first-time requests from different new devices can both observe `count < deviceLimit` and both insert, so the number of tracked devices exceeds the configured `device_limit`. Because tagging now runs synchronously on the authentication path, this race is easy to trigger with parallel browser sessions. The limit needs to be enforced atomically (e.g. a single conditional insert that also checks the count, or serialization via a lock), otherwise the configured limit is only advisory.

title: Zero affected rows is conflated with 'device limit reached', producing false limit errors
body: `updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` whenever the UPDATE affects 0 rows. Zero rows means 'no row matched the WHERE clause', which also happens for legitimate cases that are not a limit breach: (a) a device that already exists but has not been updated in the last 30 days is excluded from `CountDevices` but its old `updated_at` is outside the `BETWEEN now-30d AND now+1m` window, so it can never be re-activated while the store is at capacity and is incorrectly reported as 'limit reached'; (b) on MySQL, `RowsAffected` reports *changed* rows, so if client_ip/user_agent are unchanged and `updated_at` is truncated to the same value the row matches but 0 rows are reported, yielding a false limit error. The error means 'could not refresh this device', not specifically 'limit reached', so callers and users are misled.

title: Device-limit rejection is returned as a raw error and surfaces as an internal server error
body: When `TagDevice` returns `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached`, `Authenticate` returns `nil, err`. That error is a plain `fmt.Errorf` with no HTTP status mapping, so the authn middleware has no way to translate it and the client over the limit receives an internal-server (500) response rather than a defined status such as 403/429. The raw 'device limit reached' string is also exposed. A dedicated typed/status error should be returned so the caller can respond with a meaningful status and message.

title: Anonymous authentication now performs a synchronous DB call using the request context
body: The previous implementation tagged the device in a detached goroutine (`context.Background()` with a 2-minute timeout and a panic recovery). The new code calls `TagDevice(ctx, ...)` inline in `Authenticate` with the inbound request context. This adds a DB round-trip (a count plus an upsert) to the anonymous auth path, makes tagging fail if the inbound request context is cancelled or short-lived, and removes the panic recovery so a panic in tagging now propagates into authentication. If synchronous enforcement is required, at least keep panic recovery and use a bounded/detached context rather than the raw request context.

title: Provider signature changed without regenerating wire_gen.go
body: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` changed its dependency from `anonstore.AnonStore` to `db.DB`, and `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` now requires an extra `int64` argument for which there is no wire provider. `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` is registered through Grafana's wire dependency graph, and `pkg/server/wire_gen.go` is generated but committed. That file is not part of this PR, so it still calls the old signature and the build will fail to compile unless `wire_gen.go` (and any wire set referencing `ProvideAnonDBStore`) is regenerated.

title: No test covers the primary enforcement path or the cache-driven bypass
body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only asserts that a brand-new device gets `ErrDeviceLimitReached` a single time; it does not assert that an existing, in-window device can still be successfully re-tagged while the store is at capacity (the main reason for `updateDevice`), nor does it exercise the end-to-end rejection through `Anonymous.Authenticate`. `impl_test.go` only runs with the default limit of 0. As a result, neither the retry-after-error bypass (cache set before write, see impl.go) nor the false-limit cases in `updateDevice` are caught by the tests.

title: Frontend type allows undefined but backend always sends 0
body: `anonymousDeviceLimit` is typed `number | undefined` here (and defaulted to `undefined` in `GrafanaBootConfig`), but the backend DTO field `FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit int64` has no `omitempty`, so the JSON always contains the key and it is `0` when the feature is unlimited. Consumers that test `=== undefined` to detect 'not configured' will never match; they must treat `0` (or `<= 0`) as unlimited. Either make the DTO field a pointer with `omitempty` or type it as `number` and document that 0 means unlimited.

title: Local cache is filled before the DB write, letting devices bypass the limit on retry
body: In tagDeviceUI the device's cache key is written with `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` *before* `CreateOrUpdateDevice` is called. This PR now propagates the DB error out of TagDevice (the added `return err` at the end of TagDevice) and client.go turns `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` into an authentication failure. So when a brand-new device is rejected because the limit is reached, its cache key is already populated for 29 minutes. The next request from that same device hits the cache, tagDeviceUI returns nil, TagDevice returns nil, and authentication succeeds even though the limit is still reached and the device was never persisted. In practice the device limit can be defeated by simply retrying/refreshing. Transient DB errors have the same effect (no retry for 29 minutes). Populate the cache only after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, or delete the key on error.

title: Provider signatures changed without updating callers/generated DI, breaking the build
body: `ProvideAnonDBStore` now requires an extra `deviceLimit int64` argument and `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` (impl.go) changed its third parameter from `anonstore.AnonStore` to `db.DB`. Both are dependency-injection providers whose call sites live outside the changed files (the wire provider set / generated `wire_gen.go`). Those callers still invoke the old signatures (passing an `AnonStore` where `db.DB` is now expected, and calling `ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore)` with one arg), so the package will not compile. The generated/registered providers must be regenerated/updated in this PR; wire cannot synthesize the bare `int64` argument either.

title: Device-limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice runs `CountDevices` in one DB session and then performs the INSERT/UPDATE in a separate session with no transaction or locking. Under concurrent anonymous traffic, two (or more) new devices can both observe `count < s.deviceLimit` and both insert, so the configured cap can be exceeded by up to the degree of concurrency. Enforce the limit atomically (single transaction with row locking, or an atomic conditional insert) if the cap is meant to be hard.

title: Device tagging moved onto the synchronous authentication hot path
body: Tagging used to run in a fire-and-forget goroutine with a 2-minute background timeout, so DB writes never affected request latency. It is now a synchronous call in Authenticate using the request context. Every cache-miss request (once per device per ~29 min, and always when the limit check runs it also issues a COUNT plus INSERT) now blocks authentication on DB round trips, adds latency to anonymous requests, and lets a slow or cancelled request context silently drop the tag. Consider keeping the write off the auth path or bounding it with a timeout/background context.

title: Frontend type says `number | undefined` but server always sends a number
body: The Go DTO field is `int64` without `omitempty`, so `anonymousDeviceLimit` is always present in the frontend settings (0 when unset), and GrafanaBootConfig's default of `undefined` is overwritten by 0. The TS declaration `number | undefined` therefore can never be undefined at runtime. Consumers cannot distinguish "not configured" from an explicit 0, and any `!== undefined` check will treat the disabled default as a real limit of 0. Either emit it as `omitempty`/pointer on the server and keep `undefined` in TS, or type it as `number` and document that 0 means "no limit".

title: New `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` option is not documented in the sample config
body: The new `device_limit` key is read in `readAuthSettings` but is not added to `conf/sample.ini`/`conf/defaults.ini` (or the docs). Operators have no way to discover the option or its default (0 = disabled). Add the documented default to the sample config and reference documentation.

title: New test only covers rejecting new devices, not allowing existing ones at the limit
body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only asserts that a second, new device gets ErrDeviceLimitReached. It does not exercise the other required behavior: when the limit is reached, an already-tracked device must still be allowed to refresh via the updateDevice path. That branch contains non-trivial `updated_at BETWEEN ... AND ...` window logic, and a regression there (e.g., legitimately active devices being wrongly rejected) would not be caught. Add a test that re-tags the existing device after the limit is reached and expects success.

title: Device limit is bypassed because the device ID is cached before the store write
body: tagDeviceUI writes the device cache key before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. With the new limit enforcement, a new device over the limit gets ErrDeviceLimitReached from the store, but the cache entry stays. The next request from that device hits localCache.Get and returns nil without calling the store, so Anonymous.Authenticate succeeds and the device is never counted. Parallel requests from the same device can also pass immediately while the first request is still being rejected. Move SetDefault until after a successful create/update, or delete the key on error.

title: Device limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice first runs CountDevices in one DB session, then performs the upsert in another session. Two concurrent requests from different new device IDs can both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert, exceeding the configured limit. Because device IDs are supplied by the client and requests can be parallel, this is reachable.
