A client-specific resource is created whenever any client-specific permission exists for that client, even if it belongs to a different admin. As a result, a user with global `manage`/`configure`/`view` on all clients can be denied access to a client merely because some unrelated client-specific permission exists for it; global deny policies can be bypassed in the same way. The evaluator must combine applicable permissions from both the per-client resource and the all-clients resource rather than treating the per-client resource as a complete replacement.

title: getClientsWithPermission cannot see per-client resources
body: `getClientsWithPermission` queries `resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`, but per-client resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` are created with `resourceStore.create(server, name, owner)` and never assigned type `Clients`; only the all-clients resource created in `init` has that type. Consequently, when only per-client grants exist this method returns an empty set, and when an all-clients grant exists it adds the literal name `Clients` instead of actual client IDs. Callers that use the returned set to filter clients by per-client permission will see incorrect results. Either set the resource type when creating per-client resources or query them in another way.

title: getResourceName does not handle Clients resources
body: `getResourceName` resolves `Users` resources to usernames and maps the all-users resource to "All users", but the schema now also defines `Clients` and this method has no corresponding branch. Client-specific resources are named with the internal client ID and the all-clients resource is named `Clients`, so permission listings fall back to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is null or an internal ID instead of the client ID or "All clients". Add client resolution analogous to the existing user handling.

title: Client deletion no longer cleans up permissions when only V2 is enabled
body: The listener now wraps all cleanup in `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (the V1 feature). With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled and V1 disabled, the `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` branch is skipped, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` anyway, so there is no V2 cleanup path. Per-client resources and scope permissions created for `Clients` survive after their client is deleted, leaving stale authorization data in the admin-permissions client. A V2-specific cleanup path is needed for removed clients.

title: Exit code 4 changes meaning from recreate-required to feature-disabled
body: This PR changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and assigns 4 to the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` result. Exit code 4 was the actual value emitted by the previous implementation, so any existing automation that used the real binary contract (rather than the older documentation) will now interpret a disabled-preview-feature result as “recreate upgrade required” and may proceed to shut down the deployment instead of treating the command as unavailable. Since the documentation explicitly calls the exit code the stable scripting interface, avoid reusing the existing numeric code for a new condition or ensure all consumers are updated in the same change.

title: Documented exit codes are not asserted in the CLI tests
body: The new feature-disabled test only asserts the error text, not that the command exits with the newly documented code 4. Likewise, `testWrongVersions` only checks the incompatibility message and does not assert that an incompatible result exits with the newly documented code 3. Since the PR changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`, a regression in the exit-code contract would pass these tests even though automation relies on those codes. Add `assertEquals(4, result.exitCode())` for the disabled-feature case and `assertEquals(3, result.exitCode())` for the incompatible-version cases, covering both `metadata` and `check` subcommands where applicable.

title: Default update-strategy tests skip enabling the now-mandatory rolling-updates feature
body: The new operator documentation says the `rolling-updates` feature must be enabled or the Operator will fail, but `createInitialDeployment` returns before adding the feature to the Keycloak CR whenever `updateStrategy == null`. Both `testImageChange` and `testCacheMaxCount` are parameterized with `null` (the default `<not set>` strategy), so these cases either rely on the test image built by `Dockerfile-custom-image` already having the feature baked in, or they will fail if run against an image without it. The documented CR-based enabling path is therefore not exercised for the default strategy. Enable the feature in the CR for all test cases, or scope the documentation requirement to explicit update strategies.

title: Recreate exit code changes from 4 to 3, breaking existing automation
body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` changes from 4 to 3 while 4 is reused for the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` result. Any CI/CD pipeline that currently checks the actual runtime exit code 4 for a recreate-required result will now either see 3 or misinterpret 4 as “feature disabled”. The guide already documented 3, so this fixes a code/doc mismatch, but it is still an unannounced behavior change to the command’s scriptable contract. Prefer assigning a new code such as 5 to `FEATURE_DISABLED` to preserve the existing recreate value, or explicitly call out and version the breaking change.

title: New and changed exit codes are not asserted
body: The feature-disabled test only asserts the stderr message and never checks that the process exits with the documented code 4. Likewise `testWrongVersions` never asserts the recreate-required exit code after `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` changed to 3. Since the exit code is the primary scriptable API of this command, a regression in `picocli.exit` or `CompatibilityResult` would pass the test suite. Add assertions for `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` and `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE`, and cover the feature-disabled path for both `metadata` and `check`.

title: Exit codes changed by this PR are not asserted in any test
body: The documented contract of `update-compatibility check` is its exit code: update-compatibility.adoc tells consumers to rely only on the exit code (0 = rolling possible, 3 = recreate required, 4 = feature disabled). This PR changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`, but `UpdateCommandDistTest` only asserts log text. `testFeatureNotEnabled` (line 49) and `testWrongVersions` (lines 97 and 106) never call `result.exitCode()`; `testCompatible` is the only test checking a code (0). A regression in the 3/4 codes would pass CI unnoticed. Add `assertEquals(4, ...)` for the feature-disabled case and `assertEquals(3, ...)` for the incompatible-version cases.

title: Default (null) strategy cases do not enable rolling-updates that the new docs call mandatory
body: `createInitialDeployment` returns early when `updateStrategy` is null, so `testImageChange(null)` and `testCacheMaxCount(null)` run against a CR that does not enable the `rolling-updates` feature. The docs added in this PR (advanced-configuration.adoc CAUTION) state the feature must be enabled or the Operator will fail, and `testCacheMaxCount(null)` expects a rolling update on a configuration change — behavior the flag is supposed to gate. Unless `getTestKeycloakDeployment(true)` already enables preview features, these two parameterized cases will either fail or silently exercise the un-gated path. Enable the feature for the null case as well, or reconcile the documentation with the actual behavior.

title: setEnabledFeatures replaces any existing enabled features on the test deployment
body: After creating a `FeatureSpec` only when it is null, the code calls `setEnabledFeatures(List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))`, which overwrites the entire enabled-features list. If `getTestKeycloakDeployment(true)` returns a CR that already enables other features needed by the deployment (the null check implies a non-null FeatureSpec is possible), adding rolling-updates silently drops them and changes what the test actually deploys. Append to the existing list (or assert it is empty) instead of replacing it.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: The method collects groupResource.getId() (the generated authorization-resource UUID) into the returned set, and line 122 passes that same value to hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...). But group resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource with name = the group id while the resource id is a generated UUID, and hasPermission resolves its argument via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). For a per-group resource the lookup therefore misses and evaluation falls back to the all-groups resource, so the set never contains real group ids. Callers use this set as a group-id filter: UsersResource.searchForUser puts it into the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute and UsersResource.getUsersCount and BruteForceUsersResource pass it to the user provider. Consequences: (1) per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions never restrict the database query, so pagination is applied to the unfiltered user list and users the caller can see can be missing from a page, and the count is not group-restricted; (2) when the caller has VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on the all-groups resource, the set contains the all-groups resource UUID, which no group has, so user search and count return no users at all. The new tests only grant per-group member permissions and use first=-1/max=-1, so neither case is covered.

title: canManage() accepts VIEW scope, so a view-only admin can create groups
body: canManage() (no group argument) returns true when the caller has any of VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource, while canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires MANAGE. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup calls auth.groups().requireManage(), which uses this method, so an admin granted only VIEW on all groups can create top-level groups. The javadoc added to GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() repeats the VIEW-or-MANAGE rule, so both the implementation and the documentation should be corrected to require MANAGE.

title: All-groups permission is ignored once any per-group resource exists
body: hasPermission only falls back to the all-groups resource when resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) returns null. As soon as a per-group resource exists for any scope, only that resource is evaluated and the all-groups resource is never consulted. Concrete case: an admin holds MANAGE on the all-groups resource and some per-group permission (for example VIEW_MEMBERS) was created for group G; canManage(G), canView(G) and canManageMembership(G) then look only at G's resource, find no MANAGE/VIEW, and deny the action even though the global permission grants it. Global and per-group permissions should be combined (with DENY overriding) instead of treating the existence of a per-group resource as a replacement for the global one.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc names the wrong method
body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says the ForbiddenException is thrown when canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false, but the implementation checks canManageMembers(GroupModel). This documents the wrong permission required to call the method.

title: canManage() grants manage rights to view-only admins
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller only holds the `view` scope on the all-groups resource, because it evaluates `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` and hasPermission returns true if either scope is granted. The no-arg requireManage() is what GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses to authorize the operation (it calls auth.groups().requireManage()), and that endpoint both creates a new top-level group and moves an existing group to the top level when the representation carries an id. So an administrator whose only grant is "view all groups" can create and move groups. The sibling canManage(GroupModel) below correctly checks only MANAGE; this method should be `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. The javadoc added to GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() ("Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") documents the same mistake and should be corrected as well.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns resource ids and never detects per-group grants
body: GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is documented and consumed as returning the ids of groups whose members the caller may see: UsersResource.searchForUser puts the set into the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute consumed by the user search, BruteForceUsersResource does the same, and UsersResource.getUsersCount calls userProvider.getUsersCount(realm, groupIds). The new implementation breaks that contract in two ways. First, `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` only yields the single "Groups" container resource created by AdminPermissionsSchema.init; the per-group resources created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (around lines 118-128) are created via resourceStore.create(...) without any setType() call, so type-based lookup never returns them and per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants are silently ignored. Second, the callback calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...), but hasPermission looks resources up by name (`resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`), so for a real resource the id lookup fails, the code falls back to the "Groups" container resource, and then `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` stores the container's resource id. Consequences: for an admin with VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on all groups, the returned singleton (the container resource id) is used as a group-id filter, so user search and /users/count return no users; for per-group grants the set is empty, so the database-level group restriction is dropped and pagination/`/users/count` are computed over all users even though only some are visible. The set must contain actual group ids (the resource name is the group id, per AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup) and the per-group resources must be discoverable (set their type when created or stop relying on findByType).

title: hasPermission() dereferences a possibly null Groups schema resource
body: When no resource exists for the requested group, hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`. getResourceTypeResource() explicitly returns null when the schema is not supported or when findByName(server, "Groups") finds nothing (for example a realm that enabled admin fine-grained authz v2 before this PR, since AdminPermissionsSchema.init only runs once when the admin-permissions client is created and returns early for existing clients). The policy store dereferences the resource (resource.getId()), so this authorization check throws a NullPointerException / 500 instead of denying access. A null check that returns false (or treats it as "no all-groups permission") is needed.

title: No coverage for members scopes on all groups or for VIEW-only group creation
body: All new visibility tests grant VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on one specific group (createGroupPermission for topGroup), and testViewGroups only exercises the `view` scope. Nothing grants VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on the Groups resource type (createAllGroupsPermission) and then calls GET /users or /users/count, which is exactly the path that consumes GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() and where the new implementation returns resource ids instead of group ids. Similarly, testManageAllGroups only verifies group creation after MANAGE is granted; no test asserts that a VIEW-only grant on all groups must NOT allow creating or moving groups, so the canManage() treating VIEW as MANAGE is not caught. Adding these two cases would cover the regressions.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: The set built by this method is consumed by UsersResource.searchForUser/getUsersCount and BruteForceUsersResource, which pass it into `UserModel.GROUPS`; the user store interprets those values as *group* IDs. This method adds `groupResource.getId()` (the internal authorization Resource UUID) and calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`, which does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` — group resources are named by the group id (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup), so passing the resource id makes the lookup miss and fall back to the shared 'Groups' resource. On top of that, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` never calls `setType(...)` on the resources it creates, so `findByType(server, "Groups")` only ever returns the shared 'Groups' resource and never the per-group ones. Consequence: when an admin is granted VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on the all-groups resource (and cannot view all users via roles/scope), the returned set is non-empty and contains a non-group UUID, so the user search/count is filtered by a group id that matches nothing and returns no users even though the admin should see members of every group; per-group grants are never turned into group ids at all. Add `groupResource.getName()` (the group id) and treat an all-groups grant as 'no filter' (empty set) or expand it to all group ids. The new tests only cover per-group grants and never list users/count with an all-groups member permission, which is why this is not caught.

title: Global canManage() accepts the group VIEW scope, allowing group creation with read-only permission
body: `canManage()` returns true when the caller only has an all-groups VIEW permission (`hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`). This no-arg method is used for enforcement, not just UI: `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` calls `auth.groups().requireManage()`, so an admin who was granted only read access to all groups can create new top-level groups. The per-group counterpart `canManage(GroupModel)` (lines 74-80) correctly requires only the MANAGE scope, so this looks like a copy of `canView()`. Restrict the global check to `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE`.

title: Group removal fails when the V2 group permission management methods are reached
body: GroupPermissionsV2 overrides the management methods (`setPermissionsEnabled`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions`, `resource`, ...) with UnsupportedOperationException, but they are still reachable. `AdminPermissions.registerListener()` registers a `GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent` listener whenever the V1 feature is enabled, and its handler executes `management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)` (AdminPermissions.java line 94). `management()` returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever the V2 feature is enabled, and MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() now returns GroupPermissionsV2 (before this PR it returned the V1 implementation, where the call was a harmless no-op). So in a deployment with both features enabled, deleting any group throws UnsupportedOperationException inside the synchronous provider event and the deletion fails with a 500. The same unsupported methods are reached from `GroupResource.get/setManagementPermissions`, which are only guarded by the V1 feature check. The listener and endpoints must not dispatch to methods the selected implementation rejects (skip the V1 cleanup when V2 is active, or make GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled a no-op).

title: Existing admin-permissions clients never get the new Groups resource type and scopes
body: `init()` returns immediately when the realm already has an admin-permissions client (lines 250-252), so the newly added 'Groups' resource and its scopes (`manage-members`, `view-members`, `manage-membership`) are only created for realms that enable admin permissions after this change. For a realm that already enabled fine-grained admin permissions (the V2 feature is a preview that existed before this PR), the client exists without them. Afterwards every group permission check goes through GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(), which falls back to `getResourceTypeResource(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`; that returns null for such clients and the code immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)` and `new ResourcePermission(null, resource.getScopes(), ...)`, producing an exception (500) for group listing/checks, while creating a group permission fails in `getOrCreateResource()` with ModelException("No scopes found.") because the group scopes were never created. `init()` needs to add missing resource types/scopes to an existing client (or a migration/versioning step is required), and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission should null-check the resource-type resource before dereferencing it.

title: Permissions targeting a group are rendered with the raw group id
body: `getResourceName()` resolves USERS resources to a friendly name ('All users' or the username) but has no branch for GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE. Group resources are created with the group id as their name (`resolveGroup()` returns `group.getId()`), so the resources listed for a group scope permission in the admin API/console are group UUIDs instead of group names. Add a GROUPS branch analogous to the USERS one (resolve the name via `session.groups().getGroupById(...)`).

title: Group listing now performs one permission evaluation per group
body: The pre-computed `canViewGlobal = groupsEvaluator.canView()` short-circuit was removed here and in GroupResource.getSubGroups (line 179), so `canView(g)` is invoked for every returned group. For an admin who holds a global group VIEW/MANAGE permission but no realm-management role - exactly the case the FGAP v2 feature targets - GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel) does not short-circuit on the global grant: it performs a resource lookup plus a policy evaluation per group. Listing a realm with many groups therefore executes one authorization evaluation per group instead of one for the whole request, on every group/subgroup listing call.

title: Javadoc documents a Stream return value for a Set-returning method
body: The `@return` tag says 'Stream of IDs of groups with view permission', but `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns `Set<String>`. Callers reading the contract will assume wrong semantics (stream vs. materialized set, and the Javadoc's 'Stream of IDs' wording). Correct the documented return type.

title: Anchor allowance check is order-sensitive and removes the wrong occurrence
body: In `santizeAnchors` the `Matcher` is built over the original `value`, but inside the loop `value` is reassigned to a shorter string via `value.replaceFirst(...)`. `replaceFirst` removes the first occurrence of the English anchor text from the current string, not the occurrence the matcher is inspecting, and because positions are taken from the old string, matching is only correct when the translation contains the anchors in exactly the same order and count as the English source. A legitimate translation that keeps both anchors but reorders them is reported as "Didn't find anchor tag" (false positive, fails the build); conversely, if English has more anchors than the translation the extra `matcher.find()` never runs and a translation that dropped a required link is not reported (false negative). This undermines the verifier's purpose. Compare the full set of anchor tags (e.g. collect and compare multisets) and strip them based on actual match positions.

title: Account console message changed from i18next {{n}} to Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat
body: This file is the account console's i18next catalog and everywhere else uses `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, `{{2}}` (e.g. `error-invalid-length-too-short` on line 27). The change rewrites `error-invalid-multivalued-size` to Java MessageFormat placeholders `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` plus a ChoiceFormat pattern `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`. The React account console only interpolates `{{...}}` and has no ChoiceFormat support, so if this message is displayed the user will see literal `{0}`, `{2,choice,...}` text instead of the attribute name and limits. Keep the `{{n}}` form in this catalog.

title: Admin console message changed from i18next {{n}} to Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat
body: The admin console catalog uses i18next `{{n}}` placeholders throughout, but this change rewrites `error-invalid-multivalued-size` to Java `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` and adds the Java-only ChoiceFormat `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`. The React admin console cannot interpret `{n}` or ChoiceFormat, so the message will render the raw placeholder/choice text for users if this key is used. This should stay in the `{{n}}` form; Java ChoiceFormat belongs only in the server-side `messages_en.properties`.

title: Lithuanian account messages now contain Italian text
body: The new value `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, not Lithuanian. The previous value was Lithuanian (`Įdiekite ...`), so this is a language regression that will show Italian instructions to Lithuanian users. Replace it with a Lithuanian translation (e.g. `Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo telefone:`).

title: Lithuanian login messages now contain Italian text
body: `loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, but this is the Lithuanian (`messages_lt.properties`) bundle and the previous value was Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see Italian instructions. Replace with a proper Lithuanian string.

title: Simplified Chinese bundle got Traditional Chinese text
body: The rest of this file is Simplified Chinese (`打开应用`, `应用`, `验证码`), but the new `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional characters (`手機`, `應用程式`). The locale is `zh_CN`, so this should be Simplified (`在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`); the current text is a localization regression.

title: Missing English counterpart aborts build with an uncaught RuntimeException
body: `verify()` only catches `IOException` and converts it to `MojoExecutionException`, but `verifySafeHtml()` throws a bare `RuntimeException` when it cannot open the derived English file (`throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e)`). If the derived path does not exist (e.g. a locale whose `_en.properties` counterpart is absent or whose name is not rewritten correctly by the `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` heuristic), the Maven build dies with a stack trace instead of a clean, aggregatable verification message. Throw `MojoExecutionException` (or surface a proper error message) so the plugin reports the problem consistently.

title: Tests only cover failures; no test proves allowed HTML and matching anchors are accepted
body:
All four tests assert that something is flagged (`Duplicate keys`, `Illegal HTML`, `Didn't find anchor tag`). There is no test that exercises the positive path: that a translation containing allowed HTML (`

`, ``, `
`) for an English key that has HTML is accepted, or that a translation whose ``/`` tags match the English source is accepted. Since the PR relies on `POLICY_SOME_HTML` and `santizeAnchors` to avoid false positives (and touched many translation files to satisfy the new check), the anchor-matching bug (order/count handling) and any policy regression would go unnoticed. Add fixtures where verification returns no messages for valid HTML/anchors.

title: Verifier compares sanitizer-canonicalized HTML to raw text, flagging valid markup
body:
verifySafeHtml() compares the OWASP sanitizer output with the original translation using Objects.equals (line 99). The sanitizer re-serializes allowed markup in its own canonical form (it renders `
`/`
` as `
`), so a translation using an equivalent but differently written tag is reported as "Illegal HTML" even though it is valid and permitted by POLICY_SOME_HTML. This already forced the PR to rewrite the `webauthn-error-*` lines in ~15 locale files from `
` to `
` for no functional reason, and the next translator who writes `
` (or `
`) will get a failing build with a misleading message. Both sides should be normalized (e.g. compare sanitized forms of value and expected value, or normalize `` before reporting).

title: Anchor mismatch message does not say which key/file failed
body: When a translation's anchor tag does not exactly match the English source, the verifier adds "Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string" to the messages list. Unlike the Illegal HTML message, it contains neither the message key nor the file. Because the verifier runs over every locale of every theme, a failing build cannot tell the developer which entry to fix, and the same entry typically also produces a generic "Illegal HTML" message. Include key and file, as the Illegal HTML message does.

title: Lithuanian account totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The new value of `totpStep1` is `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. The old Lithuanian sentence was replaced with a string copied from another locale while fixing the stale <a> links, so Lithuanian users of the account console will now see Italian text on the OTP setup page. It needs a real Lithuanian translation (e.g. of "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:").

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: `loginTotpStep1` was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` (Italian) in the Lithuanian login bundle. The removed value was Lithuanian; this replacement is a copy/paste from the Italian locale, so Lithuanian users see Italian instructions during OTP/TOTP setup. It must be translated to Lithuanian.

title: Simplified Chinese bundle receives Traditional Chinese text
body: The new `totpStep1` value `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 應用程式) in the zh_CN (Simplified) file; the rest of this file uses Simplified forms (e.g. `mobile=手机`). The text appears to have been copied from a zh_TW translation and needs to be converted to Simplified Chinese (手机/应用程序).

title: Frontend message changed from {{n}} interpolation to Java MessageFormat choice syntax
body: Every other entry in this account-ui bundle uses the frontend i18n placeholder style `{{0}}`/`{{1}}` (e.g. `error-invalid-length='{{0}}' must have a length between {{1}} and {{2}}.`), but `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `Attribute {{0}} ... {{1}} ... {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} ... {1} ... {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` — single-brace Java MessageFormat syntax plus a ChoiceFormat sub-message. If this key is rendered by the same i18n mechanism as its neighbours, the `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` placeholders will not be substituted and users will see the raw `{2,choice,...}` expression. The same change was made to `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties` line 3139 (which also previously used `{{0}}`).

title: No positive-case tests for the new HTML verification
body:
All added tests only assert that problems are detected (illegal tag, HTML in a no-HTML message, changed anchor). There is no test asserting that a valid file produces an empty messages list, i.e. that a translation using the same anchors as the English source, an allowed `
`, and the special-cased keys (`error-invalid-multivalued-size`, `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`) passes cleanly. A regression that makes the sanitizer reject every legitimate translation (as the `
` serialization issue already shows is easy) would not be caught by unit tests, only by a repository-wide build.

title: Italian text placed in the Lithuanian login translation
body: `loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, not Lithuanian. The PR was supposed to strip the `<a>` links from this key because the English source (`messages_en.properties` `loginTotpStep1`) contains no HTML, but instead the Italian translation was pasted in. Lithuanian users will see Italian instructions for setting up their authenticator. Should read a Lithuanian sentence equivalent to 'Install one of the following applications on your mobile:'.

title: Italian text placed in the Lithuanian account translation
body: `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian in the Lithuanian account message bundle (the same mistake as the login bundle). The other locales in this PR (fi, sv, sk) received properly translated text; the Lithuanian one appears to have been copied from the Italian bundle. Lithuanian users will see Italian text for the TOTP setup step.

title: error-invalid-multivalued-size switched to Java MessageFormat in an i18next bundle
body: This account-console bundle uses i18next `{{...}}` interpolation for numeric arguments throughout (e.g. `error-invalid-length-too-short='{{0}}' ... {{1}}.`). This PR changes `error-invalid-multivalued-size` from `... {{0}} ... {{1}} ... {{2}} value(s).` to `... {0} ... {1} ... {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` — single braces plus a Java `ChoiceFormat` expression. i18next does not understand either form, so when this key is rendered it will show the raw placeholders (including the literal `{2,choice,0#values|...}`) instead of an interpolated message. The same incorrect change is applied in `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties` (~line 3139). Those client bundles should keep the `{{...}}` style; the `choice` format belongs only in the Java theme bundles.

title: Message bundles read as ISO-8859-1 while files are UTF-8
body: `new PropertyResourceBundle(new FileInputStream(file))` decodes the properties using ISO-8859-1, but Keycloak message files are UTF-8 (they contain raw CJK/Arabic/etc. characters, e.g. `messages_zh_CN.properties` `doLogIn=登录`). This differs from `verify()` which reads the file with `Files.readString` (UTF-8). Tag detection still works because tags are ASCII bytes, but every non-ASCII value is decoded to mojibake; consequently the diagnostic strings produced from `value.substring(...)` (and any non-ASCII-dependent logic) will be corrupted, and the two code paths disagree about the file content. Use `new PropertyResourceBundle(new InputStreamReader(fis, StandardCharsets.UTF_8))`.

title: Traditional Chinese characters in a zh_CN (Simplified) bundle
body: `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional characters (`手機`, `應用程式`) in the Simplified-Chinese (zh_CN) resource. Mainland Simplified wording would be `在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`. As written the locale shows the wrong script to Simplified-Chinese users.

title: No positive test that legitimate/matching HTML produces no messages
body:
All added tests assert that something is flagged (`Illegal HTML` or `Didn't find anchor tag`) or that duplicate keys are detected. There is no test asserting that a translation which faithfully reproduces the English HTML — matching `` anchors, allowed `/

//
` — yields an empty message list. Because the check compares the sanitizer's normalized output against the raw value, false positives from benign normalization (e.g. `
` vs `
`, attribute quoting, uppercase tags) are the main failure mode, and with no positive/negative test a regression that starts rejecting valid translations would go unnoticed by the unit suite.

title: Adding non-default getShortcut breaks existing grant provider implementations
body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` now has a new abstract `getShortcut()` method. Any custom grant factory compiled against an older Keycloak does not implement it. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `getShortcut()` for every registered OAuth2 grant factory during server startup, so such an extension will throw `AbstractMethodError` and prevent startup. Make this a default method with a safe fallback, or explicitly tolerate providers that do not implement it.

title: Decoder hard-codes 2-character shortcuts but the factory contract does not
body: The decoder assumes the encoded prefix is exactly 6 characters and splits it into three fixed 2-character fields. The grant field comes from `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()`, whose contract does not enforce a 2-character value (its Javadoc even says 'usually like 3-letters'). A custom grant returning e.g. `foo` will be encoded successfully as `onrtfoo:<id>`, but `getTokenContextFromTokenId` will then reject it because the prefix is 7 characters. Enforce the length at registration or make the decoder length-aware; otherwise Keycloak can issue tokens that it cannot parse itself.

title: validateToken unconditionally tags recreated tokens as refresh-token grant
body: `validateToken` recreates an access token from an existing `oldToken`, and this new line always stores `refresh_token` in `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`. This method is used outside the refresh flow as well (legacy token exchange uses it while validating the subject token and producing the exchanged access token), so those exchanged tokens get the refresh shortcut `rt` instead of the actual token-exchange grant. The grant type should be set by the calling flow, as `StandardTokenExchangeProvider` does, or only set to refresh in the refresh-specific path.

title: Constructor checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
body: The second `Objects.requireNonNull` call is intended to validate `rawTokenId`, but it still passes `grantType` with the message `Null rawTokenId not allowed`. A null raw token ID is therefore accepted. In `encodeTokenId`, concatenating a null raw ID produces the literal string `onrtac:null`, so multiple tokens can share the same `jti` rather than failing fast. Change the second check to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

title: isAccessTokenId has an inverted/wrong grant-shortcut check
body: For an ID like `onrtac:<uuid>`, the grant shortcut occupies indices 4-6 (`ac`), but the matcher reads `substring(3, 5)` (`ta`) and returns false when that value equals the expected shortcut. As written, the grant portion is effectively never checked: any correctly shaped prefix with a UUID suffix passes. If the substring were corrected without also fixing the condition, correct IDs would be rejected. Use `items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` for the positive check and guard the prefix length to avoid `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

title: Incorrect-grant test passes on NPE instead of testing the intended failure
body: The test's `before` method constructs the factory but never sets a `KeycloakSessionFactory`. Looking up an unknown shortcut such as `ac` therefore calls `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` on null and throws NPE. The test catches any `RuntimeException`, so it passes without ever verifying the intended `IllegalArgumentException` for an unknown grant shortcut. Initialize the factory dependency and assert the exception type/message.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing grant provider factories
body: Adding getShortcut() as an abstract method to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is a source/binary incompatible change for every custom grant provider compiled against the old interface. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() iterates all OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances and calls getShortcut(), so an existing provider will throw AbstractMethodError at server startup. Provide a default method or handle missing/unsupported values explicitly.

title: getShortcut() contract does not enforce exactly two characters required by the token ID parser
body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider hardcodes a six-character context and splits it into three two-character pieces, and getTokenContextFromTokenId() rejects prefixes whose length is not 6. The new getShortcut() contract only says 'usually like 3-letters' and does not require a non-null two-character value. A custom grant returning a three-character shortcut produces an access-token jti that the decoder rejects with 'Expected length of 6'; returning null makes ConcurrentHashMap.put throw during postInit. Validate non-null/two-character shortcuts at startup or make the encoding self-delimiting.

title: rawTokenId null check is missing and grantType check is duplicated
body: The constructor checks grantType twice and never checks rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is accepted and then string-concatenated into a jti ending in ':null', while a null grantType throws the misleading message about rawTokenId. The second Objects.requireNonNull call should check rawTokenId.

title: isAccessTokenId does not actually verify the grant shortcut
body: The matcher extracts items[0].substring(3, 5), which is not the grant-shortcut position in the six-character prefix (grant is at [4, 6]), and it returns false when that slice equals the expected shortcut instead of true. As written it never verifies the grant type and passes any prefixed token with a UUID suffix, so the updated integration tests cannot catch wrong grant encoding. It can also throw if the prefix is shorter than five characters. Fix both the offset and the comparison, and validate the prefix length.

title: Removal of public Context(Context) copy constructor breaks API
body: The public OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) copy constructor is removed by this change. Existing extensions or tests that use it to create a copied context will fail to compile, and precompiled callers will fail to link. If removal is not intentional, keep the constructor and copy the new grantType field as well; otherwise the compatibility break should be explicitly documented.

title: New abstract getShortcut breaks existing grant provider factories
body: The new abstract `getShortcut()` method on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` has no default implementation. Existing third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations compiled against an older Keycloak version do not implement it; `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` calls `gtf.getShortcut()` for every registered grant, so such a provider will fail at server startup with `AbstractMethodError` (and source builds will no longer compile). Add a default implementation or avoid calling the method for factories that do not support it, and provide a migration path.

title: Grant shortcut length is not validated against the fixed 6-character format
body: `encodeTokenId` concatenates `grantShort` without checking that it is exactly two characters, while `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` requires the encoded context to be exactly six characters (`sessionType` 2 + `tokenType` 2 + `grantType` 2). The new `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` Javadoc explicitly says a shortcut is usually like 3 letters; a provider following that contract produces an ID such as `onrtabc:<uuid>`, which later fails parsing with `Expected length of 6` (or misreads the grant segment). Validate shortcut length when building the maps (or make the encoder/parser length-aware) and align the Javadoc. There is no test for a non-2-character shortcut.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher does not validate the expected grant shortcut
body: `isAccessTokenId` does not validate the expected grant type. For a valid prefix such as `onrtac`, the grant shortcut is at indexes 4-6 (`ac`), but the matcher reads `substring(3, 5)` (`ta`); it also returns `false` when the compared segment equals `expectedGrantShortcut`, which is inverted. Consequently any token ID of the form `<six chars>:<uuid>` passes regardless of the encoded grant type, so the updated event assertions cannot detect wrong or missing grant encoding. It can also throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` for a colon-containing ID with a short prefix. Use `substring(4, 6)` and reject only when the segment is not equal.

title: Null check on rawTokenId is missing
body: The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...)` twice instead of checking `rawTokenId`. A null raw token ID is therefore accepted; `encodeTokenId` later silently appends the literal `null` (for example `onrtac:null`) instead of failing, and the error message for a null grant type incorrectly says rawTokenId is null.

title: Public Context copy constructor was removed
body: This diff removes the public `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context)` copy constructor. External `OAuth2GrantType` implementations or tests that clone a request context will no longer compile, and there is no replacement constructor that also copies the newly added `grantType` field. Keep and deprecate the constructor, or add an equivalent replacement.

title: Recovery-code creation reads the wrong credential input field
body: CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential builds the UserCredentialModel as new UserCredentialModel("", type, recoveryCodesJson), which stores the JSON in getValue() and leaves getChallengeResponse() null. This update path reads input.getChallengeResponse() as the credential data, so the federated recovery-code credential is persisted with null credentialData. A later getCredentials() call cannot reconstruct a usable RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel from that data, so the new test will fail when rendering or validating the recovery-code form. Read the value from the UserCredentialModel (or populate challengeResponse in the helper consistently).

title: All-codes-used removal does not remove federated credentials
body: After this change getCredential() can return a credential supplied by user storage. When such a credential reports all codes used, this branch calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...), which only removes credentials from Keycloak's local credential store; it does not remove a federated credential from user storage. The exhausted recovery credential therefore remains visible to isConfiguredFor()/getCredential(), and the recovery-code form can still be selected for a credential that has no usable codes (RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean may even call get() on an empty next-code Optional). Removal/disablement needs to go through the federated-aware credential-updater API (for example disableCredentialType) or be delegated explicitly to the user-storage provider.

title: Rebuilt federated recovery credential loses the stored credential id
body: getCredentials() rebuilds the recovery-code credential with RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) but never copies myUser.recoveryCodes.getId(). The reconstructed object therefore has a different (newly generated or null) id than the credential originally stored by updateCredential(). Any caller that identifies the credential by id—account REST deletion or the all-codes-used removal in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator—cannot address the stored credential. Set the id on the reconstructed model from myUser.recoveryCodes.

title: Raw, unhashed recovery codes are handed to user storage while the read path expects hashed credential data
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the plain `generatedCodes` list with `JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)` and passes it to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`, whereas the local branch stores `credentialModel`, whose credentialData is the hashed `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialData` produced by `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues`. The read paths (`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` followed by `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel` in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean and RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator) assume the stored credentialData is that hashed object. A user storage provider that persists the value it receives and returns it in a `CredentialModel` (the normal credential-store contract) will (a) keep the recovery codes in plaintext, so compromising the user store directly yields usable login codes, and (b) cause `createFromCredentialModel` to fail deserializing a JSON array into `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialData`, breaking the login form. The bundled BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage only avoids this because its `getCredentials` re-hashes the raw codes itself.

title: Exhausted recovery-code credential in user storage is never removed and can break the next login
body: After a successful code validation, when the credential reports `allCodesUsed()` the code calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...)`. That method only operates on Keycloak's local credential store; now that recovery-code credentials may live in a user storage provider, a federated credential is not removed (and its id is provider-generated, not a local id). If a provider reports all codes used, the credential and `isConfiguredFor(type)` remain true, so the next login selects the recovery-code authenticator and `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` calls `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()` on an empty Optional, throwing NoSuchElementException (HTTP 500); at best the stale credential is left behind. Removal should be done through the credential manager's type-based disable or the user storage provider.

title: getCredentials dereferences a possibly null MyUser
body: `getCredentials` does `var myUser = getMyUser(user)` and then dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes`, unlike `isValid` (line 285) which returns false when the user is not present in this provider. If `getCredentials` is invoked for a user that is not backed by this provider (for example a local user when the provider is enabled in the realm), it throws NullPointerException. Add a `myUser == null` guard returning `Stream.empty()`.

title: No coverage for local fallback or single-use behavior of user-storage recovery codes
body: The new test only covers the case where the user storage advertises and stores recovery codes. There is no test that recovery codes still end up in local storage when the user storage does not support the type (the other branch of createRecoveryCodesCredential), nor that a user-storage-backed recovery code stops working after use. The bundled provider's `isValid` compares the raw code without marking it used and `getCredentials` always rebuilds the model with all codes unused, so the replay-prevention behavior of the new user-storage path is untested.

title: Recovery codes are written to user storage in plaintext instead of the hashed credential data
body: In the local branch this helper stores `credentialModel`, whose credential data contains SHA-512 hashes of the codes because `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues` hashes every raw code via `hashRawCode`. In the user-storage branch it instead serializes the raw `generatedCodes` list and passes it to `CredentialInputUpdater.updateCredential`. A user storage provider therefore receives and persists the one-time recovery codes in plaintext; anyone able to read the user store can use them (the testsuite provider confirms this: `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid` compares stored values against the raw user input). The value also has a different shape (a bare JSON array) from the `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialData` document the model expects, so a provider that returns the stored value verbatim cannot be parsed by `createFromCredentialModel` (the testsuite provider hides this by rebuilding the model in `getCredentials`). Pass the already-hashed credential data (or hash before serializing) and use the same representation as local storage.

title: Creating recovery codes in user storage leaves a stale local recovery-codes credential
body: When `updateCredential` succeeds in user storage, the method only skips local creation; it never removes a local recovery-codes credential of the same user. Such a local credential is common for federated users, because before this change `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction` always created recovery codes locally. After reconfiguration both credentials exist. The new `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` prefers the federated credential, so `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` displays the next code number from the user-storage set, while `credentialManager().isValid` still consults the built-in local provider and accepts a code from the stale local set. The prompt and the credential actually accepted can disagree. Remove/disable the credential in the other store when one is created, or make lookup and validation consistently use the same source.

title: All-codes-used cleanup cannot delete a recovery-codes credential held in user storage
body: After a successful validation, when all codes are used the authenticator calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. That API addresses the local credential store by id; a credential obtained from `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` via `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` lives in user storage and is not removed this way (the testsuite provider does not even set the stored credential id on the model it returns). The user-storage removal path (`CredentialInputUpdater.disableCredentialType`/update) is never used, so a fully consumed recovery-codes credential remains configured in user storage. No test covers exhausting all codes for a user-storage user.

title: Recovery codes created in user storage are never marked used, so a used code stays valid and is replayed
body: `updateCredential` stores the raw code list, `isValid` only does `anyMatch` against it, and `getCredentials` rebuilds the model with `createFromValues`, which resets every `used` flag. Consequently a recovery code created in user storage is never consumed: the same code can be used for unlimited logins, `allCodesUsed()` never becomes true (so the cleanup/reconfigure logic is unreachable), and the login page always asks for the first code. The new `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` performs a single login, so it does not catch this. Either consume the code through the user-storage updater on successful validation or add a test and clearly document that user storage is responsible for one-time semantics.

title: Recovery-codes model returned from user storage has no id and re-hashes the stored data
body: `getCredentials` builds a new `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` via `createFromValues` and adds it without transferring the id of the stored `myUser.recoveryCodes`. The credential exposed from user storage therefore has a null id, so id-based operations (the form authenticator's all-codes-used removal, account-console deletion) cannot address it, and the test never notices because it only calls `hasRecoveryCodes`. In addition, reconstructing via `createFromValues` hashes the stored values again, which would double-hash if the stored data were already hashed as in the local format. Set the stored id and build the model from the stored credential data.

title: Optional.get() turns a missing or unreadable user-storage credential into a login 500
body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` can return an empty Optional: the user storage may not be configured for the type, or its `getCredentials` may fail to deserialize and return nothing (the testsuite provider logs and returns an empty stream on IOException). Calling `.get()` then throws `NoSuchElementException`, so rendering the recovery-code login page fails with a server error instead of a controlled authentication error. `createFromCredentialModel` can likewise throw if a provider exposes a credential without parseable `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialData`. The bean should handle the absent/invalid case explicitly (e.g., fail the authenticator or prompt reconfiguration).

title: Concurrent-deletion NPE is still reachable through the other getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: The fix only makes getSubGroupsCount() tolerate modelSupplier.get() returning null. The neighbouring overrides getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) (line 256), getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer) (line 262) and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) (line 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` and dereference the result without a null check. When a CachedGroup is read while its row has been deleted concurrently - the exact scenario this PR targets - the delegate returned by modelSupplier is null, so calling these methods on the cached adapter (which is what the paginated/filtered subgroup endpoints do) still throws NPE. The fix is therefore incomplete unless the same null handling is applied there (or the model is fetched and null-checked in one place).

title: Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion can miss the exception it is looking for
body: The reader thread is started and never joined: the main thread deletes the 100 groups, sets deletedAll, and immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty (line 157). Any read request that is still in flight when the last group is deleted - precisely the window in which the NPE occurs - can add its exception to the list after the assertion has already run, so the test can pass even though the bug is present and is inherently racy. In addition, if a remove() call throws before deletedAll is set, this non-daemon thread loops forever, continuing to issue admin requests into subsequent tests and potentially hanging the JVM. The loop should be wrapped in try/finally, the flag set in the finally block, and the thread joined (with a timeout) before asserting.

title: Test never requests subgroup counts, so the method changed by this PR may not be exercised
body: The reader calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)`, which only fills in search/first/max/briefRepresentation. Subgroup counts are populated only when the request opts into them (the subGroupCount request parameter that leads to GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount), and with briefRepresentation=true and no such flag the server never calls GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() - the method this PR modifies. If so, the test would pass on the unfixed code and provides no regression coverage. The read request should explicitly ask for subgroup counts (e.g. the overload with the subGroupCount parameter) so getSubGroupsCount() is on the request path.

title: Unthrottled reader loop hammers the server for the whole duration of the deletions
body: The background loop has no delay/backoff and repeatedly issues `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` admin requests as fast as the client can go while 100 groups are deleted sequentially. On CI this generates a large burst of concurrent requests (each building a list of up to 100 groups) that can starve the server, cause timeouts and make the test flaky. Add a small sleep/backoff or cap the number of iterations.

title: getSubGroupsCount now returns null where it previously always returned a count
body: This method previously never returned null (it either produced a count or threw), so callers had no reason to treat the Long as nullable. With the change, a deleted cached group yields null, which will throw NPE for any caller that auto-unboxes the value (comparisons, arithmetic, or passing it to a primitive parameter) and silently drops the count from serialized representations. The nullability should be documented/handled explicitly, and the callers of GroupModel#getSubGroupsCount audited for unboxing assumptions.

title: Concurrency test never requests subgroup counts and does not exercise getSubGroupsCount
body: The call `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` passes true as `briefRepresentation`; the separate `subGroupsCount` parameter remains at its default false. `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount`, and therefore `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount`, is only invoked when subgroup counts are requested. As written, this regression test would pass even without the production change because the code path that produced the NPE is never executed. The test needs to issue the list request with `subGroupsCount=true` while deletes are happening.

title: Reader thread is never joined or reliably stopped
body: The test starts a non-daemon thread that loops while `deletedAll` is false. `deletedAll.set(true)` is only reached after the delete loop at line 155, so if any `remove()` call throws, the flag is never set and the reader thread keeps issuing requests forever, potentially preventing the test JVM from terminating. Even on the success path the assertion at line 157 runs without joining the reader, so a request already in flight can still add an exception to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion or continue running into the next test. The delete loop should be wrapped in try/finally, the reader must always be signalled to stop, and the test should join/await it before asserting.

title: No synchronization ensures the reader thread performs any read during deletion
body: After `Thread.start()` returns, the main thread immediately starts deleting all 100 groups and then sets `deletedAll`. Scheduling is not guaranteed: the reader may first observe the flag after it has already been set, so its loop body never executes and the test passes without performing any concurrent read. A latch or barrier should ensure the reader has entered at least one list request while groups are being deleted, plus a completion signal so the test can wait for it.

title: New concurrency test never requests sub-group counts, so it does not exercise the fixed method
body: The reader thread calls `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)`. The fourth parameter of that admin-client overload is `briefRepresentation` (see `getGroupsWithBriefAndFullRepresentation` in the same file, where `false` yields full attributes), so the `subGroupsCount` query parameter is not sent and defaults to `false` on the server. `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` (the method changed in this PR) is only invoked via `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount`, which is guarded by `if (subGroupsCount)`. As written, this test never calls the fixed method and would pass with the fix reverted, so it provides no protection against the NPE it is meant to cover. The read must request sub-group counts (e.g. the overload that passes `subGroupsCount=true`) or otherwise force `getSubGroupsCount()` to run while the groups are being deleted.

title: Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion races with it and can pass vacuously
body: `new Thread(...).start()` is fire-and-forget: after the deletes, `deletedAll.set(true)` is followed immediately by `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())`. The assertion can run before the worker has completed (or even started) a single list request, so the test passes without exercising the concurrent read at all, and an exception thrown by an in-flight request after the assertion is silently lost. In addition, if any `remove()` throws, `deletedAll` is never set and the non-daemon worker keeps calling the admin client during and after realm teardown. Set the flag in a `finally` block, `join(timeout)` the worker before asserting, and fail if the thread did not run at least one read iteration.

title: Same NPE still present in the getSubGroupsStream(search/exact, first, max) overloads
body: The fix guards `modelSupplier.get()` against null only in `getSubGroupsCount()`. The three overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 still do `return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` directly. `modelSupplier` resolves to `cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(realm, cached.getId())`, which returns `null` when the group is removed concurrently - exactly the condition this PR fixes for the count. A request for subgroups with search/paging on a concurrently deleted group therefore still throws an NPE and returns a 500. The same null handling should be applied here (e.g. return `Stream.empty()` when the delegate is gone).

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key crashes on datetime fields
body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` reads the raw model attribute and passes it to `math.floor()` / `math.ceil()`. The audit log endpoint calls this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `getattr(item, "datetime")` is a `datetime` object, and `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime`. Unlike `DateTimePaginator`, this class has no `multiplier` / `strftime("%s.%f")` conversion. Because `build_cursor` calls `key(results[-1])` even on the very first page, every request that reaches this paginator returns HTTP 500, so the optimized branch can never serve a result.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns an int where a datetime is required
body: `value_from_cursor()` returns `cursor.value` unchanged (an integer/timestamp number). `BasePaginator.build_queryset()` then interpolates that value into a raw `WHERE` clause on the ordered column (`... WHERE audit_log_entry.datetime <= %s`). For audit logs the column is a timestamp, so comparing it to an integer either raises a Postgres "operator does not exist: timestamp with time zone <= bigint" error or produces wrong ordering. `DateTimePaginator` deliberately overrides this method to convert the cursor value back with `datetime.fromtimestamp(value / multiplier)`; the optimized paginator must do the same (or reuse `DateTimePaginator`) for datetime-ordered querysets. Any request carrying a cursor (page 2+) will fail or paginate incorrectly.

title: enable_advanced_features kwarg is not accepted by Endpoint.paginate
body: `self.paginate(...)` is `Endpoint.paginate`, whose signature is `(request, queryset, order_by, paginator_cls, on_results, default_per_page, max_per_page, max_hits, count_hits, known_hits, cursor)`. It has no `enable_advanced_features` parameter and does not forward arbitrary kwargs to the paginator constructor (it instantiates `paginator_cls(queryset, order_by=..., on_results=..., max_limit=...)`). Passing `enable_advanced_features=True` therefore raises `TypeError: paginate() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_advanced_features'`, so a superuser/global-access user requesting `?optimized_pagination=true` gets a 500 instead of an optimized page. If a constructor option is needed it must be threaded through `paginate` explicitly.

title: Negative-offset "advanced" branch raises instead of paginating
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `start_offset = cursor.offset` and then `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django `QuerySet` slicing explicitly rejects a negative start (`ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`), so the comment claiming "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false and this branch raises a 500 for any cursor carrying a negative offset. Even if the ORM allowed it, negative slicing returns rows from the end of the queryset, which is not the intended "reverse pagination" semantics. Handle negative offsets by clamping/validating (as `OffsetPaginator`, `ChainPaginator`, and `MergingOffsetPaginator` do with `BadPaginationError`) rather than by slicing with a negative index.

title: Switching paginator class by query param breaks cursor continuity
body: The endpoint chooses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` vs `DateTimePaginator` from the client-supplied `optimized_pagination=true` query param, but the two paginators encode the cursor `value` differently: `DateTimePaginator` uses millisecond epoch values and converts them back with `datetime.fromtimestamp`, while `OptimizedCursorPaginator` stores/interprets the raw field value. The `next`/`prev` cursor links generated by `paginate` do not include `optimized_pagination=true`, so a client that follows a next link silently falls back to `DateTimePaginator` with a cursor produced under different semantics, yielding wrong pages or SQL errors. Likewise a superuser who drops the param cannot resume a pagination session started with it. Cursor values must be interchangeable across the paginators (or the chosen paginator must be encoded in the cursor/links) before letting a request parameter switch implementations.

title: Negative-offset clamping in BasePaginator silently changes malformed-cursor behavior
body: For forward cursors (`is_prev` false) this changes `queryset[offset:stop]` to `queryset[max(0, offset):...]`, and for `is_prev` it assigns `offset` unchanged. For all valid (non-negative) cursors it is a no-op, so it does not add the advertised negative-offset capability; it only turns a previously-erroring malformed cursor (negative offset on a forward cursor) into a silent first-page response. That masks client/API bugs and is inconsistent with the other paginators that raise `BadPaginationError("Pagination offset cannot be negative")`. Either reject negative offsets explicitly or document that they are clamped.

title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported but no support was added
body: The added comment says negative offsets are allowed for "advanced pagination scenarios", but the diff only adds a comment—`self.offset = int(offset)` is unchanged. Moreover negative offsets are not actually usable: `OffsetPaginator`, `ChainPaginator`, `MergingOffsetPaginator`, and `CombinedQuerysetPaginator` explicitly raise `BadPaginationError` for negative offsets, and `BasePaginator`'s `is_prev` path still slices with the negative start (which Django rejects). The comment documents behavior that does not exist and will mislead future callers.

title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new endpoint branch
body: The PR adds a new paginator class and a new conditional code path in the audit log endpoint but no tests. Because `OptimizedCursorPaginator` diverges from `BasePaginator`/`DateTimePaginator` in `get_item_key` and `value_from_cursor`, a single test paging an audit-log queryset with `optimized_pagination=true` would have caught the `math.floor(datetime)` crash, the integer-vs-timestamp `WHERE` clause, and the unaccepted `enable_advanced_features` kwarg. Add coverage for the first page, next page, previous page, cursors with non-zero values, and negative/invalid cursor offsets.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime keys
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint routes optimized_pagination=true requests to OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", so self.key is "datetime". This class's get_item_key() calls math.floor()/math.ceil() directly on the datetime value, and value_from_cursor() returns the raw integer cursor instead of converting it back to a datetime. build_cursor() calls get_item_key() on every non-empty page, so the optimized branch raises TypeError ("must be real number, not datetime"); even if that were fixed, build_queryset() would compare a datetime column against an integer cursor value. Any optimized audit-log request with results will fail, and cursors are not interoperable with DateTimePaginator.

title: Advanced negative-offset branch passes negative bounds to Django QuerySet
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, start_offset is left negative and passed to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets do not support negative slice bounds; they raise ValueError/AssertionError ("Negative indexing is not supported") rather than returning reverse-pagination results. A client can supply such a cursor, so the new advanced path produces a 500 instead of working. Negative offsets must be rejected or translated into a valid non-negative offset before slicing.

title: Negative offsets are only partially clamped in BasePaginator
body: The new shared BasePaginator logic clamps negative offsets only for forward cursors: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. A previous-page cursor with a negative offset still passes a negative bound to queryset[...] and raises. For a forward cursor with a negative offset, the query is silently shifted to row 0 while build_cursor() still receives the original negative cursor offset, so _build_next_values()/_build_prev_values() can generate inconsistent offsets and a has_prev flag for a page that does not exist. Negative offsets should be normalized or rejected up front instead of being handled differently by direction.

title: No tests cover the new optimized audit-log pagination path
body: No tests were added for OptimizedCursorPaginator or for the new optimized_pagination branch. A simple test with AuditLogEntry rows and order_by="-datetime" would have caught the datetime TypeError, and a test with a negative-offset cursor would have caught the unsupported Django negative slicing. Without coverage this new privileged code path can ship completely non-functional while the existing DateTimePaginator path continues to pass tests.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on the datetime key used by the audit log endpoint
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint instantiates this paginator with order_by='-datetime', so self.key is 'datetime'. Here get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, 'datetime'), which is a datetime object; both raise TypeError ('must be real number, not datetime'). build_cursor calls get_item_key on the first result even for the initial page, so every request with optimized_pagination=true made by a superuser or global-access member returns a 500. The class needs the strftime-based conversion used by DateTimePaginator.get_item_key (or the endpoint must not use this paginator for datetime ordering).

title: value_from_cursor returns a number for a datetime column, so subsequent pages filter incorrectly or fail
body: value_from_cursor returns cursor.value verbatim, an int/float. BasePaginator.build_queryset appends this value as the SQL parameter for the range predicate on the sort column, so against the audit log's timestamp column it will issue something like 'WHERE ...datetime <= <integer>'. PostgreSQL has no implicit cast from integer to timestamptz, so this produces a DB error or wrong comparisons on page 2 and beyond even after the get_item_key TypeError is fixed. DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor converts the cursor value back into a datetime; this paginator must do the same.

title: Advanced negative-offset branch passes negative indices to a Django QuerySet, which raises ValueError
body: The comment states the underlying Django ORM 'properly handles negative slicing automatically', but QuerySet.__getitem__ raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.') whenever the start index is negative. Cursor offsets are user-controlled via Cursor.from_string, so a crafted cursor with offset < 0 combined with optimized_pagination=true reaches this branch and produces a 500 rather than enabling reverse pagination. Negative offsets must be rejected (4xx) or clamped; passing them straight to a QuerySet cannot be a performance optimization.

title: Negative offset guard in BasePaginator only applies to non-prev cursors
body: start_offset is clamped with max(0, offset) only when cursor.is_prev is false; when is_prev is true the raw cursor offset is used unchanged. Because Cursor.from_string parses negative integers, a request with a cursor such as '0:-5:1' still reaches queryset[<negative>:stop], and Django raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.'), returning a 500. The new comment claims negative offsets are safe, but the previous-page path remains unguarded.

title: New comment claims negative offsets are allowed, but the change is comment-only
body: The diff only adds comments above `self.offset = int(offset)`. That line already accepted negative integers before this PR, and Cursor.from_string already parses them, so nothing about offset handling changed. The comment is misleading and implies guards/validation that do not exist, which is especially dangerous because negative offsets actually cause Django to raise ValueError in the paginator slicing paths.

title: No tests for the new OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new endpoint branch
body: The PR adds a ~100-line paginator class and a new request-controlled branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, but no tests. Basic tests exercising the optimized path against the real order_by='-datetime' queryset, or a cursor with a negative offset, would have caught both the datetime TypeError and the negative-slicing ValueError. Add tests for the optimized endpoint branch, cursor round-tripping, and negative/prev cursor handling.

title: Changing span buffer keys from sets to sorted sets breaks existing Redis data during rollout
body: Span buffers are stored at `span-buf:s:{project:trace}:span_id`. Before this change those keys are Redis sets; this diff starts writing them with `ZADD` and later calls `ZCARD`/`ZSCAN`/`ZUNIONSTORE` (`buffer.py` lines 197 and 434, plus `add-buffer.lua`). During a rolling deploy, any old set key touched by the new consumer, or any old consumer touching a new zset key, will get a `WRONGTYPE` error. Existing keys have a TTL up to `redis_ttl` (default 3600 seconds), so affected batches can fail and spans/segments can be lost or stuck until keys expire. There is no dual read/write path, versioned key prefix, or migration/flush step.

title: Optimized audit-log path selects a paginator that cannot handle datetime keys
body: The endpoint passes `order_by="-datetime"` together with `OptimizedCursorPaginator` when `optimized_pagination=true` for privileged users. `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the model value, and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric cursor value. `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `datetime`, so `build_cursor` raises `TypeError` on the first page, and cursor filtering would compare a datetime column against an integer. Any authorized request entering this new branch will 500 instead of returning audit logs.

title: Negative offsets are still passed to Django QuerySet slicing and raise ValueError
body: The new clamp only applies when `cursor.is_prev` is false: for previous-page cursors the original negative offset is passed through, and `OptimizedCursorPaginator`'s advanced branch (around line 882) explicitly passes `cursor.offset` directly to `queryset[start:stop]`. Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` rejects negative start/stop with `ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.')`. A crafted cursor such as `value:-1:1`, or the endpoint's new `enable_advanced_features=True` path, therefore produces a 500. The comments claiming Django handles negative slicing are incorrect; offsets need validation/clamping or a `BadPaginationError`.

title: Span buffer hard-codes 1000-span cap and ignores SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans
body: Eviction is now `if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin(...)` inside the Lua script, while the Python span-count check was removed from `_load_segment_data`. `SpansBuffer` still exposes `max_segment_spans` (default 1001) and passes nothing to the script, so any configured value is silently ignored and the actual limit is always 1000, which is also one lower than the default. Operators/tests cannot tune the cap, and the Python span-count safety check no longer matches the Lua behavior.

title: ZUNIONSTORE sums duplicate timestamp scores instead of preserving the latest
body: The script uses `zunionstore set_key, 2, set_key, span_key` (and the same for `parent_key`) without an `AGGREGATE` option. Redis's default is `SUM`, so if a span payload is present in both source sets its score becomes the sum of two `end_timestamp_precise` values rather than the max/latest timestamp.
