body: For an `eventTypeId` filter, `buildFilterConditions` pushes `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` and, when it is the only filter, returns that fragment without an outer grouping (and the test at line 385 asserts this unparenthesized form). `getBaseConditions` compensates by wrapping it in parentheses, but `getFilterConditions` is a public method returning a bare `Prisma.Sql`; any other consumer that embeds it next to another `AND`/`OR` in a WHERE clause (e.g. `WHERE ${getFilterConditions()} AND ...`) would hit operator-precedence and match too many rows. Consider always returning a fully parenthesized fragment so the method is safe to compose.

title: Caching behavior tests removed while caching logic remains
body: The PR deletes the entire "Caching" describe block (the `should cache authorization conditions` and `should cache filter conditions` tests), but the service still caches results via `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` in `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions`. The caching paths are now untested, so a regression in cache-keying or cache invalidation would go unnoticed.

title: Removal of public findMany() is a breaking change for existing callers
body: This change deletes the public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method (which previously merged the caller's `where`/`select`/pagination with auth+filter conditions and returned rows) and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a raw SQL fragment. Any existing consumer of `InsightsBookingService` that calls `service.findMany({ where, select, take, ... })` (e.g. the insights tRPC router or other server code) will now fail to compile or silently have no equivalent one-call API, because the caller must instead build its own `$queryRaw`/Prisma query and manually AND the returned fragment into a WHERE clause. The PR only touches the service and its test file, so it does not demonstrate that all call sites were migrated. A maintainer should verify there are no remaining `findMany` callers (and that the caller side now executes raw SQL correctly) before merging.

title: Only DB-executing test checks a positive match, no negative/authorization-exclusion assertion
body: The single test that actually runs SQL against `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` (the `getBaseConditions` case) only asserts that the expected user's booking is returned. For a change explicitly flagged as high-risk authorization logic, there is no test asserting that data belonging to other users/teams/orgs is *excluded* by the generated SQL (e.g. a booking owned by a different user in the same org, a team booking outside the requested team, or a non-owner/member's org data). Without a negative case, a subtle mistake in the AND/OR parenthesization or in the `isTeamBooking`/`teamId` predicates would pass tests while leaking data. Add at least one test that creates a booking the caller must NOT see and asserts the raw query returns nothing for it.

title: Public condition builders return unparenthesized OR fragments that are unsafe to compose with AND
body: `buildFilterConditions` (line 106) and the org/team authorization builders (lines 164-174, 196-207) return fragments such as `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` or `(teamCond) OR (userCond)` without wrapping the whole expression in parentheses when there is a single element (or when the OR is the resulting top-level expression). `getBaseConditions` currently wraps these as `(${auth}) AND (${filter})`, so it is safe today, but these methods are public (`getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions`). Any caller that composes a returned fragment with `AND`/`OR` without adding its own parentheses will get wrong precedence — e.g. `(A) OR (B) AND x` evaluates as `(A) OR ((B) AND x)`. The tests now assert the unparenthesized strings, locking in the fragile contract. Return fully parenthesized, self-contained predicates so fragments are safe to concatenate.

title: Org-scope test asserts an array whose order is not guaranteed by the query
body: The org-scope assertion compares the generated SQL values array against `[testData.user.id, user2.id, user3.id]`. These ids come from `Array.from(new Set(userIdsFromOrg))`, where `userIdsFromOrg` is obtained from `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds` with no `ORDER BY`. Postgres may return membership rows in any order, so the `.values` array (and the teams array) can differ between runs, making this assertion flaky. Sort the ids before asserting, or assert set membership rather than exact array order.

title: Caching tests removed while caching logic remains
body: This PR deletes the entire `describe("Caching")` block that verified `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` reuse `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions`. The caching fields and the `=== undefined` guards in the service are unchanged, so the removed tests leave that behavior uncovered. Since the caching was previously exercised, restore equivalent tests (second call returns the same cached `Prisma.Sql`) rather than dropping the coverage.

title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only fires the optional `onSuccess`/`onChanged` callback on success; it never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (unlike `disconnectMutation`, which explicitly invalidates it in `onSettled`). The `cacheUpdatedAt` shown in this component comes from that internal `connectedCalendars` query in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`. Unless the consumer's `onChanged` happens to refetch that exact query (it is not guaranteed to), the dropdown keeps showing the stale "Cache Status / Last updated" entry and the "Delete cached data" action after the cache has already been deleted, so the UI misreports that cached data still exists until a manual page refresh.

title: Overwriting SelectedCalendar.updatedAt on cache repopulation conflates cache refresh with calendar change
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` ends with `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`, whose comment says it updates `updatedAt` for all calendars of the credential. `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is also written by the Google webhook handler to record when a calendar's contents actually changed. Bumping it whenever the cache is (re)populated therefore overwrites that "last calendar change" signal with "last cache write", which can corrupt any consumer relying on `updatedAt` to detect real changes. Additionally, passing an empty `data: {}` to Prisma `updateMany` to trigger the `@updatedAt` side effect is fragile — if Prisma performs no update for empty data the intended timestamp bump silently never happens. This write is redundant given the UI reads `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache` instead.

title: Cache status query ignores expiresAt, reporting timestamps for expired caches
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows for the given credentials and returns `max(updatedAt)` without filtering on `expiresAt >= now()`. When every cached entry for a credential has expired (i.e. no cache is actually servable), the handler still returns an `updatedAt`, and the UI renders a "Cache Status — Last updated" entry plus the "Delete cached data" action for a cache that contains no usable data. This misleads the user into thinking availability is currently being served from cache. The `where` clause should exclude expired rows (or the UI should distinguish expired vs. live cache).

title: Cache timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
body: The "Last updated" timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` regardless of the user's locale, so non-English users see US date/time formatting even though the surrounding strings are localized via `t()`. This should derive the locale from `useLocale()` (or the user's time zone/locale) so the date matches the rest of the localized UI.

title: sed -i '' syntax fails on GNU/Linux
body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E "s|...|...|"` to rewrite `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` in the env file. The empty-string argument to `-i` is BSD/macOS sed syntax; on GNU sed (the common Linux dev/CI environment) it is interpreted as the script name and errors out, so the env file is never updated and the webhook URL is not applied. The script also shells out to `tmole` without checking that it is installed, and derives `ENV_FILE="../.env"` relative to the current working directory rather than the script location.

title: Delete-cache action shown for delegation/team credentials that the handler rejects
body: deleteCacheHandler authorizes solely by `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`. Delegation credentials (and team credentials with a null userId) are owned by a different user/admin, so this lookup returns null and the mutation throws "Credential not found or access denied". However, CredentialActionsDropdown only hides the remove-app action for delegation (`canDisconnect = !delegationCredentialId && ...`); it still renders the "Delete cached data" action whenever `hasCache` is truthy, and delegated Google calendars do have a cache row keyed by that credential's DB id, so `cacheUpdatedAt` is set. Result: delegated/team users see "Delete cached data" but every attempt fails with the error toast. Either authorize using the same rule that builds connectedCalendars, or hide the delete action when the credential isn't owned by the session user.

title: Deleting cache does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status
body: deleteCacheMutation.onSuccess only calls `onSuccess?.()` (= props.onChanged). Unlike disconnectMutation, which explicitly invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in onSettled, the cache mutation never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. When the parent does not pass a refetching `onChanged` (it is optional in SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper), the tRPC cache retains the old `cacheUpdatedAt`, so after a successful delete the dropdown still shows "Cache Status" and "Delete cached data" until a manual page reload. Invalidate the connectedCalendars query in onSuccess/onSettled as the disconnect path does.

title: No test for deleteCache authorization ceiling
body: deleteCache permanently deletes calendar cache rows and its only safety property is the ownership check. There is no test asserting that a user cannot delete the cache of a credential they do not own (mutation should reject) and can delete their own. Given this is a destructive, authorization-gated mutation, a unit/integration test covering the not-owner rejection and the owner success path should be added before merge.

title: Migration backfills all existing caches with the migration timestamp
body: Adding `updatedAt TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` sets every pre-existing CalendarCache row to the migration run time. getCacheStatusByCredentialIds surfaces this value as "Last updated", so for the existing rows the UI will report the deploy time as the last update for up to the cache TTL (CACHING_TIME = 30 days), which is misleading. Since the real update time can be approximated as `expiresAt - CACHING_TIME`, consider backfilling with that (or leaving the column nullable for legacy rows) instead of NOW().

title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only and breaks on GNU/Linux
body: `sed -i '' -E "s|...|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the macOS form of `sed -i`. On GNU sed (typical Linux dev boxes / CI) `-i` treats `''` as the (empty) suffix and then interprets the following expression/arguments incorrectly, so the inline replacement fails and GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is left unchanged (or the command errors). Use a portable approach (e.g. write to a temp file and move it, or detect the OS) so the script works cross-platform.

title: Unnecessary SelectedCalendar.updatedAt update with no reader
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now ends with `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`. This issues an extra UPDATE across all SelectedCalendars for the credential on every cache population (i.e. every sync/webhook), only to bump `@updatedAt`, yet nothing reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for display — the UI uses CalendarCache.updatedAt via cacheUpdatedAt. The PR notes this too. It is dead work on a latency-sensitive path; remove it (or add the consumer that justifies it).

title: Deleting cache does not invalidate connectedCalendars, so cache status stays on screen
body: The `deleteCacheMutation` onSuccess only shows a toast and calls `onSuccess?.()` (which is the parent's optional `onChanged`). It never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike the sibling `disconnectMutation` which calls `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled`. After a successful cache deletion, if `onChanged` does not itself refetch the query (in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` it is just `props.onChanged`), the dropdown/first render keeps showing the old `cacheUpdatedAt` and the 'Delete cached data' action, even though the cache is gone. Add invalidation of `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in the deleteCache mutation's onSettled.

title: Delegation-credential users can see Delete cache but the handler rejects them
body: The handler authorizes by `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`. For a delegation credential the underlying `Credential` row is owned by the admin/organization, not the delegate user, so a delegate user who has cache data will get 'Credential not found or access denied'. Meanwhile `CredentialActionsDropdown` renders the 'Delete cached data' item purely on `hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` (it does not exclude `delegationCredentialId` the way `canDisconnect` does), so the button is shown to delegate users and fails with an error toast. Either exclude delegation credentials from the delete-cache UI, or authorize deletion using the delegation path / userId-based cache ownership.

title: updateManyByCredentialId with empty data is a redundant write that may not bump updatedAt
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` intending to refresh `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. Passing an empty `data` object is a no-op for the columns; Prisma's `@updatedAt` is not reliably applied when there are no fields to change, so the intended timestamp refresh likely does not happen. Furthermore, nothing reads `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` for this feature (the PR states the frontend uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`), so this is an unnecessary extra DB write on the hot cache-population/webhook path for every credential. Remove it (or pass explicit data and surface it in the UI if it is actually needed).

title: Cache status ignores expiry, so expired cache is reported as present
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` aggregates `_max(updatedAt)` over all `CalendarCache` rows for the credential without filtering on `expiresAt`. Cache entries past `expiresAt` are never served by `getCachedAvailability`, but the UI will still show 'Cache Status' / 'Last updated' and offer to delete it, implying a usable cache exists. Consider adding `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the `where` if 'has cache' should mean 'has servable cache'.

title: Widening the exported UserWithCalendars input type to require updatedAt/googleChannelId risks compile breaks
body: The exported `UserWithCalendars` type now requires `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on both `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars`, yet nothing in `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` consumes these fields for this feature. Only the `findUnlockedUserForSession` producer in `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts` was updated. Any other caller that builds this input without selecting those columns (e.g. the `@calcom/platform-libraries` re-export of this function, or other query sites feeding `allSelectedCalendars`) will now fail type-check. If these fields are not actually used, drop the type change; otherwise update every producer/select.

title: sed -i '' is macOS-only; script silently misbehaves on Linux
body: The in-place edit uses BSD sed syntax `sed -i '' -E ...`. On GNU sed (Linux CI/devcontainers) `-i ''` is parsed differently, so the GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL line is not replaced as intended. Given this is a committed dev/test helper, use a portable approach (e.g. write to a temp file and move) or detect the platform.

title: Cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded en-US locale
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })` ignores the user's locale. Cal.com users in other locales will see US-style dates in the 'Last updated' string even though the rest of the UI is localized via `useLocale`. Format using the active locale (or pass no locales to `Intl.DateTimeFormat` so the runtime default is used).

title: Reschedule path still relies on immediate SendGrid cancel, bypassing the new cancellation mechanism
body: When rescheduling, the old booking's workflow reminders are cancelled with `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`, i.e. `immediateDelete = true`. That path performs the SendGrid `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends {status:"cancel"}` synchronously and returns without setting `cancelled = true` on the row. This is exactly the mechanism the PR says is broken: SendGrid keeps up to 100 pending cancellations, so once that limit is hit new cancel requests fail. Because the reminder is never marked `cancelled`, the CRON job (`scheduleEmailReminders`) will not pick it up and retry it, so the reminder email is still sent for rescheduled bookings — the very bug the PR claims to fix for reschedules. The reschedule flow should mark the reminder `cancelled` (non-immediate path) and let the CRON job cancel it, so that failures are retried.

title: immediateDelete neither deletes the DB row nor marks it cancelled, leaving a stale scheduled reminder on failure
body: In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, when `immediateDelete` is true and `referenceId` exists, the function cancels the SendGrid batch and then `return`s without deleting the `workflowReminder` row and without setting `cancelled = true`. Callers that do not cascade-delete the row (notably the reschedule flow in `handleNewBooking`, where the old booking stays in the DB) are left with a row that still has `scheduled = true` and a live `referenceId`. If the SendGrid cancel call fails (e.g. the 100-pending-cancellations limit), the row is not marked as cancelled, so the CRON job cannot retry it, and the email is still delivered. The row is also left dangling until the CRON cleanup deletes it by date. The immediate path should at minimum record the cancellation (or delete the row) so a failed SendGrid call is recoverable.

title: One failed cancellation aborts all remaining cancellations and all DB deletes
body: The loop that cancels reminders is wrapped in a single try/catch (lines 53-77). Inside it, each `client.request` is awaited sequentially and the Prisma delete operations are only pushed to `workflowRemindersToDelete` and executed later via a single `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` after the loop. If any `client.request` throws (e.g. a rate-limited/failed SendGrid cancel), the loop exits, the `Promise.all` at line 74 is never reached, and therefore none of the deletions for already-cancelled reminders run, and the remaining reminders in `remindersToCancel` are never cancelled. The catch only logs. The next CRON run re-attempts them, but one bad reminder can repeatedly block the whole batch and prevent emails from being cancelled in time. Each reminder should be handled in its own try/catch so a single failure doesn't abort the rest.

title: remindersToCancel query lacks method/scheduled filters
body: The `findMany` for `remindersToCancel` filters only on `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now + 1h`, without `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` (or `scheduled: true`). The cancellation branch then unconditionally calls the SendGrid scheduled_sends cancel endpoint with `batch_id: reminder.referenceId`. Today only EMAIL reminders ever get `cancelled = true`, but nothing enforces this, and `referenceId` for an SMS reminder is a Twilio SID rather than a SendGrid batch id. Any future code path that marks a non-email reminder cancelled would send a bogus batch id to SendGrid. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` to the query to make the intent explicit and safe.

title: Unused `Prisma` import after removing Prisma.BatchPayload usage
body: The diff moved `Prisma` into the runtime import from `@prisma/client`, but the only previous use (`PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>`) was removed and no `Prisma.` reference remains in the file. An unused import will be flagged by `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` and may fail the lint/CI step. Remove `Prisma` from the import (do the same check for the reformatted import block, which also dropped the trailing comma after `Prisma`).

title: Reminder cancellation promises are not awaited
body: In the reminder-cancellation loop, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but are invoked inside `updatedBookings.forEach(...).forEach(...)` without `await`ing them, and the resulting promises are never collected or awaited. For EMAIL reminders the only thing that prevents delivery is the `cancelled: true` DB write performed inside `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`; if that floating promise has not completed when the handler returns (likely on serverless, where the lambda can be frozen right after the response is sent), the reminder stays scheduled and the email is still delivered — the exact bug this PR is meant to fix. Collect and `await Promise.all(...)` all cancellation promises before returning.

title: Reschedule reminder cleanup: try/catch is dead code and calls are unawaited
body: The new reschedule cleanup wraps the loop in `try { originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true); deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...) }) } catch (error) { log.error(...) }`. The callback is async and its promises are not awaited, so (a) any rejection from the cancellation calls becomes an unhandled rejection and is never caught by this `catch`, making the error handling dead code, and (b) the SendGrid cancellation / DB update may not complete before the handler finishes, so reminders for the old (now rescheduled) booking can still be sent. Additionally, passing `immediateDelete=true` for email performs an immediate SendGrid `status: cancel` POST, which is exactly the pending-cancellation behaviour (max 100 entries in `scheduled_sends`) this PR is trying to avoid, so reschedule-heavy accounts can still exhaust that limit and fail to cancel. Await the calls and consider using the mark-cancelled path for reschedules too.

title: requestReschedule reminder cancellation not awaited
body: In `requestReschedule`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` are called inside `bookingToReschedule.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` without awaiting. For EMAIL these functions only mark the row `cancelled: true`, so if the floating promise does not run before the request completes (serverless freeze), the reminder for the now-cancelled/rescheduled booking stays live and the reminder email is still sent — the bug being fixed. Await or `Promise.all` these calls.

title: Past-reminder cleanup deletes cancelled reminders before they can be cancelled
body: The handler first runs `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { method: EMAIL, scheduledDate: { lte: now } } })` and only afterwards looks up `cancelled: true` reminders with `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. Because the cleanup runs first, any cancelled reminder whose `scheduledDate` has just passed is deleted from the DB without ever being cancelled in SendGrid, so the reminder email is delivered. Since this cron runs every 15 minutes, a cancellation made within ~15 minutes of a reminder's send time (after the last cron run while the reminder was still in the future) falls into this gap and the email goes out. The cancellation pass should run before/independent of the past-reminder cleanup, and the window/cadence must guarantee every reminder is cancelled before its send time.

title: immediateDelete path leaves orphan WorkflowReminder rows
body: When `immediateDelete` is true the function cancels the send in SendGrid and returns, but it never deletes the `workflowReminder` row nor marks it `cancelled`. Callers in `handleNewBooking` (reschedule) no longer perform a separate `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany`, so for a rescheduled booking the old reminders remain in the table as `scheduled: true` rows referencing the cancelled booking until the cron's past-reminder cleanup eventually deletes them. Delete the row here (or set `cancelled`) so the DB state matches the actual SendGrid state.

title: Past-due cancelled reminders are deleted before they are cancelled
body: The cron first deletes every EMAIL reminder whose scheduledDate is <= now, and only later looks for cancelled:true reminders within the next hour. A reminder cancelled shortly before it is due can therefore be deleted by this deleteMany without ever receiving a SendGrid cancel call. The same cleanup drops cancellations whose SendGrid request failed on a previous run. With a 15-minute cron interval, cancelling a reminder minutes before send can still result in the email being sent. Process cancellations before deleting past-due rows, and for reminders due before the next cron run cancel immediately or otherwise guarantee a run before send.

title: Reschedule still uses direct SendGrid cancellation and bypasses the new cancelled flag
body: When rescheduling, old email reminders are cancelled with immediateDelete=true. That performs a direct SendGrid scheduled_sends cancel instead of setting cancelled for the cron path. This is the same flow that can hit SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation limit; when the request fails the helper only logs, no cancelled state is persisted, and the old reminder can still be sent after the booking was rescheduled. Normal reschedules should use the deferred cancelled flag, with immediate cancellation only when the send is imminent.

title: Workflow reminder cancellations are not awaited on booking cancellation
body: The updatedBookings.forEach invokes deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder without await or Promise.all. The handler can return, or continue to send cancellation emails, before these async DB/SendGrid/Twilio operations complete. In a serverless runtime pending work may be dropped, leaving email reminders with cancelled unset so the cron never cancels them and the reminder email is still sent. Collect and await these cancellation promises.

title: requestReschedule no longer awaits workflow reminder cancellation
body: The previous code awaited the Prisma reminder deletions. The new forEach fires deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting them, and the Promise.all was removed. The requestReschedule mutation can finish before the reminders are marked cancelled; if those updates are lost, the old reminder remains uncancelled and will still be sent after the booking is cancelled/rescheduled. Await the cancellation promise set.

title: immediateDelete branch leaves the WorkflowReminder row uncancelled and without retry state
body: When immediateDelete is true, the helper cancels the SendGrid batch and then returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder or setting cancelled. Reschedule callers do not cascade-delete this row, so it remains as a scheduled reminder. If the SendGrid request fails, the catch only logs and no persisted state allows the cron to retry, so the reminder can still be sent. Either delete the row after a successful cancel or persist cancelled so it can be retried and cleaned up.

title: Disabled event-type reminder cancellations are now fire-and-forget
body: The previous code collected Prisma delete promises and awaited Promise.all. The new remindersToDelete.flat().forEach calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting them. The mutation proceeds to update event-type associations and return before the cancellations finish; if the process is torn down, reminders for disabled event types are never cancelled and emails continue to be sent. Collect the returned promises and await them.

title: Async forEach means reschedule cancellations are not awaited
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) }) discards the async callback promises. Since getCalendar is now awaited inside the callback, Reschedule can send the reschedule email and return true before calendar/video cancellation has even started. The surrounding try/catch also cannot catch rejections from those discarded promises, so failures become unhandled rejections. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop.

title: Async forEach means reschedule cancellations are not awaited
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) }) does not wait for its callbacks. Because getCalendar is now asynchronous, Reschedule continues to send the reschedule email and returns true while calendar/video deletion may still be pending, or may never start in a short-lived serverless invocation. Rejections from getCalendar/deleteEvent become unhandled because the try/catch only surrounds the synchronous forEach call. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop.

title: Reschedule mutation returns before calendar/video deletion completes
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) }) discards every callback promise. After this PR getCalendar is awaited inside the callback, so the mutation can finish and sendRequestRescheduleEmail can send before any calendar or video deletion is initiated. Any rejection from getCalendar or deleteEvent is also unhandled. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop.

title: Recurring booking calendar deletes are pushed after Promise.all may have run
body: In the recurring-cancellation branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` is not awaited. The callbacks only push into apiDeletes after they resume from the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent calls, so the later `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` can run with an empty or partial array. Calendar deletions for recurring bookings can therefore be skipped/unawaited and failures become unhandled rejections. Use a `for...of` loop with await or `await Promise.all(...map(...))`.

title: appStore export now returns promises while most consumers still expect modules
body: The default export was changed from a map of module namespaces to a map of `import()` promises. Every existing `appStore[name]` access now yields a Promise unless the caller awaits it. This PR updates only a small set of call sites, so other consumers will read `.lib`, `.metadata`, or `.credentials` from a Promise and get undefined, breaking calendar, video, and payment integrations at runtime (and likely failing typecheck where the old module type is expected). Either keep a synchronous metadata map or update every consumer and the exported type to the async contract.

title: getCalendarCredentials now silently returns calendar promises
body: Because `getCalendar` became async, `getCalendarCredentials` now stores a `Promise<Calendar | null>` in the `calendar` field while remaining a synchronous function. Only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to await that field. Any other caller of this exported function that treats `calendar` as a Calendar will call methods on a Promise. Make the function async and await `getCalendar`, or explicitly change the return type to expose promises and migrate all callers.

title: Async forEach in reschedule is not awaited and try/catch cannot catch its failures
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` starts async callbacks but does not await the returned promises. `Reschedule` can return before `getCalendar` and `deleteEvent` finish, and the surrounding try/catch is ineffective for rejections from those awaits, producing unhandled rejections and potentially leaving calendar events undeleted. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a `for...of` loop.

title: Async forEach in reschedule is not awaited and try/catch cannot catch its failures
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` starts async callbacks but does not await the returned promises. `Reschedule` can return before `getCalendar` and `deleteEvent` finish, and the surrounding try/catch is ineffective for rejections from those awaits, producing unhandled rejections and potentially leaving calendar events undeleted. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a `for...of` loop.

title: requestReschedule fires calendar deletion asynchronously without awaiting it
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` now awaits `getCalendar` inside an async callback that the mutation never awaits. The mutation can return before calendar/video cleanup starts or completes, and failures become unhandled rejections rather than being handled by the mutation. Collect the promises with `map` and `await Promise.all` so reschedule cleanup is reliable.

title: Recurring cancellation may skip calendar deletes because async forEach is not awaited
body: In the recurring-bookings branch, credentials are processed with `forEach(async ...)`. The callback awaits `getCalendar` and only then pushes deletion promises into `apiDeletes`, but the outer handler does not await the callbacks. It may reach `await Promise.all(...apiDeletes)` before those deletions are pushed, leaving recurring calendar events undeleted, and callback rejections become unhandled. Convert this to an awaited `for...of` loop or `Promise.all` over the credentials.

title: Dynamic imports are initiated eagerly, so app loading is not actually lazy
body: Each `import("./...")` call in the object literal is evaluated as soon as `packages/app-store/index.ts` is imported. That starts loading/evaluating every app chunk immediately, so this change does not defer app loading and can still pay the full startup cost. If the goal is lazy loading, store thunks such as `() => import("./app")` and call/await only the selected app.

title: Async forEach means reschedule cleanup is not awaited
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` is not awaited and `forEach` ignores the returned promises. The callback now awaits `getCalendar` before calling `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting`, so the mutation continues to send the reschedule email and webhooks and returns while calendar/video cancellation has only started. In a serverless environment that work can be lost entirely, and failures become unhandled rejections. Use `for...of` with `await` or `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`.

title: Recurring cancellation API deletes are pushed after Promise.all
body: In the recurring-booking branch, calendar cancellations are performed inside `forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` without awaiting the callback. After adding `await getCalendar(credential)`, the callback yields before pushing into `apiDeletes`; the later `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` therefore sees an empty `apiDeletes` and returns without waiting for those calendar deletions. Recurring calendar events may never be cancelled before the handler finishes. Collect promises with `await Promise.all(...)` or use a `for...of` loop.

title: Reschedule calendar/video deletion races because async forEach is unawaited
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` is not awaited. The newly added `await getCalendar(...)` yields before `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` is even called, so `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` and the function return happen while the original calendar/video event may still be present. Any rejection from `getCalendar` or the delete calls is also an unhandled rejection instead of being caught by the surrounding `try/catch`. Use `for...of` or `await Promise.all(...)`.

title: Reschedule cleanup starts after the response because async forEach is unawaited
body: The callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` is now `async` and contains `await getCalendar(...)`, but `forEach` does not wait for it. Calendar/video cancellation can therefore start after `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` has run and after the function has returned; failures are unhandled. This is the same unsafe pattern as in the Vital reschedule flow and should be converted to `for...of`/`Promise.all`.

title: Dynamic imports are eagerly started for every app
body: Each `import("./...")` in the object literal is evaluated as soon as this module is loaded, so all app modules start loading immediately. This does not provide lazy loading and may keep the same startup cost as the previous static imports. If the intent is to load app modules only when used, store loader functions such as `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")` and call the loader at the use site.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns promises in its calendar field
body: `getCalendarCredentials` remains synchronous, but `getCalendar` is now async. As a result the exported helper returns objects whose `calendar` property is `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`. `getConnectedCalendars` in this file awaits it, but any other exported consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` that treats `calendar` as a Calendar will break at runtime or type-check time. Either make `getCalendarCredentials` async and resolve all calendars, or update the type/contract and every caller.

title: Date override path skips busy-time check and allows double booking
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, once a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot is inside it, the function returns `true` immediately at line 134. That bypasses the `busy.every(...)` check at the end of the function, so existing Cal bookings and calendar busy times are ignored whenever the user has a date override. A fixed host with a 9-12 override and an existing 10-11 booking will make the 10-11 slot appear available, allowing a round-robin booking to double-book them. The date override should only bypass the normal working-hours check; busy times still need to be evaluated.

title: Slot end is computed from start time in working-hours check
body: The working-hours check computes `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`, which is identical to `start`; it never computes the slot's end. It therefore only verifies that the slot starts before the end of a working-hour range, not that the whole slot fits. For example, a fixed host working 9-10 with a 60-minute event will accept a 9:30 slot even though it ends at 10:30. Use `slotEndTime` or `start + eventLength` for `end`.

title: Working-hours `find` logic rejects split shifts and allows days with no availability
body: The callback passed to `workingHours.find` returns `true` when the slot is outside a given working-hour range, and any truthy result causes the function to reject the slot. With split availability such as 9-12 and 13-17, a valid 9:30 slot is rejected because it is outside the 13-17 entry. Conversely, if `workingHours` has no entry for the slot's weekday, `find` returns `undefined` and the code falls through to the busy check, treating the slot as available. In round-robin filtering this can drop valid slots for split shifts while still allowing a host with no availability that day to be selected. The check should find a matching-day range that contains the slot and reject only when no such range exists.

title: Zero-length date overrides are never detected because Dayjs objects are compared with `===`
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct Dayjs object instances, so it is always false. The intended branch for an override whose start and end are the same is therefore dead code. For an all-day-unavailable override represented by start===end, slots overlapping that point can fall through to `return true` at line 134 instead of being blocked. Use `.isSame(...)` for the comparison.

title: Timezone offset conversion discards the day shift, placing overrides on the wrong invitee day for large offset gaps
body: The new conversion computes override start/end as minute-of-day after adding the invitee/organizer offset. If that offset moves the override across midnight, the date part is lost. For example, an organizer in UTC+14 with an override at 23:00 on Jan 2 and an invitee in UTC-12 should see it at 21:00 on Jan 1, but the naive `override.start` still matches the Jan 2 invitee day in `activeOverrides`, while the computed time is 21:00 on Jan 2. The override is then applied 24 hours off. The converted override boundaries need to drive the day selection as well, not just the minute-of-day.

title: No test covers the stated round-robin fixed-host date override fix
body: The PR's primary stated fix is that date overrides for fixed hosts are honored in round-robin events, but the added test only varies the invitee timezone for a personal event. There is no scenario with `schedulingType: "ROUND_ROBIN"`, a fixed host with a date override, and a round-robin host, and no case where the fixed host also has an existing busy booking on the override day. As a result, the new `checkIfIsAvailable` logic that skips busy times and mishandles working hours is not exercised.

title: Date override path returns true before busy-time checks
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a slot falls inside a date override the function sets dateOverrideExist and then returns true at line 133 before the busy.every(...) check at line 153. The busy array contains the host's Cal bookings and calendar busy times. As a result, any fixed host with a date override appears free for the whole override even when already booked, so personal and round-robin events can create double bookings on override days. The override should bypass normal working-hour checks only; busy times still need to be evaluated.

title: Working-hours check mishandles days off and split shifts
body: The new working-hours guard uses workingHours.find and returns false only when the first entry whose days includes slotStartTime.day() does not contain the slot. This has two failure modes: (1) if the user has no working-hours entry for that weekday, find returns undefined and the slot falls through as available, so fixed hosts can be booked on their days off; (2) if the user has multiple ranges on the same weekday, such as 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00, an afternoon slot is compared only against the first range and rejected even though it is within the second range. In addition, line 142 sets end equal to start instead of using slotEndTime, so a slot that starts before closing but ends after closing is not rejected. The check needs to reject missing weekday entries and test the slot against all matching ranges, including the slot end.

title: Date override interval only rejects slots wholly before or after it
body: The containment test rejects a slot only when slotEndTime is before/equal overrideStart or slotStartTime is after overrideEnd. It therefore accepts slots that partially overlap an override: a 13:30-14:30 slot with a 14:00-18:00 override starts before the override but ends inside and is treated as within the override; a slot starting exactly at 18:00 is also accepted because the end check uses strict isAfter. Combined with the early return on dateOverrideExist, these slots bypass normal working hours and busy checks. The condition should require slotStartTime >= overrideStart and slotEndTime <= overrideEnd. Separately, the zero-length override check at line 114 compares two Dayjs objects with ===, so a start-equals-end override is never recognized as the unavailable case.

title: Active date overrides are still selected by the override wall-clock UTC date
body: activeOverrides is selected by comparing dayjs.utc(override.start) directly against the invitee's local day boundaries. Date override start values are stored as wall-clock times (for example, 14:00 Asia/Kolkata is stored as 14:00Z), so this comparison works only when the organizer and invitee dates happen to align. For a large positive invitee offset such as UTC+14, an override stored at 14:00Z on the invitee day falls after the invitee day's UTC end boundary (10:00Z the same day), so the override is filtered out and the new timezone conversion is never applied. The filter should compare the converted instant or otherwise test overlap against the invitee day.

title: No test covers the fixed-host round-robin date override fix
body: The PR description says fixed-host date overrides in round-robin events are fixed and should prevent bookings when the fixed host is unavailable, but the added test only changes the invitee timezone for a personal event. It has no ROUND_ROBIN event, no fixed host with a date override, and no busy booking on the override day. As a result, the regressions in checkIfIsAvailable (busy times being skipped and the working-hours filtering) are not caught. Add a scenario with a round-robin event, a fixed host whose date override restricts availability, a loose host, and an existing booking during the override.

title: Date override returns available before checking busy times
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, once a date override on the slot's date is detected and the slot is considered inside it, the function executes `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` before the `busy.every(...)` check. Any accepted booking or calendar busy time during a date override is therefore ignored for fixed hosts and loose hosts, so a host with a date override can be offered/booked while already busy. The override should only change the working-hours rule; it must still fall through to busy-time validation.

title: Date override window accepts partial overlaps and the end boundary
body: The date-override check only rejects slots that end at/before the override start or start after the override end. It never requires the slot to fit inside the override. A 60-minute event with an override 10:00-11:00 therefore accepts 09:30-10:30 (starts before override) and 11:00-12:00 (starts exactly at override end, because `isAfter` is strict). Those slots are marked available for a fixed host even though they are outside the host's override availability. The condition should require `slotStartTime >= overrideStart` and `slotEndTime <= overrideEnd`.

title: Working-hours end is computed from the slot start
body: The new working-hours check sets `end` to the same value as `start` (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`), so `end > workingHour.endTime` can never detect a slot that runs past the host's working-hours end. A fixed host whose working hours end earlier than the aggregate event availability can be offered a slot that starts before their end but finishes after it. `end` should be computed from `slotEndTime`.

title: Multiple date overrides on the same date are treated as one range
body: `dateOverrides.find(...)` returns true and `checkIfIsAvailable` immediately returns false as soon as the slot is outside any override whose date matches. If a user has two overrides on the same date, e.g. 10:00-11:00 and 14:00-15:00, a slot at 14:30 is checked against the first override, found to be after its end, and rejected even though the second override covers it. The code needs to evaluate all overrides for the date and only reject the slot if it is outside every one of them.

title: Active override filter still compares placeholder wall time to invitee day
body: `activeOverrides` filters using `dayjs.utc(override.start)` against the invitee's day, but `override.start` is a wall-clock placeholder stored with UTC fields, not the real UTC instant. For offsets that move the real override onto a different invitee day, the override is dropped or assigned to the wrong day before the new offset calculation runs. Example: organizer Asia/Kolkata override at 14:00 on Jan 2 and invitee timezone +14; the real slot is Jan 2 22:30 invitee time, but raw Jan 2 14:00Z is outside the Jan 2 invitee day, so no override availability is generated for Jan 2. The filter should use the override's actual UTC instant or compare days in the organizer timezone.

title: New test does not cover fixed-host date override filtering
body: The added test only changes the invitee timezone for a personal event. It does not exercise the new fixed-host/round-robin filtering or a date override that conflicts with an existing booking or calendar busy time, so the early-return, partial-overlap, end-boundary, and multiple-override bugs in `checkIfIsAvailable` would not be caught.

title: Embedding response emits only host ids, but the client expects a side-loaded embeddable_hosts collection
body: The serializer declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids`, and `Admin::EmbeddingController#show` renders it without `include: [:embeddable_hosts]`. The response therefore contains `embeddable_host_ids` but no root `embeddable_hosts` array. The new client hydration code in store.js looks up each id in `root['embeddable_hosts']`; because that collection is absent, it replaces the ids with an array of `undefined` values. The admin embedding template iterates that array and passes `undefined` into the `embeddable-host` component, so existing allowed hosts do not render and the page can throw when the component reads `host.isNew`. Either include the association in the render call or change the serializer to side-load the host objects.

title: Migration dereferences a result row that may not exist when the old settings were never persisted
body: `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the `embed_category` join returns at least one row. Site setting defaults are not necessarily stored as rows, and even when `embed_category` exists its value may not match any category name; in either case `execute(...)[0]` is nil and the migration raises before it can finish. The fallback lookup for `uncategorized_category_id` has the same problem. This will abort upgrades on installs that never explicitly changed `embed_category`. Use a nil-safe query result and a valid default/fallback.

title: Old embeddable_hosts values are copied without normalization or escaping
body: The migration interpolates rows from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting directly into an INSERT. The old setting explicitly supported values with `http://`, `https://`, and paths (as shown by the removed specs). Those values are stored verbatim in the new `host` column, but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` only compares `URI(host).host`, so a migrated row like `http://example.com` will never match and existing embeds break. Single quotes in old values also break the generated SQL. Normalize the values through the model/strip scheme and path, downcase the host, and quote/escape them for the INSERT.

title: Allowed-host lookup is case-sensitive for the incoming URL
body: The query is `where('lower(host) = ?', host)`, but the bound `host` comes directly from `URI(host).host` without being downcased. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so a referer or embed URL with an uppercase host (for example `HTTP://EVILTROUT.COM/...`) will not match a stored lowercase host even though it should be allowed. Downcase the input or compare `lower(host) = lower(?)`.

title: Missing host crashes before_validation instead of producing a validation error
body: `self.host.sub!` raises `NoMethodError` when `host` is nil, which can happen when an API client omits the parameter or creates an `EmbeddableHost` without a host. Because this runs in `before_validation`, the record never reaches the format validator and the controller returns a 500 instead of a 422 with validation errors. Guard against nil (or use `to_s`) before stripping.

title: Hosts are not unique, so the category for a host can be ambiguous
body: The model only validates host format, and the new table has no unique index or uniqueness validation on `host`. An admin can create two rows for the same host with different categories, and `record_for_host` will return whichever row the database returns first. Imported topics then land in an arbitrary category. Add a uniqueness constraint on the normalized host (for example a unique index on `lower(host)`) and validate it in the model.

title: Missing record in update/destroy causes an unhandled 500
body: Both `update` and `destroy` fetch with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately call methods on the result. If the id is invalid or the host was deleted, `host` is nil; `save_host(nil)` or `nil.destroy` raises and returns a 500. Use `find_by` and render a proper not-found response when the record is absent.

title: New admin CRUD controller is only tested for class inheritance
body: The only test asserts that `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` subclasses `Admin::AdminController`. There are no request specs covering create/update/destroy, invalid/missing host values, category fallback, or non-admin access. This leaves the new admin API unprotected against regressions such as nil-host 500s, missing-record 500s, and incorrect category assignment. Add controller specs that exercise the actions and authorization.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category or uncategorized_category_id setting row is absent
body: The migration does `execute(...)[0]['id']` and later `execute(...)[0]['value']` without checking whether the query returned any rows. On installs where these settings were never persisted, or where the old `embed_category` value does not match an existing category name, `execute(...)[0]` is nil and the migration aborts with `NoMethodError` before the host data is imported. The queries should use safe `first`/guard logic and fall back to the uncategorized category/default when absent.

title: Migrated host strings are inserted raw and SQL-interpolated, breaking existing embeds
body: The old `embeddable_hosts` setting accepted values such as `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234` (the old specs use exactly these), but this migration inserts each `h` verbatim into `embeddable_hosts.host`. The new lookup extracts only `uri.host` and compares it to the stored value, so migrated rows containing a scheme or path will never match and embedding will stop working after upgrade. The same line also interpolates the DB value directly into SQL, so a host containing an apostrophe will break the migration and untrusted DB content can inject SQL. Normalize host values with the same rules as the model and use bound parameters.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host instead of returning a validation error
body: `self.host.sub!` is called before validation runs, so a new `EmbeddableHost` with a nil host (for example an admin POST missing `embeddable_host[host]`) raises `NoMethodError` and returns a 500 from the controller instead of an invalid-record response. The model should guard against nil/blank host before calling `sub!`.

title: record_for_host compares lower(host) against a case-preserved, port-less URI host
body: `record_for_host` extracts `uri.host` (which preserves the case supplied in the referer and excludes the port) and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` without lowercasing the parameter. A referer with an uppercase host will not match a stored lowercase host, and a stored host containing an allowed port (`example.com:3000`) will never match because `uri.host` is only `example.com`. This makes otherwise valid embeddable hosts fail the allow-list check. Normalize both sides and compare host without port, or store/compare consistently.

title: All `*_ids` keys in rest_serializer payloads are now treated as embedded associations and can be corrupted
body: The new `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` branch treats every key ending in `_ids` as an embedded association. If the payload has a `*_ids` key but no matching side-loaded plural collection, `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined` for every id, and the code still deletes the original key and replaces it with `[undefined, ...]`, silently losing the IDs. If the value is null or a non-array, `.map` throws. This affects any existing `__rest_serializer` response with `*_ids` fields, not just the new embedding payloads.

title: Update/destroy assume the host exists and 500 on missing ids
body: `update` and `destroy` both use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and immediately dereference the result. If the id is stale or invalid, `update` calls `save_host(nil)` (which does `host.host = ...`) and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, producing a 500 instead of a 404. Use `find_by!`/`find` with a guard and render a not-found response.

title: Embedded find test requests fruit 2 but asserts fruit 1 data
body: The test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` but the pretender `/fruits/:id` handler always returns `fruits[0]` (apple, with `color_ids: [1,2]`), and the assertions expect those color ids. The test therefore does not verify that the requested id is honored; if the pretender were corrected to return fruit 2 (banana, `color_ids: [3]`), this test would fail. Either the request id or the expected fixture should be corrected.

title: New admin embeddable-hosts endpoint has no behavioral tests
body: The spec only asserts that `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` subclasses `Admin::AdminController`. The new create/update/destroy behavior is untested: host and category persistence, defaulting a blank category to uncategorized, rejecting invalid hosts, handling missing nested params, and handling non-existent ids. This is why regressions like the nil-host crash and missing-record 500s are not caught.

title: db/schema.rb is not updated for the new embeddable_hosts table
body: This migration creates `embeddable_hosts`, but the PR does not update `db/schema.rb`. Discourse's test setup and fresh installs load the schema file, so the new table will be absent from test databases; the new `EmbeddableHost` model, fabricator, and admin endpoints will fail in specs. The migration must be reflected in schema.rb as well.

title: Migration crashes when old site_settings rows are absent
body: The migration assumes `execute(...)[0]` always returns a row for `embed_category` and, on line 15, for `uncategorized_category_id`. In a normal install `embed_category` may have no row at all (defaults live in memory, not necessarily in the table), so `[0]` is nil and `['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the upgrade. Use `execute(...).first`/`try` and handle the empty-result case.

title: Old host values are interpolated directly and are not normalized
body: Each host from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is inserted straight into SQL with string interpolation. A value containing a quote breaks the migration (and is effectively SQL injection from persisted configuration). More importantly, the migration bypasses `EmbeddableHost` normalization, so old entries such as `http://example.com` or `example.com/path` are stored unchanged; `record_for_host` looks up only `URI(host).host` (`example.com`), so those hosts will never match after upgrade and embedding silently stops working.

title: Feed-polled imports lose category after embed_category removal
body: TopicEmbed now derives its category only from `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)`. `SiteSetting.embed_category` has been removed, but TopicEmbed is also used by feed polling, where feed URLs are not necessarily registered as embeddable_hosts. Those imports now pass a nil category and fall into uncategorized, a behavior regression for feed polling. Either keep a fallback setting or require/register feed hosts before removing the global category setting.

title: Nil host causes a 500 instead of a validation error
body: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!` without checking for nil. The admin controller assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly, so a request with a missing or nil host raises `NoMethodError` before validation can report an error. This should return a normal validation failure; add a presence check or guard the callback.

title: Duplicate hosts are allowed and can map to different categories
body: There is no uniqueness validation on `host` and the migration adds no unique index. The admin UI can therefore create multiple records for the same host with different categories. `record_for_host` uses `.first` without an order, so imported posts can be categorized unpredictably. Add a case-insensitive unique index and model validation.

title: Port is accepted by validation but never matched during lookup
body: The format validator explicitly permits an optional `:port`, but `record_for_host` compares `uri.host` (which excludes the port) against the stored host value. A record stored as `example.com:8080` can therefore never match an embed URL/referer for that host. Either strip the port on save or include the port in the lookup consistently.

title: New hosts saved without a selected category lose their category in the UI
body: For a new host, `categoryId` is null unless the user explicitly chooses a category. The server defaults blank categories to `uncategorized_category_id`, but after save the component overwrites `host.category` with `Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId)`, i.e. with null. The row then displays no category and a later edit starts with a blank chooser even though the server stored uncategorized. Use the saved `category_id` from the server response instead of the client-side `categoryId`.

title: New admin controllers only have subclass specs
body: The new `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and `Admin::EmbeddingController` specs only assert inheritance. There are no request specs for create/update/destroy, authorization, missing host, invalid id, or category defaulting. Those paths contain the nil-host and nil-record failure modes introduced by this controller, so the current tests would not catch them.

title: In-place image downsize can corrupt the uploaded file on failure
body: The new auto-downsize code calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`, overwriting the original upload file in place, and ignores the boolean return value. If ImageMagick/gifsicle fails partway through (unsupported or malformed image, missing delegate, killed process), the destination path may already be truncated or partially written. The loop then retries on the damaged file up to five times before `Upload.create_for` stores whatever remains, so a failed resize can turn a valid upload into a corrupt or empty file. The resize should write to a separate temporary path and atomically replace the original only on success, and the caller should stop/fail when conversion returns false.

title: Animated GIF detection uses the tempfile path and strips animation
body: `OptimizedImage.optimize` decides whether to use the animated conversion path by checking `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. The controller passes `tempfile.path` as `from`; Rack upload tempfile paths normally have no `.gif` extension, even when the uploaded filename is `.gif`. As a result `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` has no effect for normal uploads: a large animated GIF falls back to `convert from[0]`, which keeps only the first frame. The original upload then loses its animation (or the conversion fails). Animated handling should be based on the original filename/content type, not the tempfile path.

title: Five fixed 80% passes may leave the image above max_image_size_kb
body: The resize loop runs at most five times and then proceeds without checking whether the file is now within `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. Five 80% linear resizes reduce area to roughly 10.7%, so a 10 MB image can remain above a 1 MB limit; for smaller configured limits the gap is larger. In that case `Upload.create_for` receives an oversized file and the upload either fails server-side validation or, if validation does not enforce this path, stores an image larger than the configured limit. The loop should verify the final size and fail explicitly if the target cannot be reached.

title: Client upload limit is hardcoded instead of respecting site settings
body: `validateUploadedFile` now uses a fixed 10 MB limit for every upload type and no longer reads `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. For attachments this ignores the configured `max_attachment_size_kb`, allowing users to select files the server will reject; for images it also rejects images above 10 MB even if an administrator configured a larger limit. The 413 handler at line 246 similarly reports 10 MB instead of the configured limit, giving a misleading error message. The client should continue using the appropriate site setting where server-side auto-downsizing is not applicable.

title: No tests cover the automatic image downsize path
body: The PR adds a new server-side resize path and a new `OptimizedImage.downsize` overload but does not add tests. There is no coverage for oversized image reduction, non-image uploads, conversion failure behavior, or animated GIF handling. Those are exactly the paths where the in-place mutation and animation-detection issues above can regress unnoticed.

title: Duplicate downsize definition silently removes the existing width/height API
body: Ruby does not support method overloading: defining `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the earlier `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145. Any existing caller using the old signature, e.g. `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, temp, 100, 100, opts)`, will now raise ArgumentError. A four-positional call passing width and height will be interpreted as width plus opts and fail when the code reads `opts[:allow_animation]`. The old public method is no longer usable, so this needs to be a distinct method name or a single method that accepts both forms.

title: Downsize loop can proceed with a file still over the limit and ignores failed conversions
body: The loop makes at most five 80% resize attempts, then calls `Upload.create_for` without checking `tempfile.size` again against `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. If five attempts are not enough, the new guard has not actually enforced the limit and the oversized file proceeds to upload. The loop also ignores the boolean result of `OptimizedImage.downsize`, so a failed conversion still consumes an attempt and leaves the original size unchanged. The code needs a post-loop size check and an explicit abort/error path when conversion fails or the file remains too large.

title: Hard-coded 10 MB no longer honors configured attachment size limits
body: `validateUploadedFile` is used for both images and attachments, but the new code replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a fixed `10 * 1024` KB. For attachments this bypasses `max_attachment_size_kb`: files up to 10 MB are allowed client-side even when the site limit is lower, and files larger than 10 MB are rejected even when the site setting allows them. The 413 handler at line 246 repeats the same hard-coded assumption and can display the wrong limit.

title: Animated GIF detection uses the temp path, so uploaded animations can be flattened
body: The new call passes `tempfile.path` as the source to `OptimizedImage.downsize`. `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects the animated branch only when the source path matches `/\.GIF$/i`, but Rack multipart temp files normally do not carry the original uploaded extension. As a result, `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is ineffective for normal uploads and animated GIFs are handled by the static `downsize_instructions`, whose `convert ... #{from}[0]` keeps only the first frame. Animated uploads can silently become static images.

title: Remote URL downloads now ignore configured size limits for all upload types
body: Changing `FileHelper.download` from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to `10.megabytes` applies to every URL upload, including non-images. A site with a smaller `max_attachment_size_kb` or `max_image_size_kb` will now fetch up to 10 MB from the remote URL before validation, increasing resource use and bypassing the configured limit. If larger images are intended only so they can be auto-downsized, the download limit should be conditional on the upload type or based on an explicit setting.

title: No tests cover the new auto-downsize path
body: The PR changes upload size enforcement, overwrites uploaded image files, and relies on method dispatch inside `OptimizedImage`, but adds no tests for oversized static images, animated GIFs, failed conversions, non-image uploads, or the five-attempt cap. Regressions such as the duplicate `downsize` method or the animation branch being skipped would not be caught.

title: Duplicate self.downsize definition silently replaces the width/height overload
body: The file now defines `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 and `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. Ruby does not support overloading: the second definition replaces the first, so the width/height version is dead code. Any caller using `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, 100, 200)` will now hit the 3-argument method with `dimensions = 100` and `opts = 200`; `optimize` then calls `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer and raises NoMethodError (or, worse, builds `-resize 100` geometry with no aspect handling). The `force_aspect_ratio` path is likewise unreachable through the width/height form. This is an API break for an existing public class method. Use a single signature, or rename the dimensions form (e.g. `downsize_to_dimensions`), or accept both dimensions and options explicitly.

title: Downsize loop ignores failure and never verifies the target size was reached
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false when the convert/gifsicle step fails, but the loop does not check the return value and never re-checks that the file shrank: it just calls downsize up to five times on the same path and then proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with whatever is on disk. If the image format has no extension on the tempfile path, if ImageMagick cannot parse `80%>` geometry, or if five 80% reductions simply cannot get under `max_image_size_kb`, the loop burns five CPU-heavy conversions and the oversized (or corrupted/truncated, since convert reads and writes the same file) image is uploaded and stored anyway, contrary to the configured limit. Additionally, because `from == to`, a failed convert can leave the tempfile truncated and that corrupt file is still uploaded. Break out on failure and, after the loop, reject the upload with a clear error if `tempfile.size` is still over the limit.

title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types
body: The API download path was previously bounded by `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`; it is now hardcoded to `10.megabytes` regardless of the `type` parameter. This means non-image attachments (e.g. `type=attachment`) supplied via `url` can now make the server download up to 10MB even on sites configured with a much smaller limit, and each such upload may additionally trigger five downsize conversions. The enlarged download bound should be applied only when the target is an image (and arguably should still be a configurable/site-derived limit), not to every API upload.

title: Client validation no longer honors configured max size settings, including for attachments
body: Replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` raises the client-side limit for every upload type. Only images are downsized server-side; attachments are still rejected by the server against `max_attachment_size_kb`. On a site configured with, say, a 1MB attachment limit, an 8MB PDF now passes `validateUploadedFile`, is uploaded, and only then fails with a server error. The message in `displayErrorForUpload` (line 246) has the same problem: the 413 case hardcodes 10MB and will report the wrong limit whenever the web-server threshold differs. The larger limit should be scoped to images (and ideally still derived from the site settings), leaving attachment limits unchanged.

title: No tests cover the new automatic-downsize behavior
body: The PR adds a new synchronous downsize loop plus a new `OptimizedImage.downsize` signature/overload, but no specs are included. There are no tests for: reaching the target size after N reductions, the loop giving up after 5 attempts, conversion failure (return false) being surfaced, the API-URL path, or animated GIFs via `downsize_instructions_animated`. The zero-arity/argument ambiguity between the two `downsize` definitions would also be caught by a simple unit test and currently is not.

title: Unsubscribe action crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (any logged-in user who never visited/interacted with that visible topic — e.g. a colleague who opens a forwarded unsubscribe link, or a user hitting the URL manually). The very next line dereferences `tu.notification_level`, and later `tu.save!`, so a nil result produces an unhandled NoMethodError (HTTP 500) on a user-facing endpoint. The action should use `TopicUser.change` (which creates the row when missing) or guard against nil.

title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change and leaves notifications_reason_id nil
body: The unsubscribe action mutates the notification level with `tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change` (which `set_notifications` uses). `TopicUser.change` sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id = :user_changed`, and publishes the change on MessageBus. Writing directly leaves `notifications_reason_id` as nil. Both `TopicUser.update_last_read` (its `case when tu.notifications_reason_id is null ... then :tracking`) and `TopicUser.auto_track` (guarded on `notifications_reason_id: nil`) will re-upgrade a topic to tracking/watch based on continued reading whenever the reason is nil. So the user unsubscribes, then normal reading silently re-subscribes them — the feature does not stick. It also skips the MessageBus publish, so an open client won't reflect the new level.

title: State-changing action performed via GET allows CSRF
body: `unsubscribe` is routed as `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` (and the no-slug variant) and mutates the user's notification level. Rails CSRF protection only covers non-GET requests, and this action additionally does `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`. A logged-in user who loads any third-party page containing `` will be silently unsubscribed from that topic. The action should require a non-idempotent method (POST/DELETE) with CSRF, or use a signed token so mere navigation cannot trigger the change.

title: New unsubscribe_url option and unsubscribe endpoint have no meaningful tests
body: The spec adds `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to `message_with_unsubscribe`, but only so the new `unsubscribe_link` locale interpolation doesn't raise; nothing asserts that the per-topic URL actually appears in the generated email body or that it is formatted correctly (the real value is an absolute URL while the spec passes a relative one). There is also no spec at all for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (nil TopicUser, watching→regular vs regular→muted transitions, slug redirect). The core behavior of this PR is effectively untested, so a regression would go unnoticed.

title: Email unsubscribe text overstates behavior for tracking/watching topics
body: For a topic at tracking or watching level the action downgrades to `regular` (`if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] ... = :regular`), not mute. But the email/client text claims `stop_notifications: "You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}."` A user who was watching still receives notifications on replies and mentions, so the message is misleading and they will be surprised to keep getting email for a topic they clicked to unsubscribe from.

title: unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (e.g. the link is forwarded/shared, or the user follows `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` for a topic they never interacted with, or a notification was generated without creating a TopicUser). The next line `if tu.notification_level > ...` dereferences nil and raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 to the user instead of handling the case. The action should guard against a missing TopicUser (create one via `TopicUser.change`, or treat it as already-unsubscribed).

title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change side effects
body: The action mutates `tu` and calls `tu.save!` directly instead of using `TopicUser.change`. As a result: `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not updated (so the topic's notification reason stays e.g. `auto_watch_category`, which is why the client route has to null out `notificationReasonText` to hide it), no `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... })` is sent (other open tabs/clients keep showing the old state), and `observe_after_save_callbacks_for`/UserActionObserver are not run. The unsubscribe should go through `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` so the same bookkeeping as the rest of the app happens.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking emails that don't pass it
body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` string was changed to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}` in addition to `%{user_preferences_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` render `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` for every message built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url:`; any other path that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url:` will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` while building the message. The existing spec had to add `unsubscribe_url:` for exactly this reason. Either supply a default `unsubscribe_url` in `MessageBuilder#initialize`, or make the interpolation tolerant.

title: Template name does not match the topicUnsubscribe route
body: The route is declared as `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' })` and has no custom `renderTemplate`/`templateName`. Ember therefore looks up the default template for route name `topicUnsubscribe` (i.e. `topic-unsubscribe`), matching the added controller and view files which use the dashed name. The template added here is `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which resolves to the template name `topic/unsubscribe` (the form used for a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route). With the current route name this template will not be found, so the unsubscribe route renders no template (blank page).
