Rename the file to `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs` or provide an explicit `renderTemplate`/`templateName`.

title: Unsubscribe mutates state via a GET request with no CSRF protection
body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` changes the user's notification level but is reachable through the GET routes `t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`, and the action is added to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`. Rails does not apply the CSRF token check to GET requests, so a third-party page can embed `` and, for a logged-in user, silently mute that topic without their consent. The same GET also makes the action vulnerable to link prefetching/scanning by clients that try to follow links. State-changing actions reached from emails should use a confirm step or a signed/tokenized request rather than a bare GET.

title: No tests for the new unsubscribe behavior
body: The only spec change is adding `unsubscribe_url:` to an existing message-builder example; nothing asserts the new behavior. There are no specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (including the nil-TopicUser case and the redirect when slug is blank), the new `t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` / `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` routes, `Topic#unsubscribe_url`, or the fact that the per-topic link actually appears in the rendered email body/HTML. Given the action contains a crash path and bypasses the normal `TopicUser.change` path, these paths need coverage before merge.

title: Global unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for every email
body: The new unsubscribe_link string interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}. Email::MessageBuilder renders this key whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true, but it does not provide a default unsubscribe_url. Any mailer or plugin that passes add_unsubscribe_link: true without also passing unsubscribe_url will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument while building the email, so the email is not sent. This PR only updates the notification mailer and one spec, so the contract break is easy to miss.

title: unsubscribe assumes a TopicUser row exists and can raise NoMethodError
body: The action does TopicUser.find_by(...) and immediately reads tu.notification_level. For any logged-in user who has no topic_users row for that topic, tu is nil and the request raises NoMethodError, returning a 500. Email recipients usually have a row because send_notification_email calls TopicUser.change, but the route is accessible to any logged-in user, e.g. via a forwarded email or manual URL. Using TopicUser.change would upsert the row; it would also update notifications_changed_at/reason and publish the MessageBus notification_level_change event that direct save! currently bypasses.

title: State-changing unsubscribe endpoint is a GET with no CSRF protection
body: GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe changes the current user's notification_level using only the session cookie. A malicious page can embed this URL as an image or link and, for a logged-in user who can see the topic, silently downgrade or mute the user's subscription. Email link scanners can trigger the same state change. The link needs an unguessable per-user token or the mutation needs to be a POST protected by CSRF.

title: New per-topic unsubscribe behavior has no meaningful test coverage
body: The spec change only adds unsubscribe_url to an existing builder so it no longer exercises the missing-interpolation path. There is no assertion that the new URL appears in the rendered body or HTML, no controller test for creating/muting a TopicUser, no test for the nil-TopicUser case, and no test for Topic#unsubscribe_url. These omissions leave the 500 on missing TopicUser and the global unsubscribe_link interpolation requirement unguarded.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, allowing blocklist bypass
body: `should_block?` looks up the raw email with `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`, and the model's uniqueness validation is also exact. The User model does not normalize the email before the validator runs. On PostgreSQL, `bad@spam.com` and `Bad@Spam.com` are different values, so a blocked address can be used again simply by changing capitalization. Downcase the value for storage and lookup (for example with `Email.downcase`) and make uniqueness case-insensitive; otherwise the blocklist is trivially bypassable.

title: Email validation mutates match statistics, so a blocked signup is counted twice
body: This validator calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which increments `match_count` and saves the record. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save` on the same user. For a blocked address both calls run this validator, so one signup attempt increments `match_count` twice, and any repeated `valid?` call also writes to the database. Validation should be side-effect free; record the match when the rejection is actually handled, or otherwise ensure it is counted once.

title: match_count update is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` loses updates when concurrent validations hit the same blocked email: two requests can read the same count and both write the same incremented value. Since this counter is meant to track how often the blocklist matches, use an atomic update such as `increment_counter`/`update_counters` (plus `update_column` for `last_match_at`) rather than saving the model after reading the value into Ruby.

title: Domain whitelist regex is not anchored, allowing whitelist bypass
body: `email_in_restriction_setting?` builds `Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true)` and uses `value =~ regexp`, so it matches an allowed domain anywhere after `@`. With a whitelist of `example.com`, `user@example.com.attacker.net` matches and is accepted even though its real domain is not whitelisted; the blacklist has the same suffix-matching problem in reverse. Anchor the domain at the end of the address (and escape the configured domains) so whitelist/blacklist checks compare the actual domain.

title: Validator specs stub the blocklist and do not cover the real paths
body: Both examples stub `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, so they do not exercise the real blocklist record, case normalization, the returned `user.email.blocked` message, or the whitelist/blacklist logic that was moved into this new validator. A regression in those shipping paths would still pass these specs. Add coverage using real `BlockedEmail` records, mixed-case addresses, and at least one whitelist/blacklist case.

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and does not normalize input
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` looks up the email with `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`, an exact, case-sensitive comparison. Signup does not normalize the address (`User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` directly), so a blocked address such as `foo@spam.com` can be bypassed by submitting `Foo@Spam.com` or ` foo@spam.com `. The existing whitelist/blacklist regex is case-insensitive, making this blocklist trivially bypassable. Normalize (strip + downcase) both the stored value and the lookup value, and ideally enforce the same normalization in the unique index/model.

title: Blocked-email validation mutates statistics and double-counts failed signups
body: The validator calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which increments `match_count` and saves the record (app/models/blocked_email.rb:14-16). Because `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` at line 168 and then `user.save` at line 172, the same email is validated twice, so one failed signup increments `match_count` twice and updates `last_match_at` twice. Any other `valid?` call also changes the stats. Move the match statistics update out of the validation path (record it in the controller only when the email is actually rejected), or make the validator check read-only. The read-modify-write is also not atomic, so concurrent checks can lose increments.

title: No tests for the moved domain whitelist/blacklist validation
body: This PR moves the `email_domains_whitelist` / `email_domains_blacklist` checks out of `User#email_validator` into the new `EmailValidator`, but the new spec only exercises the blocked-email branch. There is no coverage for allowed/rejected domains, the interaction between a domain error and a blocked email, or the case-insensitive domain regex. The spec also does not stub or clear those two settings, so it can fail if another test leaves a whitelist/blacklist set. Add tests for both restriction settings and set the settings explicitly in the spec.

title: Locally rejected email overrides third-party authenticated email
body: The new `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` check runs before the `authOptions.email_valid` check. If a user first gets an email error (e.g. email already registered) and later authenticates that same email through a social provider, the form still reports the email as invalid and `submitDisabled` remains true, even though the server would accept the authenticated address. Move the `authOptions` trust check ahead of the local rejection check, or clear the rejected entry when `authOptions` confirms ownership.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case/whitespace sensitive and bypassable
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` compares the raw submitted email with exact string equality. There is no normalization in the new validator or in the User email assignment path, so on a case-sensitive database (Discourse uses PostgreSQL) a blocked address like `spam@example.com` can be submitted as `Spam@example.com` (or with surrounding whitespace) and will not match. The account is then allowed despite the block. Normalize the value before lookup and when storing block records, e.g. strip/downcase consistently and query with the normalized form.

title: Validation has write side effects and double-counts blocked matches
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` is a predicate but performs a read-modify-write on `match_count` and saves the record every time it is called. It is called from a model validator, so ordinary `user.valid?` checks mutate the blocklist table. This is especially visible in `UsersController#create`, which calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`: a blocked signup increments `match_count` twice for one attempt. The non-atomic `record.match_count += 1; record.save` also loses increments under concurrent requests. As a result, `match_count`/`last_match_at` are not reliable, and validation requests cause unnecessary writes. Move the statistics update out of the validator or make it an atomic, once-per-actual-attempt operation.

title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored and bypassable
body: The domain restriction regexp is built without an end anchor. With a whitelist setting of `example.com`, it compiles to `@(example\.com)`, which also matches the prefix of `user@example.com.evil.com`; that address is therefore accepted even though its domain is not whitelisted. Conversely, a blacklist can overblock unrelated hosts. Anchor the match to the actual domain boundary (or parse the domain and compare exact values) instead of using an unanchored substring regexp.

title: Tests stub out the critical block lookup and never cover User validation
body: Both new validator examples stub `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, so they do not exercise the real database lookup, email normalization, or the `User` validation path. There is also no spec asserting that a `User` with a blocked or mixed-case blocked email is invalid, and no coverage for the whitelist/blacklist logic that was moved from `User` into this validator. These gaps are exactly what would catch the blocklist bypass and the unanchored domain regex. Add model/integration specs using real `BlockedEmail` records and a `User`/`valid?` path.

title: Invalid ERB `end if` breaks the best template
body: The conditional opened on line 2 is closed with `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. `end if` is invalid Ruby because the trailing `if` modifier has no expression, so rendering this template for an existing topic raises a SyntaxError and `/embed/best` returns 500 instead of showing the discussion. Controller specs do not render views, so this failure is not caught.

title: Unescaped embed URL is injected into raw imported HTML
body: Line 13 interpolates `url` directly into `#{url}` without HTML escaping. `url` can come from an RSS item or from `params[:embed_url]` as long as the host matches `embeddable_host`. Because `TopicEmbed.import` stores the result as a `raw_html` post and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` emits `raw post.cooked`, a URL containing a single quote or `

title: RSS item HTML is imported raw without sanitization
body: `poll_feed` passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` straight to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `TopicEmbed.import` does not sanitize `contents`, and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` renders `raw post.cooked`. A malicious or compromised feed can therefore inject `<script>` tags or event-handler attributes that execute in the Discourse origin when the embed page loads. The Readability path sanitizes allowed tags and attributes, but the RSS path bypasses that protection; feed HTML needs sanitization before being stored as raw HTML.

title: Non-atomic SETNX/EXPIRE can permanently throttle an embed URL
body: `retrieved_recently?` calls `$redis.setnx` and then a separate `$redis.expire`. If the process dies between those two calls, the key is left without a TTL, so every subsequent attempt for that URL sees it as retrieved and never performs retrieval again. Use an atomic `SET key value EX 60 NX` (or a MULTI/EXEC) so the throttle cannot become permanent.

title: Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten as root-relative
body: The `start_with?('/')` checks at lines 64 and 70 also match protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/a.png`. The code then strips all leading slashes and prefixes the feed host, producing `http://feedhost/cdn.example.com/a.png`, which is wrong and breaks links or images in imported content. Only prefix when there is exactly one leading slash and the URL is not protocol-relative.

title: Invalid ERB close tag prevents the embed view from rendering
body: The template opens a normal `if @topic_view.posts.present?` at line 2 and closes it with `<%- end if %>`. ERB compiles that to Ruby `end if`, which is not valid syntax. Any request that renders `embed/best` raises a SyntaxError, so the embedded comments never display. It should be `<%- end %>`.

title: Imported feed content is stored as unsanitized raw HTML
body: `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: raw_html`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for that mode. `Jobs::PollFeed` feeds `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` into this path, so an RSS/Atom item containing encoded markup such as `<script>...</script>` is stored and later rendered with `raw post.cooked`; the script executes in the forum/embed origin. Remote feed content is not trusted; it must be sanitized/allowlisted before being stored as raw HTML, or this path must not use `raw_html`.

title: Embed URL is interpolated into raw HTML without escaping
body: The imported URL is inserted directly into a single-quoted href and link text: `#{url}`, and this content is saved as raw HTML. A URL containing a single quote or `<` (the only validation is that it starts with http:// or https://) can break out and inject arbitrary HTML/JS into the post. Escape `url` for HTML before building the link.

title: Kernel#open on a caller-supplied URL can execute shell commands
body: `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` on a URL supplied by callers. Ruby's `Kernel#open` executes a command when the filename starts with `|`; the Disqus importer passes `t[:link]` from the XML export directly into this method with no scheme validation, so a malicious export can run arbitrary shell commands when the importer is executed. Validate the URL scheme/host and use a non-command-opening HTTP API, or at least reject pipe and non-http URLs.

title: PollFeed assumes every feed item has content and aborts on common RSS feeds
body: `PollFeed` assumes every item has `i.content`; RSS 2.0 commonly exposes the body as `description`, and Atom items may use `summary`, so `i.content` can be nil. `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting `poll_feed` for all items. Since this job has `retry: false`, a single item without `content` prevents the feed from being imported. Use nil-safe fallback fields and handle failures per item.

title: Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten to the source host
body: The absolutization only handles paths beginning with `/` by stripping all leading slashes and prefixing the source host. For a protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/image.png`, it produces `http://sourcehost/cdn.example.com/image.png` instead of `http://cdn.example.com/image.png`, breaking embedded images and links. Treat URLs beginning with `//` as protocol-relative and use the source scheme.

title: Origin check accepts any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl
body: The check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` tests whether the origin is a substring of `discourseUrl`, not whether it matches the expected origin. For example, if `discourseUrl` is `http://example.com`, a message from `http://example.co` is accepted because that string is a prefix. Any page that can post to this window and has a matching substring origin can forge resize messages. Compare `e.origin` exactly to the parsed origin of `discourseUrl`.

title: PollFeed setting tests short-circuit on feed_polling_enabled
body: The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' examples only stub the one setting to nil but leave `feed_polling_enabled?` at its default false, so the first condition short-circuits and `poll_feed` is never called regardless of the setting under test. These specs would pass even if the URL/username checks were broken. Stub the other conditions true in each example.

title: Unsanitized feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered as cooked HTML
body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` using content taken directly from external RSS/Readability sources. Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged for raw_html posts, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders `raw post.cooked`. A malicious or compromised feed can therefore store `<script>` or event-handler HTML that executes in the Discourse origin (stored XSS). The imported_from footer also interpolates the feed URL into raw HTML without escaping. Imported HTML must be sanitized before storage, or this path must use the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline.

title: Invalid `end if` makes the best embed view fail to compile
body: The template closes the header conditional with `<%- end if %>`. There is no condition after the `if`, so Ruby parses this as an incomplete modifier-if and raises a SyntaxError when the template is compiled. Any successful embed request that finds a `topic_id` and renders `best.html.erb` will fail with a 500. It should be `<%- end %>`.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching
body: The listener validates messages with `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`. This accepts any origin that appears as a substring of `discourseUrl`; for example, `http://eviltrout.co` passes when `discourseUrl` is `http://eviltrout.com`. An untrusted window can then send forged `discourse-resize` messages to the embedding page. The origin should be compared exactly against the parsed `discourseUrl` origin.

title: Protocol-relative URLs are corrupted during absolutization
body: The absolutizer treats every href/src beginning with `/` as root-relative. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/image.png` starts with `/`, so it is rewritten to `http://origin/cdn.example.com/image.png`, breaking links and images in imported feed content. Detect `//` separately and preserve the scheme (or use URI.join).

title: PollFeed assumes every feed item has `content`
body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls `scrub` on `i.content` without checking for nil. Many RSS/Atom feeds expose body text only through `description` (or have empty/missing content), in which case `i.content` is nil and the job raises NoMethodError. Since this job sets `retry: false`, such a feed stops importing items. Guard missing content and fall back to `description` or skip the item.

title: `open(url)` is used without requiring open-uri
body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url)` but this file does not require `open-uri`. Only `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` requires it, so when the retrieve-topic job or the Disqus task calls `import_remote` first, Ruby's `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a local filename and raises `Errno::ENOENT`. Add `require 'open-uri'` in this file or in every caller before fetching remote content.

title: Existing migration now drops the top_topics table with `force: true`
body: This PR changes an already-existing migration from `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. If the migration is ever run against a database where `top_topics` exists but the migration is not recorded (for example after a partially failed migration or a restored schema), Rails will drop the table and all of its rows before recreating it. Migrations should be immutable; use a new migration or guard with `unless table_exists?` instead of adding `force: true`.

title: Making .small-action a flex container breaks the action button's right alignment
body: The change makes `.small-action` a flex container, but its action button still relies on `float: right` (`.small-action button`, around line 306) to sit at the right edge. Floats are ignored on flex items, and `.small-action-desc` is not given `flex: 1` or `margin-left: auto`, so the button will now render immediately after the description instead of right-aligned. The button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the description needs `flex: 1`) to preserve the previous layout.

title: Making .small-action a flex container silently disables the button's float: right
body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex` (@include flexbox()), but the still-unmodified rule at line 306-310 right-aligns the action button with `float: right;`. Per the flexbox spec, `float` is ignored on flex items, so the button is no longer pushed to the right edge of the row. Because `.small-action-desc` (line 279) has no `flex: 1` / `margin-left: auto`, it will only be as wide as its content, leaving the button sitting immediately after the description text (and at the far left when the description is empty). This changes the visual layout of every small-action row (deleted posts, etc.). Either give `.small-action-desc` `flex: 1`, add `margin-left: auto` to the button, or drop the flex change.

title: `order` mixin maps order values to -webkit-box-ordinal-group/-moz-box-ordinal-group without the required +1 offset
body: The 2009 box model properties `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based and must be positive integers, while the modern `order` property is 0-based and also accepts negatives. Passing `$val` straight through means `@include order(1)` emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 1`, which is the default and therefore a no-op, and `@include order(0)` emits an invalid value that old WebKit/Gecko discard. The current call sites (`order(2)`, `order(3)`) happen to keep the correct relative order only because the unordered `.title` implicitly stays at group 1, but the mixin is unsafe for any future use. Emit `$val + 1` for the `*-box-ordinal-group` properties.

title: Removing float: right from .panel loses right alignment in non-flex / legacy-box renderers
body: `.panel` previously used `float: right;` to sit at the right edge of the header. That rule was removed and replaced by `margin-left: auto;` inside the new flex `.contents` container. Auto margins on flex items are not supported by the 2009 `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` implementations (the reason those prefixed `display` values are emitted by the `flexbox` mixin), and are ignored entirely by browsers with no flex support (e.g. IE9), which is why the prefixed `display` values exist. In those renderers the panel loses its float and now flows immediately after `.title`/`.extra-info-wrapper` instead of being right-aligned, so the header layout degrades exactly in the browsers the mixin is meant to cover. Keep the float as a fallback (floats are inert inside a real flex container) or otherwise provide a fallback.

title: align-items mixin emits a non-existent -ms-align-items declaration and invalid -webkit-box-align values
body: `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a real property — IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, which is already emitted — so that line is dead code. More importantly, `-webkit-box-align` (line 118) does not accept the `baseline` value, which is exactly what the new call site in `app/assets/stylesheets/common/components/badges.css.scss:57` passes (`@include align-items(baseline)`). In old WebKit, where this mixin switches the element to `display: -webkit-inline-box`, the declaration is discarded and `-webkit-box-align` falls back to `stretch`, so the bullet badge children can be stretched to the line box instead of baseline-aligned; previously those browsers got the `inline-block` fallback and normal inline alignment. Consider dropping the bogus `-ms-align-items`, and either omitting `baseline` for the prefixed property or documenting that it only applies to the standard declaration.

title: Flexbox on .small-action makes the action button's float ineffective
body: Adding `@include flexbox()` to `.small-action` makes its children flex items, and `float` is ignored on flex items. The existing `button { float: right; }` at line 309 therefore no longer pushes the button to the right; because `.small-action-desc` has no `flex-grow` and the button has no `margin-left: auto`, the button will sit immediately after the description instead of at the far right. This is a layout regression for small-action rows such as post notices.

title: align-items mixin does not cover the same legacy engines as flexbox mixin
body: `@mixin flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box`, but `@mixin align-items()` never emits the matching legacy Mozilla property `-moz-box-align`. In engines that use the old Mozilla box model, the flex container is created but vertical alignment is ignored, so `.d-header .contents` and `.small-action` are not centered as intended. The mixin also emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a real IE property; the valid property is `-ms-flex-align` (already present). Add `-moz-box-align` or drop the `-moz-box` display, and remove the invalid `-ms-align-items`.

title: order mixin maps 0-based order values directly to 1-based legacy ordinal groups
body: The legacy `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` properties are 1-based (default 1), while the modern `order` property is 0-based (default 0). `@mixin order($val)` passes `$val` unchanged to both families. The current callers use `order(2)` and `order(3)`, so relative ordering happens to work, but any future caller using `order(1)` — or relying on parity with the modern default — will get incorrect ordering in legacy engines. The legacy properties should use a 1-based value such as `$val + 1`, or the mixin should document/enforce the difference.

title: website_name leaks a profile website hidden from anonymous viewers
body: `website_name` is derived from `object.user_profile.website`, but it is not in the `untrusted_attributes` list, which hides `:website` when `scope.restrict_user_fields?` is true for TL0 users viewed anonymously, and it has no other scope check. An anonymous viewer can still receive the website host and path through `website_name` even though `website` itself is suppressed. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` or apply the same restriction in its include method.

title: `include_website_name` is not recognized as an inclusion guard
body: ActiveModel::Serializers only consults methods named `include_<attribute>?`; a method named `include_website_name` without the trailing question mark is ignored. Consequently `website_name` is always serialized when the attribute exists (and `website_name: null` is emitted for users without a website), and the intended `website.present?` guard is dead code. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

title: Test coverage misses website_name restriction for anonymous TL0 users
body: The TL0/anonymous test only checks the existing untrusted attribute list and never sets a website, while the new website_name tests use a normal viewer. There is no regression test proving `website_name` is omitted when `scope.restrict_user_fields?` hides the profile website, which is exactly the case where the new attribute currently leaks data.

title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` and is never invoked
body: ActiveModel::Serializers decides whether to emit an attribute by calling `include_<attr>?` (with a question mark). The new method is defined as `include_website_name` (no `?`), so it is never called and the condition is ignored. As a result `website_name` is always serialized, emitting `website_name: null` for every user with no website (and any other case the guard was meant to exclude). It should be renamed `include_website_name?` to match the convention used by every other include check in this file (`include_email?`, `include_user_fields?`, etc.).

title: `website_name` bypasses the untrusted-attribute restriction and leaks a TL0 user's website domain
body: `website` is declared in `untrusted_attributes`, so its `include_website?` returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (e.g. a TL0 user viewed by anonymous). The new `website_name` attribute is a plain attribute and its include condition only checks `website.present?`, not `restrict_user_fields?`. So even though `website` is suppressed, `website_name` is still emitted and discloses the user's website host/path to viewers who are explicitly not allowed to see that field. Add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (or gate its include condition on `scope.restrict_user_fields?`) and add a spec covering the TL0/anonymous case with a website set.

title: New website_name bypasses TL0 website privacy restriction
body: website_name is added to attributes (line 43) but is missing from untrusted_attributes (lines 105-111). For a TL0 user viewed anonymously, the existing untrusted_attributes :website rule removes the website field, but website_name is still computed from object.user_profile.website and sent to the client. The user profile template renders model.website_name, so the hidden website host and path become visible. The TL0 spec does not catch this because its untrusted_attributes list omits :website_name and its fabricated user has no website. Add :website_name to untrusted_attributes or make the inclusion hook return false when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object), and extend the spec accordingly.

title: website_name inclusion hook is never called
body: The method is named include_website_name without the trailing question mark. ActiveModelSerializers looks for include_<attribute>? to decide whether to emit an attribute, so this method is dead code. website_name is therefore emitted for every serialized user, including as null when no website exists, and any inclusion logic placed here is ignored. Rename it to include_website_name? and combine it with the untrusted-field check.

title: Domain comparison misclassifies unrelated hosts under multi-label public suffixes
body: The elsif branch treats any two hosts with the same label count greater than two and the same suffix after the first label as the same domain. For example, with instance host foo.co.uk and user website bar.co.uk, both have three labels and suffix co.uk, so the code appends the full path from bar.co.uk even though it is a different registrable domain. The same false positive occurs for foo.github.io and bar.github.io, and similar public suffixes. This defeats the stated same-domain check and can expose a path that would otherwise be hidden. Use a public-suffix-aware registrable-domain comparison or avoid matching multi-label public suffixes this way.

title: Wrong lightness values for embedded post author link
body: The embedded-post meta data link `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This both changes the light-theme color from the intended 30% primary to 70% primary and uses the wrong secondary complement for dark themes. It should preserve the original lightness and use the complementary dark value, i.e. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. As written, the author link becomes too faint in light themes and has incorrect contrast in dark themes.

title: Group member name color no longer matches original light-theme value
body: `.group-member-info .name` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`; otherwise the name no longer contrasts with the adjacent `.title` field as originally intended.

title: Mobile group member name uses wrong lightness pair
body: The mobile `.group-member-info .name` rule was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. title: Mobile topic-map heading color changed from 20% to 50%
body: The mobile `.topic-map h3` color was originally `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but the PR changes it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. title: Custom message length color swapped for light and dark themes
body: `.custom-message-length` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, but the PR changes it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. title: Category badge notification still uses primary-only lightness
body: The conversion is incomplete in this file: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still has `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. title: Embedded post author link uses wrong lightness pair
body: The original rule used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) for light themes and scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%) for dark themes, so the embedded post author link becomes much lighter/lower-contrast on the light theme and darker on the dark theme. title: Group member name color changed from 30% to 50% lightness

title: Wrong lightness in embedded post author link color conversion
body: This conversion changes the light-theme branch from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), even though only the dark-theme branch needed adding. title: Topic map heading color converted with wrong lightness values

This makes light-theme topic-map headings lighter than before (20% to 50%) and does not use the complementary 80% lightness for $secondary in dark themes. The new dark-light-choose uses 50% for both $primary and $secondary, so light-theme group member names are rendered lighter than before and the dark-theme branch is not the complementary $secondary(70%) color. title: Pagination totalPages is off by one for exact multiples
body: In `totalPages`, the formula `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` returns an extra page whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (for example 50 members with a 50-member page). The UI then shows a last page that is empty, and `showingLast`/the next button are wrong on the real last page, so clicking next lands on an empty member list. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` with the zero case, or equivalent.

title: Public group member page now silently truncates at 50 members
body: The public `members` action now always applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` to every group and returns only that page. The public `group/members` template has no pagination controls and the route calls `findMembers()` without any way to advance pages, so any non-automatic group with more than 50 members silently hides the remainder. This is a regression from the previous behavior where non-automatic groups returned all members.

title: Public members endpoint response shape is a breaking change
body: The response body for `GET /groups/:group_id/members.json` changed from a top-level serialized array to an object with `members` and `meta` keys. Any existing API client that still expects the array will break; this public route is not versioned and no compatibility shim is provided.

title: Automatic-group guard is evaluated against the member, not the group
body: Because this template is rendered as the `itemView` for each member, the bare `automatic` lookup resolves against the member object, not the parent group. It is therefore always falsy/undefined, so remove controls are shown even for automatic groups; clicking one sends the DELETE request and the backend returns 422 from `can_not_modify_automatic`. The flag must be passed into the item view or the control guarded in the parent group template.

title: Removal test uses PUT although the new route is DELETE
body: The automatic-group removal spec calls `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the production route added in this PR is `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members`. Controller specs do not exercise routing, so this test would still pass if the DELETE route or route params were wrong. Add a routing/request spec for the new endpoints.

title: totalPages overcounts when the member count is an exact multiple of the page size
body: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`, so a group with exactly 50 members and limit 50 reports 2 pages. `showingLast` therefore remains false on the only real page, and the next action sets offset to `user_count`, loading an empty page. The admin UI then shows an empty final page such as `2/2` instead of disabling next. The page count should be based on `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the zero case handled), and/or the next offset should be clamped to the last valid page start.

title: Public group members page only loads the first 50 members with no pagination controls
body: The route now calls `model.findMembers()` once and the group model always requests the first page with `limit: 50`. The public template `group/members.hbs` renders only the returned `members` array and has no next/previous controls or infinite loading. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members. As a result, any group with more than 50 members now hides members 51+ from non-admin users with no way to reach them.

title: Remove-member control is rendered for automatic groups
body: This template is rendered with each `member` (a `Discourse.User`) as its context, but the guard is `{{#unless automatic}}`. `automatic` is looked up on the user, not on the parent group, so it is undefined and the remove link is rendered even for automatic groups. The server rejects the DELETE with a 422 for automatic groups, and the client has no error handling after the AJAX rejection. The group-level `automatic` flag needs to be passed into the item view or checked through the parent controller.

title: Public members endpoint response shape changed from an array to an object
body: `GET /groups/:group_id/members(.json)` previously returned a bare JSON array of users. It now returns `{ members: [...], meta: {...} }`. This is a breaking API change for any existing client, plugin, or integration that consumes this endpoint directly. The in-repo Ember model was updated, but there is no compatibility path or documentation for external consumers, so consumers parsing an array will start failing.

title: Automatic-group remove test uses PUT although the route is DELETE
body: The test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the new route is defined only as `delete "members"` and the front end sends DELETE. Controller specs bypass routing, so this test would still pass if the DELETE route were missing or wired incorrectly. It should use `xhr :delete, :remove_member` so it matches the actual contract.

title: Public group members page now silently truncates to 50 members
body: The public `members` action used to return every member for non-automatic groups (and up to 200 for automatic groups). It now always applies a `limit` (default 50), but the only consumer that renders the public membership list, `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`, still iterates `members` with no pagination controls and `Group#findMembers` sends the default limit/offset. As a result any public group with more than 50 members silently shows only the first 50 and offers no way to load the rest. The admin page was given pagination in this PR, but the non-admin group page was not, so this is a regression for large groups. Either the public page needs a pager/see-more, or the old unlimited/200 behavior must be preserved for this endpoint.

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. This equals the correct ceiling except when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`: e.g. 50 members with limit 50 yields `floor(50/50)+1 = 2` pages, and 100 members yields 3 pages, even though there are only 1 and 2 real pages. Because `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to `totalPages`, the `next` action remains enabled on the real last page; clicking it sets `offset` to `user_count` and loads a completely empty page (the request returns zero members). The formula should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the existing `user_count == 0` guard).

title: Members endpoint response shape changed from array to {members, meta}
body: `GroupsController#members` previously rendered a bare array of serialized users (`render_serialized members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer`); it now renders `{ members: [...], meta: { total:, limit:, offset: } }`. The route `/groups/:name/members` is a public route, and any client other than the Ember app updated here (mobile apps, plugins, scripts) that expects a top-level array will break. If the shape change is intentional it should at least be called out as an API change, and ideally the old route/format kept or a versioned/new endpoint introduced.

title: limit/offset on public members endpoint are unbounded and can 500
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are taken directly from request params with no clamping. A caller can pass a very large `limit` to force the server to load and serialize an arbitrarily large result set on this unauthenticated-to-any-user-who-can-see-the-group endpoint, and a negative `offset` produces an `OFFSET -5` query that PostgreSQL rejects (HTTP 500). These should be validated/clamped (e.g. `offset = [params[:offset].to_i, 0].max`, `limit = params[:limit].to_i.clamp(1, 200)`).

title: New member routes and paginated members endpoint are untested at the routing/HTTP level
body: The `.add_members`/`.remove_member` specs call controller actions directly with `xhr`, which bypasses routing entirely, so the new routes (`delete/put "members" => groups#add_members/remove_member`) and the `params.require(:group_id)` / `params[:user_id]` contract are never exercised — a verb or `:group_id` vs `:id` mismatch would not be caught. Additionally the new behavior of `GroupsController#members` (the `{members, meta}` shape, `total`/`limit`/`offset` in `meta`, and the removal of the old 200-member automatic-group cap) has no controller spec at all. Add request specs covering the new admin routes and a `GroupsController#members` spec asserting the pagination meta and that limit/offset are honored.

title: New fallback behavior ships with no tests
body: This PR changes core translation resolution (custom `I18n.fallbacks`, on-demand loading of the fallback chain, removal of Rails' `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` in production/profile/cloud66) but adds no tests. The behavior is subtle and easy to regress: fallback ordering (user locale -> SiteSetting.default_locale -> :en), deduplication, behavior when the default locale is unavailable, and the interaction with the LRU cache in `I18n.translate` are all untested. A maintainer cannot verify that `I18n.t` for a key missing in the current locale now returns the default-locale/en string (and that missing keys still raise/return 'translation missing' when nothing exists). Add specs for these paths.

title: Fallback locales are only preloaded inside controller requests
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is invoked only from `ApplicationController#set_locale`, so the fallback chain (current locale, `SiteSetting.default_locale`, `:en`) is loaded only during web requests. Outside requests — background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console — `I18n.translate` (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68) loads only `config.locale`, and the `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` translation path calls `super` for fallback locales without triggering `load_locale` for them. Result: in those contexts a key missing from the active locale may resolve to 'translation missing' instead of the intended default-locale/`:en` string, because those locale files were never loaded in that process. Loading the fallback chain should happen centrally (e.g., in the patched `I18n.translate`/`ensure_loaded!`, or an initializer), not solely in a controller filter.

title: Inconsistent and fragile backend include target for fallbacks
body: Pluralization is mixed into `I18n::Backend::Simple` directly (line 5), but fallbacks are mixed into `I18n.backend.class` (line 9). This forces eager instantiation of `I18n.backend` at initializer time and, more importantly, means fallbacks are only attached to whichever backend class happens to be active during this initializer. If `I18n.backend` is later replaced (e.g., by a Chain backend in some environment or a future change), the `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` module silently drops off and fallbacks stop working with no error. Use the same explicit `I18n::Backend::Simple.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` form used for pluralization (or otherwise guarantee the included backend is the one actually used).

title: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but only overrides `[]`, breaking standard Fallbacks API
body: `I18n.fallbacks` is normally an `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`, which exposes `[]`, `[]=`, `key?`, `fetch`, `each`, `to_h`, `defaults`, etc. `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` stores no keys and only overrides `[]`, so any code (current or in future i18n gem internals) that iterates `I18n.fallbacks`, checks `key?`, or relies on the stored mapping will see an empty Hash and behave incorrectly. Subclass `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` and override `[]` instead, so the object remains a real fallbacks collection while still customizing the chain.

title: Fallback locales are not loaded for non-controller translation calls
body: The new fallback mechanism relies on ApplicationController#set_locale calling I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! to load all fallback locale files. However, I18n.translate still only calls load_locale for config.locale. Any translation performed outside a controller request—mailers, background jobs, rake tasks, console, or an explicit I18n.with_locale—will not have SiteSetting.default_locale or :en translations loaded. The I18n::Backend::Fallbacks backend will try those locales, find no loaded translations, and still raise/return a missing translation even though the fallback should have resolved it. Fallback loading needs to happen in translate/load_locale itself, not only in the controller before_filter.

title: Translation cache key ignores the dynamic fallback chain
body: The LRU cache key is built only from the key, current locale, and backend id. A cached value may actually have come from a fallback locale, and the fallback chain depends on the runtime value of SiteSetting.default_locale. If an admin changes the site default locale, previously cached fallback translations for a user's locale remain stale until evicted—e.g. a missing French key cached from the old English fallback will keep returning English after the site default switches to German. The cache key should include the fallback chain/default locale, or the cache should be cleared when the default locale changes.

title: No tests for fallback order or fallback loading
body: This PR adds non-trivial behavior: a custom fallback order, inclusion of I18n::Backend::Fallbacks, and lazy loading of fallback locale files. No tests are added to verify that a missing key in a user's locale falls back to SiteSetting.default_locale and then to English, or that fallback locales are actually loaded. This is easy to regress and affects user-visible strings.

title: Fallback locales are only preloaded inside ApplicationController, so fallbacks fail outside web requests
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only invoked from `ApplicationController#set_locale`, so the fallback chain returned by `FallbackLocaleList` (current locale, `SiteSetting.default_locale`, `:en`) is only loaded into the `Simple` backend during HTTP requests. Any translation performed outside a controller — mailers, background jobs, rake tasks, `rails runner`, console — goes through `I18n.translate`, which only calls `load_locale(config.locale)`. Because the default/`:en` files were never loaded, the `Fallbacks` backend's `super(fallback, ...)` lookups find nothing and the fallback silently does not happen. For a server-side fallback feature this means the behavior only works for requests; e.g. notification emails generated in jobs will still show missing translations instead of falling back to the site default/English. The fallback locales should be ensured-loaded from `translate`/`load_locale` (or lazily from the backend) rather than only from the controller filter.

title: Fallback resolver depends on SiteSetting (DB) and can raise during boot/CLI
body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym`. This method is invoked by the i18n `Fallbacks` backend on every translation miss, so the global fallback resolver now depends on `SiteSetting`/the database. During boot or CLI tasks where the `site_settings` table or `SiteSetting` is not ready (e.g. fresh `rake db:migrate`, `assets:precompile`, early initializers, `rails runner` before DB connection), a translation miss will call into `SiteSetting.default_locale` and can raise instead of simply returning a missing translation. In addition, `.compact` is applied after `.to_sym`, so it cannot protect against a nil `default_locale`; if `SiteSetting.default_locale` ever returns nil this raises `NoMethodError` before `compact` can filter it. Guard/normalize the value and avoid depending on the DB from this hot global resolver.

title: Fallbacks are now enabled globally (including test/development) with no tests
body: Previously `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` existed only in `config/environments/production.rb`, `config/environments/profile.rb`, and `config/cloud/cloud66/files/production.rb`; this initializer turns fallbacks on for every environment. In development/test, where fallbacks were previously off, missing translations will now silently resolve to the site default/English instead of surfacing, which can mask i18n regressions and break any tests that assert on missing-translation behavior. The PR also adds no tests exercising the new fallback chain (user locale -> site default -> English) or the new `ensure_loaded!` path, so this behavior change is unverified.

title: ensure_loaded! mutates shared @loaded_locales outside the LOAD_MUTEX
body: `ensure_loaded!` does `@loaded_locales ||= []` and then reads `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` without holding `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` mutates the same array under the mutex and `reload!` replaces it (`@loaded_locales = []`). On the first concurrent requests multiple threads can each evaluate `@loaded_locales ||= []` against a nil/being-reset value, creating/assigning competing arrays, so previously-recorded loaded locales can be dropped and files reloaded redundantly; a reader can also observe a half-updated array. The nil-init and membership check should be done inside the existing mutex (or `load_locale` should be relied on for the synchronized check).

title: Denial cache key omits identity type, so anonymous and renderer collide on UID 0
body: The new denial-cache key is built from `checkReq.UserUID`, which for different identity types can be the same string. Anonymous subjects arrive as `anonymous:0` (UID `0`) and render-service subjects as `render:0` (UID `0`), so both produce the same key `namespace.perm_0_<action>_<name>_<parent>`. If an anonymous user is denied access to a dashboard (caching a denial under UID `0`), a renderer check for the same dashboard/action/folder within the 30s TTL takes the early `return &authzv1.CheckResponse{Allowed:false}` at line 120 and is denied even though `getRendererPermissions` grants `*` for `dashboards:read`/`folders:read`. Consequence: image/PDF rendering intermittently fails to read dashboards whenever an anonymous denial was recently cached for the same resource. The key must include the identity type (and ideally use the resolved identity, not the raw subject UID).

title: Denial cache is not invalidated on permission changes, re-introducing the creator-lockout in a race
body: The denial is cached with `shortCacheTTL` (30s) and there is no hook to evict `permDenialCache` when permissions are granted (new dashboard/folder owned by creator, team/dashboard permission added, etc.). The PR's goal is to let a creator fetch a resource they just created; if the first `Check` for the new resource runs before the permission row is visible to `GetUserPermissions` (propagation/commit delay), that first check returns false and stores a denial keyed by the resource. The creator's retries are then served by the denial cache for up to 30s, so they still cannot access the newly created dashboard/folder during the window — the exact symptom being fixed. Consider invalidating denial entries on writes or using a much shorter TTL for denials of just-created resources.

title: Denial-cache write path and cache-served denial are untested
body: `TestService_CacheCheck`'s "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" seeds `permDenialCache` directly, so it only exercises the read path. Nothing verifies that a real denial (line 154 of service.go) writes to `permDenialCache`, nor that a second identical `Check` is subsequently answered from the denial cache without hitting the store (e.g., asserting `store.calls` stays constant on the second call). The new write path and the intended performance benefit are therefore unprotected against regressions.

title: permissionCacheUsage conflates the denial cache with the permission cache
body: The `permissionCacheUsage` metric is incremented on a denial-cache hit (line 118) as if it were a permission-cache hit, and on a permission-cache hit that ultimately denies the request it is recorded as `"false"` (line 137). Since the metric is meant to measure the permission cache, mixing in the new denial cache makes dashboards/alerts on cache effectiveness misleading (denial hits look like permission-cache hits, and permission-cache hits that deny look like misses). Consider a distinct counter for the denial cache or only recording permission-cache outcomes.

title: Denial cache is never invalidated and can re-deny newly granted (e.g. newly created) resources for 30s
body: The new permission-denial cache is written whenever a full DB re-query returns not-allowed (service.go:154) and is consulted at the top of Check (service.go:117) to short-circuit to `Allowed:false` without any re-validation. No code path ever deletes these keys on permission changes; they only expire via `shortCacheTTL` (30s). Consequence: once a check is denied, a subsequent grant (including the exact "creator of a just-created dashboard/folder" scenario this PR targets, e.g. a check that runs before the grant is committed) keeps returning `Allowed:false` for up to 30s, reintroducing the bug the PR is meant to fix. Also, because the cache hit is decided by key presence rather than the stored value, any future code that stores `false` under this key would still deny. Consider invalidating denial keys on permission writes (or making this cache consistent with the freshness guarantee of the allow path).

title: Every denied check now performs a full DB permission query
body: When the cached permission map is present but does not contain the requested resource, `checkPermission` returns false and Check falls through to `s.getIdentityPermissions` (service.go:139). Since the cache read inside `getUserPermissions` was removed, this path always executes a full DB query (user identifiers, basic role, teams, permissions). The only thing that prevents a DB query on a repeat denied check is the per-resource denial cache. Consequence: the first check for each distinct resource a user cannot access now hits the DB, whereas previously the cached permission map short-circuited it. For denial-heavy traffic or checks over many inaccessible resources, this is a substantial increase in DB load. Consider recording that a cached permission set is known-complete/current so genuine denials can be served without a DB round-trip.

title: Ambiguous denial-cache key can collide across distinct resources
body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` joins namespace, user, action, name and parent with '_' without escaping, so different tuples can produce the same key. For example (action="a", name="b_c", parent="d") and (action="a_b", name="c", parent="d") both produce `...perm_<uid>_a_b_c_d`. Folder/dashboard UIDs and parent UIDs can contain underscores, so two distinct resources can map to the same denial key. Consequence: a denial cached for one resource is then served for a different resource the user may be allowed to access (up to the TTL). Use an unescapable delimiter or length-prefix/hash the components.

title: List has no DB fallback for a stale permission map, so newly created resources are omitted
body: `List` only re-queries the DB when `getCachedIdentityPermissions` returns an error, i.e. when the entire per-action permission map is absent. When the map is present but stale, `List` builds its response purely from that cached map, so scopes for dashboards/folders created after the map was cached are omitted for up to `shortCacheTTL` (30s). If the reported issue is observed through listing (new resource not appearing right after creation), this path remains unfixed: only `Check` received the DB fallback on a cache miss. Consider applying the same freshness handling to `List`.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type, so anonymous and renderer checks collide
body: userPermDenialCacheKey is built from namespace, subject UID, action, resource name, and folder, but not the identity type. Anonymous and renderer subjects both resolve to user UID "0" (for example anonymous:0 and render:0), and users and service accounts can also share a UID. A denial written for one principal is therefore returned for another principal on the same action/resource/folder. Concretely, an anonymous Check for dashboards:read/dash1 stores key org-12.perm_0_dashboards:read_dash1_, and a later renderer Check for the same dashboard hits that key and is denied without consulting renderer permissions, breaking rendering. Include the identity type (or full subject type) in the denial key.

title: Denial cache key is ambiguous because fields are joined with underscores
body: The denial key concatenates user UID, action, resource name, and parent folder with literal "_" separators. Grafana UIDs can contain underscores and resource name/folder are caller-controlled, so different tuples can produce the same key. For example, name "a_b" with parent "c" and name "a" with parent "b_c" both produce the same suffix. A denial cached for one resource would then deny an unrelated resource. Use length-prefixed or escaped components, or hash a structured key.

title: Every distinct denied resource name causes a fresh permission DB query
body: When cached identity permissions exist but do not allow the requested resource, Check falls through to getIdentityPermissions and queries the permission store. The denial cache only remembers the exact (action, name, parent) tuple, so callers can send checks for arbitrary distinct dashboard/folder UIDs (for example anonymous probes of /api/dashboards/uid/<random>) and force one permission DB query per UID. Previously these cache-hit checks were served without touching the DB. This is a DB-load/DoS regression; consider coalescing or marking a user/action as freshly queried rather than falling back per resource name.

title: Tests seed the denial cache manually and never verify Check populates it
body: The new denial-cache test manually calls permDenialCache.Set before invoking Check. There is no test that performs a Check returning false from the permission store and then asserts the denial is written, nor a test that a denial for one identity type does not affect another identity type. As a result, a regression where Check never writes denials, writes them under a mismatched key, or collides anonymous and renderer entries would pass the current test suite.

title: Delete and Pause menu items never render in the alert list view because they are gated on rulerRule
body: The Delete item is rendered under the condition `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165), and the Pause item under `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && ...` (line 123). This PR changes the list view so that GrafanaRuleListItem -> RuleActionsButtons.V2 -> AlertRuleMenu is given only `promRule` (rulerRule is undefined; see GrafanaRuleListItem's `actions: <RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule}.../>`). With `rulerRule` undefined both guards are false, so Delete and Pause disappear from the list even when the new prom-rule abilities make `canDelete`/`canPause` true. This is a regression from the previous GrafanaGroupLoader/GrafanaRuleLoader behavior, which loaded the ruler rule and passed it down. The guard is also stale: in RuleActionsButtons.V2 `handleDelete={() => showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)}` ignores the rulerRule argument entirely, so Delete can be rendered and handled without a rulerRule. PauseMenuItem only needs the ruler rule object to perform its mutation, so if pausing must stay functional in the list it needs to fetch the ruler rule on demand rather than silently hide the item.

title: Grafana branch of the rules list lost its React key
body: In the `rules.map(...)` render, the `origin === 'grafana'` branch previously rendered `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ... />` but now renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} ... />` without a `key`. The surrounding `datasource` and default branches still pass `key={key}`. Rendering a mapped array without keys produces React reconciliation warnings and, more importantly, lets React reuse component instances between rows. Each row contains RuleActionsButtons.V2, which keeps local state (delete modal, silence drawer, clone redirect); during infinite-scroll appends or list mutations this can cause state to bleed across rows (for example a delete/silence dialog belonging to the wrong rule). Add `key={key}` to the GrafanaRuleListItem.

title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
body: `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` previously computed `const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group);`. The refactor to take a `RulerRuleDTO | undefined` plus a `RuleGroupIdentifierV2` no longer has access to the group object, so it now hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` (line 245, with a TODO). Federated rule groups (Mimir Enterprise cross-tenant federation, identified by `source_tenants`) can only be modified through the ruler on the owning tenant and were intentionally made read-only in Grafana by feeding `isFederated` into the `immutableRule` calculation. With this change `immutableRule` is false for federated rules, so Update/Pause/Restore/Delete abilities become allowed for them and users can attempt edits that Grafana cannot correctly persist. The group's `source_tenants` needs to be threaded through to keep federated rules immutable.

title: Test grants delete permission but asserts Delete is absent, locking in the deletion regression
body: The `should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked` test grants `AlertingRuleDelete` (and true folder delete access in `setFolderAccessControl`) and then asserts the menu contains exactly 4 items (`expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)`) - silence, copy link, duplicate, export - i.e. it explicitly expects the Delete item to be missing. This encodes the bug where Delete/Pause are hidden because the list view no longer supplies a rulerRule (see AlertRuleMenu). Because of this assertion, fixing Delete in the list will make the test fail, so it should instead assert that the Delete menu item is present when the user has the delete permission.

title: Pause and Delete actions never render when the menu is used with promRule only (list view)
body: The PR makes `AlertRuleMenu` usable with only a `promRule` from the new list view, and adds `grafanaPauseAbility`/`grafanaDeleteAbility` so `canPause`/`canDelete` can become true in that case. However both menu items are still gated on a `rulerRule`: the pause item at line 123 requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and the delete item at line 165 requires `rulerRule && ...`. The new list components (`GrafanaGroupLoader` and `FilterView`) render `GrafanaRuleListItem` -> `RuleActionsButtons.V2` with only `promRule` and never pass a `rulerRule`, so `rulerRule` is always undefined there. As a result, in the new (prom-only) list view the user can no longer Pause or Delete a rule even when the computed `canPause`/`canDelete` (from the Grafana prom abilities) are true and `handleDelete` is wired up. The `canPause`/`canDelete` computations and `handleDelete` prop are effectively dead in that view. Either drop the `rulerRule` guards (the delete handler and `MenuItemPauseRule` should use the prom rule / identifier) or stop computing those abilities for prom-only consumers.

title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable after delegating to useAllRulerRuleAbilities
body: Before this change `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` from the `CombinedRule` group and used it to mark federated rule groups as immutable (no Edit/Delete/Pause). The new implementation delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `isFederated = false` (line 245, with a `// TODO: Add support for federated rules` comment) because a `RulerRuleDTO` alone does not carry the group's `source_tenants`. Any component still consuming `useAlertRuleAbility`/`useAlertRuleAbilities` (e.g. RuleDetails) will therefore show Edit/Delete/Pause affordances for federated Mimir rule groups, which are read-only, leading to actions that the backend rejects. The federation check needs to be preserved (pass the group or the federated flag through to the ruler-abilities hook).

title: Missing React `key` on GrafanaRuleListItem in the rule list map
body: In the `switch (origin)` inside `rules.map(...)` the `grafana` branch renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` without a `key`, even though the loop destructures `key` from `ruleWithOrigin` and the `datasource`/`default` branches both pass `key={key}`. This triggers the React "each child in a list should have a unique key" warning and forces index-based reconciliation for these rows, whose children (`RuleActionsButtons`) hold per-row state (silence drawer, clone redirect). It should pass `key={key}` like the other branches.

title: View link no longer carries returnTo, breaking back-navigation from the rule view
body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader`'s `GrafanaRuleListItem` built the view URL with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo: createReturnTo() })`. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem` builds it as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo`, so navigating from the list into a rule and pressing the "back" control in the rule viewer will no longer return the user to the list/filter they came from. This is a behavior regression from the previous implementation.

title: Stale comment/variable name referencing ruler preloading that was removed
body: The ruler `prefetch` call was removed from `getGroupsAndProvideCache`, but the surrounding comment still says "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX" and the local variable is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload`. Since only Prometheus groups are cached now, the comment and name are misleading about what the code does and should be updated to reflect that only the Prometheus group cache is being warmed.

title: Grafana list items rendered without a React key
body: In the `rules.map` switch in `FilterViewResults`, the `'grafana'` branch now returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` without a `key` prop. Every other branch (`'datasource'`, default) still passes `key={key}`. The loop already computes a stable `key` (getRuleKey) and the old `GrafanaRuleLoader` was passed `key={key}`, so this is a regression. A `map` that returns elements without keys triggers React 'Each child in a list should have a unique key' warnings and forces reconciliation by array index, which can cause stale state/misrendering when the list grows or reorders. Add `key={key}` to the `GrafanaRuleListItem` element.

title: Federated rule-group detection silently removed from useAllAlertRuleAbilities
body: The refactored (deprecated) `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`. The old implementation computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` from the CombinedRule's group; the new shared `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` (with a TODO) because it only receives a rule and a group identifier, not the group's `source_tenants`. As a result, federated Mimir/Metrics-Enterprise rule groups (which must be treated as immutable) are no longer marked immutable in any caller of `useAllAlertRuleAbilities`, so the UI will offer Edit/Delete/Pause for rules that the backend considers read-only. This is a behavioral regression for existing consumers that still use this hook.

title: Delete action is never shown for Grafana rules in the ruler-less list view
body: The Delete menu item is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule` (`handleDelete(rulerRule, groupIdentifier)`). In the new list view (`RuleActionsButtons.V2`, used by `GrafanaRuleListItem`), only `promRule` is passed and `rulerRule` is always `undefined`, so the Delete item never renders even though `canDelete` is now correctly computed from the prom-rule abilities. This means users can no longer delete Grafana-managed rules from the alert list (the GrafanaGroupLoader test that grants `AlertingRuleDelete` and asserts only 4 menu items confirms it). `RuleActionsButtons.V2` already ignores the arguments and calls `showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)`, so the `rulerRule` requirement in this gate (and the `handleDelete` signature) should be relaxed to use the identifier for the list-view path if delete is meant to remain available.

title: View link no longer carries returnTo for Grafana rules
body: The `href` for the rule is built as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view')`, dropping the `returnTo` query parameter that the previous `GrafanaRuleLoader`/`GrafanaRuleListItem` added via `createReturnTo()` (`createRelativeUrl(path, { returnTo })`). Consequently, navigating from the rule list/group view into a rule's detail page loses the origin, so the detail page's back navigation no longer returns the user to the filtered/hierarchical list. If the returnTo behavior is still desired, the `returnTo` parameter should be restored.

title: Early interpolation bypasses the $__range splitting guard
body: `runSplitQuery` now interpolates each query via `applyTemplateVariables` before passing it to `querySupportsSplitting`. That check intentionally calls `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to avoid splitting queries that use `$__range`, because each split chunk would otherwise evaluate the range variable against the wrong range. After interpolation, `$__range` is replaced by a literal duration, so `isQueryWithRangeVariable` no longer matches and these queries are split. Each chunk then uses the full-range duration instead of the chunk range, producing overlapping/duplicated results for range-based aggregations. The range-variable check must inspect the original expression, or interpolation must happen after that classification.

title: Shard path interpolates every target twice
body: `runShardSplitQuery` now calls `applyTemplateVariables` on each target, then passes the already-interpolated targets into `runSplitQuery`, which also calls `applyTemplateVariables` on its targets. The updated shard test asserts five interpolation calls, confirming this double application. This is not safe to assume idempotent: `applyTemplateVariables` receives `request.filters`, so ad-hoc filters can be appended on both passes, and variable values that themselves contain `$...` patterns can be expanded a second time, changing the LogQL sent to Loki. Interpolation should occur once at the entry point, or `runSplitQuery` needs an option to skip interpolation when its caller has already done it.

title: $__range guard is evaluated after interpolation
body: runSplitQuery now interpolates each target before calling `partition(...)`/`querySupportsSplitting`, but `querySupportsSplitting` relies on `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to keep `$__range` queries out of time splitting. Once `applyTemplateVariables` has run, `$__range` has already been substituted (with the full request range), so the check no longer sees the placeholder and those queries are split anyway. The code’s own comment states these queries must not be split because each split uses a different time range; replacing the variable once at the start and then splitting can therefore produce incorrect results. The predicate should be evaluated against the original target expression before interpolation (or the raw flag should be carried through), with a regression test for a `$__range` query.

title: Targets are interpolated twice in shard splitting
body: runShardSplitQuery interpolates every target here, then `splitQueriesByStreamShard` calls `runSplitQuery`, which now also interpolates all targets. The shard test was updated to expect `applyTemplateVariables` to be called 5 times for a single original target, confirming the double pass. Template interpolation is not guaranteed to be idempotent: variable values containing `$`/variable syntax can be expanded a second time, and any non-idempotent rewriting is applied twice after the shard selector has already been injected. Interpolation should happen at one entry point only: either pass already-interpolated targets to a non-interpolating `runSplitQuery` variant, or move interpolation up so shard splitting does not pre-interpolate before calling it.

title: Shard path now interpolates every target twice
body: `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates each target with `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` here, then passes those already-interpolated targets as sub-requests into `runSplitQuery` (line 163). Since this PR, `runSplitQuery` also interpolates its targets (querySplitting.ts:299), so in the sharding path every target goes through `applyTemplateVariables`/`templateSrv.replace` twice. The updated test 'Interpolates queries before running' asserts `applyTemplateVariables` was called 5 times for a single query (1 here + 1 per each of the 4 shard sub-requests), which confirms the duplication; before this PR the shard path interpolated exactly once. A second replace pass over already-resolved text is usually a no-op, but it corrupts expressions whose interpolated values themselves contain `$name`/`${name}` sequences (e.g. a label value or regex containing `$`) and it doubles templating work. Guard against this, e.g. add an option so `runSplitQuery` skips interpolation when the caller already did it, or stop pre-interpolating in the shard path and expose the selector needed for `fetchLabelValues` another way.

title: $__range splitting guard is untested after interpolation
body: Interpolation now runs before the `partition(queries, (query) => !querySupportsSplitting(query))` split. `querySupportsSplitting` relies on `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to keep queries that use `$__range` out of splitting, precisely because `$__range` is supposed to be resolved from each query's time range. There is no test covering a `$__range` query after interpolation. If the datasource's `applyTemplateVariables` resolves `$__range`/`$__range_ms`/`$__range_s` from `request.scopedVars`, `isQueryWithRangeVariable` will no longer find the variable, the guard silently stops protecting the query, and it gets time-sliced with `$__range` computed per sub-range rather than for the full range. Add a test asserting a `$__range` query still lands in the non-splitting partition after interpolation.

title: Plugin request logs no longer include traceID
body: The previous implementation explicitly appended the tracing ID from `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` to every "Plugin Request Completed" log. This diff removes that block, and the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` only adds `endpoint`, `pluginId`, optional datasource fields, and `uname` to the context attributes. Unless another layer injects traceID, plugin request completion logs lose the field needed to correlate logs with traces.

title: New contextual logger middleware is untested
body: The only test change in this PR is updating the metrics middleware constructor call. There is no test that verifies the newly extracted `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` actually enriches the context with `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, and `uname`, nor that `LoggerMiddleware` now emits those contextual fields via `FromContext`. A regression where context attributes are dropped or not propagated would pass CI.

title: FromContext silently discards context when the concrete type assertion fails
body: `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` returns the infrastructure `log.Logger` interface, but the wrapper asserts it to `*log.ConcreteLogger` and falls back to `d.New()` if that assertion fails. If the infrastructure logger returns a context-aware wrapper or any other implementation, the fallback returns a logger without the supplied context, silently dropping all contextual fields. Since `LoggerMiddleware` now relies on this method for plugin request fields, that failure mode would make contextual logging appear enabled while losing the data.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, discarding recorded log calls
body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver, so anything logged through `FromContext` is recorded on a discarded logger and is invisible to a test holding the original `*TestLogger`.
