title: Per-client resource shadows all-clients permissions
body: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) looks up the resource for the specific client; only if that resource is null does it fall back to the "Clients" all-resource. This means that as soon as any per-client resource exists (e.g. created because someone once granted VIEW on that client), all permissions granted via the all-clients resource are ignored for that client. Concretely, an administrator who was granted MANAGE on all clients via an all-clients permission will lose MANAGE (and CONFIGURE, which delegates to canManage) for a client that merely has a separate per-client VIEW permission. The two resources should be evaluated with OR semantics, or the all-clients grant must still be consulted when the per-client evaluation does not grant the requested scope.

title: Missing null check on all-clients resource can cause NPE
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, scope), AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) can return null (e.g. if the realm does not support the schema, or the "Clients" all-resource was never created). The returned value is then passed to policyStore.findByResource(server, null) and, if non-empty, to new ResourcePermission(null, resource.getScopes(), ...), which will throw. The sibling method hasPermission(String) correctly guards with `if (resource == null) return false;`, but this method does not, so a missing all-clients resource results in a 500 instead of a permission denial.

title: Existing realms never receive the new Clients resource and scopes
body: init() returns immediately when the admin-permissions client already exists. Realms whose admin-permissions client was created before the CLIENTS resource type was introduced will therefore never get the new "Clients" resource, nor the new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) added to resourceServerRep.setScopes(...). Creating a client permission in such a realm will then fail — either the per-client resource creation throws ModelException("No scopes found.") because getOrCreateResource cannot find the scope, or scope validation in getScope rejects the request — and evaluation will hit the null all-clients resource path. A migration/backfill is needed to create any missing schema scopes/resources for realms that already have the client.

title: getResourceName does not resolve Clients resources
body: getResourceName special-cases only the USERS resource type (returning "All users" for the type resource and the username for a per-user resource). For the newly added CLIENTS resource type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Per-client FGAP resources are named with the client's internal UUID (see getOrCreateResource/resolveClient) and do not set a display name, so listings of client permissions will show a blank/incorrect name instead of the client's clientId. Add a CLIENTS branch that resolves the client (and an "All clients" label for the type resource) analogously to the USERS branch.

title: Listener guard does not prevent V2 UnsupportedOperationException
body: The listener body is now gated only on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1). But when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is also enabled, management(...) returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled(...) throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). In a realm configured with both features, removing a client (ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent), role, or group will therefore hit role()/clients()/groups().setPermissionsEnabled(...) and fail. The guard should also exclude the V2 case (e.g. skip the cleanup when V2 is enabled) so client/role/group deletion keeps working.

title: Upgraded realms never receive the new Clients resource type and scopes
body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already non-null. A realm that had FGAP V2 enabled before this change already has that client, but its resource server only contains the Users resource/scopes; after upgrading, the 'Clients' resource and the configure/map-roles-client-scope/map-roles-composite scopes are never created. As a result, creating a client permission fails in getScope() with ModelValidationException("Scope [configure] does not exist."), getOrCreateResource() for a client throws ModelException("No scopes found."), and ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission() dereferences the null Resource returned by getResourceTypeResource() when calling policyStore.findByResource(server, null). init() must reconcile and add missing resource types/scopes instead of returning when the client exists.

title: getClientsWithPermission cannot find per-client resources
body: getClientsWithPermission() iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). However, the per-client resources built by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() are created via resourceStore.create(...) and never get their type set to 'Clients' (only the 'all-clients' resource created in init() has that type and its name is 'Clients'). Consequently per-client grants are never returned; at best the single all-clients resource is evaluated and its name 'Clients' (not a client id) is added to the result. Any caller that uses this method to filter/return the clients an admin can act on receives wrong data. The fix is either to set the resource type when creating per-client resources, or to iterate the actual client resources and evaluate each.

title: V2 client role-mapping checks ignore the manage-clients realm role and manage scope
body: canMapRoles(), canMapCompositeRoles() and canMapClientScopeRoles() only evaluate the fine-grained MAP_ROLES / MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE / MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE permissions. Unlike every other method in this class (canManage, canManageClientScopes, canView, canConfigure), they never check root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) nor canManage(client). An administrator holding only the built-in manage-clients role (the normal case, no fine-grained permissions) will therefore be denied adding/removing client roles and composites once V2 is enabled, which is a functional regression versus V1 and is inconsistent with the manage-implies-configure/view behavior implemented in this same class. These methods must also honor the built-in role and/or the manage scope.

title: UnsupportedOperationException thrown from authorization paths that are actually invoked
body: setPermissionsEnabled()/isPermissionsEnabled() and canExchangeTo() throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning false/no-op. These are reachable: AdminPermissions.registerListener() calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on ClientRemovedEvent (and roles()/groups() equivalents) whenever Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled; since V1 is enabled by default and can be on together with V2, deleting a client/role/group in a V2 realm will raise UnsupportedOperationException and abort the deletion. Conversely, when only V2 is enabled the listener is skipped entirely, so no cleanup of the deleted entity's resource/policies occurs. canExchangeTo() is invoked by the token-exchange authorization flow and will surface as HTTP 500 rather than a proper denial. These methods should return false/no-op (or be implemented), and the listener guard/cleanup should handle V2.

title: Per-client resource lookup uses the wrong owner
body: The per-client permission lookup passes `server.getId()` as the resource owner, but `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates these resources with `resourceServer.getClientId()`. A resource server id and its clientId are different values, so this lookup normally misses. Per-client grants are then ignored (or only the all-clients fallback is evaluated), which breaks permissions such as `MANAGE` or `VIEW` granted for a single client.

title: Per-client resources cannot be found by type
body: `getClientsWithPermission` queries resources with type `Clients`, but `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates individual client resources with `resourceStore.create(...)` and never calls `setType(CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. Those resources therefore have no type and are not returned here. An admin with only a per-client grant will not get that client in the filtered client list. The all-clients resource is also added to the returned set under its name `Clients`, which is not a client id.

title: Client resource names are not resolved
body: `getResourceName` only special-cases the `Users` resource type. For `Clients` it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, but resources created by `getOrCreateResource` have no display name, and the all-clients resource is named `Clients`. Permission/resource listings for client permissions will therefore show null or unhelpful names instead of the client id or a meaningful "All clients" label.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not migrated to the Clients schema
body: `init` returns immediately when `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient()` is already non-null. Realms that initialized the admin-permissions client before this change will never receive the new `Clients` resource type, the `Clients` all-resource, or the new scopes (`configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, `map-roles-composite`). Creating a Clients permission on such a realm fails in `getScope` (scope does not exist) or hits a missing all-clients resource during evaluation. The schema change needs an upgrade/migration path for existing clients.

title: Missing Clients all-resource can cause a null dereference
body: When no per-client resource exists, `getResourceTypeResource` can return null if the all-clients `Clients` resource is missing (for example an existing realm that has not been migrated to the new schema). The result is then passed to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`, which can throw instead of denying access. The code should guard against a null fallback and return false.

title: Listener can call unsupported V2 cleanup methods
body: The cleanup listener is gated only by `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1). If V2 is also enabled, `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`, and the client-removal branch calls `clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)`. `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides that method to throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, so deleting a client can fail with a 500 when both features are enabled. The listener must also account for V2, or the V2 implementation must provide a no-op for this cleanup path.

title: Client role-mapping checks ignore legacy manage-clients and MANAGE grants
body: `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only check explicit `MAP_ROLES*` scopes and never call `super` or `canManage(client)`. Under V2, a caller who has the legacy `MANAGE_CLIENTS` role (which `canManage(ClientModel)` still honors) or a `MANAGE` grant on the client will be denied client role mapping, unlike V1 and the other client operations. These methods should include the same manage fallback unless V2 intentionally removes that behavior.

title: Reassigning exit code 4 breaks existing automation
body: This changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and reuses 4 for FEATURE_DISABLED. The exit codes are the documented programmatic contract of update-compatibility, so scripts built against the previous release will now treat a recreate result (3) differently and will interpret 4 as feature-disabled rather than recreate-required. Even for a preview tool, this is a breaking contract change; preserving 4 for recreate and allocating a new code for FEATURE_DISABLED would avoid the break.

title: New exit-code paths are not asserted
body: The new feature-disabled path returns CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4), and the recreate path now returns 3, but the tests only assert stderr text. testFeatureNotEnabled asserts the error message and testWrongVersions asserts the incompatibility message, but neither checks the process exit code. A bug in picocli.exit or a future change to the constants could silently break the documented exit-code contract. Add assertEquals(4, cliResult.exitCode()) to testFeatureNotEnabled and assertEquals(3, result.exitCode()) to testWrongVersions.

title: Warning overstates when the rolling-updates feature is required
body: The caution says the Operator will fail unless `rolling-updates` is enabled, but the PR's own UpgradeTest runs the default strategy case (`spec.update` not set) without enabling the feature and expects deployments and upgrades to work. The feature is only required when `spec.update` is configured. Scope the warning to that case so users do not believe an existing CR must enable a preview feature just to keep the operator running.

title: Renumbering RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 breaks the documented exit-code contract
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was 4 and is now changed to 3, while 4 is reused for the new FEATURE_DISABLED constant. The user guide (and this PR's own docs) explicitly instructs automation to rely solely on the command's exit code, so any pipeline or external caller that treated exit code 4 as 'recreate required' will now receive 3 for that case and 4 for 'feature disabled' — a silent behavioural break. Introducing FEATURE_DISABLED as a new value (e.g. 5) and leaving recreate at 4 would have preserved the contract. Also verify that all internal consumers reference the constant rather than a hard-coded 4, since a literal would now be misinterpreted.

title: New exit code 4 and renumbered exit code 3 are never asserted
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the printed error string and does not assert that the command exits with FEATURE_DISABLED (4). Likewise testWrongVersions only asserts the error message and never checks the recreate exit code, which this PR just changed from 4 to 3. Since the documented contract is that consumers rely only on the exit code, the two values that matter most for automation are untested; a regression in either the feature-disabled path or the recreate path (e.g. a wrong picocli.exit value) would not be caught.

title: Caution says the operator fails without rolling-updates, contradicting the default-strategy test
body: The new [CAUTION] states the feature rolling-updates must be enabled or the Operator will fail. But UpgradeTest#createInitialDeployment returns without enabling the feature whenever updateStrategy is null (the default '<not set>' strategy), and both testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount expect that default deployment to succeed (recreate on image change, rolling on config change). So the operator demonstrably does not fail in the default case. The caution should be scoped to using the new update.strategy field rather than implying every deployment needs the preview feature, otherwise operators are misled into enabling a preview flag unnecessarily.

title: Caution overstates when rolling-updates feature is required
body: The caution says the Operator will fail unless `rolling-updates` is enabled. The updated UpgradeTest only adds the feature to the CR for explicit `spec.update.strategy` values; for the default (`strategy == null`) it returns before enabling the feature and still expects successful rolling/recreate behavior in `testImageChange[null]` and `testCacheMaxCount[null]`. Either the requirement only applies when `spec.update` is set and the caution should say so, or those tests are missing the required feature and are not exercising the documented gate.

title: testMissingOptionOnSave can pass when feature gate exits early
body: The test only asserts that `Missing required argument` is absent. With the new feature check in `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()`, a run where `--features=rolling-updates` is not recognized exits with the feature-disabled error before option validation, and this assertion still passes. The test should assert that the metadata command actually ran, for example no feature-disabled error, exit code 0, or metadata output, otherwise it no longer verifies that `--file` is optional.

title: Documented exit codes 3 and 4 are not asserted
body: The new documented contract has exit code 4 for feature-disabled and changes recreate from 4 to 3. `testFeatureNotEnabled` only checks the error text, and `testWrongVersions` only checks the incompatibility message; neither asserts the exit code. A regression that prints the right text but returns the wrong code would go unnoticed, despite the exit code being the scriptable contract described in `update-compatibility.adoc`.

title: VIEW permission is treated as MANAGE for groups
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() evaluates hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). The global canManage() check is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() through requireManage(), so a caller with only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource is allowed to create top-level groups. This is a privilege escalation; the method should require only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE.

title: Group view-permission lookup returns resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() iterates group resources but adds groupResource.getId() to the result and passes that same resource ID into hasPermission(). Callers expect actual group IDs: UsersResource.getUsersCount(realm, ..., getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()) and UsersResource.searchForUser() storing the set under UserModel.GROUPS both use the result as a group-ID filter. Because group resources are named by group ID (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup() returns group.getId()), this produces a set containing resource IDs that match no group, so user search/count filters can return no users or wrong results. It also means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are not evaluated, because findByName(server, resourceId) fails and falls back to the all-groups resource. Use the group ID/name from the resource and evaluate that.

title: Per-type resources are created without their resource type
body: In getOrCreateResource(), resources created for the schema resource types (now including Groups) are persisted with resourceStore.create(...) but resource.setType(resourceType) is never called. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() discovers group resources via resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). Group resources created when a group-specific permission is added will therefore have no type and will be skipped by that lookup, so group-specific VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are ignored by the group filtering path. Set the resource type when creating the resource.

title: Created test group is not cleaned up
body: testManageAllGroups() creates a group named "testGroup" through realmAdminClient but never registers it in realm.cleanup(), unlike the other groups created in this test class. Other tests assume exact group counts (for example testViewGroups() expects exactly two visible groups after granting view-all), so this leftover group can make the suite order-dependent and flaky. Register the group for cleanup or remove it at the end of the test.

title: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage with only view permission
body: The no-argument canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource: it calls hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). As a result a principal that only has the `view` scope passes requireManage(), which is invoked by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() before creating a top-level group. That lets a view-only administrator create/modify realm group structure, a privilege escalation. The per-group overload canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires only MANAGE, and manage should imply view but not the reverse. The VIEW branch here should be removed (and the interface Javadoc for canManage() that documents VIEW-or-MANAGE is likewise wrong).

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource ids, not group ids
body: The findByType callback receives a Resource and uses groupResource.getId() both for the permission lookup (hasPermission(...) internally does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)) and for the returned granted set. Per-group resources are named with the group id (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource sets name = group.getId()); getId() is the generated Resource UUID, not the group id. So hasPermission() looks up a resource named after a UUID, fails to find it, and silently falls back to the all-groups resource, while the set returned to callers contains resource UUIDs. Callers UsersResource.searchForUser()/getUsersCount() put this set into UserModel.GROUPS to filter users, so users visible only via a group permission are omitted from search/count, and an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS permission injects a bogus id into the filter. It should use groupResource.getName().

title: Per-object resources created by getOrCreateResource never get their type set
body: getOrCreateResource creates the per-user/per-group Resource via resourceStore.create(...) and updates its scopes but never calls resource.setType(resourceType); only the type-level resources created in init() (e.g. "Groups") get a type. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission relies on resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) to enumerate per-group resources. Because per-group resources are created without a type, findByType only finds the single "Groups" type-level resource, so per-group view-members/manage-members permissions are never seen and group-based user filtering cannot work. The created resource should have resource.setType(resourceType).

title: requireManageMembers Javadoc references the wrong method
body: The Javadoc on requireManageMembers(GroupModel) states it throws when {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} is false, but the implementation delegates to canManageMembers(GroupModel). The link is wrong and will mislead maintainers into thinking a different permission is checked; it should reference canManageMembers.

title: Existing realms never receive the new Groups scopes/resources
body: Adding Groups to SCHEMA is not applied to realms that already have an admin-permissions client. init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is non-null, so existing V2 realms keep only the old Users/Clients scopes and all-resource resources. Group scopes such as view-members and the all-groups resource will be missing; creating group permissions then fails in getOrCreateResource with 'No scopes found' (or getScope throws), and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission can evaluate a null all-groups resource. This needs an upgrade/migration path or an ensure-missing-scopes/resources update.

title: Per-group resources are created without a resource type
body: getOrCreateResource creates a resource for a group and updates its scopes, but never calls resource.setType(resourceType). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission enumerates group grants with resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...), so per-group resources created here are invisible to that lookup (only the type-tagged 'Groups' all-resource is returned). As a result group-scoped member permissions cannot be found for user search/listing. Set the resource type when creating the resource.

title: Group member permission lookup uses authz resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission the callback calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...), but hasPermission treats its first argument as a group id and looks it up with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). For a per-group resource the resource name is the group id, not the resource id, so the lookup falls back to the all-groups resource (or fails), and the method adds groupResource.getId() (an authz resource id) to the granted set. UsersResource then puts those ids into UserModel.GROUPS, so per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants are ignored and an all-groups grant can make user search return no users. Use groupResource.getName() (the group id) or evaluate the resource directly, and add the group id, not the resource id.

title: canManage() grants group management with only VIEW scope
body: The global canManage() returns true when the caller has only VIEW on all groups because it evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup calls auth.groups().requireManage() before creating a top-level group, so a caller with view-only all-groups permission can create groups. canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires MANAGE; canManage() should require only MANAGE as well.

title: Groups resource type is not resolved to a group name for display
body: getResourceName handles only USERS. For a policy with resourceType Groups it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), and because group resources are named with the group id, the admin console/events show the raw id instead of the group name (and there is no 'All groups' label). Add a GROUPS branch analogous to the USERS branch.

title: Group removal cleanup is not registered for V2
body: Group-removal cleanup is still gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and not ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. In a V2-only deployment the listener is never registered, so deleting a group leaves its Groups resource and policies orphaned. If both features are enabled, management(...).groups() returns GroupPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, causing group deletion to fail. The new Groups resource type needs a V2-safe cleanup path.

title: Account UI message switched to Java MessageFormat placeholders
body: This is a frontend i18n bundle: the rest of the file (and the old value of this key) uses double-brace interpolation such as `'{{0}}'` and `{{1}}`. The new value uses single-brace Java placeholders and a `{2,choice,...}` ChoiceFormat expression, which the account UI's JS i18n layer will not substitute. English users will see literal `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2,choice,...}` text instead of the actual validation error. Keep the frontend interpolation format and implement pluralisation in code/i18n plural forms.

title: Admin UI message switched to Java MessageFormat placeholders
body: This Admin UI bundle is consumed by the JS i18n layer and its other error messages use `{{0}}`-style interpolation. Changing `error-invalid-multivalued-size` to `{0}` / `{2,choice,...}` means the Admin UI will render the placeholders and ChoiceFormat expression literally instead of substituting the attribute and size values. This is a user-visible regression in English Admin UI error messages.

title: Lithuanian account totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The changed value is `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. This file is `messages_lt.properties`, so Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction during OTP setup. It should be replaced with a proper Lithuanian translation, e.g. an equivalent of `Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo telefone:`.

title: Lithuanian login totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: `loginTotpStep1` was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, Italian text in the Lithuanian login bundle. Lithuanian users will get an Italian OTP setup instruction. Replace it with the correct Lithuanian translation instead of the Italian string.

title: Simplified Chinese message uses Traditional Chinese characters
body: The changed value `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese terms (`手機`, `應用程式`) in the `zh_CN` (Simplified Chinese) bundle, whose surrounding strings use Simplified characters such as `应用` and `设备`. Use the Simplified form, e.g. `在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`.

title: No positive tests for allowed HTML or matching anchors
body:
The new tests only assert that illegal HTML, illegal anchors and disallowed HTML produce messages. There is no test verifying that a translation containing an allowed tag from the English source (e.g. ``, ``, `
`) or a matching anchor tag produces no message. That leaves the verifier's main false-positive risk untested. The illegal-HTML fixture also uses malformed `
tag

title: UI message switched from i18next placeholders to Java MessageFormat
body: This file is consumed by the React account UI, and its other validation messages use i18next double-brace interpolation such as {{0}} and {{1}}. The new value uses single braces and a Java ChoiceFormat expression: Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}. i18next will not substitute {0}/{1}/{2}, so the account UI will display literal placeholders and the raw choice expression instead of the attribute name and count for multi-valued validation errors. Keep the UI placeholder syntax (and localize plural forms using the UI's plural support) rather than copying the server-side MessageFormat string.

title: Admin UI message switched from i18next placeholders to Java MessageFormat
body: The admin UI message bundle uses double-brace interpolation (e.g. {{0}}) throughout, but error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed to single-brace Java MessageFormat placeholders plus a ChoiceFormat expression. The admin UI's i18n layer will render the placeholders and choice syntax literally instead of substituting the attribute name and value count, breaking this validation error message in the admin console. The server-side MessageFormat syntax is not valid for this JS resource.

title: Lithuanian account messages replaced with Italian text
body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian account message bundle was changed to the Italian string 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. Lithuanian users will now see Italian text on the account TOTP setup page. The replacement needs to be a Lithuanian sentence, not a copy of the Italian translation.

title: Lithuanian login messages replaced with Italian text
body: loginTotpStep1 in the Lithuanian login message bundle was changed to the Italian string 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. This makes the Lithuanian login TOTP setup page display Italian text. It should be a Lithuanian translation.

title: Simplified Chinese bundle now contains Traditional Chinese text
body: The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) account bundle now has totpStep1 set to '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', which uses Traditional Chinese characters and vocabulary (手機, 應用程式). This is a regression for Simplified Chinese users; the value should be written in Simplified Chinese.

title: Choice-format normalization erases HTML before sanitization
body: normalizeValue removes the entire {n,choice,...} expression for error-invalid-multivalued-size and linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit* by replacing it with '...'. If a translation places HTML or script inside a choice alternative, that markup is removed from the string handed to the OWASP sanitizer, so the verifier will not report it even though it can be rendered at runtime. This creates a false negative in the exact check the PR is adding. Strip only the choice syntax needed for verification, or validate each choice alternative separately.

title: No positive test for allowed HTML or matching anchors
body:
All four tests only assert that an error is reported for bad fixtures. There is no fixture where valid HTML (for example when English contains , or
) or a matching anchor is expected to produce no message. A regression that rejects every translation containing HTML or anchors would still pass this test suite.

title: Account UI message now uses Java single-brace placeholders
body: The other account UI error messages in this file use double-brace interpolation such as `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, and `{{2}}`. This change replaces them with single-brace Java-style placeholders and adds a Java `ChoiceFormat` expression (`{2,choice,...}`). The account UI message layer will not substitute those placeholders, so users will see literal `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and the choice text instead of the attribute name and value count. Keep the JS interpolation syntax or format the plural in the UI.

title: Admin UI message now uses Java single-brace placeholders
body: This JS admin UI bundle uses double-brace placeholders (`{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`) throughout. The changed `error-invalid-multivalued-size` value uses single braces and a Java `ChoiceFormat` expression (`{2,choice,...}`), which the admin UI interpolation does not process. The result is a user-visible error message with literal placeholders rather than the attribute name and count.

title: Lithuanian account message replaced with Italian text
body: The new `totpStep1` value is `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian account users will see Italian instructions after this change. The text needs to be restored to a Lithuanian translation.

title: Lithuanian login message replaced with Italian text
body: The new `loginTotpStep1` value is `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. This makes the Lithuanian login page show Italian instructions. It should be a Lithuanian translation.

title: Simplified Chinese bundle contains Traditional Chinese text
body: The new `totpStep1` text `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese characters and Taiwan-style wording (`手機`, `應用程式`) in the `zh_CN` Simplified Chinese bundle. Users of the Simplified Chinese locale will see mixed script. It should be converted to Simplified Chinese.

title: Sanitizer tests cover only rejection cases, not valid HTML
body:
The added tests only verify that illegal HTML, unchanged anchor mismatches, and duplicate keys produce errors. There is no test proving that a translation containing HTML allowed by the English source (for example `

`, `
`, ``, or an exact matching anchor) passes without a false positive. This is important because the verifier is now applied to large resource bundles and false positives block the build.

title: rawTokenId is never null-checked
body: The second Objects.requireNonNull call checks grantType again instead of rawTokenId. A caller can therefore construct an AccessTokenContext with a null raw token ID. encodeTokenId then produces an ID like "onrtac:null", and getTokenContextFromTokenId returns the literal string "null" as the raw ID. The check should be Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed").

title: isAccessTokenId does not actually verify the grant shortcut
body: For an encoded ID such as "onrtac:uuid", the grant shortcut is at zero-based indexes 4..5 ("ac"), but the matcher reads items[0].substring(3, 5), which yields "ta". It also returns false when that slice equals the expected shortcut, reversing the intended condition. Consequently, the matcher returns true for any UUID-suffixed ID regardless of the encoded grant type, so integration tests will not catch wrong grant shortcut encoding. Use substring(4, 6) and return true when it equals expectedGrantShortcut.

title: Grant shortcuts are not validated against the 2-character decoder contract
body: postInit accepts any string returned by OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() and stores it without checking its length. The default encoder hard-codes a 6-character context (session 2 + token 2 + grant 2), and getTokenContextFromTokenId throws when the encoded context length is not 6. The SPI javadoc even says shortcuts are "usually like 3-letters", so an extension following that documentation can start successfully but produce tokens that cannot be decoded by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider. Validate that every shortcut is exactly 2 characters during postInit and fix the SPI documentation.

title: Adding an abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant implementations
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is implemented by custom OAuth2 grant providers. Adding an abstract method without a default implementation means every existing external implementation must be updated before it will compile or load. If this SPI needs to remain compatible, provide a default method (for example returning a reserved/unknown shortcut) or explicitly document and handle this as a breaking SPI change.

title: Incorrect-grant test passes because of an NPE, not the intended error
body: before() never calls factory.postInit(), so factory.sessionFactory remains null. When getGrantTypeByShortcut looks up an unknown shortcut such as "ac", it attempts sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...) and throws a NullPointerException, which testIncorrectGrantType catches as a generic RuntimeException. The test therefore passes for the wrong reason and does not validate the real unknown-grant behavior. Initialize or mock sessionFactory and assert the expected exception type/message.

title: isAccessTokenId does not actually verify the encoded grant shortcut
body: The new matcher checks `items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` and returns false when it matches. There are two defects: the grant shortcut occupies zero-based positions 4-5 (`substring(4, 6)`), not 3-4, and the condition is inverted. Consequently any access token id with a colon and a UUID suffix passes the matcher regardless of the encoded grant type, so the updated integration tests cannot catch wrong grant-type encoding. It should reject when the prefix length is not 6 or when `substring(4, 6)` is not equal to the expected shortcut.

title: rawTokenId is never null-checked
body: The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` a second time instead of checking `rawTokenId`. A null raw token id is therefore accepted, and `encodeTokenId` can later produce a malformed token id such as `onrtac:null`, defeating the constructor invariant. The second check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

title: Grant shortcut length is not enforced even though the parser requires exactly two characters
body: `encodeTokenId` concatenates the grant shortcut directly, while `getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires exactly 6 characters before the colon (lines 74-81). The new `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory#getShortcut()` contract does not require a two-character shortcut, and its Javadoc even says shortcuts are "usually like 3-letters". A custom grant returning a 3-character shortcut will make this server issue token ids like `onrtabc:...` that its own parser rejects with `IllegalArgumentException`, so the encoded context cannot be decoded. Validate that every grant shortcut is exactly two characters and contains no `:`, or make the parser length-aware.

title: setFormParams leaves the cached grantType stale
body: `Context.grantType` is derived from `formParams` in the constructor, but the public `setFormParams` setter replaces `formParams` without recomputing `grantType`. Any caller that mutates the form parameters will still get the old grant type from `getGrantType()`, and `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` will write that stale value into `clientSessionCtx`, causing the access token id to encode the wrong grant shortcut. Recompute `grantType` in `setFormParams` or avoid caching it as separate mutable state.

title: Decoder assumes exactly two-character grant shortcuts
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId() requires encodedContext.length() == 6 and then splits the prefix as 2 chars for session type, 2 for token type, and 2 for grant type. However OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() is documented as usually a 3-letter shortcut and does not enforce a 2-character length. A custom grant factory returning a valid 3-character shortcut (for example "abc") will generate an ID such as "onrtabc:<uuid>", which this decoder rejects with IllegalArgumentException. Any endpoint that later parses token context from such an access token will fail. Either enforce exactly two characters when collecting shortcuts in the factory or make the encoding/decoding format length-independent.

title: isAccessTokenId checks the wrong substring and has an inverted comparison
body: The matcher reads items[0].substring(3, 5) for the grant-type shortcut, but the grant shortcut occupies characters 4-5 (0-based indexes 4 and 5) in the 6-character prefix. It also returns false when the substring equals the expected shortcut, which is the inverse of the intended assertion. As a result, the matcher accepts token IDs whose grant shortcut is not the expected one and the updated expectCodeToToken()/expectRefresh()/device/CIBA assertions do not actually validate the encoded grant type. It can also throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException if the prefix is shorter than 5 characters.

title: Constructor checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
body: The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") a second time instead of validating rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted, and encodeTokenId() would concatenate it as the literal text "null" into the token ID. The error message for the repeated grantType check is also misleading. This should use rawTokenId in the second requireNonNull call.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: Adding a non-default abstract getShortcut() method to the public OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface is a source and binary compatibility break. Existing custom grant-type factories compiled against the previous interface will not implement this method and can fail at startup with AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() calls gtf.getShortcut() for every registered grant factory. Provide a default implementation or otherwise handle legacy factories without breaking startup.

title: Removal of public Context copy constructor breaks extension callers
body: The public OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context) copy constructor was removed from the Context class. This is a source and binary compatibility break for any custom grant implementation that used it to clone/modify a context. The new grantType field could simply be copied in that constructor, so removing the constructor is unnecessary for the feature.

title: Exhausted recovery codes are deleted only from local storage
body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` now returns a user-storage credential before a local one, but when all codes are used this branch still calls `credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...)`. That method removes only locally stored credentials, so for a federated credential the delete is a no-op: the exhausted credential remains in user storage. A later login can then reach `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`, where `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()` has no value and throws. The user-storage path needs a federated-aware removal/disable operation instead of local deletion.

title: User storage receives raw recovery codes instead of hashed credential data
body: The user-storage branch serializes `generatedCodes`, i.e. the plaintext recovery codes, into the `UserCredentialModel`. The local branch instead persists `credentialModel`, whose codes were hashed by `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues`. The new test provider follows the user-storage path by storing this raw JSON directly as `credentialData` and validating by plaintext comparison, so this PR establishes a path where usable recovery codes are stored unhashed in user storage and the hashed model/used-flag metadata is lost. The helper should pass the hashed credential data, or the hashing contract must be explicit and the test storage must not persist plaintext codes.

title: Federated recovery-code test does not verify one-time use
body: The new `isValid` implementation returns true whenever the submitted code matches any stored raw code, but never marks that code as used or updates `MyUser.recoveryCodes`; `getCredentials` also rebuilds every code as unused via `createFromValues`. The added integration test performs only one successful login, so it would pass even though the same recovery code remains reusable and the all-codes-used reconfiguration path is never exercised. The user-storage test provider should persist used state, or the test should assert that a previously used code is rejected, so the federated path actually covers the one-time-use guarantee.

title: Recovery-code JSON is written to the wrong UserCredentialModel field
body: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` creates the federated credential input with `new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)`. The three-argument `UserCredentialModel` constructor populates `value`, not `challengeResponse`. The new user-storage implementation reads `input.getChallengeResponse()` when saving the recovery credential (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential`), so the serialized code list is lost and `credentialData` is null. On the next login, `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` asks the storage for credentials and `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials` attempts to deserialize that null data, so the user-storage recovery-code setup/login path fails. Use `setChallengeResponse` or make the storage read `getValue()`.

title: Exhausted recovery credentials in user storage are not removed
body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` now returns a credential from federated user storage when present, but the exhausted-code cleanup still calls `removeStoredCredentialById`, which is the local credential-store API. If all codes in a user-storage credential are used, the external credential remains configured. The next login will still select the recovery authenticator, but `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` calls `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()` on a credential with no remaining codes and throws, instead of redirecting the user to configure new codes. The removal/disable path must handle federated credentials.

title: New user-storage test stores recovery codes in plaintext and permits replay
body: The new user-storage handler stores the recovery-code payload verbatim in `credentialData`, and `isValid` at line 340 compares the submitted code to the raw stored strings. It never hashes incoming codes or marks a code as used. The production recovery-code provider stores hashes and consumes used codes. As written, the integration test models a storage backend that persists password-equivalent recovery codes in plaintext and accepts replay, and it would not catch a real user-storage implementation that fails to hash or consume codes.

title: Exhausted recovery-code credential from user storage is not actually removed
body: The authenticator now resolves the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(), which returns the federated (user-storage) credential first when before it only looked at Keycloak's local store. When allCodesUsed() is true the code calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()). That call only deletes from the local credential store; it does not remove or disable a credential owned by a user-storage provider. In addition, models built from RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues (the shape the user-storage path produces) do not carry the original stored id, so getId() can be null and passing null into the credential store (JPA EntityManager.find) throws IllegalArgumentException. Consequence: for a user-storage user who exhausts all recovery codes the cleanup either throws or is silently ignored, the old federated credential stays in the user store, and it must be relied on that the subsequent required action overwrites it.

title: Raw recovery codes are persisted to user storage while only hashed codes go local
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generatedCodes list and passes that JSON as the value of the UserCredentialModel to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...). If the user-storage provider persists the value it is handed (as the provided test provider does), the recovery codes are stored in cleartext in external storage. The local branch instead uses credentialModel, which contains only the hashed codes and per-code used flags (see RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.createFromValues). Recovery codes are single-use password-equivalent secrets, so storing them unhashed in an external user store is a meaningful exposure if that store leaks, and the asymmetry means the same credential has different representations depending on where it landed. The code should pass a hashed representation (or otherwise guarantee/require the provider hashes before persisting).

title: User-storage recovery codes are replayable and single-use behavior is never exercised
body: updateCredential stores the raw codes JSON, isValid compares input.getChallengeResponse() against that raw list without ever marking a code used, and getCredentials rebuilds the model with RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(), which re-hashes the raw codes and sets every code's used flag back to false. As a result allCodesUsed() is always false, getNextRecoveryAuthnCode() always returns code #1, and a recovery code can be used repeatedly for a user in this provider. The new testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin does only one login with the first code, so it does not cover the single-use guarantee or the 'all codes used -> re-configure' path. This both leaves the core security property of recovery codes untested and makes the test provider an unsafe model for real user-storage implementations.

title: Recovery-codes credential cannot be disabled/removed in the user-storage test provider
body: The provider now creates, validates and reports recovery-authn-codes as configured, but getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() still only adds CredentialModel.OTP and disableCredentialType() only handles OTP (it logs 'Unsupported to disable credential of type: ...' for anything else). Consequently once a recovery-codes credential is written into this user storage it cannot be disabled through the admin or account credential APIs, and that removal path is never tested, so a broken/compromised/exhausted credential cannot be cleaned up.

title: Concurrent reader thread is neither synchronized nor joined
body: The background reader is started and group deletion proceeds immediately, with no latch confirming that a read actually started before deletion. After deletion the test only sets `deletedAll` and asserts, without joining the thread. Exceptions from reads still in flight can therefore be recorded after the assertion, so the test can pass even when the concurrent-read bug occurs. Additionally, if any `groupUuid` deletion throws, `deletedAll` is never set in a finally block and the non-daemon thread keeps issuing requests indefinitely, potentially hanging the test run. Use a startup latch, set the stop flag in a `finally`, join the thread with a timeout, and assert only after it has terminated.

title: Test does not exercise the changed getSubGroupsCount path
body: The reader calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)`, where the last argument is only `briefRepresentation`. It does not request subgroup counts. The server code only calls `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` when the `subGroupsCount` option is enabled, and `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount` is the method this PR fixes. As written, the regression test can pass on the unfixed base because it never reaches the NPE path. The test should explicitly request subgroup counts or otherwise invoke `getSubGroupsCount` for groups being deleted.

title: Same null-delegate NPE remains in getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: The PR only adds a null guard in `getSubGroupsCount`, but the search/pagination overloads of `getSubGroupsStream` at lines 256, 262, and 268 still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` directly. If the cached group has been deleted concurrently, `modelSupplier.get()` returns null and these methods still throw an NPE, so concurrent subgroup access remains broken. These methods should handle a missing delegate consistently, for example by returning an empty stream or delegating through the same guarded path.

title: Null guard only covers getSubGroupsCount; subgroup stream methods still NPE on concurrent deletion
body: The PR only null-checks the delegate in getSubGroupsCount. The overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` directly. `modelSupplier.get()` returns null when the cached group's database row has been deleted concurrently, so these methods throw an NPE exactly like the original getSubGroupsCount bug. A request that filters or paginates subgroups of a group deleted by another request can still fail with a 500. Apply the same null handling, or return a controlled not-found result, consistently across these methods.

title: Regression test does not request subgroup counts, so it may not exercise getSubGroupsCount
body: The new test's reader thread calls `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)`. The fourth argument is the brief-representation flag; it does not request subgroup counts. Subgroup counts are only populated through `populateSubGroupCount` -> `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` when the subGroupsCount option is enabled. The test would therefore likely pass even with the old NPE and does not guard the changed method. It should request sub-group counts and ideally assert the returned count so it covers the fixed path.

title: Reader thread is never joined or stopped on failure, allowing test hang or false pass
body: The test starts a non-daemon thread at line 139 and only sets deletedAll after all deletes. There is no try/finally around the deletes and no join after line 155. If any delete throws, the thread loops forever and can hang the test JVM; even on success the assertion at line 157 runs while the reader may still be in flight, so an exception can be added after the assertion and be silently missed, and the thread can keep using the realm after teardown. Use try/finally to stop the loop and join the thread, and coordinate the first read (for example with a latch) so the race is actually exercised.

title: Concurrent-deletion NPE fix is incomplete: subgroup listing overloads still dereference a null model
body: getSubGroupsCount() was changed to tolerate modelSupplier.get() returning null (the case where the cached GroupAdapter is still usable while the group has already been removed from the database), but the three sibling overloads were not fixed: getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(firstResult, maxResults) at line 262 and getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, firstResult, maxResults) at line 268 all still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. Under the same race that motivated this PR (cached group visible while concurrently deleted), these methods throw a NullPointerException, so the reported concurrent-access NPE is only fixed for the subgroup-count path, not for the subgroup listing endpoints that use the very same supplier. Apply the same null handling to those overloads (e.g. return Stream.empty() / a null-aware result or fall back consistently) rather than patching only one call site.

title: Background reader thread is never joined and can hang the test JVM or let the assertion race
body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a non-daemon reader thread (new Thread(...).start() at line 139) and only stops it by setting deletedAll in the normal path; there is no try/finally. If anything in the deletion loop throws (e.g. an admin DELETE returns an error) or the test aborts before line 155, deletedAll is never set, so the loop keeps issuing groups() requests forever and the non-daemon thread prevents the test JVM from exiting. In addition, the assertion assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty()) at line 157 executes immediately after deletedAll.set(true) without joining the reader, so a read that is still in flight can record its exception after the assertion runs, allowing a regression to pass unnoticed. The thread should be stopped in a finally block, joined before the assertion, and ideally created as a daemon.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime order_by used by audit logs
body: The audit-log endpoint selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"` (organization_auditlogs.py:79), but this class reuses `BasePaginator` numeric key handling instead of `DateTimePaginator`'s datetime conversion. `get_item_key` calls `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` on the `AuditLogEntry.datetime` value, which raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime` while `build_cursor` constructs cursors, so the first request with `optimized_pagination=true` returns 500. Additionally, `value_from_cursor` returns `cursor.value` unchanged, so pagination would pass an integer cursor value into `build_queryset`'s datetime `<=` filter, producing an invalid or incorrect query. The optimized path needs the same datetime-to-int and int-to-datetime conversions as `DateTimePaginator`.

title: Negative-offset advanced path passes negative slices to Django QuerySet
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, `get_result` calls `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexes; this raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` rather than returning data. Cursor offsets are parsed from user-supplied cursor strings by `Cursor.from_string` and are not validated, so an authorized user of the optimized path can trigger a 500, and the advertised reverse-pagination feature never works. Validate/reject negative offsets or translate them into a supported query plan instead of passing them to ORM slicing.

title: New optimized pagination path has no tests
body: No tests were added for `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, the new `optimized_pagination` branch, or the authorization gate in `organization_auditlogs.py`. Basic coverage of first-page fetches, forward/backward cursors, datetime keys, negative offsets, and the non-admin fallback would have caught both the datetime `TypeError` and the negative-slicing `ValueError` in this PR.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime-keyed querysets used by audit logs
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key (line 838-840) and value_from_cursor (842-843) are numeric-only: get_item_key does `int(math.floor(value) ...)` on the attribute named by the order_by key, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value. The new audit-log endpoint instantiates this paginator with order_by="-datetime", where AuditLogEntry.datetime is a DateTimeField. On the very first page (after fetching rows) `build_cursor` calls `get_item_key(results[-1])`, and `math.floor()` on a `datetime` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`, producing a 500. Even if that were fixed, value_from_cursor returning an int would be fed into `build_queryset`'s WHERE clause as the datetime value, so subsequent pages would filter incorrectly or error in Postgres. This paginator should extend DateTimePaginator (which formats/parses datetimes) rather than duplicating Paginator's numeric handling. As written, every request that reaches the optimized path crashes.

title: Negative-offset 'advanced' branch passes a negative slice to Django and raises
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, the code does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with start_offset = cursor.offset (negative). Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing; `QuerySet.__getitem__` raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` (ValueError in some versions) for a negative slice start. The comment claims 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', which is false. A client can craft a cursor like `value:-1:0` (Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets), triggering a 500 for anyone who reaches this code path. The negative-offset feature is therefore non-functional and provides a way to crash the endpoint.

title: Possible AttributeError on organization_context.member when it is None
body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `organization_context.member` without a None check. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is optional (None when no org membership mapping is present, which can happen on control-silo endpoints). When the user is not a superuser and member is None, this line raises AttributeError and 500s instead of falling back to the standard paginator. Guard with `organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access` or use the member-access helpers.

title: BasePaginator 'negative offset' change is a no-op and the comment misdescribes behavior
body: The new `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` is behavior-identical to the previous `queryset[offset:stop]` for all non-negative offsets, and for is_prev it keeps offset unchanged, so it does not enable 'bidirectional pagination without full dataset scanning' as the comment claims. For a negative non-prev offset it only changes behavior by silently clamping to 0 (previously the negative slice errored) rather than improving performance. The comment is misleading about both the purpose and the safety of the change; the underlying Django ORM does not support negative offsets, so they are neither efficient nor safe.

title: Cursor comment claims negative offsets are allowed but code is unchanged
body: The added comment says 'Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios', but `self.offset = int(offset)` is exactly the original line and performs no validation or special handling. Cursor offsets have always been able to be negative (from_string parses arbitrary ints); the comment implies a new capability that does not exist and contradicts the actual negative-offset handling elsewhere. It should be removed or reworded to describe real behavior.

title: No tests for the new OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized endpoint branch
body: The PR adds a new paginator class and a request-controlled branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint (including an authorization check and a negative-offset code path) with no unit or endpoint tests. Given that the datetime-key mismatch and negative-offset crash above would be caught by even a single test exercising optimize_pagination=true on the audit-log endpoint, the absence of tests means these regressions ship undetected. Add tests covering the optimized path with datetime ordering, the permission gate, and crafted negative-offset cursors.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is not datetime-aware but is used with order_by="-datetime"
body: The audit-log endpoint instantiates `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, but this class copies the integer `Paginator` behavior: `get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the model attribute. For `AuditLogEntry.datetime` that attribute is a `datetime`, so on the first page with any results `build_cursor` calls `get_item_key` and raises `TypeError`, making `optimized_pagination=true` requests fail with a 500. Additionally, `value_from_cursor` returns the raw integer cursor value instead of converting it back to a datetime like `DateTimePaginator` does, so subsequent page queries would compare the timestamp column to an integer and fail or return incorrect results. The paginator needs `DateTimePaginator` semantics (multiplier and cursor conversion) or the endpoint must not use it.

title: Negative-offset branch uses unsupported Django negative slicing
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is true and the cursor offset is negative, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` passes a negative start index into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets explicitly reject negative indexing/slicing with `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`, so any caller who supplies a cursor with a negative offset (possible through `Cursor.from_string`) receives a 500 instead of a page. The comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing is incorrect; the branch cannot work as written and should validate/reject negative offsets or use a supported pagination mechanism.

title: Partial negative-offset clamping produces inconsistent pagination metadata
body: The change clamps negative offsets to zero only when `cursor.is_prev` is false, but the original negative `offset` is still passed to `build_cursor`. For `is_prev=False`, a malformed cursor with a negative offset now returns the first page while `_build_prev_values` sees a truthy `offset` and emits a `prev` cursor with `has_results=True`, incorrectly telling the client there is a previous page. For `is_prev=True`, the offset is left negative and still hits Django's negative-slicing `ValueError`. Negative offsets should be validated consistently rather than partially clamped.

title: No tests cover the new paginator, datetime usage, or negative cursors
body: This PR adds a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and an endpoint branch that uses it, but adds no tests. A basic non-empty audit-log request with `optimized_pagination=true` would have exposed the datetime `TypeError`, and a cursor with a negative offset would have exposed the invalid negative slice. Tests should cover the datetime endpoint path, cursor round-tripping, and negative/malformed cursor handling.

title: Span buffer keys change from Redis sets to sorted sets without migration
body: This line starts writing `span-buf:s:*` keys with `ZADD`, and the Lua script now uses `ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE`/`ZPOPMIN` while `_load_segment_data` uses `ZSCAN`. The key namespace and TTLs are unchanged, so old workers and existing keys still contain Redis SETs created by `SADD`/`SSCAN`. During a rolling deploy, or for up to `redis_ttl` seconds of pre-existing keys, new workers will hit `WRONGTYPE` on SET keys and old workers will hit `WRONGTYPE` on ZSET keys. That aborts span ingestion and flushing and can drop spans. A versioned key prefix or a dual read/write migration is needed.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate the datetime order_by used by audit logs
body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor(getattr(item, self.key))`, but `organization_auditlogs.py` instantiates it with `order_by=-datetime`, so the value is a `datetime`. `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError` as soon as `build_cursor` calls the key function on the first result. Its `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw cursor integer instead of converting it back to a datetime, so later pages would compare a datetime column with an integer. Any audit-log request with `optimized_pagination=true` and the required permission will 500 instead of paginating. The optimized paginator needs the datetime conversion used by `DateTimePaginator`, or the endpoint needs a compatible paginator.

title: Advanced negative-offset path slices a Django QuerySet with a negative index
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is true and a user-supplied cursor has `offset < 0`, this branch calls `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing or negative slice starts and raise `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`, so a crafted cursor such as `?cursor=...:-1:0` on the audit-log endpoint produces a 500. Even if negative slicing were allowed, `stop = start_offset + limit + extra` remains positive, so `[-N:positive]` would return an empty or wrong page rather than reverse pagination. The negative-offset feature does not work as documented.

title: Eviction cap is hard-coded to 1000 and ignores max_segment_spans
body: The Lua eviction always keeps at most 1000 spans, while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` defaults to 1001 and is still accepted as a constructor argument. The Python-side `max_segment_spans` check was removed from `_load_segment_data`, so that setting is now a no-op: configuring a lower limit will not bound segment size, and the default behavior silently drops one span from a 1001-span segment instead of honoring the configured threshold. The cap should be passed into the script or enforced consistently in Python.

title: No test exercises the new >1000-span eviction path
body: All span-buffer tests in this file build segments of at most five spans, so the new `zpopmin` eviction branch is never executed. The hard-coded cap, interaction with `max_segment_spans`, cleanup of redirects and TTLs for evicted spans, and root-span retention under eviction are unverified. Add a test with more than 1000 spans in one segment and assert the intended survivors and key cleanup.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime keys used by audit logs
body: The new OptimizedCursorPaginator implements get_item_key by calling math.floor/math.ceil on the raw model attribute. The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with order_by="-datetime", so the attribute is a datetime and the first page raises TypeError. Its value_from_cursor also returns the raw integer cursor value instead of converting it back to a datetime, so even if the key conversion were fixed, build_queryset would compare a datetime column against an integer. Any request with optimized_pagination=true for a superuser or globally privileged member returns a 500.

title: Negative-offset branch slices Django QuerySet with a negative index
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, get_result assigns start_offset=cursor.offset and evaluates queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported"); the stop value is also computed from the negative start and may be negative or nonsensical. Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets, so a crafted cursor can trigger this path instead of the intended advanced pagination behavior.

title: Changing span-buf:s keys from sets to sorted sets breaks rolling deployment
body: The buffer now writes span payloads with zadd and reads/merges them with zcard/zscan/zunionstore, but the Redis key namespace span-buf:s is unchanged while old deployments stored those keys as Redis sets. During a rolling deploy, old and new consumers will operate on the same keys with conflicting types: zadd/zcard/zscan on an existing set and sadd on an existing zset both raise WRONGTYPE. Unflushed segments created before the deploy will therefore fail ingestion/flushing until their TTL expires unless the keys are migrated or the namespace is versioned.

title: Span-count limit is no longer enforced when loading segments
body: The max_segment_spans check was removed from _load_segment_data, and SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans is now unused; eviction is instead hard-coded to 1000 inside the Lua script. If the Python zadd pipeline writes more than 1000 spans and the following EVALSHA calls fail or the process dies between the two pipelines, the set is never evicted. Because the loader no longer rejects oversized segments, such a set can be flushed downstream. The constructor option also no longer controls anything, and its default of 1001 no longer matches the hard-coded 1000 cap.

title: ZUNIONSTORE default aggregation corrupts eviction scores for duplicate spans
body: The two zunionstore calls use the default SUM aggregation. If the same span payload exists in both the destination set and the set being merged (for example, at-least-once duplicate delivery after a parent merge), its score becomes the sum of the two end_timestamp_precise values rather than the actual timestamp. Subsequent zpopmin eviction then treats that duplicate as newer than it really is and may evict newer spans instead. Using AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN, depending on the desired tie behavior) would preserve timestamp semantics.

title: Redirect-chain limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 without handling deep traces
body: The parent-redirect walk now stops after 1000 iterations, down from 10000. For segment trees deeper than that, set_span_id will remain an intermediate span instead of resolving to the root, so later spans can be placed in the wrong segment. The change is intentional-looking but untested; if the lower bound is desired it should be justified and covered, otherwise it is a silent regression for very deep traces.

title: No test covers the new eviction cap or duplicate-score behavior
body: The PR's central behavior is eviction during insert, but every buffer test inserts at most five spans. There is no test that pushes a segment past 1000 spans and asserts that the oldest entries are evicted, no test that verifies max_segment_spans is still honored or intentionally removed, and no test for the zunionstore duplicate-member score behavior. A regression in the cap or in the removed load-time guard would pass CI.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime order keys
body: The new OptimizedCursorPaginator derives keys exactly like Paginator: get_item_key does int(math.floor(value))/math.ceil(value) on getattr(item, self.key), and value_from_cursor simply returns cursor.value (an int). It does NOT override these like DateTimePaginator does (which converts a datetime to a float millis value and back). The only caller being added, organization_auditlogs.py, instantiates it with order_by="-datetime", so self.key is "datetime". When build_cursor calls the key on a result whose datetime is a datetime object, math.floor/ceil(datetime) raises TypeError, and build_queryset would also compare the datetime column against an int value_from_cursor. Result: every request that reaches the optimized path (admin + ?optimized_pagination=true) returns a 500. To be usable for datetime ordering this paginator must reuse DateTimePaginator's get_item_key/value_from_cursor.

title: Negative-offset path slices a Django queryset with a negative index and raises
body: The "advanced feature" branch does start_offset = cursor.offset when it is negative, then results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop]). Django querysets do not support negative indices; slicing with a negative start raises AssertionError("Negative indexing is not supported."). The inline comment claiming "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false. A client can supply such a cursor because Cursor.from_string parses int(bits[1]) with no sign restriction, so any admin request to the audit-log endpoint with enable_advanced_features=True and a cursor whose offset field is negative will crash. (Same branch also computes the is_prev trimming check as len(results) == offset + limit + extra using the original offset while the slice used start_offset, so the arithmetic is inconsistent when they differ.)

title: Unguarded access to organization_context.member can raise AttributeError
body: enable_advanced is computed as request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is Optional; when it is None (a user with superuser off who reaches this endpoint without a resolved member, e.g. global staff/other access paths) the attribute access raises AttributeError and the endpoint 500s. The value should be derived defensively (e.g. organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access) or the flag should not gate on member at all.

title: Silent span eviction during insert with no metric; max_segment_spans no longer enforced
body: The new eviction (zpopmin set_key, span_count - 1000) silently drops the lowest-score (earliest end_timestamp) spans once a segment exceeds 1000 entries, with no counter/metric to make the loss observable. In the same change, buffer.py removed the _load_segment_data max_segment_spans check that previously logged and skipped oversized segments, so that safety signal is gone as well. Note the hardcoded 1000 here also disagrees with SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (default 1001), which is now configurable but completely unused. Net effect: spans in large segments are discarded with no visibility, and the documented config limit is ignored; at minimum an eviction metric and consistency with max_segment_spans are needed.

title: Redirect resolution depth reduced from 10000 to 1000 without accounting for the removed limit comment
body: The redirect-walk loop was lowered from `for i = 0, 10000` to `for i = 0, 1000` (and the explanatory comment about segment trees of depth 10k removed). This bounds how far a chain of parent_span_id redirects is followed when merging subsegments. For traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 the walk stops before reaching the true segment key, so the span is attached to an intermediate key and the segment can be flushed split/duplicated rather than merged into its root. If the intent was to bound work, it should at least be justified and ideally tied to max_segment_spans, not silently set to 1000.

title: Eviction path and new optimized paginator have no tests
body: None of the updated buffer tests insert more than a handful of spans, so the new zpopmin eviction branch in add-buffer.lua (span_count > 1000) is never exercised; a regression there would be invisible. Likewise there is no test covering OptimizedCursorPaginator or the organization audit-log optimized_pagination branch, which is why the datetime-key crash and negative-slice crash above are not caught. Tests should cover a segment exceeding 1000 spans (asserting eviction keeps the expected spans and emits a metric) and the new paginator, including datetime ordering and negative-offset cursors.

title: Upsampling eligibility uses outer dataset and original request query
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` and the actual `query` to execute, but it calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)`. `dataset` is the closure's original dataset, and the helper reads `request.GET['query']`, not the `query` argument. In the dashboard split path this method is invoked with `discover` plus synthesized `errors_only_query`/`transactions_only_query`; a generic query split into errors will not be upsampled, and a transaction-only split derived from a request containing `event.type:error` can be upsampled even though it targets transaction rows. This yields wrong counts and may query sample_weight for transaction data. Pass `scoped_dataset` and the actual query string into the eligibility check.

title: Substring check treats negated and mixed event.type queries as error-only
body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the raw query contains the substring `event.type:error`. A query such as `!event.type:error` (which excludes errors) or `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` is classified as error-only, so `count()` is rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` for transaction or mixed results. Transaction events have no meaningful sample_weight, so counts are understated or zero. The tests only cover exact positive and transaction-only examples and miss negation/OR cases.

title: upsampled_count drops events whose sample_weight is NULL
body: `upsampled_count` is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no coalesce/default. The new factory helper only sets a sample rate when `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` exists, and the code explicitly assumes every event has a sample_weight. Any event without a sample rate (older events, unsampled errors, or mixed projects after allowlisting) contributes NULL and is omitted from the sum instead of contributing 1, so allowlisted projects undercount errors.
