The tests only cover events that have client_sample_rate and would not catch this; the aggregate should use `sum(coalesce(sample_weight, 1))` or equivalent.

title: Top-events ordering still uses unsampled count()
body: When `topEvents` is used, only `timeseries_columns` is rewritten to `upsampled_count()`. The `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` argument, including any default count ordering, still references the original `count()` aggregation, so Snuba selects the top N groups using raw counts while the response displays upsampled counts. With a large sample-rate skew the endpoint can return the wrong set of top events. The transformed aggregation needs to be applied to orderby/equations as well.

title: Accidental gitlink without .gitmodules
body: This PR adds a gitlink entry named `sentry-repo` pointing at the base commit, but no `.gitmodules` entry or URL is added. A checkout with submodule initialization will fail with `No url found for submodule path 'sentry-repo' in .gitmodules`, and the repository gets an unintended empty submodule. Remove this file/gitlink unless a submodule is genuinely intended.

title: Upsampling check uses the outer dataset and original request query
body: _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset and query, but the new call to is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects passes the endpoint's captured dataset and the original request, not the dataset/query being executed. In the dashboard split path _get_event_stats is called with discover and errors_only_query or transactions_only_query. A transaction-only split can therefore still be classified as an error query when the original request contained event.type:error, and its count() is rewritten to sum(sample_weight) even though transactions have no sample_weight, causing zero or undercounted results. Conversely, an error-only split is not upsampled when the original request did not contain event.type:error. Pass scoped_dataset and query.

title: Substring match treats negated or mixed event.type:error queries as error-only
body: _is_error_focused_query only checks whether the lowercased query contains the literal substring event.type:error. Queries such as !event.type:error, NOT event.type:error, event.type:transaction OR event.type:error, or free text containing that substring are not error-only queries, but the helper returns True. For the discover dataset this rewrites count() to sum(sample_weight) for queries that can include transactions or other events without sample_weight, so the response undercounts or returns zero. This needs a query-aware check rather than a substring search.

title: Top-events ordering is still based on raw count
body: Only the y-axis/timeseries columns are rewritten when upsampling is enabled. The orderby passed to run_top_events_timeseries_query here and to top_events_timeseries later is still self.get_orderby(request), typically -count(). The top N groups are therefore selected using raw event counts while the returned series use sum(sample_weight), so the selected groups and displayed charts are inconsistent and the top groups may be wrong. Transform the orderby aggregate and count-containing equations the same way, or avoid upsampling for top-events queries.

title: Accidental gitlink/submodule added
body: The PR adds a path named sentry-repo containing only a subproject commit and no .gitmodules entry. This has nothing to do with error upsampling and will make checkouts contain an unresolved gitlink; CI or packaging that expects a normal tree can fail or leave an empty directory. Remove the accidental submodule entry.

title: Public eligibility/caching function is not tested
body: The new test module imports and exercises only the private helpers. is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, which is the public entry point combining allowlist eligibility, caching, dataset selection, and request-query interpretation, is never called. This leaves cache hit/miss behavior and the interaction between the actual executed query and the request query untested, allowing the dashboard-split and negated-query bugs above to slip through. Add tests for the public function, cache invalidation, and split-query behavior.

title: Accidental gitlink/submodule added to repository
body: The PR adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`, but there is no `.gitmodules` entry or submodule metadata. This is an accidental repository artifact: checkouts and CI tooling can treat it as an uninitialized submodule, create an empty directory, or fail submodule validation. Remove this file from the PR.

title: Upsampling check uses the wrong dataset in split-query paths
body: `_get_event_stats` receives a `scoped_dataset` argument, but the new upsampling eligibility call passes the closed-over `dataset` from `get_event_stats_factory`. In dashboard-widget split paths, `_get_event_stats` is called with `discover` or another dataset while the closure still holds the original dataset. `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` then evaluates the wrong dataset, so error queries split to `discover` from a metrics dataset are not upsampled. The inverse could also transform columns using a dataset that `scoped_dataset` does not support. Pass `scoped_dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`.

title: Substring check misclassifies negated and mixed queries as error-only
body: `_is_error_focused_query` treats any query containing the literal text `event.type:error` as an error-only query. This incorrectly classifies negated queries such as `!event.type:error`, mixed queries such as `event.type:transaction OR event.type:error`, and even string literals containing that text. For the `discover` dataset the endpoint then rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count()` = `sum(sample_weight)`, so transaction or mixed rows are aggregated with a column that does not apply to them. That can produce undercounted or otherwise incorrect results. Parse the search query or require an exact, non-negated event-type term before enabling upsampling.

title: Top-events ranking still uses raw count after count() is upsampled
body: Only `final_columns` is transformed for upsampling. The top-events call still passes `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` unchanged (also at line 241 for the RPC path). If a top-events request orders by `count()`, groups are selected using raw event count while the returned time series uses `upsampled_count()`. Groups with different sample weights can therefore be ranked incorrectly, and the returned top-N groups can disagree with their displayed upsampled counts. Transform count() in the orderby expressions too, or make the orderby use the upsample-aware alias.

title: Error events are paired with the wrong IDs when nodestore returns partial results
body: fetch_error_details builds node_ids from error_ids and then zips error_ids with events.values(). nodestore.backend.get_multi omits missing node IDs, so when any event is absent, every later event payload shifts and is paired with the previous error_id. The returned ErrorEvent dicts then carry the wrong id (and any later consumer of that id gets incorrect data). Iterate over the returned mapping and match by node id, or fetch each id individually.

title: Browser report validation permits reports with neither timestamp nor age
body: BrowserReportSerializer makes timestamp and age optional and only checks the other field via truthiness. A report containing both age and timestamp passes when one value is 0, and a report containing neither is accepted at all. The Reporting API requires one of the two on a report; add an object-level validator requiring exactly one and check key presence rather than truthiness.

title: Table widget renders an empty table when new visualization flag is enabled
body: In the table branch, when organization.features includes 'use-table-widget-visualization', the code renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}. It ignores result.data, result.meta, fields, title, loading state, and dataset custom renderers, so any org in the rollout sees a blank table instead of its widget data. Feed the actual result/meta/fields into the new visualization or keep the old table until it is wired up.

title: Attribute-keys query cache is not scoped to organization
body: The request URL is /organizations/${organization.slug}/trace-items/attributes/, but the React Query key is only ['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]. queryOptions contains project IDs and trace type but not the organization slug, so a cache entry created for one organization can be reused after the organization changes (especially when the project selection is empty), showing another org's attribute keys. Include organization.slug or the full org-scoped URL in the query key.

title: Table widget feature flag renders an empty table
body: The new `use-table-widget-visualization` branch passes hard-coded empty `columns` and `tableData` (`data: []`, empty `meta.fields`/`units`) instead of the real `result.data`, `result.meta`, and `fields`. When the feature flag is enabled, every dashboard table widget will render with no rows or columns, so the feature is non-functional and existing dashboards appear empty. The branch must forward the actual table results or fall back to the existing table until it does.

title: Error IDs can be paired with the wrong nodestore records
body: `fetch_error_details` zips `error_ids` with `events.values()` from `nodestore.backend.get_multi`. If any event is missing, `get_multi` omits it from the returned dict, so `.values()` shifts and later error IDs can be associated with the wrong event data. That produces incorrect error titles/messages in generated summaries. Iterate over the node IDs and use `events.get(node_id)` so missing entries remain aligned with their `error_ids`.

title: New PR comment helpers are called on the wrong class
body: `get_comment_body` calls `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` and `self.get_environment_info(issue)`. Those helpers were added to `CommitContextIntegration`, but `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow` is a `PRCommentWorkflow` that holds an integration rather than inheriting from it. Building a suspect PR comment will therefore raise `AttributeError`; the GitLab workflow has the same issue. The helpers should live on `PRCommentWorkflow` or be called through `self.integration`, and `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` should not reference `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title` unless that method exists there.

title: 60-second deadline can leave an auth identity batch unprocessed
body: `check_auth` marks `last_synced` for every selected identity before scheduling `check_auth_identities`, and that task processes up to 100 identities sequentially and only reschedules at the end. A 60-second processing deadline can kill the task before it finishes or reaches the reschedule, leaving the remaining identities unprocessed until the next ~24-hour cycle. Increase/remove the deadline, or update/reschedule identities incrementally so a timeout does not silently skip work.

title: Custom renderer return value is checked by truthiness
body: `if (cell)` treats valid custom renderer results like `0` or the empty string as “no custom renderer” and falls back to the default renderer. Any table cell intentionally rendered as a falsy value will be rendered incorrectly. Check `cell !== undefined` (and similarly for the head renderer at line 32).

title: Zero values bypass age/timestamp mutual exclusion
body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` test `self.initial_data.get(...)` for truthiness. Since `0` is a valid value for both `age` and `timestamp`, a report containing both fields can pass validation when the conflicting value is `0`. Use an explicit `is not None` check so zero does not bypass the mutual-exclusion rule.

title: Table widget feature flag renders an empty table instead of the actual data
body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the org has `use-table-widget-visualization` the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`. All of the already-fetched `result.data`/`result.meta`/`eventView`/custom renderers are ignored, so any org with this flag enabled gets a completely blank table (and no loading placeholder either, since `loading` is no longer passed). This is a user-visible regression gated only by a feature flag rather than a WIP placeholder, so it will break dashboards as soon as the flag is turned on. The branch should pass through the real `result.data`/`result.meta`/`columns` (and handle `loading`), or not be wired up yet.

title: useTraceItemAttributeKeys can now return undefined attributes instead of an empty TagCollection
body: The hook was rewritten to `useQuery` and returns `attributes: isFetching ? previous : data`. Before this change `attributes` was always an object (a `TagCollection` built from `result.data ?? []`, defaulting to `{}`). Now, while the query is disabled (`enabled: false`), before the first fetch resolves (`data` is `undefined` and `previous` is `undefined`), or if the query is skipped, `attributes` is `undefined`. Callers that treat the result as a `TagCollection` (e.g. iterating it, spreading/merging it into a tag map, or calling `Object.keys`/`hasOwnProperty`) will throw. Either default `data` (`data ?? {}`) or keep the empty-object fallback.

title: Error details are paired with event IDs by list position, which can misattribute errors
body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids` and then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())` where `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`. This assumes the returned dict contains exactly one entry per requested id, in the same order as `error_ids`. If the nodestore backend omits ids it couldn't find (common for `get_multi` implementations), all pairs after the first missing id shift, so an error's title/message is attached to the wrong event id. Even if the backend returns a `None` value for misses, the code still relies on dict iteration order matching `error_ids`. Build the result from `events.items()` (recovering the event id from the key/node_id) or map event ids to data explicitly.

title: KeyError when existing integration metadata has no "sender"
body: The user-match check reads `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` directly. However, `build_integration` only writes `metadata["sender"]` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy, and none of the pipeline views bind `sender` (the happy-path test even asserts that the resulting metadata contains no `sender` key). This means integrations created by this very pipeline have no `sender` in metadata. Whenever such an ACTIVE integration exists without a remaining OrganizationIntegration (e.g. a re-install/re-link after the org integration row was removed, or an orphaned integration), this line raises `KeyError` and returns a 500 instead of the intended friendly failure page. It also means the new 'authenticated user == installer' protection can never apply to pipeline-created integrations. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and handle the missing case explicitly, and/or bind `state["sender"]` from the OAuth-authenticated user in the pipeline so `build_integration` records it.

title: Uncaught exceptions from token exchange and get_user_info produce 500
body: `safe_urlopen(...)` (line 423) and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` (line 434) are not wrapped in error handling. Only `safe_urlread`/`parse_qsl` are guarded. Network failures/timeouts or a non-success response (which these helpers raise as exceptions, e.g. ApiError) will propagate and yield a 500 rather than the pipeline's friendly failure page. Since the PR explicitly promises a graceful failure when GitHub cannot produce an access token, these calls should be wrapped and routed through `error(...)`.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the 404/build_integration path
body: `test_installation_not_found` stubs the installation info endpoint with a 404, but the second request sends `state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`, which does not match the pipeline signature, so the request now fails at the new state check with 'Invalid installation request.' and never reaches `build_integration`. The previous assertion (`The GitHub installation could not be found.`) was replaced, so the `ApiError`-404 handling in `build_integration` has lost all coverage, and the test name is now misleading (it tests a state mismatch, not a missing installation). Add a separate test that reaches `build_integration` with a valid state and a 404 installation.

title: No test for the missing/invalid access_token failure path
body: The PR description lists 'GitHub could not generate correct access_token from the code (wrong or attempt of re-use of code)' as a required failure case, but no test covers the branch at line 431 where the token response contains no `access_token`. The new tests only exercise the happy path, state mismatch, and the user-mismatch path. Add a test that stubs the access_token endpoint to return no token (or an error body) and asserts the 'Invalid installation request.' failure page, since this is a stated security-relevant guarantee.

title: Unguarded access to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] can raise KeyError
body: The new sender check does `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. However `build_integration` only stores `sender` in metadata when `state.get("sender")` is truthy (`if state.get("sender"): integration["metadata"]["sender"] = state["sender"]`), so `sender` is not guaranteed to be present. Existing/older GitHub integrations (created before `sender` was persisted, or created via the pipeline path where no sender state was bound) will have metadata without a `sender` key. In the branch where an `Integration` exists with `status=ACTIVE` but has no `OrganizationIntegration` for the org, this line raises `KeyError` (or `TypeError` if `sender` is not a dict), producing a 500 error page instead of the intended graceful failure. This should use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and fall through to the error page when the sender is unknown.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the installation-not-found path
body: The test still stubs `GET /app/installations/{id}` as 404, but after this PR the two requests it issues no longer reach `build_integration`: the first `setup_path?...installation_id=...` request has no `state`, so `OAuthLoginView` redirects to GitHub authorize (response discarded), and the second request uses `state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`, which does not match `pipeline.signature`. The resulting `Invalid installation request.` comes from the OAuth state-mismatch branch, not from the 404 handling in `build_integration` (which used to yield `The GitHub installation could not be found.`). As a result the 404/IntegrationError path is now uncovered and the test name is misleading; it should be rewritten to complete the OAuth step with a valid signature and a fresh installation id so it actually reaches `get_installation_info`.

title: OAuth token-exchange network failures are not handled
body: The only error handling in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` wraps `safe_urlread(req)` (catching exceptions during body read). The `safe_urlopen(...)` call that actually performs the token exchange (and the subsequent `get_user_info(...)` call) are outside any try/except, so a GitHub outage, timeout, or 5xx during token exchange raises an unhandled exception and returns a 500 instead of the intended `github-integration-failed.html` page. Since this PR explicitly aims to surface failures in the installation pipeline, these calls should be wrapped and routed to `error(...)` on failure.

title: KeyError when existing integration metadata has no "sender"
body: The new identity check reads `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` unconditionally. But `build_integration` only adds the `sender` key to metadata when `state.get("sender")` is truthy (lines 376-377), and the existing `test_basic_flow` asserts that a normally-created GitHub integration's metadata has no `sender` key at all. Any integration that was created via the normal Sentry-initiated pipeline (no `sender` in state) and is later re-attached (Integration exists but has no OrganizationIntegration, so this branch runs) will raise `KeyError` and return a 500 instead of the intended "Invalid installation request" error page. The check should guard for a missing/empty sender (e.g. `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")`) and fail closed with the error page.

title: Token exchange / user lookup errors are not caught, producing 500s
body: `safe_urlopen(...)` at line 423 and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` at line 434 are called outside any try/except (only `safe_urlread` is wrapped). `safe_urlopen` raises on non-2xx/network failures and `get_user_info` raises when the `/user` request fails. During a GitHub outage, an invalid/expired token, or a re-used `code`, these will propagate as an unhandled exception and render a 500 rather than the intended `github-integration-failed.html` error page that the PR describes for exactly these failure cases. Wrap these calls so failures deterministically fall through to `error(request, self.active_organization)`.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests installation-not-found
body: `test_installation_not_found` stubs the `/app/installations/{id}` endpoint to 404 and expects the old "The GitHub installation could not be found." message. After this PR the second request uses a state value (`ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`) that does not match the pipeline signature, so the flow short-circuits in `OAuthLoginView` at the state check and returns "Invalid installation request." before ever reaching `get_installation_info`. The 404 stub is now dead code and the installation-not-found path (the `IntegrationError` in `build_integration`) is no longer covered by any test, while the test name is misleading. Either drive the request with the correct signature and assert the not-found error, or rename/split the test so both the state-mismatch and installation-not-found behaviors are actually exercised.

title: Dataclass default for `queued` is evaluated once at import, not per instance
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a plain dataclass default, so `timezone.now()` is executed a single time when the module is imported. Every `AssignmentSource` ever constructed (via `from_integration`, `from_dict`, or directly) therefore carries the same process-start timestamp instead of the moment the assignment was queued. Any staleness/TTL/dedup logic that is supposed to read `queued` will be silently wrong. This should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` (import `field` from dataclasses). The accompanying test `test_to_dict` only asserts `queued is not None`, so it does not catch this.

title: `from_dict` swallows all parse errors, silently disabling the cycle guard
body: `from_dict` catches `ValueError`/`TypeError` and returns `None`. Callers (`sync_assignee_outbound` at tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:53-56) then pass `None` into `should_sync`, which treats it as "no source" and proceeds with the outbound sync. If the serialized `assignment_source_dict` is ever malformed or has an unexpected key (e.g., schema drift after the `queued` datetime round-trips), the round-trip silently degrades to no guard at all, re-introducing the very sync loop this PR is meant to fix, with no log or metric to signal it. Consider logging/metrics on failure or making the failure explicit rather than silently returning None.

title: `to_dict` puts a raw datetime into Celery task kwargs
body: `to_dict()` uses `asdict`, which returns `queued` as a `datetime` object, and `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes this dict straight into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={...})` (integrations/utils/sync.py:136-144). Celery serializes task kwargs with JSON by default; a raw `datetime` is not JSON-serializable, so `apply_async` can raise at publish time, breaking outbound assignee sync for all integrations. Even under a pickle serializer, `from_dict` rehydrates with `cls(**input_dict)` without any type coercion, so `queued` would be a `str` after a JSON round-trip and the field's type contract is violated. `queued` is not actually used by `should_sync` (only `integration_id` is compared), so it should either be excluded from the serialized payload or explicitly (de)serialized.

title: No test that other integrations still receive the outbound update
body: The PR's stated behavior is that only the originating integration is suppressed while "other integrations still propagate changes outward." The new `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` only asserts the negative case (`mock_sync_assignee_outbound.assert_not_called()` for the source integration). There is no test with two linked integrations verifying that the non-source integration's outbound sync is still invoked, so a regression where the new `sync_source` guard over-suppresses (e.g., comparing wrong id) would go undetected.

title: AssignmentSource.queued is frozen at import time and not round-tripped as a datetime
body: The `queued` field uses `timezone.now()` as a dataclass default, which Python evaluates once at module import, so every `AssignmentSource` constructed without an explicit value shares the process-start timestamp rather than recording when the source was queued. In addition, `from_dict` calls `cls(**input_dict)` directly, so when Celery's JSON serializer turns `queued` into an ISO string, the deserialized object has a `str` in a `datetime`-typed field and malformed values are silently accepted. This makes the field unusable for ordering/staleness/latency logic and breaks its declared type contract. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` and explicitly parse/validate `queued` in `from_dict`, or remove the field if it is not intended to be used.

title: Core inbound and cross-integration suppression behavior is untested
body: The only new test for cycle suppression calls `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` directly with a matching `AssignmentSource` and a single integration. It does not exercise the changed `sync_group_assignee_inbound` path that is supposed to attach the source from an inbound webhook, nor does it verify that a source from integration A still allows outbound sync to a different integration B. A regression where inbound forgets to pass the source, or where `should_sync` suppresses every non-`None` source, would still pass this suite even though the original loop would remain in production. Add tests that run `sync_group_assignee_inbound` with mocked outbound sync for both assign and deassign, plus a two-integration case proving that only the source integration is suppressed.

title: queued timestamp is evaluated once at import time
body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated when the module is imported, not when an `AssignmentSource` is created. Every instance in a long-lived worker therefore gets essentially the same timestamp (process start), so the field is not a real queue time. Any future staleness, ordering, or debugging logic based on it will be wrong. Use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead, and have the test assert the value is a recent datetime rather than just non-None.

title: No coverage for deassign loop prevention or cross-integration propagation
body: The new tests cover `assign` when the source integration matches the target, but not the corresponding `deassign` path that was also changed, and they only use a single integration. There is no assertion that an assignment triggered by integration A is still propagated to integration B. A regression that suppresses all outbound syncs whenever a source is present, or that leaves the deassign loop in place, would pass these tests. Add cases with two linked integrations and a matching-source deassign.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and only contains `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract members `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, so MetricAlertDetectorHandler remains abstract. MetricAlertFire still sets `detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler`, and Detector.detector_handler calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`. Any detector whose type resolves to metric_alert_fire will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` instead of processing. Implement the abstract methods or remove/avoid registering this handler until they exist.

title: Expected occurrence uses the wrong group key in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe
body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` is called with group key `'val1'`, so the expected IssueOccurrence fingerprint is built as `[f'{detector.id}:val1']`. The assertion below calls `evaluate_group_key_value` with `expected_result.group_key`, which is `'group_key'`; the production hook therefore builds the actual occurrence with fingerprint `[f'{detector.id}:group_key']`. IssueOccurrence equality includes the fingerprint, so this assertion fails. Build the expected occurrence using `'group_key'` (or `expected_result.group_key`).

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: The evaluate docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method signature and implementation now return a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. This is the contract subclasses implement, so the stale text misdocuments the new API.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler was changed from a concrete DetectorHandler (which implemented `evaluate` returning `[]`) to `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[...]): pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler is an abc.ABC that declares `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` as abstract, so this class implements none of them and remains abstract. Any code that resolves a Detector of type `metric_alert_fire` will call `Detector.detector_handler`, which does `group_type.detector_handler(self)` and therefore raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...`. Previously this path returned an empty result set without error and without throwing, so this is a behavioral regression that will surface as an unhandled exception during detector processing rather than a graceful no-op. Either provide real implementations, or make the property/class fail explicitly with a clear NotImplementedError / skip before instantiation.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: The `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` docstring still reads 'Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`', but the method's return type and implementation were changed in this PR to return a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` keyed by group key. Callers reading the docstring will be misled about the shape of the return value (e.g. iterating over it yields keys, not results). Update the docstring to describe the dict return value.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data` as abstract methods, so instantiating MetricAlertDetectorHandler will raise TypeError. Detector.detector_handler calls `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(self)` for detectors whose type resolves to MetricAlertFire, turning the previous concrete no-op handler into a runtime failure. Implement the required methods or keep the handler concrete.

title: Expected occurrence is built with a different group key
body: In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe, `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` is called with `"val1"`, but `expected_result` and `evaluate_group_key_value` use `"group_key"`. The helper builds the occurrence fingerprint from the supplied group key, so the expected occurrence will not match the result produced for `"group_key"` (or, if equality ignores the fingerprint, the test fails to verify the key-specific fingerprint). Build the expected occurrence with `"group_key"`.

title: Test helper passes a GroupType class as IssueOccurrence.type
body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` sets `type=handler.detector.group_type`, but `IssueOccurrence.type` is the integer group type id. Since every occurrence in these tests is built by the same helper, the tests will not catch an invalid occurrence type, and any path that serializes or validates the occurrence will see a malformed payload. Pass `handler.detector.group_type.type_id` instead.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: The return type of `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` changed from `list[DetectorEvaluationResult]` to `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but the docstring still says it returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`. This misleads implementers and callers about the new contract.

title: schedule_type display conversion computed but not used in monitor context
body: `get_monitor_environment_context` builds a local `config` copy on line 160 and, if present, replaces `config["schedule_type"]` with `monitor.get_schedule_type_display()` on line 162. The return dict on line 168 however emits `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the raw config) instead of the modified `config`, so the display conversion is dead code and the `config` variable is unused. The monitor context attached to issue occurrences therefore exposes the raw stored `schedule_type` value rather than the human-readable display string. (This logic was moved verbatim from `mark_failed.py`, but it is now in a new file and still wrong; either return `config` or drop the dead conversion block.)

title: Renamed/relocated monitor helpers may break existing importers
body: This PR renames `mark_failed_threshold` to `try_incident_threshold`, moves the `SimpleCheckIn` TypedDict from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` into `sentry.monitors.types`, and moves/renames `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context` out of `mark_failed`. None of the other (test or production) modules that may import these symbols from their old locations are updated in this PR. Any importer of `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, or `SimpleCheckIn` from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` will fail to import. Confirm via grep/CI that all references were updated (and that tests import the new locations) before merging.

title: Removed/renamed helpers from mark_failed can break existing importers and tests
body: This refactor deletes `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, and `SimpleCheckIn` from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`, moving or renaming them into the new modules. No other callers or tests are updated in this PR. Any existing `from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed import ...` or `mock.patch("sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.mark_failed_threshold")` in tests/plugins will now fail at import or patch time. Search for all old-name references and update them, or leave backwards-compatible aliases before merging.

title: Computed monitor config with schedule_type display is discarded
body: `get_monitor_environment_context` copies the monitor config and replaces `schedule_type` with `get_schedule_type_display()`, but then returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the computed local `config`. The local variable is unused, so the occurrence's monitor context always contains the raw schedule_type value instead of the human-readable display value. Return `config` here.

title: Public helpers removed from mark_failed without compatibility shims or confirmed import updates
body: This refactor deletes several module-level symbols from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed: `mark_failed_threshold` (renamed `try_incident_threshold` in incidents.py), `create_issue_platform_occurrence` (renamed `create_incident_occurrence` in incident_occurrence.py), `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, and the `SimpleCheckIn` TypedDict (moved to sentry.monitors.types). None of the old names are re-exported from mark_failed. Any other module, test, or downstream import that does `from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed import mark_failed_threshold / create_issue_platform_occurrence / get_failure_reason / get_monitor_environment_context / SimpleCheckIn` will raise ImportError at load time, breaking the import graph. The PR only changes these 4 files, so search all call sites and update them (or leave thin aliases in mark_failed) before merging.

title: get_monitor_environment_context builds a modified config copy but returns the original, so schedule_type display is lost
body: get_monitor_environment_context() copies the monitor config into the local `config`, replaces `config["schedule_type"]` with `monitor.get_schedule_type_display()`, but then returns `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the mutated `config`. The `get_schedule_type_display()` conversion is therefore dead code and the event context ships the raw schedule_type value. This was carried over verbatim from the old mark_failed.py, but since this file is newly added it should be fixed here: return the modified `config`.

title: get_failure_reason docstring examples do not match the produced strings
body: The docstring claims outputs like "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected" and "A failed check-in was detected", but the implementation joins only the bare status labels ("missed", "timeout", "error") via get_text_list, so the actual mixed result is "2 missed, 1 timeout and 1 error check-ins detected", and the singular branch can only return one of the SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP strings ("A missed/error/timeout check-in was detected"), never "A failed check-in was detected". The docstring should reflect the real output (and "humam readible" is misspelled).

title: join() breaks before terminating remaining flusher processes
body: In SpanFlusher.join, if the shared deadline has already passed when the loop reaches a process, the loop executes `break` before reaching `process.terminate()`. Because `self.next_step.join(timeout)` runs first and can consume the whole timeout, this can result in *no* flusher processes being terminated at all; if one process consumes the deadline, later processes are also skipped. On shutdown this can leave hung/running flusher processes alive (e.g. still producing to Kafka) after the consumer believes shutdown finished. The loop should still terminate every process, using the deadline only to bound how long each wait takes.

title: Invalid flusher process counts are silently accepted
body: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `0` as “unset” and falls back to all shards, while a negative value survives the `or`. A negative `--flusher-processes` then makes `self.num_processes` negative, so `process_to_shards_map` and `_create_processes()` create zero flusher processes. `SpanFlusher.submit()` will still forward messages to `next_step` (CommitOffsets), so consumer offsets can be committed while no segments are ever flushed. Validate or clamp `flusher_processes` to at least 1 before constructing the flusher.

title: New wait in test_basic is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
body: `test_basic` patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at line 15, so the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 does not actually wait. The comment says it is giving the flusher thread time to process after the drift change, but it provides no synchronization. As a result the test can race with the background flusher before `step.join()` sets the stopped flag, making it flaky or allowing false positives. Use a synchronization primitive that is not patched out, or limit the monkeypatch to the flusher's sleep call.

title: New multiprocess flusher test never exercises real processes
body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` passes `produce_to_pipe=messages.append`. In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, the presence of `produce_to_pipe` forces `make_process = threading.Thread`, so the new test only asserts the internal shard map/count while running threads. The actual production path introduced by this PR—`multiprocessing` spawn, pickling each shard buffer and shared Values, killing/restarting a real process, and parallel flushing from multiple processes—is not covered. A regression in process startup, restart, or shutdown could therefore pass this test suite.

title: Inserting flusher_processes before produce_to_pipe breaks positional callers
body: `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` previously took `produce_to_pipe` as the sixth parameter; the new `flusher_processes` parameter is inserted before it. Any existing caller passing `produce_to_pipe` positionally will now bind that callable to `flusher_processes` and leave `produce_to_pipe` as `None`, causing `SpanFlusher` to try to use the callable as a process count (and to start multiprocessing instead of the pipe/thread path). Either keep `produce_to_pipe`’s original position or make callers use keyword arguments consistently.

title: Added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op because `time.sleep` is monkeypatched away
body: The test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to a no-op at line 15 (`monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`), which replaces the global `time.sleep`. The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 (and `join()`'s internal sleeps) therefore return immediately and do not actually give the background flusher thread any time to produce. The comment 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' is false, so the test still races `step.join()` (which sets `stopped=True`, causing the flusher loop to exit without flushing) against the flusher thread. This makes `test_basic` flaky: `(msg,) = messages` can fail with an empty list. The wait should use an un-patched sleep (e.g. `from time import sleep as real_sleep` or poll until `messages` is populated), not the patched `time.sleep`.

title: Hung thread workers are never stopped and get duplicated on restart
body: `_ensure_processes_alive` only calls `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. In the `produce_to_pipe` code path (used by tests), workers are `threading.Thread` instances, so a thread flagged as hung (healthy_since exceeded `spans.buffer.flusher.max-unhealthy-seconds`) is never stopped. `_create_process_for_shards` is then called for the same shards, creating a second thread with a fresh `SpansBuffer`. Two flusher threads then concurrently call `flush_segments`/`done_flush_segments` on the same shards, producing duplicate segment messages and racing on segment acks. Thread mode should either be excluded from the health-restart logic or the old thread must be cooperatively stopped before spawning a replacement.

title: Docstring claims one process per shard but default is a single shared process
body: The class docstring now says 'Creates one process per shard for parallel processing.' The implementation actually creates `min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))` processes and round-robins shards across them (`i % num_processes`). Moreover, the `--flusher-processes` click option defaults to 1, so with default configuration a single process handles all shards (the original behavior). The docstring misrepresents both the sharding scheme and the default; it should say that shards are distributed across up to `max_processes` flusher processes and that the default is one process for all shards.

title: Inconsistent metric tag name (`shard` vs `shards`) and misleading shard tag value
body: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` (line 185) and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` (line 192) tag with `{"shard": shard_tag}`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` (line 199) tags with `{"shards": shard_tag}`. `shard_tag` is a comma-joined list of all shards handled by the process, not a single shard. The mismatched tag key means dashboards/alerts filtering on `shard` will silently miss `wait_produce`, and the singular `shard` tag now carries a multi-value string, breaking per-shard aggregation that previously keyed on a single (or absent) shard. Use one consistent tag key and document that its value is a shard list.

title: `_create_process_for_shard` is dead code
body: The newly added `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` method (lines 127-132) is never called anywhere in the codebase; `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly. Leaving unused code adds maintenance burden and suggests a shard-level restart path that does not exist. It should be removed (or wired up) before merge.

title: Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched in this test
body: test_basic does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at module-attribute level, so the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` (with the comment "Give flusher threads time to process after drift change") does not sleep at all — it calls the patched lambda. The intended delay to let the flusher thread observe the drift change before `step.join()` sets `stopped=True` never happens, so the test relies on the busy-spinning thread happening to flush in time and can be flaky. Note test_flusher.py avoids this because it does `from time import sleep`, which still references the real function. Use the same import pattern (or patch differently) so the delay is real.

title: New multiprocess test only checks bookkeeping, not flush correctness
body: test_flusher_processes_limit asserts `len(flusher.processes) == 2`, `max_processes == 2`, `num_processes == 2`, and that the shard count sums to 4. It never writes spans to the shared-process shards and verifies that exactly the expected segments are flushed to the produce pipe (and not duplicated or dropped). Since the whole point of this PR is to safely shard flushing across processes, a regression where a shard is never flushed, or two processes flush the same shard, would still pass this test. Add an end-to-end assertion on produced output for the multi-process/shared-shard case.

title: Inconsistent metric tag key ("shards" vs "shard") on wait_produce timer
body: The `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer now uses `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` while the sibling metrics `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`. The label name is different, so dashboards/alerts that slice by `shard` across these metrics will silently omit wait_produce. Use the same key (`shard`) for all three.

title: Class docstring claims one process per shard, but default creates a single process for all shards
body: The docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing", but `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))` and `max_processes` defaults to 1 (both in the click option default and via `max_processes or len(...)` when None). With the default, all shards are handled by a single process, and even when `max_processes < num_shards` multiple shards share a process. The docstring misdescribes the actual behavior and should state that shards are distributed across up to `max_processes` flusher processes.

title: join() timeouts leave remaining flusher processes un-terminated; remaining_time is unused
body: In `join()`, when the deadline elapses (`remaining_time <= 0`) the loop `break`s, so the remaining child processes in `self.processes` are neither waited on nor `terminate()`d — only the ones iterated before the break are terminated. Additionally `remaining_time` is computed but never used. On a bounded-timeout shutdown/rebalance this can leave flusher processes running past the deadline (relying on daemon-kill at parent exit), which could keep producing segments concurrently with a new assignment. Terminate/join the remaining processes after the loop (or handle them explicitly) instead of breaking out silently.

title: Uses Python 3.13-only queue shutdown APIs
body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown calls q.shutdown(immediate=False), and OrderedQueueWorker catches queue.ShutDown. queue.Queue.shutdown and queue.ShutDown were added in Python 3.13; this repository runs on an older Python. On that runtime every q.shutdown call raises AttributeError (which is only logged), the blocked worker get() calls are never woken, and worker.join(timeout=5.0) is then called for each of the 20 workers. Shutdown can hang for roughly 100 seconds and leak daemon threads, and the new tests that call shutdown can time out.

title: Worker marks offsets complete even when processing fails
body: OrderedQueueWorker.run calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in a finally block. If result_processor raises, the exception is logged and the offset is still marked complete, so the commit loop commits past a failed message and it is never retried. This contradicts the strategy docstring guarantee that offsets are committed only after successful processing. The problem is worse in real use because ResultProcessor.__call__ catches its own exceptions, so failures look like success to the worker. The new test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling expects no commit for a failing message, but it stops 0.2s after processing, before the commit loop's 1s interval, so it does not catch this behavior.

title: Offset tracker can commit past a gap after the first commit
body: get_committable_offsets computes start = max(last_committed + 1, min(all_offsets)). After 100 is committed, mark_committed removes it, leaving all_offsets={102} if 101 was not submitted. start then becomes 102, and a completed 102 is committed without ever seeing 101. The tracker therefore does not actually block commits across a gap except while last_committed+1 is still inside the tracked set. This contradicts the documented guarantee and the intent of test_offset_gaps_block_commits/test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_gaps; if 101 is expected to arrive later, it can be skipped.

title: Strategy close permanently shuts down the factory-owned shared queue pool
body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ and passes that same object to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy returned by create_with_partitions. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close, which is called through join on partition revocation, calls queue_pool.shutdown(), permanently stopping the workers and queues. On a subsequent partition assignment the factory reuses the same shut-down pool, so submits go to a dead queue pool and offsets stop being committed. Factory.shutdown then calls shutdown again on the same object. Either create/dispose a pool per strategy, or do not tear down the factory-owned pool from the strategy's close.

title: Graceful shutdown exits workers before draining queued work
body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True for every worker before calling q.shutdown(immediate=False). The worker loop condition is `while not self.shutdown`, so after finishing the current item a worker exits and never calls get() again; queued items are left unprocessed. The immediate=False drain semantics therefore never happen, and close abandons pending queued work while its offsets remain uncommitted. The stop flag should be set only after the queues have drained, or the worker loop should continue processing non-empty queues after shutdown is requested.

title: Queues are unbounded, so there is no backpressure despite the doc claim
body: FixedQueuePool constructs queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and submit only calls put(), which never blocks. If one subscription is slow, its queue and OffsetTracker.all_offsets grow without bound while the consumer keeps polling, which can eventually OOM the consumer. The class docstring promises "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", but nothing limits the queue depth or propagates pressure back to the consumer. Use bounded queues and/or block or stop polling when total queued work exceeds a threshold.

title: Failed work items are marked completed and committed
body: In OrderedQueueWorker.run, complete_offset is called in a finally block, so it runs even when result_processor raises. The exception is logged and swallowed, and the commit thread then treats the offset as successfully processed and commits it. A transient processing failure therefore loses the message instead of retrying it; the new error-handling test also expects the offset not to be committed after a processing failure.

title: Submit exceptions are converted into successful offsets
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit catches every exception from decoding, grouping, or enqueueing, then calls add_offset and complete_offset for the message. That marks the message as processed even though no work item was queued, so the offset is committed and the message is dropped. Failures should propagate or be routed to a DLQ rather than being completed.

title: OffsetTracker can commit past a gap after the first commit
body: get_committable_offsets starts at max(last_committed + 1, min_offset). After marking offset 100 committed, all_offsets is pruned and if the remaining set is {102, 103}, start becomes 102, so the method returns 103 and commits offset 104 even though offset 101 was never added or processed. This contradicts the class's stated guarantee and the new gap test; once the first commit occurs, a missing prior offset is no longer treated as blocking.

title: Uses Python 3.13-only queue shutdown APIs
body: Queue.shutdown() and queue.ShutDown were added in Python 3.13. On the older Python versions supported by this repository, q.shutdown raises AttributeError (caught and logged), leaving workers blocked in Queue.get() and making the join timeouts ineffective. Additionally, when a worker catches a processing exception, evaluating the except queue.ShutDown clause raises AttributeError and kills the worker thread.

title: Queues are unbounded, so there is no backpressure
body: Each queue is created with queue.Queue() without a maxsize, and submit always enqueues immediately. If one group or worker is slow, the consumer continues pulling Kafka messages into memory without limit. The documented 'natural backpressure when queues fill up' never happens, and a slow group can cause unbounded memory growth or an OOM.

title: Shutdown does not drain queued work
body: shutdown sets worker.shutdown = True before calling queue.shutdown(immediate=False). Because the worker checks that flag at the top of its loop, it exits after at most the current item and leaves any remaining queued items unprocessed, even though immediate=False is intended to allow draining. This makes the advertised graceful shutdown incomplete and leaves pending offsets uncommitted.

title: Unbounded work queues provide no backpressure
body: FixedQueuePool builds each work queue as an unbounded `queue.Queue()` and `submit()` never blocks; `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.poll()` only records a gauge. If a group's single worker falls behind (e.g. one slow subscription), its queue grows without bound while the consumer keeps polling and advancing/committing offsets, consuming memory and risking OOM. The class docstring's claim 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up' is therefore false. Use a bounded queue (maxsize) and either block in submit() or stop polling when queues are full.

title: Graceful shutdown abandons queued items instead of draining
body: OrderedQueueWorker.run() tests `while not self.shutdown` *before* calling `queue.get()`. In FixedQueuePool.shutdown() (line 231) every worker's `shutdown` flag is set to True, and only afterwards is `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` called. Because the loop exits as soon as the flag is set, a worker processes at most the one item it had already fetched and then drops everything still queued, so the `immediate=False` drain semantics never take effect. In-flight results are silently discarded on a graceful shutdown. The loop should keep calling `get()` and break only when it raises `queue.ShutDown`.

title: Failed results are still committed and lost (no retry/DLQ)
body: Offset completion happens in a `finally` block, so `complete_offset()` runs even when `result_processor` raises, and `ResultProcessor.__call__` already swallows all exceptions internally. Combined with the offset tracker, a message whose processing permanently fails is still considered done, committed, and never retried or routed to a DLQ — it is silently lost, contradicting the class docstring's 'Only commits offsets after successful processing'. Similarly, submit() (line 317) catches exceptions from decoding/grouping and marks the offset complete, dropping those messages. Errors must leave the offset outstanding (or send to DLQ) rather than be committed.

title: Commit thread stopped before queue drain, leaving work uncommitted
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() sets shutdown_event and joins the commit thread *before* calling queue_pool.shutdown(). Items still drained by the workers after that point complete their offsets but the commit thread is already dead, so those offsets are never committed and the results are reprocessed on restart (duplicates). terminate() also calls the graceful queue_pool.shutdown() rather than abandoning pending work. The queue should be drained/shut down before the commit thread stops, and terminate/close should have distinct semantics (drop vs flush).

title: join() ignores its timeout and can block for ~100s
body: join(timeout) discards the argument and delegates to close(), which calls FixedQueuePool.shutdown(). shutdown() joins each worker sequentially with a hard-coded `timeout=5.0`; with the default 20 queues that is up to ~100 seconds of blocking in the worst case, far beyond arroyo's expected join timeout and potentially past the broker's max.poll.interval.ms during shutdown/rebalance. Respect the passed timeout and join workers against a shared deadline.

title: arroyo Commit invoked from a background thread
body: The commit function passed into create_with_partitions (arroyo's `Commit`) is called every second from a dedicated `commit_thread`, i.e. concurrently with the consumer's poll loop and rebalance handling, whereas every other mode commits from the strategy's processing thread. arroyo's Commit is not designed for cross-thread invocation; if it is not fully thread-safe this can corrupt or lose committed offsets. Either serialize commit calls onto the strategy thread (a lock coordinated with poll/join) or confirm arroyo's Commit is safe to call from another thread.

title: Error-handling test asserts behavior the implementation cannot produce
body: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling patches ResultProcessor.__call__ to raise for the first message and then asserts `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`, i.e. that a failed message blocks the commit. But the worker calls complete_offset() in a `finally` even when result_processor raises, so both offsets 100 and 101 are marked complete and are committed; the assertion will fail. Either the exception handling must leave failed offsets outstanding, or the test's expectation is wrong and must be corrected to match the current commit-on-error behavior.

title: test_stats_reporting is racy against active workers
body: test_stats_reporting submits 10 items to a pool with 3 already-running worker threads and immediately asserts `stats['total_items'] > 0`. The workers can consume all items before get_stats() executes, making total_items 0 and flaking the test. Make it deterministic by asserting on a state that cannot race with consumption (e.g. pause/block the workers, or check committed counts rather than instantaneous queue depth).

title: PasswordField type prop is overridden when props.type is passed
body: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` (line 176), `<PasswordField type="password" ... />` is rendered. In `PasswordField` (`packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx`), `{...props}` is spread after `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` on `<InputField>`. When `type="password"` is passed by the caller, it overwrites the computed `type` attribute, so clicking the show/hide password eye button in `EnableTwoFactorModal` has no effect and the password stays masked.

title: Third-party (Google/SAML) 2FA login cannot use backup codes and fails if attempted
body: When a user with a third-party identity provider (e.g., Google or SAML) and 2FA enabled logs in, they are redirected to `/auth/login?totp=<jwt>`, which sets `totpEmail`. In `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` (lines 180-182), `ExternalTotpFooter` is rendered instead of `TwoFactorFooter` when `totpEmail` is set, so the "Lost access" button to enter a backup code is never shown. Furthermore, in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (lines 113-119), the third-party IdP checks (`if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode)`) only check `!credentials.totpCode` and not `!credentials.backupCode`, so even if a backup code were submitted without a `totpCode`, `authorize` would throw `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` instead of verifying the backup code.

title: First E2E test does not close backup codes modal and uses an unawaited promise in expect
body: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` (lines 52-53), after `fillOtp` completes in the first test (`"should allow a user to enable 2FA and login using 2FA"`), the modal transitions to the new `DisplayBackupCodes` step, which keeps the modal open and blocks `onEnable()` from being called until the user clicks `[data-testid="backup-codes-close"]` (unlike the second test at line 125). The test only passes because `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` checks the truthiness of an unawaited `Promise<boolean>` (which is always truthy) instead of `await expect(page.locator(...)).toBeChecked()`, and the subsequent step immediately navigates away with `page.goto("/auth/logout")`.

title: `{...props}` in `PasswordField` overrides `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` when caller passes `type="password"`
body: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` (line 176), `<TextField type="password" ... />` was replaced with `<PasswordField type="password" ... />`. However, inside `PasswordField` (`packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx`), `{...props}` is spread after `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}`. Because `EnableTwoFactorModal` explicitly passes `type="password"`, that prop overwrites the computed `type`, so clicking the show/hide password eye toggle button in the Enable 2FA modal has no effect and the password always remains hidden. Either remove `type="password"` in `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` or spread `{...props}` before `type` in `PasswordField`.

title: Third-party IdP 2FA login (`?totp=`) cannot use backup codes
body: In `authorize`, lines 114, 118, and 122 only skip the `IdentityProvider.CAL` and password checks when `credentials.totpCode` is truthy (`!credentials.totpCode`), not when `credentials.backupCode` is provided. Also, in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` (line 180), when `totpEmail` is set (the OAuth/SAML 2FA flow via `/auth/login?totp=...`), `ExternalTotpFooter` is rendered instead of `TwoFactorFooter`, which hides the "Lost access" button altogether, and even if a backup code were submitted, `authorize` would reject the login with `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` because `credentials.totpCode` is empty. Users who log in via Google or SAML with 2FA enabled are therefore unable to use backup codes.

title: `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` passes a Promise to `expect()` without awaiting it, and the first test never closes the backup codes step
body: In the first e2e test (`should allow a user to enable 2FA and login using 2FA`), after `fillOtp` enables 2FA, the modal transitions to the new `DisplayBackupCodes` step and stays open (because `onEnable` is now only called when clicking `backup-codes-close`). The test does not click `backup-codes-close`, and as noted by the `FIXME` comment added on line 50, `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` only passes because `isChecked()` returns a `Promise<boolean>`, and a Promise object is always truthy in synchronous `.toBeTruthy()`—the switch is actually still unchecked in the UI (`onEnable` was never invoked). The test should click `backup-codes-close` and use `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]')).toBeChecked()` (or check `data-state="checked"`).

title: Closing the modal on the backup codes step via backdrop or Escape key leaves 2FA UI state stale and modal state unreset
body: In `EnableTwoFactorModal`, enabling 2FA now transitions to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` and defers calling `onEnable()` and `resetState()` until the user clicks the "Close" button (`data-testid="backup-codes-close"`). However, `<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>` still allows the user to dismiss the dialog by clicking the backdrop, pressing Escape, or clicking the dialog's close icon, which triggers `onOpenChange` directly without calling `onEnable()` or `resetState()`. Because the backend has already enabled 2FA at that point, dismissing the dialog that way leaves the parent settings page showing 2FA as disabled and leaves `step` stuck on `DisplayBackupCodes` if the modal is reopened.

title: Third-party IdP users with 2FA enabled cannot log in or use backup codes
body: In `next-auth-options.ts` (lines 114-129), the checks for third-party identity providers (`user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL`) and password verification only skip execution when `credentials.totpCode` is truthy (`!credentials.totpCode`), without checking `credentials.backupCode`. Furthermore, in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` (lines 180-183), when `totpEmail` is set (the JWT-based 2FA flow used for Google/SAML logins), `ExternalTotpFooter` is rendered instead of `TwoFactorFooter`, so the "Lost access" button to switch to a backup code is never shown, and even if a backup code were submitted, `authorize` would reject it with `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` because `credentials.totpCode` is empty.

title: First 2FA E2E test does not complete the new backup codes step and passes due to a broken assertion
body: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, the first test (`"should allow a user to enable 2FA and login using 2FA"`) was not updated to close the new backup codes modal step (`backup-codes-close`) after `fillOtp`. As noted by the `FIXME` comment added on line 50, `expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` passes only because `isChecked()` returns a `Promise<boolean>` (which is always truthy when not `await`ed and without `.resolves`), while the modal is still open over the page and `onEnable()` has never been called.

title: Unchecked property access on `mainHostDestinationCalendar` throws TypeError when `destinationCalendar` is empty or null
body: In `EventManager.create`, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` as `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or `[]`. On line 119, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining (`?.`). Any booking with `location === MeetLocationType` (`integrations:google:meet`) and no destination calendar configured will throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` instead of falling back to `integrations:daily`.

title: Co-host destinationCalendars are silently dropped when the organizer has no destinationCalendar
body: On lines 1063-1067, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set. On line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining, which is a no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`. As a result, in a collective event where the main organizer has no destination calendar set on their account/event type, all other hosts' destination calendars in `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded and their calendar events are never created.

title: `calendar.events.patch` for Meet link uses `undefined` calendarId instead of falling back to `"primary"`
body: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, `selectedCalendar` was previously defaulted to `"primary"` (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.externalId ? ... : "primary"`). Now `selectedCalendar` is `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, which can be `undefined` (for example, when `destination.credentialId` is not set or no entry matches). While `calendar.events.insert` on line 154 uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, the subsequent `calendar.events.patch` call on line 168 passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly without `|| "primary"`, causing the patch that adds the Google Meet hangout link to the event description to fail.

title: Fallback lookup in `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` compares `cal.externalId` against falsy `externalCalendarId`
body: In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback branch of the ternary `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`""`, `null`, or `undefined`). Searching for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` in that branch can therefore never match a valid calendar `externalId` and will always evaluate to `undefined` (replacing the previous fallback to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). In `updateEvent`, this passes `calendarId: undefined` to `calendar.events.update`.

title: Removed `organization` selection from `loadUsers` breaks organization slug resolution for dynamic bookings
body: In `loadUsers` (lines 735-739), `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` was removed from the `prisma.user.findMany` select clause when `!eventTypeId` (dynamic group bookings). The inferred return type of `loadUsers` and downstream code that accesses `user.organization.slug` on dynamic booking users will no longer have `organization` loaded.

title: Unrelated change in organization `createHandler` inverts `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` slug logic
body: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts` line 151, `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` was changed to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. When team billing is enabled, the slug is supposed to be held in `metadata.requestedSlug` (line 153) until billing is completed, and only set directly on `slug` when billing is disabled (`!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`). Flipping this condition sets `slug` immediately when billing is enabled and leaves `slug` unset when billing is disabled, breaking self-hosted/non-billed organization creation and bypassing the billing gate on billed instances.

title: Missing optional chaining on `mainHostDestinationCalendar` throws TypeError when `destinationCalendar` is empty or null
body: In `EventManager.create`, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` as `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or `[]`. The very next line accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining (`if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`), which will throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` whenever a Google Meet booking is created for a user or event type without a destinationCalendar.

title: Co-hosts' destination calendars are dropped in collective events when the main organizer has no destination calendar
body: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set (lines 1063-1067). At line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining on `null`, which becomes a no-op. As a result, if the primary host/organizer does not have a `destinationCalendar` configured, none of the collective co-hosts' destination calendars in `teamDestinationCalendars` are added to `evt.destinationCalendar`.

title: `calendar.events.patch` receives `calendarId: undefined` when `selectedCalendar` is not found
body: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, `selectedCalendar` was previously defaulted to `"primary"` at assignment, so both `calendar.events.insert` and the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` (when a `hangoutLink` is generated) received `"primary"`. With this change, `selectedCalendar` can be `undefined` and `|| "primary"` was only added to `calendar.events.insert` (line 154). At line 168, `calendar.events.patch` still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which will be `undefined` and cause the Google Calendar API patch call to fail when `selectedCalendar` is not set.

title: Fallback lookup in `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` searches for a falsy `externalCalendarId`
body: In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback branch of the ternary runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`""`, `null`, or `undefined`), yet it evaluates `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Because `externalCalendarId` is falsy in that branch, it looks for a calendar whose `externalId` is `""` / `null` / `undefined` instead of falling back to the event's destination calendar (e.g., `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`), so `selectedCalendar` will be `undefined` (`updateEvent` doesn't even fallback to `"primary"`).

title: `organization` relation removed from `loadUsers` query for dynamic bookings
body: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` selection was removed from the `prisma.user.findMany` query in `loadUsers` when `!eventTypeId` (dynamic group bookings). Elsewhere in `handleNewBooking.ts`, `organizerUser.organization?.slug` is used to build `bookerUrl`, so dynamic bookings for users in an organization will now have `organization` undefined and generate incorrect URLs.

title: Unrelated and inverted `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` slug logic in organization creation
body: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts` (lines 151-153), an unrelated change flips `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` when setting `slug`. When billing is enabled, the slug is supposed to be held in `metadata.requestedSlug` until payment completes and only set directly on the team when billing is disabled (`!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`). With this change, self-hosted / billing-disabled instances no longer get `slug` or `requestedSlug` set at all on organization creation, and billing-enabled instances set both `slug` and `requestedSlug` immediately.

title: Unconditional property access on `mainHostDestinationCalendar` throws `TypeError` when `destinationCalendar` is empty or null
body: In `EventManager.create`, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` is followed immediately by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without optional chaining. Whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or `[]` (which happens for any user without a configured destination calendar) and `evt.location === MeetLocationType`, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and this line throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`, crashing booking creation.

title: Co-hosts' destination calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar
body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set. On line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op because of optional chaining on `null`. In a collective event where the main host has no destination calendar configured (e.g., relying on fallback or no calendar) but other hosts do have destination calendars, all co-hosts' destination calendars are silently discarded and their calendar events are never created. Initialize `destinationCalendar` as `[]` or assign `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

title: `calendar.events.patch` uses `undefined` `calendarId` instead of `"primary"` fallback
body: Previously `selectedCalendar` defaulted to `"primary"`. After this change, `selectedCalendar` is `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, which is `undefined` when no matching entry exists (or `externalId` is not set). While `calendar.events.insert` uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, the subsequent `calendar.events.patch` call (used to add the Google Meet `hangoutLink` to the event description) passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly, causing the patch request to fail with a missing `calendarId`.

title: Fallback lookup in `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` searches for falsy `externalCalendarId`
body: In `updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback branch of `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`""`, `null`, or `undefined`). Searching `event.destinationCalendar` for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` in that branch can therefore never match a valid calendar ID and will always evaluate to `undefined` (causing `updateEvent` to pass `calendarId: undefined` to Google Calendar API).

title: Unrelated change inverts `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` condition for organization `slug`
body: Line 151 changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. When team billing is enabled, organizations are supposed to store only `requestedSlug` in metadata until payment/verification completes, and only set `slug` directly when billing is disabled (`!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`). Inverting this condition breaks organization creation when billing is disabled (slug is never set) and prematurely assigns the live slug before billing when billing is enabled. This also appears to be an accidental change unrelated to `destinationCalendar`.

title: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses `[z.string().toString()]` as object keys, evaluating to `"[object Object]"`
body: In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, the computed property names `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate at runtime to the literal string key `"[object Object]"`.
