Because `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, parsing any token response with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` strips the actual expiry field (e.g. `expires_in` or `expiry_date`) and every other field except `access_token`. To allow arbitrary additional fields or numeric expiry fields, use `.passthrough()` or `.catchall(...)` instead of computed keys on `z.string()`.

title: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` return wrapper is saved directly as the credential `key` in the database
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed data itself. In `GoogleCalendarService`, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` is written directly to `prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key } })`. This overwrites `credential.key` in the database with `{ success: true, data: { ... } }`, which corrupts the stored credential and causes `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on line 75 to throw a validation error on every subsequent request.

title: `prisma` is used without being imported and refreshed `access_token` is never passed to `jsforce.Connection`
body: In `SalesforceCalendarService.getClient`: (1) `prisma.credential.update(...)` is called on line 96, but `prisma` is never imported in this file, causing a `ReferenceError` at runtime and breaking type-checking; (2) the token refresh `fetch` on line 75 does not use `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential syncing is bypassed; and (3) after refreshing the token, `new jsforce.Connection` on line 106 still passes the old `credentialKey.access_token` instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

title: `credentialId` is passed instead of `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`, and `fetch` response is incompatible with `axios` response
body: In `BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, `credentialId` (`credential.id`) is passed as the third argument (`userId`) to `refreshOAuthTokens`, sending the credential ID instead of the user ID as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint. Additionally, when credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a native `fetch` `Response` object, whereas the callback uses `axios.post` which returns `{ data: ... }`. Accessing `tokenInfo.data.error` on line 96 will throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')` whenever syncing is enabled. The same `axios` vs `fetch` response mismatch also affects `GoogleCalendarService` (line 94), `ZohoCrmCalendarService` (line 217), and `HubspotCalendarService` (line 192, where the SDK returns the token object directly rather than a `Response`).

title: Google Calendar credential key is saved as Zod SafeParseReturnType `{ success: true, data: ... }` instead of the token object
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), whereas previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the parsed token object directly. On lines 97-100, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` is written straight to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. After the first token refresh, the stored `credential.key` in the database becomes `{ success: true, data: { ... } }`, so the next time `GoogleCalendarService` is instantiated `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) will fail with a Zod validation error and break Google Calendar integration for that user.

title: `prisma` is not imported in Salesforce `CalendarService.ts` and `refreshOAuthTokens` is never called
body: `prisma.credential.update` is called on line 96, but `prisma` is not imported anywhere in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`. This causes a TypeScript compilation error and a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime whenever Salesforce is used. Additionally, the token refresh `fetch` on line 75 was not wrapped in `refreshOAuthTokens`, and lines 106-107 pass the stale `credentialKey.access_token` to `new jsforce.Connection(...)` instead of the newly refreshed `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

title: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses `[z.string().toString()]` which defines literal `"[object Object]"` keys and strips expiry fields
body: In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` evaluate `toString()` on Zod schema instances, producing the literal property name `"[object Object]"` (and overwriting the first with the second). Because `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` strips every field except `access_token` (including `expires_in` / `expiry_date`) and does not require any numeric expiry field. Callers such as Zoom (`newTokens.expires_in * 1000`), Google (`token.expiry_date`), and Office365 then compute `NaN` or `undefined` for the token expiration.

title: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response`, breaking callers that expect an Axios/googleapis response with `.data`
body: When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` calls `fetch(...)` and returns a standard `Response` object (where the JSON payload is accessed via `await response.json()`). However, several callers pass callbacks that return objects with a `.data` property and immediately read `res.data`: `GoogleCalendarService` (`const token = res?.data` on line 94), `BiginCalendarService` (`tokenInfo.data` on line 96), `ZohoCrmCalendarService` (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` on line 217), and `HubspotCalendarService` (which expects a parsed `HubspotToken` object directly on line 192). When syncing is enabled, `res.data` is `undefined` and token refresh throws a `TypeError` in all of those integrations.

title: Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId` instead of `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`
body: `refreshAccessToken` receives `credentialId` (`credential.id`) and passes it as the third argument (`userId`) to `refreshOAuthTokens` on line 93. `refreshOAuthTokens` sends this value as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint, so the sync endpoint will be queried with the credential's primary key ID rather than the Cal.com user's ID.

title: Requests to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are sent without any authentication header
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` sends a `POST` request with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no secret or signature header (such as `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). Any party that can reach `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` can request fresh OAuth access tokens for arbitrary `calcomUserId` values without authentication.

title: Google Calendar credential key is overwritten with a Zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full `SafeParseReturnType` object (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), whereas `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` previously returned the unwrapped credential object. Passing that wrapper directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` stores `{ success: true, data: { ... } }` in `credential.key`. On the next instantiation of `GoogleCalendarService`, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on line 75 will fail because the top-level keys (`access_token`, `refresh_token`, etc.) are now nested under `data`, breaking Google Calendar for the user after the first token refresh.

title: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses `[z.string().toString()]` as literal property keys and strips unknown fields
body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` do not define index signatures in Zod; they evaluate `.toString()` on the schema object (producing `"[object Object]"`) and register a literal property with that name requiring a `number` (overwritten by `z.unknown().optional()`). Because `z.object` strips unrecognised keys by default, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` strips every field except `access_token` (including `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, `refresh_token`, etc.). When credential syncing is enabled, callers like Office365 and Zoom receive `undefined` for the expiry field, leading to `NaN` expiry dates or broken credentials.

title: `prisma` is not imported, `refreshOAuthTokens` is not used, and refreshed token is not passed to jsforce
body: Three issues in `SalesforceCalendarService.getClient`: (1) `prisma.credential.update` is called on line 96, but `prisma` is never imported in this file, causing a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime; (2) the token refresh `fetch` on line 75 is called directly instead of through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce credentials are never synced via `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and every `getClient` call unconditionally hits Salesforce's token endpoint; (3) lines 105-107 still pass `credentialKey.access_token` (the old token) instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` when constructing `new jsforce.Connection(...)`.

title: Return type mismatch between `fetch` in `refreshOAuthTokens` and Google/HubSpot/Zoho callers
body:
`refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` object when `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is enabled, but returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns when disabled. Several callers expect library-specific return shapes instead of a `fetch` `Response`:
- `GoogleCalendarService` (line 94) reads `res?.data` (an axios/gaxios response property), which is `undefined` on a `fetch` `Response`, causing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'access_token')`.
- `HubspotCalendarService` (`packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177`) expects a parsed `HubspotToken` object (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`, `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken`), which do not exist on a `fetch` `Response`.
- `BiginCalendarService` (`packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:96`) and `ZohoCrmCalendarService` (`packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:217`) expect an Axios response with `.data`, which is `undefined` on a `fetch` `Response`.

title: `credentialId` is passed instead of `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`
body: `refreshAccessToken` passes `credentialId` (the primary key of the `Credential` row) as the third argument (`userId`) to `refreshOAuthTokens`. When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` sends this value as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint, requesting tokens for the wrong user ID.

title: Webex token refresh does not use `parseRefreshTokenResponse`
body: `webexAuth` calls `refreshOAuthTokens` on line 62, but still validates the response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse(responseBody)` on line 88 instead of `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. When `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is used and returns only the minimum token response (access token and expiry), `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` fails validation because `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in` are required.

title: Sync webhook stores raw `keys` without setting `refresh_token` fallback required by app schemas
body: When credentials are created or updated via `/api/webhook/app-credential`, the decrypted `keys` payload from the parent application (which according to the PR only needs to provide the access token and expiry) is written directly to `prisma.credential` without ensuring a `refresh_token` placeholder is present or transforming `expires_in` to `expiry_date`. Integrations such as `GoogleCalendarService` (`googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)`) and `ZoomVideoApiAdapter` (`zoomTokenSchema.parse(credential.key)`) parse `credential.key` before calling `refreshAccessToken` and require `refresh_token: z.string()` (and for Zoom, `scope`, `token_type`, `expiry_date`), so initial parsing of synced credentials will fail before any refresh can occur.

title: Team admin/owner permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`. Because a team member has a single role (either `ADMIN` or `OWNER`), depending on how `isTeamAdmin` is implemented (whether it strictly checks `role === 'ADMIN'`), using `&&` requires both conditions to be true simultaneously. This should use `||` so that either a team admin or a team owner is authorized to add guests.

title: EventManager is initialized with the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
body: `addGuestsHandler` allows an attendee or team admin/owner (who is not the booking organizer) to add guests, but lines 158-163 build `EventManager` using `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. When an attendee or another team admin calls `addGuests`, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will try to update the calendar event using the caller's credentials and user record rather than the booking organizer's (`booking.user`), causing calendar updates to fail or target the wrong account.

title: Duplicate emails in `input.guests` and case differences bypass deduplication and blacklist checks
body: In `addGuestsHandler`, `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing `booking.attendees` and `blacklistedGuestEmails` using exact case-sensitive string matching (`guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), while `blacklistedGuestEmails` was lowercased on line 71. Additionally, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts` does not enforce uniqueness on `input.guests` (only client-side validation in `AddGuestsDialog` does). Calling the procedure directly with duplicate emails or uppercase characters in `guests` will insert duplicate attendee rows, bypass `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, and send `guests` (rather than `uniqueGuests`) to `sendAddGuestsEmails` on line 168.

title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores event type email disable settings (`disableStandardEmails`)
body: Unlike `sendScheduledEmails`, `sendRescheduledEmails`, and `sendLocationChangeEmails` right above it, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept `eventTypeMetadata` or check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)`. Bookings on event types where standard host or attendee emails are disabled will still send emails when guests are added.

title: Team admin/owner permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Because `isTeamAdmin` checks `role === "ADMIN"` and `isTeamOwner` checks `role === "OWNER"`, a single membership cannot satisfy both conditions unless `isTeamAdmin` also accepts `OWNER` (and even then, `&&` restricts it to owners only, blocking team admins). It should use `||` so that either a team admin or a team owner is permitted to add guests.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials
body: `addGuestsHandler` allows an attendee or team admin/owner (who may not be the booking organizer) to add guests, but lines 158–163 instantiate `EventManager` with `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. When an attendee or another team admin calls this endpoint, `EventManager` will try to update the calendar event using the caller's credentials rather than the organizer's (`booking.user`), causing the calendar update to fail or target the wrong account.

title: Duplicate emails in `input.guests` and case-variant emails bypass deduplication and blacklist checks
body:
`uniqueGuests` only filters against existing `booking.attendees` and `blacklistedGuestEmails` using exact case-sensitive string comparisons, and does not deduplicate within `input.guests` itself:
1. If a client calls the tRPC procedure directly with `guests: ["a@b.com", "a@b.com"]` (since `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` does not enforce uniqueness), duplicate attendee rows will be created.
2. `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased on line 71, but `guest` is not lowercased before `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` or before comparing with `attendee.email`, so `User@Example.com` bypasses both the blacklist and existing-attendee checks.

title: Raw `guests` array passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of filtered `uniqueGuests`
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the unfiltered `guests` input rather than `uniqueGuests`. If `guests` contains an email that was already an attendee on the booking (filtered out of `uniqueGuests`), `sendAddGuestsEmails` will match `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` for that existing attendee and send them an `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`.

title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores event type `disableStandardEmails` metadata settings
body: Other email manager functions (such as `sendLocationChangeEmails` and `sendScheduledEmails`) accept `eventTypeMetadata` and check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` before sending emails to the host or attendees. `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not check these flags, so adding guests will send emails even when standard emails are disabled on the event type.

title: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` instead of `||`, blocking team admins from adding guests
body: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts` at lines 46-48, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Because `isTeamAdmin` checks for `MembershipRole.ADMIN` and `isTeamOwner` checks for `MembershipRole.OWNER` (or equivalent mutually exclusive/distinct roles), requiring both to be true means a team admin who is not an owner (or vice versa) will evaluate to `false` and receive a `FORBIDDEN` error when trying to add guests to a team booking. This should use `||` instead of `&&`.

title: Calendar event is updated using the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
body: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts` at lines 158-165, `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` use the currently logged-in caller (`ctx.user`) rather than the booking's organizer (`booking.user`). `addGuestsHandler` explicitly allows attendees and team admins/owners who are not the organizer to add guests (lines 46-56). When an attendee or team admin calls `addGuests`, `EventManager` will try to update the calendar event using the caller's credentials and user record instead of the organizer's, failing to update the organizer's calendar event.

title: Duplicate emails in `input.guests` and case differences bypass deduplication and blacklisting
body:
In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts` at lines 74-78, `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing `booking.attendees` and `blacklistedGuestEmails` using case-sensitive comparisons, and does not deduplicate `input.guests` itself:
1. If the tRPC endpoint is called directly with duplicate entries in `guests` (e.g. `["a@b.com", "a@b.com"]`), `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts` does not enforce uniqueness, so duplicate attendee rows will be created in the database and multiple emails sent.
2. `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased on line 71, but `guest` is not lowercased before `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` or `guest === attendee.email`, so submitting `User@Example.com` bypasses both the blacklist and existing-attendee checks.
3. On line 168, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is passed the raw `guests` array instead of `uniqueGuests`, so if an existing attendee's email was included in `guests`, that existing attendee will receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`.

title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores event type `disableStandardEmails` metadata settings
body: In `packages/emails/email-manager.ts` at lines 525-550, unlike `sendLocationChangeEmails`, `sendScheduledEmails`, and `sendRescheduledEmails`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept `eventTypeMetadata` or check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)`. Event types configured to suppress standard host or attendee emails will still send emails whenever guests are added.

title: `OR` condition in `deleteMany` omits `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and causes a full table scan
body: In `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany`, the second branch of `OR` is `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` without `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. Because `WorkflowReminder` only has indexes on `(method, scheduled, scheduledDate)` and `(cancelled, scheduledDate)` and no index on `retryCount`, an `OR` with an unindexed `retryCount` predicate forces PostgreSQL to scan the entire `WorkflowReminder` table on every cron run (and will also delete non-SMS reminders if any ever use `retryCount`). Keeping `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` at the top level of `where` (or adding `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduled: false` to the second branch so it uses the `(method, scheduled, scheduledDate)` index) scopes the delete to SMS reminders and allows index usage.

title: Caller-appended SQL clauses can bypass authorization due to unparenthesized OR expressions
body: `getAuthorizationConditions`, `getFilterConditions`, and `getBaseConditions` (when `filterConditions` is `null`) return `Prisma.Sql` fragments that have top-level `OR` operators without outer parentheses—for example, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` returns `(("teamId" = ANY($1)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)) OR (("userId" = ANY($2)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false))`, and `buildFilterConditions` with only `eventTypeId` returns `("eventTypeId" = $1) OR ("eventParentId" = $1)`. Because SQL `AND` has higher precedence than `OR`, any caller that interpolates `getBaseConditions()` into a query alongside additional `WHERE` predicates (e.g., `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ${startDate}`) will only apply the trailing `AND` predicate to the right-hand branch of the `OR`, causing the left-hand branch to ignore the additional filter or authorization constraint. Wrap compound `OR` expressions (or the return value of `getBaseConditions` / `getAuthorizationConditions` / `getFilterConditions`) in outer parentheses.

title: Removed caching tests for authorization and filter conditions
body: The `describe("Caching", ...)` block testing that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return cached `Prisma.Sql` instances on repeated calls was deleted rather than updated to the new `Prisma.sql` format, leaving the caching behavior in `InsightsBookingService` (`cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`) untested.

title: Fallback to filterConditions when authConditions is missing can bypass authorization
body: In `getBaseConditions()`, if `authConditions` were ever falsy and `filterConditions` were present, the `else if (filterConditions)` branch would return `filterConditions` alone without any authorization check. Even though `getAuthorizationConditions()` currently returns a `Prisma.Sql` object (`NOTHING_CONDITION` on failure), this fallback logic is dangerous for an authorization gate: if `authConditions` is ever `null`/`undefined`, the method should fail closed and return `NOTHING_CONDITION` rather than returning `filterConditions` unguarded.

title: Removed caching tests for authorization and filter conditions
body: The `describe("Caching", ...)` test block verifying that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` cache their results across calls was deleted in this PR, even though `InsightsBookingService` still implements `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`.

title: Deleting cache does not invalidate the `connectedCalendars` query
body: `deleteCacheMutation` does not call `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled` or `onSuccess` (unlike `disconnectMutation` right below it on lines 61-64). In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`, `onChanged` is optional and is not passed by all callers, so after deleting cached data the `connectedCalendars` query remains stale and the dropdown continues to show the old `cacheUpdatedAt` status and "Delete cached data" action until the page is refreshed.

title: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` includes expired cache entries
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups `CalendarCache` rows by `credentialId` without filtering by `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (whereas `getCachedAvailability` on lines 112 and 127 only treats entries with `expiresAt >= now` as cached). If a credential only has expired cache rows in the database, the UI will still report an active cache status and offer to delete cached data even though no valid cache is being served.

title: `deleteCacheMutation` does not invalidate `connectedCalendars` query after deleting cache
body: `deleteCacheMutation` in `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx` does not invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSuccess` or `onSettled` (unlike `disconnectMutation` right below it on line 62). Because `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` often renders without an `onChanged` callback that refetches connected calendars, `connectedCalendar.cacheUpdatedAt` remains stale in the React Query cache after the user deletes the cache, so the dropdown continues showing the old "Cache Status" and "Delete cached data" action until the page is reloaded.

title: `credentialIds` can contain `null` or `undefined`, causing Prisma validation errors in `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`
body: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, `connectedCalendars.map((cal) => cal.credentialId)` is passed directly to `cacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(credentialIds)`, which executes `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy({ where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } } })`. On `CalendarCache`, `credentialId` is a non-nullable `Int`, whereas `connectedCalendar.credentialId` can be `null` or `undefined` (for example on broken/delegation credentials). Passing `null`/`undefined` inside the `in` array to Prisma for a non-nullable column throws a `PrismaClientValidationError` at runtime and breaks the `connectedCalendars` query. Filter `credentialIds` with `.filter((id): id is number => typeof id === "number")` before querying.

title: `deleteCacheMutation` does not invalidate `connectedCalendars` query after deleting cache
body: `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and invokes `onSuccess?.()`, whereas `disconnectMutation` below it invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`. Because `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` fetches `connectedCalendars` internally and its callers often do not pass an `onChanged` callback that refetches that query, `cacheUpdatedAt` will remain populated in the React Query cache after the user deletes the cache, so the dropdown continues to show the old cache status and 'Delete cached data' option until a manual page refresh. Add `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled` (or `onSuccess`) of `deleteCacheMutation`.

title: `ConnectedCalendarList` receives `disableConnectionModification` instead of `shouldDisableConnectionModification`
body: On line 166, `shouldDisableConnectionModification = isDisabled || disableConnectionModification` is computed and passed to `SelectedCalendarsSettingsHeading`, but line 182 passes the raw `disableConnectionModification` prop to `ConnectedCalendarList`. When `disabledScope === scope` (`isDisabled === true`) and `disableConnectionModification` is not explicitly set, `CredentialActionsDropdown` will still allow disconnecting the integration or deleting cache even though the current scope is disabled. Pass `shouldDisableConnectionModification` (or include `isDisabled`) instead.

title: SendGrid `@sendgrid/client` API key is never set in `scheduleEmailReminders`
body: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` is called on line 19, but `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` (for `@sendgrid/client`) is never called (unlike in `emailReminderManager.ts` lines 25-26). As a result, when this cron endpoint runs in a serverless invocation that hasn't imported `emailReminderManager.ts`, all `client.request(...)` calls—including the new `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` cancellation call at lines 57-64 and `POST /v3/mail/batch` at lines 188-191—will fail with 401 Unauthorized from SendGrid, preventing scheduled email reminders from being cancelled or scheduled.

title: `immediateDelete` in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` bypasses the deferred cancellation queue and leaves stale DB rows
body:
When `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is called with `immediateDelete = true` (which this PR passes when rescheduling a booking in `handleNewBooking.ts:968`, deleting a workflow in `workflows.tsx:214`, or deleting a workflow step in `workflows.tsx:521`), it immediately sends `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` to SendGrid and returns without deleting or updating the `workflowReminder` record in the database. This causes two problems:
1. For reminders scheduled up to 72 hours out, immediate cancellation occupies one of SendGrid's 100 pending `scheduled_sends` cancellation slots until `scheduledDate`—the exact limit this PR was designed to avoid by deferring cancellations to within 1 hour of `scheduledDate`.
2. When rescheduling a booking (`handleNewBooking.ts`), the `workflowReminder` row is neither deleted nor marked `cancelled: true`; if the booking is later cancelled or modified, the reminder will be processed a second time.

title: Cancelling a paid booking returns early before cancelling workflow reminders or scheduled jobs
body: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, if `bookingToDelete.paid` is true (line 363), the handler refunds the payment, updates the booking status to `REJECTED`, and returns early at line 464. Because `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`, and `cancelScheduledJobs` are only invoked at lines 480-493 after that early return, any scheduled email or SMS workflow reminders for a cancelled paid booking are never cancelled and will still be sent to the attendee and host.

title: Unawaited reminder cancellations in `forEach` race with `eventManager.reschedule`
body: In `handleNewBooking.ts` lines 966-972, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async functions invoked inside a synchronous `forEach` without `await` (so the surrounding `try / catch` also cannot catch any rejections). Immediately after, `await eventManager.reschedule(...)` runs, which deletes the old booking's `workflowReminders` via `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany`. The unawaited `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` / `update` calls inside `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` race with `eventManager.reschedule` and will fail with Prisma P2025 (record not found) or may be skipped if the serverless function finishes before the promises settle. The same unawaited `forEach` pattern before deleting the parent record also occurs in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx` at lines 212-225 and 519-531.

title: Passing immediateDelete=true on reschedule bypasses the deferred SendGrid cancellation fix
body: In `handleNewBooking.ts` (when rescheduling a booking) and in `workflows.tsx` (lines 214 and 521, when deleting a workflow or a workflow step), `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is called with `immediateDelete = true`. In `emailReminderManager.ts` (lines 213-223), when `immediateDelete` is true, the function immediately calls `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` on SendGrid instead of marking `cancelled: true` for the cron job to cancel within the 1-hour window, and it also returns early without deleting or updating the `workflowReminder` row in the database. Because workflow steps and workflow reminders are not deleted when a booking is rescheduled (and `immediateDelete` skips the DB update/delete), this both leaves stale `workflowReminder` records in the database and reintroduces the exact SendGrid 100-pending-cancellations limit problem described in the PR for rescheduled bookings and deleted workflows/steps.

title: @sendgrid/client API key is never set in scheduleEmailReminders cron handler
body: `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` imports `client` from `@sendgrid/client` and uses `client.request(...)` at lines 57 and 188, but only calls `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` at line 19 and never calls `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)`. Unless `emailReminderManager.ts` happens to have been imported in the same serverless instance before this API route runs, `@sendgrid/client` has no API key configured and all requests to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` (to cancel emails) and `/v3/mail/batch` will fail with 401 Unauthorized.

title: Unawaited async reminder cancellation calls in forEach loops
body: In `handleCancelBooking.ts` (lines 485-493), `handleNewBooking.ts` (lines 966-972), `bookings.tsx` (lines 488-494), and `workflows.tsx` (lines 212-218, 376-382, 519-525, 574-580), `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async functions invoked inside `.forEach(...)` without `await` or `Promise.all`. In serverless/API route environments, the handler can finish and return the response (or proceed to subsequent DB operations like `workflow.deleteMany` / `workflowStep.delete` in `workflows.tsx`, which cascade-delete the `WorkflowReminder` rows) before the Prisma updates/deletes or Twilio/SendGrid API calls inside those functions complete, causing race conditions, P2025 record-not-found errors, or dropped cancellations.

title: SendGrid `@sendgrid/client` API key is never initialized in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`
body: `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` calls `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` at line 19, but never calls `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` on the imported `@sendgrid/client` instance (unlike `emailReminderManager.ts` which sets both at lines 25-26). In serverless / isolated route environments where `emailReminderManager.ts` has not been imported in the same process, `client.request(...)` at lines 57 and 188 will fail with an unauthorized error from SendGrid, preventing both the cancellation of scheduled emails and the creation of batch IDs for newly scheduled emails.

title: Rescheduling a booking immediately cancels SendGrid batch IDs instead of deferring to the cron job
body: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, when cancelling workflow reminders of the original rescheduled booking, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` is called with `immediateDelete = true`. Inside `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, `immediateDelete = true` bypasses setting `cancelled: true` in the database and immediately calls `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` on SendGrid (and also leaves the `WorkflowReminder` row in the database without deleting it or marking it cancelled). This directly defeats the purpose of the PR for rescheduled bookings—it will still hit SendGrid's 100 pending `scheduled_sends` limit when bookings are rescheduled more than 1 hour in advance—and leaves stale `WorkflowReminder` records attached to the rescheduled booking.

title: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` with `immediateDelete = true` does not delete the `WorkflowReminder` database record
body: When `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is called with `immediateDelete = true` (e.g., when a workflow or step is deleted, or during booking reschedule), it sends the cancel request to SendGrid and returns early at line 222 without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row from `prisma.workflowReminder`. For booking reschedules (`handleNewBooking.ts`), the row is not cascade-deleted because the original booking row is kept with `status: CANCELLED`, leaving orphaned `WorkflowReminder` rows in the database until their `scheduledDate` passes.

title: Cancelling a paid booking returns early before cancelling workflow reminders or scheduled jobs
body: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, if `bookingToDelete.paid` is true (lines 363-465), the handler refunds the payment, marks the booking as `REJECTED`, and returns at line 464. Because the loop that cancels `workflowReminders` (`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`) is at lines 485-493 after this early return, workflow reminders for cancelled paid bookings are never cancelled and will still be sent to the attendee and host.

title: Unawaited `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` calls before deleting workflow or step
body: In `workflowsRouter.delete` (lines 212-225) and `workflowsRouter.update` when a step is deleted (lines 519-531), `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are invoked inside `.forEach(...)` without `await`, immediately followed by `await ctx.prisma.workflow.deleteMany(...)` or `await ctx.prisma.workflowStep.delete(...)`. Because `WorkflowReminder` has `onDelete: Cascade` on `workflowStepId`, the cascade delete races with the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` calls inside `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` and `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (when `referenceId` is null), causing `Record to delete does not exist` Prisma errors, and in serverless environments the unawaited SendGrid/Twilio network requests may be terminated after the mutation response returns.

title: `import()` expressions in object literal are still evaluated eagerly at module load
body: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, each entry of `appStore` is written as `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")` instead of a function like `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`. Because the `import(...)` calls are property value expressions on the object literal, JavaScript evaluates every dynamic import immediately when `@calcom/app-store` is imported, loading all 28 app modules upfront rather than on demand when a specific app is accessed.

title: `async` callback in `.forEach` pushes `deleteEvent` promises after `Promise.all` has already run
body: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts` (lines 458-470), `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... const deletedEvent = await calendar?.deleteEvent(...); apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` uses an `async` callback inside `.forEach`. Because `.forEach` does not await the returned promises, execution immediately continues past the loop and reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) before `getCalendar` or ` calendar.deleteEvent` has resolved and before anything is pushed into `apiDeletes`. As a result, recurring calendar event deletions are not awaited (and in serverless environments may be terminated before completing), and any errors they throw become unhandled promise rejections.

title: `import(...)` in object literal still eagerly imports all apps at module evaluation time
body: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, the `appStore` object values are written as `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")` rather than functions like `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`. Because `import(...)` is called directly when constructing the `appStore` object literal, importing `@calcom/app-store` immediately triggers dynamic imports of all 28 app packages in parallel instead of loading them lazily on demand when a specific app is accessed.

title: `async` callback in `.forEach` pushes deletions after `Promise.all` has already run
body: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts` around lines 458-470, `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` is used when cancelling remaining recurring bookings. Because `.forEach` does not await the async callback, `await getCalendar(credential)` and `await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` suspend execution while the outer function continues synchronously to `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) before `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)` is ever reached. As a result, calendar event deletions for recurring bookings are not awaited before the handler finishes (which can terminate execution early in serverless environments), and any rejected promises inside the `forEach` callback become unhandled rejections.

title: `async` callback in `forEach` inside `try/catch` will not catch errors or await completion
body: In `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts` (lines 124-139) and `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts` (lines 124-139), `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` is wrapped in a `try { ... } catch`. Because `forEach` ignores the returned promises, the `Reschedule` function does not wait for `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` to complete, and any error thrown after `await getCalendar(...)` will result in an unhandled promise rejection rather than being caught by the surrounding `try/catch` block. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` instead.

title: `import()` expressions in object literal are evaluated eagerly on module load
body: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, each entry is written as `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")` rather than a factory function `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`. Because the `import(...)` calls are not wrapped in functions, JavaScript evaluates every dynamic `import()` immediately when `@calcom/app-store` is imported, loading all 28 app modules in parallel on startup instead of lazily loading only the app being accessed. To defer loading until an app is actually used, make each property a function returning the `import()` promise (and call it at the access sites).

title: Async `forEach` callback causes `apiDeletes` to be populated after `Promise.all` runs
body: When cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring event (lines 458-470), `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` is used. Because `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await async callbacks, execution pauses at `await getCalendar(credential)` (line 461) and `await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` (line 466), while the outer `handler` function continues immediately to `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 before any calendar deletion promises have been pushed into `apiDeletes`. As a result, calendar event deletions for recurring bookings are not awaited before the handler returns (and in serverless environments may be terminated before completing), and `apiDeletes` ends up holding resolved values instead of promises.

title: Early return on `dateOverrideExist` bypasses all busy-time checks
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, if a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls within the override's time window, lines 133-135 immediately `return true` before reaching the `busy.every(...)` loop at line 153. As a result, any existing bookings or external calendar busy events on a day with a date override are completely ignored, allowing already-booked slots to be shown as available and double-booked.

title: Dayjs object reference comparison and boundary checks in date override validation are broken
body:
Inside the `dateOverrides.find` callback in `checkIfIsAvailable`:
1. Line 114 compares two fresh Dayjs instances with `===` (`dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)`), which compares object references and is always `false`. An all-day 'unavailable' date override (where `start` and `end` are equal) is therefore never detected as Equal, and if a slot happens to match that timestamp it won't be rejected.
2. Lines 118-125 reject a slot only when `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime > overrideEnd` (i.e. completely disjoint from the override), rather than when `slotStartTime < overrideStart || slotEndTime > overrideEnd`. Slots that only partially overlap the date override window, or that start at `overrideEnd`, are treated as valid.
3. Using `.find()` means that if a user has multiple date override ranges on the same day, the first range that does not contain the slot causes `find` to return truthy and the whole check to return `false`, even if the slot falls inside a second override range on that day.

title: Working hours check in `checkIfIsAvailable` uses `slotStartTime` for `end` and rejects valid split schedules
body:
In `checkIfIsAvailable` (lines 138-151):
1. Line 142 computes `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` instead of using `slotEndTime`, so it never verifies that the end of the slot fits within `workingHour.endTime`.
2. Because it uses `workingHours.find(...)` to look for a violated entry rather than checking whether *some* working-hour interval contains the slot (`!workingHours.some(...)`), any user with multiple working-hour blocks on the same day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) will have every slot rejected: a morning slot fails the afternoon block's `start < workingHour.startTime` check, and an afternoon slot fails the morning block's `end > workingHour.endTime` check.
3. If a user has no working hours at all on `slotStartTime.day()`, `find` returns `undefined` and the function treats the user as available on their day off.

title: `dateOverrides` already have organizer UTC offset applied, causing double offset or day-wrap errors in `getSlots`
body: `getUserAvailability` already shifts each `dateOverride.start` and `end` by the organizer's UTC offset when constructing `dateOverrides`. In `getSlots` (lines 212-224), `override.start` is shifted again by `inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` instead of just `inviteeUtcOffset`, and `startTime`/`endTime` are computed with `.hour() * 60 + .minute()` after adding the offset. When the timezone offset pushes `override.end` to `00:00` of the next day (or `override.start` into the previous day), `.hour() * 60 + .minute()` wraps around to `0` (or a large value from the previous day), producing an invalid range (`startTime >= endTime`) and dropping all slots for that override.

title: checkIfIsAvailable skips busy-time check when a date override exists
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, if a date override exists for the slot's date and the slot falls within the override window, `dateOverrideExist` is set to `true` and lines 133-135 immediately `return true` before running `busy.every(...)` at line 153. As a result, any existing bookings or calendar busy times on a day with a date override are completely ignored, allowing double-bookings during date override hours.

title: Dayjs object reference comparison with === is always false and boundary conditions are off
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, line 114 compares two newly constructed Dayjs instances using `===` (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`), which compares object references and is always `false`; `.isSame(...)` must be used to detect zero-length (unavailable-all-day) overrides. Additionally, lines 118-125 reject a slot when `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime > overrideEnd`, instead of checking whether the slot `[slotStartTime, slotEndTime]` is not fully contained within `[overrideStart, overrideEnd]` (i.e. `slotStartTime.isBefore(overrideStart) || slotEndTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`). A slot that starts before the override begins (but ends after `overrideStart`) or starts before `overrideEnd` (but ends after `overrideEnd`) will be treated as valid.

title: Working hours check in checkIfIsAvailable uses slotStartTime for end and rejects multi-range schedules
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable` lines 138-151: (1) `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` uses `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so a slot whose end extends past `workingHour.endTime` is not caught; and (2) `workingHours.find(...)` returns `true` (causing `checkIfIsAvailable` to return `false`) as soon as *any* workingHour entry for that day does not contain the slot. If a user has split working hours on the same day (e.g., 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) or multiple entries for a day, a slot in the afternoon will fail against the morning entry and be falsely rejected.

title: Date override timezone shift can cross midnight or fail activeOverrides filter
body: In `getSlots` (`packages/lib/slots.ts`), `activeOverrides` (lines 206-208) filters `dateOverrides` by checking if `dayjs.utc(override.start)` (which stores the organizer's local wall-clock time as UTC) falls within `[startOfInviteeDay, startOfInviteeDay.endOf("day"))`. When the invitee and organizer are in different timezones, an override on day D in the organizer's timezone can fall on day D-1 or D+1 in the invitee's timezone, or `override.start` (as raw UTC) may lie outside `[startOfInviteeDay, endOf("day"))`. Furthermore, lines 218-223 compute `startTime` and `endTime` using `.add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...`, which wraps around modulo 1440 when `override.start + offset` crosses midnight UTC, producing inverted or wrong minute-of-day bounds (e.g. `startTime > endTime`).

title: Early return when date override exists skips busy time checks
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, if a date override exists for the slot's date and the slot falls within the override's bounds, `dateOverrideExist` is set to `true` and lines 133-135 immediately `return true` before reaching the `busy.every(...)` check at line 153. As a result, any existing bookings or calendar busy times on a day with a date override are completely ignored, allowing double-bookings during overridden hours.

title: Dayjs object reference comparison with `===` is always false and boundary checks are wrong
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, line 114 compares two newly constructed Dayjs instances using `===` (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`), which compares object references and always evaluates to `false` instead of detecting an all-day unavailable override (where start equals end). Furthermore, the range checks on lines 118-125 use `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` and `slotStartTime > overrideEnd` instead of checking whether the entire slot `[slotStartTime, slotEndTime]` fits within `[overrideStart, overrideEnd]` (i.e. `slotStartTime.isBefore(overrideStart) || slotEndTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`), allowing slots that only partially overlap the override window.

title: Multiple date overrides on the same day or across UTC midnight are not handled
body: `dateOverrides.find` rejects the slot as soon as the first override on that date does not contain the slot. If a user configures multiple date override time ranges on the same day (split shifts), any slot in the second range will fail against the first range and be marked unavailable. Additionally, `dateOverrides` from `getUserAvailability` are already converted to UTC timestamps, so adding `utcOffset` again shifts the override time a second time and comparing `format("YYYY MM DD")` in UTC fails when the override crosses UTC midnight.

title: Working hours check in `checkIfIsAvailable` uses `slotStartTime` for `end` and fails on split working hours
body: In the `workingHours.find` block (lines 139-147), `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` instead of using `slotEndTime`, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after working hours is not rejected. Also, because `.find()` returns truthy if *any* working-hour entry for that day does not contain the slot, a user with multiple working-hour blocks on the same day (e.g., 9:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) will have all slots rejected because every slot lies outside at least one of the blocks.

title: Double timezone offset applied to `dateOverrides` in `getSlots`
body: `getUserAvailability` already shifts `dateOverrides` start and end dates from the organizer's timezone into UTC. In `getSlots`, lines 212-223 compute `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` and add it to `dayjs(override.start).utc()`. Because `override.start` is already in UTC (not in local organizer time stored as UTC), subtracting `organizerUtcOffset` again shifts the override by the organizer's offset a second time. Furthermore, `.hour() * 60 + .minute()` wraps around modulo 1440 if adding the offset crosses midnight in the invitee's timezone.

title: Migration crashes with IndexError when `embed_category` is not set and does not normalize host values
body: `execute(...)` returns a `PG::Result` whose `[0]` accessor raises `IndexError: Index 0 is out of range` whenever the query returns 0 rows. On any database where the `embed_category` site setting was never stored or does not match an existing category name, `execute(...)[0]['id']` will fail and abort the migration (the same risk applies to line 15 if `uncategorized_category_id` is absent from `site_settings`). In addition, line 25 inserts raw `h` values directly with string interpolation without stripping `http(s)://` prefixes or `/...` paths the way `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` hook does, so previously valid `embeddable_hosts` entries containing a scheme or path will not match `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` after migration.

title: `before_validation` raises `NoMethodError` when `host` is nil and `record_for_host` fails on uppercase or port-qualified hosts
body: In `before_validation`, `self.host.sub!` is called unconditionally, which raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` if `EmbeddableHost.new` is validated with a `nil` host. Also, in `self.record_for_host(host)` (lines 14-17), `uri.host` is not downcased before `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, so any referer URL with uppercase characters in the hostname will fail to match, and although the format validation on line 2 explicitly allows a port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), `uri.host` strips the port, so a stored host with a port will never be matched by `record_for_host`.

title: Contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` are swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was replaced with `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` while the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were placed in `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. The two files have their contents transposed.

title: Saving a new host with default category sets `host.category` to `undefined`
body: When a new `embeddable-host` row is added, `categoryId` on the component starts as `null`. On save, the server defaults a blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` and returns it in the payload, which updates `host.category_id`. However, the `.then()` callback immediately runs `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))` using the component's `null` `categoryId` instead of `host.get('category_id')` (or initializing `categoryId` to the uncategorized category id), leaving `host.category` as `undefined` in the UI until the page is reloaded.

title: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category or uncategorized_category_id is not in site_settings
body: In `CreateEmbeddableHosts#change`, `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` assumes the query returns at least one row. On any database where `embed_category` was never modified from its default (or does not match a category name), `execute(...)[0]` returns `nil` and calling `['id']` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil:NilClass`, aborting the migration. The fallback query on line 15 (`SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'`) has the exact same problem if `uncategorized_category_id` is not stored in `site_settings`. Check `result.cmd_tuples > 0` before indexing into `result[0]`.

title: Migrated embeddable_hosts values are not normalized and are interpolated directly into SQL
body: Previously, `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` allowed entries with schemes or paths (e.g. `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234`), whereas `EmbeddableHost` strips `^https?://` and `/.*$` in `before_validation` and `record_for_host` compares `lower(host) = uri.host`. Because the migration inserts raw lines via `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` without stripping the scheme/path (or quoting `h`), any existing host entry that included `http://`, `https://`, or a path will stop matching in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` after the migration, and any single quote in the setting will break the SQL statement.

title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil and does not match non-lowercase URLs
body: In `EmbeddableHost`, the `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If `EmbeddableHost.new` is validated with `host: nil` (for example via missing params or in tests/console), `nil.sub!` raises `NoMethodError` instead of adding a validation error. Additionally, `record_for_host` queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` where `host = URI(url).host`; if the passed URL has an uppercase hostname (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com/foo`), `uri.host` preserves case (`"EvilTrout.com"`), so comparing `lower(host)` against a non-downcased `host` parameter will fail to match.

title: EmbeddableHost.record_for_host ignores ports even though validation allows them
body: `EmbeddableHost` validates `:host` with a regex that explicitly permits `:port` (e.g. `example.com:8080`), and `before_validation` preserves the port in `self.host`. However, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against `uri.host`, which strips the port. As a result, any `EmbeddableHost` saved with a port will never be matched by `record_for_host` or `host_allowed?`.

title: String.prototype.replace('_', '-') only replaces the first underscore
body: In `basePath`, `type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore in `type`. If an admin model name has more than one underscore (e.g. `site_customization_something`), only the first underscore is converted and the lookup in `ADMIN_MODELS` fails. Use `type.replace(/_/g, '-')` (or `Ember.String.dasherize(type)`).

title: Contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was replaced with `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators. The two files have their contents reversed.

title: Spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests what it claims
body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` and no longer checks `EmbeddableHost`. In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb`, the test `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` now runs before `SiteSetting.embed_truncate = true` and `topic.stubs(:has_topic_embed?).returns(true)` are set up, so it passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to `false`, not because `embeddable_host` is blank.

title: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category or uncategorized_category_id setting is not in DB
body: In `CreateEmbeddableHosts#change`, lines 9-11 run `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. On any Discourse instance where `embed_category` was never modified from its default (or does not match an existing category name), the `PG::Result` has 0 rows, so `[0]` raises `IndexError: Index 0 is out of bounds` (or `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil:NilClass`), aborting the migration. The same problem exists on line 15 for `uncategorized_category_id` if that row is not present in `site_settings`. Check `cmd_tuples > 0` before indexing `[0]`.

title: Migrated embeddable_hosts values are inserted without stripping scheme/path or SQL escaping
body: The previous `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` implementation accepted entries in `embeddable_hosts` with `http://`/`https://` prefixes or trailing paths (as seen in the old specs). `CreateEmbeddableHosts` inserts each line verbatim via raw SQL (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` hook that strips `^https?://` and `/.*$`. Because `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` later compares `lower(host)` against `uri.host` (hostname only), any existing host setting saved with a scheme or path will stop matching after migration, breaking embedding for those sites. In addition, `h` is interpolated directly into SQL without `quote`.

title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil and does not normalize or compare port/case
body: In `EmbeddableHost`: (1) `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally, which raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` when `EmbeddableHost.new` is validated with a `nil` `host` (e.g. missing param). (2) In `self.record_for_host(host)`, `host = uri.host` is not downcased (though `URI` usually downcases ASCII hosts) and strips any port (`uri.port`), whereas the validation regex on line 2 allows saving a host with `:port` (e.g. `example.com:8080`). A saved host with a port will never match `uri.host` in `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`.

title: Topic#expandable_first_post? no longer checks if any EmbeddableHost exists, breaking spec
body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1403`, the test `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` only passes by accident because `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` defaults to `false` when no `before` block runs; if `embed_truncate` is `true` and a topic has a `TopicEmbed` record, `expandable_first_post?` now returns `true` even when no `EmbeddableHost` records exist.

title: String.prototype.replace('_', '-') only replaces the first underscore
body: In `basePath`, `type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore in `type`. If an admin model name has more than one underscore (or if `Ember.String.dasherize(type)` was intended), `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(...)` will fail to match. Use `type.replace(/_/g, '-')` or `Ember.String.dasherize(type)`.

title: category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contents are swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was overwritten to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators. The two files have each other's contents.

title: `self.downsize` is redefined, overwriting the 4/5-argument version
body: Ruby does not support method overloading by arity. Defining `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149 completely overwrites `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` on line 145. Any existing caller passing `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` (or 5 arguments with `opts`) will now either pass `max_height` as `opts` (causing `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` when `opts[:allow_animation]` is evaluated on a numeric `max_height`) or fail with `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 5, expected 3..4)`.

title: Client-side size check ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` for non-image uploads
body: `validateUploadedFile` previously checked `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, which enforced `max_attachment_size_kb` for non-image attachments and `max_image_size_kb` for images. Replacing this with a hard-coded `10 * 1024` (10 MB) for all upload types means non-image attachments are no longer validated against `max_attachment_size_kb` on the client (even though the server will not downsize attachments and will still reject them or conversely allow larger attachments than configured until the upload completes).

title: `tempfile.size` is cached on open Ruby `Tempfile`/`File` objects or not refreshed after external modification
body: In `create_upload`, `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` modifies the file on disk via an external `convert`/`gifsicle` process while `tempfile` is an open `Tempfile` handle. Additionally, if `OptimizedImage.downsize` fails (for example, on an SVG, WebP without delegate, corrupt image, or animated GIF when `--resize-fit 80%` is rejected by `gifsicle`), `downsize` returns `false` without shrinking the file, yet the loop still runs all 5 attempts unconditionally instead of breaking on failure.

title: `gifsicle --resize-fit` does not accept percentage dimensions like `"80%"`
body: `UploadsController` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. When an animated GIF is uploaded and `allow_animation` is enabled, `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which runs `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%`. `gifsicle`'s `--resize-fit` option requires `WxH` pixel dimensions (unlike `--scale`), so passing `"80%"` causes `gifsicle` to exit with an error on every attempt and leaves the GIF unresized.

title: Redefining `self.downsize` overwrites the 5-argument version
body: Ruby does not support method overloading by arity. Defining `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149 overwrites `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined on line 145. Any existing caller passing `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` (or 5 arguments with `opts`) will either pass `max_height` as `opts` (causing `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` when `opts[:allow_animation]` is accessed) or raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)`.

title: Hardcoded 10MB client-side limit ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` and `max_image_size_kb` site settings
body: Replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (and similarly in `displayErrorForUpload` on line 246) bypasses configured site limits for non-image attachments (which are not downsized on the server) and blocks uploads larger than 10MB even when an administrator has configured `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB.

title: `gifsicle` does not support percentage geometry in `--resize-fit`
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` passes `"80%"` as `dimensions`. When `allow_animation` is enabled and the upload is a `.gif`, `OptimizedImage.optimize` invokes `gifsicle` with `--resize-fit 80%` (via `resize_instructions_animated`), which is invalid syntax for `gifsicle` (`--resize-fit` requires `WxH`, whereas percentages require `--scale`). `gifsicle` will exit with status 1 and the GIF will fail to downsize on every attempt.

title: `tempfile.size` may return a stale cached value or fail to shrink for SVGs and failed conversions
body: In the downsize loop, `OptimizedImage.downsize` neither checks the return value nor handles formats that `convert` cannot shrink (or SVGs/corrupted images where `convert` fails). When `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false`, the loop still runs all 5 attempts invoking `convert` repeatedly on the same file. Additionally, depending on the Ruby version/Tempfile implementation, `tempfile.size` queries the open file object whose state may not reflect external replacement by `ImageOptim`, so `File.size(tempfile.path)` should be used and the loop should break if `downsize` returns false or the file size stops decreasing.

title: `self.downsize` is redefined and overwrites the 5-argument version
body: Ruby does not support method overloading by arity. Defining `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149 overwrites the `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` method defined right above it on line 145. Any existing caller passing `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` (or 5 arguments with `opts`) will now either pass `max_height` as `opts` (causing a `TypeError`/`NoMethodError` when `opts[:allow_animation]` is accessed on an Integer) or raise an `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)`.

title: Client-side size check ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` for non-image uploads
body: In `validateUploadedFile`, `maxSizeKB` was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) regardless of `type`. However, the server-side downsizing in `UploadsController` only runs when `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` is true. For non-image attachments (`type === 'attachment'`), `max_attachment_size_kb` is no longer enforced on the client: attachments larger than `max_attachment_size_kb` will now be uploaded up to 10MB before being rejected by the server, or attachments > 10MB will be blocked on the client even if an admin configured `max_attachment_size_kb` higher than 10MB.

title: `tempfile.size` may return a cached/stale size or fail to shrink for non-resizable images like SVG
body:
In the downsizing loop:
1. If `OptimizedImage.downsize` fails (for example, on an `.svg` file, which `FileHelper.is_image?` treats as an image, or when `gifsicle` fails because `--resize-fit 80%` is not valid gifsicle syntax), `downsize` returns `false`, yet the loop ignores the return value and repeats all 5 attempts pointlessly.
2. `tempfile` is an open `Tempfile`/`File` object; when external `convert` / `ImageOptim` tools rewrite or replace `tempfile.path` on disk (especially if `ImageOptim` replaces the file via atomic rename to a new inode), `tempfile.size` queries the open file descriptor (`fstat`) rather than the path on disk (`File.size(tempfile.path)`), and when `tempfile` is later read in `Upload.create_for` it may read from the old unlinked inode instead of the newly written file at `tempfile.path`.

title: Nil dereference in TopicsController#unsubscribe when TopicUser does not exist
body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` if the logged-in user has never visited, interacted with, or been emailed about the topic (or if they visit `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` directly). Calling `tu.notification_level` on line 107 will then raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass` resulting in a 500 error. Even if a `TopicUser` row exists, mutating `@topic_view` requires updating or reloading the notification level (or using `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` before constructing `@topic_view`), because `@topic_view` instantiated on line 99 has already cached `@topic_user` with the old `notification_level`, so `perform_show_response` will serialize the stale notification level to the client.

title: Frontend transition to topicUnsubscribe route does not actually unsubscribe the user
body: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `model` calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)`, which fetches `/t/:id.json` (`TopicsController#show`) or consumes the `topic_<id>` preload from `perform_show_response`. Meanwhile, `TopicsController#unsubscribe` mutates the `TopicUser` notification level on the `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` request itself—and does so *after* `TopicView.new` has already memoized `@topic_user` with the pre-unsubscribe `notification_level`. As a consequence: (1) on a direct page load of `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`, the preloaded `TopicViewSerializer` JSON still contains the old `notification_level`, so the `topic-notifications-button` shown on the page displays the old state instead of the updated muted/regular state; and (2) if the user isn't logged in when clicking the email link or transitions to the route client-side, `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is never called in JSON mode.

title: State-changing unsubscribe action is performed on a GET request
body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is routed via `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and immediately mutates `TopicUser#notification_level` in the database without user confirmation or a POST/PUT request. Email security scanners, link prefetchers, browser pre-rendering, or an `` tag on any page can trigger this GET endpoint and silently downgrade a user's topic notification level from watching/tracking to regular, or from regular to muted (and hitting it twice mutes a watched topic).

title: Nil dereference when TopicUser record does not exist during unsubscribe
body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` looks up `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and immediately accesses `tu.notification_level` on line 107 without checking whether `tu` is nil. If a user visits `/t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` for a topic they have no `TopicUser` row for (or before one has been created), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass` and returns a 500 error. In addition, mutating `tu` directly bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which handles creating missing `TopicUser` records, setting `notifications_changed_at` / `notifications_reason_id`, and publishing changes to MessageBus.

title: State-changing unsubscribe happens on GET and toggles from regular to muted on repeat visits
body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is routed via `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and immediately modifies the user's notification level on the GET request. Because the logic sets `notification_level` to `regular` when `> regular` and otherwise sets it to `muted`, a second GET request to the same URL (for example, an email client or link scanner prefetching the link before the user clicks it, or the user refreshing the page) will drop the user's notification level from `regular` down to `muted` without their intent.

title: Nil dereference when unsubscribing without an existing TopicUser record
body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` if the user has never visited or interacted with the topic (for example, a user receiving notifications via mailing list mode without a pre-existing `TopicUser` row, or visiting `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` directly). Accessing `tu.notification_level` on line 107 will then raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass`. In addition, when `tu` is mutated before `perform_show_response`, `@topic_view` has already been initialized and memoized its `@topic_user` on line 99, so the serialized `TopicView` preloaded into the page will still report the old notification level to the client unless `TopicView` is instantiated after updating `TopicUser` (or `TopicUser.change` is used prior to creating `TopicView`).

title: Unsubscribing via GET mutates state on link preloading or crawlers and bypasses TopicUser.change
body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is exposed on `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and immediately mutates the user's notification level on the GET request. Moreover, because it toggles `watching`/`tracking` down to `regular`, and `regular` down to `muted`, a second GET request (for example from an email client/browser link prefetcher, anti-virus scanner, or the user refreshing the page) will unexpectedly downgrade the topic from `regular` to `muted`. Also, updating `tu.notification_level` directly with `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, so `notifications_changed_at`, `notifications_reason_id`, and the MessageBus notification level update are not recorded.

title: Case-sensitive email lookup in BlockedEmail allows trivial bypass
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?(email)` queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` using an exact, case-sensitive match, and `BlockedEmail` does not normalize `email` (e.g., via `Email.downcase`) on save or lookup. Because `User` validates `email` before downcasing it (or if a user signs up with uppercase characters like `Spammer@example.com` while `spammer@example.com` is in `blocked_emails`), the blocked email check can be bypassed simply by changing the casing of the email address.

title: Double validation during user creation increments BlockedEmail match_count twice
body: In `UsersController#create`, when `SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` is enabled, `user.valid?` is called on line 168 and then `user.save` (which runs validations again) is called on line 172. Because `EmailValidator` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, which mutates and saves `match_count` as a side effect of validation, a single signup attempt with a `:do_nothing` (or `:block`) record will increment `match_count` multiple times if validations run more than once.

title: Changing email does not validate against BlockedEmail or domain restrictions
body: In `UsersController#change_email`, an `EmailToken` is created with `user.email_tokens.create(email: lower_email)` and an activation email is sent without running `EmailValidator` on the new address. When the user later confirms the token via `EmailToken.confirm`, if `EmailToken` updates the user's email or if `EmailToken` itself does not use `EmailValidator`, a user can either bypass `BlockedEmail` on email change or receive a confirmation email for an address that will fail validation upon confirmation.

title: Case-sensitive BlockedEmail lookup allows bypassing email blocks with uppercase characters
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` without normalizing the input email's case (e.g., via `Email.downcase(email)`), and `BlockedEmail` does not normalize `email` before saving or validating uniqueness. Because `User` validates `email` before downcasing it (or accepts mixed-case emails in `User.new_from_params`), a user can bypass a blocked entry for `bad@spammers.org` simply by signing up with `Bad@spammers.org`.

title: Validation runs twice during user creation, double-counting blocked email matches
body: In `UsersController#create`, `user.valid?` is called on line 168 (when `SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` is enabled) and then `user.save` runs validations a second time on line 172. Because `EmailValidator` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which increments `match_count` and saves the record as a side effect of validation, any signup attempt with a tracked email (for instance one configured with `:do_nothing`, or whenever `valid?` is called before `save`) will increment `match_count` multiple times for a single signup attempt.

title: Case-sensitive email matching allows bypassing blocked emails
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` and `BlockedEmail` stores `email` without normalizing case. Because `User` does not downcase `email` before validation runs during `UsersController#create`, a user can bypass a blocked address (e.g. `bad@spam.com`) simply by signing up with mixed case (e.g. `Bad@spam.com`). `BlockedEmail` should normalize `email` to lowercase before saving and in `should_block?`.

title: `BlockedEmail.match_count` is incremented multiple times per signup attempt
body: `User` runs `EmailValidator`, which calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?` and increments `match_count` on every validation call. In `UsersController#create` (lines 168 and 172), `user.valid?` is called when `SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` is enabled, followed immediately by `user.save` (which runs validations again). Even when `valid?` is false or when `save` runs, a single signup or validation pass can increment `match_count` multiple times, and calling `user.valid?` as a read-only check has the side effect of mutating the database.

title: Changing email bypasses `EmailValidator` and `BlockedEmail` checks
