body: `UsersController#change_email` creates an `EmailToken` for `lower_email` without running `EmailValidator` (or validating `User#email` until confirmation, and `EmailToken.confirm` updates the user's email). If `EmailToken` does not validate `email: true`, a user can sign up with an allowed email and then change their email to a blocked or domain-blacklisted address.

title: Reflected XSS via unescaped request.referer in inline script
body: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` line 11, `request.referer` is interpolated directly into a JavaScript string literal: `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>');`. Although `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` checks that `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, the path, query string, or fragment of the Referer URL can still contain single quotes, `</script>`, or JavaScript code (depending on the client/browser sending the Referer header or unencoded characters accepted by Ruby's `URI`). Because ERB HTML-escapes `'` as `'` or leaves characters that break out of `<script>` contexts, or if `raw` / JS escaping is not used, an attacker can break out of the JS string or `<script>` tag and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the Discourse origin. Use `.to_json` or `escape_javascript` (`j`) instead.

title: Raw HTML cook_method bypasses sanitization, enabling stored XSS from RSS feeds
body: In `app/models/post.rb` line 133, `Post#cook` returns `raw` untouched when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` lines 35-36) unescapes HTML from RSS/Atom feed items (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` without any HTML sanitization (unlike `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which runs `Readability::Document` with a tag/attribute whitelist). Any `<script>`, `<iframe>`, or `onerror`/`onload` attributes in the RSS feed (or added when a staff user edits a `raw_html` post) will be stored in `cooked` and rendered unescaped to all forum users (`<%= raw post.cooked %>`).

title: Invalid Ruby syntax `end if` causes SyntaxError when rendering best.html.erb
body: Line 6 of `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` has `<%- end if %>`. In Ruby, `end if` is not valid syntax to close an `if` block (unlike VB); ERB compiles this to `end if;` which raises a `SyntaxError` whenever `embed/best` is rendered for an existing topic.

title: NoMethodError in PollFeed when RSS items use `description` instead of `content`
body: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` line 35, `i.content.scrub` assumes `i.content` is non-nil. In standard RSS 2.0 feeds parsed by `SimpleRSS`, items typically populate `description` (or `content_encoded`) rather than `content` (which is an Atom construct), so `i.content` is `nil` and calling `.scrub` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass`, aborting the entire feed poll job.

title: Invalid ERB syntax `<%- end if %>` raises a SyntaxError when rendering `embed/best`
body: In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` on line 6, the `if` block opened on line 2 is closed with `<%- end if %>`. `end if` is not valid Ruby syntax (`if` is not an expression here, and Ruby closes conditionals with `end` alone). Rendering `embed/best` when a topic exists will fail at template compilation time with a `SyntaxError`.

title: Unescaped `request.referer` interpolated into JavaScript string enables reflected XSS
body: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` line 11, `<%= request.referer %>` is interpolated directly inside a single-quoted JavaScript string literal: `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. Standard ERB HTML escaping does not escape backslashes, newlines, or `</script>`, and in Rails 3 (still supported per the `Gemfile`) single quotes are not escaped by `ERB::Util.html_escape` either. Because `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` only validates `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, an attacker can craft a URL on the embeddable host whose path or query string contains characters such as `</script><script>...` (or `'` / `\`) and cause arbitrary JavaScript to execute in the context of the Discourse origin when the iframe loads. Use `to_json` / ` escape_javascript` (or pass the origin derived from `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) instead of interpolating `request.referer` directly.

title: `raw_html` cook method bypasses HTML sanitization, allowing stored XSS from RSS feeds or edited posts
body: In `app/models/post.rb` line 133, `Post#cook` returns `raw` untouched when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, skipping `PrettyText.cook` and its HTML sanitizer as well as `:after_post_cook` plugin filters. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` lines 35-36) feeds `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` from an external RSS/Atom feed directly into `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Any `<script>`, `onload=`, `onerror=`, or `javascript:` URL present in the feed (or introduced later by any user who can edit that first post in Discourse) is stored verbatim in `cooked` and rendered unescaped into the forum and into `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` (`<%= raw post.cooked %>`), resulting in stored XSS.

title: `PollFeed` crashes with `NoMethodError` on RSS 2.0 feeds or entries without `<content>`
body: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` line 35, `i.content.scrub` assumes every parsed item has a non-nil `content` string. `SimpleRSS` only populates `i.content` / `content_encoded` when Atom `<content>` or `<content:encoded>` is present; standard RSS 2.0 items use `i.description` (or `i.summary`), leaving `i.content` as `nil`. In addition, `String#scrub` is a Ruby 2.1 method and raises `NoMethodError` on Ruby 1.9/2.0. When `i.content` is `nil`, polling the feed raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass` and aborts the entire job before importing remaining items.

title: Reflected XSS via unescaped request.referer in inline script
body: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` line 11, `request.referer` is interpolated into a single-quoted JavaScript string literal (`'<%= request.referer %>'`). Standard ERB HTML-escaping (`<%= %>`) only escapes HTML characters (`<`, `>`, `&`, `"`, and `'`); if `'` is not escaped or if a referer URL contains a backslash or other JS-significant sequence on an allowed `embeddable_host` (e.g., via the path or query string), it can break out of the JS string literal and execute arbitrary script in the Discourse origin context. `to_json` (or extracting the origin on the server) should be used when embedding values into JavaScript.

title: Invalid Ruby syntax `<%- end if %>` causes SyntaxError when rendering best.html.erb
body: Line 6 of `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` closes the `if` block with `<%- end if %>`. In Ruby/ERB, `end if` is not valid syntax for closing an `if` statement (it parses as `end` followed by a trailing `if` modifier with no condition and no `end`), which will raise a `SyntaxError` whenever `EmbedController#best` renders the `best` template.

title: Unsanitized RSS/Atom feed HTML is stored and rendered raw, enabling stored XSS
body: `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` unescapes the feed item content (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) and passes it directly to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Because `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly without running `PrettyText` or any HTML sanitizer when `cook_method` is `raw_html`, any `<script>` tags or event handlers present in the RSS feed (or if the feed is compromised or contains user-supplied content) will be stored in `cooked` and executed in the browser of every user viewing the topic or embedded frame.

title: NoMethodError when RSS feed items use `description` instead of `content`
body: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` line 35, `i.content.scrub` assumes `i.content` is always a non-nil `String`. In RSS 2.0 feeds parsed by `SimpleRSS`, items typically populate `description` (or `content_encoded`) rather than `content`, leaving `i.content` as `nil`. Calling `.scrub` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError` and aborts polling for the entire feed.

title: Loop overwrites `post` variable, causing imported Disqus replies to fail or attach to wrong topic
body: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` line 148, `post` holds the initial topic post created by `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. Inside `t[:posts].each` on line 174, `post = PostCreator.new(post_user, attrs).create` overwrites that outer `post` variable. If `PostCreator#create` returns `nil` or an unsaved post (e.g., due to validation failure), line 175 (`post.post_number`), subsequent iterations' `post.topic_id` (line 161), and line 177 (`post.topic`) will either raise `NoMethodError` on `nil` or reference a failed post with no `topic_id`.

title: Converting `.small-action` to flexbox breaks right-alignment of child `button` elements
body: `.small-action` is changed to `display: flex`, making its direct children flex items. Inside `.small-action`, `button` (lines 306-310) relies on `float: right;` to align to the right edge of the post action row, and `.small-action-desc` has no `flex-grow`. Because `float` has no effect on flex items, the delete/edit buttons in `.small-action` will no longer be pushed to the right side and will instead sit immediately next to `.small-action-desc` (unlike `.d-header .panel`, where `margin-left: auto` was added when `float: right` was removed).

title: `include_website_name` is missing `?` and `:website_name` is not marked as an untrusted attribute
body: `ActiveModel::Serializer` expects conditional inclusion methods to end with `?` (`include_website_name?`), so `def include_website_name` on line 153 is never called and `website_name` is always serialized into the JSON (even as `nil` when `website` is blank). Furthermore, `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) so that it is hidden for TL0 users when viewed by anonymous users (`scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`), whereas `website_name` is not. As a result, a TL0 user's website domain/path is leaked to anonymous users via `website_name`. Adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (and removing the manual `include_website_name` method, since `untrusted_attributes` defines `include_website_name?` automatically) fixes both issues.

title: `" ." << website_host` mutates a string literal in place
body: On line 149, `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses `String#<<`, which mutates the receiver string literal `"."` rather than allocating a new string with `+`. If `frozen_string_literal: true` is enabled this will raise a `FrozenError` / `RuntimeError` (`can't modify frozen String`), and in older Ruby versions where string literals are shared across calls in some contexts or if `website_host` were ever passed on the left-hand side, in-place mutation causes subtle bugs. Use `".#{website_host}"` or `"." + website_host` instead.

title: `website_name` is not updated on the client after saving user preferences
body: Previously, `websiteName` was a computed property on the controller observing `model.website`, so editing and saving `website` in user preferences immediately updated the displayed website name on the user profile. Now that `website_name` is computed on the server in `UserSerializer`, `User#save` (around line 210, where `self.set('bio_excerpt', data.user.bio_excerpt)` is updated from the PUT response) does not copy `data.user.website_name` back onto the model. After a user updates their website in preferences and navigates back to their profile without a full page reload, `model.website_name` will remain stale (or undefined if they previously had no website).

title: `include_website_name` is missing `?` and `website_name` is missing from `untrusted_attributes`
body: `UserSerializer` defines `def include_website_name` without the trailing question mark required by ActiveModel::Serializer (`include_website_name?`), so the method is never invoked and `website_name` is always included in the serialized JSON (as `nil` when `website` is blank). In addition, `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) so that TL0 users' websites are hidden from anonymous viewers, while `website_name` is not. If `website_name` is added to `untrusted_attributes` (which automatically defines `include_website_name?` checking both `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` and `website_name.present?`), both the always-included key bug and the TL0 information leak to anonymous users are fixed.

title: `"\.".<< website_host` mutates a string literal in place
body: On line 149, `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses `<<` on the string literal `"."`, which mutates the literal or raises `FrozenError` when `frozen_string_literal` is enabled. Use string interpolation (`".#{website_host}"`) or `+` instead of `<<`.

title: `include_website_name` is missing `?` and `:website_name` is not marked as an untrusted attribute
body: `include_website_name` is defined without a trailing question mark, so ActiveModel::Serializer ignores it and always includes `website_name` in the serialized payload (even when `website` is blank, emitting `"website_name": null`). Furthermore, `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) so that TL0 users' websites are hidden from anonymous viewers (`scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`), whereas `website_name` is not. As a result, a TL0 user's website domain/path is leaked to anonymous users via `website_name` even when `website` itself is suppressed. Rename the method to `include_website_name?` or add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (and remove the custom `include_website_name` method, since `untrusted_attributes` already checks `send(attr).present?`).

title: `" ." << website_host` mutates a non-frozen string literal across calls in Ruby 2.x
body: On line 149, `"." << website_host` uses the mutating shovel operator `<<` on the string literal `"."` instead of `+`. Unless `# frozen_string_literal: true` is active, Ruby evaluates the literal object and mutates it in place, or (if frozen in later Ruby versions) raises `FrozenError: can't modify frozen String`. Use `"." + website_host` or `"#{website_host}"` interpolation instead.

title: `website_name` is not updated on the client after saving user preferences
body: Previously, `websiteName` was a computed property on the controller derived from `model.website`, so editing and saving `website` in user preferences immediately updated the displayed website name on the user profile. Now `website_name` is only computed on the server in `UserSerializer`, and `User#save` (lines 206-214) only copies `bio_excerpt` from the PUT response back onto the model (`self.set('bio_excerpt', data.user.bio_excerpt)`). After a user updates their `website` in preferences and navigates back to their profile without a full page reload, `model.website_name` remains stale (or undefined if they didn't previously have one). `User#save` should also update `self.set('website_name', data.user.website_name)`.

title: Inverted lightness percentages in `.custom-message-length`
body: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss` line 102, `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The 30% and 70% values are swapped compared to the original rule and the matching desktop rule in `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/modal.scss` line 94 (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`), making the custom message length counter much darker in light themes and much lighter in dark themes on mobile.

title: Lightness values for .custom-message-length are inverted compared to original and desktop
body: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss` on line 102, `.custom-message-length` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The lightness percentages (30% and 70%) are swapped compared to the original value (70% for light themes) and the identical rule in `desktop/modal.scss` (line 94), which uses `70%` for `$primary` and `30%` for `$secondary`. This makes the hint text much darker on light themes and much lighter on dark themes than intended.

title: Off-by-one error in totalPages when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` computes `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is a positive multiple of `limit` (e.g. `user_count = 50` and `limit = 50`), this yields `2` instead of `1`. As a result, the UI shows `1/2`, `showingLast` is false, and clicking "next" sets `offset` to `user_count` (50) and fetches an empty second page (`Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` should be used instead).

title: Admin::GroupsController#create ignores alias_level parameter
body: `Discourse.Group#asJSON` sends `name`, `alias_level`, and `visible` when creating a group via `POST /admin/groups`, and the new group form exposes the `alias_level` combo box before saving. However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `group.name` and `group.visible` and never sets `group.alias_level`, so any alias level chosen during group creation is silently discarded.

title: Unbounded and unvalidated limit/offset in GroupsController#members
body: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed directly to ActiveRecord's `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` without bounds checking. A caller can pass an arbitrarily large `limit` to serialize the entire `users` table in one request, or pass negative values for `limit` or `offset` which causes PostgreSQL to raise `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` (`LIMIT/OFFSET must not be negative`) resulting in an unhandled 500 error.

title: Adding an already-existing member to a group raises a uniqueness error
body: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `group.add(user)` is called for each resolved username without checking whether the user is already a member of `group`. `Group#add` appends to `group_users` (`self.group_users.build(...)` / `users << user`), which triggers a `RecordNotUnique` / validation failure on `(group_id, user_id)` if any of the submitted usernames is already in the group.

title: Off-by-one error in totalPages and pagination offset when user_count is a multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`, which is 1 too high whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 50 users with a limit of 50 yields 2 pages instead of 1; use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` or `Math.floor((user_count - 1) / limit) + 1`). Consequently, clicking `next` on the last actual page is not blocked by `showingLast` and sets `offset` to `user_count` (line 33), loading an empty extra page (`2/2` with 0 members).

title: alias_level is ignored when creating a new group
body: `Admin::GroupsController#create` sets `name` and `visible` on the new `Group` record, but ignores `params[:alias_level]` even though the group creation form (`admin/templates/group.hbs`) displays the alias level selector and `Discourse.Group#asJSON` sends `alias_level` in the POST payload. Any alias level chosen by the admin when creating a group is silently discarded.

title: Adding an already-present member to a group raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
body: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `group.add(user)` (`group.users.push(user)`) is called without checking whether the user is already a member of the group (`group.users.include?(user)` or `GroupUser.exists?(group_id: group.id, user_id: user.id)`). Because `group_users` has a unique index on `(group_id, user_id)`, adding an existing member raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and returns a 500 error instead of succeeding or returning a validation error.

title: Unbounded and unvalidated limit/offset parameters in GroupsController#members
body: `GroupsController#members` accepts user-supplied `params[:limit]` and `params[:offset]` directly (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`, `offset = params[:offset].to_i`) without clamping them. A client can pass a negative `limit`/`offset` (causing a Postgres `PG::Error: LIMIT/OFFSET must not be negative` 500 error) or a huge `limit` to serialize all users in a large group in a single request.

title: totalPages calculation is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` computes `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is a non-zero multiple of `limit` (for example `user_count = 50` and `limit = 50`), this returns `2` instead of `1` (`Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`). As a result, `showingLast` stays false on the last real page, the UI shows `1/2`, and clicking `next` advances `offset` to `user_count` and loads an empty page `2/2`.

title: Admin::GroupsController#create ignores alias_level parameter
body: `Discourse.Group#asJSON` sends `alias_level` when creating a group via `POST /admin/groups`, and the new group form exposes the alias level selector before saving. However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `name` and `visible` and never reads `params[:alias_level]`, so any alias level chosen when creating a group is silently discarded and has to be set again in a subsequent update.

title: Adding an existing member to a group raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
body: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `group.add(user)` (which does `group.users.push(user)`) is called without checking whether the user is already in `group.users`. Because `group_users` has a unique index on `(group_id, user_id)`, adding a username that is already a member of the group will raise an unhandled `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (500 error) instead of skipping the duplicate or returning a validation error.

title: Unbounded and unvalidated limit/offset in GroupsController#members
body: `GroupsController#members` sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` without clamping them. A caller can pass a negative `limit` or `offset` (causing a Postgres `LIMIT must not be negative` / `OFFSET must not be negative` error and a 500 response) or a huge `limit` to force serialization of the entire user table in one request. Additionally, if `limit` is `0`, the client's `offset / limit` page calculation in `admin-group.js.es6` divides by zero (`NaN`).

title: Fallback locales are not loaded when `I18n.translate` is called outside a controller request
body: `I18n.translate` only loads `config.locale` (`load_locale(config.locale) unless @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)`), while fallback locales are only loaded via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` inside `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any translation performed in a background job (Sidekiq), rake task, mailer, console, or test that does not go through `ApplicationController#set_locale`—or that passes an explicit `locale:` option to `I18n.t`—will not have the fallback locales (such as `SiteSetting.default_locale` or `:en`) loaded into `@loaded_locales`. Because Discourse's `translate_accelerator` patch suppresses automatic `load_translations`, `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` will look up keys in unloaded fallback locales and return missing-translation results instead of falling back.

title: `Pluralization` is included before `Fallbacks`, breaking fallback when a locale has an incomplete pluralization table
body: In `config/initializers/i18n.rb`, `I18n::Backend::Pluralization` is included into `I18n::Backend::Simple` before `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks`. In Ruby's ancestor chain, `Fallbacks#translate` will call `super`, which invokes `Pluralization#pluralize` on the result. However, if a translation key exists as a hash in the primary locale with a missing plural form (or if `i18n.plural.rule` is missing for the primary locale and falls back to `:en`'s rule, which returns a key like `:one` or `:other` not present in the partial locale hash), `I18n::InvalidPluralizationData` is raised and is not caught by `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` (which only rescues `I18n::MissingTranslationData`), causing a 500 error instead of falling back.

title: String vs Symbol mismatch in `@loaded_locales` causes redundant reloading or missed loads
body: `ApplicationController#set_locale` sets `I18n.locale` from `current_user.effective_locale` or `SiteSetting.default_locale` (which are Strings, and `I18n.config.locale` converts them to Symbols), whereas `FallbackLocaleList#[]` returns `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`. If `ensure_loaded!` or `FallbackLocaleList#[]` is called with a String `locale` (e.g., `I18n.fallbacks["de"]`), `uniq` in `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq` will not deduplicate `"de"` and `:de`, and `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` in `load_locale` will treat `"de"` and `:de` as distinct, loading all YAML files for that locale twice.

title: Fallback locales are not guaranteed to be loaded outside of controller requests
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only called inside `ApplicationController#set_locale`. When `I18n.t` is invoked outside of a controller request (such as in Sidekiq background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, or tests), or when `I18n.t(key, locale: ...)` is called with an explicit locale, `I18n.translate` in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` only loads `config.locale` and never loads the fallback locales (`SiteSetting.default_locale` and `:en`). Because `I18n::Backend::Simple` has its automatic loading bypassed by `translate_accelerator.rb`, `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` will look up keys in unloaded fallback locales and return missing translation results instead of falling back.

title: `@loaded_locales` mixes symbols and strings and is nil before `ensure_loaded!` or `reload!`
body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` returns an array of symbols (and `I18n.locale` is a symbol), so `ensure_loaded!` populates `@loaded_locales` with symbols, whereas `SiteSetting.default_locale` / `current_user.effective_locale` can be strings or symbols depending on how `config.locale` is read. Additionally, if `I18n.t` is called before `ensure_loaded!` or `reload!` has ever been called (for example during boot or in a job), `@loaded_locales` is `nil` and line 68 (`@loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)`) raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'include?' for nil:NilClass`.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded in controller requests, breaking fallbacks in background jobs and mailers
body: Because `translate_accelerator.rb` lazily loads locale YAML files and `I18n.translate` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)` for the primary locale, fallback locales must be explicitly loaded via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` before `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` looks up keys in the backend. Calling `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` only in `ApplicationController#set_locale` means any translation performed outside a controller request (such as in Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, or specs) or when `I18n.t(..., locale: ...)` is called with an explicit locale will not have the fallback locales (`SiteSetting.default_locale` and `:en`) loaded into the backend, causing fallback lookups to miss and return `translation missing` even when the key exists in the fallback locale.

title: Pluralization and Fallbacks are included in incompatible order and on different target classes
body: Line 5 includes `I18n::Backend::Pluralization` into `I18n::Backend::Simple`, and line 9 then includes `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` into `I18n.backend.class`. In Ruby, the last included module is placed first in the method lookup chain (`ancestors`). For `I18n::Backend::Pluralization` to work with `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` when a pluralization rule (`i18n.plural.rule`) is defined in the locale or a fallback locale, `Pluralization` must be included after `Fallbacks` (or `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` / `pluralize` will be bypassed or resolved in the wrong order). Additionally, if `I18n.backend` is ever replaced with a new `I18n::Backend::Simple.new` instance (e.g., in tests), `Fallbacks` is included on the current backend's class while `Pluralization` is hardcoded to `I18n::Backend::Simple`.

title: `@loaded_locales` can be `nil` in `I18n.translate` before `ensure_loaded!` is ever called
body: `ensure_loaded!` initializes `@loaded_locales ||= []`, whereas `translate` at line 68 calls `@loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)` directly without initializing `@loaded_locales`. Previously `@loaded_locales` was only initialized in `reload!`. If `I18n.t` is called before `reload!` or `ensure_loaded!` has run, `@loaded_locales` is `nil` and line 68 raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'include?' for nil:NilClass`. `translate` should call `ensure_loaded!(config.locale)` (or `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`) instead.

title: Translation cache key does not include `SiteSetting.default_locale`, serving stale fallback translations when default locale changes
body: `I18n.translate` caches zero-argument translations under `k = "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With `FallbackLocaleList`, the result of translating a key for a user locale `L` now depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` whenever `L` is missing the key. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` is changed (e.g., in multisite requests or when an admin updates the setting), the LRU cache will continue returning the translation from the previous default locale.

title: Denial cache test sets cached permission to false instead of true
body: In `TestService_CacheCheck` ("Should deny on explicit cache deny entry"), the test intends to seed `permCache` with an allow entry to verify that `permDenialCache` short-circuits the check. However, it sets `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}` instead of `true`. Because `checkPermission` checks `if scopeMap[t.scope(req.Name)]`, a `false` value denies access anyway (and the backing `fakeStore` has no permissions either), so this test would pass even if `permDenialCache` were never consulted.

title: Denial cache test sets cached permission to false instead of true
body: In `TestService_CacheCheck` ("Should deny on explicit cache deny entry"), `s.permCache` is populated with `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}` despite the comment stating `// Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked`. Because the map value is `false` and the underlying `fakeStore` has no permissions configured, `s.Check` would return `Allowed: false` even if `permDenialCache` were never consulted. The map value should be `true` so the test actually verifies that the denial cache short-circuits the permission check.

title: Denial cache key uses raw UserUID instead of resolved UID and omits IdentityType
body: `Check` constructs `permDenialKey` directly from `checkReq.UserUID` (the raw ID from the request subject) without including `checkReq.IdentityType` or resolving user identifiers via `GetUserIdentifiers` (unlike `permCache`, which resolves numeric IDs to `userIdentifiers.UID` and separates anonymous permissions). This has two consequences: (1) different identity types with the same ID (e.g., `anonymous:0` vs `user:0` or `service-account:1` vs `user:1`) share the same denial cache key, so a denial for an anonymous request can falsely deny a user or service account with the same numeric ID; and (2) a user checked by numeric ID (`user:123`) and by UID (`user:uid123`) will use two different denial cache keys instead of sharing the entry.

title: Stale folderCache prevents inheriting permissions on newly created nested folders/dashboards
body: When `Check` falls back to `getIdentityPermissions` on a permission cache miss (lines 139-146), it refreshes `permCache` from the database, but `checkInheritedPermissions` still calls `buildFolderTree`, which reads from `s.folderCache` without invalidating or bypassing it. If a user creates a subfolder `child` inside a `parent` folder where they have permissions, and then creates or accesses a resource inside `child` while `folderCache` still holds the pre-creation folder tree (cached for `shortCacheTTL`), `tree.Ancestors("child")` will return no ancestors, `checkPermission` will return `false`, and `s.permDenialCache.Set` (line 154) will cache the false denial for 30 seconds.

title: Test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' sets permCache to false instead of true
body: In `TestService_CacheCheck` ('Should deny on explicit cache deny entry'), the comment on line 981 says `// Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked`, but line 982 sets `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}` instead of `true`. Even if `permDenialCache` were completely ignored, `checkPermission` would still return `false` (and `fakeStore` has no permissions either), so the test does not actually verify that `permDenialCache` short-circuits `permCache`.

title: Pause and Delete menu items are hidden for Grafana rules in the list view when rulerRule is omitted
body: In `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`, `canPause` and `canDelete` are updated to check `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(promRule)` so that abilities work in the alert list view where `rulerRule` is no longer fetched. However, rendering the Pause menu item at line 123 still checks `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, and rendering the Delete menu item at line 165 still checks `canDelete && rulerRule` (and `handleDelete` is typed as `(rule: RulerRuleDTO, groupIdentifier: RuleGroupIdentifierV2) => void`, even though `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` ignores the arguments and uses `identifier`). Additionally, in `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` line 104, `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` is gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, so clicking "Silence notifications" in the list view sets `showSilenceDrawer(true)` without rendering the drawer. As a result, Grafana rules in the list view cannot be paused or deleted from the menu, and clicking "Silence notifications" does nothing.

title: Recording rules and un-loaded folders have wrong ModifyExport and Silence abilities in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities
body: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `ModifyExport` is set to `[isAlertingRule, exportAllowed]` (line 324), whereas `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` sets it to `[isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, exportAllowed]` (which is true for both Grafana alerting and recording rules). Using `isAlertingRule` disables export for Grafana-managed recording rules. Additionally, `Silence` is set to `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` (line 323) without checking that `rule` is defined or that `useFolder(rule?.folderUid)` has finished loading and returned a folder; if a user has the global `AlertingInstanceCreate` permission, `canSilenceInFolder` is `true` even while the folder is missing or still loading, unlike `useCanSilence` which returns `[false, false]` when `folderIsLoading || !folder`.

title: Missing React `key` prop on `GrafanaRuleListItem` in `FilterViewResults`
body: When replacing `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ... />` with `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` inside `rules.map(...)`, the `key={key}` prop was dropped. Rendering list items in an array without a `key` triggers React warnings and can cause incorrect component state reuse when the filtered rule list updates.

title: Rule view link in `GrafanaRuleListItem` drops the `returnTo` query parameter
body: In the removed `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`, the view link was constructed with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. In the new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` (line 40), `href` is created with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` without `returnTo`, breaking the "Back to list" navigation from the rule details page when opened from the rule list.

title: Missing `key` prop on `GrafanaRuleListItem` in filtered rules list
body: When replacing `<GrafanaRuleLoader>` with `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` inside `rules.map(...)`, the `key={key}` prop was removed. Without a React `key` on elements rendered in an array, React will log a warning and cannot track item identity across list updates and infinite-scroll batches, which can cause state/DOM mismatches and unnecessary re-renders.

title: Silence, Pause, and Delete actions are broken or missing for Grafana rules in the list view
body:
In the new list view (`GrafanaGroupLoader` and `FilterView`), `GrafanaRuleListItem` renders `<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} compact />` without passing `rule` (the `RulerRuleDTO`). However:

1. In `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` (line 104), `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` is gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`. Even though `AlertRuleMenu` now shows the "Silence notifications" menu item based on `promRule` abilities, clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer(true)` and nothing opens because `rule` is `undefined`.
2. In `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` (lines 123 and 165), the Pause menu item (`canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`) and the Delete menu item (`canDelete && rulerRule`) still require `rulerRule` to be defined, despite computing `grafanaPauseAbility` and `grafanaDeleteAbility` from `promRule`. As a result, Grafana rules in the list view can no longer be paused or deleted from the menu.

title: Federated rules check removed in `useAllAlertRuleAbilities`, allowing edit/delete on federated rule groups
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` was refactored to delegate to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`. Previously, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` computed `const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group);`, which marked rules in federated Mimir/Loki rule groups (`source_tenants`) as immutable (`immutableRule = true`), disabling Update and Delete. `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hardcodes `const isFederated = false;`, so callers of `useAlertRuleAbility` / `useAlertRuleAbilities` / `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` will now treat federated rules as editable and removable.

title: Silence ability for `GrafanaPromRuleDTO` ignores folder loading and missing folder state
body: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `AlertRuleAction.Silence` is set to `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]`. Unlike `useCanSilence` (lines 576-578), which returns `[false, false]` while `folderIsLoading || !folder` or when `!rule`, `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` does not check `loading` or whether the folder exists. For a user with global `AlertingInstanceCreate` permission (`hasGlobalSilencePermission === true`), `canSilenceInFolder` is immediately `true` even while the folder is still loading or if the folder fails to load.

title: Pause, Delete, and Silence actions are broken or hidden in the alert list view when `rulerRule` is undefined
body:
`AlertRuleMenu` and `RuleActionsButtons.V2` compute abilities (`canPause`, `canDelete`, `canSilence`) using `promRule` via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` when `rulerRule` is omitted in the alert list view, but the menu items and handlers still gate on `rulerRule`:

1. **Pause** (`AlertRuleMenu.tsx:123`): gated by `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && ...`, so the Pause menu item is never rendered when `rulerRule` is undefined.
2. **Delete** (`AlertRuleMenu.tsx:165`): gated by `canDelete && rulerRule`, so the Delete menu item is never rendered in the list view when `rulerRule` is undefined (even though `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:99` only needs `identifier` and `groupIdentifier` in `showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)`).
3. **Silence** (`AlertRuleMenu.tsx:126` & `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104`): the "Silence notifications" menu item is rendered because `canSilence` is true, but clicking it does nothing because `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` in `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104` is gated by `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`.

As a result, Grafana-managed rules in the alert list view cannot be paused or deleted from the menu, and clicking "Silence notifications" silently fails to open the drawer.

title: Missing React `key` prop on `GrafanaRuleListItem` in `FilterView`
body: When replacing `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ... />` with `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` inside `rules.map(...)`, the `key={key}` prop was dropped. Rendering list items without a `key` causes React warnings and can lead to incorrect component state reuse when rules are appended or re-rendered.

title: Grafana-managed recording rules lose `ModifyExport` ability when checked via `promRule`
body: In `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` (line 268), `AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport` is `[isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, exportAllowed]`, where `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule` is `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` (true for both Grafana alerting and recording rules). In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (line 324), it is set to `[isAlertingRule, exportAllowed]`, where `isAlertingRule` is `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, which is false for recording rules (`PromRuleType.Recording`). Moreover, when `rule` is `undefined` (i.e. `skipToken` is passed), `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` still returns `[true, ...]` for `View` and `Explore` and `[true, createPerm]` for `Duplicate` because `MaybeSupported` defaults to `AlwaysSupported` even when `rule` is `undefined`.

title: Interpolating before `querySupportsSplitting` breaks `$__range` detection
body: `runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on line 299 before `querySupportsSplitting(query)` is evaluated on line 300. `applyTemplateVariables` replaces `$__range`, `$__range_s`, and `$__range_ms` in `query.expr` with their literal durations (e.g. `72h`) via `templateSrv.replace`. As a result, `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` inside `querySupportsSplitting` will always return `false` because the `$__range*` token has already been replaced, causing queries that use `$__range` to be split into daily chunks and evaluated with the full-range duration over each 1-day sub-range (or re-interpolated on the backend with the 1-day sub-range if left unreplaced). `querySupportsSplitting` needs to inspect the un-interpolated `expr` (or `isQueryWithRangeVariable` must be checked before `applyTemplateVariables`).

title: Queries are interpolated multiple times and ad-hoc filters are injected repeatedly during shard splitting
body: `runShardSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` at the start (line 52), and then for each shard batch `splitQueriesByStreamShard` delegates to `runSplitQuery(datasource, subRequest, ...)` (line 163), which calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` again on the already-interpolated targets (and `datasource.runQuery` -> `super.query` will call it a third time). Because `LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables` injects `request.filters` (ad-hoc filters) into `query.expr` on every call and re-runs template variable replacement on the already-expanded expression, ad-hoc filters will be added to the stream selector multiple times and any variable values containing `$` syntax will be re-interpolated on each shard cycle.

title: Interpolating before `querySupportsSplitting` breaks `$__range` detection
body: `runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on line 299 before passing the queries to `querySupportsSplitting(query)` on line 300. `querySupportsSplitting` calls `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to avoid splitting queries that use `$__range`, `$__range_s`, or `$__range_ms` (because splitting them causes the backend to re-evaluate the range against the 1-day chunk instead of the full query range). However, `applyTemplateVariables` replaces `$__range*` in `query.expr` with the literal range duration (e.g., `7d`), so by the time `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` runs, the variable reference is already gone and always evaluates to `false`. As a result, queries containing `$__range`, `$__range_s`, or `$__range_ms` will now be erroneously split into 1-day chunks, or `applyTemplateVariables` will have already baked in the unsplit range while `datasource.runQuery` may re-split the time range.

title: Queries are interpolated multiple times when shard splitting delegates to `runSplitQuery`
body: `runShardSplitQuery` calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` on all targets up front (line 52), and then `splitQueriesByStreamShard` delegates each shard batch to `runSplitQuery` (line 163), which now also calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` on every target (as seen in `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts` line 112 where `applyTemplateVariables` is called 5 times for a single query). Because `LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables` also injects ad-hoc `request.filters` into the LogQL stream selector each time it is called, running `applyTemplateVariables` twice (and then a third time inside `super.query` / `runQuery`) will duplicate ad-hoc filter matchers in the query expression and can corrupt queries whose interpolated variable values contain `$` characters.

title: Nil request dereference in ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods
body: In `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`, `QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics` dereference `req.PluginContext` without checking whether `req` is `nil`. Previously, `MetricsMiddleware` (formerly `InstrumentationMiddleware`) ran before `instrumentContext` and failed early in `pluginTarget` when a plugin was not registered, whereas `LoggerMiddleware` explicitly guards against `req == nil` (lines 63, 77, 90, 104 of `logger_middleware.go`) and tests in `logger_middleware_test.go` exercise nil requests. If `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` is invoked with a `nil` request (or if `req == nil` reaches it before any check), `req.PluginContext` will panic with a nil pointer dereference. Add a `if req == nil` check before calling `instrumentContext` in each of these methods.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new detached TestLogger, discarding recorded logs
body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` (a fresh instance) rather than `f`. In `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest`, logging was changed from `m.logger.Info(...)` to `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. Any test that passes a `*TestLogger` into `NewLoggerMiddleware` and then inspects `testLogger.InfoLogs` (such as existing tests in `logger_middleware_test.go`) will now see 0 calls because the `Info` call is recorded on the throwaway `TestLogger` returned by `FromContext` instead of on `f`. `FromContext` (and likely `New`) on `TestLogger` should return `f` so assertions on the injected test logger continue to work.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new instance, discarding logged messages
body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver `f`. When code under test logs via `logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (such as `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` in `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go`), the log call is recorded on a newly allocated, unreachable `TestLogger` rather than the `TestLogger` instance held by the test, so assertions on `f.InfoLogs` / `f.ErrorLogs` will see zero calls and empty messages.

title: Nil request dereference in ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods
body: `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics` unconditionally dereference `req.PluginContext` before passing `req` to `m.next`. Other client middlewares (for example `LoggerMiddleware` in `logger_middleware.go` lines 63, 77, 90, 104) explicitly guard against `req == nil` and forward nil requests to `m.next`. Because `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` is registered ahead of `LoggerMiddleware` in the middleware chain, a nil `req` will now panic with a nil pointer dereference in `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` before reaching those guards.

title: Nil request dereference in ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics when req is nil
body: `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics` (lines 40, 45, 50, 55) unconditionally dereference `req.PluginContext` before passing the request down the middleware chain. Previously, `InstrumentationMiddleware` only called `instrumentContext` after `m.pluginTarget` succeeded, and `LoggerMiddleware` explicitly guards against `req == nil` (e.g. `if req == nil { return m.next.QueryData(ctx, req) }` in `logger_middleware.go`). Because `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` is registered ahead of `LoggerMiddleware` in `CreateMiddlewares`, any call with a `nil` request (such as those tested in `logger_middleware_test.go` or `tracing_middleware_test.go`) will panic with a nil pointer dereference when `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` is in the chain.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new instance, discarding recorded logs on the receiver
body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of `f`. In `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest`, logging was changed from `m.logger.Info(...)` to `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. Any test that passes a `*log.TestLogger` into `NewLoggerMiddleware` (such as `logger_middleware_test.go`) and inspects `testLogger.InfoLogs` will now see zero recorded calls because the log entry is written to the freshly allocated `TestLogger` returned by `FromContext` and immediately discarded.

title: Device is cached before database limit check, bypassing the limit on subsequent requests
body: In `tagDeviceUI`, `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` is called before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)`. When the anonymous device limit has been reached, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and the first request is rejected in `Anonymous.Authenticate`. However, because the device's cache key is already stored in `localCache` (with a 29-minute TTL), any subsequent request from the same `X-Grafana-Device-Id` will hit the cache at line 83, cause `tagDeviceUI` to return `nil`, and allow the anonymous user to authenticate despite exceeding the device limit. `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` should only be called after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds.

title: MySQL `RowsAffected` returns 0 when updated values are unchanged, falsely triggering `ErrDeviceLimitReached`
body: In `updateDevice`, `result.RowsAffected()` is checked for `0` to determine if the device did not exist in the active window and `ErrDeviceLimitReached` should be returned. On MySQL (when `clientFoundRows` is not enabled in the DSN, which is the default), `UPDATE` returns `0` rows affected if a matching row is found but the column values (`client_ip`, `user_agent`, `updated_at`) are identical to the existing values in the database. Since MySQL's `DATETIME` / `TIMESTAMP` columns in Grafana have 1-second precision, if an already-registered device makes two requests within the same second (e.g., before caching or across instances) with the same IP and User-Agent while at the device limit, `RowsAffected()` will be `0` and the valid device will be rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

title: `untagDevice` does not evict the device from `localCache` on login
body: When a user logs in, the post-login hook `untagDevice` deletes their device from `anon_device` in the database so it no longer counts toward the anonymous device limit. However, `untagDevice` does not remove the device key from `a.localCache`. If the user logs out within the 29-minute cache TTL and continues browsing anonymously while the instance is at `deviceLimit`, `tagDeviceUI` will see the cached key and return `nil` without re-inserting the device or checking the limit, allowing an untracked anonymous session.

title: Device ID is cached before CreateOrUpdateDevice, allowing device limit bypass on subsequent requests
body: `tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` on line 87 before calling `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)` on line 93. When the device limit is reached, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and the first request fails authentication, but the rejected `deviceID` remains in `localCache` for 29 minutes. On the very next request with the same `X-Grafana-Device-Id`, `a.localCache.Get(key)` on line 83 hits the cache and `tagDeviceUI` returns `nil`, allowing the over-limit device to authenticate without ever being persisted or counted. Cache insertion should only happen after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds.

title: MySQL RowsAffected() returns 0 on no-op UPDATE, falsely triggering ErrDeviceLimitReached for existing devices
body: In `updateDevice`, when the device limit is reached and an already-registered device makes a request within the same second (MySQL `DATETIME` has 1-second precision and Grafana does not enable `clientFoundRows` on the MySQL DSN), `updated_at`, `client_ip`, and `user_agent` are identical to the stored row. MySQL's `RowsAffected()` returns 0 when matched rows have no changed column values, causing line 95 (`if rowsAffected == 0`) to return `ErrDeviceLimitReached` for a valid, already-counted device.

title: Changed ProvideAnonymousDeviceService signature without regenerating Wire DI code
body: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` changed its parameter from `anonStore anonstore.AnonStore` to `sqlStore db.DB`, and `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` changed from `ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore db.DB)` to `ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore db.DB, deviceLimit int64)`. Neither `pkg/server/wire_gen.go` nor the Wire provider sets in `pkg/server/wire.go` were updated in this PR, which will break the build.

title: Device ID is cached before checking the device limit, allowing any repeat request to bypass the limit
body: In `tagDeviceUI`, `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` (line 87) is executed before calling `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)` (line 93), and the cache entry is not removed when `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns an error. When the device limit has been reached, the first request from a new anonymous device will fail with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, but its device ID is now stored in `localCache` for 29 minutes. Every subsequent request from that same device hits `if _, ok := a.localCache.Get(key); ok { return nil }` on line 83, causing `TagDevice` to return `nil` and `Anonymous.Authenticate` to succeed. Only the cache entry after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds (or delete the cache entry on error).

title: MySQL RowsAffected() returns 0 when updated values are unchanged, falsely triggering ErrDeviceLimitReached
body: In `updateDevice`, `result.RowsAffected()` is checked for `== 0` to determine whether the device existed within the active 30-day window, and if 0, `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned. On MySQL (when `clientFoundRows` is not enabled in the DSN) and SQLite/Postgres in certain configurations or rapid requests within the same second (since MySQL `DATETIME` / timestamp columns have 1-second resolution), an `UPDATE` where `client_ip`, `user_agent`, and `updated_at` match the existing row values reports `0` affected rows even though the row matched the `WHERE` clause. When the device limit is reached, an existing valid device making another request within the same second on MySQL will get `0` rows affected and be wrongly rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

title: Cleanup service ticker interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
body: In `CleanUpService.Run`, the ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`, while the cleanup job timeout in `clean` remains `9 * time.Minute` (line 89). Running all background cleanup jobs (temporary files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, and query history) every minute instead of every 10 minutes looks like leftover local testing code and will significantly increase background database and filesystem load.

title: Debug logging left at Error level in annotation cleanup
body: `CleanAnnotations` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 576, 579) call `r.log.Error(...)` on every batch iteration even when no error occurred, and include the full slice of `ids` (up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize`) in the log fields. Because the cleanup job runs periodically and executes at least one batch per annotation type and tag check, this will spam error logs with large ID arrays during normal operation.

title: Quadratic string concatenation when building SQLite DELETE query for large batches
body: In `deleteByIDs`, when running on SQLite with `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, the `IN` list is constructed in a loop using `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` (lines 609-612). Because Go strings are immutable, this copies the growing `values` string on every element, resulting in O(N^2) allocations and CPU time in the batch size (e.g. ~32k iterations in the new test case). Use a `strings.Builder` or chunk the `DELETE` into batches of at most 999 parameters.

title: Unbounded SQL parameter count in deleteByIDs can exceed PostgreSQL and MySQL limits
body: `deleteByIDs` only guards against SQLite's parameter limit (line 608) and otherwise builds `DELETE FROM <table> WHERE id IN (?, ?, ...)` with `len(ids)` bound parameters. PostgreSQL and MySQL both enforce a maximum of 65,535 prepared-statement parameters (and older SQLite versions default to 999 when `len(ids) > 999`). If `annotation_cleanup_job_batch_size` is configured above 65,535, cleanup will fail with a database driver error on every run.

title: Cleanup service ticker interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
body: In `CleanUpService.Run`, the ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1` (likely left over from local debugging), while `srv.clean` still uses `const timeout = 9 * time.Minute`. This causes all background cleanup jobs (temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, and query history) to run 10x more frequently than intended.

title: Leftover debug `r.log.Error` calls log every cleanup batch as an error with full ID slices
body: `CleanAnnotations` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 576, 579) call `r.log.Error` unconditionally on every batch iteration, even when `err` is `nil`, and include the full `ids` slice in the log fields. Because `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` can be thousands of IDs, this will emit large error-level log entries on every batch of every cleanup run.

title: Quadratic string concatenation when building SQLite DELETE IN clause
body: In `deleteByIDs`, when running on SQLite with `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, the `IN` list is constructed in a loop using `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)`. Because strings are immutable in Go, re-formatting `values` on each iteration copies the entire accumulated string every time, taking O(N^2) time and allocations (for example, ~32k iterations in the new test case allocate hundreds of megabytes). Building the list with `strings.Builder` and `strconv.AppendInt` avoids the quadratic allocation.

title: Cleanup service ticker interval unintentionally reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
body: In `CleanUpService.Run`, the cleanup ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1` (while `clean` still uses a 9-minute timeout assuming a 10-minute period). This appears to be leftover local debugging code and will cause all background cleanup jobs (temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) to run 10x more frequently in production.

title: Leftover Error-level debug logs in cleanup loop will spam logs with full ID slices
body: `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` call `r.log.Error` before and after every batch deletion (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579), even when no error occurred and when `len(ids) == 0`. In addition to logging normal operation at `Error` level on every cleanup run, these calls log the entire `ids` slice, which can contain thousands of IDs per batch.

title: Quadratic string concatenation when building SQLite DELETE IN clause
body: In `deleteByIDs`, when building the `IN` list for SQLite with `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` is executed in a loop over `ids`. Because strings in Go are immutable, this copies the entire accumulated string on every iteration (O(N^2) time and allocations); for a batch of 32,767 IDs, a single call allocates hundreds of megabytes of transient strings. Use a `strings.Builder` (or `strconv.AppendInt`) instead.

title: Storage failures in Create and Update record metrics as legacy durations
body: In `DualWriterMode3.Create` (line 45) and `DualWriterMode3.Update` (line 129), when `d.Storage.Create` or `d.Storage.Update` returns an error, `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`. Conversely, in `DeleteCollection` (line 166), the asynchronous `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` call records its duration with `d.recordStorageDuration` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`. This misattributes unified storage errors to legacy storage metrics and legacy delete-collection durations to unified storage metrics.

title: Object name is passed as the kind label in Delete storage duration metric
body: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, line 106 calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passing the object `name` instead of `options.Kind` as the third argument (whereas line 103 and all other methods pass `options.Kind`). Aside from reporting the wrong label value, object names are unbounded per-resource identifiers, which introduces high-cardinality labels into the Prometheus metric.

title: Asynchronous legacy writes use the request context and can be canceled when the HTTP handler returns
body: In `Create` (line 51), `Delete` (line 110), `Update` (line 135), and `DeleteCollection` (line 163), the background goroutine derives its timeout context from the request `ctx` (`context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). Because the outer method returns immediately after the unified storage call completes, the HTTP server will finish the request and cancel `ctx`, which cancels the in-flight background `d.Legacy` operation before it finishes. The context passed to the goroutine should be detached from parent cancellation (e.g. using `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`).

title: Asynchronous Legacy.Create shares and mutates the input object concurrently and loses generated fields
body: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, `d.Storage.Create` returns the newly created object `created` (which has generated name, UID, timestamps, and resourceVersion populated), while the background goroutine calls `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` with the original `obj` (or if `Storage.Create` mutated `obj` in place, the caller/serializer may read `created` while `Legacy.Create` concurrently accesses or mutates the same struct). Furthermore, if a name was generated (e.g., via `generateName`), `obj` may not match `created` or may generate a different UID/name in legacy storage. A deep copy of `created` (or `obj`) should be passed to the background goroutine.

title: Delete attaches the base logger to context instead of the enriched logger
body: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, line 96 constructs `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)`, but line 97 passes `d.Log` instead of `log` to `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`, losing the `name`, `kind`, and `method` log fields for downstream consumers of the context.

title: Mode 3 unit tests race between background legacy goroutines and shared mock setup
body: In `TestMode3_Create`, `TestMode3_Delete`, `TestMode3_DeleteCollection`, and `TestMode3_Update`, both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` share the same `*mock.Mock` instance `m`, and the tests return immediately after `dw.<Method>` returns without synchronizing with the background goroutine launched by Mode 3. In `TestMode3_Delete` and `TestMode3_DeleteCollection`, only ` m.On("Delete", ...)` once is configured, and in `TestMode3_Create`'s error case (lines 38-44) `setupLegacyFn` registers the expectation on `m` (which actually matches `us.Create` because `m` is shared). If the background goroutine runs concurrently with assertions or after the test finishes, `testify/mock` is accessed concurrently without synchronization or panics on unexpected calls.

title: Async legacy writes use the request-scoped context and will be canceled when the HTTP handler returns
body: In `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection` (lines 51, 110, 135, 163), the background goroutine derives its timeout context directly from the incoming request context `ctx` via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`. Because the method returns immediately after the unified `Storage` call completes, the HTTP server will finish the request and cancel `ctx`, which immediately cancels the derived context in the background goroutine and aborts the in-flight `Legacy` write. Use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` before applying the timeout so the async legacy operation is not canceled by request completion.

title: Data race on `obj` between async `Legacy.Create` and caller using returned object
body: `Create` passes `obj` directly into the asynchronous `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` goroutine while simultaneously returning `created` (which in Kubernetes REST storage implementations is often the same pointer or shares underlying state with `obj`) to the caller for serialization and post-processing. If `Legacy.Create` or `createValidation` reads or mutates `obj` while the caller accesses it, a data race occurs. `obj` (or `created.DeepCopyObject()`) should be deep-copied before being passed to the background goroutine.

title: Object `name` passed instead of `options.Kind` to `recordStorageDuration` in `Delete`
body: On line 106, `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the resource instance `name` instead of `options.Kind` for the `kind` metric label. This records the wrong label value and introduces unbounded label cardinality into the Prometheus metric (one time series per deleted object name). Also on line 97, `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` is called instead of `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`, dropping the `name`, `kind`, and `method` log fields from the context.

title: Storage and legacy duration metrics are swapped in `Create`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection`
body:
Several metric recording calls record against the wrong store:
- Line 45 (`Create`): when `d.Storage.Create` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
- Line 129 (`Update`): when `d.Storage.Update` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
- Line 166 (`DeleteCollection`): inside the async goroutine for `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection`, `d.recordStorageDuration` is called instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`.

title: Storage create and update failures record legacy metrics instead of storage metrics
body: In `DualWriterMode3.Create` (line 45) and `DualWriterMode3.Update` (line 129), when `d.Storage.Create` or `d.Storage.Update` returns an error, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`. Conversely, in `DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection` (line 166), the asynchronous `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` call records its duration via `d.recordStorageDuration` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`. This misattributes storage failures to legacy metrics and legacy delete-collection metrics to unified storage.

title: Delete passes resource name instead of kind to metric label causing high cardinality
body: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete` at line 106, `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes `name` (the individual resource's name/UID) as the `kind` argument, whereas every other metric call passes `options.Kind`. Additionally, at line 97, `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` is called instead of `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`, dropping the `name`, `kind`, and `method` log values created on line 96. Passing `name` into a Prometheus metric label meant for `kind` will cause unbounded label cardinality as unique resource names are deleted.

title: Asynchronous legacy writes use request context that is canceled when the HTTP handler returns
body: In `Create` (line 51), `Delete` (line 110), `Update` (line 135), and `DeleteCollection` (line 163), the background goroutine derives its timeout context from the request `ctx` (`context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). Because the outer method returns immediately after the unified storage operation finishes, the HTTP server will cancel the request `ctx` as soon as the response is sent, aborting the in-flight asynchronous legacy write before it can complete (unless `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` is used).

title: Asynchronous Legacy.Create races with generated names and mutates shared object
body: In `DualWriterMode3.Create` (line 55), the background goroutine passes the original `obj` (rather than `created` or a deep copy of `created`) to `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)`. First, if the object used `generateName` (as tested in `playlist_test.go` with `playlist-generate.yaml`), `d.Storage.Create` populates the generated name on `created`, while `obj` may not have it or `Legacy.Create` will generate a different UID/name in the legacy store, causing the two stores to diverge. Second, because the caller receives `created` (which may share underlying state with `obj`) and continues processing it on the request goroutine while `Legacy.Create` reads/mutates `obj` concurrently, this introduces a data race.

title: Unit tests share a single testify Mock across concurrent goroutines without synchronizing
body: In `dualwriter_mode3_test.go` (`TestMode3_Create`, `TestMode3_Delete`, `TestMode3_DeleteCollection`, `TestMode3_Update`), both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` wrap the same `m := &mock.Mock{}` instance, and the tests return immediately after `dw.<Method>` returns while the background goroutine is concurrently calling methods on `ls` (which records calls into `m.Calls`). Furthermore, in the error test cases (e.g. `TestMode3_Create` line 40), `setupLegacyFn` registers the error expectation on `m`, which is actually consumed by `us.Create` only because both mocks share `m`. Sharing a `mock.Mock` across goroutines without waiting for the async goroutine to finish causes data races under `go test -race` and does not verify that `Legacy` was actually called.

title: Unlocked read of b.cache in TotalDocs causes a concurrent map read/write panic
body: `TotalDocs()` iterates over `b.cache` without acquiring `b.cacheMu.RLock()`. With `BuildIndex` now only locking around `b.cache[key] = idx` (and `getOrCreateIndex` being called from concurrent `Search` and watch-event handlers), calling `TotalDocs()` while another goroutine builds and inserts an index will trigger a fatal concurrent map iteration and map write panic.

title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows concurrent builds of the same key to collide on disk or leak indices
body: Previously `BuildIndex` held `b.cacheMu` for the entire build. Now it only locks when assigning `b.cache[key] = idx` at the end, and `searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex` has no per-key synchronization. If two callers (e.g., concurrent `Search` requests or watch events for an unindexed namespace) miss the cache in `GetIndex` at the same time, both will run `BuildIndex` for the same `NamespacedResource`: for file-backed indices (`size > b.opts.FileThreshold`), the second `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` fails because the directory/BoltDB file already exists; for memory indices, one index overwrites the other in `b.cache` and `IndexTenants` metrics are double-incremented.

title: If NewResourceServer fails during s.Init(ctx), the cancelable server context and any started background routines are leaked
body: `NewResourceServer` creates `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(...)` on line 229 and now calls `s.Init(ctx)` on line 258. If `s.Init(ctx)` returns an error (for example in `s.search.init` or `s.initWatcher`), `NewResourceServer` returns `nil, err` without calling `cancel()` or stopping `s.lifecycle`, leaking the context and any background goroutines started during partial initialization.

title: Removing s.Init checks from RPC handlers allows requests to proceed after Stop() is called
body: `Stop()` sets `s.initErr = fmt.Errorf("service is stopping")` / `"service is stopped"` to reject subsequent requests via `s.Init(ctx)`, which returns `s.initErr`. Removing the `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil` checks from `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `Read`, `List`, `Watch`, `Search`, `History`, `Origin`, `IsHealthy`, `PutBlob`, and `GetBlob` means `s.initErr` is no longer consulted by any RPC handler, so calls made while or after the server stops will no longer be rejected.

title: TotalDocs iterates over b.cache without holding cacheMu
body: `bleveBackend.TotalDocs` (called from `searchSupport.init` at line 216 of `pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go`) iterates over `b.cache` without acquiring `b.cacheMu.RLock()`. Now that `BuildIndex` only locks `b.cacheMu` when writing to `b.cache` (and `getOrCreateIndex` can also trigger `BuildIndex` concurrently via watch events or search calls), reading `b.cache` without synchronization is a data race that can panic at runtime if concurrent map writes occur.

title: Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key can race and corrupt or leak indexes
body: Previously `BuildIndex` held `b.cacheMu` across the entire index creation, serializing all builds. Moving the lock to only cover `b.cache[key] = idx` means two concurrent callers for the same `NamespacedResource` (e.g. a watch event in `handleEvent` and a `Search` request both hitting `getOrCreateIndex` when the index was skipped at startup due to `initMinSize`) will both build an index concurrently. For file-backed indexes (`size > b.opts.FileThreshold`), both goroutines will call `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same directory, causing one to fail or corrupt the on-disk index; for in-memory indexes, one index is silently overwritten without being closed and `IndexTenants` metrics are double-incremented.

title: Cancel function and background resources are leaked if s.Init fails in NewResourceServer
body: In `NewResourceServer`, `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(...)` is created at line 229, and `s.Init(ctx)` is called at line 258. If `s.Init(ctx)` returns an error (for example, `s.initWatcher()` fails after `s.lifecycle.Init` and `s.search.init` have already started background goroutines), `NewResourceServer` returns `nil, err` without calling `cancel()` or stopping the already-initialized components, leaking the context and any background goroutines started during partial initialization.

title: Data race on shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` across `errgroup` workers in `init`
body: In `searchSupport.init`, each `group.Go` closure mutates the outer variables `totalBatchesIndexed` (`totalBatchesIndexed++`) and `err` (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) without synchronization. Previously, `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` held `b.cacheMu.Lock()` for the entire build, which largely serialized these workers; with fine-grained locking in `BuildIndex`, multiple workers now execute `s.build` and assign to `err` concurrently whenever `WorkerThreads > 1`. This causes a data race (failing under `-race`) and can cause a worker's `return err` to read another goroutine's `nil` error, silently swallowing index build failures.

title: Concurrent map read in `TotalDocs` and map write in `BuildIndex`
body: `searchSupport.init` starts the background watch goroutine (`s.handleEvent` -> `s.getOrCreateIndex` -> `s.search.BuildIndex`) before calling `s.search.TotalDocs()` on line 216. In `bleveBackend.TotalDocs` (`pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:146`), `b.cache` is iterated without acquiring `b.cacheMu.RLock()`, while `BuildIndex` writes to `b.cache` under `b.cacheMu.Lock()`. If a watch event arrives for an unindexed resource while `TotalDocs()` is running, Go will panic with a concurrent map iteration and map write error.

title: Removing `s.Init` checks from RPC handlers makes `Stop` state checks ineffective
body: `server.Stop` sets `s.initErr` to `"service is stopping"` / `"service is stopped"` (lines 321, 328, 339). Previously, every gRPC handler called `s.Init(ctx)`, which returned `s.initErr` once `s.once` had completed, rejecting new requests after `Stop` was called. Because the `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `Read`, `List`, `Watch`, `Search`, `History`, `Origin`, `IsHealthy`, `PutBlob`, and `GetBlob`, mutations to `s.initErr` in `Stop` are never read and requests continue to be processed after `Stop`.

title: Call to non-existent zero-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` fails to compile
body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the method defined on the superclass `UsernamePasswordForm` (line 160) has the signature `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. This causes a compilation error (`method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled in class UsernamePasswordForm cannot be applied to given types; required: UserModel; found: no arguments`). Pass `context.getUser()` to match the superclass method signature.

title: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` requires `user != null`, breaking passkey login on initial authentication
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. During a normal (non-re-authentication) login, `context.getUser()` is `null` when `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate` and `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge` run, so `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` evaluates to `false` and `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never called. As a result, WebAuthn conditional UI attributes and the challenge are never added to the login form on initial login, completely breaking passkey authentication when no user is pre-selected. Additionally, when `user != null` (re-authentication), this check does not verify whether that user actually has a passkey credential (`webauthnAuth.configuredFor(...)`), so passkey UI will be rendered even for users without registered passkeys when realm passkeys are enabled. The condition should allow `user == null` or check `webauthnAuth.configuredFor(context.getSession(), context.getRealm(), user)` when `user != null`.

title: Compilation error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called with no arguments
body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but `UsernamePasswordForm` only defines `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` taking a `UserModel` parameter. This causes a compilation failure (`method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled in class UsernamePasswordForm cannot be applied to given types`).

title: Passkeys conditional UI is broken for initial login because user != null is required
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. During normal initial login, `context.getUser()` is `null`, so `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` at lines 115 and 137 always evaluates to `false`.
