Consequently, `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never called when no user is pre-selected, completely breaking passkey / WebAuthn Conditional UI login on initial login forms and after failed login challenges when the user was not already known.

title: Compilation error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called with no arguments
body: In `UsernameForm.authenticate`, `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is called without any arguments, but the method defined on the superclass `UsernamePasswordForm` (line 160) has the signature `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. This causes a compilation failure (`method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled in class UsernamePasswordForm cannot be applied to given types`).

title: Passkeys conditional UI is broken for initial login when user is null
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Because it requires `user != null`, `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is skipped in both `authenticate(context)` (line 115) and `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137) whenever `context.getUser()` is `null`—which is the normal initial login case before any user has been identified. As a result, the WebAuthn conditional UI form attributes and challenge are never populated on initial login, breaking passkey authentication whenever a user is not already set in the context.

title: Organization disabled prevents login cache invalidation when updating or removing an organization-linked IDP
body: `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` (and `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` on remove) uses `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to decide whether the IDP qualifies for login. In `update()`, `original` (`idpById`) is obtained via `getById(...)`, which wraps the model with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. That wrapper overrides `isEnabled()` to return `false` whenever the linked organization is currently disabled. Meanwhile, the JPA `getForLogin` query populates the login cache based on the database column `enabled = true` without checking whether the organization is enabled. Consequently, if an organization is temporarily disabled while an IDP linked to it is in the login cache, any update to that IDP (such as disabling it, setting `hideOnLogin = true`, setting `BROKER_PUBLIC = false`, or unlinking it from the organization) or removing it sees `getLoginPredicate().test(original) == false` and skips invalidating the login cache. If the organization is later re-enabled, `getForLogin` will continue serving stale cached results containing the disabled, hidden, or unlinked IDP.

title: Test cleanup registers literal "alias" instead of the created IDP's alias
body: In `testCacheIDPForLogin` (lines 381 and 425), cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` using the literal string `"alias"` instead of the actual alias of the created identity provider (`"idp-alias-" + i` and `"idp-alias-20"`). As a result, the 20+ identity providers created during this test are never removed after the test finishes and will leak into subsequent tests in the suite.

title: `getLoginPredicate()` returns false for enabled IDPs linked to a disabled organization
body: In `update(IdentityProviderModel model)`, `original` is retrieved via `getById(model.getInternalId())`, which wraps the cached model in `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` (line 432). That wrapper overrides `isEnabled()` to return `false` whenever the linked organization is currently disabled. Because `LoginFilter.ENABLED` calls `IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled`, `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` evaluates to `false` for an enabled IDP if its organization happens to be disabled at the time of the update. Conversely, `getForLogin` queries `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)` in JPA, which checks the IDP's own `enabled` column without checking the organization's `enabled` state, so IDPs of disabled organizations ARE stored in the `getForLogin` cache (and filtered later by `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`). If an IDP is added, removed, or updated while its organization is disabled (e.g., changing `hideOnLogin` or unlinking it from the disabled organization), `getLoginPredicate()` wrongly concludes the IDP is not a login IDP and skips invalidating the login caches. Once the organization is re-enabled, `getForLogin` will serve stale cached IDP lists.

title: Test cleanup registers literal `"alias"` instead of the created IDP alias
body: At lines 381 and 425 of `testCacheIDPForLogin`, the cleanup handler is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` using the literal string `"alias"` instead of the actual alias of the created identity provider (`"idp-alias-" + i` and `"idp-alias-20"`). None of the 20 created identity providers are removed after the test finishes (and cleanup will fail with a 404 trying to delete `"alias"`), leaking test data into subsequent tests in the class.

title: `remove(alias)` throws NullPointerException when removing a non-existent alias and the cache key is invalidated
body: In `remove(String alias)`, `storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` can be `null` if no identity provider exists for the given alias. When `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is true, `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` is called unconditionally, which dereferences `storedIdp.getInternalId()` on line 366 and throws a `NullPointerException` instead of returning `false` as required by the `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove` contract. `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` (and `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`) should be guarded by a `storedIdp != null` check.

title: Cleanup callbacks in `testCacheIDPForLogin` reference literal `"alias"` instead of the created IDP alias
body: On lines 381 and 425, cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` using the literal string `"alias"` instead of `"idp-alias-" + i` / `"idp-alias-20"`. As a result, none of the 20+ identity providers created by `testCacheIDPForLogin` are removed after the test finishes (and the cleanup attempts to delete a non-existent `"alias"` provider), leaking state into subsequent tests in the same class/realm.

title: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getSignature throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking JWT client authentication
body: `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getSignature(String sigAlgName)` throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.")`. However, `authz-client` supports `client-jwt` authentication via `JWTClientCredentialsProvider`, which signs client assertion JWTs using `KeyWrapper` -> ` AsymmetricSignatureSignerContext` -> `ServerECDSASignatureSignerContext` / `ServerAsymmetricSignatureSignerContext` (in `keycloak-core`), or `JWKSUtils` / `JWSInput` verification, which call `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getSignature(alg)`. When `AuthzClient` runs with `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` as the active `CryptoProvider` (i.e. without `keycloak-crypto-default` on the classpath, which is the intended use case for this provider), any signature operation going through `CryptoProvider.getSignature` will fail with `UnsupportedOperationException`.

title: ECDSAAlgorithmTest uses a P-256 key for ES384 and ES512 and never verifies the re-encoded DER signature
body: In `ECDSAAlgorithmTest`, `keyPair` is generated once with `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` (which defaults to a 256-bit curve) and reused for `ES256`, `ES384`, and `ES512`. Because a 256-bit key always produces ~32-byte `r` and `s` values, `testES384` and `testES512` never exercise 48-byte or 66-byte `r`/`s` values (especially the 66-byte `secp521r1` case where the leading byte is `0x00` or `0x01` and DER length exceeds 127 bytes). Furthermore, `test()` only checks that `asn1derToConcatenatedRS(concatenatedRSToASN1DER(rsConcat))` equals `rsConcat`, without verifying `asn1Des` using `Signature.verify(asn1Des)`. If `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` produced invalid DER that `ASN1Decoder` happened to accept symmetrically, the test would still pass.

title: Redundant unused ASN1Encoder allocations in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` and discard the resulting encoders before lines 119-120 perform the exact same operations inside `writeDerSeq(...)`. Those two statements are dead work and allocate unnecessary `ASN1Encoder` and `ByteArrayOutputStream` instances on every ECDSA signature conversion.

title: UnsupportedOperationException in getKeyFactory and getSignature breaks JWT client credentials
body: `AuthzClient` supports `client-jwt` credentials via `JWTClientCredentialsProvider`, which loads the client's private key from a keystore and signs a JWT using `KeyWrapper` and `AsymmetricSignatureSignerContext`. During that flow, `KeyWrapper` and `KeyUtils` invoke `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getKeyFactory(...)`, `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getSignature(...)`, `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getPemUtils()`, and `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getEcdsaCryptoProvider()` (which are also used when verifying tokens or parsing keys). In `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, `getKeyFactory` and `getSignature` throw `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.")`. When `AuthzClient` runs with `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` as the active `CryptoProvider` (i.e. without `keycloak-crypto-default` on the classpath, which is the scenario this provider is added for), any client authentication or token operation that uses `getKeyFactory` or `getSignature` will fail at runtime with `UnsupportedOperationException`.

title: Indefinite-length ASN.1 sequence or element causes negative allocation or infinite loop
body: `ASN1Decoder.readLength()` returns `-1` when it encounters the indefinite-length byte `0x80` (lines 133-135). However, callers do not handle `-1`: in `readInteger()` and `readNext()`, `read(length)` is called with a negative value (or `length` after `reset()`), throwing `NegativeArraySizeException` instead of `IOException`; in `readSequence()`, `length` is `-1` so the `while (length > 0)` loop is skipped and an empty sequence is returned. In DER encoding, indefinite lengths are invalid and should throw an `IOException` rather than returning `-1`.

title: Redundant unused ASN1Encoder allocations in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` and discard the returned encoders, immediately repeating the exact same work on lines 119-120 inside `writeDerSeq(...)`. Those two statements allocate `ByteArrayOutputStream`s and encode the integers for no effect.

title: ECDSAAlgorithmTest uses a single P-256 key pair for ES384 and ES512 and does not verify the re-encoded DER signature
body: `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` generates a single default `EC` key pair (256-bit) in the constructor and reuses it for `ES256`, `ES384`, and `ES512`, and only asserts that `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` -> `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` -> `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` round-trips to the same byte array. It never passes `asn1Des` back to `Signature.verify(asn1Des)` to confirm the DER output produced by `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` is actually valid ASN.1 DER accepted by the JCA `Signature` verifier, nor does it test with 384-bit (`secp384r1`) or 521-bit (`secp521r1`) keys where `r` and `s` have lengths > 127 bytes (which exercises multi-byte ASN.1 length encoding in `ASN1Encoder`/`ASN1Decoder`).

title: Negative (indefinite) ASN.1 length causes NegativeArraySizeException instead of IOException
body: `ASN1Decoder.readLength()` returns `-1` when it encounters the indefinite-length byte `0x80` (lines 133-135). However, callers (`readSequence`, `readInteger`, and `readNext`) do not handle `-1` as an indefinite length: `readInteger()` passes `-1` directly to `read(length)` which throws `NegativeArraySizeException` on `new byte[length]`, and `readNext()` adds `reset()` (typically 2) to `-1` and reads 1 byte instead of failing, corrupting parsing or causing an infinite loop in `readSequence()`. Since DER encoding does not allow indefinite lengths (or if indefinite length is not supported), `readLength()` should throw an `IOException` when `length == 0x80`.

title: ECDSAAlgorithmTest uses a single P-256 key for ES384 and ES512 and does not verify the re-encoded DER signature
body: `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` generates a single default EC key pair (256-bit / P-256) in the constructor and reuses it across `testES256`, `testES384`, and `testES512`. Because the key is 256-bit, `signature.sign()` always produces ~64-byte R/S values (32 bytes each) even with `SHA384withECDSA` and `SHA512withECDSA`, so `testES384` (96-byte signatureLength) and `testES512` (132-byte signatureLength, where 66-byte R/S requires multi-byte DER length encoding > 127 bytes) never exercise full-size P-384 / P-521 signatures or long-form DER lengths. In addition, `test()` only checks that converting DER -> RS -> DER -> RS yields the same RS array, without verifying `asn1Des` against `Signature.verify(asn1Des)` to ensure the produced ASN.1 DER is accepted by the JCA `Signature` verifier.

title: Unused ASN1Encoder allocations in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` and discard the returned encoders before immediately repeating the exact same calls inside `writeDerSeq(...)` on lines 119-120. Those two statements are dead code that allocate and populate `ByteArrayOutputStream` instances for nothing.

title: `getClientsWithPermission` does not find per-client resources because their resource type is never set
body: `getClientsWithPermission(String scope)` queries `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. However, in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(...)` (lines 104-110), when a per-client (or per-user) resource is created via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())`, `resource.setType(resourceType)` is never called (only the top-level "all-resource" resources created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init(...)` have `type` set). As a result, `findByType` will never return individual client resources, and `getClientsWithPermission` (which is used by `ClientsResource.getClients` to filter and list clients a caller has access to when they don't have global view/manage permissions) will not return the IDs of clients granted individual permissions (or will only return the literal string `"Clients"` if an all-clients permission is granted, which is not a valid client ID). Notice that `PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient` only passed `clients().findAll()` because `myclient` was given `MANAGE`, which makes `canConfigure(myclient)` -> `canView(myclient)` return true when iterating, whereas `ClientsResource` relies on `getClientsWithPermission` for filtering when listing.

title: `getResourceName` does not handle `CLIENTS` resource type
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` (lines 304-326) only resolves human-readable names for `USERS.getType()` (returning `"All users"` or `user.getUsername()`) and falls back to `resource.getDisplayName()` for other resource types. For `CLIENTS` resources, `displayName` is not set, so representations of client permissions/resources (e.g., in the Admin UI / REST API policy resource list) will return `null` (or the internal UUID) instead of `"All clients"` or the client's `clientId`.

title: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` ignores the "all-clients" permission when a per-client resource exists for a different scope
body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)` (lines 214-234), if a resource for `client.getId()` exists in `resourceStore` (for example, because a permission was created on that specific client for `VIEW`), `resource` is non-null, so the fallback to the `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` ("all-clients") resource in lines 215-222 is skipped completely. If the caller was granted `MANAGE` on "all-clients" and a separate permission exists on `client` for `VIEW` (or for another user), evaluating `hasPermission(client, MANAGE)` will only evaluate permissions attached to the specific client resource and will return `false`, failing to fall back to the "all-clients" permission (unlike `UserPermissionsV2`, which evaluates both the user resource and the all-users resource).

title: `getClientsWithPermission` only finds the 'Clients' resource-type resource because per-client resources have no type set
body: `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(String scope)` queries `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` to find all client resources that have been granted the given scope. However, when individual client resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(...)` (lines 104-111), `resource.setType(resourceType)` is never called—only the top-level 'all-resource' resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init(...)` has `type` set to `"Clients"`. As a result, `findByType` only ever matches the single `Clients` resource-type resource (returning `"Clients"` as a client ID in the set) and never returns the IDs of individual clients for which permissions were created. Note that `PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient` only passes `clients().findAll()` because the caller is authenticated via `myclient`, which `ClientsResource.getClients` always includes when its own ID is in the token, masking the fact that `getClientsWithPermission` returned an empty set.

title: `getResourceName` does not handle `CLIENTS` resource type
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` only has a branch for `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` (lines 310-322) to translate the resource name (which stores the entity's internal UUID or the resource type name) into a human-readable name (`"All users"` or `user.getUsername()`). It was not updated to handle `CLIENTS.getType()`, so for client permissions it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` (which is null/UUID rather than `"All clients"` or `client.getClientId()`), causing policy/permission representations for Clients to return raw UUIDs or null instead of clientIds.

title: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` ignores the all-clients permission when a per-client resource exists for a different scope
body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)` (lines 214-224), if a resource for `client.getId()` exists in `resourceStore`, ONLY that resource is evaluated and the `Clients` resource-type resource is never checked. A per-client resource is created as soon as any permission targets that specific client (for example, a permission granting only `map-roles` on `clientA`, or a negative permission on another scope). If an administrator also has an all-clients permission granting `view` or `manage` on the `Clients` resource type, evaluating `hasPermission(clientA, VIEW)` will find the `clientA` resource, evaluate only the policies attached to `clientA` (which don't grant `view`), and return `false` instead of falling back to the `Clients` resource-type permission (compare with `UserPermissionsV2`, which evaluates both the user resource and the `Users` resource-type resource).

title: `getClientsWithPermission` returns empty set for per-client permissions because individual client resources have no type
body: `getClientsWithPermission(String scope)` queries `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. However, when a permission is created for a specific client, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (line 104) creates the resource via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` without setting its `type` (only the 'all-clients' resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` has `resource.setType(type)`). As a result, `findByType` will never find per-client resources, and `getClientsWithPermission` will only ever match the `Clients` resource-type resource (returning the literal string `"Clients"`, which is not a client ID) instead of the IDs of clients with granted permissions. In `ClientsResource.getClients`, when `canView()` is false, this causes the client list to be empty even when the caller has `view`, `configure`, or `manage` permissions on individual clients (note that in `PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient`, `findAll()` only passed because `myclient` has `alwaysDisplayInConsole` or similar, or `view` wasn't tested with a non-console client).

title: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName` does not handle `CLIENTS` resource type
body: `getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` only checks `if (USERS.getType().equals(resourceType))` to resolve the human-readable name (returning `"All users"` or `user.getUsername()`), and falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` for `CLIENTS`. Because client resources are created with the client's internal UUID as `name` and no `displayName`, representations of policies/permissions for `Clients` will return `null` (or the internal UUID) as the resource name instead of `"All clients"` or `client.getClientId()`.

title: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` ignores `all-clients` permission when a per-client resource exists for a different scope
body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, if a resource for `client.getId()` exists in `resourceStore` (for example, because a permission was created on that specific client for `map-roles`), `resource` is non-null at line 215, so the `all-clients` (`CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`) resource is never evaluated. If the caller was granted `view` or `manage` via an `all-clients` permission, `hasPermission(client, VIEW)` or `hasPermission(client, MANAGE)` (when called via `canConfigure(client)` or `canManage(client)`) will evaluate only the per-client resource and falsely return `false`. Compare with `UserPermissionsV2`, which evaluates both the specific resource and the resource-type resource (or combines their permissions).

title: `isPermissionsEnabled` and `getAccess` in `ClientPermissionsV2` break `ClientResource.getClient` when FGAP V2 is enabled
body: `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides `isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel)` to throw `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`, while inheriting `getAccess(ClientModel)` from `ClientPermissions`. When `ClientResource.getClient()` (i.e. `GET /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}`) is called, it invokes `auth.clients().getAccess(client)` which works, and if `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` is also enabled or if any admin endpoint calls `isPermissionsEnabled`, it will throw an unhandled `UnsupportedOperationException` (HTTP 500). Furthermore, `ClientPermissions.canView()` (called by `super.canList()`) or other inherited methods in `ClientPermissions` must be checked to ensure they don't call unsupported V1 methods.

title: `@Launch` defaults to expecting exit code 0, which will fail `testFeatureNotEnabled`
body: In `UpdateCommandDistTest.testFeatureNotEnabled`, `@Launch({UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME})` is used without specifying `exitCode`. Quarkus's `@Launch` annotation has a default `exitCode = 0` and automatically asserts that the process exit code matches it before invoking the test method. Because `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` now calls `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` (exit code 4) when `rolling-updates` is not enabled, this test will fail with an assertion error expecting exit code 0 unless `exitCode = CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` is specified on `@Launch`.

title: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants global manage access when caller only has VIEW permission
body: In `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()`, line 70 calls `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Because `VIEW` is included in the expected scopes, any admin granted only the `view` scope on the `Groups` (all-groups) resource will have `canManage()` return `true`. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` guards group creation and moving groups to the top level with `auth.groups().requireManage()`, so an admin with only `view` permission on all groups can create top-level groups or move existing groups to top level. `canManage()` should only check `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (and the Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` at line 75 should be updated accordingly).

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses resource ID instead of group ID (resource name) and ignores resource type on creation
body:
In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` is used to find group resources, and then `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` are called. There are three issues here:
1. When `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates a per-group resource (lines 121-127 of `AdminPermissionsSchema.java`), it sets the resource's `name` to `group.getId()`, while `resource.getId()` is a newly generated resource UUID, and it never calls `resource.setType(...)` on individual resources (only the 'all-groups' resource created in `init()` has `type = "Groups"`). As a result, `findByType` will not find individual group resources at all.
2. `hasPermission` looks up the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. Passing `groupResource.getId()` (the resource UUID) instead of `groupResource.getName()` (the group UUID) causes `findByName` to return `null` and fall back to the all-groups resource.
3. `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` adds the authorization `Resource` UUID instead of the `GroupModel` ID (`groupResource.getName()`), so subsequent user queries filtering by `UserModel.GROUPS` will not match any group memberships.

title: User search restricts results to group members even when admin has permission to view users directly
body: In `UsersResource.searchForUser` (and identically in `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` at line 147), the `if (!auth.users().canView())` guard was removed before calling `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`. Additionally, in FGAP V2, an admin can have `view` permission on specific individual users (without global `auth.users().canView()`) AND `view-members` permission on a group. When `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` is set, the user storage query restricts the DB search to *only* members of `groupIds`, which filters out any users outside those groups that the admin had direct user-level permission to view, and also sets `usersEvaluator.grantIfNoPermission(true)` (line 459), which in `UserPermissions` bypasses per-user view checks.

title: AdminPermissionsSchema does not handle Group resources in getResourceName and resolveGroup
body: In `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` (lines 328-350), only `USERS.getType()` is handled to resolve a human-readable name (`"All users"` or `user.getUsername()`). For `GROUPS` (and `CLIENTS`), `getResourceName` falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is `null` for resources created by `getOrCreateResource`, causing policy/permission representations returned by the API to have `null` resource names instead of the group name or `"All groups"`.

title: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` grants manage permission when the caller only has `view` scope on all-groups
body: In `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` (line 70, and documented in `GroupPermissionEvaluator` line 75), `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` is called, which checks whether the caller has either `view` OR `manage` permission on the all-groups resource. Because `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` calls `auth.groups().requireManage()`, any user granted only the `view` scope on the `Groups` resource type can create or move top-level groups in the realm. `canManage()` should only check `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE`.

title: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` in `GroupPermissionsV2` does not match group resources and returns resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (lines 121-125): (1) `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` only finds resources whose `type` is set to `"Groups"`. However, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never sets the resource type on individual group resources when creating them (only the all-groups resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` has `type = "Groups"`). (2) Inside the callback, `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` is called, but `hasPermission` looks up the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` where the resource's `name` is the group's ID (not `groupResource.getId()`). (3) `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` adds the authorization resource's internal ID rather than the `GroupModel` ID (`groupResource.getName()`). As a result, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` will never return the actual group IDs, breaking user search and user count filtering by group view permissions in FGAP V2.

title: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName` does not handle `GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE`
body: In `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName` (lines 328-350), only `USERS` is handled to translate a resource name (which stores the entity ID) into a human-readable name. For `GROUPS`, individual group resources are created with `name = group.getId()` and no display name, so `getResourceName` falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` and returns `null` (or the raw resource name for the `Groups` resource-type resource instead of a label like `"All groups"`).

title: `canManage()` grants group management permission to callers with only `view` scope on all-groups
body: In `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()`, line 70 calls `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Because `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` checks `auth.groups().requireManage()`, any caller who is granted only the `view` scope on the all-groups resource (`Groups`) will pass `canManage()` and be able to create or move top-level groups in the realm. `canManage()` should only check `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (and the Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` at line 75 should be updated accordingly).

title: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` passes authz resource ID instead of group ID and returns resource IDs
body: When `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates a group resource, it sets the resource's `name` to `group.getId()` (while `resource.getId()` is the newly generated UUID of the authorization `Resource`, and for the all-groups resource `name` is `"Groups"`). In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, lines 121-125 iterate over resources of type `Groups` and: (1) pass `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)`, which looks up `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` — because `findByName` matches the group ID (stored in `resource.getName()`), looking up by `groupResource.getId()` returns `null` and falls back to the all-groups resource instead of evaluating the specific group resource; and (2) add `groupResource.getId()` (the authz resource UUID) to `granted` instead of `groupResource.getName()` (the actual group ID), causing user queries filtered by `UserModel.GROUPS` to match no users (unless the all-groups resource itself is matched, which also has name `"Groups"` rather than a group ID).

title: `canCreateGroupMembers` checks only V1 feature flag, breaking user creation via group permissions in V2
body: `UsersResource.canCreateGroupMembers` (line 178) returns `false` when `!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`. When `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled (and V1 is disabled), an admin with `manage-members` and `manage-membership` permissions on a group cannot create a user directly in that group via `POST /users`, because `canCreateGroupMembers` immediately returns `false` instead of evaluating the group permissions.

title: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName` does not handle `GROUPS` resource type
body: In `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName` (lines 328-350), only `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` is handled to resolve the human-readable resource name, while `GROUPS` (and `CLIENTS`) fall through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Because `getOrCreateResource` creates group resources with `name = group.getId()` and no display name, policies/permissions for groups will return `null` (or raw UUIDs) as the resource name in representations instead of `"All groups"` or the group's name/path.

title: Javadoc on `requireManageMembers` references `canManageMembership` instead of `canManageMembers`
body: On line 133 of `GroupPermissionEvaluator.java`, the Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel group)` states `Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}`, but the method actually checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`.

title: Prefix and suffix diff stripping can overlap and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body: When computing the difference between `value` and `sanitized` for the error message, `start` and `end` are incremented independently without ensuring `start + end <= Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length())`. If one string is a prefix/suffix of the other with repeated characters around the difference (for example, `value` is `"<b><b>"` and `sanitized` is `"<b>"`), `start` reaches 3 and `end` reaches 3, causing `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` to call `substring(3, 0)` and throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`. The second loop condition should also require `start + end < sanitized.length() && start + end < value.length()`.

title: ANCHOR_PATTERN matches any tag starting with 'a', not just <a> tags
body: `ANCHOR_PATTERN` is defined as `Pattern.compile("</?a[^>]*>")`. Because there is no word boundary or whitespace/closing-bracket check after `a`, this regex also matches other HTML tags whose names begin with `a`, such as `<abbr>`, `<article>`, `<aside>`, `<audio>`, or `<applet>`. A translation containing `<applet>` or `<audio>` will be treated as an anchor tag in `santizeAnchors` rather than being evaluated by the HTML sanitizer policy. The pattern should require `>` or whitespace after `a` (e.g., `</?a(?:\s[^>]*)?>`).

title: i18next message replaced with Java MessageFormat syntax in account-ui and admin-ui bundles
body: In `js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3/account/messages/messages_en.properties` (and `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties` line 3138), `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The `account-ui` and `admin-ui` apps use i18next on the frontend, which expects `{{0}}` interpolation placeholders (like all other keys in these two files) and does not support Java `MessageFormat` `{2,choice,...}` syntax. When rendered through i18next, the placeholders and choice pattern will be displayed literally without substitution.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: In the Lithuanian localization files `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties` (line 101, `totpStep1`) and `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` (line 71, `loginTotpStep1`), the Lithuanian text was replaced with Italian: `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`.

title: Potential StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when diffing strings with overlapping prefix and suffix
body:
In `verifySafeHtml()`, `start` is incremented from the beginning while `value` and `sanitized` match, and `end` is incremented from the end independently without checking `start + end < value.length()` and `start + end < sanitized.length()`. When one string is formed by inserting or deleting repeated characters inside a run of identical characters (for example, `value = "

"` vs `sanitized = "

"`, or `value = "aaa"` vs `sanitized = "aa"`), `start + end` will exceed the shorter string's length, causing `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` (or the `value.substring` call) on line 111 to throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of recording a validation message.

title: `ANCHOR_PATTERN` matches any tag starting with `a`, such as `<abbr>`, `<article>`, or `<audio>`
body: `ANCHOR_PATTERN` is defined as `Pattern.compile("</?a[^>]*>")`, which matches any HTML tag whose name begins with `a` (e.g. `<abbr>`, `<address>`, `<area>`, `<article>`, `<aside>`, `<audio>`), not just `<a>` tags. A disallowed tag like `<audio src=...>` or `<article>` will be treated as an anchor tag by `santizeAnchors` rather than being evaluated by the HTML sanitizer policy (or could even be stripped before sanitization if present in the English string). title: i18next message replaced with incompatible Java MessageFormat `choice` syntax in Account and Admin UI
body: In `js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3/account/messages/messages_en.properties` (line 188) and `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties` (line 3138), `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from i18next interpolation syntax (`Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).`) to Java `MessageFormat` syntax (`Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`). The Account UI and Admin UI are React/i18next applications that use `{{0}}` double-brace placeholders (like all other `error-*` keys in these files) and do not evaluate Java `ChoiceFormat` expressions, so placeholders and `{2,choice,...}` will be rendered literally to users in the UI.

title: Lithuanian `totpStep1` / `loginTotpStep1` replaced with Italian translation
body: In both `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties` (line 101) and `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` (line 71), the Lithuanian translation was replaced with the Italian text `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` instead of Lithuanian.

title: Potential StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when computing diff for prefix/suffix overlapping strings
body: In `verifySafeHtml()`, when `value` and `sanitized` share both a common prefix and a common suffix that overlap (for example, `value = "<b><b>"` and `sanitized = "<b>"`, or `value = "a<x>a"` and `sanitized = "aa"`), `start` and `end` are incremented independently without checking `start + end <= Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length())`. As a result, `start` can exceed `value.length() - end` or `sanitized.length() - end`, causing `substring(start, ... - end)` on line 111 to throw a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of reporting the validation error. Guard the second `while` loop with `start + end < sanitized.length() && start + end < value.length()`.

title: `ANCHOR_PATTERN` matches any HTML tag starting with `a`, not just `<a>` tags
body: `ANCHOR_PATTERN` is defined as `Pattern.compile("</?a[^>]*>")`, which matches any tag whose name begins with `a` (such as `<applet>`, `<audio>`, `<area>`, `<article>`, or `<aside>`), not only anchor tags. Those tags will be processed by `santizeAnchors` rather than the HTML policy, producing misleading error messages ("Didn't find anchor tag <audio>...") or stripping them if they happen to match. The regex should require a word boundary or whitespace/closing bracket after `a`, e.g. `</?a(?:\s[^>]*)?>`.

title: i18next message in Account UI replaced with Java MessageFormat syntax
body: In `js/apps/account-ui/.../messages_en.properties` (and `js/apps/admin-ui/.../messages_en.properties`), `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from i18next interpolation syntax (`Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).`) to Java `MessageFormat` / `ChoiceFormat` syntax (`Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`). The React-based account-ui and admin-ui use i18next (note every other key in these files uses `{{...}}`), which does not support Java `MessageFormat` single-brace placeholders or `choice` formats, so placeholders will render literally as `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` in the UI.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian account messages (`messages_lt.properties`, line 101) and `loginTotpStep1` in the Lithuanian login messages (`themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties`, line 71) were replaced with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian rather than Lithuanian.

title: Null check in AccessTokenContext constructor checks grantType instead of rawTokenId
body: In the `AccessTokenContext` constructor, line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. As a result, a null `rawTokenId` is accepted without throwing a `NullPointerException`, violating the constructor's intended invariant.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong substring indices and inverted equality check
body: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the prefix before `:` is 6 characters long (`<2-char sessionType><2-char tokenType><2-char grantType>`, e.g., `onrtac`), so the grant shortcut is at `substring(4, 6)` rather than `substring(3, 5)`. Furthermore, the condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is inverted (missing `!`). Because `substring(3, 5)` extracts the second character of the token type plus the first character of the grant type (e.g., `ta`), it never equals `expectedGrantShortcut`, causing the matcher to accidentally pass without ever verifying the grant shortcut (and it would throw `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if `items[0]` has fewer than 5 characters).

title: Javadoc for getShortcut() says 3-letters shortcut, but encoder requires exactly 2 characters
body: The Javadoc on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` states `@return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants`. However, all implementations return 2-character shortcuts and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` strictly requires the encoded context to be 6 characters total (`encodedContext.length() != 6`) and extracts the grant shortcut via `encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`. Implementing a 3-letter shortcut as suggested by the Javadoc will cause token ID decoding to fail with an `IllegalArgumentException`.

title: Inverted condition and wrong substring indices in isAccessTokenId matcher
body:
In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut)`, the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` has two bugs:
1. The prefix before `:` is 6 characters long (`<2-char sessionType><2-char tokenType><2-char grantType>`), so the grant type shortcut is at indices `(4, 6)` (matching `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId`), not `(3, 5)`.
2. The equality check is not negated: it returns `false` when the substring equals `expectedGrantShortcut` and `true` when it does not. Because `substring(3, 5)` extracts the second character of the token type plus the first character of the grant type (e.g. `"ta"` for `"onrtac"`), it never equals `"ac"`, causing the assertion to accidentally pass for any grant shortcut (and it would also throw `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if `items[0]` has fewer than 5 characters).

title: Constructor checks grantType for null twice instead of checking rawTokenId
body: In the `AccessTokenContext` constructor, line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. Passing a null `rawTokenId` will therefore not be rejected as intended.

title: Javadoc on OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() says 3-letters shortcut
body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` documents the return value as "usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants", whereas `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` strictly requires the grant shortcut to be 2 characters long (expecting a total prefix length of 6 characters and slicing `encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`). Implementing a custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with a 3-letter shortcut as suggested by the Javadoc will cause `getTokenContextFromTokenId` to fail with `IllegalArgumentException: Incorrect token id ... Expected length of 6`.

title: Null check in AccessTokenContext constructor checks grantType instead of rawTokenId
body: In the `AccessTokenContext` constructor, line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. As a result, a null `rawTokenId` is accepted by the constructor and stored in `this.rawTokenId`, rather than failing fast with the intended `NullPointerException`.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong substring indices and inverted equality check
body: `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` checks the grant shortcut with `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` (and does not check that `items[0].length() == 6`). In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider`, the 6-character prefix is encoded as sessionType (indices 0..2), tokenType (indices 2..4), and grantType (indices 4..6). Using `substring(3, 5)` extracts the second character of tokenType and the first character of grantType (e.g. `"ta"` for `"onrtac"`), and the condition returns `false` when it equals `expectedGrantShortcut` instead of when it does not equal `expectedGrantShortcut`. The matcher therefore only passes by accident because `substring(3, 5)` almost never matches the expected grant shortcut, and it fails to verify that the token ID actually contains the expected grant shortcut.

title: Javadoc for OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() says 3-letters shortcut instead of 2 characters
body: The Javadoc on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` states `@return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants`, whereas `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` requires the entire encoded context prefix (`sessionType` + `tokenType` + `grantType`) to be 6 characters long (`encodedContext.length() != 6`) and parses the grant shortcut as `encodedContext.substring(4, 6)` (2 characters). Any `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation returning a 3-letter shortcut as suggested by the Javadoc will cause `getTokenContextFromTokenId` to throw `IllegalArgumentException`.

title: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential bypasses custom UserStorageProvider.getCredentials() implementations
body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` looks up recovery codes by calling `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()` and falling back to `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)`. `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` only queries `session.userFederatedStorage()` (Keycloak's built-in federated storage table), whereas `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream` queries both local storage and `UserStorageProvider.getCredentials(...)`. However, in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest`, `UserModel` extends `AbstractUserAdapterFederatedStorage`, where `credentialManager().getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...)` delegates to `getFederatedCredentialsStream(...)` unless the provider implements `getCredentials`. More importantly, if a user has recovery codes in both federated storage and local storage, or if a `UserStorageProvider` does not use `userFederatedStorage()` and does not override `getCredentials()` to return a full `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` (for instance, a legacy storage provider that only implements `CredentialInputUpdater` and `CredentialInputValidator` as in Keycloak 4.8.3), `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` will return `Optional.empty()`. In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` (line 19), `credentialModelOpt.get()` is called unconditionally without checking `isPresent()`, which will throw `NoSuchElementException` when rendering the recovery code login form for such a provider, and in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` (line 90), `recoveryCodeCredentialModel == null` will force `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES` after a single login.

title: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage overrides getCredentials, breaking its 4.8.3 backwards-compatibility contract
body: The class-level Javadoc of `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` states: "UserStorage implementation created in Keycloak 4.8.3. It is used for backwards compatibility testing. Future Keycloak versions should work fine without a need to change the code of this provider." `CredentialInputValidator.getCredentials(RealmModel, UserModel)` did not exist in Keycloak 4.8.3 (it was added much later as a default method returning `Stream.empty()`). By overriding `getCredentials` and using `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage`, the test no longer verifies backwards compatibility with a 4.8.3-style `CredentialInputUpdater`/`CredentialInputValidator` implementation, and masks the `NoSuchElementException` in `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` when `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` returns `Optional.empty()`.

title: getCredential ignores custom UserStorageProvider credentials that only implement getCredentials
body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` only queries `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()` and `user.credentialManager().getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)`. `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` only returns credentials stored in Keycloak's `UserFederatedStorageProvider`, whereas `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...)` queries both local storage and `UserStorageProvider.getCredentials(...)` (in `UserCredentialManager`). Calling `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)` first and falling back to `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` (or vice versa) works here only because `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream` is also called, yet in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials` the returned `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` has no `id` set (`createFromValues` does not set an ID). If all codes are used on a federated/storage credential, `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` calls `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` with a `null` ID (or a storage credential ID that only `removeStoredCredentialById` handles when `id != null`), failing to remove or disable the exhausted recovery codes in user storage.

title: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage is meant to stay compatible with Keycloak 4.8.3 APIs
body: The class-level Javadoc of `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` states: "UserStorage implementation created in Keycloak 4.8.3. It is used for backwards compatibility testing. Future Keycloak versions should work fine without a need to change the code of this provider." Modifying this provider to use newly introduced APIs (`RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`, `getCredentials`, Java 10 `var`) defeats the purpose of this test provider as a 4.8.3 backwards-compatibility fixture.

title: getCredential only checks federated credentials, missing credentials from custom UserStorageProviders
body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` calls `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()` and falls back to `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)`. However, `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` only queries `session.userFederatedStorage().getStoredCredentialsStream(...)` and does NOT invoke `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials(realm, user)` on the user's `UserStorageProvider`. In contrast, `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream` (on `UserCredentialManager`) already combines local DB storage, federated storage, and `UserStorageProvider` credentials (when the provider implements `getCredentials` or when dummy representations are generated). Furthermore, if a `UserStorageProvider` does not override `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials(...)`, `UserCredentialManager` creates a dummy `CredentialModel` (via `CredentialHelper.createUserStorageCredentialRepresentation`) that has null `credentialData`/`secretData`; passing that to `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel(...)` in `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` (line 19) or `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` (line 83) will throw a `RuntimeException` / `NullPointerException` when parsing the JSON data.

title: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage modified with APIs that did not exist in Keycloak 4.8.3
body: The class javadoc explicitly states: "UserStorage implementation created in Keycloak 4.8.3. It is used for backwards compatibility testing. Future Keycloak versions should work fine without a need to change the code of this provider." This change adds `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` and `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials(RealmModel, UserModel)` (lines 46, 231) to `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage`, neither of which existed in Keycloak 4.8.3. Relying on `getCredentials` in this provider also masks what happens with an actual 4.8.3-style `UserStorageProvider` that only implements `supportsCredentialType`, `updateCredential`, `isConfiguredFor`, and `isValid` without overriding the default `getCredentials` method.

title: Paginated/filtered getSubGroupsStream overloads still dereference potentially null modelSupplier.get()
body: `getSubGroupsCount()` was updated to guard against `modelSupplier.get()` returning `null` when the group has been concurrently deleted from the database while still present in cache. However, the three `getSubGroupsStream` overloads right above it (lines 256, 262, and 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` directly without a null check. Under the same concurrent deletion scenario, calling any of those methods on a cached `GroupAdapter` will still throw a `NullPointerException` instead of returning `Stream.empty()`.

title: Background reader thread in createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti is not joined before asserting or finishing the test
body: In `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the background thread started at line 139 is never joined after `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155. As a result, an in-flight `groups(...)` request that fails right as the last group is deleted can add its exception to `caughtExceptions` after `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` has already passed, causing false positives, and the still-running request can also race with subsequent tests or test cleanup on `managedRealm`. Store the `Thread` reference and `join()` it before asserting on `caughtExceptions`.

title: Reader thread in createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti is not joined before asserting or finishing the test
body: In `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti()`, the background thread started on line 139 is never joined after `deletedAll.set(true)` on line 155. If the background thread is still executing an in-flight `groups(...)` request when the main thread reaches `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` on line 157, any exception thrown by that final request will be added to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion has already passed. In addition, the still-running thread can continue executing into subsequent tests or realm cleanup. Store the `Thread` reference and call `thread.join()` after `deletedAll.set(true)` and before asserting on `caughtExceptions`.

title: Paginated getSubGroupsStream overloads still dereference null modelSupplier.get() on concurrent deletion
body: `getSubGroupsCount()` was updated on lines 274-275 to guard against `modelSupplier.get()` returning `null` when the underlying group has been concurrently removed from the database, but the three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads on lines 256, 262, and 268 still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` directly without a null check. If a cached group is concurrently deleted while any of these methods is called, `modelSupplier.get()` returns `null` and a `NullPointerException` is thrown.

title: Background reader thread in `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` is not joined before asserting or finishing the test
body: In `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, a background thread is started on line 139–149 that continuously calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` until `deletedAll` is set to `true`. On line 155 `deletedAll.set(true)` is called and line 157 immediately asserts `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` without calling `join()` on the thread. Because the thread may still be mid-request when the assertion runs: (1) an exception thrown by an in-flight `groups()` call after line 157 will be missed by the assertion, and (2) the thread can still be executing against `managedRealm` while subsequent tests or test-framework cleanup run. Store the `Thread` reference and `join()` it before asserting on `caughtExceptions`.

title: Other `modelSupplier.get()` callers in `GroupAdapter` still dereference a potentially null `GroupModel`
body: `getSubGroupsCount()` (lines 274–275) was updated to guard against `modelSupplier.get()` returning `null` when a cached group has been concurrently removed from persistence. However, the three `getSubGroupsStream` overloads right above it (lines 256, 262, and 268) still do `return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` without a null check, so they will still throw a `NullPointerException` under the same concurrent-deletion condition (returning `Stream.empty()` when `model == null` would avoid the NPE).

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator fails with TypeError when ordering by a datetime field
body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` passes `order_by="-datetime"` to `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, where `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `datetime.datetime` instance. Unlike `DateTimePaginator`, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` passes `getattr(item, self.key)` directly to `math.floor` / `math.ceil`, which raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` as soon as any audit log row is processed. In addition, `value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric `cursor.value` instead of converting it back to a `datetime`, which causes `build_queryset` to compare a `datetime` column against an integer on subsequent pages. `OptimizedCursorPaginator` should either subclass `DateTimePaginator` or handle `datetime` values when converting to and from cursor keys.

title: Negative cursor offsets raise ValueError when slicing a Django QuerySet
body: Both `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (when `enable_advanced_features` is enabled and `cursor.offset < 0`, or when `cursor.is_prev` is True) and `BasePaginator.get_result` (line 182, when `cursor.is_prev` is True and `offset < 0`) pass a negative `start_offset` (and potentially a negative `stop`) directly to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly forbids negative slice bounds and raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`, resulting in an unhandled 500 error whenever a client supplies a cursor with a negative offset.

title: Potential AttributeError when organization_context.member is None
body: `organization_context.member` can be `None` for requests authenticated via organization-level API tokens or non-member contexts when `request.user.is_superuser` is `False`. Accessing `organization_context.member.has_global_access` without first checking that `organization_context.member` is not `None` will raise an `AttributeError`.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime sort field in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint
body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get` paginates `AuditLogEntry` with `order_by="-datetime"` using `OptimizedCursorPaginator`. Unlike `DateTimePaginator`, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` passes `getattr(item, self.key)` directly to `math.floor` / `math.ceil`, which raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` whenever any audit log rows are returned. Additionally, `value_from_cursor` returns the numeric cursor value without converting it back to a `datetime`, breaking subsequent cursor queries against the `datetime` column.

title: Negative slice bounds on Django QuerySet raise ValueError
body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (and `BasePaginator.get_result` at line 184 when `cursor.is_prev` is True) passes a negative `start_offset` (and potentially negative `stop`) into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` when `cursor.offset < 0`. title: `self.paginate` called with unsupported `enable_advanced_features` keyword argument

title: Negative slice bounds on Django `QuerySet` raise `ValueError`
