body: On line 71, `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated whenever `request.user.is_superuser` is `False`. For requests authenticated via organization-level tokens or integrations (where `request.user` is an `AnonymousUser` and `organization_context.member` is `None`), accessing `.has_global_access` will raise an `AttributeError`.

title: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint passes unsupported keyword argument to Endpoint.paginate and uses non-datetime paginator on datetime field
body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get()` calls `self.paginate(..., paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator, order_by="-datetime", enable_advanced_features=True)`. First, `Endpoint.paginate()` in Sentry does not accept `enable_advanced_features` unless it forwards `**kwargs` to `paginator_cls` (and even if it does, `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is a `Paginator`-style class rather than `DateTimePaginator`). In `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, `get_item_key` calls `math.floor(getattr(item, self.key))` on `AuditLogEntry.datetime` (a `datetime` object), which raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`, and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric cursor value instead of converting it to a `datetime` for the SQL comparison on the `datetime` column. Finally, these audit log / paginator changes are completely unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (spans buffer insertion).

title: Allowing negative offsets in BasePaginator and OptimizedCursorPaginator causes ValueError on Django QuerySet slicing
body: In `BasePaginator.get_result` (line 182) and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (lines 880-886), negative `cursor.offset` values are passed directly into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` when `cursor.is_prev` is true or `enable_advanced_features` is enabled. Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly forbids negative slice indices and raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` Furthermore, if `start_offset` is negative and `stop` (`start_offset + limit + extra`) is positive, a client supplying a crafted cursor string like `0:-10:1` will trigger an unhandled 500 error (`ValueError`) on any endpoint using `BasePaginator` or `OptimizedCursorPaginator`.

title: Unrelated audit log pagination changes break on datetime ordering and unknown `paginate` argument
body:
`OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get` appears to contain unrelated changes for `OptimizedCursorPaginator` that will fail at runtime when `optimized_pagination=true` is passed by a superuser or global-access member:

1. `self.paginate(...)` does not accept an `enable_advanced_features` keyword argument (paginator constructor kwargs are not forwarded as arbitrary kwargs by `Endpoint.paginate`), causing a `TypeError`.
2. `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` orders by `-datetime` (`DateTimeField`), but `OptimizedCursorPaginator` implements `Paginator`'s numeric `get_item_key` (`math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)`) and `value_from_cursor` instead of `DateTimePaginator`'s timestamp conversion, which raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` when serializing cursors.

title: Allowing negative cursor offsets in QuerySet slicing raises `ValueError`
body: Both `BasePaginator.get_result` (when `cursor.is_prev` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`) and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (lines 877-886) pass a negative `start_offset` directly into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django `QuerySet` slicing does not support negative indices and immediately raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`, resulting in an unhandled 500 error whenever a client supplies a cursor string with a negative offset (e.g. `cursor=0:-5:1`).

title: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get` passes an unsupported kwarg to `self.paginate` and uses a non-datetime paginator on `-datetime`
body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get` calls `self.paginate(..., paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator, order_by="-datetime", ..., enable_advanced_features=True)`. First, `Endpoint.paginate` does not accept `enable_advanced_features` and does not forward `**kwargs` to `paginator_cls`, so any request with `optimized_pagination=true` from a superuser or global-access member will raise `TypeError: paginate() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_advanced_features'`. Second, `OptimizedCursorPaginator` (lines 838-843 of `paginator.py`) implements `get_item_key` using `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `getattr(item, self.key)` and `value_from_cursor` by returning the raw numeric cursor value, rather than converting `datetime` objects to/from timestamps like `DateTimePaginator` does; ordering by `-datetime` will therefore fail with `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` when building cursors (and pass a numeric cursor value against a `datetime` column on subsequent requests). Finally, these audit-log and paginator changes are completely unrelated to the PR's stated purpose of optimizing spans buffer insertion.

title: Allowing negative cursor offsets in `BasePaginator` and `OptimizedCursorPaginator` causes `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported` in Django QuerySets
body: In `BasePaginator.get_result` (line 182) and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (lines 877-886), negative `cursor.offset` values are passed directly as the slice start to `queryset[start_offset:stop]` (when `cursor.is_prev` is True in `BasePaginator`, or when `enable_advanced_features` is True in `OptimizedCursorPaginator`). Django `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly forbids negative slice indices and raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` (or `AssertionError` in older Django versions). In addition, if `start_offset` is negative enough that `stop = start_offset + limit + extra` is also negative or less than `start_offset`, slicing fails before reaching the database. Because `Cursor.from_string` parses user-supplied cursor strings and allows negative integers for `offset`, any client supplying a cursor like `0:-1:1` will trigger an unhandled 500 error on endpoints using `BasePaginator` subclasses.

title: Changing `span-buf:s:*` from Redis sets to sorted sets without migrating or namespacing keys will cause `WRONGTYPE` errors on deploy
body: `process_spans` now writes to `span-buf:s:{project_and_trace}:{parent_span_id}` using `ZADD` (line 197), `add-buffer.lua` uses `ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE`/`ZPOPMIN`, and `_load_segment_data` reads with `ZSCAN` (line 434), whereas previously these same `span-buf:s:*` keys were Redis `SET`s accessed with `SADD`/`SCARD`/`SUNIONSTORE`/`SSCAN` (with a 1-hour TTL). During a rolling deploy, existing `span-buf:s:*` keys in Redis are still of type `set`, so executing `ZADD`, `ZCARD`, `ZUNIONSTORE`, or `ZSCAN` against them will fail with `redis.exceptions.ResponseError: WRONGTYPE Operation against a key holding the wrong kind of value`, crashing consumer batches until old keys expire or are flushed.

title: Accidental git submodule `sentry-repo` committed to the repository root
body: The commit adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink/subproject pointing to commit `a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This looks like a nested checkout of the repository that was staged by mistake and will break `git submodule` commands for anyone cloning the repo.

title: Shared cache key uses Python's randomized `hash()` and caches stale allowlist state across processes
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` build the shared-cache key with `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. In Python 3, `hash()` is salted per process (`PYTHONHASHSEED`) and only affects tuples when they contain hashed elements or across interpreter restarts/hash-seed differences; more importantly, `hash()` can collide across different project-id tuples, causing an organization's query over an un-allowlisted project set to reuse a cached `True` from a different project set. Furthermore, `sentry.options.get(...)` already has an in-memory TTL cache backed by `default_store`, and nothing in the codebase calls `invalidate_upsampling_cache` when the option `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` is updated, so this extra cache layer both risks cross-project collisions and serves stale results in tests and production (for example, in `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest`, if two tests in the same process used the same `(org.id, project_ids)` pair with different mocked option values, the second test would read the first test's cached result).

title: Upsampling check uses outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset` and ignores the rewritten `query`
body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` is called with the outer `dataset` and `request` rather than the `scoped_dataset` and `query` passed into `_get_event_stats`. When `get_event_stats_factory` splits a dashboard widget query (lines 362-452), it calls `_get_event_stats` with `scoped_dataset=discover` and a modified `query` (e.g. `f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` or `f"({query}) AND event.type:transaction"`), while the outer `dataset` is `metrics_enhanced_performance` or `metrics_performance`. Because `dataset` is not `errors` or `discover`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` always returns `False` for those split queries; conversely, if `request.GET["query"]` contained `event.type:error` and `_get_event_stats` was called for the transactions-only split query, checking `request` instead of `query` would wrongly treat the transaction query as an error query.

title: Unrelated change to `topEvents <= 0` error message breaks existing endpoint tests/contract
body: Line 124 changes the 400 error detail from `"If topEvents needs to be at least 1"` to `"topEvents needs to be at least 1"`. While the original phrasing had a typo, this change is unrelated to error upsampling and alters the response body expected by existing callers/tests for `OrganizationEventsStatsEndpoint`.

title: `upsampled_count` sums `sample_weight` without handling `0` or NULL/default weights for non-sampled events
body: `upsampled_count` is defined as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with `private=False` (the default on `SnQLFunction`). For events in allowlisted projects that were ingested before client error sampling was enabled or from SDKs that do not send a sample rate, `sample_weight` in Snuba can be `0` or unset, causing `sum(sample_weight)` to count those events as `0` instead of `1` (e.g. `sum(if(greater(sample_weight, 1), sample_weight, 1))` or `coalesce`). Additionally, omitting `private=True` exposes `upsampled_count()` as a user-queryable function on the discover dataset for any organization, bypassing the project allowlist check.

title: Accidental git submodule `sentry-repo` committed at repository root
body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink/submodule entry (`Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`) without a corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This will cause `git submodule` commands and checkouts with `--recurse-submodules` to fail. Remove the `sentry-repo` entry from the commit.

title: Upsampling cache key uses non-deterministic `hash()` and caches across test cases
body: In `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (line 27) and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (line 73), the shared cache key is constructed with Python's built-in `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Because `PYTHONHASHSEED` is randomized per process by default, different worker processes will compute different cache keys for the same `(organization_id, project_ids)`, so `invalidate_upsampling_cache` called in one worker will fail to invalidate entries written by other workers, and different project ID tuples can collide under a 64-bit hash. In addition, caching this in `sentry.utils.cache` (when `sentry.options` already caches option values in memory/Redis) causes stale cache hits in tests when `options.get` is mocked across requests for the same projects. Either rely on `sentry.options`'s built-in caching directly, or use a deterministic representation (e.g. a comma-joined sorted list or SHA-256 digest) for the cache key.

title: `_get_event_stats` passes outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset` to upsampling check
body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` is called with the outer `dataset` variable rather than the `scoped_dataset` parameter or `query` argument. When `get_event_stats_factory` splits a dashboard widget query (lines 362-452), it invokes `_get_event_stats` with `scoped_dataset=discover` and a modified `query` (such as `f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` or `f"({query}) AND event.type:transaction"`), while the outer `dataset` is `metrics_enhanced_performance` or `metrics_performance`. Because `dataset` is not `errors` or `discover`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` always returns `False` for those split queries even when querying error events on `discover`. Pass `scoped_dataset` (and check the effective `query` string) instead of the outer `dataset`.

title: `upsampled_count` sums `sample_weight` without handling NULL/0 values for unsampled events
body: `upsampled_count` is defined as `Function("toInt64", [Function("sum", [Column("sample_weight")])], alias)`. In Snuba's errors/discover schema, events ingested without client error sampling (or historical events ingested before `sample_weight` was populated) have `sample_weight` as `NULL` or `0` rather than `1.0`. Summing `sample_weight` directly means unsampled events contribute `0` to the count instead of `1` (e.g., a bucket containing only unsampled events will report a count of `0`). Use `ifNull(if(greater(sample_weight, 0), sample_weight, 1), 1)` (or `greatest(sample_weight, 1)`) inside the sum so each unsampled event still counts as 1.

title: Unrelated change to `topEvents <= 0` error message breaks existing endpoint contract/tests
body: Line 124 changes the 400 error message for `topEvents <= 0` from `"If topEvents needs to be at least 1"` to `"topEvents needs to be at least 1"`. This is unrelated to error upsampling and changes the response payload asserted by existing `OrganizationEventsStatsEndpoint` tests.

title: Accidental git submodule `sentry-repo` committed at repository root
body: A git submodule entry `sentry-repo` pointing to commit `a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` was added at the root of the repository without a corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This will cause `git submodule` commands and tooling that inspects the tree to fail or behave unexpectedly, and should be removed before merging.

title: Cache key uses non-deterministic `hash()` and redundant cache layer breaks tests and cross-worker invalidation
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` build a shared cache key using Python's built-in `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Because `PYTHONHASHSEED` randomizes `hash()` across processes (and even for tuple of ints, `hash()` is not a stable cache key primitive across Python versions/architectures and can collide), `invalidate_upsampling_cache` called from one worker is not guaranteed to match keys written by another. In addition, `sentry.options.get` already caches option values in memory and in `default_store.cache`, so this extra 60-second cache in `django.core.cache` is redundant and causes stale results in tests (and production) whenever the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes within 60 seconds for the same `(org_id, project_ids)` pair—which is actually happens in `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest` if the cache is not flushed between test methods.

title: Upsampling check passes outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset` and ignores `query` parameter
body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` is called with the outer `dataset` rather than `scoped_dataset`, and `_is_error_focused_query` inspects `request.GET.get("query")` instead of the `query` argument passed to `_get_event_stats`. When dashboard widget splitting runs in `get_event_stats_factory`, `_get_event_stats` is invoked with `scoped_dataset=discover` and modified queries such as `f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` or `f"({query}) AND event.type:transaction"` while the outer `dataset` is `metrics_enhanced_performance` (or `metrics_performance`). Because `dataset` is not `discover` or `errors`, upsampling will never be applied to split error widget queries, or if `request.GET["query"]` contained `event.type:error`, it would also be evaluated against the wrong query string when checking transaction-only splits.

title: `upsampled_count` does not handle NULL/0 `sample_weight` and should be marked `private=True`
body: In `DiscoverDatasetConfig.function_converter`, `upsampled_count` is defined as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with `default_result_type="number"` and without `private=True`. For events in allowlisted projects that were ingested before client error sampling was enabled or from SDKs that did not set `sample_weight`, `sample_weight` can be `NULL` or `0` (unlike `ifNull(nullIf(sample_weight, 0), 1)`), causing those events to contribute `0` to the sum instead of `1` and undercounting real errors. Furthermore, because `private=True` is omitted, `upsampled_count()` is exposed as a public Discover query function to all users and organizations, and its `default_result_type` is `"number"` instead of `"integer"` (unlike `count()`, which returns `"integer"`).

title: Mutual exclusion check between `age` and `timestamp` ignores `0`
body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` use truthiness checks (`if self.initial_data.get("age"):` and `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"):`) instead of checking for key presence or `is not None`. Because `0` is a valid integer value for both `age` (a report generated 0ms ago) and `timestamp` (`min_value=0`), a payload containing `{"age": 0, "timestamp": 1640995200000}` (or vice versa) will bypass the mutual-exclusion validation and be accepted with both fields present.

title: `fetch_error_details` pairs `error_ids` with `events.values()` instead of matching by node id
body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by `node_id` whose keys and ordering are not guaranteed to align 1-to-1 with `error_ids` (for example, implementations that omit missing keys or return keys in arbitrary order). Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` can therefore associate an `event_id` with the wrong event payload or silently drop tail items. Look up each `node_id` in `events` (e.g. `for event_id, node_id in zip(error_ids, node_ids): data = events.get(node_id)`).

title: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` are only filtered out when a search query is entered
body: In `Attributes`, `if (!searchQuery.trim()) { return sorted; }` returns the unfiltered attribute list before the `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` check on line 67 runs. As a result, `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are displayed whenever the search box is empty and only hidden once the user types a search query.

title: Mutual exclusion check between `age` and `timestamp` ignores `0`
body: `BrowserReportSerializer.validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` check `if self.initial_data.get("age"):` and `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"):` using truthiness rather than `is not None`. Because `0` is a valid non-negative integer for both `age` (a report generated 0ms ago) and `timestamp` (`min_value=0`), a payload containing both fields where one of them is `0` (e.g. `{"age": 0, "timestamp": 1640995200000}`) will bypass the mutual-exclusion validation instead of raising a `ValidationError`. Also, a report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` is accepted even though both specs require one of the two.

title: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` can pair event IDs with the wrong nodestore data
body: `fetch_error_details` calls `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then iterates `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by `node_id` whose key order and completeness are not guaranteed to match `node_ids` (for example, some backends omit missing keys or return results in arbitrary order). Pairing `error_ids` positionally with `events.values()` can associate an `event_id` with another event's payload or silently drop events. Iterate over `zip(error_ids, node_ids)` and look up `events.get(node_id)` instead.

title: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` are only filtered out when a search query is entered
body: In `Attributes`, `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` directly when `!searchQuery.trim()` (lines 61-63), and only applies `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` inside the search filter branch (lines 65-69). As a result, `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are still displayed in the attributes tree whenever the search bar is empty.

title: Mutual exclusion check between `age` and `timestamp` ignores `0`
body: In `BrowserReportSerializer`, `validate_timestamp` checks `if self.initial_data.get("age"):` and `validate_age` checks `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"):`. Because `0` is falsy in Python, a report containing `"age": 0` alongside a valid `timestamp` (or `"timestamp": 0` alongside a valid `age`, where `0` is explicitly allowed by `min_value=0`) will bypass both validation checks instead of raising a `ValidationError`. These checks should test `self.initial_data.get("age") is not None` and `self.initial_data.get("timestamp") is not None`.

title: `fetch_error_details` pairs `error_ids` with `events.values()` by position instead of by node_id
body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids = [Event.generate_node_id(project_id, event_id=id) for id in error_ids]`, calls `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, and then iterates `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `nodestore.get_multi` returns a dict mapping `node_id -> data` whose keys are neither guaranteed to be in `node_ids` order nor guaranteed to include missing keys in all backends. Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` can associate an `event_id` with the wrong event payload or silently drop/shift entries when some events are missing from nodestore. Iterate over `zip(error_ids, node_ids)` and look up `events.get(node_id)` instead.

title: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` are only filtered out when a search query is entered
body: In `Attributes`, `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` directly when `!searchQuery.trim()` (lines 61-63), and only applies `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` inside the `filter` call when `searchQuery` is non-empty (lines 65-69). As a result, `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are visible in the default (unsearched) view and only disappear once the user types into the search box. The `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` filter should be applied before checking `searchQuery.trim()`.

title: `Integration.objects.get` in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` is not scoped to `provider='github'`
body: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` (line 478) and `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` (lines 494-496) look up `Integration` rows without filtering by `provider=GitHubIntegrationProvider.key`. title: Direct access to `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises `KeyError` when `sender` is absent

However, `GitHubIntegrationProvider.build_integration` only sets `metadata["sender"]` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy (lines 376-377), so an existing `Integration` created through the pipeline (for example, one whose `OrganizationIntegration` was later deleted and is now being reinstalled, as in `test_github_installed_on_another_org`) will not have `"sender"` in `integration.metadata`. title: `test_installation_not_found` fails on OAuth state mismatch instead of testing a 404 installation lookup

title: `queued` default timestamp is evaluated once at import time instead of per instance

title: Passing `assignment_source` to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound` breaks integrations that do not accept `**kwargs`

title: `AssignmentSource.queued` default value is evaluated once at import time

title: `assignment_source` added to `sync_status_outbound` instead of `sync_assignee_outbound`, and passed to implementations that may not accept it

title: `assignment_source` added to `sync_status_outbound` instead of `sync_assignee_outbound`, and passed to subclass implementations
body: `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_status_outbound` was updated with `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`, even though status sync never passes `assignment_source`, while `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound` was not updated. title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler does not implement required abstract methods of StatefulDetectorHandler
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` is changed to inherit from `StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]` with an empty `pass` body, removing its previous `evaluate` implementation. title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is an uninstantiable abstract class
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]` with a `pass` body, without implementing any of `StatefulDetectorHandler`'s abstract methods (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler does not implement abstract methods of StatefulDetectorHandler

title: `get_monitor_environment_context` returns original config instead of modified `config` copy
body: In `get_monitor_environment_context`, lines 160-162 copy `monitor_environment.monitor.config` into a local `config` dict and replace `config["schedule_type"]` with its human-readable display value (`get_schedule_type_display()`), but line 168 returns `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of `"config": config`. As a result, the `config` copy is unused and the raw integer `schedule_type` is sent in the event's monitor context instead of the display string.

title: Flusher processes are not terminated when join timeout expires
body: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the loop over `self.processes` checks `if remaining_time <= 0: break` before calling `process.terminate()`. If `self.next_step.join(timeout)` or waiting on the first flusher process consumes the entire `timeout`, the loop breaks early and skips calling `process.terminate()` on all remaining alive flusher processes. Those worker processes are left running in the background (for example across consumer partition rebalances), continuing to flush Redis shards and produce duplicate segments alongside newly spawned flusher processes.

title: ZeroDivisionError when consumer is initialized with no assigned partitions
body: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, if `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty (which happens when a Kafka consumer instance is assigned 0 partitions), `self.num_processes` evaluates to `0`, and `process_index = i % self.num_processes` or a passed `max_processes=0` with non-empty shards raises `ZeroDivisionError: integer modulo by zero`. Even when `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty so the loop does not execute, passing `--flusher-processes 0` with non-empty shards will crash with `ZeroDivisionError` because `max_processes or len(...)` falls back only on falsy values while negative values are not guarded.

title: Inconsistent metric tag name `shards` vs `shard` on `wait_produce` timer
body: Lines 185 and 195 tag metrics with `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`, whereas line 199 tags `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` with `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` (plural). This makes the tag key inconsistent across the flusher metrics.

title: Flusher processes are not terminated in `join()` when timeout expires
body: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the loop over `self.processes` checks `if remaining_time <= 0: break` before calling `process.terminate()`. If `self.next_step.join(timeout)` or waiting for an earlier flusher process consumes the entire timeout budget, the loop breaks out early and leaves all remaining flusher processes running instead of terminating them. Instead of breaking out of the loop, it should skip the `while process.is_alive()` wait and still call `process.terminate()` on each remaining alive process.

title: Inconsistent metric tag name `shards` vs `shard` in `SpanFlusher.main`
body: In `SpanFlusher.main`, `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` (line 185) and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` (line 195) use `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`, whereas `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` (line 199) uses `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` (plural). This makes the tag key inconsistent across flusher metrics.

title: `time.sleep(0.1)` in `test_basic` is a no-op because `time.sleep` is monkeypatched
body: Line 15 monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so the added `time.sleep(0.1)` on line 62 (intended to give flusher threads time to process after the drift change) does nothing and returns immediately, which can make the test flaky.

title: Expired join timeout leaves remaining flusher processes un-terminated
body: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the loop over `self.processes.items()` checks `remaining_time = deadline - time.time()` and executes `break` if `remaining_time <= 0` before calling `process.terminate()`. When a timeout is passed to `join(timeout)`, `self.next_step.join(timeout)` or waiting on the first process in the loop can consume the entire timeout budget. The `break` then exits the loop immediately, leaving all subsequent child processes in `self.processes` running instead of terminating them. Instead of breaking out of the loop when the deadline has passed, the loop should skip waiting and still call `process.terminate()` on every remaining `multiprocessing.Process`.

title: Zeroassigned shards causes ZeroDivisionError when max_processes is set
body: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` evaluates to `0` when `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty and `max_processes` is `None` (or `0`), making `self.num_processes = 0`. Even if `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` is 0, the loop doesn't run, which is fine; however, if `max_processes` is passed as `<= 0` (e.g. `--flusher-processes 0`) while `buffer.assigned_shards` is non-empty, `self.num_processes` becomes `0` (or negative) and `i % self.num_processes` on line 65 raises `ZeroDivisionError` (or `KeyError` for negative modulo). `max_processes` / `--flusher-processes` should be validated to be at least 1.

title: Inconsistent metric tag name `shards` vs `shard`
body: Lines 185 and 195 emit `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` with `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`, whereas line 199 emits `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` with `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` (plural). Using two different tag keys (`shard` vs `shards`) for the same `shard_tag` value across sibling flusher metrics makes dashboarding and grouping by shard inconsistent.

title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched at the start of the test
body: Line 15 of `test_basic` patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so the added `time.sleep(0.1)` on line 62 (with comment `# Give flusher threads time to process after drift change`) does not actually sleep at all and provides no synchronization.

title: Kafka consumer commit is invoked from a background thread instead of Arroyo's main loop
body: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` spawns a background thread (`self.commit_thread`) that periodically calls `self.commit_function(committable)`, which invokes Arroyo's `Commit` callback. In Arroyo, `KafkaConsumer` (wrapping `confluent_kafka.Consumer`) is not thread-safe and expects `commit` to be called on the main `StreamProcessor` thread (typically inside `poll()` or `submit()`). Calling `commit` from a separate thread races with `consumer.poll()` / rebalance callbacks in `StreamProcessor` and can also commit offsets after partition revocation.

title: `FixedQueuePool` is instantiated on the factory and destroyed on the first partition rebalance
body: `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__` creates a single `self.queue_pool = FixedQueuePool(...)`, and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` / `terminate()` calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`. In Arroyo, `create_with_partitions` is called every time partitions are assigned, and `close()`/`terminate()` is called on the active strategy whenever partitions are revoked or rebalanced. After the first rebalance, `self.queue_pool` has all of its queues and worker threads permanently shut down (and `offset_tracker` retains stale offsets from the old assignment), so subsequent strategies created by `create_with_partitions` will raise `queue.ShutDown` on `submit()` and stop processing any messages.

title: Unbounded work queues provide no backpressure and can exhaust memory
body: `FixedQueuePool` creates each `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize` (unbounded), and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()` never raises `MessageRejected` or blocks. Because `StreamProcessor` polls Kafka as fast as `submit()` returns, the consumer will read messages into memory at Kafka network speed regardless of how slowly `OrderedQueueWorker` threads process them (contrary to the docstring claim of "Natural backpressure when queues fill up"). Under load or a slow downstream dependency, this will buffer an unbounded number of messages in memory until the process OOMs, and during `close()`/`join()` the workers cannot drain before `join_timeout`.

title: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` sets `worker.shutdown = True` before draining queues, dropping queued items
body: In `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()`, `worker.shutdown = True` is set on every worker before `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` is called. Because `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` loops on `while not self.shutdown:`, any worker that finishes its current item (or wakes up from `q.shutdown`) immediately exits the `while` loop without draining the remaining items in `work_queue`, and without calling `join()`'s final offset commit. Consequently, on graceful shutdown (`close()`/`join()`), all still-queued messages are abandoned and completed offsets after the last 1-second tick are never committed.

title: `OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets` gets permanently stuck if a partition has non-contiguous offsets
body: `get_committable_offsets()` iterates `for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1):` and breaks as soon as an integer is not in `all_offsets`. In Kafka, offsets within a partition are not guaranteed to be strictly consecutive integers (for example, compacted topics, transactional markers/control batches, or filtered messages that were not submitted). Furthermore, when a consumer starts up or rebalances and receives its first message at offset `N`, `last_committed` is `-1` and `min_offset` is `N`, which works for the first batch; however, if any single offset number is missing between two messages (or if a partition is reassigned at a higher offset after `last_committed` was set), `offset in all_offsets` is `False`, the loop breaks immediately, `highest_committable` never advances, `all_offsets` grows without bound, and no further offsets are ever committed for that partition.

title: Calling `commit` from a background thread violates Arroyo/confluent-kafka thread safety
body: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` spawns a background `commit_thread` that calls `self.commit_function(committable)`, which invokes the Arroyo `Commit` callback passed into `create_with_partitions`. In Arroyo's `StreamProcessor`, that callback calls `self.__consumer.stage_positions(...)` and `self.__consumer.commit(...)` on the underlying `KafkaConsumer` (and `confluent_kafka.Consumer`), while the main processor thread is concurrently calling `poll()` / `stage_positions()` on the same consumer and unsynchronized internal dicts (`__PartitionState.__staged_offsets`). Arroyo strategies are expected to invoke `commit` from `poll()`, `submit()`, or `join()` on the main consumer thread. Calling `commit` from a separate thread introduces data races on Arroyo's offset state and concurrent calls into the librdkafka consumer.

title: `close()` and `terminate()` shut down the shared `FixedQueuePool`, breaking partition rebalances
body: `ResultsStrategyFactory` creates a single `self.queue_pool` in `__init__` and reuses it across every `create_with_partitions` call. In Arroyo, whenever partitions are revoked or rebalanced, the active strategy has `close()`/`join()` (or `terminate()`) called on it, and `create_with_partitions` is then called again to build a new strategy instance. Because `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` and `terminate()` call `self.queue_pool.shutdown()` (which permanently shuts down all queues and stops all worker threads), the first rebalance will leave `self.queue_pool` dead: subsequent `submit()` calls on the newly created strategy will raise `queue.ShutDown` (caught and immediately marked completed in `submit()`), silently dropping all messages and committing their offsets without processing.

title: Work queues are unbounded and `submit()` never raises `MessageRejected`, allowing unbounded memory growth
body: In `FixedQueuePool.__init__`, each `queue.Queue()` is created with `maxsize=0` (unbounded), and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` never raises Arroyo's `MessageRejected`. Although the class docstring claims "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", the main consumer loop will read from Kafka at full speed and buffer an arbitrary number of `WorkItem` objects (each retaining the raw `Message` and decoded payload) in memory if any worker falls behind, risking OOM kills and also failing to flush remaining queued items on shutdown because `worker.shutdown = True` causes workers to exit their loop on the next iteration instead of draining the queue.

title: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` sets `worker.shutdown = True` before draining, dropping queued items and skipping final commit
body: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` sets `worker.shutdown = True` on all workers and then calls `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`. Because `OrderedQueueWorker.run` checks `while not self.shutdown:`, any worker that finishes its current item sees `self.shutdown == True` and exits immediately instead of draining the remaining items in `work_queue` (which `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` is meant to allow). Furthermore, `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` stops `commit_thread` before calling `queue_pool.shutdown()` and never performs a final commit afterwards, so offsets for items completed during shutdown are never committed.

title: Committing offsets from a background thread violates Kafka consumer thread-safety and can commit revoked partitions
body: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` spawns a background thread (`self.commit_thread`) that periodically calls `self.commit_function(committable)`, which invokes Arroyo's `commit` callback on the underlying `KafkaConsumer`. Arroyo's `StreamProcessor` and `KafkaConsumer` are single-threaded and expect `commit` to be called only from `submit()`, `poll()`, or `join()` on the main consumer thread. Calling `commit` from a separate thread causes concurrent access to `KafkaConsumer` state (such as offset staging and `confluent_kafka` consumer calls) alongside `StreamProcessor._run_once()`. Furthermore, during a rebalance, `StreamProcessor` calls `strategy.close()`/`join()` and then revokes partitions; because `close()` stops `commit_thread` *before* draining `queue_pool` and does not perform a final commit, offsets completed while draining aren't committed, or if `commit_thread` is still running it can call `commit` for partitions after they have been revoked. Offset commits should be performed in `poll()` and `join()` on the strategy's caller thread rather than a background thread.

title: Sharing `FixedQueuePool` on the strategy factory breaks consumer rebalances
body: `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__` creates a single `FixedQueuePool` instance (`self.queue_pool`) and passes it into `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` in `create_with_partitions()`. When a Kafka consumer group rebalance occurs, Arroyo closes the active strategy—which calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`—and then calls `factory.create_with_partitions()` again for the new assignment. Because `shutdown()` permanently stops all `OrderedQueueWorker` threads and shuts down all `queue.Queue` instances (raising `queue.ShutDown` on subsequent `put()` calls), and because `OffsetTracker` retains stale offset history from the previous assignment (`last_committed`, `all_offsets`, `outstanding`), the consumer will fail to enqueue or process any messages after the first rebalance. A fresh `FixedQueuePool` (or per-strategy worker/tracker state) needs to be created per `create_with_partitions` lifecycle, or `FixedQueuePool` must not be shut down by `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()`/`terminate()` while its `OffsetTracker` is reset for the new partition assignment.

title: Unbounded work queues provide no backpressure and can exhaust memory
body: `FixedQueuePool.__init__` initializes each `work_queue` as an unbounded `queue.Queue()` (`maxsize=0`). Although `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy`'s docstring states "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", `work_queue.put(work_item)` in `FixedQueuePool.submit` will never block or raise `Arroyo`'s `MessageRejected`. The main Kafka consumer thread will continue polling and decoding messages at full speed even if worker threads are slow or blocked on I/O, buffering an unbounded number of `WorkItem` objects (including full decoded payloads and raw Kafka messages) in memory until the process runs out of memory.

title: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` abandons queued items instead of draining them
body: In `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()`, `worker.shutdown = True` is set on every worker before calling `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`. Because `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` checks `while not self.shutdown:`, each worker exits its loop as soon as it finishes the single item it is currently processing, leaving all remaining items sitting in `work_queue` unprocessed (even though `immediate=False` was passed to `q.shutdown()`). In addition, `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` stops `commit_thread` *before* calling `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, so even the in-flight items that finish during `queue_pool.shutdown()` never have their offsets committed.

title: Non-contiguous Kafka offsets (e.g. compacted topics or transactions) permanently stall offset commits
body: `OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets` iterates `for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1):` and breaks as soon as an integer `offset` is not in `all_offsets`. After the first commit sets `last_committed`, `start` becomes `last_committed + 1`. If Kafka ever delivers non-consecutive offsets on a partition—which happens when control records/transactions are present, after log compaction, or if a wrapper strategy filters a message before `submit()`—`last_committed + 1` will never be added to `all_offsets`, and `get_committable_offsets` will never advance commits for that partition again, causing `all_offsets` to grow without bound. Since Kafka delivers messages in offset order per partition, tracking seen offsets in order (or iterating `sorted(all_offsets)` rather than `range(start, max_offset + 1)`) avoids assuming every integer offset exists.

title: `PasswordField` password visibility toggle fails when `type="password"` is passed as a prop
body: In `PasswordField`, `{...props}` is spread on `InputField` after `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}`. When a caller passes `type="password"` explicitly—as `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` does at line 176 (`<PasswordField type="password" ... />`)—the spread `props.type` overwrites the computed `type` attribute, so clicking the show/hide password eye button never switches the input to `type="text"`.

title: Dismissing the modal on the backup codes step leaves parent 2FA state out of sync
body: `handleEnable` (line 135) now transitions to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` instead of calling `onEnable()`, and `onEnable()` is only invoked when the user clicks the footer `Close` button (`backup-codes-close`, line 269). However, `Dialog` still uses `onOpenChange={onOpenChange}` directly. If the user dismisses the dialog at the `DisplayBackupCodes` step via the Esc key, clicking the backdrop, or the dialog header close icon, `onOpenChange` closes the modal without calling `onEnable()` or `resetState()`. Because 2FA has already been enabled on the server by `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/enable`, the parent settings UI remains in the "2FA disabled" state and reopening the modal starts at `DisplayBackupCodes`.

title: Third-party IdP users with 2FA enabled cannot use backup codes to log in
body: In `authorize`, lines 114–129 skip the `IdentityProvider.CAL` and password checks only when `!credentials.totpCode` is false (which is how `/auth/login?totp=...` works for Google/SAML users who have 2FA enabled). They do not check `credentials.backupCode`, and `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` (line 180) renders `ExternalTotpFooter` instead of `TwoFactorFooter` when `totpEmail` is set, hiding the "Lost access" button. As a result, a Google or SAML user with 2FA enabled has no way to use a backup code at login (and even if submitted, `authorize` would reject the request with `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled`).

title: `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on a Promise instead of the switch state
body: `page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()` returns a `Promise<boolean>` (and moreover, a Radix UI `Switch` renders a `<button role="switch" aria-checked="...">` rather than a checkbox input). Passing that Promise to synchronous `expect(...).toBeTruthy()` without `await` always passes because any Promise object is truthy, and the test never closes the new backup codes modal via `backup-codes-close` (so `onEnable` is never called in this test). Use `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch][data-state="checked"]')).toBeVisible()` after closing the backup codes step, as the second test does.

title: Used backup code slots set to null can be matched if backupCode is not a string or via external Totp flow
body: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` lines 113-129, third-party identity provider (Google/SAML) users with 2FA enabled are only exempted from `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` and password checks when `credentials.totpCode` is truthy (`!credentials.totpCode`). When such a user loses access to their authenticator and tries to log in using a `backupCode` (where `credentials.totpCode` is empty), `authorize` throws `ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` at line 114 before reaching the backup code check at line 131. Furthermore, in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` line 180, when `totpEmail` is set (the 2FA step after SSO login), `ExternalTotpFooter` is rendered instead of `TwoFactorFooter`, so the "Lost access" button to enter a backup code is never even shown to SSO users.

title: Unvalidated `req.body.backupCode` allows bypassing 2FA disable check once a backup code has been used
body: When a backup code is used during login (`packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` line 148), the consumed entry in the `backupCodes` array is replaced with `null` (`backupCodes[index] = null`) and re-encrypted. In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, `req.body` is not validated with a schema before use. If a caller sends a JSON body with a truthy non-string `backupCode` or if `req.body.backupCode` is not type-checked, or more importantly if `replaceAll` is called on a non-string it throws, while if someone crafts `backupCodes.indexOf(...)`, note that in `disable.ts` line 61 `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` only produces a string, so `indexOf` won't match `null` directly—however, if `req.body.backupCode` is not a string (e.g. an object/array/boolean), `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` throws an unhandled `TypeError` resulting in a 500 response instead of a 400.

title: Closing the modal on the backup codes step via backdrop/Escape leaves UI out of sync with enabled 2FA
body: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, 2FA is already enabled on the server when `handleEnable` succeeds (line 134), which transitions the modal to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` without calling `onEnable()` yet. `onEnable()` and `resetState()` are only invoked when the user clicks the explicit "Close" button (`data-testid="backup-codes-close"`, line 266). If the user dismisses the dialog via the `X` close button, pressing Escape, or clicking the overlay (which triggers `Dialog`'s `onOpenChange`), `onEnable()` is never called so the parent settings page still shows 2FA as disabled, and `resetState()` is never called so reopening the modal starts on the backup codes step instead of resetting.

title: Passing `type="password"` to `PasswordField` overrides the show/hide password toggle
body: In `packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx` lines 36-39, `PasswordField` sets `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` BEFORE spreading `{...props}` onto `InputField`. In `apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` line 176, `PasswordField` is rendered with `type="password"`, which overwrites the computed `type` prop and makes the eye toggle button unable to reveal the password.

title: `PasswordField` show/hide password toggle fails when `type="password"` is passed
body: In `PasswordField`, `{...props}` is spread on `InputField` at line 39, after `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` at line 36. Any caller that passes `type="password"` (such as `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` at line 176, which was converted from `TextField` to `PasswordField` in this PR) overwrites the internal `type` prop, making the eye-icon toggle button unable to reveal the password. `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` should be placed after `{...props}` (or `type` should be omitted from the spread props).

title: Closing the 2FA modal via overlay or Escape on the backup codes step leaves the parent UI out of sync
body: In `EnableTwoFactorModal`, 2FA is already enabled on the server once `handleEnable` succeeds and transitions to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` (line 135), but `onEnable()` is now only called when clicking the custom `Close` button (line 269). If the user dismisses the dialog at the backup-codes step by clicking the backdrop, pressing Escape, or clicking the dialog's close icon (`onOpenChange`), `onEnable` is never invoked and `resetState()` is never run. The parent settings page therefore keeps the 2FA switch in the unchecked/disabled state even though 2FA is active on the account, and reopening the modal starts on the backup codes step instead of resetting.

title: Third-party IdP users with 2FA enabled cannot use backup codes or lacks "Lost access" option on login
body: In `next-auth-options.ts` lines 113-129, the checks `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode)` and `if (!user.password && user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode)` only bypass password/IdP checks when `credentials.totpCode` is provided, not when `credentials.backupCode` is provided. Additionally, in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` line 180, when `totpEmail` is set (the 2FA flow for Google/SAML users), `ExternalTotpFooter` is rendered instead of `TwoFactorFooter`, which omits the "Lost access" button altogether. As a result, users who authenticate via a third-party identity provider and have 2FA enabled cannot use backup codes to log in.

title: First 2FA E2E test leaves the backup codes modal open and asserts a Promise object is truthy
body: In the first E2E test (`should allow a user to enable 2FA and login using 2FA`), after `fillOtp` on line 44, the modal now transitions to the `DisplayBackupCodes` step rather than closing and calling `onEnable()`. Because the test never clicks `backup-codes-close`, `onEnable()` is never triggered and the switch stays unchecked. As noted in the `FIXME` comment added on line 50, `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` only passes because `locator.isChecked()` returns a `Promise<boolean>` (which is always truthy without `await`), not because the switch is actually checked. This test should close the backup codes step (or use `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()`) so it actually verifies the post-setup state.

title: Unchecked property access on mainHostDestinationCalendar throws TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty or null
body: In `EventManager.create`, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` will set `mainHostDestinationCalendar` to `undefined` whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or an empty array `[]` (which many callers now pass when no destination calendar is configured). Line 119 then evaluates `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without optional chaining (`?.`), which throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` whenever an event's location is Google Meet (`MeetLocationType`) and the user has no destination calendar.

title: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition when setting organization slug
body: Line 151 was changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. This inverts the intended logic: when team billing is enabled, the slug is only supposed to be stored as `requestedSlug` in metadata until payment/verification completes, and when team billing is disabled (self-hosted), `slug` should be set directly on the organization at creation time. With this change, self-hosted instances no longer get `slug` set on created organizations, while billed instances get `slug` set immediately before billing completes.

title: Fallback lookup in updateEvent and deleteEvent compares against falsy externalCalendarId
body: In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback when `externalCalendarId` is falsy is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Because this branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`""`, `null`, or `undefined`), comparing `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` will never match a valid calendar `externalId` and will always evaluate to `undefined`.

title: Google Meet patch call can receive undefined calendarId instead of falling back to "primary"
body: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is now `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, which can be `undefined` (whereas previously `selectedCalendar` defaulted to `"primary"`). While `calendar.events.insert` on line 154 uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, the subsequent `calendar.events.patch` call on line 168 passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly. When `selectedCalendar` is `undefined`, patching the Google Meet hangout link into the event description will fail because `calendarId` is missing.

title: Co-host destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
body: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set (lines 1063-1067). On line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining on `null`, so if the primary organizer has not set a destinationCalendar, all collective co-hosts' `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded and calendar events are not created in their destination calendars.

title: Non-Google calendar services always use the first destinationCalendar instead of matching the current credential
body: In `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` (line 73), `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` (line 128), and `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (line 156), the target calendar is chosen via `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`. In a collective event with multiple hosts, `event.destinationCalendar` contains entries for all hosts, and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` invokes `createEvent` for each host's credential. Using `event.destinationCalendar[0]` means a co-host using Office 365, Lark, or CalDAV will attempt to create the event using the first host's `externalId` (which belongs to a different user/account) instead of finding the `DestinationCalendar` entry matching the credential being used.

title: Unconditional property access on `mainHostDestinationCalendar` throws TypeError when `destinationCalendar` is empty or null
body: In `EventManager.create`, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` as `undefined` whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or `[]`. On line 119, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`). When `evt.location === MeetLocationType` and the user has no destination calendar configured, this throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` instead of falling back to Cal Video.

title: Co-hosts' destination calendars are dropped when main organizer has no destination calendar
body: On lines 1063-1067, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` if neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set. On line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining on a `null` value, so `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded whenever the primary organizer has not set a destinationCalendar, even if collective co-hosts have destination calendars configured. Initializing `destinationCalendar` to `[]` (or assigning `teamDestinationCalendars` when it is null) avoids dropping the co-hosts' calendars.

title: Inverted `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` check sets organization slug before billing completes and breaks self-hosted org creation
body: Line 151 was changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. When team billing is enabled, a new organization is supposed to store the slug only in `metadata.requestedSlug` until payment succeeds, and when team billing is disabled, the `slug` should be set directly on creation. Inverting this condition causes organizations created when billing is disabled to have `slug: null` (and `requestedSlug` unset), and sets the live `slug` immediately before payment when billing is enabled.

title: `calendar.events.patch` uses `undefined` `calendarId` instead of falling back to `"primary"`
body: On line 147, `selectedCalendar` is now `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find(...)?.externalId`, which can be `undefined` (previously it defaulted to `"primary"` at assignment). While `calendar.events.insert` on line 154 was updated to pass `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, the subsequent `calendar.events.patch` call on line 168 still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. If `selectedCalendar` is `undefined`, patching the event description with the Google Meet hangout link will fail because `calendarId` is required by the Google Calendar API.

title: Fallback lookup in `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` searches for a falsy `externalCalendarId`
body: In `updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback branch of `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`""`, `null`, or `undefined`). Searching `event.destinationCalendar` for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` in that branch will never match a valid calendar ID and always evaluates to `undefined`. In `updateEvent`, this passes `calendarId: undefined` to `calendar.events.update`, causing the Google Calendar API call to fail whenever `externalCalendarId` is not stored on the booking reference.

title: Non-Google calendar services always use `destinationCalendar[0]` instead of matching the current credential
body: `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each entry in `event.destinationCalendar`. However, `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` (line 73), `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` (line 128), and `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (line 156) all read `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` instead of finding the destination calendar matching `credentialId`. In a collective event where the second host uses Office 365, Lark, or CalDAV, their service will use the first host's `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` (which may belong to another user or even another integration like Google Calendar), causing event creation for the second host to target the wrong calendar ID or fail.

title: Unchecked property access on `mainHostDestinationCalendar` throws TypeError when `destinationCalendar` is empty or null
body: In `EventManager.create`, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` sets `mainHostDestinationCalendar` to `undefined` whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or an empty array `[]` (which many callers now pass when no destination calendar is configured). Line 119 then evaluates `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`), throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` whenever an event with Google Meet location is created for a user without a destination calendar.

title: Unrelated inversion of `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` check when setting organization slug
body: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, line 151 was changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. Previously, when team billing was enabled, the slug was stored only in `metadata.requestedSlug` (until billing/payment completed) and not set directly on the organization; when team billing was disabled (e.g., self-hosted), the slug was set immediately. This change inverts that logic and appears to be an unintended edit unrelated to `destinationCalendar`.

title: Collective host destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destinationCalendar
body: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set (lines 1063-1067). Immediately afterwards on line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining on `null`, so if the primary organizer has no `destinationCalendar` configured, `teamDestinationCalendars` for all other collective hosts are silently discarded and their calendar events are never created. `evt.destinationCalendar` should be initialized to `[]` (or assigned `teamDestinationCalendars`) so other hosts' destination calendars are preserved.

title: `calendar.events.patch` receives `undefined` `calendarId` instead of falling back to `"primary"`
body: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is now `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, which can be `undefined` (whereas previously `selectedCalendar` defaulted to `"primary"`). While `calendar.events.insert` on line 154 was updated to use `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, the subsequent `calendar.events.patch` call on line 168 (used to attach the Hangout/Meet link to the description) still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. When `selectedCalendar` is `undefined`, the patch request will fail with a missing `calendarId`.

title: Fallback lookup for `selectedCalendar` in `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` is dead code
body: In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback branch when `externalCalendarId` is falsy searches `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Because this branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`""`, `null`, or `undefined`), comparing `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` will never match a valid calendar's `externalId`, so the fallback always evaluates to `undefined`. In `updateEvent`, this leaves `selectedCalendar` as `undefined`, causing `calendar.events.update` to fail when `externalCalendarId` is not stored on the booking reference.

title: Non-Google calendar services always use `destinationCalendar[0]` instead of matching the current host's credential
body: In `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` (line 128), `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` (line 73), and `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (CalDAV, line 156), the target calendar is chosen via `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` rather than finding the entry in `event.destinationCalendar` matching the `credentialId` being used (as `GoogleCalendarService` does). In a collective event where a non-main host uses Lark, Office365, or CalDAV, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` invokes `createEvent` with that host's credential, but the service will attempt to create the event in `destinationCalendar[0]?.externalId` (which belongs to the primary host and possibly a completely different provider), causing event creation to fail with a 404/invalid calendar ID.

title: `updateEvent` called with `undefined` credential when DB lookup fails or app has no slug
body: In `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents` (lines 515-542), if `reference.credentialId` is not in `this.calendarCredentials`, it queries `prisma.credential.findUnique`. If the credential was deleted or `credentialFromDB.app?.slug` is falsy, `credential` remains `undefined`, yet line 542 unconditionally calls `updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId)`. Inside `CalendarManager.updateEvent`, accessing `credential.appName` / `credential.type` will throw a TypeError and abort all other calendar updates in the `try` block. Line 542 should guard with `if (credential)` just as `createAllCalendarEvents` does on line 369.

title: Saving Zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper instead of parsed data corrupts Google Calendar credentials
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` object (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), unlike the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` call which returned the parsed credential object directly. Passing `key` directly to `prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key } })` overwrites the stored credential `key` in the database with `{ success: true, data: { ... } }`. On the next instantiation of `GoogleCalendarService`, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on line 75 will fail because the top-level keys (`access_token`, `refresh_token`, etc.) are now nested under `data`, permanently breaking the user's Google Calendar integration after its first token refresh.

title: Invalid computed property keys in `minimumTokenResponseSchema` do not match dynamic expiry properties
body: In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` evaluate `toString()` on Zod schema instances, which produces `"[object Object]"`. This defines a schema that requires a literal `"[object Object]"` property with a numeric value and strips all other properties beyond `access_token` (such as `expiry_date` or `expires_in`). When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` will always fail on normal token responses and throw `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"`.

title: `prisma` is not imported and refreshed Salesforce access token is not used by the connection
body: In `SalesforceCalendarService.getClient`: (1) `prisma.credential.update` is called on line 96, but `@calcom/prisma` is never imported in this file, causing a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime whenever `SalesforceCalendarService` is instantiated. (2) Even before that, the refresh request is not wrapped in `refreshOAuthTokens`, and on line 106 the `jsforce.Connection` is initialized with the old `credentialKey.access_token` instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

title: `credentialId` is passed instead of `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`
body: `refreshAccessToken` passes `credentialId` (the ID of the `Credential` row) as the third argument `userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`. When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` sends this value as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint, which will look up the wrong user.

title: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response` that is incompatible with callers expecting SDK/axios return shapes
body:
When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` always returns a standard `fetch` `Response` object. Several callers pass SDK or axios callbacks that return different structures and immediately access properties that do not exist on a `fetch` `Response`:
- `GoogleCalendarService` (line 94) reads `res?.data` (`googleapis` response format).
- `HubspotCalendarService` (line 192) treats the return value directly as a `HubspotToken` (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`, `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken`) and saves the raw `Response` object to `prisma.credential.update`.
- `BiginCalendarService` (line 96) and `ZohoCrmCalendarService` (line 217) read `tokenInfo.data` (`axios` response format).

For all four integrations, token refresh will fail or write an invalid `key` to the database when credential syncing is enabled.

title: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by directory name, not `app.slug`, breaking webhook for several apps
body: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by the app directory name (e.g., `googlecalendar`, `office365calendar`, `office365video`, `larkcalendar`, `zoomvideo`), whereas `prisma.app.slug` and `appMetadata.slug` use the config slug (e.g., `google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `lark-calendar`, `zoom`). Indexing `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` returns `undefined` for all of these apps, causing the webhook to return 404 `"App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug"` even when a valid `appSlug` is provided.

title: Inconsistent `appSlug` `"zoomvideo"` passed to `refreshOAuthTokens`
body: Zoom's app slug in `config.json` and the database is `"zoom"` (as used in `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` line 63: `appId: "zoom"`), but `refreshOAuthTokens` is called here with `"zoomvideo"`. The sync endpoint receiving `appSlug` will get `"zoomvideo"` during token refresh while the webhook endpoint `/api/webhook/app-credential` requires `"zoom"`.

title: Google Calendar credential.key is overwritten with a Zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `SafeParseReturnType` object (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed data itself. In `GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` is written directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. After the first token refresh, `credential.key` in the database becomes `{ success: true, data: { ... } }`, so the next time `GoogleCalendarService` is constructed `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) will throw a `ZodError` and break Google Calendar for that user.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses `[z.string().toString()]` instead of a dynamic key validator
body: In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` evaluate `z.string().toString()` at module load time, producing the literal property key `"[object Object]"`. Because `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` requires a numeric property literally named `"[object Object]"` and strips every other property (such as `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, `refresh_token`, etc.). As a result, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` will always fail validation with `Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` unless the response happens to contain `"[object Object]": <number>`, and even then all expiry fields will be stripped.

title: refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, which is incompatible with SDK/axios callers
body: When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `Response` from `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`. However, several callers expect the return shape of their own client library rather than a Fetch `Response`: `GoogleCalendarService` (line 94) reads `res?.data.access_token`, `BiginCalendarService` (line 96) and `ZohoCrmCalendarService` (line 217) read `tokenInfo.data` (Axios response), and `HubspotCalendarService` (line 192) reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` and `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` directly off the returned object. None of these properties exist on a Fetch `Response`, so token refresh with credential syncing enabled will fail or write `undefined` tokens into the database for Google Calendar, HubSpot, Zoho Bigin, and Zoho CRM.

title: Salesforce CalendarService references `prisma` without importing it and uses stale access_token
body: `SalesforceCalendarService.getClient` calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)` on line 96, but `prisma` is never imported in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, causing a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` on every Salesforce calendar operation. In addition, line 75 refreshes the token via `fetch(...)` on every `getClient` call without using `refreshOAuthTokens`, and line 106 still passes the old `credentialKey.access_token` instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` to `new jsforce.Connection(...)`.

title: Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId` instead of `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects the third argument to be `userId: number | null` and sends it as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint. In `BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, `credentialId` (`credential.id`) is passed instead of `credential.userId`, so the sync endpoint will be queried with the credential's primary key rather than the Cal.com user ID.

title: Looking up `appStoreMetadata` by `app.slug` fails for apps whose key in `appStoreMetadata` differs from their slug
body: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by the app directory name (e.g. `googlecalendar`, `office365calendar`, `office365video`, `zoomvideo`, `larkcalendar`), whereas `prisma.app.slug` and `appMetadata.slug` use the config slug (e.g. `google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `zoom`, `lark-calendar`). Indexing `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` on line 50 returns `undefined` for all of these apps and causes the webhook to respond with 404 `"App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug"`.

title: Google Calendar credential key is saved as Zod SafeParseReturnType instead of credential data
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed token object itself. Here, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` is passed directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. This overwrites `credential.key` in the database with `{ success: true, data: { ... } }`, which corrupts the stored credential and causes `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on line 75 to throw a Zod validation error on every subsequent Google Calendar call.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses [z.string().toString()] which defines literal "[object Object]" key
body: In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` evaluate `toString()` on Zod schema instances at module load time, producing the literal property key `"[object Object]"`. As a result, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` requires a numeric property literally named `"[object Object]"` and strips all other properties (including `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, and `refresh_token`), so `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` will always fail when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is active.

title: Missing import of prisma in SalesforceCalendarService causes ReferenceError
body: `prisma.credential.update` is called on line 96, but `prisma` is not imported anywhere in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`. Instantiating `SalesforceCalendarService` will fail at runtime with `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined`. Additionally, lines 75-84 call `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` directly instead of wrapping it in `refreshOAuthTokens`, and line 106 passes the stale `credentialKey.access_token` instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` to `new jsforce.Connection`.

title: credentialId passed instead of userId to refreshOAuthTokens in Zoho Bigin
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects `(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)`, and sends `calcomUserId: userId.toString()` to the sync endpoint. In `BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, `credentialId` (the primary key of the `Credential` row) is passed as the third argument instead of `credential.userId`, so the sync endpoint will be queried with the wrong user ID.

title: refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response incompatible with callers expecting SDK/axios return shapes
body: When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` object. However, several callers expect the return value of their SDK/HTTP client inside `refreshFunction`: `GoogleCalendarService` (line 94) reads `res?.data` (gaxios response), `HubspotCalendarService` (line 192) reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` and `.accessToken` directly on the returned object, `BiginCalendarService` (line 96) and `ZohoCrmCalendarService` (line 217) read `.data` (axios response). None of these properties exist on a `fetch` `Response`, so token refresh with credential syncing enabled will throw or store `undefined` tokens for all four integrations.

title: appStoreMetadata is keyed by directory name, not app.slug, breaking lookup for several apps
body: `appStoreMetadata` keys are generated from the app directory names in `packages/app-store` (e.g. `googlecalendar`, `office365calendar`, `office365video`, `zoomvideo`, `larkcalendar`), whereas `prisma.app.slug` stores the `config.json` slug (e.g. `google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `zoom`, `lark-calendar`). Indexing `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` on line 50 returns `undefined` for all of these apps, causing the webhook to return 404 "App not found" whenever credentials are synced for Google Calendar, Office 365 Calendar, MS Teams, Zoom, Lark Calendar, etc.

title: Team admin check uses `&&` instead of `||`
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Because `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` check for distinct roles (`ADMIN` vs `OWNER`) or require both conditions to be true simultaneously, a user who is only a team admin (and not the team owner) will fail this check and receive a `FORBIDDEN` error when trying to add guests to a team booking. This should use `||` instead of `&&`.
