title: Calendar update uses caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` use the currently logged-in caller (`ctx.user`) rather than the booking's organizer (`booking.user`). `addGuestsHandler` explicitly allows attendees and team admins/owners (who are not the organizer) to add guests. When an attendee or team admin invokes `addGuests`, `EventManager` is initialized with their credentials instead of the organizer's, so `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will fail to update the organizer's external calendar event (or attempt the update against the wrong account).

title: `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow` with `id: booking.userId || 0` can return an arbitrary user or throw when `booking.userId` is null
body: When `booking.userId` is `null` or `0`, `where: { id: booking.userId || 0 }` queries for a user with `id: 0`, which will throw `NotFoundError` (an unhandled 500 error instead of a proper `TRPCError`). Additionally, `booking.user` is already fetched in the initial `prisma.booking.findFirst` query (lines 35-40), so this extra query is redundant if `booking.user` is selected with the needed fields.

title: Duplicate emails in `input.guests` and case differences bypass deduplication and blacklist checks
body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` on the server (`addGuests.schema.ts`) does not enforce uniqueness or lowercase normalization on `guests`. If a client calls the TRPC endpoint directly with duplicate emails in `guests` (e.g. `['a@b.com', 'a@b.com']`), both pass the `uniqueGuests` filter and duplicate attendee records are created in the database. Furthermore, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased, but `guest` and `attendee.email` are compared without lowercasing, so mixed-case emails bypass both the blacklist check and existing attendee check.

title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores event type email disable settings (`disableStandardEmails`)
body: Unlike `sendScheduledEmails`, `sendRescheduledEmails`, and `sendLocationChangeEmails` right above it, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept `eventTypeMetadata` or check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)`. Event types configured to suppress standard host or attendee emails will still send emails when guests are added.

title: Team admin check uses `&&` instead of `||`, blocking team admins from adding guests
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Because `isTeamAdmin` checks for `ADMIN` or `OWNER` role while `isTeamOwner` checks strictly for `OWNER`, using `&&` means the expression is only true when the user is a team owner, and always false for a team admin who is not an owner. It should use `||` (or simply `await isTeamAdmin(...)` if that helper already includes owners) so team admins have permission as intended by the variable name.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials
body: `addGuestsHandler` allows an attendee or a team admin/owner (who is not the booking organizer) to add guests to a booking. However, on lines 158-163 it fetches credentials for `ctx.user` (the logged-in caller) and constructs `EventManager` with `user` instead of `booking.user` (the organizer). When an attendee or team admin adds guests, `EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` will lack the organizer's calendar credentials and fail to update the actual calendar event on the organizer's external calendar.

title: Duplicate guest emails in request input and case differences bypass deduplication and blacklist checks
body: `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing `booking.attendees` and `blacklistedGuestEmails`, without deduplicating the incoming `guests` array itself or normalizing email case. If a client calls the tRPC endpoint directly with duplicate emails in `guests` (e.g. `['a@b.com', 'a@b.com']`), or with uppercase characters that bypass `blacklistedGuestEmails` (which was lowercased on line 71, while `guest` is not lowercased on line 77) or existing attendees with different casing, duplicate attendee records will be created in the database and blacklisted addresses will not be filtered.

title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings
body: In `BookingListItem.tsx`, `editBookingActions` (including `add_members`) is rendered for past confirmed bookings (`isBookingInPast && isConfirmed` on line 554) and `addGuestsHandler` does not check `booking.status` or whether the booking has already ended. As a result, users can add guests to past, cancelled, or rejected bookings, triggering calendar updates and 'Guests Added' / 'Scheduled' emails for events that are no longer active.

title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores `disableStandardEmails` metadata settings
body: Unlike `sendScheduledEmails`, `sendRescheduledEmails`, and `sendLocationChangeEmails` in `packages/emails/email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept `eventTypeMetadata` or check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`. Bookings on event types configured to suppress standard host or attendee emails will still send emails to the organizer and all attendees when guests are added.

title: Team admin check uses `&&` instead of `||`
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. In Cal.com's team membership model a user's role is either `ADMIN` or `OWNER`, not both, depending on how `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` are implemented (`isTeamOwner` requires `role: 'OWNER'`). Using `&&` instead of `||` means a team admin who is not the team owner (and not the booking organizer or attendee) will be denied permission with `FORBIDDEN` when trying to add guests to a team booking.

title: Calendar update uses caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials
body: `addGuestsHandler` allows an attendee or a team admin/owner to add guests to a booking (`isTeamAdminOrOwner || isOrganizer || isAttendee`), but then fetches credentials with `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and constructs `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` using the logged-in caller (`ctx.user`) rather than `booking.user` (the organizer). When an attendee or a team admin who is not the organizer adds guests, `EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` will try to update the calendar event using the caller's credentials and calendar integrations instead of the organizer's, so the organizer's external calendar invite (Google/Office365, etc.) will not be updated with the new attendees.

title: Duplicate emails in `input.guests` and case-insensitive duplicates are not deduplicated on the server
body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `z.array(z.string().email())` without enforcing uniqueness, and `uniqueGuests` in `addGuestsHandler` only filters against existing `booking.attendees` (with case-sensitive `===`) and `blacklistedGuestEmails` (which is lowercased while `guest` is not). If a client calls the tRPC endpoint with duplicate emails in `guests`, or with an email that differs only in casing from an existing attendee or blacklisted address, duplicate attendee rows will be created in the database and blacklisted guests can bypass the blacklist when uppercase characters are used.

title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores `disableStandardEmails` eventType metadata settings
body: Other email sender functions in `packages/emails/email-manager.ts` (such as `sendLocationChangeEmails`, `sendScheduledEmails`, `sendRescheduledEmails`) accept `eventTypeMetadata` and check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` before sending emails to hosts or attendees. `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not check these flags at all, so bookings on event types configured to suppress standard host or attendee emails will still send emails to the organizer, team members, and all attendees when guests are added.

title: "Additional Guests" action is shown for past bookings
body: `editBookingActions` (which now includes `add_members`) is rendered via `bookedActions` even when `isBookingInPast` is true (lines 553-554: `isBookingInPast && isConfirmed ? <TableActions actions={bookedActions} /> : null`), and `addGuestsHandler` does not check whether the booking has already ended. Users can therefore add guests to past bookings, which triggers calendar updates and sends "Guests Added" / "New event scheduled" invitation emails for meetings that have already taken place.

title: `isInvalidEmail` error banner is not cleared on successful submission or when reopening the dialog
body: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails, and is only reset to `false` in the Cancel button's `onClick`. It is not reset when the user edits the email fields, when `addGuestsMutation` succeeds, or when the dialog is closed via the backdrop / Escape key (`onOpenChange`). If a user triggers a validation error once and then fixes the email and submits (or closes the dialog via Escape and reopens it), the red error message remains visible.

title: `deleteMany` `OR` condition omits `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` on the `retryCount` branch and causes full table scan
body: In `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany`, the `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter was moved inside only the first branch of the `OR` clause (`scheduledDate <= now`), while the second branch (`retryCount > 1`) has no `method` filter and no index on `retryCount`. Because `WorkflowReminder` only has composite indexes starting with `method`, `bookingUid`, `workflowStepId`, `seatReferenceId`, or `cancelled`, a top-level `OR` with an unindexed `retryCount > 1` branch prevents Postgres from using the `(method, scheduled, scheduledDate)` index and forces a sequential scan of the entire `WorkflowReminder` table on every cron run (and would also delete non-SMS reminders if any ever used `retryCount`). Keep `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` at the top level of the `where` clause alongside the `OR` (or delete the reminder directly when `reminder.retryCount >= 1` in the failure handler).

title: `deleteMany` with top-level `OR` across unindexed `retryCount` causes a full table scan on `WorkflowReminder`
body: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts` (lines 29-45), the `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` query was changed from filtering on `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } }` (which is covered by the composite index `@@index([method, scheduled, scheduledDate])`) to a top-level `OR` whose second branch is `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`. `retryCount` is not indexed on `WorkflowReminder` in `packages/prisma/schema.prisma`, and placing it in a top-level `OR` without `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` forces PostgreSQL to sequentially scan the entire `WorkflowReminder` table (including `EMAIL` and `WHATSAPP` reminders) on every cron invocation. Scoping the `where` clause by `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` at the top level and/or indexing `retryCount` (or deleting the reminder directly when `reminder.retryCount >= 1` instead of incrementing and deleting on the next run) avoids scanning the whole table every cron tick.

title: Unindexed OR clause in deleteMany causes full table scan on WorkflowReminder
body: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` was changed to use an `OR` condition combining `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } }` and `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`. However, `retryCount` is not indexed on `WorkflowReminder` in `packages/prisma/schema.prisma`, and the second `OR` branch does not filter by `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. In PostgreSQL, an `OR` across an unindexed column forces a sequential scan of the entire `WorkflowReminder` table on every cron invocation, and would also delete non-SMS reminders if any ever had `retryCount > 1`. Scope `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the top-level `where` clause and either add an index covering `retryCount` or delete the reminder directly when `reminder.retryCount >= 1` upon failure instead of incrementing and scanning in `deleteMany`.

title: Unparenthesized returned SQL conditions allow operator-precedence bypass in caller WHERE clauses
body:
`getBaseConditions`, `buildAuthorizationConditions`, and `buildFilterConditions` return raw `Prisma.Sql` fragments containing top-level `OR` operators without outer parentheses in several branches:

- `getBaseConditions()` returns `authConditions` directly when `filterConditions` is `null` (line 75). For `team` and `org` scopes, `authConditions` has the form `((...) AND (...)) OR ((...) AND (...))` with no outer parentheses.
- `buildFilterConditions()` returns `("eventTypeId" = ...) OR ("eventParentId" = ...)` without outer parentheses when `eventTypeId` is the only filter.
- `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` are public methods that return these unparenthesized `OR` expressions.

When a caller embeds `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ...` (standard pattern in `$queryRaw` queries), SQL's higher precedence for `AND` over `OR` parses the query as `branch1 OR (branch2 AND "createdAt" >= ...)`, causing the first `OR` branch (e.g., all team bookings for the team/org) to ignore any subsequent `AND` filters in the caller's `WHERE` clause (date ranges, statuses, etc.), or worse, if `filterConditions` or `authConditions` is combined with other clauses, leaking rows outside the intended filter or authorization scope.

title: `getBaseConditions` returns unparenthesized `OR` clauses when `filters` are absent
body: When no filters are provided (`filterConditions` is `null`), `getBaseConditions()` returns `authConditions` directly without wrapping it in outer parentheses (line 75). For `team` and `org` scopes (when users exist in the team/org), `authConditions` is a top-level `OR` expression: `((...) AND (...)) OR ((...) AND (...))`. If a caller embeds `getBaseConditions()` in a raw SQL `WHERE` clause alongside other `AND` predicates without adding their own parentheses (e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ${startDate}`), SQL operator precedence (`AND` binds tighter than `OR`) will cause the additional `AND` predicates to apply only to the second branch of the `OR`, allowing rows matching the first branch (`isTeamBooking = true`) to bypass the caller's additional filters (such as date range or status filters). Wrapping the returned expression in parentheses or parenthesizing `OR` expressions in `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` / `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` prevents this precedence bug.

title: `getBaseConditions` returns unparenthesized `OR` clauses when `filters` are absent
body: When no filter conditions are set (`filterConditions === null`), `getBaseConditions()` returns `authConditions` directly without outer parentheses. For `org` and `team` scopes, `authConditions` is a top-level `OR` expression (`(A) OR (B)`). If a caller embeds `${baseConditions}` inside a larger `WHERE` clause alongside `AND` conditions (e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ...`), SQL operator precedence binds `AND` tighter than `OR`, evaluating as `(A) OR ((B) AND "createdAt" >= ...)` and leaking unauthorized rows from branch `A` regardless of the additional predicates. `buildFilterConditions` has the same issue when only `eventTypeId` is set (`("eventTypeId" = ...) OR ("eventParentId" = ...)`). Wrap top-level `OR` expressions (or the return value of `getBaseConditions`) in parentheses so they are safe to compose with `AND`.

title: `deleteCacheMutation` does not invalidate `connectedCalendars` query after deleting cache
body: `disconnectMutation` invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`, but `deleteCacheMutation` (lines 42-50) does not invalidate the `connectedCalendars` query. When `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` renders without an `onChanged` callback (or with one that doesn't refetch `connectedCalendars`), deleting the cache leaves the stale `cacheUpdatedAt` in the React Query cache, so the dropdown continues showing the old cache status and the "Delete cached data" action until the page is reloaded.

title: `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany` with an empty `data` object does not update `updatedAt`
body: Line 1024 calls `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` with the comment `// Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars under this credential`. Unlike `prisma.selectedCalendar.update`, Prisma's `updateMany` does not automatically inject `@updatedAt` when `data` is `{}` (or at all unless `updatedAt` is explicitly passed in `data`), and an empty `data: {}` becomes a no-op in Prisma. If `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` needs to be bumped, `updatedAt: new Date()` must be passed explicitly in `data` (or the call removed if `CalendarCache.updatedAt` has superseded it).

title: `connectedCalendarsHandler` bypasses `CalendarCache.init` feature-flag check
body: Other callers in the codebase initialize the calendar cache via `await CalendarCache.init(null)`, which checks the `calendar-cache` feature flag and returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the feature is disabled. Here `new CalendarCacheRepository()` is instantiated directly (line 28), so `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` will query the `CalendarCache` table and surface cache status/actions in the UI even when the `calendar-cache` feature flag is disabled (making the new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method on `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` unused).

title: Deleting cache does not invalidate connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in UI
body: `deleteCacheMutation` shows a toast and calls `onSuccess?.()`, but unlike `disconnectMutation` below it (lines 61-64), it never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`, `onChanged` is optional and the component relies on its internal `trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.useQuery` for `cacheUpdatedAt`. After a user deletes the cache, the dropdown continues to show the old `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamp and the "Delete cached data" action until the page is manually refreshed. Add an `onSettled` handler on `deleteCacheMutation` that calls `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`.

title: `updateMany({ data: {} })` does not update `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` calls `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data: {} })`. In Prisma, `updateMany` with an empty `data` object does not automatically set `@updatedAt` columns (and may be a no-op), unlike single-record `update` or passing `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly. If the intent is to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` for all rows under the credential, pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` (or remove this call if `CalendarCache.updatedAt` is the only timestamp used).

title: Direct instantiation of `CalendarCacheRepository` bypasses the `calendar-cache` feature flag
body: `connectedCalendarsHandler` instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init(null)` (which returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the `calendar-cache` feature is disabled, and is why `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` was also added to `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` in this PR). Instantiating `CalendarCacheRepository` directly queries `prisma.calendarCache` even when the feature is disabled and leaves `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` unused.

title: `deleteCacheMutation` does not invalidate `connectedCalendars` query
body: `deleteCacheMutation` does not invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled` (unlike `disconnectMutation` on line 61). In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`, `onChanged` is frequently not passed by callers, so after deleting cached data the `connectedCalendars` query will remain stale in the React Query cache and the dropdown will continue showing the old `cacheUpdatedAt` status and "Delete cached data" action until the page is reloaded.

title: `updateMany` with empty `data: {}` will not update `updatedAt` in Prisma
body: Calling `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes `data: {}` to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany`. Unlike `prisma.model.update()`, Prisma's `updateMany()` does not automatically inject `@updatedAt` when `data` is empty (it becomes a no-op or fails to touch the column in SQL). To actually update `updatedAt` with `updateMany`, `updatedAt: new Date()` must be explicitly passed in `data`.

title: SendGrid client API key is not initialized in scheduleEmailReminders
body: `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` imports `client` from `@sendgrid/client` and calls `client.request(...)` on lines 57 and 188, but never calls `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` (only `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` is called on line 19). Unless `emailReminderManager.ts` happens to have been imported in the same serverless instance beforehand, `@sendgrid/client` has no API key set and both cancelling scheduled sends (`/v3/user/scheduled_sends`) and creating batch IDs (`/v3/mail/batch`) will fail with 401 Unauthorized.

title: Rescheduling a booking immediately cancels in SendGrid and deletes the booking before reminders are cleaned up
body:
In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` is called with `immediateDelete = true` (line 968) and without `await`, right before `eventManager.reschedule(...)` (line 978). There are two issues here:
1. Passing `immediateDelete = true` sends a `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` immediately to SendGrid even when the reminder is days away, re-introducing the 100 pending cancellations limit that this PR is meant to avoid, and `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` does not delete the `WorkflowReminder` row in the `immediateDelete` branch.
2. `eventManager.reschedule` deletes the `originalRescheduledBooking` row in the database, and because `WorkflowReminder.booking` has `onDelete: Cascade`, any un-awaited `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` calls race with the cascade delete (and if changed to `immediateDelete = false`, the cascade delete would wipe out the `WorkflowReminder` row before the cron job in `scheduleEmailReminders` ever sees `cancelled: true`, leaving the scheduled email active in SendGrid).

title: A single SendGrid error in the cancellation loop aborts all deletions in the batch
body: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` (lines 53-77), `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` promises are collected in `workflowRemindersToDelete` and only executed at `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` after the loop finishes (Prisma queries are lazy until awaited). If `client.request` throws for the Nth reminder (for example, if its `referenceId` is missing or rejected by SendGrid), the `catch` block is entered before `Promise.all` runs, so none of the prior N-1 reminders that were already cancelled in SendGrid get deleted from the database and they will be retried on every cron run.

title: Un-awaited reminder cancellations race with cascade deletion of workflow and workflowStep
body: In `workflowsRouter.delete` (lines 212-225) and `workflowsRouter.update` when a step is deleted (lines 519-531), `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called inside `.forEach(...)` without `await`, immediately followed by `await ctx.prisma.workflow.deleteMany(...)` or `await ctx.prisma.workflowStep.delete(...)`. Because `WorkflowStep` and `WorkflowReminder` have `onDelete: Cascade`, the database cascade deletes the `WorkflowReminder` rows while `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (when `referenceId` is null) and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are concurrently trying to `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminder.id } })`, causing P2025 record-not-found errors and risking unfinished external API calls if the serverless function terminates after the mutation returns.

title: Rescheduling bookings uses immediateDelete, bypassing the deferred SendGrid cancellation fix
body: `handleNewBooking.ts` calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` with `immediateDelete = true` when rescheduling a booking. In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, `immediateDelete = true` immediately calls SendGrid's `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` endpoint instead of marking the reminder `cancelled: true` for the cron job to cancel within 1 hour of the send time, and it also returns early without deleting or updating the `workflowReminder` record in the database. Rescheduled bookings will therefore still consume SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation limit right away (defeating the purpose of this PR for reschedules) and leave orphaned `workflowReminder` rows in the database.

title: SendGrid `@sendgrid/client` API key is never initialized in `scheduleEmailReminders`
body: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` is called at line 19, but `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` is never called (unlike in `emailReminderManager.ts` line 26). Unless `emailReminderManager` happens to be imported in the same serverless instance prior to this endpoint running, `client.request({ url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends", ... })` (and `/v3/mail/batch`) will fail with `401 Unauthorized` from SendGrid, preventing scheduled email reminders from being cancelled or scheduled by the cron job.

title: One failed SendGrid cancellation aborts all remaining cancellations and DB deletions
body: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop awaits `client.request(...)` for each reminder inside a single outer `try` block and defers all `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` operations to `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` after the loop. Note that Prisma's `.delete()` returns a lazy `PrismaPromise` that only executes when awaited. If any single `client.request` call throws (e.g., an invalid `batch_id` or transient SendGrid error), none of the already-cancelled reminders are deleted from the database and none of the subsequent reminders in the batch are processed. On the next cron run, the same failing reminder will be retried and block the queue again. Each iteration should have its own `try/catch` and `await` the DB delete immediately after its SendGrid call succeeds.

title: Editing a workflow step queries already-cancelled reminders and overwrites `cancelled: true`
body: In `workflows.tsx` inside the `update` mutation (line 507), `remindersFromStep` is fetched with `where: { workflowStepId: oldStep.id }` without filtering out `cancelled: true`. Earlier in the same mutation (lines 376-382), reminders for removed event types were marked `cancelled: true` via `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (which is also not awaited, creating a race condition). In addition, reminders from previously cancelled bookings on that step also have `cancelled: true` in the DB. When `oldStep` is edited, `remindersToUpdate` (lines 567-580) will include those already-cancelled reminders; if `oldStep` is deleted (lines 519-525), `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` will be called on already-cancelled reminders without deleting their DB rows. `remindersFromStep` should filter `NOT: { cancelled: true }` (or `cancelled: false`), and the async calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` should be awaited.

title: Rescheduling bookings bypasses deferred email cancellation and deletes booking before reminder cleanup finishes
body:
In `handleNewBooking.ts`, rescheduling calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` inside an unawaited `forEach` loop right before `await eventManager.reschedule(...)`. There are two issues here:
1. Passing `immediateDelete = true` immediately sends `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` to SendGrid rather than setting `cancelled: true` on the `WorkflowReminder` record for the cron job to process within 1 hour of the send time. This defeats the purpose of the PR for rescheduled bookings and will still contribute to hitting SendGrid's 100 pending `scheduled_sends` limit.
2. `eventManager.reschedule` deletes the `originalRescheduledBooking` row from the database. Because `WorkflowReminder.booking` has `onDelete: Cascade` in `schema.prisma`, deleting the original booking cascades and deletes its `WorkflowReminder` rows. If `immediateDelete` were `false`, cascading deletion would wipe out the `WorkflowReminder` rows before the cron job (`scheduleEmailReminders`) ever runs to cancel them in SendGrid; and with unawaited async calls in `forEach`, it also races with `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`.

title: `@sendgrid/client` API key is never initialized in `scheduleEmailReminders`
body: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` is called on line 19, but `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` is never called on the `@sendgrid/client` instance (unlike in `emailReminderManager.ts` line 26). When the cron endpoint runs in a serverless function or process where `emailReminderManager.ts` has not been imported, `client.request({ url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends", ... })` (line 57) and `client.request({ url: "/v3/mail/batch", ... })` (line 188) will fail with 401 Unauthorized from SendGrid, preventing scheduled emails from being cancelled or batch-scheduled.

title: Single SendGrid failure in cancellation loop aborts all deletions, including already-cancelled reminders
body: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` (lines 53-77), each `client.request` to SendGrid is awaited inside the `for` loop, while the corresponding `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` promises are pushed into `workflowRemindersToDelete` and only executed at `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` after the loop finishes (Note: Prisma's `.delete()` is a `PrismaPromise` that only executes when awaited/then'd). If cancelling the Nth reminder throws an error (for example, if `referenceId` is missing or SendGrid returns an error for one batch ID), control jumps to the `catch` block: the remaining reminders in `remindersToCancel` are skipped, and none of the first N-1 reminders that were already cancelled in SendGrid are deleted from the database, causing them to be re-processed on the next cron run.

title: Paid booking cancellations return early before cancelling workflow reminders or scheduled jobs
body: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, when `bookingToDelete.paid` is truthy (lines 363-465), the handler refunds the payment, marks the booking as `REJECTED`, and returns on line 464. Because the code that cancels `scheduledJobs` and `workflowReminders` is located further down at lines 480-493, cancelling a paid booking never cancels its scheduled workflow email or SMS reminders (nor its Zapier scheduled jobs), so reminders will still be sent for cancelled paid bookings.

title: Unawaited `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` races with `workflowStep.delete` cascade
body: In `workflows.tsx` (lines 518-531) and in `delete` (lines 212-225), `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` are invoked inside a synchronous `.forEach(...)` without `await`, immediately followed by `await ctx.prisma.workflowStep.delete(...)` (or `workflow.deleteMany`). Because `WorkflowReminder.workflowStep` has `onDelete: Cascade` in `schema.prisma`, deleting the workflow or step cascades and deletes the `WorkflowReminder` rows in Postgres while `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` / `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` are still awaiting network calls to Twilio/SendGrid, causing their subsequent `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` calls to fail with `P2025` (record not found), and risking unfinished external API calls if the serverless execution finishes as soon as the mutation returns.

title: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` with `immediateDelete` leaves orphaned `WorkflowReminder` row in DB
body: In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (`emailReminderManager.ts` lines 213-223), when `immediateDelete` is true, it sends the cancel request to SendGrid and immediately returns without deleting the `workflowReminder` record from the database (or marking it cancelled). If the caller does not cascade-delete the parent workflow/step, the `WorkflowReminder` row remains in the database with `cancelled: null`.

title: All app modules are still eagerly imported at module evaluation time
body: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, the values in `appStore` are `import("./applecalendar")`, `import("./caldavcalendar")`, etc., rather than functions like `() => import("./applecalendar")`. Because `import(...)` is called directly when constructing the `appStore` object literal, every single app package is still loaded and evaluated immediately as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported, defeating the purpose of lazy/on-demand async imports. Additionally, if any of those dynamic imports reject at startup before being awaited, it will trigger an unhandled promise rejection. Each entry should be a thunk (`() => import(...)`) invoked only when that specific app is requested.

title: `forEach` with `async` callback populates `apiDeletes` after `Promise.all` is already reached
body: In `handleCancelBooking.ts` (lines 458-470), `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` uses an `async` callback inside `.forEach()`. Because `.forEach()` does not await promises returned by its callback, execution immediately continues past the `if (bookingCalendarReference)` block right after the first `await getCalendar(credential)` suspends. As a result, `apiDeletes` is still empty (or incomplete) when `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) or `await apiDeletes` (line 617) runs, so the calendar event deletions for recurring bookings are not awaited and may be terminated early in serverless environments or fail silently without being caught.

title: Async `forEach` inside `try/catch` will not await calendar/video deletions or catch errors
body: In `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts` (lines 124-139), `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` is wrapped in a `try/catch` block. Because `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await the promises returned by an `async` callback, `Reschedule` will proceed to send emails and return `true` before `getCalendar` and `calendar.deleteEvent` complete, and any rejection inside the async callback will become an unhandled promise rejection instead of being caught by the surrounding `try/catch`. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` instead. (The same issue is present in `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts` at line 125 and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` at line 553.)

title: Dynamic imports in appStore are still evaluated eagerly at module load time
body: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, each entry in `appStore` is defined as `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")` rather than a lazy factory function `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`. Because the `import(...)` expressions are evaluated immediately when the `appStore` object literal is constructed, importing `@calcom/app-store` still triggers loading of all 28 app-store packages at startup/module initialization rather than on demand when a specific app is requested. To actually defer loading until an app is used, each property should be a function (or getter) returning the `import()` promise and callers should invoke it.

title: Async `forEach` callback pushes `deleteEvent` promises into `apiDeletes` after `Promise.all` runs
body: When cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring event (lines 458-470), `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... const deletedEvent = await calendar?.deleteEvent(...); apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` is used. Because `forEach` does not await its async callback, execution immediately moves past the loop while `await getCalendar(credential)` is still pending. By the time `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) or `await apiDeletes` (line 617) executes, `apiDeletes` does not contain the calendar deletion promises, so the handler returns before recurring calendar events are actually deleted (and in serverless environments, the background deletions may be terminated mid-flight). Additionally, `await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` pushes the resolved result rather than the promise into `apiDeletes`.

title: `try/catch` around `forEach(async ...)` will not catch errors or await calendar event deletion
body: In `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts` (lines 124-139) and identically in `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts` (lines 124-139) and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (lines 553-567), `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); ... })` is used. `Array.prototype.forEach` ignores the promise returned by an `async` callback: the surrounding `try { ... } catch` block will not catch any rejections from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` (resulting in unhandled promise rejections instead of logging via `logger.error`), and `Reschedule` / `requestReschedule` will proceed to send emails and return before calendar and video deletions have been initiated or completed. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))` instead.

title: Dynamic imports in appStore are evaluated eagerly at module load time
body: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, each entry in `appStore` is defined as `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")` rather than a factory function like `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`. Because `import(...)` is called directly when constructing the `appStore` object literal, all 28 app modules are still imported immediately as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported anywhere, rather than lazily loading only the needed app on demand. Additionally, if any unused app module fails to load at startup, it will produce an unhandled promise rejection.

title: Async forEach callback pushes to apiDeletes after Promise.all is already called
body: When cancelling all remaining bookings in a recurring series (`allRemainingBookings` at lines 458-470), `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` is used. Because `forEach` does not await its async callback, execution immediately continues past the `if (bookingCalendarReference)` block right after hitting `await getCalendar(credential)`. By the time `getCalendar` and `calendar.deleteEvent` resolve inside the callback, `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 (or `await apiDeletes` at line 617) has already been invoked on an array that does not contain those delete promises, so the calendar deletions are not awaited before the handler returns and any rejections go unhandled.

title: Async forEach inside try/catch neither awaits deletions nor catches errors
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` is wrapped in a `try { ... } catch (error) { ... }` block. Because `forEach` ignores the promises returned by the async callback, `Reschedule` does not wait for `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` to finish before sending emails and returning, and any error thrown after the first `await` will become an unhandled promise rejection instead of being caught by the surrounding `try/catch`. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))` instead.

title: Async forEach inside try/catch neither awaits deletions nor catches errors
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` is wrapped in a `try { ... } catch (error) { ... }` block. Because `forEach` does not await the promises returned by its async callback, calendar and video deletions run detached in the background and any rejection after `await getCalendar(...)` bypasses the `try/catch` block as an unhandled promise rejection. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))` instead.

title: getCalendarCredentials starts getCalendar promises for non-calendar variants and discards them
body: In `getCalendarCredentials`, `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` is called before checking `app.variant === "calendar"`. Now that `getCalendar` is `async` and returns a `Promise`, calling it unconditionally starts an async operation for every credential of any app whose type ends with `_calendar` (such as `closecom_other_calendar` or `wipemycalother`), and if `app.variant !== "calendar"`, the returned promise is immediately discarded without a rejection handler. `getCalendar(credential)` should only be called when `app.variant === "calendar"`.

title: Early return on date override skips busy-time check, allowing double bookings on override days
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (lines 133-135), when `dateOverrideExist` is true and the slot falls within the date override window, the function immediately returns `true` without executing the `busy.every(...)` check at line 153. As a result, any calendar busy times or existing Cal.com bookings on a date with a date override are completely ignored, causing already-booked or busy slots to be returned as available.

title: Comparing two Dayjs objects with `===` is always false, breaking full-day unavailability overrides
body: Line 114 checks `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` to detect an all-day unavailable override (where `start` and `end` are equal). Because `dayjs(...)` constructs a new object each time, `===` compares object references and always evaluates to `false` (and `slotEndTime` is never before/same as `start` while `slotStartTime` is only `isAfter` `end`, not `isSame`), so a slot starting at `date.start` is not rejected. Use `.isSame(...)` instead of `===`.

title: Date override boundary check allows slots that partially overlap the start or end of the override
body: Lines 117-125 reject a slot only when `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime > overrideEnd` (overlap test instead of containment test). This means: (1) a slot that starts before the date override begins but ends after `overrideStart` is considered valid, (2) a slot that starts before `overrideEnd` but ends after `overrideEnd` is considered valid, and (3) a slot whose `slotStartTime` equals `overrideEnd` is also considered valid because `isAfter` is strict. To require the slot to be within the date override window, the rejection condition should be `slotStartTime.isBefore(overrideStart) || slotEndTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`.

title: Working hours check rejects valid slots when a user has multiple working hour intervals on the same day and ignores slotEndTime
body: In lines 138-151, `workingHours.find(...)` returns truthy (causing `checkIfIsAvailable` to return `false`) as soon as ANY workingHour entry for that weekday does not contain `slotStartTime`. If a user has split working hours on the same day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, or hours split across UTC midnight), a slot in the second interval fails the check against the first interval and is rejected. Additionally, line 142 computes `end` from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so a slot extending past the end of working hours is not caught, and when `slotStartTime` and `slotEndTime` cross UTC midnight (or on days with no matching `workingHour.days`), the check does not work as intended.

title: Multiple date overrides on the same day and `utcOffset` calculation in `checkIfIsAvailable`
body: In lines 106-127: (1) `dateOverrides.find(...)` rejects a slot if it is outside the first matching override for that date, even when the user has multiple date override ranges on the same day and the slot falls inside a second override range. (2) `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone)` on a `Date` object interprets `date.start`'s local wall-clock time in the server's timezone rather than UTC, and adding `utcOffset * -1` shifts a timestamp that was already converted to UTC by `getUserAvailability` back to organizer wall-clock time while `slotStartTime` is in real UTC (`time.utc()`), so comparing `slotStartTime` and `slotEndTime` against `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares UTC slot times against organizer-local override times whenever `organizerTimeZone` is not UTC.

title: Early return on date override skips busy-time check, exposing already-booked slots as available
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, when a date override matches the slot's date and the slot falls within the override's hours, `dateOverrideExist` is set to `true` and lines 133-135 immediately `return true`. This returns before the `busy.every(...)` check at line 153 runs. As a consequence, on any day where a host has a date override, all existing Cal bookings and external calendar busy times for that host are ignored during `checkIfIsAvailable`, allowing double-bookings during the date override window.

title: Comparing two Dayjs instances with `===` is always false, breaking full-day unavailable date overrides
body: Line 114 checks `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` to detect a 0-length date override (which represents marking the entire day as unavailable). Because each `dayjs(...).add(...)` call returns a distinct object reference, `===` between the two is always `false`. Use `.isSame(...)` (or compare timestamps) instead; otherwise a "unavailable all day" date override falls through to the range checks and slots matching the boundary or logic mistakes may not be treated as a full-day block.

title: Date override range check in `checkIfIsAvailable` allows slots that partially overlap the override boundaries
body: Lines 117-125 reject a slot only when `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime > overrideEnd`. This fails to reject slots that start before `overrideStart` and end after `overrideStart`, slots that start before `overrideEnd` and end after `overrideEnd`, or slots that start exactly at `overrideEnd` (`slotStartTime.isSame(overrideEnd)`). Moreover, if a user has multiple date override ranges on the same day (e.g., 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00), `.find(...)` returns `true` on the first range that does not contain the slot, causing slots in the second range to be rejected as unavailable. A slot is valid for the day's overrides only if at least one override on that day satisfies `slotStartTime >= overrideStart && slotEndTime <= overrideEnd`.

title: Working-hours check in `checkIfIsAvailable` uses `slotStartTime` for `end` and rejects valid split schedules
body: In lines 138-151, `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` instead of using `slotEndTime`, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after working hours is not caught. In addition, using `workingHours.find(...)` to return `false` when any working-hour entry for that day does not contain the slot breaks split working hours on the same day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) and multi-day/UTC-wrapped working-hour entries: a slot in the afternoon will fail the morning entry in `.find(...)` and be marked unavailable.

title: `date.start` and `date.end` in `dateOverrides` are already shifted to UTC in `getUserAvailability`, so adding `utcOffset` shifts them a second time
body: `getUserAvailability` (via `getDateOverrides`) already constructs `override.start` and `override.end` as UTC `Date` instants corresponding to the organizer's local override times (for example, in the test `IstWorkHoursWithDateOverride`, 14:00 IST is stored as `08:30:00.000Z` in `dateOverrides`). In `checkIfIsAvailable`, line 107 computes `utcOffset = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` and lines 110-123 add `utcOffset` to `dayjs(date.start)` and `dayjs(date.end)`, shifting an already-UTC timestamp by another `-utcOffset` (e.g. 08:30Z becomes 03:00Z for IST) and comparing that against `slotStartTime` (which is in UTC, 08:30Z). Similarly, in `packages/lib/slots.ts` lines 212-223, `override.start` is already in UTC, so subtracting `organizerUtcOffset` shifts the override by the organizer's offset a second time whenever `override.start` is already UTC-adjusted.

title: Early `return true` on `dateOverrideExist` skips busy-time check, allowing double bookings on override dates
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, when a slot falls within a date override, `dateOverrideExist` is set to `true` and lines 133-135 immediately return `true` before reaching `busy.every(...)` at line 153. As a result, existing Cal bookings and external calendar busy times are completely ignored on any day that has a date override, causing already-booked slots to be shown as available and allowing double-booking.

title: Comparing two Dayjs objects with `===` is always false, breaking full-day unavailable overrides
body: Line 114 checks `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` to detect a 0-length (unavailable all day) date override. Because `dayjs(...)` returns a new object instance each time, `===` compares object references and always evaluates to `false`. Use `.isSame(...)` instead (or compare `date.start.getTime() === date.end.getTime()`).

title: Boundary conditions in date override check allow slots that only partially overlap or start at override end
body:
In `checkIfIsAvailable` (lines 117-125), a slot is rejected only if `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime > overrideEnd`. This has three defects:
1. If `slotStartTime` equals `overrideEnd`, `isAfter` is false, so a slot starting right when the override ends is treated as inside the override.
2. A slot that starts before `overrideStart` and ends after `overrideStart` (or starts before `overrideEnd` and ends after `overrideEnd`) is not rejected, allowing bookings that extend outside the override window.
3. If a user defines multiple date override ranges on the same day, `.find()` rejects the slot as soon as it is outside the first range without checking whether it fits inside another range on that day.

A slot is within an override range iff `slotStartTime >= overrideStart && slotEndTime <= overrideEnd`.

title: Working hours check in `checkIfIsAvailable` uses `slotStartTime` for `end` and fails with split working hours
body:
In `checkIfIsAvailable` (lines 138-151):
1. Line 142 computes `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` instead of using `slotEndTime`, so the event's duration is ignored and a slot starting before `workingHour.endTime` that extends past the end of working hours is still considered valid.
2. Using `workingHours.find(...)` to return `false` when a slot is outside *any* matching entry breaks schedules with multiple working-hour blocks on the same day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00), because a slot in the afternoon block will be outside the morning block, causing `.find` to match and `checkIfIsAvailable` to return `false`.
3. If `workingHours` has no entry for `slotStartTime.day()` at all, `.find` returns `undefined` and the slot is treated as available on a non-working day.

title: Redundant `utcOffset` shift on `date.start`/`date.end` in `checkIfIsAvailable` double-shifts or un-shifts override times
body: `getUserAvailability` already returns `dateOverrides` with `start` and `end` converted to the actual UTC instants of the override (e.g. a 14:00 IST override is returned as `08:30:00.000Z`). In `checkIfIsAvailable`, line 107 computes `utcOffset = organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0` and adds it to `date.start` and `date.end` before comparing against `slotStartTime` (which is in UTC). For an organizer in IST (+05:30), `utcOffset` is -330, shifting `08:30Z` to `03:00Z` and comparing that against UTC `slotStartTime` (`08:30Z`). In the added test (`getSchedule.test.ts`), `TestData.schedules.IstWorkHoursWithDateOverride` has `date` as a plain string rather than a `Date` object, so `getUserAvailability` skips it (`!!availability.date && availability.date instanceof Date`) and this code path in `checkIfIsAvailable` was never exercised by the test.

title: Migration crashes on fresh or unconfigured databases when querying site_settings
body:
In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, lines 9-11 and line 15 index `[0]` directly on the PG::Result returned by `execute(...)` without checking whether any rows were returned:

```ruby
category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c
                    INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name
                    WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i

if category_id == 0
  category_id = execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i
end
```

If `embed_category` was never modified from its default (so no row exists in `site_settings`, or its value doesn't match a category name), the first query returns 0 rows and `[0]` raises `IndexError: tuple index 0 out of range` (or `NoMethodError` on `nil`). Similarly, on a fresh database being migrated before seeding, `uncategorized_category_id` is not in `site_settings`, causing line 15 to fail as well. Both queries need a `cmd_tuples > 0` check (like line 19 does) and a fallback when no row is found.

title: Migrated embeddable_hosts are not normalized and bypass SQL escaping
body:
In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` line 25, existing `embeddable_hosts` values are inserted directly into the table via raw SQL interpolation:

```ruby
execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
```

Previously, `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped `http://` / `https://` and extracted `URI(h).host` at check time (as tested in the removed specs in `site_setting_spec.rb`), whereas `EmbeddableHost` now strips the scheme and path in a `before_validation` callback and compares `lower(host) = ?` against `uri.host`. Because the migration uses raw `INSERT` instead of the model or stripping the scheme/path/whitespace (`\r`), any existing setting stored with `http://`, `https://`, a path, or trailing `\r` will be inserted verbatim and will fail to match in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`.

title: `before_validation` raises NoMethodError when `host` is nil
body:
In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb` lines 5-8, the `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!` unconditionally:

```ruby
before_validation do
  self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')
  self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')
end
```

If an `EmbeddableHost` is validated when `host` is `nil` (for example, `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?` or a request with missing `host` param), `self.host.sub!` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` instead of failing validation cleanly.

title: `record_for_host` fails to match when the input URL has an uppercase hostname or non-standard port
body:
In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb` lines 10-18:

```ruby
def self.record_for_host(host)
  uri = URI(host) rescue nil
  return false unless uri.present?

  host = uri.host
  return false unless host.present?

  where("lower(host) = ?", host).first
end
```

1. `URI(url).host` preserves the case of the input string in Ruby (e.g., `URI('http://EvilTrout.com/foo').host == 'EvilTrout.com'`). Comparing `lower(host) = ?` against an un-downcased `host` parameter will never match if the referer/embed URL contains any uppercase characters in the hostname (`host.downcase` should be used).
2. The format regex on line 2 explicitly allows ports (e.g., `example.com:8000`), which get saved in the `host` column, but `uri.host` strips the port, so any `EmbeddableHost` saved with a port will never be matched by `record_for_host`.

title: Fabricator definitions are swapped between `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`
body: The contents of `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` and `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` are inverted: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines `Fabricator(:category)` and its variants.

title: Misleading spec description and setup in `expandable_first_post?`
body:
In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` lines 1403-1405:

```ruby
it "is false if embeddable_host is blank" do
  expect(topic.expandable_first_post?).to eq(false)
end
```

`Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer checks `EmbeddableHost` at all (`SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). In this test, neither `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` nor `has_topic_embed?` is set, so it returns `false` regardless of whether an `embeddable_host` exists.

title: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category or uncategorized_category_id is not set in site_settings
body: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, lines 9-11 and 15 index `[0]['id']` and `[0]['value']` directly on the `PG::Result` returned by `execute(...)`. On any database where `embed_category` has never been saved to `site_settings` (or where `uncategorized_category_id` is not yet in `site_settings`, e.g., a fresh database running migrations from scratch), `execute(...)` returns 0 rows, `result[0]` is `nil` (or raises `IndexError` on `PG::Result`), and `['id']` / `['value']` raises an exception, aborting `rake db:migrate`. Additionally, on line 25, `h` is interpolated directly into the `INSERT` SQL without stripping `http(s)://` or paths (which the new `EmbeddableHost` model's `before_validation` does) or escaping quotes.

title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil and does not lowercase host for record_for_host
body: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally on lines 6-7, which raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` if `host` is `nil` instead of failing validation cleanly. Also, in `record_for_host` (lines 14-17), `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` compares `lower(host)` against `uri.host` without downcasing `uri.host` (or normalizing port numbers, which the format validator on line 2 allows in `EmbeddableHost#host` while `URI#host` strips the port), so uppercase characters in the input URL or a stored `:port` will cause `record_for_host` and `host_allowed?` to fail to match.

title: Contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was overwritten with `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` while the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were placed in `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. The two files have each other's contents.

title: Test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests what it describes
body: In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` line 1403, the spec `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` passes only because `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` defaults to `false` and `has_topic_embed?` is `false` on the unpersisted topic. `Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer checks `EmbeddableHost` at all (`SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`), so this test is misleading and redundant with the tests inside the `with an emeddable host` block.

title: Migration crashes on fresh or unconfigured databases when querying site_settings
body: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, lines 9-11 and line 15 index `[0]` directly on the PG::Result returned by `execute(...)`. On a fresh database or any installation where `embed_category` (or `uncategorized_category_id`) has never been saved to the `site_settings` table, the query returns 0 rows (`cmd_tuples == 0`), so `[0]` evaluates to `nil` and `[0]['id']` / `[0]['value']` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil:NilClass`, aborting `rake db:migrate`. Additionally, line 25 interpolates `#{h}` directly into the `INSERT` SQL without sanitizing or stripping `http(s)://` and paths (unlike `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation`), which will fail if a host contains a single quote or leave unnormalized hosts in the table.

title: `before_validation` raises NoMethodError when `host` is nil
body: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb` lines 6-7, the `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If `EmbeddableHost.new` is validated or saved with `host: nil` (for example via a malformed API request to `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`), `self.host` is `nil` and calling `.sub!` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` instead of failing validation cleanly.

title: `record_for_host` fails to match uppercase referer hostnames or configured ports
body: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb` line 17, `record_for_host` queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` where `host = uri.host`. Because Ruby's `URI.parse` preserves the case of the hostname, an incoming URL with uppercase characters in the host (e.g., `http://Example.com/post`) will compare `lower(host)` against `'Example.com'` and fail to match (`host.downcase` is needed). Furthermore, the format validator on line 2 explicitly allows a port in `EmbeddableHost#host` (e.g. `localhost:3000`), and `before_validation` does not strip ports, yet `uri.host` excludes the port, so any `EmbeddableHost` saved with a port will never match in `record_for_host`.

title: Contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` are swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was overwritten to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators. The two files have their contents swapped.

title: Misleading spec description in `expandable_first_post?` after removing `embeddable_hosts` check
body: In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` lines 1403-1405, the spec `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` only passes because `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` defaults to `false` and `topic.has_topic_embed?` is `false` on a new `Topic`. `Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer checks `EmbeddableHost` at all, so this test and the surrounding `describe 'with an emeddable host'` block no longer test what their descriptions claim.

title: Redefining `self.downsize` overwrites the 4-argument overload instead of overloading it
body: Ruby does not support method overloading by arity. Defining `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149 immediately overwrites `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined on line 145. Any existing caller passing `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` (or `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)`) will either bind `max_height` to `opts` (causing `NoMethodError` when `opts[:allow_animation]` is indexed on an Integer, and passing only `max_width` as the geometry string) or raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)`.

title: `gifsicle --resize-fit` does not accept percentage dimensions like `"80%"`
body: `UploadsController#create_upload` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. When the uploaded file has a `.gif` extension and `allow_animation` is true, `optimize` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which delegates to `resize_instructions_animated` and runs `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%`. In gifsicle, `--resize-fit` only accepts `WxH`, `Wx_`, or `_xH` pixel dimensions (percentages require `--scale 0.8`). Gifsicle exits with a non-zero status on `80%`, so animated GIFs larger than `max_image_size_kb` are never downsized across all 5 attempts and fail the upload.

title: Client-side size check ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` and `max_image_size_kb` > 10MB
body: `validateUploadedFile` replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB for all upload types. Because the server only downsizes images, non-image attachments between `max_attachment_size_kb` and 10 MB are no longer rejected before upload and will be uploaded in full only to fail on the server; conversely, if a site configures `max_attachment_size_kb` or `max_image_size_kb` above 10 MB, the client now blocks valid uploads.

title: Downsize loop ignores `OptimizedImage.downsize` failure and retries 5 times on unconvertible files
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` when `convert` or `gifsicle` fails (for example on SVG uploads, which `FileHelper.is_image?` treats as images, or corrupt image files). The `while` loop in `create_upload` does not check the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` or whether `tempfile.size` actually decreased, so it spawns the external command 5 times in a row with identical inputs before proceeding.

title: Redefining `self.downsize` overwrites the 4-argument version (Ruby has no method overloading)
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` is defined twice: first on line 145 with signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then again on line 149 with signature `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby does not support method overloading by arity, so the second definition completely replaces the first. Existing callers that pass `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` (or `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)`) will now either fail with `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)` or treat `max_height` as `opts` (causing `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` when `opts[:allow_animation]` is accessed) and pass only `max_width` as `dimensions`.

title: `gifsicle --resize-fit` does not accept percentage dimensions like `"80%"`
body: `UploadsController#create_upload` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. When `allow_animation` is true and the file has a `.gif` extension, `OptimizedImage.optimize` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which delegates to `resize_instructions_animated` and invokes `gifsicle ... --resize-fit #{dimensions}`. `gifsicle`'s `--resize-fit` only accepts `WxH` pixel dimensions (e.g. `100x100`, `_x100`, `100x_`), not a percentage like `80%` (for scaling, `gifsicle` uses `--scale 0.8`). As a result, `gifsicle` exits with a non-zero status on every iteration and animated GIFs larger than `max_image_size_kb` are never downsized.

title: Client-side size check ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` and `max_image_size_kb` site settings
body: `validateUploadedFile` previously checked `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, which enforced `max_attachment_size_kb` for non-image attachments and `max_image_size_kb` for images. Replacing it with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10 MB) means non-image attachments up to 10 MB now pass client-side validation even when `max_attachment_size_kb` is smaller (and the server does not downsize non-images, so the upload is uploaded in full only to be rejected server-side), and admins who configure `max_attachment_size_kb` or `max_image_size_kb` above 10 MB will have uploads blocked on the client with a misleading 10 MB limit error.

title: Redefining `self.downsize` overwrites the 4-5 argument version in Ruby
body: Ruby does not support method overloading by arity. Defining `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149 immediately overwrites `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined on line 145. Any existing caller passing `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` (or `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)`) will now either have `max_height` treated as `opts` (causing a `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` when `opts[:allow_animation]` is accessed on an Integer) or raise an `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)`.

title: Client-side size check ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` and server settings
body: Replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10 MB) disables the configured `max_attachment_size_kb` check on the client for non-image attachments (which are not downsized by the server), and also blocks uploads when an administrator has configured `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` higher than 10 MB.

title: Animated GIF downsizing fails because `gifsicle --resize-fit` does not accept percentage dimensions
body: When a GIF is uploaded and `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is enabled, `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which runs `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. `gifsicle`'s `--resize-fit` option requires `WxH` pixel dimensions (unlike `--scale`), so `gifsicle` fails with a non-zero exit status on every iteration and the loop runs 5 times without downsizing the GIF.

title: Nil dereference when TopicUser record does not exist on unsubscribe
body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` if the user has never visited or interacted with the topic (for example, if they were mentioned or invited in a topic they haven't opened yet, or received a mailing list notification before a `TopicUser` row existed). Accessing `tu.notification_level` on line 107 will then raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass`. In addition, directly mutating and saving `tu` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which sets `notifications_changed_at`, `notifications_reason_id`, creates the row if missing, and publishes the change on MessageBus.

title: Visiting the unsubscribe URL twice in a row mutes the topic instead of being idempotent
body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, if the user's notification level is `watching` or `tracking` (`> regular`), the first GET request lowers it to `regular`. If the user reloads the page, clicks the email link a second time, or if an email client / link scanner prefetches the GET URL before the user clicks it, the second GET sees `notification_level == regular` and takes the `else` branch, setting the level to `muted`. Moreover, when the user is already at `regular` (e.g. they received an email because they were `@mentioned` or quoted), unsubscribing mutes the topic, whereas when they were `watching` it only drops them to `regular` (where they will still receive `@mention`/reply emails despite the page saying "You will stop receiving notifications"). A GET unsubscribe endpoint should be idempotent and have consistent semantics.

title: `unsubscribe` raises NoMethodError when the user has no `TopicUser` row for the topic
body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` (for example, if a user receives an email via mailing-list mode on a new topic before visiting it, or navigates directly to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` without having previously visited or interacted with the topic). Calling `tu.notification_level` on line 107 will then raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass` and return a 500 error. Also, modifying `tu` directly bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row when absent, sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id`, and publishes the change on MessageBus.

title: State-changing `unsubscribe` action runs on GET and acts as a toggle on repeat visits
body: `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` mutates the user's notification level on a GET request and steps the level down on each request (`watching`/`tracking` -> `regular`, then `regular` -> `muted`). Because email scanners, link previewers, browser prefetching, or a user refreshing the page will issue additional GET requests, a user who was watching/tracking a topic and clicked the link expecting to drop to `regular` will instead be muted on the second GET. Additionally, when the user is navigated to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` via Ember client-side routing (or when `PostStream.loadTopicView` fetches `/t/:id.json`), the behavior between initial server render (which mutates via `TopicsController#unsubscribe`) and client-side transition (which calls `TopicsController#show` via `loadTopicView`) is inconsistent.

title: Nil dereference when `TopicUser` record does not exist
body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` if the user has never visited or interacted with the topic (for example, if they received the notification email via `mailing_list_mode`, were mentioned in a topic they haven't opened yet, or followed an unsubscribe link directly). Accessing `tu.notification_level` on line 107 will then raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass` and return a 500 error. Also, mutating and saving `tu` directly bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which sets `notifications_changed_at`, `notifications_reason_id`, and publishes the change on `MessageBus`.

title: GET request to `unsubscribe` mutates topic notification level without confirmation
body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is wired to a `GET` route (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) and immediately modifies the user's `TopicUser#notification_level` in the database. Furthermore, because the Ember `TopicUnsubscribeRoute` calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` (which fetches `/t/:id.json`) rather than `/unsubscribe`, and the HTML response preloads `topic_#{id}` with the already-mutated state, automated email link scanners, browser prefetchers, or accidental refreshes will change the user's notification level on a `GET` request (and a second hit will drop a `regular` user down to `muted`).

title: Client-side navigation to `/unsubscribe` does not actually unsubscribe
body: `TopicUnsubscribeRoute#model` calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)`, which only fetches the topic view (`/t/:id.json` or preloaded data) and never hits `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`. It only works on a full-page load because the Rails `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action runs on the initial HTML request and preloads the topic JSON. If the route is entered via a client-side transition, or if the user must log in first and is redirected back within the Ember app, `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is never called and the user's notification level is not changed, even though the template tells them they have stopped receiving notifications.

title: Case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` can be bypassed with uppercase characters
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?(email)` queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` using the raw `email` value without normalizing case (e.g., via `Email.downcase(email)`), and `BlockedEmail` does not downcase `email` before saving. On PostgreSQL, string comparisons on `varchar` columns are case-sensitive, and `User` does not downcase `email` before running validations during signup (`User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` directly). As a result, a blocked address such as `bad@spammers.org` can bypass the block simply by signing up with `Bad@spammers.org`.

title: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` is called twice during signup, double-incrementing `match_count`
body: `User` runs `EmailValidator` on every validation call (`validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?`), and `EmailValidator` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, which mutates the database by incrementing `match_count` and updating `last_match_at`. In `UsersController#create` (lines 168 and 172), `user.valid?` is called when `SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` is enabled, followed immediately by `user.save` (which runs validations again). For a blocked email, `should_block?` will execute on `user.valid?` and again on `user.save`, incrementing `match_count` twice for a single signup attempt (and also incrementing it on non-persisting `valid?` checks).

title: Case-sensitive email lookup allows bypassing blocked emails
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` without normalizing the case of `email` (e.g., via `Email.downcase(email)`), and `BlockedEmail` does not normalize `email` before saving either. In PostgreSQL, `=` on `varchar` is case-sensitive, and `User.new_from_params` does not downcase `params[:email]` before running validations. As a result, a blocked address like `bad@spammer.com` can be bypassed simply by signing up with `Bad@spammer.com`.

title: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` mutates match statistics every time validation runs
body: `EmailValidator` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` during standard ActiveRecord validation, and `should_block?` increments `match_count` and updates `last_match_at` in the database on every call. In `UsersController#create`, `user.valid?` is called on line 168 and `user.save` (which runs validations again) is called on line 172. For an email with `action_type == :do_nothing` (or whenever validations are invoked multiple times during a request), `match_count` will be incremented multiple times for a single signup attempt.

title: `change_email` does not check `EmailValidator` / `BlockedEmail` before sending confirmation email
body: In `UsersController#change_email`, an `EmailToken` is created and an authorization email is enqueued without validating the new address against `EmailValidator` or `BlockedEmail` (unless `EmailToken` itself runs `EmailValidator`, which is only added to `User` in this PR). Even if `EmailToken.confirm` later fails when updating `user.email`, the system still sends an email to the blocked address and only fails at confirmation time.

title: Case-sensitive email lookup and storage allows trivial bypass of blocked emails
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` without normalizing the email address (e.g., via `Email.downcase(email)`), and `BlockedEmail` does not normalize `email` before saving or validating uniqueness. On PostgreSQL (Discourse's database), `=` on `varchar` is case-sensitive, and `UsersController#create` passes `params[:email]` directly to `User.new_from_params` without downcasing it first. As a result, a blocked address like `bad@spammers.org` can be bypassed during signup simply by entering `Bad@spammers.org`.

title: Validation mutates BlockedEmail match_count multiple times per signup attempt
body: `EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` during ActiveRecord validation, which increments `match_count` and saves the `BlockedEmail` record every time `valid?` runs. In `UsersController#create`, `user.valid?` is called on line 168 (when `SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` is enabled) and then `user.save` runs validations again on line 172. Any caller that checks `valid?` before `save` will increment `match_count` multiple times for a single signup attempt, and read-only validation checks unexpectedly perform database writes.

title: Invalid Ruby syntax `<%- end if %>` causes template rendering to fail
