body: Line 6 closes the `if` block with `<%- end if %>`, which is invalid Ruby syntax (`end` followed by an incomplete `if` modifier with no expression). In Ruby/ERB, conditional blocks are closed with `end`, not `end if`. Rendering `embed/best.html.erb` will raise a `SyntaxError` whenever a topic embed is found and displayed.

title: `raw_html` cook method bypasses all HTML sanitization, enabling stored XSS
body: When `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly without passing through `PrettyText.cook` or any HTML sanitizer. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using raw HTML from RSS/Atom feeds (`Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` unescapes feed item content directly via `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` without sanitization), and any user who can later edit that post (or any post with `cook_method == raw_html`) can also inject arbitrary `<script>` tags or event handlers that will be stored in `cooked` and rendered unescaped to all viewers.

title: Unvalidated `embed_url` passed to `Kernel#open` allows SSRF and arbitrary command/file read
body: In `EmbedController#best`, the user-supplied `params[:embed_url]` is enqueued to `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`. `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` checks `URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, which does not restrict the URI scheme or port (for example, `ftp://`, `gopher://`, or arbitrary internal ports if the host resolves Internally or via DNS rebinding), and in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (which is also callable directly) `open(url).read` uses `Kernel#open` (`open-uri`). If `import_remote` is ever called with a string starting with `|` or a `file://` URL, `Kernel#open` will execute a shell command or read local files. Even through `TopicRetriever`, `URI.parse` allows any scheme with a matching host. `embed_url` should be restricted to `http`/`https` schemes and fetched with an HTTP client rather than `Kernel#open`.

title: Unescaped `request.referer` interpolated into JavaScript string literal allows XSS
body: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, `request.referer` is interpolated directly into a single-quoted JavaScript string: `'<%= request.referer %>'`. `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` only validates that `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Because `URI.parse` allows single quotes in the path or query string (or in browsers that do not percent-encode them in the `Referer` header), a referer such as `http://<embeddable_host>/?a='+alert(1)+'` will break out of the JS string literal and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the Discourse origin. Use `.to_json` (or pass the origin constructed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) instead of raw ERB interpolation.

title: `i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds that use `<description>`, causing `NoMethodError`
body: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, line 35 calls `i.content.scrub`. In `SimpleRSS`, `item.content` only maps to Atom `<content>` or `<content:encoded>`; standard RSS 2.0 items that only provide `<description>` have `i.content == nil` (with the body in `i.description`). Calling `.scrub` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass` and aborts the entire feed poll.

title: `TopicEmbed.import` mutates the caller's `contents` string in place
body: Line 13 uses `contents << ...` to append the 'Imported from' footer, mutating the string argument in place. If the caller passes a frozen string, this raises `RuntimeError: can't modify frozen String`; if the caller reuses the string (as in `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`), the footer is appended multiple times. Use `contents = "#{contents}..."` or `contents + ...` instead.

title: Invalid Ruby syntax `<%- end if %>` causes template compilation/runtime error
body: In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` line 6, the conditional block is closed with `<%- end if %>`. `end if` is not valid Ruby syntax for closing an `if` block (unless followed by a modifier condition) and will raise a `SyntaxError` when Rails compiles and renders the `embed/best` template. Replace `<%- end if %>` with `<%- end %>`.

title: Posts with `raw_html` cook_method bypass HTML sanitization when edited by users
body: `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly without sanitization or filtering whenever `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. While initial creation happens through `TopicEmbed.import`, the resulting post is a normal first post in a forum topic that can be edited by its author (`embed_by_username`) or any moderator/admin, or even wiki-edited if made a wiki. Any subsequent edit through standard post revision (`PostRevisor`) keeps `cook_method` as `raw_html` and sets `cooked = raw` verbatim, allowing unsanitized `<script>` tags and arbitrary HTML (stored XSS) into the forum and the embed view. Furthermore, RSS feed contents in `PollFeed` are not sanitized at all before being imported with `raw_html`, so any script or event handler in the RSS feed is rendered directly inside Discourse.

title: `PollFeed#poll_feed` crashes with `NoMethodError` when RSS items use `<description>` instead of `<content>`
body: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` line 35, `i.content.scrub` is called unconditionally on each item returned by `SimpleRSS`. Standard RSS 2.0 feeds typically populate `i.description` (or `i.content_encoded`) rather than `i.content`, leaving `i.content` as `nil`. Calling `.scrub` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass` and aborts the entire feed polling job.

title: `TopicEmbed.import` mutates the caller's `contents` string in place
body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends the `imported_from` footer using `contents << ...`, mutating the string passed by the caller (and will raise `RuntimeError: can't modify frozen String` if a frozen string is passed). Use `contents = contents + ...` instead of `<<`.

title: Loop variable `post` overwrites the topic's root post and breaks subsequent iterations on failure
body: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` line 148, `post` holds the root post created by `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. Inside the `t[:posts].each` loop on line 174, `post = PostCreator.new(post_user, attrs).create` overwrites that outer `post` variable. If `PostCreator#create` fails validation (for example, a short comment failing `min_post_length`, since `skip_validations: true` is not passed), `post` becomes an unsaved post or `nil`, and `post.post_number` / `post.topic_id` on subsequent iterations (and `post.topic` on line 177) will either be `nil` or raise a `NoMethodError`. Additionally, `attrs` passes `cooked: p[:cooked]`, which `PostCreator#setup_post` ignores.

title: Using `Kernel#open` on `url` allows command injection / local file read if URL validation is bypassed
body: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (line 48) and `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (line 29), `open(...)` from `open-uri` is called directly. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does not validate that `url` begins with `http://` or `https://` before calling `open(url).read` (the regex check only happens later inside `TopicEmbed.import`). If a caller passes a string starting with `|` or a local path (e.g. from a Disqus XML file `<link>` element in `disqus.thor` or `feed_polling_url`), `Kernel#open` can execute arbitrary shell commands or read local files. Parse with `URI.parse` and restrict to `URI::HTTP`/`URI::HTTPS` before opening.

title: Unescaped `request.referer` interpolated into JavaScript string in `embed.html.erb`
body: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` line 11, `<%= request.referer %>` is interpolated directly inside a single-quoted JavaScript string literal: `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. Although `ensure_embeddable` checks `URI(request.referer).host`, the path or query portion of a valid URI can still contain characters (or `</script>`) that break out of the JS string or script block when rendered into HTML. Use `to_json` / `escape_javascript` or construct the origin from the validated scheme, host, and port.

title: Invalid Ruby syntax `<%- end if %>` in ERB template causes SyntaxError
body: Line 6 closes the `if` block with `<%- end if %>`, which is not valid Ruby syntax (Ruby uses `end`, not `end if`). When `EmbedController#best` renders `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, ERB compilation will fail with a `SyntaxError` because `if` has no condition following `end`.

title: `raw_html` cook method bypasses HTML sanitization and post filters, enabling stored XSS
body: When `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly without passing it through `Sanitize` or `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. Posts imported via `Jobs::PollFeed` (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36`) pass raw RSS `<content>` directly into `TopicEmbed.import` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Any `<script>` tags, inline event handlers (`onload`, `onerror`), or `javascript:` URLs in the RSS feed (or if a regular user edits a `raw_html` post) will be stored verbatim in `cooked` and rendered unescaped to all users viewing the topic.

title: `Kernel#open` called with external URL allows command/file read injection and SSRF
body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` (via `open-uri`) on `url`. While `TopicRetriever` checks that `URI(embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, `URI('http://allowed-host/|malicious_command').host` or similar tricks, or callers like `Disqus#import` (`lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148`) that pass URLs from an XML export without any scheme/host validation, can pass strings starting with `|` or local file paths to `Kernel#open`, leading to arbitrary command execution or local file disclosure. Even with HTTP URLs, `open-uri` follows redirects to `file://` or internal network hosts (SSRF) if `embeddable_host` redirects. Use `URI.parse(url).open` (or `Net::HTTP` / `RestClient`) after verifying the scheme is `http` or `https`.

title: `TopicEmbed.import` mutates the caller's `contents` string in place, breaking frozen strings
body: `TopicEmbed.import` uses `contents << ...` to append the imported-from footer, which mutates the `contents` argument in place. If a caller passes a frozen string or reuses the string across calls, this will raise `RuntimeError: can't modify frozen String` or append duplicate footers. Use `contents = "#{contents}\n<hr>..."` or `contents = contents.dup << ...` instead.

title: `PollFeed#poll_feed` crashes with `NoMethodError` when RSS items use `<description>` instead of `<content>` or on Ruby < 2.1
body: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35`, `i.content.scrub` assumes two things that frequently do not hold: (1) standard RSS 2.0 feeds populate `i.description` rather than `i.content`, so `i.content` is `nil` and calling `.scrub` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass`; (2) `String#scrub` was only introduced in Ruby 2.1, whereas this repo supports Ruby 1.9/2.0 (see `Gemfile` line 213). Fallback to `i.description` when `i.content` is blank and guard against `nil`.

title: Adding `force: true` to an existing migration will drop `top_topics` data if re-run
body: `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` is an existing migration unrelated to topic embeds, and changing `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` causes the table to be dropped and recreated if the migration is run against a database that already has `top_topics`. This looks like an accidental leftover from local migration testing.

title: `order` mixin passes 0-indexed value to 1-indexed `box-ordinal-group`
body: In the 2009 flexbox specification (`-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group`), ordinal groups are 1-indexed (default is `1`, and `0` or negative values are invalid), whereas standard `order` / `-ms-flex-order` / `-webkit-order` are 0-indexed (default is `0`). Passing `$val` directly to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` means `@include order(0)` produces an invalid rule in older WebKit/Firefox browsers, and positive values are off by one relative to un-ordered siblings (which default to group 1). Those two properties should use `$val + 1`.

title: `include_website_name` is missing `?` and is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`
body: `UserSerializer` defines `def include_website_name` (without a trailing `?`), whereas ActiveModel::Serializers checks `include_<attr>?` to decide whether to serialize an attribute. Because the `?` is missing, `website_name` is always included in the serialized JSON (as `nil` when the user has no website). In addition, `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` so that it is hidden for TL0 users when viewed by anonymous visitors (`scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`), but `website_name` is not added to `untrusted_attributes`. As a result, a TL0 user's website domain/path is leaked via `website_name` to anonymous users even when `website` itself is suppressed. Adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (and removing the broken `include_website_name` method, since `untrusted_attributes` already defines `include_website_name?`) fixes both issues.

title: `website_name` is not updated on the client after saving user preferences
body: Previously, `websiteName` was a computed property on the controller observing `model.website`, so editing and saving `website` in user preferences immediately updated the displayed website name on the profile page. Now that `website_name` is computed server-side in `UserSerializer`, `User#save` (around line 210, where `self.set('bio_excerpt', data.user.bio_excerpt)` is updated from the PUT response) does not copy `data.user.website_name` back onto the model. After a user updates their `website` in preferences and navigates back to their profile without a full page reload, the profile will continue displaying the stale `website_name` (or nothing if they previously had no website).

title: `include_website_name` is missing `?` and bypasses `untrusted_attributes` restrictions
body: ActiveModel::Serializer requires conditional inclusion methods to be named `include_<attribute>?` (with a trailing question mark). Because `def include_website_name` is missing `?`, AMS ignores it and always includes `website_name` in the serialized JSON (as `nil` when no website is set). Furthermore, `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) so that it is hidden for TL0 users when viewed by anonymous users (`scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`), and `untrusted_attributes` automatically defines `include_<attr>?` for every attribute passed to it. Adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (and removing the manual `include_website_name` method) fixes both the missing `?` and the leak of TL0 users' websites to anonymous visitors.

title: `User#save` does not update `website_name` from the server response
body: Previously `websiteName` was a computed property on the controller observing `model.website`, so editing and saving a user's `website` in preferences immediately updated the displayed website name on their profile. Now that `website_name` is computed on the server in `UserSerializer`, `User#save` (lines 206-214) only copies `bio_excerpt` from `data.user` back onto the model (`self.set('bio_excerpt', data.user.bio_excerpt)`). After saving preferences, `model.website_name` on the client remains stale (or `undefined` if a website was newly added) until a full page reload.

title: `website_name` is missing `?` on its `include_` method and is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`
body: `UserSerializer` defines `def include_website_name` without a trailing question mark (ActiveModel::Serializer requires `include_website_name?`), and does not include `:website_name` in the `untrusted_attributes` list on line 105 (which already includes `:website`). Because `include_website_name?` is never defined, AMS always serializes `website_name`—even as `nil` when a user has no website, and even for TL0 users viewed by anonymous visitors when `restrict_user_fields?` is true, leaking the user's website domain/path despite `website` itself being suppressed (`user.hbs` renders `{{model.website_name}}` whenever it is truthy). Adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (and removing the broken `include_website_name` method) fixes both issues.

title: Saving user preferences does not update `website_name` on the client model
body: Previously `websiteName` was a computed property on the user controller observing `model.website`, so editing and saving the `website` field in user preferences immediately updated the displayed website name on the profile page without a reload. Now `website_name` is computed server-side in `UserSerializer`, but `User#save` (around line 210 of `user.js.es6`) only copies `bio_excerpt` from the `PUT /users/:username` response back onto the model (`self.set('bio_excerpt', data.user.bio_excerpt)`). After a user updates their `website` in preferences and navigates back to their profile, `model.website_name` remains stale (or undefined if they had no website before) until a full page refresh.

title: Unintended lightness change for `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`
body: In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` line 291, `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the diff inverted the lightness values and changed the light-theme branch to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and the dark-theme branch to `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)`. body: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss` line 102, `.custom-message-length` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, swapping the 70% and 30% lightness arguments. body: In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss` line 522, `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` instead of `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. body: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss` line 182, `.topic-map h3` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` instead of `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))` (which is what `desktop/topic-post.scss` line 321 and `mobile/topic-post.scss` line 247 use). This makes `.topic-map h3` lighter on light themes and removes the contrast difference between `h3` and `h4`.

title: totalPages calculation is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` computes `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (for example, `user_count = 50` and `limit = 50`), this evaluates to `2` instead of `1`. This causes the UI to display `1/2` and enables the `next` button, which then fetches an empty second page (`offset = 50`). It should be `Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"))` (or `Math.floor((user_count - 1) / limit) + 1`).

title: alias_level is ignored when creating a group
body: The `Admin::GroupsController#create` action sets `group.name` and `group.visible` from `params`, but never assigns `group.alias_level`, even though the admin group creation form displays the alias level selector and `Discourse.Group#asJSON` sends `alias_level` in the `POST /admin/groups` payload. Any alias level selected while creating a new group is silently discarded and reset to the database default.

title: Adding an existing member to a group raises a uniqueness/duplicate key error
body: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `group.add(user)` (`group.users.push(user)`) is called for each resolved username without checking whether the user is already a member of the group (`group.users.include?(user)` or `GroupUser.exists?(group_id: group.id, user_id: user.id)`). If an admin submits a username that is already in the group (or duplicates a username in the comma-separated list), inserting the duplicate `group_users` record will fail with a database uniqueness constraint violation (`ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`) and return a 500 error.

title: Unbounded and unvalidated limit/offset parameters in GroupsController#members
body: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed directly to ActiveRecord without bounds checking. A client can pass a huge `limit` (e.g., `limit=1000000`) to force loading and serializing all users at once, or a negative `limit`/`offset` which causes Postgres to raise an `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` (`LIMIT/OFFSET must not be negative`) resulting in an unhandled 500 error.

title: Group members page fails to render members because GroupMembersController is an ArrayController
body: `GroupMembersRoute` sets the `Group` model (a `Discourse.Model`, not an array) as the `model` of `GroupMembersController`, and this template was changed from `{{#each m in model}}` to `{{#each m in members}}`. Unless `GroupMembersController` is an `ObjectController` (in Discourse it defaults to/is an `ArrayController` when not defined as `ObjectController`), property lookup for `members` on the controller will not proxy to `model.members`, leaving the member list blank on `/groups/:name/members` (`model.members` would be needed or an `ObjectController`).

title: Off-by-one error in totalPages calculation when user_count is a multiple of limit
body: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (for example, 50 users with a limit of 50), this returns `2` instead of `1`, allowing the user to paginate to an empty second page. It should use `Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"))` (or `Math.floor((user_count - 1) / limit) + 1`).

title: Admin::GroupsController#create ignores alias_level parameter
body: In `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb`, the `create` action sets `group.name` and `group.visible` from `params`, but never assigns `group.alias_level` even though the admin form displays the alias level selector on new groups and `Discourse.Group#asJSON` sends `alias_level` in the POST payload. Any alias level chosen when creating a group is silently discarded.

title: Adding an already-existing group member raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
body: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `group.add(user)` (which does `group.users.push(user)`) is called for each username without checking whether the user is already a member of the group (`group.users.include?(user)` or `group.group_users.where(user_id: user.id).exists?`). If an admin submits a username that is already in the group, the uniqueness constraint on `group_users (group_id, user_id)` raises an unhandled `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (500 error) instead of ignoring the duplicate or returning a validation error.

title: Unbounded and negative limit/offset parameters in GroupsController#members
body: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed directly to `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` without bounds checking. A client can pass a very large `limit` to load and serialize all users in a large group in a single request, or pass negative values which cause Postgres to raise an `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` (`LIMIT/OFFSET must not be negative`). `limit` should be clamped (e.g. between 1 and a maximum like 1000) and `offset` should be clamped to `>= 0`.

title: Off-by-one error in totalPages when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (for example, 50 members with the default limit of 50), this returns `2` instead of `1`. Consequently `showingLast` (`currentPage === totalPages`) is false on the last real page, allowing the user to click "Next" to an empty page where `offset` equals `user_count`. It should use `Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"))` (or `Math.floor((user_count - 1) / limit) + 1`).

title: Admin::GroupsController#create ignores alias_level parameter
body: `Discourse.Group#asJSON` sends `name`, `alias_level`, and `visible` when creating a new group via `POST /admin/groups`, and the admin group form allows selecting an `alias_level` before saving a new group. However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `group.name` and `group.visible` and never reads `params[:alias_level]`. Any alias level chosen when creating a group is silently discarded and has to be set again in a subsequent update.

title: GroupsController#members allows unbounded or negative limit and offset
body: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed directly to ActiveRecord `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` without bounds checking. A client can pass a very large `limit` (e.g. `limit=1000000`) to load and serialize all users in a large group in one request, or pass a negative `limit`/`offset` which causes PostgreSQL to raise an `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` (`LIMIT must not be negative` / `OFFSET must not be negative`) resulting in an unhandled 500 error.

title: Adding an already-present member in add_members raises a uniqueness constraint error
body: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `group.add(user)` (`group.users.push(user)`) is called for each username without checking whether the user is already a member of the group. `GroupUser` has a unique index on `(group_id, user_id)`, so if any of the submitted usernames is already in the group (or if the same username appears twice in `usernames`), `group.add(user)` raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and returns a 500 error instead of skipping existing members.

title: I18n::Backend::Fallbacks included before translate_accelerator monkey-patch breaks lazy loading of fallback locales
body: `config/initializers/i18n.rb` includes `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` into `I18n::Backend::Simple` (line 9), which overrides `translate` to loop over `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` and call `super(fallback, key, options)`. However, `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` only wraps the top-level `I18n.translate` (line 67) to lazy-load `I18n.config.locale`, and `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only called in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any translation performed outside a controller request (e.g. background Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console, or explicit `I18n.t(key, locale: ...)` calls) will not have called `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, so fallback locales (including `:en` or `SiteSetting.default_locale`) will not be loaded in `I18n.backend` and translations will raise/return missing-translation errors instead of falling back.

title: Symbol vs String mismatch in `@loaded_locales` causes redundant locale reloading
body: `I18n.ensure_loaded!(locale)` checks `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` and `load_locale` appends `locale` as passed. `FallbackLocaleList#[]` returns symbols (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`, though `locale` itself may be a String or Symbol depending on caller), while `I18n.config.locale` in `translate` is always a Symbol (because `I18n.locale=` converts to `to_sym`). If `ensure_loaded!` is called with a String (or if `FallbackLocaleList[locale]` receives a String `locale`), `@loaded_locales` will contain both `'en'` and `:en`, causing `load_locale` to reload and re-parse all YAML translation files for that locale a second time. `ensure_loaded!` / `load_locale` (and `FallbackLocaleList#[]` on line 17 of `config/initializers/i18n.rb`) should normalize `locale = locale.to_sym`.

title: Translation LRU cache key does not account for changes to `SiteSetting.default_locale`
body: In `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` line 72, cached translations are keyed only by `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With `FallbackLocaleList` dynamically reading `SiteSetting.default_locale` on every lookup (`config/initializers/i18n.rb` line 17), a translation for a user locale that falls back to `SiteSetting.default_locale` will be permanently cached under the user's locale in `@cache` even if an admin changes `SiteSetting.default_locale`.

title: Fallback locales are not loaded outside of web requests (e.g. background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, or I18n.with_locale)
body: `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` is only called from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Because `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` lazily loads locale YAML files on demand and `I18n.translate` (line 68) only loads `config.locale` and not its fallbacks, any translation performed outside a controller request (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, scheduled tasks, console, specs) or inside an `I18n.with_locale(...)` block will not have the fallback locales (`SiteSetting.default_locale` and `:en`) loaded into `I18n.backend`. When a key is missing in the active locale, `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` will query the backend for the fallback locales without triggering `load_locale`, finding no translations loaded for them and returning a missing-translation result instead of falling back.

title: Translation LRU cache is not invalidated and does not key on SiteSetting.default_locale
body: `I18n.translate` caches parameterless translations under the key `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With `FallbackLocaleList` now using `SiteSetting.default_locale` as the intermediate fallback before `:en`, changing `SiteSetting.default_locale` at runtime will leave stale fallback results in `@cache` for any user locale that fell back to the previous site default locale, and may also serve lookups from before the new default locale's YAML files were loaded.

title: Including I18n::Backend::Fallbacks into I18n::Backend::Simple breaks lazy loading of fallback locales
body: `config/initializers/i18n.rb` includes `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` into `I18n.backend.class` (`I18n::Backend::Simple`), while `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` only ensures the primary `config.locale` is loaded when `I18n.translate` is called (and `ApplicationController#set_locale` only runs during controller requests, not in background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, or specs, nor when `I18n.t(key, locale: ...)` is called with an explicit locale). When a translation is missing in the primary locale and falls back to `SiteSetting.default_locale` or `:en`, `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` iterates over `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` and calls `super` directly on the backend, bypassing `I18n.translate` and its `load_locale` hook. If a fallback locale has not been loaded yet, the backend has no translations for it in memory and the lookup fails with `I18n::MissingTranslationData` instead of returning the fallback translation.

title: Translation cache is not invalidated when SiteSetting.default_locale changes
body: `I18n.translate` caches results in `@cache` keyed only by `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With `FallbackLocaleList` now dynamically resolving fallbacks using `SiteSetting.default_locale`, changing `SiteSetting.default_locale` at runtime will not invalidate `@cache`, so previously cached fallback translations for a user's locale will continue to serve values from the old `default_locale` (or cached values from before a fallback locale was loaded).

title: No specs added for fallback locale resolution or FallbackLocaleList
body: This PR introduces custom server-side locale fallback behavior (`FallbackLocaleList`, `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, and controller integration) without any unit or integration tests verifying that missing translations fall back from user locale to `SiteSetting.default_locale` and then to `:en`.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type and uses raw UserUID, causing cross-identity collisions
body:
`userPermDenialCacheKey` is constructed using `checkReq.UserUID` directly without incorporating `checkReq.IdentityType` or resolving `checkReq.UserUID` to the canonical `userIdentifiers.UID`. This causes two problems:
1. Different identity types can share the same `UserUID` (e.g., `anonymous:0`, `render:0`, `user:0`, or `service-account:0` all have `UserUID == "0"`). If `anonymous:0` is denied access to a resource (such as `dashboards:read`), that denial is cached under `0` and will subsequently block `render:0` or `user:0` from accessing the same resource until the cache expires.
2. `GetUserIdentifiers` accepts either a numeric internal ID or a string UID, and `permCache` keys on the resolved `userIdentifiers.UID`. Because `permDenialCache` keys on the raw `checkReq.UserUID`, denial cache entries will not be shared between requests using the numeric ID and requests using the string UID.

title: Outdated folder tree cache prevents newly created subfolders or items in new subfolders from being accessed
body: When a permission check against `cachedPerms` returns `false`, `Check` re-queries user permissions from the database via `getIdentityPermissions` and re-runs `checkPermission`. However, `checkPermission` calls `checkInheritedPermissions` -> `buildFolderTree`, which still reads from `s.folderCache` without invalidating or bypassing it. If a user creates a subfolder inside a folder they have permissions on (where access is granted via inheritance from the parent folder rather than a direct permission on the new subfolder) or creates a dashboard inside a newly created subfolder, `buildFolderTree` will return the stale cached folder tree that does not contain the new subfolder, causing `Check` to return `Allowed: false` and cache the denial in `permDenialCache` for `shortCacheTTL`.

title: Test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' sets permission map value to false instead of true
body: In `TestService_CacheCheck` ('Should deny on explicit cache deny entry'), the comment states `// Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked`, but line 982 sets `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`. Even if `permDenialCache` were completely ignored, `permCache` would still evaluate to `false` (and fall through to the empty `fakeStore`, which also returns `false`). To actually verify that `permDenialCache` takes precedence over `permCache`, the map value in `permCache` must be `true`.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type and uses unnormalized user identifier, causing cross-identity collisions
body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` is built in `Check` from `checkReq.UserUID` (the raw identifier parsed from `req.Subject`) without including `checkReq.IdentityType` or normalizing `UserUID` via `GetUserIdentifiers` (unlike `permCache`, which uses `userIdentifiers.UID`). Because `validateSubject` accepts `user`, `service-account`, `anonymous`, and `render` subjects, two different principals with the same identifier (for example `anonymous:0` vs `render:0`, or `user:1` vs `service-account:1`, or a user referenced by numeric ID `1` in one call and UID `u1` in another) share or split the same denial cache key `<ns>.perm_<id>_<action>_<name>_<parent>`. An unprivileged `anonymous:0` check that is denied will populate `permDenialCache` and cause subsequent `render:0` checks for the same resource to be denied for up to `shortCacheTTL`, and a denial recorded under a user's numeric ID will be bypassed when the same user is checked by UID.

title: Stale folder tree cache causes false denial and caches the denial when a newly created subfolder is checked
body: When `Check` misses `permCache` (or the cached permissions do not grant access) and falls back to `getIdentityPermissions`, the subsequent `s.checkPermission(ctx, permissions, checkReq)` still evaluates inherited folder permissions against `s.buildFolderTree`, which returns the cached `folderCache` entry without refreshing it. If a user creates a subfolder under a folder they have permissions on (where permissions are inherited from the parent folder rather than granted directly on the new subfolder) and immediately accesses the new subfolder or a dashboard inside it, `tree.Ancestors(req.ParentFolder)` will not find the newly created folder in the cached tree, `checkPermission` will return `false`, and line 154 will cache that false result in `permDenialCache` for 30 seconds.

title: Denial cache test sets `dashboards:uid:dash1` to `false` instead of `true` in `permCache`
body: In `TestService_CacheCheck` ("Should deny on explicit cache deny entry"), the comment states "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but line 982 sets `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`. Even if `permDenialCache` were bypassed and `permCache` were consulted, `checkPermission` would still return `false` (and with an empty `fakeStore`, the DB fallback would also return `false`), so the test would pass even if `permDenialCache` did nothing. The map value should be `true`.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type and does not normalize user identifier, causing cross-identity collisions
body:
`userPermDenialCacheKey` in `Check` is constructed using the raw `checkReq.UserUID` from `types.ParseTypeID(subject)` without including `checkReq.IdentityType` or normalizing user IDs via `GetUserIdentifiers` (unlike `permCache`, which resolves `userIdentifiers.UID`). Because subjects can be `anonymous:0`, `render:0`, `user:<id_or_uid>`, or `service-account:<id_or_uid>`, two problems occur:
1. If an anonymous check (`subject = "anonymous:0"`) is denied for a resource, `permDenialKey` is cached with `UserUID = "0"`. A subsequent check for `render:0` on the same resource will hit this denial cache entry and be falsely denied.
2. If a user or service account is checked by numeric ID (`user:42`) and denied, and is later checked by UID (`user:uid42`), or vice versa, they produce different denial cache keys.

Include the identity type (or canonical subject) and the resolved `userIdentifiers.UID` when building `permDenialKey`.

title: Cached folder tree is not refreshed on permission cache miss, breaking access to newly created nested folders/dashboards
body: The goal of this PR is to allow users to access newly created dashboards and folders by falling back to the database when the cached permissions do not grant access. However, on the fallback path in `Check`, `getIdentityPermissions` refreshes `permCache` from the DB, and then `checkPermission` -> `checkInheritedPermissions` -> `buildFolderTree` still reads from `s.folderCache` without bypassing it. If a user has permission on a parent folder (`folders:uid:parent`), creates a subfolder `child` inside `parent`, and then creates or accesses a dashboard inside `child` while `folderCache` is already populated, `tree.Ancestors("child")` will not find `parent` in the stale cached folder tree, `checkPermission` will return `false`, and that denial will then be written into `permDenialCache` for `shortCacheTTL` (30s).

title: Test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' sets permCache value to false instead of true
body: In `TestService_CacheCheck` / `Should deny on explicit cache deny entry`, line 982 sets `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}` with the comment `// Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked`. Because the map value is `false` (and no fakeStore permissions are configured), `s.Check` would return `Allowed: false` even if `permDenialCache` were completely ignored. The map value should be `true` to actually verify that `permDenialCache` takes precedence over `permCache`.

title: Missing React `key` prop on `GrafanaRuleListItem` in `rules.map()`
body: In `FilterViewResults`, when replacing `<GrafanaRuleLoader>` with `<GrafanaRuleListItem>`, the `key={key}` prop was removed. Because `GrafanaRuleListItem` is returned directly from `rules.map(...)`, omitting `key` will cause React to emit a missing-key warning and can lead to incorrect component state reconciliation when the filtered rule list updates.

title: Silence notifications action is broken in list view when `rulerRule` is omitted
body: In the new alert list view (`GrafanaRuleListItem`), `RuleActionsButtons` is rendered with only `promRule` and `rule` (`rulerRule`) is `undefined`. `AlertRuleMenu` computes `canSilence` using `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(promRule, ...)` and renders the "Silence notifications" menu item, which calls `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)` on click. However, `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` on line 104 is gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, which evaluates to `false` when `rule` is `undefined`. Clicking "Silence notifications" in the list view will do nothing because the drawer never renders.

title: Pause and Delete menu items are never rendered when only `promRule` is provided
body: `AlertRuleMenu` was updated to compute `canPause` and `canDelete` from `promRule` via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` when `rulerRule` is not passed (as in `GrafanaRuleListItem`). However, the JSX conditions for rendering those menu items still require `rulerRule`: line 123 checks `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and line 165 checks `canDelete && rulerRule`. Consequently, for Grafana rules in the list view where `rulerRule` is `undefined`, the Pause and Delete actions will never appear in the menu despite permissions being checked.

title: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` disallows Pause, Restore, ModifyExport, and DeletePermanently on recording rules
body: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `isAlertingRule` (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`) is used to gate `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore`, and `DeletePermanently` (lines 324-330). In `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, those actions are gated on `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule` (`rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`), which is true for both Grafana alerting rules and Grafana recording rules. Using `alertingRule` instead of ` prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` unintentionally disables these abilities for Grafana-managed recording rules.

title: `AlertRuleAction.Silence` ability is marked allowed before folder permissions finish loading
body: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `[AlertRuleAction.Silence]` is set to `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]`. Unlike `useCanSilence` (which returns `[false, false]` when `!rule || folderIsLoading || !folder`), this does not check whether `folder` has loaded or exists, and `useCanSilenceInFolder` returns `true` whenever the user has global `AlertingInstanceCreate` permission even if `folder` is still loading or `undefined` (including when `skipToken` is passed, although `isAlertingRule` happens to be `false` then). If a user has global `AlertingInstanceCreate` but the folder doesn't exist or is still loading, `Silence` will be reported as supported and allowed inconsistently with `useCanSilence`.

title: `returnTo` query parameter lost in rule view link
body: In the removed `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`, the rule view link was constructed with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. In the new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx`, `{ returnTo }` was dropped (`createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)`), breaking the "Back to list" navigation from the rule details view when navigating from the rule list or filter view.

title: Missing `key` prop on `GrafanaRuleListItem` inside list `.map()`
body: In `FilterViewResults`, when replacing `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ... />` with `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` inside `rules.map(...)`, the `key={key}` prop was dropped. `key` is still destructured from `ruleWithOrigin` on line 152, and not passing it to `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` causes a React missing-key warning and can lead to incorrect component reconciliation when the filtered rule list updates.

title: Silence notifications menu item does nothing in the alert list view when `rulerRule` is omitted
body: In the new list view (`GrafanaRuleListItem`), `RuleActionsButtons` is rendered with only `promRule` and `rule` (`rulerRule`) is `undefined`. `AlertRuleMenu` now uses `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` on `promRule` to compute `canSilence`, so the "Silence notifications" menu item is displayed and clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer` to `true`. However, `RuleActionsButtons` still gates rendering `<SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer>` on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` (line 104), which is `false` when `rule` is `undefined`. As a result, clicking "Silence notifications" on a Grafana rule in the alert list view silently does nothing.

title: Pause and Delete menu items are hidden for Grafana rules in the alert list view
body: `AlertRuleMenu` was updated to compute `canPause` and `canDelete` from `promRule` via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` when `rulerRule` is not provided (as in `GrafanaRuleListItem`). However, the JSX conditions rendering the menu items still require `rulerRule` to be defined: line 123 checks `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && ...` and line 165 checks `canDelete && rulerRule`. Because `GrafanaRuleListItem` only passes `promRule` (and not `rule`/`rulerRule`) to `RuleActionsButtons`, both the Pause and Delete actions are completely missing from the "More" menu for Grafana-managed rules in the list view.

title: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` disallows Pause, Restore, and ModifyExport on Grafana recording rules
body: In `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, `Pause`, `Restore`, `DeletePermanently`, and `ModifyExport` are supported for all Grafana-managed rules (`rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which includes both alerting and recording rules). In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, those actions are gated on `isAlertingRule` (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`), which is `false` for `GrafanaPromRecordingRuleDTO`. Consequently, Grafana-managed recording rules lose `Pause`, `Restore`, `DeletePermanently`, and `ModifyExport` abilities when evaluated via `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`.

title: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` allows silencing even when `rule` is undefined or folder is still loading
body: In `useCanSilence` (used for `RulerRuleDTO`), silencing returns `[false, false]` if `!rule`, `folderIsLoading`, or `!folder`. In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `useCanSilenceInFolder(rule?.folderUid)` is called directly without checking `loading` or `!folder`: if a user has the global `AlertingInstanceCreate` permission, `canSilenceInFolder` is `true` even while the folder is still loading or failed to load. This causes `AlertRuleAction.Silence` to report `[true, true]` before folder data is available (inconsistent with `useCanSilence`).

title: `returnTo` query parameter dropped from rule view link in `GrafanaRuleListItem`
body: In the removed `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`, `GrafanaRuleListItem` constructed the rule view link with `createRelativeUrl(\`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view\`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. In the new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` (line 40), `returnTo` is omitted (`createRelativeUrl(\`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view\`)`), so navigating to a Grafana rule from the list or filter view no longer preserves the `returnTo` URL for the "Back" button in the rule viewer.

title: Missing `key` prop on `GrafanaRuleListItem` inside `.map()`
body: In `FilterViewResults`, when replacing `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ... />` with `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` inside `rules.map(...)`, the `key={key}` prop was dropped. Rendering list items in an array without a `key` causes React console warnings and can lead to incorrect component state reconciliation when the filtered rule list updates.

title: Silence notifications menu action does nothing in the alert list view
body: In the new alert list view (`GrafanaRuleListItem`), `RuleActionsButtons` is called with only `promRule` and `rule` (`rulerRule`) is `undefined`. `AlertRuleMenu` now uses `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` to enable and render the "Silence notifications" menu item, which calls `handleSilence={() => setShowSilenceDrawer(true)}`. However, `RuleActionsButtons` renders `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` conditionally on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`. Because `rule` is `undefined` when rendered from the list view, clicking "Silence notifications" sets `showSilenceDrawer` to `true` but the drawer never renders.

title: Pause and Delete menu items are hidden in the alert list view because `rulerRule` is undefined
body: In `AlertRuleMenu`, `canPause` and `canDelete` were updated to compute abilities from `promRule` via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` when `rulerRule` is not provided (as in `GrafanaRuleListItem`). However, the JSX conditions for rendering those menu items still require `rulerRule`: line 123 checks `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and line 165 checks `canDelete && rulerRule`. Because `GrafanaRuleListItem` only passes `promRule` (leaving `rulerRule` undefined), neither Pause nor Delete will ever be rendered in the alert rule list view for Grafana-managed rules.

title: Early template variable interpolation breaks detection of $__range and ad-hoc filters
body:
In `runSplitQuery`, `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` is now called before partitioning and before `runShardSplitQuery` delegates sub-requests to `runSplitQuery`. This causes two problems:

1. `querySupportsSplitting` (line 287) checks `!isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` so that queries containing `$__range`, `$__range_s`, or `$__range_ms` are not time-split (as the comment notes, splitting them produces wrong results because `$__range` should reflect the full request range, not a 1-day chunk). If `applyTemplateVariables` interpolates or transforms the expression before `querySupportsSplitting` runs, or if `runShardSplitQuery` has already called `applyTemplateVariables` (line 52 of `shardQuerySplitting.ts`) and then calls `runSplitQuery` (line 163 of `shardQuerySplitting.ts`), `applyTemplateVariables` is executed twice on the same query.
2. Calling `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` in both `runShardSplitQuery` and `runSplitQuery` (and potentially again inside `datasource.runQuery` / `super.query`) applies `request.filters` (ad-hoc filters) multiple times to `query.expr`, injecting duplicate label matchers into the LogQL selector.

title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting breaks skipping splitting for $__range/$__range_s/$__range_ms queries
body: `runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, ...)` on line 299 before calling `querySupportsSplitting(query)` on line 300. `querySupportsSplitting` relies on `!isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to detect literal `$__range`, `$__range_s`, or `$__range_ms` in `query.expr` so those queries are not split across time ranges. However, `LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables` replaces `$__range`, `$__range_s`, and `$__range_ms` (via `this.templateSrv.replace`) with concrete duration values from `scopedVars` (or leaves them already substituted), so by the time `querySupportsSplitting` runs, `query.expr` no longer contains `$__range*`. As a result, queries using `$__range`, `$__range_s`, or `$__range_ms` will now be treated as normal splittable queries and split into 1-day chunks while keeping the full-range duration in their range vector, producing completely wrong query results.

title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting breaks $__range detection and doubly applies adhoc filters
body:
In `runSplitQuery`, `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` is now called before `querySupportsSplitting` and before `datasource.runQuery` (or `runSplitQuery` when invoked from `shardQuerySplitting.ts`). This causes two issues:

1. `querySupportsSplitting` checks `!isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` so that queries containing `$__range`, `$__range_s`, or `$__range_ms` are not split (since `$__range` is supposed to represent the full query range rather than each split chunk). However, if `applyTemplateVariables` (or a custom template variable) replaces `$__range` or if `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates the query and then calls `runSplitQuery` which calls `applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` a second time (And then `datasource.runQuery` / `super.query` calls `applyTemplateVariables` a third time), `request.filters` (adhoc filters) will be injected into `query.expr` multiple times if `request.filters` is non-empty, duplicating stream selector matchers on every pass.

title: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns a new disconnected `TestLogger`, breaking test log assertions
body: In `pkg/plugins/log/fake.go`, `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver `f`. In `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go` (line 58), `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. When a test passes a `*TestLogger` into `NewLoggerMiddleware(cfg, logger)` and later inspects `logger.InfoLogs` (such as in `logger_middleware_test.go`), all log calls are recorded on the throwaway `TestLogger` returned by `FromContext` rather than on `f`, leaving `f.InfoLogs.Calls` at 0 and causing existing tests and any caller inspecting `TestLogger` state to fail.

title: `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` dereferences `req` without nil checks
body: `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics` immediately access `req.PluginContext` without checking whether `req == nil`. Other client middlewares in this package (for example `LoggerMiddleware` at lines 63, 77, 90, and 104) guard against `req == nil` and pass the call through to `m.next`. Because `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` is registered ahead of `LoggerMiddleware` in `CreateMiddlewares`, a nil request that previously reached `LoggerMiddleware` (such as in unit tests for nil-request handling or callers passing nil) will now panic with a nil pointer dereference in `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`.

title: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns a new instance, discarding logged calls on the original `TestLogger`
body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver `f`. Callers in tests hold a reference to the original `*TestLogger` and inspect `f.InfoLogs`, `f.ErrorLogs`, etc., after exercising code under test. With `LoggerMiddleware` now calling `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, any logs written through `FromContext` are recorded on the newly allocated `TestLogger` and silently lost on the original `TestLogger`, breaking existing `logger_middleware_test.go` assertions (and any other test that inspects `TestLogger` fields after `FromContext` is used). `FromContext` (and likely `New`) should return `f`.

title: `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` dereferences `req` without nil checks
body: `QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics` in `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` unconditionally access `req.PluginContext` before passing the call to `m.next`. Other client middlewares in this package (including `LoggerMiddleware` right after it in the chain) explicitly guard against `req == nil` and forward to `m.next` when `req` is nil. Because `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` sits ahead of `LoggerMiddleware`, a nil request will now panic with a nil pointer dereference instead of being safely passed through.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new instance, discarding logged messages on the receiver
body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of `f`. When code under test calls `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (as `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now does), the log call is recorded on the newly allocated `TestLogger` and immediately discarded, leaving the original `TestLogger` passed into `NewLoggerMiddleware` with `InfoLogs.Calls == 0`. Any unit test asserting on a `*log.TestLogger` passed to `LoggerMiddleware` will fail to observe logs written via `FromContext`.

title: ContextualLoggerMiddleware dereferences nil request pointers without nil checks
body: `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics` immediately access `req.PluginContext` without checking whether `req == nil`. Previously, `InstrumentationMiddleware` failed early via `pluginRegistry.Plugin` lookup on `QueryData`/`CallResource` or only after other checks, while `LoggerMiddleware` (and other middlewares in `clientmiddleware`) explicitly guard with `if req == nil { return m.next.<Method>(ctx, req) }`. Passing a nil request through the middleware chain will now panic with a nil pointer dereference in `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`.

title: Device ID is cached before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, allowing rejected devices to bypass the limit on retry
body: In `tagDeviceUI`, `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` is called on line 87 before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)` on line 93. When `AnonymousDeviceLimit` is reached and `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the new device's key remains in `localCache` for the 29-minute TTL. On any subsequent request from the same device, `tagDeviceUI` hits the cache on line 83 and returns `nil`, allowing `Anonymous.Authenticate` to succeed and completely bypassing the device limit after the first failed request. Move `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` to after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds.

title: wire_gen.go was not regenerated after changing ProvideAnonymousDeviceService and ProvideAnonDBStore signatures
body: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go` changed its parameter from `anonStore anonstore.AnonStore` to `sqlStore db.DB`, and `ProvideAnonDBStore` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go` added a `deviceLimit int64` parameter, but `pkg/server/wire_gen.go` (and any wire provider sets) was not updated in this PR. The server build will fail until Wire is re-run.

title: MySQL RowsAffected() returns 0 when UPDATE matches a row without changing values, falsely triggering ErrDeviceLimitReached
body: In `updateDevice`, `result.RowsAffected()` is used to determine whether the device existed within the active window, returning `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when `rowsAffected == 0`. On MySQL (unless `clientFoundRows` is enabled on the DSN), `RowsAffected()` returns the number of rows actually modified rather than matched. If two requests for an existing device occur within the same second (MySQL's default timestamp precision, or when `updated_at`, `client_ip`, and `user_agent` are identical), `RowsAffected()` will be 0 even though the device row exists and matched the `WHERE` clause, falsely rejecting an already-registered device with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

title: Device is cached before database limit check, allowing device limit bypass on second request
body: In `tagDeviceUI`, `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` (line 87) is executed before calling `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)` (line 93). When the anonymous device limit has been reached, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and the first request from a new device fails authentication as intended. However, because the device's cache key was already written to `localCache` with a 29-minute TTL, any subsequent request with the same `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header hits the cache at line 83 (`if _, ok := a.localCache.Get(key); ok { return nil }`) and bypasses `CreateOrUpdateDevice` entirely, succeeding authentication despite exceeding the device limit. `a.localCache.SetDefault` should only be called after `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds.

title: Wire dependency injection broken after changing ProvideAnonymousDeviceService signature
body: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` was changed to accept `sqlStore db.DB` instead of `anonStore anonstore.AnonStore`, and `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` was changed to require `deviceLimit int64`, but `pkg/server/wire.go` and the generated `wire_gen.go` files were not updated in this PR. Because `wire.go` wires `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and `anonimpl.ProvideAnonymousDeviceService`, the server package will fail to compile or fail `make gen-go` until the wire providers and generated files are updated.

title: MySQL RowsAffected() returns 0 when column values are unchanged, falsely triggering ErrDeviceLimitReached
body: In `updateDevice`, `result.RowsAffected()` is checked for `0` to determine whether the device matched an active row within the expiration window. In MySQL (when `clientFoundRows=false`, the default in `go-sql-driver/mysql`), `UPDATE` returns `0` rows affected if a matching row is found but the new values (`client_ip`, `user_agent`, `updated_at`) are identical to the existing column values. Because MySQL `DATETIME` columns or fast repeat calls within the same second can have identical timestamps, a valid existing device can receive `rowsAffected == 0` and be rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

title: auth.anonymous settings ignore environment variable overrides
body: `readAuthSettings` reads `iniFile.Section("auth.anonymous")` directly instead of `cfg.SectionWithEnvOverrides("auth.anonymous")`. As a result, `GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT` (and the other keys in that section) will not work via environment variables unless `SectionWithEnvOverrides` is used.

title: Local cache populated before device limit check allows bypassing the limit on subsequent requests
body: In `tagDeviceUI`, `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` is executed before calling `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)`. When the configured `device_limit` has been reached, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and the first request from a new anonymous device is rejected. However, because the device's cache key was already stored in `localCache` (with a 29-minute TTL), any subsequent request from the same device will hit the cache check at line 83 (`if _, ok := a.localCache.Get(key); ok { return nil }`) and succeed without hitting the store, completely bypassing the device limit. `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` should only be called after `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds.

title: Changing `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` signature without updating Wire breaks dependency injection
body: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` changed its parameter from `anonStore anonstore.AnonStore` to `sqlStore db.DB`, and `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` changed its signature to require `deviceLimit int64`, but `pkg/server/wire.go` and `pkg/server/wire_gen.go` were not updated in this PR. The server wire provider set still wires `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and the old `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` signature, which will fail to compile or fail `make gen-go`.

title: `RowsAffected() == 0` on MySQL can falsely trigger `ErrDeviceLimitReached` for existing devices
body: In `updateDevice`, `result.RowsAffected() == 0` is used to determine that the device was not found within the active window and therefore `ErrDeviceLimitReached` should be returned. On MySQL (when `clientFoundRows` is not enabled on the DSN), `RowsAffected()` returns the number of rows actually changed rather than matched. If an existing active device makes two requests within the same second (MySQL `DATETIME`/`TIMESTAMP` default precision) with the same `client_ip` and `user_agent`, the `UPDATE` matches the row but modifies no column values, so `RowsAffected()` returns 0 and the valid existing device is falsely rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

title: Cleanup background job interval changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
body: `CleanUpService.Run` changes `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` to `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)` without mention in the PR description. This appears to be a leftover from local testing and will cause all cleanup jobs (temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, user invites, short URLs, query history) to run 10x more frequently in production, increasing database load. Note also that `clean` uses a 9-minute timeout (line 89), which was chosen to fit inside the original 10-minute tick interval.

title: Debug logging left at Error level and logs full ID slice on every cleanup batch
body: In `CleanAnnotations` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 576, 579), `r.log.Error` is called unconditionally on every batch iteration even when there is no error (`err` is guaranteed `nil` at lines 534, 554, and 576), and it logs the entire `ids` slice (up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` elements). This looks like leftover debugging code and will flood error logs with large ID arrays during normal cleanup runs.

title: Quadratic string concatenation when building SQLite DELETE statement for large batches
body: In `deleteByIDs`, when running on SQLite with `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, the `IN` list is built in a loop with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` (lines 609-612). Because strings in Go are immutable, each iteration copies the entire accumulated string, resulting in O(N^2) allocations and time for N IDs (e.g., 32,767 IDs in the added test case). Use `strings.Builder` or `strconv.AppendInt` into a byte slice (as done in `getAccessControlFilter` at lines 387-395) instead.

title: SQLite parameter limit check compares configured batch size instead of actual number of IDs
body: Line 608 checks `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit`, and the `else` branch (line 615) binds `len(ids)` parameters (`?`). If `len(ids)` is small (for example, 1 or 2 rows on the final batch) while `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, it unnecessarily inlines literals; conversely, if `deleteByIDs` is ever called with `len(ids) > 999` when `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize <= 999` (or unconfigured/0), it will exceed SQLite's parameter limit. Checking `len(ids) > sqliteParameterLimit` directly matches the actual number of bound parameters.

title: Global cleanup service interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
body: In `CleanUpService.Run`, the ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This runs all background cleanup jobs (temp files, expired snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, user invites, short URLs, and query history) every minute instead of every 10 minutes, while each cleanup cycle still has a 9-minute timeout (`const timeout = 9 * time.Minute` on line 89). This appears to be a leftover local debugging change and will significantly increase background database and filesystem load in production.

title: Leftover Error-level debug logging in CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags
body: In `CleanAnnotations` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 576, 579), `r.log.Error` is called unconditionally on every batch iteration, even when `err == nil`, and dumps the entire slice of `ids` (which can contain tens of thousands of IDs per batch) along with the SQL condition. Because cleanup runs periodically in the background, this will flood production error logs with large payloads on every cleanup cycle even when no errors occur and no annotations are deleted.

title: Quadratic string concatenation when building SQLite DELETE IN clause
body: In `deleteByIDs`, when running on SQLite with `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, the `IN` list is constructed in a loop using `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` (lines 609-612). Because strings in Go are immutable, this copies the entire accumulated string on every iteration, resulting in O(N^2) allocations and time complexity over the batch size (e.g., 32,767 IDs in the added test case). Using a `strings.Builder` or `strconv.AppendInt` (as done in `getAccessControlFilter` at lines 387-395) avoids the quadratic allocations.

title: Parameter limit check in deleteByIDs only handles SQLite and checks config instead of len(ids)
body: `deleteByIDs` checks `r.db.GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite && r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit` before falling back to an parameterized `IN (?, ?, ...)` query. However, PostgreSQL and MySQL also enforce a maximum number of bind parameters per prepared statement (65,535 in both PostgreSQL's extended query protocol and MySQL). If `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` is configured above 65,535 (or `len(ids)` exceeds the limit), `deleteByIDs` will fail on PostgreSQL and MySQL when preparing the `DELETE` statement.

title: Accidental debugging change reduces global cleanup job interval from 10m to 1m
body: In `CleanUpService.Run`, the ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This runs all background cleanup jobs (temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, user invites, short URLs, and query history) every minute instead of every 10 minutes, with a 9-minute timeout per run. This appears to be a leftover from local testing and will significantly increase background database and filesystem load.

title: Leftover `r.log.Error` debugging logs in annotation cleanup
body: In `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579), `r.log.Error` is called unconditionally on every batch iteration, even when `err` is `nil`, and dumps the entire slice of `ids` (which can be thousands of IDs per batch). This will flood error logs and alerting systems during normal cleanup runs. These should be removed or changed to `Debug` level without logging the full `ids` slice.

title: O(N^2) string concatenation when building SQLite DELETE query
body: In `deleteByIDs` (lines 609-612), when `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999` on SQLite, the ID list string is built in a loop using `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)`. Because strings in Go are immutable, this copies the entire accumulated string on each iteration, resulting in O(N^2) allocations and time (e.g. for the 32,767 batch size in the test, this allocates gigabytes of memory). Use `strings.Builder` or `strconv.AppendInt` instead.

title: PostgreSQL and MySQL parameter limits are not handled when `ids` is large
body: In `deleteByIDs`, only SQLite's parameter limit (999) is bypassed by inlining integer IDs or chunking; for other databases, `len(ids)` placeholders (`?`) are generated in a single `DELETE FROM ... WHERE id IN (...)` statement. Both PostgreSQL and MySQL have prepared-statement parameter limits of 65,535 (`uint16`). If `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` is configured above 65,535 (or even large enough in general), `session.Exec` will fail on PostgreSQL and MySQL. Since `ids` is a `[]int64`, formatting the integers directly (with a `strings.Builder`) or chunking the `DELETE` statement across all dialects avoids parameter limit failures on all databases.

title: Generated object names are lost when writing to legacy storage in Create
body: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, `d.Storage.Create` is called with `obj` and returns `created`. When an object uses `generateName` (instead of an explicit `metadata.name`), `d.Storage.Create` generates and assigns the name on the returned `created` object, or mutates `obj` concurrently if `obj` is shared. Passing the original `obj` to `d.Legacy.Create` in a background goroutine means either `Legacy.Create` receives an object without the generated name/UID from unified storage (causing legacy and unified storage to have different identifiers or fail validation), or it races with mutations on `obj`/`created` while the caller is serializing `created` for the HTTP response. `created.DeepCopyObject()` should be passed to `d.Legacy.Create`.

title: Async legacy writes use request context that is canceled as soon as handler returns
body: In `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection` (lines 51, 110, 135, 163), the background goroutines derive their timeout context directly from the request `ctx` (`context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). Because `DualWriterMode3` returns immediately after `d.Storage.<Op>` completes, the HTTP server finishes the request and cancels `ctx` right away, which will cancel the in-flight or not-yet-started `d.Legacy.<Op>` calls in the goroutine. Use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` before applying `context.WithTimeoutCause` so the background legacy write is not aborted when the HTTP request finishes.

title: Wrong metrics recorded in Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection
body:
Several metric recording calls in `DualWriterMode3` record against the wrong store or with the wrong label:
- Line 45 (`Create`): when `d.Storage.Create` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
- Line 106 (`Delete`): `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the object `name` as the `kind` parameter (causing high-cardinality metric labels) instead of `options.Kind`.
- Line 129 (`Update`): when `d.Storage.Update` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
- Line 166 (`DeleteCollection`): inside the async legacy goroutine, `d.recordStorageDuration` is called instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`.

title: Delete attaches un-enriched logger to context
body: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, line 96 constructs `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)`, but line 97 passes `d.Log` instead of `log` to `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`, losing those structured log fields in downstream calls.

title: Shared testify mock.Mock in tests races with async legacy goroutines
body: In `TestMode3_Create`, `TestMode3_Delete`, `TestMode3_DeleteCollection`, and `TestMode3_Update`, both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` share a single `&mock.Mock{}` instance, and `Delete`/`DeleteCollection` do not even set up expectations on `Legacy`. Because `DualWriterMode3` invokes `d.Legacy.<Op>` in a background goroutine without synchronization, the goroutine accesses `m.Called(...)` concurrently with subsequent test assertions or after the test finishes, causing data races under `go test -race` and panics when `Delete`/`DeleteCollection` goroutines hit unexpected `Legacy` mock calls.

title: Create passes original unmutated object to Legacy.Create instead of the created object
body: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, `d.Storage.Create` is called first and returns `created` (which has generated fields populated, such as `Name` when `GenerateName` is used, `UID`, `ResourceVersion`, and `CreationTimestamp`), while `d.Legacy.Create` is then called in a goroutine with the original `obj` (or if `Storage.Create` mutates `obj` in place, reading/mutating the same pointer concurrently with the caller returning `created` and serializing it is a data race). When `GenerateName` is used (as tested in `playlist_test.go`), `Legacy.Create` will either generate a different name/UID than unified storage or fail/race on shared state.

title: Async legacy writes derive context from the HTTP request context, causing cancellation as soon as the handler returns
body: In `Create` (line 51), `Delete` (line 110), `Update` (line 135), and `DeleteCollection` (line 163), the background goroutine creates its timeout context from the request `ctx` (`context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). Once the synchronous `d.Storage.*` call completes and the method returns to the HTTP handler, the HTTP server cancels the request `ctx` as soon as the response is written. This will immediately cancel the in-flight or not-yet-scheduled `d.Legacy.*` operation in the background goroutine instead of giving it the intended 10s timeout. `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` should be used before applying the timeout.

title: Wrong metric recorded in Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection
body:
Several metric recording calls in `DualWriterMode3` record the wrong metric or label:
- Line 45 (`Create` error path): calls `d.recordLegacyDuration` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration` when `d.Storage.Create` fails.
- Line 106 (`Delete` success path): passes `name` (the object name, which is unbounded cardinality) instead of `options.Kind` as the `kind` argument to `d.recordStorageDuration`.
- Line 129 (`Update` error path): calls `d.recordLegacyDuration` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration` when `d.Storage.Update` fails.
- Line 166 (`DeleteCollection` async legacy path): calls `d.recordStorageDuration` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration` for the `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` call.

title: Unit tests share a non-thread-safe testify mock.Mock with background goroutines
body: In `TestMode3_Create`, `TestMode3_Delete`, `TestMode3_DeleteCollection`, and `TestMode3_Update`, both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` wrap the same `mock.Mock` instance, and `DualWriterMode3` invokes `d.Legacy.*` in a background goroutine without any synchronization before the test returns. Moreover, in `TestMode3_Delete` and `TestMode3_DeleteCollection` (and the error cases of `Create`/`Update` where `setupStorageFn` is nil), expectations are not even set up for both calls or `m.On` matches the wrong store. When the background goroutine runs concurrently with test completion or subsequent calls on `m`, `testify/mock` will either race on `m.Calls` or panic with an unexpected method call (e.g., `Delete` is only mocked once, or `Legacy.Delete` is called with no expectation or races).

title: Async legacy Create uses pre-creation input object instead of created object
body: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, `d.Storage.Create` returns `created`, which contains server-generated fields such as `Name` (when `GenerateName` is used), `UID`, and `ResourceVersion`. However, the async goroutine calls `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` with the original `obj` rather than `created` (or a deep copy of `created`). When `GenerateName` is used, `obj` has no name or a different UID than what was persisted in unified storage, causing the legacy store to either fail or create an inconsistent resource with a different identifier. Furthermore, passing `obj` or `created` without deep-copying into a background goroutine risks data races while the main goroutine serializes `created` for the response.

title: Async legacy writes use the request context, which is canceled when the HTTP handler returns
body: In `Create` (line 51), `Delete` (line 110), `Update` (line 135), and `DeleteCollection` (line 163), the background goroutines derive their timeout context directly from the request `ctx` (`context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). Because the goroutines run asynchronously and the methods return immediately after unified storage completes, the HTTP server will finish the request and cancel `ctx` while the legacy storage operation is still in flight, causing the background legacy writes to fail with `context.Canceled`. The context passed to the goroutine should be detached from parent cancellation (e.g. `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`).

title: Incorrect metric recording methods and label values in Mode 3 operations
body:
Multiple metric recording calls in `DualWriterMode3` record to the wrong metric or with the wrong label:
1. Line 45 (`Create`): When `d.Storage.Create` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
2. Line 106 (`Delete`): When `d.Storage.Delete` succeeds, `name` (the object instance name, which is also high-cardinality) is passed as the `kind` argument in `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` instead of `options.Kind`.
