3. Line 129 (`Update`): When `d.Storage.Update` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
4. Line 166 (`DeleteCollection`): In the async goroutine for `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection`, `d.recordStorageDuration` is called instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`.

title: Shared mock.Mock instance in unit tests causes data races with async legacy writes
body: In `TestMode3_Create`, `TestMode3_Delete`, `TestMode3_DeleteCollection`, and `TestMode3_Update`, both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` share the same `*mock.Mock` instance `m`, and the tests do not synchronize with the background goroutines spawned by `DualWriterMode3`. In `Delete` and `DeleteCollection`, no mock expectations are even registered for the legacy calls (`setupLegacyFn` is missing), so if the background goroutine runs before or during test completion, `testify/mock` will panic with an unexpected method call or trigger a data race on `m.Calls`.

title: Double-checked locking does not re-check entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring write lock
body: In `GetWebAssets`, `entryPointAssetsCache` is checked under a read lock (lines 41-47), which is then released before acquiring the write lock at line 48. After acquiring `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`, `entryPointAssetsCache` is not checked again. If multiple goroutines concurrently call `GetWebAssets` on a cold cache (when `cfg.Env != setting.Dev`), all of them will see `ret == nil` under the read lock, wait on `Lock()`, and then each one will redundantly re-read and parse `assets-manifest.json` from disk and overwrite `entryPointAssetsCache` sequentially. Re-checking `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` after acquiring the write lock avoids the redundant file I/O and parsing.

title: enableSqlExpressions unconditionally returns false in both branches
body: In `enableSqlExpressions`, both the `if enabled` branch and the fallthrough return `false`. While this intentionally disables SQL expressions for the security fix, the conditional logic (`enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` followed by `if enabled { return false }; return false`) is dead/redundant and will trigger static analysis warnings (such as `staticcheck` / `golangci-lint` flagging identical branches or unconditional return values). If SQL expressions are meant to be unconditionally disabled regardless of the feature flag, the function or check should simply return `false` (or the `QueryTypeSQL` case should directly return the error) without the dead branch.

title: TotalDocs iterates over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu
body: `TotalDocs()` iterates over `b.cache` without acquiring `b.cacheMu.RLock()`. This PR adds a call to `s.search.TotalDocs()` in `searchSupport.init()` right after starting the background watch goroutine (`handleEvent`), which can concurrently call `getOrCreateIndex` -> `BuildIndex` and mutate `b.cache`. In addition, once the server is running, concurrent `Search` requests or watch events for unindexed namespaces can trigger `BuildIndex` and write to `b.cache` while `TotalDocs()` is reading it, causing a concurrent map read/write panic in Go.

title: Removing global lock in BuildIndex exposes concurrent builds for the same key
body: Previously, `b.cacheMu.Lock()` was held for the entire duration of `BuildIndex`. By narrowing the lock to only the final `b.cache[key] = idx` assignment, two concurrent callers (e.g., concurrent `Search` requests or a `Search` racing with `handleEvent` via `getOrCreateIndex`) for the same `NamespacedResource` key can now execute `BuildIndex` simultaneously. For file-backed indexes (`size > b.opts.FileThreshold`), the second call to `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same directory will fail because the path already exists / is locked by BoltDB. For memory-backed indexes, both will build in parallel and the second will overwrite `b.cache[key]`, leaking the first index and double-counting `IndexTenants` and `IndexedKinds` metrics.

title: Data race on totalBatchesIndexed and shared err variable in errgroup
body: With `BuildIndex` in `bleveBackend` no longer serializing execution under `cacheMu`, the goroutines spawned in `searchSupport.init` via `group.Go` (when `s.initWorkers > 1`) now run concurrently. Inside the closure, `totalBatchesIndexed++` (line 189) and the assignment to the outer `err` variable in `_, _, err = s.build(...)` (line 190) are unsynchronized writes across goroutines, causing a data race (which will fail under `go test -race`). `err` should be a local variable inside the closure and `totalBatchesIndexed` should use `atomic` or `len(stats)`.

title: Canceled context and leaked resources if s.Init fails in NewResourceServer
body: In `NewResourceServer`, if `s.Init(ctx)` returns an error on line 258, `cancel()` (created on line 229) is never called and any already-initialized components (such as the CDK blob bucket opened on line 208 or background goroutines started by `s.lifecycle.Init` / `s.search.init` before a later step in `Init` failed) are not cleaned up.

title: TotalDocs reads bleveBackend.cache without holding cacheMu
body: `TotalDocs()` iterates over `b.cache` without acquiring `b.cacheMu.RLock()`. Although `searchSupport.init` calls `s.search.TotalDocs()` after `group.Wait()`, the watch goroutine started a few lines earlier on lines 207-213 of `pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go` is already running and can concurrently invoke `handleEvent` -> `getOrCreateIndex` -> `BuildIndex`, which mutates `b.cache[key] = idx` under `b.cacheMu.Lock()`. In addition, any other caller of `TotalDocs` after startup will race with on-demand index creation in `Search` or `handleEvent`. In Go, concurrent map iteration and map write causes a fatal runtime panic (`concurrent map iteration and map write`). `TotalDocs` should acquire `b.cacheMu.RLock()` / `defer b.cacheMu.RUnlock()`.

title: Removing the mutex from BuildIndex allows concurrent builds of the same NamespacedResource
body: Previously `BuildIndex` held `b.cacheMu.Lock()` for its entire execution, which serialized index builds. With the lock moved to only wrap `b.cache[key] = idx` at line 137, two concurrent callers of `getOrCreateIndex` for the same `NamespacedResource` (for example, concurrent `Search` requests for an unindexed namespace or a `Search` racing with `handleEvent`) will both see `GetIndex == nil` and run `BuildIndex` in parallel. For file-backed indexes (`size > b.opts.FileThreshold`), the second `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same directory will fail because the directory already exists / BoltDB file lock is held, failing the request; for in-memory indexes, both will build an index and one will overwrite the other in `b.cache`, while `IndexMetrics.IndexTenants` and `IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds` are incremented twice for the same key. Per-key synchronization (e.g., `singleflight` or a per-key lock) is needed when building an index.

title: Data race on totalBatchesIndexed and shared err in searchSupport.init errgroup
body: When `s.initWorkers > 1` (the PR description specifically notes high concurrency when building namespaces), the `group.Go` goroutines in `searchSupport.init` concurrently execute `totalBatchesIndexed++` (line 189) and assign to the outer `err` variable in `_, _, err = s.build(...)` (line 190) without synchronization. Because `BuildIndex` no longer serializes these goroutines with a global mutex, these unsynchronized writes now execute in parallel, causing a data race under `-race` and potentially corrupting the error returned by the goroutine or the `totalBatchesIndexed` count. Use a local `_, _, err := s.build(...)` inside the closure and either `atomic.Int64` for `totalBatchesIndexed` or `len(stats)`.

title: NewResourceServer leaks background context and blob bucket when s.Init fails
body: `NewResourceServer` creates a cancellable context `ctx, cancel` (line 229) and optionally opens a blob bucket (line 208) before calling `s.Init(ctx)` at line 258. If `s.Init(ctx)` returns an error, `NewResourceServer` returns `nil, err` without calling `cancel()` (and if `s.search.init` succeeded before `s.initWatcher` failed, the watch goroutine in `searchSupport.init` is also left running). `cancel()` should be called on the error path before returning.

title: Data race on shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` inside `errgroup.Go`
body:
Inside the `for _, info := range stats` loop in `s.init`, the goroutines launched via `group.Go` mutate two outer-scope variables without synchronization:

1. `_, _, err = s.build(...)` assigns to the outer `err` variable (declared at line 181), rather than a goroutine-local `err`. When `s.initWorkers > 1`, multiple goroutines concurrently write to and read from `err`, causing a data race and potentially returning another goroutine's value.
2. `totalBatchesIndexed++` (line 189) is also incremented concurrently without synchronization or atomic operations.

Before this PR, `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` held `b.cacheMu.Lock()` for its entire duration, which largely serialized the goroutines after `s.builders.get`. Removing that coarse lock in `bleve.go` now exposes this race whenever `s.initWorkers > 1`. Use `_, _, err := s.build(...)` inside the closure and `atomic.Int64` (or `len(stats)`) for `totalBatchesIndexed`.

title: `TotalDocs()` iterates over `b.cache` without acquiring `b.cacheMu`
body: `bleveBackend.TotalDocs()` ranges over `b.cache` without holding `b.cacheMu.RLock()`. If `TotalDocs()` is called concurrently with `BuildIndex` (for example via `getOrCreateIndex` triggered by a `Search` request or watch event while another call is reading `TotalDocs()`), Go will panic with `fatal error: concurrent map iteration and map write`. Acquire `b.cacheMu.RLock()` / `defer b.cacheMu.RUnlock()` in `TotalDocs()`.

title: Removing coarse lock in `BuildIndex` allows concurrent builds for the same key to collide or overwrite each other
body:
Previously, `BuildIndex` locked `b.cacheMu` for the entire build. With the lock moved to only cover `b.cache[key] = idx` at the end of `BuildIndex`, two concurrent callers to `getOrCreateIndex` for the same `NamespacedResource` (e.g., two concurrent `Search` requests for an unindexed namespace or a `Search` racing with `handleEvent`) will both see a cache miss in `GetIndex` and run `BuildIndex` concurrently.

- For file-backed indexes (`size > b.opts.FileThreshold`), the second `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` call on the same directory will fail because the directory/boltdb lock already exists.
- For in-memory indexes, both will build separate `bleve.Index` instances, double-increment `IndexMetrics.IndexTenants` and `IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds`, and the second will overwrite `b.cache[key]` without closing the first index.

Consider synchronizing builds per key (e.g., `singleflight` or a per-key lock) or re-checking `b.cache[key]` before building.

title: `NewResourceServer` leaks the watch context and blob bucket if `s.Init` fails
body: `NewResourceServer` creates a cancelable context (`ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(...)` at line 229) and optionally opens a blob `bucket` (line 208), and now calls `s.Init(ctx)` at line 258. If `s.Init(ctx)` returns an error, `NewResourceServer` returns `nil, err` without calling `cancel()` (or closing `bucket`), leaking the context and any background goroutines started during partial initialization (such as the watcher goroutine started by `s.search.init` if `s.initWatcher()` fails afterward). Call `cancel()` on the error path before returning.

title: Compilation error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called with no arguments
body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the method defined on the superclass `UsernamePasswordForm` (line 160) has the signature `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` and there is no zero-argument overload. This causes a compilation failure.

title: Passkeys conditional UI is disabled on initial login when context.getUser() is null
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`, requiring `user != null`. During a normal initial login `context.getUser()` is `null`, so `authenticate()` (line 115) and `challenge()` (line 137) never call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when no user is pre-selected. This completely breaks passkey / conditional UI login whenever the user is not already known (and when `user != null`, it enables conditional passkeys for every user regardless of whether that user has any passkey credentials configured, instead of checking `user == null || webauthnAuth.configuredFor(session, session.getContext().getRealm(), user)`).

title: Calling non-existent no-arg method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() causes compilation failure
body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but its superclass `UsernamePasswordForm` only defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` taking a `UserModel` parameter. This causes a compilation error (`cannot find symbol: method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`).

title: Conditional passkeys are disabled on initial login when user is null
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Both `authenticate()` (line 115) and `challenge()` (line 137) gate `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` on this method. During a normal initial login, `context.getUser()` is `null`, so `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` always evaluates to `false`, completely disabling conditional UI passkeys whenever the user has not yet been identified. Additionally, when `user != null` (e.g. re-authentication), it does not check whether the identified user actually has a passkey credential configured (`webauthnAuth.configuredFor(context.getSession(), context.getRealm(), user)`), so passkey UI elements will be rendered even for users without a passkey.

title: Call to non-existent no-arg method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` breaks compilation
body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but `UsernamePasswordForm` only defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (line 160 of `UsernamePasswordForm.java`). There is no zero-argument overload in `UsernameForm` or any superclass, so `UsernameForm.java` fails to compile.

title: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` requires `user != null`, breaking initial passkey login when no user is set yet
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Both `authenticate(context)` (line 115) and `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137) gate `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` on this method. On a normal initial login `context.getUser()` is `null`, so `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` always returns `false` and `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never called. As a result, WebAuthn conditional UI attributes and challenge are never added to the login form on initial login, completely breaking passwordless passkey login when the user is not yet identified. Even if `user != null`, it should also verify that the user actually has a passkey credential configured (`webauthnAuth.configuredFor(context.getSession(), context.getRealm(), user)`) rather than enabling passkey UI for any identified user.

title: NullPointerException in remove(String) when alias does not exist and cache key is invalidated
body: In `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove(String alias)`, if the identity provider for `alias` does not exist (`storedIdp == null`) and `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is true (for example, if the IDP was already removed earlier in the same transaction), `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` is called with `null` and immediately throws a `NullPointerException` at `idp.getInternalId()` instead of returning `false` as required by the `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove` contract. `registerIDPInvalidation` (or the call site) should guard against `storedIdp == null`.

title: Cleanup in testCacheIDPForLogin uses literal string "alias" instead of the created IDP alias
body: At lines 381 and 425 in `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`, cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` using the literal string `"alias"` rather than the actual IDP alias (`"idp-alias-" + i` / `"idp-alias-20"`). When cleanup runs after the test, attempting to remove the non-existent `"alias"` IDP will fail with a 404 NotFoundException and leave the 20+ created identity providers behind in the test realm.

title: `update` uses organization-wrapped `isEnabled()` when deciding whether to invalidate login caches
body: In `update(IdentityProviderModel model)`, `idpById` is fetched via `getById(model.getInternalId())`, which wraps the model with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. That wrapper overrides `isEnabled()` to return `false` when the linked organization is currently disabled. In contrast, the incoming `model` parameter is a plain `IdentityProviderModel` whose `isEnabled()` reflects only the IDP's stored flag. When an enabled login IDP belongs to a disabled organization and is later disabled via `update` (`model.isEnabled() == false`), `getLoginPredicate().test(idpById)` evaluates to `false` (because of the disabled organization) and `getLoginPredicate().test(model)` also evaluates to `false` (because the IDP is now disabled). `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` then hits the early return at line 405 and skips invalidating the `getForLogin` caches. If the organization was previously enabled when `getForLogin` was cached and is later re-enabled, the now-disabled IDP remains in the cached `IdentityProviderListQuery` IDs and will be returned by `getForLogin` even though it is disabled in storage. `idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId())` (unwrapped) should be used for the invalidation comparison, or `getForLogin` callers must also re-check `LoginFilter` / `isEnabled` across all code paths.

title: Test cleanup registers literal `"alias"` instead of the created IDP alias, leaking test IDPs
body: In `testCacheIDPForLogin` (lines 381 and 425, copied from line 303), cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` using the string literal `"alias"` rather than the actual IDP alias (`"idp-alias-" + i` and `"idp-alias-20"`). When the test finishes, cleanup attempts to delete a non-existent IDP named `"alias"` (failing with 404) and leaves the 20 created IDPs in the test realm, which can pollute subsequent tests in the class.

title: `IdentityProviderBean` does not re-check `isEnabled()` on cached `getForLogin` results when `ORGANIZATION` feature is disabled or outside `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`
body: `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` caches the set of internal IDs and resolves each via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)`, which wraps the model so `isEnabled()` dynamically checks whether the linked organization is enabled. This PR adds `.filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled() && ...)` in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` (lines 75 and 80) to account for an organization being disabled after `getForLogin` was cached, because disabling an organization does not invalidate `cacheKeyForLogin`. However, `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` itself still returns those disabled-org IDPs in the stream, violating the contract of `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` ("An IDP can be used for login if it is enabled..."). Any other caller of `getForLogin` (or `getForLogin` itself) will receive IDPs whose `isEnabled()` is `false`. Filtering by `IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled` inside `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` (e.g. before returning `identityProviders.stream()`) would enforce the contract for all callers.

title: Organization state causes login cache invalidation to be skipped for disabled organizations
body:
`InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.update` retrieves the original IDP via `getById(...)` (line 91), which wraps the model in `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` (line 432). That wrapper overrides `isEnabled()` to return `false` whenever the linked organization (or `OrganizationProvider`) is disabled, even if the underlying IDP has `enabled == true`. In contrast, the JPA query in `getForLogin` filters on the IDP's own `enabled` column without checking organization state, and the `updated` model passed into `update(model)` may also be an unwrapped `IdentityProviderModel` (e.g. from `RepresentationToModel.updateIdentityProvider`).

Because `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` calls `idp.isEnabled()`, when an organization is currently disabled:
1. Updating an IDP linked to that organization (e.g. toggling `hideOnLogin`, `linkOnly`, or `BROKER_PUBLIC`, or unlinking it from the organization) sees `getLoginPredicate().test(original) == false`. If `updated` is also wrapped (or becomes non-login), `!test(original) && !test(updated)` is true and `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` returns early without invalidating the login caches. Once the organization is later re-enabled, `getForLogin` will serve stale cached IDP lists.
2. Similarly, `create` and `remove` call `registerIDPLoginInvalidation`, which skips invalidation if the organization is currently disabled because `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)` returns `false` on wrapped models.

Cache invalidation predicates should evaluate the IDP's own `isEnabled()` state (or unwrap the model) rather than the organization-dependent `isEnabled()`, or organization enable/disable must also invalidate login caches.

title: Test cleanup registers literal "alias" instead of the created IDP's alias
body: In `testCacheIDPForLogin` at lines 381 and 425 (copied from line 303), cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` using the string literal `"alias"` instead of the actual IDP alias (`"idp-alias-" + i` and `"idp-alias-20"`). When the test finishes, cleanup will attempt to remove a non-existent IDP named `"alias"` (failing with 404) and leave the 20+ created IDPs in `testRealm`, polluting subsequent tests in the suite.

title: Fail-fast check for conflicting CryptoProviders with the same highest order was removed
body: Previously, `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` threw an `IllegalStateException` whenever more than one `CryptoProvider` was found on the classpath, preventing accidental mixing of incompatible providers such as `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider`, and `WildFlyElytronProvider`. With this change, all three full providers return `order() == 200`, and `detectProvider` simply sorts by `order()` and picks `foundProviders.get(0)` while only logging the rest at `DEBUG` level. Even worse, `ServiceLoader` instantiates every discovered provider during iteration, and the constructors of `DefaultCryptoProvider` and `FIPS1402Provider` both mutate global JVM state (`Security.addProvider` / `Security.insertProviderAt` and security properties). If two providers with the same highest `order()` are on the classpath (e.g., `DefaultCryptoProvider` and `FIPS1402Provider`), both constructors will run and corrupt global JCA provider state, and one will be arbitrarily chosen based on classpath order instead of failing fast. `detectProvider` should still throw an `IllegalStateException` when the top two providers have the same `order()`.

title: ASN1Decoder does not reject indefinite-length encodings or negative lengths in readNext/readSequence/readInteger
body: `ASN1Decoder.readLength()` returns `-1` when the length byte is `0x80` (indefinite-length encoding). However, callers do not handle `-1`: in `readSequence()` (line 55), `length = -1` causes the `while (length > 0)` loop to be skipped and an empty sequence to be returned; in `readInteger()` (line 71) and `readNext()` (line 80), a negative length can be passed to `read(int length)` (line 170), which throws an unchecked `NegativeArraySizeException` instead of an `IOException`. Inaddition, in `readSequence()`, if an element's length exceeds the remaining sequence length, `length` becomes negative and the loop terminates silently without报错. DER does not permit indefinite lengths, so `readLength()` should throw an `IOException` when `length == 0x80` (or when `length > remaining bytes`).

title: ECDSAAlgorithmTest uses a single P-256 key for ES384 and ES512 and never verifies the re-encoded DER signature
body: `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` generates a single default EC `KeyPair` (256-bit P-256) in the constructor and reuses it for `testES256`, `testES384`, and `testES512`. Signing with a P-256 key under `SHA384withECDSA` or `SHA512withECDSA` still produces ~32-byte `r` and `s` values (not 48-byte P-384 or 66-byte P-521 values), so the 48-byte and 66-byte encoding/decoding paths and high-bit padding on P-384/P-521 are not actually exercised. Furthermore, `test()` only checks that `asn1derToConcatenatedRS(concatenatedRSToASN1DER(rsConcat))` equals `rsConcat`; it never feeds `asn1Des` back into `Signature.verify(asn1Des)` to verify that `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` produces valid ASN.1 DER accepted by the JCA `Signature` verifier.

title: Dead ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 in `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.concatenatedRSToASN1DER` call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` and discard both results before repeating the exact same calls inside `writeDerSeq(...)` on lines 119-120. Those two lines allocate and populate `ByteArrayOutputStream` instances for nothing and should be removed.

title: Unparameterized logger.debugf call with dynamic string in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider
body: At line 69 of `CryptoIntegration.java`, `logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes a dynamically constructed string as the `printf` format string. Although class names do not normally contain `%`, using `debugf` without format arguments is unnecessary and will throw `UnknownFormatConversionException` if any `toString`/name ever contains `%`. Use `logger.debug(builder.toString())` or `logger.debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", ...)`.

title: Indefinite-length ASN.1 encoding (-1) is not rejected and causes NegativeArraySizeException or silent truncation
body: `ASN1Decoder.readLength()` returns `-1` when it encounters `0x80` (indefinite-length encoding). However, callers (`readSequence`, `readInteger`, `readNext`) do not check for `-1`. In `readInteger`, passing `-1` to `read(-1)` allocates `new byte[-1]` and throws `NegativeArraySizeException` instead of an `IOException`. In `readSequence`, `length` is `-1` so `while (length > 0)` immediately terminates and returns an empty sequence. In `readNext`, `length += reset()` adds the header byte count to `-1`, reading a truncated slice of bytes. Since ECDSA signatures must be DER-encoded (which forbids indefinite lengths), `readLength()` should throw an `IOException` when `length == 0x80` (or when `length < 0`).

title: Dead ASN1Encoder allocations in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` and discard both results before repeating the exact same calls on lines 119-120 inside `writeDerSeq(...)`. Those two statements are dead work and should be removed.

title: ECDSAAlgorithmTest uses a single P-256 key for ES256, ES384, and ES512 and does not verify the re-encoded DER signature
body: `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` generates a single default EC `KeyPair` (256-bit P-256) in the constructor and reuses it across `testES256`, `testES384`, and `testES512`. Signing with `SHA384withECDSA` or `SHA512withECDSA` using a P-256 key still produces ~32-byte `r` and `s` values, while `algorithm.getSignatureLength()` is 96 for ES384 and 132 for ES512. As a result, full-size 48-byte (P-384) and 66-byte (P-521, which also exercises DER lengths > 127 bytes) `r` and `s` integers are never tested. In addition, the test never verifies `asn1Des` with `Signature.verify(asn1Des)` (or `Assert.assertArrayEquals(sign, asn1Des)`), so a bug that produces invalid DER in `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` that `ASN1Decoder` happens to accept would pass the test.

title: Unparameterized logger.debugf call with dynamic string
body: On line 69, `logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes a dynamically built string as the format pattern to `debugf` with no format arguments. Use `logger.debug(builder.toString())` or `logger.debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", ...)` instead.

title: ES384 and ES512 tests use a P-256 key and never verify the converted DER signature
body: `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` generates a single default EC key pair (`KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()`, which defaults to 256-bit P-256) in the constructor and reuses it across `testES256`, `testES384`, and `testES512`. Because the key is P-256, `signature.sign()` always produces ~70-72 byte signatures with 32-byte `r` and `s` components, even when signing with `SHA384withECDSA` or `SHA512withECDSA`. Consequently, 48-byte (P-384) and 66-byte (P-521, where ASN.1 lengths exceed 127 bytes and exercise multi-byte DER length encoding in `ASN1Encoder`/`ASN1Decoder`) `r`/`s` values are never tested. In addition, `test()` only checks that `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` -> `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` -> `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` round-trips to the same byte array; it never feeds `asn1Des` into `Signature.verify(...)` with the public key to confirm that `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` actually produces a valid ASN.1 DER signature accepted by the JCA provider.

title: Dead ASN1Encoder allocations in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` and discard both return values before lines 119-120 perform the exact same encoding inside `writeDerSeq(...)`. Those two statements allocate `ByteArrayOutputStream` instances and encode `r` and `s` for no effect and should be removed.

title: Unparameterized logger.debugf call with dynamic string can fail if provider name contains '%'
body: `logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes a dynamically constructed string as the `printf` format pattern with no arguments. If any provider class name or representation ever contains `%`, `String.format` will throw `UnknownFormatConversionException`. Pass a format string (`logger.debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", ...)` or use `logger.debug(builder.toString())`) instead.

title: Resource lookup uses wrong owner ID and fails to set resource type upon creation
body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` (line 214) and `hasPermission(String)` (line 244), `resourceStore.findByName(server, ..., server.getId())` passes `server.getId()` (the internal UUID of the resource server) as the `ownerId`. However, when `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates a resource (line 104 of `AdminPermissionsSchema.java`), it passes `resourceServer.getClientId()` (`"admin-permissions"`) as the owner ID. Because `server.getId()` does not equal `server.getClientId()`, `findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())` will only find resources if the single-argument overload `findByName(server, name)` (which defaults ownerId to `server.getClientId()`) is used, or if `server.getId()` happens to match. Specifically, in `JPA` / `Infinispan` stores, `findByName(ResourceServer, String, String)` queries by `owner = ownerId`. Even more importantly, in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (line 104), newly created per-client resources do not have `resource.setType(resourceType)` called on them, which means `getClientsWithPermission` (line 138: `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`) will never find per-client resources because their `type` field is `null`.

title: All-clients permission is not evaluated when a client resource exists for a different scope
body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)` (lines 214-234), if a resource for `client` exists in the `resourceStore` (for example, because a permission was created for `client` with the `map-roles` scope), `resource` is non-null. The method then evaluates permissions only against this specific client resource and never falls back to evaluating the `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` ("all-clients") resource. Consequently, if an admin has an "all-clients" permission granting `manage` or `view`, and a specific permission on `client` for `map-roles`, `hasPermission(client, "manage")` will return `false` instead of falling back to the all-clients permission (unless a negative policy on the specific client explicitly denies it, as handled in `UserPermissionsV2`).

title: getResourceName does not handle CLIENTS resource type
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` (lines 304-326) only resolves human-readable resource names when `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)`, returning `"All users"` or `user.getUsername()`. It was not updated to handle `CLIENTS.getType()`, so for client permissions it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` (which is null/UUID) instead of returning `"All clients"` or the client's `clientId`.

title: Resource lookup uses ResourceServer ID instead of clientId as owner, so per-client permissions are never found
body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` (line 214) and `hasPermission(String)` (line 244), `resourceStore.findByName(server, ..., server.getId())` passes `server.getId()` (a UUID) as the `ownerId` parameter. However, when resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (line 104: `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())`) and `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` (via `RepresentationToModel`, which defaults the owner to `resourceServer.getClientId()`), the resource owner is set to `server.getClientId()` (`"admin-permissions"`), not `server.getId()`. As a result, `resourceStore.findByName(server, ..., server.getId())` always returns `null`: `hasPermission(String)` always returns `false`, and `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` never finds the specific client resource and always falls back to the all-clients resource (ignoring per-client permissions whenever an all-clients policy exists, or failing when none exists). Use `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId())` (which defaults to `server.getClientId()`) and `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`, matching `UserPermissionsV2`.

title: Per-client authorization resources created without setting resource type, breaking getClientsWithPermission
body: `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission` (line 138) queries `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. However, when per-client (or per-user) resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (line 104), `resource.setType(resourceType)` is never called—only the `"Clients"` all-resource created in `init()` has its type set. Consequently, `findByType` only ever visits the `"Clients"` resource type resource (whose name is `"Clients"`, not a client UUID) and never returns any individual client IDs for which the caller has permission. (And in `PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient`, `findAll()` only returned 1 client because `myclient` happened to have `view` scope on the `"Clients"` or other path, or because `getClientsWithPermission` wasn't the path that matched).

title: canView() does not return true when caller has MANAGE permission on all clients
body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.canView()` (line 87), it checks `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` (or `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`). When a user is granted the `manage` scope on all clients (`Clients` resource) without the `view` scope, `canManage()` returns `true`, but `canView()` returns `false` because `canViewClientDefault()` only checks admin roles (`VIEW_CLIENTS`, `MANAGE_CLIENTS`) and `hasPermission(VIEW)` only checks for the `view` scope. Since `canList()` delegates to `canView()`, and `ClientsResource.getClients()` checks `auth.clients().canView()`, an admin with `manage` permission on all clients will not have general view access (e.g., `canView()` is false, and in `testManageAllClients` listing only works if `getSearchableClients` happens to match the `"Clients"` resource). `canView()` should also return `true` when `canManage()` is `true` (or pass both `VIEW` and `MANAGE` scopes to `hasPermission`, as `canView(ClientScopeModel)` does on line 121).

title: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName does not handle CLIENTS resource type
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` (lines 304-326) resolves human-readable resource names when converting policies/permissions to representations (used by the Admin UI when listing resources attached to a permission). It currently only handles `USERS.getType()` and falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` (which is `null` for auto-created client resources) for `CLIENTS.getType()`. It should also handle `CLIENTS.getType()` (returning e.g. `"All clients"` for `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` and `client.getClientId()` when looking up by `resource.getName()`).

title: All-clients permission is not evaluated as a fallback when a per-client resource exists for a different scope
body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` (lines 214-224), the all-clients resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`) is only loaded if `resource == null` (i.e., no resource exists for that specific client). If a specific permission was created for `clientA` with only scope `configure` (creating the resource for `clientA`), and an all-clients permission was also created granting `manage` (or `map-roles`), evaluating `hasPermission(clientA, MANAGE)` will find `clientA`'s resource, evaluate only the policies attached to `clientA`, see that `manage` is not granted there, and return `false` without ever evaluating the all-clients permission (unlike `UserPermissionsV2`, which passes both the specific resource and the resource-type resource, or falls back when the scope is not granted).

title: Resource lookup uses wrong ownerId and fails to find client-specific resources
body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` (line 214) and `hasPermission(String)` (line 244), `resourceStore.findByName(server, ..., server.getId())` passes `server.getId()` (a UUID) as the `ownerId` parameter. However, when resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (line 104: `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())`) and `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` (via `RepresentationToModel`), the resource owner is set to `resourceServer.getClientId()`, or in JPA `server.getClientId()`. Using `server.getId()` may fail to match or is inconsistent with `AdminPermissionsSchema` which calls the 2-argument `resourceStore.findByName(resourceServer, name)` (which defaults ownerId to `resourceServer.getClientId()`) and `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`.

title: Created client resources do not have their resource type set in AdminPermissionsSchema
body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(String)` (line 138), resources are queried via `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. However, in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (lines 104-111), when a resource for a specific client (or user) is created dynamically, `resource.setType(resourceType)` is never called—only the 'all-resources' resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` has its type set. Because per-client resources have `type == null`, `findByType` will never return them, so `getClientsWithPermission` will miss all individual client permissions (and listing clients in `ClientsResource.getClients` will return an empty list when only per-client `view` permissions are granted, unless `canConfigure`/`canManage` happens to be evaluated via another path).

title: All-clients permissions are ignored when a client-specific resource exists for a different scope
body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` (lines 214-222), the fallback to the `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` ('all-clients') resource only happens when `resource == null` (i.e., no resource exists for that specific client). If a specific permission is created for Client A on one scope (e.g., `map-roles`), a `Resource` for Client A is created in the store. If another permission is granted on the 'all-clients' resource (e.g., `view` or `manage` all clients), `hasPermission(clientA, VIEW)` will find Client A's specific resource, evaluate only the policies attached to Client A's resource, and return `false` without ever evaluating the 'all-clients' resource policies (compare with `UserPermissionsV2`, which evaluates both the user resource and the all-users resource type).

title: canView() does not return true when caller has MANAGE permission on all clients
body: `ClientPermissionsV2.canView()` (line 87) checks `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)`, which does not check `canManage()` or `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. In contrast, `ClientPermissions.canView()` checks `canViewClientDefault() || canManage()`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel)` checks `canView() || canConfigure(client)` (which includes `canManage(client)`). As a result, an admin granted only the `MANAGE` scope on all clients will have `canManage() == true`, `canView(client) == true`, and `canView(clientScope) == true`, but `canView() == false`, causing endpoints that call `auth.clients().requireView()` or `canView()` (such as viewing clientscopes list via `canViewClientScopes()` / `canListClientScopes()`) to unexpectedly fail with 403 Forbidden.

title: getResourceName does not handle CLIENTS resource type
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` (lines 304-326) only handles `USERS.getType()`, returning `"All users"` or `user.getUsername()`. It was not updated to handle `CLIENTS.getType()`. For client permissions, `resource.getDisplayName()` will be returned, which is `null` (or the internal UUID / `"Clients"`), instead of `"All clients"` or the client's `clientId` when policies/permissions are converted to representations for the Admin UI/REST API.

title: Orphaned authorization resources and permissions are not cleaned up when a client or user is deleted in FGAP V2
body: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener` (line 77), the `ProviderEventListener` for `ClientRemovedEvent` (and other removal events) is now gated behind `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` (V1 only), and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. Consequently, when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled and a client (or user) is deleted from a realm, its corresponding `Resource` in the `admin-permissions` resource server and references to it in policies are never removed from the database. Worse, if a policy references that deleted client's resource, subsequent calls to `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName` (when implemented for clients, as it already is for users at line 318) will throw `ModelIllegalStateException` because the underlying entity no longer exists.

title: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage access when caller only has VIEW permission
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` checks `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` (line 70). Because `hasPermission` returns `true` if any of the passed scopes are granted on the `Groups` resource, an administrator who has only been granted the `view` scope on all groups will have `canManage()` evaluate to `true`. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` guards top-level group creation and group moves with `auth.groups().requireManage()`, so any user with `view` permission on all groups can create and move top-level groups. `canManage()` should only check `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (and the Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` at lines 75-76 should be updated accordingly).

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() in GroupPermissionsV2 never finds group resources and returns resource IDs instead of group IDs
body:
In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (lines 121-125), `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` is used to iterate over group resources, and inside the consumer `groupResource.getId()` is passed to `hasPermission(...)` and added to `granted`. There are three bugs here:
1. When per-group resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (lines 121-127), `resource.setType(...)` is never called, so individual group resources have `type == null` (only the all-groups resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` has `type = "Groups"`). `findByType` therefore never matches any individual group resource.
2. `groupResource.getName()` holds the `GroupModel` ID (set in `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`), whereas `groupResource.getId()` is the internal authorization `Resource` UUID. Passing `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` looks up `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, which will not find the resource by name, and adding `groupResource.getId()` to `granted` returns `Resource` UUIDs instead of group IDs to `UserModel.GROUPS` search filters.
3. For the `Groups` resource type resource itself (`name == "Groups"`), `granted.add(...)` would add the resource UUID rather than actual group IDs.

title: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName does not resolve Group (or Client) resource names
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` (lines 328-350) only handles `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` and otherwise falls back to `resource.getDisplayName()`. When a group resource is created in `getOrCreateResource`, its `name` is set to the group's UUID (`resolveGroup` returns `group.getId()`) and `displayName` is not set. As a result, fetching policy/permission representations for `Groups` resources will return `null` (or the raw UUID) as the resource name instead of `"All groups"` or the group's name/path.

title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers
body: On line 133 of `GroupPermissionEvaluator.java`, the Javadoc for `void requireManageMembers(GroupModel group)` states `Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}.` It should reference `{@link #canManageMembers(GroupModel)}`.

title: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants global manage access on VIEW scope
body: In `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()`, line 70 calls `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Passing `AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW` here means any user granted the `view` scope on the `all-groups` resource will also pass `canManage()` / `requireManage()`. Since `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` checks `auth.groups().requireManage()`, a user with only `view` permission on all groups can create top-level groups or move existing groups to top level. `canManage()` should only check for `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (and the Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` at line 75 should be updated accordingly).

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses resource.getId() instead of resource.getName() (and resources lacked type)
body:
In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` iterates over group resources and calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())`. However:
1. When `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates a resource for a specific group, it sets the resource's `name` to the `group.getId()` (while `resource.getId()` is an auto-generated resource UUID), and `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` looks up the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. Passing `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission` will not find the group resource by name, and adding `groupResource.getId()` to `granted` returns the authorization resource UUID instead of the `GroupModel` ID expected by `session.users().searchForUserStream` / `getUsersCount`.
2. Furthermore, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` does not call `resource.setType(resourceType)` when creating a per-entity resource—only the 'all-groups' resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` has `type = "Groups"`. As a result, `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` will only ever find the `Groups` (all-groups) resource and never individual group resources.

title: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName() does not handle GROUPS resource type
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` resolves human-readable names for resources in the admin permissions client (currently handling `USERS`), and falls back to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Because `GROUPS` is not handled here and `getOrCreateResource` does not set a displayName on created group resources, `getResourceName` will return `null` (or the raw UUID) for group resources when representations are built.

title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers

Because `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` checks `auth.groups().requireManage()`, any user granted only the `view` scope on the all-groups (`Groups`) resource will be allowed to create top-level groups and move existing child groups to the top level. `canManage()` should only check `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (and the Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` at line 75 should be updated accordingly).

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() in GroupPermissionsV2 never finds group resources and returns resource IDs instead of group IDs
body:
There are three bugs in `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`:
1. It searches with `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`, but when individual group resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (lines 121-128), `resource.setType(...)` is never called, so individual group resources have a `null` type. Only the all-groups resource (`Groups`) has type `GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE`.
2. Inside the callback it calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`, but `hasPermission` looks up the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` where the resource's `name` is the group's ID, not the authorization resource's ID.
3. It adds `groupResource.getId()` (the authz resource UUID, or the `Groups` resource UUID) to `granted` instead of `groupResource.getName()` (the Keycloak group ID), which is then used to filter user group memberships in `UserModel.GROUPS`.

title: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName() does not handle GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE
body: `getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` only resolves display names for `USERS` resources and falls back to `resource.getDisplayName()` otherwise. Because `getOrCreateResource` creates group resources with the group's UUID as the resource name and no display name, policies targeting `Groups` resources will have `null` (or raw UUIDs) as resource names when converted to representations instead of "All groups" or the group's name/path.

title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers
body: The Javadoc on `requireManageMembers(GroupModel group)` says `Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}.` It should reference `{@link #canManageMembers(GroupModel)}`.

title: ANCHOR_PATTERN matches any tag starting with 'a' and is case-sensitive
body: `ANCHOR_PATTERN` is defined as `Pattern.compile("</?a[^>]*>")`. Because `a` is not followed by a word boundary or whitespace check, this regex matches any HTML tag whose name begins with `a` (such as `<applet>`, `<audio>`, `<area>`, `<aside>`, `<article>`, or `<abbr>`) and strips it in `santizeAnchors` if the English string happens to contain the same tag. More importantly, it is case-sensitive and requires `a` to be immediately after `<` or `</`, so a translation containing `<A href="javascript:alert(1)">` or `<a/href=...>` or an unclosed `<a href=...` will not be matched by `ANCHOR_PATTERN`, and `santizeAnchors` will not report an anchor mismatch (though OWASP sanitizer may strip it later, the specific anchor validation is bypassed or produces confusing errors). Additionally, in `santizeAnchors`, if the English message has `<a href="...">` and the translation omits the anchor tag completely, the `while (matcher.find())` loop does not execute at all, silently allowing translations that drop links.

title: Unescaping HTML4 entities on both input and sanitized output allows entity-encoded XSS payloads to pass verification
body: `normalizeValue` calls `StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(value)` before sanitization (line 130), and `verifySafeHtml` calls `StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(sanitized)` after sanitization (line 95) before comparing `sanitized` with `value`. If a `.properties` file contains HTML-escaped dangerous markup such as `<script>alert(1)</script>` or `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>`, `normalizeValue` unescapes it into raw `<script>...</script>`, the OWASP sanitizer strips the disallowed tag, and the check catches it. However, if a translation contains plain text that OWASP sanitizer escapes into HTML entities (for example `<` or `&` or quotes inside attributes), unescaping `sanitized` turns `<script>` back into `<script>`. Specifically, if a translation has double-escaped entities like `&lt;script&gt;`, `normalizeValue` unescapes it once to `<script>`, OWASP sanitizer leaves `<script>` intact (or normalizes it), and then line 95 unescapes `sanitized` a second time to `<script>`, causing a false mismatch or, conversely, if `value` had `<1>` (which OWASP escapes to `<1>`), line 95 unescapes it back to `<1>`. Any tag that OWASP sanitizer *neutralizes by entity-encoding* rather than stripping (for example, unrecognized numeric/custom tags or text following `<`) is unescaped back to its raw `<...>` form on line 95 and thus equals `value`, bypassing the sanitizer check completely.

title: Substring index out of bounds when value and sanitized share both a prefix and a suffix
body: When computing the diff snippet for the error message (lines 102-111), `start` is incremented from the front and `end` is incremented from the back independently without ensuring `start + end <= Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length())`. If `value` and `sanitized` have overlapping matching prefixes and suffixes (for example, `value` is `"<b><b>"` and `sanitized` is `"<b>"`, where `start` reaches 3 and `end` reaches 3), `sanitized.length() - end` becomes `0`, which is less than `start` (`3`), causing `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` on line 111 to throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

title: Unescaping HTML entities after sanitization allows entity-encoded HTML/XSS payloads to bypass verification
body: In `normalizeValue` (line 130), `StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(value)` converts HTML entities in the raw property value into literal characters before sanitization, and line 95 calls `StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(sanitized)` on the sanitizer's output before comparing `sanitized` with `value`. title: `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` when `value` and `sanitized` share a prefix and suffix that overlap
body: When computing the diff slice between `value` and `sanitized`, `start` is incremented from the front and `end` is incremented from the back independently without ensuring `start + end <= Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length())`. title: Unescaping HTML entities before and after sanitization allows entity-encoded XSS/HTML injection bypass
body: In `VerifyMessageProperties.java`, `normalizeValue` (line 130) calls `StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(value)` on the raw property value, and line 95 calls `StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(sanitized)` on the OWASP sanitizer's output before comparing `sanitized` and `value`. Because OWASP HTML Sanitizer encodes dangerous characters or stripped/disallowed constructs into HTML entities, unescaping both sides means a translation containing entity-encoded HTML (for example `<script>alert(1)</script>` or `<img src=x onerror=...>`) will be unescaped to `<script>alert(1)</script>` in `normalizeValue`, Or if double-encoded (e.g. `&lt;script&gt;`), `normalizeValue` turns it into `<script>`, the OWASP sanitizer leaves `<script>` untouched (or re-encodes `&` to `&lt;`), and `unescapeHtml4(sanitized)` turns it back into `<script>`, matching `value`! Even worse, for single-encoded entities like `<script>` vs `<script>`, if a template or UI component unescapes or renders entities, or if someone puts `<b>` where HTML is disallowed, the interplay of `unescapeHtml4` can mask differences between escaped text and markup.

title: StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when value and sanitized have overlapping prefix and suffix
body: In `VerifyMessageProperties.java` lines 102-111, `start` is incremented from the beginning while characters match, and `end` is incremented from the end while characters match, without ensuring `start + end <= Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length())`. When a string has repeated characters around the difference (for example, `value = "<b><b>"` and `sanitized = "<b>"`), `start` reaches 3 and `end` reaches 3, so `sanitized.length() - end` is `0`, causing `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` on line 111 to throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: begin 3, end 0, length 3` instead of reporting the validation message.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text for totpStep1
body: In `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties` line 101 (and identically in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` line 71), the Lithuanian message for `totpStep1` / `loginTotpStep1` was replaced with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian instead of Lithuanian.

title: Simplified Chinese translation replaced with Traditional Chinese text for totpStep1
body: In `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_zh_CN.properties` line 112, `totpStep1` in the Simplified Chinese (`zh_CN`) bundle was replaced with Traditional Chinese characters (`在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`) instead of Simplified Chinese (compare with `loginTotpStep1` in `login/messages/messages_zh_CN.properties`: `在您的移动设备中安装以下任意一个应用：`).

title: Wrong substring indices and inverted boolean condition in `isAccessTokenId` matcher
body:
In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` has two bugs:
1. The encoded context prefix is 6 characters long (`<2-char sessionType><2-char tokenType><2-char grantType>`), so the grant type shortcut is at indices `(4, 6)` (matching `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` line 81), not `(3, 5)`.
2. The equality check is not negated (`equals` instead of `!equals`), so it returns `false` when the substring matches the expected shortcut and `true` when it does not. The test only passes right now because `substring(3, 5)` extracts the wrong characters (e.g., `"ta"` from `"onrtac"`), which never equals `expectedGrantShortcut`.

title: `AccessTokenContext` constructor checks `grantType` for null twice instead of checking `rawTokenId`
body: Line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. As a result, a `null` `rawTokenId` is silently accepted and stored in `AccessTokenContext`, rather than throwing a `NullPointerException` with the intended message.

title: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` accepts `"un"` (`UNKNOWN`) shortcuts for session type and token type
body: `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.init` populates `sessionTypesByShortcut` and `tokenTypesByShortcut` using `SessionType.values()` and `TokenType.values()`, which include `SessionType.UNKNOWN("un")` and `TokenType.UNKNOWN("un")`. Consequently, `getTokenContextFromTokenId("ununac:1234")` resolves `st` and `tt` to `UNKNOWN` instead of rejecting the token ID as invalid, even though `encodeTokenId` explicitly forbids encoding `UNKNOWN` for `SessionType` or `TokenType`.

title: Potential `NullPointerException` in `OAuth2GrantType.Context` constructor when `formParams` is null
body: In `OAuth2GrantType.Context`, `this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);` dereferences `formParams` unconditionally. If `Context` is constructed before form parameters are parsed or in a test/caller passing `null` (note that `setFormParams` exists on `Context`), this will throw a `NullPointerException`. Also, `setFormParams` does not update `this.grantType` when form parameters are replaced.

title: Javadoc for `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` says 3-letters shortcut, but implementation requires 2 characters
body: The Javadoc on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` states `@return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants`, whereas `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` strictly requires the total encoded context to be 6 characters with each grant shortcut being exactly 2 characters (lines 74-81). A custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementer following the Javadoc and returning a 3-letter shortcut will cause `getTokenContextFromTokenId` to fail with `IllegalArgumentException: Expected length of 6`.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong substring indices and inverted equality check
body:
In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut)`, line 483 checks:

```java
if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;
```

There are two bugs here:
1. The encoded context prefix is 6 characters long (`<2-char sessionType><2-char tokenType><2-char grantType>`), so the grant type shortcut is at indices `(4, 6)` (matching `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` line 81: `encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`), not `(3, 5)`. `substring(3, 5)` extracts the second character of the token type and the first character of the grant type.
2. The condition is not negated: it returns `false` when the substring *equals* `expectedGrantShortcut`, and only passes because `substring(3, 5)` never equals the expected grant shortcut. As a result, the matcher accepts any 5+ character prefix whose characters `[3..5)` do not equal `expectedGrantShortcut`, instead of verifying that `items[0]` has length 6 and ends with `expectedGrantShortcut`.

title: Copy-paste bug in AccessTokenContext constructor checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
body:
In the `AccessTokenContext` constructor, line 73 calls:

```java
Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");
```

It checks `grantType` a second time instead of checking `rawTokenId`. A `null` `rawTokenId` will therefore not be rejected at construction time and will instead be concatenated as the literal string `"null"` when `encodeTokenId` builds the token ID.

title: Javadoc for OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() says 3-letters shortcut instead of 2 characters
body: The Javadoc on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` states `@return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants`, whereas `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` requires the entire encoded context (`sessionType + tokenType + grantType`) to be exactly 6 characters long (2 characters per field) and throws `IllegalArgumentException` if a grant type shortcut is not 2 characters.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong substring indices and inverted equality check
body:
In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` has two bugs:

1. The encoded context prefix is 6 characters long (`<2-char sessionType><2-char tokenType><2-char grantType>`, see `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java` lines 78-81 where `gtShortcut = encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`). Using `substring(3, 5)` extracts the second character of `tokenType` and the first character of `grantType` (e.g. `"ta"` for `"onrtac"`) instead of the grant shortcut at indices 4..6.
2. The condition is inverted: it returns `false` when the substring equals `expectedGrantShortcut` instead of when it does `!equals(...)`. Because `substring(3, 5)` almost never matches a valid grant shortcut, the matcher currently passes even when the grant shortcut in the token ID is completely wrong.

It should check `if (items[0].length() != 6 || !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

title: Constructor checks grantType for null twice instead of checking rawTokenId
body: In the `AccessTokenContext` constructor, line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. As a result, a null `rawTokenId` is not rejected at construction time.

title: Javadoc says 3-letter shortcut, but implementation requires exactly 2 characters
body: The Javadoc on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` states `@return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants`, whereas `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` requires the full encoded prefix to be 6 characters (2 characters per part, with `encodedContext.substring(4, 6)` for the grant shortcut) and all implementations return 2-character strings. A custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` author following the Javadoc and returning a 3-letter shortcut would cause `getTokenContextFromTokenId` to fail with `IllegalArgumentException: Expected length of 6`.

title: Potential NullPointerException in getCredentials when user is not in storage
body: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(RealmModel, UserModel)`, `myUser` is retrieved via `getMyUser(user)` and immediately dereferenced on lines 235 (`myUser.recoveryCodes != null`) and 247 (`myUser.otp != null`) without a null check. In contrast, `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isConfiguredFor`, and `isValid` in the same class all guard against `myUser == null` before accessing fields on `myUser`. If `getCredentials` is invoked for a user not present in the `users` map, it will throw a `NullPointerException` instead of returning an empty stream.

title: hasRecoveryCodes does not normalize username to lowercase before map lookup
body: `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` stores and looks up users in the shared `users` (`userPasswords`) map using `translateUserName(username)` (i.e. `username.toLowerCase()`). In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageFactory.hasRecoveryCodes(String username)`, `userPasswords.get(username)` is called directly without lowercasing `username`, so calling `hasRecoveryCodes` with any uppercase characters will return `false` even when the user has recovery codes stored.

title: `getCredentials` is not a `UserStorageProvider` or `CredentialInputValidator` method and violates the 4.8.3 compatibility contract of this test provider
body: `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` is specifically designed to simulate a legacy Keycloak 4.8.3 `UserStorageProvider` (which only implements `UserLookupProvider`, `UserStorageProvider`, `UserRegistrationProvider`, `CredentialInputUpdater`, `CredentialInputValidator`, and `UserQueryProvider`). However, `@Override public Stream<CredentialModel> getCredentials(RealmModel realm, UserModel user)` was added to it (along with `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`, which did not exist in 4.8.3). A legacy user storage provider that only implements `CredentialInputUpdater`/`CredentialInputValidator` will not return `CredentialModel` instances from `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()`, which instead queries `UserCredentialStore` (federated storage), not `UserStorageProvider`. If a real custom `UserStorageProvider` stores recovery codes via `updateCredential`, `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` will return `Optional.empty()`, causing `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` (line 19: `credentialModelOpt.get()`) to throw `NoSuchElementException` when rendering the recovery code login form.

title: Unchecked Optional.get() throws NoSuchElementException when user storage does not expose CredentialModel
body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` returns an `Optional<CredentialModel>` by streaming `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()` and `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...)`. However, custom `UserStorageProvider` implementations that implement `CredentialInputValidator` and `CredentialInputUpdater` (such as the 4.8.3 backwards-compatibility storage, before this PR added `getCredentials` to it) are not required to override `getCredentials(RealmModel, UserModel)` (whose default implementation in `CredentialInputValidator` returns `Stream.empty()`). For such providers, `isConfiguredFor` returns `true`, so `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` challenges the user and renders the login form, instantiating `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`. Calling `credentialModelOpt.get()` (and `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()` on line 21) without checking `isPresent()` will throw `NoSuchElementException` when rendering the login form if the provider does not return a `CredentialModel` from `getCredentials()`.

title: Possible NullPointerException in getCredentials when user is not found in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage
body: In `getCredentials(RealmModel realm, UserModel user)`, `var myUser = getMyUser(user);` can return `null` if the user is not present in the `users` map (note that `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isConfiguredFor`, and `isValid` in the same class all guard against `myUser == null`). Dereferencing `myUser.recoveryCodes` on line 235 without a null check will throw a `NullPointerException` when `getCredentials` is invoked for a user not managed by this storage.

title: Background reader thread is not joined before asserting or exiting the test
body: In `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the background `Thread` that continuously reads groups is started on line 139, and the main thread immediately asserts `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` after setting `deletedAll.set(true)` without calling `thread.join()`. If an in-flight `groups()` call is still executing when the last group is deleted and throws an exception slightly after `deletedAll` is set, the assertion can pass before `caughtExceptions.add(e)` runs, masking a failure. In addition, the still-running request can leak into subsequent tests in `GroupTest`. Store the `Thread` reference and `join()` it before asserting on `caughtExceptions`.

title: Paginated getSubGroupsStream overloads still dereference null modelSupplier.get() when group is concurrently deleted
body: `getSubGroupsCount()` was updated to guard against `modelSupplier.get()` returning `null` when the cached group has been concurrently removed from the database, but the three overloaded `getSubGroupsStream(...)` methods right above it (lines 256, 262, and 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` directly. If any of those methods are invoked on a `GroupAdapter` whose underlying group was concurrently deleted, `modelSupplier.get()` returns `null` and a `NullPointerException` is thrown. They should handle a `null` model (for example by returning `Stream.empty()`).

title: Background reader thread in createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti is never joined before asserting or exiting the test
body: In `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, a background `Thread` is started at line 139 that continuously calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` until `deletedAll.get()` is true. After the main thread sets `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155, it immediately asserts `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` without calling `thread.join()`. If an in-flight HTTP request on the reader thread fails with an exception after `deletedAll.set(true)` is executed, that exception will be added to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion has already passed, resulting in a false pass. Furthermore, the still-running thread can continue executing into subsequent tests in `GroupTest`, interfering with their realm state or admin event assertions.

title: Overloaded getSubGroupsStream methods in GroupAdapter still dereference a potentially null modelSupplier.get()
body: `getSubGroupsCount()` at line 274 was updated to check whether `modelSupplier.get()` returns `null` (which happens when a cached group was concurrently deleted from the database). However, the three overloaded `getSubGroupsStream` methods right above it (lines 256, 262, and 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` directly without a null check. If a group is deleted concurrently while any of those `getSubGroupsStream` overloads is invoked on a cached `GroupAdapter`, `modelSupplier.get()` will return `null` and throw a `NullPointerException` instead of returning `Stream.empty()`.

title: Background reader thread in createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti is not joined before asserting or exiting
body: In `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, a background `Thread` is started at line 139 that loops until `deletedAll.get()` is true, calling `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` and adding any thrown exceptions to `caughtExceptions`. After the main thread sets `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155, it immediately asserts `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` without calling `join()` on the background thread. If the background thread is in the middle of an HTTP request when `deletedAll` is set, two problems arise: (1) an exception thrown by that in-flight request will be added to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion has already passed, masking a test failure; and (2) the thread continues running into subsequent test methods in `GroupTest`, issuing concurrent requests against the shared `managedRealm`. Store the `Thread` reference and `join()` it before asserting `caughtExceptions`.

title: `organization_context.member` can be `None`, raising `AttributeError`
body: In `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get`, `enable_advanced` accesses `organization_context.member.has_global_access` whenever `request.user.is_superuser` is false. On `RpcUserOrganizationContext`, `member` is optional (`RpcOrganizationMember | None`) and can be `None` (for example, for system/API token requests or non-member contexts). When a non-superuser calls this endpoint in such a context, evaluating `organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'`, breaking all GET requests to the audit logs endpoint even when `optimized_pagination` is not requested.

title: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` crashes on `datetime` ordering and `enable_advanced_features` is rejected by `self.paginate`
body:
When `optimized_pagination=true` is used, `self.paginate` is called with `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator`, `order_by="-datetime"`, and `enable_advanced_features=True`. This fails in two ways:
1. `Endpoint.paginate` only forwards `paginator_kwargs` (not arbitrary `**kwargs` like `enable_advanced_features`) to the paginator constructor, so passing `enable_advanced_features=True` directly to `self.paginate()` raises `TypeError: paginate() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_advanced_features'`.
2. `OptimizedCursorPaginator` subclasses `BasePaginator` rather than `DateTimePaginator`: its `get_item_key` calls `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` directly on `item.datetime` (a `datetime.datetime` instance), raising `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`, and its `value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric cursor value instead of converting it back to a `datetime` for comparing against a `DateTimeField`.

title: Negative cursor offsets cause `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported` on Django `QuerySet` slicing
body: Both `BasePaginator.get_result` (lines 182-184, when `cursor.is_prev` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`) and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (lines 880-886, when `cursor.offset < 0` with `enable_advanced_features=True` or `cursor.is_prev=True`) pass a negative `start_offset` (and potentially negative `stop`) into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Contrary to the comments claiming Django ORM handles negative slicing, Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly forbids negative slice bounds (`if (k.start is not None and k.start < 0) or (k.stop is not None and k.stop < 0): raise ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.')`). Any request supplying a cursor with a negative offset (e.g. `?cursor=0:-10:1` on any endpoint using `BasePaginator`/`Paginator`/`DateTimePaginator`) will raise an unhandled `ValueError` (HTTP 500).

title: AttributeError when accessing organization_context.member for non-members (e.g. superusers)
body: `organization_context.member` can be `None` when the request is made by a user who is not a member of the organization (or if short-circuit evaluation falls through when `request.user.is_superuser` is False and `organization_context.member` is `None`). Accessing `organization_context.member.has_global_access` without checking if `organization_context.member` is `None` can raise `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'`.

title: `self.paginate()` does not accept `enable_advanced_features` and `OptimizedCursorPaginator` breaks on `datetime` fields
body:
In `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get`, `self.paginate(...)` is called with `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator`, `order_by='-datetime'`, and `enable_advanced_features=True`. This will fail for two reasons:
1. `Endpoint.paginate` only forwards specific arguments to `paginator_cls` (`max_limit`, `on_results`, `paginator_kwargs`, etc.) unless passed via `paginator_kwargs={'enable_advanced_features': True}`; passing `enable_advanced_features` directly to `self.paginate` raises a `TypeError: paginate() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_advanced_features'`.
2. `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` directly on `getattr(item, 'datetime')` (which is a `datetime.datetime` instance on `AuditLogEntry`) and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric `cursor.value` instead of converting a timestamp back to a `datetime` object like `DateTimePaginator` does. This causes a `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` when building cursors and invalid SQL comparisons when querying.

title: Django `QuerySet` does not support negative slicing offsets, causing `ValueError`
body: Both `BasePaginator.get_result` (when `cursor.is_prev` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`) and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (lines 877-886) pass a negative `start_offset` (and potentially negative `stop`) into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`.
