If a request supplies both a non-empty `totpCode` (e.g., `"1"`) and a `backupCode`, `verifyPassword` is skipped and the user is authenticated using only the backup code without verifying either their password or TOTP token.

title: Closing the modal on the backup codes step without clicking 'Close' leaves 2FA UI state out of sync and form state dirty
body: When `TwoFactorAuthAPI.enable(totpCode)` returns HTTP 200 in `handleEnable`, 2FA is already enabled on the server, but `onEnable()` is now deferred until the user clicks the `backup-codes-close` button (line 269). If the user dismisses the dialog at `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` by pressing Escape or clicking the backdrop (`onOpenChange`), neither `onEnable()` nor `resetState()` runs, leaving the 2FA switch on the settings page unchecked even though 2FA is enabled in the database. In addition, `resetState()` (lines 71-75) never clears `totpCode` in `form`, so the 6-digit code remains in React Hook Form state if the modal is cancelled or reopened without reloading the page.

title: First 2FA E2E test does not awaitbackup code completion and races with /auth/logout
body: In the first test (`"should allow a user to enable 2FA and login using 2FA"`), after `fillOtp` fills the 6th digit (lines 44-48), the test does not wait for the backup codes step or click `backup-codes-close`. Line 52 (`waitForSelector('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]')`) resolves immediately because the switch is already in the DOM behind the modal, and line 53 (`expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy()`) passes an unawaited `Promise<boolean>` to `toBeTruthy()`, which always passes immediately. The test then navigates to `/auth/logout` on line 59 while the `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/enable` POST request triggered by `fillOtp` may still be in flight.

title: Passing type="password" to PasswordField breaks the show/hide password toggle
body: `EnableTwoFactorModal` switches from `TextField` to `PasswordField` on line 174 but still passes `type="password"` on line 176. In `packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx` (lines 35-39), `PasswordField` renders `<InputField type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"} ... {...props} />`, spreading `{...props}` after its computed `type`. Passing `type="password"` in `props` overrides the toggle state so clicking the eye icon button never reveals the password.

title: Cancelling or closing DisableTwoFactorModal does not reset twoFactorLostAccess, form values, or errors
body: `resetForm()` and `setTwoFactorLostAccess(false)` are only called when disabling 2FA succeeds (lines 60-61), not when the user clicks Cancel (`onClick={onCancel}` on line 122) or dismisses the dialog (`onOpenChange` on line 89). If a user switches to the backup code view or triggers an error and then cancels and reopens the modal, it reopens on the backup code screen with the stale error message and form values still present.

title: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition breaks organization slug assignment
body: In `createHandler`, `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` was changed to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. This inverts the intended logic in an unrelated file: when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is `false`, newly created organizations will have neither `slug` nor `metadata.requestedSlug` set, and when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is `true`, the slug is assigned immediately before billing completes.

title: Null-dereference on mainHostDestinationCalendar when destinationCalendar is empty or null
body: In `EventManager.create`, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or `[]`. On line 119, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` is evaluated without optional chaining, which throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType` and no destination calendar is set.

title: Collective hosts' destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destinationCalendar
body: At lines 1063-1067, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is defined. At line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining on `null` and becomes a no-op, silently dropping all other collective hosts' `destinationCalendar` entries.

title: Broken fallback calendar lookup in GoogleCalendarService updateEvent, deleteEvent, and createEvent patch
body: In `updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback branch of `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`null`, `undefined`, or `""`), so `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` can never match a destination calendar and `selectedCalendar` evaluates to `undefined`. Additionally, in `createEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is now `string | undefined` (`"primary"` is only applied inline at line 154), so `calendar.events.patch` at line 168 passes `calendarId: undefined` instead of `"primary"` when updating the event with a Hangout link.

title: Non-Google calendar services always use the primary host's destinationCalendar for all hosts
body: `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` (line 73), `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` and `createAttendees` (`packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` lines 128, 164), and `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` line 156) all destructure `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` instead of matching by `credentialId`. In a collective booking, when `createEvent` runs for any host other than the first, these services use the first host's `externalId` (which belongs to another user and potentially a different calendar provider), causing event creation on Office 365, Lark, and CalDAV calendars to fail or be skipped for additional hosts.

title: Recurring booking cancellation only uses organizer credentials and first calendar reference
body: When cancelling all remaining instances of a recurring booking (`allRemainingBookings`), lines 449-461 iterate over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` (only the primary organizer's credentials, ignoring `calendarCredential` fetched from the database for other collective hosts) and look up `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` (only the first calendar reference). Because this block is also nested inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`, it repeats the organizer's deletions for each reference while never deleting the recurring events from other collective hosts' calendars.

title: Unchecked undefined credential passed to updateEvent in updateAllCalendarEvents
body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents` (lines 511-542), if `reference.credentialId` is not found in `this.calendarCredentials` and the database lookup either returns `null` or a credential without `app?.slug`, `credential` remains `undefined`. Unlike `createAllCalendarEvents` (line 369), line 542 calls `updateEvent(credential, ...)` without checking `if (credential)`, which causes `CalendarManager.updateEvent` to throw when accessing `credential.appName`.

title: Unchecked property access on mainHostDestinationCalendar crashes when destinationCalendar is empty or null
body: When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or `[]` (which is now the default when a user has no destination calendar), `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` evaluates `mainHostDestinationCalendar` to `undefined`. Line 119 then accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining (`?.`), throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` whenever an event with `MeetLocationType` (Google Meet) is created for a user without a destination calendar.

title: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED check breaks organization slug assignment
body: Line 151 changed `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` in an unrelated file. Previously, `slug` was set directly only when billing was disabled, and stored as `metadata.requestedSlug` when billing was enabled until payment completed. With the inverted condition, self-hosted/non-billing instances (`IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED === false`) create organizations with neither `slug` nor `requestedSlug`, while billing-enabled instances immediately assign `slug` before payment.

title: Non-Google calendar services always use the first host's destinationCalendar instead of matching the credential
body: In a collective booking, `event.destinationCalendar` contains the destination calendars of all hosts, and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` calls `createEvent` once per host credential with the full `event`. Unlike `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent` (which looks up the entry matching `credentialId`), `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` (line 73), `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` (`packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` lines 128 and 164), and `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` line 156) all take `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`. When a secondary host uses Office 365, Lark, or CalDAV/Apple Calendar, their service will use the first host's `externalId` (e.g., a Google Calendar address), causing Office 365 and Lark API calls to fail with 404/invalid calendar ID and causing `BaseCalendarService` to filter out all calendars and silently skip creating the event.

title: Fallback calendar lookup in updateEvent and deleteEvent can never match and leaves calendarId undefined
body: In `updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback branch of `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`undefined`, `null`, or `""`). Comparing `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` against a falsy value will never match any `DestinationCalendar` (whose `externalId` is a non-empty string), so the fallback always evaluates to `undefined`. In `updateEvent`, `selectedCalendar` also has no `"primary"` fallback, so `calendar.events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined`. Similarly, in `createEvent` (line 168), `calendar.events.patch` passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without `|| "primary"`, which is `undefined` when no `destinationCalendar` matches `credentialId`.

title: Collective host destination calendars are dropped when organizer and eventType have no destinationCalendar
body: Lines 1063-1067 initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` to `null` when both `eventType.destinationCalendar` and `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` are null. Line 1078 then executes `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`. As a result, if the primary organizer has no `destinationCalendar` set, all other collective hosts' `destinationCalendar` entries in `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded.

title: updateAllCalendarEvents calls updateEvent even when the referenced credential is undefined
body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents` (lines 511-543), if `reference.credentialId` is not found in `this.calendarCredentials` and the database lookup (`credentialFromDB`) returns `null` or has no `app.slug`, `credential` remains `undefined`. Unlike `createAllCalendarEvents` (line 369), line 542 calls `updateEvent(credential, ...)` without checking `if (credential)`. `CalendarManager.updateEvent` then accesses `credential.appName` (line 314) and throws a `TypeError`, causing `Promise.all(result)` to reject and abort updates for the remaining calendar references.

title: updateLocation sets undefined externalCalendarId and credentialId on calendar references
body: In `EventManager.updateLocation` (lines 201-211), `referencesToCreate` now reads `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. However, `CalendarManager.updateEvent` (called by `updateAllCalendarEvents`) does not populate `externalId` or `credentialId` on its returned `EventResult` (nor does it set `createdEvent`), so calendar results in `updateLocation` produce duplicate `BookingReference` entries with `uid: ""`, `externalCalendarId: undefined`, and `credentialId: undefined`.

title: Unchecked property access on mainHostDestinationCalendar crashes when destinationCalendar is empty or null
body: In `EventManager.create`, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` will set `mainHostDestinationCalendar` to `undefined` whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or `[]`. On line 119, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` accesses `.integration` without optional chaining (`?.`), throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` for any Google Meet booking where the host has no destination calendar configured.

title: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition breaks organization slug assignment
body: Line 151 changed `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, inverting the boolean condition in a file unrelated to `destinationCalendar`. When `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is `false`, newly created organizations will have neither `slug` nor `metadata.requestedSlug` set, leaving them without a slug; when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is `true`, `slug` is prematurely assigned before billing is completed.

title: Co-hosts' destination calendars are dropped when the primary organizer has no destination calendar
body: Lines 1063-1067 set `evt.destinationCalendar` to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is defined. On line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` becomes a no-op due to optional chaining on `null`, so if the primary host has no `destinationCalendar` configured, all other collective hosts' `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded and no events are created in their destination calendars.

title: Fallback calendar lookup in updateEvent and deleteEvent can never match and leaves calendarId undefined
body: In `updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback branch of `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`null`, `undefined`, or `""`). Comparing `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` in that branch compares a non-empty calendar ID string against a falsy value and always evaluates to `undefined`. In `updateEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is passed directly as `calendarId` without defaulting to `"primary"`, causing `calendar.events.update` to fail whenever `externalCalendarId` is not present on the booking reference.

title: calendar.events.patch receives undefined calendarId when selectedCalendar is not found
body: In `createEvent`, `selectedCalendar` (lines 147-149) is `undefined` when no `destinationCalendar` entry matches `credentialId` (for example, when `destinationCalendar` is empty or has a `null` `credentialId`). While `calendar.events.insert` on line 154 falls back with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, `calendar.events.patch` on line 168 passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly, which is `undefined` and causes patching the Google Meet hangout link into the event description to fail.

title: Non-Google calendar services always use the first host's destinationCalendar instead of matching the credential
body: In `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` (line 73), `LarkCalendarService.createEvent`/`createAttendees` (`packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` lines 128 and 164), and `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` line 156), the target calendar is selected via `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` rather than finding the entry matching the credential being used. In a collective booking where a secondary host uses Office365, Lark, or CalDAV, these services will use `event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId` (the primary host's calendar ID, potentially from a different provider like Google Calendar), causing event creation for the secondary host to fail or be skipped.

title: updateAllCalendarEvents calls updateEvent even when credential lookup returns undefined
body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents` (lines 511-542), if `reference.credentialId` is not in `this.calendarCredentials` and the database lookup either finds no credential or `credentialFromDB.app?.slug` is nullish, `credential` remains `undefined`. Unlike `createAllCalendarEvents` (line 369), line 542 does not guard with `if (credential)` before calling `updateEvent(credential, ...)`, which will throw a `TypeError` when `updateEvent` accesses `credential.appName`.

title: Cancelling all remaining recurring bookings in a collective event ignores co-host credentials and references
body: Inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` (lines 423-472), when `allRemainingBookings` is true for a recurring event, lines 449-461 ignore the resolved `calendar` for `reference.credentialId` and instead iterate over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and only delete the first calendar reference (`updBooking.references.find(...)`) of each recurring booking. For collective bookings with multiple hosts, this repeats deletions on the primary organizer's calendar once per reference while never deleting the recurring event instances from the other hosts' calendars.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses [object Object] as property keys and strips expiry fields
body: In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` call `Object.prototype.toString()` on Zod schema instances, which both evaluate to the literal key `"[object Object]"`. The second computed property overwrites the first, and because `z.object()` strips unknown keys by default, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` neither validates that a numeric expiry field exists nor preserves expiry fields such as `expires_in` or `expiry_date` in `refreshTokenResponse.data`. Downstream callers that read `expires_in` or `expiry_date` from the parsed result (e.g. Zoom and Office 365) will get `undefined` / `NaN`.

title: Defaulting missing refresh_token to literal "refresh_token" overwrites valid stored refresh tokens
body: Lines 25-27 set `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` whenever the refresh response omits `refresh_token`, even when credential sharing is disabled. For providers like Office 365 where the refresh response may omit `refresh_token` (`refreshTokenResponseSchema` defines `refresh_token: z.string().optional()`) and the parsed data is merged onto the existing credential (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`), this overwrites the user's real `refresh_token` in the database with the literal string `"refresh_token"`, breaking future token refreshes.

title: GoogleCalendarService saves the SafeParseReturnType wrapper object into credential.key and fails on fetch Response
body: There are two bugs in `refreshAccessToken`: (1) `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed credential object that `googleCredentialSchema.parse()` previously returned. Passing `key` directly to `prisma.credential.update` overwrites `credential.key` in the database with `{ success: true, data: ... }`, which causes `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on line 75 to throw on all subsequent requests even when credential syncing is disabled. (2) When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response` object rather than a Gaxios response with `.data`, so `const token = res?.data` on line 94 is `undefined` and `token.access_token` throws a `TypeError`.

title: Missing prisma import, missing refreshOAuthTokens call, and stale accessToken used in SalesforceCalendarService
body: In `SalesforceCalendarService.getClient`: (1) line 96 calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)`, but `prisma` is not imported in this file, causing a build error and runtime `ReferenceError`; (2) line 75 calls `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` directly instead of wrapping the request in `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce token refreshes never use `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`; and (3) after refreshing the token, line 106 passes the old `credentialKey.access_token` to `new jsforce.Connection` instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

title: BiginCalendarService passes credentialId instead of userId to refreshOAuthTokens and expects an Axios response
body: In `BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, line 93 passes `credentialId` (the primary key of the credential row) as the third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` instead of `credential.userId`, sending the wrong ID as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint. Additionally, the `refreshFunction` callback returns an Axios response (`{ data: ... }`), whereas `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` when credential syncing is enabled, so `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` on line 96 will throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')`.

title: ZohoCrmCalendarService expects an Axios response object from refreshOAuthTokens
body: In `ZohoCrmCalendarService`, the `refreshFunction` callback passed to `refreshOAuthTokens` uses `axios` and returns `{ data: ... }`, but when credential syncing is enabled `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` object where `.data` is `undefined`. Accessing `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` on line 217 will throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')`.

title: HubspotCalendarService treats the fetch Response from refreshOAuthTokens as a parsed HubspotToken
body: When credential syncing is disabled, `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken` resolves to a parsed `TokenResponseIF` object (`{ accessToken, expiresIn, ... }`). When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns an unparsed `fetch` `Response` object. Lines 192-202 then read `.expiresIn` and `.accessToken` directly off the `Response` instance (both `undefined`), resulting in `expiryDate: NaN`, persisting the raw `Response` object into `credential.key`, and passing `undefined` to `hubspotClient.setAccessToken`.

title: Zoom adapter passes "zoomvideo" instead of app slug "zoom" to refreshOAuthTokens
body: Line 92 passes `"zoomvideo"` (the directory name) as `appSlug` to `refreshOAuthTokens`, whereas Zoom's app slug in the database and in `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` is `"zoom"`. The sync endpoint will receive `appSlug=zoomvideo` instead of `zoom`.

title: Webex adapter validates synced refresh responses against full webexRefreshedTokenSchema
body: In `webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` calls `refreshOAuthTokens` but still validates the response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse(responseBody)` instead of `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. Because `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` requires `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in`, any response from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` containing only the access token and expiry will fail validation and reject with `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"`.

title: LarkCalendarService deletes synced credentials lacking refresh_token and parses sync responses with handleLarkError
body: In `LarkCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, lines 61-64 delete the credential and throw if `refresh_expires_date` is expired or `refresh_token` is missing, line 66 requires a Lark `appAccessToken` even when delegating to the sync endpoint, and line 84 parses the response with `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>` (which requires Lark's `{ code: 0, data: { access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, refresh_expires_in } }` payload) instead of `parseRefreshTokenResponse`.

title: Invalid Zod computed property keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema strip expiry and other fields
body: In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` evaluate `Object.prototype.toString()` on the Zod schema instances at runtime, which produces the literal property key `"[object Object]"` for both entries (with the second overwriting the first). Because `z.object()` strips unknown keys by default, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` neither validates that a numeric expiry property exists nor preserves any fields other than `access_token` (stripping `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, `instance_url`, etc.). Callers that read `expires_in` or other properties from `.data` (such as Zoom, Office 365 Calendar, and Salesforce) will receive `undefined`, resulting in `NaN` expiry dates or broken credentials.

title: Saving SafeParseReturnType wrapper instead of `.data` corrupts Google Calendar credentials in DB
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `SafeParseReturnType` object (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed credential data itself. In `GoogleCalendarService`, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` is passed directly to `prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key } })` instead of `key.data`. This overwrites `credential.key` in the database with `{ success: true, data: { ... } }` on the first token refresh (even when credential syncing is disabled), causing `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on line 75 to throw a `ZodError` on all subsequent uses of the credential.

title: GoogleCalendarService expects `res.data` but `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a Fetch `Response`
body: When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a Fetch `Response` object, whereas the fallback callback returns `fetchTokens.res` (a `GaxiosResponse` with a `.data` property). On line 94, `const token = res?.data` evaluates to `undefined` when syncing is enabled, causing `token.access_token` on line 95 to throw a `TypeError` (which is then swallowed in the `catch` block because `message !== "invalid_grant"`, leaving the expired token in place).

title: Missing `prisma` import, missing `refreshOAuthTokens` call, and stale `accessToken` used in SalesforceCalendarService
body:
In `SalesforceCalendarService.getClient`:
1. Line 96 calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)`, but `@calcom/prisma` is not imported in this file, causing a compile error and a runtime `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined`.
2. Lines 75-84 call `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` directly instead of wrapping the request in `refreshOAuthTokens`, so `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is never used.
3. Lines 105-106 pass the old `credentialKey.instance_url` and `credentialKey.access_token` to `new jsforce.Connection(...)` instead of the newly refreshed values from `accessTokenParsed.data`.

title: Wrong ID (`credentialId` instead of `userId`) passed to `refreshOAuthTokens` and incompatible `Response` shape in Zoho Bigin
body: In `BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, line 93 passes `credentialId` (`credential.id`) as the third argument (`userId`) to `refreshOAuthTokens`, which sends the credential primary key as `calcomUserId` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` instead of `credential.userId`. Additionally, when credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a Fetch `Response` object rather than an Axios response (`{ data: ... }`), so accessing `tokenInfo.data.error` on line 96 throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')`.

title: HubspotCalendarService treats the Fetch `Response` from `refreshOAuthTokens` as a parsed `HubspotToken`
body: When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw Fetch `Response`, whereas the fallback `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...)` returns a parsed `TokenResponseIF` object (`{ accessToken, refreshToken, expiresIn }`). Lines 192-202 read `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` and `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` directly without parsing the response JSON or mapping `access_token`, setting `expiryDate` to `NaN`, saving the raw `Response` object to `credential.key` in the database, and passing `undefined` to `hubspotClient.setAccessToken`.

title: ZohoCrmCalendarService expects an Axios `{ data }` response from `refreshOAuthTokens`
body: In `ZohoCrmCalendarService`, the fallback in `refreshOAuthTokens` uses `axios(...)` which resolves to `{ data: ... }`, whereas `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a Fetch `Response` when credential syncing is enabled. Line 217 then accesses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`, which throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')` when syncing is active.

title: Webex `refreshAccessToken` validates synced token responses against full `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`
body: In `packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` calls `refreshOAuthTokens` but validates the response using `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse(responseBody)` instead of `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. Because `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` strictly requires `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in`, a minimal response from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` containing only `access_token` and expiry will always fail validation and reject with `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"`.

title: Zoom `VideoApiAdapter` passes directory name `"zoomvideo"` instead of app slug `"zoom"` to `refreshOAuthTokens`
body: Line 92 passes `"zoomvideo"` (the directory name) as `appSlug` to `refreshOAuthTokens`, whereas Zoom's app slug in `prisma.app`, `appStoreMetadata`, and `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` is `"zoom"` (and `/api/webhook/app-credential` looks up the app by `slug`). This causes `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` to receive inconsistent `appSlug` values between credential creation (`"zoom"`) and token refresh (`"zoomvideo"`).

title: Outbound token refresh request to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` does not send the webhook secret header
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` sends a `POST` request to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` but includes no authentication headers (such as `[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]: process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`), giving the self-hosted sync endpoint no way to verify that the request for user OAuth tokens originated from Cal.com.

title: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses `[z.string().toString()]` as computed keys, evaluating to `"[object Object]"` and stripping expiry fields
body: In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` invoke `Object.prototype.toString()` on the Zod schema instances, which both evaluate to the literal property name `"[object Object]"`. The second property overwrites the first in the object literal, and because `z.object()` strips unknown keys by default, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` neither validates that a numeric expiry field is present nor preserves any fields other than `access_token` (such as `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, or `instance_url`). Any caller relying on expiry or provider-specific fields in `refreshTokenResponse.data` will receive `undefined`.

title: `GoogleCalendarService` persists the Zod `SafeParseReturnType` wrapper as `credential.key` and assumes `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a Gaxios response
body:
There are two bugs in `refreshAccessToken`:
1. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), whereas previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` returned the parsed credential object directly. Passing `key` to `prisma.credential.update` saves `{ success: true, data: ... }` as `credential.key` in the database, corrupting the credential so that `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on line 75 will fail with a `ZodError` on subsequent requests (even when credential sharing is disabled).
2. When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a standard `fetch` `Response` object rather than the `GaxiosResponse` returned by `myGoogleAuth.refreshToken`. `res?.data` on line 94 will be `undefined`, causing `token.access_token` on line 95 to throw a `TypeError`.

title: Missing `prisma` import, missing `refreshOAuthTokens` wrapper, and stale `accessToken` used in `SalesforceCalendarService`
body:
In `SalesforceCalendarService.getClient`:
1. Line 96 calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)`, but `prisma` is not imported in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, causing a TypeScript build failure and a runtime `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined`.
2. Line 75 calls `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` directly instead of wrapping the request in `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce token refreshes never use `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`.
3. Line 106 passes the stale `credentialKey.access_token` to `new jsforce.Connection(...)` instead of the newly refreshed `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

title: `BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken` passes `credentialId` instead of `userId` and crashes when `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response`
body:
1. Line 93 passes `credentialId` (`credential.id`) as the third argument (`userId`) to `refreshOAuthTokens`, which sends the credential's database ID instead of `credential.userId` as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint.
2. The fallback callback uses `axios.post(...)` (which returns `{ data: ... }`), whereas `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a native `fetch` `Response` when credential syncing is enabled. On a `fetch` `Response`, `tokenInfo.data` is `undefined`, causing `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` on line 96 to throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')`.

title: `ZohoCrmCalendarService` expects an Axios response with `.data`, throwing a `TypeError` when `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response`
body: In `refreshAccessToken`, the callback passed to `refreshOAuthTokens` uses `axios(...)`, which returns an object with a `.data` property, but when credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response` object. Accessing `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` on line 217 throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')`.

title: `HubspotCalendarService` treats the raw `fetch` `Response` from `refreshOAuthTokens` as a parsed `HubspotToken`
body: `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken` resolves directly to a `TokenResponseIF` object (`{ accessToken, expiresIn, refreshToken, tokenType }`), whereas `refreshOAuthTokens` returns an unparsed `fetch` `Response` when credential syncing is enabled. Consequently, `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` and `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` are `undefined`, `hubspotRefreshToken.expiryDate` evaluates to `NaN`, and `prisma.credential.update` overwrites `credential.key` with the `Response` object.

title: `ZoomVideoApiAdapter` passes `"zoomvideo"` instead of `"zoom"` as `appSlug` to `refreshOAuthTokens`
body: Line 92 passes `"zoomvideo"` as the `appSlug` argument to `refreshOAuthTokens`, whereas the Zoom app's slug in the database and `appStoreMetadata` (and used in `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` and `/api/webhook/app-credential`) is `"zoom"`.

title: `WebexVideoApiAdapter` does not use `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, causing synced token responses to fail schema validation
body: `refreshAccessToken` calls `refreshOAuthTokens`, but line 88 still validates `responseBody` with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse(responseBody)` instead of `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseBody, webexRefreshedTokenSchema)`. Because `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` strictly requires `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in`, a minimal response from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` containing only the access token and expiry will fail validation.

title: Team admin/owner permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`. Because it uses `&&` rather than `||`, a user must satisfy both `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` simultaneously. A team admin who is not the team owner (or any user if `isTeamAdmin` only matches the `ADMIN` role) will fail authorization with `FORBIDDEN` when trying to add guests to a team booking.

title: `EventManager` is initialized with the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
body: `addGuestsHandler` allows team admins/owners and attendees (in addition to the organizer) to add guests to a booking, and fetches `booking.user` with `credentials` and `destinationCalendar` in the initial query. However, lines 158-165 fetch credentials for `ctx.user` and initialize `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` using the logged-in caller rather than `booking.user`. When an attendee or team admin adds guests, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will attempt to update the organizer's calendar event using the caller's credentials, failing to update the organizer's calendar.

title: Guest email filtering is case-sensitive, does not deduplicate input, and `sendAddGuestsEmails` receives unfiltered `guests`
body:
There are three issues with how `guests` is filtered and used:
1. `blacklistedGuestEmails` lowercases entries on line 71, but `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` and `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` compare against `guest` without lowercasing it, allowing mixed-case emails to bypass both the blacklist and existing-attendee checks.
2. Neither `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` nor `uniqueGuests` deduplicates the `guests` array itself, so duplicate emails in a direct API call will insert duplicate attendee rows.
3. Line 168 calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw `guests` array instead of `uniqueGuests`. If the input included an already-existing attendee email alongside a new one, that existing attendee will match `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`.

title: `isInvalidEmail` error state is not cleared on valid submission or dialog close
body: Once `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is triggered by a validation failure, `isInvalidEmail` is only ever reset if the user clicks the Cancel button. It is not reset when validation succeeds in `handleAdd`, in `addGuestsMutation.onSuccess`, or when the dialog is dismissed via `onOpenChange` (Escape key or backdrop click). As a result, the invalid email warning remains visible during the mutation and persists if the dialog is reopened.

title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores `disableStandardEmails` event type metadata settings
body: Unlike `sendScheduledEmails`, `sendRescheduledEmails`, and `sendLocationChangeEmails`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept `eventTypeMetadata` or check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)`. Event types configured with `metadata.disableStandardEmails.all.host` or `metadata.disableStandardEmails.all.attendee` will still send emails to the organizer, team members, and attendees when guests are added.

title: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses logical AND (`&&`) instead of OR (`||`)
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`. Using `&&` requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner simultaneously. A team admin who is not an owner (or any user if `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` check mutually exclusive roles) will evaluate to `false` and receive a `FORBIDDEN` error when trying to add guests to a team booking. This should use `||`.

title: `EventManager` is initialized with the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
body: `addGuestsHandler` permits team admins/owners and existing attendees—not just the booking organizer—to add guests. However, lines 158–165 fetch credentials for `ctx.user` (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`) and construct `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` with the caller's user object rather than the booking organizer (`booking.user`, whose `credentials` and `destinationCalendar` were fetched in the initial `prisma.booking.findFirst` query at lines 35–40 but never used). When a team admin/owner or attendee adds guests, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will lack the organizer's calendar credentials and fail to update the calendar event.

title: Case-sensitive email checks allow blacklist bypass and duplicate attendees
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` lowercases each configured address (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares against the raw `guest` string without lowercasing it, so any email containing uppercase characters bypasses the blacklist. Likewise, `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` is case-sensitive, and neither `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` nor `uniqueGuests` deduplicates the `guests` array itself, allowing duplicate attendee records to be created if duplicate or differently cased emails are submitted to the endpoint.

title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` is passed unfiltered `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw `guests` input array rather than `uniqueGuests`. Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails`, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` decides whether an attendee receives `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (intended only for newly added guests) or `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (intended for existing attendees). If the submitted `guests` list includes an existing attendee's email alongside a new guest, that existing attendee will be sent `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`.

title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores event type settings that disable standard host/attendee emails
body: Unlike `sendLocationChangeEmails`, `sendScheduledEmails`, and `sendRescheduledEmails` in `email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept `eventTypeMetadata` or check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)`. When an event type has standard host or attendee emails disabled in its metadata, adding guests will still send notification emails.

title: Validation error state `isInvalidEmail` is not cleared on valid submit or dialog close
body: When email validation fails in `handleAdd`, `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is called, but `isInvalidEmail` is never reset to `false` when validation passes, in `addGuestsMutation.onSuccess`, or when the dialog is dismissed via `onOpenChange` (e.g., clicking the close icon, pressing Escape, or clicking the backdrop). Once a user triggers a validation error, the error message remains visible even after reopening the dialog, and closing the dialog without clicking the Cancel button also leaves stale entries in `multiEmailValue`.

title: Team admin check uses `&&` instead of `||`, blocking team admins who are not owners
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`. Because `isTeamOwner` only returns true for users with the `OWNER` role, using `&&` instead of `||` causes any team `ADMIN` who is not also an `OWNER` to fail the permission check and receive a `FORBIDDEN` error when adding guests.

title: `EventManager` is initialized with the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
body: `addGuestsHandler` permits team admins/owners and attendees (`isTeamAdminOrOwner`, `isAttendee`) to add guests, and fetches `booking.user` with `credentials` and `destinationCalendar` on lines 35-40. However, lines 158-165 initialize `EventManager` with `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` instead of the booking organizer. When an attendee or a team admin/owner (who is not the organizer) adds guests, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` will run against the caller's credentials rather than the organizer's and fail to update the calendar event.

title: Blacklist and existing-attendee checks are case-sensitive and `guests` is not deduplicated on the server
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` lowercases each configured address on line 71, but `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` on line 77 compares against the un-lowercased `guest` input, so any uppercase letter in a guest email bypasses the blacklist. Similarly, `guest === attendee.email` on line 76 is case-sensitive, and neither `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` nor `uniqueGuests` deduplicates the `guests` array itself, allowing duplicate attendee rows to be inserted if the endpoint is called directly with repeated emails.

title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` receives unfiltered `guests` and ignores disabled standard email settings
body: Line 168 passes the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. If `guests` contains an email that already belonged to an existing attendee alongside a new guest email, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in `sendAddGuestsEmails` (`packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541`) will treat the existing attendee as a new guest and send them `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Additionally, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` or `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` like `sendLocationChangeEmails` and other functions in `email-manager.ts`.

title: `isInvalidEmail` error state is not reset on valid submission or dialog close, and `onError` fallback is unreachable
body: Once `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true`, it is only cleared when clicking the Cancel button. If the user fixes the invalid email and submits, or closes the dialog via Escape/outside click (`onOpenChange`) and reopens it, `isInvalidEmail` remains `true` and the error message stays displayed. Also, in `onError` (lines 43-44), `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`` is always a non-empty string, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never be reached.

title: Unindexed `OR` branch on `retryCount` in `deleteMany` forces a full table scan and isn't scoped to unscheduled SMS reminders
body:
In `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany`, adding `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` as a top-level `OR` branch without `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or `scheduled: false`) and without an index on `retryCount` has two consequences:

1. PostgreSQL cannot use the existing `@@index([method, scheduled, scheduledDate])` index to satisfy `WHERE (method = 'SMS' AND scheduledDate <= ...) OR retryCount > 1`, forcing a sequential scan of the entire `WorkflowReminder` table on every cron run.
2. Because `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and `scheduled: false` are omitted from the second `OR` branch, this query will also delete non-SMS `WorkflowReminder` rows if they ever use `retryCount`, as well as any reminder that was concurrently marked `scheduled: true` after a prior retry failure (orphaning its Twilio `referenceId` so it can no longer be cancelled on booking cancellation/reschedule).

Deleting the reminder directly in the failure branches when `reminder.retryCount >= 1` (instead of incrementing to 2 and scanning for `retryCount > 1` on the next cron run), or scoping the condition to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduled: false` with a supporting index, avoids the full table scan and unintended deletions.

title: Unparenthesized OR in authorization and base SQL conditions breaks operator precedence when combined with AND
body: For `org` and `team` scopes, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` (lines 171-174) and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` (lines 204-207) return a top-level `OR` expression without enclosing parentheses: `(("teamId" = ...) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)) OR (("userId" = ...) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false))`. When no filters are active (`filterConditions` is `null`), `getBaseConditions()` (line 74) returns `authConditions` directly without wrapping it in parentheses. Because `AND` has higher precedence than `OR` in SQL, any query that combines `baseConditions` with other predicates such as `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" >= ...` (or `WHERE ... AND ${baseConditions}`) will only apply those predicates to one branch of the `OR`, returning unfiltered rows for the other branch. The same issue applies to `getFilterConditions()` when only `eventTypeId` is set (line 106). Additionally, the `else if (filterConditions)` branch on lines 76-77 would return filter conditions without authorization if `authConditions` were ever falsy; if `!authConditions`, it should always return `NOTHING_CONDITION`.

title: Caching test suite was deleted instead of updated for Prisma.sql
body: The `describe("Caching", ...)` tests for `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` were removed completely from `insightsBooking.integration-test.ts`, even though `InsightsBookingService` still maintains `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`. These tests should be updated to assert the `Prisma.sql` output rather than deleted.

title: Unparenthesized OR clauses in SQL conditions break operator precedence when combined with AND
body: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition`, and `buildFilterConditions` (when only `eventTypeId` is provided) return top-level `OR` SQL fragments without outer parentheses (e.g., `(("teamId" = ...) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)) OR (("userId" = ...) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false))`). When `filterConditions` is `null`, `getBaseConditions()` returns `authConditions` directly without wrapping it in parentheses. Because `AND` binds tighter than `OR` in SQL, embedding `${baseConditions}` (or `${authConditions}` / `${filterConditions}`) into a raw query with additional predicates—such as `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" >= ...`—causes PostgreSQL to parse the condition as `A OR (B AND "startTime" >= ...)`, so one branch of the `OR` completely ignores the remaining `WHERE` filters. Additionally, the `else if (filterConditions)` branch on lines 76-77 would return `filterConditions` without any authorization constraint if `authConditions` were ever falsy; `getBaseConditions()` should always enforce `authConditions` and wrap compound `OR` conditions in parentheses.

title: Caching tests for authorization and filter conditions were removed
body: `InsightsBookingService` still caches `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` in `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()`, but the entire `describe("Caching", ...)` test block was deleted rather than updated for the `Prisma.sql` return values, leaving the caching behavior untested.

title: Unparenthesized OR conditions in getBaseConditions break SQL operator precedence when combined with AND
body: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` (line 173), `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` (line 206), and `buildFilterConditions` for `eventTypeId` (line 106) produce `Prisma.Sql` fragments with a top-level `OR` that is not wrapped in outer parentheses (for example, `(("teamId" = $1) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)) OR (("userId" = ANY($2)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false))`). When both `authConditions` and `filterConditions` are present, `getBaseConditions()` wraps each in parentheses (`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})`), but when `filterConditions` is `null` (line 74-75), it returns `authConditions` directly without outer parentheses. Because `AND` has higher precedence than `OR` in SQL, any caller that interpolates `${baseConditions}` (or `${authConditions}` / `${filterConditions}`) into a `WHERE` clause alongside other conditions such as date bounds or status checks (e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ...`) will only apply the additional `AND` predicates to one branch of the `OR`, leaking rows that do not match the other filters.

title: Fallback branch in getBaseConditions returns filterConditions without authorization if authConditions is falsy
body: In `getBaseConditions()`, lines 76-77 contain `else if (filterConditions) { return filterConditions; }`. While `getAuthorizationConditions()` currently always returns a truthy `Prisma.Sql`, if it is ever changed to return `null`/`undefined` on failure (matching `getFilterConditions()`), `getBaseConditions()` would silently return `filterConditions` alone with no authorization predicate instead of `NOTHING_CONDITION`. If `authConditions` is not present, `getBaseConditions()` should always return `NOTHING_CONDITION`.

title: Deleting cache does not invalidate `connectedCalendars` query
body: `deleteCacheMutation` does not invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled` (unlike `disconnectMutation` on lines 61-64). title: `connectedCalendarsHandler` bypasses `CalendarCache.init` feature-flag check
body: `connectedCalendarsHandler` directly instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` instead of calling `await CalendarCache.init(null)`. `CalendarCache.init` checks whether the `calendar-cache` feature is enabled and returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when it is disabled. Instantiating `CalendarCacheRepository` directly bypasses the feature flag, leaves `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` unused, and runs `calendarCache.groupBy` queries and exposes cache status UI even when `calendar-cache` is disabled.

title: Unused `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` writes and session payload fields
body: `CalendarService.fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` to touch `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, and `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` (in `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts`, lines 899-900) selects `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on every `SelectedCalendar` during session loading. Because the feature now reads `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, these `SelectedCalendar` fields are unused, causing an unnecessary `UPDATE` on all selected calendars on every cache refresh and enlarging the session user payload.

title: Relative `.env` path and macOS-only `sed -i ''` break script when run from repo root or on Linux
body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory rather than the script's directory (`$(dirname "$0")/..`), so running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repository root creates/modifies `../.env` outside the repository. title: Deleting calendar cache does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
body: `deleteCacheMutation` only calls `showToast` and the optional `onSuccess` callback, without invalidating `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (unlike `disconnectMutation` below it, which calls `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled`). body: `connectedCalendarsHandler` instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of using `await CalendarCache.init(null)`. `CalendarCache.init` checks whether the `calendar-cache` feature is enabled and returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when it is disabled. Instantiating `CalendarCacheRepository` directly makes the newly added `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method unreachable and executes the `calendarCache.groupBy` query even when the calendar cache feature is disabled.

body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` executes `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` across all selected calendars for the credential, and `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` (in `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts`) was updated to select `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on every session lookup. title: Unused SelectedCalendar fields added to UserWithCalendars break type compatibility and trigger unnecessary DB writes
body: `UserWithCalendars` now requires `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars`, `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` selects them on every session fetch, and `GoogleCalendarService.fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` (line 1024) runs `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` on every cache refresh. title: Throwing a generic Error returns HTTP 500 instead of a TRPCError
body: When the credential does not exist or does not belong to the current user, `deleteCacheHandler` throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` instead of `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or `"FORBIDDEN"`), causing tRPC to surface an unhandled 500 `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`.

title: Webhook test script uses cwd-dependent ../.env path and macOS-only sed syntax
body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` (line 5) assumes the script is executed from inside `scripts/`; when run from the repository root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`), it creates or modifies a `.env` file in the parent directory outside the repository instead of the project's `.env`. In addition, `sed -i '' -E` on line 68 uses BSD/macOS-only syntax that fails on Linux with GNU `sed` (`sed: can't read : No such file or directory`).

title: Rescheduling a booking passes `immediateDelete = true`, bypassing deferred cancellation and leaving orphaned reminder rows
body: When cancelling reminders for `originalRescheduledBooking`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` is called with `immediateDelete = true`. In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, when `immediateDelete` is `true`, it immediately sends `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` to SendGrid instead of marking `cancelled: true` for the cron job, and then returns early without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row from the database (since rescheduling only marks the original booking `CANCELLED` rather than deleting it). Consequently, rescheduled bookings still immediately consume SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellations limit (for up to 72 hours), and the `WorkflowReminder` record remains in the database where subsequent workflow edits can mark it `cancelled: true` and cause the cron job to attempt a duplicate cancellation.

title: Single failure in `remindersToCancel` loop skips remaining cancellations and leaves already-cancelled reminders in DB
body: The `try/catch` block and `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` wrap the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop rather than each individual reminder. Because `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` returns a lazy `PrismaPromise` that only executes when `await Promise.all(...)` is reached, if `client.request` throws for any reminder in the batch: (1) all remaining reminders in `remindersToCancel` are skipped, and (2) reminders earlier in the loop that were already cancelled in SendGrid are never deleted from the database. On the next cron run, those already-cancelled reminders will be queried again and `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` will be called with the same `batch_id`, which SendGrid rejects as a duplicate, permanently wedging the loop on every subsequent run.

title: SendGrid `@sendgrid/client` API key is never set in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`
body: `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` calls `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` (which only configures `@sendgrid/mail`'s internal client instance) but never calls `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` on the `@sendgrid/client` singleton (unlike `emailReminderManager.ts`). When the cron job calls `client.request` to cancel scheduled sends at `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` (or create batches at `/v3/mail/batch`), the client has no `Authorization` header configured and will fail with `401 Unauthorized` unless `emailReminderManager.ts` happened to be imported in the same process beforehand.

title: Deferring cancellation to the 15-minute cron job when `scheduledDate` is already within 1 hour allows imminent emails to be sent
body: When a booking is cancelled or rescheduled, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` only sets `cancelled: true` on the `WorkflowReminder` and relies on the `scheduleEmailReminders` cron job (which runs every 15 minutes) to cancel reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour. If a booking is cancelled when the reminder's `scheduledDate` is already less than 15–25 minutes away (SendGrid does not guarantee cancellation less than 10 minutes before `send_at`, and the next cron tick may occur after `scheduledDate`), the reminder email will be sent before the cron job cancels it. Reminders whose `scheduledDate` is already within the next hour should be cancelled in SendGrid and deleted immediately.

title: Unawaited `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` calls race with cascade deletes and response completion
body: In `workflows.tsx` (lines 212–218, 376–382, 519–525, 574–580), `handleCancelBooking.ts` (lines 485–493), `handleNewBooking.ts` (lines 966–972), and `bookings.tsx` (lines 488–494), the async functions `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are invoked inside `.forEach(...)` without `await` or `Promise.all`. In `workflows.delete` (line 220) and `workflows.update` step deletion (line 527), `workflow.deleteMany` / `workflowStep.delete` runs immediately and cascade-deletes the `WorkflowReminder` rows while `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` (or `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` when `referenceId` is null) is still running, causing `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` to fail with `P2025` (record not found). In the booking handlers, returning the HTTP response before awaiting these promises risks terminating the database updates and external API calls prematurely in serverless environments.

title: Single SendGrid failure in cancellation loop aborts remaining cancellations and wedges future cron runs
body: In `scheduleEmailReminders`, the `try / catch` block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop, and `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` promises are only executed at the end via `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`. If `client.request` fails for any single reminder in the batch, execution jumps to the `catch` block: (1) all subsequent reminders in `remindersToCancel` are skipped and not cancelled before their send time, and (2) `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is never reached, so the reminders that were already cancelled in earlier iterations of the loop are not deleted from the database. On the next cron run, SendGrid will return HTTP 400 for those already-cancelled `batch_id`s on the first iteration, wedging the cancellation loop on every subsequent run until their `scheduledDate` passes. Each iteration should have its own `try / catch` and `await` the database deletion immediately after cancelling with SendGrid.

title: Rescheduled bookings pass `immediateDelete = true`, bypassing deferred cancellation and leaving stale reminder rows
body: When cancelling reminders for `originalRescheduledBooking` in `handleNewBooking.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` is called with `immediateDelete = true`. This causes two problems: (1) it immediately calls SendGrid's `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` instead of deferring to the cron job via `cancelled: true`, so rescheduled bookings up to 72 hours out still count against SendGrid's 100 pending cancellations limit and will fail once that limit is full; and (2) in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, the `if (immediateDelete)` branch returns without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row from the database, while `originalRescheduledBooking` itself is only marked `CANCELLED` (not deleted), leaving the reminder record in the database with `cancelled: null`.

title: Deferring cancellation to the 15-minute cron job for reminders due within the next hour allows emails to be sent
body: When `immediateDelete` is not set, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` unconditionally sets `cancelled: true` in the database and relies on the `scheduleEmailReminders` cron job (which runs every 15 minutes) to cancel reminders scheduled within the next hour. If a booking is cancelled or rescheduled when a reminder's `scheduledDate` is already less than 15 minutes away (or within 10+ minutes of send time, as SendGrid requires cancellations before the send window), `scheduledDate` will pass before the next cron run, SendGrid will send the email for the cancelled booking, and the cron job's initial `deleteMany` for past `scheduledDate` will silently delete the record. Reminders whose `scheduledDate` is already within the 1-hour window should be cancelled with SendGrid and deleted immediately.

title: Async reminder cancellation calls are not awaited across booking and workflow handlers
body: Previously, the `workflowReminder` database operations were collected and awaited with `await Promise.all(...)`. Now those database updates/deletes and external API calls happen inside the async functions `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`, which are invoked inside `.forEach(...)` without being awaited (here in `handleCancelBooking.ts`, as well as in `handleNewBooking.ts` line 966, `bookings.tsx` line 488, and `workflows.tsx` lines 212, 376, 519, and 574). In `workflows.tsx` (lines 220 and 527), `workflow.deleteMany` and `workflowStep.delete` run immediately and cascade-delete the `WorkflowReminder` rows while `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are still in flight, and in serverless deployments the HTTP handler can return before the database updates or SendGrid/Twilio requests complete.

title: Rescheduled bookings pass `immediateDelete = true`, bypassing deferred cancellation and leaving stale reminder rows
body: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, rescheduling a booking calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` with `immediateDelete` set to `true`. In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (`emailReminderManager.ts` lines 213-223), when `immediateDelete` is `true` and `referenceId` is non-null, it immediately posts a cancel request to SendGrid's `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` endpoint and returns without deleting or updating the `WorkflowReminder` database record. Because rescheduling does not delete `originalRescheduledBooking` (it only marks it as `CANCELLED`), this has two consequences: (1) rescheduled bookings scheduled more than 1 hour in advance still immediately consume slots in SendGrid's 100-pending-cancellations limit instead of deferring cancellation to the `scheduleEmailReminders` cron job, and (2) the `WorkflowReminder` rows remain in the database with `cancelled: null` and `scheduled: true`, so they will be processed again if the workflow is later edited or deleted or when the cron job runs.

title: `@sendgrid/client` API key is never set in `scheduleEmailReminders` cron handler
body: `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` calls `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` on line 19, but unlike `emailReminderManager.ts` (line 26), it never calls `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` on the `@sendgrid/client` singleton. Because `@sendgrid/mail` maintains its own internal `Client` instance and does not configure the default `@sendgrid/client` instance, `await client.request({ url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends", ... })` on line 57 (and `/v3/mail/batch` on line 188) will be sent without an API key and fail with `401 Unauthorized` whenever `emailReminderManager` has not already been loaded in the same process.

title: Single failure in `remindersToCancel` loop aborts remaining cancellations and skips deleting already-cancelled rows
body: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` lines 53-77, a single `try / catch` block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop, and `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` calls (which return lazy `PrismaPromise` objects that do not execute until awaited) are only awaited after the loop finishes via `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`. If `client.request` throws for any reminder in `remindersToCancel` (for example, if its `referenceId` was already cancelled or is invalid), all subsequent reminders in the batch are skipped, and `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is never reached—leaving the database rows for reminders that were already cancelled in earlier iterations of the loop undeleted so they will be retried on every future cron run. Each iteration should have its own `try / catch` (similar to `unscheduledReminders` on line 106) and `await` the database delete immediately.

title: Un-awaited `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` calls race with cascade deletes and handler completion
body: Across `workflows.tsx` (lines 212-218, 376-382, 519-525, 574-580), `handleCancelBooking.ts` (lines 485-493), `handleNewBooking.ts` (lines 966-972), and `bookings.tsx` (lines 488-494), the async functions `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called inside `.forEach(...)` without `await` or `Promise.all` (whereas previously the Prisma delete promises were awaited via `Promise.all`). In `workflows.delete` (line 220) and `workflows.update` (line 527), `ctx.prisma.workflow.deleteMany` and `ctx.prisma.workflowStep.delete` run immediately and cascade-delete the `WorkflowReminder` rows in Postgres while `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are still executing their SendGrid/Twilio API calls and subsequent `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` queries, causing race conditions and allowing serverless handlers to return before the external cancellation requests finish.

title: All app modules are still eagerly imported at module initialization time
body: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, the `appStore` object properties are assigned the result of calling `import("./...")` directly (e.g., `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`) rather than functions that call `import()` on demand (e.g., `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`). Because every `import()` expression in the object literal is evaluated immediately when `packages/app-store/index.ts` is loaded, importing `@calcom/app-store` still triggers loading all 28 app packages at once instead of lazily importing only the requested app when accessed.

title: Unawaited async `forEach` prevents recurring calendar deletions from being awaited in `apiDeletes`
body: When cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring event (lines 458-470), `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` awaits `getCalendar(credential)` and `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` before calling `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)`. Because `forEach` does not wait for `async` callbacks, execution proceeds to `await apiDeletes` (line 617) and `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) before the `forEach` callbacks have pushed their promises into `apiDeletes` or completed deleting the calendar events. Use a `for...of` loop (as done on lines 480-483) or `Promise.all` with `.map` so the deletions are tracked in `apiDeletes` and awaited.

title: Async `forEach` inside `try/catch` does not await deletions and leaks unhandled rejections
body: On lines 124-139, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` is wrapped in a `try / catch` block. Because `forEach` ignores the Promise returned by an `async` callback, `Reschedule` does not wait for `getCalendar`, `calendar?.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` to finish before returning, and any error thrown or rejected inside the callback will become an unhandled promise rejection rather than being caught by the surrounding `try / catch`. Replace `forEach` with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))`.

title: Async `forEach` inside `try/catch` does not await deletions and leaks unhandled rejections
body: On lines 124-139, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` is wrapped in a `try / catch` block. Because `forEach` ignores the Promise returned by an `async` callback, `Reschedule` does not wait for `getCalendar`, `calendar?.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` to finish before returning, and any error thrown or rejected inside the callback will bypass the `try / catch` block as an unhandled promise rejection. Replace `forEach` with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))`.

title: Unawaited async `forEach` in `requestReschedule` discards calendar and video deletion promises
body: In `requestReschedule` (lines 553-567), `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` awaits `getCalendar` and returns the promises from `calendar?.deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting` to `forEach`, which ignores them. As a result, `calendar?.deleteEvent` is no longer even started synchronously, the mutation resolves without waiting for calendar events or video meetings to be deleted, and any rejection in `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` goes unhandled. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` instead.

title: All app modules are still eagerly imported at module load time
body: Each property in `appStore` is assigned the result of calling `import("./...")` directly (e.g. `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`). Because these expressions are evaluated when `packages/app-store/index.ts` is loaded, importing `@calcom/app-store` immediately triggers dynamic imports for all 28 apps in parallel rather than loading only the requested app on demand. To defer loading until an app is accessed, each property should be a getter (e.g. `get applecalendar() { return import("./applecalendar"); }`) or a thunk (`() => import("./applecalendar")`).

title: Unawaited `forEach(async ...)` leaves `apiDeletes` empty when cancelling recurring bookings
body: In the recurring booking cancellation branch (`allRemainingBookings`), `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` uses an `async` callback inside `.forEach`. Because `.forEach` does not await promises, execution suspends at `await getCalendar(credential)` and reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (and `await apiDeletes` for paid bookings) before any `deleteEvent` calls are started or pushed into `apiDeletes`. Unlike the `else` branch on lines 477-483 (which was converted to a `for...of` loop), recurring calendar event deletions are no longer awaited before the handler returns.

title: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` does not await deletions and bypasses `try/catch`
body: Converting the `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` callback to `async` in `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts` (line 125), `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts` (line 125), and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (line 553) causes `.forEach` to ignore the returned promises. As a result, `Reschedule` / `requestReschedule` no longer waits for `getCalendar` and `calendar.deleteEvent` / `deleteMeeting` to finish before completing, and any rejection inside the `async` callback escapes the surrounding `try / catch` block as an unhandled promise rejection instead of being caught and logged. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))` instead.

title: Dynamic imports in `appStore` are evaluated eagerly at module load time
body: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, each property value is written as `import("./...")` directly inside the `appStore` object literal. In JavaScript, object property values are evaluated immediately when the object is constructed, so importing `@calcom/app-store` still triggers all 28 dynamic `import()` calls eagerly at module initialization time rather than loading only the requested app on demand. To defer loading until a specific app is accessed, wrap each import in a getter (`get applecalendar() { return import("./applecalendar"); }`) or a thunk (`applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`).

title: Unawaited `forEach(async ...)` causes recurring event deletions to miss `apiDeletes`
body: When cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring event (lines 458-470), `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` is used. Because `forEach` does not await its `async` callback, execution suspends at `await getCalendar(credential)` and `await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` before anything is pushed to `apiDeletes`. As a result, `apiDeletes` does not contain these deletion operations when `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (or `await apiDeletes`) runs, so the handler returns before recurring calendar events are deleted. This should iterate with `for (const credential of ...)` (as was done in the `else` branch on lines 480-483) or `Promise.all` with `.map`.

title: `forEach(async ...)` inside `try/catch` does not await deletions or catch rejections
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` ignores the promises returned by the `async` callback. Because `getCalendar` is now awaited inside the callback, `calendar?.deleteEvent` is invoked asynchronously after the `try` block has already exited: any error thrown by `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` will bypass the surrounding `try / catch` block as an unhandled promise rejection, and `Reschedule` will send emails and return without waiting for the calendar/video deletions. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` instead.

title: `forEach(async ...)` inside `try/catch` does not await deletions or catch rejections
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` ignores the promises returned by the `async` callback. Because `getCalendar` is now awaited inside the callback, `calendar?.deleteEvent` is invoked asynchronously after the `try` block has already exited: any error thrown by `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` will bypass the surrounding `try / catch` block as an unhandled promise rejection, and `Reschedule` will send emails and return without waiting for the calendar/video deletions. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` instead.

title: `forEach(async ...)` in `requestReschedule` does not await calendar and video deletions
body: In `requestReschedule`, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` does not await the `async` callback or the promises returned by `calendar?.deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting`. With `await getCalendar(...)` added before `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`, the deletion call itself is now deferred until after `forEach` finishes, so the mutation sends reschedule emails, fires webhooks, and returns before calendar and video deletions have completed, and any rejection in the callback goes unhandled. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))`.

title: Early return on `dateOverrideExist` bypasses busy-time checks and allows double bookings
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls within the override's hours, `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` returns immediately before reaching `return busy.every(...)` at line 153.
