Because `getTimeSlots` does not filter out busy times, `checkIfIsAvailable` is the only place where existing Cal.com bookings and external calendar busy blocks are checked. Returning `true` here causes all busy times to be ignored on any day that has a date override, allowing hosts to be double-booked. `dateOverrideExist` should only skip the `workingHours` check (`if (!dateOverrideExist) { ... }`) and still fall through to `busy.every(...)`.

title: `workingHours` check in `checkIfIsAvailable` uses `slotStartTime` for `end`, ignores non-working days, and breaks on multiple/split intervals
body:
The `workingHours` check added to `checkIfIsAvailable` has three defects:

1. On line 142, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` uses `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime` (making `end` identical to `start`), so slots that start at `workingHour.endTime` or extend past `workingHour.endTime` are not rejected.
2. If a host does not work at all on `slotStartTime.day()` (for example, a fixed host is off on Tuesday while a round-robin host works Tuesday), `workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())` is `false` for all entries, so `workingHours.find(...)` returns `undefined` and the host is treated as available all day.
3. If a host has more than one `workingHours` entry for the same day (either from multiple shifts like 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, or because `getWorkingHours` splits schedules that cross 00:00 UTC into `[0, endTime]` and `[startTime, 1439]`), `workingHours.find(...)` returns a match as soon as a slot is outside any single entry, rejecting all slots for that host on that day.

title: Date override validation in `checkIfIsAvailable` uses `===` on `Dayjs` objects, misses partial overlaps, and breaks with multiple overrides or UTC day boundaries
body:
The `dateOverrides.find(...)` check in `checkIfIsAvailable` has several logic bugs:

1. Line 114 compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` using `===` between two distinct `Dayjs` object instances, which always evaluates to `false` instead of `.isSame(...)`. For an all-day unavailable override (where `start` and `end` are both 00:00), this check never triggers and a slot starting at 00:00 is not rejected.
2. Lines 117-125 only reject slots where `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime > overrideEnd`. Slots that start before `overrideStart` and end inside the override, slots that start inside the override and end after `overrideEnd`, and slots that start exactly at `overrideEnd` are not rejected.
3. Using `.find(...)` to reject a slot if it is outside any matching override on that day breaks when a user defines multiple override ranges on the same day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00), because a slot inside the first range is outside the second range.
4. Comparing `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` compares UTC calendar dates rather than the date in `organizerTimeZone`. When the organizer's local day spans two UTC dates (e.g. `America/Los_Angeles`), slots on the override day that fall after 00:00 UTC have a different UTC date than `date.start` and fail to match the override, while slots from the previous local day that fall after 00:00 UTC falsely match the override.

title: Date override timezone shift wraps modulo 24h and matches the wrong day when overrides cross midnight in the invitee's timezone
body:
In `getSlots`, shifting `override.start` and `override.end` by `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` and taking `.hour() * 60 + .minute()` wraps around at 24:00 (0 minutes):

1. If the timezone offset pushes `override.end` to or past midnight in the invitee's timezone while `override.start` remains before midnight (for example, a 14:00-18:00 UTC override viewed from `Asia/Tokyo` UTC+9 is 23:00-03:00, yielding `startTime = 1380` and `endTime = 180`, or an override ending at 24:00 invitee time yielding `endTime = 0`), `startTime >= endTime` and `buildSlots` discards the range (`if (start >= end) continue`), returning no slots.
2. `activeOverrides` (line 206) checks `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, startOfInviteeDay.endOf("day"), null, "[)")` using the unshifted `override.start` (which encodes organizer local time as UTC). When the timezone difference shifts the override into the previous or next calendar date in the invitee's timezone, `activeOverrides` does not match on the invitee date where the slots actually fall, and when it does match, `buildSlots` anchors the wrapped `startTime` to `startOfInviteeDay`, shifting the resulting UTC slot timestamps by 24 hours.

title: checkIfIsAvailable returns true early when a date override exists, bypassing busy time checks
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, when a date override exists for the slot's date and the slot falls within that override window, `dateOverrideExist` is set to `true` and `dateOverrides.find(...)` returns `undefined`. Lines 133-135 (`if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }`) then immediately return `true` before reaching `return busy.every(...)` on line 153. As a result, on any date where a host has a date override, all of their existing Cal bookings and external calendar conflicts in `busy` are ignored, allowing already-booked times to be shown as available and double-booked. Instead of returning `true` at line 134, the `workingHours` check on lines 138-151 should only run when `!dateOverrideExist` so execution still proceeds to the `busy` check.

title: Broken date override boundary and full-day unavailability checks in checkIfIsAvailable
body:
The date override check in `checkIfIsAvailable` (lines 114-125) has three logic bugs:
1. Line 114 compares two `Dayjs` instances using `===` (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`), which compares object references and is always `false`. Full-day unavailable overrides (where `start` and `end` are equal, e.g. 00:00 to 00:00) will never match this condition, and a slot starting at 00:00 will not be rejected by lines 117-125 either. Use `.isSame(...)` instead.
2. Lines 117-125 only reject a slot if `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime > overrideEnd`. This allows slots that partially overlap the override boundaries (e.g., a slot starting before `overrideStart` and ending after `overrideStart`, or starting before/at `overrideEnd` and ending after `overrideEnd`, including a slot whose `slotStartTime` equals `overrideEnd` since `isAfter` is `false` for equal times). A slot is outside the override window whenever `slotStartTime.isBefore(overrideStart)` or `slotEndTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`.
3. Because `dateOverrides.find(...)` returns `true` on the first override for that date that does not contain the slot, if a user has multiple date override intervals on the same day, slots falling in the second interval are rejected when tested against the first.

title: workingHours check in checkIfIsAvailable uses slotStartTime for end, ignores non-working days, and breaks split schedules
body:
The `workingHours` check in `checkIfIsAvailable` (lines 138-151) has several defects:
1. On line 142, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` computes `end` from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so `end` equals `start` and slots that start inside working hours but end after `workingHour.endTime` are not rejected.
2. On line 140, `if (workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day()))` only checks entries that include that day of the week. If a fixed host does not work on `slotStartTime.day()` at all (no `workingHour` entry includes that day), `workingHours.find(...)` returns `undefined` and the host is treated as available on their day off whenever another host has availability/overrides on that day.
3. If a host has multiple `workingHours` intervals on the same day (e.g., morning and afternoon shifts, or hours split across UTC midnight), `.find()` returns `true` as soon as the slot is outside any one of those intervals, rejecting all slots on that day. When `workingHours.length > 0`, it should verify that at least one (`workingHours.some(...)`) interval on that day contains the full slot.

title: Date override timezone conversion in getSlots fails when the override crosses midnight or shifts dates between timezones
body:
In `packages/lib/slots.ts` (lines 206-225):
1. On line 207, `activeOverrides` filters with `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, startOfInviteeDay.endOf("day"), null, "[)")`. However, `override.start` encodes the organizer's local clock time as UTC (e.g. `2023-05-10T15:00:00.000Z` for 15:00 in the organizer's timezone), while `startOfInviteeDay` and `startOfInviteeDay.endOf("day")` are real UTC instants. Without subtracting the organizer's UTC offset from `dayjs.utc(override.start)`, overrides can fail to match `startOfInviteeDay` or match on the wrong invitee day when organizer and invitee timezones differ.
2. On lines 218-223, `startTime` and `endTime` are calculated via `.hour() * 60 + .minute()` after adding `offset` minutes. Whenever adding `offset` causes the override to cross midnight in the invitee's timezone (or end at `00:00`), `endTime` wraps modulo 1440 to a value less than or equal to `startTime` (e.g., 20:00 to 01:00 becomes `startTime: 1200, endTime: 60`), which `buildSlots` drops at `if (start >= end) continue;`, resulting in no available slots.

title: Missing test coverage for fixed-host date overrides in round-robin events
body: One of the main goals of this PR is to ensure that date overrides of fixed hosts are respected in round-robin events, but `apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts` only adds a test for a single-user event in a different timezone and includes no test for a `ROUND_ROBIN` event with a fixed host who has a date override.

title: Early return when `dateOverrideExist` is true skips all busy-time and booking checks
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, when a slot falls within a date override on that day, `dateOverrideExist` is set to `true` and lines 133-135 immediately execute `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` before reaching `return busy.every(...)` at line 153. As a result, whenever a host has a date override on a day, all existing Cal.com bookings, external calendar busy periods, and event buffers for that day are completely ignored, allowing double-bookings during any date override. The `workingHours` check at line 138 should instead be guarded by `if (!dateOverrideExist)` so execution continues to the `busy.every(...)` check.

title: Broken date override boundary, equality, day-matching, and multi-range checks in `checkIfIsAvailable`
body:
The `dateOverrides.find` block in `checkIfIsAvailable` (lines 105-131) has several logic errors:
1. Line 114 compares two newly constructed `Dayjs` instances with `===` (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`), which compares object references and is always `false`, so full-day unavailable overrides where `start` equals `end` are never detected by this check.
2. Lines 117-125 only reject a slot if `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime > overrideEnd`, instead of rejecting when `slotStartTime < overrideStart` or `slotEndTime > overrideEnd`. Slots that partially overlap the start or end of the override (or start exactly at `overrideEnd`) are erroneously allowed.
3. Using `dateOverrides.find` to return `false` when a slot falls outside any single override on that day breaks multiple override windows on the same day (e.g., 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00), since a slot in the first window is rejected by the second window and vice versa.
4. Lines 109-111 compare `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` using the shifted UTC date (and local server timezone on `dayjs(date.start)`), rather than comparing the slot's date in `organizerTimeZone` against the override's calendar date (`dayjs.utc(date.start).format("YYYY MM DD")`). When a slot or override crosses midnight UTC, the dates do not match and the override is either ignored on the actual day or applied to the wrong UTC day.

title: `workingHours` check in `checkIfIsAvailable` uses `slotStartTime` for `end`, allows non-working days, and breaks split shifts
body:
Lines 138-151 check whether a slot falls within `workingHours`, but contain three bugs:
1. Line 142 computes `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` using `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so a slot whose start is inside working hours but whose end extends past `workingHour.endTime` is not rejected.
2. If a host has no working hours on `slotStartTime.day()` (e.g., a fixed host does not work on Saturdays while a round-robin host does), `workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())` is `false` for every entry, so `workingHours.find(...)` returns `undefined` and `checkIfIsAvailable` treats the host as available all day on their day off.
3. If a host has multiple `workingHours` entries for the same day (either from a split schedule like 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, or because their working hours cross midnight UTC and `getWorkingHours` splits them into two entries on the same day), `workingHours.find(...)` returns `true` because any slot will be outside at least one of the entries, rejecting all slots for that host.

title: Timezone offset shift on date overrides wraps around midnight and double-applies DST
body:
In `getSlots` (lines 206-225), converting date overrides to invitee local minutes fails when the timezone difference crosses midnight or a DST boundary:
1. Lines 218-223 compute `startTime` and `endTime` using `.hour() * 60 + .minute()` after `.add(offset, "minute")`. Because `.hour()` wraps modulo 24, if adding `offset` pushes `end` to or past midnight in the invitee's timezone (e.g., 24:00 becomes `0`, or 02:00 next day becomes `120`), `endTime` becomes less than or equal to `startTime`, causing `buildSlots` (`if (start >= end) continue`) to drop the override slots completely.
2. Line 207 filters `activeOverrides` by checking if `dayjs.utc(override.start)` (which stores the organizer's wall-clock time as UTC) is between `startOfInviteeDay` and `startOfInviteeDay.endOf("day")` without subtracting `organizerUtcOffset` first. When the override falls on a different calendar date in the invitee's timezone than in the organizer's timezone, `activeOverrides` matches it on the wrong invitee day (shifted by 24 hours) or misses it.
3. Lines 212-214 compute `offset` using the UTC offsets at `override.start`, but `buildSlots` (lines 102-110) subsequently adds `organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff` (the DST offset difference between `dayjs()` today and `startOfInviteeDay`) to every slot, shifting date override slots by an extra hour when booked across a DST transition.

title: Missing tests for round-robin fixed-host date overrides and date overrides with existing bookings
body: The PR only adds an assertion for a single-user event with a +30 minute timezone difference (`Asia/Kolkata` to `Asia/Dhaka`). There are no tests for a round-robin event where a fixed host has a date override (one of the primary bugs this PR targets) and no tests for a date override on a day that also has an existing booking or calendar busy time.

title: Migration crashes with IndexError when embed_category or uncategorized_category_id is not in site_settings
body: Lines 9-11 and 15 index directly into the `PG::Result` returned by `execute` (`execute(...)[0]['id']` and `execute(...)[0]['value']`) without checking `cmd_tuples > 0`. On any database where `embed_category` was not saved in `site_settings` (the common case, and always true on a fresh database before seeds run), the query returns 0 rows and `result[0]` raises `IndexError: Index 0 is out of range`, aborting `db:migrate`.

title: Migrated embeddable_hosts are inserted without normalizing URLs or escaping SQL
body: The previous `embeddable_hosts` site setting allowed full URLs with schemes and paths (e.g. `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234`), which `EmbeddableHost` normally strips in a `before_validation` callback. Because the migration inserts raw lines via SQL (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), any existing host entries containing a scheme or path will be stored un-normalized and will fail to match `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` (which compares `lower(host)` against `uri.host`). Interpolating `h` directly into SQL can also break the migration if the setting contains single quotes.

title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
body: In the `before_validation` callback, `self.host.sub!` is called unconditionally. If `host` is `nil` (for example `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?` or a request with a missing `:host` param), calling `.sub!` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError` instead of adding a validation error.

title: record_for_host returns false on invalid input, fails on uppercase hosts, and ignores ports
body:
`EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` has three issues:
1. It returns `false` on lines 12 and 15 when `uri` or `uri.host` is blank, instead of `nil`. In `TopicEmbed.import` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb:43`), the return value is used as `eh.try(:category_id)`. In ActiveSupport, `Object#try` only short-circuits on `nil`; calling `false.try(:category_id)` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'category_id' for false:FalseClass`.
2. `URI(host).host` preserves the case of the input string, so `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` will fail to match if the URL's hostname contains uppercase letters (`host.downcase` is needed).
3. The validation regex on line 2 allows port numbers (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and `before_validation` keeps them in `self.host`, but `uri.host` strips the port, so a host saved with a port (e.g. `example.com:8080`) will never match in `record_for_host`.

title: Saving a new host without selecting a category leaves host.category undefined in the UI
body: When creating a new `embeddable-host`, `edit()` is not called, so `this.get('categoryId')` is `null` unless the user explicitly changes the category chooser. When `save()` succeeds, the server defaults blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` and returns it in the payload, which `host.save(props)` applies to `host.category_id`. However, line 38 then sets `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))` using the component's `null` `categoryId` instead of `host.get('category_id')` (or `Discourse.Site.currentProp('uncategorized_category_id')`), leaving `host.category` as `undefined` and hiding the category badge until the page is reloaded.

title: Contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was overwritten with `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while all the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were placed in `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`.

title: Spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests embeddable_host presence
body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (`app/models/topic.rb:868`) was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` and no longer checks whether any `EmbeddableHost` exists. In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb`, the `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` example was moved outside the `before` block where `SiteSetting.embed_truncate = true` and `topic.stubs(:has_topic_embed?).returns(true)` are set, so it only passes because `embed_truncate` and `has_topic_embed?` default to `false`.

title: Migration crashes with IndexError when `embed_category` site setting is not present
body: The migration indexes directly into the `PG::Result` returned by `execute` with `[0]['id']`: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. On any database where `embed_category` was never modified (and thus has no row in `site_settings`) or does not match an existing category name, the query returns 0 rows and `result[0]` raises `IndexError: Index 0 is out of range` (or `NoMethodError` on `nil`), aborting the migration. The same issue applies to line 15 if `uncategorized_category_id` has no row in `site_settings`.

title: Migrated `embeddable_hosts` values are not normalized and will fail host matching
body: Previously, `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` accepted entries containing schemes (`http://`, `https://`) or paths (e.g. `https://example.com/1234`), which `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` parsed via `URI(h).host`. `EmbeddableHost` strips schemes and paths in a `before_validation` callback and `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` directly against `uri.host`. Because the migration inserts raw `h` strings via SQL `INSERT`, the `before_validation` normalization is bypassed and any existing host entries with a scheme or path will no longer match incoming requests.

title: `before_validation` raises `NoMethodError` when `host` is `nil`
body: In the `before_validation` callback, `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` is called unconditionally. If `host` is `nil` (for example, `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?` or a request with a missing `host` parameter), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` instead of failing validation with a model error.

title: `record_for_host` fails to match uppercase hostnames or hosts with ports
body: In `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, `uri = URI(host)` and `host = uri.host` preserve uppercase characters from the input URL (e.g. `URI('http://Example.com/foo').host` returns `'Example.com'`), while `where('lower(host) = ?', host)` only lowercases the database column and not the query parameter (`host.downcase`). Additionally, the format validation on line 2 explicitly allows ports (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), which are preserved in `self.host`, but `uri.host` excludes the port, so any `EmbeddableHost` configured with a port will never match.

title: Contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` are swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was overwritten with `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were placed in `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`.

title: Saving a host leaves stale buffered state and sets `category` to `undefined` when defaulted
body: In `save()`, if a new host is saved without explicitly choosing a category, `this.get('categoryId')` is `null`. The server defaults `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` and returns it in the response payload, but line 38 overwrites `host.category` with `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))` (`undefined`) instead of using `host.get('category_id')`. Additionally, `commitBuffer()` / `rollbackBuffer()` is not called after `host.save(props)`, so if the server normalizes `host` (e.g. stripping `https://` or a path), re-entering edit mode displays the un-normalized buffered string rather than the saved `host.host`.

title: `expandable_first_post?` spec for blank `embeddable_host` is a false positive
body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer checks whether any `EmbeddableHost` exists (it only checks `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb`, the `before` block setting `SiteSetting.embed_truncate = true` and stubbing `has_topic_embed?` was moved inside `describe 'with an emeddable host'`, so `it 'is false if embeddable_host is blank'` only passes because `embed_truncate` and `has_topic_embed?` are both `false` in that scope.

title: Migration crashes when `embed_category` is unset and inserts unnormalized hosts
body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` directly indexes `[0]` on the `PG::Result` without checking whether any rows were returned. On any database where `embed_category` was never saved in `site_settings` or does not match an existing category name (as well as on line 15 if `uncategorized_category_id` is absent), `[0]` raises `IndexError: Index 0 is out of range` and aborts the migration. Additionally, line 25 inserts each host via raw SQL without stripping schemes (`https?://`) or paths (`/.*`) as `EmbeddableHost` does in `before_validation`, so migrated hosts that included a scheme or path will fail to match `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`.

title: Contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` are swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was overwritten with `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains `Fabricator(:category)` and the other category fabricators.

title: `before_validation` raises `NoMethodError` on nil host and `record_for_host` fails on uppercase hosts or ports
body: In `before_validation`, `self.host.sub!` is called without checking `self.host.present?`, raising `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` if `host` is `nil`. In addition, `self.record_for_host` queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` using `uri.host` without calling `.downcase` (so URLs with uppercase characters in the host will not match) and ignores `uri.port` even though the format validation on line 2 permits `:port` in stored `host` values.

title: Saving a host with default category leaves `host.category` undefined and buffer uncommitted
body: When creating a new `embeddable-host` without choosing a category, `this.get('categoryId')` is `null` and the server assigns `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` in the response payload. However, the `.then` callback runs `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`, which overwrites `host.category` with `undefined` instead of looking up `host.get('category_id')`. In addition, `save()` never resets/commits the `buffered` proxy, so if the server normalizes the `host` value (e.g. stripping `http://`), clicking edit again will show the stale unnormalized input.

title: `expandable_first_post?` spec claims to test blank `embeddable_host` but only passes because `embed_truncate` is false
body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer checks whether an `EmbeddableHost` exists, and the test `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` only passes because `SiteSetting.embed_truncate = true` and `topic.stubs(:has_topic_embed?).returns(true)` were moved into the nested `describe 'with an emeddable host'` block.

title: Second definition of `OptimizedImage.downsize` overwrites the 4/5-argument version
body: Ruby does not support method overloading by arity. Defining `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149 completely replaces `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined on line 145. Any caller invoking `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height)` with 4 arguments will now bind `dimensions` to `max_width` and `opts` to `max_height` (causing `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` / `opts[:allow_animation]` to raise `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer`), and any 5-argument call with `opts` will raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)`.

title: `tempfile.size` and `tempfile` FD become stale when `OptimizedImage.downsize` replaces the file on disk
body: `Tempfile#size` calls `@tmpfile.stat.size` (`fstat` on the open file descriptor), not `File.size(tempfile.path)`. Inside `OptimizedImage.downsize`, `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` writes to a temporary file and atomically renames it over `tempfile.path`. Once that rename happens, `tempfile`'s open file descriptor still points to the old, unlinked inode while subsequent `convert` runs modify the new inode at `tempfile.path`. As a result, `tempfile.size` in the `while` condition and in `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)` reports the stale size from the old inode, and reading from the `tempfile` IO object reads the pre-replacement contents. In addition, the loop does not check the boolean return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize`, so unsupported images (such as SVGs, which pass `FileHelper.is_image?`) or failed conversions will pointlessly retry all 5 attempts.

title: Animated GIF downsizing fails when given percentage dimensions like `"80%"`
body: `UploadsController#create_upload` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. For a `.gif` file with `allow_animation` enabled, `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which invokes `gifsicle` with `--resize-fit 80%`. `gifsicle`'s `--resize-fit` option only accepts `WxH` pixel dimensions (scaling by a factor in `gifsicle` requires `--scale`), so `gifsicle` exits with a non-zero status and animated GIFs are never downsized.

title: Hardcoding `maxSizeKB` to 10MB breaks `max_attachment_size_kb` and larger site settings
body: `validateUploadedFile` is used for both `'image'` and `'attachment'` uploads, but `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` was replaced with a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. Non-image attachments are not downsized by the server, yet the client will now allow attachments up to 10MB even when `max_attachment_size_kb` is smaller (and will block both attachments and images when `max_attachment_size_kb` or `max_image_size_kb` is configured above 10MB).

title: Redefining `self.downsize` overwrites the 4-argument `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` overload
body: Ruby does not support method overloading by arity. Defining `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149 overwrites `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined on line 145. Existing callers that pass `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` will now bind `max_width` to `dimensions` and `max_height` (an integer) to `opts`, causing `opts[:allow_animation]` in `self.optimize` to raise `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer`, while callers passing 5 arguments `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` will raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)`.

title: `tempfile.size` and `tempfile` become stale after `ImageOptim` replaces `tempfile.path`
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` calls `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)`, which writes optimized output to a temporary file and atomically renames it over `tempfile.path`. However, `tempfile` is an open `Tempfile` object whose underlying file descriptor still points to the original (now unlinked) inode, and `tempfile.size` calls `fstat` on that open descriptor rather than checking `File.size(tempfile.path)`. Once `ImageOptim` replaces the file on the first iteration, subsequent iterations modify the new inode at `tempfile.path` while `tempfile.size` never changes, causing the loop to run all 5 attempts unnecessarily and pass the stale `tempfile` descriptor and old `tempfile.size` to `Upload.create_for` (which can still fail the size check or record the wrong file size).

title: Animated GIF downsizing fails when given a percentage dimension like `"80%"`
body: `UploadsController#create_upload` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. For a `.gif` file with `allow_animation` enabled, `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which runs `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%`. `gifsicle`'s `--resize-fit` flag only accepts `WxH` pixel dimensions (percentage scaling in `gifsicle` requires `--scale`), so `gifsicle` exits with an error on all 5 attempts and animated GIFs are never downsized.

title: Hardcoding `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` breaks attachment size validation and ignores site settings above 10MB
body: `validateUploadedFile` validates both `'image'` and `'attachment'` uploads, previously checking `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. Hardcoding `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` stops checking `max_attachment_size_kb` for non-image attachments—which are not downsized by the server and will be rejected only after the upload finishes—and also blocks uploads larger than 10MB when an administrator has configured `max_attachment_size_kb` or `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB.

title: Second definition of `self.downsize` overwrites the 4-argument overload
body: Ruby does not support method overloading by arity. Defining `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149 overwrites `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` on line 145. Any caller using the `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` signature will either raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)` when `opts` is provided, or pass `max_height` as `opts` (an Integer) when called with 4 arguments, raising `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` when `opts[:allow_animation]` is evaluated in `self.optimize`.

title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` and larger site settings
body: Replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` applies the 10MB limit to all upload types, including non-image attachments (`type === 'attachment'`). Because the server only downsizes images, attachments larger than `max_attachment_size_kb` are no longer caught by client-side validation before upload. Additionally, if an administrator configures `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB, the client will reject valid uploads (and report the hardcoded 10MB limit on HTTP 413 at line 246).

title: Downsizing with `"80%"` fails for animated GIFs and retries 5 times on any failure
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` is called with dimensions `"80%"` and `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`. For GIF files when `allow_animation` is true, `OptimizedImage.optimize` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which delegates to `resize_instructions_animated` and runs `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%`. `gifsicle`'s `--resize-fit` option requires `WxH` pixel dimensions rather than a percentage (percentage scaling in `gifsicle` uses `--scale`), so the command always fails. Furthermore, because the `while` loop does not check the boolean return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` (which also fails on formats like SVG), it will repeat the failing command all 5 times.

title: `tempfile` descriptor and `tempfile.size` become stale after `ImageOptim` replaces `tempfile.path`
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` runs `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)` on `tempfile.path`. `ImageOptim#optimize_image!` writes the optimized image to a new file and atomically replaces the destination path via `File.rename`, meaning `tempfile.path` points to a new inode while the open `tempfile` object still holds a file descriptor to the old, unlinked inode. Because `Tempfile#size` queries `fstat` on the open descriptor rather than `File.size(tempfile.path)`, `tempfile.size` in the `while` loop and in `Upload.create_for` (as well as reads from `tempfile` itself) will not reflect the replaced file unless `tempfile` is reopened.

title: `unsubscribe` crashes when no `TopicUser` row exists and bypasses `TopicUser.change`
body:
`TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns `nil` if the user does not yet have a `TopicUser` row for the topic (for example, if they received an email sent before this change, or visit `/t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` for a topic they have not visited). Line 107 then raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass`.

In addition, mutating the record with `tu.save!` instead of calling `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` fails to set `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id = TopicUser.notification_reasons[:user_changed]` (and skips publishing the change to `MessageBus`). When `notifications_reason_id` remains `nil` (such as on records created by `UserNotifications#send_notification_email`), `TopicUser.update_last_read` and `TopicUser.auto_track` will treat the notification level as never explicitly set by the user and automatically switch the user back to `tracking` when they view or interact with the topic.

title: State-mutating `GET` endpoint is non-idempotent on reload and skipped on client-side transitions
body:
`TopicsController#unsubscribe` mutates `notification_level` directly inside a `GET` request and branches on the current level (`> regular` becomes `regular`, otherwise `muted`). If the user refreshes the page, clicks the link twice, or has an email client/scanner prefetch the URL, the second `GET` will downgrade the topic from `regular` to `muted` (or overwrite a level the user just chose in the page's dropdown).

Conversely, if a user is logged out when clicking the link in their email, `ensure_logged_in` redirects them to `/login`. Once they log in and Ember routes client-side to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`, `TopicUnsubscribeRoute#model` (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` line 6) calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)`, which requests `GET /t/:id.json` (`TopicsController#show`) rather than `TopicsController#unsubscribe`. In that flow, the unsubscribe action never runs on the server, the notification level remains unchanged, and the page falsely informs the user that notifications have been stopped.

title: `MessageBuilder` raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` if `add_unsubscribe_link` is set without `unsubscribe_url`
body: `config/locales/server.en.yml` updates `unsubscribe_link` to require `%{unsubscribe_url}`, and `MessageBuilder#html_part` (line 67) and `MessageBuilder#body` (line 90) evaluate `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true. However, `MessageBuilder#initialize` only populates a default for `:user_preferences_url` in `@template_args`, not `:unsubscribe_url`. Any caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`.

title: Missing specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe`
body: There are no controller specs covering `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (such as transitioning from watching/tracking to regular, transitioning from regular to muted, handling a user without an existing `TopicUser` row, or redirecting when the slug does not match).

title: Nil TopicUser crash and bypassed TopicUser.change bookkeeping in unsubscribe
body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` if the user does not yet have a `TopicUser` row for the topic, causing `tu.notification_level` on line 107 to raise `NoMethodError` (500 error). Additionally, saving via `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change` leaves `notifications_reason_id` and `notifications_changed_at` untouched (and skips publishing the change on `MessageBus`). When a `TopicUser` row was created by `UserNotifications#send_notification_email`, `notifications_reason_id` is `nil`; leaving it `nil` means `TopicUser.update_last_read` or `TopicUser.auto_track` will later automatically reset the user's notification level back to `tracking` when they view or post in the topic.

title: Unsubscribe GET endpoint is non-idempotent and fails to stop emails for tracking users
body:
`TopicsController#unsubscribe` mutates state on a `GET` request based on the current `notification_level`: if `> regular`, it sets `regular`; otherwise it sets `muted`. This causes two problems:
1. It is not idempotent: if a `watching` user reloads the page, clicks the email link a second time, or has the link prefetched by their email client/browser, the second request sees `regular` and downgrades the topic to `muted` (or overwrites a notification level the user just selected in the UI).
2. A user at `tracking` (the default after replying to or reading a topic) only receives emails when directly replied to, quoted, or `@mentioned`—the exact same email triggers as `regular`. Changing `tracking` to `regular` does not stop any email notifications for that topic despite the page stating "You will stop receiving notifications".

title: Client-side transitions to topicUnsubscribe do not call the unsubscribe endpoint
body: `TopicUnsubscribeRoute#model` calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)`. On a direct full-page load of `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`, `loadTopicView` consumes the preloaded JSON produced by `TopicsController#unsubscribe`. However, if the route is entered via a client-side transition (when `topic_<id>` is not in `PreloadStore`), `PostStream.loadTopicView` requests `/t/:id.json` (`TopicsController#show`) rather than `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe.json`. The server never executes `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, so the user's notification level is not changed even though the UI states they have been unsubscribed.

title: Overriding computed property details.notificationReasonText breaks when changing level
body: `afterModel` hides the notification reason text by calling `topic.set("details.notificationReasonText", null)`. Because `notificationReasonText` is a computed property on `Discourse.TopicDetails` observing `notification_level` and `notifications_reason_id`, as soon as the user selects a new notification state in the `topic-notifications-button` dropdown on the unsubscribe page, the computed property recomputes and renders the reason paragraph inside the inline `.notification-options` container.

title: add_unsubscribe_link without unsubscribe_url raises MissingInterpolationArgument
body: `config/locales/server.en.yml` adds `%{unsubscribe_url}` to the `unsubscribe_link` translation, and `Email::MessageBuilder` interpolates `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is truthy (lines 67 and 90). However, `@template_args` does not define a default for `:unsubscribe_url` (unlike `:user_preferences_url`). Any caller constructing `Email::MessageBuilder` with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`.

title: Nil TopicUser crash and missing metadata update in TopicsController#unsubscribe
body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` fetches the user's topic state with `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and immediately accesses `tu.notification_level`. If no `topic_users` row exists for the user and topic (for example, if the user visits the unsubscribe URL before interacting with the topic or clicks a link from a forwarded email), `tu` is `nil` and the action raises `NoMethodError`. Additionally, mutating `tu.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` directly instead of using `TopicUser.change` fails to set `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (and skips MessageBus publication); if `notifications_reason_id` was `nil`, `TopicUser.update_last_read` and `TopicUser.auto_track` will treat the level as unset and automatically switch the topic back to `tracking` when the user views or interacts with it.

title: GET unsubscribe endpoint is non-idempotent and mutates state on page load
body: `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` mutates the user's notification level directly inside the `GET` handler, and the mutation is non-idempotent: if the user's level is `watching` or `tracking`, the first `GET` lowers it to `regular`, while refreshing the page (or a browser prefetch/prerender) issues a second `GET` that sees `regular` and lowers it again to `muted`. Conversely, if a user navigates to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` via a client-side Ember transition where `PreloadStore` is empty, `topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` (which requests `GET /t/:id.json`, routed to `TopicsController#show`), so the UI displays the unsubscribed message without ever invoking `TopicsController#unsubscribe`.

title: MessageBuilder raises MissingInterpolationArgument when add_unsubscribe_link is used without unsubscribe_url
body: The `unsubscribe_link` locale string in `config/locales/server.en.yml` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, which `Email::MessageBuilder` passes to `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` in both `html_part` (line 67) and `body` (line 90) whenever `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is truthy. Unlike `user_preferences_url`, `unsubscribe_url` is not given a default in `@template_args` or guarded by its presence, so any caller passing `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without an `unsubscribe_url` option will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`.

title: No controller or model specs for topic unsubscribe functionality
body: The PR adds `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `Topic#unsubscribe_url`, and the new `/t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` routes, but only updates a single fixture argument in `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb`. There are no specs covering `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (authentication, slug redirects, notification level transitions, or missing `TopicUser` records) or verifying that `unsubscribe_url` is rendered into notification emails.

title: Case-sensitive email lookup allows bypassing blocked emails
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` without normalizing or downcasing `email`, and `BlockedEmail` does not downcase `email` before saving either. Because `User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` directly without downcasing and PostgreSQL string comparisons on `varchar` are case-sensitive, a user whose address is stored in `blocked_emails` as `bad@spammers.org` can bypass the block by signing up with `Bad@spammers.org`.

title: Mutating `BlockedEmail#match_count` inside validator double-counts on signup
body: `EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, which increments `match_count` and saves the `BlockedEmail` record every time validations run. In `UsersController#create` (lines 168-172), `user.valid?` is evaluated first in `if user.valid? && SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` and then `user.save` runs validations a second time (after clearing `user.errors`), causing `BlockedEmail.should_block?` to execute twice and increment `match_count` by 2 for a single signup attempt.

title: Case-sensitive email lookup allows bypassing blocked emails
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` without normalizing the input's case, and `BlockedEmail` does not downcase `email` before saving or enforce case-insensitive uniqueness. Because `User` does not downcase `email` prior to validation and PostgreSQL `=` comparisons on string columns are case-sensitive, a user can bypass a blocked email entry simply by capitalizing any character in the address (e.g., `Bad@spammers.org` vs. `bad@spammers.org`).

title: Side-effecting validation increments `match_count` twice per signup attempt
body: `EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, which increments `match_count` and saves the `BlockedEmail` record during model validation. In `UsersController#create` (lines 168 and 172), `user.valid?` is evaluated first and then `user.save` is called unconditionally, running validations a second time. As a result, a single signup attempt with a blocked or tracked email executes `BlockedEmail.should_block?` twice and increments `match_count` by 2 instead of 1.

title: Case-sensitive lookup in BlockedEmail.should_block? allows bypassing blocked emails
body: `BlockedEmail` neither normalizes `email` (e.g., via `Email.downcase`) before saving nor downcases the input `email` in `BlockedEmail.should_block?(email)` before querying `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`. Because PostgreSQL `varchar` equality comparisons are case-sensitive, an entry blocking `bad@spammers.org` can be bypassed simply by signing up with `Bad@spammers.org`.

title: Mutating match_count during validation double-counts on account creation
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` increments `match_count` and saves the record inside `EmailValidator#validate_each`, which runs on every `valid?` call. In `UsersController#create` (lines 168 and 172), `user.valid?` is evaluated first and `user.save` is then called unconditionally (which runs validations a second time). As a result, every signup attempt in `UsersController#create` executes `BlockedEmail.should_block?` twice and increments `match_count` by 2 instead of 1.

title: Unanchored domain regex in email_in_restriction_setting? allows whitelist bypass and false positives
body: `EmailValidator#email_in_restriction_setting?` builds `Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true)` without anchoring the match to the end of the address (`\z`). If `email_domains_whitelist` contains `example.com`, an address such as `user@example.com.attacker.com` will match and bypass the whitelist; conversely, if `email_domains_blacklist` contains `mail.com`, legitimate addresses such as `user@mail.company.org` will be falsely rejected.

title: Invalid ERB syntax `<%- end if %>` causes a SyntaxError when rendering `embed/best`
body: Line 6 closes the `if @topic_view.posts.present?` block with `<%- end if %>`. In Ruby, `end if` without a trailing condition is invalid syntax (`SyntaxError: unexpected ';'`), so rendering the `embed/best` template will crash at runtime. (The controller spec passes only because RSpec controller specs stub view rendering by default.) This should be `<%- end %>`.

title: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url)` without requiring `open-uri` or validating the URL scheme first
body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` on line 48 without `require 'open-uri'` in `app/models/topic_embed.rb` and before `TopicEmbed.import` checks `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` on line 11. If `open-uri` has not been loaded by another class (such as `Jobs::PollFeed`), `Kernel#open` treats `url` as a local file path and raises `Errno::ENOENT`. Worse, because `Kernel#open` is invoked before the `^https?://` check, passing a non-HTTP string (such as a local path or a `|...` pipe command via callers like `import_remote`) allows arbitrary file reads or command execution. `open-uri` should be explicitly required and the `http`/`https` scheme validation should happen before `open(url)`.

title: `raw_html` cook method bypasses HTML sanitization, enabling stored XSS from RSS feeds and embedded pages
body: When `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly without running Discourse's HTML sanitizer (`PrettyText.cook`). In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35`), feed item content is unescaped with `CGI.unescapeHTML` and passed directly to `TopicEmbed.import` using `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Any `

title: `i.content.scrub` raises `NoMethodError` on RSS 2.0 feeds where `i.content` is `nil`
body: In `SimpleRSS`, standard RSS 2.0 `<item>` elements populate `i.description` (or `i.content_encoded`) rather than `i.content` (which is only populated for `<content>` tags such as in Atom feeds). For RSS 2.0 feeds without `<content>` elements, `i.content` is `nil`, so `i.content.scrub` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass` and aborts the job. Additionally, `String#scrub` was only introduced in Ruby 2.1 and will raise `NoMethodError` on Ruby 2.0.

title: `absolutize_urls` corrupts protocol-relative URLs starting with `//`
body: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` (lines 64-65 and 70-71), any `href` or `src` where `start_with?('/')` is true has leading slashes stripped via `sub(/^\/+/, '')` and `#{prefix}/` prepended. Because protocol-relative URLs (e.g., `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg`) also start with `/`, they are rewritten into `http://<embed-host>/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`, breaking external links and images that use protocol-relative URLs.

title: `TopicEmbed.import` raises `NoMethodError` when updating an embed whose post was deleted
body: When a `TopicEmbed` record already exists for `url`, line 32 fetches `post = embed.post`. Because `Post` uses `Trashable` soft deletion, `embed.post` returns `nil` if the post has been deleted. If the remote content later changes (`content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`), `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(...)` is called with `post = nil` and crashes with `NoMethodError: undefined method 'raw' for nil:NilClass`.

title: Origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` allows partial/substring origin matches
body: In `postMessageReceived`, `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` only checks that `e.origin` appears somewhere inside `discourseUrl`. Because `discourseUrl` includes a trailing slash or path (e.g., `http://discourse.example.com/`), any origin that is a prefix substring of the hostname (such as `http://discourse.example` or `http://discourse.example.co`) will pass `indexOf !== -1` at index 0. The check should compare parsed origins or verify `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin + '/') === 0`.

title: Invalid Ruby syntax `<%- end if %>` causes a SyntaxError when rendering `embed/best`
body: Line 6 closes the `if @topic_view.posts.present?` block with `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. In Ruby/Erubis, `end if;` is not valid syntax for closing an `if` block and raises a `SyntaxError` whenever `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` is compiled/rendered. (This was not caught by `embed_controller_spec.rb` because RSpec controller specs do not render views by default.)

title: `i.content.scrub` raises `NoMethodError` on RSS 2.0 feeds and Ruby < 2.1
body: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, line 35 calls `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. With `SimpleRSS`, standard RSS 2.0 items populate `i.description` (or `i.content_encoded`) rather than `i.content` (which is an Atom element), so `i.content` is `nil` and calling `.scrub` on it raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass`. Additionally, `String#scrub` was only introduced in Ruby 2.1 and will raise `NoMethodError` on Ruby 2.0/1.9.

title: Unescaped `url` and unsanitized HTML stored with `cook_method: raw_html` allow Stored XSS
body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to `contents` without escaping `url` and creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which causes `Post#cook` to return `raw` directly and bypass `PrettyText` HTML sanitization. Because Ruby's `URI.parse` allows single quotes (`'`) in URLs, an attacker can request `/embed/best?embed_url=http:///valid-path?x='onmouseover='alert(1)` (with a matching `Referer` header), passing `URI(@embed_url).host` validation in `TopicRetriever` and injecting arbitrary attributes/HTML into the created forum post. In addition, `Jobs::PollFeed` passes raw unescaped feed HTML directly to `TopicEmbed.import` without sanitization, and `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string in place (failing if `contents` is `nil` or frozen).

title: `invalid_host?` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` do not validate URI scheme or nil host before calling `open`
body: In `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` does not check that `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is present or that the URI scheme is `http`/`https`. If `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is `nil`, any relative URI or file path (such as `"/etc/passwd"` or `"not_a_url"`) has `URI(@embed_url).host == nil`, so `nil != nil` evaluates to `false` (valid). Even when `embeddable_host` is set, non-HTTP schemes such as `ftp://<embeddable_host>/...` or arbitrary ports pass `invalid_host?` and are passed to `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (line 48) before `TopicEmbed.import` ever checks `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`. Furthermore, `fetch_http` on line 49 calls `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` without checking if `embed_by_username` is `nil`.

title: `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` corrupts protocol-relative URLs starting with `//`
body: `absolutize_urls` checks `href.start_with?('/')` (and `src.start_with?('/')` on line 70) and rewrites the attribute to `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`. Protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` start with `'/'`, so `absolutize_urls` strips the leading `//` and prepends the article's host prefix, turning them into broken URLs like `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`.

title: `TopicEmbed.import` raises `NoMethodError` when updating an embed whose post was deleted
body: neither `Topic` nor `Post` destroys associated `TopicEmbed` records on deletion, and `Post` includes `Trashable` (which scopes out soft-deleted posts). If an imported topic or post is deleted by a moderator, `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` will still be found on subsequent imports, but `embed.post` will be `nil`. When the remote content changes, `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!` on line 36 will raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'raw' for nil:NilClass`.

title: `loading` response is cached for 1 minute while `loading.html.erb` reloads after 30 seconds
body: `EmbedController#best` calls `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` unconditionally, including when `topic_id` is `nil` and the `loading` template is rendered. However, `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` schedules `document.location.reload()` after 30 seconds (`30000` ms). Because the `loading` response has a 60-second `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` header, the 30-second reload will be served the stale `loading` page from cache even if the background `RetrieveTopic` job has already finished.

title: `Jobs::PollFeed#feed_key` is unused, causing `TopicRetriever` to re-download and re-parse the entire RSS feed on every cache miss
body: `Jobs::PollFeed#feed_key` defines a Redis key for tracking feed polling, but it is never used in `poll_feed` or `execute`. Because `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` (`lib/topic_retriever.rb:41`) invokes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously whenever a requested `@embed_url` is not yet in `topic_embeds`, any request for an older article (not present in the current RSS feed) will synchronously download, parse, and import the entire RSS feed before falling back to `fetch_http`.

title: Invalid Ruby syntax `<%- end if %>` in ERB template causes SyntaxError
body: Line 6 closes the `if @topic_view.posts.present?` block with `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. In Ruby, `end if` is not valid syntax for closing an `if` block (it is parsed as `end` followed by a trailing `if` modifier with a missing condition), so rendering `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` will raise a `SyntaxError` whenever an embedded topic is viewed.

title: Unvalidated `open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` allows local file read / SSRF and lacks `require 'open-uri'`
body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` without requiring `'open-uri'` (which is only required in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`) and without validating the URL scheme. First, when `import_remote` is called from `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (when `feed_polling_enabled` is false) or `disqus.thor`, `open-uri` may not be loaded, causing `Kernel#open` to treat `url` as a file path and raise `Errno::ENOENT`. Second, `TopicEmbed.import` only checks `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` after `import_remote` has already called `open(url).read`, and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only checks `URI(@embed_url).host` without checking `URI(@embed_url).scheme`. A protocol-relative URL such as `//<embeddable_host>/etc/passwd` passes the host check in `TopicRetriever` and causes `Kernel#open` to read arbitrary files from the server filesystem (and if `import_remote` is called with a leading pipe character, `Kernel#open` will execute shell commands).

title: Stored XSS via unescaped `url` and unsanitized HTML with `raw_html` cook method
body: `Post#cook` bypasses the entire sanitization and rendering pipeline when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, returning `raw` verbatim. In `TopicEmbed.import`, `url` is interpolated directly into `#{url}` without HTML/attribute escaping, and `Jobs::PollFeed` passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` directly into `TopicEmbed.import` without HTML sanitization. Because `EmbedController#best` allows any unauthenticated user to enqueue `RetrieveTopic` for any `embed_url` whose host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, a URL containing characters valid in Ruby's `URI.parse` such as single quotes (e.g. `http://example.com/post?'onmouseover='alert(1)`) will break out of the `href` attribute and store arbitrary JavaScript in the cooked post.

title: `i.content.scrub` raises `NoMethodError` on standard RSS 2.0 feeds where `content` is `nil`
body: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, `i.content.scrub` assumes every feed item has a non-nil `content` attribute. In `SimpleRSS`, standard RSS 2.0 feeds populate `i.description` (or `i.content_encoded`) rather than `i.content` (which is only populated for Atom `<content>` elements). When polling an RSS 2.0 feed or an Atom entry without `<content>`, `i.content` is `nil`, causing `i.content.scrub` to raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass` and abort the job.

title: `absolutize_urls` corrupts protocol-relative URLs starting with `//`
body: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, links and images are checked with `href.start_with?('/')` and `src.start_with?('/')`, and then rewritten using `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`. Protocol-relative URLs (such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg`) also start with `'/'`, so all leading slashes are stripped and the embed host is prepended, turning `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` into `http://<embed_host>/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`.

title: `TopicEmbed.import` does not handle failed post creation or soft-deleted embedded posts
body: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `post = creator.create` returns the unsaved `Post` instance even if `PostCreator#create` rolled back (for example, when `rollback_if_host_spam_detected` triggers because `skip_validations` does not bypass the host spam check). Because `post.present?` is `true` for an unsaved ActiveRecord object (`post.id` is `nil`), `TopicEmbed.create!` is called with `post_id: nil`, raising a database `NOT NULL` constraint violation. Similarly, in the `else` branch on line 32, if the previously created post was soft-deleted, `embed.post` returns `nil` and `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!` raises `NoMethodError`.

title: Unescaped/HTML-escaped `request.referer` in `<script>` corrupts `postMessage` `targetOrigin`
body: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, `<%= request.referer %>` is interpolated directly into a JavaScript string literal passed as `targetOrigin` to `parent.postMessage`. Because ERB applies HTML entity escaping (`&` -> `&`, `'` -> `'`) which is not decoded inside a `<script>` block, any referer URL containing `'`, `&`, or `\` can produce an invalid `targetOrigin` or break the JavaScript string literal instead of passing the referer's origin.

title: `.small-action-desc` shrinks to content width inside flex container, breaking right-floated buttons
body: Making `.small-action` a flex container (`@include flexbox()`) turns `.small-action-desc` into a flex item with default `flex: 0 1 auto` (`width: auto`) instead of a full-width block element. Because `.small-action-desc` no longer spans the full width of `.small-action` (e.g., via `width: 100%` or `flex: 1`), the edit/delete buttons (`button { float: right; }`) inside `.small-action-desc` will sit immediately next to the description text instead of aligning to the far right edge of the post row (and any `button` that is a direct child of `.small-action` will have `float: right` ignored entirely because floats do not apply to flex items).

title: Header `.panel` can shrink and wrap when topic extra info is long, and fails to right-align in `-webkit-box`
body:
With `.d-header .contents` changed to a flex container and `float: right` replaced by `margin-left: auto` on `.panel`, two layout issues arise:
1. Neither `.panel` nor `.title` has `flex-shrink: 0` (or `flex: 0 0 auto`). Because `.panel` contains floated children (`.icons`, `.login-button`, `button.sign-up-button`), when `.extra-info-wrapper` is shown in the header with a long topic title, the flex layout shrinks `.panel`, causing its floated buttons and icons to wrap onto multiple lines.
2. In legacy browsers that fall back to `display: -webkit-box` or `display: -moz-box` from `@mixin flexbox()`, `margin-left: auto` is ignored on box children, so `.panel` will sit adjacent to `.title` on the left instead of aligning to the right edge of the header.

title: `align-items` mixin omits `-moz-box-align` and passes incompatible values to legacy syntaxes
body: `@mixin align-items($alignment)` includes `-ms-align-items` (which is not a valid CSS property in any version of IE) while omitting `-moz-box-align: $alignment` even though `@mixin flexbox()` and `@mixin order()` emit `-moz-box` rules. Additionally, if standard values `flex-start` or `flex-end` are passed to `align-items`, `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` will be invalid because the 2009 and 2012 flexbox specs only accept `start` and `end`.

title: `include_website_name` is missing `?` and `website_name` bypasses `untrusted_attributes` restrictions
body:
`ActiveModel::Serializer` requires conditional inclusion methods to end with a question mark (`include_website_name?`). Because the method is defined as `def include_website_name`, it is never called by the serializer, causing `:website_name` to always be serialized in the JSON output (even as `nil` when the user has no website).

Additionally, `:website` is declared under `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) so that it is hidden when an anonymous visitor views a TL0 user (`scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`). Because `:website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, a TL0 user's website domain/path is still serialized and displayed on their profile (`{{#if model.website_name}}` in `user.hbs`) to anonymous users. Adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (and removing the manual `include_website_name` method) will automatically define `include_website_name?` with both the `restrict_user_fields?` check and the `.present?` check.

title: `include_website_name` is missing `?` and bypasses `untrusted_attributes` restrictions for TL0 users
body: `ActiveModel::Serializer` requires conditional inclusion methods to end with a question mark (`include_website_name?`). Because `def include_website_name` has no `?`, it is never called and `website_name: nil` is always serialized even when a user has no `website`. In addition, `website` is declared in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) so that it is hidden when blank or when an anonymous visitor views a TL0 user (`scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`). Because `website_name` is not in `untrusted_attributes`, a TL0 user's website is still serialized in `website_name` and rendered on the profile page to anonymous users. Adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and removing `def include_website_name` (which would otherwise overwrite the `include_website_name?` method generated by `untrusted_attributes`) fixes both issues.

title: `User#save` does not update `website_name` after saving profile preferences
body: Previously, `websiteName` was a client-side computed property observing `model.website`, so editing `website` in user preferences immediately updated the displayed name. Now that the template renders the server-serialized `model.website_name`, `User#save` needs to copy `data.user.website_name` onto the model alongside `self.set('bio_excerpt', data.user.bio_excerpt)`. Without this, when a user adds or updates their website in preferences and views their profile without a full page reload, `model.website_name` remains `undefined` or stale while `model.website` points to the new URL.

title: Subdomain websites of an apex Discourse instance do not include the URL path
body: When the Discourse instance is hosted on an apex domain (e.g. `example.com`) and the user's website is on a subdomain (e.g. `http://www.example.com/user`), execution reaches the `else` branch where `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` evaluates to `false`. As a result, `website_name` returns only `www.example.com` without `/user`, whereas the symmetric case (`forums.example.com` with `http://example.com/user`) includes the path.

title: `include_website_name` is missing `?` and bypasses `untrusted_attributes` restrictions
body:
`ActiveModel::Serializer` expects conditional inclusion methods to end with a question mark (`include_website_name?`). Because `def include_website_name` has no trailing `?`, it is never called and `website_name` is always serialized into the JSON output (even as `nil` when the user has no website).

In addition, `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) so that TL0 users' profile URLs are hidden from anonymous visitors via `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`, but `website_name` is not. As a result, a TL0 user's website host/path is still exposed in the JSON and rendered as text on the user profile page for anonymous users. Adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (and removing `def include_website_name`) will define `include_website_name?` with both the trust-level restriction and `.present?` check.

title: Domain comparison mishandles multi-part TLDs and subdomains of apex instance domains
body:
The domain matching logic in `website_name` has two flaws:

1. In the `elsif` branch, comparing `split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` whenever both hosts have the same number of labels (`> 2`) treats any two unrelated domains under a two-level public suffix (e.g. `discourse_host = 'example.co.uk'` and `website_host = 'other.co.uk'`, or `.com.au`, `.org.uk`) as the same domain because both strip the first label and match on `'co.uk'`.
2. When the Discourse instance is hosted on an apex domain (e.g. `example.com`) and the user's website is on a subdomain such as `http://www.example.com/user` or `http://blog.example.com/user`, `website_host == discourse_host` is false, the `elsif` branch is skipped because label counts differ (`3 != 2`), and the `else` branch checks `'example.com'.ends_with?('.www.example.com')` which is false, so the path is unexpectedly omitted.

title: `website_name` is not updated on the user model after saving preferences
body: Previously, `websiteName` was a client-side computed property on the controller observing `model.website`, so saving a new `website` in user preferences updated the displayed website name immediately. Now that `website_name` is computed on the server, `User#save` (around line 210, where `self.set('bio_excerpt', data.user.bio_excerpt)` is updated from the `PUT /users/:username` response) does not copy `data.user.website_name` onto the model, leaving `model.website_name` stale or blank when navigating back to the user profile without a full page reload.

title: Inverted lightness percentages in `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`
body: The original rule `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, swapping the `30%` and `70%` lightness values. This changes the light-theme color from 30% to 70% lightness and leaves embedded post author links low-contrast against the background in both light and dark themes. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` (matching `.names span a` in `common/base/topic-post.scss`).

This makes `.custom-message-length` much darker in light themes and much brighter in dark themes than intended, and is inconsistent with the same selector in `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/modal.scss` (line 94), which uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

title: `.topic-map h3` lightness changed from 20%/80% to 50%/50%
body: In `.topic-map h3`, `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` was changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` instead of `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))` (compare with `.topic-map h3` in `desktop/topic-post.scss` line 321). This alters the light-theme color and gives `h3` the same muted shade as `h4` in the mobile topic map.

body: In `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification`, `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%);` was not wrapped in `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` (unlike the matching `.category .badge-notification` rule in `app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss` line 301).

title: Off-by-one error in totalPages when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is a non-zero multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 members with the default limit of 50), this returns `2` instead of `1`. As a result, `showingLast` (`currentPage === totalPages`) is `false`, the next-page button remains enabled, and clicking it sets `offset` to `50` and fetches an empty page `2/2`. It should use `Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"))` (or `Math.floor((this.get("user_count") - 1) / this.get("limit")) + 1`), and `offset` in `next` / `Group#findMembers` should not be allowed to reach `user_count`.

title: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), bypassing counter cache and raising on non-members
body:
Replacing `group.remove(user)` with `group.users.delete(user_id)` on the `has_many :users, through: :group_users` association causes two issues:
1. Because `:dependent` is not `:destroy` on the `has_many :through` association, ActiveRecord executes `delete_all` on `group_users` rather than destroying the `GroupUser` records, bypassing `GroupUser`'s `belongs_to :group, counter_cache: "user_count"` callback and leaving `groups.user_count` un-decremented.
2. Passing an integer `user_id` to `collection.delete` causes ActiveRecord to call `group.users.find(user_id)` first, which raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` if the user is already not a member of the group.

title: add_members raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique when adding an existing member
body: `add_members` calls `group.add(user)` for each username without checking whether the user is already in `group.users`. Because `group_users` has a unique index on `(group_id, user_id)` and the admin UI neither filters out existing members nor clears the `user-selector` input after adding, attempting to add a user who is already in the group raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (HTTP 500).

title: Admin::GroupsController#create ignores alias_level parameter
body: The admin group template displays the `alias_level` selector when creating a new group and `Discourse.Group#asJSON` includes `alias_level` in the `POST /admin/groups` payload, but `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `name` and `visible` and ignores `params[:alias_level]` (unlike `update`, which sets `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?`). Any alias level selected during group creation is silently lost.

title: Public group members page only displays the first 50 members with no way to view the rest
body: `GroupsController#members` and `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now paginate with a default `limit` of 50, but the public group members template (`group/members.hbs`) and route (`group-members.js.es6`) have no pagination or load-more mechanism. Any group with more than 50 members will only ever show the first 50 members on `/groups/:name/members`.

title: Off-by-one error in totalPages when user_count is a multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. Whenever `user_count` is a positive multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 members with `limit = 50`), `totalPages` evaluates to `2` instead of `1`. As a result, the page counter displays `1/2`, `showingLast` remains `false`, and clicking `next` sets `offset` to `50` and loads an empty page. It should use `Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"))` (or `Math.floor((this.get("user_count") - 1) / this.get("limit")) + 1`).

title: Offset is not clamped below total count when reloading members after deletion
body: In `findMembers`, `offset` is computed as `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))`, and `GroupsController#members` applies `params[:offset].to_i` directly without clamping it to the new `total`. If an admin is on the last page with a single member (e.g. 51st member at `offset = 50`, `limit = 50`) and removes that member, `removeMember` calls `findMembers()` with `offset = 50` while the group now has 50 members. The server returns an empty `members` array with `meta.total = 50` and `meta.offset = 50`, leaving the admin viewing an empty page even though 50 members remain in the group.

title: Group creation ignores alias_level parameter
body: The admin group form (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs`) renders the `alias_level` combo-box when creating a new group, and `Discourse.Group#create` sends `alias_level` in its POST payload via `asJSON()`. However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `group.name` and `group.visible` and ignores `params[:alias_level]` (unlike `update`, which sets `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?`). Any alias level selected during group creation is silently discarded.

title: Adding an existing member in add_members raises a duplicate key error
body: `add_members` splits `usernames` and calls `group.add(user)` for each found user without checking whether the user is already a member of `group` (or listed more than once in `usernames`). Because the new member list is paginated and the user-selector autocomplete does not exclude current group members, adding a user who is already in the group will attempt to insert a duplicate `group_users` record and fail with `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (HTTP 500).

title: Public group members page is truncated to 50 members with no pagination
body: `GroupsController#members` now limits results to 50 members by default for all groups, and `GroupMembersRoute` calls `model.findMembers()` which only fetches the first 50 members (`limit: 50, offset: 0`). Unlike the admin group template, the public group members view (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`) has no pagination or load-more mechanism, so any group with more than 50 members can no longer display members beyond the first 50.

title: Unvalidated limit and offset parameters in GroupsController#members
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed directly to `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` without bounds checking. Passing a negative `limit` or `offset` in the query string raises an unhandled `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` (`PG::InvalidRowCountInLimitClause` / `PG::InvalidRowCountInResultOffsetClause`, HTTP 500), and there is no upper cap on `limit`.

title: remove_member spec uses PUT instead of DELETE
body: In the `.remove_member` spec context, the test `'cannot remove members from automatic groups'` invokes `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, whereas `remove_member` is routed via `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members` (`xhr :delete`).

title: Off-by-one error in `totalPages` when `user_count` is a multiple of `limit`
