body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact non-zero multiple of `limit` (for example, 50 members with the default `limit` of 50), this returns `2` instead of `1`. Because `showingLast` checks `currentPage === totalPages`, the Next button remains enabled on the last page and clicking it sets `offset` to `50` and loads an empty page `2/2`. This should be `Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"))`.

title: `add_members` raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` if a user is already in the group
body: `add_members` calls `group.add(user)` for each username without checking whether the user is already a member of the group (e.g. `unless group.users.include?(user)`). Because `group_users` has a unique index on `(group_id, user_id)`, adding an existing member or passing duplicate usernames raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (HTTP 500). This is especially easy to hit from the UI because `addMembers` in `admin-group.js.es6` (line 62) does not clear `this.get("usernames")` after adding members, so subsequent additions re-submit previously added usernames.

title: `usernames` is never cleared after adding members or when switching groups
body: In `AdminGroupController`, `usernames` is not cleared after `addMembers` runs (and is not reset in `AdminGroupRoute#setupController` when switching between groups). Any usernames entered in the selector remain bound to the singleton controller, so adding another batch of users or navigating to another group keeps the old usernames in the input.

title: `Admin::GroupsController#create` ignores `alias_level`
body: The new-group form in `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs` displays the `alias_level` combo-box and `Discourse.Group#asJSON` sends `alias_level` in the `POST /admin/groups` payload, but `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `name` and `visible` (unlike `update`, which sets `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?`). Any alias level selected during group creation is silently ignored and saved as the default (`0`).

title: Removing the last member on a page leaves pagination stuck on an empty out-of-bounds page
body: When removing the sole member on the last page (e.g. the 51st member when `limit` is 50 and `offset` is 50), `removeMember` calls `findMembers()` while `user_count` in memory is still `51`. `findMembers()` sends `offset: 50` to the server, which now has `total: 50` and returns `members: []` with `meta: { total: 50, limit: 50, offset: 50 }`. `setProperties` then sets `user_count: 50` and `offset: 50`, leaving the UI displaying an empty member list at an out-of-bounds offset instead of clamping `offset` to the last valid page.

title: Fallback locales are not loaded when `I18n.t` is called outside `ApplicationController` or with a `:locale` option
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only called in `ApplicationController#set_locale`, while `I18n.translate` in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)`. When `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` iterates over `I18n.fallbacks[locale]`, it calls `super(fallback, key, options)` directly on `I18n.backend`, bypassing `I18n.translate`. As a result, whenever `I18n.t` is called outside a controller action (e.g. in Sidekiq jobs, `UserNotifications` mailers, rake tasks, or specs), after `I18n.reload!`, or with an explicit `I18n.t(key, locale: ...)` / `I18n.with_locale(...)`, the fallback locales (or the passed `:locale`) are never loaded into `I18n.backend`. Fallback lookups then fail with missing translations, and for zero-argument `I18n.t(key)` calls, the missing-translation result gets cached in `@cache`. Ensuring fallback locales are loaded inside `load_locale`/`translate` in `translate_accelerator.rb` (including when `options[:locale]` is passed) avoids this.

title: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` and `ensure_loaded!` do not normalize `locale` to a symbol
body: In `FallbackLocaleList#[]`, `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` leaves `locale` as-is while converting `SiteSetting.default_locale` and `:en` to symbols. When `I18n.t(key, locale: "en")` or `I18n.fallbacks["fr"]` is called with a string locale (such as `SiteSetting.default_locale` or `user.effective_locale`), `.uniq` does not deduplicate `"en"` and `:en` (returning `["en", :en]`), causing duplicate lookups on missing keys. Likewise, `I18n.ensure_loaded!` and `I18n.load_locale` in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` do not convert `locale` with `.to_sym`, so passing a string locale when the symbol locale is already in `@loaded_locales` will reload all YAML files for that locale a second time.

title: No tests for server-side localization fallbacks
body: This PR introduces `FallbackLocaleList` and enables server-side locale fallbacks across all environments, but adds no specs verifying the `[user_locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]` fallback chain or that unloaded fallback locales are loaded on demand.

title: Fallback locales are not loaded when `I18n.translate` is called outside `ApplicationController` or with `:locale`
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only invoked in `ApplicationController#set_locale`, while `I18n.translate` in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)`. Because `translate_accelerator.rb` overrides `I18n::Backend::Base#load_translations` to prevent automatic loading of all locale files, any `I18n.t` call made outside a controller action (such as in Sidekiq jobs, `UserNotifications` mailers, rake tasks, or specs) or after `I18n.reload!` will not have `SiteSetting.default_locale` or `:en` loaded in the backend, so fallback lookups will fail with `translation missing`. Furthermore, for zero-argument `I18n.t(key)` calls, `@cache.getset(k)` at line 74 will cache the `"translation missing: ..."` result, poisoning subsequent controller requests as well. Calling `I18n.t(key, locale: other_locale)` also fails to load `other_locale` and its fallbacks. `I18n.translate` (or `load_locale`) should ensure the requested locale and all of its `I18n.fallbacks` are loaded.

title: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` does not convert `locale` to a Symbol before deduplicating
body: In `FallbackLocaleList#[](locale)`, `locale` is combined with Symbol locales in `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` without converting `locale` to a Symbol. While `I18n.locale` is a Symbol, `I18n.translate(key, locale: ...)` passes `options[:locale]` directly to the backend without calling `.to_sym` (and methods like `SiteSetting.default_locale` and `User#effective_locale` return Strings). When `locale` is a String such as `"en"`, `["en", :en, :en].uniq` returns `["en", :en]` instead of `[:en]`, causing redundant fallback lookups and mismatches with Symbol entries in `@loaded_locales`.

title: No tests covering server-side locale fallbacks
body: This PR introduces `FallbackLocaleList` and lazy loading for fallback locales in `translate_accelerator.rb` without any test coverage verifying that missing translations fall back from the active locale to `SiteSetting.default_locale` and then to `:en`.

title: Fallback and explicit `:locale` translations are not loaded outside `ApplicationController#set_locale` or after `I18n.reload!`
body:
`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only invoked in `ApplicationController#set_locale`, while `I18n.translate` in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` still only runs `load_locale(config.locale)`. Because `translate_accelerator.rb` overrides `I18n::Backend::Base#load_translations` to prevent automatic loading, `I18n.backend` only contains translations for locales explicitly passed to `load_locale`. Consequently:
1. Any translation call outside a controller request (such as in Sidekiq background jobs, `UserNotifications` mailers, rake tasks, or specs) or after `I18n.reload!` is called will only load `config.locale` and leave the fallback locales (`SiteSetting.default_locale` and `:en`) unloaded. Fallback lookups will fail with `"translation missing"` and cache the missing-translation string in `@cache`.
2. Calling `I18n.t(key, locale: other_locale)` when `other_locale` has not yet been loaded will not load `other_locale` at all; with `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` enabled, it will silently return the `:en` / `SiteSetting.default_locale` fallback even when a translation exists for `other_locale`.

title: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` does not normalize `locale` to a symbol
body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` builds `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` without converting `locale` to a symbol. When `locale` is passed as a `String` (for example via `I18n.t(key, locale: "en")` or `I18n.fallbacks["en"]`), `.uniq` will not deduplicate `"en"` against `:en` (returning `["en", :en]`), and `I18n.load_locale` will not match `"en"` against `:en` in `@loaded_locales`, causing all YAML files for that locale to be parsed and loaded a second time.

title: Missing specs for server-side locale fallbacks
body: This PR introduces custom server-side locale fallback ordering (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`) and lazy fallback loading via `FallbackLocaleList`, but adds no specs verifying fallback lookup behavior, pluralization fallback behavior, or lazy loading of fallback locales.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type, colliding across anonymous, render, user, and service-account subjects
body: In `Check`, `permDenialKey` is constructed with `userPermDenialCacheKey(checkReq.Namespace.Value, checkReq.UserUID, ...)`, where `checkReq.UserUID` is the ID portion extracted by `types.ParseTypeID( req.GetSubject())` without the identity type prefix. Both `"anonymous:0"` and `"render:0"` parse to `checkReq.UserUID == "0"`, and `"user:<id>"` and `"service-account:<id>"` share the same `UserUID` when numeric IDs are used. If an anonymous request (`"anonymous:0"`) is denied `dashboards:read`, `folders:read`, or `datasources:read` on a resource, `permDenialCache` records a denial under `<ns>.perm_0_<action>_<name>_<folder>`. Subsequent `Check` calls for the render service (`"render:0"`) within the 30s TTL will hit `permDenialCache` and return `Allowed: false`, even though the render service is granted wildcard read permissions in `getRendererPermissions`. Include the identity type (or full subject) in `userPermDenialCacheKey` (and/or skip `permDenialCache` for `TypeRenderService`).

title: Non-cache-miss errors from `getCachedIdentityPermissions` cause duplicate `GetUserIdentifiers` DB queries
body: `getCachedIdentityPermissions` calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers(ctx, ns, userID)` for `TypeUser` and `TypeServiceAccount`, which queries the database when the user identifier is not in `idCache`. If `GetUserIdentifiers` returns an error (e.g., the user does not exist or the DB fails), both `Check` (line 124) and `List` (line 181) treat any non-nil error as a cache miss and immediately call `s.getIdentityPermissions`, which calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers` a second time for the same user. `Check` and `List` should only fall back to `getIdentityPermissions` when `errors.Is(err, cache.ErrNotFound)` and return other errors immediately.

title: Denial cache test sets `permCache` entry to `false` instead of `true`
body: In `TestService_CacheCheck` (`"Should deny on explicit cache deny entry"`), line 982 sets `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}` in `s.permCache` with the comment `// Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked`. Because the map value is `false` (and `fakeStore` has no permissions), `checkPermission` would return `false` even if `permDenialCache` were never consulted. The map value should be `true` so the test actually verifies that `permDenialCache` overrides an allow in `permCache`.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type, causing collisions between anonymous:0 and render:0
body:
`validateSubject` parses `req.GetSubject()` via `types.ParseTypeID` into `checkReq.IdentityType` and `checkReq.UserUID`. However, `userPermDenialCacheKey` at line 116 only includes `checkReq.UserUID` (`namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent`) and omits `checkReq.IdentityType`.

Because both anonymous users (`anonymous:0`) and the render service (`render:0`) have `UserUID == "0"`, whenever `anonymous:0` is denied access to a dashboard, folder, or datasource, that denial is cached under `UserUID = "0"`. Any subsequent `Check` request from `render:0` for the same resource within `shortCacheTTL` (30s) will hit `permDenialCache` and return `Allowed: false` before `getRendererPermissions` is reached, breaking dashboard/panel rendering. The same collision can also occur between `user:<id>` and `service-account:<id>`. Include `checkReq.IdentityType` (or the full subject) in `userPermDenialCacheKey`.

title: Denial cache test sets permission map entry to false instead of true
body: In `TestService_CacheCheck` ("Should deny on explicit cache deny entry"), line 982 has the comment `// Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked`, but sets `permCache` to `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}` while `fakeStore` has no permissions. Because `checkPermission` checks `if scopeMap[t.scope(req.Name)]`, `s.Check` would return `Allowed: false` even if `permDenialCache` were not consulted at all. The value in `permCache` should be `true` so the test actually verifies that the denial cache short-circuits the permission check.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type, colliding between anonymous:0 and render:0
body: `validateSubject` parses `req.GetSubject()` with `types.ParseTypeID`, which sets `checkReq.UserUID` to `"0"` for both `anonymous:0` (`types.TypeAnonymous`) and `render:0` (`types.TypeRenderService`). Because `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses only `checkReq.UserUID` and does not include `checkReq.IdentityType` (or the full subject), when `anonymous:0` is denied `dashboards:read`, `folders:read`, or `datasources:read` on a resource, `permDenialCache` stores the denial under `<namespace>.perm_0_<action>_<name>_<parent>`. Any subsequent `Check` from `render:0` for the same resource within `shortCacheTTL` (30s) will hit that denial cache entry and return `Allowed: false`, breaking dashboard rendering even though `TypeRenderService` has wildcard read permissions. Additionally, for user subjects specified by numeric ID versus UID, `permDenialCache` keys on the raw `checkReq.UserUID` while `permCache` normalizes via `GetUserIdentifiers`.

title: Check and List execute duplicate DB lookup when GetUserIdentifiers fails
body: `getCachedIdentityPermissions` calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers(ctx, ns, userID)`, which queries the database when `idCache` misses. If `GetUserIdentifiers` returns an error (for example, if the user does not exist or the database query fails), `Check` (line 124) and `List` (line 180) treat any non-nil error as a cache miss and immediately invoke `s.getIdentityPermissions`, which calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers` a second time and repeats the failing database query. Callers should return early when `err != nil && !errors.Is(err, cache.ErrNotFound)` (or `getCachedIdentityPermissions` should only read from `idCache`).

title: Denial cache test sets cached permission to false instead of true
body: In `TestService_CacheCheck` ("Should deny on explicit cache deny entry"), line 982 sets `s.permCache` with `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}` even though the comment above it says `// Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked`. Because the scope value is `false` and the fake store has no permissions, `s.Check` would return `Allowed: false` even if `permDenialCache` were completely ignored. The value in `permCache` should be `true` to verify that `permDenialCache` short-circuits `permCache`.

title: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` returns supported abilities when `skipToken` / `undefined` is passed
body: When `skipToken` is passed to `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` or `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (such as in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` when `promRule` is a data-source-managed rule or `undefined`), `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)` is called. For `rule === undefined`, `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(undefined)` returns `{ isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading: false }`, so `loading` is `false` and `isPluginProvided` is `false`. This makes `MaybeSupported` and `duplicateSupported` evaluate to `true`, and `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)` returns `[true, ctx.hasPermission(AccessControlAction.AlertingRuleCreate)]` for `AlertRuleAction.Duplicate` (as well as `[true, ...]` for `View` and `Explore`). In `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`, `canDuplicate` combines the ruler and Grafana prom abilities with `||`, so any user with the internal Grafana `AlertingRuleCreate` permission will see the `Duplicate` action enabled on non-Grafana rules even when duplication is unsupported or the user lacks external rule write permissions. When `!rule`, all abilities should return `[NotSupported, false]`.

title: Delete and Pause menu items are still gated on `rulerRule` and never render in the alert list view
body: `AlertRuleMenu` now computes `canPause` and `canDelete` from `promRule` via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` because `rulerRule` is no longer fetched in the alert list view (`GrafanaRuleListItem` renders `<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} compact />` with `rule` / `rulerRule` undefined). However, rendering the Pause item on line 123 is still guarded by `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and rendering the Delete item on line 165 is still guarded by `&& rulerRule`. As a result, neither Pause nor Delete is ever shown for Grafana rules in the alert list view (even though `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` line 99 already invokes `showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)` without needing `rulerRule`).

title: Clicking "Silence notifications" for Grafana rules in the alert list view does nothing
body: In the alert list view, `GrafanaRuleListItem` renders `RuleActionsButtons` with `promRule` only and `rule` (`RulerRuleDTO`) undefined. `AlertRuleMenu` renders the "Silence notifications" menu item based on `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(promRule, ...)`, and clicking it calls `handleSilence={() => setShowSilenceDrawer(true)}`. However, line 104 gates `<SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer>` on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`. Because `rule` is `undefined`, `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is always `false` and the silence drawer never opens.

title: Missing `key` prop on `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` inside `rules.map`
body: When replacing `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ... />` with `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` inside `rules.map`, the `key={key}` prop was omitted. Rendering list items without a `key` triggers React warnings and can cause incorrect component reconciliation when filtering or paginating rules.

title: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` no longer treats federated rule groups as immutable
body: Previously, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` checked `const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and treated federated rules as immutable (setting `Update`, `Delete`, `Pause`, `Restore`, and `DeletePermanently` to `NotSupported`). By delegating to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`—where `isFederated` is hardcoded to `false` on line 245—callers of `useAlertRuleAbility`, `useAlertRuleAbilities`, and `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` will now erroneously treat federated rules as editable and removable.

title: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` disables export, pause, restore, and permanent delete for Grafana recording rules
body: In `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore`, and `DeletePermanently` are supported for all Grafana-managed rules (`rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which includes both alerting and recording rules). In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, lines 302 and 324-330 instead gate those actions on `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` rather than `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which marks `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore`, and `DeletePermanently` as unsupported for Grafana-managed recording rules.

title: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` returns supported/allowed abilities when `skipToken` (`undefined`) is passed
body: When `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` or `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` is called with `skipToken` (for example, in `AlertRuleMenu` and `RuleActionsButtons.V2` when `promRule` is a data source/cloud rule or `undefined`), `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` is invoked with `rule = undefined`. Inside `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `loading` is `false` and `MaybeSupported` evaluates to `AlwaysSupported` (`true`), so `AlertRuleAction.Duplicate` returns `[true, ctx.hasPermission(rulesPermissions.create)]` and `View`/`Explore` also return `[true, ...]`. Because `AlertRuleMenu` combines abilities with `(duplicateSupported && duplicateAllowed) || (grafanaDuplicateSupported && grafanaDuplicateAllowed)`, any user with `AlertingRuleCreate` permission will see the Duplicate action enabled on all non-Grafana rules (including plugin-provided rules, rules on data sources without Ruler enabled, or external rules where the user lacks `AlertingRuleExternalWrite`). When `rule` is `undefined`, all returned abilities should be `[NotSupported, false]`.

title: Silence drawer never opens for Grafana rules in the list view because `rule` (`rulerRule`) is `undefined`
body: In the updated list view (`GrafanaGroupLoader` and `FilterView`), `GrafanaRuleListItem` renders `<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} compact />` without passing a `rule` (`RulerRuleDTO`) prop. `AlertRuleMenu` computes `canSilence` from `promRule` via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` and renders the "Silence notifications" menu item, which sets `showSilenceDrawer(true)` on click. However, line 104 still guards `<SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer>` with `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, which is always `false` when `rule` is `undefined`, so clicking "Silence notifications" in the alert list view does nothing.

title: Delete and Pause menu items are still gated on `rulerRule`, preventing them from rendering in the alert list view
body: `AlertRuleMenu` now computes `canDelete` and `canPause` using `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(promRule, ...)` for the alert list view where `rulerRule` is no longer fetched. However, rendering the Delete item on line 165 still checks `{canDelete && rulerRule && ...}` and rendering the Pause item on line 123 still checks `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`. Because `GrafanaRuleListItem` only passes `promRule` (leaving `rulerRule` as `undefined`), neither Delete nor Pause is ever rendered for Grafana rules in the list view (even though `RuleActionsButtons.V2` already passes a `handleDelete` callback that only requires `identifier` and `groupIdentifier`). In addition, `canPause` being `true` while the Pause item is not rendered can cause `showDivider` on line 119 to render a leading `<Menu.Divider />` with no items above it.

title: Missing `key` prop on `GrafanaRuleListItem` when mapping filtered rules
body: When replacing `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ... />` with `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` inside `rules.map(...)`, the `key={key}` prop was removed. Rendering list items in an array without a `key` prop triggers React key warnings and can lead to incorrect component state reuse when the filtered list updates.

title: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` marks `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore`, and `DeletePermanently` as unsupported for Grafana recording rules
body: In `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule` is `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which is `true` for both Grafana alerting rules and Grafana recording rules. In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `isAlertingRule` is computed with `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` (which is `false` for `GrafanaPromRecordingRuleDTO`) and used as the support flag for `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore`, and `DeletePermanently` on lines 324-330. As a result, Grafana-managed recording rules will no longer support exporting or pausing when abilities are evaluated from `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`.

title: Refactoring `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` drops the federated rule group immutability check
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` previously checked `const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` so that rules in federated rule groups were treated as immutable (`Update` and `Delete` unsupported). It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false` on line 245, allowing edit and delete actions on federated rule groups for callers of `useAlertRuleAbility` and `useAlertRuleAbilities`.

title: Delete and Pause menu items never render when `rulerRule` is omitted
body: In the alert list view, `GrafanaRuleListItem` renders `RuleActionsButtons` with only `promRule` and leaves `rulerRule` undefined. Although `AlertRuleMenu` now computes `canDelete` and `canPause` using `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(promRule, ...)`, rendering of the Delete menu item on line 165 is still gated on `{canDelete && rulerRule && (` and rendering of `MenuItemPauseRule` on line 123 is still gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`. Because `rulerRule` is undefined, neither the Delete nor the Pause menu item can ever appear for Grafana rules in the list view (and if `canPause` is the only truthy item in the first section alongside `canExport`, `showDivider` on line 119 will also render a leading divider at the top of the menu).

title: Silence notifications action in the list view does not open the silence drawer
body: When `RuleActionsButtons` is rendered from `GrafanaRuleListItem`, only `promRule` is provided and `rule` (`RulerRuleDTO`) is `undefined`. `AlertRuleMenu` enables the "Silence notifications" menu item via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, and clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer` to `true`. However, line 104 still guards `<SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer>` with `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`. Because `rule` is `undefined`, `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` evaluates to `false`, so clicking "Silence notifications" in the rule list view does nothing.

title: `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(skipToken)` reports `Duplicate` as supported and allowed for non-Grafana rules
body: When `skipToken` is passed to `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` or `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (which `AlertRuleMenu` and `RuleActionsButtons` do for any non-Grafana / data source rule), `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)` is called. For `rule = undefined`, `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(undefined)` returns `loading: false`, so line 309 sets `MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported` (`true`) and line 313 sets `duplicateSupported = true`. Line 318 then computes `[AlertRuleAction.Duplicate]: toAbility(true, getRulesPermissions('grafana').create)`. Because `AlertRuleMenu` ORs `rulerDuplicateAbility` with `grafanaDuplicateAbility`, any user with permission to create Grafana rules (`AlertingRuleCreate`) will have `canDuplicate = true` on all data source rules—even if the data source has no Ruler API, the rule is plugin-provided, or the user lacks `AlertingRuleExternalWrite`. When `rule` is `undefined`, `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` should return `[NotSupported, false]` for all actions.

title: Grafana recording rules lose `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore`, and `DeletePermanently` abilities
body: In `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` (line 246), `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule` is computed with `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which is `true` for both Grafana alerting and recording rules. In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (line 302), `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is used instead and applied to `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore`, and `DeletePermanently` (lines 324-330). For a `GrafanaPromRecordingRuleDTO`, `isAlertingRule` is `false`, so Grafana-managed recording rules in the rule list view cannot be exported with modifications, paused, restored, or permanently deleted. Only `AlertRuleAction.Silence` should require `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, while the other actions should check `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`.

title: Missing `key` prop on `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` in `FilterViewResults`
body: When replacing `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ... />` with `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` inside `rules.map(...)`, the `key={key}` prop was dropped. This triggers React's missing `key` warning for every Grafana rule rendered in the filter view and prevents React from properly reconciling list items across updates.

title: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` no longer marks federated rule groups as immutable
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` previously checked `const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` so that `Update`, `Delete`, `Pause`, `Restore`, and `DeletePermanently` were marked `NotSupported` for federated rule groups. Refactoring `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` to delegate to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)` replaces that check with `const isFederated = false` (line 245), allowing edit/delete abilities to report as supported on federated rule groups.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new disconnected TestLogger, discarding all contextual logs
body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, which allocates a fresh `*TestLogger` instance that the caller has no reference to. In `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go` (line 58), `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` was updated to call `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. When `LoggerMiddleware` (or any other component) is tested with `TestLogger`, the `.Info(...)` call mutates the temporary `TestLogger` returned by `FromContext` and discards it, leaving `InfoLogs` on the original `TestLogger` empty (`Calls == 0`). Additionally, because `LoggerMiddleware` no longer appends `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName`, or `dsUID` directly and `TestLogger.FromContext` ignores `ctx`, existing `LoggerMiddleware` unit tests cannot observe those attributes or the log call itself.

title: ContextualLoggerMiddleware dereferences req without nil check and lacks unit tests
body: In `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`, `QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics` immediately access `req.PluginContext` without checking `if req == nil`. Other middlewares in this package (such as `LoggerMiddleware`, which runs immediately after `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`) explicitly guard against `req == nil` and pass the call through to `m.next`. A nil request will now panic in `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` before reaching `LoggerMiddleware`. Additionally, no unit tests were added for `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new TestLogger instance, discarding logged entries
body: TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger() instead of returning the receiver f (or recording logs back to f). Because LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), calling FromContext on a TestLogger allocates a temporary TestLogger whose InfoLogs are mutated and immediately discarded, leaving the caller's TestLogger.InfoLogs empty (Calls == 0) and breaking unit tests that assert on TestLogger output (including logger_middleware_test.go).

title: Missing nil-request guards in ContextualLoggerMiddleware and missing test coverage
body: ContextualLoggerMiddleware.QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, and CollectMetrics dereference req.PluginContext without checking if req == nil. Because ContextualLoggerMiddleware is registered immediately before LoggerMiddleware (which explicitly guards if req == nil in all four methods), a nil request will panic in ContextualLoggerMiddleware before reaching LoggerMiddleware. In addition, no unit tests were added for ContextualLoggerMiddleware and logger_middleware_test.go was not updated to reflect moving pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, and dsUID out of LoggerMiddleware.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new TestLogger instance, discarding logged entries
body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver `f` (or propagating recorded logs to `f`). In `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` (`pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go:58`), logging was changed from `m.logger.Info(...)` to `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. When a `*TestLogger` is passed to `NewLoggerMiddleware`, `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` returns a temporary `TestLogger` whose `InfoLogs` are immediately discarded, leaving `InfoLogs` on the caller's `TestLogger` instance empty (`Calls == 0`) and breaking tests that assert on `LoggerMiddleware` logs. In addition, `TestLogger.FromContext` ignores `ctx`, so contextual attributes added via `log.WithContextualAttributes` are lost.

title: LoggerMiddleware tests are not updated and ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no unit tests
body: `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` removed explicit `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `traceID`, `dsName`, and `dsUID` log parameters, relying instead on `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` to populate `ctx` and `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` to read them. However, `logger_middleware_test.go` was not updated to reflect that `LoggerMiddleware` alone no longer emits these fields, and no unit tests were added for `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (`contextual_logger_middleware.go`) to verify that `QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics` populate the context with the expected attributes.

title: ContextualLoggerMiddleware dereferences req without checking for nil
body: `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics` (lines 39-57) dereference `req.PluginContext` without checking `if req == nil`. `LoggerMiddleware` explicitly guards against `req == nil` on each of those methods (`logger_middleware.go` lines 63, 77, 90, and 104), but because `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` is registered ahead of `LoggerMiddleware` in `CreateMiddlewares` (`pluginsintegration.go:160-161`), passing a `nil` request will now panic in `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` before reaching `LoggerMiddleware`.

title: Rejected devices are cached in localCache before DB check, bypassing the device limit on subsequent requests
body: In `tagDeviceUI`, `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` is called on line 87 before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)` on line 93. When the device limit has been reached, the first request from a new device fails with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, but its device key is already stored in `localCache` for 29 minutes. On the very next request from that same device (including follow-up requests during the same page load), `a.localCache.Get(key)` on line 83 succeeds and `tagDeviceUI` returns `nil` without querying the store, allowing `Anonymous.Authenticate` to succeed and bypassing the device limit. `localCache.SetDefault` should only be called after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds (and `untagDevice` should also evict the key from `localCache` when deleting a device).

title: Provider signature changes in ProvideAnonymousDeviceService and ProvideAnonDBStore break Wire DI compilation
body: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` was changed from accepting `anonStore anonstore.AnonStore` to `sqlStore db.DB`, and `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` was changed to take `(sqlStore db.DB, deviceLimit int64)`. However, the Wire dependency injection files (`pkg/server/wire.go` and `pkg/server/wire_gen.go`, as well as any other wire sets referencing these providers) were not updated in this PR, which will cause `pkg/server` compilation and `wire` generation to fail.

title: updateDevice relies on RowsAffected() == 0, which falsely rejects existing devices on MySQL when values are unchanged
body: In `updateDevice`, `rowsAffected == 0` is used to infer that the device was not found in `anon_device`, returning `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. On MySQL (where `clientFoundRows` is disabled by default and `DATETIME` columns have 1-second precision), `UPDATE` reports 0 rows affected if a row matches the `WHERE` clause but `client_ip`, `user_agent`, and `updated_at` (within the same second) do not change. When an already-registered device makes concurrent requests within the same second (or across multiple Grafana replicas that do not share `localCache`), `RowsAffected()` will return 0 on MySQL and wrongly fail with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

title: GrafanaBootConfig.anonymousDeviceLimit is inferred as type undefined instead of number | undefined
body: In `GrafanaBootConfig`, `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` is declared without an explicit type annotation (unlike `loginError: string | undefined = undefined;` on line 85 or optional properties using `?:`). Because the exported `config` singleton in `@grafana/runtime` is typed as `GrafanaBootConfig`, TypeScript infers `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` as having type `undefined` rather than `number | undefined`, preventing callers from treating it as a `number`. Declare it as `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;` or `anonymousDeviceLimit?: number;`.

title: Rejected devices are cached in localCache before CreateOrUpdateDevice, bypassing the device limit on subsequent requests
body: In `tagDeviceUI`, `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` is called before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)`. When the device limit has been reached, the first request from a new device fails with `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached`, but its device key is still stored in `localCache` for 29 minutes. On the very next HTTP request from that same device, `a.localCache.Get(key)` returns a cache hit and `tagDeviceUI` returns `nil` without querying the store, allowing `Anonymous.Authenticate` to succeed and bypassing `AnonymousDeviceLimit`. `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` should only be called after `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)` succeeds (and `untagDevice` should also evict the key from `localCache` when a device is deleted on login).

title: Missing test coverage for updating an existing device when at the device limit
body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` verifies that a second distinct device is rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when `deviceLimit` is 1, but does not verify that calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice` again for the already-registered device (`"32mdo31deeqwes"`) succeeds via `updateDevice` once the limit has been reached.

title: tagDeviceUI caches the device before CreateOrUpdateDevice, bypassing the device limit on subsequent requests
body: In `AnonDeviceService.tagDeviceUI`, `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` is called on line 87 before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)` on line 93, and the cache key is not evicted when `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns an error. Because `Anonymous.Authenticate` now relies on `TagDevice` returning `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` to reject over-limit devices, a new device that exceeds the limit will fail on its first request, but its key will remain in `localCache` for the 29-minute TTL. Every subsequent request from that same device hits `a.localCache.Get(key)` on line 83 and returns `nil`, completely bypassing the device limit check. `a.localCache.SetDefault` should only be called after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds (and `untagDevice` should also evict the device key from `localCache`).

title: updateDevice relies on RowsAffected() which returns 0 on MySQL when values do not change within the same second
body: In `AnonDBStore.updateDevice`, when the device limit has been reached, an existing device is updated via `UPDATE anon_device SET client_ip = ?, user_agent = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?` and `rowsAffected == 0` is treated as `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. In MySQL, `updated_at` has second precision (`DATETIME`) and `RowsAffected()` reports the number of rows whose values actually changed rather than rows matched. If an already-registered device issues concurrent requests within the same second with the same IP and User-Agent (for example, parallel requests during initial page load before `localCache` is populated), MySQL returns `0` rows affected and `updateDevice` falsely rejects the valid device with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. Additionally, line 81 computes the `BETWEEN` window from `device.UpdatedAt` instead of `time.Now()` as used in `CountDevices` on line 110.

title: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit does not test that existing devices can still be updated at the limit
body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` verifies that inserting a second device (`"keep"`) fails with `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when `deviceLimit` is 1, but it does not verify the other half of the contract: that calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice` again for the already-registered device (`"32mdo31deeqwes"`) succeeds and updates its record when the limit has been reached.

title: Cleanup service ticker interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
body: In `CleanUpService.Run`, the ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This appears to be leftover debugging code and will cause all background cleanup jobs (annotations, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, temp files, user invites, short URLs, and query history) to run every minute instead of every 10 minutes, which also conflicts with the 9-minute job timeout in `clean()`.

title: Leftover Error-level debug logs in annotation cleanup loop spam error logs with ID slices
body: `CleanAnnotations` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 576, 579) call `r.log.Error` before and after every batch even when `err` is `nil` and when no rows are matched. Because these run on every cleanup cycle for each annotation type and for every batch, they will continuously emit false error logs in production and dump entire `ids` slices (up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` elements per batch) into the logs.

title: Quadratic string concatenation when building SQLite DELETE IN clause
body: In `deleteByIDs`, when running on SQLite with `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, the `IN` list is constructed with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` inside a loop over `ids`. This performs O(N^2) allocations and memory copies; for a batch of 32,767 IDs (as in the integration test), this allocates and copies several gigabytes of strings per batch. Use `strings.Builder` or `strconv.AppendInt` (as in `getAccessControlFilter` on line 387) to build the clause in O(N) time.

title: Cleanup service ticker interval unintentionally reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
body: In `CleanUpService.Run`, the ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This appears to be leftover debugging code: it causes all background cleanup jobs (annotations, snapshots, dashboard versions, expired images, user invites, short URLs, and query history) to run 10x more frequently than intended and conflicts with the 9-minute timeout configured in `clean()`.

title: Leftover debug statements log at Error level and dump all batch IDs on every iteration
body: `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` call `r.log.Error` twice per batch iteration (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579) even when operations succeed and `err` is `nil`. Additionally, lines 534, 554, and 576 serialize the full `ids` slice into the error log on every batch, flooding production error logs during normal cleanup runs.

title: Quadratic string concatenation when constructing SQLite IN clause for large batches
body: In `deleteByIDs`, when on SQLite with `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, the comma-separated ID list is constructed in a loop using `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)`. Because this only runs for batch sizes above 999, the repeated string copying is O(N^2) in both CPU and memory (for a batch of 32,767 IDs as in the test, a single batch allocates multiple gigabytes of temporary strings). A `strings.Builder` or `strconv.AppendInt` buffer should be used instead.

title: Cleanup service ticker interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
body: `CleanUpService.Run` changes the cleanup ticker from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This appears to be a leftover local testing change and causes all background cleanup jobs (annotations, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, user invites, short URLs, and query history) to run 10x more frequently than intended, while `clean()` still assumes a 10-minute period with `const timeout = 9 * time.Minute`.

title: Leftover debug logging at Error level dumps ID slices on every cleanup batch
body: `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579) call `r.log.Error` twice per batch even when no error occurred (on lines 534, 554, and 576 `err` is always `nil`) and even when `len(ids) == 0`. In addition, logging `"ids", ids` serializes the entire batch of annotation IDs into the error logs on every batch iteration, which will heavily spam production error logs.

title: Quadratic string concatenation when building SQLite DELETE IN clause
body: In `deleteByIDs`, when running on SQLite with a batch size above 999, `values` is built in a loop with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)`. This performs O(n^2) string copies and allocations over `len(ids)` (for example, with the tested batch size of 32,767, a single batch allocates hundreds of megabytes of intermediate strings). Additionally, the condition checks `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit` instead of `len(ids) > sqliteParameterLimit`, so even small batches inline the IDs when a large batch size is configured. Use `strings.Builder` or `strconv.AppendInt` (as done in `getAccessControlFilter` in this file) and check `len(ids) > sqliteParameterLimit`.

title: Async legacy writes derive context from the request context and get canceled when the request finishes
body: In `Create` (line 51), `Delete` (line 110), `Update` (line 135), and `DeleteCollection` (line 163), the background goroutines create their timeout context via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, ...)` directly from the incoming request `ctx`. Because these methods return immediately after `d.Storage` completes, the HTTP request handler will finish and cancel the request `ctx`, which immediately cancels the derived context in the goroutine and aborts in-flight `d.Legacy` writes with `context.Canceled`. Detach cancellation first with `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` before applying `context.WithTimeoutCause`.

title: Wrong duration metrics and high-cardinality `kind` label recorded in `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection`
body:
Several metric calls in `DualWriterMode3` record to the wrong metric or pass the wrong label value:
- In `Create` (line 45) and `Update` (line 129), when `d.Storage.Create` or `d.Storage.Update` returns an error, `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration(...)`.
- In `DeleteCollection` (line 166), the async goroutine for `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` calls `d.recordStorageDuration(...)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)`.
- In `Delete` (line 106), `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the object `name` instead of `options.Kind`, corrupting the `kind` label and introducing unbounded label cardinality in Prometheus.

title: `Delete` passes `d.Log` instead of enriched `log` to context and async legacy errors are not logged
body: In `Delete`, line 96 constructs `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)`, but line 97 calls `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`, discarding the added fields. In addition, errors returned by `d.Legacy.Create` (line 55), `d.Legacy.Delete` (line 112), `d.Legacy.Update` (line 139), and `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` (line 165) in the background goroutines are no longer logged, so legacy write failures will fail silently.

title: Mode 3 write tests share a single `mock.Mock` across goroutines and never verify async legacy writes
body:
In `TestMode3_Create`, `TestMode3_Delete`, `TestMode3_DeleteCollection`, and `TestMode3_Update`, `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` wrap the same `m := &mock.Mock{}` instance and the tests return without waiting for the background `Legacy` goroutine:
- The background goroutine calls `m.Called(...)` concurrently with the test goroutine finishing or starting the next subtest, which is a data race on `mock.Mock` state and the shared Prometheus registry `p`.
- In `TestMode3_Create` (lines 40-42), the test case `"error when creating object in the unified store fails"` configures `setupLegacyFn` instead of `setupStorageFn`, which only passes because `ls` and `us` share `m`.
- None of the tests assert that the asynchronous `Legacy` methods were actually called (`TestMode3_Delete` and `TestMode3_DeleteCollection` do not set up legacy expectations at all).

title: Storage and legacy duration metrics are recorded to the wrong collectors
body:
Several methods in `DualWriterMode3` call the wrong metric recorder:
- In `Create` (line 45), when `d.Storage.Create` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
- In `Update` (line 129), when `d.Storage.Update` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
- In `DeleteCollection` (line 166), after `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` finishes in the background goroutine, `d.recordStorageDuration` is called instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`.

This skews latency and error metrics between unified storage and legacy storage.

title: Delete passes object name instead of options.Kind to recordStorageDuration
body: On line 106 in `Delete`, `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the resource `name` as the `kind` argument instead of `options.Kind`. This records each individual object name in the `kind` metric label, producing incorrect labels and unbounded metric cardinality.

title: Async legacy writes derive context from the request context and get canceled when the request returns
body: In `Create` (line 51), `Delete` (line 110), `Update` (line 135), and `DeleteCollection` (line 163), the background goroutine creates its timeout context with `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, ...)` directly from the request `ctx`, and the outer function immediately returns. When the HTTP handler finishes serving the request, the server cancels the request `ctx`, which immediately cancels the derived context in the background goroutine and aborts in-flight legacy storage writes. The goroutines should detach from parent cancellation (e.g., `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`) before applying the timeout.

title: Delete stores d.Log instead of the enriched logger in context
body: In `Delete`, line 96 creates `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)`, but line 97 calls `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`. Any downstream code extracting the logger from `ctx` loses the `name`, `kind`, and `method` log fields.

title: Mode 3 unit tests share a single mock between Legacy and Storage and do not await async legacy writes
body: In `dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, `ls := legacyStoreMock{m, l}` and `us := storageMock{m, s}` wrap the same `m := &mock.Mock{}` instance, and the write tests (`Create`, `Delete`, `DeleteCollection`, `Update`) return without waiting for or asserting on the background goroutine that writes to `Legacy`. As a result, `TestMode3_Create`'s error case (line 40) configures `setupLegacyFn` to test a unified storage failure and only passes because both mocks share `m`, while `TestMode3_Delete` and `TestMode3_DeleteCollection` do not verify whether `Legacy` is called at all.

title: Swapped storage and legacy duration metrics in Create, Update, and DeleteCollection
body:
Several metric recording calls in `DualWriterMode3` record against the wrong storage backend metric:
- Line 45 (`Create`): When `d.Storage.Create` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`.
- Line 129 (`Update`): When `d.Storage.Update` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`.
- Line 166 (`DeleteCollection`): Inside the async legacy goroutine, `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` is called for `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...)`.

This skews latency and error metrics by attributing unified storage errors to legacy storage and legacy collection-delete latencies/errors to unified storage.

title: Async legacy writes derive from the request context and will be canceled when the handler returns
body: In `Create` (line 51), `Delete` (line 110), `Update` (line 135), and `DeleteCollection` (line 163), the background goroutines derive their timeout context directly from the incoming request context via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, ...)`. Because the outer method returns immediately after spawning the goroutine, the HTTP server finishes the request and cancels `ctx`, which immediately cancels the child context in the background goroutine and causes the asynchronous `d.Legacy` writes to fail with `context.Canceled`. The background context should detach from parent cancellation first (e.g., `context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 10*time.Second, ...)`).

title: Data race on input object and UpdatedObjectInfo between synchronous response and async legacy write
body:
In `Create` (line 55) and `Update` (line 139), the input `obj` and `objInfo` are passed directly into the background goroutine calling `d.Legacy.Create` and `d.Legacy.Update` while the main goroutine returns `created`/`res` to the apiserver handler for serialization:
- In `Create`, `d.Storage.Create` and `d.Legacy.Create` (via strategy `PrepareForCreate`/validation) can mutate `obj` in place concurrently with the caller serializing `created`.
- In `Update`, `rest.UpdatedObjectInfo` (such as `rest.DefaultUpdatedObjectInfo`) holds a single decoded `runtime.Object` that is mutated in place when `UpdatedObject` is called. Calling `d.Legacy.Update` concurrently with the same `objInfo` re-runs `UpdatedObject` and mutates the same object while the HTTP response is being serialized.

A deep copy of the object created/updated by `d.Storage` should be passed to the background goroutine instead.

title: Delete attaches unenriched logger to context instead of `log`
body: In `Delete`, line 96 constructs `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)`, but line 97 calls `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`. Any downstream code retrieving the logger from `ctx` will miss the `name`, `kind`, and `method` fields.

title: Delete passes object `name` instead of `options.Kind` as the `kind` metric label
body: On line 106 in `Delete`, `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the individual object's `name` instead of `options.Kind` as the `kind` label parameter. In addition to recording an incorrect `kind` label on successful deletes, `name` is an unbounded per-resource identifier and will cause high-cardinality metric explosion in Prometheus.

title: Mode 3 unit tests share a single mock between stores and do not synchronize with async legacy calls
body:
In `dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, `ls` and `us` are initialized with the same `m := &mock.Mock{}` instance, and the tests do not synchronize with the background goroutines spawned by `Create`, `Delete`, `DeleteCollection`, and `Update`:
- Because `ls` and `us` share `m`, expectations set on `m` match calls to either store. For example, in `TestMode3_Create` (line 40, "error when creating object in the unified store fails"), the test configures `setupLegacyFn` instead of `setupStorageFn` and only passes because both stores use `m`.
- None of the write tests wait for the background `d.Legacy` goroutine to complete or assert that `d.Legacy` was invoked, causing the background goroutine to race with test completion while recording metrics on the shared package-level Prometheus registry `p`.

title: Missing cache re-check after acquiring write lock
body: `GetWebAssets` checks `entryPointAssetsCache` under `RLock()`, releases the read lock, and then acquires `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`, but does not re-check whether another goroutine populated `entryPointAssetsCache` while waiting for the write lock. When multiple concurrent requests arrive before the cache is initialized (and `cfg.Env != setting.Dev`), every waiting goroutine will redundantly open and parse `assets-manifest.json` under the exclusive lock instead of returning the newly cached result.

title: Data race on shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` variables in `searchSupport.init`
body: Now that `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` no longer serializes the entire build under `b.cacheMu.Lock()`, the `group.Go` worker goroutines in `searchSupport.init` run `s.build` concurrently. Inside the closure, `totalBatchesIndexed++` (line 189) and `_, _, err = s.build(...)` (line 190) mutate variables declared in the outer `init` scope without synchronization, while the main goroutine also writes `err = group.Wait()` at line 195. In addition to triggering the race detector when `s.initWorkers > 1`, a non-nil error returned by `s.build` in one worker can be overwritten with `nil` by another worker before `return err` executes on line 191, silently swallowing index build failures during startup. Use a local `_, _, err := s.build(...)` inside the closure and an `atomic.Int64` (or `len(stats)`) for `totalBatchesIndexed`.

title: Unsynchronized map iteration in `bleveBackend.TotalDocs` races with `BuildIndex`
body: `TotalDocs()` iterates over `b.cache` without acquiring `b.cacheMu.RLock()`. In `searchSupport.init` (line 216 of `pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go`), `s.search.TotalDocs()` is called immediately after starting the background `WatchWriteEvents` goroutine (line 207), which can invoke `handleEvent` -> `getOrCreateIndex` -> `BuildIndex` and write to `b.cache[key]` under `b.cacheMu.Lock()`. Any concurrent call to `TotalDocs()` while an index is being added to `b.cache` will crash the process with a concurrent map iteration and map write panic.

title: Concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for the same key can fail on disk or overwrite cached indexes
body: Removing the lock around `BuildIndex` without per-key synchronization in `getOrCreateIndex` or `BuildIndex` means two concurrent callers for the same unindexed `NamespacedResource` (for example, concurrent `Search` requests or a `Search` racing with `handleEvent` for a resource with count <= `initMinSize`) will both see `GetIndex == nil` and run `BuildIndex` in parallel. When `size > b.opts.FileThreshold`, the second concurrent `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` call on the same directory path will fail; when using an in-memory index, the second build to finish unconditionally overwrites `b.cache[key] = idx`, discarding any updates written to the first cached index (such as from `handleEvent`) and double-counting the `IndexTenants` and `IndexedKinds` metrics.

title: Postgres test failure in Drone is caused by hardcoded `localhost` in `addStorageServerToConfig`
body: Previously, `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` passed on Postgres in Drone only because `ResourceServer.Init` was called lazily on the first gRPC request, so the test never connected to the `resource_api` database. Now that `NewResourceServer` calls `s.Init(ctx)` at startup, `InitializeModuleServer` connects to the database immediately, which fails in Drone because `addStorageServerToConfig` (lines 75-80) hardcodes `db_host` to `localhost` for Postgres whereas Drone runs Postgres in a separate container. Reading the Postgres host and credentials from the `[database]` section of `cfg` (populated by `db.InitTestDBWithCfg(t)`, just as the MySQL branch does on lines 82-90) will allow this test to run on Postgres instead of skipping it.

title: `ListIterator`, `WriteEvent`, and `ReadResource` still discard the span context
body: While `GetResourceStats` (line 126) and `searchSupport.build` were updated to capture `ctx, span := ...` for trace propagation, `ListIterator` (line 388, which is called by `searchSupport.build` to populate each index), `WriteEvent` (line 158), and `ReadResource` (line 353) still use `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)`. As a result, downstream operations inside those methods (such as `fetchLatestRV`, database queries, `cb(iter)` document building, and `create`/`update`/`delete` spans) will not be parented under their respective `sql.resource.*` spans.

title: Data races on shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` variables across index build workers
body: With `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` no longer holding `cacheMu.Lock()` across the entire build, the `group.Go` workers in `searchSupport.init` now run concurrently. Inside the `group.Go` closure (lines 187-192), `totalBatchesIndexed++` and `_, _, err = s.build(...)` both mutate variables declared in the outer `init` scope without synchronization, while the main goroutine also writes `err = group.Wait()` at line 195. Aside from triggering the race detector when multiple namespaces are indexed with `initWorkers > 1`, a concurrent write of `err = nil` by one finishing worker can overwrite a non-nil `err` in another worker before `return err` is evaluated, causing index build failures to be silently ignored. `err` should be shadowed as a local variable inside the closure (`_, _, err := s.build(...)`) and `totalBatchesIndexed` should use `atomic.Int64` (or `len(stats)`).

title: `TotalDocs()` iterates over `b.cache` without holding `b.cacheMu.RLock()`
body: `bleveBackend.TotalDocs()` ranges over `b.cache` without acquiring `b.cacheMu.RLock()`. In `searchSupport.init` (line 216 of `pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go`), `s.search.TotalDocs()` is now called after the background `WatchWriteEvents` goroutine has been started (lines 207-213). If a watch event (or concurrent search request) triggers `getOrCreateIndex` -> `BuildIndex` and writes `b.cache[key] = idx` while `TotalDocs()` is iterating over `b.cache`, the process will crash with a fatal `concurrent map iteration and map write` runtime error.

title: Narrowing `cacheMu` lock allows concurrent duplicate builds for the same `NamespacedResource`
body: Moving `b.cacheMu.Lock()` from the start of `BuildIndex` to line 137 means two concurrent callers of `getOrCreateIndex` (e.g. a `Search` request and `handleEvent` for a namespace not pre-indexed at startup) can both see `GetIndex == nil` and execute `BuildIndex` for the same `key` simultaneously. If `size > b.opts.FileThreshold`, both goroutines will call `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same directory path, causing the second to fail with an existing-path/lock error. For in-memory indexes, the second build will overwrite `b.cache[key] = idx` at line 138 without checking whether an index was already stored, leaking the first index and dropping any documents written to it in the meantime.

title: Removing `s.Init(ctx)` checks from RPC handlers makes `Stop()` state changes ineffective
body: `server.Stop` sets `s.initErr` to `"service is stopping"` and `"service is stopped"` (lines 321, 328, 339). Previously, every gRPC handler called `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil`, which returned `s.initErr` after `s.once.Do` had completed, rejecting requests once `Stop` was called. Because all `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from the RPC methods (`Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `Read`, `List`, `Watch`, `Search`, `History`, `Origin`, `IsHealthy`, `PutBlob`, `GetBlob`), `s.initErr` is never checked after `NewResourceServer` returns, and requests arriving during or after `Stop` will continue executing against the stopped backend.

title: Postgres integration test fails in Drone because `addStorageServerToConfig` hardcodes `localhost`
body: `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` started failing on Postgres in Drone because `NewResourceServer` now connects to the `resource_api` database eagerly at startup (`s.Init`), whereas previously the test never triggered lazy initialization. In `addStorageServerToConfig` (lines 75-80), the `postgres` branch hardcodes `db_host` to `"localhost"`, while in Drone CI Postgres runs on a separate container hostname configured in the `[database]` section (just as the `mysql` branch on lines 81-90 parses the host from `[database]`). Reading the Postgres connection parameters from the `[database]` section allows the test to run in Drone instead of skipping Postgres coverage.

title: Data race on `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` in `searchSupport.init` worker goroutines
body: In `searchSupport.init`, each `group.Go` closure increments `totalBatchesIndexed++` and assigns to the outer `err` variable (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) before returning `err`, while the parent goroutine also assigns `err = group.Wait()`. Previously, `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` held `b.cacheMu.Lock()` for its entire execution, largely serializing these workers. With the lock narrowed to the final cache assignment, `s.build` now executes concurrently across `s.initWorkers` goroutines, causing data races on both `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` (and allowing a `nil` result from one worker to overwrite a non-nil `err` in another worker before `return err` is evaluated). Use a local ` _, _, err := s.build(...)` inside the closure and an `atomic.Int64` (or `len(stats)`) for `totalBatchesIndexed`.

title: Unsynchronized `b.cache` read in `TotalDocs` and unguarded concurrent `BuildIndex` for the same key
body:
Narrowing `b.cacheMu.Lock()` in `BuildIndex` to only guard `b.cache[key] = idx` introduces two concurrency issues:
1. `TotalDocs()` (lines 144-154, now called in `search.go:216` after the `WatchWriteEvents` goroutine has already started) iterates over `b.cache` without acquiring `b.cacheMu.RLock()`. If a watch event or search request triggers `BuildIndex` concurrently, Go will panic with a concurrent map iteration and map write error.
2. When `getOrCreateIndex` encounters a cache miss concurrently for the same `NamespacedResource` (e.g. from concurrent `Search` calls or `handleEvent`), multiple goroutines will now run `BuildIndex` for the same `key` simultaneously. For file-backed indexes (`size > b.opts.FileThreshold`), the second `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` call on the same path will fail; for in-memory indexes, the second build will overwrite `b.cache[key]` and drop any writes applied to the first instance.

title: Postgres integration test fails in Drone due to hardcoded `localhost` in `addStorageServerToConfig`
body: `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` only started failing on Postgres with this PR because `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` at startup, whereas previously the test never made any gRPC calls and therefore never connected to the `resource_api` database. In `addStorageServerToConfig` (lines 75-80), the `postgres` branch hardcodes `db_host` to `"localhost"` instead of reading the host and credentials from `cfg.Raw.GetSection("database")` like the MySQL branch does, which fails in Drone where Postgres runs in a separate service container. Parsing the Postgres connection config instead of skipping the test preserves integration test coverage for Postgres startup.

title: Context leak on `NewResourceServer` init failure and unread `s.initErr` after `Stop`
body: In `NewResourceServer`, `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(...)` is created on line 229, but if `s.Init(ctx)` fails on line 258, `cancel()` is not called before returning the error, leaking the context and any background goroutines started prior to the failure (such as the watcher goroutine if `s.initWatcher()` fails after `s.search.init(ctx)`). Additionally, removing `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil` from all RPC handlers means the `s.initErr` assignments in `Stop()` (`"service is stopping"` / `"service is stopped"`) are never checked, so RPC methods will no longer reject requests once `Stop()` has been called.

title: Call to non-existent no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` fails to compile
body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the superclass `UsernamePasswordForm` only defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (line 160). Because no zero-argument overload exists in `UsernameForm` or its supertypes, this file will not compile.

title: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` requires `user != null`, breaking passkey login when user is not yet identified
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. On initial login (and in `challenge(...)` when `context.getUser()` is `null`), `context.getUser()` is `null`, so `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` evaluates to `false` at lines 115 and 137. As a result, `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never called during normal unauthenticated login challenges, preventing the WebAuthn conditional UI attributes and form from being rendered on the initial login page.

title: Compilation failure: call to non-existent no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`
body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the superclass `UsernamePasswordForm` only defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. No zero-argument overload exists in the class hierarchy, so `UsernameForm` fails to compile. Pass `context.getUser()` (i.e. `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`) or match the method signature in `UsernamePasswordForm`.

title: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` returns `false` when `user` is `null`, breaking passkey login on initial authentication
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. During a normal initial login (before a user has been identified) or after a failed login where the user is cleared from the context, `context.getUser()` is `null`. Because of the `&& user != null` check, `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` evaluates to `false` in both `authenticate()` (line 115) and `challenge()` (line 137), so `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never called and passkey/conditional UI authentication is never initialized on the login page. When `user` is `null`, conditional passkeys must still be enabled if passkeys are enabled for the realm (e.g. `user == null || webauthnAuth.configuredFor(session, session.getContext().getRealm(), user)`).

title: Compilation error: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` called without required `UserModel` argument
body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the superclass `UsernamePasswordForm` only defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. This causes compilation to fail; `context.getUser()` needs to be passed (or an overload provided).

title: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` returns `false` when `user` is `null`, breaking initial passkey login
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. During normal initial login (before a user is identified in the authentication context) and on error challenges where the user is cleared, `context.getUser()` is `null`, so `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` evaluates to `false` and `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never called. As a result, WebAuthn conditional UI attributes and challenges are not added to the login form on initial login. Conversely, when `user != null` (such as during re-authentication), it does not check whether the user actually has a passkey credential configured (e.g., `user == null || user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthnAuth.getCredentialType())`), so passkey UI will be enabled and `UsernameForm` will not be skipped even for users without passkeys.

title: Login cache invalidation on update fails when an organization is disabled or when a cached IDP is mutated in-place
body: In `update(IdentityProviderModel model)`, `idpById = getById(model.getInternalId())` returns a model wrapped by `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`, where `isEnabled()` returns `false` whenever the linked organization is disabled, even if the IDP itself is enabled in storage. Meanwhile, `getForLogin` populates its cache from `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)`, which includes enabled IDPs belonging to disabled organizations. Because `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` checks `IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled`, when an organization is disabled `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` is always `false`. If an IDP in that disabled organization (whose `internalId` is cached in `getForLogin`) is updated to be unavailable for login (e.g., `hideOnLogin = true`, `linkOnly = true`, or `BROKER_PUBLIC = false`), `getLoginPredicate().test(updated)` is also `false`, so `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` returns early without invalidating `cacheKeyForLogin`; once the organization is re-enabled, the hidden/link-only/private IDP will still be returned by `getForLogin`. Conversely, if `updated` was also obtained via `getById`/`getByAlias` (so it is also wrapped) and updated to become login-eligible while the organization is disabled, both predicates evaluate to `false` and the cache is again not invalidated. Furthermore, when `Profile.Feature.ORGANIZATION` is disabled, `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` returns the cached `IdentityProviderModel` reference without copying it, so mutating a model from `getById` in-place and passing it to `update(model)` causes `original` and `updated` to be the same instance and skips invalidation.

title: `remove(String alias)` leaves stale `internalId` entries in cache when IDP was only cached via `getById`
body: In `remove(String alias)`, `getForLogin` (line 246) and `getByOrganization` (line 202) populate the cache by calling `session.identityProviders().getById(id)`, which caches `CachedIdentityProvider` under `internalId` without populating `cacheKeyIdpAlias(realm, alias)`. When `remove(alias)` is later called for such an IDP, `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is `false` and `realmCache.getCache().get(cacheKey, CachedIdentityProvider.class)` returns `null`, so `registerIDPInvalidation` is never called despite `storedIdp` already having been loaded on line 100. As a result, the `internalId` cache entry remains in `realmCache`, causing subsequent `getById` and `getByOrganization` calls to return the deleted IDP. Additionally, if `remove(alias)` is called with a non-existent alias while `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is `true`, `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` on line 103 will throw a `NullPointerException` because `storedIdp` is `null`.

title: `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` returns disabled IDPs when their organization is disabled
body: The contract of `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` specifies that only enabled identity providers suitable for login are returned. `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` wraps returned models with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` (which makes `idp.isEnabled()` return `false` when the linked organization is disabled), but does not filter the resulting stream by `IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled`. Instead, the `idp.isEnabled()` filter was added only in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`, leaving `getForLogin` itself returning disabled IDPs to any other caller.

title: Test cleanup in `testCacheIDPForLogin` uses literal `"alias"` instead of the created IDP alias
body: Lines 381 and 425 register cleanup callbacks using `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` with the hardcoded string `"alias"` instead of `idpRep.getAlias()` (`"idp-alias-" + i` and `"idp-alias-20"`). Because no IDP with alias `"alias"` exists, the cleanup calls fail with HTTP 404 (ignored by `TestCleanup`) and the realm-level IDPs created by `testCacheIDPForLogin` are never removed from the test realm.

title: Login IDP cache is not invalidated when updating an IDP linked to a disabled organization
body: In `update(IdentityProviderModel model)`, `idpById` is fetched via `getById(model.getInternalId())`, which wraps the model using `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. That wrapper overrides `isEnabled()` to return `false` whenever the linked organization (or `OrganizationProvider`) is disabled; `model` is likewise wrapped if the caller obtained it from `session.identityProviders()`. However, the login cache in `getForLogin` is populated from `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)` (which only checks the IDP's own `enabled` state in the database), and enabling or disabling an organization does not invalidate `cacheKeyForLogin`. As a result, if an organization is disabled while one of its login IDPs is updated to no longer qualify for login (e.g., setting `hideOnLogin` to `true`, `linkOnly` to `true`, or `BROKER_PUBLIC` to `false`)—or if a wrapped model is updated to become login-eligible—`getLoginPredicate().test(original)` and `getLoginPredicate().test(updated)` both return `false` because `isEnabled()` returns `false` on the wrapper. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` then returns early without invalidating the login caches. When the organization is re-enabled, `getForLogin` will continue serving the stale login IDP set (and since `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` only re-checks `idp.isEnabled()`, hidden, link-only, or non-public IDPs will still be shown on the login page).

title: Test cleanup references literal "alias" instead of the created IDP alias, leaking realm IDPs
body: In `testCacheIDPForLogin` (lines 381 and 425), cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` using the literal string `"alias"` instead of `idpRep.getAlias()`. Because no IDP named `"alias"` exists, each cleanup call throws `NotFoundException` (which `TestCleanup` ignores), and the realm-level IDPs created by the test (`idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-9`, which are not deleted when the test organizations are removed) are leaked into the test realm for subsequent tests.

title: Login IDP cache is not invalidated when updating an IDP belonging to a disabled organization
body:
In `update(IdentityProviderModel model)`, `idpById` is loaded via `getById(model.getInternalId())`, which wraps the model with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. For an IDP linked to an organization, the wrapper overrides `isEnabled()` to return `org != null && provider.isEnabled() && org.isEnabled() && super.isEnabled()`. However, `getForLogin` populates `IdentityProviderListQuery` from `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)`, which only checks the IDP's own `enabled` column in the database and ignores whether the organization is currently enabled.

If an organization is disabled (`org.isEnabled() == false`) after the login cache was populated, `getLoginPredicate().test(idpById)` evaluates to `false` even though the IDP's `internalId` is cached in `IdentityProviderListQuery`.
