If the IDP is then updated while the organization is disabled so that it should no longer be available for login (e.g., setting `hideOnLogin = true`, `linkOnly = true`, `BROKER_PUBLIC = "false"`, or `enabled = false`), `getLoginPredicate().test(updated)` also evaluates to `false`. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` hits `if (!getLoginPredicate().test(original) && !getLoginPredicate().test(updated)) return;` and skips invalidating `cacheKeyForLogin`. When the organization is subsequently re-enabled, the stale `IdentityProviderListQuery` remains in cache and continues to serve the hidden, link-only, or non-public IDP on the login page. The same issue occurs in reverse when a disabled/hidden org IDP is updated to qualify for login via a wrapped `IdentityProviderModel` while its organization is disabled.

title: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove skips ID invalidation on alias cache miss and can throw NPE
body:
In `remove(String alias)`, `storedIdp` is now unconditionally fetched via `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` at line 100, but lines 101-109 still branch on `isInvalid(cacheKey)` and whether `cacheKeyIdpAlias` is present in `realmCache`:

1. If an IDP was cached by `internalId` (for example via `getForLogin`, `getByOrganization`, or `getById`) without `getByAlias(alias)` having been called, `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is `false` and `cached` is `null`. `registerIDPInvalidation` is never called even though `storedIdp` was just loaded, leaving `storedIdp.getInternalId()` (and any `IdentityProviderListQuery` entries keyed by `cacheKeyOrgId` that depend on `internalId` invalidation) stale in the cache.
2. If `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is `true` and `remove` is called for an alias that no longer exists (`storedIdp == null`), `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` throws a `NullPointerException` when dereferencing `idp.getInternalId()`.
3. When `cached` is present and valid in `realmCache`, `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is still executed unnecessarily instead of reusing `cached.getIdentityProvider()`.

title: getForLogin returns disabled identity providers when their organization is disabled
body: `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` specifies that returned identity providers must be enabled, not link-only, and not hidden on login. In `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` (lines 218, 249, and 254), each returned `IdentityProviderModel` is wrapped with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`, whose `isEnabled()` returns `false` when its linked organization (or `OrganizationProvider`) is disabled. However, `getForLogin` does not filter the returned stream by `IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled`. While `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` was updated in this PR to work around this by re-checking `idp.isEnabled()`, any other caller of `getForLogin` will receive disabled identity providers when an organization is disabled.

title: Test cleanup in testCacheIDPForLogin uses literal "alias" instead of the created IDP alias
body: At lines 381 and 425 of `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`, cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` using the literal string `"alias"` instead of `idpRep.getAlias()`. Consequently, cleanup attempts to delete a non-existent IDP named `"alias"` and leaves the realm-level identity providers created by the test (`idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-9`) in the test realm after the test finishes.

title: ES384 and ES512 tests use a 256-bit EC key and never test >127-byte DER lengths or JCA verification
body: `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` generates a default 256-bit (`secp256r1`) key pair that is reused across `testES256`, `testES384`, and `testES512`. Because the ECDSA signature integers `r` and `s` are bounded by the curve order of the key (32 bytes for P-256) regardless of the hash algorithm, `BigInteger` strips the leading zero padding added in `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` and encodes 32-byte integers in all three tests. Consequently, `testES384` and `testES512` never test 48-byte (`secp384r1`) or 66-byte (`secp521r1`) signature integers, and `testES512` never exercises the multi-byte DER length encoding/decoding path (`length > 127` in `ASN1Encoder.writeLength` and `ASN1Decoder.readLength`, since a real P-521 DER signature sequence is ~136 bytes). In addition, the test only checks that `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` can decode its own output (`Assert.assertArrayEquals(rsConcat, rsConcat2)`), without verifying `asn1Des` against `Signature.verify(asn1Des)` or `sign`.

title: Indefinite length (0x80) and sequence length mismatches are not handled safely in ASN1Decoder
body: `readLength()` returns `-1` when the length byte is `0x80` (BER indefinite-length encoding, which is not valid DER), but none of its callers check for `-1`. In `readInteger()`, passing `length = -1` to `read(length)` throws an unchecked `NegativeArraySizeException` instead of `IOException`. In `readNext()`, `length += reset()` adds the header byte count (typically 2) to `-1`, resulting in `read(1)` which desynchronizes the stream position in `readSequence()`. Furthermore, in `readSequence()`, the loop `while (length > 0)` subtracts `bytes.length` without checking that `length == 0` when finished, so an inner element whose length exceeds the sequence length causes `length` to go negative and silently terminates the loop.

title: Redundant ASN1Encoder allocations and writes in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` and discard the resulting `ASN1Encoder` instances before performing the exact same calls on lines 119-120 inside `writeDerSeq(...)`.

title: ES384 and ES512 tests use a 256-bit EC key and do not verify the re-encoded DER signature
body: `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` generates a single default `EC` key pair (256-bit `secp256r1`) in the constructor and reuses it for `ES256`, `ES384`, and `ES512`. Because ECDSA signature components `r` and `s` are bounded by the key's curve order rather than the hash size, signing with a 256-bit key always produces ~32-byte `r` and `s` values (~70-byte DER signatures) even when using `SHA384withECDSA` and `SHA512withECDSA`. As a result, `testES512` never produces a DER sequence longer than 127 bytes, leaving the multi-byte DER length encoding and decoding paths (`length > 127` in `ASN1Encoder.writeLength` and `ASN1Decoder.readLength`) untested. In addition, `test()` only asserts that `asn1Des` decodes back to `rsConcat2` without verifying `asn1Des` against `Signature.verify(asn1Des)` (or `Assert.assertArrayEquals(sign, asn1Des)`), so a broken DER encoding that round-trips through `ASN1Decoder` would not be caught. Each algorithm should be tested with its matching curve (`secp256r1`, `secp384r1`, `secp521r1`) and the re-encoded DER signature should be verified with `Signature.verify`.

title: Unused ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: In `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` and discard the returned encoders before performing the exact same encoding again inside `writeDerSeq(...)` on lines 119-120. Lines 114-115 are dead code that perform unnecessary allocations and encoding on every signature conversion.

title: ECDSAAlgorithmTest uses a 256-bit key for ES384/ES512 and never verifies the DER signature
body: `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` initializes a single default `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")` key pair (256-bit `secp256r1`) and reuses it across `testES256`, `testES384`, and `testES512`. Because ECDSA `r` and `s` values are bounded by the curve order, signing with a 256-bit key always produces `r` and `s` of at most 32 bytes (~70-byte DER signature) even with `SHA384withECDSA` and `SHA512withECDSA`. As a result, `testES384` and `testES512` never test 48-byte (`secp384r1`) or 66-byte (`secp521r1`) components, and never exercise the multi-byte ASN.1 length encoding/decoding (`length > 127`) in `ASN1Encoder.writeLength` and `ASN1Decoder.readLength` that real ES512 signatures (~138 bytes) require. Additionally, `test()` only checks the round-trip back to `rsConcat2` with its own decoder and never checks `signature.verify(asn1Des)` with the JCA `Signature` verifier.

title: Indefinite length (0x80) returns -1 in readLength() and causes NegativeArraySizeException or stream corruption
body: `readLength()` returns `-1` when it encounters `0x80` (indefinite-length encoding), but none of its callers handle `-1`. In `readInteger()`, `length = -1` is passed directly to `read(length)`, throwing an unchecked `NegativeArraySizeException` at `new byte[length]` instead of an `IOException`. In `readNext()`, `length += reset()` adds the header byte count to `-1`, reading a truncated byte array and corrupting subsequent reads in `readSequence()`. Because DER forbids indefinite-length encodings, `readLength()` should throw an `IOException` when `length == 0x80`.

title: Redundant ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` and discard the returned encoders immediately before lines 119-120 perform the exact same encoding inside `writeDerSeq(...)`. Lines 114-115 should be removed.

title: canView(ClientModel) short-circuits via canView(), bypassing client-specific negative permissions
body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel client)`, calling `canView()` at the start evaluates `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` against only the `"Clients"` (all-clients) resource and immediately returns `true` if that succeeds, without ever calling `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` on the specific `client`. Unlike V1 where `canView()` only checked `canViewClientDefault()` (realm-management admin roles), in V2 an administrator can grant `view` on all clients via the `"Clients"` resource and define a negative permission denying `view` on a specific client (analogous to `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testViewUserPermission`). Because `canView()` evaluates only the `"Clients"` resource, `canView(client)` returns `true` even for a client with an explicit negative `view` permission. `canView(ClientModel)` should check `canViewClientDefault()` (like `canManage(ClientModel)` checks `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)`) and let `hasPermission(client, ...)` evaluate the client resource or fall back to the `"Clients"` resource.

title: canView() returns false when caller has MANAGE or CONFIGURE permission on all clients
body: `ClientPermissionsV2.canView()` checks `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` and does not consider `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (or `CONFIGURE`). In the parent class `ClientPermissions`, `canList()`, `canViewClientScopes()`, `canListClientScopes()`, and `requireView()` all delegate to `canView()`. Consequently, an admin granted only the `manage` scope on all clients will have `canManage() == true`, `canManageClientScopes() == true`, `canView(ClientModel) == true`, and `canView(ClientScopeModel) == true`, but `canView()`, `canList()`, `canViewClientScopes()`, and `canListClientScopes()` will all return `false`.

title: getClientsWithPermission queries resources by type that is not set on per-client resources and ignores transitive scopes
body: `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(String scope)` calls `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and checks `hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope)`. This has three problems: (1) `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates per-client resources via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` without calling `resource.setType(resourceType)`, so individual client resources have a `null` type and are never found by `findByType`; (2) the all-clients resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` does have type `"Clients"` and name `"Clients"`, so `granted.add(resource.getName())` adds the literal string `"Clients"` instead of client UUIDs; and (3) `hasGrantedPermission` only checks exact scope equality (`scope.equals(s)`), so a caller with `manage` or `configure` permission on a client will not match when `getClientsWithPermission("view")` is queried.

title: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName does not resolve resource names for Clients resource type
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` only handles `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` (returning `"All users"` or the user's username) and was not updated for `CLIENTS`. When a policy has resource type `"Clients"`, `getResourceName` falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` (which is `null`), instead of returning `"All clients"` for the `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` resource or `client.getClientId()` for an individual client resource.

title: Incorrect Javadoc on requireView() and requireViewClientScopes()
body: The Javadoc comments added for `void requireView()` (line 96) and `void requireViewClientScopes()` (line 101) state `Returns {@code true} if ... returns {@code true}`, but both methods return `void` and throw `ForbiddenException` when the corresponding `canView*()` check returns `false`.

title: canView(ClientModel) short-circuits on canView(), bypassing client-specific negative permissions
body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel client)`, calling `canView()` checks `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` against the all-clients (`"Clients"`) resource before `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` is reached. If an all-clients `view` permission is granted, `canView()` returns `true` and `canView(client)` immediately returns `true` without evaluating permissions on the specific client's resource. Any negative/deny `view` permission configured for that specific client is therefore bypassed. `canView(ClientModel)` should check `canViewClientDefault()` (admin roles) rather than `canView()`, letting `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` handle the fallback to the all-clients resource when no client-specific resource exists.

title: canView() does not return true when caller has manage permission on all clients
body: `ClientPermissionsV2.canView()` only checks `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` and does not check `canManage()` (i.e. `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`). Because `canViewClientScopes()`, `requireViewClientScopes()`, `requireView()`, `canList()`, and `canListClientScopes()` in `ClientPermissions` all delegate to `canView()`, an administrator granted `manage` permission on all clients (without an explicit `view` scope or `query-clients` role) will have `canView()` return `false` and receive `403 Forbidden` on endpoints requiring view or list access to clients and client scopes.

title: getClientsWithPermission never finds individual client resources and returns resource type name
body: `getClientsWithPermission(String scope)` looks up client resources using `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. However, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates individual client resources without calling `resource.setType(resourceType)`, leaving their type as `null`. The only resource with type `"Clients"` is the all-clients resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init`, whose name is `"Clients"`. As a result, `getClientsWithPermission` never finds any individual client resources, and if the all-clients resource has the requested scope, it adds the literal string `"Clients"` instead of client IDs. In addition, `hasGrantedPermission` only checks `scope.equals(s)`, so `getClientsWithPermission("view")` will not include clients where the caller was granted `"manage"` or `"configure"`.

title: Possible NullPointerException and evaluation when adminPermissionsEnabled is disabled on the realm
body: When `adminPermissionsEnabled` is turned off on a realm after the `admin-permissions` client has been initialized, `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient()` and `root.realmResourceServer()` remain non-null, while `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` returns `null` because `supportsAuthorizationSchema` checks `isAdminPermissionsEnabled(realm)`. In `hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, `resource` is not null-checked after calling `getResourceTypeResource`, so passing `null` to `findByResource(server, resource)` and `resource.getScopes()` will throw a `NullPointerException`. Furthermore, if a client-specific resource already exists (or in `hasPermission(String scope)` which queries `resourceStore.findByName` directly), permissions continue to be evaluated even though `adminPermissionsEnabled` is `false` on the realm.

title: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName does not resolve Clients resources
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` only handles `USERS.getType()` and falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` for `CLIENTS.getType()`. Because `getOrCreateResource` creates client resources with `name = client.getId()` and does not set a `displayName`, calling `getResourceName` for a `Clients` policy (e.g. when querying a permission's resources via the Admin REST API) returns `null` for individual client resources instead of `client.getClientId()`, and `"Clients"` instead of `"All clients"` for the all-clients resource.

title: `canView()` ignores `MANAGE` permission and `canView(ClientModel)` bypasses negative client permissions
body:
There are two permission evaluation bugs in `canView(ClientModel)` and `canView()`:

1. `canView()` (line 86) only checks `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` and does not check `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (or `canManage()`), unlike `canView(ClientScopeModel)` at line 121 and `UserPermissionsV2.canView()`. If an admin is granted `MANAGE` permission on all clients (`Clients`), `canView()` returns `false`, causing `requireView()`, `canViewClientScopes()`, `requireViewClientScopes()`, `canList()`, `canListClientScopes()`, and `clients().findAll(true)` (`viewableOnly=true`) to fail.
2. `canView(ClientModel client)` (line 78) calls `canView()` before evaluating permissions on `client`. Because `canView()` evaluates the all-clients `Clients` resource first, if an admin has a positive `VIEW` permission on all clients and a `Logic.NEGATIVE` permission denying `VIEW` on a specific client (analogous to `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testViewUserPermission`), `canView()` returns `true` and `canView(client)` short-circuits to `true`, completely ignoring the negative permission on `client`.

In addition, `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` only checks a single scope even though `root.evaluatePermission` already evaluates all scopes on the resource, so `canView(client)` can trigger up to four separate policy evaluations (`canView()`, `canManage(client)`, `canConfigure(client)`, and `hasPermission(client, VIEW)`) instead of checking `VIEW`, `CONFIGURE`, and `MANAGE` in a single evaluation.

title: `getClientsWithPermission` never matches individual client resources or implied scopes
body:
`ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(String scope)` looks up client resources via `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. However:

1. When `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (line 104) creates a resource for a specific client, it never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. Only the all-clients resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` (with `name = "Clients"`) has `type = "Clients"`. As a result, `findByType` never finds any individual client resources and instead only matches the all-clients resource (adding the literal string `"Clients"` rather than client IDs).
2. `hasGrantedPermission(Resource, String)` (line 274) only checks exact scope equality (`scope.equals(s)`). When `ClientsResource.getClients` calls `auth.clients().getClientsWithPermission(ClientPermissionManagement.VIEW_SCOPE)` (for example, when `viewableOnly=true` via `clients().findAll(true)`), clients on which the caller was granted `manage` or `configure` permissions (which imply `view`) are not matched.

Consequently, `clients().findAll(true)` returns an empty list whenever a caller only has permissions (`view`, `configure`, or `manage`) on specific clients, or `manage` permission on all clients.

title: `getResourceName` does not handle the `CLIENTS` resource type
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` stores `client.getId()` (the internal UUID) as the resource name when creating a resource for the `Clients` resource type, just as it stores `user.getId()` for `Users`. However, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` (lines 304-326) only handles `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` (returning `"All users"` or `user.getUsername()`) and was not updated for `CLIENTS.getType().equals(resourceType)` (to return `"All clients"` or `client.getClientId()`). As a result, converting policy resources to representations for `Clients` permissions returns raw client UUIDs (or `"Clients"`) instead of the client's `clientId`.

title: Unused `getEvaluationContext` method, `logger` field, and imports in `ClientPermissionsV2`
body: `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` (lines 262-272), `logger` (line 51), and the imports `Logger`, `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `Scope`, `EvaluationContext`, and `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` are never used in `ClientPermissionsV2` (`getEvaluationContext` and `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` were only used by `canExchangeTo` in V1 `ClientPermissions`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException` in V2).

title: Documentation inaccurately states that the Operator fails unless `rolling-updates` is enabled
body: The caution block states: "While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail." and the example below enables `rolling-updates` for `strategy: Recreate|<not set>`. However, the Operator does not validate or require the `rolling-updates` server feature flag for the default (`<not set>`) or `Recreate` strategies, and it does not fail when the feature is disabled (as also seen in `UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment`, which leaves the feature disabled when `updateStrategy` is `null`). This misleads users into thinking the Operator will fail unless `rolling-updates` is enabled on their deployments.

title: `testFeatureNotEnabled` does not cover the `check` subcommand or assert exit codes
body: This PR gates both `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` (`metadata`) and `UpdateCompatibilityCheck` (`check`) behind the `rolling-updates` feature flag and changes `CompatibilityResult` exit codes (`RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` changed from 4 to 3, and `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` was added). However, `testFeatureNotEnabled` only invokes the `metadata` subcommand (not `check`) and never asserts that the process exit code matches `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` (nor does `testWrongVersions` assert `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE`).

title: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage access when caller only has VIEW permission
body: In `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()`, the permission check calls `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Because `AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW` is included in the expected scopes, an admin who only has the `view` scope on all groups will have `canManage()` evaluate to `true`. Since `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` guards group creation and moving existing groups to the top level with `auth.groups().requireManage()`, a read-only admin with `view` permission on groups can create new top-level groups or move existing groups to the top level. `canManage()` should only check `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (and the Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` at line 75 should be updated accordingly).

title: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() never resolves group IDs and returns resource UUIDs instead
body:
`GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is broken in three ways:

1. `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)` when creating a resource for an individual group; only the all-groups resource (`"Groups"`) created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` has its type set to `AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE`. As a result, `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` never visits any individual group resources, returning an empty set for per-group permissions. This causes `UsersResource.getUsersCount()` to return `0` and `UsersResource.getUsers()` / `BruteForceUsersResource.searchUser()` to not set `UserModel.GROUPS` on the session (breaking paginated user queries for group admins).
2. Inside the `findByType` consumer, `groupResource.getId()` is passed to `hasPermission(...)` and added to `granted`. However, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` stores the `GroupModel` ID in `groupResource.getName()`, while `groupResource.getId()` is the internal authorization `Resource` UUID. Because `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` looks up resources via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, passing `groupResource.getId()` misses the group resource (falling back to the all-groups resource), and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` puts the authorization `Resource` UUID into `UserModel.GROUPS` instead of the `GroupModel` ID.
3. Because the all-groups resource (`name = "Groups"`) has `type = "Groups"`, `findByType` visits it. If an admin has `view-members` or `manage-members` on all groups, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` adds the all-groups resource's UUID to `granted`, causing `UsersResource` and `BruteForceUsersResource` to filter user queries by a non-existent group ID and return no users.

title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers
body: The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel group)` states `Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}.` It should reference `{@link #canManageMembers(GroupModel)}`.

title: canManage() grants group management access when caller only has VIEW permission
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) is called instead of checking only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE (and the same mistake is documented in GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() at line 75). Because GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() checks auth.groups().requireManage(), any admin granted only the 'view' scope on the all-groups resource will pass requireManage() and be able to create new top-level groups or move existing subgroups to the top level.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() fails to find per-group resources and returns Resource IDs instead of Group IDs
body:
GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is broken in three ways:
1. AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() (line 121) never calls resource.setType(resourceType) when creating a resource for an individual group; only the 'all-groups' resource created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init() has its type set to AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE. As a result, resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) never finds any individual group resources.
2. Inside the findByType callback, groupResource.getId() (the internal UUID of the authorization Resource entity) is passed to hasPermission(...) and added to granted, whereas the GroupModel ID is stored in groupResource.getName(). Because hasPermission(String groupId, ...) looks up the resource via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), passing groupResource.getId() misses the group resource and falls back to the 'all-groups' resource, and granted.add(groupResource.getId()) collects Resource UUIDs rather than GroupModel IDs.
3. Because the 'all-groups' resource itself has type 'Groups', findByType visits it as well; if an 'all-groups' permission grants view-members or manage-members, its non-group Resource ID is added to granted.

Consequently, for admins with view-members or manage-members on specific groups, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() always returns an empty set, causing UsersResource.getUsersCount() to return 0 and user searches to skip setting the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute. Conversely, for admins with view-members or manage-members on all groups, UserModel.GROUPS is set to the 'all-groups' Resource UUID, causing user searches to match no group and return 0 users.

title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers
body: The Javadoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.requireManageMembers(GroupModel) states 'Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}', but the implementation checks canManageMembers(GroupModel).

title: canManage() grants manage access when caller only has VIEW permission
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` checks `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` instead of only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (and the Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` documents this same check). Because `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` (`POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups`) calls `auth.groups().requireManage()`, any admin granted only the `view` scope on the `Groups` resource type will pass `requireManage()` and be able to create new top-level groups or move existing subgroups to top-level.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() fails to find group resources and returns Resource IDs instead of Group IDs
body:
`GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` has three compounding issues:
1. In `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (line 121), individual group resources are created without calling `resource.setType(resourceType)`. Only the all-groups resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` has `type = "Groups"`. Consequently, `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` never finds any per-group resources.
2. Inside the `findByType` callback, `groupResource.getId()` (the internal UUID of the authorization `Resource`) is passed to `hasPermission(...)` and added to `granted`. However, the `GroupModel` ID is stored in `groupResource.getName()`. `hasPermission` looks up the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, so passing `groupResource.getId()` never matches the group resource, and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` returns authorization `Resource` UUIDs instead of group IDs.
3. When an admin has `view-members` or `manage-members` on the all-groups resource, `findByType` matches the all-groups resource and `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns a set containing the all-groups resource UUID. `UsersResource.searchForUser` and `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` then set `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` to that non-existent group ID, causing user searches to return 0 results. Conversely, for per-group `view-members`/`manage-members` permissions, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns an empty set, causing `UsersResource.getUsersCount` (`GET /users/count`) to return 0 and bypassing database-level group filtering during paginated user searches.

title: hasPermission() does not fall back to all-groups resource when a group resource exists for another scope
body: In `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes)`, the all-groups resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`) is only evaluated when `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` returns `null`. If a specific group has a resource created for one scope (e.g., `manage-membership` or `view-members` on `topGroup`) and the caller has a different scope (e.g., `view` or `manage`) granted via an all-groups permission, `resourceStore.findByName(server, topGroup.getId())` returns the `topGroup` resource (`resource != null`). `evaluatePermission` then only evaluates policies attached to `topGroup`, fails to find the `view` or `manage` scope, and returns `false` without checking the all-groups resource.

title: Javadoc on requireManageMembers references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers
body: The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel group)` says `Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}.` It should reference `{@link #canManageMembers(GroupModel)}`.

title: Prefix/suffix diff calculation can cross over and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body: In `verifySafeHtml()`, the `end` loop (`while (end < sanitized.length() && end < value.length() && ...)`) does not stop when `end` reaches `sanitized.length() - start` or `value.length() - start`. When `value` and `sanitized` share identical characters on both sides of a pure insertion or deletion (for example, an extra closing tag like `{0}` vs. `{0}`, or an unclosed tag like `hello` vs. `hello`), `start + end` exceeds the shorter string's length and `substring(start, ... - end)` on line 111 throws a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

title: Anchor regex matches non-anchor tags starting with 'a' and skips anchor validation on English files
body: `ANCHOR_PATTERN` (`Pattern.compile("</?a[^>]*>")`) matches any HTML tag whose name starts with `a` (such as `<audio>`, `<applet>`, `<area>`, `<article>`, `<aside>`, `<abbr>`, or `<address>`), not only `<a>` tags. In addition, when `VerifyMessageProperties` runs on an `*_en.properties` file, `englishFile` resolves to the same file, so `englishValue` is identical to `value`; `santizeAnchors()` therefore matches every `<a...>` tag in `messages_en.properties` against itself and removes it before the OWASP sanitizer runs, allowing unsafe attributes on `<a>` tags (e.g., `onclick` or `javascript:` URLs) or tags like `<audio onerror=...>` in English bundles to bypass sanitization completely. Also note that the error message added on line 157 omits both `key` and `file`, making failures hard to locate.

title: Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax used in i18next resource bundle for account-ui
body: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. `account-ui` translates messages on the frontend with `i18next`, which expects double-brace interpolation (`{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`, as used by all other `error-*` keys in this file) and does not support Java `MessageFormat`/`ChoiceFormat` syntax. As a result, placeholders and the choice pattern will be rendered literally to users.

title: Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax used in i18next resource bundle for admin-ui
body: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. `admin-ui` uses `i18next` with double-brace placeholders (`{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`) rather than Java `MessageFormat`, so `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}`, and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` will not be interpolated and will be displayed verbatim in the UI.

body:
In `verifySafeHtml()`, the two `while` loops that find the common prefix (`start`) and common suffix (`end`) between `value` and `sanitized` run independently without bounding `start + end` by the lengths of the strings. When the difference occurs next to repeated characters or tags (for example, a duplicate closing tag like `value = "{0}"` vs. `sanitized = "{0}"`, where `start = 20` and `end = 9` for `sanitized.length() == 20`, or an unescaped `>` in `value = "

title: Anchor sanitization is bypassed for English files, matches non-anchor tags, and omits file/key in errors
body:
`santizeAnchors` has three issues:
1. When verifying an `_en.properties` file, `englishFile` resolves to the same file as `file`, so `value` and `englishValue` are identical. Every match in `value` therefore matches itself in `englishValue` and is stripped before `policy.sanitize(value)` runs, allowing arbitrary `<a ...>` tags (including `javascript:` URLs or event handler attributes) in `_en.properties` to bypass the OWASP sanitizer.
2. `ANCHOR_PATTERN` (`</?a[^>]*>`) has no word boundary after `a`, so it also matches any other tag starting with `a` (such as `<audio>`, `<applet>`, `<area>`, `<article>`, or SVG `<animate>`).
3. The error message on line 157 (`"Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string"`) omits both `key` and `file`, making it unclear which file and property caused the verification failure.

title: PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream) reads UTF-8 property files as ISO-8859-1
body: `new PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream)` on lines 68 and 77 is specified by the JDK to decode the stream using `ISO-8859-1`, whereas the message `.properties` files in this repository are UTF-8 encoded (and line 49 reads `file` as UTF-8 via `Files.readString`). Reading UTF-8 bytes as `ISO-8859-1` turns non-ASCII translations into mojibake and causes false mismatches or garbled diagnostic output when HTML entities (such as `»` unescaped to `\u00BB`) are compared against raw UTF-8 characters (`\u00C2\u00BB`). Pass a UTF-8 `Reader` (e.g. `Files.newBufferedReader(path, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)`) to `PropertyResourceBundle` instead.

title: Grant shortcut check in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId uses wrong substring indices and inverted condition
body: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` has two bugs: (1) in the 6-character prefix `<2-char sessionType><2-char tokenType><2-char grantType>` (e.g. `onrtac`), the 2-character grant type shortcut is at indices 4..6 (`substring(4, 6)`), whereas `substring(3, 5)` extracts the second character of the token type and the first character of the grant type (e.g. `"ta"`); and (2) the `.equals(...)` check is not negated, so it returns `false` on a match and continues on a mismatch. Because `substring(3, 5)` never equals valid grant shortcuts like `"ac"` or `"rt"`, the condition is always `false` and the matcher erroneously passes without verifying the grant type shortcut. It should check `items[0].length() == 6` and `!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)`.

title: Null check in AccessTokenContext constructor checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
body: In the `AccessTokenContext` constructor, line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`, checking `grantType` a second time instead of `rawTokenId`. Passing a `null` `rawTokenId` will not be rejected at construction time.

title: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() Javadoc specifies 3-letter shortcuts but encoder requires 2 characters
body: The Javadoc on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` states `@return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants`, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` does not validate shortcut length. However, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires the entire encoded context prefix to be 6 characters (`encodedContext.length() != 6`) and slices the grant shortcut from indices 4 to 6 (`encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`). Any `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation that follows the Javadoc and returns a 3-character shortcut will produce encoded token IDs that fail decoding with `IllegalArgumentException`.

title: testIncorrectGrantType catches NullPointerException instead of testing IllegalArgumentException
body: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest`, `before()` does not call `factory.postInit(...)`, leaving `factory.sessionFactory` as `null`. When `testIncorrectGrantType()` calls `provider.getTokenContextFromTokenId("ofrtac:5678")` with the unregistered shortcut `"ac"`, `factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac")` attempts to call `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` and throws a `NullPointerException`, which is caught by `catch (RuntimeException iae)`. Consequently, the `IllegalArgumentException` branch in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` for an unknown grant type shortcut is never reached.

title: Inverted condition and off-by-one substring indices in isAccessTokenId matcher
body: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` has two defects that cancel each other out: (1) the encoded prefix has 2-character segments for session type (0..2), token type (2..4), and grant type (4..6), so `substring(3, 5)` slices across the token type and grant type instead of extracting `substring(4, 6)` (and does not check that `items[0].length() == 6`); (2) the `.equals(...)` check is not negated, so it returns `false` on a match rather than a mismatch. Because `substring(3, 5)` (e.g. `"ta"` for `"onrtac"`) never equals the expected grant shortcut, the matcher currently passes for any 2-part token ID regardless of the actual grant shortcut.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
body: In the `AccessTokenContext` constructor, line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. A null `rawTokenId` will bypass this check and be stored on the instance, resulting in `"...:null"` when encoded.

title: testIncorrectGrantType catches NullPointerException instead of testing IllegalArgumentException
body: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before()`, `factory.postInit(...)` is not called, leaving `factory.sessionFactory` null. When `testIncorrectGrantType` calls `provider.getTokenContextFromTokenId("ofrtac:5678")`, `factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac")` misses the map and dereferences the null `sessionFactory`, throwing a `NullPointerException`. Because the test catches `RuntimeException` rather than asserting `IllegalArgumentException`, the `NullPointerException` is silently ignored and the unknown-grant-type error handling in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` is never exercised.

title: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() Javadoc specifies 3-letter shortcuts while encoder requires 2 characters
body: The Javadoc on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` states `@return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants`, whereas `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires the total encoded context to be 6 characters and extracts the grant shortcut from indices 4..6 (exact length of 2). Any grant type factory implementing a 3-letter shortcut per the Javadoc will produce 7-character prefixes in `encodeTokenId` that fail decoding with `IllegalArgumentException("Incorrect token id: '...'. Expected length of 6.")`.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong substring indices and inverted equality check
body: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the encoded prefix before `:` is 6 characters long (`0..2` session type, `2..4` token type, `4..6` grant type), as decoded in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` with `encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`. However, line 483 checks `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. This has two bugs: (1) `substring(3, 5)` extracts the second character of the token type and the first character of the grant type (e.g. `"ta"` from `"onrtac"`) instead of `substring(4, 6)`, and (2) the condition is missing a negation (`!`), so it returns `false` when the shortcut matches and `true` when it does not. Because `substring(3, 5)` never equals any of the expected grant shortcuts, the `if` branch is never taken and the matcher silently passes for any grant type.

title: Constructor null-check validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
body: In `AccessTokenContext(SessionType, TokenType, String, String)`, line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. Passing a `null` `rawTokenId` will not be rejected by the constructor.

title: Javadoc states grant shortcut is 3 letters while encoder requires 2 characters
body: The Javadoc on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` states `@return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants`, whereas `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires the entire prefix (`sessionType` + `tokenType` + `grantType`) to be 6 characters and slices the grant shortcut at `encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`. Any `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation that follows the Javadoc and returns a 3-letter shortcut will produce 7-character prefixes that fail decoding with `IllegalArgumentException: Incorrect token id ... Expected length of 6`.

title: testIncorrectGrantType catches NullPointerException from uninitialized sessionFactory instead of testing unknown grant rejection
body: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before()`, `factory.postInit(...)` is not called, leaving `factory.sessionFactory` as `null`. When `testIncorrectGrantType()` looks up the unregistered `"ac"` shortcut, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut` attempts to call `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` and throws a `NullPointerException` before `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` can throw `IllegalArgumentException`. Catching `RuntimeException` hides the `NullPointerException` and leaves the `IllegalArgumentException` path untested.

title: Exhausting federated recovery codes calls removeStoredCredentialById instead of disabling in user storage and can fail on null ID
body: When recovery codes come from a federated `UserStorageProvider` via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(authenticatedUser)`, exhausting the last recovery code (`recoveryCodeCredentialModel.allCodesUsed()`) still calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. `removeStoredCredentialById` only deletes from local or `UserFederatedStorage` credential stores and does not remove/disable the credential in the `UserStorageProvider` (which is done via `disableCredentialType`). Furthermore, if the provider constructs the model with `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)` without setting an ID (as `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials` does), `getId()` is `null`, causing `EntityManager.find(..., null)` in the JPA credential store to throw an `IllegalArgumentException`.

title: Missing null check for myUser and missing credential ID in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials
body: `getCredentials(RealmModel realm, UserModel user)` dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp` without checking `if (myUser == null)` (unlike `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isConfiguredFor`, and `isValid` in the same class). Because `UserCredentialManager.getFederatedCredentialsStream()` calls `getCredentials` on all enabled `CredentialInputValidator` providers in the realm when resolving credentials for a local user, calling `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` for any user not present in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` will throw a `NullPointerException` before the fallback to local stored credentials can run. Additionally, `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)` on line 237 does not copy the ID set on `myUser.recoveryCodes` in `updateCredential` (`model.setId(myUser.recoveryCodes.getId())`), leaving the returned credential's ID as `null`.

title: Potential NullPointerException and missing credential ID in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials
body: In `getCredentials(RealmModel realm, UserModel user)`, `myUser` (returned by `getMyUser(user)`) is dereferenced at `if (myUser.recoveryCodes != null)` without a null check. `UserCredentialManager.getFederatedCredentialsStream()` queries all enabled `CredentialInputUpdater` providers in the realm, including for local users or users from other providers that are not in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.users`. Unlike `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isConfiguredFor`, and `isValid` in the same class, `getCredentials` does not guard against `myUser == null`, resulting in a `NullPointerException` whenever federated credentials are listed for a non-storage user. Additionally, `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)` on line 237 does not copy the ID set on `myUser.recoveryCodes` in `updateCredential` (line 195), leaving `model.getId()` as `null`.

title: Exhausted user-storage recovery codes are not removed via removeStoredCredentialById and can fail on null ID
body: With `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(authenticatedUser)` now returning credentials from `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`, `optUserCredentialFound` may come from a `UserStorageProvider` rather than local storage. When `recoveryCodeCredentialModel.allCodesUsed()` is true, calling `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` only searches local/federated DB credential stores and does not remove or disable the credential in the `UserStorageProvider` (which uses `disableCredentialType`). Moreover, if the `CredentialModel` constructed by the `UserStorageProvider` has a `null` ID (for example, when created via `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues` as in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials`), passing `null` to `removeStoredCredentialById` causes JPA `EntityManager.find` to throw an `IllegalArgumentException`.

title: Exhausted recovery codes in user storage are not removed by removeStoredCredentialById
body: When `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(authenticatedUser)` returns a credential from a federated `UserStorageProvider` (via `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`) and `recoveryCodeCredentialModel.allCodesUsed()` is true, calling `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...)` only invokes `CredentialProvider.deleteCredential(...)` on local credential providers and has no effect on a `UserStorageProvider`. `UserStorageProvider` implementations of `CredentialInputUpdater` do not support deletion by ID and instead remove credentials via `disableCredentialType(RealmModel, UserModel, String)` (the fallback used by `AccountCredentialResource` when `removeStoredCredentialById` returns `false`). As a result, exhausted recovery code credentials stored in external user storage remain present after all codes have been used.

title: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage does not consume used recovery codes or preserve credential ID
body: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage`, `isValid` validates recovery codes with `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` without checking that the input matches the next expected code and without removing the used code from `myUser.recoveryCodes`. Consequently, `getCredentials` (lines 235-242) always reconstructs a `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` with all codes unused, so the login form always prompts for code #1 and allows the same code to be reused indefinitely. Additionally, `getCredentials` does not guard against `myUser == null` (unlike `isConfiguredFor`, `isValid`, and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`), does not copy `myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()` (set on line 195) onto the returned `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`, and `disableCredentialType` / `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` were not updated to support `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`.

title: Background reader thread in createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti is never joined or guaranteed to stop
body: In `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the background thread that repeatedly calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` is started with `new Thread(...).start()` without saving the `Thread` reference or calling `join()` before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())`, and `deletedAll.set(true)` is not placed in a `finally` block. As a result, an in-flight `groups(...)` request that fails after `deletedAll.set(true)` will record its exception in `caughtExceptions` after the assertion has already run (masking the failure) and may still be executing while subsequent tests run against `managedRealm`. In addition, if any `remove()` call throws an exception, `deletedAll` is never set to `true` and the background thread will spin indefinitely for the rest of the test suite.

title: Reader thread in `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` is not joined and can leak on failure
body: In `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the background thread started on line 139 is never joined before asserting `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` on line 157. If a `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` request is still in flight when `deletedAll.set(true)` is called, any exception it throws will be added to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion has already passed, and the request can overlap with subsequent tests sharing `managedRealm`. Additionally, because `deletedAll.set(true)` on line 155 is not in a `finally` block, an exception thrown while deleting groups in lines 152-154 will leave the background thread spinning in `while (!deletedAll.get())` for the remainder of the test suite run. Set `deletedAll.set(true)` in a `finally` block and `join()` the reader thread before asserting on `caughtExceptions`.

title: Background reader thread in createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti is never joined
body: In `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the thread started on line 139 to concurrently call `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` is never joined before asserting `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` and returning from the test. When `deletedAll.set(true)` is called on line 155, an HTTP request on the reader thread is likely still in flight: if that call throws an exception, it will be added to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion on line 157 has already passed, masking a test failure. Additionally, the unjoined thread can still be running while subsequent tests in `GroupTest` execute against the shared `managedRealm`. Join the reader thread after `deletedAll.set(true)` and before asserting on `caughtExceptions`.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator fails with TypeError when sorting by datetime fields
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint configures OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", where AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime.datetime instance. However, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor(value) / math.ceil(value) directly on getattr(item, self.key), which raises TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime as soon as any audit log row is processed. Additionally, value_from_cursor returns the raw numeric cursor.value instead of converting it back to a timezone-aware datetime object (as DateTimePaginator does), which causes subsequent cursor queries to compare a timestamp column against a number.

title: Passing negative offsets to Django QuerySet slicing raises unhandled ValueError
body: Both BasePaginator.get_result (line 182, when cursor.is_prev is True) and OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (lines 877-886, when enable_advanced_features is True or cursor.is_prev is True) pass negative cursor.offset values directly into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Contrary to the inline comments, Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ does not support negative slice bounds and immediately raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported."). Any request supplying a cursor with a negative offset (e.g., cursor=0:-1:1) will trigger an unhandled 500 Internal Server Error instead of clamping the offset or raising BadPaginationError.

title: Unchecked access to organization_context.member raises AttributeError for token requests
body: Line 71 evaluates request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access on every GET request. When the endpoint is accessed via an organization API token (or any non-superuser principal without an associated OrganizationMember record), organization_context.member is None and this line raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access', breaking the endpoint even when optimized_pagination is not requested.

title: Incorrect length check prevents trimming the extra row when offset is non-zero
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, queryset[start_offset:stop] is sliced with stop = start_offset + limit + extra, so results can contain at most limit + extra items. Line 891 checks elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra:, which can never be true whenever offset != 0, leaving an extra unrequested item in the page results when paginating backward with a non-zero offset.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator fails with TypeError when ordering by a DateTimeField
body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get` configures `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, where `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `DateTimeField`. Unlike `DateTimePaginator`, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` passes `getattr(item, self.key)` directly to `math.floor` / `math.ceil`, which raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` whenever results are present. In addition, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric cursor value rather than converting it to a `datetime` object, causing `build_queryset` to compare a timestamp column against a number in SQL.

title: Negative cursor offsets cause unhandled ValueError in Django QuerySet slicing
body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (lines 877-886) and `BasePaginator.get_result` (lines 182-184), negative `cursor.offset` values are passed directly as `start_offset` into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` (when `enable_advanced_features` is True with `cursor.offset < 0`, or whenever `cursor.is_prev` is True and `offset < 0`). Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly rejects negative slice bounds with `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`. Because `Endpoint.paginate` only catches `BadPaginationError` around `paginator.get_result`, supplying a negative offset in a cursor produces an unhandled 500 Internal Server Error instead of a 400 response.

title: Unchecked organization_context.member access raises AttributeError for non-member requests
body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated on every `GET` request whenever `request.user.is_superuser` is `False`, even when `optimized_pagination` is not enabled. When this endpoint is called using an organization token, API key, or Sentry App installation (where `request.user.is_superuser` is `False` and `organization_context.member` is `None`), dereferencing `organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'`.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime fields used by OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get configures OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", where AuditLogEntry.datetime is a DateTimeField. However, OptimizedCursorPaginator implements get_item_key and value_from_cursor for numeric fields rather than datetime fields: get_item_key passes getattr(item, "datetime") (a datetime.datetime instance) to math.floor() and math.ceil(), raising TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime whenever any audit log entries are returned. In addition, value_from_cursor returns the raw numeric cursor.value instead of converting it back to a timezone-aware datetime object like DateTimePaginator does, which causes the SQL query to fail when comparing the timestamp column against a number.

title: Unconditional access to organization_context.member raises AttributeError when member is None
body: Line 71 evaluates request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access on every GET request to OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint. In RpcUserOrganizationContext, organization_context.member can be None (for example, when authenticating with an organization auth token or API token where request.user is an AnonymousUser and request.user.is_superuser is False). Dereferencing organization_context.member.has_global_access without a None check will raise an unhandled AttributeError (HTTP 500) even when optimized_pagination is not requested. Additionally, Sentry endpoints should check is_active_superuser(request) rather than request.user.is_superuser so inactive superuser sessions do not grant elevated access.

title: Negative cursor.offset slicing on a Django QuerySet raises ValueError and computes invalid slice bounds
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (lines 877-882) and BasePaginator.get_result (lines 182-184), negative offsets are passed directly into queryset[start_offset:stop] when enable_advanced_features is True or cursor.is_prev is True. Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ does not support negative indexing and immediately raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.") whenever start < 0 or stop < 0. Moreover, computing stop = start_offset + limit + extra with a negative start_offset (e.g. -5) and positive limit + extra (e.g. 101) produces a positive stop index (96), resulting in a malformed slice [-5:96] that mixes negative and positive indices.

title: Clamping negative offset to 0 in BasePaginator.get_result corrupts generated cursors
body: In BasePaginator.get_result (line 182) and OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (line 884), start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset silently clamps a negative cursor.offset to 0 when slicing the queryset for forward pagination instead of rejecting the invalid negative offset. Because cursor.offset remains negative when passed into build_cursor, _build_prev_values evaluates has_prev = bool(value or offset) as True even on the first page (value=0), and _build_next_values computes next_offset = offset + limit using the negative offset when page boundary keys are equal.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes when paginating AuditLogEntry.datetime
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get passes paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", where AuditLogEntry.datetime is a DateTimeField (datetime.datetime). Unlike DateTimePaginator, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor(value) / math.ceil(value) directly on the datetime attribute, which raises TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime. In addition, OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw numeric cursor value instead of converting it to a timezone-aware datetime object, causing subsequent SQL comparisons against the timestamp column to fail.

title: Unconditional access to organization_context.member raises AttributeError when member is None
body: enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access is evaluated on every GET request to OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint. When request.user.is_superuser is False and organization_context.member is None (for example, with organization-scoped API tokens or non-member contexts), accessing organization_context.member.has_global_access raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'. Furthermore, checking request.user.is_superuser directly instead of is_active_superuser(request) bypasses active superuser session validation, and member.has_global_access is True for all members when an organization has open membership enabled, not just administrators.

title: Slicing a Django QuerySet with a negative start_offset raises ValueError
body: Both BasePaginator.get_result (lines 182-184, when cursor.is_prev is True and cursor.offset < 0) and OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (lines 877-886, when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0) pass a negative start_offset into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ does not support negative indexing and immediately raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported."), resulting in an unhandled 500 error whenever a cursor with a negative offset is supplied. Additionally, when cursor.is_prev is False and offset < 0, clamping start_offset = max(0, offset) while keeping offset negative corrupts downstream slice-trimming (len(results) == offset + limit + extra) and next-cursor offset calculations in build_cursor.

title: Evicting spans via zpopmin leaks redirect entries in span-buf:sr and ignores max_segment_spans
body: In add-buffer.lua, every incoming span_id is inserted into the redirect hash main_redirect_key (span-buf:sr:{project_id:trace_id}) on line 40, and then lines 62-64 evict spans with the lowest end_timestamp_precise via zpopmin when span_count exceeds 1000. Because SpansBuffer.done_flush_segments only calls HDEL on span-buf:sr:{project_id:trace_id} for spans present in the flushed segment, the redirect hash entries for all evicted spans are never deleted upon flush and remain in Redis until the 1-hour TTL expires. Additionally, if the root/segment span has an earlier end_timestamp_precise than async child spans, zpopmin will evict the root span itself while leaving span-buf:hrs set to 1. Finally, the limit of 1000 is hardcoded in Lua rather than using SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans, leaving the max_segment_spans attribute on SpansBuffer dead.

title: No test coverage for span eviction when a segment exceeds 1000 spans
body: The PR replaces the read-time max_segment_spans check in SpansBuffer._load_segment_data with write-time eviction via zpopmin in add-buffer.lua when a segment exceeds 1000 spans, but tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py only updates existing 4-5 span test fixtures with end_timestamp_precise and adds no test verifying eviction behavior above 1000 spans.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime field in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint
body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get` paginates `AuditLogEntry` with `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` and `order_by="-datetime"`. Unlike `DateTimePaginator`, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on `getattr(item, self.key)`, which is a `datetime.datetime` instance on `AuditLogEntry.datetime`, raising `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` whenever results are present. In addition, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric cursor value instead of converting it back to a `datetime` object for the queryset filter.

title: Unconditional dereference of organization_context.member can raise AttributeError
body: On line 71, `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated on every GET request before checking `use_optimized`. `organization_context.member` on `RpcUserOrganizationContext` is optional and can be `None` (for example, when authenticated via an organization API token or non-member integration). When `request.user.is_superuser` is `False` and `organization_context.member` is `None`, this raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'`.

title: Negative slice offsets on Django QuerySet raise ValueError
body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (lines 877-886) and `BasePaginator.get_result` (lines 182-184), negative cursor offsets are passed directly as `start_offset` into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` when `enable_advanced_features=True` or `cursor.is_prev=True`. Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly rejects negative slice indices with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`, causing an unhandled 500 error whenever a client supplies a cursor with a negative offset. Furthermore, when `cursor.is_prev` is `False` and `offset < 0`, `start_offset` is clamped to `0` for the slice, but the unclamped negative `offset` is still passed into `build_cursor`, corrupting the next/previous cursor offsets.

title: zpopmin can evict the segment root span when capping segment size
body: When `span_count > 1000`, `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` evicts the spans with the smallest `end_timestamp_precise` scores without excluding the root/segment span (`set_span_id`). If child spans finish after the root span (e.g., async children or clock skew) or share the same `end_timestamp_precise` and sort after the root span's payload, `zpopmin` will evict the root span from `set_key` while `has_root_span_key` remains set to `"1"`, causing the flushed segment to be emitted without its root span.

title: Unrelated audit log pagination changes crash with AttributeError and TypeError
body:
Aside from being unrelated to the spans buffer PR, the changes in `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get` contain two runtime bugs:
1. Line 71 evaluates `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` on every request. When a non-superuser request has no associated organization member (for example, an organization-level API token or Sentry App with `org:admin` permission), `organization_context.member` is `None`, raising `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'`.
2. When `optimized_pagination=true` is passed, lines 76-83 paginate `AuditLogEntry` ordered by `"-datetime"` using `OptimizedCursorPaginator`. However, `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `datetime.datetime` instance, and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on the field value (unlike `DateTimePaginator`), raising `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`. Likewise, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric cursor value instead of a `datetime`, causing a database type error on subsequent pages.

title: Negative offset slicing on Django QuerySets raises ValueError
body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (lines 877-882), when `self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0`, `start_offset` is set to the negative `cursor.offset` and used to slice `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Contrary to the comment claiming that the Django ORM handles negative slicing automatically, Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` whenever `start < 0` or `stop < 0`, resulting in an unhandled 500 error. The same crash occurs in `BasePaginator.get_result` (line 182) and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (line 884) whenever `cursor.is_prev` is `True` and `cursor.offset < 0` (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). Furthermore, when `cursor.is_prev` is `False` and `offset < 0`, clamping `start_offset` to `0` while passing the negative `offset` into `build_cursor` produces corrupted `next` and `prev` cursor offsets.

title: Evicting spans via zpopmin leaks redirect map entries and can evict the root span
body:
When `span_count > 1000`, `add-buffer.lua` evicts the spans with the lowest `end_timestamp_precise` from `set_key` using `zpopmin`, which introduces two issues:
1. Every ingested span has its `span_id -> set_span_id` mapping written to `main_redirect_key` (`span-buf:sr:{project_id:trace_id}`) at line 40, but `SpansBuffer.done_flush_segments` (`src/sentry/spans/buffer.py`, lines 478-482) only deletes `span_id`s that are present in `flushed_segment.spans`. Any span evicted by `zpopmin` is never removed from `main_redirect_key` on flush, leaking those hash entries until the 1-hour TTL expires and causing any late-arriving child of an evicted span to be redirected to the already-flushed segment.
2. `zpopmin` evicts purely by lowest `end_timestamp_precise` without protecting the segment's root/head span (`set_span_id`). If the segment span finishes earlier than 1,000 async/background child spans in the same segment, the root span itself will be evicted while `has_root_span_key` remains `"1"`.

title: max_segment_spans parameter is now unused and eviction (>1000 spans) lacks test coverage
body: `SpansBuffer.__init__` still accepts `max_segment_spans: int = 1001` and stores `self.max_segment_spans` (lines 150 and 158), but its only usage in `_load_segment_data` was removed and replaced with a hardcoded `1000` limit in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` (line 62). `max_segment_spans` should either be passed to `add-buffer.lua` as an argument or removed from `SpansBuffer.__init__`, and `tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py` should include a test covering segments with more than 1,000 spans.

title: `upsampled_count` does not fall back to 1 when `sample_weight` is null or unset
body: `upsampled_count` is defined as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`, assuming every error event in an allowlisted project has a populated `sample_weight`. In practice, unsampled error events, events ingested before client error sampling was enabled for the project, or events from SDKs that do not send `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` have `sample_weight` as `NULL` or `0` (or `<= 1`). Summing `sample_weight` directly causes all such unsampled events to contribute `0` instead of `1` to the count (returning `0` when no events have `sample_weight` set). The aggregation should fall back to `1` when `sample_weight` is null or not greater than `1` (e.g., `if(greater(sample_weight, 1), sample_weight, 1)` or `greatest(ifNull(sample_weight, 1), 1)`).

title: Caching allowlist eligibility causes stale results and breaks when allowlist option changes
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` in `sentry.utils.cache.cache` for 60 seconds keyed by `organization.id` and `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. However, `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere when `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` is updated (and cannot practically invalidate arbitrary cached `(organization_id, project_ids)` combinations when a global option changes). This contradicts `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`'s documented behavior of reading the allowlist fresh each time, causes stale eligibility results when the option changes (including across tests that mock or update `options` for the same organization and project IDs), and adds an unnecessary external cache lookup on every stats query when `sentry.options.get` already caches option values in memory with automatic invalidation.

title: `_get_event_stats` passes outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset` to upsampling check
body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` is called with the outer `dataset` variable rather than the `scoped_dataset` parameter passed to `_get_event_stats`. When `get_event_stats_factory` handles dashboard widget splitting under `metrics_enhanced`, the outer `dataset` is `metrics_performance` or `metrics_enhanced_performance`, while `_get_event_stats` is invoked with `scoped_dataset=discover` for error queries. Passing `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset` causes `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` to see the metrics dataset and always return `False` for those error queries.

title: Substring check in `_is_error_focused_query` matches negated or compound queries
body: `_is_error_focused_query` checks `if "event.type:error" in query:` using a raw substring match on the query string. A query that explicitly excludes errors such as `!event.type:error` (for example, when querying transactions) or a disjunction such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` still contains the substring `"event.type:error"` and will erroneously trigger error upsampling on non-error events.

title: Accidental git submodule `sentry-repo` committed
body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` git submodule/gitlink pointing to `a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` at the repository root without a corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This appears to be an accidentally committed nested repository and should be removed.

title: `upsampled_count` does not handle NULL or missing `sample_weight`, dropping unsampled errors
body: `upsampled_count` is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. In Snuba/ClickHouse, `sample_weight` is only populated when an event is ingested with a sample rate (e.g. from `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate`); unsampled events in an allowlisted project (such as events ingested before sampling was enabled or from SDKs that do not send `client_sample_rate`) have `sample_weight` as `NULL` (or `<= 1`). In ClickHouse, `sum(sample_weight)` treats `NULL` rows as `0` instead of `1`, silently excluding all unsampled error events from the count and returning `0` when a bucket contains only unsampled events. `sample_weight` should fall back to `1` when `NULL` or `<= 1` (e.g. `ifNull(if(greater(sample_weight, 1), sample_weight, 1), 1)`).

title: Allowlist caching in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` serves stale state and runs on every non-error query
body:
`is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` in `sentry.utils.cache.cache` for 60s under `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`. This has several issues:
1. The cache read/write and `options.get` check execute *before* `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)`, so every stats request (including transactions, spans, metrics, and non-error queries) pays the cache lookup/write cost even when the dataset is ineligible.
2. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere and cannot practically invalidate entries when the global `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes, because the cache key hashes the specific subset of `project_ids` in each query ($2^N$ possible combinations per organization). This also directly contradicts the docstring on `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` stating that the allowlist is intentionally read fresh on each call.
3. Python's built-in `hash()` is not guaranteed to be consistent across processes or collision-free, making it unsafe for shared cache keys, while `options.get` is already cached in process memory by `OptionsStore`.

title: `_get_event_stats` passes outer `dataset` and `request` instead of `scoped_dataset` and `query`
body: Inside `_get_event_stats(scoped_dataset, query_columns, query, ...)`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is called with the outer `dataset` variable and `request` (from which `_is_error_focused_query` reads `request.GET.get("query", "")`) instead of the `scoped_dataset` and `query` arguments passed into `_get_event_stats`. In `get_event_stats_factory` (lines 362-436), dashboard widget splitting invokes `_get_event_stats` with a overridden `scoped_dataset` (e.g. `discover` when the outer `dataset` is `metrics_enhanced_performance`) and modified `query` strings (`errors_only_query` / `transactions_only_query`), so upsampling eligibility is evaluated against the wrong dataset and query.

title: `_is_error_focused_query` matches negated and disjunctive queries like `!event.type:error`
body: `_is_error_focused_query` checks `"event.type:error" in query` via a plain substring match.
