When EventManager creates events for a collective booking with multiple CalDAV hosts, the service instance for host B authenticates as host B but filters the calendar list against host A's `externalId`; no calendar matches, `responses` is empty, `responses.some((r) => !r.ok)` is false, and the method returns a successful `NewCalendarEventType` without creating any event. Host B silently gets no calendar event while the booking reports success. The filter must use the destination calendar that corresponds to the credential being used, not `destinationCalendar[0]`.

title: Lark createEvent uses first destination calendar's externalId with the wrong credential
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;` — with multiple destination calendars (the new collective-event behavior), the Lark service always uses the first host's calendar id no matter which host's credential is instantiated. When EventManager iterates destinations and creates an event for a non-first host via their Lark credential, the request `/calendars/${calendarId}/events/create_event` targets the first host's calendar with the second host's access token, which either fails with a permission error or writes to the wrong calendar. Like GoogleCalendarService, the calendar should be resolved by matching `credentialId`.

title: Condition for setting team slug inverted relative to previous behavior
body: The diff changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which inverts the logic: previously the organization's team row got `slug` only when team billing was NOT enabled; now it gets `slug` only when billing IS enabled. This is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (destination calendars) and is not explained in the description. On deployments where `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false, newly created organizations will no longer have a team slug, breaking organization URLs that previously worked. If the inversion is intentional it needs its own PR/justification; otherwise this is a regression.

title: Team destination calendars silently dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null
body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` is a no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, which is exactly the value assigned a few lines above when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists. For a collective event where the organizer/event type has no destination calendar but team member hosts do have one, those hosts' calendars are silently discarded and they get no calendar event — the core scenario this PR is meant to fix. The push should happen unconditionally, e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

title: updateEvent result lacks credentialId/externalId, so updateLocation creates references without credential linkage
body: `CalendarManager.updateEvent` returns only `{appName, type, success, uid, updatedEvent, originalEvent, calError, calWarnings}` — it never sets `credentialId` or `externalId`, even though `EventResult` now declares them and `EventManager.updateLocation` (editLocation.handler.ts) builds `referencesToCreate` from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. Every booking reference created after a location edit will therefore have `credentialId: undefined` and `externalCalendarId: undefined`, degrading all later updates/cancellations to the legacy "iterate all calendar credentials" path and losing the per-host credential targeting this PR adds. `updateEvent` should return `credentialId: credential.id` and the external calendar id like `createEvent` does.

title: destinationCalendar webhook payload shape changed from object to array — breaking change for consumers
body: Changing `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from `DestinationCalendar | null` to `DestinationCalendar[] | null` changes the JSON payload sent to all BOOKING_CREATED / BOOKING_REJECTED / BOOKING_CANCELLED / BOOKING_REQUESTED webhook subscribers (the whole `evt` is sent via `sendPayload`). Existing integrations that read `payload.destinationCalendar.integration` or `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` will now get `undefined` because the value is an array. The PR is labeled "non-breaking change" and no migration/communication for webhook consumers is included; the e2e expectations in webhook.e2e.ts confirm the payload shape changed. This should be documented as a breaking change or the payload should keep backwards compatibility.

title: No tests added for the multi-destination-calendar behavior
body: The PR explicitly states "I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works", while it rewrites the calendar-event creation/update/deletion flow across EventManager, CalendarManager, three calendar services, cancellation, and payment webhooks. There is no unit test covering: a collective booking creating one event per host's destination calendar, cancellation deleting all hosts' events via the new per-reference credentialId handling, or the legacy single-destination fallback for pre-existing bookings. Given the regressions visible in the fallback paths (e.g. undefined calendarId in Google updateEvent/deleteEvent), regression tests for existing bookings without `externalCalendarId`/`credentialId` references are particularly important before merging.

title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
body: In EventManager.create, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` is followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without optional chaining. When `destinationCalendar` is null/empty (e.g. organizer has no calendar app installed) and the event location is Google Meet — exactly the 'Meet selected w/o a Google Cal' scenario this code is meant to handle — `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and reading `.integration` throws a TypeError, aborting the whole booking creation. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` which was null-safe. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` (or better, `some(cal => cal.integration === "google_calendar")` now that it is an array).

title: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition for organization slug
body: The change `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` → `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` inverts the logic. Previously the slug was set immediately only when team billing was disabled (with billing enabled, the org pays first and the slug is assigned later from `requestedSlug` in metadata). Now the slug is set at creation time when billing IS enabled — bypassing the payment-gated slug assignment flow — and is never set when billing is disabled, leaving organizations without a slug/subdomain. This change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose and looks accidental; it should be reverted to the negated condition.

title: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback find() is dead code and loses destination calendar
body: In updateEvent, `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — in the fallback branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so `find()` can never match anything and `selectedCalendar` is always `undefined`. `calendar.events.update` is then called with `calendarId: undefined`, which fails. The same pattern in deleteEvent (line 315) falls through to `"primary"`, so the event is deleted from the wrong calendar (or 404s silently) instead of the destination calendar. The fallback should use the first destination calendar's externalId (the pre-PR behavior), e.g. `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

title: Hangout-link patch uses selectedCalendar without the 'primary' fallback
body: In createEvent, the insert call uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` that adds the hangout link to the description uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` with no fallback. When no destination calendar matches the current `credentialId` (so `selectedCalendar` is undefined), the event is created on `primary` but the patch is sent with `calendarId: undefined` and fails, so meeting links never make it into the event description. The patch should use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` value as the insert.

title: Non-Google calendar services still only use the first destination calendar
body: Office365 (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`), Lark (packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128) and the CalDAV BaseCalendarService (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156) all read only the first element of the now-array `destinationCalendar`. Since EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent once per destination with each host's own credential, for a collective event with multiple hosts on these providers the second host's credential is used against the first host's `externalId`, creating the event in the wrong calendar or failing with an auth/404 error. Only the Google service was adapted (find by credentialId), so the multi-host fix this PR claims only works for Google Calendar. The same per-credential selection is needed in these services.

title: Team hosts' destination calendars dropped when organizer has none
body: For COLLECTIVE events the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. But `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer user has a destination calendar (the ternary chain ends in `null`). Optional chaining makes the push a no-op in that case, so team members' destination calendars are silently discarded — precisely the collective scenario the PR is meant to fix — and no calendar events get created for those hosts. The code should assign `evt.destinationCalendar = teamDestinationCalendars` when it is null rather than relying on `?.push`.

title: organization select removed from dynamic-booking user query
body: The refactored `loadUsers` for the no-eventTypeId (dynamic link) branch drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the prisma.user.findMany select that the previous code included. Any downstream logic for dynamic bookings that reads `user.organization` (e.g. organization-aware routing/slug building for dynamic group bookings) will now see `undefined` and behave as if the user belongs to no organization. This removal is unrelated to the destinationCalendar change and looks accidental; the select should be restored.

title: Breaking change to webhook payload destinationCalendar shape
body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is sent verbatim in BOOKING_* webhook payloads, and its shape changes from a single `DestinationCalendar` object (or null) to an array. External webhook subscribers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` etc. will break with no migration note, even though the PR is marked 'non-breaking'. Additionally the empty value is inconsistent across emitters: handleNewBooking emits `null` while confirm/cancel/payment handlers emit `[]` (see the e2e expectations at lines 119 `null` vs 249 `[]`), so consumers must handle both. This should be documented as a breaking webhook change and the empty representation unified.

title: Recurring cancellation deletes each booking event once per calendar reference
body: The recurring `allRemainingBookings` branch now lives inside a `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop over all calendar references, and for each reference it iterates ALL of the organizer's calendar credentials × ALL updated bookings, calling deleteEvent. With multiple calendar references (the multi-host case this PR introduces) the same booking's calendar event is deleted N times, and it is deleted with whichever credentials the organizer happens to have rather than the reference's own credential. At best this produces duplicate delete calls (only tolerated because Google treats 410/404 as success); other providers may error and surface as a failed cancellation.

title: No tests for the new multi-destination collective behavior
body: The PR checklist explicitly states no tests were added. The core change — destinationCalendar becoming an array, per-credential calendar selection in EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, Google's find-by-credentialId, and the collective push of team calendars — is only covered by an updated e2e assertion for BOOKING_REJECTED. Unit tests for EventManager (create/reschedule/cancel with multiple destination calendars, empty destinationCalendar + Google Meet location, destination calendars without credentialId) are missing, which is how the crash at EventManager.ts:119 and the `?.push` no-op escaped review.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported in SalesforceCalendarService
body: The new token-refresh code in `getClient()` calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)` at line 96, but the file's imports (lines 1-20) contain no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` (unlike every other CalendarService changed in this PR). This fails type-check/build, and at runtime throws `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` the first time a Salesforce credential is used, breaking Salesforce event creation entirely.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys are broken and the schema strips all expiry/refresh fields
body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key "[object Object]" (Zod schemas have no custom toString), so the schema is effectively `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown-optional }`. The comment claims "any property with a number is the expiry" but nothing like that is implemented — no expiry field is validated. Worse, zod's `z.object().parse` strips unknown keys by default, so when credential sync is enabled the returned `data` contains only `access_token` (plus the dummy refresh_token injected at line 26). Callers that persist this data — Google CalendarService (`data: { key }`) and Salesforce (`data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, ... } }`) — will save credentials that have lost `refresh_token`, `expiry_date`, `instance_url`, `scope`, etc., permanently corrupting the stored credential. For Zoom, `newTokens.expires_in` is then undefined so `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` stores NaN.

title: Dummy `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` overwrites real refresh tokens, including when sync is disabled
body: When the parsed token response lacks `refresh_token`, the code unconditionally sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. This is not limited to the sync-enabled path — it also runs for the normal per-app schema. Microsoft's refresh-token endpoint legitimately omits `refresh_token` on refresh responses (the existing refresh token stays valid); previously Office365CalendarService preserved the old token via `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`, but now the placeholder string "refresh_token" is spread over the real token and written to the DB. The next refresh will send `refresh_token=refresh_token` and fail with invalid_grant, breaking Office 365 calendar sync for existing non-sync users as a regression from this PR.

title: Sync mode returns a raw fetch Response but callers expect library-specific objects (axios responses, hubspot tokens, gaxios res)
body: When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response` object. Several callers cannot handle that: HubspotCalendarService (CalendarService.ts:177-202) treats the return as a `HubspotToken` and reads `.expiresIn`/`.accessToken` (→ NaN expiryDate stored, `setAccessToken(undefined)`); zoho-bigin (CalendarService.ts:96) and zohocrm (CalendarService.ts:217) read `.data` on it (→ TypeError "Cannot set properties of undefined", crash); GoogleCalendarService (CalendarService.ts:94) reads `res?.data` from what used to be a gaxios response (`fetchTokens.res`), which is undefined on a fetch Response → `token.access_token` throws. Enabling the advertised sync feature breaks these apps outright; each caller needs the sync response normalized into the shape it expects.

title: Salesforce connection is built with the stale access token after refreshing, and refresh now runs on every use
body: In `getClient()`, a new access token is fetched via the token endpoint and persisted to the DB (lines 75-99), but the `jsforce.Connection` returned at line 101 is constructed with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token` — the *old* token read from the credential before the refresh. The newly obtained `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` is never used, so API calls run against the stale (possibly expired) token. Additionally, unlike the other services, there is no expiry check: `getClient()` is called from the constructor on every service instantiation, so every booking operation now performs a Salesforce token refresh and a DB write even when the stored token is still valid. The `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` check at line 92 is also dead code since `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure.

title: zoho-bigin passes credentialId as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFn, "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` sends the *credential* id where the function's third parameter is `userId` and is transmitted to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. In credential-sync mode the parent application receives the wrong identifier, so it will look up the wrong user's tokens (or none), breaking token refresh for Zoho Bigin whenever sync is enabled. The correct value is `credential.userId`, as used by all other apps.

title: Webhook handler: uncaught ZodError/decrypt/JSON.parse errors return 500, no method check, and decrypted keys stored unvalidated
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on malformed input, and `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` (line 57) throw on bad ciphertext or non-JSON plaintext — none are caught, so the caller gets an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx. The handler also never checks `req.method`, so it mutates credentials on GET/PUT/etc. Finally, the decrypted `keys` object is written straight into `credential.key` without validating it against the target app's credential schema (e.g. `googleCredentialSchema`), so arbitrarily-shaped JSON can be persisted and will only fail later inside the app's service code.

title: Credential update does not clear the `invalid` flag and may clobber the wrong credential
body: When updating an existing credential (line 73), the `invalid` field is not reset to false, so if the credential was previously marked invalid (e.g. after an invalid_grant), syncing fresh valid keys leaves it permanently disabled. Additionally, `findFirst` on `{ userId, appId }` picks an arbitrary record when a user has multiple credentials for the same app slug (Cal.com supports multiple installed credentials per app per user, e.g. multiple Google accounts), so the new keys can overwrite the wrong account's tokens.

title: Webhook secret compared with plain !== instead of constant-time comparison
body: The shared-secret check `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` uses ordinary string comparison, which is not constant-time and leaks timing information about the secret's length/prefix to an attacker probing the endpoint. Since this secret authorizes writing arbitrary OAuth credentials for any user id, the comparison should use a constant-time equality check (e.g. `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers).

title: No tests for the new OAuth sync helpers or the credential webhook
body: The PR introduces a new unauthenticated-surface webhook endpoint, a global switch that changes the token-refresh code path of ten apps, and schema/parse helpers with non-trivial behavior — and the PR checklist explicitly states no tests were added. Given that several of these paths are broken as written (dummy refresh_token injection, schema stripping, fetch-Response type mismatches), unit tests for `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (both modes) and `refreshOAuthTokens`, plus an integration test for `/api/webhook/app-credential`, would have caught these regressions and are needed before merge.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported in SalesforceCalendarService
body: The new token-refresh block added to `getClient` calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` (line 96), but the file's imports do not include `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` (only jsforce, RRule, zod, logger, HttpError, getAppKeysFromSlug, parseRefreshTokenResponse and types are imported). Since `getClient` is invoked from the constructor, every use of the Salesforce calendar service (event creation, updates, deletions) will throw `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime, completely breaking the Salesforce integration for all installations, not just those opting into credential sync.

title: Computed zod schema keys collapse to the literal string "[object Object]"
body: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. `z.string()` returns a ZodString instance whose `toString()` is `Object.prototype.toString`, i.e. the literal string `"[object Object]"`. Both computed keys are identical, the second overwrites the first, and the resulting schema only validates `access_token: z.string()` plus a meaningless optional `"[object Object]"` property. The stated intent ("assume any property with a number is the expiry") is not implemented at all: the expiry field returned by the sync endpoint (e.g. `expires_in`/`expiry_date`) is neither required nor validated, so an endpoint response missing the expiry silently passes validation and propagates `undefined`/`NaN` expiry values into stored credentials.

title: Sync-mode parsing strips all credential fields and writes a literal "refresh_token" placeholder, corrupting stored credentials
body: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the response is parsed with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead of the app schema. zod objects strip unknown keys by default, so the parse result keeps only `access_token`. Then, because `refresh_token` was stripped, line 26 assigns the literal string `"refresh_token"` as the refresh token. In GoogleCalendarService this means the credential written back to the DB via `prisma.credential.update` loses the real `refresh_token`, `expiry_date`, and every other field, keeping only `{ access_token, refresh_token: "refresh_token" }`. The next refresh attempt uses the bogus token and fails permanently. The same stripping drops `expires_in` in the Office365 path (leaving the old, already-expired value so `isExpired` is always true and tokens are refreshed on every request) and in Zoom produces `Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` = `NaN` persisted as `expiry_date`. Additionally, in the non-sync path the placeholder also overwrites a legitimately absent-but-optional `refresh_token` (Office365's schema declares it optional) with the garbage literal.

title: Sync-mode return value is a raw fetch Response but every caller expects a `.data` property
body: In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the `fetch` `Response` object directly. All call sites were written for their provider SDK's response shape and read `res.data` / `tokenInfo.data` (Google: `const token = res?.data` then `token.access_token` → TypeError; hubspot: `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` → `Date.now() + undefined * 1000` = NaN; zoho-bigin and zohocrm: `tokenInfo.data.error` → TypeError on undefined). A fetch Response has no `.data`; the body must be consumed via `.json()`/`.text()`. As written, the credential-sync feature crashes or silently corrupts token data in every adapted app the first time a token refresh is attempted. The response is also never checked for `response.ok`.

title: Outbound credential-sync request carries no authentication
body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body — no secret, header, or signature (CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET exists but is only used to authenticate the inbound webhook). The self-hosted endpoint therefore cannot verify the request originated from the Cal.com instance, so anyone who can reach the endpoint can request fresh OAuth access tokens for arbitrary users by guessing/enumerating user IDs. At minimum the webhook secret should be sent as a header so the receiving side can authenticate the request.

title: Unvalidated `.parse` and unguarded decrypt/JSON.parse turn bad requests into 500s
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on an invalid body, and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` (line 57) throws if the ciphertext is malformed or not valid JSON. Neither is caught, so the endpoint returns an unhandled 500 (with stack details in some configurations) instead of a 400 with a meaningful message. The endpoint also has no `req.method` guard, so any HTTP method is accepted. Malformed-input paths of an internet-exposed webhook should return 4xx, not 500.

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==`
body: The shared secret check `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` uses plain string comparison, which is not timing-safe; other webhook verifications in the codebase/industry use `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. Also, `req.headers[name]` can be `string[]` for repeated headers, which silently fails the comparison. Low practical risk, but this is the sole authentication for an endpoint that can overwrite any user's app credentials.

title: Salesforce token is now refreshed unconditionally on every service construction
body: The new code in `getClient` always POSTs to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and writes the credential row, with no expiry check. `getClient` runs from the class constructor, so every calendar operation (create/update/delete event, contact search) now performs an extra OAuth token round-trip to Salesforce plus a DB write, even when the stored access token is still valid. Previously jsforce refreshed lazily. Beyond the latency/DB churn, Salesforce refresh tokens can be invalidated by excessive refresh frequency.

title: Zoom expiry_date becomes NaN when sync mode strips expires_in
body: After `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseBody, zoomRefreshedTokenSchema)` runs in credential-sync mode, `newTokens` contains only `access_token` (plus the `"refresh_token"` placeholder) because the minimum schema strips `expires_in`, `token_type` and `scope`. Line 122 then computes `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000)` = `NaN`, which is persisted to the credential row. `isTokenValid` (`(token.expires_in || token.expiry_date) < Date.now()`) returns false for NaN, so the adapter treats the credential as permanently valid and never refreshes again — all subsequent Zoom API calls fail with an expired access token.

title: No tests for the credential-sync webhook or token-refresh helpers
body: The PR adds a security-sensitive, unauthenticated-input-handling webhook (secret check, AES decryption, credential upsert) and two shared helpers (`refreshOAuthTokens`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) that alter the token-parsing behavior of ~10 app integrations, yet includes no unit or integration tests (the PR checklist confirms none were added). Several of the defects in this review (schema stripping, raw-Response `.data` access, missing prisma import) would have been caught by basic tests exercising the sync-enabled path and the webhook handler with malformed payloads.

title: prisma is used but never imported in SalesforceCalendarService
body: The new token-refresh block calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` (line 96) and the file's import list contains no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This is a compile-time failure (type-check/build breaks) and, if it somehow ran, a runtime ReferenceError. The newly added refresh flow can never work as shipped.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema is broken and strips fields, corrupting stored credentials
body: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", so the 'any numeric property is the expiry' and 'allow other properties' intent is not implemented. Worse, z.object() strips unknown keys by default and this helper returns `safeParse(...).data`, so when credential sync is enabled every caller receives only `{access_token}` plus the injected `refresh_token: "refresh_token"` placeholder (line 26). Concrete consequences: ZoomVideoAdapter computes `expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` = NaN and persists it; Google's stored key loses expiry_date/scope/token_type; Salesforce's stored key loses instance_url/signature/token_type (breaking the next getClient call since instance_url becomes undefined); Office365 calendar credentials get their real refresh_token overwritten with the literal string "refresh_token". The schema needs `.passthrough()` and a real expiry field, and the fake refresh_token should not be persisted into the credential.

title: Google token refresh crashes in sync mode: fetch Response has no `.data`
body: When credential sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` Response, but the non-sync path returns a gaxios response whose token lives in `.res.data`. The code does `const token = res?.data;` then `token.access_token`, which is a TypeError (reading property of undefined) for every Google Calendar token refresh when sync is on — i.e. any booking/calendar operation after access-token expiry throws. The response from the sync endpoint must be JSON-parsed before use.

title: HubSpot refresh stores garbage credentials in sync mode
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` in sync mode returns a `fetch` Response, but the code treats it as a HubspotToken: `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` is undefined (so `setAccessToken(undefined)` is called) and `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` is undefined, making `expiryDate = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` = NaN. That NaN expiryDate and the empty token are then persisted to the credential via prisma.update, silently corrupting the stored credential and breaking subsequent HubSpot operations.

title: credentialId passed to refreshOAuthTokens instead of userId
body: The third argument of `refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFn, appSlug, userId)` is documented and used as the Cal.com user id sent to the credential sync endpoint, but the Zoho Bigin adapter passes `credentialId` (the credential row id). When sync is enabled the endpoint receives a credential id as `calcomUserId`, so it will fail to find the user or return another entity's credentials — token refresh for Zoho Bigin cannot work under sync.

title: Zoho CRM refresh throws TypeError in sync mode: fetch Response has no `.data`
body: In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` Response, but the code immediately accesses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`. A fetch Response has no `.data` property, so this is a TypeError (cannot read properties of undefined) on every Zoho CRM token refresh when credential sync is enabled — the adapter was only adapted for the axios response shape.

title: Zoom stores NaN expiry_date and destroys the stored refresh token in sync mode
body: When sync is enabled, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` validates against the minimum schema and strips the response, so `newTokens.expires_in` is undefined and `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` is NaN, which is persisted to the DB. Additionally `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` writes the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" over the real refresh token. The credential is left with a NaN expiry (so `isTokenValid`'s comparison is always false and the stale access token is reused indefinitely) and is unrecoverable if credential sync is later disabled.

title: Webex refresh always fails in sync mode: full schema validated against sync response
body: Unlike Zoom/Office365, the Webex adapter wraps its refresh in `refreshOAuthTokens` but still validates the response with the full `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse`, which requires scope (exact literal), token_type, and refresh_token — none of which the credential-sync endpoint returns (it only returns access token + expiry). Every Webex token refresh under sync mode will reject with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". It should use `parseRefreshTokenResponse` like the other adapted apps, or the schema needs to differ per mode.

title: Lark refresh incompatible with sync response shape
body: The refresh result is passed to `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log)`, which expects Lark's envelope `{code: 0, data: {access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, refresh_expires_in}}`. The credential-sync endpoint returns a plain `{access_token, expiry}` body with no `code`, so `handleLarkError` will treat it as an error (or `data.data.*` will be undefined), making Lark token refresh fail — or worse, persist credentials with undefined refresh_token/refresh_expires_date — whenever sync is enabled.

title: MS Teams credential key replaced wholesale, dropping refresh_token and email
body: In `refreshAccessToken`, `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: responseBody } })` replaces the entire stored key with the refresh response. In sync mode the response only contains access token + expiry, so the persisted credential loses `refresh_token` and `email`. Even though the parent app is the source of truth while sync is enabled, the local credential is silently destroyed: turning sync off, or any code path that hits the local refresh (e.g. a team credential where userId is null and `refreshOAuthTokens` falls back to the local refresh function) will then fail because the refresh token is gone.

title: Outbound credential sync request carries no authentication
body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` — no shared secret, signature, or header of any kind. The endpoint's response contains the user's third-party access token, so unless the self-hoster independently protects that URL, anyone who can reach it and guess/enumerate a user id can retrieve arbitrary users' OAuth access tokens. The webhook flow in the other direction is authenticated with CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET; this direction should send a comparable secret (e.g. the same webhook secret as a header).

title: Webhook handler: no method check and unhandled parse/decrypt errors return 500s
body: The handler never checks `req.method` (a GET with no body will run the logic), and it uses `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` (throws ZodError on malformed input) plus `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` (throws on wrong encryption key or non-JSON plaintext). All of these are unhandled, so invalid requests produce opaque 500 errors instead of 400s. Use `safeParse`, wrap decryption, and gate on POST.

title: Credential sync does not reset the `invalid` flag on update
body: When updating an existing credential the handler only sets `key`. If the credential was previously marked `invalid: true` (e.g. by the invalid_grant handling in Google/Zoom/Webex), pushing fresh valid keys through the webhook will not re-enable it — the app stays broken for that user even though the sync succeeded. The update should also set `invalid: false`.

title: Webhook secret compared with plain string inequality
body: `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is not constant-time. For a shared-secret check on an endpoint that can write OAuth credentials, use a timing-safe comparison (crypto.timingSafeEqual) to avoid leaking the secret byte-by-byte to an attacker who can measure response times.

title: Salesforce connection is created with the stale access token after refreshing
body: The new code refreshes the token, persists it, but then constructs `new jsforce.Connection({ ..., accessToken: credentialKey.access_token, ... })` using the OLD (possibly expired) token from the credential snapshot instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`. So the refresh has no effect on the connection actually used, and expired credentials stay broken. Additionally there is no expiry check, so this token refresh + DB write happens on every single `getClient` call (every booking), which is both a performance problem and a rate-limit risk against Salesforce's token endpoint.

title: Success check `response.statusText !== "OK"` is unreliable
body: HTTP status text is not guaranteed to be "OK" (it can be empty, e.g. HTTP/2, or localized by some clients/proxies). Use `response.ok` / `response.status === 200` instead; otherwise valid responses may be rejected as errors and refresh may fail spuriously.

title: No tests for the webhook or the sync-mode refresh paths
body: The PR adds a new externally-callable endpoint that writes OAuth credentials and rewires token refresh for ~10 apps behind an env flag, with zero automated tests (the checklist explicitly says no tests were added). At minimum: webhook auth/validation/404/200 paths, and refresh behavior for each adapted app with sync both enabled and disabled. Given the number of adapters that break in sync mode (Google, HubSpot, Zoho, Webex, Lark, Zoom), tests would have caught most of these regressions before merge.

title: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, breaking the permission check
body: The check is `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId))`, but the variable is named and intended as 'admin OR owner'. With the AND, a user who is a team admin but not the team owner is denied (FORBIDDEN), and a team owner who is not recorded as an admin is also denied. The intended behavior (matching other handlers in the codebase, e.g. editLocation, which use `||`) is that either role grants permission. Consequence: team admins cannot add guests to team bookings even though the UI/API contract suggests they should be able to.

title: Guest emails are not deduplicated against each other, only against existing attendees
body: The server-side Zod schema (addGuests.schema.ts) only validates that each string is an email; the uniqueness refinement exists only in the client-side dialog. The handler's `uniqueGuests` filter only removes guests that already exist in `booking.attendees` or are blacklisted — it never dedupes the request array itself. A request like `{ bookingId, guests: ["a@b.com", "a@b.com"] }` passes validation and the subsequent `createMany` inserts two identical attendee rows for the same booking, corrupting the attendee list and causing duplicate emails/ICS invites. The uniqueness constraint must be enforced server-side (in the schema or by deduping `uniqueGuests`).

title: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check is case-sensitive and can be bypassed
body: The blacklist is normalized with `.toLowerCase()` (`process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_emails.split(",").map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guest` values are compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. An email like `Bad@Example.com` will not match a blacklisted `bad@example.com` and will be added, defeating the blacklist. The same case-sensitivity problem affects `guest === attendee.email` on line 76 and the `isAttendee` check on line 52 (`attendee.email === user.email`), allowing duplicate attendee entries that differ only in case. All email comparisons here should be case-insensitive.

title: EventManager is built with the requesting user's credentials, not the booking organizer's
body: The handler authorizes team admins/owners and attendees (not just the organizer) to add guests, but then constructs `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` using `ctx.user` (the caller) and credentials from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. When a team owner or an attendee triggers this mutation, the calendar update (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`) runs with the wrong user's calendar credentials — most likely none matching the booking's destination calendar — so the external calendar event is not updated for the new guests, or the operation errors. The EventManager should be constructed from the booking organizer (`booking.user`, which is already included with credentials in the initial query) so calendar attendee updates work regardless of who calls the endpoint.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails event type metadata
body: Every other email-sending function in this file (sendScheduledEmails, sendRescheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails, etc.) accepts an `eventTypeMetadata` parameter and skips host/attendee emails when `disableStandardEmails.all.host` / `.attendee` is set. The new `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and unconditionally sends both organizer and attendee emails. Event types that have standard emails disabled (a supported configuration) will still blast out 'Guests Added' emails to hosts and attendees, violating the organizer's email preferences. The function should accept and honor `eventTypeMetadata` like its siblings.

title: No booking status or seat-capacity checks before adding guests
body: The handler never checks `booking.status`, so guests can be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings; those guests then receive an email with an ICS of `status: "CONFIRMED"` (attendee-add-guests-email.ts line 15) for an event that no longer exists. Additionally, for event types with `seatsPerTimeSlot`, the handler blindly `createMany`s attendees with no capacity check and without creating the associated `seatsReferences`/booking-seat records that the seats flow relies on, which can overbook a seat-limited event and leave attendee records in a state that breaks seat cancellation logic.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw `guests` input instead of the guests actually added
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the original request array, but only `uniqueGuests` were actually persisted. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` decides whether an attendee gets the 'scheduled' email (as a new guest) or the 'guests added' notification. If a requested email was filtered out (already an attendee with different casing, or blacklisted), the classification is made against emails that were never added, and emails that *were* added are classified using stale input. Passing `uniqueGuests` (normalized to match stored attendee emails) would make the recipient classification accurate.

title: Email send failure is silently swallowed with console.log
body: The catch block is `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` — the caught `err` is discarded, no logger is used, and the mutation still returns success ("Guests added"). Operators get no signal (no structured log, no error) when guest notification emails fail, making delivery problems undiagnosable. At minimum log the error via the `logger` used elsewhere in the codebase and include the booking id.

title: Hardcoded, untranslated user-facing string "Remove email"
body: The tooltip content in the MultiEmail component is the literal string `"Remove email"` while every other user-facing string in the new components goes through `t()` / `useLocale()`. Non-English users will see English text for this tooltip. It should use `t("remove_email")` (with the key added to common.json), consistent with the rest of the file.

title: Error toast renders raw TRPC error codes and the fallback message is unreachable
body: `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`` produces strings like "BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid" or "undefined: ..." when `err.data` is missing, exposing internal error codes to users. Additionally, `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` never falls back because a template literal is always truthy, so the newly added "unable_to_add_guests" locale string is dead code. Errors that aren't translation keys (e.g. network failures) will also be passed to `t()` verbatim. The message should be mapped from known error codes to translated, human-readable text.

title: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so team admins are incorrectly denied
body: The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, ...)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, ...))`. The `&&` means a user must be BOTH an admin and an owner of the booking's team. A team admin who is not the owner (the common case for teams with a separate owner) fails this check and gets a FORBIDDEN error unless they happen to also be the organizer or an attendee, even though the check is clearly meant to allow either role (the name says 'Or'). The condition should use `||`.

title: EventManager is constructed with the requesting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
body: The handler explicitly allows any attendee of the booking to add guests (`isAttendee` check passes), but then builds `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` from `ctx.user` (the requester) and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. When the requester is an attendee rather than the organizer, the EventManager runs with the attendee's calendar credentials, which do not own the calendar event for this booking — the calendar update will fail or be attempted against the wrong account. The EventManager should be constructed from the booking's organizer (`booking.user`) and their credentials, not the requesting user.

title: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check is bypassable via letter case
body: The blacklist entries are lowercased when parsed (`email.toLowerCase()`), but the guest emails being tested are not: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. An email like `Spam@Example.com` will not match a blacklisted `spam@example.com`, so the blacklist is trivially bypassed by changing the case of any character. The same case-sensitivity applies to the duplicate check `guest === attendee.email`, so `Alice@Example.com` can be added when `alice@example.com` is already an attendee. Both comparisons should lowercase the guest email first.

title: No check on booking status — guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings
body: The handler fetches the booking and only checks the requester's identity; it never inspects `booking.status` or `booking.endTime`. A user can add guests (and trigger calendar updates plus emails to every attendee) for a CANCELLED or REJECTED booking, which is nonsensical and confusing to recipients. The query/authorization block should reject bookings whose status is not ACCEPTED (or at minimum not CANCELLED/REJECTED), and consider whether adding guests to already-ended bookings should be allowed.

title: No upper bound on the number of guests — email-bombing / spam vector
body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max(...)` limit. Any authorized user (including any attendee of a booking, per the handler's permission check) can submit thousands of emails in one request. Each request causes `createMany` of that many attendee rows and, via `sendAddGuestsEmails`, an email to every existing attendee plus a 'scheduled' email to every new 'guest'. This is a trivially abusable mass-email/spam vector (the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS env var only helps if pre-configured). Add a sane maximum to the schema.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw input instead of the filtered uniqueGuests list
body: The handler carefully computes `uniqueGuests` (excluding emails already on the booking and blacklisted ones) but then calls `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original, unfiltered input. Any email in the request that was already an attendee (and thus filtered out of the DB write) still appears in `newGuests`, so in `sendAddGuestsEmails` that existing attendee matches `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` and receives a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` — a duplicate 'booking scheduled' email — instead of the intended guests-added notification. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

title: New-guest detection in sendAddGuestsEmails is case-sensitive
body: `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` compares emails with exact string matching, but email addresses are case-insensitive in practice and are stored/normalized inconsistently. If the guest email supplied by the user differs in case from the value written to the attendees table (or vice versa), a newly added guest will be misclassified and receive the 'guests added' notification meant for existing attendees rather than their own 'scheduled' email (which contains their join details as a new participant). Normalize both sides to lowercase before comparing.

title: Caught error is swallowed with a console.log that omits the error object
body: The `catch (err)` around `sendAddGuestsEmails` only logs the constant string `"Error sending AddGuestsEmails"` — `err` is never logged, so email delivery failures (bad SMTP config, template rendering errors, etc.) are completely undiagnosable in production while the handler still returns success ("Guests added"). At minimum log the error (ideally via the project logger, not console.log).

title: isInvalidEmail error state is never cleared on retry
body: When validation fails, `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` shows the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error. But the flag is only reset by the Cancel button or a successful mutation. If the user corrects the emails and clicks Add again, the request is sent while the stale error message remains visible until the dialog closes, and if the dialog is reopened via the menu (without Cancel), the previous error is still shown. Clear `isInvalidEmail(false)` at the start of `handleAdd` (or when the value changes / dialog opens).

title: No tests for the new addGuests handler, schema, or permission logic
body: This PR adds a new tRPC mutation with non-trivial authorization (organizer vs. attendee vs. team admin/owner), blacklist filtering, deduplication against existing attendees, DB writes, calendar updates, and email fan-out — but includes no unit or integration tests. The kinds of bugs present in this diff (the `&&` vs `||` in the team check, the case-sensitive blacklist comparison, passing `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`) are exactly what a handler test exercising each permission path and filtering rule would have caught. Tests should cover: each allowed/denied role, duplicate attendee emails, blacklisted emails (including mixed case), and non-ACCEPTED booking statuses.

title: Team admin/owner authorization uses && instead of ||
body: The permission check is `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the caller to be BOTH an admin and an owner of the booking's team. The variable is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, so the intent is clearly OR. As written, a team admin who is not the owner (or an owner who is not flagged admin) is denied the ability to add guests with a FORBIDDEN error, even though the surrounding UI exposes the action to them (e.g. `booking.isUserTeamAdminOrOwner` elsewhere in the codebase treats admin OR owner as authorized). Change `&&` to `||`.

title: Guest email blacklist is bypassed via letter casing
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is built by lowercasing each entry of `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` (line 71), but the membership test `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares the raw, un-normalized guest email. A guest email like `Blocked@Example.com` will not match the lowercased `blocked@example.com` entry and will be added anyway, defeating the purpose of the env-var blacklist (which exists to stop unwanted guests from being invited/leaking the meeting link). The guest email must be lowercased before comparison.

title: Duplicate-attendee check is case-sensitive, allowing duplicate attendee records
body: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` compares emails with strict equality. Emails are routinely written with different casing (e.g. a user typing `John@Mail.com` when the attendee was stored as `john@mail.com`), so a guest that already exists on the booking will pass the filter and be inserted a second time via `createMany`, creating duplicate attendee rows. These duplicates then receive duplicate emails and appear twice in the booking UI. Both sides should be compared case-insensitively (as the blacklist comparison a few lines up already assumes).

title: EventManager is constructed with the calling user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
body: `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is used to push the new guests onto the organizer's calendar event, but the EventManager is built from `ctx.user` (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, ... })`). When the caller is an attendee or a team admin rather than the booking's organizer, their credentials do not include the calendar integration that owns the booking's destination calendar, so the calendar event will not be updated (or may target the wrong calendar). The organizer's user record is already fetched (with credentials included in the booking query at line 35-40); the EventManager should be built from `booking.user`, matching how other booking mutations handle this.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw guests list instead of the filtered uniqueGuests
body: The email fan-out is called as `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, using the original request input rather than `uniqueGuests` (the list after removing already-present and blacklisted emails). Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts line 541) the decision of whether an attendee gets `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` is based on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, so stale/blacklisted emails influence which email template existing attendees receive. Additionally that `includes` check is case-sensitive, so a new guest whose email casing differs from the stored attendee row will get the 'guests added' notice instead of the full 'scheduled' email containing their booking details. Pass `uniqueGuests` and compare case-insensitively.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails metadata
body: Every other notification helper in this file (sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails, sendCancelledEmails, etc.) accepts `eventTypeMetadata` and short-circuits on `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`, honoring the organizer's 'disable standard emails' setting. The new `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` takes no metadata parameter and unconditionally emails the organizer, all team members, and all attendees. Organizers who explicitly disabled standard emails for the event type will still receive these guest-added emails, breaking the documented email-suppression contract.

title: Attendees are persisted before the calendar update, leaving unrecoverable partial state on failure
body: The handler writes the new guest rows with `prisma.booking.update` (line 92) and only afterwards calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` (line 165) outside any error handling. If the calendar update throws (e.g. expired OAuth token, as in the previous finding where the wrong user's credentials are used), the tRPC mutation returns an error, but the guests are already persisted in the database. When the user retries with the same emails, `uniqueGuests` becomes empty and they get the misleading `emails_must_be_unique_valid` BAD_REQUEST error, so they cannot recover without changing emails. The DB write and calendar update should be ordered/handled so a calendar failure doesn't strand a half-applied change (e.g. wrap the calendar update in try/catch like the email send, or roll back).

title: Email send failure is swallowed with a console.log that drops the error object
body: The catch block around `sendAddGuestsEmails` only prints the fixed string "Error sending AddGuestsEmails" and discards `err`, so there is no way to diagnose why emails failed (bad mail transport config, template error, etc.). Unlike a UI issue, this is a server-side silent failure with no log entry containing the actual error. Log the error (preferably via the app's logger) and include the error message/stack.

title: Guests array has no min/max constraints
body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` accepts an empty array and an arbitrarily large one. An empty array is not rejected by the schema and instead surfaces later as the misleading `emails_must_be_unique_valid` BAD_REQUEST error, while an unbounded array lets one request create hundreds of attendee rows and trigger hundreds of outbound emails (each existing attendee gets an email per call), which is an email-bombing / resource-exhaustion vector even for an authenticated attendee. Add `.min(1)` and a sensible `.max(...)` (e.g. 10, matching the booking page guest limits).

title: Invalid-email error is never cleared when the user corrects the input
body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true when validation fails, but it is only reset by the Cancel button or a successful mutation; it is never cleared when the user edits the email fields. After one failed attempt, the 'Emails must be unique and valid' warning stays displayed even while the user types valid emails, and remains visible during the subsequent in-flight mutation. Reset `isInvalidEmail` in the `MultiEmail` onChange path (or at the start of `handleAdd`).

title: retryCount-based deletion is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The deleteMany at the top of the handler now has an OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and no `scheduled: false`) filter, unlike the sibling branch. `retryCount` is a column on the shared WorkflowReminder model for all methods (EMAIL, SMS, WHATSAPP), so this SMS cron endpoint will delete any workflow reminder row of any method whose retryCount exceeds 1. Today only this endpoint writes retryCount, but the schema change makes the field available to every reminder type, and any other writer (e.g. a future WhatsApp/email retry mechanism, or manual data fixes) would have its rows silently destroyed by the SMS cron. The condition should be constrained to `method: SMS` (and ideally `scheduled: false`).

title: retryCount incremented via read-modify-write instead of atomic increment
body: Both the failure branch (line 184) and the catch block (line 195) update retryCount with `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, using the value read at the start of the loop. If two cron invocations overlap, or the same reminder is processed concurrently, one increment is lost, so the reminder is retried more times than the intended two before deletion. Prisma supports an atomic form: `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`, which avoids the stale-read problem entirely.

title: Reminders skipped for empty message or missing sendTo never increment retryCount and retry forever
body: The retry-count logic only runs inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)`. When the message resolves to empty/null (e.g. no reminderBody and a non-REMINDER template) or `sendTo` is missing (e.g. the booking has no smsReminderNumber and the action is not SMS_NUMBER), neither the success nor the failure branch executes: the reminder stays `scheduled: false` with retryCount 0 and is picked up again on every cron run until scheduledDate passes. This is exactly the endless-retry behavior the PR description says it is fixing, but for the 'silently skipped' class of failures. The else-branch (or an outer else) should also bump retryCount so these reminders are eventually cleaned up.

title: Failed reminders are hard-deleted, losing audit trail and referenceIds
body: Once a reminder exceeds the retry budget it is removed with `deleteMany`, which destroys the row including workflowStepId, bookingUid and any referenceId. There is no record that a reminder was attempted and abandoned, so neither support nor the booking owner can tell that an SMS reminder was dropped (e.g. due to an invalid phone number), and the failure reason is only available in server console logs. Consider marking the row (e.g. a status/needsAction flag) or logging the deleted reminder ids before removal, rather than silently deleting.

title: No tests for the new retry-count and deletion behavior
body: The PR adds a new state machine (retryCount incremented on Twilio failure or thrown error, rows deleted when retryCount > 1, deletion query rewritten as an OR) but ships no unit or integration tests. Worth covering at minimum: (1) a reminder whose scheduleSMS throws twice is deleted on the following run, (2) a reminder that succeeds after one failure is not deleted, (3) the deleteMany does not remove EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders, and (4) reminders skipped due to missing sendTo do not loop forever.

title: Retry-based deletion is not scoped to unscheduled SMS reminders
body: The new `deleteMany` clause `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` is combined with the original SMS/scheduledDate condition via `OR`, so it applies to any WorkflowReminder row of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) and any state (including already-scheduled ones) whose retryCount exceeds 1. The branch should be constrained the same way the rest of this cron job is: `method: SMS` and `scheduled: false`. Today only this SMS cron increments retryCount, so the damage is latent, but the moment any other code path (e.g. an email reminder retry) writes retryCount, this endpoint will silently delete those reminders, dropping emails/WhatsApp messages that were still pending.

title: Retry counter uses stale read-then-write increments
body: Both retry paths write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, where `reminder.retryCount` was read at query time. If two cron invocations overlap (slow Twilio calls make this plausible), both runs read the same value and both write the same incremented value, losing one failure count. Using a relative increment (`retryCount: { increment: 1 }` in Prisma) would make the counter accurate under concurrency and keep the retry limit behavior (delete after 2 failures) from being extended indefinitely.

title: Reminders with missing sendTo never retry and are never counted
body: The retry counter is only incremented inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)` or in the catch block. When `sendTo` is empty (e.g. booking has no `smsReminderNumber`) or the message body resolves empty, the reminder is silently skipped with no increment, so it stays in the unscheduled set and is re-fetched and re-skipped on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes. This is the exact 'invalid phone number' scenario the PR description targets, and it still results in an unbounded retry loop for that class of reminders; the skip branch should either increment retryCount or otherwise mark the reminder.

title: No tests for the new retry/deletion behavior
body: The PR introduces a stateful behavior change (reminders are permanently deleted after two failed scheduling attempts, plus a new column and migration) but ships no unit or integration tests. There are no tests verifying that a reminder failing twice is deleted, that a reminder failing once is retried and can still succeed, or that successfully scheduled reminders are not affected by the retryCount cleanup. Given this code path silently deletes user-facing reminder data, regression coverage is warranted before merging.

title: retryCount deletion filter is not scoped to SMS and deletes reminders of any method
body: The deleteMany at the top of the handler now includes an OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` without a `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` condition (the first branch has it, this one does not). Any WorkflowReminder row whose retryCount exceeds 1 is deleted, regardless of whether it is an EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminder. Today only this SMS cron increments retryCount, but any future code path (or a WhatsApp/email retry implementation) that bumps retryCount on a non-SMS reminder will have its rows silently destroyed by the SMS cron job, cancelling reminders that were never related to SMS. The branch should be `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` (and ideally also `scheduled: false`).

title: Database update inside the catch block can itself throw, aborting the entire cron run
body: The new code in the catch block performs `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` before the console.log. If that update throws (e.g., the reminder was concurrently deleted by the deleteMany of an overlapping cron run, or a transient DB error), the exception propagates out of the catch and out of the for-loop, so the handler never sends a response (the caller gets a 500) and all remaining unscheduled reminders in the batch are not processed in this run. Previously the catch only logged, so one bad reminder could not break the loop. The update inside the catch should be wrapped in its own try/catch (or the whole per-reminder processing should be isolated) so a single failure cannot abort the batch.

title: Comment no longer matches what the deleteMany does
body: The comment on line 28 says "delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date", but the query now also deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of scheduled date or method. A maintainer reading the comment will misunderstand the destructive scope of this query; update the comment to reflect both conditions.

title: Reminders dropped after two failures with no logging or record of the loss
body: When the deleteMany removes reminders because retryCount > 1, nothing is logged and no record is kept of which bookings lost their reminders. The per-attempt failures only `console.log` the raw error with no reminder id, so after the row is deleted there is no way to audit that an attendee stopped receiving an SMS reminder. Since two consecutive failures can be caused by a transient Twilio outage (the cron may run every few minutes, so both retries can happen during one incident), reminders can be permanently and silently dropped. At minimum, log the ids/count of deleted retry-exhausted reminders.

title: New retryCount predicate in deleteMany cannot use any existing index
body: The existing indexes on WorkflowReminder are on bookingUid, workflowStepId, seatReferenceId, [method, scheduled, scheduledDate] and [cancelled, scheduledDate]. The added `retryCount > 1` OR-branch matches none of these, so the periodic deleteMany will degrade to a sequential scan over the WorkflowReminder table on every cron invocation. As this table accumulates rows over time this adds avoidable load; consider adding an index on retryCount or combining the conditions so the method/scheduledDate index applies.

title: Public findMany() method removed and condition return types changed without updating callers
body: This PR removes the public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method from InsightsBookingService and changes the return type of `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` from `Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` to `Prisma.Sql`. No callers are updated anywhere in this PR, so any production code that calls `service.findMany(...)` or passes these conditions into a Prisma `where` clause (e.g. `where: { AND: [conditions] }`) will break - either a compile error or a runtime query-validation error. Note that the PR description claims only tests were updated because the service "was previously converted", but the diff shows the service conversion, including this API removal, happens in this PR. Before merging, verify every usage of InsightsBookingService in the repo has been updated to the new `getBaseConditions()`/raw-SQL contract, or keep a `findMany` wrapper for backward compatibility.

title: Assertions compare reduce-composed nested Prisma.Sql against flat template literals, and the tests were never executed
body: The PR author explicitly states the test runner failed, so none of these rewritten assertions have been verified. Several of them (team scope at line 296, org scope at line 333, combined filters at line 430) compare a condition the service builds by nesting `Prisma.Sql` objects (e.g. `Prisma.sql\`(${a}) OR (${b})\``, where `.values` contains `[Sql, Sql]` and `.strings` is `['(', ') OR (', ')']`) against a single flat template literal whose `.strings`/`.values` contain the raw scalars. `toEqual` performs deep structural comparison of the `Sql` objects, so unless Prisma flattens nested `Sql` at construction time, these assertions will fail even though the generated SQL is semantically identical. Run the suite before merging; if they fail, compare via a helper that renders both sides to SQL (or compares `.strings`/`.values` recursively after flattening) instead of direct object equality.

title: Caching tests deleted without replacement
body: The previous version of this file had a "Caching" describe block verifying that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` memoize their results on repeated calls. That block was deleted entirely rather than converted to the new Prisma.sql format. The service still implements caching via `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` (insightsBooking.ts lines 84-95), but that behavior now has zero test coverage, so a regression in memoization (e.g. refetching org memberships on every call, or cache invalidation bugs) would go undetected. Re-add equivalent caching tests using the new SQL-object expectations.

title: Org-scope expectation hard-codes array order from unordered DB queries, making the test flaky
body: The org-scope assertion expects the `= ANY(...)` parameter arrays in a specific order ([org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id] and [user.id, user2.id, user3.id]), but the service builds these arrays from `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId` and `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`, which run `findMany` queries without an `orderBy` clause, so the database row order is not guaranteed. Since the new assertions deep-compare the `Prisma.sql` values arrays element-by-element, any different row ordering from Postgres makes the test fail intermittently even though `= ANY` is order-insensitive. Sort the expected IDs (or normalize both sides to sets) in the assertion to make the test deterministic.

title: Public findMany method removed with no caller updates in this PR
body: This PR deletes the `findMany` method from `InsightsBookingService` (it previously ran `prisma.bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany` with the auth/filter conditions merged into the `where` clause) and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. No callers are updated in this PR. Any existing code that constructs `InsightsBookingService` and calls `findMany({ select, ... })` will fail to compile (or fail at runtime in untyped usage), and every caller now has to write its own `$queryRaw` with select/pagination/ordering logic, moving query construction out of the service. Before merging, verify there are zero callers of `findMany` (and of the old constructor option type) across the repo, or update them in this PR.

The PR description explicitly states the tests were never executed ('I encountered test runner configuration issues, so please verify the tests actually pass'). This PR rewrites the authorization logic of an insights service from Prisma where-inputs to hand-built raw SQL fragments (the highest-risk kind of change: security scoping for user/team/org data), and every assertion in this file was changed, yet none of them have been run. Notably, the new assertions compare `Prisma.Sql` objects with `toEqual`, which depends on Prisma's internal representation (own `_strings`/`values` properties), and the final test queries the `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` table, whose population path for bookings created directly via `prisma.booking.create` is unverified. The tests must be executed and confirmed passing before merge rather than delegating verification to the human reviewer checklist.

title: Order-dependent assertion on user ID arrays built from unordered membership queries
body: The org-scope test asserts the exact `Prisma.sql` fragment including `"userId" = ANY(${[testData.user.id, user2.id, user3.id]})`. The service builds this array from `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds` results deduplicated with `Array.from(new Set(...))`, which preserves whatever order the database returns rows in. If the repository query has no deterministic `ORDER BY`, the resulting array order is not guaranteed, and since `toEqual` on the `Prisma.Sql` values array is order-sensitive, this test can flake. The assertion should compare the ID set order-independently (or the service should sort the IDs).

title: Caching tests deleted instead of converted
body: The previous test file had a 'Caching' describe block verifying that `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` return cached results on second call. Those tests were removed rather than updated to the new `Prisma.Sql` return types, even though the caching logic (`cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` with `=== undefined` checks, including the subtle null-vs-undefined distinction for filter conditions) still exists in the service. This leaves a regression-prone behavior (e.g., breaking the null cache by using a falsy check) untested.

title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates the connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in the UI
body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop on success. Unlike `disconnectMutation` in the same component (which invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`), it never refetches/invalidates the `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` query that supplies `cacheUpdatedAt`. `onSuccess` maps to the wrapper's optional `onChanged` prop, which many usages don't provide or which doesn't refetch this query. Result: after successfully deleting cached data, the dropdown keeps showing 'Cache Status / Last updated: ...' for the deleted cache until a full page refresh, and the delete action can be invoked again against already-deleted data. Add the same `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` (or a refetch) to the delete mutation's onSettled.

title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt, so expired cache rows are reported as active cache
body: The groupBy in `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` filters only on `credentialId` and takes `_max.updatedAt`, without any condition on `expiresAt >= now()`. CalendarCache rows are not deleted when they expire (`getCachedAvailability` filters by `expiresAt` at read time, but expired rows linger in the table). Consequence: the UI will show 'Cache Status: Last updated ...' and a 'Delete cached data' action for credentials whose cache is entirely expired and never served, misleading users about the state of the cache. Filter out expired rows (e.g. `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }`) in the where clause.

title: updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object; the updatedAt bump is purely implicit and fragile
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` payload. The code comment says the intent is to 'Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt', but no field is set explicitly; the effect relies entirely on Prisma's implicit `@updatedAt` behavior on an empty update, which varies by Prisma version (some versions reject empty update data with a validation error, and if the model's column lacks `@updatedAt` this is a silent no-op). If it throws, it breaks `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`, which is called from the `unwatchCalendar` flow after cache repopulation. Pass the intent explicitly (e.g. `data: { updatedAt: new Date() }`) and verify it works against the Prisma version in use.

title: Cache timestamp formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of the user's locale
body: The component calls `useLocale()` for all translated strings but formats `cacheUpdatedAt` with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`. Non-English users will see a mixed-language UI with US-style dates (MM/DD/YYYY), which is ambiguous in most of the world (e.g. 03/04/2025 reads as March 4 vs 3 April). Use the locale from `useLocale()` (falling back appropriately) as the first argument to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId on selected calendars, tightening the contract for all callers
body: The `UserWithCalendars` type's `allSelectedCalendars`/`userLevelSelectedCalendars` now `Pick` `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` from SelectedCalendar. Every caller that constructs this type must now select those columns (the PR already had to patch `findUnlockedUserForSession` in user.ts to compile), including external consumers such as platform-libraries that build users with selected calendars. Per the PR's own notes, `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not even displayed in the frontend, so this widening forces extra DB columns to be selected on every session-user fetch for no consumer. If the fields aren't required by this feature, revert the type to avoid the breaking contract; if they are, verify all call sites (including platform packages) were updated.

title: sed -i '' syntax is macOS-only and fails on GNU/Linux
body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E "s|...|...|"` which is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed (standard on Linux CI/dev containers), the empty-string argument after `-i` is not treated as an in-place suffix, so sed interprets `''` as the script and the substitution expression as a filename, causing the command to fail with an error and leaving `.env` unmodified (or worse, running the wrong edit). Use a portable approach (e.g. `sed -i.bak` + remove the backup, or detect the OS), since this script is committed to the shared repo.

title: Handler throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError, producing an opaque 500 to clients
body: `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` in a tRPC mutation surfaces as an unhandled INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR; in production the message may be stripped, and the client cannot distinguish 'not found' from 'unauthorized'. The rest of the codebase's tRPC handlers throw `TRPCError` with proper codes (e.g. `new TRPCError({ code: "UNAUTHORIZED" | "NOT_FOUND" })`). The client UI then only shows the generic 'error_deleting_cache' toast regardless of cause. Use TRPCError so the failure is properly coded and consistent with the surrounding routers.

title: No tests for the new cache-status query, deleteCache handler, or the new UI component
body: This PR adds a new repository method (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, including its groupBy/max semantics and how it interacts with expired rows), a new tRPC mutation (`deleteCache.handler`, including its ownership check), and a new interactive component (CredentialActionsDropdown with two destructive actions), but ships no unit or e2e tests for any of them. The PR description itself notes local end-to-end verification was not possible. At minimum, add unit tests for the credential-ownership/authorization path of deleteCacheHandler (e.g. a credential belonging to another user is rejected) and for getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, since these guard data deletion.

title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates the connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in the UI
body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only calls the optional `onSuccess?.()` prop (mapped to `onChanged`, which is undefined for most usages such as the installed-apps page) and never invalidates `trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`.
