Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, which invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`, the delete-cache flow has no cache invalidation. Since the wrapper's query is configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, after a user successfully deletes cached data the toast says 'Cache deleted successfully' but the dropdown keeps showing the old 'Cache Status / Last updated' entry and the 'Delete cached data' action until a full page reload. Fix by adding an `onSettled` that invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`.

title: Exported UserWithCalendars type now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId fields that the function never uses, breaking consumers
body: The exported `UserWithCalendars` type now requires `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on every entry of `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars`, but neither field is read anywhere in `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb`. This is a breaking contract change for an exported type (the file even notes it is the 'Legacy export for @calcom/platform-libraries'): any caller that constructs a user object with selected calendars lacking these two fields now fails to compile. The ripple is already visible in this PR, which had to add `updatedAt`/`googleChannelId` to the `findUnlockedUserForSession` Prisma select purely to satisfy the new type. If the fields aren't needed here, revert the type (and the user.ts select change); if they are needed for a future feature, that should land with the code that uses them.

title: Cache timestamp formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of the user's locale
body: The component calls `useLocale()` for all its strings but then formats the cache timestamp with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })`. All users, regardless of their configured locale, will see the date/time in US English format (e.g. month/day ordering). The formatter should use the locale from `useLocale()` (or the browser default) so the display matches the rest of the localized UI.

title: Handler instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository directly, bypassing the mock used when the calendar-cache feature is disabled
body: `connectedCalendarsHandler` does `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of going through the `CalendarCache.init(...)` factory that the rest of the codebase (e.g. GoogleCalendarService) uses to select between the real repository and `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock`. On deployments where the calendar-cache feature is disabled, the real repository is still used, so an extra `groupBy` query against the `CalendarCache` table runs on every connectedCalendars request even though the rest of the app deliberately avoids touching that table. `deleteCache.handler.ts` similarly calls `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` directly, leaving the mock's `deleteManyByCredential` dead code. Use the factory/abstraction so behavior stays consistent when the feature is off.

title: No tests for the new deleteCache mutation, its authorization check, or getCacheStatusByCredentialIds
body: This PR adds a destructive mutation (`deleteCache` performs `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany`), a new repository query (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), and a new UI component, but ships no tests. The authorization path (credential belonging to the requesting user vs. 'Credential not found or access denied') and the credentialId→cache-status mapping used by the UI are exactly the kind of logic that regress silently. At minimum, add unit tests for the handler covering: valid own-credential deletion, another user's credentialId being rejected, and a non-existent credentialId; plus a test for `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` grouping/max behavior (including credentials with multiple cache rows and credentials with none).

title: Cache status includes expired cache rows, so 'Last updated' can be shown for a cache that is never served
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows by credentialId with no filter on `expiresAt`, while the read path (`getCachedAvailability`) only serves rows with `expiresAt >= now`. If a credential's cache entries have all expired (the caching TTL is one month) and were not cleaned up, the UI will still show a 'Cache Status / Last updated' entry and a 'Delete cached data' action for data that is effectively dead. Either filter the groupBy on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` so the status reflects served cache, or make the UI distinguish expired from live cache.

title: Buttons nested inside DropdownMenuItem produce invalid ARIA menu structure
body: The dropdown items wrap a `DropdownItem` (renders a `<button>`) inside a `DropdownMenuItem` (renders a `role="menuitem"` element), and the 'Cache Status' block is also rendered as a selectable `DropdownMenuItem` even though activating it does nothing. Nesting an interactive button inside an element with `role="menuitem"` is an ARIA violation (interactive content must not be a descendant of a menuitem), and screen-reader/keyboard users may be unable to activate the inner buttons or may be misled by the non-functional 'Cache Status' item. Render the destructive actions directly as menu items and the status block as a non-interactive label/group within the menu content.

title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only and fails on Linux
body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E "s|...|...|" "$ENV_FILE"`, which is the macOS/BSD syntax for in-place editing. On GNU/Linux (and in most CI containers), `sed -i` does not accept a separate empty suffix argument, so the command fails with `sed: can't read : No such file or directory` and the `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` in `.env` is never updated. Use a portable approach (e.g. `sed -i.bak` plus cleanup, or `sed -E ... > tmp && mv tmp "$ENV_FILE"`). Also note `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the current working directory, so running the script from any directory other than `scripts/` silently creates/updates the wrong .env file.

title: Cache status never resolves for delegated (in-memory) credentials
body: The cache status is looked up with `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(connectedCalendars.map(cal => cal.credentialId))`, but for delegated Google Calendar connections the connectedCalendar.credentialId is a synthetic negative in-memory id (see `isInMemoryDelegationCredential` in the cache repository, and the userId+key based lookup in `getCachedAvailability`). CalendarCache rows for delegated users are stored/retrieved keyed by userId, not by that credentialId, so the groupBy on these ids returns nothing and `cacheUpdatedAt` will always be null. Since calendar cache is primarily a team/organization (delegation) feature, the new cache status and delete-cache UI will silently never appear for the main audience of this feature. The status query needs a userId-based path (mirroring `getCachedAvailability`) to cover delegated credentials.

title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars, leaving stale cache status
body: After a successful `trpc.viewer.calendars.deleteCache` call, only `onSuccess?.()` (the parent's `onChanged`) is invoked. Unlike the sibling `disconnectMutation`, which explicitly invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`, the deleteCache mutation never invalidates that query. `onChanged` in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` is the caller's callback and does not refetch the tRPC `connectedCalendars` query, so after deleting the cache the 'Cache Status' row and 'Last updated' timestamp remain visible until a manual page refresh, contradicting the success toast.

title: Cache timestamp formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale
body: The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` instead of the user's locale. The component already calls `useLocale()`; every other localized string in the dropdown respects the user's language, but the date will always render in US English format (e.g. '12/25/2025, 3:00 PM') for all users, which is wrong for non-US locales and inconsistent with the rest of the UI.

title: Cache status includes expired cache rows
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups CalendarCache rows by credentialId with no `expiresAt` filter. `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows where `expiresAt >= now`, so a cache that expired over a month ago (and is no longer used for availability lookups) will still report a `updatedAt` value. The UI will then show a 'Cache Status' with a stale 'Last updated' time and a 'Delete cached data' action for data that is effectively already gone, telling the user they have an active cache when they don't. The where clause should include `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to match what the cache actually serves.

title: deleteCache throws generic Error instead of TRPCError
body: When the credential lookup fails, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. In a tRPC procedure this surfaces to the client as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR with the message potentially logged as an unexpected server error, rather than a typed TRPCError (e.g. UNAUTHORIZED/NOT_FOUND) like the other handlers in this router use. The client cannot distinguish authorization failure from a real server fault, and the message conflates two different conditions ('not found' vs 'access denied'). Use `TRPCError` with an appropriate code.

title: No tests for the new cache-status and delete-cache code paths
body: This PR adds a new tRPC mutation (`deleteCache`), a new repository method (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), a new repository method (`updateManyByCredentialId`), a Prisma schema change, and a new UI component, but includes no tests at all: no test for the authorization check in `deleteCacheHandler` (e.g. that a user cannot delete another user's cache by passing an arbitrary credentialId), no test that `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` returns the max updatedAt per credential, and no test for `updateManyByCredentialId`. The PR description itself notes end-to-end verification could not be performed locally, making the missing automated coverage more significant.

title: sed -i '' syntax is macOS-only and fails on Linux
body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E "..." "$ENV_FILE"`. The `sed -i ''` form (empty suffix as separate argument) only works on BSD/macOS sed; on GNU/Linux sed (used by most CI and dev containers) it fails with 'can't read : No such file or directory' because the empty string is treated as a filename. The update of GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL will error out on Linux. Also note this development-only tunnel script appears unrelated to the feature in this PR and adds maintenance surface to the repo.

title: dev:cron now depends on unpinned 'npx tsx' that is not a declared dependency
body: The `dev:cron` script was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not present in devDependencies (only `ts-node` is). With npx, tsx will be fetched/ad-hoc resolved at run time (requiring network access and giving an unpinned version), or fail in offline/restricted environments. If tsx is the intended runner it should be added to devDependencies with a pinned version; also this change is unrelated to the calendar cache feature and shouldn't ride along in this PR.

title: Reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget; handler returns before cancellation is persisted
body: In handleCancelBooking.ts (lines 485-493) `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async functions invoked inside a `forEach` without being awaited, and the request responds immediately afterwards. All of the new cancellation logic (marking the WorkflowReminder row `cancelled: true`, deleting unscheduled rows, calling SendGrid/Twilio) therefore runs after the response has been sent. On serverless platforms (cal.com runs on Vercel) background work after the response is not guaranteed to complete; if the function is frozen or recycled the reminders are never marked cancelled and the emails/SMS are still sent for the cancelled booking — exactly the bug this PR is meant to fix. The same unawaited pattern exists in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx lines 488-494 (requestReschedule) and packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts lines 966-972 (reschedule path, which is even wrapped in a try/catch that can never catch anything because the promises are never awaited). These calls should be collected and awaited before returning.

title: Cancellations within the last cron interval before the send date are still too late
body: Booking cancellation only sets `cancelled: true` on the WorkflowReminder; the actual SendGrid cancellation happens in this cron job, but only for reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour, and the cron runs every 15 minutes. If a booking is cancelled when its reminder's `scheduledDate` is less than one cron interval away, the next cron run happens after the email has already been sent. Worse, the `deleteMany` at the top of the handler (lines 34-41) deletes all EMAIL reminders with `scheduledDate <= now` — including ones marked `cancelled: true` that were never cancelled at SendGrid — so the missed cancellation is silently cleaned up with no retry and no error. Consider using the `immediateDelete` path (already implemented and used for reschedules) for reminders whose `scheduledDate` is imminent, or at minimum cancelling reminders whose date has just passed instead of deleting them.

title: immediateDelete branch leaves no persistent state and no retry on failure
body: When `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is called with `immediateDelete: true` and a `referenceId`, it POSTs the cancel to SendGrid and returns without deleting the row or setting `cancelled: true`. If the SendGrid request fails (e.g. the 100-pending-cancellations limit this PR describes, a network error, or an already-processed batch), the error is swallowed by the catch and the reminder row is left with `scheduled: true` and `cancelled` unset — so the cron-based retry mechanism will never pick it up and the email is still sent. For comparison, the non-immediate path at least persists `cancelled: true` so the cron retries. The immediate path should also mark the row (e.g. set `cancelled: true` before the request, or keep the row on failure) so a failed cancellation is recoverable. This path is used by the reschedule flow in handleNewBooking.ts, so a failed cancel here means the attendee gets a reminder for the old booking time.

title: One failed SendGrid cancellation aborts all remaining cancellations in the cron run
body: In the cancellation loop (lines 53-77) each `client.request` cancel call is awaited inside a single try/catch that wraps the whole loop, and the prisma deletes are only executed after the loop completes. If any single cancel request throws (invalid batch id, rate limit, already-processed batch — e.g. batches created for EMAIL_ADDRESS steps where no message was ever sent), the exception jumps straight to the catch: none of the remaining reminders in `remindersToCancel` are cancelled at SendGrid, and none of the DB deletes run. Since all of these reminders have `scheduledDate` within the next hour, they will be sent even though their bookings were cancelled. Each cancel/delete should be handled in its own try/catch so one bad batch id cannot block the rest.

title: Race: booking cancelled while cron is scheduling its reminder still results in the email being sent
body: The cron fetches all unscheduled reminders at line 80 and then iterates them, calling `sgMail.send` (line 196) before updating the row with the batch id (line 211). If a booking is cancelled while this loop is running (the loop performs multiple awaits per reminder and can easily run for minutes with many reminders), the cancel path deletes the reminder row (the `!referenceId` branch of `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`), but the cron has already read the row into memory and still sends the email. The subsequent `prisma.workflowReminder.update` fails with P2025, which is only caught and logged, and the batch reference is never stored, so the sent email cannot be cancelled afterwards. The handler should re-check that the reminder still exists and is not `cancelled` immediately before calling `sgMail.send`, or perform the row update (e.g. claim it) before sending.

title: No tests for the new reminder cancellation logic
body: This PR changes the core cancellation contract (new `cancelled` flag, deferred cron-based SendGrid cancellation, three distinct branches in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, immediate vs. deferred delete semantics across five call sites) but adds no unit or integration tests anywhere in the PR. The behavior has several boundary conditions that regress easily (reminder with null referenceId, immediateDelete flag, cancellation window in the cron, reschedule path). At minimum the branching of `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and the cron's cancel-selection query (`cancelled: true` AND `scheduledDate` within 1 hour) should be covered by tests.

title: Reminder cancellation calls are fire-and-forget; promises are never awaited
body: In handleCancelBooking.ts (lines 485-493) the loop calls the async functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside a synchronous forEach without awaiting them. The subsequent `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` does not include these promises. On serverless/short-lived runtimes (e.g. Vercel functions) the response can be returned and the execution frozen before the SendGrid cancel request or the `workflowReminder.update({cancelled: true})` / delete queries run, so the reminder is never cancelled and the workflow email is still sent — exactly the bug this PR aims to fix. The same un-awaited pattern exists in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx (requestReschedule, lines 488-494) and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx (lines 212-218, 376-382, 519-525, 574-580), where the previous code at least awaited the Prisma deletions via Promise.all.

title: try/catch around async forEach cannot catch rejection; also uses the immediate SendGrid cancel the PR says is broken
body: Two problems in the new block at lines 963-975: (1) The `try { originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...) }) } catch` cannot catch anything, because the async function calls are not awaited inside a synchronous forEach — any real rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection and the `log.error("Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders")` path is dead code. (2) It calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder with `immediateDelete: true`, which performs the immediate POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends cancel. Per the PR description, this is precisely the operation that fails once 100 pending cancellations accumulate (pending cancellations persist in scheduled_sends until the send date, up to 72h away for these reminders). Reschedules are a common operation, so the failure mode described in issue #7225 can re-occur through this path; the deferred `cancelled: true` mechanism is not used here.

title: Cron cancellation window leaves last-minute cancellations uncancelled
body: The new cancellation flow only marks `cancelled: true` at booking-cancel time and relies on this cron (runs every 15 minutes) to actually cancel, and the cron only picks reminders with `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. If a booking is cancelled less than ~15 minutes before its reminder's send time (e.g. cancelled 5 minutes before the scheduled email goes out), the flag is set but the next cron run happens after the email has already been sent. The previous code attempted the SendGrid cancellation synchronously at cancel time, so this is a regression window in which cancelled bookings still receive reminder emails — the exact symptom of #7225.

title: One failed SendGrid request aborts cancelling all remaining reminders in the run
body: In the cancellation loop (lines 56-73) the `await client.request(...)` calls are sequential inside a single try block that wraps the whole loop. If the SendGrid request for one reminder fails (network error, invalid/expired batch_id, or a null referenceId since the query at lines 44-51 does not filter `referenceId: null`), the exception jumps to the outer catch and none of the remaining reminders in `remindersToCancel` are cancelled in this run. Their DB rows are also not deleted (Promise.all is skipped), so they are retried only on the next cron run up to 15 minutes later, which may be after their send time. Each reminder should be cancelled and deleted independently with per-item error handling.

title: immediateDelete path cancels in SendGrid but leaves the workflowReminder row stale
body: In deleteScheduledEmailReminder, the `immediateDelete` branch (lines 213-223) POSTs the cancellation to SendGrid and returns without deleting the workflowReminder row and without setting `cancelled: true`. In handleNewBooking.ts (reschedule path, line 968) this is called on the previous booking's reminders, and that old booking continues to exist with status CANCELLED — its reminder rows keep `scheduled: true` with a live-looking referenceId until the cron's past-due cleanup (`scheduledDate <= now`) deletes them up to 72h later. The database no longer reflects reality during that period: any code inspecting workflowReminders (e.g. the workflow edit flow, which re-cancels these rows) operates on reminders that were already cancelled, and there is no durable record that they were cancelled. The row should be deleted (or at least marked cancelled) in this branch, as the SMS counterpart deleteScheduledSMSReminder does.

title: No tests for the new reminder cancellation logic
body: The PR changes the core cancellation contract (new `cancelled` flag on WorkflowReminder, deferred cancellation via cron, changed signatures of deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder) across six call sites, but adds no unit or integration tests. The timing-sensitive behavior (cron interval vs. 1-hour window vs. scheduled send time, immediate vs. deferred cancellation, cleanup of cancelled rows) is exactly the kind of logic that regressed before (PR #6991 was wrong and went unnoticed). At minimum, tests should cover: cancelling a booking marks EMAIL reminders cancelled and deletes SMS/unscheduled rows; the cron cancels only due cancelled reminders and deletes them afterwards; reminders with null referenceId are handled.

title: Reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget; the 'cancelled' DB update can be lost
body: In handleCancelBooking, the loop `updatedBookings.forEach((booking) => { booking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId); ... }) })` calls async functions without awaiting them, and the resulting promises are not added to `prismaPromises` (the old code collected the reminder deletes and awaited them via `Promise.all`). `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` now performs a Prisma `update` setting `cancelled: true` (or a `delete` when there is no referenceId), and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` performs a Twilio call plus a DB delete. If the request handler returns before these complete (which is a real risk on serverless), those writes never happen, the reminder stays `scheduled: true` with `cancelled` unset, the cron never picks it up, and the email is sent for the cancelled booking — exactly the bug this PR is meant to fix. The cancellation calls should be collected and awaited before responding.

title: Reschedule reminder cancellation is unawaited and the surrounding try/catch is dead code
body: In the reschedule branch of handleNewBooking, `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true); ... })` fires async operations (SendGrid cancel request via `client.request`, Twilio cancel, Prisma delete) without awaiting any of them. The surrounding `try { ... } catch (error) { log.error(...) }` can never catch anything because no promise is awaited inside it. If the handler responds before these complete (serverless), the old booking's scheduled email/SMS is never cancelled in SendGrid/Twilio, and the reminder rows are never removed, so reminders for the superseded booking are still delivered. Await the promises (e.g. `await Promise.all(...)`) and let the try/catch actually guard them.

title: requestReschedule cancels reminders without awaiting the async delete calls
body: In the `requestReschedule` mutation, `bookingToReschedule.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId); ... })` invokes async functions whose promises are discarded. The old code gathered the DB deletes and awaited them with `Promise.all(remindersToDelete)`. Now the Prisma write that marks the email reminder `cancelled: true` (or deletes the row when unscheduled) and the Twilio/DB work in `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` may not complete before the mutation returns; on serverless the work can be killed entirely, leaving the reminder active so the attendee still receives a reminder for a booking that was cancelled pending reschedule.

title: Workflow update fires reminder cancellations in unawaited forEach callbacks
body: In the `update` mutation, `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); })` (and the same pattern at the removed-event-types loop around line 376 and the deleted-step loop around line 519) never awaits the async callbacks. These calls now perform DB writes (setting `cancelled: true`, deleting rows) and network calls (SendGrid/Twilio), so their outcome is nondeterministic relative to the rest of the mutation and the HTTP response; on serverless the pending work may be terminated before executing. This means reminders for edited steps / disabled event types can remain scheduled and still be sent. Collect and await the promises.

title: immediateDelete path has no retry and reintroduces the 100 pending-cancellation limit
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete=true)` (used on reschedule in handleNewBooking, workflow deletion, and step deletion/edit) immediately POSTs a cancellation to SendGrid and returns without deleting the row or marking it `cancelled: true`. Two problems: (1) if the SendGrid request fails — including failure caused by SendGrid's cap of 100 pending cancellations, which is the very issue this PR is meant to solve, since these immediate cancels can be for emails scheduled up to 72 hours out — the error is only console.logged, the DB row keeps `scheduled: true` and `cancelled` unset, and the cron in scheduleEmailReminders will never retry the cancellation, so the email is sent anyway. (2) Even on success, the workflowReminder row is left in the DB (neither deleted nor marked cancelled), relying on the cron's past-dated `deleteMany` for cleanup. A failure here should at minimum fall back to marking the reminder `cancelled: true` so the cron retries.

title: Cancellations are deferred to the next cron run, so reminders sending within ~15 minutes are still sent
body: When a booking is cancelled, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` only sets `cancelled: true` and relies on this cron (running every 15 minutes) to actually cancel the SendGrid batch, and only for reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour. If a reminder's `scheduledDate` (the SendGrid `send_at`) falls within the window between the cancellation request and the next cron execution (up to 15 minutes later), the cron runs after the email has already been sent, and the SendGrid cancel arrives too late. `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` should cancel immediately when `scheduledDate` is within the cron interval (or within the hour, matching the cron's own lookahead) instead of always deferring to the cron.

title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation loop and skips all DB deletes
body: In the new cancellation block of the cron, the `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop awaits `client.request(...)` inside a single outer try/catch. If any single SendGrid cancellation request throws (invalid batch id, rate limit, network error), the loop aborts immediately: none of the remaining cancelled reminders are cancelled in SendGrid, and — because Prisma query builders are lazy and only execute when awaited — none of the already-collected `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` calls in `workflowRemindersToDelete` execute either. Since the failing reminder stays in the result set every run, it can permanently block cancellation of all reminders that come after it, causing their emails to be sent for cancelled bookings. Wrap the SendGrid request and the corresponding delete in a per-reminder try/catch.

title: No tests cover the new cancellation lifecycle
body: This PR changes the core cancellation semantics of workflow reminders (new `cancelled` flag, deferred cancellation via cron, changed signatures of `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` now taking `reminderId` and nullable `referenceId`), but adds no unit or integration tests. The reworked paths include several edge cases that are easy to regress: reminders with `referenceId === null`, the `immediateDelete` flag, SendGrid failure handling, and the cron's cancel-then-delete ordering. At minimum, tests for `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`'s three branches and the cron's cancellation query/loop would guard the fix for the issue this PR addresses.

title: Recurring-booking cancellation now defers calendar deletions past Promise.all, leaving external events orphaned
body: In the recurring-events branch of the cancellation handler, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` now contains an `await getCalendar(credential)`. Because `forEach` does not await the async callback, the `apiDeletes.push(calendar?.deleteEvent(...))` calls only execute after the await resolves, i.e. after `forEach` has returned. Previously `getCalendar` was synchronous, so the deleteEvent promises were pushed synchronously and were included in the `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at the end of the handler. After this change `apiDeletes` is still empty when `Promise.all` runs, so the external calendar events of cancelled recurring bookings are deleted in an unawaited background task that races with the deletion of the booking references and the HTTP response; failures surface as unhandled rejections and the calendar entries can be left orphaned. The loop must be awaited (e.g. `for...of` with await, or Promise.all over the credentials) before calling Promise.all.

title: `forEach(async ...)` makes event deletion fire-and-forget and bypasses the surrounding try/catch
body: The reschedule handler wraps `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` in a try/catch, but `forEach` ignores the returned promises. Since the callback now awaits `getCalendar(...)`, the subsequent `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` / `deleteMeeting(...)` calls are scheduled only after the await resolves, so (a) the function returns and the reschedule email is sent before the external calendar/video events are actually deleted, and (b) any error thrown while loading the app module or deleting the event is not caught by the surrounding try/catch and becomes an unhandled promise rejection. The loop should be awaited, e.g. `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))`.

title: `forEach(async ...)` makes event deletion fire-and-forget and bypasses the surrounding try/catch
body: Same defect as in vital/lib/reschedule.ts: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` inside a try/catch. `forEach` does not await the async callbacks, so after `await getCalendar(...)` the `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` / `deleteMeeting(...)` calls run detached from the handler: the booking is marked cancelled and the reschedule email sent before the external events are deleted, and any error (module load failure, calendar API failure) escapes the try/catch as an unhandled promise rejection instead of being logged by it. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`.

title: requestReschedule deletes calendar/video events via unawaited `forEach(async ...)`
body: In the `requestReschedule` mutation, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` is never awaited. `forEach` discards the async callbacks, so the deletion of the organizer's external calendar events and video meetings happens in the background after the mutation has already responded and after the booking row has been marked CANCELLED. Failures are silently lost as unhandled rejections, and a user can be told the reschedule request succeeded even though their calendar event was never removed (or is removed much later). Await the deletions, e.g. with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.

title: Dynamic imports are invoked eagerly, defeating the lazy-loading purpose of the change
body: The object literal evaluates `import("./applecalendar")`, `import("./caldavcalendar")`, etc. at module-evaluation time. Dynamic `import()` starts fetching/loading the module as soon as the expression is evaluated, so merely importing `@calcom/app-store` (which videoClient, CalendarManager, the booking handlers, etc. all do) kicks off loading of all 28 app packages immediately — only the binding access is deferred. On the server this means every app dependency is loaded on cold start regardless of which integrations a request uses, and in any client bundle that pulls this module all app chunks are requested at startup. To actually load apps on demand, the store should hold thunks (`applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) that are invoked only for the needed app. Additionally, if one of these eagerly-started imports rejects and that key is never awaited, it surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection.

title: getCalendarCredentials stores an unawaited promise that can reject before it is ever awaited
body: `getCalendarCredentials` calls the now-async `getCalendar(credential)` without awaiting and stores the promise in the returned structure; only `getConnectedCalendars` later awaits it inside its try/catch. If `getConnectedCalendars` is not called for a given set of credentials (or is called much later), a rejected import/app-load promise sits unhandled in the meantime, producing unhandled-rejection warnings that can terminate the Node process under default settings. Either await the promise at creation, or attach a no-op catch until it is consumed.

title: No tests cover the sync-to-async appStore/getCalendar contract change
body: This PR changes a widely consumed contract: `appStore[key]` and `getCalendar(...)` now return Promises instead of values, and several call sites were converted by hand (some incorrectly, as the unawaited `forEach(async ...)` sites show). There are no accompanying tests verifying that calendar/video/payment app resolution still works end-to-end (e.g. getCalendar returns a CalendarService for a `google_calendar` credential, getVideoAdapters resolves adapters, payment refund/delete paths resolve the PaymentService). Given that a missed await produces silently broken integrations rather than type errors at runtime call sites like `forEach`, at minimum regression tests for getCalendar, getVideoAdapters, and the booking cancellation/reschedule flows should be added before merging.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions are fire-and-forget after async change
body: In the `allRemainingBookings` recurring-event branch, the credentials are iterated with `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... })`. Because the callback is now async (it awaits `getCalendar`), it returns before any deletion happens, and nothing awaits the resulting promises. Consequences: (1) `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)` at line 467 executes only after `await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` resolves, so by the time the handler reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) these entries have not been pushed and are never awaited; (2) the handler then deletes the booking references from the DB and returns, so in a serverless environment the function can freeze before the external calendar events for the remaining recurring occurrences are deleted, leaving orphaned events on users' calendars with no DB reference left to retry. This branch must be converted to an awaited loop (like the non-recurring branch in this same PR already was).

title: forEach(async ...) makes deletion errors unhandled and unawaited
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` is never awaited. The surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections from an async forEach callback, so any failure in the dynamic app import, `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection (which crashes Node by default). Additionally, the function returns `true` and sends the reschedule email before the calendar/video deletions have completed, so in a serverless deployment the deletions may never run. The identical pattern exists in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx line 553; all three should use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` instead.

title: forEach(async ...) makes deletion errors unhandled and unawaited
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` is never awaited. The surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections from an async forEach callback, so failures in the dynamic import, `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` become unhandled promise rejections (crashing Node by default). The function also returns and sends the reschedule email before the external calendar/video events are actually deleted, which in a serverless environment means the deletions may never complete. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.

title: requestReschedule deletions are fire-and-forget async forEach
body: In the `requestReschedule` mutation, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` is not awaited. The promises returned by the async callback are discarded, so: rejections from the dynamic app import or the calendar/video deletion surface as unhandled promise rejections (process-crashing in Node), and the mutation returns (and the reschedule email/webhook fire) before the organizer's external calendar events are actually deleted — in a serverless deployment the function can be frozen before the deletions run, leaving the old events on attendees' calendars even though the booking was already marked CANCELLED in the DB.

title: Eagerly evaluated import() calls defeat the purpose of lazy loading
body: The object literal `{ applecalendar: import("./applecalendar"), ... }` invokes every `import()` at module-evaluation time. As soon as any module imports `@calcom/app-store` (e.g. `packages/core/videoClient.ts`, `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, `handleCancelBooking.ts` — all core booking-flow modules), all ~30 app packages start loading immediately. This means the PR's stated goal ("Async imports of all apps") achieves no deferral for the main consumers: memory footprint and module-load work are essentially the same as the previous static imports, while adding promise indirection on every access. To actually defer loading, the entries should be lazy, e.g. `get applecalendar() { return import("./applecalendar"); }` or a `getApp(name)` helper that performs the `import()` only when requested.

title: getCalendarCredentials silently changed to embed an un-awaited Promise in its return value
body: `getCalendarCredentials` is still a synchronous function, but after this PR the `calendar` field of each returned item is a `Promise<Calendar | null>` rather than a `Calendar | null`. The only in-file consumer was updated (`getConnectedCalendars` now does `await item.calendar`), but the function is exported, so every external consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` must now await `calendar` — a silent contract change of a public API. Callers that don't await will get a truthy Promise where they previously got `null` for unsupported calendars, breaking the `if (!calendar)` null-check semantics and producing runtime failures like calling `.listCalendars()` on a Promise. Either await inside `getCalendarCredentials` (make it async) or make the Promise explicit in the return type so the compiler forces all call sites to handle it.

title: `await apiDeletes` awaits an array, not the deletions
body: In the paid-booking cancellation path, `await apiDeletes;` awaits a plain array of promises, which resolves immediately without waiting for any of the deletions. The handler then returns "Booking successfully cancelled" while external calendar-event deletions (which now additionally include dynamic-import latency after this PR) may not have started, so a serverless freeze after the response can leave the paid event on the organizer's calendar. It should be `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)`. This line is pre-existing, but the added async import latency in this PR widens the race window for the code paths feeding `apiDeletes`.

title: Eager import() calls mean all apps load at import time and failed chunks become unhandled rejections
body: The appStore object literal evaluates `import("./x")` for every app as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is first imported, so all ~29 app chunks start loading immediately on any code path that touches appStore — the intended deferral is not achieved for cold starts. Worse, each of these promises is created without a rejection handler: if any app chunk fails to load (a common case on Next.js/Vercel when in-flight requests reference chunks invalidated by a new deploy), the promise for that app rejects before anything awaits it. Since Node 15+, an unhandled rejection crashes the process by default, so one app's failed chunk can take down the whole server even though no request ever used that app. To be genuinely lazy and safe, the store should use getters (e.g. `get stripepayment() { return import("./stripepayment"); }`) so the import (and its promise) is only created when actually requested.

title: async forEach discards deletion promises; reschedule completes before calendar/video events are deleted
body: This PR changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => {...})` to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})`. `Array.forEach` ignores the returned promises, so nothing waits for the `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls. Consequences: (1) `Reschedule` returns `true` and the reschedule email is sent before the external calendar events and video meetings are actually deleted; on a serverless platform the execution context can be frozen after the response, so the deletions may never run and stale events remain on users' calendars; (2) the surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections from these async callbacks, so any failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))` instead.

title: async forEach discards deletion promises; reschedule completes before calendar/video events are deleted
body: This PR changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => {...})` to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})`. `Array.forEach` ignores the returned promises, so nothing waits for the `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls. Consequences: (1) `Reschedule` returns `true` and the reschedule email is sent before the external calendar events and video meetings are actually deleted; on a serverless platform the execution context can be frozen after the response, so the deletions may never run and stale events remain on users' calendars; (2) the surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections from these async callbacks, so any failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))` instead.

title: requestReschedule fires-and-forgets calendar/video deletions via async forEach
body: In the `requestReschedule` mutation, this PR changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => ...)` to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)`. forEach does not await the async callbacks, so the mutation proceeds to send the reschedule-request email and webhooks and returns the response while the old calendar events (`calendar?.deleteEvent`) and video meetings (`deleteMeeting`) are still being — or have not yet begun to be — processed. There is also no try/catch or `.catch()` on these promises, so any deletion failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection. In a serverless environment the function can be suspended after the response, leaving the old calendar events permanently in place. Collect the promises with `.map()` and `await Promise.all(...)` before returning.

title: Recurring-cancellation branch pushes into apiDeletes after awaits, racing the final Promise.all
body: In the recurring-event cancellation branch (lines 458-470), the PR adds `await getCalendar(credential)` inside a `forEach(async (credential) => {...})` that pushes results into `apiDeletes`. Because forEach does not await the callbacks, the handler continues to line 652 (`await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`) while the forEach callbacks are still suspended at their awaits; the Promise.all therefore snapshots a `apiDeletes` array that may be empty or partial, and the cancellation API response is returned before the calendar deletion calls have even been started. The attendee/bookingReference DB deletes then complete while external calendar events are still pending, so a subsequent process freeze or crash leaves external calendars with events that no longer exist in Cal.com. Convert the forEach to an awaited `Promise.all(credentials.map(...))` and push the deletion promises before awaiting them.

title: getCalendarCredentials creates getCalendar promises that are never awaited for non-calendar variants
body: `getCalendarCredentials` now stores the un-awaited `getCalendar(credential)` promise in the returned objects, and only `getConnectedCalendars` awaits `item.calendar`. Two problems: (1) `getCalendar(credential)` is called for every app credential before the `app.variant === "calendar"` filter, so for non-calendar variants a promise is created and immediately discarded — if the app's dynamic import rejects, this is an unhandled rejection (fatal by default on Node 15+); (2) the exported return type of `getCalendarCredentials` silently changed from `calendar: Calendar | null` to `calendar: Promise<Calendar | null>`, a breaking contract change for any caller outside this file that accesses `.calendar` directly (they will now hold a Promise where they expect a service instance). Await the promise inside this function or only construct it for calendar-variant apps, and document/verify all callers.

title: `await apiDeletes` awaits an array, not a promise, in the paid-booking branch
body: In the paid-booking cancellation path, line 617 does `await apiDeletes;`. `apiDeletes` is an array of promises (populated by `deleteMeeting`/`calendar?.deleteEvent` calls which this PR makes asynchronous), not a promise itself, so awaiting it resolves immediately without waiting for any of the contained deletions. The comment says the code deliberately deletes booking references, but the external calendar/video deletions should still be awaited before returning, e.g. `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)`. Since this PR touches the surrounding async deletion logic, this is the place to fix it.

title: No tests accompany the async conversion of booking create/cancel/reschedule flows
body: This PR changes the timing semantics of core booking flows: getCalendar/getVideoAdappers/deleteMeeting became async, appStore lookups are now awaited dynamic imports, and several loops became async forEach. None of these paths (calendar event creation/update/deletion, booking cancellation, reschedule request, payment refund) have accompanying tests added or updated in the PR. Given the fire-and-forget issues this conversion introduces (deletion promises not awaited), at minimum regression tests for cancel/reschedule asserting that external deletions are awaited before the handler resolves should be added before merging.

title: Slots inside a date override bypass the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, when a slot falls on a day that has a date override, `dateOverrideExist` is set to true inside the `dateOverrides.find()` callback, and the callback returns undefined for slots that are *within* the override window. Control then hits `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` and the function returns immediately, before the `busy.every(...)` check at the bottom. Consequence: for any slot covered by a date override, the host's existing bookings and calendar busy times are never consulted, so a host with a date override who already has a conflicting booking (Cal booking or external calendar event) will still be shown as available and can be double-booked. The override check must not short-circuit the busy check.

title: Dayjs object identity comparison `===` is always false, killing the start==end override case
body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly created Dayjs object references, which are always distinct, so this condition never fires (it is dead code). The intent was to detect overrides where start equals end (Cal.com's representation for an unavailable period). Because the check is dead, a slot that starts exactly at such an override's start time fails all the other conditions (`slotEndTime` is not before the start, `slotStartTime` is not after the end), `find` returns undefined, `dateOverrideExist` is true, and the function returns `true` — marking the slot available when the user explicitly blocked it. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `.valueOf()`.

title: Working-hours check computes `end` identical to `start`, so slot end time is never validated
body: In the new working-hours check inside `checkIfIsAvailable`: `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(); const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` — `end` is the same expression as `start`, so `end > workingHour.endTime` only ever compares the slot's *start* minute against the working-hours end. A slot that starts within working hours but ends after them passes the check. `end` should be derived from the slot end (e.g. `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute() + eventLength`, or better from `slotEndTime`), otherwise this availability validation is wrong for any event whose slot would overrun the host's working hours.

title: Date-override day comparison is formatted in the server's local timezone, making results server-TZ dependent
body: The day-match uses `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`. `slotStartTime` is explicitly UTC (`.utc()`), but the left-hand side is a plain Dayjs formatted without `.utc()`/`.tz()`, so it renders in whatever timezone the Node process runs in. On a server whose TZ is not UTC (common in non-UTC deployments), the same override/slot pair can land on different formatted days, so the override either fails to match (override ignored, host shown available on an overridden day) or matches the wrong day. Additionally, only the override's *start* day is compared, so an override window that crosses midnight UTC is only applied to one of the two UTC days it spans. The shifted value should be formatted with `.utc()` to match the right-hand side.

title: `override.timeZone` is used without a fallback although the type declares it optional
body: `const organizerUtcOffset = dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset();` assumes `override.timeZone` is always set, but this PR adds `timeZone?: string` to `TimeRange` as optional. Any caller of `getSlots` that supplies date overrides without a timezone (which the type explicitly permits — only the `getSchedule` call site populates it) will have dayjs fall back to the process/browser-local timezone for the offset computation, silently producing wrong override windows. Either make the field required on the `GetSlots` input type or fall back to `organizerTimeZone`.

title: No test for the headline fix: date overrides of fixed hosts in round-robin events
body: The PR's primary bug fix (#8207) is that date overrides of *fixed* hosts are enforced for ROUND_ROBIN events (the new `isFixed`-aware filtering plus the date-override/working-hours logic in `checkIfIsAvailable`). The only test added exercises a single-user event's date override in a different invitee timezone; every team-event scenario in the suite uses `hosts: []` and no date overrides, so all round-robin hosts are loose hosts. There is no regression test where a fixed round-robin host has a date override and the slot list must be restricted accordingly — exactly the logic most likely to regress (and where the busy-check bypass above would be caught). Add a test with a ROUND_ROBIN event, one fixed host with a date override, one round-robin host without, asserting only the fixed host's override window is offered.

title: Slots inside a date-override window bypass the busy-time check, allowing double bookings on override days
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a slot's date matches one of the host's date overrides and the slot falls inside the override window, the function executes `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` and returns before the `busy.every(...)` check at the bottom of the function. Since timeSlots produced by getSlots are generated purely from working hours/overrides and the ONLY place busy times (calendar events and existing Cal bookings) are applied is this function, a host with a date override on a given day will show every slot inside the override window as available even if they already have bookings or calendar events at those times. This applies to both fixed hosts and round-robin hosts (both call sites spread `...schedule`/`...userSchedule`, which includes dateOverrides), so this reintroduces double-booking on exactly the days users most often override (vacation/partial-day blocks). The override branch should verify the working-hours/override window and then still fall through to the busy check instead of returning true unconditionally.

title: Dayjs instances compared with === never match; start==end override branch is dead code
body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly constructed Dayjs object instances with strict equality, which is always false regardless of the underlying times. The intent is clearly to detect overrides where start equals end (the 'blocked' override case) and mark all slots unavailable, but this branch can never execute. As a result, such overrides are handled only by the general before/after conditions, and a slot that straddles the override's start instant (slotStart < start < slotEnd) slips through as available. The comparison must use `.isSame()` or compare `.valueOf()`/`.diff()`.

title: Working-hours check uses slot start time for both start and end, ignoring event length
body: In the new working-hours validation inside checkIfIsAvailable, `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` and `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` compute the identical value — `end` is a copy-paste of `start` and never adds the event length. The check `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` therefore only validates that the slot's *start* minute is inside the fixed host's working hours. For a round-robin event, timeSlots are generated from the union of all hosts' availability, so a slot can start inside a fixed host's window but run past that host's working-hours end (e.g., host A works until 12:30 UTC, host B until 13:00; a 60-minute slot at 12:00 generated from B's frame passes A's check). This is exactly the class of bug the PR claims to fix — fixed hosts being bookable when unavailable — and it still leaks through at the end-of-day boundary. `end` should be computed from `slotEndTime` (start + eventLength).

title: Days with no working-hours entry are treated as fully available for fixed hosts
body: The working-hours check only excludes a slot when `workingHours.find(...)` locates a working-hour entry whose `days` array includes the slot's weekday and whose time range excludes the slot. If the fixed host has no working-hours entry at all for the slot's day (e.g., the host works Mon–Fri while a round-robin co-host also works weekends), `find` returns undefined, the exclusion branch is skipped, and the slot proceeds to the busy check — i.e., the host is considered available on their day off. Since round-robin slot generation uses the union of all hosts' availability, weekend slots generated from other hosts will be offered with a fixed host who never works that day. The logic should treat 'no working hour covering this slot's day/time' as unavailable, not just 'a same-day working hour exists but the time is outside it'.

title: Override day comparison mixes server-local and UTC timezones
body: The day-match test compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` with `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`. `slotStartTime` is explicitly UTC (`time.utc()`), but `dayjs(date.start)` parses the Date in the server's local timezone and `format()` renders in that same local zone. On any server not running in UTC, the two day strings can disagree for overrides/slots near midnight, causing overrides to be attached to the wrong calendar day (slots on the override day treated as normal working hours and vice versa). The override instant should be normalized with `dayjs.utc(date.start)` before the day comparison.

title: No automated test for the headline fix: round-robin event with a fixed host's date override
body: The PR's primary purpose (issue #8207) is making date overrides of fixed hosts restrict round-robin availability, but the only test added covers the timezone conversion of an override on a single-user personal event. There is no test creating a ROUND_ROBIN event with a fixed host plus a loose host and a date override on the fixed host, so regressions of the core fix would not be caught. Additionally, there is no test combining a date override with an existing booking or calendar busy time on the same day — such a test would have exposed that checkIfIsAvailable returns early (before the busy check) for slots inside an override window, permitting double bookings.

title: Slots inside a date override bypass the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a slot's date matches a date override and the slot falls inside the override window, the code hits `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` and returns before evaluating the `busy` array. That means for any host that has a date override on a given day, existing ACCEPTED bookings and external calendar events that fall inside the override window are completely ignored, and those slots are returned as available. An attendee can then book over an existing booking (double booking / data integrity). The busy check must still run for slots that lie within a date override; only the working-hours check should be skipped for override days.

title: Working-hours check treats days outside the host's schedule as available
body: The new working-hours filter uses `workingHours.find((workingHour) => { if (workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())) { ... } })`. If the slot's weekday is not included in any of the host's working-hours entries (e.g. a Saturday slot for a Mon-Fri host), the callback returns undefined for every entry, `find` returns undefined, and the code falls through to the busy-only check — i.e. the slot is considered available. For round-robin events the aggregate availability is the union of hosts, so slots generated from another host's Saturday availability will pass this fixed-host check even though the fixed host never works that day. A day with no matching working-hours entry must be treated as unavailable, not available.

title: `end` is a duplicate of `start`, so slots overrunning the host's working hours are not rejected
body: In the new working-hours check, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start` and never accounts for the event length (it should be derived from slotEndTime). As a result the condition `end > workingHour.endTime` only rejects slots that *start* after the working hours end; a slot that starts before closing but extends past it (e.g. a 60-minute event starting 30 minutes before the fixed host's end of day) passes the check and is offered even though the host is not available for the full duration. This is precisely the class of bug (fixed hosts bookable when unavailable in round-robin) that this PR claims to fix, so the fix is undermined for end-of-day slots.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === , so the equal-start/end override branch is dead code
body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two Dayjs object references, which is always false regardless of the underlying times. The intended check — detecting overrides where start equals end (the "unavailable" full-day marker) — never executes, and such overrides instead fall through to the window comparisons, where a slot starting exactly at the override timestamp is returned as available. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `.valueOf()`/`.getTime()`.

title: Override date is formatted in the server's local timezone but compared against a UTC date
body: The date gate compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` with `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`. `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()` (UTC mode), but `dayjs(date.start)` is in the server's local timezone, so its `.format()` renders the date in the server's timezone. On any deployment where the process timezone is not UTC, the two dates disagree for times near midnight, causing date overrides to fail to match (slots wrongly unavailable via the fall-through, or wrongly available). The left side should be built with `dayjs.utc(date.start)` so both dates are rendered in UTC.

title: Optional override.timeZone silently falls back to the server's local timezone
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` uses the new optional `timeZone` field of TimeRange. If a caller supplies date overrides without `timeZone` (the type explicitly allows this), `dayjs.tz(..., undefined)` falls back to the server's local timezone, and the computed organizer UTC offset — and therefore every converted override start/end — will be wrong with no error. getSlots already receives `organizerTimeZone` as a parameter; that should be the fallback (or the field should be required) so a missing value cannot silently corrupt slot times.

title: Overrides shifted across midnight by the timezone conversion are applied to the wrong invitee day
body: activeOverrides is selected by checking `dayjs.utc(override.start)` (the raw stored wall-clock-UTC value) against the invitee's day window, but the override times are then converted to invitee-local minutes-of-day. When the offset shift moves the override across a midnight boundary, those minutes belong to a different calendar day than the one being built. Example: an organizer in UTC+13 with an override stored at 23:00–23:30 UTC and an invitee in UTC-11 yields an offset of -1440 minutes; the invitee-local times are 23:00–23:30 on the *previous* day, but the filter attaches the override to the invitee day containing the stored 23:00 UTC, so availability is added on the wrong day (and the user's normal working hours for the wrong day are removed).

title: No test for the headline fix: round-robin with a fixed host having a date override
body: The PR description states the primary fix is that date overrides of fixed hosts are respected in round-robin events (issue #8207), but no test covers that scenario: all team-event tests use empty `hosts` or non-fixed configurations, and the only new test added is the timezone variant of a single-user personal event (which also only differs by 30 minutes of offset, both on the same side of the override window). Additionally, there is no test combining a date override with an existing booking, which is exactly the interaction that the new `dateOverrideExist` short-circuit in checkIfIsAvailable gets wrong (slots inside an override are never checked against busy times). Both scenarios should be covered before merging.

title: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category setting was never customized
body: The migration runs `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. Discourse only writes a site_settings row when a value differs from its default, so on a fresh install (or any site where the admin never changed `embed_category`) this query returns zero rows and `[0]` is nil, making `[0]['id']` raise NoMethodError and the migration fail. The `if category_id == 0` fallback never gets a chance to run. The same nil-dereference pattern exists on line 15 for `uncategorized_category_id`. The migration must handle empty result sets before indexing into them.

title: Raw string interpolation of host values into INSERT SQL
body: The migration builds `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` by interpolating each line of the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting directly into SQL. A host value containing a single quote (a typo like `o'brien.com`) will break the SQL statement and abort the migration mid-way, and in general this is an injection vector. The values should be quoted/escaped (e.g. via `sanitize_sql_array` or `quote`) or inserted through ActiveRecord models.

title: update and destroy raise NoMethodError (500) for unknown or malformed requests
body: `update` does `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then passes the result to `save_host`, which calls `host.host = ...` — if no record exists with that id, `host` is nil and the controller raises NoMethodError. `destroy` (line 15-16) has the same problem with `host.destroy`. Additionally, `save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` without checking that the `:embeddable_host` key exists, so a request without that payload also 500s. These should render a 404/validation error instead.

title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a silent no-op
body: The `update` action re-serializes `@embedding` without reading or persisting anything from the request body. The route (config/routes.rb line 139) exposes a PUT endpoint and the admin controller's `saveChanges` action calls `embedding.update({})`, but the server discards whatever is sent. Any client that believes it saved embedding settings gets a success response while nothing was stored. Either the action should apply and persist the submitted attributes, or the route/action and the client `saveChanges` code should be removed.

title: Embed referer check now performs an uncached, unindexed DB query on every request
body: `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` / `record_for_host` run `where("lower(host) = ?", ...)` against the database, and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` calls this on every `/embed/comments` and `/embed/count` request — these are hit on every page view of every embedding site. The previous implementation read a cached in-memory site setting. The new `embeddable_hosts` table has no index on `host` (and none is added in the migration), so each embed request is a full table scan. Add an index and/or cache the host list.

title: Category and embeddable_host fabricators are in swapped files
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` definition, while all the category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category) were moved into `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. The fabricators still register globally so tests pass, but the file organization is inverted and will confuse anyone maintaining these specs; each fabricator should live in its own named file.

title: Validation permits a port but host matching never includes it, so such hosts can never work
body: The format regex accepts hosts like `localhost:3000` (the `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` group), and `before_validation` only strips the scheme and path — not the port. However `record_for_host` compares against `uri.host`, which excludes the port. So an admin can save an embeddable host containing a port, it validates fine, and then every embed request from that host is rejected because `localhost:3000 != localhost`. Either strip/forbid the port or compare on host:port.

title: create_table with force: true silently drops an existing embeddable_hosts table
body: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` will drop and recreate the table if it already exists (e.g. created by a plugin or a partially-applied migration) without warning, destroying any rows. `force: true` is a development convenience and should not ship in a production migration. Also, the raw `execute` statements inside `change` make the migration non-reversible despite using `change`.

title: New admin controllers have no behavioral tests
body: Both new controller specs (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController) only assert `Controller < Admin::AdminController`. There are no tests for create/update/destroy of embeddable hosts (including the nil-id 500 behavior), for the category_id defaulting to uncategorized, or for the embedding show/update endpoints. The migration's data conversion from the old site settings is also untested.

title: "is false if embeddable_host is blank" test no longer tests the blank-host case
body: After the refactor, this test no longer creates any embeddable host but also does not set `embed_truncate`, so the assertion `topic.expandable_first_post? == false` passes merely because `embed_truncate` is false by default — not because there is no embeddable host. The old test explicitly set `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil`. Since `expandable_first_post?` no longer consults hosts at all (app/models/topic.rb line 869), the test name is misleading and the guard it claims to verify was removed; it should be renamed or updated to reflect the new condition.

title: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category is unset or invalid
body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. Site settings rows only exist when a value has been changed from its default, so on any install where `embed_category` was never set (or was set to a value that doesn't match a category name, including the default empty string), the query returns zero rows and `[0]` is nil, making `[0]['id']` raise NoMethodError. The `category_id == 0` fallback on line 14 never gets a chance to run. This breaks `db:migrate` for the majority of existing sites. The code must handle an empty result (e.g. `result.first.try(:[], 'id').to_i`) before indexing.

title: Migrated hosts are not normalized, so existing embeds silently break
body: The migration inserts the raw strings from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting directly via SQL, bypassing the model's `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` prefixes and paths. The old setting explicitly accepted values like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` (the previous code and tests did `h.sub(/^https?\:\/\//, '')` when matching). After migration, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against the parsed URI host (`discourse.org`), so a stored value of `http://discourse.org` will never match and embedding will stop working for those hosts with no error shown to the admin. The migration should apply the same scheme/path stripping before inserting.

title: SQL string interpolation of site setting values in INSERT
body: The INSERT statement interpolates the raw host string `h` (read from the `site_settings.value` text column) directly into SQL: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. Any stored value containing a single quote (possible since the old setting was free-form text) will either break the migration with a SQL syntax error or produce a malformed row. Use `sanitize_sql`/quoted values or `EmbeddableHost.create!` instead of string interpolation.

title: update and destroy raise NoMethodError (500) when the host id doesn't exist
body: Both `update` (`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` then `save_host(host)` which calls `host.host = ...`) and `destroy` (`host.destroy`) operate on the result of a `.first` lookup without checking for nil. A request with a stale or invalid id (e.g. an admin UI with an out-of-date row, or a deleted record) produces `NoMethodError: undefined method ... for nil:NilClass` and a 500 error instead of a 404. Guard with `fail ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` or an equivalent not-found response.

title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a silent no-op
body: The `update` action is identical to `show`: it re-fetches and re-serializes the embedding object without reading or persisting any request parameters. Meanwhile the client controller wires `saveChanges` to `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which issues this PUT. Any caller of this endpoint gets a 200 success response while nothing is saved, which is a misleading API contract (and the `saveChanges` client action is dead/misleading UI code). Either implement persistence or remove the PUT route and the client action.

title: before_validation raises on nil host instead of producing a validation error
body: The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If the `host` attribute is nil (e.g. a create/update request where `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is missing, so the controller assigns nil), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` and returns a 500 error rather than a 422 validation failure. Guard with `if self.host.present?` and rely on `validates_format_of` (plus a presence validation) to reject blank hosts.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
body: After this change, `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` contains the `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` definition, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `Fabricator(:category)`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` definitions. Because Fabrication loads all files in the directory the specs still pass, but the files are misnamed relative to their contents, which will confuse anyone editing category or embeddable-host fixtures later. The contents should live in the correctly named files.

title: New admin controllers have no behavioral tests
body: Both `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and `Admin::EmbeddingController` specs only assert that the class is a subclass of `AdminController`. There are no tests for create/update/destroy (including the blank category falling back to uncategorized, validation error rendering, or non-existent id handling) or for the show/update serialization of the embedding endpoint. Basic request specs would have caught the nil-host 500 in the controllers and the no-op `update` action.

title: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category is unset or doesn't match a category
body: The migration looks up the old `embed_category` site setting via `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. On any install where the `embed_category` setting is empty (its default is '') or its value doesn't match a category name, the query returns zero rows, so `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. The `if category_id == 0` fallback on line 14 was clearly meant to handle the 'not found' case, but it is unreachable because the code crashes before it. The lookup must tolerate an empty result set (e.g. `rows[0].try(:[], 'id').to_i`) before the fallback can work.

title: Migrated host values are inserted verbatim (no scheme/path stripping) and interpolated raw into SQL
body: The migration takes each line of the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting and inserts it directly via raw SQL. The old setting accepted values like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` (the PR's own controller spec fabricates exactly such values), but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` matches with `lower(host) = uri.host` (e.g. 'discourse.org'). Because the INSERT bypasses the model's `before_validation` callbacks that strip the scheme and path, any migrated host containing a protocol prefix or path will never match a referer, silently breaking embedding for those sites after upgrade. Additionally, the value is interpolated into the SQL string with `#{h}`; a value containing a single quote (possible in the free-text setting) breaks the SQL statement. The migration should normalize each host the same way the model does and use quoted/parameterized values.

title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError (500) when the host id doesn't exist or params are missing
body: In `update` and `destroy`, `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown id; `save_host(nil)` then does `host.host = ...` on nil, and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, both producing a 500 instead of a 404. Similarly, `save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` without checking the param exists, and if `host` is assigned nil the model's `before_validation` block (`self.host.sub!`) raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Stale ids (e.g. the record deleted in another tab) will surface as server errors rather than a clean error response.

title: Category and embeddable_host fabricator contents are swapped between files
body: This PR puts the `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` definition into `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` (whose entire category content was deleted) and moves all the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) into the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. Tests still pass because Fabricator loads all files, but the file names no longer reflect their contents at all; anyone adding or editing a category fabricator will look in the wrong file, and this is clearly an accidental file mix-up rather than an intentional move. The contents should be swapped back so each fabricator lives in its matching file.

title: EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that reports success without saving anything
body: The `update` action (routed via `put "customize/embedding"`) fetches the embedding data and re-renders it, but never applies any submitted attributes. The admin controller's `saveChanges` action calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` against this endpoint, so a client saving changes gets a 200 with the unchanged payload while any data is silently discarded.
