body: The serializer lists `website` in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), which suppresses it when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (e.g. a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor). The new `website_name` attribute is not added to that list, so for those same users the API still serializes `website_name`, which now includes not just the host but the full URL path (e.g. `example.com/private-page`). This defeats the purpose of hiding `website` for untrusted profiles and leaks information the site explicitly intends to hide. `website_name` must be added to `untrusted_attributes` alongside `website`.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing question mark, so the include guard is never called by AMS
body: ActiveModel::Serializers only invokes the conditional-include hook named `include_<attribute>?` (with a question mark) — every other guard in this file follows that convention (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_stats?`, `include_card_image_badge?`). The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no `?`), so it is dead code: the serializer never calls it. Consequently, when a user has no website, the JSON still contains `"website_name": null` instead of omitting the key, and the intended `website.present?` guard has no effect. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

title: Untrusted-attributes spec list was not updated to cover website_name
body: The `untrusted_attributes` list in the 'TL0 user seen as anonymous' context still contains only `bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background`. Since this PR adds a new attribute derived directly from `website`, `:website_name` should be added to that list so the spec verifies it is suppressed for restricted users. As written, the existing test suite would not catch the leak of `website_name` (host plus full path) for TL0 profiles viewed anonymously — adding it would make the spec fail today and force the fix.

title: URI(website.to_s) is re-parsed up to three times per serialization
body: The `website_name` method calls `URI(website.to_s)` once for the host (line 138) and again for the path (lines 143, 146, 149), meaning the URL string is parsed up to three times for every user serialized. This runs for every user in any payload using UserSerializer (user pages, staff lists, etc.). Parse the URI once into a local variable and reuse it for both `host` and `path`.

title: Query string and fragment are silently dropped from the displayed path
body: `website_name` builds the display string as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`, discarding the query string and fragment. A user whose website is `http://example.com/profile?user=42` on a same-domain instance will see `example.com/profile` in their profile, which links correctly (the href uses the full `website`) but displays a URL that does not correspond to the link target. If showing the complete URL is the goal, the query/fragment should be preserved (or this limitation acknowledged).

title: Embedded post author link lightness wrongly changed from 30% to 70%
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The rewrite produced `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, changing the light-theme value from 30% to 70% lightness and giving the dark-theme branch 30% instead of 70%. The matching rule in common/base/topic-post.scss (.names span a) correctly uses 30%/70%. Result: in light themes the author name on expanded/embedded posts becomes much lighter than before (visual regression), and in dark themes it renders darker than intended.

title: Mobile topic-map h3 lightness wrongly changed from 20% to 50%
body: In `.topic-map h3`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The rewrite produced `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme value from 20% to 50% and using 50% instead of 80% for the dark-theme branch. The equivalent desktop rule (desktop/topic-post.scss .topic-map h3) correctly keeps 20%/80%, and the adjacent `.map .number, i` rule in this same file also keeps 20%/80%. Result: the mobile topic map heading is washed out in light themes and too dim in dark themes relative to the rest of the topic map.

title: Mobile custom-message-length lightness inverted (70% became 30%)
body: In `.custom-message-length`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The rewrite produced `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, i.e. the two branches were swapped: the light-theme color got 30% and the dark-theme color got 70%. The desktop counterpart (desktop/modal.scss .custom-message-length) correctly uses 70%/30%. Result: on mobile the character-count hint text in the flag modal is much darker than before in light themes and much lighter than intended in dark themes, diverging from desktop.

title: Group member name lightness changed from 30% to 50% in light themes
body: In `.user-stream .group-member-info .name`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The rewrite produced `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, silently changing the light-theme appearance (30% -> 50% lightness). The purpose of this PR is to add a dark-theme alternative, not to alter light-theme colors; comparable username styling in common/base/user.scss keeps 30%/70%. The member name in the group members table will now be lighter/less prominent in light themes than before.

title: Mobile group member name lightness changed from 30% to 50% in light themes
body: In `.user-stream .group-member-info .name`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The rewrite produced `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme value from 30% to 50% lightness instead of preserving it and using 70% for the dark branch (as done for `.username a` in common/base/user.scss). This is an unintended light-theme visual change that also makes the dark-theme value inconsistent with the equivalent username styling.

title: Category badge-notification color missed by the dark-theme conversion
body: This PR converts every `scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%)` color in the touched files to `dark-light-choose(..., scale-color($secondary, $lightness: (100-X)%))` so colors work on dark themes, and this file was otherwise fully converted (th, td, topic-excerpt, etc.). However `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` at line 115 still reads `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%);` with no dark-theme branch. On a dark color scheme, scaling the dark $primary lighter by 50% yields a color nearly identical to the background, making the topic/category count badge unreadable — the exact bug this PR is meant to fix.

title: Light-theme lightness of embedded-post username link unintentionally changed from 30% to 70%
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The mechanical dark-theme conversion used everywhere else in this PR keeps the `$primary` lightness argument unchanged and only adds a complementary `$secondary` branch. Here the `$primary` branch was changed to `$lightness: 70%`, so light themes now render the username link in embedded/in-reply-to posts much lighter than before, while the intended fix was only about dark themes. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: .custom-message-length light-theme color changed from 70% to 30% lightness, diverging from desktop
body: The rule `.custom-message-length` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The PR changed it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, altering the light-theme value (30% instead of 70%) — every other conversion in this PR preserves the `$primary` lightness. The equivalent desktop rule in `desktop/modal.scss` was correctly converted to 70%/30%, so mobile and desktop now disagree and mobile light themes get a much darker character-counter color. It should be 70%/30%.

title: .topic-map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50%, altering light-theme rendering
body: In the mobile topic map, `h3` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. Both the light value (20% → 50%) and the dark value (expected complement 80%, got 50%) were changed, so light themes get a lighter map heading and dark themes get a less-contrast heading than the intended conversion. The desktop counterpart (`desktop/topic-post.scss` .topic-map h3) correctly uses 20%/80%, so mobile is now inconsistent with desktop for the same element.

title: group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50% in both theme branches
body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The `$primary` lightness should have stayed 30% (with a 70% complement for `$secondary`), so light-theme group member names are now lighter than before, and the dark-theme value is not the complement of the original. Compare with the sibling `.username a` rules elsewhere which correctly keep 30%/70%.

title: Same 30%→50% lightness regression in mobile group-member-info .name
body: In `mobile/user.scss`, `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. As with the desktop copy, the `$primary` lightness should have remained 30% (dark branch 70%), so light-theme rendering changes unintentionally and the dark value is not the complement. This mirrors the desktop/user.scss error and should be 30%/70%.

title: Missed conversion: category badge-notification still scales only $primary
body: This PR converts every `scale-color($primary, ...)` color to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, ...), scale-color($secondary, ...))` so it works on dark themes, but `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification { color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%); }` in the same file was left untouched. On a dark color scheme (where `$primary` is light), scaling `$primary` toward 50% lightness produces a mid-gray that is the same pattern this PR exists to fix, so this instance looks like an oversight rather than an intentional exclusion — the adjacent `th`/`td` rules in the same file were converted.

title: Embedded-post username link lightness changed from 30% to 70% (should be 30/70 pair)
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the light-theme value identical and adds the complementary dark-theme value (primary X% / secondary 100-X%), e.g. the matching rule for `.names span a` in common/base/topic-post.scss uses 30%/70%. Here the primary lightness was silently changed from 30% to 70%, so in light themes the embedded-post author link becomes much lighter than before, and the pair is not complementary. It should be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`.

title: Mobile .custom-message-length primary lightness changed from 70% to 30%, diverging from desktop
body: `.custom-message-length` in mobile/modal.scss was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The desktop counterpart in desktop/modal.scss (same selector, changed in this PR) uses 70%/30%. The mobile change therefore alters the light-theme color of the flag message character-count hint from a 70% lightness tint to a 30% tint (much darker), which is both a light-theme visual regression and an inconsistency with desktop. It should be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)`.

title: Mobile topic-map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50%, diverging from desktop
body: The `.topic-map h3` color in mobile/topic-post.scss was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The equivalent rule in desktop/topic-post.scss (also changed in this PR) uses 20%/80%. The mobile change silently alters the light-theme heading color of the topic map summary (e.g. "Topic Summary" / participants headers) from a near-full-strength color to a 50% tint, and the pair is not complementary. It should be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)`.

title: group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50% instead of 30/70 pair
body: In `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` (desktop/user.scss), the color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The conversion pattern used everywhere else in this PR (and for the analogous `.username a` rule in common/base/user.scss, which correctly uses 30%/70%) preserves the light-theme value. Here the primary lightness was changed from 30% to 50%, lightening the group-member name in light themes and making the pair non-complementary. It should be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`.

title: Mobile group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50% instead of 30/70 pair
body: In `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` (mobile/user.scss), the color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. As with the desktop counterpart changed in this PR, the light-theme value was silently altered from a 30% tint to a 50% tint and the primary/secondary lightness pair is not complementary (correct form is 30%/70%, matching `.username a` in common/base/user.scss). This changes the visible color of group-member names in light themes on mobile.

title: totalPages off-by-one creates a phantom empty page
body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members with limit 50, i.e. exactly 2 pages), this yields 3, so showingLast (currentPage == totalPages) is never true on the real last page. The 'next' arrow stays enabled, and clicking it sets offset to min(offset+limit, user_count) = 100, which returns an empty member list while the pager shows '3/3'. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) instead.

title: PUT /admin/groups/:id silently flips visible to false for old clients
body: The update action now reads flat params (params[:visible], params[:name], params[:alias_level]) instead of the previous nested params[:group][...] payload, and create likewise changed from params[:group][:name] to params[:name]. Any existing client (admin API script, plugin, or older cached frontend assets still in a user's browser) that PUTs group: {visible: "true", name: ...} will now hit `params[:visible] == "true"` evaluating to false, silently turning group visibility off, while the name and alias_level changes are silently dropped. The parameter format change breaks the published admin API contract with a data-corrupting failure mode rather than a loud error.

title: Unvalidated limit/offset in public members endpoint
body: The members action takes `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` straight from the query string with no upper bound or sign check. The old code capped automatic-group listings at 200; now a single request with limit=100000000 forces the server to load and serialize the entire membership of a group (e.g. trust_level_0 can be every user on the site), an easy amplification/DoS vector on a public, non-admin endpoint. Additionally, negative values (limit=-1 or offset=-1) are passed to ActiveRecord's limit/offset and raise an unhandled error, returning a 500. Clamp limit (e.g. to a few hundred) and reject non-negative offset/limit.

title: Response shape of /groups/:name/members.json changed from array to object
body: The members endpoint previously rendered a bare JSON array of serialized members (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`) and now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}`. This is a public, user-facing endpoint; any consumer other than the in-repo frontend (themes, plugins, external API users parsing the array) will break, since code expecting an array will now iterate the object or read undefined. Even if intentional, this is an unversioned breaking change to a public API that should be called out and, ideally, covered by a controller spec — there are no tests at all for the new pagination/meta format.

title: Stale offset after removing a member leaves admin on an empty page
body: After removeMember succeeds it calls findMembers() with the old offset. The clamp on line 23 uses the client's stale user_count (still pre-removal), so e.g. with 51 members at offset 50, removing the last member re-requests offset 50; the server returns total=50, offset=50 and an empty members array. The UI then shows an empty member list with currentPage=2 and totalPages=1 (so showingLast is false and 'next' keeps firing no-op requests at the same offset). The offset should be re-clamped against the refreshed total (or reset toward the last valid page) when the response comes back.

title: save() error handler crashes when the rejection has no JSON body
body: The failure path does `$.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors` unconditionally. If the promise rejects for anything other than a JSON error response (network failure, timeout, gateway 502 returning HTML, or a rejection value without responseText), `e.responseText` is undefined, $.parseJSON throws, and the user gets no feedback at all (plus a JS error) instead of an alert. It also assumes the payload has an `.errors` key. Guard the parse and fall back to a generic message.

title: remove_member automatic-group test uses PUT instead of DELETE
body: The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, but the route wired up in config/routes.rb is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. Because controller specs invoke the action directly, this test passes regardless of whether the DELETE route exists or is correctly constrained — it provides no verification of the actual routing added in this PR. The 'is able to remove a member' test uses :delete correctly, so only the automatic-group guard test is testing the wrong verb.

title: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when name is empty
body: The guard clause changed from `return Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` to a bare `return;`. The method's contract was 'returns a promise'; the two current call sites happen not to chain on the result, but any caller doing `group.findMembers().then(...)` (as the previous versions of both routes did via afterModel, and as any plugin or future code would naturally write) will now throw TypeError on undefined. Keep returning a resolved promise for the empty-name case.

title: totalPages off-by-one creates a phantom empty last page
body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members, limit 50), this yields 3 pages instead of 2. The correct formula is Math.ceil(user_count / limit). Consequence: showingLast is never true on the real last page, so the 'next' arrow stays enabled; clicking it sets offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count) = user_count (see the next action at line 33), the server returns an empty member list, and the admin is shown an empty page '3/3' with no members. The same clamp in the next action should cap at the last valid offset, not at user_count.

title: members action does not validate limit/offset; negative values cause 500s
body: The members action now always applies user-supplied limit and offset to the query (limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i; offset = params[:offset].to_i) with no clamping. A request like GET /groups/<name>/members.json?offset=-1 or ?limit=-1 passes a negative value to ActiveRecord's limit/offset, which produces invalid SQL and a 500 error on a public, unauthenticated-for-visible-groups endpoint. There is also no upper bound on limit, so limit=1000000 dumps an arbitrarily large member list in one query. Values should be clamped (e.g. offset = [offset, 0].max, limit capped at a sane maximum). There are also no controller specs covering this new pagination endpoint (pagination correctness, negative input).

title: create silently drops the alias_level submitted by the client
body: The admin UI's group form always shows the alias-level combo box, and the client model's asJSON() sends alias_level on POST /admin/groups, but the create action only reads params[:name] and params[:visible]. An admin who sets an alias level on the 'New Group' form and saves will silently get a group with the default alias_level of 0; the value is discarded without any error. The update action accepts alias_level, so the asymmetry is clearly an oversight. Either accept and apply params[:alias_level] in create or stop sending/collecting it for unsaved groups.

title: remove_member bypasses Group#remove and deletes the join record directly
body: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), which deletes the has_many :through join records at the SQL level, bypassing any logic in Group#remove (the method the previous controller code called, and still the counterpart of the group.add(user) call used by add_members in this same controller). If Group#remove performs bookkeeping such as clearing primary_group/title references or invalidating caches, that work is silently skipped and user records can be left referencing a group they are no longer in. The add and remove paths should go through the same model API (group.add / group.remove) to keep side effects symmetric.

title: PUT/POST /admin/groups silently ignore the former group[usernames] membership parameter
body: Previously PUT /admin/groups/:id and POST /admin/groups accepted group[usernames] and applied membership changes; the new controller drops that parameter entirely and moves membership to the new PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members endpoints. The old PATCH-based incremental update (changes[:add]/changes[:delete]) is also removed along with its tests. Any existing API consumer (scripts, plugins) that sends group[usernames] will now receive a 200 success while the membership change is silently ignored — a no-op data change reported as success. Since this is an intentional redesign, at minimum the removal should be called out, and ignoring the parameter with a success response is the worst option; an explicit 4xx for unrecognized membership parameters would be safer.

title: After removing a member on the last page, the member list goes blank instead of stepping back a page
body: removeMember calls findMembers() with the current offset unchanged. If the admin was on the last page and that page's last member is removed, user_count drops below offset (e.g. count 51 -> 50 with offset 50), so the reloaded list is empty while the stale offset is retained (the server echoes the requested offset back in meta). The UI then shows an empty '2/2' page and the admin must click 'previous' manually. After a successful removal, offset should be recomputed against the new total (e.g. offset = Math.min(offset, Math.max(total - limit, 0))).

title: addMembers/removeMember have no failure handlers, so server errors fail silently
body: Both addMembers and removeMember only attach a .then() success handler to the AJAX call. If the server rejects the request (422 for automatic groups, validation failure, network error), the promise rejects with no handler: the user gets no feedback even though they confirmed the action in a bootbox dialog, and the member list is not reloaded or corrected. A rejection handler showing the returned errors (and keeping state consistent) is needed.

title: remove_member spec issues PUT while the route is DELETE
body: The spec exercises remove_member with 'xhr :put, :remove_member, ...', but the route wired up in config/routes.rb is delete "members" => "groups#remove_member". Controller specs bypass routing, so the test passes while exercising a verb that cannot reach the action in production. It should be xhr :delete so the spec reflects the real contract.

title: remove_member spec issues a PUT but the route only exists for DELETE
body: The spec 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but the new route in config/routes.rb only defines `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (PUT /admin/groups/members is mapped to add_members). There is no PUT route to Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, so this request raises an UrlGenerationError/routing error and the test will fail rather than asserting the intended 422. It must be `xhr :delete, :remove_member, ...` (as the other spec in the same context correctly uses).

title: Pagination math is off by one, producing an empty phantom last page
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members, limit 50), totalPages becomes 3 even though there are only 2 pages, so `showingLast` never becomes true on the real last page. Combined with the `next` action clamping `offset` to `user_count` (line 33: `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), clicking next on the last real page sets offset to 100 and fetches an empty third page (currentPage 3/3 with no members). totalPages should use Math.ceil and offset should be clamped to the largest valid page start, not to user_count.

title: PUT /admin/groups/:id silently drops membership updates from existing API consumers
body: The old `update_put` action processed `params[:group][:usernames]` to replace group membership, and `update_patch` handled `params[:changes]` add/delete deltas (the PATCH route is also removed from config/routes.rb). The new `update` action only handles name/alias_level/visible, yet still returns success_json for a PUT containing a `group[usernames]` payload. Any existing API client, plugin, or script that manages memberships via PUT /admin/groups/:id will now get a 200 success while the membership change is silently ignored, with no error and no deprecation warning. Membership mutations should either still be accepted or rejected explicitly so consumers notice.

title: create action ignores the alias_level parameter sent by the client
body: The frontend Group#create (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js) posts `asJSON()` which includes `alias_level`, but the server's create action only assigns `name` and `visible`. When an admin creates a new group with an alias level other than the default selected in the form, that setting is silently discarded and the group is created with alias_level 0; the admin only sees the correct value if they notice and save again. `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?` (as done in update) is missing from create.

title: Public group members page now truncated to 50 members with no pagination UI
body: Previously the public members endpoint returned all members for non-automatic groups (limit was only applied, with a default of 200, to automatic groups). Now `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` caps every group at 50 members, and the public group page (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs) has no pagination controls, so the members list is silently cut off at 50 for larger groups. This is a user-visible regression: members 51+ are unreachable on the public group page. Either the template needs pagination like the admin page, or the default limit for the public route must not truncate.

title: Unvalidated limit/offset parameters on the public members endpoint
body: `limit` and `offset` are taken directly from params with no bounds validation. A client can request `/groups/<name>/members.json?limit=1000000` forcing serialization of the entire membership in one response (a cheap enumeration/DoS vector on large groups), and negative values (e.g. `limit=-1` or `offset=-5`) are passed straight into `.limit()/.offset()` which produces invalid SQL and a 500 error on PostgreSQL. The values should be clamped (e.g. limit between 1 and a max cap, offset >= 0).

title: Save error handler crashes on non-JSON error responses
body: In the `save` action's rejection handler, `$.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors` assumes the error body is always JSON containing an `errors` key. If the server returns a non-JSON body (e.g. a 500 HTML error page, a proxy timeout page, or an empty response), `$.parseJSON` throws and the user sees neither the real error message nor any feedback — the button just re-enables via .finally with no alert. The handler should fall back to a generic message when parsing fails or `errors` is absent.

title: Fallback locales are not loaded outside the controller request path, so fallbacks fail in jobs and mailers
body: With fallbacks enabled, when a key is missing in the current locale the I18n backend walks the fallback chain (user locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en). However I18n.translate in the accelerator only calls load_locale(config.locale), so the fallback locales' translation files stay unloaded unless someone explicitly called I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. That call is only made in ApplicationController#set_locale. Background jobs (Sidekiq), ActionMailer deliveries, rake tasks and console code set I18n.locale directly without ensure_loaded!, so a lookup for a key missing in e.g. :fr will probe :en (or the default locale) while its YAML files are not loaded and will return 'translation missing: fr.xxx' even though the English translation exists. The web UI shows the English fallback while emails/jobs show missing-translation strings. translate should also ensure the fallback locales (I18n.fallbacks[config.locale]) are loaded when fallbacks are configured.

title: Translation cache key ignores SiteSetting.default_locale, so cached fallback results go stale when the default locale changes
body: The LRU cache key is "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}". With the new fallback chain, the cached result for a key missing in the user's locale also depends on SiteSetting.default_locale (which is consulted by FallbackLocaleList#[] on every lookup). If an admin changes default_locale at runtime, translations previously resolved through the old default locale remain cached in the process-local LRU cache (size 300, so hot keys persist indefinitely) and users keep seeing the old language until eviction or restart. Nothing invalidates @cache when default_locale changes. The default locale (or a fallback-chain fingerprint) needs to be part of the cache key, or the cache must be flushed when the setting changes.

title: FallbackLocaleList silently discards the standard I18n fallbacks assignment API
body: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides [] to always compute the chain from SiteSetting.default_locale, never consulting stored entries. The documented i18n extension point I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [:xx, :en] (used by plugins and by I18n::Locale::Fallbacks' own defaults mechanism, e.g. mapping language-specific fallbacks like pt to pt-BR) becomes a silent no-op: the assignment succeeds but is never read back. Any plugin relying on that API will appear to work while its fallbacks are ignored. Either delegate to super for explicitly-set locales or document that per-locale fallback registration is unsupported.

title: Fallbacks are now enabled in development/test, masking missing-translation regressions, and the PR ships no tests
body: Previously config.i18n.fallbacks = true was production/profile/cloud66-only; the new initializer enables fallbacks in every environment, including test. As a result, translations missing from a non-English locale now silently render English in the test suite, so tests can no longer detect keys that were not translated or were accidentally removed. On top of that, the PR adds no specs at all for the new behavior: nothing covers FallbackLocaleList ordering (user locale -> default -> en), ensure_loaded!, or that a key missing in the current locale resolves via the fallback chain. Add tests that assert the fallback resolution, and consider asserting on translation-missing detection separately so fallbacks don't hide gaps.

title: Lazy locale loading ignores fallback locales, caching "translation missing" results
body: I18n.translate only calls load_locale(config.locale) for the currently active locale, but with the new fallback chain [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en] every lookup also consults the site default locale and :en. Those fallback locales are only pre-loaded by ApplicationController#set_locale's I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!, which runs exclusively for controller requests. Any translation performed outside a controller request (background jobs, mailers, serializers invoked from jobs, console/rake tasks) that sets I18n.locale directly will find the current locale loaded but the fallback locales empty, so the fallback chain resolves to a missing-translation value, and translate() then freezes that wrong value into the LRU_CACHE (translate_no_cache(key).freeze at line 75). The stale "translation missing" string keeps being served from cache even after the fallback locale is eventually loaded, until the entry is evicted or I18n.reload! runs. load_locale/translate should ensure the whole fallback chain (as returned by I18n.fallbacks[config.locale]) is loaded, not just config.locale.

title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain, so changing default_locale serves stale translations
body: The LRU cache key is built from only the translation key, config.locale, and the backend object id. With the new FallbackLocaleList, the value of I18n.t(key) for a given user locale now also depends on SiteSetting.default_locale (the middle entry of the fallback chain). If an admin changes SiteSetting.default_locale at runtime, the cache is not invalidated (nothing in this PR clears @cache on that setting change; it is only cleared by I18n.reload!), so translations that fell back to the old site default locale keep being served from the LRU cache even though the correct fallback is now the new locale. The cache key needs to incorporate the fallback chain (e.g. the joined list from I18n.fallbacks[locale]) or a default_locale change must flush the cache.

title: No tests for the fallback behavior, and fallbacks are now enabled in dev/test where they previously were not
body: This PR removes config.i18n.fallbacks = true from the production/profile/cloud66 environment files and instead enables the custom FallbackLocaleList globally, so development and test environments now have fallbacks for the first time. That silently masks missing translation keys during development and in the test suite (a missing key in a locale now falls back to the site locale/:en instead of surfacing "translation missing"), which is exactly how incomplete locale files will regress unnoticed. The PR also ships zero tests for the new behavior: nothing verifies the fallback order (user locale -> SiteSetting.default_locale -> :en), that ensure_loaded! preloads the chain, or that the translate accelerator cache interacts correctly with fallbacks. Add specs covering FallbackLocaleList#[] ordering and I18n.t fallback resolution, and consider keeping fallbacks disabled in the test environment so missing-key regressions still fail loudly.

title: Translation cache key ignores fallback locales, so cached fallback strings go stale when default_locale changes
body: With the new fallback chain (user locale -> SiteSetting.default_locale -> :en), the value returned for I18n.t(key) under a given locale now depends not only on that locale's YAML file but also on SiteSetting.default_locale. However, the LRU cache key in I18n.translate is built as "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}", which does not include the fallback locales. SiteSetting.default_locale is a runtime-changeable setting (admins can change it from the site settings UI without a restart or I18n.reload!), so after such a change, requests for a key missing in the user's locale will keep serving the previously cached string from the OLD default locale until the cache is cleared. The cache key (or the cache invalidation) needs to account for the fallback list.

title: Fallback locales are only preloaded in the web request path; background jobs and mailers get broken fallbacks
body: The translate accelerator only lazy-loads I18n.config.locale inside I18n.translate (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb line 68: load_locale(config.locale)). When the Fallbacks backend resolves a miss by looking up the key in the default locale or :en, those locales' YAML files are never loaded by that code path. The PR compensates for this by calling I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! in ApplicationController#set_locale, but that before_filter only runs for web requests. In background jobs and mailers (e.g. user-targeted emails where I18n.locale is set to the recipient's locale), the fallback locale files are not loaded, so fallback lookups will miss and produce 'translation missing' strings (or the raw missing-translation marker) instead of falling back to the default/English text. The preloading should happen wherever locale is switched, or the accelerator should load the fallback locales for config.locale inside translate/load_locale.

title: No tests for the new fallback behavior
body: This PR introduces a nontrivial behavior: a custom FallbackLocaleList whose [] computes [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en] on every lookup, a per-request ensure_loaded! in ApplicationController#set_locale, and interaction between fallbacks and the caching/lazy-loading translate accelerator. None of this is covered by tests. At minimum there should be specs verifying that (a) a key missing in the user's locale is served from the site default locale and then :en, (b) the fallback order is correct when locales coincide, and (c) the accelerator still caches correctly across locales. Without these, regressions in translation resolution (e.g. from future i18n gem upgrades or changes to the accelerator) will ship silently.

title: Fallbacks are now enabled in development and test, masking missing-translation errors
body: Previously `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` was only set in production, profile, and the cloud66 production config; development and test ran without fallbacks, so a missing key in a locale file surfaced as a visible 'translation missing: xx.key' string. By moving fallback configuration into config/initializers/i18n.rb, fallbacks to the site default locale and English are now active in every environment, including the test suite. This means tests and development rendering that used to fail loudly on incomplete locale files will now silently render English, hiding locale-file regressions (missing/renamed keys) until production-like behavior differs from what was validated. If global fallbacks are intended, consider keeping a way (e.g. raising on missing translations in test) to detect incomplete locale files.

title: Permission denial cache locks in denies for 30s with no invalidation, defeating the new DB fallback for repeat checks
body: In Check(), once a DB query confirms a deny, the result is written to permDenialCache (line 154) and every subsequent Check for the same (namespace, user, action, resource name, folder) returns deny from the denial cache before the permission cache or the database is ever consulted. This means the new 'requery the DB when cached permissions deny' fallback (the core fix of this PR) only ever runs once per resource: after the first denied check, a permission granted on that exact resource (e.g. an admin shares a dashboard with a user who was just denied, or a permission row commits shortly after a racing check during resource creation) is not honored for up to 30 seconds. There is also no invalidation hook: in the in-proc path the service uses a private LocalCache that Grafana's accesscontrol cache-invalidation on permission changes cannot reach, and in the shared-cache (RegisterRBACAuthZService) path a denial written by one instance blocks all instances. Consider not writing a denial entry when the deny could race with a grant/creation, or invalidating the denial key when a fresh DB query for the same user/action returns an allow (e.g. via a List or another resource's fallback).

title: Denial-cache test does not actually verify the short-circuit and its comment contradicts its data
body: In the 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' subtest, the comment says 'Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked', but the permCache entry is set to map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} — i.e. a deny, not an allow. Because the value is false, and the default fakeStore in setupService returns no permissions, the test would pass even if the permDenialCache check in Check() were deleted entirely: the permCache deny would fall through to the DB path, which also returns deny. To actually prove the denial cache short-circuits, the permCache entry should be {"dashboards:uid:dash1": true} and the fake store should return that permission, so that only the denial entry can produce the expected false.

title: permissionCacheUsage metric now conflates denial-cache hits with permission-cache hits and mislabels decisive-but-denying hits as misses
body: After this change a denial-cache hit increments permissionCacheUsage with label "true" (line 118), so a fast negative answer from the new permDenialCache is indistinguishable from a permission-cache allow in this metric. Conversely, when cached permissions are found but checkPermission denies and the request falls through to the DB, the code increments permissionCacheUsage with "false" (line 137) even though the permission cache was hit — a real hit is recorded as a miss. The metric can no longer be used to observe the new DB-fallback path or the denial-cache hit rate, which are exactly the behaviors this PR introduces and would want to monitor in production. Consider separate label values or a distinct metric for the denial cache and for 'cache hit but denied, fell back to DB'.

title: In-proc authz client cache removal puts a gRPC call plus per-check JSON decode on every access check
body: For the default (in-proc) mode the client is now built with a NoopCache, so every authorization check in Grafana core — which happens several times per HTTP request on the hottest path — performs an in-proc gRPC roundtrip, and on the server each cache hit requires JSON-unmarshaling the user's full permission scope map (cacheWrap uses encoding/json, and users with many scoped dashboard/folder permissions have large maps). The previous 30s client-side cache absorbed repeated identical checks entirely in memory. Removing it is necessary for the correctness fix (the client cache served stale denies for newly created resources), but a client-side cache that only caches positive responses would preserve most of the benefit without reintroducing the stale-deny bug, since denies would still always reach the server (where the new denial cache provides the fast negative path). Worth measuring the per-request overhead before merging, or implementing positive-only client caching.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type, colliding anonymous and render subjects
body: The permission-denial cache is keyed by userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, checkReq.UserUID, action, name, parent), where UserUID is the raw identifier parsed from the subject. Both the anonymous identity ("anonymous:0") and the render service ("render:0") parse to the identifier "0", and the denial cache is consulted in Check() before any identity-type-specific logic. So a denial recorded for an anonymous Check (denials are cached for anonymous users via the normal path) will short-circuit a subsequent render-service Check for the same action/resource/folder and return Allowed=false, even though getRendererPermissions() unconditionally grants read access to all dashboards/folders. The reverse contamination is also possible: the render service gets an empty permission map for non-read actions, and those denials are cached under "0", which then blocks anonymous checks that should have gone to the database. The consequence is broken dashboard rendering and incorrect denials whenever these two identity types share the "0" identifier. The key should include the identity type (and the resolved user UID).

title: Denial cache is never invalidated and bypasses the new DB-requery fallback
body: Check() consults permDenialCache before anything else and returns deny immediately on a hit, and the entry is only written after a database query returns deny, with a 30s TTL (shortCacheTTL) and no invalidation path anywhere in the service. This undermines the PR's own fix: when cached permissions lack a resource, Check now re-queries the database so that newly granted permissions take effect — but if the (user, action, name, parent) combination was denied within the last 30 seconds, the denial entry short-circuits before the requery, so a permission grant on a previously denied resource is not visible for up to the full TTL. In the remote/cloud deployment (RegisterRBACAuthZService) the injected cache may be shared across instances, so the stale denial applies fleet-wide. There is no Delete/invalidate call for permDenialCache on permission changes, so any grant/revocation asymmetry is purely time-bounded. Maintainers should either invalidate denial entries when permissions change or exclude recently-denied entries when a fresh DB query is the intended source of truth.

title: Denial cache key uses ambiguous '_' delimiters with unescaped components
body: userPermDenialCacheKey builds the key as namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent, where name (resource UID) and parent (folder UID) are caller-supplied and user-influenced strings that may themselves contain underscores. Two different requests can therefore produce identical keys, e.g. name="x", parent="y_z" and name="x_y", parent="z" both yield "..._x_y_z". A denial cached for one resource/folder pair would then incorrectly deny a different resource for up to 30 seconds. Since the values are arbitrary identifiers, the key components should be escaped or a non-ambiguous encoding (e.g. length-prefixed or hashed) should be used.

title: permissionCacheUsage metric conflates denial-cache hits and perm-cache misses with existing semantics
body: On a denial-cache hit, Check() increments permissionCacheUsage with label "true", making denial-cache hits indistinguishable from permission-map cache hits in dashboards/alerts. Additionally, when the permission map is found in cache but the specific resource is absent (cache hit, deny), the code falls through and increments permissionCacheUsage with "false", so a genuine cache hit is now recorded as a miss. Existing monitors built on this metric's previous meaning (hit = allowed-from-cache) will silently change behavior after this PR; a separate label or metric for the new denial cache would preserve the contract.

title: "should return error if store fails" test never triggers an error
body: In TestService_getUserPermissions, the case named "should return error if store fails" sets permissions to nil but the fakeStore constructed in the loop never sets err: true, and the test then calls require.NoError(t, err). It therefore exercises the empty-permission success path rather than the error path it claims to cover, giving false confidence that store failures are handled. Relatedly, after this PR removed the cache-hit case, the testCase.cacheHit field and the "if tc.cacheHit" assertion branch (including the "only get user id" expectation) are dead code that no test can reach; either restore a cache-hit case at the new getCachedIdentityPermissions level or remove the field.

title: Cached denial entries block the DB fallback and override newer grants, reintroducing the bug this PR fixes
body: Once a Check is denied, the result is written to permDenialCache with a 30s TTL (shortCacheTTL) and every subsequent Check for the same (user, action, resource, parent) returns deny immediately, without consulting permCache or the database. This defeats the PR's own fix in two ways: (1) if a Check for a newly created dashboard races the permission insert (or hits a lagging read replica, which is the normal deployment for legacysql in cloud), the denial is pinned for 30s and the creator is locked out of the dashboard they just created — the exact symptom the PR claims to fix; (2) when permissions are granted after a denial was recorded (admin grants access, folder moved), the user stays denied for up to 30s even though the database now allows it. Additionally, the denial cache is consulted *before* the positive permCache, so a denial entry written at time T wins over a permCache entry refreshed at T+20 with allowing scopes. There is also no invalidation of denial entries when permissions change. Consider checking the denial cache only after a positive permCache/DB lookup fails, or deleting the denial entry whenever a fresh DB query allows.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type, so anonymous:0 and render:0 share entries
body: userPermDenialCacheKey is built from namespace, UserUID, action, name and parent — but not the identity type. The subject "anonymous:0" (TypeAnonymous) and "render:0" (TypeRenderService) both parse to UserUID "0", so they produce identical denial keys. Because the denial cache is checked before any identity-type handling, an anonymous user's denial for e.g. dashboards:read on dashboard X (anonymous users can lack read scope on specific dashboards) will cause the render service to be denied rendering of X for up to 30s, even though getRendererPermissions unconditionally grants wildcard read to renderers — and vice versa, a renderer denial of a write action can deny an anonymous user who has that action via a custom Viewer-role permission. Include the identity type in the denial key.

title: Denial cache key concatenates components with '_' without escaping, allowing key collisions
body: userPermDenialCacheKey joins namespace, userUID, action, name and parent with single underscores and no delimiter escaping. Two different requests can therefore map to the same cache entry, e.g. name="a_b" with parent="c" produces the same key as name="a" with parent="b_c". Today Grafana UIDs are alphanumeric so this is unlikely to trigger, but user/service-account identifiers and future actions are not guaranteed to be underscore-free, and a collision produces a wrong deny verdict for a different resource. Use a separator that cannot appear in the components (or length-prefix/hash the components).

title: Denial cache has unbounded cardinality (one entry per user×action×resource×parent)
body: Unlike permCache, which is bounded per (namespace, user, action), the denial cache creates a distinct entry for every denied (user, action, resource, parent-folder) combination. In the standalone server deployment (RegisterRBACAuthZService) the underlying cache may be a shared external cache (e.g. Redis). A user — or an attacker — enumerating resource names via Check requests will write one denial entry per unknown/unauthorized resource per user, each held for 30s. With batch/Check-heavy clients this can flood the shared cache with garbage entries and cause memory/eviction pressure on the cache cluster. Consider bounding the denial cache (e.g. only caching denials for resources known to exist, using an LRU, or per-user entry limits).

title: No test covering access after a permission is granted post-denial (the issue this PR fixes)
body: TestService_CacheCheck covers allow-from-cache, DB fallback on miss, DB fallback on stale cache, and deny-from-denial-cache, but there is no test for the critical ordering: a denial entry written before a permission was granted (or before the resource existed) versus a later DB/permCache state that allows. Given that the PR's stated purpose is 'creator can't access the dashboard they just created', a test should pin down the expected behavior when a Check for the not-yet-permitted resource precedes the creation/grant — currently that test would fail (deny wins), which suggests the intended semantics are not covered anywhere.

title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a React key in the rules list
body: In FilterViewResults, the 'grafana' switch branch renders <GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} groupIdentifier={...} ... /> without passing the `key` prop. The old <GrafanaRuleLoader> had `key={key}`, and the sibling branches ('datasource' and the default) still pass `key={key}`. The KeyedRuleWithOrigin type comment explicitly states the artificial key exists 'to prevent key duplication' in the rule list. Without a key, React falls back to index-based reconciliation, which can misassociate state (e.g. open dropdowns, drawers) with the wrong rule when items are added/removed during infinite scroll or polling, and produces duplicate-index warnings. Pass `key={key}` to GrafanaRuleListItem.

title: Silence notifications menu item does nothing in the new Grafana rule list
body: The 'Silence notifications' menu item is shown whenever `canSilence` is true, and `canSilence` can now be satisfied purely via the new `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` path (which only needs the prom rule). However, the drawer that the click handler opens is gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`, where `rule` is the ruler rule. In the new list view (GrafanaRuleListItem -> RuleActionsButtons) no ruler rule is passed, so `rule` is undefined, the condition is always false, and the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer never renders. Users with silence permission see the menu item, click it, and nothing happens. Either pass the prom rule to the drawer or gate the menu item on the drawer actually being openable.

title: Delete (and Pause) menu items can never render in the ruler-less list view despite abilities being computed for them
body: AlertRuleMenu now computes `canDelete` (and `canPause`) as an OR of the ruler-rule ability and the new grafana prom-rule ability, specifically so the menu works in the alert list view where no ruler rule is fetched. But the render conditions still require the ruler rule: the Delete item is `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}` (line 165) and the Pause item is `{canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && ...}` (line 123). Since RuleActionsButtons passes `rulerRule={rule}` with `rule === undefined` in the new list, Delete and Pause silently disappear from the list view even for users with AlertingRuleDelete/Update permissions — a regression from the previous list where ruler rules were fetched and these actions were available. The grafana-based canDelete/canPause computations are dead code as rendered. Either remove the rulerRule gate and make the handlers work from the prom-rule identifier, or drop the grafana ability path for these actions.

title: Test codifies the missing Delete action instead of catching the regression
body: The test 'should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked' grants AlertingRuleDelete (and AlertingRuleUpdate) permissions via grantUserPermissions and setFolderAccessControl, yet asserts `menuItems.length` is exactly 4 (silence, copy link, duplicate, export) with no Delete item. This locks in the regression where Delete (and Pause) are unreachable in the ruler-less list view, and the comment 'all 4 menu actions should be available' contradicts the granted permissions. The test should assert that Delete is present when the user has delete permission, and there is no test covering clicking 'Silence notifications' (which would reveal the drawer never opens) or the pause action.

title: Removed ruler reconciliation drops transient Creating/Deleting states
body: GrafanaGroupLoader previously merged the Prometheus and Ruler group responses: ruler-only rules (just created, not yet propagated to Prometheus) rendered as 'Creating', and prom-only rules (deleted in the ruler, not yet propagated) rendered as a read-only 'Deleting' item. Now only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` is rendered. Consequences: (1) a newly created rule is invisible in the list until Prometheus propagation completes, with no feedback; (2) a rule the user just deleted still renders as a fully normal, active list item with an Edit button (and copy-link/export) that operate on a rule that no longer exists in the ruler, producing failing actions and confusion. If eventual consistency is now guaranteed, that should be validated; otherwise the eventual-consistency handling needs to be preserved.

title: Rule view link no longer carries returnTo, breaking back-navigation to the list
body: The deleted GrafanaRuleLoader/GrafanaRuleListItem built the rule href as createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }) using createReturnTo(), so navigating to the rule view preserved the list context for the back/return navigation. The new GrafanaRuleListItem (line 40) builds `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no returnTo. Users who click a rule in the filtered list and then try to go back lose their filter/search context. If this was intentional it should be noted; otherwise restore the returnTo parameter.

title: Delete and Pause menu items can never render in the alert list view
body: The PR removes all ruler API fetches from the list view, so AlertRuleMenu is now rendered with `rulerRule === undefined` there (GrafanaRuleListItem passes only `promRule` to RuleActionsButtons.V2, which passes `rulerRule={rule}` = undefined to AlertRuleMenu). However, the Delete menu item is still gated on `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165) and the Pause item on `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123). Since rulerRule is always undefined in the list view, these items never render, even though the newly added `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` checks for Delete and Pause were clearly added to enable them (they are otherwise dead code). This is a functional regression: users who could previously delete or pause Grafana-managed rules from the alert list (when ruler rules were fetched) can no longer do so. The render conditions need promRule-based alternatives (e.g. a prom-rule-based pause menu item and a delete path that uses the identifier instead of the rulerRule).

title: Silence menu item is shown in the list view but the silence drawer never opens
body: In the list view, RuleActionsButtons is rendered with only `promRule` (no `rule`/RulerRuleDTO), so `canSilence` is now computed via the new grafana prom-rule abilities and the 'Silence notifications' menu item does render. But clicking it only calls `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`, and the drawer is conditionally rendered as `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} .../>`. With `rule` undefined, this condition is always false, so clicking 'Silence notifications' silently does nothing. The silence drawer needs to be adapted to work from a GrafanaPromRuleDTO (or the menu item must be hidden) — as shipped, users get a clickable action that has no effect.

title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a React key inside rules.map()
body: The switch in `rules.map()` previously rendered `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ...>`; the replacement `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} ... />` drops the `key` prop (the other branches, e.g. DataSourceRuleLoader and UnknownRuleListItem, still set `key={key}`). Rendering array children without keys makes React reconcile by index, which can cause stale/wrong item state when the list grows via infinite scroll or when items are removed, and produces a React warning. The `key={key}` should be restored on the GrafanaRuleListItem element.

title: Refactor drops the federated-rule-group immutability check for useAllAlertRuleAbilities consumers
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (still used by `useAlertRuleAbility`, which backs the non-V2 RuleActionsButtons, RuleDetails, etc.) previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` so that rules in federated (Mimir cross-tenant) rule groups were treated as immutable — Edit/Delete/Update were not supported. The refactor delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` with only a TODO comment. As a result, federated cloud rules now show Edit/Delete/Pause as supported and allowed based on folder permissions, where previously they were disabled. This is a behavior regression for Mimir federated rule groups; either the federated check needs to be preserved for the CombinedRule path or this should be explicitly tracked as a known limitation before merge.

title: Rule view link lost the returnTo query parameter
body: The deleted GrafanaRuleListItem built the item href as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`, so navigating to a rule's view page preserved a way back to the list context. The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no returnTo, so users clicking a rule in the list lose the back-navigation context that the previous implementation provided. If this drop is not intentional, the `{ returnTo }` option should be restored.

title: Stale comment and variable name reference ruler preloading that no longer happens
body: The `useGrafanaGroupsGenerator` cache-population block still carries the comment 'This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX / Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load...' and the local variable is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload`, but this PR removed the `alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)` call, so no ruler preloading occurs anymore. The comment and name now describe behavior that doesn't exist and will mislead future maintainers.

title: Silence drawer never opens for rules rendered from promRule only (new alert list view)
body: The silence drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is truthy, where `rule` is the optional RulerRuleDTO prop. In the new alert list view (FilterView → GrafanaRuleListItem → RuleActionsButtons), only `promRule` is passed and `rule` is undefined, so this condition is always false. However, the 'Silence notifications' menu item in AlertRuleMenu is shown based on the new promRule-based ability check (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` for AlertRuleAction.Silence), so a user with silencing permissions clicks 'Silence notifications', `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)` fires, and nothing renders — the action is a silent no-op. Either pass a Grafana prom-rule-compatible drawer or gate the menu item on the ruler rule being present. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test only asserts the menu item renders, not that the drawer opens, so this regression is untested.

title: Delete and Pause menu items are unreachable in the new alert list view despite the new promRule ability checks
body: AlertRuleMenu now ORs ruler-rule abilities with the new Grafana prom-rule abilities (`canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`, same for pause), which was added specifically so the list view can work without ruler data. But the render conditions were not updated: the Pause item requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123) and the Delete item requires `rulerRule` to be truthy (line 165, and `handleDelete` needs a RulerRuleDTO). Since the new list view (GrafanaRuleListItem → RuleActionsButtons) passes only `promRule` and no rulerRule, both `grafanaDeleteAbility` and `grafanaPauseAbility` results are dead code there: users with full permissions can no longer pause or delete Grafana-managed rules from the alert list, a regression from the previous GrafanaRuleLoader-based list which fetched ruler rules. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test that expects exactly 4 menu items (no Delete, no Pause) with all permissions granted confirms the actions are gone rather than this being intentional gating.

title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a key inside rules.map()
body: In FilterViewResults, the switch over rule origin renders the new GrafanaRuleListItem without a `key` prop, while the 'datasource' and default branches both set `key={key}` on their elements. React will fall back to index-based reconciliation for these list items, producing a missing-key warning and causing component state (open dropdown menus, redirect-to-clone state, silence-drawer state held inside GrafanaRuleListItem/RuleActionsButtons) to be attached by position rather than by rule when the list changes, which can attach an open menu or pending action to the wrong rule. Pass `key={key}` like the other branches do.

title: Federated rule group detection lost when useAllAlertRuleAbilities delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities
body: The refactored `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` (line 245, with only a TODO to re-add support). The previous implementation computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`. Federated rule groups (Mimir/Metrics Enterprise cross-tenant rule federation) are read-only, and the federated flag fed into `immutableRule`, which disabled Update/Delete/Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently abilities. All existing consumers of `useAlertRuleAbility`/`useAlertRuleAbilities` with a CombinedRule (e.g. the RulesTable / RuleActionsButtons code paths) will now show Edit, Delete, and Pause actions for rules in federated groups, where previously they were hidden; attempting those actions against a federated group fails on the backend. The federated check must be preserved (e.g. by reading `source_tenants` from the group identifier or passing the CombinedRule's group through) before this delegation ships.

title: Stale JSDoc and props comment reference the removed Ruler fetch
body: The component JSDoc still says "Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints" (line 25) and the `expectedRulesCount` prop comment (lines 16-21) still says "Ruler response might contain different number of rules", but this PR removed the `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` call and all ruler handling from GrafanaGroupLoader. The docs now describe behavior that no longer exists and will mislead maintainers.

title: Comment and variable name reference removed ruler-rule preloading
body: In `useGrafanaGroupsGenerator`, the comment at line 81 ("This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX / Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load...") and the variable name `cacheAndRulerPreload` (line 84) describe the `alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)` call that this PR deleted. Only the prometheusApi cache upsert remains, so both the comment and the name are now wrong and should be updated.

title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting() defeats the $__range guard and splits range-variable queries incorrectly
body: runSplitQuery() now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() on each target (line 299) before the queries are partitioned by querySupportsSplitting() (line 300). That function excludes queries containing $__range/$__range_ms/$_interval etc. via isQueryWithRangeVariable() precisely so they are NOT time-split (see the comment at lines 285-288: these variables are meant to be resolved by the backend against each sub-request's split time range). applyTemplateVariables runs templateSrv.replace with request.scopedVars, and panel/Explore requests include built-ins like __range in scopedVars, so a query such as count_over_time({a="b"}[$__range]) is rewritten to a fixed full-range duration (e.g. [2d]) before the guard runs. The guard then no longer matches, the query is classified as splittable and split into 1-day chunks, each of which evaluates a 2-day window: the chunks overlap, data is double-counted, and the combined result is wrong. Before this change these queries were sent as a single unsplit request. Either the range-variable check must run on the pre-interpolation expr, or interpolation must preserve/skip the built-in range variables.

title: Shard-split queries are template-interpolated twice
body: runShardSplitQuery() now applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables() to every target (line 52), and those interpolated targets are later passed as subRequest.targets into runSplitQuery() (line 163), which - after this same PR - applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables() again on each of them (querySplitting.ts line 299). The result is that every shard-split query is interpolated twice. Double interpolation is not idempotent: a literal escaped dollar written as $$var becomes $var after the first pass and is then expanded to the variable's value by the second pass, and variable values that themselves contain $ or text matching another variable name get re-expanded. Previously interpolation happened exactly once (via interpolateVariablesInQueries in runShardSplitQuery, with runSplitQuery doing none). The updated tests don't catch this because the mocked applyTemplateVariables only does a no-op-on-second-pass string replace. runShardSplitQuery should either skip its own interpolation now that runSplitQuery interpolates, or runSplitQuery needs a way to know the targets are already interpolated.

title: No regression test that $__range queries are still excluded from splitting after interpolation
body: The only new test ('Interpolates queries before execution') covers $__auto/$step interpolation, but there is no test asserting that a query using $__range (or another range variable) is still routed to the non-splitting group now that interpolation happens before the querySupportsSplitting()/isQueryWithRangeVariable() check in runSplitQuery. Since that guard inspects the raw expr for the literal $__range token and the new interpolation step can remove that token, a test pinning the 'queries with $__range are not split' behavior is needed to catch the regression; without it, the wrong-results scenario for range-variable queries ships silently.

title: Shard-split queries are now interpolated twice (once here, again in runSplitQuery)
body: runShardSplitQuery maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables and then passes those already-interpolated targets to splitQueriesByStreamShard, which builds sub-requests handed to runSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts:163). runSplitQuery now interpolates the same targets again via datasource.applyTemplateVariables (querySplitting.ts:299), once per shard group and once per retry — the updated test 'Interpolates queries before running' even asserts 5 calls of applyTemplateVariables for a single query (1 here + 4 inside runSplitQuery). This is only safe if template interpolation is idempotent: any variable whose interpolated value itself contains '$'-prefixed text (e.g. regex-valued variables, a value containing a literal '$' followed by an existing variable name) will be substituted a second time on the already-resolved string, silently corrupting the executed query. The shard selector inserted by interpolateShardingSelector is also fed back through variable substitution. Interpolation should happen exactly once — either drop the map in runShardSplitQuery and let runSplitQuery own it, or skip re-interpolation in runSplitQuery when invoked from the shard path.

title: $__range exclusion in querySupportsSplitting is evaluated after interpolation and may no longer trigger
body: querySupportsSplitting's `!isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` check now runs on expressions that have already been through datasource.applyTemplateVariables (the map at line 299 happens before the partition at line 300). If LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables resolves the Loki range variables ($__range, $__range_s, $__range_ms — it does resolve other built-ins such as $__auto, as the new tests demonstrate), the check can never match anymore, so $__range queries will now be split into 1-day chunks. That is a significant behavior change: each chunk would evaluate the full-range lookback window (a 30-day $__range split into 30 chunks scans roughly 30x the data), and if Loki clips range-vector lookback at the sub-query start, the results near chunk boundaries would be wrong. The comment above the check ("interpolated on the backend with the split timeRange") also no longer describes the new flow, since interpolation now happens on the frontend first. Please verify whether applyTemplateVariables resolves the range variables: if it does, the guard is dead code and the split of $__range queries must be an intended, tested behavior (comment updated accordingly); if it does not, make it explicit that this check still relies on $__range surviving frontend interpolation.

title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting() disables the $__range guard, causing wrong results for range-variable queries
body: Queries are now mapped through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() (line 299) before the split/no-split decision at line 300. querySupportsSplitting() relies on isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) to detect `$__range`, `$__from`, `$__to`, etc. in the raw expression, but after template interpolation those variables have already been substituted with the full dashboard range, so the check never matches. The code comment at line 285-287 explicitly says such queries must not be split because the range variable becomes incorrect per sub-request. Consequence: a query like `count_over_time({a="b"}[$__range])` now gets split into 1-day chunks with the full range (e.g. `[2d]`) baked in, and each sub-request's start/end truncates the lookback window, so the returned counts differ from the unsplit query — a silent data-correctness regression. The range-variable check must be evaluated against the pre-interpolation expression (or such queries must otherwise stay unsplit). There is also no test covering queries containing $__range after this change, so nothing would catch this.

title: Template variables are applied twice in the shard-splitting path
body: runShardSplitQuery() now maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() (line 52), and then splitQueriesByStreamShard() delegates each sub-request to runSplitQuery() (line 163), which — after this same PR — applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables() again to those already-interpolated targets (querySplitting.ts line 299). So every query is interpolated at least twice, and once more per additional shard group cycle. A second interpolation pass is not idempotent in general: if a variable's value, a label value, or a log-line filter regex legitimately contains `$` or `${...}` sequences (common in log content), the second pass will re-expand them against template variables, corrupting the query sent to Loki. The updated test 'Interpolates queries before running' shows applyTemplateVariables being called 5 times for a single query, but the test mock's replace is trivially idempotent, so this corruption is not covered. The interpolation should happen in exactly one layer, or runSplitQuery should skip interpolation for targets that were already interpolated by the caller.

title: No test that queries with range variables are still excluded from splitting after upfront interpolation
body: The new tests only cover happy-path interpolation of `$__auto` and `$step`. There is no test asserting that a query containing `$__range` (or `$__from`/`$__to`) is still routed to the non-splitting path now that interpolation happens before the querySupportsSplitting() check. Since interpolation substitutes these variables, the existing guard silently stops matching, and without a regression test this data-correctness behavior (documented in the comment on querySupportsSplitting) can break unnoticed — as it appears to in this PR.

title: traceID field dropped from "grafana-data-egress" log events
body: The previous implementation of LoggerMiddleware.logRequest appended a `traceID` field (obtained via `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)`) to the "Plugin Request Completed" log line. The new implementation logs only status, duration, eventName, time_before_plugin_request and error, plus whatever contextual attributes ContextualLoggerMiddleware injects — and `instrumentContext` (contextual_logger_middleware.go:27-37) only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname, not traceID. Unless `log.FromContext` automatically derives the trace ID from the span in the context, every "grafana-data-egress" log event loses its trace correlation, which breaks linking these egress log events to traces for anyone consuming them. This should either be verified against the infra log FromContext implementation or the traceID attribute should be added to instrumentContext.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new logger, discarding the receiver's recorded state
body: `func (f *TestLogger) FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger { return NewTestLogger() }` returns a fresh instance and throws away `f`. LoggerMiddleware now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (logger_middleware.go:58), so any test that creates a TestLogger, runs the middleware, and asserts on `logger.InfoLogs.Calls` / `Message` / `Ctx` will see zero calls — the log records go to the throwaway instance. The fake should return `f` (and ideally replay the contextual attributes from the context) so tests can actually assert on the new contextual logging behavior; as written it makes the fake unusable for testing exactly the code path this PR introduces.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no tests, and LoggerMiddleware's log fields are now silently dependent on chain ordering
body: The PR adds a brand-new middleware (ContextualLoggerMiddleware) with zero test coverage, and simultaneously changes LoggerMiddleware so that its "Plugin Request Completed" lines no longer read pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname from the request itself but rely on ContextualLoggerMiddleware appearing earlier in the middleware chain (pluginsintegration.go:159-161). Both constructors are exported, so LoggerMiddleware used standalone — or a future reordering of CreateMiddlewares — will silently emit log lines missing the plugin identity fields, with nothing failing. The old InstrumentationMiddleware even carried a doc comment saying it must live at the top of the stack; that constraint is now implicit and untested. A test asserting that LoggerMiddleware's output contains the contextual fields (and/or that the middleware pair is wired correctly) is needed.
