An unlocked map iteration concurrent with a map write is a fatal runtime error in Go ('concurrent map iteration and map write'), crashing the whole server process. TotalDocs must take b.cacheMu.RLock (and the DocCount calls should be made outside the lock or the lock held for the whole iteration).

title: Eager Init makes any index-build error fatal to server startup, including bleve 'path already exists' on restart
body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init synchronously and returns an error, so any failure while building the search index prevents the server from being created at all. This interacts badly with bleveBackend.BuildIndex: it always calls bleve.New (never bleve.Open) on a fixed path under opts.Root for indexes above FileThreshold, and bleve.New returns an error if the directory already exists. The index cache is in-memory only, so on every process restart the cache is empty and BuildIndex runs again against the same directory left over from the previous run. With lazy init this surfaced as a failed Search RPC while the server kept serving storage requests; now it aborts NewResourceServer and the storage server cannot start until the stale index directory is manually deleted. Transient errors (e.g., a DB hiccup while listing documents during init) similarly become startup-fatal. Either the backend must open/reuse existing on-disk indexes, or startup should tolerate/degrade gracefully on search init failure.

title: Context and goroutines leak when Init fails in the constructor
body: When s.Init(ctx) fails, NewResourceServer returns nil, err without calling the cancel function created for the server's background watcher context (line 229). Additionally, a partially-failed search init may have already started the watch-events goroutine in searchSupport.init, which runs on context.Background() with no cancellation path and blocks forever on the events channel. So a failed construction leaves leaked goroutines and an uncancellable context alive while the caller believes the server was not created. The error path should invoke s.cancel() (and ideally stop the search watcher) before returning.

title: Postgres integration coverage for the storage server target is silently disabled
body: The test now skips whenever GRAFANA_TEST_DB is postgres with a TODO saying it does not work in Drone but works locally. Since this is the only integration test that boots the storage server module end to end, postgres support is now completely untested in CI, and regressions specific to the postgres dialect (e.g., in the SQL backend or the eager-init startup path this PR introduces) will not be caught. The underlying Drone failure should be diagnosed rather than skipped, or the skip should at least be tracked so it is not forgotten.

title: Removing the coarse BuildIndex lock allows concurrent duplicate builds of the same index key
body: BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the whole function, which (accidentally) serialized builds. Now the lock only guards the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write, but the caller-side check in searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex (pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go, which its own TODO admits has no per-key dedup) is a check-then-act: two concurrent callers (e.g. a gRPC Search request and the watch-event goroutine in handleEvent, or two simultaneous Search requests for a cold namespace) both get nil from GetIndex and both run a full build. The last writer wins in the cache, so the losing bleveIndex becomes orphaned while the watch goroutine may still be writing documents into it - searches then run against a different index instance and silently miss those updates. It also double-counts IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds, and for disk-backed indexes (size > FileThreshold) two concurrent bleve.New calls on the same directory will make one fail with 'path already exists'. A per-key singleflight or keyed mutex is needed to preserve the old serialization semantics for the same key while allowing different keys to build in parallel.

title: Data race on shared err and totalBatchesIndexed across init errgroup workers
body: In searchSupport.init, each group.Go closure assigns to the function-scoped `err` variable (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and increments `totalBatchesIndexed` from multiple worker goroutines with no synchronization. With WorkerThreads > 1 this is a data race (caught by -race) and makes both the error value observed by `return err` and the `namespaced_indexed` span attribute unreliable. Each goroutine should use its own local error variable and the counter should be atomic (or aggregated from group results). This function is the direct target of this PR's concurrency changes, so the race is worth fixing alongside them.

title: Search event goroutine panics when the storage watch channel is closed
body: The goroutine started in init does `v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v)` with no ok-check. The SQL backend's poller closes the stream channel when the backend is stopped (backend.Stop -> b.cancel() -> poller returns -> close(stream)), e.g. during server shutdown. After close, the receive returns nil immediately in a hot loop, and handleEvent dereferences evt.Type on the nil event, panicking and crashing the process. It should be `v, ok := <-events; if !ok { return }` (and ideally also honor a cancellable context). Since this PR makes init run unconditionally at construction, every server with search configured now runs this goroutine and will hit the panic on shutdown.

title: Trace propagation fix was missed in bleve BuildIndex
body: The PR's stated goal is to fix trace propagation by keeping the span context (done in search.go init/build and sql/backend.go GetResourceStats), but bleveBackend.BuildIndex still does `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)`, discarding the child span context. The builder callback and everything it calls (storage.ListIterator, document building) therefore run with the parent context, so their spans are not children of the BuildIndex span and the BuildIndex trace is missing all its nested work. It should be `ctx, span := ...` like the other fixed call sites.

title: Constructor leaks context and goroutines when Init fails
body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) and returns nil on error, but never calls the cancel() created for the server's internal context. If init fails partway (e.g. search.init succeeded and started its watch goroutine, then initWatcher failed), the cancellable context is leaked and the search watch goroutine - which runs on a detached context.Background() - is never cleaned up. The error path should invoke s.cancel() (and ideally s.Stop) before returning.

title: Postgres integration test skipped with an unexplained failure instead of being fixed
body: The PR adds a permanent skip for postgres ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.') to the only integration test covering the storage-server target. This removes CI coverage for a supported database exactly when the initialization model changes from lazy per-request to blocking at construction - a change that could plausibly behave differently on postgres (e.g. timing/migration ordering during InitTestDB). The root cause should be diagnosed and fixed, or at least an issue linked, rather than silently dropping postgres coverage; otherwise a real postgres regression from this change will go undetected.

title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
body: UsernameForm.authenticate calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but no zero-argument method with that name exists in the sources changed by this PR: the only definition is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (UsernamePasswordForm.java line 160), which requires a UserModel argument (neither UsernameForm nor AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator declares an overload). Unless an overload is added, this change does not compile and breaks the build. The call presumably should be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, so that the form is skipped during re-authentication only when the already-identified user cannot use conditional passkeys.

title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, removing passkey UI from the anonymous login page
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`, and it now gates every `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` call in UsernamePasswordForm (lines 115 and 137). Before this PR, the webauthn data (challenge, RP ID, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI attribute, autocomplete='username webauthn') was set up exactly when the user was NOT yet selected, i.e. on the initial anonymous login page. With the new condition, a first-time login where `context.getUser()` is null gets no webauthn attributes at all, so the passkey conditional-UI autofill and the `//form[@id='webauth']` element disappear from the standard login page, and after a wrong password the re-rendered anonymous page loses them too. This breaks discoverable-key login from the login screen and contradicts this PR's own tests: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey asserts the webauthn form is present immediately after `oauth.openLoginForm()` with no user identified, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest do the same, and the webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey tests expect automatic passkey login from the anonymous page. The condition must not exclude the anonymous case (e.g. `user == null || user has a passwordless webauthn credential`).

title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys realm-wide instead of testing a user without a passkey
body: The test is named (and commented) as covering re-authentication of a user without a passkey, but it implements this by disabling the passkeys policy for the whole realm (`setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`), so `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.isPasskeysEnabled()` is false for every user. The genuinely interesting branch introduced by this PR — passkeys enabled in the realm while the re-authenticating user has no passkey credential (where `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` must decide whether to show the passkey UI / whether UsernameForm may skip the form) — is never exercised by any test in the PR. A test with passkeys enabled realm-wide and a user that has no passwordless WebAuthn credential should be added, otherwise regressions in that path (e.g. showing an unusable passkey-only page to a passkey-less user during re-authentication) would go undetected.

title: Call to undefined no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() now calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but no no-argument version of this method is defined anywhere in the class hierarchy shown in this PR. The only definition is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in UsernamePasswordForm (line 160), and neither UsernameForm itself, AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, nor any other changed file defines a no-arg overload. Java will not resolve a zero-argument call to a one-argument method, so this is a compilation error that breaks the build. Either the call must be isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), or a no-arg overload (e.g. checking `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`) must be added.

title: Re-authentication no longer skips username form for users without any passkey
body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) only checks that the passkeys feature/policy is enabled for the realm and that a user is set; it never checks whether that particular user actually has a passwordless WebAuthn credential. As a result, UsernameForm.authenticate() no longer auto-succeeds during re-authentication for ANY user of a realm with passkeys enabled — including users who only have a password. Those users now get an extra mandatory username-confirmation page (with hidden username) on every re-authentication (e.g. prompt=login), even though the conditional-UI passkey option is useless to them. Consider also checking user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(WebAuthnCredentialModel.TYPE_PASSWORDLESS) (or equivalent) so the skip optimization still applies to users without passkeys.

title: try/assertThat/fail pattern in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey is misleading and can pass vacuously
body: The negative assertions for the webauthn form (lines 291-296 and 312-317) use `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail("Not expected to have webauthn button"); } catch (Exception e) {}`. driver.findElement() either returns a non-null WebElement or throws, so `assertThat(element, nullValue())` can never pass; when the form IS present the AssertionError (an Error, not caught by `catch (Exception)`) escapes before fail() is reached, making the fail() message dead code. Worse, the broad `catch (Exception)` silently swallows any other exception (e.g. a WebDriver timeout or stale element), so an unrelated infrastructure failure makes the test pass vacuously. Use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) as is already done in PasskeysUsernameFormTest (line 202) for consistency and a clear failure message.

title: Comment gives wrong reason for passkeys being absent in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey
body: The comment at line 304 (and the test name) says passkeys are not shown "as this user does not have passkey", but the test actually disables passkeys realm-wide via setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE). The assertion passes because of the realm policy, not because the user lacks a passkey credential, so the comment misleads future readers about what behavior is verified. It should state that passkeys are disabled in the realm policy.

title: No test covers a failed passkey attempt during re-authentication (the createErrorResponse fix path)
body: The PR adds AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) to WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse specifically so that, when a passkey attempt fails while re-authenticating, the re-rendered form keeps the username hidden. None of the new tests exercise this path: all passkey re-authentication tests succeed on the first try, and webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey only combines a wrong password with a subsequent successful passkey/password. There is no test that submits a failing passkey during prompt=login re-authentication and then asserts the username field remains hidden and password retry still works, so a regression in this newly added code would go undetected.

title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but after this change no zero-argument method with that name exists anywhere in the class hierarchy: UsernamePasswordForm (the only superclass that defines anything similar) only defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) at line 160, and neither AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator nor AbstractFormAuthenticator provides a no-arg version. The services module therefore fails to compile. Either a no-arg overload must be added to UsernamePasswordForm, or the call must be changed to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()).

title: Requiring an identified user drops WebAuthn conditional-UI setup on the initial login page
body: In authenticate() (line 115) and challenge(context, error, field) (line 137), the WebAuthn setup is now gated on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which (lines 160-162) additionally requires user != null. On a normal initial login no user is set yet, so webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) is never invoked: the login page never receives the WebAuthn challenge, RP ID or enableWebAuthnConditionalUI attributes, the hidden form //form[@id='webauth'] is not rendered, and passkey autofill / automatic discoverable-key login cannot work. The base code this PR removes explicitly set up the webauthn data "when the user is not already selected". The PR's own tests contradict the new behavior: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey and webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication assert the webauthn form and the 'username webauthn' autocomplete on the initial page before any user is identified, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey asserts the same after a failed username, and the webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey tests expect the user to be logged in automatically straight from oauth.openLoginForm(). The fill must also happen when context.getUser() == null (i.e. the condition must not require an identified user), otherwise passkey login on the standard first login page is broken.

title: Broad catch (Exception) can make the 'no webauthn button' check pass spuriously
body: In reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey (and the identical block around line 312), the absence of the webauthn form is verified with: try { assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), nullValue()); fail("Not expected to have webauthn button"); } catch (Exception nsee) { }. Two problems: (1) driver.findElement never returns null, so assertThat(..., nullValue()) can never succeed and the fail() line is dead code; (2) catching Exception rather than NoSuchElementException means any unrelated driver/page error (timeout, stale element, page not loaded) is silently swallowed and the test passes without actually verifying the webauthn form is absent. If the webauthn form is present the AssertionError correctly propagates, but the check should use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) as done in the other test classes to avoid false passes.

title: Test cleanup removes literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDPs, leaking test data and failing cleanup
body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup registrations use `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` with the hard-coded string "alias" instead of the actual aliases that were created ("idp-alias-" + i at line 381, and "idp-alias-20" at line 425). None of the 20+ identity providers created by the test are ever removed, so they leak into subsequent tests in the realm (any test that counts or lists realm IDPs will see stale brokers). Additionally, at cleanup time the registered runnable calls remove() on the non-existent "alias" resource, which returns 404 and can make the cleanup itself fail. The correct call is `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove)` (and `get("idp-alias-20")` for the later one). Note the same copy-pasted defect exists at line 303 in testCacheIDPByOrg, which suggests the bug was copied from there.

title: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate evaluates the login predicate on the organization-wrapped model, so invalidation can be wrongly skipped
body: In update(), the "original" model passed to registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate comes from getById(), which returns a model wrapped by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. That wrapper overrides isEnabled() to return false whenever the linked organization (or the organization provider) is disabled, regardless of the IDP's own enabled flag. The login caches, however, are populated purely from intrinsic IDP properties (enabled, linkOnly, hideOnLogin, brokerPublic, organizationId) — an IDP belonging to a disabled org is still stored in the cached login lists. Scenario: (1) an org-linked, public, enabled IDP is cached in the login list; (2) the organization is disabled (this does not touch the IDP, so no cache invalidation); (3) an admin updates the IDP to disabled or non-public — the wrapped original fails getLoginPredicate() (isEnabled()=false due to the disabled org) and the updated model also fails, so registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate returns early and the login caches are NOT invalidated even though the IDP is in them and no longer qualifies; (4) when the org is re-enabled, getForLogin serves the stale cached list containing an IDP that is disabled/non-public, violating the SPI contract that getForLogin returns only IDPs available for login. The impact on the login page is currently masked because OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean re-filters, but any other consumer of getForLogin gets stale results. Fix: compute the predicate on the raw delegate model (e.g. idpDelegate.getById(...)) instead of the wrapped one, so the skip-invalidation decision depends only on intrinsic IDP properties.

title: Test cleanup registers removal of literal IDP alias "alias" instead of the created aliases
body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` (also repeated at line 425 for "idp-alias-20"). The literal string "alias" is used instead of the loop variable `alias` ("idp-alias-" + i), so the cleanup targets a non-existent identity provider. As a result, the 21 IDPs created by the test (10 of which are explicitly linked to organization "orga" via addIdentityProvider) are never removed from the test realm. Besides leaking brokers between tests in the same realm, this can break other tests in the class that assert on IDP counts per organization — e.g. testCacheIDPByOrg asserts `assertEquals(6, identityProviderListQuery.getIDPs("-1.-1").size())` for orga, which would fail if the leftover orga-linked IDPs from testCacheIDPForLogin are still present, depending on test execution order.

title: No test removes a login-eligible IDP to verify login cache invalidation on removal
body: The new `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` code path in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove() is only exercised in the test with "idp-alias-1", which is disabled and therefore never present in the login caches. There is no test that removes an IDP that actually appears in the cached getForLogin results (e.g. one of the enabled "idp-alias-0/2/4..." providers) and asserts that the FetchMode caches are invalidated and repopulated without the removed IDP. Since removal invalidation depends on evaluating the login predicate against the model fetched from the delegate before deletion, a regression in this new logic (e.g. evaluating the predicate on the wrong model or skipping invalidation) would go undetected.

title: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate evaluates the login predicate on the organization-aware wrapper, causing spurious invalidations
body: In update(), the `original` model passed to registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate comes from getById(), which returns a model wrapped by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. That wrapper overrides isEnabled() to return false whenever the linked organization is missing or disabled. The login predicate (which uses IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled) therefore reports the original IDP as not login-eligible even though the stored IDP itself is enabled, public and not hidden. For any update of an org-linked IDP whose organization is disabled (or has been removed), the skip conditions in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate are bypassed and all three login cache entries (REALM_ONLY, ORG_ONLY, ALL) are invalidated cluster-wide on every trivial update (e.g. a displayName change), defeating the cache. Correctness is not affected, but the invalidation can be avoided by fetching the raw stored model from idpDelegate (as done in remove()) instead of using the wrapped getById() result.

title: Test cleanup registers removal of literal "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases
body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` (lines 381 and 425), using the literal string "alias" rather than the actual alias of the created provider ("idp-alias-" + i / "idp-alias-20"). As a result, none of the 21 identity providers created by the test are registered for cleanup, and cleanup instead issues DELETE requests for a non-existent "alias" provider (likely 404, which can fail the cleanup phase). The leaked providers include 10 IDPs that remain linked to organization "orga", so if testCacheIDPForLogin runs before testCacheIDPByOrg (JUnit method order is not guaranteed), testCacheIDPByOrg's assertion of exactly 6 IDPs for orga (orga-identity-provider + 5 linked) will fail. The same copy-paste bug exists at line 381 inside the creation loop and at line 425 for idp-alias-20 (and pre-exists at line 303 in testCacheIDPByOrg).

title: remove() skips invalidating the internalId cache entry when the alias key is not cached
body: In remove(alias), when the alias cache key is not in the session's invalidation set and there is no cached entry under the alias key, no invalidation is registered for the provider's internalId (the else-branch only calls registerIDPInvalidation when `cached != null`). An IDP can, however, be cached under its internalId via getById() without ever having been looked up by alias, so after remove() completes, a subsequent getById(internalId) can return the already-deleted identity provider from cache. This staleness matters even more now that getForLogin() and getByOrganization() resolve cached list entries through session.identityProviders().getById(id). The fix is to always invalidate the internalId (e.g. registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) in both branches, guarding for null). Note this hole pre-exists but the method was reworked in this PR and the new list caches depend on getById freshness.

title: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate compares an org-aware wrapped original against the raw updated model
body: In update(), the "original" model passed to registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate comes from getById(), which returns the anonymous wrapper whose isEnabled() returns false whenever the linked organization is disabled (createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel). The "updated" model is the raw caller-supplied model whose isEnabled() is the stored value. The skip decisions in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate therefore depend on the organization's runtime enablement state rather than only on stored IDP attributes. Concrete scenario: an org-linked, public, enabled IDP whose organization is disabled appears in the cached getForLogin lists (the JPA query is config-based); if an admin then disables that IDP, both predicate tests evaluate to false and the login caches are NOT invalidated, leaving a disabled IDP in the cached getForLogin() stream. Correctness then relies entirely on every consumer re-checking isEnabled() — only the two OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean paths patched in this PR do so. Using the raw delegate model (idpDelegate.getById) as "original" would make the invalidation decision deterministic and independent of org state.

title: Multiple crypto providers no longer fail fast; selection between equal-order providers is classpath-dependent and only logged at DEBUG
body: detectProvider() previously threw IllegalStateException when more than one CryptoProvider was found on the classpath, which was a deliberate fail-fast guard (e.g. against having both keycloak-crypto-default and keycloak-crypto-fips1402 present). Now it silently picks the provider with the highest order(). All three in-tree providers (DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, FIPS1402Provider) return order() == 200, so when more than one of them is present the winner is decided by ServiceLoader encounter order, i.e. by classpath/JAR ordering, which is not deterministic across deployments. Concretely: a FIPS deployment that accidentally also has keycloak-crypto-default on the classpath can silently initialize and register the plain (non-FIPS) BouncyCastle provider instead of BCFIPS, with no error; the 'Ignored crypto providers' message is emitted only at DEBUG level so operators will not notice the wrong provider being used. Either give the providers distinct orders, break ties deterministically, or at least log the ignored providers at WARN.

title: order() added as an abstract method breaks the public CryptoProvider SPI
body: The new int order() method was added to the public CryptoProvider interface without a default implementation. CryptoProvider is an SPI intended to be implemented outside the Keycloak tree (the same repo has three implementations and third-party/forks exist, e.g. in the keycloak-client repo that this PR's description says will be synced later). Any existing compiled implementation of CryptoProvider will still load via ServiceLoader but will throw AbstractMethodError as soon as CryptoIntegration.detectProvider() calls order() on it during sorted(...), breaking initialization of those deployments at runtime, and source-level implementors fail to compile. Declaring it as default int order() { return 0; } would preserve backward compatibility while still allowing the authz-client provider (order 100) to lose against the built-in providers (order 200).

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JVM default KeyStore provider (usually SUN), violating the interface contract
body: The CryptoProvider contract documents getBouncyCastleProvider() as '@return BouncyCastle security provider' (non-FIPS or FIPS BC). AuthzClientCryptoProvider implements it as KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which returns the default JCA keystore provider - typically SUN - not BouncyCastle. Any code path that obtains the provider via CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getBouncyCastleProvider() and uses it as BC (requesting BC-only algorithms like AES/GCM with BC semantics, PKCS7 padding, BCFKS keystores, or registering the returned provider) will now get a provider that does not implement those algorithms and fail with NoSuchAlgorithmException at a distance from the real cause. If BC is genuinely never needed in this provider, throwing UnsupportedOperationException like the other unsupported methods, or returning null after documenting it, would fail fast instead of silently returning a wrong provider.

title: Provider only implements ECDSA r/s conversion, but registers globally and is latched by AuthzClient.create() for the whole JVM
body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider throws UnsupportedOperationException for getAlgorithmProvider(), getPemUtils(), getKeyFactory(), getSignature(), getX509CertFactory(), createECParams(), etc. However it is registered through META-INF/services and AuthzClient.create(Configuration) now calls CryptoIntegration.init(...), which sets the JVM-wide static provider. keycloak-core code that authz-client users commonly exercise routes through these methods: org.keycloak.common.util.PemUtils' PEM key/certificate decoding goes through CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getPemUtils(), and JWS signing helpers go through getAlgorithmProvider()/getSignature(). Concretely, an application that uses only the authz-client artifact (the exact scenario this PR targets - no BouncyCastle-based provider on the classpath, so the order-100 stub wins) and configures signed-JWT client credentials (jwt client authenticator) will hit UnsupportedOperationException when decoding the PEM private key, a feature the authz-client supports. There is no test or analysis in the PR demonstrating that the implemented surface (only ECDSA r/s conversion) covers what the authz-client actually invokes through CryptoIntegration; at minimum the JWT client-credentials flow should be tested end-to-end with this provider as the only one on the classpath.

title: ECDSA test round-trip is too weak to catch truncation/padding bugs and misses leading-zero edge cases
body: The test only checks that concat -> DER -> concat is self-consistent (rsConcat == rsConcat2). It never asserts that the re-encoded DER equals the original minimal-DER signature produced by JCA (Arrays.equals(sign, asn1Des)), so a bug that truncates or mis-pads r/s on the concat side could still pass, since the same buggy conversion is applied in both directions. Additionally, each test signs once with a freshly generated key, so the probability of exercising the tricky edge cases - r or s whose encoding has a leading zero byte or is shorter than the curve length, which is exactly what the hand-rolled ASN.1Encoder/ASN1Decoder code must handle via integerToBytes and the len+1 zero-padding - is roughly 1/256 per component per run and effectively never happens. The test should loop over many signatures (or use fixed vectors with known leading-zero r/s values) and also assert DER equality against the original signature bytes.

title: No test for the new order-based provider selection logic
body: The core behavior change of this PR - CryptoIntegration now tolerates multiple CryptoProviders on the classpath and selects the one with the highest order() instead of throwing IllegalStateException - has no test coverage anywhere in the changed files. A regression in the comparator (e.g. dropping .reversed() would silently pick the lowest-order provider, meaning AuthzClientCryptoProvider would win over DefaultCryptoProvider in the testsuite) or in the tie-breaking would go unnoticed. A unit test should assert that with two providers of different order the higher one is selected, and document/assert the intended behavior for equal orders, since all three built-in providers currently return 200.

title: Dead code: two ASN1Encoder instances created and immediately discarded in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 ('ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger); ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);') create encoders, write the integers into them, and throw the results away - the actual encoding happens in the return statement below. These are leftover no-op statements from an earlier iteration of the method; they allocate objects for nothing and suggest an incomplete edit. They should be removed so the method is not misleading.

title: New abstract method order() breaks all existing CryptoProvider implementers
body: The PR adds `int order();` as a non-default method to the public SPI interface `CryptoProvider`. Any third-party or downstream implementation of this interface (custom crypto providers deployed with Keycloak or with client libraries depending on keycloak-common) will no longer compile against the new interface, and classes compiled against the old interface will fail at runtime with `AbstractMethodError` when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` invokes `CryptoProvider::order` during provider sorting (CryptoIntegration.java line 57), which happens on every `CryptoIntegration.init` call. Since this is a public extension point, the method should have a default implementation (e.g. `default int order() { return 0; }`) to preserve source and binary compatibility.

title: Equal-order providers are now selected non-deterministically and misconfiguration no longer fails fast
body: The previous behavior threw an IllegalStateException when more than one CryptoProvider was found on the classpath, which protected against accidental misconfiguration. Now providers are silently sorted by `order()` and the first one wins. However, `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider` and `WildFlyElytronProvider` all return order 200, so when two of them are present the winner is decided solely by ServiceLoader iteration order (i.e. classpath/jar ordering), which is not deterministic. Concretely, a FIPS deployment that accidentally also has the non-FIPS default provider module on the classpath can silently start using non-FIPS-validated crypto with only a debug-level log line ("Ignored crypto providers"), instead of the previous hard failure. Ties on order should either be rejected or at least logged at warn/error level.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JVM default keystore provider, violating the interface contract
body: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is specified in `CryptoProvider` to return the BouncyCastle security provider, and callers in keycloak-common/core use it to obtain BC-specific algorithms (e.g. keystore types like BCFKS, PKCS7 ciphers). This implementation returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which on a stock JVM is the SUN provider. Any shared code path that reaches this method will get a provider that does not implement the BC algorithms the caller expects and fail in confusing ways (e.g. NoSuchAlgorithmException for BCFKS, or wrong padding behavior). Since the stated purpose of this provider is a minimal no-BC implementation where unsupported operations throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, this method should do the same rather than return an unrelated provider.

title: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER creates and discards two ASN1Encoder instances
body: Lines 114-115 (`ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger); ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);`) create two encoders, write the values into them and throw the results away; only the sequence built on lines 117-121 is returned. This is dead code left over from development that allocates objects for nothing and is confusing to readers. It should be removed.

title: Test only checks round-trip, not that the converted DER signature is a valid ECDSA signature
body: The test converts ASN.1 DER -> concatenated RS -> DER -> concatenated RS and asserts the two concatenated forms match. This would pass even if the DER re-encoding were wrong in a way that cancels out in the round-trip (e.g. incorrect minimal-encoding or sign handling in ASN1Encoder.write(BigInteger) producing invalid INTEGER encodings that the decoder mirrors). The test should verify the DER output with `Signature.initVerify(keyPair.getPublic())` (or compare `asn1Des` with the original `sign` bytes), and it should also cover edge cases such as r/s values with leading zero bytes or the high bit set. There is also no test that `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())` actually selects `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` via the new META-INF/services file and the ordering logic, which is the core mechanism introduced by this PR.

title: Adding abstract method order() to the CryptoProvider SPI breaks existing implementations
body: The new `int order();` method is added to the public `CryptoProvider` SPI interface without a default implementation. CryptoProvider is a published extension point loaded via ServiceLoader (documented Keycloak crypto SPI), so any third-party or downstream implementation compiled against the previous interface will (a) no longer compile and (b) at runtime fail with AbstractMethodError as soon as `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` calls `CryptoProvider::order` in the comparator while sorting the loaded providers. Previously-working custom crypto providers are therefore completely broken by this change, not just the new ordering feature. The method should be declared as `default int order() { return 0; }` (or similar) to preserve source and binary compatibility of the SPI.

title: Silent, order-tied provider selection removes the FIPS misconfiguration safeguard
body: detectProvider previously threw IllegalStateException when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath, which acted as a hard safety check against misconfigured deployments (most importantly a classpath accidentally containing both the non-FIPS DefaultCryptoProvider and FIPS1402Provider). Now it silently picks one and only logs ignored providers at debug level. Both DefaultCryptoProvider and FIPS1402Provider return order() == 200, so in a deployment that accidentally contains both, the winner is decided by ServiceLoader iteration order (classpath order), which can silently select the non-FIPS-approved provider in an environment intended to run in FIPS mode, with no warning at any noticeable log level. At minimum, equal-order providers should produce a warning, and the FIPS/non-FIPS collision should be handled deterministically or fail loudly as before.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JVM default keystore provider, violating the interface contract
body: The CryptoProvider contract for `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is to return the BouncyCastle (or BCFIPS) security provider. This implementation instead returns the provider of `KeyStore.getDefaultType()` (typically the SUN provider). Any shared code path in keycloak-common/keycloak-core that obtains the provider via this method and relies on BC-specific services (algorithms, keystore types like BCFKS/PKCS12 via BC, etc.) will get a provider that does not provide them, resulting in confusing NoSuchAlgorithmException/KeyStoreException failures rather than a clear 'not supported' signal, or worse, subtly different cryptographic behavior. Unlike the other methods that clearly throw UnsupportedOperationException, this one silently returns something that does not match the documented contract.

title: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER creates and discards two ASN1 encoders
body: Lines 114-115 (`ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger); ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);`) create two encoders, write the integers into them, and throw the results away; only the `writeDerSeq(...)` chain on lines 117-121 contributes to the returned value. The statements have no effect, allocate objects unnecessarily on every signature conversion (a hot path during JWT signature verification), and look like leftover debugging code that will confuse future readers.

title: ECDSA tests use a single P-256 keypair for ES384/ES512 and never verify the DER signature
body: The test generates one keypair with the JVM default curve (P-256) and reuses it for all three algorithms. For ES384/ES512 the concatenated r/s halves are zero-padded 32-byte values, so the tests never exercise values whose most significant byte within the target length is set, nor the truncation branch of integerToBytes for real 48/66-byte r/s values. Additionally, the test only checks the concat→DER→concat round trip; it never verifies that the DER produced by concatenatedRSToASN1DER is a valid ECDSA signature via Signature.verify with the public key, which is the actual purpose of the conversion. A bug producing a well-formed but value-incorrect DER encoding would only be caught indirectly. The tests should generate curve-appropriate keypairs (P-384, P-521) and assert Signature.verify(convertedSignature). There is also no test at all for the core mechanism of this PR: the ServiceLoader registration of AuthzClientCryptoProvider and the CryptoIntegration order()-based provider selection/priority logic.

title: getClientsWithPermission cannot return real client IDs and adds a bogus 'Clients' entry
body: getClientsWithPermission(String scope) collects results via resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). Per-client resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (AdminPermissionsSchema.java line 104) with resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner) and never have their type set to "Clients", so findByType will not match them; the only resource that carries the type is the all-type resource itself, whose name is the literal string "Clients" — not a valid client ID. Consequently the method can only ever return an empty set, or a set containing the invalid entry "Clients" when an all-clients permission grants the requested scope. Any consumer that uses this set to filter client lists (the V1 contract returns client IDs for this purpose) will either silently drop all clients that have explicit per-client permissions, or attempt to resolve the non-existent client "Clients". There is no test covering this method, so the defect is not caught by the new tests.

title: UnsupportedOperationException from inherited methods surfaces as HTTP 500 on existing admin REST endpoints
body: ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException from isPermissionsEnabled (line 188), setPermissionsEnabled (line 193), resource (line 198), getPermissions (line 203) and canExchangeTo (line 148). These methods are part of the inherited ClientPermissions contract and are still called by non-feature-gated code when the V2 feature is enabled: the standard admin endpoints GET/PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management/permissions (ClientManagementPermissionsResource) call AdminPermissions.management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled/isPermissionsEnabled/getPermissions. Since AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever the V2 feature flag is on (AdminPermissions.java line 67), those endpoints will return an uncontrolled HTTP 500 instead of a graceful 400/404 or a "not supported" response. The V2 feature should either gate these endpoints or return a proper error response rather than an unhandled runtime exception.

title: No migration for existing admin-permissions realms: new Clients scopes and resource are never created
body: init() returns early when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists (lines 226-228). For realms where the admin permissions client was initialized by a previous build (i.e., before the Clients resource type was added to the schema), the new scopes "configure", "map-roles-client-scope" and "map-roles-composite" and the "Clients" all-type resource are never created, and no migration is included in this change. On such upgraded realms, creating any Clients permission fails: getScope() throws ModelValidationException("Scope [configure] does not exist.") and getOrCreateResource() throws ModelException("No scopes found.") (line 108) because the scopes cannot be resolved. Existing V2-enabled realms therefore break after upgrade until the admin permissions client is deleted and re-created.

title: getResourceName not updated for the Clients resource type, returns null for client resources
body: getResourceName() only special-cases the Users resource type (resolving "Users" to "All users" and per-user resources to the username). For the newly added Clients type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Per-client resources are created in getOrCreateResource via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner) with name set to the client's internal ID and no display name, so getDisplayName() is null; the all-type "Clients" resource likewise has no display name. Any consumer of getResourceName (used to render resource names for permissions in the admin REST/console) will get null for every Clients permission, showing blank identifiers instead of the client name or an "All clients" label, unlike the Users behavior implemented in the same method.

title: Null resource passed to findByResource in hasPermission(ClientModel, String) fallback
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), when the per-client resource is not found the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) (line 217), which can return null (it returns null whenever supportsAuthorizationSchema is false, e.g. the realm's admin permissions are disabled while the admin permissions client and its resource server still exist). The result is passed directly to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) at line 219 without a null check — unlike the sibling hasPermission(String scope) at line 245 which does check for null. Depending on the store implementation this either relies on undefined behavior for a null lookup or risks a NullPointerException; the fallback should null-check the resource and return false, as the other overload does.

title: Javadoc for requireView()/requireViewClientScopes() claims they return a boolean
body: The javadoc added in this PR for requireView() (line 96, "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.") and requireViewClientScopes() (line 101, "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}.") describes a boolean return, but these are void methods that throw ForbiddenException when the check fails. The documentation should state that they throw ForbiddenException (as done for requireManage/requireConfigure/requireList), otherwise callers reading the interface may assume a return value.

title: Dead code: unused getEvaluationContext, TOKEN_EXCHANGE import, Scope import and logger
body: ClientPermissionsV2 contains leftovers from an abandoned token-exchange implementation: the private method getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) (lines 262-272) is never called, the static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46) and the import of org.keycloak.authorization.model.Scope (line 27) are unused, and the Logger field (line 51) is never used. This dead code should be removed together with the now-unsupported canExchangeTo, or the token-exchange support should be completed, so readers do not assume exchange evaluation is wired up.

title: NPE risk: getResourceTypeResource can return null and is passed directly to findByResource
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String) the fallback path does `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and then immediately calls `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)`. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the resource server is not the admin-permissions client, when admin permissions are disabled for the realm, or simply when no resource named "Clients" exists in the store (which is the case for any realm whose admin-permissions client was initialized before this resource type was added to the schema, since AdminPermissionsSchema.init() only creates the type resources on first creation). Passing a null Resource to findByResource will throw a NullPointerException (or a store-level error) during an authorization check, turning permission evaluation into a 500 error instead of a deny. The result of getResourceTypeResource must be null-checked before use.

title: Existence of a per-client resource silently disables the all-clients permission fallback
body: hasPermission(client, scope) only falls back to the "Clients" resource-type resource when no resource exists for the specific client. But a resource for a client is created as a side effect of ANY scope permission referencing that client, even one that grants the current admin nothing (e.g. a permission created by/for a different administrator). From that point on, evaluation only considers the per-client resource and the all-clients (resource-type) permission is ignored entirely. Consequence: an administrator who was granted e.g. MANAGE or VIEW on all clients via a resource-type permission will be wrongly denied access to any client that has any per-client permission defined, contradicting canManage()/canView() realm-wide semantics and the V1 behavior where realm-level and per-object permissions are combined. There is also no test covering the combination of an all-clients permission with a per-client permission for Clients, so this regression is unguarded.

title: getClientsWithPermission can return the literal "Clients" as a client ID
body: getClientsWithPermission(scope) iterates all resources of type CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE and adds resource.getName() to the result set. This includes the resource-type-level resource named "Clients" (created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init with type "Clients"), so when an all-clients permission grants the requested scope, the string "Clients" is added to a set that callers treat as a set of client IDs. Any caller doing a client lookup or membership check with these IDs will fail to resolve "Clients", producing wrong filtering (e.g. an admin with an all-clients map-roles permission getting an empty/bogus list of clients they can map roles for). The type-level resource must be excluded from the collected names (and ideally the caller informed that all clients are granted).

title: canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException and can surface as HTTP 500 in the token exchange flow
body: canExchangeTo(ClientModel, ClientModel, AccessToken) is part of the authorization evaluation API used by the token exchange code path to decide whether exchange into a target client is allowed. Overriding it to throw UnsupportedOperationException means that, in realms with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, any code path that still calls this method will fail with an unhandled exception (HTTP 500 on a token request) rather than a proper deny (returning false) or a clean 4xx. The same applies to the other evaluation-adjacent overrides (isPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource). If these are intentionally unsupported in V2 they should return a safe default or the endpoints/call sites should be feature-gated so they are never reached under V2, not blow up at runtime.

title: registerListener guards on the V1 feature flag but management() dispatches to V2, causing exceptions or missing cleanup
body: The listener now only runs when Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled, but AdminPermissions.management() returns a MgmtPermissionsV2 (and thus ClientPermissionsV2) whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. Two problems follow: (1) if both features are enabled at once (nothing prevents `--features=admin-fine-grained-authz,admin-fine-grained-authz-v2`), the ClientRemovedEvent handler calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which ClientPermissionsV2 overrides to throw UnsupportedOperationException — the exception fires inside the client-removal event listener and can abort client deletion with a 500. (2) with V2-only, no cleanup happens at all, so per-client authorization resources in the admin-permissions resource server are orphaned when a client is deleted, accumulating stale resources that keep being returned by getClientsWithPermission. The guard and the dispatch target use different feature flags and need to be reconciled.

title: No migration path: existing admin-permissions realms lack the Clients resource and the new scopes
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns early when the realm already has an admin-permissions client, so it only creates the schema resources/scopes at first enablement. A realm that enabled admin permissions before this change has only the "Users" resource and the scopes manage/view/impersonate/map-roles/manage-group-membership. After this change, such a realm has no "Clients" resource and no configure/map-roles-client-scope/map-roles-composite scopes, so creating any client permission referencing those scopes fails with "Scope [x] does not exist", and getResourceTypeResource for "Clients" returns null (which then triggers the NPE described for ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission). Even if the V2 feature is preview and migration is not guaranteed, either a migration/upgrade step or a lazy re-sync of schema resources and scopes on realm load is needed, otherwise previously working realms break on upgrade.

title: getResourceName not updated for the Clients resource type, returning null display names
body: getResourceName resolves user resources to a username and special-cases the "Users" all-resource as "All users", but no branch was added for the new CLIENTS resource type. For per-client resources, which are auto-created in getOrCreateResource with name = client's internal ID and no display name, the method falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is null. Any consumer of getResourceName (e.g. building policy/permission representations for the admin UI) will render null instead of a client name/clientId for client permissions, and the "Clients" all-resource will show its raw type name instead of a friendly label like "All clients".

title: Client removal listener throws UnsupportedOperationException under V2 because guard checks the V1 feature flag
body: In registerListener, the event handling is now guarded by Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) (the V1 flag), but the handler calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). When the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 feature is enabled (which depends on the V1 feature being enabled), management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). The ClientRemovedEvent listener therefore throws on every client deletion on a server with V2 enabled, breaking client deletion even in realms that do not use fine-grained admin permissions. The guard should also exclude the V2 feature (or the V2 implementation should be a no-op instead of throwing).

title: canExchangeTo/isPermissionsEnabled/getPermissions throw UnsupportedOperationException from live request paths
body: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo (line 149), isPermissionsEnabled (line 189), getPermissions (line 204) and setPermissionsEnabled (line 194) all throw UnsupportedOperationException. These are not dead code: the token exchange flow invokes canExchangeTo on the admin permission evaluator (AdminPermissions.evaluator returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever the V2 feature is enabled), and the admin REST 'management/permissions' endpoints for a client invoke isPermissionsEnabled/getPermissions/setPermissionsEnabled. With the V2 feature enabled, those requests will fail with a 500 error instead of being denied or handled. These overrides should return a safe default (e.g. false/null) rather than throwing, or the calling code must be updated to handle V2.

title: hasPermission(client, scope) can pass a null Resource to PolicyStore.findByResource and NPE
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no resource exists for the specific client, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE). That method returns null when the schema is not supported for this resource server (e.g. realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled() is false while the admin permissions client still exists) or when the aggregate 'Clients' resource was never created (realms whose admin permissions client was initialized before this change, since init() only creates resources on first setup). The null is then passed directly to authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource), which throws a NullPointerException (store implementations dereference resource.getId()) instead of cleanly denying access. A null check on the result of getResourceTypeResource is needed before querying the policy store.

title: init() does not migrate existing admin permissions clients: 'Clients' resource and new scopes are never created
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null (lines 226-228), so realms that already enabled admin permissions under V2 before this change (Users resource type only) will never get the new 'Clients' aggregate resource or the new scopes 'configure', 'map-roles-client-scope' and 'map-roles-composite'. On such realms, creating a Clients permission referencing those scopes fails ('Scope [configure] does not exist' / 'No scopes found' ModelException from getOrCreateResource line 108), and ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String scope) at line 244 silently returns false because findByName for 'Clients' yields nothing — admins appear to have no client permissions at all with no diagnostic. A migration step is needed to add the new scopes and the 'Clients' resource to existing admin permissions clients.

title: getClientsWithPermission includes the aggregate 'Clients' resource name in the returned client-id set
body: getClientsWithPermission iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). The aggregate 'Clients' resource created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init() also carries type 'Clients', so it is included in the callback. When a blanket permission on it is granted, the method adds the literal string "Clients" to the returned set of names. Callers that treat the result as the set of client IDs the admin may access get a bogus entry that matches no client, and more importantly a blanket all-clients grant is represented as a single meaningless ID rather than 'all clients', so a filtering caller would show the admin an empty client list despite the grant. The aggregate resource (name equal to CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) should be excluded, and a grant on it should be surfaced as a wildcard/all-clients result.

title: Javadoc for requireView()/requireViewClientScopes() incorrectly describes them as boolean getters
body: The newly added javadoc on requireView() (lines 95-98) reads "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}" — but requireView() is a void method that throws ForbiddenException based on canView(), not canViewClientScopes(). Likewise the javadoc for requireViewClientScopes() (lines 100-103) says "Returns {@code true} if ..." for a void require-method. The docs contradict the method signatures and reference the wrong predicate.

title: Null-strategy test parameterization does not actually test the 'feature disabled' path; it relies on the feature being baked into the custom image
body: createInitialDeployment returns early for the null (default) strategy without enabling the `rolling-updates` feature in the Keycloak CR, which reads as if the default-strategy tests exercise the operator without the feature. However, the same PR modifies operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image to run `kc.sh build ... --features=rolling-updates`, so the feature is enabled inside the image the tests deploy regardless of the CR. This means the documented behavior in docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc ("While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail") is never actually tested: there is no test where the feature is genuinely absent and the operator's failure mode is asserted. In particular testCacheMaxCount with the null strategy expects eventuallyRollingUpgradeStatus, which only works because the operator's compatibility check succeeds against the image-baked feature. A real user deploying a stock image without the feature would hit the documented failure, which no test covers. Either the parameterization should explicitly enable/disable the feature in the CR for both strategies, or a negative test for the feature-disabled failure should be added.

title: No test asserts the new exit code 4 (feature disabled), the documented scripting contract
body: The PR introduces exit code 4 (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) and documents it in docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc as the contract for CI/CD scripts ("Exit Code 4: Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled."). However, testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message text via cliResult.assertError(...); it never asserts that the process actually exits with code 4. Since the whole point of the exit-code table is to be relied upon by automation, and the check command's feature-disabled path is not tested at all (only the metadata command is), a regression that returns a different exit code would go unnoticed. Add exit-code assertions (e.g., assertEquals(4, result.exitCode())) and a test for the check subcommand with the feature disabled.

title: Exit code 4 description is inaccurate for the metadata subcommand
body: The exit-code table describes exit code 4 as "Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled." That description only makes sense for the `check` subcommand. The `metadata` subcommand (update-compatibility metadata) also exits with code 4 when the feature is disabled (UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()), but in that case no rolling-upgrade evaluation happened and no metadata was produced — it is simply a command failure. Script authors handling both subcommands with one exit-code table will misinterpret a code 4 from `metadata` as an incompatibility verdict rather than 'the command did not run'. The table should state that exit code 4 means the command was not executed because the feature is disabled.

title: CAUTION claims the operator fails without the rolling-updates feature, but the scope is wrong
body: The new CAUTION block in the 'Managing Keycloak Operator Updates' section states unconditionally: 'While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail.' This is contradicted by this PR's own tests (UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment): when no update strategy is set (the default case, which the same page documents as a valid configuration), the ROLLING_UPDATES feature is NOT enabled and the operator is expected to work (testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount run with null strategy and no feature). A reader will conclude that every deployment — or at least any deployment using the default update behavior — must enable the feature or the operator breaks, which is not the case per the tests. The caution should be scoped to explicitly setting `spec.update.strategy` (e.g. `Recreate`), matching what the tests and the rest of the section actually require.

title: New and changed exit codes (3 and 4) are never asserted in tests
body: This PR changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and introduces exit code 4 for the feature-disabled case, and the documentation explicitly promises these exit codes to scripting/CI consumers ('they should rely only on the exit code of the check command'). Yet no test asserts them: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the stderr message, not exit code 4; testWrongVersions asserts only the error message, not exit code 3; testCompatible only asserts exit code 0 for the metadata command, not for the check command. A regression in any of these exit codes (e.g. accidentally reusing 4, or returning the picocli default 1) would pass the entire suite while breaking the documented contract that automation depends on.

title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changes from 4 to 3 and 4 is reused for feature-disabled
body: The check command previously exited with 4 when a recreate upgrade was required; it now exits with 3, and 4 is repurposed to mean 'the rolling-updates feature is disabled'. While this aligns the code with the existing documentation (which already documented 3 for recreate), any user who scripted against the actually-shipped behavior will now see exit code 4 (previously 'recreate needed') only when the feature is disabled, and exit code 3 where they expected 4 — i.e. existing pipelines that branch on these codes will misclassify results. Since both values ultimately mean 'do not do a rolling upgrade' the practical impact is limited, but the release notes / upgrade docs should call out this behavioral change for early adopters of the preview command.

title: New preview feature ROLLING_UPDATES is not added to the documented feature list
body: This PR introduces a new preview feature, ROLLING_UPDATES (key 'rolling-updates'), but the server documentation page that enumerates supported/preview/experimental features (docs/guides/server/features.adoc, the 'Enabling and disabling features' guide) is not updated. Users looking up what `--features=rolling-updates` enables, or which preview features exist, will find no mention of it, even though other guides in this same PR instruct users to enable it. The feature table should be updated in the same change that adds the enum entry.

title: Exit code 4 is repurposed from 'recreate required' to 'feature disabled'
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3, and the new FEATURE_DISABLED code takes the value 4. The documentation has always stated 3 means 'recreate required', so the code change fixes an inconsistency; however, any automation written against the previously shipped binary observed exit code 4 for 'recreate required'. After this change, such a script that checks `exit == 4` will instead see it when the rolling-updates feature is disabled, and could wrongly conclude a recreate (downtime) upgrade is required, or vice versa miss a genuine recreate signal now delivered as 3. Since the guide explicitly tells users to build automation on the exit codes, a release note or version-aware handling should accompany this repurposing.

title: Feature-disabled path only tested for 'metadata' and without asserting the new exit code 4
body: The new testFeatureNotEnabled only launches the `metadata` subcommand and only asserts the error message text. The documentation added in this PR promises a specific exit code 4 ('The feature rolling-updates is disabled') and the same gate is implemented in both UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata, but neither the exit code nor the `check` subcommand's disabled path is verified. If the gate is accidentally removed, the exit code changes, or the check command crashes (e.g., NPE from Profile not being initialized) instead of exiting 4, no test would catch it. The test should assert exitCode() == 4 and cover `check` as well.

title: Global canManage() accepts the VIEW scope, allowing view-only admins to create groups
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (the no-arg, realm-wide check) falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Because the expected-scope list includes VIEW, an admin who was granted only the `view` scope on the type-level Groups resource passes `canManage()`/`requireManage()`. `requireManage()` guards `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` (POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups), so a view-only admin can create (and via the same check path move) top-level groups. This looks like a copy-paste from canView(); it should be `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, mirroring the per-group override at line 79 which correctly checks only MANAGE.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs (UUIDs) instead of group IDs
body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code does `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` and `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`. Per-group resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` where the resource *name* is the group ID; the resource *ID* is a store-generated UUID. The private hasPermission(String groupId, ...) at line 141 looks resources up with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, i.e. it expects a name, so passing a resource ID never finds the per-group resource and silently falls back to the type-level "Groups" resource. Worse, the returned set is consumed as *group IDs* by UsersResource.searchForUser/getUsersCount and BruteForceUsersResource (it is set as the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute used for storage-level filtering by group membership). An admin whose visibility comes from group member permissions therefore gets a set of resource UUIDs: the storage filter matches no groups, user searches return no users and user counts return 0 — notably for a type-level view-members/manage-members permission, where the UUID of the type-level resource is the only entry added. The V1 implementation this replaces explicitly derived group IDs from resource names (GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, `resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())`). Additionally, getOrCreateResource never sets a resource type, so findByType("Groups") may only match the type-level resource and per-group view-members permissions may not be reflected in the set at all. The code should use groupResource.getName() for both the permission lookup and the granted set.

title: V2 group permission management throws UnsupportedOperationException in code paths that are still invoked
body: GroupPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled (and isPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource, etc.) to throw UnsupportedOperationException. But these methods are still called when the V2 feature is active: (1) AdminPermissions.registerListener (AdminPermissions.java:94) registers a GroupRemovedEvent listener whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled — which is the base feature the V2 feature builds on — and the listener calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)`. With MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() now returning GroupPermissionsV2, deleting any group fires the event and the listener throws, failing the group deletion (and if only V2 is enabled the listener is not registered, so per-group resources/policies are never cleaned up and stale authorization data accumulates). (2) GroupResource.getManagementPermissions/setManagementPermissionsEnabled call permissions.groups().isPermissionsEnabled(group)/getPermissions(group), which previously worked (MgmtPermissionsV2 used the V1 GroupPermissions implementation) and now turn into HTTP 500 responses. These operations need real V2 implementations (e.g. resource/policy cleanup) rather than throwing.

title: Tests leak created groups, making count assertions order-dependent
body: In GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest, testManageAllGroups creates the group "testGroup" (later renamed to "newGroup") via ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse without registering a realm.cleanup() entry (compare the other tests that do `realm.cleanup().add(r -> r.groups().group(id).remove())`), and testManageGroup creates "subGroup" through the subGroup(...) call at line 226 (expecting 201) also without cleanup. The managed realm persists across test methods in the class, while testViewGroups asserts exact result sizes (hasSize(0), hasSize(1), hasSize(2)) and testManageAllGroups asserts exact counts of visible groups. Depending on JUnit's method execution order, the leaked groups make these assertions fail intermittently.

title: getResourceName does not handle the newly added Groups resource type
body: This PR adds the Groups resource type to the schema, but getResourceName() still only special-cases USERS: for a Users type-level resource it returns "All users" and maps per-user resources to the user's username. Group resources fall through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which for per-group resources created by getOrCreateResource is the raw group ID (the resource name). Permission/resource listings in the admin API and console will therefore show bare UUIDs for group permissions instead of a group name or path, unlike users.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code iterates group resources and does `granted.add(groupResource.getId())`. Per-group resources in the V2 schema are created (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource) with the group's ID as the resource *name* and a store-generated internal ID, which is what `getId()` returns. Every consumer of the returned set treats it as a set of group IDs: UsersResource.getUsersCount passes it to `session.users().getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)`, and UsersResource.searchForUser / BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser set it as the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute used for DB-level membership filtering. With resource UUIDs instead of group IDs, those queries match no groups, so a group-scoped admin gets empty user searches and wrong (zero) user counts. Additionally, on line 122 `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` passes a resource ID into a method that resolves resources via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` (i.e. it expects a group ID), so the per-group resource is never matched and evaluation silently falls back to the all-groups resource — per-group view-members/manage-members permissions therefore never contribute their group to the set. The V1 implementation correctly derived the group ID from the resource name (`resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())`); this should use `groupResource.getName()`. The new tests don't catch this because the per-user `canView` filter compensates in the search endpoint; no test exercises getUsersCount or the DB-level GROUPS filtering with group permissions.

title: canManage() grants manage access when only the VIEW scope is granted on the Groups resource type
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (the no-arg, realm-wide variant) is implemented as `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it returns true when the caller has *either* the view or the manage scope on the all-groups resource. This is inconsistent with canManage(GroupModel) (line 79), which correctly checks only the MANAGE scope, and with canView(), which legitimately accepts view-or-manage. Consequence: an admin who was granted only the `view` scope on the "Groups" resource type passes `auth.groups().requireManage()` and can create top-level groups (GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup) and move existing groups to the top level — a privilege escalation within fine-grained admin permissions. It also produces the nonsensical state where such an admin can create a group but then cannot update or delete it (canManage(group) correctly denies). The line should be `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. The new tests never attempt a manage operation with a view-only permission, so this is uncaught.

title: setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking the group-removal cleanup listener under V2
body: GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(group, enable) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). However, AdminPermissions.registerListener (AdminPermissions.java line 94) registers a ProviderEventListener that, on GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent, calls `management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)`. When both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (which gates listener registration) and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 (which makes AdminPermissions.management() return MgmtPermissionsV2, whose groups() now returns GroupPermissionsV2 — previously it returned the V1 GroupPermissions) are enabled, deleting any group triggers the UnsupportedOperationException during event processing, failing the delete request or its permission cleanup. Before this change MgmtPermissionsV2 inherited the working V1 implementation. Either the V2 class must perform equivalent cleanup (or no-op safely) or the listener must be adjusted for V2. Note the same applies to GroupResource.setManagementPermissionsEnabled, which calls permissions.groups().setPermissionsEnabled and would now return a raw 500 UnsupportedOperationException instead of a graceful error.

title: hasPermission can dereference a null fallback resource from getResourceTypeResource
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(), when no per-group resource exists, the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. That method returns null whenever `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false — e.g. when the realm's admin permissions flag is disabled while the admin permissions client (and thus its resource server) still exists. The result is then passed to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later `resource.getScopes()` without a null check, producing a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) on any group permission check (group view/manage/members) for an admin without realm roles. The identical pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2, but this new code copies it; a null check returning false (mirroring the `server == null` early return) is needed.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission mixes resource IDs with group IDs and cannot find per-group resources
body: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission enumerates resources with resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and then both looks up permissions with hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the result set.
