This is wrong on two counts: (1) per-group resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, clientId) with the group id as the resource NAME and a store-generated ID, and without setting the resource type, so findByType("Groups") never returns them; (2) hasPermission resolves resources with findByName(...), so passing a resource's generated ID as a 'group id' finds nothing and falls through to the all-groups type resource. Consequences: an admin holding only per-group view-members/manage-members grants gets an empty set, so the UserModel.GROUPS filter used by UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource user search and getUsersCount is never applied at the DB level — searches scan all realm users and rely on the in-memory canView filter, which breaks pagination (first/max are applied before filtering) and returns wrong counts. Worse, an admin holding a view-members/manage-members grant on the type-level 'Groups' resource gets that resource's UUID added as a bogus 'group id', so user search and getUsersCount return zero users even though canView(user) evaluates to true. The existing tests pass only because the in-memory usersEvaluator::canView filter compensates; nothing covers the all-groups or paginated cases.

title: canManage() (no-arg) grants manage rights for a view-only permission on Groups
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (the global, no-argument variant) falls back to hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), i.e. a caller granted only the 'view' scope on the Groups type resource passes the manage check. requireManage() (no-arg) guards POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups (GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup), which both creates top-level groups and, when the representation carries an existing group id, moves that group to the top level via realm.moveGroup. So an admin explicitly granted only 'view' on Groups can create groups and move arbitrary existing groups. The per-group variant canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires MANAGE only, as does UserPermissions.canManage() for the Users resource; the no-arg variant should not accept VIEW. The javadoc added in GroupPermissionEvaluator matches this code, but the behavior contradicts the method's contract and the per-group semantics.

title: UnsupportedOperationException thrown on live code paths (group deletion, management-permissions endpoints)
body: GroupPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled, isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, viewPermission, etc. to throw UnsupportedOperationException, but these methods are still invoked on real paths when the V2 feature is active. AdminPermissions.registerListener (guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ flag, which can be enabled together with — or implied by — ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2) calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) on every GroupRemovedEvent, so deleting any group in a V2 realm throws UnsupportedOperationException and the DELETE fails with a 500. Similarly GroupResource.getManagementPermissions/setManagementPermissionsEnabled call isPermissionsEnabled(group)/getPermissions(group) after ProfileHelper.requireFeature(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), which now returns 500 instead of the previous working V1 behavior (before this change MgmtPermissionsV2 fell back to the functional V1 GroupPermissions implementation). Either these paths must be guarded/disabled for V2 realms or the V2 implementation must handle them instead of throwing.

title: Existing admin-permissions realms never get the Groups resource or the new group scopes (no migration)
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null. Realms where the admin permissions client was already created (e.g., with the earlier Clients resource type support) will therefore never receive the new 'Groups' type-level resource or the new group scopes (manage-membership, manage-members, view-members) that init() creates from the schema. In such realms, creating any group scope permission fails: getOrCreateResource does scopeStore.findByName(...) for each schema scope and throws ModelException("No scopes found.") when a scope is missing, and getScope rejects the request with "Scope [...] does not exist". Additionally getResourceTypeResource(session, server, "Groups") returns null because the type resource was never created, which makes GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission fall into the null-resource path. A migration (or lazy creation of missing type resources/scopes for existing admin-permissions clients) is needed; otherwise upgraded realms cannot use the new Groups resource type at all.

title: hasPermission can NPE when the 'Groups' type resource cannot be resolved
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission, when the per-group resource is not found the code assigns resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) without a null check, then calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later resource.getScopes(). getResourceTypeResource returns null whenever supportsAuthorizationSchema is false — e.g., the realm's admin permissions flag is disabled while the admin permissions client (and its resource server) still exists, or the 'Groups' type resource is missing in a pre-existing realm (see the init()/migration issue). In those states, any group permission evaluation (canView(group), requireView(group) on GET /groups/{id}, etc.) throws a NullPointerException instead of denying access. A null check returning false is needed. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission, but GroupPermissionsV2 is newly added by this PR.

title: No test covers user search/count with a type-level (all-groups) permission or pagination under group-scoped permissions
body: The new tests only exercise user search for admins holding per-group view-members/manage-members grants on a single group in a realm with two users, where the in-memory usersEvaluator::canView filter masks any problem in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission. There is no test for: (a) an admin holding view-members on the type-level 'Groups' resource performing user search/getUsersCount (this currently returns zero users because the resource UUID is used as a group id); (b) pagination/first/max correctness when the DB-level group filter is absent or wrong (currently searches scan all users and filter in memory); (c) getUsersCount with group-scoped admins. Adding these would catch the broken group-id enumeration in GroupPermissionsV2.

title: Lithuanian translations replaced with Italian text
body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian account messages file was changed to "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian, not Lithuanian (the old text was Lithuanian). The same happens in themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties line 71 (loginTotpStep1). Lithuanian users will now see an Italian sentence on the OTP setup page.

title: Traditional Chinese text inserted into Simplified Chinese file
body: The new totpStep1 value "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：" uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機/應用程式) and Traditional-style phrasing, while the rest of messages_zh_CN.properties is Simplified Chinese (手机/应用). The replacement should be "在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：".

title: error-invalid-multivalued-size switched from i18next to Java MessageFormat syntax in JS themes
body: The value was changed from "Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s)." to "Attribute {0} ... {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.". The admin-ui (keycloak.v2) and account-ui (keycloak.v3) React apps render their messages via i18next, which uses {{param}} interpolation and has no support for Java MessageFormat choice patterns. With the new value, users of these JS themes will see literal "Attribute {0}" and the raw "{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}" string instead of an interpolated message. The same change was made in js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3/account/messages/messages_en.properties (line 188) and js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources-community/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_zh_CN.properties. The choice-format version is only correct for the server-side Java themes under themes/src/main/resources.

title: Missing English bundle crashes the verifier with a raw RuntimeException
body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file path by string-replacing the absolute file path (replaceAll("resources-community", "resources") plus a locale-suffix regex) and then throws a bare RuntimeException if that file cannot be opened. Any message file whose _en counterpart is not at the exact derived location (e.g. a theme that only exists in resources-community, a differently named directory, or a file without a locale suffix such as messages.properties mapping onto itself) will abort the whole mojo with a stack trace instead of being reported as a verification message like every other problem the verifier finds. The failure should be recorded in the returned messages list (or wrapped in MojoExecutionException), and the path derivation is too fragile to be a hard precondition.

title: ANCHOR_PATTERN also matches non-anchor tags starting with 'a'
body: The pattern "</?a[^>]*>" used to detect anchors matches any tag whose name starts with the letter 'a' — <article>, <abbr>, <address>, <audio>, etc. — because [^>]* consumes the rest of the tag name. If a translation legitimately contains such a tag (or one is introduced later), santizeAnchors will treat it as an anchor, fail to find it in the English source, and emit a spurious "Didn't find anchor tag" error. The pattern should be "</?a(\s[^>]*)?>" so only the anchor element is matched.

title: Policy allows br/p/strong/b whenever English has any HTML, including only anchors
body:
The per-key policy decision is containsHtml(englishValue) ? POLICY_SOME_HTML : POLICY_NO_HTML, where containsHtml matches any tag. So for a key whose English value contains only an tag (anchors are removed afterwards by santizeAnchors), a translation may freely add ,

, or
elements that the English source never had. This is weaker than the stated intent ("only if the English source string contains HTML we also allow HTML in the translation") and lets translations introduce formatting/markup the source string does not contain.

title: No test that valid translations produce no findings
body: All new tests assert that violations are detected; there is no test asserting that a legitimate translation (e.g. one containing the same anchors as the English source, allowed tags like <strong>, escaped entities, or the {2,choice,...} pattern) passes with an empty message list. The verification logic relies on subtle round-trips (unescapeHtml4 on both sides, "<!-- -->" removal, anchor stripping) where a false-positive regression would only surface as build failures on the real theme files rather than a clear unit test failure.

title: error-invalid-multivalued-size switched from i18next {{n}} to Java MessageFormat syntax, breaking interpolation in the account console
body: The keycloak.v3 account console is a React app whose message bundle is formatted with i18next double-curly-brace interpolation - every other parameterized key in this same file uses '{{0}}'/'{{1}}' (e.g. error-invalid-length-too-short on line 27, error-username-invalid-character on line 14). This change rewrites error-invalid-multivalued-size to single-brace '{0}' plus a Java ChoiceFormat pattern '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}'. i18next does not interpolate single braces and cannot evaluate Java choice syntax, so users who trigger the multivalued-attribute validation error will see the literal string "Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}." The choice syntax is only valid for the server-side (FreeMarker/Java MessageFormat) bundles under themes/src/main/resources; the React bundles should keep '{{n}}' (and express pluralization differently, e.g. i18next plural forms).

title: error-invalid-multivalued-size switched from {{n}} to Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax in the i18next-based admin console bundle
body: The keycloak.v2 admin console messages are rendered by the React admin UI with i18next double-curly-brace interpolation; the previous value of this key used '{{0}}', '{{1}}', '{{2}}' like the other parameterized keys in this bundle. The new value uses single-brace '{0}' and the Java-only ChoiceFormat pattern '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}', which i18next cannot interpolate or evaluate. When this validation message is shown in the admin UI, users will see the raw placeholders and the literal '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' text instead of a formatted message. The choice-format variant belongs only in the server-side bundles (themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/{login,admin}/messages), not in the React apps' bundles.

title: Missing English reference file aborts the whole verification with a raw RuntimeException
body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English reference file by string-replacing "resources-community" with "resources" and rewriting the locale suffix of the absolute path with the regex "_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties" -> "_en.properties" (lines 74-75). If the derived file does not exist - a new locale file with no English counterpart, a module whose directory layout does not follow this convention, or an English file named differently - the code throws a bare RuntimeException. verify() only converts IOException to MojoExecutionException, so this exception propagates uncaught and aborts the entire verification run with an unrelated stack trace, instead of being reported as a per-file message like the other problems this verifier detects. The path-based mapping itself is fragile: it silently depends on the exact maven directory naming of every module containing message properties.

title: Diff-highlighting substring can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when common prefix and suffix overlap
body: When a value and its sanitized form differ, the code computes the longest common prefix (start) and suffix (end) and then calls sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end) and value.substring(start, value.length() - end). Nothing guarantees start + end <= sanitized.length(). Example: for the value "text><b>y" under POLICY_NO_HTML the sanitizer drops the <b> tag and yields "text>y"; the common prefix is "text>" (start=5) and the common suffix is ">y" (end=2), so start+end=7 exceeds the sanitized length 6 and sanitized.substring(5, 4) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. This only happens on the error-reporting path - i.e. exactly when a violation has been found - so instead of emitting the intended "Illegal HTML in key ..." message the build crashes with a stack trace and the actual violation is never reported.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: As part of removing the hardcoded FreeOTP/Google Play links, loginTotpStep1 was rewritten as "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:" - which is Italian, not Lithuanian (correct would be e.g. "Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame telefone:"). The same Italian string was also pasted into the Lithuanian account bundle (totpStep1 in themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties, line 101).

title: Lithuanian account totpStep1 replaced with Italian text

This appears to be a copy-paste from an Italian translation; Lithuanian users of the account console's OTP setup page will see Italian text instead of Lithuanian.

title: Traditional Chinese text used in the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) account bundle

This looks like it was copied from the zh_TW translation. Users of the Simplified Chinese account console will see Traditional characters, which is inconsistent with the rest of the bundle.

title: No positive test covering valid translations that the sanitizer must accept
body:
All four tests assert that violations are detected; there is no test asserting that a legitimate translation passes verification. The acceptance path contains substantial normalization logic - HTML entity unescaping round-trip, removal of the sanitizer-inserted "" around double-curly-brace placeholders, the "
" (with space) versus "
" distinction, the email RTL style stripping, and the choice-format stripping for error-invalid-multivalued-size / linkExpirationFormatter keys. A regression in any of these (e.g. the sanitizer changing how it emits
or {{...}}) would turn every valid translation into a false 'Illegal HTML' failure and break the build, and the current test suite would give no signal that the verifier ever accepted valid input.

title: error-invalid-multivalued-size now uses single-brace placeholders and Java ChoiceFormat in an i18next-consumed bundle
body: This file is consumed by the React account console via i18next, which is why every other entry uses double-brace interpolation (e.g. "error-username-invalid-character='{{0}}' contains invalid character." on line 14) and <0>-style Trans component tags (line 13). The new value "Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}." uses single braces, which i18next does not interpolate, and Java MessageFormat choice syntax, which i18next cannot evaluate. If this key is rendered in the account UI, users will see the literal text "{0}", "{1}" and "{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}" instead of a formatted message. The Java-side MessageFormat version belongs in themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages (where {0} is correct), not in the keycloak.v3 JS bundle.

title: error-invalid-multivalued-size changed to Java ChoiceFormat syntax in the admin console JS message bundle
body: The keycloak.v2 admin messages bundle is loaded by the admin console's JS i18n layer (i18next), not by Java MessageFormat. Replacing "value(s)" with "{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}" means the admin UI cannot render this validation message: the choice expression will be displayed literally to administrators, and single-brace {0}/{1}/{2} placeholders are not interpolated by i18next's default {{...}} syntax. The MessageFormat variant should only live in the server-side theme bundles (themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/admin/messages and themes/src/main/resources-community/...), not in this JS resource.

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: totpStep1 was changed from a Lithuanian translation to the Italian sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". Lithuanian users of the account theme's authenticator setup page will now be shown instructions in Italian. It should read e.g. "Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame telefone:".

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: loginTotpStep1 in the Lithuanian login theme was replaced with the Italian sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:" instead of a Lithuanian translation, so the OTP setup page of the login theme will show Italian text to Lithuanian users.

title: Simplified Chinese file updated with Traditional Chinese text
body: totpStep1 was changed to "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：", which is Traditional Chinese (機/應/個), in the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) account bundle. The correct Simplified rendering would be "在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：". This is consistent with the original text being copied from a zh_TW/zh_HK source rather than translated.

title: English reference bundle located via fragile path string rewriting; missing counterpart crashes the mojo with a raw RuntimeException
body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file by running replaceAll("resources-community", "resources") and replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties") on the absolute file path, then does "new FileInputStream(englishFile)" and throws a bare RuntimeException on IOException (lines 76-80). Two problems: (1) any messages file that exists only under resources-community (or under a JS module theme whose product counterpart is absent) has no derived _en sibling, so the whole verification build aborts with "unable to read file ..." instead of reporting a per-file message like the rest of the checker; (2) the replaceAll of "resources-community" operates on the entire absolute path, so any other occurrence of that substring (e.g. in a checkout/workspace directory name) silently corrupts the resolved path. Failure to locate the English bundle should degrade to a reported message (or MojoExecutionException), not an uncaught RuntimeException, and the mapping should be done on the file name/directory structure explicitly.

title: Anchor check requires anchors to appear in the same order and byte-identical form as the English source
body: santizeAnchors() walks anchors in the translation and the English value in parallel and only accepts a pair when matcher.group() equals englishMatcher.group() exactly. A legitimate translation that reorders two links within one message (common when sentence structure differs), or that differs in attribute quoting/spacing inside the <a> tag while keeping the same href, will be rejected with "Didn't find anchor tag ..." even though it contains exactly the anchors from the source. This will produce false build failures for future translation contributions and push translators toward keeping English word order.

title: No positive test: valid HTML matching the English source should produce no messages
body:
All new tests assert that violations are detected (illegal tag, HTML without English counterpart, changed anchor). There is no test that a translation containing exactly the anchors and allowed tags (/

//
) present in the English source yields an empty message list. Without such a passing-case test, a regression in the normalization/unescaping pipeline that makes the checker flag every file with HTML (e.g. the "" stripping or the unescapeHtml4 round-trip) would not be caught by the suite.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong offset, so it never validates the grant shortcut
body: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId (line 483), the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is inverted: it returns false (no match) exactly when the extracted characters EQUAL the expected grant shortcut, and continues (match) when they differ. Additionally, the offset is wrong: in the encoded token ID the grant-type shortcut occupies characters at indices 4-5 (after 2 chars of session type and 2 chars of token type), so it should be `substring(4, 6)`; `substring(3, 5)` reads the second token-type char plus the first grant char. Net effect: for a correctly encoded ID like `onrtac:<uuid>`, the matcher extracts "ta", which never equals "ac", so the grant shortcut is effectively not checked at all — tests using expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken would pass even if the server encoded the wrong grant type, and could spuriously fail for IDs whose characters 3-4 coincidentally equal the expected shortcut. Fix both the negation and the substring bounds.

title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
body: In AccessTokenContext's constructor, line 73 reads `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` — a copy/paste of the grantType check on line 72. The `rawTokenId` parameter is therefore never null-checked: a null rawTokenId is silently accepted, and if it ever triggered, the exception message would misleadingly say "Null grantType not allowed". Change the second check to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

title: New abstract getShortcut() method breaks existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: Adding `String getShortcut();` as an abstract method to the public SPI interface OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is a source- and binary-incompatible change: every existing custom grant-type factory deployed as an extension will fail to compile against the new version, and pre-built jars will throw AbstractMethodError at runtime when Keycloak's DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory calls getShortcut() during postInit (which happens at server startup, so the whole server can fail to boot for those deployments). Provide a `default` implementation (e.g. deriving a shortcut from getId() or returning a documented fallback) to preserve compatibility.

title: Public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) removed and grantType becomes stale after setFormParams
body: Two related issues in OAuth2GrantType.Context: (1) The public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` was deleted. It was part of the public SPI surface (this class lives in server-spi-private and is implemented/used by third-party grant extensions), so removing it is a compile-time break for any external code that wrapped or derived a Context. (2) The new `grantType` field is captured once in the constructor from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`, but `setFormParams(...)` (which external grant implementations can use to swap in re-parsed form params) does not refresh `grantType`. Consequently, when token issuance later reads `context.getGrantType()` in OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse and encodes it into the access-token ID, the encoded grant type can be wrong/stale relative to the form params actually in effect, silently corrupting the context metadata this PR introduces.

title: Lazy map refresh can silently corrupt grant-type/shortcut mappings on shortcut collisions
body: In getShortcutByGrantType (and getGrantTypeByShortcut), when a grant type is not found in the cached maps, the factory refreshes the cache by blindly doing `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` without checking whether that shortcut is already mapped to a different grant type. If a newly deployed custom grant reuses a shortcut already assigned to another grant (e.g. "ac"), the put overwrites the existing reverse mapping, and from then on tokens containing that shortcut decode to the wrong grant type — data corruption in the token context with no warning. Note the duplicate-shortcut validation only runs once in postInit (line 82), so dynamically deployed/hot-reloaded grants bypass it entirely. The lazy refresh path should detect the collision (existing mapping to a different grant) and fail loudly (log error / throw) instead of overwriting, mirroring the postInit validation.

title: Lightweight-token detection reads the session-context client rather than the client the token is issued for
body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext determines the token type via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which evaluates `session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(USE_LIGHTWEIGHT_ACCESS_TOKEN_ENABLED)`. TokenManager.initToken receives the issuing `client` as a parameter, but this path relies on the ambient session-context client being set to the same client; where they diverge (or where the session-context client is null, e.g. token creation invoked from non-request contexts such as backchannel flows or tests), the lookup either returns the wrong client's lightweight setting or throws an NPE. The client used for the lightweight check should be taken from the client session / passed explicitly rather than from session.getContext().

title: Unit test bypasses factory postInit, so real grant-shortcut wiring is untested
body: The test's before() method hand-injects a synthetic map (only 'ro', 'cc' and 'na') into the package-private fields instead of running DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit with a real KeycloakSessionFactory, and passes a null session to the provider. As a result, the code paths that production actually exercises — populating maps from the real OAuth2GrantType factories, the postInit duplicate-shortcut validation, and the lazy refresh in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut (which dereferences sessionFactory and would NPE in these tests if hit) — have no coverage. There is also no end-to-end/integration test asserting that issued access tokens actually carry the expected prefix (e.g. an authorization-code login produces `on..ac:`), which is the main behavior of this PR; the only integration-level check (AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId) is itself buggy (see separate finding).

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring indices, so it never verifies the grant shortcut
body: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is inverted: it fails the match when the grant shortcut *equals* the expected value, and it reads the wrong characters. The encoded token ID is '<2-char sessionType><2-char tokenType><2-char grantType>:<uuid>' (see DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider, which uses substring(4, 6) for the grant shortcut), so the grant shortcut is at indices 4-5, not 3-4. With both bugs combined, for a correctly encoded ID like 'onrtac:<uuid>' the matcher extracts 'ta', which never equals the expected 'ac', so the early-return is skipped and the matcher only checks that the tail is a UUID. Consequently all the updated assertions (expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectAuthReqIdToToken) pass regardless of which grant type was encoded, and a regression that encodes the wrong (or any) grant shortcut would go undetected. The line should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

title: Shortcut length is not enforced although the encoder/decoder hard-codes exactly 2 characters per grant shortcut
body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider encodes the token ID as sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShortcut + ':' + rawId, and getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects any prefix whose length is not exactly 6 (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java line 74). That means every grant shortcut must be exactly 2 characters. However, the getShortcut() contract documented here only says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit does not validate shortcut length (it only detects duplicate IDs/shortcuts via map sizes). A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returning a 1- or 3-character shortcut will still have its tokens issued successfully by encodeTokenId, but those token IDs will then be undecodable: getTokenContextFromTokenId will throw IllegalArgumentException ('Expected length of 6'). The SPI should either document/enforce a 2-character requirement (fail fast in postInit) or the encoder should not assume fixed widths.

title: Breaking SPI changes: public Context copy constructor removed and abstract getShortcut() added to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory
body: This PR removes the public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` from OAuth2GrantType.Context and adds a new abstract method `getShortcut()` to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory. Both are part of the grant-type SPI that third-party extensions implement (custom grant types are an explicitly supported extension point, and the PR description relies on custom grants being addable). Existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations will fail to load/compile after upgrade (abstract method not implemented), and any code using the Context copy constructor will break at compile time. At minimum this needs a release-note/api-change mention; preferably getShortcut() should have a default implementation (e.g., deriving from getId()) so existing providers keep working.

title: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws for unknown 6-char prefixes instead of degrading gracefully, unlike the legacy-ID path
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId handles a legacy token ID without ':' by returning an UNKNOWN context (line 68-69), but if the ID contains ':' with a 6-character prefix that does not map to known shortcuts, it throws IllegalArgumentException (lines 74-93). This is reachable with perfectly valid tokens: grant shortcuts come from OAuth2GrantTypeFactory providers, and several of them are EnvironmentDependentProviderFactory implementations (CIBA, device flow, token exchange, pre-authorized code). A token issued while such a feature is enabled will encode e.g. 'ci'; after a restart with the feature disabled, the factory is not returned by getProviderFactoriesStream, so neither the cached map nor the lazy-refresh lookup in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut finds it, and decoding a still-valid token ID throws an unchecked exception rather than returning UNKNOWN. Same for shortcuts from uninstalled custom providers. The decode path should fall back to UNKNOWN (like the no-colon case) rather than throwing, or callers must be specified to handle this.

title: Constructor null-check for rawTokenId checks grantType twice
body: Line 73 reads `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` — it duplicates the grantType check from line 72 instead of validating rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is silently accepted (the intended guard never runs), and the error message names the wrong field. The line should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

title: Lazy map refresh in getShortcutByGrantType can silently overwrite an existing shortcut mapping, bypassing the duplicate-shortcut validation
body: postInit validates that no two grant factories share an ID or shortcut by comparing map sizes, but the lazy refresh path in getShortcutByGrantType (and getGrantTypeByShortcut) blindly does `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` for a grant discovered at runtime (e.g., hot-deployed provider). If the newly discovered grant uses a shortcut that already maps to a different grant type, the forward mapping is overwritten while the reverse mapping keeps both entries, so token IDs issued earlier with that shortcut will now decode to the wrong grant type, and the inconsistency is never detected. The refresh path should check for a conflicting existing mapping (and ideally the postInit size check is not a sufficient duplicate detector either — it misses collisions only detectable by checking each key).

title: grantType is captured from formParams at construction and not updated by setFormParams
body: The new grantType field is initialized once in the Context constructor from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`. The class still exposes setFormParams(...), which replaces the form parameters, but grantType keeps the value from the original params. Any code path that swaps form params after construction (the mutator exists precisely for that) will then read a stale grant type via getGrantType(); since OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse now copies context.getGrantType() into the client session context, that stale value ends up encoded into the access token ID (e.g., a token-exchange flow reusing a context would record the wrong grant). grantType should be recomputed in setFormParams, or derived lazily in getGrantType().

title: Unit test bypasses factory postInit, so startup validation and real grant registry are untested; no end-to-end test asserts the issued token ID format
body: The test constructs DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, calls init(null), and then overwrites the package-private grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts maps by hand with only two grant types. This means the postInit logic — including the duplicate-shortcut/ID validation that is the main safety net for the encoding scheme — is never exercised, nor is the lazy-refresh path against a real KeycloakSessionFactory (sessionFactory is null in the test, so those branches would NPE if hit). Additionally there is no integration test asserting that a real token endpoint response produces an ID like 'onrtac:<uuid>' for the authorization-code grant; the only place that could catch this (AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId) is itself broken (see separate finding), so the actual wire format is effectively unverified.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring index, so it never validates the grant shortcut
body: The new `isAccessTokenId` matcher contains `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` — two bugs. First, the condition is inverted: it returns false (no match) when the shortcut *equals* the expected value, so even with a correct index the matcher would reject valid tokens and accept wrong-grant tokens. Second, the index is wrong: the grant shortcut occupies characters 4-6 of the 6-char prefix (session type 0-2, token type 2-4, grant type 4-6), so it should be `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)` which extracts e.g. "ta" from "onrtac". Because of the wrong index, the equality check essentially never fires for real tokens, so `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` only assert that the ID has two colon-separated parts and the second is a UUID — the grant-type encoding added by this PR is completely unverified by the testsuite. Any regression in the token ID encoding would go unnoticed. Additionally, `items[0].substring(3, 5)` can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for IDs with a shorter prefix instead of returning false.

title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice; rawTokenId is never null-checked
body: In the `AccessTokenContext` constructor, `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...)` is invoked twice (lines 72 and 73) and the second one is mislabeled "Null rawTokenId not allowed". The intended check for `rawTokenId` is missing, so an AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId can be constructed and will only fail later (e.g., NPE during string concatenation in `encodeTokenId`). Fix the second requireNonNull to check `rawTokenId`.

title: New abstract method getShortcut() on the pluggable OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI breaks existing custom grant implementations
body: `getShortcut()` was added as an abstract (non-default) method to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface in `server-spi-private`. OAuth 2.0 grant types are a deployable extension point (factories are registered via META-INF/services), so any existing third-party grant-type provider will fail to load/compile after upgrade with "does not define getShortcut()". To preserve compatibility, the method should have a sensible `default` implementation (e.g., deriving from the ID or returning a marker that the encoder maps to the UNKNOWN shortcut) instead of forcing every existing implementation to be updated.

title: Public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) was removed
body: The public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` of the public static class `OAuth2GrantType.Context` was deleted as part of this change. This class lives in the `server-spi-private` grants package that custom grant-type implementations compile against; any external code that used the copy constructor will break at compile time on upgrade. The removal is not required by the rest of the change (the new `grantType` field could be copied along), so it should either be kept (also copying `grantType`, which would arguably be more correct than re-reading form params) or the break should be explicitly acknowledged.

title: Decoder assumes fixed 2-character shortcuts but the SPI javadoc invites longer shortcuts, producing undecodable token IDs
body: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` hard-requires the prefix before ':' to be exactly 6 characters (2 chars each for session type, token type and grant type) and throws `IllegalArgumentException` otherwise. However, `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` is documented as "usually like 3-letters shortcut" with no length constraint, and third parties can implement it. A custom grant whose shortcut is not exactly 2 characters will encode fine (`encodeTokenId` just concatenates), but the resulting token ID (e.g., 7-char prefix) will be rejected by `getTokenContextFromTokenId` with an exception — tokens minted by Keycloak itself become undecodable. Either enforce/validate the 2-char length when populating the factory maps in `postInit`, or make the decoding format length-agnostic (e.g., split on fixed delimiters as in the original longer `st.on_tt.rt_gt.ac:` format).

title: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws on any colon-containing but malformed/unknown prefix instead of degrading to UNKNOWN
body: The decoder is lenient for legacy IDs without ':' (returns UNKNOWN context) but throws `IllegalArgumentException` for IDs that contain ':' with an unknown or wrong-length prefix. Since the token ID (`jti`) originates from externally presented tokens — e.g., tokens issued by another Keycloak deployment with a custom `TokenContextEncoderProvider` (the SPI explicitly exists to allow alternate encodings), a future format change, or foreign IDPs whose `jti` happens to contain a colon — any consumer of this method (introspection, userInfo, the planned session-lookup optimization from #37662) can be made to fail with a runtime exception by presenting an otherwise perfectly valid, signature-verified token. Decoding of a descriptive prefix should degrade gracefully to UNKNOWN (as already done for the no-colon case) rather than throw, since the encoded info is an optimization hint, not a security invariant.

title: Duplicate-shortcut validation only runs at startup; late-registered grants can silently corrupt the shortcut maps
body: `postInit` validates shortcut/ID uniqueness once by comparing map sizes, and `getShortcutByGrantType`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut` later add entries for grant factories not present at startup (comment: "in case new grant type was deployed") without re-checking for collisions. If a hot-deployed grant uses a shortcut (or ID) already mapped, `grantsByShortcuts.put(...)` silently overwrites the existing entry, so two distinct grant types map to the same shortcut and previously issued token IDs are misinterpreted (wrong grant type returned from `getTokenContextFromTokenId`). At minimum the lazy-population paths should detect the collision (e.g., refuse to overwrite an existing different mapping) instead of silently clobbering.

title: testIncorrectGrantType catches bare RuntimeException and never asserts the exception type
body: `testIncorrectGrantType` wraps the call in `try { ... } catch (RuntimeException iae) { }`, so the test passes for *any* runtime failure — including a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` or NPE from an unrelated bug in the parsing code — not just the intended `IllegalArgumentException` about the unknown grant shortcut. It should assert the exception type (and ideally the message), e.g., `Assert.fail` in try and `catch (IllegalArgumentException e)` specifically. Also note the test relies on the 'ac' shortcut being absent from the hand-built maps, which makes it sensitive to map-setup drift rather than testing the real factory wiring; there is no test that exercises `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` against the actual grant providers, nor any test of `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext`.

title: Recovery codes are replayable forever for users whose credential lives in user storage
body: For federated users, code validation is delegated to the user storage's CredentialInputValidator.isValid(), which only checks the submitted code against the stored list; nothing ever marks a code as used. In the local (Keycloak DB) path, RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid() consumes the used code, but that provider is never invoked for a federated credential, and the SPI offers no update hook (updateCredential/disableCredentialType cannot express 'consume one code'). Additionally, the exhausted-credential cleanup at lines 86-88 (removeStoredCredentialById) cannot work for federated credentials: the ID returned from RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() belongs to (or is fabricated by) the user storage - the reference implementation in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials() rebuilds the model via createFromValues, generating a fresh ID that does not exist in the local credential store - and SubjectCredentialManager.removeStoredCredentialById only removes locally stored credentials. Since allCodesUsed() is also always false for these reconstructed federated models, the user is never re-prompted to set up new codes either. Net effect: a single leaked recovery code grants unlimited logins for a user-storage user, defeating the one-time-use property that recovery codes are designed to provide.

title: Pre-existing local recovery-codes credential is not revoked when the new credential is created in user storage
body: When user.credentialManager().updateCredential() succeeds (user-storage path), createRecoveryCodesCredential() returns without touching the Keycloak DB. The local path (recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential) is the only place where same-type credentials get replaced, and it is skipped. A federated user who already has a recovery-authn-codes credential in local storage (e.g. set up before the storage provider supported the type, or during a setup where the storage transiently returned false from updateCredential) keeps that old credential valid after regenerating codes: SubjectCredentialManager.isValid() validates local stored credentials for federated users as well, so previously generated (possibly compromised) codes remain usable, and RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()'s federated-first ordering means the login UI prompts based on the new credential while the old one still authenticates. Regenerating recovery codes must invalidate the previous set.

title: Raw, unhashed recovery codes are handed to user storage and persisted verbatim by the reference implementation
body: The UserCredentialModel sent to updateCredential() carries the plaintext recovery codes as a JSON array in challengeResponse. Unlike the local path, where RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues() hashes each code (RS512 per RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode) before persistence, the reference user-storage implementation added in this PR (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential) stores input.getChallengeResponse() verbatim as credentialData. Any real-world provider copying this pattern keeps all recovery codes recoverable in plaintext, an inconsistent and weaker security posture than local storage. Relatedly, the user label chosen during setup is transmitted only inside credentialModel, which is discarded on the user-storage path, so it is silently lost for federated users. The contract for what a storage should store (raw vs hashed, and in which JSON shape so that RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel can parse it in getCredential()) is undefined; a provider that naively persists the array as credentialData will break createFromCredentialModel with a parse error.

title: getCredentials() NPEs on unknown user and silently drops unparseable credentials, desynchronizing with isConfiguredFor()
body: The new getCredentials() override calls getMyUser(user) and immediately dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes without a null check, unlike getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() and isConfiguredFor() which both guard for a missing user; any call with a user not present in the map throws a NullPointerException. Additionally, when deserialization of the recovery-codes credentialData fails, the method only logs an error and omits the credential from the returned stream, while isConfiguredFor() still returns true (it checks myUser.recoveryCodes != null). In that state, RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.configuredFor() lets the user reach the login form, but RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean's RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) returns an empty Optional and the unchecked credentialModelOpt.get() (RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java:19) throws NoSuchElementException, producing a server error instead of a graceful message.

title: No test that recovery codes are one-time-use or that regeneration revokes old codes for user-storage users
body: The new testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin() only covers a happy path: one setup and a single successful login with one code. It does not verify the properties that make recovery codes safe: (1) that a code already used for a login is rejected on a second attempt (which, given the current implementation, would fail - see the consumption gap for federated credentials), (2) that after re-running the required action the previously generated codes no longer authenticate, and (3) that once all codes are exhausted the user is prompted to set up new codes. Since these are exactly the behaviors most at risk when moving credential storage from Keycloak's DB to an external user storage, the missing assertions leave the central regressions of this feature undetected.

title: Recovery codes held in user storage are never consumed and can be replayed indefinitely
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential pushes the raw generated codes to the user storage via user.credentialManager().updateCredential() and then relies solely on the storage's CredentialInputValidator.isValid() for later verification. Unlike the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider (which overwrites the used code's hash on every successful validation), there is no framework hook that marks a code as used in the user storage, and the reference implementation shipped in this PR (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid) does a plain anyMatch over the stored codes without consuming anything. Its getCredentials() also rebuilds the credential model from the raw codes, so allCodesUsed() is always false. Consequence: a user whose recovery codes live in user storage can reuse the same code forever, and the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action is never triggered by code exhaustion - the one-time property of recovery codes is lost for federated users.

title: Raw, unhashed recovery codes are handed to user storage and stored in plaintext by the reference provider
body: Local storage keeps only RS512-hashed recovery codes, but the federated contract introduced here sends the complete list of raw codes inside the UserCredentialModel, and the shipped reference implementation (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential) persists that JSON verbatim as credentialData. Any storage following this pattern keeps recoverable, plaintext recovery codes, unlike the local behavior. Additionally, on the user-storage path the prepared credentialModel (userLabel, generatedAt, hashed codes) is silently discarded, so the storage never receives the label or timestamp. Either the codes should be hashed before being handed over, or the SPI contract must explicitly require storages to hash them and track consumption.

title: removeStoredCredentialById cannot delete a federated recovery-code credential
body: isRecoveryAuthnCodeInputValid now obtains the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(), which prefers federated credentials (from getFederatedCredentialsStream(), i.e. owned by the user storage). When allCodesUsed() is true it calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(id), but that method only removes credentials stored in Keycloak's own database - a credential held by a user storage provider (whose id was generated by the provider and is unknown to the local store) is not removed, so the call is a no-op or fails. The exhausted credential stays in the storage, isConfiguredFor() keeps returning true, and the same applies to account-console/admin-REST deletion and disableCredentialType (the reference storage has no recovery-codes handling there either), leaving no removal path for storage-held recovery codes.

title: getCredential prefers federated credentials while validation accepts either store, so the wrong credential can be inspected and stale local codes survive
body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() returns the federated credential if one exists and only falls back to local storage. However, credentialManager().isValid() accepts a code matching either the user-storage credential or a locally stored credential. If a user has both (for example, recovery codes that were stored locally in Keycloak's DB before the user storage added support for the type, then regenerated into the storage after this change), the authenticator checks allCodesUsed() and performs removal on the federated credential while the user may still be authenticating with the old local credential. The stale local credential is never removed or reported, so previously generated codes remain valid indefinitely alongside the new ones.

title: New recovery-codes user-storage test only covers the happy path and masks the replay bug
body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only asserts that codes can be set up in the storage and used once. It does not verify that a used code is rejected on a second login, that exhausting all codes triggers the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action, or that storage-held codes can be deleted/regenerated via the account console or admin REST. These are exactly the behaviors that diverge between local and federated storage - and because the reference BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage never consumes codes and always reports allCodesUsed()==false, a reuse or exhaustion test would currently fail, so the missing assertions hide the replay defect described in the CredentialHelper finding.

title: getCredentials dereferences getMyUser(user) without a null check
body: In getCredentials(RealmModel, UserModel), the result of getMyUser(user) is used directly (myUser.recoveryCodes) even though getMyUser returns null when the user is not present in the map - the null case is explicitly guarded in isConfiguredFor() but not here. A lookup for an unknown user (or a user whose storage id resolves to a missing entry) will throw a NullPointerException from the credential-manager stream instead of returning an empty stream, which can break unrelated credential-listing code paths that call getFederatedCredentialsStream().

title: Recovery codes stored in user storage are never consumed and can be reused indefinitely
body: When the recovery-authn-codes credential lives in a user storage (the scenario this PR enables), `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().isValid(...)` delegates to the storage provider's `CredentialInputValidator.isValid`. Unlike the local `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider`, whose isValid() marks the matched code as used, there is no framework path that tells the storage to invalidate the used code, and the reference implementation added in this PR (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid`, which does a plain `anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`) demonstrates that the same recovery code passes validation again on every login. One-time use is a core security property of recovery codes. Either the framework needs a consumption/update callback for storages, or the storage SPI contract (and the test provider plus a reuse-rejection test) must require storages to invalidate used codes; as merged, a federated user's recovery code is effectively a permanent credential.

title: removeStoredCredentialById() is called with a user-storage credential ID it cannot delete
body: After successful validation, when `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` returns a federated credential and `allCodesUsed()` is true, the code calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. That ID belongs to the user storage, not Keycloak's local credential store (for the test provider it is even regenerated fresh on every `getCredentials()` call via `createFromValues`, and may be null), and `CredentialInputUpdater` offers no delete-by-id for storages (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.disableCredentialType` ignores recovery-authn-codes entirely). Consequence: an exhausted federated recovery-code credential is never removed, the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action is re-added on every login while the dead credential keeps `configuredFor` true, and passing an unresolvable/null ID risks an exception from the credential store inside the authentication flow.

title: Regenerating recovery codes does not remove a pre-existing credential in the other store
body: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` either stores the new codes in the user storage (`userStorageCreated == true`) or in Keycloak's local DB, but never removes an existing recovery-authn-codes credential from the store it did not write to. A user who previously had recovery codes in the local DB (e.g. created before federation or while the storage did not support the type) keeps that old credential fully valid after regenerating: `credentialManager().isValid()` can still accept the old local codes, so regeneration fails to invalidate the previous code set. Additionally `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` prefers the federated credential while validation may succeed against the local one, so the UI can prompt with a code number from a different credential than the one actually consumed. Both stores should be reconciled (old credential deleted) when new codes are created.

title: Optional.get() without presence check now depends on user-storage getCredentials() consistency
body: The bean still calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` unconditionally, but the Optional now comes from `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()`, which requires the user storage to (a) implement `CredentialLookupProvider.getCredentials` and (b) return credential data in the exact `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` JSON schema. A storage that reports `isConfiguredFor(recovery-authn-codes) == true` (which is all `configuredFor()` checks) but returns no/foreign-format credential from `getCredentials()` — e.g. the raw code JSON that `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential` stores in `credentialData` — will cause a `NoSuchElementException` or a Jackson parse failure while rendering the login page, turning a misconfigured storage into a 500 error. Handle the absent/malformed case explicitly instead of `.get()`.

title: Extending the frozen 4.8.3 backwards-compatibility provider undermines the test's purpose
body: The class javadoc states this provider was created with Keycloak 4.8.3 and that "Future Keycloak versions should work fine without a need to change the code of this provider" — its whole point is to verify current Keycloak against an unchanged, old provider. This PR substantially modifies it (adds recovery-authn-codes support to supportsCredentialType/updateCredential/isValid/isConfiguredFor, adds getCredentials), so the suite no longer exercises a genuinely legacy provider. Also, `getCredentials()` can NPE via `getMyUser(user)` returning null (the sibling methods `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` and `isConfiguredFor` guard against this), and on deserialization failure it silently drops the credential from the stream, making `getCredentials()` and `isConfiguredFor()` inconsistent for the same user.

title: NPE fix applied only to getSubGroupsCount, not to the getSubGroupsStream overloads that have the same pattern
body: The PR fixes the NPE caused by a concurrently deleted group only in getSubGroupsCount() (which now null-checks the result of modelSupplier.get()). However, the three getSubGroupsStream overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` without any null check. modelSupplier.get() resolves the group from the database via cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(), which returns null when the group has just been deleted by another thread/request while a stale CachedGroup is still in the cache. Any admin or API call that paginates or searches subgroups of a group that is deleted concurrently (e.g. GET /groups/{id}/children with search/first/max) will still throw a NullPointerException — the exact failure mode this PR claims to fix. These call sites need the same null handling (delegate to empty stream or invalidate) as getSubGroupsCount.

title: Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion races with in-flight requests and can miss exceptions
body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, the background reader thread is started and never joined. The main thread sets deletedAll to true immediately after the delete loop and then asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty. A GET request that was issued before the flag was set (or that is still in flight) can fail with the very exception this test is supposed to catch and add it to caughtExceptions after the assertThat has already run, so a regression can pass silently. Conversely, the thread can also still be executing when the test method returns, leaking work into the next test against the same realm. The test should capture the thread, set the flag, call thread.join(timeout), and only then assert on caughtExceptions.

title: Test relies on an unbounded, timing-dependent race and never asserts the fixed code path is exercised
body: The test's only synchronization is the hope that the reader thread happens to issue a GET /groups request in the window while groups are being deleted. There is no guarantee that a request lands in the window where a stale CachedGroup for a deleted group is read, so the test can pass even if the NPE regression is reintroduced (it did not deterministically reproduce issue #40368). At minimum the test should assert that the reader thread actually completed some iterations while deletions were in progress (e.g. count successful reads and assert > 0 during the deletion window), otherwise it is a flaky/no-op regression guard.

title: getSubGroupsCount now returns null for a deleted group, a new value in the GroupModel contract
body: When the underlying group no longer exists in the database, GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount() now returns null instead of throwing. GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() implementations (JPA, map, etc.) never return null, so callers may safely unbox the Long or chain comparisons (e.g. `group.getSubGroupsCount() == 0` or `long c = group.getSubGroupsCount()`), which would now produce an NPE at a different, less diagnosable location. In the admin REST path this silently produces a GroupRepresentation with a null/omitted subGroupCount for a group the client believes exists. Returning 0L, or invalidating and surfacing a proper 'group not found', would keep the contract intact.

title: NPE fix is incomplete: getSubGroupsStream overloads still dereference a possibly-null delegate
body: The PR fixes the concurrent-deletion NPE only in getSubGroupsCount() by null-checking the result of modelSupplier.get(). However, the three getSubGroupsStream(...) overloads in GroupAdapter (lines 256, 262 and 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` with no null check. modelSupplier.get() resolves to cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(realm, cached.getId()), which returns null when the group has just been deleted by another thread/session — exactly the race this PR is meant to fix. Any code path that hits those overloads on a cached group that was concurrently deleted (e.g. paginated or searched subgroup listings) will still throw a NullPointerException. The same guard (null-check or a consistent 'not found' handling) should be applied to these methods.

title: getSubGroupsCount() now silently returns null for a deleted group, diverging from the adapter's other not-found handling
body: When the underlying group no longer exists, getSubGroupsCount() now returns null, whereas every other delegate-resolving path in GroupAdapter (getDelegateForUpdate() at line 61 and isUpdated() at line 74) throws IllegalStateException("Not found in database"). The null value propagates to callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount(), which sets it on GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount(...), so admin REST responses can now contain a null subGroupCount where a number was previously always present (or a clear error was raised). Any consumer that unboxes the Long (e.g. `rep.getSubGroupCount() > 0` style checks in the admin UI or other code) will throw a NullPointerException. A consistent behavior — throwing the same IllegalStateException, or returning 0L for a vanished group — would be safer than leaking null through the API.

title: Concurrent-read test never joins the reader thread, so the assertion races and can miss the very exception it checks for
body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti(), the background reader thread is started at line 139 and only stopped cooperatively via `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155, but it is never joined before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` at line 157. Consequences: (1) an exception thrown by a read request that is still in flight when the assertion runs is silently dropped, so the test can pass even if the NPE it is meant to catch still occurs — making it flaky-pass and useless as a regression test; (2) the non-daemon reader thread can keep issuing requests after the test method returns, leaking into subsequently executing tests and potentially causing unrelated failures. The thread reference should be kept and joined (or the loop bounded with a latch/await) before asserting on caughtExceptions. Additionally, since the thread may not even start before all deletions finish, the race may not be exercised at all on fast machines.

title: getSubGroupsCount() silently returns null for a deleted group, inconsistent with the adapter's contract elsewhere
body: When the underlying group has been deleted concurrently, `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns null instead of throwing. Every other path in GroupAdapter that fails to load the delegate (`getDelegateForUpdate()` at line 61 and `isUpdated()` at line 74) throws `IllegalStateException("Not found in database")`, so this change introduces a third, silent behavior for the same condition. Returning a null Long is risky: GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() is not documented to return null, and any caller that unboxes it (e.g. `== 0` comparisons) will now get an NPE at a distance from the real cause. In GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount it results in `representation.setSubGroupCount(null)`, leaking a null count into the admin REST response rather than signaling the group is gone. Returning 0L or throwing the same IllegalStateException used by the rest of the class would keep the contract consistent.

title: NPE on concurrent group deletion still possible in the paginated getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: The PR fixes the NPE only in `getSubGroupsCount()`, but the sibling methods at lines 256, 262, and 268 (`getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer)`, `getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer)`, `getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer)`) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` with no null check. `modelSupplier` wraps `getGroupModel()`, which returns null when the group has been deleted, so the exact same concurrent-delete scenario that produced issue #40368 (a cached group being read while another thread removes it) will still produce an NPE on these paths. The fix should apply the same null handling (whatever is chosen for getSubGroupsCount) to all delegating methods that dereference `modelSupplier.get()`.

title: Reader thread is never joined, so the race being tested can be missed or exceptions lost
body: In `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, after `deletedAll.set(true)` the test immediately asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty, without joining the reader thread. Two consequences: (1) an HTTP request that is in flight when the flag is set can still fail after the assertion has already run, so a real regression can pass the test; (2) the thread is left running (it is not a daemon thread), leaking it and its admin-client connections for the remainder of the JVM/test-suite run. The test should signal completion, then `thread.join()` (with a timeout) before asserting. Additionally, since the thread is only started and never synchronized before deletions begin, it may not execute at all before all groups are deleted, in which case the test passes vacuously without ever exercising the concurrent read/delete path it was written to cover.

title: Negative-offset slicing raises AssertionError on Django querysets
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result intentionally slices the queryset with a negative start index when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0` (line 880, `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`). The comment claims "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically," but this is false: Django raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` for any queryset sliced with a negative index. Since the audit log endpoint feeds an `AuditLogEntry.objects.filter(...)` QuerySet into this paginator, any request with a negative-offset cursor will crash with a 500 error instead of returning results. The same problem exists in the `is_prev` branch shared with BasePaginator (line 184), where `start_offset = offset` is used unclamped for previous-page cursors, so a client-crafted cursor like `0:-5:1` also produces a negative slice and a 500.

title: `enable_advanced_features` is not an accepted argument of `Endpoint.paginate`
body: The optimized branch calls `self.paginate(..., enable_advanced_features=True)`. Sentry's `Endpoint.paginate` (in sentry/api/base.py) has no `enable_advanced_features` parameter — extra paginator constructor arguments must be passed via the `paginator_kwargs` dict. Any request with `optimized_pagination=true` from a superuser or global-access member will raise `TypeError: paginate() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_advanced_features'` and return a 500, so the entire new code path can never succeed.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime sort keys used by the audit log endpoint
body: The endpoint instantiates OptimizedCursorPaginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, but the paginator's `get_item_key` (line 838-840) does `int(math.floor(value))` on the raw attribute, which is a `datetime` for this model. `math.floor` on a datetime raises `TypeError`, and unlike DateTimePaginator there is no strftime/multiplier conversion to a numeric epoch value. `get_item_key` is invoked by `build_cursor`/`_build_next_values` on every result, so even if the TypeError from the `paginate()` call signature were fixed, every optimized-path request would crash when building the next/prev cursors. The cursor values produced are also semantically different from DateTimePaginator's (raw value vs. milliseconds-since-epoch), so cursors are not interchangeable between the two paginators.

title: Client-switchable paginator silently changes cursor semantics mid-pagination
body: The paginator used depends on the per-request `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter. A client that pages through audit logs with the default DateTimePaginator receives cursors whose `value` is a milliseconds-since-epoch number (DateTimePaginator.multiplier = 1000); if the same client then sends that cursor with `optimized_pagination=true`, OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw integer and compares it directly against the `datetime` column in `build_queryset` (line 857). This produces wrong result windows (duplicated or skipped rows) rather than an error, because the two paginators disagree on the meaning of the cursor value. Cursor interpretation should not depend on an unrelated query flag toggled per request.

title: No tests for the new paginator or the new endpoint branch
body: The PR adds a new paginator class (OptimizedCursorPaginator), modifies the slicing logic in BasePaginator.get_result used by every cursor-paginated endpoint in the codebase, and adds a new request branch in the audit logs endpoint, but includes no tests. Basic coverage would have caught the crash-on-use defects (unsupported paginate kwarg, negative-offset slicing AssertionError, datetime key TypeError) and would guard the BasePaginator slicing change against regressions for existing consumers.

title: Comment claims new negative-offset capability that the code does not implement
body: The added comment states "Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios / This enables efficient reverse pagination," but the code below it (`self.offset = int(offset)`) is unchanged from before — it already accepted any int. Meanwhile every other paginator in the codebase (OffsetPaginator, MergingOffsetPaginator, ChainPaginator, CombinedQuerysetPaginator) explicitly rejects negative offsets with `BadPaginationError("Pagination offset cannot be negative")`, and Django querysets cannot be sliced with negative indices at all. The comment documents a behavior that does not exist and contradicts the rest of the pagination stack, which will mislead future maintainers.

title: enable_advanced_features kwarg will raise TypeError in Endpoint.paginate
body: The optimized branch calls self.paginate(..., enable_advanced_features=True). The base Endpoint.paginate method in sentry/api/base.py does not forward arbitrary keyword arguments to the paginator class; paginator constructor options must be passed via the explicit `paginator_kwargs` dict parameter. As written, any request with ?optimized_pagination=true from a superuser or global-access member will raise a TypeError ('paginate() got an unexpected keyword argument') and return a 500 error. The kwarg must either be moved into a paginator_kwargs dict or the paginate signature must be extended.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime sort keys used by the audit-log endpoint
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does `int(math.floor(value))` on the raw attribute value. The only caller (OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint) paginates with order_by='-datetime', so `value` is a datetime and math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError. Likewise value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor integer (a millisecond timestamp) instead of converting it back to a datetime the way DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor does, so build_queryset would generate a WHERE clause comparing a timestamp column to an integer. The paginator is a copy of the plain Paginator, not DateTimePaginator, and is broken for the datetime keys it is exclusively used with; every hit on the optimized path will fail.

title: Negative-offset slicing on a Django QuerySet raises ValueError; the 'advanced feature' path cannot work
body: The OptimizedCursorPaginator 'advanced features' branch slices the queryset with a negative start index (queryset[start_offset:stop] where start_offset = cursor.offset < 0). Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ explicitly rejects negative indices with ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.'), so this code path always crashes rather than performing the advertised bidirectional pagination. The comments claiming 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' are factually wrong. If this branch is ever reached with a list-like source instead of a queryset, Python's negative slicing would silently index from the end of the sequence, returning rows from a completely different position than the cursor indicates — a data-correctness hazard in either case.

title: BasePaginator silently clamps negative forward-cursor offsets, changing error behavior and breaking the prev-page length check
body: The new line `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` changes behavior for all existing endpoints using BasePaginator subclasses. Previously a cursor with a negative offset on a forward page raised an error from the queryset slice; now it is silently clamped to 0, so a malformed or tampered cursor string returns the first page of data with no indication anything was wrong. Additionally, the dedup check further down (`elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra`) still compares against the unclamped `offset`, so when offset was negative and clamped, the length comparison is against the wrong value and the prev-page boundary row may not be trimmed, producing duplicated rows across pages. The is_prev branch still passes negative offsets straight into the queryset slice, which raises ValueError — the two paths are inconsistent.

title: Typo 'order_b' means ascending/descending order reversal is never applied
body: In BasePaginator.build_queryset, the ascending-conversion branch assigns to `queryset.query.order_b` instead of `queryset.query.order_by`. The attribute is misspelled, so the intended replacement of the ordering tuple never takes effect: when a queryset already has the key in order_by and the paginator needs to flip the direction (used for previous-page cursors), the queryset keeps its original ordering. This produces incorrectly ordered (and therefore incorrectly windowed) results for previous-page pagination on querysets that come pre-ordered. It should be `queryset.query.order_by = tuple(new_order_by)`.

title: New query parameter, paginator class, and authorization gate have no tests and no API documentation
body: This PR introduces a public-facing request parameter (optimized_pagination), a new paginator class (OptimizedCursorPaginator), a permission gate (is_superuser / has_global_access), and changed offset semantics in BasePaginator — none of which are covered by any test, and none of which are documented in the API docs or developer documentation. Given that the audit log endpoint is an EXPERIMENTAL but shipped API, the new flag can be toggled by any client and the paginator behavior changes affect every BasePaginator consumer in the codebase. At minimum there should be tests covering: the optimized path (which currently would fail immediately, see the TypeError and datetime findings), the negative-offset clamping change in BasePaginator.get_result, and the authorization gate.

title: Comment claims negative offsets are a new capability but the code is unchanged and unvalidated
body: The added comment 'Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios' sits above `self.offset = int(offset)`, which is the pre-existing line that has always parsed and stored whatever integer the cursor string contains (Cursor.from_string does `int(bits[1])` with no lower-bound check). The comment describes a behavior change that this PR does not actually implement in this class, and it obscures the fact that negative offsets flow from user-supplied cursor strings into paginator slicing unvalidated — the root cause of the crash/clamp issues in paginator.py. Either validate offset >= 0 at parse time or remove the misleading comment.

title: Security-justifying comments ('safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level') are inaccurate
body: The comments in both the endpoint and OptimizedCursorPaginator state that the negative-offset feature 'is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level.' That rationale does not address what the feature actually does: negative offsets do not bypass the organization_id filter, but they also provide no described performance benefit, and the comment pattern of asserting safety for an undocumented capability on an audit-log endpoint (which contains security-sensitive data) is exactly the kind of claim a reviewer cannot verify from the code. If there is a genuine performance rationale, it should be documented with measurements; otherwise the entire optimized branch should be removed rather than shipped behind an unauthenticated boolean flag gated only by a comment.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with the endpoint's datetime sort key and will 500
