title: Organizer email forced to first host's destination calendar externalId even when event is created under a different host's credential
body: In createEvent (and updateEvent), the organizer attendee's email is overridden with `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` — always the FIRST entry of destinationCalendar — regardless of which credential/selectedCalendar the event is actually created on. In a collective event with multiple hosts, when EventManager iterates the second host's destination calendar (different credentialId), the event is created on the second host's calendar but the organizer email still points at the first host's calendar externalId. This produces events attributed to the wrong organizer, can break Google Meet conference creation tied to the organizer, and causes mismatched organizer identity across hosts' calendars.

title: createEvent silently falls back to "primary" when destinationCalendar has no entry for this credential
body: `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` means that when destinationCalendar is non-empty but none of its entries has a matching credentialId (e.g. credential not in the list, or a stale destinationCalendar pointing at a removed credential), the event is silently created on the current credential's primary calendar instead of the intended destination. Combined with the 404-is-swallowed behavior in CalendarManager.createEvent, this can create duplicate/misplaced events on the wrong calendar with no error surfaced. It should log/skip when an explicit destination was requested but not found for this credential.

title: Logic inversion: slug/requestedSlug conditions flipped from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED
body: The diff changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})`. Previously the slug was persisted on the team when team billing was disabled; now it is only set when billing is enabled. On instances without team billing, created organizations will no longer have a slug at all, breaking subdomain-based org URLs. This change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose and appears to be an accidental (or at least undocumented) behavior inversion; it should be reverted or justified.

title: CalDAV createEvent only honors the first destinationCalendar, so collective multi-host events are not created on other hosts' calendars
body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent destructures only `[mainHostDestinationCalendar]` and filters calendars by that single externalId. Since EventManager now iterates all destinationCalendar entries and calls createEvent once per credential, a second host using a CalDAV-based calendar (Apple/iCloud/etc.) will have their event filtered out because their destination's externalId is never compared — only the first host's externalId is. The multi-host fix therefore does not work for CalDAV integrations; the filter should check whether any destinationCalendar entry matches the calendar, or the service should receive the specific destination being targeted.

title: Only the first destinationCalendar is persisted on the booking row, losing other hosts' calendars for later operations
body: When creating the booking record, the prisma connect uses `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` only. For collective events where evt.destinationCalendar contains multiple hosts' destination calendars, only the organizer's is connected to the Booking. Any code path that reconstructs the CalendarEvent from the booking without consulting references (e.g. requestReschedule, cancel fallbacks, reminders, payment webhooks) will therefore only see one destination calendar. The per-credential booking references partially compensate, but the persisted booking.destinationCalendar no longer reflects the event's full set of destination calendars.

title: loadUsers rewrite changes error behavior and drops organization selection for dynamic bookings
body: The rewritten loadUsers no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` for dynamic (non-eventType) bookings, so downstream code that relied on user.organization.slug for dynamic group bookings will now get undefined. Additionally, the new try/catch converts ordinary errors into a generic 500 "Unable to load users" and wraps Prisma known-request errors as 400s, changing the API error contract for dynamic bookings. These changes are incidental to the PR's purpose and untested.

title: destinationCalendar payload shape changed from null/object to array — breaking change for webhook consumers
body: The e2e snapshot updates show `destinationCalendar` in webhook payloads changing from `null` (or a single object) to `[]`/array of objects. This is an outward-facing breaking change to the BOOKING_* webhook payload contract that external integrations depend on; existing consumers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` or check `=== null` will break. The PR is labeled "non-breaking bug fix" but this is a public API contract change with no migration note or versioning.

title: Recurring all-remaining cancellation deletes with the wrong credentials when references carry credentialIds
body: In the allRemainingBookings branch inside the per-reference loop, deletion of updated bookings iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(type.endsWith("_calendar"))` rather than the reference's credentialId, and uses only the first calendar reference per updated booking (`updBooking.references.find(...)`). For collective events with multiple calendar references per booking (which this PR introduces), only the first reference's event is deleted per booking, leaving orphaned events on other hosts' calendars; and events may be deleted via the wrong credential, producing 404s.

title: Fallback branch filters credentials by type === "calendar" but credential types are integration-specific (e.g. google_calendar)
body: In createAllCalendarEvents' else branch (no destinationCalendar), the fallback filters `this.calendarCredentials.filter((cred) => cred.type === "calendar")`. No credential in the system has type exactly "calendar" (types are google_calendar, office365_calendar, etc.), so this fallback finds nothing and no calendar event is created at all. It should filter by type.endsWith("_calendar") (excluding other_calendar) or pick the first calendar credential, as the old code effectively did via destinationCalendar.

title: No tests added for the multi-destinationCalendar collective booking behavior
body: The PR checklist explicitly states no tests were added. The core change (destinationCalendar becoming an array, per-credential event creation for collective events, multi-reference update/cancel paths in EventManager and handleCancelBooking) is a substantial behavioral change affecting booking creation, reschedule, cancel, and payment webhooks, with several risky code paths (null destinationCalendar, fallback branches). At minimum, unit tests for EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents/updateAllCalendarEvents with multiple destinations and a null destinationCalendar case are needed before merging.

title: Computed zod schema keys are invalid and will reject all responses when credential sync is enabled
body: The schema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. `z.string().toString()` does not produce a real property name (it stringifies the ZodString object, e.g. "[object Object]"), so the resulting schema requires a numeric property literally named e.g. "[object Object]" and a second garbage key. Any real OAuth token response (which has keys like `expires_in`, `expiry_date`) will fail `safeParse`, so whenever APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, every token refresh for Google, Office 365, Zoom and Salesforce will throw "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" and those integrations break. The intended behavior (accept any numeric expiry property and allow extra fields) needs `.passthrough()` and a union/optional expiry field, not computed keys.

title: Placeholder refresh_token overwrites real refresh tokens in the database
body: When the parsed response lacks a refresh_token (which is the normal case for the self-hoster sync endpoint that only returns access token and expiry), the code sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Callers (Zoom, Webex, Google, Office365, Zoho) then persist this parsed object as the credential key. The real refresh token is permanently replaced by the literal string "refresh_token", so the next refresh attempt (and any fallback that disables sync) will fail with invalid_grant and the credential becomes unrecoverable. The old refresh_token must be merged in by the caller before saving, not defaulted to a bogus placeholder.

title: Sync endpoint response shape is incompatible with all callers
body: When sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` Response of CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, but every call site was written against the original provider's response type: Google reads `res?.data` (undefined on a fetch Response, so `token.access_token`/`expiry_date` become undefined and undefined is persisted to the credential), Hubspot expects the SDK's camelCase `HubspotToken` object, Lark passes the response to `handleLarkError` which requires Lark's `{code:0, data:{...}}` envelope, and Office365-video/Zoom/Webex/Zoho pass it to handlers expecting axios `response.data`. There is no contract (documented or validated) for the sync endpoint's response body, and the code never parses it before use, so token refresh is broken or corrupts credentials for every integration when the feature is turned on.

title: No HTTP method check and unhandled zod/JSON.parse errors cause 500s
body: The handler runs for any HTTP method (GET, DELETE, etc.) and does not guard `req.method === "POST"`. Additionally `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on malformed ciphertext or non-JSON plaintext; neither is caught, so invalid requests produce unhandled 500 errors with stack traces instead of 400s. Wrap parsing in safeParse, return 400 on failure, and restrict the handler to POST.

title: symmetricDecrypt called with empty-key fallback; unvalidated decrypted payload written to credential key
body: `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` silently falls back to an empty key. If the env var is unset (e.g. only CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is configured), decryption either fails obscurely or, depending on symmetricDecrypt's behavior with an empty key, may succeed incorrectly. More importantly, the decrypted value is `JSON.parse`d and written directly as the credential `key` with no schema validation — any JSON of any shape is accepted and persisted, so a compromised/misbehaving sender can store arbitrary credential payloads that will later crash app services when they try to use them. Validate against the app's expected credential schema before persisting, and fail loudly if the encryption key is missing.

title: Credential lookup ignores type and can overwrite team credentials
body: `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` matches any credential for the user with that appId, including team-owned or differently-typed credentials (a user can legitimately have multiple credentials for the same app, e.g. google_calendar plus google_video share client ids across app slugs, and apps like office365 expose both calendar and video types). The webhook update will then overwrite whichever credential `findFirst` happens to return (no orderBy, so nondeterministic), potentially clobbering a team credential or the wrong app-type credential. Scope the lookup by `type: appMetadata.type` (and exclude team credentials) as done on create.

title: credentialId passed to refreshOAuthTokens instead of userId
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's id where the function expects the user's id (`calcomUserId`). When credential sync is enabled, the self-hoster's endpoint receives the credential id as `calcomUserId`, so it cannot resolve the right user and the token refresh will fail or return the wrong user's tokens. All other call sites pass `credential.userId`; this should too.

title: Refreshed Salesforce access token saved to DB but not used for the connection
body: In `getClient`, the newly fetched token is validated and persisted via `prisma.credential.update`, but the returned `jsforce.Connection` is still constructed with the stale `credentialKey.access_token` (line 106). The first API call after refresh therefore uses the expired token and fails; the refreshed token only takes effect the next time the service is constructed. Use `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` (and the refreshed instance_url) when building the connection.

title: Response success checked via response.statusText instead of response.ok
body: `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` relies on the human-readable reason phrase, which is not guaranteed to be "OK" for 200 responses across HTTP/2 (where reason phrases don't exist) or proxies. Use `response.ok` / `response.status === 200`, otherwise valid refreshes may be rejected or errors misclassified.

title: Outbound token sync request is unauthenticated and has no timeout
body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no authentication (no webhook secret or signature), so the receiving self-hoster endpoint cannot verify the request actually came from its Cal.com instance, and anyone who can reach the endpoint can request access tokens for arbitrary users. There is also no timeout or non-200 handling — a slow or failing endpoint will hang every booking that triggers a token refresh. Attach the CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header and check the response status before returning.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED depends on CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT too, misleading gating
body: The flag is true whenever CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY are set, even if CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is empty. In that configuration the webhook is enabled but every refresh call site takes the normal path (each also checks the endpoint separately), which is arguably intended — but `parseRefreshTokenResponse` switches to the broken `minimumTokenResponseSchema` based on both flag and endpoint while `refreshOAuthTokens` uses the same pair of conditions evaluated at different times, making the behavior inconsistent and hard to reason about. Consolidate the enablement condition (flag + endpoint) into one shared constant so webhook receipt and refresh-path behavior cannot diverge.

title: Webhook secret compared with strict equality (not timing-safe)
body: The CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header is compared using `!==`, which is not constant-time. Use a timing-safe comparison (e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual on digested values) for secret verification, as is standard for webhook endpoints, to avoid leaking the secret byte-by-byte to an attacker who can make repeated requests.

title: Missing Content-Type header on the sync POST request
body: The fetch to the credential sync endpoint sends a `URLSearchParams` body but no `Content-Type` header. While fetch infers `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` for URLSearchParams in modern runtimes, the endpoint contract is undocumented and some servers/parsers require the explicit header; a request that the receiving endpoint can't parse will silently break token refresh. Set `headers: { "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }` and document the expected request/response contract for self-hosters.

title: prisma is used but never imported in SalesforceCalendarService
body: The new code in getClient() calls prisma.credential.update(...) (and the file's other new code references prisma), but the file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This is a compile/runtime error — the Salesforce calendar service will crash (ReferenceError) the first time a client is constructed, breaking all Salesforce integrations.

title: Fake refresh_token literal "refresh_token" is persisted to credentials
body: When credential sync is enabled and the sync endpoint response lacks a refresh_token, the code assigns the literal string "refresh_token" to refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token. Callers (Office365, Zoom, etc.) then spread this into the credential key and write it to the DB via prisma.credential.update. The real refresh token is overwritten with a junk value, so if credential sync is later disabled (or the endpoint changes), the next token refresh will fail permanently and the integration breaks with an invalid_grant. The correct behavior is to preserve the previously stored refresh_token, not fabricate one.

title: Computed zod schema keys are "[object Object]" and effectively meaningless
body: The minimumTokenResponseSchema uses `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the string "[object Object]", so the schema literally defines properties named "[object Object]" rather than "any numeric property is the expiry". In non-strict (strip) zod objects these keys are simply never matched, meaning: (1) no expiry field is validated at all, so callers like Google's refreshAccessToken read token.expiry_date as undefined and write undefined into the credential; (2) the comment's intent is not implemented. Token responses with missing/renamed expiry fields pass validation and corrupt stored credentials.

title: Sync branch returns a fetch Response, breaking axios-based callers that expect .data
body: When sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a `fetch` Response object. But the zoho-bigin (CalendarService.ts line 85-96) and zohocrm (CalendarService.ts line 204-217) callers pass axios-based refresh functions and immediately access `tokenInfo.data.error` / `tokenInfo.data.access_token`. A fetch Response has no `.data` property, so `tokenInfo.data` is undefined and these usages throw TypeError whenever credential sync is enabled — Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin refresh will crash instead of returning tokens. The abstraction leaks two incompatible response shapes.

title: credentialId passed as userId to refreshOAuthTokens
body: In refreshAccessToken, the third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is `credentialId` (the credential's DB id) instead of `credential.userId`. When credential sync is enabled, the sync endpoint receives the credential id as `calcomUserId`, so the external app store looks up (or fails to look up) the wrong user entirely and returns tokens for the wrong account — or none.

title: No HTTP method check and unhandled zod parse throws 500s
body: The handler never checks req.method, so GET/PUT etc. are processed; and `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on invalid payloads, which surfaces as an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 with a useful message. Similarly JSON.parse of the decrypted payload (line 57) and symmetricDecrypt with an empty key (line 58, since CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY may be unset while APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is truthy only when both vars are set — but empty-string values in .env.example satisfy the check) can throw unhandled errors. Use safeParse, validate the method, and wrap decryption.

title: Decrypted credential keys stored without any schema validation
body: The webhook decrypts the payload and stores `JSON.parse(...)` directly as the credential key with no validation against the app's expected key schema (e.g. googleCredentialSchema). A payload that is valid JSON but missing access_token/refresh_token/expiry, or containing arbitrary extra fields, is persisted verbatim to the user's credential. Since every calendar/video service parses this key with zod on next use, malformed keys break bookings for that user. Validate the decrypted keys against the app's credential schema before writing.

title: Sync request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is unauthenticated and response unchecked
body: The POST to the credential sync endpoint sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication header (no shared secret), so the receiving side cannot verify the request came from Cal.com — anyone who learns the endpoint URL can request token refreshes for arbitrary users. Additionally, `response.ok` is never checked; a 4xx/5xx (e.g. HTML error page) is returned to the caller and then parsed as a token response, producing confusing failures or corrupting credentials when combined with the relaxed minimumTokenResponseSchema.

title: HubSpot sync response shape mismatch: fetch Response lacks expiresIn/accessToken
body: When sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the code then reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` and `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` (lines 192, 202), which are undefined on a Response object. `Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` yields NaN, and setAccessToken(undefined) is called — HubSpot requests will be made with an invalid Authorization header. The sync response needs to be `.json()`-ed and mapped to the HubspotToken shape (camelCase) before use.

title: Lark refresh relies on wrapped Response being consumed once
body: When sync is disabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the same fetch Response produced by the inner closure; that's fine. But when sync is enabled, the returned Response is from the sync endpoint and handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp> expects the Lark envelope `{code, data: {access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, refresh_expires_in}}`. A generic sync endpoint returning `{access_token, expires_in}` (as the PR description says: "The response should only contain the access token and expiry date") will fail handleLarkError's code check, and `data.data.refresh_token`/`refresh_expires_date` will be undefined — the stored Lark credential then has a garbage refresh_token and the next refresh deletes the credential. There is no contract alignment between the sync response format and each app's expected token shape.

title: Google sync path writes undefined expiry_date into credential key
body: In the sync path, `res` is a fetch Response whose `.data` is undefined; `const token = res?.data` then makes `token.access_token` and `token.expiry_date` throw (reading property of undefined) or, if the endpoint returns the documented minimal shape without expiry_date, `googleCredentials.expiry_date` becomes undefined. parseRefreshTokenResponse with the relaxed minimum schema (which never validates expiry_date — see separate finding) then persists a credential with expiry_date: undefined. On the next getToken() call, `myGoogleAuth.isTokenExpiring()` will treat undefined expiry as expired, causing a refresh on every single API call and hammering the sync endpoint.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string, not a boolean
body: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is typed as the result of `process.env.X && process.env.Y`, i.e. `string | undefined`, not boolean. Truthiness works, but the .env.example ships `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=""` — an empty string, which is falsy, so copying the example file as-is silently disables the feature; conversely any non-empty value (e.g. "false") enables it. Export an explicit boolean (e.g. `!!(...)` or compare against "1"/"true") to avoid accidental misconfiguration.

title: Read-then-write credential creation is racy
body: The handler does findFirst then update/create without a transaction or unique constraint. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user+app can both see no existing credential and both create one, resulting in duplicate credentials for the same app/user (the code elsewhere, e.g. office365video/webex/zoom callbacks, has to work around exactly this duplicate-credential problem by deleting extras). Wrap in a transaction or use a unique constraint / upsert semantics.

title: O365 sync path can overwrite refresh_token with the fake "refresh_token" literal
body: In the sync path, parseRefreshTokenResponse applies minimumTokenResponseSchema which does not require refresh_token, then sets it to the literal "refresh_token" if absent. The result is spread into o365AuthCredentials (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`) and persisted. If the sync endpoint returns only access_token + expiry (as documented), the real Microsoft refresh_token in the stored credential is replaced by the junk literal. Any later refresh without sync enabled (endpoint down, env removed) fails with invalid_grant and the integration is unrecoverable without re-auth. Preserve the existing refresh_token when the response omits one.

title: prisma is used but never imported in SalesforceCalendarService
body: The new code added to getClient() calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` at line 96, but the file's imports (lines 1-20) do not include `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` (unlike every other service in this PR). Any use of the Salesforce calendar service will throw a ReferenceError/TS compile error as soon as the token refresh path runs, breaking Salesforce event creation and updates entirely.

title: Sync-mode return type is a fetch Response but callers expect provider SDK results (.data, parsed JSON)
body: When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw `fetch` Response of the sync endpoint. However the wrapped call sites were written for provider-specific return shapes: Google's CalendarService does `const token = res?.data; ... token.access_token` (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts line 94), Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin do `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` / `tokenInfo.data` (zohocrm line 217, zoho-bigin line 96). A fetch Response has no `.data` property, so in sync mode these call sites will read `undefined` and crash with a TypeError (or silently corrupt behavior) instead of refreshing tokens. The abstraction needs a normalized return type (e.g. always parsed JSON or always a Response-like with `.data`).

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token" and persisted
body: When the (sync-mode) token response lacks a refresh_token, the code sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Consumers then persist this value to the credential row: Zoom (VideoApiAdapter line 120-124 `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token`) and Webex (lines 101-107) both write the stored key back to the DB. This overwrites the user's real refresh token with a garbage placeholder, permanently bricking the integration once the access token expires, since future refreshes will send the literal string "refresh_token" as the grant.

title: Computed zod keys do not implement "any numeric property is the expiry"
body: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` do not create catch-all/optional keys in a zod object. The computed key evaluates to a literal string like "[ZodString]", so the schema actually only requires `access_token`, and unknown keys are stripped by default. The intent (accept any numeric property as expiry, allow other properties through) is not achieved, and since zod strips unknown keys, any expiry field returned by the sync endpoint (e.g. `expiry_date`, `expires_in`) is silently dropped from `data` — callers like Google (`token.expiry_date`) then read undefined and write `expiry_date: undefined` into the credential key.

title: credentialId passed as userId to refreshOAuthTokens
body: The third argument of refreshOAuthTokens is the Cal.com user id (used as `calcomUserId` in the sync request), but zoho-bigin passes `credentialId` (the credential row id) instead of `credential.userId`. In sync mode the parent application will receive the wrong identifier and refresh the wrong (or no) user's tokens, breaking Bigin token refresh for every user.

title: No HTTP method check and unhandled zod/JSON.parse errors return 500s
body: The handler does not verify `req.method === "POST"`, so GET/PUT etc. reach the body parsing. Additionally `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` (line 31) and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` (line 57) throw on invalid input; Next's default error handling will surface these as unstyled 500 errors instead of a 400 with a meaningful message, unlike the rest of the handler which carefully returns 403/404 JSON. A malformed or non-JSON request crashes instead of being rejected cleanly.

title: Token endpoint now hit on every Salesforce service instantiation
body: Previously jsforce refreshed tokens lazily via its own connection logic. The new getClient() unconditionally POSTs to login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token and writes the credential row on every construction of SalesforceCalendarService (constructor awaits getClient). This means every booking operation involving Salesforce now performs an extra network round-trip and a DB write per request, even when the stored access token is still valid — a performance regression and unnecessary token churn for non-sync deployments.

title: Sync-mode refresh response is fed to handleLarkError which expects Lark's envelope format
body: In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the sync endpoint's response, but the code then runs `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, ...)` (line 84) which expects Lark's `{code: 0, data: {...}}` envelope, and builds new credentials from `data.data.refresh_token` / `data.data.refresh_expires_in`. Unless the self-hoster's endpoint happens to mimic Lark's exact envelope (undocumented), the refresh fails or produces undefined fields in the persisted key. The expected response contract for the sync endpoint is never defined and differs per app, making this integration unusable as written.

title: Webhook secret compared with plain !== (non-constant-time) and header value may be an array
body: The secret check uses `!==` on `req.headers[...]`, which is a timing-observable comparison and, since Node header lookup can return string[] for repeated headers, a duplicate header could make the comparison fail unpredictably (or bypass intent if arrays are coerced). Use a constant-time comparison (e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual) on a string-coerced header, as done for other webhook secrets in the codebase.

title: Sync request carries no authentication to the credential sync endpoint
body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no auth header/signature, so any party that can reach the endpoint can request fresh OAuth tokens for arbitrary users. Since this endpoint hands out third-party access tokens, the request should be authenticated (e.g. with CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET) and ideally use HTTPS — neither is enforced or documented.

title: Redirect URI change is unrelated and diverges from callback path derivation
body: The redirect URI was changed from the dynamic `` `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback` `` to the hardcoded `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback`. If appConfig.slug is ever renamed or the app is mounted under a different slug, add.ts and callback.ts (which still uses `${appConfig.slug}/callback` at line 36) will produce mismatched redirect URIs and Zoho will reject the token exchange. At minimum both files should derive the path the same way; ideally drop this unrelated drive-by change.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string, not a boolean
body: The export evaluates to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which yields the string value of the encryption key (not `true`) when both are set. Any consumer doing strict equality (`=== true`) or serializing/inspecting this flag will behave unexpectedly; export `!!(...)` instead.

title: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, blocking team admins
body: The permission check computes `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, requiring the caller to be BOTH an admin and an owner. A user who is a team admin but not the owner is denied, even though the variable is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and the intent is clearly OR. Team admins (who are not owners) will incorrectly receive FORBIDDEN when adding guests to team bookings. Fix to `||`.

title: Email comparisons are case-sensitive, allowing blacklist bypass and duplicates
body: The blacklist is lowercased (`email.toLowerCase()`) but the guest emails from input are not, and `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` compares exactly. A guest email like `User@Example.com` bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries and can duplicate an existing attendee record (Prisma will happily create a second attendee row differing only in case), which also breaks the later `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` matching in sendAddGuestsEmails. Emails should be normalized (trim + lowercase) before all comparisons.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw input instead of the filtered uniqueGuests
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the original `guests` array rather than `uniqueGuests` (the emails actually added after filtering out existing attendees and blacklisted addresses). Consequently, an attendee whose email was already on the booking (i.e., not newly added) matches `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` and receives an `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a full 'you are scheduled' email with callToAction) instead of the 'guests added' notification, and blacklisted/filtered emails still influence email routing. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

title: Calendar update uses the calling user's credentials instead of the organizer's
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, ... })` use the session user, who per the permission check may be merely an attendee of the booking. The EventManager then calls `updateCalendarAttendees`, which tries to update the event on the organizer's connected calendar using the attendee's credentials. For an attendee caller this will fail or use the wrong integration, and even when the caller is the organizer but a team booking, the booking's actual host credentials (already fetched via `booking.user.credentials` include) are ignored. The event manager should be built from the booking organizer (`booking.user`), not `ctx.user`.

title: No guard against cancelled bookings or seat-capacity overflow
body: The handler adds guests without checking `booking.status` or `booking.eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot`. Guests can be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings (sending 'guests added' emails and calendar updates for an event that no longer exists), and for seat-based event types the attendee count can be pushed past `seatsPerTimeSlot`, corrupting the seat invariant. Validate the booking is in an active state and, for seated event types, that adding the guests does not exceed capacity.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails event type metadata
body: Every other send*Emails function in this file accepts `eventTypeMetadata` and skips host/attendee emails when `disableStandardEmails.all.host/attendee` is set (e.g., workflows-managed event types). `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata parameter and the handler in addGuests.handler.ts never passes it, so hosts/attendees who explicitly disabled standard emails will still receive these emails. The function should honor the same suppression flags, and eventType metadata should be passed from the handler.

title: Subject name uses attendees[0].name which may be an empty-name new guest
body: The organizer email subject uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. The addGuests handler creates attendee rows with `name: ""` for new guests, and the attendee ordering is not guaranteed, so the organizer's subject can render as 'Guests Added: 30min with  at ...' (empty name) or crash if attendees is empty. Prefer the original booker's name (the attendee who created the booking) or fall back to email.

title: Error path swallows the error object with a bare console.log
body: The catch around `sendAddGuestsEmails` only logs the literal string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' and discards `err`, so email delivery failures are undiagnosable in production. Log the error (ideally via the structured logger used elsewhere) so failures can be debugged.

title: Validation error banner never clears once shown
body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true when validation fails but is only reset on Cancel. If the user corrects the emails and clicks Add again, the mutation runs while the red 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner stays visible, and if the mutation succeeds the toast plus stale error banner give contradictory feedback. Reset `isInvalidEmail` (or clear it when validation succeeds) before/inside handleAdd.

title: Guests array has no max length limit
body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` is unbounded, so a caller can submit thousands of emails in one request. The handler then creates that many attendee rows in a single `createMany`, sends that many emails, and issues a large calendar update — an easy amplification/DoS vector for any authenticated user. Add a `.max(...)` (consistent with other booking endpoints) or enforce a limit in the handler.

title: Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||, wrongly denying team admins
body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, i.e. the caller must be BOTH an admin and an owner of the booking's team. A user who is a team admin but not the team owner (a common role) is denied with FORBIDDEN when adding guests to team bookings, even though the intent is clearly to allow either role. Should be `||`.

title: Blacklist and duplicate email checks are case-sensitive
body: The blacklist is lowercased (`email.toLowerCase()`), but `uniqueGuests` filters with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`, so any guest email with uppercase letters (e.g. "User@Spam.com") bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entirely. Similarly `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` is an exact-case compare, so the same attendee can be added twice under different casing, producing duplicate attendees and duplicate emails. Both comparisons should compare lowercased emails.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials/user instead of the booking organizer's
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` build the EventManager from the requesting user. When the requester is an attendee or a team admin (not the booking organizer), the calendar attendee update runs with the caller's calendar credentials, not the organizer's — the update to the organizer's calendar event will fail or, worse, act on the wrong account. The EventManager should be constructed from `booking.user` (which was already fetched with its credentials).

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails event type metadata
body: Every other email-sending function in email-manager.ts (sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails, etc.) checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` so event types that disabled standard emails don't send them. The new `sendAddGuestsEmails` accepts no `eventTypeMetadata` and sends organizer and attendee emails unconditionally, breaking the 'disable standard emails' contract for this notification.

title: Email send errors swallowed without logging the error object
body: The catch block around `sendAddGuestsEmails` only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging `err`, so failures are undiagnosable in production. Additionally, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` at line 165 is not wrapped in any error handling — if it throws, the attendees have already been persisted to the DB (line 92) and the mutation rejects while the guests are actually added, leaving DB and calendars out of sync with a confusing error shown to the user.

title: Guests stored with empty name and no validation of booking status
body: New guests are created with `name: ""`, so attendee lists and emails render blank names for these guests (e.g. `to: `${this.attendee.name} <${...}>`" produces `" <a@b.com>"`). Also, the handler does not check `booking.status`, so guests can be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings, mutating data and sending 'guests added' emails for events that no longer exist.

title: Stale validation error state when reopening the dialog
body: `isInvalidEmail` is only reset on the Cancel button click. If the user submits invalid emails (error shown), then closes the dialog via the X / overlay (Dialog onOpenChange) and reopens it, the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error is still displayed even though the input was reset on success or still holds the old values otherwise. Validation state should reset when the dialog opens/closes or when the input changes.

title: No tests for the new addGuests endpoint
body: The PR adds a new mutation with non-trivial authorization rules (organizer / attendee / team admin), dedup and blacklist filtering, and email side effects, but no unit or e2e tests are added for any of this — particularly the currently-broken team-admin authorization (`&&` instead of `||`), which a test would have caught.

title: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||
body: The check `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` requires the caller to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner. A team admin who is not an owner (the common case for delegated management) will fail this check even though the intent is clearly 'admin OR owner'. Use `||` so team admins can add guests to their team's bookings.

title: Any booking attendee can add arbitrary guests via the API
body: The handler authorizes any logged-in user whose email matches one of the booking's attendees (`isAttendee`). The UI only exposes this action to the organizer, but the tRPC mutation is callable by any authenticated attendee, letting an external guest with a cal.com account add unlimited arbitrary email addresses to someone else's booking (spam vector, data exposure of the event/ICS to arbitrary addresses). There is also no rate limit and no cap on the number of guests per request. Authorization should be restricted to the organizer / team admin.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` build the EventManager from the calling user. If the caller is an attendee or a team admin (not the booking organizer), the calendar update (`updateCalendarAttendees`) runs against the caller's calendar/credential set, not the booking owner's, so the guest update will be applied to the wrong calendar or fail. The organizer's credentials (already included in the booking query via `user.credentials`) should be used.

title: Duplicate and blacklist email checks are case-sensitive
body: Blacklist entries are lowercased (`email.toLowerCase()`) but then compared with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` using the raw guest string, so `User@Example.com` bypasses a blacklisted `user@example.com`. Similarly `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive, so a guest already on the booking with different casing is re-added as a duplicate attendee row (and receives duplicate emails). Both the guest input and stored emails should be normalized (e.g. lowercased) before comparison.

title: Email failure swallowed and wrong guests list passed to sendAddGuestsEmails
body: Two problems: (1) the catch block only logs `"Error sending AddGuestsEmails"` without the error object, so failures are undiagnosable and silently ignored; (2) `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is passed the raw input `guests` rather than the filtered `uniqueGuests`, so emails that were skipped (already attendees or blacklisted) are still treated as 'new' in email-manager's `newGuests.includes(...)` check (case-sensitively too), causing an existing attendee who was also submitted again to receive a full 'scheduled' email instead of the add-guests email.

title: Error toast interpolates translation of a translation key that may not exist
body: `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`` assumes `err.message` is a translation key present in common.json. TRPC errors thrown from other layers (e.g. Prisma or calendar update failures) return raw English messages or keys like `booking_not_found` that are not guaranteed to exist, producing a toast like `BAD_REQUEST: booking_not_found` untranslated. Also, the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never trigger since the template string is always non-empty.

title: Add-guests action offered for cancelled/past/unconfirmed bookings
body: The `add_members` entry is added unconditionally to `editBookingActions`, which is included in `bookedActions` for past and even cancelled bookings (cancel filter only removes the cancel action). Adding guests to a cancelled or already-ended booking still fires calendar updates and sends 'new guests added' confirmation emails for an event that no longer happens. The action should be gated on `!isCancelled` and the booking being in the future.

title: No tests for the addGuests handler
body: The new mutation contains non-trivial authorization logic (organizer / team admin / attendee), dedup, blacklisting, and a calendar side effect, but the PR adds no integration or unit tests. The `&&` vs `||` admin bug (see separate finding) is exactly the kind of regression a permission test would have caught. At minimum, tests for the forbidden path, the duplicate-guest path, and the blacklist path should be added before merge.

title: retryCount deletion branch is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The `deleteMany` uses `OR: [{method: SMS, scheduledDate lte now}, {retryCount > 1}]`. The second branch has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and no `scheduled`/`scheduledDate` condition, so any WorkflowReminder row of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) whose retryCount exceeds 1 will be deleted by this SMS cron job. Today only this file increments retryCount, but the column is on the shared WorkflowReminder model and any other code path (or a future email/whatsapp retry implementation) that increments it will have its reminders silently destroyed by the SMS scheduler. The retryCount condition should be conjoined with `method: SMS` (and ideally `scheduled: false`).

title: Reminders skipped due to empty message or missing sendTo never increment retryCount
body: The retryCount increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)`. When `sendTo` is null/empty (e.g. booking has no smsReminderNumber and step action is not SMS_NUMBER) or the computed message is empty, neither the success nor the failure branch runs, so retryCount stays 0 and the reminder is re-fetched and re-skipped on every cron run until scheduledDate passes — exactly the 'kept scheduling until date is reached' behavior this PR claims to fix. These reminders should either be deleted or have retryCount incremented so they are purged.

title: retryCount increment uses stale in-memory value
body: The update writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` based on the value read when the batch was queried, rather than an atomic `increment: { retryCount: 1 }`. If the cron job runs concurrently (overlapping invocations or a manual trigger while the scheduled run is in progress), increments can be lost, so a reminder can fail more than twice before being deleted. Use `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` instead.

title: Exhausted reminders are silently deleted with no audit or notification
body: When a reminder exceeds the retry limit it is hard-deleted from the WorkflowReminder table. There is no log, no record of which booking/step failed, and no signal to the workflow owner, so users silently stop receiving SMS reminders (e.g. invalid phone numbers) with no way to diagnose it. Consider logging the deleted reminder ids or soft-cancelling (setting `cancelled`) instead of deleting, and/or notifying the workflow owner.

title: retryCount-based deleteMany drops the SMS method filter
body: The new `OR: [{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]` branch of the deleteMany has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or `scheduled: false`) condition, unlike the existing branch. Any WorkflowReminder of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) whose retryCount exceeds 1 will be hard-deleted by this SMS cron endpoint. Today only this file increments retryCount, but the column is on the shared WorkflowReminder model and other flows (e.g. WhatsApp/email scheduling crons or future code) may use it; when they do, this cron will silently delete their pending reminders. The condition should be scoped to unscheduled SMS reminders.

title: Retry counter incremented from stale in-memory value instead of atomic increment
body: Both the failure path (line 184) and the catch block (line 195) write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, computed from the value fetched at the start of the run. If two runs of this cron overlap (or a run is retried), increments are lost and a permanently failing reminder can be retried indefinitely, defeating the intended two-attempt limit. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead.

title: Reminders skipped for missing message/sendTo never count a retry and never get cleaned up
body: When `message` is empty or `sendTo` is missing (e.g. attendee has no SMS number), the code falls through without scheduling and without incrementing retryCount. Such a reminder stays `scheduled: false` and is re-fetched and re-skipped by every cron run until scheduledDate passes the 7-day window, wasting queries. Since this PR's stated goal is to stop endlessly reprocessing failing reminders, this skip path should also increment retryCount (or delete the reminder) so it is retired after two attempts.

title: retryCount delete condition is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The deleteMany OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, unlike the other branch. Any WorkflowReminder row of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) whose retryCount exceeds 1 will be deleted by this SMS cron job. Even though today only this file increments retryCount, the column is shared by all methods (WhatsApp reminders are handled by a separate cron, and the same retry pattern is likely to be reused there), so an email or WhatsApp reminder that failed twice would be silently destroyed by the SMS cron, dropping reminders that other schedulers still need. The retryCount condition should be ANDed with `method: SMS` (and probably `scheduled: false`).

title: retryCount incremented from stale in-memory value instead of atomic increment
body: The update writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, using the value read at query time. If two cron invocations overlap (or the handler is retried), both read the same retryCount and both write the same incremented value, so failures are undercounted and the retry limit is effectively never enforced. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead.

title: Deletion of over-retried reminders happens a run late and deletes scheduled:false rows mid-cycle
body: Deletion of reminders with retryCount > 1 happens only at the start of the next cron run. A reminder that failed twice (retryCount = 2) is still picked up and scheduled again in the current run (the findMany does not filter retryCount), so it can actually be attempted 3 times, and the Twilio call happens before the deleteMany of the next run removes it. If the intent is 'delete after failing twice', the findMany should exclude retryCount >= 2, or the delete filter timing should be documented/adjusted. This also means a reminder that succeeds on the third attempt is then deleted by the next run's deleteMany (retryCount 2 > 1), discarding the referenceId needed to cancel the scheduled SMS.

title: Public findMany() method removed, breaking existing callers
body: The refactor deletes the class's `findMany()` method, which was the main query entry point that took Prisma `BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs` and returned bookings. It is replaced only by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment. Any existing code that constructs `InsightsBookingService` and calls `service.findMany({ select, where, ... })` will now fail to compile or throw at runtime. The PR contains no changes to callers, so unless all call sites were already migrated in a prior PR, this is a breaking API change. The PR description also does not mention any caller migration.

title: Passing JS arrays to `= ANY(...)` may fail depending on Prisma driver serialization
body: In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` (line 164/168) and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` (line 201), plain JavaScript arrays are interpolated into `Prisma.sql` and used as `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})`. Depending on the Prisma engine/driver version, raw query parameters that are JS arrays are not always serialized as PostgreSQL array types, which can produce errors like "op ANY/ALL (array) requires array on right side" or unexpected type coercion for the `teamIds` (int) case. The idiomatic safe form is `${Prisma.join(teamIds)}` inside the parentheses or an explicit `::int[]` cast. Since the author explicitly states the integration tests were never run ("I encountered test runner configuration issues"), this serialization risk is unverified and the query construction should be confirmed to actually execute against a real database before merging.

title: Integration tests were never executed; author flags manual verification as required
body: The PR description states the test runner had configuration issues during development and asks a human to "Run integration tests manually" because the author could not verify them. The entire PR's purpose is to make these tests pass against the new raw-SQL implementation, yet there is no evidence they were run. Merging unexecuted tests for authorization-critical SQL (org/team scoping, owner/admin checks) risks shipping broken queries that either fail at runtime or, worse, produce conditions that leak or wrongly restrict data. The tests must be executed and passing in CI before merge.

title: Caching behavior tests were deleted without replacement
body: The old test suite had a dedicated "Caching" describe block asserting that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return identical (cached) results on repeated calls. The refactor keeps the caching fields (`cachedAuthConditions`, `cachedFilterConditions`) and logic but the tests for it were removed entirely. Since the cache field types changed (from Prisma where-input objects to `Prisma.Sql`), a regression here (e.g., `Prisma.Sql` identity checks failing, or an always-truthy `1=0` fragment being treated as 'already computed') would go undetected.

title: Final integration test asserts exact result set and depends on denormalized-table cleanup
body: The `getBaseConditions` test runs `SELECT id FROM "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" WHERE ${baseConditions}` and asserts the result is exactly one row (`[...toEqual([{ id: userBooking.id }])]`). Because `createTestData` also creates a booking tied to a team event type, and other tests/users may leave residual rows, any leftover denormalized row matching the same `userId`/`teamId IS NULL`/`eventTypeId` conditions will make this assertion fail or, conversely, hide bugs. The cleanup deletes the `Booking` rows but there is no explicit cleanup of `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` rows; if that table is not cascade-deleted with bookings, stale rows from prior test runs will accumulate and break the strict `toEqual`. An assertion on membership (`results.some(r => r.id === userBooking.id)` / length filtering) or explicit denormalized-row cleanup would be more robust.

title: Public findMany method removed, breaking existing callers
body: The service's public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method was deleted and replaced with `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a raw SQL fragment. Any existing code in the repository that constructs InsightsBookingService and calls `findMany(...)` to fetch bookings will now fail at compile time (or worse, at runtime if untyped) with 'findMany is not a function'. The PR description only mentions test updates, so this removal appears to be an unannounced breaking API change. Either keep `findMany` (implemented via $queryRaw with the base conditions) or update all call sites in the same PR.

title: Caching tests removed without replacement
body: The previous test suite had a 'Caching' describe block verifying that `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` return cached results on second call. These tests were deleted entirely rather than converted to the new Prisma.sql format. The service still contains caching logic (`cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` with the undefined-vs-null distinction), and that logic is now completely untested; a regression in the caching (e.g. caching null filter conditions incorrectly) would go undetected.

title: Tests were never executed; PR author reports test runner failures
body: The PR's own review checklist states 'I encountered test runner configuration issues, so please verify the tests actually pass.' None of the assertions in this file — especially the structural `toEqual(Prisma.sql\`...\`)` comparisons and the `$queryRaw` query against "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" — have been confirmed to pass. Notably, `$queryRaw` in Postgres returns BigInt for bigint columns, so the `expect(results).toEqual([{ id: userBooking.id }])` comparison at line 487 will fail if the table's id column is bigint, and the denormalized table must be populated (e.g. by trigger) for the booking created via `prisma.booking.create` for the row to appear at all. These tests must be run and confirmed green before merging.

title: Array parameters passed to ANY() rely on Prisma raw array serialization
body: The org- and team-scope conditions pass plain JavaScript arrays as raw query parameters, e.g. `Prisma.sql\`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))\``. Whether this works depends on how the Prisma query engine serializes JS arrays for raw queries; the established, safe pattern is `${Prisma.join(teamIds)}` inside an `IN (...)` clause. If serialization sends the array as a JSON/text parameter rather than a Postgres array, `= ANY(...)` will throw a type error at query time — and since the PR author could not run the tests, this has not been verified. Verify `ANY(${array})` executes correctly against Postgres, or switch to `IN (${Prisma.join(ids)})`.

title: Passing JS arrays into Prisma.sql with = ANY(...) produces invalid SQL
body: In buildOrgAuthorizationCondition (line 164, `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))`) and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition (line 201, `("userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam}))`), a plain JavaScript array is interpolated directly into a Prisma.sql template. Prisma's sql tag does NOT bind a JS array as a single Postgres array parameter — it expands array elements into separate positional placeholders (which is why Prisma.join exists for IN lists). So `ANY(${[1,2,3]})` becomes `ANY($1, $2, $3)`, which is a Postgres syntax/runtime error, or worse, `ANY($1)` with a scalar when the array has one element, silently matching nothing. The correct construction is `ANY(${Prisma.sql`ARRAY[${Prisma.join(teamIds)}]::int[]`})` or equivalent. The tests at lines 296 and 333 of the integration test compare against Prisma.sql templates built the same wrong way, so a deep-equal structural comparison can pass even though the generated query is broken when actually executed — and the PR description explicitly states the tests were never run.

title: findMany() removed, breaking existing callers of the service
body: The diff deletes the public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method, which accepted Prisma BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs and returned typed rows. It is replaced only by `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>`, which returns a raw SQL fragment that callers must embed into a hand-written raw query themselves. Any existing caller (e.g. insights repositories/routes that did `service.findMany({ select, orderBy, where })`) will fail to compile or, if untyped, fail at runtime. There is no deprecation shim or migration in this PR; the maintainer must verify every call site has been converted to $queryRaw with correct table names, select lists, and ordering before merging.

title: Final test queries BookingTimeStatusDenormalized but only inserts into Booking
body: The getBaseConditions test creates rows via `prisma.booking.create` and `prisma.eventType.create`, then runs `SELECT id FROM "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" WHERE ...` expecting the user booking's id to be returned. Unless BookingTimeStatusDenormalized is a live view or is populated by a trigger/denormalization job that runs synchronously on booking insert, the table will not contain the new row and the assertion will fail (or pass vacuously if rows are absent). The PR author notes the tests were never executed due to runner configuration issues, so this is unverified.

title: Caching tests deleted while caching behavior still exists in the service
body: The previous test file contained a "Caching" describe block verifying that getAuthorizationConditions and getFilterConditions return cached results on repeated calls. The service still implements this caching (cachedAuthConditions / cachedFilterConditions in insightsBooking.ts lines 84-95), but all coverage for it was removed rather than updated to the Prisma.Sql format. This is a regression in test coverage for behavior that remains in production code, including the subtle case where a cached `null` filter condition must not trigger a rebuild.

title: toEqual on Prisma.Sql objects may not validate actual SQL correctness
body: All condition tests compare results with `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql\`...\`)`. Prisma.Sql equality via vitest's deep equality only compares the internal strings/values structure; it does not verify the fragment is executable SQL. Combined with the fact that the author states the tests were never run, the expectations could match structurally while the produced SQL is invalid when executed (see the ANY(array) finding). At least one test per code path should execute the condition against the database via $queryRaw, as only the final test attempts to do.

title: deleteCache ownership check fails for delegated credentials
body: The handler authorizes the request with `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`. Delegation credentials often have `userId: null` (or an in-memory/negative id), so a user whose Google calendar is connected via a DelegationCredential will always get 'Credential not found or access denied' even though the UI (CredentialActionsDropdown) shows the 'Delete cached data' action for those credentials (hasCache is true when delegationCredentialId is set and canDisconnect is false). The user will always see 'Error deleting cache'. The check needs to account for delegated-to credentials the user has access to, or the UI must hide the delete action for them.

title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
body: After successfully deleting the cache via `trpc.viewer.calendars.deleteCache`, the component only calls `onSuccess?.()`. Unlike the disconnect mutation (which invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in onSettled), the delete-cache path never invalidates the `connectedCalendars` query. In the web wrapper `onChanged` is often undefined, so the UI will keep showing the old 'Cache Status / Last updated' timestamp (and the delete option) until an unrelated refetch happens, making the user think deletion didn't work.

title: Timestamp hardcoded to en-US and ignores user locale
body: The cache 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` instead of using the user's locale from `useLocale()`. All non-US users will see US-formatted dates (MM/DD/YYYY, 12-hour clock), inconsistent with the rest of the localized UI.

title: Nested interactive elements / non-interactive DropdownMenuItem
body: `DropdownItem` (renders a `<button>`) is nested inside `DropdownMenuItem`, which itself renders a menu item element — this produces invalid nested interactive DOM and can break keyboard navigation and screen readers. The cache-status block is also rendered as a selectable menu item (line 84) that does nothing when clicked/activated, which is confusing for keyboard users; it should be a non-interactive label.

title: Deleting the cache does not repopulate it while webhooks remain active
body: `deleteCacheHandler` deletes all CalendarCache rows for the credential but leaves the Google webhook channel subscriptions intact and never triggers `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`. The cache is only repopulated on webhook events (which only fire on actual calendar changes) or the unwatch flow. For organizations relying on the calendar-cache feature, this means after deletion every availability check falls back to live Google freebusy API calls indefinitely until some calendar change occurs, defeating the purpose of the cache and risking Google API quota exhaustion. Deletion should trigger a re-fetch (as `unwatchCalendar` does with `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`).

title: Authorization failure thrown as generic Error instead of TRPCError
body: When the credential isn't found/owned, the handler throws a plain `Error('Credential not found or access denied')`, which tRPC surfaces as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) with the message leaking to the client. Cal.com's convention is to throw `TRPCError({ code: 'UNAUTHORIZED' | 'NOT_FOUND' })` so clients get correct status codes and no server error noise/alerting.

title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data object is opaque and fragile
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` relies on Prisma's implicit `@updatedAt` bump when `data` is empty to work at all. This is undocumented/fragile behavior (some Prisma versions reject empty update data), updates rows even when the preceding cache writes failed, and communicates no intent. It also clobbers nothing but bumps `updatedAt` for all selected calendars of the credential, which the PR description itself flags as unused by the frontend — either give it an explicit data payload or remove the call until the field is consumed.

title: sed -i '' syntax is macOS-only and fails on Linux
body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E "..." "$ENV_FILE"`. On GNU/Linux sed, `-i ''` is interpreted as an empty file operand and the command fails, so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated on Linux dev machines. Also the relative `ENV_FILE="../.env"` depends on the caller's cwd. Use a portable check (e.g. `sed -i.bak`) or detect the platform.

title: No tests for new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds or deleteCache handler
body: The PR adds a new repository method (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, including the groupBy/_max mapping and null handling), a new tRPC mutation (`deleteCache`), and new enrichment logic in `connectedCalendarsHandler`, but includes no unit or e2e tests for any of them. In particular the credential-ownership check and the empty-credentialIds edge case are untested.

title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data object does not update updatedAt (and can throw)
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache ends with `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credentialId, {})`. The comment says it updates SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, but an empty `data` object contains no fields, so Prisma will either fail validation ("at least one field") or perform a no-op; in either case `updatedAt` is not bumped because @updatedAt is only refreshed when an update actually writes fields. The intended cache-refresh timestamp tracking therefore silently never happens. Pass an explicit field (or rely on a dedicated touch), e.g. `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` if that is the goal.

title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status
body: After a successful cache deletion the component only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback (which in SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper is `props.onChanged` and may be undefined). Unlike the disconnect mutation, there is no `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`, so the "Cache Status / Last updated" entry in the dropdown keeps showing the old timestamp until a full page reload or unrelated refetch. Add the same invalidation used in disconnectMutation's onSettled.

title: deleteCacheHandler throws plain Error instead of a TRPCError, producing an opaque internal server error
body: When the credential is not found or not owned by the user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. In cal.com's tRPC setup plain errors are masked as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, so the client shows the generic "Error deleting cache" message with no way to distinguish a permission problem. Throw a TRPCError with code UNAUTHORIZED/NOT_FOUND instead. Also note that for delegated (in-memory) credentials the UI passes a negative credentialId which will always land on this error path.

title: sed -i '' -E is macOS-only and fails on Linux
body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E "..." "$ENV_FILE"`. The `sed -i ''` (empty backup suffix) syntax only works on BSD/macOS sed; on GNU/Linux sed it fails with "can't read : No such file or directory". This dev script is not portable to the Linux environments most contributors use. Use `sed -i.bak -E ... && rm -f "$ENV_FILE.bak"` or detect the platform.

title: Extra groupBy DB query runs on every connectedCalendars call even when no cache can exist
body: The handler unconditionally instantiates CalendarCacheRepository and runs a groupBy over calendarCache for all credentialIds on every invocation of this very hot query (used by onboarding, settings, booking pages). Consider guarding the extra round-trip (e.g. only query when there is at least one Google Calendar credential, or fold the max(updatedAt) into the existing credential fetch) to avoid adding latency to every connectedCalendars request.

title: Behavior change: Alert rows now hide disconnect button when disableConnectionModification is set
body: Previously, the error/Alert branch rendered the disconnect control whenever `!connectedCalendar.delegationCredentialId` regardless of `disableConnectionModification`; the new CredentialActionsDropdown applies `disableConnectionModification` in both branches, so users in contexts that pass that flag (e.g. certain embed/event-type scopes) lose the ability to remove a broken integration from the Alert row where it was previously available. If intentional, confirm; otherwise pass the prop only for the non-Alert branch.

title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data object will throw at runtime
body: The new call `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object. Prisma's `updateMany` rejects an empty `data` argument with a validation error ("Argument `data` must provide at least one field"). Since the comment says the intent is to bump `updatedAt`, this call will throw every time `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` completes (i.e. on every calendar watch/unwatch cycle), breaking webhook-driven cache refresh. It should pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` instead.

title: Cache status timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale, ignoring user locale
body: The component formats `cacheUpdatedAt` with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, ignoring the user's selected locale even though the component already has `useLocale()`. All non-English users will see US-formatted dates. Should use the locale from `useLocale()`.

title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars, leaving stale cache status
body: On successful cache deletion, the component only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback (which is only passed as `onChanged` in some usages). It never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike the disconnect mutation. If `onChanged` is undefined or does not refetch, the UI continues to show the old "Cache Status / Last updated" entry and the "Delete cached data" option even though the cache is gone, until a manual page refresh.

title: Cache status lookup misses caches stored for in-memory delegation credentials
body: For in-memory delegation credentials (negative credentialId), `CalendarCache` rows are keyed by `userId` + key rather than the (nonexistent) DB credentialId (see `CalendarCacheRepository.getCachedAvailability`). `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` only groups by `credentialId`, so delegated Google Calendar users will never see their cache status and cannot clear it from the UI, even though a cache exists and is actively served. Either look up by userId for delegation credentials or document the limitation.

title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds reports expired cache entries as active
body: The groupBy query does not filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }`. A credential whose only cache rows have expired will still return an `updatedAt` value, so the UI will show a "Cache Status / Last updated" timestamp and a "Delete cached data" action for cache data that is no longer served. This is misleading and lets users trigger a no-op delete with a confirmation dialog.

title: sed -i '' is macOS-only and fails on Linux
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` uses the BSD/macOS form of in-place editing; on GNU/Linux (Linux CI/dev containers) `sed -i ''` fails with "can't read : No such file or directory". Use a portable form (e.g. `sed -i.bak` + remove the backup) or detect the platform.

title: dev:cron uses npx tsx but tsx is not a declared dependency
body: The script was changed from `ts-node` to `npx tsx`, but `tsx` is not in dependencies or devDependencies (only `ts-node` is, and it remains unused for this script). `npx` will download `tsx` ad hoc on each run (or fail offline / behind a proxy). Add `tsx` to devDependencies.

title: Cron re-schedules and sends emails for reminders already marked cancelled
body: The query that finds unscheduled email reminders to schedule (around line 80) filters only on method=EMAIL, scheduled=false and scheduledDate <= now+72h, but does not exclude reminders with cancelled=true. When a booking is cancelled, deleteScheduledEmailReminder only sets cancelled=true on the DB row; if the reminder was not yet scheduled (referenceId null, scheduledDate >72h out at booking time), the row stays in the DB with cancelled=true and scheduled=false. The CRON job will then pick it up in the 'unscheduledReminders' query and schedule/send the email anyway — exactly the bug this PR claims to fix. The where clause needs `cancelled: false` (or cancelled: null), and cancelled-but-unscheduled rows should be deleted.

title: Cancel query includes SMS reminders and reminders without a referenceId, and one SendGrid error aborts all cancellations
body: The remindersToCancel query (line 44) has no method filter, so cancelled SMS reminders (whose referenceId is a Twilio SID) are POSTed to SendGrid's /v3/user/scheduled_sends endpoint, which will fail. Likewise, cancelled reminders with referenceId=null (never scheduled) produce a batch_id of null and SendGrid returns an error. Because the loop `await client.request(...)` throws on the first failure, execution jumps to the catch block, so the accumulated workflowReminder.delete() promises collected so far are never executed and all remaining reminders in the list are not cancelled that run. Filter on method=EMAIL and referenceId not null, and handle per-reminder errors instead of aborting the batch.

title: Try/catch around reminder cancellation is ineffective; promises are fire-and-forget and cancellation can be lost
body: In the reschedule path, deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async functions invoked inside a synchronous forEach without await. The surrounding try/catch can never catch anything since no promise is awaited; if the serverless function returns and the process is frozen/terminated before the pending DB updates or SendGrid/Twilio calls complete, the old booking's reminders remain active and are sent for the cancelled slot. The calls should be awaited (e.g. Promise.all over the mapped promises).

title: Reminder cancellation on booking cancel is fire-and-forget and unawaited
body: The forEach at line 485 calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting them. If the request handler completes (or the serverless invocation ends) before those promises resolve, the `cancelled: true` flag is never written and the scheduled email/SMS is still sent for the cancelled booking. These calls set the DB state that the CRON job depends on, so they must be awaited before responding.

title: immediateDelete path cancels at SendGrid but leaves the DB row as scheduled=true with a live referenceId
body: When immediateDelete is set (workflow deletion, deleted/edited steps, reschedule in handleNewBooking), the function POSTs the cancel to SendGrid and returns without deleting or flagging the WorkflowReminder row. The row remains scheduled=true with its referenceId until the CRON's `deleteMany where scheduledDate <= now` cleanup runs (which only happens for email reminders whose date has passed). Until then, any other code that iterates a booking's or workflow's reminders (e.g. a subsequent reschedule, or workflows.update's edited-step path) will try to cancel the same batch again and can hit errors, and the stale rows misrepresent state. The row should be deleted (or at least marked cancelled) in this branch too.

title: Cron schedules reminders with scheduledDate less than 60 minutes (or in the past) away, defeating the cancellation design
body: The unscheduledReminders loop calls sgMail.send with sendAt = scheduledDate.unix() without verifying the SendGrid minimum of 60 minutes in the future (the check exists only in scheduleEmailReminder at booking time). A reminder whose scheduledDate is now+10 minutes is scheduled with a sendAt in the near past, which SendGrid processes immediately — so if a booking is cancelled right after a cron run, the cancellation (which only happens on the next 15-minute cron run) cannot win the race and the email is still sent, the exact bug being fixed. Reminders with scheduledDate < now+1h should not be scheduled via sendAt (send immediately is intended only for non-scheduled triggers).

title: Unused Prisma import and noisy re-indentation of commented-out code
body: The `Prisma` value imported from @prisma/client (line 9) is no longer used after the Prisma.BatchPayload delete logic was removed, which will fail lint/TS noUnusedLocals in stricter configs. Additionally, the diff re-indents a large block of commented-out (/* */) code in the testAction section, adding review noise and churn with no functional change; prefer leaving commented-out code untouched or deleting it.

title: Cancellation query includes unscheduled reminders, and one SendGrid failure aborts all remaining cancellations
body: The query selecting `remindersToCancel` filters only on `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now+1h`, without filtering `scheduled: true` (or method EMAIL). Reminders that were marked cancelled while still unscheduled (`scheduled: false`) have `referenceId: null`, so the SendGrid request `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` with `batch_id: null` will fail.
