Because the entire for-loop is wrapped in a single try/catch, that first failure throws out of the loop and none of the remaining cancelled reminders are cancelled at SendGrid — their scheduled emails will still be sent, which is exactly the bug this PR claims to fix. Filter to scheduled reminders with a non-null referenceId, and handle failures per-reminder instead of aborting the batch.

title: Prisma delete promises created in loop but only awaited at end; leaked on error
body: Inside the cancellation loop, `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({...})` is called (creating the query promise) and pushed to an array, but the array is only awaited after the loop. If any SendGrid cancel request throws (see the surrounding try/catch that aborts the loop), the already-created delete promises are never awaited, so those rows are never deleted (and Prisma query promises left unawaited keep the connection busy / are silently dropped). The reminder rows would then be retried on the next cron run. Delete each row right after its successful cancellation, or wrap each iteration in its own try/catch.

title: Reminder cancellation calls are fire-and-forget; request can complete before DB updates persist
body: The old code collected the reminder deletions into `prismaPromises` and awaited them via `Promise.all` before responding. The new code calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` inside a `forEach` without awaiting any of them. These functions perform DB writes (`cancelled: true` update or row delete) and external API calls; on a serverless deployment the function can be frozen/terminated right after the response is returned, so the `cancelled` flag may never be persisted — the scheduled email would still be sent for the cancelled booking. The same unawaited-forEach pattern was introduced in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (requestReschedule, ~line 488) and `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts` (~line 966), where the surrounding try/catch also cannot catch the async rejections. Await these calls (e.g. `await Promise.all(...)`).

title: Deferred cancellation window leaves reminders due within ~15 minutes still sent
body: In the non-immediate path, cancelling a scheduled email only sets `cancelled: true`; the actual SendGrid cancellation happens in the CRON job, which (per the PR description) runs every 15 minutes and only cancels reminders whose scheduledDate is within the next hour. A booking cancelled when its reminder is due in less than one cron interval (e.g. 5 minutes from now) will not be cancelled before the scheduled send time — the email/SMS reminder is still delivered for a cancelled or rescheduled booking. The previous behaviour cancelled immediately at SendGrid. Either cancel immediately when scheduledDate is within the cron interval, or run cancellation more frequently / without the 1-hour window.

title: immediateDelete path leaves the WorkflowReminder row in scheduled state
body: When `immediateDelete` is true and a referenceId exists, the function cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting or flagging the DB row. Callers like the workflow `delete` mutation rely on DB cascade to remove rows, but callers that don't cascade (e.g. edited workflow steps in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`) leave a row with `scheduled: true`, `cancelled: null` and a live referenceId until the CRON's past-date cleanup deletes it. Any future query that assumes `scheduled: true` means 'an active send exists' (or that re-reads and re-cancels) will operate on stale state. Deleting the row in this branch (as done for SMS) would make the semantics consistent.

title: Cancellation query does not filter by method EMAIL, so SendGrid is called with Twilio SIDs
body: The `remindersToCancel` query only filters on `cancelled: true` and scheduledDate, without `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`. If a non-email (SMS) reminder row ever ends up with `cancelled: true`, the loop will POST its Twilio message SID to the SendGrid `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` endpoint as a `batch_id`. That request fails, the thrown error is caught by the surrounding try/catch which aborts the whole loop, and all remaining email reminders in the batch are left uncancelled (and their DB rows undeleted) for that run. Each reminder should be cancelled/deleted individually with per-reminder error handling, and the query should filter `method: EMAIL`.

title: immediateDelete path never marks or deletes the DB row, so a failed SendGrid cancel is unrecoverable
body: In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, when `immediateDelete` is true the function only issues the SendGrid cancel request and returns; it never sets `cancelled: true` and never deletes the workflowReminder row. If the SendGrid request fails (network error, invalid batch id, rate limit), the error is swallowed by the catch and the row remains `scheduled: true, cancelled: null`. The cron job only cancels reminders with `cancelled: true`, so there is no retry: the email is still sent even though the booking was rescheduled (handleNewBooking uses `immediateDelete=true` for reschedules). The failure should set `cancelled: true` as a fallback so the cron can retry, or the row should be deleted/marked after a confirmed cancel.

title: Async reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget and not awaited
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async functions but are called inside `forEach` without awaiting (same pattern in packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:488 and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx in the delete/update handlers). The handler responds and continues (e.g. deletes attendees and booking references) while the cancellation DB update / SendGrid / Twilio calls are still in flight. Besides unhandled rejections, in workflows.tsx `delete` the subsequent `workflow.deleteMany` cascades to workflowStep and deletes the workflowReminder rows, which can race with the pending `prisma.workflowReminder.update({cancelled: true})` and make it fail with P2025 (silently caught), leaving the scheduled email uncancellable. All cancellation calls should be collected and awaited.

title: Cancellation only happens within 1 hour of the scheduled date, allowing late cron runs to miss emails
body: Reminders are only cancelled once `scheduledDate` is within the next hour, and the cron runs every 15 minutes. A booking cancelled shortly before a reminder's scheduled date (e.g. 10 minutes before) will only be processed at the next cron tick, which can be after the email has already been sent by SendGrid. There is no compensation for this window (e.g. cancelling immediately when the request comes in, or SendGrid-side suppression), so the original bug ('cancelled bookings still receive reminders') persists for reminders close to their send time.

title: If Twilio cancelSMS fails the reminder row is not deleted and never retried
body: In `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`, if `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` throws, the subsequent `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` is skipped (the catch swallows the error). The row survives with its referenceId, but nothing ever retries the cancellation — the callers have already moved on — so the SMS is still sent for a cancelled/rescheduled booking. The Twilio cancel and the DB delete should be decoupled so a Twilio failure doesn't prevent cleanup, or the row should be marked for retry like the email path.

title: Cancellation loop aborts entirely on the first SendGrid failure
body: The per-reminder SendGrid cancel request is inside a single try/catch wrapping the whole loop. One failing request (e.g. a stale/invalid batch_id for a reminder whose email was already sent) throws, skips the DB delete for that reminder and skips cancelling every subsequent reminder in `remindersToCancel` for this run; the failed reminder will fail again on every future run, permanently blocking the rest of the queue. Each reminder should be cancelled and deleted inside its own try/catch.

title: New `cancelled` column is nullable with no default, weakening queries and invariants
body: The migration adds `cancelled BOOLEAN` (nullable, no default) to WorkflowReminder. Existing and new rows have `cancelled = null` rather than `false`, so filters like `cancelled: true` work but any future filter for 'not cancelled' must treat null, and the Prisma type is `boolean | null` everywhere. `Boolean @default(false)` would make the semantics explicit and the cron queries simpler/safer.

title: Recurring-event calendar deletions are lost due to async forEach pushing into apiDeletes after awaits
body: In the recurring-event cancellation branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials...forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` is fire-and-forget. Since `getCalendar` is now async, the pushes into `apiDeletes` happen only after the dynamic import resolves — by which time the later `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` has already snapshotted an (empty) array and completed. External calendar events for cancelled recurring bookings will never be awaited (and may be skipped entirely if the process ends), leaving orphaned events on users' calendars. Before this PR, `getCalendar` was synchronous so the pushes happened before `Promise.all`. Fix by collecting with `Promise.all(credentials.map(async ...))` and awaiting it before the final Promise.all.

title: Dynamic import() calls are invoked eagerly, defeating the stated purpose of the PR
body: The appStore object is a module-level object literal whose property values are `import("./applecalendar")` etc. These import() calls all execute as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is first imported — every app module begins loading immediately, in parallel. The PR description says it makes app imports async/lazy, but no app loading is actually deferred; only the *await* is deferred. To make loading truly lazy, the store should hold factory functions (`() => import("./applecalendar")`) that are called on demand, otherwise this change adds promise indirection with no startup-time benefit (and a burst of simultaneous module loads on first import).

title: forEach(async ...) discards deletion promises; booking marked cancelled before external events are actually deleted
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` never awaits the returned promises. With the now-async `getCalendar`, each callback suspends at the first await and the surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch any errors thrown inside (rejections become unhandled promise rejections, not logged). The function then proceeds to send the reschedule email and return success while external calendar/video deletions may still be in flight (or fail silently), so users' external calendars can keep the old event even though the booking was already set to CANCELLED in the DB at line 67. The same pattern exists in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx line 553 (requestReschedule). Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` instead.

title: getCalendarCredentials now stores a Promise in the `calendar` field, silently changing its contract
body: `getCalendarCredentials` calls `getCalendar(credential)` without awaiting, so each returned item's `calendar` property is now a `Promise<Calendar | null>` rather than a `Calendar | null`. The internal consumer `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to `await item.calendar`, but `getCalendarCredentials` is an exported function; any other caller that uses `item.calendar` directly (e.g. calling `calendar.listCalendars()` or checking `if (!calendar)`) now operates on a Promise, which is always truthy, so null-checks stop working and method calls will fail at runtime with no TypeScript error if the consumer widened the type. The promise should be either awaited in `getCalendarCredentials` (making it async) or explicitly typed so callers know to await it.

title: Static app imports in EventManager and other core files undermine the async appStore refactor
body: While appStore was converted to dynamic imports, `packages/core/EventManager.ts` still statically imports `FAKE_DAILY_CREDENTIAL` from `@calcom/app-store/dailyvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter`, `handleCancelBooking.ts` statically imports from dailyvideo and zapier app packages, and `videoClient.ts` statically imports `getDailyAppKeys` from `@calcom/app-store/dailyvideo/lib/getDailyAppKeys`. These static imports pull the dailyvideo and zapier app modules (and their dependency trees) into every bundle/serverless function that includes core, negating the code-splitting the PR intends. At minimum this inconsistency should be noted or resolved, otherwise the refactor provides no bundle-size benefit for the booking flow.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes asynchronously and never awaited
body: In the `allRemainingBookings` path, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... const deletedEvent = await calendar?.deleteEvent(...); apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` uses an async callback inside forEach. The push into `apiDeletes` happens only after the await, i.e. on a later microtask/macrotask tick, while the surrounding handler continues and reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) before the forEach callbacks have pushed anything. Previously (with the sync `getCalendar`) the deleteEvent promise was pushed synchronously and thus awaited. As a result, cancellation of all remaining recurring events returns success while the external calendar-event deletions are still in flight (or may never complete if the request/process ends), leaving orphaned events on users' calendars.

title: forEach(async ...) makes calendar/video deletions fire-and-forget and the try/catch dead
body: The change from `forEach((bookingRef) => {...})` to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` means the returned promises are discarded: `Reschedule` returns and `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` runs without waiting for the external calendar deletions, and the surrounding `try { ... } catch` can never catch rejections from the async callbacks (they become unhandled promise rejections). If the serverless function is frozen/terminated after the response, calendar events and video meetings for the rescheduled booking may never be deleted. The callbacks should be collected and awaited via Promise.all. Same issue exists in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx line 553.

title: Dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly, so the appStore is not actually lazy and failures become unhandled rejections
body: `const appStore = { applecalendar: import("./applecalendar"), ... }` calls `import()` at module-evaluation time for every app. This defeats the stated purpose of the PR (async/lazy imports): merely importing `@calcom/app-store` still triggers loading of all ~28 app packages. Worse, if any single app module throws at load time, its promise rejects with no `.catch` anywhere, producing an unhandled promise rejection at startup (a hard crash under Node's default behavior). To be lazy, the store should expose getters or functions (e.g. `get applecalendar() { return import("./applecalendar") }`) so imports only run on access.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions are fire-and-forget and may never run before the request completes
body: In the allRemainingBookings branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` uses an async callback inside forEach. Nothing awaits these promises: `apiDeletes` is later consumed via `await apiDeletes;` (line 617), which awaits a plain array (a no-op), and `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 can run before the async forEach bodies have pushed anything (the first `await getCalendar(credential)` yields before any deleteEvent is pushed). Consequence: when cancelling all remaining recurring bookings, external calendar events may not be deleted at all, or deleted after the response/DB cleanup, and any failures surface as unhandled promise rejections. Replace with `for...of`/`Promise.all` and actually await the resulting promises.

title: forEach(async ...) swallows the returned promises, so deletions are unawaited and errors escape the try/catch
body: The loop `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` discards the promises returned by the async callbacks. Because the callback is now async (it was made async by this PR to await getCalendar), the surrounding try/catch can no longer catch errors thrown while resolving the app import or getCalendar — any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection, and Reschedule() can return before calendar/video events are actually deleted. The identical pattern exists in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125 and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553. Collect the promises (e.g. `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`) so they are awaited and errors are handled.

title: Async forEach callback results discarded; deletion errors become unhandled rejections
body: Same issue as vital/lib/reschedule.ts: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` fire-and-forgets the async work. Previously getCalendar was synchronous, so sync errors were caught by the enclosing try/catch; after this change, rejections from the dynamic import or getCalendar escape the try/catch as unhandled promise rejections, and the function proceeds to send the reschedule email and return `true` regardless of whether calendar/video events were actually deleted. Await the collected promises instead.

title: All dynamic imports are started eagerly at module evaluation; failed chunk loads produce unhandled rejections
body: The appStore object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")` (and all others) at module-evaluation time, so merely importing `@calcom/app-store` kicks off loading every app chunk immediately — the lazy-loading benefit only applies to bundling, not to runtime loading, and on the server every app module is still loaded whenever app-store is imported. Additionally, if any of these top-level import promises rejects (e.g. a broken app build), it becomes an unhandled promise rejection that can crash the Node process even for code paths that never use that app. Wrap the entries in functions/thunks (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) or attach a rejection handler so failures are surfaced only to the code that awaits them.

title: `await apiDeletes` awaits an array, not a promise — deletion failures are silently ignored on paid-booking cancellation
body: In the paid-booking branch, `await apiDeletes;` awaits a plain Array (which resolves immediately), so none of the calendar/video deletion promises pushed into apiDeletes are actually awaited before returning "Booking successfully cancelled.". Combined with this PR's change to push into apiDeletes from an async forEach callback (line 460-470), deletions may not even have been started yet. Use `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)` so integration deletions complete (and failures are observed) before responding.

title: Slots inside a date override skip the busy-time check entirely
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, once a slot is found to be on a day with a date override and inside the override window, the function returns `true` immediately (`if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }`) without ever evaluating the `busy` array. This means that for fixed hosts (the primary path this PR adds, where `checkIfIsAvailable` is the only busy-time filter), any existing booking or calendar busy time that falls inside a date-override window will be reported as available. The attendee can be shown (and attempt to book) a slot where the host already has a meeting. The override should restrict the time window, not bypass conflict checking.

title: Working-hours check compares UTC slot minutes against organizer-timezone working hours
body: In the new working-hours validation inside `checkIfIsAvailable`, `slotStartTime` is a UTC dayjs, so `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` yields minutes since midnight UTC. But `workingHour.startTime/endTime` (from `getUserAvailability` / `getAggregateWorkingHours`) are minutes since midnight in the organizer's timezone. For any organizer not in UTC (e.g. Asia/Kolkata in the test data, working hours 09:30–18:00 local), the comparison `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` uses the wrong clock, wrongly marking valid in-hours slots as unavailable or letting out-of-hours slots through. Additionally, `const end` is computed identically to `const start` (both from `slotStartTime`), so the `end > workingHour.endTime` condition never tests the slot's end time — the event length is not accounted for at all.

title: Date overrides that cross midnight in the invitee timezone are silently dropped
body: The new override computation converts the override start/end to minutes since midnight in the invitee timezone (`dayjs(...).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...minute()`). `hour()` wraps at 24, so an override such as 23:00–01:00 (invitee time) produces `startTime: 1380, endTime: 60`. `buildSlots` then skips this timeframe via the `if (start >= end) continue;` guard, so the override disappears entirely instead of splitting into two ranges. The previous code had the same wrap problem, but this rewrite was the opportunity to fix it; users with overnight overrides will see their normal working hours applied (or no availability) instead of the override.

title: Object-identity comparison makes the unavailability-override check dead code
body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the check `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly created dayjs objects with `===`, which is always false regardless of the underlying times. The intent (per the surrounding logic) was to detect a zero-length override, i.e. an override marking the whole day unavailable (start === end). Such 'blocked day' overrides will not be recognized by this branch; instead they fall through to the subsequent `slotEndTime.isBefore(...)` checks, which for an empty range will mark every slot as outside the override and the day will incorrectly become unavailable (or available depending on order) — in any case the special-cased behavior can never trigger and is dead code.

title: Override-day matching compares organizer-local date against UTC slot date
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` compares the organizer-local calendar date of the override start with the UTC calendar date of the slot. For organizers in non-UTC timezones, slots in the first hours of a UTC day (or last hours) belong to a different local day, so the override-day detection is off by one day for those slots. Slots just after midnight UTC on the override day will not be treated as override-day slots (and vice versa), producing wrong availability at day boundaries.

title: No test for the fixed-host date override in a round-robin team event
body: The PR's headline fix is that date overrides of fixed hosts are respected in round-robin events (issue #8207), but the added test only covers a single-user event with a date override and a different invitee timezone. There is no test with a ROUND_ROBIN event containing an `isFixed` host with a date override plus a non-fixed host, so the main code path added in `getSchedule` (`fixedHosts.every(...)` with date overrides) and the buggy busy-time bypass it introduces are not exercised by any test.

title: DST offset computed once from override start may be wrong for override end
body: The offset applied to the override is derived from a single instant (`override.start`): `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. If the override range spans a DST transition (possible for multi-hour or multi-day overrides), the end time is shifted by the start instant's offset, misplacing the end of the availability window by the DST delta. The offset should be evaluated at the respective instant for both start and end.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === never match, breaking 'unavailable' date overrides
body: In checkIfIsAvailable the guard for a full-day block is `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`. Dayjs factory calls always return distinct object instances, so this strict equality is never true regardless of the underlying times. The intended 'start equals end means mark the whole day unavailable' case is therefore never detected: for a blocked day, a slot that spans the block timestamp falls through all the other conditions, find() returns undefined, dateOverrideExist is true, and the function returns true (available). Result: slots overlapping an 'unavailable' date override are still shown as bookable. Use .isSame() (or compare .valueOf()) instead.

title: Working-hours check compares slot end minutes to slot start minutes
body: In the newly added working-hours check inside checkIfIsAvailable, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start` two lines above. Because of this, the condition `end > workingHour.endTime` can never be true, so slots that start inside working hours but whose end (start + eventLength) exceeds the end of the working hours are incorrectly reported as available. The `end` computation should include the event length, e.g. `start + eventLength`.

title: Working-hours minutes compared in different timezones (organizer vs UTC)
body: The new working-hours check computes `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` from the slot's UTC time and compares it to `workingHour.startTime`/`endTime`. Per the WorkingHours type comment (packages/types/schedule.d.ts), those values are 'minutes since midnight; serialized to UTC by using the organizer timeZone'. So the comparison mixes organizer-local minutes with UTC minutes and is wrong whenever the organizer's timezone is not UTC: for example an organizer in IST with hours 09:30-18:00 local gets workingHour.startTime=570, but a 04:00 UTC slot (09:30 IST) yields 240 < 570 and is rejected, while a 12:00 UTC slot (17:30 IST) passes even though only 30 minutes of the day remain. The slot time must first be converted to the organizer timezone (organizerTimeZone is already passed in) before extracting hour/minute. Note this same mismatch affects the day-of-week check via slotStartTime.day().

title: Date-override day match compares organizer-local date against UTC slot date
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, the override's day is computed by converting `date.start` into the organizer's wall-clock time (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD')`) but it is compared against `slotStartTime.format('YYYY MM DD')`, which is the slot's UTC date. When the organizer's timezone is not UTC, the two dates only coincide by accident; for organizers east of UTC an override late in their local day maps to the next UTC day's slots and vice versa, so overrides apply to (or are skipped for) the wrong day. The slot date should be converted to the organizer timezone (e.g. dayjs.tz(slotStartTime, organizerTimeZone)) before the comparison.

title: Override minute conversion drops day information and can produce inverted ranges
body: The new offset conversion computes startTime/endTime as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, 'minute').hour() * 60 + .minute()`. Only the wall-clock hour/minute of the shifted instant is kept, so when the timezone offset shifts the override into the previous or next calendar day relative to the invitee day being computed, the resulting minute value silently wraps around midnight: an override whose shifted start is 23:30 yields startTime=1410 while endTime (shifted to 00:30 next day) yields 30, giving startTime > endTime. buildSlots then discards the range ('bypass invalid value' when start >= end), so the override disappears and the day falls back to nothing (the user's normal working hours for that day were already spliced out), leaving zero availability instead of the override window. The calculation should also adjust for the day shift (e.g. compare dates and add/subtract 24h of minutes).

title: Override offset computed via Date.toString() parsed in server-local timezone
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` stringifies the Date in the server's local timezone and re-parses it with dayjs (also local), then converts to the organizer timezone. Because both the stringify and the parse use the same local zone the instant is approximately preserved, but this is fragile (toString includes a timezone name/offset that dayjs parsing may or may not honor consistently) and it is simpler and safer to use `dayjs(override.start).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. Additionally, `override.timeZone` is optional in the TimeRange type; if a caller omits it (e.g. dynamic-event paths or other consumers of getSlots), `dayjs(...).tz(undefined)` silently falls back to the server's local timezone, producing wrong offsets with no error. Consider making it required or defaulting explicitly.

title: No test for the primary fix: round-robin date overrides of fixed hosts
body: The PR's headline fix (#8207) is that date overrides of fixed hosts are respected for round-robin events, implemented via the new dateOverrides/workingHours logic in checkIfIsAvailable and the isFixed filtering in getSchedule. The only test added is the timezone-variation case for a personal event's date override. There is no test with a ROUND_ROBIN event containing a fixed host with a date override (the scenario described in the PR's own manual test plan), so a regression in the fixed-host filtering (e.g. the working-hours minutes bug above) would go undetected. Add a test mirroring the manual steps: round-robin event, one fixed host with an override, one round-robin host, assert only fixed-host-available slots are returned.

title: Slots inside a date override bypass all busy-time checks
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a slot falls on a day that has a date override and the slot is inside the override window, `dateOverrideExist` is set to true and the function returns true immediately (lines 133-135), never reaching the `busy.every(...)` check at the bottom. Consequence: a fixed host (or any host) who has a calendar event or an accepted Cal booking during the override window will still be reported as available for that slot, allowing double bookings — the exact class of bug this PR claims to fix for round-robin. The override check should mark the slot as within-override and then still evaluate busy times.

title: Working-hours check compares UTC slot hours to organizer-local working hours and computes wrong end
body: The new working-hours validation computes `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(); const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` — start and end are identical, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends past workingHour.endTime is never rejected (end should be start + eventLength). Additionally, `slotStartTime` is a UTC dayjs (time.utc()), so `hour()` returns the UTC hour, while `workingHour.startTime/endTime` are minutes-since-midnight in the organizer's timezone. For any organizer not on UTC the comparison is off by the organizer's UTC offset, so valid slots get rejected and invalid ones accepted.

title: Object-identity comparison of dayjs instances is always false
body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two distinct dayjs object references with `===`, which is always false regardless of values. The intended zero-length-override (unavailability) check is dead code and never fires; presumably `.isSame(...)` was meant.

title: Selected-slots filter drops dateOverrides and workingHours, weakening availability check
body: In the final selectedSlots filter (line ~581), checkIfIsAvailable is called with `busy`, `...availabilityCheckProps`, and `organizerTimeZone`, but without the host's `dateOverrides` or `workingHours`. For events with seat selection or reserved slots, the date-override logic just added elsewhere is not applied here, so behavior differs between the fixed/loose host checks and this path; slots that should be blocked by a fixed host's date override can still be returned in this branch.

title: Override times that cross midnight after offset conversion produce inverted minute ranges
body: The override startTime/endTime are computed as `hour() * 60 + minute()` after applying the invitee-organizer offset. If the shift moves the override start or end across midnight (e.g., an organizer override ending at 00:30 local), the minute-of-day arithmetic produces a wrong or inverted range (endTime < startTime), which buildSlots then discards (`if (start >= end) continue`) or clips incorrectly, silently dropping availability that should exist. There is no handling for day rollover introduced by the offset.

title: No test for the round-robin fixed-host date-override fix described in the PR
body: The PR's headline fix (date overrides of fixed hosts constraining round-robin availability) has no corresponding test: the only new test re-checks the personal-event timezone behavior, and the existing ROUND_ROBIN tests use plain IstWorkHours schedules without date overrides for the fixed host. A regression in the checkIfIsAvailable changes (e.g., the busy-time bypass or the broken working-hours comparison) would not be caught for the round-robin scenario the PR claims to fix.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting is absent or empty
body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` without checking that a row was returned. On any site where the `embed_category` site setting was never saved (the default is ''), the query returns zero rows, `[0]` is nil, and calling `['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration and blocking deploys. The same unguarded `[0]['value']` pattern applies to the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15. Both lookups need nil checks before indexing.

title: SQL injection / broken migration via unescaped host values in INSERT
body: The migration interpolates each migrated host value directly into a SQL string: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. Host values come from the admin-editable `embeddable_hosts` site setting and may contain a single quote (the old setting had no strict validation), which either breaks the migration with a syntax error or allows arbitrary SQL to run during migrate. Use `quote`/sanitize or ActiveRecord inserts with connection quoting instead of string interpolation.

title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError when the host id doesn't exist
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a nonexistent or already-deleted id, and the controller then calls `host.host = ...` (update) or `host.destroy` (destroy) on nil, producing a 500 error instead of a 404. This is easy to hit from the admin UI by double-clicking delete on the same row. Guard for a nil record and return not_found.

title: create/update crash with 500 when embeddable_host params are missing
body: `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` assumes the nested params hash exists. A PUT/POST request without the `embeddable_host` key (e.g. from an outdated client, a manual API call, or the embedding controller's empty `update({})` payload) raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 rather than a 400/422 validation error. Use `params.require(:embeddable_host).permit(:host, :category_id)` or safe navigation.

title: EmbeddingController#update is a no-op but is wired to the frontend save button
body: The `update` action just re-renders the serialization of freshly loaded data; it never reads or persists any request parameters. The admin UI's `saveChanges` action calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which PUTs to this route, so the 'save' button silently does nothing. Either implement the update (persist the embedding settings) or remove the PUT route and the save button until it does something.

title: No uniqueness constraint on host allows duplicate embeddable hosts
body: There is no uniqueness validation or unique index on `embeddable_hosts.host`, so an admin can create the same host multiple times (also a race between two admins). `record_for_host` then uses `.first`, so the category applied to new embedded topics is nondeterministic among the duplicates. Add a uniqueness validation (case-insensitive, matching the `lower(host) = ?` lookup) and a unique index in the migration.

title: record_for_host compares a possibly mixed-case referer host against lowercased stored hosts
body: The lookup is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` — only the stored side is lowercased. `URI(...).host` preserves the case of the referer (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com/page` yields `EvilTrout.com`), so a referer with uppercase letters fails to match even though the equivalent lowercase referer works. The comparison should be `where("lower(host) = ?", host.to_s.downcase)`.

title: category_id is not validated to reference an existing category
body: The controller assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` directly and saves. There is no validation that the category exists (the model only has a format validation on `host`), so an arbitrary integer (or a stale id from the UI after a category was deleted) is stored, and topics embedded from that host will be created in a nonexistent category. Add a presence/existence validation for category.

title: save() leaves the row in edit mode and loses unsaved state feedback on failure paths
body: On save, `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId))` runs only in the success handler, but if `categoryId` is blank (admin cleared the category chooser) `findById(null)` returns undefined and the UI shows an empty category while the server silently falls back to uncategorized — the displayed state does not match what was saved. Additionally the buffered `host` name is never synced back onto the record (`host.save(props)` behavior aside), so cancelling after a failed save can show stale values. Mirror the server's uncategorized fallback or block blank categories client-side.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category and embeddable_host files
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `embeddable_host` fabricator, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the `category` fabricators. The code works because Fabricator loads all files, but the file names no longer describe their contents, which will confuse future edits (e.g. someone adding a category fabricator to category_fabricator.rb creating a duplicate-definition conflict with the other file). The contents should live in the correctly named files.

title: No functional tests for the new admin controllers' CRUD behavior
body: Both new controller specs only assert the controller's superclass. There are no tests for create/update/destroy, including the nil-record 500s on nonexistent ids, missing-param handling, blank category fallback to uncategorized, or authorization (the routes use AdminConstraint but the controller's own before_filter only requires staff). Since this PR introduces the whole persistence path for embeddable hosts, these behaviors are currently untested.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category site setting row is absent
body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. Site settings are only persisted to the site_settings table once changed from their default, so on most installs (where embed_category was never set) the query returns no rows and `[0]` is nil, raising NoMethodError and failing the migration for everyone. Same problem on line 15 for the uncategorized_category_id lookup. Both lookups need nil-safe handling (e.g. use `SiteSetting` defaults or guard against empty results).

title: Host values interpolated directly into INSERT SQL
body: The migration builds `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` by string interpolation. The embeddable_hosts setting was free-form text, so any line containing a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) will break the migration or inject unintended SQL. Values should be quoted/escaped (e.g. via `quote_value` or ActiveRecord inserts).

title: create_table with force: true and irreversible data migration inside change
body: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` will silently drop an existing embeddable_hosts table (data loss if the migration is ever re-run against a partially migrated database). Additionally, the data copy and the `DELETE FROM site_settings` make the migration effectively irreversible while living in a `change` method, so `rake db:rollback` will fail or destroy the old settings with no way back.

title: update/destroy crash with 500 when host id does not exist
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown/stale id, then `save_host(host)` calls `host.host = ...` and `host.destroy` on nil, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of a 404. Should render not_found when the record is missing.

title: before_validation calls sub! on possibly-nil host
body: The `before_validation` block runs `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If a request creates/updates a host without a `host` parameter (params[:embeddable_host][:host] is nil or the key is missing), `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. It should guard with `if self.host.present?` so the format validation can report the error properly.

title: Host validation regex too restrictive
body: The format regex requires a dot and a 2–5 letter TLD (`\.[a-z]{2,5}`), so valid hosts like `localhost:3000`, `my_host.example.com` (underscore), hosts with new long TLDs, or trailing dots are rejected. Since this list drives which sites can embed comments, admins on intranet/dev setups will be unable to configure valid hosts and will get only a generic format error.

title: update action is a no-op
body: PUT /admin/customize/embedding simply re-serializes the current state and ignores the request body entirely, while the new admin UI's `saveChanges` action calls `embedding.update({})` as if it persisted something. The endpoint silently discards any submitted changes; either implement the update or remove the save control so admins are not misled into thinking embedding settings were saved.

title: Fabricator contents swapped between files
body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. The files' contents are exchanged. It happens to work because fabricators are loaded globally, but every future edit (e.g. someone adding a category fabricator to the 'right' file or deleting what looks like a duplicate) will be error-prone; the contents should be in their correctly named files.

title: No index on embeddable_hosts.host despite per-request lookup
body: `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` on every `/embed/comments` and `/embed/count` request (these are high-traffic, cacheable embed endpoints hit by every page view of embedding sites). There is no index on `host`, so each embed request triggers a full table scan once more than a handful of hosts exist. Add an index (on `lower(host)` for Postgres) in the migration.

title: New hosts saved without a category send null and lose user's choice context
body: For a newly added host, `categoryId` is initialized to null and the category-chooser starts empty; save sends `category_id: null`, which the server silently converts to the uncategorized category. Combined with `Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer checking host presence and `TopicEmbed.import` using the host's category for new topics, hosts accidentally created without a category will post embedded topics to Uncategorized with no warning. Also, `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))` returns undefined for a null category, leaving `host.category` unset after save until reload.

title: No request specs for new admin controllers
body: Both new controller specs only assert the controller's superclass. There are no tests for create/update/destroy of embeddable hosts (including the nil-host-param crash, blank category fallback to uncategorized, and validation error rendering) or for the embedding show/update endpoints. Given this PR replaces a working site-setting mechanism with new endpoints and a data migration, the behavior is essentially untested.

title: expandable_first_post? no longer requires any embeddable host
body: The check `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && ...` was reduced to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. A stale TopicEmbed with no matching EmbeddableHost (e.g. after the host was deleted, which nothing prevents) will still be treated as expandable, triggering `TopicEmbed.expanded_for` remote fetches for hosts that are no longer allowed. If the host requirement was intentionally dropped, the migration should also clean up orphaned topic_embeds or the retrieval should be validated against EmbeddableHost.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting is absent (fresh installs)
body: The migration unconditionally does `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. On any site that never set the `embed_category` site setting (including all fresh installs and test databases), the query returns zero rows, so `[0]` is nil and calling `['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration entirely. The `embeddable_hosts` lookup below is guarded with `cmd_tuples > 0`, but the category lookup is not. The result string must be checked for emptiness before dereferencing.

title: SQL injection / broken INSERT via unescaped host values in migration
body: The migration builds `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` by string interpolation with no quoting. The host values come from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting, which was free-form text; a value containing a single quote (or any SQL metacharacter) will either break the migration with a syntax error or inject arbitrary SQL. Use `sanitize_sql`/quote or ActiveRecord inserts instead.

title: create_table uses force: true, silently dropping existing data
body: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` will drop and recreate the table if it already exists (e.g. if the migration is re-run in a weird state or the table was created by an earlier deploy), silently destroying all embeddable host rows. A fresh migration should not use `force: true`.

title: EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that pretends to save
body: The `update` action is routed (PUT /admin/customize/embedding) and the frontend `saveChanges` action calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, but the controller never reads params or persists anything — it just re-renders the current state. Any admin who hits save gets a success response while nothing is saved. Either persist the submitted attributes or remove the route/action until there is something to update.

title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError on unknown id
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil when the id doesn't exist (e.g. the record was deleted in another tab). `save_host(nil)` then raises NoMethodError on `host.host =` and `destroy` raises on `host.destroy`, producing a 500 instead of a 404. Guard for a missing record and render not_found.

title: Nil/blank host value causes NoMethodError before validation can report an error
body: `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is assigned straight onto the record, and the model's `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)`. If `host` is nil (empty input or missing param), `sub!` raises NoMethodError and the request 500s instead of returning a validation error via `render_json_error`. Also note `sub!` on a frozen/nil value and the fact that `validates_format_of` would have handled a blank value if the callback didn't crash first.

title: No uniqueness validation on host
body: There is no `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (and no unique index in the migration). An admin can save the same host twice; `record_for_host` then uses `.first`, so only one of the duplicate categories is ever used for embedding, and the second record silently shadows the first. Add a uniqueness validation and a unique index on lower(host).

title: Host regex rejects valid hostnames and long TLDs
body: The validation regex `\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` rejects hosts with TLDs longer than 5 characters (e.g. `.museum`, `.travel`, internationalized/punycode `xn--` labels), hosts with underscores, and `localhost`. Since before_validation strips schemes/paths anyway, the port/path portions of the regex are also dead weight. Valid-looking hosts will fail with a confusing format error.

title: Fabricator contents are in swapped files
body: The embeddable_host fabricator now lives in `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` while all the category fabricators were moved into `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. It happens to work because Fabrication loads all files, but the file names no longer reflect their contents, which will confuse anyone looking for the category or embeddable_host fabricator definitions. The contents should be in the correctly named files.

title: New admin controllers have no request specs
body: Both new controller specs only assert the controller's superclass. There are no tests for create/update/destroy behavior: success serialization, validation error rendering (render_json_error), the blank-category fallback to uncategorized_category_id, or authorization (only the route-level AdminConstraint is exercised). Given the nil-record and nil-host crash paths above, these endpoints are untested against real inputs.

title: Hardcoded 10MB client-side limit ignores SiteSetting max image/attachment sizes
body: The client-side upload validation previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] (i.e. max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb) but now hardcodes 10MB. This breaks validation in both directions: on sites where the admin set a lower limit (e.g. 4MB), oversized files pass the client check and only fail on the server with a confusing generic error; and the hardcoded 10MB cap cannot be raised by admins. The same hardcode in the 413 handler (line 246) shows users a wrong maximum size in the error message. The stated goal of the PR (allow large images that the server will downsize) is undermined because the client still blocks any image over 10MB and, worse, blocks images over the (possibly small) configured limit that the new server-side downsizing was meant to accept — the client check should be relaxed or removed for images, not fixed at 10MB.

title: In-place downsize: convert is run with input and output as the same file path
body: OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) executes ImageMagick's `convert /tmp/xxx /tmp/xxx`, i.e. the source and destination are the same path. ImageMagick reads the input lazily and can truncate/corrupt the file while writing, or fail outright, depending on format and buffering. The result can be a corrupted or zero-byte upload. The downsized output should be written to a separate temp file and then replace the original.

title: Animated GIFs lose animation and animated path is never selected for uploads
body: The animated-image branch in OptimizedImage.optimize is chosen only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but `tempfile.path` for an uploaded file is a Tempfile path with no .gif extension (e.g. /tmp/d discourse-upload...). So animated GIFs always go through `convert #{from}[0] ...`, which keeps only the first frame, silently destroying animation. Additionally, `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is passed, but the actual check inside optimize tests the file path's extension, not the flag, so the setting has no effect here. Files with no recognizable animation possible (corrupt images) will also make `convert` fail repeatedly (see next finding).

title: Downsize loop ignores failures and still submits the oversized file
body: The while loop decrements `attempt` but never checks the return value of OptimizedImage.downsize, which returns false when convert fails (corrupt image, missing ImageMagick, etc.). On failure the file size never changes, so the loop pointlessly shells out 5 times and then passes the still-oversized file to Upload.create_for, which will reject it with a generic error. The loop should break out and fail fast (or surface a clear error) when downsize returns false.

title: Duplicate definition of self.downsize; first (width/height) form is dead code
body: The class now defines `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 and then redefines `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. Ruby silently discards the first definition (with a 'method redefined' warning in some modes), and both have the same arity so callers passing width and height as separate integers will now hit the second definition and produce a broken dimension string like "640x480" vs "1024-768"-style concatenation issues... concretely, a caller invoking downsize(from, to, 100, 75) now gets dimensions "100" passed to ImageMagick (75 is bound to opts), producing wrong output rather than an error. The two-integer variant should be removed entirely or the definitions merged, not left as shadowed duplicate definitions.

title: API URL download cap hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
body: FileHelper.download for API-provided URLs now uses a fixed 10.megabytes cap instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. On sites where max_image_size_kb (or max_attachment_size_kb) is configured above 10MB, valid API uploads are now truncated/fail at 10MB with no way to configure it; below 10MB, non-image downloads are no longer bounded by the image setting at all. The cap should be derived from the relevant setting (e.g. [max_image_size_kb, max_attachment_size_kb].max) rather than hardcoded.

title: Downsized image keeps original filename but stored sha/filesize mismatch metadata assumptions
body: After downsizing, the upload is created with the original `filename` and the new (smaller) tempfile.size, but the content no longer matches the file the user chose; more importantly, uploads of type where FileHelper.is_image? matches by extension (e.g. .svg) will run ImageMagick `convert` on an SVG with "80%" geometry, which either rasterizes the SVG (destroying its vector nature) or fails. SVGs should be excluded from the downsize path the same way OptimizedImage.create_for special-cases .svg.

title: Duplicate downsize method definition overrides the width/height variant
body: The file now defines `self.downsize` twice: once as `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) and again as `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149). In Ruby, the second definition completely replaces the first. Any existing caller invoking `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height)` (four positional arguments) will now hit the new signature, where `height` is bound to `opts`; since `height` is an Integer and not a Hash, this raises `TypeError: no implicit conversion into Hash`, or at best silently produces a broken dimensions string. The old width/height variant is dead code that can never run. Either remove it or consolidate into one signature that accepts both.

title: Client-side max upload size hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
body: `validateUploadedFile` previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, respecting the admin-configurable `max_image_size_kb` and `max_attachment_size_kb`. It is now hardcoded to 10MB for both images and attachments. Consequences: (1) on sites where the attachment limit is lower than 10MB, the client will let users pick oversized attachment files and push the whole upload to the server only to be rejected; (2) on sites where the image limit is higher than 10MB, valid uploads are blocked client-side with a wrong error message; (3) it contradicts this PR's own purpose — large images that the server would now automatically downsize are still refused in the browser. Same issue for the hardcoded 10MB in the 413 handler at line 246, which is also shown to users for oversized attachments where the message was previously image-specific.

title: Downsizing loop may exit with image still over the limit, then proceeds anyway
body: The loop runs at most 5 iterations of an 80% resize, which reduces file size by at most ~67% (0.8^5), and only roughly — file size does not scale linearly with linear dimensions. An image that is more than ~3x the configured `max_image_size_kb` will still exceed the limit when the loop exits, yet the code proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with the oversized file, which will then fail with a generic server error instead of either being downsized further or rejected with a clear message. There is no check or handling after the loop for `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`.

title: In-place downsize (from == to) can corrupt the uploaded file, and failures are not detected
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` uses the same path as both input and output. For animated GIFs this dispatches to `gifsicle ... --output <same file>`, and writing the output over the file being read is not a supported/safe operation and can truncate or corrupt the image. Additionally, `downsize` returns false when the `convert`/`gifsicle` invocation fails, but the return value is ignored here; if the external command fails partway through, the (possibly truncated or emptied) temp file is passed straight to `Upload.create_for`, storing a corrupted image. The loop should downsize to a distinct temp path and abort the upload (or fall back to the original) when `downsize` returns false.

title: Synchronous CPU-heavy image resizing runs in the request thread with no size cap on remote URL downloads
body: Two related problems: (1) the API URL-download branch now downloads up to 10MB (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`) instead of the site-configured limit, and the subsequent downsize loop with ImageMagick/ImageOptim runs synchronously inside `create_upload` for `synchronous` API requests — a multi-second CPU-heavy operation blocking a web worker. (2) In the deferred path, the same heavy conversion runs in the Scheduler::Defer thread, but the tempfile was created in the request and is fine, yet the client has already been told `success_json` before the resize happens, so any downsizing failure surfaces only as an opaque MessageBus error. Consider capping the download back to a site setting and validating the downloaded size before attempting the resize.

title: Duplicate downsize definition breaks existing 4-argument callers
body: The class now defines `downsize` twice (lines 145 and 149). In Ruby the second definition silently overrides the first, so the width/height variant is dead code and any existing caller invoking `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height)` now hits the new signature where `dimensions` receives the width integer and `opts` receives the height integer. The dimensions string passed to convert becomes just the width (e.g. "800" instead of "800x600"), producing a malformed ImageMagick resize argument, and opts is a Fixnum so `opts[:allow_animation]` will raise NoMethodError. All existing thumbnail-generation callers of the old API break at runtime.

title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores site settings
body: The client-side upload validation previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` so it matched the server's per-type configured limits. It now hardcodes 10MB for both images and attachments. On sites configured with smaller limits the client will let a file through that the server then rejects, and on sites with larger attachment limits (e.g. max_attachment_size_kb > 10MB) valid uploads are blocked client-side with a wrong error message. This is a functional regression of the configurable limits.

title: 413 error message hardcodes 10MB regardless of server config
body: The 413 handler now reports "10 MB" as the max size instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. When a site has a different max image size configured, the user is shown an incorrect limit in the error dialog, misleading them about what they can upload.

title: API URL download limit raised to hardcoded 10MB bypassing site setting
body: The remote-download size cap for API-provided URLs was `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` and is now a hardcoded 10.megabytes. This applies to all downloads via the API path (including attachments, not just images that will be downsized), so a site that deliberately lowered max_image_size_kb to limit bandwidth/storage exposure now allows API clients to pull up to 10MB per request from arbitrary URLs, defeating the configured limit.

title: Downsize loop can silently fail and oversized image still submitted
body: The loop downsizes to "80%" up to 5 times (max ~33% area reduction) and ignores the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize`. If conversion fails (e.g. ImageMagick error, unsupported format such as SVG or a corrupted image), the loop runs all 5 attempts on an unmodified file and then `Upload.create_for` is called anyway with the still-oversized tempfile. Also, five 20% steps are frequently insufficient for a genuinely large image (e.g. a 40MB photo with a 1MB limit), so the upload will fail with a generic error after the CPU cost of up to 5 image conversions. The downsize result should be checked and a stronger reduction strategy (e.g. scaling toward the target size directly) used.

title: In-place convert on the same path can corrupt or fail on the source tempfile
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` runs `convert from[0] ... to` with from == to. ImageMagick reads the input fully before writing, so this usually works, but for animated GIFs the animated path uses gifsicle reading and writing the same file, and any partial write failure leaves the tempfile in a corrupted/truncated state that is then passed to Upload.create_for, potentially producing a broken stored upload. Writing to a separate temp file and replacing the original would be safe.

title: Downsized file keeps original extension/content_type even when format changes
body: After downsizing, the file is registered via `Upload.create_for(..., filename, ...)` with the original filename and content_type. If ImageMagick's convert writes a different format than the extension suggests (or the animated path produces a different output), the stored upload's extension, content type, and actual bytes can disagree, which can later break thumbnail generation and cause browsers to mis-handle the file.

title: GET /unsubscribe toggles state and crashes when no TopicUser record exists
body: The unsubscribe action performs a state-changing toggle on a plain GET request. Two concrete problems: (1) `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil when the logged-in user has no topic_users row for that topic (e.g. they received the email via a mention/watch category without ever visiting, or the row was cleaned up); `tu.notification_level` on the next line then raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a graceful response. It should use TopicUser.change or handle the nil case. (2) Because the toggle is a side effect of a GET, simply refreshing or re-visiting the emailed link flips the user back and forth between muted and regular, and any third-party page can trigger the state change for a logged-in user via an /link (CSRF via GET). The mutation should be a POST/PUT (or done through the Ember route with an explicit action), not performed on every GET.

title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
body: The unsubscribe action sets notification_level directly on the TopicUser AR object and calls save!, instead of using TopicUser.change. TopicUser.change is the canonical path that also stamps notifications_changed_at, notifications_reason_id, publishes the MessageBus notification_level_change event to the user's open tabs, and handles record creation races. Saving directly leaves notifications_changed_at/reason stale and open clients won't see the level change until reload.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking any email that sets add_unsubscribe_link without it
body: The rewritten `unsubscribe_link` locale string now interpolates both %{user_preferences_url} and %{unsubscribe_url}. Email::MessageBuilder#body and #html_part call I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) whenever @opts[:add_unsubscribe_link] is true, but unsubscribe_url is only supplied by UserNotifications#send_notification_email. Any other builder invocation with add_unsubscribe_link: true and no :unsubscribe_url option (other mailers, plugins, or future call sites — and the old spec case before it was patched in this same PR) will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument (or emit a broken literal `%{unsubscribe_url}` link) when building the email. The per-topic sentence should be a separate locale key used only when the URL is present.

title: No request specs for the unsubscribe controller action or route
body: The PR adds a new authenticated, state-mutating controller action (topics#unsubscribe) plus two new routes, but includes no request/controller specs covering: the redirect when the slug is missing/mismatched, the toggle behavior at each starting notification level, the nil-TopicUser case, access control for topics the user cannot see, and the logged-out redirect. The only test touched is the message_builder spec, so the most fragile new code (the toggling GET) ships untested.

title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser record exists
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately calls `tu.notification_level`. A TopicUser row is only created when a user has viewed/tracked/posted in a topic, but the email unsubscribe link is sent to users who may have received a notification (e.g. via watch category or a mention) without ever having opened the topic. For those users find_by returns nil and `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of muting the topic. The code should use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` which upserts the row.

title: State-changing GET endpoint with no CSRF token or confirmation
body: The unsubscribe action permanently changes the user's notification level (potentially to muted) as a side effect of a plain GET request, with no CSRF token and no confirmation step. Email scanners, link prefetchers (mail clients, antivirus, some browsers) follow links in emails; if the user's browser session is active or the link is fetched through a prefetching proxy that carries cookies, the topic can be muted without the user ever clicking. The rest of the codebase uses keyed, token-protected unsubscribe endpoints (see `email/unsubscribe/:key`); the per-topic link should either be tokened or the GET should only display a page where the change is made via a POST/XHR.

title: Direct AR save bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
body: unsubscribe mutates the TopicUser record directly with `tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!` instead of going through TopicUser.change. As a result `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are never updated (they should be set to user_changed), and no `notification_level_change` MessageBus message is published to `/topic/:id` for that user, so an open tab will keep showing the stale notification level. All other paths that change notification level in the app use TopicUser.change for these reasons.

title: Toggle to 'regular' contradicts the 'stop receiving notifications' message
body: When the user's level is tracking or watching, the action sets it to `regular`, not `muted`. But a regular user still receives notifications for direct replies and mentions. The email text ('To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here') and the client locale ('You will stop receiving notifications for...') promise that notifications stop, yet the user will continue to be emailed on replies. Either the action should always mute, or the copy must say notifications are reduced to direct replies only.

title: unsubscribe_link locale now requires %{unsubscribe_url} for all callers
body: The server locale `unsubscribe_link` was changed to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`, and MessageBuilder renders it whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true (both in html_part and body). Only UserNotifications#send_notification_email passes `unsubscribe_url`. Any other caller (plugins, or future core mailers) that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without supplying `unsubscribe_url` will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when building the email. Either the locale should tolerate a missing URL or the builder should default unsubscribe_url when absent.

title: List-Unsubscribe header not updated to the per-topic URL
body: MessageBuilder#header_args still sets the List-Unsubscribe header to `user_preferences_url` even when a topic-specific `unsubscribe_url` was supplied in the same opts. Mail clients that use the List-Unsubscribe one-click header will therefore send users to global preferences instead of the per-topic unsubscribe page, defeating the feature for those clients.

title: No test that the per-topic unsubscribe URL appears in the email
body: The spec was only updated to pass `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` so the existing assertions keep passing; there is no assertion that this URL actually appears in the body or html_part, and no controller or mailer spec for the new TopicsController#unsubscribe action (nil TopicUser case, redirect on slug mismatch, toggle semantics). The core behavior of this PR is untested.

title: unsubscribe crashes with nil TopicUser when the user has no topic_user record
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately calls `tu.notification_level`. For any logged-in user who never viewed/posted/tracked the topic (e.g. they were watching via a category default or received the email via a group mention), no topic_users row exists, so `tu` is nil and the action raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing the user. It should use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` which creates the record when missing.

title: State-changing GET endpoint can be triggered by email scanners/link prefetchers
body: The unsubscribe link in emails is a plain GET to /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe that immediately mutates the user's notification level (topics_controller.rb line 98-116, route added in config/routes.rb line 440-441). Mail clients and security scanners (antivirus proxies, Gmail link scanning, Apple Mail prefetch) routinely GET links in emails without the user clicking them. Any such scan silently mutes the user's topic, or worse toggles them to regular, without consent. Standard practice (and what the existing /email/unsubscribe/:key flow does) is a token-authenticated link or a confirmation page; this endpoint requires only a logged-in session and a guessable numeric topic id, and it also lets any logged-in user flip their own state via CSRF-free GET from any page (img tag on any site they visit while logged in, since there is no CSRF check on GET).

title: Direct save of TopicUser skips notifications_changed_at, reason, and MessageBus updates
body: The unsubscribe action assigns `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly instead of going through `TopicUser.change`. TopicUser.change is the canonical path: it sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (so the UI shows why the level changed) and publishes a `notification_level_change` MessageBus message to /topic/:id so open tabs update. Saving directly leaves the reason stale (e.g. still 'auto_watch') and other clients' UIs out of sync. Also, an unsubscribe click when the level is 'regular' or below sets it to 'muted', but when it is 'tracking'/'watching' it only drops to 'regular' — a 'regular' user still receives replied-to/mentioned notifications for that topic, so the email's promise 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' (config/locales/server.en.yml) is not kept for those users.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url} for all callers of MessageBuilder
body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` locale string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder#body` (lib/email/message_builder.rb line 90) and `#html_part` (line 67) render this string with `template_args` for any caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`; any other caller (plugins, themes, or future core mailers) that enables `add_unsubscribe_link` without supplying `unsubscribe_url` will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and the email will fail to build. A safer design keeps the per-topic sentence in a separate translation or makes the segment conditional.

title: topicUnsubscribe client route is shadowed by the topic resource's fromParamsNear route
body: The new route `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' })` is registered after `this.resource('topic', { path: '/t/:slug/:id' }, ...)` whose child route `fromParamsNear` has path '/:nearPost' (a wildcard segment). Because the topic resource is declared first, a URL like /t/my-slug/123/unsubscribe can be matched by topic.fromParamsNear with nearPost='unsubscribe', loading the full topic instead of the unsubscribe page. The unsubscribe route needs to be registered before the topic resource (or the nearPost segment constrained to digits) so it takes precedence.

title: No tests for the new unsubscribe controller action or route
body: The PR adds a new mutating endpoint (TopicsController#unsubscribe), new routes, a mailer change, and a locale change, but the only test modification is passing `unsubscribe_url` to an existing MessageBuilder spec. There are no request specs covering: successful unsubscribe, the nil-TopicUser case, the slug redirect branch, or the toggle logic (watching → regular, regular → muted). Given the nil-crash and the mute-vs-regular semantics questions above, these behaviors need test coverage before merging.

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive, allowing trivial bypass
body: BlockedEmail.should_block?(email) queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` with the exact string passed in, but email addresses elsewhere in the app are normalized (e.g. UsersController#change_email uses Email.downcase, and users may sign up with mixed case). A blocked address stored as 'bad@spam.com' will not match a signup using 'Bad@Spam.com', so the block list can be bypassed simply by varying case. The lookup (and the unique index/uniqueness validation) should compare downcased emails.

title: should_block? performs a DB write inside model validation
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? is invoked from EmailValidator.validate_each, i.e. from within ActiveRecord validation of a User. It increments match_count and calls record.save on the BlockedEmail row as a side effect of validating another model. This means every failed signup attempt (including repeated retries of the same form) triggers a write, the increment is a read-modify-write race under concurrency (lost updates on match_count/last_match_at), and if the BlockedEmail save fails (e.g. stale record) the method silently continues. Statistics tracking should be done outside the validation path, or via an atomic UPDATE (update_counters / SQL increment).

title: Blocked-email check applied to existing users changing email, with no admin path to manage block list
body: The email:true validation runs whenever email_changed? on any User, so an existing (possibly long-standing) member whose address appears in the blocked_emails table can no longer save any change that touches email, and their email changes are rejected with a generic 'is not allowed' message. There is also no admin interface, seed, or API anywhere in this PR that ever creates BlockedEmail records, so the block list cannot be populated and the feature (and its match_count statistics) is effectively dead code as shipped.

title: rejectedEmails comparison is case-sensitive against server-echoed value
body: On a failed signup, the email echoed back in result.values.email is pushed into rejectedEmails, and emailValidation checks `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` with an exact string comparison. If the user retypes the same address with different casing or surrounding whitespace, the client-side rejection is skipped and the form is resubmitted to the server, which rejects it again — the user gets no inline feedback explaining the email is blocked. Normalizing both sides (trim/lowercase) before comparing would make the client check reliable.

title: Blocked email is reported to user as 'invalid'
body: When a signup fails because the email is on the server's block list, the client shows I18n.t('user.email.invalid'), i.e. a malformed-address message, rather than a message explaining the address is not permitted (the server has user.email.blocked for this). The user is told their syntactically valid email is invalid, which is confusing and wrong.

title: Failed-signup response echoes submitted name/username/email back to the client
body: The create failure path now returns `values: user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")` to any anonymous requester. Combined with the CSRF skip on create (`skip_before_filter :verify_authenticity_token, only: [:create]`), this endpoint can be probed without a valid token and used as an oracle to enumerate which emails are blocked/blacklisted or already registered, and reflects attacker-controlled input back. Consider not echoing the submitted values (the client already knows what it submitted).

title: Blocked email lookup is case/format sensitive and easily bypassed
body: BlockedEmail.should_block?(email) does a plain `where(email: email)` match with no normalization (no downcasing, no stripping). Users can trivially bypass the block by registering with different casing (e.g. 'Bad@SpamClub.com' vs a stored 'bad@spamclub.com') or surrounding whitespace.
