The User model stores emails without downcasing (only some flows use Email.downcase), so a blocked address will still validate successfully whenever the submitted string isn't byte-identical to the stored one. The lookup and the stored records should be normalized (downcase/strip, ideally at both write time in a before_validation on BlockedEmail and at lookup time).

title: Validation has write side effects: should_block? saves records during model validation
body: EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which increments match_count and saves the record. This means every User validation run (including intermediate validations, invalid attempts, or any other code path that calls user.valid?) performs a database write. Consequences: side effects from a read-only operation, writes inside validation callbacks, and skewed match_count statistics from repeated failed signup attempts. The statistic update should be decoupled from the predicate (e.g. done only on actual signup attempts in the controller, or via an atomic UPDATE).

title: match_count increment is a read-modify-write race
body: should_block? increments match_count in Ruby (`record.match_count += 1`) and saves the full record. Under concurrent signup attempts for the same email, increments can be lost, and full-record saves can also overwrite other columns with stale values. Use an atomic counter update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])`.

title: Blocked-email check only runs when email_changed?, skipping existing users
body: The `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` guard means the BlockedEmail check is skipped for any record whose email attribute was not changed (e.g. a previously-created user whose email was later added to the block list, or records loaded and re-saved). If the intent is only to gate signups this is fine, but the BlockedEmail feature then provides no protection on any path where an existing/loaded user is validated or saved (e.g. password_reset saves the user with the same email). Confirm the guard matches the intended scope of the blocklist.

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and can be bypassed
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does an exact, case-sensitive match: BlockedEmail.where(email: email). An attacker (or ordinary user) whose address is on the block list can register as "Bad@SpamClub.com" when the list contains "bad@spamclub.com" and the check will not match. The lookup should compare normalized (downcased/stripped) emails, e.g. where(email: Email.downcase(email)).

title: should_block? performs writes (match_count increment) inside model validation
body: EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block? during User validation, and should_block? increments match_count and saves the record. In UsersController#create the user is validated via user.valid? (line 168) and then validated again by user.save, so each blocked signup attempt increments match_count twice and issues two UPDATE statements. Validations should be side-effect free; the statistics update should be moved out of the validation path (e.g. into the controller after a failed save) to avoid inflated counts, unnecessary writes, and unexpected behavior when a model is validated for other reasons.

title: match_count increment is not atomic
body: should_block? does record.match_count += 1 followed by record.save. Under concurrent requests two processes can read the same count and both write count+1, losing increments. Use BlockedEmail.where(email: email).update_all(["match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?", Time.zone.now]) or an atomic counter update.

title: change_email endpoint is not covered by the blocked-email check
body: The new EmailValidator (with the BlockedEmail check) only runs when email_changed? on a User record, but UsersController#change_email never assigns the new email to the user — it directly creates an email_token with the new address and sends the confirmation mail. A user can therefore sign up with an unblocked address and then switch to a blocked address via change_email, completely bypassing the blocked-email feature. The controller should also call BlockedEmail.should_block?(lower_email) (and the whitelist/blacklist check) before creating the token.

title: Blocked check silently skipped when a domain-restriction error was already added
body: The blocked-email check only runs if record.errors[attribute].blank?. If the email fails the whitelist/blacklist check, should_block? is never called, so match_count/last_match_at statistics for that blocked email are not recorded. This makes the analytics fields unreliable and the ordering dependency between the two checks is fragile (a future error added earlier would silently disable the block check). The block check should run independently of prior errors.

title: RSS feed content is stored and rendered as raw HTML without sanitization
body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method: raw_html, which makes Post#cook return raw unchanged (app/models/post.rb line 133). When called from the PollFeed path (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 35-36), `contents` is the raw feed item content with only CGI.unescapeHTML applied — no HTML sanitization occurs. The embed view (app/views/embed/best.html.erb line 19) then renders these posts with `raw post.cooked`. Any <script>, inline event handlers, or other malicious markup in the external feed is stored verbatim and executed in the Discourse origin for every visitor of the embedded page, allowing a compromised or malicious feed to hijack Discourse sessions/perform CSRF. The import_remote path limits tags/attributes via readability, but the feed path has no such filtering; contents should be sanitized (e.g. via Sanitize/Nokogiri whitelist) before being stored as raw_html.

title: Referer header injected unescaped into inline JavaScript
body: The layout embeds `'<%= request.referer %>'` directly inside a <script> block. The referer is an attacker-controlled HTTP header; ensure_embeddable only checks that URI(referer).host equals the configured embeddable_host, so a referer such as `http://<embeddable_host>/';alert(1);//` passes the host check and breaks out of the JS string literal (and `</script>` sequences break out of the script tag entirely), executing arbitrary script in the Discourse iframe origin. The value must be JSON/JS-escaped (e.g. `json_escape`/to_json) and ideally validated as a full origin before interpolation.

title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without content
body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls methods on i.content without checking presence. Many RSS feeds provide only a description/summary and no content element (simple-rss returns nil for missing tags), so the scheduled job will raise NoMethodError on nil. With `sidekiq_options retry: false` the exception is swallowed and, more importantly, it aborts processing of the remaining feed items in the same run, so topics after the offending item are never imported until the next hour. Guard with `i.content || i.description` or a nil check.

title: feed_key is dead code; no conditional-fetch deduplication is implemented
body: The `feed_key` method (used nowhere) and its 'feed-modified:' redis key suggest the intent was to skip polling when the feed has not changed (e.g. via Last-Modified/ETag), but poll_feed unconditionally re-opens the feed URL and re-processes every item every hour. Every existing embed's content is re-fetched/recomputed and each unchanged item still goes through a TopicEmbed lookup and SHA1 comparison; if content SHA matches it is skipped only after the DB read. Either remove the dead method or wire it up to store/compare the feed's modified time so polling is skipped when unchanged.

title: Weak origin check on postMessage via substring match
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any message whose origin appears anywhere in discourseUrl. E.g. with discourseUrl 'http://meta.discourse.org', a sender at 'http://meta.discourse.org.evil.com' passes the check (its origin string contains the discourseUrl as a substring) and can drive iframe.height with arbitrary values. The check should compare the parsed origin of discourseUrl to e.origin with strict equality.

title: setnx followed by separate expire is not atomic
body: retrieved_recently? uses $redis.setnx and then a separate $redis.expire. If the process dies (or redis restarts) between the two calls, the key 'retrieved:<url>' exists with no TTL and permanently blocks retrieval for that embed URL until manual redis intervention. Use a single SET key value EX 60 NX (or setex-style) operation so the TTL is set atomically with the key creation.

title: Update path crashes if the embedded post has been deleted
body: On re-import of an existing embed, `post = embed.post` is used without a nil check before `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `embed.update_column`. If the topic's post was deleted (or post_id points to a removed record — the association has no dependent handling and nothing destroys the TopicEmbed when its post is destroyed), the poll job will raise NoMethodError on nil every run for that URL. Guard for a missing post (and consider destroying the TopicEmbed alongside the post).

title: RSS-imported HTML is stored and served with no sanitization (raw_html cook method)
body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], and Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim for that method, bypassing Discourse's entire markdown/sanitization pipeline. Any script/iframe/event-handler markup present in the RSS feed content (or in a page fetched by TopicRetriever/import_remote from the embeddable host) is stored as-is in `cooked` and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb line 19, and also on the main forum topic page. A compromised or malicious feed/embeddable site therefore gets stored XSS on the Discourse instance. The imported content must be sanitized (e.g. via Sanitize/Nokogiri whitelist) before storing.

title: Unescaped URL interpolated into HTML in imported_from footer
body:
`contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "` interpolates the raw feed item URL into an href attribute and link text with no HTML/attribute escaping. A feed entry whose link contains a single quote or angle brackets (e.g. `x' onclick='...`) injects arbitrary markup into the post body, which — combined with the raw_html cook path — is stored and served unsanitized. The URL must be escaped before being embedded in the HTML string.

title: Weak origin check uses substring match on discourseUrl
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any origin that appears anywhere in the discourseUrl string. An attacker page at e.g. `http://evil.com/https://forum.example.com` or an origin like `http://forum.example.com.attacker.com` (which contains the forum origin as a substring) passes the check, and the handler then writes an attacker-controlled `e.data.height` into the iframe height. The check must compare parsed origins for equality, not substring containment.

title: request.referer interpolated raw into inline JavaScript
body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` interpolates the Referer header into a single-quoted JS string with no JS-string escaping. ERB's HTML escaping does not neutralize single quotes or backslashes inside a <script> block (entities are not decoded there), so a Referer such as `http://embeddable-host/'};alert(1);//` breaks out of the string and executes arbitrary script in the embed frame. Use a fixed targetOrigin (the Discourse base URL) or json_escape/j() the value.

title: Feed polling has no error handling and retry disabled, so failures are silently swallowed
body: Jobs::PollFeed sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` and `poll_feed` calls `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `TopicEmbed.import` for each item with no rescue. If the feed URL is temporarily down, returns malformed XML, or any item raises (e.g. `i.content` nil causing NoMethodError, or an invalid link), the exception propagates and the job dies without retry or notification; hourly polling then effectively stops working with no visibility. Exceptions should be caught/logged, and the whole job should not abort on a single bad item.

title: Entire feed re-imported every hour; feed_key/dedup key defined but never used
body: The `feed_key` method builds a redis key for the feed's last-modified state but is never called anywhere. Every hour the job iterates all feed items and runs TopicEmbed.import for each one, performing SHA1 comparisons and (when content changed) full post revisions for every historical item, forever. Feeds commonly keep hundreds of items, so this grows unboundedly. Use the feed's ETag/Last-Modified (the feed_key) or skip items whose URL was already imported.

title: force: true added to an already-released migration will drop existing tables
body: This PR modifies the previously shipped CreateTopTopics migration to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which drops any existing top_topics table before recreating it. On any deployed database where this migration is re-run (db:migrate:redo, restore-from-schema edge cases, or multi-site setups that replay migrations), all accumulated top_topics data is silently destroyed. `force: true` is only appropriate for development scratch tables, never for migrations against production data (same concern applies to the new create_topic_embeds migration, though that table is new).

title: Import crashes if the embedded post was deleted
body: In the update branch, `post = embed.post` may be nil if the topic's first post was deleted (the topic_embeds row is not cleaned up when posts are destroyed). The subsequent `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!` then raises NoMethodError, which in the poll feed job aborts processing of the entire feed. It should check `embed.post.blank?` and re-create or skip instead.

title: import mutates the caller's contents string
body: `contents << "..."` uses String#<< on the argument passed by the caller, permanently appending the 'Imported from' footer to the caller's string. In the poll feed loop this mutates local variables held by SimpleRSS items; if a caller reuses the string (e.g. logs it or compares it), it sees unexpected modifications. Use `contents = contents + ...` instead.

title: Loading view reloads the iframe forever even when retrieval fails
body: The loading page unconditionally reloads every 30 seconds. If the RetrieveTopic job failed (invalid embeddable host, fetch error, embed_by_username unset so TopicRetriever#fetch_http returns early), no TopicEmbed is ever created, and every visitor of the embedding page triggers an endless reload loop plus a new enqueued job per minute per visitor, generating continuous load on both the embedding site and the Discourse instance. The reload should be limited to a few attempts.

title: Job requires irrelevant dependency 'email/sender'
body: The RetrieveTopic job begins with `require_dependency 'email/sender'` although it has nothing to do with email; this appears to be copy-paste residue and loads unrelated mailer code in every sidekiq worker process running this job. It should require only 'topic_retriever'.

title: Stored XSS: embed URL interpolated unescaped into raw HTML post
body: TopicEmbed.import builds the post body with `contents << "...#{url}..."` without any HTML escaping, and the resulting post is stored with cook_method raw_html (Post#cook returns raw verbatim, bypassing the markdown/sanitization pipeline). The `url` here is the user-supplied `embed_url` request parameter (only checked with a /^https?:\/\// regex), so a URL containing a single quote and a `, is injected into the post body and rendered unsanitized. The embed view renders it with `raw post.cooked`, so any visitor of the embedded page is exposed to stored XSS. The URL must be escaped (CGI.escapeHTML / ERB::Util.html_escape) and ideally validated with URI.parse.

title: request.referer interpolated unescaped into inline JavaScript
body: The layout embeds `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`. The controller only validates that the referer's *host* equals embeddable_host; the path/query of the referring URL is attacker-influenced (any page on the embeddable host, or a crafted referer with quotes). A referer containing a single quote or `</script>` breaks out of the JS string literal, allowing script injection into the embed iframe's DOM. Use `escape_javascript`/json encoding for the value instead of raw ERB interpolation.

title: create_table with force: true will silently drop an existing table
body: The migration uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which issues DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating. If this migration runs against a database that already has topic_embeds data (e.g. it was created outside migrations, or a partial deploy happened), all rows are silently destroyed. The same problem is introduced in this PR by changing db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb to `force: true`, which can drop production top_topics data on environments where the table already exists. `force: true` should only ever be used in development/test schemas, never in shipped migrations.

title: poll_feed crashes when a feed item has no content element
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every RSS/Atom item has a `content` element. SimpleRSS returns nil for missing elements, so any feed item that only provides `description` (or an Atom feed without content) raises NoMethodError on nil. Since the job has `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the whole hourly poll is aborted at the first such item and no further items are imported. Guard with `i.content || i.description` and handle nil.

title: Import crashes if the existing embed's post has been deleted
body: In the update branch, `post = embed.post` may be nil (topic/post deleted by moderators, which is common for spam), and the next line calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` on nil, raising NoMethodError. PollFeed runs hourly and TopicRetriever calls it inline, so a single deleted post for a feed URL permanently breaks feed polling for all items after it (retry disabled). Handle a nil post by recreating the topic or skipping.

title: No error handling around feed fetch; network error kills scheduled job with retry disabled
body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` can raise OpenURI::HTTPError, SocketError, timeouts, or RSS parse errors. With `sidekiq_options retry: false`, any transient network failure silently aborts the poll until the next hour with no logging. Wrap the fetch/parse in begin/rescue with logging so transient errors don't go unnoticed.

title: Anonymous requests can trigger unauthenticated enqueues of retrieval jobs
body: Any request passing the referer check (which only checks the host header of the referer, trivially spoofable via server-side fetch or a page on the host) with arbitrary embed_url values enqueues a RetrieveTopic job per unique URL. Although TopicRetriever throttles per-URL to once per 60s, an attacker can rotate unlimited distinct embed_url values (all on the embeddable host), each spawning a job that performs an outbound HTTP fetch (or a full PollFeed run) — a job-queue and outbound-traffic amplification vector with no global rate limit.

title: import_remote does not restrict scheme, enabling file:// reads
body: TopicEmbed.import checks `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, but import_remote calls `open(url)` *before* that check, and Ruby's open-uri follows `file://` (and other schemes via redirects). The embed_url comes from the public controller via the RetrieveTopic job. Although TopicRetriever.invalid_host? compares hosts first, a URL like `file:///etc/passwd` has host nil != embeddable_host and is rejected there; however any code path calling import_remote directly (e.g. the disqus thor task with feed data) passes the URL straight to open(). Use an explicit http(s) check before open(), not just inside import.

title: Weak origin check on postMessage handler
body: The receiver validates messages with `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, an unanchored substring test. Any string merely *containing* the discourse origin passes (e.g. an origin like `http://discourse.example.com.attacker.tld` if the forum URL is a substring of it), and the check compares the full URL string against only the origin scheme+host. Use `e.origin === new URL(discourseUrl).origin` for an exact comparison. Impact is limited (message only sets iframe height), but it should be an exact check.

title: feed_key is defined but never used, so polling has no modified/etag check
body: The job defines `feed_key` (apparently intended for caching feed modified state) but never reads or writes it, and poll_feed re-imports every item on every hourly run, re-fetching and re-parsing each item's page via TopicEmbed.import (dedup is by embed_url, so content changes are re-imported even when the feed hasn't changed). Either wire the key into the polling logic or remove it; as-is it is dead code and the comment-implied caching behavior does not exist.

title: float: right on .small-action button is a no-op now that the parent is a flex container
body: `.small-action` was changed to `@include flexbox()`, but the `button { float: right; }` rule inside it was kept. Floats are ignored on flex items, so the button (e.g. the 'change owner' / moderation button rendered in small actions) will no longer be pushed to the right edge; it will sit inline after the description as an ordinary flex item. The rule should be replaced with a flex-based right alignment (e.g. `margin-left: auto` on the button), otherwise the small-action button placement regresses visually on topic pages.

title: Header right panel loses its right alignment on browsers using the legacy flexbox syntax
body: The old `float: right` on `.d-header .panel` was replaced with `margin-left: auto`. `margin-left: auto` for end-alignment only works in the modern flexbox model; the 2009 box model that the `flexbox()` mixin also emits (`display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box`) does not honor auto margins — there you need `-webkit-box-pack: end` on the container. On any browser that only supports the old syntax (older Android/Safari that the prefixes were presumably added for), the login/sign-up panel will sit immediately after the title instead of being right-aligned, and since the floats were removed there is no fallback. Either add the box-pack fallback or keep a float-based fallback.

title: Removal of .title float leaves no layout for browsers without flexbox support
body: The diff deletes the `.d-header .contents .title { float: left; }` rule and replaces the layout entirely with the flexbox mixins on `.contents`. Browsers that support none of the five `display` variants emitted by `flexbox()` will fall back to block layout, where the title, extra-info and panel will each stack on their own line instead of laying out horizontally. If those browsers matter, a float fallback should be retained; otherwise the extra prefixed values serve no purpose.

title: order() mixin mixes 2009 and 2012 spec syntaxes that don't work together
body: The `order($val)` mixin emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` (2009 spec, integer-only, works only alongside `display: -webkit-box`) together with `-ms-flex-order`/`order`. In the corresponding layout files, `flexbox()` is applied to one element and `order(2)`/`order(3)` to different elements (.extra-info-wrapper, .panel), so within any single legacy engine only one of the pair of declarations applies and the reordering silently does nothing; also the 2009 engines require the group values to start at 1 (order 0 default vs. 2/3 here is fine, but the emitted 2009 declarations have no matching old-spec box on the sibling items). Practically this means visual order of the header contents differs between legacy and modern browsers; if legacy engines are not targeted, the 2009-era prefixes should be dropped from these mixins to avoid a false sense of compatibility.

title: float: right on button is ignored now that .small-action is a flex container
body: .small-action was changed to `@include flexbox()`, but its direct child `button { float: right; }` (line ~306-309) still relies on floating. Floats have no effect on flex items, so the button (e.g. the 'delete' action on small-actions) will no longer be pushed to the right edge; it will sit immediately after the description text. It should be replaced with `margin-left: auto` inside the flex container. The `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` and `.small-action-desc .avatar` similarly no longer does anything.

title: -ms-align-items is not a real property
body: The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. There is no such CSS property; the Microsoft pre-flexbox property is `-ms-flex-align` (already emitted on the previous line). This dead declaration just bloats the compiled stylesheet on every use of the mixin and suggests the vendor prefix list was copied without verification. It should be removed.

title: .valign-helper vertical centering hack breaks inside the new flex container
body: `.d-header .contents` is now a flex container (`@include flexbox()` + `align-items(center)`), but the legacy `.valign-helper { display: inline-block; height: 100%; vertical-align: middle; }` (lines 21-25) remains. In a flex container `vertical-align` is ignored and `height: 100%` resolves against the container's content-box height, so the helper no longer vertically centers its siblings the way it did in the old inline/float layout. Any markup still relying on valign-helper (e.g. in plugins or older header markup) will render misaligned. The rule should be removed or converted to flex-based centering.

title: order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper only works when its parent is the flex header
body: `.extra-info-wrapper` now uses `@include order(2)` with no accompanying display change, so `order` only has an effect when the element happens to be a direct child of a flex container (the header `.contents`). Everywhere else `.extra-info-wrapper` appears (it is also used outside the header, e.g. above the topic list in category pages) the declaration is inert. If reordering is only intended in the header, it should be scoped as `.d-header & { @include order(2); }` to make the intent explicit; otherwise the non-header usages silently keep their DOM order and any layout change there is unintended.

title: Invalid -ms-align-items property in align-items mixin
body: The align-items() mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. There is no such CSS property in any IE version (IE10/11 use the standard `align-items` for modern layout, and `-ms-flex-align` for the old syntax, both of which are already emitted). This line is dead code that will be discarded by the CSS parser; it suggests a misunderstanding of the vendor prefix matrix and could mislead future maintainers into relying on it. It should be removed.

title: float rules on children of new flex container are inert
body: `.small-action` is now a flex container (via `@include flexbox()`), which makes `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` (line 270) and `button { float: right; }` (line 309) no-ops: per the flexbox spec, `float` is ignored on flex items. The layout now depends entirely on flex defaults (row, no wrapping, flex-start alignment), so the avatar will sit next to the description and the button will follow it — a visual change that may or may not be intended. Either the float declarations should be deleted as dead code, or explicit flex ordering/alignment (e.g. `margin-left: auto` on the button) should be added so the button is still pushed to the right edge; currently nothing in the diff guarantees the right-aligned button placement the old float provided.

title: clear: both has no effect on a flex container
body: `.small-action` ends with `clear: both;`. With the element now converted to a flex container, `clear` still applies to the container itself as a block-level box, but since the container no longer has floated children (floats on flex items are ignored), the rule serves no purpose and, more importantly, the old clearfix-style guarantee that the small-action box contains its content is now handled differently. If the rule was meant to clear sibling floats (e.g. floated post streams above), it still works, but the comment-free combination of `clear: both` with floats and flexbox on the same element is contradictory and should be cleaned up to make the intended layout mechanism explicit.

title: Header .title float removed but no flex sizing added; old-webkit-box fallback drops align-items
body: `.d-header .contents` is now a flex container, and the `.title { float: left; }` rule was deleted. Two concerns: (1) In browsers that pick up the old `-webkit-box` display (older iOS Safari), the `align-items(center)` from the mixin will not apply because `-webkit-box` uses `-webkit-box-align` — that is emitted, but `center` is valid there so alignment is fine; however the `order(3)` on `.panel` is emitted as `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 3`, which old WebKit honors, so ordering is fine — but `margin-left: auto` (the new right-pushing mechanism for `.panel`) is NOT supported as a flex-item auto-margin in the old -webkit-box model, so the panel will not be pushed to the right in those legacy browsers and the login/buttons will sit immediately next to the logo. (2) The old `float: left` on `.title` was the only thing constraining the title block; with flex and no explicit flex-grow, layout is unchanged for modern browsers, but the mixin emits five `display` values, meaning different browsers get different box models while only the modern properties (auto margins) are guaranteed to work in one of them. The legacy `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box`/`-ms-flexbox` fallbacks should either be dropped (Discourse does not target Firefox 21/IE10) or the layout must not depend on auto margins.

title: order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper only works if it is a direct flex child
body: `@include order(2)` was added to `.extra-info-wrapper`. The `order` property only affects flex items, i.e. direct children of a flex container. This works only if `.extra-info-wrapper` is a direct child of `.d-header .contents`. The PR also removed the `margin-top: 5px` compensation for `.badge-wrapper.bullet` inside it while adding `line-height: 1.5` — if `.extra-info-wrapper` is not a direct flex child (or on pages where the header title area renders differently, e.g. topic pages vs. category pages), the `order` is silently ignored and the vertical spacing fix that was removed will not be replaced by flex centering, causing the category bullet badge to sit misaligned. Verify the element hierarchy across all header variants.

title: website_name is not registered as an untrusted attribute, leaking hidden TL0 profile data
body: The serializer defines `untrusted_attributes` to hide `website` (and bio, location, etc.) for TL0 users viewed anonymously, but the new `website_name` attribute was only added to the plain `attributes` list. As a result, when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true, the JSON omits `website` but still includes `website_name`, which now (when the website domain matches the instance domain) contains the full URL path. This leaks exactly the information the untrusted-attribute restriction is meant to hide, and it bypasses the existing spec at spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11-15 which only checks the enumerated attribute list. `website_name` should be added to `untrusted_attributes` (and a test added).

title: website_name drops query string and fragment from the URL
body: When the website domain matches the instance domain, `website_name` is built as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`, discarding the query string and fragment. A profile website like `http://example.com/page?id=42` would be displayed as `example.com/page`, so the shown 'complete URL path' is wrong/incomplete for URLs with query parameters. Use `URI(website.to_s).request_uri` or `[path, query].compact.join('?')` instead.

title: Domain-matching logic misses websites on subdomains of the instance domain
body: The elsif branch only compares hosts when the label counts are equal and greater than 2, and the else branch only matches when the instance hostname ends with `.#{website_host}` (i.e. the website is a parent of the instance). A website on a subdomain of the instance domain, e.g. website `http://sub.forums.example.com/page` on instance `forums.example.com`, falls through to the else branch where the ends_with check fails, so only the bare host is shown even though it is under the same registrable domain and the PR's intent ('same domain') would suggest showing the full path. The three-way string-split comparison is also ad hoc: `a.b.example.com` vs `x.y.example.com` matches (showing full path) while `sub.forums.example.com` vs `forums.example.com` does not, which is inconsistent.

title: Scheme-less website URLs yield nil website_name while include_website_name stays true
body: `URI(website.to_s).host` is nil for values like `example.com/user` (no scheme), so `website_name` returns nil, yet `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?` and therefore still emits a `website_name: null` key. The old client-side `website.split("/")[2]` was equally limited, but if the profile website field accepts scheme-less input on any code path, the profile will render no website label at all where it previously showed the raw string in the link/title. Consider normalizing with a scheme before parsing and guarding inclusion on the computed value.

title: website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, leaking hidden website data of TL0 users to anonymous visitors
body: The serializer hides `website` (and other untrusted attributes) for TL0 users viewed anonymously via `untrusted_attributes :website, ...` (line 109), so that anonymous users cannot see a TL0 user's profile website. However the newly added `website_name` attribute (line 43) is not added to that list, and its `include_website_name` predicate only checks `website.present?`. As a result, for a TL0 user viewed anonymously, the JSON payload will omit `website` but still include `website_name`, which contains the host and full path of that website — effectively bypassing the privacy restriction and leaking exactly the information the untrusted_attributes mechanism is meant to hide. Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing question mark, so AMS never uses it as an inclusion predicate
body: ActiveModel::Serializers determines inclusion by calling `include_#{attribute}?` (with a question mark). The method here is defined as `include_website_name` (line 153) without the `?`, so it is never invoked by the serializer framework. The consequence is that `website_name` is serialized unconditionally: for users with no website the payload will contain a `website_name: null` key (inconsistent with other optional attributes like `website_name` being expected to be absent), and any future conditional logic placed in this method will silently not run. Rename to `include_website_name?`.

title: website_name drops query string and fragment from the website URL
body: When the website domain matches the instance domain, `website_name` is built as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`, which discards the query string and fragment. A user whose website is `https://example.com/page?id=42` would see the profile display `example.com/page`, which is not the complete URL path the PR intends to show and could mislead users about where the link points. Include `URI(...).query` and `fragment` when present.

title: No test that website_name is hidden for TL0 users seen anonymously
body: The existing 'with a TL0 user seen as anonymous' context asserts that all untrusted attributes (including `website`) are not serialized, but the new `website_name` attribute is not added to that assertion list. Combined with the fact that `website_name` was not added to `untrusted_attributes` in the serializer, this test gap allowed a privacy regression to slip through. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` in the spec (and set a website on the fabricated user profile so the leak would be caught).

title: include_website_name is missing the '?' suffix so the guard is never invoked
body: ActiveModel::Serializers decides whether to include an attribute by calling `include_#{attribute}?` (with a trailing question mark). The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no `?`), so it is never called by the serializer framework. The intended check — only serialize website_name when the website is present — does not run, and website_name is serialized unconditionally (yielding a null key when no website is set, unlike every other guarded attribute in this serializer). Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

title: website_name is not registered as an untrusted attribute, leaking TL0 profile data
body: `website`, `location`, `bio_raw`, etc. are listed in `untrusted_attributes` so they are hidden when a TL0 user is viewed by anonymous visitors (scope.restrict_user_fields?). The new `website_name` attribute is derived directly from `website` but was not added to that list, so the domain/path of a TL0 user's website is serialized to anonymous users even though `website` itself is suppressed. This defeats the existing privacy control. The spec's `untrusted_attributes` list (spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb line 11) also wasn't updated, so the 'doesn't serialize untrusted attributes' test does not cover the new leak.

title: website_name drops query strings and uses bare rescue on URI parsing
body: When the domains match, the returned website_name is `host + URI(website).path`, discarding any query string or fragment from the user's URL (e.g. `example.com/page?id=3` becomes `example.com/page`). The PR description says 'show complete URL path', so this silently truncates URLs. Additionally, `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` swallows all exceptions from malformed URLs; while this returns nil for blanks, a blanket rescue hides unexpected errors — an explicit presence/parse check would be safer.

title: Lightness value changed from 30% to 70% during dark-light-choose conversion
body: In .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the conversion changed it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The light-theme branch's lightness was silently changed from 30% to 70%, making embedded-post usernames much lighter than before on light themes. The light argument should have stayed 30%.

title: Custom-message-length light-theme color changed from 70% to 30% lightness
body: The rule for .custom-message-length was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme value changed from 70% to 30% lightness (darker text), and the dark-theme value uses 70% where the equivalent desktop rule (desktop/modal.scss) uses 30% for the dark branch. This is inconsistent with both the original color and the desktop counterpart, so the mobile flag-modal character counter will render with noticeably different contrast than before and than desktop.

title: Group-member name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: The .group-member-info .name rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme branch changed from 30% to 50% lightness, altering the existing light-theme appearance instead of just adding a dark-theme fallback. The same unintended change is repeated in app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss (.group-member-info .name, 30% → 50%).

title: Topic-map h3 color lightness changed from 20% to 50%
body: The .topic-map h3 rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 20% to 50% lightness, making the mobile topic-map heading significantly lighter than before on light themes, while the desktop topic-map h3 (desktop/topic-post.scss) keeps its 20%/80% pair. The first argument should have remained 20%.

title: Light-theme lightness value changed from 30% to 70% in embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The PR changes it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, i.e. the light-theme branch was changed from 30% to 70% lightness. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original light-mode value and only adds the dark-theme variant (expected: 30% / 70%). This makes the username link in expanded/embedded posts much lighter than before on light color schemes, reducing contrast and breaking visual consistency with the equivalent common/base/topic-post.scss rule (30%/70%).

title: .custom-message-length lightness values inverted relative to original and desktop
body: The mobile `.custom-message-length` rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme value was changed from 70% to 30%, and the dark value is 70% — the opposite of the pattern used everywhere else in this PR (including desktop/modal.scss, which uses 70%/30% for the same `.custom-message-length` selector). On light color schemes this makes the flag character-count hint far darker than before, and it will now diverge between mobile and desktop.

title: Topic map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50% on mobile
body: The mobile `.topic-map h3` rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. All other 20%→converted rules in this PR use 20%/80% (see the adjacent `.map .number, i` rule in the same file, and desktop/topic-post.scss h3 which uses 20%/80%). The light-theme branch was silently changed from 20% to 50%, making the topic map heading noticeably lighter on mobile light themes and inconsistent with desktop.

title: group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: In `.user-stream .group-member-info .name`, the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 30% to 50%, which does not match the analogous rule in common/base/user.scss (`.username a` uses 30%/70%) or the dark value that should mirror it (70%). Member names in the group member list will be lighter/lower-contrast than before on light themes.

title: Mobile group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: Same issue as the desktop counterpart: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme value from 30% to 50%. The consistent conversion (30%/70%) is used elsewhere (e.g. common/base/user.scss). This silently lightens member names in the mobile group member list on light color schemes.

title: Embedded-post username link lightness changed from 30% to 70% in light themes
body: In the .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a rule, the original value was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), but the replacement uses dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The dark-theme branch (30%) follows the 70/30 inversion convention, but the light-theme value was silently changed from 30% to 70%, making usernames in reply expansions much lighter than before on light themes. The light value should stay 30%.

title: group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: The .user-stream .group-member-info .name rule changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). Per the convention used throughout this PR (light/dark values summing to 100%), the light-theme value should have remained 30% with a 70% dark counterpart, not been changed to 50%. Group member names become visibly lighter on light themes.

title: Mobile group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: Same as the desktop counterpart: .user-stream .group-member-info .name changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to a 50%/50% dark-light-choose pair. The light-theme value was unintentionally altered from 30% to 50%, deviating from the 70/30 inversion pattern applied to the adjacent .title rule (kept at 50% correctly). Group member names on mobile light themes lose their intended emphasis.

title: custom-message-length light-theme lightness inverted (70% -> 30%)
body: The .custom-message-length rule changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). The desktop version of the same rule (desktop/modal.scss) was converted to 70%/30%, preserving the original light-theme 70% value. The mobile conversion inverts the values, so the character-counter hint text becomes much darker on light themes and inconsistent with desktop.

title: Topic map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50%
body: In .topic-map h3, the original scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) was replaced with dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). The equivalent desktop rule (desktop/topic-post.scss .topic-map h3) was correctly converted to 20%/80%. The mobile change silently alters the light-theme value from 20% to 50%, making the topic map heading noticeably lighter than before and inconsistent with desktop.

title: Member add/remove routes are declared at collection scope, so the URLs the client calls don't exist
body: The `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` lines are placed directly inside the `resources :groups` block (not inside a `member do ... end` block), so they generate the collection routes `/admin/groups/members` with no `:id` segment. However, the frontend calls `/admin/groups/<group_id>/members.json` (see `Discourse.Group#addMembers`/`#removeMember` in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js), and the controller actions do `params.require(:group_id)`. Those requests will 404 (no route matches `/admin/groups/1/members`), making both adding and removing group members from the admin UI completely non-functional. The routes need to be wrapped in `member do ... end` (or declared as `put "/groups/:id/members"`).

title: Automatic-group removal test uses the wrong HTTP verb (PUT instead of DELETE)
body: The test "cannot remove members from automatic groups" issues `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but the route for remove_member is a DELETE (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`). Once the route is correctly scoped as a member route, this test will fail with a routing error (or hit nothing) instead of asserting the 422 automatic-group behavior. It should be `xhr :delete, :remove_member, ...` to match the other remove_member test and the actual route verb.

title: `automatic` is not in scope in the member item view, so remove links are shown for automatic groups
body: The group_member template uses `{{#unless automatic}}` to hide the remove link, but this template is rendered in the context of the `group-member` item view whose content is the individual member (a Discourse.User), not the group. `automatic` is not a property of a user, so it evaluates as falsy and the remove link is rendered for every member — including members of automatic groups. Clicking it fires `removeMember`, which the server rejects with 422 ("can not modify automatic"), producing a silently failing/confusing action with no user-facing error handling (there is no failure handler on `removeMember` in the model or controller).

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members with limit 50, or 100 with limit 50), this yields one page too many (2 pages for 50 members). The `showingLast` computed then never becomes true on the real last page, so the "next" arrow stays enabled and clicking it fetches an empty member page, showing an empty list while claiming page 2/2. The calculation should use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

title: add_members silently ignores non-existent usernames and reports success
body: `add_members` iterates the submitted usernames and only adds users found via `User.find_by_username`, but if a username doesn't match any user it is silently skipped and the endpoint still returns `success_json`. The admin UI then reloads the member list and gives the operator no indication that some (or all) of the requested members were not added — typos appear to succeed. The endpoint should report which usernames could not be found so the client can surface an error.

title: create drops the alias_level parameter the client sends
body: The new `Discourse.Group#create` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js) posts `asJSON()` which includes `alias_level`, but the server's `create` action only assigns `name` and `visible`; `alias_level` is never read. A newly created group therefore always gets the default alias level regardless of what the admin selected in the form, and the value is only applied later if the admin saves again. `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?` should also be applied in `create`.

title: members endpoint accepts an unbounded limit parameter
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is passed straight into `group.users.limit(limit)` with no maximum cap and no guard against nonsense values. Any client (this is a public, non-admin endpoint) can request `/groups/<name>/members.json?limit=1000000` and force serialization of the group's entire membership in one request, which on large groups (e.g. trust_level_0) is an expensive query and serialization. A sane cap such as `[limit, 1000].min` (and flooring at 0) should be enforced.

title: totalPages off-by-one when user_count is a multiple of limit
body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is exactly divisible by limit (e.g. 100 members with limit 50), this yields 3 pages instead of 2, so the 'next' arrow stays enabled and the admin can page past the last page, and the page indicator shows an impossible page count. It should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (and be 0 when there are no members).

title: Remove link shown for members of automatic groups
body: The template guards the remove link with {{#unless automatic}}, but inside the item view the context is the member (a Discourse.User), not the group, so `automatic` is undefined and the link is rendered for automatic groups too. Clicking it fires removeMember, which hits DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members and is rejected with 422 ('can not modify automatic'), leaving the admin with a broken control. The group's automatic flag needs to be passed into the item view (e.g. via a controller or view property).

title: remove_member automatic-group test uses the wrong HTTP verb
body: The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' issues `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, but the remove_member route is DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members. A PUT to that URL routes to add_members, which calls params.require(:usernames) and raises ActionController::ParameterMissing (500/400) rather than returning the asserted 422. The test as written cannot pass against the defined routes and does not actually exercise remove_member; it should use xhr :delete.

title: Unbounded limit on public group members endpoint
body: The members action now applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` directly to the query with no upper bound. The old code capped automatic-group listings at 200 members; now any (anonymous, for visible groups) request can pass limit=1000000 and force the server to load and serialize the entire membership. The limit should be clamped to a sane maximum.

title: add_members silently ignores unknown usernames
body: add_members iterates the comma-separated usernames and only adds users found by User.find_by_username; nonexistent usernames are silently skipped and success_json is still returned. The admin UI gives no feedback that some members were not added (previous PATCH-based code had tests asserting this behavior; those tests were deleted rather than ported). Either report which usernames could not be added, or fail the request.

title: Save error handler assumes JSON response body
body: On failure the save action does $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors. If the server returns a non-JSON error (e.g. 500 HTML page, or a response handled by Discourse's global error handling that returns no body), parseJSON throws and the user sees no message, and 'disableSave' is still reset only because the throw happens inside .then's callback which still triggers .finally — but bootbox.alert is never called. Guard the parse or use a fallback message.

title: findMembers returns undefined for unnamed groups, breaking promise chains
body: When the group has no name, findMembers now returns undefined instead of a resolved promise (the old code returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([])). Any caller that chains .then on the result (e.g. future code in routes that return model.findMembers() from setupController/model hooks) will crash on undefined. Return RSVP.resolve() to keep the contract.

title: Pagination off-by-one shows a blank last page
body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which is wrong when user_count is an exact multiple of limit. With 100 members and limit 50, totalPages = 3 even though there are only 2 pages. Worse, the next() action (line 33) clamps offset to Math.min(offset + limit, user_count), so from page 2 it sets offset = 100, and findMembers requests offset=100 which returns an empty member list. The admin ends up on a blank page 3/3 for a group whose members all fit on two pages. The clamp and the totalPages formula need to use Math.ceil and clamp to user_count - limit.

title: Group create action silently drops alias_level
body: The JavaScript model's asJSON() (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js line 62) sends name, alias_level and visible, but the create action only reads params[:name] and params[:visible]. If an admin picks an alias level (e.g. 'everyone') in the new-group form, the group is created with alias_level 0 and the selection is silently lost. The update action (line 37) does honor params[:alias_level], so the two actions are inconsistent.

title: Remove-member link rendered for automatic groups
body: The template gates the remove link on {{#unless automatic}}, but this partial is rendered by the group-member item view whose context is the individual member (a Discourse.User), not the group. The member user object has no 'automatic' property, so the guard is always truthy-negative and the remove link is shown for automatic groups too (where the parent group.hbs template deliberately hides the add-members UI for automatic groups). Clicking it triggers removeMember on an automatic group, which the server rejects with a 422 and no user-visible error handling. The view should receive the group's automatic flag explicitly (e.g. via a computed property on the view or controller).

title: add_members returns success even when no users matched
body: add_members splits the username list and skips any username that doesn't match a user (the `if user = User.find_by_username(username)` guard), then unconditionally renders success_json. An admin who typos a username in the add-members box gets a success response and a member list refresh that doesn't contain the user, with no indication anything failed. The action should report which usernames could not be added (render_json_error) so the UI can surface it.

title: Public members endpoint allows unbounded limit
body: The members action takes `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` with no upper bound, on a route reachable by any logged-in (and possibly anonymous, subject to visibility) user. Passing limit=1000000 makes the server serialize up to a million member records in one response. The previous code capped the practical default at 200 for automatic groups; the new code should clamp limit to a sane maximum (e.g. 1000) before using it in the query.

title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses wrong HTTP verb
body: The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route defined in config/routes.rb is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. Controller specs bypass routing so the test passes, but it does not exercise the actual DELETE route. Additionally, there is no request/routing spec at all for the new `put/delete /admin/groups/members` endpoints, so a routing regression would go unnoticed. The spec should use xhr :delete.

title: Translation cache key ignores fallback locales, causing stale/wrong cached translations
body: I18n.translate caches results under a key of "#{key}#{config.locale}#{backend.object_id}". With fallbacks enabled, the result of a translation now also depends on SiteSetting.default_locale (e.g. translating key X in locale :es may return the :es string, or fall back to the site default locale's or English string). Because the cache key only contains the requested locale, a cached fallback result will be reused even after the site's default_locale changes (or, on a multi-process deployment where the cache lives per process, results computed under an old default_locale persist until the cache is evicted or the process restarts). Users would see translations from the wrong locale until restart. The cache key should include the fallback chain (e.g. I18n.fallbacks[config.locale].join) or the cache must be cleared when default_locale changes.

title: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides [], making it a broken/unused Hash
body: FallbackLocaleList inherits from Hash but its `[]` ignores all hash state and always computes [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]. Any other Hash behavior (each, key?, merge, dup, defaults handling in i18n's Fallbacks code) will not see any entries and will behave as an empty hash. i18n-gem code that manipulates the fallbacks object as a hash (e.g. I18n.fallbacks.merge!, inspecting it, or copying it) will silently do nothing or produce wrong results. Either use a plain object that duck-types `[]`/`ensure_loaded!` without the Hash superclass, or actually store the computed fallback chain in the hash so Hash semantics stay consistent.

title: Fallback list can contain the literal symbol of an invalid locale and mixes string/symbol locales
body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` assumes SiteSetting.default_locale is always a symbolizable valid locale; if it is ever nil or an unsupported value, `nil.to_sym` raises NoMethodError inside every I18n lookup via the fallback chain, breaking all translations for the request. Additionally, `locale` may be a string or symbol depending on caller (I18n.locale vs raw keys), and `uniq` on mixed types ("de" vs :de) will not deduplicate, potentially causing the same locale to be tried twice per lookup. Normalize all entries with to_sym before uniq and guard against nil.

title: ensure_loaded! only runs for web requests; fallback locales are never loaded in jobs/mailers
body: I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is called only in ApplicationController#set_locale. Background jobs, mailers, and any other entry point that sets I18n.locale (e.g. Discourse's job locale handling, I18n.locale = user locale) will use the fallback chain without the fallback locales being loaded into the backend. Because translate_accelerator forces explicit loading (load_translations ignores empty args) and only loads config.locale inside translate, lookups for the fallback locales (site default locale, or :en) will miss and silently return the next fallback — meaning users get English strings instead of the site-default-locale translations in emails and scheduled jobs. The ensure_loaded! should be invoked wherever I18n.locale is set outside controllers, or translate should load all fallback locales.

title: Translation cache key ignores fallback locales, serving stale results after default_locale change
body: I18n.translate caches results in an LRU cache keyed by "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}". With the new fallbacks enabled, the translation result for a given locale now also depends on SiteSetting.default_locale (per config/initializers/i18n.rb, the fallback chain is [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]). An admin changing SiteSetting.default_locale at runtime will not invalidate this cache and the key does not include the fallback locale, so all web processes continue serving translations resolved against the old fallback chain until the cache evicts or the app restarts. The cache key should incorporate the fallback locales (or the cache should be cleared when default_locale changes).

title: Fallback translations are not loaded outside the controller path, causing 'translation missing' in jobs/mailers
body: The only place the fallback locales' translation files get loaded is ApplicationController#set_locale calling I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Everywhere else (background jobs, Sidekiq, ActionMailer, rake tasks), I18n.translate only triggers load_locale(config.locale), which loads the primary locale's yml files but not the fallback locales (default site locale or :en). When the Fallbacks backend then tries to look up a missing key in an unloaded fallback locale, the backend has no translations for it and the user gets 'translation missing' text instead of the English fallback. Loading of all locales in the fallback chain should happen whenever the primary locale is loaded (e.g., inside TranslateAccelerator#load_locale or I18n#translate), not only in the controller before_filter.

title: Fallback chain queries SiteSetting.default_locale on every lookup, breaking DB-less contexts
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] unconditionally calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym on every fallback resolution. Because fallbacks are now enabled in every environment (the per-environment config.i18n.fallbacks settings were removed and the initializer is global), any I18n.t with a missing key that occurs in a context without a database connection (rake db:create/migrate on a fresh install, assets:precompile, or when the DB is temporarily down) will attempt a DB read and can raise, instead of simply falling back to :en. A rescue/guard around the SiteSetting read (falling back to :en when unavailable) would make this robust.

title: ensure_loaded! mutates @loaded_locales outside the load mutex
body: The new ensure_loaded! method does '@loaded_locales ||= []' and reads @loaded_locales.include?(locale) outside LOAD_MUTEX, while load_locale mutates @loaded_locales inside the mutex. Two threads calling ensure_loaded! concurrently on a fresh process can both see a nil/short array, both pass the include? check, and both enter load_locale; while load_locale itself re-checks under the lock so the locale is only loaded once, the unsynchronized '@loaded_locales ||= []' write can also race with the assignment inside load_locale's critical section, potentially losing a locale entry and causing repeated re-loading. The check-and-init should be done under LOAD_MUTEX (or ensure_loaded! should just delegate to load_locale, which is already idempotent).

title: Fallback locales are never loaded outside of the ApplicationController#set_locale path
body: I18n.translate loads only `config.locale` (line 68) before delegating to the real translate, which will now walk the fallback chain defined by FallbackLocaleList (user locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en). The fallback locales are only pre-loaded via ApplicationController#set_locale's `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` call. Any translation performed outside a web request — background jobs (Sidekiq), mailers, rake tasks, one-off scripts — will look up keys in fallback locales that were never loaded, so the Fallbacks backend will return 'translation missing' strings instead of the English/default text. The accelerator should ensure all fallback locales for the current locale are loaded inside `translate`/`load_locale`, not rely on the controller filter.

title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain, serving stale translations after default_locale changes
body: The cache key is built from `key`, `config.locale` and the backend object id. With this PR the effective translation for a given I18n.locale also depends on SiteSetting.default_locale (via FallbackLocaleList#[]). When an admin changes default_locale at runtime, the fallback order changes but the cache key does not, so previously cached results from the old fallback chain keep being served for up to LRU_CACHE_SIZE (300) entries until they age out. There is no I18n.reload!/cache invalidation hooked to the default_locale SiteSetting in this change, so users in a non-default locale will continue seeing translations from the old default locale. The key should incorporate the fallback locales (or the cache should be cleared when default_locale changes).

title: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but only overrides [], so all other Hash behaviors report it as empty
body: FallbackLocaleList is a Hash whose lookup semantics are entirely in `[]`, with no stored entries. Any code in the i18n gem, Rails, or plugins that interacts with `I18n.fallbacks` through Hash methods other than `[]` (e.g. `each`, `key?`, `keys`, `merge!`, `store`) will see an empty hash: per-locale fallback rules configured that way are silently dropped, and any code that iterates the fallbacks map (for preloading, validation, or locale resolution) will do nothing. Subclassing Hash while making `[]` lie about the contents is fragile; a plain object responding to `[]` (and to whatever the i18n version in use requires) would be safer, or the entries should actually be stored in the hash.

title: Fallback lookup dereferences SiteSetting.default_locale on every translation, which is not safe during boot or before SiteSetting is available
body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` on every translation lookup. During application boot (initializers, eager loading, asset precompilation) or in contexts where the settings table/connection is not available, SiteSetting may raise or return nil; `nil.to_sym` yields a symbol that then goes through the load path and could trigger DB queries or errors at times when translations are used before the app is fully initialized. A safer approach is to memoize the fallback list and only refresh it when the setting actually changes, and to guard against SiteSetting being unavailable.

title: Initializer relies on implicit filename ordering ('order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb') which is fragile
body: The comment at the top states the file must load after 02-freedom_patches.rb, and this happens to work because Rails loads initializers alphabetically and digits sort before letters. But the i18n initializer's `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` must apply to the backend class before it is used, and the pluralization include replaces the removed config/initializers/pluralization.rb — whose old filename sorted before i18n.rb, so any load-order dependent behavior (e.g. plugins or freedom patches touching I18n) silently depends on string sort order. If anyone renames this file (e.g. to `20-i18n.rb` or adds a locale-related initializer), the ordering requirement breaks with no error. The dependency should be explicit (require the freedom patch file, or use config.initializer with `before`/`after`), not a comment.

title: Denial cache reintroduces the exact bug this PR is meant to fix
body: The new negative cache caches a deny decision for shortCacheTTL (30s) keyed on (namespace, user, action, resource name, parent folder), and there is no invalidation when permissions or resources change. Scenario: a user requests a dashboard that does not yet exist / they have no permission for (Check returns deny and the entry is written at line 154). The user then creates that dashboard or folder (or an admin grants access). The very next Check for the same resource hits the denial entry at line 117 and is denied for up to 30 seconds, with no DB fallback. This is precisely the 'creator can't access the dashboard they just created' failure the PR description says it fixes — it is now bounded to ~30s instead of removed. Same for newly granted permissions: access is delayed by up to 30s. Consider invalidating the denial entry on writes, keying it more coarsely with shorter TTL, or not caching denials when the resource was simply absent from the scope map.

title: Denial cache key can collide with permission cache key (unescaped underscore concatenation)
body: userPermDenialCacheKey builds keys by plain underscore concatenation: namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent. Both userUID and name/parent are attacker-influenced strings that may themselves contain underscores, so two distinct (user, action, name, parent) tuples can produce the same key (e.g. uid "a", action "x", name "b_c" vs uid "a", action "x", name "b", parent "c" with an underscore shift). Worse, the key shares the "<ns>.perm_" prefix space with userPermCacheKey(ns, userUID, action), so a denial entry for one user/action tuple can be read as another user's permission set (or vice versa) if components line up — in Check, permCache.Get is keyed by the same scheme and the denial cache shares the same underlying cache.Cache instance. Use a separator that cannot appear in UIDs/actions (or hash/encode components) to make the keys unambiguous.

title: No test that a deny decision actually writes the denial cache entry
body: TestService_CacheCheck's 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' case only verifies that a manually pre-populated permDenialCache entry causes a deny. There is no test asserting that after Check returns Allowed=false from a DB query, the service writes the denial entry (service.go:154) and that a subsequent Check for the same resource short-circuits without hitting the store. This is the core new behavior of the PR (negative caching) and its write path is untested; a regression that never writes the entry (making the whole feature a no-op) would pass the current suite.

title: Denial-cache hit misreported as a permission-cache hit in permissionCacheUsage metric
body: When the denial cache is hit, the code increments s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage with label "true" (cache hit) even though the permission cache was not consulted. Additionally, when cached permissions exist but evaluate to deny, permissionCacheUsage is incremented with "false" (line 137) despite the perm cache actually being hit. Both skew the cache-hit-rate metric in opposite directions, making it unusable for evaluating whether the caching changes are effective.

title: Deny path with cached permissions always re-queries the DB, defeating singleflight in common case
body: When a user has cached permissions that don't cover the requested resource (a very common deny case for legitimate users, e.g. dashboard they don't own), Check falls through to getIdentityPermissions and performs a full DB permission query, and a denial entry is only written afterward. For users with genuinely no permission for the action at all, getIdentityPermissions returns an empty/stale-cached scope map which is re-fetched and re-set into permCache each time before checkPermission denies. The permCache is refreshed with identical data on every request for such users (singleflight only dedups concurrent, not sequential calls). Consider not re-setting permCache when the fetched map is identical, or caching 'no permissions for action' explicitly, to avoid write amplification on the hot deny path.

title: Denial cache can deny access after permissions are granted, with no invalidation path
body: The new permDenialCache is checked before anything else in Check() and is only ever written (never deleted/invalidated). When a user is denied a resource, the denial is cached for shortCacheTTL (30s). If the user's permissions are subsequently changed (e.g. an admin grants access to that dashboard, or the user is added to a role/team), the denial entry still takes precedence over the freshly-recomputed permission state: the code returns Allowed=false immediately at the top of Check() without ever consulting the (possibly updated) permission cache or DB. Unlike the permission cache, which gets overwritten on the next DB query, there is no mechanism anywhere in this PR to evict a denial entry, so a granted user can be locked out for up to 30 seconds. If any existing permission-invalidation hooks exist they do not clear this new cache.

title: userPermDenialCacheKey is ambiguous due to '_' separators
body: userPermDenialCacheKey builds the cache key by concatenating action, name and parent with '_' separators: namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent. Because the resource name and parent folder UID are free-form strings that may themselves contain underscores, two distinct requests can produce the same key (e.g. name="a", parent="b_c" vs name="a_b", parent="c"). A denial cached for one resource would then be incorrectly returned for a different resource, causing wrongful denial. Use a separator that cannot appear in the components or hash/escape the parts.

title: permissionCacheUsage 'miss' metric is emitted even when the cache lookup failed for non-miss reasons
body: In Check(), getCachedIdentityPermissions can return an error for reasons other than a cache miss — notably GetUserIdentifiers failing with a DB error, or an unsupported identity type (which returns a hard error). In all those cases the code still increments permissionCacheUsage with hit="false" and then proceeds to getIdentityPermissions, which will also fail. This distorts the cache-hit-ratio metric: genuine backend errors are counted as cache misses, making the cache look less effective than it is during incidents.

title: Dead cacheHit field and removed cache-hit test case in TestService_getUserPermissions
body: The 'should return permissions from cache if available' test case was deleted, but the testCase struct still has the cacheHit field and the test body still contains the 'if tc.cacheHit' branch asserting store.calls == 1. Since no remaining test case sets cacheHit=true, this code is dead and the caching behavior of getUserPermissions/getIdentityPermissions (that a permCache hit avoids the store call) is no longer covered at that level. Either remove the dead field/branch or restore a cache-hit case so the cache path stays tested.

title: Denial cache reintroduces the 'cannot access newly created resource' bug the PR fixes
body: The permDenialCache entry for (namespace, user, action, name, parentFolder) is set with a 30s TTL whenever a Check is denied, and any later Check with the same key short-circuits to denied before the permission cache or DB is consulted (service.go:116-121). Consider the exact scenario the PR describes: a user without a scoped permission triggers a Check for e.g. dashboards:read on name 'newdash' in folder 'fold1' (e.g. a pre-flight check, a duplicate-name check, or a failed attempt), which populates a denial entry. The user then creates the dashboard/folder, which writes the permission row to the DB. The next Check for that same (user, action, name, folder) hits the denial cache and returns Allowed=false without ever re-querying the DB — so the creator is still locked out of their newly created resource for up to 30 seconds. Any mechanism that invalidates/refreshes permCache (e.g. a DB requery triggered by a different resource name) does not invalidate the denial entry, so the denial can even outlive a freshly queried permission map that would allow the request. The denial cache needs to be invalidated when permissions change (e.g. on permission/role writes or resource creation), or its scope/TTL must be bounded so it cannot mask fresh grants.

title: Denial cache key uses the raw subject identifier, not the resolved user UID
body: userPermDenialCacheKey is built from checkReq.UserUID (the raw ID parsed from the subject string), whereas the permission cache key (userPermCacheKey) is built from the resolved userIdentifiers.UID obtained via GetUserIdentifiers (service.go:360, 379). Since GetUserIdentifiers accepts both numeric user IDs and UIDs as the subject identifier (service.go:463-469), the same user can be addressed as 'user:112' or 'user:<uid>'. The denial decision was computed from the resolved identity's permissions, but it is stored under the caller-supplied identifier. Consequences: (1) denial entries are not shared between the two spellings, causing unnecessary duplicate DB requeries; (2) if the mapping between a numeric ID and UID ever changes (user deletion/recreation), a stale denial entry keyed by the numeric ID remains valid and keeps denying the new identity for up to 30s. The key should use the resolved UID, consistent with the permission cache.

title: Denial-cache hits are counted as permission-cache hits in metrics
body: When the denial cache short-circuits a Check, the code increments s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage with label "true" (cache hit). This conflates the new denial cache with the permission cache, making the permissionCacheUsage metric misleading for operators tuning cache behavior: a denial hit is reported as a permission cache hit even though the permission cache was never consulted. A separate label or metric (e.g. permissionDenialCacheUsage) should be used.

title: No test covers the denial cache being populated by a denied Check and its interaction with later allowed checks
body: The only denial-cache test ('Should deny on explicit cache deny entry') manually pre-populates permDenialCache; there is no test that a Check returning Allowed=false actually writes a denial entry and that a subsequent identical Check short-circuits without touching the store. More importantly, there is no test for the interaction the feature exists for: after a denial is cached, a subsequent grant of the permission in the store (simulating resource creation) — the 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' sibling case where permCache/DB allow but the denial entry denies. Without such a test the stale-denial regression risk (denial entry masking a fresh DB allow) is unguarded.

title: Silence drawer can never open when only promRule is provided
body: The 'Silence notifications' menu item is shown based on promRule abilities (canSilence can be true via the new useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities path), and clicking it calls setShowSilenceDrawer(true).
