title: totalBatchesIndexed is incremented from multiple errgroup goroutines without synchronization
body: In searchSupport.init, each group.Go closure does totalBatchesIndexed++ on a plain int shared across up to s.initWorkers concurrent goroutines. This is a data race (undefined behavior; the span attribute 'namespaced_indexed' can be wrong). Use sync/atomic or collect counts per goroutine.

title: Goroutine writes to shared err variable raced by main test goroutine
body: The goroutine launched at line 50 assigns to the outer err variable (err = ms.Run()), while the main test goroutine subsequently reads and reassigns the same err at lines 59-62 (client.Get, res.Body.Close) and again in require.NoError. This is a data race that can also cause a require.NoError on line 60 to see the 'context canceled' error set by the goroutine during shutdown, producing flaky failures. Use a local variable inside the goroutine.

title: Removing the full BuildIndex lock allows concurrent duplicate builds of the same index
body: Previously `BuildIndex` held `cacheMu` for the whole function, which (coarsely) guaranteed only one build per key ran at a time and that a cache entry existed before another `GetIndex`/`BuildIndex` could proceed. Now the lock is only taken around the final cache write. `resource.getOrCreateIndex` has no per-key synchronization (its own TODO admits this): two concurrent Search requests for a namespace whose index is not yet cached will both see `GetIndex` return nil and both call `BuildIndex` concurrently. For indexes above the file threshold, both goroutines call `bleve.New` on the same directory; the second one fails (bleve refuses to create an index in an existing path), so the request returns an error, and the two half-built indexes can also clobber each other in `b.cache`. The fix needs a per-key singleflight/mutex, not just moving the lock.

title: Data race on shared err variable and totalBatchesIndexed in concurrent index build
body: In `init`, the worker goroutines launched via `group.Go` all assign to the captured outer `err` variable (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and increment `totalBatchesIndexed` without any synchronization. Since this PR explicitly increases concurrency of index builds (worker pool plus finer-grained bleve locking), these unsynchronized writes are now a genuine data race (Go race detector will flag it; a lost or torn error value can mask build failures, and the `namespaced_indexed` span attribute can be wrong). Each goroutine should use its own local err, and the counter should be atomic or accumulated from return values.

title: Constructor does not clean up on Init failure
body: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure, but never calls `s.cancel()` or `s.Stop(ctx)`. If the failure happens after lifecycle hooks ran (lifecycle.Init may have started resources) or after `searchSupport.init` started its watch-event goroutine, the cancellable context and any goroutines started during partial init are leaked. On the error path the constructor should tear down what was started (at minimum `s.cancel()`).

title: Watch-event goroutine panics on nil event when the events channel is closed
body: The goroutine started in `init` does `v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v)` with no `ok` check and no loop-exit condition. The SQL backend's poller closes the stream channel when the backend is stopped (`b.cancel()` in `Stop`). After the channel is closed, `<-events` yields a nil `*WrittenEvent`, and `handleEvent` immediately dereferences `evt.Type`, panicking the process. Additionally the goroutine uses `context.Background()`, so it is never terminated on shutdown. It should check `evt, ok := <-events; if !ok { return }` and use a cancellable context tied to server shutdown.

title: Postgres variant of the integration test is silently skipped with a TODO
body: The only change to this test is skipping postgres entirely ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally'). This removes coverage for the storage server target on one of the two supported databases with no tracking issue referenced, so a postgres-only regression in unified storage startup (which this PR makes eager via `NewResourceServer`) would go undetected. Either link the TODO to an issue or fix the Drone environment so the coverage is not silently lost.

title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows concurrent duplicate builds and lost index writes
body: BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for its whole duration, which (despite the perf cost) guaranteed only one index per NamespacedResource was ever built and published to the cache. Now the lock is only taken around `b.cache[key] = idx`. Two callers can build the same key concurrently: during `searchSupport.init` (multi-worker errgroup) and via `getOrCreateIndex` triggered by a watch event or a Search request arriving while init is still building. Consequences: (1) two bleveIndex objects exist for the same key; the loser of the last cache write keeps getting writes (e.g. from handleEvent) into an index that is no longer in the cache, so those documents silently vanish from search results — data loss for the index; (2) for file-backed indexes (`size > FileThreshold`), both builds call `bleve.New(dir, ...)` on the same directory, which will fail (index already exists) or corrupt the on-disk index. getOrCreateIndex's own TODO comment ("we don't want to block while anything is building, just the same key") confirms per-key serialization is required; this change removed even the coarse serialization without adding a per-key one.

title: NewResourceServer now performs full index build synchronously, changing the constructor contract for all callers
body: Init() (which builds the entire search index over all namespaces and can take a long time on large installations) is now invoked inside NewResourceServer, and any init failure makes the constructor return an error. Previously, callers such as embedded/in-process usage of the resource server (e.g. apiserver storage wiring, tests, single-binary Grafana where the unified storage may be created alongside other services) got a server immediately and initialization happened lazily or in the background. Those callers now block startup for the whole index build and will fail hard if the index build errors (e.g. transient DB issue during startup), where previously reads/writes could still be served. The PR description itself flags this ("Does anything else depend on initializing US lazily?") — the callers of NewResourceServer outside the storage-server target need to be audited; no such audit or feature flag is included.

title: Failed Init in constructor leaks the server's background context and goroutines
body: When s.Init(ctx) fails inside NewResourceServer, the function returns nil, err, but s.cancel() is never called. Init may have already started background work before failing — notably searchSupport.init's watch-event goroutine (started after WatchWriteEvents succeeds) and the lifecycle hooks' partial initialization. With no reference to the server retained by the caller, those goroutines and the cancelable context are leaked for the life of the process. The error path should call s.cancel() (or s.Stop) before returning.

title: Data race on shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` in init's worker goroutines
body: In searchSupport.init, the loop over stats spawns goroutines (limited by initWorkers, so several run concurrently) that both execute `totalBatchesIndexed++` and assign `_, _, err = s.build(...)` where `err` is the outer function-scope variable declared at `stats, err := s.storage.GetResourceStats(...)`. These are unsynchronized concurrent read/writes of shared variables — a data race under Go's memory model (and `go test -race` will flag it), and the shared `err` can be clobbered by a later goroutine, causing a real build error to be lost so init reports success with a missing index. Each goroutine should use its own local counter/err (e.g. `i, e := 0, error(nil)` captured per closure), with totals aggregated after group.Wait().

title: Watch event goroutine has no termination path and panics on closed channel
body: The goroutine started at the end of init reads `v := <-events` in an infinite loop with no select on a done channel. When the storage backend closes the events channel (e.g. the SQL poller exits when b.done fires on Stop, which closes the stream), the receive yields nil forever and s.handleEvent(watchctx, nil) dereferences evt.Type/evt.Key, panicking the process. Additionally, because this uses context.Background(), there is no way to stop it on shutdown. Now that init runs in the constructor for the storage-server target, every server start creates this goroutine, so it must be tied to the server's cancelable context.

title: Init ordering change: watch events consumed by searchSupport.init but broadcaster started after — event gap risk and misordering rationale
body: The diff moves initWatcher() to after s.search.init(). searchSupport.init internally starts its own WatchWriteEvents subscription, so this ordering is intentional (watch events are captured while the index builds). However, the server's broadcaster (used by the Watch RPC) is only started after the potentially long index build completes. During that window, Watch RPCs that do reach the server (the gRPC server may already be serving since the module server registers services before/around construction) will fail or block on s.broadcaster — notably s.broadcaster is nil until initWatcher succeeds, so a Watch call during init will nil-pointer panic on `s.broadcaster.Subscribe`. At minimum the nil broadcaster needs a guard, or initWatcher should run before search init (with search's own event subscription providing continuity, which is the pre-existing design).

title: Storage-server integration test disabled for postgres with no follow-up issue
body: The only integration test covering the storage-server target (which is exactly the code path changed by this PR — eager init of unified storage at startup) is now skipped for postgres with a TODO comment ("not working with postgres in Drone"). This means the main behavioral change in this PR (synchronous index init at startup) has no integration coverage on one of the two supported databases, and the failure cause is neither diagnosed nor tracked. Since this test is the regression guard for the change, the skip should be replaced by a fix or linked to a tracked issue.

title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() — module does not compile
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only such method defined in the class hierarchy (UsernamePasswordForm, line 160) is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which takes a parameter. Neither AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator nor any other shown class defines a no-arg overload. As shipped, this file will not compile, breaking the whole services module build. Either a no-arg overload (e.g. `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`) is missing from UsernamePasswordForm, or the call in UsernameForm must pass `context.getUser()`.

title: Conditional passkey UI no longer rendered when no user is set in the context
body: The refactor changed both `authenticate()` and `challenge(context, error, field)` to gate `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` behind the new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` helper, which returns false when `context.getUser() == null`. Previously, `fillContextForm` was invoked precisely when the user was NOT already selected (the old comments said 'setup webauthn data when the user is not already selected'). After this change, on a fresh login where no user is in the context, the WebAuthn challenge/attributes (WebAuthnConstants.CHALLENGE, RP_ID, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI, etc.) are no longer set on the login form, so conditional-ui (autofill) passkey login on the initial username/password page is silently disabled. Note that tests in this same PR (e.g. PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey, which asserts the `webauth` form is present on the very first login page before any username is submitted) only pass if some other execution renders the conditional UI; for any deployment where the username/password form itself was the sole provider of the conditional passkey UI for unidentified users, this is a functional regression. If the intent was only to also enable it during re-authentication, the user==null case must be preserved, not dropped.

title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() — does not compile / wrong overload
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only method defined (in UsernamePasswordForm, line 160) is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. No no-arg overload exists in UsernamePasswordForm, AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, or any superclass shown. Either this does not compile, or if an overload exists elsewhere it is being invoked unintentionally. The call must pass the user (e.g. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`) so the skip-form shortcut is suppressed exactly when conditional passkeys are active for the re-authenticating user.

title: Conditional passkey UI no longer rendered on the initial login page when no user is set
body: The refactoring moved `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` out of the `else` (user == null) branch and now only calls it when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, and that helper (line 160-162) requires `user != null`. On the initial username/password page the user is not yet known, so the WebAuthn challenge/RP-ID/conditional-UI attributes are never set and the passkey autofill (`//form[@id='webauth']`) disappears from the first login page for non-discoverable keys. This regresses the passkeys feature for the common first-visit case and contradicts the test expectations in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey (line 144-146) and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey (lines 189-194), which assert the webauthn form is present on the initial page before any username is submitted. The gate should enable conditional passkeys when passkeys are enabled for the realm, regardless of whether the user is already set.

title: Re-authenticating users without any passkey are now forced through the username form
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() previously auto-succeeded during re-authentication when the user was already set and had no linked brokers. Now, whenever `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is true (a realm-level passkeys policy flag, not per-user), the form is always shown. A user who has never registered a passkey (and whose administrator merely enabled passkeys for the realm) must re-enter their username on every re-authentication (e.g. prompt=login), even though the user identity is already known. The suppression should also check that the user actually has a passwordless WebAuthn credential, not just the realm policy flag.

title: shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators hook can now be true while user is null
body: fillContextForm previously guarded the WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean construction on `user != null`; the new `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` hook defaults to `context.getUser() != null` in WebAuthnAuthenticator, so behavior is preserved there — but any subclass that returns true without a user (the hook is now an extension point) would pass a null user into `new WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean(...)` at line 103, risking an NPE. The null-user invariant should be enforced in fillContextForm itself (e.g. `user != null && shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)`), not delegated to every subclass.

title: No test for passkey failure during re-authentication after wrong password (error path keeps username hidden)
body: The new helper AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError and its use in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse (the passkey-fails-during-re-auth path, where the username must remain hidden and registration disabled) is not covered: webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey only tests a wrong *password* followed by a successful passkey, never a failing passkey submission during re-authentication. A regression that re-renders the re-auth form with a visible/editable username field would go undetected.

title: Call to undefined no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() in UsernameForm
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only definition in the class hierarchy (UsernamePasswordForm, shown in full in this PR) is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. There is no zero-argument overload anywhere in the changed files, so this does not compile; if the intent was `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, that should be passed explicitly.

title: Passkeys check in UsernameForm silently disabled when authenticator built without a session
body: UsernameForm has a no-arg constructor that leaves `webauthnAuth` null (inherited from UsernamePasswordForm). Any passkeys-enabled check that depends on `webauthnAuth != null` (as the base `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` does) will return false for instances created via the no-arg constructor, so the re-authentication form will be skipped exactly in the deployments that use the factory-created authenticator, defeating the purpose of this fix. The check needs to work independently of how the authenticator was instantiated (e.g., consult the session/realm policy from the AuthenticationFlowContext).

title: Conditional passkeys UI no longer initialized when no user is set on the login page
body: The new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` requires `user != null`, and both call sites in `authenticate()` and `challenge()` were changed to use it, whereas the old code called `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when the user was NOT yet selected. In a browser flow where UsernamePasswordForm is the first/only execution (no prior WebAuthnPasswordless execution), the initial login page will no longer receive the WebAuthn challenge, RP ID, and conditional-UI attributes, so the passkeys autocomplete/'try another way' button disappears for unidentified users. If this regression is intended only for flows that already set up conditional UI earlier, the condition should be documented/tested for the plain UsernamePasswordForm-first flow; otherwise passkey login on the first page is broken.

title: Test cleanup removes IDP with literal alias "alias" instead of the created alias
body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, after creating each IDP the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` — the string literal "alias" is used instead of the variable `alias` ("idp-alias-" + i). The cleanup therefore targets a non-existent resource, so none of the 21 IDPs created by the test are ever removed. Consequences: leaked identity providers accumulate in the test realm across test methods (the same test class runs other tests against the same realm), which can break subsequent assertions that count providers, and the cleanup call itself may throw a 404 when executed. The same bug exists at line 425 for the "idp-alias-20" provider. The fix is `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove);`.

title: registerIDPInvalidation NPEs when the IDP model is null (remove of unknown/nonexistent alias)
body: In remove(), `storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` can be null when no IDP with that alias exists; the code then unconditionally calls `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` (null-safe via the Objects::nonNull predicate), but the pre-existing `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` path at line 103 dereferences it (`idp.getInternalId()`), throwing a NullPointerException on remove of an unknown alias. While the null-deref itself predates this PR for the invalid-cache branch, the change now also makes the delegate lookup happen on every remove, so any caller removing a nonexistent alias hits it. A null guard in registerIDPInvalidation (or before calling it) is needed.

title: getForLogin cache hit can return IDPs whose organization-aware enabled state differs from the cached list
body: The cached getForLogin result stores only internal IDs and re-fetches each IDP via session.identityProviders().getById(id), which returns the organization-aware wrapper. For an IDP linked to an organization that has since been disabled, the cached login list still contains it and only the consumer-side isEnabled() re-check (added in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean) filters it out. Any other caller of getForLogin that does not re-check isEnabled (the SPI contract says results are "suitable for being displayed in the login pages") will get disabled-org brokers from the cache. Disabling/removing an organization does not invalidate the cacheKeyForLogin entries, only IDP CRUD does. At minimum the contract should be documented, or the org disablement path should invalidate the login caches.

title: Test cleanup registers wrong alias (literal "alias") so created IDPs are never cleaned up
body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` instead of using the actual alias variable (`alias` = "idp-alias-" + i). The same mistake is repeated at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". Consequence: the 21 IDPs created by this test are never removed by the cleanup (the cleanup targets a non-existent provider and may itself fail with 404), leaving the realm polluted and potentially causing cross-test interference and flaky failures for tests that count realm IDPs.

title: registerIDPLoginInvalidation can throw NPE when the login predicate evaluates a model with null config
body: The new `getLoginPredicate()` in IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter evaluates `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` without a null guard on `getConfig()`. While `Objects::nonNull` guards the model itself, `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` can return null for models constructed from representations/deserialization before `setConfig` is called. This predicate is invoked on every create() and remove() path (registerIDPLoginInvalidation), so a create/remove of an IDP whose config is null would throw a NullPointerException and abort the operation. A null-safe config access (e.g. `idp.getConfig() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(...)`) is needed.

title: Login-cache invalidation on update compares organizationId but not BROKER_PUBLIC semantics of the fetch modes
body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate skips invalidation when the IDP qualifies for login before and after the update and `organizationId` is unchanged. However, for FetchMode.REALM_ONLY the delegate query filters on organizationId being null, while for ORG_ONLY/ALL with no specific organizationId it filters on BROKER_PUBLIC=true. If an IDP keeps the same organizationId but its BROKER_PUBLIC config changes in a way that keeps the predicate result unchanged while the set of cached queries it belongs to changes... more importantly, the predicate now treats a non-public org IDP (BROKER_PUBLIC=false) as not a login IDP, but the cached ORG_ONLY list keyed per searchKey may still legitimately contain org-linked IDPs in other states; the mismatch between the predicate-based invalidation decision and the actual delegate query criteria means there are update combinations (e.g. an IDP that is enabled and public before and after, but whose org linking via OrganizationProvider paths does not route through update()) where stale cached login lists are served. The invalidation logic should mirror the delegate's query filters exactly, and the organization unlink path (removing an IDP from an organization, which may bypass this provider's update()) needs an explicit invalidation of the login cache keys.

title: getForLogin caches IDP lists per organizationId indefinitely, so new organizations' IDP links reuse stale entries without invalidation
body: The login cache is keyed by (realm, FetchMode) with searchKey per organizationId. When an identity provider is linked to an organization through the OrganizationProvider (OrganizationManager.addIdentityProvider), Keycloak updates the IDP's organizationId via the storage provider, which is handled. However, when a new organization is created and IDPs are linked, the cache entry for searchKey "" (ORG_ONLY with organizationId=null, i.e. all org-linked public IDPs) is only invalidated if the IDP's predicate result flips. An IDP that is already public and org-linked (predicate passes) being moved from org A to org B keeps organizationId non-null on both sides only if the update is seen; but linking an already-public realm-level IDP to an org goes from organizationId=null to non-null, which is covered. The uncovered case: an IDP already linked to org A (passes predicate) gets linked to org B instead (organizationId changes) — this IS covered by the orgId comparison. The remaining gap is that the empty-string searchKey (ORG_ONLY, null org) aggregates across all organizations, and adding an IDP to a *new* organization where the IDP previously passed the predicate with the same organizationId is impossible, so the actual residual risk is operations performed through bulk/organization removal paths (org deletion cascades unlinking or deleting IDPs at the JPA level) that never invoke create/update/remove on this provider — those leave the cached login lists stale with IDs of deleted/unlinked IDPs. The getById-null fallback mitigates rendering but only per-request; the cache entry itself is never invalidated and is recomputed from a stale set on subsequent requests until something else invalidates the key.

title: getLoginPredicate NPEs when an IDP has a null config map
body: The new clause in getLoginPredicate calls idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) whenever idp.getOrganizationId() != null. IdentityProviderModel.getConfig() can be null (e.g. models built programmatically or deserialized without a config map; other code in the codebase null-guards getConfig()). Any create/update/remove of an IDP that is linked to an organization but has a null config will now throw a NullPointerException inside registerIDPLoginInvalidation / registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate, breaking the write operation. Guard with idp.getConfig() == null || ... instead.

title: Cleanup registers removal of literal "alias" instead of the actual IDP alias
body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) uses the literal string "alias" rather than the constructed alias variable ("idp-alias-" + i). The registered cleanup will target a non-existent identity provider and either throw 404 during cleanup or silently fail, leaking the 20 created IDPs between test runs and potentially making subsequent runs fail on alias conflicts. The same bug exists at line 425 for "idp-alias-20".

title: Cached getForLogin loses the delegate's result ordering
body: When served from cache, getForLogin collects the IDPs into a HashSet and returns identityProviders.stream(), whereas the uncached/delegate path returns the delegate's stream, which for the JPA storage is ordered by alias. Callers that sort (like IdentityProviderBean) are unaffected, but any other consumer of IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin that relies on the ordering of the delegate (a behavioral difference between cached and uncached invocations) will see non-deterministic ordering only when the cache is warm. Use a LinkedHashSet or sort before returning to keep behavior consistent.

title: order() added as abstract method breaks third-party CryptoProvider implementations
body: The new `int order()` method on the public `CryptoProvider` interface has no default implementation. Any existing external implementation of `CryptoProvider` (e.g. custom providers used by downstream projects or the adapter SPI consumers) will fail to load at runtime once keycloak-common is upgraded: ServiceLoader instantiation throws ServiceConfigurationError with AbstractMethodError on first call to order(), or the class no longer compiles. Since CryptoProvider already uses `default` methods elsewhere in this same interface (getSupportedKeyStoreTypes, getSupportedRsaKeySizes), `order()` should be declared as `default int order() { return 0; }` (or similar) to preserve binary and source compatibility.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default JKS KeyStore provider, not a BouncyCastle provider
body: The implementation returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which on a stock JVM is the Sun provider (for "pkcs12"/"jks"), not BouncyCastle. The interface contract ("@return BouncyCastle security provider") is violated, and any code path in keycloak-core/authz-client that calls `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getBouncyCastleProvider()` expecting BC-specific behavior (e.g. algorithms only BC provides, or null-check semantics used by WildFlyElytronProvider consumers) will silently get a wrong provider. Either return null (as WildFlyElytronProvider does when no BC is available) or document why the default keystore provider is acceptable here.

title: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER creates and discards encoder objects
body: Lines 114-115 (`ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger); ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);`) build two encoders whose results are thrown away; only the `writeDerSeq` chain on lines 117-121 is used. This is leftover debugging/dead code that allocates needless objects on every signature conversion and confuses readers into thinking those calls have an effect. The two lines should be removed.

title: readSequence() silently accepts indefinite-length encodings and returns an empty list
body: When readLength() encounters the indefinite-length marker 0x80 it returns -1; readSequence()'s `while (length > 0)` loop then never executes and an empty list is returned without consuming any content octets. Callers like asn1derToConcatenatedRS will only detect this indirectly via the size!=2 check, but any future caller iterating the returned list would treat a malformed BER indefinite-length sequence as a valid empty sequence instead of receiving an error. Indefinite length should be rejected explicitly (it is not valid DER).

title: integerToBytes silently truncates out-of-range signature integers
body: In asn1derToConcatenatedRS, integerToBytes keeps only the low `qLength` bytes when the decoded BigInteger is longer than the expected half-signature length (`qLength < bytes.length` branch takes the *last* bytes of toByteArray(), which for a positive value drops the most significant bytes). A DER signature whose r or s exceeds the curve order would be silently accepted and mangled rather than rejected, producing a signature that could verify against a different value than what was signed in length-mismatch scenarios. Validation (throwing when the value does not fit in qLength) would be the safe behavior for signature conversion.

title: New abstract order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider.order() is added to the interface without a default implementation. Any third-party or downstream implementation of CryptoProvider (this is a public SPI, e.g. custom FIPS/non-FIPS providers) will fail to compile/run against this version with 'does not override order()'. Since ServiceLoader instantiation fails with ServiceConfigurationError, previously-working deployments will break at runtime. A default value (e.g. default int order() { return 0; }) should preserve compatibility.

title: Providers with equal order() have nondeterministic selection; multi-provider error removed
body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order() == 200. The previous code threw an IllegalStateException when more than one CryptoProvider was found, forcing operators to fix the classpath; now detectProvider silently picks one. When two providers with the same order are present (e.g. default and elytron, or default and fips1402), ServiceLoader ordering is classpath-dependent and effectively arbitrary, so a deployment can silently get the wrong crypto provider (e.g. non-FIPS provider in a FIPS environment) with no error or warning beyond a debug log. Either the orders should differ per provider, or ties should be rejected/logged at warn level.

title: Most CryptoProvider methods throw UnsupportedOperationException, breaking signed-JWT client credentials in authz-client
body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider is installed as the only CryptoProvider on a plain authz-client classpath (via the new META-INF/services file), but getSignature, getKeyFactory, getKeyPairGen, getAesCbcCipher/GcmCipher, getSecretKeyFact, getX509CertFactory etc. all throw UnsupportedOperationException. The authz-client JWT client-credentials flow (Http/TokenCallable using JWTClientCredentialsProvider in keycloak-core) signs the client assertion via CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getSignature(...) and related calls, and token verification/PemUtils paths call getPemUtils(). A user who adds only keycloak-authz-client and configures 'signed_jwt' credentials (or any feature touching the unsupported methods) will now get UnsupportedOperationException instead of the previously-working default JCA behavior. These methods should return JCA defaults (Signature.getInstance(...), KeyFactory.getInstance(...), etc.) rather than throwing.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default KeyStore provider, not a BC provider
body: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which on a stock JVM is the SUN provider (or whatever is configured). Callers of this method (e.g. code that derives algorithm names or provider behavior from 'the BouncyCastle provider') will silently operate on an unrelated provider; returning null would be more honest than masquerading the SUN provider as BouncyCastle.

title: Indefinite-length BER sequences silently decode as an empty element list
body: readLength() returns -1 for the indefinite-length encoding (0x80), and readSequence()'s 'while (length > 0)' loop then exits immediately, returning an empty list with no error. asn1derToConcatenatedRS will report the misleading 'Invalid sequence with size different to 2' instead of a proper parse error. Indefinite-length input should be rejected explicitly (or handled), since this decoder otherwise claims DER support.

title: ECDSA test does not verify the DER output against the original signature
body: The test converts DER->concat->DER->concat and asserts the two concatenated forms match, but never asserts that the round-tripped DER equals the original 'sign' bytes, nor that the recovered r/s values actually verify against the public key. A bug that corrupts both conversions symmetrically (e.g. wrong offset handling for a fixed input) would still pass. Adding Assert.assertArrayEquals(sign, asn1Des) or a Signature.initVerify check would strengthen it.

title: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder instances and write r/s into them, then discard the results; only the encoders used in writeDerSeq at lines 117-121 matter. The dead statements are confusing and should be removed.

title: Adding abstract order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider SPI implementations
body: The new `int order()` method was added to the public `CryptoProvider` interface as an abstract (non-default) method. Any third-party or downstream implementation of this SPI (custom crypto providers, adapters, older keycloak-client jars on the same classpath) will no longer compile and, if precompiled, will fail at runtime with an AbstractMethodError when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` calls `CryptoProvider::order` on them. Since this is a public extension interface, the new method should have a default implementation (e.g., `default int order() { return 0; }`) to preserve binary compatibility.

title: Equal order() values across DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider make provider selection nondeterministic
body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order() == 200. CryptoIntegration.detectProvider previously threw an IllegalStateException when multiple providers were found; now it silently picks the first after sorting, but the sort is stable only relative to ServiceLoader iteration order, which depends on classpath ordering. In a deployment that (accidentally or intentionally) has more than one of these providers on the classpath, e.g. a FIPS environment where keycloak-crypto-fips1402 and keycloak-crypto-default are both present, the non-FIPS provider may win arbitrarily, silently disabling FIPS mode. Either the FIPS provider should have a strictly higher order, or ties among full-featured providers should still be reported as an error.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default KeyStore provider (e.g. SUN), not a BouncyCastle provider
body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which on a stock JVM is the SUN provider, not BouncyCastle. Callers of this method (e.g. code in keycloak-common that fetches the provider to register it or relies on it being BC/BCFIPS, or that checks `getBouncyCastleProvider().getName()`) will silently get a provider that does not implement the BC algorithms they expect, leading to hard-to-diagnose NoSuchAlgorithmException failures. At minimum this is misleading for the interface contract documented as 'BouncyCastle security provider'; if BC is not available, throwing UnsupportedOperationException (as done for the other methods) would fail fast and predictably.

title: Most CryptoProvider operations throw UnsupportedOperationException, breaking authz-client features beyond ECDSA signature conversion
body: The provider registered via META-INF/services in the authz-client jar throws UnsupportedOperationException for getPemUtils(), getCertificateUtils(), getX509CertFactory(), getKeyFactory(), getSignature(), getAlgorithmProvider() etc. CryptoIntegration.init is now called from AuthzClient.create, so if this is the only provider discoverable via the AuthzClient classloader, any code path in keycloak-common/authz-client that touches those APIs will fail at runtime — for example parsing PEM keys/certificates for client JWT assertion signing, or JWKS handling. Previously, these paths worked whenever BC was on the classpath via DefaultCryptoProvider; now a working deployment can regress to UnsupportedOperationException. Each unsupported method should either be implemented with JCE defaults (as WildFlyElytronProvider does) or the design should ensure DefaultCryptoProvider is used when available.

title: Dead code: two ASN1Encoder instances created and written to, then discarded
body: In concatenatedRSToASN1DER, lines 114–115 create two ASN1Encoder instances, write the r and s BigIntegers into them, and throw the results away; the actual encoding happens in the following statement. This is leftover debug/dead code that wastes work and confuses readers; it should be removed.

title: Indefinite-length DER (0x80) is returned as -1 and causes NegativeArraySizeException instead of a clean error
body: readLength() maps the indefinite-length marker 0x80 to -1. In readSequence(), a length of -1 makes the `while (length > 0)` loop simply skip parsing and return an empty list (silently accepting malformed input), and in readNext() the -1 propagates to read(-1), where `new byte[-1]` throws an uncaught NegativeArraySizeException rather than an IOException. Since BER indefinite-length encodings are not valid DER for ECDSA signatures, they should be rejected with an explicit IOException.

title: Test uses one default-curve key pair for all algorithms and only checks round-trip, not interop with the BC implementation
body: The test generates a single key pair with KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC") without specifying a curve, so ES384/ES512 cases run with (typically) a P-256 key and only exercise zero-padding logic, never real 48/66-byte coordinates. More importantly, it only verifies that this provider's conversion round-trips with itself; it does not compare output against DefaultCryptoProvider/BouncyCastle (e.g., BCECDSACryptoProvider) to guarantee signature compatibility with what the Keycloak server produces/expects. A cross-check against the BC implementation per curve would catch subtle encoding mismatches (leading-zero handling, negative integers) that a self-round-trip cannot.

title: NPE risk when falling back to the all-clients resource in hasPermission(ClientModel, String)
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no per-client resource exists, the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...), which can return null (e.g. when admin permissions are disabled for the realm, or when the type-level resource has not been created). The very next line then calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) with a null resource, which will throw a NullPointerException (or behave unpredictably) instead of returning false. Any admin API call guarded by canManage/canView/canConfigure on a client can therefore fail with a 500 instead of a clean authorization denial.

title: Per-client resource shadows the all-clients permission fallback
body: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) only falls back to the type-level 'Clients' resource when resourceStore.findByName returns null for the client's own resource. If a per-client resource exists (e.g. created earlier by a view-only permission) but no permission on it grants the requested scope, the type-level (all clients) permission is never evaluated. An admin who was granted 'manage' on all clients would then be denied manage on that specific client simply because some other, narrower permission once referenced it. The two levels should both be evaluated (or the evaluation should check type-level permissions regardless).

title: getClientsWithPermission finds no per-client resources and leaks the type-level resource name
body: getClientsWithPermission lists resources via resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). However, per-client resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId()) without setting a type, so they are not returned by a type query; the only resource that carries type 'Clients' is the type-level resource created in init(). Consequently the method (a) fails to return the IDs of clients that have per-client permissions granted, and (b) adds the name 'Clients' (the type-level resource name, not a client ID) to the result set when a type-level permission matches, which consumers will treat as a client ID. Either set the resource type when creating per-client resources, or query by name and filter out the type-level resource.

title: Client-removed listener can throw UnsupportedOperationException when V2 feature is enabled
body: registerListener now gates the event handling on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) and then calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). But management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 (and thus ClientPermissionsV2) whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException('Not supported in V2'). When both features are enabled (V2 is a preview feature that can coexist with V1), deleting any client (or removing a role/group) will trigger this listener and throw an UnsupportedOperationException inside the removal flow, breaking client/role/group deletion.

title: Dead code: getEvaluationContext is unused and canExchangeTo is unimplemented
body: The private method getEvaluationContext (lines 262-272) is never referenced anywhere in the class; it appears to be a leftover from token-exchange support. Together with the unused imports (Scope, EvaluationContext, TOKEN_EXCHANGE constant, and the unused logger), it suggests token-exchange evaluation was intended but canExchangeTo just throws UnsupportedOperationException. If token exchange for clients is not supported in V2 yet, the dead code should be removed; if it was intended to work, canExchangeTo throwing UnsupportedOperationException is a functional regression versus V1 for realms that enable the V2 feature.

title: Event listener calls V2 setPermissionsEnabled which always throws UnsupportedOperationException
body: registerListener gates on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) being enabled, but when V2 is also enabled (the normal way V2 is used), management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients().setPermissionsEnabled(), roles().setPermissionsEnabled() (inherited V1 paths) / groups().setPermissionsEnabled() paths route to the V2 implementations that throw UnsupportedOperationException('Not supported in V2'). Concretely, ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (line 193) always throws. So whenever both features are enabled together, a ClientRemovedEvent / RoleRemovedEvent / GroupRemovedEvent fired during normal admin operations will throw inside the provider event listener and break client/role/group deletion. The guard must also exclude the V2 case (or the V2 implementations must be no-ops) for these cleanup events.

title: NPE when per-client resource is absent and the 'Clients' type resource cannot be resolved
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String) (lines 214-222), when resourceStore.findByName for the client-specific resource returns null, the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately dereferences it via authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource). However getResourceTypeResource can return null (e.g., when supportsAuthorizationSchema is false because admin permissions are disabled in the realm or the resource server is not the admin-permissions client, or when the resource type lookup fails). Passing a null resource to findByResource causes an NPE instead of a clean 'no permission' result, so admin endpoints evaluating client permissions can fail with a 500 instead of 403.

title: getClientsWithPermission includes the 'all clients' resource name 'Clients' in the returned client-id set
body: getClientsWithPermission iterates resources found by type Clients and adds resource.getName() to the granted set. The resource-type resource created at schema init is named 'Clients' (AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and is also of that type, so when a type-level permission grants the scope, the literal string 'Clients' is added to the set alongside real client IDs. Callers using this set to filter clients by ID will never match a client with id 'Clients', effectively breaking the 'manage all clients' case for permission-based list filtering. The type-level resource should be detected and handled as a wildcard rather than added as a client id.

title: getResourceName returns null display name for client resources
body: getResourceName was extended with the Clients resource type in the schema, but its implementation only handles USERS: for a Clients policy on a per-client resource it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is null because per-client resources are created with only a name (the client's ID) in getOrCreateResource (resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId()), line 104). Any admin UI/REST rendering of client scope-permission resources will show a null/empty name instead of the client's clientId, unlike the Users case which resolves and returns the username. A branch resolving the client by ID and returning client.getClientId() is missing.

title: Dead code and unused imports (getEvaluationContext, TOKEN_EXCHANGE, Scope, EvaluationContext, logger)
body: The private method getEvaluationContext and the imports TOKEN_EXCHANGE, Scope, EvaluationContext, ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext, and the logger field are unused in this class. This is leftover from token-exchange support which is explicitly not implemented in V2 (canExchangeTo throws). Dead code around an unimplemented security-relevant feature invites confusion about whether token-exchange permission evaluation is actually performed; it should be removed.

title: Client deletion throws UnsupportedOperationException with V2 enabled via the ClientRemovedEvent listener
body: AdminPermissions.registerListener() handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). Before this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2 did not override clients(), so the V1 ClientPermissions implementation was used and this call worked. Now clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled() throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). The listener guard only checks Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), which is typically enabled together with V2, so deleting any client in a realm where the fine-grained admin authz features are active will throw an exception inside the provider-event listener, likely failing or corrupting the client-removal flow. setPermissionsEnabled (and the other inherited V1 methods that no longer have a working implementation) need a no-op/compat implementation, or the listener must skip the clients branch for V2.

title: No migration for realms that already initialized the admin permissions client: new Clients resource and scopes are never created
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns early when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null. Any realm that enabled admin permissions before this change has a resource server containing only the Users resource type and only the Users scopes (manage, view, impersonate, map-roles, manage-group-membership). The new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) and the "Clients" all-resource will never be created for such realms. Consequences: creating a Clients scope permission will fail (getScope lookup fails or resource lookup in getOrCreateResource finds nothing and throws "Could not map resource object..."), and ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission can hit a null "Clients" resource (see separate NPE finding). A migration step (or extending init() to create missing scopes/resources for existing admin permission clients) is required.

title: NPE when the all-clients resource does not exist in hasPermission(ClientModel, String)
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), when no per-client resource exists, the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately passes the result to authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource explicitly returns null when the resource type is unknown or no resource with that name exists (which is exactly the situation for realms initialized before this change, or if the "Clients" resource was never created). findByResource(server, null) will then throw a NullPointerException (or store-dependent error), turning a permission check into a 500 instead of returning false. The null case must be handled before calling findByResource.

title: getClientsWithPermission leaks the "Clients" all-resource name and ignores all-clients grants
body: getClientsWithPermission iterates resources found by type Clients and adds resource.getName() for each granted resource. The "Clients" all-resource itself has type Clients, so if the admin holds a scope permission on it (granted for all clients), the literal string "Clients" is added to the returned set — a value that is not a client ID. Worse, the intended semantics of an all-clients grant (the caller should see every client) are not handled at all: callers filtering client lists by this set will get an empty/incorrect result even though the admin is allowed to act on all clients. The method should either translate an all-clients grant into the full client set or exclude the type-level resource from the iteration.

title: canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking token-exchange permission evaluation paths
body: canExchangeTo(ClientModel, ClientModel, AccessToken) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. This method is part of the ClientPermissions contract used by token-exchange admin/permission evaluation code that is not gated on the V2 feature flag; if any of those paths execute while V2 is enabled, the caller receives a 500 error instead of an authorization decision. Either the V2 implementation must provide a decision (e.g., delegate to the scope-based evaluation or deny), or all call sites must be verified to be unreachable under V2 — with the unreachable ones documented/tested. The same concern applies to the other thrown methods if any remaining code path (e.g., the registerListener cleanup path) invokes them.

title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3, breaking existing scripts
body: This PR changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 (and reassigns 4 to FEATURE_DISABLED). Any automation or CI/CD pipeline written against the previous release that branches on exit code 4 to detect 'recreate upgrade required' will now silently misinterpret the result: exit code 4 now means the feature is disabled, and recreate is signaled by a different code. Since the whole point of this tool is to be scriptable via exit codes (as documented), this is a breaking contract change for existing consumers. If the renumbering is intentional, it should at least be called out in the PR description/release notes; alternatively pick an unused code (e.g. 5) for FEATURE_DISABLED to preserve compatibility.

title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert the new exit code 4
body: The new test testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message but not the process exit code. The feature-disabled path introduces a new documented exit code (4), which is the primary machine-readable contract of this tool. A regression that prints the message but exits with the wrong code (e.g. 1 or 0) would not be caught. The test should assert result.exitCode() == 4, as the other tests assert exit codes explicitly (e.g. testCompatible asserts 0).

title: CAUTION claims the Operator fails without the rolling-updates feature, but the default strategy is documented as usable
body: The added CAUTION states 'the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail.' However the same section documents that the default (`<not set>`) strategy mimics Keycloak 26.1 or older behavior, and the accompanying UpgradeTest only enables the rolling-updates feature when a strategy is explicitly set (updateStrategy != null). This means the operator does not fail for the default strategy without the feature, contradicting the CAUTION. The doc should clarify that the feature is required only when spec.update is configured (e.g. with an explicit strategy), otherwise users following the doc will enable the feature unnecessarily or distrust the doc after observing the default path works without it.

title: New exit-code behavior (4 for disabled feature, 3 for recreate) is not asserted in tests
body: The PR changes the RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and introduces exit code 4 (FEATURE_DISABLED), and documents both in update-compatibility.adoc. However, no test asserts these exit codes: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the error text, and testWrongVersions only checks the error messages without asserting exit code 3. Since the documented exit-code contract is the primary interface for automation pipelines, a regression in the codes would go unnoticed. Add assertEquals(4, result.exitCode()) in testFeatureNotEnabled and assertEquals(3, ...) after the incompatible-version runs.

title: Disabled feature exit code 4 is ambiguous for scripts that only check non-zero as 'recreate needed'
body: The guide now says the check command fails with exit code 4 when the rolling-updates feature is disabled, while exit code 3 means 'rolling upgrade not possible, recreate required'. A pipeline that treats any non-zero-but-not-error exit as 'do a recreate upgrade' (a natural reading of the documented table since both 3 and 4 are 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible') would silently shut down the deployment because the operator forgot to enable the feature, rather than failing loudly. The doc should explicitly warn that exit code 4 must be treated as a configuration error, not as a recreate signal.

title: Feature-disabled case does not assert the new exit code 4
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message 'Unable to use this command. The preview feature rolling-updates is not enabled.' but does not verify the process exit code is CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4). The exit code is the documented, scriptable contract for this tool (the guide documents exit code 4 specifically for the disabled-feature case), so a regression that prints the message but returns the wrong exit code would go unnoticed. Add assertEquals(4, cliResult.exitCode()) or equivalent.

title: Default-strategy (null) test runs without the rolling-updates feature enabled
body: In createInitialDeployment the ROLLING_UPDATES feature is only enabled when updateStrategy is non-null. The docs (advanced-configuration.adoc) state that while the rolling-updates feature is in preview it must be enabled or the operator will fail whenever the update spec is used. The null-strategy parameterization therefore exercises the CR update path without the feature, which per the documented contract is unsupported. If the operator is later changed to reject update-spec usage without the feature, this test will break; conversely, if the feature is not actually required for the default strategy, the documentation caution is misleading. Clarify the contract and align test and docs.

title: Global canManage() grants manage rights to admins holding only the VIEW scope on all groups
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-arg) falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Since hasPermission returns true if ANY of the listed scopes is granted, an admin who only has the `view` scope on the all-groups resource passes canManage(). This method backs `auth.groups().requireManage()`, which guards group creation (GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup) and other write paths, so a view-only fine-grained admin can create/modify top-level groups — a privilege escalation. The same pattern does not exist for users (UserPermissions.canManage() only checks MANAGE_SCOPE). The javadoc in GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() ("permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") appears to have replicated this mistake rather than describing intended behavior. It should only accept the MANAGE scope, and a negative test (view-only all-groups permission must not allow group creation) should be added.

title: NPE in hasPermission when the group resource and the all-groups resource are both missing
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission, when `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` returns null (no per-group resource exists), the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`. That method returns null when the resource server is not the admin-permissions client or admin permissions are not enabled, and can also simply find no 'Groups' type resource. In that case `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)` and the subsequent `resource.getScopes()` on line 152 will throw a NullPointerException instead of returning false. The null case must be handled (return false), as done implicitly by the early null checks in the V1 GroupPermissions.hasPermission.

title: getResourceName has no Groups handling, so group permission resources display null names
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName special-cases the USERS resource type (returning "All users" or the username) but has no branch for GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE. For group policies, it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, and group resources created via getOrCreateResource never set a display name (only name = group id). Any UI/logic that renders policy resources for the admin-permissions client will therefore show a raw group id or null instead of a human-readable group name. A resolveGroup-based branch (mirroring the Users handling) is needed.

title: No negative test that a VIEW-only all-groups permission does not grant manage operations
body: testManageAllGroups only verifies that MANAGE on all-groups enables group creation/update, but there is no test asserting that an admin holding only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource is still forbidden from creating or updating groups (GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup / GroupResource.updateGroup). Because GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope in its fallback (see separate finding), this exact regression is currently unguarded by the test suite; adding such a negative test would catch it.

title: canManage() falls back to the VIEW scope, so a view-only admin can manage groups
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-arg) returns true when `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` succeeds. Since the check passes if EITHER scope is granted, an admin who was only granted the `view` scope on the Groups resource (or on the all-groups type resource) will have canManage() return true. This evaluator backs GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()/requireManage(), GroupResource.deleteGroup() and other manage checks, so a view-only admin can create, modify and delete groups. The fallback should only accept the MANAGE scope (as canManage(GroupModel) correctly does on line 79).

title: hasPermission can NPE when the 'Groups' type resource is missing
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission, when no per-group resource is found, `resource` is reassigned from AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...). That method returns null when the resource-server is not the admin-permissions client, when admin permissions are disabled, or simply when the 'Groups' type resource has not been created / was deleted. The code then calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` with a null resource, which depending on the store implementation throws a NullPointerException and turns every group permission check into a 500 error. A null check (returning false) is missing after the fallback lookup.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission no longer honors manage permission, hiding manageable users from search
body: The early-return in GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (and the equivalent change in GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission) only checks `root.users().canView()`. Previously (V1 getGroupsWithViewPermission) the check was `root.users().canView() || root.users().canManage()`. In V2, an admin can hold the all-users `manage` permission without `view`: UserPermissionsV2.canManage(UserModel) accepts MANAGE, and canView(user) accepts VIEW or MANAGE, so per-user checks say the admin can see/manage every user. But getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns the (empty) set of group permissions, so UsersResource.searchForUser sets UserModel.GROUPS to an empty set and getUsersCount(..., groupIds) counts 0 — the admin's user search and count return nothing even though the admin can manage all users. The early-return should also treat users().canManage() as unrestricted, or the per-user/per-type view evaluation should be used.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission evaluates a full policy evaluation per group resource
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission iterates all resources of type 'Groups' via resourceStore.findByType and, for each one, runs a complete authorization policy evaluation through hasPermission (which itself does another resourceStore lookup and evaluatePermission). In realms with many groups and many per-group permissions this makes every user search/count call (UsersResource.getUsers/searchForUser, BruteForceUsersResource) perform N full policy evaluations, which can be very expensive. The old V1 implementation had the same shape, but now that per-group resources are expected to be created routinely for FGAP v2 this should be batched or cached per request.

title: Global canManage() grants manage access with only the VIEW scope
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-arg) falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Including VIEW in a manage check means an admin holding only a `view` scope permission on the all-groups resource is considered able to manage groups. This method is used by `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` (`auth.groups().requireManage()`) and by `canManage(GroupModel)` callers, so a view-only admin could create, update, or delete top-level groups — a privilege escalation compared to canManage(GroupModel), which correctly checks only MANAGE. The expectedScopes for the global manage check should be MANAGE only.

title: NPE when per-group resource and all-groups resource are both absent
body: In hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes), when `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` returns null, the code calls `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`, which returns null whenever the resource type resource does not exist or the schema is not supported for the resource server. The result is passed straight to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later `resource.getScopes()` without a null check, causing a NullPointerException (500 error) instead of a clean `false` for admins without any group permissions. The analogous UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission has the same shape; at minimum the new GroupPermissionsV2 copy needs a null guard.

title: Removal of cached canViewGlobal causes repeated permission evaluation per subgroup
body: getSubGroups previously computed `canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView()` once and short-circuited the filter. Now `auth.groups()::canView` is evaluated per subgroup. For an admin without the manage-users/view-users roles, each invocation of the V1 (and V2) global canView() runs a full authorization-policy evaluation against the admin permissions resource server, so listing a group with many subgroups performs N policy evaluations instead of one. The same pattern was removed in GroupsResource.getGroups. Cache the global result (or make canView() memoize) to avoid the per-element evaluation cost.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc references the wrong method
body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says "Throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false" — copy-pasted from requireManageMembership. It should reference canManageMembers(GroupModel). Since this PR adds javadoc to the whole interface, the newly written contract text is wrong for this method and will mislead implementers/users of the evaluator.

title: resolveGroup only accepts the internal group id, unlike users/clients which also accept names
body: resolveUser and resolveClient fall back to lookup by username/clientId when the id lookup fails, but resolveGroup only does getGroupById. When creating a group policy via getOrCreateResource with a group name or path instead of the internal id, the method throws IllegalStateException("Could not map resource object..."). Either this asymmetry is intentional (then it deserves a comment) or the group path/name lookup is missing; as written, the API behaves inconsistently across resource types and callers passing a group path get a 500-level error.

title: getScope NPEs when resourceType is null or unknown
body: In getScope, when the schema is supported, `SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType)` is dereferenced without a null check. If a caller passes a null or unrecognized resourceType (e.g., a permission being created without a resource type before validation runs), this throws a NullPointerException instead of the intended ModelValidationException ("Scope %s was not found for resource type %s."). A null/unknown-type check with a meaningful validation error is needed.

title: verifySafeHtml throws raw RuntimeException, crashing the build instead of reporting a message
body: When the derived English reference file cannot be opened (see separate finding), or the current file cannot be re-read, verifySafeHtml throws a plain RuntimeException. The surrounding verify() method only catches IOException and wraps it into a MojoExecutionException; an uncaught RuntimeException will propagate out of the mojo and abort the build with a stack trace rather than being added to the reported `messages` list. A verification tool should report the problem as a message (or wrap it in MojoExecutionException) so users get a readable diagnostic.

title: English-file path rewriting is wrong for community-only theme directories, causing the verifier to fail
body: The English reference file is computed as file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties"). This only works for files under themes/src/main/resources-community whose English counterpart exists under themes/src/main/resources. For the JS themes (js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources-community and js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources-community) there is no sibling "maven-resources" directory containing the _en file in the community repository, so the English bundle cannot be loaded and the verifier throws a RuntimeException (see other finding) for every such file. Additionally, many community-only locales (e.g. messages_ca, messages_ka under resources-community) have no _en-independent counterpart issue but product resources may lack them too; any locale file whose English file does not exist at the rewritten path will crash the verification rather than being skipped or reported.

title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax is not supported by the account UI's JS i18n stack
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from 'Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).' to 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.'. The keycloak.v3 account theme is a React app whose message properties use double-brace interpolation ({{0}}, {{1}} everywhere else in this file). The single-brace Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax is not evaluated by that JS i18n stack, so users of the account console will likely see the literal string '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' (and possibly un-interpolated {0}/{1}/{2}) instead of a pluralized message. The same change is made in js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources-community/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties (error-invalid-multivalued-size) which is also a React (i18next) UI. The choice format is correct only for the server-side FreeMarker themes (themes/src/main/resources...), where those files were updated consistently.

title: Italian text introduced into Lithuanian message files
body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian account messages was replaced with 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' — an Italian sentence. The same Italian text was also put into themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties (loginTotpStep1, line 71). Lithuanian users will see Italian on the OTP setup page. It should be translated to Lithuanian (e.g. 'Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių į savo mobilųjį telefoną:').

title: PropertyResourceBundle reads the file as ISO-8859-1 while the duplicate-key check uses UTF-8
body: verifyNoDuplicateKeys reads the file via Files.readString (UTF-8), but verifySafeHtml loads the same file with new PropertyResourceBundle(new FileInputStream(file)), and PropertyResourceBundle(Properties.load(InputStream)) decodes as ISO-8859-1. These message files are UTF-8 (Arabic, Chinese, Thai, etc.), so the values used for HTML comparison will be mojibake. In most cases value and sanitized are corrupted identically so the comparison still passes, but any character whose UTF-8 bytes contain 0x3C ('<') or 0x26 ('&') in a trailing byte after ISO-8859-1 decoding can produce spurious 'Illegal HTML' findings or, worse, hide real differences. The bundle should be loaded with an InputStreamReader specifying UTF-8.

title: containsHtml only recognizes lowercase tags, so uppercase HTML in the English source disables HTML in translations
body:
HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>") only matches lowercase tag names. If an English source string contained e.g. '
' or '

' (case-insensitive HTML is legal), containsHtml() returns false and POLICY_NO_HTML is used, while the OWASP sanitizer strips tags case-insensitively — a translation carrying the same uppercase tag would be flagged, and one with lowercase variants would be inconsistently treated. Use (?i) in the pattern.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The PR replaces loginTotpStep1 in the Lithuanian file with the Italian sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:" instead of a Lithuanian translation. Lithuanian users on the TOTP setup page will see Italian text. The same wrong-language text was also put into themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties line 101 (totpStep1). Both should be Lithuanian, e.g. "Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame telefone:".

title: error-invalid-multivalued-size now uses Java MessageFormat choice syntax that the JS UI cannot render
body: The account UI (and the admin UI in js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources-community/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties line 3138, same change) is a React app using i18next-style interpolation with double braces (the previous value used {{0}}, {{1}}, {{2}}). The new value uses single braces {0} and a Java ChoiceFormat pattern {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}. i18next does not understand Java ChoiceFormat and single braces are not the interpolation syntax there, so users will see the raw literal string "Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}." instead of a formatted message. This key should keep the {{n}} placeholders and plain wording in the JS theme files; the choice format is only valid for the server-side FreeMarker/Java themes (themes/src/main/resources...).

title: Missing English properties file crashes the build with a RuntimeException instead of being reported/skipped
body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file path via string replaceAll("resources-community","resources") plus a regex renaming the locale suffix to _en, then opens it with FileInputStream and throws a bare RuntimeException if it is missing. Any message file for which that derived path does not exist (e.g. a locale file with no messages_en.properties sibling, or a path where the 'resources-community' → 'resources' mapping does not hold, such as the js/ maven-resources theme trees) will abort the mojo with an unhandled RuntimeException rather than produce a MojoExecutionException or a recorded verification message. This also breaks the existing contract of verify(), which only declares MojoExecutionException and collects problems into the message list.

title: santizeAnchors removes the first occurrence of an anchor, not the matched one, and only checks pairwise order
body: When a translation contains the same anchor text more than once, value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "") deletes the first occurrence in the string, which may not be the occurrence the matcher found (earlier identical anchors may already have been removed at different positions, or an English anchor may appear before the matched one). This can silently leave a disallowed anchor in the value that then passes the policy check, or produce misleading 'Didn't find anchor tag' reports when the translation reorders anchors relative to English. The removal should target the index of the current matcher match (matcher.start()/end()), and the comparison should be order-independent or explicitly documented as order-sensitive.

title: Simplified Chinese file gets Traditional Chinese text for totpStep1
body: The new totpStep1 value in messages_zh_CN.properties is written in Traditional Chinese ("在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：" using 機/裝/應用程式) while this is the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) resource. Simplified users expect 在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：. The Traditional variant belongs in messages_zh_TW.properties.

title: containsHtml only matches lowercase tags, so mixed-case English tags disable the HTML allowance
body:
HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>") only recognizes lowercase tag names. If an English source value ever contains an uppercase or mixed-case tag (e.g.
or ), containsHtml() returns false and the policy degrades to POLICY_NO_HTML for that key, so legitimate translations carrying the same tag would be flagged as illegal HTML (false positive) — or conversely the check silently diverges from what the sanitizer allows. A case-insensitive match ([a-zA-Z]) would be more robust.

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The fix for the HTML-sanitizer findings replaced the Lithuanian translation of totpStep1 with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'). Lithuanian users of the account theme now see an Italian sentence on the OTP setup page. The same Italian string was also introduced in themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties (line 71). Both should be restored to a proper Lithuanian translation.

title: error-invalid-multivalued-size switched from {{n}} to single-brace MessageFormat syntax in the JS UI resource
body: In the account console (React/i18next-based) message bundle, error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from '{{0}} ... {{2}} value(s).' to 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,...}'. All other keys in this file use double-brace interpolation (e.g. error-invalid-length on line 140), so the single-brace placeholders and the Java-MessageFormat choice pattern are not interpolated by this UI; users would see literal '{0}', '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' text. The same change was made to js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources-community/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties (line 3138). If these keys are only rendered server-side via the Java base themes the change is fine, but then the JS copies should be verified against the UI's interpolation format before merging.

title: Missing English sibling file crashes verification with a raw RuntimeException
body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English reference file by regex-replacing the locale suffix of the current file's absolute path, then opens it with new FileInputStream and wraps any IOException in a RuntimeException. If a locale properties file has no *_en.properties sibling in the same directory (e.g. a bundle that intentionally has no English file, or a file whose name does not match the assumed naming scheme), the RuntimeException escapes verify() (which only catches IOException) and aborts the whole build with an unhelpful stack trace instead of being reported as a per-file message or a MojoExecutionException. The failure mode should be a clean, actionable error.
