With multiple host calendar references, it repeatedly tries to delete that first event using unrelated credentials and never processes the remaining references. This leaves recurring events on some host calendars and can issue deletion attempts against the wrong account.

title: Google Meet description patch no longer uses the primary-calendar fallback
body: Insertion falls back to `calendarId: "primary"` when no matching destination calendar is found, but the follow-up patch uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which is undefined in that case. Google requires a calendar ID for `events.patch`, so events created in the primary fallback path can fail the asynchronous patch and retain an incomplete description/hangout-link information.

title: Organization slug persistence condition was inverted
body: The organization `slug` is now persisted only when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is true, whereas the prior behavior persisted it when that feature was disabled. This makes newly created organizations lack a slug in non-team-billing deployments and assigns an active slug in the mode that previously retained it only as `metadata.requestedSlug`, changing organization routing/verification behavior unrelated to destination calendars.

title: Google Meet fallback dereferences an absent destination calendar
body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` when an event has no destination calendar, which is a supported case handled later by the fallback calendar logic. For a Google Meet event, the condition evaluates `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` unconditionally and throws instead of falling back to Cal Video. This breaks booking creation for Google Meet events without a selected destination calendar.

title: Office 365 always creates collective events in the first host calendar
body: Each collective destination is processed with its own credential by `EventManager`, but this service ignores the credential being used and always selects `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. Consequently, when a collective booking has multiple Office 365 hosts, later hosts either attempt to create the event in the first host's calendar using their own token (often failing authorization) or create duplicates there; their configured destination calendars are never used.

title: Lark creation ignores destinations after the first collective host
body: The multi-destination creation loop constructs a Lark service for each destination credential, but `createEvent` always takes the first entry in `event.destinationCalendar`. Thus all Lark host creations target the first host's calendar rather than the destination associated with the credential currently being processed, so collective Lark hosts do not receive their calendar events.

title: CalDAV creation cannot target each collective destination
body: CalDAV event creation filters calendars using only `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. `EventManager` invokes this service once per destination/credential, but the selected destination external ID is not passed into the service, so every invocation targets the first host's calendar. Collective events with multiple CalDAV destinations will therefore be duplicated in or fail against the first destination and omitted from the other hosts' calendars.

title: Recurring collective cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference under every credential
body: For each calendar reference, the recurring-cancellation branch iterates every calendar credential but obtains each recurring booking's reference with `.find(...)`, which always selects only the first calendar reference. With the new multiple-host references, it repeatedly attempts to delete that first event through all credentials and never selects the corresponding references for the other host calendars. Cancelling all remaining instances of a collective recurring booking consequently leaves events on other hosts' calendars (and can issue deletes against unrelated calendars).

title: Google Meet fallback dereferences an absent destination calendar
body: `destinationCalendar` is optional and is now commonly represented as an empty array. Destructuring an empty array makes `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined, but this condition immediately reads `.integration`. Any booking with Google Meet selected but no destination calendar will throw before the calendar/video event is created, rather than falling back to Daily as intended. Guard this access with optional chaining or treat a missing destination calendar as non-Google.

title: Office 365 always uses the first host's destination calendar
body: EventManager invokes this service once per destination credential for a collective event, but this implementation always selects `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. When processing a later host's Office 365 credential, it therefore attempts to create the event in the first host's calendar, which that credential generally cannot access, or creates it in the wrong calendar. The selected destination must be matched to the credential being used (as the Google implementation does), not array position.

title: Lark collective events are written to the first host calendar for every credential
body: The collective-event loop creates an event for each destination/credential, but Lark derives `calendarId` solely from the first element of `event.destinationCalendar`. A Lark credential belonging to a subsequent host will try to write to the first host's calendar and will fail authorization or place the event incorrectly. Select the destination calendar associated with the active credential instead of destructuring the first element.

title: CalDAV collective events only target the first destination calendar
body: For each destination credential, EventManager calls this calendar service, but event creation filters the calendars returned for that credential using only `event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId`. Consequently, later collective hosts either have no matching calendar (so no event is created) or target the first host's URL, which is not accessible with their credentials. The target must be resolved per credential/destination rather than globally from index zero.

title: Confirming a collective booking loses all non-primary host destinations
body: This handler reconstructs the event from the booking using only its single `destinationCalendar` relation (or the confirming user's calendar) and wraps that one item in an array. It does not load the collective event type's hosts or their destination calendars. Thus a pending/confirmation-required collective booking will create calendar references only for the primary host when confirmed, even though normal booking creation now includes all hosts. Persist/load the full destination set or rebuild it from the collective hosts before calling `handleConfirmation`.

title: Recurring collective cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference of each occurrence
body: Inside the loop over all calendar references, the recurring branch finds a single reference with `updBooking.references.find(...)`. For a collective booking each occurrence has multiple calendar references, so only the first one is selected; the code then retries that same reference through every calendar credential and never deletes the other hosts' events. This leaves orphaned events in non-primary host calendars (and can issue deletion requests with the wrong credential). Iterate every calendar reference and use its recorded credential ID when deleting it.

title: Organization slug is no longer stored when team billing is disabled
body: The previous condition stored `slug` when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` was false. This change reverses that behavior and omits the slug entirely in that mode. Since organization URLs and collision checks use the slug, organizations created with team billing disabled can no longer be addressed by their requested subdomain/slug. This unrelated condition change should be reverted unless the corresponding organization routing/storage behavior was migrated.

title: Salesforce service references Prisma without importing it
body: The newly added credential update calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this module has no `prisma` import. This fails TypeScript compilation (`Cannot find name 'prisma'`) and, if type checking is bypassed, throws a `ReferenceError` whenever the Salesforce service initializes.

title: Google refresh persists the Zod parse-result wrapper as the credential key
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a SafeParse result object (`{ success, data }`), unlike the former `googleCredentialSchema.parse` call which returned the credential payload itself. This code stores that wrapper in `Credential.key` at line 100. On the next request `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` receives `{success,data}` rather than Google token fields and rejects the credential, so a successfully refreshed Google integration becomes unusable.

title: HubSpot sync treats a Fetch Response as a HubSpot token object
body: When credential sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the result of `fetch`, i.e. a `Response`, but this caller casts it directly to `HubspotToken` and reads `expiresIn`, `accessToken`, and serializes it into the credential. Unlike the normal HubSpot SDK path, it never calls `response.json()`. Consequently synced HubSpot refreshes produce undefined/invalid token fields and can fail to save a valid credential or authenticate subsequent API calls.

title: Zoho Bigin sync uses a Fetch Response as though it were an Axios response
body: The normal refresh callback returns an Axios response with a `.data` payload, but the sync branch in `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a native `fetch` `Response`. The subsequent code reads and mutates `tokenInfo.data` without parsing the response body, so with syncing enabled it cannot obtain an access token and attempts to persist/use invalid values. In addition, the third argument is `credentialId`, which is sent as `calcomUserId`; credential IDs are not user IDs, so the remote app is asked for the wrong user's token.

title: Zoho CRM sync path never parses the remote Fetch response
body: Without syncing this code receives an Axios response and accesses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data`. With syncing enabled `refreshOAuthTokens` instead returns a native `Response`, and no `.json()` call is made before accessing `.data`. The refreshed credential therefore has no token payload and Zoho CRM calendar operations fail whenever the sync endpoint is used.

title: Salesforce refresh bypasses the configured credential-sync endpoint
body: This new refresh implementation always posts the stored refresh token and app secret directly to Salesforce rather than using `refreshOAuthTokens`. Thus Salesforce is included in the changed integrations but continues to make Cal.com the refresh-token holder/source of truth, contrary to the credential-sync feature; deployments enabling sync cannot refresh Salesforce credentials through their external app store.

title: Salesforce connection is initialized with the expired pre-refresh token
body: After obtaining and saving `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`, the connection is still constructed with `credentialKey.access_token`, which is the token that prompted the refresh. The current request therefore authenticates to Salesforce with the expired token and fails; only a later service construction that rereads the database could use the saved token.

title: Credential-sync token requests contain no authentication
body: The outbound request identifies a user solely by the predictable `calcomUserId` and app slug and sends neither the configured webhook secret nor any signature/authorization header. A self-hosted app-store endpoint has no information with which to distinguish a Cal.com refresh request from an arbitrary caller requesting another user's integration token. The documented secret is only checked on the reverse webhook and does not protect this endpoint.

title: Zoom requests a different app slug than the credential's configured app ID
body: The Zoom callback creates credentials with `appId: "zoom"`, but the refresh-sync request sends `appSlug: "zoomvideo"`. The sync API is explicitly keyed by app slug, so a source application that maps credentials by the configured app ID will not find Zoom credentials and cannot return a refreshed token.

title: Webhook credential upsert is race-prone and can create duplicate credentials
body: The handler implements an upsert as a separate `findFirst` followed by `create`, with no transaction or database uniqueness constraint. Concurrent sync webhooks for the same user and app can both observe no credential and both create one. Multiple credentials for an integration cause nondeterministic `findFirst` selection and leave stale third-party tokens in the database.

title: Salesforce service references Prisma without importing it
body: `prisma.credential.update` is called here, but this file has no `prisma` import. Type checking/building the app-store package will fail with `Cannot find name 'prisma'`, blocking the application build.

title: The fallback token schema discards every expiry field from sync responses
body: Both computed property names evaluate to the same string (`"[object Object]"`), with the latter overwriting the former; they do not define a numeric-key catch-all. Moreover, `z.object` strips unknown keys by default. When credential syncing is enabled, a response such as `{ access_token, expiry_date }` is therefore parsed down to just `access_token` (plus the fabricated refresh token below). Callers then store an undefined/invalid expiry, causing tokens to be considered expired on every request; Zoom can persist `NaN` for `expiry_date`.

title: Sync mode changes the refresh result from provider data to a Fetch Response
body: The sync branch returns the native `fetch` `Response`, while several existing callers expect their provider/axios response object directly. For example, HubSpot reads `expiresIn` and `accessToken` from the returned value, and the Zoho Bigin/CRM services read `tokenInfo.data`; those properties do not exist on a Fetch `Response`. Enabling `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` therefore makes refreshes for these integrations fail or save undefined token fields. The helper needs a normalized result contract (or all callers must explicitly parse the response consistently).

title: Zoho Bigin sends the credential ID as the Cal.com user ID
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects its third argument to be a user ID and serializes it as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId` rather than `credential.userId`. Credential primary keys are unrelated to user IDs, so the configured source application will refresh credentials for the wrong user or reject the request. If IDs happen to match another user, the returned token can be persisted onto this user's credential.

title: Zoom refresh requests use a different app slug than the installed app
body: The outbound sync payload identifies this integration as `zoomvideo`, whereas the Zoom app/credential is consistently identified as `zoom` (for example, the OAuth callback creates `appId: "zoom"`). A source application that routes refreshes by app slug will not recognize this request, so Zoom credential sync cannot refresh successfully.

title: Webex rejects the documented minimal credential-sync response
body: The shared refresh helper documents that a sync endpoint returns only an access token and expiry, but Webex bypasses the relaxed parser and validates the response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in`. Consequently, a conforming sync endpoint response is always rejected and Webex refresh fails whenever syncing is enabled.

title: Salesforce refresh bypasses the credential sync endpoint entirely
body: This newly added Salesforce refresh always posts directly to Salesforce and never calls `refreshOAuthTokens` or checks `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Thus Salesforce is one of the modified integrations for which enabling credential syncing has no effect, contrary to the feature's source-of-truth behavior.

title: Credential create/update is not atomic and can create duplicate credentials
body: The handler performs `findFirst` and then separately creates a credential if none was found. Concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no row and both create one. Since the code explicitly cannot use an upsert and there is no shown uniqueness constraint, duplicate credentials can remain; downstream integrations commonly use `findFirst`, making the selected credential nondeterministic. Use a transaction with an appropriate unique constraint/upsert or otherwise serialize this operation.

title: Salesforce service references Prisma without importing it
body: This file now calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but its imports do not include `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. TypeScript compilation of the app-store package will fail with `Cannot find name 'prisma'`, preventing this change from building.

title: The minimum sync response schema strips every expiry field
body: The computed property names here are evaluated to the literal string `"[object Object]"`; they do not create dynamic Zod properties. The second duplicate property also overwrites the first, and `z.object()` strips all unrecognized fields by default. Consequently, when credential syncing is enabled, a normal sync response such as `{ access_token, expires_in }` is parsed down to only `access_token` (plus the synthetic refresh token). Callers such as the Zoom adapter then calculate an expiry using `newTokens.expires_in`, which is undefined, producing `NaN` and potentially failing the credential update; other adapters retain stale expiry values and repeatedly refresh.

title: Google refresh stores the Zod safe-parse wrapper as the credential key
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), but this update stores that result itself as `credential.key` rather than `key.data`. This occurs for every Google token refresh, including when sync is disabled. On the next use, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` receives the wrapper instead of Google credentials and rejects it, leaving the user with an unusable Google Calendar connection.

title: HubSpot treats a fetch Response from the sync endpoint as a HubSpot token
body: The native HubSpot refresh API returns a token object directly, but `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response` whenever syncing is enabled. This code casts that Response to `HubspotToken` and immediately reads `expiresIn` and `accessToken`; both are undefined because the response body is never parsed. It then persists the Response-shaped object and sets the HubSpot client access token to undefined, so synced HubSpot credentials cannot refresh or create meetings.

title: Zoho Bigin sends the credential ID as the Cal user ID to the sync endpoint
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects its third argument to be the owning Cal user ID and serializes it as `calcomUserId`. This call passes `credentialId` instead. The external app store will therefore look up a user whose ID equals the database credential ID, usually returning no credential and, in the event of an ID collision, potentially returning another user's token.

title: Webhook credential create/update is not atomic
body: The handler performs `findFirst` followed by either `update` or `create`, with no transaction or uniqueness constraint. Concurrent deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no credential and create duplicates. Later deliveries update an arbitrary `findFirst` result while stale duplicate credentials remain eligible for use, so the app store can no longer reliably be the source of truth.

title: Team administrators are rejected by an ANDed role check
body: The authorization check requires the caller to satisfy both `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`. Team membership roles are distinct, so an administrator who is not the booking's organizer fails this condition and receives FORBIDDEN, despite the product UI treating team admins or owners as eligible (`isUserTeamAdminOrOwner`). Use an OR check so either role can manage a team booking.

title: The guest list has no server-side size limit
body: Any authenticated attendee is authorized to call this endpoint, and `guests` is an unbounded array. A caller can submit thousands of arbitrary valid addresses in one request, creating corresponding attendee records, calendar invitations, and emails; repeated calls also notify every existing attendee. This makes the endpoint an email-spam and resource-exhaustion primitive. Enforce a reasonable maximum number of guests server-side (and ideally a per-booking/event-type guest policy).

title: Attendees are persisted before calendar synchronization succeeds
body: The handler writes the new attendees to the booking before calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`. If the calendar update fails (for example, because an attendee/admin actor lacks the organizer's calendar credentials), the mutation rejects but the database still shows the guests as added, while the external calendar and notification flow were not updated. This leaves booking state inconsistent and retries can behave differently. The operation needs compensation/outbox handling or a deliberate failure strategy that does not leave the completed database mutation presented as a failed add.

title: Guest and blacklist comparisons are case-sensitive
body: Email addresses are compared directly against stored attendees and the lowercased blacklist, but input guest addresses are never normalized. A request using a different case can bypass `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` and can add a second logical copy of an existing attendee (or trigger a database uniqueness failure, depending on collation/constraints). Normalize and compare email addresses case-insensitively before filtering, persistence, and deciding which recipients are new.

title: The endpoint permits adding guests to cancelled or rejected bookings
body: Authorization is the only booking-state validation; a direct API caller who was an attendee, organizer, or team manager can add guests to a cancelled or rejected booking. The handler then creates attendee records and sends confirmed calendar/email updates for an event that will not occur. Restrict this mutation to the supported active booking statuses (and any applicable time/recurrence rules) on the server rather than relying on the dashboard action visibility.

title: Team admins and owners are incorrectly denied permission to add guests
body: The team permission check combines `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` with `&&`. A membership normally has one of these roles, so a team admin who is not the booking's assigned organizer (and an owner if the helpers are role-specific) fails this check even though the UI explicitly exposes this action to `isUserTeamAdminOrOwner`. Use `||` (or the project’s established combined-role authorization helper) so either privileged team role is accepted.

title: The API permits duplicate guest emails in a single request
body: `uniqueGuests` only filters out attendees that existed before this mutation; it never deduplicates `guests` itself. Although the dialog validates duplicates, callers can invoke the tRPC endpoint directly because the server schema has no uniqueness refinement. A request such as `["guest@example.com", "guest@example.com"]` therefore attempts to create duplicate attendee records (or fails the entire operation if a database uniqueness constraint exists), and can produce duplicate calendar/email effects. Deduplicate and normalize the input server-side, or reject duplicate input before `createMany`.

title: Attendee-initiated updates use the attendee's calendar credentials instead of the organizer's
body: The handler explicitly authorizes any existing attendee at line 52, but obtains credentials from `ctx.user` here. For an attendee adding a guest, these are the attendee's integrations, not the booking organizer's destination-calendar credentials. `updateCalendarAttendees` will consequently be unable to update the organizer's calendar (or may target an inappropriate connected calendar), after the attendee rows have already been inserted. Resolve credentials for the booking owner/calendar connection when updating the booking's calendar.

title: A calendar-update failure leaves permanently inconsistent booking state
body: The new attendees are committed to the database at lines 92-106 before the external calendar update is attempted here. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation returns an error but the database still contains the guests; retrying then filters those emails as already present and rejects the request, so the caller cannot repair the missing calendar invitation/update through this feature. Add compensation/retry handling or structure the operation so failed external synchronization is recorded and can be retried rather than treating the database write as a completed update.

title: Existing addresses in a mixed request receive a new-booking email
body: The email sender is passed the original `guests` array rather than `uniqueGuests`. If a request contains one already-attending email plus one genuinely new email, `sendAddGuestsEmails` classifies the existing attendee as a newly added guest and sends it `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a booking confirmation) even though no attendee was added for that address. Pass the filtered list of actually-created emails to ensure only new invitees receive the scheduled email.

title: Team administrators and owners are incorrectly denied access
body: The authorization check requires a user to be both a team admin and a team owner (`isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`). Those roles are distinct, so a team admin or owner who is not the booking organizer/attendee will be rejected even though the UI and variable name indicate either role should be permitted. Use an OR check (or the existing team-admin-or-owner authorization helper) so either authorized role can add guests.

title: Guest addresses are neither normalized nor deduplicated on the server
body: The API schema permits duplicate email addresses and this filter only excludes addresses already present on the booking; it does not deduplicate `guests` itself and compares addresses case-sensitively. A direct API caller can submit the same address repeatedly (or an existing/blacklisted address with different casing). Depending on the attendee database constraint this either creates duplicate attendees or makes the whole mutation fail, and casing can bypass the blacklist or create a second representation of the same mailbox. Normalize addresses and deduplicate them server-side before checking existing attendees, the blacklist, and `createMany`.

title: Database attendees are committed before the calendar update succeeds
body: New attendee rows are written before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` is called. If the calendar provider update fails, the mutation returns an error but the booking already contains the new guests; they receive no notifications and are absent from the external calendar. A retry may then reject them as existing, leaving the booking and calendar permanently out of sync. Handle/compensate for calendar failures or arrange the workflow so a failed external update does not leave silently committed attendee data.

title: Attendee-initiated updates use the attendee's calendar credentials instead of the organizer's
body: The endpoint explicitly authorizes an existing attendee to add guests, but constructs `EventManager` using `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. For an attendee request those credentials belong to the attendee, not the booking organizer whose destination calendar and event references need updating. The handler already loads `booking.user.credentials` but does not use them. Consequently attendee-added guests commonly fail to update the organizer calendar (or attempt an update with an unrelated account); construct the manager with the booking organizer's credentials for this operation.

title: Email classification uses unfiltered requested guests rather than guests actually added
body: Only `uniqueGuests` are persisted, but email sending receives the original `guests` array. For example, when a request contains one existing attendee and one new address, no row is created for the existing attendee, yet `sendAddGuestsEmails` treats that attendee as a newly added guest and sends them an `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a booking confirmation) rather than the guests-added update. Pass the actual added addresses (`uniqueGuests`, after normalization) to the mailer.

title: The mutation permits adding attendees to cancelled or rejected bookings
body: After locating and authorizing the booking, the handler does not validate its status or whether it is still actionable. A caller can invoke this authenticated endpoint directly for a cancelled or rejected booking, creating attendee rows, updating the calendar, and emailing attendees that guests were added to an event that is no longer occurring. Reject non-active booking statuses (and define the intended past-event policy) before modifying attendees.

title: Retry-limit deletion is not restricted to SMS reminders
body: The second branch of this `OR` filters only on `retryCount`, so any `WorkflowReminder` method (including EMAIL or WHATSAPP) with a count above one will be deleted by the SMS scheduling cron. The retry cleanup condition should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or the outer query should constrain the method) so this endpoint cannot remove reminders owned by other delivery mechanisms.

title: The condition permits a third scheduling attempt after two failures
body: A reminder starts at `retryCount = 0`; its first and second failed attempts set the count to 1 and 2. On the next cron run `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` is evaluated only before scheduling, so the row is deleted then, but it will already have been eligible for the second failure? More specifically, after the first failure it is retried; after the second failure it becomes 2 and is removed on the following run. This produces two attempts, but the cleanup timing leaves a persisted failed reminder. If the intended contract is to delete immediately after the second failed scheduling attempt, the failure update should delete at the limit or use a transaction/conditional operation. Otherwise the stated behavior is delayed until the next cron execution and failed rows remain available to other workers.

title: Retry count updates can lose increments under overlapping cron runs
body: The handler reads `reminder.retryCount` and later writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`. Two concurrent cron invocations can both select the same unscheduled reminder, both fail to schedule it, and both write the same value (for example, 1). This loses one failure, prevents the retry limit from being reached reliably, and both invocations can issue duplicate provider scheduling calls. Use an atomic database increment and claim/conditionally update the reminder before scheduling to ensure only one worker processes a reminder.

title: Reminders with no recipient or generated message still retry forever
body: Retry count is incremented only when `scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value or throws. If `sendTo` is empty (for example, an attendee has no SMS number) or template generation leaves `message` empty, this condition is skipped without marking the reminder scheduled, failed, or exhausted. The reminder therefore remains in every cron query until its scheduled date, retaining the infinite retry behavior this change is intended to stop. Treat an unsendable reminder as a failed attempt or explicitly delete/cancel it.

title: Retry cleanup is not restricted to SMS reminders
body: The new `retryCount > 1` branch is an OR condition without a `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` constraint. Consequently, any non-SMS `WorkflowReminder` (for example, email or WhatsApp) whose retryCount exceeds one will be permanently deleted by this SMS cron endpoint, even though this job neither schedules nor owns those reminder types. Keep the retry threshold inside an SMS-scoped condition so this destructive cleanup cannot remove unrelated workflow reminder records.

title: Retry counts can be lost when cron executions overlap
body: The retry value is read in `findMany` and then written back as `reminder.retryCount + 1`. If two authorized cron invocations process the same unscheduled reminder concurrently, both can read (for example) 0 and both write 1 after failures. The row will then receive an extra retry despite two failed scheduling attempts, so the intended two-attempt limit is not enforced (and concurrent executions can continue submitting duplicate provider requests). Use an atomic database increment and/or atomically claim the reminder before scheduling; the catch-path update at line 195 has the same lost-update issue.

title: Reminders with no sendable message or recipient never consume retries
body: RetryCount is incremented only after `scheduleSMS` returns false or throws. When `message` is empty/null or `sendTo` is absent, the condition at this line is skipped entirely, leaving the reminder `scheduled: false` and `retryCount` unchanged. The cron will select and reprocess that permanently unsendable reminder on every run until its scheduled date, which preserves the retry loop this change is intended to stop. Mark these cases as failed attempts (or delete/cancel them explicitly) so they are bounded by the same retry policy.

title: Retry cleanup is not restricted to SMS reminders
body: The new `retryCount > 1` branch is a top-level OR condition with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` restriction. Consequently, any EMAIL or WHATSAPP `WorkflowReminder` whose retryCount is greater than one will be permanently deleted by this SMS cron endpoint, even though this retry policy is intended only for SMS. Scope the retry-count predicate to SMS reminders (and, if appropriate, unscheduled reminders) so this job cannot remove reminders owned by other delivery paths.

title: Reminders with no renderable message or recipient never consume retries
body: `retryCount` is only incremented after `scheduleSMS` returns false or throws. If `sendTo` is absent (possible because both the booking SMS number and workflow step recipient are optional) or message generation results in an empty value, this condition is skipped entirely. The reminder remains `scheduled: false` and is fetched on every cron run until its date passes, which leaves a common unsendable-SMS case unfixed by the retry cap. Treat an unusable recipient/message as a failed scheduling attempt, or delete/mark the reminder as unsendable.

title: Retry count updates can lose increments when cron invocations overlap
body: The handler reads `reminder.retryCount` and writes `reminder.retryCount + 1` rather than using an atomic database increment. Two overlapping cron requests can both read 0, both fail scheduling, and both write 1; the reminder then survives another run despite two failed attempts. Overlapping invocations are also especially plausible while a reminder remains unscheduled. Use Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` update (and consider claiming the reminder/conditional updates to avoid concurrent scheduling) so the deletion threshold reflects actual failures.

title: The public findMany API was removed without a replacement query API
body: This change deletes `InsightsBookingService.findMany`, which previously executed the authorized `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany` query and accepted normal Prisma findMany arguments. The only replacement is `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a SQL fragment and requires every caller to reimplement query execution, selection, pagination, ordering, and safe composition. Existing consumers invoking `service.findMany(...)` will fail to compile (or fail at runtime for untyped consumers), and no caller migrations are included in this PR. Preserve a compatible execution method or update all consumers as part of the same change.

title: The public findMany API was removed without a replacement query API
body: This change deletes `findMany`, which previously applied authorization and filter conditions and returned records from `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized`. `getBaseConditions` only returns a SQL fragment; it does not accept or apply the caller's `findMany` arguments, perform the query, or provide an equivalent typed result API. Existing consumers of the exported `InsightsBookingService` that call `findMany` will fail to compile/runtime, and consumers migrated only to this method must reimplement query construction and risk omitting authorization conditions. Preserve `findMany` or introduce an equivalent supported raw-query method and migrate all callers atomically.

title: Team and organization raw authorization predicates are never executed against the database
body: The team and org tests only compare `Prisma.Sql` objects constructed by the service with `Prisma.Sql` objects constructed in the expectation. They do not execute the predicates. The sole `$queryRaw` test at lines 481-484 uses user scope, which has neither the `ANY(${...})` array bindings nor the OR branches used by team/org authorization. Consequently, PostgreSQL serialization/type errors for array parameters, SQL precedence issues, or predicates that return unauthorized/missing bookings in the team and org scopes can pass this suite. Add database-backed tests for both scopes, including matching and non-matching team and member bookings.

title: Removing `findMany` breaks the exported service API
body: `findMany` was the service's data-access API and applied the authorization and filter predicates together with caller-provided `findMany` arguments. This change removes it and exposes only a raw SQL fragment, while no dependent call sites are migrated in this PR. Existing consumers of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` will fail to compile/run, and replacement callers must now independently choose the correct table/view and reimplement Prisma query features such as selection, ordering, pagination, and additional `where` clauses. Preserve a compatible query method or update all consumers as part of this change.

title: Deleting cache does not refresh the connected-calendars cache status
body: The delete mutation only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback. This component is also rendered with no guarantee that callback invalidates/refetches `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (and it may be absent), unlike the disconnect mutation which explicitly invalidates its dependent queries. Consequently, after a successful deletion the UI continues to receive/render the old `cacheUpdatedAt`, still reporting cached data and offering the delete action until an unrelated refresh or reload. Invalidate or update the connectedCalendars query when the delete mutation settles successfully.

title: Webhook setup script uses a macOS-only sed invocation
body: `sed -i '' -E` is BSD/macOS syntax. On Linux, where GNU sed treats the empty string differently, this command fails after Tunnelmole has been started, so `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is not updated and local webhook testing cannot work as advertised. Use a portable file-replacement approach or branch on the installed sed implementation.

title: Deleting cache does not invalidate the displayed calendar cache status
body: The delete-cache mutation only invokes the optional onSuccess callback. Unlike the disconnect mutation, it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. In this wrapper `onChanged` is optional, so after a successful deletion the active query can retain its previous `cacheUpdatedAt` indefinitely (window-focus refetch is disabled), continuing to show cache status and the delete action for data that no longer exists. Invalidate or refetch `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` when the deletion settles.

title: The cron development command relies on an undeclared, unpinned tsx executable
body: `tsx` is not declared in this workspace's dependencies or devDependencies, so `npx tsx` must resolve/download whatever current registry version is available when the command is run (and can fail in offline/CI or non-interactive environments). This makes `yarn dev:cron` non-reproducible and can execute an unexpected version. Add a pinned `tsx` dependency and invoke its workspace binary (or use the existing declared runner).

title: The env-file update command fails on GNU/Linux sed
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` uses BSD/macOS `sed` syntax. On GNU sed, which is used by typical Linux development and CI environments, the separated empty argument is treated as an input filename (or otherwise causes an error), so an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is not updated. Use a portable temporary-file replacement or select the `sed -i` form based on the platform.

title: Deleting cache does not invalidate the connected-calendars query
body: The delete-cache mutation only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback. Unlike the disconnect mutation below it, it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, which is the query supplying `cacheUpdatedAt`. When this component is used without a callback that explicitly refetches that query, a successful deletion leaves the UI showing the old cache timestamp and the delete action until a manual reload. Invalidate the connected-calendars query on mutation settlement/success (and optionally integrations if needed).

title: Cache timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded US locale
body: The component uses `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US")` even though its surrounding labels are localized through `useLocale`. Users with non-US locales will always receive US date ordering and formatting for the cache status, which conflicts with the localized UI. Format using the active application/user locale instead of a literal `en-US`.

title: Webhook helper cannot update env files on GNU/Linux sed
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed, commonly used on Linux development environments and CI, the separate empty argument is not handled as the intended backup suffix and the command fails rather than updating `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL`. Use a portable conditional for BSD versus GNU sed, or rewrite the file without relying on platform-specific `sed -i` behavior.

title: Past-due cleanup drops cancelled reminders before they are cancelled at SendGrid
body: The handler deletes every email reminder whose scheduledDate is in the past before querying and cancelling `cancelled` reminders. If a booking is cancelled shortly before its reminder and the next 15-minute cron invocation occurs after the reminder's send time, this deletion removes the only cancellation record and no SendGrid cancellation request is made. The already scheduled SendGrid email can therefore still be delivered, which is precisely the case this change is intended to prevent. Cancelled reminders must be handled before cleanup, and cancellation should not depend on a cron execution occurring before `sendAt`.

title: Standard reschedules still immediately consume SendGrid cancellation slots
body: The reschedule flow passes `true` for `immediateDelete`, causing `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` to call SendGrid immediately rather than mark the reminder as cancelled for the cron-based cleanup. This preserves the old behavior that accumulates SendGrid scheduled-send cancellations and hits the provider's 100 pending-cancellation limit during reschedules. Errors are swallowed by the helper and no `cancelled` flag is set as a fallback, so reminders whose immediate cancellation is rejected will still be sent.

title: The cron's SendGrid client is never authenticated
body: This module configures only `sgMail` with `sgMail.setApiKey`; it never calls `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` for the separately imported `@sendgrid/client` instance. The new cancellation request at this line uses that client directly, so it will be sent without SendGrid authorization and fail. The catch only logs the failure, leaving the reminder in the database and allowing the email to be sent.

title: Reminder cancellation writes are not awaited before completing booking cancellation
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async, but the nested `forEach` discards their promises. Consequently the booking cancellation request can complete while the email reminder's `cancelled` update or SMS cancellation/delete is still pending. In a serverless/request-scoped runtime those operations can be interrupted after the response, and the cron can observe the reminder before it is marked, resulting in a reminder being sent for a cancelled booking. Collect and await these operations (and apply the same treatment in the other modified cancellation paths).

title: Cancellations can wait until after the reminder has been sent
body: Cancelled email reminders are only submitted to SendGrid when this 15-minute cron next runs and the reminder is within the next hour. For example, if a reminder is due in five minutes and the booking is cancelled immediately after a cron run, no cancellation request is made for up to 15 minutes, so SendGrid can deliver the reminder at its scheduled time. This leaves the primary cancelled-booking case unfixed for reminders cancelled shortly before they are due; cancellation needs to be performed promptly enough to beat the send time (or the scheduling job needs to run with a sufficiently tight guarantee).

title: Expired cancelled reminders are deleted without cancelling their SendGrid send
body: The expired-reminder cleanup runs before the new cancellation loop and deletes every email reminder whose scheduledDate is at or before now, including rows marked cancelled. If the cron is late or SendGrid has not yet processed a send scheduled for that timestamp, the local record is removed and the later cancellation pass can no longer submit the required SendGrid cancellation. The scheduled email can consequently still be delivered, and there is no remaining row to retry cancellation. Cancelled reminders should be handled/cancelled before generic expiry cleanup, and failed cancellations should remain retryable.

title: The raw SendGrid client used for cancellation is never authenticated
body: This handler only calls `sgMail.setApiKey`, but the newly added cancellation path uses the separately imported `@sendgrid/client` instance at line 57. `sgMail` configures its own client instance and does not configure this exported raw client. Consequently the POST to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` will be unauthorized/fail, the catch block will swallow the error, and the cancelled reminders will remain scheduled in SendGrid and still be delivered. Configure this client with `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` before making raw client requests.

title: Normal reschedules still create immediate SendGrid cancellation entries
body: The primary booking-reschedule flow passes `true` as `immediateDelete`, causing `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` to immediately POST `status: "cancel"` to SendGrid instead of marking the reminder as cancelled for the cron job. These cancelled scheduled-send entries remain counted by SendGrid until their send date, which is the capacity limit this PR is intended to avoid; after 100 pending cancellations, later reschedules can again fail to cancel and send stale reminders. This path should use the deferred cancellation mechanism (and preserve the reminder row for the cron), rather than `immediateDelete`.

title: One failed cancellation prevents all later reminders from being cancelled
body: All SendGrid cancellations are performed inside one try block. If `client.request` fails for any reminder, execution exits the loop immediately and no later reminders are cancelled during that run. Since the initial cleanup deletes email reminder rows once their scheduled date has passed, reminders skipped near their send time can lose their cancellation marker without ever having been cancelled at SendGrid, allowing them to be delivered. Handle failures per reminder (and retain failed rows for retry) rather than aborting the entire batch.

title: Reminder cancellation writes are fired without awaiting completion
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async, but are invoked from `forEach` and their promises are discarded. The cancellation handler can return successfully before the email reminder has been marked `cancelled` (or an unscheduled/SMS reminder has been deleted). In a serverless/request-scoped runtime those unawaited operations may be interrupted after the response, leaving reminders active and allowing cancelled-booking notifications to send. Collect and await these promises before completing the handler.

title: Recurring calendar deletions are raced against the final cleanup wait
body: The async `forEach` is not awaited. Since each callback now awaits `getCalendar()` before pushing its deletion promise into `apiDeletes`, execution can reach the later `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` while `apiDeletes` is still empty or incomplete. The cancellation request can therefore finish (and in a serverless worker be terminated) without deleting some recurring events from external calendars, and import/delete failures become unhandled rejections. Build and await a `Promise.all` for these callbacks before relying on `apiDeletes`.

title: Reschedule cleanup launches unobserved async calendar deletions
body: Changing this callback to `async` without replacing `forEach` with an awaited `Promise.all` means the new `await getCalendar()` and the subsequent `deleteEvent()` are detached from `Reschedule`. The surrounding `try/catch` does not catch rejections from async `forEach` callbacks, so a failed dynamic import or external calendar deletion is unhandled while the function continues to send the reschedule email and return success. Await the mapped cleanup operations inside the try block.

title: Reschedule cleanup launches unobserved async calendar deletions
body: Changing this callback to `async` without replacing `forEach` with an awaited `Promise.all` means the new `await getCalendar()` and the subsequent `deleteEvent()` are detached from `Reschedule`. The surrounding `try/catch` does not catch rejections from async `forEach` callbacks, so a failed dynamic import or external calendar deletion is unhandled while the function continues to send the reschedule email and return success. Await the mapped cleanup operations inside the try block.

title: Request-reschedule returns before asynchronously loaded integrations are deleted
body: The async callback passed to `forEach` is never awaited. With the new asynchronous `getCalendar`, this mutation marks the booking cancelled and sends the reschedule email before the calendar module has necessarily loaded or its event deletion has run; failures are also unhandled. This can leave the old external calendar/video meeting active even though the booking is cancelled. Collect the callback promises with `map` and await `Promise.all` before completing the mutation.

title: Calendar/video deletion promises are detached during rescheduling
body: Using `forEach(async ...)` discards every callback promise. Because `getCalendar` now always awaits a dynamic-import promise before `deleteEvent` is invoked, this function proceeds to send the reschedule email and returns without waiting for deletion to start or finish. Rejections from either the import or the provider deletion also bypass the surrounding `try/catch` and can become unhandled rejections. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (or an awaited `for...of`) so cancellation is completed and failures are handled before the operation finishes.

title: Calendar/video deletion promises are detached during rescheduling
body: Using `forEach(async ...)` discards every callback promise. Since `getCalendar` now yields at the dynamic import, the reschedule flow can return and send its email before calendar deletion has even been invoked; import/provider failures are not caught by the surrounding `try/catch` and may be unhandled. Await a mapped `Promise.all` or use an awaited loop to ensure these integration cancellations run deterministically and errors are handled.

title: Reschedule mutation does not await dynamic calendar deletion
body: The async callback passed to `forEach` is not awaited. With the new `await getCalendar(...)`, every calendar deletion is deferred past the callback's first await, while the mutation immediately sends the reschedule email and can complete successfully. A failed dynamic import or `deleteEvent` call is also detached from the mutation and has no error handler. Replace this with an awaited `Promise.all` over the filtered references (and handle its errors as appropriate).

title: Recurring calendar deletions are no longer included in the awaited work
body: The async callback passed to `forEach` is not awaited. Each callback now suspends at `await getCalendar(credential)`, while the handler continues to build and eventually awaits `Promise.all(apiDeletes)` at line 652. At that point the callbacks commonly have not yet pushed any delete promises into `apiDeletes`, so a recurring cancellation can complete and delete booking references before its external calendar events are deleted. Rejections from imports or deletions are also detached from the handler. Build an array of promises (or use `Promise.all` over credentials/bookings) and await it before proceeding.

title: Reschedule endpoint fires calendar/video cleanup in an unawaited async forEach
body: Changing this callback to `async` makes every calendar deletion wait for module loading, but `forEach` discards the resulting promises. The mutation sends the reschedule email and returns without waiting for calendar/video cleanup, and failures from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` become unhandled promise rejections rather than an endpoint error/logged failure. Replace the `forEach` with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` (with explicit per-operation error handling as appropriate).

title: Vital reschedule cleanup is detached from the enclosing error handling
body: `forEach(async ...)` does not await its callbacks. Consequently the surrounding `try/catch` only covers scheduling the callbacks; an import failure or `deleteEvent` failure is not caught, and the reschedule flow continues to email/return before cleanup is complete. Since `getCalendar` now always introduces an await point, this is reliably asynchronous rather than merely an unawaited provider deletion. Collect and await the callback promises with `Promise.all`.

title: WipeMyCal reschedule cleanup is detached from the enclosing error handling
body: The new async `forEach` callback is never awaited. Calendar loading and deletion can still be pending when this function sends email and returns, while errors from either operation bypass the surrounding `try/catch` and can become unhandled rejections. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or an awaited loop so cleanup completion and failures are handled by this flow.

title: Zero-length date overrides are never recognized as equal
body: `dayjs(...) === dayjs(...)` compares two distinct Dayjs object references, so it is always false even when `start` and `end` represent the same instant. A zero-length override, which represents an unavailable date/time, therefore falls through to the range checks; notably the slot beginning exactly at the override instant is treated as available. This allows bookings during an explicitly blocked override. Compare the instants with `isSame` (or timestamps) instead.

title: Fixed hosts with multiple working-hour ranges are checked as an intersection
body: The working-hours check returns unavailable as soon as the slot is outside any matching range because it uses `find` with an out-of-range predicate. For a common split schedule such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a 10:00 slot is outside the second range and a 14:00 slot is outside the first, so every slot is rejected for the fixed host. The check must instead accept a slot if it fits at least one applicable working-hour range.

title: Working-hours validation ignores the event duration
body: Both `start` and `end` are calculated from `slotStartTime`, so the new fixed-host working-hours validation only verifies that the slot start is before the end of availability. For example, a 60-minute event starting at 16:30 is accepted for a host whose hours end at 17:00. This can expose round-robin slots that the fixed host cannot actually attend; `end` needs to include `eventLength`.

title: Multiple date-override ranges on one day are treated as mutually exclusive
body: The callback passed to `dateOverrides.find` returns true when a slot is outside any one override range. Consequently, if a host has two availability override windows on the same date, a slot inside the first window is outside the second and is rejected. Date override ranges should be combined as a union: the slot should be accepted when it fits at least one override range, and rejected only when it fits none.

title: No regression test covers the fixed-host round-robin behavior claimed by this PR
body: The added test only exercises a single-host event's override under two nearby time zones. It does not create a ROUND_ROBIN event with a fixed host and a loose host, nor verify that an override or normal fixed-host availability removes otherwise available loose-host slots. The new `checkIfIsAvailable` path is only used for that host filtering and currently has range-handling defects that this missing scenario would have caught.

title: Zero-length date overrides are never recognized as such
body: The code compares two newly-created Dayjs objects with `===`, which compares object identity and is always false even when `date.start` and `date.end` represent the same instant. Consequently, the special handling for a zero-length/full-day override never executes. Such an override can leave a slot at its boundary available instead of marking the host unavailable, allowing a booking during an intended day off. Compare the timestamps (for example with `isSame`) instead.

title: Fixed-host working-hours validation ignores the event duration
body: `end` is calculated from `slotStartTime` exactly as `start` is, so the condition only verifies that the slot starts before `workingHour.endTime`; it never verifies that the event ends before it. For round-robin events with a fixed host, a slot generated from a loose host's availability can therefore be retained even though the fixed host's shift ends partway through the event (for example, a 60-minute event starting at 09:30 with the fixed host available only until 10:00). The end value must include `eventLength` and be checked against the fixed host's availability.

title: Multiple override windows on one day are treated as an intersection
body: The `find` callback returns `true` when a slot is outside any individual override window, and the outer code immediately rejects the slot. If a host has two availability override ranges on the same date, a slot inside the first range is necessarily outside the second range and is rejected. This makes all slots unavailable whenever date overrides contain multiple separate windows, rather than accepting slots covered by at least one window. The logic should first collect the overrides for the date and accept a slot if it fits within any applicable override range.

title: Fixed-host override validation accepts slots that extend outside the override
body: The override check only rejects a slot when it ends at/before the override start or starts strictly after the override end. A slot that starts inside the override but ends after it, or starts exactly at the override end, falls through and is treated as available. For example, with a fixed host override of 10:00-11:00 and a 60-minute event, an 10:30 or 11:00 slot can be returned for a round-robin event even though the fixed host is unavailable for part or all of it. The check must require the entire slot to be within the override interval, including rejecting equality at the end boundary.

title: Empty date overrides are compared by object identity and do not block their start slot
body: `dayjs(...) === dayjs(...)` compares two distinct Dayjs objects by reference, so this condition is always false even when `date.start` and `date.end` represent the same instant. Empty/zero-length date overrides (used to represent no availability) therefore fall through; the slot beginning exactly at that instant is considered available because neither subsequent strict boundary check matches it. Compare the instants with `isSame` (or timestamps) and reject the override date as unavailable.

title: Override selection ignores timezone-driven date changes
body: Overrides are selected by comparing the unadjusted UTC-encoded `override.start` date to the invitee day, but their times are subsequently shifted by the organizer/invitee offset. When that shift crosses midnight, the override is applied to a different invitee calendar day than the one used by this filter, so it is omitted entirely. For example, an early-morning Asia/Kolkata override can correspond to the prior calendar day for an America/New_York attendee; requesting that attendee day will return regular availability instead of the override. Filter based on the override interval after converting it to the invitee timezone (and account for intervals overlapping the day).

title: Working-hours validation rejects valid slots for split schedules
body: The code uses `workingHours.find` to find any working-hours interval that does not contain the slot, rather than confirming that at least one interval contains it. With a normal split schedule such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a 14:00 slot is rejected as soon as the first interval is examined, even though it is valid in the second interval. This can hide otherwise bookable round-robin slots for fixed hosts. The validation should accept when any same-day interval fully contains the slot, and reject only when none do.

title: Migration crashes when no persisted embed_category setting exists
body: The migration unconditionally indexes `[0]['id']` from the `embed_category` query. Site settings that retain their default are commonly not persisted in `site_settings`, and new installs also have no legacy `embed_category` row, so this query can return no rows and raise before the fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` is reached. This prevents the database migration from completing. Handle an empty result before reading the ID and then use the uncategorized fallback.

title: Legacy URL-form hosts are copied without normalization and stop matching
body: The migration inserts each legacy host string directly, bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s normalization callback. The previous setting accepted values such as `http://discourse.org` and URLs with paths, but `record_for_host` later compares the stored `host` column directly against `URI(referer).host` (for example, `discourse.org`). Consequently every migrated host configured with a scheme or path will no longer be allowed, disabling embeds and retrieval for those existing installations. Normalize each migrated host before insertion (and use bound inserts rather than SQL interpolation).

title: Allowed hosts containing an allowed port can never match
body: Validation explicitly accepts hosts with ports (for example `example.com:8443`), and the normalization callback preserves that port. However, `URI(host).host` returns only `example.com`, while this query compares it to the stored `example.com:8443`, so `host_allowed?` always returns false for such a record. Either reject ports if they are unsupported or normalize/query the stored value consistently with URI parsing.

title: Duplicate hosts can route embeds to an arbitrary category
body: There is no uniqueness validation or database unique index for `host`, while `record_for_host` resolves a host using `where(...).first` without ordering. Staff can create the same host more than once with different category assignments, after which imported embeds are assigned according to whichever duplicate the database happens to return. Enforce case-insensitive uniqueness (ideally with a matching database index) so each host has one deterministic category relationship.

title: Blank host submissions raise instead of returning a validation error
body: The `before_validation` callback calls `sub!` on `self.host` unconditionally. A create or update request missing `embeddable_host[host]` therefore raises `NoMethodError` before `validates_format_of` can report an invalid record, producing a 500 response from the admin endpoint. Guard the normalization callback for a nil host so malformed requests receive the normal validation error.

title: Migration crashes when no configured embed category exists
body: The query result is indexed unconditionally with `[0]['id']`. On installations where `embed_category` is still its default/blank value (or no site_settings row exists for it), the join produces no rows and `[0]` is nil, raising `NoMethodError` before the fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` can run. This makes the migration fail for the normal configuration it is supposed to migrate.

title: Legacy host entries are inserted without normalization and stop matching requests
body: The migration inserts old `embeddable_hosts` values through raw SQL, bypassing EmbeddableHost's `before_validation` normalization. The previous setting accepted entries such as `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234` (and existing tests cover those forms), but the new lookup compares `URI(referer).host` (for example, `discourse.org`) against the stored host string. Consequently those migrated hosts no longer authorize embeds or retrievals after upgrade. Normalize each legacy value before insertion (and safely quote/bind it) so the persisted value is just the hostname.

title: Blank host submissions raise instead of producing a validation error
body: The validation callback unconditionally calls `self.host.sub!`, so creating an EmbeddableHost with a missing host causes `undefined method sub! for nil:NilClass`. This is reachable through the new admin create API by submitting an empty `embeddable_host` payload, yielding a 500 rather than the model's normal invalid-record response. Guard the normalization for nil/blank values and add a presence validation.

title: Update and delete nonexistent hosts return server errors
body: Both `update` and `destroy` use `where(...).first` and immediately dereference the result. For an unknown ID, update passes nil to `save_host` and destroy calls `nil.destroy`, producing a 500 response instead of a 404. The admin client or any API caller can encounter this after a concurrent deletion; use `find_by` with an explicit not-found response (or `find`) before operating on the record.

title: Valid modern domain names cannot be added as embeddable hosts
body: The hostname validation limits the final label to 2 through 5 characters. Valid domains with longer TLDs, such as `example.museum`, `example.travel`, or `example.technology`, are rejected by the new admin UI/API and therefore cannot be configured for embedding. The previous host-list behavior did not impose this TLD-length restriction; use URI/hostname validation that permits valid TLD lengths.

title: Migration crashes when the legacy embed_category setting was never persisted
body: The migration unconditionally indexes the first row returned by the `embed_category` query (`...[0]['id']`). Site settings with their default value are not necessarily stored in `site_settings`, so a deployment that configured allowed hosts but left the category at its default has no `embed_category` row. In that common case `[0]` is nil and the migration aborts before it can fall back to Uncategorized. Handle an empty result before indexing it (and likewise make the fallback query robust).

title: Legacy hosts are copied without normalization and stop matching requests
body: The old setting accepted values such as `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/path` (the existing tests explicitly cover those forms), but this migration inserts those strings verbatim. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` subsequently extracts only the request hostname and compares it to the stored `host`, so a migrated row containing a scheme or path can never authorize that host. Existing embedding installations using those supported legacy formats will begin rejecting embeds and topic retrievals after migration. Normalize each legacy value to its hostname before inserting it.

title: Duplicate host mappings make the destination category nondeterministic
body: There is no uniqueness validation or database unique index on `host`, while the admin UI/API permits creating multiple rows for the same host. `record_for_host` uses `.first` with no ordering and `TopicEmbed.import` uses that record's category, so duplicate entries for one hostname can route imported posts to an arbitrary category depending on database query order. Enforce a case-insensitive unique host constraint (and clean/deduplicate migration input) so each hostname has one unambiguous mapping.

title: Updates and deletes of nonexistent hosts raise 500 errors
body: `update` and `destroy` use `where(...).first` and immediately call `save_host` or `destroy` without checking whether a row was found. A stale admin page or request for an unknown ID therefore raises `NoMethodError` instead of returning a normal 404/not-found response. Use `find`/`find_by!` or explicitly render a not-found error before dereferencing the record.

title: The existing four-dimension `downsize` API has been removed by Ruby method redefinition
body: Ruby does not overload methods. The new definition at line 149 replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition, so callers using the previously supported width/height form now receive `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments`. The preceding definition is therefore dead code. Keep a single implementation that accepts both forms (or update all existing callers and intentionally change the contract).

title: Client-side upload validation no longer honors configured attachment and image limits
body: This replaces `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` with a hard-coded 10 MB limit for every upload type. Sites with a smaller attachment limit will now let users select files that the server subsequently rejects, and sites configured to allow files larger than 10 MB will have those uploads blocked in the browser. Automatic image reduction does not justify applying a fixed image-sized limit to non-image attachments; retain the configured limit for attachments and make any larger-image allowance explicit and consistent with server behavior.

title: Image conversion is invoked with the same input and output path
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` is called with `tempfile.path` for both `from` and `to`. The generated `convert`/`gifsicle` command is therefore asked to overwrite its input while reading it; these tools can reject identical input/output files or truncate/corrupt the source depending on format/version. As a result, oversized uploads will commonly fail to be reduced (and may leave an invalid tempfile) before `Upload.create_for` runs. Write to a separate tempfile, verify conversion succeeded, then replace the original only after success.

title: The new downsize overload removes the existing five-argument API
body: Ruby does not support method overloading. Defining `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` here replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition entirely. Any existing caller using the previously supported width/height form now receives `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments`, breaking thumbnail/image-processing callers outside this diff. Preserve both calling conventions with a single variadic method or use a differently named helper.

title: Client-side upload validation now ignores configured per-type limits
body: The upload validator formerly used `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` according to `type`; it now accepts every file up to a hard-coded 10 MB. This means attachments above a site's configured attachment limit are sent only to be rejected by the server, while sites configured to permit files larger than 10 MB are rejected in the browser. The automatic-reduction exception should be limited to images and the configured attachment limit must remain enforced.

title: 413 errors report a hard-coded limit rather than the site limit
body: The error shown for a server-side 413 always says 10 MB, even when the server/proxy rejected the upload because the site's configured image or attachment limit is different. This gives users an incorrect actionable limit and is inconsistent with the server configuration.

title: The new destructive upload transformation has no coverage
body: There are no tests for the new upload-time resize path, including successful reduction below `max_image_size_kb`, conversion failure handling, animated GIF handling, and preserving normal attachment limits. This is particularly important because the implementation mutates the uploaded tempfile before persistence and because the current same-path conversion call can fail silently before the upload validation response.

title: The new overload replaces the existing four-dimension downsize API
body: Ruby does not overload methods by arity. Defining `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` here replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition, rather than adding a second accepted signature. Any existing caller using the formerly supported width/height form will now raise `ArgumentError` (five arguments supplied to a method accepting three or four), breaking thumbnail/image-processing callers outside this diff.

title: Five fixed 80% reductions cannot ensure the upload meets the configured maximum
body: The reduction loop is capped at five iterations and each iteration only reduces dimensions to 80%, so a 10 MiB image is still roughly 3.3 MiB after all five attempts (and may compress even less effectively depending on image contents). Sites configured with a lower `max_image_size_kb` will still have the upload rejected by `Upload.create_for`, despite this path claiming to automatically reduce images to the allowed size. The resize ratio/iteration strategy needs to be based on the configured target or continue until the target is reached with a safe termination condition.

title: Client-side validation now ignores both configured image and attachment limits
body: Replacing `max_<type>_size_kb` with a hard-coded 10 MiB limit means attachments are now accepted by the browser even when `max_attachment_size_kb` is much smaller, only to fail on the server later. It also prevents clients from uploading images above 10 MiB when an administrator has configured a larger image limit. The larger pre-processing allowance should be limited to images that can actually be downsized; attachments must continue to use their configured limit.

title: A GET request changes a user's notification state
body: The `unsubscribe` action is exposed as a GET route and explicitly skips the XHR/CSRF protection, but it writes `TopicUser.notification_level`. Any third-party page can cause a logged-in user's browser to request a known `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` URL (for example via an image), muting or changing that user's topic notifications without consent. Link scanners and prefetchers can also trigger the mutation. Make the state change a CSRF-protected non-GET request, or use a purpose-bound signed unsubscribe token that is safe to consume from an email link.

title: The unsubscribe link does not reliably unsubscribe watched/tracked users
body: For notification levels above `regular`, following the email's “stop receiving notifications” link changes the level only to `regular`, not `muted`. Regular users can still receive topic notifications such as replies or mentions, so the link's stated result is not achieved. It also makes the outcome dependent on the current level: a second invocation changes regular to muted, while an initial invocation for a watcher does not. Set the intended unsubscribed state directly (normally `muted`) so the operation is idempotent.

title: Directly saving TopicUser bypasses notification-change bookkeeping
body: This action mutates and saves the TopicUser row directly instead of using `TopicUser.change`, which is the established path for notification-level changes. As a result it does not set `notifications_changed_at`, does not mark `notifications_reason_id` as `user_changed`, and does not publish the MessageBus notification-level update. In particular, a row whose reason remains nil may subsequently be auto-promoted back to tracking by `update_last_read`, undoing the unsubscribe; active clients can also continue to display stale notification state. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` rather than assigning and saving the record.

title: Unsubscribe state is changed through a cross-site GET request
body: The new `unsubscribe` action changes `TopicUser.notification_level` on a GET route, and the action is explicitly excluded from the XHR check. GET requests are not protected by Rails CSRF tokens, so any third-party page can cause a logged-in visitor's browser to request `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` and silently alter that visitor's topic notification state. This should be a CSRF-protected non-GET action (with the email link leading to a confirmation page), or use a purpose-specific signed unsubscribe token.

title: Direct TopicUser save does not record this as a user-selected notification level
body: The action updates and saves the `TopicUser` record directly instead of using `TopicUser.change`, which is the normal notification-level update path. Consequently it leaves `notifications_reason_id` and `notifications_changed_at` unchanged. In particular, a topic-user row whose reason is still nil can subsequently satisfy `TopicUser.auto_track`'s `notifications_reason_id: nil` check and be automatically changed back to tracking, undoing a user's mute/unsubscribe choice. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` so the change is marked with the `user_changed` reason and published consistently.

title: Unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change and can be undone by auto-tracking
body: The action writes `notification_level` directly and leaves `notifications_reason_id` nil for topic-user records created by ordinary visits. `TopicUser.update_last_read` treats a nil reason as eligible for automatic promotion to `tracking`; therefore, after this endpoint mutes such a topic, a later read that crosses the auto-track threshold can silently change it back to tracking and resume topic email notifications. Use the notification-state update path (or explicitly persist a user-changed reason and timestamp) rather than directly saving the record. The direct save also omits the MessageBus notification used to synchronize other open clients.

title: A GET request changes a user's notification preference
body: `unsubscribe` mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` in response to a GET request, and the action is explicitly exempted from the XHR check.
