Because initialization is now performed in `NewResourceServer`, this goroutine is started unconditionally whenever search is configured, making shutdown of an otherwise unused server susceptible to this panic. Handle closed channels and tie this watch context to the server lifecycle rather than `context.Background()`.

title: Concurrent builds for the same namespace/resource are still unsynchronized
body: Only the final cache assignment is protected. Two concurrent Search requests for an absent index can both observe a cache miss in GetIndex and both execute BuildIndex for the same key. For file-backed indexes, the second bleve.New targets the same directory and can fail; for memory-backed indexes, both builds complete and one fully-built index is silently overwritten in the cache. This also duplicates indexing work and metrics. Synchronize get-or-create/build on a per-key basis (and re-check the cache after acquiring that lock) rather than only locking the map write.

title: Search watch is detached from the ResourceServer shutdown context
body: The startup search watcher is created with context.Background rather than the cancelable context supplied by ResourceServer. Since initialization is now unconditional in NewResourceServer, every configured server starts this watcher during construction, but server.Stop only cancels s.ctx and cannot stop this watch for backends that rely on the passed context. This can leave polling/watch goroutines and backend resources alive after shutdown. Pass the initialization/server context to WatchWriteEvents instead of creating a background context.

title: Closing the search event channel causes a nil-event panic
body: The watcher goroutine receives from events without checking the channel's open status. If a backend closes its event channel during shutdown or on an error, the receive returns nil repeatedly and handleEvent immediately dereferences evt.Type, causing a panic. The goroutine should use `v, ok := <-events` and return when !ok (and ideally also select on its context).

title: The storage-server integration test is now disabled for PostgreSQL in CI
body: PostgreSQL is a supported non-SQLite storage-server backend, but this change skips the only shown integration test for it rather than fixing the failure. As a result, CI will not exercise startup/initialization behavior against PostgreSQL, including the new eager initialization path. The test should be made reliable for PostgreSQL or replaced by an equivalent PostgreSQL-backed test rather than permanently skipped.

title: Call to nonexistent zero-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled method prevents compilation
body: UsernameForm calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but its superclass only declares `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` and neither this class nor AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator defines a zero-argument overload. This is a Java compile-time method resolution error, so the services module cannot be built until the call supplies a user or a matching overload is added.

title: Conditional passkeys are disabled for all initial unauthenticated login forms
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` now requires `user != null`, while both `authenticate` and the error challenge use it to decide whether to call `fillContextForm`. During a normal initial login there is no context user, so the WebAuthn conditional-UI attributes and challenge are never populated. This removes passkey/autofill authentication from the initial UsernamePasswordForm flow (and from UsernameForm through the inherited authenticate path), contradicting the existing initial-login tests that expect the `webauth` form and preventing passkey-only users from signing in. Re-authentication needs the user-present case added without dropping the existing user-absent conditional-UI setup.

title: Call to nonexistent no-argument passkey helper prevents compilation
body: `UsernameForm` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but its superclass only defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. There is no no-argument overload in this class hierarchy, so this source does not compile. Pass `context.getUser()` (or add an appropriate overload) before merging.

title: Conditional passkey setup is skipped for unauthenticated login screens
body: The new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` predicate requires a non-null user, while an initial browser login has no user selected yet. Previously `fillContextForm` was explicitly invoked in that case whenever passkeys were enabled, which sets the challenge and conditional-UI form attributes used to initiate a passwordless WebAuthn login. As a result, initial username/password-form logins no longer render or initialize conditional passkeys, and passkey-only users cannot start a passkey login until some other step identifies them.

title: Call to a nonexistent no-argument passkeys helper prevents compilation
body: `UsernameForm` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only inherited method introduced in `UsernamePasswordForm` is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. Neither `UsernameForm` nor `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` supplies a no-argument overload. This source therefore does not compile; pass `context.getUser()` or add the intended overload.

title: Conditional passkeys are no longer initialized for an anonymous initial login
body: The new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` predicate requires a non-null user. On the initial username/password page `context.getUser()` is normally null, so `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is skipped even when passkeys are enabled for the realm. As a result the form does not receive the conditional-UI flag, challenge, RP ID, or WebAuthn attributes, disabling passkey/conditional-UI login before a user has been selected. The previous code intentionally initialized WebAuthn in this null-user branch; retain that behavior while also initializing it for reauthentication.

title: Initial-login error responses drop conditional-passkey form state
body: The error challenge now calls `fillContextForm` only when `context.getUser()` is non-null. For an anonymous initial login (for example an invalid username/password submission), the returned form is missing the conditional-passkey attributes and a fresh challenge despite passkeys being enabled. This regresses retry behavior by making the passkey UI disappear after an initial-login validation error; the condition should allow enabled passkeys when no user is selected as well.

title: Login-list invalidation uses organization-wrapped effective enabled state
body: `original` is obtained through `getById`, which wraps organization-linked providers so that `isEnabled()` is false whenever the linked organization is disabled. `getLoginPredicate()` therefore treats both the old and updated provider as unavailable while an organization is disabled, even if an update changes a field that controls the underlying login query (for example `hideOnLogin` from true to false, or the reverse). The method then skips invalidation, although the delegate's `getForLogin` query filters the provider's stored enabled/hide/link/public fields rather than the organization wrapper's effective enabled state. This can leave the cached ID set missing or retaining that provider; after the organization is enabled again, callers continue to receive an incorrect login-provider list until an unrelated invalidation occurs. Determine eligibility for invalidation from the unwrapped/stored model fields (or otherwise invalidate when those query fields change), rather than calling the wrapper-sensitive predicate on `original`.

title: The login-query cache conflates a null organization ID with an empty organization ID
body: `getForLogin`'s delegate distinguishes `organizationId == null` (all public organization IDPs for ORG_ONLY/ALL) from `organizationId.equals("")` (a specific, empty ID search), but both are stored under the same `searchKey` (`""`). Consequently, a call with an empty ID can reuse the unscoped null-ID result and expose IDPs from every organization, or an unscoped call can reuse an empty result cached by the empty-ID call. Use a distinct sentinel for null (or otherwise encode null separately) so the cache preserves the delegate method's behavior.

title: The new test registers cleanup for the literal alias instead of each created IDP
body: Each iteration creates `idp-alias-<i>`, but the cleanup action targets `identityProviders().get("alias")`. Therefore none of the 20 providers created by this test (nor the later `idp-alias-20`) are removed by the registered cleanup. This pollutes the shared test realm and can make repeated execution or later tests observe unexpected providers. Register cleanup using the iteration's actual alias.

title: Register cleanup for the created IDP alias, not the literal "alias"
body: Each created provider is named `idp-alias-<i>`, but the cleanup callback is registered against `identityProviders().get("alias")`. The cleanup will therefore attempt to delete a non-existent provider and leave all providers created by this test behind (the same issue occurs for `idp-alias-20` at line 425). This can pollute the shared test realm and cause later tests or reruns to observe unexpected IDPs. Register cleanup using the actual alias created in each case.

title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public service-provider interface, but `order()` is added as a required abstract method. Any provider compiled against the previous interface (including third-party providers discovered through ServiceLoader) does not implement this method. Such providers will fail with `AbstractMethodError` when `CryptoIntegration` sorts providers, and source-compatible providers will no longer compile until updated. Make this a default method (with an appropriate default priority) or provide a compatibility path before invoking it.

title: Equal provider priorities make crypto-provider selection classpath-order dependent
body: Provider selection now silently chooses the first provider after sorting by `order()`, but DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return the same priority (200). For a classpath containing more than one of these providers, the comparator leaves ties in ServiceLoader discovery order, which depends on classpath/resource ordering rather than an explicit security policy. In particular, a deployment containing both FIPS1402Provider and DefaultCryptoProvider can silently select the non-FIPS provider instead of failing as it did previously, defeating the expected FIPS configuration. Assign unambiguous priorities or reject equal-priority candidates rather than selecting one arbitrarily.

title: ES384 and ES512 tests use a P-256 key and do not exercise their signature encodings
body: The test constructs one unspecified default EC key pair, which is normally P-256, and uses it for ES256, ES384, and ES512. Consequently the ES384/ES512 cases only convert 32-byte P-256 R/S values padded to larger requested lengths; they do not exercise 48-byte ES384 values, 66-byte ES512 values, or the long-form DER sequence length that ES512 commonly requires. Generate keys on secp256r1, secp384r1, and secp521r1 respectively (and ideally verify the reconstructed DER signature) so the tests cover the encoding paths claimed by each algorithm.

title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public ServiceLoader SPI, but `order()` was added as an abstract method. Existing external implementations will no longer compile against this interface; implementations already compiled against the previous version can still be discovered but will fail with `AbstractMethodError` when `CryptoIntegration` evaluates `CryptoProvider::order`. Provide a default order implementation (or otherwise version the SPI) so existing providers remain usable.

title: Equal-priority FIPS and default providers are selected by unspecified ServiceLoader order
body: DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider, and WildFlyElytronProvider all return order 200. When more than one is visible, this code now silently keeps whichever provider happens to appear first from ServiceLoader rather than failing as it did before. ServiceLoader ordering across jars/modules is not a safe configuration mechanism, so a FIPS deployment with both FIPS and default providers can select the non-FIPS provider. Moreover, all candidates are instantiated while collecting them, so the ignored FIPS provider can still mutate global Java security providers/properties. Reject equal highest-priority providers or make the selection explicit and ensure mutually exclusive providers cannot be silently ignored.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns an unrelated default keystore provider
body: The CryptoProvider contract promises the BouncyCastle security provider, but this implementation returns the provider selected for the JVM's default keystore type (commonly `SUN` for JKS/PKCS12). That provider is unrelated to BouncyCastle and may not support algorithms callers expect from this method. Code using the CryptoProvider API can therefore receive a misleading provider and fail when it attempts BouncyCastle-specific operations. Return an actual registered BouncyCastle provider, or adjust the provider/API behavior so callers do not receive an unrelated provider.

title: ES384 and ES512 tests sign with a default P-256 key
body: The test creates one `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")` key pair without selecting a curve and reuses it for ES256, ES384, and ES512. The JDK default is typically P-256, so the ES384 and ES512 cases do not exercise 48- and 66-byte ECDSA coordinates/signatures that those algorithms require. Generate a key on the matching named curve for each algorithm and verify the reconstructed DER signature with the corresponding public key, rather than only checking a conversion round trip.

title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public ServiceLoader SPI, but `order()` was added as an abstract method. Any provider compiled against the previous interface can still be discovered at runtime, but `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider()` now invokes this missing method and will fail with AbstractMethodError, preventing startup. Make this a default method with a safe default priority (or otherwise provide a compatibility path) so existing external providers remain usable.

title: Crypto provider selection is nondeterministic when providers have equal priority
body: The selection sorts only by `order()` and silently chooses the first provider. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so when more than one is visible the winner is determined by ServiceLoader/classpath resource ordering rather than an explicit configuration. In particular, a FIPS-capable deployment that also exposes the default provider can accidentally select the non-FIPS provider instead of failing as it did previously, bypassing the intended crypto mode. Reject ties at the selected priority or define an explicit, deterministic and safe precedence.

title: ES384 and ES512 tests generate P-256 keys instead of the corresponding curves
body: The shared key pair is created using `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()`, which uses the JVM default EC curve (normally P-256), for all three tests. Thus the ES384 and ES512 cases only exercise a P-256-sized DER signature padded to 96/132 bytes; they do not test conversion of real P-384 and P-521 signatures, including their boundary-length and leading-zero behavior. Generate keys with ECGenParameterSpec("secp384r1") and ECGenParameterSpec("secp521r1") for those algorithms.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never upgraded with the Clients schema
body: `init` returns as soon as an admin-permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled FGAP v2 before this change therefore retain only the old Users resource/scopes and never receive the Clients resource type, its six scopes, or the all-Clients resource. Client authorization cannot be configured in those realms; moreover `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, ...)` can obtain a null all-Clients resource and pass it to `findByResource`/`ResourcePermission`. Initialize or migrate missing schema scopes/resources even when the admin-permissions client already exists, and add an upgrade-path test.

title: manage-clients administrators lose role-mapping access under v2
body: The overrides for `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` evaluate only a v2 resource permission and omit the normal `MANAGE_CLIENTS` admin-role bypass. Consequently, an administrator assigned the standard `manage-clients` role is forbidden from client role mappings, composite role changes, and client-scope role mappings whenever FGAP v2 is enabled, despite retaining that role's established permissions. Preserve the admin-role behavior (and any intended manage transitivity) before evaluating fine-grained scopes.

title: Removal cleanup is disabled when only the v2 feature is enabled
body: The event listener now processes role/client/group removal only when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, but the new implementation is selected by the distinct `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` feature. A deployment enabling v2 without the old feature will skip `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)` on removals, leaving associated authorization policies/resources behind for deleted objects. Gate this on v2 as well (or retain the previous unconditional cleanup behavior) so v2-only deployments clean up correctly.

title: Existing V2 admin-permissions clients are never upgraded with the Clients schema
body: `init` returns immediately whenever the admin-permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore retain only the old Users scopes and resource-type resource; they never receive the Clients resource, nor configure/map-role client scopes. Creating a client permission in such a realm will fail while resolving missing scopes (and client authorization evaluation can reach a null all-clients resource). Initialization must reconcile/add newly introduced schema scopes and resource-type resources for an existing client, not only create them for a new client.

title: V2 drops MANAGE_CLIENTS-role access for client role mapping
body: The overrides for `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only evaluate an FGAP resource permission and do not preserve the `MANAGE_CLIENTS` admin-role shortcut used by the legacy evaluator. Consequently, when V2 is enabled, an administrator who has `realm-management`'s `manage-clients` role but no explicitly created authorization policy is denied client role assignment/composite/client-scope role mapping, even though the same role continues to authorize the other client-management operations. These methods need the equivalent root admin-role check (or delegation to the superclass) before FGAP evaluation.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never upgraded with the Clients schema
body: `init` returns as soon as the realm already has an admin-permissions client. Realms which enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore retain only the old Users resource/scopes and never receive the Clients all-resource or the new configure/map-role scopes. Creating a Client permission in such a realm will fail when `getOrCreateResource` cannot find the required scope, and all-clients evaluation cannot work. The initialization/migration path must add missing schema scopes and resource-type resources to an existing admin-permissions client rather than returning unconditionally.

title: Per-client resources are created without their Clients type
body: Resources created for an individual client are assigned scopes but never assigned `resourceType` (for example via `resource.setType(resourceType)`). `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission` later uses `resourceStore.findByType(..., "Clients", ...)` to determine which clients the caller may access, so it will not discover any of these untyped per-client resources. Consequently a user granted view/manage for one client can be omitted from filtered client listings/access calculations despite the direct permission evaluating successfully.

title: Role-mapping checks discard the manage-clients authorization path
body: `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only test their respective fine-grained scope. Unlike the other client operations, they do not allow `MANAGE_CLIENTS` through `canManage(client)`. Thus an administrator with the normal `manage-clients` role (or a V2 manage permission) is denied client-role mapping/composite operations unless separately granted every map scope, which regresses the established meaning of manage-clients and makes existing administrators fail after V2 is enabled.

title: Do not renumber the existing recreate-upgrade exit code
body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` was changed from 4 to 3 while the command is explicitly documented as scriptable and consumers are told to rely on its exit code. Existing automation that interprets exit code 4 as “recreate required” will, after upgrading, either receive 3 unexpectedly or misinterpret the new 4 feature-disabled result as a recreate requirement. Preserve the existing code and assign the new feature-disabled condition a previously unused value (or provide an explicit compatibility/migration strategy).

title: Global group view permission is treated as permission to manage groups
body: `canManage()` evaluates both `view` and `manage` scopes on the all-groups resource. Consequently, an administrator granted only the Groups `view` scope passes `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()`, which relies on `requireManage()`, and can create groups despite having no manage permission. `canManage()` must require only the `manage` scope; `view` should remain sufficient only for view/list operations.

title: User search is filtered with authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` adds `groupResource.getId()`, which is the generated authorization Resource ID, not the Keycloak group ID. Callers put this set into `UserModel.GROUPS` and pass it to user search/count providers, which expect actual group IDs. As a result, an admin granted `view-members` or `manage-members` on a group cannot discover that group's users through list/search/count endpoints (despite direct per-user authorization succeeding). Add the resource name, which is created from the group ID, rather than the authorization resource ID.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never updated with the new Groups schema
body: `init()` returns immediately whenever the realm already has an admin-permissions client. Realms that enabled fine-grained authorization before this change therefore retain a resource server with no Groups resource, no Groups scopes, and no corresponding schema resource. Creating a Groups scope permission subsequently fails because `getOrCreateResource()` cannot find the new scopes, while permission evaluation can dereference a missing all-groups resource. Initialization needs to reconcile/add newly introduced schema scopes and resource-type resources for existing clients, or an explicit database migration must do so.

title: Global group view permission grants group management
body: `canManage()` evaluates both `view` and `manage` on the all-groups resource. Consequently, a principal granted only the `view` scope for Groups passes `requireManage()` and can create top-level groups, as well as perform management operations that use the global check. The global management check must require only the `manage` scope; `view` should only be accepted by view/list checks.

title: Group-member user searches are filtered using authorization resource IDs
body: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns `groupResource.getId()`, which is the authorization Resource entity ID. The user search/count overloads consume this set as realm `GroupModel` IDs (the V1 implementation correctly derives the group ID from the resource name). Authorization resources are created with the group ID as their name, but have a distinct generated resource ID, so admins with `view-members` or `manage-members` on an individual group will not receive that group's users in filtered user searches/counts. Add `groupResource.getName()` (the group model ID) instead.

title: Master-admin role no longer grants per-user view/manage access in V2
body: This removes `AdminRoles.ADMIN` from the direct per-user `canView` and `canManage` checks. A master-realm administrator with the `admin` role managing another realm is not in the target realm (`isAdminSameRealm()` is false), so after this change authorization-resource fallback cannot restore access. Such administrators will receive forbidden responses for direct user operations that previously succeeded. Preserve the `ADMIN` bypass (and apply the corresponding super-admin semantics consistently to the new group evaluator).

title: Global view permission is treated as global group-management permission
body: `canManage()` grants access when the caller has either `view` or `manage` on the all-groups resource. This method guards operations such as `POST /groups`, so an administrator assigned only the read-only `view` scope can create top-level groups. Restrict this evaluation to the `manage` scope; `view` should only be accepted by the view/list checks.

title: Individually created group authorization resources are not assigned the Groups type
body: Resources created by `getOrCreateResource` receive scopes but never have their type set to `resourceType`. `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` enumerates individual grants using `resourceStore.findByType(..., "Groups", ...)`, so resources created for individual groups are omitted from that enumeration. As a result, a `view-members` or `manage-members` grant on a specific group will not constrain user searches to that group's members. Set the resource type when creating schema resources (at least for the Groups resource type).

title: Group-member search uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: The code passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission`, which looks up a resource by name, and then adds that same authorization-resource ID to the returned set. Schema resources are named with the Keycloak group ID, while their resource IDs are separately generated. Consequently the lookup misses the individual resource and the set later supplied to user queries contains IDs that do not identify any group, causing delegated group-member visibility/searches to return no matching users. Use `groupResource.getName()` for both the permission lookup and the returned group-ID set.

title: Existing enabled admin-permissions clients are never upgraded with the Groups schema
body: `init` returns immediately whenever an admin-permissions client already exists. Realms which enabled fine-grained admin permissions before this change therefore retain a resource server without the new Groups resource and its scopes. Creating or evaluating group scope permissions in those realms can fail because the scopes/resource cannot be found, and there is no migration path in this code to add them. Initialization must reconcile the existing resource server with newly introduced schema scopes and all-resource entries rather than returning unconditionally.

title: Changed a frontend interpolation key to Java MessageFormat syntax
body: This account UI message bundle uses i18next-style placeholders such as `{{0}}`, `{{name}}`, and React component placeholders such as `<0>`. Replacing `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, and `{{2}}` with `{0}`, `{1}`, and `{2}` means the account UI will no longer interpolate the attribute name or bounds and will display those braces literally. The Java `choice` expression is also not a pluralization format understood by this frontend message format.

title: Changed an admin UI translation from its supported placeholder syntax
body: The admin UI message resources use `{{0}}`-style frontend interpolation. This change switches the message to Java MessageFormat placeholders and a `choice` expression, so the admin UI will render `{0}`, `{1}`, and `{2,...}` as literal text rather than substituting the validation values. Keep this bundle in the frontend translation format and handle pluralization using the UI i18n mechanism if needed.

body: `messages_lt.properties` is the Lithuanian account-theme bundle, but the new `totpStep1` value is Italian (`Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare`). Lithuanian users will see an unrelated-language instruction during authenticator setup.

body: The Lithuanian login-theme bundle now contains the Italian sentence `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare` for `loginTotpStep1`. This is user-visible on the Lithuanian login flow and should be replaced with a Lithuanian translation.

body: This bundle is consumed by the account UI, whose existing messages use i18next-style placeholders such as `{{0}}` (and React component placeholders such as `<0>`). The new `{0}` and `{2,choice,...}` syntax is Java `MessageFormat` syntax and will not be evaluated by that UI, so validation errors will display literal `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}`, and the choice expression to account-console users. title: Lithuanian login message was replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian `loginTotpStep1` translation is now `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian. This is displayed during the login OTP setup flow, so Lithuanian users receive the setup instruction in the wrong language; replace it with Lithuanian text.

body: This bundle is consumed by the account React UI, where the surrounding validation messages use `{{0}}`-style interpolation. Replacing this entry with Java `MessageFormat` syntax (`{0}` and `{2,choice,...}`) means the UI will not substitute the attribute and bounds and will display the choice expression literally when a multivalued attribute violates its size constraint. The new `{0}`/`{2,choice,...}` Java MessageFormat expression is not interpreted by the frontend localization layer, so multivalued attribute size validation errors in the admin console will expose raw placeholders and choice syntax instead of the supplied values.

body: `messages_lt.properties` is the Lithuanian account bundle, but the new `totpStep1` value is Italian ("Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare"). Lithuanian users will see an unrelated-language instruction during authenticator setup; replace it with a Lithuanian translation.

body: The `loginTotpStep1` entry in the Lithuanian login bundle now contains Italian text. This is displayed in the login-time OTP setup flow, so Lithuanian users receive an untranslated/wrong-language instruction. Supply the Lithuanian wording instead.

title: Simplified-Chinese bundle now contains Traditional-Chinese text
body: This is the `zh_CN` (Simplified Chinese) account bundle, but the replacement `totpStep1` uses Traditional Chinese characters such as `手機`, `應用程式`, and `以下`. This produces inconsistent localization for Simplified-Chinese users; use a Simplified-Chinese translation.

title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing custom grant providers
body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` is an extension interface, and adding `getShortcut()` as an abstract method makes all already-built third-party implementations binary incompatible. During startup `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` calls this method on every grant factory, so an extension compiled against the previous interface will fail with `AbstractMethodError` (and source implementations will no longer compile) rather than allowing the server to start. Provide a default implementation/fallback for providers that do not supply a shortcut, or introduce a compatible optional interface.

title: Grant shortcut contract permits values the encoder cannot decode
body: The new API documentation says a shortcut is usually three letters, but `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` unconditionally parses exactly two characters for the grant shortcut and requires the entire encoded context to be six characters. A custom factory following this documented contract with a three-character shortcut will successfully issue IDs such as `onrtabc:<uuid>`, but `getTokenContextFromTokenId` will reject them as malformed. The factory must validate and enforce exactly two-character shortcuts (including dynamic providers), or the encoding needs a length-delimited format and matching documentation.

title: rawTokenId is not null-checked
body: The constructor checks `grantType` twice; the second check has the raw-token error message but does not validate `rawTokenId`. A caller of this public SPI can construct a context with a null raw ID, and `encodeTokenId` will then produce an ID ending in the literal string `null` instead of failing fast. Validate `rawTokenId` in the second `requireNonNull` call.

title: Access-token ID matcher does not verify the expected grant shortcut
body: The matcher extracts `substring(3, 5)`, although the grant occupies positions 4-5 in the six-character prefix, and then returns false when that extracted value equals the expected shortcut. Consequently, a token with a wrong grant shortcut normally passes the matcher, while certain matching values fail. The updated event assertions therefore do not test the grant encoding they were added for; compare `substring(4, 6)` to the expected shortcut and fail when they differ.

title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing custom grant providers
body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` is an extension SPI, and this adds a new abstract `getShortcut()` method. Existing third-party grant factories compiled against the previous interface will fail with `AbstractMethodError` when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` invokes the method; providers rebuilt without implementing it will not compile. Provide a backward-compatible default method and handle its absence/unknown result, or otherwise establish an explicit migration path before making token issuance depend on this method.

title: Grant shortcuts are not constrained to the fixed two-character wire format
body: The encoder concatenates `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` directly into the token ID, while the decoder unconditionally requires a six-character context and extracts exactly two characters for the grant shortcut. No validation enforces this requirement, and the factory interface documentation even says shortcuts are usually three letters. A custom grant provider returning (for example) `foo` will successfully issue IDs such as `onrtfoo:<uuid>`, but those IDs can never be decoded by this provider because their context length is seven. Enforce exactly two-character unique shortcuts during factory initialization/registration, or encode the context in a format that supports variable-length shortcuts.

title: Removing the public Context copy constructor breaks grant implementations
body: The public `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context)` constructor was removed. Custom OAuth2 grant implementations using that constructor will no longer compile after an upgrade, and already-built implementations will fail at runtime with `NoSuchMethodError` when they attempt to create the copy. Retain the constructor, including the new `grantType` field in the copy, unless this is intentionally released as a documented incompatible SPI change.

title: Access-token event matcher does not verify the grant shortcut
body: The six-character context puts the grant shortcut at indexes 4-5, but this matcher reads `substring(3, 5)`, which includes the final token-type character and only the first grant character. It also returns `false` when that incorrectly extracted value equals the expected shortcut. Consequently the updated event assertions accept IDs with an incorrect grant shortcut (for example, an authorization-code expectation accepts `onrtzz:<uuid>`) and do not test the feature they were added to cover. Compare `substring(4, 6)` to the expected shortcut and return that comparison result.

title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing OAuth grant providers at startup
body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` is a provider factory interface, and existing custom grant factories compiled against the previous version do not implement `getShortcut()`. They can still be discovered, but `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` invokes this new method for every discovered factory, causing an `AbstractMethodError` and preventing the server from starting when such a provider is installed. Preserve binary compatibility with a default method or otherwise avoid calling the new method on providers that do not implement it.

title: Grant shortcut contract permits values the token decoder cannot parse
body: The interface documentation permits a shortcut that is “usually like 3-letters” and the implementation does not validate its length, but `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` concatenates the entire value while `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` requires the context prefix to be exactly six characters and reads exactly two grant characters. A custom grant provider returning a three-character shortcut will issue access-token IDs which the default decoder always rejects as malformed. Require and validate exactly two-character shortcuts (including at provider initialization), or encode the context in a length/version-delimited format.

title: Access-token event matcher does not validate the expected grant shortcut
body: The matcher extracts `substring(3, 5)`, although the grant shortcut occupies offsets 4 and 5 in the six-character prefix, and it returns `false` when that extracted value equals the expected shortcut. Consequently IDs such as `onrtac:<uuid>` are accepted for an expected `ac` grant because the extracted value is `ta`, while an ID whose incorrectly extracted substring happens to match is rejected. The updated integration assertions therefore do not test the encoded grant type and can mask regressions; compare `substring(4, 6)` to the expected value and fail when they differ.

title: Federated recovery credentials permanently shadow locally generated replacements
body: The helper always returns a federated/user-storage recovery credential when one exists and only considers the local credential when none exists. However, `createRecoveryCodesCredential` falls back to local storage whenever a user-storage provider returns `false` from `updateCredential` (for example, a read-only provider). If that provider already exposes an older recovery-code credential, a recovery-code reset creates and displays a new local set, but this helper continues to use the old federated credential for the code-number display and all-codes-used/required-action handling. This makes recovery-code regeneration inconsistent and can leave the user unable to complete the expected reconfiguration flow. The fallback must either replace/disable the old federated credential, avoid creating a local credential while a federated one remains authoritative, or use an unambiguous precedence mechanism.

title: Recovery credential enumeration returns a different credential ID than the stored credential
body: `recoveryCodesModel` is rebuilt with `createFromValues`, which has no input for the ID assigned at line 195, so the credential returned by `getCredentials` cannot retain `myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()`. Consumers use the enumerated ID to remove credentials; in particular the recovery-code authenticator calls `removeStoredCredentialById` after all codes are consumed. Consequently this test storage cannot exercise removal of the actual stored recovery credential, and account/API credential operations may target an unknown ID. Preserve the original credential ID (and other persisted metadata) on the model returned by `getCredentials`.

title: Test user storage validates recovery codes without consuming them
body: The recovery-code validator accepts any matching generated code but never marks the matching code as used or persists an updated credential. Recovery authentication codes are one-time credentials; this provider therefore permits indefinite replay of every code. The new integration test logs in with only one code and does not attempt a replay or consume all codes, so it passes despite this broken behavior and does not verify the all-codes-used path. Update the provider/test fixture to persist code consumption and add replay/exhaustion assertions.

title: Raw recovery codes are persisted in user storage
body: The user-storage path serializes and passes `generatedCodes`, which are the plaintext recovery codes, as the credential challenge response. The local recovery-code credential model stores hashed code values, but an accepting user-storage provider receives and will commonly persist this plaintext JSON (as the added compatibility provider does). This gives anyone with access to the external user store reusable recovery codes, unlike the existing local-storage behavior. Pass a representation containing the hashed recovery-code data (and require validation to hash incoming codes), rather than the generated plaintext list.

title: Recovery codes accepted by the user-storage implementation are never consumed
body: The recovery-code validator only checks whether the submitted value occurs in the stored list and never removes or marks that value used. Consequently the same recovery code can authenticate repeatedly for this user-storage path. Recovery codes are one-time credentials; this provider needs to atomically consume the matching code on successful validation, and the integration test should attempt a second login with the same code and assert that it fails.

title: Recovery codes in the user-storage fixture are never consumed
body: The recovery-code validator only checks whether the submitted value is present in the stored JSON list and leaves that list unchanged. Consequently, a recovery code accepted once will be accepted again indefinitely, contrary to the one-time recovery-code contract. The new integration test logs in with only one code and therefore passes while this regression remains undetected. The fixture should mark the matching code as used/remove it in a way that is reflected by getCredentials(), and the test should attempt a second login with the same code and verify that it is rejected.

title: Concurrent reader is neither synchronized nor joined before assertions
body: The test starts a reader thread but does not retain or join it. The deletion loop can complete before the reader is ever scheduled, so `deletedAll` is set and the thread exits without issuing any concurrent read; the test then passes without exercising the race it is intended to cover. Conversely, a request already in flight can add an exception after line 157 has asserted the list is empty, leaving an unobserved failure and a thread that can continue into subsequent test cleanup. Coordinate the reader and deleter with latches/barriers and join the thread (preferably in a finally block) before checking captured exceptions.

title: Concurrency regression test does not wait for or synchronize the reader thread
body: The reader thread is started and then discarded. The test immediately deletes all groups, sets `deletedAll`, and asserts `caughtExceptions` without joining the thread or waiting for it to execute a request while deletion is in progress. Consequently, the test can pass when the reader has not run yet, or when its final in-flight request fails after the assertion; it can also leave requests running into subsequent test cleanup. Retain the thread and coordinate it with latches/barriers so at least one read overlaps deletion, then join it before asserting collected failures.

title: Other subgroup access paths still dereference a concurrently deleted group
body: `modelSupplier.get()` can return null when the cached group is removed concurrently, as the new null check in `getSubGroupsCount()` acknowledges. The three paginated/search `getSubGroupsStream` overloads (starting here and at lines 262 and 268) still immediately dereference that value. A request fetching a group's subgroups can therefore still fail with an NPE/500 when deletion wins the race; these paths need the same deleted-model handling (for example, returning an empty stream or the API's defined not-found behavior).

title: The concurrency test can finish before the reader executes or reports its failure
body: The reader thread is started and discarded without a latch/barrier to prove that it has made a read request, and it is never joined before asserting `caughtExceptions`. Deletion can complete before the new thread is scheduled, or the assertion can run while the final read is still in progress; an NPE occurring afterward will not fail the test. The test should retain the thread/future, synchronize at least one overlapping read with deletion, stop it in a finally block, and wait for it before checking exceptions.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs
body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` while ordering `AuditLogEntry` by `-datetime`, but this paginator's `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on the `datetime` field. `build_cursor` invokes this method after fetching the first page, so any authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true` and audit-log rows will raise a TypeError rather than return a response. This paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible datetime cursor serialization/conversion (or the endpoint must use a datetime-aware optimized paginator).

title: Negative cursor offsets cause Django queryset slicing errors
body: The advanced path deliberately passes a negative `start_offset` to a Django QuerySet. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`; it does not implement the boundary behavior claimed in the comment. Since cursor offsets are parsed from client-provided cursor strings, an authorized caller can trigger a 500 response with a negative offset. Reject invalid offsets or normalize them before slicing rather than passing them to the ORM.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs
body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the ordered field value. The audit-log endpoint instantiates it with `order_by="-datetime"`, so for any non-empty result set `build_cursor` calls this method with a `datetime` and raises `TypeError`. Consequently, an administrator requesting `optimized_pagination=true` receives a 500 instead of audit-log results. This paginator needs the datetime cursor conversion used by `DateTimePaginator` (or should subclass it).

title: Advanced negative offsets cause Django queryset slicing errors
body: The advanced branch passes a negative `start_offset` directly to a Django `QuerySet` slice. Django explicitly rejects negative indexing/slicing on querysets with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`, contrary to the comment's assertion that the ORM handles it. Cursor parsing accepts negative offsets, so an authorized caller using the advertised advanced negative-offset cursor capability can trigger a 500 response. Negative offsets must be translated to a supported query strategy or rejected as invalid pagination input.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs
body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` passes `order_by="-datetime"`, so `get_item_key` receives a `datetime` from each `AuditLogEntry`. This implementation calls `math.floor(value)`/`math.ceil(value)`, which raises `TypeError` for datetimes when `build_cursor` constructs the response cursors. Consequently every authorized request using `optimized_pagination=true` that returns audit-log rows will fail with a 500. This paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible timestamp conversion (or should subclass/reuse `DateTimePaginator`) rather than numeric rounding.

title: Advanced negative-offset path uses unsupported Django queryset slicing
body: The new advanced path intentionally passes a negative `start_offset` into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, but Django `QuerySet` does not support negative indexing or slicing and raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` A client can supply a cursor with a negative offset, so an authorized user opting into this paginator can turn such a request into a 500 rather than receiving a valid page or a pagination validation error. Clamp or explicitly reject negative offsets; negative offsets cannot implement reverse traversal through ORM slicing.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate the audit log datetime key
body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, but this implementation inherits the numeric `Paginator` key logic and calls `math.floor(value)`/`math.ceil(value)`. `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `datetime`, so an authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true` reaches cursor construction and raises `TypeError` instead of returning a page. This paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible `get_item_key` and cursor conversion, or the endpoint must continue using `DateTimePaginator`.

title: Changing live buffer keys from sets to sorted sets has no compatibility path
body: This now issues `ZADD` against the existing `span-buf:s:*` key names, while deployed versions stored those keys as Redis sets. During a rolling deploy, or for up to the existing one-hour TTL after deployment, any trace with an already-buffered set causes Redis `WRONGTYPE` here; the corresponding pipeline/batch fails and spans are not processed. The Lua script has the same incompatibility via `ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE`. Use versioned keys or explicitly migrate/handle legacy set keys before reading or writing them.

title: Reduced redirect traversal limit can split deep traces into separate segments
body: Redirect mappings are not rewritten for every descendant when a partial tree is merged, so resolving an old descendant can require walking the parent chain. Lowering the bound from 10,000 to 1,000 means traces deeper than this are resolved to an intermediate buffer rather than the actual segment root. Subsequent spans are then stored and flushed as a different segment, losing the intended trace assembly. Retain the prior bound or introduce path compression/a safe mechanism that preserves correctness for deep trees.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs
body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, but `get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the model field value. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a `datetime`, so even the first optimized request reaches this method while building its cursor and raises TypeError. Authorized users requesting `optimized_pagination=true` will receive a 500 instead of an audit-log page. This paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible timestamp conversion (or needs to inherit from DateTimePaginator).

title: Advertised negative cursor offsets cause Django queryset failures
body: The advanced branch passes a negative `start_offset` directly into a Django QuerySet slice. Django QuerySets explicitly reject negative indexing/slicing with ValueError rather than interpreting it as reverse pagination. Since cursor offsets are parsed from client input, an authorized caller can trigger a 500 using a negative offset; this does not provide the claimed bidirectional pagination behavior. Negative offsets must be rejected or translated into a valid ranged query.

title: Changing live span keys from sets to sorted sets has no migration path
body: This now executes ZADD against `span-buf:s:*` keys, while deployed versions created these keys as Redis sets. During a rolling deployment, any active buffered trace with a pre-existing set will make ZADD fail with WRONGTYPE (and later ZSCAN/ZCARD and the Lua script will fail similarly). A single such key can fail the pipeline/batch and prevent span processing until the old key expires, losing or delaying spans. Use a versioned key namespace or explicitly migrate/handle legacy set keys before issuing sorted-set commands.

title: Lua eviction bypasses the configurable segment-size limit
body: The script unconditionally retains only 1,000 members, while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` remains a constructor option and was previously enforced by `_load_segment_data`. Configurations below 1,000 are no longer honored (oversized segments are emitted rather than rejected), and configurations above 1,000 silently lose spans. The configured limit needs to be passed to the script and used for eviction, or the obsolete option and its contract need to be removed consistently.

title: Reducing redirect traversal depth can split valid deep traces
body: Redirect resolution was reduced from 10,000 links to 1,000. For a trace whose parent chain exceeds 1,000 spans and arrives out of order, the loop stops before reaching the existing segment root, stores the span under an intermediate key, and produces separate/incomplete segments. The prior code explicitly documented the depth limit as the condition under which trees can fail to merge; lowering it is a functional regression unless ingestion guarantees a maximum depth of 1,000.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs
body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` while ordering `AuditLogEntry` by `-datetime`. This paginator's `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on the field value, which is a `datetime`, so building cursors for any non-empty optimized response raises `TypeError`. Even if that were avoided, `value_from_cursor` returns a numeric cursor value rather than converting it to a datetime for the subsequent queryset filter. Thus an administrator requesting `optimized_pagination=true` receives a 500 on a non-empty audit-log response. This endpoint needs a datetime-aware paginator (or the optimized paginator needs the DateTimePaginator key/cursor conversion behavior).

title: Changing Redis collection type breaks existing buffered segments during rollout
body: This writes each existing `span-buf:s:*` key with `ZADD`, whereas previously the same keys were Redis sets populated with `SADD`. Buffered keys can remain for up to `redis_ttl` (default one hour), so a rolling deployment will encounter old set keys: `ZADD` will return WRONGTYPE, and the new Lua script's `ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE` and new flusher's `ZSCAN` likewise cannot operate on them. This can repeatedly fail consumer batches and prevent both ingestion and flushing until the old keys expire. Use versioned keys or provide a compatibility/migration path before switching the Redis data structure.

title: Eviction ignores the configured max_segment_spans limit
body: The buffer still exposes `max_segment_spans` as a constructor option, but the only span-count enforcement is now hard-coded to 1000 in Lua. The previous flush-side limit used `self.max_segment_spans`; after this change custom deployments cannot lower or raise the limit, and segments between their configured limit and 1000 are emitted rather than rejected/limited as configured. Pass the configured limit to the script and enforce that value, or remove/document the option and update callers if a fixed 1000-span contract is intentional.

title: Redirect traversal limit is reduced and can split deep traces
body: The redirect-chain traversal limit is reduced from 10,000 to 1,000. For a trace whose buffered parent chain exceeds 1,000 links, the script stops resolving redirects and attaches the arriving span to an intermediate buffer rather than the root buffer. Those buffers can then be queued and flushed as separate segments, producing incorrect segment IDs and incomplete trace segments. Retain the prior limit or add a safe chain-compression strategy rather than silently reducing the supported tree depth.

title: Detecting error-only queries with a substring can upsample transaction rows
body: `_is_error_focused_query` treats any query containing the text `event.type:error` as error-only. Valid Discover queries such as `!event.type:error` or `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` therefore enable `sum(sample_weight)` even though they include non-error events. Transactions do not have a meaningful error sample weight, so these requests can fail in Snuba or return counts that omit/incorrectly weight transaction events. Determine eligibility from the parsed query and require that its event-type predicate excludes non-error events rather than matching a raw substring.

title: Upsampling eligibility is evaluated against the outer dataset and original request query, not the query being executed
body: `_get_event_stats` accepts `scoped_dataset` and `query`, but calls the eligibility helper with the enclosing `dataset` and `request`. In the dashboard split path, an originally metrics-enhanced widget can execute a Discover error query (for example the generated `(<query>) AND !event.type:transaction` query), while eligibility still sees the original metrics dataset and unmodified request query and returns false. Consequently those split error results are never upsampled. Eligibility needs to use `scoped_dataset` and the actual query string passed to `_get_event_stats` (or an equivalent parsed query context).

title: Count expressions with aliases are not transformed
body: The transformation only recognizes a column whose entire normalized text is exactly `count()`. Event-stats/Discover aggregate expressions can be aliased (for example `count() as errors`), and those requests are left as raw counts even when all projects are allowlisted, producing inconsistent results depending only on the caller's output alias. Parse the aggregate expression or preserve and reapply its alias while replacing the `count()` function.

title: Error-only detection treats mixed and negated Discover queries as error queries
body: The Discover eligibility check is a raw substring search for `event.type:error`, rather than determining that the query is restricted to errors. Queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, `!event.type:error`, or a search value containing that text will therefore be transformed to `upsampled_count()`. Those queries can include transactions, for which `sample_weight` is not applicable, producing incorrect totals (or a backend query error) for allowlisted projects. Parse/inspect the query conditions and only enable the transform when the effective event-type predicate excludes non-error events.

title: Upsampling eligibility is evaluated against the outer dataset instead of the dataset being queried
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, and the dashboard split path calls it with a different dataset (notably `discover` for the error half of a metrics-enhanced widget), but eligibility is checked with the closed-over `dataset`. As a result, an error split that is actually executed against Discover is treated as a metrics query and is never upsampled, even when its projects and query are eligible. The check should use `scoped_dataset` so the transformation corresponds to the query that will actually run.

title: Process-randomized hash makes distributed cache invalidation ineffective
body: The cache key embeds Python's built-in `hash()`, which is randomized per interpreter process. A key written by one web worker cannot be addressed by `invalidate_upsampling_cache` running in another worker, despite the helper documenting that invalidation keeps the cache consistent; each worker also misses entries populated by others. After an allowlist change, workers can consequently retain and use a stale eligibility decision until TTL expiry. Use a deterministic key component (for example a sorted, delimited ID string or a stable digest) so all processes share and invalidate the same key.

title: Raw substring check enables upsampling for non-error Discover queries
body: The Discover eligibility check treats any query containing the text `event.type:error` as error-only. This is not a semantic query check: for example, `!event.type:error` (a supported syntax used elsewhere in this endpoint) contains that substring but explicitly selects non-error events, and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` selects transactions as well. Those queries will be rewritten to sum `sample_weight`, even though transactions/non-error events do not have error sampling weights, producing failed queries or incorrect counts. Determine event-type constraints from the parsed query and require that the query cannot include non-error event types.

title: Upsampling eligibility uses the outer dataset instead of the dataset actually queried
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, but eligibility is evaluated against the `dataset` captured from the original request. In the dashboard split path, an enhanced-metrics widget can call `_get_event_stats(discover, ..., errors_only_query, ...)` while the captured dataset is a metrics dataset. `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` rejects metrics datasets, so this explicitly error-only Discover subquery is never upsampled despite all projects being allowlisted. Evaluate eligibility against `scoped_dataset` and the actual `query` argument rather than the original request context.

title: The internal upsampling aggregate is exposed to client queries
body: `upsampled_count` is registered without `private=True`, unlike the adjacent internal aggregate. As a result, clients can request `upsampled_count()` directly through Discover/Event Stats without passing the allowlist and event-type checks in `error_upsampling.py`. This permits unallowlisted or mixed-event queries to use `sample_weight`, yielding unsupported/incorrect results (or query failures where the field is unavailable). Mark the function private and expose it only through the guarded rewrite.

title: Upsampled counts truncate fractional sampling weights
body: The implementation applies `toInt64` to `sum(sample_weight)`. Sampling rates are floats (the added test factory explicitly converts `client_sample_rate` to float), so weights such as `1 / 0.3` and sums of heterogeneous weights are not necessarily integral. Casting the final sum to an integer truncates the estimate and systematically underreports error counts. Return the numeric sum directly, or use the established rounding behavior for sampled-count estimates if the API contract requires integral counts.

title: Feature-flagged dashboard tables are rendered with empty data
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, this branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and a hard-coded empty `tableData` object instead of `result.data`, `result.meta`, and the widget's configured fields. Consequently every dashboard table for an enabled organization displays an empty table regardless of query results, replacing the currently working `StyledSimpleTableChart` output.

title: Missing nodestore events can associate error details with the wrong error ID
body: `get_multi` returns a mapping only for records that exist, but this code zips the complete `error_ids` list with `events.values()`. If an earlier error event has expired or is absent from nodestore, subsequent returned values shift left and are emitted using the wrong event ID (and potentially at the wrong timestamp). The replay summary can therefore send Seer an error title/message attributed to another error. Look up each generated node ID in the returned mapping while iterating the corresponding error ID instead of relying on `values()` alignment.

title: Browser reports without either timestamp format are accepted
body: Both `age` and `timestamp` are optional, and their validators only reject the other field when its value is truthy. A report containing neither field passes validation, despite the supported Reporting API formats requiring one of these time fields; reports containing `age: 0` and `timestamp: 0` also pass because both `.get()` checks are falsy. This accepts malformed reports and corrupts the collected reporting data. Add object-level validation requiring exactly one key based on field presence rather than truthiness.

title: Feature-gated table visualization discards the query result
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the dashboard table branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and an empty `tableData` object instead of passing `fields`, `result.data`, and `result.meta`. Consequently every enabled dashboard table is blank regardless of the query response, whereas the fallback branch renders the actual result.

title: Attribute-key query cache is shared across organizations
body: The new React Query key contains only `queryOptions`, which does not include the organization slug. Since the fetch function closes over the current organization but the cache key remains identical after switching organizations with the same time range/projects/type, React Query can serve attribute keys fetched for the previous organization and may not refetch them. Include the organization slug (or endpoint path) in the query key.

title: Mutually exclusive report fields are accepted when one is zero
body: The age/timestamp exclusivity checks use truthiness of `self.initial_data`. A report containing both `timestamp: 0` and `age: 0` (or either field at zero alongside the other) bypasses the corresponding validation even though both fields are present. Presence should be tested with key membership or `is not None`, not truthiness.

title: Hook now returns undefined attributes during the initial fetch
body: Previously this hook always constructed and returned a `TagCollection` (an empty object while the request had no data). The replacement returns `previous` while `isFetching`; on the first request both `data` and `previous` are undefined. Existing consumers of `attributes`/`tags` can therefore receive undefined rather than a collection and fail when enumerating or spreading it. Preserve an empty-object fallback while no cached result exists.

title: Feature-gated dashboard tables discard the query result
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, this branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and a hard-coded empty `tableData` instead of the current `result.data`, `result.meta`, and widget field configuration. Consequently every table widget for enabled organizations renders an empty table with no headers or rows, even though the query completed successfully. Pass the actual table result and derived columns/renderers into the new visualization before enabling this path.

title: Attribute-key query cache key is not scoped to the organization
body: The React Query key contains only the date/project/type query options and omits `organization.slug`, whereas the request made by `useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys` is organization-scoped. In particular, an all-project query has no project IDs and will readily collide when navigating between organizations with the same time range. The hook also deliberately returns the previous data while a fetch is in progress, so keys from the prior organization can be displayed in the next organization's Explore UI. Include the organization slug (or endpoint path) in `queryKey` to prevent cross-organization cache reuse.

title: Browser report age accepts invalid negative values and zero-valued mixed fields
body: `age` has no non-negative constraint even though the Reporting API age is an elapsed duration, so reports with a negative age are accepted. In addition, the mutual-exclusion checks at lines 52 and 58 use truthiness; a report containing both `age: 0` and `timestamp: 0` passes validation even though the endpoint intends these alternative-format fields to be mutually exclusive. Validate field presence rather than truthiness and set `min_value=0` for `age`.

title: New installation records bypass the GitHub installer identity check
body: When no `Integration` record exists yet, this returns `pipeline.next_step()` before checking the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user. The subsequent `build_integration` call obtains installation details but does not obtain or persist the installer identity. GitHub webhook delivery that creates the Integration can be delayed or fail, so an attacker who supplies another installation ID during that window can complete the flow after authorizing their own GitHub account and attach that installation to their Sentry organization. The flow must fail closed until an installer identity from a trusted installation webhook is available, or otherwise validate the installer before creating the integration.

title: Installer comparison crashes for integrations without webhook sender metadata
body: This direct indexing assumes every active Integration has `metadata['sender']['login']`, but integrations created by this pipeline do not set `sender`: `OAuthLoginView` only stores `github_authenticated_user`, and `build_integration` only copies `state['sender']` when it exists even though no view binds that state. The existing basic-flow test also expects metadata without `sender`. Any later install/reinstall attempt that reaches this branch for such an integration (including pre-existing integrations) raises `KeyError` and returns a 500 rather than the intended installation error. Handle missing sender metadata explicitly and fail safely (or ensure it is persisted before this branch is reachable).

title: The authenticated GitHub user is not verified when the installation record has not arrived yet
body: When `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises, this branch immediately advances the pipeline and creates the integration without comparing the OAuth-authenticated user to the installation webhook sender. Webhook delivery is asynchronous, so this is a normal window after an app installation (or whenever a webhook was missed). A user can complete OAuth for their own GitHub account and substitute a known victim installation ID in the callback/request during that window, causing that installation to be associated with the attacker's Sentry organization. The flow must not accept a new installation ID until it has trusted installer identity data to compare, or must obtain an authoritative installer identity before advancing.

title: Optional sender metadata can crash the installation pipeline
body: `build_integration` only adds `metadata['sender']` when pipeline state contains a sender, so sender is explicitly optional (and existing integrations may also predate sender storage). On the existing-Integration/no-OrganizationIntegration path, indexing `integration.metadata['sender']['login']` raises `KeyError` or `TypeError` instead of returning the intended failed-installation response. This can occur after an organization association is removed while its Integration remains, leaving users with a 500 and preventing recovery. Treat absent or malformed sender metadata as an invalid installation request.

title: New installations bypass the GitHub installer identity check
body: When no Integration row exists yet, this branch immediately advances to integration creation without checking the GitHub account that installed the app. This is a normal race because the browser redirect from GitHub can reach this pipeline before the installation webhook has created the Integration containing `metadata.sender`; `build_integration` only fetches installation details and does not establish the installing user. A user can start their own valid Sentry/OAuth pipeline and submit a newly created/known installation ID during that window, causing the installation to be linked to their Sentry organization even though their OAuth user is not the app installer. The identity check must be performed from trustworthy installation/user data before allowing this branch, or the flow must wait for/require the webhook record with a sender.

title: Existing integrations without webhook sender metadata cause a server error
body: The comparison indexes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`, but `build_integration` creates GitHub integrations without a `sender` field and all integrations created before this change also lack it. If such an Integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed (or was created through the no-record branch above), a later installation attempt reaches this code and raises KeyError instead of returning the intended installation failure response. Treat missing or malformed sender metadata as an unverified request and return the error page (or migrate/populate the metadata) rather than indexing it directly.

title: `queued` timestamp is evaluated only once at module import
body: `timezone.now()` is executed while the dataclass is defined, so every `AssignmentSource` created by a worker process receives the same `queued` value until that process restarts. This makes the context payload's queue time inaccurate (and would break any future age/ordering/expiry logic based on it). Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each source records its own creation time.

title: `queued` is shared across every AssignmentSource created by a process
body: `timezone.now()` is evaluated when the class body is imported, not when an `AssignmentSource` instance is created. Consequently every source created by a worker process receives and serializes the same startup-time `queued` value, rather than the time that inbound assignment was queued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so the timestamp is generated per instance.

title: `queued` timestamp is shared by every AssignmentSource instance
body: `timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the class is defined, so every AssignmentSource created for the lifetime of a worker process receives the same `queued` timestamp rather than the time that assignment was queued. This makes the serialized context metadata inaccurate (and will break any age/order logic added around this carrier). Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance records its own creation time.

title: Metric alert handler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` but implements none of its required abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). Accessing `Detector.detector_handler` for a detector whose type is `metric_alert_fire` will therefore raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler...`, rather than returning the previously usable no-op handler. Implement the required stateful interface or retain a concrete non-stateful handler until metric alerts support stateful evaluation.

title: Stateful evaluate docstring still documents the old list return type
body: The method now returns a dictionary keyed by `DetectorGroupKey`, but its docstring says it “returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`.” This gives implementers of the abstract handler contract incorrect API guidance and can lead to list-based implementations that fail when `process_detectors` calls `.values()`.

title: Registered metric-alert handler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: `MetricAlertFire` still registers `MetricAlertDetectorHandler`, but this class now inherits abstract `StatefulDetectorHandler` without implementing `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, or `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Accessing `Detector.detector_handler` for a detector of this type calls `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(detector)` and raises `TypeError` instead of preserving the prior no-op behavior. Either provide a concrete implementation or do not register/use this handler until it is implemented.

title: Evaluate docstring still documents the old list return contract
body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` now returns a dictionary keyed by `DetectorGroupKey`, but its docstring says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". This is the public subclassing contract for detector implementations, so the stale documentation can cause new handlers to implement the previous list-based API and fail when `process_detectors` calls `.values()`.

title: Multi-group occurrence test does not validate the value passed to the hook
body: The packet supplies `group_2` with value `10`, but the expected occurrence is constructed with value `6`; additionally, the mock occurrence builder ignores its `value` argument. Consequently this test passes even if `evaluate_group_key_value` passes the wrong group value to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, which is the key new hook contract for producing occurrence-specific payloads. Make the mock output/assertions depend on `value` and expect `10` for `group_2`.

title: Registered metric-alert handler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now inherits `StatefulDetectorHandler` but implements none of its abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). `Detector.detector_handler` instantiates the registered handler with `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, so processing any detector whose type is `metric_alert_fire` will raise `TypeError` instead of safely evaluating as the previous concrete no-op handler did. Keep this handler on the non-stateful base until it is implemented, or provide implementations for all required stateful hooks.

title: Stateful detector evaluation documentation advertises the old list contract
body: The `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` docstring says it returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`, but the method now returns a dictionary keyed by group key. This is the extension point subclasses implement; following the documented contract would cause `process_detectors` to fail when it calls `.values()` on the returned object. Update the docstring to describe the keyed dictionary and its duplicate-key behavior.

title: Preserve or migrate the removed mark_failed module exports
body: This refactor removes the previously importable `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, and `SimpleCheckIn` symbols from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`, but does not provide compatibility re-exports or update any consumers outside these four files. Any existing worker, integration, or test importing one of those non-private symbols from the old module will now fail at import time. Re-export the moved symbols from the old module (or update every caller in the repository and any supported downstream integrations) before merging.

title: Timed shutdown can leave flusher worker processes running
body: When `next_step.join(timeout)` consumes the timeout, or when an earlier worker consumes the remaining deadline, this `break` exits the loop without terminating any remaining flusher processes. This is a regression from the single-process implementation, which always terminated its worker after waiting.
