Once it acquires the write lock, it unconditionally rereads the manifest and overwrites the already-populated cache. Under concurrent initial requests this serializes one filesystem manifest read per caller; additionally, a later transient read failure can replace a valid cached value with nil. After acquiring the write lock, return the cache when `cfg.Env != setting.Dev` and it has been populated, while preserving the reload behavior for development mode.

title: Concurrent cache misses are serialized but not coalesced
body: After a caller observes a nil cache under the read lock, it acquires the write lock and unconditionally reloads the manifest. Every other concurrent non-Dev caller that observed nil before the first caller populated the cache will wait for the lock and then also perform its own file/CDN read while holding the write lock. During startup or after an initial failed load, this makes N concurrent requests execute N sequential manifest loads and delays all of them. Recheck `entryPointAssetsCache` after acquiring the write lock (for non-Dev configurations) and return the populated value if another caller filled it.

title: No regression test verifies SQL expressions remain disabled
body: This security fix adds a permanent rejection path for SQL expression queries, but the PR adds no automated coverage for it. A test should assert that `QueryTypeSQL` is rejected both when `FlagSqlExpressions` is enabled and disabled, and that the legacy SQL command construction/execution path cannot create a usable command. Without this coverage, a future feature-toggle or database implementation change can inadvertently re-enable the RCE/LFI-prone behavior without being caught by CI.

title: No automated regression coverage verifies SQL expressions stay disabled
body: This security fix changes the SQL query path to reject requests regardless of the `sqlExpressions` feature flag, but the PR adds no test covering that behavior. Add tests that submit a SQL expression with the flag both enabled and disabled and assert that no SQL command is constructed or executed; the legacy `NewSQLCommand`/`UnmarshalSQLCommand` path should also be covered because it does not pass through this reader. Without coverage, a future feature-toggle cleanup or restoration of the DB implementation can silently re-enable the RCE/LFI attack surface.

title: Add regression coverage for SQL-expression rejection
body: This security-sensitive behavior is changed without any test covering it. Add tests that parse a SQL expression with `FlagSqlExpressions` both enabled and disabled and verify that it is rejected before `NewSQLCommand`/execution, plus coverage for the legacy `UnmarshalSQLCommand` path if it remains supported. Without this, a later refactor of the permanently-false helper or replacement of the stub DB can silently re-enable SQL execution and reintroduce the RCE/LFI attack surface.

title: Concurrent builds for the same key can publish divergent indexes
body: The cache lock now protects only the final map assignment, but there is no per-key build coordination or cache recheck before creating an index. Two concurrent searches for an uninitialized namespace/resource can both observe a cache miss, independently build indexes, and then whichever completes last overwrites `b.cache[key]`. The request using the discarded index continues to query an index that will no longer receive watch-event writes, producing permanently stale search results for that request; for file-backed indexes the concurrent `bleve.New` calls can also contend for the same directory. Use a keyed singleflight/lock and recheck the cache after acquiring it before building.

title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without its mutex
body: `BuildIndex` now writes `b.cache` under `cacheMu`, while `TotalDocs` ranges over the same map without acquiring an `RLock`. Any caller that collects total documents while an index is being built can trigger Go's concurrent map iteration/write panic (and a race-detector failure). Guard the complete iteration with `cacheMu.RLock()`/`RUnlock()`.

title: Startup index counter is updated concurrently without synchronization
body: Each errgroup worker increments `totalBatchesIndexed` concurrently. With `initWorkers > 1`, these unsynchronized read-modify-write operations are a data race and can lose increments, causing incorrect tracing data and race-detector failures. Use an atomic counter or protect the increment with a mutex.

title: Concurrent builds of the same key can replace a newer index with a stale one
body: Moving the cache lock to only the assignment removes the only synchronization between the GetIndex cache miss and BuildIndex. Two concurrent getOrCreateIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource can both build independent indexes and whichever finishes last overwrites the cache. A write event can be applied to the first cached index after its snapshot was built but before the second build publishes; the second, stale snapshot then replaces it and that write is no longer searchable. For file-backed indexes, the concurrent bleve.New calls also contend for the same directory and can make one request fail. Use a per-key singleflight/lock and re-check the cache before building or publishing.

title: Startup index build has an unrecoverable write-event gap
body: The search watcher is started only after all initial BuildIndex calls finish. WatchWriteEvents initializes its SQL polling cursor to the latest resource versions at the time it is called, so writes made by another server after an index's ListIterator snapshot but before line 202 are neither in that snapshot nor replayed by the watcher. The build method returns the snapshot resource version specifically needed to catch up, but it is discarded. In HA deployments this leaves indexes permanently stale until another write to each affected object occurs. Start/watch from a cursor established before the snapshot and replay events after the returned build resource version, or otherwise coordinate snapshot and watch registration.

title: Index updates can be lost during startup rebuild
body: The search watcher is subscribed only after all namespace indexes have been built from point-in-time ListIterator scans. Writes made after a namespace has been scanned and before WatchWriteEvents is opened are not included in that namespace's rebuilt index, and the SQL watch implementation starts from the latest revision when it subscribes, so it will not replay that gap. In HA deployments, writes from another server during a potentially long startup build will therefore leave search results permanently stale until each affected object is modified again. Subscribe/buffer before taking rebuild snapshots, or replay events from each build's returned resource version before publishing the index.

title: TotalDocs ranges over the cache without synchronization
body: BuildIndex now permits concurrent index construction and mutates b.cache under cacheMu at lines 137-139, while TotalDocs iterates the same map without even an RLock. A concurrent TotalDocs call can race with the assignment and can terminate the process with Go's "concurrent map iteration and map write" panic (as well as producing a race-detector failure). Hold cacheMu.RLock for the entire iteration, or iterate over a protected snapshot.

title: Bleve build span context is still discarded
body: BuildIndex starts a tracing span but assigns its returned context to `_`, so the builder callback and any work it invokes continue using the parent context rather than the Bleve BuildIndex span. This leaves the newly added BuildIndex span without the expected descendant storage/build spans and does not satisfy the stated trace-context propagation goal. Assign the returned context and pass it to downstream work (which may require the builder callback contract to accept a context).

title: Conditional passkeys are no longer initialized for an unselected user
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` returns false whenever the username/password form is first displayed because no user has been resolved yet. Consequently `fillContextForm` is not called for normal initial login (or after a failed normal password attempt, where the user is cleared), so the page lacks the WebAuthn challenge and conditional-UI attributes required to offer/discover passkeys. Previously this was deliberately initialized whenever passkeys were realm-enabled, including before identity selection. This breaks passwordless/passkey login from the standard Username Password Form and also contradicts the existing tests that expect the `webauth` form on the initial page.

title: Conditional passkeys are no longer initialized for anonymous login
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` returns false whenever no user has been selected. Consequently, the initial username/password page does not call `fillContextForm`, which is the call that sets `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI`, creates/stores the WebAuthn challenge, and supplies the WebAuthn form attributes. This disables conditional/passkey authentication before a username is entered, defeating discoverable-passkey login. The same user-null guard in the error challenge path also removes passkeys after an invalid username submission. The pre-existing behavior intentionally initialized the conditional UI when passkeys were enabled even with no selected user; retain that behavior while additionally supporting the selected-user reauthentication case.

title: Conditional passkeys are no longer initialized for an unauthenticated login
body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` requires a non-null user, but the initial UsernamePasswordForm request has no selected user. Consequently `fillContextForm` is skipped on the initial login page (and again after a bad password clears the user), so the conditional-WebAuthn form/challenge is absent and a user cannot initiate a passkey login from the normal username/password screen. This reverses the prior behavior, which initialized conditional passkeys specifically while no user was selected; the updated integration tests that expect `#webauth` on the initial UsernamePasswordForm page will fail.

title: The test does not actually verify that the WebAuthn form is absent
body: This block catches every `Exception`, including the assertion failure when the form exists and the explicit `fail()` when it does not. As a result, both presence and absence of `#webauth` make the test pass, so the stated regression case (passkeys disabled during re-authentication) is untested. Catch only `NoSuchElementException` or use an explicit absence assertion; the equivalent block at line 313 has the same issue.

title: Cleanup removes a literal nonexistent alias instead of the created IDP
body: The cleanup callback is registered against `get("alias")`, rather than the `alias` value created in this loop (`idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-19`). Consequently none of the IDPs created by this test are removed during cleanup (and the cleanup may issue failing deletes for a nonexistent provider named `alias`). The same problem is repeated for `idp-alias-20` at line 425. Register cleanup using the actual alias for each created provider.

title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public service-provider interface, and adding `int order()` as an abstract method makes every existing third-party implementation binary-incompatible. An implementation compiled against the prior interface can still be discovered by ServiceLoader, but `detectProvider()` now invokes `order()` and will fail with AbstractMethodError; source consumers also cannot recompile without changes. Provide a default implementation (for example, a neutral/default priority) so existing providers remain usable.

title: Equal-priority crypto providers are selected in nondeterministic ServiceLoader order
body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider are all assigned order 200. When more than one of these providers is present, this code no longer rejects the invalid configuration as it did before; the stable sort preserves the unspecified ServiceLoader discovery order and silently uses whichever appears first. In particular, a deployment that includes both the default and FIPS providers can select the non-FIPS provider, defeating the expected FIPS crypto configuration. Retain rejection for tied highest-priority providers or assign an explicit, safe precedence.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns a non-Bouncy-Castle provider
body: The CryptoProvider contract requires `getBouncyCastleProvider()` to return the Bouncy Castle security provider, but this implementation returns the provider backing the JVM's default keystore type. On standard JDKs that is commonly SUN/SUNJCE, not Bouncy Castle. Any code using the selected CryptoProvider to obtain the advertised BC provider can therefore receive an unrelated provider and fail when requesting BC algorithms or behavior. Since this provider intentionally has no BC dependency, it should not claim a default-keystore provider as Bouncy Castle; return an appropriate value/adjust the contract and callers, or implement the required provider behavior.

title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public service-provider interface, so implementations can exist outside this repository and may already be compiled against the previous version. Adding abstract order() makes those providers fail source compilation when rebuilt and throw AbstractMethodError when CryptoIntegration invokes order() at runtime. Give this method a default implementation (for example, returning 0) so existing providers remain binary and source compatible.

title: Equal-priority crypto providers are selected in ServiceLoader order
body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider are all assigned order 200. Comparator sorting preserves the unspecified ServiceLoader encounter order for equal values, and this code now silently selects the first provider instead of rejecting multiple providers as it did previously. Consequently, a classpath containing both FIPS and non-FIPS providers can nondeterministically initialize a non-FIPS provider, undermining the intended cryptographic mode. Reject ties for the highest priority or assign priorities that make the selection unambiguous.

title: Adding `order()` as an abstract SPI method breaks existing crypto providers
body: `CryptoProvider` is an SPI loaded through `ServiceLoader`, so third-party implementations compiled against the previous interface will not implement this newly abstract method. They will either fail to compile when rebuilt or throw `AbstractMethodError` when `CryptoIntegration` invokes `order()` during provider detection. Make this a default method with a neutral priority (for example, `default int order() { return 0; }`) so existing providers remain usable while new providers can opt into prioritization.

title: ECDSA conversion silently accepts signatures longer than the algorithm-defined size
body: `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` copies only `signLength` bytes from the supplied raw JOSE signature and ignores any trailing bytes. Consequently, a valid ES256/384/512 signature with arbitrary bytes appended is converted to the same DER signature and can verify successfully, even though the JWS ECDSA signature has an invalid length. A too-short input also escapes as an unchecked `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`. Validate that `signature.length == signLength` before copying and reject mismatches with the method's declared `IOException`.

title: ES384 and ES512 tests use a P-256 key rather than their required curves
body: The test generates the default `EC` key pair, which is normally P-256, and reuses it for ES256, ES384, and ES512. As a result, the ES384/ES512 cases only test padding a P-256 scalar to a larger output size; they do not exercise P-384 or P-521 integer encodings, including the 67-byte signed `BigInteger` representation possible for P-521. Generate `secp256r1`, `secp384r1`, and `secp521r1` keys respectively and verify that the DER output after conversion is accepted by the corresponding public key.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never migrated to include the Clients schema
body: `init` returns as soon as an admin-permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore retain a resource server with neither the new client scopes nor the `Clients` all-resource. Creating a client-targeted permission in such a realm fails when `getOrCreateResource` cannot find its scopes, and evaluating an unmaterialized client can subsequently dereference the missing all-resource in `ClientPermissionsV2`. Initialize or migrate the newly added scopes/resources when the client already exists.

title: All-clients manage permission does not grant global view/list access
body: `canView()` only recognizes default role-based view access and the global `view` scope; it does not recognize the global `manage` scope. Although `canView(ClientModel)` happens to get manage transitively through `canConfigure`, endpoints that gate listing or other global reads through `canView()`/`canList()` reject an administrator granted only `Clients/manage`. This also contradicts the expected manage-all behavior exercised later in the added test. Include the global manage permission in the global view decision.

title: V2 role-mapping checks discard the existing manage-clients admin role
body: `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only evaluate the new resource scope and never allow `AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS`. The established client permission evaluator grants a realm-management `manage-clients` administrator these operations, and the other V2 methods explicitly preserve that role. Enabling V2 will therefore cause existing manage-clients administrators to receive 403 responses when assigning client roles or editing composites unless separate V2 policies are created. Preserve the admin-role fast path in all three methods.

title: Client deletion leaves V2 client authorization resources and policies orphaned
body: The client-removal listener either skips handling when only the V2 feature is enabled (it tests the old `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature) or invokes `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. Consequently, deleting a client with a materialized `Clients` resource does not remove that resource or its scope-permission policy references from the realm admin authorization server. Repeated client creation/deletion accumulates stale authorization data and exposes deleted client identifiers in permission administration; V2 needs explicit cleanup rather than the unsupported legacy per-client permission toggle.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never upgraded with the Clients schema
body: `init` returns as soon as an admin-permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore retain only the previously-created Users resource/scopes and never receive the Clients all-resource or the new `configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, and `map-roles-composite` scopes. Creating a Clients permission in such a realm will fail when `getOrCreateResource` cannot find its scopes, and global client permissions cannot be evaluated because the Clients resource is absent. Schema initialization needs an idempotent upgrade path that creates missing scopes and resource-type resources for an existing client.

title: V2 client role-mapping checks drop the manage-clients administrator bypass
body: `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only evaluate a V2 resource permission. Unlike the existing client evaluator behavior, they do not allow a caller holding the built-in `manage-clients` role. Since `MgmtPermissionsV2` is selected globally whenever the V2 feature is enabled, realm administrators with `manage-clients` will be forbidden from assigning client roles or managing composite/client-scope role mappings unless separate V2 policies are created. Preserve the built-in admin-role bypass (and any existing transitive manage behavior) before performing the V2 scope evaluation.

title: Client deletion either invokes an unsupported V2 operation or leaves V2 permission data orphaned
body: The deletion listener is now gated on the old `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature, but `management()` selects `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled. If both features are enabled, deleting a client calls `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`, which always throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (line 193), potentially failing the deletion event. If V2 alone is enabled, the listener is skipped, so client-specific Clients resources and policies stored on the realm admin-permissions client are never removed when the target client is deleted. Implement V2-aware cleanup for client removal rather than routing it through the unsupported legacy permission-management method.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never migrated to the Clients schema
body: `init` returns as soon as an admin-permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore retain only the old Users resources/scopes and never receive the `Clients` resource, `configure`, or the new role-mapping scopes. Creating a client permission in such a realm will fail scope/resource resolution (and all-clients permissions have no resource to attach to), so the newly added feature only works in newly initialized realms. The initialization path needs to reconcile/add missing schema scopes and resource-type resources for an existing admin-permissions client.

title: MANAGE_CLIENTS administrators lose client role-mapping access under V2
body: All three role-mapping checks (`canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles`) evaluate only a V2 authorization permission. Unlike the legacy evaluator, they do not grant access to callers holding the built-in `MANAGE_CLIENTS` admin role. Consequently, an ordinary realm administrator with `manage-clients` can manage a client but receives Forbidden responses when assigning that client's roles or managing composites unless an additional V2 policy is created. Preserve the built-in-role short-circuit in these methods.

title: V2 client resources are left orphaned when a client is removed
body: The removal listener is now gated on the legacy `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature rather than the V2 feature. When only `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled, removing a client no longer invokes the cleanup path at all. This PR creates per-client authorization resources and policies, so deleting clients accumulates orphaned resources/policies in the admin-permissions resource server. The V2 implementation currently throws from `setPermissionsEnabled`, so it needs an explicit V2 cleanup implementation (or equivalent listener handling) rather than suppressing the event.

title: Exit-code contract for disabled feature is not tested
body: The new behavior exposes exit code 4 as the machine-readable result when `rolling-updates` is disabled, and the documentation instructs automation to rely on that code. This test only checks stderr, so a regression returning a generic Picocli/software-error code would still pass. Assert the result exit code for this disabled-feature invocation; similarly, the incompatible-version paths should assert the newly assigned recreate exit code 3.

title: Do not reassign the existing recreate-upgrade exit code
body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` is changed from 4 to 3 while 4 is reassigned to the new feature-disabled condition. The update-compatibility documentation explicitly directs automation to rely on these exit codes, so existing scripts that correctly interpret exit code 4 as "perform a recreate upgrade" will instead treat a normal incompatibility as a disabled feature after upgrading. Preserve the existing recreate code and allocate a previously unused code for feature-disabled (or provide an explicit compatibility/migration path).

title: The feature-gate warning overstates when the operator fails
body: The warning says the operator will fail whenever `rolling-updates` is not enabled, but the accompanying integration test still deploys and updates a Keycloak CR with no `UpdateSpec` and no enabled rolling-updates feature (`UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment(null)`). The gate appears relevant to selecting an explicit update strategy, not to all operator operation. This wording can cause users of the default strategy to believe their otherwise valid deployments are broken; qualify the warning with the configuration that actually requires the feature.

title: View permission on all groups grants group management
body: `canManage()` evaluates the all-groups resource with both `VIEW` and `MANAGE` scopes. This method guards creation of top-level groups (`GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup`) and is also used as the global management shortcut, so an administrator granted only the read-only `view` scope on the Groups resource can create groups and receive management access that should require `manage`. Evaluate only `MANAGE` here.

title: Group member visibility lookup uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: `groupResource.getId()` is the ID of the authorization `Resource`, whereas group-scoped resources are stored with the Keycloak group ID as their name. Passing the resource ID to `hasPermission` causes `findByName(server, groupId)` to miss the scoped resource and fall back to the all-groups resource; adding that same authorization resource ID to `granted` also supplies IDs that do not match user group memberships. Consequently a caller with `view-members` or `manage-members` on a particular group will not get that group in the user-search group filter and cannot discover its members through user search (and may instead receive incorrect results when an all-groups policy exists). Use `groupResource.getName()` for both the permission evaluation and the returned group ID.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never upgraded with the new Groups scopes/resources
body: `init` immediately returns when the realm already has an admin-permissions client. After upgrading a realm that had FGAP v2 enabled before this change, that client therefore lacks the newly introduced `Groups` resource type and the `manage-membership`, `manage-members`, and `view-members` scopes. Creating a group-scoped permission then cannot resolve its scopes/resources (for example `getOrCreateResource` throws when a scope is absent), leaving the new feature unusable for existing realms. Add an upgrade/reconciliation path that creates missing schema scopes and resource-type resources for an existing admin-permissions client.

title: Global group view permission grants group management
body: `canManage()` evaluates both the `view` and `manage` scopes on the all-groups resource. This method guards write operations such as `POST /groups`, so an administrator granted only the read-only all-groups `view` scope can create groups (and receive other operations guarded by global `requireManage`). Only the `manage` scope should satisfy this check.

title: Group member visibility collects authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: While iterating group authorization resources, this passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission` and adds that same value to `granted`. `getId()` is the authorization Resource's ID, whereas per-group resources are named with the Keycloak group ID and `UserModel.GROUPS` is consumed as a set of Keycloak group IDs. Consequently, per-group `view-members`/`manage-members` permissions are not found here and the user search filter receives unusable IDs, so administrators cannot discover members through user search based on a specific group permission. Use `groupResource.getName()` (the group ID) for both the permission lookup and returned set.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never upgraded with Groups resources and scopes
body: `init` returns as soon as an admin-permissions client already exists. After this schema adds the Groups resource type and its three new scopes, realms that enabled V2 before this release retain a resource server without those scopes or the all-groups resource. Creating a Groups scope permission will fail scope validation, and group permission evaluation can fall through with a null all-groups resource. Initialization needs an upgrade/reconciliation path that adds missing schema scopes and type resources to existing admin-permissions clients.

title: Global group view permission grants group-management access
body: `canManage()` evaluates both `VIEW` and `MANAGE` scopes for the all-groups resource. This method backs operations such as creating top-level groups, so an administrator granted only the read-only `view` scope can create and modify group hierarchy. `canManage()` must evaluate only the `manage` scope; `view` should remain limited to read/list operations.

title: Member-visible group IDs are derived from authorization-resource IDs
body: `groupResource.getId()` is the ID of the authorization Resource, not the realm GroupModel ID. It is passed back into `hasPermission`, which looks up resources by group-ID name, and it is added to the set later used by user providers as `UserModel.GROUPS`. Consequently, a scoped `view-members`/`manage-members` permission generally cannot match its group and user searches are filtered with IDs that do not identify any group, so members of permitted groups are omitted. Evaluate using the resource name (which is the group ID for this schema) and add that name to `granted`.

title: MessageFormat syntax breaks the account UI interpolation contract
body: This is an i18next/react message bundle, as shown by the surrounding `{{0}}` placeholders and React-style `<0>` tags. Changing this entry to Java `MessageFormat` syntax means the account UI will not substitute the attribute name, bounds, or plural form; users will see literal `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2,choice,...}` text in the validation error. Keep the UI bundle's interpolation syntax (or add the appropriate ICU formatting support and update its call site) rather than copying the server-side MessageFormat string.

title: MessageFormat syntax breaks the admin UI interpolation contract
body: The admin UI message resources use i18next-style `{{0}}` placeholders. Replacing them with Java `MessageFormat` and `choice` syntax is not interpreted by the UI translation formatter, so multivalued attribute validation errors in the admin console will render the placeholders and choice expression literally instead of the supplied values.

title: Lithuanian TOTP instruction was replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian account message `totpStep1` now contains `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian. Lithuanian users selecting this locale will receive a TOTP setup instruction in the wrong language.

title: Lithuanian login TOTP instruction was replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian login message `loginTotpStep1` now contains Italian text instead of Lithuanian. This produces a visibly incorrect localized instruction during the login-time TOTP enrollment flow.

title: Lithuanian TOTP instruction was replaced with Italian text
body: The `totpStep1` value in the Lithuanian account message bundle is now Italian ("Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare"). Lithuanian users of the account console will see an unrelated-language instruction when configuring TOTP; replace it with a Lithuanian translation.

title: Lithuanian login TOTP instruction was replaced with Italian text
body: The `loginTotpStep1` value in the Lithuanian login message bundle is now Italian ("Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare"). This makes the TOTP setup flow display an Italian instruction for the Lithuanian locale; it needs a Lithuanian translation.

title: Simplified Chinese bundle now contains a Traditional Chinese TOTP instruction
body: The `totpStep1` value in the `zh_CN` bundle uses Traditional Chinese characters (for example, `手機`, `應用程式`, and `以下`). Users selecting Simplified Chinese will receive a mixed-script account UI; this string should be translated in Simplified Chinese.

title: Lithuanian account message was replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian `totpStep1` translation is now Italian ("Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:"). Lithuanian account-console users will see an unrelated-language instruction during OTP setup; replace it with a Lithuanian translation.

title: Lithuanian login message was replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian `loginTotpStep1` value is Italian rather than Lithuanian. This is displayed in the login OTP enrollment flow, so Lithuanian users receive an incorrect-language instruction. Restore a Lithuanian translation.

title: Simplified Chinese resource now contains a Traditional Chinese translation
body: `messages_zh_CN.properties` is the Simplified Chinese locale, but the new `totpStep1` value uses Traditional Chinese characters and wording (for example, "手機", "應用程式"). This produces inconsistent localization for `zh_CN` users; use a Simplified Chinese translation or place this text in the appropriate Traditional Chinese resource.

title: Custom grant shortcuts are not constrained to the fixed two-character token format
body: The encoder format unconditionally writes the grant shortcut, while `getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires the entire context prefix to be exactly six characters and slices the grant shortcut as exactly characters 4-5. `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` neither enforces nor documents a two-character requirement (its Javadoc even says it is usually a three-letter shortcut). Consequently, an extension implementing a valid-looking shortcut such as `custom`/`abc` can issue access tokens successfully, but those token IDs cannot subsequently be decoded and will throw `IllegalArgumentException`. Validate shortcut length and uniqueness during factory initialization (and dynamic refresh), or make the format length-delimited.

title: Access-token event matcher does not validate the expected grant shortcut
body: `isAccessTokenId` checks `substring(3, 5)`, although the two-character grant portion of the documented six-character prefix starts at zero-based offset 4. It also returns false when that substring equals the expected shortcut, rather than when it differs. For normal IDs such as `onrtac:<uuid>`, the extracted value is `ta`, so every expected shortcut is accepted as long as the suffix is a UUID. The updated integration assertions therefore cannot detect a missing or incorrect grant-type encoding; compare `substring(4, 6)` and reject when it is not equal to `expectedGrantShortcut`.

title: Raw token ID is not null-checked despite the constructor contract
body: The final null check repeats `grantType` while using the error message for `rawTokenId`, so `rawTokenId` may be null. `encodeTokenId` then silently concatenates it as the literal string `null`, producing a syntactically valid encoded ID that decodes to a different raw ID instead of failing fast. Check `rawTokenId` here to preserve token-ID integrity for SPI callers.

title: Removing the Context copy constructor breaks existing grant providers
body: `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context)` was removed rather than deprecated. This is a public nested type in the grant SPI, so external grant implementations compiled against the previous server SPI that clone their context will fail at runtime with `NoSuchMethodError`; source consumers also no longer compile. Retain the constructor (including the new `grantType` field) to preserve provider compatibility.

title: Grant shortcuts are not constrained to the fixed two-character encoding
body: The encoder/parser protocol assumes exactly two characters for every grant shortcut: encoding concatenates the shortcut into a six-character prefix, while `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects any prefix whose length is not six. `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` has no two-character constraint (its documentation even says shortcuts are usually three letters), and this factory stores custom shortcuts unchanged. A custom grant returning `foo` will successfully issue IDs such as `onrtfoo:<uuid>`, but those IDs cannot be decoded and will throw `IllegalArgumentException`. Validate shortcut length/format and uniqueness at registration, or make the wire format length-delimited.

title: rawTokenId is never null-checked
body: The fourth null check checks `grantType` a second time instead of `rawTokenId`. Consequently an `AccessTokenContext` with a null raw token ID can be constructed despite the error message and apparent invariant; the default encoder then serializes it as the literal string `null`. Check `rawTokenId` here so malformed contexts fail at construction.

title: Access-token event matcher does not validate the expected grant shortcut
body: The matcher extracts `substring(3, 5)`, but in the six-character prefix the grant shortcut is at indexes 4 and 5 (`substring(4, 6)`). It also returns `false` when the extracted value equals the expected shortcut. For normal expected shortcuts such as `ac`, `rt`, `dg`, and `ci`, the condition is false and the matcher accepts any six-character context prefix as long as the suffix is a UUID. Thus the updated integration assertions do not test that the emitted grant encoding is correct. Require a six-character prefix and return the equality comparison for `substring(4, 6)`.

title: Access-token ID matcher rejects valid grant shortcuts
body: `isAccessTokenId` compares the wrong substring and inverts the result. For a valid ID such as `onrtac:<uuid>`, `substring(3, 5)` is `ta`, not the grant shortcut `ac` at positions 4-6, so the authorization-code expectation returns false. Conversely, an ID whose incorrectly selected characters happen to match the expected shortcut is rejected. This causes the updated event assertions to fail for valid tokens (or accept invalid ones), so they do not validate the new format.

title: Decoder cannot handle shortcuts permitted by the grant-factory contract
body: The decoder hard-requires the encoded context to be exactly six characters, which means every grant shortcut must be exactly two characters. `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` neither enforces that requirement nor documents it (its new Javadoc even says shortcuts are usually three letters). A custom grant provider returning a three-character shortcut can issue an access token successfully, but attempting to decode its token ID always throws `IllegalArgumentException`. Validate and reject non-two-character shortcuts during factory initialization, or make the encoding self-delimiting/length-aware and document the supported format.

title: Public Context copy constructor was removed without replacement
body: This change removes the public `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context)` constructor. Grant-type implementations in other modules/providers can use that constructor to preserve the request context while deriving a context, and will now fail to compile (or fail with `NoSuchMethodError` if compiled against the prior version). The added `grantType` field does not require removing the constructor; retain it and copy the new field to avoid this SPI compatibility break.

title: Constructor does not validate raw token ID
body: The fourth null check mistakenly validates `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId`. As a result, callers can construct an `AccessTokenContext` with a null raw ID despite the error message and apparent contract; encoding then produces an ID ending in the literal string `null` rather than failing fast. Check `rawTokenId` in this call.

title: Regenerating into user storage leaves an older local recovery-code credential active
body: When a federated user previously had recovery codes stored locally (for example, while its user-storage provider did not support this credential type), and the provider later accepts updateCredential, this branch writes the new codes to user storage but does not delete the existing local recovery-code credential. The code now intentionally considers both sources (getCredential falls back to local storage), and credential validation/future provider configuration changes can therefore make the superseded local recovery codes usable again. Recovery-code regeneration must revoke all prior codes; remove or replace the local credential when creation in user storage succeeds.

title: The added user-storage recovery-code implementation does not consume successful codes
body: isValid returns true when a submitted code is present in the stored list but never removes or marks that code as used. Recovery authentication codes are one-time credentials, so the same code can be replayed indefinitely in the newly added integration fixture. Consequently, the new login test only proves initial validation and cannot catch regressions in code consumption or exhausted-code handling; the fixture should update its stored recovery-code state after a successful validation and the test should verify that a used code is rejected.

title: Creating codes in user storage leaves any prior local recovery credential active
body: When a user storage provider starts accepting recovery-code updates, this path returns after `updateCredential` succeeds and does not remove an existing local `recovery-authn-codes` credential. This can occur for users whose codes were previously created locally because the provider did not support the type, or after a provider configuration/upgrade change. The local credential provider replaces its own credential during regeneration, but here the old local codes remain. Credential validation can still fall back to that local credential when the new user-storage credential rejects an old code, so previously issued recovery codes can remain valid after the user regenerates them. On successful user-storage creation, the implementation needs to invalidate/remove any local credential of this type (or otherwise ensure validation cannot use it).

title: Recovery codes stored by the user-storage provider are never consumed
body: The recovery-code validation path only checks whether the submitted code is present in the deserialized list and never removes that code or updates the stored credential. Consequently, every recovery code created through this user storage remains valid indefinitely and can be replayed after a successful login, violating the one-time-use security property of recovery codes. The storage provider must atomically mark/remove the matched code on successful validation, and the integration test should authenticate with the same code twice and verify the second attempt fails.

title: Federated recovery credential reconstruction drops the persisted credential identity
body: `recoveryCodesModel` has a generated ID when it is persisted, but `createFromValues` is called with only the codes, creation time, and label, so the returned credential cannot retain that persisted ID. Consumers now use this reconstructed federated credential; in particular, the recovery authenticator removes an exhausted credential by the returned ID. That ID is null or a newly generated value rather than the stored credential ID, so cleanup/removal cannot reliably target the provider's credential and credential metadata has an unstable identity. Preserve the persisted ID (and other persisted metadata such as the label) when exposing the `CredentialModel` from `getCredentials`.

title: The concurrent reader is not joined before asserting failures
body: The test sets `deletedAll` and immediately asserts that `caughtExceptions` is empty, but the reader thread may already be inside `groups(...)` and can add an exception after this assertion has passed. This allows the regression test to pass even when the concurrent read fails, and leaves a live background thread running into subsequent test/realm cleanup. Signal the thread to stop, join it with a timeout, and only then assert the collected failures (and fail on timeout).

title: Concurrent reader is neither synchronized with nor awaited by the test
body: The test starts a raw reader thread but never waits for it to begin issuing requests or to terminate. The deleting thread can delete all groups and set `deletedAll` before the reader is scheduled at all, so this test can pass without exercising the concurrent access race. Conversely, a request already in progress can add an exception after the assertion at line 157 has run. Coordinate startup (for example with a latch) and join/await the reader after setting the stop flag before asserting the captured failures.

title: The concurrent reader thread is never joined before asserting failures
body: The test sets `deletedAll` and immediately asserts that `caughtExceptions` is empty, but the reader may already be executing a request (or enter its catch block) when the assertion runs. An exception from that in-flight request can therefore be added after the assertion, allowing the test to pass despite the regression. The unjoined thread can also continue running into subsequent test/realm cleanup. Keep the thread reference and join it after signalling termination (with a timeout), then assert its completion and collected exceptions.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate DateTime audit-log ordering
body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the ordered field value. The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so once any results are returned, cursor construction calls this method with a `datetime` and raises `TypeError` (`datetime` does not implement floor/ceil). Subsequent cursor requests would also pass the integer cursor value directly to a datetime comparison in `build_queryset`. As a result, an authorized caller using `optimized_pagination=true` receives a 500 instead of audit-log results. This paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible key serialization and cursor deserialization, or the endpoint must use a paginator that supports datetime keys.

title: Advanced negative offsets cause Django QuerySet slicing errors
body: The advanced branch deliberately passes a negative `start_offset` to a Django `QuerySet` slice, but Django does not support negative indexing/slicing for querysets and raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The cursor parser accepts signed integer offsets, so an administrator can trigger this path with an `optimized_pagination=true` request containing a cursor with a negative offset, producing a 500. Negative offsets must be rejected or translated into a supported query; they cannot be used as Python-style reverse indexes on querysets.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs
body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the ordered field value. The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so each result has a `datetime` value and cursor construction raises `TypeError` on the first optimized request. Unlike `DateTimePaginator`, this class neither converts datetimes to a numeric cursor value nor converts cursor values back to datetimes for the ranged query. Consequently, an administrator requesting `optimized_pagination=true` receives a 500 rather than audit-log results.

title: Advanced negative-offset path uses unsupported Django queryset slicing
body: The new advanced path passes a negative `start_offset` directly to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing or slicing and raise an error rather than interpreting it as reverse/boundary pagination. Cursor parsing accepts negative offsets (`Cursor.from_string` converts the offset with `int`), so an authorized caller can cause the optimized audit-log endpoint to return a 500 with a cursor such as `0:-1:0`; the advertised reverse-pagination feature is not functional.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs
body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `get_item_key` receives an `AuditLogEntry.datetime` value. This implementation calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on that `datetime`, which raises `TypeError` when `build_cursor` processes the first page. Consequently, any authorized request using `optimized_pagination=true` will return a 500 rather than audit-log results. The optimized paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible datetime cursor conversion (or must inherit/use that implementation).

title: Advanced negative cursor offsets cause Django queryset slicing errors
body: The advanced path passes a negative `start_offset` into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets explicitly reject negative indexing/slicing and raise an error; they do not handle it automatically as the comment states. Since cursor offsets are parsed from client-provided cursor strings, an authorized caller can trigger a 500 with a negative offset while `optimized_pagination=true` is enabled. Negative offsets must be rejected or translated into a valid query rather than passed to a QuerySet slice.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate the audit-log datetime field
body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` while ordering by `-datetime`, but this paginator's `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `item.datetime`. Django model datetimes are `datetime` objects, so even the first optimized request reaches `build_cursor` and raises `TypeError` rather than returning a page. It also lacks the datetime cursor conversion implemented by `DateTimePaginator`, so cursor-following requests would compare the datetime column to a raw integer. The optimized paginator must support datetime keys (for example, subclass/use `DateTimePaginator` behavior) before it can be used by this endpoint.

title: Changing live Redis set keys to sorted sets is not rollout-compatible
body: Existing buffered segments are Redis Sets (`SADD`/`SSCAN`), while this change writes the identical `span-buf:s:{...}` keys with `ZADD` and the Lua script reads/merges them with sorted-set commands. During a rolling deployment, any segment created by an old worker and still within its TTL will cause `ZADD`, `ZCARD`, or `ZUNIONSTORE` to fail with Redis `WRONGTYPE`; the processing batch then fails and spans cannot be buffered. Use versioned keys or a migration/compatibility path until all old keys have expired.

title: Reducing redirect traversal can split deep traces into incorrect segments
body: The redirect-chain traversal limit was reduced from 10,000 to 1,000 with no fallback or indication that the chain was truncated. For a trace whose spans arrive in an order that creates more than 1,000 redirects, the script stops before reaching the actual segment key, writes the new span under an intermediate key, and records a redirect to that intermediate key. Those buffers can flush separately, producing incomplete/incorrect segments. Retain the prior bound or explicitly handle a truncated traversal so the span is joined to the true root.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate AuditLogEntry datetime keys
body: This endpoint orders by `-datetime`, but `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on the value of that field. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a `datetime`, not a numeric value, so an authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true` will raise a TypeError while constructing cursors and return a 500. The optimized paginator needs datetime key conversion equivalent to `DateTimePaginator`, or this endpoint must continue to use a datetime-aware paginator.

title: Deploying this script against existing set-backed buffers causes Redis WRONGTYPE failures
body: Existing buffered segment keys were created as Redis SETs by the previous version. This script now executes `ZCARD` and `ZUNIONSTORE` on those same keys. Redis does not permit ZSET commands on SET values, so any trace with an in-flight pre-deployment buffer will make the script fail with WRONGTYPE, failing span processing until the old key expires (up to `redis_ttl`, normally an hour). A rollout-compatible migration/fallback or a versioned key namespace is required.

title: max_segment_spans configuration is no longer honored
body: `max_segment_spans` remains a constructor parameter and instance attribute, but the only enforcement was removed from `_load_segment_data`; the Lua script instead always retains 1000 members. Deployments that configure a different limit now silently get a hard-coded retention policy, and segments over the configured limit are emitted rather than skipped as before. Either pass the configured limit to Lua and enforce it there, or remove/change the public configuration deliberately.

title: Reducing redirect traversal depth can split deep traces into separate segments
body: The redirect-chain traversal limit was reduced from 10,000 to 1,000. For a trace whose parent/child buffers form a chain deeper than 1,000, resolution stops before reaching the actual segment root; subsequent spans are merged into an intermediate buffer and flushed as a separate segment. This changes the prior supported depth and produces incorrect segment assignments for deep traces.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate the audit-log datetime field
body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the ordering value. The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so once results are fetched, `value` is a `datetime` and cursor construction raises `TypeError`. Any administrator using `optimized_pagination=true` on this endpoint will receive a 500 response. This paginator needs datetime key conversion equivalent to `DateTimePaginator`, or the endpoint must use a paginator compatible with datetime ordering.

title: Changing existing span buffer keys from sets to sorted sets has no rollout compatibility
body: This now writes `ZADD` to the existing `span-buf:s:*` keys, while buffers created by the currently deployed version are Redis Sets. Redis will return WRONGTYPE for `ZADD` (and the new Lua script's `ZCARD`) until every old key expires, causing `process_spans` batches for affected traces to fail and preventing those spans from being buffered. A production rollout needs a key-version/migration strategy or compatibility handling for old Set keys during the Redis TTL window.

title: Configured max_segment_spans is ignored and replaced by a hard-coded eviction limit
body: `SpansBuffer` still exposes and stores `max_segment_spans`, but the Lua script always retains 1000 members and receives no configured limit argument. Deployments which set a different `max_segment_spans` value will silently have their configuration ignored; unlike the prior behavior, excess data is also silently evicted rather than detected and skipped by `_load_segment_data`. Pass the configured limit to the script (and define the intended overflow behavior) or remove the unsupported configuration contract.

title: Discover upsampling is enabled for mixed and negated event-type queries
body: The Discover eligibility check is a substring match for `event.type:error`, rather than establishing that the query can only return errors. Queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` and `!event.type:error` contain that substring but can return transactions (which do not have the error sampling weight). Those requests will be rewritten to `upsampled_count()`, producing a weighted/missing-value total instead of the requested event count. Parse or otherwise constrain the event-type condition so the rewrite only occurs when every returned event is known to be an error.

title: Eligibility is checked against the outer dataset rather than the dataset being queried
body: `_get_event_stats` accepts `scoped_dataset`, including calls made for dashboard split queries, but passes the captured outer `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. In the metrics-enhanced dashboard split path, an error-only query is executed against `discover` while the captured dataset remains a metrics dataset, so `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns false and the error result is not upsampled. Pass `scoped_dataset` to the eligibility check so the decision describes the query that will actually execute.

title: Weighted counts are truncated to integers
body: `upsampled_count` wraps `sum(sample_weight)` in `toInt64`. Sampling rates are represented as floats (the added test factory explicitly converts `client_sample_rate` to `float`), and rates such as 0.3 produce non-integral inverse weights. Casting the aggregate truncates the estimate, systematically undercounting every bucket; summing multiple fractional weights can also lose a full event. Return the sum as a numeric value, or use an explicitly specified rounding policy if integer output is required.

title: The PR accidentally adds a gitlink pinned to the base commit
body: This entry is a submodule/gitlink pointing at the base revision, but no corresponding `.gitmodules` configuration is included. Clones of this revision will receive an uninitialized `sentry-repo` directory and tooling may attempt to initialize an undefined submodule. Remove this unrelated repository entry unless adding a properly configured submodule is intentional.

title: Discover upsampling is enabled for mixed or negated event-type queries
body: The discover eligibility check is a raw substring match for `event.type:error`, which does not establish that the query contains only error events. Queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` and `!event.type:error` both match and will replace `count()` with `sum(sample_weight)`. Transaction rows do not have error sampling weights, so their events are omitted or incorrectly weighted, producing incorrect counts. Parse/inspect the query condition and enable this only when it constrains the result set exclusively to error events.

title: Upsampling eligibility is evaluated against the outer dataset rather than the dataset being queried
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, including calls made for dashboard discover splits, but passes the closed-over original `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. For example, a metrics-enhanced dashboard that is split into a `discover` error query evaluates eligibility as a metrics dataset and never applies upsampling. The decision needs to use `scoped_dataset` so the columns match the actual query being executed.

title: Upsampled counts truncate fractional sample weights
body: The custom aggregate wraps `sum(sample_weight)` in `toInt64`. Sample weights derived from arbitrary client sampling rates are not necessarily integral (for example, a 0.3 sample rate produces an expected weight near 3.33), so truncating the aggregate silently undercounts sampled errors. Return the sum as a numeric/float result unless the stored sample-weight contract guarantees integral values.

title: Aliased count aggregations are not upsampled
body: Only a column whose entire text is exactly `count()` is transformed. Valid selected aggregations such as `count() as errors` remain raw counts even when every project is allowlisted, yielding inconsistent and incorrect results depending solely on whether the caller aliases the aggregation. Preserve and transform supported count aliases (and their output aliases) when rewriting query columns.

title: Allowlist changes leave cached count behavior stale with no invalidation integration
body: Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds, and although `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is provided, this PR does not connect it to changes of `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`. Consequently, enabling or disabling a project can continue returning raw or upsampled counts until TTL expiry, including returning upsampled counts after sampling has been disabled. Invalidate affected keys when the option changes, or avoid caching configuration whose changes must take effect immediately.

title: Discover upsampling is enabled for mixed event-type queries
body: The discover eligibility check only tests whether the raw query string contains `event.type:error`. A valid query such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` therefore gets rewritten to `upsampled_count()`, even though it includes transaction events. Transactions do not have `sample_weight` (as noted by `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` itself), so their rows will be omitted from or corrupt the summed count. Only enable this transformation after parsing/validating that the executed query excludes all non-error event types.

title: Upsampling eligibility is evaluated against the outer dataset instead of the dataset being queried
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, including the `discover` dataset used by dashboard split queries, but passes the enclosing `dataset` variable to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. Consequently, when a metrics-enhanced dashboard query is split into an error-only Discover query, the helper sees the original metrics dataset and refuses to upsample. The converse mismatch is also possible whenever this helper is called with a different scoped dataset. Pass `scoped_dataset` (and preferably the actual `query`) to the eligibility logic.

title: Aliased count aggregations are not upsampled
body: The transformation matches only a column whose entire text is exactly `count()`. Stats queries can use an aliased aggregation such as `count() as errors` (and query builders may produce aliases), which remains a raw count even for fully allowlisted error projects. This yields inconsistent and undercounted results depending only on the requested output alias. Parse the aggregation/alias or preserve the supplied alias while replacing the count function.

title: An unconfigured git submodule was added accidentally
body: This change adds a gitlink named `sentry-repo` pointing at the base commit, but no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry or repository URL is included. Fresh checkouts cannot initialize it and it contributes no usable source or configuration to the project. Remove this stray submodule entry unless the submodule configuration is intentionally added as part of the change.

title: Feature-flagged table widgets discard the query result
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, this branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with hard-coded empty `columns` and an empty `tableData` object rather than `fields`, `result.data`, and `result.meta`. Consequently every flagged dashboard table is blank regardless of the query result (and no loading/error behavior from the existing table is preserved). Pass the actual result data and metadata into the new visualization before enabling this path.

title: Error IDs can be paired with the wrong nodestore records
body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a mapping keyed by node ID and can omit records that are missing. Zipping the original `error_ids` with `events.values()` assumes both identical ordering and one value per requested ID. If any requested event is absent, all later IDs can be paired with another event's title/message/timestamp, causing the AI summary to receive incorrect error context. Look up each generated node ID explicitly and retain its associated error ID instead of consuming mapping values positionally.

title: Browser report timestamp/age invariants are not enforced for zero values or absent fields
body: Both `age` and `timestamp` are optional, and the mutual-exclusion validators test `self.initial_data.get(...)`. A report containing `age: 0` and `timestamp: 0` passes because both values are falsey; a report containing neither also passes. This accepts malformed reports despite the stated requirement to support one of the two spec formats, and allows ambiguous data to enter metrics processing. Check field presence (`"age" in initial_data` / `"timestamp" in initial_data`) and add object-level validation requiring exactly one of the two fields.

title: Feature-flagged table visualization discards all dashboard query results
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the new `TableWidgetVisualization` is always given `columns={[]}` and a hard-coded empty `tableData` object instead of `result.data`, `result.meta`, and the widget fields. Consequently every table widget for organizations with this feature renders an empty table regardless of the query result, replacing the existing populated `StyledSimpleTableChart`.

title: Browser report validation permits reports with neither timestamp nor age
body: Both spec-specific fields are optional and validation only runs when one is supplied, so a report containing neither `timestamp` nor `age` is accepted and counted. The endpoint claims to support the two formats, each of which requires its respective timing field; accepting neither lets malformed reports pollute the collection metrics. Add object-level validation requiring exactly one of the two fields.

title: Mutual exclusion of age and timestamp fails for zero values
body: The checks use `self.initial_data.get(...)`, which treats `0` as absent. Thus a request with `timestamp: 0` and `age: 0` passes validation even though it mixes the two mutually exclusive reporting formats. Presence should be checked with key membership (or object-level validated data), not truthiness.

title: Error IDs can be paired with the wrong nodestore event when an event is missing
body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a mapping, but the implementation pairs `error_ids` with `events.values()` by position. If the backend omits a missing node from the mapping (as multi-get implementations commonly do), all subsequent values shift and error details are attributed to the wrong replay error IDs. Look up each result by its generated node ID and retain the corresponding original event ID rather than zipping with mapping values.

title: Falsy custom cell render results incorrectly invoke the fallback renderer
body: The documented renderer contract says fallback rendering occurs when a custom renderer returns `undefined`, but this code uses `if (cell)`. Intentional valid React render results such as `0`, an empty string, or `false` are treated as absent and replaced by the default field renderer. Test specifically for `cell !== undefined` (and make the same correction in the header renderer at line 31).

title: Feature-flagged table visualization discards all widget results
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, this branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and an empty `tableData` object instead of passing `result.data`, `result.meta`, the widget fields, loading state, or configured columns. Every table widget for an organization with this flag will therefore render as an empty table regardless of the query result, making the feature unusable.

title: Mutually exclusive age and timestamp fields are accepted when one is zero
body: The exclusivity checks use truthiness (`self.initial_data.get(...)`) rather than field presence. Valid numeric zero values are falsy, so a report containing `age: 0` and `timestamp` (or `timestamp: 0` and `age`) passes validation even though the endpoint intends to reject reports mixing the two Reporting API formats. Check key presence/non-None instead so zero-valued fields do not bypass validation.

title: Attribute-key query cache is not scoped to the organization
body: The new React Query key contains only `queryOptions`, which has dates, projects, type, and item type but no organization slug. Unlike the previous `useApiQuery` key, it therefore aliases requests from different organizations that happen to use the same project IDs and filters. On organization navigation, cached attribute names from the prior organization can be returned before/refetch instead of the current organization's attributes, leaking metadata across organization boundaries. Include `organization.slug` (or the endpoint URL) in the query key.

title: New installations can bypass the GitHub-user verification when the webhook record is not present
body: When no `Integration` row exists yet, this returns `pipeline.next_step()` before checking `github_authenticated_user` against an installer identity. The identity used by the later check is populated asynchronously from the GitHub installation webhook, so a user can complete the setup callback before that webhook has created the row (or when webhook delivery failed) and link an arbitrary known installation ID to their Sentry organization. This is precisely the path where the proposed authorization check is unavailable; the flow should wait for/require a verified installation sender record rather than treating a missing record as safe.

title: Existing integrations without webhook sender metadata cause a server error
body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes every active existing GitHub integration has a sender object. Integrations created through the previous setup flow did not populate this metadata (and the normal setup test's expected metadata has no `sender`), so if such an integration has no OrganizationIntegration—for example after uninstalling and attempting to install it into another organization—this raises `KeyError` and returns a 500 instead of the installation failure response. Handle missing or malformed legacy metadata explicitly, ideally by rejecting it safely or obtaining a verified sender.

title: New installations bypass the GitHub installer identity check
body: When there is no existing `Integration` row for the supplied installation ID, this branch immediately advances the pipeline without comparing the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user to the app installation sender. The integration is then created from the installation ID in a later pipeline step. Consequently, a Sentry organization administrator who knows or obtains another GitHub App installation ID can authorize with their own GitHub account and attach an installation that has not yet been recorded by Sentry (for example before its webhook is processed) to their Sentry organization, potentially gaining Sentry-mediated access to that installation's repositories. The validation must also be enforced for the first creation of an integration, using a trustworthy installer identity rather than only existing webhook-backed records.

title: Legacy or pipeline-created integrations without sender metadata cause a 500
body: The comparison indexes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` unconditionally. Integrations created by the normal pipeline do not populate `sender` in `build_integration`, and integrations created before this change also lack it (the updated basic-flow test still asserts metadata without `sender`). If such an active integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed and is installed again, this path raises `KeyError` instead of returning the installation failure response. Handle absent sender metadata explicitly and provide a safe validation/migration path.

title: OAuth transport and user-info failures escape as server errors
body: Only parsing the access-token response is guarded. `safe_urlopen` can raise for a GitHub/network HTTP failure, and `get_user_info` can raise when the returned token is rejected or the user API is unavailable. Either exception escapes the pipeline and returns a 500 rather than the intended invalid-installation response. Catch the expected HTTP/API exceptions around both the token exchange and user lookup and return `error(...)` so invalid, reused, or failed OAuth codes fail safely as described.

title: Fresh installations bypass the GitHub installer identity check
body: When the installation webhook has not yet created an `Integration`, this branch immediately advances the pipeline without checking the GitHub user that installed the app. The OAuth step and app-install step are separate browser interactions, so a user can authorize OAuth as one GitHub account and then install the app as another account (or simply win the race against webhook delivery); the subsequent integration creation has no installer identity to compare. This leaves the exact fresh-install/race case unprotected despite the new validation requirement. The pipeline must defer completion until a trusted installer identity is available, or otherwise obtain and validate it before creating the integration.

title: Installer validation crashes for integrations without sender metadata
body: The code indexes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` unconditionally. Existing GitHub integrations, and integrations created through the normal build path when no webhook sender has been attached, can have metadata without `sender` (the updated basic-flow test itself expects metadata with no sender). If such an active integration exists without an organization integration, for example during recovery/reinstallation or after an older installation, this produces a KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the intended failed-installation response. Treat missing sender information as an unverifiable installation and return `error` (or implement a safe migration/lookup).

title: OAuth exchange and user lookup failures are not converted to installation failures
body: Only parsing `safe_urlread` is protected by the try block. `safe_urlopen` can fail for GitHub HTTP/network errors, and `get_user_info` can fail when GitHub rejects the newly exchanged token or its `/user` request fails. Those exceptions escape the pipeline and result in a 500, rather than the failed-installation page promised for invalid/reused codes or token generation failures. Catch the relevant HTTP/API exceptions around both the exchange and user-info request and return `error`.

title: `queued` is evaluated once at module import rather than per assignment source
body: `timezone.now()` is called while the dataclass is defined, so every `AssignmentSource` created by this worker process receives the same `queued` timestamp. Consequently `to_dict()` emits a startup-time value rather than the time the webhook assignment was queued, making the context metadata incorrect and unusable for ordering, expiration, or debugging. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance gets its own timestamp.

title: `queued` is evaluated once when the module is imported
body: `timezone.now()` is evaluated while defining the dataclass, so every `AssignmentSource` constructed without an explicit `queued` value receives the same import-time timestamp rather than the time that webhook-triggered assignment was queued. This makes the context metadata incorrect for the lifetime of a worker process (and would break any future age/ordering logic based on this field). Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance captures its own creation time.

title: `queued` is evaluated once at module import rather than per AssignmentSource
body: `timezone.now()` is executed when the dataclass is defined, so every `AssignmentSource` created for the lifetime of a worker/process receives the same `queued` timestamp. This makes the serialized context inaccurate and would break any ordering, expiration, or debugging based on when an assignment was queued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance records its own creation time.

title: Registered metric alert handler is now uninstantiable
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` but implements none of its abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). Because `MetricAlertFire` registers this class as its `detector_handler`, accessing `detector.detector_handler` for a metric-alert detector will raise `TypeError` instead of returning a handler, causing detector processing to fail. Keep this handler on the non-stateful base until it is implemented, or provide all required implementations.

title: Evaluate documentation still describes the old list return type
body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` now returns a dictionary keyed by group key, but its docstring says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". This is the public extension point for detector implementations, so the stale documentation can cause new handlers to implement or consume the previous contract incorrectly.

title: Registered metric-alert handler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now inherits `StatefulDetectorHandler` but implements none of its required abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). Because `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` points at this class, resolving `Detector.detector_handler` for a detector of this type calls `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(self)` and raises `TypeError` instead of returning a handler. Either retain a concrete no-op handler until metric alerts are implemented or implement all required methods.

title: Registered metric alert handler is abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now inherits `StatefulDetectorHandler` but implements none of its required abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). `Detector.detector_handler` instantiates the registered handler with `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, so processing any detector whose type is `metric_alert_fire` will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` rather than safely returning no results as before. Either keep this type on a concrete no-op handler until it is implemented, or implement the stateful handler contract.

title: New group-key evaluation test builds the expected occurrence for a different group key
body: `test_dedupe` constructs its expected occurrence with group key `"val1"`, but invokes `evaluate_group_key_value` with `expected_result.group_key`, which is `"group_key"`. The occurrence fingerprint is generated from the group key, so the expected fingerprint is `<detector id>:val1` while the actual occurrence fingerprint is `<detector id>:group_key`; as a result this assertion will fail once `IssueOccurrence` value equality is applied. Build the expected occurrence using `"group_key"`.

title: Removing the existing mark_failed module helpers breaks their import contract
body: This refactor deletes `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, and `get_monitor_environment_context` from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` rather than retaining compatibility aliases or updating all consumers. Any existing worker code, integrations, or tests importing these previously available functions will now fail with `ImportError` at startup/test collection. Keep forwarding aliases in this module (at least for the renamed functions) or update every import site as part of the change.

title: Return the normalized monitor config in occurrence context
body: `get_monitor_environment_context` copies the monitor config and replaces `schedule_type` with its display value in the local `config` variable, but the returned context uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead.
