body: `enableSqlExpressions` returns false regardless of the global `sqlExpressions` flag value, so deployments that have configured the documented flag cannot enable the feature and receive "sqlExpressions is not implemented" instead. The PR leaves the feature-toggle documentation unchanged despite changing that configuration contract. Update the documentation to state that SQL expressions are disabled/removed (and that the flag has no effect), or remove the stale flag documentation.

title: The security disablement has no automated regression coverage
body: No test is added to verify that a `QueryTypeSQL` query is rejected even when `FlagSqlExpressions` is globally enabled. The legacy `UnmarshalSQLCommand` path also bypasses this reader and is only disabled indirectly because the replacement DB returns "not implemented". Add regression tests for both entry points which assert that SQL is rejected before it can be parsed or executed; otherwise a future attempt to restore the DB implementation or simplify the feature check can reintroduce the RCE/LFI path without test detection.

title: Add an automated regression test for the SQL-expression kill switch
body: This security-critical rejection has no accompanying test. In particular, a test should construct an SQL expression while `FlagSqlExpressions` is globally enabled (the state that previously allowed this path) and assert that parsing/command creation is rejected and cannot reach SQL execution. Without this coverage, the redundant unconditional-false toggle logic or the placeholder database implementation can be inadvertently simplified or re-enabled later, reintroducing the RCE/LFI path without CI detecting it.

title: The permanent SQL-expression disablement has no regression coverage
body: This PR changes no test files, so there is no test that verifies a `QueryTypeSQL` query is rejected when `FlagSqlExpressions` is enabled. That is the primary security boundary here: `enableSqlExpressions` intentionally returns false in both toggle states. Add coverage for the enabled-toggle case (and the legacy `UnmarshalSQLCommand` path, which is disabled through the stub DB) so a future cleanup cannot inadvertently re-enable the RCE/LFI-prone implementation.

title: The error message and retained feature-toggle documentation misstate the feature status
body: SQL expressions are now deliberately disabled regardless of the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle, but this reports only that they are "not implemented." Operators who have enabled the documented toggle will receive a misleading error and have no indication that their configuration is intentionally ignored due to the security removal. Update the user-facing error and feature-toggle documentation to state that SQL expressions are disabled/removed and, where appropriate, reference the security advisory.

title: Concurrent callers can build and publish different indexes for the same key
body: The cache is now locked only when assigning `b.cache[key]`, so two callers can both observe a missing index in `GetIndex` and execute the full `BuildIndex` concurrently for the same NamespacedResource. For file-backed indexes, the second `bleve.New` attempts to create the same directory and fails, causing otherwise valid searches or watch-event indexing to fail. For memory indexes, whichever build finishes last replaces the cache with its snapshot; that snapshot can predate writes indexed by the other build, making recently written documents disappear from the active index. Coordinate cache lookup and creation per key (for example, with keyed singleflight) while allowing distinct keys to build concurrently.

title: Eager startup makes normal shutdown able to panic on a closed watch channel
body: `NewResourceServer` now always calls `Init`, which starts this watcher even if the server never handles an RPC. When the SQL backend is stopped, its poller closes the event stream; receiving from that closed channel yields a nil `*WrittenEvent`, and the immediately following accesses to `v.Type` and `v.Key` panic. The equivalent unchecked receive in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go` line 209 has the same problem for the search watcher. Receive with `v, ok := <-events` and exit when `ok` is false (and ensure the goroutines observe cancellation) so an idle server can start and stop safely.

title: Constructor failures leave initialized background services running
body: If `s.search.init` succeeds but `s.initWatcher` subsequently fails, this path returns `nil, err` without cancelling `s.ctx` or stopping the lifecycle hooks. `search.init` has already started a watch loop using `context.Background()`, so the discarded server can continue polling the backend indefinitely; the successfully initialized lifecycle resources are also never stopped. This is newly reachable because initialization now occurs inside the constructor and the caller receives no server instance on which to call `Stop`. Clean up/cancel initialized components before returning a constructor error, and do not use an uncancellable background context for the search watcher.

title: Concurrent builds of the same namespace can replace a newer index with a stale one
body: Removing the mutex around the full build leaves only the final map assignment synchronized. Two concurrent Search requests (or a Search and the watch handler) can both observe a cache miss for the same NamespacedResource and build from different storage snapshots. If the build using the older snapshot completes last, this assignment replaces the index that already included a newer write, and subsequent searches permanently omit that write until another event happens to repair the index. File-backed indexes can also have concurrent bleve.New calls for the same directory. Coordinate builds per cache key (for example with a keyed singleflight/building map) and only publish one reconciled index.

title: Failed eager initialization leaks initialized lifecycle resources and watchers
body: NewResourceServer now returns immediately on s.Init failure without cancelling s.ctx or invoking the Lifecycle Stop hook. This is observable when Lifecycle.Init succeeds but search initialization or initWatcher later fails: the constructor returns no server handle to the caller, while initialized resources remain active. In particular, search.init may already have created its background WatchWriteEvents goroutine before initWatcher fails. Clean up the partially initialized server (cancel it and stop initialized lifecycle components) before returning the construction error.

title: The storage-server integration test is no longer run for PostgreSQL
body: PostgreSQL is a supported unified-storage backend, but this change unconditionally skips this integration test for it. The test therefore no longer validates the storage-server startup path on PostgreSQL, precisely where initialization has moved from the first RPC into construction. The underlying PostgreSQL/Drone failure should be fixed or isolated rather than removing this coverage.

title: Startup index build drops writes committed while indexes are being built
body: The indexes are populated from ListIterator snapshots before the write-event watch is opened. The SQL WatchWriteEvents implementation initializes its cursor from the latest resource versions at subscription time, so any write committed after an index's list snapshot but before this call is treated as already seen and is never sent to handleEvent. In HA deployments, writes from another server during startup can therefore leave added documents missing, modified documents stale, or deleted documents searchable until another relevant write occurs. Start/buffer the watch before building, or replay events from the resource version returned by each build.

title: Closing a backend watch channel can panic the server during shutdown
body: This receive does not check the channel's ok result before dereferencing v. A normal backend shutdown closes its event channel (the SQL poller closes its stream), after which this loop receives a nil *WrittenEvent and panics while evaluating v.Type. Stop invokes Lifecycle.Stop before s.cancel, and this PR now starts initWatcher during every ResourceServer construction, so even servers that never serve a request can hit this shutdown crash. Exit the loop when the channel is closed and make the loop observe cancellation.

title: The eagerly started search watcher panics when its event stream closes
body: The search watcher also receives from events without checking whether the channel was closed. On normal SQL backend shutdown the poller closes the stream, causing v to be nil and handleEvent to dereference it. This is now started during construction whenever search is configured, and it uses context.Background(), so server cancellation does not stop it. Check the receive ok value and use a server-owned cancellable context for the watcher.

title: Parallel index workers race on totalBatchesIndexed
body: errgroup runs these functions concurrently when WorkerThreads is greater than one, but each one increments the shared totalBatchesIndexed integer without synchronization. This is a Go data race, causes race-detector failures, and can emit an incorrect tracing count. Use an atomic counter or collect per-worker results after the group completes.

title: Failed eager initialization leaves partially started resources running
body: If search.init succeeds and starts its watch goroutine but initWatcher subsequently fails, NewResourceServer returns an error without calling cancel or Lifecycle.Stop. No ResourceServer is returned to the caller, so it cannot later be stopped; the search watcher is particularly leaked because it was created with context.Background(). Ensure constructor failure cleans up the server context and any successfully initialized lifecycle resources before returning the error.

title: The new passkey predicate is invoked with the wrong signature
body: `UsernameForm` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the predicate added on `UsernamePasswordForm` is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. No no-argument overload is declared in this class hierarchy, so this does not compile. Pass `context.getUser()` to the predicate (or provide a matching overload) before merging.

title: Conditional passkeys are no longer initialized for an initial login
body: The new predicate returns false whenever `context.getUser()` is null. This predicate now guards `fillContextForm` in both `authenticate` and the error challenge path, whereas the previous code explicitly initialized conditional WebAuthn when no user had been selected. Initial browser logins necessarily have no context user, including discoverable-passkey login, so the form no longer receives the conditional-UI flag, RP/challenge data, or WebAuthn form and users cannot start a normal passkey login. The predicate/call sites must still initialize conditional passkeys when the feature and realm policy are enabled with no selected user.

title: Call to a nonexistent no-argument passkeys helper prevents compilation
body: `UsernameForm` invokes `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but its superclass only defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` (and no inherited no-argument overload is present). This is a Java compilation error, so the services module cannot be built. Pass `context.getUser()` (or add the intended overload) before merging.

title: Initial unauthenticated passkey login no longer initializes the WebAuthn form
body: The new shared condition calls `fillContextForm` only when `context.getUser()` is non-null, because `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` explicitly requires a user. On the initial login page there is normally no selected user, so no WebAuthn challenge or conditional-UI form attributes are generated. As a result the login form no longer renders/starts the passkey conditional UI for unauthenticated users, breaking the normal passwordless/passkey login path (and contradicting the existing tests that expect `#webauth` on the first page). Preserve the previous realm-feature check for the initial no-user form, while also enabling the selected-user reauthentication case.

title: Call to conditional-passkey helper has no matching overload
body: `UsernameForm` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the helper added in its superclass is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. No no-argument overload is defined in this class hierarchy shown by this change, so the services module will fail to compile. Pass `context.getUser()` (or add a deliberate no-argument overload) before merging.

title: Conditional passkeys are disabled for unauthenticated initial logins
body: The new helper returns false whenever `user` is null. `authenticate()` now relies exclusively on this helper before calling `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)`, but a normal initial UsernamePasswordForm login has no context user. As a result, the WebAuthn challenge and conditional-UI form attributes are no longer populated on the initial login page, so passkey conditional UI will not render or authenticate until a user is already selected. The previous code explicitly initialized WebAuthn in the `context.getUser() == null` branch; initialization needs to remain enabled for both anonymous initial login and re-authentication.

title: Login-list invalidation is skipped for updates made while an organization is disabled
body: `original` is obtained through this provider's `getById`, which wraps organization-linked providers so that `isEnabled()` is false when their organization is disabled. A caller can likewise pass the wrapped model returned by `session.identityProviders().getById()` to `update`. In that case, an update that changes a cached-list-relevant property (for example `hideOnLogin`, `BROKER_PUBLIC`, or the organization ID) while the organization is disabled makes both predicate evaluations false and returns at line 405 without invalidating the login-list keys. The lists themselves were populated from the raw JPA delegate, however, so they still contain IDs based on the static IDP properties. After the organization is enabled, an old organization query can return an IDP now linked to a different organization, or omit an IDP that became login-eligible. Invalidation decisions need to use the raw stored login properties or invalidate on these updates rather than using the organization-aware `isEnabled()` wrapper.

title: The new test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of created providers
body: Each of the twenty providers created in this test is registered for cleanup using `identityProviders().get("alias")`, not its actual `idp-alias-N` value; the additional provider at line 425 has the same problem. Cleanup therefore leaves the providers created by this test in the shared test realm (and may remove an unrelated provider actually named `alias`), allowing later tests or retries to observe polluted data and making their result counts non-deterministic. Register cleanup using the alias created for each representation.

title: Update invalidation uses organization-decorated state instead of the stored IDP state
body: `idpById` is obtained through `getById`, which wraps organization-bound providers and makes `isEnabled()` depend on the organization being enabled. The new login-cache invalidation predicate therefore sees an IDP in a disabled organization as not login-capable even when its stored `enabled` flag is true. For example, after a public IDP has been cached while its organization is disabled, changing it to `hideOnLogin=true`, `linkOnly=true`, or non-public makes both the decorated original and the updated model fail the predicate, so `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` does not clear the list cache. The cache-hit path reloads the IDP by ID but never reapplies the hide/link/public filters, so it can return the removed provider; once the organization is enabled again it can be displayed on the login page despite the update. Determine membership changes from the raw persisted original model (or invalidate for these field changes regardless of dynamic organization enablement).

title: The new test registers cleanup for a nonexistent identity-provider alias
body: The cleanup callbacks at lines 381 and 425 are bound to `identityProviders().get("alias")`, but this test only creates `idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-20`. Teardown therefore attempts to remove an unrelated/nonexistent provider and leaves the newly created providers in the test realm, which can leak state into later tests or cause duplicate-alias failures on reruns. Register cleanup using each generated alias instead.

title: Login-list invalidation uses an organization-aware original model
body: `original` is obtained through `getById()` in `update()`, which wraps organization-linked providers so that `isEnabled()` is false whenever their organization is disabled. The updated model is normally the raw model, however. Consequently, while an organization is disabled, changing a previously public/enabled provider to hidden, link-only, disabled, or non-public makes both predicates false and this early return leaves the login list cached. When the organization is enabled again, that cached list still contains the provider and `getForLogin()` does not reapply the hide/link/public predicate while resolving cached IDs, so the provider can be returned/displayed despite no longer qualifying. Determine eligibility from the persisted/raw original model (for example, load it from the delegate) rather than the organization-aware wrapper before deciding whether to invalidate.

title: New test cleanup registrations remove a nonexistent literal alias
body: Each provider created in the loop registers cleanup for `identityProviders().get("alias")` rather than for the generated `idp-alias-<n>` alias; the same mistake is repeated for `idp-alias-20` at line 425. The cleanup therefore does not remove the providers created by this test, which can leave test data behind and contaminate subsequent tests or cause cleanup failures. Register cleanup using the actual alias for each created representation.

title: Equal-priority crypto providers are now selected by classpath order
body: All built-in server providers return the same priority (200): DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider. This sort has no tie handling, so if more than one is present the selected provider is whichever ServiceLoader resource happens to be encountered first. Previously this configuration failed closed; now, for example, a deployment containing both the default and FIPS providers can silently select the non-FIPS provider. The collection also instantiates every provider before choosing one, so ignored providers still execute constructor side effects such as Java security-provider registration. Reject equal highest priorities (or define an explicit safe policy) rather than continuing with an arbitrary provider.

title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public ServiceLoader SPI, and making order() abstract is binary- and source-incompatible with implementations built against the previous interface. Existing provider jars will load but throw AbstractMethodError when CryptoIntegration sorts them and invokes order(), preventing application startup; source implementations no longer compile either. Provide a default order() implementation so existing providers remain usable, while allowing new implementations to override it.

title: ECDSA conversion accepts signatures with trailing bytes
body: concatenatedRSToASN1DER copies only the first signLength bytes and never checks signature.length. A fixed-width ECDSA JOSE R||S value with a valid signLength-byte prefix plus arbitrary trailing bytes is therefore converted to the same DER value as the original signature and can verify successfully. Conversely, short input produces an unchecked array-copy exception instead of a controlled invalid-signature result. Validate that signLength is valid and signature.length is exactly signLength before splitting R and S.

title: ES384 and ES512 tests do not use their required EC curves
body: The test creates one uninitialized EC KeyPairGenerator and reuses its default key pair for ES256, ES384, and ES512. On typical JDKs that is a P-256 key, so the ES384 and ES512 cases do not exercise P-384 and P-521 component sizes; in particular ES512 never exercises the long-form DER sequence length and 66-byte scalar handling expected for P-521. Generate keys explicitly with the curve corresponding to each algorithm and verify that the regenerated DER signature validates with the public key.

title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: `CryptoProvider` is a public ServiceLoader SPI, and adding `order()` as an abstract method makes every provider compiled against the previous interface incompatible. During `CryptoIntegration.init`, the comparator invokes `order()` on such a provider and throws `AbstractMethodError`, preventing startup even when that provider was the only valid provider before this change. Make this a default method with a legacy-safe priority (or otherwise provide a compatibility adapter) so existing implementations remain loadable.

title: Equal-priority crypto providers are silently selected by classpath order
body: The new selection logic accepts multiple providers with the same highest priority and chooses whichever ServiceLoader returns first. `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider`, and `FIPS1402Provider` are all assigned priority 200, so a classpath containing both default and FIPS providers no longer fails fast as it did previously; it can select the non-FIPS default provider based on classpath/resource ordering. This can silently disable the intended FIPS crypto integration. Reject ties for the highest priority (while still allowing lower-priority providers such as the authz client provider), or make selection explicitly configured and deterministic.

title: ECDSA raw signature conversion accepts and ignores trailing signature bytes
body: `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` copies exactly `signLength` bytes but never verifies that `signature.length` equals `signLength`. Any bytes after the expected R||S value are silently discarded, so distinct raw JOSE ECDSA signature values with the same prefix are converted to the same DER value and can be accepted by a verifier. Short inputs also fail with an unchecked array-copy exception rather than being treated as invalid signatures. Validate the exact fixed signature length up front and throw the declared `IOException` for malformed input.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns an unrelated JDK keystore provider
body: The `CryptoProvider` contract states that this method returns the Bouncy Castle provider, but this implementation returns the provider backing the JVM's default keystore. On a normal JVM that is typically `SUN`, not Bouncy Castle. Once this provider is selected by `CryptoIntegration`, callers relying on this method to obtain Bouncy Castle functionality receive an unrelated provider and may use unsupported algorithms or fail unexpectedly. A provider with no Bouncy Castle integration should report that absence consistently (as the Elytron provider does) or supply an actual Bouncy Castle provider.

title: ES384 and ES512 tests generate a default EC key instead of the algorithm's curve
body: All three tests use an unparameterized `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")`; in common JDKs this produces a P-256 key. Consequently the ES384 and ES512 cases sign P-256-sized R/S values and merely zero-pad them to 48 and 66 bytes, rather than exercising P-384 and P-521 signatures. In particular, the ES512 test does not cover the long-form DER sequence length used by real P-521 signatures, and it only round-trips through the same custom encoder/decoder rather than verifying the generated DER with the public key. Generate `secp256r1`, `secp384r1`, and `secp521r1` keys respectively and verify the converted DER signatures end-to-end.

title: Adding `order()` as an abstract SPI method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: `CryptoProvider` is a ServiceLoader SPI, so providers compiled against the previous interface do not implement this new abstract method. Such providers now fail to compile when rebuilt and can throw `AbstractMethodError` when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` compares them with another provider (for example, the newly added authz-client provider). Make this a default method with a backward-compatible priority (such as 0), so existing provider implementations remain usable.

title: Equal provider priorities make FIPS selection depend on classpath order
body: The built-in Default, Elytron, and FIPS providers all return priority 200. For providers with the same priority, this sort preserves the ServiceLoader encounter order, which is determined by classpath/resource order rather than an explicit security policy. Consequently, when both the default and FIPS service descriptors are visible, the default provider can be selected and the FIPS provider merely logged as ignored; previously this unsafe combination failed fast. Give the intended FIPS provider a distinct higher priority or reject ties for the highest priority.

title: The selected authz crypto provider cannot perform documented JWT client authentication
body: `AuthzClient.create` initializes this provider in a standalone authz-client runtime, but this implementation throws `UnsupportedOperationException` for both PEM handling here and JWS signature creation in `getSignature` (line 219). The authz client documents JWT client credentials as a supported credential type; that flow must parse the configured private key and sign a client assertion, so it will fail once this provider is selected. Provide the standard JCA/PEM implementations for these operations, or avoid installing this incomplete provider as the global CryptoIntegration provider.

title: ES384 and ES512 tests do not use their required elliptic curves
body: All three tests use an uninitialized generic EC key generator, which normally produces a P-256 key. Thus the ES384 and ES512 cases sign with P-256 coordinates padded to the requested output length, rather than exercising P-384 and P-521 coordinate sizes and DER edge cases. The test also only checks conversion round-tripping, not whether the reconstructed signature verifies. Initialize keys explicitly to secp256r1, secp384r1, and secp521r1 respectively and verify the converted signature.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never upgraded with the Clients schema
body: `init` returns as soon as an admin-permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore retain an authorization server containing only the Users resource and its scopes; they never receive the Clients all-resource or the new configure/map-role scopes. Creating a Client permission in such a realm will fail when `getOrCreateResource` cannot find the new scopes, and global Client permission evaluation can encounter a missing all-Clients resource. Initialization must reconcile and add missing schema scopes/resources for existing clients rather than treating their presence as proof that the schema is current.

title: A realm-wide Clients/manage grant does not grant global view or list access
body: `canManage()` recognizes a V2 all-Clients `manage` permission, but `canView()` checks only the legacy default roles and the V2 `view` permission. As a result, an administrator granted only all-Clients `manage` can manage a specific client through `canManage(client)`, but fails global view/list checks (`canList()` is defined in terms of `canView()`). This contradicts the per-client path, where manage/configure implies view, and prevents the expected list/view behavior after granting the all-Clients manage scope. Include the manage implication in the global view decision.

title: Role-mapping checks no longer honor manage permission
body: The three role-mapping methods at lines 92, 97, and 102 only test their exact V2 map scope. They bypass `canManage(client)`, unlike configure/view, so both the established `manage-clients` admin role and a V2 Clients/manage grant lose the ability to map client roles, map composites, or map client-scope roles. Existing administrators that could perform these operations are consequently rejected with 403 when V2 is enabled. These checks need to preserve the manage implication before testing their dedicated scopes.

title: Client-resource cleanup is disabled for V2-only deployments
body: The client-removal listener is now guarded by the legacy `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature flag, while V2 evaluation is selected by the independent `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` flag. In a V2-only deployment, deleting a client no longer invokes any cleanup for the per-client authorization resource created by this change, leaving its resource and policies orphaned in the admin-permissions resource server. Conversely, if both flags are enabled, the listener calls `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. V2 needs its own client-removal cleanup path (or a compatible implementation) rather than suppressing the listener based on the legacy flag.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not upgraded with the Clients schema
body: `init` returns immediately when the realm already has an admin-permissions client. A realm that enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore keeps only the old Users resource/scopes: it never receives the Clients all-resource or the new `configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, and `map-roles-composite` scopes. Creating a per-client permission then attempts to attach every Clients scope and fails with `No scopes found`, while global-client permission evaluation can also encounter a missing resource. Add a non-destructive schema backfill/migration path for existing admin-permissions clients.

title: The all-clients manage permission does not grant list/view access
body: `canView()` recognizes only the all-clients `view` scope, unlike `canView(ClientModel)`, which reaches `canManage(client)` through `canConfigure(client)`. The inherited `canList()` and client-scope listing checks depend on this zero-argument method, so an administrator granted only the all-clients `manage` scope can create, update, and delete clients but cannot list them. This contradicts the intended manage permission behavior and makes the added `testManageAllClients` listing expectation fail. Include `manage` here (or delegate through `canManage()`).

title: Role-mapping checks drop the built-in manage-clients authorization
body: `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only evaluate V2 authorization resources. They do not preserve the `MANAGE_CLIENTS` admin-role fallback used by the other client checks, so a normal realm-management administrator with `manage-clients` is denied client-role assignment and composite-role changes whenever FGAP V2 is enabled unless separate V2 policies are created. The map-role checks need to honor the built-in management role (and the intended manage-scope inheritance, if applicable) before evaluating the resource scope.

title: Deleting a client leaves its V2 authorization resource and policies behind
body: The client-removal listener now runs only when the legacy `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature is enabled. In a V2-only deployment, a `ClientRemovedEvent` is ignored, while the per-client resource and its scope permissions live under the admin-permissions resource server and have no foreign-key relationship to the deleted target client. They remain orphaned indefinitely; if a client with the same internal ID is later restored/imported, `getOrCreateResource` resolves the old resource by name and the deleted client's grants become effective for the new client. Add V2-specific resource/policy cleanup on client removal.

title: Existing V2 realms never receive the new Clients resource or scopes
body: `init` returns as soon as an admin-permissions client already exists. A realm that enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore retains only the old Users resource and scopes after upgrade; it never gets the Clients resource or the configure/map-roles client scopes. Creating a Clients permission will fail scope validation, and `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, ...)` can reach the missing all-clients resource path. Reconcile/create missing schema scopes and resource-type resources for an existing admin-permissions client instead of returning unconditionally.

title: The all-clients manage scope does not permit listing clients
body: `canView()` only considers the legacy view roles and the V2 `view` scope, while the inherited `canList()` contract is based on `canView()` (or query roles). A caller granted only the new all-clients `manage` scope can manage/view a known client through `canView(ClientModel)`, but cannot call the client list endpoint. This also contradicts the new `testManageAllClients`, which expects `findAll()` to succeed after granting only `manage`. Include the all-clients manage grant in the realm-level view/list decision, consistent with the per-client transitive behavior.

title: V2 drops built-in manage-clients access for role mapping
body: The overrides for `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only evaluate the new authorization scopes. Unlike the inherited evaluator, they do not preserve the `MANAGE_CLIENTS` admin role shortcut. Consequently an administrator with the standard `realm-management/manage-clients` role loses the ability to map client roles, manage composites, and map client-scope roles whenever FGAP V2 is enabled, unless separately granted new schema permissions. Retain the legacy admin-role check before evaluating V2 scopes.

title: Per-client resources are created without the Clients resource type
body: When a permission targets one client, the schema creates a resource and assigns scopes but never assigns `resourceType` to it. `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission()` subsequently uses `resourceStore.findByType(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and therefore cannot discover these individual client resources. Any caller using that method will treat client-specific grants as absent. Set the resource type when creating an object resource (as is already done for the all-resource entry during initialization).

title: Client deletion skips V2 permission-resource cleanup
body: The removal listener is now gated by `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ`, but V2 authorization is selected using the distinct `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` feature. In a V2-only deployment the listener does nothing when a target client is deleted, leaving its per-client authorization resource and policies in the admin-permissions resource server permanently orphaned. If both flags are enabled, the listener instead selects `ClientPermissionsV2` and calls its `setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. Add V2-specific cleanup for deleted target clients and gate it on the V2 feature rather than suppressing the event.

title: Void require-view methods are documented as returning a boolean
body: The Javadoc above `requireView()` says it "Returns true" even though the method is `void`; the same incorrect statement is repeated above `requireViewClientScopes()` at line 101. These methods should document that they throw `ForbiddenException` when the corresponding capability is absent, as the other `require*` methods do.

title: Changing the recreate result exit code breaks the documented automation contract
body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` was previously 4 and is changed to 3 so that 4 can be reused for the disabled-feature case. The update-compatibility guide explicitly instructs automation consumers to rely on the `check` command's exit code to choose between rolling and recreate updates. Existing pipelines that treat 4 as the recreate-required result will now see 3 as an unexpected failure and may not perform the required recreate upgrade. Preserve the existing recreate code and allocate a new unused code for feature-disabled (or make this an explicitly versioned breaking API change with a migration path).

title: The newly documented exit-code behavior is not asserted
body: The disabled-feature test verifies only stderr text and never checks that the command exits with code 4. Likewise, the incompatible-version cases only check their messages and do not assert the newly changed recreate-required code 3. Since these numeric codes are documented as the scriptable interface, a regression that returns 0, a generic error code, or swaps the two codes would pass this test suite. Assert `CLIResult.exitCode()` for disabled and incompatible `check` invocations.

title: The newly documented exit-code contract is not asserted
body: The disabled-feature test only checks stderr and does not assert that the process exits with code 4. Likewise, the incompatible-version cases only check their messages and do not assert the newly changed recreate exit code 3. These numeric exit codes are explicitly documented for automation, so a regression in `picocli.exit(...)` handling or the constants would pass this suite while breaking GitOps/CI consumers. Assert the exit codes for disabled metadata/check commands and for incompatible checks.

title: Assert the feature-disabled exit-code contract for both subcommands
body: The new disabled-feature test only checks stderr for the `metadata` subcommand. It neither asserts the newly documented exit code 4 nor exercises `check`, which has an independently added guard. A regression that prints this same message but exits with 0, 1, or the recreate code would pass while breaking automation that the guide instructs users to drive from the exit code. Add exit-code assertions for both `metadata` and `check` when `rolling-updates` is disabled.

title: Cover the changed recreate-required exit code
body: This PR changes an incompatible compatibility result from exit code 4 to 3, but the incompatible-version tests only assert the error text. Therefore the changed script-facing contract is unverified and a future change could return the feature-disabled or a successful status while these tests still pass. Assert exit code 3 for the incompatible Keycloak and Infinispan metadata cases.

title: A view-all-groups permission grants permission to create groups
body: `canManage()` is used by `POST /groups` to authorize top-level group creation, but it evaluates both the `view` and `manage` scopes. Consequently, an administrator granted only the read-only all-groups `view` scope can create arbitrary top-level groups. This is a write privilege escalation; `canManage()` should require only the `manage` scope, matching the per-group `canManage(GroupModel)` behavior.

title: Individual group authorization resources are created without a resource type
body: When a permission references an individual group, this method creates its authorization resource and scopes but never calls `resource.setType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` enumerates resources using `findByType(..., "Groups", ...)`, so these untyped individual resources are omitted. As a result, a delegate with `view-members` or `manage-members` on a specific group cannot have that group's members included in user searches or counts. Set the resource type when creating schema-managed resources.

title: User filtering uses authorization resource IDs instead of realm group IDs
body: The callback passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission` and adds that same value to the returned set. This ID is the authorization-store resource ID, whereas the resource name is the realm `GroupModel` ID established by `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`. `hasPermission` subsequently looks up a resource by name, so it misses the individual resource and falls back to the all-groups resource; moreover, `UserModel.GROUPS` and the user-count overload expect realm group IDs, not authorization resource IDs. Specific group member permissions therefore produce invalid query filters and users/counts are incorrectly empty or otherwise incorrect. Evaluate and return `groupResource.getName()` after ensuring it represents a group resource.

title: Existing enabled admin-permissions realms are never upgraded with Groups scopes and resource
body: `init` returns immediately whenever an admin-permissions client already exists. The new `Groups` all-resource and its scopes are only created later in this method, so realms that enabled V2 before this version retain no `Groups`, `manage-membership`, `manage-members`, or `view-members` records. Creating a group scope permission in such a realm fails scope validation because the scope does not exist, and group authorization checks cannot resolve their all-groups resource. Add an idempotent schema upgrade path for existing admin-permissions clients rather than only bootstrapping new clients.

title: V2-only deployments no longer clean up authorization resources for deleted groups
body: V2 evaluators are selected by `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`, but the provider event listener is now registered only when the separate V1 `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature is enabled. In a V2-only configuration, `GroupRemovedEvent` has no handler, so group-specific authorization resources and their policies created for the new Groups type remain after the realm group is deleted. These orphaned records accumulate and remain visible/usable through the authorization store. Register a V2-aware cleanup handler (without calling the V1-only `setPermissionsEnabled` implementation) whenever V2 is enabled.

title: A global group view grant is treated as permission to manage groups
body: `canManage()` evaluates both `view` and `manage` on the all-groups resource. Consequently, a principal granted only the `view` scope passes `requireManage()` for operations that do not yet have a concrete group, including `POST /groups`. That permits creating top-level groups and moving an existing group to the top level, despite the policy granting read-only access. Only the `manage` scope should satisfy this method.

title: Existing admin-permissions realms are never initialized with the new Groups schema
body: `init()` returns as soon as an admin-permissions client already exists. Realms created with the previous V2 schema therefore retain no `Groups` resource, no group scopes, and no group-specific resources after an upgrade. Creating a group scope permission then fails because `getScope()` cannot find the new scope, while group evaluators cannot resolve the all-groups resource. Initialization needs to reconcile missing schema scopes/resources for an existing admin-permissions client, or an explicit migration is required.

title: Resources created for individual groups are not assigned the Groups type
body: When `getOrCreateResource()` creates a resource for a group ID, it updates its scopes but never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` discovers scoped group grants using `findByType(..., "Groups", ...)`, so these individual resources are not discovered at all. As a result, group-member grants are omitted from the group filter used by user search/count operations; authorized users can disappear from paged searches and counts. Newly created resources need their schema resource type assigned.

title: Group-member discovery uses authorization resource IDs as realm group IDs
body: The callback receives an authorization `Resource`, but passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission()` and adds that same value to the returned set. Authorization resource IDs are generated independently from the realm group ID; the domain group ID is the resource name established by `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup()`. This makes the name lookup in `hasPermission()` miss the individual resource and sends opaque authorization IDs as `UserModel.GROUPS` to the user provider. Scoped group-member grants therefore do not filter users correctly, and an all-groups member grant can filter every user out. Use the resource name/domain group ID for both operations.

title: Listing groups re-evaluates a global authorization policy for every group
body: The previous `canViewGlobal` short circuit was removed, so every group in a non-hierarchical listing now calls `groupsEvaluator.canView(group)`. Under V2, even an all-groups `view` grant causes each call to look up/evaluate the authorization resource and its policies before falling back to the all-groups resource. This changes a global-view list from one policy evaluation to one evaluation per returned group (and the same regression exists in `GroupResource.getSubGroups`), which is expensive for realms with many groups. Cache `groupsEvaluator.canView()` once and only evaluate individual groups when it is false.

title: A global group view grant authorizes group creation
body: `canManage()` accepts either the `view` or `manage` scope. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` uses this no-argument check before creating a group, so an administrator granted only the Groups `view` scope can create top-level groups. The view scope must not be considered sufficient for `canManage()`; only `manage` should authorize this write operation.

title: Group member filtering returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: The callback passes `groupResource.getId()` into `hasPermission()` and later returns that value in `granted`, but schema-created individual resources are named with the `GroupModel` ID while their authorization-resource ID is a distinct generated ID. The lookup therefore misses the individual resource and falls back to the all-groups resource; when that fallback does grant access, the returned IDs still cannot match user group memberships. `UsersResource` and the brute-force endpoint use this set for provider-side group filtering and user counts, so scoped `view-members`/`manage-members` grants produce empty or incomplete counts and paginated searches. Evaluate the resource being iterated and return the corresponding actual group ID (while handling the aggregate Groups resource separately).

title: Per-object schema resources are never assigned their resource type
body: `getOrCreateResource()` creates an individual resource and assigns scopes but never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` discovers individual group resources exclusively through `resourceStore.findByType(..., "Groups", ...)`, so resources created for single-group policies are not enumerated at all. As a result, member-based user filtering cannot obtain the groups authorized by those policies. Set the resource type when creating the resource and migrate any already-created per-object resources as needed.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not upgraded with the Groups schema
body: `init()` returns immediately when an admin-permissions client already exists. A realm that enabled V2 before this change therefore retains only the old Users/Clients scopes and aggregate resources; it never receives the new group scopes or the aggregate `Groups` resource. Creating a group scope permission in such a realm reaches `getOrCreateResource()` and fails because the requested scopes do not exist, making the newly added authorization type unusable after upgrade. Initialization must be idempotent and add missing schema scopes/resources for existing clients, or a migration must backfill them.

title: Use the account UI interpolation format instead of Java MessageFormat
body: This bundle uses the account UI's `{{0}}` interpolation syntax (as do the surrounding validation messages), but this change replaces it with Java `MessageFormat` syntax including a `choice` expression. The frontend translator will not substitute `{0}`, `{1}`, or evaluate `{2,choice,...}`, so this validation error is rendered with raw placeholders/pattern text. Keep the existing UI interpolation syntax and implement pluralization using the frontend i18n mechanism if needed.

title: Use the admin UI interpolation format instead of Java MessageFormat
body: The admin UI resource previously used `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}`, which is the frontend message interpolation contract. Replacing it with Java `MessageFormat` and `choice` syntax leaves the parameters and choice expression uninterpreted by the admin UI, causing the multivalued-attribute validation message to display raw formatting tokens.

title: Safe HTML is rejected when the sanitizer merely canonicalizes it
body:
The verifier treats any byte-for-byte difference between the input and sanitizer output as illegal HTML. The OWASP sanitizer canonicalizes valid allowed markup, for example `
` to `
`, even though no unsafe content was removed. The many unrelated `
` to `
` edits in this PR are evidence of this behavior. Future translations containing valid equivalent HTML will fail verification and be reported as unsafe; validation should distinguish removal of disallowed content from harmless serialization normalization, with positive tests for accepted safe variants.

title: Lithuanian account TOTP instruction was replaced with Italian text
body: `messages_lt.properties` is the Lithuanian account bundle, but `totpStep1` now says `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see an untranslated/wrong-language setup instruction; replace it with Lithuanian text.

title: Lithuanian login TOTP instruction was replaced with Italian text
body: `messages_lt.properties` is the Lithuanian login bundle, but `loginTotpStep1` now contains the Italian sentence `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. This makes the login-time TOTP setup instruction appear in the wrong language for Lithuanian users.

title: Simplified Chinese bundle now contains a Traditional Chinese TOTP instruction
body: The `zh_CN` bundle otherwise uses Simplified Chinese, but the new `totpStep1` text uses Traditional Chinese characters such as `手機` and `應用程式`. This creates an inconsistent wrong-script message for the Simplified Chinese locale; use a Simplified Chinese translation.

title: Do not use Java MessageFormat syntax in the account UI bundle
body: This is a JavaScript account UI translation bundle, whose interpolation syntax is `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, etc. (as used by the previous value and other entries in this file). Replacing it with Java `MessageFormat` syntax and a `choice` expression means the client translation layer will not interpolate the attribute or bounds and will render `{0}`, `{1}`, and `{2,choice,...}` literally in validation errors. Keep the client-side placeholder syntax and implement pluralization using the UI i18n mechanism if needed.

title: Do not use Java MessageFormat syntax in the admin UI bundle
body: The admin console message resources use the JavaScript i18n interpolation form `{{0}}`, as the removed value did. The new `{0}`/`{1}` placeholders and Java `choice` grammar are not interpreted by that client-side formatter, so multivalued-attribute validation errors will expose the raw formatting expression instead of the attribute name and limits. Restore the client bundle's interpolation format and use its pluralization support rather than Java MessageFormat syntax.

title: Lithuanian account message was replaced with Italian text
body: `messages_lt.properties` is the Lithuanian bundle, but the new `totpStep1` value is Italian ("Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare"). Lithuanian account users will see an unrelated language when configuring TOTP; replace it with the intended Lithuanian translation.

title: Lithuanian login message was replaced with Italian text
body: The `loginTotpStep1` entry in the Lithuanian login bundle now contains the same Italian sentence ("Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare"). This is user-visible during login-time TOTP setup and should be translated into Lithuanian rather than copied from another locale.

title: Simplified Chinese bundle now contains Traditional Chinese text
body: `messages_zh_CN.properties` is the Simplified Chinese locale, but the replacement `totpStep1` uses Traditional Chinese characters and vocabulary such as "手機" and "應用程式", unlike the surrounding Simplified Chinese strings. Use a Simplified Chinese translation for this `zh_CN` resource; Traditional Chinese belongs in the `zh_TW` bundle.

title: Locale-to-English resolution does not support valid locale suffixes
body: The suffix regex only accepts letters and underscores. Valid resource-bundle locale names containing a numeric region or hyphen, such as `messages_es_419.properties`, are not rewritten to `_en.properties`. For a translated bundle under `resources-community`, verification then tries to open a nonexistent `resources/.../messages_es_419.properties` and aborts; where a same-named file does exist, it is incorrectly used as its own English baseline. Extract the locale suffix without restricting it to this character set before resolving the English bundle.

title: Account UI message was changed to unsupported MessageFormat syntax
body: This account-ui bundle uses the React/i18next interpolation convention (`{{0}}`, `{{username}}`) throughout. Replacing this message with Java `MessageFormat` placeholders and a `choice` expression means the UI will not interpolate the attribute/min/max values or evaluate the plural choice; users will see literal `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2,choice,...}` text when this validation error is displayed.

title: Admin UI validation message uses Java formatting instead of UI interpolation
body: The admin UI resource previously used `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, and `{{2}}`, matching the UI localization engine's interpolation syntax. The new single-brace Java `MessageFormat`/`choice` expression is not evaluated by that engine, so the multivalued-attribute validation error will render its placeholders and choice expression literally rather than showing the supplied values.

title: Lithuanian account TOTP instruction was replaced with Italian text
body: `messages_lt.properties` now contains `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian rather than Lithuanian. Lithuanian account-console users will receive an unrelated-language instruction during TOTP setup.

title: Lithuanian login TOTP instruction was replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian login bundle now sets `loginTotpStep1` to the Italian sentence `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. This makes the first TOTP setup instruction appear in the wrong language on the Lithuanian login flow.

title: Simplified-Chinese bundle now contains Traditional-Chinese text
body: The `zh_CN` resource is a Simplified Chinese bundle, but the replacement uses Traditional Chinese characters and wording (`手機`, `安裝`, `應用程式`). This is inconsistent with the rest of the bundle and presents the account TOTP instruction in the wrong script for the China locale.

title: The new abstract method breaks existing custom OAuth2 grant providers at startup
body: Adding `getShortcut()` as an abstract interface method is binary-incompatible with OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations compiled against the previous release. The new default token-context factory invokes this method for every registered OAuth2 grant factory during post-initialization, so an existing extension without the method will throw AbstractMethodError and prevent the server from starting. Provide a default/compatibility implementation and handle unrecognized legacy grants as unknown, or otherwise avoid invoking the new method on old implementations.

title: Grant shortcut lengths accepted by the factory cannot be decoded
body: The decoder hard-codes a six-character context, which requires a two-character grant shortcut, but OAuth2GrantTypeFactory documents shortcuts as usually three letters and the factory does not validate their length. A custom grant returning (for example) `foo` will mint IDs such as `onrtfoo:<uuid>`, then getTokenContextFromTokenId will reject those same IDs with "Expected length of 6." Require exactly two-character shortcuts during factory initialization and document that requirement, or make the encoding self-delimiting.

title: rawTokenId is never null-checked
body: This line checks `grantType` a second time instead of checking `rawTokenId`, despite the error message claiming that a null raw token ID is prohibited. A caller of this public context API can therefore construct a context with a null raw ID, and the default encoder will serialize it as the literal string `:null` rather than rejecting an invalid token ID. Check `rawTokenId` here.

title: The access-token event matcher does not validate the expected grant shortcut
body: The matcher extracts characters 3-4 even though the grant shortcut occupies characters 4-5 of the six-character prefix, and it returns false when the extracted value equals the expected shortcut. For example, `onrtac:<uuid>` with expected `ac` extracts `ta` and passes; a token with a different grant shortcut also passes in the normal cases. Consequently the updated event assertions do not catch regressions in grant-type encoding. Compare `substring(4, 6)` to the expected shortcut positively, after validating the prefix length.

title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks already deployed grant providers at startup
body: Existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations compiled against the previous interface do not implement getShortcut(). DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() invokes this method for every registered grant factory, so an unchanged provider JAR causes AbstractMethodError during server initialization (and source-based providers no longer compile). Provide a compatible default/migration path or otherwise avoid making this new method abstract for existing provider implementations.

title: The public OAuth2 grant context copy constructor was removed
body: The previous public Context(Context) constructor was removed rather than updated to copy grantType. Custom grant providers can use this constructor to derive a context before invoking another grant flow; binaries compiled against the prior server SPI will fail with NoSuchMethodError when that path executes, and source users cannot compile. Restore the constructor and copy the new grantType field.

title: Grant shortcuts are not constrained to the two-character token wire format
body: This factory accepts and stores arbitrary getShortcut() values, but the encoder writes the shortcut directly into the ID while the decoder only accepts exactly six context characters and slices the grant field to two characters. A custom grant returning a three-character shortcut (which the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory documentation currently even describes as usual) will issue IDs such as onrtabc:<id> that this provider subsequently rejects as malformed. Validate that shortcuts are exactly two characters when registering factories, or change the format/parser to support variable-length shortcuts and document the contract consistently.

title: rawTokenId is never null-checked
body: The constructor checks grantType twice; the second check has the rawTokenId error message but still passes grantType. Consequently an AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId is accepted and encodeTokenId serializes it as the literal string "null", causing otherwise identical token contexts to share the same JTI. Check rawTokenId instead so invalid contexts fail before an invalid/non-unique token ID is generated.

title: Access-token event matcher accepts IDs with the wrong grant shortcut
body: isAccessTokenId extracts substring(3, 5), although the six-character prefix stores the grant at indexes 4..5, and it returns false when that incorrectly extracted value equals the expected shortcut. For example, onrtac:<uuid> is accepted for expected "ac" only because "ta" does not match. Thus the updated integration assertions do not verify the encoded grant type and can pass when the implementation emits an incorrect shortcut. Compare substring(4, 6) and reject non-matching values.

title: Adding an abstract method breaks existing OAuth grant provider factories
body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` is an extension interface, and existing third-party factories compiled against the previous version do not implement `getShortcut()`. The new default encoder's `postInit` unconditionally invokes this method on every installed grant factory, so an existing binary provider causes an `AbstractMethodError` during server initialization; recompiling it also fails until it is changed. Preserve compatibility with a default method or provide a migration path that does not prevent servers with existing custom grants from starting.

title: The public grant context copy constructor was removed
body: The previously available `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context)` constructor has been removed while adding the grant-type state. Custom grant implementations that copy the request context now fail to compile, and already compiled providers will fail with `NoSuchMethodError` when that path executes after an upgrade. Restore the constructor (including the new `grantType` field in the copy) to avoid breaking provider implementations.

title: Grant shortcut lengths accepted by the encoder cannot be decoded
body: The default encoder concatenates whatever `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` returns, but the decoder rejects every encoded context whose prefix is not exactly six characters. The factory interface documentation currently even describes shortcuts as usually three letters, and the factory performs no two-character validation. A custom grant returning `abc` therefore successfully issues an ID such as `onrtabc:<uuid>`, but `getTokenContextFromTokenId` always throws because its context length is seven. Enforce and document an exact two-character shortcut at registration time, or make the encoding self-delimiting/parser support variable lengths.

title: The raw token ID null check validates the grant type a second time
body: The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. Consequently an `AccessTokenContext` with a null raw ID is accepted, and the default encoder turns it into a literal `...:null` token ID. Multiple invalid contexts can then produce the same JTI and collide with the valid literal raw ID `null`. Check `rawTokenId` here as the error message claims.

title: Access-token event assertions do not validate the expected grant shortcut
body: `isAccessTokenId` reads `substring(3, 5)`, although the grant shortcut in the six-character format occupies indexes 4 and 5, and it returns false when the extracted value equals the expected shortcut. For example, `onrtac:<uuid>` tested for `ac` extracts `ta`, does not return false, and passes solely because the suffix is a UUID. Thus all updated event tests can pass with an incorrect grant encoding. Compare `substring(4, 6)` and fail when it is not equal to the expected shortcut.

title: Recovery-code metadata is discarded when writing to user storage
body: The supplied RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel contains the generated-at timestamp and user label, but the UserCredentialModel sent to user storage contains only the type and a JSON array of raw codes. A user-storage provider has no way to recover the original timestamp or label from this input. Consequently, externally stored recovery-code credentials cannot preserve the same credential metadata as locally stored ones (the added test provider already substitutes the save time and returns a null label), affecting credential/account metadata and audit consistency.

title: Returned recovery-code credentials do not retain their persisted ID
body: updateCredential assigns an ID to myUser.recoveryCodes, but getCredentials reconstructs a new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel with createFromValues and never copies that persisted ID. The model returned to Keycloak therefore has no ID, or an ID unrelated to the stored record. RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator uses the returned ID when all codes are exhausted and calls removeStoredCredentialById, so the external credential cannot be reliably removed; account credential operations also cannot address the actual stored recovery credential.

title: The user-storage recovery validator leaves accepted codes reusable
body: The recovery-code validation branch only checks whether the submitted value occurs in the stored JSON list and never removes or marks that value as used. Every successful recovery code can therefore be submitted repeatedly, and the all-codes-used path is never reached. Recovery codes are required to be one-time credentials; the newly added integration test authenticates only once, so it passes while failing to exercise this essential behavior. The storage fixture should persist consumption (and remove the credential after the final code), with a test proving that a reused code is rejected.

title: Federated recovery-code creation drops the credential metadata
body: When user storage accepts the update, it receives only a UserCredentialModel containing the type and JSON list of raw codes. The generated-at timestamp and user label already present on credentialModel are not propagated; unlike the local fallback, a storage provider therefore cannot recreate the same RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel. The added test provider demonstrates this by storing the current time and no label, so a configured label is later returned as null. This makes recovery-code metadata inconsistent between local and federated storage and loses the originally generated timestamp/label.

title: The federated test provider accepts recovery codes indefinitely
body: The recovery-code validation branch only checks whether the submitted value occurs in the persisted list. It never removes the matched code or records it as used, so the same recovery code succeeds on every login. getCredentials reconstructs all codes as unused as well. The new integration test performs only one successful login, so it passes despite violating the one-time recovery-code requirement. Persist consumption atomically and add a second-login assertion showing that reuse of the same code is rejected.

title: Recovery credentials returned by the test storage lose their persisted ID
body: updateCredential assigns the persisted recovery credential an ID at line 195, but getCredentials reconstructs a new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel from the raw values without copying that ID. The returned credential consequently has no ID, or an ID unrelated to the backing record. Callers use credential IDs for credential-management operations, and the recovery authenticator uses the returned ID when cleaning up an exhausted credential, so those operations cannot address the stored recovery-code record. Preserve myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() on the reconstructed model and cover exhaustion/removal in the integration test.

title: Federated recovery-code creation drops credential metadata
body: When a user-storage provider accepts the update, it receives only an empty credential ID, the type, and a JSON array of raw codes. The supplied RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, which carries the verified generated-at timestamp and user label, is otherwise discarded. Unlike the local fallback, a storage provider therefore cannot reconstruct the same credential metadata; recovery-code labels and the original creation time are lost for federated users and will be missing or incorrect in credential/account representations. Pass the required metadata in the storage update contract (for example, a recovery-code-specific input/serialized DTO) rather than only the code list.

title: Exhausted federated recovery credentials are removed through the local-store API
body: getCredential() now returns a credential from user storage before consulting local storage, but this branch still calls removeStoredCredentialById(), which operates on the stored/local credential path. An exhausted credential returned by a user-storage provider is therefore not removed by this call. Providers that retain a credential with all codes marked used can remain configured with an unusable recovery credential, leaving stale data and potentially causing subsequent recovery flows to request a non-existent next code. Deletion needs to be dispatched to the credential's actual source, or federated providers need an explicit, enforced exhausted-credential lifecycle.

title: The new user-storage fixture accepts the same recovery code indefinitely
body: The recovery-code validator only checks whether the submitted raw code is present in the persisted list and never removes it or records it as used. getCredentials() consequently reconstructs every code as unused on every request. The added integration test validates one successful login only, so it would pass even though a recovery code can be replayed without limit. Persist consumed-code state (or remove the code) in the fixture and add a second-login assertion that reuse is rejected.

title: The concurrent reader is neither synchronized nor joined before asserting
body: The test starts the reader thread and immediately begins deletion, then asserts `caughtExceptions` without waiting for the reader to have made even one request or for its in-flight request to complete. Depending on scheduling, the reader can start only after all groups are deleted, or it can add the failure after the assertion has already passed, so this regression test can pass even with the NPE still present. Retain the thread (or use an executor), coordinate that a read is in progress before deletion, signal it in a finally block, and join it with a timeout before checking the captured exceptions.

title: The regression test does not request subgroup counts
body: The four-argument `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` overload uses `true` for `briefRepresentation`; it does not enable the `subGroupsCount` query parameter. The production change is exclusively in `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()`, which is reached by `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` only when subgroup counts are requested. Consequently this test can pass without executing the fixed code path or reproducing the original NPE. Invoke the endpoint overload/query option with `subGroupsCount=true` while the deletes run.

title: The concurrent reader is not awaited before asserting its failures
body: After setting `deletedAll`, the test immediately asserts that `caughtExceptions` is empty without joining or otherwise waiting for the reader thread. A request already in progress can fail and add an exception after this assertion, and the reader may not have been scheduled at all before deletion completes. This makes the test capable of passing without exercising concurrency and leaves a background thread running into later test activity. Keep the thread/future and await its completion (and preferably use a latch to confirm at least one read overlaps deletion) before checking the collected exceptions.

title: The concurrent reader is neither coordinated nor joined before asserting
body: The test starts a background reader and immediately deletes the groups, sets the stop flag, and asserts the exception list without waiting for the reader to begin or terminate. The reader can therefore be scheduled only after `deletedAll` is true (performing no request at all), or it can record an exception after the assertion has already passed. It can also continue issuing a request after the test has returned. This makes the regression test capable of passing without exercising the delete/read race. Coordinate a reader request with the delete operation and stop/join the thread (preferably in a finally block) before checking `caughtExceptions`.

title: The paginator configuration is passed to get_result instead of the paginator constructor
body: `Endpoint.paginate` forwards its extra keyword arguments to `paginator.get_result`, not to the paginator constructor. Therefore an authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true` calls `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result(..., enable_advanced_features=True)`, but that method does not accept this argument, resulting in an uncaught `TypeError` and a 500 response. Construct the paginator with this option (for example via a configured paginator class) or make the option part of the supported `get_result` contract.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate AuditLogEntry datetime ordering
body: The audit-log endpoint orders by `-datetime`, so `get_item_key` receives a `datetime` object. This implementation passes that object to `math.floor`/`math.ceil`, which only accept real numbers. `build_cursor` invokes this key function for any non-empty page, so the optimized audit-log path fails with a `TypeError` even if the constructor-option issue is corrected. This paginator needs DateTimePaginator's timestamp conversion behavior, or should inherit from DateTimePaginator.

title: Negative-offset pagination uses unsupported QuerySet slicing
body: The advanced branch passes a negative `start_offset` directly to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets reject slices with negative bounds (`ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`); they do not handle them as the comment claims. A permitted caller can supply a negative cursor offset, causing the audit-log request to fail with a 500 rather than providing reverse pagination. Implement reverse traversal using a valid cursor/range query, or reject negative offsets as a bad cursor.

title: Unsupported paginator option causes optimized requests to fail before pagination
body: `self.paginate` does not accept or forward an `enable_advanced_features` keyword to paginator constructors. Since no pagination plumbing was changed to support this new argument, an authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true` raises `TypeError` at this call instead of constructing `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, resulting in a 500 response. Extend the shared pagination API to pass an explicit constructor option, or remove/configure this option without passing it to `paginate`.

title: Optimized paginator treats AuditLogEntry datetime keys as numeric values
body: The audit-log endpoint instantiates this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, where `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `datetime`. On every non-empty first page, cursor construction calls `get_item_key`, and `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on that datetime raises `TypeError`. Even if that conversion were avoided, `value_from_cursor` leaves the generated numeric cursor value as an integer, so subsequent queryset filtering compares the datetime column with an integer. The optimized paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible key and cursor-value conversion (for example, by subclassing `DateTimePaginator`) for this endpoint to work.

title: Negative offsets are not supported by Django QuerySet slicing
body: This branch passes a negative `start_offset` directly to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, but Django QuerySets reject negative indexing and slicing with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` `Cursor.from_string` accepts signed integer offsets, so an authorized caller can request an optimized cursor such as `0:-1:0` and receive a 500 instead of the advertised reverse-pagination behavior. Validate/reject negative offsets or implement reverse traversal using supported queryset bounds; they cannot be used as Python-style negative slices on a QuerySet.

title: The advanced flag is passed to the pagination helper instead of the paginator constructor
body: `enable_advanced_features` is an `OptimizedCursorPaginator.__init__` argument, but this call supplies it to `self.paginate`. The endpoint pagination helper does not expose this as a paginator-constructor option, so an optimized request will fail with an unexpected keyword argument (or, if helper kwargs are forwarded to `get_result`, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` will reject it there). Consequently every authorized request using `optimized_pagination=true` fails before returning audit logs. Construct the paginator with this option through supported helper plumbing, or remove the unused option.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate the audit-log datetime sort key
body: The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `item.datetime` is a `datetime.datetime`. `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on that datetime while `build_cursor` is processing the first nonempty page, which raises `TypeError` rather than producing a response. Unlike `DateTimePaginator`, this class also does not convert cursor values back to datetimes for the ranged query. The optimized paginator must reuse the datetime key encoding/decoding from `DateTimePaginator` (or otherwise support datetime keys) before it can be used by this endpoint.

title: The advertised negative-offset path uses an invalid Django QuerySet slice
body: When advanced features are enabled and a cursor has a negative offset, this slices the Django `QuerySet` with a negative start. Django explicitly rejects negative QuerySet indexing/slicing with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`; it does not implement the boundary handling described in the comments. Since `Cursor` accepts signed offsets, an advanced cursor with a negative offset produces a server error instead of reverse pagination. Reject such cursors as invalid or implement reverse traversal using non-negative queryset bounds.

title: Changing span keys from sets to sorted sets has no rollout compatibility path
body: Existing live span-buffer keys are Redis Sets, created by the previous SADD/SUNIONSTORE implementation and retained for up to redis_ttl. After deploying this change, ZADD against any such key raises WRONGTYPE; the new Lua script also calls ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE on those keys and will fail. During a rolling deployment, old workers likewise cannot SADD to keys created by new workers. This can make span processing fail for active traces until the old keys expire, with no migration, key versioning, or coordinated drain included.

title: The optimized paginator cannot paginate AuditLogEntry datetime values
body: This branch passes order_by="-datetime" to OptimizedCursorPaginator, but that paginator computes cursor keys with math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key). AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime object, so building the first cursor for any non-empty result page raises TypeError and returns a 500 to authorized users requesting optimized_pagination=true. The paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible datetime serialization/deserialization, or this endpoint must continue using DateTimePaginator.

title: ZUNIONSTORE makes replayed span scores non-idempotent
body: ZUNIONSTORE uses SUM as its default aggregate. A normally expected Kafka replay can put the same payload in both set_key and the temporary parent/span key: for example, replaying a child after its parent redirect has already moved that child into the destination. The union then doubles end_timestamp_precise for that member, and repeated replays continue increasing it. Since ZPOPMIN uses this score for eviction, replayed spans are incorrectly protected while newer valid spans are evicted. Use an explicit aggregate such as MAX (or otherwise preserve the existing member score) when merging.

title: Eviction ignores the configured max_segment_spans limit
