body: SpansBuffer still accepts and stores max_segment_spans, but the prior enforcement was removed from _load_segment_data and the Lua script now unconditionally caps every segment at 1000. Callers configured with a lower limit can now flush up to 1000 spans despite their memory/safety setting, while callers configured with a higher limit silently lose spans at 1000. Pass the configured limit as a script argument and use it for eviction.

title: Negative cursor offsets cause invalid Django queryset slices
body: The advertised advanced path passes a negative start_offset directly to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet explicitly rejects negative indexing/slice bounds with ValueError rather than interpreting them as reverse pagination. Thus an authorized client supplying a negative cursor offset receives a 500, not the documented bidirectional pagination behavior. Negative offsets need to be translated into a supported cursor query or rejected during cursor validation.

title: Reducing redirect traversal fragments deeply nested traces
body: The redirect walk was reduced from 10,000 iterations to 1,000 without another mechanism to collapse old redirect chains. For a trace whose parent chain exceeds roughly 1,000 links, a later child resolves only to an intermediate span buffer and is recorded there instead of the root buffer, producing separate incomplete segments. The 1,000-member payload eviction limit does not bound redirect-chain depth, because redirect mappings remain after payload eviction. Preserve the previous traversal bound or add path compression/a defined depth handling strategy.

title: Changing active buffer keys from Redis sets to sorted sets has no migration path
body: Previously deployed workers store every `span-buf:s:*` key as a Redis Set via `SADD` and read it with `SSCAN`. This code issues `ZADD` against the same key names and later reads them with `ZSCAN`; Redis does not permit changing a key's collection type, so any unexpired legacy segment will produce `WRONGTYPE` errors when a new worker receives another span for it or tries to flush it. Since these keys can live for `redis_ttl` (one hour by default), a normal or rolling deployment can fail span batches and leave queued segments unflushable until expiry. Use versioned keys or provide a compatible migration/read path before switching types.

title: ZUNIONSTORE corrupts end-timestamp scores for retried spans
body: The new sorted-set score is `end_timestamp_precise` and is used to decide eviction, but both `ZUNIONSTORE` calls use Redis's default `SUM` aggregation. If an identical payload is already in `set_key` and is inserted again into a temporary child/parent key before redirect resolution (a normal at-least-once retry/replay scenario), the union stores that member with the sum of its timestamps rather than its actual end timestamp. Repeated retries therefore make old spans appear arbitrarily new and cause `ZPOPMIN` to evict the wrong spans. Specify an aggregation such as `AGGREGATE MAX`/`MIN` appropriate for the timestamp when merging.

title: The redirect traversal limit now splits deep traces that previously merged
body: The redirect walk was reduced from 10,000 to 1,000 hops without another mechanism to resolve the remaining chain. For a deeply nested trace received across batches in child-before-parent order, redirects form a chain; once this loop reaches the new limit, the script maps the incoming span to an intermediate buffer rather than the root buffer. The result is multiple independently flushed segment IDs for one trace rather than one merged segment. Retain the previous bound or explicitly handle/truncate over-limit chains in a way that preserves the segment association.

title: The configured max_segment_spans limit is now ignored
body: `SpansBuffer` still accepts and stores `max_segment_spans`, but the previous enforcement in `_load_segment_data` was removed and the Lua script always retains exactly 1,000 members. Callers configured with a lower cap can now retain up to 1,000 spans, while callers configured with a higher cap are silently limited to 1,000; even the default behavior changes from accepting 1,001 spans to retaining 1,000. Pass the configured limit to the script and use it for eviction, or remove/replace the configuration contract deliberately.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate AuditLogEntry datetimes
body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects this paginator while ordering by `-datetime`, so `get_item_key` receives a `datetime.datetime`. Calling `math.floor` on that object raises `TypeError` while building the first response cursor, causing every authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true` to return HTTP 500. Even if that conversion were bypassed, `value_from_cursor` returns the numeric cursor directly, so subsequent queries would compare the database datetime column to an integer. This paginator must use DateTimePaginator's datetime serialization/deserialization behavior for this endpoint.

title: Advertised negative-offset pagination raises on Django QuerySets
body: The advanced branch intentionally passes a negative `start_offset` into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, but Django QuerySet slicing rejects negative indices with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`. `Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets, so an advanced cursor using the feature described here produces a server error instead of reverse pagination. Implement reverse traversal using valid non-negative/ranged queries, or reject negative cursors before slicing.

title: The Redis value type change is not compatible with existing live buffers
body: Existing `span-buf:s:*` keys are Redis SETs written by the previous version, while this version issues `ZADD` against the same keys. Redis returns WRONGTYPE for that operation (and the new Lua script's `ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE` calls also fail on those keys). During a rolling deployment, any active segment from the preceding version will make span processing fail rather than commit its Kafka batch, and old workers will likewise fail if they encounter a newly-created sorted set. Use versioned keys or an explicit migration/rollout strategy before changing the Redis datatype.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate audit-log DateTime fields
body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` while ordering by `-datetime`, but this paginator's `get_item_key` passes the model's `datetime` value to `math.floor`/`math.ceil`. Unlike `DateTimePaginator`, it does not convert datetimes to a numeric cursor value. As soon as an authorized request uses `optimized_pagination=true` and the query returns an audit log entry, cursor construction raises `TypeError`, producing a 500 response instead of a paginated result.

title: Advanced negative offsets are rejected by Django QuerySets
body: The new advanced branch passes a negative `start_offset` directly to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet slicing explicitly rejects negative slice bounds with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`; it does not provide the claimed reverse-pagination behavior. Since `Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets, an advanced-pagination caller can trigger this error with a negative cursor rather than receiving a valid page.

title: ZUNIONSTORE changes span timestamps when buffers overlap
body: `ZUNIONSTORE` uses `SUM` as its default score aggregation. If a payload already exists in both the destination buffer and a buffer being merged—for example, when an at-least-once replay overlaps a previously buffered descendant—the resulting score becomes twice its `end_timestamp_precise` value. The score is now used to choose entries for `ZPOPMIN`, so these duplicated members look artificially newer and cause the wrong spans to be retained or evicted. Merge with an aggregation that preserves the timestamp (such as `MAX`) rather than the default sum.

title: Insertion eviction ignores the configured segment span limit
body: `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` remains a constructor setting, but the prior enforcement of that setting was removed from `_load_segment_data` and no limit is passed into this Lua script. The script instead always retains exactly 1000 members. Deployments configured with any other limit now silently discard spans at 1000 (and the default behavior changes from allowing 1001 members to retaining 1000), so the buffer configuration no longer controls its documented capacity.

title: Reducing redirect traversal fragments deep out-of-order traces
body: The redirect traversal bound was reduced from 10,000 to 1,000 without handling the case where the bound is reached. A valid deeply nested trace ingested from child toward root can create a redirect chain longer than 1,000 entries; subsequent spans then stop at an intermediate buffer and are mapped there instead of to the true segment root. This splits one trace into separately flushed segments and assigns incorrect segment IDs.

title: Substring matching applies error weights to non-error Discover queries
body: Checking whether the raw query merely contains `event.type:error` does not establish that every selected event is an error. For example, `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` both satisfy this check (the endpoint itself demonstrates `!event.type:...` syntax), so an allowlisted Discover request rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count()`. This causes transaction/non-error rows to be counted with `sample_weight` even though the helper documents that transactions do not have that field, producing invalid counts or query failures. Determine eligibility from the parsed/effective query and require all query branches to be restricted to error events.

title: Eligibility is checked against the outer dataset instead of the dataset being queried
body: `_get_event_stats` executes queries against `scoped_dataset`, but this call passes the captured outer `dataset` into the upsampling predicate. In the dashboard split flow, an outer metrics-enhanced widget calls `_get_event_stats(discover, ..., errors_only_query, ...)`; the predicate sees the metrics dataset, returns false for it, and leaves the Discover error query as raw `count()`. Sampled errors in that dashboard path are therefore systematically undercounted. Evaluate eligibility against `scoped_dataset` (and the query actually passed to this invocation).

title: Upsampled counts are truncated to integers
body: The aggregate casts `sum(sample_weight)` through `toInt64`. Client sample rates are floats, so sample weights and their sums are not guaranteed to be integral (for example, a 0.3 sample rate produces a non-integral inverse weight). ClickHouse truncates this value before it reaches the API, creating a systematic low bias in the upsampled count. Preserve the numeric sum, or apply an explicitly chosen rounding policy only if the API contract requires integral results.

title: The internal weighted aggregate is directly exposed to user queries
body: `upsampled_count` is registered as a normal SnQL function and has no eligibility guard or `private=True` restriction. A caller can request `yAxis=upsampled_count()` directly, bypassing the allowlist and error-event checks in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`; this permits weighted counts for non-allowlisted projects and attempts to use `sample_weight` on transaction data. Keep this aggregate internal and/or enforce the same project and dataset eligibility at the resolver boundary.

title: Process-randomized hash makes shared-cache keys and invalidation inconsistent
body: Python's built-in `hash()` is salted per interpreter process. In a multi-worker deployment, the same organization/project selection produces different cache keys on different workers, so the shared cache does not actually share eligibility results. More importantly, `invalidate_upsampling_cache` running on one worker cannot delete entries created by another worker. Build the key from a stable serialized sorted project-ID list or a deterministic digest instead.

title: Substring matching applies upsampling to mixed or negated Discover queries
body: The eligibility check treats any query containing the text `event.type:error` as error-only. Valid filters such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` and `!event.type:error` therefore enable `upsampled_count()`. Those queries include transaction rows, for which this change explicitly says `sample_weight` is unavailable, so transactions are omitted from the sum (or the query fails depending on the backing schema) and the returned count is incorrect. Determine eligibility from the parsed query and require that all possible branches select sampled error events.

title: Dashboard split queries are checked against the outer dataset instead of the dataset being queried
body: `_get_event_stats` accepts `scoped_dataset`, but the upsampling decision uses the captured outer `dataset` and the original request query. In the metrics-enhanced dashboard split path, the endpoint invokes `_get_event_stats(discover, ..., "(<query>) AND !event.type:transaction", ...)` to retrieve error events while the captured dataset remains a metrics dataset. The helper consequently rejects the query before transformation, and an error-only split widget returns raw sampled counts rather than upsampled counts. Base the decision on `scoped_dataset` and the query argument actually sent to that invocation.

title: Weighted counts are truncated to an integer
body: `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` truncates the aggregate rather than preserving or rounding the sampling estimate. Client sample rates are floats and are not restricted here to rates whose inverse is integral; for example, a 0.3 sample rate produces a non-integral weight. This systematically undercounts such queries, and floating-point accumulation can also turn otherwise integral totals into a value just below the integer boundary. Return the weighted sum as a numeric value or apply the intended explicit rounding rule.

title: The PR adds an unconfigured nested-repository gitlink
body: This adds `sentry-repo` as a gitlink pinned to the base commit, rather than adding source content, and the PR contains no accompanying `.gitmodules` update to define how it can be initialized. Checkouts that initialize submodules can fail or leave this path unpopulated, while the nested repository is unrelated to the feature. Remove this accidental gitlink before merging.

title: Raw substring matching applies upsampling to non-error Discover queries
body: The Discover eligibility check treats any query containing the text `event.type:error` as error-only. Valid queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, `!event.type:error`, or a quoted search term containing that text therefore have `count()` replaced with `upsampled_count()`. Those queries can include transaction/non-error rows, for which this code explicitly says `sample_weight` is not available, producing invalid queries or incorrect totals. Determine event-type eligibility from the parsed query and require that the query is semantically restricted to errors rather than using a substring check.

title: Upsampling eligibility is evaluated against the original dataset instead of the executed dataset
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, but passes the outer `dataset` closure to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. In the dashboard split flow, the original metrics-enhanced request invokes `_get_event_stats(discover, ..., errors_only_query)` for the error portion, while the outer dataset remains a metrics dataset. The helper rejects metrics datasets, so these actual error queries never receive upsampled counts. Eligibility needs to use the dataset/query being executed (and, for split queries, the split query rather than only the original request parameters).

title: The internal upsampled aggregation is exposed without the allowlist guard
body: `upsampled_count` is registered as a normal public SnQL function, unlike the adjacent internal aggregation marked `private=True`. A caller can submit `yAxis=upsampled_count()` directly to a Discover/events-stats query for unallowlisted projects or transaction data, bypassing `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and getting an invalid or misleading aggregate. Mark this function private or enforce the same project/dataset validation at the resolver boundary.

title: The PR adds an unrelated nested-repository gitlink
body: This adds a `sentry-repo` subproject entry pinned to the base commit, despite the feature not requiring a submodule and without any accompanying submodule configuration change. Fresh or recursive checkouts will treat this path as a nested repository dependency rather than normal source content, potentially failing to initialize it or needlessly cloning another repository. Remove the gitlink unless this is an intentional, properly declared submodule dependency.

title: Merged PR comment rendering calls a helper that is not on the workflow
body: `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow` (and the equivalent GitLab workflow) invokes `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)`, but the new helper was added to `CommitContextIntegration`, not to `PRCommentWorkflow`/its subclasses. Moreover, that helper calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title`, although `_truncate_title` was also added only to `CommitContextIntegration`. Generating a merged-PR suspect-issue comment will therefore raise `AttributeError` rather than posting or updating the comment. Move both helpers to the workflow base class, or invoke them through the integration consistently.

title: Feature-flagged dashboard tables discard the query result
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, this branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and a hard-coded empty `tableData` object instead of the current `result.data` and `result.meta`. Consequently every table widget for organizations with this flag enabled renders an empty table, including after successful queries. Adapt the widget result into the visualization props rather than passing placeholder data.

title: Age and timestamp exclusivity can be bypassed with zero values
body: The mutual-exclusion validators test `self.initial_data.get(...)`, which treats valid integer value `0` as absent. A report containing both `age: 0` and `timestamp: 0` passes validation even though the endpoint explicitly requires the two format-specific fields not to coexist. Check key presence (for example, `'age' in self.initial_data`) rather than truthiness in both validators.

title: Attribute-key query cache is no longer partitioned by organization
body: The new React Query key contains only the filter-derived `queryOptions`; unlike the previous `useApiQuery` key, it does not include the organization slug. With the common all-project selection (an empty project list), navigating from one organization to another with the same date range and item/type reuses the prior organization's cached attribute collection, which is also retained while the new request is fetching via `usePrevious`. This displays cross-organization metadata and incorrect suggestions. Include `organization.slug` in the query key.

title: Falsy custom cell output incorrectly triggers the default renderer
body: The public renderer contract uses `undefined` to request fallback rendering, but this code tests `if (cell)`. Valid React nodes such as `0`, an empty string, `false`, or `null` are therefore ignored and replaced by the default cell/header renderer. Test specifically for `cell !== undefined` in both the body and header renderer paths so custom renderers can intentionally render falsy values or suppress a cell.

title: Merged PR comment helpers are attached to the wrong class
body: `_truncate_title`, `get_environment_info`, and `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` were added to `CommitContextIntegration`, but the GitHub and GitLab workflows call them on `PRCommentWorkflow` instances. Those workflow instances do not expose these methods, so generating a merged PR/MR comment raises `AttributeError` before it can be posted. Additionally, this method invokes `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title` even though the helper was declared on `CommitContextIntegration`. Move the helpers to `PRCommentWorkflow` or call them through the workflow's integration object consistently.

title: Feature-gated dashboard tables discard the query result
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the table path renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and a hard-coded empty `tableData` object instead of `fields`, `result.data`, and `result.meta`. Consequently every dashboard table widget for an enabled organization has no headers or rows, and it also bypasses the existing loading and error behavior. Adapt and pass the actual table result to the new visualization before enabling this path.

title: Attribute-key query cache key is not scoped to the organization
body: The new React Query key contains only `queryOptions`, while the query function fetches from an organization-specific URL. In particular, with no selected projects, switching organizations with the same date range and attribute type reuses the same cache key, so attributes from the previously selected organization can be displayed (and may not be refetched). Include `organization.slug` or the full endpoint path in `queryKey`.

title: Zero-valued age and timestamp bypass mutual-exclusion validation
body: The validators use `self.initial_data.get(...)` to test whether the other field was supplied. JSON reports containing both `age: 0` and `timestamp: 0` therefore pass both checks because zero is falsy, despite the endpoint requiring the two report formats to be mutually exclusive. Test field presence (for example, `'age' in self.initial_data`) rather than truthiness in both validators.

title: Falsy custom cell render results incorrectly fall back to the default renderer
body: Both default renderer wrappers use `if (cell)` even though the renderer contract says only `undefined` should request fallback and `React.ReactNode` validly includes `0`, `false`, an empty string, and `null`. A custom body renderer cannot intentionally render a blank cell or a numeric zero; the default field renderer is used instead. Check `cell !== undefined` in both the head and body renderer paths.

title: Feature-gated table widgets discard the query result
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, this branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and an empty `tableData` object instead of the current `result.data`, `result.meta`, and derived fields. Consequently every dashboard table widget for an enabled organization renders with no columns and no rows, even though its query completed successfully. Pass the actual table result and column configuration to the new visualization (and preserve its loading behavior) before enabling this path.

title: PR-comment formatting helpers are defined on the wrong class
body: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` and `_truncate_title` were added to `CommitContextIntegration`, but the new callers are `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow` and `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow`, which call `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` from the `PRCommentWorkflow` hierarchy. Those workflow instances do not receive methods added to the integration class, so generating a merged-PR comment raises `AttributeError` rather than posting/updating the comment. Move these helpers to `PRCommentWorkflow` (where this method also expects `_truncate_title`), or invoke them through the workflow's integration object.

title: Zero-valued age and timestamp bypass the mutual-exclusion validation
body: The cross-field checks use `self.initial_data.get(...)`, which treats `0` as absent. A report containing both `{"age": 0, "timestamp": 0}` passes both validators even though both timing fields are present and timestamp explicitly permits zero. This makes the collector accept a format that its validation is intended to reject; test key presence (or perform this in serializer-level `validate`) rather than truthiness.

title: Attribute-key query cache key is not scoped to the organization
body: The new React Query key contains only the item type, attribute type, date range, and project IDs; unlike the previous API-query key, it omits the organization slug. With no projects selected (the common all-projects state), two organizations using the same range produce the same cache key. On an organization switch the hook can render the prior organization's cached custom attribute names, and can retain them if the refetch fails. Include `organization.slug` in the key so cached `TagCollection` data cannot bleed between organizations.

title: Fresh installations bypass the GitHub installer identity check
body: When no Integration row exists yet, this branch advances the pipeline and creates/attaches the integration without checking `github_authenticated_user` against an installer identity. GitHub's installation webhook, which supplies `metadata.sender`, is asynchronous and can arrive after the setup callback (the normal test flow itself succeeds without a webhook). Consequently, a caller who can submit a newly created installation ID before its webhook is processed can associate it with their Sentry organization after authorizing any GitHub account, defeating the new installer/user validation. The flow must wait for or otherwise obtain and validate the installation sender before allowing this branch to create the organization integration.

title: OAuth token and user-info request failures escape as server errors
body: `safe_urlopen` is executed outside the try/except, and `get_user_info` is also unguarded. A cancelled OAuth authorization callback has a valid `state` but no `code`, and a rejected/reused code can make GitHub return a non-success response; the token request can therefore raise before the code reaches the `access_token` check. Likewise, a failed `/user` request can raise. These expected failure paths produce a 500 instead of the installation failure response promised by this flow. Catch transport/API errors around both calls and return `error(...)`.

title: Existing sender-less integrations crash during reinstallation
body: This directly indexes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`, but `build_integration` creates metadata without `sender` unless some separate state source populated it; the regular setup test explicitly produces such metadata. If its OrganizationIntegration is later removed while the active Integration remains (for example, cleanup of the organization integration or a missed webhook), this is exactly the existing-integration/no-OrganizationIntegration path and it raises KeyError rather than returning the failure page. Treat missing or malformed sender metadata as an unverifiable installation request (or obtain the sender before proceeding).

title: Fresh installations bypass the GitHub installer identity check
body: When no Integration row exists yet, this immediately advances the generic installation pipeline without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to the GitHub App installation sender. Webhook delivery and the browser setup redirect are asynchronous, so a legitimate newly-created installation can reach this branch before its installation webhook has created the Integration row. An attacker who supplies such an installation ID can therefore link the app installation to their Sentry organization after authorizing their own GitHub account, which is precisely the mismatch this flow is intended to prevent. The pipeline must wait for/obtain a trusted installer identity before creating or linking an unknown installation, rather than treating a missing Integration as verified.

title: Missing webhook sender metadata crashes the setup flow
body: This direct nested lookup raises KeyError/TypeError when an existing Integration has no `metadata.sender` or a sender without a `login`, producing a 500 instead of the installation failure page. Integrations created by the normal pipeline do not populate `sender` (the basic-flow test asserts metadata without it), and older or partially-cleaned-up Integration rows can also reach the explicitly supported state where the Integration exists but no OrganizationIntegration does. Handle absent/malformed sender metadata as an unverifiable installation (or migrate it) before attempting the comparison.

title: OAuth provider failures escape as server errors
body: Only decoding/parsing `safe_urlread` is wrapped in the try block. `safe_urlopen` itself can raise for token-endpoint HTTP/network failures, and `get_user_info` after the block can raise for a rejected token or GitHub API failure. Those cases bypass `error()` and return a 500, rather than the invalid-installation response promised by this flow. Catch the provider/API exceptions around both the token exchange and user lookup and render the failure response.

title: Proceeding when the webhook integration is absent bypasses installer validation
body: The identity comparison is only performed after an Integration record with webhook-derived `metadata.sender` already exists. If the installation webhook is delayed, dropped, or has not yet been processed, this `Integration.DoesNotExist` branch advances to the creation step without any installer identity check. That creation step can fetch arbitrary Sentry GitHub App installation details using the app credential, so a Sentry org administrator who knows an installation ID can link an installation before its webhook record is available, even though their OAuth GitHub user was not the installer. Do not advance this path until an authenticated installation event has recorded the sender (or obtain an equivalent authoritative installer identity).

title: Missing webhook sender metadata causes a 500 during reinstallation
body: `sender` is not guaranteed to be present in Integration metadata: `build_integration` only persists it when a pipeline state supplies `sender`, while ordinary frontend-created integrations do not supply that state. If such an active integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed, this is exactly the branch reached, and indexing `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError instead of returning the installation failure response. This blocks relinking/reinstalling affected existing integrations and exposes an internal error; safely handle absent or malformed sender metadata as a failed verification.

title: `queued` is fixed at module import rather than source creation
body: `timezone.now()` is evaluated when this module is imported, so every `AssignmentSource` constructed without an explicit `queued` value receives the same timestamp for the lifetime of the worker process. Consequently the serialized source metadata does not represent when an inbound assignment was queued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each source gets its own creation timestamp.

title: `queued` is fixed at module-import time instead of source creation time
body: `timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the dataclass is defined, so every `AssignmentSource` created by a worker process receives the same `queued` timestamp for the lifetime of that process. This makes the serialized context inaccurately report when an inbound assignment was queued and would break any time-based handling added around this field. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance records its own creation time.

title: Compute the queued timestamp for each AssignmentSource instance
body: `timezone.now()` is evaluated once when this module is imported, so every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` value carries the worker process startup time rather than the time the assignment was queued. This stale value is serialized into every outbound task, making the provenance timestamp incorrect and unusable for ordering or age-based handling. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to create a timestamp per instance.

title: Metric alert detector handler is now uninstantiable
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now inherits `StatefulDetectorHandler` but implements none of its abstract requirements (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). Any detector with type `metric_alert_fire` will raise `TypeError` when `Detector.detector_handler` tries to instantiate this handler, rather than safely evaluating to no results as it did before. Keep this as a concrete `DetectorHandler` until the stateful methods are implemented, or implement all required hooks.

title: The evaluate docstring still describes the old list return type
body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` now returns a dictionary keyed by `DetectorGroupKey`, but its docstring says it returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`. This documents the obsolete API contract and will mislead future handler implementations and callers.

title: Occurrence tests do not verify that each group's value reaches the new hook
body: The packet gives `group_2` the value `10`, but the expected occurrence is constructed with `6`; the helper also ignores its `value` parameter. Similar tests construct expected occurrences with values different from the input packet. Consequently, the tests would still pass if `evaluate_group_key_value` passed a stale or incorrect value to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, leaving the new hook's key input untested. Make the mock occurrence/event data depend on `value` and expect the packet's actual per-group value.

title: Metric alert detector handler cannot be instantiated
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now inherits `StatefulDetectorHandler` but implements none of its abstract requirements (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). When a detector with type `metric_alert_fire` is processed, `Detector.detector_handler` attempts to instantiate this class and raises `TypeError` instead of safely evaluating it (the previous handler returned an empty result). Implement the stateful interface or retain a concrete non-stateful handler returning the new dict result shape.

title: Stateful evaluation documentation still describes the old list return contract
body: The `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` docstring says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`", but the method now returns a dictionary keyed by `DetectorGroupKey`. This is the implementation documentation subclass authors will use for the newly changed handler API, so it should describe the keyed mapping and its uniqueness semantics.

title: Multi-group occurrence test does not verify the value passed to the new hook
body: The packet supplies `group_2` with value `10`, but the expected occurrence is built with value `6`. Since `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` does not include `value` in either returned object, this assertion still passes even if `evaluate_group_key_value` invokes `build_occurrence_and_event_data` with the wrong per-group value. Make the mock output/value observable or mock the hook and assert that `group_2` is called with `10`.

title: Registered metric-alert handler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` inherits `StatefulDetectorHandler` but implements none of its abstract requirements (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, or `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). `Detector.detector_handler` instantiates the configured handler directly, so processing any detector whose type is `metric_alert_fire` now raises `TypeError` before evaluation. Previously this handler was concrete and safely returned no results. Implement the stateful methods or do not register this class as the group type's handler until an implementation exists.

title: Stateful detector evaluation documentation still describes the old list API
body: The `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` docstring says it returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`, while the method now returns a dictionary keyed by group key. This is the extension contract detector implementations must follow; an implementation following the docstring will return a list and `process_detectors` will fail when it calls `.values()`. Update the documentation to describe the dictionary result and its key invariant.

title: Multi-group occurrence test does not verify the value passed to the new hook
body: The input gives `group_2` the value `10`, but the expected occurrence is built with `6`; moreover, `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores its `value` argument. Consequently, this test would still pass if evaluation incorrectly passed the first group's value to every `build_occurrence_and_event_data` call. Make the test helper consume the value or mock and assert the hook's arguments, including `10` for `group_2`.

title: Return the normalized config rather than the original monitor config
body: `get_monitor_environment_context` copies the monitor config and replaces `schedule_type` with its display value on lines 160-162, but line 168 returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the modified `config` copy. As a result, occurrence event contexts continue to contain the raw schedule type and the normalization code has no effect. Return `config` here so the serialized monitor context matches the intended display values.

title: Preserve or update the removed mark_failed helper API
body: This extraction renames `mark_failed_threshold` to `try_incident_threshold` and removes it from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`; the same change removes the previously importable `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, and `get_monitor_environment_context` symbols from that module. Any existing callers, integrations, or tests importing these non-private helpers from their former path will now fail with ImportError/AttributeError rather than receiving a compatibility path. Update every consumer in the repository and/or leave forwarding aliases in `mark_failed.py` (ideally with a deprecation plan) before merging.

title: Hung spawn workers are not killed before their replacements start
body: Workers are created with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which produces a `SpawnProcess` that is not an instance of the top-level `multiprocessing.Process` class. Consequently this guard is false in production. When a worker is declared hung, it is left running and a replacement is started for the same shards. If the original worker recovers, both workers can flush and produce the same Redis segments concurrently, causing duplicate buffered-segment messages and conflicting backpressure/health updates. Check against the spawn context's base process type (or capability) and join/kill the old worker before replacing it.

title: The default CLI configuration still creates only one flusher worker
body: Click always supplies the default `flusher_processes=1` to `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory`, so `SpanFlusher` receives a limit of one rather than its per-shard fallback. Thus a normal `process-spans` invocation without an explicit flag continues to run a single flusher even when it owns multiple Redis shards, and the stated per-shard parallelization/capacity improvement is never enabled by default. Use a per-shard default (for example, pass `None` through to `SpanFlusher`) or configure the intended shard-count limit in the consumer's default deployment arguments.

title: `--flusher-processes` accepts invalid values that can prevent consumer startup
body: The option accepts any integer. A negative value is truthy in `SpanFlusher`, making `num_processes` negative; no process-map entries are created and assigning the first shard then raises a `KeyError`. A value of zero is silently treated as false and instead creates one worker per assigned shard, violating the requested maximum. Restrict the option to integers of at least one (and validate the constructor as well for non-CLI callers).

title: The added wait is disabled by the test's own sleep monkeypatch
body: This test replaces `time.sleep` with a no-op at line 15, so `time.sleep(0.1)` does not give the flusher thread time to observe the changed drift. `step.join()` can therefore set the stop flag before the thread flushes, making the assertion dependent on thread scheduling and allowing intermittent tuple-unpacking failures or false coverage. Preserve the real sleep for this synchronization point or use an event/polling condition that waits for `messages`.

title: Hang recovery does not kill spawned flusher processes
body: Workers are always created with the explicit `spawn` context, which produces `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` instances. `SpawnProcess` is not an instance of the public default-context `multiprocessing.Process` class, so this guard is false for production workers. When a worker is deemed hung, the code starts a replacement for the same shard group without killing the old worker; the old process is then no longer tracked and can continue flushing/producing concurrently. Repeated health failures leak workers and can duplicate segment output. Test against the spawn-context process/base-process type (or simply use a `kill` capability check) and wait for the old worker before replacing it.

title: Timed joins abandon remaining flusher workers
body: Once `next_step.join(timeout)` or waiting for an earlier worker exhausts the deadline, this `break` exits the loop without attempting cleanup for the current or later workers. A worker blocked in Redis or Kafka can therefore outlive `SpanFlusher.join`, leaving multiple daemon workers running after the consumer has shut down or rebalanced. Apply the deadline to waiting, but still terminate/join every worker after the deadline is reached.

title: Inserting max_processes breaks positional produce_to_pipe callers
body: `produce_to_pipe` was the third optional positional argument to `SpanFlusher`; adding `max_processes` before it changes `SpanFlusher(buffer, next_step, callback)` to treat the callback as a process count. Construction then fails when `min` compares that callable with the shard count. Preserve the existing positional contract by placing `max_processes` after `produce_to_pipe` or making the new argument keyword-only.

title: Invalid flusher process counts are accepted and crash initialization
body: The new option accepts arbitrary integers. With `--flusher-processes -1` and any assigned shard, `SpanFlusher` computes `num_processes == -1`, creates an empty process map, and then raises `KeyError` when assigning the first shard to index 0. A value of zero also silently means one process per shard because of the `or` fallback, contrary to the stated maximum. Restrict the Click option to positive integers (and validate direct construction similarly).

title: The new process-limit test only runs thread-based workers
body: Passing a non-null `produce_to_pipe` forces `SpanFlusher` to use `threading.Thread`, so this test never executes the spawn-process branch used in production. It only inspects the shard map and does not verify that multiple spawned workers can initialize, flush, restart, or shut down. Add coverage using actual spawn workers and process-safe output/producer mocking; this would exercise the new lifecycle code.

title: Spawn-context flusher workers are not killed before replacement
body: Workers are always created from `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, so production workers are `SpawnProcess` instances. `SpawnProcess` is not an instance of the default-context `multiprocessing.Process` class, causing this guard to be false. When a worker is declared hung, the manager starts a replacement for the same Redis shards without killing the original worker; if the original recovers, both workers can flush and produce the same segments concurrently. The same incorrect type check at line 346 also prevents forced shutdown of these spawned workers. Detect process workers independently of the default context (or explicitly exclude only `threading.Thread`) before calling `kill`/`terminate`.

title: A timed-out join leaves remaining flusher workers alive
body: For multiple workers, once the shared join deadline is exhausted this `break` exits the loop before terminating the current or any later worker. `next_step.join(timeout)` may consume the entire timeout before the loop begins, and waiting for the first flusher can consume it for all subsequent workers. A worker blocked in Kafka `future.result()` will not observe the cooperative stopped flag, so those unvisited workers remain running after consumer shutdown/rebalance and can continue operating on revoked shards. Terminate all still-alive process workers after the deadline rather than breaking out before cleanup.

title: The new flusher process count accepts values that break or defeat the limit
body: `--flusher-processes` accepts zero and negative values. A negative value reaches `SpanFlusher`, makes `num_processes` negative, creates no process-map entries, and then raises `KeyError` while assigning the first shard. Zero is treated as false by `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, unexpectedly starting one worker per shard rather than rejecting the invalid limit. Restrict this option to integers of at least one and validate direct constructor callers as well.

title: The new limit test never exercises the multiprocessing implementation
body: Passing `produce_to_pipe=messages.append` selects the `threading.Thread` branch in `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, so this test only checks the in-memory shard map and starts no spawned worker. The production path added by this change initializes Sentry, pickles a shard-specific buffer, creates `SpawnProcess` workers, and must handle their lifecycle; none of that is covered. Add a test that runs the process branch (with Kafka production mocked or an interprocess-safe sink) and verifies shard flushing and shutdown/restart behavior.

title: The added synchronization delay is a no-op
body: The test replaces `time.sleep` with a no-op at line 15, so this purported 0.1-second wait does not give the asynchronous flusher thread any time to observe the drift and emit a segment. `step.join()` then sets the stopped flag, allowing the worker to exit before flushing depending on scheduling. This makes the assertion race-prone; synchronize on an event, queue result, or a bounded polling condition instead of the patched sleep.

title: Shutdown uses Queue APIs unavailable on supported Python versions
body: `Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were only added in Python 3.13. On earlier supported interpreters, `q.shutdown()` raises `AttributeError` (which is merely logged here), leaving workers blocked indefinitely in `Queue.get()`. Each subsequent `join(timeout=5)` then waits its full timeout, so the default 20-worker consumer can spend roughly 100 seconds shutting down and leak daemon threads.

title: The worker queues are unbounded, so a slow group can exhaust process memory
body: `queue.Queue()` defaults to an unlimited size, while `submit` always accepts work immediately. A slow result or persistently slow group therefore causes its queue, retained `WorkItem` payloads, and offset-tracker sets to grow without bound while the Kafka consumer continues polling. This provides no natural backpressure despite the strategy's stated guarantee and can OOM the consumer during a backlog.

title: Normal strategy close can abandon work and miss its final offset commit
body: `close` stops and joins the commit thread before shutting down the workers. A worker that finishes its current item after the commit thread's final iteration will mark the offset complete with no thread left to commit it. In addition, `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` sets every worker's shutdown flag before draining queued items, so workers exit after at most their current item. A normal rebalance/deploy can therefore leave completed work uncommitted and replay it after restart, producing duplicate result side effects rather than performing the advertised graceful shutdown.

title: Negative max-workers silently acknowledges every message without processing it
body: The CLI accepts any integer for `max_workers`, and a negative value is truthy here, so `FixedQueuePool` is constructed with a negative queue count. Its initialization creates no queues; each submission then raises while indexing `self.queues`. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` catches that exception and adds/completes the offset, allowing the commit loop to acknowledge messages that were never sent to a worker. Validate that the configured queue/worker count is positive instead of accepting negative values.

title: Worker exceptions are acknowledged as successfully processed
body: The `finally` block completes the offset even when `result_processor` raised and the exception was only logged by the preceding handler. Once earlier offsets complete, the commit loop will commit this failed message and Kafka will not retry it, permanently dropping failed result handling. This contradicts the strategy's documented promise to commit only after successful processing; failures need to remain outstanding or be routed through an explicit retry/DLQ policy.

title: Failed result processing is acknowledged and committed
body: The worker catches every exception from `result_processor` and then unconditionally marks the offset complete in `finally`. The commit loop will subsequently commit that offset, so a transient database/API failure permanently drops the result instead of retrying or sending it to a DLQ. This contradicts the strategy's stated guarantee that offsets are committed only after successful processing; the added error-handling test also does not wait for the one-second commit loop, so it can pass before the erroneous commit occurs.

title: Negative --max-workers silently drops all consumed messages
body: `--max-workers` accepts arbitrary integers, but a negative value is passed as `num_queues`. `range(num_queues)` then creates no queues or workers; each submission raises while indexing `self.queues`, and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` catches that error and marks the message complete. The commit loop will therefore advance Kafka offsets without processing any results. Reject non-positive worker counts rather than using `max_workers or 20`.

title: The queue pool has no backpressure and can grow without bound
body: Each work queue is constructed as an unbounded `queue.Queue()`, and `submit` always returns after an O(1) enqueue. If a queue's worker is slow or blocked, the consumer continues polling and accumulating full Kafka payloads in memory indefinitely. This defeats the documented natural backpressure and can OOM a consumer during a downstream outage or a hot group; the queues need a bounded capacity and a corresponding pause/blocking policy.

title: Shutdown relies on Python 3.13-only queue APIs
body: `Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were added in Python 3.13. On Python 3.12 and earlier, `q.shutdown()` raises `AttributeError`, which is swallowed here, leaving idle workers blocked forever in `get()`. Because workers are joined sequentially with five-second timeouts, shutting down the default 20 queues can take roughly 100 seconds and leaks daemon threads. Use sentinels or timed `get()` calls unless the project has dropped all pre-3.13 runtimes.

title: Closing a strategy disables the worker pool reused by later assignments
body: `ResultsStrategyFactory` creates one `FixedQueuePool` and reuses it for every `create_with_partitions` call, but this strategy's `close`/`terminate` shuts that shared pool down. `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` sets every worker's shutdown flag and never recreates workers. If the processing strategy is recreated after a partition reassignment/rebalance, the factory hands the new strategy the same dead queues, so newly submitted work is never processed and its offsets remain outstanding. Allocate a fresh pool per strategy assignment or reset/restart the pool before reuse.

title: Use of Python 3.13-only queue shutdown APIs breaks supported runtimes
body: `queue.Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were introduced in Python 3.13. On earlier supported Python versions, `q.shutdown(...)` raises `AttributeError` (which is only logged here), leaving workers blocked forever in `get()`. Each subsequent `worker.join(timeout=5.0)` then waits the full timeout, so the default 20 queues can make every consumer shutdown take roughly 100 seconds and leak daemon workers. An exception raised while processing work also attempts to resolve `queue.ShutDown` in the exception handler and can terminate the worker with an `AttributeError`. Use a compatible sentinel/event-based shutdown mechanism or require and enforce Python 3.13.

title: Closing one assignment permanently disables the factory-owned pool
body: The pool is created once on `ResultsStrategyFactory` and is shared by every strategy returned from `create_with_partitions`, but `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` shuts that shared pool down. After a Kafka partition revoke/reassignment causes Arroyo to close/terminate one strategy and create another from the same factory, the new strategy receives the already-shut-down pool and no workers. On Python 3.13, `Queue.put()` then raises `ShutDown`, and `submit()` catches that error and marks the offset complete, so the new strategy can commit messages that were never processed. On older Python versions, the puts succeed into queues with no workers and offsets never advance. The pool must be scoped to a single strategy assignment or recreated/reset after strategy teardown.

title: The worker queues are unbounded, so the new mode provides no backpressure
body: `queue.Queue()` defaults to `maxsize=0`, meaning `FixedQueuePool.submit()` never blocks regardless of how far a slow worker falls behind. The consumer will continue decoding and retaining every fetched message (including both the decoded result and original `Message`) in memory while lag grows. A slow remote-subscription handler can therefore cause unbounded memory growth and OOM the consumer, contrary to the strategy's stated backpressure guarantee. Configure a bounded queue size and integrate blocking/full-queue handling with the consumer's polling/backpressure behavior.

title: The purported graceful shutdown abandons queued work before a final commit
body: Workers are marked `shutdown=True` before their queues are shut down. A worker that is currently processing exits after that item, and a worker that was blocked in `get()` processes at most one item before its next loop-condition check exits; remaining queued items are never drained. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` also stops and joins the commit thread before this worker shutdown, so an item finishing during shutdown has no later commit opportunity. This causes arbitrary accepted work to be replayed after normal deploys/rebalances, potentially duplicating side effects and creating large restart backlogs. Shutdown should drain accepted work (or deliberately cancel it with a coordinated retry policy) and commit completed offsets after the drain.

title: Import Prisma before using it
body: The new credential update references `prisma`, but this module neither imports nor declares it. This fails TypeScript checking and, if transpiled without checking, throws a ReferenceError whenever Salesforce client initialization reaches the update, preventing Salesforce operations.

title: Persist the parsed Google credentials, not the safeParse result
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{ success: true, data: ... }`, whereas the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credentials themselves. Saving this result directly as `key` nests all tokens under `data`. After a successful refresh, the next GoogleCalendarService instance cannot parse the saved credentials. This also corrupts credentials when sharing is disabled; persist the result's `data` instead.

title: Define actual token fields instead of stringifying Zod schemas
body: Using `z.string().toString()` as an object key does not define a wildcard: both computed keys evaluate to the literal `[object Object]`, and the second overwrites the first. Zod also strips unknown fields by default, so a sync response containing `access_token` and `expires_in` loses its expiry and refresh token. Zoom consequently calculates a NaN expiry, and Office365 cannot retain the new expiry. Define explicit supported expiry fields and preserve the required response properties.

title: Normalize the sync response to the callers' expected shape
body: The sync branch returns a Fetch `Response`, but several wrapped callbacks return incompatible shapes: Google and both Zoho adapters expect `.data`, while HubSpot expects a decoded token object with `accessToken` and `expiresIn`. None of those callers decodes the sync response. With syncing enabled, Google/Zoho dereference undefined and HubSpot uses undefined token fields, even when the endpoint returns valid JSON. Establish a consistent decoded response contract and adapt each caller.

title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a placeholder
body: This assignment runs even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365 explicitly permits refresh responses without `refresh_token` and merges the parsed response into the existing credentials. Adding the literal `refresh_token` therefore overwrites the user's valid refresh token when Microsoft omits a replacement, causing the next refresh to fail. Preserve the existing refresh token when no replacement is returned.

title: Pass the credential owner's user ID to the sync endpoint
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` interprets its third argument as a user ID and sends it as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes the credential's database ID. These IDs are unrelated. The parent application will either fail to find the user or select another user's Bigin credentials. Carry `credential.userId` through to this method and pass that instead, retaining the credential ID only for database updates.

title: Send the Zoom app slug rather than its integration directory name
body: The sync request sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are created with `appId: "zoom"`, and the inbound webhook identifies apps by their database slug. A parent application using that same app identity cannot match this refresh request to the synced Zoom credentials. Pass `zoom` here.

title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
body: Unlike the other adapters, Salesforce now unconditionally refreshes directly against Salesforce rather than calling `refreshOAuthTokens`. Enabling credential syncing changes its response parser but never changes the refresh destination. For credentials whose refresh token is held by the parent application, client initialization fails with an invalid refresh token even if a valid access token was synced. Use the external refresh path when configured.

title: Authenticate outbound credential requests
body: The request asking the parent application to return a user's OAuth access token contains only a predictable user ID and app slug. It sends neither the configured shared secret nor another authentication proof. An endpoint protected by a shared secret cannot accept these requests; an endpoint that trusts this payload alone exposes users' third-party tokens to anyone who can reach it. Add an authenticated outbound request contract rather than requiring the token-serving endpoint to trust these identifiers.

title: Support the minimal sync payload in Webex token validation
body: The new sync helper specifies that the endpoint should return only an access token and expiry, but this adapter still validates that response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token expiry. A response following the new contract is always rejected, so synced Webex credentials stop working when their access token expires. Add a sync-specific response path that preserves existing metadata and does not require a remotely held refresh token.

title: Adapt Lark refresh handling to externally managed tokens
body: Only the request destination changes here; the following code still expects Lark's nested `data` envelope and both `refresh_token` and `refresh_expires_in`. The helper's documented access-token-and-expiry response therefore fails parsing. Even if the parent supplies a Lark envelope with only those minimal fields, the saved credential loses its refresh token and the next refresh deletes it at the local refresh-token check. Handle synced credentials separately so the parent can own refresh tokens without Cal.com rejecting or deleting the integration.

title: Import Prisma before using it in the Salesforce service
body: The new credential update references `prisma`, but this module neither imports nor declares it. This fails TypeScript checking and, if transpiled without checking, throws a ReferenceError after a successful token refresh, preventing Salesforce operations.

title: Persist the parsed Google credentials rather than the safeParse result
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{ success: true, data: ... }`, whereas the previous schema `.parse()` returned the credentials themselves. Saving this result directly as `credential.key` replaces the credential with a validation-result wrapper. This also affects installations with syncing disabled: after the first successful refresh, subsequent GoogleCalendarService instances cannot parse the stored credentials. Persist the result's `data` instead.

title: Replace computed schema keys with actual token-field validation
body: `z.string().toString()` does not define a wildcard property: it produces the literal key `[object Object]`. Both computed keys resolve to that same key, so the optional unknown schema overwrites the numeric schema. Since Zod objects strip unknown properties by default, a sync response such as `{ access_token: "token", expires_in: 3600 }` loses its expiry and any refresh token. Zoom then computes a NaN expiry, and Office 365 cannot persist the refreshed expiry. Define and preserve the actual supported response fields.

title: Normalize the sync response for SDK and Axios callers
body: The sync branch returns a Fetch `Response`, but several callers retain the return contract of their original refresh function. Google Calendar and both Zoho services read `.data`, while HubSpot reads `.accessToken` and `.expiresIn` directly. None of these properties exists on a Fetch Response, regardless of its JSON body. Enabling syncing therefore makes those refresh paths throw or use undefined tokens. Establish a consistent response contract and deserialize/adapt the response in each caller.

title: Do not replace existing refresh tokens with a placeholder
body: The literal `"refresh_token"` is inserted whenever a response omits a refresh token, including when credential sharing is disabled. Office 365 explicitly accepts refresh responses without a new refresh token and merges the parsed data into the existing credentials. This new placeholder overwrites the valid saved refresh token, so the next refresh fails. Preserve the existing token when the provider does not return a replacement; do not fabricate one in the shared parser.

title: Pass the Bigin credential owner's user ID to the sync endpoint
body: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a user ID and is sent externally as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes the credential row's ID. These IDs are unrelated. The parent application will either find no matching user or return another user's Bigin token, potentially causing CRM writes against the wrong account. Carry `credential.userId` through to this method instead.

title: Delegate Salesforce refreshes when credential sharing is enabled
body: The new Salesforce refresh always posts directly to Salesforce instead of using the configured credential-sync endpoint. For externally managed credentials, Cal.com may only have an access token and no usable refresh token; this request then fails before the connection is constructed, even if the supplied access token is still valid. Route this refresh through the same delegation mechanism as the other integrations and use the returned token in the connection.

title: Send Zoom's app slug rather than its integration directory name
body: The sync request sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are created with `appId: "zoom"`, and the new webhook identifies apps by their database slug. A parent application using that same slug to store and retrieve credentials cannot resolve this refresh request. Pass `"zoom"` here to keep the inbound and outbound contracts consistent.

title: Authenticate requests that retrieve external access tokens
body: The outbound request contains only a numeric user ID and app slug, with no secret, signature, or authorization header. An ordinary HTTP sync endpoint therefore has no application-level way to distinguish Cal.com from a caller requesting another user's token. A protected endpoint must reject these requests; accepting them without additional infrastructure exposes tokens to anyone who can reach it. Add an authenticated outbound protocol rather than requiring an unauthenticated token lookup.

title: Make initial webhook credential creation atomic
body: The lookup and create are separate operations without serialization. Two concurrent deliveries for the same new user/app pair can both observe no credential and create separate rows. Later deliveries update only whichever row `findFirst` selects, leaving the other credential stale and potentially causing duplicate integration processing. Make this operation idempotent under concurrent webhook delivery.

title: Clear invalid status when replacing credentials through the webhook
body: The update path replaces only `key`. Integrations such as Google Calendar and Zoom mark credentials `invalid: true` after unrecoverable authentication failures. Sending replacement credentials through this webhook returns success but leaves that invalid status intact, so an external reconnection does not restore a healthy installed credential. Reset the invalid flag when accepting replacement credentials.

title: Adapt Webex validation to the delegated token response
body: The new helper documents a sync response containing only an access token and expiry, but Webex still validates that response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token lifetime. A response following the delegated-refresh contract is always rejected as invalid, preventing Webex meeting operations after token expiry. Add a delegated-response adapter and preserve the necessary existing credential metadata.

title: Import Prisma before using it in the Salesforce client
body: The new credential update references `prisma`, but this file never imports or declares it. This fails TypeScript checking and, if emitted anyway, throws a ReferenceError after a successful token refresh, preventing Salesforce client initialization.

title: Persist the parsed Google tokens, not the safeParse result
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{ success: true, data: tokens }`, unlike the previous schema.parse call, which returned the tokens themselves. Saving that entire result as the credential key removes access_token, refresh_token, and expiry_date from the top level. The next GoogleCalendarService instance cannot parse the stored credential. This affects ordinary Google refreshes even when credential sharing is disabled; persist the result's data instead.

title: Replace computed schema keys with actual token fields
body: `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` both produce the literal property name `[object Object]`; they do not declare wildcard properties. The second declaration overwrites the first, and Zod strips all undeclared fields. Consequently, a sync response containing access_token, expires_in, and refresh_token loses its expiry and refresh token. Zoom then calculates a NaN expiry, while Office 365 cannot retain the refreshed expiry. Define and normalize the supported expiry fields explicitly and preserve the required token fields.

title: Normalize refresh responses before returning them to adapters
body: The sync branch returns a fetch Response, but the fallback branch returns whatever the provider callback returns. Google and both Zoho adapters expect a response with `.data`, while HubSpot expects a decoded token object with `.accessToken` and `.expiresIn`. A fetch Response has none of these properties, regardless of the JSON sent by the sync server. Enabling syncing therefore breaks refreshes for these integrations. Decode and adapt the sync response to a consistent contract, and update the callers accordingly.

title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a dummy value
body: This fallback runs even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365CalendarService explicitly accepts refresh responses without a refresh_token and merges the parsed response over the existing credentials. Adding the literal `refresh_token` causes that merge to overwrite the real refresh token, so the next refresh fails and the user must reconnect. Leave omitted refresh tokens absent so callers can preserve the existing value.

title: Pass the user ID rather than the credential ID to token syncing
body: The third argument of refreshOAuthTokens is serialized as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes the credential record's ID. Those IDs are unrelated. The parent platform will either fail to find the user or return another user's Bigin token when the IDs happen to overlap. Carry credential.userId through to this method and use it for the sync request.

title: Send the actual Zoom app slug to the sync endpoint
body: This sends `zoomvideo` as appSlug, but Zoom credentials are created with appId `zoom`, and the webhook identifies apps by their stored slug. A parent platform using the same app identifiers for ingestion and refresh cannot resolve this request. Use `zoom` rather than the integration directory name.

title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
body: The newly added Salesforce refresh unconditionally calls Salesforce directly instead of refreshOAuthTokens. With sharing enabled, a credential whose refresh token is managed by the parent platform cannot initialize this client, even if its current access token is valid: initialization immediately attempts a direct refresh using a missing or placeholder refresh token. Honor the same sync routing used by the other adapters and initialize the connection with the refreshed credentials.

title: Authenticate outbound credential-sync requests
body: The request asks the parent platform to return a user's access token using only a numeric user ID and app slug, with no authentication header or signature. The configured webhook secret is checked only on inbound requests. A normally authenticated parent endpoint will reject these requests; accepting them as implemented would expose users' third-party access tokens to anyone who can reach that endpoint and enumerate IDs. Include a configured authentication mechanism in the outbound request.

title: Clear the invalid flag when replacing revoked credentials
body: The update path replaces only the key. Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credentials invalid after an invalid_grant response, so syncing fresh credentials after a user reconnects on the parent platform leaves the existing record marked invalid. The webhook reports success without restoring the integration. Reset invalid to false when accepting replacement credentials.

title: Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache
body: The delete-cache success handler only calls the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper does not provide a default refetch callback and disables refetchOnWindowFocus, so a successful deletion can leave the old timestamp and Delete cached data action visible until the page is reloaded. Invalidate connectedCalendars after deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

title: Resolve persistent cache records for in-memory delegated credentials
body: For delegated connections represented by negative, in-memory credential IDs, querying CalendarCache by the displayed credentialId cannot find their cache records. The cache repository explicitly supports serving these connections from persistent records using userId and the calendar key instead. Consequently, a delegated calendar can actively serve cached availability while this endpoint returns cacheUpdatedAt: null, hiding both status and deletion controls. Resolve the corresponding persistent cache records within the current user's scope and support that same mapping in the deletion handler.

title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script
body: ENV_FILE="../.env" is relative to the caller's working directory, not the script's directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore creates or modifies .env in the repository's parent directory rather than the application's environment file. The script reports success, but the application never receives GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. Derive the repository path from BASH_SOURCE before selecting the environment file.

title: Use a portable in-place replacement for the webhook URL
body: The sed -i '' syntax works with BSD sed but fails with GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, the replacement fails and the script still prints that it updated the file, leaving the application pointed at the previous tunnel. Use a cross-platform replacement and check its exit status before reporting success.

title: Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache
body: The delete-cache success handler only invokes the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper passes an optional caller callback rather than refetching that query, and disables refetchOnWindowFocus. Consequently, deleting the cache can show a success toast while continuing to display the old cache timestamp and deletion action until the page is reloaded. Invalidate connectedCalendars on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

title: Resolve cache status for in-memory delegation credentials
body: Connected calendars can use in-memory delegation credentials, but this lookup assumes every displayed credential ID is a database credential ID. CalendarCacheRepository.getCachedAvailability explicitly handles in-memory credentials by querying userId and the cache key, since their cache is stored under a real credential ID. Looking up status solely using the displayed credential ID therefore returns no status for those delegated calendars even when availability is being served from cache. Since the dropdown hides all cache actions when cacheUpdatedAt is null, affected users cannot inspect or clear that cache. Resolve the user's backing cache records for delegated connections and support that same identity in the deletion flow.

title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script
body: ENV_FILE="../.env" is resolved relative to the caller's working directory, not the script's directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore edits or creates an .env outside the repository, leaving the application's GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL unchanged despite printing success. Derive the repository path from BASH_SOURCE before locating .env.

title: Use an environment-file replacement compatible with GNU sed
body: The sed -i '' syntax requires BSD sed. On Linux with GNU sed, the empty argument is interpreted as the editing script and this command fails instead of replacing an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. Because the failure is unchecked, the script still reports that the URL was updated, leaving webhook testing pointed at the previous tunnel. Use a portable replacement approach or handle the sed variants explicitly and check the result.

title: Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache
body: The cache-deletion success handler only calls the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper forwards an optional onChanged callback and disables refetchOnWindowFocus, so without a caller-provided refetch the UI continues displaying the deleted cache's timestamp and deletion action after reporting success. Invalidate connectedCalendars here, as the disconnect mutation already does.

title: Resolve cache status for in-memory delegation credentials
body: Connected calendars can contain in-memory delegation credentials with negative IDs, whereas CalendarCache rows reference persisted credentials. Looking up status solely by the displayed credentialId therefore returns no cache for these connections, even when availability is being served from cached data. CalendarCacheRepository.getCachedAvailability explicitly handles this case through userId and the calendar key, including reuse of pre-delegation cache rows. Resolve the corresponding persisted cache records for delegated connections as well; otherwise these users cannot see or clear their active cache through the new UI.

title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script location
body: ENV_FILE is relative to the caller's working directory, not the script directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root writes ../.env outside the repository, creating it if necessary, while leaving the application's environment unchanged. Derive the repository root from BASH_SOURCE before selecting .env so the advertised webhook configuration is actually applied.

title: Make the environment update work with GNU sed
body: The sed -i '' invocation uses BSD/macOS syntax and fails under GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, the script consequently leaves the old URL in place but still prints that it updated the file successfully. Use a portable replacement strategy or distinguish the sed implementations, and check the command result before reporting success.

title: Invalid ERB Ruby prevents rendering existing discussions
body: The tag `<%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby: the block should close with `end`, without the trailing `if`. Every embed request that finds an existing topic will fail with a template syntax error instead of displaying the discussion. The controller tests stub rendering, so they do not catch this; add a test that renders this view.

title: Raw HTML posts bypass sanitization on import and subsequent edits
body: Returning `raw` directly makes external HTML executable forum content. `PollFeed` passes feed HTML to `TopicEmbed.import`, which only parses and rewrites URLs with Nokogiri; it does not remove scripts, event handlers, or unsafe URL schemes. These posts are then rendered as trusted cooked HTML. Subsequent edits also retain the raw-HTML cook method, allowing an author who can edit an imported post to inject executable markup even if its initial import was safe. Sanitize raw-HTML posts before assigning their cooked content.

title: Automatic redirects bypass the embed host restriction
body: `TopicRetriever` checks only the hostname of the initial URL, but `open(url)` follows redirects to other hosts without repeating that check. An allowlisted URL that redirects to an internal HTTP endpoint therefore causes the worker to fetch that endpoint and potentially publish its contents as a topic.
