Validate redirect destinations and resolved addresses before connecting, or disable automatic redirects and handle them through a restricted fetcher.

title: Feed polling assumes every entry has Atom-style content
body: Valid RSS entries can provide their body through `description` or `content:encoded`, and Atom entries can contain only a summary. For these entries, `i.content` is absent, so accessing it or calling `scrub` fails and aborts the entire polling run. The same exception also prevents `TopicRetriever` from reaching its HTTP fallback when feed polling is enabled. Select the supported body fields with a fallback and handle entries without a body; test actual RSS and Atom fixtures rather than only delegation to `poll_feed`.

title: URL rewriting corrupts protocol-relative links and misses relative paths
body: The slash-prefix rewrite treats `//cdn.example.com/image.png` as a path on the article host, producing a URL such as `https://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/image.png`. Conversely, document-relative references such as `images/photo.png` and `../article` are left unchanged and resolve against the Discourse page rather than the imported article. Both anchor and image handling have this problem. Resolve references against the article URL using URI resolution instead of manually concatenating the host.

title: Invalid ERB closing statement prevents rendering existing discussions
body: The opening conditional is closed with `end if` rather than `end`. This produces invalid Ruby in the compiled template, so requests for an existing embedded topic fail instead of displaying the discussion. Change this to `<%- end %>` and exercise the endpoint with view rendering enabled.

title: Raw HTML posts bypass sanitization and allow stored XSS
body: Returning `raw` unchanged bypasses the rendering pipeline's HTML sanitization. The RSS poller passes external HTML directly to `TopicEmbed.import`, and `absolutize_urls` only parses and rewrites URLs; it does not remove scripts or event handlers. Consequently, feed content such as an image with an `onerror` handler is stored as executable cooked HTML under the forum's origin. Subsequent edits to these posts also retain this bypass. Sanitize raw-HTML posts before storing or rendering their cooked content.

title: Escape the source URL before interpolating it into HTML
body: The source URL is inserted into both a single-quoted attribute and link text without escaping. A URL on the permitted host with a fragment such as `#'onclick='alert(1)` can pass URI host validation and fetch the original article, but produces an injected `onclick` attribute in the imported attribution link. This link is appended after Readability processes the article and is rendered through the raw-HTML path. Build the link with an escaping HTML helper rather than string interpolation.

title: Handle RSS items that do not contain an Atom content field
body: The poller unconditionally reads `i.content.scrub`, but valid RSS items commonly supply their body through `description` or `content:encoded`, and Atom entries can have only a summary. For these feeds the content value is absent, causing the poll to fail before importing the item or any subsequent entries. Select the appropriate available body field and handle entries without a body explicitly; add coverage using actual RSS and Atom fixtures.

title: Resolve relative URLs without corrupting protocol-relative links
body: Treating every leading slash as a root-relative path rewrites `//cdn.example.com/image.png` into a path on the article host, breaking protocol-relative images and links. Conversely, document-relative references such as `images/photo.png` and `../other-page` remain unchanged and resolve against the Discourse page rather than the source article. Resolve both `href` and `src` against the full source URL with URI resolution instead of manually stripping slashes.

title: Revalidate redirect destinations when retrieving an embedded article
body: `TopicRetriever` checks only the host of the initial URL, while `open(url)` automatically follows redirects without applying that restriction. An allowed-host redirect to another host, including a loopback or private-network HTTP service, therefore makes the worker fetch an otherwise forbidden destination and potentially publish its response as a topic. Validate each redirect destination and reject private/internal addresses before making the request.

title: Preserve the original thread creation date during Disqus imports
body: The previous topic creation passed `t[:created_at]` to `PostCreator`; the replacement passes only the title, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` creates the first post with the current time. Replies still retain their historical timestamps, so imported topics now appear newly created and have replies dated before their opening post. Carry the original creation timestamp through the new import path.

title: Invalid ERB closing statement prevents discussion rendering
body: The conditional ends with `end if` instead of `end`. This generates invalid Ruby when Rails compiles the template, so requests for an existing embedded topic fail rather than display the discussion. The controller specs do not render views and therefore miss this failure. Replace the closing statement and add a view-rendering test.

title: Raw HTML imports bypass sanitization and enable stored XSS
body: Returning `raw` directly makes imported HTML executable forum content. `PollFeed` passes feed content to `TopicEmbed.import`, which only parses and rewrites URLs with Nokogiri; neither step removes scripts, event handlers, or unsafe link schemes. Furthermore, `TopicEmbed.import` interpolates the source URL into HTML without escaping it, allowing quotes in a fetched URL's query to inject attributes into the attribution link. These posts are subsequently rendered as trusted cooked HTML. Sanitize imported HTML, escape the attribution URL, and retain sanitization when raw-HTML posts are edited.

title: Feed polling assumes every entry has an Atom content field
body: Valid RSS entries commonly provide their body through `description` or `content:encoded`, and Atom entries can provide only a summary. SimpleRSS exposes these separately, so `i.content` can be nil and calling `scrub` raises an exception. One such entry aborts the entire polling run and also prevents TopicRetriever from reaching its HTTP fallback. Select the available body field and handle entries without content; cover an actual RSS feed in the tests.

title: URL rewriting corrupts protocol-relative links and misses relative paths
body: The leading-slash check treats `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` as a path on the article's host, rewriting it to something like `https://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. Conversely, document-relative URLs such as `images/image.jpg` are left unchanged and resolve against the forum instead of the source article. The same problem exists in the image branch below. Resolve references against the complete source URL using URI resolution rather than concatenating a host prefix.

title: Disqus imports no longer preserve thread creation dates
body: The previous PostCreator call supplied the exported thread's `created_at`, but the replacement passes only its title. TopicEmbed creates the topic and initial post with the current time, while imported replies still use their historical dates. This loses the original thread timestamps and can leave replies dated before the topic's initial post. Pass the exported creation time through the import helpers to PostCreator.

title: Preserve right alignment in the legacy flexbox fallback
body: The new flexbox mixin explicitly falls back to `display: -webkit-box`, but that older layout model does not distribute free space to auto margins. On box-only browsers such as Android 4.3's stock browser and Safari 6, removing `float: right` and relying on `margin-left: auto` therefore leaves the navigation panel immediately after the logo/topic information instead of at the right edge. No child is given `-webkit-box-flex` to absorb the remaining space. Provide a compatible expanding spacer/item for that fallback, or retain a working non-flex layout for those browsers.

title: Preserve right alignment in the legacy flexbox fallback
body: The new `flexbox()` mixin explicitly falls back to `display: -webkit-box`, but that older layout model does not distribute free space through auto margins. On browsers using this fallback (such as the Android 4.x stock browser), removing `float: right` and relying on `margin-left: auto` leaves the header panel immediately beside the logo/topic information instead of against the right edge. Provide a compatible flexible spacer or retain a working fallback layout for these browsers.

title: Preserve the full-width action description when switching to flexbox
body: Making `.small-action` a flex container turns `.small-action-desc` into an auto-sized flex item with no flex growth. It therefore no longer fills the remaining row width. The existing right-floated action button inside the description is positioned beside the description text rather than at the right edge of the row. Give the description the remaining space (for example, with `flex: 1` and an appropriate minimum width) so action controls retain their previous placement.

title: Rejected devices are cached as successfully admitted
body: TagDevice calls tagDeviceUI, which populates localCache before CreateOrUpdateDevice checks the limit. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, that cache entry remains. The next request from the same device returns nil from the cache lookup, so Authenticate grants anonymous access for the remainder of the 29-minute cache lifetime. A rejected device can therefore bypass the limit simply by retrying. Cache only successful admissions, and add a test that repeatedly authenticates a rejected device.

title: Make device admission atomic with the limit check
body: CountDevices and the subsequent INSERT run in separate database sessions without any serialization. With one slot remaining, concurrent requests from distinct new devices can both observe a count below the limit and both insert successfully. Those devices then remain eligible for updates even though the configured cap has been exceeded. Serialize the count-and-admit operation across requests and Grafana instances using appropriate database locking or an equivalent atomic admission mechanism.

title: Requests without a device header bypass the configured limit
body: Authenticate relies entirely on TagDevice returning ErrDeviceLimitReached to enforce the cap, but TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. Consequently, even when the device limit is exhausted, an anonymous caller can omit this client-controlled header and continue accessing protected APIs without being counted or rejected. Define an enforcement path for requests without a device identifier, while allowing any necessary initial page bootstrap, rather than treating missing tracking information as successful admission.

title: Rejected devices remain cached as successfully admitted
body: tagDeviceUI inserts the device into localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and leaves it there when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Consequently, the first request from an over-limit device fails, but its next request hits the cache and returns nil, allowing Anonymous.Authenticate to admit it for the remainder of the 29-minute cache lifetime. Cache only successful admissions, and ensure concurrent requests cannot observe an admission before its store operation succeeds. Add a service-level test that retries a rejected device.

title: Omitting the device header bypasses the configured limit
body: Authentication now relies on TagDevice to enforce the limit, but TagDevice immediately returns nil when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. An anonymous client can therefore omit this client-controlled header and continue authenticating and accessing APIs even when the device limit is exhausted, without being counted. Enforcement needs a device-identification/admission path that cannot be skipped simply by dropping the header, while explicitly handling requests such as initial page loads that do not carry it.

title: Make the device-count check and admission atomic
body: CountDevices runs in a separate database session from the subsequent insert, with no locking or atomic admission mechanism. When the count is one below the limit, simultaneous requests from distinct devices can both observe available capacity and both insert successfully. This also occurs across Grafana replicas, and the excess devices remain admitted because subsequent requests are allowed to update existing devices. Serialize the count-and-admit operation across database clients or use an equivalent atomic quota mechanism, and test concurrent admissions at the boundary.

title: Rejected devices are cached as successfully admitted
body: TagDevice now propagates ErrDeviceLimitReached, but tagDeviceUI still populates localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the limit is reached, a new device's first request fails while its cache entry remains. Every subsequent request with that device ID returns nil from the cache check, so Anonymous.Authenticate grants access for the next 29 minutes despite the limit. Cache only successful admissions, and ensure concurrent requests cannot observe an admission before the store operation succeeds.

title: Make the capacity check and device admission atomic
body: CountDevices runs separately from the subsequent INSERT, with no transaction or locking that serializes admissions. If the count is one below the limit, two requests for different new device IDs can both observe available capacity and both insert successfully. This also occurs across Grafana replicas sharing a database. Those excess devices then remain eligible for updates even after the limit is reached. Serialize the count-and-admit operation across instances and add a concurrent-admission test.

title: Requests without a device header bypass the configured limit
body: Authentication now relies on TagDevice returning ErrDeviceLimitReached to enforce the limit, but TagDevice immediately returns nil when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. Consequently, even with a full device quota, an anonymous caller can omit this client-controlled header and continue accessing protected APIs without being counted or rejected. Enforce admission on anonymous API requests even when the header is missing, while explicitly handling any bootstrap requests that cannot yet supply a device ID.

title: Do not grant group management from the view scope
body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses this check to authorize both creating groups and moving existing subgroups to the top level. Consequently, an administrator granted only read-only access to all groups can perform these mutations. Require MANAGE here and add a negative test that attempts these operations with only VIEW.

title: Return group model IDs rather than authorization resource IDs
body: groupResource.getId() is the authorization resource's generated ID, not the GroupModel ID (which the schema stores as the resource name). Passing it to hasPermission() therefore misses the resource lookup by name, and adding it to the returned set supplies invalid group IDs to user search/count filtering. In particular, granting VIEW_MEMBERS on all groups causes the synthetic Groups resource's ID to be returned, so user searches are restricted to a nonexistent group and return no members. Evaluate actual group IDs, and handle the all-groups resource separately rather than returning its authorization ID.

title: Enable group-member creation for V2 permissions
body: The fallback for creating users in managed groups still requires the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature. With only V2 enabled, an administrator granted the new MANAGE_MEMBERS and MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP scopes on a group is rejected before either group permission is evaluated when POSTing a user assigned to that group. Extend this feature gate to V2 and test creation using group-scoped permissions without global user-management permission.

title: Require manage scope for global group mutations
body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE, so an administrator granted only view access to all groups passes requireManage(). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses that check to authorize both creating groups and moving existing subgroups to the top level. This gives a read-only administrator write access to the group hierarchy. Check only MANAGE here and add a negative test that an all-groups VIEW permission cannot create or move groups.

title: Resolve actual group IDs when building the user-search filter
body: groupResource.getId() is an authorization resource ID, not a GroupModel ID: the schema creates a separate authorization resource with the model ID as its name. Passing this ID to hasPermission() makes its findByName() lookup miss, and returning it makes UsersResource filter membership using nonexistent group IDs. In particular, an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS permission grants evaluation of the synthetic Groups resource, whose authorization ID is then used as the membership filter, causing user searches to return no members. Resolve concrete resources to model group IDs and expand the all-groups resource to actual groups instead of returning its ID. Cover both individual-group and all-groups member permissions in search/count tests.

title: Require manage scope for top-level group mutations
body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on all groups. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses requireManage() as its authorization check, so an administrator granted only read access to all groups can create groups and move existing subgroups to the top level by supplying their IDs. Check only MANAGE here and add a negative test ensuring an all-groups VIEW permission cannot authorize these writes.

title: Return actual group IDs rather than authorization resource IDs
body: groupResource.getId() identifies the authorization resource, not the GroupModel: AdminPermissionsSchema creates a separate resource whose name holds the group ID. Passing the resource ID to hasPermission() therefore misses the name lookup and falls back to the all-groups permission; adding that ID to the result also supplies an invalid group filter to user searches and counts. In particular, granting VIEW_MEMBERS on all groups causes the synthetic Groups resource's ID to be returned, so user searches are restricted to a nonexistent group and return no members. Resolve actual group IDs and handle the synthetic all-groups resource separately rather than treating it as a group.

title: Enable group-member creation for V2 permissions
body: The fallback for creating users in delegated groups still requires the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature. With only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, an administrator granted the new MANAGE_MEMBERS and MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP scopes on a group cannot create a user in that group: requireManage() fails without global user-management permission, and canCreateGroupMembers() returns false before evaluating either group scope. Allow this fallback for V2 as well and test user creation with group-only permissions.

title: Invalidate existing local recovery codes when replacing them in user storage
body: When updateCredential succeeds in external storage, this method leaves any existing locally stored recovery-code credential untouched. This occurs for users who configured recovery codes before their storage provider supported storing them externally. Regenerating their codes now saves a new external set without revoking the old local set, which can still be accepted by local credential validation when external validation fails. Remove the superseded local recovery credential after successfully storing the replacement externally, and test that codes from the previous local set no longer authenticate.

title: Exercise consumption of externally stored recovery codes
body: The new recovery-code validator only checks whether the submitted code occurs in the original list; it never consumes a successful code or updates its position. getCredentials also recreates a fresh credential from that unchanged list on every call. Consequently, this fixture permits unlimited reuse, always presents the first code, and never exercises the authenticator's exhausted-code handling. The new integration test logs in only once, so it passes despite these violations of the recovery-code lifecycle. Implement consumption in the fixture and test replay rejection, advancement to the next code, and regeneration after exhaustion.

title: Invalidate existing local recovery codes when replacing them in user storage
body: When the external storage accepts the new codes, this method leaves any existing locally stored recovery-code credential untouched. This affects users enrolled before this change, when recovery codes were always created locally. Credential validation can fall back to the local provider when external validation fails, so their old recovery codes remain usable after regeneration. Remove the previous local recovery-code credential when successfully replacing it externally, and test that codes from the previous set are rejected.

title: Exercise consumption and exhaustion of federated recovery codes
body: The new recovery-code validator only checks membership and never consumes the accepted code. In addition, getCredentials reconstructs a fresh credential from the entire original list each time. Consequently, this fixture allows unlimited reuse, always presents the first code, and never exercises the authenticator's exhausted-code handling. The new integration test stops after one login and therefore passes despite these broken lifecycle semantics. Make the fixture persist consumption state and extend the test to verify replay rejection, advancement to the next code, and regeneration after exhaustion.

title: Convert the legacy OTP model before exposing it as a federated credential
body: The new getCredentials implementation returns myUser.otp directly, but updateCredential stores that model with the input type (`totp` or `hotp`), not the credential-provider type `otp`. Previously this provider exposed OTP through getDisableableCredentialTypesStream, which reports `otp`. Returning the legacy model changes the advertised credential type and breaks consumers such as the existing account REST test, which looks for the credential under `OTPCredentialModel.TYPE`. Expose a correctly converted OTPCredentialModel while preserving the stored credential ID.

title: Exercise consumption of federated recovery codes, not just successful validation
body: The recovery-code validator accepts any generated code without consuming it, and getCredentials reconstructs a fresh model with every code unused on each call. Consequently, repeated logins can reuse the same code indefinitely, the form always requests the first code, and the authenticator's exhaustion/regeneration path is never exercised. The new integration test stops after one login, so it passes with this invalid recovery-code lifecycle. Persist consumption in the test provider and extend the test to check replay rejection, the next requested code, and regeneration after exhaustion.

title: Keep the registered metric alert handler instantiable
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement its abstract counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, or build_occurrence_and_event_data members. It remains registered as MetricAlertFire.detector_handler, so accessing detector.detector_handler for a metric_alert_fire detector now raises TypeError instead of returning the previous no-op handler. process_detectors does not catch this exception, so that detector also prevents subsequent detectors from being processed. Implement the required members or retain a concrete no-op handler until the stateful implementation is ready.

title: Build the expected occurrence for the group key being evaluated
body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds its expected occurrence using group key "val1", but calls evaluate_group_key_value with "group_key". The occurrence builder includes that key in the fingerprint, so the expected occurrence has fingerprint '<detector id>:val1' while the actual occurrence has '<detector id>:group_key'. This is an inconsistent expected result for the new hook and fails when occurrence equality compares fingerprints. Build the expected occurrence with "group_key" so the test validates the occurrence actually requested by the evaluation.

title: Keep the registered metric alert handler instantiable
body: Changing MetricAlertDetectorHandler to inherit from StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data makes it abstract. MetricAlertFire still registers this handler, so accessing detector.detector_handler for a metric_alert_fire detector now raises TypeError when the property instantiates it. Consequently, process_detectors aborts instead of returning the previous empty result, also preventing subsequent detectors from being processed. Implement the required methods or retain a concrete no-op handler until the stateful implementation is ready.

title: Keep the registered metric alert handler instantiable
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits abstract methods from StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of them: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data remain abstract. MetricAlertFire still registers this class as its handler, so accessing detector.detector_handler for a metric_alert_fire detector now raises TypeError instead of returning the previous no-op handler. This also aborts process_detectors before subsequent detectors can be processed. Keep the concrete no-op implementation until the stateful methods are implemented, or implement all required methods here.

title: Spawned workers fail the process type check and are never killed
body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, whose SpawnProcess class is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process. This isinstance check therefore returns false for production workers, skipping kill() before starting a replacement. A hung worker remains alive and can resume flushing the same shards concurrently with its replacement, causing duplicate production and leaking processes across restarts. The same check in join() also skips termination. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or the actual spawn-context process class instead.

title: Terminate remaining workers after the join deadline expires
body: When next_step.join() or an earlier worker consumes the shutdown timeout, this break skips every remaining worker, including their termination logic. Setting the shared stopped flag does not interrupt a worker blocked in Redis or future.result(), so those workers can survive a rebalance and later flush shards now owned by another consumer. Once the deadline expires, stop waiting but still terminate and reap all remaining workers.

title: Use the correct process type when killing unhealthy workers
body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances. These are not instances of multiprocessing.Process, so this check is false for production workers and process.kill() is never called. A worker declared hung therefore remains alive while its replacement starts flushing the same shards, potentially producing duplicates and updating the replacement's shared health/backpressure state. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess instead; the termination check in join() has the same problem.

title: Terminate remaining workers when the join deadline expires
body: When the shared deadline expires, this break skips cleanup for the current worker and every subsequent worker. For example, if the first worker consumes the timeout waiting for Kafka, none of the other workers receive termination, even after the process-type check is corrected. Setting stopped only stops workers once their current flush/produce call returns, so blocked workers can survive a rebalance after their strategy is discarded. Stop waiting when the deadline expires, but still terminate and reap every remaining process.

title: The process type check skips killing spawned workers
body: Workers are created using multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances. These inherit from BaseProcess, not multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check is false for production workers. When a worker is declared hung, it is therefore left running while a replacement is started for the same shards. This leaks workers and allows the old worker to resume flushing concurrently with its replacement. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or explicitly distinguish threads from processes before killing the worker.

title: Do not skip remaining workers when the join deadline expires
body: Once the shared deadline expires, this break bypasses cleanup for every remaining worker. This happens if next_step.join consumes the timeout or an earlier flusher uses the remaining time. Setting stopped does not interrupt a worker blocked on Redis or a Kafka future, so those workers can survive a rebalance and continue operating on shards assigned to new workers. Apply the deadline only to graceful waiting, and still terminate all surviving processes before returning.

title: Persist the parsed credentials rather than the safeParse result
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result, { success: true, data: ... }, whereas the previous parse call returned the credentials themselves. Saving this result as credential.key removes access_token and refresh_token from the top level. After any successful Google token refresh, including with syncing disabled, the next GoogleCalendarService construction will fail googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key). Persist the result's data instead.

title: The computed schema keys do not preserve token response fields
body: Calling toString() on a Zod schema produces an ordinary string key (typically '[object Object]'), not a wildcard property validator. Both computed keys collide, and z.object strips unrecognized properties by default. With syncing enabled, expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token and other real response fields are therefore discarded. Zoom subsequently computes an invalid expiry from undefined, and Office 365 loses its refreshed expiry. Define explicit expiry fields and preserve the required provider fields rather than using schema objects as property names.

title: Normalize sync responses for SDK and Axios callers
body: The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but several newly wrapped callers expect a different result shape: Google reads res.data, Zoho CRM and Bigin read tokenInfo.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken/expiresIn directly. A fetch Response exposes none of these properties, regardless of its JSON body. Consequently these integrations throw or use undefined tokens whenever syncing is enabled. Decode and adapt the sync response at each caller, or establish a consistent decoded return contract for the helper.

title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a dummy value
body: This fallback also runs when credential syncing is disabled. Office 365 explicitly permits refresh responses without refresh_token and merges the parsed response into the existing credentials. Previously that preserved the existing refresh token; now it overwrites it with the literal 'refresh_token'. The next refresh then fails and the user must reconnect. Leave omitted refresh tokens absent so callers can retain the existing value.

title: Import the Prisma client before using it
body: The new refresh path calls prisma.credential.update, but this file has no prisma import or declaration. This fails TypeScript checking and, if transpiled without checking, throws ReferenceError after a successful token response, preventing Salesforce client initialization.

title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
body: Unlike the other integrations, Salesforce unconditionally refreshes directly against login.salesforce.com and never uses CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. In the new source-of-truth setup, where the parent application owns refresh tokens and supplies access tokens, this request fails before a connection can be constructed. Even when a local refresh token exists, this bypasses the parent application's token management. Use the sync-aware refresh path and initialize the connection with the returned credentials.

title: Pass the user ID instead of the credential ID to token syncing
body: refreshOAuthTokens interprets its third argument as a user ID and sends it as calcomUserId. Bigin passes credentialId, which identifies a credential row rather than its owner. When the IDs differ, the parent application either cannot find the user or returns another user's Bigin token, potentially causing CRM writes to the wrong account. Carry credential.userId into this method and pass that instead; team credentials should retain the null-user fallback.

title: Send Zoom's app slug rather than its integration directory name
body: The sync request sends appSlug='zoomvideo', but Zoom credentials are created with appId='zoom' in the callback, and the incoming credential webhook resolves apps by their stored slug. A parent application keyed by the same app slug used to push credentials will not find 'zoomvideo', so Zoom refresh syncing fails. Pass 'zoom' here.

title: Persist parsed token data rather than the safeParse result
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns { success: true, data: tokens }, whereas the previous schema.parse returned the tokens themselves. Saving that wrapper as credential.key removes the top-level access_token and refresh_token expected by googleCredentialSchema. Even with credential sharing disabled, the first successful refresh corrupts the stored credential and subsequent Google Calendar service construction fails. Save the result's data property instead.

title: Computed schema keys do not preserve expiry or token fields
body: Calling toString() on a Zod schema produces a literal object-property name, not a wildcard. Both computed keys resolve to '[object Object]', and z.object strips undeclared properties. With sharing enabled, valid responses therefore lose expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token, and other provider fields. For example, Zoom computes its new expiry from an undefined expires_in and overwrites its refresh token with the placeholder. Define explicit fields and preserve required provider metadata instead.

title: Normalize the sync response for SDK and Axios callers
body: The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but several converted callers expect a different return shape: Google reads res.data, Zoho CRM and Bigin read tokenInfo.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken/expiresIn directly. A fetch Response has none of these properties, regardless of the JSON returned by the endpoint. Enabling syncing consequently breaks refreshes for these integrations. Parse the response and adapt it to each caller's contract, or change all callers to a consistent contract.

title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a dummy value
body: The helper injects the literal 'refresh_token' even when sharing is disabled. Office365's refresh response schema deliberately permits an omitted refresh_token, and its caller merges the parsed response into the existing credentials. Previously this preserved the existing refresh token; now a successful response without a replacement overwrites it with an unusable string, causing the next refresh to fail. Leave absent refresh tokens absent so callers can retain the existing value.

title: Import Prisma before using it in Salesforce refresh
body: The new code calls prisma.credential.update, but this file does not import or declare prisma. This fails TypeScript checking and, if executed without type checking, throws ReferenceError after every successful Salesforce token refresh, preventing the connection from being created.

title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
body: Unlike the other integrations, Salesforce now unconditionally refreshes directly against login.salesforce.com and never calls refreshOAuthTokens. In sharing mode the parent application is supposed to own refreshes and return access tokens; credentials without a locally usable refresh token will fail here even if the configured sync endpoint can supply a valid token. This also refreshes on every connection construction rather than using the existing valid access token.

title: Pass the user ID rather than the credential ID to syncing
body: The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is sent to the parent application as calcomUserId, but Bigin passes credentialId. Credential and user IDs are independent, so the endpoint will look up a nonexistent user or return another user's credentials when the numbers coincide. Thread credential.userId through refreshAccessToken and pass that instead; team credentials should retain the null user ID so they use the local refresh path.

title: Use Zoom's app slug in the sync request
body: The sync request sends appSlug='zoomvideo', but Zoom credentials are registered with appId='zoom' in the OAuth callback and the incoming webhook resolves apps by their database slug. A parent application using those same slugs cannot resolve this refresh request. Pass 'zoom' rather than the integration directory name.

title: Serialize credential creation for concurrent webhook deliveries
body: The findFirst followed by create is not atomic. Two simultaneous deliveries for a user/app with no credential can both observe no row and create separate credentials. Later deliveries update only one arbitrary matching row, leaving the other credential stale and available to integration consumers. Protect the lookup/create operation with appropriate database serialization or an idempotency mechanism so retries cannot create duplicate installations.

title: Computed schema keys discard the token expiry and refresh token
body: Calling toString() on a Zod schema produces a literal property name (normally "[object Object]"), not a wildcard key. Both computed keys collide, and z.object strips unrecognized properties by default. Consequently, a sync response containing access_token, expires_in and refresh_token loses the latter two fields. Zoom then calculates a NaN expiry, and Office 365 cannot retain the refreshed expiry. Define explicit response fields and appropriate passthrough/normalization instead.

title: Persist the parsed credentials rather than the safeParse result
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a safeParse envelope shaped as { success: true, data: ... }, whereas the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse call returned the credentials themselves. Saving this envelope as credential.key removes access_token and the other credential fields from the top level. This affects ordinary Google refreshes even with syncing disabled; subsequent service construction cannot parse the saved credential. Persist the result's data field.

title: Normalize sync responses for SDK and Axios callers
body: The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but several callers expect the return type of their original refresh function. Google Calendar, Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read response.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly. A fetch Response has none of these properties, regardless of the JSON returned by the endpoint, so enabling syncing breaks their refresh paths. Parse and adapt the sync response to a consistent contract and update these callers.

title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a placeholder
body: The helper unconditionally injects the literal "refresh_token" when a response omits a refresh token, including when credential sharing is disabled. Office 365 explicitly allows the provider to omit refresh_token and merges the parsed response into the existing credentials. This change overwrites the existing usable refresh token with the placeholder, causing the next refresh to fail. Preserve the existing token when no replacement is returned.

title: Import Prisma before using it in Salesforce initialization
body: The new initialization path calls prisma.credential.update, but this file does not import or declare prisma. This causes a TypeScript error and, if transpiled without type checking, a ReferenceError after a successful token refresh, preventing Salesforce client initialization.

title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
body: The added Salesforce refresh always posts directly to Salesforce using credentialKey.refresh_token; it never uses refreshOAuthTokens or checks whether credential sharing is enabled. Synced credentials whose refresh tokens are managed exclusively by the parent application therefore cannot initialize the Salesforce integration. Use the configured refresh source, and initialize the jsforce connection with the newly returned access token rather than the old credentialKey.access_token.

title: Pass the credential owner's user ID to the sync request
body: The third argument of refreshOAuthTokens is a Cal.com user ID and is sent as calcomUserId, but this call passes the credential row ID. These IDs are unrelated, so the parent application will look up the wrong user or fail to find one. Once response handling is corrected, this can also save another user's token onto this credential. Carry credential.userId into refreshAccessToken and pass it here.

title: Send Zoom's app slug rather than its integration directory name
body: This call sends appSlug="zoomvideo" to the parent endpoint, while Zoom credentials and the app store use appId/slug="zoom" (as shown in the Zoom callback). A parent application mapping refresh requests by the same appSlug used for credential synchronization cannot resolve this request. Pass "zoom" here.

title: Clear credential invalidation when replacing credentials
body: Updating an existing credential only replaces key and leaves invalid unchanged. Google and Zoom, among others, mark credentials invalid after an unrecoverable authentication failure. If the parent application reconnects the account and sends fresh credentials through this webhook, the endpoint reports success but the credential remains invalid and unavailable for normal use. Reset invalid when accepting a valid replacement credential.

title: Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache
body: The cache-deletion success handler only calls the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates connectedCalendars. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper passes an optional external onChanged callback rather than refetching its query, and disables refetchOnWindowFocus. Consequently, when no refetching callback is provided, successful deletion leaves the old cache timestamp and Delete cached data action visible. Invalidate the connectedCalendars query on success, as the disconnect mutation already does.

title: Set updatedAt explicitly instead of issuing an empty update
body: Calling updateManyByCredentialId with an empty data object does not advance Prisma's @updatedAt field: Prisma leaves that timestamp unchanged for empty updates. Thus this new call does not record successful cache refreshes in SelectedCalendar.updatedAt as intended. Pass an explicit updatedAt timestamp, or remove this call if CalendarCache.updatedAt is the only refresh timestamp needed.

title: Invalidate connected calendars after deleting cached data
body: The delete-cache success handler only invokes the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper passes through an optional onChanged callback and does not refetch this query itself, so deleting the cache can leave the old timestamp and delete action visible after a success toast. Window-focus refetching is also explicitly disabled in that wrapper. Invalidate utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does, so the displayed status reflects the deletion without a page reload.

title: Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache
body: The delete-cache success handler only invokes the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper passes its optional onChanged prop through without refetching that query and disables refetchOnWindowFocus. When no refetching callback is supplied, a successful deletion therefore leaves the old cache timestamp and Delete cached data action visible. Invalidate connectedCalendars on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

title: Use a portable in-place edit for the webhook environment variable
body: The `sed -i '' -E` invocation uses BSD/macOS syntax and fails with GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, the script does not update it but still prints the success message, leaving Google webhook testing pointed at the previous tunnel. Use a portable replacement approach and check that the edit succeeds before reporting success.

title: Fix the invalid Ruby closing the header conditional
body: `<%- end if %>` is not a valid closing statement for this conditional: the trailing `if` has no condition. Rendering the best template therefore raises a template syntax error, so every embed with an existing topic fails instead of displaying comments. Use `end` and add a controller test that actually renders this view; the current mocked controller tests do not exercise the template.

title: Sanitize imported HTML before storing it as cooked content
body: Feed content reaches this method directly from PollFeed and is stored with the raw_html cook method, which returns the input without sanitization. `absolutize_urls` only parses and rewrites links; it does not remove scripts, event handlers, or unsafe URL schemes. Consequently, active HTML in a feed entry executes in the forum origin when the imported post is viewed. Sanitize the final HTML on both creation and revision, including the imported-from link, whose URL is also interpolated without HTML escaping.

title: Handle RSS entries that expose description instead of content
body: The poller unconditionally calls `i.content.scrub`, but valid RSS entries commonly contain only `description` (or `content:encoded`) rather than Atom's `content` field. For such an entry, `i.content` is nil and the job raises instead of importing it or processing subsequent entries. Select the available body field and handle entries without a body; add tests using actual RSS and Atom payloads rather than only testing delegation to poll_feed.

title: Resolve relative URLs against the article URI
body: The URL rewriting treats all references beginning with `/` as paths on the article host. A protocol-relative image such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` is therefore changed to `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. Conversely, path-relative references such as `images/photo.jpg` and `../other-article` are left unchanged and resolve against the forum URL when displayed. This breaks images and links in imported articles. Resolve both href and src with URI reference resolution against the complete source URL instead of concatenating the host.

title: Fix the invalid Ruby closing the header conditional
body: `<%- end if %>` produces invalid Ruby: the trailing `if` has no condition. Every request that finds an existing embedded topic will fail when Rails compiles this template instead of displaying the discussion. Use `<%- end %>` and add a controller test with view rendering enabled; the current mocked controller tests do not exercise template compilation.

title: Sanitize imported HTML before storing it as cooked content
body: Feed content reaches this method directly from PollFeed and is saved with the new `raw_html` cook method, which returns the input without sanitization. `absolutize_urls` only parses and rewrites links; it does not remove scripts, event handlers, or unsafe URL schemes. Consequently, active HTML in a feed (including escaped markup decoded by PollFeed) becomes stored XSS executed on the forum origin when the post is rendered. Sanitize the final imported HTML, including the interpolated source link, before bypassing the normal cooking pipeline.

title: Support feed entries without a content element
body: The poller unconditionally calls `scrub` on `i.content`, but ordinary RSS entries can provide their body only in `description` (or `content:encoded`), and Atom entries can contain only a summary. For these valid feeds, `i.content` is nil and polling raises rather than importing the entry; all subsequent entries are also skipped. Select the available body field and handle missing bodies explicitly, with tests that parse actual RSS and Atom fixtures.

title: Resolve relative references using the article URL
body: The URL conversion treats all leading-slash references as local paths, so `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` becomes `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. It also leaves path-relative references such as `images/photo.jpg` and `../other-article` unchanged, causing them to resolve against the forum rather than the imported article. The same problem affects the image loop below. Use URI resolution against the full source URL so imported links and images retain their intended destinations.

title: Invalid Ruby prevents the discussion template from rendering
body: The template closes its conditional with `end if` rather than `end`. The trailing `if` has no condition, so ERB generates invalid Ruby and rendering raises a syntax error. Every embed request that finds an existing topic fails instead of displaying the discussion. Replace this with `end` and add a controller test that renders the actual view.

title: Imported feed HTML is published without sanitization
body: Feed contents are passed through `absolutize_urls`, which only parses and rewrites links, and then saved using `raw_html`. `Post#cook` returns that HTML unchanged, so scripts, event-handler attributes, and dangerous links in feed content survive into rendered forum posts. The feed polling path does not use the Readability allowlist used by remote article imports. Sanitize imported HTML before storing/rendering it, including on updates, rather than treating external feed content as trusted forum-origin HTML.

title: Feed polling fails on entries without a content element
body: The poller unconditionally calls `scrub` on `i.content`. Valid RSS feeds commonly supply their body in `description` or `content:encoded`, and Atom entries may supply only a summary; these entries need not have `content`. A missing value causes an exception and aborts the entire poll, including subsequent entries. Select the supported body fields with fallbacks and explicitly handle entries with no body. The current tests only check delegation and never parse a feed.

title: URL rewriting corrupts protocol-relative links and misses relative paths
body: The URL conversion treats every href beginning with `/` as a path on the article host. For example, `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` becomes `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`; the image loop has the same problem. Conversely, document-relative references such as `images/photo.jpg` or `../other-post` remain unchanged and resolve against the forum instead of the source article. Resolve references against the complete source URL using URI joining so imported links and images continue to work.

title: Do not cache devices before admission succeeds
body: TagDevice now propagates the limit error to authentication, but tagDeviceUI still populates the local cache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When a new device is rejected because the limit is reached, its cache entry remains. Retrying with the same device ID returns nil from the cache and successfully authenticates for the next 29 minutes, despite the device never being admitted. Cache only successful admissions and add a test that repeats a rejected request.

title: Make the limit check and device admission atomic
body: CountDevices and the subsequent upsert run in separate database sessions without serialization. If two new devices arrive when one slot remains, both can observe a count below the limit and both are inserted and authenticated. This also occurs across Grafana replicas, and the excess devices continue to be accepted by the update-only path. Serialize the count and admission at the database level so concurrent requests cannot exceed the configured limit.

title: Handle requests without a device ID when enforcing the limit
body: Authentication relies exclusively on TagDevice returning ErrDeviceLimitReached, but TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is missing. An anonymous client can therefore omit this client-controlled header and continue accessing Grafana without being counted or checked, even when the configured device limit is full. Define and enforce admission for requests without a device ID rather than treating skipped tracking as successful admission.

title: Rejected devices are cached as successfully admitted
body: Propagating the store error does not make limit enforcement persistent: tagDeviceUI adds the device to localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice, and leaves that entry in place when ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned. The first request from an over-limit device is rejected, but a retry with the same device ID hits the cache, returns nil, and successfully authenticates for the next 29 minutes. Cache devices only after successful admission, and add a test that repeats a rejected request.

title: Make the device count check and admission atomic
body: CountDevices runs in a separate database session from the subsequent insert, with no locking or transaction that serializes admissions. When one slot remains, concurrent requests with different device IDs can all observe a count below deviceLimit and all insert successfully. Those devices then remain eligible for updates even though the configured limit has been exceeded. Serialize the count-and-insert operation across instances using database-level coordination, and test concurrent admissions at the limit.

title: Do not cache devices whose admission was rejected
body: Propagating the store error does not make the device limit effective because tagDeviceUI inserts the device into localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When a new device is rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached, its cache entry remains for 29 minutes. The next request with the same device ID hits that entry, returns nil, and successfully authenticates anonymously despite the limit. Only cache successful admissions, and add a test that repeats a rejected request.

title: Make the device-count check and admission atomic
body: CountDevices runs in a separate database session from the subsequent insert, with no locking or other serialization. If two new devices arrive when one slot remains, both can observe a count below deviceLimit and both insert successfully. This also occurs across Grafana instances sharing the database. Once inserted, both devices qualify for updates even while over the limit. Enforce the count check and admission atomically using database-level concurrency control, and cover concurrent admissions in tests.

title: Require manage scope for global group management
body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE, so an administrator granted only view permission on all groups passes requireManage(). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup uses that check to authorize both creating groups and moving an existing subgroup to the top level. This gives a read-only administrator write access to the group hierarchy. Only MANAGE should satisfy this check; add a test that a VIEW-only grant cannot POST groups.

title: Return model group IDs rather than authorization resource IDs
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() enumerates authorization resources and passes/returns groupResource.getId(), but these IDs are not GroupModel IDs: AdminPermissionsSchema creates a resource with a generated ID and stores the model group ID in its name. hasPermission() subsequently looks up by name, and UsersResource uses the returned set to filter users by group membership. In particular, with an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS grant this enumerates the synthetic Groups resource and returns its authorization ID, causing user searches to filter on a nonexistent group and return no members. Individual resources also are not assigned a Groups type by getOrCreateResource(), so this enumeration does not discover them. Resolve actual group IDs, handle the all-groups grant explicitly, and test user search/count with both individual and all-groups member permissions.

title: Do not accept view scope for group management
body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE, so an administrator granted only view permission on all groups passes requireManage(). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses that check to authorize both creating groups and moving existing subgroups to the top level. This gives a read-only administrator write access to the group hierarchy. Require only MANAGE here and add a negative test for group creation with only VIEW.

title: Return model group IDs rather than authorization resource IDs
body: This enumeration confuses authorization resources with group models. AdminPermissionsSchema creates individual resources with the group ID as their name, not their resource ID, and does not set their type to Groups. Consequently findByType does not enumerate those individual groups. For an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS grant, it instead finds the synthetic Groups resource and adds its authorization resource ID to the result. UsersResource uses this set as the group-membership filter for user searches and counts, so the all-groups grant produces a filter matching no actual group and hides all members. Individual group grants also fail to supply the IDs needed for counts and pre-pagination filtering. Resolve actual group IDs, evaluate individual resources using their names, and handle the synthetic all-groups resource explicitly; cover both individual and all-groups member searches and counts in tests.

title: Do not accept view scope for group management
body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE, so an administrator granted only view permission on all groups passes requireManage(). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses this check to authorize both creating groups and moving existing groups to the top level. A read-only administrator can therefore mutate the group hierarchy. Require MANAGE here and add a test that an all-groups VIEW grant cannot POST groups.

title: Resolve actual group IDs when constructing the user-search filter
body: This enumeration treats authorization resource IDs as GroupModel IDs, but AdminPermissionsSchema creates resources with generated IDs and stores the group ID in the resource name. hasPermission() then looks up that generated ID by name, and the returned set also contains generated IDs rather than group IDs. In particular, an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS grant matches the synthetic Groups resource and returns its authorization ID; UsersResource installs that nonempty set as UserModel.GROUPS, filtering out every actual member. Individual resources created by getOrCreateResource() also have no Groups type set, so this type query does not enumerate them. Resolve real groups (including the all-groups case), evaluate using their IDs, and return actual group IDs; cover both user search and count with group-member grants.

title: Exercise single-use recovery codes in the federated-storage test
body: The new recovery-code validator returns true for any matching code without consuming it or persisting updated state. Its getCredentials() method also reconstructs a fresh, unused recovery-code model on every call. Consequently, the test provider accepts the same code indefinitely, always requests code 0, and never exercises the authenticator's exhaustion/re-enrollment path. The new integration test stops after one login, so it passes despite this broken recovery-code lifecycle. Make the provider track consumed codes and extend the test to verify replay rejection, advancement to the next code, and re-enrollment after exhaustion.

title: Consume recovery codes in the federated test provider and test their lifecycle
body: The new recovery-code validator only checks whether the submitted code is in the original list; it never consumes it. Moreover, getCredentials() recreates a fresh recovery credential from that unchanged list on every call. Consequently the same code remains valid indefinitely, the login form always requests the first code, and the authenticator's allCodesUsed() path is never exercised. The added integration test performs only one login, so it passes despite this broken one-time-code lifecycle. Make the fixture persist consumption state and extend the test to verify replay rejection, progression to the next code, and regeneration after exhaustion.

title: Consume recovery codes in the federated test provider and test their lifecycle
body: The new recovery-code validator only checks whether the submitted value is in the original list; it never removes or marks a code as used. Moreover, getCredentials() rebuilds a fresh model from that same list on every call. Consequently the same recovery code can authenticate indefinitely, the form always requests the first code, and the authenticator's exhausted-code/regeneration path is never exercised. The added integration test stops after one successful login, so it passes with this broken lifecycle. Update the test provider to persist consumption and extend the test to verify replay rejection, advancement to the next code, and regeneration after exhaustion.

title: Keep the registered metric alert handler instantiable

title: Spawned flushers never pass the new kill guard
body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances. These are not instances of multiprocessing.Process (the default-context Process class), so this guard is false for production workers. When a worker is declared hung, it is no longer killed before its replacement starts, and its handle is overwritten. If the old worker resumes, both workers can flush the same shards concurrently and produce duplicate segments; repeated hangs also leak workers. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or the explicit SpawnProcess type and kill/reap the old worker before replacing it.

title: Clean up every worker even after the join deadline expires
body: When the join deadline expires, this break skips all remaining workers without terminating them. This occurs if next_step.join consumes the timeout or an earlier flusher takes the remaining time. Setting stopped only requests cooperative shutdown, so workers blocked in Redis or Kafka can remain alive across a rebalance while a new strategy starts replacement flushers. The timeout should limit waiting, not cleanup: terminate and reap all remaining workers when the deadline is exhausted, using a type check that recognizes SpawnProcess.

title: Spawned workers do not pass the multiprocessing.Process type check
body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, whose SpawnProcess class is not a subclass of the top-level multiprocessing.Process class; both inherit from BaseProcess. Consequently this check is false for production workers and a hung worker is never killed before its replacement starts. If the original worker resumes, both workers can flush the same shards and update the same health/backpressure state, potentially producing duplicate segments. The identical check in join() also skips termination. Use BaseProcess or the actual spawn-context process class to distinguish processes from test threads.

title: Terminate remaining workers when the join deadline expires
body: Once the join deadline expires, this break skips cleanup of every remaining worker. This happens if next_step.join() consumes the timeout or an earlier flusher takes the remaining time. Setting stopped only requests cooperative shutdown: workers blocked in Redis or Kafka calls can remain alive after join returns and retain ownership of shards that are reassigned during a rebalance. Even after correcting the process type checks, all remaining processes need termination when the shared deadline is exhausted, rather than exiting the cleanup loop.

title: Spawned workers do not pass the multiprocessing.Process check
body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances. SpawnProcess and multiprocessing.Process are separate subclasses of BaseProcess, so this isinstance check is false for production workers. Consequently a hung worker is never killed before its replacement starts, leaving both workers able to flush the same shards and update the same health/backpressure values if the original recovers. The same check at line 346 also prevents shutdown termination. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess (or the explicit SpawnProcess type) instead.

title: Terminate remaining workers after the join deadline expires
body: When the shared join deadline expires, this break skips cleanup for every remaining worker. If next_step.join consumes the timeout, no workers are handled at all; if the first worker hangs until the deadline, subsequent workers are skipped. Setting stopped only requests cooperative shutdown and cannot stop a worker blocked in Redis or future.result(). Even after correcting the process type check, these workers can remain alive after a rebalance and later resume flushing shards assigned to another consumer. Apply forced termination to all remaining live workers when the deadline is exhausted rather than breaking out of cleanup.

title: Import Prisma before using it in the Salesforce refresh path
body: The new code calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this module neither imports nor declares `prisma`. This fails TypeScript checking and, if checking is bypassed, throws a ReferenceError after a successful token refresh, preventing Salesforce operations even when credential sharing is disabled.

title: Persist the parsed Google credentials, not the safeParse result
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `{ success: true, data: ... }` wrapper, whereas the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credentials themselves. Saving that wrapper as `credential.key` removes the token fields from the root of the stored credentials. This happens even with sharing disabled, so the next service initialization cannot load the Google credentials correctly. Persist the result's `data` instead.

title: Use real schema fields instead of stringifying Zod schemas
body: Both computed property names evaluate to the literal string `[object Object]`; they do not define arbitrary numeric or optional properties. Since Zod objects strip unknown fields by default, a normal sync response loses its expiry, refresh token, and other metadata. For example, Zoom then calculates its new expiry from an undefined `expires_in`, producing NaN. Define and preserve the actual response fields, including the expiry information consumed by each adapter.

title: Adapt fetch responses for callers that expect SDK or Axios results
body: The sync branch returns a raw fetch `Response`, but Google, Zoho CRM, and Bigin read `.data` from the result, while HubSpot treats the result itself as a parsed token object. A fetch Response has none of those token properties, regardless of the JSON returned by the endpoint. Consequently, successful sync requests throw on undefined fields or fail to install the returned tokens. Decode and adapt the response at these callers, with an explicit return contract rather than `any`.

title: Do not replace an existing refresh token with a placeholder
body: This fallback runs for native provider responses as well as shared credentials. Office 365 explicitly permits a refresh response without a new `refresh_token`; its caller previously retained the existing token when merging the response. The helper now inserts the literal `refresh_token`, which overwrites that valid token in the database and causes the next refresh to fail. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not rotate it.

title: Pass the credential owner's user ID to Bigin credential sync
body: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a user ID, but this call supplies the credential row's ID. The helper sends that value as `calcomUserId`, so whenever these independent IDs differ it requests a nonexistent or different user's integration. It also incorrectly routes team credentials through user sync because their credential IDs are non-null. Pass `credential.userId` separately from the ID used for database updates.

title: Authenticate outbound credential-refresh requests
body: The token-retrieval request sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no shared-secret header, signature, or other authentication. An externally reachable parent endpoint cannot distinguish this request from an arbitrary caller supplying the same identifiers: it must either reject these calls or risk exposing users' third-party access tokens. Add an explicit server-to-server authentication mechanism to the refresh protocol.

title: Send Zoom's app slug rather than its directory name
body: This sends `appSlug=zoomvideo` to the parent store, but Zoom is installed with `appId: "zoom"` and the credential webhook identifies apps by their database slug. A parent store keyed by that same slug cannot match the refresh request to the synced Zoom credential. Use `zoom`, consistently with installation and webhook requests.

title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
body: Unlike the other modified integrations, Salesforce always posts directly to the provider and never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`. Enabling credential sharing therefore has no effect on where Salesforce obtains tokens. Credentials whose refresh tokens are managed only by the parent store fail this request instead of using the configured sync endpoint, defeating the new feature for Salesforce.

title: Accept the minimal sync response in the Webex adapter
body: The new sync helper documents a response containing only the access token and expiry, but Webex still validates that response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token lifetime. A successful response following the sync contract is therefore rejected as invalid when the access token expires. Add sync-specific decoding and retain the existing provider metadata rather than requiring native refresh-response fields.

title: Decode shared Lark tokens without requiring a native response envelope
body: The sync response is passed directly to `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>` and then read through `data.data`, including refresh-token lifetime fields. The helper's documented access-token-and-expiry response has neither Lark's `code`/`data` envelope nor that refresh-token metadata, so a valid shared-token response cannot refresh this integration. Handle the sync response separately from Lark's native refresh response.

title: Clear the invalid flag when replacing repaired credentials
body: Google, Zoom, and Webex can mark a credential `invalid: true` after an unrecoverable authentication failure. If the user reconnects in the parent application and sends fresh keys through this webhook, the update changes only `key`, leaving the same row marked invalid. The webhook reports success without restoring the connection. Clear the invalid flag when accepting valid replacement credentials.

title: Make initial credential synchronization idempotent under concurrency
body: The lookup and creation are separate operations with no serialization or stable upsert key. Two simultaneous deliveries for a user/app with no existing credential can both observe no row and both create one. Subsequent webhook updates modify only the first matching row, leaving the duplicate with stale tokens. Serialize creation for the logical credential or introduce an idempotent identity that can be atomically upserted.

title: Import Prisma before updating Salesforce credentials
body: The new credential update references `prisma`, but this file never imports or declares it. Type-checking fails with `Cannot find name 'prisma'`; if type-checking is bypassed, a successful token refresh throws a ReferenceError before returning the Salesforce connection. Import the shared Prisma client.

title: Persist the parsed Google credentials, not the safeParse result
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{ success: true, data: credentials }`, whereas the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credentials themselves. Passing this result directly to `prisma.credential.update` nests all token fields under `key.data`. This also happens with syncing disabled: after an ordinary refresh, subsequent calendar operations no longer find the expected root-level OAuth fields. Persist the result's `data` instead.

title: Define actual expiry fields instead of computed Zod object keys
body: Calling `toString()` on these Zod schemas produces the literal key `[object Object]`, not a wildcard property definition; the second computed property also overwrites the first. Because Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, a synced response containing `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, and `refresh_token` loses those fields. Zoom then computes a NaN expiry, and Office365 cannot update its expiry correctly. Define and preserve the actual supported response fields.

title: Normalize external refresh responses for the SDK-based callers
body: The sync branch returns a native fetch `Response`, but Google Calendar and both Zoho services still read `.data`, while HubSpot expects a decoded token object with `accessToken` and `expiresIn`. None of those callers reads the response body. Even a successful JSON response therefore produces undefined token fields or throws before the credentials can be refreshed. Establish a consistent return contract and adapt these callers to decode the external response.

title: Pass the credential owner's user ID to the sync endpoint
body: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a user ID, but this call passes the credential row's primary key. The helper sends that value as `calcomUserId`, so a credential whose ID differs from its owner's ID requests another user's tokens or fails lookup. Any returned tokens are then saved to the current credential and used for its CRM operations. Carry the actual nullable `credential.userId` into this method.

title: Do not replace an existing native refresh token with a placeholder
body: The placeholder assignment also runs when credential syncing is disabled. Office365's response schema explicitly allows a refresh response without a replacement `refresh_token`, and its caller merges the parsed response into the existing credentials. Such a response now overwrites the valid stored refresh token with the literal `refresh_token`, making the next refresh fail. Leave an omitted native refresh token unset so the caller can preserve the existing value.

title: Authenticate outbound credential-sync requests
body: This token-retrieval POST contains only a user ID and app slug; it attaches no secret, signature, or other authentication. A public sync endpoint accepting this protocol cannot distinguish Cal from another caller requesting the same user's bearer token, while an endpoint requiring the configured shared secret will reject these calls. Add authenticated server-to-server requests, for example using the configured secret header, rather than relying on enumerable identifiers.

title: Send Zoom's canonical app slug
body: The refresh request sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are installed with `appId: "zoom"`, and the webhook identifies apps by that canonical slug. A parent store looking up the synced Zoom integration by the supplied slug will not find it. Pass `zoom` rather than the integration directory/API route name.

title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
body: The new Salesforce refresh always posts directly to Salesforce and never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`. Consequently, enabling sharing and setting `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` has no effect on Salesforce token retrieval: Cal still requires a locally usable refresh token and refreshes independently of the parent store. Externally managed credentials whose refresh token is retained by the parent cannot work through this path.

title: Handle the access-token-only sync response in Webex
body: After routing Webex refreshes to the external endpoint, the response is still validated with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token expiry. An endpoint following the helper's documented access-token/expiry-only response therefore always fails with `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned`. Add a sync-specific parsing and merge path that does not require the parent to disclose its refresh token.

title: Do not delete externally managed Lark credentials based on local refresh tokens
body: Before reaching the new sync request, `refreshAccessToken` still deletes the credential if its local refresh token is absent or expired. With external credential management, the parent can hold a valid rotated refresh token even when Cal's local copy is missing or stale. Cal then deletes a recoverable integration without consulting the source of truth. Keep the local refresh-token validation and deletion inside the native-provider fallback.

title: Clear the invalid flag when replacing invalidated credentials
body: The existing-credential branch updates only `key`. Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credentials `invalid: true` after unrecoverable authentication failures, so pushing fresh valid credentials through this webhook leaves the integration marked invalid despite returning success. Reset the invalid state when accepting a valid replacement so the parent store can reconnect an invalidated integration.

title: Make initial webhook delivery idempotent under concurrency
body: The lookup and creation are separate operations. Two simultaneous deliveries for the same user and app can both find no credential and then create separate rows. Later deliveries update only one row through `findFirst`, leaving duplicate integrations with stale credentials. Serialize creation for the same sync identity or introduce a database-enforced idempotency mechanism rather than relying on this check-then-create sequence.

title: Persist the parsed Google tokens, not the safeParse result
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a wrapper shaped like { success: true, data: tokens }, unlike the removed googleCredentialSchema.parse call. Saving that wrapper directly as credential.key moves all token fields under data.
