After any successful refresh, even with credential sharing disabled, the next service instance cannot parse the saved key with googleCredentialSchema. Persist the successful result's data instead.

title: Import the Prisma client used by Salesforce refresh
body: The new prisma.credential.update call references prisma without importing or defining it in this module. This fails type checking and, if type checking is bypassed, throws before the Salesforce connection can be created. Import the shared Prisma client before using it.

title: Replace the computed schema keys with actual token fields
body: Calling toString() on these Zod schemas produces the literal property name '[object Object]'; it does not declare arbitrary response properties. Both computed keys collide, and Zod strips ordinary fields such as expires_in, expiry_date, and refresh_token as unknown keys. With sharing enabled, a normal token response therefore loses its expiry and refresh token. Zoom subsequently calculates a NaN expiry, while Office365 retains its old expired timestamp. Define and normalize the supported expiry fields explicitly and preserve the required token properties.

title: Make delegated refresh responses compatible with their callers
body: The delegated branch returns an unread Fetch Response, while several callers expect the SDK or Axios result returned by refreshFunction. Google Calendar, Zoho CRM, and Bigin read response.data; HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly. None of those callers decodes the delegated response body, so enabling syncing makes valid refresh replies fail or yield undefined tokens. Normalize the response contract and adapt these callers instead of returning incompatible result types behind any.

title: Preserve existing refresh tokens when no replacement is returned
body: The literal 'refresh_token' fallback also runs when credential sharing is disabled. Office365 explicitly permits a successful token response without a replacement refresh_token and merges the parsed response into the existing credentials. This fallback overwrites the usable stored refresh token with that literal string, causing the next native refresh to fail and requiring reconnection. Leave an omitted refresh token absent so the existing value can be retained.

title: Pass the credential owner's user ID to Bigin token sync
body: The third refreshOAuthTokens argument is a user ID and is sent to the parent application as calcomUserId, but this call supplies the credential table's primary key. These IDs are unrelated, so the parent either cannot find the user or returns tokens belonging to another user whose ID happens to match. It also incorrectly delegates team-owned credentials because their credential ID is non-null. Carry credential.userId separately from the ID used for database updates.

title: Send Zoom's canonical app slug to the sync endpoint
body: The Zoom app is stored and installed with appId/slug 'zoom', as shown in its OAuth callback, but this request sends appSlug='zoomvideo'. The webhook also identifies apps by their canonical database slug. A parent application keyed by the same slug used to sync the credential will therefore fail to find Zoom tokens when they expire. Send 'zoom' rather than the integration directory name.

title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
body: This new refresh request always goes directly to Salesforce and never calls refreshOAuthTokens, so CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is ignored for this integration. When the parent application owns or rotates the refresh token, the local refresh token can be absent or stale; this mandatory request then prevents connection creation even if a valid access token was synced. Use the delegated refresh path when enabled and initialize the connection with its returned tokens.

title: Handle minimal sync responses separately from native provider responses
body: refreshOAuthTokens documents that the sync endpoint returns only an access token and expiry, but the delegated Webex response still goes through webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires scope, token_type, refresh_token, and refresh_token_expires_in. A valid minimal sync response is therefore rejected at the first refresh. Lark's delegated path similarly still expects its native code/data envelope and refresh-token fields. Add sync-specific parsing and preserve existing credential metadata rather than requiring the parent to return the native refresh-token response.

title: Identify the connected account before replacing its credentials
body: A user can have multiple credentials for the same app, including multiple Google Calendar accounts, but the webhook identifies a connection only by userId and appSlug and overwrites findFirst's result. A sync intended for the second account can replace the first account's tokens while leaving calendar selections and booking references attached to that first credential ID. Accept a stable connection/account identifier, or reject ambiguous matches rather than silently choosing one.

title: Make initial credential synchronization idempotent under concurrency
body: The existence lookup and credential creation are separate operations. Two overlapping deliveries for a previously unsynced connection can both observe no credential and create separate rows. Subsequent deliveries update only one row through findFirst, leaving the duplicate with stale tokens. Use an atomic or serialized operation keyed by the synced connection so concurrent webhook deliveries cannot create duplicates.

title: Clear credential invalidation when fresh credentials are synced
body: Google, Zoom, and Webex can mark a credential invalid after an unrecoverable grant error. If the user reconnects in the parent application, this webhook finds that existing row but updates only its key, leaving invalid=true despite the replacement tokens. The credential remains marked disconnected and unavailable to consumers that exclude invalid credentials. Reset the invalid flag when accepting validated replacement credentials.

title: Refresh cache status after successful deletion
body: The delete-cache success handler only invokes an optional callback; it never invalidates or updates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The wrapper passes its optional onChanged callback directly through and disables refetchOnWindowFocus. Without a callback that explicitly refetches, deleting the cache therefore leaves the old timestamp and delete action visible after the success toast. Invalidate the connected-calendars query on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

title: Resolve backing cache records for delegated connections
body: When a connected calendar uses an in-memory delegation credential, its negative credential ID cannot match CalendarCache rows stored against database credentials. The existing getCachedAvailability implementation explicitly handles this case using userId and the cache key, but this status lookup only uses the displayed credential ID. Consequently, a delegated connection can serve cached availability while reporting cacheUpdatedAt as null. Because the duplicate non-delegated connection is filtered out and delegated connections cannot disconnect, the dropdown then disappears entirely, preventing these users from viewing or clearing their cache. Resolve the backing cache records for delegated connections and use that same authorized scope for deletion.

title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script
body: ENV_FILE is relative to the caller's working directory, not the script's location. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root writes GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL to ../.env outside the repository, potentially creating that file, while leaving the application's configuration unchanged. Derive the repository environment-file path from BASH_SOURCE so the normal root-level invocation updates the intended file.

title: Use an environment-file replacement compatible with GNU sed
body: The sed -i '' syntax is BSD-specific. On Linux with GNU sed, the empty argument is treated as the sed program and the replacement expression as a filename, so an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is not updated. The script nevertheless prints its success message, leaving webhook registration pointed at the previous tunnel. Use a portable replacement or select the appropriate in-place syntax for the installed sed.

title: Invalidate cache status after deleting cached data
body: The delete-cache mutation only invokes the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates connectedCalendars. The wrapper forwards an optional onChanged callback and disables refetchOnWindowFocus, so deleting the cache can leave the old timestamp and delete action displayed after the success toast. Invalidate viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars after deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does, so the displayed status reflects the database.

title: Resolve persisted cache records for delegated calendar connections
body: Connected calendars can use in-memory delegation credentials with negative IDs, while CalendarCache rows belong to persisted credentials. getCachedAvailability explicitly supports this by looking up delegated availability using userId and key, including reusing an existing OAuth connection's cache after delegation is enabled. This new credential-ID-only lookup cannot find those same rows, so cacheUpdatedAt becomes null and the dropdown hides both status and deletion for the delegated connection even while its cached availability is being served. Resolve the user's persisted cache credentials for these connections and use an ownership-checked deletion path for them.

title: An empty Prisma update does not refresh updatedAt
body: updateManyByCredentialId forwards this empty object directly to Prisma. Prisma does not bump an @updatedAt field when the update data is empty, so this call leaves SelectedCalendar.updatedAt unchanged after every cache refresh instead of recording the refresh time as intended. Supply updatedAt explicitly, or remove this unused timestamp-tracking call if CalendarCache.updatedAt is the sole freshness marker.

title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script
body: ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's working directory, not the script's location. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore creates or modifies .env in the repository's parent directory, leaving the application's environment unchanged while reporting success. Derive the repository root from the script's location before selecting the environment file.

title: Make the environment update work with GNU sed
body: The sed -i '' invocation uses BSD/macOS syntax and fails with GNU sed. On Linux, once GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, rerunning this helper leaves the old URL in place but still prints that it was updated successfully. Subsequent Google Calendar watches consequently use the stale tunnel endpoint. Use a portable replacement strategy or handle both sed variants, and check the command's exit status before reporting success.

title: Invalidate calendar status after deleting the cache
body: A successful cache deletion only shows a toast and invokes the optional onSuccess callback. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper allows that callback to be omitted and does not invalidate its connectedCalendars query itself. Consequently, the dropdown continues showing the deleted cache's timestamp and deletion action after reporting success; window-focus refetching is also disabled. Invalidate connectedCalendars on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

title: Resolve persisted cache records for delegated connections
body: Connected calendars can contain in-memory delegation credentials, but CalendarCache rows reference persisted credential IDs. The existing availability reader explicitly handles this by looking up delegated cache entries using userId and key. Querying status only by the connected credential ID therefore returns no status for those delegated accounts even when they are actively serving cached availability. Since their regular connection is hidden and they cannot be disconnected, the dropdown disappears entirely, leaving no way to inspect or clear that cache. Resolve the underlying persisted cache records and a valid deletion target for delegated connections.

title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script
body: ENV_FILE is relative to the caller's working directory. Running `bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repository root writes to `.env` in the repository's parent directory rather than the root environment file used by the application. The script reports success while CalendarService continues using the old webhook URL. Derive the repository root from the script's location before constructing this path.

title: Make the environment update work with GNU sed
body: The `sed -i ''` syntax is specific to BSD/macOS sed. With GNU sed, updating an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL fails and leaves its value unchanged. Because the exit status is ignored, the script still announces that the new tunnel URL was installed, so subsequent calendar subscriptions use the stale endpoint. Use a portable replacement strategy or handle the platform-specific sed syntax and check for failure.

title: Sanitize HTML even when skipping Markdown rendering
body: Returning raw here bypasses HTML sanitization entirely. PollFeed passes feed HTML into TopicEmbed.import, where Nokogiri parses it but does not remove scripts or event-handler attributes. These posts use raw_html, and their cooked content is rendered unescaped. A feed item containing an onerror handler therefore introduces stored XSS under the forum's origin. Subsequent edits to imported posts bypass the same protection. This mode should skip Markdown conversion while still sanitizing HTML on every cook.

title: Close the template conditional with a plain end
body: The tag uses `end if` without a condition instead of closing the opening conditional with `end`. This produces invalid Ruby when the ERB template is compiled, so requests for an existing embedded topic fail instead of displaying the discussion. The controller specs do not render this template and therefore miss the failure.

title: Validate redirect destinations before fetching remote articles
body: TopicRetriever validates only the initial URL's hostname, while open-uri follows HTTP redirects without applying that validation again. If the configured site exposes an external redirect endpoint, a caller can supply an allowed-host URL that redirects to a private-network service. Its response can then be imported into a public topic. The Referer check does not prevent requests from clients that supply that header themselves. Validate each redirect destination, including its resolved address, before issuing the request.

title: Handle RSS entries that do not have an Atom content field
body: Standard RSS entries commonly provide their body in `description` or `content:encoded`, rather than `content`. SimpleRSS exposes these as separate fields, so `i.content` is nil for such entries and calling scrub raises an exception. One such entry aborts the entire poll; it also prevents TopicRetriever from reaching its HTTP fallback when feed polling is enabled. Select the available content field and handle entries with no body safely.

title: Resolve relative references using URI joining
body: The slash-prefix substitution corrupts protocol-relative URLs: `//cdn.example/image.png` becomes a path on the article's host instead of a URL on cdn.example. It also leaves path-relative references such as `images/image.png` and `../other-page` untouched, so browsers resolve them against the forum URL. Imported articles consequently contain broken images and links. Resolve href and src values against the article URL with URI joining rather than manually prefixing slashes.

title: Defer post-processing jobs until the outer transaction commits
body: PostCreator#create enqueues feature_topic_users and process_post before returning. Its internal transaction joins this new outer transaction, so the topic and post are still uncommitted when those jobs are submitted. A Sidekiq worker can execute them before their records are visible, and a later failure creating TopicEmbed can leave queued work for rolled-back records. Preserve atomic creation of the embed and post, but defer job submission until the outer transaction commits.

title: Preserve the original discussion timestamp during Disqus import
body: The previous PostCreator call supplied the thread's created_at timestamp, but import_remote does not accept or forward it. Imported topics and their first posts now receive the current time, while replies still retain their historical timestamps. This makes old discussions appear newly created and gives their opening posts timestamps later than their replies. Carry the source thread timestamp through the TopicEmbed import API.

title: Sanitize HTML even when bypassing Markdown rendering
body: The new raw_html mode returns raw content without sanitization. PollFeed passes external feed content into this mode through TopicEmbed.import, and Nokogiri parsing only rewrites URLs—it preserves scripts, event handlers, and unsafe link schemes. For example, an imported image with an onerror handler becomes executable stored HTML in the forum's origin. Edits to these posts retain the same bypass. Keep an HTML sanitization step on every cook.

title: Remove the incomplete postfix condition from the closing tag
body: This tag emits `end if` without a condition instead of closing the block with `end`. The incomplete Ruby statement breaks compilation of the ERB template, so requests for URLs with an existing TopicEmbed fail when rendering the discussion. The controller specs do not render views and therefore do not catch this.

title: Validate redirect destinations before fetching them
body: TopicRetriever checks the initial URL's hostname, but open-uri follows redirects here without rechecking the destination. An allowed-host URL that redirects to another host, including an internal HTTP service, bypasses the embed-host allowlist; the server fetches that response and may publish its content as the configured import user. Validate each redirect target before issuing the next request rather than following redirects unchecked.

title: Handle RSS description fields and entries without content
body: Valid RSS items commonly provide their body through description or content:encoded rather than the Atom content field; Atom entries can also contain only summary. For those entries, i.content is nil and calling scrub raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire feed import. Select the available body field and handle missing content explicitly. The current specs only test whether poll_feed is called, not whether a real feed can be imported.

title: Resolve relative references using the source URL
body: The string concatenation mishandles standard URL references. For an article at https://blog.example/posts/one, src='//cdn.example/image.png' becomes https://blog.example/cdn.example/image.png, while href='two.html' is left unchanged and resolves against the forum instead of the source article. Both links and images can therefore break after import. Resolve references against the complete source URI rather than stripping leading slashes and prepending the host.

title: Defer post-creation jobs until the outer transaction commits
body: PostCreator.create enqueues process_post and feature_topic_users before returning. Wrapping it in this additional Topic.transaction means those jobs are now published while the new topic and post remain uncommitted. A fast worker can execute them before their records are visible, causing processing to fail or be skipped; a subsequent rollback also leaves jobs for nonexistent records. Preserve the atomic import but defer job publication until the enclosing transaction commits.

title: Set the retrieval marker and its expiry atomically
body: SETNX and EXPIRE are separate operations. If the worker exits after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE runs, the marker remains indefinitely and retrieved_recently? suppresses every subsequent retrieval of that URL. Without feed polling, the embed stays on the loading page permanently despite repeated requests. Create the marker with its expiry in one atomic Redis operation.

title: Preserve exported thread timestamps during Disqus imports
body: The previous PostCreator call supplied the exported thread's created_at value. TopicEmbed.import_remote does not forward a creation timestamp, so historical topics and their first posts are now dated at import time while their replies still use the original exported dates. This corrupts discussion chronology and makes old threads appear newly created. Pass the thread timestamp through the new import API.

title: Compare postMessage origins exactly
body: A substring check accepts origins that are merely prefixes of the configured origin. For example, discourseUrl='https://forum.example.com/' accepts a message from 'https://forum.example.co'. A window on that different domain with a reference to the embedding page can send resize messages to hide or stretch the comments iframe. Compare against the parsed, exact Discourse origin and verify that e.source is the iframe's contentWindow.

title: Fix the invalid conditional terminator in the embed template
body: `<%- end if %>` contains an `if` without a condition and produces invalid Ruby when the template is compiled. Every embed request that finds an existing topic therefore fails instead of rendering its comments. Replace this with an ordinary `end` and add a test that actually renders the template; the mocked controller tests do not exercise it.

title: Retain HTML sanitization for raw-HTML posts
body: This return bypasses sanitization for both creation and subsequent edits. PollFeed supplies external HTML directly, while TopicEmbed appends a source link containing an unescaped URL. For example, an otherwise valid article URL ending in `?x='onclick='alert(1)` injects an event-handler attribute into that link. Nokogiri parsing preserves such attributes, and the resulting cooked HTML is rendered as trusted content in the forum origin. Sanitize the complete raw-HTML output and escape the generated source link.

title: Validate import URLs before passing them to Kernel.open
body: `import_remote` opens its argument before the HTTP URL check in `import`. The Disqus importer calls this method directly with a thread link from the XML export, bypassing TopicRetriever's validation. Ruby's `Kernel.open` interprets a leading pipe as a subprocess, so an export containing a link such as `|id` executes a command as the application user before any URL rejection occurs. Validate the HTTP(S) URI before I/O and use a client without filesystem or subprocess fallback.

title: Enforce the host restriction across HTTP redirects
body: Only the original embed URL is checked here, but `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses open-uri, which automatically follows redirects to other hosts. An allowed-host URL with an open redirect can therefore cause a public embed request to fetch an internal HTTP service or another otherwise-disallowed host, potentially importing its response into a public topic. Validate each redirect destination before following it rather than relying solely on the initial host comparison.

title: Handle feed items without a content element
body: A valid RSS item can provide its body in `description` or `content:encoded` without a `content` element, and Atom entries can provide only a summary. Calling `scrub` unconditionally on `i.content` raises when that field is absent, aborting the entire poll and preventing later items from being imported. Select the appropriate available body field and handle entries with no body explicitly.

title: Resolve relative URLs against the article URI
body: The prefix concatenation treats protocol-relative URLs as root-relative paths: `//cdn.example.com/image.png` becomes a path on the article's host instead of retaining the CDN host. Path-relative references such as `images/image.png` are left unchanged and subsequently resolve against the forum rather than the original article. Both links and images can therefore break in imported posts. Use URI reference resolution against the article URL for both attributes.

title: Defer post-creation jobs until the outer import transaction commits
body: `PostCreator#create` enqueues post-processing and featured-user jobs after its own transaction block, but that transaction joins this outer `Topic.transaction`. Consequently those jobs are published before the imported post and topic are committed, and are also published if the subsequent TopicEmbed insertion fails. A worker can see missing records and skip or fail processing. Preserve the atomic import while deferring these jobs and publication side effects until the outer transaction commits.

title: Preserve the original thread creation time during Disqus import
body: The previous PostCreator call supplied the exported thread's `created_at`, but the replacement passes only its title, and TopicEmbed does not forward a creation timestamp. Imported first posts are now dated at import time while their replies retain their historical dates. This loses original chronology and can place replies before the apparent start of their discussion. Extend the import helper to accept and preserve the exported timestamp.

title: Compare postMessage origins exactly
body: Substring matching does not establish that a message came from the Discourse origin. For example, `https://forum.example.co` passes this check when discourseUrl is `https://forum.example.com/`. Another window with a reference to the embedding page can therefore send resize messages that hide the comments or disrupt the page layout. Compare against the parsed, exact Discourse origin and verify that the message source is the embedded iframe.

title: Preserve panel right alignment in the legacy flexbox fallback
body: The new `flexbox()` mixin falls back to `display: -webkit-box`/`-moz-box`, but those legacy box layouts treat auto margins as zero. In browsers selecting that fallback, removing `float: right` and relying on `margin-left: auto` leaves the header panel immediately after the logo/topic title instead of at the right edge. The dropdowns are positioned relative to that panel with `right: 0`, so the wide search dropdown can consequently extend off the left side of the viewport. Provide equivalent legacy-box spacing, or preserve the float layout for those browsers rather than enabling this fallback.

title: Preserve right-alignment in the legacy flexbox fallback
body: The new `flexbox()` mixin selects `display: -webkit-box` on browsers such as stock Android 4.0–4.3 and Safari 6.0, but that older box model does not distribute free space through `margin-left: auto`. With `float: right` removed and no corresponding `box-flex` or `box-pack` rule, the navigation panel sits immediately after the logo/topic information instead of at the right edge. Its right-anchored dropdowns move left as well, potentially placing the wide search menu partly offscreen. Add an old-box-compatible distribution rule or retain a working float fallback for those browsers.

title: Preserve right alignment in the legacy box fallback
body: The new `flexbox()` mixin enables `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` on older engines, but that legacy box model does not distribute free space to auto margins. In those browsers, replacing `float: right` with `margin-left: auto` leaves `.panel` beside the logo/topic information instead of at the header’s right edge. Wide dropdowns right-anchored to this panel can consequently extend off the left side of the viewport. Provide a working legacy alignment mechanism, such as a flexible spacer, or retain a non-box fallback for those engines.

title: Cache devices only after admission succeeds
body: tagDeviceUI caches the device before CreateOrUpdateDevice checks the limit. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, that cache entry remains for 29 minutes. A second request with the rejected device ID therefore returns nil from the cache check, and Anonymous.Authenticate grants access without enforcing the limit. Simply retrying bypasses the restriction. Populate the cache only after a successful store operation, and test repeated requests from a rejected device.

title: Make device admission atomic across requests
body: CountDevices and the subsequent upsert run in separate database sessions without synchronization. With one slot remaining, concurrent requests from different new devices can all observe a count below the limit and then all insert successfully. Those excess devices subsequently qualify for updates and can remain admitted indefinitely. Serialize the count-and-admit operation at the database level so the limit also holds across Grafana instances.

title: Do not treat a missing device ID as successful admission
body: Anonymous authentication now relies on TagDevice to reject requests beyond the limit, but TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. Consequently, even with the configured limit exhausted, a caller can omit this client-controlled header and receive an anonymous identity for API requests without being counted or checked. Limited anonymous access needs an admission path for requests without a device ID rather than treating them as admitted.

title: Make the device limit configurable through environment overrides
body: The new device_limit key is read from the raw INI section but is not added to conf/defaults.ini. Grafana's normal environment-override pass visits keys already present in the loaded configuration, so setting GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone leaves this value at 0 and silently disables enforcement. Add the key to the defaults or read it through SectionWithEnvOverrides, with a test covering an environment-only configuration.

title: Do not cache devices whose admission was rejected
body: tagDeviceUI populates the 29-minute local cache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the limit is reached, a new device's first request returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, but its next request hits that cache and returns nil, allowing Anonymous.Authenticate to grant access. Concurrent requests can bypass the rejection the same way. Only cache a device after successful admission, and add a regression test that retries a rejected device.

title: Make the device-limit check and admission atomic
body: CountDevices and the subsequent upsert run in separate database sessions without serialization. With one slot remaining, two requests for different new devices can both observe a count below the limit and both insert successfully. Subsequent requests keep both devices admitted because the at-limit branch permits updates to existing rows. Serialize the count-and-admit operation across Grafana instances so concurrent arrivals cannot exceed the configured limit.

title: Register device_limit for environment-variable overrides
body: This reads the new option directly from the INI file without adding a device_limit entry to conf/defaults.ini. Grafana's environment-override pass operates on existing INI keys, so setting only GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT in a standard deployment leaves this value at zero and silently keeps anonymous devices unlimited. Add the default configuration key or read it through the environment-aware settings accessor.

title: Give the runtime device limit its numeric union type
body: This initializer infers anonymousDeviceLimit as undefined; implementing GrafanaConfig does not inherit its number | undefined member type. The exported runtime config is a GrafanaBootConfig, so numeric assignments fail type checking and consumers that guard against undefined then format the limit encounter a never type, despite the backend supplying a number. Declare the field as number | undefined explicitly.

title: Do not cache failed device admissions
body: tagDeviceUI caches the device ID before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and returns nil on subsequent cache hits. When the store rejects a new device with ErrDeviceLimitReached, this error return leaves that ID cached for 29 minutes. Retrying with the same ID therefore succeeds, and Anonymous.Authenticate grants access without admitting or counting the device. Populate the cache only after successful admission, and test repeated requests from a rejected device.

title: Make the capacity check and admission atomic
body: CountDevices and the subsequent upsert run in separate database sessions without synchronization. With one remaining slot, concurrent requests for different device IDs can both observe a count below the limit and both insert successfully. Subsequent requests then accept both as existing devices, so the overage is not corrected. Admission needs database-level locking or another atomic capacity-reservation mechanism that also works across Grafana instances.

title: Do not interpret an untagged request as an admitted device
body: Authentication now relies on TagDevice to enforce the limit, but TagDevice immediately returns nil when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. A client can therefore omit this header and obtain an anonymous identity even when the configured limit is full, without being counted. Resource requests subject to the limit need an admitted device identity; skipping tracking must not implicitly authorize them.

title: Enable environment overrides for the new setting
body: The new device_limit key is read through iniFile.Section, but no entry is added to conf/defaults.ini. Grafana's regular environment-override pass visits keys already present in the loaded INI, so setting only GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT does not populate this option: it defaults to zero and leaves access unlimited. Add the key to defaults.ini or read the section through SectionWithEnvOverrides.

title: Read-only group permission authorizes group creation
body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-Groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses this check to authorize POST /groups, so an administrator granted only read access can create groups or move existing subgroups to the top level. This check must require MANAGE rather than VIEW; add a negative test for a view-only all-Groups permission.

title: Authorization resource IDs are used as group IDs
body: groupResource.getId() is the authorization resource's generated ID, not the GroupModel ID stored in its name. Passing it to hasPermission() therefore looks up the wrong name, and adding it to granted supplies invalid IDs to user membership queries. In particular, a view-members or manage-members grant on all Groups returns the aggregate authorization resource's UUID; UsersResource then filters by that UUID and returns no users, and /users/count is also incorrect. Collect actual group IDs and handle the aggregate Groups resource separately.

title: V2 group managers cannot create group members
body: The group-member creation fallback still checks only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, the V1 feature flag. With V2 enabled, an administrator granted the new manage-members and manage-membership scopes on a group receives 403 from POST /users even when the representation assigns the new user only to that authorized group: canCreateGroupMembers() exits before evaluating those permissions. Allow this fallback for V2 as well and cover group-scoped user creation in the new tests.

title: Require manage scope for group creation
body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE because hasPermission() grants access when any requested scope matches. Consequently, an administrator with only view permission on all Groups passes GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()'s requireManage() check and can create groups or move existing subgroups to the top level. Restrict this check to MANAGE so read-only group permissions cannot authorize writes.

title: Build the user-search filter from actual group IDs
body: This method returns authorization resource IDs, but its callers use the result as realm group IDs in UserModel.GROUPS. Granting view-members or manage-members on all Groups therefore adds the synthetic all-groups resource's UUID to the membership filter, causing user searches—including the brute-force users endpoint—to return no members. Individual group resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() also have no Groups type, so this scan misses their grants and skips the intended database filtering before pagination. Enumerate or resolve actual GroupModel IDs, and handle all-groups grants explicitly, rather than using authorization resource IDs.

title: Enable group-member creation authorization for FGAP V2
body: The user-creation fallback still requires the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature, which is not enabled when V2 is selected. A delegated V2 administrator granted manage-members and manage-membership on a group, but not manage on all Users, therefore receives 403 when creating a user with that group in the representation. The new group permissions authorize managing existing members but cannot reach the checks intended to authorize creating members. Include V2 in this feature guard and test group-restricted user creation.

title: Do not grant group management through the view scope
body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() relies on this check, so an administrator granted only read access can create groups and move existing subgroups to the top level by posting their IDs. This permits unauthorized hierarchy changes, not just viewing. Require MANAGE here and add a negative test for group creation and movement with only VIEW.

title: Return model group IDs rather than authorization resource IDs
body: The authorization resource ID is not the GroupModel ID: AdminPermissionsSchema stores the group ID as the resource name, while hasPermission() looks resources up by name. Both passing groupResource.getId() to that method and returning it as a group ID are incorrect. In particular, granting VIEW_MEMBERS on all groups causes this loop to return the synthetic Groups resource's UUID. UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource then use that UUID as a membership filter, returning no users despite the grant. Resolve actual group IDs and handle the all-groups resource separately.

title: Enable the group-member creation fallback for FGAP V2
body: The group-member creation fallback still checks only the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature. With V2 enabled, an administrator granted MANAGE_MEMBERS and MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP for a group, but not global user management, cannot create a user assigned to that group: requireManage() fails and this guard returns false before evaluating either group permission. Include V2 in this feature check so the newly implemented group scopes work for the existing group-member creation workflow, and cover this case with an integration test.

title: Revoke locally stored recovery codes after replacing them in user storage
body: When a federated user already has recovery codes stored in Keycloak, a successful user-storage update leaves that existing credential untouched. This is particularly relevant when upgrading, since the required action previously always stored recovery codes in Keycloak. Credential validation can fall back to the local provider when external validation fails, so regenerating codes now leaves the old local codes usable alongside the new set. Remove the existing local recovery-code credential after successfully replacing it in user storage, and cover this migration/regeneration case in a test.

title: Remove exhausted credentials from their actual storage
body: The new lookup can return a credential owned by an external user-storage provider, but the exhaustion branch below still passes its ID to removeStoredCredentialById, which only deletes Keycloak-stored credentials. For a provider that keeps its credential record configured after consuming the final code, the exhausted record therefore remains. If the user abandons the subsequent regeneration page, the next login selects that record and RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() on an empty Optional, preventing login. Disable/remove external credentials through their provider instead. The new test fixture never consumes codes, so an exhaustion test with a stateful provider is needed to exercise this path.

title: Revoke local recovery codes when replacing them in user storage
body: For a federated user who already has recovery codes stored in Keycloak—the creation path used before this change—a successful external update leaves the existing local recovery credential untouched. Credential validation can still fall back to that local credential when the external validator rejects an input, so regenerating recovery codes does not invalidate the old set. Remove the previous local recovery credential when the external replacement succeeds, and test replacing an existing local set with a user-storage set.

title: Remove exhausted credentials through the appropriate storage API
body: The credential fetched here can now belong to external user storage, but the allCodesUsed() branch still calls removeStoredCredentialById(), which removes Keycloak-stored credentials rather than invoking the external CredentialInputUpdater. For a provider that retains exhausted credentials until disabled, this deletion does nothing. If the user abandons the subsequent reconfiguration action, the exhausted credential can remain configured, and the next recovery login fails when RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). Route exhausted external credentials through the user-storage disable/removal operation.

title: Test recovery-code consumption rather than indefinitely reusable codes
body: The new recovery validator accepts a matching code without consuming it, and getCredentials() reconstructs a completely unused credential from the original list on every read. Consequently, this fixture keeps requesting code 0 and accepts the same code indefinitely. The added integration test performs only one login, so it cannot detect broken advancement, replay rejection, or exhaustion handling in the newly supported federated path. Persist consumption state in the fixture and extend the test to reject reuse and exercise the last-code/reconfiguration path.

title: Revoke the previous local recovery set when writing to user storage
body: When updateCredential succeeds in user storage, this helper leaves any existing recovery credential in the Keycloak database untouched. Existing federated users can have such credentials because the required action previously always created them locally. Credential validation can still fall back to the local recovery-code provider, so those old codes remain usable after the user regenerates their recovery codes. Remove the previously stored recovery credential after a successful external replacement, and cover the transition from locally stored to externally stored codes.

title: Disable exhausted credentials in the storage that owns them
body: The new lookup can return a credential owned by a user-storage provider, but the exhaustion branch still calls removeStoredCredentialById. That removes a Keycloak-stored credential, not the external credential exposed by the provider. If the provider retains the exhausted credential and reports it as configured, abandoning the subsequent setup action leaves the next login trying to render an empty recovery set; RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() and fails. Use the user-storage disabling path for an exhausted external credential rather than attempting only a stored-credential deletion.

title: Exercise consumption of externally stored recovery codes
body: The new test provider accepts any matching code without consuming it, while getCredentials reconstructs a completely unused recovery set on every call. Consequently, the same code remains valid indefinitely, the requested code number never advances, and allCodesUsed can never become true. The new integration test stops after one successful login, so it does not verify that the changed federated lookup observes consumption or exhaustion. Maintain consumption state in the test provider and test replay rejection, advancement to the next code, and regeneration after exhaustion.

title: Keep the registered metric-alert handler instantiable
body: The empty StatefulDetectorHandler subclass leaves counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data abstract. MetricAlertFire still registers this class, and Detector.detector_handler instantiates registered handlers, so accessing the handler for a detector with type='metric_alert_fire' now raises TypeError. process_detectors does not catch this exception, so that detector aborts the batch instead of retaining the previous no-op behavior. Implement the required methods or retain a concrete placeholder returning an empty dict.

title: Build the expected occurrence with the evaluated group key
body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds its expected occurrence with group_key='val1', but invokes evaluate_group_key_value with group_key='group_key'. The helper incorporates that key into the occurrence fingerprint, so the expected fingerprint ends in ':val1' while the actual fingerprint ends in ':group_key'. The result equality assertion therefore fails even with the correct implementation. Build the expected occurrence using 'group_key'.

title: Keep the registered metric-alert handler instantiable
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits four abstract members without implementing them: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. MetricAlertFire still registers this class, and Detector.detector_handler instantiates it unconditionally. Accessing the handler for a metric_alert_fire detector therefore raises TypeError and aborts process_detectors, whereas previously it returned no results. Implement the required members or retain a concrete no-op handler until the stateful implementation is ready.

title: Build the expected occurrence for the group being evaluated
body: The expected occurrence is built for "val1", but the evaluation below uses "group_key". Since build_mock_occurrence_and_event incorporates that argument into the fingerprint, the expected occurrence identifies a different issue from the actual occurrence. Build it using "group_key" and explicitly check the resulting fingerprint so this test validates that the new hook attributes occurrences to the evaluated detector group.

title: Keep the registered metric-alert handler concrete
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler remains registered as MetricAlertFire.detector_handler, but it now inherits four abstract members without implementing them: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. Accessing detector.detector_handler for a metric_alert_fire detector therefore raises TypeError when the model instantiates this class. process_detectors does not catch that exception, so processing aborts instead of retaining the previous no-op behavior. Keep the handler concrete or leave it unregistered until its required methods are implemented.

title: Use the evaluated group key in the expected occurrence
body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds its expected occurrence with group key "val1", but calls evaluate_group_key_value with "group_key". The new hook consequently builds an actual occurrence whose fingerprint is ["<detector_id>:group_key"], while the expected fingerprint is ["<detector_id>:val1"]. The DetectorEvaluationResult equality assertion fails even when the implementation behaves correctly. Build the expected occurrence using "group_key".

title: Recognize spawn-context processes before killing unhealthy workers
body: Workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process are SpawnProcess instances, not instances of the default-context multiprocessing.Process class. This condition is therefore false for production workers. When a worker hangs, the manager starts a replacement without killing the original and overwrites its tracked reference. The original can remain stuck or resume flushing alongside its replacement. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or the actual context's Process class; the termination guard in join() has the same problem.

title: Clean up every worker even after the join deadline expires
body: If next_step.join() consumes the timeout, or waiting for one worker exhausts it, this break skips cleanup of all remaining workers. Setting stopped only requests an exit between flush iterations, so workers blocked in Redis operations or Kafka futures can survive the rebalance and overlap the replacement strategy. The deadline should limit graceful waiting, but every remaining process still needs forced termination and cleanup.

title: Wait for flushing with an unpatched synchronization mechanism
body: test_basic replaces time.sleep with a no-op at line 15, so this added sleep does not wait for the flusher to observe the advanced drift. The following join() sets the worker's stopped flag immediately. Depending on thread scheduling, the worker can exit without emitting the expected segment, leaving the messages assertion flaky. Wait for the produced message or a completion event before joining, using an unpatched synchronization primitive.

title: The process type check prevents hung workers from being killed
body: Workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process are SpawnProcess instances, not instances of the top-level multiprocessing.Process class. This condition is therefore false for production workers. When a worker is classified as hung, its dictionary entry is replaced without killing it, leaving an untracked process that can resume flushing the same shards and updating the same health/backpressure values as its replacement. Check against SpawnProcess or BaseProcess and stop the old worker before replacing it.

title: Continue worker cleanup after the join deadline expires
body: If waiting for one flusher exhausts the timeout, this break skips termination of every remaining worker. It also skips all workers if next_step.join(timeout) consumes the deadline. Setting stopped only helps workers that return to the top of their loop; workers blocked in Redis or Kafka calls can remain alive after join returns and overlap with replacement flushers following a rebalance. The deadline should stop further waiting, but cleanup must still terminate every outstanding child.

title: Check the correct process type before killing unhealthy workers
body: Workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process are SpawnProcess instances, not instances of multiprocessing.Process; those classes separately inherit BaseProcess. This check therefore skips kill() for every production worker. When a live worker hangs, its replacement overwrites the tracked handle while the original remains alive, leaking processes and allowing concurrent flushing of the same shards if the original recovers. Check against the spawn context's Process class or BaseProcess and clean up the old worker before replacing it.

title: Clean up every worker after the join timeout expires
body: If next_step.join() or an earlier worker consumes the timeout, this break skips cleanup for every remaining worker. Setting stopped is insufficient for workers blocked in Redis or future.result(), since they cannot inspect that flag until the operation returns. Consequently, join() can return during a rebalance while old workers remain alive and retain their shard assignments indefinitely. Apply the deadline only to graceful waiting, then terminate and reap all workers that have not exited.

title: Backup-code consumption is vulnerable to concurrent replay
body: This read-modify-write sequence is not atomic: two login requests can both read the same stored code, both find it, and both authenticate before either update is visible. Concurrent use of different codes can also overwrite one another and restore a code that was already consumed. Since backup codes are promised to work exactly once, consume them with an atomic conditional update or transaction/lock so only one request can succeed.

title: The external-provider 2FA flow does not offer backup-code recovery
body: When OAuth or SAML login redirects to the `totpEmail` flow, this conditional renders `ExternalTotpFooter` instead of `TwoFactorFooter`, so users never see the new “Lost access” option or a backup-code input. This can affect users whose account has 2FA enabled when its identity provider changes; even if the UI offered recovery, `authorize` also rejects a non-CAL user's request without `totpCode` before reaching the backup-code branch. Such users cannot use their backup codes to sign in.

title: Backup-code redemption is not atomic
body: Two login requests can read the same backup-code list before either update completes. Both can validate the same code, then both write a list with that code nulled and both issue authenticated sessions. This makes a supposedly single-use recovery code reusable under concurrent requests. Consume the code with an atomic conditional update or equivalent serialization, and reject the request if another redemption already changed the list.

title: OAuth 2FA login has no backup-code option
body: The new “Lost access” control is only rendered in `TwoFactorFooter`; the login page instead renders `ExternalTotpFooter` when `totpEmail` is present. OAuth login can route a user with 2FA enabled to this `totpEmail` flow, so that user cannot select or submit a backup code and is locked out if they lack their authenticator.

title: Backup-code authentication is not tested
body: The added test only checks that backup codes can be displayed, copied, and downloaded; it never redeems one during login or verifies that a redeemed code is rejected on reuse. Those are the core authentication and single-use guarantees of this feature, so regressions in the new credential-validation and persistence path can pass the suite unnoticed.

title: Backup codes can be redeemed concurrently
body: This read-modify-write is not atomic: two login requests can both read the same stored code, both pass the membership check, and both write their own stale copy with that code nulled. Both requests then issue authenticated sessions, so a code advertised as single-use can be used more than once. Make validation and consumption conditional/atomic, for example with a transaction that verifies the stored value has not changed before updating it.

title: Backup-code authentication has no test coverage
body: The added test only checks that backup codes can be downloaded and copied; it never logs in with a code or checks that a redeemed code is rejected on reuse. This leaves the core authentication behavior, including its single-use guarantee, unverified. Add tests for successful backup-code login and rejection of a second use.

title: Meet bookings crash when no destination calendar is configured
body: When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, destructuring leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined, and this condition dereferences `.integration`. Creating an event with Google Meet and no destination calendar therefore throws before calendar or meeting events can be created; the previous optional-chain check handled this case.

title: Non-Google calendar services receive the wrong destination for additional hosts
body: `createAllCalendarEvents` invokes this function once per destination, passing that destination's external ID, but this call forwards only the credential ID to the calendar service. Lark, Office 365, and CalDAV creation still select `event.destinationCalendar[0]`, so calls for later hosts target the first host's calendar (or fail for lack of access) instead of the destination being processed. Collective bookings with multiple hosts using these integrations consequently fail to create events in each host's calendar.

title: Google update cannot fall back to the configured destination calendar
body: When `externalCalendarId` is absent, this lookup searches for a destination whose `externalId` equals that absent value, so it cannot select a configured destination calendar. `calendarId` is then undefined and Google event updates fail, even though the event contains the destination calendar. The analogous lookup in `deleteEvent` also falls through to `primary`, which can leave the event in its actual destination calendar.

title: Rescheduling a multi-calendar booking deletes only one old calendar event
body: This change collects and updates all calendar references, but the old-event cleanup below still uses `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes only the first calendar reference. When a booking has multiple host calendar events, rescheduling with `newBookingId` leaves the remaining old events on their calendars as stale duplicates.

title: Recurring cancellation does not delete events for every calendar reference
body: For recurring bookings, this loop iterates the organizer's credentials and then selects only the first calendar reference for each updated booking. It does not use the current reference being processed or match each booking reference to its credential. With multiple host calendar references, cancellation can repeatedly target the first calendar and leave the other hosts' recurring events behind.

title: Handle an empty destination calendar array before checking Google Meet
body: When `destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]`, destructuring leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined and accessing `.integration` throws. This happens while creating events that use Google Meet but have no destination calendar, so booking creation fails instead of following the previous fallback behavior.

title: Select the destination calendar for the current host credential
body: Collective bookings pass the full destination-calendar array to each host's calendar service, but this always selects element zero. For every secondary Office 365 host, the request then targets the first host's calendar ID using the secondary host's access token. The request fails or creates the event in the wrong calendar, leaving those hosts without the booking. Select the destination associated with the current credential instead.

title: Do not use the first host's calendar for every Lark credential
body: Each collective host's Lark service receives the full destination-calendar array, but this selects only its first entry. A secondary host's credential is therefore used against the first host's calendar ID, which can fail authorization or put the event in the wrong calendar. Select the destination belonging to the current credential.

title: Create CalDAV events in the calendar belonging to the current host
body: For collective bookings, each host's CalDAV service receives the entire destination-calendar array, but this filters calendars using only the first destination. Secondary hosts' credentials consequently try to create the event at the first host's calendar URL; that URL may be inaccessible with their credentials, so their calendar event is not created. Match the destination to the current credential.

title: Use the current host's destination email in the Google attendee list
body: The Google event is inserted into the calendar selected by `credentialId`, but the organizer attendee email is always taken from the first destination calendar. For a secondary host's event, this identifies the first host as the organizer instead of the host whose calendar is being used, so the event can be attributed to or invite the wrong host. Choose the destination matching `credentialId` here too.

title: Fall back to the destination calendar when updating legacy references
body: When `externalCalendarId` is absent, this searches for a destination whose `externalId` is also absent, so it returns `undefined` rather than the configured destination calendar. Updates for bookings with legacy references that lack an external calendar ID are then sent without a valid Google `calendarId` and fail. Fall back to the appropriate destination calendar, as the previous implementation did.

title: Delete legacy Google events from their configured destination calendar
body: If a reference has no `externalCalendarId`, this lookup searches for a destination with an undefined external ID and returns no calendar. The subsequent fallback is `primary`, even when the event was created on a configured non-primary destination calendar. Google returns 404 for that deletion, which this method treats as success, leaving the event orphaned in the calendar.

title: Handle events with no destination calendar before checking the integration
body: When `destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array, destructuring leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined and this dereference throws. A Google Meet booking without a configured destination calendar therefore fails during event creation instead of taking the fallback path that existed before this change.

title: Select the Lark destination belonging to the credential being used
body: Collective creation invokes the calendar service once per destination using that host's credential, but this always selects the first destination in the whole event. For later hosts, the service attempts to create the event in the first host's Lark calendar, which can fail due to permissions or create it in the wrong calendar. Select the destination whose `credentialId` matches this service's credential.

title: Select the Office 365 destination belonging to the credential being used
body: Collective creation invokes this service once per host credential, but this always uses the first destination calendar in the event. A later host's Office 365 account will consequently target the first host's calendar ID, which may be inaccessible or cause the event to be written to the wrong calendar. Choose the destination associated with the current credential.

title: Create CalDAV events in the destination for the current credential
body: The event is filtered to the first destination calendar regardless of which credential is creating it. Since collective event creation calls the service for each host, each CalDAV account targets the first host's calendar URL; other hosts' events can fail or be created in the wrong calendar. Match the destination to the current credential before filtering.

title: Use the matching destination calendar for the Google organizer attendee
body: For a collective event, this code uses the first host's destination calendar as the organizer email in every host's event copy. When creating or updating the copy for another credential, the organizer therefore refers to a different host's calendar instead of the calendar associated with that credential, which can produce incorrect organizer details or cause Google to reject the event. Select the destination matching the current credential (and do the same in `updateEvent`).

title: Restore a calendar fallback when updating or deleting without an external ID
body: When `externalCalendarId` is absent, the lookup compares each calendar's `externalId` to that same absent value and returns `undefined`; it never falls back to the event's destination calendar. Updates then send an undefined `calendarId`, and deletes fall through to `primary`, potentially failing to update or deleting from the wrong calendar for legacy references without an external calendar ID.

title: The sync path returns a Fetch Response instead of the provider's token response
body: When credential syncing is enabled, this returns the raw `fetch` `Response`, while the fallback returns each provider's native response shape. Callers are written for those native shapes: Google reads `res.data`, Bigin and Zoho CRM read `tokenInfo.data`, and HubSpot reads token fields directly. Those accesses fail or produce undefined token fields in sync mode, so refreshes break for these integrations. Normalize the sync response to the shape each caller expects, or update callers to parse the response consistently.

title: The minimum schema strips refreshed token fields
body: This computed key is a literal property name, not a wildcard for numeric expiry fields. Zod objects also strip unrecognized keys by default, so parsing a synced response retains only `access_token` and discards expiry and other provider fields. Callers then persist incomplete credentials; for example, Zoom assigns the missing `refresh_token` from the parsed response and can no longer refresh again, while Office 365 does not receive a new expiry. Preserve the response fields and explicitly extract the expiry value.

title: Salesforce token refresh bypasses credential syncing
body: This refresh request still calls Salesforce directly rather than using `refreshOAuthTokens`. With credential syncing configured, Salesforce credentials therefore continue to refresh against Cal.com's app credentials instead of the self-hosted source of truth, so the feature does not work for Salesforce.

title: Salesforce client is initialized with the pre-refresh access token
body: The refresh response is saved to the credential, but the connection below is constructed using `credentialKey.access_token`, which is the token loaded before the refresh. When that token has expired, the current operation still uses the expired token and fails even though a new token was successfully obtained. Initialize the connection with `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

title: Bigin sends the credential ID as the Cal.com user ID
body: The third argument is used by `refreshOAuthTokens` as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`, which is the credential row's database ID. A sync endpoint that looks up credentials by Cal.com user ID will look up the wrong user and cannot refresh this credential. Pass the owning user's ID instead.

title: The sync token schema strips required token fields
body: These computed keys are not wildcards: `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the same literal key for both entries, so the second property overwrites the first. Zod also strips unrecognized object properties by default. In credential-sync mode, parsing therefore drops fields such as `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, and `refresh_token`; token refresh then stores stale or missing values, causing repeated refreshes or unusable credentials.

title: Persist the parsed credential, not the Zod result wrapper
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the entire `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), but this code stores that object as the credential key. After the first token refresh, the database key no longer has Google token fields, so subsequent authentication fails when it parses the credential or tries to refresh again. Store the parsed `data` instead.

title: The synced refresh response is treated as a HubSpot token object
body: When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw Fetch `Response`, but this code treats its result as `HubspotToken`. The response has no `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, or `expiresIn` properties, so the code computes and persists undefined token fields and sets an invalid HubSpot access token. Parse the response body into the expected token shape before using it.

title: Salesforce refresh bypasses the credential sync endpoint
body: This refresh flow calls Salesforce directly instead of using `refreshOAuthTokens`, unlike the other integrations changed for this feature. With credential sharing enabled, Salesforce credentials therefore continue to refresh against Cal.com's configured app rather than the self-hoster's credential source of truth, so the advertised synchronization does not work for Salesforce.

title: The minimum token schema strips expiry fields and refresh tokens
body: These computed keys are stringified Zod schema objects, not wildcards for arbitrary response properties; both expressions resolve to the same literal property name, so the second also overwrites the first. Zod therefore strips real fields such as `expiry_date` and `expires_in` from the parsed response. The function then substitutes the literal `"refresh_token"` when the real refresh token was stripped or absent. Token refreshes can consequently save credentials without a valid expiry or refresh token, causing repeated refreshes or permanently breaking future refreshes.

title: The sync branch returns a Fetch Response to callers expecting parsed token data
body: When credential syncing is enabled, this returns the raw `Response` from `fetch`, whereas several callers treat the result as parsed data or an Axios response. For example, Bigin and Zoho CRM read `tokenInfo.data`, and HubSpot reads token fields directly from the returned value; with the sync branch active those fields are undefined, so token persistence and authentication fail. Parse the endpoint response into the same shape each caller expects, or give the helper a consistent return contract.

title: Salesforce constructs its connection with the expired tokens
body: The code refreshes the Salesforce access token and saves the refreshed response, but constructs the connection using `credentialKey.instance_url` and `credentialKey.access_token` from the original credential. If that access token was expired, the new connection still uses it and Salesforce API calls fail despite the successful refresh. Build the connection from the refreshed token response.

title: Salesforce token refresh bypasses the credential sync endpoint
body: This refresh path calls Salesforce directly instead of using `refreshOAuthTokens`, so configuring `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` has no effect for Salesforce credentials. Self-hosters who rely on their app store as the source of truth will still refresh Salesforce credentials using Cal.com's provider credentials, contrary to the syncing behavior added for the other integrations.

title: Bigin sends a credential ID as the remote user ID
body: The third argument is used by `refreshOAuthTokens` as `calcomUserId` in the sync request, but this call passes `credentialId`, not the credential owner's `userId`. The self-hosted app store therefore receives a credential record ID where it expects a user ID and cannot reliably refresh the correct user's token. Pass `credential.userId`.

title: Concurrent sync requests can create duplicate credentials
body: The handler performs a `findFirst` followed by a separate `create` when no credential is found. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no row and create duplicates; subsequent `findFirst` calls may then update an arbitrary duplicate. Make this operation atomic, for example with an appropriate unique constraint and upsert or a transaction that prevents duplicate creation.

title: Team admins and owners are incorrectly required to hold both roles
body: This uses `&&` between the admin and owner checks, so a user must be both a team admin and a team owner to pass this authorization branch. Admin-only and owner-only users are denied even though the booking UI treats admins or owners as authorized. Use an OR condition so the API matches the intended permission.

title: Blacklist checks can be bypassed by changing email case
body: The blacklist entries are lowercased, but `guest` is compared without normalization. Email addresses are case-insensitive for delivery, so a blacklisted address submitted with uppercase letters bypasses this check and is added and emailed. Normalize the submitted address before checking the blacklist.

title: Guests can be added to bookings that are no longer active
body: The handler updates attendees without checking the booking status. A direct API call can add guests to a cancelled or rejected booking, after which the handler sends confirmed calendar invitations for that event. Reject bookings whose status does not permit adding guests before writing attendee records.

title: Calendar update failures leave attendee records committed without notifications
body: Attendee records are committed at line 92 before this external calendar update. If the calendar provider call throws, the mutation fails and execution never reaches the email send, but the guests remain in the database; retrying with those guests can then fail as duplicates. Handle this failure consistently, for example by rolling back the write or recording a retryable calendar/email job.

title: Email notifications use the unfiltered guest list
body: `guests` can include addresses already attending the booking, but those addresses are removed from `uniqueGuests` before insertion. Passing the original list to `sendAddGuestsEmails` makes the email code treat those existing attendees as newly added and send them a normal scheduled-booking email when the request also includes a genuinely new guest. Pass the filtered list instead.

title: Team authorization requires users to be both admin and owner
body: The team permission check joins `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` with `&&`, so a team admin who is not also an owner is rejected. This prevents the team-admin role from using the endpoint even though the booking UI treats admins and owners as authorized. Use an OR between the role checks.

title: Guest email normalization lets callers bypass the blacklist
body: Blacklist entries are lowercased, but submitted guest addresses are compared without normalization. Because email validation does not lowercase addresses, a caller can submit a blacklisted address with different casing and have it inserted and sent invitations. Normalize both sides before checking; the same normalization should be used when detecting existing attendees.

title: A calendar sync failure leaves guests inserted but prevents notifications
body: The database attendee update has already committed before this external calendar update runs. If the update throws, the mutation fails before sending any emails, but the guests remain in the database; retrying those addresses then finds no new guests and errors. The operation can therefore leave guests added without calendar updates or invitations, with no way to recover through the same request. Handle this partial-failure case, for example by making retries idempotent and ensuring notifications/sync can be retried.

title: The endpoint allows guests to be added to cancelled bookings
body: The handler never checks the booking status, so an authorized attendee can call this mutation for a cancelled or rejected booking even though the UI only offers the action for confirmed bookings. The new attendee is then sent a scheduled email with a confirmed calendar invitation for an event that is no longer active. Reject bookings that are not in an eligible status on the server.

title: Add-guest notifications ignore event-type email-disable settings
body: Unlike the other booking email senders, this function does not check the event type's `disableStandardEmails` settings. Adding guests therefore sends host and attendee notifications even when standard emails are disabled for that event type, defeating the configured preference. Apply the host and attendee disable checks here as well.

title: Team admins and owners are incorrectly required to hold both roles
body: This permission check combines `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` with `&&`, so a user who is only an admin or only an owner is denied access. The booking UI and variable name treat these as alternative roles; use an OR check so either authorized role can add guests.

title: Email comparisons allow case-variant duplicates and blacklist bypass
body: Guest addresses are compared verbatim against existing attendees and against a blacklist whose entries were lowercased. Since email addresses are case-insensitive, a differently cased address can bypass the blacklist and can be added again as a duplicate attendee. Normalize addresses consistently before filtering and persistence.

title: Calendar attendee updates use the requesting user's credentials
body: This endpoint explicitly permits attendees and team admins to add guests, but it loads credentials from `ctx.user` and uses them to update the booking's calendar attendees. For a non-organizer requester, those credentials may not own or have access to the organizer's calendar, so the update can fail or leave the calendar unchanged even though the database attendee list was already modified. Use credentials that can update the booking's calendar, or avoid attempting that update when the requester cannot do so.

title: A calendar update failure leaves the booking changed while the request fails
body: The attendee records are committed at line 92 before this external calendar update. If the calendar operation throws, the mutation returns an error even though the guests were added; the notification step is then skipped, and retrying the same guests can fail because they now exist. Handle this partial-success case explicitly, such as by reporting the committed result and retrying calendar/email side effects separately.

title: Guest-add notifications ignore disabled standard email settings
body: Unlike the existing location-change and scheduling email senders, this function sends organizer and attendee notifications without checking the event type's `disableStandardEmails` settings. Adding guests therefore still emails recipients for event types configured to disable standard host or attendee emails. Pass the event type metadata into this sender and honor the corresponding settings.

title: Reminders without a recipient or message never reach the retry limit
body: When `sendTo` is empty or `message` is empty, this condition skips scheduling without incrementing `retryCount` or otherwise removing the reminder. The cron job will select the same unscheduled reminder on every run, so these unprocessable reminders are never cleaned up despite the retry limit.

title: Concurrent failures can lose retry-count increments
body: This writes an absolute value derived from the count read earlier, rather than incrementing the database value atomically. If overlapping cron invocations process the same reminder and both read the same `retryCount`, both can write the same next value; repeated overlaps can prevent the count from reaching 2, leaving failed reminders eligible for retries indefinitely. Use an atomic increment (and coordinate processing if concurrent sends must also be prevented).

title: Retry increments can be lost when cron runs overlap
body: This writes a value derived from the reminder snapshot fetched earlier rather than atomically incrementing the database value. If two cron invocations process the same failed reminder concurrently, both can read `retryCount = 0` and write `1`; repeated overlaps can prevent the count from reaching the `gt: 1` cleanup threshold, so persistently failing reminders are not reliably deleted after two failures. Use an atomic increment (and consider preventing concurrent processing of the same reminder).

title: Reminders without a destination or message never consume a retry
body: When `message` is empty or `sendTo` is falsy, this condition skips scheduling, but neither the failure branch nor the catch increments `retryCount`. The reminder therefore remains unscheduled and is selected again on every cron run, so reminders with a missing phone number (or message) are never removed by the retry limit.

title: Concurrent failures can lose retry increments
