The first such gap makes this loop stop advancing even when every delivered message is complete; later messages then remain uncommitted and may be replayed indefinitely. Track the order of observed messages rather than requiring numeric adjacency.

title: The queues are unbounded and provide no backpressure
body: `queue.Queue()` defaults to an unlimited size, and `submit()` can keep adding work without waiting for workers. If Kafka intake outpaces processing, queued `WorkItem`s and their message payloads can grow without limit until the consumer runs out of memory. Use bounded queues and propagate saturation back to polling or another explicit backpressure mechanism.

title: Queue shutdown APIs are unavailable before Python 3.13
body: `Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were added in Python 3.13. On supported Python runtimes before 3.13, this call raises `AttributeError` and is swallowed; workers remain blocked in `get()`, and `shutdown()` then waits up to five seconds per worker before leaving daemon threads behind. Use a shutdown mechanism compatible with the project's minimum Python version or require Python 3.13+.

title: A negative worker count creates a pool that commits without processing
body: `max_workers` is accepted as an unrestricted integer, and a negative value is truthy, so it produces a negative `num_queues` and starts no workers. Submissions then index an empty queue list; the strategy catches that error and marks the message offset complete, so results can be committed without processing. Reject non-positive worker counts before creating the pool.

title: Backup-code login can bypass password verification
body: Password verification above this branch is skipped whenever credentials.totpCode is nonempty. The new backup-code branch takes precedence over TOTP validation, so a request containing a valid backupCode and any arbitrary nonempty totpCode authenticates without a correct password or a valid TOTP. This makes a stolen backup code sufficient to access a password-based account. Require password verification for password-based backup-code login independently of whether a totpCode was supplied.

title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic
body: The remaining codes are computed from the user record read earlier and then written with an unconditional update by user ID. Two concurrent requests can both validate and successfully use the same supposedly single-use code. Requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's changes, restoring a consumed code. Consume codes atomically, for example with a conditional update against the original stored value and rejection or retry when that update loses the race.

title: OAuth two-factor users cannot reach backup-code recovery
body: The backup-code input is only shown after twoFactorLostAccess is set by the Lost access button, but login pages with totpEmail use ExternalTotpFooter, which only offers Cancel. Consequently, Google/SAML users redirected to this two-factor screen cannot use their saved backup codes after losing their authenticator, including users who generated codes before switching their account to OAuth. The credentials provider also rejects non-CAL users when only backupCode is supplied because its identity-provider checks require totpCode. Support recovery in both the external-login footer and the corresponding server checks.

title: A dummy TOTP value lets backup-code login bypass the password
body: Password verification above this branch runs only when credentials.totpCode is empty. A caller can therefore submit an account's email, a valid backupCode, and any nonempty totpCode (for example, "x") without supplying the password. This new branch accepts the backup code and never validates the supplied TOTP, so authentication succeeds with only the recovery code instead of both authentication factors. Ensure password authentication for CAL accounts cannot be skipped by supplying an unverified TOTP alongside a backup code.

title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic
body: The backup-code list is read before validation and then overwritten with an update conditioned only on the user ID. Two concurrent login requests can read the same list, validate the same code, and both successfully authenticate, violating the single-use guarantee. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's removals, making a consumed code usable again. Consume codes atomically, such as through a conditional update against the previously read ciphertext whose success is checked before granting access.

title: Identity-provider users cannot access backup-code recovery
body: When totpEmail is present after Google or SAML authentication, the page renders ExternalTotpFooter instead of TwoFactorFooter. Only TwoFactorFooter exposes the Lost access button, so these users can never reach the backup-code input. This affects accounts that generated backup codes while using CAL authentication and subsequently switched to an identity provider: the authentication callbacks retain their enabled 2FA and backup codes. The server also rejects a third-party account's backup-only submission because its identity-provider guards require totpCode. Provide a recovery route for this flow and make the server accept its backup-code authentication; otherwise users with valid saved codes remain locked out after losing their authenticator.

title: Backup-code login can bypass password verification
body: Password verification above this branch is skipped whenever credentials.totpCode is nonempty, but the new backup-code branch takes precedence and never validates that TOTP. A request containing an email, a valid backupCode, and any arbitrary nonempty totpCode therefore authenticates without the account password. This turns a backup code into a standalone login credential instead of a replacement second factor. Ensure the required primary authentication is verified regardless of which second-factor field is supplied.

title: Consume backup codes atomically to prevent replay and lost updates
body: Backup codes are read with the initial user lookup, checked in memory, and then overwritten using an update constrained only by user ID. Two concurrent requests can both read and successfully consume the same code, violating its single-use guarantee. Requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's changes and restore a consumed code. Use an atomic conditional update or appropriately locked transaction, and only authenticate if consumption succeeds.

title: Expose backup-code recovery for external-provider 2FA logins
body: When totpEmail is supplied after Google/SAML authentication, the page renders ExternalTotpFooter instead of TwoFactorFooter, so there is no 'Lost access' action and the backup-code input cannot be reached. This affects users who generated backup codes as CAL accounts and subsequently linked an external provider—the account-linking flow preserves their enabled 2FA and codes. Such users cannot use their saved recovery codes after losing their authenticator. Supporting this flow also requires adjusting the credentials provider's external-provider guard, which currently rejects requests without totpCode even when backupCode is supplied.

title: Guard the missing destination before checking its integration
body: When Google Meet is selected and destinationCalendar is null or empty, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined. Accessing its integration now throws instead of falling back to Cal Video as the previous optional access did. This prevents bookings from being created when the host has no destination calendar.

title: Pass the current destination to non-Google calendar adapters
body: Each host's credential is now used to create an event, but every call receives the entire destinationCalendar array. Office365, Lark, and BaseCalendarService still select only its first entry. For a collective booking, a secondary host therefore tries to create an event in the main host's calendar using their own credentials. Office365 and Lark can reject the request, while CalDAV can filter out every calendar and report success without creating anything. Scope the event's destination to the current host or make all adapters select by credentialId.

title: Keep secondary destinations when the organizer has no calendar
body: The event initializes destinationCalendar to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination. The optional push then silently discards teamDestinationCalendars, even if other collective hosts have connected calendars. Those hosts receive no directly created calendar events. Initialize an empty array and append the secondary hosts' destinations regardless of whether the organizer has one.

title: Preserve credential IDs on video references
body: This assignment now sets credentialId to undefined for every video result, whereas it previously preserved result.credentialId. The cancellation handler only deletes a video meeting when its booking reference has a credentialId. Newly created Zoom and other credential-backed video meetings will consequently remain active after their bookings are cancelled.

title: Preserve destination selection for calendars without a credential ID
body: DestinationCalendar.credentialId is nullable, and EventManager explicitly supports that case by trying credentials of the matching integration. This lookup cannot match such a destination to the supplied credentialId, so creation now falls back to primary instead of using the configured externalId. Existing destinations without a credential association can therefore receive bookings in the wrong calendar.

title: Restore a usable fallback when a reference lacks an external calendar ID
body: This branch runs only when externalCalendarId is absent, but then searches for a destination whose externalId equals that absent value. It cannot select a real destination, so Google updates receive an undefined calendarId and fail. The corresponding delete fallback also searches this way and instead targets primary, potentially leaving the original event behind. Older booking references without externalCalendarId must still be able to use their destination calendar.

title: Reconstruct all collective destinations when confirming a booking
body: Confirmation still constructs destinationCalendar from only the booking's single stored destination or the confirming user's destination. The secondary collective destinations assembled during handleNewBooking are not persisted, and this handler does not reload them. Since pending bookings create their integration events upon confirmation, collective events requiring approval still create an event for only one host. The payment webhook creation paths have the same omission.

title: Cancel recurring events using each reference's credential
body: For cancellation of all remaining recurring bookings, the newly resolved secondary host credential is ignored. The inner loop uses only the booking owner's credentials and selects just the first calendar reference from each occurrence. Although the outer loop now visits every host reference, it repeats the same first-reference deletion rather than deleting secondary hosts' events. All occurrences are marked cancelled while those hosts' calendar events remain active.

title: Do not reverse organization slug creation based on billing
body: The slug condition was reversed from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED. With team billing disabled, a newly created organization now gets neither a slug nor requestedSlug, despite the handler configuring its requested domain. With billing enabled, it publishes the slug immediately rather than retaining it solely as requestedSlug. This unrelated change breaks the existing organization provisioning behavior and should be reverted.

title: Guard the missing destination calendar before checking Google Meet
body: When destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or empty, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar. For a Google Meet location, accessing its integration throws instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. Booking creation therefore fails for event types that still select Google Meet after their destination calendar has been removed. Use optional chaining here.

title: Pass each calendar adapter its own destination
body: Every host's credential receives the entire destinationCalendar array. Only the Google adapter selects a destination by credentialId; Office365, Lark, and BaseCalendarService all use the first element. Consequently, a secondary host's Office365 or Lark credential attempts to create an event in the main host's calendar, typically failing with an inaccessible or invalid calendar ID. CalDAV can filter out every calendar and report success without creating anything. Pass a per-destination event to these adapters or make all adapters select by credentialId.

title: Preserve credential IDs on video references
body: This change sets credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result, discarding the credential ID returned by video meeting creation. handleCancelBooking only deletes a video meeting when its booking reference has a credentialId. Newly created Zoom and other dedicated video bookings will therefore leave their remote meetings active after cancellation. Preserve result.credentialId for video references.

title: Initialize the destination array before adding collective hosts
body: If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null. The optional push then silently discards all destination calendars collected from the other collective hosts. Those hosts receive no calendar events even when their calendars are connected. Initialize an empty array and append the collected destinations regardless of whether the organizer has one.

title: Retain destination selection for calendars without a credential ID
body: EventManager explicitly supports destination calendars without a credentialId by invoking the credentials matching their integration. This new lookup cannot match such a destination to the numeric credentialId passed to createEvent, so Google always inserts into primary rather than the configured externalId. Existing destinations using that fallback will start putting bookings in the wrong calendar. Preserve the legacy selection when the destination has no credentialId.

title: Cancel recurring events using each reference's credential
body: In the allRemainingBookings branch, the credential resolved for the current host is discarded. The code instead loops only over the booking owner's credentials and selects the first calendar reference from each recurring booking. With multiple collective hosts, this repeats deletion of the first host's events while never deleting the other hosts' events, despite marking every booking cancelled. Iterate each updated booking's calendar references and resolve the corresponding credentialId for each deletion.

title: Reconstruct collective destinations when confirming pending bookings
body: Confirmation reconstructs destinationCalendar with only the booking's single stored destination or the confirming user's destination. The additional collective destinations assembled in handleNewBooking are not persisted on the booking, and this handler does not reload them. Thus collective bookings requiring confirmation still create calendar events for only one host when approved. Reload the participating hosts' destinations before invoking handleConfirmation; the payment confirmation paths need the same treatment.

title: Restore organization slug assignment when team billing is disabled
body: The condition for storing the organization slug has been inverted. With IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED false, organization creation now stores neither slug nor requestedSlug, even though the supplied slug is checked for collisions and used to configure the domain. Self-hosted or other non-billing deployments therefore create organizations without the slug needed to identify their organization URLs. Preserve the previous non-billing slug assignment.

title: Guard the missing destination before checking its integration
body: When Google Meet is selected and destinationCalendar is null or empty, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar. Reading its integration throws before the intended Cal Video fallback can run. The previous optional access supported this case; bookings with a missing or disconnected destination calendar now fail instead of falling back.

title: Pass each calendar adapter its matching destination
body: Every host's credential is invoked with the entire destinationCalendar array, but the Office 365, Lark, and CalDAV adapters select only the first entry. For example, with two Office 365 hosts, the second host's token attempts to create an event in the first host's calendar rather than its own. This normally fails; CalDAV can instead filter out all calendars and return success without creating anything. Scope the event to the current destination or make all adapters select by credentialId, as the Google adapter does.

title: Retain collective destinations when the organizer has no calendar
body: The event initializes destinationCalendar to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination. The optional push then discards all collected teamDestinationCalendars, even when other collective hosts have connected calendars. Initialize an array and append the other hosts' destinations so those hosts still receive calendar events.

title: Reconstruct collective host destinations when confirming a booking
body: Confirmation reconstructs destinationCalendar using only the booking's single persisted destination or the confirming user's destination. The new-booking handler collects other collective hosts' destinations only in memory, and no calendar events are created until confirmation for pending bookings. Consequently, confirming a collective booking still creates an event for just one host. The confirmation path needs to recover the participating hosts' destinations as well; the payment webhook creation paths have the same omission.

title: Restore a usable Google calendar fallback for references without an external ID
body: When externalCalendarId is null or absent, this fallback searches for a destination whose externalId equals that missing value. Valid destinations have string IDs, so the search always returns undefined and events.update is called without its required calendarId. Older references without externalCalendarId can no longer be rescheduled even when the event has a valid destination. The analogous delete fallback now silently targets primary instead of the configured destination, potentially leaving the event undeleted.

title: Preserve credential IDs on video booking references
body: Reference creation now sets credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result, whereas previously it preserved result.credentialId for video meetings. The cancellation handler deletes a video meeting only when its booking reference has a credentialId. Newly created dedicated video meetings therefore lose the information needed for cancellation and remain active at the provider after the booking is cancelled.

title: Cancel recurring events using each host's matching reference and credential
body: In the allRemainingBookings branch, the resolved credential for the current calendar reference is ignored. Instead, each outer reference repeats a traversal of only the organizer's credentials, and each recurring booking contributes only its first calendar reference. Other collective hosts' credentials fetched from the database are never used, so their recurring calendar events remain scheduled even though all bookings are marked cancelled. Iterate each updated booking's calendar references and resolve the matching credential for each one.

title: Do not reverse organization slug assignment based on billing
body: This changes slug assignment from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED while requestedSlug remains conditional on billing being enabled. With team billing disabled, newly created organizations now receive neither slug nor requestedSlug, despite the handler configuring a domain using the requested slug. With billing enabled, the slug is assigned immediately rather than kept as a requested slug. Restore the original condition unless the organization publication flow is intentionally being changed and updated alongside it.

title: The minimum response schema strips expiry and refresh-token fields
body: Using a Zod schema's `.toString()` as an object key does not define a wildcard property. These computed keys resolve to literal strings (both normally `[object Object]`), and Zod objects strip unknown properties by default. Consequently, a sync response containing `access_token`, `expires_in`, and `refresh_token` loses the expiry and refresh token during parsing. Zoom then computes an invalid expiry, and Office 365 cannot retain the returned expiry. Define explicit supported fields or use an appropriate catchall/passthrough schema.

title: Google refresh persists the parse-result wrapper instead of credentials
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a safeParse result shaped as `{ success: true, data: ... }`, unlike the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` call, which returned the credential object itself. Saving that result directly as `Credential.key` removes the access token and other required fields from the top level. After the first successful refresh, subsequent GoogleCalendarService instances cannot parse the saved credentials. This also affects installations with credential syncing disabled; persist the parsed `.data` instead.

title: Sync refresh returns a Fetch Response to callers expecting SDK results
body: The sync branch returns an unparsed Fetch `Response`, while several callers expect the return shape of their original refresh function. Google reads `res.data`, Zoho CRM and Bigin read `tokenInfo.data`, and HubSpot reads `accessToken` and `expiresIn` directly. None of those properties exist on a Fetch Response. Enabling syncing therefore causes those integrations to throw or use undefined tokens even when the endpoint returns valid JSON. Normalize the sync response and adapt each caller to a defined return contract.

title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a dummy token
body: This fallback runs even when credential syncing is disabled. Office 365's response schema explicitly allows an omitted `refresh_token`; previously its merge preserved the existing usable refresh token in that case. The helper now inserts the literal `refresh_token`, which overwrites the stored token during the merge. The next refresh sends that dummy value to Microsoft and fails. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not return a replacement.

title: Import Prisma before updating Salesforce credentials
body: The new code calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this file does not import or declare `prisma`. This fails TypeScript checking and, if executed without checking, throws a ReferenceError after the token request succeeds. Import the Prisma client so Salesforce client initialization can complete.

title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
body: Salesforce unconditionally refreshes directly against Salesforce instead of using `refreshOAuthTokens`. When syncing is enabled, its parser nevertheless switches to the shared-response schema. Thus Salesforce never asks the configured parent application for refreshed credentials and continues independently refreshing its tokens, contrary to the source-of-truth behavior implemented for the other integrations. Apply the same endpoint routing here before selecting the shared-response parser.

title: Pass the Bigin credential owner's user ID, not the credential ID
body: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a Cal.com user ID and is sent to the parent application as `calcomUserId`. This caller passes `credentialId`, which identifies a credential row instead. Those IDs are independent, so the endpoint either cannot find the owner or returns tokens for a different user whose user ID happens to match. Carry `credential.userId` into this method and pass that value.

title: Use the actual Zoom app slug in sync requests
body: The refresh request sends `appSlug: "zoomvideo"`, but Zoom credentials are installed with `appId: "zoom"` and the webhook identifies apps by their database slug. A parent store using that same slug contract cannot match this refresh to the Zoom credentials it synced. Pass `"zoom"` rather than the integration directory name.

title: Make first-time credential synchronization atomic
body: The existence check and credential creation are separate operations, and user/app credentials are not unique. Two concurrent deliveries for a user's first sync can both find no credential and both create one. Future deliveries update only the arbitrary row returned by `findFirst`, leaving another credential stale and available to integration consumers. Serialize this operation or introduce an appropriate unique identity and atomic upsert so concurrent webhook deliveries cannot create duplicates.

title: The shared-response schema strips expiry and refresh-token fields
body: Using a Zod schema's toString() as a computed property name does not create a wildcard validator. These properties become literal keys (normally "[object Object]"), and z.object strips unrecognized fields. With credential sharing enabled, a response containing access_token, expires_in and refresh_token therefore loses its expiry and refresh token. Zoom subsequently calculates an invalid expiry, and Office 365 cannot retain the returned expiry. Define explicit response fields or use an appropriate catchall/passthrough schema.

title: Google refresh persists the safeParse result instead of credential data
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse wrapper { success: true, data: ... }, unlike the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse call, which returned the credentials themselves. Saving this wrapper as Credential.key removes access_token and the other expected fields from the top level. After any successful refresh, including with syncing disabled, the next GoogleCalendarService construction fails googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key). Persist the parsed data rather than the wrapper.

title: The sync branch returns a different response type from SDK refreshes
body: The sync branch returns an unparsed fetch Response, but several callers expect their refresh callback's SDK-specific return value. Google reads res.data, Zoho CRM and Bigin read tokenInfo.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken/expiresIn directly. A fetch Response has none of those fields, so enabling syncing causes these integrations to throw or use undefined tokens even when the endpoint returns valid JSON. Normalize and decode the sync response into the contract expected by each caller.

title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a dummy token
body: The helper inserts the literal "refresh_token" whenever the response omits refresh_token, even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365CalendarService accepts refresh responses without a new refresh token and merges parsed fields into its existing credentials; this new dummy field overwrites the valid stored refresh token. The next refresh then sends the dummy value to Microsoft and fails. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not return a replacement.

title: Import Prisma before using the new credential update
body: The new refresh path calls prisma.credential.update, but this file has no prisma import or declaration. This fails TypeScript checking and, if executed without checking, throws ReferenceError after Salesforce successfully returns a token. Import the Prisma client used by the other integration services.

title: Salesforce refresh bypasses the configured credential-sync endpoint
body: The new Salesforce refresh unconditionally posts to Salesforce rather than using refreshOAuthTokens. Thus, even with credential sharing and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT configured, Cal.com independently refreshes the provider token and requires a locally stored refresh token. An external app store supplying only an access token cannot keep this integration working, and it is not the source of truth for refreshes as it is for the other integrations. Route this refresh through the sync helper.

title: Pass the Bigin credential owner's user ID, not its credential ID
body: refreshOAuthTokens treats its third argument as a user ID and sends it as calcomUserId, but Bigin passes credentialId. Credential IDs and user IDs are unrelated, so a sync endpoint will either fail to locate the account or return another user's token when the numbers happen to match. Carry credential.userId through to this call while retaining credentialId only for the database update.

title: Use the installed Zoom app slug in sync requests
body: The refresh request sends appSlug="zoomvideo", while the Zoom OAuth callback creates credentials with appId="zoom" and the new webhook resolves applications by their actual slug. A parent app store using that same slug to look up credentials cannot resolve this refresh request. Send "zoom" consistently with the credential and webhook contracts.

title: The advertised minimal sync response is incompatible with provider parsers
body: The helper says the sync endpoint should return only an access token and expiry, but its fetch-based callers still require provider-specific response structures. Webex validates scope, token_type, refresh_token and refresh_token_expires_in; Lark requires a success code and nested data containing refresh-token expiry fields. An endpoint implementing the stated minimal contract cannot refresh either integration. Add adapters that merge the minimal response with existing credentials, or define and document the provider-specific contract actually required.

title: The shared response schema strips expiry and other token fields
body: Using a Zod schema's `.toString()` as a computed property name does not define a wildcard property validator; it creates a literal key such as `[object Object]`. Zod objects also strip unrecognized properties by default. Consequently, a normal shared response containing `access_token` and `expires_in` or `expiry_date` loses its expiry and refresh-token fields. Consumers such as Zoom then calculate an invalid expiry from `undefined`, preventing shared credentials from being refreshed and persisted correctly. Define explicit supported expiry fields and preserve the fields consumers need.

title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a literal placeholder
body: This assignment also runs when credential sharing is disabled. Office365's refresh response schema explicitly allows the provider to omit `refresh_token`, in which case the existing token must be retained. The helper instead supplies the literal string `refresh_token`, which Office365CalendarService merges into the stored credentials, overwriting the valid token. The next refresh then fails and requires reconnection. Preserve the existing token when the response does not contain a replacement.

title: Normalize shared responses to the return contract expected by callers
body: The shared branch returns an unparsed Fetch `Response`, whereas several wrapped refresh functions return already-decoded SDK or Axios results. GoogleCalendarService reads `res.data`, the Zoho services read `tokenInfo.data`, and HubSpot reads `accessToken` and `expiresIn` directly. None of those properties exist on a Fetch `Response`, regardless of the JSON returned by the configured endpoint. Enabling sharing therefore breaks refreshes for these integrations. Decode and adapt shared responses, or make each caller explicitly handle a common response contract.

title: Persist parsed Google credentials rather than the safeParse result
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the complete `safeParse` result, shaped as `{ success: true, data: ... }`, unlike the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` call, which returned credentials directly. This result is assigned to `key` and written into the credential JSON. Even with sharing disabled, the first successful Google refresh stores tokens underneath `data`; the next service construction fails because `googleCredentialSchema` expects token fields at the top level. Persist the parsed `.data` instead.

title: Import Prisma before using it in the Salesforce refresh path
body: The new refresh code calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this file does not import or declare `prisma`. This causes a TypeScript compilation error and, if type checking is bypassed, a ReferenceError whenever the Salesforce client is initialized. Add the Prisma client import.

title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured credential source
body: The newly added Salesforce refresh unconditionally contacts Salesforce using the locally stored refresh token instead of calling `refreshOAuthTokens`. Thus Salesforce never uses `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, even when sharing is enabled. Shared credentials whose refresh tokens are managed only by the parent platform cannot initialize a Salesforce client. This also performs a direct provider refresh before jsforce is constructed with the old access token, rather than using the token just fetched. Use the configured refresh source and initialize the connection with its refreshed credentials.

title: Send the Bigin credential owner's user ID, not the credential ID
body: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a Cal.com user ID, but Bigin passes `credentialId`. The helper sends this value as `calcomUserId`, so the parent platform looks up credentials for the wrong user whenever credential and user IDs differ. This can either fail the refresh or select another user's Bigin account. Passing a credential ID also makes team credentials enter the user-sharing branch despite having no user owner. Thread `credential.userId` through this refresh method.

title: Use the actual Zoom app slug in shared refresh requests
body: The shared refresh request identifies the app as `zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are created with appId `zoom`, and its installed-app slug is also `zoom`. A parent endpoint keyed by the same app slugs accepted by the credential webhook cannot find the Zoom credential under `zoomvideo`. Send `zoom` so webhook imports and refresh requests identify the same app.

title: Clear the invalid flag when replacing credentials
body: Updating an existing credential replaces only its key. Integrations such as Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credentials `invalid: true` after unrecoverable authorization failures. Sending valid replacement credentials through this webhook leaves that flag set, so the replacement does not restore the integration for consumers that exclude invalid credentials. Clear `invalid` when accepting a valid replacement.

title: Make first-time credential synchronization atomic
body: The existence check and credential creation are separate operations with no locking or uniqueness enforcement. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user and app can both find no credential and each create a row. Subsequent deliveries update only one arbitrary row through `findFirst`, leaving another credential stale; calendar integrations can then see duplicate or obsolete accounts. Use an atomic identity constraint/upsert or serialize creation for the intended user/app identity.

title: Use the booking organizer's credentials for calendar updates
body: The handler permits attendees and team administrators to add guests, but constructs EventManager with the caller and the caller's credentials. When the caller is not the organizer, these credentials cannot update the organizer's existing calendar event; they may also target the caller's calendar instead. Load the booking owner's credentials and initialize EventManager for that owner so that adding guests actually updates the calendar event associated with the booking.

title: Authorize team administrators or owners, not both
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&. A team administrator who is not the owner therefore fails this check and receives FORBIDDEN unless they are also the organizer or an attendee. Use an OR check to grant the intended access to either team role.

title: Deduplicate guests on the server before inserting attendees
body: uniqueGuests only removes addresses already present in the booking; it does not remove repeated addresses within the request. The server schema accepts duplicate strings, so a direct mutation with the same new email twice passes validation and sends both entries to createMany, producing duplicate attendees or an insertion failure if a database constraint rejects them. The uniqueness refinement in the dialog does not protect the API. Enforce uniqueness in the server schema or deduplicate before insertion.

title: Normalize guest addresses when applying the blacklist
body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is converted to lowercase, but each submitted guest is compared without normalization. A blacklisted address submitted with uppercase characters passes the email schema and bypasses the blacklist, allowing an invitation to the blocked mailbox. Normalize submitted addresses before the blacklist comparison and use the same normalization for duplicate detection.

title: Respect disabled standard-email settings when adding guests
body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally sends organizer and attendee emails and does not accept event-type metadata. Other booking notification functions in this file honor disableStandardEmails.all.host and disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding guests consequently sends standard notifications even for event types whose owners explicitly disabled them, potentially duplicating custom workflow notifications. Pass the event-type metadata from the handler and apply the existing host and attendee suppression checks.

title: Provide recovery when calendar synchronization fails after insertion
body: New attendees are committed to the database before updateCalendarAttendees is awaited. If calendar synchronization throws, the mutation returns an error even though the guests were added, and notification emails are never attempted. Retrying the same request then filters out those guests and returns BAD_REQUEST, so the normal retry path cannot repair the calendar or deliver their invitations. Make synchronization retryable for already-added guests or otherwise handle partial completion explicitly rather than leaving the booking permanently out of sync after an error.

title: Update calendars using the booking organizer's credentials
body: The handler allows attendees and team administrators to add guests, but constructs EventManager with the caller and the caller's credentials. When the caller is not the booking organizer, those credentials do not authorize updates to the organizer's existing calendar event. Guests are already persisted before this update is attempted, so the booking can gain attendees while the actual calendar invitation remains unchanged or the mutation fails. Use the booking organizer's credentials for the calendar update.

title: Authorize team administrators or owners rather than requiring both
body: The isTeamAdminOrOwner check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&. This requires the caller to satisfy both role checks instead of either one. A team administrator who is neither the organizer nor an attendee is consequently rejected with FORBIDDEN when trying to add guests to a team booking. Combine the role checks with OR.

title: Deduplicate incoming guests on the server
body: uniqueGuests only removes addresses already present in the booking; it does not remove repetitions within the submitted guests array. The server schema accepts duplicate addresses, so a direct API request containing the same new address twice passes validation and sends both entries to createMany. This can create duplicate attendees and duplicate invitations despite the UI's uniqueness validation. Enforce uniqueness server-side before inserting attendees.

title: Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist
body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased, but incoming guest addresses are compared without lowercasing them. Zod's email validation accepts uppercase characters, so submitting a mixed-case version of a blacklisted address bypasses the blacklist and receives an invitation. Normalize incoming addresses before applying the blacklist and existing-attendee checks.

title: Respect event-type email suppression when adding guests
body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally emails the organizer and every attendee, unlike the adjacent scheduling and location-change flows that honor disableStandardEmails metadata. The handler also does not pass event-type metadata to this function. Adding a guest therefore sends standard emails even for event types whose host or attendee notifications have explicitly been disabled. Accept the metadata and apply the existing host and attendee suppression checks.

title: Handle seated bookings through the seat allocation flow
body: This mutation accepts seated bookings but inserts ordinary attendees without checking seatsPerTimeSlot or creating seat references. The new action is also exposed for these bookings. As a result, callers can add attendees beyond the configured capacity, and those attendees have no seat reference for the seat-specific cancellation and rescheduling links used by the booking UI. Either reject seated bookings in this flow or allocate guests through the seat-booking logic with capacity checks and seat references.

title: Reject guest additions to inactive or unconfirmed bookings
body: The handler checks permissions and guest addresses but never checks the booking status. An authorized caller can invoke it for a cancelled or rejected booking, after which new guests receive AttendeeScheduledEmail and existing attendees receive an ICS request marked CONFIRMED. Pending bookings can likewise receive confirmed invitations without being approved. Validate that the booking is in a supported status before inserting guests or issuing calendar updates and notifications.

title: Allow team admins or owners rather than requiring both roles
body: The permission check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, although either role should authorize managing a team booking. A team administrator who is neither the booking organizer nor an attendee will therefore receive FORBIDDEN. Use an OR check so administrators and owners can add guests to their team's bookings.

title: Use the booking organizer's credentials for calendar updates
body: This handler permits attendees and team administrators to add guests, but constructs EventManager with the logged-in user's identity and credentials. When someone other than the organizer invokes it, those credentials do not authorize updating the organizer's existing calendar event. The database attendee insertion has already completed, so this can leave Cal.com's guest list updated while the organizer's calendar remains unchanged, or fail the request after persisting the guests. Resolve the calendar credentials from the booking organizer instead.

title: Deduplicate guests on the server before inserting attendees
body: The uniqueGuests filter only excludes addresses already present in the booking; it does not remove duplicates within the submitted guests array. The server schema accepts duplicate addresses, so a direct request with the same new email twice passes validation and supplies two identical attendees to createMany. This can create duplicate attendee records and notifications, or fail the insertion if a database uniqueness constraint rejects them. Enforce uniqueness server-side rather than relying on the dialog's validation.

title: Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist
body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is converted to lowercase, but submitted guest addresses are compared without normalization. The email validator accepts uppercase characters, so submitting a case variant of a blacklisted address bypasses this restriction and causes an invitation to be sent to the blocked mailbox. Normalize incoming addresses for the blacklist comparison and existing-attendee checks.

title: Honor event-type email suppression when sending guest updates
body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally emails the organizer and every attendee and does not accept event-type metadata. Other booking notification functions in this file honor disableStandardEmails.all.host and disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding guests therefore sends standard notifications even for event types whose owners disabled them, potentially duplicating workflow emails. Pass the event-type metadata from the handler and apply the same suppression checks.

title: Validate booking status before sending confirmed invitations
body: The handler checks that the booking exists but never checks its status. An authorized caller can add guests to a cancelled or rejected booking, after which the new email templates send calendar REQUEST attachments with status CONFIRMED and new guests receive scheduled-booking emails. Pending bookings can also reach this action through the existing past-pending edit menu. Reject unsupported booking statuses, or use status-appropriate notification behavior, rather than inviting people to events that are not confirmed.

title: Increment the retry counter atomically
body: Both failure paths write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read before processing the batch. If cron invocations overlap and both fail to schedule the same reminder with retryCount 0, both write 1, so two failed attempts are recorded as only one and the reminder is retried again instead of being deleted. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both paths to avoid losing failed attempts.

title: Do not let failure bookkeeping abort the entire reminder batch
body: The new database update inside the catch block can itself throw, but has no error handling. For example, if a reminder is deleted while the Twilio request is in flight, the update fails because the record no longer exists; a database error in the preceding update can likewise recur here. Previously these per-reminder errors were logged and processing continued. Now the handler exits before processing any remaining reminders, so one failed bookkeeping update prevents unrelated SMS reminders from being scheduled. Handle bookkeeping failures separately so the loop can continue.

title: Increment the retry counter atomically
body: Both failure paths write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value fetched before processing the batch. If two cron invocations overlap and both fail to schedule the same reminder, they can both read 0 and write 1, losing one failure. The reminder then survives despite having failed twice and receives additional scheduling attempts. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths rather than assigning a value from the stale snapshot.

title: Keep retry bookkeeping failures from aborting the entire batch
body: The catch block now awaits a database update without handling errors from that update. If the reminder has been deleted while scheduling was in progress (for example, by an overlapping cron's expired-reminder cleanup), Prisma's update throws because the row no longer exists. A database outage can likewise make both the original update and this recovery update fail. That exception escapes the per-reminder catch, aborting the handler and leaving every remaining reminder in the batch unprocessed; previously the catch logged the error and continued. Handle failures of the retry-count update separately so one reminder's bookkeeping failure does not stop the batch.

title: Increment the retry counter atomically
body: Both failure paths write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read before processing the batch. If cron invocations overlap, two failed scheduling attempts can read the same count and overwrite each other with the same incremented value. The reminder then survives more than the intended two failures. Use Prisma's atomic `increment` operation in both failure paths so each failed attempt is recorded.

title: Keep retry bookkeeping failures from aborting the entire batch
body: The new database update inside the catch block is itself unprotected. If a `workflowReminder.update` in the try block fails because the database is unavailable, the catch immediately attempts another update that can fail for the same reason, escaping the loop and aborting the request. A reminder deleted while scheduling is in flight similarly causes both updates to fail. Previously these per-reminder errors were logged and processing continued; now one such error prevents all remaining reminders in the batch from being attempted. Handle failures of the retry-count update separately, including reminders that no longer exist.

title: Removing findMany breaks the existing service API
body: The service previously exposed findMany(args), which executed a query with authorization and filter conditions applied. This change removes that method and replaces it with getBaseConditions(), which returns SQL rather than query results. Existing consumers of findMany will no longer compile (or will throw at runtime), and consumers of the condition-building methods must also switch from Prisma where inputs to raw SQL. This PR only updates the service and its integration tests; retain a compatible query method or migrate the consumers together with this API change.

title: Keep the returned base predicate grouped when no filters are present
body: For team and organization scopes with members, authConditions contains two branches joined by OR. When no service filters are supplied, getBaseConditions returns that expression without enclosing parentheses. Composing it as `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <date/status condition>` therefore applies the additional condition only to the second branch, because AND binds more tightly than OR. Team bookings in the first branch can then be counted outside the requested date range or status. Return an enclosing parenthesized predicate in this path as well, so the base conditions remain a single expression when used in a larger raw query.

title: Migrate callers before removing the findMany API
body: This replaces the public `findMany(args)` method with `getBaseConditions()`, but the PR only migrates the integration test and includes no production caller updates or compatibility method. Existing callers of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` will fail TypeScript compilation (or throw `findMany is not a function` at runtime). Keep a compatible query method or migrate all consumers to execute raw queries with the new conditions in the same change.

title: Group the authorization predicate before returning it without filters
body: When no service filters are supplied, getBaseConditions() returns the authorization SQL without enclosing parentheses. For team and organization scopes with members, that SQL contains a top-level OR. A raw query composed as `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <date/status condition>` therefore applies the additional condition only to the personal-booking branch, while all authorized team bookings bypass it. The previous Prisma where object preserved the grouping automatically. Return `Prisma.sql` with parentheses around the authorization expression so consumers can safely combine the base predicate with other query conditions.

title: Invalidate calendar status after deleting the cache
body: The cache-deletion success handler does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query; it only invokes an optional onSuccess callback. The wrapper passes its optional onChanged prop rather than refetching this query, and the query disables refetching on window focus. With no callback that explicitly refreshes calendar data, successful deletion leaves the old cache timestamp and delete action visible. Invalidate viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars after deletion so the displayed cache status reflects the database.

title: Explicitly set updatedAt when touching selected calendars
body: Passing an empty data object to Prisma updateMany does not advance an @updatedAt field: Prisma leaves the timestamp unchanged for an empty update. Consequently, this new call does not record the cache refresh in SelectedCalendar.updatedAt as its comment claims. Pass an explicit updatedAt value if this tracking is needed, or remove the ineffective call.

title: Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache
body: The cache deletion success handler only invokes the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper passes its optional external onChanged callback rather than a query refetch, and disables refetchOnWindowFocus. When no refetching callback is supplied, successful deletion therefore leaves the old cache timestamp and deletion action visible until the page is reloaded. Invalidate utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars on success, as the disconnect mutation already does.

title: Use an in-place edit command that also works on Linux
body: The command `sed -i '' -E ...` uses BSD/macOS syntax. With GNU sed on Linux, the empty argument is treated as the script or an input filename and the command fails instead of updating an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL entry. The script does not check the exit status and still prints that the URL was updated, leaving webhook tests pointed at the old tunnel. Use a portable edit strategy or select the appropriate sed syntax for the host platform.

title: Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache
body: The cache-deletion mutation only invokes the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper does not refetch that query itself, and its onChanged callback is optional and window-focus refetching is disabled. Consequently, a successful deletion leaves the old cache timestamp and deletion action visible until another refetch or page reload. Invalidate connectedCalendars on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

title: An empty update does not advance SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
body: Passing an empty data object to Prisma updateMany does not update an @updatedAt field: empty updates leave the timestamp unchanged. Thus this new call does not record successful cache refreshes in SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, contrary to its stated purpose. Pass an explicit updatedAt timestamp, or remove the call if this tracking is no longer needed.

title: Use a sed invocation that works on Linux
body: The command uses BSD/macOS syntax, sed -i '', which fails with GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists in the environment file, the script therefore leaves the previous URL unchanged but still prints that it updated the file successfully. Subsequent webhook subscriptions use the stale tunnel URL. Use a portable replacement mechanism or handle GNU and BSD sed separately, and check that the update succeeded.

title: Cancel imminent reminders immediately instead of waiting for cron
body: Scheduled emails are now only marked cancelled, even when their send time is before the next 15-minute cron run. For example, cancelling a booking two minutes before its reminder is due leaves the email scheduled in SendGrid until after it has been sent; the cron then deletes the expired database row before attempting cancellation. Reminders near their send time need an immediate cancellation path rather than unconditional deferral.

title: Rescheduling bypasses the deferred cancellation mechanism
body: Rescheduling passes immediateDelete=true for every scheduled email, so cancellations for reminders days in the future still occupy SendGrid's limited pending-cancellation slots until their scheduled dates. This recreates the 100-pending-cancellation failure described in the PR. When that immediate request fails, deleteScheduledEmailReminder only logs the error and never sets cancelled=true, so the cron cannot retry it and the old booking's reminder is still sent. Rescheduling needs the same durable, deferred cancellation mechanism as booking cancellation, except where immediate cancellation is necessary.

title: Persist successful cancellations before processing the next reminder
body: Database deletions are accumulated as lazy Prisma promises and executed only after every SendGrid cancellation succeeds. If any request in the loop fails, execution jumps to the outer catch, no successful cancellation is removed from the database, and all subsequent reminders are skipped. The next run consequently retries already-cancelled batches as well as the failed batch, which can fail again and block the remaining reminders until they are sent. Handle failures per reminder and persist each successful cancellation independently.

title: Await reminder cancellation work before returning the response
body: The reminder cancellation helpers are invoked in nested forEach callbacks without awaiting their promises or including them in prismaPromises. Unlike the previous implementation, there is now no awaited database operation that deletes unscheduled reminders or durably marks scheduled emails cancelled. The request can therefore return while these essential writes and SMS cancellations are still running; in a serverless deployment they can be suspended when the response completes, leaving reminders active for a successfully cancelled booking. Collect and await these promises before completing the cancellation request.

title: Cancel imminent reminders without waiting for the cron job
body: Scheduled emails are now only marked cancelled, even when their send time is before the next 15-minute cron run. For example, an email due at 10:10 for a booking cancelled at 10:01 after the 10:00 run will still be sent. At 10:15, scheduleEmailReminders deletes the expired reminder before attempting cancellation, so it never contacts SendGrid for that email. Reminders close to their send time need an immediate cancellation path.

title: Do not bypass deferred cancellation for every reschedule
body: Passing immediateDelete=true cancels every old rescheduled-booking email immediately in SendGrid, including emails scheduled days ahead. Those cancellations remain pending until their original send dates and consume the same 100-pending-cancellation limit identified in this PR. Once that limit is reached, the helper catches the failure without setting cancelled=true, leaving the old reminder scheduled with no cron retry. Rescheduling therefore still exhausts the cancellation quota and sends obsolete reminders.

title: Isolate cancellation failures and persist each successful cancellation
body: The entire cancellation loop shares one try/catch, and its Prisma deletes are lazy promises executed only after every SendGrid request succeeds. If any request fails, all later reminders are skipped and none of the earlier successful cancellations are removed from the database. A persistent failure can consequently block unrelated cancellations on every run until their emails are sent. Handle errors per reminder and execute each database deletion after its corresponding successful cancellation.

title: Await reminder cancellation before completing the booking cancellation
body: The reminder helpers now perform the database update or deletion themselves, but their returned promises are discarded by the nested forEach calls. Previously, database reminder deletions were included in the awaited Promise.all. The handler can now report a successful cancellation while its cancelled flags or unscheduled-reminder deletions are still pending; in a serverless request those operations can be interrupted after the response, leaving reminders eligible to be sent. Collect and await these helper promises, including the equivalent requestReschedule calls.

title: Deferred cancellation misses reminders due before the next cron run
body: Cancellation now only marks a scheduled email as cancelled, leaving SendGrid cancellation to this 15-minute cron job. If a booking is cancelled at 10:01 and its reminder is due at 10:10, SendGrid sends it before the next run at 10:15. That run also deletes the expired reminder record before querying cancellations, so it never attempts cancellation. Reminders close to their send time need immediate cancellation rather than relying exclusively on the cron job.

title: Rescheduling bypasses the deferred cancellation mechanism
body: Passing immediateDelete=true cancels the old email in SendGrid immediately, even when its send date is days away. These cancellations remain pending until their scheduled dates and consume the same 100-pending-cancellation quota described in this PR. Once the quota is exhausted, deleteScheduledEmailReminder catches the failure without marking the reminder cancelled, so the cron job cannot retry it and the old booking's reminder is sent. Rescheduling needs to persist cancellation intent and use the deferred mechanism too.

title: Await reminder cancellation persistence before completing the request
body: The cancellation helpers are asynchronous, but their returned promises are discarded by both nested forEach calls and are not included in the final Promise.all. Previously, deletion of the reminder records was awaited. The handler can now report successful cancellation while the cancelled flag or unscheduled-reminder deletion is still pending; in a serverless deployment, outstanding work can be suspended when the response finishes, leaving reminders eligible to send. Collect and await these promises before returning. The request-reschedule handler has the same issue.

title: Isolate cancellation failures and commit each successful cancellation
body: A single failed SendGrid request exits the entire cancellation loop, preventing every subsequent reminder from being cancelled in that run. Furthermore, the Prisma delete operations collected for earlier successful cancellations are lazy promises and are only executed by Promise.all after the loop; an exception skips that call, leaving all those records in the queue too. A persistently failing batch can therefore block other cancellations until their emails are sent. Handle errors per reminder and await deletion immediately after each successful cancellation.

title: Await the async reschedule cleanup callbacks
body: `forEach` discards the promises returned by these new async callbacks, so the surrounding try/catch no longer catches failures from `getCalendar`, including calendar-service constructor errors that were previously thrown synchronously. Such failures now become unhandled rejections while the function continues sending the reschedule email and returns success. Await a `Promise.all` over mapped callbacks (or use an awaited loop) so initialization and deletion failures reach the error handler. The same change is needed in `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts`.

title: Await the asynchronous reschedule cleanup callbacks
body: The async callbacks passed to forEach are discarded, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch failures from the newly asynchronous getCalendar call, including module-loading and CalendarService-construction errors. Previously, synchronous initialization errors reached this catch; now they become unhandled promise rejections while Reschedule proceeds to send email and report success. Await Promise.all over a map, or use an awaited loop, so initialization and cleanup failures are handled. The same change is needed in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.

title: Defer import calls until an app is requested
body: Every import() expression in this object executes immediately when the app-store index is evaluated. Consequently, requesting a single calendar or payment provider still starts loading and evaluating all app packages, including unused providers; awaiting one property does not make the other imports lazy. This retains the all-app startup work the change is intended to avoid. Store loader functions (and optionally cache their promises) instead, and invoke only the selected loader.

title: Await the asynchronous reschedule cleanup callbacks
body: The new async callback is passed to forEach, which discards its returned promise. Errors from the newly asynchronous getCalendar call—including CalendarService constructor errors that previously reached the surrounding try/catch—now become unhandled rejections instead of being logged. The reschedule operation also proceeds without waiting for calendar initialization and deletion. Await Promise.all over mapped callbacks, or use an awaited loop inside the try block. The same conversion in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and the viewer bookings requestReschedule mutation needs the same treatment.

title: Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts
body: When an override exists for the slot's date, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before checking the host's busy intervals. A date override specifies working availability, not permission to ignore existing bookings or calendar events. Consequently, both fixed and round-robin hosts with overrides are treated as available even when they already have a conflicting booking. Continue through the busy-time checks after validating the override.

title: Require the entire slot to fit within an override
body: The override checks only reject slots ending before the override starts or starting after it ends; overlapping slots are accepted even when they extend outside the override. For example, a fixed host's 10:00–11:00 UTC override permits a round-robin candidate at 09:30–10:30 or 10:30–11:30, and even a slot starting exactly at 11:00. Candidate slots generated from another host's availability can therefore be offered when the fixed host is unavailable. Validate that the slot start and end are both contained in an allowed interval.

title: Check membership in any working interval instead of rejecting against each interval
body: The new working-hours check rejects a slot if any interval on that weekday does not contain its start. For a normal split schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected against the afternoon interval and a 15:00 slot is rejected against the morning interval, removing all availability. Conversely, a weekday with no intervals falls through as available, and the end calculation repeats the slot start rather than using slotEndTime. Require the entire slot to fit within at least one working interval; this is especially important for fixed hosts whose availability must constrain candidates generated by other hosts.

title: Preserve the date when shifting override times across midnight
body: The timezone conversion reduces the shifted override start and end to hour/minute values, discarding any change of date, while activeOverrides is still selected using the unconverted override.start. For example, an Asia/Kolkata override on date D from 01:00–02:00 should appear to a UTC attendee on D−1 from 19:30–20:30. This code selects it for D and adds 19:30–20:30 to D instead, offering availability a day late and omitting the real slots. Convert the complete override interval to actual instants and intersect it with the attendee's day before deriving minute boundaries.

title: Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts
body: When a slot falls on a date with an override, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before evaluating the host's busy intervals. An override defines working availability; it does not make existing bookings or calendar events available. Consequently, both fixed and round-robin hosts can be offered for slots that conflict with existing commitments. Accepted override slots must still pass the busy-time check.

title: Override validation accepts partially overlapping slots
body: The override checks only reject slots ending before the override starts or starting after it ends. They do not require the entire event to fit inside the override, and even a slot starting exactly at the override's end passes. For example, a fixed host with a 10:00–11:00 override is considered available for a 10:30–11:30 event generated from another host's availability. Require full containment within an override interval before considering the host available.

title: Working-hours validation rejects valid split schedules
body: The workingHours.find predicate rejects a slot if it is outside any working interval for the weekday, rather than accepting it if it fits one interval. With ordinary split availability of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected for being outside the afternoon interval, and a 14:00 slot is rejected for being outside the morning interval. This removes all available slots for such hosts. Validate membership in at least one applicable interval instead; a weekday with no applicable intervals should also be unavailable.

title: Working-hours end check uses the slot start time
body: The end variable is calculated from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime. This lets events extend past a host's working-hours boundary as long as their start is inside it. In particular, when another host's date override generates additional candidates, a fixed host working until 11:00 can pass this check for a 10:30–11:30 event. Compare the actual event end against the working interval's end.

title: Timezone conversion drops overrides that cross attendee midnight
body: The converted override endpoints are reduced to hour/minute values, discarding their dates. An override from 22:00–23:00 UTC viewed in UTC+1 becomes startTime 1380 and endTime 0. buildSlots treats that as an invalid range and produces no slots, although 23:00–00:00 is valid availability. Preserve the converted day boundaries and split ranges at attendee midnight instead of wrapping the end back to zero.

title: Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts
body: When an override exists for the slot's date, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before evaluating busy. An availability override does not make existing calendar events or bookings disappear. For example, a host with a 10:00–12:00 override and an existing 10:00–11:00 booking is now reported as available at 10:00. This affects both fixed hosts and round-robin hosts and exposes conflicting slots for booking. Continue checking busy after validating override availability.

title: Require the entire slot to fit within an override
body: The override checks reject slots entirely before the override or starting after its end, but accept slots that only partially overlap it. With a fixed host's 10:00–11:00 override, a 09:30–10:30 or 10:30–11:30 candidate generated from another round-robin host passes this check. A slot starting exactly at 11:00 also passes because isAfter excludes equality. Consequently, the fixed host can still be booked outside their override. Validate that the slot starts at or after the override start and ends at or before its end.

title: Treat multiple override ranges as alternatives
body: dateOverrides.find returns a rejecting range as soon as a slot is outside any override on that date. If a host has overrides of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected by the afternoon range, while a 14:00 slot is rejected by the morning range. Valid split-day overrides therefore lose their available slots. The check should accept a slot contained in any override range for that date, rather than reject it for being outside another range.

title: Do not reject slots outside a different working-hours range
body: The workingHours.find predicate rejects a slot if it is outside any working-hours range for its weekday. For a normal split schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, every morning slot is outside the afternoon range and every afternoon slot is outside the morning range, so all valid slots are filtered out. This is a regression for personal events as well as team events because this check now runs for their hosts. Determine whether any applicable range contains the slot instead.

title: Check the slot's actual end against working hours
body: The variable end is calculated from slotStartTime, exactly like start, instead of from slotEndTime. As a result, this check permits an event to extend beyond a host's working-hours end. For example, a fixed host available until 11:00 passes a 10:30–11:30 candidate generated from another host's availability. Compare the actual event end with the working-hours boundary so the entire event fits in the host's schedule.

title: Migration fails when no embed category is configured
body: The category query is indexed with `[0]['id']` before checking whether it returned any rows. Sites using the default empty embed_category, sites without that setting stored, and sites whose configured category was deleted will return no rows and raise instead of reaching the uncategorized fallback. This prevents otherwise valid installations from completing the upgrade. Handle an empty result before accessing the first row.

title: Normalize existing hosts before inserting them
body: The migration copies old host entries verbatim through SQL, bypassing the new model's normalization callback. The previous host check explicitly supported entries such as `https://eviltrout.com`, but the new lookup compares the stored value directly with URI.host (`eviltrout.com`). Such entries are migrated successfully but no longer authorize embedding or topic retrieval. Normalize the migrated entries before deleting the old settings so existing supported configurations continue to work.

title: Hosts saved with a port can never match
body: The host validator accepts values such as `example.com:8080`, and normalization preserves the port, but record_for_host extracts only URI.host and queries for `example.com`. Consequently, an allowed host saved with a port never authorizes any request, including requests from that exact host and port, and its category mapping is never used. Make storage and lookup use the same host/port representation.

title: Host validation rejects valid longer top-level domains
body: The top-level domain is limited to two through five letters, rejecting valid domains such as `example.museum`, `example.online`, and `example.technology`. Administrators cannot add these sites to the embedding allowlist even though they are valid hosts. Use hostname validation that supports current top-level domains rather than this length restriction.

title: Prevent multiple category mappings for the same host
body: There is no host uniqueness validation or database constraint, so the Add Host action can save the same hostname multiple times with different categories, including case variants. record_for_host selects only the first matching row, so editing another displayed mapping has no effect on where imported topics are posted, and deleting one row may leave the host authorized by another. Enforce uniqueness on the normalized, case-insensitive hostname so each displayed relationship has an unambiguous effect.

title: Migration fails when no embed category is configured
body: The category query is indexed with `[0]['id']` before checking whether it returned a row. When `embed_category` is unset, blank, or names a deleted category, the join returns no rows and accessing row zero raises instead of reaching the uncategorized fallback. This prevents ordinary installations that have never configured embedding from upgrading. Check for an empty result before reading the ID, and handle a missing uncategorized setting row as well.

title: Normalize existing hosts before inserting them
body: The migration copies host strings directly into the table, bypassing the new model's scheme/path normalization. The previous implementation explicitly accepted entries such as `https://eviltrout.com`, but the new lookup compares the stored value with only `URI(url).host`. Such migrated entries will never match, so existing embeds stop working after upgrading, and the original setting is then deleted. Normalize migrated hosts using the same rules as newly created records.

title: Valid domains with longer top-level names cannot be configured
body: The host validator limits the final domain label to two through five letters. Valid domains such as `example.museum` and `example.technology` therefore cannot be added or saved in the embedding editor, even though they are usable HTTP hosts. Use domain validation that supports current top-level domains rather than imposing this length limit.

title: Accepted hosts containing ports never match requests
body: The validator accepts values such as `example.com:8080`, and normalization leaves the port intact, but `record_for_host` extracts only `uri.host`, which is `example.com`. Consequently, a successfully saved host with a port never authorizes embedding and never supplies its category during import. Make storage and lookup consistent about ports, or reject port-bearing entries rather than saving unusable configuration.

title: Duplicate hosts make category mappings ambiguous
body: There is no uniqueness validation or database constraint for hosts, so the editor can save the same hostname more than once with different categories. Imports select only the first matching record, ignoring the other mappings; editing a later duplicate can therefore appear successful while having no effect on where topics are posted. Enforce uniqueness on the normalized, case-insensitive hostname so each host has one unambiguous category mapping.

title: Handle an unset embed_category before indexing the query result
body: The category query can return no rows when embed_category is unset, blank, or names a deleted category. The migration indexes the first row before checking whether a category was found, so it raises instead of reaching the uncategorized fallback. This blocks upgrades for sites that have never configured embedding, as well as fresh database migrations. The fallback query also needs to tolerate a missing site-setting row.

title: Normalize legacy hosts when migrating them
body: The old embedding configuration accepted entries such as http://eviltrout.com and https://discourse.org, but this migration inserts those strings unchanged using SQL, bypassing the new model's normalization callback. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares the stored value with URI.host, which contains neither a scheme nor a path. Consequently, previously working scheme-prefixed hosts stop authorizing embeds and topic retrieval after the upgrade. Normalize migrated entries using the same rules as newly saved hosts before deleting the old setting.

title: Allow valid hosts with longer or internationalized TLDs
body: The hostname validator restricts the final label to two through five ASCII letters. Valid domains such as example.technology and domains with punycode TLDs therefore cannot be added or edited. The previous hostname lookup imposed no such restriction, so this also prevents administrators from saving some migrated hosts. Use hostname validation that accommodates valid DNS labels rather than this limited TLD pattern.

title: Make accepted port-qualified hosts match incoming URLs
body: The validator accepts and stores port-qualified hosts such as example.com:8080, but record_for_host extracts only URI.host from an incoming URL.
