For memory indexes, one completed index can receive watch updates and then be replaced in the cache by another build that did not include those updates, leaving search results stale. File-backed builds also compete to create the same directory and can fail. Use per-key locking or singleflight, with a cache recheck, so different keys can build concurrently without duplicating a build for the same key.

title: Synchronize the new TotalDocs call with cache writes
body: The new initialization log calls TotalDocs after starting the write-event consumer. That consumer can build an index for a previously unindexed namespace while TotalDocs iterates the Bleve backend's cache map without cacheMu. BuildIndex writes that map under a mutex, but an unlocked reader is still unsafe: this startup path can race and terminate the process with 'concurrent map iteration and map write'. Protect TotalDocs with the cache read lock or take a synchronized snapshot before counting.

title: Retain the stopped-state check in request handlers
body: Removing the Init checks also removes the request handlers' shutdown guard. Stop sets initErr to 'service is stopping' or 'service is stopped', which previously caused subsequent Create, Update, Delete, and other calls to fail before accessing the backend. These handlers now continue operating after Stop; in particular, writes can still succeed against the SQL backend even though its event pollers have been stopped, so those changes are no longer propagated to watchers or the search index. Keep an explicit lifecycle-state check even though initialization is now eager.

title: Serialize index creation per resource key
body: Locking only the cache assignment allows concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource. For example, a search and a write-event handler can both miss the cache and build separate in-memory indexes. If the event handler publishes its index and applies the event before the other build finishes, the other build can overwrite the cache with an older snapshot, losing the indexed update. GetIndex previously blocked behind the build lock, preventing this interleaving. Keep builds for different keys parallel, but coordinate creation and publication for the same key.

title: Synchronize TotalDocs with cache publication
body: The new startup log calls s.search.TotalDocs() after starting the write-event consumer. That consumer can build an index for a previously uncached resource and publish it concurrently. The Bleve implementation of TotalDocs iterates b.cache without taking cacheMu, so this new call can race with cache writes and terminate the process with 'concurrent map iteration and map write'. Protect the cache iteration with the read lock, or take a protected snapshot before counting documents.

title: Preserve rejection of requests after Stop
body: Removing the Init checks also removes the stopped-service guard: Stop sets s.initErr to a stopping/stopped error, which subsequent RPCs previously returned through Init. Create, Update, and Delete now proceed directly to the backend after Stop. In the SQL backend, Stop only cancels polling and leaves database operations usable, so these requests can successfully persist changes after the server has stopped processing watch/index events. Replace the lazy-initialization checks with an explicit lifecycle-state check rather than dropping this protection.

title: Call to passkey helper does not compile
body: UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without arguments, but UsernamePasswordForm defines only isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel). There is no zero-argument overload in its superclass hierarchy shown here, so the services module fails to compile. Pass the context user or provide the intended overload.

title: New passkey predicate disables passkeys for normal login
body: The new helper requires user != null, but a normal login starts with context.getUser() == null. Both authenticate() and the error challenge now use this helper to decide whether to call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(), so ordinary login pages no longer receive the conditional WebAuthn UI attributes or challenge. This removes passkey login precisely when it must discover the user's identity, preventing passkey-only users from logging in and breaking the existing initial-login tests. Preserve passkey setup for an unidentified user while also supporting re-authentication.

title: Pass the user to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled
body: This calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without arguments, but the method added to UsernamePasswordForm requires a UserModel argument. There is no zero-argument overload in the supplied hierarchy, so UsernameForm does not compile and the services module cannot build. Pass context.getUser() to the helper.

title: Keep conditional passkeys enabled before a user is identified
body: The new helper requires user != null, but ordinary login starts with context.getUser() == null. Both authenticate() and the error challenge now use this helper, so they no longer call fillContextForm() during ordinary username/password or username-only login. Consequently, the initial page lacks the conditional WebAuthn UI and challenge, breaking discoverable-passkey login and the existing tests that expect passkeys before entering a username. The predicate must support unidentified users as well as re-authentication.

title: Pass the user to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled
body: This calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without arguments, but the method added to UsernamePasswordForm requires a UserModel argument and there is no zero-argument overload in the class hierarchy shown here. The services module will not compile, preventing the application and the new tests from building.

title: Keep conditional passkeys enabled when no user is selected
body: The new helper requires user != null, but on a normal initial login context.getUser() is null. Both authenticate() and the error challenge now use this helper, so they no longer call fillContextForm() for ordinary username-less login. Consequently the login page loses its passkey form, challenge, and conditional UI, preventing discoverable-passkey login through these forms until a user has already been selected. Enable passkeys for an unidentified user as well as for re-authentication; the existing initial-login passkey tests exercise this regression.

title: Use stored enabled state when deciding login-cache invalidation
body: The original model passed here comes from getById(), which wraps organization-linked providers so that isEnabled() returns false while their organization (or the organization feature in the realm) is disabled. However, getForLogin() populates its cached ID set using the delegate's stored enabled state. For example, cache an enabled public organization provider, disable its organization, then change BROKER_PUBLIC to false. Both predicates here return false, so the cached login list is retained. Once the organization is enabled again, that now-private provider is still returned from the cache and displayed by OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean, which only rechecks isEnabled(). Compare the original and updated persisted provider states, rather than organization-aware enabled states, when deciding whether query membership changed.

title: Register cleanup for the actual provider aliases
body: The new test creates providers named idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-19, but every cleanup callback removes the literal alias "alias". The additional callback at line 425 has the same problem for idp-alias-20. These callbacks therefore do not remove the created providers and can fail with a not-found response during teardown. In particular, the realm-level providers survive organization cleanup and pollute subsequent tests or cause duplicate-alias failures on another run. Register each callback using the alias of the provider it created.

title: Compare stored login eligibility rather than organization-aware enabled state
body: The original model passed here comes from getById(), which wraps isEnabled() to return false when its organization is disabled (or organizations are disabled for the realm). The login query, however, selects IDs using the stored enabled flag. If a public, enabled organization IdP is already cached, its organization is disabled, and the IdP is then made hidden-on-login or link-only, both predicates here return false and invalidation is skipped. Re-enabling the organization leaves that IdP in the login cache; OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only rechecks isEnabled(), so it displays the now-hidden or link-only provider. Compare the original persisted eligibility flags without the organization-aware wrapper when deciding whether query membership changed.

title: Do not merge an old query after a concurrent invalidation
body: When an organization search is missing, this branch carries all results from the previously read query into a replacement tagged with a freshly obtained revision and current counter. A concurrent transaction can change an IdP's login eligibility or organization and invalidate the login cache after this request reads query but before invalidateObject() runs. The replacement then reinstates the old organization's stale ID set under the new revision, even though only the newly requested organization's results were reloaded. Subsequent logins can omit newly eligible providers or display hidden/link-only providers until another invalidation. Rebuild without the old query when its revision is no longer current, and ensure a concurrent invalidation cannot be bypassed by stamping stale results with the current counter.

title: Register cleanup for the actual provider alias
body: The new test registers every cleanup against the literal alias "alias", rather than the provider it just created ("idp-alias-0" through "idp-alias-19"). The additional registration at line 425 has the same problem for "idp-alias-20". Cleanup therefore attempts to delete a nonexistent provider and leaves the created providers behind, including realm-level providers that organization deletion cannot clean up. This can cause cleanup failures and contaminate later tests. Capture and use each created provider's actual alias.

title: Use stored enablement rather than organization-aware enablement for invalidation
body: The original model passed to this method comes from getById(), which wraps isEnabled() to return false when the associated organization is disabled. The updated model can also fail the login predicate because the update sets hideOnLogin or linkOnly. Consequently, both predicates can be false and this branch skips invalidation even though the IDP is still present in an existing login cache. For example, populate the cache for a public organization IDP, disable the organization, hide the IDP, and re-enable the organization. The cached ID remains, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only rechecks isEnabled(), so the hidden IDP is displayed again. Compare the persisted IDP flags independently of organization enablement when deciding whether query membership changed.

title: Do not republish an old query under a fresh revision
body: When adding an uncached organization search, this code copies all searches from the previously read query but publishes them using a revision obtained after invalidateObject() and the current counter. If another transaction changes login eligibility and invalidates this key between reading the old query and invalidateObject(), the old searches are copied back under the newer revision. For example, enabling an IDP can invalidate a cached empty organization result, only for a concurrent search for another organization to restore that empty result. Subsequent logins then omit the newly enabled provider until another invalidation or eviction. The merged query must retain or validate the revision of the original query rather than treating its old results as freshly loaded.

title: Register cleanup for the actual provider aliases
body: The test creates providers named idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-19, but every cleanup callback removes the literal alias "alias" instead. The same mistake occurs for idp-alias-20 at line 425. Cleanup therefore requests removal of nonexistent providers, which can fail with a not-found response, and leaves the created providers behind if the realm is reused. Capture each actual alias when registering its cleanup callback.

title: Reject ambiguous highest-priority crypto providers
body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200, so sorting does not resolve a classpath containing more than one of these providers. The first service-loader entry is silently selected instead of the previous initialization failure. In particular, a classpath containing both the default and FIPS providers can select the non-FIPS implementation based on classpath order. Reject ties at the highest priority, or introduce an explicit selection mechanism, so an ambiguous configuration cannot silently use the wrong cryptographic implementation.

title: Provide a compatible default for the new provider method
body: Adding order() as an abstract method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations: their source no longer compiles, and previously compiled implementations can throw AbstractMethodError when the new provider comparator invokes order(). This also prevents selection of a valid built-in provider when an older custom provider is discovered alongside it. A default implementation would allow existing providers to remain loadable while the built-in providers override their priorities.

title: Generate the appropriate EC curve for each algorithm
body: Every test generates a key using the JCA provider's default EC curve, which is normally P-256. Selecting SHA384withECDSA or SHA512withECDSA does not change that key's curve, so the ES384 and ES512 tests only pad P-256 signature components to larger output sizes. They never exercise actual P-384 or P-521 signatures, including the long-form DER sequence length needed for P-521. Initialize the key generator with the algorithm's corresponding curve and verify that the reconstructed DER signature validates the original data, rather than only comparing two conversions performed by the same implementation.

title: Reject ambiguous highest-priority crypto providers
body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200. When more than one is present, sorting leaves their relative order dependent on ServiceLoader discovery order and the first is silently selected. Previously this configuration failed explicitly. In particular, a classpath containing both the default and FIPS providers can now select the non-FIPS implementation instead of rejecting an ambiguous security configuration. Reject ties at the highest priority (while still allowing the lower-priority authz provider), or introduce an explicit selection mechanism.

title: Exercise the actual curves and verify the converted signatures
body: Every test generates the same default EC key, which is P-256 on the standard JDK provider. Selecting SHA384withECDSA or SHA512withECDSA does not change that key's curve, so the ES384 and ES512 tests merely pad P-256 signature components. Consequently, the ES512 test never exercises the long-form DER sequence length required by real P-521 signatures. The assertion also checks only the converter against itself, allowing a consistently incorrect conversion to pass. Generate keys explicitly using secp256r1, secp384r1, and secp521r1, and verify the reconstructed DER signature with JCA (or compare it with the original DER signature).

title: Reject signatures whose length differs from the expected JOSE length
body: concatenatedRSToASN1DER copies exactly signLength bytes without checking signature.length. An oversized input is therefore accepted and its suffix silently discarded, producing the same DER signature as the valid prefix. An undersized input instead throws an unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException rather than the declared IOException. JOSE ECDSA signatures must have exactly the expected fixed length; validate the input length before copying so malformed signatures cannot be normalized into valid ones.

title: Generate the matching EC curve for each algorithm test
body: All three tests generate an EC key pair using the JCA default curve, which is P-256 on the standard JDK provider. Selecting SHA384withECDSA or SHA512withECDSA changes the digest, not the curve, so the ES384 and ES512 tests merely pad P-256 signature values to larger widths. In particular, the ES512 test never exercises a real P-521 signature or the long-form ASN.1 sequence length that it requires. Initialize the generator with secp256r1, secp384r1, and secp521r1 respectively, and verify the reconstructed DER signature with JCA rather than relying only on a round trip through the two new conversion methods.

title: Global view permission bypasses client-specific denials
body: canView(ClientModel) returns true as soon as canView() grants the all-clients view permission, without evaluating permissions for the requested client. Consequently, an administrator granted view on all clients can still read a client whose client-specific view policy explicitly denies access. This defeats the specific-resource precedence implemented by hasPermission(ClientModel, String). Keep the administrative-role shortcut, but evaluate fine-grained view access through the client-specific permission lookup and its all-clients fallback.

title: Handle existing permission servers that lack the Clients resource
body: A realm initialized with FGAP V2 before this change has only the Users resource and the previous scopes. AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when the admin-permissions client already exists, so upgrading does not create the new Clients resource or client-only scopes. For such a realm, the fallback here returns null and is passed to findByResource, followed by an unconditional resource.getScopes() call if execution continues. Client permission checks can therefore fail instead of denying access, and the new client-only scopes cannot be used. Reconcile the schema for existing permission servers and guard against a missing fallback resource.

title: Global view permission bypasses client-specific denials
body: canView(ClientModel) returns true as soon as canView() grants the all-clients view permission, without evaluating permissions for the requested client. Consequently, an administrator granted view on all clients can still view a client with an explicit client-specific denial. This defeats the V2 resource-specific override behavior demonstrated by the existing user permission tests. Global fine-grained grants should be used as a fallback when no client-specific permission applies, rather than bypassing its evaluation.

title: Handle existing permission servers without the Clients resource
body: For a realm whose admin-permissions client was created before this change, the authorization store contains only the Users resource and the previous scopes. AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when that client already exists, so adding Clients to the schema does not create its resource or new scopes. When checking a client without an individual resource, getResourceTypeResource() therefore returns null; this code passes it to findByResource() and subsequently dereferences it with resource.getScopes(), causing client authorization requests to fail with a server error instead of denying access. Reconcile existing permission servers with the expanded schema and guard against a missing fallback resource.

title: Global view permission bypasses client-specific denials
body: canView(ClientModel) returns true immediately when canView() grants the all-clients VIEW permission, without evaluating permissions on the requested client. Consequently, an administrator granted VIEW on all clients can still view a client with an explicit client-specific denial. This defeats the resource-specific override behavior exercised by the existing user-permission tests. Evaluate the client's effective permission before allowing a global fine-grained grant; only the administrative-role shortcut should bypass that evaluation.

title: Handle existing permission servers without the new Clients resource
body: The fallback assumes getResourceTypeResource() always returns a Clients resource, but realms initialized before this change have only the Users resource. AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when the admin-permissions client already exists, so it never adds the new Clients resource or client-only scopes to those realms. Client permission checks can therefore pass null to findByResource() and subsequently dereference resource.getScopes(), producing server errors instead of an authorization decision. Reconcile existing permission servers with the expanded schema and make this fallback null-safe.

title: Assert the new exit-code contract in distribution tests
body: This PR changes the incompatible-update exit code from 4 to 3 and assigns 4 to a disabled feature, but the disabled-feature and incompatible-version tests only assert error text. They would still pass if either command returned success or the wrong exit code. Since automation is explicitly instructed to rely on exit codes rather than messages, assert exit code 4 for disabled-feature invocations of both metadata and check, and exit code 3 for the incompatible-version checks.

title: View-only group permission authorizes group creation and moves
body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses requireManage(), which delegates to this method, so an administrator granted only view permission can create top-level groups or move existing subgroups to the top level by supplying their IDs. Only the MANAGE scope should satisfy this check; add a negative test for an administrator with only all-groups VIEW permission.

title: Return model group IDs rather than authorization resource IDs
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() passes groupResource.getId() to a helper that looks up resources by their model group ID/name, and then adds that authorization resource ID to the returned set. Authorization resources have independently generated IDs; their names hold the actual group IDs. UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource use this set to restrict user searches by group membership, and user counts also consume it. For example, an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS grant causes the Groups authorization resource's ID to be returned as a group filter, so searches and counts return no members even though direct user access is authorized. Evaluate the correct resource and return actual model group IDs, including handling an all-groups member grant across real groups.

title: Initialize the new resources and scopes for existing permission clients
body: The Groups resource type introduces new scopes and an all-groups resource, but init() immediately returns whenever the realm already has an admin-permissions client. Consequently, a realm initialized before this change never receives manage-membership, manage-members, view-members, or the Groups resource. Creating group permissions with these scopes fails with "No scopes found", and group evaluation can dereference a null all-groups resource. Update existing permission clients idempotently or provide a migration for the newly added schema entries.

title: View-only group permission authorizes group creation and moves
body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses this check to authorize both creating groups and moving existing groups to the top level. Consequently, an administrator granted only read access to all groups can perform these mutations. This check must require MANAGE, with a regression test verifying that VIEW alone cannot create or move groups.

title: Use group model IDs rather than authorization resource IDs
body: Authorization resources for individual groups are named with the group model ID, but have their own separately generated resource ID. This loop passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission(), which looks up a resource by name, so it fails to evaluate the individual group's permission and instead falls back to all-groups permissions. It also returns authorization resource IDs as group IDs, which UsersResource passes to the user storage membership filter and count queries. Thus individual view-members/manage-members grants do not reliably populate user searches or counts. Evaluate the resource using its group-model name and return actual group model IDs; the synthetic all-groups resource must also be handled separately rather than returned as a group ID.

title: Group membership filtering excludes users with direct user permissions
body: When an administrator lacks global user-view permission, any nonempty result from getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() becomes a mandatory storage-level group membership filter. V2 also supports direct permissions on individual users, so an administrator allowed to view Alice directly and members of Bob's group should see both Alice and Bob. This query excludes Alice before usersEvaluator.canView() can evaluate her direct grant. The candidate search must include the union of directly authorized users and users authorized through groups, rather than restricting all candidates to the permitted groups. The brute-force user search has the same problem.

title: View-only group permission authorizes group creation and reparenting
body: canManage() accepts either the VIEW or MANAGE scope on all groups. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses requireManage() as its authorization check, so an administrator granted only VIEW can create top-level groups and move existing child groups to the top level by supplying their IDs. This write authorization must require MANAGE, not VIEW; add a negative test for a view-only administrator.

title: Group-member search restrictions use authorization resources instead of group IDs
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() queries authorization resources by type and returns groupResource.getId(), but those IDs are authorization-resource UUIDs, not GroupModel IDs (the group ID is stored in the resource name). Moreover, AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() does not assign a type to individual group resources, so this query normally finds only the synthetic all-groups resource. With an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS grant, it returns that synthetic resource's UUID, which UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource pass to the user provider as a group-membership restriction; no users belong to that ID, so searches incorrectly return no members. Individual group grants are also absent from the returned set, breaking group-restricted counts. The method needs to return actual permitted group IDs, including handling all-groups grants, rather than authorization-resource IDs.

title: Initialize the new Groups schema objects for existing permission clients
body: The new Groups resource type and member scopes are only provisioned by init(), which immediately returns when the realm already has an admin-permissions client. A realm that enabled V2 permissions before this change therefore never receives the Groups resource or the new scopes. Creating a group-member permission then fails because getOrCreateResource() cannot find its scopes, and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() can proceed with a null all-groups resource. Update existing permission clients with the missing schema objects instead of limiting initialization to newly created clients.

title: Choice-format branches bypass HTML validation entirely
body: Replacing the entire choice expression with "..." removes its rendered text from security validation, not just the choice operator. For example, an error-invalid-multivalued-size translation containing `{2,choice,0#<script>alert(1)</script>|1#value}` passes this verifier because the script is discarded before sanitization, although MessageFormat can emit it at runtime. Validate the contents of each choice branch rather than excluding the whole expression. The same bypass affects linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit keys.

title: Overlapping prefix and suffix cause diagnostic generation to throw
body:
The suffix comparison is not bounded by the prefix already consumed. If a message is `a
`, sanitization produces `a`, and both start and end become 1. The subsequent `sanitized.substring(1, 0)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of reporting illegal HTML. Bound the suffix scan so it cannot overlap the matched prefix in either string; otherwise ordinary invalid translations abort verification without the intended diagnostic.

title: Preserve the React consoles' interpolation syntax
body: This resource uses i18next interpolation (`{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, and `{{2}}`), but the replacement uses Java MessageFormat placeholders and a Java choice expression. i18next will not substitute these single-braced parameters or evaluate the choice expression, so multivalued-size validation errors display literal formatting syntax instead of the attribute and limits. The same change in the admin-ui English resource has the same problem. Keep console-compatible formatting rather than copying the server-side MessageFormat string.

title: The Lithuanian OTP instruction was replaced with Italian
body: The new totpStep1 value, `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, is Italian, not Lithuanian. This replaces a Lithuanian instruction and makes OTP setup instructions appear in the wrong language for Lithuanian users. The identical replacement in the Lithuanian login bundle's loginTotpStep1 also needs a Lithuanian translation.

title: Keep the console message in i18next interpolation syntax
body: This React console resource previously used {{0}}, {{1}}, and {{2}}, but now uses Java MessageFormat placeholders and a choice expression. i18next does not interpret that syntax, so multivalued-size validation errors will display literal placeholders and choice text instead of the attribute name and limits. The same regression is introduced in the admin-ui English resource. Keep these console messages in the frontend's supported format rather than copying the server-side MessageFormat string.

title: Validate HTML inside choice alternatives instead of discarding them
body: For error-invalid-multivalued-size and linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit keys, normalization removes the entire choice expression before HTML validation. A translation such as {2,choice,0#|1#value|1

title: Prevent the common suffix from overlapping the common prefix
body: The prefix and suffix scans run independently, so their matched regions can overlap. For example, a message value of foo<script>foo sanitizes to foo: both scans match three characters, and the subsequent sanitized.substring(3, 0) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. Instead of reporting the illegal HTML, verification aborts with an unchecked exception. Bound the suffix scan by the unmatched lengths remaining after the prefix scan.

title: Restore Lithuanian text for the OTP installation instruction
body: The replacement text, 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', is Italian rather than Lithuanian. This replaces an existing Lithuanian instruction with another language during authenticator setup. The identical mistake is introduced in the Lithuanian login bundle's loginTotpStep1. Translate the new instruction into Lithuanian in both bundles.

title: Keep React message resources in i18next format
body: This replaces i18next's `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, and `{{2}}` interpolation tokens with Java MessageFormat tokens and a Java choice expression. The React account console does not evaluate MessageFormat, so multivalued-size validation errors will display literal placeholders and choice syntax instead of the attribute name and limits. The same regression is introduced in the admin UI's `messages_en.properties` at line 3138. Keep these React resources in the format supported by i18next.

title: Validate HTML inside choice branches instead of discarding them
body: For `error-invalid-multivalued-size` and `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`, normalization removes the entire choice expression before HTML validation. A translation such as `{0,choice,0#seconds|1#|1

title: Restore Lithuanian OTP setup instructions
body: The new `totpStep1` value is Italian (`Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare`), although this is the Lithuanian resource bundle. The same Italian text is introduced as `loginTotpStep1` in the Lithuanian login bundle at line 71. Lithuanian users now receive OTP setup instructions in an unrelated language; replace both values with Lithuanian translations.

title: Access-token matcher does not validate the expected grant
body: The grant shortcut occupies indices 4 through 5 of the six-character prefix, but this matcher reads substring(3, 5). It also returns false when the substring equals the expected grant, rather than when it differs. Consequently, the authorization-code, refresh, device, and CIBA event assertions accept tokens with incorrect or unknown grants, hiding failures to propagate the grant context. Validate the prefix length and reject when substring(4, 6) does not equal the expected shortcut.

title: Document the required two-character grant shortcut
body: The new SPI documentation recommends a three-letter shortcut, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires an encoded context of exactly six characters and reserves exactly two characters for the grant. A custom grant following this documented contract will issue token IDs that the default decoder rejects with IllegalArgumentException. Document the exact two-character requirement and validate it when registering grant factories so incompatible shortcuts cannot silently produce undecodable tokens.

title: Unknown-grant test passes on an unrelated NullPointerException
body: The test factory is initialized manually without postInit(), leaving its sessionFactory null. Decoding the unregistered 'ac' shortcut therefore throws NullPointerException in getGrantTypeByShortcut() while attempting to refresh the mapping, before the decoder can throw its intended IllegalArgumentException. Catching any RuntimeException makes this test pass without exercising unknown-grant validation. Provide a mocked session factory with no matching grant and assert the specific IllegalArgumentException.

title: Access-token matcher does not check the expected grant
body: The grant occupies prefix indices 4 through 5, but this matcher reads substring(3, 5), and it rejects equality rather than inequality. For example, both `onrtac:<uuid>` and `onrtna:<uuid>` pass when the expected grant is `ac`. Consequently, the updated authorization-code, refresh, device, and CIBA assertions do not detect missing or incorrect grant context. Validate the prefix length and compare substring(4, 6) against the expected shortcut, rejecting mismatches.

title: Shortcut contract recommends a length the decoder cannot accept
body: The new getShortcut() contract recommends a three-letter shortcut, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires an exactly six-character context prefix and allocates exactly two characters to the grant. A custom grant following this documentation can register successfully and issue tokens, yet those tokens cannot be decoded by the same provider. Document the mandatory two-character length and validate it when registering grant shortcuts so incompatible values cannot silently produce undecodable token IDs.

title: Unknown-grant test passes on a NullPointerException
body: The test fixture never calls factory.postInit(), leaving sessionFactory null. Decoding the unregistered `ac` shortcut therefore reaches getGrantTypeByShortcut() and throws a NullPointerException while attempting to refresh the registry, rather than the intended IllegalArgumentException for an unknown grant. Catching any RuntimeException makes the test pass despite not exercising the expected rejection behavior. Supply a session-factory mock with an empty provider stream and assert the specific IllegalArgumentException.

title: Access-token matcher does not verify the expected grant
body: The grant occupies indexes 4–5 of the six-character prefix, but this matcher reads substring(3, 5) and rejects equality instead of inequality. Consequently, an ID such as `onrtna:<uuid>` passes an assertion expecting the authorization-code grant `ac`. This leaves the updated authorization-code, refresh, device, and CIBA assertions unable to detect missing or incorrect grant encoding. Check the prefix length and reject when substring(4, 6) does not equal the expected shortcut.

title: Enforce the shortcut width required by the token format
body: Grant shortcuts are accepted without a length check, while the decoder requires exactly six context characters and reads exactly two characters for the grant. The new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory contract even describes a typical shortcut as three letters. A custom grant following that contract can therefore start successfully and issue tokens whose IDs cannot be decoded by this same provider. Document the two-character requirement and validate it when registering shortcuts, including the lazy registration paths, so unsupported shortcuts cannot produce unreadable token IDs.

title: Remove exhausted credentials from the storage that owns them
body: The new lookup can return a credential owned by an external user-storage provider, but the exhaustion branch still calls removeStoredCredentialById, which only removes locally stored credentials. An exhausted external credential therefore remains configured. If the user abandons the subsequent recovery-code setup, the next login can select that empty credential, and RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(), causing an error instead of displaying a usable authentication challenge. Handle external credential exhaustion through the owning provider rather than the local credential-removal API.

title: Exercise single-use consumption in the federated recovery-code test
body: The new test provider accepts any matching recovery code without removing or marking it used, and getCredentials reconstructs a fresh credential from the unchanged list on every call. Consequently, the same recovery code can authenticate indefinitely, the displayed code number never advances, and the exhaustion/reconfiguration path is never exercised. The added integration test checks only one successful login, so it passes despite violating the single-use recovery-code contract. Consume codes in the fixture and extend the test to verify replay rejection, advancement, and regeneration after exhaustion.

title: Consume recovery codes and test their one-time-use behavior
body: The new recovery-code validator accepts any code in the original list without removing or marking it used. getCredentials() also rebuilds the credential from that unchanged list, so every login continues to request code 0, previously used codes remain valid, and exhaustion never triggers regeneration. The added integration test performs only one login and therefore passes with this broken recovery-code lifecycle. Make the test provider track consumption and extend the test to verify replay rejection, advancement to the next code, and regeneration after exhaustion.

title: Keep the backwards-compatibility provider compatible with its baseline
body: This provider is explicitly intended to remain source-compatible with Keycloak 4.8.3, but it now imports and calls RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, which did not exist in that version, and overrides the newer getCredentials SPI method. It can no longer be compiled against the baseline whose compatibility this test is meant to exercise. Put the recovery-code implementation in a separate contemporary test provider rather than changing the legacy compatibility fixture.

title: Consume recovery codes in the federation test provider and test reuse
body: The new recovery-code validator accepts any matching code without removing it or recording that it was used. In addition, getCredentials() reconstructs the credential from the unchanged original list on every call, so the login form always requests the first code and the authenticator never observes an exhausted credential. The new integration test therefore passes even though the same recovery code can authenticate indefinitely and regeneration after exhaustion is never exercised. Update the test provider to persist consumption, and extend the test to verify that a used code is rejected, the requested code advances, and exhausting the codes triggers configuration of a new set.

title: Stop and join the reader before asserting its results
body: Setting deletedAll to true does not wait for the reader's current HTTP request to finish. The assertion can therefore see an empty caughtExceptions list and pass even if that in-flight request subsequently fails with the NPE this test is intended to catch. Also, if any deletion throws, deletedAll is never set and the non-daemon reader continues making requests after the test fails. Retain the reader thread, signal it to stop in a finally block, and wait for it to terminate before checking caughtExceptions.

title: Stop and join the reader before checking for failures
body: Setting deletedAll does not wait for an already-running groups() request to finish. The assertion can therefore pass before that request throws and adds an exception, allowing the regression test to miss the failure it is intended to catch. Also, if any remove() call throws, deletedAll is never set and the non-daemon reader keeps issuing requests indefinitely, potentially interfering with subsequent tests or preventing JVM shutdown. Keep a reference to the reader, stop it in a finally block, and wait for it to terminate before asserting caughtExceptions.

title: Stop and join the reader before checking its exceptions
body: Setting deletedAll does not wait for the reader thread's current HTTP request to finish. The assertion can therefore see an empty list and pass even though that in-flight request subsequently fails with the concurrency error this test is meant to catch. Also, if a deletion throws, deletedAll is never set and the reader continues issuing requests after the test exits. Keep a reference to the thread, stop it in a finally block, and join it before asserting on caughtExceptions so all reader failures are observed and the worker cannot leak into subsequent tests.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime fields
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses this paginator with order_by="-datetime", so get_item_key receives an AuditLogEntry datetime, not a number. Calling math.floor or math.ceil on it raises TypeError when build_cursor processes any nonempty result set, making optimized audit-log requests fail with a server error. value_from_cursor also returns the raw numeric cursor rather than converting it to a datetime for the database predicate. Reuse DateTimePaginator's key and cursor conversions for this endpoint.

title: Django querysets do not support the advertised negative offsets
body: When advanced features are enabled and a cursor has a negative offset, this branch passes a negative slice start to a Django QuerySet. Django explicitly rejects negative indexing with ValueError; it does not handle these boundary conditions automatically as the comment claims. Consequently, the new negative-offset feature produces a server error instead of a page. Implement reverse traversal using supported nonnegative slices and ordering, or reject such cursors with a pagination validation error.

title: Do not dereference an optional organization member on every request
body: RpcUserOrganizationContext.member can be None for organization-scoped API-token requests, which do not represent an organization member. For a non-superuser request, this expression dereferences that missing member and raises AttributeError. Because enable_advanced is computed even when optimized_pagination is absent, this breaks previously supported ordinary audit-log requests as well as optimized ones. Guard against a missing member and only evaluate advanced eligibility when the optimized path is requested.

title: Use datetime-aware cursor conversion for audit logs
body: The audit-log endpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to the field value. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so building cursors for any nonempty optimized page raises TypeError and returns a server error. value_from_cursor also returns a number instead of converting the timestamp back to a datetime. Reuse DateTimePaginator's conversions (or inherit from it) so both initial requests and subsequent cursor requests work.

title: Django querysets do not support negative slicing
body: When advanced features are enabled and the cursor offset is negative, this branch passes a negative slice start to a Django QuerySet. Django explicitly rejects negative indexing with ValueError rather than handling boundary conditions automatically. Thus the advertised negative-offset feature produces a server error, even with cursor value zero, before any rows are retrieved. Reject invalid offsets with a pagination error or translate them into a supported query instead of slicing with a negative index.

title: Handle organization contexts without a member
body: Organization-authenticated API requests can have organization_context.member=None, such as requests authorized through an organization API token. This new expression unconditionally dereferences that member whenever request.user.is_superuser is false, even when optimized_pagination was not requested. Such requests previously used the normal paginator but now fail with AttributeError. Only evaluate advanced authorization when requested, and explicitly handle contexts without a member.

title: Use datetime-aware cursor conversion for audit logs
body: The audit-log endpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but get_item_key() applies math.floor()/math.ceil() directly to the field value. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so building cursors for any nonempty optimized response raises TypeError and returns a server error. value_from_cursor() also returns a raw number rather than converting it back to a datetime for subsequent queries. Inherit from DateTimePaginator or implement its datetime conversions before using this paginator for audit logs.

title: Do not pass negative offsets to Django QuerySet slicing
body: When advanced features are enabled and a cursor has a negative offset, this branch passes that offset directly into a Django QuerySet slice. Django explicitly rejects negative slice indexes with ValueError; it does not handle them as the comment claims. Consequently, the advertised negative-offset pagination always fails with a server error rather than navigating backwards. Implement reverse navigation using supported ordering and nonnegative bounds, or reject these cursors with a pagination validation error.

title: Migrate or version existing Redis keys before switching to sorted sets
body: The buffer still uses the same `span-buf:s:*` keys, but existing deployments store Redis sets at those keys. `ZADD`, the updated Lua script's `ZCARD`, and the flusher's `ZSCAN` all fail with WRONGTYPE on those existing sets. Deploying this change with buffered segments therefore breaks ingestion and flushing; rolling deployments also leave old and new consumers using incompatible commands against the same keys. Introduce a migration or versioned key namespace with a way to drain the old buffers.

title: The optimized audit-log paginator cannot handle datetime keys
body: The audit-log endpoint selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, but this implementation passes the model's datetime value to `math.floor` or `math.ceil`. Any nonempty first page raises TypeError while building its cursors instead of returning audit logs. Additionally, `value_from_cursor` returns a numeric cursor value rather than converting it back to a datetime. Use the datetime key encoding and decoding provided by `DateTimePaginator` for this endpoint.

title: Negative offsets are not supported by Django QuerySet slicing
body: With advanced features enabled, a negative cursor offset is passed directly into a Django QuerySet slice. Django explicitly rejects negative indexes and raises ValueError; it does not handle them automatically as the comment claims. An authorized audit-log request using optimized pagination and a cursor such as `0:-1:0` therefore fails instead of performing reverse pagination. Reject invalid offsets with a pagination error or implement reverse traversal using supported queries.

title: Preserve timestamp scores when merging duplicate span payloads
body: `ZUNIONSTORE` defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`. If a span payload already exists in the resolved segment and is replayed into a staging set keyed by its original parent, merging the sets adds its two end timestamps together. Its score is then no longer an end timestamp and it can survive `ZPOPMIN` eviction ahead of genuinely newer spans. This makes retention depend on replay history rather than span completion time. Specify an appropriate aggregation mode, such as MAX, for both sorted-set merges.

title: The optimized audit-log paginator cannot handle datetime keys
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint selects this paginator with order_by="-datetime", but get_item_key passes the AuditLogEntry datetime to math.floor/math.ceil, which raises TypeError. Consequently, an authorized user's optimized_pagination=true request fails whenever results are nonempty. value_from_cursor also returns a numeric value instead of converting it to a datetime. This paginator needs the datetime conversions provided by DateTimePaginator.

title: Django querysets do not support negative slicing
body: When advanced features are enabled and a supplied cursor has a negative offset, this branch slices a Django QuerySet with a negative start. Django raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.") rather than handling the boundary automatically. Thus the advertised negative-offset feature produces a server error on the optimized audit-log endpoint. Reject invalid offsets with a pagination error or implement reverse traversal without negative queryset indices.

title: Changing existing Redis keys from sets to sorted sets requires a migration
body: The buffer now uses ZADD and ZSCAN on the same span-buf:s:* keys that the previous version populated with SADD. Any buffered segment present during deployment remains a Redis set, so new insertions and flushing those segments fail with WRONGTYPE. Mixed-version consumers also cannot read or write each other's buffers. Provide a compatible conversion or a versioned-key rollout that drains the old buffers before switching; otherwise deployment stalls processing of existing data.

title: Unioning sorted sets must preserve timestamps rather than sum them
body: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM. A replayed span can exist both in the destination buffer and in a newly staged parent buffer when that parent has already been redirected. Merging those buffers doubles the duplicate payload's end-timestamp score, although its actual timestamp has not changed. Subsequent ZPOPMIN eviction then retains these replayed old spans ahead of genuinely newer spans. Use an aggregation mode such as MAX so merging duplicate payloads preserves their timestamp.

title: Insertion eviction ignores the configured segment span limit
body: SpansBuffer still accepts and stores max_segment_spans, but the Python span-count check was removed and this script unconditionally caps every segment at 1000. A caller configuring a smaller limit now receives segments exceeding that limit, while a larger configured limit silently loses spans at 1000. Pass the configured limit to the insertion script and use it for eviction, or explicitly remove the configurable contract rather than leaving it ineffective.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate audit-log datetimes
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses this paginator with order_by="-datetime", but get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil to the field value. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so any nonempty optimized response raises TypeError while building its cursors. value_from_cursor also lacks the timestamp-to-datetime conversion required for subsequent queries. Use DateTimePaginator's key and cursor conversions for this endpoint.

title: Django querysets reject the advertised negative offsets
body: When advanced features are enabled, a cursor with a negative offset is passed directly to QuerySet slicing. Django does not support negative queryset indexes and raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported."). Consequently, the newly advertised negative-offset pagination fails instead of returning a page. Reject such cursors with BadPaginationError or implement reverse traversal using supported query operations.

title: Changing Redis key types in place breaks existing buffered data
body: The previous implementation stores Redis sets at the same span-buf:s:* keys that this implementation now accesses with ZADD, ZSCAN, and sorted-set Lua commands. Existing buffered segments therefore cause WRONGTYPE errors after deployment, and old workers likewise cannot access segments written by new workers during a rolling deployment. This can block ingestion and flushing until keys expire, losing buffered spans. Introduce a versioned key namespace or an explicit compatible migration/drain strategy.

title: Use a non-additive aggregation when merging timestamp scores
body: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM. If a payload already exists in the destination and is inserted again into a source buffer—for example, when replaying a child span whose parent has a redirect—merging adds its two end timestamps together. That duplicate then receives a score roughly twice its actual timestamp and survives eviction ahead of genuinely newer spans. The old set union deduplicated without changing ordering information; use an aggregation such as MAX to preserve the timestamp score in both merge operations.

title: Insertion eviction ignores the configured segment span limit
body: Eviction is hard-coded to 1000 spans, while SpansBuffer still accepts and stores max_segment_spans and no longer enforces it during loading. A caller configuring a smaller limit now receives segments above that limit, and a caller configuring a larger limit silently loses spans at 1000. Pass the configured limit into the insertion script and enforce it consistently, or explicitly remove the configuration contract rather than leaving it ineffective.

title: Parse the query before deciding it contains only errors
body: A substring match for `event.type:error` does not establish that the query excludes transactions. For example, `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` both enable upsampling for the Discover dataset. Their count is then replaced with an aggregation over `sample_weight`, even though the helper explicitly states that transactions do not support that field. This can cause query failures or incorrect counts for valid Discover queries. Eligibility must be based on the parsed query's constraints, not the presence of this text.

title: Check the dataset and query actually being executed
body: The eligibility check uses the outer `dataset` and the original request query rather than `scoped_dataset` and the callback's `query`. Dashboard splitting invokes this callback with Discover error queries even when the original dataset is metrics-enhanced performance. Those queries are always deemed ineligible because the original metrics dataset is not supported by the helper, so allowlisted projects still return sampled counts in error-only dashboard results. Pass the actual execution dataset and query into the eligibility check, including the error-only constraint added by dashboard splitting.

title: Apply upsampling consistently to top-event selection
body: Only `timeseries_columns` is transformed for top-event requests; `selected_columns` and `orderby` still come directly from the request. A request grouping events and ordering by `count()` therefore selects its top groups using stored-event counts, then charts those groups using upsampled counts. When groups have different sampling rates, a group with fewer stored events but a larger estimated error count can be omitted in favor of a smaller group. Transform the aggregation used to select and rank the top events as well as the time-series aggregation.

title: Parse the query instead of using a substring to identify error-only searches
body: The presence of `event.type:error` does not mean a Discover query selects only errors. For example, `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` and `!event.type:error` both pass this check. For allowlisted projects, their count is then replaced with an aggregation over `sample_weight`, even though the helper explicitly states that transactions do not have that field. These valid searches can consequently fail or return incorrect counts. Determine whether the parsed query actually restricts results to errors before applying the transformation.

title: Check upsampling against the dataset actually being queried
body: The eligibility check uses the outer `dataset`, while query execution uses `scoped_dataset`. These differ in the dashboard splitting paths: a metrics-enhanced request can execute an error-only query against Discover, but this check still sees the metrics dataset and rejects upsampling. As a result, sampled error charts produced by those paths continue to report stored counts rather than estimated counts. Pass the actual scoped dataset and effective query into the eligibility check.

title: Apply weighted counting to top-event selection as well as its time series
body: For top-events requests, only `timeseries_columns` is transformed to weighted counting; `selected_columns` and `orderby` are still passed directly from the original request. A request selecting and ordering by `count()` therefore chooses its top groups using stored-event counts, then plots weighted counts for those groups. With differing client sample rates, a group with fewer stored events can have the largest estimated count and still be excluded from the chart. Transform the selection and ranking aggregates consistently with the time-series aggregate.

title: Substring matching does not establish an error-only query
body: The presence of `event.type:error` in the query string does not mean the query selects only errors. For example, `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` both enable upsampling for Discover, even though they can select transactions. This replaces count() with an error-specific sample_weight aggregation for non-error results, producing incorrect counts or an unsupported-column query. Determine eligibility from the parsed filter semantics rather than a substring match.

title: Top-event selection still uses the unweighted aggregation
body: Only `timeseries_columns` is transformed for top-events queries; `selected_columns` and `orderby` are still taken unchanged from the request. A request grouping by a field and ordering by count() therefore chooses its top groups using stored-event counts, then displays weighted counts for those groups. With different client sampling rates, the group with the highest estimated error count can be omitted entirely. Apply consistent upsampling to the aggregates used to select and order the top groups, not just their subsequent time series.

title: Check the dataset and query actually being executed
body: The eligibility check uses the outer `dataset` and the original request query rather than `scoped_dataset` and the `query` passed to this invocation. The dashboard-splitting paths below explicitly execute error-only Discover queries while the outer dataset is metrics-enhanced. Those calls are always deemed ineligible because the helper rejects metrics datasets, so an allowlisted dashboard's error series continues reporting sampled counts. Base eligibility on the effective dataset and filter for each execution, including filters added by the dashboard split.

title: Include the organization in the attribute-key cache key
body: The new React Query key contains only the query options, although the fetch function calls an organization-specific endpoint. When switching between organizations with identical filters—for example, all projects and the same relative date range—both organizations share a cache entry. Cached custom attribute names from the previous organization can therefore appear in the next organization, and concurrent observers can reuse the wrong organization's response. Include the organization slug or endpoint path in the key.

title: Normalize error and recording timestamps before merging
body: Error timestamps read from nodestore are Unix seconds, while rrweb recording event timestamps are Unix milliseconds. Comparing these values directly places virtually every error before the first recording event, regardless of when it actually occurred. The generated error messages also retain the seconds value while recording messages use recording timestamps, giving Seer inconsistent timing context. Normalize both sources to the same unit before comparison and message generation, and test with realistic epoch timestamps.

title: Pass actual query results to the new table visualization
body: When an organization has `use-table-widget-visualization`, the dashboard renders the replacement table with empty columns, empty rows, and empty metadata instead of the fetched result. Consequently, every table widget becomes empty for that organization even when its query returned data. Wire the result and configured fields into the new component before enabling this branch, or retain the existing visualization until that integration is ready.

title: Only fall back when a custom renderer returns undefined
body: The custom renderer contract says that returning `undefined` requests fallback rendering, but the implementation uses a truthiness check. Valid React nodes such as `0`, an empty string, or `null` are discarded and replaced with the default cell content. This prevents custom renderers from displaying zero directly or intentionally suppressing a cell. Check `cell !== undefined` in both the body and header renderer wrappers.

title: New table visualization discards the widget's query results
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the chart passes empty columns, empty data, and empty metadata to TableWidgetVisualization instead of the actual `result`. Every dashboard table widget in an enabled organization therefore renders empty even when its query returned rows. Pass the real results and configured columns into the new visualization before enabling this branch.

title: Attribute query cache is not scoped to the organization
body: The new query key contains only the query options, while the query function fetches an organization-specific endpoint. Two organizations with the same project selection (for example, all projects), date range, item type, and attribute type share a cache entry. Switching organizations can therefore display custom attribute names fetched from the previous organization, and concurrent consumers can reuse the wrong organization's results. Include the organization slug or endpoint path in the query key.

title: Normalize error and recording timestamps before merging
body: Error timestamps read from nodestore are Unix seconds, but recording events use rrweb timestamps in Unix milliseconds. Comparing these values directly causes essentially every error to be emitted before the first recording event, regardless of when it actually occurred. The new tests use seconds for recording timestamps and consequently miss this production behavior. Convert recording timestamps to seconds, or error timestamps to milliseconds, before performing the chronological merge.

title: Respect falsy results from custom cell renderers
body: Both custom renderer wrappers use `if (cell)` to decide whether to accept the custom result, although the documented contract says only `undefined` invokes the fallback. Valid React results such as `0`, an empty string, or `null` are therefore replaced by the default renderer. This prevents callers from intentionally rendering zero or suppressing a cell's contents. Check explicitly for `undefined` in both the header and body wrappers.

title: Pass the actual query results to the new table visualization
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, every dashboard table receives `columns={[]}` and hard-coded empty data and metadata instead of the fetched `result`. Consequently, enabling the feature replaces populated dashboard tables with empty tables. Wire the result's rows, metadata, and configured columns into the new visualization before selecting this branch.

title: Include the organization in the attribute query cache key
body: The new React Query key contains only a constant and query options; it no longer includes the organization-specific endpoint path. Two organizations with the same date range and project selection (for example, the all-projects selection) therefore share a cache entry even though the query function requests different organization endpoints. Switching organizations can display the previous organization's custom attribute names and can cause concurrent consumers to reuse the wrong request. Include the organization slug or ID in the key.

title: Normalize timestamp units before merging errors with recording events
body: Error event timestamps from nodestore are Unix seconds, whereas raw replay recording events use rrweb timestamps in milliseconds. Comparing these values directly causes essentially every error to be emitted before the first recording event, even when it happened later in the replay. This gives Seer incorrectly ordered context. Convert both timestamps to the same unit before comparing them, and test with realistic millisecond recording timestamps rather than the second-valued fixtures currently used.

title: Do not bypass installer verification when the integration is missing
body: If no Integration row exists for the supplied installation_id, this branch completes the installation without comparing the authenticated GitHub user with the installer. This can happen before the installation webhook is processed or when its delivery fails. The subsequent build_integration fetches the installation using app credentials, which does not establish that the OAuth user has access to it. Consequently, a user supplying another installation's ID can still attach it to their Sentry organization. Fail closed until trusted installer information is available, or verify access using the authenticated user's token.

title: Handle integrations without sender metadata
body: The new check unconditionally indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"], but build_integration only includes sender when it is present in pipeline state. The basic setup flow in this file's tests explicitly creates integration metadata without sender. If such an integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed, attempting to attach it again now raises KeyError and returns a server error rather than a controlled installation failure. Handle missing installer metadata explicitly and obtain trusted verification information before proceeding.

title: Compare immutable GitHub user IDs instead of logins
body: Installer identity is checked using the login saved in webhook metadata and the current OAuth user's login. GitHub usernames can change and old usernames can be claimed by another account. A legitimate installer who renames their account will therefore be rejected, while a different account claiming the old username can pass this check for an unlinked installation. Store and compare the immutable GitHub user ID returned by both the webhook sender and the authenticated-user endpoint.

title: Do not bypass installer verification when the integration is missing
body: When no Integration row exists for the supplied installation_id, this branch advances the pipeline without checking the authenticated GitHub user against the installer. build_integration then retrieves that installation using app credentials, which does not establish that the OAuth user has access to it. A user who supplies another installation's ID before its installation webhook has created the Integration row can therefore attach it to their Sentry organization. The missing-row path needs to fail closed or independently verify ownership rather than skipping the new security check.

title: Handle integrations without sender metadata
body: The new check unconditionally indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"], but sender is optional in build_integration, and the basic installation flow in this file's tests explicitly creates metadata without it. If such an Integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed, attempting to attach it again now raises KeyError and returns a server error instead of completing or displaying the invalid-installation message. Handle missing sender metadata explicitly and obtain trustworthy installer information if it is required.

GitHub usernames can be changed and subsequently claimed by another account, so these strings do not reliably identify the same user. After the installer renames their account, the legitimate installer is rejected, while a different account claiming the old username can pass verification for an unlinked installation. Store and compare the immutable GitHub user ID from both responses instead.

A caller can therefore link someone else's installation if its webhook has not yet been processed (or was not delivered). Require trusted installer information and validate it before advancing, including in this branch.

The normal setup flow in the tests explicitly creates metadata without sender. If such an Integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed, attempting to link it again now raises KeyError and returns a server error instead of a controlled installation failure. title: Generate the queued timestamp for each AssignmentSource instance
body: `timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, so every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` value receives the same timestamp, potentially from days earlier in a long-running worker. Both `from_integration()` and `from_dict()` when the timestamp is omitted use this default, so the serialized metadata does not record when the assignment was queued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to generate a fresh timestamp for each instance.

title: Generate the queued timestamp per AssignmentSource instance
body: `timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` value receives the same worker-startup timestamp. Consequently, the `queued` metadata serialized into outbound tasks does not represent when those assignments were queued and can be arbitrarily stale in long-running workers. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to generate a fresh timestamp for each instance.

title: Generate the queued timestamp for each AssignmentSource instance
body: `timezone.now()` is evaluated once when this module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` value receives the same worker-startup timestamp. In a long-running process, the context serialized into outbound tasks therefore records an incorrect queue time. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to generate a fresh timestamp for each instance.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement its abstract counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, or build_occurrence_and_event_data members. Accessing detector.detector_handler for a metric_alert_fire detector therefore raises TypeError at handler construction, and process_detectors aborts instead of returning no results as the previous placeholder did. Keep a concrete no-op handler until the stateful implementation is available, or implement the required members.

title: Expected occurrence uses a different group key from the evaluation
body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds its expected occurrence with group key "val1", but evaluates group key "group_key". The mock occurrence builder includes the group key in the occurrence fingerprint, so the expected fingerprint is ["<detector_id>:val1"] while the returned occurrence has ["<detector_id>:group_key"]. The equality assertion consequently fails even when the implementation is correct. Build the expected occurrence using "group_key".

title: Keep the registered metric-alert handler instantiable
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of its abstract members: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. It therefore cannot be instantiated. Accessing detector.detector_handler for the registered metric_alert_fire type raises TypeError, causing process_detectors to abort rather than returning the previous empty result. Keep a concrete no-op handler until these methods are implemented, or implement the required methods before registering this stateful handler.

title: Build the expected occurrence with the group key being evaluated
body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds its expected occurrence using group key "val1", but calls evaluate_group_key_value with "group_key". The helper includes that key in the occurrence fingerprint, so the expected occurrence has fingerprint "<detector_id>:val1" while the handler correctly produces "<detector_id>:group_key". This is an incorrect expected result for the new occurrence-generation path; construct the expected occurrence with "group_key" so the assertion checks the occurrence belonging to the evaluated group.

title: Registered metric alert handler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of its abstract members: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, or build_occurrence_and_event_data. MetricAlertFire still registers this class as its detector_handler, so accessing detector.detector_handler for type 'metric_alert_fire' raises TypeError instead of returning the previous no-op handler. This also aborts process_detectors rather than safely skipping the unimplemented detector. Keep a concrete no-op handler until the stateful implementation is provided, or implement the required members.

title: Expected occurrence uses a different group key from the evaluation
body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds its expected occurrence with group key 'val1', but calls evaluate_group_key_value with expected_result.group_key, which is 'group_key'. The occurrence builder includes the group key in the fingerprint, so the actual occurrence has fingerprint '<detector_id>:group_key' while the expected occurrence has '<detector_id>:val1'. The new equality assertion therefore fails. Build the expected occurrence with the same group key passed to the evaluator.

title: Spawned workers fail the Process type check and are never killed
body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances. SpawnProcess is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check is false for production workers. When a worker is declared hung, it is therefore left running while a replacement is started and its reference is overwritten. The old worker can resume flushing the same shards concurrently with its replacement, and repeated hangs leak workers. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or distinguish processes from threads another way before killing them.

title: Do not skip cleanup of remaining workers when the join deadline expires
body: When the shared join deadline expires, this break exits the worker loop without terminating any remaining workers. For example, if the first worker consumes the timeout waiting on Kafka, all subsequent workers are abandoned even if they are also blocked. Setting stopped only takes effect when a worker returns to its main loop, so it does not stop workers stuck in Redis or future.result(). During rebalancing these workers can remain alive after replacement flushers start. Apply the deadline only to waiting, and perform termination cleanup for every worker regardless of whether time remains.

title: Spawned workers fail the multiprocessing.Process type check
body: Workers are created using multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, whose SpawnProcess class is not a subclass of the default-context multiprocessing.Process class. Consequently, this isinstance check is false for production workers, so an unhealthy worker is never killed before its replacement starts. A hung worker that later resumes can flush the same shards concurrently with its replacement. The identical check in join() also prevents terminating workers that exceed the shutdown timeout. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or explicitly distinguish threads from spawned processes in both places.

title: Shutdown skips remaining workers when the shared deadline expires
body: When the join deadline expires, this break skips every remaining worker without attempting to terminate it. With multiple flusher processes, one worker blocked on Redis or Kafka can consume the entire timeout, leaving other blocked workers alive after join() returns. During rebalancing, those workers can outlive their partition assignment and overlap with new flushers. Stop waiting once the deadline expires, but still perform termination cleanup for every worker.

title: Spawned workers fail the process type check and are never killed on restart
body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, whose SpawnProcess class is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process. Consequently, this isinstance check is false for production workers and process.kill() is skipped. When a worker hangs, its replacement starts while the original remains alive and shares the same health and backpressure values. If the original resumes, both workers can flush the same shards concurrently, risking duplicate production and incorrect health reporting. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or otherwise distinguish workers from test threads, and exercise restart behavior with a real spawned process.

title: Do not skip remaining workers when the shutdown deadline expires
body: When the shared join deadline expires, this break skips cleanup for the current worker and every remaining worker. A worker blocked in Redis or waiting for Kafka delivery can therefore survive join(), including across partition reassignment, while its process handle is abandoned with the old strategy. The stopped flag does not interrupt those blocking operations. Apply the deadline only to graceful waiting, then terminate and reap every remaining process rather than breaking out of the cleanup loop.
