title: Recreate the queue pool when a strategy is recreated
body: The factory creates one queue pool in its constructor and passes that same pool to every strategy. During a Kafka rebalance, Arroyo closes the old strategy and creates another through create_with_partitions; closing the old strategy shuts down this pool's queues and workers. The replacement strategy consequently submits to already-shutdown queues. Those submissions raise, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit catches the exceptions and marks the offsets complete, so results received after a rebalance can be committed without being processed. The pool and its offset tracker need a lifecycle tied to the individual strategy rather than being reused after shutdown.

title: Bound queued work and apply backpressure
body: Each queue is constructed without a maxsize, and submission always accepts more work without raising MessageRejected. If result processing is slower than Kafka consumption—or one worker is blocked—the consumer continues retaining decoded results, original Kafka messages, and offset-tracking entries indefinitely. Unlike the bounded batching path, this mode has no limit on outstanding work and can exhaust process memory under sustained load. Bound outstanding work and reject submissions until capacity becomes available.

title: Drain accepted work and commit it before completing graceful shutdown
body: close() stops the commit thread before shutting down workers, and pool.shutdown() sets each worker's shutdown flag before calling queue.shutdown(immediate=False). Workers therefore exit after their current item rather than draining accepted queued items; completions after the commit thread exits are never committed. In addition, worker.join(timeout=5.0) can return while a result processor is still running, and strategy.join() ignores its supplied timeout and simply calls close() again. During a rebalance this can leave an old worker modifying subscription state after a new partition owner starts processing replayed results, breaking per-subscription ordering. Graceful close/join must drain accepted work, wait for in-flight processing within the requested timeout, and commit the final completed offsets before returning.

title: Create a fresh queue pool for each processing strategy
body: The factory creates one queue pool in its constructor and reuses it for every create_with_partitions call, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close shuts that pool down. Arroyo closes and recreates strategies when partition assignments change, so after the first rebalance the new strategy receives queues whose workers have stopped and whose queues have been shut down. Submissions then fail and the submit exception handler marks those messages completed, allowing unprocessed results to be committed. The pool and its offset tracker need a lifecycle scoped to each strategy rather than being reused after shutdown.

title: Bound queued work and propagate backpressure
body: Every worker queue is created with the default maxsize=0, which makes it unbounded, and submit always accepts more work. If processing is slower than Kafka ingestion, or a worker is blocked on a slow result, the consumer continues accumulating decoded results, original Kafka messages, and offset-tracking entries in memory without limit. This can exhaust the consumer's memory instead of applying the advertised backpressure. Use bounded capacity and signal Arroyo to retry submissions when capacity is exhausted.

title: Drain accepted work and commit completion before graceful shutdown
body: close stops the commit loop before shutting down the pool, and pool shutdown sets every worker's shutdown flag before draining its queue. Consequently, queued results are abandoned and results completed during worker shutdown are never included in a final commit. join simply calls close again and ignores its timeout, so it does not provide Arroyo's graceful draining phase either. On shutdown or rebalance this causes accepted work to be replayed, including already-applied results; workers that exceed the fixed five-second join can also keep applying old results after processing resumes elsewhere. Separate closing submissions from draining workers, honor the join timeout, and commit the final completed offsets after draining.

title: Do not acknowledge messages when submission fails
body: The broad submit exception handler treats any decoding, grouping, or enqueueing exception as successful completion by adding and immediately completing the message's offset. For example, if build_payload_grouping_key raises or work_queue.put fails because the queue is shut down, the result was never handed to a worker but the next commit can advance past it permanently. Expected invalid-payload handling already has the decoder's None path; unexpected submission failures should propagate or remain pending rather than acknowledge unprocessed results.

title: Invoke the commit callback on the consumer thread
body: The commit callback is invoked from the new background commit thread. Arroyo's StreamProcessor commit callback stages and commits offsets through KafkaConsumer, whose operations must run on its consumer thread. This can fail thread-affinity checks instead of committing offsets; the exception is merely logged and retried indefinitely. Collect completed offsets in the workers, but invoke the callback from poll() on the processing thread.

title: Create a fresh queue pool for each processing strategy
body: The factory creates one queue pool and passes it to every strategy, but closing or terminating a strategy shuts that pool down. StreamProcessor recreates strategies when partition assignments change, so the next strategy receives stopped workers and shut-down queues. Submissions then fail in queue.put(), and submit() catches those failures and marks their offsets complete, allowing unprocessed messages to be committed. The pool and its offset tracker need a lifecycle scoped to the strategy rather than being reused after shutdown.

title: Bound queued work and apply backpressure
body: queue.Queue() has no size limit, and submit() never rejects work or otherwise slows ingestion. If a worker is slow or processing throughput falls below Kafka ingestion throughput, queued messages grow without bound. A slow outstanding offset also prevents the tracker from releasing later completed offsets for that partition. This can exhaust consumer memory instead of applying the documented backpressure. Bound the pending work and use Arroyo's backpressure mechanism when capacity is exhausted.

title: Drain accepted work before ending graceful shutdown
body: close() stops the commit thread before waiting for processing, then pool.shutdown() sets every worker's shutdown flag before the queues are drained. Workers therefore abandon queued items after their current item, and completions occurring after the commit thread exits receive no final commit. Moreover, worker.join(timeout=5.0) can return while a result processor is still running, so strategy.join() can finish while old workers continue mutating subscription state after partition reassignment. Separate graceful close/join from termination: drain accepted work, wait within the supplied timeout, and commit the completed offsets before declaring the strategy joined.

title: Backup-code authentication can bypass password verification
body: The new backup-code branch accepts a valid backup code regardless of whether a supplied totpCode is valid. Earlier password verification is skipped whenever credentials.totpCode is nonempty. An attacker can therefore submit a valid backup code together with an arbitrary totpCode (for example, "x") and authenticate to a password-based account without knowing its password; the TOTP is never checked because the backup-code branch takes precedence. Ensure password verification cannot be bypassed by an unverified field when authenticating with a backup code.

title: Consume backup codes atomically to enforce single use
body: Backup-code verification reads the encrypted array and then overwrites it using an unconditional update by user ID. Two simultaneous login requests can read the same unused code, both validate it, and both successfully authenticate, violating the single-use guarantee. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's changes and restore a consumed code. Use an atomic compare-and-swap with retry or a suitably serialized transaction, and only authenticate after successfully consuming the code.

title: Backup-code authentication can bypass password verification
body: The existing password check runs only when credentials.totpCode is falsy, but the new backup-code branch takes precedence over TOTP validation. A caller can submit a valid backupCode together with any nonempty totpCode and an incorrect or missing password: password verification is skipped and the arbitrary TOTP is never checked. This allows possession of a backup code alone to authenticate a password-based account. Ensure the required primary credential is verified independently of which second-factor branch is selected.

title: Consume backup codes atomically to enforce single use
body: Backup codes are read from the user record, checked in memory, and then overwritten with an unconditional update by user ID. Two concurrent login requests can both read the same unused code and both authenticate successfully. Requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's changes, restoring a code already consumed by the other request. Use an atomic conditional update (checking the previously stored value and rejecting or retrying on conflict) or transactional locking so that successful authentication guarantees the code was consumed exactly once.

title: Backup-code login can bypass password verification with a dummy TOTP value
body: The preceding password verification runs only when `credentials.totpCode` is empty, but the new backup-code branch takes precedence over TOTP verification whenever `backupCode` is supplied. A caller can therefore submit an email, a valid backup code, and any nonempty `totpCode` to sign in without knowing the password; the dummy TOTP is never validated. This turns a backup second factor into a standalone login credential. Ensure the password (or verified identity-provider authentication) is checked independently of which second factor is submitted.

title: Consume backup codes atomically to enforce single use
body: Backup-code validation reads the encrypted code list and then unconditionally overwrites it using an update filtered only by user ID. Two concurrent login requests can read the same list, validate the same code, and both successfully authenticate. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's removals, making a consumed code usable again. Use an atomic compare-and-swap against the original stored value, or a transaction with appropriate locking, and reject or retry when another request has changed the list.

title: Guard the missing destination calendar in the Meet fallback
body: When an event uses Google Meet but has no destination calendar, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar and accessing its integration throws. Previously the optional access allowed this case to fall back to Cal Video. Booking creation now fails instead of using that fallback.

title: Pass the current destination to non-Google calendar adapters
body: Each destination's credential is used to create an event, but every adapter receives the full destination array. Office365CalendarService, LarkCalendarService, and BaseCalendarService always select the first entry rather than the entry for that credential. In a collective booking, secondary hosts therefore attempt to write to the primary host's calendar ID, which can fail authorization; CalDAV can also silently create nothing because no listed calendar matches. Scope the event's destination to the current destination or make all adapters select by credential ID.

title: Retain secondary host calendars when the organizer has none
body: The destinationCalendar field is initialized to null if neither the event type nor organizer has a destination calendar. The optional push then discards all collected secondary-host destinations. A collective event whose main host has no calendar but whose other hosts have connected calendars consequently creates no calendar events for those hosts. Initialize an empty array before appending the team destinations.

title: Preserve credential IDs on video references
body: Reference creation now sets credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result, dropping the credential ID returned by createVideoEvent. Cancellation only deletes a video meeting when its booking reference has a credentialId, so newly created Zoom and other video meetings will no longer be deleted when their bookings are cancelled. Preserve result.credentialId for video results as before.

title: Restore the destination fallback for legacy Google references
body: When externalCalendarId is null or absent, the new fallback searches destination calendars for an externalId equal to that missing value, which cannot match a normal calendar ID. Google update requests consequently receive no calendarId and fail for legacy booking references without a stored external calendar ID, even when the event has a valid destination calendar. The analogous delete fallback instead targets primary and can leave events in non-primary calendars undeleted.

title: Delete recurring instances using each reference's own credential
body: In the all-remaining-recurring-bookings branch, the fetched credential for the current reference is ignored. The code instead iterates only the organizer's credentials and selects just the first calendar reference from each instance. For the newly supported collective bookings, secondary hosts' calendar events are never deleted, even though every booking is marked cancelled. Iterate the references of each updated booking and resolve their matching credentials.

title: Do not reverse organization slug assignment
body: This changes slug assignment from when team billing is disabled to when it is enabled. With billing disabled, newly created organizations now receive neither a slug nor a requestedSlug, despite the requested subdomain being configured above. With billing enabled, the slug is assigned immediately instead of remaining a requested slug. Restore the original condition so organization routing and the billing-gated slug workflow retain their existing behavior.

title: Guard the missing destination before checking its integration
body: When a Google Meet event has no destination calendar, destructuring the empty array leaves mainHostDestinationCalendar undefined. Reading its integration throws instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. Booking creation therefore fails for Google Meet event types whose calendar was disconnected or is otherwise unset.

title: Select the destination belonging to the current credential
body: EventManager now calls this service separately for every collective host but passes the entire destinationCalendar array each time. This service always uses the first host's calendar ID with the current host's access token. Secondary Office 365 hosts (including those paired with a Google organizer) therefore attempt to write to another account's calendar and fail rather than receiving an event. LarkCalendarService and BaseCalendarService have the same first-element selection problem; these services need credential-specific destination selection as Google now has.

title: Restore the destination fallback for references without a calendar ID
body: When externalCalendarId is null or absent, the new fallback searches for a destination whose externalId equals that absent value, so it cannot select a configured calendar. Google updates then receive an undefined calendarId and fail. The analogous deletion fallback defaults to primary, leaving events on non-primary calendars undeleted while treating Google's 404 as success. This affects existing references without externalCalendarId, including the credential-less destination creation branch that still does not populate result.externalId.

title: Preserve the credential ID on video references
body: The reference builder now sets credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result, discarding the credential ID returned by createMeeting. The cancellation handler only deletes video meetings when their reference has a credentialId, so newly created Zoom and other dedicated video meetings will no longer be deleted when their booking is cancelled. Retain result.credentialId for video results.

title: Initialize destinations before adding collective co-host calendars
body: If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null. The optional push then silently drops all teamDestinationCalendars, even when other collective hosts have connected calendars. Those hosts receive no directly created calendar events. Initialize an empty array or assign the collected destinations instead of skipping the append.

title: Cancel recurring events using each reference's credential
body: The new outer loop resolves each collective host's credential, but the allRemainingBookings branch ignores that credential and loops only over the booking owner's credentials, selecting only the first calendar reference of each occurrence. Consequently cancelling an entire collective recurring series leaves secondary hosts' calendar events intact, despite marking all bookings cancelled. Iterate each updated booking's references and delete each with its matching credential.

title: Do not invert organization slug assignment
body: The previous code assigned the organization slug when team billing was disabled and stored only requestedSlug when billing was enabled. This change reverses the slug condition: billing-disabled installations now create organizations without a slug, while billing-enabled installations assign the requested slug immediately rather than deferring it. This unrelated change breaks organization URL provisioning and should retain the original condition.

title: Guard the missing destination before checking its integration
body: When Google Meet is selected and destinationCalendar is null or empty, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar. Accessing its integration throws instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. Bookings with a missing/disconnected destination calendar therefore fail during event creation.

title: Select the destination belonging to the current credential
body: EventManager now calls this service separately for each collective host but passes the entire destinationCalendar array each time. This service always uses the first host's calendar ID, including when authenticated as another host. With distinct Office 365 accounts, secondary-host event creation targets an inaccessible calendar and fails. LarkCalendarService and BaseCalendarService have the same first-element problem; these services must select by the credential being used or receive an event containing only its destination.

title: Preserve credential IDs on video references
body: The reference builder now sets credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result, discarding the credentialId supplied by createMeeting. Cancellation only deletes video meetings when the video reference has a credentialId, so newly created Zoom and other dedicated video meetings will no longer be deleted when their bookings are cancelled.

title: Restore a usable calendar fallback for references without an external ID
body: When externalCalendarId is null or missing, the new fallback searches for a destination whose externalId equals that same null/missing value, which cannot match a normal destination. Google updateEvent consequently receives no calendarId and fails for older references lacking an externalCalendarId, even when the event has a valid destination. The analogous deleteEvent change falls back to primary rather than the configured destination, leaving events on non-primary calendars undeleted.

title: Initialize the destination array before adding collective hosts
body: If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null. The optional push then silently drops all teamDestinationCalendars, even if the other collective hosts have connected calendars. Those hosts receive no calendar events; the array should still contain their destinations when the organizer has none.

title: Cancel recurring events using each reference's own credential
body: For an all-remaining recurring cancellation, the code ignores the credential resolved for the current reference and instead loops only over the booking owner's credentials, deleting only the first calendar reference of each updated booking. The outer loop repeats this operation for every host rather than deleting each host's reference. Secondary collective hosts' recurring events therefore remain on their calendars even though all bookings are marked cancelled.

title: Do not reverse the billing-dependent organization slug condition
body: This unrelated change reverses the condition for persisting the organization slug: installations with team billing disabled now create organizations without a slug, while billing-enabled installations immediately persist the requested slug. Previously the former received the slug and the latter stored only requestedSlug in metadata. This breaks organization URL provisioning on non-billing installations and bypasses the deferred slug assignment behavior on billing-enabled installations.

title: Computed Zod keys do not validate or preserve token expiry fields
body: Using a Zod schema's toString() as an object key produces a literal key such as "[object Object]", not a dynamic property validator. The two computed keys also collide. Since z.object strips unknown properties, synced responses lose expires_in, expiry_date, and refresh_token instead of preserving them. Consumers such as Zoom then calculate expiry from undefined and cannot persist usable credentials. Define explicit supported fields or a passthrough schema with appropriate expiry validation.

title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a placeholder
body: This helper assigns the literal string "refresh_token" whenever the parsed response omits a refresh token, including when credential sharing is disabled. Office 365 permits refresh_token to be absent and previously retained the existing token when merging the response. The new placeholder overwrites that valid token in the database, causing the next refresh to fail. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not return a replacement.

title: Persist the parsed token data rather than the safeParse result
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse wrapper { success: true, data: ... }, whereas the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse returned the credentials themselves. Saving this wrapper as credential.key removes access_token and refresh_token from the expected top-level location. After any Google token refresh, even with syncing disabled, subsequent service construction fails googleCredentialSchema validation.

title: Normalize the sync response for SDK and Axios callers
body: The sync branch returns a native fetch Response, but the fallback branch returns whatever the provider callback returns. Google and the Zoho integrations read response.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly from an SDK token object. None of those properties exist on a fetch Response, regardless of the JSON returned by the sync endpoint. Enabling syncing therefore breaks refreshes for these integrations. Parse and normalize the response or adapt each caller to the sync response contract.

title: Pass the user ID rather than the credential ID to token syncing
body: The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is a Cal.com user ID, but Bigin passes credentialId. The helper sends that value as calcomUserId to the parent platform, requesting tokens for the wrong user whenever these IDs differ. This can fail refreshes or associate another user's tokens with this credential. Carry credential.userId through to this call; team credentials should retain the provider fallback.

title: Import Prisma before using it in Salesforce refresh
body: The new getClient implementation calls prisma.credential.update, but this file does not import or declare prisma. This fails TypeScript checking and throws ReferenceError at runtime after a successful token request, preventing Salesforce client initialization and event operations.

title: Use the installed Zoom app slug in sync requests
body: The refresh request sends appSlug "zoomvideo", but Zoom credentials and the callback use the app ID/slug "zoom". A parent app store resolving the supplied appSlug against the same slugs used by the credential webhook cannot find this integration. Send "zoom" so refresh and credential creation identify the same app.

title: Computed Zod keys do not validate or preserve expiry fields
body: Calling toString() on a Zod schema produces a literal property name (normally "[object Object]"), not a wildcard for response properties. Both computed keys therefore collide, and this z.object also strips unrecognized properties such as expires_in, expiry_date and refresh_token. With credential sharing enabled, valid refresh responses lose their expiry and refresh token; Zoom then computes a NaN expiry and other integrations cannot persist usable refreshed credentials. Use explicit supported fields or a passthrough schema with appropriate validation.

title: Do not replace omitted refresh tokens with a placeholder
body: This helper injects the literal string "refresh_token" whenever a response omits a refresh token, including when credential sharing is disabled. Office365 explicitly allows refresh_token to be omitted and merges the parsed response into the existing credentials, so this now overwrites the real stored refresh token with an unusable placeholder. The following refresh fails and the user must reconnect. Preserve the existing token when the provider does not return a replacement.

title: Persist parsed Google credentials rather than the safeParse result
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result envelope, { success: true, data: ... }, whereas the previous schema.parse returned the credential object itself. Writing this result directly to credential.key stores the envelope instead of access_token, refresh_token and expiry_date at the top level. The next GoogleCalendarService construction fails googleCredentialSchema.parse, breaking calendar access after a refresh even with syncing disabled. Store the result's data.

title: Normalize sync responses to the contracts expected by SDK callers
body: The sync branch returns a native fetch Response, but several callers still expect the result of their original refresh function: Google and both Zoho integrations read response.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly from a decoded SDK object. A native Response has none of those properties, regardless of its JSON body, so enabling syncing makes these refreshes throw or store invalid tokens. Decode and adapt the sync response for these callers, or change them to consume a consistent response contract.

title: Pass the Bigin credential owner's user ID to the sync endpoint
body: The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is a Cal.com user ID, but this call passes credentialId. Consequently the external endpoint receives a credential table primary key as calcomUserId instead of the owner's ID. Since those IDs are unrelated, it can fail to find the account or return another user's credentials when the numbers coincide. Carry credential.userId through the refresh method and pass that value; team credentials should retain the null-user fallback.

title: Import Prisma before using it in Salesforce refresh
body: The new refresh path calls prisma.credential.update, but this module does not import or declare prisma. This fails TypeScript checking and, if transpiled without checking, throws ReferenceError on every Salesforce client initialization. Import the Prisma client used by the other integration services.

title: Send the Zoom app slug rather than its integration directory name
body: The refresh request sends appSlug: "zoomvideo", but Zoom credentials are registered with appId "zoom" and the OAuth callback also uses the slug "zoom". An external app store routing refreshes by the supplied appSlug cannot match this request to the Zoom app, preventing refreshes for synced Zoom credentials. Send "zoom" consistently.

title: Computed Zod keys do not preserve expiry fields
body: Calling toString() on a Zod schema produces a literal property name (normally "[object Object]"), not a wildcard key validator. The second computed property also overwrites the first, and z.object strips unrecognized properties. Consequently, synced responses lose expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token, and other actual token fields. For example, Zoom computes its saved expiry from an undefined expires_in. Use an explicit response schema or a catchall/passthrough schema with a defined expiry contract.

title: Google saves the safeParse result instead of credential data
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse wrapper { success: true, data: ... }, but this code writes that entire wrapper into credential.key. This happens even when credential syncing is disabled. After the first successful refresh, the stored key no longer has access_token and other Google credential fields at its top level, so subsequent GoogleCalendarService instances cannot parse it. Save the parsed data rather than the wrapper.

title: Sync returns a Fetch Response to callers expecting SDK or Axios objects
body: The sync branch returns an unparsed Fetch Response, whereas the fallback preserves each caller's native return shape. Google reads res.data, HubSpot reads accessToken/expiresIn directly, and Zoho CRM and Bigin read tokenInfo.data. None of these properties exists on a Fetch Response, so their synced refreshes throw or use undefined tokens even if the endpoint returns valid JSON. Normalize the response and adapt these callers to the same contract.

title: Bigin sends a credential ID as the Cal.com user ID
body: The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is a userId, which is posted as calcomUserId to the parent application. Bigin instead passes credentialId. Credential IDs and user IDs are independent, so the endpoint looks up the wrong user (or no user), and may return another user's credentials. Pass the credential's userId through to this method.

title: New Salesforce persistence uses an unimported Prisma client
body: The added prisma.credential.update call references prisma without importing or declaring it anywhere in this file. This fails TypeScript checking and, if transpiled without checking, throws ReferenceError on every Salesforce client initialization after token refresh. Import the Prisma client before using it.

title: Missing refresh tokens are replaced with an unusable literal
body: This helper inserts the literal "refresh_token" whenever the response omits refresh_token, including when syncing is disabled. Office365's response schema explicitly allows omission, and its caller merges parsed data over the existing credential. The inserted literal therefore overwrites the valid stored refresh token, causing the next refresh to fail. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not return a replacement.

title: Zoom refresh uses a different app slug from credential installation
body: The sync request sends appSlug "zoomvideo", but Zoom credentials are installed with appId "zoom" and the webhook accepts the app-store slug. A parent app store looking up credentials using the supplied slug cannot match Zoom refresh requests to the installed app. Send "zoom", consistently with the callback and webhook contract.

title: Use OR for team admin or owner authorization
body: The team authorization requires both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner to succeed. Admin and owner are distinct membership roles, so a team administrator or owner who is not also the booking organizer or an attendee is denied permission to add guests. Combine these checks with OR to implement the intended admin-or-owner permission.

title: Update the calendar using the booking organizer's credentials
body: The handler permits attendees and team administrators to add guests, but constructs EventManager with the requesting user's credentials rather than the booking organizer's. When an attendee adds a guest, the calendar reference belongs to the organizer and cannot be updated using the attendee's calendar credentials. This leaves the persisted attendee list out of sync with the organizer's calendar (or fails after the database insert). Use the booking owner's credentials for the calendar update.

title: Deduplicate incoming guests on the server
body: uniqueGuests only filters against existing booking attendees; it does not remove duplicates within the incoming guests array, and the server schema accepts duplicate addresses. A direct mutation with the same email twice therefore passes both entries to createMany, creating duplicate attendees or failing on a database uniqueness constraint. The dialog's client-side refinement does not protect this endpoint; validate or deduplicate the request on the server.

title: Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist
body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased, but incoming guest addresses are compared without lowercasing. A blacklisted address submitted with uppercase characters passes this filter and receives an invitation. Normalize incoming addresses before blacklist comparison and persistence.

title: Honor disabled standard email settings for guest additions
body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally emails the organizer and every attendee, unlike the other booking notification functions which respect eventTypeDisableHostEmail and eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail. Consequently, adding guests sends standard emails even for event types configured to disable them, including existing attendees who should receive no standard notifications. Pass the event type metadata through the handler and apply the same suppression checks here.

title: Use OR for team admin/owner authorization
body: The team permission check requires the caller to be both a team admin and a team owner. These are alternative membership roles, so a team admin or owner who is not also the booking organizer or an attendee is rejected with FORBIDDEN. Combine the checks with OR so either authorized role can add guests.

title: Update the calendar using the booking organizer's credentials
body: The handler allows attendees and team administrators to add guests, but constructs EventManager with the caller and the caller's credentials. The booking's calendar references belong to the organizer, not necessarily the caller. When an attendee adds guests, the organizer's calendar event therefore cannot be reliably updated, even though the new attendees have already been persisted. Load the booking owner's credentials and use that owner for the calendar update.

title: Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist
body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased, but incoming guest addresses are compared without normalization. An address such as Blocked@example.com passes validation and bypasses a blacklist entry of blocked@example.com, allowing invitations to addresses explicitly configured as blocked. Normalize incoming addresses before performing this comparison.

title: Deduplicate guests on the server before inserting attendees
body: The variable uniqueGuests only filters addresses already in the booking; it does not remove duplicates within the request. The server schema accepts duplicate addresses, so a direct request containing the same new email twice sends both entries to createMany, resulting in duplicate attendee records or an insertion failure if uniqueness is enforced. The dialog's client-side refinement does not protect the API; enforce uniqueness on the server.

title: Honor event-type email suppression when sending guest updates
body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally sends organizer and attendee emails and accepts no event-type metadata. Other booking notification paths honor disableStandardEmails.all.host and disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding guests consequently sends standard notifications even for event types explicitly configured to suppress them, potentially duplicating custom workflow notifications. Pass the event-type metadata through and apply the same suppression checks.

title: Authorize team admins or owners, not both roles at once
body: The team authorization check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&. A team member with either the ADMIN or OWNER role should be allowed, but requiring both excludes admins/owners who are not also the booking organizer or an attendee. Use an OR check so team administrators can add guests to their team's bookings.

title: Update the calendar using the booking organizer's credentials
body: This handler allows attendees and team administrators to add guests, but constructs EventManager with the calling user's credentials rather than the booking organizer's. When an attendee adds a guest, those credentials cannot update the organizer's calendar event (and may contain no calendar integration at all). The database has already been updated at this point, leaving the attendee list out of sync with the actual calendar invitation. Load and use the booking owner's credentials for this update.

title: Deduplicate the submitted guest list on the server
body: uniqueGuests only removes addresses already present in the booking; it does not remove duplicates within guests. The server schema accepts repeated addresses, so a direct mutation with the same new email twice passes this filter and sends both entries to createMany, producing duplicate attendees or a database constraint failure. The dialog's uniqueness validation does not protect the API. Deduplicate or reject duplicate addresses server-side before writing.

title: Normalize guest emails before checking the blacklist
body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased when loaded, but the submitted guest address is compared without lowercasing it. A blacklisted address submitted with an uppercase character passes validation and is added and emailed. Normalize the submitted address before comparing it to the blacklist so casing cannot bypass this restriction.

title: Respect disabled standard-email settings for guest notifications
body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally emails the organizer and every attendee and does not accept event-type metadata. Other booking notification functions in this file honor disableStandardEmails.all.host and disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding a guest therefore sends standard booking emails even for event types configured to suppress them, potentially duplicating custom workflow notifications. Pass the event-type metadata from the handler and apply the existing host/attendee suppression checks.

title: Increment the retry counter atomically
body: Both failure paths write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read before processing the batch. If cron invocations overlap and both fail to schedule the same reminder, they write the same value, so two failed attempts are recorded as one and the reminder remains eligible for further attempts instead of reaching the deletion threshold. Use Prisma's atomic `increment` operation in both failure paths.

title: Do not let failure bookkeeping abort the entire batch
body: The catch block now awaits a Prisma update without handling errors from that update. If a reminder is deleted while the batch is processing (for example, by an overlapping cleanup invocation), the update throws a record-not-found error out of the catch block. This aborts the cron request and skips every remaining reminder in the batch; previously the scheduling error was logged and processing continued. Handle bookkeeping failures separately, including reminders that no longer exist, so one failed reminder cannot stop the batch.

title: Increment retryCount atomically instead of writing a stale value
body: Both failure paths set retryCount to the value fetched at the beginning of the cron run plus one. If two cron requests overlap and both fail to schedule the same reminder, they read the same count and overwrite each other, so two failures are recorded as only one. This allows reminders to exceed the intended two-failure limit. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths.

title: Do not let failure bookkeeping abort the remaining reminder batch
body: The new workflowReminder.update inside the catch block can itself throw and is not protected. For example, if a reminder is deleted after findMany (by a concurrent cleanup run or workflow deletion), scheduling or the success update can fail, and this catch then attempts to update a nonexistent row. Prisma throws, terminating the handler and leaving every remaining reminder in the batch unprocessed. Previously the catch logged the error and continued. Make the retry update tolerate deleted rows and preserve per-reminder error isolation.

title: Do not let retry bookkeeping abort the entire reminder batch
body: The catch block now awaits a Prisma update without handling failures from that update. If a reminder is deleted while this batch is running (for example, during booking cancellation or workflow removal), the update throws because the row no longer exists; a database outage likewise causes this error handler to throw. Previously the per-reminder catch logged the error and continued. Now the request exits early and all remaining reminders in the batch are skipped. Handle retry-update failures separately so one failed or removed reminder does not prevent unrelated SMS reminders from being scheduled.

title: Increment retry counts atomically instead of writing a stale snapshot
body: Both failure paths assign retryCount using the value read by findMany at the start of the request. If cron requests overlap and both attempt the same unscheduled reminder, they can read the same count and then write the same incremented value, losing one failed attempt. This allows more scheduling failures than the intended two-attempt limit. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths rather than computing the new count from the fetched reminder.

title: Preserve or migrate the existing findMany API
body: This replaces the public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method with `getBaseConditions()`, but the PR contains no migration of production consumers. These APIs are not interchangeable: `findMany` executed a query, honored selection and other query arguments, and applied authorization and filters, whereas `getBaseConditions` only returns a SQL fragment. Existing callers of `service.findMany(...)` will now fail type checking (or throw at runtime). Update all consumers to execute appropriately authorized raw queries in the same change, or retain a compatible query method until they are migrated.

title: Preserve or migrate the removed findMany API
body: The exported InsightsBookingService no longer exposes findMany; it now only returns SQL fragments through getBaseConditions. Existing callers of findMany will fail type checking (or throw at runtime), and callers using the previous WhereInput-returning condition methods cannot pass the new Sql objects to Prisma model queries. This PR updates only the integration test, not production consumers. Migrate all consumers to parameterized $queryRaw queries in the same change, or retain a compatible querying API until that migration is complete.

title: Removing findMany breaks the existing service API
body: This replaces the public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method with `getBaseConditions()`, but the PR only migrates the integration test and does not provide a compatibility method or migrate production consumers. Existing callers of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` will no longer compile (or will throw at runtime), and a SQL condition is not a drop-in replacement for the previous query execution, selection, and pagination API. Preserve the existing method until consumers are migrated, or include the consumer migrations in this change.

title: Invalidate connected calendar queries after deleting cached data
body: The delete-cache mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The wrapper passes props.onChanged directly, which is optional and does not itself refresh the wrapper's query, and that query disables refetchOnWindowFocus. Consequently, a successful deletion can leave the old cache timestamp and Delete cached data action visible even though the cache no longer exists. Invalidate the connected-calendar queries on success, as the disconnect mutation already does, so all scopes display the updated cache status.

title: Invalidate connected calendar queries after deleting cache
body: The cache deletion success handler only invokes the optional onSuccess callback and never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The wrapper displaying cacheUpdatedAt owns that query but merely forwards props.onChanged, which is optional and does not guarantee a refetch; it also disables refetchOnWindowFocus. Consequently, after a successful deletion the dropdown can continue showing the old cache timestamp and offering deletion of data that no longer exists. Invalidate the connected calendar queries on successful cache deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

title: Invalidate connected calendars after deleting cached data
body: The cache deletion mutation only invokes the optional onSuccess callback and never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The wrapper gets cacheUpdatedAt from that query, disables refetchOnWindowFocus, and does not provide a default onChanged callback that refreshes it. Consequently, a successful deletion leaves the old cache timestamp and delete action visible until the query is otherwise refreshed. Invalidate the connected-calendars query on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

title: Make the environment-file update work with GNU sed
body: The command uses the BSD/macOS form `sed -i ''`, which fails with GNU sed on Linux because the empty argument is interpreted as the script rather than an in-place backup suffix. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, the script therefore leaves the old tunnel URL in the environment file but still prints a success message. Subsequent webhook subscriptions use the stale URL. Use a portable update mechanism or handle BSD and GNU sed separately, and check the update's exit status.

title: Cancel imminent reminders immediately instead of waiting for cron
body: Scheduled emails are now only marked cancelled, even when their send time is before the next 15-minute cron run. For example, cancelling a booking five minutes before its reminder sends leaves the email scheduled at SendGrid until after delivery. The cron also deletes past reminders before processing cancellations, so it then discards this cancellation entirely. Reminders close to their send time need an immediate cancellation path.

title: Reschedules still bypass the pending-cancellation limit workaround
body: Every rescheduled booking passes immediateDelete=true, which immediately creates a SendGrid pending cancellation regardless of how far away the reminder is. This retains the 100-pending-cancellations failure described by this PR for reschedules. Furthermore, that branch catches API errors without marking the reminder cancelled, so when the limit is reached the cron cannot retry and the old booking's reminder is still sent. Reschedules should use deferred cancellation with a persisted retry state, except when immediate cancellation is necessary.

title: Persist successful cancellations before another request can fail
body: The cancellation loop accumulates lazy Prisma delete promises and executes them only after every SendGrid request succeeds. If any request fails, execution jumps to the catch and none of the successfully cancelled reminders are deleted. Subsequent cron runs therefore submit those same batch IDs again; an already-cancelled batch can fail and repeatedly prevent later reminders from being processed. Persist each successful cancellation and handle errors per reminder so one failed request cannot block the rest of the queue.

title: Await reminder cancellation database operations before returning
body: The cancellation helpers now perform the database deletion or cancelled-state update themselves, but their promises are discarded inside forEach. Previously the reminder database deletions were included in the awaited Promise.all. The handler can now return successfully before cancellation is persisted, and a serverless request may finish before these operations complete, leaving reminders active. Collect and await both email and SMS helper promises; the same issue occurs in the changed requestReschedule handler.

title: Cancel imminent reminders immediately instead of waiting for cron
body: Scheduled emails are now only marked cancelled, even when their send time is before the next 15-minute cron run. For example, cancelling a booking five minutes before its reminder is due leaves the email scheduled in SendGrid until after it is sent. The cron also deletes past-due reminder rows before processing cancellations, so it cannot recover this case. Reminders close to their send time need immediate provider cancellation.

title: Await reminder cancellations before completing the request
body: The cancellation helpers now perform the database deletion or cancelled-flag update, but their promises are discarded inside forEach and are not included in the awaited promises below. Previously the database reminder deletions were explicitly awaited. The handler can therefore return success before cancellation is persisted; in a serverless deployment, execution can stop after the response, leaving reminders active for a cancelled booking. Collect and await these helper promises, including the equivalent request-reschedule and workflow-update call sites.

title: Keep immediate cancellations recoverable when SendGrid rejects them
body: The immediateDelete path still submits cancellations arbitrarily far ahead of the send date, which consumes the same 100 pending-cancellation slots described in this PR. handleNewBooking uses this path for every reschedule. If SendGrid rejects a cancellation because that limit is reached, the error is swallowed and the reminder is never marked cancelled, so cron will not retry it and the old booking's email will still be sent. Workflow and step deletion also use this path and then cascade-delete the reminder rows, losing any retry opportunity.

title: Persist successful cancellations before another request can fail
body: The Prisma delete promises accumulated in the loop are lazy and execute only at Promise.all after every SendGrid cancellation succeeds. If any provider request fails, control jumps to the outer catch and none of the earlier successfully cancelled reminders are deleted. On subsequent runs those batches are submitted again; an already-cancelled batch can itself be rejected by SendGrid, repeatedly aborting processing before later reminders are reached. Handle failures per reminder and persist each successful cancellation independently so one failed batch cannot block all remaining cancellations.

title: Deferred cancellation misses reminders due before the next cron run
body: Booking cancellation now only marks scheduled emails as cancelled, while this job performs the SendGrid cancellation every 15 minutes. If a booking is cancelled five minutes before its reminder is due and the next cron run is ten minutes away, SendGrid still sends the reminder. The job then deletes the expired reminder at lines 34–41 before it can attempt cancellation. Reminders close to their send time need immediate cancellation rather than relying exclusively on the cron.

title: Immediate reschedule cancellation retains the original SendGrid quota problem
body: Rescheduling passes immediateDelete=true for every old email reminder, causing an immediate SendGrid cancellation even when the reminder is days away. These cancellations occupy the same 100 pending-cancellation slots that motivated this PR. Furthermore, the immediateDelete branch returns without marking the reminder cancelled, so if SendGrid rejects the request because the quota is full, the cron will never retry it. Repeated reschedules can therefore still cause old booking reminders to be sent; reschedules need the deferred cancellation/retry path as well.

title: One failed cancellation prevents persistence of all preceding successes
body: The Prisma delete calls are lazy promises accumulated until after every SendGrid request succeeds. If any request in the loop fails, execution jumps to the outer catch without executing any of those deletes, including deletes for batches successfully cancelled earlier. Those records are fetched again next run, and attempting to cancel an already cancelled batch can fail and repeatedly block later cancellations. Persist each successful cancellation before moving on and handle failures per reminder so one batch cannot prevent processing the rest.

title: Await reminder cancellation updates before completing the request
body: The cancellation helpers now perform the database deletion or cancelled=true update themselves, but their promises are discarded inside forEach and are not included in the awaited operations. Previously the database reminder deletions were collected and awaited. The handler can now return before these critical writes finish; on a serverless deployment execution can be suspended at that point, leaving reminders unmarked or unscheduled reminders still available to the scheduler. Collect and await the helper promises before responding.

title: Defer dynamic imports until the corresponding app is requested
body: Each import() is executed immediately when the app-store registry is evaluated, so importing the registry still starts loading and evaluating every app, including apps unused by the request. This does not provide on-demand loading and adds concurrent chunk loading to cold starts. Store loader functions and invoke only the selected loader instead. It also avoids leaving rejected imports for unused apps without a rejection handler.

title: Await the async reschedule cleanup callbacks
body: The new async callback is passed to forEach, which discards its returned promise. In particular, failures while importing or constructing the calendar in getCalendar now become rejected promises that the surrounding try/catch cannot catch; previously synchronous calendar-construction errors were caught there. Reschedule can report success with cleanup still running or failed, and these failures can produce unhandled rejections. Await a mapped Promise.all (or use an awaited loop) inside the try/catch. The same change is needed in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.

title: Defer import execution until an app is requested
body: Every import() in this object executes as soon as the app-store index is loaded, so accessing a single calendar or payment provider still starts loading and evaluating all app packages. This splits the modules into chunks but does not defer unused apps, retaining the all-app initialization cost on cold starts. Store loader functions instead and invoke only the selected loader at the call sites. This also allows import failures to be handled by the requesting caller rather than leaving rejected promises for unused apps unobserved.

title: Defer dynamic imports until the app is requested
body: Each import() is invoked while the appStore object is constructed, so importing this registry still starts loading and evaluating every app, even when a request only needs one calendar or payment provider. This does not provide on-demand loading and retains the startup work this change is intended to avoid. Store loader functions instead, and invoke only the selected loader at each consumer.

title: Await the asynchronous reschedule cleanup callbacks
body: The new async forEach callback returns a promise that forEach discards. In particular, failures from the now-asynchronous getCalendar call (including CalendarService constructor failures) no longer reach the surrounding try/catch and become unhandled rejections. Reschedule can report success without handling those failures. Await a Promise.all over mapped callbacks, or use an awaited loop, so cleanup errors reach the logger. The same newly introduced callback change exists in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.

title: Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts
body: When a slot's date has an override, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before checking the host's busy times. An override defines working availability, not an exemption from existing bookings or calendar conflicts. Consequently, both fixed and round-robin hosts can be shown as available during an existing meeting on an override date. Validate the override window and then continue through the busy-time checks.

title: Override validation accepts slots only partially inside availability
body: The override checks reject slots ending at or before the override start and slots starting after its end, but do not require the whole slot to fit inside the override. For example, a fixed host with a 10:00–11:00 override accepts a 09:30–10:30 or 10:30–11:30 slot generated by a round-robin host. A slot starting exactly at 11:00 also passes. Require slotStartTime >= override start and slotEndTime <= override end for at least one override interval.

title: Split working hours reject slots inside valid intervals
body: The workingHours.find predicate rejects a slot if it falls outside any working-hours interval on that weekday, rather than accepting it if it fits inside at least one interval. For a schedule with 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the afternoon interval, and afternoon slots are rejected by the morning interval. This newly added check removes valid availability for ordinary split-day schedules. Check for containment in an applicable interval, using the slot end time rather than the slot start for the end boundary.

title: Timezone conversion discards date changes at midnight
body: The converted override boundaries are reduced to hour/minute values without preserving a day rollover, while activeOverrides is still selected using the unconverted override start date. For example, a UTC organizer's 22:00–23:00 override viewed in UTC+3 becomes 01:00–02:00 but is inserted into the original attendee date instead of the following date. An interval crossing attendee midnight can also produce startTime > endTime and disappear entirely. Convert the full override interval to attendee time, select it by overlap with the attendee day, and clip or split it at day boundaries before extracting minutes.

title: Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflict checks
body: When an override exists on the slot's date, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before evaluating busy times. An override defines working availability, not permission to ignore existing bookings or external calendar events. Consequently, personal events and fixed or round-robin hosts with an override can expose slots that overlap their existing bookings. Continue to the busy-time checks after validating the override.

title: Override validation checks overlap instead of full slot containment
body: The new override checks reject only slots ending at or before the override start or starting after its end. For a fixed host available from 10:00 to 11:00, a round-robin slot from 09:30 to 10:30 or 10:30 to 11:30 therefore passes, even though the host is unavailable for part of the meeting. A slot starting exactly at 11:00 also passes. Require the entire slot to fit within an override interval.

title: Multiple override intervals reject slots inside a valid interval
body: dateOverrides.find searches for any interval that excludes the slot, rather than an interval that contains it. If a host has overrides of 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00 on the same date, a 10:00 slot is rejected by the afternoon interval and a 15:00 slot by the morning interval. Split date-override availability can therefore lose all its slots. Group overrides by date and accept containment in any of that date's intervals.

title: Working-hours validation rejects ordinary split schedules
body: The workingHours.find predicate rejects a slot if it is outside any working-hours interval on that weekday. For a normal schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, morning slots fail against the afternoon interval and afternoon slots fail against the morning interval. Because every host now goes through this check, this removes valid slots even on dates without overrides. Validate that the full slot is contained in at least one applicable interval instead.

title: Timezone conversion discards midnight rollover
body: The converted override boundaries retain only hour and minute, discarding their date. For example, a UTC override from 22:00 to 23:00 viewed in UTC+01:30 becomes startTime 1410 and endTime 30. buildSlots discards that range because start is greater than end, so the valid 23:30–00:30 availability disappears. Converted overrides that cross an attendee's midnight need to be split across the corresponding attendee dates rather than reduced to a single minute-of-day range.

title: Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts
body: When an override exists for the slot's date, this function returns true before checking `busy`. Overrides specify working availability, not freedom from bookings or calendar events. A host with a 10:00–12:00 override and an existing 10:00–11:00 booking will therefore be advertised as available at 10:00. Continue through the busy-time checks after validating the override.

title: Split working hours reject slots inside either valid interval
body: The new working-hours check rejects a slot if it is outside any interval on that weekday, rather than accepting it if it fits at least one interval. For a normal split schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the afternoon interval, and afternoon slots are rejected because they are outside the morning interval. This can remove all availability for split schedules.

title: Override validation accepts partially overlapping slots
body: The override check only rejects slots that end before the override starts or start after it ends. It does not require the full event to fit inside the override. In a round-robin event, slots generated from another host's availability can therefore pass a fixed host's 10:00–11:00 override even when they run 09:30–10:30 or 10:30–11:30 (or start exactly at 11:00). Require slot start >= override start and slot end <= override end.

title: Multiple override intervals are treated as simultaneous constraints
body: Using `find` to reject a slot outside any override interval makes multiple intervals on the same date mutually exclusive. With overrides 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00, a morning slot is rejected by the afternoon interval and an afternoon slot by the morning interval. Check whether the slot fits any interval on the override date instead of rejecting it based on another interval.

title: Migration fails when no embed category is configured
body: The category query unconditionally indexes row 0 before converting the ID to an integer. If embed_category is unset (its default is empty), or names a category that no longer exists, the query returns no rows and this access raises instead of reaching the uncategorized fallback. Consequently, ordinary installations without embedding configured cannot run this migration or upgrade. Check for an empty result before reading the ID, and handle an absent fallback setting as well.

title: Normalize existing allowed hosts during migration
body: The migration inserts old embeddable_hosts entries verbatim, bypassing the new model's normalization callback. The old host check supported entries such as http://eviltrout.com and https://eviltrout.com, but the new lookup compares the stored value directly against URI.host, such as eviltrout.com. Those migrated entries will never match, so previously working embeds and topic retrieval stop working after upgrade. Normalize the migrated entries before inserting them.

title: Hosts saved with ports can never match an embedding URL
body: The host validator accepts entries such as example.com:8080, and the normalization callback preserves the port. record_for_host, however, extracts only URI.host and compares example.com against the stored example.com:8080. Thus an administrator can successfully save a port-qualified host but all requests from it are rejected and its category mapping is never used. Normalize storage and lookup consistently, or reject port-qualified entries explicitly.

title: Host validation rejects valid long top-level domains
body: The new validation restricts the final domain label to two through five letters. Valid embedding hosts such as example.museum or example.technology therefore cannot be added or saved, despite being ordinary DNS hostnames supported by the previous host lookup. Use hostname validation that supports valid longer top-level domains rather than this five-character limit.

title: Migration crashes when no embed category is configured
body: The category query can return no rows when embed_category is unset (its default is an empty string) or names a deleted category. Indexing [0]['id'] then dereferences nil before the uncategorized fallback is reached. This prevents migrations from completing on ordinary installations that have never configured embedding. Handle an empty result before accessing the row.

title: Migrated hosts are not normalized for the new lookup
body: The migration inserts old embeddable_hosts entries verbatim, bypassing the new model's normalization callback. The previous host check accepted entries such as http://eviltrout.com and https://eviltrout.com, but the new lookup compares the stored value directly with URI.host, which is only eviltrout.com. Those previously working configurations stop allowing embeds after upgrade, and the original settings are deleted. Normalize migrated entries to the same representation used by the new lookup.

title: Hosts saved with ports can never match incoming URLs
body: The host validator accepts values such as example.com:8080 and the normalization callback preserves the port, but record_for_host compares that value against uri.host, which excludes the port. Thus a host successfully added as example.com:8080 will reject even http://example.com:8080 and will not supply its configured category to imports. Make storage and lookup agree on how ports are handled.

title: Host validation rejects valid longer top-level domains
body: The new format validation restricts the final domain label to two through five letters. Valid hosts such as example.museum or example.technology therefore cannot be added or saved in the embedding editor, although the previous host setting and lookup had no such restriction. Use hostname validation that supports valid longer top-level domains.

title: Migration crashes when no embedding category is configured
body: The category lookup unconditionally indexes the first result and reads ['id']. If embed_category is unset (its default is empty), or names a category that no longer exists, the SELECT returns no rows and this raises before the uncategorized fallback can run. This prevents upgrades and fresh database migrations on sites without a valid embedding configuration. Handle an empty result before reading the ID; the fallback query should likewise tolerate a missing setting row.

title: Normalize existing hosts before migrating them
body: Existing embeddable_hosts settings support entries such as 'http://eviltrout.com' and 'https://example.com/1234', but this INSERT copies entries verbatim and bypasses the new model's normalization callback. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares the stored value with URI.host, so these migrated entries never match. After the migration deletes the original settings, previously working embeds and topic retrieval stop working until administrators manually edit the hosts. Strip schemes and paths during migration using the same normalization as new records.

title: Host validation rejects valid longer top-level domains
body: The hostname validator limits the final domain label to two through five letters. Valid hosts such as example.museum and example.technology therefore cannot be added or saved in the embedding editor, despite being usable DNS names and previously accepted by the host setting. Use hostname validation that accommodates valid modern top-level domains.

title: Accepted hosts with ports can never match incoming URLs
body: The validator permits and the normalization callback retains a port, so an administrator can successfully save 'example.com:8080'. However, record_for_host extracts only URI.host ('example.com') and compares it to the entire stored value. Consequently that allowed-host record never authorizes even 'http://example.com:8080', and its category mapping is never used. Normalize ports away consistently or include the appropriate port in the lookup.

title: The new downsize definition replaces the existing width/height API
body: Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature: this second `self.downsize` definition replaces the definition accepting `max_width, max_height, opts`. Existing callers passing width and height now either raise ArgumentError (when also passing options) or pass the height as `opts`, causing `optimize` to fail when it accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`. Preserve a single method that supports both calling conventions, or give the dimensions-string variant a different name.

title: Large animated GIF uploads lose their animation even when allowed
body: The resize call passes the temporary file's path rather than a path with the original filename's extension. `OptimizedImage.optimize` only selects its animated implementation when the source path ends in `.gif`, but multipart upload temporary paths normally have no such extension. Consequently, even with `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled, a large animated GIF goes through the `convert` instructions using `[0]` and is permanently replaced by its first frame. Detect animation/image type independently of the temporary path before modifying the original upload.

title: The fixed size limit also overrides attachment upload settings
body: `validateUploadedFile` validates both images and attachments, but the new unconditional 10 MB limit replaces `max_attachment_size_kb` as well as the image limit. Attachments cannot benefit from the new image downsizing: sites permitting attachments larger than 10 MB now have valid uploads blocked in the browser, while sites with smaller attachment limits unnecessarily accept files for upload that the server will reject. Apply the relaxed limit only to images and retain the configured attachment limit.

title: The second downsize definition replaces the existing API
body: Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature: this definition replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` method. Existing callers supplying width, height, and options will now raise ArgumentError. Callers supplying only width and height will bind the height to `opts`, then fail when optimization accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`. Preserve both calling conventions in a single method or give the dimensions-string variant a separate name.

title: Large animated GIFs lose their animation even when it is allowed
body: The new downsizing call passes the upload's temporary path rather than its original filename. `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects animated processing only when the source path ends in `.gif`, but multipart upload tempfiles normally have no such extension. Consequently, even with `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled, a large animated GIF is processed by the static ImageMagick instructions, which read only frame `[0]`. Because this operation overwrites the upload itself, the animation is permanently discarded before storage. Detect the image format independently of the tempfile extension or use a correctly suffixed temporary file.

title: The new downsize definition replaces the existing width/height API
body: Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature: this second definition of `self.downsize` replaces the definition immediately above it. Existing calls using `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` now raise ArgumentError, and calls with four arguments treat the height as `opts`, causing `optimize` to fail when it accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`. Preserve the existing width/height interface or explicitly dispatch between the two supported forms.

title: Resizing uploaded GIFs discards animation even when animation is allowed
body: The controller passes the multipart tempfile path to `OptimizedImage.downsize`, but `optimize` selects its animated implementation only when that path ends in `.gif`. Multipart tempfile paths generally do not retain the uploaded filename extension, so even with `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled an oversized animated GIF goes through `convert` with the `[0]` frame selector. Because the conversion overwrites the upload itself, the remaining animation frames are permanently discarded. Select the animated processing path using the actual image format or original filename rather than the temporary path suffix.

title: Keep the configured size limit for non-image attachments
body: The fixed 10 MB validation limit applies to attachments as well as images, although the new server-side downsizing only handles images. Attachments exceeding `max_attachment_size_kb` now pass client validation and are uploaded only to be rejected by the server; conversely, sites configured to allow attachments larger than 10 MB can no longer upload them through this client. Apply the relaxed limit only to images and retain the configured attachment limit.

title: Do not change notification preferences through an authenticated GET
body: The new GET route invokes TopicsController#unsubscribe, which immediately saves a lower notification level for the currently logged-in user. GET requests are not protected by Rails' CSRF token verification, and the action also skips the XHR check. An external site can therefore navigate a logged-in user to this URL and disable their topic notifications without consent. Serve the preference page on GET and perform the mutation through a CSRF-protected POST.

title: Record the unsubscribe as an explicit user preference change
body: Saving notification_level directly leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged, unlike TopicUser.change, which records the user_changed reason. For automatically tracked topics whose reason is still nil, TopicUser.update_last_read automatically sets the level back to tracking once the reading-time threshold is reached. Consequently, a subsequent visit can undo the unsubscribe. Use the normal notification-change mechanism so the explicit preference is preserved.

title: Handle users without an existing TopicUser record
body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, but the action unconditionally reads tu.notification_level. The URL is not tied to the email recipient, so a user opening a forwarded email or opening it while logged into another account can have access to the topic without having a TopicUser row. That valid request raises NoMethodError and returns a server error instead of allowing the user to unsubscribe. Create or update the preference through TopicUser.change, which supports missing records.

title: Notification preferences are mutated by an unprotected GET request
body: The new GET unsubscribe route immediately saves notification preferences for the session's current user, without a recipient token or a POST confirmation. Rails CSRF protection does not protect GET requests, so another site can navigate a logged-in user to this URL and silently downgrade or mute notifications for a topic. Keep GET read-only and perform the change through a CSRF-protected request (or an appropriately validated recipient-specific unsubscribe token).

title: Direct save allows automatic tracking to undo unsubscribe
body: The unsubscribe action updates notification_level directly and saves the TopicUser without setting notifications_reason_id. For users whose topic tracking was automatic and whose reason is still nil, TopicUser.update_last_read explicitly restores tracking once the reading-time threshold is exceeded. Consequently, reading the topic after unsubscribing can undo this explicit preference. Use TopicUser.change, as set_notifications does, so the user_changed reason and notification-change metadata are recorded.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when the current user has no TopicUser record
body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for a visible topic the current user has never visited. This can happen when an email link is opened while logged into a different account or when a forwarded link is opened. The action then dereferences tu.notification_level and returns a server error instead of handling the unsubscribe. Resolve the default notification level and create the user's preference record when none exists.

title: Client-side entry never performs the unsubscribe operation
body: The Ember unsubscribe route only loads the ordinary topic view through PostStream.loadTopicView; it never calls the unsubscribe endpoint or changes the notification level. When this URL is entered through client-side navigation, the Rails HTML GET action does not run, yet the template tells the user they will stop receiving notifications. Ensure this flow explicitly performs the preference change rather than relying on an initial full-page server request.

title: Do not change notification preferences through an unprotected GET
body: The new GET endpoint changes the logged-in user's topic notification level using only the topic ID and session cookie. GET requests are not protected by Rails' CSRF verification, and unsubscribe explicitly skips the XHR check, so an external page can direct a logged-in user to this URL and unsubscribe or mute a topic without their consent. Render a confirmation page on GET and perform the change through a CSRF-protected POST, or require an appropriately scoped unsubscribe token.

title: Record unsubscribe as an explicit notification preference change
body: Saving notification_level directly bypasses TopicUser.change, which sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed and records notifications_changed_at. For users whose reason is still null, TopicUser.update_last_read automatically sets the level back to tracking once their reading time exceeds the auto-track threshold. Consequently, reading the topic after unsubscribing can silently undo the preference. Use the normal notification-change API so the unsubscribe is recorded as an explicit user choice.

title: Handle users without an existing TopicUser record
