title: Access-token matcher does not check the expected grant
body: The grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 of the six-character prefix, but this matcher reads substring(3, 5) and rejects equality rather than inequality. Consequently, a token with an incorrect grant (including the unknown 'na' grant) passes the authorization-code, refresh, device, and CIBA assertions as long as its suffix looks like a UUID. Check the prefix length and require substring(4, 6) to equal expectedGrantShortcut so these integration tests actually validate the newly encoded grant.

title: Shortcut contract recommends a length the decoder cannot accept
body: The new getShortcut() contract recommends a three-letter shortcut, whereas DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires a six-character context prefix and reads exactly two characters for the grant. A custom grant following this documentation will issue token IDs that the default encoder's own decoder rejects with IllegalArgumentException. Document the mandatory two-character length and validate it when registering grant factories, rather than allowing incompatible IDs to be issued.

title: Grant shortcut matcher uses the wrong offset and inverted comparison
body: The encoded grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 of the six-character prefix, but this matcher reads substring(3, 5) and returns false when it equals the expected shortcut. Consequently, IDs with an incorrect or unknown grant (for example onrtna instead of onrtac) pass the authorization-code assertion as long as the suffix looks like a UUID. Validate the prefix length and reject when substring(4, 6) does not equal the expected shortcut.

title: Shortcut contract recommends a length the decoder cannot support
body: The new getShortcut() contract recommends a three-letter shortcut, whereas DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires an exactly six-character context consisting of three two-character shortcuts. A custom grant following this documented contract will issue IDs with a seven-character prefix that the default decoder always rejects. Document the mandatory two-character length and validate it when registering grant shortcuts so invalid providers cannot issue undecodable IDs.

title: Grant-type matcher checks the wrong characters and reverses the comparison
body: The encoded grant shortcut occupies indexes 4 and 5, but this matcher reads substring(3, 5), and returns false when that substring equals the expected value rather than when it differs. Consequently, an ID such as 'onrtna:<uuid>' passes an authorization-code expectation of 'ac', so the updated integration assertions do not detect missing or incorrect grant context. Validate the prefix length and reject when substring(4, 6) does not equal the expected shortcut.

title: Shortcut contract permits values the encoder cannot decode
body: The new factory contract recommends a three-letter shortcut, while DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires an exactly six-character context prefix composed of three two-character shortcuts. The factory accepts longer shortcuts without validation and encodeTokenId emits them, so a custom grant implementing the documented three-letter shortcut produces token IDs that getTokenContextFromTokenId immediately rejects. Specify exactly two characters in the contract and validate that requirement when registering grant shortcuts.

title: Federated recovery-code validation never consumes a code
body: The new recovery-code validator returns true for any matching code without removing it or recording its use. In addition, getCredentials() reconstructs a fresh credential from the complete original list on every call. Consequently, the same recovery code can authenticate repeatedly, the login form always requests the first code, and exhaustion never triggers regeneration. The new integration test only performs one login, so it passes despite this broken one-time-code lifecycle. Consume successful codes in the test provider and test replay rejection, progression to the next code, and exhaustion.

title: Consume recovery codes and test their one-time-use lifecycle
body: The new recovery-code validator accepts any code in the original list without removing or marking it used, and getCredentials() reconstructs a fresh credential from that unchanged list on every call. Consequently, the same recovery code can authenticate indefinitely, the login form always requests the first code, and exhaustion never triggers replacement. The new integration test only performs one login, so it passes despite these violations of the recovery-code contract. Make the test provider persist consumption and extend the test to verify rejection of a reused code, progression to the next code, and replacement after exhaustion.

title: Consume recovery codes in the test provider and test their lifecycle
body: The new recovery-code validator returns true for any matching code without removing or marking it used. Moreover, getCredentials() reconstructs the credential from the unchanged full list on every call. Consequently, the same recovery code can authenticate indefinitely, the login form always requests code 0, and the exhausted-code regeneration path is never exercised. The new integration test only performs one login, so it passes despite this violation of the single-use recovery-code contract. Make successful validation consume the code, expose the remaining-code state, and test replay rejection, progression to the next code, and regeneration after exhaustion.

title: Wait for the reader to finish before checking its exceptions
body: The reader thread can still be executing a groups request when deletedAll is set and caughtExceptions is asserted. If that in-flight request fails, it can add its exception after the assertion, allowing this regression test to pass despite the concurrency failure it is intended to detect. Keep a reference to the thread and join it before asserting; stop and join it in a finally block as well, since a deletion failure currently leaves the reader looping indefinitely and issuing requests during later tests.

title: Wait for the reader to finish before asserting its failures
body: Setting deletedAll does not wait for the reader's in-flight groups request to complete. That request can fail and add its exception after the empty-list assertion has already passed, so this regression test can miss the concurrent-access failure it is intended to detect. Retain the reader thread and join it before asserting, and signal shutdown in a finally block so a failed deletion does not leave the reader running indefinitely.

title: Wait for the reader to finish before checking its exceptions
body: Setting deletedAll does not wait for an in-flight groups request to complete. The assertion can run while the reader is still awaiting a response, so a failure from the concurrent deletion can be added to caughtExceptions after the test has already passed. Retain the reader thread and join it before asserting. Stop and join it in a finally block as well: if a deletion throws, the current code never sets deletedAll and leaves a non-daemon thread continuously issuing requests into subsequent tests.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate audit-log datetimes
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses this paginator with order_by="-datetime", so get_item_key receives a datetime, not a number. math.floor/math.ceil on that value raises TypeError when build_cursor processes any nonempty page, making optimized audit-log requests fail instead of returning logs. value_from_cursor also returns the raw numeric cursor rather than converting it to a datetime for the query. Use DateTimePaginator's key encoding and cursor decoding for this endpoint.

title: Negative offsets are not supported by Django QuerySet slicing
body: When advanced features are enabled and a cursor has a negative offset (for example, cursor=0:-1:0), this branch passes a negative slice start to a Django QuerySet. Django rejects negative indexing with ValueError; it does not handle the boundary automatically as the comment claims. Consequently, the explicitly advertised negative-offset feature fails before executing a query. Reject such cursors with a pagination error or implement reverse traversal using supported nonnegative slicing and query ordering.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate audit-log datetime values
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses this paginator with order_by="-datetime", so get_item_key receives a datetime object. math.floor/math.ceil cannot convert a datetime and raise TypeError when build_cursor processes any nonempty result set. Consequently, eligible users requesting optimized_pagination=true get a server error instead of audit logs. The cursor conversion also returns a raw number rather than a datetime for subsequent queries. Use the DateTimePaginator key encoding and decoding for this endpoint.

title: Django querysets do not support the advertised negative-offset slicing
body: When advanced features are enabled and a cursor has a negative offset (for example, 0:-1:0), this branch passes that offset directly to QuerySet slicing. Django explicitly rejects negative slice indices with ValueError; it does not handle these boundary conditions automatically as the comment claims. Thus the new negative-offset feature produces a server error rather than reverse pagination. Translate offsets into supported nonnegative queries or reject them with a pagination validation error before slicing.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate the audit log datetime field
body: The audit log endpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to the field value. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so any nonempty optimized response raises TypeError when build_cursor computes its keys. value_from_cursor also returns a number unchanged rather than converting it to a datetime for the SQL comparison. Use the DateTimePaginator key encoding and decoding for this endpoint; otherwise enabling optimized_pagination breaks audit log retrieval.

title: Negative offsets are not supported by Django QuerySet slicing
body: The advanced-feature branch passes a negative cursor offset directly into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet.__getitem__ rejects negative slice bounds with ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'); it does not handle these boundary conditions automatically as the comment claims. Thus the advertised negative-offset feature always fails for the audit log queryset. Validate and reject unsupported offsets as a pagination error, or implement reverse traversal using supported queries rather than negative slicing.

title: Migrate or version Redis keys before changing sets to sorted sets
body: The new ZADD and ZSCAN operations reuse the same span-buf:s:* keys that the previous consumer populated with Redis sets. Existing buffered segments therefore cause WRONGTYPE errors on insertion or flushing after deployment; during a rolling deployment, old and new consumers also cannot read each other's buffers. This can stall ingestion and leave buffered spans to expire without being produced. Use a versioned namespace with a drain strategy, or explicitly migrate existing keys before switching operations.

title: Use datetime cursor conversion for the audit-log paginator
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint selects this paginator with order_by='-datetime', but get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on AuditLogEntry.datetime, which is a datetime object rather than a number. An optimized request with any results therefore raises TypeError while building its cursors instead of returning audit logs. value_from_cursor also returns the numeric cursor unchanged rather than converting it to a datetime for the database comparison. Inherit DateTimePaginator or implement its timestamp conversions.

title: Reject negative offsets instead of passing them to Django slicing

title: Honor the configured span-count limit during eviction
body: Eviction is hard-coded to 1000 spans while SpansBuffer still accepts and stores max_segment_spans, and the flush-time enforcement of that parameter has been removed. A caller configuring a smaller limit now receives segments above that limit, while a caller configuring a larger limit silently loses spans at 1000. Pass the configured limit to the script and apply it there, or explicitly remove the configuration contract rather than leaving it ineffective.

Existing buffered segments remain Redis sets, so new ingestion into those keys and flushing them will fail with WRONGTYPE after deployment. Mixed-version consumers also cannot read each other's buffers. Introduce a versioned key namespace with a drain strategy, or explicitly migrate/drain existing keys before switching commands, to avoid blocking processing and losing buffered segments.

Django explicitly raises ValueError for negative indexes; it does not handle them automatically as the comment claims. An authorized caller supplying a negative offset therefore gets a server error rather than reverse pagination. Reject invalid offsets with a pagination error or implement reverse traversal using supported queryset operations.

title: Changing existing Redis set keys to sorted sets requires a migration

Existing buffered segments therefore cause WRONGTYPE errors on insertion or flushing after deployment, and old and new workers cannot safely share these keys during a rolling deployment. This can stall ingestion and leave buffered spans to expire without being emitted. Introduce a versioned key namespace or an explicit drain/conversion rollout before switching Redis types.

title: Insertion eviction ignores the configured segment span limit
body: The Lua script always truncates segments to 1000 spans, while SpansBuffer still exposes max_segment_spans and the flush-time enforcement of that setting has been removed. A buffer configured with a smaller limit now emits segments above its configured limit, and one configured with a larger limit silently loses spans at 1000 anyway. Pass the configured limit into the script and define the corresponding eviction behavior rather than leaving the public configuration ineffective.

title: Substring matching does not establish that a Discover query contains only errors
body: The presence of `event.type:error` anywhere in the query enables upsampling, including queries such as `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. These queries can select transactions, despite the helper's requirement that sample-weight aggregation apply only to errors. Consequently, valid Discover requests can be rewritten to aggregate a field that is not supported for transactions, causing query failures or incorrect counts. Determine eligibility from parsed filter semantics rather than a substring search, and add coverage for negation and OR expressions.

title: Top-event selection still uses unweighted counts
body: For top-events requests, only `timeseries_columns` is transformed to `upsampled_count()`, while `selected_columns` and `orderby` are still taken unchanged from the request. A request grouping by a field and ordering by `count()` therefore chooses its top groups using stored event counts but plots their sample-weighted counts. With different sampling rates, the groups with the largest estimated error volume can be omitted in favor of groups with more stored events. Apply consistent upsampling to the aggregates used for top-group selection and ordering, and test groups with different sample weights.

title: Substring matching does not establish an errors-only query
body: The presence of `event.type:error` anywhere in the raw query does not mean the query selects only errors. For example, `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` both pass this check. For allowlisted projects on Discover, these requests are consequently rewritten to aggregate `sample_weight` even though they select transactions, which this helper explicitly says do not have that field. This can produce incorrect counts or query failures. Determine eligibility from parsed query constraints rather than a substring.

title: Top-event selection still uses the unweighted count
body: Only `timeseries_columns` is transformed for top-events requests; `selected_columns` and `orderby` still come directly from the original request. A request selecting and ordering by `count()` therefore chooses its top groups by stored event count, then displays their weighted counts. With different client sample rates, a group with fewer stored events can have the largest upsampled count and still be omitted from the chart. Apply consistent weighted aggregation to the top-group selection and ordering as well as the returned time series.

title: Use the dataset and query actually being executed for eligibility
body: The eligibility check uses the outer `dataset` and the original request query instead of `scoped_dataset` and the `query` passed to this invocation. The dashboard-splitting path explicitly calls this function with Discover and an errors-only query while the outer dataset is metrics-enhanced performance. The helper rejects that outer dataset, so counts for sampled error events remain unweighted in those dashboard results, including widgets already classified as error events. Base eligibility on the scoped execution context so these error queries receive the same upsampling as direct error queries.

title: Parse the query before deciding it contains only errors
body: The substring check treats queries such as `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` as error-only queries. For allowlisted projects this replaces count() with a sample-weight sum even though the query excludes errors or includes transactions, which this helper explicitly says do not have sample_weight. This can produce incorrect counts or fail the query. Determine eligibility from parsed query constraints that actually restrict the result to errors, rather than the presence of this text.

title: Apply upsampling consistently to top-event selection and ordering
body: For topEvents requests, only timeseries_columns is transformed; selected_columns and orderby are still read unchanged from the request. A request selecting and sorting groups by count() therefore chooses its top groups using stored event counts, then displays sample-weighted counts for those groups. When groups have different sampling rates, the groups with the largest upsampled counts can be omitted and the displayed ranking is incorrect. Transform the count aggregation used in top-group selection and ordering consistently with the timeseries aggregation.

title: New table visualization discards the actual query results
body: When the organization has `use-table-widget-visualization`, every dashboard table is rendered with empty columns, empty data, and empty metadata instead of the fetched `result`. Consequently, enabling the feature makes populated table widgets appear empty. Pass the result data and metadata and the configured columns to the new visualization before switching away from the existing table.

title: Include the organization in the attribute query cache key
body: The new React Query key contains only a constant and query options, while the query function requests an organization-specific URL. Two organizations with the same project selection (particularly the all-projects selection), date range, dataset, and attribute type therefore share a cache entry. Switching organizations can display attribute names cached from the previous organization, and simultaneous consumers can reuse the wrong request. Include the organization slug or the full endpoint path in the key, as the previous API query key did.

title: Normalize recording and error timestamps before merging logs
body: Error timestamps fetched from nodestore are Unix seconds, whereas rrweb recording event timestamps are Unix milliseconds. Comparing these values directly causes errors to be emitted before essentially every recording event, regardless of when they actually occurred, rather than interleaving them chronologically. The new tests use seconds for synthetic recording events and thus miss this production behavior. Convert the recording timestamp to seconds (or the error timestamp to milliseconds) for the comparison.

title: New table visualization discards the query results
body: When the organization has `use-table-widget-visualization` enabled, every dashboard table is rendered with empty columns, empty rows, and empty metadata instead of the fetched `result`. Consequently, populated widgets appear empty regardless of their query results. Pass the actual result data and corresponding columns/metadata to the new visualization before enabling this branch.

title: Attribute cache key no longer distinguishes organizations
body: The new React Query key contains only query options, although the query function requests an organization-specific endpoint. With identical filters (for example, all projects and the default date range), switching organizations reuses the previous organization's cached attribute collection and can also share an in-flight request. Include the organization slug in the query key so attribute suggestions cannot come from a different organization.

title: Normalize error and recording timestamps before merging
body: Error timestamps fetched from nodestore are Unix seconds, whereas raw rrweb recording event timestamps are Unix milliseconds. Comparing them directly makes errors appear earlier than all recording events, so errors occurring midway through a replay are emitted at the beginning of the summary input rather than alongside the relevant breadcrumbs. Normalize the recording timestamp to seconds (or the error timestamp to milliseconds) before comparing. The new tests use seconds for recording timestamps and therefore do not exercise the production format.

title: Include the organization in the attribute cache key
body: The new React Query key contains only query options and omits the organization, although the fetch uses an organization-specific endpoint. Switching between organizations with the same date range, dataset, attribute type and project selection (especially the all-projects selection) reuses the same cache entry. This can show one organization's custom attribute names in another organization and lets concurrent consumers overwrite each other's results. Include the organization slug or endpoint path in the key.

title: Pass actual results to the feature-gated table visualization
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, every dashboard table is rendered with an empty columns array and hard-coded empty data and metadata, ignoring the fetched `result`. Consequently, enabling the feature makes populated table widgets appear empty. Adapt the actual result and fields to the new component, or leave this branch disconnected until that adapter is implemented.

title: Normalize error and recording timestamps before merging
body: Error timestamps loaded from nodestore are Unix seconds, whereas replay recording (rrweb) event timestamps are Unix milliseconds. Comparing these raw values causes all errors to be emitted before the first real recording event instead of at their chronological positions. The generated error messages also use seconds while breadcrumb messages use recording timestamps, giving Seer inconsistent time coordinates. Normalize both sources to the same unit before comparison and log generation; the added tests use seconds for recording events and therefore miss this production case.

title: Missing integration rows bypass installer verification
body: When no Integration row exists for the supplied installation_id, this branch advances the pipeline without comparing the authenticated GitHub user to the installer. The pipeline then retrieves the installation using app credentials in build_integration, which does not verify the user either. Thus a user authenticated to any GitHub account can claim an installation whose webhook has not yet created its Integration row (for example, during webhook delivery delays). Fail closed or verify the user's authority over the installation before advancing this branch.

title: Handle integrations without sender metadata
body: The installer check unconditionally indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"], but sender is optional in build_integration, and the basic installation flow in this PR explicitly produces metadata without it. If such an Integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed, attempting to reconnect it now raises KeyError and returns a server error instead of completing or displaying the authenticity error. Handle missing installer metadata explicitly and fail closed.

title: Compare immutable GitHub user IDs instead of logins
body: The authorization decision compares the current OAuth user's login with a login stored from an installation webhook. GitHub usernames can change and old usernames can be acquired by another account. An account that acquires the installer's old username can therefore pass this check for an unlinked installation, while the actual installer will be rejected after renaming their account. Store and compare the immutable GitHub user ID available in both the webhook sender and authenticated user response instead.

title: Do not bypass installer verification when the integration row is missing
body: When no Integration row exists for the supplied installation ID, this branch advances directly to completion without comparing the authenticated GitHub user with the installer. Completion can fetch the installation using the app's credentials in build_integration(), so authenticating as any GitHub user is sufficient to claim such an installation. This also creates a bypass window before the installation webhook has created the row. Missing installer information must fail closed or be verified through another trusted source rather than skipping the new security check.

title: Handle integrations that lack sender metadata
body: The new verification unconditionally indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"], but build_integration() only adds sender when it is present in pipeline state; the updated basic-flow test explicitly creates an integration without this field. If an integration created through that path remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed, attempting to install it again raises KeyError and returns a server error instead of the intended invalid-installation response. Handle absent sender information explicitly and fail closed.

title: Do not skip installer verification when the Integration row is missing
body: When no Integration exists for the supplied installation_id, this branch immediately advances the pipeline without comparing the authenticated GitHub user to the installer. The subsequent build_integration call fetches the installation using app credentials, which does not establish that the OAuth user owns it. Thus, if the installation webhook has not yet created the row (or the row was deleted), a user authenticated with an unrelated GitHub account can supply that installation ID and attach it to their Sentry organization. Missing installer information must fail closed or be verified through another authoritative source rather than bypassing the new security check.

title: Handle integrations without sender metadata
body: The new check unconditionally indexes integration.metadata['sender']['login'], but sender is optional in build_integration, and the basic installation flow in this PR explicitly creates metadata without it. If such an Integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed, a subsequent installation attempt reaches this check and raises KeyError instead of rendering the invalid-installation response. Handle missing sender information explicitly and fail closed with the intended error page.

title: Generate the queued timestamp for each AssignmentSource instance
body: `timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` value receives the worker's module-import timestamp rather than the time of the assignment. Long-lived workers therefore serialize stale, identical queue timestamps for unrelated updates. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to generate the timestamp when each instance is constructed.

title: Evaluate the queued timestamp for each AssignmentSource instance
body: `timezone.now()` is evaluated when this module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` value receives the same process-start timestamp, rather than the time of its assignment. In long-running webhook workers, the serialized context therefore reports an incorrect queue time for every subsequent change. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to generate the timestamp per instance.

title: Generate the queued timestamp per AssignmentSource instance
body: `timezone.now()` is evaluated when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` value gets the same process-start timestamp, rather than the time of its assignment. Long-running webhook workers will consequently serialize stale, identical queue times for unrelated changes. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to generate the timestamp for each instance.

title: Registered metric-alert handler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of its abstract methods: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. Accessing detector.detector_handler for a detector with type 'metric_alert_fire' therefore raises TypeError when Detector.detector_handler attempts to instantiate it, instead of returning the previously working no-op handler. This also aborts process_detectors for the packet. Implement the required methods or retain a concrete no-op handler until metric-alert evaluation is implemented.

title: Expected occurrence uses a different group key from the evaluated occurrence
body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds its expected occurrence using group key 'val1', but calls evaluate_group_key_value with 'group_key'. The new occurrence-building hook uses the evaluated key to build the fingerprint, so the actual occurrence has fingerprint ['<detector id>:group_key'] while the expected occurrence has ['<detector id>:val1']. The equality assertion fails even when the implementation is correct. Build the expected occurrence with 'group_key' as well.

Accessing detector.detector_handler for the registered metric_alert_fire type therefore raises TypeError instead of returning the previous no-op handler. process_detectors does not catch this exception, so processing a detector of this type aborts the batch. The new occurrence builder includes the group key in the fingerprint, so the actual occurrence has fingerprint '<detector id>:group_key' while the expected occurrence has '<detector id>:val1'. The result equality assertion consequently fails. Build the expected occurrence using the same group key passed to the evaluation.

Detector.detector_handler unconditionally instantiates the registered handler, so accessing that property for a metric_alert_fire detector now raises TypeError rather than returning the previously working no-op handler. The new hook builds the actual occurrence using the evaluated group key, so its fingerprint is ['<detector id>:group_key'] while the expected occurrence has ['<detector id>:val1']. title: Spawned workers do not pass the multiprocessing.Process type check
body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances, not instances of the default-context multiprocessing.Process class. Consequently this check is false for production workers and a hung worker is never killed before its replacement starts. The old and replacement workers can then flush the same shards concurrently, causing duplicate production and accumulating stuck processes. The identical check in join() also skips termination. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or explicitly distinguish threads from processes instead.

title: Terminate remaining workers even after the join deadline expires
body: When the shared join deadline expires, this loop breaks before cleaning up the remaining workers. If the first worker consumes the timeout, all later workers are left running, potentially blocked in Redis or Kafka calls despite the stopped flag. During rebalancing the new strategy can start replacement flushers while these old workers still own the same shards. The deadline should limit waiting, not skip termination of the remaining processes.

title: Spawned workers do not pass the multiprocessing.Process type check
body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which creates SpawnProcess instances. These are not instances of the top-level multiprocessing.Process class, so this check skips kill() for every production worker. When a worker hangs, the manager starts a replacement without stopping the original; the original can subsequently resume flushing the same shards, causing concurrent processing and duplicate production. The identical check in join() also skips termination. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or explicitly distinguish threads from the spawn-context process type.

title: Terminate all remaining workers when the join deadline expires
body: When the shared join deadline expires, this loop breaks before stopping the current worker or any subsequent workers. This also happens if next_step.join(timeout) consumes the entire timeout. A worker blocked in Redis or Kafka therefore remains alive after the strategy is discarded during rebalancing, and may later resume flushing shards now owned by another consumer. Even after correcting the process type check, this early break still leaks workers. The deadline should limit waiting, not skip termination of the remaining processes.

title: Spawned workers do not pass the Process type check
body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, whose instances are SpawnProcess objects, not instances of the separate multiprocessing.Process class. This check therefore skips kill() for every production worker. When a worker is considered hung, its replacement is started while the original remains alive and is removed from self.processes. If the original resumes, both workers can flush the same shards, and the original can no longer be supervised. The same incorrect check at line 346 also skips termination during shutdown. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or the actual spawn-context process class instead.

title: Shutdown abandons remaining workers when the deadline expires
body: When the shared join deadline expires, this loop breaks without terminating any of the remaining workers. Those workers may still be blocked in Redis or Kafka operations despite the stopped flag. During a rebalance the consumer can subsequently create a new flusher for those shards while the old workers remain alive and unsupervised. Deadline expiry should stop waiting, but should still terminate and clean up every outstanding worker.

title: The added wait is patched into a no-op
body: test_basic replaces time.sleep with a no-op at line 15, so this time.sleep(0.1) does not give the background flusher time to observe the updated drift. step.join() then sets the stop flag, allowing the worker to exit before flushing the span and leaving messages empty. The test remains scheduling-dependent rather than reliably testing flushing. Use an unpatched sleep or, preferably, wait for an explicit indication that the output has been produced before joining.

title: Rebalances reuse a pool whose workers have already been stopped
body: The queue pool is created once in the factory and reused for every strategy returned by create_with_partitions(), but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/join() shuts that pool down. When Arroyo replaces the strategy after a partition rebalance, the new strategy therefore receives the old, stopped pool. Its submissions either fail because the queues are shut down (and are then marked completed by the exception handler) or accumulate without any workers. Create a fresh pool and offset tracker for each strategy assignment rather than sharing their lifecycle across strategies.

title: Graceful shutdown abandons queued work and stops commits before draining
body: Setting worker.shutdown to True makes each worker exit after its current item, even when its queue still contains accepted messages; queue.shutdown(immediate=False) does not override that loop condition. In addition, strategy.close() stops the commit thread before shutting down the workers, so work completed during shutdown never receives a final commit. Thus close()/join() neither drains accepted work nor commits its final completed offsets, causing replay and potentially duplicate uptime side effects on shutdown or rebalance. Graceful close should stop accepting submissions, drain workers, and commit the final safe offsets before returning.

title: Unbounded queues remove consumer backpressure
body: Each work queue is constructed without a maxsize, and submit() always accepts messages without raising MessageRejected or otherwise limiting in-flight work. If processing falls behind Kafka ingestion, especially when a slow result blocks one queue, the consumer continues retaining decoded results and original messages indefinitely. The offset tracker also retains later completed offsets behind that slow item. This can exhaust process memory rather than applying the advertised backpressure. Bound total in-flight work and reject submissions until capacity becomes available.

title: Create a fresh queue pool for each partition assignment
body: The factory creates its queue pool only once and passes that same pool to every strategy. Closing or joining a strategy shuts down that pool's workers and queues, but a Kafka rebalance subsequently calls create_with_partitions on the same factory and receives another strategy backed by the stopped pool. New messages then either accumulate without workers or fail to enqueue and are marked completed by submit's exception handler, allowing unprocessed results to be committed. Allocate assignment-scoped workers and offset tracking when creating each strategy.

title: Bound queued work and apply backpressure
body: Each work queue is created with no maximum size, and submit always accepts more messages without raising MessageRejected. If processing is slower than Kafka ingestion, or a worker stalls, the consumer continues retaining decoded results and original messages indefinitely. The offset tracker also retains all later offsets behind unfinished work. This can exhaust consumer memory under exactly the slow-item workload this mode is intended to handle; queued and in-flight work need a bound with backpressure.

title: Drain accepted work before stopping workers and committing final offsets
body: Graceful shutdown sets every worker's shutdown flag before shutting down the queues. Workers therefore exit after their current item instead of draining queued items, despite shutdown(immediate=False). In addition, strategy.close stops the commit thread before waiting for workers, so results completed during shutdown never receive a final commit. Normal shutdown or partition revocation abandons accepted work and replays already processed results on the next assignment. close/join should drain accepted work (within the supplied timeout) and commit its completed offsets before stopping.

title: Track delivered offset order rather than requiring consecutive Kafka offsets
body: The tracker stops at any integer offset absent from all_offsets, even if every delivered message has completed. Kafka can legitimately deliver nonconsecutive offsets, for example when transactional control records or aborted transactions are skipped. If completed offsets 100 and 102 are present in the same commit scan, it commits only 100 even though 102 is safe; with ongoing work after such gaps this unnecessarily retains completed offsets and increases replay and memory usage. Determine the safe prefix of delivered offsets, stopping at outstanding work rather than at offsets Kafka never delivered.

title: Create a fresh queue pool for each partition assignment
body: The factory creates one queue pool in its constructor and reuses it for every strategy. However, SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() shuts that pool down. Arroyo closes and recreates strategies when partition assignments change, so after the first rebalance the replacement strategy receives queues whose workers have stopped (and whose queues have been shut down). New results can no longer be processed; submission errors are caught and marked complete, potentially committing results that were never handled. Allocate assignment-scoped pools and offset trackers rather than reusing the closed pool.

title: Bound queued work and propagate backpressure
body: queue.Queue() has no size limit, and submit() always accepts more work without signaling backpressure to Arroyo. If a worker blocks or incoming results exceed processing throughput, the consumer continues reading Kafka and retains every decoded result, original message, and tracked offset in memory. This can exhaust process memory rather than leaving the backlog in Kafka. Use bounded queues and reject submissions for retry when capacity is reached.

title: Do not require Kafka offsets to be numerically contiguous
body: The tracker stops at any integer offset absent from all_offsets, even if every delivered record before the next outstanding record has completed. Kafka can legitimately deliver nonconsecutive offsets, for example because of transactional records or compaction. If offsets 100, 102, and 103 are delivered and completed before a commit, this code commits only 100 and then remains stuck on the nonexistent 101 while 102 and 103 remain tracked. Track completion in delivered-record order rather than requiring every integer offset to exist.

title: Drain accepted work before stopping workers on graceful close
body: Setting worker.shutdown to True makes each worker exit its loop after its current item, leaving queued items unprocessed despite shutdown(immediate=False). Strategy.close() also stops the commit loop before shutting down the workers, so results completed during shutdown never receive a final commit, and join() merely repeats close() rather than draining work. On shutdown or rebalance this abandons accepted results and replays already processed results; a worker that exceeds the five-second join can also continue processing after ownership is relinquished. Graceful close/join should drain accepted work, wait within the supplied timeout, and commit completed offsets before stopping; reserve abandonment for terminate().

title: Backup-code authentication can bypass password verification
body: Password verification for CAL accounts is skipped whenever credentials.totpCode is nonempty. The new backup-code branch then authenticates without validating that TOTP value. A request containing an email, a valid backup code, an arbitrary totpCode such as "x", and an incorrect or empty password therefore succeeds. Require verified first-factor authentication before accepting the backup code; an unvalidated TOTP field must not exempt the request from password verification.

title: Consume backup codes atomically
body: Backup-code validation reads the encrypted array from the earlier user query, then replaces the entire array with an unconditional update by user ID. Two concurrent requests can both validate and authenticate with the same supposedly single-use code. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's changes, restoring a consumed code. Validation and consumption need an atomic conditional update or a transaction that locks the row before reading and checking the codes.

title: Backup recovery is unavailable in the external-provider 2FA flow
body: The new Lost access button is rendered only through TwoFactorFooter, while logins with totpEmail use ExternalTotpFooter, which contains only Cancel. A user who generates backup codes as a CAL account and later links Google or SAML retains those codes, but cannot reach the backup-code input after signing in through that provider. Posting a backup code without a TOTP code is also rejected by the external-provider guards in authorize. Wire backup recovery into the external-provider verification flow so these users can recover without their authenticator.

title: Notify the caller when 2FA has actually been enabled
body: After the enable endpoint succeeds, onEnable is now deferred until the custom backup-codes Close button is clicked. Dismissing the dialog through its normal onOpenChange path, such as Escape, never invokes onEnable even though 2FA is already enabled on the server. This breaks the callback contract and leaves callers relying on it uninformed about the successful change. Ensure every dismissal after successful enablement propagates that result, or synchronize the enabled state independently of closing the backup-code screen.

title: Wait for clipboard success before confirming the codes were copied
body: navigator.clipboard.writeText returns a promise that can reject, for example when clipboard access is denied. This handler does not await or catch it and immediately displays "Backup codes copied!" regardless of the outcome. Users can close the backup-code screen believing they copied their recovery credentials when the clipboard was never updated. Show success only after the write resolves and report copying failures.

title: Keep the password visibility control keyboard-accessible
body: Adding tabIndex={-1} to the shared PasswordField visibility button removes it from the keyboard focus order everywhere this component is used. Keyboard-only users can no longer reach and activate Show password or Hide password with Tab and Enter/Space, although the control remains available to mouse users. Keep this interactive control in the tab order.

title: Do not override PasswordField's visibility-controlled input type
body: The replacement PasswordField still receives type="password". PasswordField spreads its props after setting the input type from its visibility state, so this explicit prop overrides the computed "text" type. Clicking the new Show password control changes its icon but never reveals the password. Remove the explicit type prop here or prevent it from overriding PasswordField's internal visibility state.

title: Do not let an unverified TOTP value bypass password verification
body: Password verification above runs only when credentials.totpCode is falsy, but the new backup-code branch takes precedence and never validates totpCode. A request containing an email, a valid backupCode, and any nonempty totpCode therefore authenticates a CAL account without its password. Someone possessing a backup code can bypass the first factor simply by supplying a dummy TOTP value. Enforce password verification for backup-code authentication independently of the supplied totpCode.

title: Consume backup codes atomically
body: Backup codes are checked against the user snapshot fetched earlier, then the entire array is overwritten using only the user ID. Two concurrent requests can both validate and successfully consume the same supposedly single-use code. Requests consuming different codes can also overwrite each other's changes, restoring a code that was already used. Perform validation and consumption under a database lock or use a conditional update that detects a changed backupCodes value and rejects or retries the stale request.

title: Support backup recovery in external-provider 2FA challenges
body: The Lost access control exists only in TwoFactorFooter, while Google/SAML 2FA redirects set totpEmail and render ExternalTotpFooter, which offers only Cancel. CAL accounts converted to Google/SAML retain their enabled 2FA and generated backup codes, so these users can possess valid recovery codes but have no way to use them after losing their authenticator. A backup-only request would also be rejected by the credentials provider's non-CAL guards, which still require totpCode. Wire backup recovery into both the external challenge UI and its authentication path.

title: Notify the parent when successful setup is dismissed
body: After the enable endpoint succeeds, 2FA is already active, but onEnable is now called only by the backup-codes-close button. Dismissing the backup-code dialog through Escape, the backdrop, or its ordinary close control invokes onOpenChange without emitting the successful-enable callback. A caller relying on the documented onEnable callback therefore keeps stale 2FA state even though subsequent logins require it. Ensure every dismissal after successful enablement notifies the parent, or separate the success notification from closing the backup-code screen.

title: Report clipboard success only after the write completes
body: navigator.clipboard.writeText returns a promise, but it is ignored and the success toast is shown immediately. If the browser rejects the write, such as when clipboard permission is blocked, the user is told that the backup codes were copied even though the clipboard is unchanged, and the rejection is unhandled. This can cause users to save unrelated clipboard contents instead of their recovery codes. Await the write and display an error rather than a success toast when it fails.

title: Remove the fixed type from the new PasswordField
body: The replacement PasswordField still receives type="password". PasswordField sets its visibility-dependent type before spreading the caller's props, so this explicit prop overrides type="text" whenever the visibility toggle is activated. The new Show password control changes its icon and tooltip but never reveals the password. Omit the fixed type when using PasswordField.

title: Keep the password visibility control keyboard-accessible
body: Adding tabIndex={-1} removes the shared Show/Hide password button from sequential keyboard navigation. There is no alternative keyboard control for this action, so keyboard-only users can no longer activate password visibility on login and other forms using PasswordField. Keep the button in the tab order or provide an equivalent keyboard-accessible action.

title: A dummy TOTP value lets a backup code bypass password verification
body: Password verification above this branch is skipped whenever credentials.totpCode is nonempty. The new backup-code branch takes precedence over TOTP validation, so a request containing an email, a valid backupCode, an arbitrary totpCode such as "x", and an empty or incorrect password successfully authenticates. The dummy TOTP is never checked. This makes a backup code sufficient by itself rather than a replacement for the second factor. Require a verified first factor before accepting the backup code.

title: Consume backup codes atomically
body: Backup codes are checked against the user snapshot read earlier, then the entire encrypted array is overwritten with an unconditional update. Two concurrent requests using the same code can both validate it and successfully log in. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's changes, restoring a code that was already consumed. This violates the advertised single-use guarantee and permits replay. Use locking or a conditional update against the original stored value, and authenticate only when consumption succeeds.

title: Backup recovery is unavailable in the third-party 2FA flow
body: A user can generate backup codes with a CAL account and subsequently link Google or SAML; the sign-in code changes their identity provider while retaining their 2FA settings and backup codes. Their subsequent 2FA challenge has totpEmail and renders ExternalTotpFooter, which has only Cancel—not the new Lost access control. Consequently twoFactorLostAccess cannot become true and the backup-code field is unreachable. The credentials provider also rejects backup-only submissions for non-CAL users because its identity-provider guards recognize only totpCode. These users cannot use their saved recovery codes after losing their authenticator.

title: Finalize successful enablement on every dialog dismissal path
body: After the enable endpoint succeeds, onEnable is no longer called; it is deferred to the custom backup-codes-close button. Closing the backup-code dialog through Escape or the dialog's standard close control invokes only the passed-through onOpenChange handler, so onEnable never fires even though 2FA is already enabled on the server. This breaks the callback contract and leaves consumers relying on it with stale security settings. Notify the parent on success, or ensure every dismissal path after success invokes onEnable.

title: Do not override PasswordField's visibility-controlled input type
body: The replacement PasswordField still receives type="password". PasswordField sets its input type from isPasswordVisible but spreads props afterward, so this explicit prop overrides the dynamic type. Clicking the new show-password control changes its icon and label but never reveals the password. Remove the explicit type prop so PasswordField can control visibility.

title: Guard the missing destination calendar in the Google Meet fallback
body: When destinationCalendar is null or empty, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar. A booking with Google Meet selected then throws while reading .integration, instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. This can happen after disconnecting Google Calendar while retaining a Google Meet event location. Use an optional access or explicitly handle the missing destination.

title: Select the current host's destination before invoking calendar adapters
body: Every credential receives the complete destinationCalendar array, but Office365, Lark, and CalDAV still select its first entry. Consequently, a second Outlook host attempts to create an event in the first host's calendar using the second host's credentials; CalDAV can filter out every calendar and silently report success without creating anything. Google's organizer attendee also uses the first externalId, which is not a valid email when the main destination is Outlook or CalDAV. Scope adapter input to the current destination or implement credential-aware selection throughout.

title: Restore the organization slug condition when billing is disabled
body: This reverses the existing condition for assigning an organization's slug. With team billing disabled, newly created organizations now receive no slug despite registering or requesting their subdomain, breaking resolution at that address. With billing enabled, the slug is assigned immediately alongside requestedSlug rather than being deferred. Preserve the original !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition for slug.

title: Reuse one Google Meet conference across collective host events
body: For a collective Google Meet booking, each host's calendar receives the same event containing a conferenceData.createRequest. Each Google events.insert creates a conference for its own event, and this loop never copies the first result's conference data into subsequent inserts. The cohost's directly created calendar event therefore has a different meeting link from the main host's event. Generate the conference once and reuse its returned conference data for the other hosts.

title: Preserve credential IDs on video booking references
body: The new conditional always writes undefined as the credentialId for video results, discarding result.credentialId that was previously preserved. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when the video reference contains a credentialId. Newly created Zoom or other dedicated-video bookings therefore cannot delete their external meetings when cancelled.

title: Retain cohost destinations when the organizer has no calendar
body: If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null. The optional push then discards all collected teamDestinationCalendars, even when other collective hosts have connected calendars. EventManager consequently creates no events for those hosts. Initialize an array or assign the collected destinations rather than skipping them when the main destination is absent.

title: Rebuild collective destinations before deferred calendar creation
body: handleNewBooking collects multiple host destinations but persists only destinationCalendar[0] on the booking. This confirmation handler reconstructs an array containing only that persisted calendar, so EventManager never creates the cohosts' destination events when a collective booking requires approval. The payment webhook handlers have the same limitation. Deferred creation needs to reconstruct the booked hosts' destinations, not merely wrap the organizer's calendar.

title: Delete every host's references when cancelling a recurring series
body: Inside the new per-reference loop, the allRemainingBookings branch ignores the calendar obtained for the current reference. It instead iterates only bookingToDelete.user.credentials and selects the first calendar reference from each recurring booking. For collective bookings, this repeatedly deletes the organizer's event while never deleting the cohosts' events, even though all bookings are marked cancelled. Iterate each updated booking's references and resolve the credential belonging to each reference.

title: Use reference credential IDs when requesting a collective reschedule
body: Calendar deletion still resolves credentials by integration type from only the requesting user's credentials. With the multiple-host references introduced here, two Google references are both deleted using that user's Google account, so the cohost's deletion returns 404 and is ignored. References for providers the requester has not installed are excluded entirely. The booking is marked cancelled while cohost calendar events remain; resolve each reference by its credentialId instead.

title: Preserve Google calendar selection for destinations without credential IDs
body: EventManager explicitly retains a compatibility path for destination calendars whose credentialId is absent, choosing credentials by integration type. Such a destination can never match the numeric credentialId in this lookup, so createEvent now writes to primary regardless of its configured externalId. Previously the selected externalId was honored. Keep a destination fallback for this supported legacy path.

title: Restore a usable Google destination fallback for updates and deletions
body: This fallback searches for an externalId equal to externalCalendarId precisely when externalCalendarId is null, undefined, or empty. Normal destination IDs cannot match that value. A booking reference without externalCalendarId therefore sends an undefined required calendarId to Google updates, despite the event containing a valid destination. The equivalent deletion fallback searches primary instead and treats a 404 as success, potentially leaving an event on a secondary calendar. Select the applicable destination rather than comparing against the missing ID.

title: Avoid updating nontraditional calendar integrations twice
body: The new filter includes references such as closecom_other_calendar, so the main reference loop now updates those integrations. The dedicated other_calendar loop below still updates them again. For a booking with a normal calendar and Close.com connected, every reschedule, location change, or attendee update now issues two CRM writes instead of one. Exclude these references from the main loop or remove the duplicate processing.

title: Handle an empty destination list in the Google Meet fallback
body: When destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or empty, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar. Selecting Google Meet then dereferences its integration property and throws instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. This prevents bookings with Google Meet and no destination calendar from completing. Restore the optional access or explicitly handle the missing destination.

title: Select the current host's destination for non-Google adapters
body: Each host's credential is passed the complete destinationCalendar array, but Office365, Lark, and BaseCalendarService still select only its first element. Consequently, a second host's request uses the first host's calendar ID with the second host's credentials. Office365 and Lark requests fail for unshared calendars; CalDAV filters out every calendar and reports success without creating anything. Scope the destination to the current host or make all adapters resolve it by credentialId.

title: Preserve credentialId on video booking references
body: The new conditional discards result.credentialId for every non-calendar result, including dedicated video meetings. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when the video reference has a credentialId, so newly created Zoom and other video bookings will be cancelled in Cal.com without deleting their underlying meetings. Keep the video result's credentialId when constructing the reference.

title: Retain organization slugs when team billing is disabled
body: This reverses the original condition for storing slug. With IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED disabled, organization creation now stores neither slug nor metadata.requestedSlug. The organization therefore cannot be resolved through its requested subdomain, and the slug collision query cannot find it on subsequent creation attempts. Preserve the original billing-disabled condition when rewriting this spread.

title: Delete every host's references when cancelling a recurring series
body: The allRemainingBookings branch ignores the co-host credential fetched by the new outer loop. Instead, it repeatedly iterates the organizer's credentials and selects only the first calendar reference from each occurrence. For a collective recurring series, this deletes the organizer's events repeatedly but never uses the other hosts' credentials or event UIDs. All occurrences are marked cancelled while co-host calendar events remain and continue blocking availability.

title: Use each host reference's credential when requesting a reschedule
body: Collective bookings now contain calendar references belonging to multiple users, but this deletion path still looks up credentials by integration type from the requesting user's credentials. With two hosts using personal Google accounts, both references are deleted using the requesting host's token; deleting the other host's calendar event fails, and Promise.allSettled hides the failure. The booking is cancelled but the co-host's event remains. Resolve each reference by credentialId, including credentials belonging to the other booked hosts.

title: Keep co-host destinations when the organizer has no calendar
body: If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null. This optional push then does nothing, discarding all connected co-host destinations collected above. A collective event whose first host has no calendar therefore creates no entries for the other hosts, even when their calendars are connected. Initialize an empty array or concatenate the co-host destinations independently of the organizer's destination.

title: Restore collective destinations during deferred confirmation
body: Only the first destination is persisted on Booking by handleNewBooking. For a collective booking requiring confirmation, this reconstruction therefore supplies EventManager with only the organizer's destination, and approving the booking never creates the co-host calendar entries added by this PR. Rebuild the destination list from the booked collective hosts when confirming; the deferred payment creation paths have the same singleton reconstruction problem.

title: Preserve calendar selection for destinations without credentialId
body: EventManager still supports destinations without a credentialId by selecting credentials according to integration. For those destinations, this lookup cannot match the supplied credential ID, so insertion silently falls back to primary despite a configured destination.externalId. These bookings previously went to the configured calendar and now go to the wrong one. Retain destination selection for this supported credential-less case.

title: Use a valid Google calendar fallback when the reference ID is absent
body: When externalCalendarId is null or omitted, the fallback searches for a destination whose externalId equals that same absent value. Valid destination IDs cannot match, so updates receive an undefined calendarId and fail even when the event has a configured destination. deleteEvent repeats this expression and instead tries primary, potentially leaving non-primary events behind while treating 404 as success. This is reachable through references created without externalId and through CalendarManager.deleteEvent, which omits the argument.

title: Avoid updating non-traditional calendar references twice
body: The new filter includes references such as closecom_other_calendar, so the main loop now queues updates for them alongside traditional calendar references. The separate non-traditional integration block below still queues those same updates again. A booking connected to both Google and a CRM therefore sends two concurrent CRM updates for each reschedule, location change, or attendee update, unnecessarily consuming API quota. Exclude other_calendar references from one of these paths.

title: Video references lose the credential needed for cancellation
body: The non-calendar branch now stores an undefined credentialId instead of result.credentialId. Newly created bookings using connected video apps therefore lose the credential associated with their meeting. handleCancelBooking only deletes a video meeting when its reference contains a credentialId, so cancelling these bookings leaves the external meeting alive. Seat cancellation also skips updating these references. Preserve result.credentialId for video results.

title: Non-Google co-host events target the organizer's calendar
body: Each destination's credential receives the complete, unchanged destinationCalendar array. Office365CalendarService, LarkCalendarService, and BaseCalendarService still select the first array item rather than the destination associated with that credential. For example, an Office365 co-host following a Google organizer sends the organizer's Google address as a Microsoft calendar ID, causing creation to fail. CalDAV can instead filter out every calendar and report success without creating anything. Route each creation to the current credential's destination.

title: Non-Google calendar IDs are sent as Google attendee emails
body: The organizer attendee's email is taken from the first destination's externalId regardless of its integration. In a collective event with an Office365 organizer and a Google co-host, that value is a Microsoft calendar ID, not an email address. Google rejects the co-host's event with an invalid attendee email even though the target calendar is correctly selected by credentialId later. The same problem exists in updateEvent. Only substitute an appropriate Google calendar email; otherwise retain the organizer's email.

title: An empty destination list crashes the Google Meet fallback
body: destinationCalendar is optional, nullable, and can be empty, so destructuring it can leave mainHostDestinationCalendar undefined. Accessing its integration without optional chaining throws when a Google Meet event has no destination calendar—the exact case this fallback is intended to handle. Booking creation or confirmation now fails instead of switching to Cal Video. Preserve the previous null-safe check.

title: Co-host calendars are discarded when the organizer has none
body: When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null. The optional push then silently discards all calendars collected from the other collective hosts. A collective booking with an unconnected organizer and a connected co-host consequently never passes the co-host's calendar or credential to EventManager, so nothing is created in that host's destination calendar. Initialize an array before adding the co-host destinations.

title: Legacy Google destinations are silently redirected to primary
body: EventManager explicitly supports destinations without a credentialId by selecting credentials using the integration name. In that path, this lookup cannot match a destination's null credentialId to the numeric credentialId argument. Google therefore inserts into primary instead of the configured externalId. Existing configurations targeting a secondary or shared calendar silently start writing bookings to the wrong calendar. Retain destination-based routing for the legacy integration-selection path.

title: Missing reference calendar IDs no longer use the destination fallback
body: When externalCalendarId is null or undefined, the fallback searches for a destination whose string externalId equals that missing value, so it cannot find one. This replaces the previous fallback to the configured destination and calls Google update without its required calendarId. The equivalent lookup in deleteEvent instead falls back to primary, where a secondary-calendar event returns a 404 that is treated as successful deletion. Bookings with missing reference calendar IDs can no longer reschedule correctly and can leave calendar events behind after cancellation.

title: Deferred confirmation loses collective co-host destinations
body: handleNewBooking persists only the first destination calendar on Booking. When a collective booking requires confirmation, this handler reconstructs the event using only that stored destination or the confirming user's destination; it never restores the other hosts' calendars. EventManager's new creation loop therefore receives only one destination and writes only that host's calendar event. Rebuild the participating hosts' destinations before deferred calendar creation. The payment webhook event builders have the same single-destination limitation.

title: Recurring cancellation ignores the resolved co-host credential
body: For cancellation of all remaining recurrences, this branch ignores the calendar credential just resolved for the current reference and iterates only the organizer's credentials. It also selects only the first calendar reference from each recurrence. With multiple host references, the outer loop consequently repeats deletion of the organizer's events but never deletes the co-host's events using their own credentials. All bookings are marked cancelled while the co-host's calendar remains occupied. Process each recurrence's references with their associated credentials.

title: Reschedule requests use one user's credential for every host
body: Collective bookings now contain calendar references for multiple hosts, but requestReschedule still resolves references through a map keyed only by integration type and populated from the requesting user's credentials. Two Google hosts' references are therefore both deleted using one host's Google token; references for co-host integrations absent from the map are skipped entirely. The booking is already marked cancelled, and deletion failures are swallowed, so requesting a reschedule leaves co-host events blocking their calendars. Resolve each reference using its credentialId.

title: Organization creation drops the slug when billing is disabled
body: This reverses the original condition for saving the organization slug. When IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is false, creation now saves neither slug nor metadata.requestedSlug, despite provisioning or announcing the domain using the requested slug earlier in the handler. Newly created organizations on billing-disabled installations therefore cannot resolve at their requested organization address. Preserve the original negated condition for slug.

title: Import the Prisma client before updating Salesforce credentials
body: The new database update references `prisma`, but this module neither imports nor defines it. This fails type checking and, if checks are skipped, fails at runtime before getClient returns a Salesforce connection. Salesforce event creation, updates, and deletion are therefore broken even when credential sharing is disabled.

title: Persist parsed token data rather than the safe-parse result
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safe-parse result shaped as `{ success: true, data: tokens }`, whereas the previous schema.parse call returned the tokens themselves. Passing this result directly as the credential key stores the wrapper instead of the Google credential fields. The next service initialization fails googleCredentialSchema.parse because access_token and the other fields are nested under data. This corrupts credentials on ordinary Google refreshes even with sharing disabled.

title: Preserve the response contract expected by each refresh caller
body: The sharing branch always returns a native Fetch Response, but several callbacks normally return different objects. Google and both Zoho adapters immediately read `.data`, while HubSpot reads SDK fields such as `.accessToken` and `.expiresIn` directly. None of these callers deserializes the shared Fetch Response, so sharing produces undefined token fields or throws before refreshing credentials. Parse and adapt the shared response, or update these callers to consume a consistent response contract.

title: Use actual response fields in the minimum token schema
body: Calling toString() on these Zod schemas produces the literal property name `[object Object]`; it does not match arbitrary response properties. Both computed keys use that name, so the optional unknown property also overwrites the numeric requirement. Since z.object strips unknown properties, a shared response loses expires_in, expiry_date, and any supplied refresh_token. For example, Zoom subsequently computes its expiry from undefined, while Office365 receives no updated expiry.

title: Do not replace omitted refresh tokens with a literal placeholder
body: This fallback also runs when credential sharing is disabled. Office365's response schema explicitly permits an omitted refresh_token, and its caller previously merged the response into the stored credentials to retain the existing token. Adding the literal `refresh_token` now overwrites that valid stored token, causing the next direct OAuth refresh to fail. Preserve the existing token when the provider does not return a replacement.

title: Send the credential owner's user ID rather than the credential ID
body: The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is sent to the parent platform as calcomUserId, but this call supplies the Credential table's primary key. Credential IDs and user IDs are unrelated. Whenever this ID matches another user, the parent is asked to refresh and return that other user's Bigin integration; otherwise the lookup fails. Propagate credential.userId through this refresh path instead.

title: Use the actual Zoom app slug in delegated refresh requests
body: The delegated request sends appSlug `zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are created with appId `zoom`, and `zoom` is the app-store slug. A parent platform using the same slug contract as the credential webhook cannot find this integration under `zoomvideo`, so Zoom refreshes fail whenever sharing is enabled.

title: Delegate Salesforce refreshes to the configured sync endpoint
body: This new refresh request always goes directly to Salesforce and never calls refreshOAuthTokens, even when credential sharing and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are configured. Applying the sharing-aware parser afterward does not delegate the refresh. Synced credentials without a local provider refresh token fail here, while credentials containing one are refreshed outside the parent platform rather than through the configured source of truth.

title: Keep local refresh-token expiry checks out of delegated refreshes
body: The new delegation is reached only after refreshAccessToken checks the locally stored refresh token and deletes the credential if that token is missing or expired. In sharing mode, the parent owns refreshes and the helper specifies that its response only needs an access token and expiry; the local refresh token can therefore be absent or stale while the parent can still supply a valid access token. This path deletes the synced integration instead of contacting the parent. Perform the provider-only validation inside the direct OAuth fallback.

title: Accept the token-only sync response in the Webex refresh path
body: After delegating to the sync endpoint, this adapter still validates the response with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires scope, token_type, refresh_token, and refresh_token_expires_in. The documented shared response containing only the access token and expiry is rejected as an invalid refresh response. The sharing path needs to consume that response and retain the necessary existing credential metadata rather than require a complete Webex OAuth response.

title: Preserve absolute expiry dates returned by the sync endpoint
body: A shared response containing access_token and a future expiry_date reaches code that unconditionally replaces expiry_date with Date.now() plus expires_in, defaulting the missing expires_in to zero. The freshly obtained token is consequently stored as immediately expired, forcing another delegated refresh on every subsequent operation. Handle the shared absolute expiry separately from Microsoft's expires_in duration.

title: Clear the invalid flag when replacing credentials
body: Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credentials invalid after unrecoverable authentication failures. This webhook finds those same records but updates only their key, leaving invalid=true after valid replacement tokens are synchronized. The webhook reports success without restoring the installation's validity. Reset the invalid flag when accepting replacement credentials.

title: Make credential creation idempotent under concurrent webhooks
body: The findFirst followed by create is not atomic. Two concurrent deliveries for a user's first credential can both observe no record and create separate credentials for the same user and app. Later webhook deliveries update only one arbitrary match, leaving the other credential stale and the database inconsistent with the parent source of truth. Serialize the per-user/app operation or enforce an appropriate idempotency constraint.

title: Import Prisma before using the new credential update
body: The new code calls prisma.credential.update, but this module neither imports nor declares prisma. This fails TypeScript checking and, in builds that skip type checking, throws a ReferenceError whenever Salesforce client initialization reaches the database update.

title: Persist the parsed Google credentials rather than the SafeParse result
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the complete safeParse result, shaped as { success: true, data: ... }, whereas the previous schema.parse call returned the credential object itself.
