Saving that result as credential.key moves all OAuth fields under data. The next GoogleCalendarService instance cannot read the stored access token, refresh token, or expiry at their expected locations, breaking the integration after a successful refresh even when credential sharing is disabled.

title: Use actual field validation instead of computed Zod object keys
body: Calling toString() on a Zod schema does not create a wildcard property matcher. Both computed keys evaluate to the literal '[object Object]', and the optional definition overwrites the numeric one. Because z.object strips unknown properties by default, a normal synced response loses expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token, and other metadata. Zoom then calculates its expiry from undefined, while Office365 retains an already-expired value. Preserve and validate the actual response fields.

title: Preserve the adapters' refresh-result contracts on the sync path
body: The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but the fallback returns whatever the provider client produces. Google and both Zoho adapters immediately read result.data, while HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly; none of those properties exists on a fetch Response. Consequently, even a successful JSON response from the sync endpoint causes exceptions or undefined token values for these integrations. Decode and normalize the remote response, and adapt the callers to a consistent result contract.

title: Send the credential owner's user ID rather than the credential ID
body: The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is serialized as calcomUserId, but this call passes credentialId. Credential IDs and user IDs identify different records, so the external store can either fail the lookup or return another user's OAuth token, which is then saved on this credential. Passing a credential ID also bypasses the helper's intended exclusion of team-owned credentials. Thread credential.userId into this call.

title: Do not replace an existing refresh token with a placeholder
body: This assignment runs even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365's native response schema explicitly permits an omitted refresh_token, and its caller merges the parsed response into the existing credential. Previously that preserved the current refresh token; now the literal string 'refresh_token' overwrites it. The next native refresh submits that placeholder and fails, requiring the user to reconnect. Leave an omitted refresh token absent so callers can retain the existing value.

title: Authenticate outbound credential-refresh requests
body: The request to the external token broker contains only a guessable calcomUserId and appSlug, with no authentication header or other caller credential. For an Internet-reachable sync endpoint, requests generated by this protocol are indistinguishable from requests made by an attacker seeking another user's access token. An endpoint enforcing shared-secret authentication would instead reject every refresh. Add an authenticated exchange, such as sending the configured shared secret in the configured header.

title: Use the canonical Zoom app slug in sync requests
body: This sends appSlug='zoomvideo', but Zoom credentials are created with appId='zoom' and its app keys are also looked up using 'zoom'. 'zoomvideo' is the integration directory name, not the app-store slug used by the new webhook contract. An external store indexing credentials by the canonical app slug cannot resolve this request, so Zoom token synchronization fails.

title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
body: The newly added refresh always posts directly to Salesforce and never uses refreshOAuthTokens. Even when credential sharing and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are configured, Salesforce therefore ignores the platform designated as the credential source of truth and still requires a usable local refresh token. Platform-managed credentials cannot follow the new refresh flow. Apply the same user/team-aware sync routing used by the other adapters.

title: Handle the access-token-only sync response in Webex and Lark
body: The shared helper documents a sync response containing only an access token and expiry, but Webex still validates it with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires scope, token_type, refresh_token, and refresh_token_expires_in. A compliant sync response is therefore rejected before its token is used, breaking Webex operations once the old token expires. Lark has the same mismatch: it expects nested data.data and refresh-token metadata. These adapters need sync-specific response handling rather than retaining native OAuth response requirements.

title: Use the refreshed Salesforce token for the current connection
body: The new refresh result is written to the database but never applied to credentialKey. The jsforce.Connection constructed immediately afterward still receives the original access_token and instance_url. If the original token is expired, the current operation uses that expired token and jsforce must refresh again despite the successful refresh just performed. Initialize the connection from the refreshed values instead of adding a redundant token request and database write.

title: Make webhook credential creation idempotent under concurrent delivery
body: Finding an existing credential and creating one are separate, unsynchronized operations. Two concurrent first deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no credential and create separate rows. Subsequent deliveries update only one row through findFirst, leaving another installed credential with stale tokens. Serialize the keyed find-or-create operation or use an appropriate uniqueness and retry mechanism so concurrent webhook delivery cannot create duplicate credentials.

title: Clear the invalid flag when replacing invalid credentials
body: Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credential rows invalid=true after an invalid_grant. When the source platform reconnects an account and sends working replacement keys, this webhook finds the existing row and changes only key, leaving invalid=true. The refreshed integration remains marked invalid despite the successful sync response and cannot be restored through this endpoint without deleting or reinstalling it. Reset the invalid state when accepting replacement credentials.

title: Import Prisma before updating Salesforce credentials
body: The new credential update references `prisma`, but this file does not import or declare it. This fails TypeScript checking with `Cannot find name 'prisma'`; if emitted without checking, every Salesforce client initialization reaches a ReferenceError after refreshing its token. Import the Prisma client used by the other adapters.

title: Persist the parsed Google credentials, not the validation result
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod safe-parse result `{ success: true, data: credentials }`, whereas the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credentials directly. This code saves the entire result as `Credential.key`. Even with credential sharing disabled, the next GoogleCalendarService construction cannot parse that key because the token fields are nested under `data`, breaking calendar availability and event operations after a successful refresh. Persist the result's `data` property.

title: Define actual token fields instead of stringifying Zod schemas
body: Stringifying these Zod schema objects produces the literal property name `[object Object]`, not a wildcard for response properties. Both computed keys are the same, so the optional unknown definition also overwrites the numeric definition. Because `z.object` strips unknown fields by default, a normal synced response containing `access_token` and `expires_in` loses its expiry and refresh token. Zoom subsequently calculates a NaN expiry, while Office365 does not advance its stored expiry. Define the supported expiration fields explicitly and preserve any required additional fields.

title: Normalize external responses for SDK-based refresh callers
body: The sync branch returns a native fetch `Response`, but the fallback can return a Google Gaxios response, a Zoho Axios response, or a HubSpot token object. Their callers still read those original shapes: Google and both Zoho adapters access `.data`, while HubSpot accesses `accessToken` and `expiresIn`. A successful external refresh therefore produces undefined data or tokens rather than usable credentials. Decode and adapt the external reply for each caller instead of substituting a raw Response for these incompatible return types.

title: Do not replace an existing refresh token with a placeholder
body: This fallback runs even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365 explicitly permits a refresh response without `refresh_token`; previously, merging that response preserved the existing refresh token. The helper now injects the literal string `refresh_token`, which overwrites the real token during the merge. The current access token works, but the next refresh sends this placeholder to Microsoft and fails. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not return a replacement.

title: Pass the Bigin credential owner's user ID
body: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a Cal.com user ID and is transmitted as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`, derived from `credential.id`. These IDs are unrelated. The parent service consequently looks up the wrong user or returns not found; a coincidentally matching ID can request another user's credentials. It also routes team credentials through user syncing because their credential ID is non-null. Pass `credential.userId` through to this method separately.

title: Authenticate outbound credential refresh requests
body: The request to the parent application's token endpoint contains only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no authentication header. These identifiers do not prove that the caller is Cal.com, yet the endpoint is expected to return third-party access tokens. The parent cannot validate this request using the configured webhook secret: requiring that secret breaks refreshes, while accepting the shown request allows token enumeration if the endpoint is publicly reachable. Send an authentication credential, such as the configured shared secret under its configured header name.

title: Adapt access-token-only sync replies for Webex and Lark
body: The delegated refresh contract specifies only an access token and expiry, but Webex still validates the reply with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token expiry. Every reply following that contract is rejected. Lark has the same incompatibility: its new delegated call still expects the provider's nested `data` response and refresh-token metadata. These adapters need a delegated-response path that updates access token and expiry while preserving the existing provider metadata.

title: Delegate Salesforce refreshes to the configured source
body: Unlike the other changed integrations, this new refresh always calls Salesforce directly and never uses `refreshOAuthTokens`. Configuring `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` therefore does not make the parent application the source of truth for Salesforce credentials. In particular, synced credentials without a locally usable refresh token fail here instead of obtaining an access token from the parent. Route Salesforce refreshes through the same delegation mechanism before parsing and saving the result.

title: Send the actual Zoom app slug
body: The refresh request sends `appSlug: 'zoomvideo'`, but Zoom's callback stores credentials with `appId: 'zoom'`, and the credential webhook resolves app slugs against the App table. `zoomvideo` is the integration directory/route name, not the app-store slug. A parent service keyed by the same slugs used for credential synchronization cannot locate this integration, so delegated Zoom refreshes fail. Send `zoom`.

title: Clear invalid status when replacing credentials
body: Updating an existing credential replaces only its key. Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credentials `invalid: true` after an invalid grant, so pushing fresh working tokens into one of those records leaves it marked invalid. The webhook returns success without restoring the integration's usable status. Clear the invalid flag when accepting replacement credentials.

title: Make initial credential synchronization atomic
body: The existence check and creation are separate operations with no serialization or uniqueness guard. Two concurrent initial webhook deliveries for the same user and app can both find no credential and create separate records. Later deliveries update only the arbitrary record returned by `findFirst`, leaving duplicate credentials with stale keys available to calendar and conferencing code. Make synchronization idempotent under concurrent delivery using a stable credential identity and an atomic or serialized update/create operation.

title: Use the booking organizer's credentials to update the calendar
body: The authorization check permits attendees and team admins to add guests, but EventManager is constructed with the caller's credentials. For a logged-in attendee with no connected calendar, those credentials cannot update the organizer's existing calendar references. The new guests are saved to the booking, but the organizer's Google/Outlook event remains unchanged. Construct the manager with the booking organizer and their credentials instead.

title: Authorize either team admins or team owners
body: The team authorization check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&. A team admin who is not the owner therefore fails this check and receives FORBIDDEN when adding guests to another member's booking, unless they are also an attendee. Use || so either privileged team role grants access.

title: Deduplicate guest addresses on the server
body: uniqueGuests only filters addresses already present in the booking; it does not remove duplicates within the submitted array. The server schema also accepts duplicates, so a request containing the same new address twice passes both values to createMany, creating duplicate attendees and sending duplicate invitation emails. The dialog's client-side Set validation does not protect the mutation from direct requests. Enforce uniqueness server-side before inserting guests.

title: Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist
body: Blacklist entries are lowercased, but submitted guest addresses are compared without normalization. z.string().email() accepts uppercase characters, so a blacklisted address such as blocked@example.com can be invited by submitting BLOCKED@example.com. Normalize submitted addresses before checking BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS so casing cannot bypass the configured exclusion.

title: Honor disabled standard-email settings for guest additions
body: sendAddGuestsEmails sends host and attendee emails unconditionally and has no event-type metadata parameter. Unlike the scheduled and location-change email helpers, it never checks disableStandardEmails.all.host or disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding a guest consequently sends notifications to recipients whose standard emails were explicitly disabled, including existing attendees, and can duplicate replacement workflow emails. Pass the event-type metadata from the handler and apply the existing email-disable checks.

title: Validate booking status before sending confirmed invitations
body: After finding the booking, the handler checks authorization but never checks its status. An organizer or attendee can therefore add guests to a CANCELLED, REJECTED, or PENDING booking. The subsequent guest-update emails attach an ICS with status CONFIRMED and method REQUEST, sending confirmed invitations for an event whose stored status remains cancelled, rejected, or pending. Reject unsupported booking states before creating attendees or use a status-appropriate notification flow.

title: Use the booking organizer's credentials for calendar updates
body: The handler allows attendees and team administrators to add guests, but retrieves credentials for the requesting user and constructs EventManager for that user. When someone other than the organizer invokes this mutation, their credentials do not provide access to the organizer's referenced calendar event. Guests are already saved, but the organizer's calendar can remain unchanged or the update can fail. Initialize the calendar update with the booking organizer's credentials instead.

title: Prevent guest additions from bypassing seated-event reservations
body: This mutation creates attendee rows without checking seatsPerTimeSlot, remaining capacity, or creating corresponding seat-reference records. The new action is also exposed on seated bookings, and existing attendees are authorized to invoke it. Consequently, an attendee can add arbitrary guests to a fully booked slot, exceeding its configured capacity and bypassing the normal seat-management lifecycle. Either reject seated bookings or add guests through the seat-reservation flow.

title: Accept either the team administrator or owner role
body: The isTeamAdminOrOwner check joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, requiring both checks to succeed. A team administrator without the owner role therefore receives FORBIDDEN when adding guests to another host's team booking, unless they happen to be an attendee. Use || so either authorized team-management role can perform this operation.

title: Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist
body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are converted to lowercase, but incoming guest addresses are compared without normalization. The server schema accepts uppercase email addresses, so a caller can submit BLOCKED@example.com to bypass a blacklist entry for blocked@example.com and still create and email that guest. Normalize incoming addresses before blacklist comparison and storage.

title: Enforce guest uniqueness on the server
body: The uniqueGuests filter only removes addresses already present in the booking; it does not remove duplicates within the submitted array. The server schema also accepts duplicates, so submitting the same new email twice passes both checks and sends both entries to createMany, producing duplicate attendees and notifications. The dialog's Set validation does not protect direct API calls. Deduplicate or reject duplicate addresses on the server before persisting them.

title: Check booking status before issuing confirmed invitations
body: There is no booking-status validation before adding guests and sending notifications. The UI exposes this action for past PENDING bookings, and cancelled or rejected bookings can also be submitted directly through tRPC. The mutation sends booking-confirmation emails to new guests and CONFIRMED iCalendar requests to existing attendees, incorrectly representing these meetings as confirmed. Restrict the operation to accepted bookings or make its notifications explicitly respect the current booking status.

title: Honor disabled standard-email settings for guest additions
body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally sends organizer and attendee emails and does not accept event-type metadata. Unlike the neighboring scheduling and location-change paths, it cannot honor disableStandardEmails.all.host or disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding a guest therefore sends standard emails—including scheduled emails to new guests—even when the event owner disabled them in favor of custom notifications. Pass the event metadata from the handler and apply the existing host and attendee email-disable checks.

title: Use the booking organizer's credentials to update the calendar
body: The handler permits attendees to add guests, but constructs EventManager using the caller and the caller's credentials rather than booking.user. For an attendee with no calendar credentials, the organizer's event cannot be updated; an attendee's own credentials likewise do not authorize updates to the organizer's event references. Guests can therefore be saved and emailed without being added to the actual calendar event. Resolve the calendar credentials from the booking organizer.

title: Make failed calendar updates recoverable on retry
body: The attendee insertion has already committed when updateCalendarAttendees is awaited. If that update throws, the mutation fails before sending notifications, but the new attendees remain saved. Retrying the same guest list then removes every address as already present and returns BAD_REQUEST before attempting the calendar update or emails again. A transient integration failure thus leaves an inconsistent booking that this action cannot repair. Make retries complete missing side effects or otherwise recover the failed operation.

title: Authorize team admins or owners rather than requiring both
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines the admin and owner checks with &&. A team admin who is not the owner, organizer, or attendee fails authorization even though the handler explicitly intends to grant team administrators access. Use a disjunction so either authorized team role can add guests.

title: Enforce guest uniqueness on the server
body: uniqueGuests only filters addresses against existing attendees; it does not deduplicate the submitted array. The server schema accepts repeated addresses, so a direct request containing ["new@example.com", "new@example.com"] passes both entries to createMany, producing duplicate attendees and duplicate notifications. The dialog's uniqueness validation does not protect the API. Validate or deduplicate guest addresses server-side before insertion.

title: Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist
body: The configured blacklist is lowercased, but each submitted guest address is compared without normalization. If blocked@example.com is blacklisted, submitting Blocked@example.com passes email validation and bypasses this exclusion, allowing an invitation to the blocked address. Normalize the submitted address before comparing it with the blacklist.

title: Check booking status before sending confirmed invitations
body: The handler never checks booking.status, so an authorized caller can add guests to pending, rejected, or cancelled bookings. sendAddGuestsEmails then sends scheduled invitations to new guests and REQUEST attachments with status CONFIRMED to existing participants. This announces an accepted meeting even when it was never approved or has been cancelled, and can recreate a cancelled calendar invitation. Reject inappropriate booking states or send notifications reflecting the actual status.

title: Respect disabled standard-email settings when adding guests
body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally emails the organizer and attendees and does not accept event-type metadata. Unlike the existing scheduled, rescheduled, and location-change senders, it therefore ignores disableStandardEmails.all.host and disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding a guest sends standard notifications even for event types whose owners explicitly disabled them. Pass the booking's event-type metadata and apply the existing host and attendee disable checks.

title: Populate team members when constructing the calendar event
body: The generated CalendarEvent never includes team information, even for collective bookings with multiple hosts. sendAddGuestsEmails only sends co-host notifications through calendarEvent.team.members, so that branch is always skipped for this handler and hosts other than booking.user are not notified about added guests. Load and populate the booking's participating team members before sending the update.

title: Retry cleanup can delete successfully scheduled reminders
body: The retry-limit branch does not require scheduled=false. Two overlapping cron invocations can both fetch an unscheduled reminder with retryCount=1: one fails and stores 2, while the other succeeds and marks it scheduled without resetting the counter. The next cron run then deletes this successfully scheduled reminder before its scheduled date. Twilio still has the queued SMS, but its local reference is lost, preventing subsequent cancellation or rescheduling through that reminder. Restrict retry-based cleanup to unscheduled SMS reminders.

title: Failure bookkeeping can abort the entire reminder batch
body: The update inside the catch block can itself throw, escaping the per-reminder error handling. For example, another cron invocation can delete a reminder after this invocation fetched it because its date has passed or its retry count reached the limit. Updating that missing row throws, and the catch block attempts to update the same missing row again. The resulting uncaught error stops processing all remaining reminders and returns an error for the whole job. Make failure recording tolerate missing rows and handle bookkeeping errors without terminating the batch.

title: Increment retry counts atomically to avoid losing failed attempts
body: Both failure paths assign reminder.retryCount + 1 using the snapshot fetched before processing the batch. If two cron invocations overlap and both read retryCount=0, their failed scheduling attempts both write 1. Two failures therefore leave the reminder below the deletion threshold, allowing additional scheduling attempts despite the intended two-failure limit. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths rather than overwriting the counter from the fetched value.

title: Exclude successfully scheduled reminders from retry cleanup
body: The retry-count branch deletes reminders regardless of their scheduled status. If overlapping cron invocations load an unscheduled reminder with retryCount = 1, one can successfully store scheduled = true and the Twilio reference while the other fails and writes retryCount = 2. The next invocation then deletes the successfully scheduled reminder even though its send date is still in the future. Twilio's message remains queued, but its reference is lost, preventing subsequent cancellation or rescheduling. Restrict exhausted-retry cleanup to reminders that are still unscheduled.

title: Increment retryCount atomically instead of using the batch snapshot
body: Both failure paths assign reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value fetched before processing the batch. If two cron invocations load retryCount = 0 and both fail, both write 1, so two failed attempts are recorded as only one and the reminder is attempted again instead of being retired. Repeated overlaps similarly undercount failures. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths so concurrent failures are not lost.

title: Keep failure bookkeeping from escaping the per-reminder catch
body: If another cron invocation's cleanup deletes a reminder after this invocation loads its batch, updating that reminder raises Prisma's record-not-found error. The catch now attempts another update against the same deleted ID, and that rejection is unhandled. Consequently, one stale reminder aborts the entire request and leaves all later reminders unprocessed, whereas the previous catch logged the error and continued. Handle missing rows or separately guard the retry-count write so it cannot terminate the batch.

title: Exclude successfully scheduled reminders from retry-limit cleanup
body: The retry-count deletion branch also matches reminders with `scheduled: true`. If two invocations load a reminder with retryCount 1, one can successfully schedule it while the other fails and writes retryCount 2. The next invocation then deletes the successfully scheduled future reminder and its Twilio reference, even though the message remains queued externally. This loses the tracking needed to cancel or reschedule that message. Limit retry cleanup to unscheduled SMS reminders and prevent stale failure updates from modifying successfully scheduled rows.

title: Increment retry counts atomically in both failure paths
body: Both failure paths calculate the new count from the snapshot returned by `findMany`. If two cron invocations overlap and both load retryCount 0, two failed scheduling attempts each write 1, losing one failure. A subsequent invocation then attempts scheduling again despite the intended two-failure limit. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths rather than assigning `reminder.retryCount + 1`.

title: Keep retry bookkeeping failures from aborting the entire batch
body: The new database update inside the per-reminder catch block can itself throw without being caught. For example, another invocation's cleanup can delete a selected reminder while this invocation awaits Twilio. Its first update then fails because the row is missing, and the catch block repeats an update against the same missing row, throwing again. Unlike the previous log-and-continue behavior, this aborts the handler and skips every remaining reminder. Make the retry update tolerant of deleted rows, such as through a conditional `updateMany`, and preserve per-reminder error isolation.

title: Parenthesize the OR-based authorization predicate before returning it
body: For team/org scopes with members and no optional filters, authConditions is an unparenthesized `A OR B` expression. Returning it directly makes normal raw-query composition unsafe: `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" >= ${from}` becomes `A OR (B AND dateConstraint)`, so the team-booking branch bypasses the date constraint. Placing additional constraints before the fragment instead leaves the personal-booking branch unconstrained. Wrap the returned authorization predicate in parentheses and test composition with an additional WHERE constraint for team/org scopes without optional filters.

title: Parenthesize the base authorization fragment when no filters exist
body: For org/team scopes without service-level filters, `authConditions` contains a top-level OR between team bookings and members' personal bookings, and this branch returns it without enclosing parentheses. Composing the new fragment as `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <date/status predicate>` therefore applies the additional predicate only to the personal-booking branch; all matching team bookings bypass it. The previous `findMany` implementation combined authorization and caller conditions structurally with AND. Return a parenthesized fragment here as well, and test an org/team query with an additional predicate to preserve that behavior.

title: Invalidate connected calendars after deleting cache data
body: The deletion success handler only invokes the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper passes its optional onChanged prop and disables window-focus refetching, so callers without a refresh callback retain the old cacheUpdatedAt after deletion. The dropdown consequently continues showing a cache timestamp and deletion action for data that no longer exists. Invalidate the connected-calendars query on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

title: An empty update does not advance SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
body: This call supplies an empty data object to Prisma updateMany. Prisma leaves @updatedAt unchanged when the update payload is empty, so successful cache refreshes never perform the SelectedCalendar timestamp update promised by this new logic. Pass updatedAt explicitly if that metadata should track refreshes, or remove the ineffective call if CalendarCache.updatedAt is the sole intended timestamp.

title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script
body: ENV_FILE is resolved against the caller's working directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore creates or modifies .env in the repository's parent directory rather than the repository's environment file. The script reports success, but the application never receives the new webhook URL. Resolve the path relative to BASH_SOURCE instead.

title: Use an in-place edit compatible with GNU sed
body: The existing-variable branch uses BSD-specific sed -i '' syntax. With GNU sed on Linux, the empty argument becomes the script and the replacement expression is treated as an input filename, producing an error without updating GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. The unchecked failure is followed by a success message, leaving webhook registrations pointed at the previous tunnel. Use portable replacement logic and check that the update succeeded.

title: Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache
body: The delete-cache success handler only invokes an optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query. The wrapper forwards props.onChanged rather than refetching its query, and disables refetchOnWindowFocus. When no callback is supplied, deletion succeeds but the UI continues showing the deleted cache's timestamp and deletion action until a reload. Invalidate connectedCalendars here, as the disconnect mutation already does.

title: Resolve backing cache records for in-memory delegated connections
body: An in-memory delegated Google connection has a synthetic negative credential ID, but CalendarCacheRepository.getCachedAvailability can serve it from a real credential's cache using userId and the calendar key. Looking up status only by the synthetic ID always returns null. The connected-calendar helper also hides the matching nondelegated connection, so delegated users cannot inspect or clear cache that is actually serving their availability. Resolve the backing user-owned cache for these connections; the deletion handler must likewise support that ownership resolution rather than requiring the synthetic ID to exist in Credential.

title: Explicitly write the selected-calendar refresh timestamp
body: Passing an empty data object to Prisma updateMany does not advance @updatedAt; Prisma leaves that field unchanged for an empty update. Consequently, this new call does not update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt after a successful availability refresh, despite its stated purpose. Supply an explicit updatedAt value, or remove the call if selected-calendar refresh tracking is no longer needed.

title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script location
body: ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's working directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore writes ../.env outside the repository, creating it if necessary, instead of updating the repository's environment file. The script reports success while the calendar service retains its previous webhook URL. Derive the environment-file path from the script's directory.

title: Avoid the macOS-only sed invocation
body: The separated empty argument in sed -i '' is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed, used on Linux, it is interpreted as an empty editing script and the substitution expression is treated as a filename, so an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is not replaced. The script still prints that the update succeeded, leaving webhook subscriptions pointed at the old tunnel. Use a portable replacement mechanism or handle BSD and GNU sed separately.

title: Invalidate calendar status after deleting the cache
body: The successful delete mutation only calls the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates connectedCalendars. The wrapper passes its optional onChanged prop rather than refetching its own query, so deleting the cache with default props leaves the old timestamp and delete action visible after the success toast. That query also disables window-focus refetching. Invalidate connectedCalendars here, as the disconnect mutation already does.

title: Resolve cache status for in-memory delegated credentials
body: Connected calendars can use negative IDs for in-memory delegation credentials, while their reusable cache entries belong to real database credentials. CalendarCacheRepository.getCachedAvailability explicitly handles this by looking up the cache using userId and key, but this new status lookup only matches credentialId. Such delegated Google connections therefore receive cacheUpdatedAt=null and cannot show or clear the cache even when availability is being served from it. Use the same user-scoped resolution strategy and provide a corresponding ownership-safe deletion path.

title: Preserve the existing selected-calendar input contract
body: Adding updatedAt and googleChannelId as required properties changes the input contract of getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb, including its explicitly retained legacy getConnectedDestinationCalendars export. Callers supplying the previously sufficient externalId, integration, and eventTypeId projections are now rejected by TypeScript. Neither new field is read by this function, and cache status is queried separately, so this creates an unnecessary source-compatibility break. Keep the previous input shape or make these additional properties optional.

title: An empty update does not advance SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
body: Calling updateManyByCredentialId with an empty data object does not update any fields; Prisma also leaves @updatedAt unchanged for empty updates. Consequently, this call does not record successful cache refreshes in SelectedCalendar.updatedAt as its comment promises. Pass an explicit updatedAt value if refreshes should update that metadata, or remove the no-op if only CalendarCache.updatedAt should track refresh time.

title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script
body: ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's working directory, not the script location. Running the normal repository-root command `bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` therefore writes to an .env file above the repository instead of the repository's .env. The script reports success, but the application never receives the tunnel URL and an unrelated environment file may be modified. Derive the repository path from BASH_SOURCE before selecting the environment file.

title: Use an environment-file update compatible with GNU sed
body: The `sed -i ''` invocation uses BSD/macOS syntax and fails with GNU sed on Linux. This branch runs whenever GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, so subsequent tunnel sessions leave the old URL in the environment file. Because the script ignores the command's exit status, it still reports that the URL was updated, and Google webhook subscriptions can continue targeting the previous tunnel. Use a portable replacement operation and stop if updating the file fails.

title: Reschedules still bypass the deferred cancellation mechanism
body: handleNewBooking passes immediateDelete=true for every reschedule, so this branch immediately cancels the SendGrid batch rather than recording it for cron. SendGrid retains these cancellations until the original send dates, so 100 future reschedule cancellations still exhaust the limit that caused this bug. Subsequent POST failures are only logged, and cancelled=true is never persisted for cron to retry. Old reminders can therefore still be delivered after rescheduling.

title: Cancel imminent reminders before waiting for cron
body: Scheduled-email cancellations now only set cancelled=true, even when the send time is close. With the 15-minute cron interval, a reminder due at 12:24 and cancelled at 12:01 after the 12:00 run is not processed until 12:15. It is then inside SendGrid's ten-minute no-cancellation window, although an immediate cancellation would have succeeded. These reminders will still be sent; near-term batches need immediate cancellation rather than unconditional deferral.

title: Isolate failures and commit each successful cancellation
body: The entire cancellation loop shares one try/catch, and database deletes are deferred until every SendGrid POST succeeds. Prisma queries are lazy, so if any POST rejects, none of the queued deletes execute and every remaining reminder is skipped. A repeatedly failing batch can keep aborting subsequent runs, while successfully cancelled batches are unnecessarily submitted again. Valid reminders can miss their cancellation windows and be delivered. Handle errors per reminder and execute each successful reminder's delete before moving on.

title: Await the reminder cancellation writes before returning
body: The promises returned by both cancellation helpers are discarded, while the previously awaited reminder database deletions have been removed. These helpers now perform the only write that marks a scheduled email cancelled or removes an unscheduled reminder. The handler can therefore return success before those writes commit; a serverless invocation can finish with cancellation work still pending, leaving reminders active. Collect and await the helper promises, including the equivalent changed call sites.

title: Cancel near-due reminders without waiting for the cron
body: Scheduled reminders are now only marked cancelled, leaving SendGrid cancellation to the 15-minute cron. If a booking is cancelled just after a cron run and its reminder is due 12 minutes later, SendGrid sends the reminder before the next run. That run then deletes the now-past reminder row before processing cancellations. Near-due reminders need synchronous cancellation; otherwise cancelled bookings still receive reminders even when the cron runs reliably.

title: Rescheduling bypasses the deferred cancellation fix
body: Passing true makes deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancel immediately even when the original reminder is scheduled days away. Those cancellations occupy SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation slots until their original send dates, recreating the quota exhaustion described in this PR. Once the quota is full, the helper only logs the failure and never marks the reminder cancelled, so the cron cannot retry it and the old reminder is sent. Rescheduling needs a durable deferred cancellation path too.

title: Handle cancellation failures per reminder
body: The try/catch surrounds the entire cancellation loop, so one rejected SendGrid request skips every remaining reminder and also skips Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete). Because Prisma queries are lazy, even the database deletions queued for earlier successful cancellations never execute. A persistently failing batch can therefore block other cancellations across cron runs until reminders are sent or removed as past. Catch failures per reminder and execute each successful cancellation's deletion independently.

title: Await reminder cancellation persistence before completing the request
body: The asynchronous cancellation helpers are called from forEach without awaiting or collecting their promises, and they are absent from the subsequent Promise.all. These helpers now perform the only database update or deletion that prevents the cron from sending a cancelled booking's reminders. The handler can return while those writes are pending; in a serverless deployment, execution may be suspended before they finish, leaving live reminders behind despite a successful cancellation response. Include these promises in the awaited work.

title: Handle imminent reminders before deferring cancellation to cron
body: The default cancellation path only sets cancelled=true, leaving the email queued at SendGrid until the 15-minute cron runs. If a booking is cancelled at 10:01, its reminder is due at 10:10, and the next cron runs at 10:15, the reminder is still sent. The cron then deletes the overdue database row before attempting cancellation. Reminders close to their send time need synchronous cancellation rather than unconditional deferral.

title: Rescheduling bypasses the new cancellation queue
body: Every rescheduled booking passes immediateDelete=true for its old email reminders, bypassing the one-hour cancellation window. SendGrid retains these cancellation entries until their original send times, so rescheduling 100 reminders scheduled days ahead can still exhaust the pending-cancellation quota described in this PR. Subsequent requests fail, and the immediate branch only logs the error without setting cancelled=true, so cron never retries those reminders and they remain scheduled for the old booking.

title: Persist successful cancellations and isolate failures per reminder
body: The Prisma delete operations accumulated here are lazy and execute only in the Promise.all after every SendGrid request succeeds. If any cancellation request fails, the outer catch skips that Promise.all, leaving even successfully cancelled reminders in the database. It also skips every remaining reminder. A persistent error for one batch can therefore repeatedly block unrelated cancellations, allowing their emails to reach their send times. Delete each successfully cancelled row promptly and handle request failures per reminder.

title: Await the database changes that record reminder cancellation
body: Reminder deletion and cancellation-flag updates now happen inside the async reminder-manager functions, but these nested forEach calls discard their promises. The operations are also no longer included in the awaited prismaPromises, unlike the previous database deletions. Consequently, the handler can return success before unscheduled reminders are deleted or queued emails are marked cancelled. In a serverless invocation, outstanding writes can be suspended after the response, leaving reminders eligible to be scheduled or sent. Collect and await these cancellation promises.

title: Await the asynchronous reschedule cleanup callbacks
body: `forEach` discards the promises returned by this now-async callback. If `getCalendar()` rejects, including when constructing `CalendarService` throws, the failure no longer reaches the surrounding `try/catch` as it did when `getCalendar()` was synchronous. Instead, it becomes an unhandled rejection while the rescheduler can continue sending the email and reporting success despite failed cleanup. Await the promises from `bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)` inside the `try`. The same async-callback conversion in `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125` and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553` also needs its returned promises observed.

title: Handle rejections from eagerly started app imports
body: Every import() here starts when the registry is evaluated, but consumers await only the entry for their selected app. The other import promises have no rejection handlers. If an unused app fails to load or throws during initialization, its rejection bypasses the importing caller's error handling and can terminate the Node worker. Defer imports until requested, or explicitly handle every eagerly started promise.

title: Await the asynchronous reschedule cleanup callbacks
body: forEach discards the promises returned by the new async callback. Errors from getCalendar, including CalendarService construction failures that previously reached the surrounding try/catch, now become unhandled rejections instead of being logged. Use an awaited Promise.all with map, or an awaited for...of loop. The same regression exists in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and the requestReschedule mutation in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx, where initialization errors now also escape the mutation's error handling.

title: Avoid starting import promises that have no rejection handler
body: Every import() starts when this module is evaluated, but consumers await only the entries they need. If an unused app's chunk fails to load or its module throws during initialization, that promise has no rejection handler. The failure becomes an unhandled rejection and can terminate the Node process, even when the current request never uses that app. Export loader callbacks and invoke the selected loader so its failure propagates to an awaiting caller, or explicitly handle every eagerly started import.

title: Await the newly asynchronous reschedule callbacks
body: forEach discards the promises returned by its newly async callback. Consequently, a rejection from getCalendar—including a CalendarService constructor failure that the surrounding try/catch previously caught—now becomes an unhandled rejection instead of being logged. Reschedule also proceeds to emails and can return true before calendar loading and deletion finish. Await Promise.all over a map, or use an awaited for...of loop. The same conversion in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and bookingsRouter.requestReschedule needs the same treatment.

title: Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts
body: When a slot overlaps a date override, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before checking busy times. This affects both fixed and round-robin hosts, including personal events. For example, an override allowing 10:00–11:00 makes a 10:00 slot available even when an accepted booking or external calendar event occupies that time. An override should replace working hours, not bypass conflict checks.

title: Require the entire booking to fit within an override
body: The override checks reject only disjoint intervals, so any partial overlap is treated as availability. With a fixed-host override of 10:00–11:00, a 60-minute slot generated for another host at 09:30 or 10:30 passes, despite extending outside the fixed host's availability. A slot starting exactly at 11:00 also passes because isAfter excludes equality. Both booking boundaries must be contained in an allowed override interval.

title: Split working hours cause every slot to be rejected
body: The new working-hours guard rejects a slot if it is outside any interval on that weekday, rather than accepting it if it is inside an interval. For a normal schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00 UTC, morning slots fail against the afternoon interval and afternoon slots fail against the morning interval. Consequently, personal and team events using lunch-break schedules become unbookable even without date overrides.

title: The working-hours end check uses the slot's start time
body: Both start and end are calculated from slotStartTime, so the check never verifies that the booking finishes within the host's working hours. For example, a fixed host available 09:00–10:00 passes validation for a 60-minute slot at 09:30 generated by another round-robin host's date override. This permits bookings extending beyond the fixed host's availability; end must be calculated from slotEndTime.

title: Apply overrides according to the host's local calendar date
body: The override's converted start and the slot are compared by UTC calendar date, but a date override replaces a day in the host's timezone. For a Kolkata fixed host normally available Monday 00:00–01:00, a Monday override of 14:00–15:00 must remove the regular early-morning availability. A slot on Sunday at 19:00 UTC is Monday 00:30 locally, yet this comparison misses the override and allows it through the regular working-hours check. Overrides can also incorrectly suppress availability on the adjacent local day.

title: Multiple override intervals reject each other's slots
body: dateOverrides.find searches for any same-day interval that does not overlap the slot. If a host has two override windows, such as 10:00–11:00 and 14:00–15:00, a slot in the first window is rejected by the second, and a slot in the second is rejected by the first. Valid split date overrides therefore produce no availability. The check must accept a slot contained in at least one window, rather than reject it for being outside another window.

title: Split converted overrides when they cross attendee midnight
body: The timezone conversion extracts only hours and minutes, discarding any date rollover. A 20:00–23:00 UTC override viewed in UTC+2 becomes startTime 1320 (22:00) and endTime 60 (01:00). buildSlots treats this as an invalid interval because startTime exceeds endTime, so a personal event loses the entire override instead of showing its portions on the two attendee dates. Preserve the converted dates and split the interval at midnight.

title: Override timezone conversion applies DST correction twice
body: The new offset uses timezone offsets on the override date, so the resulting minutes already account for that date's DST. buildSlots subsequently adds organizerDSTDiff minus inviteeDSTDiff, which is intended to correct working hours calculated with today's offsets. For example, while New York is on UTC−4, a future January override of 10:00–11:00 New York converts correctly to 15:00–16:00 UTC here, but buildSlots shifts it again to 16:00–17:00. Override slots need to avoid that additional correction.

title: Date overrides bypass booking and calendar conflict checks
body: When an override applies, this branch returns true before checking `busy`. A user with a 10:00–11:00 override and an existing 10:00–10:30 booking or calendar event will therefore have the occupied 10:00 slot advertised as available. Both fixed and rotating hosts pass their overrides into this function. Overrides should replace working hours, not bypass busy-time checks.

title: Require the entire slot to fit inside the override
body: These checks reject only completely disjoint intervals, so partial overlap is treated as availability. For example, a fixed host's 10:00–11:00 override accepts a 09:30–10:30 candidate generated by a rotating host, even though the fixed host is unavailable for the first half-hour. Check that the slot starts at or after the override start and ends at or before its end.

title: Check the actual slot end against working hours
body: `end` is calculated from `slotStartTime` again, so the event duration is ignored. With a fixed host available 09:00–10:00 UTC, a rotating host's override can generate a 60-minute 09:30–10:30 candidate that passes this check as if it ended at 09:30. This still offers round-robin events extending beyond the fixed host's availability.

title: Treat working-hour windows as alternatives
body: The `find` rejects a slot if any working-hour window excludes it. For a schedule with 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 on the same weekday, morning slots are rejected by the afternoon window and afternoon slots by the morning window, leaving no availability. A slot should be accepted when it fits one applicable window, not required to fit every window.

title: Do not reject valid slots against another override window
body: A date can contain multiple override intervals, but this search rejects a slot whenever it is disjoint from any interval on that date. With 10:00–11:00 and 14:00–15:00 UTC overrides, the valid 10:00 slot is rejected by the second interval and the valid 14:00 slot by the first. Consequently, split date overrides lose all their slots, including on personal events.

title: Split timezone-converted overrides across attendee dates
body: Keeping only the converted hour and minute discards date rollover. A 10:00–12:00 UTC override viewed in Pacific/Tongatapu (UTC+13) becomes 23:00–01:00, represented here as startTime 1380 and endTime 60. `buildSlots` skips that range because its start exceeds its end, so the availability disappears instead of being split across two attendee dates.

title: Avoid applying DST compensation twice to overrides
body: These offsets use the override date, but `buildSlots` subsequently applies `organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff` based on today's offsets. If New York is currently UTC−5 and a future 10:00–11:00 override occurs while it is UTC−4, a UTC attendee's slot is correctly converted to 14:00 here, then shifted back to 13:00 by `buildSlots` and rejected by the availability check. Already date-adjusted overrides must not receive that second DST correction.

title: Continue checking busy times after matching a date override
body: When an override exists for the slot's date, this branch returns true before checking busy. For example, an override allowing 10:00–11:00 makes that slot available even when an existing booking or calendar event occupies 10:00–11:00. This affects both fixed and round-robin hosts. An override should replace normal working hours, not bypass calendar and booking conflicts.

title: Require a matching working-hours interval instead of rejecting on any nonmatch
body: The working-hours check rejects a slot when any interval for its weekday excludes it. With ordinary split availability such as 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, every morning slot is rejected by the afternoon interval and every afternoon slot by the morning interval, leaving no available slots even for a personal event. Availability must require at least one matching interval, rather than require compatibility with every interval.

title: Treat multiple date-override windows as alternatives
body: This find searches for an override that excludes the slot and rejects the slot as soon as one is found. If a date has overrides for 10:00–11:00 and 14:00–15:00, a valid 10:00 slot is rejected because it precedes the second override, while a valid 14:00 slot is rejected because it follows the first. Multiple windows on one date therefore produce no availability. The check should accept a slot covered by any override window.

title: Require the complete event to fit inside the override
body: The override checks reject only wholly disjoint slots, so any partial overlap is accepted. For a fixed host with a 10:00–11:00 override, a 10:30–11:30 round-robin slot supplied by another host passes these checks and reaches the dateOverrideExist return true, despite the fixed host being unavailable for its final half hour. A slot beginning exactly at 11:00 is also accepted. Validate both the slot start and slot end against the override boundaries.

title: Identify overridden days using the organizer's calendar date
body: Override existence is determined from the date of its UTC-shifted start, rather than the organizer's overridden calendar day. For example, a fixed host in Asia/Kolkata with a Tuesday 00:30–01:30 override has an interval starting Monday at 19:00 UTC. A Tuesday 10:00 IST slot from another host consequently does not match the override's date and falls back to the fixed host's regular working hours, potentially exposing the rest of Tuesday as available. Determine the overridden day in the host's timezone before checking the converted interval.

title: Use the event's end time when checking working hours
body: The end variable is calculated from slotStartTime again, so this check never verifies that the event finishes before the host's closing time. For example, with a fixed host working 09:00–17:00 and another host's date override generating a 16:30–17:30 slot, both start and end are evaluated as 16:30 and the fixed host is marked available. Use slotEndTime and require the complete event to fit within a working-hours interval.

title: Split converted overrides at the invitee's midnight
body: Adding the timezone offset and then retaining only hour and minute loses calendar-day rollover. A UTC override from 17:00–19:00 viewed in UTC+6 becomes startTime 1380 and endTime 60. buildSlots discards this as an invalid start >= end range, so the valid 23:00–01:00 availability disappears. The next day cannot recover it because activeOverrides only selects by the override's start. Convert full timestamps and split or clip the interval against each invitee day.

title: Avoid applying the DST adjustment twice to overrides
body: These offsets are calculated on the override's date, so the converted minutes already account for that date's DST. buildSlots subsequently applies organizerDSTDiff minus inviteeDSTDiff again, as it does for recurring working hours normalized using current offsets. If today is in winter, a July 10:00–11:00 override in America/New_York viewed in UTC is converted correctly to 14:00–15:00 here, then shifted to 13:00–14:00 by buildSlots. The router can then reject that shifted slot entirely. Overrides need to bypass this additional recurring-hours DST correction.

title: Handle missing category rows before indexing the query result
body: When embed_category is unset, empty, or names a deleted category, the join returns no rows. Accessing [0]['id'] then raises before the uncategorized fallback can run. This blocks db:migrate for installations that never configured embedding, including clean installs. Read the result conditionally; the fallback query also needs to handle an absent persisted uncategorized_category_id setting.

title: Normalize legacy host entries before inserting them
body: The old allowlist supported full URLs such as http://discourse.org and https://example.com/1234, but this migration copies them verbatim. Direct SQL bypasses EmbeddableHost's callback that strips schemes and paths, while the new lookup compares the stored value with the bare URI hostname. After upgrading, these previously working entries no longer authorize embedding or topic retrieval. Apply the same hostname normalization during migration.

title: Match port-qualified hosts consistently
body: The model accepts example.com:8080 and retains the port in the stored host, but URI('http://example.com:8080/page').host returns only example.com. This query therefore cannot find the saved record. Administrators can successfully configure a port-qualified host, yet embedding requests from it are rejected and its category mapping is never found. Normalize stored entries and lookup keys consistently.

title: Allow valid top-level domains longer than five characters
body: The [a-z]{2,5} suffix rejects valid domains such as example.museum and example.technology. Stripping the scheme and path does not change that restriction, so administrators cannot save these legitimate embedding hosts in the new editor. Host validation should not impose a five-character maximum on top-level domains.

title: Enforce one category mapping per normalized hostname
body: There is no uniqueness validation or database constraint for host, so Add Host can save the same hostname multiple times with different categories, including differently cased spellings. record_for_host returns only the first matching record, meaning a successfully saved or edited mapping on another row is silently ignored when topics are imported. Enforce case-insensitive uniqueness for the normalized hostname so category routing is unambiguous.

title: Handle an unset embed category before indexing the query result
body: The category query returns no rows when embed_category was never configured or names a deleted or renamed category. Indexing its result with [0]['id'] then raises before reaching the uncategorized fallback. This prevents db:migrate from completing on installations that do not use embedding, including clean databases. Read the optional result safely and also handle a missing uncategorized_category_id setting.

title: Normalize legacy hosts during migration
body: The old host-matching logic supported entries containing schemes and paths, such as https://example.com/1234. This INSERT copies those entries verbatim and bypasses EmbeddableHost's normalization callback. The new lookup compares the stored value with URI.host, so these migrated entries never match example.com. Existing embedded comments consequently return access errors and topic retrieval stops after upgrading. Normalize each legacy entry before inserting it.

title: Quote host values instead of interpolating them into SQL
body: Each legacy host value is interpolated directly into a single-quoted SQL literal. A URL containing an apostrophe in its path, such as https://example.com/it's, breaks the INSERT and aborts the upgrade; crafted values can also alter the SQL statement. Use bound values or connection.quote rather than treating persisted setting text as SQL.

title: Allow valid hostnames with longer top-level domains
body: The hostname regex limits the final suffix to two through five letters, rejecting valid domains such as example.museum and example.technology. Administrators cannot add these hosts. Legacy entries inserted by the migration bypass validation, but subsequently changing their category also fails validation. Hostname validation should not impose this obsolete TLD-length restriction.

title: Make port-qualified host storage and lookup consistent
body: Validation accepts example.com:8080, and normalization retains the port, including when an administrator enters https://example.com:8080. However, URI.host returns only example.com, which can never match the stored example.com:8080 value. A successfully saved port-qualified host therefore cannot embed comments or retrieve topics. Normalize storage and lookup consistently, or reject port-qualified entries explicitly.

title: Enforce one category mapping per normalized hostname
body: Neither the model nor the table prevents duplicate hostnames, including case variants. Administrators can save example.com twice with different categories, but record_for_host always selects the first matching row. Editing the other row succeeds without changing the category used for imports, leaving a configuration that the application silently ignores. Enforce case-insensitive hostname uniqueness in validation and the database.

title: Guard missing hosts before string normalization
body: The before_validation callback calls sub! on host without checking for nil. Creating or updating through the new endpoint with an omitted or null host therefore raises NoMethodError instead of returning the validation errors handled by save_host. The same exception occurs when validating EmbeddableHost.new. Guard normalization and validate the required host so malformed input produces a controlled error response.

title: Handle an unset embed_category before indexing the query result
body: The category query can return no rows when embed_category was never configured, is blank, or names a deleted category. Indexing row zero then fails before the intended uncategorized fallback runs. This also happens on a fresh database and on sites that never enabled embedding, so the migration blocks installation or upgrade. Handle empty results explicitly, including the fallback query.

title: Normalize legacy allowed-host entries during migration
body: The old embedding configuration accepts entries such as http://example.com and https://example.com/some-path. This migration inserts those values verbatim, bypassing the new model's protocol/path normalization. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares the stored value against URI.host, which is only example.com, so migrated URL-form entries stop allowing comments and topic retrieval after upgrade. Normalize the legacy entries before inserting them.

title: Quote legacy host values in the INSERT
body: Each legacy allowed-host value is interpolated directly into a quoted SQL literal without escaping. URL-form entries can contain apostrophes in their paths, such as https://example.com/o'reilly; such a value produces invalid SQL and aborts the migration. Use bound parameters or the connection's quoting API rather than concatenating the setting value into SQL.

title: Allow valid DNS names in host validation
body: The new hostname regex limits the top-level domain to five letters and prohibits consecutive hyphens. Consequently, valid hosts such as blog.technology, example.museum, and the punycode hostname xn--bcher-kva.de cannot be added or edited through the embedding configuration. Use hostname validation that supports valid DNS labels and current top-level domains.

title: Make port-qualified host entries match incoming URLs
body: Validation accepts example.com:8080, and the normalization callback retains the port, but record_for_host compares that stored string with URI.host, which returns example.com without the port. A successfully saved port-qualified entry therefore never allows even http://example.com:8080 and never supplies its category during import. Normalize storage and lookup consistently, or compare the host and port explicitly.

title: Enforce a unique normalized host-to-category mapping
body: Neither the model nor the migration prevents multiple records for the same hostname, including differently cased variants. Administrators can therefore save the same host with different categories, while record_for_host silently selects the first matching record. The other relationship appears successfully configured but is ignored when importing topics. Enforce uniqueness on the normalized, case-insensitive hostname, including a database constraint.

title: Guard missing host values before normalization
body: The before_validation callback calls sub! on host unconditionally. Creating or updating a host with an embeddable_host payload that omits host assigns nil and raises NoMethodError before the format validator or render_json_error can run. Missing required input should produce a validation response rather than a server error; guard blank values before normalizing them.

title: Preserve the existing width/height downsize API
body: Ruby does not overload methods by arity: this definition replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition. Existing four-argument calls now treat the numeric height as `opts` and fail when `optimize` accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`; five-argument calls raise `ArgumentError`. Support both argument forms within one definition rather than silently removing the existing API.

title: Keep attachment validation tied to its configured size limit
body: The hardcoded 10 MB limit also applies to attachments, although the controller only downsizes images. Attachments larger than `max_attachment_size_kb` now pass client validation and are uploaded unchanged, while attachments permitted by a configured limit above 10 MB are now blocked. Relax the image limit without replacing the configured attachment limit.

title: Identify animated GIFs independently of the tempfile suffix
body: This passes the temporary path rather than the original filename to the optimizer. For an animated GIF backed by an extensionless multipart tempfile, `OptimizedImage.optimize` does not select its animated instructions because it checks whether the input path ends in `.gif`. It instead runs `convert` with the `[0]` frame selector and overwrites the uploaded original with a single frame, even when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is enabled. Determine the animation format from the original filename or file contents before resizing.

title: Use supported resize dimensions for the animated GIF branch
body: When the input path does end in `.gif` and animation is enabled, this percentage-based call reaches `resize_instructions_animated`, which generates `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. Gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects pixel dimensions in `WIDTHxHEIGHT` form, not a percentage, so the command fails. The controller ignores the result and repeats the same invalid command five times without reducing the oversized GIF. Calculate pixel dimensions for this branch or use an animation-preserving operation that supports percentage resizing.

title: The new downsize definition replaces the width/height API
body: Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature, so this second definition replaces the existing downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) method. Calls using four arguments now treat max_height as the options hash and fail when optimize accesses opts[:allow_animation]; calls supplying a fifth options argument fail with ArgumentError. Preserve the previously supported width/height form in a single compatible implementation.

title: Reopen the tempfile after in-place optimization
body: OptimizedImage.downsize calls ImageOptim.optimize_image!, which can replace the file at its pathname with an optimized file. The already-open tempfile then still references the old inode. Subsequent tempfile.size checks can remain stuck at an earlier size, and the filesize passed to Upload.create_for can differ from the resized file on disk. This can reject an image that was successfully reduced below the limit or record an incorrect filesize. Reopen the resulting file before checking its size and creating the upload, or resize into a separate tempfile.

title: Percentage geometry is unsupported by the animated GIF resizer
body: When allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled and the GIF tempfile has a .gif extension, downsize selects the animated implementation, which emits gifsicle --resize-fit 80%. That option requires width/height geometry rather than a percentage, so all five attempts fail and the oversized animated GIF remains above the upload limit. Use a GIF scaling operation or calculate explicit target dimensions.

title: Do not impose the image input ceiling on attachments
body: This hard-coded 10 MiB limit applies to attachments as well as images, replacing the configured max_attachment_size_kb limit even though attachments are not downsized. A site configured to permit attachments larger than 10 MiB now has otherwise-valid uploads rejected by the browser before they reach the server. Retain the configured attachment limit and apply the preprocessing ceiling only to images.

title: The second downsize definition replaces the existing API
body: Ruby does not overload methods by argument count, so this definition replaces the width/height version immediately above it. Existing calls to downsize(from, to, width, height, opts) now raise ArgumentError, while calls without an options hash bind height to opts and fail at opts[:allow_animation]. Preserve the existing width/height interface by handling both argument forms in one method or giving percentage downsizing a separate name.

title: The new reduction path cannot preserve animated GIF uploads
body: Animated-image dispatch checks whether tempfile.path ends in .gif, not the uploaded filename or actual format. An extensionless multipart tempfile therefore uses convert's [0] branch and overwrites the original with only its first frame, even when animation is enabled. If the tempfile does have a .gif suffix, the animated branch passes "80%" to gifsicle --resize-fit, which expects pixel dimensions rather than a percentage and fails. Oversized animated GIFs are consequently either silently flattened or left oversized and rejected. Detect animation independently of the temporary filename and use GIF-compatible resizing instructions.

title: Keep the configured size limit for attachments
body: The fixed 10 MB limit applies to attachments as well as images, although the server only downsizes images. This stops honoring max_attachment_size_kb: a 12 MB attachment allowed by a configured 20 MB limit is now rejected by the browser, while an attachment exceeding a smaller configured limit is uploaded before the server rejects it. Relax validation only for images and retain the configured attachment limit.

title: Protect unsubscribe mutations against CSRF
body: The new GET endpoints change the logged-in user's notification settings without a signed unsubscribe token. Rails does not require CSRF tokens for GET requests, and this action also bypasses the XHR check. A third-party page can therefore request a predictable URL such as /t/123/unsubscribe.json in an authenticated browser and silently lower or mute that user's notifications. Keep GET read-only and perform the change through a CSRF-protected request, or validate a recipient-specific unsubscribe token.

title: Handle users without an existing TopicUser record
body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for a logged-in user who has never interacted with this topic. For example, this happens when a public-topic email link is forwarded or opened while logged into a different account. TopicView does not establish that a TopicUser row exists, so dereferencing tu.notification_level raises an exception and returns a server error. Treat a missing row as the default notification level and use the create-or-update path when unsubscribing.

title: Persist unsubscribe as an explicit notification preference
body: Saving only notification_level leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged. For a user whose reason is nil, an unsubscribe that sets the topic to muted can later be undone by TopicUser.update_last_read: that method automatically assigns tracking whenever the reason is nil and the reading-time threshold is met. Thus reading the topic can unmute an explicitly unsubscribed user. Use TopicUser.change, or otherwise record the user_changed reason and notification-change timestamp along with the new level.

title: Unsubscribe when the URL is reached through client-side navigation
body: This route only loads the ordinary topic view; it never invokes the unsubscribe action or changes the notification level. The preference changes only when a full-page request reaches TopicsController#unsubscribe. If the URL is followed through an Ember transition, such as a same-site link while the application is already running, the page displays the unsubscribe confirmation while the user remains subscribed. Ensure the operation is performed for client-side navigation too, rather than relying on the initial HTML request.

title: Mute watched topics for mailing-list recipients
body: The new per-topic link is also included in emails generated by mailing_list_notify. However, for a mailing-list user whose topic is watching or tracking, this branch only lowers the level to regular. Regular does not opt a topic out of mailing-list delivery, so subsequent posts keep producing the same emails despite the unsubscribe confirmation. Mailing-list recipients need the topic muted to stop those emails; account for mailing_list_mode when choosing the new level.

title: Do not change notification preferences through an unprotected GET
body: This GET invokes TopicsController#unsubscribe, which immediately saves a new notification level for the logged-in user. The URL is predictable, has no unsubscribe token, and bypasses check_xhr; Rails' normal CSRF protection does not validate GET requests. An attacker can therefore send a logged-in victim through a cross-site navigation to silence notifications for an accessible topic. Make GET display a confirmation and perform the change through a CSRF-protected POST.

title: Persist the unsubscribe change during client-side navigation
body: This route only loads the ordinary topic view; it never invokes the unsubscribe endpoint or changes the notification level. If an already-loaded Discourse application navigates to the unsubscribe URL client-side, the initial HTML request to TopicsController#unsubscribe never happens. The page nevertheless tells the user notifications will stop, while their subscription remains unchanged. The client-side flow needs to perform the subscription change explicitly.

title: Mark unsubscription as an explicit notification preference change
body: Saving notification_level directly bypasses the bookkeeping in TopicUser.change, particularly setting notifications_reason_id to user_changed. For an existing topic-user row whose reason is NULL, an unsubscribe can set the level to Muted but leave it eligible for automatic tracking. TopicUser.update_last_read then changes it back to Tracking once the reading-time threshold is met, undoing the mute and re-enabling notifications. Use the normal notification-change helper so the explicit preference is preserved.

title: Handle an absent TopicUser record
body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil: for example, a forwarded notification for a public topic can be opened by another logged-in account that has never visited that topic. Access to the topic does not guarantee a topic-user row exists. Dereferencing tu.notification_level then raises NoMethodError and returns a server error instead of unsubscribing. Treat the missing row as the default notification level and create the preference through TopicUser.change.

title: Keep the topic URL optional in the shared unsubscribe footer
