body: The shared unsubscribe_link translation now unconditionally requires unsubscribe_url, but Email::MessageBuilder still accepts add_unsubscribe_link without supplying that value. A previously supported call such as MessageBuilder.new(address, body: "hello", add_unsubscribe_link: true).body now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument instead of building an email. Both text and HTML footer generation use this translation. Preserve the generic preferences-only footer and add the topic paragraph only when a topic unsubscribe URL is available.

title: Do not promise that Regular disables all topic notifications
body: The confirmation says the user will stop receiving notifications for the topic, but the controller changes Watching or Tracking users to Regular rather than Muted. Regular still allows notifications and notification emails for mentions and replies to the user, so the confirmation promises more than the operation provides. Describe the notifications that remain enabled, or change the operation to match the promise.

title: Do not change notification preferences through an unprotected GET
body: Both unsubscribe routes use GET, but TopicsController#unsubscribe immediately changes the authenticated user's notification level without an authorization token or confirmation. Rails CSRF protection does not validate GET requests, and this action also skips check_xhr. An external site can therefore send an authenticated user to a predictable unsubscribe URL and demote or mute a topic without consent. Keep GET read-only and perform the change through a CSRF-protected POST, or require a signed, recipient-scoped unsubscribe token.

title: Perform the unsubscribe when navigating through Ember
body: This route only loads the ordinary topic view with PostStream.loadTopicView; it never invokes the unsubscribe action or changes the notification level. Following an internal unsubscribe link in an already-running application therefore bypasses the server-side HTML request that performs the mutation. The page says notifications will stop even though the user remains subscribed. Perform the unsubscribe explicitly through a client action rather than relying exclusively on a full-page request.

title: Handle users without an existing TopicUser record
body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for a logged-in user who has never interacted with the topic, such as someone following a forwarded notification email. This action does not create a per-topic record before dereferencing tu.notification_level, so an otherwise valid unsubscribe request fails with NoMethodError and a 500 response. Handle the missing record using the regular notification level as the default and create the preference through TopicUser.change.

title: Record unsubscribe as an explicit notification preference change
body: Saving notification_level directly leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged. For a regular or automatically tracked TopicUser whose reason is nil, TopicUser.update_last_read changes the level to tracking once the viewed-time threshold is exceeded, even if this action just set it to muted. Reading the topic can therefore silently undo the unsubscribe. Use TopicUser.change so the preference is marked user_changed, its timestamp is updated, and the notification-level change is published.

title: Preserve unsubscribe footers for callers without a topic URL
body: The shared unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url, but Email::MessageBuilder does not provide a default for it. The previously supported call Email::MessageBuilder.new(to, body: 'hello', add_unsubscribe_link: true) now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when building the body or HTML footer. Generic callers should still be able to add the preferences link without having a topic URL. Append the topic-specific stanza only when unsubscribe_url is supplied.

title: Normalize email addresses before storing and matching blocklist entries
body: The lookup uses case-sensitive equality, and BlockedEmail does not normalize addresses when storing them or checking them. An entry for `blocked@example.com` therefore does not match `blocked@EXAMPLE.COM`, although domain casing does not change the mailbox. The signup flow assigns the submitted email directly, allowing a blocked user to bypass this restriction by changing the domain's casing. Apply consistent email canonicalization to both stored entries and lookup values.

title: Require a nonempty email-error array before rejecting an address
body: EmailValidator reads `record.errors[:email]` even when the email passes validation, which creates an empty array in ActiveModel::Errors. The controller's `errors.to_hash` consequently includes `email: []` when signup fails for another field. Empty arrays are truthy in JavaScript, so this condition caches the valid address as rejected—for example, after a username becomes unavailable between the availability check and submission. Correcting the username then leaves submission disabled until the email changes or the page reloads. Check that the email-error array contains an error before caching the address.

title: Update match statistics atomically
body: The method reads match_count, increments it in Ruby, and saves it without locking the row. Concurrent checks for the same address can both read the same count and overwrite each other with the same incremented value, losing matches. An older request can also overwrite a newer last_match_at value. Use an atomic database update or a row lock to preserve these statistics.

title: Blocked-match statistics are rolled back by failed user saves
body: Calling the mutating should_block? method during User validation makes its statistics update part of the surrounding User#save transaction. When the address is blocked, this validator adds an error and the user save rolls back, undoing BlockedEmail's match_count and last_match_at updates too. Paths that call save directly, such as User.create_for_email, therefore reject the address without recording the match. Persist match tracking outside the failing user-save transaction and cover a blocked User#save in an integration test.

title: Case-sensitive matching allows blocked addresses to bypass the ban
body: Neither BlockedEmail creation nor this lookup normalizes the address. A block for `bad@spammers.org` therefore does not match `bad@SPAMMERS.ORG`, even though email domains are case-insensitive. A user can change the domain's capitalization to pass the new validation and register with the same blocked mailbox. Apply consistent email normalization when storing and looking up blocked addresses.

title: Concurrent matches lose counter increments
body: The read-modify-save sequence is not atomic. Two requests matching the same address can both read match_count as N and both save N+1, recording only one of the two matches. Concurrent registration attempts therefore undercount blocked-email activity. Increment the counter atomically in the database or protect the update with a row lock.

title: Rejected user saves roll back the match statistics
body: When this helper runs inside User.save or User.save!, the BlockedEmail save joins the enclosing user transaction. The email validator then adds a blocking error, causing Rails to roll back that transaction—including match_count and last_match_at. Paths such as User.create_for_email, which calls save! without a preceding standalone valid? call, reject the address without recording the match. Persist rejected-match statistics independently of the failed user transaction and cover this through a user-save integration test.

title: Canonicalize email addresses before matching blocked entries
body: Blocked emails are stored as ordinary strings and matched with case-sensitive equality, without normalization. A block for `bad@SpamClub.com` therefore does not match `bad@spamclub.com`, although email domains are case-insensitive and these identify the same mailbox. Mixed-case block imports or differently cased input can silently bypass the block. Normalize stored addresses and lookup values consistently using the application's email canonicalization.

title: An empty email error array incorrectly rejects a valid address
body: The new EmailValidator reads `record.errors[:email]` even when the email is valid, which creates an empty array entry in ActiveModel::Errors. If registration fails for another field, such as a username taken after the availability check, `errors.to_hash` can return `email: []`. Empty arrays are truthy in JavaScript, so this condition caches the valid email as rejected and disables resubmission even after the username is corrected. Require a nonempty email error array before rejecting the address.

title: Rejected user saves roll back the block-match statistics
body: When email validation runs inside `User#save` or `save!`, this nested save participates in the user's transaction. Adding the blocked-email validation error causes the outer save to fail and roll back both the counter increment and `last_match_at`. For example, `User.create_for_email` calls `save!` without a preceding standalone validation, so its rejected attempts leave no match statistics. The direct `should_block?` tests do not exercise this rollback. Record attempt statistics outside the transaction that rejects the user.

title: Update match counters atomically
body: The counter is updated through an unlocked read-modify-save sequence. Two concurrent checks for the same address can both read a count of N and save N+1, losing one match; out-of-order saves can also replace `last_match_at` with an older timestamp. This makes the blocking statistics unreliable under concurrent requests. Use an atomic database increment and a concurrency-safe timestamp update, or lock the row.

title: Fix the invalid ERB conditional terminator
body: The template closes its conditional with `end if`, leaving a trailing `if` without a condition. This produces invalid Ruby when Rails compiles the ERB template, so requests for an existing embedded topic fail with a template syntax error instead of displaying the discussion. The terminator should be `end`.

title: Preserve HTML sanitization for raw-HTML posts
body: Returning `raw` bypasses HTML sanitization on both creation and subsequent edits. PollFeed passes external feed HTML into TopicEmbed.import without sanitizing it, and Nokogiri fragment parsing does not remove scripts or event handlers. TopicEmbed also appends an attribution link containing an unescaped embed URL after Readability filtering. These values reach `post.cooked` and are rendered with `raw`, allowing stored JavaScript to execute on the forum origin. Skipping Markdown rendering must not skip HTML safety checks.

title: Validate redirect destinations before fetching remote content
body: TopicRetriever checks only the initial URL's host, while open-uri follows redirects here without rechecking the destination. An anonymous embed request pointing to a redirect on the allowed host can therefore make the worker fetch a non-allowlisted host or an internal HTTP resource, whose content may then be imported into a public topic. Validate the scheme and destination of every redirect rather than treating the initial host check as sufficient.

title: Support RSS bodies outside the Atom content field
body: Valid RSS feeds commonly store item bodies in `description` or `content:encoded`, and Atom entries can provide only `summary`. Those entries have no `i.content`, so calling `.scrub` here raises instead of importing them and aborts the rest of the polling run. Select the available body field and handle entries without a body; tests should exercise actual RSS and Atom fixtures rather than only the execute guards.

title: Resolve relative URLs against the complete article URL
body: This conversion treats protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` as local paths, producing a broken URL such as `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. It also leaves path-relative references such as `images/photo.jpg` and `../other-article` unchanged, so browsers resolve them against the Discourse page rather than the source article. The same problems affect images below. Use URI resolution against the complete article URL for both href and src.

title: Defer post jobs until the outer import transaction commits
body: PostCreator.create enqueues processing and featured-user jobs after its own Post.transaction block, but that transaction joins the outer Topic.transaction opened here. Consequently, those jobs are enqueued before the post and topic are committed, and before the TopicEmbed insertion can fail. Another worker can process rows that are not yet visible, or work for an import that subsequently rolls back. Arrange for these jobs and publication side effects to run only after the outer transaction commits.

title: Update imported content and its hash under one lock
body: The post revision and content_sha1 update are separate operations without a transaction or row lock. Scheduled polling and retrieval-triggered polling can overlap: one import can save body A, another save body B and hash B, then the first write hash A. The stored hash then describes different content from the post, and a subsequent import of A skips a necessary revision because the hashes match. Serialize updates for an embed and commit its post revision and hash together.

title: Set the retrieval throttle and its expiration atomically
body: SETNX and EXPIRE are separate commands. If the worker terminates between them, the retrieval key remains without an expiration. Every later non-staff attempt then sees SETNX fail and refuses to retrieve that URL indefinitely, leaving the embed stuck on the reloading screen. Use an atomic Redis operation that sets the key only when absent and assigns its TTL in the same command.

title: Preserve historical topic timestamps during Disqus imports
body: The previous topic creation passed the exported thread's `created_at`, but TopicEmbed.import_remote has no creation-time option and creates the first post at the current time. Replies still receive their historical timestamps. Importing an old export therefore makes every topic appear newly created and gives its first post a timestamp later than its replies, corrupting discussion history and chronological statistics. Pass the exported creation time through the new import path.

title: Compare message origins exactly rather than by substring
body: The substring check accepts origins that merely prefix the configured forum origin. For example, with `discourseUrl` set to `https://forum.example.com/`, a message from `https://forum.example.co` passes this check. An unrelated frame or window with a reference to the embedding page can then send trusted resize messages and manipulate the comments frame's height. Compare against the parsed origin exactly and verify that the message source is this iframe.

title: Fix the invalid closing conditional in the embed template
body: The template closes its conditional with `end if`, but the trailing `if` has no condition. ERB therefore generates invalid Ruby and raises a syntax error when rendering this view. Once an embedded topic has been retrieved, requests switch from the loading page to a server error instead of displaying the discussion.

title: Preserve HTML sanitization for raw-HTML posts
body: Returning `raw` bypasses sanitization as well as Markdown rendering. RSS bodies reach this path after only entity decoding and a Nokogiri parse, which preserve scripts and event handlers. The importer also interpolates the attribution URL directly into HTML, so a valid article URL containing `?x='onmouseover='alert(1)` can inject an event-handler attribute even when Readability cleaned the article. This output is persisted as cooked HTML and rendered unescaped on the forum origin. Imported posts also retain this unsafe cooking mode on subsequent edits.

title: Validate redirect destinations during embedded-page retrieval
body: TopicRetriever checks the allowlisted host only on the original embed URL, but `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects without rechecking their destinations. An allowed-host URL that redirects elsewhere can therefore make the worker fetch off-allowlist or internal services, potentially importing their responses into a topic. The embed-triggered retrieval path must enforce its host restriction before following each redirect.

title: Bound remotely downloaded content before parsing it
body: The visitor-controlled embed URL is restricted only by host, so it can identify a large video, archive, or other asset on the allowed site rather than an article. `open(url).read` downloads and buffers the complete response, then passes it to Readability/Nokogiri without a size limit or content-type check. Such requests can exhaust the Sidekiq process's memory. Enforce a download-size limit and reject unsuitable responses before HTML parsing.

title: Handle standard RSS body fields and entries without content
body: Valid RSS feeds commonly put article HTML in `description` or `content:encoded`, while Atom entries may provide only `summary`. These entries do not have an `i.content` value, so calling `scrub` on it fails and aborts the entire polling run before subsequent entries are imported. Select an available body field and explicitly handle entries with no body.

title: Resolve relative URLs using URI semantics
body: The current rewriting turns a protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` into `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`, losing the intended host. It also leaves path-relative values such as `images/photo.jpg` unchanged, so they resolve against the Discourse page instead of the source article. This breaks common imported links and images. Resolve both href and src values against the article URL rather than stripping leading slashes and concatenating a host prefix.

title: Defer post-processing jobs until the outer import transaction commits
body: PostCreator.create enqueues feature_topic_users and process_post after its own transaction block, but this caller wraps that block in an outer Topic.transaction. The nested transaction has not committed when those jobs are published, so separate Sidekiq workers can run before the post or topic is visible. If creating the embed subsequently fails, the jobs reference rolled-back records. Job publication needs to occur after the outermost transaction commits.

title: Handle simultaneous imports of the same URL
body: The existence lookup occurs before the creation transaction and does not serialize imports. The hourly feed poll and on-demand retrievals can import the same feed concurrently, allowing both callers to observe no embed and create a topic before one loses the unique embed_url insert race. The resulting RecordNotUnique exception aborts that feed's remaining entries, and scheduled polling has retries disabled. Serialize creation per URL or recover from the conflict by loading the winning embed.

title: Set the retrieval throttle and its expiration atomically
body: SETNX creates the throttle key without an expiration, and EXPIRE is issued separately. If EXPIRE fails or the worker exits between these commands, the article has not been retrieved but its key remains permanently present. Every later retrieval then reports it as recently retrieved, leaving the embed on the loading page indefinitely. Set the key and its TTL in one atomic operation.

title: Preserve original thread timestamps during Disqus imports
body: The old topic creation forwarded the Disqus thread's created_at value, but import_remote receives only its title and creates the initial post with the current time. Replies still retain their historical dates. Imported discussions therefore have a first post newer than their replies and are dated and ordered as newly created discussions rather than preserving the exported history. Forward the thread timestamp through the import helpers.

title: Do not require archived Disqus source pages to remain reachable
body: Importing each thread now performs a remote page fetch without exception handling. A normal 404 or connection failure for an archived permalink raises from open-uri and aborts the entire import, even though that thread's comments and all subsequent threads are already available in the XML export. Retain a permalink-only fallback when retrieving the source article fails so the comment migration can still complete.

title: Update dependency locks for the other supported Rails boot modes
body: The new dependencies are unconditional, but only Gemfile_rails4.lock is updated. This Gemfile still selects Gemfile.lock in RAILS3 mode and Gemfile_rails_master.lock in RAILS_MASTER mode. Frozen or deployment installs using those modes now have lockfiles that disagree with the Gemfile and fail dependency installation. Update the corresponding lockfiles or scope the dependencies to the supported mode.

title: Fix the invalid ERB block terminator
body: The opening if/else block is closed with `end if` rather than `end`. The trailing `if` has no condition, so the generated Ruby cannot compile. Requests that find an existing embedded topic will fail while rendering this template instead of displaying the discussion. The controller specs do not render views, so they do not catch this failure.

title: Sanitize raw HTML before storing it as cooked content
body: This branch returns HTML unchanged, but the feed import path does not sanitize it: PollFeed decodes feed content, and TopicEmbed only parses it to rewrite URLs. Script tags, event-handler attributes, and javascript links can therefore survive into `post.cooked`, which the embed view renders with `raw` on the forum's origin. Edits to imported posts retain the same sanitization bypass. Raw HTML rendering must still apply an HTML safety policy to prevent stored XSS.

title: Handle standard RSS description and encoded-content fields
body: The poller assumes every item has an Atom-style `content` field. Standard RSS items commonly provide `description` or `content:encoded` instead; SimpleRSS exposes those separately, leaving `i.content` nil. Calling `scrub` then raises and aborts the entire poll, so ordinary RSS feeds cannot be imported. Select the available content field and handle entries with no body.

title: Validate redirect destinations during remote retrieval
body: TopicRetriever checks only the initial URL against `embeddable_host`, while `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects without applying that restriction again. An allowed-host URL that redirects to another host, including a private HTTP service, causes the forum server to fetch that destination and potentially publish its HTML under the original allowed URL. Validate the scheme and destination of every redirect before issuing the next request.

title: Resolve relative URLs using standard URL semantics
body: The URL rewriting treats every leading slash as a path on the article host. A protocol-relative resource such as `//cdn.example.com/image.png` consequently becomes `http://blog.example/cdn.example.com/image.png`. Conversely, path-relative resources such as `images/image.png` are left unchanged and resolve against the forum rather than the source article. Both links and images are affected. Resolve relative references against the article URL while preserving protocol-relative hosts.

title: Defer post jobs and publication until the outer transaction commits
body: TopicEmbed.import wraps PostCreator.create in an outer transaction. PostCreator enqueues feature-topic-users and process-post jobs, and publishes the new-topic event, after its own nested transaction returns—but that does not commit this outer transaction. Workers can therefore receive IDs before the corresponding rows are visible, and a subsequent TopicEmbed creation failure can roll back rows whose jobs and events have already been emitted. Defer these side effects until the outermost transaction commits.

title: Preserve exported thread timestamps in Disqus imports
body: The previous topic creation passed the Disqus thread's `created_at`, but the replacement passes only its title. TopicEmbed.import_remote does not propagate a creation timestamp, so imported topics are now created with the current time while their comments still retain historical exported dates. This produces topics whose creation date is later than their replies and loses the original thread chronology. Pass the exported timestamp through the embed importer to PostCreator.

title: Preserve panel right alignment in the legacy box fallback
body: The new flexbox mixin emits `display: -webkit-box` and `display: -moz-box`, but those legacy box layouts do not distribute free space to `margin-left: auto` as modern flexbox does. In browsers using that fallback, such as Safari 6, removing `float: right` leaves the header panel immediately after the logo/topic information instead of against the right edge. The legacy-box path needs its own space-distribution rule to preserve the navigation layout.

title: Emit the alignment property for the Mozilla box fallback
body: Both display mixins emit Mozilla's legacy box layout (`-moz-box` or `-moz-inline-box`), but `align-items()` never emits `-moz-box-align`. Neither standard `align-items` nor the WebKit-prefixed properties control that layout. Firefox versions selecting this fallback therefore ignore the requested centering of header and small-action content and the baseline alignment of bullet badges. This is especially visible for small actions because their previous vertical padding is removed in this change. Add the matching Mozilla alignment declaration.

title: Preserve right-aligned controls in the small-action flex layout
body: The new flex layout leaves `.small-action-desc` content-sized because it has no positive flex-grow, while action buttons still rely on `float: right`. That float cannot preserve right-edge placement: it is ignored on direct flex children, and buttons inside the description can only float to the edge of its now-narrow box. Short action notices therefore pull their controls next to the notice instead of keeping them at the row's right edge. Make the description consume the remaining space and use flex-aware positioning for the controls.

title: Preserve panel positioning in the legacy flexbox fallback
body: Browsers using the newly emitted `display: -webkit-box` fallback, such as the Android 4.3 stock browser, do not distribute remaining space through auto margins in that box model. With `float: right` removed and no preceding item assigned `-webkit-box-flex: 1`, the header panel is packed immediately after the logo/topic information rather than against the right edge. The legacy fallback needs a flexible preceding item or another compatible right-alignment mechanism.

title: Include alignment for the Mozilla box fallback
body: The display mixins emit `-moz-box` and `-moz-inline-box`, but the alignment mixin omits `-moz-box-align`. Firefox versions using those legacy display values ignore all the emitted alignment properties and retain the default stretch alignment. In particular, switching bullet badges from their inline-block fallback to `-moz-inline-box` now loses the intended baseline alignment between the category marker and its text. Emit the matching Mozilla alignment property.

title: Preserve right alignment of small-action controls
body: Making `.small-action` a flex container leaves `.small-action-desc` at the default `flex: 0 1 auto`, so short descriptions no longer fill the row. The existing `button { float: right; }` consequently cannot keep controls at the row's right edge: nested buttons float within the content-width description, while direct flex-item buttons ignore the float. Controls move next to short messages instead. Give the description flex growth or replace the float with a flex-compatible auto margin.

title: Provide right alignment for the legacy box fallbacks
body: The new `flexbox()` mixin selects `display: -webkit-box` or `display: -moz-box` in browsers that only support the legacy box model, such as Safari 6. Those implementations resolve auto margins to zero rather than using them to absorb free space. With `float: right` removed and no child using `box-flex`, the header panel sits immediately beside the logo or topic information instead of at the right edge. Add an equivalent legacy alignment mechanism or retain the previous layout for those browsers.

title: Apply the website visibility restriction to website_name
body: Unlike `website`, `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`. For anonymous views of restricted TL0 users, `website` is omitted but the new field still exposes its host and, for matching domains, its path. The template also displays this value even when `website` is absent. Gate the derived field with the same restriction. The added `include_website_name` method lacks the required `?` suffix and is not a serializer inclusion hook.

title: Keep the website label synchronized after preference edits
body: `website_name` is now a plain server-provided value rather than a computed property observing `model.website`. However, `User.save()` submits website changes and only applies `bio_excerpt` from the response; it never refreshes `website_name`. Until user details are reloaded, adding a website can leave it invisible, changing one can display the old site's label with the new href, and removing one can leave the old label visible. Update the derived value when saving or retain a reactive calculation.

title: Compare hostnames case-insensitively
body: Ruby's `URI(...).host` preserves hostname case, but the equality and suffix comparisons here are case-sensitive. For an instance at `example.com`, a valid website such as `https://EXAMPLE.COM/user` therefore displays only `EXAMPLE.COM`, despite referring to the same domain. Normalize both hostnames for comparison so these URLs receive the complete path too.

title: Apply the website visibility restriction to website_name
body: Unlike `website`, `website_name` is not covered by `untrusted_attributes`, so it bypasses `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. For a TL0 user viewed anonymously, the serializer now exposes the hidden website's host and potentially its path, and the updated template displays that information even though `website` is omitted. The `include_website_name` method is also not a recognized inclusion predicate because it lacks the trailing `?`; correcting that alone would still leave the trust restriction bypassed. Apply the same visibility guard used for `website`.

title: Keep website_name synchronized when the website changes
body: The label now uses a value fetched from the server rather than a computed property dependent on `model.website`. When the loaded user model's website is edited and saved, `User.save()` only copies `bio_excerpt` from the response and never refreshes `website_name`. Consequently, the existing profile header can display the old host/path while its link points to the new website, or continue hiding the website if it was initially empty. Update the derived value after saving or retain a client-side computation that follows website changes.

title: Do not identify shared domains by removing the first DNS label
body: Comparing everything after the first label treats unrelated domains under multi-label public suffixes as the same domain. For example, an instance at `example.co.uk` and a website at `https://other.co.uk/user` both have three labels and both reduce to `co.uk`, so this branch incorrectly displays the full path for an unrelated website. Use a registrable-domain-aware comparison, or restrict matching to explicitly supported host relationships, rather than assuming the first label is always a subdomain.

title: Apply website visibility restrictions to website_name
body: website_name is not included in untrusted_attributes, so anonymous viewers receive a TL0 user's website host and same-domain path even when scope.restrict_user_fields? hides website. The updated template also displays this otherwise restricted information. include_website_name does not prevent this: it lacks the serializer hook's trailing question mark and only checks presence. Apply the same visibility restriction as website and cover website_name in the anonymous-user serializer test.

title: Keep the website label synchronized with website edits
body: The label now uses a server-loaded property instead of the computed property that observed model.website. User.save() submits the edited website but only updates bio_excerpt from the response, leaving website_name unchanged. Consequently, an already loaded profile can show the old domain while its link points to the new website; adding or clearing a website also leaves the display stale until the user is fetched again. Update website_name after saving or preserve reactive label computation.

title: Do not hide websites containing non-ASCII URL paths
body: Ruby's URI parser rejects raw non-ASCII characters anywhere in the URL. For a browser-supported website value such as http://example.com/café, this rescue sets website_host to nil, website_name returns nil, and the template hides the website entirely—even when only the host needs displaying. The previous split-based host extraction handled this value. Normalize or escape the URL for parsing rather than treating such a parsing failure as an absent website.

title: Do not treat a shared public suffix as the same domain
body: Removing the first label from equally sized hostnames incorrectly identifies unrelated domains as the same site. For example, an instance at discourse.co.uk and a website at example.co.uk both have three labels, so this comparison matches co.uk and displays the website's full path. Independent sites under github.io have the same problem. The same-domain exception should compare registrable domains or explicitly supported hostname relationships, not merely the remaining labels.

title: Preserve the light-theme color of embedded-post metadata links
body: This conversion changes the light-theme lightness from 30% to 70%, rather than preserving it. In a black/white light scheme, the small embedded-post metadata link changes from #4d4d4d to #b3b3b3, giving only about 2:1 contrast against the light background and making the navigation link difficult to read. Retain 30% for $primary in the light branch and use the complementary 70% for $secondary in the dark branch.

title: Keep notification badge text readable on the new dark background
body: The dark-theme background now uses a dark shade derived from $secondary, but both the badge foreground and its [href] foreground still use $secondary. With a black secondary color, this produces black 11px text on #4d4d4d, approximately 2.5:1 contrast, replacing the previously light background. Generic notification badges without a subclass background override become difficult to read. Adjust the dark-theme foreground, including the [href] rule, or choose a background with sufficient contrast.

title: Preserve the stronger light-theme contrast of topic-map headings
body: The light branch changes the topic-map heading lightness from 20% to 50%. These headings are only 1em and normal-weight; in a black/white light scheme their color changes from #333333 to #808080 on the near-white topic-map background, dropping contrast below 4.5:1. This introduces a light-theme readability regression while fixing dark themes. Preserve 20% for the light branch and use 80% for the dark branch, as the desktop heading rule does.

title: Preserve the original light-theme contrast of group-member names
body: The group-member name's light-theme lightness changes from 30% to 50%. On the white user-stream item background, a black primary color now produces #808080 instead of #4d4d4d, reducing normal-sized text contrast from about 8.5:1 to 4:1. The same regression occurs in mobile/user.scss at line 497. Preserve the original 30% light branch and use the complementary 70% dark branch in both files.

title: Restore the 30%/70% shades for embedded-post author links
body: The original author-link color used 30% lightness, but this replacement uses 70% for light themes and 30% for dark themes. Both branches now give these small author links the much dimmer shade: a black/white palette produces #b3b3b3 on white or #4d4d4d on black, with only about 2:1–2.5:1 contrast. Preserve 30% in the light branch and use 70% in the dark branch, as the regular post-author links do.

title: Update the badge foreground along with its dark-theme background
body: The base notification badge still sets its text color to $secondary, including the [href] variant. Changing its dark-theme background to scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%) therefore puts dark text on another dark color. With a black secondary color, the 11px count becomes black on #4d4d4d, approximately 2.5:1 contrast, whereas the previous light background kept it legible. Badges using this base background need a contrasting dark-theme foreground as well.

title: Preserve the original topic-map heading shade
body: This changes the light-theme topic-map heading from 20% lightness to 50%, rather than only adding a dark-theme alternative. These headings are normal-weight, normal-size text on a near-white topic-map background; for a #222 primary and white secondary, the new shade is approximately #919191 and has only about 3:1 contrast. Retain 20% for light themes and use the complementary 80% for dark themes, matching the desktop heading rule.

title: Keep group-member names at their original contrast level
body: The group-member name previously used 30% lightness, but the new light branch uses 50%. The same change appears in app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss at line 497. This unnecessarily reduces the contrast of normal-size member names in light themes: with a #222 primary and white secondary, it changes approximately #646464 to #919191, dropping contrast from about 5.9:1 to 3.2:1. Preserve the 30% light-theme value and use 70% for its dark-theme counterpart instead of copying the title's 50% shade.

title: Preserve the original contrast of embedded-reply links
body: The light-theme branch for `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` changes the existing lightness adjustment from 30% to 70%. For example, with a #333 primary on a white background, these small links change from #707070 to #c2c2c2, reducing contrast from about 5:1 to 1.8:1 and making them difficult to read. Preserve the original 30% light-theme value and use the corresponding secondary-based 70% value for dark themes.

title: Keep the original light-theme value for topic-map headings
body: The `.topic-map h3` conversion also changes the light-theme adjustment from 20% to 50%, rather than only adding dark-theme handling. With a #333 primary, this changes the heading from #5c5c5c to #999999 on the light topic-map background. Since these headings are only 1em, the reduced contrast makes them substantially harder to read. Retain 20% for the light branch and use 80% for the secondary-based dark branch, as the desktop topic-map heading does.

title: Avoid reducing group-member name contrast in light themes
body: The light-theme branch for `.group-member-info .name` changes the previous adjustment from 30% to 50%. On the user-stream item's white background, a #333 primary therefore produces #999999 instead of #707070, dropping normal-sized member-name text from roughly 5:1 contrast to 2.8:1. The same regression appears in `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:497`. Preserve the existing 30% light-theme value in both bundles and use the complementary secondary-based 70% adjustment for dark themes.

title: Legacy membership PATCH requests now silently change visibility
body: The resources route still sends PATCH requests to update, but the incremental membership handler has been removed. For a visible group, PATCH /admin/groups/:id with changes: {delete: "alice"} now ignores the requested removal, sets visible to false because that parameter is absent, and returns success. Existing callers can believe membership was revoked when it remains intact. Preserve the supported PATCH behavior or explicitly reject legacy payloads instead of silently applying an unrelated update.

title: Public member lists are truncated without pagination
body: This action now limits every group to 50 members, but the public group-members route calls findMembers only once and its template has no pagination or further loading. Nonautomatic groups with more than 50 members therefore lose the remainder of their public member list, whereas previously all members were returned. Add public pagination or incremental loading alongside the endpoint change.

title: Exact page-size multiples produce an extra empty page
body: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 overcounts pages whenever the member count is an exact multiple of the limit. With 50 members and a limit of 50, the controller reports two pages and enables Next on the only populated page; clicking it requests offset 50 and displays an empty list. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), retaining the zero-member handling.

title: Capture the group before opening the removal confirmation
body: The confirmation message names the current group, but its callback retrieves the controller's model again. If the administrator navigates to another group while the Bootbox dialog remains open, such as through browser Back, confirming removes the user from the newly selected group rather than the group named in the dialog. Capture the original group before opening the confirmation and invoke removeMember on that captured model.

title: Membership reloads use an unsaved editable group name
body: Both membership mutations reload through findMembers, which addresses the group by model.name. The admin name field changes that property immediately, before Save persists the rename. If an administrator edits the name and then adds or removes a member, the mutation succeeds using the group ID, but the reload requests the nonexistent new name and fails, leaving the displayed membership stale. Reload using a persisted identifier or persisted name.

title: Reset pending usernames when switching groups
body: The admin-group controller is reused across group routes, and usernames is now standalone controller state. setupController changes only the model, while addMembers also leaves usernames populated after success. Users selected or added in group A consequently remain selected after navigating to group B and are included in its next Add request, potentially granting unintended membership. Clear the selection when changing groups and after a successful addition.

title: Ignore stale member-page responses
body: Next and Previous update the offset immediately and allow another request before the first finishes, while every findMembers response unconditionally overwrites members and offset. Clicking Next twice can request offsets 50 and 100; if the offset-100 response arrives first, the later offset-50 response moves the display back to the earlier page. Serialize pagination requests or track request order so an older response cannot overwrite the latest navigation.

title: Preserve or explicitly reject PATCH membership updates
body: The resource still routes PATCH /admin/groups/:id to this action, but the previously supported changes.add and changes.delete payloads are now ignored. An existing membership-removal request returns success while leaving the user in the group, potentially retaining access that the caller intended to revoke. Because that request does not include visible, it also unexpectedly hides the group. Preserve the PATCH contract or explicitly reject incompatible requests rather than silently succeeding.

title: Provide pagination for the public member list
body: Group.findMembers now requests only 50 members and replaces the members collection with that page. This public route calls it once, and the public members template has no pagination or load-more controls. Consequently, members beyond the first 50 are unreachable in the public UI; non-automatic groups previously displayed their complete membership. Add public pagination or load the remaining pages.

title: Avoid adding an empty page for exact multiples of the page size
body: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 overcounts pages whenever the membership count is an exact multiple of the limit. For a group with 50 members and a limit of 50, the UI displays two pages and enables Next, which requests offset 50 and displays an empty member list. Use ceiling division for the page count.

title: Do not fetch membership using an unsaved group name
body: The editable name field is two-way-bound to the group's name. After an administrator changes it without saving, pagination and the refresh following addMembers or removeMember fetch membership using that unsaved name, while the membership mutation still targets the original group ID. The refresh therefore fails with a missing group or displays another group's members if the proposed name already exists. Use a persisted identifier or persisted name until the rename succeeds.

title: Prevent stale member requests from overwriting newer pages
body: Every findMembers response unconditionally replaces both offset and members, while the navigation actions allow another request before the previous one completes. Clicking Next twice can issue requests for offsets 50 and 100; if the offset-100 response arrives first, the slower offset-50 response then moves the UI back to the older page. Serialize navigation requests or ignore responses that no longer correspond to the latest request.

title: Existing membership PATCH requests now return false success
body: The resources route still accepts PATCH /admin/groups/:id, which previously supported changes.add and changes.delete. This update action ignores changes and sets visible to false when that parameter is absent. An existing membership-removal request therefore returns success while leaving the user in the group and changing unrelated visibility. Preserve the membership PATCH handler or explicitly reject these requests before saving.

title: Public group member lists are truncated without navigation
body: findMembers now requests only 50 members by default, but the public members route and template have no pagination controls or subsequent fetches. Groups with more than 50 members therefore expose only the first 50 alphabetically, with no way to view the remaining members. Add public pagination or preserve complete loading for this page.

title: Exact page-size multiples produce an extra empty page
body: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 overcounts pages whenever the member count is an exact multiple of the limit. For example, a 50-member group displays 1/2 and enables Next, which requests offset 50 and displays an empty second page. Use ceiling division for the total page count.

title: Member reloads use the unsaved group name
body: The admin name field updates this model's name immediately, while membership additions and removals operate on the persisted group ID. If an administrator edits the name and then changes membership or pages before pressing Save, findMembers requests the unsaved name and normally receives a 404. If the draft name belongs to another group, it instead displays that group's members while subsequent mutations still target the original ID. Load members using a stable persisted identifier rather than the editable name.

title: Removing the last member on a page leaves an invalid offset
body: After removing a member, findMembers reloads using the old offset and cached member count, then retains the response offset even if the total has shrunk below that page. For a 51-member group, removing the sole member at offset 50 leaves an empty member list at offset 50 even though 50 members remain. When the returned total makes the requested page invalid, move to the last populated page and fetch it.

title: Include the site fallback locale in the translation cache key
body: Fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator caches no-options I18n.t calls using only the translation key, requested locale, and backend object ID. For a key missing from a user's selected locale, two sites with different default locales can therefore receive the same cached fallback translation. Changing the default locale can likewise leave that user seeing the old fallback language. The cache must account for the fallback configuration or be appropriately partitioned and invalidated.

title: Load fallback locales for translations outside controller requests
body: This before-filter is the only added call that loads fallback translation files. The translation accelerator itself still loads only I18n.config.locale, while the backend fallback module looks up other locales without loading their files. A background job or mailer translating in one locale can therefore skip an unloaded, non-English site-default locale even when that locale contains the missing key, returning English or a missing-translation result instead. Fallback loading needs to occur in the translation path, not only during HTTP requests.

title: Fallback results are cached without the site-default locale
body: Translations now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator caches no-option I18n.t calls using only the key, current locale, and backend object ID. A missing French key resolved through German will therefore remain German after the site default changes to Spanish. The same cache collision can occur between sites sharing a multisite process. Include the fallback context in the cache key or invalidate cached translations when it changes.

title: Load fallback locales outside controller requests too
body: Fallback locales are loaded only by this controller callback. The accelerator disables automatic translation loading, and I18n.translate still loads only the current locale. A background worker translating in French on a site whose default is German will skip existing German fallback strings unless that locale happened to be loaded previously, returning English or a missing-translation message instead. Load the fallback chain through the shared translation entry point so non-controller callers receive the same fallback behavior.

title: Load fallback catalogs for non-controller translations too
body: Loading the fallback catalogs here only covers controller requests. The translation accelerator still loads only I18n.config.locale, and I18n::Backend::Fallbacks looks up each fallback directly on the backend without invoking the lazy loader. A background mail job using a user's partially translated locale can therefore skip translations present in the site's default locale if that catalog has not already been loaded. Load the fallback chain at the translation entry point rather than relying solely on ApplicationController#set_locale.

title: Account for the site fallback locale in the translation cache
body: Fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, but translate_accelerator caches no-argument translations using only the key, current locale, and backend object ID. For a user whose locale remains unchanged, a missing key resolved through the old site default can remain cached after the default locale changes, causing subsequent requests to serve the old language without evaluating this fallback list. Include the effective fallback chain in the cache key or invalidate these entries when the site default changes.

title: Include the identity type in denial-cache keys
body: The denial key includes the parsed UID but omits IdentityType. Accepted subjects anonymous:0 and render:0 therefore share an entry for the same namespace, action, name, and folder. If an anonymous dashboard read is denied, the renderer's subsequent check returns false from this cache without reaching getRendererPermissions, which grants dashboard reads unconditionally. This can break rendering for 30 seconds. Include the full subject or identity type in the key.

title: Encode denial-cache key components unambiguously
body: Joining Name and ParentFolder with an unescaped underscore allows distinct requests to share a denial entry. For the same namespace, user, and action, Name="dash_a", ParentFolder="b" and Name="dash", ParentFolder="a_b" produce identical keys. A denial for the first request consequently rejects the second for 30 seconds, even if the user's permission map explicitly grants access to dashboard "dash". Use escaping, length prefixes, or another unambiguous tuple encoding.

title: Avoid extending denials caused by a stale folder tree
body: Refreshing the permission map does not refresh the folder tree used by checkInheritedPermissions. For example, a user granted dashboard access on ancestor G can be denied a dashboard whose parent C was just created under G: the cached tree lacks C, and the fresh permission query still correctly returns only the grant on G. This line then caches that stale-tree denial for another 30 seconds. A check just before the folder-cache expiry can therefore remain denied well after the tree expires or is refreshed, whereas previously it would recover when the tree expired. Refresh the relevant hierarchy before caching an inherited denial, or avoid extending denials derived from stale hierarchy data.

title: Actually grant access in the explicit-denial cache test
body: The test says it grants dashboard access to prove that the denial cache takes precedence, but the permission value is false. Without the denial-cache shortcut, checkPermission rejects this entry and the empty fake permission store also denies access, so the test still passes. Set the permission to true so removing or bypassing the denial-cache lookup makes the test fail; asserting that the permission store is not queried would also verify the intended shortcut.

title: Include the identity type in denial-cache keys
body: The denial key uses only the parsed UserUID, so distinct subjects such as `anonymous:0` and `render:0` share an entry for the same action, resource name, and folder. If an anonymous dashboard-read check is denied, a subsequent renderer check hits that denial before reaching the renderer's unconditional read grant. This incorrectly blocks rendering for 30 seconds. Include the identity type or full typed subject in the key.

title: Encode denial-cache key components unambiguously
body: Joining the resource name and parent folder with underscores creates collisions for UIDs containing underscores. For example, `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` produce the same key for the same user and action. Denying the first request therefore also denies the second, even if its permissions allow access, because denial-cache hits bypass permission evaluation. Use an escaped, length-prefixed, or structured encoding of the components.

title: Use an actual cached grant in the denial-precedence test
body: The test says it grants dashboard access to prove that the denial entry takes precedence, but the cached scope value is `false`, which `checkPermission` treats as no grant. The fake permission store also returns no permissions, so the test still passes if the denial-cache lookup is removed entirely. Set this scope to `true` so the test detects failure to honor the denial entry.

title: Include the identity type in denial-cache keys
body: The denial key uses only the parsed UserUID, dropping IdentityType. Valid subjects anonymous:0 and render:0 therefore produce identical keys for the same namespace, action, name, and folder. If an anonymous request is denied access to a dashboard, a subsequent renderer check returns Allowed:false for 30 seconds, even though renderer permissions grant wildcard dashboard read access. Include the typed subject in the key so one identity's denial cannot block another.

title: Avoid delimiter collisions between resource and parent names
body: Joining unescaped components with underscores makes Name="a_b", ParentFolder="c" produce the same denial key as Name="a", ParentFolder="b_c" for the same namespace, user, and action. These inputs pass Check request validation. A denial for the first resource consequently denies access to the second for 30 seconds, even if the user has an explicit grant for it, because the denial cache is checked before permissions. Use an unambiguous encoding of the key components.

title: Seed a granted permission in the denial-cache precedence test
body: The "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" test seeds dashboards:uid:dash1 with false, despite intending to grant access. Without the denial-cache lookup, the cached permission check would still fail and the fake permission store would return no grants, so this test passes even if the new denial-cache fast path is removed. Set this permission to true so the test actually verifies that the denial entry takes precedence over a cached grant.

title: Restore per-rule pause and delete actions in the new list
body: Grafana list rows now pass only promRule to RuleActionsButtons, but AlertRuleMenu still renders pause/unpause only when rulerRule is a Grafana rule and Delete only when rulerRule exists. Consequently, both actions disappear from every Grafana row in the grouped and filtered lists, even when the newly calculated permissions allow them. Adapt these actions to use the rule identifier/Prometheus DTO or load the definition on demand.

title: Make Silence notifications work for Prometheus-only rows
body: The new Grafana list rows have promRule but no ruler rule. Their menu can now display Silence notifications using Prometheus abilities, but clicking it only sets showSilenceDrawer; this condition still requires rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule), which is false when rule is undefined. The visible action therefore does nothing. Fetch the definition when invoked or adapt the drawer to accept the identifier/Prometheus rule.

title: Return neutral abilities when skipToken is supplied
body: skipToken is converted to undefined, but useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) treats Duplicate as supported and allows it whenever the user has Grafana rule-create permission. AlertRuleMenu supplies skipToken for non-Grafana rules and ORs this result with the ruler abilities. A user who can create Grafana rules is therefore offered Duplicate on external rules even when external-write permission is denied or the external ruler is unavailable. Skipped input must not contribute an affirmative ability.

title: Preserve federated-group immutability for CombinedRule consumers
body: Delegating useAllAlertRuleAbilities to useAllRulerRuleAbilities drops the previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check, and the delegated implementation hardcodes isFederated to false. For Mimir groups with source_tenants and an enabled ruler, existing CombinedRule consumers now report Update/Delete as supported for users with external-write permission, whereas these federated groups were previously explicitly immutable. Preserve the group-level restriction when adapting the CombinedRule hook.

title: Keep export available for Grafana-managed recording rules
body: ModifyExport support is now based on isAlertingRule, which is false for GrafanaPromRecordingRuleDTO. Both Grafana list paths now supply only the Prometheus DTO, so there is no ruler-based ability to enable the Export menu as a fallback. Grafana-managed recording rules therefore lose their previously available export action even for users with read permission. Export support should recognize both Grafana alerting and recording rules.

title: Preserve the return location in rule-view links
body: The previous Grafana list item included createReturnTo() in this link, but the replacement omits the returnTo parameter entirely. Opening a rule from a filtered list no longer passes the current list URL to the viewer's return navigation, so returning to the list loses the user's filters/view state. Keep the current return location when constructing the new link.

title: Preserve Pause and Delete for Prometheus-only list rows
body: Every Grafana row in the new list now passes only promRule to RuleActionsButtons, but AlertRuleMenu still requires a Grafana rulerRule to render Pause and a defined rulerRule to render Delete. Consequently, both actions disappear from the grouped and filtered lists even for authorized users. The new Prometheus ability checks do not remove these rendering guards. Adapt the actions to use the identifier or load the ruler configuration on demand.

title: Open the silence drawer for Prometheus-only rules
body: The new Prometheus ability checks expose Silence notifications for Grafana list rows, but clicking it only sets showSilenceDrawer. The drawer still mounts only when rule is a Grafana alerting ruler DTO, whereas the new list supplies no rule at all. Thus clicking Silence notifications in the new list does nothing. Load the ruler rule when opening the drawer or support opening it from the Prometheus rule and identifier.

title: Return disabled abilities when skipToken is supplied
body: skipToken is converted to undefined, but useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities still marks Duplicate supported and allows it whenever the user has Grafana rule-create permission. AlertRuleMenu invokes this hook with skipToken for data-source rules and ORs its result with the ruler abilities. A user who can create Grafana rules therefore sees Duplicate for Mimir/Loki rules even without external-rule write permission or ruler support. Return unsupported/disallowed abilities for skipped rules instead of allowing the Grafana fallback to override data-source restrictions.

title: Retain the federation check for combined-rule consumers
body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously checked isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group), but now delegates to this implementation, which hardcodes isFederated to false. The delegation discards source_tenants, and useIsRuleEditable receives only the source and rule DTO, so it cannot restore that group-level restriction. Existing combined-rule consumers now offer Update and Delete for federated Mimir groups that were previously treated as immutable. Preserve the federation information when delegating.

title: Keep management abilities available for Grafana recording rules
body: isAlertingRule is false for Grafana-managed recording rules, but it now gates ModifyExport, Pause, Restore, and DeletePermanently. The ruler-based implementation supported these actions for both Grafana alerting and recording rules. Since the new list has no ruler DTO to provide fallback abilities, recording rules immediately lose their Export menu despite sufficient read permission. Use the broader Grafana-rule check for management actions and reserve the alerting-only check for Silence.

title: Preserve the originating list URL in rule-view links
body: The replacement link drops the returnTo parameter that GrafanaRuleLoader previously populated with createReturnTo(). Opening a rule from a filtered list therefore no longer supplies the originating URL to the viewer's return navigation, causing it to fall back to the default list rather than preserving the filters. Include the returnTo parameter in this link as before.

title: Silence does nothing for Prometheus-only Grafana rows
body: Grafana list rows now pass only promRule, leaving rule undefined. The menu exposes Silence notifications using the new Prometheus abilities, but clicking it only sets showSilenceDrawer; this condition still requires a Grafana ruler rule before rendering the drawer. Consequently, the advertised action does nothing in the new list. Fetch the required ruler rule on demand or adapt the drawer to accept the Prometheus rule.

title: Pause and Delete remain gated on the removed ruler data
body: The new Grafana list supplies promRule without rulerRule. Although this component now calculates Pause and Delete permissions from promRule, the Pause item still requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule), and the Delete item still requires rulerRule. Both actions therefore disappear from every Grafana row in the new list, including for users with update/delete permissions. The rendering and handlers need a Prometheus-only path or an on-demand ruler fetch.

title: Return neutral abilities when skipToken is supplied
body: skipToken is converted to undefined, but useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still returns Duplicate as supported and checks the user's Grafana rule-create permission. AlertRuleMenu passes skipToken for non-Grafana rules and ORs this result with the source-specific ruler ability. A user with Grafana create permission but no write permission on an external rule source therefore gets a Duplicate action for that external rule. Skipped abilities must return false/false rather than granting Grafana abilities to unrelated rules.

title: Preserve the federated-group immutability check
body: Delegating CombinedRule abilities to useAllRulerRuleAbilities drops the previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check. The delegated implementation hardcodes isFederated to false, so existing useAlertRuleAbility consumers now advertise Update and Delete for Mimir groups containing source_tenants whenever the user has write permission. These groups were deliberately treated as immutable because federated-rule editing is unsupported. Preserve the group’s federation status when delegating.

title: Keep export available for Grafana recording rules
body: ModifyExport now requires a Grafana alerting rule, whereas the previous ruler-based ability supported both Grafana alerting and recording rules. GrafanaRuleListItem now supplies only promRule, so recording rules have no ruler-based export fallback and lose the Export menu even for users with read permission. Use the Grafana-managed rule check for export rather than the alerting-only check.

title: Preserve the return destination on rule-view links
body: The previous list item included createReturnTo() in the rule-view URL, but this replacement drops the returnTo parameter. Opening a rule from a filtered list therefore no longer gives the viewer’s return link the original list URL and search parameters, losing the user's filtering context when returning. Retain the returnTo parameter while changing the row's data source.

title: Avoid interpolating expanded targets again in subrequests
body: This expands template variables before splitting, but the subrequests still go through datasource.runQuery and the normal backend-query path, which calls applyTemplateVariables again with the same scoped variables. Shard requests are additionally expanded at their entry point. Template replacement is not idempotent: for a query containing `|= "$pattern"`, a pattern value of `error $code` is expanded again if `code` is another dashboard variable, changing the literal filter and therefore the results. Ordinary split queries previously interpolated only in the execution path. Ensure expanded subrequests bypass subsequent interpolation; the new tests mock runQuery and therefore miss this regression.

title: Avoid interpolating expanded targets again during execution
body: These expanded targets are still passed to `datasource.runQuery()`, whose backend-query preparation applies template variables again. Sharded queries also arrive here already expanded by `runShardSplitQuery()`. Template replacement is not idempotent: if a single-valued variable `label` contains the literal value `$region`, `{label="$label"}` first becomes `{label="$region"}` and the next pass replaces that literal with the dashboard's `region` value. Enabling splitting can therefore change label or filter values and return incorrect results. The execution path needs to avoid re-interpolating targets expanded here; the new tests mock `runQuery()` and do not exercise that path.

title: Filter empty expressions after interpolation
body: The previous implementation filtered empty expressions after interpolation, but this implementation filters only the original expressions. A target whose entire expression is a variable resolving to an empty string now remains in `splittingTargets`. When such a target is placed in the non-sharded group alongside a valid sharded query, that group reaches `runSplitQuery()`, which removes its blank target and constructs no requests. `runSplitGroupedQueries()` then dereferences `[0].partition` on the empty request list and throws, preventing the valid queries from completing. Retain the post-interpolation empty-expression filter.

title: Avoid interpolating prepared targets again during execution
body: This adds a template-interpolation pass, but the subrequests still go through datasource.runQuery and the normal backend datasource query path, which applies template variables again. Shard requests also arrive here already interpolated by runShardSplitQuery. Substitution is not idempotent: if dashboard variable needle has the literal value "$host" and host is another variable, `{app="x"} |= "$needle"` now replaces the intended literal "$host" with the host variable's value on the next pass, silently querying different data. Ensure targets are interpolated only once. The added test mocks runQuery, so it does not exercise the subsequent interpolation.

title: Filter empty expressions after interpolation
body: Previously, query.expr was filtered after interpolation; now only the original expression is checked. A full-expression variable such as "$SELECTOR" that expands to an empty string therefore remains in the shard targets. When combined with a valid sharded query, the blank target can form a separate group whose call to runSplitQuery filters out every target. runSplitGroupedQueries then dereferences the first element of an empty requests array and throws, preventing the valid query from completing. Keep the empty-expression filter after applyTemplateVariables so interpolated blank queries are skipped as before.

title: Preserve recorded logs when deriving a contextual test logger
body: FromContext returns a fresh TestLogger with independent recording state. LoggerMiddleware now emits completion logs through logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so injecting a TestLogger records every completion on a temporary object that is immediately discarded, leaving the injected logger's InfoLogs empty. Previously these logs were recorded on the injected instance. Return the existing fake or share its recording state with the contextual child so logging assertions remain meaningful.

title: Preserve captured logs when deriving a contextual TestLogger
body: FromContext returns a fresh TestLogger with independent log records. LoggerMiddleware now calls logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) for every completion message, so passing a TestLogger to that middleware leaves the injected fake's InfoLogs empty; the completion record exists only on a temporary logger that is immediately discarded. This prevents tests from observing the updated request-logging path. Return the existing fake or make contextual children share its recorded logs.

title: Preserve recorded calls when deriving a contextual test logger
body: LoggerMiddleware now writes request-completion logs through logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...). This implementation returns a fresh TestLogger whose records are inaccessible to the caller, so the supplied fake's InfoLogs remains empty even when a request is logged. Tests using that fake can no longer observe or assert request logging. Return the existing fake or make the contextual child share its recording storage.

title: Cache only successfully admitted devices
body: tagDeviceUI adds the device to localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the store rejects a new device with ErrDeviceLimitReached, this return propagates the error but leaves the cache entry in place for 29 minutes. The next request with the same device ID hits the cache, returns nil, and receives an anonymous identity despite the limit still being reached. Only cache successful admissions, and ensure concurrent requests cannot treat an admission still in progress as successful.

title: Requests without a device header bypass the limit
body: Authenticate relies entirely on TagDevice returning ErrDeviceLimitReached to deny access, but TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. Consequently, even when the configured limit is full, a client can omit this client-controlled header and continue accessing anonymous APIs without being counted or rejected. Device admission must not be optional merely because the request omits its identifier.

title: Make the device count check and admission atomic
body: CountDevices runs in a separate database session from the subsequent unconditional upsert, with no serialization between them. For example, with a limit of one and an empty table, two concurrent requests for different devices can both observe zero devices and then both insert successfully. This also occurs across Grafana instances sharing the database. The count check and admission need database-level serialization or another atomic mechanism to prevent exceeding the configured cap.

title: Register the setting before environment overrides are applied
body: The PR reads device_limit here but does not add it to conf/defaults.ini. Grafana applies environment overrides to keys already present in the loaded INI before readAuthSettings runs, so creating this key here is too late. On an otherwise default configuration, GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT is silently ignored and the limit remains zero, meaning unlimited devices. Add the default INI key or read this setting through an environment-aware lookup.

title: Cache devices only after successful admission
body: tagDeviceUI adds the device ID to the 29-minute cache before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, and leaves it cached when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Consequently, a new device's first request is rejected, but its next request hits the cache, returns nil, and authenticates successfully without being counted. Only cache successful admissions, so rejected devices cannot bypass the limit by retrying.

title: The optional device header allows clients to bypass the limit
body: Authenticate relies on TagDevice to enforce the limit, but TagDevice immediately returns nil when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. Even when the configured limit is exhausted, an API client can omit this client-controlled header and receive an anonymous identity without any quota check. Enforcement needs an identifier clients cannot simply omit to opt out, such as a server-issued device cookie.

title: Make the quota check and device insertion atomic
body: CountDevices runs separately from the subsequent upsert, with no transaction or synchronization covering the admission decision. Concurrent requests for different new devices can all observe a count below deviceLimit and then all insert successfully, exceeding the configured limit. This also occurs across Grafana instances sharing the database. Serialize or atomically perform the quota check and insertion across database writers.

title: Register the new setting for environment overrides
body: The new device_limit key is not added to conf/defaults.ini. Grafana's environment-override pass visits keys already present in the loaded INI, while this read creates the missing key afterward. Setting GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone therefore leaves AnonymousDeviceLimit at zero and silently disables the limit unless device_limit is also declared in a configuration file. Add the key to the defaults or read it through an environment-aware configuration section.

title: Only cache devices after successful admission
body: tagDeviceUI adds the device to localCache before CreateOrUpdateDevice checks the limit. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, that cache entry remains. The next request with the same device ID returns nil from the cache lookup, so Anonymous.Authenticate grants access without checking the limit again. Every rejected device can therefore bypass the limit by retrying, for the 29-minute cache lifetime. Cache only successful admissions, and do not treat an in-flight admission as successful.

title: Requests without a device header bypass the limit
body: The authentication gate relies entirely on TagDevice, but TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. An anonymous client can omit this client-controlled header and continue accessing Grafana APIs even when the configured device limit has been reached; no count or admission check runs. Requests subject to the limit need a server-established device identifier or another admission path rather than treating missing tracking information as successful admission.

title: Make counting and admitting a device atomic
body: CountDevices and the subsequent upsert execute in separate database sessions without serialization. Two requests for different new device IDs can both observe a count below deviceLimit and then both insert successfully. For example, with a limit of one and an empty table, concurrent requests can admit multiple devices, which remain eligible for updates afterward. Admission must atomically enforce the count across concurrent requests and Grafana instances.

title: Register device_limit in the default configuration
body: This PR reads device_limit but does not add that key to conf/defaults.ini. Grafana's environment override pass visits keys already present in the loaded INI configuration, before readAuthSettings runs. Consequently, setting GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone in a normal deployment is ignored, and this getter reads zero, silently disabling the limit. Add the key to the default configuration or read it through an environment-aware accessor.

title: Preserve the numeric type of anonymousDeviceLimit
body: The initializer infers this class property as undefined, not number | undefined. The exported runtime config therefore declares that anonymousDeviceLimit can never contain the number supplied by the backend, despite GrafanaConfig declaring that numeric contract. Consumers that narrow the property before using number methods get a never type and cannot type-check. Explicitly annotate the property as number | undefined.

title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors
body: The new fetch and delete tracing calls unconditionally use Error, even when no error occurred or no rows need cleaning. The same happens in count-based cleanup and orphaned-tag cleanup, so healthy cleanup runs now generate error-level records, potentially triggering false alerts and dumping large ID lists into normal production logs. These traces should use Debug; Error should be reserved for actual failures.

title: Large cleanup batches exceed PostgreSQL's parameter limit
body: The new DELETE binds one parameter per selected ID, but only SQLite receives parameter-limit handling. PostgreSQL accepts at most 65,535 bind parameters, so a sufficiently large backlog with cleanupjob_batchsize above that limit makes every delete fail and prevents retention cleanup from progressing. The previous subquery-based DELETE did not have this restriction. Cap or split the deletion batches according to the database's parameter limit.

title: SQLite ID-list construction performs quadratic copying
body: Each iteration formats the entire accumulated ID string into a new string, making SQL construction quadratic in the number of IDs. A batch containing tens of thousands of IDs, explicitly supported by the new test, creates gigabytes of transient allocations just to construct a DELETE statement.
