This adds substantial CPU and GC overhead to cleanup. Build the list with a strings.Builder or an append-based byte buffer instead.

title: The shortened ticker increases load from every cleanup job
body: Changing the shared ticker from ten minutes to one minute also runs snapshot, dashboard-version, image, invitation, short-URL, and query-history cleanup ten times as often. Each pass still has a nine-minute timeout; if a pass takes longer than one minute, a buffered tick causes the next pass to start immediately, potentially keeping these database maintenance jobs running continuously. Preserve the existing shared interval rather than changing all cleanup jobs as part of the annotation SQL fix.

title: Respect parameter limits on PostgreSQL and MySQL
body: The non-SQLite path creates one bound parameter per ID without capping the batch. PostgreSQL and prepared MySQL statements support at most 65,535 parameters, so a cleanup batch configured above that limit fails whenever enough eligible rows exist. The previous subquery-based DELETE did not have this restriction. Cleanup then returns without deleting the batch and fails again on subsequent runs, preventing retention cleanup from progressing. Cap or subdivide DELETE batches according to the database's parameter limit.

title: Build the SQLite ID list without repeatedly copying it
body: Each fmt.Sprintf copies the entire accumulated ID list into a new string, making construction allocate O(n²) bytes. A roughly 32,000-ID batch produces several gigabytes of transient allocations for a final SQL list of only a few hundred kilobytes. This specifically penalizes the large batches the SQLite fallback is intended to support, adding substantial CPU and garbage-collection work to cleanup. Use a strings.Builder or byte buffer to construct the list linearly.

title: Do not report successful cleanup batches as errors
body: The new annotation and tag cleanup paths call log.Error unconditionally after successful queries and deletes. This includes empty batches with no eligible rows and a nil error, so healthy scheduled cleanup now emits error-level messages on every run, often with an entire batch of IDs. This creates false failure signals for operators and error-based monitoring while adding unnecessary log volume. Remove these diagnostics or log them at Debug, reserving Error for actual failures.

title: Preserve the cadence of the global cleanup scheduler
body: This ticker controls all eight cleanup jobs, not just annotation cleanup. Changing it from ten minutes to one minute schedules database and filesystem cleanup ten times as often. The existing cleanup timeout remains nine minutes, so runs lasting longer than one minute can also leave a tick pending and restart immediately, making cleanup effectively continuous. This introduces a broad background-load regression unrelated to splitting the annotation SQL statements; retain the existing interval or schedule annotations separately if a faster cadence is required.

title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors
body: The new logging in CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags uses Error unconditionally, including when fetching and deleting succeed and when the final batch is empty. Normal cleanup therefore produces error-level messages even when nothing is wrong, triggering false failure alerts and logging entire ID batches at normal production verbosity. These messages should be removed or logged at debug level, reserving Error for actual failures.

title: The shorter ticker increases load for every cleanup job
body: Changing the ticker from ten minutes to one minute accelerates all cleanup jobs, including dashboard-version deletion, snapshot deletion, filesystem cleanup, and query-history maintenance—not just annotations. This can run their database queries and filesystem scans up to ten times as often. Since a cleanup pass may run for nine minutes, passes lasting over one minute will also have a tick queued and can restart immediately, keeping maintenance continuously active. Preserve the existing cadence or isolate any intended annotation scheduling change.

title: SQLite ID-list construction has quadratic allocation cost
body: In deleteByIDs, each iteration formats the entire accumulated SQLite ID list into a new string. Building a batch of n IDs therefore copies and allocates O(n²) bytes. At the newly tested batch size of 32,767, this entails several gigabytes of cumulative copying and allocation to produce a DELETE statement only a few hundred kilobytes long, adding substantial CPU and garbage-collection overhead to cleanup. Build the list with a strings.Builder or an append-based buffer instead.

title: Parameterized deletes exceed PostgreSQL's bind-parameter limit
body: deleteByIDs now creates one bind parameter per selected ID on PostgreSQL, which supports at most 65,535 parameters in a statement. With a configured AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize above that limit and enough eligible rows, the DELETE fails and cleanup repeatedly aborts without removing that batch. The previous subquery-based DELETE did not impose this parameter limit. Bound each DELETE to the dialect's parameter limit or split the selected IDs into smaller deletes.

title: Detach asynchronous writes from request cancellation
body: All four asynchronous write paths derive their timeout context from the incoming request context. HTTP request contexts are canceled when the handler returns, and WithTimeoutCause does not remove that parent cancellation. Consequently, a successful unified-storage write can be followed by a canceled legacy write as soon as the response is sent, rather than receiving the intended ten-second window. Preserve request values while detaching cancellation, for example with context.WithoutCancel, before applying the background-write timeout.

title: Preserve mutation order in asynchronous legacy writes
body: Each successful mutation launches an independent goroutine, so legacy writes can execute out of order even for sequential client requests. For example, a client can successfully create an object and then delete it while the legacy create is delayed. The legacy delete can see NotFound before the create finishes, leaving the deleted object present in legacy storage indefinitely. The timeout does not prevent this. Mirror operations need ordering per object, or another mechanism that preserves unified-storage commit order.

title: Mirror the committed update instead of replaying UpdatedObjectInfo
body: UpdatedObjectInfo can calculate a patch from the existing object. Passing the original callback to Legacy.Update evaluates that patch against legacy state rather than copying the result committed by Storage.Update. If legacy is behind after a failed mirror write, a patch changing only the title can retain stale interval or item values in legacy even though unified storage contains the correct values. The removed updateWrapper previously supplied the committed result to legacy. Restore that behavior so the mirror receives the accepted object rather than independently replaying the client update.

title: Do not use object names as duration-metric label values
body: The successful delete path passes name to recordStorageDuration where the other paths pass options.Kind. This produces a distinct metric label value for every deleted object rather than a bounded value per kind, and successful and failed deletes use different labeling conventions. Prometheus retains those series, so continued creation and deletion of uniquely named objects causes growing metric cardinality and memory/scrape costs. Pass the kind consistently.

title: Attribute duration and error metrics to the backend actually called
body: The Storage.Create error branch records a legacy duration even though legacy was never called; Storage.Update has the same error at line 129. Conversely, the asynchronous Legacy.DeleteCollection call records a storage duration at line 166. Unified create/update failures therefore disappear from unified-storage error metrics, while legacy collection deletes add extra unified-storage samples and never appear in legacy metrics. Use recordStorageDuration for primary calls and recordLegacyDuration for mirror calls.

title: Use independent backend mocks and assert asynchronous calls
body: The new tests give legacy and unified storage the same mock.Mock, so an expectation configured for either backend satisfies calls to both. For example, the create failure case configures only setupLegacyFn, yet that expectation also supplies the unified-storage failure. The tests also neither wait for nor assert the asynchronous mirror calls. They can therefore pass when reads use the wrong backend or legacy writes are omitted entirely. Use separate mocks, explicit call expectations, and synchronization to verify the asynchronous writes before each test finishes.

title: Detach background writes from request cancellation
body: All four background writes derive their timeout context from the original request context. WithTimeoutCause preserves parent cancellation, and an HTTP request's context is canceled when its handler returns. Consequently, returning after the unified-storage write can immediately cancel the legacy write, even though its ten-second timeout has not elapsed. This makes successful requests routinely leave legacy storage unsynchronized. Preserve the request's context values while detaching cancellation, then apply the background timeout.

title: Replicate the committed update instead of replaying objInfo
body: The legacy update now receives the original UpdatedObjectInfo instead of a wrapper containing the object committed to unified storage. For PATCH and server-side apply, UpdatedObjectInfo computes the update from the old object supplied by the store. Legacy storage can have a different or stale old object, so replaying the update can preserve stale fields or produce a different result from the successful unified update. Restore replication of the committed result rather than independently evaluating the request against legacy state.

title: Preserve operation ordering in asynchronous legacy writes
body: Each write launches an independent goroutine, with no ordering between operations on the same resource. Even a client that waits for a create response before deleting can have the legacy delete run before the pending legacy create. The delete then returns NotFound, its error is ignored, and the late create leaves a legacy object that no longer exists in unified storage. Sequential updates can likewise overwrite newer legacy state with older state. Background replication needs per-resource ordering or an equivalent version-aware mechanism.

title: Attribute duration metrics to the backend that performed the operation
body: The unified-storage Create failure is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, although no legacy operation ran. Update has the same mistake at line 129. Conversely, the background legacy DeleteCollection call records recordStorageDuration at line 166. These observations hide unified create/update failures, falsely report legacy failures, and mix legacy collection-delete latency and errors into unified-storage metrics. Use the corresponding backend's recorder at each call site.

title: Do not use resource names as the kind metric label
body: The successful Delete observation passes name in the argument used for options.Kind everywhere else, including this method's error path. Every deleted resource name therefore creates a distinct duration-metric label value instead of sharing the resource-kind value. Normal resource churn can create unbounded Prometheus series and memory usage, while successful and failed deletions cannot be aggregated under the same kind. Pass options.Kind here.

title: Independently verify completion of legacy writes
body: The new tests give legacy and unified storage the same mock, whose expectations use identical method names. A legacy expectation can therefore satisfy a unified call; the Create error case actually configures only setupLegacyFn yet exercises the unified failure path. The tests also neither await background writes nor assert their call counts, so deleting every legacy-write goroutine would still pass these unit tests. Use separate mocks and synchronize assertions on legacy completion to verify the central mode-3 replication behavior.

title: Detach background writes from request cancellation
body: All four asynchronous legacy writes derive their timeout context from the original request context. That context is canceled when the HTTP handler completes, and WithTimeoutCause does not remove the parent's cancellation or deadline. Because these methods return immediately, legacy writes can be canceled before they start or finish despite the successful unified-storage response. Preserve the request context's values but detach its cancellation before applying the background timeout.

title: Mirror the committed update instead of replaying UpdatedObjectInfo
body: Legacy.Update now receives the original UpdatedObjectInfo rather than a wrapper around the object successfully committed to unified storage. For PATCH operations, UpdatedObjectInfo computes the new object from the backend's existing object. Since asynchronous legacy storage can lag or have missed an earlier write, replaying the patch can produce different content—for example, a title-only patch can preserve an obsolete interval in legacy. Pass the committed result through an appropriate update wrapper so the backup receives the same resource state.

title: Preserve write ordering when mirroring to legacy storage
body: Each successful write starts an independent goroutine, with no ordering between legacy operations on the same resource. A client can successfully create a resource and then delete it, but the legacy delete can execute before the legacy create; the ignored NotFound error is then followed by creation of a record that no longer exists in unified storage. Successive updates can similarly overwrite newer legacy state with older state. Use ordered replication or per-resource serialization rather than unrelated goroutines.

title: Attribute duration and error samples to the correct backend
body: The unified-storage failure branches in Create and Update call recordLegacyDuration, even though no legacy operation ran. Conversely, the asynchronous legacy DeleteCollection calls recordStorageDuration at line 166. This attributes unified failures to legacy and legacy collection-delete failures to unified storage, making the backend latency/error metrics misleading. Record each sample against the backend that performed the operation.

title: Do not use resource names as the duration metric's kind label
body: The successful unified Delete records its duration using name where the other calls pass options.Kind. This creates a distinct metric label value for every deleted resource name instead of grouping samples by kind. As deletion volume grows, retained metric series and scrape overhead can grow without bound, while successful and failed deletes are also grouped inconsistently. Pass the kind rather than the resource name.

title: Distinguish the two backends and verify asynchronous mirroring
body: The legacy and unified mocks share the same mock.Mock and use identical method expectation names, so an expectation configured for one backend can satisfy a call to the other. For example, the Create unified-failure case configures only setupLegacyFn but still exercises the unified failure path through that shared expectation. The write tests also neither await nor assert the background legacy calls, so removing legacy mirroring entirely would leave them passing. Use independent backend mocks and explicitly await and verify successful mirroring and the absence of legacy writes after unified failures.

title: Recheck the cache after acquiring the write lock
body: Concurrent non-development calls can all observe a nil cache before the first caller acquires this lock. After that caller initializes the cache, every queued caller still reopens and parses assets-manifest.json because the cache is not checked again under the write lock. These redundant loads now run serially and also block cache-hit readers behind pending writers, creating an avoidable cold-start bottleneck. After acquiring the write lock, check entryPointAssetsCache again when not in development mode and return it if another caller has populated it.

title: Recheck the cache after acquiring the write lock
body: Concurrent non-development calls to GetWebAssets can all observe a nil cache before the first caller acquires the write lock. Although the first caller then populates the cache, every queued caller still reloads and decodes the manifest while holding the exclusive lock. This serializes redundant initialization work and blocks other cache readers, increasing cold-start request latency with the number of concurrent cache misses. After acquiring the write lock, recheck entryPointAssetsCache and return it when populated, while preserving the reload behavior in development mode.

title: Recheck the cache after acquiring the write lock
body: Multiple production requests can read a nil cache before the first request acquires the write lock. Each of those requests then unconditionally reopens and decodes assets-manifest.json, even after the first request has populated the cache. Because these loads now run under an exclusive lock, concurrent cache misses cause serialized manifest loads and unnecessary request delays. After acquiring the write lock, recheck entryPointAssetsCache and return it when non-nil and cfg.Env is not setting.Dev.

title: Prevent concurrent builds for the same namespaced key
body: Holding cacheMu only for publication allows GetIndex to return nil while another build for that key is in progress. getOrCreateIndex has no per-key synchronization, so a search request and the write-event consumer can build separate indexes for the same namespace/resource. The consumer can publish and update one index, then a slower build can overwrite the cache with an older snapshot, losing that update from subsequent searches. Disk-backed builds can also concurrently call bleve.New for the same directory. Add per-key synchronization or singleflight while retaining parallel builds for different keys.

title: Protect TotalDocs from concurrent cache insertion
body: This new TotalDocs call runs after the search write-event goroutine has started. The Bleve implementation of TotalDocs iterates b.cache without taking cacheMu.RLock. A write event for a namespace omitted from initial indexing can concurrently call BuildIndex and insert into that map, causing a data race and potentially a fatal concurrent-map-iteration/write error during startup. Synchronize TotalDocs with cache writes, or obtain the count before starting the consumer.

title: Handle closed event channels before eagerly starting consumers
body: Eager Init now starts the search event consumer during construction, even when no storage RPC is ever made. With the SQL backend also supplied as Lifecycle, server.Stop calls backend.Stop, and the SQL poller closes its event stream. The consumer in search.init receives from that channel without checking whether it is closed and calls handleEvent with nil, which dereferences evt.Type and panics. Thus constructing and stopping a search-enabled server without making any RPC now exercises a crashing lifecycle that previously started no consumer. Make the event loop exit on channel closure or cancellation.

title: Retain stopped-state rejection in request handlers
body: Removing Init from the request handlers also removes their stopped-state check. Stop records "service is stopping" or "service is stopped" in initErr, which the old handler calls to Init returned to callers. Eager constructor initialization does not replace that check after shutdown begins. For example, SQL backend.Stop only stops polling and leaves the database usable, so authenticated Create/Update/Delete calls can still commit after the resource server is stopped, without functioning watch/index maintenance. Retain a lifecycle-state guard independently of initialization.

title: Serialize index builds for the same key
body: Restricting cacheMu to the final assignment allows multiple builds for the same namespace/resource to run concurrently. For an index skipped at startup, a search can begin building it while a watch event sees the cache miss and starts another build. The second index can receive subsequent watch updates before the slower first build replaces it in the cache with an older snapshot, losing updates or resurrecting deleted search results. Keep per-key build synchronization while allowing different keys to build concurrently.

title: Synchronize TotalDocs with cache writes
body: The event-handling goroutine starts before this new TotalDocs call. An event for an uncached namespace/resource can therefore invoke BuildIndex and modify bleveBackend.cache while TotalDocs iterates that map without acquiring cacheMu. This can terminate the process with a concurrent map iteration/write error during startup, even though the initial build errgroup has finished. TotalDocs needs to acquire the cache read lock or iterate a snapshot taken under that lock.

title: Make watch consumers handle channel closure before eager initialization
body: Eager initialization makes constructing and stopping an otherwise unused search-enabled SQL server start and then stop its watch pollers. When the SQL backend's Stop cancels the poller, the poller closes its event channel. searchSupport.init receives with `v := <-events` without checking whether the channel is closed, then passes nil to handleEvent, which dereferences evt.Type and panics. The server watch consumer has the same unchecked receive. Previously an unused server had not started these loops. Make both consumers exit on channel closure so the new construct-then-stop path does not crash the process.

title: Retain stopped-state checks in request handlers
body: Removing the per-request Init calls also removes the handlers' stopping/stopped checks: server.Stop sets initErr to those errors, which Init previously returned to callers. Create, Update, and Delete now reach the backend even after Stop. The SQL backend's Stop only cancels polling and leaves the database open, so these requests can commit successfully after watch/index propagation has ended. Preserve a separate running-state guard even though initialization is now eager.

title: Deduplicate concurrent builds for the same index key
body: Protecting only the final cache assignment allows GetIndex to return a cache miss throughout an in-progress build. Two first searches for the same NamespacedResource can therefore build separate indexes and unconditionally overwrite each other in the cache. If one finishes and receives a watch update before the other publishes its older snapshot, that update is lost from subsequent searches. Keep the cache-miss/build path single-flight per key while allowing different keys to build concurrently.

title: Synchronize TotalDocs with background cache writes
body: This new log evaluates TotalDocs after starting the write-event consumer. Bleve's TotalDocs iterates its cache map without acquiring cacheMu, while the consumer can build an index for a previously uncached namespace and insert it into that map. With writes arriving during startup, counting documents can therefore race with cache insertion and crash the process with concurrent map iteration and map write. Protect cache enumeration with the read lock, or obtain the count before starting the consumer.

title: Preserve the stopped-state check when removing lazy initialization
body: The removed per-request Init calls also checked initErr, which Stop sets to reject requests while stopping or stopped. Eager initialization does not replace that lifecycle guard. The SQL backend's Stop only cancels its pollers and leaves the database usable, so Create, Update, and Delete now continue accepting writes after Stop even though watch delivery has stopped; IsHealthy can also continue reporting SERVING. Retain a separate lifecycle-state check on requests.

title: Unwind initialized resources when constructor initialization fails
body: The constructor now returns nil on an Init failure without cancelling or stopping work that Init already started. For example, search initialization can successfully start its SQL event poller, then initWatcher can fail on the second WatchWriteEvents database query. The caller receives no server handle with which to call Stop, leaving the first poller and initialized lifecycle resources running. Unwind successfully initialized components on this error path, including the search watcher that uses a detached background context.

title: Call the passkeys helper with its required argument
body: UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without arguments, but UsernamePasswordForm defines only isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), and there is no zero-argument overload in the hierarchy. This causes a compilation error and prevents the services module from building. Pass the context user or provide the intended overload.

title: Preserve passkey initialization when no user is selected
body: The new helper returns false when the user is null, which is the normal state on a fresh login. Both authenticate() and the error challenge path now use this helper to decide whether to call fillContextForm(), so ordinary logins no longer receive the conditional WebAuthn attributes or a stored challenge. This disables existing discoverable-key and explicit passkey login flows, including the initial login required by the new reauthentication tests. Initialization must remain enabled for unidentified users while also supporting reauthentication.

title: Pass the required argument to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled
body: UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without arguments, but the helper defined in UsernamePasswordForm requires a UserModel and has no zero-argument overload. This causes the services module to fail compilation, preventing the build and tests from running. Supply the context user or introduce a matching overload.

title: Preserve passkey support when no user has been identified
body: Requiring user != null disables passkeys during normal login, where context.getUser() is intentionally null until a credential identifies the user. Both authenticate() and the error challenge now skip webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(), so the initial login page receives neither the conditional-UI configuration nor the WebAuthn challenge. This regresses existing passkey logins and prevents passkey-only users from signing in after logout. The helper must allow unidentified-user authentication as well as selected-user reauthentication.

title: Pass the user to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled
body: This calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` without arguments, but the helper added to `UsernamePasswordForm` requires a `UserModel` argument. No matching zero-argument method exists, so `UsernameForm` does not compile and the services build is blocked.

title: Do not require an identified user to enable conditional passkeys
body: The new helper returns false whenever `user` is null, which is the normal state when initially displaying a login form. Both `authenticate()` and the error-challenge path now use this helper, so they no longer call `fillContextForm()` for ordinary login. Consequently, conditional passkey UI and its WebAuthn challenge are absent until a user has already been identified; discoverable-key login stops working, and passkey-only users cannot sign in through these forms. Keep passkeys enabled for unidentified users as well as during re-authentication.

title: Use stored login eligibility when deciding cache invalidation
body: The original model comes from getById(), which wraps organization IDPs so that isEnabled() returns false when their organization is disabled. However, the cached ID lists are selected by the JPA delegate using the IDP's stored enabled flag. If a public, enabled IDP is cached and then made hidden or private while its organization is disabled, both predicates here are false and invalidation is skipped. After the organization is re-enabled, the cached IDP is returned and the login bean only rechecks isEnabled(), so the hidden/private broker is displayed. Compare the original persisted flags rather than the organization-aware enabled state.

title: Do not merge an old query after a concurrent invalidation
body: The query being merged was read before invalidateObject() and the revision lookup. If another transaction creates or updates a login IDP and invalidates this key between those operations, this branch obtains the newer revision but still carries forward the old query's organization results. addRevisioned() then uses the current counter, allowing those stale results to be republished as current. For example, a newly created IDP can remain absent from a previously cached organization's results until another invalidation. Verify that the original query is still current before preserving its searches, or discard it when a concurrent invalidation occurred.

title: Register cleanup for the actual provider aliases
body: Every cleanup action targets the literal alias "alias", but the providers created here are named "idp-alias-0" through "idp-alias-19". These actions therefore delete the wrong resource, normally returning 404, instead of cleaning up the test data. In particular, the realm-level providers are not removed by organization cleanup and can contaminate later tests or repeated runs. Register each created provider's actual alias, and fix the same literal at line 425 for idp-alias-20.

title: Use stored IDP state when deciding login-cache invalidation
body: The original model comes from getById(), whose organization-aware wrapper reports isEnabled() as false when the organization is disabled. However, the login cache is populated from the JPA delegate using the stored IDP enabled flag. If a cached provider is made hidden, link-only, or non-public while its organization is disabled, both predicates here return false and the cache is not invalidated. getForLogin() then continues returning that provider despite its changed eligibility; when the organization is enabled, the bean's enabled-only recheck can display it. Compare the raw persisted IDP state rather than the wrapper's effective enabled state.

title: Do not merge query results from an invalidated revision
body: The query being copied was read before invalidateObject() and getCurrentRevision(), but the replacement is published using the current counter. If an IDP update invalidates the cache after this method reads a query containing organization A's results, a request for an uncached organization B can copy A's stale results into a replacement carrying the newer revision. Subsequent logins for A then use the pre-update provider set, potentially including providers now hidden or non-public. Validate that the original query's revision is still current before merging, or discard its searches after a concurrent invalidation.

title: Invalidate the by-ID entries populated by login searches on removal
body: getForLogin() now populates each provider's internal-ID cache through getById(), without populating its alias cache. remove(alias) only invalidates the internal-ID entry when the alias entry exists or is already locally invalidated. Consequently, a login search followed by remove(alias), without an intervening cached alias lookup, leaves the deleted provider's internal-ID entry intact. Later getById() or getByIdOrAlias() calls return the deleted provider instead of null. Removal should invalidate the stored provider's internal ID unconditionally when the provider exists.

title: Register cleanup for the actual provider aliases
body: The test creates providers named idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-19, but every cleanup callback targets the literal alias "alias". The same mistake occurs for idp-alias-20 at line 425. These callbacks never remove the created providers and can receive 404 responses during cleanup, leaving realm-level providers behind to cause duplicate-alias failures or unexpected login-provider counts in later runs. Register each provider's actual alias.

title: Do not republish an invalidated query when adding an organization search
body: The existing query is read before this branch invalidates the key and samples a new revision. If a concurrent IdP update invalidates the login cache between those operations, this constructor carries the old query's result sets into an entry published with the post-update revision and current counter. For example, moving an IdP from organization A while another request adds a search for organization B can permanently restore A's stale membership. Subsequent login searches can then offer an IdP belonging to another organization. Preserve previous results only after verifying their revision is still valid, or cache organization searches independently.

title: Evaluate invalidation against stored eligibility, not organization-aware enabled state
body: The original model comes from getById(), whose organization-aware wrapper reports isEnabled() as false when the organization is disabled. However, the login cache is populated through the JPA delegate using the IdP's stored enabled flag, so it can contain enabled public IdPs from disabled organizations. Changing such an IdP to hidden, link-only, or non-public makes both predicates false here and skips invalidation, even though the stored query membership changed. Cached getForLogin() calls consequently continue returning the now-ineligible IdP. Compare the original persisted eligibility fields rather than the organization-aware enabled state, and cover updates while an organization is disabled.

title: Clean up the actual aliases created by the test
body: Every cleanup callback targets the literal alias `alias`, but the loop creates providers named `idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-19`. The callback at line 425 repeats the mistake for `idp-alias-20`. These callbacks therefore attempt to delete a nonexistent or unrelated provider instead of the test fixtures, potentially producing 404 failures during teardown and leaving realm-level providers behind. Register cleanup using each provider's actual alias.

title: Reject ambiguous priorities between full crypto providers
body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return priority 200, so this comparator cannot distinguish them. When both default and FIPS providers are loadable, selection depends on ServiceLoader enumeration order. A configuration that previously failed startup can now silently select DefaultCryptoProvider, whose operations explicitly use the non-FIPS BC provider. Continue rejecting multiple providers at the highest priority, or explicitly select the crypto mode, while allowing the lower-priority authz fallback.

title: Enforce the SEQUENCE boundary when reading child elements
body: readSequence() reads an entire child before subtracting its encoded length and accepts a negative remainder. For example, 30 04 02 01 01 02 01 02 returns two integers even though the second extends beyond the declared four-byte SEQUENCE payload. AuthzClientCryptoProvider consequently accepts this malformed DER and converts it into an R/S signature instead of throwing IOException. Read children from a bounded payload and reject any child that exceeds the remaining sequence length.

title: Provide a default priority for existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: Adding order() as an abstract method breaks existing implementations of this public service interface. A provider compiled against the previous interface still loads through ServiceLoader, but comparing it with the newly registered authz provider invokes a method its class does not implement and throws AbstractMethodError, preventing crypto initialization. Source implementations also stop compiling. Make order() a default method with an appropriate legacy priority, retaining the explicit overrides for the built-in providers.

title: Generate the matching EC curve for each algorithm test
body: The constructor generates the default EC key, which is P-256 on the standard JDK provider, for all three tests. Selecting SHA384withECDSA or SHA512withECDSA does not change that key's curve. Thus the ES384 and ES512 tests only convert 32-byte scalars padded to larger output lengths; they never exercise full-sized P-384/P-521 scalars or the long-form DER SEQUENCE length needed for P-521. Generate secp256r1, secp384r1 and secp521r1 keys for their respective algorithms so the new encoder and decoder are tested across their actual signature formats.

title: Reject conflicting highest-priority crypto providers
body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200. Removing the multiple-provider error therefore allows conflicting full providers and selects whichever ServiceLoader enumerates first. For example, when both default and FIPS providers are visible, the non-FIPS provider can win and FIPS is merely logged as ignored; this configuration previously failed initialization. Retain conflict detection for multiple highest-priority providers, while allowing the lower-priority authz fallback, so classpath ordering cannot silently determine FIPS behavior.

title: Validate the concatenated ECDSA signature length
body: concatenatedRSToASN1DER copies exactly signLength bytes without checking signature.length. Consequently, a valid ES256 signature with arbitrary bytes appended converts to exactly the same valid DER signature rather than being rejected. JOSE requires an exact signature length of 64, 96, or 132 bytes, depending on the algorithm. Reject mismatched lengths with IOException before copying; otherwise callers relying on this converter accept malformed, overlong signatures.

title: Provide a backward-compatible default for order()
body: Adding order() as an abstract method breaks existing ServiceLoader CryptoProvider implementations compiled against the previous interface. Such a provider can still be instantiated, but loading it alongside the newly registered authz provider makes the sorting comparator invoke the missing method and throw AbstractMethodError, preventing AuthzClient creation. A default implementation with an appropriate baseline priority would preserve existing providers while allowing implementations to override their ordering.

title: Exercise the actual curves required by each ECDSA algorithm
body: The tests generate an uninitialized EC key pair, which on the normal JDK defaults to P-256, and reuse that curve for ES384 and ES512. Those tests therefore only pad P-256 signature values into larger buffers; they never exercise full-width P-384/P-521 values or the long-form DER sequence length required by P-521 signatures. Initialize the key generator with the algorithm-specific curve and verify the reconstructed DER signature against the original data, rather than only comparing values after the first conversion.

title: Reject ties between the highest-priority crypto providers
body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return priority 200. When more than one is present, this sort preserves their ServiceLoader encounter order and silently selects the first. In particular, if the default implementation is encountered before the FIPS implementation, cryptographic operations use the non-FIPS implementation despite the FIPS provider being present. The previous implementation rejected this ambiguous configuration. Retain a fail-fast check for tied highest-priority providers while allowing the lower-priority authz provider to coexist.

title: The abstract order method breaks existing provider implementations
body: Adding order() as an abstract interface method breaks already-compiled CryptoProvider implementations. When an existing implementation is loaded alongside the newly registered authz provider, the sorting comparator invokes order() on both and throws AbstractMethodError for the existing implementation, preventing crypto initialization. Provide a backward-compatible default priority that preserves existing full providers' precedence over the lightweight authz provider.

title: Exercise the matching curves for ES384 and ES512
body: The EC key generator is never initialized with the curve for the algorithm under test, so on OpenJDK all three tests use the default P-256 key. Consequently, testES512 never exercises a real P-521 signature, whose DER sequence normally exceeds 127 bytes and requires the new encoder and decoder's long-form length handling. Initialize keys with secp256r1, secp384r1 and secp521r1 respectively, and verify the reconstructed DER signature with JCA so the tests establish signature correctness rather than only converter self-consistency.

title: Global view permission bypasses client-specific denials
body: Granting view on the synthetic Clients resource makes canView() return true, so this branch succeeds without evaluating the target client's permissions. A client-specific negative view permission therefore cannot exclude that client from an all-clients view grant, unlike V2's resource-specific override behavior demonstrated by the user permission tests. Delegated administrators can read explicitly excluded clients. Only built-in admin roles should bypass the per-client evaluation; the all-clients permission should be a fallback.

title: Type-based enumeration misses individual client permission resources
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates individual client resources with a name and scopes but does not assign their type. Only the synthetic Clients resource receives the Clients type during initialization. Consequently, findByType cannot enumerate individual client grants: getClientsWithPermission returns an empty set for client-specific permissions and can return the literal "Clients" for a global permission instead of client IDs. Consumers using this set to filter accessible clients receive incorrect results.

title: Provision the new schema entries for already-enabled realms
body: The new Clients resource and scopes are provisioned only when init creates the admin-permissions client, but init immediately returns when that client already exists. A realm initialized with the previous Users-only schema therefore never receives the Clients resource or the configure/map-roles-client-scope/map-roles-composite scopes. Creating an individual client permission then fails because getOrCreateResource tries to attach all Clients scopes and throws "No scopes found." for the missing entries. Existing resource servers need their schema reconciled rather than being skipped.

title: Handle client deletion for V2 permission resources
body: When V2 is enabled without the legacy feature, this guard skips ClientRemovedEvent handling entirely, and no V2 cleanup is added. Individual V2 client resources are owned by the admin-permissions client and merely use the target client's UUID as their name, so deleting the target client does not remove those resources through ownership cleanup. Deleting a client with V2 permissions leaves dangling authorization resources and permission associations. Add a V2 removal path instead of ignoring the event.

title: Resolve resource labels for Clients permissions
body: Clients resources are now supported, but getResourceName still handles only Users and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). Neither individual client resource creation nor initialization of the synthetic Clients resource sets a display name. The resolver therefore returns null for Clients permission resources instead of a client identifier or an "All clients" label, leaving resource labels missing in permission representations. Add Clients name resolution alongside the existing Users handling.

title: Honor client-specific view denials before granting all-clients view
body: The no-argument canView() returns true for a view grant on the all-clients resource. Calling it here immediately authorizes every client without evaluating that client's resource. Consequently, an all-clients view grant combined with a client-specific negative view permission still allows the caller to view the explicitly denied client. The early bypass should be limited to role-based access; fine-grained access must evaluate the client-specific permission before falling back to all-clients permissions.

title: Return real client IDs for all-clients permissions
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() creates a synthetic resource with type Clients and name "Clients", so findByType() includes it. When an all-clients permission grants the requested scope, this method adds "Clients" to the result rather than the IDs of authorized clients. For example, an all-clients map-roles grant returns no real client IDs unless separate client resources also exist, causing consumers that filter available clients or client roles using this set to omit authorized clients. Handle the synthetic resource separately and return actual client IDs while respecting client-specific overrides.

title: Restore the login client's secret after testing rotation
body: This test rotates and then invalidates the old secret of myclient, which is also the OAuth client used by the injected realmAdminClient. No cleanup restores that secret; the @AfterEach method only removes permissions. Cached access tokens can hide the problem temporarily, but subsequent token acquisition or refresh still uses the original configured secret and fails with invalid_client, making the tests token-expiration/order dependent. Use a separate managed client for secret operations or restore the original secret in cleanup.

title: Document requireView methods as enforcement methods
body: The new Javadoc says requireView() returns true when canView() succeeds, but requireView() is void and signals denied access by throwing ForbiddenException. The same incorrect return-value contract is documented for requireViewClientScopes(). These comments should describe the exception behavior, as the other require methods do, rather than promise a nonexistent boolean result.

title: All-clients view permission bypasses client-specific denials
body: canView() now includes fine-grained VIEW permission on the all-clients resource, so this shortcut authorizes the client before evaluating its individual resource. An administrator allowed to view all clients but explicitly denied VIEW on one client can still read that client's details and other view-protected endpoints. This contradicts hasPermission(client, ...), which applies the all-clients default only when no individual resource exists. Preserve the broad admin-role bypass, but evaluate client-specific permissions before accepting the type-level grant, and add an allow-all/deny-one test.

title: Permission enumeration returns the all-clients resource name instead of client IDs
body: The schema gives the all-clients resource the type Clients, so findByType includes it in this loop. When its permission is granted, the result contains the literal string "Clients", not the IDs of clients authorized by that default permission. Clients without individual authorization resources are never enumerated at all, even though hasPermission(client, scope) grants access to them. Callers filtering clients by this set therefore omit clients authorized through a type-level grant. Handle the all-clients default explicitly and enumerate actual client IDs while respecting individual overrides.

title: Provision the new schema entries for existing FGAP V2 realms
body: Adding Clients to SCHEMA provisions its resource and scopes only for newly initialized realms. init() immediately returns when the admin-permissions client already exists, so realms initialized by the previous version retain only the Users resource and old scopes. Creating permissions with configure or either new mapping scope then fails in getScope(), and client evaluation can receive a null all-clients resource from its fallback lookup. Add a migration or schema synchronization path for existing admin-permissions clients.

title: Resolve display names for the new client permission resources
body: The new Clients branch creates resources whose names are internal client IDs and leaves displayName unset. However, getResourceName() still resolves only Users resources and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). It therefore returns null for individual client resources and for the schema-created all-clients resource, leaving returned permission resource-name metadata without identifiable targets. Extend getResourceName() to resolve individual clients to their clientId and give the type-level resource an All clients label.

title: Assert the changed exit-code contract
body: This PR changes incompatible checks from exit code 4 to 3 and assigns 4 to disabled-feature failures, but the new disabled-feature test and the incompatible-version tests do not assert those exact codes. The guide explicitly tells automation to rely on exit codes rather than messages, so retaining the old incompatible code or returning a generic error for a disabled feature could break callers without failing these tests. Assert exit code 4 for disabled metadata and check commands, and exit code 3 for incompatible checks.

title: Test the new exit-code contract, not just error messages
body: The disabled-feature test checks only error text, and the incompatible-version tests never assert the exit status. This PR changes the recreate status from 4 to 3 and assigns 4 to feature-disabled failures, but neither value is verified. The tool explicitly directs automation to rely on exit codes rather than messages, so returning the wrong status—or success—would pass these tests while misleading upgrade scripts. Assert exit code 4 for both disabled metadata and check commands, 3 for incompatible versions, and 0 for a compatible check.

title: Read-only group permission grants top-level group management
body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() relies on this method through requireManage(), so an administrator granted only VIEW can create groups or move existing subgroups to the top level. This crosses the read/write authorization boundary. Only the MANAGE scope should satisfy this check.

title: Use model group IDs rather than authorization resource IDs
body: groupResource.getId() identifies an authorization resource, not a GroupModel; AdminPermissionsSchema stores the model group ID in the resource name. Passing the authorization ID to hasPermission() makes its findByName() lookup miss and fall back to the all-groups permission. Returning that ID also supplies invalid group IDs to user search and count queries. In particular, an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS grant adds the aggregate authorization resource's UUID to the membership filter, causing searches and counts to return no matching users. Resolve actual group IDs and handle the aggregate resource separately.

title: Assign the Groups type to individual group authorization resources
body: The new group resolution path creates an authorization resource named after the group ID but never assigns it the Groups resource type. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() exclusively enumerates resources through findByType(..., "Groups", ...), so these individual resources are omitted. Consequently, a group-specific VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS grant can authorize direct user access but contributes no IDs to /users/count or pre-pagination user search filtering, producing incorrect counts and incomplete pages. Individual group resources need a matching type or a different enumeration mechanism.

title: Allow the group-member creation fallback with FGAP V2
body: canCreateGroupMembers() still returns false unless the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled. With V2 selected, that V1 feature check is false, so an administrator granted MANAGE_MEMBERS and MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP on a group cannot create a user in that group: createUser() rethrows the failed global manage-users authorization as HTTP 403 without evaluating the group grants. Update this guard to support V2 so the newly implemented group scopes work through the existing member-creation path.

title: Do not let the view scope authorize global group management
body: The parameterless canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on all groups. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() relies on this check through requireManage(), so an administrator granted only read access can POST to create groups or move an existing group to the realm root by supplying its ID. This also contradicts canManage(GroupModel), which requires MANAGE. The global management check must require MANAGE, with a regression test denying these operations to a VIEW-only administrator.

title: Collect actual group IDs for member searches and counts
body: groupResource.getId() is an authorization-resource UUID, not the GroupModel ID. Individual resources are named with the group ID by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(), and that method does not assign them the Groups type either. Consequently, this loop misses individual group permissions and, when an all-groups member permission is granted, returns the all-groups authorization UUID as a group ID. UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource pass these IDs to membership-filtered queries, causing authorized users to disappear from searches and producing incorrect counts. Enumerate actual group IDs and explicitly handle all-groups grants.

title: Enable delegated group-member creation for V2
body: The group-member creation fallback still accepts only the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ V1 feature. With only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, an administrator granted MANAGE_MEMBERS and MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP on a group cannot create a user assigned to that group: requireManage() rejects the administrator's lack of global user-management permission, and this feature check immediately disables the fallback before consulting the new group evaluator. Allow the fallback under V2 as well and test creation using only the two group scopes.

title: Provision the new schema entries for existing permissions clients
body: Adding Groups to the static schema does not install its resource or scopes into an already-initialized V2 realm, because init() returns immediately when the realm has an admin-permissions client. Such realms retain the previous Users/Clients schema and lack manage-membership, manage-members, and view-members. Creating their first group permission calls getOrCreateResource(), which attempts to attach every Groups scope and throws ModelException("No scopes found."). Synchronize the new schema entries for existing clients rather than provisioning them only when the client is first created.

title: Read-only group permissions authorize top-level group mutations
body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() relies on this check to authorize both creating groups and moving existing subgroups to the top level. Consequently, an administrator granted only read access to groups can mutate the group hierarchy. This check must require MANAGE, with a regression test confirming that VIEW alone cannot perform either operation.

title: Authorization resource IDs are used as model group IDs
body: AdminPermissionsSchema names a per-group authorization resource after the GroupModel ID, but the resource has its own independently generated ID. This loop passes the authorization ID to hasPermission(), which looks it up by name, and returns that same authorization ID as a group-membership filter. For example, an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS grant returns the synthetic resource's ID, so user searches and counts restricted by this set cannot match real memberships. Evaluate and return actual model group IDs, handling the synthetic all-groups resource separately.

title: The member-view scan excludes newly created per-group resources
body: This scan requires Resource.type to be Groups, but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates per-group resources with only a name and scopes; it does not assign their type. Only the synthetic all-groups resource initialized by the schema has that type. An individual VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS grant therefore contributes no membership filter. User searches paginate all realm users before checking canView(), so permitted members outside the unfiltered page disappear from results. Assign the type to per-group resources or enumerate them through another reliable association.

title: The delegated member-creation fallback remains gated on V1
body: canCreateGroupMembers() returns false unless the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled. With only V2 enabled, an administrator granted the new manage-members and manage-membership scopes on every group in a new user's representation still fails the global Users manage check and receives 403 without evaluating those group permissions. The existing delegated member-creation path needs to admit V2 as well, with coverage for creating a user using group-scoped permissions.

title: Existing V2 realms are not initialized with the Groups schema
body: The fallback assumes an all-groups resource exists, but AdminPermissionsSchema.init() immediately returns when the realm already has an admin-permissions client. A realm initialized before this change contains only the Users and Clients schema resources and lacks the new group-specific scopes. Its Groups lookup therefore returns null, which is passed to the policy lookup and subsequently dereferenced during evaluation; creating group permissions also cannot resolve the missing scopes. Reconcile or migrate existing resource servers before using the new resource type.

title: Validate HTML inside ChoiceFormat branches instead of discarding it
body: This replacement removes the entire ChoiceFormat expression before checking HTML, including all branch text. For example, a translated linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit.minutes value of `{0,choice,0#minutes|1#minute|1

title: Keep React validation messages in i18next format
body: This frontend resource uses i18next interpolation with double-braced arguments such as `{{0}}`, not Java MessageFormat syntax. Replacing those arguments with `{0}` and adding `{2,choice,...}` leaves unevaluated formatting text in multivalued-size validation errors instead of the field name and limits. The admin UI resource has the same change. Keep both React resources in frontend-supported interpolation/pluralization syntax; Java ChoiceFormat belongs in the server-side bundles.

title: Prevent overlapping prefix and suffix trimming
body: The suffix loop can consume characters already counted by the prefix loop. With an English message containing bold markup, a translation `` sanitizes to ``. The common prefix has length 4 and the common suffix length 5, so the diagnostic calls `sanitized.substring(4, 2)` and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. This aborts verification rather than returning the illegal-HTML diagnostic. Bound suffix trimming by the remaining length after the prefix.

title: Translate the OTP setup instruction into Lithuanian
body: The replacement `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, but this is the Lithuanian message bundle. Lithuanian users now receive an Italian instruction during OTP setup. The same sentence was also introduced for totpStep1 in the Lithuanian account bundle. Both replacements should use Lithuanian text.

title: Validate HTML inside choice branches instead of discarding them
body: Normalization replaces entire MessageFormat choice expressions with "..." before checking HTML, including all branch text. For example, a quoted `second` branch in `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit.seconds` passes verification because the link is never inspected. The resource is packaged unchanged, and MessageFormat restores that HTML when selecting the branch. Validate branch contents rather than exempting the whole expression, otherwise forbidden links and tags can bypass the new check.

title: Preserve i18next interpolation in the React message bundles
body: The account console uses i18next interpolation (`{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, and `{{2}}`), not Java MessageFormat. Replacing these placeholders with single braces and adding `{2,choice,...}` means multivalued user-profile validation errors display the placeholders and choice expression literally instead of the attribute name and bounds. Retain frontend-compatible interpolation and pluralization here and in the corresponding changed admin-ui message.

title: Restrict the anchor exemption to the actual a element
body: `</?a[^>]*>` also matches elements such as `<audio>`, `<applet>`, and `<abbr>`. When verifying an English bundle, the reference value is the same string, so these tags and their attributes are removed as supposedly approved anchors before the sanitizer sees them. For example, `key=<audio autoplay src="https://example.com/audio"></audio>` returns no violations despite being outside the allowlist. Match the complete `a` tag name rather than any name beginning with `a`.

title: Prevent the common prefix and suffix from overlapping
body: The prefix and suffix scans are independent, so they can overlap when the sanitizer inserts closing tags. With an English message `key=`, sanitization produces ``: `start` becomes 3 and `end` becomes 2, causing `value.substring(3, 1)` to throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. Malformed HTML then aborts verification instead of returning a useful violation and checking the remaining messages. Limit the suffix scan to the region left after removing the common prefix.

title: Use Lithuanian text for the Lithuanian OTP setup instruction
body: The replacement `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, not Lithuanian. The same Italian text was introduced for `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian account bundle. Users selecting Lithuanian now receive the first OTP setup instruction in another language; replace both values with Lithuanian translations.

title: Keep the zh_CN OTP instruction in Simplified Chinese
body: The new `totpStep1` value uses Traditional Chinese characters and terminology (`手機`, `安裝`, `應用程式`) in the Simplified Chinese `zh_CN` bundle. This changes the instruction to the wrong locale variant while the surrounding steps remain Simplified Chinese. Use a Simplified Chinese translation, as the login bundle's corresponding instruction already does.

title: Validate ChoiceFormat branch text instead of discarding it
body: For link-expiration units and error-invalid-multivalued-size, normalization removes the entire choice expression, including its display text, before anchor validation or HTML sanitization. A valid quoted branch such as `1#'minute'` therefore passes verification because only `...` is checked. The original resource is still shipped, and MessageFormat expands that HTML at runtime. This bypasses the restriction on new links and forbidden HTML. Validate the branch outputs rather than excluding the whole expression.

title: Retain i18next interpolation in the React console bundles
body: This React console resource replaces i18next placeholders (`{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, and `{{2}}`) with Java MessageFormat syntax. i18next does not interpolate single-braced arguments or evaluate Java choice expressions, so multivalued-attribute validation errors display literal placeholders and the choice expression instead of the attribute name and bounds. The admin-ui English bundle contains the same regression. Keep the Java syntax in server-side bundles and use i18next-compatible interpolation and pluralization in both React bundles.

title: Prevent the diagnostic prefix and suffix from overlapping
body:
The common-suffix loop can consume characters already counted by the common-prefix loop. For example, an English entry `key=

` is sanitized to `

`, producing start=3 and end=2. The subsequent call to value.substring(3, 1) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning an Illegal HTML finding. Thus malformed resources can crash verification and suppress the remaining diagnostics. Limit suffix matching to the portions left after removing the prefix.

title: Restrict the anchor exception to the actual a element
body: The anchor pattern also matches every tag whose name starts with `a`, including article, audio, and applet. English bundles are compared with themselves, so an entry such as `<article onclick="alert(1)">Click</article>` has both tags removed as supposedly trusted anchors and passes verification without its event handler reaching OWASP. Translations copying those tags pass too, despite them being outside the allowed policy. Require a tag-name boundary after `a` so non-anchor elements are validated normally.

title: Replace the Italian instruction with Lithuanian text
body: The replacement loginTotpStep1 text, `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, is Italian rather than Lithuanian. The same replacement appears in the Lithuanian account bundle's totpStep1. Users selecting Lithuanian now receive the authenticator installation instruction in another language. Translate both replacements into Lithuanian.

title: Keep the zh_CN instruction in Simplified Chinese
body: The new totpStep1 uses Traditional Chinese characters and terminology (`手機`, `安裝`, `應用程式`) in the Simplified Chinese zh_CN bundle. This replaces a correctly localized instruction with text for the other Chinese locale. Use a Simplified Chinese replacement consistent with the surrounding messages.

title: Correct the grant-type comparison in the token ID matcher
body: The grant shortcut occupies indices 4 through 5, but this matcher reads substring(3, 5). It also rejects equality rather than inequality. Consequently, an ID such as `onrtna:<UUID>` passes an authorization-code expectation, so the integration assertions do not detect missing or incorrect grant metadata. Validate the prefix length, read substring(4, 6), and reject a shortcut that differs from the expected value.

title: Specify the two-character requirement for grant shortcuts
body: The SPI documents shortcuts as normally three letters, but the default decoder requires a six-character context containing exactly two characters per field. A custom grant following this documentation and returning `abc` produces IDs such as `onrtabc:<UUID>`, which the same provider rejects during decoding. Document the exact two-character requirement and validate it when registering grant factories, or make the encoding accommodate the documented lengths.

title: Avoid passing the invalid-grant test on an uninitialized factory
body: The test setup never calls postInit or supplies a sessionFactory. Because `ac` is absent from its shortcut map, decoding invokes the factory's provider-discovery fallback and throws NullPointerException before reaching the decoder's unknown-grant validation. Catching any RuntimeException treats that setup failure as success, so the intended validation remains untested. Supply a factory that returns an empty provider stream and assert the expected IllegalArgumentException.

title: Validate rawTokenId instead of checking grantType twice
body: The final null guard checks grantType again rather than rawTokenId. A context with a null raw identifier is therefore accepted, and encodeTokenId converts it into a literal identifier such as `onrtro:null`. Multiple such contexts produce identical token IDs instead of rejecting the missing identifier. Apply this requireNonNull check to rawTokenId.

title: Existing custom grant factories now prevent server startup
body: The new abstract getShortcut() method is invoked on every registered grant factory by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(). Custom grant factories compiled against the previous interface have no implementation, so startup throws AbstractMethodError, even if their grant is never requested. Provide a compatibility path for existing factories, or explicitly document the required provider migration.

title: The access-token matcher does not check the expected grant
body: Grant shortcuts occupy indexes 4 through 5, but the matcher reads substring(3, 5) and rejects equality rather than inequality. For example, an onrtro:<UUID> token passes when the expected grant is ac. Consequently, the authorization-code, device, CIBA, and refresh event tests accept missing or incorrect grant metadata. Check the prefix length, extract substring(4, 6), and reject mismatches.

title: Accepted grant shortcuts can produce undecodable token IDs
body: Grant shortcuts are registered without checking their length, while OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() documents a three-letter shortcut. A custom grant following that documentation produces IDs such as onrtabc:<UUID>, but getTokenContextFromTokenId() requires exactly six context characters and rejects every such ID. Specify and validate the two-character requirement before accepting a factory so the encoder cannot emit IDs its decoder rejects.

title: The invalid-grant test passes on an unintended NullPointerException
body: The test setup never calls factory.postInit() or supplies a sessionFactory. Looking up the unregistered ac shortcut therefore enters getGrantTypeByShortcut()'s fallback and throws NullPointerException when accessing sessionFactory. Catching any RuntimeException makes the test pass without reaching the decoder's intended IllegalArgumentException. Initialize or mock the factory lookup and assert the specific expected exception.

title: The raw token ID null check validates the wrong argument
body: The check labeled "Null rawTokenId not allowed" checks grantType a second time instead of rawTokenId. A context with a null raw ID is therefore accepted, and encodeTokenId() emits the literal suffix ':null' rather than rejecting the invalid identifier. Validate rawTokenId here to enforce the constructor's intended invariant.

title: Correct the grant shortcut assertion
body: The grant shortcut occupies indexes 4–5, so it must be read with substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5). The comparison is also inverted: equality currently rejects the token. Consequently, an ID such as onrtrt:<uuid> passes an assertion expecting the authorization-code shortcut ac, allowing incorrect or missing grant metadata to go unnoticed. Check the prefix length and reject when the correctly extracted shortcut does not equal the expected value.

title: Specify the required two-character grant shortcut
body: This contract recommends a three-character shortcut, but the default decoder requires a six-character context prefix containing exactly two characters per field. A custom factory returning a documented three-character shortcut is accepted during registration and produces IDs such as onrtabc:<id>, which the decoder then rejects for having a seven-character prefix. Document the exact two-character requirement and validate it when registering factories.

title: Ensure the invalid-grant test exercises the intended exception
body: The test fixture never initializes the factory's sessionFactory. Because ac is absent from its shortcut map, decoding enters getGrantTypeByShortcut's provider-discovery fallback and throws NullPointerException when accessing sessionFactory. Catching any RuntimeException makes the test pass without reaching the intended unknown-grant IllegalArgumentException. Supply a mocked session factory with no matching provider and assert the specific exception.

title: Validate rawTokenId instead of checking grantType twice
body: The rawTokenId null check mistakenly checks grantType again. A context with a valid grant type and null rawTokenId is therefore accepted, and encodeTokenId serializes its identifier as the literal suffix :null instead of rejecting the missing identifier. Pass rawTokenId to this requireNonNull call to enforce the constructor's intended invariant.

title: Remove the old local recovery credential when updating user storage
body: A user can already have locally stored recovery codes, particularly because registration previously always created them locally. If the user-storage provider accepts the new set, this path leaves that existing local credential untouched. Keycloak's credential validation can still validate the old local codes when external validation fails, so regenerating recovery codes does not revoke the previous set. Remove the local recovery credential after a successful external update and test regeneration for a user with existing local codes.

title: Remove exhausted recovery credentials from their owning storage
body: The new lookup can return a credential owned by user storage, but the subsequent exhaustion branch still calls removeStoredCredentialById, which deletes credentials from Keycloak's credential store rather than the external provider. An external provider retaining an exhausted credential therefore remains configured. If the user abandons login before completing regeneration, the next login can select that exhausted credential and fail in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean when getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() encounters an empty Optional. Disable or remove the exhausted external credential through the user-storage SPI.

title: Make the test provider consume recovery codes
body: The new validator only checks membership in the original code list; it never persists consumption or advances the next-code state. getCredentials also reconstructs a completely unused model from that same list on every call. Consequently, this fixture accepts the same recovery code indefinitely, always requests code zero, and never reaches exhaustion. The added single-login test passes without exercising the essential single-use contract or exhausted-credential handling. Persist and expose used-code state, and test subsequent logins, replay rejection, and exhaustion.

title: Remove the previous local code set when storing a replacement externally
body: When a federated user already has locally stored recovery codes—the creation path used before this change—a successful external update leaves that local credential untouched. Credential validation can fall back to the local recovery-code provider when the external validator rejects an input, so codes from the previous set remain valid after the user generates a replacement externally. Remove existing local recovery-code credentials as part of a successful external replacement, and test this migration scenario.

title: Export OTP credentials with the canonical OTP type
body: The new getCredentials override returns the stored OTP model unchanged, but updateCredential sets that model's type from the registration input. CredentialHelper supplies the realm policy type, 'totp' or 'hotp', whereas OTP credential providers and account credential listings use the canonical type 'otp'. Consequently, the exported credential does not match the OTP listing, breaking the existing account-listing/removal behavior. Return an OTP-typed representation rather than exposing the legacy validation record unchanged.

title: The federation fixture never consumes validated recovery codes
body: Recovery-code validation only checks membership in the saved list and never records consumption. Since getCredentials reconstructs a credential from that unchanged list, the requested code remains code 0, previously used codes remain valid indefinitely, and allCodesUsed() never becomes true. The new test performs only one login, so it cannot exercise advancement, replay rejection, or the exhausted-federated-credential branch changed by this PR. Maintain consumption and next-code state in the fixture and extend the test to cover repeated login and exhaustion.

title: Revoke existing local recovery codes when saving a new set externally
body: When a federated user already has recovery codes in Keycloak storage—for example, codes enrolled before this change—a successful external update skips credential creation without removing the existing local credential. Credential validation can still fall back to the local provider when external validation rejects an input, so codes from the replaced set remain usable after regeneration. Remove the previous local recovery credential after successfully saving the replacement externally, and cover this migration case with a regression test.

title: Remove exhausted recovery credentials from the correct storage
body: The new lookup can return a credential owned by a user-storage provider, but this cleanup still calls removeStoredCredentialById, which removes credentials from Keycloak's local/federated database rather than disabling the external provider's credential. An exhausted external credential therefore remains present. If the user abandons the required re-enrollment, a provider that reports configuration based on credential existence will still select recovery authentication on the next login, where getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() fails because every code is used. Route exhausted external credentials through the user-storage disabling mechanism instead.

title: Make the recovery-code fixture consume successful inputs
body: The new validator accepts any code in the original list but never consumes it, and getCredentials reconstructs an entirely unused recovery credential from that list on every call. Consequently, the added login test passes while the fixture keeps requesting code zero, permits replay indefinitely, and can never exercise exhaustion or forced re-enrollment. Persist consumption in the fixture and test used-code rejection, advancement to the next code, and exhaustion so the external-storage recovery lifecycle is actually covered.

title: Wait for the reader to finish before checking its exceptions
body: Setting deletedAll only requests that the reader stop; a groups(...) request can still be in flight when caughtExceptions is checked. If that request fails, its exception can be added after the assertion has passed, allowing this regression test to miss the concurrent-access failure it is intended to detect. Retain the reader Thread and join it before asserting that no exceptions were collected.

title: Stop the background reader when deletion fails
body: If any group removal throws, execution skips deletedAll.set(true), leaving the non-daemon reader running indefinitely. The reader catches request failures and continues, so realm/client teardown does not stop it and can instead turn it into a loop accumulating exceptions throughout the remaining test suite. Signal termination in a finally block and ensure the reader is joined on failure as well as success.

title: Wait for the reader to finish before checking its exceptions
body: Setting deletedAll does not wait for an in-flight groups() request to finish. The assertion can therefore observe an empty caughtExceptions list and pass before the reader records an error from the final concurrent-deletion request. Retain the reader thread and join it before inspecting caughtExceptions so the regression test cannot miss those failures.

title: Stop the reader even when a deletion fails
body: If any group remove() call throws, execution skips deletedAll.set(true), leaving the newly started non-daemon thread repeatedly issuing requests indefinitely. It can continue accessing the realm and admin client after test teardown and interfere with subsequent tests or prevent the test process from exiting normally.
