Ensure the stop flag is set in a finally block and the worker is terminated before leaving the test.

title: Wait for the reader to finish before checking its exceptions
body: Setting deletedAll to true only prevents the reader's next iteration; a groups() request can still be in flight when caughtExceptions is checked. If that request fails, its exception can be recorded after the assertion has passed, allowing this regression test to pass despite the concurrent-access failure. Retain the reader thread and join it before asserting so all read results are accounted for and no request overlaps fixture teardown.

title: Stop the background reader even if deletion fails
body: If any remove() call throws, execution skips deletedAll.set(true), leaving the background thread polling indefinitely. Because the thread is not a daemon and has no other termination condition, a failed test leaks a reader that continues accessing the realm during teardown and subsequent tests and can prevent JVM shutdown. Signal termination in a finally block and ensure the reader is joined on failure as well as success.

title: Handle authorized requests without an organization member
body: Organization-scoped API credentials can authorize access without a user membership, leaving organization_context.member as None. For those requests, request.user.is_superuser is false and this expression raises AttributeError. Because it is evaluated even when optimized_pagination is absent, this also breaks previously working requests using the default paginator. Only evaluate the advanced-access check when needed and explicitly handle a missing member.

title: Preserve datetime cursor conversion for audit logs
body: The audit-log endpoint uses this paginator with order_by="-datetime", so get_item_key receives a datetime.datetime value. math.floor and math.ceil cannot handle that type and raise TypeError while building cursors for any nonempty page. value_from_cursor also returns the numeric cursor value unchanged instead of converting it back to a datetime for the database comparison. The optimized audit-log path needs DateTimePaginator's key and cursor conversions to work at all.

title: Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing
body: With advanced features enabled, a negative cursor offset is passed directly to a Django QuerySet slice. Django rejects negative start or stop indices with ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported"); it does not handle the boundaries automatically as the comment claims. For example, cursor=0:-1:0 makes the optimized audit-log request fail before retrieving any rows. Implement reverse traversal using supported ordering and nonnegative slices, or reject such offsets with a pagination error.

title: Handle authorized requests without an organization member
body: Organization-scoped API/integration authentication can be authorized to read audit logs without a user membership, leaving organization_context.member as None. Dereferencing member.has_global_access then raises AttributeError for these non-superuser requests. Because this expression is evaluated even when optimized_pagination is absent, the change breaks the existing audit-log path as well. Check the optional membership safely and evaluate eligibility only when the optimized path is requested.

title: The optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime fields
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint selects this paginator with order_by="-datetime", so the item value here is a datetime object. math.ceil/math.floor cannot accept that value, and building cursors for any nonempty first page raises TypeError. value_from_cursor also returns the encoded numeric value unchanged instead of converting it back to a datetime, making existing timestamp cursors invalid for the query. Use DateTimePaginator's timestamp encoding and decoding for this endpoint.

title: Django querysets do not support negative slicing
body: The advanced-feature branch passes a negative cursor offset directly into a Django QuerySet slice. Django explicitly rejects negative slice bounds with ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported."); it does not handle them automatically as the comment claims. Consequently, every negative-offset request through this branch fails instead of performing reverse pagination. Implement reverse traversal using ordering and nonnegative bounds, or reject unsupported offsets with BadPaginationError.

title: Handle requests without an organization member before checking privileges
body: The new privilege check runs even when optimized_pagination is absent and dereferences organization_context.member for every non-superuser. Organization-scoped API-token requests can be authorized to read audit logs without an associated organization member; for those requests, member is None and this raises AttributeError. Existing callers therefore receive a 500 even on the default pagination path. Evaluate this check only for opted-in requests and handle missing membership explicitly.

title: Preserve datetime cursor conversion for audit logs
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses this paginator with order_by="-datetime", so get_item_key receives a datetime rather than a number. Calling math.floor or math.ceil on it raises TypeError when build_cursor processes any nonempty page, making optimized audit-log requests fail with a 500. value_from_cursor also returns the numeric cursor unchanged instead of converting it back to a datetime for the database filter. Reuse DateTimePaginator's key encoding and decoding for this endpoint.

title: Do not pass negative slice bounds to a Django QuerySet
body: Django QuerySets reject negative slice bounds; they do not handle them like Python lists. With advanced features enabled, a cursor such as 0:-1:0 reaches this slice and raises ValueError instead of performing the advertised reverse pagination. Reject unsupported offsets with BadPaginationError or implement reverse traversal using valid ordering and nonnegative bounds.

title: Guard requests without an organization membership
body: Organization-scoped API authentication can authorize this endpoint without attaching a user membership, leaving organization_context.member as None. The new expression dereferences that member for non-superusers, even when optimized_pagination was not requested. Previously working audit-log requests using organization API authentication will therefore return an AttributeError/500. Handle absent memberships and evaluate the optimization gate only for opt-in requests.

title: Use datetime-aware cursor conversion for audit logs
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint selects OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but get_item_key passes the AuditLogEntry datetime value to math.floor/math.ceil. Building cursors for any nonempty first page therefore raises TypeError. The inverse conversion also returns a raw numeric cursor value instead of the datetime required by the query. Inherit or reuse DateTimePaginator's key and cursor conversions so the new audit-log pagination path works.

title: Do not pass negative offsets to QuerySet slicing
body: The advanced-pagination branch passes a negative cursor offset directly into a Django QuerySet slice. Django explicitly rejects negative slice bounds rather than interpreting them as reverse pagination, so an enabled request with a cursor such as 0:-1:0 raises an exception before fetching any rows. Implement reverse pagination using ordering and nonnegative bounds, or reject unsupported offsets with a controlled pagination error.

title: Migrate or version the Redis buffer keyspace
body: This replaces Redis sets with sorted sets while retaining the existing span-buf:s:* key names. Live buffers written by the old consumer remain ordinary sets, so ZADD, ZCARD, and ZSCAN will raise WRONGTYPE after deployment. Failed processing batches cannot advance their Kafka offsets, and old and new consumers are mutually incompatible during a rolling upgrade. Introduce a compatible migration/drain strategy or a versioned buffer namespace before switching command types.

title: Preserve timestamp scores when merging span buffers
body: Both ZUNIONSTORE calls use Redis's default SUM aggregation. When the same payload is present in both buffers—for example, a replayed grandchild written under its parent after an earlier batch moved it to the root—its end-timestamp score is added to the existing score. An old span can consequently receive a score far beyond every real timestamp and survive eviction while newer spans are removed. Use a score-preserving aggregation such as AGGREGATE MAX for both unions.

title: Honor the configured maximum segment span count
body: The eviction threshold is hard-coded to 1000, while the Python flush-time check has been removed and SpansBuffer still exposes max_segment_spans. That constructor argument now has no effect: a configured limit of 100 permits 1000 spans, and a configured limit of 2000 silently loses spans above 1000 that were previously accepted. Pass the configured limit into the eviction script rather than leaving the public configuration disconnected from enforcement.

title: Protect the root span during eviction
body: ZPOPMIN treats the root span like any other timestamp-scored payload. If enough children end after the root, or share its timestamp and sort after its serialized payload, pruning can remove the root. The has-root marker nevertheless remains true, so the segment receives the short root timeout but flushes without any span marked is_segment and loses the root payload. Preserve the root during truncation, and cover equal timestamps and children ending after the root in eviction tests.

title: Migrate existing Redis sets before switching to sorted sets
body: The previous implementation stores ordinary Redis sets under the same `span-buf:s:*` keys now used by ZADD, ZSCAN, and the Lua sorted-set commands. Existing buffered segments therefore cause WRONGTYPE errors during insertion and flushing after deployment. No conversion, drain, or versioned namespace is provided, so affected processing can remain blocked until those keys expire. Introduce a compatible migration or a new key namespace before changing the Redis data type.

title: Use datetime cursor conversion for the audit-log paginator
body: The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, but `get_item_key` calls math.floor/math.ceil on the resulting datetime object. Any nonempty optimized audit-log page raises TypeError while building its cursors. `value_from_cursor` also returns the numeric cursor unchanged instead of converting it back to a datetime. Reuse DateTimePaginator's key and cursor conversions so the new endpoint path can return and follow pages.

title: Preserve timestamp scores when merging overlapping buffers
body: Both ZUNIONSTORE calls use Redis's default SUM aggregation. If a child span is replayed after its parent buffer has been redirected, its payload can exist in both the temporary parent buffer and the destination buffer. Merging then doubles its end-timestamp score instead of preserving it. The subsequent ZPOPMIN eviction treats that old replayed span as newer than genuinely recent spans and discards the wrong data. Specify an aggregation such as MAX to keep merges idempotent for overlapping payloads.

title: Do not pass negative offsets to Django queryset slicing
body: With advanced features enabled, a cursor such as `0:-1:0` reaches this branch and slices the Django queryset with a negative start. Django explicitly rejects negative queryset indices; it does not handle them automatically as the comment claims. Consequently, the advertised negative-offset pagination produces an exception and an HTTP 500. Implement supported reverse-pagination bounds or reject the cursor with a pagination error before slicing.

title: Honor the configured maximum segment span count
body: Removing the span-count check leaves `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` unused, while the Lua script always trims to 1000 spans. Callers configuring a smaller maximum now receive segments exceeding that limit, and callers configuring a larger maximum silently lose spans at 1000. Pass the configured limit into the insertion script and use it for eviction rather than retaining a constructor option that no longer controls the buffer.

title: The optimized paginator cannot paginate audit-log datetimes
body: The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with order_by='-datetime', but get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to a datetime.datetime value. Every nonempty optimized page therefore raises TypeError while building its cursors. value_from_cursor also leaves timestamp cursors numeric instead of converting them back to datetimes. This path needs DateTimePaginator's conversions, not the numeric paginator implementation.

title: Changing Redis key types requires a migration or versioned keyspace
body: ZADD and ZSCAN now reuse the same span-buf:s:* keys that existing consumers populated as ordinary Redis sets. Buffered data survives deployment, and during a rolling rollout both implementations can access these keys. Redis rejects the incompatible operations with WRONGTYPE, preventing ingestion into existing segments and preventing their flush. Version the keyspace or provide a coordinated drain/migration and compatible read path before switching types.

title: Handle requests without an organization member
body: The capability check dereferences organization_context.member for every non-superuser request, even when optimized_pagination was not requested. Organization-token authentication can authorize this endpoint without a user membership, leaving member as None; those requests now raise AttributeError instead of returning audit logs. Guard the optional membership and avoid evaluating this capability for requests using the normal paginator.

title: Django querysets do not support the advertised negative slicing
body: When advanced features are enabled, a negative cursor offset is passed directly to QuerySet slicing. Django explicitly rejects negative slice bounds with ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.'), so this branch cannot perform the advertised traversal. For example, Cursor(0, -1, False) fails immediately. Translate reverse traversal into nonnegative query bounds or reject the cursor with a pagination error.

title: Preserve timestamps when merging duplicate sorted-set members
body: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM. On replay, a payload already moved into its redirected segment can be ZADDed again under its original parent, leaving the same payload in both sets. The union then doubles its end timestamp, making an old replayed span appear far newer than other spans and causing ZPOPMIN to evict the wrong data. Use an aggregation mode that preserves the timestamp, such as MAX, for both unions.

title: Protect the segment span from eviction
body: Eviction considers only end timestamps and does not protect the root/segment span. With 1000 children and a root sharing their end timestamp, Redis's lexicographic tie-breaking can evict the root; children that outlive their parent create the same problem. This 1001-span segment was previously within the default limit, but now flush_segments can emit it without any is_segment span while has_root_span remains true. Preserve the root when selecting eviction victims.

title: The max_segment_spans setting is now silently ignored
body: Removing the span-count check leaves the existing max_segment_spans constructor argument unused, while insertion always applies a hard-coded limit of 1000. A buffer configured with max_segment_spans=100 can now emit up to 1000 spans, and one configured to allow larger segments silently loses data at 1000. Propagate the configured limit into insertion or retain appropriate enforcement instead of leaving a nonfunctional configuration argument.

title: The reduced redirect limit can split valid deep segments
body: When ancestors arrive in separate batches, the redirect hash can contain a chain longer than 1000 entries. Evicting span payloads does not shorten that chain. The reduced loop bound silently stops before reaching the terminal segment, so a late child whose parent is more than 1001 redirects from the root is stored under an intermediate key and flushed as a separate segment. Retain the supported traversal depth or resolve/compress redirects rather than treating the payload limit as a redirect-depth limit.

title: Preserve unweighted events in the upsampled count
body: SUM(sample_weight) ignores NULL weights. Allowlisting a project does not backfill sampling metadata on historical events or ensure that every incoming error carries a client sample rate. Those unweighted errors therefore disappear from the reported count, and a bucket containing only historical errors can become zero. Sum a weight that defaults to 1 for unweighted events, and cover mixed sampled and unsampled events in the integration tests.

title: A substring match does not establish an error-only query
body: Queries such as `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` both satisfy this check despite matching transactions. For allowlisted projects, the endpoint consequently replaces count() with an aggregation over sample_weight, which is not available for transactions. Valid Discover queries can then fail or produce incorrect counts. Determine eligibility from the parsed query and require that the complete query restricts results to error events.

title: Apply weighted counting to top-N selection as well
body: Only timeseries_columns is transformed; the selected_columns used to find the top events still contains the original count(), with the original count ordering. A request grouping by message with field=count(), orderby=-count, and topEvents=1 therefore selects the group with the most stored events rather than the highest upsampled count. For example, two weight-2 events win over one weight-10 event, even though their displayed counts are 4 and 10. Keep the top-N selection aggregation consistent with the transformed time-series aggregation.

title: Check the dataset actually being queried
body: The eligibility check receives the outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset, which is the module used to execute the query. The dashboard splitting path can start with metrics_enhanced_performance and route an error widget to discover, but the helper rejects the original metrics dataset. Thus an allowlisted widget with an explicit event.type:error query still returns raw sampled counts after being routed to the error query. Pass scoped_dataset to the eligibility check so routed queries receive the same upsampling behavior as direct queries.

title: Require an error-only filter instead of a substring match
body: The substring check also accepts queries such as `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. For allowlisted projects, these queries consequently have count() replaced with the error-only sample_weight aggregation even though they can select transactions, where sample_weight is unsupported. This can break valid Discover queries or return incorrect counts. Eligibility needs to establish from the parsed filter that every matching event is an error, accounting for negation and OR branches.

title: Apply upsampling to top-N selection, not just its time series
body: Only timeseries_columns are transformed; selected_columns and orderby still contain the original count() aggregation. A request grouping by issue and ordering by descending count therefore selects top issues by ingested event count but displays their upsampled counts. With varying sampling rates, an issue containing one event of weight 10 can be excluded in favor of an issue containing two events of weight 1. Transform the aggregation used for top-N selection as well so selection and displayed counts use the same measure.

title: Check the dataset actually used for split dashboard queries
body: The eligibility check receives the enclosing request's dataset rather than scoped_dataset. For a metrics-enhanced dashboard request whose widget is split to ERROR_EVENTS, get_event_stats_factory explicitly executes the query against Discover, but this check still sees the metrics dataset and always rejects upsampling. Even with allowlisted projects and an explicit event.type:error filter, that error chart returns raw sampled counts. Base eligibility on the dataset and effective query actually being executed.

title: Verify counting of unsampled historical errors
body: Both fixture events have client_sample_rate=0.1, so the tests only verify rows with explicit sampling metadata. Allowlisting a project also affects queries over its pre-rollout errors, which lack that metadata. The new aggregation directly sums sample_weight and relies on a schema-default assumption that these tests never verify. Add an allowlisted-project test with unsampled errors, including a mixture of sampled and unsampled rows, and assert that each unsampled error still contributes one to the count.

title: Count errors without sampling metadata as one
body: Allowlisting a project does not backfill sampling metadata into its historical errors, and ordinary errors without a sampling rate can have a null sample_weight. A bare sum(sample_weight) ignores those events, so an allowlisted project's historical or unsampled errors disappear from the reported count; a bucket containing only such errors returns zero. Default missing weights to 1 before summing, and cover mixed sampled and unsampled errors in the integration tests.

title: Require an actual error-only constraint instead of a substring match
body: Both '!event.type:error' and 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction' contain this substring and therefore enable upsampling when all projects are allowlisted, although neither query restricts results to errors. The endpoint then replaces count() with an error-weight aggregation for non-error events, producing incorrect totals or querying an unsupported field on the transaction dataset. Eligibility must follow the parsed query's constraints, including negation and OR branches.

title: Check eligibility against the dataset actually being queried
body: The eligibility check uses the outer dataset rather than scoped_dataset. For dashboard widgets using the metrics-enhanced Discover-splitting path, the error-only query executes against scoped_dataset=discover while the outer dataset remains a metrics dataset. The helper therefore always rejects upsampling for those error queries, even with allowlisted projects and an explicit event.type:error filter, leaving dashboard counts understated. Use the scoped dataset and effective query when deciding eligibility.

title: Apply upsampling to the top-N selection aggregates too
body: Only timeseries_columns are transformed; selected_columns still contains the request's regular count() aggregate. For a top-events request with field=count() and orderby=-count, the top groups are consequently selected by observed counts while their plotted series use weighted counts. For example, two unsampled events outrank one event with weight 10, excluding the group with the larger reported count. Transform the count aggregate used for top-N selection as well, preserving its ordering alias.

title: Pass the query results to the new table visualization
body: When an organization has `use-table-widget-visualization`, every table widget receives empty columns, empty data, and empty metadata instead of the fetched `result`. Consequently, enabling the feature makes populated dashboard tables appear empty. Wire the actual fields, rows, and metadata into the new visualization rather than substituting an empty table.

title: Normalize error and recording timestamps before merging
body: Stored Sentry error timestamps are Unix seconds, while rrweb recording events use Unix milliseconds. Comparing these values directly emits all contemporary errors before the first recording event, regardless of when they actually occurred. The generated error messages also send seconds alongside recording timestamps in milliseconds. Normalize both sources to the same units before comparison and serialization, and use millisecond recording timestamps in the regression tests.

title: Include the organization in the attribute query cache key
body: The new React Query key contains only request options, but the request URL depends on the organization. Two organizations using the all-projects selection and the same relative date range have identical keys. Switching organizations can therefore reuse the previous organization's custom attributes, and changing the query function alone does not reliably trigger a fetch. Include the organization slug in the key to isolate these cached results.

title: Escape issue titles before embedding them in Markdown links
body: Issue titles are now inserted directly inside Markdown link text. A normal title containing an unmatched closing bracket, such as `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ]`, prematurely closes the link text and prevents the issue URL from rendering as a link. Previously, the separate `View Issue` link remained usable regardless of the title. Escape Markdown delimiters in the truncated title before formatting the link, and cover bracket-containing titles in tests.

title: Respect falsy results from custom cell renderers
body: The custom-renderer contract specifies that `undefined` requests fallback rendering, but this truthiness check also falls back for valid React nodes such as `0`, an empty string, `false`, or `null`. For example, a renderer returning `null` to suppress a cell instead displays the underlying value. The header renderer has the same problem. Check explicitly for `undefined` rather than testing whether the result is truthy.

title: Allow valid non-HTTP document URLs in browser reports
body: A Reporting API report's URL identifies the reporting document and can validly be `about:blank` or a `blob:` URL, for example for a policy violation in an iframe inheriting its parent's policy. DRF's `URLField` uses Django's URL validator, which rejects these schemes. An otherwise valid report therefore causes the entire batch to return 422, losing metrics for every report in that batch. Validate against the Reporting API document-URL contract rather than the HTTP/FTP URL restriction.

title: Exercise null-segment deletion without mocking away the fix
body: The null-segment case is added to a test that patches `delete_matched_rows`, so it never reaches `_make_recording_filenames`, where a null maximum segment ID previously raised `TypeError`. This test would still pass if the new guard were removed. Add a regression test that executes the helper or deletion use case and verifies that a null-segment replay produces no recording filenames without failing.

title: Pass query results to the new table visualization
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, every table widget receives empty columns, empty metadata, and an empty data array instead of the query's `result`. Consequently, enabling the feature removes all headers and rows from otherwise populated dashboard tables. Wire the actual fields, metadata, and query results into the new visualization before replacing the existing table.

title: Include the organization in the attribute-key cache key
body: The new React Query key contains only filter options, while the request URL depends on `organization.slug`. Two organizations with the same date range and all-projects selection therefore share a cache entry despite querying different endpoints. Switching organizations can reuse the other organization's custom attribute names, and changing the query callback does not invalidate that entry. Include the organization slug or organization-scoped endpoint URL in the key.

title: Normalize timestamp units before merging errors and recording events
body: Nodestore error timestamps are Unix seconds, whereas rrweb recording event timestamps are Unix milliseconds. Comparing them directly makes virtually every error timestamp smaller than the first recording timestamp, so errors that occurred later in the replay are emitted before its first breadcrumb. This gives Seer incorrectly ordered context for summaries and chapters. Normalize both sources to the same unit; the new tests use second-scale recording timestamps and therefore miss this case.

title: Use a time window containing the replay for the error lookup
body: The AI tab's summary request supplies only the replay ID, but this new metadata query is bounded by `get_filter_params`' default date window. Retained replays older than that window can still have their recording segments fetched by ID, while the metadata query returns no rows. Their summaries therefore silently omit all error context. Derive the lookup window from the replay's timestamps or pass an appropriate replay-specific range from the client.

title: Accept the standard permissions-policy violation report type
body: The choices contain `permissions-policy`, but browsers emit Permissions Policy violation reports with type `permissions-policy-violation`. Unlike the previous type annotation, this new `ChoiceField` enforces the list at runtime, so valid browser reports now receive HTTP 422. A mixed batch containing such a report is also rejected before metrics are recorded for any report. Add the actual standardized report type to the accepted choices.

title: Honor falsy results from custom cell renderers
body: Both default-renderer wrappers use `if (cell)` to decide whether the custom renderer handled a cell. However, the documented fallback signal is `undefined`, and valid React results such as `0`, `null`, `false`, and an empty string are falsy. For example, a custom renderer returning `null` to leave a cell blank instead displays the original field value. Check explicitly for `undefined` in both the header and body wrappers.

title: Pass the query results to the new table visualization
body: When an organization has `use-table-widget-visualization` enabled, every dashboard table receives empty columns, empty data, and empty metadata instead of the fetched result. Consequently, tables display no results even when their queries return data. Wire the existing fields, result data, and metadata into this branch before enabling the replacement.

title: Include the organization in the attribute query cache key
body: The new query key contains only the query options, while the query function requests an organization-specific endpoint. Two organizations using All Projects and the same date range therefore share a cache entry. Switching organizations can retain the previous organization's attribute keys without triggering a new query because the key has not changed. Include the organization slug or endpoint path in the cache key.

title: Normalize timestamp units before merging errors and replay events
body: Error-event timestamps retrieved from nodestore are Unix seconds, whereas rrweb timestamps in recording segments are Unix milliseconds. Comparing these values directly drains all contemporary errors before the first replay event, including errors that actually occurred later in the recording. This supplies incorrect chronology to the summarizer. Convert both timestamps to the same unit before merging them.

title: Scope the feedback summary to the selected environments
body: The summary request includes the selected projects and date range but omits `selection.environments`. Changing the page's environment filter therefore changes neither the summary request nor its cache key. The summary displayed above a production-only feedback list can continue describing feedback from staging or other environments. Include the selected environments in the summary's filtering and cache key.

title: Use undefined rather than truthiness to select renderer fallbacks
body: Both the body and header helpers use `if (cell)` to decide whether to honor a custom renderer, although the documented contract reserves `undefined` for fallback. Valid React results such as `0`, an empty string, `false`, or `null` are consequently discarded. In particular, returning `null` to suppress a value still renders the original value. Check explicitly for `undefined` in both helpers.

title: Allow browser document URLs outside URLField's default schemes
body: DRF's `URLField` accepts only its default HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, and FTPS schemes, but a browser report's document URL can legitimately use schemes such as `about:` or `blob:`. For example, `about:blank` is rejected by this serializer. Since validation rejects the entire batch when one report fails, a valid report from such a document also prevents metrics from being recorded for the other reports in that batch. Validate against the Reporting API's URL contract rather than this restricted scheme list.

title: Escape issue titles before inserting them into Markdown links
body: Issue titles are now used directly as Markdown link labels without escaping. A title such as `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ]` prematurely closes the label and prevents the generated issue link from rendering correctly in GitHub and GitLab comments. Previously, the separate `View Issue` link remained valid regardless of title contents. Escape Markdown delimiters in the truncated title before formatting the link.

title: Enforce time-field presence instead of checking truthiness
body: The age/timestamp validators check the other field's truthiness rather than its presence, and both fields are optional. Thus a report containing both `age: 0` and `timestamp: 0`, or neither field, passes validation despite the intended mutually exclusive formats. Use object-level validation to require exactly one field and check key presence so zero values cannot bypass the contract.

title: Do not skip installer validation when the Integration row is missing
body: The Integration.DoesNotExist branch advances the pipeline before comparing the authenticated GitHub user with the installer. This can happen when the installation callback arrives before its webhook, or when webhook delivery fails. The subsequent build_integration call only fetches the installation using app credentials; it does not verify the authenticated user's relationship to it. Supplying another installation's ID in this state can therefore associate it with the current Sentry organization despite an installer mismatch. Apply the same validation on this path, or fail/retry until trusted installer metadata is available.

title: Compare immutable GitHub user IDs instead of usernames
body: The OAuth step stores the user's login, which GitHubInstallation compares with the webhook's sender.login snapshot. GitHub usernames can change, and old usernames can be claimed by other accounts. After an installer renames their account, the legitimate installer fails this check, while an unrelated account claiming the old name can pass it for an active, unlinked installation. Store and compare the immutable numeric user ID from the OAuth user response and webhook sender instead.

title: Handle existing integrations without sender metadata
body: An existing Integration is not guaranteed to contain sender metadata: build_integration only includes it when supplied in pipeline state, and the ordinary setup flow tested here produces metadata without it. If such an active Integration remains without an OrganizationIntegration, this new metadata['sender']['login'] access raises KeyError, turning a reconnect request into a server error. Missing sender data needs an explicit handled path that obtains trusted installer information or returns the installation-validation error.

title: Keep the missing-installation test exercising the GitHub 404 path
body: This test mocks the installation endpoint as returning 404 but now only asserts 'Invalid installation request.', which OAuth validation can return before that endpoint is reached. The production 404 handler is unchanged and still raises 'The GitHub installation could not be found.', so the replacement assertion allows an earlier callback rejection to satisfy the test without verifying its named behavior. Complete OAuth using the actual pipeline signature, verify that the installation endpoint was called, and retain the 404-specific error assertion.

title: Fail closed when the installation has no local Integration row
body: The Integration.DoesNotExist branch advances without comparing the OAuth user to the installation's sender. GitHub installation webhooks are asynchronous and can fail, so a valid installation can exist on GitHub without a local Integration row. An attacker authenticated with their own GitHub account can supply that installation ID and reach build_integration, which uses app credentials to fetch and attach it to the attacker's Sentry organization. Obtain trusted authorization data or reject the request when the local verification data is unavailable instead of skipping verification.

title: Compare immutable GitHub user IDs instead of logins
body: The authenticated identity stores only GitHub's login, which is subsequently compared with the login cached in the installation's sender metadata. GitHub usernames can change, and old usernames can be claimed by another account. After an installer renames their account, the legitimate installer fails verification while someone who acquires the former username can pass it and claim an unlinked installation. Store the authenticated user's immutable numeric ID and compare it with sender.id instead.

title: Handle installations without sender metadata
body: This comparison unconditionally accesses integration.metadata['sender']['login'], but build_integration only includes sender when it is present in pipeline state, and the new OAuth/UI flow never binds that state field. Consequently, active Integration records created through that flow can lack sender metadata. If such a record remains without an OrganizationIntegration, reconnecting it raises KeyError and produces a server error instead of the intended verification-failure page. Handle missing sender data explicitly and fail closed or recover trusted installer information.

title: Keep the missing-installation test on the GitHub 404 path
body: The GitHub-404 handling in build_integration is unchanged and still raises 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' This test now expects 'Invalid installation request.' instead, so a passing test validates an earlier OAuth rejection rather than the stubbed installation 404. The installation lookup can disappear entirely without this test detecting it. Use the state returned by the authorization redirect, assert that the installation request occurs, and retain the not-found message assertion to preserve coverage of the original error path.

title: Do not skip ownership validation when the Integration is missing
body: The Integration.DoesNotExist branch advances without checking the authenticated GitHub user's relationship to the installation. If the installation webhook has not yet created the local row, a caller can supply another user's installation ID and authenticate with any GitHub account. build_integration then retrieves that installation using app credentials and attaches it to the caller's Sentry organization. This leaves an ownership-check bypass, including a race with webhook delivery. Fail closed when trusted installer information is unavailable, or verify access using the authenticated user's GitHub credentials.

title: Compare immutable GitHub user IDs instead of login names
body: The authorization check compares the current OAuth login name with the historical sender.login stored by the installation webhook. GitHub usernames can be renamed and reused: after the installer changes their username, a different account can acquire the old name and pass this check for an unlinked installation despite having a different identity. The original installer would also be incorrectly rejected. Store and compare the immutable GitHub user ID returned by OAuth against sender.id.

title: Handle integrations without sender metadata
body: This lookup assumes every existing Integration contains metadata['sender']['login'], but build_integration only includes sender when it is present in pipeline state. Integrations created by the successful basic flow, including test_basic_flow, explicitly lack that metadata. If such an integration is later left without an OrganizationIntegration and reconnected, this branch raises KeyError and returns a server error instead of the intended installation-failed response. Handle absent installer metadata explicitly and fail closed or obtain trusted identity information.

title: Preserve coverage of GitHub installation lookup failures
body: The mocked installation endpoint returns 404, but this test now asserts 'Invalid installation request.', which is produced by earlier validation failures. The code handling the actual GitHub 404 still raises 'The GitHub installation could not be found.'. Consequently, the revised test no longer verifies that the installation endpoint is reached or that its 404 is handled correctly. Complete OAuth with valid state, retain the missing-installation assertion, and test invalid OAuth state separately.

title: Create the queued timestamp for each assignment
body: `timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, so every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` value receives the same timestamp. In a long-lived worker, assignments received hours later therefore carry the module-import time in their serialized context rather than their actual creation time. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to generate the timestamp for each instance.

title: Compute the queued timestamp for each assignment source
body: `timezone.now()` is evaluated when the module is imported, so every `AssignmentSource.from_integration()` call in a worker reuses that timestamp. Consequently, outbound tasks serialize the module-import time as `queued`, even for assignments received hours or days later. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each source records its own creation time.

title: Create the queued timestamp per AssignmentSource instance
body: `timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, rather than when an `AssignmentSource` is created. Consequently, every inbound assignment handled by the same process serializes the same startup-time `queued` value, even hours or days later. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to record each assignment's creation time.

title: Keep the registered metric-alert handler instantiable
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits abstract methods from StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of them, so it cannot be instantiated. Accessing Detector.detector_handler for the registered `metric_alert_fire` type now raises TypeError instead of returning the previous no-op handler. process_detectors does not catch that exception, so including such a detector aborts packet processing. Implement the required hooks or retain a concrete no-op handler until the stateful implementation is ready.

title: Build the expected occurrence for the group key being evaluated
body: The expected occurrence in test_dedupe is built for `val1`, while the subsequent evaluate_group_key_value call evaluates `group_key`. The helper includes this key in the occurrence fingerprint, so the expected fingerprint is `<detector_id>:val1` while the actual fingerprint is `<detector_id>:group_key`. The result comparison therefore fails for a correct implementation. Build the expected occurrence using `group_key` as well.

title: Metric alert handler can no longer be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits abstract methods from StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of them: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data remain abstract. Accessing detector_handler on a Detector with type="metric_alert_fire" therefore raises TypeError when the model instantiates the registered handler, causing process_detectors to abort instead of returning the previous empty evaluation. Keep this handler concrete until its stateful implementation is available.

title: Expected occurrence uses the wrong group key in the dedupe test
body: This test builds its expected occurrence for group key "val1", but the subsequent evaluate_group_key_value call evaluates "group_key". The mock handler builds occurrence fingerprints from that argument, so the expected occurrence has fingerprint "<detector_id>:val1" while the actual occurrence has "<detector_id>:group_key". The result equality assertion therefore fails before the test reaches its deduplication check. Build the expected occurrence using "group_key".

title: The registered metric-alert handler is now abstract
body: StatefulDetectorHandler requires counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data, but this subclass implements none of them. Detector.detector_handler unconditionally instantiates the registered handler, so a detector with type metric_alert_fire now raises TypeError and aborts process_detectors instead of returning the previous empty evaluation. Keep the stub concrete until these methods are implemented, or prevent the abstract handler from being instantiated.

title: The dedupe test builds its expected occurrence for the wrong group
body: The expected occurrence is built with group key "val1", but the subsequent evaluate_group_key_value call uses "group_key". build_mock_occurrence_and_event includes that key in the occurrence fingerprint, so the expected fingerprint is "<detector_id>:val1" while the actual fingerprint is "<detector_id>:group_key". The first result equality assertion therefore fails before the test reaches its duplicate-packet check. Build the expected occurrence with "group_key".

title: Spawned flusher processes fail the process type check
body: The spawn context creates multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess instances, which inherit BaseProcess rather than multiprocessing.Process. This isinstance check is therefore false for production flushers, so a hung worker is never killed before its handle is overwritten by the replacement. If the old worker recovers, both workers operate on the same shards and share heartbeat/backpressure state, undermining hang detection and leaving an untracked worker. Check against BaseProcess or explicitly distinguish threading.Thread instead. The termination check in join has the same type mismatch.

title: Terminate remaining workers after the join deadline expires
body: When the deadline is consumed by next_step.join or by waiting for an earlier worker, this break skips shutdown handling for every remaining worker. Setting stopped is cooperative: a worker blocked in Redis or Kafka future.result() cannot observe it and can survive join and the subsequent partition rebalance. Exhausting the timeout should stop waiting, but all remaining processes still need to be terminated and reaped rather than skipped.

title: Spawned workers are never killed before restart
body: Workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process are SpawnProcess instances, not instances of the multiprocessing.Process wrapper, so this check is false for production workers. When a worker hangs, the watchdog starts a replacement without killing the original. Repeated stalls accumulate untracked workers beyond max_processes, and a stalled worker that resumes can flush the same shards concurrently with its replacement. The identical check in join() also skips termination. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or explicitly distinguish threads instead.

title: An expired join deadline skips cleanup of remaining workers
body: If next_step.join() or waiting for an earlier worker consumes the timeout, this break exits the loop without terminating any remaining workers. Setting stopped is insufficient for workers blocked in Redis calls or Kafka futures, because they only inspect that flag between flush cycles. Such workers can outlive the strategy and accumulate across rebalances. The deadline should limit waiting, but cleanup must still attempt to terminate every remaining process.

title: The added flusher synchronization sleep is a no-op
body: test_basic replaces time.sleep with a no-op at the start, so this newly added time.sleep(0.1) does not actually wait for the background flusher. poll() does not wait for that worker either, and the following join() sets its stopped flag. Depending on scheduling, the worker can stop before producing the expected message, leaving messages empty and failing the tuple unpack. Synchronize on message production or use an unpatched wait with a bounded timeout.

title: The process type check prevents hung spawned workers from being killed
body: Workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process are SpawnProcess instances, not instances of multiprocessing.Process, so this check is false for every production worker. When a worker hangs, the manager starts its replacement without killing the original. Repeated restarts leak child processes, and an original worker that resumes can flush concurrently with its replacement. Use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or explicitly distinguish processes from test threads. The same incorrect check also prevents termination in join().

title: Do not skip worker cleanup when the join deadline expires
body: The deadline check breaks out of the entire worker loop. If next_step.join() consumes the timeout, no workers are cleaned up; if the first worker consumes it, all remaining workers are skipped. Setting stopped only requests cooperative shutdown and cannot stop a worker blocked in Redis or a Kafka delivery future. Such workers survive join() and can accumulate across rebalances. Regardless of the waiting deadline, perform termination cleanup for every worker.

title: The added flusher synchronization sleep is patched into a no-op
body: This test replaces time.sleep with a no-op at line 15, which also replaces this newly added time.sleep(0.1) call. Consequently, it does not wait for the background flusher to observe the drift change or produce a message. step.join() then sets the flusher's stopped flag, so the expected message can be missed depending on thread scheduling. Synchronize on production of the expected message using an event or another unpatched waiting mechanism before shutting down the flusher.

title: Do not reuse a queue pool after its strategy closes
body: The factory creates one queue pool and reuses it for every create_with_partitions() call, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() permanently shuts down that pool's queues and workers. After a partition reassignment, the replacement strategy therefore receives an already-shut-down pool. Queue submissions raise queue.ShutDown, which submit() catches and treats as completed work, allowing offsets to be committed without processing their results. Give each strategy a fresh pool and offset tracker, or implement an assignment-safe reusable pool lifecycle.

title: Bound outstanding work and apply consumer backpressure
body: queue.Queue() has no size limit, and submit() always accepts another message without rejecting or throttling intake. If processing is slower than Kafka consumption, or one worker gets stuck on the slow item this change targets, queued messages and retained offset-tracking state grow without bound until the consumer runs out of memory. Bound total outstanding work and use Arroyo's backpressure mechanism rather than continuing to accept messages indefinitely.

title: Drain workers and flush offsets before completing shutdown
body: close() stops the commit thread before shutting down workers, and pool.shutdown() sets each worker's shutdown flag before its queue is drained. join() merely calls close() again. Accepted queued work is consequently abandoned, work finishing after the last commit is replayed, and a slow worker can remain alive after its fixed five-second join timeout. On partition revocation, that worker can continue processing concurrently with the new partition owner. Graceful close/join must drain accepted work, respect the supplied timeout, and flush final offsets before declaring the strategy finished.

title: Do not make failed worker items automatically committable
body: complete_offset() runs in finally even when result_processor raises. For example, if offset 100 fails and offset 101 succeeds, the commit loop can acknowledge both and advance Kafka to 102, permanently skipping the failed result. This contradicts the strategy's successful-processing guarantee and the new error-handling test's no-commit assertion; that test normally checks before the one-second commit interval elapses. Failed work needs an explicit retry, skip, or DLQ disposition rather than automatically being marked completed.

title: Compute safe commits from delivered offsets rather than integer adjacency
body: Kafka offsets can legitimately have holes, such as those left by transaction control records or compaction. This loop stops at every absent integer even when all delivered messages have completed. With completed offsets 0, 2, 4, and so on, it commits only one message per one-second commit iteration: mark_committed() removes the previous prefix, then the next iteration reaches only the next gap. This severely delays checkpoints and retains completed offsets unnecessarily. Determine the safe boundary from delivered and outstanding offsets, without requiring numerical contiguity.

title: Reject non-positive queue worker counts
body: The CLI accepts any integer for --max-workers, and a negative value passes through this expression unchanged. FixedQueuePool then creates no queues or workers because range(num_queues) is empty. Every decoded message fails queue lookup, but the strategy catches that failure and marks its offset completed, so a configuration such as --max-workers=-1 silently acknowledges all results without processing them. Validate that the configured queue count is positive and fail startup for invalid values.

title: Close the strategy during test cleanup
body: factory.shutdown() stops queue workers but does not set the created strategy's shutdown_event. The strategy's commit_thread therefore continues running forever after this test, retaining its pool and callbacks. The new uptime tests use the same cleanup pattern and leak additional commit threads. Register strategy.close() or terminate() in guaranteed cleanup so background threads cannot outlive the tests.

title: Synchronize workers before asserting a nonempty queue
body: The worker threads process submitted items immediately, so all ten items can be consumed before get_stats() runs. A zero queue depth is valid at this point, making the total_items > 0 assertion scheduling-dependent and capable of failing in CI. Block processing with an event until the initial statistics assertion is complete, or assert properties that remain valid after workers have drained the queues.

title: Invoke the commit callback on the consumer thread
body: This invokes the Commit callback supplied by StreamProcessor from commit_thread, concurrently with consumer polling, partition callbacks, and shutdown. Arroyo's processor and consumer offset bookkeeping are not synchronized for this concurrent use, so committing can race changes to partition assignments or consumer closure. Exceptions are only logged here rather than surfaced to the processor. Workers should record completions, while poll/join publish those offsets on the processor thread.

title: Do not reuse a queue pool after its strategy shuts it down
body: The factory constructs one queue_pool and passes it to every strategy, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close shuts that pool down. Arroyo recreates strategies when partition assignments change, so the strategy created after the first rebalance receives stopped workers and shutdown queues. Queue submission then raises ShutDown, which submit catches and marks complete, allowing valid results to be committed without processing. Create a fresh pool and offset tracker for each strategy lifecycle, or implement safe reuse.

title: Bound the queues and implement backpressure
body: queue.Queue() has no capacity limit, and submit always accepts messages without checking backlog. If processing is slower than Kafka consumption—or one worker stalls—the consumer continues retaining decoded results, original payloads, and tracked offsets indefinitely. Unlike the existing bounded batch processing, this can exhaust memory instead of leaving the backlog in Kafka. Use bounded queues and nonblocking MessageRejected handling when capacity is exhausted.

title: Do not mark failed processing as completed
body: An exception escaping result_processor is logged, but the finally block still completes that item's offset. The commit loop can therefore advance past a result that was never successfully processed, permanently skipping it on restart. The exception handler in submit similarly completes messages that failed to be queued. Preserve or surface these failures rather than treating them as successful completion. The new error-handling test checks before the one-second commit interval, so it does not detect this behavior.

title: Drain accepted work and flush offsets before closing
body: close stops the commit thread before workers finish, and pool.shutdown sets every worker's shutdown flag before queued work is drained. Consequently, accepted messages remain unprocessed and work completed during shutdown has no final commit. Workers exceeding the fixed five-second join can also continue after close/join returns, racing a replacement partition owner. Implement close/join so accepted work drains within the requested timeout, completion offsets are flushed, and workers cannot outlive a successful join.

title: Control worker execution before asserting a nonempty queue
body: The workers run immediately and the test processor only appends to a list. They can process all ten submissions before get_stats executes, making total_items zero even when the pool works correctly. This introduces a scheduling-dependent test failure. Hold workers on an event until the queue-depth assertions finish, then release them and verify completion.

title: Do not reuse a shut-down queue pool after a rebalance
body: Every strategy created by this factory shares self.queue_pool, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() shuts that pool down. Arroyo closes and recreates processing strategies during partition rebalances, so the replacement strategy receives exited workers and shut-down queues. Enqueuing then raises, and submit() marks those failed submissions complete, allowing offsets to advance without processing their results. Create a fresh pool and offset tracker for each strategy, or implement a safe lifecycle that keeps the shared pool usable across strategy replacements.

title: Do not mark failed processing as completed
body: complete_offset() runs in finally even when result_processor raises. If processing offset 100 fails and offset 101 succeeds, both become committable and the factory commits Kafka offset 102, permanently skipping the failed result without retrying it or sending it to a DLQ. Failed processing must remain outstanding until an explicit recovery or discard policy handles it. The new error-handling test misses this because it checks before the one-second commit loop runs.

title: Bound outstanding work and apply backpressure
body: queue.Queue() is unbounded by default, and submit() always accepts messages without signalling backpressure to Arroyo. If a worker stalls or ingestion exceeds processing capacity, the consumer continues reading Kafka and retaining every queued payload. A stalled early offset also keeps later completed offsets in OffsetTracker indefinitely. This can exhaust consumer memory rather than merely backlog Kafka. Add a finite total in-flight limit and reject submissions when that limit is reached.

title: Drain accepted work and flush offsets during graceful shutdown
body: close() stops and joins the commit thread before workers finish. It then calls pool.shutdown(), which sets worker.shutdown=True, causing workers to exit after their current item rather than drain queued work despite shutdown(immediate=False). Consequently, graceful join can return with accepted messages unprocessed, and results completed during worker shutdown are never committed. A normal shutdown or rebalance therefore unnecessarily replays successfully handled results. Stop accepting submissions first, drain accepted work in join(), and flush the final committable offsets afterward.

title: Honor the processing strategy's join timeout
body: join(timeout) ignores its timeout and calls close(), which waits up to five seconds for each worker separately. With the default twenty queues and stalled handlers, worker joins alone can take about 100 seconds even for join(timeout=0). close() also performs these blocking waits before Arroyo can apply its configured join timeout. This defeats the shutdown/rebalance deadline. Keep close() non-blocking and enforce one shared deadline across worker joins.

title: Reject negative worker counts before starting consumption
body: The CLI accepts any integer for --max-workers, so --max-workers=-1 reaches FixedQueuePool as num_queues=-1. range(-1) creates no queues or workers, and every submission subsequently raises IndexError. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy catches that error and marks the message complete, so offsets are committed while all results are discarded. Validate that the configured queue count is positive before creating the pool.

title: Synchronize workers before asserting a nonempty queue
body: The worker threads are already running and the test processor returns immediately. All ten items can legitimately be consumed before get_stats() executes, making total_items zero and failing this assertion even though the implementation behaved correctly. Hold the processors behind an event while checking queue depth, then release them to verify completion.

title: Do not require randomized hashes to populate every queue
body: Python string hashes are randomized between interpreter runs. Hashing twenty fixed group keys modulo three does not guarantee that all three queue indices occur; a valid hash seed can place every key in only two queues and fail this test. Verify distribution with controlled hashing or explicitly selected keys instead of asserting full coverage from a probabilistic sample.

title: Backup code login can skip the password
body: Password verification only runs when `user.password && !credentials.totpCode`. The new branch then accepts a backup code whenever `credentials.backupCode` is non-empty and never checks the password itself. The login UI clears `totpCode` before submitting a backup code so the password gate runs, but the credentials callback does not enforce that pairing. A caller who knows a backup code can send the victim's email, any non-empty `totpCode`, and that backup code and receive a session without the password. Backup codes are long-lived and typically stored in a downloaded text file, so this makes them a single factor rather than a replacement for the authenticator. Disable 2FA already requires the password independently of the second factor; login should do the same before accepting a backup code.

title: Consuming a backup code is a lost update
body: A valid backup code is invalidated by reading the decrypted list, setting that index to null, and writing the whole blob back with a plain `user.update`. There is no transaction, row lock, or compare-and-swap on the previous ciphertext. Two overlapping logins (double submit, retry, or two devices) both read the same list. If they use the same code, both pass `indexOf` before either write and both sessions are created, so the code is not single-use. If they use different codes, the later write restores the code the earlier request nulled, so a spent code works again. Consumption needs to be serialized, for example by locking the user row and updating only if `backupCodes` is still the value that was read.

title: Dismissing the codes dialog loses the only copy
body: After TOTP enable succeeds, the modal only advances to DisplayBackupCodes; `onEnable()` runs solely from the Close button. The dialog is still closed through `onOpenChange` (Escape, overlay, header close), which does not call `onEnable()` or `resetState()`. Codes are returned once from setup and kept only in component state. Setup refuses to run again once `twoFactorEnabled` is true, and nothing in this PR can list or regenerate them. Dismissing the dialog therefore drops the only display of the codes and can leave the settings page thinking 2FA is still off, so a later enable attempt hits TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled. The new `missing_backup_codes` string says to generate codes in settings, but no such screen exists, including for users who enabled 2FA before this column was added and have null `backupCodes`.

title: Backup-code download click does not reliably download
body: The download action is a `<Button>` nested inside `<a download href={backupCodesUrl}>`, which is invalid HTML (interactive content inside an anchor). The button handles the click, so the anchor's download navigation often never runs and `cal-backup-codes.txt` is not saved. Unlike the Copy and Close buttons in the same footer, this control also does not call `preventDefault`. It sits inside the enable `<Form>`, so if the button submits, the click re-invokes `handleEnable` with the already-used TOTP code instead of downloading. The new e2e test waits on a download from that test id and will fail or flake for the same reason.

title: OAuth/SAML second-factor screen cannot use backup codes
body: Lost access is only rendered in `TwoFactorFooter`. When login is reached with a `totp` query JWT (`totpEmail` set), the footer is `ExternalTotpFooter`, which is only Cancel, so those users never see the backup-code field. That is the path `loginWithTotp` uses after Google/SAML sign-in for an account with `twoFactorEnabled` (including CAL users whose password was cleared when the identity provider was linked). Even a direct credentials call with only a backup code fails first: `authorize` throws `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` when `identityProvider !== CAL` and `totpCode` is empty, before the backup-code branch. Those users still cannot get in with a backup code if they lose the authenticator.

title: Copy toast reports success even when clipboard write fails
body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` is not awaited and has no catch, and `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` runs immediately. `writeText` rejects when clipboard permission is denied or the page is not allowed to write the clipboard, which is common in embedded or non-secure contexts. The user is told the codes were copied, then Close is the path that finishes setup. Because codes cannot be fetched again after 2FA is enabled, a failed copy plus close leaves them with no saved codes. The e2e test only waits for `toast-success`, so it passes even when nothing was copied.

title: Backup code match does not normalize case or whitespace
body: Stored codes are lowercase hex from `randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, shown as `xxxxx-xxxxx`. Login and disable only do `replaceAll("-", "")` and then `indexOf`, so they are case-sensitive and do not trim. The backup-code input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`, which tells users to type uppercase. A code typed that way, or pasted with a trailing newline or space from the downloaded file, does not match and is rejected as incorrect even though it is the right code. The same comparison is in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` around the `replaceAll` call, so disable has the same failure.

title: Tests never log in with a backup code, and enable flow is unfinished
body: The new step shows backup codes and does not call `onEnable()` until Close, but the "enable 2FA and login using 2FA" test never clicks `backup-codes-close`. It still asserts the switch via `locator.isChecked()`, which this PR notes passes even when the switch is not checked, so the test can stay green if the post-enable UI never updates. The other test only checks download filename, a success toast, and close. Nothing submits a backup code at login, checks that a used code is rejected, or disables 2FA with a backup code. The file's own TODO calls that out, and the PR checklist says tests that prove the feature were not added. The password-skip and single-use bugs above would not be caught.

title: Backup code login can skip the password
body: The new backup-code branch in credentials authorize never checks the password. Password verification only runs when `credentials.totpCode` is empty (`if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` above this branch). A request that includes any non-empty `totpCode` (it does not have to be a valid authenticator code) plus a valid `backupCode` therefore skips both the password check and the TOTP check and is logged in. The same `totpCode` flag also bypasses the non-CAL identity-provider rejection. Backup codes are long-lived secrets users download as a text file; with this hole, that file alone is enough for account takeover, including for accounts that were later linked to Google/SAML. The branch must verify the password (for any user that has one) itself, and must not treat a dummy `totpCode` as proof of the first factor.

title: Backup code consumption is not atomic
body: After a matching backup code is found, the handler sets that slot to null and writes the whole encrypted list back with a plain `user.update`. Two concurrent authorize calls can both read the same ciphertext, both observe the code as unused, and both return a successful login. If the requests use two different codes, the later write restores the code the earlier request already consumed, so a one-time code stays valid. Disable can race the same way: a login that read the user before disable completes will write `backupCodes` back after disable nulled them. Consume the code with a conditional update (transaction/`SELECT FOR UPDATE`, or update only where the stored ciphertext is still the value that was read) and retry or fail if the row changed.

title: Backup code match is case-sensitive and not trimmed
body: Stored codes are lowercase hex from `randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, but login accepts a code only after `replaceAll("-", "")` and a strict `indexOf`. The entry placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`, and people commonly type or transcribe backup codes in uppercase or with spaces. Those inputs fail the match and the user is told the code is incorrect even though it is one of the codes they were shown. The same comparison is copied in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` at the `indexOf` on the submitted backup code, so disabling 2FA with a backup code has the same false rejection. Normalize by lowercasing and stripping every non-hex character before comparing.

title: Backup codes can be dismissed forever after 2FA is already on
body: 2FA is enabled on the server before the backup-code step is shown, and the plaintext codes exist only in this modal's state. `onEnable` (which is what the parent uses to refresh the switch and close the flow) runs only from the Close button. `onOpenChange` is passed straight through to `Dialog` and is not blocked on this step, and Cancel is hidden here, so Escape, overlay click, or the dialog close control dismisses the only view of the codes without calling `onEnable`. There is no later screen to reveal or regenerate codes (existing users with a null `backupCodes` column are told to generate them in settings, which this PR does not add). The user can end up with 2FA on, a settings switch still showing off, and no saved backup codes. Keep the dialog from closing until the user confirms they stored the codes, and call the same completion path as Close.

title: Copy reports success even when clipboard write fails
body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is not awaited and has no `.catch`, but `showToast(..., "success")` runs immediately. If the clipboard API rejects (permissions policy, insecure context, denied prompt), the user still sees "Backup codes copied!" and an unhandled rejection is thrown. Because this screen is the only time the codes are shown, a false success followed by Close leaves them with no codes. Await the write and show the success toast only after it resolves; surface a failure toast otherwise.

title: Tests never log in or disable 2FA with a backup code
body: The new coverage only clicks download, copy, and close on the setup dialog. Download checks the filename but not the file contents, and copy only waits for the success toast, which is shown even when `clipboard.writeText` fails, so a broken copy still passes. Nothing submits a backup code to credentials authorize or to `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable`, which is the path that can skip the password and that burns codes. The other enable test in this file was not updated to dismiss the new backup-code step at all, and its switch assertion is the one the new comment says passes even when the switch is unchecked, so CI will not catch a setup flow that never finishes. Add a login (and disable) that uses a code from the encrypted `backupCodes` column, including a second use of the same code that must fail.

title: Missing-backup-codes message points at a flow that does not exist
body: `missing_backup_codes` tells the user "Please generate them in your settings." This PR never adds a regenerate action. Users who enabled 2FA before the migration have `backupCodes` null, and the only way to get codes is to disable 2FA with the authenticator and set it up again. Lost-access login and disable will show this string and send them looking for a control that is not there. The copy should describe that actual recovery path (or the UI should grow a real regenerate action before the string ships).

title: Backup code plus any TOTP value skips the password
body: In the credentials authorize() path, the password is verified only when credentials.totpCode is falsy (the existing check around the password branch). The new branch then accepts a backup code whenever credentials.backupCode is non-empty and never checks the TOTP value. A caller who knows only the email and one backup code can therefore sign in by also sending any non-empty totpCode (for example "000000") and omitting or faking the password. That makes a long-lived backup code a single factor and a full account takeover secret, instead of password plus backup code. The login UI happens to send an empty totpCode, but the public credentials endpoint does not. Password verification must run for CAL users on this path, and a dummy totpCode must not select the backup-code branch.

title: Backup-code consumption is a lost-update race
body: A matching backup code is marked used by reading the decrypted array, setting that index to null, and writing the whole blob back with a plain user update. Two overlapping logins can both read the same array before either write. If they present the same code, both pass the check and both sessions are created, so a one-time code works twice. If they present different codes, the later write overwrites the earlier one, so one consumed code is restored and can be reused. The update needs to be conditional on the previous ciphertext (or done under a row lock) so a stale write cannot resurrect a used code.

title: Backup codes are compared case-sensitively
body: Stored codes are lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")), but the login check uses indexOf on the raw string after only stripping "-". The same comparison is in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts around the backupCode.replaceAll call. The login field placeholder is "XXXXX-XXXXX", so a user who types the code in the casing the UI shows is rejected with incorrect backup code even though the code is valid. Normalize by trimming and lowercasing before compare on both login and disable.

title: Backup codes are lost if the dialog is dismissed
body: After TOTP enable succeeds, the only copy of the plaintext backup codes lives in this modal, and onEnable() runs only from the Close button. The Dialog is still wired to the parent's onOpenChange, so Escape, overlay click, or the dialog close control hides it without onEnable() and without any warning that the codes cannot be shown again. There is no later API to reveal or regenerate codes while 2FA stays on, and a refresh on this step drops them too. The settings switch can also stay off because the parent is never told enable finished, so the user is left with 2FA on server-side, no saved codes, and a UI that still looks disabled. This step should block dismiss until the user explicitly finishes, and that path must call onEnable().

title: Download control submits the enable form
body: The backup-code footer is inside the Form whose submit handler is handleEnable. Copy and Close call preventDefault because a click otherwise submits that form; the Download control does not, and its Button has no type="button". It is also wrapped in an anchor. Activating Download therefore posts the TOTP enable request again (which can error once 2FA is already on, or replace the page) and can cancel the file download, so the main way to save codes fails. Set type="button" and preventDefault, or render a non-submitting link.

title: Lost access button submits the disable form
body: The new Lost access / Go back button sits inside the disable Form and does not set type="button" or preventDefault. The enable modal in this same change had to preventDefault on footer buttons for that reason. Clicking Lost access therefore submits handleDisable with an empty code at the same time as it toggles the backup-code field, so the user gets an incorrect-code or second-factor error instead of a clean switch to the backup-code input. Stop the click from submitting.

title: Missing-backup-codes copy points at a screen that does not exist
body: missing_backup_codes says "Please generate them in your settings." Nothing in this PR adds a settings action to generate or rotate backup codes after 2FA is already on; setup refuses when twoFactorEnabled is true, and existing users who enabled 2FA before the migration have a null backupCodes column. Shown at login or when disabling 2FA, the message tells a locked-out user to do something they cannot do. The string should say that codes are only issued during 2FA setup and that an account with none cannot use this fallback.

title: No test covers backup-code login or single use
body: The new login and disable-with-backup-code paths are untested. The file's own TODO calls out login and disabling 2FA with a backup code, and the checklist says no test proves the feature. The enable test never clicks backup-codes-close or asserts the codes, and the other test only checks the download filename and that a toast appears, not the file contents, clipboard text, a successful backup-code sign-in, or that a used code is rejected. Those gaps would miss the password bypass, case-sensitive compare, and non-atomic consumption bugs.

title: Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty
body: create() now does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining.
