If location is Google Meet and destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or [], mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and this throws TypeError before any video or calendar event is created, so the booking request fails. Previously `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` was used, which fell back to Cal Video instead of crashing. The same check only looks at index 0, so a collective event whose first destination is not Google Calendar is forced off Meet even when a later destination is Google.

title: Video booking references no longer store credentialId
body: In create(), referencesToCreate now sets credentialId only for calendar results (`isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`). Video results previously kept result.credentialId. handleCancelBooking deletes the meeting only when bookingVideoReference.credentialId is set and looks that credential up; with credentialId always omitted, cancelling a new booking never calls deleteMeeting, so Zoom/Daily/Meet links stay live after cancel. updateLocation() still copies result.credentialId, so only the initial create path is broken.

title: Per-host calendar create still uses only the first destination
body: createAllCalendarEvents loops every destination and calls createEvent with that destination's credential, but it passes the full event whose destinationCalendar array still starts with the organizer. Office 365 (CalendarService.ts createEvent around the eventsUrl built from destinationCalendar[0]), Lark (calendarId from destinationCalendar[0]), and CalDAV (BaseCalendarService filters to destinationCalendar[0].externalId) therefore run host 2's token against host 1's calendar id. Graph/Lark return 404 or throw, and CalDAV's filter can match nothing yet still return a successful NewCalendarEventType, so a booking reference is stored for an event that was never created. Google insert does look up by credentialId, but the organizer attendee email is still destinationCalendar[0].externalId (Google CalendarService.ts around the mainHostDestinationCalendar email), so a co-host event is created with another host marked organizer:true and Google can reject the insert. The no-credentialId branch (createEvent without externalId) never matches that lookup and silently writes to the Google primary calendar instead of the configured externalId, and can do so once per credential of that integration.

title: Collective co-host calendars dropped when organizer has none
body: evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when both eventType.destinationCalendar and organizerUser.destinationCalendar are missing, and the collective branch then does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). Optional push on null is a no-op, so every co-host destination calendar collected above is discarded. createAllCalendarEvents then takes the empty/null path and its fallback filters credentials with type === "calendar", which never matches google_calendar/office365_calendar/etc. A collective booking whose first host has no destination calendar creates no host calendar events at all, which is the case this PR is meant to fix.

title: Only the first destination calendar is stored on the booking
body: The booking create connects only evt.destinationCalendar[0]. Booking.destinationCalendar is a single relation, and confirm.handler, the Stripe and PayPal payment webhooks, edit location, and the booking reminder all rebuild CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar from that one row (or the organizer user row) wrapped in an array. Those paths call EventManager.create/update. Collective bookings that defer calendar creation until confirmation or payment therefore never see co-host destination calendars, so only the organizer gets a calendar event. The in-memory array built for the initial request is not recoverable later.

title: Google update/delete fallback can never resolve a calendar id
body: updateEvent and deleteEvent now do `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When externalCalendarId is null or omitted, the find compares every calendar to that same falsy value and never matches, so selectedCalendar/calendarId is undefined. Previously this fell back to destinationCalendar.externalId. updateEvent then calls Google with calendarId undefined and the reschedule/update fails; deleteEvent falls through to "primary" and leaves the event on a non-primary calendar. CalendarManager.deleteEvent still calls deleteEvent(uid, event) without an external id, and any booking reference with a null externalCalendarId hits this path. The hangout description patch in createEvent also uses selectedCalendar with no "primary" fallback after insert used `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, so a Meet event written to primary never gets the hangout link written back.

title: Cancelling remaining recurring bookings does not delete each host calendar event
body: The new per-reference loop wraps the recurring allRemainingBookings branch unchanged. For every calendar reference that has a credentialId, that branch ignores the reference just fetched and instead walks every organizer calendar credential and, for each remaining instance, references.find() of the first _calendar ref only, then deleteEvent on that uid. Co-host references are never selected, so their recurring events stay on the calendar. The same first event is deleted once per outer reference times every organizer calendar credential, and the credential loaded for the current reference is unused. Non-recurring cancel correctly deletes each reference with its own credential; recurring cancel does not.

title: Organization slug assignment condition was inverted
body: Unrelated to destination calendars, the org create payload changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. Previously a slug was written when team billing was disabled, and only requestedSlug was stored when billing was enabled. Now billing-disabled instances create organizations with no slug (org URLs break), and billing-enabled instances set slug immediately as well as requestedSlug, skipping the flow that waits to assign the slug. The requestedSlug ternary next to it is behavior-preserving; the slug line dropped the negation.

title: updateAllCalendarEvents calls updateEvent with a missing credential
body: When a calendar reference has a credentialId that is not on the EventManager user, the code loads it from the DB, but if that lookup misses (deleted credential, or app.slug absent so the rebuild is skipped) it still pushes updateEvent(credential, ...) with credential undefined. getCalendar then throws on credential.type. That rejection fails Promise.all for every calendar reference in the batch, and the catch returns synthetic failures and no longer console.errors the message it builds, so a reschedule/location update can report total failure after partially applying. createAllCalendarEvents correctly skips a missing credential; this path does not.

title: Seat-merge reschedule deletes only one old calendar event
body: When newBookingId is set, updateAllCalendarEvents still does booking.references.find() for a single _calendar reference and deletes only that uid. Collective bookings now store one calendar reference per host. Merging a seated booking onto an existing slot therefore removes one host's old event and leaves the other hosts' events at the old time.

title: Request-reschedule does not delete co-host calendar events
body: Calendar cleanup builds credentialsMap from getUsersCredentials(user.id) keyed only by credential.type, then deleteEvent uses credentialsMap.get(bookingRef.type). Collective bookings now have one calendar reference per host, often the same type (google_calendar) but different credentialIds. The map keeps a single credential for that type, and co-host credential ids on the references are ignored, so co-host events are deleted with the requesting user's token (Google 404) and remain on the co-host calendar. handleCancelBooking was updated to load credentialId from the DB; this path was not.

title: Webhook destinationCalendar shape is a breaking, inconsistent change
body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from a single DestinationCalendar | null to an array, and that object is spread into BOOKING_CREATED / BOOKING_CANCELLED / BOOKING_REJECTED webhook payloads. Consumers reading payload.destinationCalendar.externalId or .integration will break; the PR is marked non-breaking and does not version the payload. Emitters also disagree on the empty value: handleNewBooking still assigns null, while confirm, cancel, payment webhooks, and the rejected webhook e2e expectation use []. BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED tests still expect null, so clients cannot rely on one empty shape either.

title: Last calendar result overwrites evt.iCalUID
body: While building references, every calendar result assigns evt.iCalUID = result.iCalUID. createAllCalendarEvents now returns one result per host calendar, and each Google insert has its own iCalUID. The assignment keeps only the last host's UID on the shared event object that callers use for confirmation emails and ICS. Attendee clients can then fail to match the organizer's event. The UID is also not fed into later createEvent calls, so the host events are not correlated with each other either.

title: No test covers multi-host destination calendars
body: The PR checklist says no tests were added. Nothing covers createAllCalendarEvents with two destination calendars, the Google Meet empty-array crash, co-host calendars when the organizer destination is null, video reference credentialId, recurring cancel of multiple calendar references, or the webhook payload shape. The only e2e edit changes BOOKING_REJECTED destinationCalendar from null to [] and would not catch these regressions.

title: Google Meet fallback crashes when destination calendar is missing
body: The Meet-to-Cal-Video fallback now does `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` after destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`. If the array is missing or empty, that value is undefined and this throws TypeError before the booking is created. Previously this was optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`), so a Meet event with no destination calendar fell back to Daily. Callers in this PR (confirm, Stripe/PayPal webhooks, reminders) explicitly pass `[]` when no calendar is set, so those Meet bookings will 500 instead of being scheduled.

title: Video booking references lose credentialId
body: referencesToCreate now sets `credentialId` only for calendar results and forces `undefined` for every other result. The previous code stored `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results. Video meeting references are therefore saved without the credential that created them. Cancellation only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set and matches a credential, so newly created video meetings will be left running on the provider after the Cal.com booking is cancelled.

title: Location updates persist empty calendar reference ids
body: updateLocation now copies `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId` from the EventResult (`result.externalId` / `result.credentialId`). CalendarManager.updateEvent never sets those fields; it only returns appName, type, success, uid, updatedEvent, and warnings. Previously this path stored `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId` and fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar.credentialId`. Location changes therefore insert booking references with a null calendar id and null credential id (and an empty uid, because update results expose `updatedEvent`, not `createdEvent`). Later cancel/reschedule cannot target the provider event those references were meant to track.

title: Per-host calendar create still targets only the first destination
body: createAllCalendarEvents loops over every destination calendar and calls createEvent with that destination's credential, but it always passes the original event whose destinationCalendar array still contains every host. Lark (createEvent around line 128), Office 365 (around line 75), and CalDAV (around line 161) all take only index 0. Co-host credentials therefore write to the first host's calendar id: the call 403/404s, or CalDAV's filter matches nothing and createEvent still returns success without creating an object. The stored reference externalId is the co-host calendar, so later updates and deletes look in the wrong place. Google create does look up by credentialId, but its organizer attendee email is still taken from index 0 (CalendarService.ts line 122), so the co-host event is created as if the first host were the organizer.

title: Google update/delete fallback never resolves a calendar id
body: updateEvent and deleteEvent only use destinationCalendar when externalCalendarId is falsy, and then they search for a calendar whose externalId equals that same falsy value. That find can never match a real calendar. The old code used `event.destinationCalendar.externalId` in this branch. Legacy bookings that have no externalCalendarId on the reference now call the Google API with an undefined calendarId, so reschedule and cancel fail (delete no longer falls back to primary either). The same mistake is in deleteEvent around line 315.

title: Collective co-host calendars are dropped in common cases
body: destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, and the later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then no-ops. If the booking owner has no destination calendar but other collective hosts do, none of those hosts get a calendar event. Separately, team calendars are collected only from `users.slice(1)` (around line 990). When the event type itself has a destination calendar, the organizer's personal destination calendar is never added, so the owner host is skipped while other hosts are included. The booking row also connects only `destinationCalendar[0]`, so the persisted booking calendar does not represent the co-hosts either.

title: Recurring collective cancel deletes the wrong events, repeatedly
body: The new per-reference loop wraps the old recurring-cancel block unchanged. For each calendar reference, that block ignores the reference just fetched and instead walks every calendar credential on the booking owner, and for each remaining occurrence deletes only the first `_calendar` reference (`find`, not `filter`). Co-host events, whose credentials were loaded from the DB on the non-recurring path, are never deleted. The same delete promises are awaited inside the loop and pushed onto apiDeletes, which is awaited again later, so each remaining occurrence is deleted once per calendar reference and then a second time. A two-host recurring series will error or no-op on the other hosts' calendars and hammer the owner's calendar.

title: One missing calendar credential fails every calendar update
body: In updateAllCalendarEvents, if a reference has a credentialId that is neither on the EventManager user nor returned with an app slug, `credential` stays undefined and `updateEvent(undefined, ...)` is still pushed. That rejection fails Promise.all, and the catch now returns every calendar reference as failed without logging (the `console.error(message)` call was removed, and `message` is unused). One co-host credential that cannot be loaded therefore aborts updates for hosts whose calendar calls were valid, and the failure is invisible in logs. The create path correctly skips a missing credential; the update path should do the same.

title: Seat merge deletes only the first host calendar event
body: When newBookingId is set, the code still does `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes that single calendar event. This PR now stores one calendar reference per collective host, but this merge path was not updated to iterate them. Rescheduling into an existing seated booking removes only the first host's old provider event and leaves the other hosts' events on their calendars.

title: Paid confirmation still creates only the owner's calendar event
body: Stripe payment success builds destinationCalendar from the booking calendar or the booking user's calendar only, then calls eventManager.create(evt). Collective co-host calendars are never loaded. Paid bookings do not create provider events in handleNewBooking; they are created here, so the collective-host fix does not apply and co-hosts still get no calendar event after payment. The same single-calendar construction is in paypal-webhook.ts around line 152 and in confirm.handler.ts around line 175, which is what requires-confirmation uses before scheduling.

title: Organization slug is stored under the inverted billing flag
body: Unrelated to calendars, the org create payload changed from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`. Self-hosted installs with billing disabled used to persist the org slug immediately and will now create organizations with no slug, so org URLs and subdomain setup do not work. Cloud installs with billing enabled used to keep the slug only as metadata.requestedSlug until billing completed, and will now claim the real slug on an unverified, unpaid org. The requestedSlug ternary next to it is equivalent to the old expression; only the slug condition was flipped.

title: Webhook destinationCalendar shape is a breaking, inconsistent change
body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from a single DestinationCalendar to DestinationCalendar[] | null, and that object is spread into BOOKING_* webhook payloads. Existing subscribers that read destinationCalendar.externalId or .integration will throw or ignore the field. The PR is marked non-breaking, but the e2e update for BOOKING_REJECTED (null -> []) shows the payload changed. It is also inconsistent across events: handleNewBooking still sends null when unset, while confirm/cancel send []. Consumers cannot rely on either an object or an array.

title: Google create falls back to primary and can duplicate events
body: createEvent now chooses the calendar only by `credentialId === credentialId`, and uses "primary" when that find misses. It no longer uses the destination externalId directly. Destination calendars with a null credentialId, and EventManager's no-credentialId branch that calls createEvent once per credential of that integration (EventManager.ts around line 376), therefore write to primary instead of the configured calendar. Each matching Google credential can insert another primary event. The hangout description patch at line 168 uses `selectedCalendar` without the `|| "primary"` fallback, so that follow-up patch is sent with an undefined calendarId whenever the find misses.

title: Google Meet bookings crash when destinationCalendar is missing
body: The Google Meet fallback now reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration after destructuring evt.destinationCalendar ?? []. If the array is missing or empty (the new call sites pass null or []), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and this throws before any calendar event is created. The previous code used optional chaining (destinationCalendar?.integration), which fell back to Cal Video. Any Meet booking without a destination calendar now fails inside EventManager.create instead of booking.

title: Video booking references no longer store credentialId
body: referencesToCreate now sets credentialId only when the result type includes "_calendar", and forces undefined otherwise. Previously non-calendar results kept result.credentialId. Cancel (and any later video cleanup that looks up bookingReference.credentialId) will not find the Zoom/Daily/Meet credential, so the video meeting is left running after the booking is cancelled. New bookings created after this change are affected; updateLocation still copies result.credentialId, so the two paths disagree.

title: Google organizer email is always the first destination calendar
body: createEvent (and updateEvent) always uses destinationCalendar[0].externalId as the organizer attendee email, while the calendar written to is chosen by credentialId. EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent once per host credential with the full array, so host 2's insert is authenticated as host 2 but marked organizer with host 1's calendar id. Google rejects that insert or creates the event under the wrong organizer, so secondary collective hosts do not get a correct event even on Google.

title: Non-Google adapters still write only the first destination calendar
body: CalendarManager now passes credential.id into createEvent so each host credential can target its own calendar, but Office 365 createEvent ignores that argument and always posts to destinationCalendar[0].externalId (or /me/calendar/events). Lark createEvent/updateEvent/deleteEvent (larkcalendar CalendarService.ts around line 129) and CalDAV createEvent (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts around line 162) do the same and only read index 0. For a second host, the request is made with that host's token against the first host's calendar id. Office/Lark fail the call; CalDAV filters to no calendars and still returns success, so the host silently gets no event. The collective multi-host fix therefore only works for Google.

title: Collective host calendars are dropped when the organizer has none
body: destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, and the collective branch then does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). Optional chaining does not assign, so the array of other hosts' destination calendars is discarded. A collective event whose owner has no destination calendar creates no host calendar events at all, which is the case this PR is meant to fix. Initialize the array before pushing (for example evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]).

title: Confirm and payment flows still pass a single destination calendar
body: Only handleNewBooking appends every collective host's destinationCalendar before EventManager.create. confirm.handler, the Stripe webhook (packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts around lines 119 and 229), and the PayPal webhook (paypal-webhook.ts around line 152) still build evt.destinationCalendar from booking.destinationCalendar or the booking owner's calendar only. Collective events that require confirmation or payment create calendar events on that later path, so the other hosts never get a calendar event or a booking reference. Reschedule/cancel then have nothing to update for those hosts.

title: Cancelling remaining recurring events only deletes the first calendar reference
body: The new multi-reference loop wraps the recurring allRemainingBookings branch, but that branch still does updatedBookings references.find for a single _calendar reference and deletes it with every calendar credential on the booking owner, not with reference.credentialId. It also runs once per outer reference, so the same first event is deleted repeatedly. Other hosts' calendar events on the recurring series are never deleted, and a credential that does not own that event is used. Non-recurring cancel uses the per-reference credential and is fine; recurring collective cancel is not.

title: One missing calendar credential aborts every calendar update
body: updateAllCalendarEvents pushes updateEvent(credential, ...) even when credential is still undefined after the DB lookup (no row, or app.slug missing). getCalendar then throws inside the for-loop, before Promise.all and before later references are handled. The catch maps every calendar reference to success: false and no longer logs the error (console.error was removed), so a single bad host credential silently fails reschedule, location change, and attendee updates for every host.

title: Google update no longer falls back to a destination calendar id
body: updateEvent sets calendarId to externalCalendarId, or else find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId). When externalCalendarId is null or empty that comparison cannot match, so calendarId is undefined and events.update is called with no calendar id. The old code used destinationCalendar.externalId. Bookings whose references have no externalCalendarId (older rows, or creates that did not persist one) can no longer be rescheduled or updated on Google. deleteEvent has the same dead find, but still falls back to "primary"; update does not.

title: Hangout-link patch uses an undefined calendar id
body: Insert uses selectedCalendar || "primary", but the follow-up events.patch that writes the Meet link into the description passes calendarId: selectedCalendar with no fallback. selectedCalendar is undefined whenever no destination entry matches credentialId (or externalId is null). The event is created on primary and the patch is sent to an undefined calendar, so the description never gets the hangout link. Previously selectedCalendar was always an external id or "primary".

title: Organization slug is stored under the opposite billing flag
body: The spread was changed from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug } to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}. That inverts org creation: self-hosted (billing disabled) organizations are created with no slug, so org URLs do not resolve, and billing-enabled organizations get slug set immediately instead of only requestedSlug pending approval. The requestedSlug line below was only rewritten from && to a ternary and is unchanged in meaning. This is unrelated to destination calendars and breaks org provisioning.

title: Webhook destinationCalendar changed from object to array
body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is now DestinationCalendar[] | null, and BOOKING_* webhook payloads spread that field. Subscribers that read destinationCalendar.integration, .externalId, or .credentialId will break. The change is labeled a non-breaking bug fix. Payloads are also inconsistent: handleNewBooking still sends null when unset, while confirm/cancel/payment send []. The e2e fixture was only updated for BOOKING_REJECTED (null to []), so BOOKING_CREATED still expects null and does not lock the new array shape.

title: Google refresh writes the Zod result wrapper into credential.key
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod SafeParse object ({ success, data }), not the parsed credential. GoogleCalendarService assigns that return value straight to key and prisma.credential.update persists it. This runs on every access-token refresh even when credential sync is disabled (the old code stored googleCredentialSchema.parse(...), which returned the credential itself). After the first refresh the row is no longer a Google credential, so the next GoogleCalendarService constructor throws in googleCredentialSchema.parse and Google Calendar stops working until the user reconnects.

title: Salesforce refresh calls prisma without an import and then uses the old access token
body: getClient now always refreshes the Salesforce token and calls prisma.credential.update, but this file never imports prisma. Constructing SalesforceCalendarService therefore throws ReferenceError before any Event/Contact call, so the Salesforce integration is broken for every user, not only credential-sync deployments. The new token is also not what the client uses: jsforce.Connection is still created with credentialKey.access_token (the pre-refresh value) at line 106, and a new refresh_token from Salesforce is discarded in favor of the old one. Every calendar operation also pays an extra token round-trip, and this path never calls refreshOAuthTokens, so CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is ignored for Salesforce.

title: Absent refresh_token is overwritten with the literal string "refresh_token"
body: After a successful parse, if refresh_token is missing or empty the helper sets it to the string "refresh_token". Office365CalendarService then spreads tokenResponse.data onto the saved credential. Microsoft's refresh response often omits refresh_token (the Office 365 schema marks it optional, and the previous safeParse path left the stored token untouched). The real refresh token is replaced, the next refresh sends refresh_token=refresh_token, and Microsoft returns invalid_grant, permanently disconnecting Outlook calendar. This runs whether or not credential sync is enabled.

title: Sync-mode token schema cannot match any real token payload
body: minimumTokenResponseSchema is a z.object whose extra keys are the literal strings produced by z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString() (Zod type names / "[object Object]"), not wildcards, and the object is not passthrough. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, every refresh goes through this schema. Real bodies only have access_token and an expiry field, so safeParse always fails and the helper throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Google, Office 365, Zoom, and Salesforce token refresh cannot succeed in sync mode, and the comment's intent (treat any numeric field as expiry and keep other properties) is not implemented.

title: Sync refresh returns a raw Fetch Response that callers do not understand
body: When credential sync is on, refreshOAuthTokens returns the Fetch Response and never checks response.ok or reads response.json(). Callers were not updated to that contract: Google reads res.data (gaxios), HubSpot treats the result as a HubspotToken (accessToken/expiresIn), Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM read axios .data and persist it, and Lark passes the body to handleLarkError which expects Lark's { code, data } envelope. A sync response of { access_token, expiry } therefore throws or is written into credential.key as the wrong shape. Non-2xx responses are also treated as success. Turning on the new env vars breaks token refresh for those apps instead of delegating it.

title: Outbound token sync request carries no authentication
body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug as form fields. It does not send CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, a signature, or any other credential, and it does not require HTTPS. .env.example presents this as configuration-only, and the helper comment says the response should contain the access token. Anyone who can reach that URL can request third-party access tokens for any Cal user id. Those tokens are then stored and used as the user's Google/Zoom/Microsoft credentials. The inbound webhook authenticates with a shared secret, but the outbound call that actually returns live tokens does not.

title: Zoho Bigin passes credential id where the sync API expects user id
body: refreshOAuthTokens' third argument is the Cal.com user id (sent as calcomUserId). BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken passes credentialId instead. With sync enabled, the parent app looks up the wrong user and can return that user's access token; the following code persists tokenInfo.data onto this credential. Even before response parsing is fixed, the parent is asked to mint or rotate tokens for an unrelated id. Other adapters pass credential.userId.

title: Lark deletes the credential if the local refresh token is expired, before sync
body: refreshAccessToken still deletes the credential and throws when refresh_token is missing or refresh_expires_date is past, and only then calls refreshOAuthTokens. Credential sync is supposed to obtain a new access token from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT without a provider refresh token (that helper's comment says the response only contains an access token and expiry). For a synced Lark user whose stored refresh token is a placeholder or has expired, the row is deleted and the sync endpoint is never called, so the integration and its tokens are lost instead of refreshed.

title: Zoom sync sends app slug "zoomvideo" instead of "zoom"
body: refreshOAuthTokens is called with appSlug "zoomvideo", but the Zoom credential is stored with appId "zoom" (see the OAuth callback) and the app-store slug used by the new webhook is "zoom". The parent app, which keys credentials by the slug it posted to /api/webhook/app-credential, will not find a "zoomvideo" credential. Zoom token refresh via the sync endpoint fails or refreshes the wrong app, while every other adapter in this PR passes its real app slug (google-calendar, msteams, office365-calendar, and so on).

title: Webhook find-then-create can insert duplicate app credentials
body: The handler loads an existing credential with findFirst on (userId, appId) and, if none is found, creates one. There is no unique constraint on that pair (other OAuth callbacks in this PR delete duplicates because findFirst otherwise ignores them) and no transaction or retry on unique conflict. Two concurrent sync deliveries for the same user and app both observe no row and both insert. Later refreshes and calendar lookups also use findFirst without a stable order, so they can keep using a stale duplicate while the webhook updates a different row.

title: Sync update leaves invalid credentials marked invalid
body: When a credential already exists, the webhook updates only key. It does not set invalid: false. Adapters in this PR (Google, Webex, Zoom) set invalid: true after an unrecoverable refresh, and credential loading skips invalid rows. A later successful sync from the parent app therefore stores new tokens on a row that is still treated as disconnected, so calendar and video calls keep failing until the user deletes and reinstalls the app.

title: No tests cover token persistence or the credential webhook
body: The PR adds the credential webhook, parseRefreshTokenResponse, and refreshOAuthTokens, and the author notes that no tests were added. There is no unit test that the object written to credential.key is still the provider credential (Google currently persists the SafeParse wrapper) or that a refresh response without refresh_token keeps the previous refresh token (Office 365 now stores the literal "refresh_token"). Those regressions ship on the normal, sync-disabled refresh path and would be caught by a test that asserts the saved key.

title: Google token refresh persists the Zod result, not the credential
body: After a Google refresh, the code assigns `key` to the return value of `parseRefreshTokenResponse` and writes that object to `credential.key`. That helper returns the whole `safeParse` result (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed token. Previously this path saved `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which is the token itself. The next `GoogleCalendarService` construction calls `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` and throws, so every successful Google token refresh (credential sync off or on) corrupts the stored credential and breaks Google Calendar until the user reconnects. On the sync path this is worse: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a Fetch `Response`, which has no `.data`, so `token.access_token` throws before a valid token can be applied.

title: Salesforce client always crashes: prisma is not imported
body: `getClient` now always exchanges the refresh token and then calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this file never imports `prisma`. Constructing `SalesforceCalendarService` (which awaits `getClient`) throws `ReferenceError` before a jsforce connection is returned, so Salesforce event create/update/delete is broken for every install, not only credential-sync installs. Even if prisma were imported, the new access token is saved and then ignored: the connection is still built with `credentialKey.access_token` (the pre-refresh token) at line 106, and the token request is hardcoded to `https://login.salesforce.com` (line 75), which rejects sandbox and My Domain refresh tokens that must be sent to the org's own token URL. This path also never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`, so the new sync endpoint is not used.

title: Sync token schema requires a literal ZodString property
body: When credential sharing and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, refresh parsing uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema`. The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are the strings `"ZodString"` and `"ZodOptional"`, not a catchall for arbitrary fields. Zod object schemas also strip unknown keys. A normal body such as `{ access_token, expires_in }` therefore fails `safeParse`, and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` always throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Google, Office 365, Zoom, and Salesforce refresh all go through this helper, so enabling the feature breaks token refresh for those apps instead of accepting an access token plus expiry.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string refresh_token
body: After a successful parse, if `refresh_token` is absent the helper writes the placeholder string `"refresh_token"` onto the parsed object and returns it. Callers persist that object. Office 365 merges `tokenResponse.data` over the stored credential (`refresh_token` is optional on its schema, and Microsoft often omits a new refresh token), so a real refresh token is overwritten with `"refresh_token"` and the next refresh fails permanently. Zoom assigns `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` the same way once the sync schema does not require a refresh token. The placeholder was meant to satisfy schemas, but it is stored as a live secret.

title: Sync refresh returns an unparsed Fetch Response to callers that expect tokens
body: When sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` POSTs to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and returns the raw Fetch `Response` without checking `response.ok` or reading JSON. Callers do not share one return type. Google reads `res.data.access_token` (Gaxios shape). HubSpot treats the result as a HubSpot token (`accessToken`, `expiresIn`) and writes it back as `credential.key`. Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `tokenInfo.data` on an axios response. Lark passes the body to `handleLarkError`, which expects a Lark envelope (`code`, `data.refresh_token`, `data.expires_in`). The comment says the endpoint returns only an access token and expiry, but none of these callers adapt that shape, so a successful sync response still fails or stores a Response/wrong object. The non-sync branch returns whatever `refreshFunction` returns, so the two branches are not interchangeable.

title: Outbound token sync request is unauthenticated
body: The refresh call that is supposed to retrieve a user's third-party access token sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in a form body. It does not send `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, a signature, or any other credential, even though the new inbound webhook authenticates with that secret. Anyone who can reach `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` can request access tokens for arbitrary Cal.com user ids. The sample client is what self-hosters are told to point at their token endpoint, and nothing in this request tells that endpoint the caller is Cal.com.

title: Zoho Bigin sync sends credential id as calcomUserId
body: `refreshAccessToken` calls `refreshOAuthTokens` with `credentialId` (the credential primary key) as the third argument. That argument is documented and sent as `calcomUserId`. The parent app will look up the wrong user, or no user, and return another user's tokens or an error. The Bigin refresh method never receives `credential.userId`, so this cannot be correct even after the response-shape bug is fixed. When sync is on, the return value is also a Fetch Response, but the code immediately reads `tokenInfo.data` as if it were an axios response, so `tokenInfo.data` is undefined and the refresh throws.

title: Teams refresh replaces the whole credential with the sync body
body: After `refreshOAuthTokens`, the MS Teams adapter JSON-parses the response and saves that object as the entire `credential.key`. The sync contract is only an access token and expiry, so this drops `refresh_token`, `email`, and `scope` from the stored credential. Expiry is computed as `Date.now() + (expires_in || 0) * 1000`; if the sync payload uses a different expiry field, `expiry_date` becomes now and every subsequent call treats the token as expired and refreshes again, rewriting the key each time. With sync disabled the Microsoft token response is a full token object, so this only breaks the new sync path, but that path is what this PR adds.

title: Zoom sync uses app slug zoomvideo instead of zoom
body: The Zoom refresh calls `refreshOAuthTokens` with app slug `"zoomvideo"`. The installed app id written by the Zoom OAuth callback is `"zoom"` (`appId: "zoom"`), and every other integration in this PR passes its real app slug (`google-calendar`, `msteams`, `office365-calendar`, `hubspot`). The parent store will not find a Zoom credential for `zoomvideo`, so Zoom token sync returns the wrong app or nothing while other apps sync.

title: Webex sync refresh still requires a full Webex token body
body: Webex was switched to `refreshOAuthTokens` but still validates the body with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires `token_type: "Bearer"`, an exact scope literal, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in`. It does not use `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. A sync endpoint that returns only an access token and expiry, as `refreshOAuthTokens` documents, fails this schema and the refresh rejects with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned", so Webex credential sync cannot succeed.

title: Credential webhook leaves invalid rows invalid and can duplicate credentials
body: The update path writes only `key`. Credentials previously marked `invalid: true` by a failed refresh stay invalid, so a successful sync from the parent app does not restore the integration. The lookup is also a non-transactional `findFirst` by `userId` + `appId` followed by create (lines 62-90). There is no unique constraint handling, so concurrent webhook deliveries (retries) can insert a second credential for the same user and app. Calendar code uses `findFirst`, so later refreshes update an arbitrary row and the other keeps stale tokens. `zod` parse, `symmetricDecrypt`, and `JSON.parse` are also uncaught, so a bad body or ciphertext becomes an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx.

title: Google refresh persists the Zod result and corrupts the credential
body: After a Google token refresh, the value written to Credential.key is the object returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse, which is the Zod safeParse wrapper ({success, data}) rather than the credential object. Previously googleCredentialSchema.parse returned the tokens themselves. The next GoogleCalendarService construction calls googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) and throws because access_token is nested under data, so every Google calendar stops working after the first refresh (typically within an hour). This runs even when credential sync is disabled. When sync is enabled it is also wrong in a second way: refreshOAuthTokens returns an unparsed fetch Response, so res.data is undefined and token.access_token throws before a usable token is applied.

title: Salesforce client always refreshes, then crashes on missing prisma
body: getClient now refreshes the Salesforce token on every CalendarService construction, then calls prisma.credential.update, but prisma is never imported in this file. That throws ReferenceError, the Connection is never returned, and every Salesforce calendar/CRM operation fails after deploy. Even if the import is added, the jsforce Connection is still built with credentialKey.access_token (the pre-refresh token) rather than the access token just fetched, and a failed refresh now takes down calls that previously relied on a still-valid access token. Enabling credential sync makes this worse: parseRefreshTokenResponse switches to the minimum schema, strips instance_url and the other Salesforce fields, and the update overwrites the stored key with that stripped object.

title: Parser invents refresh_token and drops every other token field
body: If the parsed payload has no refresh_token, this sets refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token" and returns that object. Office 365 marks refresh_token optional and then spreads the parsed data over the stored credential (office365calendar CalendarService), so a normal Microsoft refresh that omits a new refresh token permanently replaces the real refresh token and the next refresh cannot succeed. The minimum schema used when sync is enabled does not do what the comments say: [z.string().toString()] is a literal key, not a catchall, and z.object strips unknown keys, so expiry_date, expires_in, instance_url, and similar fields are discarded. Callers that persist the result (Zoom, Salesforce, Office 365) then save an incomplete key and, via this stub, a fake refresh token.

title: Sync refresh returns a raw Response that callers cannot use
body: When CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, this returns the fetch Response and never checks response.ok or parses JSON. Callers were not updated to that contract. HubSpot and both Zoho services expect an axios/SDK body with .data or accessToken/expiresIn and will throw or write a non-token value into Credential.key. Google reads res.data. Lark, Webex, and Zoom expect provider-specific JSON (Lark's code/data envelope, Webex's strict scope schema, Zoom's expires_in) and will fail or, in Zoom's case, persist NaN expiry and the stub refresh token. The request also sends only calcomUserId and appSlug, with no documented response schema that those adapters share, so turning the feature on breaks token refresh for the wired apps instead of refreshing them.

title: Outbound token sync sends no shared secret
body: The sync POST that is supposed to return a third-party access token authenticates nothing: no CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, Authorization header, or signed timestamp, only calcomUserId and appSlug. The inbound webhook requires the shared secret, but the call that actually dispenses live OAuth access tokens does not. A self-hoster implementing the contract this client calls (the comment says the response should contain the access token and expiry) exposes user access tokens to anyone who can reach that URL and guess or enumerate a user id.

title: Credential sync updates an arbitrary row and can duplicate keys
body: The handler finds a credential with findFirst({userId, appId}) and no orderBy, then updates only that id. (userId, appId) is not unique: Google's OAuth callback always inserts a new credential row, and two concurrent webhook calls can both observe no row and both create. findFirst may therefore update a credential that is not the one calendar/video code loads, so the webhook returns success while the live tokens stay stale, or it creates duplicates that later refreshes keep splitting. The update path also never sets invalid: false, so a credential already marked invalid stays unusable after the source of truth pushes new keys. Zod parse and symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse are uncaught, so a bad body or ciphertext becomes an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx.

title: Zoho Bigin sync sends credential id as the user id
body: refreshOAuthTokens's third argument is the Cal.com user id, but refreshAccessToken passes credentialId. When credential sync is enabled, the parent app looks up tokens for whatever user has that numeric id, not the owner of this credential. If parsing is later fixed to accept the sync response, those tokens are written onto this credential, so one user can be given another user's Zoho access token. With the current fetch Response return value, tokenInfo.data is undefined and refresh throws instead.

title: Zoom sync uses app slug zoomvideo instead of zoom
body: The refresh call passes appSlug "zoomvideo", but the Zoom credential is stored with appId "zoom" (see the OAuth callback) and the installed-app path uses slug "zoom". The webhook and the parent app store key off the real slug, so a sync refresh asks for an app that does not exist and will not return this user's Zoom tokens. Other adapters in this PR pass the real slug (google-calendar, msteams, office365-calendar).

title: No tests for credential write or token-refresh regressions
body: The new webhook can create or overwrite OAuth credential JSON for any user, and the shared refresh helpers change the success path for Google, Office 365, Zoom, and Salesforce even when sync is off. The PR adds no tests, and the checklist confirms none were run. A test that refreshes a Google or Office 365 credential with sync disabled, and one that posts a valid webhook payload, would have caught the safeParse object being stored and the literal refresh_token overwrite before merge.

title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so the caller must be both. That does not match the variable name or the bookings UI, which treats team admin and owner as alternative managers (isUserTeamAdminOrOwner). A team admin who is not an owner is always FORBIDDEN; if those helpers treat ADMIN and OWNER as distinct membership roles, owners are forbidden too. Team managers will see Add guests on a team booking and the mutation will reject them. Use ||, and do not call either helper with teamId 0 when eventType.teamId is null.

title: Calendar update uses the actor and is not rolled back
body: Attendees are inserted with createMany before updateCalendarAttendees. The EventManager is then built from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user), while booking.user (including credentials) was loaded and never used. If a team admin or attendee adds guests, the update targets that person's calendars, not the host calendar that owns the event, so the real event's attendee list is not updated or the call throws. The throw is outside any transaction and outside the email try/catch, so the mutation errors after the rows are committed. A retry then filters those emails as already present and fails with emails_must_be_unique_valid, leaving the booking, calendars, and notifications permanently out of sync. Use the booking host's credentials and roll back the insert if the calendar update fails.

title: Cancelled and rejected bookings can be re-invited
body: Nothing checks booking.status before creating attendees and sending mail. addGuests is only authedProcedure plus the handler's role check, so an organizer, attendee, or permitted team member can call it for a CANCELLED or REJECTED booking even though the list UI hides the action. The new organizer and attendee emails attach an ICS REQUEST with status CONFIRMED, which can put the meeting back on calendars and re-send the video link for a meeting that was declined or cancelled. Gate the update on ACCEPTED (or another explicit allow-list) before writing attendees.

title: Seated events ignore capacity and seat records
body: createMany inserts Attendee rows without checking seatsPerTimeSlot (the same handler later copies that field onto the calendar payload) and without creating BookingSeat rows. Seat availability and payment are based on seat count, so these extra attendees can exceed the cap, receive the meeting link without a paid seat, and are invisible to seat cancel/reschedule flows that use seatsReferences. The emails also include the full attendee list, which leaks other people when seatsShowAttendees is false. Reject addGuests for seated event types, or enforce remaining capacity and create the matching seat records.

title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive and silent
body: uniqueGuests keeps a guest unless guest === attendee.email and unless blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest). The blacklist entries are lowercased, but the input is not lowercased or trimmed, so BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is bypassed by changing case. The same address can also be stored twice (User@x.com vs user@x.com), and duplicates inside the guests array are not removed, so one request can insert the same attendee twice. Filtered addresses are dropped with no per-email error: if any other address remains, the handler returns success and the UI says guests were added; if every address is filtered out, the error is emails_must_be_unique_valid, which is wrong for a blacklist hit. Normalize before compare, dedupe the input, exclude the organizer address, and reject blocked emails instead of skipping them.

title: Guest list has no maximum length
body: guests is z.array(z.string().email()) with no min or max. Anyone the handler allows, including any attendee on the booking, can submit thousands of addresses in one call. Each new address becomes an Attendee row, and sendAddGuestsEmails sends a full booking message (location and video link included) to every attendee. That is an unbounded write and a meeting-link spam path with no limit on this procedure. Cap the array in ZAddGuestsInputSchema and reject an empty list.

title: Emails use the raw guest list and hide send failures
body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original guests input, not uniqueGuests. In email-manager, any attendee whose email is in that list gets AttendeeScheduledEmail (a new confirmation plus ICS REQUEST) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Re-submitting someone already on the booking therefore pushes a second confirmed invite to them, while addresses that were filtered out still affect that branch. The call is wrapped in a try/catch that only console.log's a static string and then returns { message: "Guests added" }, so the dialog shows success even when nobody was notified. Pass only the addresses actually inserted, and log or surface the real send error.

title: disableGuests on the event type is ignored
body: eventType is included on the booking but disableGuests is never read. The normal booking flow refuses additional guests when that flag is set; this mutation still creates Attendee rows and emails them the meeting details. Because the permission check also allows any existing attendee, a guest on a no-guests event type can invite arbitrary people after the fact. Reject the request when booking.eventType.disableGuests is true.

title: Add-guest mail ignores standard-email disable flags
body: sendLocationChangeEmails and the other send helpers in this file skip host or attendee mail when event-type metadata has disableStandardEmails. sendAddGuestsEmails always emails the organizer, every team.members entry, and every attendee, and addGuestsHandler never passes eventType.metadata. Event types configured to suppress standard emails still get guest-added messages and ICS attachments, bypassing workflow-only notification settings. Apply the same host and attendee disable checks here.

title: Calendar payload omits team, so co-hosts are skipped
body: The CalendarEvent built for updateCalendarAttendees and sendAddGuestsEmails never sets team. sendAddGuestsEmails only notifies other hosts when calendarEvent.team.members is present, so that loop is dead for this caller. Collective and round-robin co-hosts get no guest-added email or ICS, and destinationCalendar falls back to a single booking.user calendar, so their calendars are not updated either. Populate team the same way the other booking email builders do before calling EventManager and sendAddGuestsEmails.

title: No tests for addGuests authorization or side effects
body: The new mutation decides who may add guests, how emails are filtered, and whether cancelled, seated, or disableGuests bookings are writable, but the PR adds no handler or router tests. The admin&&owner check, case-sensitive blacklist bypass, and cancelled-booking ICS path would ship unnoticed. Cover organizer, team admin, team owner, unrelated user, duplicate and blacklisted emails, seated event types, and non-ACCEPTED statuses.

title: Team admin/owner check is AND, so it never matches
body: Permission is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...), but those membership roles are alternatives (the flag is even named isTeamAdminOrOwner, and the bookings UI uses isUserTeamAdminOrOwner). If the roles are mutually exclusive the expression is always false, because a failed admin check short-circuits and a successful admin check then fails the owner check. A team admin or owner who is not the booking host and whose login email is not already an attendee is always rejected with FORBIDDEN, so they cannot add guests to team bookings from the bookings page.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the host's
body: updateCalendarAttendees is invoked through an EventManager built from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). The booking query already loads booking.user.credentials and the host destination calendar, but those credentials are never used. Anyone allowed by the attendee check (and any team manager, once the role check is fixed) will try to patch the host's calendar event with their own OAuth tokens. That call fails or updates the wrong account, so the new guests never land on the host calendar. The attendee rows are already committed by then, and a retry treats those emails as duplicates and throws emails_must_be_unique_valid, so the calendar update cannot be completed.

title: Guests are committed before calendar and email side effects
body: prisma.booking.update createMany inserts attendees immediately, with no transaction around the later calendar update and sendAddGuestsEmails. If updateCalendarAttendees throws, the tRPC mutation fails but the rows stay. The client shows an error, yet a retry filters those addresses out as already attending and, when no other new addresses remain, returns BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid. The guests exist in the database, the host calendar is unchanged, and no notification is sent, with no way to finish the operation for those addresses.

title: Seated events are not enforced and hidden attendees are emailed
body: seatsPerTimeSlot and seatsShowAttendees are copied onto the calendar event and then ignored. The handler still createMany's Attendee rows with no BookingSeat / seat-reference rows and no capacity check. On a seated event that overbooks the slot, leaves people who do not show up in seat cancellation or no-show flows, and skips per-seat payment. sendAddGuestsEmails then sends AttendeeScheduledEmail with the full attendee list. Unlike sendScheduledSeatsEmails, it never passes showAttendees, so an event type with seatsShowAttendees false leaks every other attendee's name and email to the newly added addresses.

title: Guest filter misses blacklist, case, and in-request duplicates
body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased, but each submitted guest is tested with includes(guest) and compared to existing attendees with guest === attendee.email, with no toLowerCase or trim. Zod's email check allows mixed case, so Spam@blocked.com bypasses a blacklist entry of spam@blocked.com, and A@x.com is inserted even when a@x.com is already an attendee. The variable is named uniqueGuests but the filter never dedupes the input, and the schema does not either, so one request can create two Attendee rows for the same address. There is also no unique (bookingId, email) guard around the check-then-insert, so two concurrent calls can both pass the read and insert the same guest twice.

title: Cancelled, pending, past, and no-guest event types are accepted
body: After the booking is loaded, nothing checks BookingStatus, endTime, or eventType.disableGuests. A direct call can add attendees to a cancelled, rejected, or still-pending booking and sendAddGuestsEmails will mail ICS REQUEST invites marked CONFIRMED, including the video URL and meeting password when a video reference exists. The same path ignores disableGuests, so an event type that turned guests off still accepts invites. Any logged-in user whose email matches an attendee is authorized, not only the host, so a booker can do this even when the host disabled guests. The bookings UI also offers the action for past confirmed rows, because Add guests lives on bookedActions and that menu is rendered for past confirmed bookings in BookingListItem.

title: Emails are selected from the raw guest list, not guests actually added
body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original guests array, not uniqueGuests. In sendAddGuestsEmails, every current attendee whose email is in that array receives AttendeeScheduledEmail (a new booking confirmation plus ICS REQUEST) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Submitting an address that was already on the booking therefore sends that person a fresh 'you are scheduled' invite, which calendar clients treat as a new or duplicate event. Addresses that were filtered out as duplicates still match and take the wrong template; only the addresses that were actually inserted should get the scheduled email.

title: Add-guest emails ignore disableStandardEmails
body: Every other sender in this file checks eventTypeDisableHostEmail and eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail before mailing. sendAddGuestsEmails does not take eventTypeMetadata and always emails the organizer, every attendee, and each new guest. The handler loads eventType but never forwards metadata.disableStandardEmails. Event types that turned standard host or attendee emails off still get a full fan-out, including video-call details, whenever someone uses this mutation.

title: Guest list has no maximum, so one call can mass-mail
body: guests is z.array(z.string().email()) with no .max() and no uniqueness constraint, and addGuests is a plain authedProcedure rather than the bookings procedure used by editLocation. A host or attendee can submit thousands of addresses in one mutation. Each new address becomes an Attendee row and receives AttendeeScheduledEmail with the meeting link and, when present, the video meeting password. That is an authenticated email-spam and meeting-link disclosure path with no cap.

title: Email failures are swallowed and reported as success
body: sendAddGuestsEmails is wrapped in try/catch that only console.log's a static string and drops err. The handler then returns { message: 'Guests added' }, and the dialog shows the success toast and closes. If the mailer throws, guests are stored and the calendar may already have been updated, but nobody is notified and the user is told the operation succeeded. The log line does not include the error, so the failure is also invisible in production logs.

title: Collective/round-robin hosts are never notified or updated
body: The CalendarEvent built for this flow never sets team (or the other hosts' destination calendars). sendAddGuestsEmails only loops calendarEvent.team.members, so that loop is dead and co-hosts do not get OrganizerAddGuestsEmail. destinationCalendar is only the booking calendar or the single booking.user calendar. On collective or round-robin events, other hosts keep a stale attendee list on their calendars and receive no email that guests were added.

title: New guests are stored with an empty name
body: Every added guest is inserted with name: ''. Attendee emails address them as ' <email>' (AttendeeAddGuestsEmail / AttendeeScheduledEmail use `${name} <${email}>`), and the ICS ATTENDEE CN is blank. Some clients drop or mis-file invites with an empty CN, and the organizer subject uses attendees[0].name, which is an empty string when that row is first. The email local-part or the address itself should be stored as the name, which is what booking-time guests already do.

title: No tests for auth, seat rules, or email recipient selection
body: The new mutation changes booking attendees, calendar events, and a multi-recipient email fan-out, and the PR adds no handler or email tests. Nothing covers the admin-versus-owner permission expression, blacklist and case-folding, rejection of seated or disableGuests event types, cancelled or past bookings, or which template is sent to new versus existing attendees. Those branches are where the implementation is wrong, and they will not be caught by typecheck.

title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner. Those are mutually exclusive membership roles, so the condition is never true for a normal team admin or owner. Team hosts who are not the booking user and not an attendee are always rejected with FORBIDDEN, so the team path this check was meant to allow cannot add guests.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials after the DB write
body: Attendees are inserted first, then EventManager is built from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). The booking host's credentials are loaded on booking.user and never used. When the caller is a team admin or an attendee, the update runs with credentials that do not own the event, so the host calendar/video attendee list is not updated. updateCalendarAttendees is not in a transaction and is not caught; if it throws, the mutation returns an error even though the guests are already stored, and sendAddGuestsEmails never runs, so nobody is notified and a retry is treated as a duplicate.

title: Guests can be added to cancelled, pending, or past bookings
body: The handler never checks booking.status or endTime before createMany and before sending mail. Any organizer or attendee can add guests to a CANCELLED, REJECTED, or PENDING booking. The new mail classes always attach an ICS with status CONFIRMED and method REQUEST, so people are invited to a meeting that is not an accepted upcoming event. The bookings list also keeps this action on past confirmed rows (bookedActions is rendered when isBookingInPast && isConfirmed), so the UI offers the same flow after the event has ended.

title: Host disableGuests setting is not enforced
body: eventType is loaded but disableGuests is never read. Hosts turn that flag on so bookers cannot invite extra people or forward the meeting link. This mutation still creates attendees and emails them the full invite, including videoCallData (URL and password) when a video reference exists, so the event-type privacy setting is bypassed by anyone who passes the organizer/attendee check.

title: Seated events get extra attendees without seat records
body: If eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot is set, each attendee is a seat holder backed by a BookingSeat. This handler still createMany's Attendee rows and does not create seats or check remaining capacity. Seat counts, no-show, and per-seat cancel flows that use seatsReferences will disagree with booking.attendees. sendAddGuestsEmails also sends every attendee a normal scheduled/add-guests email and never passes seatsShowAttendees, so hidden seat lists are emailed to the new addresses.

title: Guest emails are not normalized, deduped, or blacklist-safe
body: Blacklist entries are lowercased, but each guest is compared with includes(guest) and with attendee.email using raw ===. Zod's email() does not lowercase, so Guest@x.com misses a blacklist entry of guest@x.com and is also treated as a new attendee when guest@x.com is already on the booking. The filter also does not dedupe the input array, and ZAddGuestsInputSchema has no .max() or uniqueness check, so one request can insert repeated rows and fan out an unbounded number of meeting invites. The organizer address is not excluded either.

title: Notification uses the raw guest list, not the inserted guests
body: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) is called with the original input, not uniqueGuests. Inside that helper, any attendee whose email is in that list gets AttendeeScheduledEmail (a new confirmed booking invite) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Re-submitting an existing attendee, or mixing new and old addresses, therefore sends current participants a fresh 'scheduled' ICS while the people who were actually inserted can be classified wrong if casing differs from the stored email.

title: Add-guest mail ignores standard email disable flags
body: Every other sender in this file bails out when event type metadata has disableStandardEmails for the host or attendee. sendAddGuestsEmails always emails the organizer, every team member, and every attendee, and the handler never passes eventType.metadata. Event types that disabled standard mail still blast guest-added and scheduled invites, including meeting links, when guests are added.

title: New guests are stored with an empty name
body: createMany sets name to "" and copies the organizer timezone and locale. Attendee mail then builds To as `${name} <${email}>`, which is a blank display name, and the scheduled/add-guest templates greet an empty name. Guests also get times in the host timezone because the dialog never collects theirs.

title: Retry cleanup deletes reminders this job does not own
body: The new deleteMany branch matches every WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 and does not require method SMS, scheduled false, or any scheduledDate bound. WorkflowReminder also stores EMAIL and WHATSAPP rows, and an SMS row can already be scheduled true with a Twilio referenceId if a later attempt succeeds or a concurrent run records success while another run has already bumped retryCount past 1. The next cron then deletes those rows. Email and WhatsApp reminders are dropped and never send. A scheduled SMS loses its referenceId without cancelling the provider message, so the text can still go out and can no longer be tracked or cancelled. The original delete was limited to SMS; that limit was not applied to this OR branch. Scope it to unscheduled SMS rows this job actually failed.

title: Broad catch burns the two-strike limit and can duplicate SMS
body: The catch surrounds template building, the organizer profile lookup, getBookerBaseUrl, twilio.scheduleSMS, and the success update that sets scheduled and referenceId. Any throw increments retryCount and leaves scheduled false. If Twilio already accepted the message and only the following update failed, the SID is discarded and the next cron calls scheduleSMS again, sending a duplicate; after two such errors retryCount is 2 and the opening deleteMany removes the row while those provider messages stay queued. The same path treats transient failures (DB blip, booker URL, empty attendees) as permanent send failures. This cron loads every unscheduled SMS in the next 7 days, so two errored passes delete that whole backlog and those bookings never get an SMS. Only count a retry when the provider rejects the send, and if scheduleSMS already returned a SID, persist that SID instead of incrementing.

title: Missing number or empty body is retried until the send date
body: retryCount is incremented only when message is non-empty and sendTo is set, and only if scheduleSMS returns a falsy value or throws. If the step has no sendTo, the booking has no smsReminderNumber, or the rendered body is empty, the loop just continues. The row stays scheduled false with retryCount 0 and is selected again on every cron run until scheduledDate is in the past, which is the unbounded reschedule this PR is meant to stop (invalid or missing phone). Treat a missing destination or empty message as a terminal failure so those reminders are not loaded until the event date.

title: retryCount write is not atomic under overlapping crons
body: Both failure paths set retryCount to the in-memory reminder.retryCount + 1 (here and in the catch at line 195) instead of an atomic increment. The handler loops every due reminder with several queries and a Twilio call, and it is a cron POST that can be invoked again if the previous run is still going or the scheduler retries a timeout. Two runs read the same count, both can call scheduleSMS for the same unscheduled row, and both write the same retryCount, so the retryCount > 1 delete never observes the real number of attempts and does not stop duplicate sends. Use retryCount: { increment: 1 } and claim the row before calling Twilio so a second run cannot schedule it again.

title: retryCount delete is not covered by an index
body: deleteMany now ORs retryCount > 1 onto the cleanup, but WorkflowReminder only indexes (method, scheduled, scheduledDate), (bookingUid), (workflowStepId), (seatReferenceId), and (cancelled, scheduledDate). The new column in schema.prisma has no index. Postgres cannot serve that OR branch from the existing composite index, so every cron run can sequentially scan WorkflowReminder before any SMS is scheduled. That table grows with bookings; a slow cleanup makes this endpoint more likely to overlap the next cron tick.

title: No tests for the retry limit or what gets deleted
body: This change deletes reminder rows and stops SMS after a small number of failures, and nothing in the PR covers that contract. Needed cases: one failure leaves the row and a second failure makes the next run delete it; the gt: 1 cutoff matches "failed twice" and does not allow a third scheduleSMS call; EMAIL and WHATSAPP rows with any retryCount are not deleted; a falsy scheduleSMS result and a thrown provider error both increment; empty sendTo or an empty body does not get reselected until the date; a successful schedule does not increment and is not deleted while still in the future. Without those, the unscoped OR and the two-strike catch can drop or duplicate reminders unnoticed.

title: Cleanup comment no longer describes the delete
body: The comment says this deletes scheduled SMS reminders whose scheduled date is already past. The query never filters on scheduled true, and the new OR branch also deletes any method's reminder with retryCount > 1, including future rows. Someone editing this later from the comment can restore or narrow the wrong predicate and either resurrect the infinite retry or keep deleting email and WhatsApp reminders.

title: retryCount cleanup deletes unrelated and already-scheduled reminders
body: The cron deleteMany ORs past-due SMS reminders with retryCount > 1, and that second branch has no method, scheduled, or scheduledDate filter. WorkflowReminder is shared by EMAIL, SMS, and WHATSAPP, so the next run of this SMS job deletes every row with retryCount > 1, including non-SMS reminders and SMS reminders Twilio already accepted (scheduled true, referenceId set). Losing referenceId means a later booking cancellation cannot cancel the provider message, and reminders this job does not own can disappear. Restrict the predicate to unscheduled SMS rows (method SMS, scheduled false, retryCount > 1).

title: Any two errors permanently drop the SMS reminder
body: retryCount is incremented in the catch that wraps the whole reminder, not only a rejected Twilio schedule. Profile lookup, booker URL, template rendering, or a DB error after Twilio already returned a SID all count as failures. After two such errors the next cron deletes the row because retryCount > 1. A short outage therefore discards every in-window SMS reminder instead of retrying until the event. If scheduleSMS succeeded and the following update threw, the catch still increments, scheduled stays false, and the next run can schedule a duplicate while the later delete orphans the Twilio messages. Count only definitive send failures, and do not increment once a provider SID exists. If the catch's own update throws, that exception leaves the loop, the handler never responds, and the rest of the batch is skipped.

title: Missing recipient or empty body retries until the event
body: retryCount is only updated inside the branch that calls Twilio. If sendTo is missing or the message is empty, the reminder stays scheduled false with retryCount 0 and is selected again on every cron run until scheduledDate is past. That is a permanent failure (no destination never reaches Twilio) and is exactly the infinite reschedule this change is meant to stop, while also keeping the job busy reprocessing the same rows. Treat that path as a failed attempt or delete the reminder.

title: Overlapping crons lose retry increments and can double-send
body: retryCount is written as reminder.retryCount + 1 from the value read at the start of the loop, not as an atomic increment, and the row is not claimed before twilio.scheduleSMS. This handler awaits Twilio and several DB calls per reminder, so a run can outlast the cron interval and a second invocation loads the same unscheduled rows. Both workers schedule an SMS and both write the same retryCount, so the counter may never exceed 1, the new delete never fires, and the attendee gets duplicate messages. Use an atomic increment and a conditional update (id and scheduled false) to claim the reminder before calling Twilio.

title: No tests for retry limit or delete scope
body: The new delete predicate and retryCount updates have no tests. Nothing checks that EMAIL/WHATSAPP rows and already-scheduled SMS rows (with a provider referenceId) survive cleanup, that an SMS reminder is removed only after two scheduling failures, or that a missing sendTo does not spin until scheduledDate. Those are the paths that drop reminders or fail to stop the infinite cron loop.

title: retryCount cleanup deletes every workflow reminder, not just failed SMS
body: The new deleteMany ORs the existing past-due SMS clause with `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` and that second clause has no method, scheduled, or date filter. WorkflowReminder is shared by EMAIL, SMS, and WHATSAPP. Every cron run therefore permanently deletes any reminder of any method once retryCount is greater than 1, including a row that was already scheduled and still has a provider referenceId. The comment on line 28 still says this only removes past SMS reminders. Scope the predicate to unscheduled SMS (and filter the later findMany the same way); otherwise any non-SMS writer of this new column, or a scheduled SMS row that ever exceeds the cap, loses the reminder.

title: A successful Twilio schedule is counted as a failure if saving the SID throws
body: twilio.scheduleSMS runs before the update that sets scheduled and referenceId. If Twilio accepts the message and that update throws, the new catch increments retryCount and leaves scheduled false and referenceId unset. The next cron loads the same reminder again and sends another SMS. After retryCount exceeds 1 the row is deleted, so the already accepted Twilio message can no longer be cancelled from a stored SID. Only a failed scheduleSMS call should advance retryCount; if persistence fails after Twilio accepts the message, cancel that message or retry the write without treating it as a failed send.

title: Overlapping crons lose retry increments and can double-send
body: Both failure paths write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` from the value loaded at the start of the loop instead of an atomic increment. Two overlapping runs of this cron can both select the same unscheduled reminder, both call Twilio, and both store the same next count. Recipients get duplicate texts, and because the stored count never moves past that shared value the `retryCount > 1` delete may never fire, so the retry cap does not hold under overlap. Claim the row (conditional update of scheduled, or increment in the database) before calling Twilio.

title: Missing number or empty body never counts toward the retry cap
body: retryCount is incremented only when Twilio returns a falsy result or throws, and only inside `if (message?.length > 0 && sendTo)`. If the attendee or step has no phone number, or the step has no reminder body and the template is not REMINDER, the loop skips the row and leaves scheduled false and retryCount at 0. That reminder is loaded again on every cron run until scheduledDate is in the past, which is the unbounded reschedule this PR is meant to stop. Treat a missing destination or empty message as a failed attempt, or delete the reminder immediately.

title: No test locks the retry cap or the delete scope
body: The new failure accounting and deleteMany predicate have no tests.
